11200417.value: 現代社會嚴重依賴於因特網，因特網故障可能導致嚴重的社會經濟後果，所以網絡復原力非常重要。本項目旨在研究具有成本效益的多層通信網絡生存性設計新方法，從而建立可應對多種故障情況下的彈性網絡。 我們將提供接近最優的分析解決方法，這些接近最優解法可應用在使用多種傳輸技術的具有實際規模大小的網絡中，網絡業務流量模型既包含恆定流量成分也包含可變化流量成分。此次基於網絡生存性的研究極大地拓展了我們之前的工作，它增加了研究的復雜性和挑戰性，我們的目標是獲得準確的、可擴展的、可被驗證的解決方法。 本設計目標是為鏈路提供充足的有足夠的冗餘量但不過度的容量分配。我們旨在對路徑和傳輸技術提出接近最優的選擇，以便使息稅前利潤(簡稱EBIT)最大化，而息稅前利潤(EBIT)是一種很重要的金融量度，其常常應用於商業和資源分配。 我們的成本度量標準包括經營成本、攤銷資本支出以及網絡資源利用率影響的費用和服務中斷時的罰款。這種因故障／流量激增事件優先處罰原則尚未在之前的多層網絡生存性優化設計中被考慮過。 我們將會提出基於故障恢復和流量激增下的路徑選擇和容量分配的高效啟發式算法。由於成本和路徑選擇互相依賴，我們基於流量分配鏈路容量，循環計算直到收斂，這將為多層網絡生存性設計問題提出一種嶄新的解決方法。 我們將會以整數線性規劃的解和界為基準來驗證我們提出的啟發式算法。這種考慮可變化業務流量(既含短相關又含長相關模型)在多層網絡生存性模型研究中是嶄新的(也是重要的)，因為這可以使我們考慮許多實際設計中存在的問題，比如，統計多路復用、動態連接和基於流量大小的路徑選擇。 本項目方案的優勢和創新性在於我們的研究更具有實用價值，即可以應用於解決基於更實際的網絡和流量模型的可擴展性問題並獲得整數線性規劃無法得到的解。因此，本研究項目的優勢在於打破現有解決方案的限制。

11200417.label: Realisation of objectives
11200417.value: To address Objective 1, we developed a new algorithm for survivable and cost-effective design of multi-layered telecommunications networks with a general number of layers, nodes and links. This algorithm is built on and significantly extends our previous algorithm called multi-layered market algorithm (MMA) for resource allocation of multi-layered networks where survivability was not considered. We call our new algorithm Resilient MMA (RMMA). An important step towards RMMA has been the development of novel and realistic network and cost models. Our new network model includes key aspects of real networks that are either directly relevant to cost, or to operations that affect both performance and cost. We explored improved cost-effective routing and switching alternatives by bypassing the traffic to a layer below and considering a network that may consist of three different types of links: simple link, dynamic link, and virtual permanent link. We also studied in detail different traffic sharing allocation schemes in the different layers and cost optimizations. We showed that inclusion of sharing schemes in a multi-layered network optimization can significantly lead to more efficient resource provisioning. RMMA is able to allocate sufficient resources so that acceptable quality of service (QoS) of customers is still maintained even under conditions of disasters and failures. The novel aspects of RMMA include the incorporation of Variable bit-rate (VBR) traffic streams in survivable multi-layered network design together with the aim to minimize earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT). VBR and bursty traffic demands are modeled by long range dependent (LRD) processes such as the Poisson Pareto burst process (PPBP) and the LRD Gaussian process. Previous approaches only considered constant bit rate (CBR) traffic streams. EBIT is defined as annual revenues minus annual costs which include amortized CAPEX, OPEX, and penalties. Penalties are paid by an operator as a consequence of the service interruption that causes it not to meet its agreed grade of service (GoS). Given a set of failure scenarios, RMMA is developed to optimize the network operation and resource allocation taking into account common failure scenarios, e.g., single-link failures, single-node failures and multiple-link failures so that EBIT is maximized. MMA and RMMA have been implemented for a range of network traffic sharing schemes and cost models and for the various transport technologies in the different layers, and we provided cost and EBIT comparisons between these various alternatives. Significant efforts have been made to develop our multi-layered network design software based on our online software platform called network mark-up language (Netml). The new Netml platform includes a high-quality user interface that supports uploading any network and running our algorithms. This development of Netml was necessary for us to conduct numerical studies on “a wide range of network topologies, architectures, sizes, and other input parameters” (Objective 2). It is also used “to conduct experiments over a wide range of input parameters” (Objective 3). Although Netml is not explicitly mentioned in the objectives, it has been a significant preliminary hurdle that we needed to overcome. Having successfully completed the development of Netml, we were able to fully achieve all the project’s objectives. Our Netml interface is available online at https://netml.org. It is used by hundreds of students and other clients each year, to design, analyse, or simulate networks. On average each user uses the Netml system for 50 separate operations (analysing, designing, simulating, etc). For validation of MMA and RMMA, we have used, among other approaches, Integer Linear Programming (ILP) formulations. Note that ILP is not directly applicable to model VBR traffic and statistical multiplexing, so for such cases we used ILP based on peak traffic streams estimated at mean + several standard deviations. This enables ILP modeling to consider statistical multiplexing by considering these multiplexed traffic peak estimates to be lower than the sum of the peaks of the relevant sources. To address Objective 2, we generated a wide range of results of layered networks and their MMA and RMMA solutions under various settings of sharing schemes and cost models using the Netml interface. The numerical results obtained have validated and demonstrated the quality of MMA and RMMA results versus the ILP results. Note that for CBR traffic, ILP results are optimal but not scalable. Comparing the optimal solutions obtained by the scalable MMA variants versus ILP for a wide range of small network scenarios, and demonstrating that MMA achieves near optimal results, gave us the confidence to use MMA for large networks and to obtain near optimal solutions. Notice also that for cases involving VBR traffic, the ILP based on peak-rate resource allocation is not optimal, and we demonstrated that MMA achieves better results than ILP. Recall that for RMMA, we aim for EBIT maximization considering penalties and service disruptions in a multi-layered network. Another method used for validation is the so-called double-entry bookkeeping (DEB). This method is borrowed from the field of accounting, which constantly verifies that the total cost of network elements is equal to the total cost of carried traffic. Using DEB, we concluded that MMA in its current implementation produces valid and reliable results. Validation of any design algorithm in this way is, in fact, essential, and it was found, while developing RMMA that this validation was crucial for the algorithm development to succeed. In addition, we also validated the results, by visualization. Netml enables users to perceive and observe the assignment of capacity, routing, and utilization of resources. This highlights the importance of having visual tools, which enable users to see into the details of networks being investigated and to check that the results make sense intuitively. Such a method of validation by visualization is especially applicable to large networks that cannot be validated by ILP benchmarks. To address Objective 3, we provided extensive empirical results of MMA and RMMA (under normal operation and failure states). The networks used for these experiments include four-node networks, six-node networks, ring networks, NSFNET with 14 nodes and 21 links and Internet2 with 53 nodes and 122 links. We explained in detail several stopping criteria that affect the running time and demonstrated based on extensive empirical results that MMA is solvable in polynomial time, which makes it applicable to realistic size networks. All the networks used for testing are available, for perusal by the general public, in the repository of networks provided at the Netml website (https://netml.org), which includes more than 100 networks. To further address Objective 3, we studied how network performance is impacted by varying network parameters such as the traffic sharing schemes, flow-size dependent routing, statistical multiplexing as well as different GoS relaxation levels. The numerical results also demonstrated the benefit of dynamic or virtual permanent links, use of statistical multiplexing, and the use of traffic-sharing scheme for reduction of the total network cost. When traffic-sharing is used together with dynamic links more opportunities for routing flows are available and therefore more efficient solutions can be found. We explored how total cost and percentage of flow using dynamic or virtual permanent links are influenced by setting different flow set-up costs. Since the traffic streams could split for flow-size dependent routing based on a flow-size threshold value, we also explored and demonstrated the benefit of flow-size dependent routing under different thresholds in terms of reducing the total network cost.

11200417.label: Major findings and research outcome
11200417.value: In this project, for the first time, we provided scalable algorithms for cost effective resource allocation of survivable multi-layered communications networks that are applicable to practical traffic streams including VBR and CBR, by considering realistic traffic models and achieving resilience under a wide range of failure scenarios. As mentioned, this includes the use of EBIT to provide cost effective resilient design of a general multi-layered network that involves VBR streams modelled by an LRD process such as the PPBP and the LRD Gaussian processes. LRD processes capture the heavy-tailed characteristics of internet applications and therefore they are important components of internet traffic modeling and network design. None of earlier publications on survivable network design considering EBIT considered VBR traffic and multi-layered networks (with a general number of layers, nodes and links). As mentioned, previous approaches only considered CBR traffic streams. The algorithms have been thoroughly validated and tested. Our results are also applicable to scenarios that involve controlled service degradation in case of disasters and equipment failures by controlling the GoS levels which are economically beneficial to service providers. The core algorithms and software used in RMMA are also used in the MMA application of Netml (including single-layer network applications). These algorithms are all accessible from the Netml website, but run in separate processes which are CPU-time monitored, to preserve the integrity of the main server. Consequently, the key algorithms are in use very frequently, leading to high reliability in their operation. All the work described in Section 5.3 (Realisation of objectives) including the MMA and RMMA variants algorithms and their validations, is fully described in the PhD dissertation by C. Xing. Part of these results including the description and validation of MMA, the network and traffic models, sharing schemes, a demonstration that MMA is a polynomial time algorithm, and the various validation approaches including ILP, DEB and by observation, are also described in the paper by Xing et al. (2019). Both documents are provided in Part C of this report. See also a presentation by C. Xing on the current version of Nelml/MMA in http://www.ee.cityu.edu.hk/~zukerman/netml2_Eng.mp4 An alternative approach to provision of resilient connections in optical networks based on coded path protection was provided in the paper by Li et al. (2019), and for resource allocation optimization for wireless and optical virtualized connections have been presented in Q. Wang et al. (2019) and Lin et al. (2018), respectively.

11200417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11200417.value: Although the results of this project are based on realistic models and assumptions, applying these results to real-life applications still involves significant research challenges. One important such challenge is the application to multi-layered network slicing for provision of cost-effective virtualized networks to customers. Our work in Q. Wang et al. (2019) is only a first minor step in this research as it did not consider many of the important aspects we plan to consider including multi-layered networks, VBR traffic, and realistic networks and cost modeling. Another important extension of the MMA variants is to make them more applicable to the wide range of services and traffic streams that are available on the internet. Although we use realistic traffic streams modelling by a range of CBR and VBR (e.g. modeled by Gaussian and PPBP processes) that do have wide applicability, there is still a scope for more research challenges if we consider the wide range of real-life traffic sources that have wide range of access rates and behaviors. Our aim is to have service providers around the world using our Netml based tools for network design and for this more work on bridging the gap between theory and practice is needed.

11200417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11200417.value: Modern societies depend heavily on the Internet and its failure may have grave socioeconomic consequences, so its resilience is very important. One aspect of internet design is its layering structure from the application layer at the top to the physical layer at the bottom with independent protocols at each layer. This project provides novel methodologies for cost-effective design of survivable multi-layer communications networks to achieve resilience under a wide range of failure scenarios. In particular, it provides link capacity assignments, with sufficient, but not excessive, levels of redundancy. It considers realistic traffic network and cost models and achieves near optimal choices of the routing paths and transport technologies. Our cost-metrics include the operational and amortized capital expenditures, the cost of the effect of network resource utilization, and penalties paid when service disruptions occur. The project provides efficient and scalable heuristic algorithms for routing and capacity assignment considering recovery from failures, or traffic surges. Since cost and routing decisions are mutually dependent, we iterate flow and capacity assignment until convergence is achieved. This has led to a new approach to the design problem of survivable multi-layered networks. The algorithms have been validated and benchmarked against other non-scalable solutions and bounds.

11200717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11200717.value: Networked systems (NSs) are complex dynamical systems composed of a large number of simple systems interacting through a communication medium. These systems arise as natural models in many areas of engineering and sciences, such as sensor networks and cyber-physical system. However, most of the existing results need continuous successful communication, which bring high security requirements when under attacks. Also it is not easy to realize real-time communication of complete information. In this project, the main objective is to develop secure estimation and control algorithms that can be used by a NS to carry out prescribed tasks efficiently under cyber-attacks. Reliable attack detection scheme is one of the key factors for NSs to achieve desired secure performance. Incorrect or incomplete information caused by cyber-attacks will degrade the system performance seriously. It is necessary to design compensation strategy to minimize the information loss. Adaptive distributed fusion of attack detection will be studied in this proposal to deal with three kinds of cyber-attacks: Replay attacks, Denial of service attacks and false data injection attacks. These kinds of attacks occuring in NSs often exhibit different dynamical characteristics, and can be found in many cyber-physical systems. It is highly desirable to design effective information recovery schemes and event-based switching methods to improve security performance and enhance reliability and robustness against attacks. In particular, the hidden feature of attacks does bring some difficulties in designing reliable distributed fusion detection schemes for cyber-attacks, and thus indirectly affects the design of optimal compensation strategy to reduce information loss. Cooperative design of attack detection and estimation/control will be studied in this proposal to guarantee the secure estimation performance. This proposal has set up three new, challenging yet achievable objectives to the theoretical investigation. The results would have both theoretical and practical significance in communication-based network systems, in which actions must be transmitted to ensure a secure estimation and control performance. As an application example of NSs, these adaptive attack detection, secure estimation and control schemes will bring great benefit to the monitoring and control of power grid. Hence, it will improve the performance, reliability and applicability. Our results are expected to provide a fundamental secure estimation and control investigation for NSs under cyber-attacks. 网络化系统是由多个简单的系统通过通信媒介组成的一类复杂动力学系统。其在很多工程和科学领域作为自然模型出现，比如传感器网络和信息物理系统。但是，现有的绝大部分关于网络化系统的结果都是基于网络节点间连续不断的成功通信，这会导致系统在攻击下有很高的安全需求。在工程上，网络化系统实现完全信息的实时通信也是一件很困难的事情。因此，本项目的主要目标是给出网络化系统在攻击下的安全估计与控制的有效算法。 可靠的攻击检测策略是网络化系统实现期望的安全性能的关键因素。由网络攻击导致的有错误或者不完全的信息会严重破坏系统性能。因此，设计一种用于最小化信息丢失的补偿策略对网络化系统是必要的。在本项目中，我们将利用攻击检测的自适应分布式信息融合来处理三种典型的攻击：重放攻击、阻断服务攻击以及虚假数据攻击。这些攻击在信息物理系统中广泛存在，它们在网络化系统中会呈现出不同的动力学特性。 设计有效的信息恢复策略以及基于事件的切换方法来改进系统的安全性能，提高系统对于攻击的可靠性和鲁棒性是非常有必要的。特别的，对网络攻击，攻击隐藏的特性会给我们设计可靠地分布式融合检测方法带来很大的困难，进而间接地影响我们设计减少信息丢失的最优补偿策略。在本项目中，我们将提出针对攻击检测以及估计/控制的协同设计，以保证网络化系统的安全估计性能。 本项目将建立三个新的、有挑战性的和可以完成的理论研究目标。本项目的研究结果对基于安全通信的网络化系统有理论上的和应用上的重要性。作为网络化系统的重要应用，自适应攻击检测、安全估计与控制策略将会给电力网络的监测与控制带来很大的益处。它将会改进电力网络的性能、可靠性以及应用性。本项目的研究结果预期将会给出网络化系统在攻击下的安全估计与控制的基本框架。

11200717.label: Realisation of objectives
11200717.value: All three objectives are fully realized in different parts of the project. The research findings are published in IEEE Trans Cybernetics(1), IEEE Transactions On Systems, Man, and Cybernetics: Systems(3), Automatica(1), The journal Impact scores (2020) are 11.448(2/63), 13.451(1/63), 5.944 (10/63), respectively. The research works have been well recognized in top rank journals in Automation & Control Systems of WoS-Science Citation Index Expanded. Objectives realisation: This paper in [1] develops a fully distributed framework to investigate the cooperative behavior of multiagent systems in the presence of distributed denial-of-service (DoS) attacks launched by multiple adversaries (Objective 1). In such an insecure network environment, two kinds of communication schemes, that is, sample-data and event-triggered communication schemes, are discussed. Then, a fully distributed control protocol with strong robustness and high scalability is well designed (Objective 3). This protocol guarantees asymptotic consensus against distributed DoS attacks. In this paper, “fully” emphasizes that the eigenvalue information of the Laplacian matrix is not required in the design of both the control protocol and event conditions. For the event triggered case, two effective dynamical event-triggered schemes are proposed, which are independent of any global information (Objectives 2 and 3). Such event-triggered schemes do not exhibit Zeno behavior even in the insecure environment. In the presence of malicious denial-of-service (DoS) attacks, the paper in [2] investigates the tracking control of mobile robots. Some explicit characterizations are presented for frequency and duration properties of malicious DoS attacks (Objective 1). A hybrid model is established by considering malicious DoS attacks and event-triggering control. The significance of this paper is to develop a set of event-triggering conditions to ensure the tracking convergence. In addition, these conditions can guarantee the existence of uniformly positively minimum interval between any two successive transmissions (Objective 2). Finally, a practical experiment is presented by considering the tracking control of an Amigobot mobile robot over a wireless network with DoS attacks (Objective 3). An attack defense method is proposed in paper [3] to address the secure remote state estimation problem caused by linear man-in-the-middle attacks in cyber–physical systems (CPS)(Objective 2). We utilize the pseudo-random number as a watermarking to encrypt and decrypt the data transmitted through the wireless network. Via the proposed method, the transmitted data in the normal operation can be recovered (Objective 2). Since the data modified by the attacker can be marked with the water marking, the χ2 detector is capable of detecting the attack. For three different attack scenarios, we analyze the evolution of the remote estimation error covariances and the detection performance, respectively (Objective 3). In the sense of minimizing the estimation error covariance, the optimal parameter set of the watermarking is derived. Furthermore, the proposed method can even be extended to detect the false data injection attack and the replay attack (Objective 1). This paper in [4] is concerned with the fixed-time cooperative relay tracking control problem for a set of planar agents in a surveillance network. The plane is partitioned into multiple “capture regions” by using the Voronoi partition according to agents’ positions(Objective 3). Once an evader enters into a new capture region, one agent of the tracer team stops and the tracking mission is relayed to another one who is in charge of the new region. As a result, an impulsive model is proposed to describe the problem and a distributed fixed-time cooperative relay control strategy is provided (Objective 3) that is not dependent on initial condition. This article in [5] deals with the observer-based proportional-integral-derivative (PID) security control problem for a kind of linear discrete time-delay systems subject to cyber-attacks (Objective 1). The cyber-attacks, which include both denial-of-service and deception attacks, are allowed to be randomly occurring as regulated by two sequences of Bernoulli distributed random variables with certain probabilities. A novel observer-based PID controller is proposed such that the closed-loop system achieves the desired security level and the quadratic cost criterion (QCC) has an upper bound (Objective 2). Sufficient conditions are derived under which the exponentially mean-square input-to-state stability is guaranteed and the desired security level is then achieved. Subsequently, an upper bound of the QCC is obtained and the explicit expression of the desired PID controller is also parameterized. (Objective 3).

11200717.label: Major findings and research outcome
11200717.value: In this project, various attack models have been investigated such as denial-of-service (DoS) [1],[2],[5] false data injection attack [3], the replay attack [3], and deception attacks [5]. The research outcome is summarized as follows: (I) Attacks and event-triggering communication scheme under multi-agents systems [1] [2] This paper in [1] develops a fully distributed framework to investigate the cooperative behavior of multiagent systems in the presence of distributed denial-of-service (DoS) attacks launched by multiple adversaries. A hybrid model is established in [2] by considering malicious DoS attacks and event-triggering control. The significance of this paper is to develop a set of event-triggering conditions to ensure the tracking convergence. This is an important issue to save energy as well as recovering the damage under DoS. The above research result are significant to the development to the control design for sample-data and event-triggered communication schemes, A new framework has been established. (II) Remote state estimation recovery under attack [3] An attack defense method is proposed in paper [3] to address the secure remote state estimation problem caused by linear man-in-the-middle attacks in cyber–physical systems(CPS). Since the data modified by the attacker can be marked with the water marking, the χ2 detector is capable of detecting the attack. This is an interesting development to recover the performance of the CPS. (III) Relay tracking control under a surveillance network [4] To strengthen the security problem of a network, a fixed-time cooperative relay tracking control problem for a set of planar agents in a surveillance network is developed in [4]. This is a new approach to provide an insight to the "attack-defender" investigation when an evader enters into a new capture region. This model attempts to follow the evader by one agent of the tracer team in the region and the tracking mission is relayed to another one when it enters into other region. The model provides a deeper understanding of relay tracking control. (IV) Cyber-attack and PID control [5] A novel observer-based PID controller is proposed in [5] such that the closed-loop system achieves the desired security level and the quadratic cost criterion (QCC) has an upper bound. This approach has the advantages that the exponentially mean-square input-to-state stability is guaranteed and the desired security level is then achieved. The PID controller observer is aiming to maintain the security level of those traditional industrial designs under cyber-attacks (including DoS and deception attacks) .

11200717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11200717.value: The results in [2] have many potential extensions, including the characteristics for DoS attacks, the design method of the event-triggering mechanism, as well as other techniques routes used here. As for the framework considered here, finding the optimal attack and/or counter-attack strategies seems to be an interesting research topic. We have not considered the effect of potential limitations on the information communications, including quantization and delays. Moreover, we also envision the use of similar techniques to other types of attacks (like deception attacks) for the attitude coordination issues of networked VTOL aerial vehicles. Finally, the control and measurement channels are interrupted asynchronously is also another interesting research line. In this project, we utilize the secure modules for data transmission to assist the χ2 detector to detect the innovation-based linear attack in the remote state estimation scenario [3]. By reconstructing the structure of the secure modules to assist more sophisticated detectors, it seems feasible to further extend our approach to detect the general deception attack, which has an arbitrary attack model. Following the idea in [5], future research themes can be extended the use of our methods to more complicated Networked Control Systems with more sophisticated network-induced phenomena or cyber-attacks with time-varying probability distributions.

11200717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11200717.value: Networked systems (NSs) are complex dynamical systems composed of a large number of simple systems interacting through a communication medium. These systems arise as natural models in many areas of engineering and sciences, such as sensor networks and cyber-physical system. However, most of the existing results need continuous successful communication, which bring high security requirements when under attacks. Also it is not easy to realize real-time communication of complete information. In this project, the main objective is to develop secure estimation and control algorithms that can be used by a NS to carry out prescribed tasks efficiently under cyber-attacks. A new set of event-triggering communication schemes have been developed in the presence of attacks. In this project, several kinds of cyber-attacks: Replay attacks, deception attacks, Denial of service attacks and false data injection attacks were investigated. Reliable attack detection scheme has been developed to achieve desired secure performance. In addition, a relay tracking control under a surveillance network is developed. This provides a detailed constructive design on a "attack-defender" NSs model. On the whole, the research project provides both theoretical and practical significance in communication-based network. More importantly, the research result ensures a secure estimation and control performance in NSs.

11201117.value: 一种用于预测偏微分方程解的高斯建模方法

11201117.label: Project Objectives
11201117.value: To develop a GP modeling approach to predict the solution of a linear scalar PDE with boundary and initial conditions over an input domain. To develop a GP modeling approach to predict the solution of a coupled system of linear PDEs. To apply the above approaches to model parameter calibration and robust design optimization.
rows: To develop a GP modeling approach to predict the solution of a linear scalar PDE with boundary and initial conditions over an input domain.
To develop a GP modeling approach to predict the solution of a coupled system of linear PDEs.
To apply the above approaches to model parameter calibration and robust design optimization.

11201117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11201117.value: This project will develop a probabilistic method based on Gaussian process (GP) models to predict the solution of a partial differential equation (PDE) as a function of its inputs. A PDE, together with its inputs (spatial domain, equation parameters, and boundary and initial conditions), gives a prediction of one or more physical quantities over a space-time domain as its solution. For many practical problems, there is a need to quantify changes in the solution due to changes in the inputs. For instance, there is growing research in the subject of uncertainty quantification (UQ), which includes the forward problem of quantifying uncertainty in functionals of the PDE solution due to uncertainty in the inputs, and also the inverse problem of estimating unknown PDE inputs. Solving PDEs to high accuracy at many input settings is time-consuming. Thus, a statistical model that allows less accurate prediction of the solution with less computational effort but rigorous quantification of the prediction error is a useful alternative. This project will develop a GP model with these properties. It gives a probabilistic prediction of the true PDE solution as a function of the inputs using information from the PDE and its boundary conditions at a finite set of points. The proposed GP model is a nonparametric Bayesian approach to estimate the true PDE solution over an input domain. The effect of numerical errors in solving PDEs with meshless collocation methods is often ignored. Our model, which is a probabilistic meshless collocation method, will be used to quantify these errors and to develop sequential design approaches to solve the unsolved problem of balancing the quality of the discretization in the space-time and input domains. The proposed model has potentially pioneering applications in metamodel construction, parameter calibration, and product optimization. At present, discretization error in the space-time domain is ignored in metamodel building via computer experiments, i.e., the numerical solution is assumed to be the true solution, and effort is focused on quantifying the discretization error in the input domain. In parameter calibration, attempts to account for model bias lead to non-identifiable statistical models. Our model eliminates bias due to discretization error in the space-time domain. In product optimization, time-consuming high accuracy finite element simulations are performed to eliminate numerical noise that makes optimization of some functionals of the PDE solution difficult. Our model produces smooth estimates of these functionals without utilizing a fine discretization in the space-time domain.

11201117.label: Realisation of objectives
11201117.value: Objective 1 has been addressed in Article #1, Article #2, and Article #5. These articles propose Gaussian process (GP) models for predicting the output of time-consuming simulators that numerically solve a partial differential equation (PDE) with boundary and initial conditions, called an initial-boundary value problem (IBVP), as a function of parameters of the IBVP, which are inputs to the simulator. Note that herein, the term PDE refers to scalar PDE. The proposed models are constructed using data from a computer experiment, i.e., data obtained by running the simulator at points in an experiment design, and they are utilized as an emulator/surrogate of the simulator to accelerate tasks that would otherwise be too time-consuming due to the need for numerous simulator runs. Article #1 proposes a GP model for predicting the solution of a linear PDE with linear boundary and initial conditions, i.e., a linear IBVP, or the solution of an approximately linear IBVP (an IBVP that can be approximated by a linear IBVP), as a function of inputs that include parameters that affect the source term, boundary conditions, and initial conditions linearly. Note that these parameters are the coefficients of basis functions in truncated series representations of the source term, boundary conditions, and initial conditions (which are functions of space-time), and the proposed model is more generally applicable to predict a linear functional of the IBVP solution. The principle of superposition implies that for linear IBVPs, the relationship between the IBVP solution and parameters that affect the source term, boundary conditions, and initial conditions linearly conditional on all other inputs is a linear relationship, while for approximately linear IBVPs, the relationship is an approximately linear one. This conditional linear or approximate linear relationship is captured by the proposed GP model via judiciously chosen prior mean and covariance functions. As illustrated with examples, the proposed model predicts better, i.e., gives point predictions with higher accuracy and prediction intervals with shorter length and/or better coverage, than the standard (stationary) GP model. Article #2 proposes a GP model for predicting the solution of a linear or approximately linear IBVP as a function of inputs that include parameters that affect the source term nonlinearly. The proposed model is developed from Green’s representation of the solution of a linear IBVP, which is given by a convolution of Green’s function and the source term plus a residual term that does not depend on the source term. It transforms the nonlinear effect of the source term parameters into a functional linear effect, i.e., the convolution of a kernel and the source term, that can be more reliably estimated with data than the original nonlinear effect. The proposed model predicts better than several existing GP models, as demonstrated with an example. Note that the model proposed in Article #2 complements the model proposed in Article #1, as the model in Article #2 is for the case where the source term depends nonlinearly on its parameters whereas the model in Article #1 is for the case where the source term, boundary conditions, and initial conditions depend linearly on their parameters. Moreover, the model proposed in Article #2 can be extended to linear and approximately linear IBVPs with parameters that affect the boundary or initial conditions nonlinearly, as indicated in that article. Article #5 proposes a GP model that satisfies given boundary constraints, i.e., constraints on the input-output relationship at the boundary of the experiment domain. In emulator construction for simulators that solve IBVPs, boundary constraints often arise from knowledge of the IBVP solutions corresponding to simulator input values on parts of the experiment domain boundary. The proposed model is shown to predict outputs of simulators that solve IBVPs better than alternative models when there are known boundary constraints. Objective 2 has been addressed in Article #1 and Article #2. The GP models proposed in these articles for predicting the solution of an IBVP are shown in the respective articles to be also applicable for predicting the solution of a system of coupled PDEs with boundary and initial conditions, called a coupled IBVP. Specifically, the GP model proposed in Article #2 can be used to predict a scalar component of the solution of a system of linear coupled PDEs with linear boundary and initial conditions, i.e., a linear coupled IBVP, or that of an approximately linear coupled IBVP, as a function of inputs that include parameters that affect the source term nonlinearly. By modeling each scalar component with one independent version of the proposed GP model, all scalar components of the solution can be predicted. The proposed model, whose mathematical form is based on Green’s representation of the solution of a linear coupled IBVP, transforms the nonlinear effect of the source term parameters into a functional linear effect that can be more reliably estimated with data than the original nonlinear effect. Numerical examples demonstrate that the proposed model predicts better than alternative models. Additionally, the GP model proposed in Article #1 is also applicable for predicting the solution of a linear or approximately linear coupled IBVP as a function of inputs that include parameters that affect the source term, boundary conditions, and initial conditions linearly. An example demonstrates that the proposed model predicts better than the standard GP model. Objective 3 has been addressed in Article #3 and Article #4. Article #4 proposes a computationally efficient GP model for high-dimensional simulator outputs that represent IBVP or coupled IBVP solution values on a space-time grid, and applies it to solve the multi-functional target robust parameter design (RPD) problem. The proposed model uses separable regression and prior covariance functions. This enables Kronecker product matrix algebra formulas to be exploited to derive computationally efficient formulas for computing estimates of the model parameters, the posterior means of the expected loss objective functions for multi-functional target RPD, and credible intervals for the objective functions. The proposed model is employed for multi-functional target RPD of a coronary stent based on a simulator of the stent expansion process, which solves a coupled IBVP. Article #3 proposes a method that uses a radial basis function model to perform RPD with an uncertain objective function based on a stochastic simulator. It is applied to facilitate RPD of a drug delivery system modeled by a linear IBVP with stochastic boundary conditions. Note that for Objective 3, models different from those developed for Objectives 1-2 are proposed and used for specialized RPD (also called robust design optimization) problems to solve the problems appropriately. 11201117.label: Major findings and research outcome
11201117.value: Physical systems are often modeled using a PDE with boundary and initial conditions, called an IBVP, or a system of coupled PDEs with boundary and initial conditions, called a coupled IBVP. Emulator/surrogate construction for time-consuming simulators that solve linear or approximately linear IBVPs (or coupled IBVPs) has important applications. The main research outcome of this project is the development of emulators that exploit the linearity or approximate linearity of the functional relationship between the solution of a linear or approximately linear IBVP (or coupled IBVP) and its source term, boundary conditions, and initial conditions, as described in Article #1 and Article #2. By using such information, the proposed emulators improve on standard emulators that treat the simulator as a black box. Article #1 proposes a GP model for predicting the solution of a linear or approximately linear IBVP (or coupled IBVP) that takes into account the linear or approximately linear dependence of the solution on parameters that affect the source term, boundary conditions, and initial conditions linearly conditional on all other inputs. These parameters are the coefficients of basis functions in truncated series representations of the source term, boundary conditions, and initial conditions, which are common in practice. As the proposed model imposes the known conditional linear (or approximate linear) relationship in prior specification, it predicts better than the standard GP model (which ignores the prior information). Article #2 proposes a GP model for predicting the solution of a linear or approximately linear IBVP (or coupled IBVP) as a function of parameters that affect the source term nonlinearly, which are prevalent in physics-based models of the source term. The proposed model, which is developed from the expression of the solution of a linear IBVP given by a convolution of Green’s function and the source term plus a residual term, transforms the nonlinear effect of source term parameters into a functional linear effect that can be more reliably estimated with data than the original nonlinear effect. This enables the proposed model to outperform existing GP models. Another important research outcome of this project is the development of a computationally efficient GP model for high-dimensional simulator outputs that represent IBVP (or coupled IBVP) solution values on a space-time grid and its application to multi-functional target RPD, as described in Article #4. Computationally efficient formulas for model fitting and posterior computations are obtained for the proposed model via Kronecker product matrix algebra manipulations.

11201117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11201117.value: There are three areas with potential for further development. First, the proposed models in Article #1 and Article #2 assume that the space-time domain over which the IBVP is solved is fixed. However, it is common to parameterize the space-time domain and vary it in a computer experiment. For example, when it is of interest to optimize the geometry of a product, the product geometry will be parameterized by some method, and an optimization procedure will be applied to optimize the parameters. Extension of our proposed models in Article #1 and Article #2 so that they are applicable to problems with varying space-time domains is needed. Second, extension of the model proposed in Article #2 to predict the solution of a linear or approximately linear IBVP as a function of parameters that affect the boundary conditions or initial conditions nonlinearly should be investigated. Third, as optimization of simulators using a GP-emulator-based sequential design procedure called Bayesian optimization is gaining increasing attention, it is of interest to employ our improved GP models for Bayesian optimization of simulators that solve linear and approximately linear IBVPs.

11201117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11201117.value: Emulators/surrogates of time-consuming simulators of physical systems that solve a partial differential equation (PDE) with boundary and initial conditions, called an initial-boundary value problem (IBVP), are built to accelerate computation tasks involving the simulators. This project developed novel Gaussian process (GP) models/emulators that are constructed via computer experiments for predicting solutions of linear and approximately linear IBVPs, which are widely used classes of IBVPs in engineering. Unlike existing emulators that treat the simulator as a black box, the proposed models exploit the linear (or approximately linear) dependence of the solution of a linear (or approximately linear) IBVP on its source term, boundary conditions, and initial conditions. Consequently, the proposed models often predict IBVP solutions more accurately with less uncertainty than existing models. Application of the proposed models to predict solutions of linear and approximately linear coupled IBVPs, which comprise coupled PDEs, is also considered, and excellent results are obtained. Additionally, this project developed a GP emulator that satisfies boundary constraints, a GP emulator for high-dimensional outputs that represent IBVP solutions, and an emulator for uncertain objective functions. The last two emulators, which are designed to be computationally efficient, achieve good results when applied to perform robust design of engineering systems.

11201817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11201817.value: 由於良好的美觀和經濟性，玻璃幕牆已經被廣泛用於現代建築（如商場，展覽中心和辦公樓），但是玻璃幕牆卻很容易受到火災的影響，例如在火災中斷裂和破壞。一旦玻璃幕牆外牆完整性喪失，將會為新鮮空氣的進入提供一個通道，從而為火災提供水平和垂直擴展的空間，最終往往導致毀滅性的火災與悲劇性後果。例如，2009年北京央視辦公大樓的火災造成1人死亡，經濟損失2億元。目前灑水噴頭已成為建築物消防系統的一部分，也是一種提高玻璃幕牆防火性能的技術，灑水噴頭噴水形成的水幕可以緩解玻璃外表面溫度的急劇變化，並防止熱衝擊。然而，對與由水幕保護的玻璃幕牆，其不同加熱速率下的力學性能尚未闡明，仍需進行詳細研究。 傳統的有限元方法在模擬流體流動，裂紋擴展和損傷方面的效率一直受到挑戰，因此本研究擬構建基於無網格方法的計算框架，不僅考慮水幕和玻璃幕牆之間的流體-結構相互作用（流固耦合FSI），亦考慮玻璃幕牆在火災高溫下的熱機械斷裂性質。當水膜流體沿著玻璃幕牆表面流動時，流固耦合效應可能影響水膜的完整性，這往往由水膜厚度、速度、以及玻璃幕牆的結構屬性決定。此外，由噴水引起的溫度不均勻分佈將對應力狀態和應變狀態產生負面影響。因此，本研究將著重闡明水膜流體運動和玻璃幕牆斷裂共同作用的多物理場耦合機制。 本研究擬進行一系列試驗，以探究使用噴灑器時，具有向下流動的水幕的玻璃立面的熱力學行為。與試驗數據將與無網格數值模擬結果進行比較和相互驗證。同時，重點分析水幕保護玻璃幕牆防火過程中的性能參數，包括水膜和玻璃厚度、噴淋器反應時間、耐水噴霧的最高溫度和裂紋的開始和擴展路徑等，以全面了解噴淋系統對火災條件下玻璃幕牆的保護作用，並基于優化理論來開發水幕保護玻璃幕牆的最佳設計方法。

11201817.label: Realisation of objectives
11201817.value: In this proposed research project, all objectives have been realized. A computational framework to simulate multi-physics coupling between water films and glass facades has been established and a constitutive model for thermal-mechanical and fracture mechanics has been developed. We found that the interactions between incompressible water film flows and glass facade structures are nonlinear multi-physics phenomena with similarities to fluid–structure interaction (FSI) problems in engineering. To establish a robust platform for investigation of the fundamental multi-physics involved in the water-glass interaction, an FSI model was developed for numerical simulations in this research. In the process, a heat transfer model based on energy, mass and momentum conservation law was developed. Once sprinklers are activated, the water film that develops on the glass surface can transfer heat by conduction and convection with the glass surface and, at the same time, absorb transmitted flame radiation. When radiation meets the glass, it is transmitted, absorbed or reflected away from the glass, depending on the spectral properties of glass. Furthermore, the heat conduction and convection between the water or glass and ambient space were also considered. A theoretical model based on heat flux transmission and the spectral properties of glass and water was developed. The overall process from water spray to completely leaving the glass can be divided into two dynamic stages: first, the water hits the glass with perpendicular speed, along with the water film thickness decreasing; second, the interfacial shear stress increases, thereby increasing the film thickness and then maintaining a relatively stable value. A kinetic model of water film was developed by calculating the final limit flow rate of the film and the sprinkler discharge rate. Several parameters, such as glass surface roughness and air flow rate, were included. FSI analysis results in a comprehensive understanding of the specific problems involved in this research, which is challenging due to the strong nonlinearity and multidisciplinary nature of those problems. To predict water-glass interactive performance, crack initiation and breakage, a reliable thermal-mechanical fracture constitutive model was built to facilitate mechanical analysis. In this model, the crack characteristics are represented and assessed by the energy release rates and stress intensity factors. Three modes of crack modeling were adopted: crack-opening, crack-shearing and crack-tearing. These three crack modes are classified by the different loading effects inducing the crack. Hence, the loadings are also classified into three corresponding types. The stress state near the crack tip area was taken into consideration in the form of the stress intensity factor in the development of constitutive relations. A numerical model has been developed to study the thermal-mechanical performance of glass facades under water spray during a fire. The proposed FSI model was incorporated with the thermal-mechanical fracture model for meshfree modeling. To improve FSI modeling accuracy and efficiency, meshfree numerical methods were applied to compute the FSI problems, with emphasis on the stress-strain states during the interaction between the water spray and glass panes. Emphasis was laid on the coordination of data transfer and consistency between the water spray and glass structure in the meshfree FSI modeling of glass facades. The FSI meshfree method uses the generalized Gauss-Seidel approach for the coupled analysis, with the fluid and structural computation performed in a sequential manner to achieve a multidisciplinary solution. Hence, the fluid field can be solved at a given moment with an assumed interface location. Then the resulting water pressures and stresses were applied to the glass facade structure as external forces, and structural computation were then conducted to update the position of the structural surface. A new fluid state was then created to accommodate the new interface location. An iterative process was used to ensure that the interfacial conditions of both the displacement and force were satisfied at the given moment before marching on to the next time step. A series of numerical experiments on glass panes has been conducted with different parametric designs and the simulation accuracy and efficiency have been validated. The key parameters include the water film and glass thicknesses, sprinkler reaction time, maximum temperature to withstand water spray, and crack initiation and propagation. An optimization algorithm for the fire-proof design of sprinkler systems and glass facades was developed. The optimal design of an automatic sprinkler system generally aims at economy, efficiency, light weight and fire safety. To implement optimization, an objective function was built by including these key parameters and taking into consideration objectives such as the fire resistance period. Since it was very difficult to obtain analytical optimization solutions for specific problems, computational iterative techniques were performed to find convergent results for the FSI problem with water-glass interactive mechanical performance, crack initiation and glass facade breakage. Throughout the multi-physics coupling process, meshfree node solutions were obtained concurrently by numerical iteration steps, which further generated the stress-strain states of the glass facades and the flow of the water spray. The multi-objective optimization function was solved numerically by Newton’s iterative method. The iterative procedure converges to the minimum thicknesses of the glass facades, critical temperature for sprinkler system activation, and water spray rate that ensure both sprinkler system efficiency and the fire safety of glass facades. In-house computational codes were developed for implementation of the simulation and fast optimization. A general optimization and simulation computing system capable of modeling heat mass transfer, thermal-mechanical properties, and crack initiation and breakage phenomena was established. To validate the proposed meshfree numerical computational results, a series of tests were carried out to evaluate the fire resistance of glass facades equipped with water film systems. This research has led to 6 high-quality research papers being published in refereed international journals.

11201817.label: Major findings and research outcome
11201817.value: In this work, a meshfree computational framework was developed to model the interaction between sprinklers and glass façades. The modeling scheme was developed with full consideration of water-glass interaction and the glass façade crack initiation and damage process. Such a meshfree computational framework is expected to be better suited to solve water-glass interaction problems involving changing boundaries and large deformations compared with traditional FEM. A robust thermal-mechanical constitutive relationship has been established as the overall thermal-mechanical performance of glass facades under water spray is intrinsically determined by constitutive laws. Besides, a series of numerical in-house codes were developed for the meshfree analysis, which will have great impact on sprinkler system research. A numerical model was developed for the simulation of the overall thermal-mechanical performance of glass facades under water spray in fire scenarios, which provides a direct assessment on the working efficiency of a sprinkler system and water-glass interaction. A number of parameters, including the water film and glass thicknesses, sprinkler reaction time, maximum temperature to withstand water spray, and crack initiation and propagation, were considered. The cooling and protective effects of water films and the influence of water films on the fracture behavior of glass facades were assessed by this numerical model. The proposed numerical experiments on the crack and breakage behavior of glass facades during sprinkler activation can be of particular significance to fire engineering design. In addition, an optimization algorithm for the fire-proof design of sprinkler systems and glass facades was developed. The results can provide useful practical and theoretical references to various scientific fields and have great potential for improving the fire performance of glass facades in practice. The above-mentioned points are the major findings and research outcome of this project.

11201817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11201817.value: Further studies on fires involving water-film protected glass facades could benefit from this meshfree-based modeling method. The mesh-free modeling framework can be used for predicting the heat conduction, failure behavior, stress distribution, crack initiation, propagation and breakage in consideration of various types of glass facades that has been developed in recent decades to fulfill architectural design requirements. In the later work, detailed research is still needed to understand glass facades protected by water films at different heating rates. Non-uniform fire loading conditions can be considered. Based on the outcome of this research, an optimization process has been utilized to develop equations for the optimal design of water-film protected glass facades. The optimization guidelines will be used for the practical engineering design of glass facades and sprinkler systems in modern buildings (e.g. shopping malls, exhibition centers, and office buildings). The effects of different fixing formats of glass facades on fire resistance will also be considered. Through the better understanding of glass facade breakage behavior in different fire loading conditions, installation forms, and stress states, it is expected that safer and more innovative facades can be designed for the applications to fire engineering.

11201817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11201817.value: We have developed a meshfree computational framework that takes into account the fluid-structure interaction between water films and glass facades, as well as the thermal-mechanical fracture properties of glass facades at elevated temperatures during fires. The meshfree simulation accuracy and efficiency have been compared and verified with data from a series of tests. A comprehensive understanding of sprinkler systems’ effects on glass facades under fire conditions has been reached by investigating the key parameters, including the water film and glass thicknesses, sprinkler reaction time, maximum temperature to withstand water spray, and crack initiation and propagation. An optimal design of water-film protected glass facades and sprinkler systems has been proposed, which can be used for the practical engineering design of glass facades and sprinkler systems in modern buildings. The research outcomes will have great potential of improving the fire performance of glass facades in practice and also serve as an important reference for the development of guidelines and standards.

11202017.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11202017.value: 計算基本半代數集的拓撲

11202017.label: Project Objectives
11202017.value: The only objective of this proposal is to design and analyze a new algorithm to compute the homology (Betti numbers and torsion coefficients) of a basic semialgebraic set, i.e. a set given by a family of polynomial equalities and inequalities. Algorithms to do this task already exist. But they are inefficient (the only explicit upper bound on their performance is doubly exponential in the number n of variables of the defining polynomials) and suspect of numerical instability when finite precision is used. The goal of our proposal is to design an algorithm that should be more efficient (we expect its dependence on n will be single exponential only) and numerically stable.

11202017.label: Realisation of objectives
11202017.value: The objectives of the project were fully achieved. We designed an algorithm with the properties we wanted it to have: to compute the homology groups of basic semialgebraic sets, in a numerically stable manner, and with a complexity that, outside a set of exponentially small measure, is bounded by a function which is singly exponential in the number of variables of the polynomials describing the set.

11202017.label: Major findings and research outcome
11202017.value: We designed an algorithm that computes the homology groups of basic semialgebraic sets, in a numerically stable manner, and with a complexity that, outside a set of exponentially small measure, is bounded by a function which is singly exponential in the number of variables of the polynomials describing the set. The article with these findings was published in the J. of the ACM, widely considered the most influential journal in computer science. We then used the new ideas behind our algorithm and applied them to an analysis of the Plantinga-Vegter algorithm. We gave, for the first time, a mathematical explanation of its efficiency. We also worked, and wrote a paper, on flocking under switching topologies.

11202017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11202017.value: The major potential for further development lies on the extension of our algorithm to one computing the homology groups of arbitrary semialgebraic set. We are currently working in this problem and have already obtained some results.

11202017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11202017.value: The most important topological invariants of a geometric object are its homology groups. They measure the number of holes of different dimensions (the so-called Betti numbers) as well as the ways the object is twisted (the torsion coefficients). Among these geometric objects, probably the most frequently found in practice are the semialgebraic sets. Putting both facts together one can feel the importance of computing the homology groups of semialgebraic sets. Unfortunately, this task appears to be very difficult (from a complexity theoretic viewpoint). Our works represents the first important progress in the last decades on this subject.

11203017.label: Project Objectives
11203017.value: To design a scalable biohybrid system that combines piezoelectric technology with cardiac tissue engineering for generating electrical outputs. To fabricate piezoelectric devices according the design as outlined in Objective 1, and characterize the selected piezoelectric materials at macro- and micro-scales. To establish three-dimensional cultures of primary mammalian heart cells and create biocompatible interface with piezoelectric materials to form functional biohybrid devices. To characterize and improve the electrical output from the biohybrid devices by different strategies, including the integration of rectification circuits and the use of arrayed format for highly parallel operation. To utilize the biohybrid devices developed in objective 1-4 to develop a self-powered and self-sustained neural stimulator for on-board control of biohybrid robotic systems.

11203017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11203017.value: 在這項研究中, 我們將開發一種基於心肌組織工程的生物機電混合系統並應用於生物電子儀器。 該系統將新型的壓電材料與具有三維立體結構的組織工程構件，從跳動的心肌細胞陣列中獲取機械能量從而產生可調製的電能信號，並用以驅動生物電子裝置。 為了最大限度的放大"細胞發生器"的能量輸出，我們將會爸壓電聚合物製成微觀尺度的為懸臂梁陣列, 並以此為基礎培養三維心肌細胞結構。 心肌細胞會自發收縮，從而為發電提供機械能的來源。 針對單個細胞能量有限的狀況，我們特別設計了基於印刷電路板的卡擴展陣列的系統結構，將使得我們細胞發電裝置的輸出達到福特級別，為真正的生物電子設備提供電源供應。 作為應用的具體示例， 該生物機電混合的發電機系統將進一步發展成為自我供電神經刺激器, 以控制在培養神經元網路的動作電位射擊。 我們認為, 成功地實施這一專案將為開發具有生物活性的機電元器件提供一個創新的視角, 並為發展可自維持的生物混合蜂窩機電系統創造一個新的應用方向。

11203017.label: Realisation of objectives
11203017.value: All the objectives has been successfully addressed in this project, and the results are summarized below: *Design and implementation of “Cell Generator” devices The core part of the “Cell Generator” is an array of microscale piezoelectric cantilevers that measure 400 µm in length and 200 µm in width and are separated by a 200 µm gap. The micro-striped rectangle design of the cantilevers helps to achieve an inhomogeneous growth of cardiomyocytes and to manifest the overall contraction-induced deformation along the long side. The innermost P(VDF-TrFE) layer is micropatterned by injection-molding from a PDMS master backed with another flat layer of PDMS. For the easy release of the P(VDF-TrFE) micropatterns, all PDMS surfaces are pre-treated with silane. Then, the P(VDF-TrFE) layer is sputter-coated with 20 µm gold on both sides to provide electrical interfaces. In order to improve the biocompatibility for culturing cardiomyocytes and to provide electric isolation, the surface of the cantilevers is then spin-coated with a thin layer of PDMS (~50 µm). Typically, the cardiomyocytes form micro-tissues and begin to beat after being cultured for 3-4 days. Disturbances from the contraction of the cardiac tissues can then be transduced into electricity. The piezoelectric property of the cantilevers is critical for the functional electric output of the “Cell Generator”. In our preliminary experiments, we have clearly verified that no electric potential could be generated from a device without a P(VDF-TrFE) layer. Even for materials with relatively low piezoelectric performance, such as P(VDF-TrFE) without annealing and poling, the electric output was almost negligible. The patterned P(VDF-TrFE) layer was annealed at 140 ºC for 2 hours to enhance the β phase, which was evidenced by an enhanced characteristic peak at 2θ = 20°, as analyzed by X-ray diffraction (XRD). The P(VDF-TrFE) layer showed a typical elongated needle-like crystalline structure that was several micrometers long on the surface. Then, gold electrodes were sputter-coated onto both sides of the cantilevers for electron transfer. The P(VDF-TrFE) polymer was then exposed to a strong electric field of 120 V/µm for 1 hour to reorient the dipoles to further enhance the piezoelectric property. In principle, mechanical stress should induce a separation of static ionic charge in the P(VDF-TrFE) layer due to changes in the electric dipoles and consequently generate a potential difference between the top and bottom surfaces. As characterized on a 1 cm × 1 cm × 100 µm film, 4 V voltage output could be achieved by a 10 N indenting force. From the waveform of the potential output induced by a 5 N force, electric pulses from two opposite directions could be clearly observed, indicating the bidirectional potential patterns of the outputs. If the device connection was inverted, a reversed waveform of the potential was obtained, confirming that the output was indeed derived from piezoelectric effect. *3D cardiac micro-tissues and the “Cell Generator” To engineer cardiac micro-tissues, primary cardiomyocytes were isolated from E18 embryonic rats and cultured in matrigel. The morphology of the resulting micro-tissues was controlled by constraining the cell growth area. Only the cantilever surface was rendered hydrophilic by pattern-coating of the matrigel, while the rest of the surface was treated to be hydrophobic to prevent cell adhesion. After 1-2 weeks in culture, a multicellular construct was achieved with strong expression of filamentous actin, indicating good accommodation of the cardiomyocytes in the matrigel. The cardiac micro-tissues also started to beat spontaneously at ~70 times per minute at this stage. For a micro-tissue of similar size as an individual cantilever, its contraction induced ~5 μm displacement. As the force generated by cardiac micro-tissues is typically at the micro-Newton level, we characterized the piezoelectric property of the micro-cantilevers in our device by microscale indenting. A nano-indenter was used to apply forces from 100 to 800 μN onto a single micro-cantilever in our device. The indenting spot was a circle (r = 30 μm) located 100 μm away from the cantilever tip. Even at 100 μN, the cantilever was deflected by 0.85 μm and created a 0.45 mV electrical potential. When applying an 800 μN force, the displacement was 5.6 μm and the piezoelectric potential reached 2.6 mV. When cardiomyocytes were cultured on an array of 40 suspended cantilevers (CG-40), the resulting micro-tissues wrapped the cantilevers three-dimensionally, and contracted to deform each P(VDF-TrFE) cantilever. Pulsed outputs of the electric potential with various magnitudes and irregular polarities were observed induced by the disturbances. The peak value was ~70 mV over a two-week culture period. As shown in Figure 4e, the potential output gradually increased in the first 3-4 days and reached a plateau afterward due to the establishment of a synchronous beating pace at later culturing stages. The output of the “Cell Generator” could be further increased by a larger array of cantilevers or by paralleling more arrays onto a printed circuit board (PCB). * A self-powered and self-sustained neural stimulator For practical use of the random electrical outputs from the “Cell Generator,” we included a current rectifying and energy storing circuit in the system. Current rectification was designed to improve the average output voltage by transforming the negative current into a positive current via a full-wave bridge rectifier. In the energy storing part, eight capacitors (22 μF) were set up within a serial-parallel switching module, which was engaged in parallel mode during charging and switched to series mode during power supplying. For proof of concept, we first used the “Cell Generator” to illuminate a LED. The electrical output from nine functional units containing a total of 540 cantilevers was collected. The peak-potential output reached as high as ~1 V, as monitored in real-time. After rectification, the capacitors were consistently charged. When the eight capacitors were fully charged, an output voltage of ~4.8 V could be achieved to briefly light an LED. Conceptually, the “Cell Generator” would be more suitable for bioengineering applications with low power consumptions. We then tested the feasibility of using the “Cell Generator” as a self-powered neural stimulator to evoke bursting of action potentials in a neuronal network. As shown in Figure 6a, primary neurons were cultured on a multielectrode array (MEA) with 60 channels, and a “Cell Generator” was connected to one channel to provide square voltage stimulations (700 mV amplitude, 100 ms pulse width) every 5 seconds. The rest 59 MEA channels were used for extracellular recording in the neurons. As shown in figure 6b, the electrical stimulations (provided by a “Cell Generator”) reliably evoked action potentials in the cultured neurons. Substantially more spikes was observed during a ~500 ms period following each electrical stimulation. The temporal correlation between the stimulation signals and evoked spike trains were further analyzed by raster plots and peristimulus-time-histogram (PSTH). In the raster plot, each black dot represents a single action potential, and each row represents a recording trial that spanned a two second period before and after an electrical stimulation. The evoked spikes were clearly observable immediately following every stimulation. In the PSTH, each bin represents the spike counts from every 10 ms. The PSTH also showed the occurrence of increased action potentials upon the application of stimulating signals, and such evoked hyperactivity gradually faded out within 1 second after the stimulation.

11203017.label: Major findings and research outcome
11203017.value: Bio-hybrid soft robotic devices present unique advantages for designing biologically active machines that can dynamically sense and interact with complex bioelectrical signals. Here, we develop a controllable cell-based machine that harvests energy from arrays of beating cardiomyocytes to generate electricity for biomedical micro-scale robotic applications. The “Cell Generator” device is based on an array of piezoelectric micro-cantilevers wrapped with three-dimensionally patterned cardiac cells. Spontaneous contraction of the engineered cardiac constructs provides the source of mechanical energy for electricity generation. We demonstrate that a single “Cell Generator” unit with 40 cantilevers can output peak voltages of ~70 mV, and a larger array of 540 cantilevers can directly generate a pulsed output as high as ~1 V. When integrated with an electrical rectification and storage circuit, we further show that the “Cell Generator” can provide functional outputs and work as a self-powered neural stimulator to evoke action potentials in cultured neuronal networks. This demonstration of “Cell Generator” technology provides an innovative perspective of exploiting live biological powering system on biomedical micro-scale robotic devices in the human body.

11203017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11203017.value: In this project, we developed a bio-hybrid system that integrates piezoelectric material with 3D-engineered living constructs for energy harvesting and electricity generation. The device was essentially based on an array of piezoelectric cantilevers, which was deformed by the spontaneous contraction of cardiac micro-tissues, thus transducing mechanical vibration into electrical energy. This work focuses on proof-of-concept and demonstrates the essential techniques to harvest small energy from engineered cellular constructs for electrical applications, much more work can be done to improve the “Cell Generator” in the future. For example, micropatterning of aligned cardiomyocytes could potentially enhance the overall contraction stress from microscale cellular constructs; the cantilever structures, piezoelectric materials, and peripheral circuits can also be refined to increase the output and miniaturize the whole system. We hope that the “Cell Generator” technology provides an innovative perspective of engineering and exploiting live biological components and sets the stage for the development of self-sustaining cellular machines and bio-hybrid systems for a wide range of applications.

11203017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11203017.value: A novel bio-hybrid system, the “Cell Generator”, is demonstrated by three-dimensionally patterning the cardiomyocytes on an array of piezoelectric micro-cantilevers. Spontaneous contraction of the engineered cardiac constructs provides the source of mechanical energy for electricity generation. This “Cell Generator” technology presents an innovative perspective of exploiting live biological powering system on biomedical micro-scale robotic devices in the human body.

11203217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11203217.value: In human, the protein-DNA binding interactions between transcription factors (TFs) and transcription factor binding sites (TFBSs) are the fundamental steps in controlling upstream gene expression. Determining the binding specificities forms the basis for downstream gene regulation analysis. Although the existing deleterious variant predictions have been well-studied on the observed single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) variations related to TFs and TFBSs, its performance on unobserved variations remains speculative. Therefore, we aim at developing novel deleterious variant prediction models for the DNA-binding specificities of human TFs on both sides (DNA-binding regions versus protein-coding regions). Initial testing results are given for each project phase. On the DNA-binding regions, we propose to develop the first in silico k-spectrum recognition model for encoding the DNA-binding specificities of human transcription factors. The k-spectrum model not only can predict TFBS sequence patterns from the protein sequences of TFs, but also can achieve the k-spectrum resolution to such an extent that local sequence context can be taken into account for deleterious variant predictions of observed/unobserved binding regulatory SNPs (rSNP) on TFBSs bound by human TFs. A mathematical example with complexity analysis is given in the main text. (Phase A; Objective 1) On the protein-coding regions, we propose to develop the first deleterious SNP prediction model tailor-made for the non-synonymous SNPs (nsSNPs) of human TFs. It is important as the past studies usually focus on fitting one model on all human proteins while our model is tailor-made for human TFs which DNA-binding characteristics are substantially different from the other protein families. Our initial testing model (TFmedic) predictions are found to be more accurate than Harvard PolyPhen-2 and JCVI SIFT as shown in Figure 4. (Phase B; Objective 2) Given the developed models on both sides from Phases A and B, we aim at integrating the models together to identify and prioritize the genome-wide co-variated eQTL pairs between binding rSNPs on TFBSs and nsSNPs on TFs' coding regions from the existing eQTL studies in the context of the DNA-binding specificities of human TFs. (Phase C; Objective 3) At the end, the developed models and resultant data will be tested and released as open-source software and public datasets respectively for scientific reproducibility. PI's past PhD supervisor from Toronto, Zhaolei Zhang, has agreed to provide biochemical cross-validations for TF-TFBS interactions; his support letter is attached. (Phase C; Objective 4) For illustrations, the whole research plan is outlined in Figure 1. 在人類中，轉錄因子（TF）和轉錄因子結合位點（TFBS）之間的蛋白質 - DNA結合相互作用是控制上游基因表達的基本步驟，確定結合特異性是下游基因調控分析的基礎。雖然現有的有害變異預測已經對TF和TFBS相關的單核苷酸多態性（SNP）變異進行了充分觀察研究，但其對尚未觀察的變異仍然是屬於推測性。因此，我們的目標是在兩側（DNA結合區域與蛋白質編碼區域）的結合特異性的背景下開發出新的有害變體預測模型。每個項目階段的初步測試結果詳列在正文中。 在DNA結合區域，我們提出開發第一個k-頻譜識別模型以模擬人類轉錄因子的DNA結合特異性。 k-頻譜識別模型不僅可以從TF蛋白質序列中預測TFBS序列模式，而且可以實現k-頻譜分辨率，使得局部序列上下文可以被考慮用於在人類TF結合的TFBS上的已觀察或尚未觀察的調節性SNP（rSNP）的有害結合變體預測 。正文中給出了數學示例及其複雜度分析。 在蛋白質編碼區域，我們提出開發第一個針對人類TFs的非同義SNP（nsSNP）有害預測模型。重要的是，過去的研究通常側重於在所有人類蛋白質上擬合一個模型，而我們的模型是針對人類TFs而定制的，其DNA結合特徵與其他蛋白質家族存在不同特性。初步測試結果顯示，我們的初始測試模型（TFmedic）預測比哈佛PolyPhen-2和JCVI SIFT更準確。 最後，已開發的模型和結果數據將分別被釋放為開源軟件和公共數據集，以實現科學重現性。項目主持人以往的多倫多博士生導師張兆雷同意為TF-TFBS相互作用提供交叉驗證。

11203217.label: Realisation of objectives
11203217.value: For objective 1, the k-spectrum recognition modeling is proposed to address the issues at the highest possible resolutions. The k-spectrum model can capture DNA motif patterns from protein sequences at the resolution in which local sequence context and nucleotide dependency can be taken into account completely. Multiple evaluation metrics are adopted and measured on millions of k-mer binding intensities from 92 proteins across 5 DNA-binding families (i.e., bHLH, bZIP, ETS, Forkhead, and Homeodomain), demonstrating its competitive edges. In addition, it not only can contribute to DNA motif recognition modeling but also can help prioritize the observed or even unobserved binding of single nucleotide variants on transcription factor binding sites in a genome-wide manner. Wong, Ka-Chun. “DNA Motif Recognition Modeling from Protein Sequences.” iScience vol. 7 (2018): 198-211. doi:10.1016/j.isci.2018.09.003 https://dx.doi.org/10.1016%2Fj.isci.2018.09.003 For objective 2, we have developed and compared different strategies to predict deleterious non-synonymous single nucleotide polymorphisms (also known as missense mutations) on the protein-coding sequences of human TFs. Taking advantage of evolutionary conservation signals, we have developed and compared different classifiers with different feature sets as computed from different evolutionarily related sequence collections. The results indicate that the classic ensemble algorithm, Adaboost with decision stumps, with orthologous sequence collection, has performed the best (namely, TFmedic). We have further compared TFmedic with other state-of-the-arts methods (i.e., PolyPhen-2 and SIFT) on PolyPhen-2's own datasets, demonstrating that TFmedic can outperform the others. As applications, we have further applied TFmedic to all possible missense mutations on all human transcription factors; the proteome-wide results reveal interesting insights, consistent with the existing physiochemical knowledge. A case study with the actual 3D structure is conducted, revealing how TFmedic can be contributed to protein-DNA binding complex studies. Wong, K. C., Yan, S., Lin, Q., Li, X., & Peng, C. (2018).
