11203217.label: Major findings and research outcome
11203217.value: For objective 1, the proposed approach directly addressed such issues at the unprecedented resolution based on the k-spectrum MRF modeling. It has been extensively benchmarked on millions of k-mer binding intensities from 92 TFs across 5 DNA-binding families bHLH, bZIP, ETS, Forkhead, and Homeodomain. The DNA-binding intensity correlation results demonstrate that the proposed approach is robust against different numbers of top k-mers. In particular, it can be scaled and keeps improving with increasing k-mers. The DNA motif pattern recognition results also reveal that it can capture not only the in vitro patterns but also the in vivo patterns in CIS-BP (v1.02). Last, the DNA motif patterns have been overlapped with the clinically verified SNVs, revealing genome-wide insights into the DNA-binding mechanisms across five DNA-binding families. Thanks to the underlying formulation, the models also have the potential to predict the deleteriousness of unobserved SNVs for the DNA-binding specificities of TFs. It is especially important to uncover unobserved deleterious SNVs as the current studies estimated that, even if we have 500,000 sequenced individuals, we can only observe 12% of all possible SNVs under the protein-coding variant subset (Zou et al., 2016). Therefore, our approaches should be promising based on the first principle in the near future. Wong, Ka-Chun. “DNA Motif Recognition Modeling from Protein Sequences.” iScience vol. 7 (2018): 198-211. doi:10.1016/j.isci.2018.09.003 https://dx.doi.org/10.1016%2Fj.isci.2018.09.003 For objective 2, we have designed and developed different computational frameworks to predict the deleterious nsSNPs. In particular, we have benchmarked multiple strategies and concluded that Adaboost with orthologous sequence collection can perform the best (namely, TFmedic). We have also compared TFmedic to the other state-of-the-arts methods, PolyPhen-2 and SIFT. The results demonstrated that TFmedic has its own competitive edges over the other methods although PolyPhen-2 has already been fully trained. Therefore, we have applied TFmedic further to other contexts. As the first application, we have fully trained TFmedic on the HumDiv dataset and adopted it to predict all possible nsSNPs on all protein-coding sequences of human transcription factors. The proteome-wide results indicate that there are specific pairings between reference allele and variant allele enriched or depleted in its deleteriousness, consistent with the existing physiochemical knowledge. As the second application, we have utilized and mapped the previously predicted harmful nsSNPs onto all sequences of specific DNA-binding domains of interests in a proteome-wide manner. The mapping has been cross-validated with the existing 3D structure of protein-DNA binding complex. The results indicate that our previously predicted nsSNPs can even reflect the 3D structural information on protein-DNA binding complexes. Wong, K. C., Yan, S., Lin, Q., Li, X., & Peng, C. (2018). Deleterious non-synonymous single nucleotide polymorphism predictions on human transcription factors. 11203217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11203217.value: As the future works, one may be interested in integrating the existing DNA shape data into the modeling process (Yang et al., 2013). However, it is subject to data availability as well as reliability since the current DNA shape data are mostly computationally predicted (Zhou et al., 2013) and may not be applicable to our DNA-binding specificity studies (Rossi et al., 2017). In the future, the TF cooperative behavior can be explored further for combinatorial nsSNP prioritization. Its downstream targets could also be interesting and related to the current deleterious nsSNP predictions in a co-evolutionary manner.

11203217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11203217.value: The successful completion of the project provides a solid foundation for people to understand the human genetics and its implications across different genetic diseases. In the short-term, the project pushed the research frontier in protein-DNA binding studies. For the mid-term impact, the study gives us a good example on interdisciplinary research for potential collaboration. In the long-run, the research outputs can enable the development of precision medicine in the future.

11203517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11203517.value: The ambition of this project is to scale up food recognition through ingredient labels prediction, which is helpful for applications such as nutrition estimation and dietary assessment. While there are more researches carried out recently for recognition of Western and Japanese food, little efforts have been dedicated to the domain of Chinese food. Chinese dishes are rich in color, texture and shape. Different from other food domains, ingredients are often fuzzily and wildly composed to create novel dish presentation. The difficulties of recognition originate from not just the richness in visual appearances, but also the “recreations” of recipes as a result of evolution along the space (e.g., geography region) and temporal (e.g., season) dimensions. Recognizing food categories, without understanding of ingredient composition, is limited to standardized cooked food such as in restaurants, and furthermore, hardly scales up and out to dishes prepared “in wild” in the free-living environment. This project addresses two problems: fine-grained ingredient recognition and cooking recipe retrieval. The general idea is to model ingredient composition for search of recipes, which can provide nutritional clues such as non-visible ingredients (e.g., salt, sugar) and quantities of ingredients. The challenges are threefold, nevertheless. First, the appearance of an ingredient varies depending on ways of cutting and cooking. Second, there is no direct mapping between ingredient composition and dish. Specifically, the same set of ingredients may mix and end up in different dish presentations and names. Third, the preparation of dish depends on preference of tastes and availability of ingredients, which varies across occasions and results in creation of different recipe versions. Finding the exact or best-match recipe for a query food picture, analogous to translation of visual-to-text or vice versa, is a non-trivial problem. The project considers these problems from the perspective of multimedia computing, more concretely, by integrating a variety of dish-relevant cues, ranging from ingredient and cooking procedure to food context, to disambiguate food recognition. Not only ingredients, but also the process and consequence of composition are computationally modeled. In addition, recipe search is posted as a zero-shot retrieval problem to scale up and out recognition by searching recipes for “out of vocabulary” dishes or dishes not previously known. The key contributions of this project are modeling of ingredient composition and extension beyond which to recognize a pre-defined set of food categories – both are new problems not seriously explored in the literature and essential for Chinese dish recognition. 這個項目的目標是通過預測食物的原材料來擴大食物識別的規模，這對營養分析跟飲食評估等應用都有幫助。目前有很多的研究人員對西餐以及日本菜的識別進行了相關的研究，但是很少有針對中式菜識別的研究。中式菜色彩豐富，質地細膩，形狀多種多樣。並且與其他國家的食物不同，為了創造出新的菜餚，中式菜菜品的原料組成往往不是固定。識別中式菜的困難之處不僅僅源與視覺外觀的多樣性，還源於沿著空間（例如，地理区域）以及時間（例如，季节）維度的發展造成的對菜譜的重創造。如果不理解食物的原料組成，而去對食物種類進行識別，僅僅只限於識別一些有標準做法的菜，比如餐廳的菜。更進一步說，這將會很難擴展到識別一些在餐館以外的地方烹飪的食物。 這個項目主要解決兩個問題：細粒度的食物原料識別以及烹飪菜譜的檢索。該項目的主體思想是對菜肴的原料建模，並用此來檢索響應的菜譜，這對食物中的不可見原料（例如鹽，糖）以及原料的用量信息提供營養線索。然而，該項目面臨三重挑戰。首先，食材的外觀取決於切菜以及烹飪方式。其次，原料组成与菜肴之间没有直接的映射。具體來說，同樣的原料能夠烹飪出不同的菜餚並且表現出不同的外觀。第三，菜餚的烹飪取決於口味偏好以及現有的食材，而這些在不同的場合不同，並導致用戶再創造出不同的菜譜版本。給定一張菜餚圖片，找到其正確或最匹配食譜的問題等价于與視覺到文本的翻譯，反之亦然，是一個有研究意義的問題。 該項目從多媒體計算的角度考慮這些問題，更具體得說， 通過整合各種菜餚相關的線索, 例如原料，烹飪過程以及菜餚上下文信息，去消除食物識別过程中的歧異。我們不僅僅對食物原料，同時也對烹飪過程進行計算建模。此外，菜譜檢索同時也被當成一個无训练样本的检索问题，并通過檢索之前沒見到過的菜餚的菜譜擴大食物識別的範圍。這個項目的核心貢獻是對食物的成分逕行建模，並對只能識別預定義食物集合的方法逕行擴展。這兩個都是在以前的工作中沒有被認真探索的新問題，同時也是中式菜識別的基礎。

11203517.label: Realisation of objectives
11203517.value: We have proposed a multi-task neural network model for food and ingredient recognition [TIP 2021]. The key research issues studied are 1) whether ingredient recognition should be performed at the image-level or region-level, 2) feature pooling strategies, and 3) performance difference between single-task and multi-task learning. We have also constructed a large dataset, VIREO-251 containing 251 Chinese food categories and 406 ingredient labels for experiments. We compared different versions of multi-task networks in the experiments and studied ingredient localization by region-level recognition. As the imbalanced number of training examples impacts the performance of ingredient recognition, we also researched how to model ingredient relationships to boost recognition performance by graph convolutional neural network [AAAI 2020]. For this study, we have leveraged the following knowledge for multi-relational graph-based recognition: 1) “is-a” relationship among the ingredients to build a hierarchy for recognition, 2) ingredient graph based on shared attributes (e.g., color, shape, cooking methods), 3) co-occurrence relationship of ingredients. In addition to ingredient recognition, we also investigated the recognition of other cooking attributes (cooking methods and cutting methods) for food recognition [ACM MM 2017]. We proposed a multi-scale neural network to recognize rich food attributes and then model them (ingredients, cooking techniques, cutting methods) jointly to address the ambiguity in food recognition (e.g., dishes with similar ingredients but different cooking or cutting methods). We have also investigated cross-modal feature embedding techniques for zero-shot recipe retrieval [TMM 2022, ICMR 2022, ACM MM 2020, CVPR 2019, ACM MM 2018]. First, we investigated the encoding of rich text information in cooking recipes by recurrent neural networks and attention mechanisms for cross-modal embedding [ACM MM 2018]. Later, we proposed an adversarial neural network with one generator and two discriminators for cross-modal learning on Recipe 1M western food dataset [CVPR 2019]. However, although satisfactory recognition performance was attained, the model cannot be transferred for recognition of Chinese food due to the domain gap. Consequently, we studied new neural networks for retrieving recipes of different cuisines [ACM MM 2020, ICMR 2022] by exploiting the state-of-the-art transferring learning techniques. We proposed a mix-up learning strategy and a new neural architecture (called recipe residual block) for cross-domain feature learning.

11203517.label: Major findings and research outcome
11203517.value: In this project, we studied two major approaches to model ingredient composition for food recognition: 1) attribute-based approach by recognizing rich food attributes and leveraging food knowledge for recognition [ACM MM 2017, AAAI 2020, TIP 2022], 2) cross-modal embedding learning to learn the pairwise relationships between food images and recipes [TMM 2022, ICMR 2022, ACM MM 2020, CVPR 2019, ACM MM 2018]. Using the proposed deep neural architectures, the attribute-based approach can show impressive performance for ingredient localization and even for recognizing the cooking and cutting methods of an ingredient. Nevertheless, this approach requires many expert-labeled training examples for network training. As a result, scalability becomes an issue because only a predefined set of ingredients in the datasets can be recognized and eventually used for recipe retrieval and food recognition. While we have studied zero-shot ingredient recognition based on food knowledge and statistical information mined from recipes [AAAI 2020], the recognition performance of ingredients is suboptimal for food recognition and recipe retrieval. On the other hand, the cross-modal learning approach is scalable and requires much less labeling effort for training data. This is mainly due to the availability of many recipe-image pairs on the cooking sharing websites for self-supervision model training. With these paired data, we have investigated the pretext tasks (e.g., synthesis of food image from recipe features, discrimination of image and recipe features) for effective self-supervised learning of cross-modal shared embedding space [CVPR 2019, TMM 2022]. The cross-modal learning approach is scalable to unseen recipe retrieval and dish recognition based on our experiments. It attains better performance in recipe retrieval and food recognition than the attribute-based approach. Nevertheless, cross-modal learning is generally known as a “black-box” learning model and cannot perform tasks such as ingredient localization. We have specifically constructed food image and recipe datasets for Chinese food recognition through this project. The proposed neural networks can achieve around 75% to 80% of accuracy in recognizing 400++ ingredients using an attribute-based approach [TIP 2021] and almost perfect recipe retrieval performance (i.e., find the right recipe within top-10 rank results) on Cantonese and Chuan recipe datasets using the cross-modal learning approach [ACM MM 2020]. We experimented with the proposed works on other food datasets (including Japanese and Western food cuisine) and achieved very encouraging performances. Some published papers [CVPR 2019, ACM MM 2017, ACM MM 2018] have received wide attention in this research area, including accumulating more than 50 citations, as indicated in Google Scholar.

11203517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11203517.value: The current research can be extended in two different directions: 1) cross-domain food recognition, and 2) multi-dish recognition. For (1), the current approaches, either based on attribute-based or cross-modal learning, cannot be generalized to recognize different cuisines of food based on the off-the-shelf transfer learning algorithms. In our experiments, despite that the proposed deep models achieve high in-domain recognition performance, transferring the model to a different domain (cuisine) with few training examples to yield satisfactory performance is highly challenging. In the future, research studies should be conducted to investigate the learning of invariant features not just across different modalities (i.e., image and recipe) but also across cuisines for food recognition. For (2), the current approaches cannot handle the recognition of multiple dishes on a plate. To extend the current works for food recognition in the wild, research on how to segment, count, and even measure the food volume on a plate is necessary for real-world applications. In the literature, there are various deep neural networks for general object segmentation, counting, and 3D volume estimation. It is worthwhile exploring how to integrate the research outcome in this project with the existing vision models for food-domain object segmentation, counting, quantity estimation, and multi-dish recognition.

11203517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11203517.value: In this project, we have investigated new approaches to model ingredient composition for food recognition and zero-shot recipe retrieval. We have studied an attribute-based approach, based on multi-task multi-scale neural networks, to recognize ingredients, cooking, and cutting methods. In addition, we leverage food knowledge and statistical information for zero-shot recognition using the graph convolutional neural network. We have also studied the cross-modal learning approach to extract features shared between food images and cooking recipes for zero-shot recipe retrieval, by investigating adversarial learning and self-supervised learning. We have conducted extensive experiments on various cuisine of food datasets (Chinese, Western, Japanese) to verify the proposed models and achieve encouraging performance, especially for ingredient recognition and cooking recipe retrieval. The research conducted in this project also provides insights regarding the scalability of food recognition. Specifically, learning cross-modal embedding features from multi-modal paired recipe-image data is a feasible way for zero-shot recipe retrieval and food recognition. The proposed deep neural networks can capture fine-grained details such as cooking procedures in recipes for cross-modal feature learning and food image reconstruction. Nevertheless, the performance of the network is not generalizable to different cuisines of food, which reserves more research studies in the near future.

11204117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11204117.value: In cases of compartment fire, the common objective of evacuees is to get out of the fire compartment. The exit door or corridor becomes a bottleneck area when the flow rate of the evacuees surpasses the throughput capacity of the door or corridor. This is a common problem in the course of evacuation. Microscopic evacuation models have been widely adopted to identify the bottleneck areas of building layouts. Such models simulate the movements of all evacuees and the interactions between them. They also provide building designers with detailed information on evacuations, such as overall evacuation time, flow pattern and bottleneck area locations, etc., which allows them to adjust their designs to provide efficient evacuation routes. However, researchers have reported that local effects (e.g. interactions between evacuees) have strong influence on macroscopic quantities such as flow pattern and total evacuation time. Therefore, it is very critical that a microscopic evacuation model be able to closely mimic the realistic interactions between evacuees and produce a reasonable simulation. Interactions between evacuees are especially important in congested situations. Conflicted movement may occur during an evacuation when evacuees are competing for vacant space. Some models that simply apply the probabilistic approach ignore psychological factors and randomly select one evacuee as the winner of the competition. Other models use desired velocity to simulate evacuees’ impatience without considering the dynamic growth of impatience over time. Such models only relate impatience to moving velocity. Furthermore, impatience is kept constant and does not grow with time when an evacuee is blocked by others. These models do not truly reflect the dynamic nature of impatience. This project will develop a dynamic impatience model to determine the impatience level of evacuees using their velocities and travelling times. If there is a movement conflict between a few evacuees, the one with the highest level of impatience will be picked to occupy the vacant space in the next time step. The basic features of the proposed impatience model have been investigated and developed to enable the dynamic change of impatience with time. A mathematical model that satisfies those features will be developed in the project. That model will be implemented in a cellular automata model for evacuation simulation. Experimental data will be used to calibrate the model’s parameters. We will also benchmark the performance of the model with other commercial models that are widely adopted in the fire engineering industry. 在密闭空间火灾情况下，人员撤离该密闭空间是共同的目标。当人员撤离的流量超过逃生门的最大吞吐量时，该逃生门将成为瓶颈区域。这是人员撤离过程中的一个常见问题。目前工程及研究人员已广泛采用微观疏散模型来识别建筑物布局中的瓶颈位置。这些模型模拟了所有撤离者的运动及其间的相互作用。模拟结果还可向建筑设计师提供有关疏散的详细信息，如整体疏散时间，流量态和瓶颈区域等，从而让他们调整他们的设计以提供有效的撤离路线。然而，研究人员发现人员间的局部效应可能会严重影响宏观量如流量和整体撤离时间。因此，微观疏散模型能否准确地模拟撤离者之间的真实交互作用并产生合理的模拟结果是至非常重要的。撤离者之间的相互作用在拥挤的情况下是尤为重要。在撤离过程中人员间争取歩进空间时，人员间的撤离动作可能会发生占领空间的冲突。一些模型简单地用概率法来处理并忽略了撤离人员的心理因素，此类模型只是随机地选择一名撤离者作为该冲突的获胜者。其他模型使用渇求速度来模拟撤离者的焦燥而不考虑焦燥度随时间的动态增长。这种模型只考虑焦燥度跟移动速度的关系。此外，被其他人阻止前行的撤离人员其焦燥度被保持不变，并没有随着时间増长。这些模型并没有真正反映出焦燥的动态性质。这个项目将发展一个动态焦燥模型，利用撤离人员的移动速度和时间来判断该人员的焦燥水平。如果几名撤离人员之间在逃生过程中产生占领空间的冲突，当中最焦燥的人员就会被选择作为该冲突中的胜出者并占领该空间。我们对此动态焦燥模型的基本特征已经作好了研究和开发的准备。在此项目中我们将开发能满足这些基本特征的数学模型。该模型将嵌入细胞自动机平台中。我们会利用数据来校正模型的参数并会跟其他用于消防工程的商业软件进行比较。

11204117.label: Realisation of objectives
11204117.value: 1. We extracted psychological theories related to impatience from literature review. The theories explained the possible changes and characteristics of impatience level of an occupants. The are as follows. a. Impatience level equals to or larger than zero. But it has a maximum over which the occupant will take action (e.g. overtaking or quit queuing). b. Impatience level of an occupant reduces if the walking speed is increased. c. Impatience level of an occupant increases along with time when his walking speed is lower than his/her walking speed. d. Impatience level of an occupant increases when his/her walking speed is lower than the average walking speed of his/her neighbors. e. Impatience level of an occupant increases when the impatience levels of his/her neighbors increase. Based on the above psychological theories, we translated them into differential equations which were discretized to algebraic equations. We consider objective 1 was completely achieved. 2. We implement the algebraic equations into a cellular automata (CA) model for simulating building evacuations on MATLAB platform. During the simulation, the impatience levels of all occupants are evaluated by our developed models. In crowdy situation, it is very common that few evacuees competing for a vacant space in front of them. We adopted the impatience level to allow the occupant with the highest impatience level to occupy the vacant space. The calculation of impatience levels and also the rule to resolve conflict in movements were implemented on the CA model. We consider objective 2 was completely achieved. 3. We conducted evacuation experiments in Sichuan University with our collaborator. The collected data were used to calibrate the parameters of our models. The model was also fine-tuned to reflect the actual human behaviors in movement. We consider objective 3 was completely achieved. 4. The calibrated model was benchmarked with traditional CA model by using the experimental data we collected from the experiments but unseen in the phase of model calibration. The results from our model and CA model are reasonably agree with the experimental results. However, our model can depicts the dynamical impatience levels of all occupants in the whole evacuation process. We consider objective 4 was completely achieved.

11204117.label: Major findings and research outcome
11204117.value: This project is one of the pioneer works incorporating psychological theories into building evacuation simulation model. We conducted literature survey on human behaviors in movement particular on the changes of impatience in different movement situations. The effects of impatience levels to movements were also investigated. Based on these findings, we translated the relevant psychological theories into mathematical models which, if necessary, were discretized to algebraic equations. We implemented the equations into the traditional cellular automata (CA) model for simulating the movements of occupants in the course of evacuation. We conducted different evacuation experiments for calibrating the parameters of the model. The calibrated model was benchmarked with other evacuation models. We found that our model, in term of accuracy, was comparable to other models. Most importantly, our model was able to depict the impatience levels of all occupants and present the levels by different colors. Therefore, the locations of the layout at which peoples were highly impatient can be identified. It provided important information to the building managers to plan their strategies in emergency situations.

11204117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11204117.value: Impatience is one of the important psychological features of evacuees. The competitive, cooperative, coordinative, collaborative, leader-follower behaviors in psychological theories are also determinative factors contributing to the human behaviors in movement during emergency. This project explored a new direction of evacuation model development by consideration of psychological theories. There are plenty of opportunities for the scientists in psychology, fire safety, transportation, etc. to work together to develop a new generation of evacuation modelling.

11204117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11204117.value: Fire safety is important to building design. In case of fire, we should provide fire protection systems to extinguish the fire and control the smoke movement, so that the indoor environment can be maintained at the tenable condition for occupants to leave the fire scenario safely. Therefore, knowing the details of the evacuation process is ultimately important to the design for fire protection system. Evacuation process can be simulated by computer program. Traditionally, the program did not consider psychological theories but just assume the human movement as mechanical system such as fluid flow or particles with virtual forces. This project studies psychological theories and implemented them into the computer program. The simulation results by our program is comparable to others but our model is able to depict the impatience levels of all occupants. So that the building manager can identify the locations of a building with high impatience level so that he can arrange additional safety measures or security guards to direct the movement of the occupants to reduce their impatience for avoiding accidence eg. stampedes and crushes.

11204217.label: Realisation of objectives
11204217.value: 1. To study airborne pathogen emission strength and surface contamination for seated and squat toilets. Parameters such as pathogen size, sequential multiple flushing and pathogen concentration, will be investigated. Two custom made toilet systems were built, one for a seated toilet and the other for the squat toilet. Five different bacteria were tested. They were seeded to the toilet bowl in known quantities. A tailor-made Perspex box was put on the top of the toilet bowl to facilitate sampling of bioaerosols. Parameters such as pathogen size, sequential multiple flushing and pathogen concentration were all investigated. The largest pathogen tested was Pseudomonas alcaligenes, at 2 micrometers wide while the smallest one was Staphylococcus epidermidis at 0.8 micrometers. Single, double and triple sequential flushing were tested. Airborne bacteria was collected by sampling air using an Anderson impactor. Airborne droplet concentration was also measured real-time by an optical particle sizer. Typically for a single flushing, 5 minutes was needed for completing a cycle (pre-flushing, flushing and post-flushing). A parameter “emission strength” is defined as emission of airborne particles divided to the total seeding in the toilet bowl. It is observed that emission strength (per flush) increases with decreasing pathogen size. Emission strength decreases with number of times of flushing. Typically the emission strength of S. epidermidis was 300 CFU per 10^9 for the first flush, decreasing to 38 CFU per 10^9 for the second flush. Seeding concentration has no statistically significant effect on the emission strength. This objective has been achieved satisfactorily as stated in the original proposal. 2. To study diversity of microbial communities at public restrooms with only seated and squat toilets. In this objective, airborne samples were collected and analyzed from different toilets, of which three were air-conditioned and four were non-air conditioned. Some of them were seated-only toilets while some of them were mixed. Airborne samplers were collected by an Anderson impactor for each of the toilets. The samples were divided into two equal parts for DNA and RNA extraction. Genomic DNA was extracted directly from the filter using a QIAamp DNA Mini Kit according to the manufacturer’s instructions, and total RNA was extracted using TRI Reagent. The 16S rRNA gene in sample DNA extracts was PCR-amplified and purified. Equimolar amounts of amplicons from each sample were sequenced using a MiSeq Illumina system. After sequence analysis of the 16S rRNA gene, it is observed that the microbial communities for those sampled surfaces were similar for both seated only and mixed-type toilets. This objective has been achieved satisfactorily as stated in the original proposal. 3. To use a culture-based approach supplemented by molecular methods to determine emission strength, microbial diversity and surface contamination. Culture-based approach for emission strength is reported in Objective 1. In this objective 3, the emission strength of the custom-made toilets and surface contamination were also measured by the molecular method. The following surface samples were taken from each toilets. (i) Toilet Seat (ii) Door handle/lock (iii) Flushing button (iv) Faucet tap/Soap tap (v) Toilet paper holder (vi) Side Wall The samples were divided into two equal parts for DNA and RNA extraction. Genomic DNA was extracted directly from the filter using a QIAamp DNA Mini Kit according to the manufacturer’s instructions, and total RNA was extracted using TRI Reagent. The 16S rRNA gene in sample DNA extracts was PCR-amplified and purified. Equimolar amounts of amplicons from each sample were sequenced using a MiSeq Illumina system. After sequence analysis of the 16S rRNA gene, it is observed that the microbial communities for those sampled surfaces were similar for both seated only and mixed-type toilets. This objective has been achieved satisfactorily as stated in the original proposal. 4. To study emission characteristics using fluorescent particles and stroboscopic light. Green monodisperse fluorescent particles were seeded to the toilet bowl. An impactor was used to collect the airborne particles, which were then dissolved into ethyl acetate. Fluorescence was measured by a fluorometer and the emission strength was determined. A strobe light was purchased to observe the droplet motion by adjusting the strobe frequency. Measurements were made for both types of toilets under different pressures and tank heights for seated toilets. This objective has been achieved satisfactorily as stated in the original proposal. 5. To utilize LED to design a miniature localized disinfection system. This study has evaluated the efficacy of ultraviolet waveband C (UV-C) for disinfection of flushing-generated pathogen-laden aerosols through tests with localized disinfection systems for airborne and surface contaminations. A new disinfection system utilizing an UVC-LED irradiation source was developed. The system was affixed to the toilet seat and challenged by three bacteria strains. Four surface samples on the toilet seat and three air samples at different heights were collected. Three types of bacteria were chosen for investigation: Staphylococcus epidermidis, Escherichia coli, and Salmonella typhimurium. High level of disinfection efficacy were observed, ranging from 76% to 97% for bacteria-laden aerosols at sources of emission, and efficiencies of 53% to 79% for surface samples in localized systems. The results from the localized systems were further compared with those obtained with an upper-room ultraviolet germicidal irradiation (UVGI) system. This research has shown that disinfection of flushing-generated pathogen-laden aerosols in proximity to the source of emission was more effective than at more distant sites where aerosols may be dispersed to the environment. A US patent is being filed for the localized disinfection system.

11204217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11204217.value: There is always concern of the hygienic conditions of public toilets. Faeces may have very high concentration of pathogens, and toilet flushing can potentially generate contaminated airborne droplets which contain pathogens. Though possibly impactful, studies of flushing generated airborne pathogens are scarce and all focused on seated toilet. Squat toilets are very popular in Mainland China but there was no study measuring the pathogen emission of these toilets. The results suggested that flushing a squat toilet can generate a large number of small droplets into the air. Besides, the flushing-induced emission strength of airborne pathogens varied from species to species. The emission strength of Staphylococcus epidermidis during squat toilet flushing was the highest among the three tested microorganisms. This work provides valuable data on the bioaerosol emission by flushing a squat toilet, which is crucial for control mitigation and evaluation of pathogen exposure risk. The findings of this work are very valuable, as it measures the emission of pathogens from squat toilets and the results can be compared to that of seated toilets. The results also led to a patent-pending localized UVC toilet disinfection device.

11204317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11204317.value: Diseases of the immune system such as human immunodeficiency (HIV), tuberculosis (TB), and malaria, can cause fatal health problems by disrupting the defensive mechanism of the immune system; and therefore immunoresponses of the patients should be well characterized for developing the proper treatment strategies in time. Considering that leukocytes play a key role in both innate and adaptive immune responses, examination of such immune cells extracted from a patient can provide important information about the systematic immune responses. However, promising prognosis and diagnosis on the immune responses are yet very challenging, mainly hindered by the multiplexed, heterogeneous and dynamic biochemical responses (e.g. cytokine secretion) of immune cells extracted from the patient’s blood. The challenge stems are not only from the limitations of conventional methods, but also caused by the intrinsic heterogeneity and complexity of the immune cell types in the community, considering that leukocytes are actually a collection of multiple cell types including CD14+ monocytes, CD4+ and CD8+ T-cells, and CD56+ natural killer (NK) cells. For this reason, quantitative and dynamic analyses of the cytokine secretion profiles of each the immune cell type are required for precise characterization of the ‘immunophenotype’ of patients. This proposal aims at developing a novel automated microfluidic ‘immunophenotyping’ platform for efficient and high-throughput isolation, stimulation, and quantitative characterization of individual immune cell types at defined locations in the device. The proposed platform will achieve on-chip immune cell capture/isolation based on the cell surface protein expressions, and massive parallel real-time monitoring of cell cytokine secretion based on enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay using the commercial available microbeads coated with phycoerythrin-conjugated detection antibodies. We expect to achieve computer-controlled operation procedures for the system in order to achieve continuous monitoring of the cytokine secretion profiles of different leukocyte cell types. Detecting transient profiles of the cytokine secretions will provide a signature that quantitatively characterizes patients’ immunophenotypes, which in turn lead to better prognosis and diagnosis and allow for personalized medications. Given the potential rapid, small-volume, multiplex assay capabilities applicable to even whole blood samples, we strongly believe our proposed microfluidic platform will induce an effective automated medical technology for immune system disease monitoring and diagnosis, contributing to drug search for the early-stage clinical treatment. 人體免疫缺陷病毒（HIV），結核病（TB），瘧疾等免疫系統疾病可能會破壞免疫系統的防禦機制，造成致命的健康問題。因此應充分考慮患者的免疫反應，以及時制定適當的治療策略。考慮到白細胞在先天性和適應性免疫應答中起關鍵作用，從患者提取的這種免疫細胞的檢查可以提供關於系統性免疫應答的重要信息。然而，有希望的免疫反應的預後和診斷仍然是非常具有挑戰性的，主要受到從患者血液中提取的免疫細胞的多重，異質和動態生化反應（例如細胞因子分泌）的阻礙。考慮到白細胞實際上是多種細胞類型的集合，包括CD14 +單核細胞，CD4 +和CD8 + T，這種挑戰不僅來源於常規方法的局限性，而且還由社區免疫細胞類型的固有異質性和復雜性引起。細胞和CD56 +自然殺傷（NK）細胞。為此，需要對每種免疫細胞類型的細胞因子分泌譜進行定量和動態分析，以精確表徵患者的“免疫表型”。 該建議旨在開發一種新穎的自動化微流控“免疫分型”平台，用於在設備中定義的位置處對各種免疫細胞類型進行高效和高通量的分離，刺激和定量表徵。提出的平台將基於細胞表面蛋白表達實現片上免疫細胞捕獲/分離，並且基於酶聯免疫吸附測定法，使用塗有藻紅蛋白綴合檢測的商業可得到的微珠大量平行實時監測細胞細胞因子分泌抗體。我們期望實現系統的計算機控制操作程序，以實現對不同白細胞類型細胞因子分泌情況的連續監測。檢測細胞因子分泌物的瞬態譜將提供定量表徵患者免疫表型的特徵，從而導致更好的預後和診斷並允許個性化藥物。鑑於潛在的快速，小體積的多重測定能力適用於甚至全血樣本，我們強烈建議我們提出的微流控平台將為免疫系統疾病監測和診斷引入有效的自動化醫療技術，有助於早期藥物搜索臨床治療。

11204317.label: Realisation of objectives
11204317.value: Cell isolation from blood is an important process for diagnosing immune diseases. There are still demands for a user-friendly approach to achieve high cell extraction efficiency and purity of a target immune cell subtype for more promising diagnosis and monitoring. For selective immune cell isolation, we developed a microstructured device, which consists of antibody-coated micropillars and micro-sieve arrays, for isolating a target immune cell subtype from bovine blood samples. The focusing micropillars can guide immune cells flowing to the subsequent micro-sieves based on deterministic lateral shifts of the cells. The arrangement of these microstructures is characterized and configured for the maximal cell capture rate. Surface modification with a selected antibody offers selective cell capture in the micro-sieves based on the antigen–antibody reaction. In this research, we adopted a cell mixture of human CD14-expressing leukemia cells (THP-1) and epithelial cells (MDA-MB-231) in diluted blood to characterize the cell isolation operation, with a selective cell isolation yield of >80%, cell purity of ∼100% and cell viability of >93%. In essence, this microstructured device strategy can achieve high-yield selective isolation of immune cells from blood samples and support downstream genetic and biochemical cell analyses, contributing to the medical diagnosis of a broad range of immune diseases. On the other hand, quantitative and dynamic analyses of immune cell secretory cytokines are essential for precise determination and characterization of the “immune phenotype” of patients for clinical diagnosis and treatment of immune-related diseases. Although multiple methods including the enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) have been applied for cytokine detection, such measurements remain very challenging in real-time, high-throughput, and high-sensitivity immune cell analysis. In this research, we successfully devised a highly integrated microfluidic device that allows for on-chip isolation, culture, and stimulation, as well as sensitive and dynamic cytokine profiling of immune cells. Such a microfluidic sensing chip is integrated with cytometric fluorescent microbeads for real-time and multiplexed monitoring of immune cell cytokine secretion dynamics, consuming a relatively small extracted sample volume (160 nl) without interrupting the immune cell culture. Furthermore, it is integrated with a Taylor dispersion-based mixing unit in each detection chamber that shortens the immunoassay period down to less than 30 minutes. We demonstrate the profiling of multiple pro-inflammatory cytokine secretions (e.g. interleukin-6, interleukin-8, and tumor necrosis factors) of human peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) with a sensitivity of 20 pg/ml and a sample volume of 160 nl per detection. Further applications of this automated, rapid, and high-throughput microfluidic immunophenotyping platform can help unleash the mechanisms of systemic immune responses, and enable efficient assessments of the pathologic immune status for clinical diagnosis and immune therapy.

11204317.label: Major findings and research outcome
11204317.value: We developed a micro-structured device for high-yield specific isolation of immune cells from multiple-cell-type biosamples in either culture media or diluted blood. In brief, we applied rows of micropillars for cell focusing and a micro-sieve array for the subsequent cell isolation. The arrangements of these microstructures have been optimized by both simulation analysis and experiments, achieving a focusing rate of >95% and cell capture yield of ∼85% for immune cells in culture media. Isolation of a target immune cell subtype can be achieved by the specific cell surface protein binding on the antibody-coated microstructure surfaces. This work demonstrated that the target PMA-treated THP-1 cells can be isolated from a multiple cell-type mixture in diluted blood with a yield rate of >80% while the cell viability (>93%) can be maintained. Such a reduction of the isolation yield for the blood sample is possibly caused by the presence of a high density of red blood cells. The detailed cell isolation procedures can be further configured to enable the extraction of multiple defined immune cell sub types using devices with different antibody coatings and multiple backward pressure levels. The focusing micro-pillars and micro-sieve array can also be expanded as a larger flow region with the repeated microstructures for processing a high-throughput of cell isolation, meeting the requirements of specific immune cell isolation from clinical samples for a wide range of healthcare/medical applications. In addition, we developed an integrated microfluidic bio-sensing platform that can synthesize all the necessary processes for functional cellular immunophenotyping by coupling microfluidic technology with optical biosensing imaging. These include on-chip cell processing, microfluidic multiplexing, active mixing of components and a computer-based control interface for automatic, rapid, and sensitive fluorescent microbead-based cytokine detection from human PBMCs. The new platform will permit high-dimensional immune phenotype profiling (up to 16 tests from one sample) with a much shorter assay time (15–30 min), a smaller amount of sample volume (∼0.16 μl for each cytokine test), and a higher sensitivity (20 pg/ml), which provides a unique advantage over the traditional ELISA-related techniques. The resulting detection system enables both spatial and temporal mapping of cell-secreted cytokine profiles of immune cells at high throughput and sensitivity. Combining both the spatial and temporal secretion patterns detected with the new microfluidics-based optical biosensing platform would provide a significant signature that quantitatively characterizes the immunophenotypes of patients and would therefore allow for more precise diagnosis and stratification of immune-related diseases.

11204317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11204317.value: Future development of the reported immune cell isolation strategy should include the detailed protocols based on the devices with different antibody coatings and regulation of the backward pressure levels. Further development of the microfluidic cytokine measurement technique should include elimination of the microscope in order to induce a standalone system. One potential approach is to adopt a highly sensitive photo-detector for acquiring the average fluorescence level at the detection microchamber. We have studied its feasibility by performing a pilot test for the calibration curve of IL-6-sensitive microbeads based on the average intensity over the microchamber (density: 5 × 10^3 beads per μl), instead of the individual beads. With the rapid, low-volume, high-sensitivity, and multiplex assay capability and clinical compatibility, the technique holds great promise to advance a medical technology for immune disease control, monitoring, and prevention.

11204317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11204317.value: This research developed a novel autoamated microfluidic ‘immunophenotyping’ platform for efficient and high-throughput isolation, stimulation, and quantitative characterization of individual immune cell types at defined locations in the device. The platform can achieve on-chip immune cell capture/isolation based on the cell surface protein expressions, and massive parallel real-time monitoring of cell cytokine secretion based on enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay using the commercial available microbeads coated with phycoerythrin-conjugated detection antibodies. We further established computer-controlled operation procedures for the system in order to achieve continuous monitoring of the cytokine secretion profiles of different leukocyte cell types. Detecting transient profiles of the cytokine secretions can provide a signature that quantitatively characterizes patients’ immunophenotypes, which in turn lead to better prognosis and diagnosis and allow for personalized medications. Given the potential rapid, small-volume, multiplex assay capabilities applicable to even whole blood samples, this microfluidic platform technology offers an effective automated medical technology for immune system disease monitoring and diagnosis, contributing to drug search for the early-stage clinical treatment.

11204717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11204717.value: The ability to propagate and manipulate of light on the micrometer scale is important for applications such as high-contrast displays, microlasers, and integrated photonics devices. Given the difficulties to efficiently couple light into matters in the micrometer scale, microstructured materials comprising luminescent components have emerged as a promising means of producing well-regulated optical emissions following localized absorption of the incident light. Over the past ten years, various luminescent microrods and microdisks, based on semiconductors, polymers, and assemblies of organic molecules, have been constructed for simultaneous use as gain media, resonance cavities, and waveguides. Lanthanide-doped insulating crystals represent another class of luminescent materials featuring sharp emission bands, long luminescence lifetimes, and large effective Stokes shifts, characteristics that are particularly suitable for applications in optics and photonics. Despite the attractions, the lanthanide luminescence has barely been exploited in single microcrystals. In this regard, we propose to systematically investigate the synthesis and luminescence of lanthanide-doped microcrystals with controllable size and morphology (i.e., microrods, microtubes, and microdisks) as well as tunable absorption and emission wavelengths. Specifically, we aim to manipulate light-matter interactions by taking advantage of morphological effect of the crystals and to achieve active waveguiding at tunable wavelengths by single wavelength excitation. Possible lasing actions in the microstructures will also be explored. Once refined, we envisage that our study will significantly expand the scope of applications for lanthanide-based luminescent materials and open up new opportunities in diverse fields such as biology and optical communication. 在微米尺度上控制发光及其传播因在高对比度显示、微型激光器以及集成光子器件等方向的诱人前景而发展为光学技术领域的一个重要研究课题。目前用于该研究方向的的材料主要集中在有机高分子和半导体材料，这些材料通常具有较宽的吸收峰和较小的斯托克斯位移，因而在实际中容易产生高的光传输损耗。为了克服这一问题，本项目拟开发一类新的、基于稀土掺杂的微米结构发光材料。稀土发光材料的特点是谱带尖锐、斯托克斯位移较大，有望提供非常优异的光波导和激光性能。本项目计划系统开展稀土掺杂单晶微米结构材料的可控制备及光谱性质调控，以获得单一波长激发下发光颜色和传播方向可控的光学性质，同时我们也将尝试在这类微米结构材料中获取波长可控的激光发射。该研究有望对生物和光学通讯等领域的研究产生积极的推动作用。

11204717.label: Realisation of objectives
11204717.value: This project aims to develop novel microstructured materials comprising luminescent lanthanide ions to realize unprecedented optical properties, thereby expanding the range of applications for these materials in lighting, lasing, biomedical therapy. We have achieved these objectives through the following deliverables. 1. Two complementary strategies have been established to prepare lanthanide-doped microstructures. The first strategy is based on the synthesis of nanostructured lanthanide fluoride crystals followed by composting with a polymeric matrix. Specifically, we have developed several core-shell nanostructures such as NaErF4@NaYF4 and Lu6O5F8@Lu6O5F8 nanocrystals, which permit doping of multiple lanthanide ions to render highly tunable excitation and emission features. These nanocrystals have been successfully incorporated in silica microrings and glass microtubes with well-defined spatial distributions. The second strategy is based on the direct doping of lanthanide ions in microcrystals of different compositions and structures. By developing innovative hydrothermal synthesis and lithium-assisted calcination, we have successfully prepared several classes of lanthanide-doped microcrystals, including metal-organic framework, negative thermal expansion Y2W3O12/Sc2Mo3O12, and semiconducting CaZnOS crystals. 2. We demonstrate that microstructured luminescent materials can be thoroughly characterized using standard TEM, SEM, XRD, and home-build fiber optics instruments. Particularly, we have established a theoretical model to analyze internal strains in the host materials based on the twist of lattice fringes in HRTEM images and the distortion of peak profiles in XRD patterns. By coupling a mechanical control unit, a hot/cold stage, and a fiber optics spectrometer, we can systematically characterize the optical properties of the materials as a function of mechanical and thermal stimuli. These investigations have enabled us to reveal the underlying mechanism dominating the crystal growth habit and explore novel luminescence phenomena. 3. By proper selection of dopant ions and host materials, we have achieved tunable light emission spanning ultraviolet (UV) and near-infrared (NIR) by multiwavelength excitation. For example, by doping Pr3+/Gd3+ in Lu6O5F8@Lu6O5F8 nanocrystals, we have achieved deep UV emission by blue excitation. Alternatively, deep UV emission has been achieved by NIR excitation in NaErF4@NaYF4 nanocrystals. Notably, we also achieved multicolor emission by excitation of mechanical stress and magnetic force in CaZnOS doped with various lanthanide ions. As light from these materials is totally emitted by the lanthanide dopant ions, we have correspondingly achieved spatial control of the light emission by doping lanthanide ions in different regions of the host lattice and/or by assembling lanthanide-doped nanocrystals in different regions of a microstructure. The spatially controlled light emission is promising for the construction of anti-counterfeiting measures and combinatorial modulation of neuron networks. 4. Based on the sophisticated nano-synthesis and micro-fabrication, we have achieved efficient emission in various lanthanide ions that are confined in a small space. Accordingly, we have realized multiwavelength lasing by excitation in blue and NIR. For example, we have incorporated Lu6O5F8:Pr/Gd@Lu6O5F8 nanocrystals into a bottle-like silica resin microcavity, which renders tunable lasing characteristics at ~310 nm as a function of the cavity size. Besides, a NaErF4@NaYF4-based microdisk has been formed at the top of a SinO2 micropillar cavity, which shows lasing action at ~380 nm by excitation in the telecommunication wavelength range (~1550 nm). 5. By assembling the lanthanide-doped nano/microcrystals into glass/polymer microtubes, we have constructed several types of implantable microdevices for biomedical imaging and therapy. For example, an upconversion device is fabricated via a heat-pulling process using biocompatible thermoplastic polypropylene as a backbone, which is mixed with upconversion nanocrystals to form a ﬂexible optrode device that converts near-infrared irradiation into visible light for optogenetic manipulation of spinal cord tissues. We also have succeeded in co-encapsulating lanthanide-doped CaZnOS microcrystals and a magnetic microbar in a capillary tube, which can be implanted in the brain region of a mouse for remote regulation of optogenetic proteins by excitation of an external magnetic field.

11204717.label: Major findings and research outcome
11204717.value: We have established several synthetic protocols for synthesis and various nanocrystals, microcrystals, and composite microstructures. These advances have enabled us to prepare novel compositions and structures that are previously inaccessible, such as NaYbF4@NaGdF4 nanocrystals with unconventional morphologies and semiconductor crystals doped with high concentrations of lanthanide ions. Besides, our studies reveal that wet-chemistry synthesis and microfabrication such as photolithograph can be combined to produce advanced microstructures for extended control over luminescence properties of lanthanide ions. Based on the newly developed materials compositions and structures, we have discovered a series of novel optical phenomena, such as full-spectrum emission by excitation of X-ray, ultraviolet, and near-infrared photons as well as mechanical action, respectively. We also find that the long-standing problem of thermal quenching of luminescence can be resolved by using host materials featuring negative thermal expansion characteristics, such as Y2W3O12, Sc2Mo3O12, and ScF3. Notably, the ability to manipulate light emission in a thermal field has led to the development of highly sensitive luminescence thermometers that operates over a broad temperature range. The microstructural engineering of host materials not only brings about novel optical properties but also facilitates their applications in practical settings. We find that the morphology of core-shell nanocrystals can significantly affect their cellular internalization efficiency, thereby dictating their utility in biological imaging and therapy. By controlling the assembly of different nano/microcrystals, we have also pioneered the applications of lanthanide elements to anti-counterfeiting and neuromodulation that requires no optical sources for their operation. Due to our innovative and systematical works in this field, we have been invited to contribute several review papers by the American Chemical Society (Acc. Chem. Res. 2020, 53, 358), American Institute of Physics (J. Phys. D: Appl. Phys. 2020, 53, 053002), Royal Chemical Society (Nanoscale, 2021, 13, 3454; Inorg. Chem. Front., 2020, 7, 1067; J. Mater. Chem. B, 2018, 6, 2924) and the Asian Chemical Editorial Society (Chem. Asian J. 2020, 15, 21).

11204717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11204717.value: Our study highlights that controlled doping in microstructures is viable to expand the tunability of lanthanide luminescence for advanced applications, which will continue to be an effective strategy for designing new materials and devices, especially in the field of short-wavelength lasing. Particularly, our investigation of luminescence in negative thermal expansion host materials may inspire the development of novel optical materials that excel at high temperatures.

11204717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11204717.value: Lanthanide-doped luminescent materials can produce light emission across the full spectrum owing to electronic transitions between the ionic levels within individual lanthanide dopant ions. As such, the design of lanthanide-based luminescent materials is not constrained by the host composition, size, morphology, and even crystallinity. In our study, we have successfully synthesized a series of lanthanide-doped microcrystals and composite microstructures composed of lanthanide-doped nanocrystals, based upon which we have demonstrated several novel luminescence phenomena, such as spatially resolved multicolor emission and anti-thermal quenching luminescence. Accordingly, we have demonstrated several biological and photonics applications, such as short-wavelength lasing, anti-counterfeiting, and optogenetics. Our findings not only provide a technological basis for current applications but also highlight new directions for further development. For example, the discovery of negative thermal expansion induced emission enhancement may imply an innovative strategy for combating thermal quenching of photoluminescence.

11204917.label: Project Objectives
11204917.value: Developing a framework of inferring delay bounds for a set of given paths. Given a set of interested paths and a set of paths with delay measurements, we aim to derive the tightest delay bound for each interested path. The problem differs from the conventional problems from two perspectives. First, our interest is the bounds of delay rather than an absolute value of delay, and second, we directly target each interested path without the need of inferring the delay of each link. These two perspectives make more paths identifiable, and also make our problems harder to solve. Developing a framework of inferring available bandwidth bounds for a set of given paths. Given a set of interested paths and available bandwidth on a set of measured paths, we aim to derive the tightest available bandwidth bound for each interested path. In the literature there is not much work on Inferring bandwidth of a path that cannot be directly measured. The problem is more challenging because bandwidth is non-additive along a path. Enabling network calculus for network tomography. To expand the scope of network calculus, we will study a new concept known as service curve decomposition. The purpose of this new concept is to estimate the performance of some subsystems of a measured path, i.e., some special case of network tomography. Based on that, we can further enhance the performance of network tomography. Note that object 3 supports objectives 1 and 2 by providing valid inputs. Studying extended measuring strategies. For each of the above three objectives, we derive the performance bounds of the interested paths under the assumption that the set of measurable paths is given. We will make two possible extensions to make the inference more effective. The first is to study optimal monitor placement problem in order to get the tightest performance bounds on interested paths, and the second is to study how to progressively measure more paths based on the inference results in order to achieve the bound tightness constraints from the ISP.

11204917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11204917.value: Network tomography has been an important research direction in the past decade. Roughly speaking, network tomography is to infer certain network performance that is difficult or too costly, to be measured directly. The inference is derived based on a limited number of measurements that are partially or indirectly related to the target to be inferred. In the past, people have studied network tomography for different purposes, such as inferring network topology and delay of links. In this project, we study a class of new network tomography problems, referred to as bound-oriented network tomography. The problems are particularly relevant to ISPs who need to continuously invigilate the status of network resources important to their operations, for example, when the ISPs are providing verifiable services to their clients. Effective and efficient network tomography is a basic problem faced by them. Concerning the need from ISPs, our problems have two important features that have been overlooked in the past. First, we focus on inferring performance bounds rather than the absolute values. The bound-oriented inference is consistent with the fact that the SLA terms between ISPs and their clients are commonly written in terms of performance bounds. Second, for each path to be inferred, we directly infer the performance bounds of the path without always explicitly obtaining the performance of each link on the path. Knowing path performance is enough to ISPs because their service levels to clients depend on paths directly. These two features lead to new models that are less restrictive and enable low-cost solutions. Regarding the plan and methodologies, we propose three concrete tasks, inferring delay bounds, inferring bandwidth bounds, and inference by network calculus. Among the three, the first two are independent, both needing some measured bounds as input. The third task will provide valid input to the first two tasks; at the same time, the third task will also infer more information by a new concept termed as service curve decomposition. Successfully doing service curve decomposition will expand the applicable area of network calculus, making it a powerful tool for network tomography. In summary, we propose a framework for bound-oriented network tomography, which can be used for ISPs to fast gain network knowledge at low cost. 在过去的十几年里， 网络诊断(Network Tomography)已经成为一个低代价获取网络性能的重要研究方向。 网络诊断通过一些有限的测量可以推算其他一些没有直接测量的路径上的网络性能。 过去的研究主要集中在获取网络拓扑，每条链路的延迟等。本项目中， 我们将研究一类新的，旨在推算网络性能范围的网络诊断问题。 这些问题是网络运营商所关注的。 相对于已有的工作， 我们的工作将考虑两个新的因素。首先，网路运营商基于与用户的服务协议， 只关心网络性能是否在一个范围， 而不是网络性能的具体值。其次，网络运营商只关心一些关键路径的网络性能，不需要知道这些路径上每一条链路的性能。 这两个因素使得在本项目中要研究的问题成为新的问题并使得寻求更低代价的网络诊断成为可能。 在旨在推算性能范围的框架下，我们将研究三个基本问题，推算延迟范围，推算带宽范围，以及基于网络演算(Network Calculus)的推算。 前两个问题是相互独立的，这两个问题的输入可以是通过测量获取的一些延迟或带宽信息，也可以是通过第三个问题所得出的性能范围。我们拟通过对服务曲线的分解将网络演算与网络诊断结合起来。 本项目旨在提出基于网络性能范围的网络诊断的框架，使得网络运营商能够以低代价获取网络性能状态。

11204917.label: Realisation of objectives
11204917.value: This project made three contributions: 1) Different from conventional Boolean-Based network tomography, we are the first to propose and study bound-based network tomography, which derives the lower and upper bound for unidentifiable links. The performance metrics we considered include additive performance metrics such as delay, and non-additive performance metrics such as bandwidth. We developed solutions to derive bounds for both additive performance metrics and non-additive performance metrics. This contribution is made by realizing objective 1 and objective 2. 2) We developed solutions to construct measurement paths so that the tightest bounds of network tomography can be achieved. This contribution is made by realizing objective 3. 3) We further developed solutions to strategically and optimally place monitors so that the tightest bounds can be achieved. This contribution is made by realizing objective 4. Three students including two Ph.D. students and one postdoc student have been trained through this project. Six research outputs are generated from this project, including two journal papers in the best journal of the networking field, and 4 conference papers where three of them are in the flagship conference of the networking field. In the outputs of Part C 9-2 and 8-2, we extended Boolean-based network tomography to bound-based network tomography where the lower and upper bounds are derived for unidentifiable links. We developed an efficient algorithm to obtain the tightest total error bound (objective 1), and present a solution that can significantly reduce the total number of measurement paths required for deriving the tightest total error bound (objective 3). Furthermore, we proposed a method to deploy a new monitor over existing ones such that the total error bound could be maximally reduced (objective 4). Compared to the random monitor deployment and the monitor deployment that maximizes the total number of identifiable links, our monitor deployment method can lead to up to 15 and 2.4 times more reduction on total error bound, respectively. In the outputs of Part C 9-3 and 8-1, we studied bound-based bandwidth tomography. Bandwidth tomography is a long-standing open problem in the network tomography literature. The difficulty is due to the fact that no existing mathematical tool is directly applicable to solve the inverse problem with a set of min-equations. We systematically tackle this challenge by designing a polynomial-time algorithm that returns the exact bandwidth value for all identifiable links and the tightest error bound for unidentifiable links for a given set of measurement paths (objective 2). When measurement paths are not given in advance, we prove the hardness of building measurement paths that can be used for deriving the global tightest error bounds for unidentifiable links. Accordingly, we develop a reinforcement learning (RL) approach for measurement path construction, that utilizes the special knowledge in bandwidth tomography and integrates both offline training and online prediction (objective 3). Evaluation results with real-world ISP as well as simulated networks demonstrate that compared to other path construction methods, Random and Diversity Preferred, our RL-based path construction method can build measurement paths that result in a much smaller average error bound of link bandwidth. In the output of Part C 9-1, given a set of interested paths, we developed sufficient and necessary conditions for the identifiability of a given set of interested paths, and design an efficient algorithm that deploys the minimum number of monitors (objective 4). Experiments show a saving of up to 40% fewer monitors that guarantee the identifiability of a given set of paths. In the output of Part C 9-4, we developed a method that theoretically guarantees (1) the minimum number of monitors required to bring down the maximum error bound (MEB) over all unidentifiable links, and (2) the best places where these new monitors should be deployed. Using this method repeatedly, we can push down the MEB gradually until the desired level is reached (objective 4). In addition, we develop a new sequential measurement technique that reduces the number of measurement paths and in the meantime guarantees the tightest link error bound (objective 3). With extensive simulation over real-world network topology, we demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of our solution in reducing the maximum link error bound with network performance tomography.

For each of the above three objectives, we derive the performance bounds of the interested paths under the assumption that the set of measurable paths is given. We will make two possible extensions to make the inference more effective. The first is to study optimal monitor placement problem in order to get the tightest performance bounds on interested paths, and the second is to study how to progressively measure more paths based on the inference results in order to achieve the bound tightness constraints from the ISP.

11204917.label: Major findings and research outcome
11204917.value: This project systematically studied bound-based network tomography from the perspectives of both additive performance metrics and non-additive performance metrics. The research findings provide solutions to answer the following questions: 1) Given a set of measurement paths, which set of links’ performances in terms of delay and bandwidth can be identified? For unidentifiable links, what are the tightest performance bounds? 2) How to construct measurement paths so that the tightest bound on unidentifiable links can be achieved? 3) What is the minimum number of monitors to achieve the desirable performance bounds? 4) Where to place new monitors so that the required performance bounds can be achieved? The project has generated 6 outputs published in prestigious journals and conferences.

11204917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11204917.value: Monitor placement and subsequent measurement path construction are the two major challenges in network literature (for identifying identifiable links and giving tightest bounds for unidentifiable bounds). For additive metrics, the relation between MP and identifiability of link performance metric is determined by the unknown ground truth, it results in the number of candidate measurement paths growing exponentially with the network size, even we have followed the ideal topological feature for “good” measurement paths derived by theoretical analysis. Thus, employing learning-based methods to construct limited “good” measurement paths could be a promising direction for other network tomography contexts, when the relation between measurement path selection and identifiability partially or fully depends on certain randomness.

11204917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11204917.value: Network tomography has been an important research direction in the past decade. Roughly speaking, network tomography is to infer certain network performance that is difficult or costly, to be measured directly. The inference is derived based on a limited number of measurements that are partially or indirectly related to the target to be inferred. In this project, we have studied a class of new network tomography problems, referred to as bound-oriented network tomography. Focusing on inferring performance bounds is consistent with the fact that the Service Level Agreement (SLA) terms between ISPs and their clients are commonly written in terms of performance bounds. Under the umbrella of bound-oriented network tomography, we have provided solid theoretical analysis and efficient solutions for ISPs to: 1) derive the performance bounds of unmeasured paths given a set of measured paths; 2) identify a set of appropriate measurement paths so that tightest bounds can be inferred; 3) determine the minimum number of monitors so that the desired performance bounds can be achieved; 4) progressively place new monitors so that the requirements of performance bounds can be met. The project provides useful tools for ISPs to achieve monitorability of SLA at low cost.
