11205617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11205617.value: The success of artificial orthopedic implants mainly depends on osseointegration and bacterial resistance in vivo. Insufficient integration between the implants and local tissues results in loosening and detachment of prostheses and post-surgery bacterial infection can be very serious affecting the long-term success of biomedical implants. After undesirable bacteria adhesion / proliferation and subsequent biofilm formation, it is difficult to treat and a second surgery to remove the implant may be necessary. Hence, it is imperative that orthopedic implants have both antimicrobial properties and osteoconductivity. To mimic the natural bone matrix with hierarchical nanostructures, a surface with nanotopographical cues is an effective strategy to enhance the biocompatibility as well as osseointegration. However, conventional methods used to fabricate or modify the nanostructured surfaces of biomedical implants including etching, grit blasting, and anodization may spur microbial colonization resulting in a high chance of post-operation infection. Loading or embedding antimicrobial agents in the near-surface of biomaterials may suppress infection but raise the risk of resistance to common antibiotics and possibly produce deleterious effects on cell functions and osteogenic activity. Some natural biological structures such as cicada/dragonfly wings have been shown to have inherent antimicrobial characteristics due to the special nanopillar arrays on the surface. When bacteria land on the wing, the bacterial membrane is stretched and ruptured by the surface nanostructures causing their death. The favorable bactericidal properties are attributed to physico-mechanical effects rendered by the surface nanotopography in lieu of chemical ones. Since the use of extraneous chemicals is avoided, this purely bio-mechanical strategy has less side-effects and is generally much safer than chemical approaches. By taking advantage of the physicochemical differences such as size and mechanical rigidity/fluidity between prokaryotic bacteria and eukaryotic mammalian cells and their different response to nanostructured surfaces, this project will focus on the design and preparation of special surface nanostructures on Ti and its alloy as well as polymer-based biomaterials. The response of bone cells and bacteria to different nanopillar structures with different widths, heights, spacing, shape, surface energy, rigidity, as well as wettability and their inter-dependence will be evaluated in details. The purpose of this project is to fabricate mechanically-modified and clinically-viable biomaterials to preferentially enhance the biological functions of bone cells while simultaneously inhibiting microbial colonization without relying on foreign chemicals and antibiotics. The work is expected to have important scientific and technological significance as well as large clinical potential.

11205617.label: Realisation of objectives
11205617.value: We have conducted research on surface modification of functional biomaterials and following are highlights of some of our important results. Metal ions or nanoparticles are believed to be promising additives in developing antibacterial biomaterials, owing to possessing favorable bactericidal effects against antibiotic-resistant bacteria. A porous microstructure designed to trap methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) is fabricated on polyetheretherketone biomaterial surface through sulfonation (SPEEK), following which copper (Cu) nanoparticles, which can kill the trapped MRSA, are immobilized on SPEEK surface using a customized magnetron sputtering technique. In vitro antibacterial and immunological experiments indicate that the Cu-incorporated SPEEK can exert a desirable bactericidal effect against MRSA through the combination of “trap killing” and “contact killing” actions; meanwhile, macrophages cultured on the Cu-incorporated SPEEK can be activated and polarized to a pro-inflammatory phenotype along with improved phagocytic ability on the MRSA. Further in vivo implant-associated infection models evidence the superior antibacterial activity of the Cu-incorporated SPEEK. These results demonstrate multimodal antibacterial actions of the Cu-incorporated SPEEK, which is capable of imposing direct antibacterial and indirect immunomodulatory antibacterial effects simultaneously, in order to prevent and cure MRSA infection. Many postsurgical complications stem from bacteria colony formation on the surface of implants, but the usage of antibiotic agents may cause antimicrobial resistance. Therefore, there is a strong demand for biocompatible materials with an intrinsic antibacterial resistance not requiring extraneous chemical agents. In this study, homogeneous nanocones were fabricated by oxygen plasma etching on the surface of natural, biocompatible Bombyx mori silk films. The new hydroxyl bonds formed on the surface of the nanopatterned film by plasma etching increased the surface energy by around 176%. This hydrophilic nanostructure reduced the bacterial attachment by more than 90% for both Gram-negative (Escherichia coli) and Gram-positive (Staphylococcus aureus) bacteria and at the same time improved the proliferation of osteoblast cells by 30%. The nanoengineered substrate and pristine silk were cultured for 6 h with three different bacteria concentrations of 107, 105, and 103 CFU mL−1 and the cell proliferation on the nanopatterned samples was significantly higher due to limited bacteria attachment and prevention of biofilm formation. The concept and materials described here reveal a promising alternative to produce biomaterials with an inherent biocompatibility and bacterial resistance simultaneously to mitigate postsurgical infections and minimize the use of antibiotics. Prevention of bacterial infection and promotion of osseointegration are two important issues for titanium (Ti) implants in medical research. In addition, after a biofilm is formed on the surface of implants, the immune system and antibiotic therapy may fail. In this work, bio-functionalized titanium dioxide (TiO2)/molybdenum disulfide (MoS2)/polydopamine (PDA)/arginine-glycine-aspartic acid (RGD) nanorod arrays (NAs) are prepared on Ti implants to not only kill bacteria noninvasively upon co-irradiation of 660 nm visible light (VL) and 808 nm near infrared (NIR) light, but also promote the osteogenic activity simultaneously. Dual light irradiation triggers the TiO2/MoS2 NA to generate hyperthermia and reactive oxygen species (ROS) in 10 min. The synergistic effects of the generated hyperthermia and ROS increase the bacterial membrane permeability and bacteria are killed rapidly and efficiently in vitro and in vivo. The biofilm is also eradicated and RGD on the nanorods improves cell adhesion, proliferation, and osteogenic differentiation. The strategy described here for the design of bio-functionalized coatings on Ti implants has great clinical potential in orthopedics, dentistry, and other medical field. The adverse macrophage-mediated immune response elicited by the surface of polyetheretherketone (PEEK) is responsible for the formation of fibrous encapsulation and resulting inferior osseointegration of PEEK implants in the dental and orthopedic fields. A reliable and cost-effective method to construct adherent films with tunable nanoporous structures on PEEK is described. The functionalized surface not only suppresses the acute inflammatory response of macrophages, but also provides a favorable milieu for osteogenic differentiation of human bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (hBMSCs). Whole genome expression analysis reveals that the suppression effect arises from synergistic inhibition of focal adhesion. The nanoporous films fabricated on PEEK harmonize the early macrophage-mediated inflammatory response and subsequent hBMSCs-centered osteogenic functions consequently yielding superior osseointegration. Inspired by the natural antibacterial structure on insect wings, cone/pillar-like micro/nano-arrays are fabricated controllably on PEEK by colloidal lithography and plasma etching and the resulting bacterial resistance and biocompatibility are investigated. The surface-engineered PEEK possesses enhanced antibacterial properties and the underlying mechanism depends on the surface topography and dimensions of the surface structures. With regard to the microarrays, both the early mechanical stretching effect and subsequent dimensional effect contribute to the overall antibacterial effects. On the other hand, the nanoarrays that mimic cicada wings kill bacteria solely by the penetration effect. Enhanced proliferation of osteoblasts is also observed from the modified PEEK rendering it suitable for implant materials. Because of unique properties such as the lightweight, natural biodegradability, and biocompatibility, magnesium alloys are promising in biomedical implants. However, inadequate corrosion resistance in the physiological environment remains a technical hurdle and application of coatings is a viable means to overcome the deficiency. Also, the antibacterial properties are very important in order to mitigate post-implantation complications arising from bacterial infection. In this study, a biocompatible silk film is deposited on AZ31 Mg alloy to enhance the corrosion resistance and by means of oxygen plasma etching, nature-inspired nanopatterns are fabricated on the surface of the silk film to improve the inherent antibacterial properties. The antimicrobial properties of the silk coated AZ31 are better than those of the bare alloy probably due to the combined effects of the nanopatterns and alkalinity associated with leaching of Mg ions. The β-sheets formed on the silk film is found to result in 104 times reduction in the corrosion current density and 50% reduction in Mg leaching after 1 day. Although degradation of the β-sheets is observed to begin after 1 day, the amount of Mg ions leached to the medium from silk-coated AZ31 is still 17% lower than that from the bare one. The biomimicking nanopatterns on the natural silk film improve the corrosion resistance, biocompatibility, and antibacterial properties simultaneously and have large clinical potential. In bone implants, antibacterial biomaterials with nonleaching surfaces are superior to ones based on abrupt release because systemic side effects arising from the latter can be avoided. In this work, a nonleaching antibacterial concept is demonstrated by fabricating 2D nanoflakes in situ on magnesium (Mg). Different from the conventional antibacterial mechanisms that depend on Mg2+ release and pH increase, the nanoflakes exert mechanical tension onto the bacteria membranes to destroy microorganisms on contact and produce intracellular stress via physical interactions, which is also revealed by computational simulations. Moreover, the nanoflake layer decelerates the corrosion process resulting in mitigated Mg2+ release, weaker alkalinity in the vicinity, and less hydrogen evolution, in turn inducing less inflammatory reactions and ensuring the biocompatibility as confirmed by the in vivo study. In this way, bacteria are killed by a mechanical process causing very little side effects. This work provides information and insights pertaining to the design of multifunctional biomaterials.

11205917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11205917.value: Stroke is a leading cause of death and disability worldwide. As new medical and dietary interventions are being developed, there is a parallel requirement to develop measurement tools for serial monitoring of carotid atherosclerosis and stroke risk stratification. The ultimate goal of this project is to develop such measurement tools. Our group has pioneered the development of 3D carotid ultrasound as a reproducible and sensitive tool for plaque and vessel wall volume measurements. Recognizing the focal nature of carotid atherosclerosis, the PI pioneered the quantification of point-wise vessel-wall-plus-plaque thickness (VWT) and plaque surface irregularity as features to characterize plaque-and-vessel-wall evolution. Although these global/local phenotypes are useful individually, the combination of these phenotypes will lead to higher prediction accuracy for clinical outcomes, and higher sensitivity for cost-effective evaluation of dietary/lifestyle changes that are expected to confer smaller effect than medical interventions, such as pomegranate juice being evaluated in this project. The specific goal of this project is to develop a framework to integrate all available phenotypes for risk stratification and therapy evaluation. Although our previously proposed VWT-Change was able to characterize local changes, VWT-Change was unable to isolate changes in individual plaque components, but the change of individual vulnerable components is most important for patient management and assessment. In this project, we propose to quantify longitudinal voxel-based plaque-and-vessel-wall volume change (ΔVVol) to address this issue. We introduce a 3D registration framework necessary for quantifying ΔVVol, and a novel method to map ΔVVol to a 3D carotid atlas for population-based analyses. As the combination of all phenotypes will result in a high-dimensional feature vector for each patient, conventional discriminant analyses and classifiers may not work. We will develop dimensional reduction strategies suitable for serial monitoring of carotid atherosclerosis, discriminant models for treatment assessment and a novel graph-based classifier for risk stratification. We hypothesize that the proposed framework would reduce the sample size requirement in the pomegranate study by an order of magnitude and achieve a 90% prediction accuracy of vascular events in another clinical study involving 323 patients. The Co-I achieved an order of magnitude reduction in sample size required to demonstrate the effect of statin by changing from measuring 2D plaque area to 3D plaque volume using ultrasound, and the PI achieved an addition 3-time reduction using local VWT-Change measurement. This project capitalizes on our previous successes and is expected to provide the next leap in patient management and treatment evaluation strategies. 中風是導致全球死亡和殘疾的主要原因。隨著新醫療技術和膳食干預措施的發展，開發連續監測頸動脈粥樣硬化和中風風險分層的測量工具的需求也在日益增加。本項目的最終目標是開發這種測量工具。 我們團隊率先開發了三維頸動脈超聲作為可重複且靈敏的斑塊和血管壁體積測量工具。由於頸動脈粥樣硬化的局部特性，本項目的PI提出了逐點血管壁 - 斑塊厚度（VWT）和斑塊表面不規則度作為表徵斑塊和血管壁變化的特徵。儘管這些全局/局部特徵可以單獨使用，但是組合利用這些特徵會更準確預測臨床結果，並且對預期效果低於醫學乾預但低成本的膳食/生活方式變化評估（如本項目中評估的石榴汁）具有更高的靈敏度。本項目的具體目標是開發一個整合所有可用特徵的框架用於中風風險分層和治療評估。 雖然我們之前提出的血管壁- 斑塊厚度變化(VWT-Change)能夠描述局部變化，但無法分開描述每種斑塊成分的變化，然而單獨描述易損成分的變化對於患者管理和評估至關重要。在本項目中，我們擬通過量化基於體素的斑塊和血管壁體積變化（ΔVVol）來解決該問題。我們分別提出了量化ΔVVol的三維配準框架以及一種將ΔVVol映射到三維頸動脈圖譜進行基於群體分析的新方法。由於組合所有特徵會導致患者有高維特徵向量，傳統的判別分析和分類器可能不起作用。因此我們將開發連續監測頸動脈粥樣硬化的降維方法，並開發判別模型進行治療評估和基於圖的分類器進行風險分層。我們假設提出的框架將在石榴研究中將樣本量要求降低一個數量級，並且在涉及323例患者的另一項臨床研究中達到90％的血管事件預測精度。 在他汀類藥物藥效評價中，對比以往的二維斑塊面積，本項目的Co-I使用超聲測量三維斑塊體積來驗證藥效所需要的病人樣本量降低了一個數量級，本項目的PI通過使用局部VWT-Change測量進一步減少了3倍樣本量。本項目利用我們以前的成果，預計將為患者管理和治療評估策略提供下一個飛躍。

11206317.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11206317.value: 基於學習的複雜度控制高效率視頻編碼及其以外

11206317.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11206317.value: Dr Gao, Wei Prof Zhao, Tiesong

11206317.label: Project Objectives
11206317.value: To investigate an effective learning-based complexity control framework for HEVC in three stages. 1(a). Complexity estimation scheme. To achieve user-control complexity of a video coder, we must estimate the required complexity for coding tools, such as the time required for coding a Coding Tree Unit (CTU), evaluating a mode, or performing motion estimation within a block. We will discover the relationship between these complexities and coding features using advanced machine learning techniques proposed in objective 2. 1(b). Learning-based complexity allocation. Based on the aforementioned complexity model, the overall complexity shall be allocated to frames or CTU according to the video contents, such as texture and motions to achieve a better RD improvement with a given complexity constraint. Generally speaking, more coding complexity is required for key frames or macroblocks for a better overall RD performance. We will investigate the features of different patches in a video and construct the relationship between video contents and complexity. Afterward, leaning-based techniques will be used for effective complexity allocation algorithms. 1(c). RD-C optimization for complexity control. To maximize the RD performance of an encoder under complexity constraints, two RD-C optimization approaches will be investigated. One aims to reduce the number of alternative coding patterns, such as prediction mode and CU depth while the other adjusts the encoder parameters, such as Quantization Parameter (QP) and motion estimation range. Based on complexity estimation and complexity allocation of these two approaches, optimal solutions for complexity control are obtained. To investigate effective machine learning techniques to be used in the learning-based complexity control scheme. To devise a successful learning scheme, two steps need to be undertaken: a) Developing efficient sample selection, and b) Designing advanced learning strategies. 2(a). Sample selection scheme. In learning based video coding algorithms, the enormous sample set is a problem due to the differentiated nature of video content, which will prolong the training process and increase the training difficulty. In this project, we will apply active learning techniques to select representative training samples to improve the performance of the algorithms while reducing the training/predicting speed. 2(b). Advanced machine learning strategies. In the learning-based framework for complexity control, it is a key issue to devise effective regression algorithms. To enhance the good performances for these complex problems, we will explore the following two learning models: Doubly Sparse Relevance Vector Machine (DSRVM), and Generalized Relevance Vector Machine (GRVM). DSRVM is competent in handling the complicated complexity prediction of the basic coding tool, while GRVM is more efficient in joint consideration of different coding tools. It is expected that better prediction results can be achieved by adopting these advanced machine learning tools.

One aims to reduce the number of alternative coding patterns, such as prediction mode and CU depth while the other adjusts the encoder parameters, such as Quantization Parameter (QP) and motion estimation range. Based on complexity estimation and complexity allocation of these two approaches, optimal solutions for complexity control are obtained.

To investigate effective machine learning techniques to be used in the learning-based complexity control scheme. To devise a successful learning scheme, two steps need to be undertaken: a) Developing efficient sample selection, and b) Designing advanced learning strategies. 2(a). Sample selection scheme. In learning based video coding algorithms, the enormous sample set is a problem due to the differentiated nature of video content, which will prolong the training process and increase the training difficulty. In this project, we will apply active learning techniques to select representative training samples to improve the performance of the algorithms while reducing the training/predicting speed. 2(b). Advanced machine learning strategies. In the learning-based framework for complexity control, it is a key issue to devise effective regression algorithms. To enhance the good performances for these complex problems, we will explore the following two learning models: Doubly Sparse Relevance Vector Machine (DSRVM), and Generalized Relevance Vector Machine (GRVM). DSRVM is competent in handling the complicated complexity prediction of the basic coding tool, while GRVM is more efficient in joint consideration of different coding tools. It is expected that better prediction results can be achieved by adopting these advanced machine learning tools.

11206317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11206317.value: In June 6th 2016, Cisco released the White paper[1], VNI Forecast and Methodology 2015-2020, reported that 82 percent of Internet traffic will come from video applications such as video surveillance, content delivery network, so on by 2020. It also reported that Internet video surveillance traffic nearly doubled, Virtual reality traffic quadrupled, TV grew 50 percent and similar increases for other applications in 2015. The annual global traffic will first time exceed the zettabyte(ZB;1000 exabytes[EB]) threshold in 2016, and will reach 2.3 ZB by 2020. It implies that 1.886ZB belongs to video data. Thus, in order to relieve the burden on video storage, streaming and other video services, researchers from the video community have developed a series of video coding standards. Among them, the most up-to-date is the High Efficiency Video Coding(HEVC) or H.265 standard, which has successfully halved the coding bits of its predecessor, H.264/AVC, without significant increase in perceived distortion. Rate-Distortion (RD) has been commonly adopted as a metric to measure the effectiveness of HEVC based video coder. However, Rate-Distortion improvement from the new tools proposed by HEVC such as more coding unit partitions, and larger motion estimation ranges have inevitably resulted in a dramatic growth of coding complexity, which further limits the industrial deployment of HEVC, especially in power-limited and real-time applications. Many fast video coding algorithms have been developed to address this problem. However, these algorithms can usually only resolve a complexity reduction for a specific video configuration set, but not different application scenarios and systems, such as video coding on power-limited mobile devices, real-time video broadcasting, and so on. In this research, we will consider coding Complexity(C) as an important criterion in the holistic performance of HEVC and develop complexity control techniques that flexibly adapt to systems with different computation resources. We propose to develop a learning-based complexity control framework with advanced machine learning methods on sample selection and regression prediction. This learning-based framework can solve optimization problems in video coding by discovering the relationships between features from video contents and different prediction performances. As a result, the proposed controllable coding scheme can adapt to diverse video application scenarios. Furthermore, it is expected that our research will promote the use of complexity control as an essential ingredient to video optimization and flexible video coding for HEVC and its successors. The developed technology is expected to drive the future of digital media industry. 11206417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11206417.value: The ubiquitous use of battery-powered electronic devices has created a strong demand of sophisticated battery management systems (BMSs) to maintain battery safety and reliability. Prognostic and health management (PHM), a framework offering comprehensive yet individualized solutions for managing system health, has been successfully applied in BMSs. Nevertheless, the increasingly complex battery systems pose significant barriers to existing PHM methods for battery status evaluation, due to the fact that these methods are often empirical and population based. As a consequence, the estimation and prediction of battery status might be highly biased and thus lead to safety hazard and other problems in practical operations. Motivated by the new challenges encountered in existing BMSs, the proposed research develops a radically new approach for monitoring and evaluating battery health status by incorporating the advances in PHM modeling and analysis techniques. The proposed research approach focuses on effective and efficient estimation of battery health status based on integration of empirical knowledge and real-time data, and heterogeneous information on each individual, including the actual field operating conditions and ambient environment of a battery system. It is a worldwide trend in PHM research to shift the traditional paradigm from empirical to data fusion and from population based to individual based. The proposed research is promising across a wide range of battery-powered applications. The health status of rechargeable battery is mainly characterized by two key parameters: state of health (SOH) and state of charge (SOC). SOH denotes the remaining performance of a battery over its whole life cycle, which is usually quantified by remaining useful life (RUL), while SOC quantifies the remaining usable energy at the present cycle. The main objective of this research is to develop innovative modeling methods for estimating SOH and SOC by incorporating additional information and PHM advances into the modeling process. In particular, we will (i) develop degradation models and estimation methods for reliable RUL prediction of rechargeable batteries; (ii) develop effective and robust methods that provide accurate estimation for SOC of rechargeable batteries, particularly under a dynamic ambient environment; (iii) evaluate and test the proposed methods using both experimental and field data, and compare their performance with the state of art methods. 伴隨著電力電子設備的大量普及，複雜可靠的電池管理系統亟須建立以保障電池的可靠性和安全性。 目前，預測和健康管理方法(PHM)已成功的運用在電池管理系統中並為之提供全面而專業的解決方案。 然而PHM方法一般基於過往經驗並且只適用于大樣本。 因此，隨著電池系統變得愈發複雜，電池健康狀態的估計和預測可能出現較大的偏差並有可能引發實際操作中的安全和可靠問題。 現行的PHM方法正面臨嚴峻挑戰。 為了應對當前電池管理系統面臨的挑戰，本研究專案提出了一種全新的估計和監測電池的健康狀態，該方法融合了 PHM建模的優勢和統計分析手段。 此方法通過融合電池經驗知識，線上即時資料，以及電池個體的多種資訊包括電池系統的溫度環境和操作條件來實現電池狀態的準確和快速估計。 未來的趨勢裡，PHM研究中的傳統模式將由經驗學習逐漸轉向資料融合，由大眾化逐漸轉向個體性。 本專案順應這種世界性潮流，有希望廣泛的服務于各種電力設備應用中。 健康狀態 (SOH) 和荷電狀態 (SOC) 是可充電電池電池狀態的兩個關鍵參數。 SOH標識電池在它剩餘壽命週期中可以放出的最大性能，通常由剩餘可用壽命(RUL)來表示。 而SOC標識電池在當前充放電迴圈下可以釋放出的剩餘能量。 此研究專案的主要目標是通過結合多資訊融合和PHM方法優勢提出新的的可靠建模方法去估計SOH和SOC。 我們將，1，建立準確的退化模型和提出有效的估計方法來實現可充電電池的可靠剩餘壽命預測；2,提出有效並且魯棒性高的方法實現可充電電池的準確快速荷電狀態估計；3，通過實驗資料以及現場資料測試和評估提出的方法，並與現有方法進行比較。

11206417.label: Realisation of objectives
11206417.value: Objective 1: Develop degradation models and estimation methods for effective RUL prediction of rechargeable batteries. We have developed effective models and methodologies for RUL prediction of lithium-ion batteries. We developed a semi-empirical model from the relationship of CE and battery degradation to capture the capacity degradation of lithium-ion batteries. We incorporated the proposed model and the particle filter technique to perform online battery health estimation and prognostics. The framework functions to update the model parameters regularly with periodically measured data. Remaining useful life of the battery is then predicted by extrapolating the models with renewed parameters. Our experimental results indicate that the proposed prognostic method produces higher predictive accuracy than the square-root-of-time model. Besides, we also proposed a new data driven Brownian motion model that utilizes the adaptive extended Kalman filter parameter identification method. The proposed model can update model parameters online and adapt to uncertain degradation operations. This data-driven method has the flexibility and efficiency of Brownian motion models but avoids their shortcomings in model adaptability and health prognosis. The effectiveness of the proposed data driven framework in degradation modeling and RUL prediction is evaluated through simulations and experimental results on lithium-ion battery degradation data. Objective 2: Develop systematic methods that provide accurate SOC estimation of rechargeable batteries, particularly in dynamic ambient environments. We have developed effective models and methods for accurate SOC estimation. We proposed a stacked LSTM to model the complex dynamics of lithium iron phosphate batteries and infer battery SOC from current, voltage, and temperature measurements. The proposed network is trained and tested using data collected from the dynamic stress test, US06 test, and federal urban driving schedule. The performance on SOC estimation is evaluated regarding tracking accuracy, computation time, robustness against unknown initial states and compared with results from the model-based filtering approach (unscented Kalman filter). Experimental results show that the proposed network well captures the nonlinear correlation between SOC and measurable signals and provides better tracking performance than the unscented Kalman filter. In case of inaccurate initial SOCs, the proposed network presents quick convergence to the true SOC, with root mean square errors within 2% and mean average errors within 1%. Moreover, the estimation time at each time step is sub-millisecond, making it appropriate for real-time applications. Besides, we proposed a combined convolutional neural network (CNN) – long short-term memory (LSTM) network to infer battery SOC from measurable data, such as current, voltage, and temperature. The performance of the proposed network is evaluated using data collected from a new combined dynamic loading profile in terms of estimation accuracy and robustness against unknown initial state. Experimental results show that the proposed CNN-LSTM network well captures the nonlinear relationships between SOC and measurable variables and presents better tracking performance than the LSTM and CNN networks. In case of unknown initial SOCs, the proposed network fast converges to true SOC and then presents smooth and accurate results, with maximum mean average error under 1% and maximum root mean square error under 2%. Moreover, the proposed network well learns the influence of ambient temperature and can estimate battery SOC under varying temperatures with maximum mean average error under 1.5% and maximum root mean square error under 2%. Objective 3: Evaluate and test the proposed methods using both experimental and field data, and compare their performance with some existing methods. To evaluate the proposed CE model, a battery cycle life experiment is designed, in which subjects are continuously cycled under a federal urban driving schedule to simulate real-life battery usage. Our experimental results indicate that the proposed prognostic method produces higher predictive accuracy than the square-root-of-time model. To test the estimation performance of deep learning networks, the proposed network was trained and tested using data collected from the dynamic stress test, US06 test, and federal urban driving schedule. The performance on SOC estimation is evaluated regarding tracking accuracy, computation time, robustness against unknown initial states and compared with results from the model-based filtering approach (unscented Kalman filter). Moreover, different training and testing data sets are constructed to test its robustness against varying loading profiles. Experimental results show that the proposed network well captures the nonlinear correlation between SOC and measurable signals and provides better tracking performance than the unscented Kalman filter. In case of inaccurate initial SOCs, the proposed network presents quick convergence to the true SOC. Moreover, the estimation time at each time step is sub-millisecond, making it appropriate for real-time applications.

11206417.label: Major findings and research outcome
11206417.value: Finding 1: Develop a coulombic efficiency-based model for prognostics and health estimation of lithium-ion batteries We developed a semi-empirical model is derived from the relationship of CE and battery degradation to capture the capacity degradation of lithium-ion batteries. The coulombic efficiency-based model effectively captures the convex degradation trend of lithium iron phosphate batteries and presents better fitting performance than the existing square-root-of-time model. Finding 2: Develop an adaptive Brownian motion model data-driven battery health prognosis We proposed a new data driven Brownian motion model that utilizes the adaptive extended Kalman filter parameter identification method. The proposed model can update model parameters online and adapt to uncertain degradation operations. This data-driven method has the flexibility and efficiency of Brownian motion models but avoids their shortcomings in model adaptability and health prognosis. The effectiveness of the proposed data driven framework in degradation modeling and RUL prediction was evaluated through simulations and experimental results on lithium-ion battery degradation data. Finding 3: Develop a long short-term memory network (LSTM) for state-of-charge (SOC) estimation of lithium-ion batteries We proposed a stacked LSTM to model the complex dynamics of lithium iron phosphate batteries and infer battery SOC from current, voltage, and temperature measurements. Experimental results show that the proposed network well captures the nonlinear correlation between SOC and measurable signals and provides better tracking performance than the unscented Kalman filter. Finding 4: Develop a combined CNN-LSTM network for battery SOC estimation We proposed a combined convolutional neural network (CNN) – long short-term memory (LSTM) network to infer battery SOC from measurable data, such as current, voltage, and temperature. The proposed network shares the merits of both CNN and LSTM networks and can extract both spatial and temporal features from input data. The performance of the proposed network is evaluated using data collected from a new combined dynamic loading profile in terms of estimation accuracy and robustness against unknown initial state. Experimental results show that the proposed CNN-LSTM network well captures the nonlinear relationships between SOC and measurable variables and presents better tracking performance than the LSTM and CNN networks. In case of unknown initial SOCs, the proposed network fast converges to true SOC and then presents smooth and accurate results, with maximum mean average error under 1% and maximum root mean square error under 2%. Moreover, the proposed network well learns the influence of ambient temperature and can estimate battery SOC under varying temperatures with maximum mean average error under 1.5% and maximum root mean square error under 2%. Finding 5: Develop various extracted features and gradient boosting regression tree model for battery lifespan prediction We proposed a gradient boosting regression tree (GBRT) is proposed to model complex nonlinear battery dynamics and predict battery lifespan through various extracted battery features. Essentially, the GBRT works by constructing additional trees through minimizing the prediction residues from existing base models. It can identify complex and nonlinear end-to-end relationship and meanwhile provide relative importance for each input feature. Various potential features including voltage-related features, capacity-related features, and temperature-related features were constructed in both discharge time dimension and life cycle dimension and explored for effective lifespan prediction. Comparative studies confirm that the proposed method is significantly superior to other machine learning algorithms for battery lifespan prediction with limited data samples and various input features.

11206417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11206417.value: To ensure the safe, reliable and efficient operation of electric vehicles, it is critical to establish an advanced battery management system (BMS) to accurately and timely monitor the battery status. The state-of-charge (SOC) and state-of-health (SOH) are two of the key states of the BMS. Accurate SOC estimation and RUL prediction are essential for EV mileage estimation and trip planning. It can ensure the battery working within a safe operating window to extend the battery cycle life. In the future, we will continue to improve our existing methods on SOC estimation and RUL prediction. In particular, for RUL prediction, we will try to link the time series models of Finding 6 to the physicochemical degradation mechanisms of batteries (e.g., autocorrelation in SEI solid electrolyte interphase growth) since the slope change defined in the proposed model is closely related to degradation rate change in an intuitive manner. Another future work will be assessing the correlation between the physical parameters regarding battery degradation and the slope change defined in the proposed model, so that we can infer the physical parameters based on easily obtained capacity fading data. For SOC estimation, we expect to extend the current method to consider more factors, such as humidity, degradation, and battery materials. We will develop an enhanced algorithm for the battery SOC estimation under different ambient temperatures and different ambient humidity. We plan to study along these lines and will report the results in the future. Methods will all be tested using comprehensive simulations and real data sets.

11206417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11206417.value: State-of-the-art battery management system (BMS) principles and practices have been developed under many science and technology disciplines. In particular, prognostics and health management (PHM) methodologies have been recognized to be the technological foundations for the development of optimal BMSs through real-time sensor data used for predicting system health status. The direct research outputs of the present project are new advanced methodologies, effective optimizers, integrated technological systems, and potential applications that go beyond the current practice and standards. In the short term, the outcome will improve the safety, reliability, and efficiency of battery management systems through monitoring the system, estimating the system state, protecting the system, reporting the data. More importantly, this research will enhance the sustainability for future renewable energy development and benefit the whole society in the long run. The success of this project will not only have great socio-economic benefits for both Hong Kong and the Chinese mainland, but will also consolidate an invaluable image and reputation of Hong Kong in the global energy industry and enhance the prestige of Hong Kong’s science and technology in the world.

11206617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11206617.value: Soil creep is the continuous deformation of soils with time under a constant effective stress. Creep may lead to serviceability problems or even instability and catastrophic failure of foundations, slopes and infrastructures. Even worse is that creep failures are often progressive in nature, which may result in failure of geotechnical structures that are deemed safe in their current state. Breakable sands and sands subjected to a large deviatoric stress fall within the category of highly vulnerable soils against creep problems. This phenomenon has been extensively studied in the literature, however major mechanisms that govern the soil creep have not been systematically investigated or fundamentally understood. Creep of granular materials, at the macro-scale, is linked to the behavior of grains at their contacts including grain-to-grain sliding and grain damage and this behavior is highly strain-rate dependent. The aim of the project is to explore experimentally fundamental aspects of creep of granular materials at the grain scale using novel micromechanical laboratory methods. This study will contribute to develop, for the first time in soil mechanics research, high-quality laboratory data which will lead to quantification and analytical expressions of micro-quantities such as inter-particle sliding friction and stiffness and grain strength and damage against the loading velocity which expresses strain-rate effects. The project will incorporate studies on a variety of soil grain types including naturally occurred soils and aggregates and a variety of load patterns. The first category of soils will predominately involve completely decomposed sand grains and other types of weathered materials which are of major geological and geotechnical interest in Hong Kong as well as carbonate sand grains which find major applications in offshore engineering with particular interest in Southeast Asia. The second category of soils will involve crushed rock and recycled concrete aggregate with major applications in transportation and geotechnical engineering which materials are of particular interest in Hong Kong infrastructure. The project will have a major contribution to the understanding of soil creep mico-mechanisms and will produce data and analytical tools of major impact in soil mechanics research and practice. 摘要 蠕變是土壤在長期的持續荷載下隨時間不斷發生形變的現象。土壤的蠕變可能會造成一些災難性的結果，比如滑坡，地基失穩等。由於土壤的蠕變是一個長時間漸進的過程，這可能導致一些被認為很穩定的巖土結構在未來由於基礎下部土壤的蠕變而發生破壞。承載很大偏應力的易碎土或沙最容易由於蠕變而產生問題。雖然在文獻中蠕變現象已被廣泛研究，但是其本身的機理卻沒有系統、基礎的研究與報導。顆粒型材料的宏觀蠕變現象實質上是由顆粒間的滑動，破碎等現象造成的，且與應變速率直接相關。此項目的目標是利用全新設計建造的微觀力學實驗儀器，從根本原理層面研究顆粒土的蠕變。這項研究將首次在土力學的實驗研究中，測量並分析土壤微觀層面的一系列性質，例如土顆粒間的滑動摩擦，土顆粒的顆粒強度，以及應變（加載）速度對破壞的影響分析。本項目中會通過一系列不同的加載模式來測量不同種類的土顆粒（包括自然土以及集料）。在自然土中，此項研究主要將會涉及：1. 香港地質、巖土工程中非常感興趣的全風化花崗巖以及其他風化材料；2. 東南亞的離岸海洋工程中常見的鈣質沙。在香港基礎建設中非常有應用前景的碎巖集料和回收混凝土集料也將會被重點研究。此項研究的主要貢獻在於對土壤的蠕變進行微觀機理層面的解釋，同時也為土力學的研究與實踐提供必要的數據及分析工具。

11206617.label: Realisation of objectives
11206617.value: The project aimed to provide a new contribution to the state-of-the-art of micromechanics with emphasis on the interface behavior of grains/aggregates, the development of cutting-edge experimental methods and how rate effects/creep come into play. Collaborations were developed between the PI and academics from the UK, Italy, Germany and universities from Hong Kong, two research students were involved on the project to successful completion of their PhD theses, and high quality outputs were delivered. Each of the project objectives was fulfilled 100%. Specific descriptions of each individual objective and the way it was achieved are given below. Objective-1. “Investigate creep and strain rate effects of granular materials at the scale of the grain, providing new insights into soil creep and perspectives in soil mechanics modelling.” Different materials were involved on the project, from natural sand grains (example: the studies by Sandeep and Senetakis, 2018 in Materials, 2019 in Computers and Geotechnics), proppant-rock analogue systems (example: the study by He and Senetakis, 2020 in Journal of Petroleum Science and Engineering), and aggregates (example: the studies by He et al., 2019 in Construction and Building Materials). The project also involved, through an international collaboration with universities from Italy and Germany, studies on lunar simulant (Sandeep et al., 2019, Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth). These works provided new insights into the fundamental behavior of grain contacts including the influences of strain-rate effects/creep. He, Senetakis and Coop (2019 in Tribology International) provided a clear relationship between interparticle friction and shearing velocity, which was found to be more pronounced for sand grain-polymer grain combinations compared with that of dry sand grain contacts, based on experiments performed at a constant normal load while shearing takes place. However, Kasyap and Senetakis (2019 in International Journal of Geomechanics), showed that strain rate effects are also important for dry sand grain contacts as long as the experiments allow for a continuous development of both stick and slip zones while shearing, which is achieved by a continuous change of the normal load during sliding. Through an international collaboration between CityU, HKUST and UCL, new insights into strain rate effects were achieved based on impact-type experiments on soil grain-rock block types of contacts, which study showed significant influence of impact velocity on the contact behavior of geological materials (Sandeep et al., 2019 in Canadian Geotechnical Journal). Objective-2. “Develop cutting-edge facilities and methods and further improve available apparatus for micro-mechanical testing.” Cutting-edge experimental methods were developed and delivered in various international journal articles. Examples of this is a new dynamic loading apparatus developed by He, Senetakis and Coop (2019, in Tribology International) and a new impact loading apparatus developed by Sandeep et al. (2019, in Canadian Geotechnical Journal). Kasyap and Senetakis (2018 in Tribology International, 2019 in Soils and Foundations) described the development of new techniques in creating artificially coated grains, so that a broad range of analogue geological materials could be studied simulating various problems, for example gap-graded soils. He, Sandeep and Senetakis (2019, in Construction and Building Materials) presented a new interparticle loading apparatus which is capable of testing much larger size of grains/aggregates compared with previously developed equipment. Many of these works presented additional newly methods in sample preparation/characterization or novel methods in imposing complex loading conditions. Objective-3. “Produce relationships which correlate inter-particle contact friction and tangential stiffness with the rate of sliding (velocity).” He, Senetakis and Coop (2019, in Tribology International) provided a clear relationship between interparticle friction and shearing velocity for sand-viscous aggregate contacts, quantifying also strain-rate influences on tangential stiffness and energy dissipation. New insights into the shearing velocity influences were presented by He, Luo and Senetakis (2020, in Tribology International) by performing velocity stepping tests on shale-proppant analogue systems. Kasyap and Senetakis (2019, International Journal of Geomechanics, 2020 in Pure and Applied Geophysics) showed clear relationships between interface friction and loading rate based on experiments under the continuous development of stick and slip zones for dry sand grain interfaces and by examining the tribological behavior of flat sand grains in the presence of clay microparticles. Objective-4. “Investigate the effect of loading rate on the strength and damage of single grains and the behavior of multi-grain contacts.” Important insights into the damage, at different scales, and taking into account observations on individual grains and multi-grain systems were obtained in different studies throughout the project, as for example the works by PI and his team appeared in Pure and Applied Geophysics (Sandeep and Senetakis, 2018, Kasyap and Senetakis, 2020), Tribology International (Kasyap and Senetakis, 2018), and collaborative studies between the PI and the geomechanics team of HKU (Li et al., 2019 in Powder Technology, 2019 in Canadian Geotechnical Journal). One of the important outcomes was the significant contribution of loading history on the tribological behavior of saprolitic rock interfaces and that the induced grain damage (micro-to-meso scale damage) resulted in substantially different frictional response. Strong interconnections between bulk strength, interparticle friction and the role of global grain damage were observed by Li et al. (2019, in Powder Technology). Objective-5. “Apply white light interferometry to characterize grain surface characteristics and the role of time-effects on surface damage.” Interferometry and other image analysis techniques were utilized to characterize the surface morphological characteristics of grains, potential damage at different scales and the role of strain rate influences. Through image analysis, the major contributing mechanisms to interface friction were examined by Kasyap et al. (2018 in Tribology International, 2020 in Pure and Applied Geophysics) showing significant different involved mechanisms for sand grains in the presence of microparticles compared with pure sand grains. This was further linked with velocity influences. Interferometry analysis and quantification of surface roughness were important to provide clear contributing mechanisms to the frictional response and to develop constitutive relationships for grain contacts by Sandeep and Senetakis (2019, in Computers and Geotechnics). The role of surface morphology and its inter-relation with grain contact constitutive behavior and strain-rate influences was further examined in the study by Sandeep, Luo and Senetakis (2020, in Tribology International), and it comprised a key technique to provide insights into the tribological behavior of aggregate contacts by He, Sandeep and Senetakis (2019, in Construction and Building Materials) and He and Senetakis (2019, in Acta Geotechnica). Objective-6. “Explore complicated load patterns and the cyclic behavior at the grain scale applying variable frequencies.” Collaborative studies between the PI and academics from UCL and HKUST examined the cyclic behavior for various material types quantifying the role of cycle number and providing advanced modeling which has a potential to put a new important contribution in multi-scale geomechanics research (examples: Kasyap, Senetakis and Zhao, 2019 in Geotechnique, He, Senetakis and Coop, 2019, in Tribology International). Kasyap and Senetakis (2019, International Journal of Geomechanics) studied the frictional behavior of sand grain contacts achieving a complex loading pattern which allowed the application of simultaneous stick and slip zones; that study provided insights both experimentally and analytically into the contact problem and the role of strain-rate influences, while the study by Sandeep and Senetakis (2019, Computers and Geotechnics), concluded that materials of lower roughness and greater modulus have larger energy dissipation at the grain-scale, which was additionally linked with macroscopic observations on the bulk behavior of granular materials.

11206617.label: Major findings and research outcome
11206617.value: Major project outcomes were delivered in the form of 19 SCI journal articles, 2 recognized conference papers, 1 book chapter and a keynote lecture delivered by the PI. The project findings put an original new contribution to the state-of-the-art of micromechanics and multi-scale geomechanics. It was revealed that three major influencing factors on the constitutive behavior of soil grains are the surface roughness, material modulus and micro-hardness (outputs no.2, 3, 6, 10, 15, 19, 20). It was not only the micro-scale morphology, but also the meso-scale morphology (outputs no.6, 8, 20), the loading history (outputs no.4, 6, 13, 18), and the condition of the surfaces, for example the presence of impurities or the formation of debris, which also control the frictional behavior of geological materials (outputs no.4, 5, 6, 13, 16, 20). Existing contact mechanics models are not capable in simulating the response of real soil grain contacts, but they need significant modifications so that to match with what the experimental results would suggest (outcomes no.2, 10, 14, 20). The imposition of stick and slip zones at grain interfaces while shearing can lead to substantially different response compared with conventional shearing tests which normally allow only slip zones to develop (outcome no.15). The findings of the project revealed significant strain rate influences at the contacts of geological materials and overall, a behavior which is very complex, compared with the current perception that grain contacts behave in a simple way and that the complication of the behavior of granular materials is because of their “bulk” behavior (outcomes no.2, 15, 16). Throughout the project, international collaborations were developed and established between the PI and CityU team with academics and research groups from UCL UK, Italy, Germany and also local collaborations with teams from HKU and HKUST, involving inter-disciplinary research with significant international impact. The project expanded its contributions not only to geomechanics, but also to petroleum engineering applications (outputs no.17, 18), geophysics (outputs no.4, 16), impact mechanics (outputs no.11, 19). 2 research students contributed to the project outcomes along with post docs and research assistants, and the project contributed to the development of world-class experimental apparatus and methods.

11206617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11206617.value: There is a strong potential for future research developments, based on that the project findings opened new directions, for example in the analysis of the constitutive behavior of materials with applications in inter-disciplinary areas such as petroleum geomechanics/engineering, the study of landslides and protective measurements, simulations of analogue fault systems/problems, the study of various types of aggregates with applications in transportation projects. Within the 3-year duration of the project, cutting-edge experimental facilities were built which can support future proposals by the PI. One of the important establishments from the project was also the development of collaborations between the PI and academics/research groups internationally. Based on this, the PI is preparing in the near future for a GRF proposal to be as continuation of the completed GRF, which will put more emphasis on links between micro- and macro-scales and will expand the investigation of rate effects into rock mechanics problems with potential applications in underground projects, energy geomechanics and the study of railway and transportation systems. The fundamental outcomes from the project give also the opportunity to prepare a future proposal for applied research with emphasis on the development of patent and contributing to the direct solution of practical problems.

11206617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11206617.value: Creep of soils often results in the development of unacceptable settlements which can question the stability and safety of buildings, infrastructures, and slopes. Understanding at the fundamental level of grain scale the micromechanical behavior of soil grains and the influence of creep is a very important step to produce accurate models which can assess the performance of foundation systems, potential landslides and other problems with major interest in protection of infrastructures and society development. This project investigated these issues at the level of grain contacts, providing new insights into the mechanical behavior of geological materials at the micrometer level. Advanced laboratory techniques were developed and the project findings contributed to the international scientific knowledge so that to deal with problems related with creep for soils, rocks, aggregates and other materials used in civil engineering projects.

11206717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11206717.value: The benefits of cooperation, both in nature and human society, have long been recognized and exploited. In engineering, the concept of cooperation has been utilized to develop systems that consist of a number of subsystems. Examples include a team of unmanned ground/aerial vehicles, a group of satellites, and a network of sensors, which commonly appear in security and surveillance, environmental monitoring, and medical applications. These applications all require multiple tasks to be accomplished across space and time, which is difficult, if not impossible, for a single-system platform to achieve. The growing demand for such systems has stimulated a broad interest in cooperative control problems in the robotics and control systems community. It is worth noting that many cooperative control problems, such as consensus, formation, and synchronization, can be formulated as cooperative output regulation problems. Despite the efforts in the past decade, to meet the demanding challenges facing such systems in real applications, many theoretical and technical hurdles must still be overcome. One important issue is the cooperative output regulation problem for multiple uncertain nonlinear systems. The foremost objective of this research project is to investigate the cooperative output regulation problem for nonlinear systems in more practical settings than those previously studied. In particular, uncertainties in exogenous signals, unknown control directions, and changing communication networks, which are inevitable in real applications, will be taken into account. Most previous studies of cooperative control for nonlinear systems have not considered these scenarios. The main barrier to such research is that well-developed canonical internal models for output regulation of single systems cannot be easily applied to devise adaptive distributed control strategies for cooperative control of multiple nonlinear systems subject to those uncertainties. Thus, it is important to develop techniques that account for these uncertainties and also address cooperative output regulation in a distributed fashion. In this project, a novel internal model-based distributed control framework will be established. The theoretical results will be applied to a real-life engineering problem, namely, the coordination of multiple mobile robots. The success of this project will lead to a systematic framework for cooperative output regulation of some typical classes of nonlinear systems in a more general setting. It will provide solutions to a number of theoretical and technical challenges envisaged, and benefit both academic research and practical engineering applications. 無論在自然界還是人類社會，協作的優勢都早已被認知和利用。在工程中，人們利用協作的概念開發出了由多個子系統組成的系統。此類系統的例子包括無人車/無人機組，衛星組，和傳感器網絡等，並且廣泛出現在安保監控，環境監測，和醫療應用等領域中。這些應用都需要系統在不同時間、不同地點完成多個任務，單個系統無法勝任。因此，對包含多個子系統的系統的需求日益增多。這使得機器人和控制系統的研究開始廣泛關註於此類系統的協同控制問題。值得註意的是，很多協同控制問題，例如一致性問題，編隊問題，和同步問題，都可以被規劃為協同輸出調節問題。盡管在過去的十年中，很多工作都致力於解決協同輸出調節問題，但想要應對現實應用中的挑戰，還有許多理論和技術上的障礙需要克服。其中一個重要的問題便是多個不確定非線性系統的協同輸出調節問題。 此研究項目的首要目標是研究更加現實的條件下的非線性系統的協同輸出調節問題。具體來講，項目將考慮外部信號中含不確定參數，控制方向未知，和通訊網絡可變等現實應用中無法避免，而大多數已有文獻未曾考慮的情形。此項目將創建一個基於新型內模的分布式控制框架。項目的理論結果將被應用於解決多個移動機器人的協調問題。 此項目的成功，將為一些典型的非線性系統，在更一般的條件下，達到協同輸出調節提供一個系統的解決框架。此項目也將為許多理論和技術難題提供解決方法，並對學術研究和實際工程應用都頗有益處。

11206717.label: Major findings and research outcome
11206717.value: Several fundamental problems on cooperative output regulation for nonlinear multi-agent systems in more practical settings have been investigated. Some typical classes of nonlinear systems have been studied. Effective distributed control schemes have been developed to tackle several challenging issues, such as uncertainties, unknown dynamic leaders, and unmeasurable states. The cooperative output regulation problem of uncertain Euler–Lagrange multi-agent systems has been considered. The leader system is used to formulate both the reference trajectory and external disturbances, and the dynamics of the leader system contains unknown parameters. This problem setting makes the problem more realistic. In practice, the external disturbances are often unmeasurable. Take the sinusoidal signal, a class of fundamental signals, as a typical example of external disturbances. The amplitudes, phase angles, and frequencies of the sinusoidal disturbances are probably all unknown. To describe such signals, the system matrix of the leader system is allowed to contain unknown parameters in the current setting. The existence of unknown system parameters poses significant technical challenges to the solvability of the problem. Using the robust control approach and the adaptive control approach, a novel adaptive distributed control scheme has been proposed. With the proposed control law, multiple uncertain Euler–Lagrange systems can achieve consensus in the case of unknown dynamic leader systems. Then the distributed output feedback tracking problem of nonlinear multi-agent systems with the nonlinear agent dynamics depending on unmeasurable states has been investigated. Most existing results on this problem were concerned with the case that the nonlinear agent dynamics only depend on the measurable output. Whereas the case that the nonlinear functions of agent dynamics depend on unmeasurable states are more practical but remains open due to technical difficulties. When the leader is only available to a small portion of followers in the directed communication topology, we have developed a new distributed high-gain homogeneous domination design method, distributed observers, and controllers are designed to guarantee the control objectives are achieved. At the same time, several other cases have also been considered for multiple nonlinear benchmark systems with perturbations. Finally, the application of the developed control strategies to cooperative control of a group of two-link robot arms has also been investigated. It is concluded that the cooperative output regulation for nonlinear multi-agent systems is intensively studied in more practical settings. The developed control schemes provide solutions to a number of theoretical and technical challenges and will thus provide more feasibility for a wide range of applications.

11206717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11206717.value: A number of results have been obtained and published on the cooperative output regulation for nonlinear multi-agent systems with uncertainties, unknown dynamic leaders and unmeasurable states. At the same time, many intriguing problems in cooperative control of multiple agents are identified. For example, when we investigated the leader–following consensus problem of multiple uncertain Euler–Lagrange systems, we found that it is the first time that the internal model principle is introduced in the tracking control problem of uncertain robotic systems subject to external disturbances. It is hoped that the proposed approach can provide deeper insight to inspire the solution of some other robust control problems of uncertain robotic systems. It has been one of our recent interests and could be one of the future research focuses.

11206717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11206717.value: Several fundamental problems on cooperative output regulation for multiple uncertain nonlinear systems have been studied. Many cooperative control problems, such as consensus, formation, and synchronization, can be formulated as cooperative output regulation problems. One typical example is tracking control of uncertain robotic systems subject to external disturbances. Uncertainties in system dynamics, reference signals, and disturbances are all inevitable in real applications and should be taken into account. In this project, cooperative output regulation for multiple uncertain nonlinear systems in various practical settings have been addressed. Several challenging issues, such as uncertainties, unknown dynamic leaders, and unmeasurable states, have been tackled. The developed techniques and approaches will benefit both academic research and practical engineering applications in cooperative control of multiple dynamical systems. The expected outcomes of this project will advance the current state of cooperative control research, and provide a wider scope of applications for coordination of multiple mobile robots under more practical situations.

11206817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11206817.value: Networked multiple dynamic systems have been used to describe many practical control systems such as networked multiple mobile robots, networked teams of micro-satellites, and sensor networks. They are often capable of carrying out much more complex tasks than a single system. They have attracted considerable attention from control community in past years due to their distinctive advantages of good robustness and scalability, and their great potential in military and industrial applications. The recent literature review reveals that most existing works on cooperative control of networked multiple dynamic systems either do not consider time-delays at all or only consider simple forms of time-delays such as a common time-delay for all systems or constant time-delays with simple system dynamics such as single/double integrator and with simple network topologies such as fixed topologies. However, it is well known that time-delays often exist in practical systems and their presence is often the cause for instability and poor performance, and that time-delays can be of complex forms such as different time-delays for different systems or varying time-delays. It is also well known that system dynamics of many practical networked systems cannot be described by single/double integrator and that network topologies could be time-varying. Inspired by these observations, it is desirable to consider cooperative control of networked multiple systems with more general systems dynamics, more general forms of time-delays, and more general network topologies. In particular, this project will investigate cooperative control of networked multiple dynamic systems with heterogeneous system dynamics, with varying time-delays or even infinite time-delays, and with switching network topologies. More advanced theories, techniques, and tools will be developed to deal with those more challenging scenarios. The outcome of this project is expected to consolidate theoretical foundation and also enhance application potential of cooperative control for networked multiple dynamic systems. 网络多动力系统现已用于描述众多实际的控制系统，譬如网络化 的多个可移动机器人， 网络化的微型卫星组和传感器网络。相比 于单个系统，网络多动力系统能够执行更加复杂的任务。在过去 的数年中，由于其具有良好的鲁棒性和可扩展性，以及在军事应 用和工业应用方面的强大潜力，网络多动力系统受到了控制界的 极大关注。近期的文献显示，大多数现存的关于网络多动力系统 的协调控制的工作要么完全不考虑时滞，要么仅考虑简单形式的 时滞，譬如所有系统假设有一个共同的时滞或者系统的时滞是常 数且其动力学是单个或双重积分，其拓扑是恒定拓扑这样较为简 单的形式。然而，众所周知的是，时滞经常存在于实际系统中并 且其存在往往是导致不稳定和坏性能的原因，同时时滞可以具有 复杂的形式，譬如不同系统有不同的时滞或者变化的时滞。同样 广为人知的是，许多实际的网络系统的动力学不能为单个或者双 重积分的形式所描述，网络拓扑也可能是时变的。受启于以上观 察，考虑拥有更一般的系统动力学，更一般形式的时滞以及更一 般的网络拓扑的网络系统的协调控制是值得的。特别地，这个项 目将会研究拥有异构的系统动力学，变化的甚至无穷大的时滞以 及切换拓扑的网络动力系统的协调控制。更多尖端的理论、技术 和工具将会被开发出来，以用于攻克那些更加具有挑战性的难题 。项目的成果有望巩固网络多动力系统的协调控制的理论基础并 增强其应用潜力。

11206817.label: Realisation of objectives
11206817.value: All of the project objectives have been achieved successfully. More specifically, we have investigated and developed novel approaches to cooperative control of networked multiple dynamic systems with bounded transmission delays under various network topologies. We have also investigated and developed novel approaches to cooperative control of networked multiple dynamic systems with bounded transmission delays, input and output delays under various network topologies. In addition, we have investigated and developed novel approaches to cooperative control of networked multiple dynamic systems with simple agent dynamics and infinite transmission delays. It is found that cooperative control of networked multiple dynamic systems with infinite transmission delays presents a much more challenging task than bounded delays, and much more effort on the topic are warranted.

11206817.label: Major findings and research outcome
11206817.value: We have investigated cooperative control of networked multiple dynamic systems with arbitrarily large constant, time-varying, or distributed transmission delays and fixed/switching network topologies. Novel distributed dynamic controllers are proposed for such multi-agent systems with fixed and switching directed communication topologies, respectively. It is shown that the controlled heterogeneous linear multi-agent systems can reach consensus for arbitrarily large constant, time-varying, and distributed communication delays under some sufficient conditions. We have also investigated output consensus problems of heterogeneous linear multi-agent systems with switching topology and time delays. Three types of time delays are considered: communication delays, input delays, and output delays. Novel distributed predictor-based controllers are proposed and it is shown that the output consensus problems can be solved via the proposed controllers. We have further investigated leader-following output consensus problems of heterogeneous linear multi-agent systems under communication delays and unknown leader dynamics. Novel adaptive distributed observers have been developed to address the problems. It has been shown that the output consensus can be achieved for the resulting closed loop multi-agent systems. In addition, we have started to investigate the consensus problems of simple linear multi-agent systems under infinite distributed communication delays which are much more challenging than bounded communication delays. To deal with the challenge, we have first investigated the simpler stabilization problem of single linear systems with infinite delays. Based on the results obtained for single systems, we have been able to obtain some preliminary results for simple multi-agent systems under infinite communication delays. It is shown that output consensus can be achieved for single integrator multi-agent systems and homogeneous linear multi-agent systems under infinite distributed communication delays. In the process of achieving the objectives of this project, some other results such as distributed optimization, cooperative control of multi-agent systems under cyber-attacks have also been obtained. Extensive simulations via various multi-agent systems including networked mobile robots have been conducted to illustrate the effectiveness of the obtained results. As a result of our research effort, more than 10 journal papers have been either published or accepted.

11206817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11206817.value: This project has investigated cooperative control problems of multiple dynamic systems under various time delays, particularly, communication delays. However, communication channels are also often subject to other constraints such as packet dropouts and quantization. It would be interesting to investigate cooperative control problems of multiple dynamic systems under simultaneous existence of communication delays and other communication constraints such as packet dropouts and quantization. In addition, we have only studied the output consensus problem of simple multi-agent systems under infinite communication delays. Another interesting topic is to consider more general multi-agent systems under infinite communication delays.

11206817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11206817.value: Networked multiple dynamic systems have been used to describe many practical control systems such as networked multiple mobile robots, networked teams of micro-satellites, and sensor networks. It is well known that time-delays often exist in practical systems and their presence is often the cause for instability and poor performance. The recent literature review reveals that most existing works on cooperative control of networked multiple dynamic systems either do not consider time-delays at all or only consider simple forms of time-delays such as a common time-delay for all systems or constant time-delays with simple system dynamics such as single/double integrator and with simple network topologies such as fixed topologies which are often not the case in practice. This project has thus investigated cooperative control of networked multiple systems with more general agent dynamics under more general time-delays and network topologies. In particular, we have investigated and developed novel approaches for cooperative control of networked multiple dynamic systems with arbitrarily large constant, time-varying, or distributed transmission delays and fixed/switching network topologies. We have also investigated and developed novel approaches for output consensus of heterogeneous linear multi-agent systems with switching topology, communication delays, input delays, and output delays. We have further investigated and developed novel approaches for leader-following output consensus of heterogeneous linear multi-agent systems under communication delays and unknown leader dynamics. In addition, we have investigated and developed some novel approaches for consensus of single integrator multi-agent systems and homogeneous linear multi-agent systems under infinite distributed communication delays. We have also carried out extensive simulations to illustrate the effectiveness of the obtained results. The outcome of this project is expected to consolidate theoretical foundation and also enhance application potential of cooperative control for networked multiple dynamic systems.

11206917.label: Project Objectives
11206917.value: Basis functions with higher order continuity for extraordinary regions: During the initial phase of the project, schemes for constructing higher order smooth spline spaces over extraordinary regions will be investigated. Desired basis functions with higher order continuity will be constructed. Special considerations will be given to the development of schemes with nice properties, such as partition of unity, quality of the resulting scheme and computational efficiency. Unstructured T-splines with global higher order continuity: The developed basis functions will be integrated with usual T-splines in forming a new unstructured T-spline space with global higher order continuity. The new unstructured T-splines inherit all properties of usual T-splines in regular regions, while possess better properties in extraordinary regions compared with existing solutions. The unstructured T-splines will be implemented with efficient Bezier extraction that can be integrated in any T-spline spaces and subdivision-based modeling platform. Dynamic local refinements in extraordinary regions: For applications in isogeometric analysis, refinement rules will be developed for basis functions in extraordinary regions. In addition to investigations on basis function refinements, local refinement algorithms based on a dynamic local updating strategy will also be developed. Isogeometric analysis based on the new unstructured T-splines: The developed scheme of unstructured T-splines will be further used for applications in isogeometric analysis. The main purpose of this implementation is for investigating the properties of unstructured T-splines in IGA with a particular emphasis on convergence evaluation and elevation in extraordinary regions. To validate the research outcomes, some case studies will be produced on both modeling and isogeometric analysis for stress and strain analysis of models defined using unstructured T-splines.
