11206917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11206917.value: Isogeometric analysis (IGA) provides an ideal solution for integrated design and analysis by directly using the computer aided design (CAD) representation for downstream engineering analysis. Among various representation schemes commonly used in isogeometric analysis, T-splines offer a promising solution with many nice properties, such as local refinements and optimal convergence, and have been one of the key representations in IGA. In case of unstructured T-meshes with extraordinary control vertices, T-splines produce higher order smooth solutions in regular regions, that is C2 for cubic B-spline basis functions, while G1 in regions of extraordinary vertices. This project investigates alternative basis functions for control vertices of extraordinary regions such that the resulting unstructured T-splines can achieve global higher order continuity, including in regions of and at extraordinary corner positions, for both the representations of the physical domain and the solution space. Key areas to be addressed in the proposed project include the construction of high order and well-behaved basis functions for extraordinary regions, construction of a new T-spline space over unstructured T-meshes with global higher order continuity, dynamic local refinement of the proposed resulting T-splines in extraordinary regions, and applications of the unstructured T-splines in isogeometric analysis. The proposed new unstructured T-splines inherit all properties and operations of usual T-spline spaces for regular regions, while with better properties in extraordinary regions with global higher order continuity. The production of higher order smooth solutions is important for many mathematical and engineering analysis and simulation. Since the constructed basis functions for extraordinary regions are explicitly defined as polynomial splines, the resulting unstructured T-splines can be efficiently implemented through Bezier extraction for both the physical domain and the solution space. 等幾何分析（IGA）可用與計算機輔助設計相同的基函數進行工程分析，並為集成設計和分析提供了理想的解決方法。在常用的等幾何分析建模方式中，T-樣條具備許多優良屬性，如局部細化及最佳收斂性等，是用於IGA中重要兼具發展潛力的建模技术。在具有奇異控制點的非結構T-網格的情況下，現有非結構T-樣條在規則區域可生成高階連續解，即對於三次B-樣條基函數為C2，而在非规則區奇異點附近則通常為低階G1連續解。本研究項目旨在構建一類用於非规則區控制點的替代基函數，從而實現包括非规則區及奇異點位置具備全局高階連續性的非結構T-樣條。該項目主要解決的關鍵問題包括具優良屬性的高階連續替代基函數的生成、可用非結構T-網格兼具全局高階連續性的非結構T-樣條空間的構造、非规則區域動態局部細化、及這類新非結構T-樣條在等幾何分析中的應用。本項目所提出的非結構T-樣條在規則區域繼承了T-樣條空間的所有屬性和操作，在非规則區域則具有更好屬性的全局高階連續性。高階連續解的產生對於許多工程分析及仿真具有重要意義。由於為非规則區構造的基函數可以顯式定義為多項式樣條函數，所構造的非結構T-樣條在物理域和解空間都可高效地通過貝塞爾單元提取來實現。

11206917.label: Realisation of objectives
11206917.value: This project investigates alternative basis functions for control vertices of extraordinary regions of unstructured quadrilateral meshes and unstructured T-splines in general with higher order smoothness conditions and other desired properties at extraordinary positions for isogeometric analysis (IGA). Key areas addressed in the project include the construction of refinement/subdivision schemes with well-behaved basis functions for extraordinary regions, construction of a new spline space over unstructured quadrilateral meshes with global G2/C2 continuity, refinement operations for extraordinary regions with other desired properties, and their applications in isogeometric analysis. The emphasis of the project is on the development of refinement operations for extraordinary regions of unstructured quadrilateral meshes with well-behaved basis functions and the construction of optimal G2/C2 spline basis functions for unstructured quadrilateral meshes. While the refinement stencils and G2/C2 spline constructions for extraordinary regions developed through the project are mainly demonstrated using unstructured quadrilateral meshes, they can be directly applied to extraordinary regions of unstructured T-meshes for isogeometric analysis. All main project objectives have been reasonably achieved with major research activities described as follows. (1) Subdivision / refinement stencils around extraordinary vertices with quasi-G2 continuity (Objectives #1-2): During the project, a novel method has been developed for constructing subdivision / refinement stencils near extraordinary vertices with limit surfaces having quasi-G2 continuity at extraordinary positions, i.e. with G1 continuity while maintaining the optimal or least curvature variation at extraordinary positions. With the proposed method, we optimize subdivision stencils to provide the best possible curvature behavior near extraordinary vertices with respect to G2 continuity for unstructured quadrilateral meshes. The resulting subdivision stencils can be integrated with either subdivision schemes for unstructured quadrilateral meshes or unstructured T-splines. The respective scheme produces global C2 continuity except at a limited number of extraordinary vertices where quasi-G2 continuity is achieved. (Ref.: [J1, C2, C3, C6]) (2) Subdivision / refinement stencils for unstructured quadrilateral meshes with improved convergence for isogeometric analysis (Objectives #1-2 and #4): We also develop subdivision stencils for unstructured quadrilateral meshes with improved convergence rates in extraordinary regions for isogeometric analysis compared with that of Catmull-Clark and related tuned subdivision schemes. The new subdivision stencils are constructed to ensure G1 continuity with optimal bounded curvature at extraordinary positions and with further constraints in meeting desired convergence properties for isogeometric analysis. The results show that the convergence rates of the resulting scheme are consistent with the optimal convergence rate of cubic spline patches in regular regions of the subdivision scheme, which is a substantial improvement compared with that obtained using Catmull-Clark and other tuned subdivision schemes. The resulting subdivision stencils can also be directly integrated with any other stationary subdivision schemes for unstructured quadrilateral meshes and unstructured T-splines. (Ref.: [J2, C3, C4, C6]) (3) Optimal subdivision stencils with other desired properties (Objectives #1-3): During the project, we also develop other subdivision stencils for unstructured quadrilateral meshes that are free from or with substantially reduced polar artifact in extraordinary regions while maintaining the best possible bounded curvature at extraordinary positions. The subdivision stencils are firstly constructed to meet tangent plane continuity with bounded curvature at extraordinary positions. They are further optimized towards curvature continuity at an extraordinary position with additional measures for removing or for minimizing the polar artifact in extraordinary regions. A new tuned subdivision scheme is constructed by replacing subdivision stencils of Catmull-Clark subdivision with that from this scheme for extraordinary vertices. The results show that subdivision stencils from our method produce well behaved subdivision meshes with the least polar artifact while maintaining satisfactory limit surface quality. The resulting subdivision stencils can be directly integrated with any other stationary binary subdivision schemes for unstructured quadrilateral meshes or unstructured T-meshes. (Ref.: [J3, C7]) (4) Construction of a new spline space with G2/C2 continuity at extraordinary regions of unstructured quadrilateral meshes and T-meshes (Objectives #1-4): During the project, extensive works have also been conducted for directly constructing spline basis functions with G2/C2 continuity conditions over the entire domain of support, including at extraordinary positions. The basis functions are constructed through a hole filling approach for extraordinary surface patches with desired continuity conditions and other properties. The scheme is built upon a bounded curvature subdivision scheme with the least polar artifacts, but the idea can also be extended to any other subdivision schemes for unstructured quadrilateral meshes. The resulting basis functions can be stored through Bézier extraction for efficient implementation and applications in isogeometric analysis. They can also be integrated with both subdivision schemes for unstructured quadrilateral meshes and unstructured T-splines. (Ref.: [J4, C8]) (5) Smooth parameterization for isogeometric analysis (Objectives #3-4): In isogeometric analysis, parameterization of a computational domain has a large effect as mesh generation in finite element analysis. Given an arbitrary domain boundary, we fill in the region with a smooth parameterization through the solution of a partial differential equation (PDE) with desired boundary conditions. In collaboration with another project under the same PI, a general formulation of isogeometric collocation method has been developed using non-uniform rational B-spline (NURBS) with Greville abscissae collocation points for PDE-based analysis-suitable parameterization [J5, C1, C5, C9]. In addition, a variational framework was also developed for producing a smooth parameterization of a computational domain represented in B-spline form [J6, C10]. Both the above schemes can be further extended for smooth parameterization of physical domains defined using the resulting subdivision schemes and unstructured T-splines. Dynamic local refinements in extraordinary regions could also be implemented in the framework for smooth domain parameterization. (Ref.: [J5, J6, C1, C5, C9, C10]) Based on the results obtained so far, the works on the construction of subdivision stencils with optimal bounded curvature [J1] and with the least polar artifacts [J3] have been published in Computer Graphics Forum [J1, J3]. The work on subdivision stencils with improved convergence for isogeometric analysis has been published in the Journal of Graphical Models [J2]. Some results for the works on the construction of G2/C2 splines over extraordinary regions of unstructured quadrilateral meshes have been publishes in Computer Aided Design [J4]. The works on PDE-based analysis-suitable parameterization and the variational framework for smooth analysis-suitable parameterization have been published in Computer Aided Geometric Design and Computer Aided Design, respectively. The results discussed above on the construction of optimal subdivision stencils and C2/G2 splines over extraordinary regions have also been presented in various international conferences, namely in WCCM 2018 [C6] and CAD&CG-GDC 2018 [C3] on the general methodology for constructing subdivision stencils in extraordinary regions with desired properties for both modeling and isogeometric analysis, PG 2018 [C2] on the general methodology for constructing subdivision stencils with optimal bounded curvature, IGA & Mesh 2018 [C4] on the construction of subdivision stencils with improved convergence, PG 2019 [C7] on the construction of subdivision stencils with the least polar artifacts, and SPM 2020 [C8] on the construction of G2/C2 splines. Relevant works on collocation methods for unified space-time isogeometric analysis, analysis suitable mesh generation for IGA and field-aligned parameterization for IGA have been presented in IGA 2018 [C1], IGA & Mesh 2018 [C5] and WCCM-ECCOMAS 2020 [C9], respectively. The variational framework for smooth parameterization for IGA has been presented in SIAM GD/SPM 2021 [C10].

11206917.label: Major findings and research outcome
11206917.value: Major findings and research outcomes of this project are briefly highlighted as follows: (1) During the project, a novel general method has been developed for constructing optimal tuned subdivision stencils near extraordinary vertices. With the proposed method, we optimize subdivision stencils to provide the best possible curvature behavior near extraordinary vertices with respect to G2 continuity for unstructured quadrilateral meshes. (Ref.: [J1, C2, C3, C6]) (2) Based on the above method, we also develop tuned subdivision stencils for extraordinary regions of unstructured quadrilateral meshes with improved convergence rates in extraordinary regions for isogeometric analysis. Numerical results show that the convergence rates of the resulting scheme are consistent with the optimal convergence rate of cubic spline patches in regular regions of the subdivision scheme, which is a substantial improvement compared with that obtained using Catmull-Clark and other tuned subdivision schemes. (Ref. [J2, C3, C4, C6]) (3) During the project, we also develop other tuned subdivision stencils for extraordinary regions of unstructured quadrilateral meshes that are free from or with substantially reduced polar artifact in extraordinary regions while maintaining the best possible bounded curvature at extraordinary positions. The results show that subdivision stencils from our method produce well behaved subdivision meshes with the least polar artifact while maintaining satisfactory limit surface quality. (Ref.: [J3, C7]) (4) During the project, we also developed a general method for directly constructing spline basis functions with G2/C2 continuity conditions over the entire domain of support, including at extraordinary positions. The resulting basis functions can be stored through Bézier extraction for efficient implementation and applications in isogeometric analysis. They can also be integrated with both subdivision schemes for unstructured quadrilateral meshes and unstructured T-splines. (Ref.: [J4, C8]) (5) During the project, we also developed methods for smooth analysis-suitable parameterization of a computational domain for isogeometric analysis. One of the methods is based on a general formulation of isogeometric collocation method using non-uniform rational B-spline (NURBS) with Greville abscissae collocation points for PDE-based analysis-suitable parameterization [J5, C1, C5, C9]. In addition, a variational framework was also developed for producing a smooth parameterization of a computational domain represented in B-spline form [J6, C10].

11206917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11206917.value: This project focuses on the development of well-behaved basis functions in extraordinary regions of unstructured quadrilateral meshes through the construction of optimal tuned subdivision stencils and direct construction of G2/C2 splines over extraordinary regions. In connection with applications of the developed schemes for isogeometric analysis, the following areas can be further addressed. (1) During this project, some exploratory studies have been conducted on smooth analysis parameterization of computational domains for isogeometric analysis using B-splines and NURBS. The methods could be further extended for smooth analysis-suitable parameterization using other basis functions, including tuned subdivision schemes and G2/C2 splines developed through this project. Some further works are being conducted in this area in collabortaion with another GRF project under the same PI (Ref. . RGC Ref No. 11201919). (2) The construction of G2/C2 splines over extraordinary regions in this project is built upon an optimal tuned subdivision scheme with the least polar artifacts. The idea can be extended for constructing G2/C2 splines over extraordinary regions compatible with any other subdivision schemes. A unified scheme of G2/C2 splines would be preferable for the class of tuned subdivision schemes developed through this project and could also be further addressed in our future research.

11206917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11206917.value: This project investigates alternative basis functions for extraordinary regions of unstructured quadrilateral meshes and unstructured T-splines in general with higher order smoothness conditions and other desired properties for isogeometric analysis. Key areas addressed in the project include the construction of subdivision schemes with well-behaved basis functions for extraordinary regions, construction of a new spline space over unstructured quadrilateral meshes with global G2/C2 continuity, refinement operations for extraordinary regions with other desired properties, and their applications in isogeometric analysis. During the project, a general methodology has been developed for constructing optimal tuned subdivision stencils near extraordinary vertices with various desired properties. Another general method has also been developed for directly constructing G2/C2 spline basis functions over extraordinary regions of unstructured quadrilateral meshes with Bézier extraction for efficient implementation in isogeometric analysis. Other relevant works in connection with their applications in isogeometric analysis were also conducted. The emphasis of the project is on foundation theory and algorithms for the development of refinement operations with well-behaved basis functions and the construction of optimal G2/C2 spline basis functions for extraordinary regions of unstructured quadrilateral meshes, but the resulting schemes can be directly integrated with unstructured T-meshes for both modeling and isogeometric analysis.

11207117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11207117.value: Skin cancer is regarded as the most commonly diagnosed cancers especially in fair-skinned human and pet populations worldwide today. Melanoma, a type of skin cancer, accounts for around 75% of skin cancer deaths in the U.S. Meanwhile, the incidence rate of melanoma among Caucasians has increased by 3 to 7% per year, especially in the U.S. More importantly, the World Health Organization (WHO) estimated that over 65 thousand people per year worldwide would die from this malignant skin cancer. Undeniably, this malignancy poses tremendous burden on global healthcare system. Although surgery, radiotherapy and topical chemotherapy are in clinical practice, they have different degree of limitations and undesirable drawbacks. Chemotherapy is by far the most prevailing treatment for skin cancer, but the successfulness of this approach is dependent on the dosage control: overdosing induces detrimental side effects while underdosing leads to relapse or exacerbation of patients’ conditions. Therefore, systems which allow controlled drug release are critical in improving drug efficacy and public safety. On the other hand, using light as an external trigger to control the release of drug from therapeutic carriers, technically known as photoresponsive drug delivery, is anticipated to be a promising strategy for controlled drug release. More specifically, this technique is expected to allow local, on-demand drug delivery with the merits of permitting a high concentration of drug release at target sites while keeping the systemic concentration of the drug low, thereby reducing side effects due to bioaccumulation. Despite the merits have been reported and photoliberation of small molecules from nano-therapeutic carriers have been demonstrated, two key issues regarding the design of practical photoresponsive therapeutic carriers have not been addressed: (a) the therapeutic carriers cannot utilize wavelengths which can penetrate deep into human skin, thereby hampering the phototriggering process; (b) high-power light source is required to trigger the drug release process due to the low quantum efficiency for the photoliberation step, and such strong light source can bring damage to body tissue. The objectives of this proposal are to address these problems via rational design of photoresponsive drug delivery nanoparticles for melanoma. The success of this project not only can lead to a major technological breakthrough in cancer-related therapy, but it can also provide an alternative strategy towards targeted therapies for other diseases. 皮膚癌是當今人類和寵物中最常確診的癌症，而「黑色素瘤」是皮膚癌的一種，佔其美國皮膚癌死亡率的75％左右。同時，黑色素瘤在白種人中的發病率每年增加約3至7％，而此問題在美國尤其嚴重。據世界衛生組織估計，全世界每年有超過65,000人死於惡性皮膚癌。無可否認，這類惡性腫瘤對全球醫療體系造成了巨大的負擔。由於利用手術、放射治療和局部化療處理癌病在臨床測試中具有不同程度的限制和缺點，因此化療是迄今為止治療皮膚癌最常用的方法。不過，化療成效取決於劑量的控制，劑量過度會引起不良副作用，而過低則會導致患者病情復發或惡化。因此，發展控釋型藥物系統對於提高藥物療效和公共安全具深遠意義。 另一方面，使用光作為外部條件來觸發藥物從載體釋放的技術﹝光敏藥物遞送系統﹞為一項具潛力的控釋型藥物系統。具體而言，該技術能實現局部及按需要的藥物遞送，減少因生物累積所引致的副作用。儘管該技術經已實淺，但關鍵的問題尚未解決：（a）治療載體不能有效利用可深入滲透人體皮膚的波長，因此阻礙光觸發過程；（b）由於藥物的量子效率低，需要使用高強度的光源來觸發藥物釋放，而此強光可能對身體組織造成損害。此課題的目標是通過合理設計光敏藥物遞送納米粒子來解決這些問題。此項目的成功不僅為治療癌症的技術上帶來重大突破，更可作為其他疾病治療的替代策略。

11207117.label: Realisation of objectives
11207117.value: In the project, we have successfully developed synthetic routes for several classes of chromone and closely-related complexes (Dalton Trans., 2018, 47, 12838; Chem. Eur. J. 2019, 25, 9159; Faraday Discuss., 2019, 220, 196; Organometallics 2020, 39, 1299; Chem. Commun., 2020, 56, 8908; Chem. Commun., 2020, 56, 12644); cytotoxicity for complexes that are stable under ambient conditions have been investigated in several cancer cell lines. It was encouraging to note that some of our newly reported complexes exhibit moderate cytotoxicity against breast adenocarcinoma (MCF-7), cervical carcinoma (HeLa), fibrosarcoma (HT1080), hepatocarcinoma (HepG2), and lung adenocarcinoma (A549) human cell lines. Our investigation in this area also got recognition by the chemistry community, and we were invited to write reviews in this area (Chem. Eur. J. 2019, 25, 2889; Chem. Eur. J. 2020, 26, 6102; Polyhedron 2021, 197, 115023). We have also developed three phototriggerable drug release nano-platforms: (1) we reported a rational design of nano-theranostic system, denoted as Ce6-CuS/MSN@PDA@MnO2-FA NPs, which combines photodynamic therapy, photothermal therapy, magnetic resonance imaging with hypoxia-relieving and tumor-targeting functionalities (Nano Research, 2020, 13, 1389), (2) we designed an intelligent reactive oxygen species (ROS) nanogenerator Ce6/GOx@ZIF-8/PDA@MnO2 (Ce6, GOx, ZIF-8, PDA, MnO2 are chlorin e6, glucose oxidase, zeolitic imidazolate framework-8, polydopamine and manganese dioxide respectively) with O2-generating and GSH-/glucose-depleting abilities to achieve cooperative photodynamic/chemodynamic/starvation cancer therapy (Journal of Colloid and Interface Science 2021, 599, 543); (3) we reported a smart hypoxia-irrelevant free radical nanogenerator (AIPH/PDA@CuS/ZIF-8) to achieve combined photothermal/photodynamic/chemodynamic therapy (Journal of Nanobiotechnology 2021, 19, 265). We have also provided research training to several undergraduate students. They were assigned to perform literature search, simple chemical synthesis and characterization tasks, and some basic biological measurements. We therefore conclude that we have realized all our proposed objectives.

11207617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11207617.value: While research on fire behavior and fire protection in timber buildings has been conducted extensively for the wood pyrolysis, decomposition and charring, the question of how the loaded condition of a structural wood member affecting the charring rate remains unanswered. In particular, little is known with regard to the assistance of the mechanical stress towards the char formation, which eventually destroys the material. Prior research studies in this area have indicated the charring process of wood is very complicated. The timber decomposition are usually analyzed as two phases involving primary reaction of base wood pyrolysis and second reactions of resulting decomposition products. However, most pyrolysis models are empirical in nature and the decomposition of different constituents of wood is not fully considered. In addition, these existing empirical models on thermal decomposition pertain to the test environment at standard temperature regime of timber construction in no-load condition, while most of the timber structures are loaded when attacked by fire. Through the development of nano-engineering and material modeling technique, molecular dynamics simulation is capable to reveal the decomposition of the wood constituents from an atomistic perspective, as well as to predict the mechanical behavior of different constituents in a fire. The objectives of this research are to develop a reliable full atomistic model which can accurately describe wood cell wall, and to study the effect of mechanical load on the charring rate at an atomistic level using molecular dynamics simulation equipped with reactive forcefield (validated by bench-scale and medium-scale fire tests), as well as to develop a predictive model that can fundamentally describe the wood pyrolysis. It is proposed to investigate by means of a synergistic effort consisting of hierarchical modeling of wood structures (i.e. cellulose, hemicellulose and lignin), reactive molecular dynamics simulations upon charring, experimental fire testing leading to the identification of the pyrolysis products, integration of simulation and the experimental results to establish the reliable predictive model of charring process. Synergizing the knowledge developed in these research tasks, this study will form the basis for augmenting existing design specifications for wood structures by including the quantitative fire protection design provided by the char layer. It is envisioned that the knowledge of the thermal decomposition of various wood species and the formation of various pyrolysis products are crucial for further developing effective fire protection methods for timber-based materials, and for understanding the relative rating of their flammability and fire safety. 本研究的主要目的是研發一種可準確描述木質細胞壁的全原子模型，並利用分子動力學模擬和反應力場從微觀角度研究機械載荷對炭化速率的影響，通過對模擬結果與中等火災試驗測試所得結果的對比，開發一種可以預測木材熱解的模型。本研究採用構建木料分層結構（比如纖維素，半纖維素和木質素），分子模擬炭化行為和實驗確定熱解產物等手段，旨在建立一個可靠的預測炭化過程的模型。通過對炭化層的定量分析，本研究為加強現有的木材結構設計規範奠定基礎。同時，對各種木材的熱分解產物和形成的熱解產物的系統分析，有利於進一步研發更有效的木基防火材料以及更深刻地理解它們的易燃性和消防安全的相對等級。

11207617.label: Realisation of objectives
11207617.value: Objective 1 has been achieved completely. A full atomistic models of wood cell wall which consists of cellulose, hemicellulose and lignin has been created. Such model can be used to study the mechanical performance including strength and stiffness of wood material. Objective 2 has been achieved completely. A better understanding on the effect of mechanical load on the charring rate has been obtained through molecular dynamics simulations equipped with reactive forcefield which is capable in modeling the combustion process. It is found that the mechanical load can facilitate the formation of char and increase the charring rate. Objective 3 has been achieved completely. The study of the mechanical load on the charring rate has been conducted through both simulation and experiment. Bench-scale and medium-scale experiments have been conducted and the experimental results show a good agreement with what can be predicted through the full atomistic model. Objective 4 has been achieved completely. A predictive model which can describe the wood pyrolysis fundamentally and accurately has been proposed. In order to validate the newly proposed predictive model, bending test have been conducted and the load capacity as well as the char formation can be measured. It is found that the extent of char formation from the bending tests echoes with the results obtained from the predictive model.

11207717.label: Realisation of objectives
11207717.value: During the period of this project, the PI and her research team have successfully engineered multiple omniphobic and slippery surface membranes with superior wetting and fouling resistance (objective 1), studied the interactions between different low surface tension contaminants and foulants with the engineered membranes via testing against different challenging feeds (objective 2), applied in-situ and ex-situ systems to comprehensively evaluate the interaction and build-up of different foulants on the surface of the engineered membranes compared to the other commercially-available ones (objective 3), and fabricated novel membrane with a performance of theoretical and experimental studies achieving high resources recovery and concentrating ammonia from sludge digestate (objective 4), thus completed all the objectives. The details are as follows: 1. Objectives 1 and 2: We have extensively studied the design and fabrication of omniphobic slippery surface membranes and other advanced membranes (superhydrophobic and Janus) and evaluated their wetting resistance as well as wetting and fouling impacts on their physicochemical properties when tested with feeds containing different foulants and wetting agents and having different surface tension values. To this end, we have 1) developed a robust dual-layer superhydrophobic and omniphobic electrospun nanofiber membrane for MD application, especially with feed that contains surfactant and dissolved organic compounds, 2) fabricated an omniphobic membrane by electrospraying fluorinated zinc oxide (ZnO) nanoparticles (NPs) mixed with polyvinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene (PVDF-HFP) on the surface of an organosilane functionalized polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF) membrane, 3) designed a hierarchically assembled superomniphobic membrane with three levels of re-entrant structure, 4) introduced a novel hybrid electrospun-electrospray process to manipulate the hierarchical membrane structure towards enhanced surface superhydrophobicity and structural integrity, and 5) fabricated a novel patterned superhydrophobic membrane that achieved high flux production while at the same time showed an enhance fouling and wetting durability. Research highlights under this point are summarized as follows: • We illustrated the successful fabrication of an omniphobic membrane with a spherical micro/nano hierarchical structure by electrospraying ZnO NPs with PVDF-HFP over a cPF membrane. The presence of re-entrant structures stabilized the Cassie-Baxter state, preventing wetting and restricting the liquids from completely contacting the membrane surface. The fabricated membrane fluorinated with 30% ZnO NPs (w/w of PVDF-HFP), i.e., the cPFP-30Z membrane, was found to possess high liquid CAs of 159.0 ± 3.1̊, 129.6 ± 2.2̊, 130.4 ± 4.1̊, and 126.1 ± 1.2̊ with water, 0.3mM SDS saline (3.5% NaCl) solution, ethanol, and vegetable oil, respectively. Water Research 165 (2019) 114982. • We reported on the design and fabrication of a superomniphobic membrane with a carefully designed hierarchical structure comprising macro, micro, and nano re-entrant curvatures. This resulted in a superomniphobic membrane surface with remarkable anti-wetting properties repelling both high surface tension water and low surface tension oils. Measurements of contact angle (CA) with DI water, an anionic surfactant, oil, and ethanol demonstrated a robust wetting resistance against low surface tension liquids showing both superhydrophobicity and superoleophobicity. For water and oil, CA values of 160.8 ± 2.3 and 154.3 ± 1.9 were obtained, respectively. When tested in DCMD with synthetic hypersaline oily wastewaters, the fabricated superomniphobic membrane demonstrated stable, non-wetting MD operation over 24 h, even at high concentrations of low surface tension 1.0 mM Sodium dodecyl sulfate and 400 ppm oil, potentially offering a sustainable option for treatment of low surface tension oily industrial wastewater. Water Research 174 (2020) 115600. • We reported the fabrication of a two-layer patterned superhydrophobic polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) membrane by combining non-solvent induced and vapor induced phase separation processes (NIPS and VIPS) and subsequent surface fluorination to lower the membrane's surface energy. Moreover, the patterns introduced surface turbulence and favorable flow hydrodynamics that improved fouling mitigation when tested in MD with actual sweater feed. The flux was reduced by only 15.2% after 97 h of operation, compared to complete fouling and 100% flux reduction for the commercial membrane. After MD operation, SEM images of the membrane further proved the enhanced fouling mitigation where the patterned membrane showed minimal foulants depositions compared to extreme fouling and complete flux reduction for the commercial membrane. This work demonstrated that combining the effects of both patterns and superhydrophobic property produced a novel membrane that opens room for stable MD operation in treating challenging feeds. Journal of membrane science 595 (2020) 117596. 2. Objectives 3 and 4: We have developed an advanced in-situ fouling monitoring system through optical coherence tomography (OCT) and applied this real-time evaluation through several studies for several developed omniphobic and superhydrophobic membranes and compared with commercially-available ones. Additionally, ex-situ membrane autopsy was combined with the in-situ observations to provide a holistic picture of the development of foulants on the membrane surface. Moreover, an innovative and realistically appliable MD treatment process was evaluated for a developed novel Nafion membrane to achieve ammonia recovery from sludge digestate. The mechanism of ammonia recovery from sludge digestate through MD was revealed. Research highlights under this point are summarized as follows: • We have developed an advanced in-situ wetting and fouling real-time detection system coupled with Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) and Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS). We have monitored the real-time building of fouling layers on fabricated and commercial membranes through OCT. We evaluated the 2-D and 3-D cross-sectional scans, and the OCT enabled the reconstruction of the depth profile, as it can penetrate semi-transparent samples. Besides providing visualization, this approach also allowed the quantification of the fouling thickness over time. Moreover, we developed an advanced image analysis program that applies multiple threshold intensity range filters to separate the fouling and membrane layers from a single 3D image using MATLAB. Desalination. 475 (2020) 114148. Chem. Eng. J. 378 (2019) 122137. J. Memb. Sci. 564 (2018) 22–34. • We investigated the applicability of MD in resource recovery from sludge digestate by controlling the volatility and pressure of the vapor transport across the membrane to concentrate ammonia in the permeate stream. A mixture of Nafion ionomer and Multiwall Carbon Nanotubes (MWCNTs) were incorporated into a PVDF-HFP nanofiber matrix to fabricate a nanoporous honeycomb-structured Nafion membrane featuring high recovery and increased mechanical strength. The resultant Nafion (8%)/MWCNT (2.5%)/PVDF-HFP nanofibrous membrane demonstrated up to three times higher ammonia recovery when compared to the commercial PVDF membrane from a feed with an ammonia concentration of 300 mg/L. Additionally, theoretical analysis quantitatively revealed that the Nafion-containing membrane could suppress the negative effect of membrane's structural resistance on the ammonia recovery efficiency and enhance the efficiency. In addition, we also uncovered that the impact of Nafion on ammonia recovery efficiency was maximized when the Nafion 8% membrane was employed. This study demonstrated an innovative and realistically applicable MD treatment process for recovering resources, integrating low-grade heat, and scaling up in wastewater treatment plants. J. Memb. Sci. 590 (2019) 117265. It should be noted that Objective 4 regarding a semi-pilot was initially scheduled to start in 2020. However, due to the unpredicted evolution of the novel coronavirus and the consequent closures worldwide, our initial plan of demonstrating a semi-pilot ammonia recovery MD system at Hong Kong's STP was affected. Accordingly, we have kept our methodology and objective the same but changed from testing a semi-pilot scale to a bench-scale at our laboratory.

11207717.label: Major findings and research outcome
11207717.value: This research has advanced the applicability of membrane distillation (MD) to be utilized in niche challenging fields, such as industrial wastewaters where the state-of-the-art commercial desalination technology, reverse osmosis, fails. Novel MD membranes with superior wetting and fouling resistance were engineered and tested, and the relationship between their physiochemical qualities and performance was elucidated. The research has also confirmed the viability of these membranes for nutrient recovery from wastewater, as evident by their high ammonia recovery from real sludge digestate. This research has resulted in 22 papers published in top journals while contributing to three book chapters and being presented in seven international conferences and well received by peer engineers and academics. The success of this project has created a foundation for MD's application in coping with the future challenges facing the desalination and wastewater treatment market. 1. We have designed and engineered novel and advanced membranes, including superhydrophobic, slippery, omniphobic, and Janus, with superior wetting and fouling resistance against a wide range of low surface tension contaminants. As a highlight, our macro-corrugated and nano-patterned superomniphobic membrane utilized a novel fabrication technique and coated with silica nanoparticles (SiNPs) resulted in enhanced permeability, robust long-term wetting, and fouling resistance, and enabled an effective treatment of low surface tension, hypersaline oily wastewater via DCMD. 11207717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11207717.value: The current approaches used for designing and fabricating omniphobic membranes for MD still face some challenges. Firstly, complex and time-consuming steps are involved in functionalizing and attaching micro- or nano-sized particles onto the surface of the membrane for the re-entrant structure. Secondly, using long-chain fluorine compounds to reduce the membrane's surface energy imposes serious health concerns due to their extremely poor environmental degradability and their potential accumulation in living organisms, causing long-term harm. Thirdly, the PI found that omniphobic MD membranes created by depositing NPs and attaching them to the membrane surface using polymers suffer from a lower water vapor permeation due to smaller pore size and porosity. A decrease in membrane permeability would lead to an increase in both energy consumption and cost. Based on what we have learned from this GRF research, we intend to continue our MD research to tackle these challenges. We believe that the re-entrant structures' built-in MD membranes still have room for improvement in their functionality (higher permeability) and durability (stronger bonding between NPs and membrane surface). Notably, we believe there is an urgent need to develop simple fabrication methods, eliminate long-chain fluorine compounds and use chemicals with lower toxicity in membrane fabrication; and improve the permeability and durability of omniphobic re-entrant structures. Our direction for further development of this GRF research will be towards these areas for the development of greener omniphobic membranes, bringing MD commercialization closer to fruition.

11207717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11207717.value: Accelerated by unprecedented population growth, depletion of water reserves, and climate change, water scarcity has become a serious global concern. Wastewater reclamation, which can augment water supply and recover valuable resources, has become an attractive platform. To this end, membrane distillation (MD) is an emerging membrane-based thermal technology that has gained substantial interest in research and industry. Given its distinct advantages, such as tolerance to hypersaline waters, modular design, non-necessity of high pressure, and low operation temperatures, MD applications have been expanded into promising niche areas, including treating hypersaline wastewaters and brine generated from zero liquid discharge processes. However, the industrial-scale application of MD remains limited due to technical and engineering challenges. This research aims to better understand and provide solutions for two significant challenges in MD: wetting and fouling. Here, we designed and fabricated advanced membranes, including superhydrophobic, slippery, omniphobic, and Janus, by modifying their integral structure and surface to impart superior wetting and fouling resistance. We also gained an in-depth understanding of how these developed membranes interact with fouling and wetting agents of different physicochemical properties. Finally, we have utilized these advanced membranes in MD to recover ammonia, a valuable resource, from sludge digestate.

11207817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11207817.value: Although the birth rate in Hong Kong (HK) ranks among the lowest worldwide, life expectancy there is among the highest. The proportion of elderly people is projected to reach 26.5% of the population by 2031 (Census & Statistics Dept. 2015), while the number of demented elders (DEs) is projected to increase from 105,000 in 2010 to 273,000 by 2036 (a 160% increase; Yu et al. 2010). The HK government has introduced long-term care and aging-in-place policies (HKSAR 2012, 2016), and has constructed care and attention (C&A) homes to accommodate older people. However, the homes were originally designed for those with only mild physical or mental impairments (Social Welfare Dept. 2013). Without considering elders’ changing characteristics, it is impossible to satisfy their needs, especially DEs’ needs. Unlike the general elderly population, DEs have special needs for daily care and are vulnerable to any detrimental effects of their living environment. Inappropriate facilities management (e.g., unsuitable architectural design, poor ventilation, inadequate care, etc.) reduces elders’ quality of life (QoL), leading to health and safety problems. One’s physical living environment is a recognized dimension of QoL (World Health Organization QoL Assessment Group 1998), and is particularly important for DEs. Because of decline in cognitive health, such elders have to rely on facilities and facilities management (FM) to perform their daily activities. Although there is a Universal Design Guidebook for general residential buildings in HK (HKHS 2010), there are no specific guidelines for the FM of DEs. FM integrates multidisciplinary sciences, including design-related knowledge, behavioral sciences, and property operation/maintenance. Due to their unique characteristics, DEs’ daily life and activities differ greatly from those of the general elderly population. However, little has been done to improve DEs’ QoL through FM in C&A homes. Hence, the current study aims to fill this research gap. Its objectives are to: (1) update the literature and fine-tune the conceptual model for DEs; (2) factorize the FM(Dementia) components in C&A homes and the QoL indicators for the particular needs of DEs; (3) establish the relationships between the FM(D) components and QoL; (4) develop an integrated FM(D)-QoL model; (5) verify the model using a case study; and (6) propose FM(D) guidelines for enhancing DEs’ QoL. The findings can help professionals (e.g., architects, building services engineers, facilities managers, etc.) to improve FM needs; to plan specific design, operation, and renovation of C&A homes; and to enhance the QoL of DEs in the long-term. 設施管理整合了多門學科，包括設計相關知識，行為科學和物業運作/維護。由於癡呆症老人的獨特特徵，他們的日常生活活動與普通老年人有很大差異。因此，本研究旨在通過護理安老院設施管理來提高癡呆症老人的生活質量。本研究的目標包括：（1）更新文獻，並調整專為癡呆症老人的設施管理概念模型; （2）確定適合癡呆症老人的護理安老院設施管理因子，以及癡呆症老人的生活質量指標; （3）建立護理安老院設施管理與癡呆症老人的生活質量之間的關系; （4）建立癡呆症老人的設施管理與生活質量綜合模型; （5）提出專為癡呆症老人的護理安老院設施管理方針，以改善癡呆症老人的生活質量。本研究成果可以幫助專業人士（例如建築師，屋宇設備工程師，設施管理人員等）改善護理安老院設施管理需求; 規劃護理安老院的設計，運行和改造; 從而長期提升癡呆症老人的生活質量。 Revised English version of abstract: Facilities management (FM) integrates multidisciplinary sciences, including design-related knowledge, behavioral sciences, and property operation/maintenance. 11207817.label: Major findings and research outcome
11207817.value: The study identified twelve factors of three components of IBE in C&A homes (i.e., architectural design, building services, and supporting facilities) and five cognitive functional abilities of older people with dementia (i.e., memory loss, disorientation, confusion, self-care, and mobility) (Leung et al. 2021). Based on the optimum structural equation models, the statistical study conﬁrmed that: 1) surprisingly, both factors of the space management component (i.e., distances and privacy) were found to have no impact on the behavior of the residents with dementia in C&A homes; 2) a building services factor (temperature) positively inﬂuenced their self-care and mobility; and 3) three IBE factors belonging to the building services component – lighting, lifts and water supply – inﬂuenced negative emotion, positive emotion, sleeping disturbance and limited mobility of people with dementia; 4) loneliness was affected by the supporting facilities factor of furniture; 5) memory loss was negatively affected by satisfaction with lifts and furniture; 6) ﬁnishes and signage had negative impacts on the disorientation of older residents with dementia (Leung et al. 2019, 2020a, 2021). Older people with dementia experiencing memory loss have different requirements of SF than normal older persons. The study, thus, further investigated the effects of supporting facilities on memory losses and revealed that 7) none of the supporting facilities items affects long-term memory loss; 8) satisfaction with signage, ﬁnishes and furniture could lead to a reduction of short-term memory loss; 9) satisfaction with handrails, signage and ﬁnishes could enhance spatial memory; and 10) satisfaction with the location of signage could reduce time confusion (Leung et al. 2020b). Based on these ﬁndings, several practical recommendations were proposed. These include: 1) installing air-conditioning with automatic temperature adjustments during the summer months; 2) adopting anti-scald devices (temperature-activated ﬂow reducers) on showerheads and faucets; 3) designing with strong daylight and dim sleeping conditions; 4) installing lighting with automatic adjustment; 5) investigating the possibility of older people with dementia using lifts in some situations; 6) designing interiors with color contrast ﬁnishes; 7) using familiar furniture; 8) avoiding modification of its layout; 9) the provision of wardrobes with one open section for the strengthening of memory and the lessening of suspicious delusions; 10) installing handrails in C&A homes with orientation strategies, conspicuity and tactile cues; and 11) dementia-friendly signage to offset the effects of residents’ spatial disorientation (Leung et al. 2019, 2020a, 2020b, 2021). This empirical study has clariﬁed the impacts of the IBE in C&A homes on the cognitive functional ability of older residents with dementia.

11207817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11207817.value: According to the results of the current study, satisfaction with the level of lighting and thermal comfort had effects on the positive emotion, sleeping disturbance, mobility and self-care of the elderly with dementia in C&A homes. Future research is suggested to investigate the impact of actual lighting conditions (e.g., illuminance in daytime and nighttime and color temperature) and thermal environment on the emotion and sleeping disturbance of C&A home residents with dementia. The visual disabilities, sleep hours and mobility of older adults can also be recorded to further study the lighting and thermal effects of residents with dementia. Many kinds of sensors (e.g., light, temperature, humidity sensors, wind flow) and on-site measurement (e.g., room size and furniture arrangement) are recommended for collecting objective data in further study. Additionally, conducting intervention studies with different arrangements of furniture and finishes are also advised. The communication and social interactions of the elderly with dementia can be recorded to further investigate the effects of arrangement of furniture on their loneliness in the future.

11207817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11207817.value: Older people with dementia normally suffer from declined cognitive functional ability (CFA), including impaired cognition, deteriorated self-care abilities, etc. This study investigated the relationships between twelve factors of three indoor built environment components in C&A homes (i.e., architectural design, building services, and supporting facilities) and the CFA of older people with dementia (memory loss, disorientation, confusion, self-care, and mobility). The study found signiﬁcant relationships: 1) memory loss was negatively affected by satisfaction with lifts; 2) satisfaction with handrails, signage and ﬁnishes could enhance spatial memory; and 3) furniture could reduce loneliness; 4) temperature positively inﬂuenced the self-care and mobility; and 5) lighting, lifts and water supply inﬂuenced negative emotion, positive emotion, sleeping disturbance and limited mobility of people with dementia. It is recommended to: 1) design interiors with color contrasting ﬁnishes in different rooms; 2) enlarge windows for daylighting; 3) use familiar or historical furniture; 4) avoid modification of its layout; 5) select wardrobes with one open section; 6) install handrails with orientation strategies; 7) fix dementia-friendly signage (e.g., iconic information); 8) install lighting and air-conditioning with automatic adjustments; 9) adopt anti-scald devices on faucets; 10) design with strong daylight and dim sleeping conditions; and 11) add facial recognition to the lift.

11208017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11208017.value: With the advent of data science and software analytic techniques, more and more people and organizations chose to build predictive models from software engineering data to aid software engineering practices and decisions such as predicting defects, quality and efforts required for projects. Over the past decades, several novel techniques and prediction models utilizing the latest statistical theories and machine learning techniques have been proposed to improve performance in prediction accuracy. All these techniques and models claim to have significantly improved prediction performance. Unfortunately the results of these work are not fully reusable in the software industrial practice, mainly because the techniques proposed have only been validated against some publicly available static datasets collected in the 80’s, and we have no way to validate the quality of these datasets and their features within. As software is developed more rapidly than ever, the traditional data analytics approach of training from an existing dataset and to make predictions such as efforts and defects using different methods may be less relevant and unrealistic. In addition to the challenges such as cross- and within-company dataset and incomplete dataset problems, there is no way software practitioners are able to make use of the advanced techniques proposed in these software engineering studies. The prediction platform should be closely relevant to the software development environment and process such that it is able to automatically understand and analyze the entire source code base, design constrains, complexity, and software development productivity. To accomplish these objectives, human software experts are usually required. But with the complexity of software increasing, it is becoming extremely difficult to perform these tasks using human experts, and therefore being able to automatically derive useful information from software engineering raw data such as source code and other attributes is essential to support advanced software analytics. Thus, the latter results are more generalizable and practical for use in the software industry. The principal goal of this project is to develop a new software analytics framework with generalized data representations, which is suitable for deep learning. This project seeks to address a range of challenging problems, such as automated feature engineering from raw software engineering data, to create deep-learning based models for defect and effort prediction, as well as recommendations for better decisions. The outcome of this work is significant in that it endeavors to render the next generation of software analytic techniques generalizable and useful in the industry. 隨著數據科學和軟件分析技術的發展，越來越多的科研人員及機構使用軟件工程數據構建預測模型，用以輔助軟件工程實踐和決策，例如預測缺陷、工程質量或者預估項目所需的工作量。在過去的幾十年中，基於最新的統計理論和機器學習技術，一些預測技術和模型陸續被提出，所有這些技術和模型都聲稱可以顯著提高預測性能，然而，這些研究成果在軟件工業實踐中並不是完全可重用的，因為這些技術和模型僅在80年代所收集的一些靜態數據集上進行驗證，而我們無法保證這些數據集及其內部特性的質量。隨著軟件開發速度的增加，傳統的數據分析方法，即利用現有的數據集進行訓練並預測缺陷或工作量的方法，可能已經不再適用。另外考慮到數據集不完整等情況，軟件從業者事實上無法有效利用這些軟件工程研究中提出的先進技術。我們認為，預測平台應當與軟件開發環境和過程緊密相關，使其能夠自動理解和分析整個源代碼庫、設計約束、複雜性及軟件開發生產率。為了實現這些目標，傳統方法通常需要人工專家的參與，但是隨著軟件複雜性的增加，使用人工專家完成這些任務變得非常困難。因此能夠自動從軟件工程原始數據（源代碼或其他屬性）中提取有用信息對於支持高級軟件分析至關重要，後者的結果對軟件行業而言更加普及和實用。本項目的主要目標是開發一個具有廣義數據表示的適用於深度學習的軟件分析框架，用於解決一系列挑戰性的問題，例如從原始軟件工程數據中自動提取特徵，創建基於深度學習的模型以進行缺陷或工作量預測，以及提出更好的決策建議，本項目致力於使下一代軟件分析技術在工業界適用及實用，其成果意義重大。

11208017.label: Realisation of objectives
11208017.value: Thanks to the committee for their very positive feedbacks as stated in the mid-term progress report in 2018, all the objectives have been carefully addressed and further studied, supported by international publications generated. The primary operations of a software analytic prediction model is to compare and classify similarity between software characteristics. In order to provide the semantic finger-printing of raw data such as source code that will be used as the foundation of our data-preprocessing algorithm, we make use of the program’s Abstract Syntactic Tree (AST). Semantic features of a software code base could be extracted via AST according to the programming language’s syntactic structure to create the building blocks of the system as the basis. For instance, the grouping parentheses, their location or quantity, are implicit in the tree structure, and are not presented in the AST. Source files are composed of code tokens that are similar to the texts in natural languages, but the programming languages contain more structural information than natural languages. Since the source code can be parsed into the abstract syntax tree and also be reverted from the abstract syntax tree, and further processed by Deep Learning Models using CNN. DeepLoc (Reference: Publication: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.infsof.2018.08.002 ) After converting bug reports and source files into a set of vectors, the CNN model is applied to extract their features. Max-over-time pooling is used when constructing a CNN. We first find the maximum number (nS ) of sentences from each bug report and the maximum number (nL) of lines from each source file. They are then padded by zeros to be separately same with their maximum lengths. Figure 3 illustrates the process of feature detection from bug reports and source files using a CNN, in which k is the vector dimension of each sentence/line. The two CNNs have similar architecture, containing one convolutional layer with multiple filters followed by a max pooling layer. The size of filters in the max pooling layer is (nS - the height of the filter size+1) × 1 for bug reports and (nL - the height of the filter size+1) × 1 for source files. The size of the feature vectors extracted from a bug report is the number of filter sizes * the number of filters for each filter size. The size of the feature vectors extracted from a source file is also the number of filter sizes * the number of filters for each filter size. We use different filter size in the max pooling layer to ensure that the final feature vectors extracted from a bug report and source file have the same size so that they can be concatenated in parallel as the input to the subsequent enhanced CNN. Apart from the semantic information, the conventional CNN model contains no other important information related to bug localization, especially the fixing history of source files. Furthermore, bug-fixing recency and frequency have been verified as useful for bug localization. The change history of source files for bugs contains useful information for identification of fault-prone files. This implies that source files fixed recently are more likely to be buggy than those fixed long ago(bug-fixing recency) and that source files that have been fixed many times are more likely to still contain bugs than those seldom fixed or even never fixed (bug-fixing frequency). In one of the experiments, we use the enhanced CNN to learn the relationship between bug reports and corresponding buggy files. The feature vectors extracted from bug reports and those from source files are concatenated in parallel into 2-dimensional feature as the input to the enhanced CNN. The concatenation process is shown in Figure 4. The convolutional layer in the enhanced CNN uses filters with the size of 2×2 to learn the correlated relationships between bug reports and source files by convolving the input of the enhanced CNN that is a concatenation of the feature vectors extracted from bug reports and source files. The size of filters in the max pooling layer is 2 × (the number of filter sizes * the number of filters for each filter size). The enhanced CNN was used to correlate bug reports to buggy files including both linear and nonlinear relationships because of its convolutional operation and fully connected. All three CNNs use max-over-time pooling and are regularized by batch normalization to speed up the training process. DeepLoc is trained using the Adam (Adaptive Moment Estimation) Optimizer, which uses an adaptive learning algorithm. Compared to Adadelta, which retains an exponentially decaying average of past squared gradients, Adam can also store the exponentially decaying average of past gradients. In addition, Adam has shown better performance in large empirical investigations than other algorithms that automatically adjust learning rates. For the evaluation purpose of this project, we have empirically studied our DeepLoc approach. DeepLoc achieves 16% to 24% greater Accuracy@1 than BugLocator. Unlike BugLocator, whose performance for unseen bug reports is unclear due to the only parameter α being tuned on the same dataset for both training and evaluation, all of the weights for DeepLoc are learned on the training set, tuned on the validation set, and then used to predict the testing set, whose performance is scalable. At the same time, LR+WE achieves 2% to 16% lower Accuracy@1 than DeepLoc. LR+WE may be limited by the linear weighted sum of features, but DeepLoc does not suffer this problem because of the convolutional networks. Finally, DeepLoc achieves 2% to 10% higher Accuracy@1 than HyLoc. Because Lam et al. validated HyLoc’s comparable or superior performance against existing approaches, we use HyLoc as the main competitor and analyze the results. When analyzing the ranking results, we observe that some buggy files given low scores by HyLoc can be located more precisely by DeepLoc. For example, HyLoc gives one buggy file for Bug 54450 in Project Tomcat Rank 50, which is a relatively low score. However, DeepLoc predicts it as a buggy file by ranking it in fourth place because "resource" in bug reports is paired with words related to "context" (getContext, configureContext, processContextConfig) in source files many times. Another example is Bug 399401 in Project Eclipse UI. DeepLoc can relate them if these pairs have ever appeared in older bug reports and corresponding buggy files used in its training. Therefore, even when tokens in source files are mismatched with the words used in bug reports, DeepLoc can relate them, which indicates that DeepLoc can learn correlations if they frequently appear as pairs. In particular, DeepLoc’s prediction time for one bug report is much lower than HyLoc’s, which indicates that DeepLoc is more suitable in practice. These are results produced during the course of this project. Performance figures are showing improved performance, but not necessarily significant, but it solves an important challenge of human involvement in the determination of parameters for the models. In the future, we will further study and explore ways to enhance its performance and automation capability using the deep learning techniques proposed and utilized in this project. Summary Overall, we consider we have made significant progress towards the objectives of the project, and together with the great efforts we are able to produce many top journals papers during the reporting period, and successfully produced many PhD students working in the respective area of software analytics.

11208017.value: Major research findings Our proposed technique through the validation of DeepLoc and study of LSTM in Deep Learning: (Ref1: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.infsof.2018.08.002 ) (Ref2: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.infsof.2018.03.003 ) Result shows 16% to 24% greater accuracy than BugLocator (non Deep Learning based), and around 5-10% higher accuracy than HyLoc in our controlled experimental settings. 11208017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11208017.value: With the advent of data science and software analytic techniques, more and more people and organizations chose to build predictive models from software engineering data to aid software engineering practices and decisions such as predicting defects, quality and efforts required for software projects. Several novel techniques and prediction models utilizing the latest statistical theories and machine learning techniques have been proposed to improve performance in prediction accuracy. All these techniques and models claim to have significantly improved prediction performance. As software is developed more rapidly than ever, the traditional data analytics approach of training from an existing dataset and to make predictions such as efforts and defects using different methods may be less relevant and unrealistic. The principal goal of this project is to develop a new software analytics framework with generalized data representations, which is suitable for applying deep learning. This project seeks to address a range of challenging problems, such as automated feature engineering from raw software engineering data, to create deep-learning based models for defect and effort prediction, as well as recommendations for better decisions. The outcome of this work is significant in that it endeavors to render the next generation of software analytic techniques generalizable and useful in the industry.

11208517.label: Project Objectives
11208517.value: In light of our recent findings, the first objective of the proposed research is to theoretically extend our recently developed two-timescale neurodynamic approach to minimax optimization to selected global optimization problems including biconvex problems. Analytical and experimental results on the solvability and convergence of multi-timescale neurodynamic systems will be obtained, which will shed light to the developments of new multiscale neurodynamic optimization approaches. In pursuit of more powerful neurodynamic optimization approaches, our second objective is to develop neurodynamic systems operating on multiple temporal and spatial scales for tackling general constrained global optimization problems. Several related features (e.g., scale diversity vs. state convergence, spatial vs. temporal complexities) of the resulting multiscale neurodynamic systems will be thoroughly investigated based on multiscale analysis, optimization and systems theories. Systematic design rules will be also developed. Its breakthrough will significantly widen the solvability scope of computationally intelligent optimization methods to a new limit. In view of numerous global optimization problems in science and engineering, our third objective is to customize and apply the results in several interested topic areas such as neurodynamics-based matrix factorization and tensor decomposition in data and signal processing, and supervised learning in machine learning. The perceived successful paradigms will substantiate the application potentials of the proposed research.

11208517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11208517.value: 优化在科学，工程和商业中无处不在。许多优化问题由非凸目标函数或约束组成。由于存在局部最优性和缺乏有效的解决方案来寻找全局最优性，这些全球优化问题面临巨大挑战。在大数据时代，有效和高效的全局优化方法被认为是非常需要或期望的。 过去三十年见证了神经动力学优化的诞生和发展。由于其并行和分布式信息处理的固有特性以及硬件可实现性，已经出现并成熟为可行的优化方法。尽管初步成功，但几乎所有现有的神经动力学方法仅适用于单峰目标函数的凸优化和广义凸优化问题。使用多模态目标函数约束全局优化的有效神经动力学方法几乎不存在。神经动力学方法对全局优化的进一步研究势在必行。 众所周知，人类大脑在多个时间尺度上进行操作。例如，感知的时间尺度应该远远小于认知的时间尺度。此外，在多个空间尺度上的大脑建模更有效。神经动力学中不同时间和空间尺度的存在对于大脑的功能和正确建模至关重要。由于在脑动力学中多尺度建模和分析有更好的效果，在社会动力学中多元思想的比单个更好，多时空尺度上的神经动力学系统在生物学和社会学上都是合理的。最近的相关研究结果也表明，多尺度神经动力系统将更适合于全局优化。 在此项研究中，多尺度神经动力系统将被开发用于有约束全局优化。研究将由三个相关部分组成。在前两部分中，研究将重点关注在多个时空尺度上运行的神经动力系统的分析和设计，以解决具有特殊和一般非凸目标函数和约束的优化问题。构想的多尺度神经动力系统的可解性范围和收敛性将得以深入研究。在研究的第三部分中，提出的方法将应用于智能信息处理和机器学习中的几个感兴趣的主题。将致力开发基于神经动力学的数据分析和监督学习的方法。预计拟议项目的成果将从理论和实践的角度显著推进全局优化的研究。

11208517.label: Realisation of objectives
11208517.value: The three proposed objectives have been completely realized. Specifically, for the first objective, we extended the two-timescale neurodynamic approach to minimax optimization to biconvex and mixed integer optimization and based on an augmented Lagrangian developed effective and efficient two-timescale duplex neurodynamic systems for solving these problems with minimum spatial system complexity. To realize the second objective, we developed other high-performance multi-scale neurodynamic systems in the collaborative neurodynamic optimization framework for solving global, multi-objective, and combinatorial optimization problems. We theoretically analyzed various dynamic behaviors of the proposed neurodynamic systems and proved the multiple-stability, global synchronization, and almost-sure convergence of the neurodynamic models and systems. To realize the third objective, we applied the neurodynamic systems for problem-solving in many topic areas, such as vehicle-task assignment, vehicle tracking control, sparse and Boolean matrix factorization, supervised machine learning, supervised feature selection, hash bit selection, and financial portfolio selection.

11208517.label: Major findings and research outcome
11208517.value: The research was very fruitful and numerous results have been obtained in the project in terms of theory, methodology, and applications. Through extensive investigations, we found that properly designed multiscale neurodynamic systems have almost-sure global convergence properties and are able to solve many challenging optimization problems. We found that the two hyper-parameters in the collaborative neurodynamic algorithms can be selected based on Monte Carlo test results and the optimal hyper-parameters depend mainly on the efficiency of employed neurodynamic optimization models as well as the complexity and formulation of given problems. We found that employing the discrete Hopfield neural network and Boltzmann machine for scattered searches in addition to projection neural networks in the collaborative neurodynamic approaches can enhance their optimization capabilities. We also found that the multiscale neurodynamic systems are advantageous over many existing baselines in several application areas, such as vehicle motion planning and control, supervised feature selection and learning, and financial portfolio selection.

11208517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11208517.value: Many avenues are open for further investigations. From a system-theoretic viewpoint, the collaborative neurodynamic optimization approach can be extended for distributed global optimization in the presence of nonconvexity in objective function or constraints. Furthermore, from methodological perspectives, the multi-timescale neurodynamic approach could be extended for nonconvex-nonconcave minimax optimization and Nash equilibrium seeking in noncooperative games with expedited and almost-sure global convergence. In addition, from practical perspectives, the collaborative neurodynamic optimization methodology can play instrumental roles in many other operations/applications such as data processing (e.g., constrained clustering, bicriteria matrix factorization), machine learning (e.g., semi-supervised feature selection, sparse Bayesian learning, and neural ordinary differential equations), and energy system operation planning (e.g., chiller loading heating ventilation, and air-conditioning systems).

11208517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11208517.value: In this research project, we developed several neurobiologically and socially plausible dynamic systems. As brain-like computationally intelligent paradigms, neurodynamic optimization systems have been shown to be capable of solving for solving various complex optimization problems arising in numerous applications of robust control and supervised learning. This RGC-funded project was successfully completed and resulted in many publications that showcase the state of the art of neurodynamic optimization and selected applications. The multi-scale neurodynamic systems consist of multiple neural network models operating in two or more timescales. Because of the system state diversity in timescales and spatial locations, the neurodynamic systems are able to outperform existing methods in terms of solution quality or efficiency. Their efficacy and superiority have been demonstrated in several areas of applications, such as data processing, machine learning, marine vessel control, and financial investment decision-making.
