11208617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11208617.value: Polymeric materials have been increasingly used in in various fields of engineering and technology. Polystyrene (PS) is one of the most widely used polymers with its global annual consumption only second to that of polyethylene. Amongst its many applications, Expanded Polystyrene (EPS) as a solid foam possesses the unique combination of characteristics, like lightness, insulation properties, durability and an excellent processability. EPS is used in many applications such as buildings insulation, goods and food packaging, etc. In fact, as much as 70% of EPS products are used in building and construction applications. However, EPS, with its high porosity, is notoriously known to be easily ignitable and highly flammable due to its foam structure. In building fires, when ignited, the EPS burns with fast propagation of flame, rapid heat release, high smoke yield and adverse obscuration which impair escapes of building occupants and rescue operations of fire brigades causing injuries and fatalities. In the past decade, several serious fire incidents involving rapid flame spread and burning of building facades insulations which resulted in serious casualties and billions of property losses were reported in major cities of China and Australia, etc. Recently, advancements have been made to develop carbon nanotubes (CNT) flame retardant polystyrene matrix nanocomposites. Research studies revealed that such flame-retardant technique improves significantly its fire retardancy, environmental-friendliness; and promotes char formation, etc. However, they are still ignitable, flammable and therefore combustible. The potential fire hazard of using this new material in buildings remains to be a key concern causing global attention by fire researchers, government authorities, building designers, occupants and owners, locally in Hong Kong and internationally. In this research, a state-of-the-art, comprehensive and robust fire field model based on computational fluid dynamics techniques will be developed for the new Carbon Nanotubes Flame Retardant Expanded Polystyrene Foam (CNT-EPS) for understanding and predicting its fire characteristics and performances for full-scale applications in buildings with particular focus on its pyrolysis due to high porosity, heat and smoke productions from its burning. The fire field model will be validated by standard fire experimental results from both cone calorimeter and ISO room for tests. The outcomes of this research will contribute to make a significant impact to the performance-based fire engineering designs in buildings. The established fire field model and the associated methodology can be generalized to form a framework for fire behaviors and performances understanding and prediction of other flame-retardant polymer nanocomposites foam materials. 高分子材料已廣泛應用於工程技術的各個領域。 聚苯乙烯(PS)是一種應用極為廣泛的聚合物,其全球年消費量僅次於聚乙烯。 在眾多應用中,可發性聚苯乙烯(EPS)作為固體泡沫具有獨特的性質,如輕質、絕緣、耐久性和優良的加工性。 EPS已廣泛應用於建築保溫、貨物、食品包裝等領域,實際應用中有多達70%的EPS產品用於建築和建築工程。 然而,由於其泡沫結構和較高的孔隙率,EPS易於燃燒,且具有高度燃燒性。 在建築火災中,EPS一旦被引燃,便開始迅速燃燒和蔓延,產生大量熱釋放和煙氣,造成大量居民和救援消防部隊傷亡。 在過去的十年中,中國和澳大利亞等大城市都報導了一些嚴重的火災事件,這些火災都是由於建築外立面的絕緣材料被引燃所致,造成了嚴重的人員傷亡,財產損失達數十億美元。 近年來,碳納米管(CNT)阻燃聚苯乙烯納米複合材料取得了一定的進展。 研究表明,這種阻燃技術不僅具有環境友好性,而且顯著提高了聚苯乙烯的阻燃性,並能夠促進焦炭的形成。 然而,它們仍然是可燃、易燃的。 這種新材料應用在建築中的火災隱患仍然是一個關鍵問題,已引起香港和其他國際地區的消防人員、政府機關、建築設計師、住戶和業主的密切關注。 本專案基於計算流體力學技術,研究發展一項綜合特性先進的火運動場模型,用於預測全尺寸應用在建築上的碳納米管阻燃聚苯乙烯泡沫(CNT-EPS)的火災熱性,重點關注其高孔隙率所引發的熱解、燃燒熱釋放和煙氣變化規律。 火運動場模型將由錐形量熱儀和符合ISO標準的火災試驗結果進行驗證。 本專案的研究成果將對建築性能化和消防工程設計產生重大影響。 此外,所建立的火運動場模型和相關的方法可以形成一個研究體系,推廣到其他阻燃聚合物納米複合泡沫材料火災行為和特性的預測中。

11208617.label: Realisation of objectives
11208617.value: Objective 1: Develop a pyrolysis model for porous CNT-EPS incorporating contraction, phase conversion, pyrolysis and char formation due to fires In our development of the fire model for the CNT-EPS, pyrolysis of CNT-EPS involving the complicated coupled chemical and physical processes in the foam and molten phase, has been modelled by a 3-D pyrolysis model considering fully the melting of the foam to molten phase, their properties and the corresponding thermal decomposition of CNT-EPS to give emission of combustible volatile gases and the regression molten surface. 1.1 Establishment of CNT-EPS pyrolysis model The energy conservation equation with heat conduction according to Fourier’s law and convection due to internal movement of volatile gases was formulated. Full account was given to changes of densities of CNT-EPS, heat of conversion from foam to molten phase, mass losses of molten CNT-EPS, heat of pyrolysis, internal heat transfer due to conduction through the highly porous foam and molten phase and emission of the volatile gases at the surface, etc. The pyrolysis reactions of CNT-EPS were modelled by multiple Arrhenius expressions with the pre-exponential factors and activation energies to be obtained in TGA and DTG analysis in tasks relating to Objective 2. Thermal properties of the pyrolysing porous solid such as thermal conductivities and heat capacities were represented by functions of foam porosity and molten phase as well as char densities and temperature. Volatile gases were in thermal equilibrium with the foam or molten phase, respectively. Convection and radiation heat transfer at interface of CNT-EPS and gaseous combustion domains were exchanged as boundary conditions. Given the high porosity of CNT-EPS, migration of pyrolysis gaseous products to the surface of the porous CNT-EPS was assumed to be instantaneous and obtained by integration of local quantities over the pyrolysing zone. Surface regression of CNT-EPS as a result of the softening, contraction and mass loss due to pyrolysis was tracked. The CNT-EPS pyrolysis model was successfully established. 1.2 Development of CNT-EPS pyrolysis computational code The pyrolysis model for porous CNT-EPS was discretized with finite volume techniques to give a set of simultaneous linear discretised equations numerical implementation. A computational code for the pyrolysis model of the porous CNT-EPS was developed. The developed pyrolysis model and its completed code were coupled with gaseous combustion computational model to form a comprehensive fire field model for burning of porous CNT-EPS in this research project. Objective 2: Establish key kinetics for the pyrolysis model for CNT-EPS For the establishment and development of pyrolysis model of porous CNT-EPS, experimentations to observe the mass loss (i.e. pyrolysis kinetics), volatile decomposition products and solid residue were considered to be essential. These results were crucial to the comprehensive qualitative and quantitative understanding of the pyrolysis mechanism. 2.1 TGA tests Mass loss behavior was evaluated through Thermogravimetric Analysis (TGA) in which changes in physical and chemical properties of materials were measured as a function of increasing temperature with time. The CNT-EPS samples ranging from 0% to 1% CNT in PS covering the most effective synergistic flame retardant range were synthesized. A total of 20 of TGA experiments for these samples, with various rates of temperature rises from 5 to 20 K/min, were carried out (5 no. of CNT % x 4 no. of temp. rise). Each test case was repeated to ensure reproducibility and credibility. The Derivative Thermogravimetry (DTG) data were calculated from TGA curves to obtain the pre-exponential factors and activation energies for respective multiple Arrhenius expressions for the pyrolysis of the porous CNT-EPS. 2.2 TGA-FTIR and GC-MS tests Volatile decomposition products were studied using TGA coupled with the Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) (TGA-FTIR) and Gas Chromatography-Mass Spectrometer (GC-MS). These techniques have been useful tools for dynamical analysis as continuous monitoring of both the time-dependent evolution of the gases and the weight of the residue was achieved. A standard temperature rise rate of 10 K/min was used for the TGA-FTIR tests for all samples. 5 no. of porous CNT-EPS samples with 0-1% CNT were tested. Each test case was repeated to ensure reproducibility and credibility. 2.3 SEM, XRD, FTIR and XPS tests A variety of measurements including Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM), X-ray Diffraction (XRD), FTIR, X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscope (XPS) and Raman Spectrometer had been performed to investigate the morphology, structure and composition of the char for further confirmation of pyrolysis mechanism of porous CNT-EPS. Objective 3: Develop a robust fire field model comprising pyrolysis of porous CNT-EPS and its gas-phase combustion models. For the gaseous combustion, the turbulent-buoyant flow field of a fire was modelled with Large-Eddy Simulation (LES) incorporating models for combustion by detailed chemical reactions, soot formation and radiation. 3.1 Formulating fire field model for CNT-EPS The 3-D Favre-filtered conservation equations for mass, energy, momentum, mixture fractions and their scalar variances had been formulated with the turbulent closure by Smagorinsky subgrid-scale (SGS) turbulence model. The SGS based combustion model was established with the assumption that the rates of chemical reactions were faster than the mixing rate of reactants. The mixture fraction as the chosen conserved scalar was describe the mixing where the instantaneous concentrations of species were given by functions of merely the instantaneous conserved scalar. The Probability Density Function of the mixture fraction was adopted. Relationships between the mixture fraction and thermochemical scalar properties were obtained from experimental correlations in which key combustion gaseous species concentrations was a function of the mixture fraction but not the dissipation rate of the scalar. In the combustion model, the Detailed Reaction mechanisms for the chemical processes were employed to track down the concentrations of reactants such as CO, CO2 and hydrocarbons by-products including most importantly acetylene C2H2, which was the main incipient for soot formation through nucleation and surface growth processes. The soot model fully embraced the key physical processes including the inception, coagulation, surface growth and oxidation of soot particles. The rate of production of soot was governed essentially by the effects of turbulent advection in large-scale, turbulent diffusion by SGS, and finite-rate chemistry of soot. For radiation heat transfer, soot and other combustion products were considered as non-scattering gray gas. The thermal radiation was modeled with the Filtered Radiative Transfer Equations with the Discrete Ordinates Method and S4 approximation for better computational efficiency. The fire field model for CNT-EPS had been formulated for the further development of the computation code below. 3.2 Developing fire modeling computational code for CNT-EPS In this study, the Favre-filtered conservation equations were discretized using the Finite-Volume approach. To enhance numerical accuracies, second-order central differences were used for all spatial derivatives. The two-stage predictor-corrector scheme for compressible flows with low-Mach-number was implemented numerically. The simultaneous discretization equations were solved using the Preconditioned Conjugate Gradient method (PCG). The physical and theoretical models for pyrolysis and gaseous combustion were coupled to form the 3-D Fire Model for burning of the CNT-EPS (LESFR3D). A computational code had been developed for the performing simulations using Linux-based high-performance computational clusters. Since CNT-EPS only consist of a very small amount of CNT, the combustible volatiles during burning were mainly derivatives from styrene monomer where the gaseous kinetic data was readily available in literatures and chemical handbooks as well as the CHEMKIN. The fire modelling computational code for CNT-EPS had been successful developed.

11208617.label: Major findings and research outcome
11208617.value: Recently, Expanded polystyrene (EPS) incorporating carbon nanotubes (CNTs) to form Carbon Nanotubes Flame Retardant Expanded Polystyrene Nanocomposites Foam (CNT-EPS) were reported to have significantly improved its flame retardancy to greatly reducing its potential of causing fire hazards. In this research, the key issues relating to how the CNT-EPS would perform in a real fire scenarios and how much contributions they made to fire propagation had been studied. While full-scale fire experiments to simulate real situations may be used to assess the fire behavior and performance of the combustible materials, they are destructive and extremely expensive and non-environmental friendly. The development of a robust, effective fire field model of flame-retarded materials to address the needs of fire safety assessments is crucial and will be definitely contributory. In this research a new fire field model based on computation fluid dynamic (CFD) with full coupling of the newly developing pyrolysis model for porous CNT-EPS and the corresponding combustion model incorporating detailed chemistry and soot modeling had been developed. The fire model could be further validated by standard fire experimental results in both cone calorimeter and ISO room for tests in the future. This model can provide an alternative possible for use as a design tool for building fire safety engineering design and assessment. The key research outcomes achieved in this research are as follows: 1. Pyrolysis model for porous CNT-EPS with full considerations of thermal-decomposition of CNT-EPS including contraction, phase conversion, pyrolysis and char formation during fires had been developed. 2. Key kinetics required for the pyrolysis model will be obtained via various laboratory scale analysis had been obtained. 3. Robust fire field model comprising pyrolysis and gas-phase combustion models had been developed.

11208617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11208617.value: The new fire field models for CNT-EPS based on CFD techniques can be potentially a generalized engineering approach for assessment of fire behaviors and performance of flame- retardant polymers. This may provide a significant, effective design tool for building fire safety engineering design and assessment flame-retarded materials in building fires while experimental assessments are always extremely expensive, destructive and often impossible due to many practical constraints. To fully validate and confirm the robustness of this new fire field model, it is proposed to perform fire tests and to validate fire field model predictions with experimental results. For example, CNT-EPS samples can be prepared and tested in the ASTM Cone Calorimeter at various irradiation conditions. Also, full-scale fire experiments in an ISO 9705 standard room with a sheet of porous CNT-EPS placed either at the back or one side of the room can be performed. The temperature measurements in these room fire tests can be used to further validate the developed fire field model of the porous CNT-EPS by comparison of the numerical predictions with video images of flame and smoke development to confirm the quality of the developed model.

11208817.value: 室內使用者的活動會顯著影響建築能耗。前人的研究表明，基於室內空間佔用情況的控制設定能大大節省建築空調系統的能耗（多達56%）。室內空間佔用的信息同時也可以用來預測建築能耗（或空調負荷），但是由於監測技術受制於傳感器的漂移，精度不高，質量差，侵入性，使用的變化，調試不足以及隱私性的問題等，目前仍然較難達到較精確和可靠的室內空間佔用監測。最近開發的傳感器融合技術通過不同傳感器的最顯著特徵來達到控制誤差的目的，可以實現更精確的室內空間佔用估算。該技術可以作為現有傳感器網絡的有效補充，並可用於建築系統的控制和監控，也可用於基於室內空間佔用信息的能耗預測。目前，冗餘傳感器以及多環境傳感器的組合已被用於實驗來實現多傳感器融合的算法。非環境傳感器，如可穿戴傳感器和基於信息通信技術（ICT）的傳感器也已被用於研究。因此可以推測，建築中基於室內空間佔用監測的多傳感器融合算法將能夠實現更有效的建築系統的控制和操作，並提供了一種實現建築能耗預測的替代方法。 本研究的目的是開發一種基於虛擬空間佔用監測模型（VOS）的數據融合算法，用於建築內空間佔用信息的估算。本研究將評估VOS模型在預測系統能耗，提高基於PI（比例-積分）控制的定風量（CAV）空調系統的熱舒適性和能效方面的有效性。其中，室內使用空間的電力需求，攝像機的視覺信息和Wi-Fi連接信息將用來構建VOS模型。在建築物中，上述所需的三種信息都較容易獲得或已經具有，所需的傳感器也易於安裝和更換，價格相對便宜，不易受傳感器漂移的影響，或即使有漂移問題也容易及時發現，並且不容易受到室內環境變化的影響。處理VOS模型的數據並不復雜，使得VOS模型可以適應長期的傳感器漂移。本研究計劃採用建築中現有的傳感器，因此實際的監測不會對建築內的隱私狀況產生不利影響。VOS模型的測試將在面積為135平方米的研究人員辦公室中進行。其中，室內使用空間的電力需求信息會由建築物電力監控系統來記錄，視覺信息將由已經安裝在測試辦公室的監控攝像機取得，Wi-Fi連接信息將從現有的Wi-Fi路由器中提取。基於遺傳算法的相關性特徵選擇（CFS）分類器將被用來估計室內空間佔用的特徵的最佳組合。真實的室內空間佔用信息將從工作空間的出入控制系統中獲取，並用來構建CFS分類器，從而研究多種特徵組合，並判斷哪些特徵對於某些特定條件更為適合。此外，一個25個座位的教室會用來評估VOS模型在空調製冷需求預測中的有效性，會採用基於人工神經網絡（ANN）的模擬方法來檢驗各種輸入參數組合的冷負荷預測精度，所構建的冷負荷預測模型的性能會與其他公佈的冷負荷預測模型的性能進行比較。另外，也將評估基於VOS模型的定風量空調系統PI控制的熱舒適性和能效方面的有效性。所構建的VOS模型將直接用於自適應ANN模型中，用來調整定風量系統PI控制的增益。這種直接自適應ANN算法具有“先學習- 後控制”的特徵，反饋控制可以通過期望輸出和實際輸出之間的差異來更新ANN的權值，而對系統先驗模型的鬆弛使得控制器在設計和實現方面具有靈活性。特別地是，本研究會進行詳細的研究以確定估算增益的安全範圍，以確保控制系統的穩定性和魯棒性，同時將檢驗適當的控制更新間隔，以確保控制系統快速和穩定的運作。

11208817.label: Realisation of objectives
11208817.value: Introduction The operating efficiency of heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) system is critical for building energy performance. Demand-based control is an efficient HVAC operating strategy, which can provide an appropriate level of HVAC services based on the recognition of actual cooling “demand.” The cooling demand primarily relies on the accurate detection of occupancy. The current researches of demand-based HVAC control tend to detect the occupant count using cameras or other sensors, which often impose high computation and costs with limited real-life applications. Instead of detecting the occupant count, this study proposes to detect the occupancy density. There are two approaches: by using computer vision and by Wi-Fi connection counts. Computer Vision Approach The occupancy density can be estimated by image foreground moving pixels captured with computer vision, together with the indoor and outdoor information (acquired from existing sensors) which are then used as inputs to an artificial neural network model for cooling demand estimation. Experiments have been implemented in a university design studio. Instead of detecting the occupant count, this study detects the occupancy density for estimating the cooling demand. Results show that, by adding the occupancy density, the cooling demand estimation error is greatly reduced by 67.4% and the R value is improved from 0.75 to 0.96. The proposed approach also features low-cost, computationally efficient, privacy-friendly and easily implementable. It shows good application potentials and can be readily incorporated into existing building management systems for improving energy efficiency. The pixel-based method (i.e., adaptive GMM) is used to extract the foreground moving pixels as a representation of occupancy density. It is demonstrated that the use of the proposed approach in representing occupancy density is very suitable for cooling demand estimation as it represents both the occupants’ number and activity levels (or metabolic rate) that contribute to the cooling demand. The proposed sensing approach also has several practical values: (1) surveillance-level cameras can be used, which saves cost and improves the applicability; (2) since the computation requirement is not demanding, a MCU can be used, that can save cost and minimize the privacy concerns. The proposed sensing approach can be easily employed into the existing BMS and the real-time cooling demand information can be used in various aspects, such as enhancing thermal comfort, saving energy, controlling outdoor air flow and applying in demand-based control/optimization. Future works will focus on the demand-based control and zone-level indoor environment management to enhance the operating efficiency and thermal comfort of the building cooling systems. Occupancy Estimation by Wi-Fi Connection Counts Many occupancy detection methods have been developed either based on physical sensors, cameras or information & communication technology (ICT). Wi-Fi based detection is one of the ICTs that uses Wi-Fi signals (e.g. from smartphones) to represent occupants. Nowadays, new smartphone models all have the battery-saving function that will switch off Wi-Fi communication in the idle mode, causing significant detection uncertainties. This challenge has not been addressed in the current Wi-Fi based occupancy detection methods that still assume or manipulate a continuous Wi-Fi communication. Moreover, most studies are conducted in relatively simple settings with small-scale occupancy that are far from a complex indoor space. Thus, this study investigates the Wi-Fi based occupancy detection in a complex indoor space with large occupancy. This study reveals the practical challenges when applying the Wi-Fi based occupancy detection in real-life complex environment. The discontinuous Wi-Fi communication of smartphones presents a practical challenge in occupancy detection. Outside and non-human Wi-Fi devices may also bring in irrelevant or unwanted Wi-Fi communications. To tackle these challenges, an event-triggered updating method is proposed to handle the discontinuous Wi-Fi communication. A location filter is developed based on a calibrated RSS value to exclude the outside Wi-Fi devices. A MAC address filter is developed based on operation characteristics of non-human devices to screen out Wi-Fi enabled stationary equipment. One-week experiment has been conducted in a university lecture theater to verify the proposed method. Experimental results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed even triggered updating method in handling the discontinuous Wi-Fi communication. The developed filters are also effective in excluding outside and non-human Wi-Fi devices. Comparing with the conventional Wi-Fi based periodic updating method, the average detection accuracy improves from 77.3% to 96.8%. The proposed Wi-Fi based event-triggered updating method can be applied to Wi-Fi networks of new or existing buildings with minimum cost regardless of the Wi-Fi communication continuity. This study reveals that the event-triggered Wi-Fi based occupancy detection approach is effective when applying to institutional or university buildings. The practicality of the proposed Wi-Fi based detection method in other building usages or room occupancy behaviors should be further investigated. Since Wi-Fi only may not handle every complicated scenario, the proposed method can be integrated into a data fusion approach to enhance the detection reliability and accuracy.

11208817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11208817.value: Studies have revealed that by using occupancy-driven HVAC operation, HVAC systems can reduce energy consumption by as much as 56%. Occupancy level is also useful for the prediction of a building’s energy demand and is a contributing factor in building energy usage analysis. In fact many research studies have been conducted in recent years on how to develop a robust and reliable occupancy estimation system for use in buildings. Having aware of these developments, this study aims at developing a Virtual Occupancy Sensors (VOS) based on data fusion algorithm for occupancy estimation in an office, which will be useful for building system operation & control, energy demand prediction and energy usage analysis. Visual information from video camera and Wi-Fi connection profile are selected as proxies to represent office occupancy for the VOS. Unlike previous studies that mostly use secondary measures to represent occupancy, such as temperature, humidity and CO2 concentration, the proxies used in this study give a more direct representation of occupancy in an office. This information is also readily obtainable from typical building systems of both new and old buildings. The proposed VOS can be integrated into the existing building control systems of both new and old office buildings. It can supplement existing temperature/humidity/CO2 sensors for building system controls and operation, for conducting occupancy based energy usage analysis, and for the prediction of the energy demand in a building equipped with a real-time demand side management system.

11208917.value: Design a PPTR scheme that supports multi-requesters and multi-workers (M2M) crowdsourcing with keyword equality matching. The crowdsourcing systems should be able to support multiple requesters to publish tasks and multiple workers to subscribe crowdsourced tasks. Starting with the keyword equality matching, this task focuses on developing a new framework that achieves privacy-preserving while enabling M2M task matching. Design a PPTR scheme that supports efficient numeric range matching for M2M crowdsourcing. Task requirements are not limited to be expressed in keywords. They are often expressed in numeric ranges, such as a worker whose age should be ≥ 18 and who is currently within 1km from a specific location. The aim of this task is to develop a PPTR scheme that supports task matching where task requirements may contain ranges of numeric values, sometimes the range of locations. Design a PPTR scheme that supports complex structures of range and keyword matching for M2M crowdsourcing. In crowdsourcing systems, both task requirements and worker interests may be expressed in complex structures, such as multi-dimensional ranges or the (t, n)-threshold gates. The aim of this task is to design a PPTR scheme that supports matching between task requirements and worker interests that are expressed in complex structures.

11208917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11208917.value: Crowdsourcing is an emerging technology that enables task-requesters (called requesters) to outsource tasks to a large group of undefined people (called workers). As the ever increasing number of tasks that are call-for-workers, workers can no longer manually select their interested tasks. A public server (called broker) is introduced to facilitate the auto-matching of tasks with their potential workers. The broker is usually deployed in a public cloud due to the intensive computing and storage resources it needs. Information security and privacy becomes an important concern in this public crowdsourcing platform. Task requesters do not want to leak out any information about tasks to the broker, and the workers also do not want reveal any information about their personal interests to the broker. The primary goal of this project is to develop a Privacy-Preserving Task Recommendation (PPTR) scheme that can protect the privacy of both requesters and workers against the broker, while still enables the broker to perform matching between task requirements and worker interests. The project consists of three tasks: 1) Design a PPTR scheme that supports Multi-requesters and Multi-workers (M2M) crowdsourcing with keyword equality matching. The crowdsourcing systems should be able to support multiple requesters to publish tasks and multiple workers to subscribe crowdsourced tasks. 2) Design a PPTR scheme that supports efficient numeric range matching for M2M crowdsourcing. This task aims to develop a PPTR scheme that supports task matching where task requirements may contain ranges of numeric values. 3) Design a PPTR scheme that supports complex structures of range and keyword matching for M2M crowdsourcing. 众包是一种新兴的技术，能让任务请求者（请求者）将其任务外包给一大群非特定的用户（工作者）。面对日益增涨的任务数量，工作者再也无法手动地挑选出他们感兴趣的任务。进而引入一个公共服务器作为代理，以实现对任务和潜在工作者的自动匹配。鉴于对计算资源和存储资源的大量需求，代理通常部署在公有云上。对于这一公共的众包平台, 信息的安全和隐私从而备受关注。请求者不愿意泄露任务信息给代理，并且工作者也不愿向代理透露他们的个人兴趣。该项目的首要目标是设计一种隐私保护任务推荐方案，在保护请求者和工作者双方隐私的前提下，代理仍然能够对任务要求和工作者兴趣进行匹配。 该项目包括三个任务： （1）设计一种隐私保护任务推荐方案，其能在多请求者和多工作者的众包环境下支持基于关键词的相等匹配。该众包系统中需要同时支持多个请求者发布任务和多个工作者订阅任务。 （2）设计一种隐私保护任务推荐方案，其能在多请求者和多工作者的众包环境下支持基于数值的范围匹配。 （3）设计一种隐私保护任务推荐方案, 其能在多请求者和多工作者的众包环境下支持基于范围和关键词的结构匹配。

11208917.label: Realisation of objectives
11208917.value: All project objectives are fully realized. 1) We proposed a suite of privacy-preserving task matching schemes in crowdsourcing, including the schemes for multi-requesters (task owners) and multi-workers (users) scenario, with anonymity, Sybil attack-resistance, and the situation without using proxy servers. 2) We developed efficient matching scheme that support range queries. A particular system we developed is the online ride hailing system that allows a rider to find the nearby taxies without revealing the location of both the rider and the drivers (called pRide). 3) We also developed a federated privacy-preserving crowdsourcing platform that allows task-owners to publish tasks over multiple crowdsource servers and users (workers) to search their matched tasks across multiple servers. Since different servers have different data format and security requirements and trust, we need to deal with issues with heterogenous security formats and to ensure the system is trustable to all task owners and users .

11208917.label: Major findings and research outcome
11208917.value: 1) developed a general framework of privacy-preserving task matching for multi-tasks and multi-users in crowdsourcing, and proved the security features of the framework. We also proposed an efficient encrypted search scheme for multi-owner (task owners) and multi-users scenarios. The work is published in ICC 2021 (Mingyue) and IEEE Internet of Things, 2018. 2) proposed a privacy preserving task matching for spatial range queries (with numerical ranges) for crowdsourcing environment. The work was published in Journal of Network and Computer Applications, Volume 123, 1 December 2018. 3) developed a protocol that allows expressive task subscription in privacy-preserving crowdsourcing system with detection of Sybil nodes. Sybil attacks are a major problem in crowdsourcing systems and it’s difficult to detect Sybil nodes in a privacy-preserving setting. This work was published in IEEE Internet of Things, 2019. 4) proposed an algorithm of privacy-preserving task matching with efficient revocation of crowdsourcing. In crowdsourcing systems, workers often join or leave. It’s always a difficult issue for a protocol that can revoke the users’ attributes who already left the system. Our proposed algorithm successfully addressed this issue and solved it efficiently. This work was accepted for publication in IEEE Trans on Dependable and Secure Computing. 5) developed a federated privacy-preserving crowdsourcing platform that allows task-owners to publish tasks over multiple crowdsource servers and users (workers) to search their matched tasks across multiple servers. We also employ the differential privacy technique to protect the privacy when releasing results to users (Lu Ou 2022). 6) developed a privacy-preserving online ride hailing system that allows a rider to find the nearby taxies without revealing the location of both the rider and the drivers (PSRide). We also developed an accurate road map building system by crowdsourcing on-road vehicles (Jiangang Shu 2022)

11209217.label: Realisation of objectives
11209217.value: • To ameliorate the calculation procedures for estimating interior daylight illuminance in a convenient manner Estimation of internal daylight availability is the key step in evaluating various daylighting schemes. In many urban cities, most of the building developments are high-rise and are constructed in densely built regions. The external obstructions may significantly reduce the amount of daylight entering to the indoor space. On contrary, rooms at the top floors facing unobstructed skies can cause excessive penetration of solar radiation and daylight into interior spaces leading to thermal and visual glare and increasing the cooling load. Simple computer programs would be helpful for architects and non-lighting experts at initial architectural and building envelope layout phase when various design schemes and ideas are being evaluated and expounded. Full scale simulation using sophisticated computer packages would be made to obtain more accurate results only when the design proposals have been finalized and ready for submission. A manual calculation approach for estimating the sky component and externally reflected component at the indoor points facing different obstruction environments under the 15 CIE Standard Skies was established. Such technique is useful for college students who are required to learn the basic daylighting calculations in their formal lectures when various schemes and concepts are being considered. It is expected the theories and procedures developed in this study can be used to other places with similar high-rise urban developments. Shading devices are required to lower the cooling demand, eliminate discomfort glare and improve daylight distribution for rooms facing unobstructed skies. External shading devices would be appropriate for designing building facades with lower energy use and better daylight quality. A number of figures showing the obstructed vertical sky components at various scattering angles with overhang, side-fin and recessed window under CIE overcast, partly cloudy and clear skies were depicted. The findings give a convenient alternative to determine the vertical daylight availability under various shading devices. A simple computer program for simulating the internal daylight under the 15 CIE Standard Skies was developed. The software was evaluated against the computed data using an advanced computer program and the field-measurement readings. In view of the user-friendly features, short time periods for running simulations and the reasonably good predictable ability of the proposed computer program, it would be very useful employing the simple software at various building design, construction and operation stage when approximate daylight performance under various standard sky conditions is required. • To formulate new daylight metrics and simple principles for the DF, ADF and VDF The conventional method for calculating the interior daylight is the daylight factor approach (DFA) which can be logically computed via simple calculation tools without the use of daylight data. Point daylight factors (PDF) are related to the electric lighting energy reduction from the daylight-linked lighting controls. The average daylight factor (ADF) correlates with window area and visual transmittance which could be varied easily to meet the standard. The vertical daylight factor (VDF) has been appropriately used for compact city regions with vast external obstructions. Such DFAs have acquired preference due to their simplicity but they are not flexible to estimate the dynamic daylight changes due to the movement of the sun under non-overcast skies. Nonetheless, practitioners have been customary to using the daylight specifications given in terms of DFs, which has been widely employed as building standards and codes in many places. Recently, DF calculations have been extended to the 15 CIE Standard Skies considering building directions, solar positions and effects due to direct and reflected sunlight and skylight. Calculation steps for VDF, ADF and PDF under the 15 unobstructed CIE Standard Skies were demonstrated. They are either models previously proposed by other well-known researchers or the PI previous works. The design tools were presented for computing PDF, VDF and ADF. Under unobstructed skies, a mean VDF of around 54% would be appropriately employed in architecture and daylighting designs. For estimating ADF, the visual transmittance and window area could be varied to meet the criteria. By multiplying the PDFs with the corresponding horizontal diffuse illuminance (EHD), the daylight illuminance at the interior points (PDI) can be obtained for analyzing the daylight-linked closed-loop lighting controls. The correlations among the various DFs were established. The VDF can be found from measured vertical diffuse illuminance and EHD. Once VDFs have been obtained, the corresponding ADFs can be determined. The SC for an indoor reference point can be predicted from the corresponding VDF using the configuration factor principle. The findings are useful to daylight linked open-loop lighting controls. ADF can be difficult to obtain but PDI can be recorded so that the PDF and then the ADF can be computed via their correlations. Further, the required Daylight Glare Possibility and Daylight Uniformity could be obtained by varying the room parameters, which are the key factors in ADF and PDF formulations. • To apply the proposed calculation tools and daylight metrics to architectural and daylighting designs Long urban canyons are the main skyline features of most urban environments and the opposite buildings are commonly evaluated based on an infinitely-long continuous horizontal band. However, the obstructions may always be irregular in actual cases. Under non-overcast skies the estimation of vertical sky-diffuse component (VSC) can be a crucial issue when the vertical planes were partly obstructed by the opposite buildings. The obstructed VSCs under irregular skyline patterns for various CIE Standard Skies were examined. The irregular skyline patterns were quantified by dividing the possible obstructed zone using several azimuth and vertical angles. Strong correlations between the angles defining the irregular skyline patterns and the corresponding upper obstruction angles αU under infinite-long canyons were mapped by both an ANN model and a simple regression model. The findings are significant for predicting the vertical solar irradiance and daylight illuminance for various applications such as renewable energy and daylighting designs. There are a number of rules of thumb and design metrics to predict the daylight performance. Traditionally, DF is the long-term use design metric but it is independent of time, non-overcast skies and window orientation. Large DF only indicates well daylit space and daytime electric lighting is seldom required. Visual discomfort, however, cannot be identified. Recently, climate-based daylight metrics (CBDMs) such as daylight autonomy (DA) and useful daylight illuminance (UDI) are employed for providing further information on the different daylight conditions throughout the year. Such daylighting metrics give a significant functional account of authentic daylighting environments, which are appropriate for evaluating visual comfort and daylight-linked lighting control systems. Nonetheless, the CBDMs need representative annual daylight data which may not be easily obtainable for many places. Even though the long-term daylight parameters are reachable, such data may not show the up-to-date daylighting criteria and situations. To obtain accurate results, lighting simulations are often required. However, a full-scale computer simulation can be costly in modelling the building geometry with a long simulation period. The schedules adopted are substantially affected the simulated results to meet the CBDMs criteria. The PDI can be obtained by multiplying the PDF and the corresponding EHD. The outcomes can be used for estimating the UDI and DAs which can be correlated with traditional DFs for buildings facing different directions. The performance of daylight-linked lighting controls and daylight glare were evaluated with different target illuminance settings.

11209217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11209217.value: The reflectance of various shading devices under the 15 CIE Standard Skies should be further considered and simple regression equations should be formed. To compute the vertical sky component under irregular skyline shapes, more complex patterns with refined subdivision of the obstructed zones can be extended. The theories and procedures developed for estimating the sky and externally reflected components can be applied to other places with similar high-rise urban developments. Simple correlations between PDF, ADF and VDF have been established. Open-loop daylight linked controls will be carried out. New daylight metrics and simple rules-of-thumb in terms of ADF, PDF and VDF will be formulated. Moreover, DFs correlations with various dynamic daylight metrics such as UDI and DA will be modeled. The effects of other room parameters including window orientations and surface reflectance related to daylight metrics will be analyzed. In addition, studies of different visual comfort variables, for instances, the daylight glare possibility and daylight uniformity will be undertaken. The analytical studies, a serious of computer simulations and small- and full-scale field measurements will be applied to verify the outcomes. Subsequent research studies to correlate the three types of DFs under obstructed (i.e. lower floors) all-sky conditions will be conducted.

11209217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11209217.value: Interior daylight illuminance is often computed using the daylight factor (DF) approach with estimations of the traditional overcast sky. Daylight criteria are usually expressed in the DF approach, which is used in many countries. In Hong Kong, the vertical DF is used to specify the daylighting performance of buildings. However, such DF methods do not consider the dynamic variations in daylight illuminance when the sun’s location varies and the sky becomes non-overcast. It cannot consider realistic or time-varying climatic conditions, thus daylight glare indices cannot be accurately determined. Recently, the International Commission on illumination (CIE) adopted a range of 15 standard model representing actual sky conditions. The associated mathematical expressions can be rather complex for non-overcast skies, which strongly depend on the sun’s position. Practitioners welcome simple design tools produced through comprehensive analysis. Some simplified methods of estimating daylight illuminance for rooms facing various environments under the 15 CIE Standard Skies have been developed. The proposed project aim to ameliorate the simple calculation tools for interior daylight illuminance and formulate design metrics for daylighting under the various CIE standard skies. The findings should be globally adopted and useful to practitioners engaged in visual comfort, fenestration and daylighting design and evaluation.

11209317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11209317.value: Secondary relaxation, also called beta relaxation, is a prominent phenomenon of local stress relaxation in glassy solids which can be correlated with materials’ mechanical and physical properties. Such correlations are of great importance to the engineering/functional applications of glassy solids, which have been long established for molecular glasses, such as polymeric glasses, but just began to be understood for atomic glasses, such as metallic glasses. In the recent works, people reported that some metallic glasses could exhibit a slow secondary relaxation mode at a temperature above the room temperature. In contrast to the slow secondary relaxation early reported, we recently discovered a “fast” secondary relaxation mode, which possesses a much lower activation energy, a faster relaxation time and less compositional dependence. Our preliminary results indicate that the fast secondary relaxation is universal to a variety of metallic-glass compositions and correlated very well with anelasticity. Interestingly, we found that these fast secondary relaxations are also correlated with shear band initiation. Based on these previous works and our new findings, we herein propose a joint research to perform a systematic study for a thorough understanding of the physical/structural origin of the fast secondary relaxation and its connection with the slow secondary relaxation in metallic glasses. In addition, the correlations between the fast secondary relaxation and fracture toughness of metallic glasses will be studied. For the three-year project, we would focus on the Zr-based and Fe-based metallic glass as the two model systems for the normal and soft-magnetic metallic glasses, respectively. Once the proposal is implemented successfully, the following two goals will be achieved: (1) establishing the constitutive relations between the beta relaxations and mechanical properties of normal and soft magnetic metallic glasses, and (2) developing the processing routes that entail multi-field (thermal, mechanical, electric) interactions to tune beta relaxations and thus to optimize the mechanical properties of metallic glasses. 二次弛豫是玻璃態物由於質動態不均性在外場作用下所表現出的一種局部能量耗散的物理現象。最近的發現表明原子尺度下的玻璃，比如金屬玻璃，可以在低溫下表現出獨特的二次弛豫現象。本項研究旨在通過實驗和模擬來揭示二次弛豫在金屬玻璃中的動力學起源，已達到調製二次弛豫并優化金屬玻璃的力學性能的目的。

11209317.label: Realisation of objectives
11209317.value: 1. Understanding the physical origin of the fast beta relaxation and its connection with the slow beta relaxation in the Zr-based metallic glasses We systematically investigated the relaxation behavior of a model metallic glass (MG) based on the extensive molecular dynamics (MD) simulations combined with the dynamic mechanical spectroscopy method, and discovered a pronounced ultra-low temperature peak on the loss modulus spectrum for the first time in MD simulations. Notably, the relaxation peak occurs at a much lower temperature than the typical temperature for the conventional β relation peak as reported in the literature. According to the atomic displacement analysis, we unravel that the reversible atomic motions, rather than the thermal vibrations or local structural rearrangements, mainly contribute to this relaxation peak. We further identify the atomic level mechanism of this fast relaxation process by characterizing the local geometrical anisotropy. Furthermore, by tracing the dynamic behaviors of these “reversible” atoms, we demonstrate the intrinsic hierarchy of the relaxation modes, which are triggered by atomic vibrations and gradually developed to include the reversible and irreversible atomic movements. Next, we explore the structural origins of these secondary relaxations in the MGs alloyed with different species of elements. With the combination of synchrotron X-ray diffraction and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations, solute-atom-centered clusters with a string-like type of medium-range order are found in the MGs, the formation of which leaves dispersed low-electron-density regions. It is found the activation energy of fast secondary relaxation increases with the reduction of low-electron-density regions, while slow secondary relaxation relates to the distance of the solvent atom in next nearest solvent-solvent atomic pairs and the size of the string-like solute-atom-centered clusters. The phenomena are interpreted within the framework of the generalized Maxell model and free volume model. Our results demonstrate fast secondary relaxation as the activation of a small concentration of liquid-like regions with extremely low viscosities preceding slow secondary relaxation and provide evidence for the correlation of secondary relaxations with short- to medium-range electronic and atomic structure in MGs. Through the combined efforts from the extensive simulations and experiments, we completely achieve the objective for understanding the physical origin of the fast beta relaxation and its connection with the slow beta relaxation in the model MGs, such as Zr-based MGs. 2. Establishing the correlations between the beta relaxations and various mechanical properties of the Zr-based metallic glasses The activation energy (EA) spectra of secondary relaxations can be linked with the mechanical properties of MGs. For this project, we systematically probed the EA spectra for numerous MGs samples with distinct local geometric ordering, which correspond to broad processing histories with MD simulations. Interestingly, we found that the shear moduli of the samples are strongly correlated with the arithmetic mean of the EA spectra rather than with the local geometrical ordering. Furthermore, we studied the correlation of the obtained EA spectra and various well-established physical parameters. The outcome of our research clearly demonstrates that the soft-mode parameter Ψ and the EA spectrum are correlated, which serves as a good indicator of MG properties. On the microscopic or atomic-scale, the beta relaxations can be associated with the activation of some flow “defects” in MGs, which are structurally loosely packed and dynamically active to external stimuli. In this project, we further proposed a machine-learned “defects” from atomic trajectories rather than static structural signatures. We analyzed the atomic motion behavior at different temperatures via a k-nearest neighbors machine learning model, and quantified the dynamics of individual atoms as the machine-learned temperature. Applying this new temperature-like parameter to MGs under stress-induced flow, we can recognize which atoms respond like “liquids” to the applied loads. The evolution of the liquid-like regions reveals the dynamic origin of plasticity (thermo- and acousto-plasticity) of MGs and the correlation between stress-induced heterogeneity and local environment around atoms, providing new insights into thermo- and acousto-plastic forming. Furthermore, we also found that beta relaxations can be related to the crystallization behavior of MGs, which is not just limited to Zr-based MGs but also extended to Fe-based MGs, the latter of which is technologically important because the soft magnetic properties of Fe-based MGs are derived from nanocrystallization. In order to study the beta relaxations and nanocrystallization in these MGs, we developed theoretical modeling and carried out extensive experiments to characterize the nanocrystallization behavior of the MGs triggered by the beta relaxations. These research activities can be considered as additional results that supplement the expected outcome of our second task. 3. Developing the processing routes to tune the beta relaxations and to optimize the mechanical properties of the Zr-based metallic glasses By fully activating atomic-scale stress relaxation within an ultrathin surface layer under ultrasonic vibrations, we accelerate the formation of atomic bonding between MG ribbons at a temperature far below the glass transition point. In principle, our approach is based on the tuning of beta relaxations in the near surface zones, which overcomes the size and compositional limitations facing traditional methods, leading to the rapid bonding of MGs of distinct physical properties without causing crystallization. The outcome of our current research opens up a window not only to synthesize BMGs of extended compositions, but also toward the discovery of multifunctional glass-glass composites, which have never been reported before. Furthermore, this ultrasound-enabled joining approach can synthesize bulk-sized MGs with single or multiple amorphous phases, which can be fundamentally related to the ultrafast surface beta relaxations. In contrast to conventional monolithic BMGs, BMGs with multiple phases and microstructures could be designed on the basis of our current method. To be more specific, this ultrasound processing technique (UPF) allows us to perform joining, forming, stamping, and punching rapidly near room temperature. In doing so, we can effectively mitigate the issue of crystallization and oxidation. As a result, we can now fabricate complicated shapes and geometries from the BMGs not suitable for thermal plastic forming, such as some Fe-based BMGs with a limited supercooled liquid region but excellent soft magnetic properties and wide applications in electronic devices. As a demonstration, we can trim a Zr-based BMG plate over 1 mm thick with a semi-circular edge at a stress level less than 100 MPa, fabricate a typical stator core for high-speed motors with a fine profile from the Fe-based amorphous ribbons through the cold shear punching within 0.05 s, much shorter than traditional electron discharge machining. Furthermore, BMGs can be cold joined through the ultrasound processing technique which is due to the combined effect of the super-plasticity and the fast beta relaxations assisted formation of metallic bonding. Likewise, we can easily fabricate an external thread through the UPF enabled extrusion and a thick BMG ring through UPF enabled punching near room temperature, at about 10% of the pressure needed for traditional punching. These processing techniques, based on the activation of beta relaxations, can significantly rejuvenate the energy state of MGs and therefore enable us to fine tune or optimize their mechanical properties.

11209317.label: Major findings and research outcome
11209317.value: The major findings of the research work funded by this project can be summarized as follows. (1) The pronounced low temperature fast beta relaxation originates from the reversible atomic motions in a metallic glass, activation of which bridges the thermal vibration mode (also known as the boson peak) and the slow beta mode dominated by “cooperative” sub-diffusion. These slow beta modes can be attributed to string-like solute-atom-centered clusters, which vary with the alloying of different elements. By comparison, the fast beta relaxation can be tuned through the change in the solute centered liquid-like or reversible atoms. (2) The activation energy spectra of beta relaxations can be correlated with the mechanical properties of MGs, such as mechanical strength and tendency of plastic flow; more interestingly, they are also related to the initiation/growth of crystals in MGs. (3) By fully activating fast/slow beta relaxations at low temperatures (i.e., below the glass transition point) by matching their characteristic relaxation times with the time of mechanical simulations in cyclic loadings, we develop an ultrasonic forming technique to quickly deform and shape MGs at a very low stress. This ultrasonic technique rejuvenates MGs to different degrees of potential energy, which, in turn, can lead to the optimization of the mechanical properties of MGs. Aside from a number of publications, the outcome of our research through the funded project is two folds. (1) We successfully trained a PhD student, who is now a postdoc in Chinese Academy of Science, working on the fundamental study and design of metallic glasses with combinatorial methods. (2) We establish collaborations with our colleagues in a few research institutions, which brings about a new NSFC-RGC project to further our study on relaxation dynamics in low dimensional MGs.

11209317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11209317.value: Fe-based soft magnetic alloys are an important material for making the next generation electric transformer that can reduce the electric energy waste. One strategy to design high-performing Fe-based soft magnetic alloy is through nanocrystallization of Fe-based metallic glasses, which, according to the research we carried out, can be tuned through beta relaxations. This is a direction that is worth further study. On the other hand, relaxation in low dimensional metallic glasses is just a new research topic in the field of metallic glasses. This is an uncharted territory which is yet to be explored.

11209317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11209317.value: Glass is known for its lack of crystalline atomic structure. Therefore, it is difficult to identify which part of a glass atomic structure act as “defects” that control the mechanical or physical behavior of the glass. In this project, we studied two stress relaxation phenomena and their correlation with the mechanical properties of metallic glasses. In principle, stress relaxation is the consequence of movement of flow defects, and therefore can be viewed as their “fingerprints”. Through a systematic study of the beta relaxations in metallic glasses, we unravel their connections with the atomic packing, mechanical properties and even crystallization behaviors of a few metallic glasses, such as Zr-, Fe- and even La-based metallic glasses. The outcome of the research deepens our understanding of strength, plastic flow initiation and even crystallization in metallic glasses.

11209717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11209717.value: 過去的十年，航空旅行需求在世界范圍內穩步增長，尤以亞太地區增長最快。這種快速增長加劇了空域擁擠，由此造成的航班延誤浪費時間、燃料，對經濟活動和環境均造成損害。為了提高運營效率，避免延誤，空中交通服務提供商正在積極尋求手段來分析現有空域的容量、效率和擁堵風險。 現有針對空域的研究明顯不足。基於代理的仿真和排隊網絡（QN）模型均是目前最先進的方法，但是兩者都受到管理和規劃的限制。前者需要廣泛的數據輸入，具有挑戰性﹔后者基於過度簡化的假設，未考慮日常運營的特點，如在途擁擠、空中等待、偏離計劃航線和航線更改等。現有方法及其進一步發展的關鍵限制在於可用的運營數據，如飛機運行、空中交通管制指令、航班調度的實時跟蹤等。這些數據受到國家或地區機構和航空公司的嚴格管制，缺乏適當的信息共享。因此，空中交通服務提供商難以把握區域空域的“大圖景”。 廣播式自動相關監視（ADS-B）的實施為空域研究帶來了新的發展機遇。ADS-B是一種基於衛星的監控技術，通過衛星跟蹤並播報每架飛機的位置。隨著越來越多的國家採用ADS-B技術，實現全球范圍內的飛機運行跟蹤和分析首次成為可能。ADS-B數據使我們能夠實時監察跨區域的空域管理狀況，並識別造成空中交通擁堵的瓶頸。 本研究的目的是開發一個利用實時飛機跟蹤數據來分析國家航空交通網絡中空域擁堵的新框架。研究目標包括（1）利用ADS-B數據對國家航空交通網絡進行特征描述，（2）構建航空交通網絡擁堵的網絡排隊論模型，（3）証實數據驅動框架在航空交通管理上的潛在應用。我們將設計軌跡聚類算法來分析交通流模式，開發排隊論網絡模型來評估現有空域和機場的擁堵情況。分析結果可以協助空中交通服務提供商識別現有的瓶頸，並建立實時監控的基准。使用本研究所提出的框架，決策者可以預測各種情景下的航班延誤風險，如網絡結構變動、基礎設施改進或航空交通管理變更等。 本研究是對項目申請人在航空運輸系統、數據分析和排隊論模型等領域已有的和進行中的研究的延伸。申請人已使用ADS-B數據進行了一項前導性研究，以比較中國和美國航空交通網絡的特性。結果表明，空域容量限制仍然是中國航班延誤的高危因素。 我們將對此研究進行拓展，並開發一個基於數據驅動的有助於航空交通管理和規劃的分析框架。 本研究將豐富航空交通管理領域的文獻。基於實時飛機跟蹤數據的“大數據”分析方法具有創新性。該項目還將有助於區域航空交通管理現代化，鞏固香港作為亞太地區和世界領先的航空樞紐地位。

11209717.label: Major findings and research outcome
11209717.value: In this research, we developed a novel framework to analyze airspace congestion in a national air traffic network using real-time aircraft tracking data. The following objectives were achieved via this project: to (1) characterize airspace operations in a national air traffic network using ADS-B data, (2) build a network queueing model of air traffic network congestions, and (3) demonstrate potential applications of the data-driven framework in air traffic management. The key methods and algorithms developed in the project include: a trajectory clustering algorithm to analyze traffic flow patterns and a queueing network model to assess congestions of existing airspace and airports. Results allow air traffic service providers to identify existing bottlenecks and establish benchmarks for real-time monitoring. Using the proposed framework, decision-makers can predict risks of flight delays under various operational scenarios, such as network structure modifications, infrastructure improvements, or changes in air traffic management.

11209717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11209717.value: Further development focusing on testing and demonstrations via close collaboration with air traffic management agencies will be needed to further validate the developed methods and models, and to make real-world impact.

11209717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11209717.value: This research develops analytical method based on “big data” analytics of real-time aircraft tracking data. The outcome of this research could allow air traffic service providers to identify bottlenecks in current air traffic network operations and establish benchmarks for real-time monitoring. Using the proposed framework, decision-makers can predict risks of flight delays under various operational scenarios, such as network structure modifications, infrastructure improvements, or changes in air traffic management. The results of the project are relevant to regional air traffic management modernization in Hong Kong, to consolidate the city’s status as a leading air hub in Asia-Pacific and the world.

11209917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11209917.value: Genetic modification is a process by which a DNA sequence of a cell is modified, and this process affects an organism. Genome editing is a type of genetic engineering involving the insertion, deletion, or replacement of DNA in the genome of a living organism by using molecular scissors, such as CRISPR/Cas system. However, current genome editing techniques with engineered nucleases are limited in terms of safety and specificity of these nucleases. Robotics microinjection in genetic modification will provide a new way vital to address this problem, with improved throughput and success rate. In this project, a novel microsurgery robotic system will be developed, which can accurately and quantitatively control injected materials into mammalian cells (<25 µm) to genetically modify single cells with sufficient efficiency and reliability. Investigations will be conducted on the basis of three perspectives. First, an automated microinjection system that can accurately and quantitatively control injected materials into mammalian cells will be examined and created. An open architecture will be established in the system to perform tasks, such as cell holding, injection, and retrieval, in one complete process, in order to enhance processing speed and throughput. A three-dimensional (3D) image processing technique will be developed to identify and locate internal cell structures and organelles automatically to facilitate highly efficient and accurate cell injection surgery. Second, a microarray chip platform will be designed and fabricated to conduct single cell trapping and on-chip culture of post-injection cells. The significance of this chip is attributed to its high trapping rate in handling small-population post-injection samples with simple and easily fabricated structures. Third, the developed microneedle-enabled robotic microinjection system will be applied to accurately control the quantity of clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats/Cas9 nuclease (CRISPR/Cas9) plasmids, which are engineered nucleases for genome editing, delivered into each cell to generate genome-modified cells. Single cell trapping and on-chip culture of post-injection cells will be further achieved by employing the developed microarray chip platform to examine the influence of genetic modification on cell biological properties. This project will provide an innovative solution to perform genome editing safely and specifically for precision and regenerative medicine. Success of this study will facilitate the development of new technology to enable automated cell surgery with high throughput and success rate for advanced applications. 本專案將組建一個機器人輔助作業系統用於實現單細胞精確定量注射，從而提高基因修飾的有效性和穩定性。本研究將從以下三個方面展開。1.搭建自動化顯微注射系統，考察並完成注射物的精確定量控制。此自動化顯微注射平臺包含細胞捕獲、注射及回收裝置。一站式集成平臺可以提高實驗速度和增加細胞操作通量。本研究利用3D影像處理技術進行細胞及細胞器的識別與定位，以利於高效地和精確地進行細胞顯微操作。2.設計並製作微流控晶片，用於捕獲單細胞、輔助顯微注射及注射後單細胞培養。本晶片的優勢是對少量細胞進行高效捕獲，而且結構簡單，易於製作。3.利用自動化顯微注射平臺將CRISPR/Cas9基因編輯系統注射到單細胞，並對注射物進行精確定量控制。通過精確控制CRISPR/Cas9質粒的量，本研究將優化注射參數，減少脫靶效應，提高基因編輯的安全性和特異性。微流控晶片不僅用於捕獲單細胞、輔助顯微注射，而且可以進行注射後單細胞培養以便於觀察基因修飾對細胞生物特性的影響。

11209917.label: Major findings and research outcome
11209917.value: This project aimed to develop a new automated cell microinjection system with high productivity, through the four approaches: 1) automatic detection of cells to replace manual selections, 2) optimizing injection paths of detected cells to save time, 3) adjusting the penetration depth adaptively, and 4) employing constant outflow-based injection to minimize clogging. The first three approaches aimed to improve the injection speed, and the last one aimed to extend the usage time of micropipettes. A robot-aided microscopy system and 3D reconstruction algorithm were developed for intracellular surgery with 3D information. A simplified sheathless cell separation approach that combines gravitational-sedimentation-based sheathless prefocusing and DEP separation methods was also developed. With the developed high-throughput robotic microinjection system and methodologies, we demonstrated that the microinjection of CRISPR/Cas9 with an enhanced green fluorescent protein (eGFP) donor template into single HepG2 cells can achieve reporter gene knock-in. The developed robotic microinjection was further compared with the other three delivery methods, showing that robotic microinjection can exhibit the higher transfection efficiency.

11209917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11209917.value: The motivation of this project is to improve the throughput of cell microinjection, which has become a bottleneck problem hindering the clinical application of microinjection technology. Existing cell microinjection systems typically use only one micromanipulator and rely on manual identification of cells, resulting in a limited ability to process cells for one experimental cycle. To improve cell processing capabilities, we may consider the use of two or multiple micromanipulators in concert to automatically identify cells through deep learning. The problem of manipulating two or multiple micromanipulators for nearby cells can be formulated as a route optimization problem, and the method can also be extended to use three or more micromanipulators. Additionally, a deep learning algorithm will be developed to identify and select cells to significantly increase processing speed.

11209917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11209917.value: In this project, we developed an automated high-productivity system and methodology for cell injections. The productivity can be increased by detecting cells automatically, optimizing injection paths quickly, adjusting the penetration depth adaptively, and avoiding clogging of micropipettes. These improvements have enabled the system to inject over 1500 cells per hour with minimum training and preparation. The high-quantity injections allow us to perform large-scale cell injection experiments for vast biomedical research. We successfully used the high-throughput robotic microinjection system to achieve high-efficiency eGFP knock-in into human cancer cells, where the efficiency of eGFP knock-in can reach 40%, and low off-target mutations were observed. A case study of injecting eGFP knock-in cancer cells into zebrafish embryos was conducted to demonstrate that the eGFP fluorescence signal can enable the tumor visualization in vivo. We also compared the effects of the proposed microinjection method with three chemical delivery carriers on MSCs in terms of multipotency and therapeutic gene function.

11210017.label: Project Objectives
11210017.value: To design and develop a generic sensory model for point-cloud and images, so that a generic dense-discrete representation can be constructed. The model will facilitate convolution operations so that CNN-centric deep learning can be uniformly conducted on both images and point-cloud. To design and develop a globally consistent map model that fuses heterogeneous sensor data using deep feature maps and regularization. The model is incrementally online maintainable. It keeps the minimum sufficient and effective data for the environment representation. To develop and implement a two-phase localization system comprised of coarse localization (place recognition) aided by deep-learning and precise localization by sensor fusion on receptive fields of recurrent CNN (rCNN). Recurrent CNN is adopted to model the work memory of the learned features from query sensor data sequences. To design and implement an open-source C/C++ library that enables high-precision outdoor localization effectively and efficiently. To gather an open-source dataset for outdoor large-scale dynamic environments across-seasons, weather conditions, and time-of-day, with ground-truth. It will function as a benchmark for further comparison with others in the future.

11210017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11210017.value: High-precision long-term localization in dynamic outdoor environments is still unsolved. As a typical robotic perception problem, a globally consistent map of the environment is the key to solving the problem. However, such a consistent map is very challenging to obtain in highly dynamic environments reliably. In this project, we deal with the dynamics as long-term (structural, and across seasons and time-of-day) and short-term (moving people and objects in the scene) separately. We try to provide a compact solution to the localization problem with a globally consistent map aided by recurrent deep learning. The localization problem for robots is considered mostly solved for static environments with a smooth movement of the robot. Static environment (or mainly static) is the primary default assumption for existing localization and mapping methods. However, exist systems rely on the repeatability of visual features will easily fail in illumination or seasonal changes; other methods that mainly depend on the geometry of the environment will fail when foliage changes or old building disappears. We propose to use recurrent deep learning to model the overall appearance using heterogeneous sensor data. The model will be further refined based on principal analysis directly onto the deeply-learned feature maps. Deep learning has been a white-hot topic of the past years. It shows astonishing success in artificial intelligence. Its inputs are commonly dense representation such as acoustic signal, images or video. Another fact is that most existing methods with deep learning are offline, by which an offline model trained by offline data is used for online tasks. In this project, we aim to break these barriers. We use deep learning in an incremental manner for localization problem and adapt sparse point-cloud as dense representation using tensor voting. As outcomes, on the one hand, the theoretical outcome of the project will push forward the understanding of why and how deep learning can help robotic navigation. These contributions include but not limited to the generic sensory modeling for vision and range-finders, development of online incremental learning model for rCNN, the model simplification and optimization, etc. On the other hand, the practical contributions include an efficient library to solve high-precision long-term localization in dynamic outdoor environments, an open-source dataset including 144 trails for benchmarking future studies, etc. Both theoretical and practical contributions indicate the high potential of the project to promote the development of service robots, autonomous driving, and advanced human-robot interfacing. 實現在室外動態環境下的高精度長時間定位現在仍是一個亟待解決的問題。作為機器人感知領域的典型課題，構建全局一致的地圖是解決此難題的關鍵所在。然而，在高度動態的環境中獲取可靠的地圖在現階段十分具有挑戰性。本項目分別針對長期環境動態（如跨季節、全天候）和短期環境動態（如移動的行人和物體），利用借助循環深度學習獲取地圖，提供解決室外定位問題的方案。 在靜態環境下，平緩移動的機器人定位問題已經大部分被解決。可以說，靜態環境是現有的定位系統和建模方法的基本前提。然而，現有的系統主要依賴於視覺特徵的重複性，容易在照明條件下或者季節變化的條件下失效；而其他依靠環境中的幾何特徵的方法也無法應對例如樹葉變化或舊建築物消失的狀況。本項目旨在利用循環深度學習，加以異構傳感器獲取的數據，對整體外觀進行建模。基於原理分析方法，該模型將進一步細化，直接生成具備深入學習特徵的地圖。 近幾年，深入學習一直是一個廣泛熱議的課題，它展示了人工智能的驚人成果。深入學習的輸入形式通常呈現出密集的表達方式，例如聲學信號、圖片、視頻等。並且，現有大多數現關於深度學習的方法都是離線的，通過離線煩人模型及數據來解決在線的任務。在這個項目中，我們將克服以上障礙，以增量的方式利用深度學習來解決定位問題，並使用張量投票將稀疏點雲轉化為稠密的表達形式。 作為研究成果，該項目能夠在理論上將更好地幫助我們理解深入學習是如何協助機器人進行導航的，其他貢獻還包括了視覺和測距儀的通用感官建模，RCNN在線增量學習模型的開發，模型簡化和優化等。在應用方面，它能幫助我們建立一個能夠實現室外動態環境下的高精度、長時間定位的高效的流庫，以及一個囊括144條軌蹟的開源數據庫，作為未來研究的評測基準。這些理論成果和應用成果展示了本項目在推動機器人發展、無人駕駛和人際交互等方面的巨大潛力和價值。

11210017.label: Realisation of objectives
11210017.value: We have finished all the previously defined research objectives. For each objective, the realization is described in the following paragraphs. Objective1 We propose cross-modality methods to localize image series on the dense point-cloud map. We investigate different dense map representations for better quantization, varying from the signed distance field to the surfel map. Firstly, we develop a system that localizes a camera in a dense map modeled by the gaussian mixture model, which can be built in advance. After the initial camera pose is tracked by the front-end, the system associates local visual observations and map components efficiently. Meanwhile, the triangulated visual structure is verified and optimized. With the geometric factors introduced in the joint optimization, the initial poses are further refined against the global map. Secondly, we also propose to track the camera pose in a surfel map. The system utilizes global planar information to associate the sparse tracked points with geometric structure. In a local sliding window, the optimization takes points with and without global association as input. The proposed method formulates all constraints in the direct photometric form, and the absolute scale of the 6-DoF pose can be recovered. To introduce convolution operations into geometric perception, we propose a slam system using global and local learnt features. We formulate the camera pose tracking in a direct and probabilistic manner, with learnt repeatability as input. 2D keypoints are parameterized with local uncertainty taken into account. We also introduce global embeddings for loop closure detection, which further improves the robustness and accuracy of the system. Experimental results on public KITTI verify the effectiveness of the proposed system. In addition, we propose an end-to-end sparse tensor-based deep neural network for introducing deep learning-based perception for point cloud processing. To be specific, the method takes two consecutive point clouds as the input, and generates masks for moving objects in the scene. Experiments on the public nuScenes dataset confirm the superiority of this method over others. leading to publications: Ye, Haoyang, et al. "Monocular direct sparse localization in a prior 3d surfel map." 2020 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA). IEEE, 2020. Huang, Huaiyang, et al. "Gmmloc: Structure consistent visual localization with gaussian mixture models." IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters 5.4 (2020): 5043-5050. Huang, Huaiyang, et al. "Incorporating learnt local and global embeddings into monocular visual SLAM." Autonomous Robots (2021): 1-15. Sun, Yuxiang, et al. "PointMoSeg: Sparse tensor-based end-to-end moving-obstacle segmentation in 3-D lidar point clouds for autonomous driving." IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters 6.2 (2020): 510-517. Objective2 We propose a visual simultaneous localization and mapping system by leveraging the learnt global and local features, which generates a localizable map represented by a bipartite graph connecting frames and landmarks. Frames store global feature information for search the initial global location of the query image. With localized initial location, sensor pose can then be refined with local feature association against the map. In addition, we propose a tightly coupled lidar-inertial odometry and mapping framework, which fuses inertial measurements with lidar point cloud for gravity aligned mapping with low drift. To keep a low computational requirement, we also present LINS, a lightweight lidar-inertial state estimator for real-time ego-motion estimation. An iterated error-state Kalman filter (ESKF) is designed to correct the estimated state recursively by generating new feature correspondences in each iteration, and to keep the system computationally tractable. Moreover, we use a robocentric formulation that represents the state in a moving local frame in order to prevent filter divergence in a long run. Extensive experiments are performed to validate the robustness and generalizability in various scenarios and the results indicate the proposed method offers comparable performance with the state-of-the-art lidar-inertial odometry. leading to publications: Ye, Haoyang, et al. "Tightly coupled 3d lidar inertial odometry and mapping." 2019 International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA). IEEE, 2019. Qin, Chao, et al. "Lins: A lidar-inertial state estimator for robust and efficient navigation." 2020 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA). IEEE, 2020. Objective3 We propose UNDONet, which implements both depth completion and ego-motion estimation. The deep-learning based method is served as a coarse outdoor localization system and trained self-supervised by the 3D constraints embedded between point cloud sequences. We propose Sparse2Ego network, which estimates the ego-motion from two consecutive point clouds. We train Sparse2Ego in the supervised way on KITTI dataset, which is a widely used benchmark dataset for outdoor robotics tasks. We demonstrate its accurate ego-motion estimation ability by evaluating them on KITTI validation dataset. Additionally, we adopt the Sparse2Dense network in a similar way and show the precise depth completion performance. We propose a complete and precise visual inertial localization system based on a hybrid map representation to reduce the computational cost and improve the positioning accuracy. The hybrid map is built by both the visual and lidar data to support hierarchical localization. To be specific, we first query global feature of the input frame to retrieve an initial location. Then the localization module refines the poses with both visual and geometric constraints. For batch optimization, instead of using visual factors, we develop a module to estimate a pose prior from the instant localization results to constrain poses. Extensive experiments and qualitative results demonstrate a competitive performance of the proposed method compared to the state of the arts, especially in the positioning accuracy and computational resources. leading to publications: Huang, Huaiyang, et al. "Geometric Structure Aided Visual Inertial Localization." arXiv preprint arXiv:2011.04173 (2020). Objective4 We have developed a C++ library for vision-dominant localization system with heterogenous sensors as the input source for the outdoor environments. The library also supports building the global map from multiple synchronized sensors. Part of our work is open-sourced under https://github.com/hyhuang1995/gmmloc, https://github.com/HyHuang1995/sp_orb_slam . Objective5 We have collected a large-scale dataset, named HKUST-Campus Dataset. It contains the raw data of a set of stereo cameras, a 16-beam LiDAR, an IMU and a GPS. The dataset is gathered by multiple rounds of the 1km loop within the campus, which covers versatile conditions, varying from day to night, sunny to cloudy. It consists of various static objects (e.g., buildings, trees, roads, etc) and dynamic objects (e.g., pedestrians, vehicles, bicycles, etc) in the outdoor environment. We make this dataset open-source under http://gofile.me/4jm56/iXovA4HIl for further comparison with others and future research purposes.
