11210017.label: Major findings and research outcome
11210017.value: As a summary, we have achieved the following facts in the period of this project. -This project proposed deep learning (DL)-based high-precision localization system which is capable of working under changing environments effectively and efficiently. The project dealt with multi-modal sensor fusion for robustness and handled moving dynamic objects with the segmentation method in driving scenarios. In addition, the project collected the large-scale outdoor dataset, which consists of various static objects and dynamic objects and covers different weather and time-of-day conditions within the campus. - We have published 19 journal papers, including those in IEEE Transactions on Image Processing, IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems, IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering (TASE), and IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L). The topics range from visual localization, SLAM, point clouds processing, etc. - We have published 20 international conference papers, including ICRA, IROS, IPIN, ROBIO, etc. The topics range from localization, mapping, SLAM, point clouds processing, etc. - We have been finalized or won 5 best conference paper awards, including the best conference paper award of IPIN2019 and ROBIO2019. - The PI received the 2018 IROS Toshio Fukuda Young Professional Award and being recognized “For outstanding contributions to mobile robot path planning and control”. - We have graduated 6 Ph.D. students from Hong Kong University of Science and Technology.

11210017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11210017.value: There are several aspects to further develop in the research route: Low-cost navigation system for logistic robots. The current vision-dominant localization system is based on the low-cost sensor suite and computation device, which is much more inexpensive compared to point-cloud based solutions. We are actively deploying the proposed approaches and systems onto the logistic robot. This low-cost system could support other modules for outdoor navigation purposes, varying from route planning to decision making. Long-term Map management. The proposed localization system leverages deep learning for feature extraction and perception, based on which long-term sensory is a valuable topic for further investigation. Along this track, we would study the long-term map management for better navigation, covering discovering structural changes in the localizable map, incrementally learn the feature representation and detecting temporary dynamic objects.

11210017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11210017.value: The project completed the necessary know-how and prototype systems for the robust and high-precision localization system with heterogeneous sensors. To complete the challenging task, we propose several relative algorithms, ranging from image and point-cloud data processing, simultaneous mapping and low-cost localization. Both qualitative and quantitative results of our proposed methods in various challenging dynamic environments validate the effectiveness of our localization system. The research outputs directly lead to 19 high-level journal papers and 20 conference papers, including the best paper awards. The conducted results may lead to a boost in not only practical applications but also thermotical research in the field of robotics.

11210317.label: Major findings and research outcome
11210317.value: Using the finite element method, the waveguide characteristics of rib-type LNOI PW at 1.55 μm wavelength were investigated. The results indicate that zero group index dispersion in the wavelength range 1.3 to 1.7 μm can be realized in the structure. The research results were published in the journal Advanced Theory and Simulations. The PW waveguide amplifier was fabricated in 0.5 mol.% Er-doped LNOI wafer, and the Er-doping of the thin-film LN was completed during the crystal growth. A 250 nm thick nichrome (NiCr) mask was first patterned on the wafer, and the pattern was transferred to the Er:LNOI surface by an argon-based reactive ion etching (RIE) process. After removing the residual NiCr mask, a chemical-mechanical polishing (CMP) process was applied, and the waveguide scattering loss was reduced by an order of magnitude. A maximum on-chip optical net gain of 5.2 dB has been measured in the 5-mm-long waveguide amplifier at 1531.6 nm signal wavelength, with a relatively low 980-nm pump power of 21 mW. The waveguide amplifier shows a stable optical net gain for signal power ranging from <10 nW to ~100 μW, indicating a dynamic operation range of 50 dB. The research results were published in the journal Optics Letters and is an Editor’s Choice, confirming the significance of the work and the results obtained. Mode evolution and polarization rotating and splitting performances in LNOI PW waveguide were also investigated. The input fundamental transverse-electric mode (TE0) and transverse-magnetic mode (TM0) are separated and then projected into the TE0 modes of two output ports of the splitter. A half-etched rib waveguide configuration was used in the PRS, so that only a single step etching process was required in the fabrication process which is compatible to the common LNOI fabrication techniques. The PRS’s performance was measured first by imaging the output facets from the rotator and the splitter and then characterized quantitatively through the conversion efficiency and polarization extinction ratio. Polarization crosstalk of ~ -10 dB for both TM0-input and TE0-input has been obtained over a broad wavelength range, from 1500 nm to 1630 nm. Furthermore, in the simulation the PRS shows a potential operation range as wide as 500 nm from 1300 nm to 1800 nm. The research results were published in the journal Photonics Research and is also an Editor’s Choice, confirming the significance of the work and the results obtained.

11210317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11210317.value: The performances of the LNOI PW amplifier and polarization rotator/splitter are suitable for system applications, and can be commercialised when there are demands for these devices.

11210317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11210317.value: Although the applications of lithium niobate on insulator (LNOI) devices are expanding rapidly, some important functionalities for photonic integrated circuit (PIC) applications, such as polarization manipulation and optical amplification, are still missing in the LNOI platform, due to the limitation imposed by the common fabrication techniques. On one hand, lithium niobate (LN) is a hard-to-etch material, and the etched waveguide sidewall slope is usually less than 75°, thus making refractive index engineering difficult to achieve in the LNOI platform using standard fabrication technologies. On the other hand, high-temperature annealing cannot be performed on LNOI chip due to thermal expansion and pyroelectric issues, and common rare earth ions thermal doping process used to achieve optical amplification in bulk LN cannot be applied directly to LNOI thin films. In this project, pioneering work on passive broadband polarization rotator-splitter (PRS) and active highly efficient rare earth erbium ions doped LNOI waveguide amplifier have been demonstrated experimentally in the LNOI platform. The devices developed could provide solutions for the long-awaited missing functionalities, including polarization manipulation and optical signal amplification, thus expanding the applications and functional degrees of LNOI photonic devices.

11210517.label: Realisation of objectives
11210517.value: For objective 1, the monitoring system for roof truss utilizing ambient vibration was develop and was verified using measured data under laboratory conditions. It must be pointed out that the developed monitoring system is applicable under ambient vibration as it is impractical to apply external forces onto existing roofing system to induce detectable vibration on the structure. The external excitation force will certain affects the normal operation of the structure (i.e., the function of the structure). The property own will not approval this from happening especially the main purpose of the vibration test is for structural health monitoring. As a result, effort was spend on the model updating and so as the damage detection of a structural system utilizing only ambient vibration data when the structure is under normal operation (no need to close the structure for measurement). The development monitoring system has been applied in several structural systems, such as the AC3 academic building of City University of Hong Kong [J1, J4, J5, C1, C5] and the metal roofing system [J2]. It must be pointed out that objective 1 also considers the development of an optimal sensor configuration method. This part was also completed. The developed sensor configuration method relies on the entropy, and a novel and computationally very efficient optimization algorithm tailor-made for identifying the near optimal sensor configuration for a given number sensors was developed. The developed optimal sensor placement method is not only applicable for roof truss system. Its theoretical development and application in railway safety monitoring are reported in [J9, C6]. This objective is 100% completed. For objective 2, a comprehensive series of vibration tests has been carried out on a series of roofing systems under laboratory conditions. Furthermore, field tests were also completed. The test results together with the works about modal identification, model updating and structural damage detection are reported in [J1, J2, J4, J5, J9, C1, C2, C5, C6]. This objective is 100% completed. For objective 3, a new MCMC based Bayesian model updating method was developed. The developed method together with the verification through measured data has been reported in [J1, J3, J4, J6, C3]. This objective is 100% completed. For objective 4, the development of the abnormal deflection method by following the Bayesian approach was completed. This method was integrated into the Bayesian-based SHM methodology, and the findings were reported in [J6, J9, C6]. The MCMC method developed in objective 3 relies on a finite element model, and it was recently extended to use autoregressive (AR) model, which significantly improve the applicability of the method. The related research development was reported in [J5]. Furthermore, the developed monitoring system in objective 1 and the testing method in objective 2 were adopted for the development of a series of horizontal axis wind turbine. The research findings were published in [J7, J8, C4, C7]. It must be pointed out that the PI of this project was invited to give a Keynote in a conference in reference [C3] because of the developed MCMC based Bayesian method. Furthermore, Mr Chu, the PhD student of the PI, awarded THE BEST PRESENTATION AWARD in the conference of reference [C7]. The PI would like to report that two Final Year Project students in academic year 2018/19 were trained based on the support from this project. Their name and project titles are given below: • MAN Shi Ching Kent: Vibration-based structural model updating of a double-layer truss • YE Zherong: Structural damage detection based on vibration test Both students are Major in Bachelor of Engineering in Civil and Structural Engineering. References: J1 to J9 are the first to the ninth journal papers reported in Part C. C1 to C7 are the first to seventh conference publications reported in Part C.

11210517.label: Major findings and research outcome
11210517.value: The monitoring system for long-span roof systems is an outcome developed in objective 1 of the project. The advantage of the proposed monitoring method is it is applicable under ambient vibration, and therefore, external force is not required. This feature is very important as no property owner will approval a forced vibration test on their building especially the purpose of the test is structural damage detection. The development monitoring system has been applied in several structural systems, such as the AC3 academic building of City University of Hong Kong [J1, J4, J5, C1, C5] and the metal roofing system [J2]. The entropy-based optimal sensor configuration method is another important outcome developed from objective 1. The developed optimal sensor placement method is not only applicable for roof truss system. Its theoretical development and application in railway safety monitoring are reported in [J9, C6]. The datasets from various laboratory tests and field tests are also important outcomes of the project. The test results together with the works about modal identification, model updating and structural damage detection are reported in [J1, J2, J4, J5, J9, C1, C2, C5, C6]. The novel MCMC based Bayesian model updating method is the most important outcome of the project. The developed method together with the verification through measured data from various structural systems were reported in [J1, J3, J4, J6, C3]. The MCMC method developed in objective 3 relies on a finite element model, and it was extended to use autoregressive (AR) model. The related research development was reported in [J5]. References: J1 to J9 are the first to the ninth journal papers reported in Part C. C1 to C7 are the first to seventh conference publications reported in Part C.

11210517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11210517.value: The developed Bayesian structural health monitoring (SHM) is very general. After the consideration of the structural characteristics, it can be applied to other types of structures, such as tall buildings and long-span bridges. The PI is preparing research proposals along this direction, and future research will be carried out if the submitted proposals are funded. A limitation of the development SHM method is the computational effort and time required in forming and updating the finite element model of the target structure. When data is continuously measured from the monitoring system, the updating process may not necessary fast enough to make real-time (or on-site) damage detection possible. To make fast-damage detection possible, the PI is now carrying out research on the use of data-driven artificial intelligence (AI) in SHM.

11210517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11210517.value: Long span roof trusses, for their structural efficiency, are very popular in Hong Kong and worldwide. Collapse of this kind of structures is cataclysmic owing to the large area of coverage (e.g., the collapse of roof truss of the Sport Hall at City University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, on 20 May 2016). Many collapse reports of roof trusses revealed that symptoms (e.g., cracking sounds and falling of concrete dust) were observed hours or even days before the collapse. The symptoms suggested that the structure may have damage accumulated on structural members and/or it may be overloaded with large deformation. The main purpose of the proposed project is to develop a practical and cost-effective smart structure system for early detection of potential structural damage and abnormal deformation of long span roof trusses by proper sensing and intelligent diagnosis based on structural responses, such as accelerations, strains, modal parameters, under operational conditions. This project developed a damage diagnosis methodology for extracting information from various measurands and quantifying the damage status of the target structure. A Bayesian probabilistic approach was adopted as it fundamentally processes the statistical information from data for making inference and decision making.

11210617.value: 傳統的空調系統旨在為房間提供均勻的熱環境, 這實際上是假設每一個人的需求都是一樣的，然而個體的差異是顯而易見的。另一方面, 有意設計不均勻的室內環境可能會提高空調系統的能效。例如非工作區的溫度顯著地高於工作區。因此，要將統一的集體環境轉變為照顧個人喜好同時又節能的環境。如何在控制環境和經濟成本的前提下提供這樣的環境是當前氣流組織研究的一個重要挑戰。個性化送風是個現有的解決方案。然而，在人員密集的房間，例如教室，除了在工作區連接數十個送風口有困難之外，各送風口可能因非常接近而互相干擾。 近年来，数学問題的逆向求解技术有了新的進展，可以求解决送風的耦合效应。这种技术可以照顧多人的喜好。一旦確定了多个位置的人員的喜好，该技术能立即确定多個送風口各自的風量和風溫。此外，为了更好的可控性，必須选擇响应快速的系统。因此将首先测试层式通风，並构建无线传感器和人机界面网络。 本項目是第一個研究共享通風系統而目的在於照顧多人的個人喜好。通過直接從前部和/或側面方向冷卻頭部，頸部和胸部，為人員提供熱舒適，同時房間的其餘部分保持更暖，因而需要更少的冷卻，實現更好的能源效率。新風被直接輸送到呼吸區，以改善吸入空氣質量。除了送風的位置，設備將幾乎與常規系統相同，從而將技術開發的風險降至最低。該系統將佔用較少的室內空間，並且初投資也將降低。 本項目將在我們獨特的環境室進行，對辦公室和教室的情況進行測試。客觀測量將通過無線傳感器收集。同時，熱感覺和熱舒適的人員主觀反應通過人機界面網絡輸入。客觀測量和主觀輸入都將被用於系統控制。系統設計將反復改進。最後，將製定一套技術應用設計指南。在逾40篇SCI學術文獻中，這一新穎的氣流組織的優點體現在下列幾個方面： 1. 更好的熱舒適性 - 滿足個人需求; 2.更好的室內空氣品質 - 頭部水平供氣; 3.更好的能源效率 - 全年能耗減少20％至40％; 4.更環保 - 生命週期中碳足跡減小; 5.研發風險較低 - 創新技術可以用傳統的通風裝置實現;和 6.更安全的安裝 - 安裝時無需腳手架（棚架）。

This technology also minimizes the complexity and cost of the sensor network.

11210617.label: Major findings and research outcome
11210617.value: The room thermal environmental conditions can be largely derived from the air supply and exhaust conditions. This technology also minimizes the complexity and cost of the sensor network. Stratum ventilation is found to be faster in response and have a shorter time constant. This technology provides people with a more comfortable and healthier environment and helps capitalize upon the substantial energy-saving potential of advanced air concentrations.

11210617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11210617.value: Correlating the thermal environment model of collective air distributions to the energy model of air conditioning systems can realize coupled operation optimizations. A thermal environment is modulated by the condition of its supply air, leading to its exit air condition; while both the supply and exit air conditions are monitored and/or controlled by the building management system. Currently available physical-based modelling technologies (e.g., CFD models, zonal models and nodal models) demand very high computational capacity and many more sensors at various locations in the air and on the walls. With the correlations, applicable values of the controllable parameters in the building management system should be explicitly identified for a desired environment regarding indoor air quality and thermal comfort. There should be several applicable values for one controllable parameter. They should be the most energy-efficiently determined to meet the requirements of indoor air quality and thermal comfort. Stratum ventilation has been proven to provide neutral thermal sensation at higher room temperature, leading to more energy saving. However, the non-uniform environment of stratum ventilation heavily depends on boundary conditions, and the room air velocity could reach 0.6m/s. This means that there is more room for modulation of thermal environment under stratum ventilation.

11210617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11210617.value: Purposely designed non-uniformity of the indoor environment could benefit energy efficiency of air conditioning (cooling) systems, e.g. allowing for significantly higher temperature in the unoccupied zone. Therefore, there is a need for a paradigm shift from uniform collective environments to environments that entertain preferences of individual occupants as well as energy efficiency. How to provide such environments cost effectively, both environmentally and economically, is a serious challenge to current air distribution research. The advantages of this novel air distribution proposed are demonstrated in the following aspects: 1. Better thermal comfort ─ individual preferences will be accommodated; 2. Better indoor air quality ─ horizontal air supply at the head level; 3. Better energy efficiency ─ 20% to 40% less year-round energy consumption; 4. More environmentally friendly ─ smaller carbon footprint throughout life cycle; 5. Lower risk in research and development ─ the innovative technology can be realized with conventional ventilation devices; and 6. Safer installation ─ no scaffolding is needed for installation.

11211317.label: Project Objectives
11211317.value: To develop and improve the synthesis techniques to obtain high-performance n-type InAs and p-type GaSb nanowires with the controlled crystallinity, geometry, morphology, electrical and structural properties. To fabricate chemically gated field-effect transistors on mechanically flexible substrates using single nanowires (e.g. InAs or GaSb) for the current conduction channel and metal-oxide thin films (e.g. SnO2, ZnO, or WO3, etc) deposited directly on top of the nanowire for the toxic-gas-sensitive (e.g. NO, NO2, NH3 or CO, etc) media. This unique hybrid device configuration, engaging p-type and n-type channels dedicated for the oxidizing and reducing gas sensing, respectively, is employed to decouple chemically sensitive regions from conducting channels in order to reduce the operating voltage and to enhance the sensor reliability. To characterize corresponding senor performances at room temperature, such as the sensitivity, selectivity, stability, drift, hysteresis, response time, reversibility and so on. All these findings are essential to further optimize the nanowire synthesis, sensor fabrication and device dimensions for the subsequent studies. To construct large-scale chemically gated transistor arrays via the nanowire contact printing technique to heterogeneously integrate optimized nanowire parallel arrays and metal-oxide thin films on plastics, followed by the evaluation of their performance limits with different operating conditions. The use of nanowire parallel arrayed films as the conduction channel would further amplify the sensor output signals and enhance their invariability and reliability. The ultimate goal is to accomplish a versatile, low-cost and powerful platform to attain high-performance, ultra-low power and long-term reliable toxic gas sensor arrays for emerging mobile and wearable applications.

11211317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11211317.value: 在過去的十年裡，無線設備、雲數據和可打印電子產品的出現，改變了我們的日常生活，並極大提高了我們的生活質量。例如，將不同的傳感器簡單地集成到我們的智能手機中，我們就可以很容易地收集到大量的外部信息，如我們的體溫、健康數據以及其他信息，這些都為下一代柔性和可穿戴傳感器的發展提供了機會，甚至化學過程也可以監測。我們可以很方便地把手機變成工具，或者把傳感帶附著在任何物體表面對危險化學品進行實時探測，這些技術對環境監測、食品安全、人身安全等都至關重要。同時,由於納米技術的快速發展,多功能納米材料，如：一維納米線和二維薄膜，具有很多優異的性能，如：大的比表面積,優異的機械彈性,低製備成本和可調節的材料性能。因此，多功能納米材料被認為在未來傳感器技術中具有良好的應用前景。到目前為止，大量的化學傳感器開發都是基於納米材料而展開，特別是在室溫下專門用於有毒氣體(NOx、CO、NH3，等)檢測。然而，這些傳感器都難以達到新興的柔性、可移動和可穿戴的傳感器平台的要求，因為它們的運行電壓和功率遠遠超出了電池系統的供應能力。這些普通傳感器的另一個問題是由金屬電極與分析物之間的密切接觸所引起的化學疲勞和長期運行後的電子應力而導致的材料退化。因此，對於可穿戴傳感器應用的性能評估，以及低成本、高性能、柔性耐用的有毒氣體傳感器的開發仍面臨許多挑戰。 本研究方案旨在重點探討如何在柔性塑料上實現具有高傳輸特性的一維半導體納米線基導電通道與沈積在其上的二維金屬氧化物薄膜基有毒氣體敏感介質的有機結合。這種獨特的複合器件結構，即：p型銻化鎵納米線通道用於氧化氣體感應，n型砷化銦納米線通道用於還原氣體感應，對導電通道中的化學敏感區域進行了去耦合，在不影響室溫下運行的傳感性能的前提下，顯著地降低了運行電壓，並提高了傳感器的可靠性。基於此,我們將致力於構建大規模的傳感器陣列，並評估其相應性能極限，從而開發出一個兼具普適性、低成本和高效性等優勢的平台，進而製備出功能納米材料基傳感器陣列，使其具有高柔性、高性能和超低功率的特點，實現其在可穿戴器件領域的應用。

11211317.label: Realisation of objectives
11211317.value: In this project, we have successfully accomplished all the objectives with 100% of completion. Specifically, we developed an enhanced synthesis technique, known as solid-source chemical vapor deposition, to obtain high-performance n-type InAs and p-type GaSb nanowires with controlled crystallinity, morphology, diameter, length and electrical properties (Objective 1). For instance, as reported in ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2020, 12, 56330−56337 (DOI: 10.1021/acsami.0c17317), high-quality InAs nanowires were synthesized with well-controlled process parameters, such as growth temperature, amount of source precursor powder, pressure, carrier gas flow rate and etc. After the nanowire synthesis, the nanowires were configured into simple back-gated field-effect transistors using conventional lithography, Ni metal deposition, and lift-off. The electrical characteristics of the fabricated nanowire devices were then measured in a vacuum probe station with a base pressure down to 1E−4 Pa and in dark conditions. A semiconductor analyzer (Keysight B1500A) was used for the electrical measurements. A scanning electron microscope (SEM, Quanta 450 FEG, FEI) was also employed to study the surface morphology of the obtained NW devices. Interestingly, the output current would decrease together with the threshold voltage shifting to the positive direction when a positive gate bias stress was applied, and vice versa for the negative gate bias stress. The significant hysteresis behavior was observed for double-sweep transfer characteristics, depending heavily on the sweeping rate and range. On the basis of complementary investigations of these devices, charge traps were confirmed to be the dominant factor for these instability effects. Importantly, the hysteresis could be simulated well by combining the rate equation for electron density and the empirical model for electron mobility. This provided an accurate evaluation of carrier mobility, contrasting distinctly to the overestimation of mobility when using the transconductance for calculation. All these findings indicated the importance of controlling charge trap dynamics and confirmed the device performance enhancement of the nanowire devices. Once the toxic gas-sensitive nanomaterials (i.e. InAs, GaSb and WO3) are synthesized with enhanced properties, they are fabricated into chemical gate field-effect transistors on different substrates, such as rigid and flexible substrates. Their device performance were then characterized with different toxic gases, such as NO and other nonanal species (e.g., aldehyde) (Objective 2 and 3). As presented in J. Mater. Chem. A, 2021, 9, 5815 (DOI: 10.1039/d0ta11287a), we developed a surface treatment using sulfuric acid to improve the sensor electrical response and the recovery rate. The acid surface-treated sensor device exhibits a detectable electrical response down to 6.7 ppb, which is two times lower than that of the as-grown WO3 hydrate nanowire sensor. It also showed the outstanding dynamic response to various concentrations (from 6.7 ppb to 2.67 ppm) of aldehyde with respectable recovery times. The molecular sensing selectivity evaluation further revealed that the acid surface-treated sensor presents excellent selectivity to aldehyde. It is clear that increasing the surface acid treatment time improves the sensor properties (i.e. increasing the sensor response and decreasing the sensor recovery time). The acid surface treatment can promote both the oxidization of aldehyde the desorption of products, nonanoic acid, from the surfaces at a temperature of 20-50 deg C, which is lower than the 300 deg C and up required for untreated surfaces. Using complementary characterization techniques, two different adsorption structures of carbonyl groups on the surface were identified, where molecules directly bounded to coordinatively unsaturated surface tungsten preferentially proceed to the catalytic oxidization reaction and the subsequent desorption process. These surface steps contributed to the sensing mechanism of aldehyde on the nanowire sensors. At the same time, the thermal durability of the surface-treated WO3 hydrate nanowire catalysts was as well evaluated. Impressively, the catalytic properties due to acid surface treatments could be maintained up to an annealing of 300 deg C, being robust enough for electrical sensing. To further examine the robustness as a time series, for the temperature range for molecular sensing experiments around 200 deg C, the catalytic effect could be maintained at least over 10 years. Even at a higher temperature up to 300 deg C, the catalytic activity remained over a year. This outstanding thermal robustness of tailored catalytic surfaces can be attributed to the thermal stability of coordinatively unsaturated W of WO3 hydrate nanowires. After that, the nanowires were fabricated into highly-dense parallel nanowire arrays by a well-developed contact printing method to construct large-scale sensor device arrays on different substrates (e.g. mechanically flexible, transparent or stretchable substrates) in order to study their device performance (Objective 4). The device arrays were evaluated at various concentrations of different gas conditions, including NO and aldehyde. Importantly, the selectivity to varied sensing media across the sensor arrays could be enhanced by decorating different metal or metal-oxide nanoclusters on the device channels. For example, Au and Pt were found to improve the catalytic activity of the oxide surface towards the detection of CO and NO, accordingly. It is found that the Au decorated sensor arrays could deliver up to 3 orders of magnitude response upon the 100 ppm CO exposure among a mixture of gases at room temperature with the response time and detection limit down to ~4 s and ~ 500 ppb, respectively. These performance parameters represented one of the best values reported so far for the nanomaterials-based CO sensors. The enhanced crystallinity, surface-to-volume ratio, and carrier mobility of nanowire materials are the main reasons for these superior device performances. In summary, we have developed low-cost, reliable, mechanically flexible and large-scale nanowire-based chemical sensor arrays for efficient toxic gas detection. Combined with the optimized nanowire materials, sensor structure, and device dimension, we have achieved outstanding device performance beyond conventional thin film technologies for future sensor utilizations.

11211317.label: Major findings and research outcome
11211317.value: In this project, there are several key findings, which lead to 7 journal publications (1 ACS Nano, 1 JMCA, 1 ACS AMI, 2 JMCC, etc) and 10 invited presentations at different international conferences. Also, there are 4 undergraduate students, 1 master student and 3 PhD students trained during the execution of the project. Specifically, as reported in ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces 2020, the gate bias stress and hysteresis effects in InAs nanowire field-effect transistors were carefully investigated. The output current was found to decrease together with the threshold voltage shifting to the positive direction when a positive gate bias stress was applied, and vice versa for the negative gate bias stress. Based on complementary investigations of these devices, charge traps were confirmed to be the dominant factor for these instability effects. The hysteresis could be simulated well by combining the rate equation for electron density and the empirical model for electron mobility. All these findings delivered an accurate evaluation of carrier mobility, being in distinct contrast to the overestimation of mobility when the transconductance was employed for the calculation, providing a deeper understanding of charge trap dynamics to enhance the device performance of nanowire transistors further. At the same time, as reported in Journal of Materials Chemistry A 2021, a simple surface treatment using strong acids was developed to enhance both the thermally robust catalysis and electrical molecular sensing of WO3 hydrate nanowires based devices for toxic gases and other carbonyl compounds, such as aldehyde. Mass-spectrometric measurements revealed that the surface treatment substantially promoted the oxidization of aldehyde and the desorption of associated products from the surfaces. Spectroscopic and structural measurements combined with numerical simulations identified two different adsorption structures of carbonyl groups on the surface, where the molecules directly bound to coordinatively unsaturated surface tungsten preferentially proceed to the catalytic oxidization reaction and the subsequent desorption process. Importantly, the thermal durability of the catalytic activity on acid-treated WO3 hydrate nanowire surfaces was estimated to be over 10 years up to 300 deg C. These results demonstrated the successful tailoring of complex nanostructured metal oxide surfaces for further sophisticated thermally robust electrical molecular sensing using chemical gate field-effect transistor nanowire-based structures. In summary, all these major findings are significant and establish relevant design guidelines of nanowires-based chemical sensor arrays, to go beyond the conventional thin-film technologies for future sensor utilizations.

11211317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11211317.value: Although many significant findings are produced from this work, there are still several major areas required to study these semiconductor nanowires-based gas sensor arrays further. For example, the gas sensors are preferred to operate at different conditions, such as at room temperature and in harsh environments with high temperature and humidity. In this case, it is essential to understand the device characteristics as a function of different operating conditions and integrate with other new materials and device designs to sustain its performance in harsh conditions. Another one is to further integrate these sensor devices with other electronic components into complete functional systems. For instance, it is ideal to utilize nanomaterials as active channels for both transistors and sensors. This way, these two devices can be easily integrated onto one platform to perform gas sensing and logic computation in a small form factor. All these further works would push forward nanowire-based gas sensor arrays' substantial technological development for practical utilizations.

11211317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11211317.value: In recent years, the advent of mechanically flexible and wearable sensors has enabled us to satisfy ever-expanding desires to monitor many different processes, which are important for environmental monitoring, food safety, health diagnosis, personal security, etc. Until now, extensive works have been focused on developing various electronic chemical sensors, especially dedicated for the toxic gas detection (e.g. NOx, NH3 and etc) at room temperature, constructed based on metal-oxide semiconductors, polymer materials and the techniques used for sensing are optical methods, calorimetric means, gas chromatography and acoustic schemes. However, these sensors are not appropriate for the emerging mobile, flexible and wearable sensor platforms due to the high power requirement. In this project, we have successfully developed a hybrid and low-cost approach utilizing the bottom-up high-performance multifunctional nanowires with the conventional top-down device fabrication processes to achieve large-scale, flexible and heterogeneously integrated nanowire sensor arrays. For example, the WO3 nanowires-based sensors exhibit excellent sensitivity and selectivity to the target gas as well as superior robustness during device operation. Ultimately, we have established a versatile and powerful technology platform to realize the mechanically flexible sensor device arrays for practical utilization.

11211417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11211417.value: The Internet technologies have been the primary force behind the popularity of Web news media (e.g., BBC News, ABC New, NBC News, CNN News, etc.), and the fast rise of social media sites (e.g., Flickr, Facebook, Twitter, etc.). The popularity of the Web news media and, since Web2.0 era, social media services, has resulted in huge amounts of (professional) journalist-reported data and user-generated data streams on the Internet. Such massive data resources serve as a treasure tank for people to explore the real-world concepts, express personal/public views, and share or report events, thereby “sensing the world” timely. As real-world events are closely related to people’s lives, they have received increasingly more attention in recent years. Multi-sourced Event Detection (MED) aims to mine and monitor various real-world events, in an efficient manner, from both the user-shared social media data and the journalist-reported news media data, so as to provide comprehensive and timely views of the events. However, MED is deemed as challenging, due to the following two primary reasons. First, the data streams are often multimedia ones which may possess multiple heterogeneous features like text, images, meta-data (e.g., timestamp-taken, GPS-tags, tags, user identity, etc.). Such multimodal data, while providing necessary and complementary information about the events, are generally difficult for traditional machine learning models to fully exploit. Second, the raw data contributed by different people ranging from ordinary users to journalists can be diverse and rather low in discriminative power due to data variations. For example, image photos may be taken from multiple viewpoints using different devices at different time, resulting in varying viewpoints, resolutions, illumination conditions, changing backgrounds, etc. Likewise, textual news/descriptions may be written by different people with various levels of professionalism from different standpoints, etc. In this project, we aim to: 1) address the issues of heterogeneity and low discriminative power of raw data, through devising a shared multimodal data representation learning model by fully utilizing the multi-sourced multimodal data; 2) improve the effectiveness and efficiency of event detection by devising hybrid clustering models and class-wise residual models; and 3) validate the effectiveness of our proposed modals upon real-world data. An experimental prototype system is to be developed to manifest the process of MED, and extensive testing will be conducted by using real-world data to evaluate our proposed research. 互聯網技術已經成為社交媒體（例如Flickr，Facebook，Twitter等）和網絡新聞媒體（例如BBC新聞，ABC新聞，NBC新聞，CNN新聞等）的普及興起的主要力量。社交媒體服務和網絡新聞媒體服務的流行產生了大量的用戶分享的數據和專業記者提供的數據。網絡上的大量數據資源成為人們探索現實世界和“感知世界”的寶庫。特別是與人們的生活密切相關的現實世界中的事件，它們吸引人們的關注、影響人們的生活。與事件有關的數據可能由業餘用戶和專業記者分享在不同的數據源中。多源事件檢測（MED）旨在從用戶貢獻的社交媒體數據和記者報導的新聞媒體數據中挖掘各種現實世界的事件，並提供全面的事件描述和觀點。 然而，從多來源數據中檢測事件是具有挑戰性的，其原因主要有兩個。首先，數據流是多媒體形式的，並且它們通常具有多個異構特徵，例如文本，圖像，元數據（例如，時間戳，GPS-標籤，標籤，用戶身份等）。多模態數據提供了描述事件的必要和互補信息，但是傳統機器學習模型難以利用多模態數據。其次，不同用戶和記者貢獻的原始數據可能由於數據的差異性而具有較低的辨別力。一方面，圖片可能使用不同的設備在不同時間從多個視點拍攝，導致不同的角度、分辨率、照明條件、變化的背景等。另一方面，文本報道可由不同的人從不同的角度撰寫等等 在這個項目中，我們的目標是：1）通過設計一個共享的多模態數據表示學習模型來處理原始數據的異構性和低判別力的問題，從而充分利用多源數據。 2）通過設計混合聚類模型和分類殘差模型，提高事件檢測的有效性和效率。 3）在真實數據中驗證方法的有效性。本項目還將開發一個原型系統來顯示MED的過程，並且將使用真實數據來評估我們提出的方法。

11211417.label: Realisation of objectives
11211417.value: In the first objective, we propose to design shared multimodal data representation learning model for MED by incorporating a number of important assumptions. During this reporting period, we devise an event detection framework to discover real-world events from multiple data domains, including online news media and social media. As multi-domain data possess multiple data views that are heterogeneous, initial dictionaries consisting of labeled data samples are exploited to align the multi-view data. Furthermore, a shared multi view data representation (SMDR) model [Yang2019] is devised, which learns underlying and intrinsic structures shared among the data views by considering the structures underlying the data, data variations, and informativeness of dictionaries. SMDR incorporates various constraints in the objective function, including shared representation, low-rank, local invariance, reconstruction error, and dictionary independence constraints. In particular, the proposed SMDR incorporates shared representation, reconstruction error, low-rank, local invariance, and dictionary independence constraints simultaneously. Specifically, the shared representation constraint is proposed to learn shared structures among multiple data views, which is illustrated as that “The multiple data views of a data sample expressing its multiple aspects, which are determined by a hidden structure”. The reconstruction error constraint models the errors that could be caused by widespread variations of real-world data, which is illustrated as “The reconstruction error of raw data based on the dictionaries results in amounts of errors, and the l2-norm of the error matrix is the smaller the better”. The low-rank constraint assumes the data are approximately sampled from a union of low-rank subspaces, which is illustrated as “The observed data views of data samples are determined by shared low-dimensional subspaces, which is expected to be approximately of low-rank”. The local invariance constraint learns similar representations for the samples that are close in the original feature space, preserving geometric structures underlying the data, which is illustrated as “The representations of data samples that are close in the observed feature space, should be close to each other in the shared feature space”. The dictionary independence constraint learns the optimal dictionaries consisting of informative bases, which is illustrated as “A discriminative and informative dictionary consists of a number of bases that are independent to each other”. In the second objective, we propose to devise from the perspective of data recovery both hybrid-clustering and class-wise residual based models [Situ2018] for event detection. Considering that the rationale of data reconstruction models is to recover data samples based on dictionaries, we exploit the class-specific residual corresponding to the class specific dictionaries for pattern analysis. In addition, online crowdsourcing systems provide us an efficient way to accelerate the process of collecting training data via distributing the enormous tasks to various annotators to help create large amounts of labelled data at an affordable cost. Nowadays, these crowdsourcing platforms are heavily needed in dealing with social media text, since the social network platforms (e.g., Twitter) generate huge amounts of data in textual form everyday. However, people from different social and knowledge backgrounds have different views on various texts, which may lead to noisy labels. When doing data collection from social media, we sometimes also need to need to deal with the problem of noisy labels, especially for those data collected via crowdsourcing and aggregated with labelling models. Therefore, we propose a noise-aware classification framework [Zhan2019] that integrates the steps of noisy label aggregation and classification. The aggregated noisy crowd labels are fed into a classifier for training, while the predicted labels are employed as feedback for adjusting the parameters at the label aggregating stage. The classification framework is suitable for directly running on crowdsourcing datasets and applies to various kinds of classification algorithms. The feedback strategy makes it possible for us to find optimal parameters instead of using known data for parameter selection. In the third objective, we propose to develop an experimental prototype system [Kang2019] with large-scaled real data to be collected from major social media sites, and test adequately the effectiveness of the theory and techniques proposed in this project. We have collected a multi-domain and multi-modality event detection (MED) dataset, which consists of 9,722 news articles and 23,500 Flickr images that are related to 100 real-world events. The news articles are collected from hundreds of data sources, including Yahoo News, Google News, Huffington Post, CNN News, New York Times, NBC News, Fox News, Washington Post, The Guardian, etc. The Flickr images are shared by 269 Flickr users. For illustration purpose, we show a set of samples in the MED dataset in Figure 1. As the news articles are reported by different news media sites, the perspectives and viewpoints could be quite different. Similarly, the images are shared by different Flickr users or taken from multiple viewpoints at different moments by using various kinds of photo capture devices. The appearance variations of the images in each row are obvious, though they are related to the same event. The data variations make it intractable to differentiate and identify events. Especially, due to the multi-modal data by user-contributed on social media websites, the social events demonstrate personalization of the users. To make better use of abundant multi-modal data and integrate social events into research in other fields, we have presented a Graph Network model (GraphRec) [Fan2019] to model social recommendation for rating prediction. Specifically, we provide a principled approach to jointly capture interactions and opinions in the user-item graph. Our experiments reveal that the opinion information plays a crucial role in the improvement of our model performance. In addition, our GraphRec can differentiate the ties strengths by considering heterogeneous strengths of social relations. Simultaneously, we extend the application of the multi-domain data in image-to-image translation. We introduce a self attention mechanism to StarGAN denoted as Self-attention StarGAN [He2019], which can model the long-range dependencies among the feature maps at all positions in the context of multi-domain image-to-image translation. Extensive experiments conducted on the CelebA dataset demonstrate that the images generated by our model have robust background and fine grained texture details. Meanwhile, Self-attention StarGAN decreases the reconstruction error, indicating its ability of transferring facial images across different attributes. Both qualitative and quantitative evaluations show the high quality and effectiveness of the proposed model for multi-domain image-to-image translation. 11211417.label: Major findings and research outcome
11211417.value: Generally speaking, handling multimodal data is an intractable problem for SED, in our research, the major findings of which are two-fold. Firstly, traditional clustering or classification models are not suited to exploit the "multimodal features" which provide necessary information about the events they depict seamlessly. Even with techniques like early fusion and late fusion, coupled with affinity graphs or adjacent matrices for the multiple modalities, manifold learning for feature subspace and dimensionality reduction etc., a severe limitation they share is the high computational complexity, hence are not scalable to deal with Flickr-like media data which is in large quantities and of a high updating rate. Secondly, the missing data problem also makes SED more challenging than traditional TDT. In particular, it is unavoidable to have missing attributes in user contributed social media data, which inevitably affects on the effectiveness of the learning processes negatively. For instance, 80% of Flickr data has no GPS-tags in spite of the significance of location information. Consequently, many works on detecting social events have simply discarded them from further analyses instead of making full use of the rich features. For the above findings, we design corresponding solutions from different aspests. The specific research outcome is as follows: 1) we propose to design shared multimodal data representation learning model [Yang2019] for MED by incorporating a number of important assumptions; 2) we propose to devise from the perspective of data recovery both hybrid clustering and class-wise residual based models [Situ2018] for event detection; 3) we propose to develop an experimental prototype system [Kang2019] with large-scaled real data to be collected from major social media sites; 4) we propose a noise-aware classification framework [Zhan2019] that integrates the steps of noisy label aggregation and classification; 5) we have presented a Graph Network model (GraphRec) [Fan2019] to model social recommendation for rating prediction; 6) we introduce a self attention mechanism to StarGAN denoted as Self-attention StarGAN [He2019] for the application of the multi-domain data in image-to-image translation; 7) we propose CEP scheme and DCEP scheme [Zhang2020] to improve the topic coherence by incorporating the concept information of the entities; 8) we proposed a series of progressively enhanced multi-task models [Cai2020] for sentiment analysis; 9) we propose a new task called Image-guided Story Ending Generation (IgSEG); 10) we propose a novel dual channel graph convolutional network (DC-GCN) for better combining visual and textual advantages and etc. Please refer to Part C for the full research outcome. Note that, for some acknowledgements of the papers, we mistyped the project number (11211417 becomes 1121417).

11211417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11211417.value: 1) Lively represented by user-contributed data on social media websites, social events refer to those which are attended or captured by the social media users, like concerts, exhibitions, local gatherings, celebrations, sport matches etc. Thus, the research project can also shed significant light on such relevant research as multimodal retrieval (a.k.a. cross media search), mining hidden valuable relationships among events, multimedia Q&A etc. In above research problems, we will plan to design the multimodal engie to align the heterogeneous data; 2) Meawhile, in the real world, social media and other platforms provide the multi-source and multi-modal data of each users. Thus, In the future, we will devote ourselves to personalized research domain based on multi-modal data, such as multi-modal recommendation systems, personalized Q&A systems etc; 3) Finally, a complete causal relationship graph between events will help people better handle with complex data. The event causal discovery of multi-modal data is also one of our next research directions with this project.

11211417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11211417.value: Internet platforms provide new ways for people to share experiences, generating massive amounts of data related to various real-world concepts. Such big collections of images and their companion tags have become a treasure tank for users to learn what's happening, to share their experiences, and to explore and “sense" the real world anytime anywhere. In this research project, we use Social event detection (SED) to mine and monitor various real-world events from the user-contributed images. We also present an event detection framework to discover real-world events from multiple data domains, including online news media and social media. It can effectively and efficiently detects social events from real world social media data. The research project makes contributions to the more general problem of event discovery and mining from user-contributed multimedia data on social media sites. The prototype laies a good foundation for the development of a practical system with similar functionalities.

11212017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11212017.value: Casimir力源自量子力學真空零點能，是廣義范德華力的一種。這些力是長程力，因此在微納尺寸的傳感器/驅動器的設計上至關重要。目前大部分的研究集中在Casimir引力效應，例如可移動傳感器與部件之間的粘附力。最近的理論和實驗研究都表明Casimir力也可表現出斥力作用，這取決於物體的形狀和組成。這個發現不僅促進對力新的理解，而且為解決微納電力系統中有害的相互作用提供新的途徑。但是在微觀尺度下，力與距離間固有的非線性特性以及顯著的表面效應使得其應用變得非常複雜。因此，尋求能夠精確預測結構機械響應的有效方法非常必要。 項目申請人已經就晶體結構中長程CL引力效應[83]以及表面應力尺寸效應[87,88]進行了研究，同時也就辛彈性力學做過若干研究。該方法能夠克服求解經典板動力學遇到的瓶頸，經典板動力學求解方法並不能應用到經典類Levy和類Timoshenko型半逆法中[45,75]。本項目將研究Casimir力和表面力作用下典型的類板狀結構。項目申請人將：（i）確定係統幾何構型和材料對Casimir引力向斥力過渡的影響；（ii）發展新的辛彈性模型和求解方法研究板在受Casimir斥力作用下的非線性力學響應；（iii）通過實驗和原子模擬驗證模型和方法的正確性；（iV）進一步探索Casimir斥力和表面應力的潛在工程應用，包括微納開關、微納驅動和傳感系統非線性振盪器和量子電動態浮選裝置。 本項目的預期研究成果如下：發表若干相關的技術文獻；為Casimir斥力和表面應力及其作用下的微納結構晶片工程響應的研究提供新的理解、認識和實驗數據及新的求解方法；培養本領域一到兩名研究生；最後，本項目的順利實施能夠為進一步的研究提供平台，同時促使新的工程分支的誕生及微納電力系統的設計和應用。

11212017.label: Realisation of objectives
11212017.value: The project started in January 2018 and it ended in June 2021. There are three objectives of the project as follows: • To identify geometries and materials of the systems that allow the tuning of the Casimir interactions from attraction to repulsion. • To establish a new symplectic elasticity model and symplectic solution methodology for the nonlinear mechanical responses of the structures to Casimir forces and size-dependent surface stresses. • To train research students with in-depth research knowledge in the field. The first two objectives are academic while the third one is related to the training of research students. It is reported here that all objectives have been fully achieved. There are a total of 33 research papers published that are fully or partially supported by the funding of this papers. Some of the papers fully addressed the objectives of the project while the other papers may not be apparently relevant which, however, can be viewed as spin-offs research outputs that are a result of the methods or principles developed while conducting the project. With respect to the objectives of the project, a new and novel Hamiltonian-based approach that capitalizes the advantages symplectic elasticity method in conjunction with the isogeometric analysis (IGA) has been established for investigating the mechanics and fracture dynamics of magnetoelectroelastic biomaterials. In this new approach, the symplectic modeling with IGA numerical algorithm have been developed for discretizing the overall physical domain and the deriving the symplectic eigenvalue and eigenvector solutions. New explicit expressions for singular physical field variables have been derived and new intensity coefficients have been introduced and determined. The physical consequences and engineering implications of this innovative coupled isogeometric-symplectic approach have been fully described (Objective 1 [12]). Further, to overcome the critical numerical challenges associated with the complex geometry and topological shapes and to ensure accurate numerical results, it is necessary to divide the overall physical domain into a near field (singular field) and a far field (regular field). A symplectic series is adopted in the near field such that the knot unknowns can be represented as undetermined coefficients in the symplectic space, while the knot unknowns in the far field remain unchanged. Consequently, the explicit expressions for each singular physical field variables and other solutions can be obtained with better accuracy and with significantly lower computational effort (Objectives 1 and 2 [12]). The symplectic elasticity methodology was further extended to study free vibration and buckling of a partially or internally cracked natural fiber reinforced composite (NFRC) plate with corner point-supports. Mechanical degradation of NFRC plate during the hygrothermal ageing was described by using a theoretical damage model. Crack effects on the plate derived by using the line spring model (LSM) were considered in the governing equation of motion in the form of crack compliance coefficients. In the framework of symplectic elasticity, free vibration and buckling eigenvalue problems for three types of boundary conditions were reduced into a set of algebraic equations by a superposition of boundaries. Highly accurate critical buckling loads, fundamental frequencies and corresponding mode shapes were solved simultaneously. A comparison of the new proposed model with finite element method was presented to validate the accuracy and effectiveness of the symplectic method. Subsequently, the influence of hygrothermal ageing and crack parameters on the free vibration and buckling behaviors of cracked NFRC plates was rigorously presented. The research results concluded that both length and crack location are important factors that affect the hygrothermal ageing of NFRC plates (Objective 2 [20]). A further aspect of the project is the analysis of Casimir forces and surface stresses of micro- and nani-sized plates. In this aspect, an accurate buckling response analysis for functionally graded graphene platelet (GPL) reinforced piezoelectric cylindrical nanoshells subject to thermo-electro-mechanical loadings was established by a rigorous symplectic expansion approach. Three types of GPL reinforced patterns were considered, and the modified Halpin-Tsai model was employed to determine their effective material properties. By using Eringen's nonlocal stress theory and Reissner's shell theory, new governing equations were established in the Hamiltonian form. Exact solutions were expanded into symplectic series and three possible forms were derived (Objective 2 [21]). Furthermore, an accurate model for vibration of a porous magneto-electro-thermo-elastic functionally graded (METE-FG) cylindrical shell made of barium titanate (BaTiO3) and cobalt diiron tetraoxide (CoFe2O4) with magneto-electro-thermal loadings was developed within the framework of Hamiltonian system and symplectic elasticity (Objective 2 [32]). Further, a general third-order shear deformation plate theory (GTSDPT) is employed to investigate the buckling behaviors of rectangular nanoplates. A new model with non-isotropic surface modulus that depends on in-plane and transverse shear strains, such as that for most crystalline faces, was established to analyze the significance of non-isotropic surface effects on buckling behaviors. The governing equations and the corresponding boundary conditions were established by using the principle of minimum potential energy. The analytical critical buckling load solutions were obtained for nanoplates with different boundary conditions. The proposed model was verified by comparing buckling results against the ones from existing plate theories (Objective 1 [30]). In a different aspect, a further work on a unified plate model predicting the buckling behaviors is proposed by incorporating both surface and size effects into the general third-order plate theory (GTPT) was developed. From the minimum potential energy principle, the governing equations were implemented with presenting the corresponding boundary conditions. Analytic buckling loads for rectangular nanoplates are obtained by considering different boundary conditions. The surface effects, size effects and geometric sizes of nanoplates on the plate instability loads were discussed by using four types of single crystalline metallic nano-materials, gold, silver, copper and nickel (Objective 1 [31]). The research model and method developed was further applied to develop a new approach for the free vibration analysis of beams under different boundary conditions. We showed that a static approach could be used for solving free vibration systems. Specifically, the basic governing equation for beams with harmonic loadings and resting on an elastic foundation was solved and the solutions were used directly to yield the beam free vibration solutions. Further, applications of the method were extended to deal with nonlinear dynamics of structures. Here the neo-Hookean material model was adopted to describe the hyperelastic behavior of a dielectric elastomer membrane (Objectives 1 and 2 [1,2,29]). Applications for energy harvesting devices were also considered (Objectives 1 and 2 [3,5,26]). The remaining publications that acknowledged and were supported by the project can be broadly classified into three main groups: thermoacoustics [4,6,10,11,28], dynamics of metamaterials [9,13,14,15,16,17,19,22,24,25] and mechanics of concrete structures [7,18,23,27,33]. Although the broad principles and applications may not be directly relevant to the objectives in this project, the methods of analysis, principles of modeling and numerical algorithm do benefited directly from the project where the theory, analytical technic and research routes developed while doing the project helped significantly in the completion of the research works in these spin-off research areas. The research staff and research students directly and indirectly supported and trained under this project include Dr L.H. Tong (2011-2015) [30,31], Dr Dafeng Tang (2012-2019) [3], Dr I.A. Tijani (2017-2020) [7,18,23,27,33], Dr Yida Mao (2016-2020) [10,11,28], Dr Zhen Zhao (2017-2021) [21], Dr Weijian Zhou (postdoctoral fellow, 2019-2021) [8,13,15,17,22,25,26], Dr Muhammad (2017-2021) [8,9,13,14,15,16,17,19,24], and Dr Zhenyu Chen (2018-2021) [1,2,15,22,25,29] (Objectives 3).

11212017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11212017.value: The symplectic elasticity approach is indeed universal and verry general. The mathematical symplectic concept was first introduced by mathematicians and applied very extensively by theoretical physicists in mathematics and physics. It was later extended by applied mechanics researchers to solid mechanics, dynamics of structures and computational mechanics areas. Since then, there has been intensive and extensive research by using the symplectic method in applied mechanics and engineering. However, this fundamental concept does not end here. It is very possible to extend the symplectic concept and research methodology to other cross-disciplinary physics and engineering disciplines including, but not limited to, thermal, electrical, electromagnetic, control, civil, and possibly some chemical engineering problems. In fact, there have been research efforts by the PI and his collaborators to endeavour some specific problems in thermal and control engineering. Some preliminary research outputs have been published or currently in progress. The research outputs from this project indeed have created a wonderful platform to further develop this very potential symplectic method for solving various engineering problems.

11212017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11212017.value: This is an applied research project that focuses on the development of a symplectic elasticity approach to model, analyze and solve the dynamic characteristics of miniaturized crystalline plate structures by considering size-dependent effects and surface stresses. The project contains two main objectives (i) to identify geometries and materials of the systems that allow the tuning of the size-dependent interactions; (ii) to establish a new symplectic elasticity model and symplectic solution methodology for the nonlinear mechanical response of the structures to size-dependent effects and surface stresses; and (iii) to train research students with in-depth research knowledge in the field. The project finds applications in the analysis and design of micro-sized and nano-sized devices that are composed of electro-mechanical structures and systems. Nevertheless, the modelling technic, solution methodology and numerical algorithm developed through this project can be applied to other cross-disciplinary research areas including, but no limited to, thermal, electrical, electromagnetic, control, civil, and possibly some chemical engineering problems. In general, the three main objectives of the project have been fully achieved through research publications in peer-reviewed journals. From the project outcomes, further extensions can be conceived that will result in further research, project proposal and funding applications and practical design applications.

11212217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11212217.value: Aramid fibre composite material (AFCM) has emerged as a popular material for both repairing old buildings and constructing new buildings. However, the polymer matrix materials, adhesives and aramid fibres are combustible. Consequently, more smoke is emitted by burning AFCM than by burning composite materials based on carbon or glass fibres. When buildings made of AFCM catch fire, the emitted smoke generates an environment that is hazardous for the occupants and firefighting personnel. In addition, it has been reported that several laboratory personnel who frequently carry out standard fire safety tests on AFCM have suffered from smoke exposure. This project will study the smoke hazards associated with burning AFCM products in building fires. The burning behaviour and smoke hazards of AFCM products (in the form of both panes and sheets, which are commonly used in buildings) will be investigated using bench-scale, medium-scale and full-scale experiments. During the early stages of a room fire, the upper part of vertically orientated AFCM products are exposed to a layer of hot gas and they can easily ignite and emit smoke. Therefore, the fire behaviour of vertically orientated AFCM products under non-uniform high radiative heat fluxes will be investigated using a cone calorimeter. Multiple radiative heat fluxes will be tested on both vertically and horizontally orientated AFCM samples in the cone calorimeter. The surface temperatures, ignition times and fire and smoke potency parameters of the AFCM samples will be measured. The concentrations of toxic gases will be measured using Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectrometry. These concentration values will be used in an N-gas model to assess the smoke toxicity emitted from burning AFCM samples (and the model will also be modified to explore the effects of taking into account different types of gas, for example, taking into account only carbon monoxide). Medium-scale experiments will be carried out on the AFCM samples using a thermal radiator that can emit higher radiative heat fluxes at the top compared to the bottom. The smoke emission resulting from changes in the thermal decomposition at various AFCM surface temperatures will be observed. Full-scale burning tests on part of a model AFCM system in a building will be carried out to investigate the toxicity of the emitted smoke and the reduced visibility. The results will then be used to propose appropriate fire safety tests for assessing the smoke hazards of AFCM. 在新建建築及既有建築的改造中，聚醯胺類纖維複合材料（AFCM）的使用越來越普遍。然而，聚合物基體材料、粘合劑以及聚醯胺類纖維都是可燃的。與碳基複合材料或玻璃纖維材料的燃燒相比，AFCM燃燒會釋放更多的煙氣。當含此類材料的建築物發生火災時，產生的煙氣會威脅內部人員和消防員的生命安全。另外，有報導稱有經常進行ACFM火災安全測試實驗的實驗人員受到了其釋放煙霧的侵害。 本專案將對建築火災中AFCM製品燃燒的煙氣危害性進行研究。研究中通過小型實驗、中型實驗和全尺寸實驗對其燃燒行為和煙氣危害性進行調查。在室內火災的初期階段，由於豎直放置的AFCM製品的上部暴露在熱煙氣層中，它們很容易被引燃並釋放煙氣，因此，本研究中將利用錐形量熱儀對非均勻、高輻射熱流作用下，豎直放置的ACFM製品的燃燒行為進行研究，並通過錐形量熱儀對多種輻射熱流作用下，AFCM樣件豎直和水準放置時的燃燒行為進行檢測。實驗中對AFCM樣件的表面溫度、引燃時間以及火災和煙氣相關的性能參數進行測量。實驗中採用傅立葉轉換紅外光譜法測量有毒氣體的濃度，通過N-gas模型對AFCM樣件燃燒釋放的煙氣的毒性進行評估，並通過探討不同類型氣體的影響，如CO，對該模型進行修正。中型試驗將利用能釋放高輻射熱流的熱輻射器在ACFM樣件上部實施較高的輻射熱流進行實驗，實驗中觀測不同AFCM表面溫度時熱解變化所產生的煙氣。全尺寸試驗在建築物內AFCM系統模型上進行。實驗中將測量煙氣的毒性以及能見度的衰減。項目的研究結果可為AFCM煙氣危害性評估提供適宜的火災安全測試方法。

11212217.label: Realisation of objectives
11212217.value: Aramid fibre composite material (AFCM) has emerged as a popular material for both repairing old buildings and constructing new buildings. Applications include bonding to strengthen or retrofit concrete structures. However, the polymer matrix materials, adhesives and aramid fibres are combustible. Smoke liberated in a building fire is hazardous for the occupants and firefighting personnel. The following three objectives proposed on smoke hazards associated with burning AFCM in post-flashover room fires have been studied thoroughly in this completed project. Six tasks with bench-scale burning tests using a cone calorimeter, medium-scale burning tests and full-scale burning tests were completed. Studying the smoke emitted from burning AFCM systems would provide an indication of how fire behaviour of other fibre-reinforced polymer should be assessed. Thermal behaviour of AFCM bonding materials to strengthen and retrofit concrete and timber was also studied up to 300oC. Objective 1. To study the smoke emitted from burning AFCM products that can be used in buildings. 1.1 Simple expressions were searched for quick assessment of smoke toxicity practically. Fractional effective dose (FED) value was proposed to be calculated based on peak carbon monoxide concentration and peak carbon dioxide concentration, and transient carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide, and oxygen concentrations. Four equations on calculating FED related to toxic effluents in the literature were selected and evaluated. The FED values were compared using literature data on toxic gases from different materials measured by cone calorimeter; full-scale burning tests; and tunnel full-scale tests. Values of FED (labelled as FED2) based on peak carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide concentrations are similar to the average values of FED calculated from more complicated equation using the oxygen consumption calorimeters. Putting appropriate values of FED2 in fire safety design guides is then recommended. 1.2 Smoke hazards of AFCM samples were studied using the cone calorimeter at CityU. Flashover radiative heat fluxes of 20 kWm-2 at floor level, 35 kWm-2 near the walls and 50 kWm-2 near the ceiling were applied. The measured transient concentrations of carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide were used to calculated FED. The FED2 is recommended to assess the smoke toxicity associated with burning AFCM. 1.3 Burning behaviour of ACFM was compared with basalt and carbon fibres commonly used in the construction industry by thermal radiator. The time to ignition was measured under radiative heat flux up to 50 kWm-2. Burning behaviour of the AFCM was observed to be not so worse as basalt fibre composite sample under high heat flux. Basalt fibre composite was ignited within 3 s under the room flashover heat flux at ceiling of 50 kWm-2. Objective 2. To study the fire behaviour of AFCM under a non-uniform distribution of radiative heat fluxes in a room fire. 2.1 A compartment model was used to study radiation heat flux generated by ejecting flame and action on building façades with ACFM. Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) package Fire Dynamics Simulators (FDS) version 6 was used. CFD-FDS results suggested the wall heat-blocking effect would affect the plume trajectory, leading to deviation between temperature field and velocity field. 2.2 Experiments were conducted by a reduced-scale compartment-façade model to examine the factors leading to the fast flame height growth. Experimental results support the CFD-FDS study on window plume characteristics as in 2.1. 2.3 Bond performance of AFCM with concrete subjected to high temperature was investigated. Results were also compared with basalt and carbon fibre composites. Acoustic-laser technique, macroscale fracture tests and microscale characterization were used. Results have shown that the deterioration percentages of both peel and shear interface fracture toughness of AFCM-bonded concrete under high temperature are larger than those of carbon and basalt. The mechanisms behind different bond performance have been revealed with variations of microscale morphology and chemical decomposition. 2.4 Application of AFCM to strengthen wood was used. The residual performance of AFCM and the bond after elevated temperature exposure were investigated through macroscale single shear fracture test and microstructure characterizations. The deterioration mechanism of AFCM was compared with those from basalt and carbon fibre composites. Objective 3. To recommend fire safety tests to assess the smoke toxicity of burning AFCM in building fires. 3.1 Smoke toxicity in a fire is difficult to measure accurately. To reduce the number of smoke toxicity tests, models have been developed to calculate the toxic doses of single or multiple gases generated by fires. Of which, the N-gas model was commonly used. It was based on the assumption that a small number (N) of types of gas in smoke account for a large percentage of the smoke toxic potency. The N-gas model was selected and justified in this project FED2 appropriate to assess smoke toxicity for AFCM. 3.2 FED2 is found to give similar estimation on evaluating smoke toxicity. Exposing the fibre composite systems under high radiative heat fluxes would emit large quantity of smoke for igniting and burning basalt, carbon and glass fibre composite systems, not just aramid. The cone calorimeter test with transient carbon monoxide concentration measured is adequate for assessing minimum smoke toxicity effects, as toxic effect of carbon dioxide is low. 3.3 A fire hazard classification system for AFCM products was proposed based on the cone calorimeter data. Appropriate fire protection strategy can then be recommended to determine fire safety provisions, both active and passive. 3.4 Many projects with new architectural features in the rapidly developing Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA) have difficulties in complying with the prescriptive fire codes. Consequently, performance-based design (PBD) in fire engineering approach (FEA) has to be applied in the GBA. Timeline analysis in PBD-FEA of projects with fibre composite buildings should be watched and applied with smoke toxicity. Fire hazards due to burning AFCM without adequate fire resistance construction are suggested to be assessed with some toxicity as an example. 3.5 Specifications for the use of AFCM in buildings and the tests on assessing the fire behaviour of AFCM cannot be based on traditional fire safety building codes. The window plume fire scenarios in building fires reported in objective 2 are suggested to be considered in fire hazard assessment. In urban areas such as those in GBA, buildings are often used to store large amounts of combustible materials, which can result in long-lasting post-flashover fires. As a summary, the above completed project studying burning AFCM in building fires have achieved the following:  Improved understanding of smoke emission from burning AFCM in building fires.  Thermal assessment of ACFM bonding material applied to strengthen and retrofit concrete and wood.  Smoke hazards of AFCM should be evaluated in addition to current criteria (stability, integrity and insulation) for assessing fire resistance in fire codes.  Smoke toxicity associated with burning AFCM in buildings is recommended to be assessed by FED2 estimated only by carbon monoxide.

11212217.label: Major findings and research outcome
11212217.value: Burning AFCM produces more smoke than burning other composite materials under low heat flux. However, results are similar to other fibre composite materials, when higher heat fluxes were applied. Window ejecting plume would ignite façades with AFCM. Increasing the heat release rate leads to ejecting plume trajectory getting closer to the wall. The heat-blocking effect of the wall would give quick attachment of the plume trajectory. Three factors affecting the horizontal location of plume trajectory were worked out on the initial velocity, the heat-blocking effect of the wall, and the induced pressure difference. The simple formula to get an appropriate FED2 estimated from peak values of carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide concentrations are similar to average values of other three common formula on estimating FED compiled from the updated literature. Therefore, FED2 can be taken as a parameter for assessing the minimum toxicity effect in burning materials. Thus, FED2 is recommended to be considered by the government in assessing smoke toxicity emitted from burning building materials. Smoke toxicity standards have not yet been included in fire safety building codes and regulations in many places in the Asia-Oceania region. Apart from limiting carbon monoxide concentration, stipulations about limiting other toxic gases are not mentioned in key fire safety building codes. The results compiled from this completed project are integrated to assess the smoke hazards of burning AFCM systems. Key parameters such as the concentration of materials or fire effluent that produces death in 50% of the animals for a specified exposure time (LC50) can be calculated from FED2 using correlation formulae and data from the cone calorimeter. Appropriate fire safety strategies for buildings with AFCM will be formulated based on the results of the smoke hazards associated with large building fires in the project. The results have been published in 5 refereed journals and 1 conference presentation. A summary of the innovative elements of the completed project is: • Hazardous consequences of burning AFCM used in buildings, including bonding to strengthen and retrofit concrete and timber. • Assessing smoke toxicity upon burning AFCM using the bench-scale cone calorimeter tests, medium-scale tests and full-scale burning tests. • Using transient carbon monoxide concentration only is adequate with appropriate adjustment to assess the smoke toxicity upon burning AFCM in building fires. • The approach should address the smoke hazards associated with burning composite materials (with adequate fire resistance rating (FRR) values).

11212217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11212217.value: The approach to address the smoke hazards associated with AFCM in this project should be extended to burning other composite materials based on basalt, carbon and glass fibres too. More full-scale burning tests are recommended to study the thermal responses and smoke emission of those fibre composite systems. Burning AFCM produces more smoke than burning other fibre composite materials. However, situations are different when burning fibre composites under higher heat fluxes. This part should be further studied. Appropriate fire safety strategies for buildings made of AFCM should be formulated based on the results of the smoke hazards associated with burning AFCM in large building fires compiled in this completed project. Fire safety management should be worked out. Additional study should be carried out on protection against smoke hazards provided to firefighting personnel tackling large building fires with AFCM. Apart from limiting carbon monoxide concentration, toxic gases are not even mentioned in local fire safety building code. This part should be further justified in new building projects using AFCM. Finally, health effects from a single exposure to a high dose of fibrous particulates and the potential synergistic effects of exposure to multiple organic chemicals should be assessed in longer terms.

11212217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11212217.value: Aramid fibre composite material (AFCM) has the potential to be a popular material for new construction and repairing old buildings. Applications include strengthening and retrofitting concrete and timber. However, AFCM are combustible. As many large fires had occurred, the fire behaviour of AFCM should be assessed thoroughly. A large amount of smoke would be released upon burning AFCM. Smoke is the main threat to life in accidental building fires due to its toxicity and the reduced visibility and increased evacuation time that it causes. Smoke hazards in burning AFCM were studied in this project. Burning behaviour of AFCM under a non-uniform distribution of radiative heat fluxes in a room fire was assessed using bench-scale cone calorimeter, medium-scale tests with a thermal radiator and full-scale experiments. Thermal behaviour of bonding AFCM to concrete and timber were studied and compared with basalt and carbon. Results are recommended to provide fire safety tests to assess the smoke toxicity of burning AFCM in building fires. Cone calorimeter test with transient carbon monoxide concentration is adequate to assess smoke toxicity by using an equation on fractional effective dose. Workable fire safety guidelines can then be established for AFCM to be used to its full potential.
