11212717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11212717.value: Modern enterprise networks heavily rely on the ubiquitous network middleboxes for advanced traffic-processing functions, such as intrusion detection, web application firewalls, and load balancers. Recent advances in software packet processing and virtualization technologies are further pushing forward the paradigm of migrating middleboxes to third-party providers, e.g., clouds and ISPs, as virtualized services, with well-understood benefits on reduced maintenance cost and increased service scalability. Despite promising, outsourcing middleboxes also raises new fundamental security challenges. This is majorly because the network traffic is now redirected to and processed by service providers, which are not necessarily in the same trust domain as enterprises. Firstly, the new service flow eliminates the enterprise's direct control on critical network functions. Yet, mechanisms to provide enterprises with strong assurances on the execution correctness of outsourced middlebox currently do not exist. Secondly, redirecting traffic to outsourced middleboxes would give service providers full access to all the traffic flows. Sensitive information of enterprises might be unwillingly revealed due to the exposure of traffic payloads and proprietary middlebox rules. How to systematically and efficiently address these new security challenges remains largely unexplored in the literature. In this project, we will develop algorithms and schemes to enable trustworthy and secure traffic processing in outsourced middelexboxes, helping enterprises to extend their visibility into outsourced middleboxes and protect their privacy. Those designs are expected to be seamlessly integrated into off-the-shelf network architectures with full-fledged implementation. Achieving these objectives is non-trivial. For practical performance, we have to exclude the generic security primitives with considerable computation and bandwidth overhead, as they would diminish the benefits of middlebox outsourcing. For the system to be readily deployable in the minimally intrusive way, we will further ensure that the proposed designs neither alter original traffic flows nor impose substantial efforts on current network entities. To this end, we will specifically design: 1) new practical execution assurance schemes with tunable level of assurances to enforce middleboxes and middlebox service chains to process packets via designated functions as intended; 2) privacy-preserving packet processing algorithms for pattern matching and range matching functions with strong protection on both packet contents and middelbox rules; 3) low-level network protocols to be implemented on the production software middlebox framework and readily compatible in existing outsourced middlebox service flows. The results will bridge the gaps which are not handled by current networks, and further contribute to the broader goal of securely adopting network function virtualization technologies. 網絡中間件在現代企業網絡中至關重要。它們能夠執行諸如入侵檢測、防火墻、負載均衡等複雜的網絡處理任務。近年來，隨著虛擬化技術的快速發展，將網絡中間件部署到第三方服務提供商（例如公有雲平台），能夠幫助企業有效降低維護成本并獲得更好的拓展性。但與此同時，外包網絡中間件會帶來新的安全隱患。其根本原因在於，企業的網絡流量需要被重定向到外部的服務提供商處理，而外部的服務提供商往往與企業不在相同的信任域中。首先，該模式使企業無法對網絡功能進行直接控制，而目前尚未存在一種有效的機制來確保外包網絡中間件的正確運行。其次，服務提供商能完全訪問所有重定向的流量，而這些網絡流量以及專有的中間件規則可能包含企業的敏感信息。現有工作尚未充分研究如何系統地、有效地解決這些新的安全問題。 本項目旨在研發一套算法及系統框架，用以實現外包中間件中可信、安全的網絡流量處理，從而保護企業的隱私。此外，該系統需要能夠兼容現有的網絡架構。為實現這些目標，該項目將面臨以下兩方面挑戰。其一，在增加安全性保護的同時應盡量減少性能的損失；其二，在系統部署的過程中應盡量減少對當前網絡實體所造成的改動。具體而言，本項目將實現以下三方面內容：一、研發一套新的運行保障框架，并支持在中間件服務中針對不同安全性進行調節。二、設計一組新的隱私保護算法，從而在模式匹配和範圍匹配的網絡中間件操作中對網絡數據內容進行保護。三、實現基於產品級中間件框架的底層網絡協議，從而兼容當前外包網絡中間件的服務模式。本項目的順利開展將會有效解決當前外包網絡中間件中所存在的安全問題，從而進一步推動網絡功能虛擬化技術在實際應用中的發展。

11213117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11213117.value: Unexpected site condition presents a major risk in geotechnical construction, and it occurs when the expected ground condition interpreted from site investigation is significantly and adversely different from the actual ground condition found during construction. It often causes significant project delays and expensive over-budget. The Guangzhou-Shenzhen-Hong Kong Express Rail Link construction project in 2014, for example, had a budget of HK$67 billion, but suffered from at least a two-year project delay and required an extra HK$20 billion. Unexpected site condition was listed as a main reason for the delay and overspending. The problem of unexpected site condition is obviously due to insufficient site investigation. To avoid this problem, the sufficiency of site investigation should be evaluated, and proper sufficiency must be achieved. However, NO scientific or quantitative method currently exists to evaluate the sufficiency of site investigation or to quantify statistical uncertainty that occurs when interpreting ground condition from sparse and limited site investigation data. Conventional statistical methods, or even geostatistical methods, only have limited applications in geotechnical site investigation, as geotechnical data are spatially correlated, but only sparsely measured during site investigation. This project aims to develop novel statistical methods and tools (e.g., statistical charts and computer software) to quantify statistical uncertainty associated with interpretation of spatially correlated, but sparsely measured, site investigation data and to evaluate the sufficiency of site investigation. The proposed methods are based on an innovative sampling theorem called compressed/compressive sensing/sampling (CS), which was awarded the prestigious Shaw Prize (widely regarded as the “Nobel of the East”) in mathematical sciences in 2013. The PI has performed preliminary studies on CS-based interpretation of site investigation data and obtained promising results. Major research components of the project include: (1) theoretical development of Bayesian CS (BCS) methods for statistical uncertainty quantification, (2) development of BCS-based methods and statistical charts for evaluating site investigation sufficiency, (3) calibration of the developed methods and statistical charts using field data and observations, and (4) development of computer software for the proposed methods. For the first time ever in geotechnical engineering, this project will provide rational and quantitative methods for evaluating site investigation sufficiency. It will also offer statistical charts and computer software to facilitate application of the proposed methods in engineering practices. The research outcome will be beneficial to geotechnical practice in Hong Kong, where many mega-infrastructure projects are currently in progress, and throughout the world. 不可预见的地质条件是指地质勘探中预期的地质状况与施工期间发现的实际地质状况有很大的差别。它是岩土工程项目的一个重大风险，常常导致项目的延误和预算的超支。以香港高铁为例：2014年香港高铁超支200亿港元，项目延误2年。不可预见的地质条件是项目延迟和超支的主要原因之一。地质勘探不足是出现不可预见的地质条件的主要原因。为了避免这一问题，必须对地质勘探的充足性进行评估。然而，目前还没有科学或定量的方法来评估地质勘探的充足性，并量化从稀疏、有限的地质勘探数据分析地质条件时出现的不确定性。因为岩土数据在空间上是相关的，但地质勘探只能进行稀疏测量，传统的统计方法，甚至是地质统计学方法，在岩土地质勘探中的应用有限。本项目将开发基于贝叶斯压缩感知的统计方法，开创性提出对地质勘探充足性的评估方法。

11213117.label: Realisation of objectives
11213117.value: All project objectives have been successfully achieved. Bayesian compressive sampling (BCS) has been systematically extended to 2D and 3D cases and used to quantify statistical uncertainty associated with the interpretation of 2D/3D geotechnical data from sparsely measured data points. Extensive parametric studies have been carried out using the developed BCS methods for quantifying the relationship between the number of measurement data points and quality of the recovered/interpreted geotechnical data. A series of statistical charts has been developed that relate the quality of the interpretation results to both the number of measurement data points and variability of the geotechnical properties of interest. A software package has also been developed to facilitate application of the developed methods. The project has resulted in publications of 24 papers in top journals, four conference papers (including one keynote lecture in the top international specialty conference), and training and graduation of two PhD students (see sections 8, 9, and 10). One journal paper from this project was awarded the Best Paper Award in 2020 by the ASCE-ASME Journal of Risk and Uncertainty in Engineering Systems, Part A: Civil Engineering. Some details on the 2D/3D BCS methods, the associated random field simulations for uncertainty quantification, and development of statistical charts are given in the following paragraphs, respectively. 2D BCS method has been formulated (Zhao et al. 2018, see Paper 1 in Section 8) and subsequently extended to 3D case (Zhao and Wang 2021, see Paper 20 in Section 8). To quantify uncertainty associated with the BCS interpretation of 2D/3D data, 3D random field generator has also been developed to directly generate 3D random field samples from sparse measurements using Markov chain Monte Carlo simulation (Zhao and Wang 2020, see Paper 10 in Section 8). The developed methods are non-parametric and data-driven. It takes sparse measurements and their corresponding 3D spatial coordinates as input and returns many high-resolution non-stationary non-Gaussian 3D random field samples as output. The developed methods effectively tackle the long-lasting challenge in selection of suitable parametric function forms for trend function, auto-correlation function, or marginal probability density function and proper estimation of their parameters from sparse measurements, particularly for non-stationary, non-Gaussian data often encountered in geotechnical engineering. The methods have been illustrated and validated using both simulated and real geotechnical data (e.g., Hu and Wang 2020, See Paper 12 in Section 8; Guan et al. 2021, See Paper 15 in Section 8), and they perform reasonably well. Using the developed BCS methods, extensive parametric studies have been carried out to develop statistical charts for determination of sample size at different levels of both accuracy and confidence for point measurements in geotechnical site investigation (Guan and Wang 2020, see Paper 7 in Section 8). In addition, extensive parametric studies were performed for line measurements (e.g., cone penetration tests, CPT, or standard penetration tests, SPT) in geotechnical site investigation (Guan and Wang 2021a&b, see Papers 17 and 21 in Section 8). The extensive parametric studies cover typical CPT/SPT data encountered in geotechnical engineering practice and use the developed BCS methods to interpolate the spatially varying, but correlated, CPT/SPT data along both depth and horizontal directions simultaneously and quantify their uncertainty using random field simulations. The statistical charts were illustrated and validated using real CPT/SPT data, and they were shown to perform well. To facilitate the application of the developed methods by geotechnical practitioners, a computer software called Analytics of Sparse Spatial Data using Bayesian Compressive Sampling (ASSD-BCS) has been developed and posted on the PI’s webpage for open access (https://sites.google.com/site/yuwangcityu/software-download). The software supports 1D, 2D and 3D data, and it can be used to perform spatial interpolation or simulate random field samples directly from sparse measurements.

11213117.label: Major findings and research outcome
11213117.value: Site investigation is indispensable in geotechnical practice, but only a small portion of the soil affected by the intended geotechnical construction is examined and/or tested in the laboratory or in situ, leading to significant uncertainties in site investigation results. The uncertainty in the site investigation results depends greatly on the number of specimens tested (i.e. sample size) during site investigation. In many other areas that involve sampling, such as polls, surveys and quality control, sample sizes are often determined using statistical charts, based on the target levels of accuracy and confidence. However, conventional statistical charts, which only deal with independent data, are seldom used in geotechnical site investigation, because geotechnical data are usually spatially correlated. No statistical chart with consideration of spatial correlation is available for determining sample sizes in geotechnical site investigation. This project developed a novel statistical method called Bayesian compressive sampling/sensing (BCS) and statistical charts to quantify statistical uncertainty associated with interpretation of spatially correlated, but sparsely measured, site investigation data and to evaluate the sufficiency of site investigation. BCS is non-parametric and data-driven, and it effectively tackles the long-lasting challenge in selection of suitable parametric function forms for trend function, auto-correlation function, or marginal probability density function and proper estimation of their parameters from sparse measurements, particularly for non-stationary, non-Gaussian data often encountered in geotechnical engineering. The developed methods and statistical charts have been illustrated and validated using both simulated and real geotechnical data, and they were shown to perform well. As summarized in Part C, this project has led to 24 papers published in top international journals, four international conference papers (including one keynote lecture in a top international specialty conference), and a Best Paper Award in 2020 from the ASCE-ASME Journal of Risk and Uncertainty in Engineering Systems, Part A: Civil Engineering. Two PhD student have been trained under this project and successfully graduated.

11213117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11213117.value: This project focused on spatial interpolation and random field simulation directly from sparse measurements to quantify the associated uncertainty for evaluation of site investigation sufficiency. The quantified uncertainty can be further used to optimize the planning and execution of site investigation (e.g., determination of sampling locations and sequences). In other words, based on the BCS results from existing site investigation data, spatial distribution of the uncertainty can be used to determine whether or not additional measurement is needed and the corresponding optimal location. This will further maximize values of every data point obtained in site investigation.

11213517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11213517.value: The axial capacity of driven piles in crushable soils presents a high degree of uncertainty for geotechnical engineers. The source of uncertainty comes from a lack of a full understanding of the mechanisms controlling penetration into the soil. Penetration resistance is known to be a function of many variables including soil crushability, initial soil density and stress level, soil gradation, pile diameter, and pile driven depth, etc. Due to the inability to quantify the effects of these variables on the pile capacity, current design methods adopted by the pile industry can be unreliable and unable to capture the behavior observed in the field. This deficiency is critical for a metropolitan city like Hong Kong, where crushable soils as diverse as offshore skeletal carbonate sediments and highly weathered decomposed granites or volcanics are found. In this proposal, we propose a comprehensive investigation of the time-dependent load carrying capacity behavior of driven piles in crushable granular soils using a coupled discrete-continuum modeling approach with experimental calibration. The detailed micromechanics underlying the pile-soil interaction will be handled by the Discrete Element Method (DEM) while the wider region of foundation soil away from the pile will be modeled using the Finite Element Method (FEM) or Finite Difference Method (FDM). The major goal of the proposed research is to develop an in-depth understanding of the grain-scale mechanisms that control the pile capacity under the influence of particle breakage during pile installation and soil ageing after installation. The outcome of this research will be a significant advancement of knowledge of the pile capacity behavior in crushable, coarse-grained soils in both short-term conditions following pile installation and long-term conditions following pile setup. The benefits of this research come from an improved understanding of the time-dependent pile capacity behavior, especially of the processes, physics and mechanisms at the soil grain scale. This improved understanding will translate into an enhanced ability of engineers to make more economic designs of pile foundations, particularly in incorporating critical, complex soil behavior such as grain crushing, interface friction degradation, soil creep and soil ageing. It is expected that the improved pile foundation designs will lead to more construction cost savings in Hong Kong and worldwide in the future. 破碎性砂土中打入桩的轴向承载力研究仍然是岩土工程中一个充满不确定性的课题。这种不确定性源自对桩的打入机理缺乏充分的认识。众所周知打入桩的轴向承载力是包括土体破碎性、初始密实度、应力水平、颗粒级配、桩体直径和打入深度等在内的多项参数的复杂函数。由于未能量化这些参数对桩基承载力的影响，目前被工业界采用的桩基设计方法可能不是完全可靠的，并且可能不能捕捉到现场观测到的一些现象。这种不足对于像香港这样，发现了诸如强风化分解的花岗岩或者火山岩这类的可破碎土的大城市来说是非常重要的。 在本方案中，提出了一个在可破碎颗粒土中，考虑打入桩的承载能力和性能的时间效应，采用耦合的离散-连续建模方法及试验对比的详细研究方案。桩-土相互作用的微观力学机理将通过离散元（DEM）来模拟，而离桩身较远的地基土将用有限元(FEM)或者有限差分法(FDM)来模拟。研究的主要目标是对颗粒尺寸上在桩打入过程中颗粒破碎及成桩后土老化对桩承载力的影响机理有更深入的了解。 本研究的预期成果是对在可破碎粗粒土中，成桩后桩的短期及长期承载性能的认识有重大进展。研究的效益源自对桩承载性能的时间效应有更好的理解，特别是对土颗粒尺寸级别的过程、现象和机理有更深入了解。这种认识上的进步将提高工程师设计出更加经济的桩基础的能力，尤其是面临诸如颗粒破碎、界面摩擦衰减、蠕动及老化等危险、复杂土性时。在未来，这种桩基设计理论上的进步在香港和全世界将节约更多的建设成本。

11213517.label: Realisation of objectives
11213517.value: Objective 1: This objective has been fully achieved. A two-dimensional discrete element method (DEM) model of the monotonic pile installation in crushable sands was constructed. The particle breakage was included in the model by setting a crushable zone around a pile that was filled with parallel-bonded agglomerates. Parametric studies were carried out to examine the effects of initial in situ vertical stress, soil void ratio, and particle crushability on the penetration resistance behavior. The validity of the DEM model was examined by comparing the simulation data with published results from laboratory centrifuge and calibration chamber tests on model pile installation. A variety of DEM analysis techniques were employed to make a detailed discrete-continuum study on the pile penetration mechanisms, particularly on the particle breakage-related soil mechanics incurred during the penetration process. Objective 2: This objective has been fully achieved. Firstly, 2D DEM Simulation results show that the in situ stress and particle breakage are the two competing factors dominating the tip resistance behavior. The underlying mechanism was elucidated through the analysis of stress and strain paths derived from pre-assigned sampling windows and their full-field distributions. Secondly, numerical experiments are conducted to investigate the effects of initial sample porosity, particle crushability, initial stress state, the ratio of pile diameter to median particle diameter and the ratio of model width to pile diameter on the pile penetration behavior. A new stress normalization method is adopted to synthesize the data at different driven depth from the simulations. The normalized vertical and horizontal stress fields surrounding the pile show invariable pattern of stress distribution, suggesting a unique penetration mechanism independent of the penetration depth. Thirdly, a study was made on the influence of lateral boundary condition on the shaft resistance of a pile driven into a crushable sand using the established DEM model. The interface shear test was performed under three different types of normal boundary condition, namely, constant normal load (CNL), constant normal stiffness (CNS), and constant volume (CV) boundary conditions. It is found that the behavior of a particle group has reached the peak state below the pile tip and the critical state after it reaches the pile shaft. The influence of normal boundary condition on the stress ratio at the critical state is not obvious. Objective 3: This objective has been fully achieved. Firstly, the problem of creep of crushable sands undergoing one-dimensional (1D) compression using three-dimensional (3D) DEM simulation. The rate process theory (RPT) based creep contact model considering rolling resistance and a probabilistic particle fracture model satisfying mass conservation are incorporated into a large-scale DEM simulation. The coupled effects of the interparticle sliding and delayed particle fracture, and the influences of rolling resistance, initial porosity and characteristic particle strength on the creep behavior are then investigated. The high capabilities of the model in reproducing many facets of the soil behavior during the 1D compression and creep seen in the laboratory is demonstrated by comparing the simulation results with published experimental data. Secondly, the creep and stress relaxation behaviors under the triaxial shearing of an idealized granular soil were studied using the three-dimensional discrete element method, into which the rate process theory was incorporated to enable simulation of these two time-dependent physical processes by a high-performance computing facility. The model was validated by comparing the simulation results with published experimental data. The study is focused on the effects of deviatoric stress during triaxial shearing of the granular soils on their creep and stress relaxation behaviors. In particular, to gain insights into their micromechanical mechanisms, a careful examination was made of the relationship between the shear-strain localizations occurring during creep and triaxial shearing, and the evolution of the contact number, average contact forces, and shear-induced anisotropies during these two time-dependent processes. The results indicate that the deviatoric stress level strongly affects the rates of creep strain and stress relaxation and dictates whether creep rupture will occur. These two time-dependent processes of the granular soil are also found to be isotach, which is evidenced by a unique normalized stress–strain relationship derived from the creep and stress relaxation tests. Objective 4: This objective has been fully achieved. The 3D DEM model of the penetration test is made up of a cylindrical container filled with balls and model pile with a tip angle of 60° pushed gradually into the granular foundation. The friction coefficient of the model pile and fixed boundary walls were set to 0.5. The pile diameter, B, is 8 mm and the model has a dimension of 240 mm (D) × 240 mm (H), where D is the diameter of the cylindrical container and H is the height of the granular foundation. The gradually increase in particle diameter is to ensure that small particles will not migrate into the voids between the adjacent larger particles. The tensile strength of particles in an outer region is lower than that in an inner region due to the scaled particle size. In order that the tensile strength remains unscaled for region II-VII. Through the incorporation of the probabilistic particle fracture model into large-scale 3D DEM models, the stress-strain behavior of the DEM material was first characterized by means of the numerical direct shear tests. The volumetric response during shearing becomes much more contractive as the particle strength is decreased. The effects of vertical stress field, initial porosity, particle strength and rolling resistance on the penetration resistance were investigated to demonstrate the high capabilities of the model in reproducing many facets of the soil mechanics during the installation process seen in the physical tests. Then, the piles were fixed for setup. After setup for 80s of simulation time, the shaft resistance of the driven pile gains about 5%. This positive gain in capacity with time is due to the increase contact number due to rearrangement of particles, soil homogenization and the dissipation of stress concentration. Objective 5: This objective has been partially achieved. The initial vertical stress field was varied by employing an artificially raised gravity acceleration of 50g or 100g that was similar to the physical effects attained in a centrifuge test. Each pile penetration test is denoted using a code of “sf0-n0- ar-ag”, where ag is the gravity acceleration. Seven numerical penetration tests were conducted. Tests were grouped to examine different issues that influence the penetration results. Specifically, the particle crushability was defined by different sf0. The model pile is pushed monotonically into the granular foundation at a constant rate of 0.1 mm/s. The simulation results show that both the pile tip and shaft resistance vary with time. After 10 s of fluctuation, both the tip and shaft resistance smoothly decrease with the time. This stress softening behavior is similar to the creep behavior observed in one-dimensional compress tests. The increase of the shaft resistance is obvious due to pile setup, while the tip resistance almost remains unchanged. Evidently, the positive gain in capacity during setup mainly attributes to the increase of shaft resistance. Some further simulation works on the effects of pile size/scale and penetration rate on the pile setup behavior is still ongoing.

11213517.label: Major findings and research outcome
11213517.value: 1. Through a careful construction of the pile–sand interaction model and the application of a series of DEM analysis techniques, we conducted a detailed and in-depth discrete-continuum study on the pile penetration mechanism, elucidating the effects of and interplay between the in situ vertical stress field, soil crushability, and void ratio on the penetration behavior (Wang & Zhao, 2014). The high capabilities of the model in reproducing many facets of the soil mechanics during the installation process seen in the laboratory or field, particularly the dominant influence of the in situ vertical stress on the tip resistance in a low crushability sand, the competition between particle breakage and in situ stress in controlling the tip resistance as the soil crushability increases, as well as the essential strain reversal phenomenon in a soil element flowing past a “stationary” pile (Liu & Wang, 2016; Wang et al., 2017). 2. Through the incorporation of the RPT-based creep model considering rolling resistance and a probabilistic particle fracture model satisfying mass conservation into a large-scale DEM simulation, parallel computation of the large-scale simulation using the open-source code LIGGGHTS has been successfully made to investigate the realistic creep behavior of sands. The validity of the model was demonstrated by comparing the simulation results with published experimental data of oedometer and triaxial tests (Liu et al., 2019). 3. A complete and coherent understanding of the macro- and micro-mechanics underlying creep and stress relaxation tests on sand is achieved by analyzing the DEM simulation results to reveal various aspects of the behavior of sand, including the stress–strain–strain rate relationships, strain localization, contact number and contact force, and stress-induced anisotropy. This provides a comprehensive picture of these two time-dependent processes at the particle level in order to explain the deformation mechanism up to shear failure, i.e., creep rupture (Wang & Xia, 2021). 4. A significant line of research that was not originally planned in this project but was conducted to support the fundamental investigation of the soil mechanics of pile driving is the X-ray CT testing (Cheng & Wang, 2019, 2020; Zhao et al., 2020) and DEM modelling of sand particle breakage behavior (e.g., Wu & Wang, 2018, 2019; Wang & Wu, 2020; Zhou et al., 2020; Xiong et al., 2020; Xiong & Wang, 2021; Wu et al., 2021).

11213517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11213517.value: A great potential exists in the further development of this research. The following research agendas that are expected to advance both the fundamental and applied aspects of the subject are proposed: 1) incorporating the real particle morphology into the DEM modelling of pile-soil interaction problem; 2) incorporating the real particle breakage behavior into the DEM modelling of pile-soil interaction problem; 3) exploring the pile installation methods (e.g., pile driving or jacking) on the pile setup behavior; 4) performing large-scale DEM modelling of pile-soil interaction and aging problems.

11213517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11213517.value: In this research project, the pile “setup” phenomenon which refers to a considerable gain in pile capacity with time in sandy soils after the pile installation has been carefully investigated. This phenomenon is generally regarded as a result of soil creep and ageing. The increase of shaft resistance, which accounts for the majority of the gain in pile capacity, results from two related processes: an increase of radial effective stress due to soil creep, and an enhanced soil stiffness, dilatancy and strength during loading as a result of soil ageing. The above processes have been explored using a 3D DEM modelling approach which incorporates the rate process theory (RPT)-based contact creep model of granular materials. The outcome of this research has made a significant advancement of knowledge of the time-dependent pile capacity behavior. The benefits of this research come from an improved understanding of the time-dependent pile capacity behavior, especially of the processes, physics and mechanisms at the soil grain scale. This improved understanding will translate into an enhanced ability of engineers to make more economic designs of pile foundations, particularly in incorporating critical, complex soil behavior such as grain crushing, interface friction degradation, soil creep and soil ageing.

11213717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11213717.value: 小腦是一種強大的自適應控制器，可以調節許多對日常生活甚至生存至關重要的功能。前庭眼反射（VOR）和視動反射（OKR）是兩個重要的反射眼運動機制，可確保動物和/或目標移動期間的穩定視野，這也是工程控制中遇到的常見問題。它們是自適應的，因為它們需要補償身體和環境以及神經電路的變化。他們的適應與其組織良好的電路和眾多可塑性實現的小腦功能密切相關。然而，分子層中間神經元（MLI）在小腦介導的學習和控制中的計算作用尚未得到很好的理解。最近的研究表明，對Purkinje（PKJ）細胞具有缺失的MLI抑制的突變小鼠表現出VOR / OKR適應的缺陷。體外研究表明，MLI至PKJ連接遵循特定的空間組織，並由突觸可塑性調節。然而，VOR / OKR的計算小腦模型可以將這些發現連接起來，以幫助解決MLI對網絡規模上的行為水平的影響。 在這個項目中，我們將通過綜合建模和硬件測試方法來研究MLI的計算作用。我們將首先開發VOR / OKR的小腦刺激神經網絡模型，以研究（1）MLI-PKJ連接的空間組織的影響;和（2）PKI發射模式和VOR / OKR學習時MLI突觸的可塑性。它們如何影響神經發射模式，從而在模擬中系統地表徵其行為。其次，隨著小腦模型與環境的閉環運行，MLI可能如何影響行為將被機器人系統調查。我們將開發一個實時的硬件系統來實現小腦模型，用於控制模擬VOR / OKR的目標穩定任務的移動機器人。硬件仿真係統將針對小腦模型進行優化，並進行模塊化，方便將來的擴展。機器人測試允許在存在物理系統和通信延遲的干擾的情況下，評估MLI影​​響下小腦模型的魯棒性。這些結果還將提供小腦控制器潛在功能優勢的證據。一起，這個項目將促進我們對小腦計算機制的理解，這將為我們的大腦逆向工程提供新的見解，並開發更自適應和更強大的機器人控制。

11213717.label: Realisation of objectives
11213717.value: In studying the computational of the cerebellum-dependent motor learning (Objective 1), we have performed comprehensive simulation to study a broad aspect of the model behavior as governed by the neural circuit properties. First, in investigating potential mechanisms contributing to failure of learning of phase rehearsal of vestibulo-ocular reflex (VOR), we have developed a spiking neural network model of cerebellum in which head movement is encoded as spike train input conveyed by 100 mossy fibers (MF), which project to 12800 granule cells (GR) and 1 medial vestibular nucleus (VN). A climbing fiber (CF) encoding the retinal slip provides input from 1 inferior olive (IO) to 16 PKJ. Synapses from parallel fiber (PF) to PKJ is the learning site where long-term depression (LTD) and long-term potentiation (LTP) are induced. Eye movements are controlled by activities of VN. In the wild-type model, the gain decreased over the first 50 trials and then increased afterwards over the next 150 trials. At the same time, the phase shift kept increasing (up to ~130) over the entire 200 trials of training. On the other hand, the mutant model demonstrated decrease in gain over the 200 trials and very minor change in the phase of VN firing. These results are comparable to the results of behavioural experiments in Wulff et al. Our model predicted that the swing of PKJ firing increased in both wild-type and mutant models during training, as a result of dominating LTP in the first half cycle and superior LTD in the second half. Furthermore, such increase is more rapid in the wild-type than the mutant model. This is because in the mutant model, baseline synaptic weights of PF-PKJ were lowered to maintain similar mean firing rate of PKJ due to the lack of BS inhibition. In this regard, the strength of LTP and LTD was also lowered in the mutant model. As a result, inhibition on VN by PKJ reduced the swing of VN firing and only in the wild-type model, such inhibition is sufficiently strong to reverse the swinging phase of VN firing, leading to phase reversal of VOR. As such, BS cells may indirectly contribute to control the strength of plasticity through altering the relative strength of excitation-to-inhibition on PKJ. Additional simulations showed that the phase shift of VN response may be progressively modulated by varying the strength of BS inhibition. We further studied the contribution of the molecular interneurons in a modified cerebellum model of delayed eyeblink conditioning (DEB) among other aspects of the model behavior. We have studied how blocking these interneurons may affect amplitude and timing of the conditioned response. Our simulation shows that more BS are blocked, hence weaker inhibition to PKJ, the development of both CR amplitudes and CR durations is slowed, and the final amplitudes and durations are reduced. Actually, this is consistent with previous animal experiments, where deficits in BS inputs impair both learning rates and CR amplitudes of DEB conditioning. One possible reason could be that the PKJ activities under CS are elevated without adequate suppression strengths from BS, even after LTD. As a result, when a similar amount of LTD is induced, the DCN would receive a stronger level of PC inhibition, which push-offs the development of CR and affects the consequent size of CR. When a larger population of BS is reserved, a greater CR would be produced, such that the BS firing is progressively enlarged and extended through feedback, which in turn suppress PC and help develop larger CRs. Together, these results imply that BS would affect the utilization of feedback pathways in DEB conditioning by controlling the excitation to inhibition balance of PKJ. As such, our modeling studies have identified some novel roles of the molecular layer interneurons in different cerebellum-dependent learning behavior. In realizing Objectives 2 and 3, we have first transplanted the simulation environment onto MATLAB for effective investigation. In order to handle the large-scale spiking neural network model, the cerebellum model was deployed on MATLAB with the support of a CUDA-enabled GPU (Nvidia) for fast parallel computing. The properties and activities of all neurons and synapses were constructed as gpuArrays in MATLAB. The simulation speed was hence significantly increased for efficient investigation of a range of various parameter manipulation. This provides a practical tools for testing various model parameters with high efficiency. Taking advantages of this, we investigated how our cerebellum neural network model might work on a robotic system. We designed a robotic system where the robot car velocity is controlled automatically by a brain-inspired controller to meet the velocity requirements. The robotic system contains a simulation environment, a robot car, and a brain-inspired controller. In this classical robotic control task, the brain-inspired controller as the control agent is expected to adjust the current robot car velocity to the target velocity given by the environment with physical constraints, such as friction, air resistance and idle acceleration. This controller was trained under a bio-inspired synaptic learning rule to make decisions through controlling a throttle pedal or a brake pedal, both of which are analog. The robotic model was transplanted from ROS (Robot Operating System, open sourced and BSD licensed) to a custom MATLAB environment. The brain-inspired control was designed to learn to drive the robotic car to the target velocity which was randomly generated between the range of 0-10 m/s by the environment. We incorporated a large-scale cerebellum spiking neuron model (modified from Objective 1) as the brain-inspired controller (~50,000 cells and >100,000 connections). It contains two cerebellar cortexes that converge their outputs as the final actions to control the robot car. Here, we encoded the difference of current velocity and target velocity into Poisson spikes and provided them to the GR cells (content signals, CS) and IO (error signals, ES) separately. In this case, the difference in current and target velocity mimic the retinal slip in a VOR task and the cerebellum controller has to learn to close this gap for proper target tracking, subject to the external (e.g. wind and rolling resistance) and internal (e.g. idle acceleration) disturbance. We computed the average firing rates of CN (FRCN) during the past 10ms window in both cortexes separately to serve as the percentage to throttle or brake. For each timestep, the environment would assess the controller to feed velocity information and collect the returned decision, which was used to update the robot car in the next timestep. We showed that such associative learning approach can effectively be implemented on a physical system for robust and flexible learning such that the robot car can track a range of target velocity with smooth control. When considering the gradually increasing and converging rewards achieved by the controller throughout the training, this testifies that our synaptic learning rule was well incorporated into the velocity control task, and the controller has learned to improve its performance generally with more simulations.

11213717.label: Major findings and research outcome
11213717.value: Our studies have shed new lights on the understanding of how the neural circuitry in the cerebellum affects the behavior using a realistic computational model. The simulation model can pinpoint specific deficits in the cerebellum circuit and study the corresponding influence on the well-characterized motor learning at behavior level. This is difficult to achieve in in vivo experiment given the high redundancy of the structure and the presence of multi-scale long-term plasticity mechanisms. In particular, we have shown that the molecular layer interneurons are critical for adjusting the inhibition-to-excitation balance at the PKJ which is the sole output of the cerebellum cortex and hence controls the downstream motor output consequent to the learning inside and outside of the cerebellum cortex. We have also shown that such associative learning based control can be a useful and flexible controller for physical system and could potentially shed new light on bio-inspired controller for more flexible and robust application. Some of our results have been presented orally in IEEE EMBC 2018. Another journal manuscript is under preparation. These modeling work has also enlightened our new experimental search for novel pathway in the cerebellum neural circuitry, which has led to our new collaboration with Prof. Sui’s team in Army Medical University, Chongqing, China.

11213717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11213717.value: Further development of this project can put the computational model to testing on clinical condition. For example, ataxia is a motor dyfunction resulted from cerebellum deficit. The model can help pinpoint specific deficit that cause the wide spectrum of symptoms in these motor dyfunction and aid diagnosis and treatment planning. The model may be also used for drug screening by simulating and predicting potential drug effects on the neural function systematically.

11213717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11213717.value: The cerebellum is an important brain region that adapts our motor behavior for the changes in the body and environment as well as the neural circuitry. While the anatomy of the cerebellum is relatively well-understood, how information is being processed in it is still an active area of research. Interestingly, cerebellum has a relatively large number of inhibitory neurons, called molecular layer interneurons, but their computational role remains unclear to the neuroscientists. We have performed comprehensive simulation studies and showed that these inhibitory neurons act like a critical knob in tuning the timing and magnitude of the motor output. We have also shown that this brain controller can also learn in a physical system and can be useful for flexible control of a robotic car for velocity tracking, demonstrating its potential application in engineering task.

11213817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11213817.value: 細胞是一種復雜且動態的生物系統，其生物物理學特性和形態特徵會隨時間改變，尤其是當細胞受到來自外部的物理或化學刺激時。舉例來說，細胞是以指數速率生長還是以線性速率生長？對一個細胞死亡的準確定義又是什麽？這些方面的爭論仍在繼續。因此，近年來單細胞分析已經成為發展最迅速的研究領域之一，且該領域已經與基因組學、轉錄組學、蛋白質組學、代謝組學等廣泛結合起來。比如在幾乎所有與細胞生物學相關的研究領域中，對單細胞特性的認識和了解都是特別重要的。可達到單個細胞水平的分析技術已經被用於生物物理學、細胞力學、生物運動學、形態學以及單個細胞形貌的探索研究。舉例來說，借助微電機系統(MEMS)和微流體技術，對單細胞質量與密度的分析就是近來開發出的兩種應用。單個細胞的質量是其最基本的物理性質，顯示了細胞代謝率及其命運；而單個細胞的密度則能夠揭示更多細胞健康狀態方面的細節。對細胞質量和密度的測定已成為一種有效監測細胞回應外部刺激(如藥物或環境的改變)的評估方法。在此項目中，我們結合光誘導動電學(OEK)、微流控技術以及微成像分析，提出開發一個新型微流控光學 (OMF) 平台，用於提取單個細胞在生物運動學、生物物理學及形態學方面的特徵。相較已存在的單細胞分析方法，這項技術具備重要且獨特的優勢。通過非侵入式的免標記過程實現，擁有一個簡單的微流體結構和相對較低的生產檢測成本，並且還可利用可見光動態操作細胞。此技術能實現提取超過40個單細胞特徵，且效率可能高於每小時一萬個細胞。這些獨特的優勢也使得該平台能夠實時測定單細胞健康狀態，同時可能識別活細胞與死細胞且正確率高達95%以上，而這將有助於觀察藥物對單個細胞的影響。項目中，我們將致力於實現以下四個主要技術目標：1、基於光誘導動電學，開發一個微流控光學(OMF)平台，用於在微流芯片內的高生產量單細胞操作；2、設計並開發一個基於顯微成像分析的單細胞表徵算法，用於高生產量、高含量的細胞特徵提取，我們期待對每個細胞提取超過40個特徵，其中包括細胞質量、密度以及其他生物運動學、生物物理學、形態學和生物化學方面的特徵；3、研究一些單細胞特徵，作為細胞生存狀態的重要指標，比如識別一個細胞已經死亡還是活著；4、用該微流控光學平台檢測各類藥物對改變人或老鼠的白血病細胞狀態的效果，比如我們將探尋使用提取出的一些特徵作為免標記(如非熒光的)標簽的可能性，該類標簽用於標記對不同種藥物的單細胞反應。為了展示這項新技術，我們需要通過一些關鍵性技術的挑戰：1、找到適合的細胞培養液，其需要能夠在細胞周圍維持適當的滲透壓，同時又能在光誘導動電微流芯片內產生足夠的介電電泳力來操控細胞的位移；2、開發一個自動且可靠的顯微成像分析算法，用於識別平台所捕捉到的圖像所顯視的細胞輪廓，由此將能夠提供精準的單個細胞的形態描述；3、闡明單個細胞的物理參數在用藥後發生改變的基本原理。如果我們能夠克服這些技術難題，我們將成為世界上首次實現一種基於單細胞水平、多物理參數圖像分析的非侵入式、高生產量、高含量藥物的篩選技術。這項技術將為藥物篩選與生物科學的研究提供具有革命性意義的新工具。

11213817.label: Realisation of objectives
11213817.value: All five key objectives of this this project were successfully completed. The methodology and processes used to complete these objectives are described below. Objective #1: We have demonstrated an opto-microfluidics (OMF) platform that is capable of measuring multiple physical parameters of single cells with high-throughput capability, i.e., the system is scalable to analyze about 25,000 cells/hour (our original objective only targeted ~10,000 cells/hour). The OMF system was developed as an optically-induced dielectrophoresis (ODEP) system for cell manipulation, and consists of an OEK chip, a microscope, a projector, a signal generator and a computer. The OEK chip consists of a sandwich structure, i.e., Aa photoconductive layer comprising of hydrogenated amorphous silicon (a-Si:H) was deposited on indium tin oxide-coated glass (ITO Glass). When a digital image is projected onto the photoconductive layer, the electrical conductivity on the illuminated area increases locally and forms an optical electrode. Utilizing the DEP force that is induced by this type of optical electrode, we have successfully manipulated cells and measured the density and mass of individual cells. The platform was developed based on a monocular microscope (NIKON, Ti-E). A high-speed camera (Andor, Zyla 5.5MP sCOMS) and a CFI Super Plan Fluor lens (ELWD, 20X, N.A. 0.45, and W.D. 8.2~6.9 mm) were used to record the experiments. A 2000X2000 pixel field-of-view was sufficient to accommodate approximately 100 cells. The illumination source was provided by a halogen lamp (12 V–100 W LL). The top and bottom ITO glass chips were connected to an AC signal generator and a cathode-ray oscilloscope. To obtain high-throughput measurements, a large-sized optical virtual electrode (0.8×0.8 mm) was generated to manipulate and record in parallel the motion of approximately 100 cells simultaneously under a 20× lens and microscope camera. This entire process takes about ~14 seconds, so the developed system is capable of analyzing ~25,000 cells per hour. This platform also has fluorescence observation compatibility owing to the transparency of the OEK chip, which enables the measurement and comparison of a number of biochemical features on the same platform in a single test. Objective #2: We have automated the OMF platform to collect single cell parameters including buoyancy mass, dry mass, density, volume, morphology, i.e., more than 40 features of each cell which can be classified into four categories data: biophysical, biokinetics, morphological, and biochemical data. To characterize the cells, they were first pipetted onto the OEK chip and were allowed settle on the bottom of the chip; the image focus on these cells was adjusted using the microscope focal length. Based on this image, the area of each single cell was calculated using an image processing technique. Then, the equivalent diameter and volume were derived from the cell area. After the cells were lifted using the optically induced DEP force to a certain height (approximately 10 µm) above the chip bottom, we let these cells fall freely by turning off the light electrode to remove the DEP force. Then, gravity, buoyancy and viscosity forces dominated the sedimentation process. Using an image matching technique, we captured the sedimentation trajectory of each individual cell by matching the standard defocused images to the cell falling images. Timestamp data in the cellular sedimentation video, falling velocity, acceleration, and viscosity were recorded. By computing the force balances, the gravity, buoyancy and viscosity forces of the cell can be calculated. Then, the density and mass of each single cell can be obtained. The buoyancy density is defined as ρ_buoyancy 〖=ρ〗_cell-ρ_fluid, where ρ is the density. The buoyancy mass is defined as m_buoyancy 〖=V〗_cell 〖×ρ〗_buoyancy, where V_cell is the cell volume. Finally, the buoyancy mass and buoyancy density were calculated. Objective #3: We have performed experimental studies on mouse lymphocytic leukemia cells (L1210) using the OMF platform developed for this project. L1210 cells (ATCC®, CCL-219™) were grown at 37°C in Leibovitz's L15 medium with glutamine, 10% (vol/vol) fetal bovine serum, 1% 100× penicillin-streptomycin, and 0.4% (w/vol) glucose. The cells were seeded at densities of approximately 5 × 104 cells/mL in 25-cm2 flasks in a 5% CO¬2 incubator. The media were refreshed every 2-3 days after reaching a density of 1 × 106 cells/mL. CMP (Abcam, ab120115) was diluted in DMSO to a final concentration of 5 mM and stored at -30°C until use. STS (Enzo, ALX-380-014-M005) was diluted in DMSO to a final concentration of 1 mM and stored at -30°C until use. For both drugs, the maximum thaw cycle was 2. L1210 cell suspensions in logarithmic phase were collected from the culturing flasks and resuspended in fresh culture medium. Then, 9 mL of new cell suspension were equally transferred to three new flasks. Subsequently, 3 µL CMP or STS was added to two separate flasks. Additionally, 3 µL DMSO was added to the third flask as the control group. Before each measurement, the cells washed twice with 0.2 M sucrose before resuspension in fresh 0.2 M sucrose at a concentration of approximately 100,000 mL−1. Finally, 20 μL of the cell samples was pipetted into the microchannel of the OEK chip. During the measurement, the OEK and sample were maintained at room temperature. Objective #4: We have applied the drugs Camptothecin and Staurosporine on the leukemia cells and test the cell response using the OMF platform. Two types of drugs, camptothecin (CMP) and staurosporine (STS), were used to induce cell death in the L1210 cells. The drug responses of the L1210 cells were characterized by the cellular volume, mass, and density over time. The results demonstrate that the cell density response was more rapid than that of the cell volume or mass. After 1.5 hours, the volume and mass of the STS-induced cells started to fluctuate compared to that of the CMP-induced cells and control group. While after 6 hours, the fluctuation of volume and mass of CMP-induced cells become observable compared to that of the control group. We have also shown that the normalized cell density had more essential and recognizable pathways than the volume parameter. Therefore, we can hypothesize that different kinds of drugs, i.e., CMP and STS, will induce different trends in cell density and volume during the cell death process. A key finding was that STS enabled a faster and more stable response than CMP, which had a more variable and milder effect. Objective #5: Finally, we have performed statistical correlation analyses between the acquired cell parameters for live and dead cells under the same biophysical environment, including intermediate states of cells. A key experiment was carried out to compare the time lapsed characteristics of the L1210 cells after treatment with different drugs. The cell volume, mass and density were compared using boxplots of L1210 cells after a treatment with CMP or STS at different time points. Mann-Whitney U-test was performed as a nonparametric test for two independent samples (ns P >= 0.05, * P < 0.05, **P < 0.01, ***P < 0.001, ****P < 0.0001). Time lapse distribution of normalized cell volume and density were also compared. The median of the distribution of the control group was normalized to 1. Because the changing amplitude of the cell density is small, the cell mass is heavily dependent on the cell volume and has a similar distribution.

11213817.label: Major findings and research outcome
11213817.value: We have developed a high-throughput, multi-parameter, single-cell analysis platform in this project -- our OMF (opto-microfluidics) platform can measure up to 100 cells in parallel to obtain multiple characteristics of each cell simultaneously. The platform can simultaneously manipulate cells and measure their biophysical and biokinetic characteristics rather than only capturing their morphological characteristics; it is also compatible with fluorescent assays, which directly link biophysical characteristics and biochemical features in the same environment. Using this platform, we demonstrated that the density of a single cell can reflect the general living state of a cell rather than the specific information provided by molecules. These measured characteristics of single cells are label-free and can also determine the different cellular death pathways induced by different types of drugs. In general, the parameters measured by the OMF platform can potentially provide a more comprehensive insight into cell death, differentiation, and disease in the study of metabolism and bioenergy of entire single cells. The ability to measure more than six types of characteristics enabled us to rapidly obtain sufficient data for statistical analyses to study cellular drug responses. We foresee that the throughput of this platform could be further increased by improving the optical microscope components of the system. We expect that future OMF platforms would be useful for the study of many cellular processes, such as cell differentiation, cell growth, cell death and the cell cycle. Through the this project fund, we have developed a novel OMF system and explored the usage of OEK (opto-electrokinetics) forces and machine learning algorithms to characterize single cells with a relatively high throughput rate. Our results have been published in 5 journal and 1 conference papers thus far, and 3 more ‘review papers’ related to physical cytometry, machine learning in drug discovery, and drug response in single cells have been submitted and are under review. We have collaborated with the 1) Shenyang Institute of Automation, CAS, 2) Shanghai University, and 3) Northeast University (Qinhuangdao Campus) in applying OKE forces in microfluidic devices to manipulate cells and microlenses, and also used OEK to characterize the electrical impedance of single cells. Our collaborative efforts have been published in 3 journal papers ready. Three PhD students were also partially supported using this project fund – their PhD dissertation work are related to applying the machine learning techniques derived from this project to decipher different sensor signals, including physiological states and material reflectivity.

11213817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11213817.value: The developed single cell characterization platform runs very efficiently using a microscope with 20× magnification lens and under an effective imaging area of 4.0 megapixels. To improve the throughput of the system, we propose to reduce of magnification of the microscope in order to include more cells within a field-of-view of a lens, so that OEK forces could be applied to more cells simultaneously in order to characterize the cells. However, in order to ensure that the motion characteristics of the cells could be tracked accurately, vision-based analysis algorithms should be improved; the resolution of the digital camera could also be improved by integrating the most advanced digital camera into the OMF system. We propose to also further explore the effects of different kinds of drugs on cell density and volume during the cell death process in order to accumulate more data on their functional mechanisms and effects on target cells. Traditional morphology-based classifications of cell death have been abandoned; instead, cell metabolism and bioenergy have been recommended by the Nomenclature Committee on Cell Death recently. We propose to explore whether the biophysical cell characteristics collected by the OMF system can reflect the metabolic response of cells in the future.

11213817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11213817.value: The death of cells is a complex and diverse process. The mass of single-cells can be used to characterize this process non-intrusively and comprehensively comparing to the traditional staining or fluorescence methods. However, the lack of a high-throughput cell-mass detection method remains a major challenge. We have developed a massively parallel, single-cell biophysical characterization platform using optoelectrokinetics principles that can detect six types of mass-related features in a single cell, and with a potential throughput rate upto 25,000 cells per hour, i.e., a providing a throughput that is 50 times higher than that achieved with micro-resonator-based approaches. Our platform can simultaneously manipulate the individual motion of approximately 100 cells and measure their diameter, volume, density, mass, buoyancy density, and buoyancy mass based on their sedimentation trajectory. By analyzing these biophysical characteristics, we revealed that dead cells that were killed by paraformaldehyde (PFA) were significantly heavier than living cells. Furthermore, we showed that the measured mass-related parameters significantly changed during the death of a single cell induced by different types of drugs.

11214317.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11214317.value: 有输入不确定性的比较选择问题

11214317.label: Project Objectives
11214317.value: Develop efficient selection procedures for selecting the best design under input uncertainty. Develop efficient selection procedures for constrained R&S under input uncertainty. Develop efficient selection procedures for feasibility determination under input uncertainty. Solve a real-world staff configuration problem in the emergency department through industrial collaboration.
rows: Develop efficient selection procedures for selecting the best design under input uncertainty.
Develop efficient selection procedures for constrained R&S under input uncertainty.
Develop efficient selection procedures for feasibility determination under input uncertainty.
Solve a real-world staff configuration problem in the emergency department through industrial collaboration.

11214317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11214317.value: The problem we consider is ranking and selection (R&S), which seeks to efficiently select the best design among a finite number of choices. The primary context is simulation, in which the performance of each design is estimated with some uncertainty through simulation experiments, and the goal is to determine the best allocation of simulation replications among the various designs. Implicit in the use of R&S procedures is the assumption that the simulation model is a faithful representation of the real system, while in practice, the simulation model is hardly a perfect reflection of the reality due to the input uncertainty: the uncertainty caused by estimating the input distributions using historical data. In this project, we are interested in R&S problems in the presence of input uncertainty, and propose to develop a series of new and efficient selection procedures for these problems. In particular, three common types of R&S problems are studied: selection of the best design, constrained R&S and feasibility determination. To account for the input uncertainty, we compare the designs based on their worst-case performances over a finite set of possible input distributions, and select the design with the best worst-case performance. We also investigate a real-world staff configuration problem in the emergency department of a hospital based on the R&S procedures developed. Some preliminary empirical results suggest that the proposed research is very promising. 本课题考虑基于仿真的ranking and selection (R&S)问题，即，如何将给定的仿真预算分配给解空间中的每个解，使得最优解能够更好地被选出来。文献中的R&S算法往往需要假设仿真模型精确无误，然而实际当中的仿真由于输入的不确定性，很难做到这一点。本课题将着重考虑在有输入的不确定性的情况下，如何设计高效的R&S算法。 具体而言，我们将考虑三类R&S问题：无约束R&S问题，有约束R&S问题以及检测可行性的R&S问题。在有输入不确定性的情况下，我们假设每个解对应有限个可能的输入值，并以这些输入值对应的最差表现当作这个解的表现。我们同时考虑一个实际的急诊室员工配置问题用以测试提出的每个算法的表现，初期的数值结果显示这些算法非常有效。

11214817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11214817.value: Cell injection is a critical requirement in biological fields, such for artificial fertilization, gene therapy, medical test and so on. In cell injection process, one core important step is to penetrate the cell membrane safely with invasive as low as possible. Generally, there are two strategies to do so: 1) decrease the tip size of glass pipette by microfabrication. 2) optimize the injection process by robotic automation. However, after several years’ development, those traditional approaches have almost reached their limit for cell injection improvement. Hence, how to improve the cell injection efficiency further becomes an urgent and challenge work nowadays. If we look at nature, we will see we always add a rotation movement when we penetrating an object, since the material is usually more sensitive to the shear stress. Therefore, we wonder can we improve the cell injection process by employing rotational injection? If so, how much improvement can we have? Next, can we develop a new cell injection system based on that? In this project, we intend to propose a novel micro robotic system for rotational cell injection to reduce the physical invasive and improve penetration efficiency. Firstly, we will develop the robotic system with 7-DOFs, including one rotational DOF for micro pipette, and integrate it with microscopy. Then, we will develop a microchip to transfer and fix the cell for injection process. In addition, we will develop a force sensing system to detect the penetration force dynamically. After that, we will study how the rotation parameters affect the injection and then to optimize the injection process. Lastly, we will develop a prototype of the cell injection system. The successful implementation of this project will have long-term impacts in many aspects: it will provide a new sight for the low-invasive cell injection; will reveal the role of shear stress in cell membrane penetration; will deliver a prototype of cell injection system with high potential for commercialization in the near future. Consequently, we believe this proposal will lead to an automatic, high efficient and low-invasive micro rotatable robotic system for cell injection, which would not only promote the fundamental biology research and practical biomedical practices, but also deliver the next generation cell injection system for commercialization. 在不對細胞造成明顯損傷的前提下，把外界物質（如細胞核、DNA、藥物等）安全、精確的轉移到細胞內部是單細胞研究中的一項關鍵的技術就是。然而，在細胞顯微注射過程中，穿刺針會對細胞產生不可避免的壓力並隨之使細胞發生物理變形。如果該形變過大，就會導致細胞的物理破損和注射失敗。此外，過大的外力刺激會也改變細胞的生化特性，從而對細胞分析帶來不可預測的干擾，嚴重影響細胞分析的精度。因此，如何降低細胞顯微注射過程中對細胞的物理侵襲，是所有單細胞研究領域，包括克隆工程、精准醫療、基因修復等，所面臨的一個共性問題。揭示細胞在穿刺過程中的變形機理，研究能降低細胞受力的穿刺方法和工藝，實現低侵襲的細胞穿刺，從而提高細胞注射的成功率並保證細胞的生物穩定性，最終研發出高端的生物醫療設備，為開展精確的單細胞研究提供關鍵的技術支持，對推動生物醫學工程的進一步發展有重要意義。 在這個項目中，我們計畫開發一種用於旋轉細胞注射的新型微機器人系統，以減少細胞注射過程中的物理侵入性並提高穿透效率。首先，我們將開發具有7自由度的機器人系統（包含一個旋轉自由度），並將其與顯微鏡結合。然後，我們將開發一個微晶片來篩選和固定注射過程的細胞。此外，我們將開發力傳感系統來動態地檢測穿透力。之後，我們將研究旋轉參數如何影響注射，並優化注射過程。最終研發出用於細胞注射的新型平臺。

11214817.label: Realisation of objectives
11214817.value: All the objectives have been achieved and the outcomes have been presented in the forms of papers (12 SCI Journal) and patents (1US Patent and 1 CN patent). 1. To develop a micro rotatable robotic system to realize the precise rotation of micropipette. We have developed a microrobotic manipulation system with 7-DOFs, including one rotational DOF, for rotational cell injection. An x-y-z robotic stage with positioning accuracy approximate 30 nm for micropipette positioning was mounted on an angle adjustment slider. And a θ-x-y robotic stage with rotational accuracy 1μ° and translational positioning accuracy 1nm for rotary cell injection was assembled on the x-y-z robotic stage. The glass micropipette for cell injection was fixed on the platform mounted on the θ-x-y robotic stage. The x-y-z robotic stage was constructed by three piezo actuators (8301-UHV, New Port Inc.). It has a movement range and positioning resolution approximate 15.4 mm and 30 nm, respectively. The θ-x-y robotic stage was constructed by two linear positioners (ECS3030, Attocube Inc.) and one rotary positioner (ECR3030, Attocube Inc.). The travel range, resolution and repeatability of the linear positioners are 20 mm, 1 nm and 50 nm respectively, and the travel range, resolution and repeatability of the rotary positioner are 360° endless, 1μ° and 5% over full range respectively. 2. To handle the cell and measure the penetration force dynamically by developing a microchip. We have developed a microchip system to handle the cell and measure the penetration force dynamically. We designed the cell capture pillars with different interspace to grasp cells with different size. Considering the measurement range (hundreds μN) of the selected test specimen (zebrafish embryo), we designed the force sensing system based on a PVDF film (MSI Co., Ltd., model LDT2-28K). The PVDF film is assembled between cell capture pillars and film hold column and the output charge of PVDF is amplified by the signal amplifier circuit board. Benefit from the measurement range (μN ~ mN) and high resolution (~ sub-μN) of the chosen sensor, the cell injection force can be obtained precisely. 3. To find out the effect of shear stress on cell penetration and to optimize the operation parameters. We established a biomembrane point-load model to elucidate the dramatic puncture force decrease based on the maximum shear stress theory. Our rotary injection model suggests that when the membrane tangential stress is introduced, the extra membrane tangential stress will lead to weaker radial injection force. We also conducted a series of control experiments to investigate the effect of tip size, tip shape, rotation speed, feeding speed on the penetration force, through which the penetration parameters were optimizely designed. 4. To automate the rotational cell injection process and develop the porotype. We introduced the microscope imaging feedback into the cell injection system and then realized the automatic rotational cell injection. To demonstrate the working ability of automatic cell injection system, we conduct the zebrafish embryo injection experiments by setting up several groups, i.e., straight injection with thick/thin smooth/sharp tip and rotary injection with thick/thin smooth/sharp tip. The results clearly indicate that the puncture deformation of rotary injection reduces approximately 25.4% (thick smooth tip), 33.2% (thick sharp tip), 11.3% (thin smooth tip) and 13.8% (thin sharp tip) compared with straight injection. Meanwhile, the average zebrafish embryo puncture force via rotational injection is approximately 1311.82 mN (thick smooth tip), 1032.10 mN (thick sharp tip), 590.48 mN (thin smooth tip) and 494.58 mN (thin sharp tip). Comparatively, the average zebrafish embryo puncture force via straight injection mode is approximately 1796.31 mN (thick smooth tip), 1455.26 mN (thick sharp tip), 670.11 mN (thin smooth tip) and 599.51 mN (thin sharp tip). The superiorities of our system in reducing the cell deformation and injection force suggest it could be a competitive candidate for low-invasive cell injection in biomedical engineering.

11214817.label: Major findings and research outcome
11214817.value: This project proposed a rotational cell injection strategy and system to reduce the physical invasive and improve penetration efficiency in the cell injection process. The major findings and research outcomes from this project can be summarized as: (1) A micro rotatable robotic system with 7-DOFs was designed and developed and the precise rotation of micropipette is realized based on this system. (2) A microchip with cell handling and force measurement abilities was designed and developed for the cell injections. (3) The mechanical model for rotational cell injection was established and the effect of shear forces and the effect of injection parameters on cell injection was investigated. (4) With our system, both the cell deformation and the cell injection force can be reduced approximate 30% compared with the conventional direct injection methods. Moreover, expect for the rotational cell injection robot, we also developed some other types of small robots for drug delivery with the support of this project. Relevant achievements have delivered 12 SCI journal paper and 2 patents (1US, 1CN). See Part C for details.

11214817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11214817.value: In this research, we proposed the rotational cell injection method, developed the prototype, and verified its superiorities in low damage to the cell in the cell injection process. As the future work, we will promote our system to practical applications, like DNA delivery, artificial fertilization and so on.

11214817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11214817.value: Technologies of introducing exogenous materials into cells play a central role in biology field, such as for artificial fertilization, gene therapy, medical test and so on. In cell injection process, one core important step is to penetrate the cell membrane safely with invasive as low as possible. With the support of this project, we proposed a rotational cell injection strategy and system to reduce the physical invasive and improve penetration efficiency in the injection process. Firstly, we developed a robotic system with 7-DOFs, including one rotational DOF for micro pipette, and integrate it with microscopy. Then, we developed a microchip with force sensing ability to handle the cell and measure the injection force dynamically. The results suggest that our method and system can reduce the cell deformation and penetration force approximate 30% compared with the conventional methods. This project delivered an automatic, highly efficient, and low-invasive micro rotatable robotic system for cell injection. We believe it would not only promote the fundamental biology research and practical biomedical practices, but also be a competitive candidate for the next generation cell injection system for commercialization.

11215017.label: Realisation of objectives
11215017.value: One of the main objectives of this project is to investigate the airborne microbiomes in commercial buildings in Hong Kong, which are mechanically ventilated and have different building functions. Given Hong Kong has four distinct seasons, the influence of seasonality is of particular interest. From a methodology point of view, this study aimed to apply metagenomics sequencing in addition to amplicon sequencing of the 16S rRNA gene. The application of metagenomics sequencing on air and surface samples is not trivial due to the low concentration of biomass but we have successfully established the methodology for both types of samples in this study. Another key objective of this study is conducting a meta-analysis of the built environment microbiomes in Hong Kong and globally. We have successfully compared global air and surface microbiomes as well as samples from key venues in Hong Kong. Specifically, in Objective 1, we analyzed both the indoor and outdoor airborne microbiomes of eight different office buildings and malls over four seasons. The dynamics of the bacteria, their assembly mechanisms and the indicator that can predict the sources of bacteria were determined. The significance of this work is that it enables us to gain a better understanding on the roles mechanical ventilation and outdoor air play in shaping the indoor airborne microbiome over seasons. With the established metagenomics sequencing method, we have applied it in Objective 2 to study the airborne microbiome of the subway in Hong Kong, which is a key indoor environment with close to five million ridership per day. In addition to analyzing samples collected from Hong Kong, as part of Objective 3, we have collaborated with researchers from New York City, Denver, London, Oslo and Stockholm to conduct a meta-analysis of the subway air microbiomes across the different cities. This global study yielded new insights into the similarities and differences of the air microbiomes on a global scale. Besides investigating air, we have extended our meta-analysis to surfaces in subways and this has led to a global study involving 60 cities with over 4,700 metagenomics samples analyzed. In this seminal work, many novel bacteria, viruses and metabolic functions were discovered. The meta-analysis in Hong Kong has compared the airborne microbiomes of subway, commercial and residential buildings located in different part of the city. We found that at a city-scale, different building types have their unique airborne microbiome, suggesting that tailored adjustments of the ventilation and other indoor parameters are the approaches that need to be adopted to manage the indoor airborne microbial communities for each building type or even each specific building. Furthermore, we have compared the indoor and outdoor surface microbiomes in our meta-analysis. In particular, we have focused our attention on the pier surfaces in Hong Kong, given the large number of piers along the coastline. We found that pier surfaces are a rich reservoir of unexplored microbial genomes and metabolic functions and the microbes detected have the capabilities to adapt to the oligotrophic conditions of surfaces. We have further determined that the composition of the public surface microbiomes can vary on a timescale of hours. Overall, all the proposed objectives in this study have been achieved and six publications have resulted from the investigation. We have gained important insights into the air and surface microbiomes of the built environments, and the local and global meta-analysis have broaden our views on the similarities and differences in the microbial taxa and metabolic functions in the microbiomes. The findings of this study have important public health implications and knowledge gained will facilitate management of the indoor environment to protect the health of occupants. In addition to research outcomes, we have trained a number of undergraduate students on microbiology and molecular techniques and we have educated them on the importance of microbiome sciences.

11215017.label: Major findings and research outcome
11215017.value: The results from this project have been published in a number of high-impact journals (Part C). The goal of Objective 1 is to characterize the seasonal dynamics and correlations between indoor and outdoor airborne bacterial populations in commercial buildings. As reported in Zhou et al. (2020), we found that the assembly mechanism of the airborne microbiome in the respective indoor and outdoor environments during each season was random. Interestingly, seasonality was not a major factor that influenced the indoor and outdoor microbiome compositions. Source tracking analysis showed that bacteria from outdoor air and occupant skin were the major contributors to the indoor airborne microbiome and indoor concentration of carbon dioxide was a robust indicator of the sources of bacteria. The goal of Objective 2 is to characterize the metabolic functions of the airborne microbiome in commercial buildings using metagenomic sequencing. For this objective, we analyzed the indoor air of the subway in Hong Kong, which has significant public health implications given the daily ridership. In order to put the metagenomics results from the Hong Kong in the perspective of subways around the world, air samples from New York City, Denver, London, Oslo and Norway were also included for a meta-analysis, which is in line with goal of Objective 3. As reported in Leung et al. (2021), geography was the main factor that drove differences in taxa and metabolic functions between the subway air microbiomes. Similar bacterial strains differed among cities in many key metabolic genes. Many biosynthetic gene clusters and city-specific coding sequences were also found in the metagenome-assembled genomes. Our meta-analysis was not limited to indoor air but also surfaces. In a global effort published in Cell (Danko et al., 2021), subway surface samples from 60 cities around the world including Hong Kong were analyzed. We contributed to this work by analyzing the antimicrobial resistance functions. In this seminal work, core taxa as well as many novel bacteria and viruses were identified. In addition, we reported in Wilkins et al. (2021) that the public surface microbiomes were dynamics on a timescale of hours. In addition to the global meta-analysis, we also conducted a city-scale comparison of the indoor airborne microbiomes within Hong Kong, focusing on subway, commercial and residential buildings. As reported in Zhou et al. (2021, submitted), the taxonomic and inferred metabolic function compositions of the indoor airborne microbiomes between building types were significantly different. In addition to indoor built environments, as part of the meta-analysis, we also analyzed outdoor pier surface microbiomes (Tong et al., 2021, submitted). We found many novel species in the pier surface microbiomes and the compositions of the pier surfaces were different from indoor surfaces. Overall, findings from this project enhanced our fundamental understanding on the types of microbes and their metabolic functions that are present in different built environments locally in Hong Kong and globally.

11215017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11215017.value: With the on-going COVID-19 pandemic, the types of microorganisms that are present in air have significant public health implications. While the current project focuses on bacteria, the established metagenomics sequencing method can be extended to study viruses in air and on surfaces. The PI is now conducting work to establish a rapid detection method for various bacteria and viruses in air to facilitate early warning. The PI has also prepared proposals to solicit support to systematically investigate the viruses that are present in the built environments using high-throughput culture-independent methods. The collaboration with our international partners will continue so that we can pursue longitudinal meta-analysis of the built environment microbiomes of global cities.

11215017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11215017.value: Citizens in metropolises such as Hong Kong spend significant amount of their time indoors, especially in mechanically ventilated buildings. Therefore, it is of importance to understand the microorganisms that are present in air and on surfaces. In this study, we applied culture-independent sequencing methods to study the microbes that are present in various commercial buildings over four seasons in Hong Kong. Outdoor air and the nearby environment were found to have significant influences on the microbial populations that are present indoors. The microbiomes on indoor surfaces are dynamics and outdoor surfaces harbor many unique metabolic functions. Meta-analysis of the different building types in Hong Kong revealed that each type has its own unique microbial signatures. When the meta-analysis was extended to different global built environments, similarities and differences in the microbial communities can be identified. Overall, this study has shed light on the air and surface microbiomes in the built environments in Hong Kong and elsewhere. The results suggest that customized strategies are required to manage the indoor microbial populations in each building type or each specific building regardless of the location of the buildings.
