11215117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11215117.value: 由于在辅助农业，侦察作战，交通运输等方面具有广阔的应用前景，人性化微小型飞行器的研究越来越受到科学家和工程师的关注。这些微小机器人或无人机有可能彻底改变我们对民用机器人的使用。有证据表明，多家跨国公司已经开始研究如何使用这些飞行器进行航空运输或快递交付任务的可能性。 然而，与传统飞机相比，厘米尺度的微小型飞行器的空气动力效率会急剧下降。空中飞行不断增加的能量需求会严重限制了飞行器的飞行时间和有效载荷能力。为了实现大额负载的传输，多机器人协作是一种实现飞行器对绳索悬挂负载物运输的有利技术。 在本项研究中，我们将研究如何结合惯性传感技术和智能控制技术，在现实世界中实现飞行器的协作运输任务。本研究将分三个步骤来处理传感与控制问题。首先，为了让飞行器在飞行中保持群体阵型，避免碰撞，我们需要知道它们的相对位置。城市环境中GPS的反馈是不可靠的而且其反馈的分辨率也不足以防止飞行器之间的碰撞。相反，惯性传感技术为飞行器提供了很好的解决方案，它通过测量承载负载的绳索中的张力来推断飞行器间的相对位置。其次，通过在电缆中引入弹性元件，系统的线性化动力学将类似于弹簧耦合的质量。其结果是，我们能够轻松地推导出控制策略，从而稳定住飞行器和负载的群体阵型。当飞行器群体阵型完成时，我们也可以使用不够完美的GPS反馈来控制它们的集体位置。最后，我们将开发一个非线性控制器来提高飞行性能，并通过研究单个刚体负载（而不是point-mass负载）的运输和多个负载同时运输来扩展本研究的适用范围。 可预知的是，本项研究将有助于机器人领域，特别是微型飞行器和多智能体系统的进步，并扩展它们的实际应用。本研究很可能会改变飞行器是如何运用于负载运输的。本研究的科学价值在于：（1）开发具有鲁棒性的惯性传感算法；（2）对具有绳索悬挂负载物的多飞行器的动力学进行研究并建立其与弹簧耦合质量类似系统间的联系；（3）实现机器人系统在各种操作下的多智能体控制原理。

11215117.label: Realisation of objectives
11215117.value: 1. Characterize the robot's thrust dynamics and develop a robust filter for estimating the cable tension on a tethered quadrotor from the onboard inertial feedback. The first objective can be regarded as the "estimation" problem. Due to the complicated dynamics of the considered experimental system, this problem concerns, (i) modeling of the multi-body dynamics; (ii) parameter identification; (iii) derivation of a suitable estimator with experimental verification. Three mentioned problems were solved using the simplified dynamic model, in which the three-dimensional space was reduced into two dimensions in [1]. Later on, this simplification was removed in [2]. In both cases, the dynamics of the robot-payload-robot system were derived via Lagrangian mechanics in generalized coordinates. The parameter identification step--mapping the input commands of the rotors to the generated thrusts--was carried out using a benchtop setup. Lastly, a filter was designed for the estimation task. The novelty of the approach is that only IMU feedback (i.e., no vision) was used for the state estimation. Due to the number of the state variables, we were unable to deploy high-fidelity filters with better accuracy such as an Unscented Kalman filter onboard thanks to the limited computational power of small controller boards. To resolve this issue, we developed a filtering method based on Extended Kalman Filter, with an additional tuning parameter inspired by Unscented Kalman Filter. To this end, the estimation results are satisfactory when benchmarked against the ground truth measurements provided by the motion capture system. Over, the results are sufficiently accurate to be later used for control tasks. 2. Demonstrate a stable formation flight of multiple quadrotors with a cable suspended load using centralized and distributed controllers derived from the linearized dynamics of the system in indoor and outdoor environments. This objective follows naturally from the first objective. After the estimation task is accomplished, the feedback required to stabilize the robot-payload-robot system is available for the stabilization task. In this task, we decided to adopt a leader-follower scheme, designating one robot as a leader and the other as a follower. This leaves the stabilization job to the follower alone. The leader may travel in any direction and the follower ensures that it keeps its relative position (as well as the payload's) constant. The strategy can be regarded as distributed, rather than (simpler) centralized control. To do so, we first analyzed the equilibrium state of the system. The linear analysis reveals that, in theory, the system is marginally stable. This means a simple PID controller has the potential to stabilize the system sufficiently well for practical purposes. In theory, only the damping (D term) is required as the proportional term is inherently available. This is beneficial as it is a non-trivial task to derive a nonlinear controller due to the complexity of the system. Therefore, to control the formation, the derived PID controller is based on the linearized dynamics of the system around the equilibrium point. The controller computes the desired attitude and collective thrust of the follower robot. With the identified robot parameters from the first objective, the attitude and thrust setpoints are mapped into the thrusts and commands of individual motors. In the experiments, we showed that the formation can be stabilized, first using the feedback from the motion capture system and then the feedback directly from the estimator. We showed that the proposed method is robust to disturbance and the formation of the system can be varied mid-air. Trajectory following flights were also demonstrated. Lastly, an outdoor flight was shown in [2]. In this implementation, the leader robot was piloted by a human operator and the follower robot autonomously stabilized the system using the proposed estimation and control scheme. The robots traveled over 20 m outdoor. This distance is longer than previously published results that rely on vision. 3. Develop a geometric controller based on the nonlinear system dynamics and perform validating flights. The findings from the previous objective suggest that a linear controller is sufficient for the cooperative transport tasks. While it is foreseeable that a nonlinear or geometric approach could enhance the tracking accuracy and robustness, the design is not trivial due to the coupled dynamics and the degree of underactuation of the system. Thus far, we have started re-analyzing the leader-payload-follower system from an energy perspective to derive a nonlinear controller based on the energy shaping or related methods. It is anticipated that this would result in a very efficient controller, comparable to a geometric approach. Based on this finding, we also realize that one effective way to stabilize the system is to use aerodynamic surfaces that would damp out the excess system energy. This avenue of research is being investigated. We have successfully implemented this in both indoor and outdoor experiments. The benefit of this approach is it eradicates the use of an estimator and onboard computation entirely. The downside is the need for mechanical parts. It can be seen as mechanical intelligence as the mechanical dampers replace the role of an estimator and the formation controller. The results are now being written up. To this end, this last objective is technically mostly but not completely satisfied. The remaining task is replaced by the passive, mechanical approach as it is deemed more interesting and impactful. Besides this, we pursue a secondary and complementary research direction. As the leader-payload-follower strategy still requires the leader to be controlled by a pilot, the next step would be autonomous navigation. Existing map-based localization and navigation methods (such as SLAM) remain computationally complex and unsuitable for small robots with the payload capacity too limited for a companion computer and high-resolution vision system. Therefore, we propose to develop an efficient visual-inertial navigation method based on the use of optic flow. This can be regarded as "direct" and "reactive" navigation, where feature recognition and tracking are not required, radically speeding up the task. Through a few publications, we have shown that a robot with standard flight controller hardware (no extra computer) can run proposed algorithms and safely fly in simple environments overground. [1] Heng Xie, Xinyu Cai, and Pakpong Chirarattananon, "Towards Cooperative Transport of a Suspended Payload via Two Aerial Robots with Inertial Sensing ," 2020 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS), 2020. [2] Heng Xie, Kaixu Dong, and Pakpong Chirarattananon, "Cooperative Transport of a Suspended Payload via Two Aerial Robots with Inertial Sensing,"IEEE/ASME Transactions on Mechatronics, under review.

11215117.label: Major findings and research outcome
11215117.value: In short, we developed a vision-less method to stabilize the system of two robots and a suspended payload. We found that around the equilibrium state, the system is theoretically marginally stable. The state can also be estimated using feedback from the inertial measurement unit of the follower robot alone. This makes it possible to stabilize the system without additional sensors or cameras. The developed estimation and control methods were experimentally verified. Furthermore, we identified another strategy to realize the same task without direct computation, but by using aerodynamic dampers. This can be regarded as mechanical intelligence, where mechanical parts replace active sensing and control. The results outlined above were preliminarily published as a conference paper in 2020 IEEE IROS---an internationally recognized robotics conference. The main results have been written up and under review for publication in IEEE/ASME Transactions on Mechatronics (TMECH). TMECH is considered one of the top (within 10%) journals in Mechanical Engineering. During the project, we have trained two PhD students and one MPhil student. One PhD student has recently graduated and the other is about to graduate after working on the project for almost four years. The MPhil student graduated approximately one year ago. In addition to the mentioned manuscripts, the secondary research direction on efficient navigation for small multirotor robots has resulted in several publications. This includes another paper in IEEE/ASME Transactions on Mechatronics in early 2021 and two papers published in IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (2020 and 2021).

11215117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11215117.value: During the project period, one MPhil student was assigned to work on the project alongside a PhD student to explore the possibility of the use of passive aerodynamic dampers for stabilizing the formation of multiple robots in a cooperative transport task. His dissertation submitted in August 2020 is titled "Passive Stability for Cooperative Transport of A Cable-Suspended Payload by Two Aerial Robots". Through analytical and numerical modeling, we find that it is possible to stabilize a system of multiple robots with one suspended payload through aerodynamic dampers. This eliminates the need for estimation of the current state of the system, communication between agents, and feedback control entirely. Preliminary experimental results were obtained and promising. To follow up on this direction, another PhD student admitted in late 2020 is following up on this initial finding. He has made decent progress. Thus far, we are able to theoretically prove the stability and extensive experimental results have been obtained. The manuscript is outlined and will be prepared for submission in the next few months.

11215117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11215117.value: In this research, we have developed a method for two multirotor vehicles to carry a suspended payload together. The challenge is to ensure that both robots coordinate in the way that they keep their relative positions fixed to avoid a collision. In current days, this is mostly accomplished by the use of machine vision. For instance, if robots can see each other and are aware of the presence of others, they can collaborate accordingly. However, machine vision involves the use of multiple cameras and demanding computation. This makes the approach unsuitable for smaller and lighter robots. To address this shortcoming, we devised a method such that each robot can sense the position of the other robot through the force it feels from the cable's tension. The tension indicates the direction of the tether. This allows the position of the other robot to be estimated. Then, the robot can use this information to ensure that it keeps a fixed distance from the other robot. In experiments, we demonstrate that this can be reliably achieved, which means we eliminate the need for a camera and complex computation. As a result, the task can be accomplished with small multirotor robots.

11215217.value: 對無線通信系統來講，天線是一個非常重要的部分，因為它能夠直接影響到信號傳輸和接收的效率。在無線通信系統中，濾波器也是不可或缺的，它可以用來降低不同頻帶信號之間的干擾。此外，在對信號進行處理之前，我們需要濾波器來抑制噪聲。由於在系統中引入濾波器會不可避免地帶來插入損耗，因此，將天線和濾波器集成到一起來避免或者降低這種損耗會變得十分有意義。我們把這種集成的器件叫做濾波天線。濾波天線的使用，可以降低整個系統的損耗從而提升系統的性能。 近年來，由於其低損耗、低成本、易於激勵等一系列的優點，介質諧振器天線被廣泛研究。但是，關於濾波介質諧振器天線的研究極少。目前為止，只有一個單頻帶單極化的設計被發表過。在本項目中，我們將會展開一個包含多種濾波介質諧振器天線的全面研究。天線融合技術將會被用來設計此類天線，即通過向天線或者饋電網絡引入寄生單元或者諧振器來實現濾波的響應。我們的設計不需要外置的濾波器，因此，它可以變得十分緊湊，同時具有低損耗的特點。 在本項目中，多種緊湊型的濾波介質諧振器天線將會被首次研究。首先，一種簡單新穎的、朝天頂方向輻射的濾波介質諧振器天線將會被探究，並用來實現極化分集的設計，以此來應對信號的多徑問題。其次，為了擴大信號的覆蓋範圍，一種全向輻射的濾波介質諧振器天線將會被研究。基於此設計，寬帶和雙頻帶的設計也會被提出。最後，我們將會研究基片集成的濾波介質諧振器天線和陣列。由於它使用介質基板來實現，因此可以十分方便地直接與電路集成。 我們將會使用ANSYS HFSS軟件來仿真這些濾波介質諧振器天線，仿真結果也會用實驗測量來驗證。我們也將提供相應的設計指南，以方便於設計這些濾波介質諧振器天線。

11215217.label: Realisation of objectives
11215217.value: (i) Objective 1: To investigate a novel broadside filtering DRA and its diversity design This objective has been achieved successfully. Three broadside filtering dielectric resonator antennas (DRAs) have been investigated. In the first filtering DRA design, a microstrip feedline is fabricated on the top layer of a substrate to excite the filtering DRA. Two stubs are extended from a 50-ohm microstrip line and laid beneath the DRA. A vertical strip is attached to the sidewall of the DRA, soldered at the microstrip feedline. By using this hybrid feeding structure, a filtering response can be observed in both the reflection coefficient and boresight gain. The DRA is excited in the TE111 mode. ANSYS HFSS was used to simulate the filtering DRA, and good agreement between the measured and simulated results has been obtained. In the second filtering DRA, a dual-loop structure composing of three vertical copper posts and a horizontal rectangular copper strip is introduced inside a cylindrical DRA. The cylindrical DRA was excited in the HEM11δ mode, which radiates like a horizontal magnetic dipole. The horizontal copper strip connects the three posts at the top of the DRA. The left and right posts are soldered to the ground plane, whereas the middle post passes through the circular slot at its center and is connected to the feedline. Since the dual-loop structure will generate an H-field, the net radiation will be zero if the dual-loop H-field cancels the H-field of the equivalent magnetic dipole of the DRA HEM11δ mode. A prototype at 2.4 GHz for WLAN applications was fabricated and measured to verify the simulation. Good agreement between the measured and simulated results has been observed. Apart from the linearly polarized (LP) filtering DRA, a circularly polarized (CP) filtering DRA has also been investigated using the similar design technique. In this case, an elliptical DRA with two notches is used to obtain CP fields. The rectangular copper strip of the LP design is replaced by a V-shaped copper strip to facilitate the CP operation. As compared with existing filtering DRAs, our designs are simpler and more compact without the need of using any extra filtering circuit or challenging feed network. A prototype of the CP design was also fabricated and measured at 2.4 GHz. The measured and simulated results are in good agreement. The third broadside filtering DRA deploys a rectangular DRA with three slots (Slots I-III) in the ground, with the DRA excited in the fundamental TE1δ1 mode. Slots I and III are rectangular slots, whereas Slot II between them has a mirror-C shape, consisting of a straight part and two bent arms. It was found that Slot I can improve the passband matching and stopband suppression. The meandered Slot II resonates in its higher-order mode. For Slot III, it operates in its fundamental mode and meanwhile excites the fundamental TE1δ1 mode of the DRA. The filtering DRA was simulated with ANSYS HFSS. A prototype was fabricated and measured, and good agreement between the measured and simulated results has been obtained. Based on this filtering DRA, a frequency-reconfigurable filtering DRA with harmonics suppression has been investigated. To make the antenna frequency-reconfigurable, three varactors and their biasing circuits are used, with minor modifications of the slots. The varactors are located on the other side of the substrate to avoid the interference between them and the DRA. Again, a prototype was fabricated and measured, with reasonable agreement between the measured and simulated results. The last filtering DRA has been obtained by using the DRA as the last-stage resonator of a bandpass filter. Its feedline consists of two terminal-loaded microstrip resonators, which provide two independently tuned nulls. The DRA is excited in the HEM113 mode. Good agreement between the measured and simulated results has been found. A two-port diversity filtering DRA was also designed based on the first broadside filtering DRA. Two identical sets of the hybrid-feeding networks are used on two adjacent sidewalls of the DRA for the diversity design. Four metal posts are symmetrically inserted into the DRA to enhance the isolation between the two ports. Ansoft HFSS was used to simulate the diversity filtering DRA. Measurements were done to verify the simulations, and the measured results agree with the simulated results. Objective 2: To investigate narrow-/wide-/dual-band omnidirectional filtering DRAs The narrow-/wide-/dual-band omnidirectional filtering DRAs have been investigated successfully. The wideband omnidirectional filtering DRA is discussed first. A cylindrical DRA was used in this study. It has a cylindrical hole at its bottom to accommodate a hybrid feed that consists of a probe and a metallic disk. The feeding probe is located at the center of the DRA to obtain an omnidirectional radiation pattern. A metallic circular disk is mounted on the probe to widen the impedance bandwidth and also improve the filtering response of the upper stopband. There is a gap between the disk and DRA. The DRA is placed on a circular patch fabricated on a substrate. A ring slot is etched on the patch, and four shorting pins are embedded evenly in the substrate to improve the filtering performance of the lower stopband. The antenna has a circular ground plane on the bottom layer of the substrate. The antenna was simulated, fabricated, and tested. Good agreement between the measured and simulated results has been observed. The dual-band omnidirectional filtering DRA has also been investigated successfully. It was evolved from the wideband design, with the metallic disk now moved upwards to touch the upper DR face of the cylindrical hole directly. The modification can divide the wide passband into two separate bands and also introduce a stopband between them. Four rectangular ring slots are symmetrically etched on the ground plane. Each ring slot has a shorting pin at one of its ends. Finally, a narrow-band filtering DRA has been obtained successfully by using the upper-band.

11215217.label: Major findings and research outcome
11215217.value: (i) Broadside filtering DRA and its diversity design The results of the first broadside filtering DRA have been summarized in [2] of Section 8. The filtering DRA has a measured impedance bandwidth of 21.9%. Two radiation nulls that lead to a filtering response have been obtained at 1.65 GHz and 2.31 GHz. The out-of-band suppression is higher than 16 dB. The second broadside filtering DRA has been presented in [3] of Section 8. Its LP version has a measured impedance bandwidth of 7.2%. The measured suppression levels in the lower and upper stopbands are 22 dB and 19.6 dB, respectively. For the CP version, the measured impedance and axial-ratio bandwidths are 4.1% and 4.9%, respectively. The third broadside filtering DRA has been presented in [4] of Section 8. It has a measured impedance bandwidth of 18.5% and stopband suppression of 17.3 dB. The reconfigurable design has measured impedance bandwidths of 13.0% (2.15–2.45 GHz), 15.3% (2.33–2.72 GHz), and 13.5% (2.48–2.84 GHz) in States I, II, and III, respectively. The last broadside filtering DRA has been presented in a conference paper ([1] of Section 9). It has a measured impedance bandwidth of 5.8 %. The measured suppression levels in the lower and upper stopbands are more than 29.8 dB and 21.5 dB, respectively. The broadside diversity filtering DRA, which is based on the first filtering DRA, has also been presented in [2] of Section 8. It has a measured impedance bandwidth of 22.5% for both ports. The out-of-band suppression is more than 16 dB. (ii) Narrow-/wide-/dual-band omnidirectional filtering DRAs Results of our narrow-/wide-/dual-band omnidirectional filtering DRAs have been summarized in [1] of Section 8. The wideband omnidirectional filtering DRA is discussed first. It has the measured and simulated impedance bandwidths of 52.8% and 54.8%, respectively. The out-of-band suppression level is ~15 dB. The dual-band omnidirectional filtering DRA was designed at 2.05 GHz and 3.5 GHz. Its lower and upper operating bands have measured impedance bandwidths of 10.1% and 3.73%, respectively. An out-of-band suppression of ~15 dB has been obtained. The narrow-band omnidirectional filtering DRA has been obtained by using the upper band. (iii) Compact absorptive filtering patch antenna The techniques obtained in this project have been used to design a compact absorptive filtering patch antenna, which is matched even outside the passband. Its measured suppression levels in the upper- and lower-stopbands are higher than 20.5 dB and 17.4 dB, respectively. The results have been summarized in [5] of Section 8.

11215217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11215217.value: This project has investigated the dual-band filtering DRA. Since more than two frequency bands may be needed in modern communications, it is of interest to develop a tri-band filtering DRA. This can be achieved by using a rectangular DRA, which has three dimensions of width, length, and height. These three dimensions can be used to satisfy three transcendental equations of the three operating frequencies. It needs to obtain a filtering response for each of the three frequency bands, making it a challenging and meaningful research problem. Also, the diversity filtering DRA studied in this project is of the polarization type, but a pattern- diversity antenna may be needed in some applications. Therefore, it is useful to develop a pattern-diversity filtering DRA. To do this, two resonant modes of a DRA can be used to provide two different radiation patterns, and their resonance frequencies can be made equal by introducing a dielectric loading at a right position of the DRA. This can tune the resonance frequency of one mode with negligible effects on that of the second mode.

11215217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11215217.value: Both antenna and filter are very crucial for a wireless communication system. The former directly affects signal transmission and reception, whereas the latter can reduce interferences between signals from different frequency bands and suppress noise before processing the signal. This project has investigated the filtering dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) that simultaneously provides the antenna and filter functions. By integrating an antenna with a filter, a system can be made more compact with lower loss. The DRA has been chosen in this project for its many advantages such as its low loss, small size, low cost, and ease of excitation. This project has investigated different broadside filtering DRAs. Their out-of-band suppressions are between 16 dB and 30 dB. A two-port diversity broadside filtering DRA has also been studied successfully. As compared with the traditional one-port antenna, the two-port diversity design can provide a higher channel capacity. Apart from the broadside filtering DRAs, this project has also investigated omnidirectional filtering DRAs to meet different needs. The narrow-band, wideband, and dual-band omnidirectional filtering DRAs have been investigated successfully. All of the designs have been simulated, fabricated, and tested, and good agreement between the measured and simulated results has been obtained.

11215817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11215817.value: 對血氧飽和度進行高分辨率定量成像能夠為許多醫學問題提供有價值的信息，例如監測化學或放射療法后的腫瘤治療的效果、輔助癌症的早期診斷、以及基於神經和血樣的高度關聯對腦神經活動進行成像等。光聲成像在深層生物組織内具有光學對比度和高分辨率。由於血紅蛋白分子在結合氧前後具有顯著不同的光學吸收譜，因此光聲成像能夠靈敏地測量血氧飽和度。光聲信號強度正比于吸收的光能。而吸收的光能是組織吸收係數和光通量的乘積。因此測量血氧飽和度需要對不同波長的光通量進行精確的補償。然而，在深層組織中精確補償光通量是一個十分具有挑戰性的難題。儘管人們已經嘗試了很多方法，例如對光子傳播進行建模、利用光聲頻譜計算吸收係數、和超聲調製補償等，在活體深層組織内精確測量血氧飽和度仍然沒有得到有效解決。本研究提出了一種非侵入式的光聲技術，對深層生物組織内血氧飽和度進行定量成像。本研究的創新之処在於探索血氧結合的溫度相關特性，利用聚焦超聲換能器調製局部的血氧飽和度值，消除未知的光通量的影響，從而實現對血氧飽和度的絕對定量測量。我們將開發具有超聲加熱功能的光聲成像系統。利用仿体和小動物模型對成像的性能和安全性進行驗證。這一成果將為診斷、監測和研究與氧代謝相關的多種疾病提供一個有效的工具。本研究將從以下三個方面展開：1，研究和驗證在生物組織中超聲調製血氧飽和度的機理；2，開發具有超聲加熱功能的光聲成像系統，優化血氧飽和度成像方法；3，在仿体、活體組織、以及腦膠質瘤模型内驗證和演示定量血氧飽和度成像。

11215817.value: According to the oxygen-hemoglobin disassociation curve, temperature can effective change sO2 when pO2 and other factors remain constant. We used focused ultrasound modulate tissue temperature in a small range, and find that sO2 can have significant periodic change. We optimize the ultrasound power to make sure tissue safety. 11215817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11215817.value: Quantitative imaging of blood oxygen saturation (sO2) with high resolution provides valuable information for many preclinical and clinical applications, such as monitoring tumor treatment outcomes, assisting cancer diagnosis, and mapping the brain activities. We developed a new technique for non-invasive imaging of absolute blood sO2. Via exploring the temperature-dependent property of hemoglobin-oxygen binding, we cancelled the unknown local fluence between the PA signals at the two sO2 levels, and finally quantified the absolute sO2. An imaging system was developed to image absolute sO2. The imaging capability and safety were validated in both phantoms and small animal disease models. This technical advance in quantitative PA imaging of absolute sO2 provides a new effective tool for diagnosing, monitoring, or studying many oxygen-metabolism related diseases. We will focus on the following three specific aims: (1) To study the mechanism and validate the safety of the ultrasound-based sO2 modulation in biological tissue; (2) To develop a PA imaging system with ultrasound heating function, and optimize the sO2 imaging method; (3) To validate the quantitative sO2 imaging with tissue phantoms and demonstrate the in vivo imaging of sO2 in Glioblastoma tumor model.

11215917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11215917.value: High-entropy alloys refer to multi-element solid-solution material in equiatomic ratio. In spite of the complex chemistry, high-entropy alloy can crystallize into an incredibly simple lattice, e.g., face centered cubic (fcc). High-entropy alloys exhibit large tensile ductility. For example, for FeCoNiCrNi alloy, the room temperature ductility reaches 40-50%. Studies have shown that at small strains, the plasticity in high-entropy alloys is mediated by dislocations. At large strains, however, an unusual strain hardening is observed: a rapidly decreasing hardening rate at small strains followed by an increase-decrease in hardening rate at large strains. Even more remarkably, the tensile ductility further increases at low temperatures. For FeCoNiCrNi, when the test temperature decreases from 293 K to 77 K, the tensile ductility increases from about 40% to more than 70%. Nanotwinning has been proposed as an additional deformation mechanism, with the main evidence coming from TEM analysis of samples taken from interrupted tests. Aside from twinning, other deformation mechanisms, e.g., stress-induced martensitic phase transformation, may also play a role. We propose to conduct in-situ neutron diffraction study to elucidate the unusual hardening mechanisms in high-entropy alloys. In-situ neutron diffraction is a powerful tool for study of mechanical behaviors as well as phase transformation in materials. Neutrons are highly penetrating, so it is particular well suited for study of bulk samples such as tensile test bars. In-situ loading experiments have made major contributions to our understanding of deformation in polycrystalline metals and in composite materials. The proposed study will focus on measurements at cryogenic temperatures and at large plastic strains. The neutron diffraction results will be corroborated with TEM analysis. Together, these experimental data will pinpoint the unusual deformation mechanisms in high-entropy alloys. Fundamental knowledge obtained from the proposed study will go a long way towards the design of new structure materials with superior mechanical properties. 高熵合金是一种等原子比多元素固溶体材料。虽然化学组成复杂，但是高熵合金可以形成十分简单的晶体结构，比如面心立方（fcc）。高熵合金具有十分优异的拉伸延展性，比如FeCoNiCr合金在室温下的伸长率可达40-50%。研究表明，在小变形范围内，高熵合金的塑性变形由位错主导。然而在大变形时，高熵合金表现出不同寻常的应变硬化行为：在小变形下硬化速率急剧减小，在大变形下呈现先增加后减小的硬化速率。更值得关注的是，高熵合金的延展性在低温下得到显著提高。当温度从293K下降至77K时，FeCoNiCr 合金的延伸率从约40%提升至高于70%。从TEM测试结果分析，纳米尺度的孪晶被认为是附加的变形机理。除了孪晶，其他的变形机理如应力引发的马氏体相变，也可能在塑形变形中起到一定作用。我们提出利用原位中子衍射研究阐明材料的变形机理以及相变行为的方法。中子的穿透力很高，所以特别适合用来研究块体材料（例如拉伸试样）。原位加载试验对于我们理解多晶金属材料和复合材料的变形机理有重要作用。本研究计划的重点在于利用中子衍射和透射电镜测试研究高熵合金在低温和大变形下的变形机理。已有的研究结果表明，本研究计划将会对设计高力学性能结构材料有重要贡献。

11215917.label: Realisation of objectives
11215917.value: This project was designed to study deformation behaviors in high-entropy alloys and elucidate the unusual hardening mechanisms. A rapidly decreasing hardening rate at small strains followed by an increase-decrease in hardening rate at large strains has been observed in high-entropy alloys. Even more remarkably, the tensile ductility further increases at low temperatures. In this project, we proposed a concerted study to determine the additional deformation modes (apart from dislocation slip) by in-situ neutron diffraction measurements with a focus on the following conditions: (a) large strains (~40%) and (b) low temperatures. The experimental data will pinpoint the unusual hardening behaviors and deformation mechanisms in high-entropy alloys. Fundamental knowledge obtained from the proposed study will go a long way towards the design of high-entropy alloys and other new structure materials with superior mechanical properties. The proposed project had four objectives, please see above. With respect to these project objectives, the project has been well executed overall, ultimately leading to 9 publications. In addition, three students have been trained. For objective 1, the in-situ neutron diffraction experiments under tensile loading up to 40% applied strain were conducted at the Engineering Materials Diffractometer TAKUMI (Beamline 19) of the Materials and Life Science Experimental Facility (MLF) at Japan Proton Accelerator Research Complex (J-PARC). The experimental data shows that the deformation progresses from dislocation slip to severe entanglement, where a sharp increase in dislocation density was observed in CrCoFeNi high-entropy alloy (see publication by Wang et al., Scripta Materialia (2018)). The fitting of the neutron data suggested possible evidence of planar defects at large strains. However, the presence of high dislocation density made the holistic peak width analysis difficult. A complementary neutron diffraction experiment was conducted at General Purpose Powder Diffractometer (GPPD) at China Spallation Neutron Source (CSNS). The high-resolution mode (0.2 %) of GPPD allows precise determination of additional deformation modes for the specimens retrieved from interrupted mechanical tests. A key to realizing objective 2 is determining the sample environments and geometries, which allows the in-situ neutron diffraction measurements under tensile loading at ultralow temperatures. The PI has been in contact with the instrument scientist at TAKUMI in J-PARC to design the specimens. Using the Cryogenic Loading Machine, the experiments were done successfully. These high-quality neutron data allow the assessment of lattice strains, texture evolution, peak with broadening, peak asymmetry, as well as phase transformation at several selected temperatures, i.e., 140 K, 40 K, 25 K, 15 K, et al. These results were used to uncover the deformation mechanisms for high-entropy alloys. Building up the success of the in-situ neutron experiments and correlating the transmission electron microscopy observation, the unusual work hardening behaviors in high-entropy alloys were elucidated (objective 3). At room temperature, the deformation was dominated by dislocation activities up to ~40% plastic strain despite the chemical complexity. The dislocation density increases sharply, accompanied by severe entanglement at large strain. The three-stage work hardening thereby is associated with the changes in dislocation behavior during deformation. At low temperatures, where an unusual increment of tensile ductility occurs, additional deformation modes, i.e., stacking faults, twinning, and serrations, play a role. For CrCoNi alloy with a low stacking fault energy, a face-centered cubic to hexagonal-close-packed martensitic transition was observed. The cooperation of the different deformation mechanisms in high-entropy alloys underpins the unusually large ductility and extreme work hardening at low temperatures. (see publications by Naeem et al., Science Advances (2020), He et al., Nano Letters (2020)) After determining the existence of multiple deformation mechanisms in high-entropy alloys at low temperatures, a detailed analysis was conducted to quantify the contribution of individual deformation mechanisms to yield stress and work hardening. Taking CrFeCoNi as an example, dislocation contributed to ~94% of work hardening at room temperature. The contribution of planar faults, including stacking faults and twinning, increases steadily with temperature decreasing, reaching ~28% at 25 K. In terms of yield stress, the Peierls stress increases significantly with temperature decreasing, while the athermal contribution was ~183 MPa at all temperatures. (see publications by Naeem et al., Acta Materialia (2021)) For the purpose of education and training, the project supported three PhD students over different period of time. • Ms. Bing Wang, who received a PhD degree in 2018 • Ms. Haiyan He, who received a PhD degree in 2020 • Mr. Muhammed Naeem, who received a PhD degree in 2020 They have travelled multiple times to neutron scattering and synchrotron facilities in Japan, Australia, US, China, and all have received ample training and experience on the use of neutron and synchrotron scattering techniques. Dr. He is now a Distinguished Young Research Fellow at the Greater Bay Area University.

11215917.label: Major findings and research outcome
11215917.value: The study of CrMnFeCoNi HEAs at ultra-low temperature (15 K) revealed the cooperation of multiple deformation mechanisms. Using in situ neutron diffraction, we demonstrated the interaction of a rich variety of deformation mechanisms in high-entropy alloys at 15 K, which began with dislocation slip, followed by stacking faults and twinning, before transitioning to inhomogeneous deformation by serrations. Quantitative analysis showed that the cooperation of these different deformation mechanisms led to extreme work hardening. The low stacking fault energy plus the stable face-centered cubic structure at ultralow temperatures, enabled by the high-entropy alloying, played a pivotal role in bridging dislocation slip and serration. This work was published in Sci. Adv., 2020. Phase transformation is another effective means to increase the ductility of a material, especially for high-entropy alloys where the stacking fault energy is low. However, the underlying mechanisms for a commonly observed face-centered-cubic to hexagonal-close-packed (fcc-to-hcp) phase transformation are far from being understood. With in situ loading study with neutron diffraction, we revealed a bulk fcc-to-hcp phase transformation in CrCoNi at 15 K under tensile loading. By correlating the deformation characteristics of the fcc phase with the development of the hcp phase, we show that the nucleation of the hcp phase was triggered by intrinsic stacking faults. The confirmation of a bulk phase transformation adds to the myriads of deformation mechanisms available in CrCoNi, which together underpin the unusually large ductility at low temperatures. This work was published in Nano Lett., 2021. The deformation behavior of CrFeCoNi high-entropy alloy was quantitatively studied by in situ neutron diffraction at room temperature, 140 K, 40 K, and 25 K. The stacking fault probability reached ∼4.7% at low temperatures. The dislocation density at 40 and 25 K evolved similarly and had a very high value of ∼9.2 × 1015 m−2. The contributions from different deformation mechanisms to the yield strength and strain hardening have been estimated. The athermal contributions to the yield strength were ∼183 MPa at all temperatures, while the Peierls stress increased significantly at low temperatures (from 148 MPa at room temperature to 493 MPa at 25 K). Dislocations contributed to ∼94% strain hardening at room temperature. Although the dislocation strengthening remained the major hardening mechanism at very low temperatures, the planar faults contribution increased steadily from 6% at room temperature to 28% at 25 K. This work was published in Acta Mater., 2021.

11215917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11215917.value: The demand for structural materials that can withstand extreme temperatures has been a major challenge facing society. During the study of deformation in CrMnFeCoNi HEAs, we found an excellent combination of strength-ductility at ultra-low temperature, superior to the mechanical property at room temperature. Using in situ neutron diffraction, in conjunction with electron microscopy analysis, we revealed the activation of multiple deformation mechanisms together with their competition and interactions at ultralow temperature. The deformation started with dislocation slip, followed by stacking faults and twinning, before transitioning to serrations, thus leading to the large working hardening and uniform elongation at 15 K. The unique combination of complex chemistry and simple crystal structure, enabled by the high-entropy alloying, may hold the key to designing new materials for application in extreme environments. We hope to continue the study of the deformation of other HEAs with excellent mechanical properties, particularly at ultra-low and ultra-high temperatures, through computation-aided compositional design, and determine the deformation mechanisms and their interplay. The proposed study will call for unique sample environments, that is, the cryogenic and high-temperature loading machines, in order to capture the structure change and characterize the deformation behaviors. This proposal has been funded as a CRF.

11215917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11215917.value: High-entropy alloys refer to alloys containing multiple principle elements in near-equal atomic ratios. They can form a single-phase solute solution with an incredibly simple lattice, e.g., fcc (face-centered cubic) and bcc (body-centered cubic), instead of the intermetallic phases. The fcc high-entropy alloys are shown to exhibit large tensile ductility (ability to stretch) and significant work hardening. More remarkably, the tensile ductility further increases at low temperatures. Therefore, high-entropy alloys become promising materials, especially for applications in extreme environments. A long-standing issue in high-entropy alloy research is to figure out the reason for the excellent mechanical performance at low temperatures. In this project, the research team revealed the cooperation of multiple deformation mechanisms, including the dislocation slip, stacking faults, twinning, and serrations. This research achievement, which has been published in the journal Science Advance, also promotes the development of the “Low-temperature Deformation” research theme. This project embodies the true spirit of international collaborations. The research has been designed at CityU, but the team took advantage of state-of-the-art facilities, the neutron scattering instrument at the Japan Proton Accelerator Research Complex in Japan and the China Spallation Neutron Source in China, the synchrotron source at the Advanced Photon Source in the United States.

11216317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11216317.value: Middleboxes are widely deployed to perform complex packet processing in production networks. The proliferation of middleboxes are accompanied with growing concerns of the problems they bring, especially the expensive hardware and complex management. These concerns motivated the networking industry to launch a concerted effort towards Network Function Virtualization (NFV), which aims at replacing dedicated network function (NF) hardware with software implementations running on commodity servers. With virtualization, NFV holds great promises to reduce the network management cost and facilitate rapid deployment of new NFs. A key enabling technology to NFV is software dataplane. It provides a virtualized platform for hosting software middleboxes with high performance packet I/O to userspace. Several NFV dataplanes have been developed recently. Despite the progress, however, there is a great lack of understanding on NFV dataplane performance in the community. Specifically, how well do these software dataplanes perform packet processing in practice? More importantly, what are the areas of improvement to make software dataplanes more competent against hardware so they can be widely adopted by the industry? The PI proposes a measurement based approach to dissect, understand, and improve the performance of NFV software dataplane. The project entails three integrated components. First, we will conduct a comprehensive measurement study of NFV dataplane. We build a small-scale testbed using commodity x86 servers and NICs, and strategically choose open source software dataplanes using different virtualization and packet I/O technologies to cover the design space. We develop NFs with distinct packet processing logic, and deploy them in various settings such as service chains to fully understand performance. Our preliminary results show that current NFV dataplanes cannot achieve 10G line rate with small packets (64KB) or in the NF chaining scenario, while in general line rate can be achieved. Second, we aim to reveal the root causes of the above performance problems and identify novel solutions to improve NFV dataplane. Our early study demonstrates that, (1) software dataplanes should be architectured with support for multi-core in order to fundamentally scale the performance especially as networks evolve to 100G; and (2) for service chains, the dataplane can dynamically resize the NFs by using containers to reduce the number of VMs used and performance loss from cross-VM I/O. Third, we will prototype our software dataplane design and evaluate its performance on our testbed. We are committed to making our measurement results and new dataplane implementation code publicly available and readily usable for the community. Middleboxes，中间盒，被广泛部署以在生产网络中执行复杂的包处理。 中间盒的扩散伴随着对它们带来的问题的越来越多的关注，特别是昂贵的硬件和复杂的管理。 这些问题促成工业界为网络功能虚拟化（NFV）共同努力，其目的是通过在商品服务器上运行特定的软件实现来替换专用网络功能（NF）硬件。 通过虚拟化，NFV有望降低网络管理成本，并促进新型NF的快速部署。 NFV的关键技术是软件数据平面。 它提供了一个虚拟化平台，用于托管具有高性能数据包I/O的用户空间的软件中间盒。 最近不少NFV数据平面系统已被开发出来。 尽管我们取得了一些进展，但对与NFV数据平面性能的理解却非常缺乏。 具体来说，这些软件数据平面在实践中能多好得执行数据包处理？ 更重要的是，现有软件数据平面系统有哪些可以改进的领域，使得其性能可以和硬件处理匹敌，从而被行业广泛采用？ PI提出了一种基于测量的方法来解剖，理解和改进NFV软件数据平面的性能。该项目有三个组成部分。首先，我们将对NFV数据平面进行全面的测量研究。我们使用x86服务器构建小型测试平台，并战略性地选择使用不同虚拟化和分组I/O技术的开源软件数据平台来覆盖设计空间。我们开发具有不同数据包处理逻辑的NF，并将其部署在各种设置（如服务链）中以完全了解性能。我们的初步结果表明，目前的NFV数据通路在处理小包（64KB）或NF链接的情况下不能达到10G速率，而一般场景下线路速率可以实现。第二，我们的目的是揭示上述性能问题的根本原因，并找出改进NFV数据平面的新方法。我们早期的研究表明，（1）软件数据平台应结构化支持多核，以便从根本上扩展性能，特别是随着网络发展到100G;（2）对于服务链，可以通过使用容器动态地调整NF的大小，以减少使用的VM数量和跨VM I/O的性能损失。第三，我们将对我们的软件数据平面设计进行原型设计，并在我们的测试平台上评估其性能。我们致力于使我们的测量结果和新的数据平台实施代码公开可用，并为社区提供便利。

11216317.label: Major findings and research outcome
11216317.value: We have carried out a comprehensive performance measurement of NFV dataplanes. Specifically, we compare two state-of-the-art open-source NFV dataplanes, BESS and ClickOS, using commodity 10GbE NICs under various typical workloads. Our key observations are that (1) both dataplanes have performance issues processing small (≤128B) packets; (2) it is not always the best to colocate all VMs of a service chain on one server due to NUMA effect. We propose resource allocation strategies to remedy the problems, including carefully adding vNIC queues and CPU cores to vNFs, and distributing VNFs of a service chain to separate servers. To essentially address these problems and scale their performance, software dataplanes need to improve the support for NIC queues and multiple cores. Our results were published at The 2nd Workshop on Cloud-Assisted Networking, colocated with ACM CoNEXT 2017. CoNEXT is one of the top conferences in computer networking. Our measurement study also helped with our collaboration effort on improving the software dataplane performance. For example, in our ICDCS 2018 paper, we have developed a new NFV framework called DHL that exploits FPGA for better forwarding performance.

11216317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11216317.value: Our measurement findings suggest that NFV frameworks need to improve their support for NIC queues and multiple CPU cores. This may inspire further research and development in industry to improve the dataplane performance of NFV. One may also target a specific application or scenario to better exploit the unique characteristics of the workloads for a new NFV system.

11216317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11216317.value: Network Function Virtualization (NFV) holds great promises to fundamentally tackle the deployment and management problems of proprietary hardware based middleboxes, by relying on virtualization and software packet processing. This project conducts a measurement based study to dissect, understand, and improve the performance of software dataplane in NFV. We build a small-scale testbed using commodity x86 servers and NICs, and strategically choose open source software dataplanes using different virtualization and packet I/O technologies to cover the broad design space. Our results reveal that there are performance bottlenecks with existing software dataplane, especially when processing small packets with multiple CPU cores. Based on the measurement study, we also design and implement several new frameworks to improve either the software forwarding performance or the management capability of NFV in data center and wide area networks.

11216817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11216817.value: Forward error control (FEC) coding is a key technique in modern digital communication systems. The length of a code block is limited by many factors. Short block length is required in environments involving low latency, sporadic packets and fast time-varying channel conditions. Most communication systems, such as cellular networks, support multiple users. However, most existing methods for short FEC code design do not consider this factor, even though their applications are for multi-user systems. The work of this project is different from the conventional methods. We will take the presence of multiple users into consideration. This project is targeted for multi-user up-link channels. The basic principle is to allow partial transmission overlapping among users, so more redundancy can be added for better error protection capability. Interestingly, such partial overlapping results in a “linear” spatial coupling effect. Spatial coupling has been an active research topic recently for FEC code design. By coupling many component codes together, spatial coupling enhances performance at the expensed of increased block length. Long block length is commonly regarded as a disadvantage in conventional spatial coupling techniques. In the proposed work, coupling is realized by the linear addition in an up-link channel. The related interference problem is resolved using iterative detection. The linear coupling technique improves performance but does not increase the block length at each user. Consequently, the new scheme can achieve the advantage of conventional spatial coupling while avoid its disadvantage. Our initial analysis and simulation results provide strong evidences that the linear coupling strategy is promising. Our work is still preliminary. More research effort is still required to conduct comprehensive and rigorous investigation into the problems involved. The block length issue has been extensively discussed recently for 5G wireless systems. Short block length is in demand for emerging services such as machine-to-machine communications. This project is to meet this demand and develop novel solutions for the short block length coding problem. 前向纠错编码是现代数字通信系统中的关键技术。编码码长受限于许多因素。短码在低延迟，突发数据和快速时变信道的环境中有重要的应用。 大多数通信系统（如蜂窝网络）都支持多个用户。然而现有的短码设计方法即使其应用是针对多用户系统，也大多不考虑多用户这个因素。 此项目与传统方法不同关键在于， 我们将考虑多个用户的存在。此项目的应用是多用户上行链路。其基本原理是允许多个用户的传输信号之间部分重叠，由此引进更多的冗余以改善纠错能力。有趣的是，这种部分重叠等价于“线性”空间耦合。所谓空间耦合是FEC码设计的一个活跃的研究课题。空间耦合通过将许多分量码耦合在一起，以增加长度为代价改善性能。因此，码长通常被认为是常规空间耦合技术的缺点。 在此项目中，我们通过在上行链路中多个用户的天然线性相加来实现耦合。由此产生的干扰问题可以通过迭代检测得到解决。这样线性耦合技术即提高性能，又不增加每个用户的码长。因此新方案可以带来空间耦合的优点又同时避免其缺点。我们的初步分析和仿真结果为此策略提供了有力证据。我们的工作还在初步阶段。还需要对涉及的问题进行全面严密的研究。 最近对5G系统的讨论广泛涉及编码长度问题。新的机器对机器的通信需要较短的码长。此项目旨在满足这一需求，为短码设计问题寻找新颖的解决方案。

11216817.label: Realisation of objectives
11216817.value: Objective 1: We have been working on an interleave division multiple access (IDMA) scheme to support high overloading applications with short frame lengths. We found an analysis technique for IDMA systems and proved its capacity approaching capability. This work is reported in journal publication 1. We developed a linear-spatial coupling technique for IDMA systems. This scheme demonstrated several remarkable features, including approaching Gaussian shaping capacity, short block length and flexible universal coding rates. This work is reported in journal publication 4. We investigated several strategies to improve the matching property for IDMA receivers, which involves superposition coding, repetition coding and zero-padding. We devised a low-cost shifted interleaving scheme to reduce implementation cost of IDMA. The combination of zero-padding and shifted interleaving is closely related to spatial-coupling. The new scheme is referred to as shift division multiple-access (CSDMA), in which user-specific shifting is used to replace user-specific interleaving in IDMA. We demonstrated that CSDMA can offer almost the same performance as the original IDMA in low-density parity-check or turbo coded systems, but with considerably lower implementation cost. We also showed that the zero-padding and shifted interleaving technique also works well with very short frame length. This work is reported in journal publication 3. In the works mentioned above, we followed the industrial standards for the 5th generation (5G) cellular systems and used practical frame lengths such as 616 and 496 information bits. We collected a large amount of experimental results to demonstrate that the new scheme can offer improved performance at short frame lengths. Objective 2 We have been working techniques to improve transmission rate and reduce error floor. With linear coupling, the transmitted signals are approximately Gaussian distributed which has a high peak to average power ratio problem. Clipping can be applied to reduce PAPR, but it leads to an error floor problem. We developed an iterative compensation method to treat clipping distortion. This technique had been studied before based on extrinsic information exchange between a decoder and a clipping distortion estimator. In our new approach, feedback in the form of a posteriori information from the decoder is investigated. Correlation may be introduced among messages in iterative processing when a posteriori information is directly used as feedback. We showed that carefully choosing a linearization model can suppress such correlation. We showed that the new technique can noticeably improve performance in multi-user systems. This part of work is reported in journal publication 2. Objective 3 We have been working the comparison between the conventional turbo linear minimum mean square error (LMMSE) algorithm and a novel extrinsic message aided orthogonal approximate message passing OAMP algorithm. The latter requires the input and output errors of local processors to be orthogonal to each other, which is more relaxed than the extrinsic requirement as in turbo. We derived a state evolution procedure to analyze the performance of OAMP in coded systems. We conjectured that this state evolution procedure is accurate, which is verified by simulation results. Under this conjecture, we showed that OAMP can potentially outperform the conventional turbo-algorithm under certain standard assumptions for iterative decoding. This finding is significant, since the turbo algorithm has long been viewed as the best solution for receiver design in complicated channel conditions. Our work offers a new and inspiring direction for better solutions. This part of work is reported in journal publications 5, 6 and 7.

11216817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11216817.value: We made a number of discoveries in this project, as listed below. - a spatially-coupled multi-user transmission and detection scheme, - a low cost IDMA transmission scheme, - an OAMP based detection algorithm, - a treatment for the clipping effect, - a new semi-blind receiver algorithm for MIMO systems, - theoretical limits of AMP and OAMP based detection algorithms. 11217217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11217217.value: Mechanical cues from microenvironment regulate diverse forms of cell physiology. For example, it may direct programmed cell live/death, by which dissolution of extracellular matrix (ECM) proteins promotes capillary involution in the formation of branching networks. Recently, our group has discovered that cells can exert a new type of force – torque. This cellular torque has an intrinsic rotational bias, i.e. clockwise or counterclockwise, depending on cell types. Similar to other cellular force, this biased torque may also couple with a type of environmental cues and potentially regulate the mechanics-related physiology. However, due to the lack of appropriate platform, this hypothesis remains greatly unknown. Emerging evidences shows that the rotational bias is related to a swirl pattern of actin filament anchored on ECM proteins, suggesting that a one-way ratchet pattern of ECM proteins may provide a mechanical cue to enhance or reverse the intrinsic rotational bias of cells. Based on this rationale, we will 1) construct a nanowire magnetoscope integrating the one-way ratchet pattern of ECM proteins to 2) characterize the modulated rotation and torque of cells for 3) exploring the dependence of programmed cell live/death. First, we will build the nanowire magnetoscope and fabricate the one-way ratchet patterns of ECM proteins through photolithography. Second, by culturing NIH 3T3 fibroblasts in the system, we will evaluate the change of rotational bias of cells based on the torque measurement and nucleus rotation. Meanwhile, actin cytoskeleton on the ratchet patterns will be analyzed to explore the potential change of the chiral alignment. Moreover, we will also explore whether the induced rotational bias of cells, if exists, can be “memorized” when the mechanical cues from ratchet patterns is subsequently removed, addressing a possibility of prolonged influence of rotational cue in cell’s fate. At last, we will evaluate cell viability in response to the induced rotational bias using MTS assay and live/death assay. It is to provide a potential association between cell’s rotational bias and the programmed cell live/death important for tissue morphogenesis. Together, this integrated platform combining ratchet patterns and nanowire magnetoscope will offer a valuable tool for understanding how rotational cues from environment is coupled with the cells’ intrinsic rotational bias, opening up a new dimension in mechanotransduction in the future. 細胞外微環境中的力學因子對多種細胞生理活動起重要的調控作用。例如，細胞外基質蛋白溶解可導致內皮細胞的程序性死亡與毛血管壁收縮，從而形成分支的毛細血管網路。近來，本團隊發現了一種全新的細胞力——細胞扭力。這種細胞扭力可依細胞類型而具有內在順時針或逆時針自旋偏向。與其他的細胞力類似，細胞扭力也可能與某種微環境因子耦合並調控與力學有關的細胞生理活動。然而，現有的細胞力學測試裝置並不足以探索這一假設。 新興的證據顯示，細胞的左右不對稱性與肌動蛋白微絲束的旋轉排列有關。由於此微絲束末端鉚接在細胞外基質蛋白上，此提示了單向的棘輪狀細胞粘附島或可提供一種機械因子以增強或逆轉細胞的自旋偏向。基於以上假設，我們計劃1）在現有的磁性納米線顯微鏡上集成單向棘輪狀細胞粘附島、2）表徵經上述調控下的細胞扭力和細胞核旋轉、3）並探索相應的細胞程序性活性/凋亡。首先，我們應用光刻法製備棘輪狀細胞粘附島，並將其集成在磁性納米線顯微鏡上。之後，我們將在裝置內接種NIH 3T3小鼠胚胎成纖維細胞，並測量在該棘輪上的細胞扭力和細胞核旋轉，並評估細胞自旋偏向的轉變。同時，我們將觀察細胞的肌動蛋白微絲束在不同方向棘輪狀細胞粘附島調控下的旋轉排列。若棘輪狀細胞粘附島經證實有效，我們將進一步探索細胞是否在後續棘輪移除後仍可「記憶」棘輪所提供的機械效應，以此判斷棘輪狀細胞粘附島對細胞的長遠影響。最後，我們將借MTS試驗與細胞活性試驗以研究棘輪狀細胞粘附島對細胞活性的影響。由此，我們將對細胞自旋偏向與程序性活性/凋亡之間建立聯繫。以上，我們通過磁性納米線顯微鏡集成棘輪狀細胞粘附島， 為探索胞外旋轉環境因子與細胞自旋的耦合機制建立了有效的實驗平臺，從而為未來的細胞機械力傳導生理與組織生成打開了一個全新的研究維度。

11217217.label: Realisation of objectives
11217217.value: This project has three objectives: 1: To develop nanowire magnetoscope integrated with microengineered one-way ratchet patterns; 2: To characterize the cellular rotational bias induced by the ratchet patterns; 3: To explore the programmed cell live/death in response to the rotational cues. The objective 1 was proposed based on our previously developed nanowire magnetoscope that uses internalized ferromagnetic nanowires for measuring the chiral bias of cell rotation. Using this platform, we have found cellular torque with chiral bias depending on cell types. However, such measurement is limited because only very few cells can internalize nanowire internalization, which makes the characterization difficult and inconsistent. To overcome this, we have developed a new strategy by measuring the chiral bias of nucleus rotation and chiral pattern of actin filament. While nanowire is not used, such assay enables great number of cells for statistical analysis. Based on it, we found a change of chiral bias upon lineage-specific induction. Specifically, cultured on circular micropatterns, human mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) exhibited an anticlockwise (ACW) -biased nucleus rotation and swirling pattern of actin filaments. Interestingly, with adipogenic induction, the chiral bias was reversed to clockwise (CW) -biased, and such reversed chirality was consistently expressed in terminally differentiated adipocytes. This part has been published in an international journal (Bao, Yuanye. , Wu, Siying. , Chu, Lok Ting. , Kwong, Hoi Kwan. , Hartanto, Hogi. , Huang, Yaozhun. , Lam, Miu Ling. , Lam, Raymond H. W. & Chen, Ting-Hsuan*. (4 Aug 2020). Early Committed Clockwise Cell Chirality Up-Regulates Adipogenic Differentiation of Mesenchymal Stem Cells. Advanced Biosystems. 4/10. 2000161 doi:doi.org/10.1002/adbi.202000161) and the first author, Yuanye Bao, graduated in Jan 2019 with a PhD degree. For objective 2, ratchet patterns were originally proposed to induce and regulate cellular rotational bias. However, our experiment does not support this hypothesis. As an alternative, we have developed 2 other strategies. First, chemical treatment was explored. We have previous found that actomyosin cytoskeleton may function as a built-in machinery underlying the cell chirality. Actomyosin activity was reported important in vivo, since the use of its inhibitors may abolish or even reverse the LR features of tissue morphogenesis. For cells on micropatterns, the expression of chirality also depends on the actomyosin activity at the micropattern boundaries. Such notion was further supported by a recent report, which directly elucidated a chiral orientation of actin filament when cultured on micropatterned circles. Using micropatterning on human mesenchymal stem cells (hMSCs), we selected Latrunculin A (LatA), which inhibits actin polymerization by sequestering monomeric actin, Lysophosphatidic acid (LPA), which stimulates RhoA and the formation of actin filaments, and Cytochalasin D (CD), which prevents actin polymerization by its high affinity to growing ends of actin nuclei. We found that LatA led to a distinct CW-biased swirling pattern of actin and nucleus rotation, which is consistent with a recent report. Notably, while the actin filament was not analyzable for cells with CD treatment, CW-biased nucleus rotation was still observed, which is expected since CD and LatA have similar effect of inhibiting actin polymerization. In contrast, LPA treatment led to a neutral, non-biased actin pattern and nucleus rotation. Together, the results demonstrated that LatA and CD treatment can induce a CW biased chirality. (Bao, Yuanye. , Wu, Siying. , Chu, Lok Ting. , Kwong, Hoi Kwan. , Hartanto, Hogi. , Huang, Yaozhun. , Lam, Miu Ling. , Lam, Raymond H. W. & Chen, Ting-Hsuan*. (4 Aug 2020). Early Committed Clockwise Cell Chirality Up-Regulates Adipogenic Differentiation of Mesenchymal Stem Cells. Advanced Biosystems. 4/10. 2000161 doi:doi.org/10.1002/adbi.202000161) and the first author, Yuanye Bao, graduated in Jan 2019 with a PhD degree. In addition, we have also found that prior culture condition with high/low density can create remnant effects on cell chirality after reseeding. For cells cultured in circular micropatterns on rigid substrate, clear actin stress fibers can be observed. However, these filaments were dissembled on soft substrate, suggesting that actin is involved in the dependence of chirality on substrate stiffness. Such dissembled actin can be observed in cells after a series of low-density cultures which disorganize the formation of actin rings. Here, by using high-density culture supplemented with inhibitors of actin polymerization, the effect of low-density cultures was recaptured, suggesting that the series of subcultures with high/low density may be an in vitro aging process that modifies the actin cytoskeleton, causing a remnant attenuation of cell chirality even after trypsin digestion and reseeding. Such finding has been published in a peer-reviewed journal (Kwong, Hoi Kwan, Huang, Yaozhun, Lam, Miu Ling & Chen, Ting-Hsuan* (4 Jun 2019). Remnant Effects of Culture Density on Cell Chirality After Reseeding. ACS Biomaterials Science & Engineering. 5. 3944 - 3953. doi:10.1021/acsbiomaterials.8b01364). We have achieved 85% for this objective 1. On the other hand, we also discovered that the projected area of cells would also regulate the expression of cell chirality. We applied arrays of fibronectin micro-islands with different circular areas, surrounding by cell-repellent Pluronic coating. Time-lapse measurement of nucleus rotation of HFF-1 fibroblasts was again used to record nucleus rotation on micro-islands. Interestingly, when cells spread on 500 μm2 pattern, the nucleus rotation is neutral. Starting from 750 μm2, nucleus rotation becomes CW-biased, i.e., 45.83 ± 1.96 % ACW with p-value < 0.01, which is consistent with the chiral bias of cell during initiate spreading. From 1000 μm2 to 2500 μm2, the chiral nucleus rotation is changed to neutral and then reversed to ACW-biased, i.e., 63.43 ± 2.90 % ACW with p-value < 0.0001 on 2500 μm2 of micro-islands. Thus, the results on micro-islands provide a direct and consistent evidence showing cell projected area as the key factor for chirality reversal. Furthermore, to test the universality of such phenomenon, we have analyzed the nucleus rotation on two other cell types, C2C12 mouse myoblasts and human mesenchymal stem cells (hMSCs). They all show the same dependence of chirality reversal based on cell spreading area, demonstrating the universality of this relationship. We have prepared a manuscript to report this finding and will submit it soon. Together. We have achieved 85% for this objective 2. For objective 3, it was proposed to test the possible regulation of cell metabolism and the programmed live/death via change of cell chirality. To our surprise, we found that lineage commitment of hMSCs can be regulated by such early differentiated chiral actin cytoskeleton. We conducted lineage-specific induction with LatA and CD treatment, which forces a CW-biased chiral actin cytoskeleton resembling cytoskeletal features upon adipogenic induction. We found a pronounced increased percentage of adipocytes in adipogenic medium supplemented with LatA. In contrast, a decrease of ALP activity was observed in cells in osteogenic and mixed induction with LatA. Consistently, similar up-regulation of adipogenic commitment was also observed in cells with CD treatment. Taking together, the results showed that the forced CW-biased chiral actin upon LatA or CD treatment can indeed up-regulate the commitment of adipogenic differentiation. 11217217.label: Major findings and research outcome
11217217.value: First, the application of micro and nanotechnology provides a new standard for characterizing cell chirality. Our use of nucleus rotation has provided a unique method for characterizing cell chirality. Cell chirality can be viewed as orientation of actin fibers, left-right-biased cell polarity, multicellular orientation, and cell migration, which is nonstandard and sometimes controversial. Here, our results show significant and consistent difference in single cell rotation on circular micro-islands. Compared to analysis of actin orientation, our method allows quantitative measurement without even the presence of distinct actin bundles, making it more applicable in broader scenario. Second, we found that cell chirality can be regulated by adjustment of the projected area of cells and inhibition of actin polymerization. While cross-linking and polymerization of actin filament has been related a reversal of cell chirality, how such modulation can lead to reversed chirality at cellular level remains vague and unresolved. Here, because reduction of the projected area of cells and inhibition of actin polymerization all suppress actin polymerization, our result suggests polymerization of radial fibers as the main driver for ACW chirality. Thus, the chirality reversal can be understood as tilting the balance between classes of actin fibers by means of adjusting cell spreading area or regulating the main factor of actin, i.e. myosin II, α-actinin-1, and mDia2, providing a general, previously unidentified mechanistic understanding of chirality reversal. Third, with such understanding, it allows strategical alternation of cell chirality to study its role in biological events. For example, we have demonstrated that transient silencing conducted before induction can still result in an increased ACW after 6 days of dual induction, and eventually causes a reduced percentage of adipocytes, suggesting the role of chirality in cell differentiation. Moreover, with increasing evidence showing that cell chirality as the main driver of asymmetry in tissue/organ orientation, our findings also allow better insight of cell chirality reversal in regulating developmental process in the even larger scale, e.g. establishment of left-right body axis for visceral distribution and chiral morphogenesis in tissue/organ architecture, providing new ways of understanding or even control of tissue formation.

11217217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11217217.value: We will bring a mechanistic understanding of chirality reversal. Cell chirality is seen by cell rotation and migration, and can be opposite from one cell type to another. While cell chirality might be originated from an axial rotation of righthanded double helix of actin filament, how such single form of molecular handedness can be unfolded to mirrored chirality at cellular level remains as vague and mysterious. Based on the finding of this project, we aim to further investigate the fundamental mechanism of how chirality in single cells is prepared with reversed chirality. By using a series of small-molecular inhibitors, we will first narrow the factors, e.g., actin polymerization, assembly of transverse arc, crosslinking of actin filament etc., that causes chirality reversal. By combining the analysis of actin distribution and alignment, a particular type/arrangement of actin fibers associated with chirality reversal will be sorted out. Next, the cytoskeletal components in those actin fibers will allow the identification of key regulator responsible for such chirality reversal, which can be further validated by siRNA silencing and overexpression assays. With such understanding, it allows strategical alternation of cell chirality, e.g., up/down regulation of the key component, to study its role in biological events.

11217217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11217217.value: Do cells have chirality, or left-right asymmetry? If yes, how to measure and control it? It is a fundamental question in basic science. In recent years, researchers observe that cells can orient and migrate with left-right bias, or chiral bias, and such bias can later cause formation of tissue architecture with left-right asymmetry. As such, it is important to understand how cell chirality emerges and how it interacts with the microenvironment. To tackle this question, we develop a series of microscopic techniques that can automatically extract the chiral rotation and orientation of cells. By characterizing cell chirality, we found that cell chirality can be regulated by adjustment of the projected area of cells and inhibition of a key component of cytoskeleton. Finally, applying our understanding of cell chirality, we found that stem cell differentiation can be regulated by such early changed chiral actin cytoskeleton. With such interaction, we reveal a new feedback loop through which stem cell differentiation can be guided into a specific fate based on the evolvement of cell chirality, enabling a specialized and engaged chiral behavior upon lineage specification and instruct the formation chiral morphology in tissue architecture.

11217317.label: Realisation of objectives
11217317.value: Obj.1 To compile a complete (thermal-EHL) numerical analysis of ZEV lubricated point contacts taking into account the boundary slip effect. (*Details can be found in Peer-reviewed publications (3, 4, and 5) in Part C.) A boundary slip thermal-EHL model was successfully constructed to consider the coupled influences of boundary slip and thermal effect under ZEV point contact. The model was solved by finite element method. Stabilization techniques (Galerkin least square/streamline upwind Petrov Galerkin and isotropic diffusion algorithms) and relaxation treatment were employed to enhance the performance of the boundary slip thermal-EHL model. Thus, the lubrication scheme under ZEV condition was numerically analyzed [Paper (3)]. The constant slip length model [Paper (3)] and the more general critical shear stress model [Paper (4)] were adopted to simulate the boundary slip. For the critical shear stress model, the slip direction upon the attainment of the critical shear stress value was successfully resolved by using a linear complementarity principle [Paper (3)]. The boundary slip is proved to be a key parameter for forming effective lubrication under ZEV condition. Another key parameter for forming effective lubrication is the surface velocity, which determines the amount of lubricant flowing through the contact area. The lubricating film thickness increases with surface speed, but temperature also increases. However, temperature rise reduces if the magnitude of slip is large. EHL can be realized under ZEV condition when the surface speed and the oleophobicity meet the required values. The developed numerical framework was further used to investigate the flow behavior and stress inside the contact bodies which are hard to study by experiments. The effects of slip coating and the interlayer on lubrication and mechanical performances were studied [Paper (5)]. In terms of lubrication performance, adopting a soft surface coating or soft coating/interlayer in pure rolling condition would increase the film thickness. Also, the pressure of the lubrication film is also reduced. The reduced pressure allows smaller von Mises stress inside the contacting bodies. Obj.2 To conduct experiments with surfaces of different levels of oleophobicity and oils of different viscosities under different load and speed conditions to obtain their effects on the ZEV EHL film formation and friction. (*Details can be found in Peer-reviewed publications [1] and [2] in Part C.) Experiments were conducted with both oleophobic surface/oleophilic surface (glass) and oleophilic surface (steel)/oleophilic surface (glass) contacts. The oleophobic surface was realized by applying a commercially available anti-fingerprint coating, AFC (with trade name “Aculon”), on the glass surface. Experimental results proved that introducing boundary slip into ZEV contact helped to form effective lubrication and avoided wear of the contacts. The influence of surface speed with two PAO oils (PAO 100 and PAO 40/PAO 100 mixture) was studied. The film thickness increased with surface speed. PAO 100, which has a higher viscosity than the PAO 40/100, acquired effective lubrication film with a smaller minimum surface speed than PAO40/100. Experiments were also conducted using a benchtop rolling bearing tester. Four retainerless bearings (SKF NCF 3004 CV) were mounted on the rotating shaft under constant load and speed in a test. The overall bearing torque was measured. The rolling elements of the chosen sample bearing type can be dismounted. Half of the total number of rollers were dip-coated with Aculon, such that their surfaces were oleophoic. The bearing was then reassembled with alternate no-coat and slip-coated rollers. The results showed that the overall friction torque of the treated bearings was reduced by around 20%, and it verified the new concept. The slip/no-slip contacts facilitate effective lubrication under ZEV condition. Obj. 3 To evaluate commercially available oleophobic coatings for the current study. Many more hydrophobic and oleophobic coatings are now available in the retail market than ever before. It represents the recent rapid growth of the technology in the field. Forty different products from 35 different brands were purchased. They were dip-coated on glass slides. Contact angle and contact angle hysteresis were measured with PAO 40 and compared. The measured contact angles are in the range of 30o to 108o, whilst the contact angle hysteresis is from 4o to 101o. Some of them produced rough surface finish, which makes them not suitable for bearing applications. The best coating that we found from the test was “Aculon”, which has a reasonably large contact angle (61o) with a very small contact angle hysteresis (8o). It is transparent and able to form a thin layer of thickness in nanometers.
