11217317.label: Major findings and research outcome
11217317.value: 1. Invention of a new type of retainerless rolling bearings. The whole project was triggered by the new idea that using a slip surface in lubricated contact with a non-slip surface would enable lubricant entrainment into the bearing contact under the so-called “zero entrainment velocity” (ZEV) condition. This project verified the idea numerically and experimentally. At the end, we implemented the idea on real rolling bearing tests and found that the new bearing type results in considerable friction reduction and service life prolongation. As a result, we filed a patent in the US. Note that the bearing test results were disseminated in the 14th National Symposium on Tribology in Guangzhou in Nov. 2019. (Refer to Papers [1] and [2] in Part C.) 2. Thermal-EHL analysis of lubricated point contacts under large slide-to-roll ratio (SRR) conditions. We successfully derived a numerical model that considers the coupled effects of boundary slip and heat transfer for EHL analyses of very large SRR contact (including ZEV, whose SRR equals infinity). With the incorporation of the linear complementarity principle to resolve the boundary slip direction, the numerical model can be applied to lubricated point contacts. The developed numerical framework is a good tool for the complete EHL analysis which includes the thermal and the boundary slip effects. We executed the complete EHL analysis for lubricated point contacts and found that the effects of slip and heat are complement to each other. The thermal effect dies down if the slip increases. The boundary slip reduces temperature rise and promotes film thickness due to the positive effect of lubricant entrainment. However, side leakage also increases with boundary slip and has a negative effect on film thickness. Hence, the lubricating film thickness may be reduced if the magnitude of the boundary slip is excessively small or too large. There exists an optimal boundary slip magnitude that delivers the optimum lubrication performance, i.e. the highest film thickness. Hitherto, the best practical way to implement endurable slip effects is by surface coatings. We applied the developed numerical algorithm to characterize the slip coating and the interlayer of different mechanical strengths and thicknesses. We found that adopting a soft surface coating or soft coating/interlayer would increase the film thickness. Also, the pressure of the lubrication film is also reduced, thereby alleviating the von Mises stress inside the contacting bodies. (Refer to Papers [3, 4 and 5] in Part C.)

11217317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11217317.value: To make the new retainerless bearing a success, one major hurdle is to have appropriate oleophobic coating. Boundary slip facilitated by physiosorbed thin molecular layers may not be sufficiently robust to sustain high shearing action in bearing contacts. Therefore, the use of hard coatings, such as diamond-like carbon (DLC), seems to be a better option for promoting the boundary slip effect from the perspectives of endurance and reliability. Recent research has determined that DLC doped with fluorine (F-DLC) enables good oleophobicity. The slip on F-DLC coated surfaces was proven by the reduction in friction in lubricated sliding friction tests. F-DLC coatings have the low surface energy and large contact angle. It is worth to work out the best formulation of F-DLC for the new bearing application.

11217317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11217317.value: This project has developed a new type of retainerless rolling element bearings. A bearing with no retainer can install more rolling elements, i.e., providing large bearing capacity. However, the rolling elements are squeezed into direct contact and slide against one another with the same surface speed but in opposite direction. While a surface drags oil into the contact, the other opposite-moving surface brings it out. As a result, no oil can be entrained into the bearing contact (termed as “zero-entrainment-velocity”, ZEV) leading to serious problems of friction and wear. We found that the friction of a lubricated sliding contact can be reduced if one of the surfaces is oleophobic (oil repelling). This concept was thus applied to a ZEV contact. The contact of oleophobic and oleophilic (oil-loving) surfaces running at ZEV can be separated by full hydrodynamic lubricating films. The new retainerless bearing design incorporates alternate "slip" (oleophobic) and "non-slip" (oleophilic) rolling elements. The rolling "non-slip" element entrains oil into the ZEV contact whilst the oil slips on the opposite-moving surface of the "slip" rollers. The lubrication problem of ZEV contact is solved, i.e. the new retainerless rolling bearing can be applied to a wider speed range with significantly reduced friction torque.

11217817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11217817.value: Rich sensors on mobile and wearable devices nowadays could offer valuable data for designing a variety of useful applications. However, these data recently are also revealed as double-edged swords, as they could form side-channels to leak aspects of user's information that is considered vital. In this project, we investigate a specific piece within this broad problem space: can the sensitive information, like passwords and personal data, frequently typed by user on mobile devices be inferred through the motion sensors of wearable devices on user's wrist? If so, the implication is serious, as the bar to launch this side-channel attack is trivial. Hence, if the answer is positive, it is natural to wonder how to prevent such motion or privacy leakage. The first aim of this project is to investigate whether the low-end wearable sensors owns the capability of accurate motion tracing to launch the side-channel attack above. User may hold the mobile device in an arbitrary gesture for typing and mobile's screen size is tiny. Lacking effective motion sensor processing technique, the typing plane, i.e., mobile's screen, cannot be reliably reconstructed in the first place, and erroneous sensor readings cannot truthfully derive wearable's moving neither. Therefore, without explicitly addressing this challenge, it is unclear whether the motion leakage is viable on miniature mobile devices with a possibly arbitrary typing plane attitude. The second aim of this project is to develop an effective countermeasure against such potential privacy leakage. Our proposed solution is inspired by the sensor-formed side-channel as well, but adopting a different channel frequency, i.e., sensor, in the design. We observe that most mobile devices are equipped with front camera. Our key idea is to use eye gaze for typing private information. This design is secure primarily due to two facts: 1) the eye gaze itself is difficult to eavesdrop and decode, and 2) no hand motions are involved in the typing. In summary, the idea proposed in this project to investigate the double-edged sides of mobile and wearable side-channels is of essential novelty, which closes the design loop for both the security risk discovery and countermeasure proposal. It can alarm people the potential privacy leakage risk when using mobile devices, while it could also provide an effective solution to migrate this issue. Moreover, the technical contributions made in motion tracing and gaze-based typing designs are also innovative. They may appeal to data analytics, sensing system design, and other domains as well. 移動穿戴設備上豐富的傳感器可用於很多實用系統和應用的設計當中。但是近些年的研究發現這些傳感器其實是一把雙刃劍，它們也可以形成各式各樣的側信道從而洩露許多與用戶相關的信息。在本項目中，我們重點研究一項重要並且具體的問題：對於用戶經常在移動設備上輸入的類似于密碼這樣的重要信息，有沒有可能通過用戶手腕上穿戴設備的傳感器推測出來？如果可能的話，這將形成用戶運動隱私的洩露，自然我們也會關心將如何應對。本項目的第一個目標就是研究商用穿戴設備的傳感器是否有能力準確恢復出用戶在敲擊過程中手部的運動從而實現如上描述的側信道攻擊，因為在用戶整個的敲擊過程中鍵盤可能呈任意的姿態同時移動設備的屏幕也可能較小。如果此過程中穿戴設備的運動不能準確恢復的話，輸入時的敲擊平面可能首先都無法正確恢復，同時推測出的移動軌跡也往往具有明顯變形。因此如果這些問題不被解決，是否能在未知姿態的小型移動設備上發起該側信道攻擊還不清楚。本項目的第二個目標就是研究有效的對策。我們的思路依舊是利用側信道，但是使用不同的傳感器。我們觀測到，絕大多數的移動設備都有前置攝像頭。因此我們的想法就是當用戶在輸入這些重要的數據的時候，用眼睛的視線代替手來輸入。這樣的方式比較安全的原因在於：第一，相對於移動傳感器的數據，用戶眼睛的視線信息比較難以破解；第二，在整個輸入的過程中沒有涉及任何手部的運動。總而言之，該項目的創新點在於同時研究了移動穿戴設備側信道的利與弊兩個方面。既揭示了側信道可能帶來的用戶運動隱私洩露的問題同時也提供了有效的解決方案。

11217817.label: Realisation of objectives
11217817.value: There are three objectives proposed in this project and we have completed all these objectives. The first objective is to explore users' privacy leak through wearable sensors. To this end, we have developed a new system to demonstrate the possibility of recovering the password typed on the mobile phone through the sensor data from the user's wearable device. In this system, we first propose an efficient motion data processing pipeline to deal with the noise and errors of motion data. With this design, each wearable device's movement displacement vector, which captures the user's finger transitions between keystrokes, can be reliably recovered. When the user enters the password on the mobile phone, these vectors constitute the entire trajectory of the user's finger. Furthermore, even if the movement trajectory of the user's finger can be recovered, the typed information still cannot be decoded immediately because of the unknown size of the keyboard - the lack of a correct decoding (or matching) reference. In this project, we observe that keyboard size information is implicit in the recovered movement trajectories, and we further propose a new method to estimate the most probable keyboard size information so that the entered password can finally be "decoded". In this project, we further find that even without wearable sensors on the user's wrist, this attack can be still enabled, i.e., leaking the information entered by the user on the mobile phone. To this end, we propose a new system design that demonstrates the possibility of inferring information typed on a mobile phone from the sound recorded by the microphone on the phone after proposing an efficient data processing method. The second objective aims to design effective countermeasures to enhance users' typing privacy. To this end, we first propose a new input solution that directly protects the user's password input. We have observed that most mobile devices are equipped with front cameras. Our main idea is to use eye gaze to enter private information. This design is secure mainly for two reasons: 1) eye gaze itself is hard to eavesdrop and decode, and 2) no hand movements are involved when typing. To this end, we propose a novel eye-sensing design that can reliably track the iris of the user's eye and further translate it into the user's gaze point. With this sensing capability, users can type on the phone with their eye gazes without having to press keys on the phone. Attacks through wearable sensors and recorded sounds cannot be launched when this new input method is used. In addition, we further consider how to secure authentication when the user takes other input methods without directly entering the password. To this end, we propose a general design that employs wireless or acoustic signals to protect users' voice command input from attacks or to provide continuous authentication services. In our daily life, using a card also avoids entering passwords, such as for access control and payments. However, this mechanism can be compromised if the card is lost or stolen. To this end, we propose a novel solution to make the card unusable for illegal users even if they get it. In summary, our proposed countermeasure methods can ensure the user’s privacy under various scenarios. The third objective is design implementation, prototyping and evaluation. We have developed and prototyped our proposed designs. Based on development, we have evaluated system performance and examined the effectiveness of attack and countermeasure designs. In conclusion, all the objectives proposed in this project have been achieved.

11217817.label: Major findings and research outcome
11217817.value: The major findings and research outcome of this project are as follows. 1) We found that although wearable and mobile devices provide great convenience to our daily life, people should pay attention to privacy issues when entering sensitive and important information on mobile devices because the sensors of wearable and mobile devices may be used by attackers to leak private information typed by the user through various side-channels due to these sensors. In this project, we have investigated the possibility of such attacks, which are presented in IEEE INFOCOM 2018 (Part-C-9-[1-2]), IEEE TMC (Part-C-8-[1]), IEEE ICDCS 2020 (Part-C-9-[4]) and IEEE TMC (Part-C-8-[3]). 2) We found that in order to defend against these attacks, we can explore new input methods that prevent the user's finger from touching the mobile device, so that the user's typing privacy is not leaked through the side-channel formed by the wearable and mobile sensors. To this end, we propose to utilize the front camera to sense the user's eyes as an input channel, where our design to sense user’s eyes is reported in IEEE TCSVS 2022 (Part-C-8-[6]). In addition, we have studied more security and privacy issues in IEEE IOTJ (Part-C-8-[7]) and NDSS 2020 (Part-C-9-[5]), and realized that people may authenticate themselves without directly typing passwords, which also faces various risks. To this end, we further propose effective mechanisms to protect user privacy when the user adopts various input methods such as voice-based input and card swiping. These designs are reported in IEEE IOTJ (Part-C-8-[2]), IEEE INFOCOM 2019 (Part-C-9-[3]), IEEE TMC (Part-C-8-[4]) and ACM IMWUT (Part-C-8-[5]). These designs can ensure the user’s privacy under various scenarios.

11217817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11217817.value: There are two potential directions for further exploration in the future. 1) Identify more advanced attacks that may occur in user’s electronic devices and alert people to such risks. 2) Propose effective solutions to defend against these new attacks to ensure user’s security and privacy.

11217817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11217817.value: The project found that as our mobile and wearable devices have more and more sensors, they can provide valuable information to enable many useful applications. However, these sensors can also be the weak point in various attacks on the device, allowing users' private information to be compromised. For the attack part, we showed that passwords that users typically need to type on a mobile device can be guessed by an attacker through such mobile or wearable side-channels. Fortunately, we further found that a variety of sensors can be leveraged to further develop effective countermeasures to defend against these attacks. In this project, we have demonstrated this possibility by developing novel and efficient methods for this purpose. Overall, this project will not only serve as a reminder that apparently innocuous sensing data can cause serious side-channel attacks when people use mobile and wearable devices, but will also explore how to fully explore the capabilities of embedded sensors to avoid these problems, which can be used to enhance user security and privacy when using mobile and wearable devices.

11218017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11218017.value: 細胞移動力對很多細胞作用都相當重要, 包括細胞移動，增生，和分裂。局部性的細胞牽引力通過焦點粘連作力(FAs)在細胞外基質(ECM)。細胞可以感知物質周圍，例如是硬度和表面形貌。 基於細胞的外圍，細胞可以表達不同的生物化學蛋白質去影響細胞移動。但是，有兩種不同層面的細胞作用現今社會仍然有着很少的知識。因為細胞牽引力在移動的時候是不斷反覆進行進化， 相當重要的是追蹤細胞移動力的即時發展對ECM互動有更深入的了解及分辨重要的細胞移動步驟。此外，ECM提供由微米到納米的細胞立體物質結構。為了去理解影響細胞牽引力在移動時候的因素，建立一個有着相似的物質特性的立體迷你環境是相當重要。所以，從迷你探測器在立體平台上對局限細胞牽引力的動態追蹤對了解細胞行為有着相當重要的影響。 除了ECM物質線索 外，外在力亦會改變細胞行為和生物過程。因此，我們可以透過對局限細胞位置施加外在力去影響細胞移動和細胞作用。但是，在對細胞力外力刺激上存在很多挑戰。因為細胞機械感知系統是可以解決納米解析度的物質差異，我們要建立能力在高解析度上準確地施加外在力。透過制造微柱作為外在力感知器和促動器，我們是可以控制細胞行為和它的移動路徑。 我們提供的立體平台當中的細胞牽引力迷你感知器可以引導細胞移動，並有着很多好處和獨特的能力包括 ：1）納米技術建立堆疊立體平台有高解析度的迷你感知器容許彈性的設計並有着準確的控制三維空間去模擬一個ECM。它能成為第一個實時追蹤細胞牽引力在不同的高度和立體面的移動過程； 2）細胞限制和引導可以結合在立體平台上。細胞牽引力的量度可以在一個局限的迷你環境上展示，並能更好地模仿細胞如何在組織上移動；3）納米結構放在微柱上容許局限的表面能量和有效的細胞接觸受控制；4）此平台能成為第一個以磁化微柱對施加外在力和局限作用力在細胞上的展示，同時能量度細胞牽引力；和5）此立體細胞移動平台可以局部地控制細胞引導過程，細胞限制，表面能量，和外在力去給我們對細胞ECM互動和細胞移動動態一個更深入的了解。 我們建立了一個迷你感知器和迷你促動器的立體細胞移動平台有着可以控制細胞引導，細胞局限，表面能量和外在力。細胞牽引力分布的動態改變可以被實時追蹤。實驗結果可以提供重要的知識讓我們更了解細胞移動的動態和細胞ECM互動。此研究能帶來深遠的影響因為它會持續影響之後微系統對控制細胞移動過程和細胞篩選，對快速及準確的診斷，預防和治療各種疾病有着重大的影響。

11218017.label: Realisation of objectives
11218017.value: Nanoimprint and dry etching technologies were developed to form the high aspect ratio microposts with guidance patterns on top of the microposts. The designs of the microposts were based on the optimization among smooth migration for cells moving on top of the microposts without being trapped in between, high sensitivity for traction force, and nanotechnology available to fabricate the needed designs and structures. Localized traction forces were measured by these microposts with integrated guiding topography and confinement. It was found that the arrangements of the microposts as well as the nanostructures on top of the microposts could significantly influence cell migration behaviors, such as speed and direction. Topographical guidance can influence the dynamic development of traction forces and can be used to regulate cell migration. This is the first study where cell traction force was monitor in real time, with and without guiding pattern, and in forward and reversed migration directions. To monitor dynamic changes in cell traction force during migration, the traction force in the leading, middle, and trailing regions were tracked every minute. Cellular shape, traction force, and cell migration speed were analyzed continuously in repeated cycles as osteoblasts underwent directional migration. The cells switched between contracted and elongated shapes during each migration cycle. When cells started to migrate with contracted cell shapes, the traction force in the leading and trailing regions reached 5.8±0.8 and 4.1±0.4 nN, respectively. As both the leading and trailing regions protruded and the cell became elongated, the traction force in both regions increased. The traction force in the leading region became larger and better aligned with the migration direction than in the trailing region during cell elongation. After the traction force peaked at 7.1±0.5 nN in the leading region and 6.0±0.5 nN in the trailing region, the trailing region was rapidly released and the cell speed peaked. After release, the traction force dropped and the cell started the next cycle of migration. The traction force took 51.9±6.7 min to build up while the cell remained elongated and 13.3±1.8 min to drop after the trailing region released. The traction force in the middle region remained small at 2.7±0.3 nN with little changes. The dynamic increments in traction force in both the leading and trailing regions during cell elongation confirmed that cell spreading was initiated by the traction force, which is consistent with previous studies which showed that initiation and maturation of focal adhesions (FAs) are triggered by the increased traction force. The highly aligned net traction force in the leading region with the migration direction could be related to the development of microtubules, which tend to align with the migration direction and grow towards the leading region. Traction force was also analyzed when the cells underwent 180° direction reversal. The traction force in the trailing region was lower than the leading region during the first cycle of forward migration. After the cell reversed its migration direction, the traction force in the original trailing region became larger and it became the new leading region. Consistent with previous observations on cell migration under durotaxis, these results indicate that cells prefer to migrate towards the region with higher traction force. Previous studies showed that traction force in the leading region was propulsive to move the cell forward, whereas the traction force in the trailing region was resistive. The results shown in this study suggest that the region with the larger traction force is the leading region which determines the cell migration direction. To compare guided and non-guided cell migration, parallel gratings were used to provide topographical guidance during cell migration. During guided cell migration, similar dynamic changes in traction force and cell shape were observed. Osteoblasts took 28.1±3.3 min to build up traction force to 4.8±0.3 nN in the trailing region as the cell became elongated. The traction force decreased rapidly, in 5.1±0.4 min, in the trailing region to 2.2±0.2 nN as the trailing region released and the cell contracted. Although the cyclic changes in cell traction force and shape were similar for guided cell migration, the magnitude of the measured traction force was lower and the migration speed was higher. During cell elongation, traction force increased in the trailing region. This may be related to the cell–extracellular matrix (ECM) interactions to form the elongated cellular shape for forward cell migration. In contrast to non-guided migration, the rates of increasing and decreasing traction force were higher for guided cell migration. The higher rate for traction force to build up during cell elongation along guided pattern was in agreement with the previous study showing that contact guiding introduced a more rapid protrusion of cellular filopodia on groove patterns. Previous work has shown that the disassembly of trailing FAs was due to the tensions from stress fibers, and this may be related to the faster traction force change rate during the release of the trailing region under guided cell migration. Real time monitoring of cell traction force was carried out for cell migration in forward and reversed directions. Dynamic traction force development under guided, directional cell migration was studied for the first time. The results showed that cell–ECM interactions are regulated by topographical guidance that could influence cell migration speed and direction.

11218017.label: Major findings and research outcome
11218017.value: Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) platforms with microtopography, nanotopographies, and nanotopographies in grating arrangements were developed and fabricated to study their effects on cell migration behaviors. The results were related to changes in cell morphologies including filopodium extension and long protrusion outgrowth of MC3T3-E1 cells. Nanostructures were found to promote the extension of filopodia and protrusions, thus enhancing the cell motility compared to flat surface. Both the flat surface and isotropic nanostructures showed low guidance effect for cell migration. Instead, the nanostructures in grating arrangements could provide cell migration guidance and resulted in better migration directionality. More filopodia/cell was observed for the cells on nanoholes and nanopillars in grating arrangements compared to only gratings, corresponding to better cell guidance. Nanotopographies with different depths/heights were also developed to study the effects of physical dimensions of nanotopographies on cell migration. Nanoholes and nanopillars with different depths/heights showed no guidance effect on cell movement but cells moved slower on nanoholes and faster on nanopillars with increasing the depth/height from 250 to 750 nm. Nanopillars in grating arrangements with 750 nm height generated the longest length of filopodia and protrusions of 10.3 and 24.7 µm, respectively, corresponding to a faster migration speed of 0.78 µm/min compared to the lower speed of 0.47 µm/min for the shorter nanopillars of 250 nm. While cells had little elongated morphology on nanoholes, they had elongation of 7 for 750 nm tall nanopillars in grating arrangements. With 750 nm tall nanopillars in grating arrangements, cells had the highest migration directionality, migration speed, and cell elongation.

11218017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11218017.value: Using the microposts to provide real time monitoring of cell traction force will lead to a better understanding of cell migration behaviors influenced by its surrounding microenvironment and guiding patterns that could result in good control of cell migration speed, directionality, and cell growth. In addition, these results are helpful for identifying filopodium formation and protrusion outgrowth on micro− and nano−topographies, as well as their effects on the cell motility. Platforms with combined micro− and nano−topographies will be useful for controlling cell migration, which could lead to cell sorting and screening.

11218017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11218017.value: To realize highly directional guidance for cell migration, both micro− and nano−scale topographies were studied to better understand the complex extracellular matrix environment. Polydimethylsiloxane based platforms with micro− and nano−topographies were developed to systematically study their guidance effects on cell migration behaviors. Compared to flat surface or grating as microtopography, nanotopographies such as nanoholes and nanopillars could promote the generation of filopodia and extension of long protrusions with increased migration speed for MC3T3-E1 cells. To enhance the cell migration directionality, the nanotopographies were patterned in grating arrangements and the results showed that both nanoholes and nanopillars in grating arrangements introduced more directional cell migration compared to gratings. The effects of physical dimensions of nanotopographies on cell migration were studied and the results showed that there were less cell elongation and less directional migration for nanoholes in grating arrangements with increasing depth of nanoholes. Platforms with nanopillars in grating arrangements and large height could be used to control cell migration speed and directionality, which could potentially lead to cell sorting and screening.

11218417.label: Project Objectives
11218417.value: Investigate the liquid transport on the tentacle of natural drain fly. The flexible multiscale and periodical structure of this natural liquid rectifier will be characterized, and the effect of structural topography on the directional droplet propagation process will be experimentally and analytically analyzed. Conduct analytical analysis to reveal the fundamental mechanisms governing the droplet directional transport. We will systematically study the dewetting transition and directional transport of condensate droplets within a single seta as well as the ballistic droplet transport modes spanning over a few knots. The performance of droplet rectifier such as droplet volume and velocity as a function of time and spatial location will also be investigated. Develop biomimetic droplet rectifier for practical application. To demonstrate the generality of the long-range and directional droplet transport, we propose to develop a scaled-up surface consisting of several scaled-up periodical knots with microscale ratchets. We will further design a bio-inspired liquid rectifier that promotes the droplet nucleation, growth and droplet collection. By integrating with the wicking structure recently developed in our lab which allows for the directional liquid spreading for efficient thin film evaporation, we can translate the directional liquid motion into a novel thermal diode. The rectification coefficient will be determined by measuring the effective thermal conductivities in the forward and reverse operating modes.

11300017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11300017.value: 該項目的目的是利用發光過渡金屬全氟芳烴絡合物作為鉗序列（苯丙氨酸-半胱氨酸-脯氨酸-苯丙氨酸）中半胱氨酸單元的新型探針，以開發用於位點專一生物共軛，活細胞成像和光誘導的蛋白質失活的創新試劑。活細胞中蛋白質的特異性標記是一項重要但具有挑戰性的工作。雖然熒光蛋白（FPs）的發展已經對研究蛋白質的表達，運輸和相互作用作出了重大貢獻，但其應用受限於相對較大的分子體積，修飾發色團的困難，及低的光穩定性。最近的一種方法是對有興趣的蛋白質融合遺傳編碼的人造肽，用作標籤引領隨後與化學探針的生物共軛反應。該方法具有FPs標記蛋白質的特異性，但只需要一個短的識別序列和兼容全面的熒光探針。近年來，發光過渡金屬絡合物顯著的發光性能和細胞毒性，推動多功能的生物成像試劑和潛在的抗癌藥物的設計。雖然許多發光金屬絡合物已經顯示了細胞器靶向屬性，仍然不可能專一標記遺傳編碼的肽或蛋白質序列中的天然氨基酸，用於生物成像和蛋白質功能研究。因此，發光金屬絡合物的有利性質包括其強烈和長壽命的發光和可控的細胞毒性不能完全被利用。隨著最近的發現，全氟芳烴衍生物可以對鉗序列（苯丙氨酸-半胱氨酸-脯氨酸-苯丙氨酸）中半胱氨酸進行高度特異性的修飾，我們預期具有前所未有的生物綴合能力的發光過渡金屬絡合物將被開發。在這個項目中，我們將設計新的發光過渡金屬全氟芳烴絡合物作為鉗序列中的半胱氨酸單元的特異性探針。該絡合物的光物理和光化學性質及其對融合鉗序列的肽和蛋白的生物共軛反應性將會被研究。另外，我們將會對絡合物的細胞攝取，細胞毒性和生物成像特性及發色基團輔助激光失活（CALI）蛋白質在水性緩衝液和活細胞的應用進行探索。我們相信將發光過渡金屬絡合物的有利性質和極具吸引力的肽識別能力進行整合，將會發展出具有位點專一生物共軛，生物成像和光誘導失活蛋白質的新型試劑。

11300017.label: Realisation of objectives
11300017.value: Cyclometalated iridium(III) polypyridine complexes appended with a perfluorobiphenyl (PFBP) moiety [Ir(N^C)2(bpy-CH2-OCONH-C2H4-S-C12F9)](PF6) were designed as bioconjugation and bioimaging reagents. Their PFBP-free counterparts [Ir(N^C)2(bpy-CH2-OCONH-C4H9)](PF6) were also prepared. All the complexes were fully characterized and gave satisfactory elemental analysis. Upon photoexcitation, the complexes displayed intense and long-lived greenish-yellow to orange emission, which was assigned to a triplet metal-to-ligand charge transfer (3MLCT) (d(pi)(Ir)->pi*(N^N)) excited state mixed with some triplet intraligand (3IL) (pi->pi*) (N^C) character. The PFBP complexes underwent facile reactions with a series of peptides containing the pi-clamp sequence (Phe-Cys-Pro-Phe) to afford highly emissive bioconjugates, which were purified by reversed-phase HPLC and characterized by MALDI-TOF or ESI-MS. The emission intensities and lifetimes of the bioconjugates were comparable to those of their parent PFBP complexes, indicating that the amino acid sequences did not perturb the electronic structures of the complexes. Most of the PFBP complexes exhibited more efficient cellular uptake and higher cytotoxic activity than their PFBP-free counterparts. Also, laser-scanning confocal microscopy showed that all the complexes stained the mitochondria of live HeLa cells, possibly due to the cationic and lipophilic nature of the complexes. Conjugation of the PFBP complexes to the pi-clamp sequence slightly reduced their cellular uptake due to the polar peptide sequence. Using one of the PFBP complexes as an example, we demonstrated that the conjugation of complexes to organelle-targeting peptides is an effective means to modulate their intracellular localization behavior as well as the photodynamic therapy performance. In a related study, rhenium(I) polypyridine PFBP complexes [Re(N^N)(CO)3(py-C2-PFBP)](CF3SO3) were developed. The crystal structures of the Ph2phen and Me4phen complexes were also obtained. One of the phenyl rings of the Ph2phen ligand was in close proximity to the PFBP moiety, with an interplanar distance of about 3.5 Angstroms, suggesting possible intramolecular pi-pi interactions. All the complexes exhibited green to yellow 3MLCT emission upon excitation. Conjugation of the complexes to peptides containing the pi-clamp sequence was performed and the formation of the conjugates was confirmed by MALDI-TOF or ESI-MS. The photophysical properties of the conjugates were similar to those of the unmodified complexes. Additionally, a conjugate containing a caspase-3 cleavable sequence and a pi-clamp sequence (DEVD-FCPF) was modified with the Ph2phen complex (on the pi-clamp sequence) and an emission quencher QSY-7 (on the N-terminal amine group). Specific enzymatic cleavage of the DEVD sequence led to significant emission turn-on of the complex in both extracellular and intracellular environments. In addition to peptide tags, we utilized iridium(III) nitrone complexes and protein tags (e.g., SNAP-tag protein) to modulate emission and 1O2-photosensitization in live cells. Iridium(III) nitrone complexes [Ir(N^C)2(bpy-nitrone)](PF6) were designed as bioorthogonal phosphorogenic probes for a benzylguanine derivative BCN-BG, which is a substrate for the SNAP-tag protein. Upon reaction in aqueous buffer, the mixtures showed significant emission enhancement and lifetime extension because of the conversion of the quenching nitrone unit into a non-quenching isoxazoline derivative. We reacted BCN-BG with SNAP-tag protein and isolated the conjugate BCN-SNAP. As expected, the complexes also displayed more intense emission upon reaction with the conjugate. CHO-K1 cells were transfected with phage UbiC SNAP-KDEL and pSNAPf that expressed ER-targeting and cytoplasm-enriched SNAP-tag, respectively. Strong emission signal was found only in cells that expressed SNAP-tag at ER and cytoplasm with pretreatment of BCN-BG, confirming that the phosphorogenicity of the complexes. The photocytotoxic activity of the complexes increased significantly after the cells expressed SNAP-tag in the cytoplasm and upon treatment with BCN-BG. These were ascribed to the more enhanced photogeneration of 1O2 when BCN-BG and SNAP-tag were co-present. In a related study involving another protein tag, HaloTag, we designed iridium(III) polypyridine tetrazine complexes [Ir(N^C)2(bpy-tetrazine-Ph)](PF6). Addition of BCN to the complexes resulted in strong emission enhancement and lifetime extension due to the conversion of the tetrazine unit into a non-quenching pyridazine derivative. However, the strained alkene TCO-OH gave much smaller changes, which could be associated with the quenching effect of the dihydropyridazine products. Using BCN-modified substrates and the protein tag HaloTag, both organelle-specific staining and modulated photocytotoxicity were achieved. We designed new bioorthogonal imaging reagents with environment-sensitive emission properties through the modification of sydnone with cyclometalated iridium(III) polypyridine complexes [Ir(N^C)2(bpy-NHCO-C6H4-sydnone)](PF6). These complexes displayed significant emission enhancement and lifetime elongation upon strain-promoted sydnone–alkyne cycloaddition (SPSAC) reaction with strained alkynes, and were utilized to label proteins and ceramide molecules in live cells. The manipulation of the photocytotoxicity of the complexes through the use of a bioorthogonal reagent was also demonstrated. In a related study, we also developed new rhenium(I) polypyridine sydnone complexes [Re(N^N)(CO)3(py-sydnone)](CF3SO3) as phosphorogenic bioorthogonal probes. Upon SPSAC reaction with the strained alkyne BCN, the complexes exhibited emission enhancement. Conjugation of the complexes with BCN-modified bovine serum albumin (BCN-BSA) led to the even more significant emission enhancement and lifetime extension. Due to the non-cytotoxic property and emission enhancement capability of the phen complex, it was utilized to image BCN-morpholine that was localized in the lysosomes. We synthesized luminescent molecular hybrids with eight iridium(III) polypyridine complexes grafted on a polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxane (POSS) unit [POSS-{Ir(N^C)2(py-im)}8](PF6)8. The properties of these iridium(III) POSS complexes were compared with those of their POSS-free counterparts [Ir(N^C)2(py-im)](PF6). Upon photoexcitation, the complexes displayed intense and long-lived orange-red to red emission originated from 3MLCT and/or 3IL excited states. The POSS complexes exhibited negligible dark- and photo-cytotoxicity toward HeLa cells, which is attributable to POSS-induced formation of nanoparticles that prevented interactions with biomacromolecules. In a related study, new neutral iridium(III) POSS complexes [Ir(N^C)2(L1-POSS)] and their POSS-free counterparts [Ir(N^C)2(L1)] and the PEG derivatives [Ir(N^C)2(L1-PEG)] were prepared. The photophysical, photochemical, and biological properties of the complexes were studied. The bsn complexes exhibited the highest 1O2 generation quantum yields. The POSS and POSS-free complexes showed exclusive lipid droplet-staining upon cellular uptake, while the PEG derivatives displayed lysosomal localization. One of complexes was utilized to study various lipid droplet-related events including the lipid droplet accumulation under oleic acid-stimulation, movement of lipid droplets, and preadipocyte differentiation. Luminescent rhenium(I) polypyridine complexes containing a benzo[ghi]perylene (BP) unit [Re(N^N)(CO)3(py-BP)](CF3SO3) and a perylene diimide (PDI) moiety through a disulfide linker [Re(Ph2phen)(CO)3(py-SS-PDI-TEG)](CF3SO3) were synthesized. Upon photoexcitation, the complexes exhibited short-lived greenish-yellow BP-based fluorescence. The PDI complex displayed FRET from the rhenium(I) polypyridine to the perylene moiety, resulting in negligible 3MLCT emission from the inorganic unit and predominant fluorescence from the perylene. The sensitivity of the PDI complex toward glutathione (GSH) was used to visualize intracellular thiols in live cells. In a related study, we developed rhenium(I) polypyridine complexes featuring a 2,4-dinitrophenylsulfonamide (DNPS) unit [Re(N^N)(CO)3(py-DNPS)](CF3SO3) as phosphorogenic bioimaging reagents and photocytotoxic agents. Upon photoexcitation, the DNPS complexes exhibited very weak luminescence as a result of PET from the excited rhenium(I) diimine moiety to the DNPS unit. However, upon treatment with GSH, the DNPS moiety was departed, resulting in emission enhancement. After reaction of the DNPS complexes with GSH in live cells, intense emission and potent photocytotoxicity were both observed. There were no significant difficulties encountered in this project. The largest problem would be the low water solubility of the transition metal complexes due to the highly hydrophobic nature of the perfluorobiphenyl unit. However, despite this limitation, bioconjugation of the pi-clamp sequence with these complexes proceeded smoothly and the conjugated peptides showed greatly enhanced water solubility. In summary, in this project, a number of photoactive transition metal complexes were explored as bioconjugation labels, imaging reagents, and activatable photocytotoxic agents for a range of biological applications.

11300017.label: Major findings and research outcome
11300017.value: In this project, a number of new luminescent iridium(III) and rhenium(I) polypyiridine complexes appended with a perfluorobiphenyl (PFBP) unit were designed and synthesized, and fully characterized with a range of spectroscopic techniques such as 1H, 13C, and 19F NMR, ESI-MS, IR, and elemental analysis. The basic electronic absorption, photophysical, photochemical, and electrochemical properties of the complexes were investigated. Additionally, the water solubility, lipophilicity, cellular uptake properties, and (photo)cytotoxic activity of all the complexes were investigated. Also, the reactivity of the PFBP unit on the ligand toward the cysteine residue of the pi-clamp sequence (FCPF) was investigated. Our results indicated that the reaction was highly selective and the labeled peptide conjugates showed intense and long-lived emission upon excitation, indicating that the metal-ligand moiety did not hamper the reactivity of the PFBP unit, and the PFBP unit did not affect the electronic structure of the luminescent metal-ligand chromophore. Various organelle-targeting and nuclear localizing peptides containing the pi-clamp sequence were modified, and the photophysical properties of the isolated and purified peptides were examined. Although the cellular uptake efficiencies of the modified peptides were lower compared to the free complexes due to higher polarity, the conjugates were still taken up by live cells and retained their luminescence properties. While the modified ER-targeting peptide was localized in the ER as expected, the modified nuclear localizing peptide was trapped in endosomal and lysosomal compartments. The photoinduced 1O2 generation capability of the peptides was also evaluated. Surprisingly, although the cellular uptake of the complex-modified organelle-targeting and nuclear localizing peptides was lower than that of complex-modified pi-clamp sequence, the former peptide conjugates were much more photocytotoxic than the latter one. These results illustrated that the photocytotoxic activity of transition metal complexes is strongly coupled with their intracellular localization and capability of forming reactive oxygen species, which is valuable information in the development of more efficient theranostic reagents. Inspired by these exciting results, we extended the studies to related systems including: 1) transition metal complex-containing specific substrates of protein tags including SNAP-tag and HaloTag as a means to modulate the luminescence responses and photocytotoxic activity of metal complexes; 2) disulfide and dinitrophenylsulfonamide complexes that are sensitive to biothiols such as GSH for controlled photophysical and photochemical behavior; 3) mesoionic sydnone systems that display highly environment-sensitive luminescence properties as phosphorogenic probes and imaging agents; and 4) POSS-containing metal complexes that show negligible dark cytotoxicity but high photocytotoxicity, resulting in attractive photocytotoxicity indexes.

11300017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11300017.value: We have shown in this project that the modification of photofunctional transition metal complexes with a PFBP unit will allow facile and selective conjugation of the pi-clamp sequence (FCPF), and the modified peptide conjugates can be utilized in bioimaging and controlled photocytotoxic applications. The selectivity of the nucleophilic aromatic substitution reaction between perfluoroarene and cysteine sulfhydryl originates from the fact that the phenyl rings of the phenylalanine residues are responsible for the recognition of the perfluoroarene group and activate the cysteine thiol, and the proline orients the residues into the correct conformation. We believe that other selective reactions between cysteine and other organic functionalities (for example, α,β-unsaturated carbonyl) can be identified using a related peptide library approach. The organic functional groups will be incorporated into a range of photofunctional transition metal complexes, and the resultant complexes will be used to modify new peptide sequences. Additionally, a number of peptides are known to exhibit protein binding properties; their conjugates with luminescent transition metal complexes are expected to show promising diagnostic potential. This, together with the efficient singlet oxygen photogeneration properties of many transition metal complexes, is anticipated to lead to the development of new and efficient photosensitizers for photodynamic therapeutic applications.

11300017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11300017.value: This project is about the utilization of luminescent transition metal complexes containing a perfluoroarene unit as molecular probes for the cysteine residue of the pi-clamp peptide sequence (Phe-Cys-Pro-Phe). Although a number of photofunctional transition metal complexes display organelle-targeting properties, it is still impossible to label a natural amino acid in a genetically encodable peptide site-specifically for bioimaging and functional studies. On the basis of the discovery of the pi-clamp sequence, we modified luminescent transition metal complexes with a perfluorobiphenyl unit to enable highly specific cysteine modification in a peptide. The spectroscopic, photophysical, and photochemical properties of the metal complexes were investigated. Additionally, their cellular uptake and (photo)cytotoxic activity were studied. The reactivity of the PFBP unit toward the cysteine residue of the pi-clamp sequence was also examined. Organelle-targeting and nuclear localizing peptides containing the pi-clamp sequence were modified, and the photophysical properties of the isolated peptides were investigated. The conjugates were readily taken up by live cells and retained their interesting luminescence and singlet oxygen-photosensitization properties. The results of this project will further illustrate the application potential of photofunctional transition metal complexes and facilitate the design and development of innovative bioconjugation reagents, biological imaging reagents, and photosensitizers for photodynamic therapy applications.

11300117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11300117.value: Interfacial fluid mixing between two fluids of different densities is a very complicated but extremely important topic in science. The phenomenon of unstable interfacial mixing appears in many natural phenomena and industrial applications, such as supernovas, inertial confinement fusion, enhanced oil recovery process, ground water contamination, etc. To understand the dynamics of unstable mixing interfaces and to provide theoretical predictions of their behavior is an important and extremely difficult task. Small disturbances at the initial interface grow in size and develop into complicated nonlinear structures at unstable interfaces. These nonlinear structures cause great dif- ficulties in experimental design, in numerical simulation and in theoretical analysis. A well-known unstable interfacial mixing problem is the Richtmyer-Meshkov (RM) insta- bility. This instability occurs when a shock hits a perturbed material interface between two fluids of different densities. Unstable fingers develop at the material interface. Un- derstanding the behavior of fingers at the RM interfaces is a classical and very difficult task in mathematics and engineering. Numerical simulations and experiments have been performed in various settings and in different dimensions. These simulations are quite time-consuming. The sophistication and difficulties in numerical algorithms increase dra- matically when we consider an unstable interface in three-dimensional space. Relative to two-dimensional simulations, it takes orders of magnitude longer in time to perform simulations in three dimensions. The purpose of this study is to establish scaling laws between the dominant behavior of RM instability in two-dimensional systems and that in three-dimensional systems. Once achieved, it will allow us to use data from RM unstable fingers in two dimensions to predict the dominant behavior of fingers in three dimensions. RM unstable system involves many physical quantities, such as fluid density, compressibility, incident shock strength, etc. The scaling laws between two-dimensional and three-dimensional systems that we are searching for are valid not only between two- dimensional and three-dimensional systems with the same physical parameters, but also between two-dimensional and three-dimensional systems with different parameters. At the completion of this project, it will provide an extremely useful theoretical tool for predicting the dominant behavior of the RM instability in three dimensions from the results in two-dimensional systems. 兩種不同密度的流體之間的界面混合是科學上一個非常複雜但十分重要的科學課題。不穩定的界面混合現像出現在許多自然現象和工業應用中，如超新星，慣性約束聚變，強化採油，地下水污染等。了解不穩定混合界面的動力學，並提供其行為的理論預測是一項既重要又極其困難的任務。不穩定的界面上的初始小擾動會發展成複雜的非線性結構。這些非線性結構給實驗設計，數值模擬和理論分析中都造成了很大的困難。Richtmyer-Meshkov（RM）不穩定界面是一個工程中經典的不穩定界面混合問題。當衝擊波撞擊带有擾動的兩種不同密度的流體界面時，會發生這種不穩定性。 了解RM不穩定界面的行為是數學和工程中一個困難的課題。对各種參數和在不同的維度上進行了數值模擬和實驗是相當耗時的。當我們研究三維空間中的不穩定界面時，數值算法的複雜性和難度顯著增加。相對於二維模擬，三維模擬所需時間至少要多一個數量級。本研究課題的目的是在二維繫統中的RM不穩定性與三維繫統中的RM不穩定性的主要行為之間建立規律。它將允許我們用二維繫統中的RM不穩定性數據的來預測三維繫統中的主要行為。 RM不穩定係統涉及許多物理量，例如流體密度，可壓縮性，入射衝擊波強度等。我們不僅要尋找在相同物理參數下二維和三維繫統之間的關係，而且要尋找在不同參數下二維和三維繫統之間的關係。本項目完成後，將為三維繫統RM不穩定性的主導行為的預測提供一個非常有用的理論工具。

11300117.label: Realisation of objectives
11300117.value: The study of fingers at gravity-induced or shock-induced unstable interfaces, known as Rayleigh– Taylor instability and Richtmyer–Meshkov instability respectively, is extremely important. Rayleigh–Taylor instability refers to a gravity driven interfacial instability between two fluids of different densities, and Richtmyer–Meshkov instability refers to a shock wave driven interfacial instability between two fluids of different densities. How to predict the growth rates of fingers at unstable interface has been very difficult topic for interfacial mixing problem. There are two types of fingers: spike and bubbles. A spike is a portion of the heavy fluid penetrating light fluid and a bubble is a portion of light fluid penetrating heavy fluid. It is well known that many factors can affect the growth rates of fingers in the Rayleigh–Taylor and Richtmyer– Meshkov instabilities: density ratio of the fluids in difference phases, finger type (spike or bubble) and the dimension of systems (in two dimensions or in three dimensions). Therefore, conducting systematic investigations for Rayleigh–Taylor and Richtmyer–Meshkov instabilities in different sets of physical parameters is very challenging and time-consuming. This is especially true for fingers in three dimensions. In this project we have discovered a surprising universality property: once the time and the growth rate are properly scaled, the behavior of all fingers in different systems follow a universal relation. This surprising scaling law is applicable not only among spikes, among bubbles, between spikes and bubbles in two dimensions, but also among fingers in systems with different parameters and even among fingers in different dimensions. This universal scaling relation allows using data for fingers in two dimensions to predict the dominant behavior of fingers in three dimensions. Both numerical results and experimental data in the literature confirm this universality property. We analyze the dynamic behavior of fingers in different systems. We examine how the density ratio, finger type and the dimensionality can affect the behavior of fingers. From the analysis, we determine the appropriate scalings for time and growth rate and consequently derive the scaling laws among fingers with different parameters, different types and even in different dimensions.

11300117.label: Major findings and research outcome
11300117.value: In this project, we have derived analytic expressions for the growth rate and for the dynamic equation of fingers at Rayleigh-Taylor or Richtmyer-Meshkov unstable interface, which are applicable to arbitrary Atwood numbers and to both two dimensions and three dimensions. These expressions reveal an intrinsic universality property: after proper scaling, the dynamics of fingers in any system approximately exhibit the same behavior. Such a property holds not only between different finger types and between systems with different density ratios, but even between systems in different dimensions. This universality property suggests that, through the derived scaling laws, the data for two-dimensional fingers can be used to predict the dominant behavior of three-dimensional fingers.

11300117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11300117.value: The universality property and the scaling laws derived in this is project are very useful. We have analyzed all data available in the literature and showed that data from numerical simulations are in excellent agreement with the predictions of our scaling law. However, there are much less data available in three dimensions than the data in two dimensions in the literature. This is due to the fact that it is extremely difficult and time-consuming to carry out numerical study of Rayleigh–Taylor instability and Richtmyer–Meshkov instability in three dimensions. Therefore, it is desirable to conduct more numerical simulations for fingers in three dimensions and to further demonstrate the usefulness our newly discovered scaling laws.

11300117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11300117.value: It is well known that the behavior of unstable fingers is very sensitive to parameters. Furthermore, fingers in three dimensions are very different from those in two dimensions. Therefore for each set of parameters one has to conduct a separate numerical simulation or experiment to reveal the behavior of fingers in that particular parameter setting. In this project we have developed a surprising relation among fingers with different parameters, of different type and even in different dimensions. This scaling law allows us just to conduct one simulation in two dimensions and use the result to predict the behavior of fingers with any parameters, for both spikes and bubbles and even in different dimensions. This represents an extremely important advance in the study of unstable interfacial mixing problem.

11300317.label: Major findings and research outcome
11300317.value: I was requested by CityU to submit this Completion Report now, because I need to be on an extended Leave starting in September 2021 (I had to apply for this extended Leave for compelling personal reasons). This explain why Objective 3 is only 50% achieved (otherwise it would have been most likely 100% achieved before the end of 2021). Our major findings are the following: First, we have been able to fully justify two-dimensional models for shells subjected to a confinement condition for the three categories of linearly elastic shells: flexural shells (Objective 1: A ms. together with my former PhD student P. Persanti is ready and will now be submitted for publication), membrane shells (Objective 2: two publications), and generalized membrane shells (Objective 3: 50% achieved; a ms. is in preparation, using techniques similar to those that we used for membrane shells). Second, we have been able to define a two-dimensional Koiter's model for shells subjected to a confinement condition that can accomodate all the three types of shells (Objective 4). For this reason, our proposed model should definitely be used in actual computations. Finally, we came to the conclusion, after an extensive bibliographical research (accounting for the 10% measure of achievement), that achieving Objective 5 is out of reach: the only available results in this direction, by G. Lebeau and M. Schatzman, are very deep, but of very limited practical applicability to more realistic problems. Our conclusion is that it is hopeless to model time-dependent problems for shells (or even for plates) subjected to a confinement condition by hyperbolic variational inequalities. In other words, the classical modeling itself is inadequate.

11300317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11300317.value: To investigate, from a mechanical point of view, what could be a realistic model for time-dependent elastic structures subjected to a confinement condition.

11300317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11300317.value: Usually an elastic structure is not attached to another supporting structure, but is instead subjected to a specific confinement condition, in the sense that it cannot "cross" the boundary of a supporting structure. This research project aims at identifying and justifying (from a mathematical point of view) several mathematical models that can be successfully used in the numerical simulation of such elastic structures.

With the collaboration with Professor Guochun Wu, we established the optimal decay rate for weak solutions with discontinuous data for the compressible fluid models, which include the isentropic Hookean compressible viscoelastic fluids. 2. As the single author, I considered the Hausdorff dimension of concentration of the kinetic energy with the help of parabolic Hausdorff measure for compressible fluid models, which also include isentropic Hookean compressible viscoelastic fluid when the adiabatic constant is between 1 and one half of the spatial dimensions.

11300417.value: 1. We applied the high-low frequency decomposition to obtain the optimal decay rate for weak solutions with discontinuous initial data for compressible fluid flows, which include isentropic compressible Hookean viscoelasticity. The work has been published in Hu, Xianpeng (PRC-CHK); Wu, Guochun (PRC-HUAQ-SM) Optimal decay rates of isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes equations with discontinuous initial data. (English summary) J. Differential Equations 269 (2020), no. 10, 8132–8172. 2. We applied the vector-field method to establish the global wellposedness for compressible viscoelasticity with zero shear viscosity and small data as the shear viscosity vanishes. The interaction among waves with different speeds had been analysed throughly. The publication information is stated as follows: Hu, Xianpeng (PRC-CHK); Zhao, Wenbin (PRC-CHK) Global existence of compressible dissipative elastodynamics systems with zero shear viscosity in two dimensions. (English summary) Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal. 235 (2020), no. 2, 1177–1243. 3. We studied in details about the Hausdorff dimension of concentration of kinetic energy associated with the compressible fluid flows as the adiabatic constant is less than one half of the spatial dimension. The results apply to the isentropic compressible viscoelasticity. 11300417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11300417.value: There are basically two potential aspects for further development of the research and the proposed course of action. They are: 1. The limit of Hausdorff dimension of the concentration set for compressible fluid flows with low Mach number for Cauchy problems. Moreover if the boundary appears, this limit behaviour will be more interesting. 2. For weak solutions of the viscoelasticity, both the entropy and the temperature could be also taken into consideration. The techniques developed in this project would be crucial in these new settings.

11300517.value: 有限元拋物方程的Lp正則性分析及應用

11300517.label: Project Objectives
11300517.value: We shall study fully discrete FEMs for a general linear parabolic equation, in which classical finite element methods are used in spatial direction and finite difference approximations are used in time direction. We will establish the maximal $L^p$-regularity for problems with time-dependent Lipschitz continuous coefficients in possibly nonsmooth domains. Then optimal $L^p$ error estimates of finite element solutions for the general linear models follow immediately. Extension to some other discretizations in temporal and spatial directions will also be studied. The $L^p$ analysis for nonlinear parabolic FE system is more challenging. In this project, we shall study commonly-used linearized schemes for a typical nonlinear parabolic equation. In the linearized schemes, one only solves a linear parabolic equation at each time step by finite element methods. The maximal $L^p$ regularity estimates for linear models may be applied for analyzing the linearized error equations with a perturbation technique and a duality argument to establish optimal $L^p$ error estimates. Finally, we apply the above framework for several nonlinear physical problems, such as incompressible flow in porous media and the equation of gradient flow. The former is governed by a nonlinear parabolic concentration equation coupled with a nonlinear elliptic pressure equation, which has wide applications in oil and ground water industries. The diffusion-dispersion tensor involved in these applications is only Lipschitz continuous. On the other hand, the equation of gradient flow is a diffusion type equation in which the diffusion coefficient is gradient-dependent. Thus this equation can be viewed as a strongly or possibly degenerate nonlinear parabolic equation. It is noted that numerical analysis for these two cases is incomplete. We believe that the maximal $L^p$ regularity analysis may provide a new tool in studying finite element solution of nonlinear problems. In addition, a systematic numerical simulation will be provided to confirm our theoretical analysis and to study new effective schemes.

11300517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11300517.value: The maximal Lp regularity analysis is an important tool in analysis of parabolic PDEs, particularly for nonlinear problems. The analysis on the discrete settings, such as finite element parabolic system, is incomplete and limited to simple linear problems, although the $L^p$ approach has shown its potential and advantage over the traditional $L2$ analysis in dealing with strongly nonlinear equations. In this project, we shall establish a solid framework of the maximal $L^p$ regularity of fully-discrete finite element solutions of general linear parabolic PDEs and then, apply it for several nonlinear physical equations. We believe that the discrete $L^p$ regularity analysis may provide a new tool in studying finite element solutions of strongly nonlinear parabolic PDEs. Lp正則性分析是拋物型偏微分方程研究的重要工具，特別是在非線性問題的研究。然而，對於離散系統，例如有限元拋物方程，這樣的正則性分析是不完整的而且僅限於線性問題的研究。在該項研究計劃中，我們首先研究關於一般線性系統的全離散有限元解的Lp正則性，然後將其推廣之若干非線性物理方程。我們相信離散Lp正則性分析將為強非線性拋物型偏微分方程有限元解的研究提供新的工具。

11300517.label: Realisation of objectives
11300517.value: In this project, we finished the following papers related to the objectives. We did an analysis of fully discrete FEM for miscible displacement in porous media with Bear–Scheidegger diffusion tensor. Fully discrete Galerkin finite element methods are studied for the equations of miscible displacement in porous media with the commonly-used Bear–Scheidegger diffusion– dispersion tensor. In terms of the maximal Lp-regularity of fully discrete finite element solutions of parabolic equations, optimal error estimate and almost optimal error estimate in norm are established under the assumption of D(u) being Lipschitz continuous with respect to u. We analysze of linearized Galerkin FEMs for a mixed formulation of the time-dependent Ginzburg–Landau equations under the temporal gauge. We provide optimal error estimates in L2-norm for the order parameter ψh and the magnetic field σh unconditionally, although the accuracy of the numerical magnetic potential Ah is one order lower than the optimal one due to the degeneracy of the magnetic potential equation. Since the states of superconductors are determined by the order parameter ψh (or the density of the superconducting electron pairs |ψh|), the accuracy of ψh is more important for the vortex simulation in superconditors. Our analysis is based on a nonclassical Ritz projection, which may reduce the pollution of inaccuracy of the numerical magnetic potential in analysis. Numerical experiments confirm our theoretical analysis. We study numerical solutions of time-fractional nonlinear parabolic problems by a class of L1-Galerkin finite element methods. The analysis of L1 methods for time-fractional nonlinear problems is limited mainly due to the lack of a fundamental Gronwall type inequality. In this paper, we establish such a fundamental inequality for the L1 approximation to the Caputo fractional derivative. In terms of the Gronwall type inequality, we provide optimal error estimates of several fully discrete linearized Galerkin finite element methods for nonlinear problems. The theoretical results are illustrated by applying our proposed methods to the time-fractional nonlinear Huxley equation and time-fractional Fisher equation. We also study numerical solutions of time-fractional parabolic equations. Due to the Caputo time derivative being involved, the solutions of equations are usually singular near the initial time t = 0 even for a smooth setting. Based on a simple change of variable s = tβ, an equivalent s-fractional differential equation is derived and analyzed. Two type finite difference methods based on linear and quadratic approximations in the s-direction are presented, respectively, for solving the s-fractional differential equation. We show that the method based on the linear approximation provides the optimal accuracy O(N−(2−α)) where N is the number of grid points in temporal direction. Numerical examples for both linear and nonlinear fractional equations are presented in comparison with L1 methods on uniform meshes and graded meshes, respectively. Our numerical results show clearly the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed methods. We also study a linearized backward Euler Galerkin-mixed finite element method for the time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau (TDGL) equations under the Lorentz gauge. By introducing the induced magnetic field σ = curl A as a new variable, the Galerkin-mixed FE scheme offers many advantages over conventional Lagrange type Galerkin FEMs. An optimal error estimate for the linearized Galerkin-mixed FE scheme is established unconditionally. Analysis is given under more general assumptions for the regularity of the solution of the TDGL equations, which includes the problem in two-dimensional nonconvex polygons and certain three-dimensional polyhedrons, while the conventional Galerkin FEMs may not converge to a true solution in these cases. Numerical examples in both two and three-dimensional spaces are presented to confirm our theoretical analysis. We also study adaptive first-order system least-squares finite element methods (LSFEMs) for second-order elliptic partial differential equations in nondivergence form. Unlike the classical finite element methods which use weak formulations of PDEs that are not applicable for the nondivergence equation, the first-order least-squares formulations naturally have stable weak forms without using integration by parts, allow simple finite element approximation spaces, and have built- in a posteriori error estimators for adaptive mesh refinements. The nondivergence equation is first written as a system of first-order equations by introducing the gradient as a new variable. Then, two versions of least-squares finite element methods using simple C0 finite elements are developed in the paper. One is the L2-LSFEM which uses linear elements, and the other is the W-LSFEM with a mesh-dependent weight to ensure the optimal convergence. Under the assumption that the PDE has a unique solution, a priori and a posteriori error estimates are presented. With an extra assumption on the operator regularity, convergence in standard norms for the W-LSFEM is also discussed. L2-error estimates are derived for both formulations. Extensive numerical experiments for continuous, discontinuous, and even degenerate coefficients on smooth and singular solutions are performed to test the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed methods.

11300717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11300717.value: 近年來，智能手機，AR / VR設備，可穿戴設備等現代信息技術的發展，極大地改變了人們的日常生活。智能手機為社交活動，電子購物，娛樂，新聞等提供標準平台; AR / VR設備為互動和娛樂提供了一個新的和令人興奮的體驗;可穿戴數字設備為個人健康和體育活動提供個人數據採集和分析。簡而言之，我們處於信息化的新時代。所有這些信息技術的背後是海量數據的生成，存儲，處理，傳輸，分析和應用。 “數據”不可避免地成為每個人生活的關鍵因素。如何有效地利用數據在公司，政府，國家乃至整個世界的許多方面起著至關重要的作用。 當今收集的數據通常是高維度，大規模的，複雜的。從這樣的信息提取和應用數據集中的智能學習已經成為當今科學研究的熱點之一。眾所周知，儘管數據是高維度，大規模的，並且具有很大的複雜性，但是它們基本上嵌入在某些流型中，或者可以被表示為圖，其在結構上是低維度和稀疏的，可以被多尺度表示系統如小波，小框架等刻畫。對偶框架小波是多尺度表示系統中最重要的類型之一，因為它們在設計上的多樣性和應用中的高度靈活性。 在這個項目中，我們將重點關注緊的黎曼流形和圖（或網絡）上的對偶框架小波的刻畫和構造，以及它們在多尺度數據分析中的應用。我們將著重於調查對偶框架小波序列，研究其MRA結構和濾波器組連接，提供在流型上構建對偶框架小波的實例，例如球形，圓環面，Grassmannian等以及圖上如社交網絡，神經網絡等相關的機器學習的圖，我們還將在實踐中對流形和圖的快速對偶框架小波變換及其應用進行研究。我們的項目的結果不僅將提供多尺度表徵系統在包括流型和圖在內的一般領域的理論刻畫，而且還為多尺度數據分析提供了快速有效的實用有用的變換算法。

11300717.label: Realisation of objectives
11300717.value: Objectives as per Section 5.1 above. Objective 1: Characterization and Construction of Dual Framelets on Manifolds and Graphs. To achieve this objective, the PI first investigated the n-dimensional quincunx refinable functions. The PI generalized the family of Deslauriers–Dubuc’s interpolatory masks from dimension one to arbitrary dimensions with respect to the quincunx dilation matrices, thereby providing a family of quincunx fundamental refinable functions in arbitrary dimensions. We show that a family of unique quincunx interpolatory masks exists and such a family of masks is of real value and has the full-axis symmetry property. Then, the PI and his collaborators investigated compactly supported tight framelets with tensor product structure, which are of great interest and importance in both theory and application. The PI and his collaborator worked on how to construct directional compactly supported tensor product complex tight framelets having varied directionality and good performance for applications in image processing. Finally, the PI investigated framelets on a smooth and compact Riemannian manifold and on a graph. The PI and his collaborators gave the construction, characterizations, and applications of framelets on such a manifold and a graph. All these investiations are important for the development of our Objective 2 (see below). In summary, the Objective 1 has been achieved completely. For major findings and research outcome, we refer to Section 6.1 of this report. Objective 2: Applications of Dual Framelets on Manifolds and Graphs. Together with the findings and developments in Objective 1, for this objective, we have several sucessful applications. First, for applications in image denoising and inpainting, Our numerical experiments show that our constructed directional compactly supported tensor product complex tight framelets have good performance for applications such as image denoising and inpainting compared with several other state-of-the-art transform-based methods. Second, for manifold data processing, e.g., on the 2-sphere, we provided explicit construction of framelets on the sphere and our numerical examples showed that such framelets can be used to sparsely represent signal on the sphere with the multiresolution manner. Last but not least, for graph data processing, decimated framelets on the graph are constructed and used for the graph data representation. In summary, the Objective 2 has been achieved completely. For major findings and research outcome, we refer to Section 6.1 of this report.

11300717.label: Major findings and research outcome
11300717.value: We generalize the family of Deslauriers–Dubuc’s interpolatory masks from dimension one to arbitrary dimensions with respect to the quincunx dilation matrices, thereby providing a family of quincunx fundamental refinable functions in arbitrary dimensions. We show that a family of unique quincunx interpolatory masks exists and such a family of masks is of real value and has the full-axis symmetry property. We give the explicit form of such unique quincunx interpolatory masks in dimension 2. See Part C, the paper in Axioms 2017, 6, 20. We provide a comprehensive review of latest soft computing tools and examples incorporating a series of machine learning models. The prediction performances of different models are evaluated and compared. The effects of the training sample size and stock patterns (viz. momentum and mean reversion) on model prediction are also investigated. Results indicate that artificial neural network (ANN)-based models yield the highest prediction accuracy. See Part C, the paper in Axioms 2019, 8, 116. We construct directional compactly supported tensor product complex tight framelets having varied directionality and good performance for applications in image processing. Our construction algorithms employ optimization techniques and put extensive emphasis on frequency response and spatial localization of their underlying one-dimensional tight framelet filter banks. Our numerical experiments show that our framelets have good performance for applications such as image denoising and inpainting compared with several other state-of-the-art transform-based methods. See Part C, the paper in SIAM J. Imaging Sciences, 2019, vol 12 (4):1739-1771. We provide the construction, characterizations, and applications of tight framelets on a compact smooth Riemannian manifold. Characterizations of the tightness of a sequence of framelet systems in both the continuous and semi-discrete settings are provided. Tight framelets associated with framelet filter banks can then be easily designed. Explicit construction of tight framelets on the sphere as well as numerical examples are given. See Part C, the paper in Applied and Computational Harmonic Analysis, 2020, vol 48: 64-95. We provide the construction and applications of decimated tight framelets on graphs. Based on graph clustering algorithms, a coarse-grained chain of graphs can be constructed where a suitable orthonormal eigenpair can be deduced. Moreover, such tight framelets are associated with filter banks with which fast framelet transform algorithms can be realized. An explicit toy example of decimated tight framelets on a graph is provided. See Part C, the paper in Proc. SPIE 11138, 2019.

11300717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11300717.value: Graph signal processing and graph neural networks (GNNs) gain more and more attentions in recent year. As demonstrated on the paper (see Part C, paper in SPIE 2019), decimated framelets can be built on a (undirected) graph for graph signal representation. A further development would be to investigate graph neural networks based on our framelet representations on graphs.

11300717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11300717.value: In recent years, there has been a great interest in developing wavelet-like representation systems for data defined on non-Euclidean domains, including manifolds and graphs. One of the motivations is from the interdisciplinary area of machine learning, where data concerned are massive and typically from social networks, biology, physics, finance, etc., which can be naturally organized as graphs or graph data. Such ‘Big Data’ can be regarded as random samples from some smooth manifold, where its ‘graph Laplacian’ is connected to the ‘manifold Laplacian’ encoding the essential information of the data to be exploited by various machine/deep learning approaches. In this research project, we focus on the characterization and construction of dual framelets on manifolds and graphs. We investigate in theory and applications of framelets on manifolds and graphs. Fast framelet transforms (FMTs) on manifolds are designed and implemented. Explicit constructions of framelets on the 2-sphere as well as numerical examples are provided. We also build decimated framelets on graph for graph signal representation and processing. Our results and fundings in this projects enriches in theory and applications of multiscale representations for signal processing in general domains.
