11300917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11300917.value: This proposal aims to better understand the fundamental molecular principles of electron transfer processes under gas-phase conditions without influence from solvent molecules for molecular peptide radical cations containing tyrosine residue, a common amino acid involved in many redox chemistry in biological systems. Because of its low ionization energy, one-electron oxidation at the aromatic phenol side chain of tyrosine is commonplace, forming phenolic radical cation intermediates during the redox reactions. These intermediates can convert to a variety of radical tautomers through rearrangements of the charge, spin and hydrogen atoms among different sites on the peptide backbone and residues’ side chains. With the recent advances in the generation of molecular peptide radical cations with well-defined initial radical sites in the gas phase using mass spectrometric techniques, many peptide radical tautomers have been experimentally identified based on their unique dissociation channels, and theoretically supported by quantum chemical molecular modeling. New discovery of more unprecedented reactions is certain to reveal intriguing insights into the chemical processes on the peptide chain. For example, a novel neutral radical loss from the N-terminal residue of tyrosine-containing molecular peptide radical cations have been discovered, which is hypothetically attributed to existence of some radical characters at the N-terminal amino group delocalized from the originally oxidized tyrosine side chain. This process probably involves a through-space interaction between the N-terminal amino group and the tyrosine side chain, supported by our preliminary experimental and theoretical studies. We plan to detail investigate the plausible factors that may govern this intriguing electron delocalization, including the sequence position of the tyrosine residue, the through-sequence and through-space proximities to the N-terminal amino group and the tyrosine residue and their electron-donating/withdrawing power. These factors will be testified systematically with peptide models containing different constituent amino-acid residues in various sequence orders using collision-induced dissociation, isotope-labelling and chemical-derivatization experiments. The dissociation mechanisms, thermodynamics and kinetics will be examined quantum chemically using density functional theory and modelled using Rice–Ramsperger–Kassel–Marcus theory.

11300917.label: Realisation of objectives
11300917.value: The collision-induced dissociation (CID) patterns of a series of well-designed molecular peptide radical cations [M]•+ with varied lengths from two to six amino acid residues in the gas phase have been investigated with mass spectrometric (MS) experiments in collaboration with The University of Hong Kong. All our studied [M]•+ contained a phenylalanine residue (Phe) at the N-terminus and a tyrosine residue (Tyr) in varied positions along the peptide chain, creating different proximal environments about the Tyr center. They were generated via the efficient one-electron dissociative transfer of corresponding ternary [Cu(II)(L)M]2+ parent complex (see Part C: no. 1, 2, 6-9). We discovered an interesting, uncommon side-chain dissociation of the N-terminal Phe, losing the benzylic radical (91Da). This novel 91Da loss from CID of [M]•+, confirmed with isotopic labeling experiments, was formed via the side-chain Cα-Cβ bond cleavage at the N-terminal Phe. MS experiments had confirmed that the efficiency of this unusual dissociation channel was decreasing with Tyr placed gradually away from the N-terminus of the peptides. Our quantum chemical analyses using density functional theories for a model dipeptide system [FY]•+ suggested that this observed side-chain cleavage of the N-terminal Phe required intermediate peptide conformers with non-bonding-π (n-π) interaction between the N-terminal amino group and the aromatic phenol ring of the side chain of Tyr. This specific interaction resulted in a through-space electron transfer from the N-terminal NH2 group to Tyr. The radical character at the resulting –NH2•+ moiety then induced β-scission at the side chain Cα-Cβ bond of Phe (see Part C: no. 1). Additional theoretical analyses, by means of density functional tight binding molecular dynamics (DFTB-MD) simulations with the dynamics structures further refined by geometry optimizations using DFT at the M06-2X level, for model tetrapeptide systems [FYGG]•+, [FGYG]•+ and [FGGY]•+ discovered that the experimentally observed 91Da loss was strongly dependent on the conformational spaces in which a reactive conformer having characteristic electronic structures was the key prerequisite, confirming the formation of n-π interaction (named as n→π+ interaction) as a preclude for the side-chain Cα–Cβ bond cleavage at the N-terminal Phe. The relative energies of such pre-requisite reactive conformers and the transition structures with respect to the lowest-energy canonical π-centered radical conformer were increasing for [M]•+ with the increasing sequence distance between Tyr and the N-terminus. The spin density was gradually transferred from the original location at Tyr side chain to the N-terminal NH2 group, then further to the dissociating side-chain of the N-terminal Phe, signifying the through-space electron transfer process, which was also ratified spectroscopically using infrared multiphoton dissociation (IRMPD) action spectroscopy in collaboration with the Free Electron Laser for Infrared eXperiments (FELIX) facility at the Radboud University, Nijmegen, The Netherlands (see Part C: no. 7-9). In combination of the theoretical and experimental methods, five representative Tyr-containing peptide molecular radical cations [FYGG]•+ conformers namely [FYo•GG]+, [FYπ•GG]+, [Fα•YGG]+, [FYβ•GG]+ and [FNY•GG]+, in which the electron-donating/withdrawing abilities of Tyr side chain were intrinsically modified due to the different tautomerizations, were identified and they were all energetically competitive. Theoretical IR spectra of [FYo•GG]+, [FYπ•GG]+ and [FNY•GG]+ were found in good agreement with the experimental IRMPD spectrum, suggesting that they were coexisting in equilibrium in the gas phase. Among these radical conformers, the higher-lying reactive conformer [FNY•GG]+ was characterized, featuring an interesting n→π+ interaction with the unpaired electron delocalized between the N-terminal NH2 and the Tyr side chain. DFT studies showed that this reactive conformer facilitated the N-terminal Phe dissociation via the dissociative electron transfer mechanism. However, similar dissociation from other conformers such as [FYo•GG]+ and [FYπ•GG]+ were kinetically impeded. Interestingly, the potential energy surface of the dissociation channel via the critical conformer was found to be consistently increased when Tyr was shifted from the N-terminal side to the C-terminal side (e.g. [FYGG]•+, [FGYG]•+ and [FGGY]•+ for the tetrapeptide series). These findings suggested that increasing the distance between NH2 and Tyr could weaken the n→π+ interaction and further impaired the dissociative electron transfer. The importance on the non-bonding electrons at the N-terminal Phe for its side-chain cleavage was also confirmed by modifying the electron properties of the NH2 group through methylations. The dissociation efficiency was indeed increased for [M]•+ with more electron rich –NHCH3 or – N(CH3)2 group. By contrast, acetylation for the N-terminal NH2 reduced the dissociation efficiency (see Part C: no. 1, 9). Our theoretical investigations had demonstrated that the formation of non-covalent interaction in peptide could give rise to specific dissociation channel which eventually served as an indicator to predict the peptide folding configuration in gas phase. With our experimental methods for the generation of M•+, we expected that similar radical cations, other than Tyr and Phe, could be generated from Cu complexes with other aromatic amino acids, such as histidine (His) and tryptophan (Trp). Through experimental attempts in collaboration with The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, we had surprisingly discovered that a self-assembled binuclear Cu(II)-His complex could be formed. More importantly, this novel binuclear complex could be applied as an analytical technique for rapid differentiation of the absolute configuration and determination of enantiomeric excess of chiral compounds (see Part C: no. 4). We had also attempted to obtain ultraviolent photodissociation (UVPD) information with the UV action spectroscopic facility at University of Innsbruck, Austria, aiming to determine the electronic characteristics of our selected M•+ (Part C: no. 3, 5).

11300917.label: Major findings and research outcome
11300917.value: One-electron oxidized peptide/protein could induce multitudes of peptide backbone or side-chain cleavages, forming a large variety of peptide fragments. Of particular interest was the unprecedented N-terminal Phe Cα-Cβ bond cleavage in electron deficient tyrosine-containing peptide radical cation, which could be efficiently generated by dissociative electron transfers of ternary [Cu(II)(L)M]2+ parent complex (Part C: no. 1, 2, 6-9). Theoretical calculations and spectroscopic investigations suggested that the dissociation channel was triggered by a higher-lying reactive conformers [FNY•GG]+ in which the unpaired electron was delocalized between the N-terminal NH2 and the Tyr side chain forming a unique n→π+ interaction (Part C: no. 1,9). This non-covalent interaction can be characterized by the unique NH2 scissor mode at 1577 cm-1 in both theoretical and experimental IR spectra. Reaction mechanism studies showed that this reactive conformer would facilitate the N-terminal Phe Cα-Cβ bond dissociation via the dissociative electron transfer where the non-bonded electron hopped from the NH2 to the Tyr electron hole and further induced the N-terminal Phe Cα-Cβ bond cleavage. The dissociative electron transfer were found to be in consistent with electron-hopping model where increasing the distance between NH2 and Tyrosine residue would impair the N-terminal Phe Cα-Cβ bond dissociation due to the unfavorable long-range electron transfer. Ultimately, the Phe side-chain loss could serve as an indicator to predict the distance between the N-terminal amino group and Tyr, which provided valuable insights into peptide folding. The copper-complexes used could also be applied to chiral differentiation of other biological compounds or drug molecules (Part C: no. 4).

11300917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11300917.value: This work had provided further research insights into peptide folding studies at longer peptide systems to understand the 3D structures of peptide folding in the gas phase. Dissociation of the N-terminal Phe induced by the dissociative electron transfer could serve as an indicator to predict the non-covalent interaction distance between the N-terminal amino group and Tyr. We had demonstrated that the dissociation of N-terminal Phe exhibited a distance dependence; the increasing distance between the N-terminal amino group and the tyrosine residue resulted in the decreasing dissociation efficiency of Phe as observed in both theoretical and experimental studies due to the weakening of the n→π+ interaction and further resulted in higher barriers for the N-terminal Phe Cα-Cβ bond cleavage. However, one may imagine such interaction between the N-terminal amino group and the Tyr electron hole could be approachable / turned on with longer peptides such as decapeptide where the peptide backbone would become very flexible to achieve end-to-end peptide folding. Hence, further studies on the N-terminal Phe Cα-Cβ bond cleavage at longer peptide chains could further provide valuable information on the 3D peptide (or even big proteins) folding information in the gas phase.

11300917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11300917.value: Oxidative damage to protein by free radical and oxidant induces a wide range of human disorders such as, neurodegenerative diseases, ischemia, stroke, aging and diabetes. In general, the reactions of free radicals in proteins produce different kinds of radical species in biological systems. It has been proposed that the protein/peptide fragmentations proceed either at the backbone or the side chain of amino acid residues. Hence, better understanding the redox chemistry of radical proteins is of fundamental importance for deciphering the oxidative damage mechanisms on proteins. In this work, the dissociative electron transfer inducing the unusual N-terminal phenylalanine residue side-chain cleavage had been investigated theoretically by means of quantum chemical calculations and experimentally using mass spectrometric techniques. Both methods demonstrated that the unprecedented side-chain cleavage triggered by the dissociative electron transfer could be used to predict the folding geometry between the N-terminal amino group and the tyrosine residue along a peptide. Eventually, this indicator can be used to harvest information for 3D structures of peptide folding in the gas phase.

11301417.label: Major findings and research outcome
11301417.value: This project started out along two fronts. We studied the impact of urbanization on rainfall associated with tropical cyclones (TCs) on both a climatological basis as well as using some case studies. For the observational study, we examined the rainfall distribution associated with landfalling tropical cyclones (TCs) along the South China coast using radar data from the Hong Kong Observatory. We found that the time evolution of the rainfall distribution can be different for TCs making landfall from different directions. The relative importance of the impact of land properties and vertical wind shear on these rainfall distributions is investigated using a numerical model. The primary factor in controlling the distributions appear to be in the orientations of the vertical wind shear in the environment. In addition, the surface friction of the landmass appears to contribute to an enhancement of rainfall intensity (Chan et al. 2019). For the climatological study, we analyzed rain gauge data from weather stations in Guangdong Province for 35 years. During periods in which a TC makes landfall along the South China Coast, the rainfall in urban areas over the Pearl River delta has been consistently more than that in surrounding areas. The precipitation in the urban areas and to their west is higher after 1995, when the urbanization accelerated (Yan et al. 2020). We then went on to perform numerical experiments to investigate further the impact of urbanization on rainfall. During the investigation, we found a significant diurnal forcing due to urbanization, with the rainfall maximum being delayed for a couple of hours in the afternoon. Sensitivity experiments also show that enhanced surface friction appears to be the primary factor (Li et al. 2021a). Such a factor also seems to contribute towards an increase in rainfall associated with TC landfall (Li et al. 2021b), in agreement with our earlier study (Chan et al. 2019). These results apparently also depend on the choice of the parameterization schemes for convection, microphysics and the planetary boundary layer. Such dependence was also studied (Wu et al. 2021; Li et al. 2021c). One important finding is that an improper treatment of ice-phase processes is potentially an important error source in the microphysics schemes. Another problem is the overactive warm-rain processes in one of the schemes.

11301417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11301417.value: One element that should be explored more is the effect of aerosol concentration. It was difficult to obtain such data and hence we only include some numerical simulations in the present study.

11301717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11301717.value: Polybrominated diphenylethers (PBDEs), widely used flame-retardant additives, are persistent and toxic contaminants. Due to their widely uses globally, PBDEs are found in various environmental compartments, and pose adverse effects on human and environmental health. The estuary, a special coastal zone, is an area strongly influenced by human impacts, and estuarine sediment serves as a pollutant sink. Extremely high concentrations of PBDEs have been recorded in estuarine sediments around the world. Although penta- and octa-BDEs have been banned since 2000s and deca-BDEs production has also been ceased in 2013, PBDEs have been exponentially concentrated in the environment as a consequence of long-term usage. It is urgently needed to develop effective remediation technologies to eliminate PBDEs in contaminated environments. Physical and chemical processes have been employed to remove PBDEs from sewage and aqueous solution but they are often expensive and contain toxic chemicals. Their effectiveness and applicability in contaminated sediments are also uncertain. Biological process relies on aerobic and anaerobic biodegradation is far cheaper but its effectiveness is limited by the low bioavailability and the steric effects of substituted halogen moieties of PBDEs. It has been proposed that abiotic reactions can help reducing the limitations of biodegradation, and integrated chemical-biological processes may enhance the success of remediation. However, previous research on integrated remediation processes in contaminated sediment is rare. The possible impacts of the added chemicals on indigenous microbial communities in sediments and the effects of microorganisms on the abiotic process are basically unknown. The relative contribution of abiotic reactions and biodegradation processes in different estuarine sediments has seldom been reported. The proposed study attempts to investigate the effects of different abiotic reactions (zero-valent irons and small organic stimulants) on the changes of the structure and function of microbial communities, particularly those involved in PBDE degradation, and the microbial degradation of PBDEs, aiming to elucidate how integrated chemical-biological processes enhance the remediation of PBDE-contaminated estuarine sediments. The kinetics, pathways and mechanisms of the remediation processes will be determined using microcosm studies and the results will be verified by a field trial. The study will also evaluate the fate of chemicals (zero-valent irons and small organic stimulants) used in abiotic reactions during the remediation processes and how the presence of microorganisms affect their fates. The results from the proposed study will fill the knowledge gap on PBDE removal and provide scientific information for developing cost-effective remediation technologies to clean-up contaminated environments.

11301717.label: Realisation of objectives
11301717.value: The objectives have been achieved based on a series of simulated bench top microcosm experiments and a greenhouse computerized controlled mangrove tide-tank study. Details are summarized in following sections. 1. Remediation of PBDE-contaminated mangrove sediments by biological and chemical processes based on tide-tank systems and microcosms studies Among all PBDE congeners, BDE-47, -99, -152 and -209 are common congeners in coastal environments, and the last one is the most abundant and persistent congener. BDE-209 is also the congener most difficult to remove and degrade. Aquaculture effluent (AE) is another pollution problem ubiquitous in coastal environments. These two pollutants often co-exist in mangrove and coastal habitats. Results obtained from the six-month microcosm study planted with Kandelia obovata and Avicennia marina, the two most dominant true species in South China mangrove swamps, reveal that BDE-99 was toxic to K. obovata but not A. marina, and the addition of AE rich in nutrients enhanced plant biomass and alleviated BDE-99 toxicity through the plant’s antioxidative defense system. The combination of planting mangroves and AE irrigation not only significantly stimulated the removal performance but also the completeness of the biodegradation of PBDEs than the planted without effluent amendment treatment. The poorest remediation was in the unplanted group without effluent. These findings demonstrate the best strategy to remedy PBDE contaminants in our environment is planting mangroves with the irrigation of nutrient-rich wastewater such as aquaculture effluent. Not only BDE-99, the one-year tide tank study also confirms a significant removal of BDE-209 by these two dominant mangrove plants and their removal was significantly enhanced by AE, possibly due to the increases of nitrogen and phosphorus content in sediment due to AE irrigation. While the concentrations of parent BDE-209 in contaminated sediments decreased, debrominated congeners like di- to nona-BDEs increased. Parent and debrominated congeners were found in plant tissues, especially roots. These findings show that AE addition not only increased the debromination of BDE-209 in contaminated mangrove sediment but also promoted the take up of BDE-209 in roots, thus enhancing the phytoremediation of BDE-209 in contaminated sediments. This one-year study was performed only on planting single mangrove species and comparing the performance of different plant species. The performance of planting mixed mangrove species in comparison of a single species in the remediation of PBDEs was subsequently investigated. To simulate the distribution of different mangrove plants in natural mangrove swamp, three dominant true mangrove species were planted in contaminated mangrove sediments in tide tanks. Results show that planting mixed mangrove species removed more BDE-209 than that without plants or with only a single species. At month 24, BDE-209 stimulated the production of root superoxide radical, and leaf and root malondialdehyde of mangrove plants. These excess reactive oxygen species were then removed by the anti-oxidative defense mechanism of mangrove plants, so plants could survive the contaminated environment. After 24-months, more than 60% and 40% of BDE-209 in contaminated sediments were removed in planted and unplanted tide-tanks, respectively. When comparing results obtained from the 6- and 12-month study, this long-term study reveals the long-term toxicity of BDE-209 on mangrove plants and the remediation performance of mangrove ecosystems. 2. Structure and function of the microbial communities, particularly those involved in PBDE degradation in mangrove sediments During the tide tank and microcosm studies, sediment samples were collected at different time intervals to evaluate the changes in the structure and function of the microbiomes, particularly the PBDE degrading microorganisms. The abundance of total, PBDE-degrading and other related bacteria in contaminated sediments was determined by the gene copies of bacterial 16S rRNA using quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR). The composition and diversity of the microbial community in sediment were evaluated by high throughput sequencing based on the V4 hypervariable region of bacterial and archaeal 16S rRNA gene, and the sequence was analyzed an Illumina MiSeq platform (paired-end 250-bp mode). Results demonstrate the significance of microbial community network in enhancing the intrinsic debromination or natural degradation of PBDEs. In mangrove microcosms with fast debrominiating capabilities, the relative abundances of Chloroflexi and Deltaproteobacteria succeed by Alphaproteobacteria and Betaproteobacteria were high. The relationships between microbial community structure and PBDEs were significant according to redundancy analyses. However, the relative abundance of the well-known dechlorinator Dehalococcoides showed no clear correlation with the debrominating capacity in the microcosm. 3. Significance of abiotic reaction, biodegradation and coupling processes in the remediation of PBDEs in contaminated sediments The effects of different carbon sources in enhancing the removal and degradation of BDE-47, a common PBDE congener in coastal sediments were investigated by a series of 5-month microcosm studies. All carbon addition significantly enhanced degradation percentages, and the residual BDE-47 percentage significantly correlated with the abundance of total bacteria and Dehaloccoides spp. The addition of carbon like methanol, acetate and succinate achieved higher degradation rates than the other carbon such as formate, pyruvate, lactate and ethanol. The stimulatory effect of extra carbon sources on BDE-47 degradation was carbon-specific. The combined effect of nanoscale zero-valent iron (nZVI) (from 0.1 to 10%) reduction and microbial debromination of BDE-209 removal in mangrove sediments under an anaerobic condition was explored by a series of 12-month microcosm studies. The regular monitoring of the changes in the concentrations of residual PBDEs (both parent and debromianted congeners), hydrogen and ferrous ions, and microbial communities over a one-year study reveals the dynamics of BDE-209 removal and degradation and the associated mechanisms during the integrated chemical-biological processes for the remediation of contaminated mangrove sediments. During this period, nZVI significantly enhanced BDE-209 removal and the iron effect was dose dependent. The removal percentages were significantly lower in the sterilized sediment slurry (without microbes) than that with indigenous microorganisms. The debromination was also high in sediments with indigenous microbes and nZVI. Higher concentrations of ferrous iron (Fe2+) were detected in sediments spiked with more nZVI, and ferrous iron concentrations significantly correlated with BDE-209 removal percentages. These results indicate the synergy between chemical and microbiological methods, and a combination of nZVI and indigenous microorganisms can be an efficient and feasible means to remedy BDE-209 in contaminated sediments.

11301717.label: Major findings and research outcome
11301717.value: Polybrominated biphenylethers (PBDEs) are widely used flame-retardant additives globally. They are found in various environmental compartments, particularly coastal sediments. PBDEs pose harms to human and environment because of their toxicity and persistence. It is urgently needed to develop effective remediation technologies to eliminate PBDEs in contaminated environments. The research work reveals mangrove sediments harbor a diverse group of degrading microorganisms such as Dehalococcoides, iron- and sulfate-reducing groups, which are important in the removal and debromination of BDE-209. These microbes are able to naturally biodegrade PBDE contaminants, and the removal and debromination percentages strongly relate to the abundance of bacterial groups involved in debromination. Our study also demonstrates plant uptake, in addition to indigenous degrading microorganisms in sediments, is also important in the removal and debromination of PBDEs. Planting suitable species in mixture, such as a combination of Kandelia obovata, Avicennia marina and Aegiceras corniculatum, enhances the remediation process. The irrigation of aquaculture effluent rich in nutrients stimulates plant growth and the uptake of PBDEs, leading to more removal and degradation of BDE-209 and other PBDE congeners in contaminated sediments. Not only nutrients in aquaculture effluent, extra carbon like methanol also enhances the removal and degradation of PBDEs. The removal and biodegradation percentages of different PBDE congeners, including BDE-47, BDE-152 and BDE-209, can be further enhanced by the addition of zero valent iron. A synergy between indigenous microorganisms and zero valent iron spiked into BDE-209 contamination sediments is recorded, as zero valent iron provides more reducing power for the debromination of PBDEs. The key findings have been published in 10 SCI journal papers and awarded one patent from Mainland China. The work has also been shared with our peers and presented at various international and national conferences. The study fills the knowledge gap related to the removal and debromination of PBDEs, especially the most persistent BDE-209. The results also provides important scientific information for developing cost-effective remediation technologies. We propose coupling biological with chemical processes, that is, a combination of planting, irrigation of wastewater and/or addition of zero-valent iron or methanol, can be a cost-effective remediation strategy to clean-up contaminated environments, as well as purify wastewater.

11301717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11301717.value: The research can be extended into the following areas: (i) elucidate how the structure and function of degrading microorganisms colonized in roots and rhizosphere sediment of different mangrove plants change by pollution, aiming to understand their adaptations; (ii) determine the microbial activities and gene expression of these degrading microorganisms involved in the removal and degradation processes and their exact roles in the remediation of persistent toxic organic pollutants in mangrove ecosystems; and (iii) isolate and cultivate the important degraders for bioaugmentation purposes and evaluate the interactions between degraders and the amendment of different chemicals, including wastewater. Our research work has led to more collaboration between academics in Mainland China, namely, Dr. Zhou Hai Chao from Shenzhen University, China; Prof. Li RL, Beijing University (Shenzhen Institute). We have successfully obtained the following two grants in year 2020: 1. “Research on mangrove environment adaptation mechanism and intelligent ecological restoration technology (Institute Key Projects on Basic Research from Shenzhen Science and Technology Innovation Committee, Shenzhen Municipal Government, RMB 625,000. 2. “The role of root iron plaque on the transportation of nutrients and pollutants in mangrove constructed wetland plants (NSF National Science Foundation, PRC, RMB 640,000)

11301717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11301717.value: Polybrominated biphenylethers (PBDEs), the widely used flame-retardant additives globally, are persistent and toxic contaminants. PBDEs are found in various environmental compartments, and pose adverse effects on human and environmental health. The estuary, a special coastal zone, is an area strongly influenced by human impacts, and estuarine sediment serves as pollutant sinks. It is urgently needed to develop effective remediation technologies to eliminate PBDEs in contaminated environments around the world. The research work demonstrates the significance of natural remediation of BDE-209 in contaminated mangrove sediments as sediments harbor a diversified group of degrading microorganisms. The removal and degradation can be enhanced by the addition of appropriate amounts of zero-valent irons, as such addition changes the structure and function of the microbial community, particularly those involved in PBDE degradation. The remediation can be further promoted by planting suitable mangrove species with the irrigation of nutrient-rich wastewater such as aquaculture effluent. The study not only fills the knowledge gap on PBDE removal, it also provides scientific information for developing cost-effective remediation technologies. The combination of planting, irrigation of wastewater and/or addition of zero-valent iron can be a cost-effective remediation strategy to clean-up contaminated environments, as well as for wastewater treatment.

11302417.label: Project Objectives
11302417.value: Establishing the recursion relations for the expansion coefficients and using them to deduce an asymptotic dynamic finite-strain shell theory consistent with the three-dimensional Hamilton's principle. Introducing proper edge boundary conditions which can reserve the proper order of the edge terms in the three-dimensional weak formulation. Deducing a virtual work principle through a proper weak formulation for the shell equations, which can be used for implementing a finite element scheme and yield the natural boundary conditions for the shell theory. Examining some benchmark problems by comparing the solutions from the reduced shell equations with those obtained in the full three-dimensional field equations. Stress couples will be calculated for these concrete problems for the purpose of comparing with existing shell theories with equations which contain stress couples. Studying two application problems, including swelling-induced instability in a polymer gel and folding instability in a sheet on a cylinder. The results will be used to understand the pattern formations.

11302417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11302417.value: 壳状结构在自然界和工程应用中是普遍存在的，比如心脏瓣膜， 血管，生物体中的上皮组织，植物花瓣，基础设施屋顶和冷却塔。 另一方面，许多材料，如生物组织，聚合物凝胶和弹性体，都非 常柔软。这种材料的一个特征是它们可以经受大应变的变形。近 年来，人们对于理解由外力引起的软物质的形态变化越来越感兴 趣，比如皮肤皱纹和大脑沟回的形成。综合以上两个方面，我们 认为非常有必要研究壳状软物质的力学行为。虽然任何物体都是 三维的， 但是壳结构的厚度要远小于其基面的长度尺寸。因此， 与其使用在解析和数值上都不好处理的三维理论，还不如使用合 理简化的二维壳理论来研究壳状软物质的力学行为。已经有很多 壳理论研究硬质材料的小应变（比如著名的Kirchhoff-Love 壳理 论和 Koiter 壳理论），但是相对来讲研究大应变的壳理论就要少 很多了。特别地，现在还没有一个一致性 动态大应变壳理论能够 同时处理弯曲和拉伸效应。从本构上来讲，我们可以通过应变能 函数（或自由能函数）来对软物质的力学行为进行建模。本项目 的主要目标是为非线性材料（本构关系非线性并且能量函数具有 一般形式）推导出一个大应变壳理论，并且该理论和三维 Hamilton 原理渐进一致。推导是建立在基于壳结构底平面的级数 展开之上的。该理论的新颖之处在于发现了应力和位移／位置系 数之间的某些线性关系（虽然该问题是高度非线性的），这让我 们能够在级数的展开系数之间建立递归关系，从而使得最终的系 统只有三个未知量。该理论也考虑了边界条件及相关的弱形式。 几个基准问题被用来测试该壳理论的有效性，并且为了表明该新 理论强大的适用性，将考虑两个应用。一个是聚合物凝胶管中由 膨胀引起的不稳定性，这和微透镜装置有关。另一个是对于乌龟 脖子上皮肤皱褶的建模。基于壳理论，我们将结合解析和数值的 方法来解决这两个问题，得到的结果将有助于理解不稳定性是如 何导致模态形成的。一些经典的小应变壳理论已经广泛应用于硬 质材料，我们希望得到的一致性动态大应变壳理论也可以广泛应 用于软物质材料。

11302917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11302917.value: This project is concerned with fundamental studies of the reactivity of chromium(VI) nitrido (CrVI≡N) and imido (CrVI=NR) complexes, as well as manganese(VI) imido (MnVI=NR) complexes. High-valent transition metal complexes are stabilized by ligands that can form multiple bonds with the metal, such as oxo, nitrido and imido ligands. Metal oxo species such as MnO4- and Cr2O72- have long been used as oxidants in synthetic chemistry. They function as oxidants via a variety of mechanisms, including simple electron-transfer, proton-coupled electron transfer, O-atom transfer and H-atom transfer. However, similar reactivity has not been demonstrated for nitrido and imido complexes of chromium and manganese, which represents a missing link in the high-valent chemistry of these metals. Hence the design of highly electrophilic/oxidizing nitrido and imido complexes of these metals which can exhibit oxo-like reactivity is of fundamental interest. Metal nitrido species are also key intermediates in chemical and biological nitrogen fixation, hence a study of their reactivity would provide insights into the mechanisms of this very important process. Nitrido and imido complexes are also potentially very useful reagents for the nitrogenation of organic substrates. Methods for the selective and efficient incorporation of N atom or NR groups into organic molecules under mild conditions is an important research area in synthetic chemistry owing to the ubiquity of N-containing compounds in natural products, agricultural and pharmaceutical agents. In this project we propose to synthesize highly electrophilic/oxidizing Cr≡N, Cr=NR and Mn=NR species that exhibits oxo-like reactivity. Although there are quite a few manganese(V) and chromium(V) nitrido and imido complexes reported in the literature, most of these complexes are either unreactive or they exhibit only nucleophilic reactivity. On the other hand, the corresponding M(VI) complexes are expected to be much more electrophilic/oxidizing, and should possess oxo-like reactivity similar to MnO4- or CrO42-. Hence in this project we propose to design a series of LCrVI≡N LCrVI=NR and LMnVI=NR complexes bearing various multidentate anxilliary ligands L. Their reactivity towards a variety of nucleophiles, such as amines, thiols, isocyanides, alkenes, anilines, alkynes and phenols, will be investigated. Our proposed studies should contribute to fundamental understanding of the reactivity of CrVI≡N CrVI=NR and MnVI=NR complexes. It could also provide new and economical methods for the selective nitrogenation of organic substrates under mild conditions. 此項目是關於铬（VI）氮（CrVI≡N），铬（VI）亞胺基（CrVI=NR）和錳（VI）亞胺基（MnVI=NR）配合物的反應性的基礎研究。高價態過渡金屬可以被能夠與其形成多重健的配體，例如氧，氮和亞胺基，穩定 。金屬氧合物如MnO4-和Cr2O72-長期以來被用作合成化學中的氧化劑。 它們通過各種機理起著氧化劑的作用，包括簡單的電子轉移，質子耦合電子轉移，氧原子轉移和氢原子轉移。但是，铬和錳的氮和亞胺基配合物從未顯示過類似反應性，這是金屬高價態化學的缺失一環。因此，具有类金属氧合物反應性的高亲电性或氧化性的金属氮和亚氨基配合物的设计是最根本的兴趣。金属氮同时是化学和生物固氮过程的重要中间体，因此對其反應性的研究將為這一非常重要的過程的機制提供見解。氮和亞氨基配合物也是有機底物氮化的潛在非常有用的試劑。 由於含氮化合物在天然產物，農藥和醫藥中的普遍存在，在溫和條件下選擇性和有效地將氮原子或亚氨基團併入有機分子的方法是合成化學中的重要研究領域。 在這個項目中，我們提出合成高親電性或氧化性的具有類似金屬氧合物的反應性的Cr≡N，Cr=NR和Mn=NR物質。 儘管在文獻中報導了相當多的錳（V）和鉻（V）氮和亞氨基配合物，但大多數這些配合物都是沒有反應性的，或者只表現出親核反應性。另一方面，相應的六價金屬M（VI）配合物預期更高親電性/氧化性，應該具有類似於MnO4-或CrO42-的類金屬氧合物的反應性。 因此，在這個項目中，我們建議設計一系列攜帶各種多齒輔助配體L的 LCrVI≡N，LCrVI=NR和LMnVI=NR配合物，研究其對各種親核試劑如胺，硫醇，異氰化物，烯烴，苯胺，炔烴和酚的反應。 我們提出的研究應有助於對LCrVI≡N，LCrVI=NR和LMnVI=NR配合物的反應性的基本了解，也可以為溫和條件下有機底物的選擇性氮化提供新的和經濟的方法。

11302917.label: Major findings and research outcome
11302917.value: We have synthesized a new manganese(V) imido complex bearing the TAML ligand. One-electron oxidation of this complex affords the first example of a manganese(VI) imido species, which readily undergoes novel nitrene transfer reaction with itself and with thioanisoles. It also abstracts H-atom from phenol and hydrocarbons with weak C-H bonds. Compounds of Mn(VI) are rare. Apart from Mn(VI) oxo species, only a few Mn(VI) nitrido species are known. However, the reactivity of these complexes towards various substrates has not been investigated. Our work should be a significant contribution to high-valent manganese imido chemistry. We have accomplished the synthesis and structure of Mn(V) nitrido complex (1) bearing the TAML ligand. By one-electron oxidation of 1, we have also isolated and determined the X-ray structure of the corresponding manganese(VI) nitrido complex (2). Complex 2 readily undergoes nitrogen atom transfer to triphenylphosphine to form triphenylphosphine imine and direct aziridination of styrenes to generate 2-phenylaziridines. Both reactions are observed for the first time with MnN. In the reaction with styrenes, 2 exhibits electrophilic reactivity with electron-rich styrenes but nucleophilic reactivity with electron-poor styrenes. M=O and M≡N species are well known to perform HAT or CPET with hydrocarbons, in which the proton is directly transferred to the oxo or nitrido ligand. In this work, we provide evidence that the reaction of 2 with NADH analogues occurs via an initial Separated CPET mechanism. Our work should be a fundamental contribution to Mn(VI) nitrido chemistry. We have investigated a Cr(V)–Cr(III) in-situ transition system to achieve low-toxic and highly efficient anti-cancer therapy. The designed stable Cr(V) nitrido complexes bearing quinolinolato ancillary ligands are highly unusual in that they react readily with both the reductant GSH (to in-situ generate Cr(III)) and the oxidant H2O2 (to generate singlet oxygen). Both reactions result in the disruption of the redox balance in cancer cells, thus inducing intracellular DNA damage and activation of p53 pathway, finally leading to caspase-dependent and mitochondria-mediated apoptotic cell death. To the best of our knowledge, these Cr-based nitride complexes are the first stable Cr(V) complexes with potent anticancer efficacy. Overall, our work may provide a new approach for the design of safe and efficient metal-based anticancer drugs by rationally design stable high valent metal nitrido complexes.

11303117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11303117.value: Cell polarity refers to spatial differences in the shape and structure of cells; cytokinesis is the physical process of cell division and is related to the regulation of cell shape change. Cell polarity coupled with the regulation of cell shape change leads to the generation of diverse cell types playing different roles in biological processes. In human beings, disruption of cell polarity or cytokinesis is usually a hallmark of abnormal cell differentiation and cancer. Thus, regulation controls of cell polarity and cytokinesis are important for normal cell development. However, the fundamental mechanisms for achieving cell polarity, cell shape change and cytokinesis remain controversial. In this project, we aim to study cell polarization processes through modeling the system of cell polarization proteins in budding yeast. We propose to build a mathematical model which includes both positive and negative feedback loops, observed in experimental data. Through analyzing the model, we will understand how the positive and negative regulations contribute on robust cell polarization. By extending the model to a moving boundary system, we will be able to study the interplay between cell polarization regulation and the control of cell shape change. The long-term aim of this study is to extend our understanding for the cause of abnormal cell development and provide us a potential treatment for clinical studies. 細胞極性是指細胞形狀和結構的差異性；同時，胞質分裂的物理過程與細胞極性的調節有關。細胞極性與細胞形態變化的調節相結合導致細胞在生物過程中發揮不同作用。在人類的細胞中，細胞極性或胞質分裂的不正常作用通常是異常細胞分化和癌症的標誌。因此，這些生物過程的調節控制對於正常細胞的發育是十分重要的。然而，實現細胞極性和細胞分裂的基本機制仍然是有爭議的。 在這研究中，我們的目標是通過對酵母細胞的極化過程進行建模來研究細胞極化的機制。這數學模型中，我們包含了實驗數據中觀察到正反饋迴路。通過分析模型，我們將了解正反饋迴路對穩健細胞極化的貢獻。通過將模型擴展到移動邊界系統，我們將能夠研究細胞極化調節與細胞形狀變化控制之間的相互作用。本研究的長期目標是擴大對細胞發育異常的理解，為臨床研究提供潛在的治療方法。

11303117.label: Major findings and research outcome
11303117.value: We have built a mathematical model for cell polarization, which includes both positive and negative feedback loops, and applied the Turing stability analysis, stochastic analysis and numerical simulations to study the system. Two papers have been published in peer-reviewed journals, Mathematical Biosciences and Engineering, and Chaos, Solitons and Fractals. Our work has applied our model for the experimental study with our collaborator and published a paper in a peer-reviewed journal, Molecular Biology of the Cell. This work provides more experimental data to support that negative feedback may play an important role in cell polarization. Two papers have been published in a peer-reviewed journal, Molecular Biology of the Cell. We have developed a numerical framework to study the moving boundary system for cell shape change during cell polarization. It can be combined with our model to provide a full picture of cell polarization in cell colony development. A review paper and an original paper are in preparation. Our work was also extended to study budding yeast colony formation and its relationship with cell polarization. The results have been published in a paper in a peer-reviewed journal, PLoS Computational Biology.

11303517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11303517.value: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) is an established treatment modality for various superficial and localized cancers. It utilizes the combined action of a photosensitizer, light of appropriate wavelength, and oxygen to generate reactive oxygen species (ROS) to eradicate cancer cells. Owing to the very short lifetime (< 40 ns) and diffusion range (ca. 20 nm) of ROS, their action is almost confined to the site where ROS are produced. Therefore, preferential localization of the photosensitizer in tumor and precise application of the light are extremely crucial that can greatly improve the therapeutic outcome. Considerable efforts have therefore been put to enhance the tumor-targeting property and pharmacokinetic profiles of photosensitizers, and to advance the fiber optics and endoscopy technologies. Apart from directing the photosensitizers to the tumor through conjugation with tumor-targeting ligands or encapsulation into multifunctional nanocarriers, controlling their photoactivity in a specific manner is another promising approach. These so-called photodynamic molecular beacons (PMBs) are either self-quenched or deactivated by the quenching component in the native form, but upon interactions with cancer-related stimuli, the photosensitizing units are activated through disaggregation or separation from the quenchers, resulting in restoration of their fluorescence and ROS generation. This approach can minimize the photodamage of normal tissues in PDT. To further improve the tumor specificity and therapeutic efficacy, it is desirable that the PMBs can only be activated by the coexistence of more than one stimulus or conjugate to a tumor-targeting ligand. These “smart” PMBs with additional controls or functions, however, remain very rare which provides an impetus for further development. This project aims to develop advanced PMBs with multiple controls for targeted PDT. We plan to connect two 2,4-dinitrobenzenesulfonate (DNBS)-substituted phthalocyanine units with a cathepsin B substrate. They are expected to be severely deactivated by self-quenching and photoinduced electron transfer to the DNBS groups. Only in the presence of both intracellular glutathione and lysosomal cathepsin B, which can remove the DNBS groups and cleave the peptide linker, respectively, these PMBs are activated. To enable specific delivery to the tumor, these PMBs will be further conjugated with a folate-modified pH-responsive cell-penetrating peptide (CPP). While the folate group can bind to the upregulated folate receptors on cancer cells, the CPP can facilitate the internalization after being protonated in the mild acidic tumor microenvironment. It is believed that these PMBs with multiple targeting-activation properties can exhibit superior photodynamic activities, which will be validated both in vitro and in vivo. 光動力學療法（PDT）是一種針對多種表面及局部癌症的治療方法。這種方法主要是將光敏劑、特定波段的光及氧分子結合起來，使其能夠產生活性氧（ROS）來殺死腫瘤細胞。由於活性氧分子具有較短的壽命（<40 ns）及較小的擴散範圍（約20 nm），因此活性氧分子只能氧化其生成位點附近的生物分子。光敏劑在腫瘤中的分佈及光的精確定位對改善光動力療法的治療效果具有非常重要的作用。目前，研究工作者在提高光敏劑的腫瘤靶向特性和藥代動力學性質，以及發展和提高光纖和內窺鏡等技術等方面做出了很多努力。除了通過將光敏劑與具有腫瘤靶向定位的配體結合或將其組裝到多功能納米載體中外，還能以其他方式來控制目標分子的光活性。光動力分子信標（PMBs）是通過分子本身的自淬滅過程或與淬滅組分相互作用使光敏劑失活。當與癌症相關的刺激物作用時，光敏劑可以通過解聚或與淬滅劑分離而被活化，使其恢復螢光和生成ROS的能力。這種治療方法可以有效減少PDT治療過程中對正常組織的光損傷。為了進一步提高光敏劑對腫瘤細胞的特定選擇性和治療效果，研究合成新型的具有多重活化位點或腫瘤特異選擇性的PMBs具有非常重要的意義。然而，對於這類智慧型PMBs的報導仍非常罕見，這也為進一步開發新型光敏劑提供了動力。該項目旨在開發研究具有多重活化位點的PMBs，並將其應用于靶向光動力學中。我們計劃在對溶酶體組織蛋白酶B具有回應的肽鏈上連接兩個具有2,4-二硝基苯磺酸（DNBS）基團的鋅酞菁染料，並預期通過自淬滅和光誘導的電子轉移使光敏劑失活。只有在谷胱甘肽和溶酶體組織蛋白酶B同時作用的條件下，這類PMBs才會通過DNBS基團的離去和肽鏈的斷裂而被活化。為了能夠將其選擇性的輸送到腫瘤部位，這類PMSs將進一步與葉酸修飾的具有pH回應的細胞穿透肽（CPP）結合。葉酸可以促進其與葉酸受體高表達的腫瘤細胞選擇性的結合，同時CPP在腫瘤組織弱酸性環境中被質子化後能進一步提高其細胞攝取量。我們預測這類具有多重活化靶向及特性的PMBs將具有良好的腫瘤特異性光動力治療效果，這將在體外實驗中得到進一步驗證。

11303517.label: Realisation of objectives
11303517.value: The first objective of this project is to design, synthesize, and characterize a series of dimeric quencher-appended phthalocyanines linked with a cathepsin B substrate and to conjugate these dual activatable photosensitizers with a folate-modified pH-responsive cell-penetrating peptide (CPP). As the first endeavor toward this objective, we designed and prepared two dual stimuli-activated photosensitizers in which two or three glutathione (GSH)-responsive 2,4-dinitrobenzenesulfonate (DNBS)-substituted zinc(II) phthalocyanine (ZnPc) units were connected via one or two cathepsin B-cleavable Gly-Phe-Leu-Gly peptide linker(s) (J. Med. Chem. 2021, 64, 17455). We extended the target compounds to the trimeric systems for comparison as we expected that they could also exhibit a superior activation effect. These dimeric and trimeric phthalocyanines were characterized with high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) and high-resolution mass spectrometry. In attempts to introduce an additional control to these dual stimuli-responsive systems, we prepared a series of ZnPcs substituted with a pH-responsive CPP based on arginine and histidine or an acid-sensitive 2,3-dimethylmaleic anhydride-protected lysine sequence. Unfortunately, these CPP-conjugated ZnPcs did not exhibit acid-promoted cellular uptake and cytotoxicity. As we were not able to identify an appropriate pH-responsive CCP that could achieve these functions, we adopted an alternative strategy and simply introduced a tumor-targeting group to the photosensitizers. We initially planned to use folate as a tumor-targeting group. However, due to the limited solubility of this ligand and the possible occurrence of isomers upon conjugation, an epidermal growth factor receptor (EGRF)-targeting cyclic peptide (labeled as cEBP) was chosen instead and introduced to the trimeric phthalocyanine, which was found to exhibit a more remarkable activation effect and higher potency than the dimeric counterpart (Chem. Eur. J. submitted). To extend the dual activation concept, a double-locked photodynamic molecular beacon (PMB) was also prepared, in which a distyryl boron dipyrromethene (DSBDP)-based photosensitizer and a Black Hole Quencher-3 (BHQ-3) moiety were connected with two peptide segments in a cyclic peptide, namely Pro-Lys-Gly-Val-Arg and Gly-Phe-Lys-Gly, which are the substrates of matrix metalloproteinase-2 (MMP-2) and cathepsin B, respectively (J. Am. Chem. Soc. submitted). The DSBDP moiety was fully quenched in the PMB owing to the Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) to the BHQ-3 unit. Only in the presence of both MMP-2 and cathepsin B, the photoactivities of the DSBDP unit could be activated. After preparing these compounds, their electronic absorption and fluorescence spectra were recorded in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) at pH 7.4 or the working buffer of cathepsin B [pH 5.0, 25 mM sodium acetate, 1 mM ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA)] in the presence of 0.5% Tween 80 (v/v) added to increase the water solubility of the compounds. The Q-band absorptions of the dimer and trimer were significantly diminished, broadened, and split when compared with the spectra recorded in N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF), indicating that they were highly aggregated in these polar media. Upon excitation at 610 nm, the fluorescence emission of the dimer and trimer remained very weak due to the photoinduced electron transfer (PET) effect of the DNBS moieties and the self-quenching of the ZnPc units. Their singlet oxygen generation efficiency as determined by using 1,3-diphenylisobenzofuran (DPBF) as the probe was also largely inhibited. The activation in fluorescence emission and singlet oxygen generation by GSH and cathepsin B was then investigated in the buffer solution at 37 °C. Upon treatment with both of these stimuli, the fluorescence emission was remarkably increased and almost reached the maximum after 25 h. This could be attributed to the detachment of the DNBS moieties and the release of free ZnPc units. The trimeric system exhibited an on/off ratio of up to 27 in term of the fluorescence emission. Under the dual activated condition, both compounds could also achieve the highest singlet oxygen generation efficiency. Similar spectroscopic and stimuli-responsive studies were also performed for the cEBP-conjugated trimer. It was found that the cEBP moiety did not exert a significant influence on these properties. For the double-locked PMB, the Q-band absorption was also broadened and diminished in PBS or the buffer solution, reflecting its high aggregation tendency in these aqueous media. Upon excitation at 610 nm, the fluorescence emission of the PMB was hardly observed. Its singlet oxygen generation ability was also quenched by the appended BHQ-3 moiety. Upon treatment with either MMP-2 or cathepsin B, the fluorescence intensity was just slightly enhanced. It is believed that although one of the peptide segments was cleaved by the corresponding stimulus, the DSBDP and BHQ-3 moieties were still connected and the FRET between these components still existed, resulting in significant quenching. Upon sequential addition of MMP-2 and cathepsin B, the fluorescence intensity was largely increased over a period of 25 h. The singlet oxygen generation efficiency was also significantly increased, showing that the PMB was almost fully activated due to the cleavage of both peptide substrates by the two enzymes. To address the last objective, we examined the in vitro activities of these compounds against a range of cancer cells. Upon internalization into A549 human lung carcinoma cells and HepG2 human hepatocarcinoma cells, the dimer and trimer showed substantial intracellular fluorescence, showing that they were activated inside the cells. The intensity was increased upon post-incubation with GSH ester or reduced upon pre-treatment with a cathepsin B inhibitor. While these compounds were non-cytotoxic in the dark, they exhibited high cytotoxicity upon light irradiation with IC50 values of 0.21-0.39 μM. The photocytotoxicity was dependent on the intracellular GSH and cathepsin B levels. Having an EGFR-targeting ligand, the cEBP-conjugated trimer showed a cell-selective property. In the EGFR-positive A549 cells and SW480 human colorectal adenocarcinoma cells, this trimer showed strong intracellular fluorescence. In contrast, its fluorescence was not notable in the EGFR-negative HeLa human cervical carcinoma cells and HepG2 cells. These results indicated that the cEBP moiety of the compound could promote its cellular uptake through the EGRF-mediated endocytosis, followed by activation by the intracellular GSH and cathepsin B. The trimer was localized in lysosomes and highly photocytotoxic toward the EGFR-positive cancer cells with IC50 values as low as 0.42 μM, causing cell death mainly through apoptosis. To examine the in vitro activation of the double-locked PMB, we utilized the MMP-2-positive A549 cells and U87-MG human glioblastoma cells, as well as the MMP-2-negative HeLa cells and HEK293 human embryonic kidney normal cells. After incubation with the PMB, the two MMP-2-positive cell lines showed significantly stronger fluorescence intensity, mainly in the lysosomes, than the two MMP-2-negative cell lines. It is believed that the PMB underwent enzymatic cleavage first by the extracellular MMP-2 and then by the intracellular cathepsin B, leading to the restoration of fluorescence emission. As expected, the intracellular fluorescence of the PMB was largely reduced upon addition of MMP-2 and cathepsin B inhibitors. This PMB also exhibited MMP-2 and cathepsin B-triggered intracellular ROS generation. Its photocytotoxicity was significantly higher toward the MMP-2-positive cells with IC50 values as low as 0.78 μM. By inhibiting the activities of MMP-2 and/or cathepsin B, the PMB became non-cytotoxic up to 4 μM. Finally, the in vivo behavior of this PMB in A549-tumor bearing nude mice was also examined. Upon intratumoral injection, it could light up the tumor and effectively suppress the tumor growth upon laser irradiation. All the above results show that the three objectives set for this project have been fully achieved.

11303517.label: Major findings and research outcome
11303517.value: To develop advanced photosensitizers with multiple controls for PDT, we first synthesized two dual cathepsin B and GSH-activated photosensitizers in which two or three DNBS-substituted ZnPc units were connected with one or two cathepsin B-cleavable peptide sequence(s) (J. Med. Chem. 2021, 64, 17455). Both compounds were largely quenched in fluorescence emission and singlet oxygen generation due to the PET effect of the appended DNBS moieties and the self-quenching effect of the ZnPc units. These compounds could be activated selectively by GSH and cathepsin B via removal of the DNBS moieties and cleavage of the peptide linkage, respectively, both in aqueous media and inside A549 and HepG2 cancer cells. The trimer exhibited slightly higher photocytotoxicity than the dimeric analogue with IC50 values as low as 0.21 μM. The photocytotoxicity was dependent on the intracellular GSH and cathepsin B levels. A related dual stimuli-responsive ZnPc trimer containing a EGFR-targeting cyclic peptide was also prepared (Chem. Eur. J. submitted). The conjugate was fully quenched in the native state, but its photoactivities could be selectively activated by cathepsin B and GSH as demonstrated in aqueous media and at the cellular level. By using a range of cancer cell lines with different expression levels of EGFR, we studied the cell-selective and dual stimuli-responsive properties of this compound. The combined effect could result in a 48-fold enhancement in the intracellular fluorescence. This trimer was highly photocytotoxic toward the EGFR-positive cancer cells with IC50 values as low as 0.42 μM, causing cell death mainly through apoptosis. The results showed that this trimer with tumor-targeting and dual stimuli-activatable properties is a promising photosensitizer for precise PDT. Apart from these ZnPc-based photosensitizers, we also prepared a double-locked PMB, in which a DSBDP-based photosensitizer and a BHQ-3 quencher were conjugated to the two sides of a cyclic peptide using the MMP-2 and cathepsin B-cleavable peptide substrates as the two locks (J. Am. Chem. Soc. submitted). The FRET between the DSBDP and BHQ-3 moieties led to inhibition of the fluorescence emission and singlet oxygen generation of the PMB. Upon exposure to both MMP-2 and cathepsin B, the photoactivities of PMB could be restored owing to the cleavage of the two peptide substrates and release of the free DSBDP moiety. The intracellular fluorescence and photocytotoxicity of the PMB against the MMP-2 positive A549 and U87-MG cells were significant higher than those toward the MMP-2 negative HeLa and HEK293 cells.

11303517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11303517.value: There has been considerable interest in the development of advanced photosensitizing systems for targeted PDT. The PMBs developed in this study exhibit several levels of control that can enhance the tumor specificity as demonstrated at the cellular level. To extend the study, detailed in vivo study using tumor-bearing nude mice should be conducted to examine their tumor-targeting and stimuli-responsive properties, as well as the treatment efficacy and side effects. The results could guide the optimization of the different components. In fact, the molecular designs of these PMBs can be extended to other systems that can be selectively activated by other tumor-associated stimuli by simply replacing the corresponding substrates and/or quenchers. Their application can also be extended beyond PDT by using other disease-related stimuli as the targets. Furthermore, as the different components of these PMBs are assembled in a covalent manner, the synthesis is tedious. The large size of the molecules may also hinder the cellular uptake and tumor localization. To make this approach more versatile, the different components could be connected and function in the biological environment through bioorthogonal chemistry. This field involving bioorthogonally activated photosensitizers is still in its infancy.

11303517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11303517.value: As a promising and clinically approved treatment modality, photodynamic therapy (PDT) has received considerable attention. Owing to the very short lifetime (< 40 ns) and diffusion range (ca. 20 nm) of reactive oxygen species, their action is almost confined to the site where they are produced. Therefore, preferential localization and activation of the photosensitizer in the tumor is extremely crucial that can greatly improve the treatment outcome. In this project, we synthesized and characterized a series of glutathione (GSH) and cathepsin B-activated zinc(II) phthalocyanine-based photosensitizing systems, as well as a matrix metalloproteinase-2 (MMP-2) and cathepsin B-responsive distyryl boron dipyrromethene-based photosensitizer for targeted PDT. These compounds were almost fully deactivated by self-quenching and/or the appended quenchers. Only in the presence of both stimuli (GSH and cathepsin B or MMP-2 and cathepsin B), these compounds could be activated due to the cleavage of the peptide linkers and detachment of the quencher, thereby releasing the photosensitizing unit(s). To enable specific delivery to the tumor, one of these compounds was also conjugated with an epidermal growth factor receptor-targeting cyclic peptide. The results showed that this molecular-based photosensitizing system with tumor-targeting and dual stimuli-activatable properties is a promising photosensitizer for precise PDT.

11303617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11303617.value: A quantum computer is expected to outperform the current information technology in many important problems. One of the most promising candidates for its realization is the semiconductor spin qubit. Compared to other materials, silicon-based quantum devices hold a unique advantage that one of the isotope of silicon, the silicon-28, carries no nuclear spin. Qubits built on isotopically enriched silicon essentially live in a "spin vacuum", and decoherence due to nuclear spin bath is greatly suppressed. With this advantage, it has been experimentally demonstrated that one may control a qubit based on isotopically enriched silicon with extremely long coherence time and very high control fidelity. Nevertheless, it remains a challenge to further suppress the gate error. The charge noise, caused by unintentionally deposited impurities near the quantum dots, is the critical contributing factor to the decoherence of a qubit based on isotopically enriched silicon. In order to combat the noise, Dynamically Corrected Gates have been developed. Among various proposals, the SUPCODE is particularly useful for the singlet-triplet qubit which uses the two-electron singlet and triplet states as the computational bases. SUPCODE has been optimized for isotopically enriched silicon quantum device: a kind of SUPCODE which treats charge noise alone are not only found to be about 40% shorter than the full SUPCODE but also offers better performances. This and many other preliminary results as detailed in the proposal suggest that it is possible to optimize the quantum gates in silicon-based semiconductor spin qubits. In this project, we will develop efficient, optimized protocols to control spin qubits based on silicon. We will start with an investigation on the change noise, in which we will focus on quantitatively how the charge noise changes under different controlling schemes. Based on these results, we will proceed to pulse design and optimization. We will use nonzero exchange interaction to shorten the pulse sequences that have been developed, employ the technique of smooth pulse shaping in order to develop optimized, experiment-friendly pulses that improve the performances of both single and two-qubit gates. We will also extend the study to multi-qubit gates, to devices with multiple electrons, and to the control problem in a rotating frame. Overall, the results of this research are expected to provide a viable means to control silicon spin qubits, which should constitute an important step forward in accomplishing fault-tolerant, scalable quantum computation using silicon quantum devices. 量子計算機被期待能夠以遠快於當代信息技術的速度解決一些重要問題。實現量子計算機的一個重要的候選者是半導體自旋量子比特。和其他材料比較，矽基量子器件有著獨一無二的優勢，因為矽的一種同位素，矽-28，沒有核自旋。基於同位素純化矽的量子比特處於“自旋真空”，而核自旋造成的退相幹被大幅降低。因此優勢，人們已證明對基於同位素純化的矽的量子比特的實驗操控可達到很長的相幹時間和極高的操控精度。然而，進一步降低量子門的誤差依然是一個挑戰。量子點附近雜質造成的電荷噪聲已證明對基於同位素純化的矽的量子比特的退相幹有著主要的貢獻。為了能夠對抗這種噪聲，人們發展了動力學修正量子門。在各種方案中，SUPCODE對單態----三重態量子比特尤為有用。單態----三重態量子比特使用雙電子態中的單態和一個三重態作為比特態。SUPCODE已經對矽系統進行過優化：一類僅處理電荷噪聲的SUPCODE不僅比其原始版本短40%，更在對抗電荷噪聲方面有更好的表現。這和其他一些初步結果表明：量子門可以在矽基半導體量子比特系統中進行優化。在這項研究中，我們將發展高效率的，優化的控制協議來操控矽基量子比特。我們從研究電荷噪聲的性質開始，尤其專註於定量研究電荷噪聲在不同的操控環境下如何變化。接下來，我們進入脈沖設計和優化。我們以非零的交換耦合來縮短量子門所需要的時間，使用平滑脈沖的技術來發展優化的、易於應用於實驗的脈沖，使之能夠提高單比特和兩比特操作的精度。我們還將把研究擴展到多比特門，多電子量子器件，以及在旋轉系中的控制問題。總體來說，這項研究的結果將會提供操作矽量子比特的有效方法，並作為最終實現以矽基量子器件進行大規模容錯量子計算的重要一步。

11303617.label: Realisation of objectives
11303617.value: All objectives set forth in the project have been realized with abundant results. We provide details below. For Task 1, we have focused in several different systems. In triple-quantum-dot devices, we studied the leakage and sweet spots when it is operated as a resonant-exchange qubit, and we have found that leakage can be greatly suppressed [2]. We have also proposed a charge qubit that can be tuned by potential barriers, which have certain advantages in manipulation [4]. We have found that, when the triple quantum dots are operated as a charge qubit, the geometry of the dots is important, and a triangular arrangement could minimize the leakage [11]. [2] Leakage and sweet spots in triple-quantum-dot spin qubits: a molecular orbital study, C. Zhang, X.-C. Yang, and X. Wang, Phys. Rev. A 97, 042326 (2018). [4] Tunable charge qubit based on barrier-controlled triple quantum dots, X.-C. Yang, G. X. Chan, and X. Wang, Phys. Rev. A 98, 032334 (2018). [11] Suppression of leakage for a charge qubit in triangular triple quantum dots, G. X. Chan and X. Wang, Adv. Quantum Technol. 2019, 1900072 (2019). In double-quantum-dot device encoded as a singlet-triplet qubit, we demonstrate, through full configuration interaction calculations, that a range of nearly sweet spots appear in the coupled singlet-triplet qubits under a large enough magnetic field. We further demonstrate that ramping to and from such nearly sweet spots using pulses from shortcut to adiabaticity offers maximal protection of the qubit against decoherence [14]. [14] Charge noise suppression in capacitively coupled singlet-triplet spin qubits under magnetic field, G. X. Chan, J. P. Kestner, and X. Wang, Phys. Rev. B 103, L161409 (2021). Based on supervised learning, we have also developed a method to measure charge noise spectrum [5]. [5] Spin-qubit noise spectroscopy from randomized benchmarking by supervised learning, C. Zhang, and X. Wang, Phys. Rev. A. 99, 042316 (2019). For Task 2, we investigated the qubit control problem in various systems. We studied the minimal decomposition of an arbitrary single-qubit gate and its dependence on the directions of the available control axes, which may suggest ways to shorten and optimize control sequences [6]. [6] Minimal nonorthogonal gate decomposition for qubits with limited control, X.-M. Zhang, J. Li, X. Wang, and M.-H. Yung, Phys. Rev. A 99, 052339 (2019). We have also studied application of geometric quantum gates to control the qubit, which employ geometric phase, a global property that is robust to local fluctuations. We have found that the geometric gates can improve the control fidelities [7,12,16]. [7] Plug-and-play approach to nonadiabatic geometric quantum gates, B.-J. Liu, X.-K. Song, Z.-Y. Xue, X. Wang, and M.-H. Yung, Phys. Rev. Lett. 123, 100501 (2019). [12] High-fidelity geometric gate for silicon-based spin qubits, C. Zhang, T. Chen, S. Li, X. Wang, and Z.-Y. Xue, Phys. Rev. A 101, 052302 (2020). [16] Implementation of geometric quantum gates on microwave-driven semiconductor charge qubits, C. Zhang, T. Chen, X. Wang, and Z.-Y. Xue, Adv. Quantum Technol. 2021, 2100011 (2021). We also tried to use machine learning techniques to quantum control problems. Using neural networks and supervised learning, we are able to efficiently generate robust single-qubit gates for singlet-triplet spin qubits [1]. [1] Neural-network-designed pulse sequences for robust control of singlet-triplet qubits, X.-C. Yang, M.-H. Yung, and X. Wang, Phys. Rev. A 97, 042324 (2018). We then focused on the reinforcement learning technique. We applied the reinforcement learning to study the transfer of a spin state on a 1d chain and found that reinforcement learning can improve the speed limit [3]. We have also made a detailed comparison between reinforcement learning techniques and other traditional methods and found that reinforcement learning is more adaptive and may be more efficient in certain situations [10]. [3] Automatic spin-chain learning to explore the quantum speed limit, X.-M. Zhang, Z.-W. Cui, X. Wang, and M.-H. Yung, Phys. Rev. A 97, 052333 (2018). [10] When does reinforcement learning stand out in quantum control? A comparative study on state preparation, X.-M. Zhang, Z. Wei, R. Asad, X.-C. Yang, and X. Wang, npj Quantum Inf. 5, 85 (2019). We also studied a related quantum control problem, namely the quantum parameter estimation. We compared results from reinforcement learning and traditional gradient-based techniques and found that the method from reinforcement learning is more generalizable, i.e. a neural network trained at one parameter value can be straightforwardly extended to other values, implying a higher efficiency compared to conventional gradient-based methods under certain situations [9]. In a follow-up paper, we studied the problem of quantum estimation of multiple parameters, introducing an analytical method which, starting from an initial optimal control, can be efficiently generalized to treat an ensemble of system with parameters varying in ranges. We have also discussed the generalizability of reinforcement learning on the problem. Compared to previous gradient-based methods which has to be re-run for each set of new parameters, our method is much more efficient and practical [15]. [9] Generalizable control for quantum parameter estimation through reinforcement learning, H. Xu, J. Li, L. Liu, Y. Wang, H. Yuan, and X. Wang, npj Quantum Inf. 5, 82 (2019). [15] Generalizable control for multiparameter quantum metrology, H. Xu, L. Wang, H. Yuan, and X. Wang, Phys. Rev. A 103, 042615 (2021). One of the major challenges in the NISQ era is the lack of a general error mitigation technique demanding minimal additional resources. In [13] we developed a protocol to mitigate error using quantum autoencoders, that is particularly useful in the NISQ era, as it does not require extra qubits, can be applied to different types of noise models and quantum data, and is more powerful than existing techniques in many situations. [13] Generic detection-based error mitigation using quantum autoencoders, X.-M. Zhang, W. Kong, M. U. Farooq, M.-H. Yung, G. Guo, and X. Wang, Phys. Rev. A 103, L040403 (2021).

11303617.label: Major findings and research outcome
11303617.value: 1. We studied how the gate crosstalk and leakage can be suppressed in triple-quantum-dot system [2]. We proposed ways to improve the fidelity of barrier-controlled triple-quantum-dot charge qubit [4]. We have also shown that the geometric arrangement affects the control fidelity and a triangular arrangement can largely suppress the leakage for a charge qubit in triple quantum dots [11]. 2. Through full configuration interaction calculations, we have found that a range of nearly sweet spots appear in the coupled singlet-triplet qubits under a large enough magnetic field, a regime where the charge noise can be substantially suppressed [14]. 3. We studied the minimal decomposition of an arbitrary single-qubit gate and its dependence on the directions of available control axes, which can be used to shorten and optimize the control pulse sequences [6]. 4. We studied the application of geometric quantum gates to quantum-dot-based qubits, and we demonstrated their power to suppress noises and improve the control fidelities [7,12,16]. 5. We applied machine learning to quantum control problems. We used supervised learning to generate noise-compensating pulses and found that their efficacy is comparable to traditional techniques [1]. We have found that reinforcement learning can improve the quantum speed limit in transferring a spin state on a 1d chain [3]. We have also found that reinforcement learning is more adaptive and can find the optimal solution more efficiently in certain problems [10]. 6. In the quantum estimation of a single parameter, we have found that reinforcement learning is more generalizable, and is therefore more efficient in treating massive measurements [9]. This generalizability mostly persists in the case of estimating multiple parameters [15]. 7. We developed a protocol to mitigate error using quantum autoencoders, which is particularly useful for NISQ devices as it does not require extra qubits, can be applied to different types of noise models and data, and is more powerful than existing techniques in many situations [13].

11303617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11303617.value: Several research directions warrant further study. First, the search for high-fidelity quantum gates, especially those for two or multiple qubits, is of crucial importance to the realization of quantum algorithms. We can use the experience we gained in this project and expand to two or more qubits. Second, geometric quantum computation has become a hot field due to its intrinsic resistance to local noises. In future work, we would like to further study how the geometric gates can be better applied to quantum-dot-based systems. Third, we would like to apply the reinforcement learning technique, as an efficient optimization algorithm, to a wider range of problems related to quantum control and quantum sensing, such as quantum hypothesis testing.

11303617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11303617.value: In this project, we studied several theoretical aspects related to quantum control of quantum-dot spin qubits, especially those based on silicon. We have found ways to improve the control accuracy on various systems, and we have also studied factors affecting the gate error, such as the arrangement of different quantum dots. We have also studied how geometric quantum gates, a family of quantum gates based on geometric phases that are global and are naturally robust against local noises, can be applied to quantum-dot systems. We further used machine learning techniques to quantum control problems and have found that the reinforcement learning can be advantageous in many ways as compared with traditional methods in a wide range of problems including quantum state preparation, quantum state transfer, and quantum parameter estimation.

11304017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11304017.value: Maxwell 算子 - 包含curl-curl算子并满足divergence-free条件, 在time-harmonic Maxwell 方程, 不可压缩磁流体方程中，起到重要的作用. 对Maxwell 算子的数值逼近，一般有下面这些缺点. 一些缺乏局部守恒律并且编程困难(H(curl)-confomring 有限元)，一些全局变量太多(Discontinuous Galerkin methods). P.I. 的长期目标是发展，在理论上和实际计算上，对于Maxwell 算子提供高效和稳定的数值计算方法，来克服上面提到的两个存在的缺点. P.I.的工作将会有助于发展真对time-harmonic Maxwell方程，不可压缩磁流体方程的高效的科学计算方法. 在这个课题中， P.I. 将集中工作在一种新的科学计算方法 - 可杂交化间断Galerkin方法. 因为可杂交化间断Galerkin方法使用间断有限元空间，所以具有局部守恒律并且编程比 H(curl)-conforming 有限元明显容易，尤其是使用高阶多项式的时候. 同时，可杂交化间断Galerkin方法的全局变量和H(curl)-conforming 有限元的在一个数量级上. 这些性质使得可杂交化间断Galerkin方法很适合来数值求解包含Maxwell算子的方程组.

11304017.label: Realisation of objectives
11304017.value: The goals of this project has been achieved successfully. I have published 9 research papers based on this project. I have listed all these 9 papers in Part C: research output. In paper 1 in Part C, an HDG method has been developed and analysed to achieve objective 1 successfully. The title of paper 1 is ``A priori and computable a posteriori error estimates for an HDG method for the coercive Maxwell equations". In papers 2, 4, 5 (``Parameter-free superconvergent H(div)-conforming HDG methods for the Brinkman equations", ``A Mixed DG method and an HDG method for incompressible magnetohydrodynamics", ``Convergence of a B-E based finite element method for MHD models on Lipschitz domains") in Part C, HDG methods and other related numerical methods are developed and analysed for steady state incompressible MHD equations. I would like to point out that the numerical discretisation of velocity field and pressure of the HDG method in paper 4 is based on the HDG method in paper 2. In papers 3 and 7 (``A semi-implicit energy conserving finite element method for the dynamical incompressible magnetohydrodynamics equations", ``Analysis of a semi-implicit structure-preserving finite element method for the nonstationary incompressible Magnetohydrodynamics equations") in Part C, I introduced and analysed two types of numerical methods for time dependent incompressible MHD equations. All my papers for incompressible MHD equations provide optimal convergence, even then the exact solution has strong singularity and the domain is three dimensional non-convex polyhedron. Thus, object 3 has been achieved completely. In papers 6 and 8 (``Analysis of an interior penalty DG method for the quad-curl problem", ``A Mixed Finite Element Scheme for Quad-Curl Source and Eigenvalue Problems") in Part C, I developed and analysed DG type methods for Quad-Curl source problem and corresponding eigenvalue problem. Thus, papers 6 and 8 help to achieve objective 2. In addition, paper 9 (``A Convergent Post-processed Discontinuous Galerkin Method for Incompressible Flow with Variable Density ") in Part C studies numerical analysis for time dependent incompressible flow with variable density. Paper 9 helps to extend my works on time dependent incompressible MHD to variable density case. Several numerical experiments have been done in most papers to verify my theoretical results.

11304017.label: Major findings and research outcome
11304017.value: I have developed and analysed HDG methods and other related numerical methods for Maxwell operator, time-harmonic Maxwell related equations, and incompressible MHD equations. The methods I developed are more efficient than most existing finite element type methods. I discovered an important L3 norm embedding inequality for discrete magnetic field, which can be useful in other numerical methods solving PDEs with Maxwell operator. I also discovered the interesting discrete H1 norm stability of the Curl of the primary variable of the Quad-Curl problem. Numerical experiments are also provided. Overall, I have published 9 research papers related to this project.

11304017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11304017.value: The discrete H1 norm stability of the Curl of the primary variable of the Quad-Curl problem (mentioned in 6.1) can be useful in numerical analysis of electromagnetic scattering problems. In addition, my paper (paper 9 in Part C) helps to develop and analyse numerical methods for time dependent incompressible MHD equations with variable density.

11304017.value: The numerical methods I developed for Maxwell operators and related research problems are more efficient than most existing finite element type methods. They will help to simulate models with Maxwell operators in a reliable and efficient way.
