11304117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11304117.value: A bound state in the continuum (BIC) is a localized or trapped mode with a frequency in the frequency interval where outgoing radiation modes exist. Mathematically, a BIC corresponds to a discrete eigenvalue in the continuous spectrum. For periodic structures surrounded by homogeneous media, the BICs are guided modes above the lightline, and they can be either standing waves or propagating Bloch modes. Recently, BICs for electromagnetic and light waves have attracted much attention since they have very interesting properties, can be used to enhance nonlinear and quantum optical effects, and have potentially significant applications in lasing, sensing, optical switching, light storage, etc. However, there are limitations in the current theoretical understanding of the BICs, and their applications have not been fully explored. In this project, we study BICs on periodic structures from three different aspects: theory, numerical computation, and applications. We intend to develop a perturbation theory to understand the robustness of BICs with respect to their underlying symmetries. We also plan to develop an accurate and reliable numerical method for computing the BICs. Applications of the BICs will be explored based on the discontinuities of transmission and reflection coefficients and the total transmission/reflection phenomena, the arbitrarily strong field enhancement by resonances near BICs, and the nonuniqueness of related diffraction problems. 連續譜中的綁定狀態（BIC）是一種局部化的特解，其頻率在外向輻射解的頻率區間之內。數學上，BIC對應連續譜中的離散特徵值。在週期結構上，BIC可以是駐波，也可以是行波。近期，光波的BIC受到了廣泛的注意。這是因為BIC有很多奇特的性質，可用來加強非線性光學或量子光學的效應，在激光，傳感，光學開關，光的存儲等領域中都有應用。但是，目前有關BIC的理論尚有很多不足。在此研究計劃中，我們將對週期結構上的BIC進行理論，計算和應用三方面的研究。我們將應用攝動方法來研究BIC的魯棒性及其同對稱性的關係，也將開發有效快速的方法來計算BIC。關於BIC的應用，我們將從三個方面來研究：傳播和反射係數的間斷性，任意大的近場增強，及衍射問題的不唯一性。

11304117.label: Realisation of objectives
11304117.value: The first objective is to develop theories, related to symmetry and robustness, for bound states in the continuum (BICs). The objective is fully achieved. The theories on BICs are developed in papers 1, 8, 11 and 12 (as in Part C). The second objective is to develop efficient numerical methods for computing BICs. The objective is fully achieved. Since a BIC is a special resonant mode with an infinite Q factor. We have developed new and efficient numerical methods for scattering and resonant modes in papers 3, 4, 6. The third objective is about applications of BICs. The objective is achieved. We make contributions on two topics (related to the applications). One is field enhancement, and in other is harmonic generation, in papers 9 and 10.

11304117.label: Major findings and research outcome
11304117.value: In paper 1, "Bound states in the continuum on periodic structures surrounded by strong resonances", we found that in dielectric periodic structures which have a reflection symmetry in the periodic direction, there can be symmetric BICs that are not protected by symmetry, but have a very useful property, namely, the Q factors of the nearby resonances scale like 1/k^4, instead of 1/k^2, where k is the wavenumber of the resonant mode. This implies that the Q factor can be very large, even when k is not very small. A large Q factor implies the resonance effect is strong, and that is useful in many applications. In paper 8, "Bound states with complex frequencies near the continuum on lossy periodic structures", we studied how a small material loss will affect the BICs. It turns out those BICs with nonzero wave vectors will be destroyed by a small loss, while those with a zero wave vectors can remain as complex BICs (which do not radiate power). This finding has practical implications for applications based on these two different types of BICs. In paper 11, "Perturbation theories for symmetry-protected bound states in the continuum on two-dimensional periodic structures", we studies how symmetry-protected BICs are destroyed by perturbations that break the required symmetry. We identified different possibilities, so that the BICs become resonances with Q factor scale differently with the magnitude of the perturbation. The finding gives guidance for designing the symmetry-breaking structures that have the desired resonances. In paper 12, "Parametric dependence of bound states in the continuum on periodic structures", we studied how BICs depend on structural parameters. For certain cases, we show that even though a BIC can be destroyed by a generic structural perturbation, it can be recovered if we add another generic perturbation with a properly chosen magnitude. Since many photonics structures are "locally separable", we have developed a special method, called vertical mode expansion method, and demonstrated its effectiveness in paper 6, "Computing resonant modes of circular cylindrical resonators by vertical mode expansions".

11304117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11304117.value: Many applications of BICs have been proposed by researchers in the photonics community. It is worthwhile to have a better understanding on the many practical aspects (such as fabrication errors, finite size, non-periodicity) in these applications.

11304117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11304117.value: Light can propagate in an optical waveguide as a guided mode, but usually, only when the frequency and the wave vector satisfy the condition so that it must decay exponentially away from the waveguide core. In structures that are infinite in at least in one direction, a bound state in the continuum (BIC) is a guided mode, but for its frequency and waveguide, waves can propagate to or from infinity. It is even more useful to regard a BIC as a special resonant mode with an infinite quality factor (Q factor). High-Q resonances gives rise to field enhancement and other properties that are useful for sensing, leasing, switch, nonlinear optics, etc. Our study clarifies how BICs are preserved or destroyed by structural or wave vector perturbations, and can help to realize is practical applications of the BICs. We also analysed a nonlinear optics application of the BICs, namely, the fourth harmonic generation.

11304517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11304517.value: Knowledge of urban winds is crucial to applications in air quality and pollutant dispersion. Yet despite advances in our ability to forecast large-scale winds, wind profiles cannot be determined quickly and accurately for arbitrary urban geometries. Existing theoretical predictions do not apply to the important limit of tall, closely packed buildings or generalise to realistic geometries. Downscaling of large-scale winds is inaccurate. Building-resolving numerical simulations are computationally expensive. An alternative strategy is to develop a simplified but accurate model of urban winds by exploiting the close connection between the velocity and the vorticity or local rotation. Recent results demonstrate that the flow regime, or qualitative structure of the velocity field, can be predicted from the vorticity at the roof and pedestrian levels of a street canyon. This proposal hypothesizes that the mean winds inside deep urban canopies are also controlled by thin and intense layers of vorticity that form near solid boundaries. Strong spatial localisation of the vorticity yields a reduced mathematical description and fast numerical solutions. The aim of this proposal is to develop a new method for estimating wind profiles inside deep urban canopies. This will be achieved by applying techniques for vorticity-dominated flows and extending recent work on the prediction of street-canyon flow regimes. (i) Reduced models of the vorticity field inside idealised and realistic street canyons will be derived from large-eddy simulation data. (ii) The velocity field implied by each vortex sheet or layer will be obtained from the numerical solution of a boundary-value problem and urban wind data provided by the Hong Kong Observatory. (iii) A velocity profile valid for the entire canopy will be constructed by matching. This proposal addresses an important unsolved problem. It will deepen understanding of winds in urban areas by highlighting the role of vorticity layers and boundaries. The underlying method offers enormous computational savings over computational fluid dynamics and will improve the accuracy of operational air quality and dispersion models. 城市風的知識對空氣質量和污染物擴散的應用至關重要。然而，儘管我們預測大尺度風場的能力有所提高，但是對於任意城市幾何形狀，卻不能快速準確地確定其風廓線。現有的理論預測不適用於高大密集的建築體或者真實的建築物形狀。對大型風降尺度的方法尚不准確的。建築物尺度級精度的數值模擬其計算量龐大。 一種替代策略是通過利用速度與渦度或局部旋轉流之間的緊密聯繫來開發預測城市風的簡化但準確的模型。最近的結果表明，可以從街谷的屋頂高度和行人高度的渦流特性對流型或速度場的定性結構進行預測。該提案假設深城市冠層內的平均風場也受到形成在固體邊界附近的薄而強烈的渦流邊界層的控制。渦流的強空間性有助於簡化數學描述從而快速獲得數值解。 該提案的目的是開發一種估算深城市冠層內風廓線的新方法。將通過應用適用於以渦度為主導流的技術以及對最近關於街谷流型預測工作的擴展來實現。（i） 理想化和實際街谷內的渦度場的簡化模型將由過大渦模擬數據進行推導。 （ii）每個渦流層所反應的流場將通過邊界值問題和香港天文台提供的城市風向數據的數值解來獲得。 （iii）通過匹配構建適用於整個冠層的速度分佈。 該提案解決一個重要但尚未解決的問題。通過強調渦流層和邊界的作用加深對城市風的認識。其核心方法將大量節省計算流體動力學的計算量，並將提高空氣質量和污染物擴散應用模型的準確性。

11304517.label: Realisation of objectives
11304517.value: The objectives were realised as follows: 1. Devise reduced vortex-sheet models of the vorticity field inside urban canopies Vortex-sheet models were defined from analysis of the time-averaged vorticity fields simulated by building-resolving computational fluid dynamics (i.e., with Large-eddy Simulation or Improved Delayed Detached Eddy Simulation). In particular, the spatial distribution of the vorticity components was examined in order to determine whether the vorticity is spatially localised. For most of the geometries (shallow, step-up and step-down canyons, realistic urban neighbourhood), vortex sheets may be defined at solid surfaces. In the case of realistic neighbourhoods, variations of the vorticity on the scale of buildings or facades are ignored, i.e., uniform vortex sheets are assumed. For deep canyons, in which there are multiple vortices, a middle vortex sheet may be introduced. For stratified flow generated by bottom heating or cooling, the arrangement of vortex sheet follows that for the single street canyon. 2. Predict wind profiles throughout the canopy Mean wind profiles were calculated from the vortex sheets by obtaining numerical solutions (Green's functions) for the corresponding Poisson equation of vortex dynamics. This is an extension of previous work on the prediction of flow regimes as a function of the aspect ratio. Reference basis functions for the different components and vortex sheets were obtained by spatial averaging and calibration; mean profiles then followed via linear superposition. Results for different wind directions were obtained after initialisation, i.e., by prescribing the vortex sheet strengths for the meteorological conditions under consideration. For the realistic neighbourhoods, the sensitivity to the number of additional sidewall or middle vortex sheets was examined. The profiles were compared to reference profiles calculated by computational fluid dynamics (CFD). 3. Characterise the influence of the building geometry on the mean flow The accuracy of the mean flow predictions for different geometries, wind directions and stratifications was compared. In particular, the relationship between the accuracy and the assumptions underlying the method, namely spatial localisation of the vorticity and weak nonlinearity or turbulence, was examined. Since the vortex method assumes linear vortex dynamics, accuracy is expected to suffer for shallower canyons (stronger turbulence), realistic domains (weaker localisation of the vorticity) and stratified flow (mean flow cannot be completely described by the vorticity). By examining the assumptions on which the method is based, the method's real-world applicability was assessed. The objectives were fully achieved. In particular: 1. Devise reduced vortex-sheet models of the vorticity field inside deep urban canopies. For a unit-aspect-ratio street canyon, the dominant contributions are made by the top and bottom vortex sheets (of streamwise vorticity) and sidewall vortex sheets (of vertical vorticity) [1]. Contributions from other vorticity components and vortex sheets is generally small. The same arrangement extends to other wind directions as well as to similar geometries, e.g. small courtyards. For more complicated geometries, i.e. asymmetric or deep canyons and realistic urban domains, additional vortex sheets are introduced [2] because the flow is inhomogeneous. In particular, middle vortex sheets are placed between upper and lower vortices or at the top of each building cluster, while additional sidewall vortex sheets are located within canyons. With manual intervention, the vortex sheets can be determined for arbitrary domains. 2. Predict wind profiles throughout the canopy. Mean wind profiles were calculated for many different cases. Not only is relatively good agreement obtained with idealised cases such as a unit-aspect-ratio street canyon with a wind perpendicular to the canyon axis [1], similar agreement is obtained for other wind directions and more realistic cases such as shallow, deep and asymmetric (step-up and step-down) canyons [2]. For realistic urban topography, accuracy improves with additional vortex sheets, but satisfactory agreement is already obtained with a basic set comprised of top and bottom vortex sheets only. Accuracy is notably compromised only for unstable stratification; however, the basic trends are captured (e.g., the relative error doubles for strongly unstable stratification but the normalised absolute error remains small). It was shown that the vortex method is robust and of wide applicability. In fact, the method was tested for a wider range of cases than specified in the revised objectives. 3. Characterise the influence of the building geometry on the mean flow. Despite the wide range of building geometries considered in this work, minimal sensitivity to the building geometry is found. This is true even when the assumptions underlying the method do not hold, i.e., the turbulent kinetic energy increasing significantly through the canopy or the spatial localisation of the vorticity being degraded. The implication is that the applicability of the vortex method is wider than that of linear vortex dynamics.

11304517.label: Major findings and research outcome
11304517.value: 1. We introduced a new, computationally efficient method for predicting mean wind profiles within urban canopies [1]. Drawing on linear vortex dynamics and previous work by the PI on the prediction of flow regimes as a function of the aspect ratio, spatially averaged profiles of the horizontal velocity components can be predicted by approximating the vorticity field with discrete vortex sheets for the top, bottom and side walls, solving 3-D Poisson equations, and summing over the calibrated basis functions. The method is significantly faster than building-resolving CFD. 2. The method works well for the benchmark case of a unit-aspect-ratio street canyon (with and without side streets) for constant density and wind directions between 0 and 90 degrees [2]. The relative pointwise error is around 30% and the absolute error (normalised by the roof-level wind speed) is less than 1%. The agreement is much better than can be obtained with standard analytical models such as the exponential, log or power-law profiles. 3. The method generalises to other geometries (shallow, step-up, step-down and realistic urban canyons) and to stratified flow [2]. These are non-trivial extensions that demonstrate the method's applicability to real cities. Nevertheless, accuracy remains comparable to that for the idealised case of a unit-aspect-ratio street canyon. 4. The performance of the method is surprisingly good as the assumption of linear vortex dynamics does not hold equally well in all cases. The turbulent kinetic energy (TKE) within the canopy is several times larger for unstable flow or a shallow canyon, yet the accuracy is largely unaffected, while the vorticity may not be localised at the walls when there is complex geometry; the vorticity cannot provide a complete description of the velocity field for stratified flow. A likely explanation is that mean wind profiles within urban canopies are relatively insensitive to details of the building geometry. Contributions from a continuous vorticity distribution or an increase in the TKE are lost in the spatial average. Stable stratification also has little effect on the mean wind profiles, likely because linear waves vanish under temporal or spatial averaging, but unstable stratification could have a stronger effect. 5. A fast dispersion model based on the vortex method has been developed [3]. For a regular building array, it yields a more accurate prediction than the classical Gaussian plume solution, which neglects the influence of obstacles.

11304517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11304517.value: In this project, a robust and surprisingly accurate method for predicting wind profiles within urban canopies was developed and tested. Future efforts will focus on applications and extensions of the method. Although the vortex method is not a replacement for a building-resolving CFD, it can serve an attractive alternative for applications in which computational efficiency is crucial and neither the three-dimensional structure nor the time dependence of the velocity field are required. Examples include the extrapolation of in situ measurements and the generation of inflow wind profiles or data for machine learning applications. Given that the method has been extensively tested [2] and already used for a fast dispersion model [3], there are strong reasons for believing that such applications would be successful. Application to arbitrary domains would be facilitated by the development of a systematic procedure for defining vortex sheets. The relative importance of arbitrary vortex sheets can be straightforwardly evaluated prior to calibration and prediction, as was done for a single street canyon. Furthermore, calibration techniques for sparse observational data may developed by extend the existing method for one-point data [1].

11304517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11304517.value: Mean wind profiles are required for many applications. For example, they are needed for both air quality and meteorological modelling and wind engineering. Within cities, however, simple mathematical models do not apply close to the ground because they neglect the play role played by buildings. An alternative approach was developed in this project. By assuming that the velocity field as a whole is controlled by regions where the velocity varies rapidly in space (typically found near walls or solid surfaces), fast but accurate predictions can be made. Predictions can be made in seconds using a standard desktop computer, while standard techniques for predicting winds within urban areas are thousands of times slower and require powerful computers with many computational cores. The method has been tested for many different directions and urban geometries, with surprisingly good agreement for more realistic configurations (e.g. actual Hong Kong neighbourhoods). Given the importance of mean wind profiles to the numerical modelling of urban areas, there is considerable scope for future applications. A fast pollutant dispersion model has already been developed. The generation of site-specific data for other methods, e.g. initial guesses for statistical or machine learning models, represents an intriguing future direction.

11304617.label: Project Objectives

11304617.label: Realisation of objectives
11304617.value: The project has been completed and all objectives have been achieved, resulting in several publications. One research student has been trained under this project. Objective 1: Several new classes of binuclear complexes and multinuclear assemblies supported by Schiff base ligands have been designed and successfully prepared. By applying the proposed ‘shape-persistent bimetallic design’ approach, binuclear systems tethered by an inert, rigid anchor component have been developed that incorporate the following features: 1) M–M interactions would be precluded, and coordinative unsaturation conserved, by the inflexible backbone and the incorporation of bulky substituents, and 2) variations in molecular conformations are essentially limited to axial rotation of the M-salphen moieties, yet such rotations can crucially enable subtle tuning of intermetallic distances and geometry. The creation of a tunable, convergent reaction space, capable of supporting enhanced reactivity and cooperativity, has been realized. Multinuclear shape-persistent assemblies featuring M-salphen moieties that undergo helical folding and intrachain stacking have been developed. A wide variety of anchor groups linking the bis-(M-salphen) moiety (including xanthene, dibenzofuran, m-mesityl, p-tetramethylbenzene) has been employed, in order to modify and control the spatial arrangement and mutual orientation (“topology”) of the cofacial M-salphen units, and the capacity of the resultant frameworks for binding and activation of small molecules has been investigated. Objective 2: The newly developed bi- and multinuclear assemblies have been characterized and probed by spectroscopic, crystallographic and computational methods. The molecular structures of several key catalysts have been elucidated by X-ray crystallography, and the relative geometries of the M-salphen units as well as the intermetallic distances have been evaluated and correlated with catalytic reactivity and behavior. Importantly, kinetic studies and DFT calculations have been employed to investigate reaction mechanisms and the possibility of cooperative reactivity. Kinetic studies using in-situ (React-IR) spectroscopy have been undertaken to probe the reaction mechanism for coupling of carbon dioxide and epoxide, revealing the existence of an intramolecular rate component and thus cooperative reactivity for di-Zn catalysts. DFT calculations have been performed to investigate the cooperative mechanism and probe different reaction pathways, namely an intramolecular process inside the cavity involving cooperating Zn centers, and a reaction occurring on the exterior of the cavity. The relative energies of the transition states for the former are revealed to be generally lower, thus indicating kinetic preference for an intramolecular, cooperative pathway involving the secondary Zn site; namely, transition states depicting: 1) Zn...iodide coordination leading to accelerated ring opening, and 2) a ring-closure (back-biting) process facilitated by Zn...O(carbonate) coordination, are found. Hence, the combined kinetics/DFT results provide strong evidence of bimetallic cooperativity in these catalysts. Objective 3: The ability of the newly developed binuclear complexes to catalyze coupling reactions and activation of small molecules such as carbon dioxide have been extensively examined. The strategy of modifying the structure and connectivity of these frameworks, in order to create bimetallic cavities as well as adjust their attendant catalytic reactivity, has been explored. In particular, catalytic coupling of carbon dioxide and epoxides to give organic (cyclic or poly-) carbonates have been investigated. Selected di-zinc catalysts are significantly more active for the production of cyclic carbonate than their mononuclear analogues under identical conditions and concentration of Zn sites. Importantly, notable catalytic performance in terms of exceptional turnover frequencies (up to 29000/h; 14500/h/metal) and high conversion rates under mild reaction conditions (down to 1 bar of carbon dioxide and 55 deg C) have been achieved. Indeed, the elevated turnover frequencies observed approach the benchmark examples in the literature under comparable conditions. For a mesityl-bridged di-zinc system, the intended coupling of carbon dioxide and epoxide afforded a polyether product in addition to the expected cyclic carbonate; such reactivity is unknown for Zn(II) catalysts. The observed results signify that the shape-persistent structures can engender suitable distances and geometries between the bimetallic centers to facilitate synergistic and unusual reactivity, as well as bimetallic cooperativity, in these catalysts.

11304617.label: Major findings and research outcome
11304617.value: A new family of conformationally rigid bis-(Zn-salphen) complexes with a planar bridging component (xanthene or dibenzofuran) have been synthesized. The complexes have been investigated as catalysts for coupling of carbon dioxide with epoxides. Selected dibenzofuran derivatives are significantly more active for the production of cyclic carbonate than their mononuclear analogues under identical conditions and concentration of Zn sites. High initial turnover frequencies (up to 29000/h; 14500/h/metal) and excellent conversion rates under mild conditions (1 bar of carbon dioxide, 55 deg C) have been achieved. Kinetic studies using in-situ (React-IR) spectroscopy and DFT calculations have been performed, which reveal the existence of an intramolecular rate component. Taken in tandem, these results provide strong evidence of cooperative reactivity for these di-zinc catalysts. [Publication 1] Multinuclear shape-persistent assemblies featuring repeating Zn-salphen moieties have been developed. The study of metallopolymers with controllable helical sense remains in its infancy. Arabinose-functionalized (Zn-salphen)-based conjugated polymers have been produced that display mirror-image circular dichroism spectra for L- and D-sugar sidechains respectively, signifying ordered helical coiling of the polymer backbone. The helical folding involves intrachain stacking of Zn-salphen units, and hence the zinc centers are brought together and asymmetric coupling reactions and cooperative reactivity become viable. [Publication 2] Shape-persistent binuclear salphen-cobalt(III) catalysts have been prepared, and the effects of altering the anchoring positions to the salphen units and attaching the salphen-Co moieties to different rigid bridges were examined. The xanthene-based catalysts, which are active for the copolymerization of carbon dioxide and propylene oxide to give poly(propylene carbonate) under mild conditions, display superior efficiencies and enhanced regiochemical control compared with dibenzofuran-bridged and mononuclear analogues. [Publication 3] A new series of bis-(Zn-salphen) complexes based on highly substituted m- and p-terphenyl backbones was developed. These catalysts are active for cyclic carbonate formation from carbon dioxide and epoxides, but for selected derivatives, a conspicuous amount of polyether was also produced. The observation of unusual catalytic reactivity between the Zn2 centers, imposed by the mesityl unit, is noteworthy. [Publication 4] New binuclear cobalt(III) Schiff base complexes derived from a highly substituted p-terphenyl backbone have been developed. Both the syn- and anti-forms of the bimetallic frameworks have been synthesized (as confirmed by crystal structures of synthetic precursors). The syn-catalysts are noticeably more efficient than mononuclear relatives for the copolymerization of propylene oxide and carbon dioxide under mild conditions, and produce poly(propylene carbonate) with high selectivity and narrow polydispersity. [Publication 5]

11304617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11304617.value: Several classes of shape-persistent bimetallic Schiff base complexes, which show the ability to mediate cooperative reactivity, have been devised. Efforts to investigate additional coupling and polymerization reactions, and study the relationship between molecular structure and catalytic behavior, are proposed. Further kinetic (React-IR) experiments to gain mechanistic insights for bimetallic systems are warranted. The intramolecular, cooperative reactivity realized for bis(Zn-salphen) catalysts plays a dominant role in efficiency at low catalyst concentrations, which is important from a practical viewpoint because reduced loadings and consumption of catalysts are clearly desirable. The utilization of abundant, non-toxic Zn is appealing, and the functionalization of salphen ligands (e.g. with nucleophilic pendants to promote epoxide ring-opening) is worthwhile. The capability of the helical metallopolymers bearing Zn-salphen moieties as catalysts for asymmetric coupling reactions should be investigated. These results emphasize that the relative orientation of active sites, and intermetallic separations and geometry, are important for synergistic effects and improved reactivity. This shape-persistent bimetallic design approach can be applicable to catalyst systems that proceed through or invoke cooperative, bimetallic mechanisms. This research paves the way for the further development of shape-persistent multinuclear systems that can mediate novel catalytic reactions with enhanced efficiency and cooperativity.

11304617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11304617.value: Carbon dioxide is a highly appealing C1 feedstock because it is abundant, inexpensive, non-toxic and renewable, and its valorization can reduce waste. The development of efficient catalytic reactions to transform such sustainable resources into valuable chemicals is therefore highly desirable. The organic (cyclic or poly-) carbonate products in this project are of interest as raw materials for drug discovery and battery electrolytes, and as biodegradable polymers. Cooperativity between metal centers in multinuclear frameworks is an established bio-inspired concept in catalyst design, but such reactivity can often be hampered by flexible ligand structures or direct metal-metal interactions. This project has focused on the design, synthesis, and application of shape-persistent binuclear complexes containing cofacial metal-organic subunits that are linked together by a rigid bridging group. Variations in molecular conformation is restricted to axial rotation of the cofacial moieties, but crucially, this permits tuning of intermetallic separations and geometry to potentially improve catalytic reactivity and engender cooperative effects. Novel metallopolymers featuring intrachain stacking of zinc Schiff base moieties have been produced. The development of enhanced catalytic efficiency, unusual reactivity, and bimetallic cooperativity for coupling and polymerization reactions involving carbon dioxide have been achieved.

11304817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11304817.value: 該項目的目的是研究可壓縮噴射流的數學理論，特別關注通過變分法研究噴氣流從半無限長噴嘴噴出的嚴格數學分析。 噴氣流可以通過從孔中平行流出到大氣中的氣體觀察到。在觀察的基礎上，我們假設噴射流和大氣是通過一個間斷面作為邊界分開的。此外，我們考慮定常等熵無旋流，並假定入口處的流體是亞音速的。 關於此類流體的更多的描述可以在Courant-Friedrichs的經典著作（參見[25，p289-290]）中可以找到。此外，射流完全不同於衝擊波，由於噴射流是特徵間斷，即波沿著速度場生成。 因此，作為氣體動力學中的基礎波的一個典型原型，可壓縮射流的數學理論研究將對於自由邊界問題的數學理論做出很大貢獻。 通過變分法研究噴氣流問題有著漫長的歷史。 對於不可壓縮無璇的歐拉流，變分方法由P.R. Guardian，H. Lewy和M. Schiffer首先介紹，用以處理[31]中的軸向對稱繞流。 然後，Alt-Caffarelli-Friedman在[1,2,3]重要作品中做出了顯著發展，並應用於[2]中的噴射流，饒流和帶重力噴流，和[3]中的兩相流體。 另一方面，對於可壓縮流量，據我們所知，關於可壓縮射流的全局存在的結果（參見[4]和[7]）很少。 但是因為可壓縮的噴射流是一個根本而且重要的問題，即使只有很少的結果，這個項目提出的目標是很有價值的。 最近幾年，我們一直進行有關問題研究。 我們建立了二維Rethy流體的適定性理論[22]和 軸對稱的情況[23]; 不可壓縮射流在出口處有各種不同壓力的情況研究[24]; 光滑亞音速歐拉流在無限長管道中的情況[12]; 和可壓縮的兩相流在無限長管道中的情況[19]。 在這個項目中，我們將主要著眼於進一步發展已有的技術，研究上述目標。 在[4]和[7]中，噴流在自由邊界的速度是預先給定以便證明流體是亞音速的。自然入口處的流體沒有給出，並且它由自由邊界上的速度確定。 所以有一個自然的問題是，入口處的流量先行給出怎麼辦。 因此，這裏得到的結果和技術也將更好地了解這個問題。

11304817.label: Realisation of objectives
11304817.value: For the first objective, we first established the existence and uniqueness of compressible subsonic jet flows issuing from the nozzle of arbitrary cross-section, and then for the case that the pressure is given at the outlet, jet flows in a de Laval nozzle with smooth detachment. For the second object, we established the existence and uniqueness of the Rethy flows in two dimensions and in three dimensions (under the asymmetric setting). For the third objective, we established two-phase fluids in the collision of inviscid fluids effluxing from two nozzles, jet flows in a de Laval nozzle with smooth detachment(it can be regarded as a cavitational flow too), the two-dimensional steady supersonic exothermically reacting Euler flows with strong contact discontinuity over a Lipschitz wall, and steady Euler flows with large vorticity and characteristic discontinuities in arbitrary infinitely long nozzles.

11305317.label: Realisation of objectives
11305317.value: In this project, fundamental understanding of the cerium redox reaction was attained by combining electrochemical analysis and DFT calculation. The impact of ligand on equilibrium potential, mass transport and charge transfer of cerium in mixed media was explored by EIS, which was theoretically interpreted by the DFT results. Additionally, diverse cerium-based flow batteries were developed with different negative electrolytes to investigate the influence of flow rate and to increase the energy density. Binary metal modification was also introduced to enhance the stability of graphite felt electrode employed in cerium electrolyte. With the completion of this project, we have 1) demonstrated the influence of supporting electrolyte, state of charge (SOC) and temperature on the solubility and stability of aqueous cerium solution; 2) illustrated the impact of ligand, concentration and SOC on the reaction kinetics of cerium redox couple on glassy carbon electrode (GCE); 3) investigated the influence of supporting acid and temperature on carbon-based electrode stability. The high reaction potential of cerium leads to high voltage of flow battery, while the low solubility in sulfuric acid limits the energy density improvement of cerium-based flow battery. Although methanesulfonic acid (MSA) or mixed media as supporting electrolyte increase the solubility of cerium, the reaction kinetics in these media are not fully understood. Further, the stability of carbon-based electrode poses a concern in high-voltage applications, particularly for Ce(IV) and high operating temperature (60 °C). Thus, the project aims to understand the solubility, stability and reaction kinetics of cerium in MSA-based electrolyte, which is crucial for the further enhancement of high-voltage and high-energy-density flow battery with electrochemical and thermal stability. Since the solubility of Ce(III) decreases and Ce(IV) increases along with MSA concentration, pure Ce(III) (SOC=0) and Ce(IV) (SOC=1) were employed separately to examine the solubility and stability, where the optimal MSA concentration for the two species was found to be 3.5 M, achieving stable 1.0 M cerium electrolyte at room temperature and 60 °C beyond one month. Such optimal electrolyte was also utilized in charge-discharge cycles of full battery at different current densities, where no precipitation occurred, implying good stability of cerium at all SOCs. Thus, the impact of medium, SOC and temperature was illustrated, achieving the first objective. The second objective is to evaluate the reaction kinetics of cerium on GCE at different conditions of supporting electrolyte and SOC. MSA, sulfuric acid, and their mixed media at a range of ratios were adopted as supporting electrolytes to study their impact on equilibrium potential, diffusion coefficient and standard rate constant of cerium redox reaction. Further, a range of SOCs of 0.1-0.9 was used for studying the dependence of these reaction behaviors on SOC. Electrochemical measurements of cyclic voltammetry (CV), Tafel plot, and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) were utilized to investigate the potential window, equilibrium potential and reaction kinetics of Ce(III)/Ce(IV), respectively. Since different impedance curves were observed on the pristine and activated GCEs, the reaction kinetics were investigated on both electrodes. The equilibrium potential was also calculated using density functional theory (DFT) to theoretically explain the influence of different ligands on the redox reaction of cerium complexes. Meanwhile, the calculated activation energy indicated the adiabatic nature of the cerium redox reaction. The carbon-based electrodes of GCE and graphite felt were found unstable in the cerium electrolyte with MSA as supporting electrolyte during CV cycling. While the current density for both pristine GCE and heat-treated graphite felt decreased with cycling, it increased on pristine graphite felt. However, these changes did not occur in the supporting electrolyte of sulfuric acid, demonstrating the impact of acid on electrode stability. Additionally, GCE stability was found limited at high temperature of 60 °C, resulting in exfoliation after CV cycling. Moreover, the current density changes on GCE were distinguished at different potential windows. The results demonstrated the dependence of carbon electrode stability on carbon oxidized state, acid medium, applied voltage and temperature, achieving the third objective.

11305317.label: Major findings and research outcome
11305317.value: In the reaction kinetics study of cerium in mixed media, pristine GCE was observed to be oxidized in both CV and EIS measurements, leading to unstable current-voltage and Nyquist curves, respectively. However, the oxidization was completed after twenty CV cycles, following which the charge transfer resistance was significantly decreased. Thus, an in-situ electrochemical treatment was proposed to activate GCE to provide guidance for achieving consistent results in electrochemical measurements. Compared to pristine electrode, reduced charge transfer resistance and increased double-layer capacitance were observed on activated GCE due to the increased content of oxygen functional groups. Meanwhile, carbon oxidation also occurred in impedance measurement on pristine GCE, indicating an impact on the accuracy of electrochemical studies. Furthermore, a comprehensive understanding of the effect of mixed media (MSA and sulfuric acid) on the cerium redox reaction was gained via the investigation of reaction kinetics on activated GCE in dilute cerium solutions. Both electron transfer and diffusion processes were enhanced in lower sulfuric acid concentration, where smaller cerium complexes dominated. The optimal concentration of MSA, however, was 2.0 M for high exchange current density. Considering the impact of MSA concentration on cerium solubility, 3.0 M MSA is recommended for achieving higher concentration with comparable reaction kinetics. The equilibrium potential of the cerium reaction in MSA was higher compared to sulfuric acid, implying larger discharge voltage and higher energy density. Meanwhile, electron transfer can be accelerated by the sulfate additive for enhancing the power density. (Ref. 1: Electrochimica Acta, 2019, 315, 1-8) To theoretically interpret the impact of different ligands on reaction kinetics, the effect of mixed ligands (methanesulfonate and sulfate) on cerium redox reaction was studied in aqueous electrolyte by DFT and EIS, where the DFT study complemented the experiments of complexes geometries and reaction energy barriers at molecular level. The DFT results provided a clear understanding of the reacting complexes, and their reorganization during the electron transfer of Ce(III)/Ce(IV) redox step, which explained the change in open circuit potential with increasing MSA concentration. Further, the activation energy of redox couples with different ligands was estimated, denoting that any difference in the reactivity of different Ce(IV) complex species should result from orbital overlap. Additionally, the exchange current densities on platinum and gold electrodes were in the same magnitude as that on GCE, demonstrating the adiabatic nature of the cerium redox reaction. Combining the experimental and theoretical results, the reaction was found to be at or close to the adiabatic limit, indicating the impossibility of effective catalysis without changing the reaction mechanism. (Ref. 4: Electrochimica Acta, 2021, 368, 137601). The reaction kinetics of cerium electrolyte was adopted in developing the numerical model of vanadium-cerium flow battery, where two innovative measures of lifetime and energy density of the battery were proposed: SOC deviation and flow efficiency (Ref. 2: Electrochimica Acta, 2019, 328, 135019). Due to the high reaction potential of cerium, it was utilized as the positive electrolyte in a novel hybrid flow battery, benefitting the energy density (Ref. 3: Journal of Power Sources Advances, 2020, 4, 100018). Moreover, the stability of heat-treated graphite felt was limited in cerium electrolyte. Thus, to enhance the stability of this commonly utilized electrode, binary metal modification was studied, achieving high voltage efficiency of 81.93% at 150 mA cm-2 and stable charge-discharge for 100 cycles (Ref. 5: Journal of Materials Chemistry A, 2021, Accepted Manuscript).

11305317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11305317.value: The fundamental knowledge of the cerium reaction in acidic media on carbon-based electrode has been gained via the incorporation of electrochemical analysis and DFT calculation. However, further research on the solvation of redox species and reaction kinetics on different carbon electrode is required to gain comprehensive understanding of cerium reaction and broadly deploy the cerium-based flow battery. The coordination forms of cerium with methanesulfonate ligands in dilute and concentrated MSA can be further calculated to estimate the reaction behavior affected by the solvation and desolvation steps. Since the limited solubility of cerium cannot satisfy practical application in flow battery, combining with other redox couples, such as V(IV)/V(V), in the positive electrolyte can further increase the energy density. Accordingly, the interaction of two or multiple redox couples should be investigated. The effect of mixed MSA and sulfuric acid media has been theoretically studied, aiding the interpretation of reaction kinetics. Further investigation on the solubility and diffusion coefficients of cerium complexes, the viscosity of the electrolytes, and the reaction mechanisms in concentrated cerium solutions are recommended. In addition to GCE, graphite electrode should be employed to compare the reaction kinetics for illustrating the impact of electrode lattice structure on the redox reaction.

11305317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11305317.value: Flow battery is promising as large-scale energy storage system for renewable energy resources due to the merits of non-flammable electrolyte, easy scale-up and long lifetime. For a given energy capacity, the energy density of a flow battery determines the volume requirement. The output voltage correlates positively with energy density, which is dominated by the reaction potential of redox species in electrolyte. Thus, cerium with high redox potential is utilized in the positive electrolyte. On the other hand, the low solubility of cerium in the commonly used supporting electrolyte of sulfuric acid restricts the energy density, where methanesulfonic acid significantly enhances the solubility and potential. Another key criterion of flow battery is power density, which is affected by the electrode size and membrane. The power density depends on the rate of redox reaction at the electrode-electrolyte interface. Therefore, it is crucial to investigate the impact of electrode and electrolyte on the cerium reaction kinetics. Moreover, carbon-based electrode is stable and low-cost and thus promising for large-scale application. Since the operating conditions of high voltage, oxidizing Ce(IV) and acid medium can be a challenge for the electrode lifetime, evaluation of the impact of these factors on carbon stability is of necessity.

11305617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11305617.value: Noble metal nanoclusters (NCs) are tiny colloidal nanoparticles composed of a few to some hundreds of atoms, with a metal core size typically less than 2 nm. As well as their small size, they have low toxicity and good biocompatibility and they may exhibit reasonably strong photoluminescence (PL), which makes them potentially useful as bio-labels. Numerous studies on luminescent Au and Ag NCs have already been performed. Compared to these two rather expensive metals, copper is a cheap and earth abundant element. Applications of Cu NCs are still limited by their relatively low emission quantum yield and a lack of detailed understanding of the PL mechanisms. Our recent work (Nanoscale 2016; Adv. Sci. 2016) made a foundation towards two methods to improve the emission quantum yield of Cu NCs to the values exceeding 20%, using a proper ligand treatment and aggregation-induced emission enhancement. In this project, we will capitalize on these initial findings focusing on unraveling the PL mechanisms of Cu NCs by performing advanced optical spectroscopy studies, probing carrier recombination processes and correlating structural and chemical properties of Cu NCs with different sized metal cores, types of ligands, and environments. After revealing the origins of the PL, Cu NCs with high emission quantum yields (exceeding 40%) will be synthesized directly by wet-chemical means, and/or proper post-synthetic treatments will be developed to improve their emission characteristics and optical/chemical stability. This will be achieved by embedding Cu NCs in metal organic frameworks (MOFs) or coating them with thin silica shells. The resulting stable, strongly emissive Cu NCs will be used for the two-photon imaging of biological entities and chemical sensing of explosives.

11305617.label: Realisation of objectives
11305617.value: Orange emitting Cu nanoclusters (NCs) were synthesized using glutathione as both the reduction agent and stabilizer, followed by solvent induced aggregation leading to the emission enhancement. Photoluminescence quantum yields (PL QY) of 24% and 43% in solution and solid state are achieved, respectively. Blue emitting Cu NCs were synthesized by reduction of polyvinylpyrrolidone supported Cu(II) ions using ascorbic acid, followed by surface treatment with sodium citrate which improves both the emission intensity and stability of the clusters, resulting in the PL QY of 14% both in solution and solid state. We then demonstrated a strategy how to improve both the stability and the emission intensity of Cu NCs based on their entrapment into metal-organic frameworks (MOFs). The latter effect reaches 20 times and is ascribed to a confinement-assisted emission enhancement similar to the aggregation induced emission (AIE) of fluorescent species in solution, evidenced by the prolonged emission lifetime. Cu NCs were distributed homogeneously over the entire MOFs structure, as confirmed by combination of structural and elemental mapping studies. Composite polymer films incorporating luminescent copper nanoclusters were fabricated by solution processing of a precursor mixture of polyvinylpyrrolidone, polyvinyl alcohol, a Cu2+ salt and glutathione in water. The formation of Cu NCs took place through chemical reactions of the precursors in a hydrogel network, whose dehydration during the subsequent aging process led to AIE enhancement. Large area (25 cm x 32 cm), flexible, transparent, thermally stable, bright orange emitting films were realized, with the PL QY reaching 30%. The emission of the Cu NCs in these films was attributed to a phosphorescence mechanism, taking place through ligand-to-metal charge transfer followed by a radiative relaxation over a triplet state. We then demonstrated UV shielding properties of composite films which are fabricated using Cu NCs as UV absorbers and cross-linked polyvinyl alcohol and polyvinylpyrrolidone as polymer framework. Cu NCs were uniformly distributed in the polymer matrix, and partially aggregate as evidenced by the AIE phenomenon. These composite Cu NC based films possessed UV shielding ability, and at the same time allow for the transmittance of light in the visible range. Moreover, those films were flexible, thermally stable, and stable against UV light exposure. Possible practical application of Cu NC based films was demonstrated by their protection ability of Rhodamine B dye from photodegradation. A water-soluble, positively-charged polymer was obtained by copolymerizing chitosan with hypromellose, and the evaluation of its biocompatibility and the capacity for the loading of exogenous agents was performed. Films based on hypromellose grafted chitosan (HGC) were employed as a matrix to fabricate composite films by dehydration-triggered aggregation of Cu NCs. The resulting HGC/Cu NC films are transparent and exhibit an AIE enhancement of copper NCs, with a resulting PL QY of 42%. The application of these orange emitting films as color converters for fabrication of remote light emitting devices was demonstrated. We further extended the principles of the Cu nanocluster synthesis to develop an H2O2-assisted top down approach to synthesize brightly luminescent, color-tunable sulfur quantum dots (SQDs), with a PL QY of up to 23%. The formation of SQDs involves dissolution of bulk sulfur powder into small particles in an alkaline environment in the presence of polyethylene glycol, followed by the H2O2-assisted etching of polysulfide species, which at the same time brings an advantage of the passivation of surface states. This synthetic strategy allows us to simultaneously control the final size of SQDs, to tune their emission color, and to improve their emission quantum yield by eliminating surface traps. Water soluble, highly luminescent SQDs realized in this work are promising luminescent materials, which can be produced from abundant precursor materials. In yet another modification of this synthetic procedure, we have shown how to make red-emissive sulfur by a two-step oxidation approach using elemental sulfur and Na2S as starting materials, and achieved reasonably high PL QY of 7.2%. In the process, polysulfide was formed first, and was partially transformed into Na2S2O3 in the first step, and then turned back to elemental S in the second step. The elevated temperature and relatively oxygen-deficient environment during the second step transformed Na2S2O3 into Na2SO3 incorporated with oxygen vacancies, thus resulting in the formation of solid state powder consisting of elemental S embedded in Na2SO3. This composite material showed AIE properties, attributed to the influence of oxygen vacancies on the emission dynamics of sulfur by providing additional lower energy states which facilitate the radiative relaxation of excitons. Finally, we have summarized our up-to-date knowledge on Cu NCs in three review articles, entitled “Ligand Functionalized Copper Nanoclusters for Versatile Applications in Catalysis, Sensing, Bioimaging and Optoelectronics”, "Aggregation-Induced Emission of Copper Nanoclusters", and “Development of Copper Nanoclusters for In Vitro and In Vivo Theranostic Applications“. The latest advances in the design, synthesis, surface engineering, and applications of copper NCs in disease diagnosis, monitoring, and treatment were reviewed, and strategies to control and enhance the emission of copper NCs were considered. With this synopsis of the up-to-date development of copper NCs as theranostic agents, it is hoped that insights and directions for translating current advances from the laboratory to the clinic can be further advanced and accelerated. We also contributed to a review article on related light-emitting materials which show as so-called clusterization-triggered emission phenomenon, entitled "Clusterization-Triggered Emission: Uncommon Luminescence from Common Materials".

11305617.label: Major findings and research outcome
11305617.value: The major findings of this project are on development of wet-chemical synthetic methods towards strongly emissive Cu NCs; and on development of reliable protocols for the post-synthetic treatment of Cu NCs by confining them in metal organic frameworks, biocompatible hydrogels and polymer films, thus improving their emission characteristics and environmental stability. We have comprehensively studied PLs mechanisms of Cu NCs by performing advanced optical spectroscopy studies, probing carrier recombination processes and correlating structural and chemical properties of Cu NCs with different sizes of metal cores, types of ligands, and matrix environments. The resulting stable, strongly emissive Cu NCs were embedded in polymer films, which can be used for ulraviolet shielding, and for loading of exogenous agents in drug delivery. We further extended the principles of the Cu NC synthesis to produce luminescent sulfur with aggregation-induced emission, and summarized our up-to-date knowledge on Cu NCs in three review articles related to their application in theranostics.

11305617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11305617.value: Our research has shown that Cu Nc are indeed possible to be produced by chemical means; they possess reasonable stability when properly encapsulated, and show rather high (in some cases, close to 40%) PLQY. Potential application areas of these materials could only have been touched upon so far, and this may be the area of research which woudl require further action. Moreover, the photoluminescence mechanisms of copper and other metal NCs is still a fascinating area of research. Most recently, a novel concept of so-called "clusterization triggered emission" (CTE) has emerged among scientists who used to work on AIRgen fluorophores; this concept needs to be advanced and studied further. Equally important, synthetic procedures which are used to produce Cu Ncs have motivated us and others to apply similar approaches to luminescent sulfur quantum dots and powders, which also can be luminescent and show AIE effects. This kind of materials are still in its infinity and more research is bound to be done.

11305617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11305617.value: Metal nanoclusters (NCs) are tiny colloidal nanoparticles composed of a few to some hundreds of atoms, with a metal core size typically less than 2 nm. As well as their small size, they have low toxicity and good biocompatibility and they can exhibit reasonably strong photoluminescence (PL), which makes them potentially useful as bio-labels. Copper is a cheap and earth abundant element, but applications of Cu NCs are still limited by their relatively low emission quantum yield and a lack of detailed understanding of the PL mechanisms. In this project, we have established the PL mechanisms of Cu NCs by performing advanced optical spectroscopy studies, probing carrier recombination processes and correlating structural and chemical properties of Cu NCs with different sized metal cores, types of ligands, and environments. Cu NCs with strong emission were produced by wet-chemical means, and by proper post-synthetic treatments such as by embedding Cu NCs in metal organic frameworks (MOFs). The resulting stable, strongly emissive Cu NCs were embedded in polymer films, which can be used for ulraviolet shielding, and for loading of exogenous agents in drug delivery. We further extended the principles of the Cu NC synthesis to produce luminescent sulfur with aggregation-induced emission.

11305817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11305817.value: 隨著交通排放源的數量增加，城市空氣質素日益惡化，空氣污染對健康的影響將更為顯著和嚴重。在這提案中，我們將根據傳統的二維 LUR模型，加入城市建築形態和空氣污染的數據，來開全發新的三維模型。本研究選擇的污染物為二氧化氮， 而研究地點則為旺角區(市區)。這研究會先整合旺角區的地理數據（例如，道路網、地形、土地使用類別和城市/建築形態），以建立二維LUR模型，然後添加不同的檢測數據，包括當地交通量和路邊二氧化氮的垂直輪廓，以製成 三維LUR模型。

11305817.label: Realisation of objectives
11305817.value: This study has been completed according to the proposed tasks and objectives. During the project period, we have collected multiple days of roadside NO2 measurement and vertical profiles for data analysis. One of the challenges in the project was to find proper buildings for vertical profile sampling. Various commercial and residential high-rise buildings from Mong Kok were considered. Unfortunately, due to either windows were not openable or the sampling locations were not correctly facing the roadside, not many buildings were fit for our application. Nevertheless, we managed to collect sufficient data from the sampling campaign to develop and validate the proposed 3D NO2 model. In the data analysis process, we applied the street-level NO2 data and developed a causal relationship between NO2 concentration and traffic volume. By categorizing NO2 concentration according to the road features (e.g., trees, hills or canyons), a strong correlation (i.e., 0.6) was obtained from the measurement data that covers nearly entire Hong Kong. It is observed that street trees generally have more disturbance to the pollutant dispersion than other street parameters. To further understand the effect of urban configuration and meteorological change on 3D NO2 concentration, a computational Fluid Dynamic (CFD), ENVI-met model, was adopted to simulate NO2 vertical profiles under different building configurations and meteorological conditions. The original simulation was planned to use the highest resolution (i.e., 1 m) possible with wind speeds ranging from 1 m/s to 4 m/s for the CFD simulations. Unfortunately, due to numerical instability in the model, only 2 m resolution was adopted. Overall, the simulated NO2 results were comparable to the measured NO2 profiles. To develop the 3D NO2 model, the ENVI-met results were adopted and applied with a machine learning method (i.e., support vector machines). Building aspect ratio, Skyview factor, daily traffic volume, road lane, wind speed/direction, and wind exposition index were found to be important parameters in determining vertical NO2 concentration in the street-canyon environment. This study has illustrated that the newly developed 3D NO2 model is capable of generating vertical NO2 concentrations, which can be directly applied to pollution exposure studies in the urban environment. Early this year, the project has been submitted to ENVI-met for competing in the UNI LAB AWARD 2022 (https://www.envi-met.com/envi_met-unilab-award/). We are proud to announce that an international prize has been awarded to this project for our innovative idea.

11305817.label: Major findings and research outcome
11305817.value: In this research, we have published three papers and one manuscript in preparation (nearly ready to submit). The first publication was related to the early mobile measurement campaign in which we have collected NO2 samples using the onboard Cavity DOAS samplers. In that study, a significant weekend and weekday variation was observed in the urban centre. The streets near the large shopping malls have experienced high NO2 concentration on weekends, which has deviated from the general weekday/weekend emission profile. The phenomenon was mainly attributed to the traffic congestion caused by queuing process near the shopping malls (Publication 1 -Zhu, 2018). This result reflects the NO2 model which we have developed may have underestimated the concentration of NO2 on weekends for those streets near the major shopping malls. In the early development of the 3D NO2 model, two non-NO2 publications have been spinning out using a similar methodology we proposed for the NO2 study. Those two studies have looked at the temperature downscaling and urban heat island under the urban street canyon in the Kowloon area (publication 3, Lam et al., 2021). The results show that the Skyview factor, road type, and other urban features are good proxies for land use regression or downscaling applications (publication 2, Chang et al., 2021). In that study, we also found that integrating machine learning methods (i.e., support vector machines (SVM)) in the prediction model would improve the overall model performance. With the experience we gained, the final 3D NO2 model was developed based on street and building configurations, and simulated NO2 vertical profiles from the computational Fluid Dynamic (CFD) model (i.e., ENVI-met). At last, the simulated results were internalized through the SVM method to create the 3D NO2 prediction model (publication 4, drafted paper).

11305817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11305817.value: The major contribution of this study is to allow one to estimate NO2 concentration in the elevated urban environment. As exposure studies require long-term concentration data, the change in traffic volume and emission factors from the historical context should be considered. It is essential to adopt the same methodology and regenerate the 3D NO2 models under different historical time frames to reflect realistic emission conditions in the past. In such a way, long-term exposure studies can be performed.

11305817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11305817.value: This study developed a three-dimensional air quality model to predict nitrogen dioxide (NO2) concentration in the elevated urban environment. The model is capable of estimating NO2 concentration at any vertical height under the street canyon condition and provides essential information for indoor NO2 exposure studies. It was observed that the effect of traffic emission was diminished to near the same as the background concentration at around 40 m in height, indicating that residents living above the 15th floor would generally receive less NO2 exposure than those who live downstairs.

11306117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11306117.value: 气体在局部热力学平衡态的运动由可压缩Euler方程描述， 其未知函数为密度，速度， 压力及内能。 在平衡态理论中， 气体可以瞬时随环境变化而调整。 这一假设在一些情形下（例如室温）是合理 的。 然而，如果温度增加， 由于化学反应及分子内部结构， 分子从振动模式到平移模式运动过程的调整需要足够长时间，这时气体不再在局部平衡态上。 在该项目中， 我们考虑只有振动非平衡态这一非平衡态过程， 而气体在平移和转动平衡态上。 这一非平衡态气体由描述质量，动量及总能量的守恒律以及描述从振动非平衡态张弛到局部平衡态定律的一个双曲偏微分方程组模拟。 这一方程组是最为重要的带张弛的非线性双曲守恒律组之一。 对这一非平衡态气体动力学方程组在固定边界情形的初边值问题，在法向速度为零的边界条件以及初值不在热力学平衡态的情况下， 项目主持人在该项目的第一部分提出研究当张弛系数趋于零时解的渐进行为。 其动机为理解在有物理边界和初始层时从热力学非平衡态到平衡态的物理过程。 由于在边界及初始时间附近在张弛参数很小时解的奇异行为，亦即初始层和弱边界层现象， 这一问题在数学分析上很有挑战性。 在该项目的第二部分中， 项目主持人提出研究在排除Rayleigh－Taylor 非稳定性的Taylor 符号条件下热力学气体非平衡态方程组自由边界问题在Sobolev空间中的局部时间适定性。这一自由边界问题 描述热力学非平衡态气体在常压力边界条件及边界随气体运动时的动力学。 流体自由边界问题是过去几十年引起很多重视的重要而又在数学理论上具有挑战性的问题。由于速度场旋度和散度， 非平衡及平衡模式及自由界面的相互作用， 本项目中将研究的自由边界问题尤其具有挑战性。 我们将发展一些分析和几何方法来解决这一问题。 应该注意到项目主持人的近期研究主要集中于流体自由边界问题的研究， 包括非退化的无粘磁流体及退化的真空自由边界问题。这些经验会为本项目中所提问题的研究作了相应准备。

11306117.label: Realisation of objectives
11306117.value: The objectives of this project is to understand the qualitative behavior for systems of nonlinear PDEs, in particular, for the system of thermal non-equilibrium gas dynamics, in the presence of physical boundaries, or free boundaries, establishing uniform regularity, well-posedness and convergence. In paper 6 attached in this report, the multi-scale zero relaxation singular limit for gas dynamics in thermal non-equilibrium with multiple non-equilibrium modes in multi-dimensions with physical boundaries from non-equilibrium to thermal equilibrium of compressible Euler equations is proved in this paper for analytical data by establishing the uniform local-in-time estimates. It is found in this paper that, for a fixed time interval independent of relaxation parameters, the solutions of the thermal non-equilibrium system of gas dynamics converges uniformly to that of the compressible Euler equations when the relaxation parameters tend to zero. A cancellation mechanism is utilized to deal with the nonlinear singular terms that cause the increase in both time and space derivatives in energy estimates. The rates of the relaxations corresponding to different non-equilibrium modes tending to zero discussed in this paper can be arbitrarily different. The results obtained in this paper is directly related to the first objective in this project. In paper 3, attached in this report, We study the free boundary of the thermal non-equilibrium gas dynamics in Eulerian coordinates, which can be reduced to the outer pressure problem in Lagrangian coordinates. The thermal nonequilibrium modes can be multiple in this paper. The uniform well-posedness and regularity are established for the initial data satisfying the compatible conditions on the boundary. The results obtained in this paper is directly related to the second objective in this project. In paper 2 attached in this report, an initial layer problem is analyzed for a compressible fluid model modelling nonthermal plasma for the ill-prepared initial data, by constructing approximate solutions of the appropriate order via an asymptotic expansion. Nonlinear asymptotic stability of initial layer approximation is established with the convergence rate. The results obtained in this paper is related to the first objective. In paper 7, attached in this report, for a system of PDEs of compressible fluids type coupled with electric fields in the presence of physical boundary, with the interaction of strong and boundary layers, the qualitative asymptotic behavior when some small physical parameters tend to zero is studied, the convergence with rates are shown also. The results obtained in this paper is directly related to the first objective in this project. Another activity in this project is to study the qualitative asymptotic behavior of solutions to the system of thermal non-equilibrium gas dynamics in the presence of boundaries in large time, related to both objectives 1 and 2 in this project. In paper 4 attached in this paper, for gas dynamics with several thermal nonequilibrium modes, for the initial boundary problem in Lagrangian coordinates, the global well-posedness of smooth solutions is established. Moreover, the exponential convergence is shown for solutions to the linearized system with a vibrational nonequilibrium mode, which illustrates a key distinction from that for the initial value problem without a boundary for which the decay is only algebraic. The last activity is this project is to investigate the convergence to some nonlinear waves of the equilibrium compressible Euler equations for solutions of systems of thermal non-equilibrium gas dynamics. In paper 5 attached in this report, the linearized asymptotic stability of rarefaction waves is obtained with convergence rate, and the life-span of the solution in terms of the rarefaction wave strength is also given when the initial data are perturbations of a smooth rarefaction wave of the equilibrium of the compressible Euler equations. The main feature of the problems is that the L2-norm of the perturbations may grow in time. In paper 1 attached in this report, the large time convergence to the traveling wave solution with shock profile is proved. In summary, the project objectives are achieved.

11306117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11306117.value: In this project, the qualitative asymptotic behavior of some partial differential equations is investigated in the presence of boundaries, either for fixed or free boundaries. The main system of partial differential equations under investigation is the system of thermal non-equilibrium gas dynamics. A gas loses its local thermodynamic equilibrium state if the temperature is increased, the molecular processes take a considerable time due to the chemical reactions and the fact that the internal structure of the molecules is no longer negligible and takes time to adjust from the vibrational mode to the translational mode. It is of fundamental importance to study the behavior of solutions of these system in the presence of boundaries since they model the very interesting and singular physical process near boundaries. Those are the main issues explored in this project. Moreover, we also investigate the behavior of solutions for large time, modelling the physical process from thermal non-equilibrium to thermal equilibrium after enough long time.

11306217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11306217.value: 由於過渡金屬N-雜環卡賓配合物有獨特的催化應用，各種環狀卡賓配體及其金屬配合物已被廣泛開發和研究。相比之下，非環狀卡賓配體及其金屬配合物的研究極少。直到最近，非環狀卡賓金屬配合物的發展才受關注。這是因為最近才發現非環狀二氨基非環狀卡賓（ADC）金屬配合物有優異的催化性能。通過將2-氨基吡啶配位到異氰錸(I)配合物，我們最近報導了一系列具有ADC配體的發光錸(I)配合物。我們的研究更首次揭示了ADC配體的NH部分可以捕獲二氧化碳及與陰離子結合。 受最近我們報導的發光錸(I)-ADC配合物的特性啟發，本項目將設計並合成具有各種ADC配體的過渡金屬配合物。通過對這些卡賓配合物的系統研究，我們將闡明金屬-卡賓的電子性質。此外，還將探討非環狀氨基卡賓配合物的陰離子和二氧化碳結合特性與及其相關的催化和化學傳感的應用。

11306217.label: Realisation of objectives
11306217.value: All objectives have been achieved. The details findings are summarized as follows: 1) Objective 1: New transition metal complexes systems with isocyanide ligands capable of serving as the precursors for the acyclic carbene have been designed and synthesized. As we proposed in the proposal, the reactions of these precursors with suitable nucleophiles have led to the formation of transition metal complexes with acyclic carbene ligands. The newly synthesized transition metal complexes have been characterized by various spectroscopic techniques such as NMR spectroscopy, IR spectroscopy, mass spectrometry, and elemental analysis. The structures of some of these complexes have also been determined by X-ray crystallography. The reactivity and electronic properties of the precursor complexes and their acyclic carbene complexes have been studied. Some of the results have been reported in journal articles, European Journal of Inorganic Chemistry 2018, Inorganic Chemistry 2018, and Inorganic Chemistry Frontier 2020, listed in Part C. The results have also been presented in international conferences, XXVIII ICOMC 2018 and EICC-5 2018. 2) Objective 2: Many of the newly designed transition metal isocyanide and carbene complexes display interesting photophysical, luminescent, and excited-state properties. The study of their electronic and spectroscopic properties has been investigated to elucidate the nature of their electronic transitions and emissive excited states. These results are reported in the European Journal of Inorganic Chemistry 2018, Inorganic Chemistry 2018, and Inorganic Chemistry Frontier 2020. As some of the transition metal complexes show interesting electrochemical properties, their memory device applications have also been explored through collaboration with material scientists. The results are reported in the Journal of Materials Chemistry C 2018 (Part C). Besides, the long-lived excited states associated with some of the newly designed metal complexes can also be used as photoredox catalysts. Their photocatalytic activity for esterification and amidation has been studied and reported in the Asian Journal of Organic Chemistry 2018 and Catalysis Science & Technology 2021 (Part C). The results have also been presented in ISPPCC 2019. 3) Objective 3: Some of the acyclic carbenes can bind to carbon dioxide and anions; the binding events lead to drastic changes in the photophysical properties of the metal complexes. Therefore, they can be used as luminescent chemosensors. The chemosensory applications of the acyclic carbene complexes have been presented in ISPPCC 2019. On the other hand, the solid-state and neat film of Ir(III) acyclic carbene complexes display strong mechanoluminescent properties. Interestingly, the mechanochromic changes could be reversed by exposure to volatile organic vapors. The potential chemosensory applications of these complexes for VOC have been reported in Inorganic Chemistry Frontier 2020, listed in Part C.

11306217.label: Major findings and research outcome
11306217.value: The research was conducted following the proposed research plan and methodology outlined in the proposal. New transition metal complexes systems with isocyanide ligands capable of serving as the precursors for the acyclic carbene have been designed and synthesized. As we proposed in the proposal, the reactions of these precursors with suitable nucleophiles have led to the formation of transition metal complexes with acyclic carbene ligands. All the newly synthesized transition metal complexes have been fully-characterized by various spectroscopic techniques such as NMR spectroscopy, IR spectroscopy, mass spectrometry, and elemental analysis to confirm their chemical identity. The structures of some of these complexes have also been unambiguously confirmed by X-ray crystallography. The reactivity, spectroscopic, electronic, and luminescent properties of the precursor complexes and their acyclic carbene complexes have been studied. Through systematic variation of the complex systems and ligands’ substituents of the newly developed metal carbene complex systems, the structure-properties correlation has been established. For the newly designed metal complexes with desirable excited-state properties, i.e. long-lived lifetimes, reversible electrochemical properties, and redox potential, their photocatalytic activities for photoredox catalytic reactions such as amidation and esterification have been studied. On the other hand, as one series of the newly developed transition metal complexes show interesting electrochemical properties, their memory device applications have also been explored through collaboration with material scientists. In short, the results of this project contribute to the development of new classes of transition metal complexes with various acyclic carbene ligands. Many of these complexes display interesting luminescent, electrochemical, and excited-state properties. Detailed study shows that these complexes can be used as building blocks for phosphorescent materials, mechanoresponsive materials, photocatalysts, and chemosensors. Some of these results have been published in internationally refereed journals (Part C), including Inorganic Chemistry, Dalton Transactions, European Journal of Inorganic Chemistry, Asian Journal of Organic Chemistry, Journal of Materials Chemistry, Inorganic Chemistry Frontiers, and Catalysis Science & Technology. Apart from publications in journal articles, the results have also been presented as a number of invited lectures or oral presentations in international conferences (Part C), including the XXVIII International Conference on Organometallic Chemistry, the 10th Asian Photochemistry Conference, 5th Euchems Inorganic Chemistry Conference, and the 23rd International Symposium on the Photochemistry and Photophysics of Coordination Compounds.

11306217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11306217.value: As mentioned in 6.1, the results of this project have led to new classes of acyclic carbene ligands and their transition metal complexes with novel properties such as phosphorescent, mechanoresponsive, and chemosensing properties. On the basis of these results, we have initiated new directions to develop new metal-based luminescent mechanochromic materials and mechanoresponsive materials. A research proposal on the development of mechanoresponsive polymers/macromolecular systems using the results of this work has been supported by RGC. Inspired by the results of this work, we have also developed a new class of robust and recyclable photoredox catalysts for organic transformations. It will open up a new direction for the development of recyclable photocatalysts.

11306217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11306217.value: To meet device development needs, the demand for advanced materials with photo-functional properties, such as luminescent materials, photocatalysts, chemical sensors, and mechanically-responsive materials, is increasing. In this project, a new family of luminescent transition metal complexes has been developed and studied. Based on these transition metal complexes, new photocatalysts, mechanically-responsive luminescent materials, and chemical sensors have been designed. The scientific results of these functional properties have been published in internationally refereed journals and presented in several invited lectures or oral presentations in international conferences. In summary, the results of this project would provide a new design strategy for developing new photofunctional materials.

11306417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11306417.value: 由于人类活动的增加全球气候变暖的影响将继续发生，在全球各地的极端天气的强度将有可能更严重。人们往往关注炎热的天气尤其是基于破纪录的高温，但很少考虑湿度对热感觉的影响。我们应该开展炎热天气的研究应为热强度 (中暑)指数带来巨大的经济、 社会和环境影响 。同样的空气温度在湿度较高 的 环境下，我们感觉更热 。这就是为什么在香港和夏季潮湿华南沿海城市湿度是热强度（中暑）指数特别是的重要参数。本研究旨在提供统计预测模型分析研究香港炎热天气的 演变趋势和未来变化预测 ，这样的研究可以提早预测预防中暑可能性的发生。统计降尺度技术将应用于先进的耦合模型 (CMIP5) 输出获取每日的最大热强度指数。这将使我们能够分析预估在=RCP 4.5 和 RCP 8.5情境下的香港 炎热天气的发生频率、 持续时间和强度变化规律。预测未来热强度指数的这项研究会明确地评估热天气相关的风险。因此，我们的研究将找到更多的适用性与更广泛的受众。例如，热强度指数在某种程度上可以为有关劳动部门、公共卫生和电力政策规划电力消费 提供服务。

11306417.label: Major findings and research outcome
11306417.value: 1. Impact of the Indian Ocean Dipole on Evolution of the Subsequent ENSO: Relative Roles of Dynamic and Thermodynamic Processes The interaction between the IOD and the concurrent ENSO [ENSO(0)] can be summarized as follows: ENSO(0) can trigger and enhance the IOD, while the IOD can enhance ENSO(0) and accelerate its demise. Regarding the impacts of IOD(0) on the subsequent ENSO(11), it is revealed that the IOD can lead to anomalous SST cooling patterns over the equatorial Pacific after the winter following the IOD, indicating the formation of a La Niña–like pattern in the subsequent year. While the SST cooling tendency associated with a positive IOD is attributable primarily to net heat flux (thermodynamic processes) from autumn to the ensuing spring, after the ensuing spring the dominant contribution comes from oceanic processes (dynamic processes) instead. 2. Position, Magnitude, and Size of Warm-Pool El Niño: Variability, Seasonal Predictability, and Climate Impact Thirteen WP El Niño events are found from 1950 to 2018 using this detector. These events have a mean (standard deviation) center position of 31.7 (12.4)° longitude, a mean peak sea surface temperature anomaly (SSTA) of 1.87 (0.62) K, and a zonal size parameter of 19.99 (5.13)° longitude. Also, stronger WP El Niño events tend to be larger and take place farther east. Based on these distributions, a set of model experiments is conducted to evaluate climate sensitivity to these three features. 3. Influence of Tropical Cyclones on Hong Kong Air Quality It is found that 57.5% of days with concentration of particulate matter with an aerodynamic diameter 10 μm (PM10) above the 90th percentile are related to TC activity. TCs in three regions, located to the east, southeast, and southwest of Hong Kong, have obvious impacts on pollutant concentration. 4. The 2019 Autumn Hot Drought Over the Middle-Lower Reaches of the Yangtze River in China: Early Propagation, Process Evolution, and Concurrence From a large-scale dynamic perspective, early propagation and development of the 2019AHD are related to the southward shift and enhancement of the subsidence branch of meridional circulations. Meanwhile, intensity variation in 200 hPa cyclonic anomalies over MLYR corresponds well with local drought development, and the enhanced intensity at the time of drought occurrence is probably related to Silk Road Pattern–like wave train propagation over Eurasia. These insights can help us understand the mechanisms and detect early signals of hot droughts
