11306517.value: ACAP1蛋白质与细胞结合的分子机制

11306517.label: Project Objectives
11306517.value: To investigate the interaction between the ACAP1 protein and the membrane by quantifying the binding energy of the PH domain to different lipid molecules. To compare the structure and dynamics of two chains in the ACAP1 protein to explore the potential intrinsic asymmetry in the protein dimer, which may affect its binding to the membrane. To formulate a new potential energy of the ACAP1 protein-membrane system as a function of the binding orientation. The potential energy takes into consideration the bending energy of the membrane and protein. The input parameters will be obtained from MD simulations. This model can be applied to study other protein-surface adsorption problems for biomedical applications.

11306517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11306517.value: This project proposes a combined computational and experimental investigation of the molecular mechanism of interactions between ACAP1 proteins and the membrane. Protein-membrane interaction is crucial to many essential cellular processes, some of which are key pathogenic factors in a number of human diseases including cancer, Alzheimer’s disease, diabetes mellitus, mental retardation and epilepsy. Numerous transportation carriers accurately and efficiently deliver molecules to desired destinations in order for cells to maintain functions such as signaling, sorting, autophagy, membrane trafficking, organelle motility and so on. These carriers are generated by complicated protein-membrane interactions. The Bin-Amphiphysin-Rvs (BAR) superfamily proteins are one group of regulator proteins that remodel cell membranes via two well-known mechanisms, i.e., scaffolding and wedging mechanisms. However, a novel mechanism different than these two mechanisms has been reported in Arfgap with Coil coil, Ankyrin repeat, and Pleckstrin Homology domain protein 1 (ACAP1) protein-membrane systems where the BAR domains do not directly interact with the membrane as they do in other BAR domain containing proteins (BAR proteins). The ACAP1 protein instead unexpectedly binds to the membrane asymmetrically using only one of its Pleckstrin Homology (PH) domains. The molecular mechanism through which the ACAP1 proteins interact with the membrane to induce membrane deformation is still unclear. In this proposal, we will first computationally investigate the interactions between ACAP1 proteins and the membrane. Specifically, since the PH domain binds to the membrane, we will quantify the binding affinity of the PH domain to different lipid molecules. Next, we will formulate a protein-membrane interaction potential to describe the protein-membrane system and search for the optimal binding orientation of the protein. To speed up the search, ACAP1 proteins will be coarse-grained and a program using the Monte Carlo method will be developed. Finally, our experimental collaborator will carry out cryo-electron microscopy (EM) reconstruction experiments to verify the computational predictions. The proposed computational approach enables a systematic investigation of ACAP1 protein – membrane interactions for the first time. The results will provide new insights into the molecular mechanism of interactions between ACAP1 protein and the membrane. The newly developed protein-membrane interaction potential is applicable to other protein-surface adsorption questions. It will be useful in the effort to design surfaces to attract enzymes or antibodies for biomedical applications. Our exploration will also shed light on designing new drugs for the aforementioned diseases. 本项目提出使用计算和试验相结合的方法来研究ACAP1蛋白质与细胞膜相互作用的分子机制。蛋白质与细胞膜的相互作用在诸多细胞活动中是至关重要的，有一些还是人类疾病的致病因素，包括癌症，帕金森病，糖尿病，智力迟钝以及癫痫病。 为了维持细胞正常的功能，例如信号传输，分类，自吞，迁移等等，细胞内外有众多的运输机器把分子精准的送到细胞各处。这些载体是通过复杂的蛋白质 - 膜相互作用而产生。 其中，Bin-Amphiphysin-Rvs（BAR）超家族蛋白使用两种众所周知的机制（即脚手架和楔入机制）改造细胞膜来辅助制造运输载体。在Arfgap与线圈，Ankyrin重复和Pleckstrin同源结构域蛋白1（ACAP1）蛋白膜系统中已经报道了一种与这两种机制不同的新机制，其中BAR结构域不像其他BAR蛋白质那样直接与膜相互作用。意外地 ACAP1蛋白质仅使用其一个PH结构域以非对称的方式结合膜。但是ACAP1蛋白与膜相互作用诱导膜变形的分子机制尚没有完全清楚。 在本科研项目中，我们将首先计算研究ACAP1蛋白与膜之间的相互作用。具体地说，由于PH结构域与膜结合，我们将量化PH结构域对不同脂质分子的结合亲和力。接下来，我们将制定蛋白质 - 膜相互作用势能来描述蛋白质 - 膜系统，并寻找蛋白质的最佳结合方向。为了加快搜索速度，ACAP1蛋白质将被粗粒化，并且将开发使用蒙特卡罗方法的程序来进行搜索。最后，我们的实验合作者将进行低温电子显微镜（EM）重建实验来验证计算预测。 我们提出的计算方法首次系统地研究ACAP1蛋白 - 膜相互作用。结果将为ACAP1蛋白与膜间相互作用的分子机制提供新的见解。新开发的蛋白质 - 膜相互作用势能也适用于其他蛋白质与表面的吸附问题。在设计表面、生物医学应用的酶或抗体将会是有用处的。我们的探索也将为诸多疾病设计新药物提供一些参考意见。

11306517.label: Realisation of objectives
11306517.value: We have investigated the interaction between the ACAP1 protein and the membrane, and we quantified the binding energy of PH domain to PI and PS molecules through two binding pockets. This energy suggested the binding energy of PI to the binding pocket is much higher than that of PS. We also have identified the key residues among ACAP1 proteins to maintain the lattice structure on the lipid tube. The structure and dynamics of two chains in ACAP1 protein are compared and the intrinsic asymmetry were observed, which resulted in its binding to the membrane asymmetrically. The potential energies of ACAP1 protein-membrane system via different orientations were calculated and compared. The asymmetrical orientation is the most energetically favourable configuration.

11306517.label: Major findings and research outcome
11306517.value: Utilising flexible fitting molecular dynamics simulation method, Monte Carlo calculations, and cryo-electron sub-tomography experiments, we explained why the ACAP1 protein binds to the membrane asymmetrically, and identified three critical protein contacting regions within the same helical strands and those cross helical strands. The three critical contacting regions include (1) R236, E239, Q240, Q247 and K248 through electron static interactions, as well as D99, H103, Q107, R118, D122, R125, D126, R129, Q150 and E154 through salt-bridges, H-bonds, (2) residues 1 to 20 interacting with res 276 to 282, (3) D92 interacting with R236, K82 interacting with D310 and D311. Besides, mutations experiments of (a) R236, E239 and K248 (b) R118, E122, R125 and D126 and (c) combine of (a) and (b), (d)D92, R236 (e) S277, N278, F280, K281 were carried out to confirm the above simulation predictions. Indeed very limited tubes were formed from liposome after mutation. Therefore these charged residues were key protein-protein contact sites that enable dimeric ACAP1 to assemble into a high-order lattice structure for membrane deformation. Moreover, we observed ACAP1 coated liposomes on both non-tubulated and tubulated regions. Sub-tomogram averaging suggested the intermediate structure for the protein lattice is the assemble of long helical stands. Furthermore, the binding affinity of the PH domain to different lipid molecules were compared and PIP2 has a higher binding affinity which may stabilised the binding of the ACAP1 protein on lipid membrane. Monte Carlo simulations were carried out to investigate the orientation by which the ACAP1 dimer is adsorbed onto a negatively charged membrane surface under different surface charge densities and ionic strength. It turns out that the asymmetrical binding orientation has the lowest potential energy compared to other orientations. This finding explained why the protein prefers to bind to the membrane via this special orientation from the energetic point of view. Finally, we compared the structure and dynamics of two chains of the ACAP1 protein and found they are intrinsically asymmetric. This result also supports the asymmetric binding orientation of the protein to the membrane.

11306517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11306517.value: First, this project demonstrated a nice combination of computational approach and the experimental method to study the ACAP1 protein-membrane interactions. The PI plans to continue the collaboration with experimental groups and explore other important membrane binding protein and the molecular mechanism of membrane bending. Second, this projects focuses on the protein-membrane interactions which participated a variety of cellular processes and contributes to different diseases. As the development of two dimensional nano-materials, more and more nano-materials are applied for biomedical applications. It would be interesting to study bio-nano interactions, such as lipid membrane-nanosheet interactions, protein-nanosheet interactions, as well as DNA-nanosheet interactions. These interactions may interfering the protein-membrane interactions studied in the current project. My group has started the investigation of the lipid membrane-nanosheet interactions and DNA-nanosheet. We plan to continue these explorations and the protein-nanosheet interactions in the future.

11306517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11306517.value: Membrane bending occurs in many cellular activities and malfunction of bending may induces different diseases. It is essential to understand the membrane bending mechanisms. BAR family proteins are one type of the proteins possessing the function to induce membrane bending. In this project, the PI explored a complicated protein-membrane system, ACAP1 protein (a BAR family protein), which binds to the lipid membrane and induces membrane bending via a unique binding configuration. Protein-lipid, protein-protein interactions and protein-membrane interactions were all investigated to understand the molecular mechanisms of this unique asymmetric protein binding (first time observed in BAR family protein) and membrane bending. Experimental observations support our simulation predictions on the key residues to maintain protein lattice. Moreover, the binding affinity of the PH domain to PIP2 and PS lipid molecules were quantified to understand how the protein stabilised itself on the membrane. Furthermore, the structure and dynamics of a single protein in solution demonstrated the intrinsic asymmetry of ACAP1 protein, which may also result in the asymmetrical binding of the protein to membrane. These results reveal a new protein-membrane interaction mechanism which induces membrane bending.

11306617.label: Project Objectives
11306617.value: Approximation theory of convolutional deep nets. The convolutional deep nets are generated by shifts of convolution kernels. We plan to estimate the complexity of the function space spanned by the components at the last level of hidden units in terms of the convolution kernels, to study rates of function approximation by outputs of convolutional deep nets, and to analyze the role of pooling for convolutional deep nets. Wavelet analysis of learning with deep nets. We plan to estimate covering numbers of the hypothesis spaces in deep learning through handling the redundancy of distributed representations by wavelet analysis, to carry out error analysis for learning with deep nets of special structures, and to analyze useful approximating functions generated from some activation functions in deep learning. Stochastic composite mirror descent and recurrent deep nets. We plan to derive necessary and sufficient conditions for the convergence of the online mirror descent algorithm associated with differentiable mirror maps in terms of step sizes, to get rates of convergence for composite mirror descent algorithms associated with non-differentiable mirror maps, and to make some mathematical analysis of learning with stochastic mirror descent and recurrent deep nets.

11306617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11306617.value: Deep learning has been developed very successfully as a super effective scheme for handling big data practically. It is implemented by deep neural networks or deep nets which often have special structures instead of being fully connected. But there is little work on approximation properties of structured deep nets which is comparable to the classical approximation theory for fully connected neural networks. This project aims at a rigorous approximation theory for some topics of structured deep nets and deep learning. First we plan to establish an approximation theory for convolutional deep nets associated with the rectified linear unit. Expected results include estimates for the complexity of the function space spanned by the components at the last level of hidden units in terms of the convolution kernels, rates of function approximation by the generated output functions, and analysis for the role of pooling in convolutional deep nets and deep learning. Then we plan to carry out wavelet analysis of learning with deep nets: estimating covering numbers of the involved hypothesis spaces to handle the redundancy of distributed representations of deep nets, and conducting error analysis for learning with deep nets of special structures. Finally some stochastic composite mirror descent algorithms including online mirror descent with differentiable mirror maps and composite mirror descent with non-differentiable mirror maps will be studied by analyzing the induced Bregman distances, which will help the theoretical understanding of recurrent deep nets in deep learning. 深度學習作為一種處理大數據的有效工具已在實際應用中得到了很成功的發展。它的執行依賴於有特殊結構的深度神經網絡或深度網,而不是全連接網絡。但對有結構深度網至今還沒有可與經典全連接神經網絡逼近論相比擬的逼近性質。本項目旨在對有結構深度網和深度學習的幾個課題建立嚴格的逼近理論。首先我們計劃建立帶整流線性單位的捲積深度網的逼近論,包括對應函數空間的複雜度,逼近階,和池作用的分析。然後我們計劃進行深度網學習的小波分析: 估計用於分佈式表示的假設空間的覆蓋數,和對有特殊結構深度網學習進行誤差分析。最後我們將利用Bregman距離研究幾個隨機複合鏡面梯度下降算法,包括帶可微鏡面映射的在線鏡面梯度下降法和帶不可微鏡面映射的複合鏡面梯度下降法,這將提高對深度學習中遞推深度網理論的理解。

11306617.label: Major findings and research outcome
11306617.value: In [1] we proposed a family of new structured deep neural networks, deep distributed convolutional neural networks, and showed that these deep neural networks have the same order of computational complexity as the deep convolutional neural networks. We also proved their universality of approximation by some ideas from ridge approximation, wavelets, and learning theory. In [2] we introduced a downsampling operator from wavelet analysis to deep convolutional neural networks for reducing the linearly increasing widths, and stablished an approximation theory, showing that the downsampled deep convolutional neural networks can be used to approximate ridge functions nicely, demonstrating advantages of these structured networks in terms of approximation or modelling. We also proved that the output of any multi-layer fully-connected neural network can be realized by that of a downsampled deep convolutional neural network with free parameters of the same order, which shows that in general, the approximation ability of deep convolutional neural networks is at least as good as that of fully-connected networks. A theorem for approximating functions on Riemannian manifolds is presented, which demonstrates that deep convolutional neural networks can be used to learn manifold features of data. In [3] we focused on generalization performance analysis for distributed algorithms with gradient descent related to recurrent deep nets in the framework of learning theory. For distributed kernel ridge regression, we succeeded in deriving optimal learning rates in expectation and in probability, and providing theoretically optimal ranges of the number of local processors. We also proposed a communication strategy to improve its learning performance and demonstrate the power of communications via both theoretical assessments and numerical experiments. In [4] we considered relations between features and the depth of deep neural networks to reflect the necessity of depth. We presented the adaptivity of features to depths and vice-verse via showing a depth-parameter trade-off in extracting both single feature and composite features. Based on these results, we prove that implementing the classical empirical risk minimization on deep nets with stochastic gradient descent can achieve the optimal generalization performance for numerous learning tasks. Our theoretical results are verified by a series of numerical experiments including a real application of earthquake seismic intensity prediction. In [5] we proposed a novel tree structure to equip deep nets to compensate the capacity drawback of deep fully connected neural networks and enhanced the approximation ability of deep convolutional neural networks. We also derived fast learning rates for an empirical risk minimization algorithm based on gradient descent and deep nets.

11306617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11306617.value: Structured deep neural networks arise from deep learning in various forms including convolutional neural networks and recurrent neural networks. Research results produced and ideas developed in this project lead to further connections to 2-D CNNs and RNNs together with other potential applications of deep learning. We will use these findings to develop the theory and applications of deep learning in our further research.

11306617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11306617.value: This project aims at a rigorous approximation theory of structured deep nets and some related deep learning algorithms. We have developed an approximation theory of convolutional deep nets. A downsampling operator from wavelet analysis was introduced to deep convolutional neural networks and we have showed that downsampled deep convolutional neural networks can be used to approximate ridge functions and learn manifold features of data nicely and their approximation ability is at least as good as that of fully-connected networks. Generalization performance of distributed algorithms with gradient descent and a communication strategy related to recurrent deep nets has been studied in the framework of learning theory using covering numbers and complexity of the hypothesis space and optimal learning rates in expectation and in probability have been derived. Relations between features, depths and tree structures of deep neural networks have been investigated to understand the necessity of network structures and depths. We have shown that implementing the classical empirical risk minimization on deep nets with gradient descent can achieve the optimal generalization performance for numerous learning tasks.

11306717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11306717.value: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) have shown desirable properties for biomedical applications. For example, due to their high drug loading capacity and potential biodegradability, nanoscale MOFs (NMOFs) have been recognized as a promising vector for drug delivery. However, there are still a number of challenges in the advance of NMOFs technology for drug delivery. In particular, size controllability in nanoscale range, morphology uniformity, and surface modifiability of NMOFs are major issues to be concerned, because these factors have significant influence on the cellular uptake, in vivo stability, drug delivery efficacy, and targetability. To solve the problems, we recently synthesized zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8) NMOF nanocomposites by employing poly(acrylic acid) PAA nanospheres as a soft template. This approach enabled us to have an effective control on the size of NMOF nanocomposites by employing PAA templates with different sizes; meanwhile flexible surface modification could be achieved by conjugating various functional groups to the PAA templates terminated with –COOH. Beyond these, we revealed that these ZIF-8 NMOF nanocomposites possessed over 45wt% doxorubicin (DOX) loading capacity, which is significantly higher than commonly used nanocarriers. Based on these encouraging preliminary results, we propose in this project to establish a soft-templating approach to synthesize a range of NMOF nanocomposites with controlled size and surface characteristics, and understand factors that influence the NMOFs growth on soft templates. Considering that the metal ions, organic linkers, and reaction conditions strongly influence the morphology, particle/pore size, stability and drug delivery performance, we will produce NMOF nanocomposites comprising different metal ions (e.g., Zn and Fe) and organic ligands (e.g., 2-methylimidazole, muconic acid, and amino terephthalic) and systematically study their impacts on the properties of the produced nanocomposites. Furthermore, as an example application, the prepared NMOF nanocomposites will be co-loaded with photosensitizers and chemotherapeutic drugs – photosensitizers conjugated to the PAA templates and anticancer drug DOX loaded to NMOFs by physical absorption. In vitro and in vivo tests will be conducted to evaluate their combinatorial photodynamic and chemotherapy performance and safety profiles. The success of this project will form a guideline for designing and fabricating new NMOF nanocomposites, and make this novel material promising for not only cancer treatment, but also for other applications such as air purification, catalysis, electronics and gas storage/separation.

11306717.label: Realisation of objectives
11306717.value: Objective 1: We have successfully synthesized a series of NMOF nanocomposites by using poly(acrylic acid) sodium salt (PAAS) as a soft template. The NMOF nanocomposites comprise nanoscale zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8) in the PAAS matrix. The size of nanocomposites is shown to be tunable from 33 nm to 200 nm by changing molecular weight of PAAS soft template from 20 K to 1.2 K. It is also demonstrated that the size of NMOFs is controllable by changing the self-assembly of PAAS soft template. In addition to the controllability on size, it is illustrated that the surfaces of nanocomposites can be modified by poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG), FITC, Cy5, folic acid and photosensitizer Chlorine e6 (Ce6). Objective 2: We have systematically studied the factors that influencing the growth of NMOF nanocomposites, for example the metal ions, organic linkers, and photosensitizers on the physical and chemical properties of the NMOFs nanocomposites. We demonstrated that the molecular weight of soft-template influenced the crystallinity of ZIF-8 NMOFs nanocomposites. It is revealed that ZIF-8 NMOF nanocomposites with higher crystallinity can be synthesized by using the PAAS soft template with larger molecular weight. Moreover, prolonging the reaction time is also able to improve the crystallinity of the nanocomposites. We conjugated a photosensitizer (Ce6) to ZIF-8 NMOF nanocomposites for photodynamic therapy, and the presence of Zn with an atomic percentage of 8.52 was achieved. Moreover, we integrated protoporphyrin XI into NMOF (nUiO-68-NH2) to form PpIX-conjugated nUiO-68-NH2 (nPCU) for combinational photodynamic therapy and photothermal therapy. The nPCU has a typical morphology of hexagonal nanoplate with the size of about 120 nm and thickness around 20 nm. In this NMOF based hybrid, various PpIX contents can be loaded with a maximum amount of 29.1 wt%. With the integration of PpIX, no obvious change in morphology, size and structure of hybrids is observed. However, the surface charge changes from positive to negative after conjugation. In addition, the nPCU shows higher size stability in aqueous solution as compared with nUiO-68-NH2. Objective 3: In this project, we evaluated the properties of Ce6 conjugated NMOFs (ZIF-8 based MOFs) and PpIX conjugated NMOFs (nUiO-68-NH2 based MOFs), including drug loading capacity, intracellular drug delivery, ROS generation, toxicity, photostability, and chemo- and photodynamic/photothermal cancer therapies. The major results are summarized below: 1) As compared with free Ce6 molecules, no obvious change is observed for Ce6 conjugated MOF (MOF-Ce6) in absorbance spectrum except a little red shift. However, the MOF-Ce6 presents a superior photostability over free Ce6 molecules. When exposed to light, the MOF-Ce6 nanocomposites show only a slow absorption decay, in sharp contrast to the dramatic absorption reduction of Ce6. Both Ce6 and MOF-Ce6 can effectively generate singlet oxygen. However, after exposed to 650 nm LED light for 30 min before ROS detection, it is noted that MOF-Ce6 can still generate ROS efficiently while Ce6 molecules lose their ROS generation capacity seriously. 2) For the intracellular delivery efficacy, we reveal that the ZIF-8 NMOFs can release the drug and be decomposed in acid environment more quickly; and the intracellular delivery efficiency is size dependent, i.e., ZIF-8 (1.2K) < ZIF-8 (8K) < ZIF-8 (20K). After incubation for 4 h, the HeLa cells treated with ZIF-8 (20K) (46 nm) NMOFs show a much stronger fluorescence signal from DOX than those treated with ZIF-8 (1.2K) (190 nm) and ZIF-8 (8K) (98 nm). In addition, through monitoring the viability of HeLa cells after incubation with free DOX, and ZIF-8 NMOFs nanocomposites loaded with 10 wt % DOX, an improved delivery efficiency is demonstrated with the aid of ZIF-8 NMOFs, particularly with those made from PAAS with a molecular weight of 20K Da. This result agrees well with our observation that ZIF-8 (20K) enters cells more efficiently than ZIF-8 (1.2K) and ZIF-8 (8K) NMOFs. We studied the performance of PEG conjugated ZIF-8 NMOFs for chemotherapy in vivo. It is illustrated that the therapeutic efficacy of free DOX molecules and the DOX delivered by ZIF-8 NMOFs without PEG surface modification are very low, as indicated by the rapidly growing tumors during the observation period. In contrast, ZIF-8 NMOFs-PEG DOX exhibits significantly improved therapeutic efficiency. Moreover, the PEG modified MOF with MTX has as well outstanding biocompatibility. From the H&E staining, higher tumor cell damage is observed in the MOF-PEG DOX treated tumor, in comparison with the MOF DOX, DOX, and PBS treated groups, which further verifies the superior anticancer efficiency of MOF-PEG DOX. 3) We demonstrate that PpIX conjugated NMOFs have minimal toxicity in dark, but discernible toxicity under laser irradiation. Moreover, the PpIX conjugated NMOFs can effectively generate ROSs and heat for photodynamic therapy and photothermal therapy, respectively. The ROS generation efficiency and photothermal conversion efficiency can be tuned by changing the weight percentage of PpIX. In the evaluation of cellular uptake and chemotherapy drug loading of PpIX conjugated NMOFs, it is found that the PpIX conjugated NMOFs enter the cells by endocytosis. Moreover, the anticancer drug, Doxorubicin, can be loaded to the PpIX conjugated NMOFs and delivered to the cytoplasmic region of A549 cells.

11306717.label: Major findings and research outcome
11306717.value: We have successfully prepared a series of NMOF nanocomposites with different sizes, organic linkers, and metal ions by using the soft-templating method. It is revealed that the metal ions, organic linkers, soft templates, reaction conditions, and solvents have great impacts on the morphology, size, crystalline structure, and properties of the prepared NMOF nanocomposites. For example, the size of nanocomposites can be tuned from 33 nm to 200 nm by changing molecular weight of PAAS soft template from 20K to 1.2K, and ZIF-8 NMOF nanocomposites with higher crystallinity are synthesized by using PAAS soft template with larger molecular weight. Moreover, prolonging reaction time is also shown to be able to improve the crystallinity of the NMOF nanocomposites. We have prepared ZIF-8 and nUiO-68-NH2 based NMOF nanocomposites, and functionalized the nanocomposites with different functional groups, such as photosensitizer (Ce6 and PpIX), fluorescent dyes (FITC, Cy5), targeting ligands (folic acids). For the intracellular delivery efficacy, we reveal that it is size dependent: ZIF-8 (1.2K) < ZIF-8 (8K) < ZIF-8 (20K). We also demonstrate that the high capability of DOX loaded ZIF-8 NMOF nanocomposites for cancer therapy and reveal their pH dependent release of drugs (rapidly drug release in acid environment and slow drug release in physiological environment). Moreover, we have conjugated photosensitizer Ce6 and PpIX to ZIF-8 and nUiO-68-NH2 NMOF nanocomposites, respectively, and obtained the following results: 1) Both MOF-Ce6 and PpIX nUiO-68-NH2 can effectively generate singlet oxygen with high efficacy and photo-stability. For the ZIF-8 based NMOFs, it is found that, with NMOF encapsulation, the photostability of the photosensitizer is significantly increased, and thus the anticancer effect is improved. 2) For the performance of PEG conjugated ZIF-8 NMOFs for chemotherapy (DOX) in vivo, ZIF-8 NMOFs-PEG DOX exhibits significantly improved therapeutic efficiency, i.e., more than 50% tumor reduction compared with free DOX drug, PBS, and ZIF-8-NMOFs DOX without PEG modification. 3) For PpIX nUiO-68-NH2 NMOF nanocomposites, it is illustrated that they enter the cells by endocytosis, and their ROS generation efficiency and photothermal conversion efficiency can be tuned by changing the weight percentage of PpIX. Our synthesis strategy by using soft-templating method provides a feasible and effective way to tune the size, morphology, crystalline structure, surface modification, and physical and chemical properties of the NMOF nanocomposites, which is favorable for designing new NMOF nanocomposites with the improved efficacy for cancer therapy.

11306717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11306717.value: A soft-templating method is developed to synthesize the NMOF nanocomposites with different size, morphology, and crystallinity in this project. Moreover, with this method, the surface of NMOF nanocomposites could also be modified with different functional molecules. However, to modify and functionalize the surfaces of NMOFs without changing or destructing their size and crystallinity is still challenging, which will affect their properties and efficacy in cancer therapy. Therefore, further studies are required on reliably controlling the size and crystallinity of NMOFs with the surface-modified functional groups. In addition, there are a plenty number of MOFs with different crystal structures and properties, and most of soft-templating fabrication processes are only applicable to one or two identical NMOFs. Therefore, there is still a need to find some general approaches to feasibly synthesize different NMOFs with desired size and morphology with the soft-templating method. In term of biomedical applications of NMOFs, further studies on the biodegradability and biosafety of NMOFs are essential. As NMOFs are much easier to be decomposed in the biosystem than inorganic nanoparticles, there will be less safety concern. However, as a new material, a more detailed safety analysis is still needed before its practical applications.

11306717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11306717.value: Metal organic frameworks (MOFs) are a group of compounds consisting of metal ions or clusters in a coordination network linked with organic ligands, and their special features, in particular a controllable porosity, lead to their attractive applications in various fields including energy harvest and drug delivery. By changing the metal ions and organic linkers, different MOFs can be constructed. However, it is still a challenge to control their size and morphology in the fabrication process, especially for the nanoscale MOFs (NMOFs). In this project, we synthesized NMOF nanocomposites by using poly(acrylic acid) sodium salt (PAAS) as a soft template. The nanocomposites comprises nanoscale zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 in the PAAS matrix. By using this approach, the size of nanocomposites could be tuned from 33 nm to 200 nm. In addition, we functionalized the NMOF nanocomposites with a variety of functional molecules, such as photosensitizers, poly(ethylene glycol), fluorescent dyes, cancer targeting molecules and drugs. The physical and photo properties of the nanocomposites, including biodegradability, photostability, capability to generate reactive oxygen species, and the anticancer performance were systematically studied. The results demonstrate that the NMOF nanocomposites with the controlled size, crystallinity, and surface modification are promising platform for cancer therapy.

11500617.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11500617.value: 囤積國際儲備:跟上瓊斯效應還是減少危機感染

11500617.label: Project Objectives

11500617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11500617.value: Economies hoard international reserves to safeguard against economic hardship caused by, say, financial crisis and unexpected capital outflow. In general, it is agreed that either an inadequate or excessive level of holding of international reserves can have serious repercussions for the local economy and adverse spillovers to the international financial system. However, there is little consensus on the optimal level of holding. The proposed project, instead of presenting theoretical arguments for the optimal level, studies the empirical determinants of international reserve holdings. In addition to the canonical economic factors considered in the literature, the project highlights the dependence of an economy’s demand for international reserves on the behavior of others. One form of interdependence is dubbed “keeping up with the Joneses” phenomenon. The rivalry in hoarding is documented in a few previous studies. The desire of curtailing crisis contagion provides another reason why an economy’s hoarding decision depends on the actions of others. The current project will assess a) the presence of the Joneses and contagion curtailment effects, b) if these effects vary over time, and c) if these two factors help, in addition to canonical economic factors, to explain the patterns of hoarding of international reserves in various historical time periods. It is anticipated that the project can shed useful insight on competitive hoarding behavior and determinants of demand for international reserves, and on evaluating whether an economy holds too little or too much international reserves. 經濟體囤積國際儲備，以預防及緩解由金融危機和突兀資本流出引起的經濟困難。一般認為，不足或過高的國際儲備可能對當地經濟產生嚴重反響,及對國際金融體系產生不良溢出效應。但是，文獻沒有最優國際儲備水平的共識。當前擬議項目，不是提出最優水平的理論論據，而是用線性回歸和面板數據回歸技術研究國際儲備持有量的實證決定因素。除了文獻中考慮的典型經濟因素外，現項目突出個別經濟體國際儲備需求對其他經濟體囤積行為的反應。“跟上瓊斯”現象是囤積國際儲備相互依存的一種形式。以前一些研究亦有記載這類對抗型的囤積行為。經濟體囤積國際儲備另一個理由為減少危機蔓延感染 - 這也是其他經濟體囤積行為影響個別經濟囤積決策取的另一個原因。 當前項目將評估a）瓊斯現象和削減危機感染效應的存在，b）這些現象和效應是否隨時間而變化，c）相對典型經濟因素來說, 這兩個因素有或沒有闡釋在各個歷史時期 國際儲備囤積的邊際解釋力。預計項目可以對競爭性囤積行為和對國際儲備需求的決定因素，以及評估經濟體是否擁有太少或太多的國際儲備提供有用的見解。

11500617.label: Realisation of objectives
11500617.value: As indicated in the midterm report, we presented our findings at that time in a conference. These findings focused on the international reserve holdings of selected Asian economies, and various regional neighborhood effects. We incorporated comments and suggestions received from the conference, and prepared the research paper “The Hoarding of International Reserves: It’s a neighborly day in Asia.” Our paper shows that, by incorporating trade links, the refined Joneses effect improves its power to explain the build-up of reserves, a country that finds itself more vulnerable than its regional neighbors would tend to accumulate more reserves, and a common regional factor related to current-account balances spurs further reserve accumulation. Contrary to previous analyses, by accounting for alternate refinements of catching up with the Joneses effect, our results suggest that only a couple of Asian countries have been holding excessive reserves. Some were actually holding less international reserves than would be optimal in the presence of neighborhood effects. Further, as stated in the midterm report, we further developed the idea and extended the analysis to cover other economies and other pertinent determinants of international reserve holdings. The outcome is a research paper “The currency composition of international reserves, demand for international reserves, and global safe assets” (with Joshua Aizenman and XingWang Qian) that examines determinants of the international reserves currency composition before and after the Global Financial Crisis. The paper applies the annual data of 58 countries, we confirm that countries that trade more with the US, euro zone, UK, and Japan, and issue more debt denominated in the big four currencies (US dollar, euro, pound, and yen) hoard more international reserves in these currencies. We find scale effects in which countries tend to diversify from the big four currencies as they increase their international reserves per GDP and that a growing shortage of global safe assets induces countries to hold more big four currencies. Countries hold less big four currencies as international reserves after the 2008 Global Financial Crisis, while they hold more of such currencies since the tapering of the Fed’s quantitative easing. The 2008 Global Financial Crisis and quantitative easing tapering weakened and sometimes reversed the effect of several economic factors. We also find that TARGET2 balances matter for the currency composition of international reserves in the euro zone; commodity-exporting countries tend to diversify their international reserves from the big four currencies when their terms of trade improve; and that the valuation effects induced by Euro/USD exchange rate changes diminish the significance of the Global Financial Crisis in explaining the currency composition of international reserves. In sum, the five project objectives – as listed below – have been achieved by the completion of these two research papers and the resulting findings.

11500617.label: Major findings and research outcome
11500617.value: As indicated above, two research papers are prepared from the project. They are “The Hoarding of International Reserves: It’s a neighborly day in Asia” (with XingWang Qian and Eli Remolona), and “The currency composition of international reserves, demand for international reserves, and global safe assets” (with Joshua Aizenman and XingWang Qian). The first paper focuses on the international reserve holdings of selected Asian economies, and various regional neighborhood effects. The second paper covers 58 countries around the world, extends the scope of the analysis, and examines determinants of the international reserves currency composition before and after the Global Financial Crisis. In the first paper, we find that refining the Joneses effect to take account of trade links strengthens its power to explain the build-up of reserves. We also observe that a country that finds itself more vulnerable than its regional neighbors would tend to accumulate more reserves. Finally, we find that a common regional factor related to current-account balances spurs further reserve accumulation. Contrary to previous analyses, our results suggest that only a couple of Asian countries have been holding excessive reserves. Some were actually holding less reserves than would be optimal in the presence of neighborhood effects. In the second paper, we confirm that countries that trade more with the US, euro zone, UK, and Japan, and issue more debt denominated in the big four currencies (US dollar, euro, pound, and yen) hoard more international reserves in these currencies. We also document time variability of international reserves hoarding behavior, that is affected by the level of hoarding, the availability of global safe assets, the quantitative easing policy, the euro zone TARGET2 balances, the term of trade, and the valuation effect.

11500617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11500617.value: Given the continuing evolution of the global market conditions due to the trade dispute and impacts of the coronavirus outbreak, countries are likely to adjust their policies of hoarding of international reserves. Thus, it is prudent to stay abreast of developments in the international financial market and resulting modification of the international reserves hoarding behavior

11500617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11500617.value: While some view the hoarding of international reserves is reflective of a country’s economic heft, some see it is a source of global instability. For instance, china’s humongous scale of international reserves has raised a few eyebrows in the international community. Some countries; including the US, asserted that China (and other emerging markets in Asia) has adopted the mercantilism policy and accumulated an excessive level of international reserves, that inflicted economic hardships to its trading partners and caused global imbalances and instability. To address this concern, one has to answer the overarching question of whether, say, China’s level of international reserves holding is “excessive” or too much. Our research project essentially points out that we have to determine the appropriate level of holding before assessing whether the holding is being excessive or not. Indeed, our empirical analysis shows that the commonly made accusations about holding too much or too little international reserves may not be true when the determinants of demand for international reserves have been considered. Further, the appropriate level of international reserves holding can change over time, as the conditions in the global market evolve.

11501117.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11501117.value: 服务水平在动态库存系统中的运营影响

11501117.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11501117.value: Prof Chao, Xiuli Prof LU, Ye

11501117.label: Project Objectives
11501117.value: Characterize the optimal inventory control policy for a periodic review inventory system over an infinite horizon that explicitly incorporates the impact of stockout on future demand. Provide valuable managerial insights to the decision makers who need to understand when they should incorporate this effect in their inventory decisions, and how to operate such a system effectively. Develop algorithms to find efficient solutions that can be implemented in practice.
rows: Characterize the optimal inventory control policy for a periodic review inventory system over an infinite horizon that explicitly incorporates the impact of stockout on future demand.
Provide valuable managerial insights to the decision makers who need to understand when they should incorporate this effect in their inventory decisions, and how to operate such a system effectively.
Develop algorithms to find efficient solutions that can be implemented in practice.

11501117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11501117.value: When customers often experience stockout in a store, they will switch to other stores for a better service. This intuition is verified by empirical studies that have shown that stockout service level affects future demand. However, the vast literature on inventory control has largely ignored this effect. In this project, we investigate the impact of the stockout service level on the firm's profit and its operational policies. We consider a periodic review inventory system in which demand in a period is encouraged by good service levels in previous periods. We want to investigate how the optimal inventory control policies for inventory systems with stockout-dependent demand differentiate from those for the classic inventory models without stockout effect. We try to offer insights on how to effectively manage these systems. We also want to identify market conditions under which the firm's profit loss due to neglecting stockout-dependent demand is most significant. 当顾客在一家店里经常买不到货时，他们会转到服务更好的店里去。大量的实证研究发现，受缺货影响的服务水平会影响到今后的需求。然而在库存管理的文献中，这一点往往被忽略了。在这个项目中，我们来探索受缺货影响的服务水平对零售商利润和运营策略的影响。在我们的动态库存管理系统中，好的服务水平可以带来更多的回头客。我们想看一看，这个新的系统下，最优库存管理的策略会发生什么变化。我们希望为管理者运营这个新的系统提供一些启示，并且探索在什么样的市场环境下，这个新的库存管理系统可以带来更多的利润。

11501117.label: Realisation of objectives
11501117.value: All the original project objectives have been successfully accomplished. We consider a periodic-review stochastic inventory system in which demand in a period is increased by high service levels and decreased by low service levels in earlier periods. We show that the optimal inventory control for this inventory system is a service-level-dependent base-stock policy and that there is a target service level that the firm should maintain. However, this target service level is dependent on the initial service level. Under some mild conditions, we show that the target service levels form a comfort zone such that if the initial service level lies outside the zone, then the dynamic optimal service levels will monotonically converge to it, but if the initial service level is within the comfort zone, it will stay where it is. We further show that the profit loss due to the neglect of stockout-dependent demand can be significant, and we identify the scenarios in which the firm's profit loss is the most severe. Moreover, motivated by the practice of a global purchasing agent, we extend our analysis to a game theoretical setting, where two upstream manufacturers compete in selling to the same retailer by varying their service levels. The equilibrium choice of the manufacturers turn out to be full-credit returns policies, which are commonly observed in practice although not predicted by previous theories.

11501117.label: Major findings and research outcome
11501117.value: Empirical studies have shown that stockout affects future demand and a company's bottom line. However, the vast body of literature on inventory optimization has largely ignored this effect. In this project, we investigate the effect of stockout on the firm's operations policies and total discounted profit. We consider a periodic-review stochastic inventory system in which demand in a period is increased by high service levels and decreased by low service levels in earlier periods. We show that the optimal inventory control for this inventory system is a service-level-dependent base-stock policy and that there is a target service level that the firm should maintain. However, this target service level is dependent on the initial service level. Under some mild conditions, we show that the target service levels form a comfort zone such that if the initial service level lies outside the zone, then the dynamic optimal service levels will monotonically converge to it, but if the initial service level is within the comfort zone, it will stay where it is. We further show that the profit loss due to the neglect of stockout-dependent demand can be significant, and we identify the scenarios in which the firm's profit loss is the most severe.

11501117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11501117.value: We showed the impact of customer service on the long-term profitability of the firm and thus call for attention to the effect of the operational decisions on strategic performance indicators. In this project, we have studied inventory decisions. There are other operational decisions that will affect both short-term and long-term profitability and that should be lifted up to a more strategic position such as pricing and assortment planning. Currently, operational decision-making models for such decisions all focus on only short-term profit. More research should be done to reevaluate the way of such decision-makings by incorporating strategic concerns.

11501117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11501117.value: Service level matters to firms' long-term images. When deciding their inventory policies, firms should consider not only the effect of their decisions on the short-term profits but also consider the effects on customers' long-term perception. This way of thinking requires an updated, new method of computing the optimal inventory policies, which is a more deliberate policy that balances the short-term gain versus long-term profitability.

11501717.label: Project Objectives

11501717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11501717.value: Research on leader-member exchange social comparison (LMXSC) has generally shown that when an individual perceives his/her exchange relationship with the leader to be better than that of a comparison target (i.e., downward LMXSC), he/she tends to present better work attitudes, well-being, and performance (Vidyarthi et al., 2010; Henderson et al., 2008). Almost all empirical research is conducted at the individual or team level (e.g., Henderson et al., 2009), but generally neglects the fact that LMXSC occurs primarily at the dyadic level, which involves two members (i.e., it is a relational phenomenon). As a result, most studies fail to understand how, why, and when a member’s engagement in LMXSC may influence the actions of the other member in a dyad (i.e., interpersonal consequences; Tse, Lam, Lawrence, & Huang, 2013). Given that a team is composed of dyads with LMX of different quality, which makes coworkers’ LMX comparisons largely unavoidable, it is important to understand the role of LMXSC in coworkers’ interactions. This project contributes in this respect by investigating how a member’s (actor’s) actions toward the other member (target) is shaped by the target’s superiority resulting from a downward LMXSC with the actor. Drawing on theories of social comparison (Festinger, 1954) and emotion-as-social-information (EASI; Van Kleef, 2009), we suggest that a target’s positive perception of his/her LMX in comparison with that of the actor will elicit distinct pride displays (authentic vs. hubristic pride; Tracy & Robins, 2007) which serve as emotional cues to shape the actor’s behavior. Our own studies, for example, suggest that social comparison elicits distinct interpersonal emotions (Lam, 2009) and, in particular, that hostile emotion resulting from LMXSC is among the most proximal causes for aggressive interpersonal behavior (Tse, Lam, Gu, & Lin, 2015), preventing individuals from engaging in helpful acts (Tse, Lam, et al., 2013). Importantly, such behaviors are largely contingent on teams’ cooperative goals (Lam, Van der Vegt, Walter, & Huang, 2011; Walter, Lam, et al., 2015). Extrapolating from these findings, we propose a dual-pathway model of LMXSC positing that: (1) a target’s LMXSC, via displays of authentic and hubristic pride, may differentially drive the actor to increase/decrease behaviors that help/harm the target; and (2) a team’s cooperative goals may function as a cross-level moderator, influencing the indirect linkage between LMXSC and interpersonal helping/harming. Using multimethod studies, we highlight the relational consequences and psychological mechanisms of LMXSC, assisting organizations to better manage leader-member-coworker relationships. 領導-成員交換關係社會比較（LMXSC）的研究指出，當個人認為領導與自己的關係(LMX)比參照對象要好時（Downward LMXSC），會傾向有更好的工作態度、表現及更高的工作滿意度（Vidyarthi et al., 2010; Henderson et al., 2008）。現時的研究大多從個人和團隊的層面進行探討（如 Henderson et al., 2009），卻忽略了LMXSC現象主要出現於雙人層面，當中包含兩位成員。然而，許多研究都未有以一對的形式探究一位成員的LMXSC影響另一成員的行為，與及其方式、原因和時間點都未有深究（Tse, Lam, Lawrence, & Huang, 2013）。一個團隊由多對不同品質的LMX成員組成，以致同事間LMX的比較難以避免，因此要瞭解LMXSC在同事交流中的角色至關重要。為此，本研究將探討當一位成員認為自己與領導的關係比另一成員好時，其中產生的優越感如何影響另一成員對其作出的行動。 根據社會比較理論（Festinger, 1954）和情緒社會信息（Emotion-as-social information; Van Kleef, 2009），本研究提出當一位成員認為自己的LMX比另一成員 (i.e., actor [行為者])好時，會誘使他明顯地展示自豪感（真實自豪與自大自豪，Tracy & Robins, 2007），成為影響行為者行動的情感線索。我們的研究亦發現社會比較會引起明顯的人際情感（Lam, 2009），尤其是LMXSC引發的敵意感是導致傷人行為的最大原因（Tse, Lam, Gu, & Lin, 2015），阻止人們幫助他人（Tse, Lam, et al., 2013），關鍵的是此等行為主要取決於團隊的協作目標（Lam, Van der Vegt, Walter, & Huang, 2011; Walter, Lam, et al., 2015）。根據這些發現，本研究提出一個LMXSC的雙路徑模式並作出以下假設：（一）一位員工的LMXSC透過展示其真實自豪和自大自豪感可能會特別誘使行為者增加或減少幫助或傷害性的行為；以及（二）團隊的協作目標可發揮調節作用，影響LMXSC與人際間互助或互害的間接聯繫。本研究採取一系列方法探討LMXSC所引伸的關聯影響和心理機制，以協助機構更有效管理領導、成員和同事間的關係。

11501717.label: Realisation of objectives
11501717.value: Across two independent field studies, we investigated how coworkers’ LMXSCs are interactively related to the reciprocal affiliative help (vs. harm) between the actor and the target and tested whether such affiliation mediates the impact of LMXSC on actor-target exchange behavioural outcomes. These investigations have satisfied both objectives 1 and 2. In addition, we further examined how the interaction between LMXSCs is moderated by team contextual factor (i.e., cooperative team goals). These investigations have satisfied objective 3.

11501717.label: Major findings and research outcome
11501717.value: The results of social relations analyses across two field studies and one experimental study revealed a two-way interaction pattern, demonstrating that the actor’s LMXSC interacted with the target’s LMXSC to affect affiliative help (rather than the harmful acts). Specifically, the actor’s LMXSC was negatively related to affiliative help only when the target’s LMXSC was low. In other words, affiliation between the actor and target was higher only when both parties’ LMXSC were lower. This co-workers’ affiliation was positively related to the co-workers’ exchange relationship quality and mediated the impact of LMXSC on co-workers’ exchange relations. This two-way interaction, however, was not moderated by cooperative team goals nor mediated by the pride displays. Our additional experiment also revealed the underlying mechanism (perceived helpfulness of the co-worker) for the impact of the interaction of LMXSCs on affiliation. Based on these results, we have produced a conference paper that was presented the Annual Conference of the Academy of Management in 2018. We have also developed a journal article which has been accepted by Personnel Psychology.

11501717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11501717.value: While the present research focuses on the positive side of LMX dyadic comparison, it would also be very interesting to extend the present findings to alternative, negative interpersonal outcomes. For example, when an employee perceives a coworker’s LMX to be lower than their own (i.e., high-LMX dyadic comparison), it likely elicits distancing behavior directed towards the lower-LMX coworker because the latter may be perceived as of inferior status and thus as someone not to be associated with (Washington & Zajac, 2005). Therefore, when both members perceive their LMX to be higher than the other’s, it may induce mutual social exclusion. Future studies could explore these possibilities to gain a more complete understanding of the joint effect of both members’ LMX dyadic comparisons.

11501717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11501717.value: Members compare their differential leader-member exchanges (LMXs) to understand the triadic relationship (Member A, Member B, and their common leader); this will affect how members interact. Prior research based on balance theory assumes that the two members have a consensus on the structure of the triadic relationship, to argue that when Member A perceives their LMX to be lower than that of Member B, such an LMX imbalance would drive Member A to interact negatively with Member B. Comparison of LMX, however, reflects one’s subjective perception, which may not be shared by the other. Therefore, we draw on social comparison theory to examine both members’ comparisons of LMX simultaneously and suggest that when they both perceive the other’s LMXas better than their own, they may engage more in affiliative behaviors and develop a higher-quality coworker exchange (CWX). The results of two studies consistently supported these hypotheses. This research extends our understanding of LMX in triadic relations and demonstrates that mismatched perceptions of LMX dyadic comparison between two members (i.e., both perceive an LMX imbalance) could motivate members to develop a positive relationship.

11501917.label: Project Objectives
11501917.value: Develop a unified time-consistent dynamic mean-variance analysis framework for integrated operational and financial hedging strategy in managing commodity risk. Explore the structure of the optimal time-consistent policies for the underlying dynamic program of the joint financial hedging, inventory replenishments from both a spot market and through long-term bilateral contracts. Analyze the distinct roles of operational instruments (e.g., inventory and long-term contract) and financial hedges to gain managerial insights into the commodity risk management problem. Identify the conditions under which operational hedges and financial hedges can be separated. Extend the analysis to analyze the systems with backorders, lead times, and price-sensitive demand and nonzero transactional costs. Implement the model using real world data and use data analytics and our decision analysis to provide practical insights for commodity sourcing and risk management for practitioners.

11501917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11501917.value: Managing commodity risks represents one of the key challenges for raw materials sourcing and procurement in supply chain management. A key characteristic of well-functioning and liquid commodity markets is coexistence of spot markets and contract markets for physical delivery and financial markets which provide derivatives for risk management. Hence, it is important to integrate physical operations and financial hedging in the raw material commodity supply management. This project aims to study the integrated operational and financial hedging problem for raw material commodities in a dynamic setting. In particular, we will investigate the interactive roles of long-term contract with volumetric flexibility as an operational hedge, spot trading and financial hedging. It is known that the dynamic hedging problems are generally analytically challenging. We will develop a modeling framework and methodology to analyze the integrated operational and financial hedging problem for raw material commodities in a dynamic setting. We take a portfolio view and adopt the well-established mean-variance framework from the financial literature. Under a time-consistent policy, we formulate the problem into a dynamic programming model with two levels of recursion which is very complex compared to traditional inventory models. Tackling such a challenge will allow us to have an in-depth understanding on the role of different operational (such as inventory and long-term contract) and financial (such as futures and options) instruments in managing the commodity risks and the strategy to manage them. Finding an effective optimal solution for such a problem requires new insights and new analytical methods, which allows us to make a significant methodological contribution to supply chain management area. We will also implement the model using real world data to provide practical insights and promote analytics as the commodity prices and financial derivatives prices can be readily accessed. The managerial implications of this study will certainly help supply chain managers to improve their commodity risk management strategies. The PI has been working on dynamic inventory problems for many years and also has been working on related models for a few years, which offers a fresh direction for taking up the challenges proposed here. 大宗商品风险管理是全球原材料采购和供应管理中的一个关键挑战。一个机制完善和流动性好的大宗商品市场往往同时存在现货市场、合约（包括期货）市场和提供金融衍生产品的金融市场。因此，把实物运营和金融衍生工具结合起来管理大宗商品的市场风险是非常重要的。 本项目正是为了研究如何把实物运作和金融对冲手段结合起来动态的管理原材料大宗商品的风险。我们将研究如何利用具有数量柔性的供应链长期合同，现货交易和金融对冲在管理大宗商品风险的相互作用和关系。这样一个动态风险管理的问题在分析上是具有显著的挑战性的—这很多程度上是因为动态风险度量具有时间不一致的问题。 在项目中，我们将提出一个新的建模框架和方法来分析如何在动态的环境中将运作和金融对冲策略集成起来管理大宗商品的风险。通过投资组合的视角，我们引入投资组合优化领域的经典的动态的均值—方差模型。我们将从一类时间一致的策略出发，通过动态规划的递规表达式来找到最优的时间一致的策略，并且在这个策略下来研究集成运营和金融对冲策略在原材料大宗商品风险管理中的意义。我们还将通过分析市场数据来进一步加深对动态风险管理的理解，展示我们的解决方案，并给出具有实践意义的建议和洞见。

11502017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11502017.value: We explore the staggered introduction of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (PCAOB) inspection regime for non-U.S. auditors as exogenous shocks to the stringency of public audit oversight in the perception of institutional investors. Looking at a sample of foreign firms listed in the U.S. and audited by non-U.S. auditors, we investigate whether these firms’ potential institutional investors value the monitoring provided by the PCAOB inspection program, and thus be more willing to hold these firms’ stocks if their auditors are exposed to PCAOB inspections. Given institutional investors’ home bias (preference to invest in domestic firms), we expect that the more stringent public audit oversight will help foreign firms to attract more institutional investors from a country other than their country of origin (e.g., the U.S. or other country). Using a difference-in-differences research design with firm fixed effects, we intend to investigate whether U.S. listed foreign firms exhibit an increased number and share ownership in U.S./other country institutional investors after their auditors are subject to PCAOB inspection access. We further investigate whether this effect is stronger for clients of non-Big 4 auditors compared with Big 4 auditors. In general, we intend to examine whether institutional investors of U.S. listed foreign firms appreciate the more stringent regulatory audit oversight as facilitated by the PCAOB’s international inspection program, and whether this is particularly the case for firms audited by small auditors. We contribute to the literature in three important ways. First, our work is among the first attempts to examine impacts of PCAOB inspection access on institutional investor home bias. Our work examines whether institutional investors trade in the U.S. market appreciate the PCAOB’s inspection program, and provides direct evidence on whether institutional investors benefit from the potentially improved audit quality brought about by a more stringent public audit oversight. Second, this study contributes to prior literature on the usefulness of PCAOB inspections. There are studies arguing about both pros and cons of the PCAOB inspection program. This study helps to explore another potential benefit of PCAOB inspections: alleviation of institutional investor home bias. Third, so far no studies look at how PCAOB inspections affect big versus small non-U.S. auditors. We separately examine how PCAOB inspection access affects institutional investments in clients of Big 4 versus non-Big 4 auditors. Our study is important because they help to show that, compared to non-Big 4, whether Big 4 auditors benefit less from PCAOB inspections.

11502017.label: Realisation of objectives
11502017.value: I have achieved all the research objectives in a paper, “Does the Threat of a PCAOB Inspection Mitigate U.S. Institutional Investors’ Home Bias?”, accepted for publication in Contemporary Accounting Research in April 2021. The results on the effect of auditor exposure to PCAOB inspections on other country institutional investments are similar to the U.S. results reported in the published version of the paper, but we did not report them following the editor’s and reviewers’ comments issued during the revision process at Contemporary Accounting Research. Following the editor’s and reviewers’ comments, we did not report the results on the impacts of public audit oversight in mitigating institutional investor home bias for clients of large and small auditors because they do not differ. Below I more clearly explain how my co-author and I achieved the project objectives in more detail. The staggered implementation of the PCAOB’s international inspection regime enables us to apply a research design that helps dispel concerns about contemporaneous regulatory changes and unrelated economic shocks. Given that foreign firms become better known in the capital markets under this stricter public audit oversight, we expect that U.S. institutional investors will acquire larger equity stakes in those U.S.-listed foreign firms to reflect the lower information asymmetry. Accordingly, we predict a positive relation between PCAOB inspection exposure and the equity positions held by U.S. institutional investors in U.S. listed foreign firms. Next, we deepen our analysis by evaluating whether any link between PCAOB inspection access and U.S. institutional investors’ home bias varies systematically with the foreign country’s surrounding institutional infrastructure. We extend Lamoreaux (2016) by analyzing whether the presence of a sound local audit oversight system mitigates the negative relation between PCAOB inspection access allowance and U.S. institutional investor home bias. Our research helps inform the debate on the role that countries’ institutional infrastructure plays in shaping the impact of the PCAOB inspection threat. To provide evidence on our research questions, we assemble a sample of foreign firms audited by U.S. and non-U.S. auditors from 1999 to 2015. Consistent with our first prediction, we find that the adjusted percentage share ownership and the number of U.S. institutional investors rise after foreign firms’ auditors become subject to PCAOB inspection. The increase in U.S. institutional holdings is also economically material: if the auditor’s home country begins to allow PCAOB inspections, our coefficient estimates translate into the adjusted share ownership and the number of U.S. institutional investors increasing by, on average, 220 basis points and 4.52 institutional investors, respectively, which for perspective represents 9.17% and 8.60% of the mean. In the event that a firm’s auditor becomes subject to PCAOB inspection, our evidence implies that it attracts, on average, US$ 149.95 million more U.S. institutional investment and 4.52 more U.S. institutional investors. This evidence supports the intuition that U.S. institutional investors become more eager to hold equity stakes in foreign firms after the threat of a PCAOB inspection motivates these firms’ auditors to supply stricter external monitoring. We undertake extensive analysis to evaluate the sensitivity of our core results. First, we conduct a time trend test and a matched sample analysis to help empirically validate the parallel trends assumption that underlies our differences-in-differences (DID) research design. Second, we verify that our evidence on the negative relation between PCAOB access and U.S. institutional investors’ home bias is robust to controlling for actual PCAOB inspections. Third, we show that our main evidence holds in 95 of 96 regressions when we successively remove firms from each individual country or when we estimate weighted least squares regressions where the least weight is assigned to countries responsible for a larger fraction of the sample (e.g., Fernandes and Gonenc 2016). Fourth, we find nearly identical evidence when we restrict the sample by requiring that auditors/companies are present in both the pre- and post-inspection access allowance periods. In cross-sectional analysis, we show that the benefit of the PCAOB inspection threat in constraining U.S. institutional investors’ home bias is concentrated in foreign countries without a strict local auditor oversight system. We also document that the importance of the PCAOB inspection threat to mitigating home bias is concentrated in active U.S. institutional investors relative to their passive counterparts. Additionally, we find that the impact of the PCAOB inspection threat alleviating U.S. institutional investor home bias only applies to firms from countries that grant PCAOB access later; i.e., after the onset of the inspection program in 2005 (late adopters). We undertake two additional analyses that further corroborate our main findings. First, we run a path analysis that verifies that the impact of PCAOB inspection access on home bias works through improved audit/financial reporting quality. Second, in a cross-country design, we extend our tests to local companies audited by auditors that are inspected by the PCAOB or subject to the PCAOB inspection threat. Complementing Fung et al.’s (2017) and Shroff’s (2020) focus on actual inspections, we find strong, robust evidence implying that the home bias that U.S. institutional investors exhibit for non-U.S.-listed clients falls when their auditors experience the PCAOB inspection threat (or an actual inspection, reinforcing Fung et al. (2017) and Shroff (2020)).

11502017.label: Major findings and research outcome
11502017.value: We exploit the staggered introduction of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board’s (PCAOB) international inspection program to examine the role that the stringency of public audit oversight plays in shaping U.S. institutional investors’ home bias. Analyzing a sample of foreign firms listed in the U.S., we evaluate whether U.S. institutional investors hold larger equity stakes in these firms if their auditors are exposed to the threat of a PCAOB inspection, which is a longstanding issue that reflects investor portfolio decisions. In a differences-in-differences framework, we find that U.S. listed foreign firms enjoy an increase in U.S. institutional investors’ equity positions after their auditors become subject to PCAOB inspection access. Cross-sectional analysis implies that the benefit of the PCAOB inspection threat in mitigating U.S. institutional investors’ home bias is concentrated in: foreign countries without a strict local audit oversight system; active U.S. institutional investors that are known to value accounting transparency; and firms from countries that grant PCAOB access later (after the onset of its international inspection program in 2005). Our evidence indicates that foreign firms become better known in the capital markets under the PCAOB inspection program, U.S. institutional investors accordingly acquire larger equity stakes in those U.S. listed foreign firms due to the lower information asymmetry under the PCAOB inspection threat.

11502017.value: The PCAOB inspection allowance status data investigated in this project could be used for other future potential projects examining the PCAOB's oversigt role.

11502017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11502017.value: We contribute to the public policy discourse by analyzing whether U.S. institutional investors’ home bias is sensitive to whether foreign firm auditors are subject to PCAOB inspection. Our evidence reconciles with both the PCAOB’s (2010) and the SEC’s (2013) position that U.S. investors are deprived of the potential benefits of inspections when foreign auditors are excluded from the PCAOB’s international inspection program. Given that many governments invoke national sovereignty concerns and conflicts with home country laws to justify barring the PCAOB from conducting inspections within their borders (PCAOB 2010), our analysis adds to recent research supporting that these inspections benefit firms in these countries.

11502117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11502117.value: The objective of this study is to investigate how different simple methods can help people to reduce their energy consumption. Existing literature has identified that reporting social comparison information on power consumption can help to reduce power consumption. However, the effect was found to be quite small (while significant) and decayed quickly. In the current study, we propose a new method to solve this problem: goal setting. Our objective is to investigate whether our new method will be more effective than social comparison. We will conduct the field experiments by cooperating with the China Light Power Company in Hong Kong. In the field experiment, we will investigate how reduction in energy consumption can be achieved by social comparison based energy reports, and goal setting. These methods are based on insights from behavior economics. In the social comparison treatments, we investigate the effectiveness of social comparison in determining power consumption when there is feedback on level of power consumption versus without. We will modify the power bill by adding information on how the power consumption of the consumer compares to their neighbours. The hypothesis is that those with high levels of power consumption will reduce their consumption level relative to the case where social comparison information is not available. In the treatments on goal setting, we systematically investigate the effectiveness of goal setting (commitment) in energy saving by having treatments with binding goals vs. non-binding goals, and with feedback versus without feedback. In the binding goal setting treatment, participants will receive a discount when they reached the goal, and pay more if they can’t. Our study will investigate both the short run, and the long run effect of the methods. Our results will not only have important scientific implications, but also have important policy implications for inducing efficient energy consumption and promoting environmental protection.

11502817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11502817.value: Voluntary disclosures, particularly management earnings forecasts, represent the most dominant channel through which corporate managers convey their inside information to the capital market. Prior research has examined equity or debt financing, shareholder litigation, proprietary cost, and various corporate governance mechanisms as potential determinants of the variations in voluntary disclosure (Healy and Palepu 2001; Hirst et al. 2008; Beyer et al. 2010). However, few studies have examined how trading activities in the secondary markets affect disclosures. One recent exception is the study by Li and Zhang (2015), which examines how short sellers in the secondary stock market affect management forecasts. While Li and Zhang show that short selling pressure has an effect on forecast precision, they fail to provide evidence that short selling activities affect the frequency or likelihood of management forecasts. Our study extends this line of literature by examining the effect of the options market on managerial decisions to issue voluntary disclosures. We argue that options trading activity can potentially increase managerial voluntary disclosures for two reasons. First, the active search and discovery of private information by options traders make it more difficult for managers to withhold information. This effect should force managers to be more forthcoming in their disclosure behaviors because of litigation or reputation concerns. We call this argument the disciplinary effect of the options market. Second, Luo (2016) suggests that managers tend to learn from stock prices in forming their earnings forecasts. If this is true, managers should be more likely to observe new information from options or stock prices after options listing and be more likely to issue or update their earnings forecasts. We call this argument the learning effect of the options market. In our empirical tests, we plan to use a sample of firms with options listing events and a propensity-score-matched sample of control firms to conduct difference-in-differences analysis. We predict the following: (1) Relative to control firms, options listing firms increases their likelihood and frequency of management forecasts upon options listing; (2) The main effect is mainly driven by bad news forecasts; (3) The main effect is more pronounced for firms with higher litigation risk and firms with more active option trading. By identifying options trading activity as one important determinant of voluntary disclosures, our study contributes to both the voluntary disclosure literature and the emerging literature on the real effects of secondary market. 自愿披露，特别是管理层盈利预测，是公司经理向资本市场传递私有信息的最主要的渠道之一。现有的研究发现股本或债务融资，股东诉讼、竞争成本和各种治理机制等因素均会影响公司的自愿性信息披露。然而，二级市场交易活动如何影响自愿性信息披露仍刚刚起步。近期Li and Zhang（2015）研究二级市场的卖空行为如何影响管理层盈利预测。他们的研究发现由于短期卖空的压力，管理层担心坏消息对股价的负面影响加大，因此管理层不愿意给出更为精确的盈利预测，尤其是当预测的消息是负面的。 本文延展这个方向的研究，我们研究期权交易是否影响管理层盈利预测。 我们认为期权交易活动会增加管理层自愿披露的动机，一方面，由于期权交易者会积极寻找和发现市场没有反映的私有信息，这使得管理层隐瞒信息更加困难。出于诉讼或声誉的担忧,我们认为管理层会更早的披露他们的私有信息，尤其是负面消息。我们称这种说法为期权市场的戒律效应。另一方面，Luo（2016）发现管理层在进行盈利预测时也会从股票价格中获取信息。当股票价格由于期权交易变得更富含信息量，管理层应该更容易从股市里得到有用的新信息，因而更可能发布和更新其盈利预测。我们称这种说法为期权市场的学习效应。 在我们的实证检验中，我们计划选取一组公司,通过比较管理层盈利预测在option listing（有期权交易）前后的变化来研究期权交易对管理层盈利预测的影响。我们预测是，相对于控制公司，这类样本公司在有期权交易之后管理层会更多地发布盈余预测，尤其是对坏消息的预测。这种变化会在较高的诉讼风险和更活跃的期权交易更为显著。 过往研究一般专著与公司行为（包括披露行为）如何影响二级市场交易，我们希望我们的研究能帮助我们更好的理解二级市场交易对公司行为的反作用。

11502817.label: Realisation of objectives
11502817.value: After completing our primary empirical analysis and some initial write-up based on the initial objectives, we found a competing paper with a similar idea in circulation (https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=3425801). To avoid direct competition and get a better chance of publication, we decided to fine-tune our project direction. Instead of focusing on voluntary disclosure in general, we changed our focus to the style of qualitative disclosure utilizing a different shock as a semi-natural experiment. We appreciate the assessment panel approved our request to change the project objectives. We have successfully achieved all the revised objectives. We presented the completed paper at two international conferences (2020 Accounting and Finance Association of Australia and New Zealand Conference and Virtual 2020 CAAA Annual Conference Sessions). We also submitted the paper to The Accounting Review, one of the top-3 accounting journals, and passed the first round review.

11502817.label: Major findings and research outcome
11502817.value: This study examines the effect of litigation risk on the readability of corporate financial reports using the 1999 Silicon Graphics Inc. court ruling as a quasi-natural experiment. This ruling unexpectedly reduced the litigation risk of firms located in the states of the Ninth Circuit Court (treated firms). We find that the treated firms increase the readability of their financial reports after the ruling, relative to the control firms located in other states. This effect is concentrated in firms prone to shareholder litigation, firms with greater external financing needs, and firms reducing forward-looking disclosures following the ruling. The improvement of readability, however, is muted among firms engaging in earnings management. We also find that the treated firms with low pre-ruling 10-K readability have more informative 10-K reports after the ruling. Collectively, our findings support the notion that litigation risk contributes to low financial reporting readability.

11502817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11502817.value: We plan to revise the paper further based on the referee's comments and get this paper published in one of the top-5 accounting journals.

11502817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11502817.value: Extant studies provide ample evidence on the effect of litigation risk on the amount of information released through voluntary disclosure in general and management earnings forecasts in particular. However, we know relatively little about how litigation risk affects the way information is communicated, which has a significant impact on disclosure processing costs. Complex or unreadable disclosures heighten investors’ information processing costs, which in turn dampen the effectiveness of shareholder monitoring and price discovery (Blankespoor et al. 2020). It is important to understand the sources of disclosure complexity. Moreover, the continual effort by the SEC and the FASB in promoting plain English reporting is a clear testament to the significance of the issue related to complex disclosures and their processing costs. Our findings support the view that litigation concerns impede the readability of financial reports and thus speak directly to the issue of disclosure processing costs and the long-lasting concern of financial regulators (e.g., Blankespoor et al. 2020; Cox 2007; SEC 1998, 2019).
