11503617.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11503617.value: 便捷资源在平台生态系统中的作用和演化，以移动应用平台为例的实证分析

11503617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11503617.value: The exciting development in mobile devices and the success of mobile application platforms draw intensive research attentions (e.g., Ghose and Han 2014, Han Park and Oh 2015, Lee and Raghu 2014, Liu Au and Choi 2014, Qiu Gopal and Hann 2016, 2013). In a mobile application platform and more generally in platform-based ecosystems, boundary resources, the tools and regulations of platforms have critical impacts (Eaton et al. 2015). In the proposed project, we extend our understanding of the composition and effects of boundary resources in app platforms. To enable a data-centric discussion, we propose to build a system that tracks app platforms regarding the boundary resource provision and governance mechanisms. The system also collects data about application releases, updates, and sales. Using the observational data collected, we will first examine the impact of a particular boundary resource, the sponsored search, on developers’ platform choices and pricing decisions, leveraging on a quasi-experiment condition arising the sequential introductions of search advertising service to Android and iOS platforms. In the meantime, we will conduct a theoretical discussion and propose a framework and a measurement scale for boundary resource provision. The scale will be validated using interviews and surveys, which will be supplemented by text features extracted from the data collected by the system. The framework and the data collected will enable us to form a dynamic view of the evolution in boundary resource provision across app platforms. We will then explore opportunities to extend our empirical analysis regarding the impacts of boundary resources. The proposed research contributes to the literature on mobile application and platform-based ecosystem and has clear practice relevance. 互聯網和智能移動設備相关技术的快速发展，以及伴随而來的移動應用平台的建立近年來吸引了很多研究人員的關注（例如，Ghose and Han 2014，Han Park and Oh 2015，Lee and Raghu 2014，Liu Au and Choi 2014，Qiu Gopal and Hann 2016，2013）。以平台為中心的新一代移動互聯網經濟模式的組織形式帶來了許多亟待解決的理論問題。特別的，在移動應用平台和更普遍的基於平台的生態系統中（Platform-based Ecosystem），邊界資源（Boundary Resources），例如平台的工具和規則對平台的建設和發展有重要的影響（Eaton et al.，2015）。在本項目中，我們力求深化對應用程序平台中邊界資源的組成和影響的理論和實證認識。這一認知的建立要基於數據為中心的探討，所以我們在本項目中將構建一個跟踪邊界資源提供和治理機制的應用平台的系統。該系統還收集有關應用程序版本，更新和銷售的數據。 使用收集的觀察數據，我們將首先檢查特定邊界資源對開發人員平台選擇和定價決策的影響，利用在Android和iOS上搜索廣告服務順序推出的準實驗條件平台。同時，我們將進行理論討論，提出邊界資源提供的框架和計量尺度。規模將通過採訪和調查進行驗證，並將利用系統收集的數據進行文本特徵分析。收集的框架和數據將使我們能夠形成一個關於應用程序平台邊界資源提供演變的動態視圖。然後我們將探討擴大對邊界資源影響的實證分析的機會。

11504017.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11504017.value: 动态风险度量的仿真数据分析法

11504017.label: Project Objectives
11504017.value: We will formulate dynamic risk measurement problems and develop a regression-based approach to solve the problems. In particular, we will consider both linear regression and logistic regression models. We will study the statistical properties of the estimators of risk measures, and test their performances for various types of portfolios. We will apply regularization techniques, e.g., Lasso and ridge regression, to balance the tradeoff between bias and variance in the regression with large number of predictors, to select important risk factors, and to provide better predictions. We will also study the statistical properties of the regularized estimators of risk measures, and test their performances for various types of portfolios. We will investigate ways to combine structural information of simulation models and regression models to improve the prediction accuracy. In particular, we will consider variance reduction techniques in conjunction with regression models to provide better estimators of risk measures.

11504017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11504017.value: 实时监控风险指标是金融风险管理中的一项重要任务。传统的基于仿真的度量风险指标的方法实施起来非常耗时，因此无法用于实时监控。在本研究中，我们将尝试使用各类大数据分析方法，结合仿真本身特点，分析事前产生好的大量仿真数据，从而将仿真方法引入到实时风险监控中。

11504017.label: Realisation of objectives
11504017.value: All the project objectives have been successfully achieved. In particular, we have formulated a dynamic risk measurement problem as an online risk monitoring problem where offline simulation is used as a tool to predict the risk. A logistic regression model has been built and asymptotic properties of the resulting estimator have been established. Regularization techniques, especially Lasso and ridge regression, simulation model structure, and additional simulation budget have also been explored to enhance the prediction accuracy. Statistical properties of the regularized estimators of risk measures have been analyzed, and numerical testing has been conducted to illustrate their performances in risk management of financial portfolios. Structural information of simulation models has been incorporated into the proposed regression models to further improve its prediction accuracy. Variance reduction techniques such as change of measures and control variates have also been incorporated into regression models to enhance the performance of the resulting estimators.

11504017.label: Major findings and research outcome
11504017.value: The research objectives of the project have been successfully achieved. Outcomes of the project include three papers published in premier journals in the field, including INFORMS Journal on Computing, Naval Research Logistics, and Asia-Pacific Journal of Operational Research, and a working paper currently under review. In particular, in the paper titled "On risk monitoring using offline simulation" published in INFORMS Journal on Computing, we formulate a dynamic risk measurement problem as an online risk monitoring problem where offline simulation is used as a tool to predict the risk. A logistic regression model has been built and asymptotic properties of the resulting estimator have been established. Regularization techniques, simulation model structure, and additional simulation budget have also been explored to enhance the prediction accuracy. In the paper titled "On gamma estimation via matrix kriging" published in Naval Research Logistics, we propose three stochastic kriging-based methods and incorporate variance reduction techniques to fit the surface of the gamma matrix, which is an important risk-management indicator for financial derivative. In a more general framework of simulation-based decision making, we study the offline simulation online applications, published in a paper titled "Offline simulation online application: A new framework of simulation-based decision making". In a working paper titled "Building closed-form formula for real-time derivative pricing and Greeks calculation using offline simulation", we propose a gradient-enhanced stochastic kriging method to build a metamodel for price and Greeks of financial derivatives.

11504017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11504017.value: In the project, we have mainly focused on the applications of online application with offline simulation to financial risk measurement. We believe that this framework may also find other business applications where simulation serves as a tool of data generating process and learning of risk mappings. While in-depth investigation of the applications of this framework to other potential application is beyond the score of this project, we will further explore this direction in our future research.

11504017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11504017.value: In this project, we have investigated the use of offline simulation in dynamic risk measurement. By combining offline simulation and statistical learning methodologies, we propose a simulation analytics approach to risk monitoring and management, which may serve as a viable real-time decision making tool for risk managers. From a theoretical perspective, we establish asymptotic results for the proposed approach. From a practical perspective, the proposed approach can be effectively applied to the daily pricing and hedging of financial derivatives, adding a new simulation analytics tool to practitioners in financial industries.

11504417.label: Project Objectives
11504417.value: To develop a cognitive model of the antecedents of distrust (and trust) formation. To empirically validate the model in the context of healthcare websites and recommendations. To explore the issue of whether distrust can be repaired and trust can be sustained.

11504417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11504417.value: The primary focus of this proposal is to theorize and validate the factors leading to distrust, a critical barrier to Internet business, despite the increasing acceptance of online business activities in the digital economy. This will be validated in the context of online healthcare, which is gaining increasing popularity due to information asymmetry of increasingly well-educated and questioning common folks who seek to verify advices of medical providers through second- or multiple opinions, supposedly well-meaning but un-validated health-related articles and recommendations, and also difficulty of access by common folks to access affordable yet high quality healthcare. While online trust has been well-studied and validated in various studies of Internet commerce, with well-understood antecedents, that of distrust has received relatively less research attention. In this proposal, the antecedents that lead to distrust are abstracted from past referent research and a conceptual cognitive model of antecedents of distrust will be empirically validated. The model integrates past conceptualizations of Internet deception, attribution theory, trust and distrust. A number of studies will be conducted. The main study seeks to validate the distrust (versus trust) cognitive model on users of healthcare websites (specifically health recommendations and advice, such as for ailment treatments) in Greater China. The research can contribute to a better understanding of factors leading to distrust formation. Further, a follow-up study explores whether trust can be sustained, and distrust repaired. 這個建議有助於揭示不信任的先行因素，實證驗證了醫療保健網站上的信任和不信任模式。對於那些受到相對較少研究關注的網站,它可以通過提取不信任的先前條件來促進信賴文獻，對於前提因素相對較為已知的, 可作比較/對比信任的形成。擬議的模型將在大中國的醫療保健網站提供給用戶，對未有品質驗証及索償之保健網站提供建議給用戶。 通過探索性研究去尋求進一步調查不信任是否可以得到修補及信任是否可以持續。實際上，這個提案的結果可以為醫療保健網站的設計和治理提供更好的指引，特別是確定導致這些網站之不信任的潛在缺陷和/或建議。它還為衛生網站決策者提供指導及治理機制，網站設計如何能更有效地幫助用戶和網站識別可能導致不信任的提示，減輕不信任和促進信任的建議。

11504417.label: Major findings and research outcome
11504417.value: A research model comprising the distrust formation and trust formation towards healthcare websites is close to finalizing. The cognitive model integrates previous conceptualizations of Internet deception, attribution theory, trust and distrust. The antecedents of distrust are proposed based upon relevant literature. An important antecedent of the research model is the dissonance of information/recommendation. We have collected and analyzed data to show that different sources of information can provide better outcomes and accuracy of prediction of health issues. This research has been published, and this research grant acknowledged in the International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health (Li, Sia, Chen and Huang, 2021). We further conducted a preliminary research (an experiment) to explore whether the provision of multiple sources of healthcare information aggregated with the searched information can increase trust and credibility, while mitigating distrust towards a healthcare website. The preliminary findings indicated that multiple sources of information indeed could raise people's perception of information credibility and quality. The preliminary research has been written up as a working paper (Lee, Shen and Sia, 2021). Overall, a pilot study using an online experiment validating the entire research model has been conducted, and a fuller scale data collection be conducted to complete the research. **Due to the Covid situation, and also due to the PI taking a one-year unpaid leave from the home institution since the last 4 months of the project duration, the progress and research activities of this project has been somewhat delayed regrettably. **

11505217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11505217.value: High-dimensional structural dynamic factor models are useful tools to analyze the effects of an economic shock over time. A structural dynamic factor model (SDFM) extracts factors from a large number of variables to recover the space spanned by the unobserved economic shocks and fits the estimated factors using a conventional structural VAR model. Compared to a conventional low-dimensional VAR, a SDFM has the advantage that it uses much more information and does not lose the parsimony. Since the economic shocks are not observed, additional assumptions are required for identification purposes. The most commonly used identification strategy is to assume that the contemporaneous effects of the shock follow a recursive structure. This is a just-identified scheme where the number of restrictions is equal to the number of unknown parameters. In a factor model, however, the number of valid restrictions can be larger than the number of unknown parameters due to the high-dimensionality. Thus, the SDFM is often over-identified. Compared with a just-identified SDFM, using over-identifying restrictions have two main advantages. First, the estimation of the unknown parameters will be more accurate under over-identifying restrictions. Second, over-identifying restrictions can be tested so that practitioners can know if the identification conditions are satisfied or not. This project will generalize the existing method in several dimensions. It focuses on the identification and estimation of SDFMs under over-identified schemes, which improve the estimation accuracy. Also, we will use various types of identification conditions, which are more general than the commonly used recursive setups. The new method can estimate the parameters of interests under a combination of multiple identification strategies, such as short-run restrictions, long-run restrictions, external instruments, and heteroscedasticity.

11505217.label: Realisation of objectives
11505217.value: 1. This objective is achieved. The research results allow multiple types of recursive or non-recursive identifying restrictions, such as short-run restrictions, long-run restrictions, and external instruments. The identification using heteroskedasticity turns out to belong to a different family of restrictions, so the results are not reported but available upon request. 2. This objective is achieved. Theorem 1 develops conditions for global identification of the structural shock under full identification schemes. Theorems 2 and 3 develop condition for partial identification of structural shocks. 3. The objective is achieved. Two estimators are proposed in Section 4. Both estimators allow for multiple types of restrictions. 4. The objective is achieved. The asymptotic distributions of the new estimators are established in Theorems 4 and 5. 5. The objective is achieved. Vast simulation has been conducted. The simulation results show that the proposed estimators are more accurate than Stock and Watson's (2018) estimator under the same identifying restrictions. 6. The objective is achieved. The new estimators are applied to estimate the structural impulse responses of U.S. macroeconomic variables to unexpected oil shocks.

11505217.label: Major findings and research outcome
11505217.value: First, this paper defines the global identification of the structural IRFs in SDFMs and studies the impact of normalization. We show that if the structural IRFs are globally identified under one normalization, then they can be globally identified under any normalization. Some commonly used identification schemes, such as recursive ordering in factor-augmented VAR (FAVAR) , are valid only under some special and nonstandard normalization schemes that may require complicated computation. We argue that such complicated computation can be avoided by imposing restrictions that are always effective regardless of the normalization. As a result, one can always use the simplest normalization based on Principal Component Analysis (PCA). Second, we develop conditions under which the structural IRFs are globally identified in SDFMs . The theory allows for various types of restrictions and extends the seminal work of Rubio-Ramirez et al. (2010) from a low-dimensional SVAR to a high-dimensional SDFMs. A new theorem is established for the partial identification of a structural shock under non-recursive identification schemes in SDFMs. The new theorem covers some important scenarios (e.g., the example on the oil shock identification in Stock and Watson (2018)) that are not covered by Rubio-Ramirez et al. (2010). Third, we develop two estimators for the structural IRFs under various types of identifying restrictions (including short-run and long-run restrictions and external instruments). The first estimator searches an orthogonal matrix so that moment conditions are close to zero as much as possible. We use Cayley transform so that the constrained minimization can be reformulated as an unconstrained one. This estimator can be used in a fully or partially identified system. The second estimator is designed for partially identified schemes. It uses an iterative approach by carrying out eigendecomposition repeatedly. We establish the asymptotic distributions of both estimators. Our simulation shows that both estimators have substantially smaller root mean squared errors in comparison to Stock and Watson's (2018) estimator under the same overidentifying restrictions.

11505217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11505217.value: Current simulation results show that our estimators have large efficiency again (smaller estimation errors) compared to Stock and Watson's (2018) estimator. Since Stock and Watson's estimator uses an iterative algorithm, its asymptotic property is not well studied. Thus, a potential further extension is to establish the asymptotic properties of Stock and Watson's (2018) estimator, so that it becomes clearer why our estimators have efficiency again relative to their estimator.

11505217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11505217.value: This paper bridges a gap in the literature on the global identification of economic shocks in dynamic factor models using big datasets. The new results concern the full identification scheme where all economic shocks are identified and the partial identification scheme where some but not all economic shocks are identified. Two new estimators are developed and their properties in big data are established. Simulations show that our estimators perform well and have smaller estimation errors compared to existing methods. The proposed estimators are highly useful in the assessment of the effectiveness of macroeconomic policies, such as monetary and fiscal policies. The new estimators can also be used to study the dynamic impacts of some unexpected shock, such as the pandemic shock, on the economic system.

11505917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11505917.value: 網絡贊助廣泛應用於搜索引擎來促進贊助商的點擊率（例如，鏈接到其產品和網站），並成為搜索引擎最重要的收入來源之一。然而，最近的調查和研究顯示，互聯網用戶往往規避贊助搜索結果。這種規避降低了贊助搜索結果的點擊率，降低了贊助搜索這種商業模式的可行性。本項目旨在了解用戶對贊助搜索結果的規避，並在消費者對消費者（C2C）的電子商務的背景下尋求可行的方案。特別地，我們研究用戶如何處理偏離他們品牌偏好的贊助搜索結果。 本項目將涉及到幾個方面。第一，我們將從偏好建構和勸導知識的角度來解釋贊助搜索結果的規避。第二，我們將研究贊助品牌聲譽的中介效應。第三，我們將進一步研究當社會影響線索同時呈現在自然搜索結果（即非贊助搜索結果）和贊助搜索結果時，這些線索對降低贊助搜索結果規避的影響。 我們將進行一系列的實驗來驗證我們的假設。這個項目將有助於研究和實踐。在贊助品牌偏離用戶的品牌偏好的情景下，我們擴展了贊助搜索結果規避的現有理論和認識。該項目還將有助於建立社會影響線索在降低贊助搜索結果規避方面的前提條件。我們的結果也可以幫助商家有效地利用社會影響線索來降低用戶對贊助搜索結果的規避，從而提升贊助搜索模式的可行性。

11505917.label: Realisation of objectives
11505917.value: The two research objectives have been fully achieved. We have theorized the role of the brand reputation of a sponsored search result (SSR) in the relationship between online social influence cues and users’ avoidance of the SSR. Furthermore, we identified two theoretical accounts to articulate how users internalize a social cue when making their avoidance decisions, thereby offering theory-based strategies to reduce users’ SSR avoidance. We posited two moderated mediation effects by identifying two mediators related to these two accounts and two contingent factors that trigger the two mediators. The first account describes when users’ suspicion is low (e.g., when an encountered SSR deviates from users’ search preferences but features a well-known brand), how and under what condition their preference for the SSR can be increased through the internalization of a social cue. This is related to the first research objective. The second account focuses on the scenario wherein users are highly suspicious of the search service provider (e.g., when the SSR not only deviates from their search preferences but also features an unknown brand). In particular, the second account explicates how users’ suspicion could be reduced by the internalization of a social cue when they are provided with additional evidence to corroborate the high evaluations of the SSR as inferred from the social cue. This account is related to the second research objective. We conducted three laboratory experiments, and the results support our theoretical accounts. We uncovered the internalization mechanism of social influence on reducing suspicious users’ SSR avoidance in online settings. It also offers practical implications for online search service providers to facilitate online users’ decision-making in their search process.

11505917.label: Major findings and research outcome
11505917.value: The results from a series of laboratory experiments revealed the moderation role of brand reputation for the effects of various social cues on users’ avoidance of sponsored search results (SSR). Our empirical results also attested to the two theoretical accounts posited in our project. The major findings are reported in a manuscript that passed the first round review at a top-tier journal, Information Systems Research (ISR). We are currently revising it for the second review at ISR. DENG, Honglin; WANG, Weiquan; LIM, Kai H., “Effects of Online Social Influence Cues on Suspicious Users’ Avoidance of Sponsored Search Results: An Internalization Perspective,” under revision for 2nd round review at Information Systems Research. This project also produced other research findings that are not essential to the two research objectives. We reported these findings in the following paper accepted in Information Systems Research: DENG, Honglin; WANG, Weiquan; LI, Siyuan; LIM, Kai H., “Can Positive Online Social Cues Always Reduce User Avoidance of Sponsored Search Results?” MIS Quarterly, forthcoming.

11505917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11505917.value: The research has great potential for further development, including the following potential areas: (1) we only applied deviation of the SSR brand from users’ search query as an instance of “anomaly” that triggers users’ suspicion. Other types of deviations and “anomalies,” such as deviations from users’ preference in terms of other product attributes (e.g., when users search for a “wired headset,” the search engine recommends a wireless headset), may exist in e-commerce. Future studies can extend our work by examining other forms of deviations beyond brand preference. (2) we only focused on several typical social cues in our research context. Search service providers may need to provide different forms of social cues or justifications to deal with different types of deviations. Future research is needed to identify these forms of social cues and justifications and examine their effects on reducing users’ avoidance of SSR. (3) we conducted laboratory experiments in this project, to increase realism and generalizability, future studies may conduct empirical tests in field settings to validate our findings in this project.

11505917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11505917.value: Online sponsorships have become a key marketing channel nowadays. They are widely applied in search engines to promote sponsors’ links, such as the links to their products and websites, and are also among the most important revenue streams for search engine providers. However, Internet users have negative schemas toward sponsored search results (SSRs) in general and tend to avoid them. Such SSR avoidance reduces the click-through rate of SSRs and challenges the viability of the business model of sponsored search. User-generated content, such as product reviews and ratings, has become a critical factor influencing online user behavior and decisions. Many SSRs receive positive reviews and ratings as social cues from prior consumers. The scholarly literature always attests to the effectiveness of social influence, regardless of offline or online contexts. However, as reported in 2019, SSRs in Google only received a click-through rate of 3.17% even when social cues are presented alongside the SSRs. This study focuses on users’ responses toward a particular type of sponsored search results (SSRs) that deviates from users’ search preferences but receives high evaluations from prior consumers. We investigate the effects of positive social cues on reducing users’ avoidance of this type of SSRs. We identify two theoretical accounts to articulate how users internalize a social cue when making their avoidance decisions, thereby offering theory-based strategies to reduce users’ SSR avoidance. We conducted three laboratory experiments, and results support our theoretical accounts. This study uncovers the internalization mechanism of social influence on reducing suspicious users’ SSR avoidance in online settings. It also offers practical implications for online search service providers to facilitate online users’ decision-making in their search process.

11506417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11506417.value: As smartphones and tablets are becoming ubiquitous, mobile ecommerce is also evolving rapidly. Consumers can shop on mobile devices in two ways; either they open a mobile browser and visit a retailer’s website or they download the retailer’s mobile app and shop within the app. While developing and maintaining either a mobile web or a mobile app involves substantial costs, how retailers should manage these two emerging channels together is not well understood. This proposed study aims to investigate the relationship between mobile web and mobile app channels by analyzing how a change to one channel affects the outcome in the other. To infer a causal relationship, I further utilize an exogenous event, Google’s use of mobile friendliness as a ranking signal in its mobile search algorithm, to assess how it influences the demand for retailers’ mobile apps. The results from this proposed study could reveal whether the two mobile channels complement or substitute each other. This study contributes to the literature of multi-channel management in mobile ecommerce and provides important managerial implications for retailers to better leverage the growing mobile channels. 隨著智能手機和平板電腦的普及，移動電子商務也在迅速發展。消費者可以通過兩種方式在移動設備上購物。他們可以打開移動瀏覽器來訪問零售商的網站或者下載零售商的手機應用程序並在應用程序內部購物。由於開發和維護移動網站或移動應用程序都需要大量成本，零售商應如何利用與整合這兩個新興渠道這一點還不太清楚。本研究項目旨在通過分析一個渠道的變化如何影響另一個渠道來調查移動網站和移動應用程序兩個渠道之間的關係。為了建立因果關係，我進一步利用Google將其移動友好性作為其移動搜索算法的排名信號這一外部事件以評估其如何影響零售商移動應用的需求。這項研究的結果可以揭示兩個移動渠道是否補充或替代。這項研究有助於豐富移動電子商務多渠道管理這方面的文獻，並為零售商提供重要的管理意義和幫助他們更好地利用不斷增長的移動渠道。

11506417.label: Realisation of objectives
11506417.value: All three objectives have been successfully and completely achieved. The first objective is to assess the economic benefit of having a mobile optimized website in terms of how it may affect a website’s traffic from mobile devices such as smartphones and tablets. We also quantify the impact of an exogenous change introduced by the leading search engine Google to boost mobile friendly websites on the mobile traffic of different websites. On February 26, 2015, Google announces that it will include mobile friendliness as a ranking signal in its search algorithm for mobile devices starting April 21, 2015. This change implies that more mobile-friendly search results will appear on mobile devices. It will also raise awareness among consumers about the increasing ease of browsing on mobile devices. Given Google’s dominant position in mobile search, any change imposed by it could potentially re-distribute the traffic among various mobile websites. We select the Top 500 retailers in U.S. as the sample to conduct our empirical analysis. One difficulty in constructing the dataset for our purposes is to identify when a website is optimized for mobile access. We obtain such historical information by subscribing to a website called CompetitorScreenshots.com, which takes screenshots of various websites viewed on mobile devices starting from January 2014. By comparing the screenshots of a website’s homepage taken on different days, we are able to identify the first date when a website viewed on mobile devices permanently changes from the desktop version to the mobile version (i.e., when a website is optimized for mobile access). We also subscribe to comScore’s Mobile Metrix product to collect the mobile traffic data for the websites owned by the Top 500 retailers in the period of July 2014 to December 2016. We run two-way fixed effects regressions with the monthly website traffic as the dependent variable. The second and third objectives are to examine the interaction between mobile app and mobile web channels. To realize these objectives, we conduct two types of analyses and examine how a change in each channel affects the usage pattern of the other channel. Specifically, we investigate how mobile website optimization affects the mobile app traffic and how mobile app launch affects the mobile web traffic. Mobile website optimization is designing the website especially for users on mobile devices. An optimized (or mobile-friendly) website should be able to adjust its content and display according to the size of the browser viewing it, and it may differ from its desktop version in many different aspects including content, navigation, presentation, visual appeal and so on. The optimized mobile website provides customers with an easy shopping experience, and, therefore, may potentially affect the demand of the corresponding retailer’s mobile app. Google’s use of mobile friendliness as a ranking signal in its mobile search algorithm is an exogenous shock to the traffic of an optimized mobile website. Similarly, when a retailer publishes a mobile app, customers have more options for shopping in addition to the existing mobile website channel. Then, the mobile website traffic is likely to be influenced too. It is ex ante unclear whether these two channels will certainly substitute each other. It is also possible that they may complement each other in the sense that a change in one channel leads to more usage of the other channel. For instance, when a customer makes a purchase on the mobile website channel and really likes the shopping experience, then this customer may download the retailer’s mobile app and gradually becomes a loyal customer. The mobile app and mobile website traffic data used to achieve these goals are purchased from comScore Inc. We select the mobile apps and mobile websites under the Retail category in comScore Mobile Metrix as the sample to conduct our analysis. To test the relationship between these two channels, we construct a retailer-month panel and specify the a fixed-effect regression model to conduct analyses.

11506417.label: Major findings and research outcome
11506417.value: We first find that mobile friendliness (i.e., making a website optimized for mobile) increases the traffic of a retailer’s website from mobile devices. Specifically, smartphone users on average spend 17.2% more time in each visit to a website optimized for mobile access than to a website that shows its desktop version to mobile users. In addition, mobile website optimization decreases the traffic of the corresponding retailer’s mobile app but mobile app launch leads to a gradual increase in the usage of the corresponding retailer’s mobile website in the long run. These findings indicate that the interactions between mobile app and mobile web channels are asymmetric. In other words, we find evidence of both channel complementary and channel substitution.

11506417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11506417.value: The interaction between mobile app and mobile website channels is examined only for the retail industry in this research project. The findings from this project may not necessarily generalize to other industries. It will be important to examine under what conditions mobile app and mobile website channels complement (or substitute) each other. Leveraging a unique dataset on mobile website and mobile app traffic for many firms in various industries, We plan to conduct a further research project to explore the contingencies that determine the different types of interaction relationships between the two channels.

11506417.value: As smartphones and tablets are becoming ubiquitous, mobile ecommerce is also evolving rapidly. Consumers can shop on mobile devices in two ways; they either open a mobile browser and visit a retailer's website, or download the retailer's mobile app and shop within the app. While developing and maintaining either a mobile web or a mobile app involves substantial costs, how retailers should manage these two emerging channels together is not well understood. This research project contributes to the understanding of the relationship between these two mobile channels by examining how a change in one channel affects the business outcome of another. We find that mobile users substitute away from a retailer’s mobile apps when its mobile website becomes more friendly but mobile users visit the retailer’s mobile website more over time after the retailer launches a mobile app.

11507117.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11507117.value: 對物聯網變革價值和動態定價的經濟分析

11507117.label: Project Objectives
11507117.value: How does a better prediction capability enabled by IoT affect the outcome of the different pricing policies of a monopoly firm, namely advance static high-price or low-price selling strategies, and dynamic pricing strategies such as contingent pricing and probabilities selling policies? How does an increased product/service value enabled by IoT affect the outcome of the different pricing policies of a monopoly firm? How does the IoT enabled capabilities improve the competitiveness of a firm against non-IoT firm in the market? And how is consumer welfare affected as a result?
rows: How does a better prediction capability enabled by IoT affect the outcome of the different pricing policies of a monopoly firm, namely advance static high-price or low-price selling strategies, and dynamic pricing strategies such as contingent pricing and probabilities selling policies?
How does an increased product/service value enabled by IoT affect the outcome of the different pricing policies of a monopoly firm?
How does the IoT enabled capabilities improve the competitiveness of a firm against non-IoT firm in the market? And how is consumer welfare affected as a result?

11507117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11507117.value: Internet of Things (IoT) technology empowers firms in making better demand forecast through collection of a variety of consumer related data, Moreover, it also facilitates creation of products or services that are more tightly match the preferences of the consumers, and generating demands that were otherwise absent. Together, the technology prepares firms with capabilities of improving demand prediction as well as demand generation. These capabilities, in turn, can have profound impact on the dynamic pricing strategies adopted by firms. However, these IoT capabilities not only requires substantial investments in the IoT infrastructure, but also competencies in analytics to analyze the deluge to data collected through the deployment of the IoT devices. Despite the heavy investments required, few have studied how the improved capabilities would translate to actual benefits for firms, especially considering that a plethora of pricing strategies are available for firms, including the increasingly prevalent dynamic pricing strategies are anchored upon in algorithmic pricing. In this study, we investigate how new capabilities introduced by IoT, when incorporated with different pricing strategies, would affect the profit advantage of a firm and consumer welfare. Our analysis centered around the key economic tradeoffs surrounding the cost justification of deploying the technology. That is, how a better demand prediction and enhancement of consumer valuation would interact with different pricing strategies. Answering those questions also allow us to shed light on how much of such technology is required. In convention wisdom, we learn that a pre-committed low-price strategy “undercharge” the high-valuation consumer, whereas a pre-committed high-price strategy would “price out” the low-valuation consumer, and dynamic contingent pricing strategy would be wasteful if the arrival of high-valuation consumer does not materialize. Moreover, enhancement in consumer valuation through IoT could potentially cannibalize the benefits from better precision in demand prediction as a “winning product” would guarantee consumer demand. Our study aims to better understand the interplay of all these factors. As algorithmic pricing is increasingly becoming mainstream, there is a greater need to understand the potential impact levied by the dynamic pricing models that are applied in supporting those algorithms. More importantly, it is important to see the role of the abundancy of data that has been applied in supporting those pricing models. The outcome of this study provides us better insights on how we can utilize the emerging IoT technology for the betterment of firms and consumers.

11507117.label: Realisation of objectives
11507117.value: This paper sets out to study three research questions. In the first research question, we compared the contingent pricing policies with other pricing strategies. We build an analytical model to answer the questions. In the second question, we study how an increase in product/service value enabled with IoT can affect the pricing decision and market outcome. In the third question, we examine how IoT enabled capabilities can affect a firm's competitiveness outcome. Our study provided insights into all three questions. The project results in two research output. The first paper specifically addressed the research questions. Based on the accepted paper, the journal further invited us to write a short article discussing the impact of IoT in the future. We further discuss how IoT would intersect with pricing decisions under different business contexts. Given the increasing interest in applying IoT together with dynamic pricing strategies, this study contributes to enhancing the understanding of IoT capability and pricing schemes. Although intuitively IoT may substitute contingent pricing in reducing demand uncertainty, we also find circumstances where they can be applied simultaneously to achieve optimal profit. In so doing, the firm can hedge against demand uncertainty while improving consumer targeting. The practical implication is firms are no longer confined to a binary decision of using a low price under weak consumer targeting or a high price under precise consumer targeting. When IoT additionally improves product value (such as through better personalization), the decision of whether to use IoT primarily depends on whether the generated surplus goes to the consumer. In a monopolist market, the firm should invest in IoT as improved targeting and personalization enable the firm to charge higher prices. Alternately, in a more competitive setting where the firm does not have the flexibility to increase pricing, the firm invests less in IoT as the benefit does not justify the cost. In all cases, higher product value induced by IoT is found to negate contingent pricing. Therefore, choosing the investment in IoT depends on the impact of IoT capability and how it could be paired with a relevant pricing strategy

11507117.label: Major findings and research outcome
11507117.value: We show that a firm may earn higher profits by using contingent pricing in conjunction with IoT systems. However, this outcome is only the optimal strategy when a firm is relatively unsure about high-valuation consumers’ demand, and when using IoT systems cannot significantly improve the targeting of high-valuation consumers. The positive outcome arises because contingent pricing helps protect the firm from failing to land a high-valuation consumer; in the meantime, an IoT system can marginally improve the likelihood that a high-valuation consumer will buy the product. However, if IoT systems can significantly improve consumer targeting, a firm should always use the high-price scheme. When IoT systems are able to help a firm improve product value, the surplus generated from product improvement can benefit either the firm or the consumers. Suppose the entire surplus is given to consumers, which is common in a market with fierce competition. In that case, the firm should invest less in IoT than in the case of no product improvement as higher product value induces consumers to buy the product, so less targeting is required. On the other hand, when the surplus is given to the firm, it becomes feasible for the firm to charge higher prices, which warrants a higher investment in IoT. However, in both cases, contingent pricing is less likely to be the optimal strategy. In the first case, contingent pricing is used less because the firm incurs a higher compensation cost. In the second case, high-price schemes are more attractive, given that targeting can achieve a higher marginal benefit than contingent pricing.

11507117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11507117.value: Future research includes considering a more realistic but more complex setting where there are multiple sellers and products. We may use the current study as a baseline to develop a more in-depth model as the basis for field studies that examine the implementation of such schemes in the field. Another direction is to analyze this and other pricing schemes that consider consumers’ uncertainty about the final products they receive. There, we would need to consider different types of information generated by the IoT capability, coupled with the effectiveness of the different pricing schemes

11507117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11507117.value: We study how to use IoT technology with different pricing schemes. We consider IoT can have two features. First, it can help firms to improve demand prediction, and it may create the value of the products sold by firms. The main pricing schemes that we studied, contingent pricing, is often used to hedge against demand uncertainty. When we do not consider IoT can improve product value, we find circumstances where IoT may complement contingent pricing to achieve optimal profit. The firm can hedge against demand uncertainty while improving consumer targeting. The practical implication is that firms in a reasonable setting, the firm can use contingent pricing with the aid of IoT to achieve a better profit outcome. When IoT systems are able to help a firm improve product value, then the outcome depends on whether the value generated from product improvement mainly benefits the firm or the consumers. In the latter case, which is common under fierce competition, the firm should invest less in IoT because a higher product value already induces consumers to buy the product. In the prior case, it becomes feasible for the firm to charge higher prices, which warrants a higher investment in IoT.

11507717.label: Realisation of objectives
11507717.value: Objective-1. To clarify the difference between intermediated and direct channels and understand funders’ channel choices We focused on exploring the differences between intermediated and understanding direct channels and understand the incentives of funders and their channel choices. major research activities are listed below: A. Economic Analysis of Disintermediation on Crowdfunding Platforms This study investigates the incentives of lenders and borrowers’ and how they would choose between the two types of platforms. We model the intermediary as a profit maximizer who filters projects, provides high quality borrowers with access to the platform, and ensures repayment rate to lenders. Our initial findings suggest that the introduction of direct P2P lending platform enables the intermediary to reduce its interest rate and to raise its screening threshold on the intermediated platform. The P2P lending platform also incentivizes more altruistic lenders to shift to the direct funding platform. These findings suggest that the introduction of disintermediated P2P platform improves social welfare on the prosocial crowdfunding platforms. Chen, Jianqing; Ge, Ling; and Guo, Zhiling, "An Economic Analysis of Disintermediation on Crowdfunding Platforms" (2018). PACIS 2018 Proceedings. B. Racial Discrimination in Crowdfunding: Evidence from Kiva We study whether the racial/ethnic discrimination exists in crowdfunding and how it may affect the projects fundraising outcomes. Using data from the largest prosocial lending crowdfunding platform, Kiva, we find that there is no significant difference in the chance of getting funded for minority loans and White loans. However, we do identify that loans to African American have averagely smaller contribution per funder, implying certain degree of risk aversion from such loans, a sign of discrimination. Luo, X., and Ge, L. (2018). “Racial/Ethnic Discrimination in Crowdfunding: Evidence from Kiva,” PACIS 2018. Objective-2. To investigate the effect of the introduction of a new channel on funders’ contribution pattern We further strengthened and extended our theoretical model and conduct empirical analysis to understand the effect of the introduction of a new channel on funders’ contribution pattern as given below: C. Funder Incentives on Prosocial Crowdfunding Platform: Theoretical Model. Donation-based crowdfunding platform Kiva seems to hold the promise of peer-to-peer lending with zero interest rate to help the poor. However, it is actually intermediated by microfinance institutions, which raise funds from Kiva lenders, disburse the funds to borrowers and collect high interest. We develop a theoretical model and explicate that the lenders trade-off is between the sustainability of her donation money and the welfare of individual borrowers. We find that only highly altruistic lenders select Zip and they tend to shift their loans from Kiva to Zip after Zip’s introduction. D. Intermediaries vs Peer-to-Peer: Empirical Study of Lender Contribution on Donation-based Crowdfunding Platform We empirically examine the question that after the direct channel is introduced, how the new channel shift funders’ contribution pattern and loan portfolio. We find that Zip funders are more likely to have a loan portfolio of lower average interest rate, larger loan amount and lower percentage of group loans. Our findings show that the Zip funders do not reduce their contribution on Kiva; on the contrary, the contribution to Kenya loans even increases after Zip while contribution to US loans remain similar. Objective-3. To examine changes in intermediaries’ operations and performance after introduction of new channel To provide insight for understanding the changes in intermediaries’ operations and performance after the introduction of the new channel, we explore how intermediaries change after they using prosocial crowdfunding. E. Impact of Crowdfunding on Intermediaries In this study, we investigate the impact of crowdfunding on traditional microfinance institutions (MFIs) in the context of a prosocial crowdfunding platform, Kiva.org. Using data from multiple sources, including loan information from Kiva.org and MFI data from Microfinance Information Exchange Market (MIX Market), we examine how access to crowdfunding influences MFIs’ sustainability and interest rate. We find that after joining Kiva, MFIs’ sustainability improves and interest rate decreases. We propose that crowdfunding platforms enable extensive information disclosure and crowd monitoring, which motivate and force MFIs to improve their operations and to be more efficient. Ge, L., Luo, X., and Wang, C. “Crowdfunding for Microfinance: New Hope?” Minor Revision, MIS Quarterly 2020. Objective-4. To explicate the interaction between funders, borrowers and intermediaries in the two channel structure using an analytical model and the social welfare implications of the system We first explored the interaction between funders and borrower and funding outcomes in the direct channel by investigating how borrowers’ narratives affect funders' behavior in a crowdfunding platform with a direct channel. We also explored the interaction between funders and platforms. The major research activities are listed below: F. Examining the role of narratives in civic crowdfunding: linguistic style and message substance Drawing on the elaboration likelihood model (ELM), the authors operationalize the linguistic style of the narrative pitch as language power and message substance as issue-relevant argument quality. In this paper, the authors examine how characteristics of both style and message are related to the outcome of civic crowdfunded projects. Our research results show that funding outcomes can be improved with psychological language dimensions (i.e. positive affective and perceptual language). This study advances the application of the dual process in ELM by identifying and examining distinct persuasive cues originating from linguistics styles and message contents. Lee, C. H., Bian, Y., Karaouze ne, R., & Suleiman, N. Examining the role of narratives in civic crowdfunding: linguistic style and message substance. Industrial Management & Data Systems, 2019. G. Mining Marketer-Generated Content for Platform Risk Signals in P2P Lending The collapse of Chinese peer-to-peer lending platforms in 2018 has caused severe financial loss to investors and a massive shakeout to the p2p lending industry. However, as a considerable financial risk, platform collapse risk currently has not been carefully investigated, perhaps because of lacking relevant methods. To address this research gap, we examine whether Marketer-Generated Content in social media can be mined for indicators of platform collapse risk. Following the Signaling Theory, we use text mining techniques to extract linguistic cues in content posted by platforms on social media. Empirical results show that platforms adopting social media are less likely to collapse while linguistic cues in posted content also offer significant signals of platform collapse risk. Huang W. & Zhao J. L., 2020. “Mining Marketer- Generated Content for Platform Risk Signals in P2P Lending,” PACIS 2020. H. Impact of Social Media on Fundraising Success in Initial Coin Offering (ICO): An Empirical Investigation Initial coin offerings (ICOs) have become a major financing method for blockchain-related projects. However, ICO initiators face big challenges to attract investor attention systematically. Due to a lack of information, it is difficult for investors to evaluate the value of ICO projects. In general, ICO initiators have limited ways to inform potential investors of project related information. Specifically, we analyze a unique dataset consisting of more than 1700 ICO projects with firm social media activities. Combining social marketing and social learning theory, our study reveals that high activeness of firms and good timing announcements on social media are helpful with attracting investors and obtain better fundraising results in ICOs. Xuan M., Zhu X. & Zhao J. L., 2020. “Impact of Social Media on Fundraising Success in Initial Coin Offering (ICO): An Empirical Investigation,” PACIS 2020.

11507717.label: Major findings and research outcome
11507717.value: We used multiple research methodologies, such as theoretical model and empirical analysis, to understand the effect of the introduction of a new channel on funders’ contribution pattern. In addition, to further understand funders’ incentives, we examined how funders’ contribution on prosocial crowdfunding is affected by borrowers’ profiles (e.g., race). Furthermore, we explored how intermediaries change after they using prosocial crowdfunding to provide insight for understanding the changes in intermediaries’ operations and performance after the introduction of the new channel. The major findings and outcomes are listed below: We developed a theoretical model to investigate the incentives of funders and borrowers’ and how they would choose between the two types of platforms. We model the intermediary as a profit maximizer who filters projects, provides high-quality borrowers with access to the platform, and ensures repayment rate to funders. Our findings suggest that the introduction of direct P2P lending platform enables the intermediary to reduce its interest rate and to raise its screening threshold on the intermediated platform. The P2P lending platform also incentivizes more altruistic funders to shift to the direct funding platform, which enables riskier borrowers to get funded. (Chen et al. 2018) We empirically examine the question (1) How would funders choose between the two channels? (2) After the direct channel is introduced, how does the new channel shift funders’ contribution pattern and loan portfolio? Our initial empirical results suggest that prosocial funders show different incentives to make contributions. In general, those who care more about the recipient’s welfare and less about risk would contribute through the direct channel. We found that funders who do not use Zip are also affected by the new channel, showing a significant increase in their contribution to US and Kenya loans on Kiva. We study whether racial/ethnic discrimination exists in crowdfunding and how it may affect the projects’ fundraising outcomes. We find that there is no significant difference in the chance of getting funded for minority loans and White loans. In addition, the percentage of US funders for African American loans is lower than other loans, suggesting even deeper discrimination from US funders (Luo and Ge 2018). We investigate the impact of crowdfunding on intermediaries. We find that after joining Kiva, the intermediaries’ sustainability improves, and interest rate decreases. Further investigation suggests that these changes mainly result from efficiency improvement, rather than increased sufficiency of low-cost funding (Ge et al., Minor Revision, MIS Quarterly).

11507717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11507717.value: Building upon the PACIS papers (Chen et al. 2018, Luo and Ge 2018), we can further extend our theoretical model to understand the underlying mechanism of funders’ contribution pattern through the intermediated and direct channels. To explicate the interaction between funders, borrowers and intermediaries in the two-channel structure using an analytical model and the social welfare implications of the system. We can further improve the empirical strategy of the analysis to enhance the causal effect of the direct channel. We can leverage the large size of our data for more advanced analysis. To further analyze funders’ choices, we can use models (e.g., mixed-logit model) to estimate the probability of a funder lending to a project by considering all available projects on both Kiva and Kiva Zip at each period. We can then identify whether a project being on Kiva or Zip matters to the probability of it getting funded. We can include project-level analysis to examine how the channel choice would affect a projects’ funding success. Building on our current research, specifically, we can empirically investigate whether and how the positive effect changes after the new channel and understand whether the direct channel affects crowdfunding’s potential to bring social welfare.

11507717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11507717.value: The research project can provide important insights on how crowdfunding platforms can design their channels and maximize the social welfare of the system. The findings suggest that the introduction of direct P2P lending platform enables the intermediary to reduce its interest rate and to raise its screening threshold on Kiva. The intermediaries need to think about ways to provide more value to borrowers and funders since the P2P direct lending would eventually push them to make other functional adjustments on the platform. Meanwhile, the intermediary still plays an essential and strategic role of market segmentation. By offering non-zero interest rate funds, the field partner effectively screens and price discriminates the borrowers. Overall, the P2P platform incentives some funders to shift their funds to Zip, which enables some high-risk borrowers to get funded. These findings suggest welfare improvement on the prosocial crowdfunding platforms. Our findings also suggest that crowdfunding platforms enable extensive information disclosure and crowd monitoring, which motivate and force intermediaries to improve their operations and to be more efficient and may improve social welfare. Despite the convenience and efficiency of P2P transactions, the crowdfunding platform needs to further consider how to more effectively mitigate risks and differentiate borrowers for sustainable developments, as well as, how to keep its positive effect on intermediaries.

11507817.label: Co - Investigator(s)

11507817.label: Project Objectives
11507817.value: To summarize the operations-oriented data structure for typical outbound call centres. To identify and develop a set of performance indicators for call centre workforce. To design a set of explanatory variables relevant to call centre performance, based on in-depth analysis of conversational records (audio files) and log-book data. 11507817.label: Realisation of objectives
11507817.value: We built a database based on the log-book data of the “Statistical Consulting Unit” (SCU) outbound call center. Conversational records for each call during our study period were extracted from the SCU’s CATI (Computer Assisted Telephone Interview) system. From the literatures about interviewer performance and productivity, we choose the number of successful interviews by each interviewer per shift, which is a count data, as the productivity measurement and performance indicator of the call center workforce. From the variables in the CATI system, we screen out different types of possible explanatory variables, which include the demographic information of interviewer (e.g. age, gender, school major), hard-working level, skills measurement, experience level, and some external conditions. The demographic information of the interviewers and their experience can be found from the interviewers’ recruitment and work record, whereas the other variables are mostly automatically recorded in the CATI system. All interviews and conversations were automatically recorded by the CATI system as one audio file for each interview. Using the recorded audio files for conducting the HK Consumer Confidence Index during the third quarter of 2017 to the second quarter of 2018, we prepared a database by extracting useful variables from these recorded audio files. Processing these audio files was a very time-consuming and challenging part; yet this step is unavoidable to perform data analysis afterwards. Examining the usefulness of the recorded audio files to identify impact factors for interviewers’ selection is also a main contribution. We spent several months to explore and examine many different software that can help to extract various measurements from the audio files. Some acoustics measures of interviewers’ voice characteristics, such as pitch, intonation, and speech rate are considered to have impact on successful interviews. We finally decided to adopt the Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficient (MFCC), which is a non-parametric extraction technique for modelling the human auditory perception system, to transform the audio files into voice feature vectors for ease of analysis. At this stage, objective 1 of the project has been achieved. After extracting the variables from audio files and build up a database, we used factor analysis model to discover some underlying factors from the voice feature vectors. Then we developed a penalized multiple inflated Poisson model to analyze the count data. It was found that this approach leads to relatively complicated computations and may overlook some real inflated points. We tried a two-stage inflated values selection method, which takes all values of count response as potential inflated values and adopts the adaptive lasso regularization method on the mixing proportion of those values. This method could select inflated values and estimate the parameters at the same time. However, because most interviewers attended more than one shifts in a survey, the repeated observations from the same interviewer are therefore highly correlated, which against the independent assumption for using general regression model. Alternatively, we tried different kinds of models and ended up using penalized generalized linear mixture model (GLMM) to analyze this kind of longitudinal count data, in which the random effects component in the model can account for the correlation within the same interviewer. The results of the GLMM model are quite good; objective 2 of the project is achieved. In the process of analyzing the database, we found that because MFCC are a sequence of eigenvectors with no real meaning, the model selection causes some elements of the eigenvectors be selected and some be eliminated. These selected elements in MFCC cannot be explained from the perspective of voice features. We reselect Auditory Spectrum Bands (ASB), which are a set of vectors containing energy values in 26 spectrum bands from 0 to 8Hz frequency to transform the audio files into a set of voice vectors. Because ASB are computed from a set of overlapping triangular filter banks from low frequency to high frequency, there may exist high correlation in the spectrum bands vector. Thus, we use factor analysis technique to reduce the large number of correlated ASB variables into fewer numbers of factors; five factors were determined using Horn's parallel analysis. Among them, Factor 1, Factor 2, and Factor 4 represent the treble, middle, and bass regions of human voice respectively. These factors with practical implications were used as potential impact factors on interviewer productivity. Objective 3 of the project has been achieved. In our database, due to the phenomenon of repeated observations from the same interviewer with more than one shifts attendance, methodology for analyzing longitudinal data is considered instead of traditional statistical regression models. First, we use the Generalized linear mixed-effects models (GLMM), which directly incorporate the within-subject association among the repeated measurements via introducing random effects, to analyze the longitudinal data. Since the heavy computational problems in GLMMs modeling is usually restricted to few predictor variables, many predictors can result in unstable estimation. In our study, there are 27 candidate impact factors on interviewer productivity with some cross-terms used as the explanatory variables. We use L1-penalty approach for variable selection on the GLMM to select the relevant variables from all candidate impact factors. In addition to GLMMs, marginal models also provide a natural way of extending generalized linear models to longitudinal data, which do not require distributional assumptions for the observations, only a regression model for the mean response. The method relies solely on assumptions about how the mean response is related to the covariates. The avoidance of distributional assumptions leads to a method of estimation known as generalized estimating equations (GEE). Since GEE method is not a likelihood-based method, QIC statistic can be used to select covariates and find an acceptable working correlation structure for a marginal model. We first choose the best working correlation structure based on the full model including all covariates with correlation information criterion (CIC), which improves the QIC performance in selecting the correct correlation structure, then we choose the best subsets of covariates with stepwise regression method using the QIC criterion. To conclude, although the original planned approach to achieve objective 4 were modified due to the phenomenon of repeated observations from the same interviewer attending more than one shift. We ended up using alternative popular longitudinal data analysis methodology, the marginal model with Generalized Estimating Equations (GEE) estimation method, together with backward elimination to identify significant impact factors on interviewer productivity from all the candidate factors in our database. Moreover, we assess model predictive performance of the marginal model compared with the Poisson regression model on call center’s data. Furthermore, we adopted an alternative approach, using the generalized linear mixed-effects model (GLMM), to analyze call center’s data. We used a two-stage method on the penalized GLMM via Lasso to select impact factors on interviewer productivity, where the re-estimation approach helps to improve estimation accuracy in GLMM modeling. Cross-validation was used to evaluate the forecasting performance of the penalized GLMM, compared with the Poisson regression model and the marginal model with GEE based on three scoring rules. The results showed that the GLMM performs better than the other two models to some extent in 1,000 CV trails. Objective 4 of the project has been achieved with two statistical modelling approaches.

11507817.label: Major findings and research outcome
11507817.value: We built a primary database for outbound call centers based on the voice records of telephone surveys. The database is constructed from an operational-oriented point of view. containing a series of information at the interviewer level, including interviewer productivity measurement, demographic information of the agents, logbook information, and agent’s behavior in conducting telephone surveys. Numerous voice features were extracted from unstructured conversational audio files. Five latent factors representing different characteristics of the human voice were identified. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study that attempts to utilize both structured data information together with voice features to predict interviewer productivity. Impact factors that affect interviewer productivity were found to select suitable interviewers, provide training guidance, and give evaluation suggestions for retaining talent. This helps improve the operational efficiency of outbound call centers and reduce operational risk. We used the longitudinal data methodology of a marginal model with GEE to impact factors can be grouped into five categories of experience, work attitude, skills, speech patterns, and voice characteristics. It was found that interviewers with accumulated experience after a higher participation rate in shifts perform better. In terms of work attitude, hard-working agents with more “total working time” and proactive agents who wait on unanswered call for a suitably long time tend to complete more surveys than others. Well-behaved interviewers can control the pace of telephone surveys without being delayed by the respondents; and show shorter average length of interviews. Regarding speech patterns, agents who introduce the survey in greater detail with longer “duration of survey introduction” help respondents understand the purpose of the interview more clearly. Interviewers using a proper speech rate to introduce the survey find that respondents accept the surveys more often. Interviewers with vocals that are too loud or too quiet are not conducive. On voice characteristics, males with lower average pitch and females with higher average pitch are more charming to respondents. Especially, interviewers with lower energy in the bass regions are found to convince respondents to participate in the interview. We also proposed a two-stage method on the penalized GLMM via Lasso to select impact factors on interviewer productivity. The re-estimation approach helped improve the estimation accuracy in GLMM modeling. It is found that the forecasting performance of the GLMM performs better than the Poisson regression model and the marginal model with GEE based on three scoring rules in the 1,000 cross-validation trails.

11507817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11507817.value: When building the required dataset for analysis and model development, the size of our dataset is not large due to the time-consuming extraction process for the voice records from the outbound call center. Should a larger resource become available, a further comparison on the performance of the studied models is recommended to confirm whether there is any limitation caused by the data size. From our result, GLMM performed better than marginal models with GEE to some extent in predicting interviewer productivity with our call center’s data. However, the marginal model has its own advantages for longitudinal data. Simulation study may be considered to investigate under which conditions the marginal model performs better and vice versa using our database for outbound call centers. The operations of outbound call centers can be transformed into an optimization problem, minimizing operating costs under given constraints, such as the total number of interviews that need to be completed, and the constraints on the attendance of interviewers. Because the workforce accounts for a vast proportion of variable costs, different salary plans can affect the operating costs in the objective function. Results from the optimization problem can help guide the operations of outbound call centers.

11507817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11507817.value: This study utilizes both structured data information together with voice features to predict interviewer productivity. Our research findings can help outbound call center managers by guiding them how to select interviewers, provide technical guidance in training, and give evaluation to retain talent. When recruiting interviewers, through vocal analysis, priority should be given to males with lower average pitch, females with higher average pitch, and candidates whose voice has lower energy in the bass region. During training, the fieldwork supervisor can guide agents to use a suitably loud sound and moderate their speech rate to introduce the survey. A suitably long waiting time, say 30 to 40 seconds, is preferred for unanswered calls. Interviewers participated in more work shifts can accumulate their experience gradually and achieve more successful interviews per shift. For retention, managers and supervisors can pay attention to outstanding agents who work hard with more “total working time” and have more conversational skills with higher completed to first refusal ratio and shorter “average length of interviews”. As a result, by recruiting and training suitable interviewers, and retaining talents, the operating efficiency of outbound call centers can be improved with the response rate increased, so as to reduce workforce costs.
