11507917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11507917.value: Despite the widespread adoption of signaling theory in business research, there exists no research on how signals are received and interpreted by receivers. The implicit assumption of is that so long as a sender sends a signal, receivers will receive and interpret the signal as intended. While this research has made a strong contribution, the receiver side has largely been ignored. The social context of the signal will affect how receivers interpret the signal. In this regard, we postulate that the social cognition of signal receivers likely influences signal efficacy during the transmission process. By theorizing and examining social cognition of receivers, our proposed research represents an attempt to fill such gap. Drawing on social judgment theory in the social cognition literature, we posit that receivers are susceptible to the social context wherein the signal is sent, and such context will influence how receivers judge the signal. A receiver is primed by the social context (social priming) and categorizes the information content associated with the stimulus (social categorization). The evaluation of a target stimulus depends on both the target stimulus itself and the non-target stimulus in the social context (social judgment). Two key social judgment effects have captured the most attention: assimilation effect and contrast effect. When target stimulus is judged as similar to non-target stimulus (target stimulus and non-target stimulus are included within the same category), the assimilation effect will take place; when the target stimulus is judged as dissimilar to the non-target stimulus (non-target stimuli becomes a standard of comparison), the contrast effect will happen. Assimilation effect influences judgment in a way that is congruent with non-target stimulus whereas contrast effect influences judgment in a way that is incongruent with non-target stimulus. The main purpose of the proposed study is to explore if and how social judgment, in terms of assimilation and contrast effects, moderates the efficacy of IPO underwriters as a signal in affecting investor sentiment and hence IPO performance. We adopt a multi-method approach. Archival data collected from various data sources are used to test the hypotheses, and lab experiments are carried out to offer stronger causal relationship tests. Using multiple methods produces results that are more robust and convincing than do single method studies. The inclusion of cognitive/behavioral phenomena, such as in our proposed study, will particularly benefit from the use of lab experiments to help explain and confirm results derived from archival data testing.

11507917.label: Realisation of objectives
11507917.value: The objectives as listed in the research grant proposal have been successfully achieved. The funded research has helped develop a detailed theoretical framework that outlines the intriguing relationships among IPO underwriters as signals, the social context of such a signal, sentiments toward IPO firms, and hence IPO performance. The importance of the lead underwriter as a strategic signal for an IPO has been widely supported in the literature; however, the focus has been very much on the reputation of the underwriter itself. We found evidence that the social context of a signal is crucial in affecting how a signal is perceived by signal receivers. The development of such a theoretical framework, as well as the supporting empirical evidence, serve to achieve one of the objectives of the research grant. Furthermore, we are able to make use of the use of social judgment theory developed in social psychology to highlight the usefulness of the socio-cognitive perspective to understand signal. We theorized and detected that both assimilation and contrast effects, as posited in social judgement theory, are present in the underwriter signal during IPO process. Such findings help understand the complex nature of IPO and enrich studies in strategic management in general by making use of a socio-cognitive theory. Furthermore, signaling theory is an economics theory that seeks to explain a strategic action in mitigating information asymmetry between signal sender and signal receiver. The funded research is able to demonstrate that social cognition theories and concepts can offer important insights to enrich economics theories. It also serves to respond to recent calls in the strategic management field to incorporate behavioral and cognitive insights in its studies. In the real world, we observe both rational and “non-rational” behaviors, and an integrated framework combining both economic and social psychological theories will be useful to explain a phenomenon and advance theory. The funded research represents an effort in this direction. In addition, this study adopted a multi-method approach. We combined online experiments and archival data for the study. By adopting such an approach, the theorization and findings of the study are richer and more robust. Sentiment is an important aspect that has not been sufficiently examined in extant research. We clarified and tested in different ways whether and how sentiment toward the IPO firm influences IPO performance. Furthermore, the introduction of sentiment in strategic management and international business, as aided by the funded research, has led to two empirical papers in this new line of research. By emphasizing the importance of sentiments, the first paper found evidence that host country public sentiments toward home countries affect international acquisition equity ownership. The paper is forthcoming in Journal of International Business Studies and was also presented at EGOS Conference. The other paper examines how host countries sentiments toward various aspects of international acquisitions influence acquisition completion. This paper currently receives an R&R at Academy of Management Journal and was presented at Strategic Management Society Annual International Conference. This set of papers, together with the above one on IPO, serve to underscore the crucial importance of sentiments in affecting international acquisitions, as well as international strategy and business behaviors and decisions in general. What is more, to capture sentiments in these studies, we collected, usually by web crawling, large amounts of textual data from many social media venues. In order to analyze these unstructured, textual data (a form of big data), we employed sentiment analysis, an advanced computer-aided text analytics, a method that has been seldom used in management research. In using this method, we demonstrate to the field how this method is useful in advancing management research. This study has also captured a large amount of textual data, and the datasets generated will be immensely valuable for more studies along these lines. Two more studies spawned by this funded research pertain to using a socio-cognitive approach in strategic management research. An earlier one based cultural psychology in the social psychology literature was presented at EGOS Conference. Another study likewise takes on a cognitive approach to examine the relationships between visual communication and IPO underwriter as a signal. This paper is accepted for presentation at Strategic Management Society Annual International Conference in 2022. It is perhaps also relevant to note we are working with PhD students in this paper, which serves as a useful learning vehicle at the same time for them. Together, these two papers further underline the usefulness of adopting a social psychological approach, especially from a cognitive perspective, in strategic management. We would like to note that the research objectives of the funded research were accomplished under a highly challenging context. In the early part of the grant period, all the PI and Co-Is had moved to new institutions. As a result, it had taken a while for us to settle in our new institutions. However, the biggest challenge began with the social event that took place in the second half of 2019 and the subsequent Covid 19 pandemic starting from early 2020. It has posed significant challenges to the PI, Co-Is, and research support staffs. Furthermore, we had been planning and kept waiting for student lab experiments possibilities but had not been able to do so since mid-2019. Finally, we accepted student lab experiments would be impossible under the circumstances of the pandemic. We therefore had to redesign and switched from lab experiments to online experiments upon approval from the RGC panel. After we had conducted the empirical analyses of the archival and experimental data and were ready to move on to the write-up stage, Hong Kong encountered the most severe wave of the pandemic in the first several months of 2022. During this difficult period, some family members of the PI and Co-I team had contracted Covid or passed away. Despite all these external, unexpected challenges, we were able to achieve the objectives of the funded grant by completing the main study and several studies spawned by the funded grant.

11507917.label: Major findings and research outcome
11507917.value: Overall, the funded research has successfully produced or helped spawned several studies. They are in various stages, including forthcoming in a top tier journal (Journal of International Business Studies), under revise-and resubmit in a top-tier journal (Academy of Management Journal), accepted for presentations in major international conferences, including Strategic Management Society Annual International Conference and EGOS Conference. As for the IPO signaling and social judgment paper, it is under final preparation to be submitted to Strategic Management Journal for publication consideration as well as to the next call for submissions by Strategic Management Society Annual International Conference. Most other papers will be submitted for publication consideration at top tier journals in this summer, targeting premier outlets of either Academy of Management Journal or Strategic Management Journal. There have been far fewer conference opportunities in the last several years due to the pandemic. Although some conferences are still held virtually or in hybrid mode, travel restrictions in Hong Kong have rendered traveling overseas to present papers in international conferences highly difficult, if not impossible, during this period. Notwithstanding this limitation, we were still able to have papers accepted at several major international conference presentations thus far, and intend to do more as the pandemic situation is improving. By and large, the research studies are able to provide support to the usefulness of adopting a social psychological approach, including social cognitive theories and concepts, to understand IPO signaling efficacy and performance, as well as strategic management behaviors and outcomes. More specifically, the main research theoretically integrates a social cognitive theory (social judgment theory) with an economics theory (signaling theory) and generate interesting, important theorization and empirical findings. This approach has led us to pursue additional studies. In addition, we shed important light on the importance of sentiments in strategic management considerations. By employing sentiment analysis, an advanced methodological tool in text analytics, we are able to capture sentiments through analyzing textual data gathered from social media. This opens up a new avenue for management research. Moreover, by using a multi-method approach to make use of both archival data and experimental data, our research helps underline the strengths of adopting such research approach. Hence, the research outcomes from this funded research grant not only helps extend theories and explain complex strategic phenomena, but also introduces and further underscores useful methodological approaches to management research.

11507917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11507917.value: The use of social psychology theory, including social cognitive theory, in our studies, especially emphasis on social judgment and sentiments, demonstrates the cognitive aspects should occupy a more important role in understanding complex business phenomena. Extant studies in strategic management have not studied this aspect sufficiently. Our research has already developed and currently fine-tuned a few related studies in this direction, and this line of research will be further developed in future studies. Although sentiment is a crucial consideration for firms, most strategy studies have not explicitly studied this construct and measured it directly. Our research uses a new methodology, sentiment analysis, to capture this important construct. Text analytics opens up valuable opportunities for management research. Many constructs that were hard to be captured can now be studied directly using textual data collected from print sources or social media. We are developing empirical studies along this line. Our research premising on social psychology or cognition theories will help develop a new line of research examining how emotions expressed at the societal level will impact business strategic decisions and outcomes. This is a promising area to explore and we will further develop our research in this area.

11507917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11507917.value: In highly uncertain environments, firms may use signals to communicate to their stakeholders about their attributes that are difficult to observe. Extant studies often assume such signal will be well received as intended. However, our research suggests and found evidence that the social context of signals is likely to determine the impact of the signals on strategic outcomes. In other words, signal receivers will be affected by other similar signals sent by other firms they received at the same time. As such, firms should consider the social context when sending signals as their signals will be judged and compared by signal receivers along all other signals. Furthermore, sentiment is crucial in business considerations. However, this aspect is not fully understood and considered thus far. Our research shed light on this crucial aspect by highlight what factors may affect various types of sentiments, how to capture them, as well as how they impact business outcomes. In essence, our research shows that business considerations and outcomes are not solely based on economic, rational considerations; social psychological or cognitive factors are also highly relevant and important. These factors will demand even more careful consideration by firms.

11508017.label: Major findings and research outcome
11508017.value: In this project, as an alternative to the surplus utility, we propose a performance-price-ratio (PPR) utility and specialize the attraction choice model with a PPR maximization criterion. With this PPR based choice model, we investigate a pricing game between retailers in a competitive market. Through transferring the decision variable from price to performance-price ratio, the first-order condition of the game becomes a linear equation system, and therefore we develop a closed-form equilibrium solution for the pricing game. The solution reveals how product performance and price sensitivity affect equilibrium pricing, market share, and revenue. Although choice models, including the representative multinomial logit (MNL) model, have been explored extensively, there are few empirical studies investigating these models under a game setting. In addition, we investigate how the equilibrium evolves with the game decision sequence, market structure, and new product entry. These are research objectives defined by Objective 1 and 2. With the theoretical results developed in this project, we carry out empirical studies with a rich data set obtained from the China TV market. We test both the PPR-based choice model and the widely used surplus MNL model in an equilibrium market. It turns out that the PPR model fits the China TV market better than the surplus MNL model. Specifically, we conduct stepwise multivariate linear regression for both the performance-price ratio (PPR) and surplus models, in which the calculated brand performance is the dependent variable and the TV model functionalities are the independent variables. The brand performance is defined as the aggregate performance of all the available TV models provided by a brand, i.e., the performance of a brand’s product portfolio. For both the PPR and surplus models, the brand performances are calculated based on the corresponding theoretical models. To this end, we have the following conclusions for research objective 3: 1. The PPR model fits the data better than the surplus model. 2. For the PPR model, the positivity/negativity of the effects of different functionalities on each brand are consistent. However, for the surplus model, some functionalities have different effects on different brands. 3. For the PPR model, the positivity or negativity of the effect of each functionality on each brand remains unchanged as the number of reservation brands changes. 4. Among all of the provided functionalities, the definition functionality affects significantly more brands’ performance than the other functionalities.

11508017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11508017.value: The existing study is based on data from physical stores. Since e-commerce has become a market trend. During this project, we attempt to make of data from both physic stores and e-commerce website. However, owning to the time limits, the data we obtained do not cover the same products, i.e., e-commerce shops carry lower-end TV products. As we observe today, both physic and e-commence shops carry identical products. A further study of data collected from both physic and e-commerce shops would be interesting. More importantly, e-commence shops may have a richer data set than physic shops. These data may contain features to enrich functionality of product-price ratio model.

11508017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11508017.value: “Performance-price ratio” (PPR) has become a keyword for both suppliers and sellers in promoting their products. As these are prime customer concerns, customer choice has received much recent attention via a number of utility-based discrete choice models. We characterize the equilibrium for the pricing game between oligopoly retailers. The state of equilibrium depends on the retailers’ price sensitivities: high sensitivity brings a price war; low sensitivity leads to a subgame with one less player; in between, a closed-form solution is obtained by transferring the first-order condition into a linear equation system with respect to the PPR vector. With the closed-form solution and assuming a positive correlation between price sensitivity and performance. Following the theoretical analysis, we carry out empirical calibrations on the PPR model with real data from the China TV market. We find 1. In terms of interpreting the variance of the data points, the PPR model is better than the surplus model. 2. In the product-level regression, the functionality coefficients for the PPR model are positive, whereas all of the functionality coefficients for the surplus model are negative. 3. In the brand-level regression, the PPR model are statistically significant, whereas the surplus model sometimes are not statistically significant.

11508217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11508217.value: Nested simulation has received a considerable amount of attention among simulation researchers and practitioners in recent years. It finds important applications in the areas of operations research and management science, especially in risk measurement for large-scale and complex financial portfolios. In this project, we propose a new simulation method, referred to as a likelihood ratio method, for nested simulation. It is expected that the proposed method has nice theoretical properties such as consistency and fast rate of convergence. We also study possible improvements for the likelihood ratio method, aiming to reduce its variance. One of the directions towards improvements selects a subset of samples that have smaller conditional variances, and takes the sample average of this subset, rather than using average of all samples. We will provide both theoretical and practical justifications on why such improved estimators work. We will also consider the extension of the proposed method to other performance measures, such as quantiles. By exploiting the connection between the probability function and the quantile functions, we expect that the likelihood ratio method can also be applied for estimating quantiles in principle. 嵌套模擬近幾年在隨機模擬領域引起了廣泛的關注。它在運籌與管理科學領域有很多重要應用，特別是應用在大規模金融投資組合的風險度量上面。在這個項目裏，我們提出一種被我們稱之爲似然比方法的新的嵌套模擬方法。從理論角度，我們期望新提出的方法會有比較好的特性，比如更快的收斂速度。我們同時研究改進似然比方法的一些可能方案，用於降低其方差。其中一個改進方案是通過對仔細選取的一個字樣本取平均。我們將從理論和實際的視角去研究爲何這些方案能有效工作。 我們同時研究如何把似然比方法推廣到其他的度量準則，比如分位數。通過利用概率函數與分位數的密切聯係，我們期望似然比方法同樣可以應用于估計金融投資組合的分位數（也被廣泛稱爲風險值）。

11508217.label: Realisation of objectives
11508217.value: We have successfully achieved the project objectives. In particular, we have investigated the problem of nested simulation, and proposed a likelihood ratio method. In the plain setting, we have studied the budget allocation for nested simulation, and proposed a bootstrap-based budget allocation rule that adaptively allocates simulation budget to outer- and inner-level simulation. When density information is available, we have proposed a likelihood ratio method that makes use of the density information. We have established consistency and rate of convergence of the likelihood ratio estimator, and developed procedures for constructing asymptotically valid confidence intervals. We have also provided an implementation guideline on taking subsamples to further reduce the variance of the resulting estimator. Application of the proposed method to performance measures such as probability of large losses, expected shortfall, and quantiles has been discussed, as well as a comparison and connection between the likelihood ratio method and the stochastic mesh method in the literature.

11508217.label: Major findings and research outcome
11508217.value: The research objectives of this project have been successfully achieved. In particular, we have investigated the problem of nested simulation, and proposed a likelihood ratio method. In the plain setting, we have studied the budget allocation for nested simulation, and proposed a bootstrap-based budget allocation rule that adaptively allocates simulation budget to outer- and inner-level simulation. When density information is available, we have proposed a likelihood ratio method that makes use of the density information. Theoretical guarantees, including both consistency and asymptotic normality, have been established for the proposed likelihood ratio method, which guide the construction of asymptotically valid confidence intervals. We have also discussed the implementation issues especially the use of subsampling for variance reduction purpose. Connection between the likelihood ratio method and stochastic mesh has also been carefully examined, with a focus on the understanding of their relative advantages. The proposed method is applicable to a wide range of functionals encountered in practical applications, including probability of large losses, expected shortfall, and quantiles (value-at-risk). The above research outcomes of the project have been presented in three papers. The first paper titled "Bootstrap-based budget allocation for nested simulation" has been accepted by a premier journal Operations Research. Results on the development of a stochastic mesh method for portfolio risk measurement have appeared in the Proceedings of the 2017 Winter Simulation Conference, titled "Portfolio risk measurement via stochastic mesh". Development of the likelihood ratio method and its asymptotic analysis have been presented in a working paper "Green nested simulation for portfolio risk measurement", which is expected to be submitted soon to Operations Research.

11508217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11508217.value: The current version of the proposed methods cannot be applied directly to some applications in operations research and management science, where the density information may not be available due to the complexity of the model dynamics. Developing innovative techniques to extend the likelihood ratio method to this context is an interesting direction for future research.

11508217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11508217.value: In this project, we have investigated a nested simulation problem that arises commonly in risk management of a financial portfolio when evaluation of some of the assets in the portfolio requires simulation, and our focus is to develop efficient simulation methods for portfolio risk measurement. On one hand, by leveraging the asymptotic properties of traditional nested estimators, we have proposed a bootstrap-based budget allocation method to adaptively allocate the simulation budget so as to estimate the portfolio risk with higher accuracy given a fixed simulation budget. On the other hand, making use of the density information in the models of financial assets, we have proposed a likelihood ratio method to estimate the portfolio risk in a fast speed. We have established theoretical supports for both of the proposed methods, and numerical examples demonstrate that they may serve as promising tools for practical problems in financial risk management.

11508417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11508417.value: The motivation for studying whether and how the influences of channel governance mechanisms across organizational boundaries on opportunism differ over hierarchical levels builds on the fairly obvious idea that boundary spanners at the top and operating levels hold different perspectives. On the one hand, opportunism has been a central focus of marketing channel research influenced by transaction cost economics (Williamson 1975, 1985). Opportunism does not necessarily occur at the organizational level as commonly conceptualized in inter-organizational research. Drawing on the insights from implicit theory of agent, we distinguish the top-level boundary spanner’s opportunism and the operating-level boundary spanner’s opportunism. On the other hand, extant studies on governance mechanisms exclusively rely on senior managers as the core informants and thus focus on the perspective of top-level management, leaving the governance issue at the operating level unobserved. This project advances a more nuanced approach by examining channel governance at different hierarchical levels. Upon it, we investigate the effectiveness of governance mechanisms in deterring dual levels of opportunism. We propose that top-level relational governance has a stronger negative relationship with top-level boundary spanner’s opportunism than top-level contract utilization, whereas operating-level contract utilization has a stronger negative effect on operating-level boundary spanner’s opportunism than operating-level relational governance. We further examine the cross-level governance alignment that mitigates top and operating-level opportunism. Specifically, operating-level contract utilization strengthens the negative effect of top-level relational governance on top-level boundary spanner’s opportunism while operating-level relational governance weakens the negative effect of top-level relational governance on top-level boundary spanner’s opportunism. The negative effect of operating-level contract utilization on operating-level boundary spanner’s opportunism is strengthened by both top-level contract utilization and top-level relational governance. This project has significant managerial implication for managing channel relationship and designing the best governance structure to deter opportunism.

11508417.label: Realisation of objectives
11508417.value: The project aimed to address four objectives. 1. To distinguish opportunism occurring at the top-level and operating-level Objective 1 is fully achieved. Opportunism was originally defined as “self-interest seeking with guile” (Williamson,1975, page 6). Opportunism includes behaviors such as lying, cheating, and other willful violations of existing contracts and norms. The essence of opportunism is guile or deceit whether at individual or firm level. Although opportunism was originally a behavioral assumption of individuals in Transaction Cost Economics, the majority of interfirm governance studies do not distinguish firm opportunism from opportunism conducted by individual boundary spanners employed by the firm. We argue that firm opportunism need not imply individual boundary spanner opportunism and vice versa. We define boundary spanner opportunism as the extent to which an individual boundary spanner is considered to have engaged in opportunistic behavior. Such behavior occurs despite a firm's cooperative intention. For example, opportunistic purchasing agents in the automotive industry sabotaged their firms' cooperative efforts to build relationships with component suppliers. Firm opportunism, on the other hand, refers to the extent to which a firm as a whole is considered to have engaged in opportunistic behavior, which may or may not involve the individual boundary spanner. Firm opportunism thus can exist without individual boundary spanner opportunism. Individual boundary spanner opportunism, however, is distinct from firm opportunism. Being proactive agents that manage interfirm relationships, individual boundary spanners can choose to act cooperatively or opportunistically regardless of the intent of the firm they work for. 2. To distinguishing the governance mechanisms implemented by channel boundary spanners at different hierarchical levels Objective 2 is fully achieved. Based on Traction Cost Economics and Relational Exchange Theory, we distinguish the governance mechanisms implemented by boundary spanners at different hierarchical levels. Boundary spanners include both top-level managers and operating-level managers at the lower levels. Top- and operating-level boundary spanners differ in two respects. First, they play different roles. Top-level boundary spanners are primarily responsible for strategic decision-making, including selecting partners, negotiating contracts, establishing alliance objectives, setting a development strategy, and renegotiating contract terms according to environment changes. In contrast, operating-level boundary spanners are responsible for everyday implementation of agreements. Second, top- and operating-level boundary spanners have different goals. The goal of top-level boundary spanners is often to facilitate and maintain long-term cooperation with partners and to boost alliance performance. In contrast, the goal of operating-level boundary spanners is to accomplish specific joint projects efficiently. Thus, the governance mechanisms implemented by at the top-level and operating-level boundary spanners are different. 3. To examine whether one type of mechanism is more effective than the other at each management level Objective 3 is fully achieved. At the top level, relational governance has a stronger negative effect on top-level opportunism and has a stronger positive effect on and alliance performance than contract utilization. At the operating level, contract utilization has a stronger negative effect on operating-level opportunisms than relational governance. Contract governance works as an effective mechanism to cope with exchange hazards inherent in interfirm relationships. Specifically, by specifying the roles and obligations of each party, contracts can safeguard transaction-specific assets against opportunistic appropriation. However, as top-level alliance boundary spanners are primarily responsible for long-term strategic issues, contract utilization may undermine alliance trust and impair the long-term relationship, whereas relational governance that emphasizes long-term relationship building, is consistent and compatible with the goals at the top level. Relational governance can facilitate social interactions and promote joint actions between alliance partners, which help operating-level boundary spanners deal with uncertainties in daily operations. However, using noncoercive power through relational governance may require repeated interactions between alliance partners, which can hinder the efficiency of alliance operation. 4. To examine how governance mechanism alignment across different hierarchical levels mitigate two levels of opportunism Objective 4 is fully achieved. The interaction between top-level and operating-level relational governance has negative impacts on operating-level opportunism and alliance performance. The interaction between top-level relational governance and operating-level contract utilization has a negative impact on operating-level opportunism. The interaction between top-level contract utilization and operating-level relational governance has a negative impact on alliance performance but has no impact on top-level opportunism. The interaction between top-level contract utilization and operating-level contract utilization has a negative effect on operating-level opportunism and a positive impact on alliance performance.

11508417.label: Major findings and research outcome
11508417.value: This project has six major findings. First, relational governance plays a more salient role than contract utilization in mitigating top-level opportunism and increasing alliance performance at the top management level. Top-level relational governance has a negative effect on top-level opportunism and has a positive effect on alliance performance whereas top-level contract utilization has a nonsignificant impact. Second, in contrast, contract utilization has a stronger negative effect on operating-level opportunism than relational governance at the operating level. Third, we find a negative interaction effect between top-level and operating-level relational governance on operating-level opportunism and alliance performance. This result reveals that the simultaneous use of relational governance at both top-level and operating-level is a double-edged sword. On one hand, utilization of relational governance at both levels helps mitigate operating-level opportunism. On the other hand, top-level relational governance and operating-level relational governance are not complementary of each other because alliance relationships governed purely by relational norms may suffer from less-than-optimal information sharing and entail high role ambiguity, which will negatively influence alliance performance. Fourth, the interaction between top-level relational governance and operating-level contract utilization has a negative impact on operating-level opportunism. Fifth, the interaction between top-level contract utilization and operating-level relational governance has a negative impact on alliance performance but has no impact on top-level and operating-level opportunism. Six, the interaction between top-level contract utilization and operating-level contract utilization has a negative impact on operating-level opportunism and a positive impact on alliance performance. According to TCE, the roles and exchange procedures prescribed in contracts help reduce transaction uncertainty and partner opportunism. In emerging markets, although contract utilization may undermine trust and hinder smooth cooperation between alliance partners, the legal sanctions caused by contract breach can largely reduce a partner’s deviant behaviors. In particular, when both levels of the management adopt contracts to govern the alliance relationship, the effectiveness of contracts in mitigating partner opportunism and facilitating interfirm cooperation is enhanced.

11508417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11508417.value: Inspired by this project and the idea on cross-level in particular, we examine the relationship between cross-level interpersonal ties and IJV innovation. We find that while top-level interpersonal ties have positive effects on both exploratory and exploitative innovation, operating-level interpersonal ties have a greater positive effect on exploitative innovation than on exploratory innovation. Furthermore, we find that knowledge exchange and knowledge integration mediate the relationship between interpersonal ties and innovation. Specifically, knowledge exchange mediates the relationship between operating-level interpersonal ties and exploitative innovation, whereas knowledge integration mediates the relationship between top-level/operating-level interpersonal ties and exploratory innovation. This project is currently under review at JBR. We will continue to develop other cross-level projects.

11508417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11508417.value: The existing literature underscores the critical role of interfirm cooperation and governance and shows the limitations of each governance mechanism. However, extant studies have largely been focused on governance mechanisms at the top level of management, neglecting the possibility that different governance mechanisms can be used at different levels of the management hierarchy. This project advances the interfirm governance literature by examining the effects of contract utilization and relational governance at different hierarchical levels. We theorize and distinguish opportunism and governance mechanisms at the top and operating levels of the channel hierarchy. This distinction is important because the role and goal of top- and operating-level management differ. Our findings indicate that relational governance has a stronger negative effect on top-level opportunism and a stronger impact on alliance performance than contract utilization at the top level. At the operating-level, contract utilization has a stronger negative effect on operating-level opportunisms than relational governance. The interactions of two governance mechanisms at both levels are much more complicated. For example, alliance managers should exert caution when relational governance is used simultaneously at both the top and operating-levels as we find that such use mitigates operating-level opportunism but hinders alliance performance.

11508517.value: 摘要 眾籌作為新興企業尋求融資的替代手段而獲得廣泛關注。2015年，眾籌業再次翻番，全球貸款總額達344億美元。眾籌的基本概念是指從互聯網相連接的個人中筹集金融資本。儘管以社交媒體發帖和產品評論等形式存在的使用者生成內容（UGC）對眾籌項目具有潛在的重要性，但很少有系統的研究來檢驗使用者生成內容（UGC）對眾籌資助決定行為的影響。此外，我們對不同環境變量也不夠瞭解，不清楚這些變量如何調節積極（或消極的）UGC與支持者資助決定行為之間的關係。特別地，儘管目前不同設計的眾籌平臺在激增，但是仍然缺乏關於如何優化設計功能來提高項目支持者的決定行為並提高其UGC消費模式的實證研究。為了彌補這些研究空白，本項目將解決以下研究問題： （1）UGC效價（積極或消極）如何影響支持者對眾籌項目的資助決定？ （2）環境變量（消費者和產品特徵等）如何調節UGC效價與支持者資助決定行為之間的關係？ （3）如何設計既能促進資助決定又能激勵平臺使用者消費相關內容的眾籌平臺？ 理論基礎：為了研究積極或消極UGC對資助者決定行為的影響，我們分別使用兩種流行的資訊處理和態度形成理論，即精度似然模型（ELM）和信號理論。 面板數據和計量經濟學分析：我們計畫從最大的眾籌平臺之一收集數據，包括關於項目發起者，項目描述，項目支持者，項目更新、評論和相關UGC在內的所有變量。通過使用不同的計量經濟模型，網路分析手段和文本挖掘技術來瞭解UGC效價和社交網路因素對資助決定過程的影響。 用實驗室實驗驗證結果：通過計量經濟學模型，社交網路和文本分析等技術對面板數據進行分析研究後，我們進一步將使用實驗室實驗來驗證這些研究結果。 設計激勵消費者參與的眾籌平臺：通過分析面板數據結果和實驗室實驗的實證結果，我們將開發一個框架，為設計更好的眾籌流程和介面，以增強平臺籌資過程。 本研究以眾籌為研究背景，通過將資訊學和經濟學理論與數據分析相結合，提供學術和實際應用等兩方面的貢獻。該項目將為設計更好的眾籌服務提供有用的見解和設計原則。

11508517.label: Realisation of objectives
11508517.value: 1. Study what factors affect successful crowdfunded projects and effective crowdfunding platforms through understanding information presentation and processing mechanisms in crowdfunding. To address this objective, we have first explored how linguistic style and message substance influence persuasion in civic crowdfunding marketplaces in which written narrative pitch become a vital communication to attract private contributions to public goods and services. In this paper, we examine how characteristics of both style and message are related to the outcome of civic crowdfunded projects (Lee et al. 2019). Second, we examine and discuss whether and to what extent a product sampling strategy is beneficial to crowdfunding campaigns. Differences in the strategy’s effectiveness across product types are also examined (Liu and Fang 2021). 2. Investigate how positive or negative valence of UGC influence backers’ decision-making process using text mining, econometrics methods, and lab experiments. The findings of this study will help project initiators design better campaigns. It will help consumers better evaluate projects and select those that have more potential for success. It will also help crowdfunding platforms design better processes and interfaces to improve matching and stimulate more user generated content. To address this objective, we have first employed the logistic regression models to assess the impact of both linguistic style and message substance on crowdfunding decisions. The results show that funding outcomes can be improved with psychological language dimensions. However, extensive use of social language does not help project creators to increase their chance of funding performance; but instead, such language reduces the likelihood of project success. Additionally, message substance or issue-relevant information such as money and risk language influences funding outcome (Lee et al. 2019). Second, we have built a research model to examine the impact of product sampling adoption on a set of campaign performance indicators, after controlling for known variables. An interaction term between product sampling and product type is created to examine how product sampling’s impacts vary with the extent to which the product can be accurately evaluated prior to consumption. A regression model is used to estimate the effect of our key independent variable (Liu and Fang 2021). 3. Use both Elaboration Likelihood Model (ELM) and Signaling Theory to develop a theoretical framework to explain how the valence of UGC shapes consumers' funding behaviors. The model will also elaborate how other factors moderate this relationship including consumer characteristics, entrepreneur characteristics, and project characteristics. To address the third objective, first, drawing on the elaboration likelihood model (ELM), we operationalize the linguistic style of the narrative pitch as language power and message substance as issue-relevant argument quality. We examine how characteristics of both style and message are related to the outcome of civic crowdfunded projects (Lee et al. 2019). Second, we discuss whether and to what extent a product sampling strategy is beneficial to crowdfunding campaigns. Differences in the strategy’s effectiveness across product types are also examined (Liu and Fang 2021). Third, we examine whether Marketer-Generated Content in social media can be mined for indicators of platform collapse risk. Following the Signaling Theory, we use text mining techniques to extract linguistic cues in content posted by platforms on social media (Huang and Zhao 2020). Fourth, we are focused on determining the extent to which online crowdfunding projects are affected by COVID-19 and investigating factors that help projects to alleviate the negative effects (Liu et al. 2021). 4. Validate the proposed model with data collected from one of the largest crowdfunding platforms and its related social media sites and through conducting lab experiments. To address this objective, we first retrieved the data on civic crowdfunding projects from Spacehive, the platform that dedicated mainly to civic projects ranging from community programs, social-oriented enterprises, to infrastructure or facility development. Each of the narrative samples is analyzed using a computerized text analysis package called the Linguistic Inquiry and Word Count to extract the features of the linguistic style and message substance in the narratives. The logistic regression models are estimated to assess the impact of both linguistic style and message substance on crowdfunding decisions (Lee et al. 2019). Second, using a unique dataset of 4,027 campaign-level observations collected from China’s highly influential JD Crowdfunding website z.jd.com, we discuss whether and to what extent a product sampling strategy is beneficial to crowdfunding campaigns. Differences in the strategy’s effectiveness across product types are also examined. Empirical results suggest that adopting online product sampling is helpful to crowdfunding performance because it increases the total number of backers, the total fundraising amounts, the average amount of funds raised per backer, the fundraising percentage, and the possibility of campaign success. The strength of product sampling, however, decreases along the search-experience product continuum (Liu and Fang 2021). Third, following the Signaling Theory, we use text mining techniques to extract linguistic cues in content posted by platforms on social media (Huang and Zhao 2020). Fourth, based on a novel panel data set collected from kickstarter.com, we employ a regression-discontinuity-in-time design to empirically examine the impacts of the shock (Liu et al. 2021). Fifth, we examine how the presence of sponsorship disclosure affects consumer engagement with the Social Media Influencers’ posts. Using a panel dataset from a large social media platform in China, we used the approaches of PSM and DID to validate our assumptions (Zhang et al. 2020). Sixth, we analyse a unique dataset consisting of more than 1700 Initial Coin Offerings projects with firm social media activities. Our study reveals that high activeness of firms and good timing announcements on social media are helpful with attracting investors and obtain better fundraising results in ICOs (Xuan et al. 2020). 5. Propose practical crowdfunding tactics and strategies to help: 1) project initiators design and launch more effective crowdfunding campaigns, 2) potential backers’ funding highly potential successful projects, and 3) crowdfunding platform operators design better processes and interfaces to facilitate crowdfunding activities. To address the fifth objective, based on the empirical findings in our research, we offer distinct recommendations for project campaigners. First, platform managers and project campaigners may leverage the impacts of the narrative pitch through the lens of our research model. The findings encourage practitioners to focus on the role of affect-related language cues in civic crowdfunding. Second, based on the direct effects of issue-relevant content cues, project campaigners are suggested to strengthen the argument quality of the narration with more detailed issues and more quantitative numbers. Third, for campaign initiators, this study encourages project campaigners to understand both linguistic style and message substance of their written narrative pitch and to balance such dual process factors that are essential to drive backers’ funding decisions (Lee et al. 2019). (6) Extensions of the main objectives: Further examines regulatory focus in e-commerce and customer misbehavior on social media. We made an extension based on the core research efforts of this project. First, we propose an innovative method to operationalize customer regulatory focus from the affective dimension, leading to operationalized regulatory focus (Wu et al. 2019). Second, customer misbehavior is a serious and pervasive problem in firm-sponsored social media, yet prior studies provide limited insight into how firms should detect and manage it. To address this gap, we first develop a data science approach to detect customer misbehavior on social media and then devise intervention strategies to deter it (Wu et al. 2021). Please refer to part c for the research outputs cited in this section.

11508517.label: Major findings and research outcome
11508517.value: We examined how positive or negative valence of UGC influence backers’ decision-making process using text mining, econometrics methods, and lab experiments. In addition, we used both Elaboration Likelihood Model (ELM) and Signaling Theory to develop a theoretical framework to explain how the valence of UGC shapes consumers' funding behaviors. Besides, we explored how to improve crowdfunding designs towards better experience. We have obtained the following results: 1. Funding outcomes can be improved with psychological language dimensions (i.e. positive affective and perceptual language). However, extensive use of social language does not help project creators to increase their chance of funding performance; but instead, such language reduces the likelihood of project success. Additionally, message substance or issue-relevant information such as money and risk language influences funding outcome. (Lee et al. 2019) 2. Empirical results suggest that adopting online product sampling is helpful to crowdfunding performance because it increases the total number of backers, the total fundraising amounts, the average amount of funds raised per backer, the fundraising percentage, and the possibility of campaign success. The strength of product sampling, however, decreases along the search-experience product continuum (Liu and Fang 2022). 3. Empirical results show that platforms adopting social media are less likely to collapse while linguistic cues in posted content also offer significant signals of platform collapse risk. Our study contributes to the literature by identifying relevant factors for assessing the stability of financial intermediaries. Furthermore, our work lays a theoretical foundation for platform selection by investors and for government regulation in internet finance (Huang et al. 2020). 4. The results showed that the pandemic threatens crowdfunding projects by decreasing both the number of backers and the amount of funds. Furthermore, we found that projects provide hedonic benefits (compared with utilitarian benefits), projects produced and delivered in digital form (compared with physical goods), and projects that adopt a narrative style with lower psychological distances are more likely to maintain the ability of fundraising (Liu et al. 2020). 5. Our study reveals that high activeness of firms and good timing announcements on social media are helpful with attracting investors and obtain better fundraising results in ICOs (Xuan et al. 2020). 6. Our research reveals that after the first presence of sponsorship disclosure in an social media influencer’s (SMI) post, consumers’ engagement with the SMIs’ posts significantly decreases. Additionally, “comment” and “share” of the SMIs’ posts decrease less than “like”. (Zhang et al. 2020).

11508517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11508517.value: Building upon the IMDS publication in 2019 by Chang Heon Lee, Yiyang Bian, Rajaa Karaouzene and Nasreen Suleiman, future research can be conducted to verify the findings of linguistic style and message substance based on cross-platform data. The comparison can further examine whether culture difference shapes the effects of narrative in civic crowdfunding. In addition, future research can be conducted to explore the effects of the narrative by combining multimedia message with textural message together and advance our knowledge regarding civic crowdfunding. Building upon the I&M submission (2nd round R&R) by Xiaochen Li and Yulin Fang, first future studies can test the proposed hypotheses in this study using data from other platforms of different countries/regions. Second, future research can consider more product attributes in addition to the search-experience product continuum as the classification standard to gain more diverse empirical results. Third, future studies can be conducted to better identify causal relationships, capture dynamic impacts of this strategy, or examine its interaction with time-varying factors with the support of an available dataset.

11508517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11508517.value: Crowdfunding gained popularity as an alternative means of seed financing for new ventures. The fundamental concept of crowdfunding is to assemble financial capital from a large group of individuals connected to the Internet. Despite the potential importance of User-Generated Content (UGC) in the forms of social media posts and product reviews about crowdfunded projects, few systematic studies have examined the effect of UGC on funding decision behavior. Furthermore, little is known about diverse contextual factors moderating the relationship between the UGC and backers’ financing decision behavior. This project has filled those research gaps by examining the impact of the positive or negative valence of UGCs on backers’ financing decision on crowdfunded projects, the moderation effect of contextual factors on the relationship between the valence of UGCs and backers’ financing decision behavior, and the design of the crowdfunding platforms that can facilitate funding decisions as well as stimulate platform users to consume relevant contents. This research provides academic and practical contributions through the combination of information and economic theories and data analytics into the crowdfunding context. Findings in this project provide useful insights and design principles that can be utilized to provide better crowdfunding services.

11508817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11508817.value: 這個項目是一項長期研究的一部分，它研究應用程式和平台之間不同的關係類型如何影響平台生態系統的生存和可持續性。我們借鑒生物學文獻，瞭解這些不同類型的關係可能會導致不同的結果（例如互利共生，共生，寄生等等）。 軟體平台生態系統，如蘋果的iOS和谷歌的Android，逐漸成為基於軟體服務的主要模式。利用可擴展的技術架構的優勢，平台通過吸引大量能夠創造互補價值的第三方應用程式來擴展其產品邊界。為了加速生態系統中的第三方開發，平台擁有者放棄了原有對應用程式功能擴展的整合要求，讓應用程式在開發中更具自主性。 另一方面，關於產品線戰略的研究表明，新產品（即本研究的新應用）與現有產品（即本研究的平台）的適當整合可以為新產品、現有產品和终端用户帶來額外價值。這項研究旨在探討應用程式開發自主性和應用程式與平台集成的臨界張力。我們借鑒在信息處理中的群體實體性(Entitativity)原則來研究在整合設計的理念下，用戶如何有意識地整合平台和應用程式，以及這種意識如何刺激平台和應用程式之間的溢出式使用(spillover usage)。具體地說，本研究關注源於群體實體性感知的空間和時間維度上兩種重要的平台-應用程式整合設計：空間嵌入性（space embeddedness）和響應性（responsiveness）。 我們計劃採用兩種不同的方法進行兩項研究。在研究1中，我們將從一個主流Web瀏覽器平台（Firefox）調查實際的平台和應用程式的使用情況。在研究2中，我們將通過進行一次實地實驗來擴展我們的實證結果。在這個實驗中，我們將操控我們感興趣的一些關鍵構念。 為此，我們收集了Firefox部分的面板數據。初步的分析結果為我們的預測提供了一些數據支持。我們也聯系了中國一個社交網路網站，並已經獲得了公司的支持，可在他們的網站上進行了實地實驗。 據我們所知，我們將是第一個實證檢驗理論框架，並解釋如何實現平台與應用程式之間的共生關係的研究。這項研究還將為軟體平台如何利用整合設計原則，以獲得更強的溢出效應和建立一個更可持續的生態系統提供具體的指導方針。

11508817.label: Realisation of objectives
11508817.value: The objectives of the project, as stated above, have been fully realized. This will be elaborated in the paragraphs below. Software platforms such as Google’s Chrome and Android are extensible codebases of software systems that provide core functionalities for third-party apps that can run on them. Leveraging this technological architecture, platforms extend their product boundaries by attracting numerous third-party apps that can create complementary value. To accelerate third-party development in software platform ecosystems, platform owners often waive their restrictions on the app user interface (UI) design, providing app developers with more autonomy in product development. While this approach has been viewed as a great strength of a software platform to “letting a thousand flowers bloom”, the literature on product line design, which is relatable to general platform design, has found that standardized UI design across products provides strategic advantages and is a necessity for firms introducing and managing their product lines. Specifically, these integrated design features such as interface standardization and interface linkages are favored because they provide a seamless user experience and thus help a newly developed product attract more users of existing products. In particular, studies on software product lines have established that UI standardization across existing and new software products, as well as interface linkage between them, enhances the performance of new products, which also reduces the cost of adopting and learning to use a new product. Moreover, increasing the use of the new product can consolidate users’ willingness to stick to existing products. That is, satisfaction and familiarity with the new component motivate users to stay with the integrated system. The product line literature has further indicated the critical role that cross-product design plays in integrating the focal product with its complementary (new) product at both interface and function levels (Nambisan 2002). This design strategy has been widely applied in product family software applications, such as Microsoft Office software suites, and Internet-based product and service linkage, such as hypertext links. The tension between app autonomy and cross-product interface design principle reflects the “seesaw” problem of platform owners who “must strike a delicate balance between autonomy granted to app developers and the integration of their work with the platform”. While the literature has argued that this tension can be managed by aligning architecture and governance at the app level, the role that integrated or coordinated interface design plays in relationships between the platform and its apps – termed integrated app-platform interface design in this study – has yet to be adequately explored. Specifically, our research question is whether or not the integrated app-platform interface design can reinforce the derivative usage between a platform and its apps, defined as the association between platform usage and app usage which mutually benefit each other. In relation to the first objective, the research team reviewed prior literature on designed principles of entitativity (renamed as topological design principles to be consistent with the literature) and contextualized three specific design principles in platform app context. We draw on and extend the theory of basic Gestalts (TBG) in the perceptual psychology domain to investigate how users perceptually group a platform and its apps according to the app-platform interface design. Along with the theoretical perspective of addressing the human visual perception of an object as a whole rather than the sum of its parts, we propose three key integrated interface design principles: interface similarity, interface embeddedness, and interface synchrony. These design principles are mutually exclusive and exhibit unique yet interdependent properties. Interface similarity refers to the degree to which apps and the platform share visual properties (e.g., color, size, or shape). Interface embeddedness refers to the degree to which an app is surrounded within the platform’s interface region. Interface synchrony is the extent to which an app changes simultaneously with the change in users’ actions on its platform’s interface. We theorize that these three interface design principles affect users’ perception as to whether an app is part of the platform or a separate entity, which the literature has termed as grouping perception. With regards to the second object, we designed a mobile app running on a platform. We further extend TBG to better understand the downstream effects of grouping perception on users’ usage behavior by delineating the mechanisms underlying its influence on two directions of derivative usage between the platform and hosted apps. We propose derivative usage to reflect mutually beneficial app-platform relations/associations, where its two directions include platform-to-app forward derivative usage – which relates to the usage derived from platform usage to app usage (the benefit that an app can draw in platform usage) – and app-to-platform backward derivative usage, which refers to the usage derived from app usage to platform usage (the benefit that the platform can draw in app usage). We conducted a randomized field experiment with 541 participants to test the hypotheses, in which interface similarity, embeddedness, and synchrony are explicitly manipulated to examine their effects on integrated interface designs. The hypotheses developed based on our theory were tested in this field experiment. The results largely confirmed out hypotheses. The results not only enrich our theoretical understanding of app-platform design, but also generate interesting insights and useful guidelines for practitioners.

To examine under a platform ecosystem context, how entitativity design can enable the spillover effect from a platform to its apps, and from the apps to its platform, to achieve a “win-win” symbiosis ecosystem.

11508817.label: Major findings and research outcome
11508817.value: This study addresses the platform ecosystem paradox wherein platform owners are challenged to strike a balance between offering autonomy for app developers to “bloom” and the successful (regulated) integration of their work with the platform. we build upon TBG from the psychology literature and expand it to understand the effects of design principles – interface similarity, interface embeddedness, and interface synchrony – on bidirectional derivative usage between platforms and their apps. Four of the five formulated hypotheses are supported, thus validating most of our theoretical arguments. This research contributes to the growing platform ecosystem literature by offering a new design perspective in conjunction with theoretical accounts of the topological relationship between platforms and their apps. By offering a fresh approach to investigating these issues, the study enriches the ecosystem paradox debate. This study contributes to the literature in two ways. First, it contributes to platform ecosystem research by providing a novel perspective on third-party product development and usage. With the open platform development strategy of “letting a thousand flowers bloom” wherein platform owners seek product variety and reach by aggressively pursuing third-party app developers – this strategy often results in the undermining of product interface design principles. This in turn may be a root cause of chaos for platforms and thus hinder their long-term development. To the best of our knowledge, this study is the first to develop theory-based arguments and empirical evidence to substantiate the need for interface design standardization in platform ecosystems. Second, the study advances our knowledge on the multi-technology usage literature. Technology usage is one central research theme of the IS domain. Within this research stream, a rich body of study has been extended from adoption to the extended usage, as well as the use of a single technology to make associations between different technologies. Reflecting on the nature of software platforms and the inadequacies of the existing conceptualization of usage associations in studying platform ecosystems – this study coins a new term, derivative usage, to characterize the mutually beneficial interactions between platform usage and app usage, which better captures the essence of usage in our research context. This reconceptualization and extension of the existing concept better serves future research efforts in platform ecosystems in particular, as well as research in other multi-technologies contexts in which the technologies involved are interdependent and complement each other.

11508817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11508817.value: This study has several limitations that indicate directions for further study. First, while we recognize two types of value creation paths in platform ecosystems, the study’s boundary is the Type 1 ecosystem in which platforms offer core value creation. Caution is needed when extrapolating this study’s findings to Type 2 ecosystems that primarily include complementary value creation. We encourage scholars to explore this line in future research. Second, in the field experiment, we manipulate the app-platform interface design of only one app. The experimental findings for a single app may underestimate the value of the app-platform interface design, particularly the effect of app-to-platform usage. Hence, future research should manipulate an appropriate number of apps to obtain more realistic and meaningful results. Third, given the current state of practice and feasible managerial implications, we only consider how the UI design of the platform and app satisfy user needs. It would be interesting to study diverse situations, such as when the UI design of a platform is shoddy or inadequate. Furthermore, interface design properties may vary their display forms in various contexts. We thus encourage future research to refine their exploration of diverse platform interface designs.

11508817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11508817.value: Our results provided several guidelines for platform owners and app developers. First, it confirms that integrated app-platform interface design is a valuable strategy for supporting platform growth. This approach has often been overlooked by platform and autonomous developers in practice. This study shows that an efficient app-platform interface design implemented from a grouping perspective may be the key to balancing this tension. The results provide specific guidelines for practitioners on how software platforms can leverage interface design principles to achieve a strong derivative usage and a successful software ecosystem. Second, the study shows that platform boundary resources – such as software tools and regulations that serve as the interface for the relationship between the platform and apps are important resources for governance. Recent studies have also recommended that software platforms utilize their boundary resources, such as APIs and software development kits (SDKs), to curb strategic exploitation by apps or competing platforms so as to retain competitive advantages. Platform firms are encouraged to consider integrated design as a new cooperative governance strategy to facilitate the mutual benefits between the platform and apps by developing different restriction and control strategies according to the apps’ interface similarity, embeddedness, and synchrony with the platform.

11508917.label: Major findings and research outcome
11508917.value: A range of novel theoretical models exploring the underpinning mechanisms for behavioral addictions in SNS and related contexts have been developed and empirically validated, paying particular attention to the role of self-regulation and related technology features. The research results have been published through 4 research papers in leading field journals. Drawing on dual-system theory, study 1 examines the role of desire for online group gaming in online social game addiction. By conducting a longitudinal online survey, we show that attitude, anticipated enjoyment, group norm, and social identity contribute to the development of desire for online group gaming. Such desire facilitates habit and self-regulation deficiency, which, in turn, fosters online social game addiction. Study 2 further built on dual-process theory and found that automatic habit strengthens the driving effects of reinforcement rewards (i.e. perceived enjoyment and mood regulation) on smartphone addiction, demonstrating an interactive effect between habit and reinforcement mechanisms (both positive and negative ones). Smartphone features activate distinct underlying mechanisms leading to addiction. Value-added function facilitates the perception of reinforcement rewards, while convenience promotes habit formation. Interestingly, automatic habit has no significant direct impact on addiction. Study 3 explored an alternative stimulus-response-reinforcement theoretical framework and found that both positive and negative reinforcements, as well as the compensatory component, invoke the feeling of urge that leads to compulsive mobile SNS use. The positive effects of interactivity as an incentive stimulus on those reinforcements and compulsive mobile SNS use were also found to be significant. Study 4 identifies essential factors for preventing relapse to information technology addiction with a self-regulation perspective. Notably, the role of mindfulness on self-regulation was explored and empirically tested. A longitudinal study was conducted. The results show that mindfulness impacts self-control and that they both contribute to reducing urges, which, in turn, prevent relapse to addiction.

11508917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11508917.value: The study of behavioral addiction in the online world (from cyberpets through MMOG to metaverse) is still at a relatively early stage. In Nature, the foremost scientific journal in the world, there have been recent calls for research into a wider variety of behavioral addictions, especially those facilitated by digital platforms such as the Internet. Moving forward, there are 3 potential directions of high potential in terms of achieving further breakthroughs in this field: 1. Recognising behavioral addiction is a dynamic and context-sensitive construct, there is a need for further theoretical and empirical work to develop and dynamic and context-sensitive measurement for this phenomenon. 2. The bulk of the extant empirical literature employs cross-sectional studies, which are of limited use in studying a dynamic phenomenon. This project has started to deploy longitudinal studies. In the future, a lot more focus needs to be put on longitudinal studies. 3. Typically, each study in the extant literature focuses on certain variables and mechanisms impacting online behavioral addiction. There is now a need to integrate them and develop more holistic overarching models to advance our theoretical and empirical understanding of this very dynamic phenomenon to the next level.

11508917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11508917.value: The prevalence of digital technology and our reliance on it has given rise to new types of behavioral addiction problems. The pertinent phenomena are serious enough that in the latest edition of the International Classification of Diseases (ICD 11) promulgated by the World Health Organization, cyber behavioral addiction such as video and online gaming addiction has been recognized as a new mental health disorder. In Nature, the foremost scientific journal in the world, there have been recent calls for research into a wider variety of behavioral addictions, especially those facilitated by digital platforms such as the Internet. Meanwhile, real-world businesses have been leveraging behavioral addiction mechanisms to attract customers, uplift consumer engagement, improve loyalty and profit. There is a pressing research need for a better understanding of the cyber behavioral addiction phenomenon and the underlying processes and mechanisms, so that effective prevention and treatment strategies may be developed. This research project contributes to this effort through 4 related theory-driven empirical studies. The results help us to better understand the mechanisms underpinning the development of this type of behavioral addiction and suggest various ways to leverage technological features to reduce addiction.

11600217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11600217.value: 朱熹解釋《詩經》，認為其中的〈鄭風〉、〈衛風〉「多是淫奔之詩」，由此提出了「驚世駭俗」的「淫詩」說。從南宋直至今日，「淫詩」說引發的爭論，未曾停止，成為《詩經》史上的中心議題之一。 對于「淫詩」說的研究，已十分豐富。特別是在傳統的經學或文學範圍內，似乎已無進一步研究的空間。但是，本計劃申請人認為，「淫詩」説不僅是一個經學或《詩經》學的問題，也不僅是《詩經》情詩文學性的問題。實際上，它的影響深入到南宋以後社會文化的各個方面。尤其是「淫詩」説對南宋以後的文學詮釋史、閱讀史的影響，還缺乏深入的研究。 朱熹「淫詩」説的核心，在于「淫者自作」説。漢儒承認《詩經》中某些詩涉及「淫奔」，但認為詩人是以此來諷刺現實；朱熹認為「淫詩」主人公就是作者，即「淫者自狀其醜」。更進一步看，「淫者自作」說觸及到如何解決情詩的字面意義和道德寓意的矛盾。這曾激發明清批評家反思《詩經》以及後世涉及男女情慾詩歌的敘述方式，反思其中的字面意義與寄託詮釋傳統的關係。 更有意思是，「淫者自作」說的理論基礎是「勸善懲惡」、「讀詩養心」說，朱熹認為《詩經》作者可以是「思有邪」的「淫者」，但是讀者必須「思無邪」，這對讀者提出了較高的期許。從讀者的閱讀反應以及明清閱讀史的背景，來看「淫詩」說的影響，值得進一步探究。比如婦女閱讀《詩經》男女情慾主題詩歌時的實際情形，批評家為明清艷情小說辯護時對朱熹「養心勸懲」說的挪用，都極有研究意義。 可以看出，對於朱熹的「淫詩說」，應該超出傳統的經學範圍，在明清閱讀史的實踐中，深入研究相關線索。這正是本計劃希望突破而有所創新的地方。 因此，本計劃不會糾纏於傳統的經學史問題，而是在詮釋史、閱讀史的背景中，研究「淫詩」 說引發的詮釋規範與閱讀實踐等問題，特別關注傳統《詩經》學著作之外的閱讀實踐。簡言之，本計劃將綜合經學史、思想史、文學批評史、詮釋史、閱讀史、性別史、新文化史等不同學科的視角，深入研究朱熹的「淫詩」説在南宋直至清代的文學詮釋、閱讀實踐等領域的影響。 Zhu Xi identified more than twenty “poems of elopement” in the Shijing. That was Zhu’s view of “licentious poetry,” a theory still hotly debated today because it to some extent recognized the legitimacy of the literal sense and acknowledged the significance of sexual desire in the Shijing. It seems that, at least in the field of classical studies, the issue of “licentious poetry” has been investigated thoroughly. However, it is still worthy of a further examination of how the theory of “licentious poetry” influenced cultural history after Song dynasty, especially literary hermeneutics and the history of reading. Actually, the kernel of Zhu Xi’s theory of “licentious poetry” lies in his assumption of “elopers composing poems themselves.” Han dynasty commentators set up an exegetical framework, believing that the poets of the Shijing were historians or gentlemen who used the erotic songs to remonstrate ironically with the rulers. On the contrary, Zhu Xi argued that the author was the eloper. This assumption motivated later critics to rethink the tradition of allegorical interpretation, especially the relation between the literal sense and the moral sense. It is more interesting that Zhu Xi insisted that the author of the Shijing could be licentious but the reader should remain virtuous. That emphasized the function of reading negative examples in the process of self-cultivation. It was the theoretical foundation of Zhu Xi’s view of “licentious poetry.” The relation between Zhu Xi’s theory of “licentious poetry” and the history of reading in Ming-Qing period is worthy of a thorough examination, especially the negotiation in women’s practice of reading “licentious poetry.” Meanwhile, there emerged numerous erotic fiction in late imperial China, and their apologetic commentaries frequently resorted to Zhu Xi’s theory of “licentious poetry.” It is related to the reader’s appropriation of the theory. Hence, a research project on Zhu Xi’s theory of “licentious poetry” can go beyond the field of classical studies, and can related it to the history of literary hermeneutics and the history of reading. The latter concern is often overlooked by scholars, and hopefully it will be the contribution of this project.

11600217.value: 本計劃的目標，基本完成。在完成的過程之中，又有新的深化與拓展，詳述如下： （1）本計劃三個目標的基本想法，即第一個目標研究南宋至清代學者對朱熹「淫詩」說和「淫者自作」說的評論、第二個目標在明清閱讀史的背景中研究婦女與初學者閱讀《詩經》「淫詩」的反應、第三個目標研究明清艷情小說的辯護及其對「淫詩」理論的挪用，被融為一個整體，以〈閱讀史視野中的淫詩理論〉為題，在香港中文大學中文系2018年5月17－19日主辦的「對立與融合：中國文學傳統中的雅和俗國際學術工作坊」上發表，引起了與會學者的關注。接著，這篇會議論文被進一步擴充、整合與改寫，成為一篇三萬多字的長文，投往台灣的《漢學研究》（中文學界最頂級的刊物之一），在吸取兩位評審的意見之後，題目修訂為〈困境與精進——明清閱讀史中的朱子「淫詩」說〉，正式發表於《漢學研究》第39卷第3期（2021年9月）。原本計劃用分散的四、五篇文章發表研究成果，但是，這篇三萬多字的長文，突破了原本想法的局限，將本計劃最核心的觀點與最重要的資料，做了一個最系統的表述，將產生更深遠的學術影響力。比如，香港浸會大學饒宗頤國學院邀請PI在2021年5月做了一個公開講座，題目為「 從經典詮釋到閱讀實踐——朱熹的「淫詩」說」。 （2）在研究的過程中，視野逐漸得到拓展，明清時代中國學者、江戶時代日本學者對朱熹「淫詩」說的不同看法的比較，成為一個新的思考方向和學術增長點。初步的探索，以〈朱熹「淫詩」理論中、日接受之比較〉為題，在台灣中央研究院中國文哲研究所2019年8月24日舉辦的「中、日《詩經》學之比較研究學術研討會」上發表，引起中日與會學者的極大興趣，台灣《國文天地》邀請將此文簡寫成適合一般讀者閱讀的撮要，以〈日本古學派對朱熹「淫詩」說的批評與接受〉為題發表在《國文天地》2019年第10期，正式的會議論文集則在2021年8月作為中央研究院「經學研究叢刊」第11種推出。這篇會議論文，後經過改寫，投往香港中文大學的《中國文化研究所學報》（中文學界最頂級的刊物之一），在吸取三位評審的意見之後，題目修訂為〈朱熹「淫詩」說中、日接受之比較：以十七至十八世紀為中心〉，正式發表於《中國文化研究所學報》第72期（2021年1月）。這篇論文，突破了原本計劃的設想，為以後提出新的GRF計劃奠定了基礎，將來可以將範圍擴展至日本、韓國及整個東亞漢字文化圈。 （3）第一個目標研究南宋至清代學者對朱熹的「淫詩」說和「淫者自作」說的評論，被上溯至南宋以前的先秦兩漢歷史源流，研究成果以〈先秦兩漢《詩經》學中的「國風好色」問題〉為題，在台灣中央研究院中國文哲研究所2018年11月8-9日舉辦的「經學史重探──中世紀以前文獻的再檢討研討會」上發表。這篇會議論文，又經過反復修改，即將投往《饒宗頤國學院院刊》發表。另一篇論文〈宋代經學詮釋「人情論」的當代意義：以《詩經》詮釋為中心〉，重新思考「淫詩」說的理論基礎「人情論」及其宋代經學背景，在台灣中央研究院中國文哲研究所2021年11月舉辦的「經學的國際化：從國際視野看經學的當代性」 國際會議上發表，並將於修改之後在學術刊物上正式發表。此外，本計劃與上一個GRF計劃「朱熹的文學觀念與宋代文學文化整體觀」（CityU11602215），有一定的關聯，上一個計劃的論文〈朱熹的淫詩比擬宋詞說〉，在後期的修改中，吸收了本計劃第一個目標的部分想法，即將發表於《清華大學學報》。 （4）第二、第三個目標，已融合在（1）中提到的三萬多字長文中，得到更為系統的闡述。更為重要的是，由第二、第三個目標所蒐集的資料，指向了一個更前沿、更有影響力的研究領域，由此引申出一個新的GRF計劃「閱讀「淫詩」：朱熹「淫詩說」與明清《詩經》閱讀史」，將研究的焦點完全轉向明清時代《詩經》閱讀史，這是一個極富挑戰性的課題。這個新的GRF計劃，已經獲得RGC的資助（CityU 11606421），將於2022年1月啟動。因此，本計劃的第四個目標，原本設想要將所有成果擴充為一部專著，現在以另一種方式，即深化為一個新的GRF計劃的方式，得到了體現，最終，兩個GRF計劃的所有研究成果，將擴充整合一部更全面、更深入的專著，期望能產生更大的學術影響。

11600217.label: Major findings and research outcome
11600217.value: 已經正式發表的〈困境與精進——明清閱讀史中的朱子「淫詩」說〉，突破了傳統經學與文學研究的局限，從朱熹「淫詩」說的理論層面轉向閱讀實踐層面，重新審視了傳統經典的閱讀效果史，為經學史和閱讀史的結合提供一個視角。另一篇正式發表的〈朱熹「淫詩」說中、日接受之比較：以十七至十八世紀為中心〉，總結了朱熹「淫詩」說在作者端、讀者端的理論，並由此兩端梳理日本江戶時代古學派對「淫詩」說的批評，並與明代中期以來中國學者的看法進行比較。另外兩篇即將發表的論文，對朱熹「淫詩」說的早期源流與時代背景，做了深入的研究。四篇會議論文，為上述正式發表或即將發表於學術刊物的論文，奠定了堅實的基礎。

11600217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11600217.value: 本研究計劃，已經啟發產生了一個新的GRF計劃「閱讀「淫詩」：朱熹「淫詩說」與明清《詩經》閱讀史」，集中考察朱熹「淫詩說」在明清《詩經》閱讀史中的各種實踐細節，已經獲得RGC的資助（CityU 11606421），將於2022年1月啟動。此外，還將繼續思考朱熹「淫詩」說在日本、韓國及整個東亞漢字文化圈的流傳和接受問題，期望在將來的兩三年內再提出一個新的GRF計劃。

11600217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11600217.value: 朱熹的「淫詩」說，指出《詩經》的〈國風〉部分有二十多首「淫詩」都是「淫奔者自述」。對於很多傳統學者來說，這種看法與《詩經》的儒家經典形象有極大衝突，但是現代學者則認為朱熹揭開了《詩經·國風》很多情詩的真實面目。因此，「淫詩」說激起了長期不止的各種爭論。本研究計劃，深入考察朱熹「淫詩」説在南宋至清代的文學詮釋、閱讀實踐等領域的影響，全面總結了朱熹「淫詩」説在《詩經·國風》的作者和讀者兩方面的革新理論，以及朱熹對理想讀者的期待。本計劃尤其強調閱讀實踐層面的影響，以往研究大多局限在經學或文學領域的理論探討，其實朱熹「淫詩」說構擬出一種理想的讀者，這種理念與閱讀實踐形成了複雜的關係。本計劃的價值與貢獻，在於重新審視傳統經典的影響史和閱讀效果史，為傳統典籍與經學的研究探索了一種新的思考方向。
