11600317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11600317.value: Vocational identity is the conscious awareness of oneself as a worker, a major developmental task for young people. From a process perspective, a vocational identity is developed through exploration of different career options and commitment to a career choice. More advanced levels of vocational identity, expressed in higher levels of career exploration and commitment, are linked to greater psychological well-being and career development. Research to assess and identify different vocational identity statuses is gaining ground in the West (e.g., Porfeli, Lee, Vondracek, & Weigold, 2011), but is relatively unexplored in Hong Kong and Mainland China. We believe that testing and assessing vocational identity status assessment among sub-degree students in Hong Kong will contribute to career theory building. In terms of practice and policy, we will address a key issue in Hong Kong: sub-degree students’ career development and graduate adjustment. With an aim to enable 60% of secondary school leavers to access higher education, the government initiated the expansion of sub-degree programs in 2000. Intakes for self-financing sub-degree courses rose almost tenfold over the past decade, and the participation rate in post-secondary education for the 17-20 age group doubled to 66% by 2006/07 (Wan, 2011). However, increasing employment difficulties of sub-degree graduates are reflected by the substantial salary drop of sub-degree holders in the past 2 decades (Zhao, 2016). By examining their vocational identity, we aim to inform their transition into workplace and to design “developmentally appropriate” interventions with reference to their vocational development status. This study will utilize quantitative and qualitative methods. A quantitative, three-wave longitudinal study will be a major component. Phase one will involve the collection of quantitative data from eight hundred sub-degree students from three institutions at the start of their graduation year to validate the Vocational Identity Status Assessment (e.g., Porfeli, Lee, Vondracek, & Weigold, 2011). The second phase will take place approximately five months later and will involve a follow-up quantitative study of participants’ career development and job search prior to graduation. Phase three will trace the academic or employment adjustment of students six months after graduation. We shall test if students with more advanced identity statuses have better psychological and career outcomes. Moreover, to promote service mapping in relation to vocational identity status assessment, we propose to conduct a focus group study during phase two to generate ideas on how to tailor appropriate career services for different groups. 11600617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11600617.value: 愛滋病（HIV），一個高度污名化疾病，被稱為「我們」疾病 :不僅愛滋病感染者（people living with HIV, PHIV）承受與愛滋病有關的醫療負擔及歧視，其配偶也受到影響。雖然恥辱及歧視對PHIV和其配偶的影響曾被作為兩個個體分別報告過，但甚少研究是關於PHIV所受到的歧視和恥辱如何導致其配偶感到痛苦 或 其配偶受到的恥辱和歧視會如何影響PHIV的尊嚴痛苦感受。這些資料有助我們了解配偶中其中一方是PHIV時，他們夫婦的對偶互動關係。此外，考察可能會加重或削弱夫婦對偶互動關係強度的潛在調節變項及影響夫婦對偶互動關係的中介變項是重要的。我們一項進行中的研究是ECS研究受愛滋病影響的夫婦，為本研究提供了很好的夫婦對偶互動數據。基於我們之前針對119對其中一方患有愛滋病的夫婦的試驗研究（Yu, Chan, & Zhang, 2016），是次研究將會探討（一） 配偶中其中一方感受到的恥辱和歧視對PHIV的尊嚴及配偶照顧者的痛苦的影響程度、（二）PHIV的感染和死亡的意義重建作為此對偶互動關係的調節變項、及（三）PHIV的自我疼惜及配偶的寬恕作為對偶互動關係的中介變項，來研究受愛滋病影響的夫婦之間的對偶互動關係。此研究中的理論依據和假設將以系統相互作用模型（systemic-transactional model）作為指引。 是次研究的參加者會是233對只有其中一方患有愛滋病的夫婦，他們將完成兩波段縱性調查。PHIV及其配偶將會完成恥辱及歧視和關於PHIV的感染和死亡的意義重建的評估。PHIV亦會完成有關尊嚴痛苦及自我疼惜的評估。配偶也會對自己作為照顧者的痛苦及寬恕作出評估。行動者與夥伴相互依賴模式（actor-partner interdependence model, APIM）將被用作分析對偶互動的數據，而半縱性中介模型將被用作測試兩波段研究中的中介變項。 此研究計劃採用一個嶄新的角度來考證：以受愛滋病影響的夫婦二人作為一體去看待，及探討被高度污名化的疾病如何對中國夫婦造成影響。本研究的結果可以幫助學者和與中國PHIV相關的從業者加深了解受愛滋病影響的夫婦的對偶互動關係。最終，這研究的發現有助為這類夫婦發展具有文化敏銳性及以配偶為本的介入方案。

11600617.label: Realisation of objectives
11600617.value: The present two-wave study recruited Chinese dyads of HIV+ patients and their spouses. They lived with low socioeconomic status and limited medical resources. HIV constituted a challenging healthcare burden to these couples. We have achieved the first objective to examine the dyadic adjustment of HIV+ patients and their spouses and the predicting roles of stigma and other contextual factors. Based on the dyadic coping and systemic framework of resilience, we examined the heterogeneous patterns of dyadic adjustment. The results identified three subgroups: (a) maladapted couples (n = 58, 36.5%) with poor wellbeing in both members, (b) resilient couples (n = 50, 31.4%) with relatively good wellbeing in both members, and (c) maladapted patients and resilient spouses (n = 51, 32.1%) with poor wellbeing in patients but good wellbeing in spouses. Furthermore, these three groups showed distinct patterns of risks (e.g., stigma, financial difficulties) and resource factors (e.g., personal resources, relational resources). These findings highlight the role of stigma and other risk and resource factors to shape the dyadic adjustment trajectories of couples affected by HIV (see our publication on AIDs Patient Care and STDs). We have completed the second objective to investigate the moderating effect of stigma in the HIV serodiscordant couples who completed the baseline assessment and one-year follow-up. Using a “we-ness” research framework, we treated these couples affected by HIV as a unit in stress coping. Our findings showed that couple identity predicted fewer depressive symptoms and better physical health in these couples. These associations were moderated by the levels of stigma, with higher stigma weakening the protective effects of couple identity on the outcomes. These results have strong implications for promoting intervention programs based on strengthening or weakening moderating factors in mental health promotion of couples affected by HIV (see our publication on AIDS Care) We have fulfilled the third objective to examine the mediating effect of personal resilience factors on the links between relational resources and the wellbeing of patients. The systems framework of resilience was used to test how resilient factors external to or within the individual and their interactions can contribute to positive adjustment. The results showed that more relational resources in the marriage and family were associated with higher general, physical, and mental wellbeing. In addition, the mediation analyses found that personal resilience factors transmitted the positive effects of relational resources on the wellbeing outcomes. Our results underscore the promising direction of providing resilience enhancement interventions in HIV management (see our publication on AIDs Care).

11600617.label: Major findings and research outcome
11600617.value: HIV is a “we” disease. Not only the patients may transmit the virus to their spouses, but also two members may develop interdependence in the dyadic coping process. Based on a two-wave longitudinal study in this project, we focused on the effect of stigma and resilience resources in the dyadic adjustment of couples affected by HIV. There are three important findings generated from this project: 1. Variations in dyadic adjustment among heterosexual HIV-discordant couples and determining factors including risk and resources factors (published on AIDs Patient Care and STDs) Based on the dyadic perspective of couple coping, we identified three heterogeneous profiles of dyadic adjustment, maladaptive couples, resilient couples, and maladaptive patients with resilient spouses. These three subgroups were distinct in risk (including HIV stigma and financial difficulties) and resource factors (including personal resources and relational resources). These findings underscore the heterogeneity of adjustment among heterosexual HIV-discordant couples in rural China and suggest the potential usefulness of services tailored to specific subgroups. 2. The moderating effect of stigma in the association between couple identity and mental and physical health (published on AIDS Care) Guided by the “we-ness” framework, we treated couples affected by HIV as a unit rather than two independent individuals. The results showed that higher level of couple identity was associated with couples’ fewer depressive symptoms and higher levels of physical health. In addition, the associations were strengthened by the low levels of stigma. Our results indicate that it is essential for clinical endeavors to decrease perceived stigma among couples affected by HIV to protect their wellbeing outcomes. 3. The mediating role of personal resilience resources in the link between close relationship and wellbeing (published on AIDs Care) The systems framework of resilience posits that resilience resources external and internal can facilitate positive adjustment. It is not clear how they work to impact the wellbeing outcomes. This study found that external resources such as good marital relationship and family relationship and personal resilience resources both contributed to the wellbeing indicators. More importantly, personal resilience resources mediated the associations between external resources and wellbeing. By elaborating the mechanism that external and internal resilience resources work, our findings highlight the role of promoting resilience in the positive adjustment of people living with HIV.

11600617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11600617.value: This study focuses on the dyadic adjustment of couples affected by HIV. Rather than treating the couple as two separate individuals, we investigated their interdependence in coping of HIV. Based on the research findings obtained, we have the following suggestions for future studies to consider: (a) Dyadic theories focusing on the couple adjustment are essential to examine how the couples adapt to stress. The individual-oriented theories such as Lazarus and Folkman’s theory of stress and coping have various limitations, and dyadic-based theories such as Bodenmann’s systemic transactional model and Lyons’ theory of dyadic illness management provide useful theoretical frameworks to address the mutual influences between two members. (b) Statistical methods to handle dyadic data (e.g., actor-partner interdependence model, response surface analysis) facilitate the investigation related to the key issues such as the interdependence of two members and the congruence and incongruence between the two members. More advanced dyadic statistical tools would be helpful to address the various research questions in dyadic research. (c) The investigations on the moderating and mediating mechanisms of dyadic adjustment provide new knowledge to elaborate the process on how two members influence each other. The potential behavioral, psychological, and social pathways deserve further studies, which may inform the development of interventions to facilitate positive adjustment of couples under stress and challenges. (d) A mixed-method approach to integrating the qualitative and quantitative studies would be promising to understand the critical research questions in the dyadic adjustment of couples facing chronic illness.

11600617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11600617.value: HIV is a “we” disease. Not only the virus but also the stigma experience and mental health problems may transmit from the HIV+ patients to their spouses. Using an innovative perspective of treating couples affected by HIV as a unit in stress coping, the present study focused on dyadic relations within couples affected by HIV. HIV discordant couples completed a two-wave longitudinal study. Our findings identified three heterogeneous patterns of dyadic adjustment, with distinct profiles characterized by the risk (e.g., stigma, financial difficulties) and resources factors (e.g., personal resources, relational resources). Furthermore, stigma moderated the associations between couple identity and the mental and physical health of these couples. In addition, personal resilience resources mediated the associations between close relationships and the wellbeing outcomes. These findings provide new evidence regarding the dyadic adjustment of couples coping with chronic illness. Future studies are suggested to examine the interdependence of couples in stress and develop dyad-based intervention programs to facilitate their positive adjustment.

11600717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11600717.value: 人們對民意環境的感知會影響到他們的行為和認知。首先，民意的分佈特徵會影響人們的選擇與偏好。在日常消費、金融投資、購房置業以及公共參與等方面，人們都會利用感知到的大眾意見氣候做出決策。其次，政府各項措施的出台，往往也是針對既有的民意特徵，做出有針對性的回應。企業為了盈利，更需要長期監測公共輿論、追踪熱點話題、分析人們對企業提供的產品與服務的情緒反應。 然而，傳統調研手段在時效性和準確度上都難以滿足民意追踪的需要。首先，問卷調查的整個過程非常耗時：從問卷設計、抽樣、招募受訪對象到發放回收問卷，一次問卷調查需要很長的時間。同時，採用問卷調查方法收集的數據，有時無法準確反映受訪人在某些議題上的態度。比如，對於敏感議題，受訪人傾向於給出符合社會期待的答案；而訪問員的樣貌、種族等特徵也可能對受訪對象施加特定的影響，從而降低調研數據的準確性。此外，既往研究表明，問卷中的不同措辭會誘導人們給出不同的答案，從而影響研究人員對意見氣候的判斷。而問卷中題目的順序、選項的設置等因素也會不同程度的影響數據質量。 與傳統數據收集方法相比，大數據方法為追踪民意提供了新的可能。研究表明，通過抓取人們在網絡公共空間的言論，可以準確判斷民意走向和公眾情緒的波動情況。使用文本分析方法，我們可以用非介入性的方式了解網絡空間中的公共情緒和熱點話題，並用可視化的手段將分析結果呈現出來。這不僅可以讓我們追踪到人們在更多議題上的態度，而且能偶更好的揭示意見氣候的變動趨勢。 我們擬建立一個網絡平台，向公眾提供香港的民意狀況。利用大數據方法，我們會抓取香港的新聞網站和論壇上的帖子，並採用自然語言分析法，剖析出熱門話題中的民意特徵。為了便於公眾理解，所有分析結果將以可視化的方式呈現出來。同時，為了促進學界研究，我們擬公開抓取到的數據，人們可以自由下載數據，對民意特徵做進一步的探索。此外，由於民意數據是一種公共物品：它難以定價，卻能惠及政府、企業、機構和普羅大眾。因此，本項目將向公眾無償提供這一公共物品，以降低人們獲取民意數據的門檻，讓民意變得更加透明，同時也有助於社會各界基於民意做出更好的決策。

11600717.label: Realisation of objectives
11600717.value: Objective #1 To conceptually design a platform capable of scraping, analyzing, and visualize public expression on the internet. We have conceptually designed a platform of data collection, data analyzing, and data visualizing for public online expression. After comparing different solutions, we decided to use two separate servers to fulfill the purpose. One server is used for collecting and analyzing data whereas the other server is a web server for hosting content. In addition, we also purchased a NAS (network-attached storage) system for the data server to back-up data on a daily basis. We set up the systems by installing Linux Ubuntu package. We decided to use Python to develop crawlers for data collection and analyzing. Objective #2 To construct a list of representative web sources in Hong Kong that can be used for collecting raw text for further analysis. We constructed a list of web sources in Hong Kong. We targeted five discussion forums: www.hkgolden.com, www.discuss.com.hk, www.baby-kingdom.com, www.uwants.com, and lihkg.com. For news websites, four websites are picked: hk.appledaily.com, hk.news.yahoo.com, www.passiontimes.hk, and std.stheadline.com. The five discussion forums we picked are the most popular forums in Hong Kong, and they are the only five large local forums. For the news websites, we focus on the ones with most news comments and replies. Objective #3 To develop a number of web crawlers that can be used to scrape content from news websites and discussion forums. We developed a number of web crawlers that can be used to scrape content from news websites and discussion forums. Crawler development is one of the most difficult parts of the project. We encountered a number of problems. First, connection stability issue is an issue we have to deal with. Our university’s internet connection sometimes is unstable and therefore the crawling program could be disrupted from time to time. We have to set up some mechanism to let the program to pause for a while when connection is unstable. Second, data structure is the second issue. Not all discussion forums use the same webpage structure. We have to develop customized program for each forum and website to collect text data. Third, not all websites and discussion forums have historical data. For those without historical data, we could only collect the data cumulatively starting from 2018. Objective #4 To select and to design a set of algorithms that can be used to conduct topic modeling, sentiment analysis, and time series analysis. After data collection, we experimented with a few ways of analyzing the textual data. First, we plan to analyze the number of posts and comments/replies as a function of time. Second, we wish to gauge the overall public sentiment. Third, we wish to obtain insights into public evaluations of specific objects (e.g., public figures, and issues, etc.) One of the technical difficulties of analyzing Chinese characters was Chinese word segmentation. Even worse, the textual data we are facing are informal, idiomatic Cantonese expressions that internet users use on the internet. Therefore, we have to firstly build a Cantonese online expression dictionary to solve the problem. During the duration of the project, we have selected several batches of text corpus to be coded manually. We involved 8 local Hong Kong undergraduate students to do the coding. Objective #5 To design a set of creative methods to visualize public opinion data. In terms of visualization, we have designed four main methods to visualize the online public opinion data we have collected. First, for those numerical data, we used simple time series to visualize them, for instance, frequency mentions of a particular concept or indicator. Second, for popular words of each platform, we used a word list to visualize them. Third, for popular sections of a particular platform, we used bar graph to visualize them. Finally, for everyday top discussion threads, we first segmented the title of the threads and then used word cloud to visualize them. Objective #6 To construct a database where data sets could be used by social scientists for secondary data analysis; and to synthesize the components of the public opinion mining platform into a user-friendly system. As for platform building, we set up the web host server using Linux Ubuntu and Apache web host package. To host the data on our website, we have to design a list of indices and variables. The indices included in our project (http://www.webopinion.hk/) can be generally categorized into three types. The first type is shown in the section “Talk of the Town” where topics of the day and hot posts of the day on the seven discussion forums are displayed. The second type is shown in the section “Public Opinion Trend” where generic public opinion trends exhibited by the 12 online platforms are visualized. The third type is public opinion towards specific topics, which includes the sections “Public Figure Popularity,” “Organization Popularity,” “Public Opinion toward the Mainland,” “Social Issues,” and “Corporate Image.” We used different methods to construct specific indices in the analysis. So far, the database/website has received more than 4000 visits. The visitors came from all over the world. Objective #7 To produce summary report of public opinion in Hong Kong on a regular basis. Within the duration of the project, we have authored three summary report of public opinion in Hong Kong. In the first report entitled “Text-Mining Online Public Opinion in Hong Kong: Methods and Procedures,” we elaborated the details of the methods and provide specific explications for each step, including data sources, data crawling, data cleaning, tokenization, lexicon development, manual coding and optimization, index construction, etc. In the second report entitled “The Ebb and Flow of Public Sentiments in Hong Kong: Analyzing Public Opinion Online from 2000 to 2017,” we analyzed online public opinion towards different issues and topics in Hong Kong. This report provides an overview of public opinion on a variety of topics such as public figures, organizations, and social issues. The time span of the analysis in this report is from January 2000 (i.e., the earliest data point obtained) to June 2017 (i.e., the end of the third Chief Executive Leung Chun-ying’s administration). In the third report entitled “The Growth of Negative Sentiment in Post-Umbrella Movement Hong Kong: Analyzing Public Opinion Online from 2017 to 2019,” we analyzed opinion data from July 2017 (i.e., the inauguration of the fourth Chief Executive Carrie Lam’s administration) to December 2019. Overall, a consistent and clear pattern we found is that negative sentiments surged on the internet in many topical domains since February 2017 and lasted during the two and a half years.

11600717.label: Major findings and research outcome
11600717.value: Overall, public dissatisfaction was on sharp growth. A consistent and clear pattern we found is that negative sentiments surged on the internet in many topical domains since 2017 and lasted for a long period of time. First, 9 out of the 12 online platforms displayed negative sentiment all the time since 2017. Passion Times, HK01, and MemeHK had the most negative sentiments. Hong Kong people expressed negative sentiments towards various entities. Across all topical domains, political topics attracted the most negative comments. People expressed negative sentiments towards politicians (e.g., the Chief Executives, members of Legislative Council, and principal officials) and government agencies (e.g., government administrative agencies, the Immigration Department, and the Hong Kong Police Force) except for the Chief Justice of the Court of Final Appeal. In particular, the fastest decrease was observed for the Chief Executive and the Hong Kong Police Force. It could be related to the 2019 Anti-Extradition Law Amendment Bill protests. In February 2019, the Hong Kong government revealed its plan to amend the Fugitive Offenders Ordinance and the Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal Matters Ordinance. A series of large-scale demonstrations with clashes between the police and the protesters occurred in June 2019. Second, the index of public sentiments grew negative at an exponential rate during 2017-2020. Another important feature of public expression on the internet is the widespread use of swearing words. Among the five news media platforms, users of Passion Times, Apple Daily, and Yahoo seemed to be more likely to use swearing words when they commented on news stories. For discussion forums, LIHKG, Hong Kong Golden, and MemeHK were the online discussion forums with highest ratio of swearing expressions. The public opinion data we collected only describes the trend of public sentiment. To derive more meaningful research findings, we combined the text-data based indicator with other forms to data. In the first project, we examined whether exposure to online incivility will influence political attitudes and political participation. In the second project, we examined whether the public opinion online can predict offline based survey data. We found that the data derived from text-mining are able to predict survey based opinion data.

11600717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11600717.value: Potential for further development of the research includes the following three aspects. First, Cantonese dictionary we developed could be used for other research projects. In particular, we could further investigate the change of language habits over time in Hong Kong cyberspace. Second, the public opinion data we collected, could be combined with other data sources to understand the dynamics of opinion. One of my students plan to use the textual discussion data to predict opinion survey results. Third, opinion and ideological polarization could be further explored. How and why political attitude polarized was developed in Hong Kong is a topic worthy of study.

11600717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11600717.value: Big data provides a new direction for public opinion analysis by taking full advantage of people’s openly shared expressions on the internet. Using automatic textual analysis, it is possible to monitor social sentiment on various topics timely and visualize the pattern of change over time. Since people’s viewpoints are presented in a relatively more natural setting on the internet on a daily basis, it will be possible to track diverse trending issues and reveal the dynamics of public opinion, particularly for societies with high levels of internet penetration. We developed a website platform to visualize public opinion data in Hong Kong. Trending topics and discussion threads on significant issues were analyzed based on natural language processing techniques. Information with regard to public opinion could be considered as a public good. A public good is difficult to charge for, while a lot of people benefit from it. This project provides infrastructure for such public good. The datasets and analyses derived from the platform could benefit decision making for various stakeholders such as the government, the public, and the academic community in the long run.

11600817.label: Project Objectives
11600817.value: Devise a theoretical model of gamification outlining the conditions under which it can be described as possible (e.g. what kind of understanding of ‘play’ or ‘games’ it would necessitate), based on a synthesis of insights on the relationship between play and non-play, and, games and non-games in existential philosophy, play theory, and computer game studies. Provide a (road)map of the current field of gamification by cataloguing examples of existing applications of gamification into a new typology to be developed according to two dimensions: contextual (e.g. field of application, popularity) and structural (e.g. use of ‘game mechanics’ or ‘game design patterns’) properties. Identify, using the typology, prototypical examples for further analysis. Provide a critical reflection on the phenomenon of gamification by analysing the prototypical examples identified. Contribute to gamification discourse by contextualizing the findings in relation to real-world practice through exchanges with gamification designers. Contribute to wider debates in play theory, new media- and game studies by describing what gamification can teach us about studying technological gameplay. Explicate how our methodological approach could be replicated / built upon by others.

11600817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11600817.value: Traditionally play and games have been understood as frivolous, creative, free, separate from everyday life, and standing in contrast to productive activities like work and education. Many are familiar with the thrilling excitement of taking risks on a whim, knowing that it’s “only a game”. Recently, a movement often referred to as ’gamification’, or, ’ludification’, i.e. the use of game elements in non-game contexts, has emerged, promising that the ‘magic’ of game-playing could be added into productive activities to make them more enjoyable, efficient, and productive. Conference talks on gamification have garnered millions of views on Youtube, and, sparked an ever-growing body of professional literature, instructing how to radically transform productive activities. While design practitioners and engineers have embraced gamification and published a number of interdisciplinary anthologies, there are no humanities-based scholarly monographs theorizing gamification and its implications. Vocabulary for a critical study of gamification is lacking, and many questions distinguishing between ideas and realities of gamification have not received the attention they warrant. Is it without problems to harness play, with all the frivolity it entails, to serve the concerns of production and efficiency? Would it not undermine the very nature of play as an ’oasis of happiness’? Is blending of play and non-play theoretically possible? If not, what actually happens when an activity is ’gamified’? Does gamification make actual use of established ‘game mechanics’? Does gamification have something to teach us about technological play and games? Theorizing gamification seems to involve addressing the liminality between play and non-play, and so touches upon questions regarding the role of play in human endeavors. We propose project resulting in a theoretically and empirically grounded critical review of gamification and in a methodological approach that can be repeated by others. Our expertise and track record in computer game studies, existential philosophy, and play theory seems very well suited for answering the above questions. Work is structured into four phases, where subsequent phases validate the preceding ones: theoretical model-building based on synthesis of existing insights, cataloguing examples of gamification into a typology, case studies of relevant examples, and reflection. Considering gamification as ‘test case’, we will also shed light on other contemporary forms of technological play such as “free-to-play games”, and, on established work/play hybrids, such as “serious” and “educational games”, gambling, and professional (e-)sports. Our findings will also help practitioners and policymakers to explore what can be realistically expected from gamification’s transformative capabilities. 傳統上，嬉戲行為與遊戲本身常被認為是自由的、有別日常生活，而且與工作和教育等生產活動形成鮮明對比。許多人都熟悉這種跟從一個怪念頭冒險而又驚又喜的感覺，明白到它最終「只是一場遊戲」。近年，一場常被稱為「遊戲化」（gamification 或 ludification）的風潮開始冒起：把遊戲元素用於非遊戲場合，期待遊戲「魔力」的注入，可以令生產活動的過程更加愉快，而且更有效率與成果。然而於人文學術範疇，關於遊戲化的理論研究與應用至今鮮見。用於遊戲化批判性研究的詞彙有限，而且很多區分遊戲化理念與現實的問題亦欠缺應得關注。利用遊戲所蘊含的隨意性，去達至生產與效率的目標，這真的沒有問題嗎？本項目將提供一個遊戲化的理論與實證研究基礎理論的批判性探討。

11600817.label: Realisation of objectives
11600817.value: As documented in the mid-term report, we found that while the concept of 'gamification' helps uniting researchers from various traditions across disciplinary borders, it has little theoretical traction in the context of humanities. During the first stage of the project, we argued that the experiential qualities of play are often very similar to those of work, i.e. they can both be 'boring' in a similar fashion, and, players, like workers, can long to 'downshifting' from the demands of the game. Following the developments noted in the mid-term report, in the second year of the project we continued work under the revised three objectives, by focusing the project on the ontology of play, games and work from a theoretical and philosophical perspective. This warranted a closer investigation of the assumed differences and similarities between play and work, not only in regard to the subjective and experiental qualities, but also concerning with the nature of the game object involved. Rather than focusing solely on those examples labelled outright as "gamification", we looked at a wide range examples which blur the boundaries often associated with play and work, including but not limited to: playful and serious, outside and inside concerns of society, useless and productive, expression and purpose. This translates to computer games that are boring, computer games which make carnival out of real-life politics, games which seek to unite people together rather than separate them through competition, experiences and attitudes of the player running counter to the intentions in the game artifact, players who play not for winning but for others to see, etc. Due to these reasons, the roadmap of gamification described under objectives 2 and 3 remain underachieved. This theoretical and philosophical orientation reflects a scaling back of ambitions due to exceptional circumstances during the social unrest in Hong Kong in 2019 (albeit which now compared to Covid-19 seem much less strenuous than at the time!), during which it was difficult to carry out research in crowded places populated by young people. Hence, the plan for producing a monography within the timeframe of this project was not feasible and we did not hire an RA for this purpose. Thus, we are returning about 70% of the allotted RGC budget.

11600817.label: Major findings and research outcome
11600817.value: First, we investigated the relationship between play and work, and how these activities can be described as intertwined especially in the context of what the Belgian philosopher Michel Feher has called the "neoliberal condition", a world in which self-fashioning and identity-building have turned subjects into "entrepreneurs and investors in themselves". We found that this intertwined nature of play and work is also reflected in the themes of many triple-A mainstream games, such as "Animal Crossing: New Horizons" and "PC Building Simulator", and building on Feher and the German media archeologist Claus Pias, we speculated that the wide acceptance of these and similar titles may be due to their resonance with the challenges and demands the young generation of players is facing in their everyday lives. Assuming that Feher's "neoliberal condition" is an accurate description of contemporary society, it follows that the play/work distinction, which served play theorists like Huizinga and Caillois and their contemporary followers, well for a century, may no longer apply. Games feel like working, and, employers would like employees to feel like they are playing. This creates a set of messy relationships, into which computer games, as commercial products needing to be marketed and consumed, can tap by replicating patterns previously associated with work. This thread of research is documented in the DiGRA 2019 paper "Games on Working, Games on Gaming, Working on Games, and Games on Working on Games: On the self-referentiality that entangles neoliberal play and work". Second, we approached the ontology of play/work from the player's perspective, theorising the relationship between a game's player and its designer. Given the interactive and ergodic (Aarseth 1997) nature of computer games, they require non-trivial effort from their players. Describing this non-trivial as 'labour' raises the question of fairness of the compensation received by the player-labourer. We asked whether the player can "own the game" through their in-game actions, and found that paradoxically the player and the designer can be described as being in diametric opposition to each other, and this tension cannot be resolved. This thread of research is documented in DiGRA 2019 "God is a Game Designer" and the DiGRA 2020 paper "The Tragedy of the Art Game". We also evaluated the flexibility of the player's position as a player-labourer: whether the attitudes and perspectives the player can overcome the impossibility of "owning" the game. This resulted in a model of two positions for the player: the naïve and the sentimental. This is documented in the paper "Computer Game as Potentiality: The Naïve and the Sentimental Player" in the proceedings of Process, Performance and Mediation: New Paths for Intermedia Studies 2020, and, in the paper "On Naïve and Sentimental Player: Rethink the Potentiality of Computer Games" in the proceedings of Chinese DiGRA 2020. Third, we investigated the nature of games and play as "remediated" (Bolter & Grusin), repurposed, and reappropriated into productive activities. For this purpose, the notion of "performance" turned out to be very useful. This not least because of its double meaning in the context of games: apart from the obvious performativity dimension, it also signifies measurement and evaluation - traits found in both games and work. We evaluated work-like, 'boring' games, through their involvement in various forms of performance, and investigated the potential of the human player's agency in realising a performance using a computer game. This strand of research is documented in the chapter "Performing Profound Boredom in Euro Truck Simulator 2", published in the LUDIFIED anthology (in press).

11600817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11600817.value: We are continuing our research on the ontology of play/work with S. Möring, and are currently in the process of turning the DiGRA2019 paper on self-referentiality into a journal article. The research on the double meaning of 'performance' in the context of games and work opened a new avenue of research which resulted in a GRF proposal in the 2021/22 round.

11600817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11600817.value: Gamification is usually understood as the attempt to make productive activities more engaging by introducing playful or game-like qualities into them, thus increasing productivity. At the time of its emergence a couple of decades ago this concept was revolutionary, and even sounded oxymoronic to those versed in play theory, as it tried to combine things that are not combinable. Through theoretical and philosophical research into the ontology of play (and work), in this project we investigated contemporary examples, which blur the assumed border between play and work, ranging from boring computer games replicating patterns of work, into attempts of using computer games in artistic performances. We argue that while games and play on the one hand, and work on the other, have traditionally been considered as significantly different, if not even diametrically opposed, in today's context, where according to the philosopher Michel Feher, everyone has become an "investor in themselves", play and work resemble each other to the extent that the concept of 'gamification' has become almost tautological.

11601017.label: Project Objectives
11601017.value: To provide a reference for resettlement strategies through an in-depth review of the squatter resettlement program in colonial Hong Kong. To determine the role of and relations between various public and non-governmental agencies in building cottages and providing social services to cottage resettlement areas. To understand the grassroots efforts in community building by reconstructing the history of the cottage resettlement areas and documenting the personal stories of the settlers. To study Hong Kong’s self-help housing tradition by documenting and analyzing the planning and architecture of the cottage resettlement areas.

11601017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11601017.value: Due to rapid population growth and urbanization, many cities have squatter settlements, creating challenging societal and planning issues. Hong Kong is often considered a success regarding the resettlement of a large squatter population after the Second World War. This experience can serve as a useful reference for countries with burgeoning informal settlements. This research is a historical study on the cottage resettlement areas designated by the government since 1948 in which relocated squatters could build simple shelters at their own expense. It challenges the official narrative that often describes the cottage resettlement as a failed squatter resettlement strategy that was quickly replaced by a massive program to construct multi-storied resettlement estates. Not only did the cottage resettlement areas survive after the introduction of multi-storied resettlement estates in 1954, but they also thrived in the 1960s, accommodating over 87,000 settlers in 15 locations. The continuation of cottage resettlement areas for five decades before the last one was eradicated in 2001 indicates their indispensable role in long-term housing development in Hong Kong. The lack of studies on cottage resettlement areas prevents a comprehensive understanding of Hong Kong’s resettlement and housing history. The government’s indifference towards cottage resettlement areas reinforces a common misconception that formal, government-built housing is the only solution to the worldwide issue of informal settlement. Hence, settlers have often been incorrectly viewed as passive, helpless receivers of government aid. To counter this prejudice, this research uses the cottage resettlement areas in Hong Kong as examples to demonstrate the multiplexity in affordable housing solutions and the housing effort of the grassroots. The self-help nature of the cottage areas offers a flexible, economical, and quick approach to squatter resettlements, without which the government could never have the opportunities to develop a long-term housing program for Hong Kong. The originality of this research is that it considers the cottage resettlement areas not as temporary housing arrangements for squatters but as self-help communities built by settlers and sometimes philanthropic organizations and churches with minimal assistance from the government. The significance of this research is that it offers a more balanced view of the colony’s housing history by recognizing the efforts of the Hong Kong people, who have worked diligently to improve their living environments despite unfavorable conditions. It can also help inform the international debate on the strategies for informal settlements.

11601017.label: Realisation of objectives
11601017.value: All the project objectives have been achieved. For objective 1, the project team carried out an in-depth policy analysis to understand the squatter resettlement programme in Hong Kong. We studied the official reports and publications of the Resettlement Department, the Public Works Department, the Urban Council and the Social Welfare Office. We also conducted extensive research on archival documents and correspondence between government departments as well as the colonial office files. Finally, we examined the Emergency (Resettlement Areas) Regulation 1952, which formed the legal basis for the squatter resettlement programme. These sources enabled the project team to trace the chronological development of Hong Kong’s squatter resettlement policy from 1948 to 1973 and depict how the policy transformed in light of the changing socio-political conditions. We understand that between 1948 and 1953, squatter resettlement in the form of self-built, cottage-style structures was the only approach the government adopted. From 1954 to 1973, resettlement was simultaneously carried out in self-built cottages and government-built, multi-storey estates. These two strategies were abandoned in 1973 when the government promulgated a new 10-year programme to expand the provision of public housing. However, clearance of the cottage resettlement areas took a long time. The last three resettlement areas, Lai Chi Kok, So Kon Po and Mount Davis, were cleared in 2001. For objective 2, the project team undertook substantial historical research on the involvement of nongovernmental organisations (NGOs) in the cottage resettlement areas. We studied the official publications and websites of major NGOs to understand their respective cottage-building programmes and the social services they provided in the resettlement areas. We also examined correspondence between these NGOs and various government departments—documents housed in both the government’s and some NGOs’ private archives. Using these collected data, the project team analysed the similarities and differences between the cottage-building programmes of major NGOs, the most prominent ones being Kowloon City Fire Relief & Rehabilitation Committee, Hong Kong Settlers Housing Corporation, National Catholic Welfare Committee, the Maryknoll Missions, the Methodist Board of Missions and the Church World Service. We compared their different approaches to fundraising, cottage design and tenure arrangement. The project team also identified what social services were provided in which cottage resettlement areas by which NGOs. For objective 3, the project team carried out extensive research to reconstruct the histories of individual resettlement areas. Altogether, 15 cottage resettlement areas were established in Hong Kong. We studied historical newspaper reports on each resettlement area published in both Chinese and English. We also traced the planning and evolution of each resettlement area through historical maps and photographs. The project team utilised these historical records and maps to perform detailed case studies of several cottage resettlement areas, such as Homantin & King’s Park, Chai Wan, Ngau Tau Kok and Tai Hang Sai. To understand the housing experience in the cottage resettlement areas, the project team interviewed several former residents and church leaders who had served in the cottage villages. The memoirs of former residents of the resettlement areas published in book form and on social media also informed the project team about life in the cottage resettlement areas. For objective 4, the project team examined nearly all the available maps and aerial photos of every cottage resettlement area surveyed by the Lands Department between the late 1950s and the 1970s. In addition, we collected historical photos and architectural drawings of some cottages constructed in the resettlement areas. The project team referred to these maps and images to produce digital drawings of the cottage resettlement areas. These drawings are used in the principal investigator’s (PI) publications. They also form the basis of the project team’s analysis of the planning and architecture of the cottage resettlement areas.

11601017.label: Major findings and research outcome
11601017.value: The project has three major findings. First, between 1948 and 1953, the site-and-services approach of the cottage resettlement areas was proposed as the sole solution to Hong Kong’s acute squatter problem. Although the government’s direct construction of multi-storey resettlement estates became the mainstream resettlement strategy by 1954, this approach did not completely replace cottage resettlement, as self-built cottages offered an easy, quick, low-cost option especially when the government needed to ensure instant resettlement. The PI presented a paper on Hong Kong’s cottage resettlement history at the 18th International Planning History Society Conference. She also published an essay, ‘戰後房荒(2)-徙置平房區’ [Post-War Housing Shortage (2)—Cottage Resettlement Areas], on an online news outlet. Second, local philanthropic and religious organisations played a significant role in the development of cottage areas. These organisations had different approaches to cottage construction or management. Some of them donated the cottages outright to the government or settlers, while others rented or sold the cottages to eligible settlers via hire–purchase agreements. A few organisations chose to administer the cottage villages themselves. The PI has submitted a Chinese article, ‘非政府機構對解決香港戰後屋荒的貢獻’ [How Nongovernmental Organizations Help to Solve Hong Kong’s Post-War Housing Shortage], using the cottage areas as key evidence of philanthropic housing development in Hong Kong. She is also preparing a journal article, ‘Cottage Villages: The Contribution of Nongovernmental Agencies to Squatter Resettlement in Post-war Hong Kong’, focused on the cottage building programmes of four major NGOs. The PI has also shared her research findings at an international conference in Hawaii, a research seminar and a public talk. Lastly, most of the cottage resettlement areas consisted of a series of man-made terraces on hillsides so steep that any other form of development would be impracticable. The government provided the areas with basic municipal services, such as roads, drains, latrines, water standpipes and street lamps. Settlers needed to build stone or sand brick cottages following the government’s specifications or hire an approved contractor to build a cottage for them. The cottages built by NGOs were usually linear blocks divided into many small units. The PI has submitted an article, ‘Minimum Government Assistance: Planning Cottage Resettlement Areas in Post-war Hong Kong’, to discuss the cottage resettlement policy and planning of the cottage areas.

11601017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11601017.value: This research, which focuses on cottage resettlement villages built by the settlers themselves or by NGOs, has the potential to be developed into a comprehensive historical study on the third way of housing provision between two hitherto predominant models of public and private housing. Today, Hong Kong’s housing market is predominantly composed of private- and public-sector housing, to the extent that most local people are unaware of other alternatives. In fact, due to the acute housing shortage after the Second World War, many nongovernmental housing agencies, founded by philanthropists, churches and charitable organisations, were established to provide low-cost, working-class accommodation not only in the form of cottage resettlement villages but also low-cost rental housing, cooperative housing, youth hostels and so on. Most of these nongovernmental agencies ceased operations in the 1980s. A comprehensive study on Hong Kong’s third-sector housing would not only acknowledge the contribution of its providers but also remind us of the other housing options beyond the public–private dichotomy. This would also provide a useful historical reference for NGOs seeking to provide affordable housing for the working class in the future.

11601017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11601017.value: After the Second World War, large squatter areas mushroomed in Hong Kong and threatened its safety and sanitation. In 1948, the government developed a resettlement programme to compel squatters to move to designated resettlement areas along the urban fringe, where they could build simple cottages or huts at their own expense. In these areas, the government provided only basic municipal services, such as roads, public latrines, water standpipes and street lamps. This research challenges the common narrative that often describes the self-built cottage resettlement areas as a failed squatter resettlement strategy that was inevitably replaced by the government’s direct construction of large-scale, multi-storey resettlement blocks. It highlights that the cottage resettlement programme was established during a period when Hong Kong was suffering from substantial economic decline due to the trade embargo with China. The research demonstrates that the self-built nature of the cottage resettlement areas offered a flexible, economical and quick approach to squatter resettlement without which the government could never have had the opportunity to develop a long-term housing programme for Hong Kong. The research uses Hong Kong’s cottage resettlement areas to demonstrate the multiplicity of affordable housing solutions and acknowledge the achievement of grassroots housing efforts.

11601917.value: 追溯公元一、二世紀時印度僧尼行事以及僧團的組織和運作。 比對「根有部律」跟他派律典的異同。 考究律制的規定跟其應用之間的落差及其原委。 揭示漢譯律典在印度佛教研究的價值。

11601917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11601917.value: 「根本說一切有部律」為藏傳佛教秉持的律藏，有頗完整的藏譯本，在上世紀初更發現梵語片段。除列述戒規外，「根本說一切有部律」還包含大量敘事成份，史實與傳說交織，部份內容的年代可上溯至一、二世紀，近年越受到國際佛學界的注意。漢譯「根本說一切有部律」在中土由唐義淨譯出，共十五種近二百卷，或為藏譯本和梵語本以外的另一傳本，有其獨立價值。由於中土歸宗《四分律》，「根本說一切有部律」自古不受重視，迄今亦未得學界的充份利用。本計劃以漢譯「根本說一切有部律」為基本資料，考究在公元初年印度僧尼的行事和生活細節、僧團的組織和營運模式，以及與俗世的互動等，期望從僧團律制的角度，加強對早期佛教的理解，亦藉此顯示漢譯佛典在印度佛教研究上的作用。 Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya 根本說一切有部律is a kind of Vinaya practiced by Tibetan Buddhism. The text is well preserved in Tibetan language, and fragments of the text, which is written in Sanskrit, were discovered in early 20th century. Besides stating the monastic rules, the text also includes considerable quantities of narrative elements, which mixing up historical facts with legends. Part of the contents can be traced back to 1st or 2nd century CE, and thus has caught the attention of Buddhist scholars from all over the world in recent years. The Chinese Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya was translated by Yijing 義淨 in Tang dynasty, and has nearly 200 volumes in total. The Chinese Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya can be regarded as an independent canonical text and worth to study in depth. In the past, since Dharmagupta Vinaya 四分律 was the dominate Vinaya in China, the Chinese Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya has long been neglected, and not been fully utilized in Buddhist studies. Focusing on the Chinese Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya, this study investigates the daily life of monk and nun, the formation and operation of monastic community, and the interaction between the monastic and secular worlds in the early Common Era in India. It also aims at demonstrating the importance of Chinese Buddhist translations in Buddhist studies.

11601917.label: Realisation of objectives
11601917.value: 佛教約於公元前五世紀於印度由釋迦牟尼佛初立，佛入滅後，遺留教法和戒律，為弟子陸續編集，成為「經藏」和「律藏」。佛教流傳百多年後，先分裂成大眾部和上座部，之後再發展出十八或二十個部派，各傳承佛典，因此律藏也有多套。本計劃探討的根本說一切有部的律典(簡稱「根有部律」)是其一。「根有部律」可說是一組律典，現存漢譯十八種，逾百萬言，除戒規律制外，還包含古印度宗教、社會、歷史等多種多樣的信息。按中土佛教自唐以後，獨尊《四分律》；「根有部律」遲至唐代譯出，卷秩浩繁，給人印象是成書年代較晚，歷來不受重視；反觀西方學界百多年前已注意這律，近年Gregory Schopen以藏譯「根有部律」、梵語斷片為基本資料，配合其他佛典語本(除漢譯本外)，以及考古遺址和碑銘等實物資料，探討律制中一些少受關注但趣味盎然的課題，給筆者很大啟發。可是，西方學者或不諳漢語，未能充份利用漢譯「根有部律」。筆者在執行計劃期間，多次通讀漢譯「根有部律」，依不同課題，檢出和整理相關資料，配合其他律藏佛典、考古報告，以及大量二手研究文獻，進行探索，完成十五篇論文近三十萬字，相信已達成原擬定的目標。以下分七項介紹，並在每項之末標出關聯的目標號。 1. 西方學界早已注意到「根有部律」的重要性，更有學者發掘出其中的古舊記載，並把這律的成立年代大大推前，對探討古印度的佛寺組織、僧尼規範，有莫大意義。筆者搜羅自十九世紀中葉以來的相關論著，舖述及歸納其理據，指出律中值得注意的課題，尤詳述Schopen這富顛覆精神的佛教學者的看法，寫成〈「根本說一切有部律」研究史回顧──以成書年代為中心〉(約2萬5千字)，作為整個計劃的論述基礎和背景。(目標1-4) 2. 寺院是僧眾之所居，也是在家人朝聖的場所。寺院的建築、設施、布局等，某程度上可反映出僧眾的日常活動以及其跟俗世交往的情況，亦牽涉到戒律威儀的制訂。在漢譯各派律藏中，「根有部律」約二世紀成書，其中提及多種寺院建築，計有門樓、香臺、僧房、邊房、供侍堂、禪堂、食堂、浴室、溫室、厨廁、洗足洗鉢處、庫、供病堂、燃火堂、貯水堂、涼室、經行處、壇場、塔、制底、中庭、簷等，為了解僧團的物質生活的珍貴資料。筆者除檢視律中對這些建築或設施的描述外，並配合考古發掘及其他文獻記載，嘗試描繪出古代西北印的寺院情況，寫成〈從漢譯「根有部律」看古代印度佛教寺院的布局〉(約2萬8千字)。又香室、制底、窣堵波等設施，跟佛教的發展有密切關連，並有大量相關的考古發現，需專文論述方能究其底蘊，故另撰〈 香室考 ──以漢譯「根有部律」和佛教遺址考古材料為中心〉(約2萬4千字) 、〈漢譯「根有部律」制底考〉(約1萬字)、〈漢譯「根有部律」窣睹波考〉(約1萬8千字)三文。 (目標1, 3, 4) 3. 隨著佛教發展，僧團內部亦有分化，出現聚落比丘和蘭若比丘兩大類，前者住近村落，便於乞求衣食；後者遠離塵囂、專注修行，更有學者以蘭若比丘或為大乘佛教崛起的緣由之一。「根有部律」有大量關於蘭若比丘的記載。筆者以此為基礎，配合其他文獻記載及考古發現，對蘭若的選址、規模、物質供應、安全性、戒律的方便應用，以及其對佛教發展的意義作考察，寫成〈阿蘭若考—─以漢譯「根本說一切有部律」為基本資料〉(約2萬1千字)。(目標1, 3, 4) 4.「根有部律」有大量僧住處地望的記錄，從中除見僧團的居住環境外，亦反映出在該律編集歷程中，佛教四方流播的概況，筆者分類枚舉這些記錄，配合考古發掘報告，寫成〈漢譯「根有部律」所記佛僧住處考〉(約1萬字)。 (目標1, 4) 5. (1)有關各派律藏的對比，前賢多以各僧尼戒條，以及受戒、布薩、安居、自恣、藥食等律制運作為主題，指出箇中異同，或逐細項比對，已累積不少學術成果，筆者亦曾有專著。而筆者細讀「根有部律」等律典，注意到在戒條或律制擬訂的過程中，六群比丘、十七群比丘、十二比丘尼扮演頗大角色，為探索戒律原理和律制實踐的重要線索，而漢語學界以至國際佛學界，對之研究較少。筆者從文獻角度出發，搜羅各派律典有關六群比丘的記載，加以辨析和比對，推敲六群比丘的身份以及其可能成員，以至計算他們在各律藏的引發制戒的頻率，嘗試弄清六群比丘的來龍去脈，撰成〈六群比丘考〉(約1萬8千字)一文。(目標1, 2, 4) (2)據律文描述，所謂「六群比丘」，學識廣博，喜歡參與世俗事務，成為僧團和俗世的中介，亦因此易墮律網；而他們執著條文，據字面意義力爭，擾亂僧團秩序。筆者撰成〈六群比丘再評價──以漢譯「根有部律」為基本資料〉(約2萬3千字) ，全面舖述六群的行徑及其與戒律制定的關聯。(目標1-4) (3)近代學人抱開放態度，以六群的行徑為方便施設，旨在令律制更趨完備，六群搖身一變成正面人物。筆者於漢譯「根有部律」及其他律藏，挑選一些六群的事例作討論，指出他們暴露了僧團運作的毛病和戒律的漏洞，從中顯示出初期佛教中道和寬容的精神，亦由此反省古今律制思考的不同面向，寫成〈六群比丘違犯律制之省思──以漢譯「根本說一切有部律」為主〉(約1萬8千字)。(目標1-4) (4) 六群比丘之首鄔陀夷，其記事不止載於各律藏，還遍見於各種佛教文獻，事蹟多樣、稱呼不一。而「根有部律」承襲和綜合前說，編集出鄔陀夷由前生種因到今世殉道的整全生涯，為各律藏中僅見。筆者儘量搜尋相關記載，分類比較，寫成〈六群比丘之鄔陀夷考：以漢譯「根有部律」為主〉(約2萬7千字)，除展示鄔陀夷的生平詳情，還就律藏的編纂提出一些觀察，補足對六群比丘的研究。(目標2, 4) (5) 「根有部律」所記引發制戒的「惡比丘」，除六群外，還有十七群比丘，為他律較少談到。十七群比丘年少出家，不適應僧團的刻苦生活，與資深比丘不和，令佛制立多戒，反映出年輕僧人的弱點，以及僧團內部運作的隱憂。筆者試圖網羅最多資料，對比考究，寫成〈十七群比丘考──以漢譯「根有部律」為基本資料〉(約2萬1千字)。(目標1-4) (6)根有部獨集出《根本說一切有部苾芻尼毘奈耶》一種，單行流傳，為各派律藏中僅見。這律典舉出十二眾比丘尼為惡尼的代表，也有別他律所言的六群比丘尼。筆者通過比對諸律的制戒因緣以及爬梳律文，檢出與十二眾比丘尼或六群比丘尼相關聯的尼眾，再綜合各律典的記載，詳釋她們的行徑，寫成〈十二眾苾芻尼與六群比丘尼考〉(約2萬3千字)。(目標1-4) 6. 中土律宗巨擘道宣把「臥具四戒」中的「臥具」理解為「三衣」，並倡禁蠶絲衣；義淨據「根有部律」反駁，成為中國律制爭議中聞名的「公案」。筆者以律藏為起點，逐層剖析這場「公案」，寫成〈中國佛教三衣臥具律制論辯〉(約2萬1千字)，釐清這場爭議的來龍去脈。(目標2, 3) 7. 「根有部律」譯者義淨於譯文中不時附夾注，提供其對印度律制的親身見聞，並批評中土佛教的戒律實踐，與義淨另一大著《南海寄歸內法傳》相呼應，但較少受學者注意。筆者分衣、食、住、律制等方面，歸納和討論義淨律譯夾注的內容及其意義，寫成〈義淨律譯夾注之研究──從中印戒律實踐角度看〉(約3萬2千字)。(目標1, 3) 本計劃進行時遇到之困難及應對情況，主要有下三項： 1.有關漢譯律典及其他佛典的檢視或考查，非通過電腦檢索或研究助理所能意識到，全要由筆者第一手接觸篩選思索，難以假手於人，費時極多，這或許是人文科學研究不能逃避的工夫，以致未能處理更多課題。 2. 部份根有部的律典現存藏語本及梵語片段，如能與漢譯本作比對，必有所發現，近期也有學者零星進行這方面的工作。筆者對古印藏語文，僅略懂一二；只能借助辭典和一些現代語譯，對個別術語作考查，深感自身學力的不足，只好專注漢譯本的探究。 3.本計劃進行期間，原先的研究助理離職，適逢疫情肆虐，未能再物色到合適人選替代，除略礙進度外，某程度上亦白費了資助，實屬遺憾。

11601917.label: Major findings and research outcome
11601917.value: 1. 漢譯「根有部律」向被視為遲出的律藏，筆者檢視和綜合先賢的研究，推測其約於二世紀西北印成立，為研究古印度佛教的資料寶庫。(成果1) 2. 從漢譯「根有部律」的記錄，檢出僧眾住處的地望、寺院的規模‧建築物‧設施‧布局，配合其他文獻記載和考古報告，從物質文明角度，勾勒出古印度僧侶的活動，有補漢語佛學界的空白。(成果2-4, 13, 14) 3. 以漢譯「根有部律」為主軸，對比各派律藏及其他佛典有關六群比丘、十七群比丘、十二群尼的記載，指出僧尼各種違犯情況，顯示僧團隱藏的危機；並考究戒律條文與實際操作之間的衝突和調和、戒律的臨時豁免等，加深對律制設立原委和應用的認識。(成果5-8, 11, 12) 4. 探討漢譯「根有部律」有關蘭若僧的記載，並與聚落僧作比對，指出其與大乘佛教興起有關，對於印度佛教發展，提供律制方面的視角。(成果10) 5. 以僧尼律制為主題，比對各律藏，探討箇中異同和演變，有助了解律典的編集過程。(成果5-12) 6. 指出義淨根據「根有部律」及其於印度的親聞，對中土戒律的實踐作批評或補充，顯示出中印戒律實踐的分歧。(成果9, 15)

11601917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11601917.value: 基於本計劃的研究成果和心得，可循三方面再作探討： 1. 為佛教中國化這老課題提供戒律方面的視角。由於已對漢譯律藏進行多面向的研究，可接續探討印度律制於古代中國佛教界的落實情況；如有任何調整、增刪，甚或豁免，原因為何。 2. 律制新思考。基於對制戒原理的探究及僧尼各種違犯的認識，可就佛教及其律制在今天的適應和調整，提供文獻和教理上的反思資源。 3. 佛典編纂歷程的探索。佛典結集一直是佛學界熱議的課題，本計劃對比各種律典，亦旁及其他經論，已對律藏在編纂過程中的變化，提出一些初步的觀察，值得進一步以專項探討。

11601917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11601917.value: 律藏是僧尼行為守則與僧團運作規範的記錄。本計劃從唐義淨譯「根本說一切有部律」出發，對比各派漢譯律藏以及其他佛典和文獻，配合考古發掘和古碑銘記錄，在物質文明方面，考究古印度僧團住處的分布，嘗試還原寺院建築及其各種設施；在律制生活方面，揭示森林僧的活動形態及其與村落僧的分野，並藉著僧尼犯戒的記載及義淨對中土僧團的批評，反思戒律條文與實際操作之間的衝突和調和，凡此對中印佛教戒律的實踐，在文獻和教理上，提供豐富和嶄新的研究資源。

11602617.label: Project Objectives
11602617.value: 本研究計畫全面地搜集元代醫書及相關文獻，並剖析這些文獻內容及其蘊含各種意義。 本研究計畫透過《聖濟總錄》從北宋至元代傳承史，了解北宋醫學知識(尤其五運六氣學說)如何歷經金元兩代，成為元代官方推廣醫學知識，並隨著三皇廟在地方上廣設，同時從中央傳至地方，如何影響元代及其後醫學發展。 本研究計畫探討《聖濟總錄》的醫學分科概念及其與金元醫學發展關係。 本研究計畫探討經歷南宋金元分裂時代，元代一統後如何整合南北醫學知識，並進而考究當時中國醫學與回回藥學的分別，從而理解元代醫學的特點。 本研究計畫分析元代醫官編撰醫書的背景、過程與方法，及其與醫學發展關係。

11603217.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11603217.value: 港独主张合宪性的比较法与法理研究

11603217.label: Project Objectives
11603217.value: To conduct a comparative study on how secession/independence request of a subunit has been dealt with normatively at constitutional level in other jurisdictions. To apply the practices and case law in those jurisdictions to Hong Kong to examine what lessons Hong Kong can learn from those jurisdictions. To conduct an analysis of various theories of secession and evaluate what moral justifications are sound reasons supporting the demand of a subunit of a sovereign state for its secession. To apply different theories of secession to Hong Kong to answer the question whether Hong Kong people should be entitled to the right of secession/independence.

To apply the practices and case law in those jurisdictions to Hong Kong to examine what lessons Hong Kong can learn from those jurisdictions.
To conduct an analysis of various theories of secession and evaluate what moral justifications are sound reasons supporting the demand of a subunit of a sovereign state for its secession.
To apply different theories of secession to Hong Kong to answer the question whether Hong Kong people should be entitled to the right of secession/independence.

11603217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11603217.value: The constitutionality issue of demanding Hong Kong (HK) independence/self-determination has perplexed HK since the Hong Kong National Party was established in March 2016 advocating for HK independence and pledging to use whatever means available to break HK away from Mainland China. Despite strong criticism from various governmental organs in Mainland China, pro-establishment political parties and individuals in HK, such demand for independence has gained more support. The results of 2016 Legislative Council (LegCo) election indicates that around 20% of the voters who voted supported those candidates in favor of HK independence or self-determination. The newly elected pro-independence/self-determination LegCo members are determined to bring the issue before the LegCo. The NPCSC’s interpretation of Article 104 of the Basic Law is unlikely to stop the issue of HK independence/self-determination from being debated in the LegCo. This research project will first address the constitutionality issue through comparative study. Since neither Chinese Constitution nor HK’s Basic Law contains a right to secede, the scope of comparative study will be limited to those countries whose constitutions are silent on the right of secession. Cases decided in countries like the United States, Spain, Canada, and the United Kingdom will be carefully examined in order to answer the questions of (i) whether at constitutional level HK can demand independence/self-determination, and (ii) how HK courts, and the NPCSC should deal with HK independence/self-determination demand. This project will then address the jurisprudential issue of whether HK people should enjoy the right of secession from Mainland China. Political theorists have come up with more than a dozen of different moral justifications to support a constitutional right to secede. This project will analyze each of them to see they can provide moral support for HK independence/self-determination demand. Both issues will be examined against the background of “one country, two systems” and the fact that China context may substantially influence answers to the two research issues because HK’s liberal position towards fundamental rights is situated in the authoritarian China context. In addition to contributing to academic discussion on the two research issues, the outputs of this research project can provide guidance to not only HK courts, but also HK Government and Chinese Central Government on how the other jurisdictions with rule of law tradition have dealt with independence requests. Further, this research shall also shed light on how independence demand in Tibet and Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Regions should be dealt with by Mainland Authorities. 自主张港独及用一切方式将香港从中国分离出去的香港民族党于2016年3月成立并之日起，港独或者香港自决的合宪性问题就一直困扰着香港。尽管中国大陆不同的政府机构、香港的建制派政党和个人对港独主张提出了强烈的批评，但是港独主张在香港却得到了更多人的支持。2016年立法会选举结果显示，有差不多百分之二十的选民在这次选举中投票支持那些主张港独或者香港自决的候选人。当选的主张港独或者香港自决的新议员表明决心要把港独或者香港自决议题带入立法会。全国人大常委会对《基本法》第104条的解释并不可能阻止立法会辩论港独或者香港自决这一议题。 本研究项目将首先通过比较法研究来探讨这一宪法问题。由于中国宪法和香港《基本法》都没有明文规定香港有从中国分离出去的权利，因此比较研究的范围将限于那些其宪法同样没有规定地方政府享有从主权国家分离出去之权利的国家。本项目将仔细研究美国、西班牙、加拿大以及英国的案例，以期回答两个问题：1. 在宪法层面香港是否能够主张独立或者自决；2.香港法院和全国人大常委会应该如何应对港独或者香港自决这类主张。 该项目研究的第二个问题是在法理层面香港人是否应该享有从中国分离出去的权利。 政治学学者们已经提出了十多种不同的道德层面的理据来支持从主权国家分离出去是一种宪法权利。该项目将研究所有这些理据是否可以为港独或者香港自决提供足够的道德层面的理据。 上述两个层面的研究都将是基于“一国两制”的背景，以及香港这个对基本权利采用自由主义立场的特别行政区是属于集权的中国这个主权国家之内这个大背景之下。 该项目的成果除了能够对上述两个问题的讨论作出学术上的贡献之外，还可以给香港法院、香港政府以及中国政府就其他法治国家是如何应对独立主张方面提供指引。而且该项目的研究成果还能给中国政府如何处理西藏和新疆的独立主张提供指引。

11603217.label: Realisation of objectives
11603217.value: The investigator has achieved all four project objectives satisfactorily. With regard to the first objective, the investigator has reviewed the constitutions of most countries in the world and also reviewed the literature on secession and noticed that there are three constitutional models to deal with the issue of secession at the constitutional level. The first is to incorporate into a constitution a mechanism to handle secession demand. The second is that the constitution is silent on this issue. The third is that such a demand will be dealt with by a piece of national legislation on a case by case basis when a country has no written constitution. For the first category, the investigator has examined the following jurisdictions: Ethiopia, former Yugoslavia, and the State Union of Serbia and Montenegro. For the second category, the investigator has examined the practice in the US, Spain, and Canada. For the third category, the investigator has examined the practice in the UK. Because both China has a written Consitution and HK has a written mini-constitution, the lessons from the second category are most relevant to HK. With regard to the second objective, the investigator has studied China's approach toward secession and HK's position in China. He then applies the practices and case law in those jurisdictions to HK. Through comparative study and discussion, the investigator comes to the conclusion that the practices in the UK, Spain, Canada, and the UK can all shed light on how HK courts should deal with a demand of secession at the constitutional level. The lesson the HKSAR can learn from the four jurisdictions is that it has to obtain consent from mainland China in order to become independent. Failing that, the only means for it to become independent is through revolution, which is clearly not feasible. With regard to the third objective, the investigator has conducted a thorough literature review of the theories of secession. There exist many moral justifications to support the independence claims of a subunit with a sovereign country. Different scholars have classified those moral justifications into different categories. The investigator has reviewed and compared theories by three scholars, Allen Buchanan, Wayne Norman, and Cass Sunstein. The conclusion is that even if a country's written constitution is silent on the right of a subunit of a sovereign state, the subunit may still demand independence on some moral grounds. With regard to the fourth objective, the investigator first examines the relevance of all twelve moral grounds and comes to the conclusion that only four of them are relevant to HK, i.e. democratic theory, national self-determination theory, choice theories, and just cause theories. Thereafter, the investigator applies each of them to HK. Through analysis, he comes to the conclusion that the only theory that can be applied to support demand for HK independence is the choice theories. Unfortunately, that is not a theory that has gained the support of the majority of scholars and sovereign states. The conclusion is that the demand for HK independence does not have good jurisprudential support. That means HK people should not be entitled to the right of independence.

11603217.label: Major findings and research outcome
11603217.value: There are two major findings. Firstly, since neither the Chinese Constitution nor the Basic Law of the HKSAR contains any provisions on the right to secession/independence, from the normative perspective, the experiences of those jurisdictions whose Constitutions are silent on the right to secession/independence are the most relevant for comparative study. This paper argues that the practices and case law in all the four jurisdictions, including the US, Spain, Canada, and the UK, are consistent and support the argument that only with the consent of the Union or all the people in the existing sovereign country will a subunit of it be possible to secede from the Union. Applying their practices and case law to the HKSAR, the only lawful means for Hong Kong people to seek independence from mainland China is to obtain the consent of all Chinese people as represented by the NPC and NPCSC. Specifically speaking, any advocates for Hong Kong independence need to resort to available means under both the Basic Law and Chinese Constitution to amend both the Basic Law and Chinese Constitution to remove the provision that Hong Kong is an inalienable part of China. Only after such an amendment will it be possible for Hong Kong to secede from China. Secondly, there exist many moral justifications to support the independence claims of a subunit with a sovereign country. Even if a country's written constitution is silent on the right of a subunit of a sovereign state, the subunit may still demand independence on some moral grounds. Out of the twelve moral grounds/theories examined, only four are relevant to HK, i.e. democratic theory, national self-determination theory, choice theories, and just cause theories. The only theory that can be applied to support demand for HK independence is the choice theories, which has gained the support of the majority of scholars and sovereign states. As a result, HK people should not be entitled to the right to independence. Two journal articles have been written, one has been published, the other has been submitted for publication.

11603217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11603217.value: The nature of this research project is to study two important legal issues, one is whether it is constitutional for HK people to demand independence from mainland China, the other whether HK people should be entitled to the right to demand independence. Its significance lies in its comparative study of similar demands in other jurisdictions and their handling by courts in those jurisdictions, the theoretical discussion of different moral justifications for independence, and their application to HK. There are two obvious values. The first is that the outcome shed light on the debate on the constitutionality of HK independence demand both from a comparative perspective and a moral perspective. The second value lies in its guidance effect for any potential litigation on the constitutionality of HK independence demand before Hong Kong courts.

11604217.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11604217.value: 企业担保案件在中国法院的审理

11604217.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11604217.value: Prof Huang, Hui Prof Jiang, Daxing Dr Qu, Charles Zhen

11604217.label: Project Objectives
11604217.value: To obtain a complete picture on the ways in which the PRC Courts allocate risks associated with corporate guarantee contracts. To identify factors the interaction of which has contributed to the constitution of the institutional environment in which the Courts resolve disputes arising out of corporate guarantee contracts. To reveal the gap between the law on the books and the law in action in the context of corporate guarantee contracts through ascertaining the extent to which the Courts adjudicate according legal rules/principles, judicial or party policies, or ulterior motives. To identify the extent to which and the ways in which the existing patterns of judicial risk-allocation need to be altered and to provide the law makers and SPC with empirical evidence and normative views for the drafting of a Judicial Interpretation by the SPC on Article 16 and the future reform of the PRC Company Law.

To identify factors the interaction of which has contributed to the constitution of the institutional environment in which the Courts resolve disputes arising out of corporate guarantee contracts.

To reveal the gap between the law on the books and the law in action in the context of corporate guarantee contracts through ascertaining the extent to which the Courts adjudicate according legal rules/principles, judicial or party policies, or ulterior motives.

To identify the extent to which and the ways in which the existing patterns of judicial risk-allocation need to be altered and to provide the law makers and SPC with empirical evidence and normative views for the drafting of a Judicial Interpretation by the SPC on Article 16 and the future reform of the PRC Company Law.

11604217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11604217.value: Guarantees provided by companies play a crucial role in securing finance for small or medium sized businesses in China. Under PRC Company Law Article 16, a company’s decision to act as a guarantor must be authorized by either the directors or the shareholders’ meeting, depending on whether the borrower is a shareholder/controller or a company outsider. A PRC company must act through its ‘Legal Representative’ (LR). This latter requirement is subject to abuse by those professing to act as the company’s LR to obtain loans for themselves or others by proffering the company as a guarantor without the latter’s authorisation. How to allocate risks of corporate guarantee contracts? This issue is vexed because rules governing the validity of corporate (guarantee) contracts and parties’ liability thereunder are either incomplete or biased against the (alleged) guarantor. The challenge for courts is how to balance the need for protecting contractors/lenders and that for safeguarding the interests of the company’s shareholders and creditors. Our pilot project based on the Supreme People’s Court (SPC) and High People’s Court (HPC) decisions of Article 16 cases listed in an authoritative database reveals that courts usually hold the alleged guarantor wholly or partially liable, irrespective of the court’s own decision on the validity of the alleged guarantee contract. This trend signifies a failure in maintaining an even hand between the two conflicting interests. Such a failure may incentivize fraud against the shareholders and creditors of the company, thereby discouraging investments. This Project will review all accessible Article 16 decisions since the enactment of that provision in 2005 to complete the picture on the ways in which risks associated with corporate guarantee have been allocated and factors that have contributed to the formation of the patterns of judicial decision-making. The Project also proposes to conduct semi-structured interviews with judges and other legal/commercial professionals to obtain information that case reports do not provide, such as the reasons why courts adjudicate in a given pattern where no guiding principles/rules exist or why judges fail to adjudicate according to existing rules. The Project will result in empirical data necessary for verifying claims on Article 16 adjudication made in the literature and for reforming the law on corporate guarantee contracts, and corporate contracting generally.

11604217.label: Realisation of objectives
11604217.value: Objectives 1 to 4 have all been achieved. Charles Zhen Qu published a journal article in 2020 and a Chapter in a CUP book. Charles Zhen Qu, Bin Li and Lauren Yu Hsin Lin have also co-authored a data-driven paper on the factors determining the outcomes of cases on corporate contracts that give a security using the data collected from the 310 case reports collected and analysed for the purposes of this project. This paper is under review by a high impact journal. Our published paper and chapter alone helped achieve objectives 1 to 4. The findings and proposals reported/made in the 2020 paper accurately anticipated the set of new rules that the Supreme People's Court announced on, among other things, the solution of disputes arising from unauthorised security contracts made in the name of a company. This set of rules, which has statutory force, was announced in the minutes of Ninth National People's Courts Conference on Civil Law and Commercial Law Matters（九民紀要 or Jiu Min Jiyao). The paper was accepted before this set of rules were announced. Our paper under review helps reinforce the contribution of that our 2020 paper and 2022 chapter on the achievement of objectives 1 to 4.

11604217.label: Major findings and research outcome
11604217.value: Our major findings include: 1. Where the primary debtor has defaulted on a loan secured by a guarantee or charge given in the name of a company without authority, the court in most of the cases held the alleged corporate surety partially or wholly liable for the unpaid part of the loan, even though the latter has never committed itself to the alleged surety contract with the creditor. 2. In most of the cases, the suspicion of the creditor on the regularity of the security should have been aroused but it, the creditor, still provides credit without making an inquiry on the regularity of the security. 3. The courts decisions in relation to both the decision outcome and the legal analysis, are highly uniform. 4. In making their decision, the courts have apparently followed two Typical Cases announced in the Supreme Court's monthly Gazette, even though both of the Typical Cases, according to our analysis and the rules announced in Jiu Min Yiyao, were wrongly decided. 5. One of the deficiencies in the existing legal framework is the lack of provisions on the rights of persons seeking to deal with a company where the company is represented by its 'Legal Representative' (who is not an 'agent')of the firm. 6. Where decisions involve closing gaps in the governing statutes, precedents, even if wrongly decided, are influential on subsequent decisions. 6. The force of the two Typical Cases' influence is negatively co-related to the rank of the deciding court.

11604217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11604217.value: 1. The soundness of the newly announced rules on resolving disputes arising from corporate security contracts requires further analysis. 2. The same rule (article 16 of the Company Law) also governs the effect of purported but unathorised corporate investment decisions. Cases on unauthorised INVESTMENT decisions requires further research. 3. A discovery will need to be made on the relationship between the influence of a precedent and the rank of the precedent court. 4. Whether precedents decided by the immediate superior court is more influential than those decided by other courts requires further study 5. Factors that terminate the influence of a Typical case also requires study. 6. The extent to which precedents influence the Supreme People's Court's selection of Typical Cases is also worth studying.

11604217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11604217.value: Our project has studied (i) how the People's Courts have resolved a complex legal issue where the governing legal rules are lacking or ambiguous, (ii) the influence of previous court decisions (precedents) on judicial decision making, (iii) the quality of both the relevant precedents and subsequent decisions. Our analysis was conducted using the data collected through an extensive case review. Our findings contribute to (i) the development of the rules on the issues under study, (ii) the understanding of the role of precedents in the Chinese legal system, (iii) the body of empirical evidence and literature on judicial behaviour in civil law systems, and (iv) the understanding on the difference between the law on the book and the law in action and the reasons why.
