11604317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11604317.value: 儘管香港長者曾對香港作出了巨大的貢獻，香港社會普遍認為長者教育程度低，經濟上和情感上亦屬於依賴的一群。學者也發現，本地有關家庭照顧的文獻，主要關注老年人作為被護理者，而不是照顧者；他們是經濟負擔而不是經濟貢獻者。此外，由於女性相對於男性的壽命較長，單身令她們在住屋上處於不利地位；而她們又被視為家庭照顧者，較少得到家庭支持及照顧。故此，年長女性往往是本地貧窮人口中最貧窮的一群。有鑑於此，香港年長婦女人口應與香港長者分開研究。 這個研究將探討年長婦女的不同經驗和身份。研究主要探討出生於1940年至1955年（2016年為61-76歲）的女性。這一代婦女在六，七十年代很多是家庭財政支柱。結婚後，她們成為家庭主婦，照顧者角色亦成為她們的主體位置。由於香港經濟轉型，從製造業轉為金融服務業，很多女性於九十年代後面臨就業不足、失業，及（強逼）退休。雖然曾有不少研究討論過這一代女性以往作為家庭財政支柱的經歷及她們的現況，但是沒有研究探討這一代婦女，因著不同的生活經驗，怎樣發展出不同的主體性，以及她們對以往及現在生活的想法，怎樣產生流動和復雜的主體性。 本研究探討這一代婦女如何對自己不斷變化的社會及角色做出反應，建立自己的身份及自尊。他們在家庭和家庭角色之外如何界定自己的身份？他們現在的日常生活是怎樣的？在香港不盡完善的福利制度下，他們如何擴大生活？

11604317.label: Realisation of objectives
11604317.value: To achieve the three objectives, the PI, Co-Is, and RAs have finished 43 interviews (each interview lasted 3-8 hours, and each case involves 1-4 visits) and all transcriptions and case notes. They were born from 1939 to 1965 (age 57 – 83). Objective 1: 1. All women interviewees came from humble background. We purposely recruited women from varied backgrounds; informants’ parents were all manual workers. 2. Among the 43 women, almost half (21) attained up to primary education level; 15 up to junior or senior high school level, nine university level with five who studied part-time while working. In 2021, 13 were working full-time, five part-time, and 25 retired. Regarding their marital status, 34 were married, eight experienced divorce, seven women’s partners passed away, two re-married, and nine were single. Only three married women have no children, and almost half have two children. Almost half (21) lived in private housing, six in government-subsidised private housing (HOS), and 16 in public housing. The interviewees’ profiles are summarised in tables 1 and 2 3. Most women lived with parents when small. Most women interviewees described their mothers worked hard. 4. Over half of our interviewees explicitly talked about their parents valued son and belittled daughters; they said they did more housework, ate less, and started paid work earlier than their brothers. Over one-third of the interviewees, as prepubescent girls, looked after younger siblings physically and did household chores; some also took care of their grandparents at home and in hospitals. 5. As most of their parents were not educated and some illiterate, all these women received no help from parents regarding study. Few mentioned their parents did not let them study, and they regretted they didn’t have chance to continue study. In study, some of them emphasised they were ‘self-reliant’. As the family did not have the atmosphere of studying, some were not interested in study, and some felt stressful as they did not understand what teacher taught in class. 6. Social welfare, food rationing, Girls’ and Boys’ Club, public library are important to these women’s young lives. Objective 2: The public/private dichotomy is frequently brought up in discussions about gender and space. Feminist geographers began to question the spatial binary of workplace/home and private/public. We focus on how Hong Kong women manage domestic work spatially, and how change throughout life relate to their subjectivities and womanhood. We analysed older women’s life stories chronologically, conducted cohort comparison, explored the fluidity and tension of domestic spatial practices, and found four kinds of domestic spatial practices pertinent to different life-course, where the intersection of domesticity, work and other daily practices vary, and domestic space intersects with other (e.g. institutional, entertainment) spaces. 1. Dutiful versatile daughters: Expanded domestic responsibilities and extended domestic space. Although women and femininity were ideologically designated to home space, interviewees’ childhood domestic responsibilities expanded beyond that. Physical care-work, housework at/near home extended to domestic practices in further away urban and workspaces, resulting in intersecting domestic and work practices within and outside the home. Hong Kong daughters before the 1970s had to be efficient and capable in homemaking and care work, self-reliant in formal education, flexible in converting home space to workspace, mobile in moving between home, school and workplace. They could not practice domesticity by simply staying inside home space. 2. Modern and independent working daughters: Making money for the family, gaining spatial (and sexual) freedom. The intersection of conservative familial values on unwed daughters’ duty to make money for the family, industrialisation, globalisation, geographical mobility, and pop culture that glorifies self-reliant factory girls changed working daughters’ family status, giving rise to a reformulation of modern womanhood as economically and spatially independent. Young working daughters, with minimal education credentials and jobs with few prospects, escaped from home and enjoyed independence and romance brought by work. Spatial freedom in local public space, however, is limiting because of Confucian values on female chastity. The further they were away from ‘home’, the more deviant sexual practices they allowed themselves. 3. ‘On my own’ working mothers/women: Intensifying domestic responsibility and flexible domestic spatiality. Among the 34 married interviewees, 31 became mothers, and those with children had the heaviest domestic responsibilities. Many women express difficulties but are proud of their success in maintaining a household materially, economically and social-psychologically. ‘On my own’ is the frequent phrase they used. Of the 31 women who became mothers, 29 had worked full-time, part-time work or in self-owned business throughout their lives whilst shouldering a range of domestic responsibilities. Full-time homemaking was not an option for most because a single income would not suffice. Facing burdensome domestic work, working mothers extended domestic space to cater for their needs. Quite a lot of working mothers monitored their children’s homework in public transport. Some leveraged social gatherings in restaurants for childcare, others created social space by bringing her children to church despite not being Christians, some like Yu even appropriated gambling venues for childcare. 4. Relieving older women: Attaining (spatial) freedom through temporal and domestic spatial demarcation. As shown from the above, interviewees’ domestic spatial practices have been constituted by the combination of their assumed responsibilities for social reproduction and family livelihood. Inter- and intrafamilial relations continue to affect these practices as they age. Some still had to bear intergenerational and/or intragenerational domestic responsibilities for their adult children. Nevertheless, some became more self-oriented with age. Realising the never-ending domesticity and their limited life-span, they chose to live in the ‘here-and-now’. Through what we call ‘temporal demarcation’ and ‘domestic spatial demarcation’, they try to re-gain domestic and spatial freedom. Objective 3: 1. Six of our eight interviewees who have grandchildren provided childcare for them. Some explicitly said they preferred working to childcare; others have mixed feelings of tiresomeness and joy. Never married women also needed to shoulder intra-familial domestic duties. Nevertheless, these dutiful sisters also learn to ‘slowdown’ and to ‘treat myself well’ by spending time on religion, voluntary work and exercise. 2. Older women realise that domesticity is a never-ending business. Instead of multiplying domestic space through creative spatial production (e.g., church, bus, and restaurant) as they have done in the past, some tactically relieve domesticity through ‘domestic spatial demarcation’. Although Tong visits her mother weekly, she distanced herself from domesticity using patrilineal boundaries. Now I learn to ask her (mother) to deal with these things, because I am old and not as energetic as before. For example, every month, we have family gathering, she does nothing and just asks me to organise…. I sometimes told my mom, ‘I am Mrs Tong, and I am not Mrs Suen. You are Mrs Suen. Please do your job’.… I am afraid of getting old, that’s why I need to treasure the present. I won’t wait, I do what I wanna do now…. I like studying a lot, but no chance to do it when I were young. That’s why I took university courses as elderly student. I am so proud of myself! Another lives with her son’s family and detaches herself from their domestic demands through what we call ‘temporal demarcation’. During weekdays, she looks after her grandson, but insists to have ‘holiday’ during weekends when she goes wherever and does whatever she wants.

11604317.label: Major findings and research outcome
11604317.value: This research interviewed 43 HK older women and examined their life stories on domesticity. We found that Hong Kong women, since childhood, have creatively employed temporal-spatial strategies to multiply and shrink domestic space to negotiate domestic responsibilities and gender hierarchy prescribed by family and society. Domestic space changes throughout life and intersects with other spaces, including workspace, institutional space, entertainment space and public space, through which various subjectivities emerge. More specifically, we argue that these women, through performing various domestic spatial practices at different points in their life course, have developed self-reliant and independent ‘modern’ womanhood and other gendered subjectivities such as dutiful daughters and tiresome working mothers, which complement, negotiate and contradict with each other, constituting to what we term ‘disjunctive modern Hong Kong womanhood’. We also find that extensive qualitative social research has equated the literal translation of talk with history (i.e., lived experience) and its representation (i.e., interviewees’ life as text). Influenced by feminist postconstructionist epistemology, feminist media theories, we created an interactive video installation and a web project to recount older women’s life experiences and subjective evaluations in contemporary Hong Kong, identify the social contexts of these life stories, and explore the relationships between representation and lived experiences. Major research outcome include two journal articles (under first and second review respectively) and a website (https://kimchoi.net/a-story-of-ones-own/).

11604317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11604317.value: In writing the manuscript, we find that there is no research in the past exploring HK women's ideas about women's ideal life. It seems that most married HK women, even though they are successful in career, still holds the ideal of performing full-time mother. The articulation of Confucianism and intensive mothering support HK women maintain their domestic role. There should be further research on this issue.

11604317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11604317.value: Using a life-stage approach, we interviewed 43 Hong Kong women (born between 1939-1965) about their lives and describe and analyse their stories in relation to gendered spatial practices and domesticity. We argue that such practices are products of cultural norms of gendered domestic roles, individual family practices and work trajectories, the change of childcare discourse, local housing policy and socioeconomic conditions. By focusing on Hong Kong women’s management of domesticity - homemaking, household budget, household members’ well-being and education, and conceiving space as the summation of multiple social relations across all spatial scales, we argue that although most interviewees are burdened by domestic responsibilities, their domestic space stretches far beyond home space. Using life-stage approach, we discuss how women comply, struggle and negotiate their feminine domestic roles in the liminal and intersecting domestic spaces. Their tour of domestic space is geographically mobile and fluid, but at the same time socially embedded, materially located, structurally situated, and historically constructed. Domesticity creates wanted and unwanted, joyful and helpless domestic spatial production and practices. Femininity and domesticity is co-constitutive.

11605017.label: Project Objectives
11605017.value: 梳理金文泰與英國殖民部、外交部、中國駐華領使、北洋政府、廣州國民政府的多元互動，觀察其於粵港關係變局下的施政方針與策略，了解香港在中英政治博奕下的角色與功能。 擴闊香港史的研究空間與思想視域；除了一貫運用的殖民地檔案、外交部檔案等官方文件外，將遍尋中國南來者、居港華商遺老、報刊資料上之在地民眾有關金文泰治下香港社會發展的評議，並將整理有關金文泰的訪談、電文信牘、演講稿、金文泰的學術著作、搜集中英兩國及美國、日本方面對金文泰管治香港期間的評論、報導，嘗試從多層次多角度觀察金文泰的治港構想及其在港建立的“殖民性”。 探討金文泰扶助儒學、籌建香港大學中文學院、與華商協作營造守舊社會風氣的各種籌算，在所謂“勾結/合作式”的民族主義以外指出香港向來存在着“批判/革命”的民族主義”，探討它們與在地紳商的文化民族主義之關聯與分野，進而釐清1920至1930年代香港社會的思想發展脈絡，補足早期香港史研究之不足。 研究1920年代華人紳商、華人代表或前清遺老的結社情況，並從中釐清他們的“新”、“舊”文化態度、國家民族認同以及他們當時周旋於民國政府與港府之間的各種深層政經考慮，嘗試使這批影響香港社會文化發展的人在人格形象上與歷史定位上顯得更加清晰和具體。

11605017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11605017.value: The initiating motivation of this research is that the PI has a feeling that Sir Clementi’s personal research as well as that of the academic community in general has been negligent in the area of Hong Kong’s developmental history, especially of the 1920s period. It is vital for the whole research field to review the topic and gain an in-depth understanding of the social, cultural as well as educational development of Hong Kong after the Cold War. While this period is not long, a proper study of its many significant events and personalities will help in the comprehension of the educational and social policies-making of Sir Clementi’s government. The research will thoroughly investigate and analyse government documents, Sir Clementi’s personal letters, memoirs, newspaper and journal articles. This will provide an understanding of Sir Clementi’s colonial management experience so as to sketch a comprehensive picture of the socio-cultural development of Hong Kong, which is an area that has long been neglected and over-simplified in the research field. The findings will provide an understanding of how “colonialism” developed gradually in Hong Kong. This is significant as it certainly has its historical tradition and integration. In fact, the sociocultural development of Hong Kong has always had a profound interaction with colonialism, nationalism and localism. With these three elements affecting one another, Hong Kong has been shaped into a society with a unique identity of its own.

11605017.label: Major findings and research outcome
11605017.value: 本計劃在執行期間，已發表了4篇論文，另有3篇已接受刊登但未正式出版；先後以相關題目參與的公開學術演講共2場，以相關研究成果在學術研討會發表的共計有8場，目前正在審核的文章有1篇，基於這項計劃而衍生的論文仍處於撰述階段的稿件有2篇。上述研究，一如申請時釐定的，梳理了金文泰與英國殖民部、外交部、英國駐華領使、北洋政府、廣州國民政府的多元互動，觀察其於粵港關係變局下的施政方針與策略，了解香港在中英政治博奕下的角色與功能。PI運用了殖民地檔案、外交部檔案等官方文件，報刊資料及居港華商遺老著作，整理了關於金文泰治下香港社會發展的相關評述。基於這些歷史文獻，PI期望在將來可以成功出版，讓廣大讀者了解1920年代至1930年代華人領袖與主政香港數年的金文泰在文化、政治上的互動，展示他們合力締造的香港漢文書院、香港大學中文學院如何見證了他們的共同努力的管治成果。此外，本計劃也關注到：隨着時變及金文泰離港，香港大學中文學院迎來新的改革。改革的一方適與曾經協助港大中文學院獲得庚子賠款的胡適互有交往，致使1930年代金文泰本身開創的教育事業有了新的變化，由此也使不受五四新風沖刷的香港迎來了新文化、新文學發展的新一頁。促使香港一度出現新舊文化交鋒的情況，不同形式的民族主義思想激盪，反映了1930年代初期國民政府大一統的政權影響香港的學術文化發展的步伐。

11605017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11605017.value: 本研究以金文泰為切入點展開的研究，本來的規劃是集中於1925年省港大罷工以來，他如何與香港的華人領袖協作穩定社會、解決工潮以及如何塑造香港的社會文化氛圍的問題，並從金文泰主導的香港大學的創辦原因的探討，進而關注庚子賠款如何落戶香港的來龍去脈問題，最後呈現它與新文學領袖胡適的關聯。原本研究的問題識，因而擴大至英國庚子賠款如何歸還中國的會議討論問題；同時也涉及胡適與香港的在地因緣問題。PI在此基礎上撰寫了新的GRF計劃《 爭逐「英庚款」：香港的觀察視角》及HSSPFS計劃《胡適的交遊與思想活動：以英國退還庚款為中心的研究》，並分別於2021年的11月及2022年的2月呈交RGC競逐項目中的新一輪撥款，希望能夠針對由本項計劃洐生的學術問題繼續作出新的知識探索。

11605017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11605017.value: 本計劃透過金文泰在香港任職港督期間的活動與交際網絡，展示1925至1930年期間的香港社會文化發展空間與新舊文化互動的社會氛圍，探究港英殖民地的香港在地管治文化與心態，從中反映香港數年間的變化如何受到來自中國國內政治文化變動的影響面貌。同時，基於本計劃的展開和相關研究成果的逐漸呈現，進一步生展了新知識領域的探究規劃──從金文泰爭取庚子賠款發展香港大學，進而探究英國政府歸還中國庚子賠款的來龍去脈；從香港大學中文學院的改革進而探究胡適與香港的在地奇妙因緣。未來一段時間，PI將在本計劃發現的知識領域上再作深入的研究。

11605917.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11605917.value: 探尋密切合作的政府之道——香港政府中的結構關係的“筒倉”問題

11605917.label: Project Objectives
11605917.value: to identify and compare the structural patterns and characteristics of the silos problem within and across government bureaus; to conduct in-depth analysis of cases of success and failure in the coordination of service delivery of government; to analyse the government's preferred coordination strategies with non-government actors in collaborative governance; and to explore the theoretical implications of the research for the academic discourse on collaborative governance.
rows: to identify and compare the structural patterns and characteristics of the silos problem within and across government bureaus;
to conduct in-depth analysis of cases of success and failure in the coordination of service delivery of government;
to analyse the government's preferred coordination strategies with non-government actors in collaborative governance; and
to explore the theoretical implications of the research for the academic discourse on collaborative governance.

11605917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11605917.value: Joined-up government, defined as a means of attaining more effective horizontally and vertically coordinated policy formulation and implementation, is a prominent public sector reform objective in many countries. Its antithesis, "government by silos", on which the reform effort has largely been concentrated, depicts a situation where hierarchically-organized departments operate in isolation from one another. Government by silos may result in serious bureaucratic dysfunctions such as delays in decision-making, duplication of resources, poor service delivery, failure to resolve cross-cutting "wicked problems" and difficulties in collaboration with non-governmental actors. Under colonial rule, the Hong Kong government was based on silos-type departments which facilitated bureaucratic control, efficiency and technical specialization. However, expanded social policy outputs subsequently required greater horizontal coordination and, in 2000, joined-up government became an explicit reform objective. Progress has nevertheless been slow. Departments have resisted calls for more coordination and silos remain the predominant organizational form. Our research aims to identify the fault lines in efforts to improve coordination, to analyse how and why they have occurred, and to explore the ways to overcome them. We conceptualize the failure to "join up" as a problem embedded in the bureaucratic structure in three domains: inward coordination between government departments; downward coordination between different levels within departments; and outward coordination with non-governmental actors. Within this framework, we develop our central research questions: What causes the silos problem? How is the problem manifested in the government structure? What consequences does it have for service delivery and the functions of government? Does a silos-type structure adversely affect collaborative governance between government and non-governmental organizations? Why is coordination effective in some cases but not in others? How can we deal effectively with the problem of silos? To address these questions, we will collect and analyse Legislative Council, budget, ombudsman and audit documents over the years 2000-2015. The aim is to identify programmes requiring coordination between departments and the problems or successes that have subsequently resulted. In each domain, we will conduct case studies and interview key government officials, Legislative Councillors and other relevant public sector personnel. This research will make two important contributions. Theoretically, it addresses key public administration issues such as organizational coordination, service delivery and collaborative governance. Practically, research on government coordination is long overdue and should help in devising more effective solutions to the enduring problem of silos for Hong Kong and other regions. 政府部門的密切合作，目的在於政策制定和執行中獲得更有效的橫向和縱向協調，是許多國家公共部門改革的一項重要目標。反之，“筒倉”問題，則是公共部門改革試圖改變的現象，指的是各層級政府部門各自為政、孤立運作的狀況。“筒倉”式政府會導致官僚系統嚴重失靈，如決策滯後、資源浪費、低效的公共服務、無法解決跨領域的“棘手問題”和與非政府主體合作中的困難。 在殖民時期，香港政府基于“筒倉”式政府部门來促进對官僚體系的控制、提升效率和技术专业化程度。然而，隨著社会政策產出的增多，對横向协调提出了更高的要求； 在2000年，密切政府部門間的合作成为一項明确的改革目标。但這一改革进展缓慢。政府部門對增強協調的呼籲予以抵制，“筒倉”依然是主要的政府組織形式。 我們的研究旨在找出增進政府間協調過程中遇到的問題，分析問題發生的機制和原因，并試圖尋找解決方式。我們將政府缺乏密切合作歸結為一個深植于官僚結構內部的問題，它需要多方位的協調才能實現，包括：政府部门之间的橫向协调；政府部門內不同層級之间的縱向协调；与非政府主體之間的外向協調。我們進一步假設，阻礙協調的結構性問題也在這三方面反映出來，由此產生我們的核心研究問題：是什么原因造成了“筒倉”问题？這一問題在政府结构中如何表現？它對政府服务的提供和政府管理职能帶來什么后果？“筒倉”式架構是否對政府和非政府组织之间的合作治理產生負面影響？为什么合作在某些情况下有效，而在另一些情況下失效？ 為了解答這些問題，我們將會搜集並分析2000年到2015年間包括立法會、預算部門、申訴專員和審計部門的文件。目的是找出需要部門間合作的項目，以及它們出現的問題或獲得成功的經驗。在每个合作領域，我们都會进行案例研究並採訪重要的政府官員、立法會議員和其他政府部門相關人員。 本研究將作出兩個重要貢獻。 理論上，它探討諸如政府內部協調、公共服務的提供以及合作治理等公共行政中的關鍵問題。在實踐層面，關於政府間協調的研究已是遠遠落後，這項研究將有助於尋求更為有效的解決辦法，以應對香港和其他地區政府的“筒倉”問題。

11606017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11606017.value: 公司治理無疑是公司組織監管的最重要議題之一，自90年代以來相關的學術研究發展迅速，實務上也積極推行公司治理評等。然而，目前的公司治理評等採用的統一標準，原本是針對股權分散的公司所制定的，忽視了大中華地區的大多數上市公司股權和經營大多是由家族或國家集中控制的特點。在學術界，針對這類股權集中企業的公司治理文獻近年來有所增加，大部分研究都是對國家層面的治理規範進行研究，卻忽略了公司實際上可以通過在公司章程中採用不同的規則，來規避國家層級治理規則的約束。為填補此部分研究的不足，並制定適用於評估股權集中企業公司治理的適當標準，本研究計畫提議研究大中華地區上市公司章程中關於公司治理的相關條款，以進一步瞭解各個公司實際採納的公司治理條款及其決定因素。 根據既有關於股權集中公司相關治理理論的研究，我們選擇了18項公司治理條款，為股權集中公司創建了公司治理指標。這些條款的規則可分為投票規則和董事選舉，董事會獨立性和利益衝突交易三大組。我們的樣本包括在上海（SSE），深圳（SZSE），香港（HKEx）和台灣（TWSE）證券交易所主機板上市的所有上市公司（不包括外國和金融公司），共計2,491家公司，其中選取了上海證券交易所1,064家公司，深圳證券交易所457家公司，港交所178家公司，臺灣證券交易所792家公司。我們打算對這些公司2007年，2015年和2018年公司章程進行編碼，得到7,473份公司年度觀察結果。該項目不僅旨在瞭解公司治理的實務運作現狀，更重要的是實證調查大中華地區公司層面治理屬性的決定因素和價值相關性。特別是，我們想看看企業價值與股權集中企業的公司治理指數之間的關係。我們還想知道企業層面治理選擇的決定因素，例如，更依賴外部融資的企業抑或是擁有固定資產較少的企業會採用更多有利於投資者的公司治理條款。鑑於國有資本在中國資本市場的統治地位，我們也計畫檢驗國有企業的治理狀況是否比私有企業的治理狀況更糟。最後，我們計劃檢驗國家層級和公司層級治理規範間的互動，亦即位處投資者保護較弱法域的企業，是否會採取更嚴格的事前治理規則以替代無效率的法律執行。

11606017.label: Realisation of objectives
11606017.value: We have met all the research objectives. We have identified governance rules in China, Hong Kong and Taiwan through the study of Company Law, Securities Regulations and relevant rules published by government authorities in these jurisdictions. Through extensive coding on corporate charters of listed companies in China, Hong Kong and Taiwan, we created a corporate governance database that evaluate the overall governance of listed companies in Greater China. We developed two working hypotheses: one is relevant to how companies respond to different regulatory approach and the other is about corporate governance of SOEs in China. To test the first hypotheses, we developed two different indexes to measure the extent to which companies deviate from default rules (the C index) and how they deviate (the L index). For the second hypothesis, we use US law as a benchmark to measure whether Chinese firms adopt a more investor friendly governance rule. There is a long-standing puzzle in the existing literature on the valuation effect of corporate governance—whether corporate governance improves firm performance and brings positive value to shareholders. Based on the corporate governance rules that we coded, we tested this hypothesis on publicly listed Chinese firms. In light of the domination of state-owned enterprises (SOEs) in Chinese economy, we further compared the corporate governance of SOEs and privately-owned enterprises (POEs) to enlighten the policy debate on whether we need a separate set of corporate governance rules for SOEs.

11606017.label: Major findings and research outcome
11606017.value: Our first paper “An Empirical Study of Default Rules and Menus in China, Hong Kong and Taiwan,” published with the Journal of Empirical Legal Studies, uses data from China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan to empirically test law and economic theories about corporate default rules and menus. We find that in these three jurisdictions, default rules and thresholds in corporate statutes were rarely opted out or opted up, respectively. Menus were often picked up. Our empirical findings thus support the notion that default rules and menus do matter. Overall, companies in China and Hong Kong, at least, are neither systematically more pro-minority nor more pro-controller. Our second paper is a book chapter on the corporate governance of Hong Kong published by the Cambridge University Press. We find that Hong Kong’s stock market differs from the NYSE and LSE, as there has always been a large concentration of ownership which brings a set of different agency problems. The increasing number of Chinese SOEs in the market brings additional agency problems, namely the failure to pursue shareholder value maximization. To add to the complication, 85% of the listed companies are not incorporated in Hong Kong, which means that many provisions in the Companies Ordinance do not apply. Thus, the regulators have to think outside the box to come up with effective measures to improve corporate governance. By and large, they have succeeded in crafting a system that is comparable to the international standards. However, room for further improvement remains in the effective enforcement of those standards. Our third paper “Do State-Owned Enterprises Have Worse Corporate Governance? An Empirical Study of Corporate Practices in China” uses a unique, hand-coded dataset on corporate charter provisions with a random sample of nearly 300 publicly listed Chinese firms to test our second working hypothesis. We demonstrates that political hierarchy, state shareholding level, and political compliance are key factors in the governance and performance of Chinese SOEs. The corporate governance of SOEs that are firmly controlled by the Chinese central government favors minority shareholders, whereas that of SOEs firmly controlled by provincial governments appears to be less protective of them. Overall, SOEs, particularly those controlled by the central government, do not perform worse than POEs, as measured by Tobin’s Q. Nonetheless, more politically compliant firms do perform worse.

11606017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11606017.value: The research results of this project have laid a solid foundation for further research. We suggest that empirical studies considering more aspects of corporate governance using multiple-year panel data and including all publicly listed firms would enable us to better understand Chinese firms, whether SOEs or POEs. Our result also suggests that future research should differentiate different types of SOEs based on political hierarchy and state ownership to better understand the governance issues embedded in different SOEs and to propose sound rules for SOE corporate governance.

11606017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11606017.value: This project fills in the literature gap and develops an appropriate standard for assessing corporate governance of controlled firms, we study firm-level governance choices in the company constitutions of public companies in Greater China. This project not only seeks to understand the current state of corporate governance in practice but, more importantly, also empirically investigates the determinants and value relevance of firm-level governance attributes in Greater China. In particular, we discern the relation between firm value and our corporate governance index for controlled firms. We also investigate the determinants of firm-level governance choices, that is, whether firms that are more dependent on external financing or with fewer fixed assets adopt more pro-investor provisions. In light of the dominance of state capital in Chinese capital market, we test whether state-owned enterprises have worse governance than privately held firms.

11606717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11606717.value: This study aims to articulate the role of social media in growing polarization between pro-establishment (i.e. pro-Beijin) and pro-democracy citizens in Hong Kong. Due to the high-choice nature of social media, it facilitates selective exposure to information that is congruent with users’ partisan identity, resulting in attitudinal and affective polarization. However, most of the previous studies presuppose two mutually exclusive partisan identities (e.g. Democrat vs. Republican in the U.S.) and little is known about the role of more complex multiple identities that coexist within an individual. Focusing on Hong Kong, where Chinese and Hong Kong identities are dynamically constructed in a non-mutually exclusive way, this study advances our understanding of the connection between social media use and mass polarization. The findings generated by this project will not only make a theoretical contribution to better understand the social and political consequences of social media but will also provide deep insight into the reality of digital citizenship in Hong Kong. 此項研究旨在釐清社交媒體在建制派（親北京派）和民主派公眾兩極分化日益擴大的香港社會中的影響。由於社交媒體的選擇多樣性，用戶能夠選擇性地接觸一些與自身的黨派屬性意見一致的信息，因而會導致態度和情感的兩極分化。但是，以往的研究大多假設了兩種互斥的黨派身份（如美國的民主黨和共和黨），極少研究關注到一個個體身上存在更複雜的多重身份認同。而聚焦在香港這個中國和香港身份認同並非互斥而是動態變化著的社會，此項研究可以增加我們對社交媒體使用與公眾兩極分化之間關聯的理解。本項目的研究成果不僅可以在學理上更好地理解社交媒體在社會和政治層面的影響，也將為了解香港的“數位公民”提供深刻洞察。

11606717.label: Realisation of objectives
11606717.value: 1. To articulate the role of social media in growing polarization between pro-establishment and pro-democracy citizens in Hong Kong. This objective was realized by fielding a two-wave panel data from Hong Kong citizens. The first wave was fielded in November and December 2018. The second wave was fielded in February 2019. Among the 1,358 respondents who completed the 1st wave, 635 respondents were successfully re-contacted in the second wave. The analysis of this rich dataset yielded insightful findings on the role of social media in growing polarization between pro-establishment and pro-democracy citizens in Hong Kong. For instance, it was for the first time revealed that WhatsApp use for news has a negative effect on affective polarization between pro-establishment and pro-democracy citizens, whereas Facebook use for news has a positive effect. These two media are often lumped under the general term of social media, but this study demonstrated that they have contrasting effects on affective polarization. 2. To understand the moderating role of multiple identities in the relationship between social media use and attitudinal and affective polarization. This objective was realized by analyzing the moderating role of identities in the relationship between social media use and affective polarization. By analyzing the first wave of the panel survey data, it was strongly indicated that the political use of social media polarizes the attitudes and affects of those who have a single Hong Kongnese identity, while it has depolarizing effects on those with dual identities of Hong Kongese and Chinese. This unique and innovative finding from Hong Kong was highly regarded by academic communities and published in New Media & Society, a top-tier A+ journal in the field of communication research. 3. To conduct a representative, multi-wave longitudinal survey coupled with an Implicit Association Test (IAT) This objective was realized by conducting the above-mentioned panel survey in which an IAT was embedded. The Hong Kong–Mainland IAT was developed through two pilot studies that were fully described in the interim report. The IAT was embedded in the 1st wave of the panel survey.

11606717.label: Major findings and research outcome
11606717.value: First, by using the panel survey data, we demonstrated that Facebook use for political communication has positive associations with polarized attitudes on issues such as the trust in the Hong Kong government and immigration from Mainland China, whereas IM use (i.e., WhatsApp and WeChat) for political communication has consistently negative associations with attitudinal and affective polarization. We also found that these effects are partially mediated by conversation on social media with people who agree or disagree about political or social issues. Social networking services such as Facebook and instant messging app such as WhatsApp are often lumped under the general term of social media, but this study demonstrated that they have contrasting effects on affective polarization. Second, by analyzing the panel survey data, we demonstrated that (1) partisan selectivity in media use is reliably detected among those with single Hong Kongese identity, but not among those with dual identities of Hong Kongese and Chinese, (2) the political use of social media polarizes the attitudes and affects of single identifiers, whereas it has depolarizing effects on dual identifiers, and (3) these contrasting effects on polarization between single and dual identifiers have downstream consequences for political participation. These findings were published in New Media & Society, a top-tier A+ journal in the field of communication research. Third, we conducted two online studies to confirm the validity of the newly developed IAT for assessing the implicit attitudes of local citizens. In each study, we first assessed the participants’ explicit attitudes toward Hong Kong and mainland China, as well as Hong Kong people and mainland Chinese people. We also collected several self-report measurements with the respondents to assess their identity. After responding to these explicit measurements, the respondents were solicited to participate in the IAT, which was designed to measure implicit attitudes. Results indicated that implicit measurements were substantially correlated with explicit measurements of attitudes in both student and adult samples, which indicated the validity of the IAT as a measure of Hong Kong people’s attitudes. More importantly, the implicit measurement developed from the IAT showed a statistically significant effect on self-reported negative stereotypes against mainland Chinese people even after controlling for the effects of explicit measurements. This suggested that the implicit measure could explain the variance of negative stereotypes against mainland Chinese people that cannot be explained by self-reported explicit measures. These findings indicated the effectiveness of the IAT.

11606717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11606717.value: First, the findings on multiple identities’ roles need to be tested in other contexts to examine its generalizability. For instance, multiple identities are prominent in contexts such as Taiwan and Northern Ireland. Successful replications in these contexts would indicate the generalizability of the findings beyond Hong Kong. Second, most of the measurements in this project relied on self-report by the respondents. However, the self-report measurement of media use has proven unreliable due to measurement errors. Therefore, behavioral measurement of media use that is digitally tracked is necessary for further development. For example, tracking individual uses of different media through smartphones is becoming feasible these years. Third, the Hong Kong-Mainland IAT developed in this project can be applied to many other research contexts. For example, the economic and social integration with the mainland can potentially change the Hong Kong citizens’ view of the Hong Kong-Mainland relationship. As self-reoprt measures may not reflect these changes, indirect measurements such as IAT would be enormously useful. In this connection, future collaboration with social psychologists would enhance the value of the newly developed IAT.

11606717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11606717.value: Polls show that affective polarization between the pro-democracy and pro-establishment people in Hong Kong today has reached a serious level. Affective polarization is a state of increased hostility between groups due to the growing difference in feelings towards the group you belong to and the group you do not belong to. This study studied the role of social media in the process of affective polarization. Social media is designed to encourage people to see what they want to see in a selective way, which can be one source of affective polarization. Analysis of online survey data collected from Hong Kong residents revealed that relatively open social networking services such as Facebook are positively associated with affective polarization, whereas the use of instant messaging apps such as WhatsApp and WeChat is negatively associated with affective polarization. Although these media are often lumped together as social media, it was revealed that they have a contrasting effect on affective polarization. We also found that affective polarization increases when people with a single Hong Kong identity use social media for political communication, whereas when dual identifiers with both Hong Kong and Chinese identities use social media for political communication, affective polarization is rather reduced.

11608717.label: Project Objectives
11608717.value: To survey media trials in China from 2000 to 2016 and to set up an archive. To classify the patterns of media trials and typology of social justice. What are the key features of different types of media trials or at different levels of trials? Who are the alleged criminals in each type? Who are the legal and media professionals (and news organizations) involved? How did the media report the cases? To investigate the construction process of social justice and its structural contingency. How do the media and the courts interactively construct justice in media trials? What claims of justice does each actor make? What are the media frames and the legal reasoning of these cases? Do the media frames and legal reasoning vary according to the type of media trial? Why? Under what conditions would media logic be consistent with, or compete against, legal logic in defining social justice? To empirically examine the effect of media trials on legal decisions, on which existing research presents ambiguous views. What factors in a case affect the legal decision? Do aspects of the news coverage influence the legal decision? To discuss the impacts of the evolving media–court relation on Chinese society. How does the media–court relation shape the process of constructing social justice? What are the implications of this relation on institutional resilience and regime stability?

11608717.value: 过去二十年，中国经历了从严格控制法庭报道，到媒体审判事件不断涌现的转变。的激增媒体报道和网络评论，如同“尚方宝剑”，促使了很多司法案件的重审，甚至改判，令嫌疑人免于起诉 (Cheung, 2014; Liebman, 2005)。越来越多的司案件受到高度曝光，这不可避免地带来一种困境：由法院定义的“法律正义”和被公众塑造的“舆论正义”常常发生冲突。媒体审判事件因此成为多种社会正义理念博弈的场域。 现有研究关注媒体审判事件时常从新闻自由和司法公正的关系入手，对媒体报道产生的影响得出了相反的观点。一些研究认为媒体对司法审判的报道有可能干扰正当司法程序，进而干预司法公正和审判独立（Chen & Zhang, 2011；纪莉，刘晶晶，2012; Kando, 1990; Phillipson, 2008; 魏永征，2002, 2007；Wright & Ross, 1997; 徐迅，2004）。而另一些研究者则对媒体的影响较为乐观。他们认为中国的司法体系并不独立，因此媒体报道反而起到了监督作用，避免司法被其他权力左右，督促司法体系公开透明，从而进一步促进了司法公正（贺卫方，1998；胡菡菡，2009；史忠治，王中伟，2008；周泽，2004）。 对于媒体报道如何影响司法公正的问题，理论上存在争论，实证研究得出的结论也不一致。然而，单独强调“新闻自由”或“司法公正”，都不足以充分概括中国在转型期流动的、建构的社会正义。社会正义指个体“获得与他/她的特点和情况相匹配的好处和负担”（Cohen,1986, p.11）。在现代社会，法院是维护司法公正的正式机构，它根据法律将惩罚分配给相匹配的罪行 (Hamilton & Rytina, 1980; Kraska, 2006; Lacey, 2007; Surette, 2014)。然而作为舆论的代表，媒体则受到意识形态 (Gitlin, 1980; Hallin & Mancini, 2004)、组织惯例 (Breed, 1955; Gans, 1979)、商业利益( Entman, 1989; McChesney, 2004) 和受众需求(Chan, 2010; He & Chen, 1998; Stockmann, 2013) 的制约。舆论正义有可能在一种情况下与司法正义一致，而在另一种情况下和司法正义产生矛盾(Greer & McLaughlin, 2011; Surette, 2014)。公众更关注实质性正义，即财富和权力在社会如何分配 (Cohen, 1986)，而法律专业人士则更强调程序正义，即法律程序的正当性和公平性 (Rawls, 1971)。因此，本研究摒弃单一、静止的社会正义概念，转而从结构性建构的视角入手，考察转型期社会媒体和法院如何共同建构多种形态的社会正义。我们利用媒体审判事件实证地讨论以上的对立观点，试图回答下列问题：在建构社会正义的过程中，什么情况下媒体逻辑会和法律逻辑冲突，什么情况下媒体逻辑又会促进法律逻辑？当一个司法审判被高度曝光时，媒体和法院的决策如何产生？媒体在何种程度上、通过什么方式影响司法决策？ 为了回答这些问题，我们对2000年至2016年的50个媒体审判事件展开了案例研究。我们首先通过法院的判决文书分析法律逻辑。如今，越来越多的中国法院将裁判文书开放给公众。这些裁判文书形成相对系统的数据库，不仅展示了法院判决背后的逻辑，而且让我们能够较为客观地观察到社会和政治力量对法庭产生的作用。另一方面，我们通过媒体对案件的报道来考察媒体逻辑。我们对相关的记者和法律专家进行访谈，了解他们如何认知正义，以及这种正义认知如何影响他们的专业行为。本研究不仅揭示了转型期社会中社会正义的性质，而且试图阐明媒体和法院之间的复杂关系，以及这种关系对中国社会的影响。

11608717.label: Major findings and research outcome
11608717.value: 1) With the increasing media coverage on legal trials, China is facing the tension between the “legal justice” defined by the courts and the “populist justice” perceived by the public. We propose “trial-based media event” as a theoretical genre to study how media events become a battleground where notions of justice have to struggle between journalistic freedom and judicial independence. (Yang and Lin, 2021) 2) By comparing the legal logic of these cases with the media logic that was embedded in news coverage of these trials, we propose an analytic typology -- tabloid, sympathetic, controversial and cooperative justice construction – to investigate the fluid and evolving nature of social justice in this transitional society (Lin and Yang, 2019; Yang and Lin, 2021). 3) This study analyzes 50 most influential trial-based media events between 2000 and 2016 in China. We find that entrepreneurs, government officials and students were dominant defendants in such events, and 26% of cases’ judicial decisions were adjusted after the extensive media coverage. More importantly, social status of defendants and whether legal discourse serving as the dominant media discourse have significant impacts on the courts’ verdicts (Lin and Yang, 2019). 4) The study further explores the three steps of social construction of justice during a media event: externalization, objectivation, and internalization through Tang Hui case. The study illustrates how media draw on legal discourse to question legal institutions, thus initiating a conflict-driven media event before the judicial trial. After the main social injustice behind the trial was redressed, the state media and the courts also exploit legal discourse to restore the legitimacy of legal authority, which reconstructed the trial back to a consensual media event, which had caused fragmented opinions of justice among news workers. (Yang and Lin, 2021) 5) We argue the temporal and regional variations of these types of justice construction echo with the political and social transition this authoritarian regime has been through (Lin and Yang, 2019; Yang and Lin, 2021) 6) We then apply such structural perspective to extend our discussion into journalists’ perceived professional norms and social status (Han and LIN, forthcoming; LIN and Han, 2020/under review); as well as the evolution of public opinion infrastructures in China in the past four decades (Lin et. al., 2019).

11608717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11608717.value: 1) To extend discourse analysis to more cases. For discourse analysis, we so far only focus on Tang Hui case which represented a pattern of justice construction shifting from controversial to cooperative justice construction. We aim to extend detail analysis on social justice construction to other types of justice construction. Such development will allow us to compare the justice construction processes in different contexts. 2) To scrutinise how journalists perceive what is just and fair. We aim to investigate how Chinese journalists perceive “justice” and how such perception shapes their news judgements and practices. 3) To apply the justice construction process into different contexts. We are considering to explore the phenomena of “vaccine justice” – to what extent do citizens perceive the distribution of vaccine is just and fair during COVID-19?

11608717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11608717.value: With the increasing media coverage on legal trials, China is facing the tension between the “legal justice” defined by the courts and the “populist justice” perceived by the public. Trial-based media events have become a battleground where notions of justice have to struggle between journalistic freedom and judicial independence. This project analyzes 50 most influential trial-based media events between 2000 and 2016 in China. The data shows that entrepreneurs, government officials and students were dominant defendants in such events, and in 26% of cases’ judicial decisions were adjusted after the extensive media coverage. In addition, social status of defendants and whether legal discourse serving as the dominant media discourse have significant impacts on the courts’ verdicts. We then further explore how media and court interactively construct social justice during a media event and how journalists internalize such justice construction into their working routines. We also propose an analytic typology -- tabloid, sympathetic, controversial and cooperative justice construction – to understand the fluid and evolving nature of social justice in China. We further argue the temporal and regional variations of these types of justice construction echo with the political and social transition that this authoritarian regime has been through.

11608917.label: Realisation of objectives
11608917.value: This GRF project aimed to examine the origins, the nature and implications of this new case of illiberal (although as of now not yet fully electoral authoritarian) rule in the Philippines, thereby contributing not just to the literature on Philippine politics but also to the broader comparative political literature on the problems of democracy in an age of illiberal populism. The research for this project had to be rethought due to outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic which made fieldwork planned for 2020 and early 2021 impossible. (In addition, as head of a department and director of a research centre, the PI found it difficult to leave Hong Kong during much of 2019 because of uncertainties caused by the Hong Kong protests.) This limited the PI's ability to explore the precise nature of this new form of political illiberalism in the depth and detail originally planned through interviews and the gathering of unpublished materials. Some fieldwork was done before and several interviews/discussions were held online during the pandemic but the project inevitably became more dependent on secondary sources and publicly available (largely online) material. The PI also benefited from feedback at several workshops and talks: University of California, Berkeley, Center for Southeast Asia Studies, April 4, 2017; Foreign Correspondents’ Club Hong Kong, November 7, 2017; "Populism in Asia" workshop, Monash University Malaysia, November 15-16 2017; Association of Asian Studies Annual Conference, Washington, D.C, March 22-25, 2018; Humboldt University, June 14, 2018; talk at De la Salle University, September 27, 2018; presentation at Philippine Studies Conference, Hiroshima University, Japan, November 17-18, 2018; European Southeast Asia Studies Association (EUROSEAS) conference, Humboldt University, Berlin, Germany, September 10-13, 2019; Association of Asian Studies (virtual) conference, March 22, 2021. This led the PI to put more emphasis on the diachronic (historical) dimension in exploring the origins of Duterte's rise as well as the synchronic (comparative) dimension in understanding the larger implications of his rule. The PI was still able to publish 15 research outputs, including five in top journals - Foreign Affairs, the Journal of Democracy, the Journal of Contemporary Asia, Democratization, and Contemporary Politics (outputs 1, 2, 7, 8, 9), one in the major Philippine political science outlet (output 6), three books chapters (outputs 4, 10, and 11), and six articles in online academic blogs and academic magazines intended for a general audience such as The Diplomat, Global Asia, and East Asia Forum. These publications covered the Duterte administration through early 2021, including analysis of its reaction to the pandemic (output 12). In terms of explanations, the PI argued that the two dominant explanations for the rise of Duterte - his populist leadership style and a general crisis of oligarchic democracy – both have key limitations (output 6). The agential populist leadership perspective explains “too little” about the underlying causes of Duterte’s victory and the nature of his presidential rule while the structural oligarchic democracy perspective explains “too much” in that Duterte was able to win the presidency with his illiberal platform despite apparent political stability and rapid economic growth during the Aquino presidency. An alternative "structurational" (Giddens) explanation was proposed that focused on Duterte's leadership but also which also takes into account how structural factors constrained and enabled it, in particular the weaknesses of the dominant post-Marcos political order which is a distinct sub-set of oligarchic democracy. The PI has termed this alternative explanation "violent populism" which goes beyond the notion of "penal populism" common in the West as Duterte’s is a particularly virulent form of illiberal rule that takes the aggressive intent of the “us versus them” polarity to its deadly extreme In the most recent journal output (8), it is argued that among contemporary illiberal populist leaders, only the Philippine president has instigated mass murder under the guise of a “war on drugs.” His violent populist strategy largely explains why he won the presidency despite limited concerns about crime, why he organized extra-judicial killings and why these continued despite domestic and international criticism. As president, Duterte nationalized the violent populism he had first developed locally which wooed rather than intimidated voters with promises to protect “good people” against drug-induced evil. These "securitized" appeals resonated given the failures of liberal reformism and with a proletarian populist alternative undermined. Using nationalism to respond to global criticism, he put opponents on the defensive. Breaking with the left, he has not undertaken major socio-economic reforms and his anti-oligarchy rhetoric benefitted his cronies. Despite killing tens of thousands and revelations of police corruption, as a legitimation strategy Duterte’s drug war has successfully diverted attention from the “death of development” with poverty levels high despite rapid growth. The Philippine case shows how the extreme dichotomisation of “good people” and criminalizsed “others” can legitimate mass killings with a populist breakthrough in a weak state with a poor record of human development. Much progress was also been made on completing a co-authored book manuscript with the co-I (Prof. Julio C. Teehankee, De la Salle University) about the Philippine presidency which aims to offer a broader understanding of the Duterte presidency through a historical institutionalist perspective with a unique theoretical model. The book employs a “relational” approach to presidential leadership in Asia's oldest democracy. This explanation applies a modified version of Skowronek’s influential theory of the U.S. presidency which takes into account both agential and structural factors (as discussed in output 6) but also makes it relevant to a developing country democracy such as in the Philippines. The author summarised the book's main argument in a 2018 book chapter (output 11) which was published in the Routledge Handbook of the Contemporary Philippines which the PI co-edited. Another output (2) placed the Philippine presidency in a broader Southeast Asian perspective. Work on a sole-authored manuscript centred on the PI's notion of Duterte's "violent populism" in which Stanford University press has shown interest was slowed by the lack of opportunity to do further fieldwork. This led the PI to reframe the book project, focusing instead on the historical precedents of Duterte's violent populism: the Philippines' "death of development", its history of political violence and sub-national authoritarianism, the "disjunction" of liberal reformism, the preemption of a "proletarian" populist alternative to illiberalism, and the impact of extreme patronage of Philippine politics and weak parties on attempts at institution building. In addition, the PI became more ambitious comparatively, going beyond the Thai comparison (analyzed in outputs 3, 10, and 13) to study a larger Southeast Asian perspective as well Trump's US and Putin's Russia (outputs 2, 7, 8, and 9, and the enclosed 2021 AAS conference paper). Employing a "structurationist" perspective discussed above, the book manuscript will attempt to address literatures on populism (Duterte's uniquely "violent" populism among contemporary populist leaders), autocratization (and how Duterte's claim of democratic legitimacy despite his administration's illiberalism has been more effective than the military-monarchical rulers of Thailand who have faced stronger opposition), and development (particularly the implications of a "successful" growth-focused strategy that because of massive inequality has not led to significant poverty reduction even after several decades). It is hoped this broader theoretical and comparative focus will still attract the interest of a major publisher when the manuscript is completed toward the end of the Duterte presidency in late 2021/or early 2022.

11608917.label: Major findings and research outcome
11608917.value: The major research findings of this project are listed below. The research outcome was 15 publications, including five in top academic journals, as well as two book manuscripts in progress. -Among contemporary illiberal populist leaders signaling aggressive intent by excluding, imprisoning or even assassinating those othered by their rhetoric, Philippine president Rodrigo Duterte has taken populist illiberalism to its most violent extreme by instigating state mass murder through his “war on drugs” which has killed tens of thousands. Killings were legitimated by a dichomotisation of “good people” and criminalised “others”. Duterte used the drug war as a political strategy to strengthen his political legitimacy and undermine liberal constraints while wrong footing domestic opposition, parrying international criticism, and deflecting from high levels of poverty that persisted despite rapid growth. Breaking with the left, he employed state violence rather than undertaking systematic social reform and attacked the oligarchy to benefit his cronies. -In the Philippines, the "disjunction" of liberal reformism, the pre-emption of a "proletarian" populist alternative, a long tradition of local warlordism, and the weakness of institutions in a patronage-dominated state provided a political opportunity of which Duterte has taken full advantage. -Violent populism has diverted attention form the Philippines' "death of development" with continued high levels of poverty despite rapid growth for a decade and a half until the recent pandemic. -Duterte has faced limited opposition both electorally and in terms of sustained protests. While the Philippine president acts illiberally, he has been able to plausibly claim continued democratic legitimacy based on competitive elections and high opinion ratings while ruling largely constitutionally. Furthermore, oppositionists to Duterte have had a difficult time building a broad coalition against his rule (as proved possible in Donald Trump’s US, for example) because the Philippine president’s support is not limited by social divisions (e.g., class/education, urban/rural, region, religion). In this sense Duterte's rule is more similar Russia’s Putin, another illiberal leader whose broad popularity at its height cut across class, regional and other social cleavage lines. But unlike in Russia, the opposition to Duterte has thus far been unable to reframe its opposition from its human rights orientation to an anti-corruption emphasis.

11608917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11608917.value: The PI hopes to develop a comparison employed in this project through a further GRF grant application which has been made to explore more systematically and in depth opposition in the Philippines compared to Thailand. The aim is to situate these two cases in the autocratization literature which has recently begun to focus more on resistance to this threat. This would be an attempt to explain why there been more pushback in elections and through protests against Thailand’s military-monarchical regime than by those opposing an aggrandizing president in the Philippines. An institutional explanation which accounts for pushback based on the degree of residual electoral, state institutional, and civil societal forms of democratic accountability despite autocratization does not explain the variation between these two countries because there has been more opposition in Thailand despite greater generalized repression and institutional manipulation there than in the Philippines. An alternative explanation is sought which explores how pushback is shaped by "framing battles" over regimes’ democratic legitimacy claims despite autocratizing. The proposed study would employ a mixture of qualitative and quantitative methods to study similarities and differences between these cases in terms of autocratization, election results, protest events, social media activism, and framing.

11608917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11608917.value: Among contemporary illiberal populist leaders globally, only Philippine president Rodrigo Duterte has instigated mass murder under the guise of a “war on drugs.” As president, Duterte nationalised the violent populism he had developed locally which wooed rather than intimidated voters with promises to protect “good people” against drug-induced evil. This resonated given the failures of liberal reformism and with a proletarian populist alternative undermined. He invoked nationalism to respond to international criticism, broke with the left, and has not undertaken major socio-economic reforms while employing anti-oligarchy rhetoric which benefitted cronies. Duterte’s drug war successfully diverted attention from the “death of development” in the Philippines with poverty levels still high despite rapid growth. Duterte has faced limited opposition because while acting illiberally, he plausibly claims continued democratic legitimacy based on competitive elections, high opinion ratings, and largely constitutional rule. Oppositionists have had a difficult time building a broad coalition against him because the Philippine president’s support is not sharply delimited by social divisions (e.g., class, urban/rural, and region). The Philippine case shows how an extreme dichotomisation of “good people” and criminalised “others” can legitimate mass killings with a populist breakthrough in a weak state with a poor record of human development.

11609417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11609417.value: Challenges to sovereignty in the form of unresolved territorial disputes and competing claims remain primary causes of tension between states. In the absence of timely and effective negotiations, territorial disputes can lead to distrust, retaliation and, ultimately, disastrous conflicts and wars. China and India are two determined Asian powers and they are rising simultaneously. They will help to shape the new world order. Against this backdrop, this project aims to critically evaluate the Sino-Indian Boundary Dispute (SIBD) in the Western, Middle and Eastern sectors from a multidisciplinary perspective and develop a peaceful and pragmatic resolution in the form of a blueprint for a bilateral boundary treaty between these states. This project adopts an analytical model, holding that an effective demarcation of territory calls for an interdisciplinary approach that takes into consideration both legal (e.g. international law, treaties, uti possidetis and effective control) as well as non-legal (including power, politics, history, economy and geography) attributes and preferences of the disputing states. This research keeps in view China and India’s international law practice, previous state initiatives, conflicting national interests and international foreign relations, and seeks to set out a comprehensive inventory of these preferences to determine the extent of cooperation between China and India to resolve the SIBD. The ultimate goal of this project is to seek out a creative yet pragmatic framework for the peaceful settlement of the SIBD that can become the basis for negotiating a bilateral boundary treaty between China and India. This study would also measure the comparative significance of each identified state preference and assess its impact on a future bilateral boundary agreement. A peaceful settlement based on bilateral negotiations represents the only means to resolve the pending SIBD. This is mainly because (1) both China and India believe in the five principles of peaceful co-existence; (2) China prefers settlement procedures that are non-judicial (such as negotiation and mediation) or semi-judicial (such as certain forms of arbitration and conciliation) with less third party intervention; and (3) as far as adjudicatory methods for dispute resolution are concerned, China has not accepted the International Court of Justice (ICJ)’s jurisdiction and India has entered a reservation on territorial disputes. Therefore, there is a need for a pragmatic and peaceful framework for the settlement of the SIBD based on negotiation, cooperation, mutual trust, and mutual respect. 時至今日，國家主權爭議，表現於懸而不決的領土紛爭與要求，仍是國際關係緊張的主因。如果缺少及時、有效的交涉，領土紛爭可以破壞互信，導致報復，最終釀成災難性的糾紛與戰爭。 中國、印度均為關鍵的亞洲國家，在同一時期崛興，有助於國際秩序之構建。本計劃則從另一方面入手，旨在採納跨學科研究方法，有批判性地檢討中印邊境糾紛，包括西段、中段、東段國界，從而提出和平與務實的方案，作為兩國簽訂邊界條約的藍本。本計劃主張，有效的領土劃界必須採取跨學科方法，兼顧法理（例如國際法、條約、保持佔有原則、實際控制）及法理以外（包括權力、政治、歷史、經濟、地理）之因素，以及涉事國家之傾向。本項研究會在此基礎之上分析問題，並着眼於中印實踐國際法的慣例、兩國既有的計畫、互相抵觸的利益，以及國際關係，將這些要素考慮在內，藉此判斷中印兩國的合作空間。 本計劃的最終目標，是探索有創見而又實際的框架，幫助和平解決中印邊境糾紛，作為兩國商議雙邊疆界條約的基礎。同時，本項研究亦會衡量兩國各種取向的重要性，評估其對未來尋求雙邊疆界協議之影響。 和平協議建基於雙邊交涉，是解決中印邊境糾紛的唯一方法，原因如下：首先，中印兩國均秉持和平共處五項原則；其次，中國傾向於利用非司法性（例如交涉、調停）或半司法性（例如一定形式的裁判、調解）的手法，不願接受第三方介入；最後，儘管糾紛可藉仲裁解決，中國並未接受國際法庭的裁決，而印度亦對邊境糾紛有所保留。因此，建基於談判、合作、互信、互相尊重的形式，務實、和平的框架，將有助於解決中印邊境糾紛。

11609417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11609417.value: At the moment the PI and Co-I are in the process of completing the mongraph on 'The China-India Border Dispute' (Routledge, 2023). In tthe concluding chapter of this monograph we are trying to explore future developments of this research and considering new approaches to settle the SIBD such as considering that borders are not immune to sociocultural discourses or quotidian politics - in fact, as centrepieces in the framing of nationalist stakes, borders are matters of immense public consequence. Historically, studies on the Sino-Indian border have been dominated by politico-security paradigms and logics of security dilemmas, privileging state-centric ideas of sovereignty, competition, conflict, and loss. These perceptions tend to frame the issue as a zero-sum matter, and conflict becomes the norm instead of the violent exception, almost normalised. Such inflexibility frames the border as a dead-end rather than a pathway, as is evident in the colonial legacies of border-mapping exercises themselves. So we are trying to understand the SIBD from the ethnographic len for the peaceful arbitration.

11610717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11610717.value: This project examines the regulatory framework for employment relations within four Asian countries to explain what factors help to promote (or inhibit) the development of labour standards established by the United Nations (UN), including the International Labour Organisation (ILO). In particular, the research explains how global North and international legal and voluntary attempts to regulate production in the Global South impact the actual regulatory regime in four Asian countries with differing levels of internal control. The initial hypothesis is that countries which have strong internal control will be more able to enforce a legal framework for employment relations but less amenable to voluntary codes. Conversely, countries which have weaker, more pluralistic regimes, will have more complex and chaotic application of standards, but also more agility in adapting to new standards and practices. In practice, it is expected the patterns may be more complex. Global commodity production and distribution networks operate within tremendously complex regulatory environments. This complexity affects both the firms operating within supply chains and the governments in whose countries labour is employed to work within these chains. The United Nations’ agreement called Global Compact further emphasised a responsibility on Multinational Corporations (MNCs) to obey local regulations whilst also committing themselves to promote voluntary codes of best practice. This regularly environment is hugely complex, with numerous regulatory initiators’, differing content, efficacy, forms of monitoring and enforcement. Add to this, incentives to attract foreign investment, such as free trade zones where some laws are suspended, developing legislative, judicial and monitoring systems, and developing countries of the Global South struggle to organise a coherent regulatory regime. Moreover, they complain that outsiders, be they foreign courts, government administrations, UN bodies, MNCs, non-government organisations (NGOs), or foreign and international labour unions, blame them when things go wrong. This research addresses this complexity, mapping the various forms of regulations, monitoring and enforcement at the level of individual counties that have traditionally made up the Global South. The four countries in this research, Bangladesh, Cambodia, China and Vietnam, represent comparisons of these complexities at several levels, including political system (elected or authoritarian governments), degree of reliance on international capital and/ or industrial sector and depth of relations with relevant UN organisations. The research involves documentary analysis from those produced by all forms of organisations relevant to the employment practices in the cases, together with interviews and review of legal judgements. 11611517.label: Realisation of objectives
11611517.value: The project has been successfully implemented, and all its objectives have been achieved. Open recruitment of schools was conducted in 2018. A written invitation to an introductory seminar was released to all primary schools in Hong Kong. The seminar was held at the City University of Hong Kong to introduce the details of the project, including the project’s theoretical background, objectives, and requirements. After the seminar, 70 schools were interested. We selected 15 for participation, considering their number of students and commitment to the project and balancing their geographical locations. All grade 1 to 4 students in the participating schools were invited to complete a screening. Parents’ consent and students’ assent were obtained. To avoid stigmatization, we promoted the project as one of the extracurricular activities. Four thousand and eighty-six children (2292 males and 1794 females) of Grades 1 to 4, aged from 6 to 10, from the 15 primary schools completed the screening questionnaire. Based on the inclusion criteria, 371 high-risk students (280 males and 91 females) were selected to participate in the experiment. They were then randomly assigned to one of the three conditions, namely (i) storytelling intervention, (ii) placebo, and (iii) no-treatment control. The school personnel, participants, and parents were blinded for the random assignment. For conditions (i) and (ii), participants from the same school in the same condition were assigned into groups of 8 to 10 students each. The groups were delivered by registered social workers and administered according to the session plans and materials prepared by the PI and the Co-I. Participants in the no-treatment control were phrased as being on the waiting list. They would participate in the storytelling group next semester if they completed the required assessments. Storytelling intervention and the placebo consisted of ten one-hour weekly sessions. All participants were assessed at baseline, post-test, and six months after treatment (follow-up) quantitatively by self-report and parent-report questionnaires. Two participants and their parents in each condition in each school were randomly selected to undergo individual qualitative interviews (baseline, post-test, and follow-up). The storytelling intervention was developed using the social information processing (SIP) model. The first phase addressed cognitively distorted SIP in reactive aggressors, especially selective cue identification and hostile attributional biases. The second phase targeted cognitive distortions and traits associated with proactive aggression, such as narcissistic and callous-unemotional traits and the tendency to underestimate the negative consequences of aggression. During the third phase, the participants were provided empathy and social competence training. Throughout the intervention, activities such as role-play, group discussion, and reflective feedback cantered on the stories, encouraging the participants to reflect on the stories told and thus on their own cognitive, emotional, and social experiences. For the placebo groups, stories of famous scientists and scientific discoveries were used instead of stories related to characteristics of reactive aggression and proactive aggression. The quantitative and qualitative results were used to evaluate the effectiveness of the storytelling intervention in reducing reactive aggression and proactive aggression in schoolchildren aged 6 to 10. The storytelling intervention could reduce participants’ reactive and proactive aggression after treatment, sustained at the follow-up (Objectives 1 and 2). The storytelling intervention also enhanced participants’ social communication skills, promoted forgiveness, and reduced impulsivity (Objective 3). However, we found improvements in social competence and anger control were observed in participants with reactive but not proactive aggression (Objective 4). To conclude, the project has successfully evaluated whether the storytelling intervention reduces reactive and proactive aggression in schoolchildren, and the results provided scientific evidence to support its effectiveness. The project objectives have been achieved.

11611517.label: Major findings and research outcome
11611517.value: Our findings support the effectiveness of the storytelling intervention in schoolchildren. Results from the linear mixed models indicated significant differences in general, reactive, and proactive aggression among experimental conditions (storytelling, placebo, and control). After controlling for the baseline scores, age, and sex, the storytelling condition had significantly lower general aggression, reactive aggression, and proactive aggression than the control; the storytelling condition also had significantly lower general aggression and proactive aggression than the placebo. The storytelling intervention effectively reduced reactive and proactive aggression in the participants. Qualitative results were consistent with the quantitative findings. Content analysis was used to analyze the interview data. We found that the storytelling intervention reduced reactive aggression in participants by enhancing their anger control, social communication skills, and forgiveness. Nevertheless, proactive aggressors’ empathy did not substantially increase after the storytelling intervention. The project team is dedicated to increasing public awareness about the innovative approach to child aggression. On 18th Dec 2020, Dr. Annis Fung (PI) and Ms. May Wong (Co-I) held a press conference promoting the utility of storytelling as a school-based aggression intervention. The press conference released the results and case studies to support the innovative approach to treating aggressive students, reported by Apple Daily, Sing Tao Daily, and HK01. Later, Ming Pao and Sing Tao Daily also made a particular topic about storytelling in January 2021 and February 2021, respectively. The PI and the Co-I also had a radio interview by 881903 about the storytelling intervention on 26th Dec 2020. In May 2021 and May 2022, a total of 158 teachers and school social workers from different primary schools attended an online training workshop. They have learned the rationale behind the program and how to run the storytelling group. They are expected to implement the storytelling program to sustainably help the aggressive students at their school. The findings generated from the project have also been presented at four international conferences (Berlin in Aug 2019, Osaka in Mar 2020, & Amsterdam in Apr 2020). Moreover, 4 articles have been published and 2 articles have been under review in high-tier international peer-reviewed journals. In addition, the project has been granted the Excellence in Knowledge Transfer Award 2021-2022 by the College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences (CLASS), City University of Hong Kong.

11611517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11611517.value: With the experiences and scientific evidence from the project, we will continue implementing the storytelling program at different primary schools, and providing training about storytelling intervention for school social workers and teachers, so that the impacts will be sustainable. We will study the effectiveness of storytelling intervention by parents at home. The storytelling program could potentially be generalized in the family system since it is one of the parent-child activities, and the stories used in the project can be assessed in the public library. We will conduct training workshops, improving their parenting efficacy and introducing storytelling as one of the parent-child activities, and measure the outcomes in children. Moreover, we will develop an online resource platform where parents can access a list of pertinent parenting resource kits and storybook recommendations. Parents can download the resources online and use them for free at home. Furthermore, we plan to extend the storytelling program to kindergartens. For a therapeutic approach to be practical for young children as young as 3 to 5, the program must be consistent with the child’s developmental stage. Storytelling is natural to children as they are drawn to pretend and fantasy play.

11611517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11611517.value: The project has examined the effectiveness of the storytelling intervention in reducing aggressive behaviors among young children aged 6 to 10, a population with limited intervention options because of their early developmental stage. We have conducted a large-scale, blinded, randomized controlled trial in which 4086 primary school students in Hong Kong underwent the screening. Three hundred and seventy-one high-risk children with aggressive behaviors were identified and randomly assigned into one of the three experimental conditions: storytelling intervention, placebo, and no-treatment control. The participants were then assessed at several time points (baseline, after treatment, and six months after treatment). Findings suggested that the storytelling intervention effectively reduced reactive and proactive aggressive behaviors in primary schoolchildren. The project has various practical implications for the individual, family, school, and social systems. Storytelling is a non-labeling, economical, and effective early intervention option for aggressive children. In the long run, substantial financial and social costs would be saved from the devastating outcomes of aggression and violent crimes in adults. With the experiences and scientific evidence from the project, we will continue implementing the storytelling program at different primary schools. We will also extend the impacts to the family system and young children in the kindergartens.

11612217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11612217.value: Consistent with the old saying “birds of a feather flock together”, research has found that romantic couples tend to have similar socio-economic status, personality traits, religious beliefs, political orientations, etc. While evidence has shown that couple similarity can result from the process of selection (i.e., people select partners similar to themselves), less is known about the process of convergence (i.e., couples become more similar over time). In particular, couple similarity in values has received little attention. As recent literature has indicated that values are predictive of behaviors and changeable over time, it is of both theoretical and practical importance to examine whether and how couple similarity in values may result from the processes of selection and convergence and, in turn, contribute to the development of romantic relationships. In a laboratory setting (Study I), experiments will be conducted to examine whether and how the degree of similarity in human values may affect perceived attractiveness between people. We will manipulate the similarity of human values (openness to change, conservation, self-enhancement, and self-transcendence) of bogus persons, according to two conditions (i.e., similar vs. dissimilar to the experimental subject) and test whether higher similarity in human values is associated with greater attraction. In a natural life setting (Study II), a longitudinal study will be carried out to examine how similarity in human values and relationship quality change over time and affect each other among early dating couples. Latent change modeling will be used to: a) test the growth trajectories of value similarity and relationship quality and, more importantly, b) disentangle the causal direction of the association between them (i.e., whether value similarity predicts later relationship quality or the reverse). Together, the two studies will enable greater theoretical understanding about the role of values in contributing to romantic relationships, both to the onset of the relationships and to their maintenance, as well as contributing to applications regarding romantic relationships. 俗語說，物以類聚。研究發現，浪漫關係中的配偶在社會經濟地位，性格，宗教信仰，政治取向等都比較相似。配偶的相似性可來源於一開始的互相選擇，或者交往過程中的逐漸趨同。相對而言，目前對後者對研究較為缺乏，尤其是關於價值觀的相似性。近年研究表明，價值觀對行為有預測性，而且會隨時間發展變化。瞭解浪漫配偶價值觀的相似性如何形成，以及影響浪漫關係的發展，有重要的理論和現實意義。 研究一在實驗環境中探索價值觀的相似性如何影響人們感知他人的吸引力。在不同實驗條件下（相似組和相異組），向受試者呈現關於假想個體的價值觀描述，以瞭解當價值觀相似或相異時，人們是否會認為該個體較吸引或者較不吸引。 研究二在自然生活環境中對浪漫關係初期的配偶進行縱向追蹤，以瞭解價值觀相似性和關係品質如何隨時間產生變化以及互相影響。研究使用潛變化模型來分析價值觀相似性和關係品質的增長曲線，以及二者之間的因果關係。 結合以上兩項研究，我們可以更深入瞭解價值觀對於人們發展和維持親密關係的理論作用以及現實生活中的應用。
