12100717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12100717.value: SIRTUIN proteins are largely NAD+-dependent protein deacetylases that couple lysine deacetylation with NAD+ hydrolysis to yield O-acetyl-ADP-ribose (OAADPR), nicotinamide, and deacetylated lysine. SIRTUINs, initially identified in yeast in the regulation of gene silencing, have now been identified in all kingdoms. SIRTUINs have been implicated in regulating a wide range of biological processes through chromatin remodeling and epigenetic regulation. The product OAADPR has also been found to functions in chromatin remodeling. Arabidopsis has two SIRTUIN-encoding genes, SRT1 and SRT2, but their cellular functions remain largely unclear. Our preliminary study suggests that Arabidopsis SRT and OAADPR might play important roles in controlling plant defense responses, possibly through epigenetic modifications. The aim of the study is to determine the functions of both the Arabidopsis SRT proteins and the unique metabolite OAADPR in cellular processes, particularly in defense responses. We will analyze the role of SRTs in mediating histone modification (deacetylation of lysines in histones), histone variant deposition, and plant defense responses. Genetic, biochemical, and molecular methods will be employed to characterize the two Arabidopsis SRTs through manipulation of their activity and identification of their substrates and effectors in order to determine the link between the SIRTUIN pathway and plant immunity. SIRTUIN 蛋白是需要NAD+的去乙酰化酶。它所介导的反应包括赖氨酸的去乙酰化以及NAD+的水解，并且产生NAD+水解的副产物OAADPR和尼克酰胺（NICOTINAMIDE）。SIRTUIN蛋白最初是在研究酵母的基因沉默的调控中被鉴定出来的，现在在几乎所有生命体中都发现了这类蛋白。SIRTUIN蛋白被发现参与调控机体中很多的生化过程，包括染色质的重塑以及表观遗传的调控。 OAADPR也被发现参与染色质的重塑。 在拟南芥中，有两个基因编码SIRTUIN蛋白，它们是SRT1和SRT2，但是它们在细胞中的功能依然不清楚。我们的初步研究表明拟南芥的SRT蛋白和OAADPR可能通过表观遗传的修饰来调控植物的免疫反应。 该研究的目标是探明拟南芥的SRT蛋白和它的独特的代谢产物OAADPR在细胞中，尤其是在植物免疫中的作用。我们将分析SRT蛋白在组蛋白的修饰（赖氨酸的去乙酰化），组蛋白变异体在染色质组分中的分布以及在植物免疫反应中的作用。在这个研究中，遗传的，生物化学的和分子生物学的手段会被用来分析拟南芥的SRT蛋白，主要的方法包括操控它们的酶活，鉴定它们的底物和效应子，从而最终明确SIRTUIN途径和植物免疫之间的关系。

12100717.label: Realisation of objectives
12100717.value: Shoudong Zhang, who was a research assistant professor at HKBU, started the project as the PI. After he left HKBU, the project was continued in the lab of Yiji Xia who has since served as the PI. Together, two groups carried out the following experiments to achieve the project objectives. Mutational analysis to study biological functions of SRT1 and SRT2 1. The Arabidopsis genome contains two genes coding for Sirtuin: SRT1 (At5g55760) and SRT2 (At5g09230). In seedlings under normal conditions, SRT2 is expressed at a higher level than SRT1. Following infection by P. syringae, the transcript level of SRT2 was found to be slightly but significantly reduced whereas the SRT1 transcript level was not significantly changed by the infection. 2. Three T-DNA insertion lines of SIR1 were obtained and characterized. The srt1-1 (Salk_086287) and srt1-2 (Salk_001493) mutants have the T-DNA insertion at the 1st and last exon, respectively, and the SRT1 transcripts could still be detected from these two alleles. Those two mutants showed no obvious morphological phenotype. Both are likely very weak alleles. The 3rd allele, sir1-4 (Sail_552_E02) has an insertion in the 5th exon that is expected to disrupt the Sirtuin domain. The sir1-4 mutation causes embryonic lethality, indicating that the gene is essential, and as a result, no sir1-4 homozygous line could be obtained. The Crispr/Cas9 system was used with the aim of generating weak alleles; however, we have not obtained an ideal allele which would show obvious phenotypic alteration but is viable. 3. For the SRT2 gene, two alleles, srt2-1 (Salk_131994) and srt2-2 (SALK_149295), were obtained and characterized. These two srt2 mutants are likely knockout mutants as no transcript was detected by RT-PCR from the mutants. Other than slight alteration in the hypocotyl length, both mutants are morphologically normal. The srt1 srt2 double mutant was generated by crossing the srt1-1 and srt2-1 single mutants. The double mutant did not display any additional discernible phenotype. The single and double mutants were subjected to analysis of their resistance phenotypes against infection P. syringae (DC3000). The srt2 and srt1 srt2 mutants showed slightly more resistance to the infection but the difference was often not statistically significant. SRT2 appears to play a role in the defense response. We could not rule out the possibility that SRT1 might have a partially overlapping function with SRT2 in defense; however, such a conclusion could not be reached due to the lethality of sir1 knockout mutation. Recently, we used Oxford nanopore direct RNA sequencing to generate and compare transcriptome profiles of WT and the srt2 mutant, including m6A methylation patterns. The data, which are under analysis, might provide more information on the role of SRT2 in mediating expression of genes involved in different pathways. Possible roles of SRTs in epigenetic modifications 4. Experiments were carried out to determine possible roles of SRT in epigenetic modifications of DNA and histones. We have used Oxford Nanopore single DNA molecule sequencing platform to sequence genomic DNA from srt2 and wildtype seedlings. A total of 4 giga sequencing data have been generated. The TOMBO, DeepSignal-plants, as well as Megalogon algorithms have been used for calling modified bases based on electric current patterns produced from nanopore reads. Preliminary results were obtained but further improvement of the algorithms is needed for machine learning and accurate calling of methylated bases in the Arabidopsis genome. A proteomic analysis was performed to obtain global histone modification patterns of wt and srt2 plants which might reveal how the sir2 mutation affects the histone acetylation and other modifications. Histones were isolated from wt and srt2 tissues by acidic extraction and separated using SDS-APGE and subjected to mass spectrometry analysis. The preliminary result did not show a significant difference in the overall histone modification patterns between wt and the mutant. The lack of an obvious difference between srt2 and wildtype might also be due to functional redundancy of the two sirtuins. Future study using other methods, such as ChIP-seq analysis using the H3K9ac antibodies, might help to determine if srt2 or srt1 mutations alter histone modifications in specific regions of the genomes. Other molecular functions of SRTs 5. The protein deacetylation reaction catalyzed by Sirtuin generates OAADPR as a product. We have used HPLC/mass spectrometry analysis to detect OAADPR but found that it is difficult to detect it from Arabidopsis tissues, indicating that its level is extremely low. It is possible that OAADPR could be a regulatory molecule and might bind to a protein to alter its activity/function. There is no report on using OAADPR as a probe to affinity-purify its binding protein, and we were not able to find a supplier who could provide such a probe (such as an OAADPR-biotin conjugate). However, the macrodomain of some proteins in human and microorganisms are known to bind to OAADPR. The Arabidopsis protein At2g44980 was found to contain the conserved macrodomain. At2g44980 also contains a SNF2 domain and helicase domain and might be involved in chromatin remodeling. We have obtained two T-DNA insertion lines of this gene to study its biological function. In-vitro binding assay (such as using gel electrophoretic mobility shift assay) would be used to determine if At2G44980 indeed binds to OAADPR. 6. After this project had started, we reported that Arabidopsis also produce NAD-capped RNAs. NAD capping is likely affected by cellular NAD levels. As sirtuins use NAD as a substrate in the protein deacetylation reaction, they are considered as a major type of NAD metabolizing enzymes and their action could alter cellular NAD levels which might affect NAD capping. Study of the possible role of SRT in NAD capping could expand our knowledge on function of sirtuins. We previously developed multiple methods for genome-wide profiling of NAD-RNAs. However, the previous methods were not sufficiently sensitive or accurate to profile NAD-RNAs in plants. More recently, we developed a method named NAD-linkSeq for NAD-RNA profiling with a higher sensitivity and more accuracy. In this method, NAD-RNAs are labeled with biotin and enriched by streptavidin resin. The biotin tag is then removed by the nudix protein nudC and RNAs are ligated with a 5’ and a 3’ linker and amplified by RT-PCR for a limited number of cycles. cDNAs are then ligated to a Splinter DNA fragment through Gibson assembly and amplified again with a limited cycle of PCR. The DNA samples are then sequenced using Oxford nanopore sequencing. From the srt2 seedlings, we identified a total of 163 putative NAD-RNAs from nuclear and mitochondrial genes, most of which are protein-coding genes but some are non-coding RNAs (including snoRNAs). The mitochondrial genes that produced NAD-RNAs including cox1, cox2, nad5/6/7, and atp8. Among the protein-coding nuclear genes that produced NAD-RNAs, those involved in photosynthesis and protein synthesis are enriched. We found that NAD-RNAs are typically short (40-200 nt) and were derived mostly from 5’ regions of those genes. The overall landscapes of NAD-RNAs from both wt and srt2 mutant are similar but some NAD-RNAs (such as those from non-coding genes) appear to have an increased level in the srt2 mutant. We have employed various approaches to understand biological and molecular functions of the sirturin genes. Some results are preliminary but could help us to develop a future research plan to further define the molecular mechanisms mediated by the sirtuins in regulating gene expression and other pathways.

12100717.label: Major findings and research outcome
12100717.value: Arabidopsis has two genes coding for sirturin proteins, SRT1 and SRT2. The SRT1 gene is essential for development and its knockout mutation leads to embryonic lethality. Knockout of SRT2 slightly increases length of hypocotyls but does not lead to any other visible phenotype. The expression of the SRT2 gene is slightly suppressed whereas SRT1 expression is not affected by pathogen infection. The srt2 knockout mutation leads to a slight increase in resistance to infection by Pseudomonas syringae. Due to the lethality phenotype caused by the srt1 knockout mutation, it remains to be determined whether SRT1 has an overlapping function with SRT2 in disease resistance. To determine the role of the sirtuins in epigenetic modifications, the Oxford nanopore sequencing technology was used to generate genomic sequencing data to identify methylated bases in the genomes of wildtype and srt2 plants. Histones of wildtype and srt2 mutants were isolated and analyzed by mass spectrometry to determine histone modification patterns. In addition to epigenetic modifications, sirtuin could have other molecular functions. The Arabidopsis protein coded by the At2g44980 gene contains the conserved macrodomain that might bind to OAADPR, which is product of the sirtuin-catalyzed protein deacetylation reaction. At2g44980 is likely a chromatin remodeling protein and its activity could be mediated by OAADPR. Sirtuin is also a NADase which uses NAD as a substrate in the deacetylation reaction, and therefore sirtuin could play a role in NAD capping of RNA. NAD-capped RNA profiling analysis was conducted and the levels of some NAD-capped RNAs were found altered by the srt2 mutation.

12100717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12100717.value: We have employed various approaches to understand biological and molecular functions of the sirturin genes. Some of the results are preliminary but will help us to develop a future research plan to future define the roles of the sirtuins in mediating gene regulation and other pathways. The inducible genome editing (IGE) system recently reported could be a useful approach to transiently knockdown SRT1 so that the biological and molecular function of SRT1 could be more conclusively determined. We are also collaborating with another group to modify and develop algorithms with improved ability to detect methylated nucleotides from Oxford nanopore single-molecule sequencing data of genomes and RNAs.

12100717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12100717.value: Sirtuin proteins in animals and yeast are known to play important roles in mediating many biological processes and their activities are linked to aging and cancer development. Sirtuins are NAD+-dependent protein deacetylases that regulate gene expression through epigenetic modifications and chromatin remodelling. Arabidopsis has two sirtuin genes, SRT1 and SRT2. We used genetic analysis to study biological functions of SRT1 and SRT2. SRT1 was found to be essential for development and loss of its function causes embryo abortion. SRT2 is apparently involved in defence against pathogen infection. Molecular functions of the plant sirtuins were investigated although some results are still preliminary. The sirtuins also likely regulate gene expression by mediating epigenetic modifications. Their action might affect function of a putative OAADPR-binding protein in Arabidopsis involved in chromatin remodelling. OAADPR is a product of the sirtuin-catalyzed deacetylation reaction. In addition, the sirtuin function could affect cellular NAD levels which in turn could affect NAD capping of RNAs to influence gene expression.

12100917.label: Project Objectives
12100917.value: We will define the insertion site of the GFP transgene associated with paternal inheritance of mtDNA /heteroplasmy by NGS. As an alternative, we will define the insertion site using PacBio or Nanopore sequencing if the NGS mapping result is not conclusive. We will generate multiple loss-of-function C. briggsae mutations by CRISPR/Cas9 technique targeting the DNA element that is disrupted by the GFP insertion. We will examine whether the mutations will recapitulate the heteroplasmy phenotype as observed in the introgression strain, which we expect to be the case. We will perform complementation tests for the heteroplasmy by introducing a BAC vector carrying a C. briggsae genomic DNA insert flanking the GFP insertion site and its neighboring genes into the introgression strain with heteroplasmy or into the mutants as stated in Objective 2. We will evaluate the presence of heteroplasmy in the crossing progeny between the males of these transgenic animals and C. nigoni females. We will confirm the heteroplasmy at the cellular level by staining the worms with MitoTracker, a mitochondrion-specific fluorescence marker. We will cross the GFP-expressing introgression males that are stained with MitoTracker with C. nigoni (JU1421) virgin females and examine the presence of heteroplasmy by fluorescence microscopy.

12100917.label: Realisation of objectives
12100917.value: The objective 1 was full achieved. We sequenced the transgenic lines showing the paternal inheritance of mtDNA /heteroplasmy by both NGS and Nanopore DNA sequencing. All transgenic insertion sites were mapped with nucleotide resolution. For the objective 2, we generated up to multiple meCherry insertions at all the GFP insertion sites to recapitulate the phenotype by the GFP insertion by CRISPR/Cas9 technique. The transgenic strains were backcrossed with the wild isolate of C. briggsae for at least five generations to minimize the other possible off-target insertions. We crossed the males each carrying a single copy of these insertions with females and tested the heteroplasmy phenotype as observed in the GFP-based introgression strain. However, none of the transgenic strains carrying the mCherry recapitulated the heteroplasmy phenotype. To understand why the mCherry-carrying transgenes were not able to recapitulate the heteroplasmy phenotypes, we reexamined the GFP transgene insertion sites by Nanopore DNA sequencing, which produced DNA sequencing reads up to 50 Kb in size. To our surprise, we found that there was a genomic site that carries multiple copies of mitochondrial DNAs! This was not surprising if we took into account of our transgenesis method. We used gene gun to produce all GFP-based transgenes. When worms were shot with these golden beads, there were reasonable chances that highly abundant mitochondrial DNAs got disrupted by the golden beads travelling with very high speed, and were wrapped outside of the beads. Some of these mitochondrial DNAs were accidentally inserted into the host genome along with the GFP-transgenes. The transgenic strain carrying both GFP and mitochondrial DNAs, when crossed with C. nigoni, were expected to produce pseudo heteroplasmy phenotype as we observed here. For the objective 3, we performed complementation tests for the heteroplasmy by introducing a BAC vector carrying a C. briggsae genomic DNA insert flanking the GFP insertion site and its neighboring genes into all the introgression strains with heteroplasmy. As mentioned above, we would expect negative results because of the pseudo heteroplasmy caused by the mitochondrial DNAs co-inserted into the host genome along with the GFP sequences. For the objective 4, despite the pseudo heteroplasmy caused by the mitochondrial DNAs, we still performed staining the worms with MitoTracker. We did this by crossing the GFP-expressing introgression males that are stained with MitoTracker with C. nigoni (JU1421) virgin females and examining the presence of heteroplasmy by fluorescence microscopy. We crossed the GFP-expressing introgression males that were stained with MitoTracker with C. nigoni (JU1421) virgin females and examined the presence of heteroplasmy by fluorescence microscopy. As expected, we did not observe any positive staining in any of the examined F1 embryos. This experiment confirmed that the transgenesis with gene gun produced an unexpected side product, i.e., genome insertion of host mitochondrial DNAs into host genome along with the transgene of interest.

12100917.label: Major findings and research outcome
12100917.value: The major finding of the project is that the maternal inheritance of mitochondrial DNAs (mtDNAs) still holds even in the hybrid progeny between two closely related species. This project stemmed from an observation that paternal leakage of mtDNAs was observed in the hybrid progeny of some transgenic C. briggsae strains generated with biolistic bombardment. This is not expected based on the assumption that maternal inheritance of mitochondria is still the case even in species hybrid. After a thorough investigation of the underlying mechanism of the observed leakage, we found that the observed leakage was due to the unexpected insertion of mtDNAs into host genome in some transgenic strains produced with biolistic bombardment, which led to the pseudo paternal leakage of mtDNA. This observation raised an important by-product of transgenesis made with biolistic bombardment.

12100917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12100917.value: This project raises an important issue associated with transgenesis method with biolistic bombardment, which have been intensively used in crop transgenesis. First, genome rearrangement or unusual lesions of genomic or mitochondrial DNAs may be common in the transgenic strains made with biolistic bombardment. A careful examination of genome integrity is necessary during interpretation of any results derived from such transgenic strains. Second, transgenic method using biolistic bombardment should be only used when other methods can not make the strains with desired features, e.g., expression of transgenic reporter is too weak to be seen as a single copy of transgene.

12100917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12100917.value: It is well known that mitochondrial DNAs (mtDNA) are transmitted exclusively from mother. “Leakage” of a tiny amount of paternal mtDNA has been found associated with diabetes and cancers in humans. However, why only maternal mtDNAs are specifically transmitted during reproduction remains elusive. Here we tried to address this issue in the hybrid of nematode species. This was because our observation of “leaked” mtDNAs from a transgenic Caenorhabditis briggsae father expressing a GFP reporter made with biolistic bombardment in its hybrid progeny with another nematode, C. nigoni. Given the tight linkage between the GFP insertion and the paternal inheritance of mtDNA, we hypothesize that the GFP insertion could disrupt some DNA elements that are responsible for the paternal inheritance of mtDNA. We mapped the GFP insertion site by Nanopore DNA sequencing, which produced sequencing reads up to 100 Kbp in size. To our surprise, we found that multiple copies of mitochondrial DNAs were inserted into the host genome, which led to the “pseudo” paternal leakage of mtDNA! This result raised an important issue of transgene made with biolistic bombardment. A careful examination of genome integrity is necessary during interpretation of any results derived from such transgenic strains.

12101117.value: 以破骨細胞介導的骨吸收亢進為主要特徵的軟骨下骨骨重塑失常是骨關節炎早期的重要病理改變，其分子機制尚不明確。我們此前證實微小核糖核酸miR-214-3p可調控骨重塑。我們近期在骨關節炎小鼠模型中進一步發現軟骨下破骨細胞內的miR-214-3p顯著升高，且早於骨吸收和軟骨退變標誌物的升高。體外實驗顯示破骨細胞miR-214-3p可抑制TIMP2並促進共培養軟骨塊的降解。因此我們假設破骨細胞內高表達的miR-214-3p介導了骨關節炎早期軟骨下骨骨重塑失常。我們擬用切除膝關節前交叉韌帶的骨關節炎小鼠模型來驗證上述假設，利用已有的破骨細胞特異性miR-214-3p敲除／敲入的基因工程小鼠以及破骨細胞靶向遞送系統等工具來研究干預破骨細胞內miR-214-3p對軟骨下骨骨重塑及軟骨退變的影響。本研究可望闡釋骨關節炎早期軟骨下骨骨重塑失常的分子機制，為早期干預骨關節炎提供新的治療策略。

12101117.label: Realisation of objectives
12101117.value: In the midterm progress report, we reported the realisation of Aim 1. After that, we further performed experiments for Aim 2 and Aim 3. To our expect, we found that osteoclast-targeted delivery of TIMP2-3'UTR but not the Mutant 3'UTR could significantly attenuate the cartilage degradation in CKI mice. Thus, Aim 2 was realised. Considering that we have realised Aim 1, which demonstrated the benificial effect of miR-214-3p loss-of-function in osteoclast by genetic approach, we thought that the original Aim 3, which intended to test whether miR-214-3p loss-of-function in osteoclast by pharmacological approach (osteoclast-targeted delivery of antagomir-214-3p) could also attenuate OA progression in ACLT mice, would be merely another prove-of-concept validation of the outcome of Aim 1. More importantly, during the execution of this project, we further observed that osteoclast-derived exosomal miR-214 could transfer to chondrocyte to affect their catabolic activity in vitro, suggesting that the exosomal miR-214-3p could mediate the osteoclast-chondrocyte crosstalk in OA. Taken together with our preliminary findings on the elevated serum exosomal miR-214-3p in ACLT mice and CKI mice, we were encouraged to further investigate whether blocking the secretion of exosomal miR-214-3p from osteoclast could rescue the OA changes in CKI mice after ACLT. As expected, we found that that osteoclast-targeted delivery of Rab27a siRNA, which could interrupt the Rab27a-mediated exosome secretion, significantly retard the OA progression in CKI mice after ACLT.

12101117.label: Major findings and research outcome
12101117.value: In this study, we found that the elevated osteoclastic miR-214-3p could contribute to the progression of surgery-induced OA in mouse model. We showed that osteoclast-specific depletion of miR-214-3p could attenuate the OA progression in CKO mice after ACLT. We further showed that osteoclast-targeted delivery of TIMP2 3'UTR could rescue the OA changes in CKI mice after ACLT, suggesting that osteoclastic miR-214-3p could contribute to the OA progression by directly targeting TIMP2 to regulate the subchondral bone remodeling. Importantly, we further observed that osteoclast-derived exosomal miR-214 could transfer to chondrocyte to affect their catabolic activity in vitro. We also showed that osteoclast-targeted delivery of Rab27a siRNA for interrupting the exosome secretion from osteoclast could also rescue the OA changes in CKI mice after ACLT. This finding indicates that the osteoclast-derived exosomal miR-214-3p could also contribute to OA progression through mediating the osteoclast-chondrocyte crosstalk. The findings of this project was previously invited to orally presented on the ASBMR 2019 Annual Meeting. They were also included in our recently published study entitled "Exosomal transfer of osteoclast-derived miRNAs to chondrocytes contributes to osteoarthritis progression" in Nature Aging (Liu et al., Nature Aging, 2021, DOI: 10.1038/s43587-021-00050-6). On the other hand, anther three recently published studies was also partially supported by the funding of this project (Zhuo et al., Advanced Sciences 2020, Chen et al., Theronostics 2020, and Li et al., Theranostics 2021).

12101117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12101117.value: The finding in this project strongly indicates that the exosomal miRNAs from osteoclast could be a therapeutic target for OA treatment. From the aspect of translational medicine, we have continued to developed an osteoclast-targeted small molecule exosome inhibitor for therapeutically blocking osteoclastic exosome secretion for OA treatment. We have currently obtained a potent compound as small molecule exosome inhibitor and successfully obtained the osteoclast-targeted exosome inhibitor (OCExoInhib). The effect of this OCExoInhib on blockage of exosome secretion from osteoclasts have been validated both in osteoclast culture in vitro and ACLT mice in vivo. One member of our research group, Dr. Jin Liu, is working on the pharmacological evaluation of this conjugate in rodent models with various surgery-induced OA. He has also submitted a proposal for the application of new GRF project.

12101117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12101117.value: The current project demonstrated that the osteoclastic miRNA, i.e., miR-214-3p, could regulate the subchondral bone remodeling and further mediate the osteoclast-chondrocyte crosstalk in exosomal manner, by which contribute to the OA progression. Targeting the osteoclastic miR-214-3p or the exosomal miRNAs derived from osteoclast could be a potential therapeutic strategy for OA.

12101417.value: 阿爾茨海默病（AD）是一種最常見的神經退行性疾病，影響4-8％的老年人口。然而令人遺憾是目前仍缺乏有效手段對其進行防治。AD的病理改變主要為細胞外β澱粉樣蛋白（Aβ）沉積形成的老年斑和細胞內過度磷酸化的Tau蛋白組成的神經原纖維纏結（NFT）。在過去幾十年裏，基於Aβ的AD藥物的研發均以失敗告終。與Aβ相比，研究發現NFT中過度磷酸化的Tau蛋白與記憶力密切相關，因此對於AD的藥物開發，越來越多地轉向以Tau蛋白為靶點。TFEB（轉錄因子EB）是自噬和溶酶體生物合成的主要調節因子，過表達TFEB可顯著改善AD動物模型中的神經毒性及相關神經退行性疾病的癥狀，因此TFEB的小分子激活劑有望成為治療AD的有效手段，但目前已知的TFEB激活劑也抑制mTOR通路。鑒於mTOR在神經細胞的生長和代謝中具有重要作用，因此，開發新型的mTOR非依賴性的TFEB激活劑，有望成為治療AD的安全、有效的候選藥物。 我們的前期研究工作發現姜黃素的衍生物C1能結合並激活TFEB以促進自噬和溶酶體生物合成，其激活TFEB不依賴於mTOR信號通路（Song JX，et al Autophagy 2016）。由於激活TFEB能夠減輕AD動物模型中Tau蛋白的病理特征，我們在細胞和動物模中評價了C1對Tau蛋白降解的影響。我們的初步數據顯示，C1能夠有效地清除AD小鼠腦中Tau蛋白的積聚，同時，C1也提高了P301S Tau轉基因AD小鼠的認知功能。基於這些前期數據，我們假設C1通過激活TFEB以減輕AD動物模型中的Tau病理學特征達到治療AD的效果。 在本項目中，我們擬研究：（1）進一步明確C1在P301S Tau AD轉基因動物模型中的神經保護作用;（2）發現C1促進清除神經細胞內異常積聚Tau蛋白的分子機制;（3）評估C1的藥代動力學和安全性。總之，本研究有望為開發一種新型的mTOR非依賴性、能透過血腦屏障的TFEB激活劑用於治療AD而提供重要的臨床前依據。

12101417.label: Realisation of objectives
12101417.value: Objective 1: To consolidate the neuroprotective effects of C1 in P301S Tau transgenic AD mice. Animals and treatment Homozygous human P301S tau transgenic mice were generous gifts from Michael Goedert (Allen et al., 2002). One-month-old mice (male and female, n = 9 per group) were treated daily with curcumin analog C1 (5 and 10 mg per kg body weight) or vehicle for 3 months. To avoid possible injury to mice from long-term oral gavage, compound C1 was mixed in regular feed according to the actual dosage used (5 and 10 mg/kg body weight, as low and high dosages, respectively). Mice at 4 months of age after treatment were used for behavior tests and then sacrificed for biochemical analysis. Results The result showed that mice treated with C1 spent longer time on the accelerating rotarod compared with vehicle-treated mice. Then, we determined the levels of phosphorylated (p-) Tau AT8 (S202/T205), PHF1 (S396/S404) and total Tau in the brain lysates extracted by RIPA buffer. The quantification data demonstrate that the ratio of AT8 and PHF1 to total Tau was significantly reduced in C1 treatment group. Next, we determined whether C1 reduces soluble or insoluble Tau species by sarkosyl fractioning of mice brains. Notably, we found that C1 treatment drastically reduced the levels of p-Tau (AT8 and PHF1), conformation-specific Tau (MC1), and total Tau in the sarkosyl-insoluble (P) fractions, and the effects are comparable to that of TFEB overexpression as previously investigated (Polito et al., 2014). Importantly, the levels of SQSTM1, an autophagy substrate, were also dramatically reduced by C1 treatment in the sarkosyl-insoluble fractions. In contrast, the levels of AT8, PHF1, MC1, total Tau, and SQSTM1 were not significantly decreased by C1 treatment in the sarkosyl-soluble (S) fractions. The immunofluorescence staining results of AT8 in the cortex and hippocampus further validated that C1 treatment drastically reduced the phosphorylated Tau. These results indicate that C1 mainly reduces insoluble Tau aggregates in P301S mice brains. To find out whether the reduction in Tau aggregates by C1 is mediated by TFEB, we simultaneously determined the levels of TFEB, the cytosolic/nuclear TFEB, the autophagy markers (LC3B and SQSTM1) and the lysosome markers (LAMP1 and CTSD) in the brain lysates. The results showed that C1 not only increased the levels of total TFEB, but also promoted the nuclear translocation of TFEB. For the autophagy markers C1 treatment significantly increased the levels of LC3B-II, while leaving SQSTM1 unchanged in the RIPA-soluble fractions. For lysosome markers, C1 treatment significantly increased the levels of LMAP1 and pro-/mature-CTSD, which are target proteins regulated by TFEB. Notably, C1 treatment significantly activated the MTOR pathway, as indicated by the increase in the levels of phosphorylated (p-) MTOR and its substrate ribosomal protein S6 kinase, polypeptide 1 (RPS6KB1/p70S6K). These results indicate that C1 treatment activates TFEB and promotes autophagy and lysosome biogenesis in the brain of P301S mice without inhibiting the MTOR pathway. Generally, we have achieved the proposed studies in Objective 1. For the proposed aim 1.2. “To investigate whether C1 could reduce neuroinflammation in P301S Tau transgenic AD mice”, we have replaced it with another more important and relevant study, which addressed the neuroprotective of C1 in 3xTg mice expressing both APP and Tau. We found that C1 efficiently promoted the degradation of APP fragments, Aβ and phosphorylated Tau aggregates in 3xTg-AD mice by promoting TFEB-mediated autophagy and lysosomal biogenesis. The data from 3xTg mice double confirmed our findings in P301S Tau mice. Objective 2: To determine the mechanism by which C1 promotes the clearance of aberrant Tau in neuronal cells. Methods To further validate that the anti-AD efficacy of C1 is mainly mediated by TFEB, we tested the effects of C1 on APP turnover and Tau degradation in neuronal cell cultures. N2a cells were cultured in DMEM/Opti-MEM (50:50) supplemented with 2% FBS. The cells were transiently transfected with human APPSwe/Ind (APP 695 Swedish/Indiana mutation, Young-Pearse et al., 2007, 30145; Addgene) or P301L-Tau (Hoover et al., 2010, 46908; Addgene) plasmids with empty vectors as the control and then treated with C1 for 16 hr or EBSS for 4 hr. For cycloheximide (CHX) chase assay, N2a-APP cells were pretreated with C1 and then treated with 50 μg/ml CHX followed by collecting cells at several time intervals. Bafilomycin A1 (1334; Tocris Bioscience; 100 nM) was used to inhibit lysosome function as previously described (Xiao et al., 2015). For TFEB knockdown, N2a cells were infected with lentivirus expressing nontarget shRNA (Sigma-Aldrich; SHC002V) or mouse Tfeb shRNA (Sigma-Aldrich; TRCN0000085548) for 48 hr and then incubated with medium containing puromycin (1.5 μg/ml) until resistant colonies were identified. Results Firstly, in N2a cells overexpressing APP695, C1 dose-dependently promoted the nuclear translocation of TFEB and reduced the levels of Fl-APP and CTF-β detected by 6E10 antibody (Tian, Bustos, Flajolet, & Greengard, 2011). Earle's balanced salt solution (EBSS) starvation for 4 hr was used as a positive control. Notably, C1 did not affect the expression of BACE1/beta-secretase 1 and PSEN1/presenilin 1 (one major component of γ-secretase), which are involved in the amyloidogenic processing of APP. To determine whether C1 promotes the lysosomal degradation of APP, we used bafilomycin A1 (Baf) to inhibit lysosomal acidification and cycloheximide (CHX) to inhibit protein synthesis. The effects of C1 on APP reduction were significantly inhibited by Baf at each indicated time point of CHX treatment. Furthermore, the effect of C1 on APP/CTF-β degradation was significantly inhibited in TFEB knockdown cells. Similar results were observed in N2a cells expressing P301L-Tau. C1 significantly reduced the levels of PHF1 and total Tau, and its effects were inhibited by lysosomal inhibition and TFEB knockdown. Together, these results demonstrated that C1 promotes the lysosomal degradation of APP/CTF-β and Tau via TFEB activation. In Objective 2, we not only addressed the Tau, but also APP/CTF-β degradation mechanisms in vitro. Objective 3: To evaluate the pharmacokinetics and safety of C1. Pharmacokinetics: In C57BL/6 mice, C1 has shown much higher blood and brain bio-availability than curcumin. C1 maximum concentration in brain was 1308.23 ± 88.96 ng (Cmax) at 30 minutes (Tmax). In blood 489.39±110.89 ng of maximum C1 concentration (Cmax) at 15 minutes (Tmax). 73.77±0.24ng of curcumin per gram of brain tissue was detected at 1 hour. Curcumin level in the brain and plasma was undetectable after 8 hours. In SD rats, the concentration of C1 was 57.97±18.65 ng/g in frontal cortex, 68.41±21.72 ng/g in hippocampus and 4.69±2.19 ng/g in striatum. 352.16±21.37 ng/ml of C1 in blood was determined. We also found 101.5±52.41 ng/ml of C1 in CSF. Curcumin level was below the detection level at 10 mg/kg, 1-hour post oral drug administration. Safety: We have determined the acute toxicity of C1 in rats. By single-dose intravenous (IV) tail vein injection, the medium lethal dose (LD50) value of C1 was 175 mg/kg. Since our findings have been patented and licensed to a biopharmaceutical company, the chronic toxicity of C1 is being evaluated by the company. Therefore, we did not perform the proposed chronic toxicity by ourselves.

12101417.label: Major findings and research outcome
12101417.value: The major objectives of this project are to determine the potential neuroprotective effects of C1, a TFEB activator, in AD animal models and the underlying mechanism of C1 in the clearance of aberrant Tau. We hypothesized that C1 activates TFEB to attenuate Tau pathology in AD animal models. In P301S Tau transgenic AD mice, we found that C1 improves motor performance in P301S Tau transgenic mice in the Rotarod test. This function improvement is accompanied by significant Tau clearance in Tau transgenic mice. Meanwhile, C1 treatment effectively promoted the nuclear translocation of TFEB and increased autophagy and lysosome markers in mice brains. Further elucidation of the therapeutic mechanism revealed that C1 may promote the clearance of p-TAU in Tau transgenic mice through TFEB-mediated induction of autophagy. Interestingly, we found that C1 promotes autophagy and lysosomal biogenesis in an mTOR-independent manner. We also showed that C1 directly binding with TFEB contributes to the role of C1 in inducing autophagy. Finally, we found that oral administration is an effective and convenient route for administering C1 in mice. C1 can easily cross the blood-brain barrier and accumulate in the brain. Collectively, we not only demonstrated the neuroprotective effects of C1 in animal models of AD but also elucidated the possible mechanisms. Based on these findings, we primarily published two peer-reviewed papers (Song JX, et al. Aging cell 2019; Song JX, et al. Drug Discov. Today 2020). Through this project, we have trained two postgraduate students and received a US patent (No. US10987319B2) and a Chinese patent (CN 113398106 A).

12101417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12101417.value: The results from this project have confirmed the therapeutic effects of C1 in animal models of AD through directly binding to TFEB and activating autophagic degradation of pathogenic p-Tau. Based on these findings, follow-up work can be adopted: 1) to facilitate translation of the findings to the clinical setting. 2) to promote the application of C1 as a TFEB activator and an autophagy inducer in the therapeutics of other neurodegenerative diseases involving autophagy impairment.

12101417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12101417.value: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is the most common neurodegenerative disorder, affecting 4-8% of the elderly population worldwide. AD is characterized by the deposition of extracellular amyloid plaques composed of β-amyloid peptides (Aβ) and intracellular neurofibrillary tangles consisting of hyperphosphorylated Tau protein in the brain. Increasing evidence has demonstrated that activation of TFEB (transcription factor EB), a master regulator of autophagy and lysosomal biogenesis, can ameliorate neurotoxicity and rescue neurodegeneration in AD animal models. However, currently known TFEB activators also inhibit mTOR, a master regulator of cell growth and metabolism. Thus, the identification of TFEB activators, as safe drugs, acting without inhibiting the mTOR pathway would be preferred and would probably have few side effects in AD treatment. Our study has shown that C1, a synthesized mono-carbonyl analog of curcumin, binds and activates TFEB to promote autophagy and lysosomal biogenesis in an mTOR-independent manner and promotes the clearance of aberrant Tau in animal models of AD. Our results have the potential to be translated to clinics helping the rapidly increasing population of AD patients.

12102217.label: Realisation of objectives
12102217.value: In this project, we conducted a comprehensive and systematical study on the distribution of chemicals in tissues and organs, as well as their variation in different growing stages. Cultivated Leonurus japonicas, the origin of Yimucao, as experimental samples were collected the aerial part in different stages (seedling, vegetative, flowering and harvest stage). By using laser microdissection (LMD), different tissues and cells from leaves and stems were separated accurately and collected. Ultra-performance liquid chromatography (UPLC) coupled with mass spectrometry (MS) was used for the qualitative and quantitative analysis of the dissected tissues and cells. With the results, the best harvest period and medicinal parts of Yimucao were found out. Furthermore, we also evaluated the decoction pieces in the market and corroborate the results. Yimucao, also known as Chinese motherwort, is the aerial part of Leonurus japonicus Houtt. from Lamiaceae family. Just like its name, it is used to treat various women’s diseases such as irregular menses, dysmenorrhea, amenorrhea, and postpartum abdominal pain traditionally. It is one of the most commonly used medicinal herb in gynecology and obstetrics, and also a widely used healthcare supplement amount women in Asia. With thousands of years of clinical experience, Yimucao is recognized to be safe and non-toxic. However, adverse reactions after using this herb were reported in recent decades. Also, the herb collected in different stages with the varied proportion of leaves and stems was easily found in the markets which induce the unstable quality for clinic use. Thus, the toxicity and quality of this traditional Chinese Materia Medica has already attracted public concern. Over 130 chemicals were found in Yimucao, alkaloids, diterpenes and flavones are the three main types of compounds . Of these, alkaloids are the major bioactive ingredients and have been studied extensively. Leonurine and stachydrine have marked effects on uterine, which can reduce the bleeding and increase the frequency and tension of contractions. They also have diuretic effect and cardiovascular effects such as antiplatelet aggregation, decrease blood viscosity and protection against myocardial ischemia. The pharmacologic studies of the compounds supported the traditional usage of Yimucao, alkaloids are now listed as the quality control compounds of the herb. Nevertheless, modern researches indicated that the alkaloids may responsible for adverse reactions of Yimucao. But for Yimucao, limited information on the distribution of compounds was found. The toxic and active compounds in plants are the secondary metabolites that accumulated in tissues and organs, types of compounds and their contents are various in them except for different growing stages. A standardized collection period and suitable proportion of various medical parts will be the first step in order to guarantee a uniform quality. Here, different growing stages of Yimucao will produce different medicinal parts for use, such as the proportion of leaves and stems, whether containing the flowers or fruits, the sizes of leaves and stems. Thus, the chemical profiles of different organs and tissue-specific chemical distributions in leaves and stems are of concern. As profiling the chemicals containing in tissues and cells of leaves and stems can correlate the chemical contents and the sizes of leaves and stems, to probe the chemical distribution and change in its different tissues and organs in samples collected from different growing stages will benefit to evaluate the toxicity and guarantee a uniform quality of Yimucao. And further ensure Yimucao with well-controlled quality and safe use in clinic. Decoction pieces are the processed form of CMMs which is ready for clinical use, which CMMs are simply wash clean and cut into appropriate size; or other advanced processing practices such as steaming and charring. In the market, different types of Yimucao decoction pieces can be found, some with leaves and stems, some only have a few leaves, some even only have old stems which is collected after the harvest of fruits. To provide scientific evidence to standardize the harvest of Yimucao, a comprehensive and systematical study were also conducted. This project provide valuable scientific data to evaluate the toxicity and quality of Yimucao by standardizing the reasonable medicinal parts with applicable proportion of leaves and stems as well as the harvest time, which is desperately in need for the medication safety and use of this widely used Chinese Materia Medica.

12102217.label: Major findings and research outcome
12102217.value: Major findings are as follows: 1. Based on the above trials, the optimal extraction method of Yimucao were established. A suitable extraction method is usually important to check the chemical components in Chinese Materia Medica. Hence, this study has clearly and preliminary identified 49 components in Yimucao, including 2 alkaloids, 18 flavonoids, 7 diterpenes, 8 aromatic acids, and 14 other classes. 2. The fingerprints of 29 batches of Yimucao in different habitats were established, and 33 chromatographic fingerprint peaks were confirmed, and the quality was found to be quite different. The main components 1-8 were the main factors affecting the quality evaluation of the Yimucao sample. Thus, an accurate, fast, stable, and reproducible.UHPLC-QTOF-MS/MS content determination method for these eight components: leonurine, 4', 5-dihydroxy-7-methoxyflavone, rutin, hyperoside, apigenin, quercetin, kaempferol and salicylic acid in Yimucao are developed. 3. Our results both showed that the leaves of Yimucao seedling had a higher percentage in the same weight. Furthermore, the stems are relatively thin and with a higher concentration of secondary metabolites than the old one. Thus, the overall quality of Yimucao seedling is better than the old Yimucao. 4. Apart from the quality of medicinal part, Yimucao from different habitats are mainly clustered into four categories: Henan and Anhui are grouped together; Yunnan and Sichuan are grouped together; Guangdong and Hubei (Yimucao seedlings) are grouped together; Hubei (old Yimucao) is grouped as one type. The comprehensive evaluation analysis showed that the quality of the Yimucao seedlings was generally good. 5. The tissue-specific profiling of compounds by laser microdissection (LMD) technique combined with ultra-performance liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS) can locate the distribution of different compounds in tissues and cells of leaves and stems from Yimucao, which help to select the appropriate medicinal parts. In our studies, leaves from the flowering plant have a higher content of alkaloids and flavones than seedling plant; highly lignified stem has rather low content of alkaloids and flavones; comparing the aerial part, deduced by mass as a whole, the seedling plant has a higher content of both alkaloids and flavones than the flowering plant. Alkaloids and flavones are concentrated in glandular scales, followed by small glandular hairs. 6. The mapping of different chemical compounds in different tissues and organs of Yimucao provide fundamental information on the further studies of its physiology, such as metabolism, biosynthetic pathways and accumulation of secondary metabolites, which could be significant for the cultivation of Yimucao.

12102217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12102217.value: Only alkaloids and flavones of L. japonicus were included in this study. The contents of other considerable compounds like diterpenes or glycosides are also worth to investigate. Most studies on Yimucao were focusing on its alkaloids stachydrine and leonurine and that may not be comprehensive enough. Further studies on the differences between the flavones and diterpenes of species in the genus Leonurus is important. Varies species from the genus Leonurus are also selling in the market, but they are the non-authorization species. Both the merchants and users should be careful in distinguishing them. They were believed to have the same therapeutic effects in historical records, however, their chemical composition and pharmacological effects should be different. Further studies on the differences between them are still significant, especially on their flavones and diterpenes, which are also the active components of the Leonurus genus. Each species should have its representative flavones and diterpenes. Both qualitative and quantitative analysis should be held to compare their chemical compositions. This could help screening on the superior species to broaden the resource of Yimucao.

12102217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12102217.value: The quality of decoction pieces are the foundation of the effectiveness and safety of Chinese medicine. The amount of bioactive compounds in Chinese Materia Medica (CMM) may be affected by various factors. Detailed studies are necessary to provide scientific data to standardize the CMM for best quality. In this project, a systematic study of Yimucao (the aerial part of Leonurus japonicus Houtt.) were conducted. This project can provide a comprehensive and detailed scientific data to support the standardization of Yimucao. The tissue-specific profiling of compounds by LMD technique combined with UPLC-MS can locate the distribution of different compounds in tissues and cells of leaves and stems from Yimucao, which help to select the appropriate medicinal parts. The mapping of chemical compounds in different tissues and organs of Yimucao can provide fundamental information on its physiology, metabolism, biosynthetic pathways and accumulation of secondary metabolites, which could be significant for the cultivation of Yimucao. The information of compounds distribution may alter the medicinal parts used for different therapeutic purposes, which can achieve a more safe and effective used of CMM. This project will provide a research model for further study of other CMMs, especially those use aerial part or whole plant.

12102417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12102417.value: 食管鱗狀細胞癌（ESCC）在中國和香港是一種高度普遍的癌症類型，是來自於食管內壁的薄而扁平的鱗狀細胞。ESCC被認為是最具侵襲性的鱗狀細胞癌之一。對正常上皮如何轉化為侵襲性ESCC表型的分子基礎的了解肯定會加強針對晚期疾病的藥物開發和鑑定更具體/敏感的預後生物標誌物。我們的初步數據表明，血清澱粉樣蛋白A1（SAA1）蛋白主要在食道正常上皮中表達，我們在ESCC腫瘤組織中觀察到SAA1的表達頻率下調或喪失。有趣的是，SAA1的表達水平與上皮間質轉化（EMT）標記物N-鈣粘蛋白呈負相關的現象。SAA1的基因敲低導致在兩個正常的食管上皮細胞系中誘導N鈣粘蛋白和EMT相關的整合素alphaV表達和獲得間質的形態。另外，當SAA1表達在ESCC細胞系中恢復時，整合素alphaV蛋白表達顯著降低，轉化生長因子beta（TGFbeta）誘導的EMT幾乎完全消除。同樣地，整合素alphaV敲低也可以抵消ESCC細胞中TGFbeta的作用。我們的初步數據表明，SAA1可能是ESCC和正常上皮細胞中EMT的強負調控因子，其表達似乎與整合素alphaV和N鈣粘蛋白呈負相關。我們想確定SAA1是否可以通過抑制正常上皮及其食道的腫瘤細胞中的整合素alphaV來抑制EMT。我們最近建立了模擬正常食管上皮的3D組織的小鼠器官和人類器官模型。將仔細檢查上皮內不同分層細胞層（具有不同程度的分化）的SAA1，整合素alphaV，N鈣粘蛋白和其他EMT標記的功能和表達。另一方面，我們將調查侵襲性ESCC細胞系中SAA1的恢復是否可以抑制EMT相關的腫瘤侵襲。我們亦將ESCC細胞系移植到小鼠食管中（原位ESCC模型），檢測入侵邊緣的腫瘤侵襲和SAA1，整合素alphaV，N鈣粘蛋白和其他EMT標記物的表達。如果整合素alphaV的抑制對於SAA1抑制EMT和腫瘤侵襲是必需，則整合素alphaV可能代表治療ESCC腫瘤進展的靶標藥物。為了獲得臨床相關性，我們旨在確定SAA1表達的喪失是否與從良性腫瘤到晚期轉移癌的整合素alphaV和N鈣粘蛋白表達增加相關。我們想確定這三種蛋白質在正常組織和腫瘤組織中的表達模式的變化是否可以用作預後的生物標誌物來預測腫瘤進展和患者的總生存期。該項目的結果將表明，SAA1是一種新型上皮標誌物，也是上皮細胞進入食管EMT程序的候選當關的因素及其相關間充質蛋白的表達模式將有助於了解複雜的正常食管上皮的結構。

12103817.label: Realisation of objectives
12103817.value: A TriCEPS-based-LRC approach was performed to identify the receptor of STC-1 on primary eel gill cells. We had the MS data to compare with transcriptome to proceed with peptide search and validation. A list of candidate peptides (P<0.05) was generated. An inter-replicate comparison was conducted to identify potential candidates with functional annotation. Since the Japanese eel high-resolution genome is not available, there was difficult to match the exact targets in the database. For compensation, we generated the high-resolution eel genome for subsequent analysis. In the meantime, a similar approach (TriCEPS-based-LRC) was implemented using mammalian samples to identify STC1 receptors for cross-species comparison. Non-adherent cells (ThP-1) cells were used for capturing pull-down receptors. There were 4 possible candidates were identified. Only one is a membrane receptor. We had the follow-up experiments (Biacore surface plasmon resonance (SRP) Assay) to verify the specificity and kinetics of the binding. STC1 binds to the immobilized receptor with high capacity (%Rmax = 70 – 100% of binding capacity) and high affinity in the 10 – 20 nM range. In addition to the two papers listed in this report, the third paper (manuscript) is under preparation (attached in this report).

12103817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12103817.value: The present study has identified the receptor binding to STC1 with high affinity and capacity. With hindsight, the current finding would help to address the previous reports describing cellular sequestration of STC1 in cell cytoplasm and organelles, and to further investiagte the underlying mechanisms to explain the myriad of biological processes, including Ca2+-transport, cell proliferation, differentiation, apoptosis, inflammation and carcinogenesis. The functional analysis could also help to understand the evolutionary change of STC1-receptor.

12103817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12103817.value: In the past years, great progress on STC1 biology has been made on both fish and mammalian models. The functional roles of STC1 in the regulation of Ca2+-homeostasis, cell growth, or inflammatory responses have been reported, and evidence strongly suggests the connection of the hormone to a variety of complex pathways. Yet, the cloning of STC1 receptor in mammals has proven to be challenging and this hampers further understanding of the mechanistic action of the hormone. This study describes the isolation and characterization of STC1 receptor to unravel the biological action of the identified evolutionary conserved gene. A deeper investigation to characterize the interaction of its signaling cascade with other Ca2+-regulatory factors will help to elucidate its action and effect on cellular and mitochondria Ca2+ homeostasis. In fact, mitochondria are known to participate in Ca2+-homeostasis and is crucial in different signaling pathways and cell functions. The data would yield important knowledge into myriads of biological functions of STC1 in mammals which may serve as a fundamental basis to the understanding on human diseases.

12103917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12103917.value: There have been repeated outbreaks of Ebola virus disease (EVD) since its first outbreaks in Sudan and Zaire in 1976. The recent 2013-2016 EVD outbreak has killed more than 11,000 people among 28,652 infection cases. The mortality of each EVD outbreak ranges from 25-90%. The deadly disease is expected to continue to threaten humans not only because there are currently no effective antiviral drugs or vaccines available for treating and preventing EVD, but also because Ebola virus can increase the ability to infect human cells upon the viral mutations, which is evidenced by the current EVD epidemic in West Africa. The present project is designed to discover new anti-Ebola lead compounds from the selected plants in Lingnan Region of China. Three plant leads have been identified to effectively inhibit Ebola virus from evaluating more than 1,500 plant extracts in our drug discovery program. They are identified as the medicinal plants Agrimonia eupatoria (Rosaceae), Eurya nitida (Theaceae) and Maesa perlarius (Maesaceae). Bioassay-guided separation of the active plant extracts led to the identification of catechin and its isomers, and several condensed tannins. Two tannin compounds showed selective inhibition activity against Ebola virus with IC50 values of 4.6 and 12.5 M, respectively, without displaying antiviral activity against the other tested viruses. Because of the nature of our initially used anti-Ebola evaluation assay system, the active compounds most likely act at the entry steps. We thus examined the binding affinity of these compounds with the potential Ebola viral glycoprotein (GP) target using molecular docking analysis. The two tannins showed high affinity to bind the GP1/GP2 complex, suggesting the GP might be the right target for this type of compounds to inhibit viral growth of Ebola. The identification of the Ebola GP inhibitors has provided strong evidence that potent anti-Ebola agents exist in the three discovered plants. The current project is designed to discover new anti-Ebola compounds from the active plants, and to determine the antiviral potential of the isolates. To achieve these objectives, the following specific aims and tasks are proposed: 1) to isolate new antiviral compounds from the identified active plant extracts and to carry out structure modification study of the active compounds; 2) to perform biological evaluation of the fractions and pure compounds generated in the current project against Ebola; 3) to elucidate the anti-Ebola targets through GP binding and cell-cell fusion interaction assay study as well as through computer docking analysis.

12103917.label: Realisation of objectives
12103917.value: The cited references refer to the following attached files in PART C (page numbers refer to the pages in Task Pane of the pdf file of the full completion report): 1. IJMS: publication No1 (p15-36); 2. Molecules: publication No2 (p37-48); 3. JOC: publication No3 (p49-66); 4. CJNM: publication No4 (p67-76); 5. ChemS: publication No5 (p77-92); 6. PhD Thesis : Student trained (Tsang Nga Yi) (p127-226); 7. MTRep: The mid-term progress report. A.1. Brief Introduction of the Anti-Ebola Active Plant Extracts The active extracts SHA0005, SHA0007, SHA0009 and SHA0255 were identified through evaluation of the anti-Ebola activity of 1,800 plant extracts prepared from the plant collection in Lingnan region. SHA0005, SHA0007, SHA0009 and SHA0255 were the methanol (MeOH) extracts made from the leaves of Agrimonia eupatoria L. (Rosaceae), the stems of Eurya nitida Korth. (Theaceae), the stems of Maesa perlarius (Loureiro) Merrill (Maesaceae), and the peach tree roots of Prunus persica (L.) Batsch (Rosaceae), respectively. The four plant extracts have been carried out in the present study to identify their anti-Ebola active components. A.2. Separation of the Plant Extracts (to fulfill Objective 1: b.1.2 and b.1.3) A total of 17 compounds were isolated from the antiviral fractions of the four plant extracts (SHA0005, SHA0007, SHA0009 and SHA0255). All the isolated compounds belong to either proanthocyanidin condensed tannins or flavan-3-ol monomers. We thus conclude that the major anti-Ebola active compounds contained in these four plants are flavan-3-ol monomers, dimers or trimers. A.2.1. Separation of SHA0009 Bioassay-guided fractionation and structure identification of the methanol extract (SHA0009) of the dry powder of the stems (5.5 kg) of M. perlarius resulted in the separation of three B-type proanthocyanidin condensed tannins (MP1-MP3), along with two flavan-3-ols [(+)-catechin (MP4) and (-)-epicatechin (MP5)]. (please see IJMS: MP1-MP5 correspond to compounds 1-5 in Figure 3 of the paper, respectively) To better understand the structure-activity relationship (SAR), additional commercially available proanthocyanidin and flavan-3-ol compounds (MP6-MP11) were obtained. (please see IJMS: MP6-MP11 correspond to compounds 6-11 in Figure 4 of the paper, respectively) A.2.2. Separation of the plant extract (SHA0255) of Prunus persica An active fraction (PPFA28) was obtained from the bioassay-guided fractionation the methanol extract (SHA0255) of the dry powder of the roots (25 kg) of P. persica. Separation of PPFA28 led to the identification of six A-type proanthocyanidin condensed tannins (PP1-PP6) including a new one (PP1). Two additional commercially available A-type proanthocyanidins (PP7 and PP8) were also obtained. (please see PhD Thesis: PP1-PP7 correspond to compounds 1-6 in Figure 13 of p73, and 18 and 19 in Figure 28 of p 133 of the thesis, respectively) A.2.3. Separation of SHA0007 Bioassay-guided fractionation and structure identification of the methanol extract (SHA0009) of the dry powder of the stems and leaves (1.8 kg) of E. nitida resulted in the separation of three flavan-3-ols [(+)-catechin (EN1), (-)-epicatechin (EN2) and epigallocatechin 3-O-gallate (EN3)] and a flavonoid glycoside [euryanoside (EN4)]. (please see MTRep: EN1-EN4 correspond to compounds ENBF 37-39 in Figure 6 of the report, respectively) A.2.4. Separation of SHA0005 Bioassay-guided fractionation and structure identification of the methanol extract (SHA0009) of the dry powder of the leaves (1.0 kg) of A. eupatoria resulted in the separation of two flavan-3-ols [(+)-catechin (AE1) and (-)-epicatechin (AE2)]. (please see MtRep: AE1 and AE2 correspond to compounds AEBF47 and AEBF48 in Figure 9 of the report, respectively) A.3. Structure Modification Based on the Active Compounds (to fulfill Objective 1: b.1.4) Both (+)-catechin and (-)-epicatechin have been isolated from the three plant extracts (SHA0005, ShA0007 and SHA0009) through bioassay-guided fractionation as active compounds. Since (-)-epicatechin showed stronger anti-Ebola activity than (+)-catechin, and it could be commercially purchased with a large quantity, the compound was selected for structure modification to obtain more active derivatives. As a result, 11 epicatechin analogues (MP12, MP13a-MP17a, MP13b-MP17b) were synthesized. (please see IJMS: MP12, MP13a-MP17a, MP13b-MP17b correspond to compounds 12, 13a-17a, and 13b-17b in Scheme 1 of the paper, respectively) A.4. Establishment of “One-Stone-Two-Birds” Antiviral Evaluation Assay (to fulfill Objective 2: b.2.2) We have established the pseudoviral protocol, referred to as “One-Stone-Two-Birds”, for evaluation of the anti-Ebola activities of the samples in our lab. The evaluation system has been used for activity screening of the samples and bioassay-guided fractionation of compound isolation from the active plant extracts. [please see IJMS: 4.5.3, 4.5.4 and 4.6; Molecules: 4.5; ChemS: Supp Inf 2.3; CJNM: p950; JOC: p5581)] A.5. Anti-Ebola Activity Evaluation (to fulfill Objective 2: b.2.2 and b.2.3) In our study, all the anti-Ebola active compounds are identified as phenolic compounds characterized as flavan-3-ol monomers, dimers and trimers, which belong to condensed tannins. We have obtained 31 different flavan-3-ol derivatives through isolation, synthesis and purchasing from commercially available source. All the compounds were evaluated for their anti-Ebola activities using our “One-Stone-Two-Birds” evaluating system. PP1-PP3, PP5, PP7, PP8, MP1 and MP6-MP9 are among the most active compounds with IC50 values in the range of 0.3-4.0 µM. Compounds PP2, PP3, PP5, MP1, MP6 and MP7 were demonstrated with low toxicities to the host cells and calculated to have selective indices of over 45. [please see PhD Thesis: the anti-Ebola activities for PP1-PP3, PP5, PP7, PP8 (Table 17 of p134); and please see IJMS: the anti-Ebola activities for MP1 and MP6-MP9 (Table 1 of the paper, respectively)] Compounds PP2, PP3, PP5, PP19, MP1, MP6 and MP7 were selected for further evaluation for their antiviral activities against infectious Ebola virus carried out in VERO E6 cells. They were found to show inhibitory effects against the Ebola “live” virus with IC50 values ranging from 0.4-5.0 µM, which are consistent to the antiviral data obtained using our “One-Stone-Two-Birds” evaluating protocol. The anti-infectious viral results further validated our antiviral assay data using the Ebola-virus-pseudotyped particles (EBOVpp). (please see IJMS: section 4.6) A.6. Elucidation of the Potential Anti-Ebola Target of the Active Compounds (to fulfill Objective 3: b.3.2 and b.3.3) The characterization of the EBOV virion structure and the availability of co-crystalized 3D structures of the Ebola viral glycoprotein (EBOV-GP) with ligands provide a basis for the molecular docking analysis. To evaluate whether EBOV-GP is the potential target of the procyanidins and its related compounds, procyanidins B1 (MP6) and B2 (MP1) were docked with the binding domains of EBOV-GP crystal structures in complex with the reported anti-EBOV compounds by using AutoDock Vina. These compounds could be docked to the binding pocket of toremifene (the known ligand of EBOV-GP) in the EBOV-GP crystal structure 5JQ7. We docked eight flavan-3-ols to the EBOV-GP binding cavity. The molecular docking results suggested that MP1 and MP6, and related compounds possibly bind to this Ebola GP cavity to destabilize the Ebola viral protein, suggesting that EBOV-GP is the potential target protein for B-type procyanidins. (please see IJMS: section 2.5) To confirm the molecular interaction of B-type procyanidins with EBOV-GP, Microscale Thermophoresis (MST) experiments were performed to measure the binding affinity of EBOV-GP and MP6. We determined the EBOV-GP Kd value for MP6 binding to EBOV-GP to be 13.0 µM, while the Kd value for toremifene (positive control) was measured as 21.4 µM, which is similar to the literature values (24.3 µM and 14 µM) reported using different assay buffer systems. The MST data revealed that EBOV-GP could be the right antiviral target for these flavan-3-ol molecules. (please see IJMS: section 2.5)

12103917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12103917.value: In the present study, we have identified potent anti-Ebola viral compounds from four plants including peach tree. These compounds possess a common structure feature belonging to flavan-3-ol derivatives. They are identified as either A- or B- type proanthocyanidin condensed tannins or flavan-3-ol monomers. Proanthocyanidin condensed tannins and flavan-3-ol monomers are common natural products, which can be found in many edible plants such as peaches and apples. To promote the phenolic compounds for their application on targeting viral infections, further research can be explored: 1) Safety is the important criteria for a hit compound to be selected for further development as a draggable agent. The toxicity and biodistribution profile of the compound may also be tested in vivo to provide safety and pharmacokinetic information, which are necessary for further preclinical antiviral investigation. 2) Because of the anti-Ebla molecular target is identified, further computational structure-based approach can be adopted to design more analogues to improve the antiviral potency. 3) Since we have identified proanthocyanidin condensed tannins as characteristic compounds of several plants, a full profiling of the antiviral compounds may provide basis to correlate the key chemicals to their antiviral activities, which will facilitate to compose a plant-based antiviral botanical product.

12103917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12103917.value: The high mortality rate caused by Ebola virus is devastating to human life in the affected regions. There are needs to develop safe and effective therapeutics to combat the virus. In the present study, a concise antiviral protocol was used to guide the separation of constituents in the roots of peach tree and other medicinal plants, leading to the identification of a number of potent anti-Ebola viral compounds. These compounds are identified with a common structure feature, characterized as flavan-3-ol monomer, dimers and trimers. The flavan-3-ol dimers and trimers are known as condensed tannins, which are found in many edible plants. Our study has demonstrated that some of the flavan-3-ols, especially the condensed tannins, could potently inhibit viral growth against both pseudotyped and infectious Ebola viruses at concentrations as low as 370 nM. We further determined that the antiviral potency of these flavan-3-ols are caused by their efficient binding on the Ebola viral glycoprotein (EBOV-GP). Because the low toxicity of the flavan-3-ols and their commonly existence in many edible plants such as apples and peaches, a botanical product with a full profiling of the antiviral compounds could be developed as a first-line defense against Ebola virus, or even other viruses.

12200217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12200217.value: This collaborative project is in line with worldwide brain-research initiatives into the connectivity and activity of large-scale complex brain cortical networks. Advanced imaging technologies have allowed to obtain both the whole brain connectome structure and cortex-wide complex dynamical patterns, for example for mice, but how the relatively static network connectivity shapes the vast repertoire of dynamics remains an elusive fundamental question. Examining the structure–dynamics relationship is important to elucidate the mechanisms of normal brain function and disorders and to develop brain-inspired computing methods and devices. Structurally, brain connectomes is a complex network with a hierarchy of modules linked by large-degree hubs and a wide range of connection strength (weight) covering orders of magnitude. Dynamically, cortical activity in intact, awake brain states displays striking scale-free avalanches characterized by a power-law distribution of activation sizes ranging from neuronal spiking to cortex-wide voltage fluctuations. We propose to study the interaction between local cortical states and the complex network connectome for the emergence of the cortex-wide scale-invariant dynamics patterns. This goal will be pursued through complementary collaborations between the expertise of the PI Dr. C.S. Zhou in the analysis and modeling of brain network connectivity and avalanches and the unique cortex-wide voltage imaging of the Co-I Prof. Thomas Knöpfel at Imperial College London. We aim to develop a dynamical network framework for data analysis and modeling to link the local cortical states to the cortex-wide scale-invariant patterns via the mouse brain connectome (data from the Allen Institute for Brain Science). From the experimental data, we hope to elucidate how the activity patterns are related to the spatial eigenmodes inherent in the underlying connectome. To obtain deeper insight into the dynamical mechanisms, we will build a large-scale cortical network model by linking biologically plausible excitation-inhibition (E-I)–balanced regional neuronal networks through the brain connectome and investigate how the spatial eigenmodes are activated differently when the local neural circuits operate in supercritical, critical, and subcritical regimes by changing the E-I balance. Hence, the proposed collaborative study addresses important and timely open issues in the dynamical network principles underlying the large-scale structure-activity relationship in the brain. A framework combining data analysis based on eigenmodes of network structure and activity patterns and the E-I network model would be useful to study the effect of altering local cortical states and network connectivity in neurodegenerative diseases or brain disorders and to search for biomarkers based on large-scale brain network dynamics. 該合作項目符合關於大型複雜腦皮質網絡的連接和活動的全球大腦研究計劃。高級成像技術已經允許獲得整個腦連接結構和皮層範圍的複雜動力學模式，例如對於小鼠，但相對靜態的網絡連接是如何塑造廣泛的動態活動模式仍然是一個難以捉摸的根本問題。研究結構動力學關係對於闡明大腦的正常功能及出現障礙的機制以及開發類腦的計算方法和設備非常重要。 在結構上，大腦連接是一個複雜的網絡，由具有大量連結的中心節點把內部連接緊密的模塊連接成層次結構， 而連接的權重覆蓋幾個數量級。 在動態活動方面，清醒的大腦狀態下皮層活動顯示出驚人的無標度雪崩，其特徵表現為從神經元發放到皮層範圍的電壓波動的激活大小呈現出冪律分佈。 我們建議研究局部皮質狀態與復雜網絡連接體之間的相互作用是如何導致出現全皮質範圍的無標度動力學模式的。這一目標將通過PI周博士在大腦網絡連接和雪崩的分析和建模的專長與倫敦帝國理工大學 （Imperial College London）的Co-I Thomas Knöpfel教授的獨特皮層電壓成像中的專業技術進行互補協作而實現。 我們的目標是發展用於數據分析和建模的動態網絡框架，以通過小鼠腦連接（來自艾倫腦科學研究所 （Allen Institute of Brain Science）的數據）將局部皮質狀態與皮層範圍的無標度模式關聯起來。從實驗數據中，我們希望闡明皮層活動模式是如何與皮層網絡連接體固有的空間本徵模式相關的。為了更深入地了解動力學機制，我們將通過鏈接網路構建大規模皮質網絡模型， 將生物學上合理​​的興奮－抑制（E-I）平衡的區域神經元網絡連結成皮層網絡，並研究當局部神經迴路通過改變E-I平衡，在超臨界、臨界和亞臨界方式下運行時，空間本徵模式的激活方式的變化。 本項目提出的合作研究將及時地幫助解決大腦中大規模結構 - 活動關係的動態網絡原理中重要的開放性問題。結合基於網絡結構和活動模式的本徵模式的數據分析框架和E-I網絡模型的框架將有助於研究在神經退行性疾​​病或腦部疾病中局部皮質狀態和網絡連接改變的作用，並尋找基於大規模腦網絡動態活動的生物標誌物。

12200217.label: Realisation of objectives
12200217.value: The overall goal of the current GRE project is to study the cortex-wide dynamical patterns and the relationship to the underlying brain network connectivity. The two objectives have been fully realized, going beyond the original design mainly focusing on mouse brain to obtain important findings in human brains. Objective 1 This objective was realized by the following subprojects: a) Hierarchical eigenmodes in human brain network and relationship to critical dynamics We developed and extended eigenmode analysis of brain network Laplacian matrix to investigate the joint contribution of hierarchical modular structural organization and critical dynamical state to brain functional diversity. We showed that the structural modes inherent to the hierarchical modular structural connectome allow a nested functional segregation and integration across multiple spatiotemporal scales. The real brain hierarchical modular organization provides large structural capacity for diverse functional interactions, which are generated by sequentially activating and recruiting the hierarchical connectome modes. Importantly, the real brain activity as measured in human fMRI is shown to operate at the critical state and this critical state can best explore the capacity provided by the eigenmodes to maximize the functional diversity. The work has been published in top journal Physical Review Letters (see [1] in Part C) b) Activity patterns in mouse brain and relationship to functional and structural networks. We have obtained the mouse structural connectome from the Allen Brain Institute. Co-I Prof. Knopfel has passed the whole-cortex voltage imaging data of 5 mice waking up from anesthesia to our group. With the datasets prepared, we have done the following analysis: i) Study the spatial and temporal complexity of brain activity. Scale-invariant dynamical patterns are the sources of spatio-temporal complexity of the brain signals, however, due to limitations in brain imaging techniques, the spatial complexity and temporal complexity are usually studied separately. Here using the high-resolution, cortex-wide voltage imaging data from the Co-I, we have studied the relationship between spatial complexity and temporal complexity and how they can assess the spatiotemporal variability of the brain signals. The results have been published in a top journal NeuroImage (see [2] in Part C). ii) Study complex waves of the cortex at anesthesia and its relationship to the underlying anatomical network Previously, spatial temporal brain patterns are studied as avalanches (spatio-temporal clusters of pixels with activation above a threshold) and the distribution of the avalanche sizes. On the other hand, the brain activities are oscillatory and are also studied as synchronized oscillations. Here, we tried to reconcile the different characterizations from the perspective of propagation waves. In collaboration with a group from Sydney University, we applied optical flow methods to obtain phase velocity field of the voltage signals across the whole cortex, which allows as to detect various types of waves, including traveling waves, sources, sinks, saddles and study the interaction of the different waves. We also discovered the relationship between the wave singularity (sources, sinks and saddles) with the underlying brain networks. The results have been published in a top neuroscience journal The Journal of Neuroscience (see [3] in Part C). c) Brain network connectome underlying dynamical patterns and metabolism The following two studies are related to the general direction of the current project, but go beyond the originally designed objectives. We further studied the network structure underlying complex patterns of chimera states and metabolism distributions in human brain. i) Spatial multi-scaled chimera states of cerebral cortex network and its inherent structure-dynamics relationship. In this work, we use neural population model to show that complex brain network structural can determine rich combination of synchronized and asynchronous states (chimera states). The network forms such states basing on the inherent effective symmetry in the underlying network structure. The work has been published in a top journal National Science Review (see [4] in Part C). ii) Benefit-risk balancing mechanism in the human brain. Human brains employ a complex underlying fiber projection network linking different brain regions to perform functions with metabolic support. Aerobic glycolysis (AG), the nonoxidative metabolism of glucose despite abundant oxygen, and crucial for various biological processes in the brain, has been found to heterogeneously distribute in the brain, especially high in regions most vulnerable to amyloid-β deposition in Alzheimer’s Disease. Using computational modelling and multimodal data from PET and fMRI, the work discovered large yet optimized wiring costs in high-AG regions (e.g., default-mode and prefrontal cortices) to support important role of these regions in functional integration. This work reveals a balancing mechanism in the brain that satisfies metabolic demand while reducing vulnerability risk. The work has been published in a top journal PNAS (see [5] in Part C). Objective 2 This objective was realized by a series of theoretical studies of local excitation-inhibition balanced neural circuits and the coupling by cortical networks to generate complex scale-free dynamics. a) Bifurcation in mean field and critical avalanches in excitation-inhibition balanced neuronal networks. We study excitation-inhibition (E-I) balanced neuronal network (N=10000 neurons) with biologically realistic synaptic kinetics. It can maintain irregular spiking dynamics with different levels of synchrony and critical avalanches emerge near the synchronous transition point. We developed a novel semi-analytical mean-field theory to derive the field equations governing the network macroscopic dynamics. It reveals that the E-I balanced state of the network manifesting irregular individual spiking is characterized by a macroscopic stable state, which can be either a fixed point or a periodic motion and the transition is predicted by a Hopf bifurcation in the macroscopic field. Furthermore, by analyzing public data, we find the coexistence of irregular spiking and critical avalanches in the spontaneous spiking activities of mouse cortical slice in vitro, indicating the universality of the observed phenomena. The results have been published in Frontiers of Systems Neuroscience (see [6] in Part C). b) Less is more in neural firing and connectivity. The brain network is notably cost-efficient, while the fundamental physical and dynamic mechanisms underlying its economical optimization in network structure and activity have not been determined. In this study, we extended the E-I network in (a) to investigate the intricate cost-efficient interplay between structure and dynamics in biologically plausible spatial modular neuronal network models representing cortical sheet. We observe that critical avalanche states from E-I balance under modular network topology with less wiring cost can also achieve lower costs in firing but with strongly enhanced response sensitivity to stimuli due to the emergence of critical state with the underlying cortical-like module connectivity. The mean-field equations in (a) was extended as coupled neural oscillators. The mechanism of low firing cost and stronger response in the form of critical avalanches is explained as a proximity to a Hopf bifurcation of the modules when increasing their connection density. The work has been published in a top journal National Science Review (see [7] in Part C). Objective 3 In this Objective we worked further to study how the composition and interaction of the waves in Objective 1 change with the brain states from anesthesia to wakefulness. We used models developed in Objective 2 to study the mechanisms of formation of complex waves due to the excitability in the local circuits and the effect of long-range connections. A manuscript has been prepared and will be submitted for publication soon (see [7] in Part C).
