12200217.label: Major findings and research outcome
12200217.value: This project has been very successful and productive to make several important findings about the dynamical properties of the brain neural circuits at local and global levels and the relationship with the underlying network structure properties. The main findings include the following aspects (1) In the local circuits, the competition and interaction of excitatory and inhibitory neurons can generate intricate dynamical modes depending on control parameters in the synaptic kinetics with time scales related to neurotransmitters. We have found that there is a transition to synchronization in the local circuits even though the firing of single neurons are sparse and irregular, random-like, reconciling the wide experimental observations of irregular spiking, neural avalanches and neural oscillations. Our novel mean field analysis revealed that the transition is related to Hopf bifurcation [6]. (2) In the mesocopic level, we showed that coupling local circuit like cortical sheet of modular network can simultaneous reduce the wiring cost and firing cost, while the network can move closer to critical state (Hopf birfucation) and be functionally much more sensitive, thus reveal the striking mechanisms of Less is More in neural systems [7]. (3) In the global whole brain level, we demonstrated that brain connectome has hierarchal modular organization [1] and it can induce the multiscale chimera states [4]. Together with critical states, the network dynamics has achieved maximal complexity [1]. The dynamical patterns propagate in the form of highly complex waves constrained by the underlying anatomical hierarchy and the temporal and spatial complexity is correlated due to such spatio-temporal wave patterns [3]. The dynamical patterns are modulated by the brain states, e.g., during the waking-up from anaesthesia [8]. (4) We demonstrated brain network is highly cost-efficient to achieve better functional value with less costs in connectivity and activity [7] and in metabolism [5] due to intricate interactions between network architecture with neural dynamics and a trade-off with the risk of metabolic waste that can lead to vulnerability for neurodegenerative diseases. These results are novel and add much deeper understanding of the structural and dynamical organization and their relationships of the neural networks at multiple levels. The results have been published in top interdisciplinary and neuroscience journals, including [1] Physical Review Letters (IF=9.227) [2] NeuroImage (IF=5.902) [3] Journal of Neuroscience (IF=5.674) [4] National Science Review (IF=16.693) [5] PNAS (IF=9.412) [6] Frontiers in Systems Neuroscience (IF, 3.20) [7] National Science Review (IF=16.693) [8] Manuscript

12200217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12200217.value: The project has created new research lines and collaborations. The analysis of hierarchal modes [1] has been extended to functional networks to quantify functional segregation, integration and their balance. We found that healthy young brains are on average at the balance of segregation and integration. In collaboration with cognitive scientist Prof. Andrea Hildebrandt from Germany, we showed that individual differences in segregation, integration and deviation from balance can predict different cognitive abilities (Wang et al, PNAS 2021). This method has great potential to study the changes of the brain with respective to development, aging and neuropsychiatric diseases and several projects are being developed to study ADHD, stress and autism using eigenmode analysis.

12200217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12200217.value: Brain is a complex dynamical network system supporting advanced functions based on the underlying network architecture, dynamics and metabolic cost. The underlying organization principles are challenging questions to be studied using interdisciplinary approaches. This project aimed to study mechanisms of critical dynamical patterns in neural networks and its relationship to underlying network structure and metabolism across different scales, using data analysis and modeling approaches from physical sciences. Our modeling revealed the dynamical transition to critical state with less cost but stronger functional value, a “less is more” strategy in the neural systems. Analyses of large-scale brain networks in mouse and human using eigemodes, entropy and waves reveal multilevel modular architecture in the brain underlying the maximally diverse dynamical patterns. The structural organization in human also reveals a trade-off in benefit and risk in metabolic requirement that can support brain function and reduce vulnerability of neurodegeneration by metabolic wastes: high demand and high risk brain areas are more optimized in the structural connections. Overall, our researches shed new light into complex brain systems, and provide analysis and modeling tools for further studies of the brain network structure and dynamics for brain cognition and diseases from the perspective of complex dynamical systems.

12200317.value: 圖像恢復中的非線性Toeplitz樣矩陣系統

12200317.label: Project Objectives
12200317.value: We study convolution structure of nonlinear Toeplitz-like matrix systems arising from image restoration with random blurs, and design efficient and effective iterative algorithms for solving such systems. We study preconditioners for these nonlinear Toeplitz-like matrix systems, and analyze the spectral property of these preconditioned systems and the convergence of the proposed iterative schemes. We study the use of dictionary learning for the representation of image covariance matrix, and analyze the proposed iterative schemes for solving the resulting sparse and nonlinear Toeplitz-like matrix systems.

12200317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12200317.value: Image Restoration is one of fundamental issues in image processing. There are many engineering and scientific applications involving image restoration problems. The image obtained from a point source under the blurring process is called the point spread function. Random blurring functions occur in many applications where the optical system's aperture or pupil itself contains random components. For instance, the randomness can be caused by fluctuations arising from atmospheric turbulence in astronomical systems, vibration of the optical instrument or jittering in scanning process in optical systems. The mathematical formulation for solving such image restoration problem needs to deal with both noise sources in point spread functions and in observed images. Therefore the covariance matrices of noises and the original image are required in the resulting optimization model. The main challenge is to solve very large nonlinear matrix systems especially when there are multiple image frames and the number of image pixels is large. For example, when the size of image is 1000-by-1000 and the number of frames is 10, then the size of the involved matrix can be 10 millons-by-10 millions. Our main focus will be proposing new numerical linear algebra solvers for nonlinear matrix systems arising from image restoration with random blurs, and developing efficient and effective solution methods for these matrix systems. Our contributions are to propose new algorithms and analyze their theoretical convergence properties. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first attempt to study and analyze circulant preconditioners for nonlinear Toeplitz-like matrix systems. Our idea is to study the convolution structure in matrix systems arising from the system of random time-varying point spread functions. By making use of Topelitz-like structure, both computational and storage cost can be significantly reduced by using Fast Fourier Transforms. Also we construct circulant preconditioners for these nonlinear matrix systems. Theoretically, we analyze the spectral properties of these preconditioned matrices, and study the convergence of these preconditioned nonlinear Topelitz-like matrix systems. On the other hand, we propose to use of sparse dictionary learning for the representation of image covariance matrix. The nonlinear matrix systems are required to be solved. Since their coefficient matrices and right hand side vectors have sparse and displacement structures respectively, we will develop an efficient iterative algorithm for solving these nonlinear matrix systems and conduct the convergence analysis of the proposed iterative scheme. 圖像恢復是圖像處理的一個基本問題。有許多涉及圖像恢復問題的工程和科學應用。圖片從模糊過程中的點源獲得的點被稱為點擴散功能。隨機模糊功能發生在許多光學應用中系統的孔徑或瞳孔本身包含隨機組件。例如，隨機性可能是由大氣湍流引起的波動引起的天文系統，光學儀器的振動或掃描過程中的抖動在光學系統中。用於解決這種圖像恢復的數​​學公式問題需要處理點擴散功能中的噪聲源和觀察到的圖片。因此，需要噪聲和原始圖像的協方差矩陣在最終的優化模型中。主要的挑戰是解決非常大的非線性問題矩陣系統特別是當有多個圖像幀和數量時圖像像素大。例如，當圖像的大小為1000-by-1000時，幀數為10，那麼所涉及的矩陣的大小可以是1千萬乘1千萬。 我們的主要焦點將是為非線性提出新的數值線性代數解算器矩陣系統產生的圖像恢復隨機模糊，並開發這些矩陣系統的高效和有效的解決方法。 我們的貢獻是提出新算法並分析其理論收斂性。 到了據我們所知，這是首次研究和分析循環利用的嘗試非線性Toeplitz樣矩陣系統的預處理器。 我們的想法是研究由隨機時變點擴散函數係統產生的矩陣系統中的捲積結構。 通過使用Topelitz樣結構，通過使用可以顯著降低計算和存儲成本快速傅里葉變換。 此外，我們為這些非線性構建循環預處理器矩陣系統。 理論上，我們分析這些預處理的光譜特性矩陣，並研究這些預處理非線性Topelitz樣的收斂矩陣系統。另一方面，我們建議使用稀疏字典學習來表示的圖像協方差矩陣。 非線性矩陣系統需要解決。由於它們的係數矩陣和右手側向量有稀疏的，位移結構，我們將開發一種有效的迭代算法求解這些非線性矩陣系統並對所提出的迭代方案進行收斂分析。

12200317.label: Realisation of objectives
12200317.value: In this project. we investigated into convolution structure of nonlinear Toeplitz-like matrix systems arising from image denoising and restoration applications. In these applications, the main computational problem is to solve the resulting matrix systems. We developed iterative algorithms for solving such systems. The convergence of the iterative schemes was established. Numerical examples of image denoising and restoration were presented to show the efficiency of our proposed methods. It is shown that the computation can be significantly reduced by comparing with the other methods in the literature. Moreover, we analyzed the use of dictionary learning for the representation of image covariance matrix. We developed iterative algorithms, which are able to solve the resulting sparse and nonlinear matrix systems in image denoising and restoration applications. We compared our algorithms with current algorithms. The experimental results show the superiority of our methods.

12200317.label: Major findings and research outcome
12200317.value: In research output [2], we studied convolution structure of nonlinear systems involving the sum of a Kullback-Leibler divergence term and a total variation term, and designed efficient and effective iterative algorithms for solving such systems. In research output [1,3], we studied iterative algorithms for solving minimization problems with non-differentiability of the L-infinity norm and image decomposition based on cartoon and texture. A semi-smooth Newton method and primal-dual method are employed to solve these nonlinear systems. The convergence of the proposed iterative schemes is analyzed. Numerical comparisons between our approach and several state-of-the-art algorithms are presented to demonstrate the efficiency of our proposed algorithms. In research output [4], we investigated into a Peaceman–Rachford splitting method with monotone plus skew-symmetric splitting for nonlinear saddle point problems which arise from image restoration applications. The convergence of the proposed algorithm is guaranteed under some mild assumptions, e.g., the strict convexity on objective functions and the consistency on constraints, even though the Lions–Mercier property is not fulfilled. In research output [5,6,7], we studied image denoising and restoration problems based on (i) structured dictionary learning and sparsity [5], (ii) tensor factorization with total variation regularization [6], (iii) saturation-value total variation in color imaging applications [7]. The global convergence of the proposed algorithms for solving the models was established. We also designed a fast implementation for the proposed algorithms. Numerical results were reported to demonstrate the better performance of our developed algorithms compared with the state-of-the-art methods.

12200317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12200317.value: Image smoothing is a longly-studied research area with tremendous approaches proposed. However, how to perform high-quality image smoothing with less computational cost still remains a challenging problem. In the future work, we try to solve this problem with our developed techniques for a newly global optimization based method named quasi weighted least squares. In our plan, the 2D image is first re-ordered into a 1D vector via a newly proposed 2D-to-1D transformation. We then properly remove some neighborhood connections in the original 2D neighborhood system. The remaining neighboring pixels can then form 1D neighborhood connections in the transformed 1D vector while they still contain the 2D neighborhood information in the original 2D image space. These together result in a quite compact linear system which can be easily solved. An efficient solver based on our developed techniques is further developed, which leads our method into a fast global image smoothing operator. The efficiency and effectiveness of our future research plan will be validated through comprehensive experiments in several image smoothing tasks.

12200317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12200317.value: Image restoration is one of fundamental issues in image processing. There are many engineering and scientific applications involving image restoration problems. The mathematical formulation for solving such image restoration problem needs to deal with both noise sources in point spread functions and in observed images. Therefore the covariance matrices of noises and the original image are required in the resulting optimization model. The main challenge is to solve very large nonlinear matrix systems. We have successfully developed numerical linear algebra solvers for solving large systems and used . dictionary learning for image restoration and image smoothing. Applications of our methods for image smoothing are important. We therefore expect our methods to be profitable across many tasks of both computer vision and computational photography.

12200817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12200817.value: A spatial influence query aims to find the influence zone or influence objects (e.g., customers) of a spatial facility (e.g., a store outlet) with respect to certain spatial criteria (e.g., reverse nearest neighbor). Owing to its broad applications in decision support, market analysis, social media advertising and recommender systems, the problem of spatial influence queries has been studied extensively in the literature. However, most of existing work focuses on spatial proximity only. With the rapid development of location-based services (LBS), a large number of spatial facilities/objects have been enriched with text information (e.g., categorical descriptions or user-generated reviews). So far, little attention has been paid to spatial influence queries for such spatial-textual facilities/objects. In this project, we propose a novel query paradigm -- keyword-based spatial influence query -- to retrieve the influence zone or influence object set of a spatial-textual facility on the basis of both spatial proximity and textual similarity. Specifically, we plan to study three representative keyword-based spatial influence queries: 1) keyword-based influence region search; 2) keyword-based influence set search; 3) maximizing keyword-based influence region/set search. We show the technical challenges of processing these queries. We plan to develop new index-based search methods and approximate algorithms for fast query evaluation. Cost models and query optimization techniques will also be investigated. In addition, we plan to build a map-based demonstration system to showcase the algorithms and techniques developed in this project. 空間影響查詢旨在針對某些空間標準（例如，反向最近鄰）找到给定空间设施的影響區域或影響對象集。由於其在決策支持、市場分析、社交媒體廣告和推薦系統等領域的廣泛應用，大量文献已对该查詢問題进行了深入的研究。然而，現有的大部分工作只關注於空間临近性。隨著位置服務（LBS）的快速發展，大量的空間設施/對像已經关联了豐富的文本信息，如分類描述或用戶評論等。目前，對這種空間文本設施/對象的空間影響查詢研究还处于起步阶段。在本項目中，我們提出了一種新穎的基于關鍵詞的空間影響查詢，其目标是在空間鄰近性和文本相似性的基礎上檢索空間文本設施的影響區域或影響對象集。具體來說，我們計劃研究三個代表性的關鍵詞空間影響查詢：1）基於關鍵詞的影響區域搜索; 2）基於關鍵詞的影響对象集搜索; 3）最大化基於關鍵詞的影響區域/對象搜索。针对處理這些查詢的技術挑战，我們計劃提出新的基於索引的搜索方法和近似算法進行快速查詢評估。我们也将研究代价模型和查詢優化技術。另外，我們計劃開發一個基於地圖的演示系統，以展示本項目開發的算法和技術。

12200817.label: Realisation of objectives
12200817.value: The project objectives have been successfully realized. With the continued proliferation of location-based services (LBS), a growing number of web-accessible objects are geotagged and have text descriptions. We have formulated the MaxiZone problem that finds the keyword set maximizing the influence zone of a specified query object. In order to solve the MaxiZone problem efficiently, we have proposed a series of new algorithms. When the candidate keyword set W is small, it is possible to examine all the subsets of W and return the keyword set having the maximum influence zone. Due to the complexity of the problem, when the candidate keyword set W is large, examining the subsets of W one by one incurs an extremely high cost. Thus, we have presented three optimization techniques by the utilization of spatial, textual and influence zone characteristics to reduce the computation cost. Moreover, to trade the quality of the answer for the running time, we have proposed a sampling-based algorithm. It gets the final result by sampling high-quality keyword subsets from the whole keyword space, which can return the result with high approximation in reasonable time. In addition, we have extended the proposed algorithms to address a variant of MaxiZone problem called t-MaxiZone problem, which finds the top-t keyword sets having the maximum influence zones. Extensive empirical study using real-world datasets demonstrates the effectiveness and efficiency of our proposed algorithms. Another important query over geo-textual data is the direction-aware spatial keyword query that aims to retrieve the top-k objects that best match query parameters in terms of spatial distance and textual similarity in a given query direction. In some cases, it can be difficult for users to specify appropriate query parameters. After getting a query result, users may find some desired objects are unexpectedly missing and may therefore question the entire result. Enabling why-not questions in this setting may aid users to retrieve better results, thus improving the overall utility of the query functionality. To this end, we have studied the direction-aware why-not spatial keyword top-k query problem. We have proposed efficient query refinement techniques to revive missing objects by minimally modifying users’ direction- aware queries. We prove that the best refined query directions lie in a finite solution space for a special case and reduce the search for the optimal refinement to a linear programming problem for the general case. Extensive experimental studies demonstrate that the proposed techniques outperform a baseline method by two orders of magnitude and are robust in a broad range of settings. We have also studied the continuous k nearest neighbor (COkNN) query in the obstructed space, which retrieves k obstructed nearest neighbors (ONNs) for every point on a query segment q. The state-of-the-art approach, called Euclidean based CONN (E-CONN), exploits an R-tree to traverse the data set P in ascending order of their Euclidean distances to q. Taking a different point of view, we have explored the idea of Voronoi diagram to define the notion of obstructed Voronoi diagram (OVD). The Voronoi cells with obstacles are divided into visible and invisible regions for quickly answering nearest neighbor queries. To facilitate efficient retrieval of Voronoi cells and processing of continuous nearest neighbor (CONN) queries, we have proposed a new grid-based index, called Voronoi diagram with Obstacles in Grid (VO-Grid), which indexes Voronoi cells and associated obstacle information with a grid file. Based on VO-Grid, we have developed an efficient algorithm, called CONN with VO-Grid Acceleration (CONN-VOA), to accelerate the CONN query processing. Moreover, we have extended CONN-VOA to the COkNN query, which explores effective filtering and early termination for reducing redundant access of data objects. In addition, we have studied the keyword-based community search problem over attributed graph data and keyword-aware route planning queries for indoor venues. An efficient system, called iZone, has been developed for determining influence zones over geo- textual data. Specifically, iZone allows users to browse geo-textual objects, evaluate the influence zones of specified geo-textual objects, and obtain explanations of the evaluation results. The system integrates two types of spatial keyword search, namely top-k spatial keyword query and reverse top-k keyword-based location query. A variety of spatial indexes have been employed to enhance the efficiency of the system.

12200817.label: Major findings and research outcome
12200817.value: We have identified and formulated a set of keyword-based spatial queries for LBS applications, including influence zone maximization query, direction-aware spatial keyword search, keyword-based community search, and keyword-aware indoor route planning query. To efficiently answer these queries, we have proposed a number of index-based search and pruning techniques. We have also proposed sampling-based approximate solutions and a series of spatial distance-based and textual similarity-based optimization techniques to expedite query processing. Cost modelling and empirical studies have been carried out for performance evaluation and analysis. In addition, we have developed a demonstration system that allows users to evaluate the influence zones of geo-textual objects and obtain explanations of the evaluation results. The research findings have been published in the top-tier conferences and journals including ACM TSAS, IEEE TKDE, and IEEE ICDE.

12200817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12200817.value: For further development, it would be interesting to investigate more variants of the spatial influence query problem. For example, the problem can be extended to consider multiple target objects. This is the case if a business has multiple branches at different locations and wants to identify the best keyword set for all the locations. Moreover, instead of assuming a Euclidean data space, we may consider road networks as the underlying space. Another variant worth investigation is that the potential customers of a target object can be mobile users. In this scenario, frequent updates in the spatial indexes are needed. This brings new challenges, and new algorithms based on safe zones or similar concepts need to be designed. In addition, distributed and parallel computing techniques can be explored to expedite query processing.

12200817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12200817.value: A spatial influence query aims to find the influence zone or influence objects (e.g., customers) of a spatial facility (e.g., a store outlet) with respect to certain spatial criteria (e.g., reverse nearest neighbor). Owing to its broad applications in decision support, market analysis, social media advertising and recommender systems, the problem of spatial influence queries has been studied extensively in the literature. However, most of existing work focuses on spatial proximity only. With the rapid development of location- based services (LBS), a large number of spatial facilities/objects have been enriched with text information (e.g., categorical descriptions or user-generated reviews). So far, little attention has been paid to spatial influence queries for such spatial-textual facilities/objects. In this project, we have studied keyword-based spatial queries that retrieve the influence zone or influence object set of a spatial-textual facility on the basis of both spatial proximity and textual similarity. We have developed new index-based search methods and approximate algorithms to efficiently answer the queries. We have also developed a demonstration system to showcase the proposed algorithms and techniques.

12200917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12200917.value: 在線社交網絡已成為人們傳播信息，思想和影響力的重要平臺。受社交媒體營銷和用戶行為預測等應用的驅動，社交網絡分析的一個重點研究是利用圖論知识調查社交網絡的結構。然而，隱私問題成為社交網絡分析的一個主要考慮因素。據最近的一項研究報導1140萬的紐約市臉書用戶中有52.6％的人隱藏了他們的朋友列表。這種隱私保護導致了一種新型的圖形模型，稱為公有/私有圖。這個新模型包含一個公有的圖，其中每個節點拥有一個私有圖。公有圖對所有人都是可見的，但每一個私有圖都是僅限對應用戶可見。從每個用戶的角度來看，整個社交網絡圖正好是公有圖和用戶自己的私有圖的一個並集。由於大規模的公有/私有社交網絡特性，許多圖查詢問題無法使用傳統技術進行有效地回答。為了克服這些障礙，在這個項目中，我們打算对公有/私有社會網絡分析進行全面的調查。研究內容主要包括以下幾個方面：1）公有/私有社交網絡建模; 2）設計有效的查詢處理算法，解決社區搜索和關鍵字搜索等問題; 3）對所提出的算法在真實生活數據上進行性能評估; 4）開發原型系統，以證明我們的建議的可行性。

12200917.label: Realisation of objectives
12200917.value: The four objectives of this project are: design a public-private graph model, collect real datasets, develop and evaluate the efficient algorithms for tackling three public-private computing tasks, and also implement a prototype system. We have designed a new graph model for public-private networks, construct four PP-DBLP datasets, develop several new algorithms for efficient community search and keyword search over large public-private graphs, and also conducted comprehensive evaluations and graph analytics demonstration systems, as detailed in the major findings and research outcome.

12200917.label: Major findings and research outcome
12200917.value: The major findings and research outcome of this project can be summarized as follows. First, we propose efficient algorithms for finding k-truss in public-private graphs. We develop a classification-based hybrid strategy of novel node insertions and edge insertions to incrementally compute k-truss in public-private graphs. Therefore, several truss-based community search can be efficiently computed in different networks, e.g., undirected graphs, directed graphs, weighted graphs, and also attributed graphs, leveraging our fast techniques of public-private k-truss discovery in IJCAI'19. Second, we propose a new keyword search framework, called public-private keyword search (PPKWS), to support three representative semantics of keyword search from the public graph and the query user's private graph. We devise an efficient framework of partial evaluation, answer refinement, and answer completion in PPKWS. Experiments show that PPKWS runs 113 times faster than the straightforward querying algorithms running on the public-private network from scratch in ICDE'20. Third, we have generated and publicly released four public-private networks PP-DBLP, which take published articles as public information and regard ongoing collaborations as hidden information in ICDMW'18. Fourth, we study several efficient community search and detection algorithms in different graphs (e.g., attributed graphs, directed graphs, and weighted graphs) and present our finding results in AAAI'18, ICDE'19, ICDE'20, WISE'19, TKDE'20, SIGMOD'20, and VLDBJ'20. Fifth, we investigate many efficient graph analytics algorithms (e.g., distance-generalized core decomposition, structural diversity search, and graph summarization) and report our finding results in CIKM'17, WISE'19, CIKM'20, WWWJ'21, and PVLDB'21. Sixth, we develop and implement the prototype systems for community search and graph analytics in ICDE'18 and PVLDB'20.

12200917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12200917.value: The efficient algorithms for public-private graph analytics have been investigated in this project. However, there exist several opportunities for further investigation, e.g., how to further improve the efficiency of query processing on public-private graphs and how to support more queries based on other kinds of dense subgraphs in different applications. We will further explore these issues in the area of public-private social network analytics.

12200917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12200917.value: With the wide application of online social networks (Facebook, Twitter, and Google+), the process of investigating social structures using network and graph theory has become a focal point of research, which has applications in social media marketing and user behavior prediction. However, privacy issues present a major concern in the algorithmic analysis of social networks, e.g., 52.6% of 1.4 million New York City Facebook users hid their friend's list. The privacy protection leads to a novel graph model of public-private network, where each user has his/her own private network. This project studies new problems of public-private network analytics. We propose efficient algorithms to tackle them. For instance, we have proposed fast indexing-based algorithms for identifying truss-based communities and answering keyword search queries in public-private networks. To validate the efficiency and quality of proposed methods, we have collected and generated real-world public-private DBLP datasets, which are also publicly available. The prototyped graph analytics systems are also developed for people to use. Our findings are reported in reputed international journals and top international conferences.

12202117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12202117.value: 策略性地運用數據和相關領域的先驗知識，對於大數據的預測性分析是非常重要的。研究如何將海量的異構數據和相關領域先驗知識進行整合，從而保證研究分析結果的可靠性和準確性，是非常重要的研究課題。基於以上，本研究主要針對在臨床環境下的異構數據：（1）開源的深切治療（ICU）數據庫：MIMIC–III（包含了病人在不同ICU治療期間所記錄的臨床事件）；（2）公開的國際標準醫學本體論，例如：ICD-9，SNOMED-CT, LOINC 等。為了整合上述兩種異構數據，本研究對ICU數據庫中臨床事件和醫學本體論進行聯合嵌入。具體來說，我們首先應用表徵學習方法得到臨床事件（序列數據）的向量表示；再利用醫學本體論（知識圖譜）進一步建模，將臨床事件嵌入到最終的共同向量空間得到臨床實體，這樣可以將ICU數據和醫學本體論整合起來。 既將原本在不同向量空間中的異構數據（不同種類的臨床事件，例如：診斷，藥品等），聯合嵌入到臨床實體所在的共同向量空間，同時得到基於醫學本體論的臨床事件和臨床實體的對應關系。為了支持多種醫療保健預測性分析（例如：死亡率的預測），我們還得到從異構空間（臨床事件）到最終共同向量空間（臨床實體）的投影。在醫療應用中安全性致為重要，所以除了預測性分析的準確率，我們更加強調模型的可解釋。我們結合稀疏性和注意力機制提出多種增強模型可解釋性的方案，以發掘出更可靠的候選表型。我們將會基於MIMIC-III進行實驗，並對多種方法的性能進行比較。除了廣泛應用的量化評價標準，我們將與臨床醫生就從數據中發掘出來的表型的可解釋性進行相關探討。

12202117.label: Realisation of objectives
12202117.value: Objective 1 To develop a representation learning methodology that can simultaneously infer the embedding spaces of heterogeneous clinical events found in the EHR data and evaluate the performance. A representation methodology has been developed which can simultaneously infer the embedding spaces of diagnoses, medications and lab tests for diagnosis prediction. While it is supervised model, we added a regularization term to respect also the co-occurrence statistics within the “context” (hospital admission) and found improvement in the generalization performance of the model learned. In addition, we found that integrating the heterogeneous clinical events (in particular, diagnoses and medications) could have some further improvement on accuracy, though very significant. Related results have been reported in [IJCAI’19]. During the investigation, we also notice that different medications prescribed within a hospital admission are corresponding to different diagnoses, which are commonly assumed in most of the related works as the correspondence information is simply absent. We further propose another methodology which integrates tensor factorization (non-negative Poisson CP in particular) and another representation learning approach based recurrent neural networks to learn the embeddings of the clinical concepts and their correspondence jointly, leading to better performance for prediction analytics tasks like mortality prediction. Related results have been reported in [IJCAI’18][AAAI’19]. In addition, we have tried to model the local and global context using RNNs, which was found effective in imputing missing values in EHR data for more accurate predictive analytics [JHIR'20]. To summarize, the results we obtained do show that the representation learning methodologies we developed can simultaneously infer the embedding spaces of heterogeneous clinical events found in the EHR data, can achieve the state-of-the-art results. Objective 2 To develop medical knowledge graphs and their embeddings based on some existing medical ontologies of international standards including ICD-9, SNOMED-CT and LOINC and evaluate the performance. ICD-9 is essentially a hierarchical categorization of diseases and SNOMED-CT contains also relationships between different types of medical concepts (e.g., medications and diagnoses). We have investigated different state-of-the-art methods and developed a particular methodology for learning the knowledge graphs based on ICD-9 and SNOMED-CT. They are then used to achieve the next objective of developing a unified framework to learn a joint embedding of clinical event sequences and medical knowledge graphs. [IJCAI’19] SNOMED-CT is much larger than ICD-9 and contains a rich set of medical concepts. Linkage between two medical concepts can be revealed by not only having one edge but a short path with multiple relations. Also, the phenotypes may contain more information. So far, most of the existing work considers phenotypes characterized by diagnoses and medications, leaving the other medical concepts untouched. We managed to incorporate the knowledge graph embedding learned based on SNOMED-CT where multiple relationship types between medical concepts can be better leveraged. We found that the properly incorporating the relationship knowledge for the joint learning of embedding can lead to much more reasonable organization of the embedding space. A paper reporting the achievement is in preparation. Objective 3 To develop a unified framework to learn a joint embedding of clinical event sequences and medical knowledge graphs for patient outcome prediction and evaluate the performance. Towards joint learning clinical event sequences and medical knowledge graphs for patient outcome prediction, we have investigated a number of related state-of-the-art methods. We noticed that most of the existing works assume that medical concepts under the same ontological category should share similar representations, which however does not always hold if the representations learned are to be consistent with on their occurrence statistics in the EHR data. One of the main reasons behind is that categorizations in different medical ontologies are developed based on different considerations and objectives, instead of prediction accuracy. To alleviate this problem, we first relax the aforementioned assumption by allowing nodes close to one another in the ontologies not necessarily close in the embedding space. To achieve so, we borrow the idea of “multi-sense” from word embedding to allow each of the non-leaf nodes to carry multiple semantic meanings. To be more specific, we learn multiple vector-based representations, instead of only one, for the non-leaf nodes in the ontologies, and each of these representations is expected to correspond to a distinct “sense” and capture a particular group of lower level medical concepts with closer semantic meanings as reflected in the EHR data. Our proposed model, named Medical concept embedding using Multiple Ontological Representations (MMORE), integrates the EHR co-occurrence statistics and the predictive task to produce more generalizable and interpretable representations. [IJCAI’19] We have also extended the MMORE to AutoMORE where the splitting process of the medical concepts can be achieved automatically. In addition, an attention mechanism was adopted to adaptively integrate multiple medical ontologies, including ICD-10 and SNOMED-CT with promising results in terms of higher accuracy and embedding space organization. A paper reporting the achievement is in preparation. Objective 4 To incorporate sparsity and attention mechanism tricks into the proposed representation learning framework to improve the interpretability of the inferred models and evaluate the performance. Several sparsity and attention mechanism tricks have been explored in the methodologies we developed and are found useful in identifying more interpretable phenotype patterns. For instance, the adoption of non-negative Poisson CP tensor factorization can make the phenotypes sparse and more distinct from each other (thus improve interpretability) [IJCAI’18][AAAI’19][TKDE’20]. Also, we applied attention mechanisms to both the embeddings learned based on ontology and the embeddings learned based on EHR data so as to more accurately pinpoint the medical concepts associated with the latent phenotype patterns embedded in the EHR data via learning [IJCAI’19]. We have also extended the attention mechanism to multiple medical ontologies, including ICD and SNOMED-CT with promising results in terms of higher accuracy and embedding space organization. A paper reporting the achievement is in preparation. In addition, PU-learning trick has been used to handle the missing value challenge in EHR data with promising results [KDD’20]. Objective 5 To conduct rigorous quantitative and qualitative evaluation of the proposed algorithms using the MIMIC III Critical Care Database for predictive tasks like mortality prediction and for high-throughput candidate phenotype generation. Rigorous quantitative evaluation has been conducted based on the MIMIC III dataset to demonstrate the effectiveness of each of the methodologies we developed as compared to the state-of-the-art methods on mortality prediction, next diagnosis prediction, length-of-stay prediction, and so on. For the candidate phenotype generated, we have conducted some case studies for evaluating their correctness of the phenotypes inferred. We have also conducted a more comprehensive qualitative evaluation. The clinical relevancy of the extracted by the algorithms has been confirmed by clinicians via a carefully designed qualitative evaluation. The results have been reported in [TKDE’20].

12202117.value: A number of effective algorithms for computational phenotyping and EHR predictive analytics have been developed based on representation learning and tensor factorization paradigms. 12202117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12202117.value: The increasing EHR adoption rate has resulted in a lot of opportunities for predictive analytics in healthcare. Yet, the healthcare process is complex and how to proper integrate heterogeneous EHR data (with diagnoses, lab test results, treatment) and medical ontologies is lacking sufficient attention, partially due to its interdisciplinary nature. In this project, we formed an interdisciplinary research team and carefully investigated different possibilities to make use of the representation learning paradigms for integrating sequential EHR data (observational) and medical ontologies (prior knowledge) for both computational phenotyping and predictive analytics. A number of effective data analytic algorithms have been developed to address the identified challenges related to the integration, and have demonstrated to be effective via rigorous empirical evaluation. We believe that the outcomes of this project can contribute to the field of healthcare data analytics, and at the same time can trigger more attention to the importance of in-depth healthcare machine learning studies.

12202417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12202417.value: With a world increasing more divided and protesting becoming the norm for expressing differences in opinion, the growing concern in public security has sparked heated interest in understanding crowd behaviours from the computer science perspective. Specifically, technologies to automatically recognize abnormal crowd behaviour could provide valuable information on individual and crowd dynamics, thus opening up for wide range of public security applications such as abnormality detection, vandalism deterrence, and traffic flow management. The key issue in abnormal crowd behaviour recognition has been to capture the dynamics of human activities in video sequences, where the smooth, nonlinear dynamics are natural characteristics in applying manifold learning methods that simulate human visual perception. However, manifold learning’s lack of explicit nonlinear mapping function limits its capacity in projecting the incoming data on the learned subspace, thus plagues further processing of the data. The limitation can be combat by integrating deep learning into the solution, with it providing natural nonlinear mapping function through simulating the physical structure and propagation of information in human visual cortex. The integrated model mimics both the way of perceiving and the architecture of the human visual system, thus is capable of providing human-like judgment in video understanding tasks. In many real-world applications, multiple cameras from different views are deployed to monitor crowd behaviours in a certain place. In this case, data generally lie on multiple video manifolds. Even in a single video clip, multiple human activities, which are the components of the same crowd behaviour, may occur simultaneously. Moreover, the rareness of abnormal crowd behaviours makes the datasets highly imbalanced. To date, there has been neither manifold learning nor deep learning scheme to model the abnormal crowd behaviours observed from multiple cameras. To discover compact and meaningful features from multi-camera videos for abnormal crowd behaviour recognition, this project works towards developing novel manifold learning mechanisms under the deep architecture. For the video from a single camera, we investigate a multi-label deep manifold learning method to characterize multiple human activities within a single manifold. For videos taken from different cameras, we explore the multi-label multi-view deep manifold learning strategy to extract the common semantic features hidden behind different visual appearances. In order to identify abnormal crowd behaviours, we further exploit the imbalanced multi-label multi-view deep manifold learning model. We will perform evaluations on both synthetic and public standard datasets and distribute our software freely for verification and comparison from fellow researchers. 随着当今社会对公共安全要求的不断提高，从计算机科学的角度理解群体行为并对其进行建模引起了越来越多的关注。有效的群体异常行为识别技术能够提供个体动态以及群体交互的重要信息，从而在公共安全领域，例如异常行为检测、交通流量管理等方面有着广泛的应用。 在群体异常行为识别的研究中，如何对视频中的个体以及群体动态过程进行建模是最重要的问题之一。作为基于人类视觉感知的非线性特征提取方法，流形学习在视频动态特征的建模中展现了很好的潜力。然而，缺乏显式映射函数使得流形学习在面对新数据时缺乏灵活性。该局限性可以通过与深度学习进行融合而弥补，因为深度学习通过模仿人类视觉皮层的物理结构与信息传播模式，提供了显式的非线性映射函数。融合了深度结构的流形学习框架从物理层面与感知层面对人类视觉系统进行了模拟，从而能够提供针对视频理解任务的类脑计算模式。 在许多实际应用中，同一场景往往由多个摄像头进行监控。在此情形下，数据将分布于多个视频流形上。即使对于单视角的视频片段，群体行为也通常由多种个体行为所组成。此外，异常行为的样本极少，因此造成了数据的高度非平衡性。目前尚未有合适的深度流形学习方法对基于多视角的群体异常行为进行建模。 基于以上分析，该项目致力于研发新颖的深度流形学习模型与算法，以抽取多视角视频数据中富有意义的简洁特征，并据此进行群体异常行为识别。对于单视角的视频数据，我们拟提出一种多标签深度流形学习算法对单流形中的多种行为进行建模。对于多视角的视频数据，我们拟提出一种多标签多视角深度流形学习算法来提取不同视角的共同语义特征。为了识别群体异常行为，我们拟提出非平衡多标签多视角深度流形学习算法。我们将在仿真数据集与真实数据集上对所提出算法进行验证，并免费提供相关算法代码下载。

12202417.label: Realisation of objectives
12202417.value: This project aimed to propose a series of deep manifold learning models with the imbalance, multi-label, and multi-view settings for video action/behavior recognition. To achieve the abovementioned goal in a progressive manner, we started from the investigation of a novel manifold learning method with the multi-label setting on a classical visual learning task -- image classification. Specifically, we proposed a novel approach called sparse multi-label bilinear embedding on Stiefel manifolds for supervised dimensionality reduction on multi-label visual data. Unlike the traditional multi-label dimensionality reduction algorithms that worked on the vectorized data, the proposed method directly took the higher-order tensor representation of visual data as the input, and thus well characterized the spatial structure of the data. Differentiating from the existing tensor-based dimensionality reduction methods that performed the eigen-decomposition in each iteration, the proposed method utilized a gradient ascent strategy to optimize the objective function in each iteration, and thus was more efficient. Moreover, we introduced column-orthonormal constraints to the transformation matrices to eliminate the redundancy between the projection directions of the learned subspace and added an L1-norm regularizer to the objective function to enhance the interpretability of the learned subspace. Experiments on a standard multi-label image dataset validated the effectiveness of the proposed method. Building upon the above investigation, we further explored how to address the multi-view and imbalanced data. To model the data with multiple views/modalities, we proposed a unified objective function to optimize the projections from different views/modalities simultaneously by discovering the common subspace for all given data views/modalities. Moreover, a modality consistency preserving criterion was introduced into the objective function to take into account the intrinsic consistency between different data views/modalities via linear transformations. Furthermore, a local geometry preserving component was embedded into the proposed objective function to characterize the manifold structure of the given datasets. To deal with the imbalanced data, we developed a so-called harmonized discriminant information preserving objective, which aimed to emphasize the minority classes with higher importance by automatically adjusting the weights of different classes in the learning process. By integrating the goals of modality consistency preserving, local geometry preserving, and harmonized discriminant information preserving as mentioned above, we formulated a generalized eigen-decomposition optimization problem and directly obtained the closed-form solution. Further, we explored the proposed model under the multi-task, metric learning, and graph learning settings, so as to extend its usability in various learning scenarios. Experiments on standard video datasets and social media datasets validated the effectiveness of the proposed methods. A common challenge in learning with the aforementioned multi-label, multi-view, nonlinear, high-dimensional, and imbalanced data is the difficulty in capturing the complex data structures, dependencies, and relationships, such as the intrinsic relationships between the low-level appearances and high-level semantics of video data, and the multi-scale dependencies and highly nonlinear behaviors existing in more general spatiotemporal data and complex dynamical systems. Deep learning is a powerful tool to model such complex data relations and has achieved incredible success over the past years. However, given a specific learning task and the corresponding dataset, how to appropriately determine the desired configuration of a deep model, theoretically analyze the model’s learning behavior, and quantitatively characterize the model’s learning capacity remains a mystery. In order to make good use of the powerful representation ability of deep learning to further enhance the performance of the proposed methods while providing the theoretical support and meaningful interpretations of the model design, we introduced a comprehensive framework for deep learning model design and information-theoretic analysis. First, we developed a novel Interactively- and Integratively-connected Deep Recurrent Neural Network model as a baseline. This model consisted of three key modules: (i) an Input module to integrate data from heterogeneous sources; (ii) a Hidden module to capture the information at different scales while allowing the information to flow interactively between layers; and (iii) an Output module to model the integrative effects of information from various hidden layers to generate the output predictions. Second, to further enhance the learning effectiveness and efficiency on datasets with complex dependencies and relationships, we designed a learning procedure that behaved in a progressive and adaptive manner (referred to as progressive learning) based on the developed baseline model. Specifically, it adapted and updated between feature selection and model learning in an iterative and integrative way to optimally achieve the learning objective for the given dataset and task. As a reuslt, the proposed model was capable of carrying out the learning task with the right information through the right model at the right time; in other words, it dynamically extracted the most crucial information from the complex data and utilized it to the maximum extent by adaptively constructing/updating appropriate learning modules. Third, to prove the learning ability of the designed model and learning procedure, we introduced an information-theoretic framework to examine the underlying learning behavior of the proposed model. In so doing, we provided a possible solution to one of the open questions in deep learning, that is, how to determine the necessary and sufficient configurations of a certain designed deep learning model with respect to the given learning datasets. To validate the theoretically derived results and the effectiveness of the proposed approach, we examined the learning behavior of our model on synthetic datasets with varying levels of complexity, and compared it with state-of-the-art learning methods through an extensive set of experiments in not only the video action recognition task but also a wide range of applications including traffic flow prediction, climate forecast, infectious disease prediction, and chaotic systems behavioral prediction, where extremely complex nonlinear behaviors caused by the intrinsic data dependencies and relationships are often encountered. Experimental results demonstrated that the proposed model not only robustly outperformed the existing methods in various applications but, more importantly, offered explicit guidance to construct desired architectures according to the given learning tasks and datasets, with the information-theoretic guarantee.

12202417.label: Major findings and research outcome
12202417.value: This research project has developed a series of novel multi-label and multi-view/modality/source machine learning models and algorithms based on the popular deep learning and manifold learning designs. By appropriately integrating data from multiple views/modalities/sources (e.g., using regularizers or optimization constraints to model the consistency between different views/modalities/sources while allowing the existence of individualities of these views/modalities/sources), information from the given data could be better preserved and represented during the learning process compared with the single-view/modality/source based learning approaches. By taking into account the discriminative information from multiple labels and modeling the nonlinearity of the datasets via manifold formulations and deep architectures, the compact and meaningful features embedded in the original high-dimensional observations can be well extracted, and thus enable the accurate analysis (e.g., recognition/prediction) in the subsequent learning tasks. We validated the effectiveness of the developed methods in applications of human action/behavior recognition in videos, multi-emotion detection in videos, and multi-label classification of images, as planned. To further demonstrate the generality and applicability of the proposed models, we extensively evaluated their performance in a range of learning tasks and applications in other related domains, including multi-view clustering over social and biological graphs, key opinion leader identification (KOL) identification over social networks, traffic flow prediction, infectious disease prediction, climate forecast, and chaotic systems behavioral prediction. Experimental results showed that the proposed methods outperformed both classical and state-of-the-art models on all datasets and learning tasks. More importantly, the proposed methods are able to capture the complex relationships among data (e.g., the spatiotemporal dependency in videos), which are meaningful in the real-world context and thus make the superiority of the developed methods interpretable. As listed in Part C, the aforementioned research has produced eight high-quality research papers, three of which have been published in leading journals in the related fields (two in IEEE Transactions on Cybernetics and one in IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems); four of which have been published in reputable conferences (one in SIGIR-18, one in ICMR-18, one in WI-18, and one in ISMIS-18); and one of which is still under review.

12202417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12202417.value: In the future, we will further develop the proposed research from both methodology and application perspectives. In the methodology perspective, we plan to: (1) explore other alternatives of the learning objective functions to model the view/modality consistency and individualities, so as to better capture the intrinsic relationships among multiple data sources; (2) investigate various deep architectures and manifold objectives, so as to further enhance the representation ability of the proposed learning models; and (3) conduct theoretical analyses of the proposed models, such as the optimality of the methods and the error bound guarantee, so as to provide the theoretical support of the developed methods. In the application perspective, we plan to: (1) further analyze the physical meanings of the learned subspace or low-dimensional representations, so as to improve the interpretability of our proposed methods; (2) incorporate the domain-specific knowledge into the general objective functions, so as to enhance the suitability of the developed methods in various applications; and (3) extend the proposed models with parallel or distributed settings, so as to make the proposed models applicable in large-scale datasets.

12202417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12202417.value: This work aimed to develop novel machine learning models and algorithms to extract meaningful features from multi-source visual data for pattern mining and analytics. By performing systematic evaluations on both synthetic and public standard datasets and conducting comprehensive comparisons with both classical and state-of-the-art algorithms, we faithfully validated the effectiveness of the proposed methods in various scenarios. The models and algorithms developed in this project are general in nature and will provide new artificial intelligence and machine learning tools. More importantly, the project outcomes will be particularly beneficial to a wide range of public security related applications involving multiple, complex data sources, such as human action recognition in videos for abnormality detection and vandalism deterrence, traffic flow prediction for smart city management, key opinion leader identification for social network management, etc. For the educational component, we have incorporated developments and findings from this project into course work as case studies or mini-projects, which will enable students to gain experience that is rarely obtained from textbook-based courses.

12300117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12300117.value: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), a member of the gammaherpsevirus, is etiologically implicated in several lymphoid and epithelial malignancies, substantially contributing to the development of a diversity of lymphomas and, especially, carcinomas. Although current treatments for EBV-associated carcinoma, such as radiotherapy and chemotherapy have long been adopted, the former is inadequate either to kill advanced, metastatic tumours or to prevent their recurrence, while the latter is still under development. The latent membrane protein (LMP1) is an oncoprotein known to be responsible for regulating EBV and human gene expression and even maintenance of EBV episome. Such presence of EBV and LMP1 in the tumor cells of EBV-associated cancers can therefore, provide an overarching basis for specific therapy. Compared with other EBV-associated cancer regulators inside nucleus, the membrane subcellular localization is easier and more effectively accomplished by targeting anti-cancer/imaging agents than in nucleus. Therefore, a lower-dosed concentration and more selective anti-EBV related cancer therapy through LMP1 can be expected. More recently, there have been several studies on the LMP1 inhibition using peptides or small molecules. However, the function of these inhibitors cannot be monitored in real-time. As justified by our recent publications on responsive luminescent lanthanide materials towards various biological tasks in solution/in vitro/in vivo, our research team has thorough expertise in lanthanide coordination chemistry, spectroscopy, peptide chemistry, and in vitro biological applications. Therefore, we aim to develop luminescent LMP1-specific lanthanide bio-probes with high selectivity towards LMP1 and capability of selectively inhibiting LMP1 on the membrane surface and in-vitro real-time monitoring as anti- EBV-related carcinoma agents. To further support our work, we have performed a range of proof-of-concept experiments to consolidate our proposal: (1) several LMP1-specific ytterbium complexes with tailor-made synthetic peptides have been prepared which can be excited in the visible, and near-infrared region, for LMP1 imaging; (2) molecular dynamic simulation shows our proposed complexes can fit in the LMP1; and (3) they are all water-soluble, and membrane specific for LMP1 in vitro imaging and inhibition of EBV specific cancer cells. This proposal paves the way for the development of new-generation lanthanide complexes conjugated with LMP1-specific peptides as dual probes with imaging and anti-tumour properties. Making a success of this research can bring to society a more powerful tool (especially with a combination of multi-photon and time-resolved technology) to unveil the mystery and understand the very roles of LMP1 in EBV-associated carcinoma, ultimately furthering cancer therapy and research. 艾博斯坦-巴爾病毒（EBV）是多種淋巴性和上皮性惡性腫瘤產生的病因，它也能導致一系列淋巴癌及其他相關性癌症的形成。目前最主要的也是運用最久的治療EBV相關性癌癥的療法是放療和化療，但前者不足以殺死晚期或已轉移的癌腫，後者仍處於發展中。潛伏性膜蛋白1(LMP1)是已知的負責調節EBV（維持EBV遊離基因）和人類基因表達的EBV病毒性蛋白，因此有望成為特異性治療EBV相關性癌症的新靶點。相比其他核內調節劑，靶向膜蛋白的抗腫瘤/成像試劑更容易實現，也更有效。因而，通過特異性靶向LMP1並在低劑量下獲得抗EBV相關性癌症療效的探針是值得被期待的。 近期就LMP1的抑制研究已有幾款多肽和小分子抑制劑的報道，然而無法對這些抑制劑的體內外功能進行實時監控。我們的研究團隊在鑭系配合物化學，光譜學，多肽化學以及體內外生物學運用方面具備紮實專業的基礎，這也可以從我們近期所報道的一些響應性鑭系材料用於解決多種溶液中或體內外的生物學難題中得到證實。基於此，我們致力於開發一款基於鑭系材料的特異性LMP1生物探針。 作為抗EBV相關性腫瘤的試劑，它不僅具備對LMP1這一病毒蛋白的高選擇性，而且還能選擇性抑制EBV陽性細胞膜表面的LMP1，並可實現同步監控該探針的體內外活動。 為了進一步支持我們在本方案中提出的研究計劃，我們實施了一系列的概念驗證性實驗：（1）我們設計並合成了幾種LMP1特異性鐿配合物，並將它們與定制性多肽接合在一起。這一系列的鐿與多肽的接合物可以通過可見或近紅外激發，實現對LMP1的成像；（2）分子動力學模擬結果顯示我們的接合物可以靶向LMP1；並且（3）這些水溶性的接合物能夠特異性的對EBV陽性細胞膜上的LMP1進行成像，並表現出了抑制效果。 本方案為新一代雙功能（成像和抑制）探針-鑭系配合物與LMP1特異性多肽的接合物的發展鋪平了道路。這一研究計劃的成功（尤其是結合多光子和時間分辨技術），將帶來一款更強有力的工具去探索和理解在EBV相關性腫瘤中LMP1的未知生物功能，並最終助力於腫瘤的研究與治療上。

12300117.label: Realisation of objectives
12300117.value: The Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) is a very common oncovirus among humans, affecting more than 90% of the global population. The latent membrane protein 1 (LMP1) is an EBV-encoded oncoprotein that has recently garnered attention as a therapeutic target due to its expression in most EBV-associated cancers. Our four objectives focused on introducing LMP1 specificity to lanthanide complexes with outstanding photophysical properties for long-term live cell imaging, with the aim of constructing a new family of novel, dual-functional agents as an imaging agent and a delivery vehicle for peptide drugs against EBV-related cancer cells. We designed and synthesized 20 lanthanide complexes and nanomaterials that showed good cell permeability and responsive luminescence changes. As LMP1 is a cell membrane protein, it is more accessible than nuclear proteins like ENBA1, and thus the ligation of target vectors should easily aid target specificity, thus enhancing cell-tracking properties and thereby reducing off-target side-effects. LMP1 is therefore a put forward as a novel target protein for anti-cancer treatments. We subsequently conjugated the complexes with peptides or certain functional groups to acquire specificity towards LMP1 and the steric hindrance of the overall ligand contributes to subcellular localization properties. The selectivity towards LMP1 was achieved by targeting FWLY motif, which plays a vital role in the intermolecular interactions with the 6 transmembrane domains (TM1-6) in LMP1. The motif mimics the key amino acid residues in the transmembrane 1 (TM1) of LMP1 and is also able to prevent the formation of LMP1 oligomers in lipid raft, thereby inactivating the NF‐κB signalling pathway. We incorporated the FWLY motif at different sites to our 3 previously developed EBNA1-specific peptides, i.e. at the C- or N-terminus ((P5: -Ahx-YFMVFGGRrRKGGFWLY; P6: -Ahx-RrRKGGYFMVFGGFWLY; P7: -Ahx-FWLYGGRrRKGGYFMVF) to impart additional FWLY-targeting ability and was subsequently conjugated with the lanthanide probes. The dual-targeting approach – first to the cell membrane at LMP1 and then into the nucleus at EBNA1 – greatly enhanced the targeting specificity and minimized undesirable inhibition/damage to other normal cells. The release of the therapeutic peptide was achieved by introducing a pH-sensitive imine linker between the lanthanide materials and the targeting peptide, in which the tumor microenvironment will induce a cleavage and the ensued release of peptide in the cancer cells. The binding between our lanthanide probes and LMP1 was investigated in vitro using optical imagining, Western blot and isothermal titration calorimetry; the probes’ ability to hinder cancer effects were also studied in LMP1-positive (Raji, C666-1, AK43T, GM12878) and LMP1-negative (HK1, Ramos, NP460) cell lines. The results of two series of complexes showed encouraging potential for the inhibition of EBV-associated cancers. P5, amongst the other targeting peptides, was found to show the strongest affinity to the nuclear proteins. We were able to monitor the whole targeting and delivery process using the responsive upconversion emissions from the upconversion luminescence of lanthanide-based nanomaterials (e.g. NaGdF4:Yb3+, Er3+@NaGdF4 upconversion nanocrystals). The performance of UCNP-P5, amongst 3 newly prepared nanocrystals was found to be the most satisfying, showing potent tumor inhibition, responsive luminescence and promising cellular and tumor uptake, prompting further studies in vitro and in vivo as well as inspiring a new generation of dual-targeting agents that could be translated into therapeutic applications on EBV-associated and other cancers. (Advanced Science, 2021, 2002919) With the encouraging results of the FWLY motif in inhibiting EBV-associated cancer, we further designed a novel peptide, P19 (Pra-KAhx-K-LDLALK-FWLY-K-IVMSDKW-K-RrRK), containing also the FWLY motif and partially mimicking the transmembrane region 1 (TM1) of LMP1, which we expect it to inhibit the LMP1 monomers from undergoing oligomerization in the lipid raft by binding to the TM3-4 regions and at the same time inactivating the NF-B signal transduction. A control peptide, P19C, was also synthesized with AAAA taking the place of FWLY in the sequence, demonstrating the function of the FWLY motif. We conjugated P19 to two cyclen-based lanthanide complexes with visible light (europium) and near infrared (ytterbium) luminescence. We hoped that these complexes could simultaneously act as an imaging agent to directly visualize LMP1 – which has not been reported in literature – and an anti-cancer drug. As a result, we successfully reported in this project the first direct imaging agent of LMP1 with our stable and biocompatible lanthanide complexes for potential applications in treating EBV-associated cancers due to its outstanding target specificity. This work also demonstrated our dual-target approach in strategizing sequential targeting of two proteins from the same cancerous cell which can be utilized onto other cancers. The selective theranostic effects of EuP19 and YbP19 were also tested and confirmed with cytotoxicity assays, Western blot and immunostaining with LMP1-positive cell lines. In vivo studies are ongoing to evaluate their tumor inhibition ability in vivo.

12300117.label: Major findings and research outcome
12300117.value: In this project, a total of 20 lanthanide nanomaterials and complexes were prepared with the aim of imaging LMP1 and inhibiting EBV-associated cancers. We designed a nanoplatform using upconversion nanoparticles with a dual-targeting peptide which is selective towards two oncoproteins at the cell membrane and nucleus respectively. We conducted a comparative study using EBV-associated cancer cells and HeLa cells to demonstrate this precision targeting and delivery strategy. The dual-targeting peptides were designed based on the incorporation of two peptides with separate targeting ability and we prepared in 3 different sequences (P5-P7, refer to above) to study its effect. We also added a pH-sensitive linker which is susceptible to be cleaved by the acidic environment in tumor cells between the nanomaterial and the targeting peptide. The combination of specific targeting towards LMP1 and the cleavability of the peptide drug made our bioprobes enhanced cellular uptake and accumulation at our site of interest thereby lowering the effective dose amount and at the same time reducing the possibility and extent of undesired side effects. Results showed that the target specificity brought about by targeting the over-expressed LMP1 protein on the cell membrane of EBV-associated cancer cells and the selective cleavage of the linker in the tumor microenvironment made our lanthanide nanomaterials an efficient and discriminatory effect against cancer cells. Our work is the first report of simultaneous imaging and inhibition of two different oncoproteins in the same cancer cell, setting a visionary example for the next generation of precision drug delivery to be used in monitoring and treating cancers. (Advanced Science, 2021, 2002919) On the other hand, we designed a novel targeting peptide P19 for conjugation with luminescent lanthanide complexes in a similar manner as those used with the nanomaterials but with modifications to mimic the amino acid residues in TM1 of LMP1 that plays an important role in regulating the signalling pathway, thereby preventing the oligomerization of LMP1 in lipid raft. The complexes, able to emit either red or near infrared light, were ligated with the targeting vector and were able to directly visualize the LMP1 protein in optical imaging – the first report in literature. They were also found to exert inhibitory effects towards both tumor growth and the NF-B pathway. The selectivity was further confirmed by comparing the results in LMP1-positive and LMP1-negative cell lines. (Light: Science & Applications, 2020, 46; PNAS, 2019, 26614, JACS Au, 2021, In Press)

12300117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12300117.value: We have developed a series of prodrugs that are target-specific, responsive, luminescent and are found to have anti-cancer effects. This is the first report of a dual-targeting mechanism in which two separate viral proteins overexpressed in EBV-associated cancers are targeted in one single molecule. The sequential targeting also improves the uptake of the drug by the tumor cells, thus allowing a lower effective dose for treatment. Based on the encouraging results, we aim to elevate the performance of our lanthanide bioprobes for clinical practices by enhancing its current target specificity towards LMP1 and incorporate additional vectors to increase its multi-specificity. We plan to conduct a systematic structural modification study on our lanthanide-based bioprobes to evaluate their membrane subcellular localization properties while retaining their capability as a drug delivery vehicle with a controllable drug-release trigger. The study will extend to biological studies in situ, in vitro and in vivo to assess the degree of translation of the bioprobes’ various properties as we have also developed the experimental protocols for performing in vivo near infrared optical imaging. Further downstream parameters such as the toxic doses, lethal doses and effective doses will be determined for assessing the best candidate for clinical trials.

12300117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12300117.value: EBV-associated cancers, such as nasopharyngeal cancer and gastric cancer, are a growing type of cancer in the world (with more than 200,000 new cases annually) with a high mortality rate. The primary goal of this project is to develop an effective treatment against EBV-associated cancers and we first have to understand their pathologies. In this project, we developed peptide sequences that specifically target proteins related to the cancers and connect it with a drug that is only activated by the slightly acidic environment inside tumor cells. The whole process could also be monitored by linking the peptide drug with a luminescence lanthanide-based imaging agent. This report is the first report that targets two viral proteins within the same cancer cell. This work also demonstrated a sequential dual-targeting approach which reduces the dosage amount and side-effects with improved selectivity. The significance of this work lies in gaining understanding of and treating EBV-associated cancers, setting a blueprint for next-generation peptide-based drugs against various cancers.

12300317.label: Project Objectives
12300317.value: Propose a proximal version of the augmented Lagrangian method and its splitting variants for some convex programming models based on the idea of using positive-indefinite proximal regularization, and consider extending the algorithmic design to some other relevant algorithms. Rigorously prove the convergence and establish the worst-case convergence rates for the newly proposed algorithms; apply the new analysis techniques to improve theoretical results for some current methods of the same kind; and analyze the optimality of the rules for choosing step sizes. 12300317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12300317.value: Splitting algorithms have been widely used for convex programming models in many areas, especially in contemporary data-driven application domains such as statistical learning and image processing. A family of splitting algorithms based on the augmented Lagrangian method (ALM) has received increasing attention since it was proposed in 1969. Associated with the growing popularity of the ALM, some new interesting and more advanced topics related to the ALM's algorithmic design and theoretical analysis have naturally arisen and urge deeper research into developing more efficient splitting algorithms for convex programming problems. The main purpose of this project will be to systematically study how to regularize the ALM and its various splitting versions by positive-indefinite proximal regularization so that a series of new ALM-based splitting algorithms can be proposed for various convex programming models. These new algorithms are expected to outperform current ALM-based algorithms that require positive definiteness or positive semi-definiteness for the proximal regularization. Using positive-indefinite proximal regularization for ALM-based algorithms is new in the literature, and it enables a large family of current ALM-based algorithms to be scaled to faster levels immediately. We also expect to develop some novel techniques for convergence analysis, and they may be meaningful additions to current theoretical results in the literature. The new algorithms and theoretical results could better justify the rationale of using ALM-based algorithms and boost more application-tailored investigations in various application domains. We will aim to substantially enhance the current understanding of this important type of algorithm both theoretically and algorithmically, and expect the new results to inspire even more meaningful research along this direction. 分裂算法被广泛地用于求解多个领域里出现的凸优化问题，特别是诸如机器学习、图像处理等受数据驱动的现代应用领域。自1969年增广拉格朗日方法的问世，一类基于它的分裂算法便一直受到学术界的持续关注。随着增广拉格朗日方法越来越受关注，一些与此方法的算法设计和理论分析相关的有意思和有深度的研究课题也应运而生，并促使学者更深入地研究如何设计求解凸优化的更有效的分裂算法。本项目的主要目的是系统地研究如何用非正定的临近点项来正则化增广拉格朗日方法以及其多种分裂的变形，从而设计出一系列新的基于增广拉格朗日方法的求解凸优化的分裂算法。我们预期这些新方法将比现有的基于增广拉格朗日方法但使用正定或半正定临近点正则项的方法要更有效。使用非正定的临近点项来正则化增广拉格朗日方法可以立刻加速一系列此类方法的计算效率，而在目前的文献中，还没有此方面的相关研究。我们也预期提出一些新的技术来进行收敛性分析，这些技术对现有的关于理论分析的文献将是有益的补充。这些新的算法设计和理论分析的研究结果将进一步说明使用增广拉格朗日方法进行算法设计的必要性，并激发多个应用领域里针对具体应用问题的研究工作。我们希望本项目可以实质性地提升我们在算法上和理论上对这一类重要方法的理解，并希望结果可以引发更有意义的相关研究。

12300317.label: Major findings and research outcome
12300317.value: We have successfully found the optimal choices for the proximal parameters of the proximal ALM and the linearized ADMM. It was shown that the well-known and by-default choices of these parameters can be further shrank by multiplying a coefficient of 0.75 and thus the step sizes for solving the involved subproblems can be enlarged by 25% immediately. We showed that it is the best improvement in sense of that the convergence of these algorithms is not guaranteed for any other number smaller than 0.75. We constructed counterexamples to illustrate the optimality. We have also extended this analysis to one representative splitting algorithm for multi-block separable convex programming problems, with which it becomes trivial to discuss similar results for various other splitting algorithms of the same kind. Our research outcome also clarifies that the proximal terms in the ALM, the ADMM as well as their variants can be even negative, and thus affirmatively shows that there is no need to discuss how to relax these proximal terms as the so-called semi-proximal terms in a number of existing papers.

12300317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12300317.value: The techniques and roadmaps developed in this project can be extended to similar discussions for some other important algorithms, and thus potentially trigger other meaningful new improvements for the optimization community. Inspired by this project, we have been also working on improving a benchmark primal-dual algorithm for saddle point problems which has been widely used in various scientific computing areas, and our result is promising. We think this project has provided a new and useful idea to improve a series of first-order algorithms with a wide range of potential applications.

12300317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12300317.value: The focus of this project is to discuss how to optimally improve some benchmark first-order algorithms in the convex optimization contexts. We found the best improvements for the proximal version of the ALM, the linearized ADMM, and their variants for multi-block convex programming problems. By these results, we provide a novel way to improve some classic algorithms to the best, which can be extended to other algorithms of similar kinds. Our results provide an immediate and universally effective strategy to accelerate these algorithms in a moderate manner, and the acceleration can be easily verified by a number of concrete applications. Moreover, our results justify the unnecessity of discussing how to relax the requirement on the proximal terms in the mentioned algorithms from positive definiteness to positive semi-definiteness in a series of existing papers in the literature.

12300917.label: Project Objectives
12300917.value: Based on the highly technical details in our recent paper [15], the way to getting around the uncertainty resolution limit is identified, and will be explored and applied to the advancement of signal and image processing, particularly for nonlinear and non-stationary signals and time series, as well as highly complex imagery of arbitrary dimensions to achieve super-resolution. As a continuation of our paper [15] on atomic decomposition of continuous-time signals, we will derive analogous results for discrete-time non-stationary signals, with non-uniform samples, by getting around the resolution barrier. We will also derive efficient and effective algorithms, with time series forecasting capability. Comparison with other state-of-the-art approaches will be performed by our students and a post doctoral assistant supported by this proposed research grant, under the guidance of the PI. Extension of the multivariate result in the same paper [15] will be explored by incorporating the ideas of curvelets and shearlets in the wavelet literatures to achieve directional independency for imagery feature extractions, particularly for 2-dimensional and 3-dimensional images. More generally, an effective imagery separation method for extracting the fundamental building blocks of a given complex image will be developed by getting around the barrier of uncertainty limit of imaging resolution as imposed by the Rayleigh criterion. Applications to image enhancement, image restoration and inpainting, image segmentation, as well as classification according to imagery features, will be carried out by a research assistant and our students supported by this proposed research grant, and guided by the P.I. We will work with the appropriate medical specialists to investigate the application of our computational algorithms for the understanding of neural oscillations (or brain waves) from EEG recording for the neurologists, and to hormonal signal separation from pulse readings in collaboration of our current endocrinologist partner (at the University of California, Davis, Medical School). We will also investigate the application of our algorithms to detect the precise locations of tiny metastases from MRI imagery, and to determine the precise shapes of such tumors, if they exist, to assist brain surgery without unnecessary damage of brain tissue, and more importantly, nerve damage. In addition to the student projects mentioned above, we will also carve out several components of our mathematical derivations and development for student participation. Such tasks, including applying our formula to develop parallel algorithms, computational architecture, and compilation of parameter libraries, should not require extensive mathematical training. The parameters to be determined experimentally, including thresholding parameters and frequency window widths, are data-dependent. Hence, an effective library of such parameters for various application areas will certainly facilitate implementation for prototype development and productization in the near future.
