12300917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12300917.value: While “time–frequency analysis” is arguably the most important approach for innovative development of powerful mathematical tools for signal and image processing as well as for data analysis in general, there are certain “scientific barriers” to this endeavor, most notably: the "Heisenberg uncertainty principle” for time-frequency localization and the “Rayleigh criterion” that gives rise to an “uncertainty limit of imaging resolution”. On the other hand, clever ways have been introduced recently in experimental physical sciences to get around these two uncertainty limits, notably: a group of researchers at Rochester and Ottawa have a way to bypass the Heisenberg uncertainty principle; and the three 2014 Nobel laureates in Chemistry, Eric Betzig, Stefan Hell and William Moerner, have developed ways to capture images of living cells at nanoscale resolution. In computational mathematics, a naiive way to bypass the Heisenberg uncertainty principle is to design parallel computational schemes. But getting around the uncertainty resolution limit would take much more sophisticated imagination. Indeed, in our recent paper [15], while carrying out localization in both time and frequency domains in our proofs, the idea of getting around the resolution limit was unfortunately buried among the highly technical details, in that by considering any time instance as the center of a frequency-window with adjustable width allows us to separate all distinct frequency contents at this time instance. In other words, using the time instant (or image pixel) as the center of an adaptive frequency-window is one way to bypass the resolution limit, allowing the design of the zoom-in/zoom-out feature to arbitrarily high or low resolutions, thereby the capability to capture signal or image contents in super-resolution. In this proposal, we will proceed to pose several outstanding problem areas that can be solved by exploring around this innovation. One of the problems is blind-source decomposition of a given real-world signal, from arbitrary (non-uniform) digital samples, into its primary building blocks, called atoms. Another problem is to incorporate the techniques from curvelets and shearlets in the wavelet literature with our blind source decomposition paradigm for extracting atoms that contain arbitrarily fine image features. This investigation gives rise to many image-based applications, including image understanding, image classification, image enhancement, imagery recovery and inpainting. Our ultimate goal along this line is to identify tiny metastatic tumors from MRI images most accurately, in order to assist brain surgeons to detect and remove such tumors without introducing unnecessary damages. 雖然 “時間--頻率分析” 可以說是創新發展, 信號和圖像處理, 以及數據分析的強大數學 工具的最重要方法. 但是這努力存在一定的 “科學障礙”, 尤其是“海森堡不確 定性原理“ 和 ”瑞利標準“ 引起了 ”成像分辨率的不確定性限制“. 另一方面, 最近 在實驗物理科學中引入了一些聰明的方法來克服這兩個不確定性限制特別是: 羅 切斯特和渥太華的一組研究人員有一條路繞過海森堡的不確定性原則; 2014 年 諾貝爾化學獎獲獎者, 埃⾥里克貝齊格, 史蒂芬·赫爾, 和 威廉莫爾 三人開發 了以納米尺度捕獲活細胞圖像的方法解析度。 在計算數學中, 繞過海森堡不確定性原理的一種新方式是設計並行計算方案。但 是, 擺脫不確定性解決限制將需要更複雜的想像力。事實上, 在我們最近的文章 [15]中, 我們的證明, 在時間和頻域進⾏本地化的同時, 圍繞分辨率限制的想法是: 因為通過考慮任何時間實例具有 可調寬度的頻率窗口的中心允許我們在此時間段分離所有不同頻率的內容. 換句 話說, 使用時刻 (或圖像像素) 作為自適應頻率窗口的中心是繞過分辨率極限的 一種方法, 允許 放大--縮⼩ 特徵的設計任意高或低分辨率從而能夠以超分辨率捕 獲信號或圖像內容。 在這個建議中,我們將著手提出幾個可以通過探索這個創新來解決的突出問題。其中⼀個問題是將任意(非均勻)數字樣本給定的真實信號, 盲源分解成 稱為原子的主要構建塊。另一個問題是在小波文獻中將曲線和小波束的技術與我 們的盲源分解範例結合起來, 以提取含有任意精細圖像特徵的原子。這項調查引發了許多基於圖像的應用,包括圖像理解,圖像分類,圖像增強,圖像恢復和修復。我們沿著這條路線的目標是最準確地識別MRI圖像中的微小轉移性腫 瘤,以幫助腦外科醫⽣檢測和去除這樣的腫瘤, 而不會引起不必要的損害。

12300917.label: Realisation of objectives
12300917.value: Objectives 5.1.1, 5.1.2, and 5.1.3 on the development of mathematical theory and computational schemes have been achieved. In particular, we have introduced an innovative approach in terms of Gaussian transform to replace the Fourier transform and Fourier series representation in the published literature, by using orthogonal Hermite polynomials, with Gaussian weights, to provide local approximation, which in turn allows us to extend theory to precisely locate point-masses restricted to very fine grids to the random spatial setting even for point-masses in high dimensions that are arbitrarily close together. This is significant in that super-resolution of point masses in two and three dimensions do not lie on grids and are almost always non-periodic. As a result, this approach enables us to get around the uncertainty barriers in atomic decomposition. The algorithms developed in this project are data-driven, but require training data. For this reason, we have paid a lot of attention to the development of deep learning, with deep neural network realization, applied to super-resolution in high dimensions. On the other hand, the postgraduate assistants were not well prepared to learn new theory and had very minimum knowledge of life sciences. Much time and effort were spent to train them, resulting in loss of time to complete the experimental aspects of the project. In addition, the proposed endocrinologist partner was extremely busy in the U.C. Davis Hospital and had little time to contribute to the proposed experimental task of the project. There will be delay, due to the current pandemic situation in California. But the interest and intention are still there. To overcome this delay, we have been working on computer simulation instead. While “time–frequency analysis” is arguably the most important approach to innovations of powerful mathematical tools for signal and image processing as well as for data analysis in general, there are certain “scientific barriers” to this endeavor, most notably: the "Heisenberg uncertainty principle” for time-frequency localization and the “Rayleigh criterion” that gives rise to an “uncertainty limit of imaging resolution”. In this project, we have developed an innovative spatial approach to enrich the popular time-frequency approach that enables us to get around the Rayleigh criterion in arbitrarily high dimension. The long-term impact of our research is significant to the advancement of many research directions in applied and computational mathematics as well as many application areas, including extraction of financial market volatility and trends, time series analysis for environmental and geosciences, and various applications in biomedicine, particularly to the understanding EEG signals in neurology, hormonal signal separation from pulse readings in endocrinology, and to assisting brain surgery in identifying and removal of tiny metastatic tumors, without unnecessary brain tissue damages. The research papers from this proposed research project have been published in the highly prestigious international journals, which should facilitate in further enhancement of the already outstanding international reputation of the Hong Kong educational institutions. As to Objectives 5.1.4 and 5.1.5, it is unfortunate that the experimental tasks were only minimally achieved due to the lack of capable assistance from the post doctors, and the difficulty in collaboration with the proposed endocrinologist partner of the Medical School of the University of California, Davis.

12300917.label: Major findings and research outcome
12300917.value: An innovative spatial approach to signal processing and image analysis is developed in this project, with emphasis on signal decomposition and image features extraction, by solving an inverse problem with the blind-source data function governed by the composite AM-FM model. The first main result in this direction is a Fourier-invariant theory established in our paper [2] to link our spatial approach with the time-frequency approach. As a result, the “point-mass isolation operator (PIO)” introduced in (3.1) in [2] can be used to characterize the separation point-masses in terms of the degrees n of the Hermite polynomials, in that point-masses that are arbitrarily close to one another can be separated by allowing increasing values of n. This is the key to enable us in getting around the uncertainty barrier, dictated by the Rayleigh criterion. The main result of the PIO characterization is Theorem 3.1 in [2]. For computational and implementational purposes, the spatial Gaussian transform is proposed in our paper [6] to introduce a mathematical model, both for the multivariate super-resolution problem and for the problem of blind-source separation of real-valued exponential sums in any dimension. The “super-resolution and exponent recovery algorithm (SERA)” is formulated in Algorithm 1 and the assurance of convergence and robust stability are consequences of Theorem 2.2, Theorem 2.3, and Theorem 4.1 in [6]. On the other hand, for very high-dimension data-sets that lie on some unknown manifold of much lower dimension, a “deep learning” algorithm is developed in our paper [1] for finding a local coordinate system of the manifold without eigen-decomposition. Deep neural networks are also proposed in [6] to realize the approximation scheme by using certain appropriate training data. The theory and construction of such deep-nets are the contents of our paper [3], in which it is proposed that each inner layer is endowed with a specific learning task. Since the Gaussian function plays an important role in our papers [2, 6] the construction of deep-nets for rotation-invariance approximation and learning is important for this project. Theory and methods for such constructions constitute the main contents of our paper [5]. Deep-net tree structure is proposed and developed in our paper [4] to facilitate computational efficiency, with emphasis on the balance of capacity and approximation ability. Our latest paper [7] is concerned with realization of spatial sparseness among massive data in arbitrarily high dimension, by constructing deep-nets with ReLU activation.

12300917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12300917.value: The main tool of our research findings is based on the Gaussian function due its attractive property of blindness to the Euclidean dimensions. Unfortunately, the Gaussian function has infinite support and there is no effective scheme for computing the function. On the other hand, a vast amount of application areas are mainly concerned with one and two spatial dimensions. For the univariate setting, it is well-known that the centered Cardinal B-splines of order n, when properly normalized, coverage to the Gaussian function as the order n increases to infinity, and of course a 3-term recursive formula for computing Cardinal B-splines are readily implementable. For higher dimensions, tensor-product extensions have similar attractive computational properties. A potential further development is to investigate the replacement of the Gaussian by the 4-directional box-splines for 2-D imaging study to getting around the uncertainty barrier, while maintaining the approximate rotational invariance property of the Gaussian and enjoying the compact support property with effective recursive computational formula. As to applications, we propose to extend our current on-going investigation of imagery separation for extraction of the fundamental image building blocks by using box splines to getting around the barrier of uncertainty limit of point-mass images.

12300917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12300917.value: “Super-resolution” in light microscopy refers to surpassing the light diffraction limit as governed by the Rayleigh criterion. By treating the clusters of light point-source as Dirac delta distributions and applying the Fourier transform, the problem of getting around the uncertainty barrier of light diffraction becomes the mathematical problem of separating a positive linear combination of unknown complex exponents that are arbitrarily close to one and other. Since the content of each summand of the linear combination consists of the frequency content and the light intensity content, the most effective method for solving this inverse problem is the time-frequency approach. However, in application to molecular biology, the masses are positive, while the Dirac delta has measure zero. This is one of the reasons we replace the Fourier transform by the Gaussian transform to preserve the positivity. By considering the Gaussian transform of the clusters of light point-source, the same problem is translated to the inverse problem of extracting the centers of the Gaussian functions with significant impact in at least three applications, namely fluorescence microscopy, magnetic resonance spectroscopy, and isotope separation in physical chemistry.

12301317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12301317.value: Fluorescent probes are very powerful tools for real-time tracking of various biomolecules, cellular activities and physiological events in living cells. Probes that show the ability to recognize a biomarker or detect a disease are a clinically useful tool for monitoring disease progression and treatment effects. Because of the use of the long-wavelength/low-energy excitation source and the characteristics of the intensity-dependence of the two-photon absorption process, the two-photon excitation offers considerable advantages for biological fluorescence imaging and sensing such as higher spatial resolution, less photobleaching and photodamage as well as deeper tissue penetration as compared to those of one-photon excitation. Probes with site-targeting specificity such as tumor or brain tissue selectivity and/or subcellular localization property offering direct and efficient delivery to the site of interest are particularly attractive and useful for practical clinical applications. A target-specific probe can also play a key role in carrying and delivering a pro-drug/drug to the target site for disease treatment giving rise to a novel theranostic capability. Such a theranostic agent would allow the investigation and monitoring of the cellular uptake and therapeutic effect at the subcellular/tissue level using the imaging technique. As a result, the development of novel biocompatible and site-targeting selective theranostic agents that show two-photon imaging capability and therapeutic treatment function are of practical significance and have recently drawn tremendous attention. Thus, we propose herein to design and synthesize novel site-targeting specific theranostic agents that are highly two-photon fluorescence active simultaneously with disease treatment capability or potential. In addition, a systematic investigation of their structure-two-photon absorption properties, exploration of their applications in two-photon bioimaging in vitro and in vivo as well as studying the potential as a pro-drug/drug for disease treatment will be carried out. The findings of this study hold promise for future improved medicine capable of diagnostics and therapeutics providing a more effective and personalized treatment. 熒光探針是一種十分強大的工具，可以實時跟踪各種生物分子，細胞活動和活性細胞中的生理事件。探針具有識別生物標誌和檢測疾病的能力，在臨床上可應用於監測疾病的進展和治療效果。由於長波長/低能量激發源的使用以及雙光子吸收過程中的光強度相關的特性，雙光子激發對於生物熒光成像和監測與單光子激發相比具有更加強大的優勢，例如更高的空間分辨率，更低的光漂白與光損害，而且具有更深的組織穿透能力。 具有靶向的探針，可以直接有效的到達感興趣的位置，例如針對腫瘤或者大腦組織的選擇性，或者對於細胞內細胞器的定位等，這對於探針運用於實際的臨床具有很大的吸引力。靶向探針也可以攜帶和運輸前藥或藥物到達目標位點，在進行疾病治療方面發揮重要的作用，從而提升新的治療診斷的能力。這樣的診斷方式可以通過使用成像技術從而在亞細胞/組織程度上調查藥物在細胞中的吸收和監測治療的效果。因此，發展新型生物相容性和位點靶向選擇性，同時具有雙光子成像的診斷和治療功能的試劑，具有重要的實用價值，近來也引起極大的關注。 本項目我們將設計合成新型的靶向性診斷治療試劑，其具有很強的雙光子熒光能力，同時也具備治療疾病的能力或潛力。此外，將系統性的研究它們的結構特點與雙光子吸收的關係，探索它們在體內或體外的雙光子生物成像中的應用，以及研究其作為疾病治療的前藥或藥物的潛力。本研究的結果對診斷治療藥物的發展有一定的前景，可以提供更有效和更個性化的治療。

12301317.label: Realisation of objectives
12301317.value: We have successfully developed several novel theranostic agents including neuroprotective Aβ-selective dual-modal imaging nanoprobe based on superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles, Aβ oligomer-targeted multimodal gadolinium-based nanoprobe, and oligomeric Aβ targeted near infrared (NIR) emissive dibutylnaphthylamine-based cyanine probes that can not only detect and image Aβ species in vivo in AD mouse models but also show inhibitory effect against Aβ self-aggregation and Aβ-induced ROS formation offering the desirable therapeutic potential for AD. A first neuroprotective NIR/MR dual-modal nanoparticle (NP)-based contrast agent for Aβ species imaging in vivo has been successfully developed by chemically conjugating Aβ-targeting turn-on NIR fluorescence cyanine dyes with magnetic resonance active superparamagnetic iron oxide NP-based contrast agent. This non-toxic nanoprobe exhibits excellent neuroprotective effect against Aβ-induced toxicities including suppression of ROS generation and inhibition of Ca2+ uploading highlighting the therapeutic/theranostic potential of the nanoprobe. Fluorescence and MR imaging in vivo demonstrated that this nano-probe was BBB permeable in both WT and Tg mice in which they exhibited different washout rate for the NPs from the brain because of the strong binding of the probe to the Aβ species in Tg mice. The selectivity of probe toward Aβ plaques was further confirmed by ex vivo fluorescence imaging. Furthermore, T2-weighted ex vivo MRI revealed more dark spots in the brain of Tg than WT mice. Therefore, all these results unanimously evidenced that this NP is a sensitive and efficient NIR/MR dual-modal probe for real-time detecting and monitoring Aβ species in an AD mouse model. We have also developed the first Aβ oligomer-specific gadolinium-based NPs, NP@SiO2@F-SLOH as a multimodal NIR imaging/T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) contrast agent for real-time visualization of Aβ contents in an AD mouse model was reported. Remarkably, the NP@SiO2@F-SLOH was successfully applied for in vivo and ex vivo NIRI with high sensitivity and selectivity for Aβ oligomers and for MRI with good spatial resolution in different age groups in an AD mouse model. Furthermore, the NP probe exhibited an inhibitory effect on Aβ fibrillation and neuroprotection against Aβ-induced toxicity indicating its desirable therapeutic potential for AD. All these results illustrate the tremendous potential of this versatile and sensitive nanomaterial as an effective theranostic MRI nanoprobe for practical use. Furthermore, a new series of Aβ oligomer-targeted NIR emissive dibutylnaphthylamine-based cyanine probes for in vivo and ex vivo imaging of Aβ in AD mouse model has developed. These new fluorophores exhibited strong solvatochromism and a large bathochromic shift of the emission spectrum upon binding with Aβ species, giving rise to advantageous NIR emission. Besides, they showed an intriguingly stronger fluorescence enhancement upon interacting with Aβ oligomers and monomers, and binding affinity toward Aβ oligomers and monomers than Aβ fibrils, suggesting they were selective to Aβ oligomers and monomers. Besides low toxicity, one of the fluorophores, DBAN-SLM, showed remarkably effective inhibitory effect on Aβ aggregation, significant neuroprotection effect against the Aβ-induced toxicities, and suppression on Aβ-induced reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. Because of excellent blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability, good biocompatibility and stability, high specificity towards Aβ oligomers as well as strong turn-on fluorescence upon Aβ binding, DBAN-SLM was successfully applied for in vivo and ex vivo imaging of Aβ in AD mouse model, signifying its great promise as a useful theranostic agent for the early diagnosis and therapy of AD. In addition, several novel series of organelle-specific two-photon (TP) fluorescent probes including BIMC, PSIOH and PSIBOH, VP and VL, MCDBI and MCDI, BTNO, DBAN-SLM for sensing and monitoring pH changes in live cells and tissues in which some of them were able to detect and differentiate cancer/tumor in liver tissues and mouse model were developed. Firstly, a novel and efficient carbazole-benzimidazole-based two-photon ratiometric fluorescence probe, namely BIMC for fast-response lysosomal pH detection and imaging was developed. BIMC exhibits an ideal pKa value of 4.46, which is found useful for quantitative detection and imaging of lysosomal pH change in the linearly proportional range of 3.8 - 5.0. Two-photon ratiometric imaging studies shows that BIMC can selectively monitor pH with excellent photostability and low cytotoxicity in the lysosomes of live cells and in living cancer tissues. Two novel high-resolution ratiometric two-photon (TP) fluorescent probes, namely PSIOH and PSIBOH derived from carbazole-oxazolidine π-conjugated system for effective sensing and monitoring acid pH in a biological system have also been developed. Remarkably, PSIOH exhibited the largest emission shift of ~169 nm from 435 to 604 nm upon pH changing from basic to acidic with an ideal pKa value of 6.6 within a linear pH variation range of 6.2-7.0, which is highly desirable for high-resolution tracking and imaging the minor fluctuation of pH in live cells and tissues. PSIOH also exhibits high pH sensitivity, excellent photostability and reversibility as well as low cytotoxicity. More importantly, this probe was successfully applied to sense and visualize the pH alteration in HeLa cells caused by various types of exogenous stimulation as well as; detect and differentiate cancer/tumor in liver tissues and mouse model, realizing its practical in vitro and in vivo applications. We also reported two novel, highly sensitive and fast responsive carbazole-based ratiometric fluorescent probes with different emission wavelengths, namely MCDBI and MCDI for lysosomal pH detection and imaging. Importantly, the MCDBI and MCDI probes bearing indole and benzoindoles as acid-sensing sites exhibit pKa values of 4.26 and 4.51, respectively, which are ideal for the quantitative analysis of lysosomal pH changes in living cells. These probes exhibited a strong pH-dependent behavior and responded linearly and rapidly to minor pH fluctuations. Moreover, the two biocompatible probes are highly lysosomal targeting, sensitive towards H+ over metal ions and some bioactive molecules, and exhibit excellent photostability and good reversibility. These probes have excellent cell membrane permeability and are further applied successfully to monitor lysosomal pH fluctuations in the lysosomes of HepG2 cells. A ratiometric fluorescent probe namely BTNO was synthesized which exhibited a remarkable ratiometric emission (F456 /F526) enhancement in response to a pH change with a linear range of pH = 9.50 - 7.00 and a pKa value of 7.91 ± 0.03, which is desirable for detection and monitoring the cytoplasmic pH changes. Because of the high fluorescence quantum yield of BTNO, the interferences of the probe on the physiological functions could be greatly reduced. This could provide enhanced measurement sensitivity. The successful demonstration of BTNO in detecting and monitoring the intracellular pH changes in live HeLa cells via a ratiometric approach confirmed that BTNO held a practical potential in biomedical research. Lastly, a mitochondrial pH sensing fluorescent probe, namely HTBT2 displayed a linear fluorescence enhancement at 612 nm in response to pH changes between 8.70 and 7.20 was developed. Its pKa was found to be 8.04 ± 0.02, which would be ideal for mitochondrial pH (pHmito, ~8.0) detection. HTBT2 also exhibited a remarkable large Stokes shift of 176 nm, which could reduce the excitation interference. The fluorescence enhancement of HTBT2 upon decreasing pH was attributed to the facilitation of intramolecular transfer (ICT) and the inhibition of photo-induced electron transfer (PET). Results of live cells imaging studies suggested that HTBT2 showed excellent mitochondrial targeting ability. Importantly, it was successfully applied to visualize mitochondrial pH fluctuations in live cells and differentiate the pHmito difference between cancer cell lines and normal cell lines. Our results consistently supported that HTBT2 holds practical promises for an investigation of physiological processes related to pHmito.

12301317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12301317.value: The development of novel theranostic agents for simultaneous detection and monitoring of toxic and pathogenic amyloid-β (Aβ) species in vivo and attenuation of Aβ-induced toxicity to enable the early detection and intervention of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) has recently drawn tremendous attention. Several novel theranostic agents including neuroprotective Aβ-selective dual-modal imaging nanoprobe, Aβ oligomer-specific multimodal gadolinium-based nanoprobe, and oligomeric Aβ targeted near infrared (NIR) emissive dibutylnaphthylamine-based cyanine probes that not only allows visualization of Aβ species ex vivo and in vivo but also inhibit Aβ self-aggregation and Aβ-induced ROS formation offering desirable therapeutic treatment potential for AD have been developed. Besides, several novel series of organelle-specific two-photon (TP) fluorescent probes for sensing and monitoring pH changes in live cells and tissues which could be used to detect and differentiate cancer/tumor in liver tissues and mouse model were developed. These probes hold practical potential for clinical use in cancer cell identification and differentiation. In short, these theranostic agents provides a powerful tool for an early AD detection and disease progression by monitoring of the pathological features in AD. Our design strategy opens up a new avenue to develop practical and medical relevant imaging tools with treatment potential for diagnosis of AD.

12301417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12301417.value: 全基因组关联分析(GWAS)已经揭示了人类复杂性状的多基因遗传结构， 即存在多个基因共同影响某种复杂性状的形成。多基因遗传结构意味着单个遗传变异点的效应非常弱小，由于单个GWAS收集的样本数量有限，这些弱效应被淹没在遗传数据的背景噪音中。因此，全世界的基因组研究人员正在组成大型的基因组学研究联盟，从而增大样本量。但是，由于基因组数据涉及到个人隐私等因素，研究人员往往不能分享样本的个体基因型数据(invidual-level genotype data)而只能分享汇总统计量(summary statistics)。 来自GWAS的汇总统计量的数据正在迅速积累，而且该类型的数据往往由基因组学研究联盟的大样本分析产生，具有很高的可靠性。如何充分利用这一类型的数据更好地探索复杂性状的遗传结构？这一问题到目前为止依然是一个难题。在本研究中，我们针对这一问题提出了系统的统计学方法并在真实数据上进行了尝试。初步结果表明，我们的方法具有良好的统计学性质，所开发的算法能够适应大规模基因组数据的分析。基于此，我们提出进一步深入研究的具体方案。我们相信，该项目所开发的方法能更好地服务于深入理解复杂性状的遗传结构。

12301417.label: Realisation of objectives
12301417.value: 1 Develop statistical models and algorithms to make the most efficient use of summary statistics We first consider combining summary statistics with individual-level data. To do so, we developed a novel statistical approach LEP [1] which integrates both types of data by LEveraging Pleiotropy to increase the statistical power of risk variants identification and the accuracy of risk prediction. The algorithm for parameter estimation is developed to handle genome-wide-scale data. To uncover the mechanistic links between genetic variants and complex traits, we propose a collaborative mixed model (CoMM) [3] to investigate the mechanistic role of associated variants in complex traits. The key idea is built upon the emerging scientific evidence that genetic effects at the cellular level are much stronger than those at the organismal level. Briefly, CoMM combines two models: the first model relating gene expression with genotype and the second model relating phenotype with predicted gene expression using the first model. The two models are fitted jointly in CoMM, such that the uncertainty in predicting gene expression has been fully accounted for. Along this direction, we have developed CoMM-S2 [9] which only requires GWAS summary statistics as input. Furthermore, we have also developed a method called Tis-CoMM-S2 [7] which can jointly analyze GWAS data and transcriptome data from multiple tissues. We have also developed scalable Bayesian methods to handle large-scale genomic data sets, including BIVAS [2], VIMCO [5], and PDAS [10]. In contrast to using Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC), these methods explored the computational efficiency of variational Bayes methods. We showed that statistical accuracy obtained from variational Bayes was comparable with the results from MCMC on small-scale data sets, while it would be much more efficient than MCMC on large-scale data sets. These works have been accepted in Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics, Bioinformatics, Biometrics, and Statistical Science. 2. Develop R packages for the proposed parallel algorithm Yes, we have made the developed software publicly available. The R package "BIVAS": https://github.com/YangLabHKUST/bivas The R package "IGREX": https://github.com/YangLabHKUST/iGREX The R package "CoMM": https://github.com/gordonliu810822/CoMM The R package "CoMM-S2": https://github.com/gordonliu810822/CoMM The R package "LEP": https://github.com/daviddaigithub/LEP The R package "REMI": https://github.com/gordonliu810822/REMI The R package "MR-LDP": https://github.com/QingCheng0218/MR.LDP The R package "VIMCO": https://github.com/XingjieShi/VIMCO The R package "TisCoMM": https://github.com/XingjieShi/TisCoMM/. 3 Evaluate model performance using comprehensive simulation studies and compare analysis results with individual-level-data-based analysis Through comprehensive simulation studies, we demonstrated the advantages of developed methods over existing methods. For example, we performed simulations to compare LEP [1] with BVSR, GPA, and Lasso. We also conducted simulation studies to demonstrate that CoMM-S2 [9] has comparable performance as the individual-level method CoMM [3]. Furthermore, we show that CoMM-S2 generally performs as well or better than competing methods that also utilize summary statistics, including S-PrediXcan, ridge regression, and Enet. 4 Apply the proposed methods in real data analysis We applied LEP [1] to perform an integrative analysis of Crohn’s disease from WTCCC and summary statistics from GWAS of some other diseases, such as Type 1 diabetes, Ulcerative colitis, and Primary biliary cirrhosis. LEP was able to significantly increase the statistical power of identifying risk variants and improve the risk prediction accuracy from 63.39% (±0.58%) to 68.33% (±0.32%) using about 195 000 variants. To demonstrate the advantages of CoMM and CoMM-S2 over existing methods, we applied CoMM to analyze 25 traits in NFBC1966 and Genetic Epidemiology Research on Aging (GERA) studies by integrating transcriptome information from the Genetic European in Health and Disease (GEUVADIS) Project. The results indicate that by leveraging regulatory information, CoMM can effectively improve the power of prioritizing risk variants. Regarding the computational efficiency, CoMM can complete the analysis of the NFBC1966 dataset and GERA datasets in 2 and 18min, respectively. By applying IGREX [6] and Tiss-CoMM-S2 [7] to the GTEX data, we not only prioritize gene-trait associations but also detect the tissue-specific role of candidate target genes in complex traits. 5 Investigate the theoretical properties of the proposed methods from both computational and statistical perspectives. We consider a fundamental question: whether it is possible to perform regression analysis if only summary statistics (Marginal information) are available. The answer is no because the correlations among predictors are not available. Fortunately, in the context of GWAS, the correlations can be estimated from the 1000 Genome Project, which makes regress with marginal information possible. We propose an L1 penalized approach, REMI [4], to estimate high dimensional regression coefficients with marginal information and external reference samples (i.e., from the 1000 Genomes Project). We establish an upper bound on the error of the REMI estimator, which has the same order as that of the minimax error bound of Lasso with complete individual-level data. In particular, when marginal information is obtained from a large number of samples together with a small number of reference samples, REMI yields good estimation and prediction results and outperforms the Lasso because the sample size of accessible individual-level data can be limited.

12301417.label: Major findings and research outcome
12301417.value: To understand the genetic basis of complex human phenotypes, thousands of genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have been conducted over the past decade. Worldwide researchers are forming genomic consortia to collect samples and share them with each other. However, many practical issues arise in data sharing due to regulations in privacy protection and logistics in data transportation and data storage. As a result, the individual-level data (i.e., the genotypes of each individual) is difficult to obtain while summary statistics (e.g., the estimated effect size of each variant and its standard error given by univariate linear regression) are often publicly available. In this project, we have developed statistical methods to explore the genetic architecture of complex phenotypes using summary statistics. As these methods only require GWAS summary statistics as input, we refer to them as summary-level statistical methods. We have shown that they can be applied to (a) characterization of the overall genetic contribution to a disease (heritability estimation); (b) quantiﬁcation of co-heritability, i.e., the genetic correlation between two diseases; (c) localization of genetic risk variants; and (d) colocalizing risk variants that affect multiple phenotypes. We have shown that the statistical accuracy of summary-level methods is comparable to individual-level methods which require both genotypes and phenotypes of individuals in GWAS. We have also shown that, compared with individual-level methods, the computational cost of summary-level methods can be greatly reduced. With the developed summary-level methods, we have provided a quantitative analysis of the genetic architecture of complex traits/diseases. First, we have shown that most of the complex traits/diseases are highly polygenic. Most of the heritability is contributed by many genetic risk variants with small effects rather than a few variants with large effects. Second, we have also identified many variants with pleiotropic effects. Third, we have also found that many diseases/traits are genetically correlated. Fourth, we have quantitatively shown how genetic variants regulate gene expression in tissue-specific manners and further affect phenotype variations.

12301417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12301417.value: Despite the fruitful findings, GWASs are limited by a lack of ancestral diversity. According to the GWAS Diversity Monitor, approximately 88.9% of GWAS participants have been of European ancestry to date. Non-European populations are severely under-represented in GWASs. For example, the proportions of participants of East Asian (EAS) and African ancestries are less than 6.9% and 0.4%, respectively. Most of GWAS findings are based on individuals of European ancestry. Unfortunately, these findings may not be directly extrapolated to non-European ancestries. Genetic studies with diversified ancestries are important in achieving global health equity. Trans-ancestry association mapping (TRAM) aiming to identify risk genetic variants across ancestries, particularly, in the under-represented populations, is a critical step toward precision medicine. TRAM has two main challenges. First, the genetic architecture of a complex trait can be heterogeneous across ancestries. Trait-associated variants may have different allele frequencies and effect sizes. Linkage disequilibrium patterns can also vary across ancestries. Second, confounding bias, such as population stratification, is still a major problem for large-scale GWAS data analysis. We anticipate that the more statistical methods developed for TRAM will be applicable to under-represented populations to provide a promising future for personalized healthcare guidance, disease screening, and therapeutic intervention.

12301417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12301417.value: Since the completion of the Human Genome Project in 2003, genome-wide association studies (GWASs) have been conducted to identify genetic risk variants associated with a wide range of human diseases/traits. Worldwide researchers are forming genomic consortia to collect samples and share them with each other. However, many practical issues arise in data sharing due to regulations in privacy protection and logistics in data transportation and data storage. Recently, summary statistics from GWASs become publicly accessible. Mining the rich data resource provides us opportunities to deepen our understanding of the genetic basis of complex diseases/traits. In this project, we have developed statistical methods which only require summary-level data as input, greatly facilitating quantitative analysis of genetic architectures of complex diseases/traits, including heritability estimation, co-heritability estimation, and colocalization of risk variants of multiple diseases/traits. These quantitative methods generate new scientific discoveries and contribute to precision health and precision medicine.

12301717.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12301717.value: 阶数确定的双重岭比阈值准则及其应用

12301717.label: Project Objectives
12301717.value: To deal with underdetermination issue, we will propose a new general methodology from which criteria for order / dimensionality determination can be constructed. The method is based on eigedecomposition for target matrices and the ratios of eigenvalues that are used to measure relative magnitudes of eigenvalues. To alleviate the effect from dominating eigenvalues, we will `standardize' all eigenvalues and then use two rounds of ratios to better separate the ratio at the true order or dimension from the others. To avoid the instability of ratios of which two eigenvalues are both close to zero, we will add ridges in the ratios. Unlike all existing eigenvalue-based criteria, we do not simply use minimizer or maximizer to define an estimate, while instead use a thresholding to select a maximum index as an estimate. This method may handle multiple local minima problems from which all existing methods suffer at the sample level, and largely avoid underdetermination due to smaller minimizer/maximizer than the true order or dimension. In hypothesis testing, local alternative regression models with more linear combinations/covariates are considered to check the sensitivity of a goodness-of-fit test for the hypothetical regression model with less linear combinations/convariates. As the local models converge to the hypothetical model at certain rate, but the corresponding number of linear combinations/covariates is not convergent, the criterion has more than one local minimum. We then discuss at what rate the determination can be correct and at what rate, the underdetermination would happen. The basic idea will be also applied to determine the dimension in multivariate linear regressions with high dimensional and tensor data. The method is applied to ultra-high dimensional approximate factor models to determine the number of common factors. We will also consider the similar problems in principal component analysis and independent component analysis. The simulations and real data analysis will be conducted to examine their performance in finite sample scenarios. We also explore its potential for other order or dimensionality problems with, say, functional data and longitudinal data.

12301717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12301717.value: Popularly used eigendecomposition-based criteria such as BIC type, ratio estimation and principal component-based criterion often underdetermine model order for semiparametric regression models, multivariate linear models, approximate factor models, principal component analysis and independent component analysis. This longstanding problem is mainly caused by the existence of one or two dominating eigenvalues compared to other nonzero eigenvalues. To alleviate this difficulty, we propose thresholding double ridge ratio criteria such that the true orders in different problems can be better identified and are less underdetermined. Unlike all existing eigendecomposition-based criteria, these types of criteria could define consistent estimates without requiring the existence of unique minimum or maximum and can then handle possible multiple local minima or maxima scenarios. This generic strategy would be readily applied to the problems with functional data or tensor data. In this project, we investigate the order determination for general sufficient dimension reduction theory with fixed and divergent dimensions; for local models that converge to its limiting model with fewer projected covariates, discuss when the order can be consistently estimated, when cannot; and for approximate factor models, study the estimation consistency for the number of common factors. The method will also be applied to functional data and tensor data. Numerical studies will be conducted to examine the finite sample performance of the method. This research project investigates an important but longstanding problem in order determination in several models, and expect the new methodology and theory developed in the course of the project will have a lasting impact in the relevant fields. 常用的基于特征分解的准则，例如BIC类型，比率估计，基于主成分的准则常常低估了模型的阶数。这些模型包括半参数回归模型，多元线性模型，近似因子 模型、主成分分析和独立分量分析。这个悬而未决的问题主要是由一两个主导的特征值与其他非零特征值相比过大造成的。为了减轻这一困难，我们提出了双重岭比阈值准则使得在各个问题中的模型阶数顺序可以更好地识别，也更少低估。与文献中所有的基于特征分解的准则不同，我们的准则可以定义出相合估计；无需最小或最大值存在的唯一性，从而可以处理可能有多个局部极小值或最大值情况。这种通用方法可以很容易地应用于函数型数据或张量数据。在这个项目中，我们研究了这个方法在维数是固定和发散情况下的充分降维理论；局部回归模型的定阶问题--讨论何时阶数可以相合地估计，合适不行；近似因子模型的共同因子个数的相合估计问题。同时，也进行数值研究。 这个项目研究一个重要但悬而未决的问题，期望新的方法和理论对相关领域产生持久的影响。

12301717.label: Realisation of objectives
12301717.value: In this report, we conclude that all the objectives have been achieved with some other applications. First, we proposed a general order dimensionality criterion and proved its estimation consistency. The criterion was constructed by using the idea of ridge ratio as we described in Objective 1. In the theoretical and empirical studies, we can see that this criterion can successfully avoid the non-uniqueness problem of minimum or maximum, which is an issue for many existing criteria. This criterion is then useful for hypothesis testing when we tried to construct adaptive-to-model tests. Then the relevant results have been applied to determine the banding width of large dimensional matrices, an estimaition problem for a biased partial linear single index model and an estimation problem in the image processing problem. We have also used it to study the banding estimation in ultra-high dimensional matrix. The numerical studies also showed its good performance.

12301817.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12301817.value: 具有爆破解非綫性拋物方程的數值算法

12301817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12301817.value: In this project, we are interested in the accurate numerical solution of nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs) whose solutions exhibit blow-up, i.e., become unbounded in finite time. Such nonlinear equations arise in many applications, including in plasma physics, combustion, turbulent flow, nonlinear optics and population dynamics. The main difficulty in solving such problems numerically lies in the highly nonlinear structure and the large function values and gradients of the solution prior to blow-up. This makes fixed, uniform grids in space and time inadequate. Although there have been studies in the literature on moving mesh methods that preserve spatial scale invariance, less is known about time-stepping methods that preserve the structure of blow-up solutions. Since it is unrealistic to attempt to design one-size-fits-all methods for such a wide array of nonlinear phenomena, our project will concentrate on two classes of problems with qualitatively different behaviour: parabolic PDEs with dominant reaction terms, and the focusing nonlinear Schrodinger equation. Here, we propose a new class of specialized methods, called space-time B-methods, which preserve both the spatial and temporal blow-up structure of the problems under consideration. For problems where the reaction terms are dominant, the construction is such that the methods can exactly integrate the underlying differential equation without the spatial derivative terms. Indeed, for a fixed spatial discretization of the reaction-diffusion equation, the truncation errors are much smaller for B-methods than for standard methods, leading to much more accurate answers in the former case. To increase accuracy in the approximation of the spatial term, we use a time-dependent mesh that becomes denser near developing singularities as the problem evolves. A key aspect we plan to investigate is how to control the density of the spatial mesh so that the spatial discretization error is similar to the time truncation error everywhere in the domain. For the nonlinear Schrodinger equation, we use a similar idea as for temporal B-methods in order to express the solution in terms of a parameter that remains bounded as one approaches blow-up. The method then computes a mesh that equidistributes the error in terms of the new parameter, which becomes denser as the singularity develops. The time step is chosen based on estimates on the rate of change of the parameter as well as its distance to the pole of the blow-up function. 爆破現象，即方程的解在有限時間內趨向無窮，經常出現在各類非綫性拋物型偏微分方程模型中，在非綫性光學、燃燒理論、湍流理論等方面具有重要的應用。由於解的奇異性質，該類微分方程需要採用更為精確的數值方法求解以滿足實際問題的需求。然而，通用的數值算法對此類具有爆破解的問題均不適用，這是因爲這些算法所使用的時間步長或者空間網格都是預先設定的，不能有效地預估奇點附近的解。本項研究的目的是結合移動網格與B方法，充分利用非綫性拋物型方程本身的幾何特性，設計出一套能夠自動調節時間與空間網格的算法，提高數值解的精確度。實踐上，我們將針對反應佔優拋物型偏微分方程與非線性薛定諤方程兩類模型開展細緻的研究工作。

12301917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12301917.value: 本項目考慮采用基於核函數的無網格方法來求解拋物型偏微分方程。無網格方法已經廣泛應用於求解穩態問題，然而當科學工程中出現了擴散或分散等物理現象時，例如水汙染或熱流擴散，就需要再引進時間項。本項目將無網格方法應用於求解此類問題。我們計劃建立新穎的數值方法，並提供理論分析。在定義了穩態問題中非常重要的標準（不是基於節點）和基於節點的試驗空間的大體框架後，我們首先證明在試驗空間內存在某些函數，它們能很好地逼近精確解。 其收斂性依賴於使用的核函數和解的光滑度，但不依賴於拋物型方程。下一個具有挑戰性的工作是提出數值上穩定的方法來根據給定的數據計算試驗空間內的函數，從而和參考解具有同樣快的收斂率。 在求解穩態橢圓偏微分方程時，已有文獻表明：無論在應用還是理論分析方面，采用比基函數個數多的配點能得到更好的結果。因此，我們的方法將會使用這種配點方式。這不僅能有效地降低問題規模，而且是非對稱的Kansa強形式配點法的穩定性和收斂性的必要條件。然而，該多配點算法至今還未被應用於求解拋物型偏微分方程。 因此，當求解時間連續的拋物型方程時，我們可以通過采用強形式的多配點法得到其半離散的解。為保證穩定性以及降低計算的複雜性，我們會將它與最小二乘方法相結合。以熱方程為例，多配點法能很好地近似非離散的解析演化算子。目前，基於多配點和試驗空間，初步的數值試驗已表明帶權重的最小二乘法優於一般的無網格方法。進一步，我們將致力於其理論分析。本項目主要是為求解拋物型偏微分方程提供一種新的數值方法，並為其建立一套堅實的理論基礎。

12301917.label: Realisation of objectives
12301917.value: In our Annual Progress Report, we reported that theoretical results in [Li, Cheung & L, Appl. Math. Compt. 2019] were established to find trial functions approximate the initial condition in Objective 1. For the sake of the numerical Objectives 3-5, our numerical investigations in [Li & L, Eng. Anal. Bdy. Elt. 2019] leaded to deterministic formula for the generic constants in PDE theory, which depend on the proportion of measures of the Dirichlet and Neumann boundaries, dimensionless volume ratios of the boundary and domain, and kernel smoothness. In terms of our work on sparse systems in Objectives 6-7, a least-squares meshfree finite difference method was proposed in [Petras, L, Piret & Ruuth, J. Compt. Phys. 2019] to solve manifold PDEs on moving surface. Now, we report how we achieved the most theoretically ambitious objective 1 of this project. To give a rigid convergence analysis for solving parabolic PDEs with least-squares kernel-based collocation methods (LS-KCM), we considered both Rothe’s methods (a.k.a. methods of horizontal lines) and methods of lines, i.e., discretize in time vs. in space first. The former called for convergent elliptic solvers. On top of our previous convergence theories [1] in domains with flat geometry, we provide in [Chen & L, SIAM Numer. Anal. 2020] a counterpart convergence estimates for LS-KCM for elliptic PDEs on closed manifolds. The proposed method was shown to be far less computational demanding than another kernel-based embedding method we used in [2] and comparable to those in the local method in [3]. Within our proposed algorithm, one can find a least-squares pseudospectral subroutine that were designed to approximate collocation conditions of differential operator. This is the solution to Objectives 6 that allow us to generate sparse system using global techniques. As far as full convergence theory goes, we can only let the spatial error at each time steps to accumulate and time-stepping control, i.e., CFL, remains ad hoc. Next, we turn our focus to the method of lines. In [Chen, Cheung & L, arXiv 2021], we provide a complete error analysis for the fully-discretized LS-KCM surface diffusion solution. Initial condition was projected to trial space as described in our Annual Progress Report. Semi-discretized (in space) trial solutions were analyzed based on the method of comparison via optimizations. A major, and somehow surprising, finding is that the theoretical derived fully-discretized solution is not a solution of ODEs but difference equations. In the same paper, we show that the solutions of ODEs and difference equations are indeed high order approximation of each other’s. Thus, our convergence estimate did apply to the commonly used straightforward approach, viz, oversampling the PDEs with a pseudoinverse to yield an ODE system that can then be solved by black-box ODE solvers with well-established automatic time-stepping. To complete Objectives 2, 5 & 7, we compare with a kernel-based Galerkin method [4] and find that both methods have similar accuracy (given the same number of basis) but required far fewer collocation (c.f. quadrature) points. Furthermore, we use the standard RK45 to simulate Allen-Cahn equations and show that the concern of CFL and numerical stability in Objectives 3-4 were eliminated. Our work on sparse systems also includes two local methods. Both are finite difference (FD) type methods on scattered data. In [Mishra, Fasshauer, Sen & L, Compt. Math. Appl. 2019], FD weights were generated via some tunable hybrid kernels. Whereas in [Tang, Fu, Chen & L, Appl. Math. 12301917.label: Major findings and research outcome
12301917.value: All objectives were addressed in the eight (with five newly added) peer-review articles published. Journals that I published or under review, which are in range of the top of the 2020 Web of Science SCE Journal Citation Reports respective category, include • Applied Mathematics and Computation [Mathematics, Applied 7/265] • Applied Mathematics Letters [Mathematics, Applied 8/265] • Computers & Mathematics with Applications [Mathematics, Applied 16/265] • SIAM Journal on Numerical Analysis [Mathematics, Applied 21/265] • Journal of Computational Physics [Physics, Mathematical 6/55] • Communications in Computational Physics [Physics, Mathematical 7/55] • Engineering Analysis with Boundary Elements [Mathematics, Interdisciplinary applications 29/108] These articles can roughly be classified into two main groups; the first is heavy on novel algorithm developments, theoretical results, and numerical analysis. These articles were mostly published in applied Mathematical journals. The second focuses on numerical experiments and applications were published in physics and engineering journals.

12301917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12301917.value: Our discoveries, including error estimate, numerical formulations, etc., in the reports are new and can fill up some missing gap between theories and applications. Yet, our theories are on linear problems. In almost all the publications in the report, we included some semi- or quasi-linear parabolic PDEs, i.e., Allen-Cahn, Cahn-Hilliard, pattern formation equations, etc. An important step forward is to work on kernel theories for quasi- or non-linear PDEs. Indeed, as of the year of writing, we can already see theoretical papers for quasi-linear elliptic equations from the meshfree community.

12301917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12301917.value: This project developed some novel algorithms for the unsymmetric radial basis function (RBF) collocation method, which is also known as the Kansa method in the community. This class of numerical methods is meshfree because there is no triangularization involved. As long as one knows how to program for an interpolation problem, it only takes minutes to understand and code up something for the Kansa method. Since invented, the Kansa method has been widely used in vast numbers of applications in physics and engineering. As Kansa methods gain popularity, this work also provides ways to stably solve the resulting severely ill-conditioned linear systems, tweaks to improve robustness of the methods, and algorithms to perform numerical differentiation.

12302017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12302017.value: 在此項目中，我們主要關注若干電磁波和彈性波反問題的理論和數值研究。 在項目的第一部份，受腦電圖及腦磁圖等腦成像技術的啟發，我們研究如下一類關於電磁波轉播中的反問題。考慮一個有界區域中包含有一種非均勻介質，同時這個非均勻介質中有一些未知的電流，電流的存在會產生向外傳播的電磁波。我們所要研究的反問題是通過在區域邊界上對電磁波場的測量來同時重構出區域內部的未知電流，以及區域內部非均勻介質的材料參數。對此類反問題，我們將致力於建立一些理論上的充分結果，即在何種情形下，人們一定可以通過測量到的數據同時重構出這些未知量。一方面，這些理論結果在某些情形下，即充分性條件都被滿足的時候，給人們以“信心”一定可以重構出未知的東西；另一方面，在某些情形下，即充分性條件不被滿足的時候，給人們以“方向”，如何漸近的逼近這些未知的量，或者去發展別的探測手段。除此之外，我們也將致力於把這些關於電磁反問題的同時重構研究推廣到相關的彈性波反問題中。此類研究對地震成像科學中，人們若想通過對地震波的測量數據，同時重構出震源和震源附近的地質概況有重要意義。 在項目的第二部分，我們主要考慮一類新型的人機互動裝置的數學設計。現今，人们主要使用诸如鼠标，键盘，触摸屏等基於文本或圖像用戶界面的裝置進行輸入和輸出。不過，也有一些新型的利用攝像機捕捉人的肢體語言來達到人機互動進行輸入輸出的技術被發展出來。我們將致力於從數學上設計兩種新型的輸入輸出裝置。此類裝置將利用電磁波反散射技術來捕捉人的肢體語言，從而達到相應的人機互動目的。此項目中，我們將對此類新型裝置的設計建立相應的數學模型，並發展中相應的數學和算法技巧來處理相關難題。

12302017.label: Realisation of objectives
12302017.value: The grant has been used to support my research on the theoretical and numerical studies of several inverse problems associated with electromagnetic and elastic wave propagations. With the support of the grant, we have achieved all the objectives of this project, which can be sumarized as follows. 1. We established the identifiability results for the inverse problem associated with the Maxwell system in simultaneously recovering an unknown electric source term and the surrounding medium parameters inside a bounded body by the corresponding EM boundary measurements. This is first objective of the project and the research finding is contained in the paper [DLU19] (please refer to the discussion in Section 6.1 of this paper as well as the PDF file attached in Part C). 2. We established the identifiability results for the inverse problem associated with the Lame system in simultaneously recovering an unknown elastic source term and the surrounding medium parameters inside a bounded body by the corresponding elastic boundary measurements. This is the 2nd objective of the In fact, we have obtained far-reaching results that even go beyond the original objective. Specifically, we have established a novel model for the Earth's geomagnetic field. Moreover, motivated by related applications, we have also considered our study in the fractional and random settings. The results are contained in the following papers [LLS18], [DLL19], [CL19], [CLL19], [LLM19] (please refer to the discussion in Section 6.1 of these papers as well as the PDF files attached in Part C) 3. We developed the mathematical principle and numerical reconstruction strategies for the design of a novel instruction/input device based on motion trajectory identification using electromagnetic waves. This is the 3rd objective 3 of the project and the results are contained in the two papers [GLLW19] and [WSGLL19]. 4. We developed the mathematical principle and numerical reconstruction strategies for the design of a novel instruction/input device based on gesture recognition using electromagnetic waves. This is the 4th objective of the project and the result is contained in the paper [LLS18]. Moreover, the grant has also provided partial support to my research on metamaterials, localizing electromagnetic fields and magnetic anomalies detections by using geomagnetic monitoring. The results obtained so far are contained in the following journal publications [DLL19, BLL18, HLL18, LL18,LRX19, DLL20], which have all acknowledged the support of this grant.

Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12302017.value: The project is concerned with the theoretical and numerical studies of a novel class of inverse problems associated with electromagnetic and elastic waves. Specifically, we consider a special situation that a medium body (whose medium content is unknown) contains an unknown source. The source generates a wave field which propagates outside the medium body, and brings information of both the unknown source and the unknown medium parameters to exterior observer. The inverse problem is recover simultaneously both the unknown source and the unknown medium by the far-field measurement. This type of inverse problems has a strong background of practical applications including brain imaging, earthquake detection and computing technology. In this project, we established the mathematical models for different applications and conducted comprehensive theoretical and algorithmic studies. The results obtained in this project may produce important impacts to the practical applications mentioned above.

12302117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12302117.value: In view of the concerns over increasing global demand for energy and the global-warming from the combustion of fossil fuels, developing a clean and sustainable alternative to fossil fuels is a matter of utmost urgency. Solar-energy is a preeminent candidate. Whilst there are many possible ways of harnessing solar-energy, one of the most promising approaches is to mimick the natural process of photosynthesis. Artificial light-driven water-reduction into hydrogen by solar-light has received tremendous attention as hydrogen is considered as an ideal energy source with high energy capacity and no carbon footprint during its combustion. Since the pioneering work by Fujishima and Honda on water-splitting over semiconductor photocatalysts, extensive efforts have been made to construct efficient heterogeneous photocatalytic hydrogen generation systems. However, wide-bandgap semiconductors are only active under UV-irradiation, only a small fraction of the incoming solar-energy can be utilized which severely limits their practical applications. Dye-sensitization, in which the surface of the semiconductor is rationally modified with photosensitizer, is a powerful strategy to enable the visible and/or infrared light-harvesting by semiconductors and is critical to increase photon-to-hydrogen efficiency. So far, the most frequently employed photosensitizers are noble metal complexes. The main drawbacks of these complexes are their relatively poor molar absorptivity for eﬃcient photon capture, high-cost and difficulty of purification for future large-scale application. On these aspects, metal-free organic photosensitizers are shown to be good strategic designs due to their structural diversity, excellent light-harvesting abilities, simple synthesis as well as low cost. To date, the hydrogen production activity obtained by organic dyes is moderate and is still far from being economically viable for real applications. Photo-deterioration under excessive light soaking and quick photogenerated charge recombination are the main issues for such efficiency limitation. Exploration for stable and efficient dyes is urgently required. Herein, we propose to develop new suite of robust metal-free organic photosensitizers with improved light-capture ability for solar-hydrogen-generation from water. Starburst and di-anchoring motifs with donor-π-acceptor molecular framework will be pursued, which not only extend the spectral responsive region of the photocatalytic system but also favour the generation of long-lived energetic charge-separated states of dyes after light-absorption to retard charge-recombination. Components with their highly stable cationic radical species will be used to account for the durability issue. With our strength in synthetic chemistry, optimization of the dye component for water-splitting will be garnered through systematic variation of the donors, π-bridges, acceptors/anchoring groups and other substituents in these photosensitizers. 由於人類社會對能源與日俱增的需求以及化石燃料燃燒所帶來的嚴重的全球變暖效應，發展一種可持續的清潔能源來代替化石燃料迫在眉睫。太陽能是這類型新能源的優越備選之一。太陽能的利用方式繁多，其中最有望解決能源問題的途徑是仿照光合作用的自然過程。人工控制下的光催化水還原產氫已經得到了極大的關注，因為氫氣被認為是一種理想的能源，它不僅具有高能量容量，而且燃燒時無碳排放量。學者Fujishima 和 Honda利用半導體光催化劑分解水的先導性工作鼓舞更多的研究人員探究和構建高效的均相光催化生成氫氣的體系。然而，由於寬能帶半導體僅在紫外輻射下具有催化活性，所以只有很小部分照射於催化劑上的太陽能能被利用，這極大地限制了光催化產氫體系的實際應用。染料敏化，即用光敏劑理性地修飾半導體表面，是一種實現半導體在可見光甚至紅外區域光捕獲的有效策略，而且這種方法能極大提高產氫效率。目前，最常見的光敏劑是一類貴金屬有機絡合物，但是這類材料捕捉光子的能力較差，摩爾吸光係數較低，成本高而且難以純化，限制了將來大規模的製備。考慮到這些弊端，不含金屬的純有機光敏劑由於其結構的多樣性，卓越的光捕獲能力，簡便的合成路線以及低廉的成本而成為非常具有前景的材料。迄今為止，有機染料的產氫活性中等，從經濟上可行性來講，離實際應用相去甚遠。體系在過渡曝光下，光子衰減和快速的光生電荷重組成為效能限制的主要的問題。因此，探索穩定而高效的染料是迫切的。鑑於以上背景，我們計劃發展一類耐受性高的，在光分解水產氫體系中具有較高光捕獲能力的無金屬有機光敏劑。我們會繼續研究具有強發光性和雙錨定結構的供體-π受體分子框架，這不僅擴展了光催化體系的光譜響應區域，也有助於在吸收太陽能後，染料的長壽命、高活力的電荷分離態的生成，從而延緩電荷重組。此外，引入的高穩定性陽離子自由基的結構利於增加產物的耐受性。利用我們在合成化學領域的優勢，通過系統地改變這些光敏劑分子中的供體、π橋基團、受體或錨點基團以及其他取代基的結構來優化用於水分解產氫的光敏染料的性能。

12302117.label: Realisation of objectives
12302117.value: Study 1 (completed): Panchromatic Sensitization with ZnII Porphyrin-Based Photosensitizers for Light-Driven Hydrogen Production (ChemSusChem 2018, 11, 2517–2528) In this study, three molecular photosensitizers with carboxylic acid anchors for attachment to platinized titanium dioxide nanoparticles were studied for light-driven hydrogen production from a fully aqueous medium with ascorbic acid as the sacrificial electron donor. Two zinc(II) porphyrin (ZnP)-based photosensitizers were used to examine the effect of panchromatic sensitization on the photocatalytic hydrogen generation (Objective 1). A dyad molecular design was used to construct a difluoro boron-dipyrromethene (bodipy)-conjugated ZnP photosensitizer (ZnP-dyad), whereas the other one featured an electron-donating diarylamino moiety (YD2-o-C8). To probe the use of the ZnP scaffold in this particular energy conversion process, an organic photosensitizer without the ZnP moiety (Bodipy-dye) was also synthesized for comparison. Ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy was adopted to map out the energy transfer processes occurring in the dyad and to establish the bodipy-based antenna effect (Objective 2). In particular, the systems with YD2-o-C8 and ZnP-dyad achieved a remarkable initial activity for the production of hydrogen with an initial turnover frequency (TOFi) higher than 300h-1 under white light irradiation (Objective 3). The use of ZnP photosensitizers in dye-sensitized photocatalysis for the hydrogen evolution reaction in this study indicated the importance of the panchromatic sensitization capability for the development of light-absorbing photosensitizers. Study 2 (completed): Molecular Engineering of Robust Starburst-Based Organic Photosensitizers for Highly Efficient Photocatalytic Hydrogen Generation from Water (https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.chemmater.2c00556) In this work, six donor−donor−π−acceptor triphenylamine-based starburst organic dyes with different electron-donating moieties and thiophene-based π-linkers were synthesized and characterized (Objective 1). Their photophysical and electrochemical properties, together with their photocatalytic hydrogen evolution performance as photosensitizers, were investigated (Objective 2). Distinctive and prolonged hydrogen evolution performances of these photosensitizers under visible-light irradiation from water in their platinized-TiO2 composites were demonstrated: a turnover number (TON) of up to 24900 (252 h) with 1560 μmol (37.6 mL) hydrogen produced, an initial turnover frequency (TOFi) of 1130 h−1, initial activity (Activityi) of 705 mmol g−1 h−1, and initial apparent quantum yield (AQYi) of 12.1% (Objective 3). To the best of our knowledge, according to the TOF and TON values, the designed photosensitizer system is one of the most efficient and robust photocatalytic H2 generation systems adopting a TiO2-anchoring molecular photosensitizer in the literature. The results showed that the starburst triarylamine-donor-moiety with phenothiazine functionality and the alkyl chain on the thiophene π-linker could boost the performance and longevity of the photocatalytic system, providing a powerful strategy for the development of starburst-based highly-efficient and robust donor−donor−π−acceptor organic photosensitizers in the future. Study 3 (completed): Development of Strong Visible-Light-Absorbing Cyclometalated Iridium(III) Complexes for Robust and Efficient Light-Driven Hydrogen Production (Chem. Eur. J. 2022, 28, e202104575) In this study, a series of cyclometalated Ir(III) complexes (Ir1–Ir5), featuring different electron-donating substituents to enhance the absorptivity, have been synthesized and studied as photosensitizers for light-driven hydrogen production from water (Objectives 1,2). Ir6–Ir7 were prepared as fundamental systems for comparisons. Electron donors, including 9-phenylcarbazole, triphenylamine, 4,4’-dimethoxytriphenylamine, 4,4’-di(N-hexylcarbazole) triphenylamine moieties were introduced on 6-(thiophen-2-yl)phenanthridine-based cyclometalating ligands to explore the donor effect on the hydrogen evolution performance of these cationic Ir(III) complexes. Remarkably, Ir4 with 4,4’-dimethoxytriphenylamine achieved the highest turn-over number (TON) of 12300 and initial turnover frequency (TOFi) of 394 h-1, with initial activity (activityi) of 547000 µmol g-1 h-1 and initial apparent quantum yield (AQYi) of 9.59%, under the illumination of blue light-emitting diodes for 105h, which demonstrated a stable three-component photocatalytic system with high efficiency (Objective 3). The TON in this study is the highest value reported to date among the similar photocatalytic systems using Ir(III) complexes with Pt nanoparticles as catalyst. The great potential of using triphenylamine-based Ir(III) photosensitizers in boosting photocatalytic performance has also been shown. Study 4 (completed): Photophysical characteristics and photosensitizing abilities of thieno[3,2-b]thiophene-Based photosensitizers for photovoltaic and photocatalytic applications (J. Photochem. Photobio. A: Chem. 2021, 406, 112979) In this work, six donor-π-acceptor organic dyes based on thieno[3,2-b]thiophene π-linker comprising different alkyl side chains were synthesized and characterized (Objectives 1,2). Their photophysical and electrochemical properties were studied and their corresponding performances as photosensitizers in dye-sensitized solar cells (DSSCs) and photocatalytic hydrogen production systems were also investigated. A power conversion efficiency of 5.25% in DSSCs and a decent hydrogen TON of 5170 (48h) in platinized-TiO2 hydrogen production system were demonstrated (Objective 3). The results indicated that alkyl chain engineering is one of the crucial steps in designing a superior photosensitizer. Study 5 (completed): Stepwise Access of Emissive Ir(III) Complexes Bearing a Multi-Dentate Heteroaromatic Chelate: Fundamentals and Applications (Inorg. Chem. 2022, 61, 4384−4393) Three multi-dentate coordinated chelates LnH2 (n = 1, 2, and 3), comprising a linked 1-(pyridin-2-yl)ethylbenzene and one pyrazolyl pyridine unit and showing either tridentate or tetradentate coordination modes, are successfully designed and synthesized and characterized (Objectives 1,2). Dinuclear Ir(III) complexes [Ir(κ4-Ln)(μ-Cl)]2 bearing tetradentate coordinated κ4-Ln chelate (2a, n=1; 2b, n=2; 2c, n=3) were next obtained en route from the respective intermediate [Ir(κ3-LnH)Cl(μ-Cl)]2 bearing the tridentate coordinated κ3-LnH chelate (1a, n=1; 1b, n=2; 1c, n=3). Next, mononuclear Ir(III) complexes Ir(κ4-Ln)(thd) (3a, n=1; 3b, n=2; 3c, n=3) with the tetradentate chelate were obtained upon treatment of 2 with 2,2,6,6-tetramethyl-3,5-heptanedione (thd)H in the presence of K2CO3. Concurrently, methylation of 2c in the presence of MeI and nBu4NCl afforded tridentate Ir(κ3-L3HMe)Cl3 (4) and, next, can be converted to tetradentate Ir(κ4-L3Me)Cl2 (5) by further cyclometalation and HCl elimination in refluxing diethylene glycol monoethyl ether solution. The Ir(III) complexes 3a, 4, and 5 were unambiguously identified using spectroscopic methods, together with single-crystal X-ray structural analyses on Ir(III) derivatives 3a, 4, and 5. Their photophysical and, electrochemical properties and device fabrication properties were also investigated and compared with results from theoretical studies (Objective 3). The photocatalytic water-splitting experiments of some Ir(III) complexes are undertaken. Study 6 (undertaken): Co-sensitization Approach with Zinc Porphyrin and Meta-Free Organic Dianchoring Dyes for Light-Driven Hydrogen Generation Presently, one of the reasons for the low hydrogen production rate obtained is due to the inability to utilize visible light efficiently. Besides structural modifications of photosensitizers to enhance the light-harvesting ability and widen the absorption coverage, molecular co-sensitization approach by coupling multiple photoactive dyes having complementary spectral absorption ability is thus a pertinent approach. The different PSs can be excited by the corresponding spectral responsive region under vis/NIR light and then the photogenerated electrons are injected to semiconductors for hydrogen production. A new series of di-anchoring dyes functionalized with triarylamine with bridging linker have been developed and characterized (Objectives 1,2). A series of photocatalytic hydrogen evolution experiments were then performed with the co-sensitization appraoch with zinc porphyrin and these organic dianchoring dyes (Objectives 3,4). Three different concentration ratios of zinc porphyrin and organic dianchoring dyes were investigated and all of them could effectively produce hydrogen over 47h. In general, the ratio of 2:1 organic dye:YD2 (porphyrin) performed best, up to 33.7 mL with TON 20800 after 47 hours, followed by the 1:2 ratio (31.3 mL). The initial TOF, Activityi and AQYi% of 1:2 organic dye:YD2 (1132.1 h-1, 707.6 and 12.1% respectively) were, however, better than those of 2:1 organic dye:YD2. This phenomenon has aroused our interests and further investigation on their dye-loading efficiencies, durability, electrochemical impedancy and perfromances under other lights (green/white light and solar simulator).

12302117.label: Major findings and research outcome
12302117.value: (1) Bodipy-conjugated zinc porphyrin(ZnP)-dyad-sensitized Pt-TiO2 was designed and used for light-driven hydrogen-generation from water (Research_Output_1). The absorption spectrum of the bodipy-conjugated ZnP-dyad successfully intensified and extended the absorption throughout the visible region. The photocatalytic system with YD2-o-C8 performed better than that of ZnP-dyad under green-light-excitation. Much higher iTOFs and total TONs when white-light-irradiation was used with a TOFi of 407h-1 and TON of 12000 over 120h. This result clearly demonstrated the importance of panchromatic-sensitization. (2) A series of novel donor−donor−π−acceptor metal-free triphenylamine starburst-donor-based photosensitizers with different donating-moieties on triphenylamine and thiophene/hexylthiophene as the π-linkers were designed (Research_Output_2). These dye-sensitized-Pt−TiO2 photocatalysts showed impressive hydrogen productivity in water under blue/green lights, over the exceptionally long irradiation. Specifically, the most efficient dye yielded 1560μmol of hydrogen produced over 252 h under blue-light with a TON of 24900, TOFi of 1130h−1, and AQYi% of 12.1. Notably, the hydrophobic and electron-rich starburst-based structure, with the introduction of the alkyl-group(s) to the thiophene-π-spacer, could potentially boost the stability and robustness and suppress the charge recombination of the organic photosensitizers in the photocatalytic hydrogen-evolution-system. (3) Five cationic Ir(III) complexes with various electron-donating functionalities with intense absorption at wavelengths extending as far as 600 nm, have been synthesized (Research_Output_3). The rational structural modification on the cyclometallating ligand makes these complexes attractive in photocatalytic hydrogen-generation under visible light. A best TON of 12300 and TOFi of 394, with activityi of 547000 µmolg-1h-1 and AQYi of 9.59% was achieved, under the illumination of blue-light-LEDs after 105h. The TON in this study is the highest value reported to date in the system of Ir(III)@Pt-NPs as the photocatalyst. (4) A series of donor-π-acceptor organic photosensitizers based on thieno[3,2-b]thiophene π-linker has been synthesized (Research_Output_4). The best performance in DSSCs with PCE of 5.25% was achieved, while the largest hydrogen TON of 5170 (48h) was attained for the light-driven hydrogen-generation. It was found that the modification of alkyl chain in donor-moiety in the confined donor-π-acceptor framework is crucial to attain a significant variation in efficiency no matter in hydrogen-generation/DSSCs. (5) Ir(III) complexes bearing a multi-dentate heteroaromatic chelate were prepared (Research_Output_5). A max. EQE of 8.28% was achieved with λmax of 530nm for the mononuclear Ir(III) complex, while complex containing two monodentate chloride ligands gave a max. EQE of 8.76% but with a redshifted λmax of 613nm, confirming the applicability in fabrication of phosphorescent OLED devices. (6) Two review articles (Research_Output_7,8) have also been published.

12302117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12302117.value: It is certified that the molecular photosensitizers hold great promise for solar-energy utilization due to the unique advantages in the modification in the structure and properties that favors the dye-sensitized photocatalytic hydrogen-evolution-reactions. However, there are still some limitations/challenges remaining unresolved in this research area, such as further extending the spectral responsive regions, suppressing the backward-reactions, and matching hydrogen-production-activity with dye regeneration under operating conditions, etc. The following future research directions for dye-sensitized-semiconductors could be carried out. Firstly, new dyes/strategies should be developed to extend the photo-absorption-region for efficient, low-cost, stable and even panchromatic light responsive solar-to-hydrogen-conversion. Secondly, develop of means to efficiently couple various components of a dye-sensitized-system for achieving energy-level-matching and optimal photoreaction conditions. An understanding of the whole-system in terms of not only the performance of individual-units but the interactions between them and their operational harmony is needed to maximize the solar-to-fuel-conversion efficiency. Moreover, a better understanding of the photocatalytic mechanisms of dye-sensitized-systems, including charge-transfer characteristics across the interface of the semiconductor/dye/co-catalyst/SED, light-harvesting and the elementary-reactions on hydrogen-production, is vital for the improvement of the photocatalytic hydrogen-generation efficiency. Finally, strategies should be developed to more effectively retard the charge-recombination, thus resulting in a long-term high photoactivity/stability for hydrogen-production.

12302117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12302117.value: Photocatalytic water-splitting by solar-light has received tremendous attention for the production of clean and renewable hydrogen energy from water. Dye sensitization, as a successful strategy for extending the spectral responsive region (even to near-infrared light) of wide-bandgap semiconductors for hydrogen production, has been investigated in this study. Several series of molecular photosensitizers, including organic dyes with starburst and rod-like structures, robust cyclometalated iridium(III) complexes with different electron donors and iridium(III) complexes bearing a multi-dentate heteroaromatic chelate, have been developed for photocatalytic hydrogen production. According to the TOF and TON values, the photocatalytic system with the triphenylamine-based starburst organic dyes is one of the most efficient and robust photocatalytic hydrogen generation systems adopting a TiO2-anchoring molecular photosensitizer in the literature. Panchromatic sensitization was also achieved with Zinc(II) porphyrin-based photosensitizers for light-driven hydrogen production and a very active hydrogen generation system has been prepared. The result clearly demonstrated the importance and advantage of panchromatic sensitization for photocatalytic hydrogen-generation. All these studies clearly stated that by the optimization of the dye component for water-splitting through systematic variation of the donors/π-bridges/acceptors/anchoring groups and other substituents in these photosensitizers are greatly important for the long-term activity and stability for hydrogen-production from water.
