12501017.label: Major findings and research outcome
12501017.value: We invoke and extend the need satisfaction paradigm to explain a neglected phenomenon in organizational politics literature - the cross-level effects of organizational politics as a group-level phenomenon. The underlying rationale is that perception of team politics interferes with the satisfaction of the three basic needs proposed by the need satisfaction paradigm (i.e., need for relatedness, need for competence, and need for autonomy) and supervisor abusive supervision irritates this negative effect because it magnifies the dissatisfaction of these three needs. 12501017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12501017.value: First, future studies may extend need-satisfaction paradigm by looking at the boundary conditions when the three basic psychological needs are serving as the intervening variables or the first stage mediators in the politics-outcome relationship. Second, the construct of organizational political climate developed by Drory (1993) may also reflect the workplace politics at the team level. We agree that as not only an organization but also its sub-units have many climates (Schneider, 1975), political climate can be applied to the organizational level as well as team level. While the political climate scale represents the techno-rational model and political model of organizational decision making, the perceptions of organizational politics scale further validated by Kacmar and Carlson. (1997) captures the general political behaviors and going along to get ahead behaviors by team members, as well as the pay and promotion politics of the work group. We hence believe that team politics can be better demonstrated by aggregating individual team members’ perceptions of organizational politics. Third, future studies may employ a longitudinal research design for a more nuanced demonstration of the interrelationships among our variables.

12501017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12501017.value: In a survey among large US firms, 150 executives reported that office politics wastes around 20% of their time! This paper studies what the outcomes are if employees think their colleagues conduct the behaviors not sanctioned by the organization with the purpose to satisfy self-interests and achieve personal objectives. We found the outcomes are at both team level and individual level. At the team level, the team members are less likely to engage in mutual and collective interaction thus will have worse performance. At the individual level, the individuals are less likely to perceive themselves as belonging to the group thus will conduct behaviors that go against the legitimate interests of an organization. Moreover, if the supervisors engage in hostile verbal and nonverbal behaviors, the situation is even worse. This study is significant which suggests that we should try our best to prevent our employees’ political behaviors and supervisors’ abusive leadership.

12501317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12501317.value: Success stories of Dropbox or Airbnb give testament to the growing importance of acceleration programs in grooming high performance startups. At the core of such programs is the mentorship process, equipping founding teams with skills to recognize opportunities faster, pivot business models more efficiently, and generate a wider variety of original and relevant ideas. Emerging research on investment relations shows that exchange with more experienced individuals is essential in generating value-added for new ventures (Huang & Knight, 2015). Knowledge and strategic guidance are arguably as important as provision of financial means. Yet, the influence of relations between the founding team and startup mentors on new venture’s performance is under-researched. Extant literature on mentorship relationships between two individuals does not provide overarching logic to understanding the multi-level relations between startup teams and mentors. Drawing on literatures on formal mentoring and divergent thinking, this study aims to provide a new perspective on how mentorship relations between startup founding teams and more experienced advisors unfold and impact the new firm performance. We introduce attitude and goal congruence between team and mentor to explain why some relations are more likely to capitalize on entrepreneurial opportunities, and why similarity between founding team and mentors is not always a good thing. We reach to similarity-attraction theory to argue that the traditionally honed congruence in formal mentorship relationship may have negative consequences in the startup setting (Dowejko, Chan, & Au, 2016; Tajfel, 1978). Startup mentors are meant to push the founding teams out of their comfort zone and help them to increase their competitiveness through being different. We propose a mediating concept of divergent thinking in the startup mentoring process that helps to achieve this objective. We argue for moderate levels of similarity between founding teams and mentors. Too much similarity breeds contempt; too much diversity introduces chaos and conflict, thus limiting the potential of divergent thinking stimulated through mentorship. Overall, if the composition of mentoring pairs can be linked to mentorship relationship performance, acceleration programs and startup teams can strategically develop matching criteria and procedures that will allow for highly efficient startup development. Using cross-level polynomial regressions and as methodological approach, we plan to test the above propositions in the course of two empirical studies. Dropbox或 Airbnb的成功故事說明創業加速項目對於培育高績效的初創公司越來越重要。這些項目的核心是創業輔導的過程，用技能裝備創始團隊，令他們迅速的識別機會，高效的轉換商業模式，並生成更廣泛的原創及其相關性的想法。最近關於投資者的研究表明，與更有經驗的個人進行交流是為初創企業創造增值的必要條件(Huang & Knight, 2015) ，知識和策略指導可以說是與財務支援同樣重要的。然而，創始團隊和創業導師之間的關係對於新企業的影響仍然有待研究。 現有的輔導關係文獻大多關是於兩個個體之間的，對於創業團隊和眾多導師的多重關係並沒有提供較全面的理解。借助輔導關係和多角性思維的研究，本研究希望提供一個新的視角，來看待初創企業的團隊和經驗更為豐富的導師之間的關係是如何展開並影響新公司業績的。 我們引入了團隊和導師態度及目標的一致性來解釋為什麼某些團隊和導師關係能更好的利用創業機會，而為什麼相似的團隊和導師往往並不是一件好事。我們利用相似性吸引力理論，提出在現有的傳統輔導關係文獻中磨合出來的相似性觀點，在初創企業的發展環境中可能會產生負面的效果(Dowejko & Au, 2017; Tajfel, 1978)。創業導師的目的是為了將創始團隊從他們的舒適區中趕出來，並幫助他們通過改變來增加競爭力。我們提出了在啟動輔導過程中多角性思維的調解概念，有助於導師實現這一目標。 我們論證了創始團隊和導師之間應該有中等程度的相似性，太過於相似會產生相互蔑視，太多不同則會引起混亂和衝突，兩者都會限制通過輔導所能激發的多角性思維的潛力。總而言之，如果指導合作的構成與創業指導的表現結合起來，加速器項目和創業團隊可以在戰略上制定匹配的標準和程式，從而實現高效的初創企業發展。利用cross-level polynomial regressions 作為方法，我們計畫在兩個實證研究的過程中對上述命題進行測試。

12501617.label: Realisation of objectives
12501617.value: Objective 1: The effect of implicit theories on consumers' reactions to products made with recycled materials. In Study 1 (stimulus: Sony headphones made with recycled materials) and Study 2 (stimulus: Bag made with recycled materials from a fictitious brand) , we gathered preliminary evidence that entity theorists were less likely than incremental theorists to purchase products made with recycled materials. Regardless of whether the product made with recycled materials was made by a real or fictitious brand, incremental theorists consistently exhibited less intention than entity theorists to purchase any product made with recycled materials and were willing to pay less for such products. In Study 3, we replicated Studies 1 and 2 except that we asked participants to indicate their preference between conventional products and products made with recycled materials. By using two products (i.e., batteries and a lamp), we found that relative to incremental theorists, entity theories preferred conventional products over products made with recycled materials. In Studies 1–3, we provide evidence that entity theorists have more negative attitude toward products made with recycled materials than incremental theorists do. Objective 2: The mediating role of perceived quality Study 4 was designed to examine whether our proposed underlying mechanism—that is, perceived quality—mediates the effect of implicit theories on consumers’ attitudes toward products made with recycled materials. In the study, participants were shown an advertisement for a fictitious brand’s denim jacket made from recycled cotton and asked to indicate their attitude toward the jacket, their intention to recommend the jacket to friends, the perceived quality of the jacket, their feeling about the jacket’s cleanliness or dirtiness, their professing fluency (e.g., “The advertisement is ________”) on a scale from 1 (easy to understand) to 7 (difficult to understand), and negative self-perception (e.g., “When imaging myself wearing the jacket, I feel annoyed”). Among the results, entity theorists showed more negative attitude toward the jacket made from recycled cotton than incremental theorists did and less intention to recommend the jacket to friends. We also found that the effect was driven by the perceived quality of the jacket. The other possible mechanisms did not mediate the effect of implicit theories on attitudes toward the jacket. Objective 3: The moderating roles of centrality and firm size In Study 5, we found that the effect of implicit theories was attenuated when recycled materials were used to manufacture a peripheral (vs. a central) part of a product. In the study, participants were shown a laptop and free laptop bag that came along with it. In the centrality condition, participants were told that the laptop was made with recycled materials, while participants in the peripheral condition were told that the laptop bag, an accessory, was made with recycled materials. Afterward, participants were asked to indicate their intention to purchase the laptop. Results showed that entity theorists had less intention to purchase the laptop when they were told that it was made with recycled materials, whereas entity and incremental theorists showed a similar intention to purchase the laptop when they were informed that its accessory, a laptop bag, was made with recycled materials. We thus found that the effect of implicit theories seems to be attenuated when consumers believe that a product’s functionality is not influenced by recycled materials, at least not in a meaningful way. Firm Size: Although we expected that firm size (e.g., whether a product made with recycled materials is manufactured by a big or small company) may influence the effect of implicit theories, we did not find any significant results concerning that variable. In our studies, entity theorists consistently demonstrated more negative attitude toward products made with recycled materials regardless of whether the products were made by a big company (e.g., Sony) or small one (e.g., a startup). We thus concluded that firm size does not influence the effect of implicit theories on consumers’ reactions to products made with recycled materials.

12501617.label: Major findings and research outcome
12501617.value: Although increasingly more consumers are willing to purchase products made with recycled materials due to heightened concern about sustaining the natural environment, some segments of the consumer population remain unwilling to purchase such products. Therefore, we examined which consumers are less (or more) willing to purchase products made with recycled materials and why, namely by focusing on the effect of consumers’ implicit theories. Across five studies, we have demonstrated that entity theories have more negative attitude (e.g., less purchase intention, less willingness to pay, and less intention to recommend products made with recycled materials to others) toward products made with recycled materials than incremental theories do. According to our results, the reason for the effect was that entity theorists perceived products made with recycled materials to be of lower quality than incremental theorists did. Moreover, the effect of implicit theories was moderated by whether recycled materials were used to manufacture a central or a peripheral part of the product in question. In addition to the effect of implicit theories on recycled products, we further found that consumers' implicit theories also influence different types of environmentally friendly consumption-intention to purchase second-hand goods. We found that entity theories are less likely than incremental theories to purchase second-hand goods. Therefore, we found that consumers are less likely to engage in environmentally friendly consumption when they have entity theories.

12501617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12501617.value: A possible direction for future research is to examine whether consumers’ implicit theories influence their intention to participate in environmentally friendly campaigns (e.g., a recycling program). Although we demonstrated in our research that consumers’ implicit theories influence their attitude toward products made with recycled materials, whether those theories influence their intention to join green campaigns remains uncertain. In two preliminary studies, we found that entity theorists have less environmental concern than incremental theorists do. Because entity theorists believe that they cannot effect change by exerting personal effort, it is possible to predict that they may be less likely than incremental theorists to participate in recycling programs or to make donations to environmental organizations, precisely because they believe that such behavior does not help to improve the natural environment or to solve current environmental problems. In the future, researchers may need to examine whether entity theorists are less willing than incremental theorists to join green programs or to donate to environmental charities and, if so, then why. Finding answers to those questions may provide insights into ways of encouraging entity theorists to engage in such programs.

12501617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12501617.value: Although studies have demonstrated that some segments of consumers remain reluctant to buy products made with recycled materials, limited research has been conducted to examine who those consumers are and why they are less willing to purchase such goods. We aimed to fill that gap by examining how consumers’ implicit theories influence their reactions to products made with recycled materials. In 2 preliminary tests and 5 studies, we found that entity theorists, who believe that human traits (e.g., personality and ability) are fixed and cannot be changed with personal effort, prefer conventional products to products made with recycled materials and have more negative attitude toward products made with recycled materials, less intention to purchase them, and less willingness to recommend them to their friends than incremental theorists do, who tend to believe that people can developed and change their personal traits. The underlying mechanism behind entity theorists’ negative reactions to products made with recycled materials was due to their perceptions of recycled products’ inferior quality. We also found that the effect of implicit theories on reactions to products made with recycled materials was attenuated when recycled materials were used to manufacture a peripheral (vs. a central) part of a product.

12502917.label: Project Objectives
12502917.value: To examine the construct validity of team job insecurity climate To examine the impact of job insecurity on knowledge sharing and knowledge hiding To examine the impact of job insecurity on team adaptive and proactive performance via the mediating role of knowledge sharing and hiding To explore the role of team structure as boundary conditions of the job insecurity climate effects

12502917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12502917.value: The dramatic changes in the nature of work and business environment in the past two decades or so have caused heightened levels of uncertainties in the workplaces today. Job insecurity (JI) has become a nearly universal phenomenon in workplaces worldwide. On the one hand, organizations are faced with pressures for change which unavoidably leads to employees’ experience of JI. On the other hand, organizations have to rely more and more on employees’ adaptivity and initiatives to develop their competitive advantage. Although JI has drawn much research attention and robust findings have been accumulated regarding the impact of JI on employees and organizations, JI’s effect has been predominantly examined at the individual level. We do not know much about how JI impacts work teams. This is unfortunate considering the facts that teams are increasingly valued for their potential to perform in today’s complex work environment. In this research, we focus on studying the validity of team level JI and how it influences team adaptivity and proactivity. We first theorize the formation of team JI climate using theories about team cognition and the emotional contagion. We then develop a model that links JI climate to team adaptivity and proactivity through knowledge exchange behaviors in teams. Specifically, we propose two mechanisms: (a) JI climate causes decreased knowledge sharing as a result of threat-rigidity effect. That is, when faced with the threat of losing jobs or desired features of their jobs, members would focus attention on saving their own jobs and at the same time, limit their attention to knowledge from others causing limited knowledge sharing in teams. (b) JI climate causes increased knowledge hiding as a result of a desire for resource control. That is, the uncertainties about job future and perceptions about limited resources associated with members’ experience of JI would drive a strong motivation to keep knowledge to themselves causing increased knowledge hiding in teams. Further, we also propose, based on the goal interdependence theory that team goal and reward structures (competitive versus cooperative) is a boundary condition of the proposed team level JI impact. We plan to collect both interview and survey data from organizations in China to test the model. We believe findings from this project will not only contribute to the literature but have practical implications for managers to better understand the collective impact of JI and knowledge management in teams. 過去近二十年來，工作性質和商業環境所發生的巨大變化使得現今的工作場所充滿著各樣的不確定性。在全球各地，人們因為可能丟掉工作而產生的不安全感已經成為一個普遍現象。組織管理者們面臨這樣一個困境和挑戰：一方面，組織面臨的變革壓力不可避免地帶來員工的不安全感，另員工的工作態度、行為受到負面影響；另一方面，組織要在日益激烈的競爭中存活，愈來愈需要依靠員工的適應性和主動性。儘管關於工作不安全感有大量的研究，現有的研究絕大部分都是在員工個人層面上的。關於工作不安全感如何對團隊產生影響，我們知之甚少。這是很可惜的，因為團隊作業在現今的組織中越來越發揮著重要價值。此研究項目正是致力於考察工作不安全感在團隊層面是否為一個有效的概念以及，如果有的話，這樣的團隊氛圍如何影響團隊在適應性和主動性方面的績效表現。我們首先從團隊認知及情緒感染的理論出發，論述團隊工作不安全感這個構念的效度，然後提出一個研究模型，即：團隊不安全感透過影響成員之間的知識分享和知識隱藏行為而另團隊的適應性和主動性表現受影響。具體一點來說，我們提出團隊工作不安全感可能產生負面影響的兩個機制：一是，當團隊成員有不安全感的時候，可能產生一種“威脅-僵化效果，”即大家都只關注在自己的工作事務上而忽略其他與工作相關的新知識，因而使團隊的知識分享受損。二是，團隊充滿不安全感的氛圍時，可能令到成員為要保住自己的工作而產生不僅不願分享更有故意隱藏知識的傾向，因而導致團隊內的知識隱藏行為。我們進一步提出，並非所有團隊面臨工作不安全感的時候都會有減少知識分享、增加知識隱藏的行為產生以至於使團隊的表現受損——這取決於團隊的目標和評估獎賞體制：當團隊成員的目標一致，評估和獎賞是基於團隊而非個人的時候，上述的後果會被減弱。我們計劃在中國大陸選取公司團隊樣本，用訪談和問卷的方法收集數據來驗證我們的研究假設模型。我們相信此項研究在工作不安全感及團隊知識管理等方面有重要的理論和實踐意義。

12502917.label: Realisation of objectives
12502917.value: We have achieved all the project objectives except for the 3rd and 4th objectives regarding the dependent variables and the moderating effects of which we have achieved 90% so far. On the conceptual side, we have conducted a thorough literature review to include more recent findings related to our study. Perhaps due to the recent pandemic situation, there are much job insecurity related research published recently. However, there is still not much research on group level job insecurity climate and the behavioral responses to that. Our literature review continues to support the key idea we proposed as well as its theoretical and practical importance, namely the impact of group level job insecurity climate on behavior-related group process and outcomes. Moreover, we theorized additional dependent variables in our model. In addition to team adaptive and proactive performance, we theorized team creativity and social undermining behaviors in teams as consequences of group job insecurity climate via team knowledge sharing and hiding. On the empirical side, we have tested the model using three samples including two in mainland China and one in Europe. In the two Chinese samples, we used well-designed sampling strategy to survey people in working teams in different cities in China and reached 162 and 175 complete teams (with 3-6 members) respectively. The first sample was surveyed in three waves and the second in two waves. Data from these two Chinese working team samples are for the main studies used to test the whole model. In addition, we went beyond the original plan to collect additional data in Belgium in year 2021 in order to examine some of the effects at the individual level in a different social and cultural context. In the European sample, we used a relatively convenient sampling to survey individuals in various organizations and industries in four waves. We have finished data analyses of the first sample and reported the study in a conference paper*. Data analyses of the other two samples are almost completed and report writing is still ongoing. In addition to comments on the conference paper, we have had our draft manuscript reviewed by colleagues and collected feedback for further revision**. *Huang G., Lee, C., & Wang L. (2019). Job insecurity, knowledge hiding, and team outcomes Paper presented at the Academy of Management Conference, Boston. Aug. 2019. **Huang G., Lee, C., De Stobbeleir, K., & Wang L. Hiding knowledge when feeling insecure? Job insecurity climate, knowledge sharing and hiding, and team outcomes. Manuscript under revision and to be submitted to the Journal of Applied Psychology. Specifically, the first project objective is to examine the construct validity of team job insecurity climate. At the initial stage of the research, we have interviewed with managers in China to examine the content validity. In general, the feedback we received shows that the phenomena we study (shared perception about job insecurity climate in teams) is understandable and relevant in the context. In our empirical model testing, we found evidence for its discriminant validity by demonstrating that individuals can form different perceptions regarding their own levels of job insecurity versus the level of collective job insecurity climate in their work teams (the two perceptions at the individual level correlate at a moderate level). Its predictive validity was demonstrated through its impact on team behavior and performance outcomes and in particular, such effect is significant for some of the outcomes even after controlling for the impact of the aggregated individual job insecurity. Regarding the impact of team job insecurity climate on knowledge sharing and knowledge hiding behaviors in teams (the second objective), we found support for both effects which suggests teams with high job insecurity climate tend to have more knowledge hiding and less knowledge sharing among members. In addition, we found the impact on knowledge hiding seems to be stronger than that on knowledge sharing. Although we did not theorize such difference, we deem it important to theoretically make sense of the results. In our proposal, we used the threat rigidity model to theorize the impact of job insecurity climate on knowledge sharing and the uncertainty management perspective to theorize the impact on knowledge hiding. Our data seem to suggest the uncertainty management effect is stronger for the threat rigidity effect in the job insecurity situation. Regarding the third project objective, we examined multiple team outcomes in the empirical study. In addition to the team adaptive and proactive performance proposed in the proposal, we also examined team task performance, creative performance, and social undermining in teams in order to explore additional theoretically reasonable outcomes. We found strong support for the impact of job insecurity climate via knowledge sharing and hiding on team task performance and social undermining behaviors. However, the impact on adaptive, proactive, and creative performance are mixed in our two samples which we are still examining. Finally, regarding the last research objectives, we examined the role of team structure including team competitive and cooperative goals as boundary conditions of the job insecurity climate effects. We found support of the moderating effect of team competitive goal on the job insecurity climate and knowledge hiding relationship in one sample but not the other sample which we are still examining.

12502917.label: Major findings and research outcome
12502917.value: Overall, we found support for the construct validity of team job insecurity climate and its negative impact on team behavior and performance outcomes. Our conceptualization and operationalization of the team job insecurity climate construct is new in the literature and it demonstrated discriminant and predictive validity in studying important team outcomes including team social undermining, and team performance. Moreover, we theorized and tested the mediating role of team knowledge exchange behaviors between job insecurity climate and team outcomes. It suggests that when members in a working team collectively perceive insecurity of their jobs, they tend to not only reduce knowledge sharing but also intentionally hide knowledge from each other which in turn harm team maintenance as well as performance outcomes. Further, the impact of hiding could be stronger than the impact of sharing. However, not all teams respond to job insecurity climate in the same way. We found teams competitive goal structure as an important moderator to the above impact. That is, team with less competitive goals responded less negatively to job insecurity climate.

12502917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12502917.value: The results we found so far suggest that research on active responses to job insecurity is very relevant at the team level—a climate of job insecurity in teams does not generate rigidity among members but it makes them actively control their own knowledge from others in the team. Data from one sample suggests the impact of hiding is stronger than that of sharing. This warrants our attention—on the one hand we need to further examine if that can be replicated in other samples; on the other hand, we can make sense of the results theoretically and further develop theoretical models to examine the different impacts. Our finding that the impact of job insecurity climate on team outcomes through knowledge hiding is only significant for teams with a strong competitive structure further confirms that team characteristics play a role in responding to team climate. However, the findings are not all consistent across the samples which also requires additional analyses conceptually and empirically. Overall, as our research demonstrated the construct validity of the team job insecurity climate, it opens many opportunities for job insecurity research to extent its focus from the individual level to a collective level.

12502917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12502917.value: Team management is especially critical and challenging for organizations in today’s uncertain times. Findings from this research offer practical implications for managers. Firstly, prior job insecurity research suggested that managers need to attend to individual employees’ job insecurity in order to deal with its negative consequences on employee health and work outcomes. Our findings suggested that managers also need to attend to how employee perceive the climate of job insecurity in their teams because such perceptions can be shared at the team level and affects the whole team. Secondly, the finding that the impact of job insecurity climate on team outcomes through knowledge hiding is only significant for teams with a strong competitive structure suggest that managers should perhaps balance the level of job insecurity climate and intra-team competitiveness—when team job insecurity climate is high, having a less competitive or more cooperative structure in the team is very critical for the team to avoid knowledge hiding and to perform and maintain social relationships in the team. Or put it in another way, when there is a high level of job insecurity climate, having a competitive structure can be particularly destructive to teams so should be avoided.

12503017.value: 在知识和专业背景不同的成员之间的知识共享（特别是在研发团队中）是激发团队成员产生有用和有创意的想法和解决问题的方法。但是，最近的研究发现，当一位团队成员与其他成员的知识和专业背景相差很远的时候，这位成员会很难理解对方共享来的知识。要想理解和运用不同背景成员的知识和专长，个体成员需要与对方进行深层交流和紧密的知识交换。虽然知识共享涉及到成员与成员之间的交换，但是过去的研究主要把知识共享建构成个体层面或团体层面的概念并进行测量，没有考虑成员与成员之间的互动交换关系，从而阻碍了我们对知识交换为什么和在什么情况下促进创造力的了解。 因此，我们提出了基于交换视角的知识共享理论；我们认为一位成员对不同背景成员的知识的最大理解，取决于交换双方能够同时及高强度的进行“深层次”知识共享。只有透过这种交换模式，个体成员才能够融会贯通和深入运用另外一位背景不同的成员的专业知识。同样道理，其中一位成员不积极参与这个知识交换过程，个体成员就很难最大化的理解对方专长。此外，我们提出个体对知识的开放程度是一个重要调节变量。

12503017.label: Major findings and research outcome
12503017.value: Knowledge exchanges between knowledge workers with dissimilar functional and professional backgrounds facilitate the generation of creative ideas and new knowledge. It is difficulthard, however, for knowledge workers to understand and integrate the expertise and knowledge of functionally dissimilar exchange partners. Although prior research suggests that intensive knowledge dialogues between functionally dissimilar members enable mutual understanding, we do not know what is dialogued and how knowledge dialogues enhance creativity. In a pilot study, we developed the dyadic-level constructs and measures of knowledge dialogue (i.e., in-depth depiction and explanation of one’s background knowledge to an interacting partner and active enquiry of the partner’s expertise) and integrative understanding (i.e., one’s understanding, integration, and application of a functionally dissimilar partner’s knowledge and expertise). In the main study, based on survey data, we showed that an employee can achieve an optimal integrative understanding of the expertise of a dissimilar partner only when both parties simultaneously and intensively engage in knowledge dialogues. We also found that a focal employee needs to achieve a high level of integrative understanding of every other dissimilar group member’ knowledge and expertise to exhibit a high level of creativity.

12503017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12503017.value: Our proposed model contributes to the literature on knowledge sharing and creativity in three ways. First, we change the course of research on knowledge sharing from the individual/group-level to the dyadic level examination of the reciprocal processes of knowledge exchanges. Second, we shed new light on the knowledge exchange process between functionally dissimilar dyadic partners by developing the constructs of knowledge dialogue and integrative understanding to provide insights into how they can make use of each other’s knowledge and expertise to generate new ones. Third, diversity is a double-edged sword. A key conundrum in the “value-in-diversity” research is to understand how diversity generates beneficial or detrimental effects on individual and group creativity (van Kippenberge, 2017; Williams & O’Reilly, 1998). Our research opens this black box by showing that individual knowledge workers can benefit from other functionally dissimilar members only when they engage in knowledge dialogue and therefore achieve an integrative understanding of the expertise of every other dissimilar members in the team. On the opposite, a poor integrative understanding of dissimilar others may impede one’s creativity.

12503017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12503017.value: Imagine that an organizational psychologist, a mathematician, and a historian are jointly developing a research project on social behaviors. How would the three scholars work together? Based on the “value-in-diversity” perspective (Gilson, Mathieu, Shalley, & Ruddy, 2005; Williams & O’Reilly, 1998; Li, Li, Guo, Li, Harris, 2018), the three scholars could collectively generate original ideas because each of them brings to the group unique expertise and viewpoints that will help expand the other members’ scope of knowledge. Indeed, research suggests that sharing knowledge with functionally dissimilar partners enhances individual creativity (Gong, Kim, Zhu, & Lee, 2013; Hargadon & Bechky, 2006; Huang, Hsieh, & He, 2014; Nonaka, 1994; Paulus, 2008). The reality, however, is far more complicated than what is predicted by this dominating perspective. The historian may find it difficult to understand the logic underlying mathematical models that the mathematician uses to predict social behaviors; the organizational psychologist may have no knowledge about how historians generate knowledge using historical analyses; and the mathematician may not understand the content and rationales of psychological theories. Our research suggests that the three scholars should engage in intensive knowledge dialogues to achieve mutual integrative understanding, enhancing creativity.

12600317.label: Major findings and research outcome
12600317.value: Major findings from this study were as follows: First, one study with six experiments revealed how different elements of metaphorical statements (novelty, presence of signals) impact perceptions of interpretability and acceptability. Overall, we found that novel metaphors are less interpretable and acceptable than conventional metaphors or literal controls. Signaling can increase the acceptability of novel metaphors, but only when signals are clearly visible (as in the case of double signals). By contrast, signaling can backfire in situations in which metaphorical statements are already interpretable and acceptable, as with conventional metaphors. In such situations, adding excessive signals may decrease interpretability and acceptability. These results demonstrate how different features of metaphors (novelty, signaling) can interact in influencing interpretability and acceptability judgments. Second, another study (with four experiments) found that novel metaphors made readers view proposed policy changes more favorably in one experiment, but this result did not hold up reliably across all the experiments. However, overall, novel metaphors were helpful in processing new topics. We hypothesize this is because the metaphors drew attention to the language with their novelty, and that helped people process the ideas more fully. In short, our studies explored the subtle influences of metaphorical language on comprehension and behavior. Implications for real-world knowledge transfer are to help people understand how metaphor is used so that they may become more aware of it and, thus, be less likely to be easily swayed by these rhetorical and conceptual patterns found in language.

12600317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12600317.value: The genre of texts in the longer passage studies were geopolitical in nature and asked respondents about their views on the situation, with a particular focus on metaphor signals, metaphor conventionality and metaphor novelty. Future work will look at how metaphors are used in business settings, particularly with respect to entrepreneurs pitching their companies to venture capitalists. This work has been proposed as a new GRF study (and begin in January of 2021). In addition, an area that has not yet been explored is the interaction between metaphor and gender – that is, whether some source domains, such as WAR, are viewed as more masculine than other source domains, such as PLANT. If so, then the question arises if men and women will have different responses to venture capital pitches by (either) a man or a woman. These studies all get the essential question of how metaphorical language may influence comprehension, decisions, and actions across different genres. In short, if metaphor use is profoundly influencing people’s opinions, we must strive to better understand the conditions surrounding this influence, as well as possible ways to mitigate it when necessary.

12600317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12600317.value: One area of interest in recent years is the degree to which a particular metaphor may influence our opinion about a complex issue. This topic has now permeated the mass culture to such an extent that when David Cameron said that a ‘swarm’ of migrants were trying to enter Britain covertly through a French port (30 July 2015), political rivals who were themselves opposed to immigration admonished him for dehumanizing migrants by comparing them to insects. In this project we ran different experimental studies that asked participants to read passages with different types of metaphors and provide rating responses to what they read. Our results showed that novel (somewhat unusual) metaphors were helpful to readers who were processing texts about new topics. We think that this may be due to the fact that these more unusual metaphors draw attention to the language with their novelty but remain familiar enough that they can still be readily understood (as in the Cameron case above). We also found that novel metaphors in single sentences were viewed as less easily understood compared with conventional metaphors. This finding shows the importance of framing a concept, as novelty is only helpful when it occurs in context.

12601017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12601017.value: The freedom of children to move around in their neighborhood without adult supervision, which is known as independent mobility (IM) (1), has been shown to be critical for cognitive, emotional, and social development in children (2). IM usually involves active modes of travel (walking and cycling) or taking public transport to various destinations. Children’s IM has attracted a lot of research interest in western countries and secular data have shown a dramatic decline of unsupervised travel during the last few decades (2, 3). Such change is worrying because lower levels of IM may result in fewer opportunities for children to engage in active travel and outdoor play, hence diminish overall physical activity (PA) participation. Hong Kong, a notable metropolis with high population density, lacks data on children’s IM and outdoor play. The issue of improving walkability of this packed city has received worldwide attention: the first ever international conference on walkability in Asia (Walk21) was recently held in Hong Kong. Reconsidering how to embrace walking as a natural mode of mobility has been urged by the government officials during the conference. It is timely to investigate IM in the Chinese context considering the significant impact of IM on individual health and the whole society. The proposed longitudinal study will examine the potential of IM to increase PA and reduce sedentary behavior, and enhance our understanding of barriers toward IM for children in Hong Kong. 450 children in grade 3 (typically aged 8-9 years) will be recruited and examined three times over a two-year period in order to record seasonal and age-related changes. A mixed-method approach will be applied, i.e. incorporating accelerometer with an integral light sensor (to measure PA and record outdoor location) and a subjective measure (to determine independence from adults). IM will be assessed by parent- and children-report questionnaires in two domains: parents’ permission for their children to travel and outdoor play, as well as the actual mobility of children. Furthermore, questions will be asked with regards to IM on weekdays and weekends separately. Finally, barriers perceived by parents to grant children greater IM will be gauged through an exploratory qualitative interview, nominal group technique. The findings will shed light on whether and how IM can be a viable intervention strategy to enhance an optimal activity profile. Better understanding of barriers toward IM is a necessary step toward informing effective intervention strategies. 兒童在其居住社區附近無需成人陪伴而可獨立自由移動之程度被稱為“獨立移動”，它通常包括動態交通（步行或踏單車）或搭乘公共交通工具前往各目的地。有研究發現，獨立移動對於兒童的認知，情緒，和社會發展非常重要。兒童的獨立移動已經引起西方學者的關注，數據顯示於近幾十年呈現明顯下降的趨勢。兒童被允許獨立活動的縮減可能導致動態交通及室外活動時間減少，繼而影響整體體力活動水平。作爲人口密度集中的大都市，香港在這方面的研究十分有限。如何增加擁擠都市的易行性已經成爲全球關注的議題，最近舉行的Walk21世界會議首次於香港召開，政府亦呼籲社會反思如何將步行融入每個人的日常交通。 因此，是項研究旨在探討獨立移動對於體力活動和靜態行爲的影響，以及限制兒童獨立移動的影響因素。本研究的對象爲450名三年班小學生。採用ActiGraph活動記錄儀測量兒童日常體力活動及室外活動時間，參與學生及其家長將填寫一份問卷以評估兒童獨立移動之程度。部份家長將獲邀參與小組訪談。預期本研究結果將對探索獨立移動作爲促進體力活動的有效手段提供參考依據。

12601017.label: Realisation of objectives
12601017.value: In order to examine the tracking of independent mobility and its relationships with activity behaviors among children (Objectives 1-3), a longitudinal study was conducted. A two-stage stratified sampling strategy were applied to select a sample of children in grade 3 (typically aged 8-9 years) residing in a variety of neighborhoods. First, the selection of neighborhoods was based on Tertiary Planning Units (TPUs), the smallest census-based geographic unit used in Hong Kong, of school location. The TPUs were classified to represent different levels of urbanization (urban, sprawl, and rural areas) in Hong Kong. The mean monthly household income data from each TPU were decided based on Census data, and then was dichotomized based on median value to either high or low socioeconomic status (SES). We sent invitations to 180 primary schools that were randomly selected from the six types of TPUs (urban/high SES, sprawl/high SES, rural/high SES, urban/low SES, sprawl/low SES, and rural/low SES). Eventually, 9 schools from 8 TPUs representing four types of neighborhoods (urban/high SES, urban/low SES, sprawl/low SES, and rural/low SES) agreed to participate in this study. Second, children studying in grade 3 of these schools were invited, and were considered eligible if they: (1) had lived in their neighborhood for at least six months before participating, and (2) were free of disability and illness precluding engagement in PA. Eventually, 330 children’ parents provided written consent forms and completed the baseline assessment which was conducted from December 2018 to June 2019 (except for one school which joined the study in November 2019). The distribution of children in the four types of TPUs was 23.3% (urban/high SES), 23.6% (urban/low SES), 45.6% (sprawl/low SES), and 7.4% (rural/low SES). The current sample size was sufficient to detect an effect size f2 of 0.04, based on a power of 0.80, a p value of 0.05 and 10 predictors in a regression model. Two third of the participating schools (6 out of 9) agreed to participated in the follow-up assessments which was conducted from September to November 2019. However, one school eventually withdrew due to class suspension in November 2019. Interval between the two assessments ranges from 7 to 9 months. Of the 330 recruited children, 296 children (125 boys) with an average age of 8.8 years provided valid data at baseline assessment. Of them, 201 (61.9%) children completed follow-up assessments and 165 children provided valid accelerometer data. Three conference abstracts reporting the preliminary findings of these results have been presented at the following international conferences: • “Independent mobility and physical activity among children” at the 2019 Annual Meeting of the International Society of Behavioral Nutrition and Physical Activity. • “Relationship between parental granting mobility license and after-school physical activity in children” and “Accelerometer-derived physical activity estimates and daily wear time in children” at the 2020 Annual Meeting of the American College of Sports Medicine. Two manuscripts reporting the findings generated from this project, entitled “Independent mobility and physical activity among children residing in an ultra-dense metropolis” and “Thinness as a risk factor for physical inactivity in children and youth”, are now under review. To explore the barriers perceived by parents to grant children greater independent mobility (Objective 4), qualitative interviews - Nominal group technique (NGT) - were conducted. Four nominal groups were conducted among 19 parents (2 fathers and 17 mothers) aged 32-50 years. The parents responded to the question “What do you think are the barriers that refrain you to allow your child to travel to school, shops and other destinations, or play outdoors in your neighborhood, on his or her own or with friends, but without adult accompaniment?” Factors were prioritized in order of their importance ranked by the parents. An abstract, entitled “Understanding the barriers of children’s independent mobility, a qualitative study using nominal group technique”, was presented at the 2020 Annual Meeting of the International Society of Behavioral Nutrition and Physical Activity. A manuscript is now under preparation and is expected to be submitted to a peer-reviewed journal by the end of October 2021.

12601017.label: Major findings and research outcome
12601017.value: This study used a complementary (quantitative and qualitative) research approach. A longitudinal investigation was performed to examine the tracking of independent mobility and to investigate the associations between children’s independent mobility and activity behavior. Parents’ perceived barriers for granting greater independent mobility for their children were explored through an exploratory qualitative interview. In this study, children’s independent mobility was defined and measured in two domains: (1) parents’ license granted to their children to travel independently and play outdoors without adults, and (2) the actual mobility behavior including travel to/from school, travel to other destinations, and going outdoors independently. Spearman rank-order correlation coefficients for parents’ license and actual mobility were 0.61 and 0.52, respectively, indicating a large tracking coefficient. Parents’ license was higher for children who were older (b = 2.80, 95%CI: 1.29, 6.12), being overweight or obese (b = 3.86, 95%CI: 1.07, 13.96), having older parents (b = 0.92, 95%CI: 0.86, 1.00), and having lower maternal education (secondary school vs. junior high or below: b = 0.14, 95%CI: 0.04, 0.52). Boys perceived greater mobility (to other destinations) than girls, whereas those who were underweight had less mobility for home-school trips compared with those being normal weight. Compared with students attending schools in urban/high SES areas, those in the other three types demonstrated higher parents’ license and independent mobility (to/from school). Furthermore, children in schools in sprawl/low SES areas perceived higher level of independent mobility (to other destinations) and independent mobility (going outdoors) than those in urban/high SES areas. Results from regression analyses revealed that parents’ license was positively associated with moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) on weekend days ( = 1.33, 95%CI: 0.15, 2.51), while independent mobility (to/from school) was positively associated with time spent in MVPA on weekdays ( = 1.14, 95%CI: 0.10, 2.18) (refer to Part C, research output 8-2, 9-2, 9-4). No relationships were found between independent mobility and light-intensity physical activity or sedentary time. Findings from qualitative interviews (Part C, research output 9-3) indicated ten unique factors as the most important barriers for parents to grant their children independent mobility, with “safety” the only barrier identified among all the type of neighborhoods. “Perceived independence/capability of the child” and “negative peer influence” were generated in three groups (urban/low SES, sprawl/low SES, rural/low SES). “Allowance by parents”, “complexity of transportation”, and “distance between home and school” were only identified among the group of parents from urban/high SES.

12601017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12601017.value: To the best of our knowledge, there was only one study that has examined independent mobility for Hong Kong children, which was based on the travel diary data from government report in 2002. This project provides important information on this topic two decades later. The results indicated that children’s independence during home-school trips did not change dramatically over the last two decades in Hong Kong. Future development of the research should include: 1. Examination of long-term relationship between independent mobility and physical activity; 2. Development of interventions to enhance independent mobility and then promote active travel and outdoor play.

12601017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12601017.value: Outdoor play and active travel, as a natural part of everyday lives for children, are valuable sources of free-living physical activity. Both of them are related to children’s independent mobility, which describes the freedom of children to move around their neighborhood without adult supervision. Children with more independence have been hypothesized to be more physically active. This study applied both quantitative and qualitative approaches to explore independent mobility among children residing in a metropolis. It was found that children in sprawl and rural areas had higher parents’ license and actual mobility than those in urban area. Children with greater parents’ licenses were more physically active on weekends and those who are allowed to travel to and from school independently had higher level of physical activity on weekdays. These findings suggest that increasing independent mobility would be useful to encourage children to be more physically active, with additional efforts required for children residing in highly urbanized areas. Parents should be encouraged to allow their children to travel independently and play outdoor. A child-friendly environment, i.e., protective and walkable, is particularly needed for children residing in inner-city in Hong Kong.

12602317.label: Project Objectives
12602317.value: To analyze the structural–institutional context and political opportunities associated with the emergence of and choice of repertories among the cases of land expropriation resistance. This will involve the collection and analysis of data from each province, including documents on the changing land policies, reforms to the Land Administration Law, location-specific experiments in rural property rights, and the changing approaches to authoritarian domination together with their impact on central–local relations. This will also involve interviews with informants (scholars, journalists, lawyers) and the officials responsible for making and implementing land policies. To identify and detail the repertories of resistance adopted and, where relevant, the organization and mobilization of the resistance. This will involve the identification of new cases of land expropriation resistance and/or follow-up on old ones for each of the provinces and, on that foundation, the collection of documents on the cases (petition/litigation materials, news reports, blogs, secondary analysis etc.). Further, this will require interviews to be conducted with the stakeholders: village leaders, rank-and-file members of the villages, village cadres, local officials, and possibly other informants. The importance of formal and informal power relations (including village administration and kin and quasi-kin relations) and the use of social media will also be investigated. To ascertain the cultural meanings that inform and structure the land expropriation resistance and, in doing so, contribute to the debates on rights consciousness and the resilience of China’s communist rule. This will involve asking a number of questions and gaining insight into the reasons why the villagers engage in resistance and choose a particular repertoire at specific points in time, the nature of their land-related economic claims, their views on the right to defend such claims through the political-judicial system, and their perspectives on central–local relations, the rule of law, and the legitimacy of communist rule when their economic and political rights are denied.

12602717.label: Project Objectives
12602717.value: To develop a theoretical model to systemically understand, examine, and explain the variety of, how, and the extent to which (achievements and limitations of) deliberative participation as an innovative governance approach may facilitate SETs with a comparative case study of Japan, South Korea, and China. By focusing on trust building, social learning, and public acceptance – three core elements of deliberative participation – we will investigate the interactions between citizens, governments, regulators, experts, utilities, business sectors, and the media, and determine conditions that are favorable or impede normative processes of deliberative participation from being realized. To distinguish national varieties and identify factors that may explain variation across Asian countries. To provide insights into the extent to which Western theories of energy transition and deliberative governance can be applied in the Asian context.

12602717.label: Realisation of objectives
12602717.value: Major project revisions on the scope of research were approved in May 2020. Major changes to the scope of research in relation to the project revisions include: 1. Change of research subject from country to city 2. Reducing case cities from three to two 3. Change of project title to “Deliberative participation, trust, and social learning for sustainable energy transitions (SETs): A comparative study of Tokyo and Hong Kong” 4. Change of objective to “To develop a theoretical model to systemically understand, examine, and explain the variety of, how, and the extent to which (achievements and limitations of) deliberative participation as an innovative governance approach may facilitate SETs with a comparative case study of Tokyo and Hong Kong” 5. Replacing the case region of South Korea (Seoul) by China (Hong Kong) 6. Reduce the sample size from 250 to 200 for each Deliberative Polls (DP) The work done so far is well in line with the research objectives. Major research tasks conducted: (i) we conducted about 21 interviews with key stakeholders in five field trips which took place in Kyoto and Seoul during this project period; (ii) we collected primary qualitative data from face-to-face interviews with 21 key informants in Hong Kong; (iii) we conducted two online DPs with valid sample size of 136 Tokyo citizens and 174 Hong Kong citizens in April and July 2020 respectively; (iv) we organised an international energy conference on the trajectories, governance and policy innovations of Asian urban energy transitions in Hong Kong Baptist University in July 2019 – which was titled “The Third Asian Energy Conference: Diversity in Urban Energy Transitions in Asia: Trajectories, Governance and Policy Innovations” with about 94 participants. This project resulted in 3 sets of outputs. The first set of outputs relate to publications, comprising 7 published journal papers and 2 manuscripts under preparation for journal submission. These include: 1. Journal of Cleaner Production (Mah et al., 2018) – “Understanding undergraduate students’ perceptions of dynamic pricing policies: An exploratory study of two pilot deliberative pollings (DPs) in Guangzhou, China and Kyoto, Japan” 2. Energy Research & Social Science (Mah, 2019) – “Community solar energy initiatives in urban energy transitions: A comparative study of Foshan, China and Seoul, South Korea” 3. Geoforum (Mah, 2020) – “Conceptualising government-market dynamics in socio-technical energy transitions: A comparative case study of smart grid developments in China and Japan” 4. Sustainability (Mah & Cheung, 2020) – “Conceptualizing Niche–Regime Dynamics of Energy Transitions from a Political Economic Perspective: Insights from Community-Led Urban Solar in Seoul” 5. Environmental Innovation and Societal Transitions (Mah et al., 2021a) – “Trust gaps in energy transitions: Japan’s National Deliberative Poll after Fukushima” 6. Environmental Policy and Governance (Mah et al., 2021b) – “Evaluating deliberative participation from a social learning perspective: A case study of the 2012 National Energy Deliberative Polling in post-Fukushima Japan” 7. Energy Policy (Mah et al., 2021c) – “Policy mixes and the policy learning process of energy transitions: Insights from the feed-in tariff policy and urban community solar in Hong Kong” 8. Manuscript 1 (under preparation) – “Public distrust and public preferences on energy futures in Asia: Insights from online deliberative pollings of citizen-led solar developments in Tokyo and Hong Kong” 9. Manuscript 2 (under preparation) – “The importance of energy autonomy in public preferences on energy futures scenarios: Comparative insights from online citizen deliberative pollings in Tokyo and Hong Kong” The second set of output relates to the creation of a new, large body of empirical data derived from (i) approximately 42 in-depth semi-structured interviews; (ii) quantitative questionnaire data from about 310 participants in the two online DPs; and (iii) 90 small groups and 4 plenary discussions transcription records of the two online DPs. The third set of output relate to the strengthening of an international, interdisciplinary research partnership through the establishment of Asian Low-Carbon University Network (ALUN) with 5 universities (Kyoto, National Taipei, Seoul National, Sun Yat-sen, and Yonsei) as founding members. The ALUN was officially launched in July 2021. The project also fostered research collaboration between 4 institutions in Hong Kong, the US (Stanford; College of the Mainland), Japan (Kyoto) and South Korea (Yonsei) that can sustain the team’s high-impact long-term research in this emerging field of energy governance. This project has largely fulfilled the objectives as follows: Objective 1 – The project developed a set of four integrated frameworks: (i) a core framework of the dynamics between state and non-state actors in energy transitions (Mah, 2020), and it is complemented by three thematic frameworks, namely (ii) a trust-based systems framework for deliberative policy-making in energy transitions (Mah et al., 2021a); (iii) learning-oriented framework of deliberative participation (Mah et al., 2021b) (iv) the political-economic perspective of niche-regime dynamics (Mah, 2020) Objective 2 – We conducted qualitative study (data collected mainly by face-to-face semi-structured interviews) and specified the uncertainties; three critical dimensions of trust (trust in information, motives and competence); and the interactions between incumbents, citizens, governments, media as the critical factors in creating favourable conditions in successful smart energy transitions (see Manuscript 1; Mah et al., 2021a, 2021b). In addition, we conducted quantitative and qualitative analysis on the two online DPs in Tokyo and Hong Kong. We provided a better understanding of how local citizens in these two cities changed their perception of and the uncertainties associated with more ambitious solar developments. We also shed light on the limitations that relate to engaging citizens and in smart energy transitions in two ways: (i) we provided a better understanding of the tensions between citizens, incumbents, new market players, different levels of government, and NGOs (see Manuscript 2); and (ii) we shed light on how deliberative participation might enhance public acceptance of more radical energy transitions pathways (see Manuscripts 1, 2; Mah et al., 2021a, 2021b). Objectives 3 – our comparative study found that although Tokyo and Hong Kong had their distinct national and city-level contextual factors, the two case cities shared similarities in that the recent socio-political and regional developments were crucial in shaping the trust and social learning capacities in energy transitions (see Manuscripts 1, 2; Mah, 2020; Mah et al., 2018). In addition, the online DPs revealed that some national level contextual factors (e.g. trust to the national governments; national energy policies, etc.) were important in explaining the citizens’ responses across the two cities. Objectives 4 – We identified that the concepts of trust; social learning; interactions between incumbents, citizens, governments, media; and national and city-level contextual factors could enrich the existing energy transitions theories in the literature. We examined these concepts utilising Tokyo and Hong Kong as empirical cases, and suggested that while different cities had distinct energy transitions trajectories from their socio-political contexts, our frameworks could be utilised to explain the similarities and differences across the two Asian cities.

12602717.label: Major findings and research outcome
12602717.value: Findings: 1. Normative mechanisms and outcomes of deliberative participation seem to apply in the Asian context (Mah et al., 2018). Through developing and testing a set of four integrated frameworks including: (i) a core framework of the dynamics between state and non-state actors in energy transitions (Mah, 2020), and it is complemented by three thematic frameworks, namely (ii) a trust-based systems framework for deliberative policy-making in energy transitions (Mah et al., 2021a); (iii) learning-oriented framework of deliberative participation (Mah et al., 2021b); and (iv) the political-economic perspective of niche-regime dynamics (Mah, 2020), DP appears to enhance public acceptance of more radical transition pathways and policy changes (Mah et al., 2018; Manuscripts 1,2). 2. Trust building, and social learning (Mah et al., 2021a, b, c) are key processes in deliberative participations. Dialogues and learning processes (Mah et al., 2018), and the interactions between incumbents, citizens, governments, media created conditions that are favourable or impede normative processes and outcomes of deliberative participation. 3. Deliberative processes yield mixed outcomes in changing citizens’ choice of more ambitious energy options (Mah et al., 2018; Mah, 2019) 4. Our comparative studies found that national and city-level contextual factors are critical in shaping citizens’ energy decisions when they are engaged in deliberative decision-making processes (Mah et al., 2018). There exists strong politico-economic contexts that created conductive conditions for niche diffusion while inhibiting and cancelling out the positive forces of niche-regime dynamics at complex multi-scalar levels (Mah, 2020). 5. Policy implications: (i) we show the importance of deliberative participation for energy transitions. DP appears to enhance public acceptance of more radical transition pathways; (ii) we propose measures to address barriers to engaging stakeholders in energy transition through deliberative participation. We found that participants’ perceptions of ambitious energy futures were influenced by tradeoffs between alternatives, perceptions of the distribution of costs and beneﬁts between utilities and electricity consumers, and a number of other contextual factors. These findings suggest that policy makers and other policy stakeholders, including utilities, need to give sufficient attention to the wide range issues that the public may be concerned about when engaging them on envisioning energy futures. Outcomes: 1. We created a new body of knowledge in energy transitions 2. We developed a conceptual framework of trust and social learning 3. We tested the application and conducted the first online DPs in the world to engage the public in making complex energy decisions 4. We provided policy recommendations

12602717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12602717.value: The findings of this project suggest 4 major potentials for further research development: 1. We can extend the comparative study of Tokyo and Hong Kong to a larger comparative study in other Asian (e.g. South Korea, Taiwan) and the western (e.g. the UK, France) regions. A similar scale online DP project can enhance the generalisability of findings and the global impacts. 2. We can test the conceptual framework in the contexts of other smart energy technological options, such as EVs and wind power. 3. We have developed and secured a Research Impact Fund (RIF) project (R2002-20F) based on the interdisciplinary research network from this project to study further on the low-carbon community and energy saving potentials under an app-based, deep engagement approach. 4. We have developed and applied for another General Research Fund (GRF; Ref No. 12618322) based on the interdisciplinary research network from this project to study on solar prosumer dynamics in the East Asian context. 5. We have fostered an interdisciplinary research network and found the Asian Low-Carbon University Network (ALUN) for further research collaboration

12602717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12602717.value: Trust building and social learning are two critical dimensions in deliberative governance in sustainable energy transitions. While public acceptance of radical energy transitions embracing risks and uncertainties of new energy technological options is crucial, this comparative study of Tokyo and Hong Kong aims to understand the extent to which new deliberative governance approaches can foster trust building and social learning, and in turn public acceptance of radical energy transitions. By conducting 42 qualitative interviews and two online deliberative pollings (DPs) with 136 Tokyo and 174 Hong Kong citizens to discuss on solar future scenarios, this project has several key findings: First, the online DPs appear to enhance public acceptance of more radical transition pathways and policy changes. Second, trust building and social learning are key deliberative processes of radical energy transitions. Third, deliberative processes yield mixed outcomes in trust building and social learning. Fourth, national and city-level contextual factors are critical in shaping trust-building and social-learning processes, and subsequently affecting citizens’ acceptance of radical energy transitions. These findings suggest that policy makers and stakeholders need to give sufficient attention to issues concerned by the public when engaging them on envisioning energy futures.

12603017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12603017.value: 本研究項目將從華南本土及全球的角度，探討華南海洋物質文化由明朝至今在文本、視覺及物質方面的意義。珊瑚、貝殼、海水珍珠、海綿向來在沿海居民的日常生活中扮演重要角色，也一直具有經濟、社會、藝術價值。華南本土加工的海洋器物，包括19世紀繪有香港維多利亞港景色的蠔殼，一直是全球遊客眼中別具意義的紀念品，由此可見海洋物質文化正是構成華南文化身份與傳統的重要元素，但由於環境污染和天然資源過度開採，海洋器物正逐漸消失，使這項研究變得更加重要，來得適時。 雖然以往曾有人研究從歐洲至北京宮廷的珊瑚貿易，但至今尚未有人將研究焦點放在華南地區的海洋器物。我們希望填補這個空白。本研究項目將跟隨穿越全球的器物，探索不同時代的海洋物質文化，審視早期現代交易模式與當代全球相互連結兩種模式之間的關係。研究項目會從明朝鄭和開拓「海上絲路」開始，研究海禁時代器物在華南本土環境和全球脈絡之間的關係，探討荷蘭及英國東印度公司大規模的亞洲海洋器物商品貿易，闡釋現代旅遊業的物質世界，並審視貝殼在當代藝術和近代華南工匠技藝中的地位。 我們研究海洋物質文化時，將採用以下的嶄新方法， (a) 綜合下列研究角度，利用跨學科方法研究特定地點的本土生態環境和傳統：(i) 從博物館及私人收藏著手，開展以器物為本的物質文化研究；(ii) 以影像為本的視覺文化研究；(iii) 以文本為本的文獻研究；(iv) 訪問策展人、匠人及藝術家。 (b) 以跨文化視野 (i) 研究本地與全球器物網絡之間的連結；(ii) 將本地研究置於全球學術研究脈絡；(iii) 融合「上層」與「下層」文化的器物為本研究。 本項目的主要目的是： (i) 探討華南海物質文化的意義； (ii) 將現有的華南、華北及宮廷研究置於相應的脈絡中； (iii) 將我們從華南本土研究所得的資料置於全球框架中。 研究項目成果如下： (i) 發表會議學術報告； (ii) 在國際刊物發表兩篇通過同儕評審的文章； (iii) 發表一篇以海洋物質文化及華南有形傳統及工藝為題的文章，以大眾為目標讀者； (iv) 建立中國海洋物質文化數據庫，羅列全球博物館的相關藏品； (v) 與本地及國際學術界、社區交流； (vi) 教材

12603117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12603117.value: The Taiping Civil War broke out in the mid-19th century, and lasted over 14 years involving 17 provinces. It is an important historic event in feudal monarchal China and had an important influence on current literature. During the war period, more than two hundred ci writers wrote more than two thousand ci poems to record and describe the war and rested events . It is such a unique literary phenomenon that it adds brand new cultural significance to the history of ci poetry and Chinese literature. However, there is little research in the relevant field. This project will fill the blank in the area. This project will focus on the following aspects:1. The mutual confirming and complementation between historical records and ci writings.2. The full and wide practice of the theory of ci history and bi xing ji tuo.3. The revelation of group consciousness in mass responsive writings of ci. 4. The unique style occurred in the war descriptions.5. Re-position the important ci writers through thorough summarization. The significance of the project lies in what it will reveal of the progress of ci poetry in terms of literary style, of how the genre of ci was influenced and strengthened by the changes of social and historic climate. It points out that ci writings on social events, especially on the Taiping War, have evolved both in width and depth, which is unprecedented in ci history. Although this project focuses on the ci writings of Taiping War, it will bring benefits for both researchers in history of Taiping War and litrary jistory of classical Chinese literature. Therefore, in order to fulfill the task, the methodology of history, literature history and literary theory will be employed. 太平天國運動是中國近代的一個重要事件，對當時的文學發展有重大影響。當時有超過200個詞人，寫作了超過2000首詞作，來表現這一事件。不過歷來沒有得到關注。本硏究課題擬討論詞的寫作與歷史的關係；詞的比興寄託理論和詞史理論在這一特殊階段中的實踐和深化；詞人的群體意識；一些著名作家的創作特色及其文學定位。等等。本課題的意義體現在，可以從一個特定方面認識太平天國，可以更好地思考歷史和文學的關係，可以填補文學史特別是詞史的一個空白，對於全面認識清詞復興，對於全面認識當時文人的心態，都有著重要的價値。

12603117.label: Realisation of objectives
12603117.value: 這一課題，既是文學的，又是歷史的，文史結合，對太平天國時期的文學和歷史進行考察，增強了對這一階段詞學發展的理解。本課題從歷史的角度更好地思考了詞體文學的發展與當時的時代的關係，而從文學的角度，則補充了對歷史的認識。太平天國時期，社會矛盾進一步激化，時代呼喚著詞壇的新思路，因此，從杜甫發展而來的詩史理論，經過陳維崧、周濟等人的宣揚，在這個時候體現出了更加強大的力量，詞人們自覺地在詞體文學中反映歷史、思考歷史，增強了作品的深度。同時，常州詞派所提倡的比興寄託理論，也在這個時候獲得了更好的發展土壤，人們更為自覺地用這個理論指導自己的創作，煥發了新的生機。在太平天國戰爭時期，詞人們的群體意識被進一步激發，他們在顛沛流離中，更加增強了彼此溝通的心理需求，不少著名作家倡導唱和，使得詞壇風貌有了新的呈現。詞體文學與戰爭的關係，一直以來沒有得到很好的研究，本課題在這個方面，有著較為全面的思考。從晚唐五代，到北宋南渡，發展到宋元之際、明清之際，一直到太平天國時期，詞體文學不斷被注入新的因素，展示了一種特定的與以往不同的面貌。本研究也致力於一些的新的角度的開發，比如圖像與文學的結合，拓展了進一步發展的空間。

12604017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12604017.value: Scholars interested in the study of silk textiles from ancient China have focused either on the historical changes of designs or on the more generalized study of weaving techniques; few have attempted to bring the two together and explore the greater socio-economic landscape behind the textile industry. The proposed project aims to explore the relationship between silk textile designs and weaving techniques in China in the period 500--200 BCE. It intends to use examples of Chinese textiles from both archaeological excavations and the collections of world renowned museums as case studies. It will explore, with the help of digital technology, how decorative patterns were created through various weaving techniques. These case studies will demonstrate how textiles were made efficiently but also with diverse designs. This type of production enabled the establishment of many exchange networks, which permitted the rapid accumulation of wealth and resources of subsequent empires like the Qin and the Han. The project is also intended to explore the use of new biomaterial from natural and genetically modified silk proteins in revitalizing early silk fibers. This technology will help increase the flexibility of those fragile fibers so that we can further study their texture and how they would have functioned on wearers' bodies. The project will shed light on an innovative interdisciplinary research orientation incorporating the fields of art history, archaeology, computer science and molecular biotechnology. 以往古代中國絲織品的研究者要不專注於探討織品設計的變化，要不就是織法的概括描述；很少有人嘗試把二者結合去探討織品行業更大的社會經濟面貌。此研究項目旨在探討約公元前500-200年中國絲織品設計與織法的關係。我們會使用一些考古發掘的織物作個案研究。同時利用數碼技術，探討織物上的紋飾是如何用不同織法製造出來。這些個案研究會展示織工如何有效率地工作，並能運用多元設計。這種生產模式催生了很多交換網絡，使之後的秦與漢帝國財富與資源能迅速累積。同時，此項目亦會嘗試從自然的絲蛋白中提取新式生化材料，以保護古代絲纖維，使本已脆弱之纖維回復某程度之彈力，這樣可使我們更好地研究絲織品之質地，又其如何影響穿戴者之身體。此項目會為跨學科研究揭示新穎的方向，以統合藝術史、考古、電腦科學與分子生物技術。
