12613217.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12613217.value: 殖民地香港的映演實踐：電影放映與接收史（1897-1925)

12613217.label: Project Objectives
12613217.value: To update the first three decades of Hong Kong film historiography. To complete a second database of early film exhibition and reception in colonial Hong Kong from 1897 to 1925. To publish two articles on screen practices in colonial Hong Kong (1897-1920).
rows: To update the first three decades of Hong Kong film historiography.
To complete a second database of early film exhibition and reception in colonial Hong Kong from 1897 to 1925.
To publish two articles on screen practices in colonial Hong Kong (1897-1920).

12613217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12613217.value: This project will present a history of screen practices in colonial Hong Kong, analyzing the modes of film exhibition and reception from 1897 to 1925. The year 1897 is the advent of film screenings, while 1925 represents the maturity of movie exhibition as an industrial practice. This application continues the 2013-14 GRF project “Early Hong Kong Cinema in English language Documents” that aimed to uncover primary source materials on film marketing, promotion, exhibition and reception published in Hong Kong English press. The 2013-14 application was awarded HKD90,000 (USD11,000). Despite the inadequate support, we fulfilled the objective by reading and collecting film coverage in The China Mail (1896-1925) and South China Morning Post (1903-1925). We confirmed that English-language newspapers covered substantial film news; we also discovered a rich history of screen practices in the first three decades of its introduction to Hong Kong audiences. By “screen practices,” we mean two things. First we treat projection of motion pictures as an entertainment event, a technological display, a public assembly, a business, and an emerging part of social and cultural life. Second, screen practices indicate the cultivation of a film industry before production entered the picture. We use screen practices to explore the formation of early film industry by identifying screening routines and patterns of business transactions. We indicate "practice" to highlight the repetition of such screen activities in achieving some form of proficiency, and recognition. A history of screen practices thus reveals the multiplicity and heterogeneity of early Hong Kong film culture, covering the apparatus, built environment, distribution and exhibition, censorship, and reception of cinema as a key part of public life in colonial Hong Kong. Two major tasks are envisioned. First, we aim to present an open access database to serve as an essential resource for research on Hong Kong film history from its beginning to the mid 1920s. We have collected more than 25,000 items of new materials, covering movie theatres, distribution companies and circuits, film advertisements, and film reviews. These primary materials will help construct a history of early screen practices. Second, we will prepare three articles on screen practices of Hong Kong from 1897 to 1920s. The large trove of data collected and the articles published will reshape our understanding of early Hong Kong film history and beyond. 這項研究分析自1897年至1925年間電影放映活動的模式與接收，以呈現殖民地香港映演實踐的歷史風貌。 此為2013-14年度優配研究金項目「英文報紙中的早期香港電影：1897-1925」的延續，目的是於香港的英文報紙中發掘電影放映、營銷、宣傳、觀眾反應等的第一手資料。雖然該項目只獲得港幣九萬元的資助，但從《德臣西報》（The China Mail , 1897-1925）及《南華早報》（ South China Morning Post , 1903-1925）兩份報紙中，我們收集到重要的電影史料，有助建構早期香港電影映演實踐的豐富歷史。 我們將「映演實踐」首先定義為娛樂活動、科技展示、公眾集會和盈利等的一項新興的社會與文化生活體驗。其次，「映演實踐」指的是製作業尚未成型的早期電影產業。我們透過映演實踐的常規作業與商業模式，研究早期電影產業的形成。而映演實踐的歷史，如電影院環境及設備的改善、電影的發行與放映、審查等，展現了早期香港電影文化的多重性與異質性，以及觀影活動作為殖民地香港公眾生活重要的一環。 此項目有兩個目標：第一，建立一個公開的資料庫，供公眾蒐索閱讀；第二，準備兩篇相關題旨的論文 。逾二萬五千項的新資料，包括電影發行、電影院及院線發展等相關的電影廣告、新聞和評論，都將成為研究早期香港電影史的寶庫。

12613217.label: Realisation of objectives
12613217.value: Objective 1 and 3: To update the first three decades of Hong Kong film historiography; to publish two articles on screen practices in colonial Hong Kong (1897-1920). One journal article, “Early Screen Culture in Colonial Hong Kong (1897-1907)” was published in Transnational Screens 10.3 (2019). A second article, “More than Law and Order: Film Regulation in Colonial Hong Kong” was revised and resubmitted for final review at the Journal of Cinema and Media Studies. Objective 2: To complete a second database of early film exhibition and reception in colonial Hong Kong from 1897 to 1925. To follow up on a previous open-access database of film ads and news collected from The Chinese Mail (華字日報1900-1941), a second open-access database, “A History of Film Exhibition and Reception in Colonial Hong Kong (1897 to 1925),” has been launched in early June, 2021. The new database intends to serve as an essential resource for research on Hong Kong film history from the initial screenings of motion pictures in the late 1890s to the mid-1920s. https://digital.library.ln.edu.hk/en/projects/flim/ The database provides online access to more than 29,000 items of news materials, which were transcribed from over 58,000 primary source materials from 1897 to 1925 in three major English-language Hong Kong newspapers, South China Morning Post, The China Mail, and Hong Kong Telegraph. The number of published news and advertisement entries is as follows: No. of entries South China Morning Post The China Mail Hong Kong Telegraph News 7,311 2,286 2,707 Advertisement 9,118 4,046 4,504 Total 16,449 6,332 7,211 29,972 Each entry contains the date of publication, original title (if any), column/section, and excerpt. Furthermore, four datasets by venues, organisations, key persons, and film projectors and titles were created, with each data item identified by a tag. The entries that include the same item can be browsed or searched easily using the tag. All the records have also been edited and proofread to ensure accuracy and consistency.

12613217.label: Major findings and research outcome
12613217.value: In the article “Early screen culture in colonial Hong Kong (1897-1907)” published in Transnational Screens 10.3 (full article in Part C), Hong Kong early screen culture is examined in conjunction with socialisation and colonial governance of Hong Kong of the early 20th century to explore the implications of film exhibition, using the concept of dispositif. Three aspects of early screen culture in colonial Hong Kong are presented to outline the multi-faceted early film screening: the primacy of technical marvels and the management of cinema machines; the symbiosis between motion pictures and 19th century live entertainment; the emergence of film exhibition as a commercial institution, subject to regulation. By offering substantial information on the film industry found in local English-language newspapers and uncovering the facets of early screen practice, the research provides a more comprehensive historiography of early Hong Kong screen culture in the deployment of colonial forces. The other article, “More than Law and Order: Film Regulation in Early Colonial Hong Kong,” under review in the Journal of Cinema and Media Studies, analyses the political and financial motives behind the ordinances on public performances and film exhibition. With the details of the practice of film regulation in the early 20th century found in newspaper reports on civil and criminal charges against the cinema business, the research pinpoints the imperialist and racial ideologies in the governance of cinema as a social and economic institution. An argument was made that race should be taken into account when examining the introduction of film regulation in Hong Kong.

12613217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12613217.value: 1. A monograph is being developed based on the findings from the newspapers. Tentatively titled “Cinema and the Colonial Dispositif: Early Screen Culture in Hong Kong (1897 to 1925),” the monograph will consist of five chapters: a. Yinghua, Photo Pictures: Re-visioning Chinese Film Histography b. Kinematography and Dispositif: Theorizing Early Screens in Hong Kong c. More than Law and Order: Film Regulation and Colonial Governance d. Movie Theatres, Modernity, and the Sanitized Public Space e. In and out of the Colonial Screen: Cinema Fans and Entrepreneurs 2. Two annexes to the database will be added, a dataset of the information (e.g., location, facilities, personnel, and equipment) of the theatres and another dataset of the projectors and other machines used to project films by the theatres. A map will also be drawn to mark the historic cinema districts. These two additons will provide useful references for researchers to grasp the development of exhibition business in Hong Kong and the technological aspect of film exhibition in early 20th century. 70% of this work has been completed.

12613217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12613217.value: Early screen culture in colonial Hong Kong is a multi-faceted practice displaying both the intrinsic and extrinsic features of early cinema practice, and it can be seen as a microcosm of the colonial history of Hong Kong. However, the standard film historiography mainly highlights the ‘forerunners’ of the film industry, while the narratives of the practices and stratifications of the early screen culture were absent due to the lack of primary sources. To move beyond hagiography, I developed an open-access database under this research project to serve as an essential resource for research on Hong Kong film history from the initial screening of motion pictures in the late 1890s to the mid-1920s. It provides online access to more than 29,000 items of news materials in three English-language Hong Kong newspapers, i.e., The China Mail, Hong Kong Telegraph and South China Morning Post. Based on the primary materials found in local English-language newspapers, we explored the pivotal role of film exhibition in connection to the social and cultural history of colonial Hong Kong. The research provides an in-depth perspective of the early screen culture, as well as its connection to the social fabric of Hong Kong of the early 20th century.

13500117.label: Project Objectives
13500117.value: To examine the effects of media coverage on firms’ choice of public debt versus private loans; To examine the channels through which media coverage impacts the debt choice; To examine the effects of media coverage on contract terms in both loan and bond markets.
rows: To examine the effects of media coverage on firms’ choice of public debt versus private loans;
To examine the channels through which media coverage impacts the debt choice;
To examine the effects of media coverage on contract terms in both loan and bond markets.

13500117.label: Realisation of objectives
13500117.value: We have achieved all the three objectives successfully: 1. We find that firms with more media coverage have a significantly lower likelihood of having bank loans on their balance sheets and a higher proportion of debt in the form of bonds and notes. 2. We find that media's effect is concentrated among firms with more available information and among firms with a higher demand for external monitoring, suggesting that the media plays a complementary role for other information sources and a substitution role for other governance mechanisms. 3. We find that positive (negative) news significantly reduces (increases) the interest spread and increases (reduces) the issuance amount for both bank loans and public bonds. Positive news has no effect on privately placed bonds, but that negative news significantly increases privately placed bonds. Regarding debt maturity, news sentiment affects only bank loans but no effects on bond issuance.

13500117.label: Major findings and research outcome
13500117.value: Our empirical analyses employ RavenPack—a leading news analytics database that covers all news articles and press releases disseminated via Dow Jones Newswires. Our sample includes all U.S. firms covered by the Dow Jones Newswire that have borrowed bank loans and/or issued bonds or nonbank private debt (bonds and notes as defined in Capital IQ) from 2001 to 2014. We find that firms with more media coverage have a significantly lower likelihood of having bank loans on their balance sheets and a higher proportion of debt in the form of bonds and notes. Our estimate suggests that an increase of one standard deviation in total news coverage reduces bank loan usage by 3.74% of total debt and increases bonds and notes by 4.01% of total debt. We also find that this effect is concentrated among firms with more available information and among firms with a higher demand for external monitoring, suggesting that the media plays a complementary role for other information sources and a substitution role for other governance mechanisms. With regard to how the media performs its information role, we find that it mainly complements other information sources rather than substitutes for them as studies in the equity market have found. It shows, among firms that have already had abundant information, the media mainly plays the role of reinterpretation and dissemination of relevant information. This is consistent with the media’s incentives to rebroadcast eye-catching events along with insightful interpretation of the information, a by no means trivial task. Our results suggest that the media is substituting for other commonly recognized governance devices—product market competition and the incentivized stakeholders in the relationship industry. The governance function of media coverage is further supported by our findings that more negative news coverage induces firms with public bond access to resort to privately placed bonds, rather than bank loans. Furthermore, news sentiment has significant implications for the access, price, and non-price terms of new debt issuance, whereas credit rating changes do not affect debt access, only the terms of the new debt. For example, we find that positive (negative) news significantly reduces (increases) the interest spread and increases (reduces) the issuance amount for both bank loans and public bonds. Positive news has no effect on privately placed bonds, but that negative news significantly increases privately placed bonds. Regarding debt maturity, news sentiment affects only bank loans but no effects on bond issuance.

13500117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
13500117.value: One challenging but interesting research topic is to examine how news content may impact the debt choice. We will focus on unfavorable news coverage. On one hand, bad news could trigger managerial action to improve governance that is instrumental for bond issuance; on the other hand, extremely bad news may deter bond issuance. The former case tends to happen in the long term, while the latter may take place in the short term. Note that the SDC database only contains registration date for those firms that successfully issue the bonds. To test the short-run effect, researchers need to hand collect the shelf registration information from Form S-3 and match with the SDC database to get the data on firms that have registered with the SEC on bond issuance but did not issue bonds at the end. We expect extremely unfavorable news to be negatively correlated with those firms that failed to issue bonds despite the registration of their intention to do so with the SEC.

13500117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
13500117.value: Our study contributes to the literature in several ways. First, we add to a growing literature that documents the media’s effect on financial markets. We find that media complements other information providers among firms with access to nonbank debt, particularly public bonds. By reinterpreting selected crucial information, media plays a complementary information role in addition to other information sources. Second, we contribute to the literature on better understanding of how firms choose financing instruments. To our best knowledge, we are among the first to examine the media’s governance role in debt structure. We add to the literature by showing that media coverage serves as a relevant governance device that mitigates firms’ reliance on bank monitoring and facilitates firms’ nonbank debt access. Third, we contribute to the understanding of the roles of different information providers in the financial system. We focus on credit rating agencies and media outlets. We find that firms with more media coverage tend to have significantly better ratings. In addition, although both rating changes and news sentiment significantly affect pricing and some non-pricing terms of debt, only news sentiment impacts the debt instrument choice. These findings indicate that media coverage fills the void left by credit rating agencies.

13500517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13500517.value: 美國證券交易委員會（SEC）證券法第33-8732A號要求公司從2006年底開始擴大披露有關高管和董事薪酬的信息。新的披露規則在兩個方面與舊規則有所不同.首先， 需要披露更多信息（擴展）：例如高管薪酬決策以及公司高管薪酬和公司業績之間的關係。其次，新規則要求公司披露首席財務官（CFO) 和首席執行官 (CEO) 以及接下來三位最高薪的高管的薪酬。以前，CEO的薪酬信息加上下四個最高薪酬高管是必需的。正如新聞稿中所述，監管機構“相信了解CFO的薪酬信息對股東很重要，因為他和CEO一樣對公司的定期報告作出認證並對公司的財務報表和其他財務信息的公平性擔負重要責任” 。由此可見， 對CFO的薪酬披露為外部人員提供了評估CFO價值的信息， 並促進外部人更好地監督CFO。反過來，更大的監測對CFO產生反饋壓力，使其更好地履行職責。 在這項研究中，我們將研究新規則如何影響CFO的行為表現。由於CFO的首要職責是把關財務報告質量，我們用財務報告的重述發生率和內部控制系統的質量來衡量財務報告質量。我們假設新的披露規則實施後， 公司的財務報告質量提升。 這項研究對信息披露的效用提供新的證據。

13500517.label: Realisation of objectives
13500517.value: The 2006 Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) rule, by changing the definition of Named Executive Officers (NEO), mandates chief financial officer (CFO) compensation disclosure. Based on hand-collected data of CFO information from firm' 10K reports, we identify a group of firms whose CFOs were not in the NEO list before the mandate and started to disclose CFO compensation information (treatment group) and a group of firms whose CFOs were in the NEO list and continue to disclose CFO compensation information after the 2006 mandate. Based on a difference-in-differences research design, we study the real effects of CFO compensation disclosure regulation on CFO job performance, measured by her firm's financial reporting quality and internal control quality - corresponding to the two objectives in the project. We hypothesize that the disclosure of CFO compensation information, by facilitating shareholder monitoring of the board in providing appropriate incentives to CFOs, leads to better CFO job performance. We examine the two objectives and find consistent results with our hypotheses.

13500517.label: Major findings and research outcome
13500517.value: We find the treatment firms, which start disclosing CFO compensation information under the 2006 rule, compared to the control firms, which already disclose CFO compensation before 2006, experience an improvement in CFO performance, as exhibited in reduced frequency of accounting restatements and internal control weaknesses. The results are more pronounced for non-family firms, firms with less independent boards, firms with CFOs subject to weaker monitoring by audit committees, and firms with higher institutional ownership. The paper received a re submission invitation from one of the B+ (top 10) accounting journal.

13500517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
13500517.value: We are revising for the journal. We will do more to mitigate the endogeneity concern regarding the non-randomness of a firm falling into a treatment or control group. We shall also examine more CFO performance measures that CFOs are largely accountable in addition to restatements and internal control quality. We shall also control for any impact of the 2006 SEC on firm's other top executives and on the their overall governance quality.

13500517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
13500517.value: In the United States, the SEC has mandated the disclosure of executive compensation since 1934 with the rationale of greater transparency facilitating shareholder monitoring of the compensation practice. The simple intuition is ‘sunshine is the best disinfectant.’ With the disclosed executive compensation information, shareholders monitor the board through exerting pressure in the process of setting the compensation schemes or ex-post intervening in board replacement decisions, if necessary. The 2006 rule changes the definition of named executive officers from including the CEO and the four other most highly compensated executive officers to including the CEO, the CFO, and the three other most highly compensated executive officers. Thus, this change in the 2006 rule has a differential effect on two groups of firms discussed previously. We examine how CFOs’ job performance differ before and after 2006 for these two groups of firms to demonstrate a real economic effect of compensation disclosure on executives’ behavior and find a relative improvement of CFO performance after 2006. Our study adds to the effect of public policies that regulate compensation disclosures, which are widely adopted by the SEC and Congress in response to public concerns about executive compensation in the U.S. More broadly, our study also enrich the understanding of the effect of disclosure regulations that aim at improving the welfare of various stakeholders.

To qualitatively investigate how changes in an ambiguous environment in the sense of Nth (N>2) order stochastic dominance influence precautionary saving decisions under a generalized two-period smooth ambiguity framework. 13500717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13500717.value: A stochastic improvement refers to the development of established risks in the stochastic dominance sense (Chiu 2012). In the two-period decision-making model, decisions tend to have the following formal structure: an agent pays the current cost for stochastic improvements of certain risks that might take place in the future. A few examples include: an agent who sacrifices current consumption to improve wealth distribution in the future; an agent who exerts effort to protect herself against any future risk of loss; or a policyholder who pays a premium for an insurance policy to reduce any variables in future wealth. We call such decisions precautionary paying for stochastic improvements. Our literature review demonstrates that very few existing studies on prevention and precaution disentangle the factors of risk, time and ambiguity. Therefore, certain types of prevention and precaution behavior cannot be explained by the existing studies. In the proposed project, we will theoretically investigate how to compare changes in ambiguous environments for the purpose of stochastic improvement. The project will use an interval dominance order comparative statics methodology (Quah and Strulovici, 2009) to deal with the fundamental theoretical problems in risk management and economics. We will provide comparative statics analysis for the models. Based on the theoretical results derived from this project, we will investigate saving, insurance and prevention issues. This project will hopefully help us to better understand the basic and relevant factors that determine saving, insurance and prevention behavior. Understanding such behavior through an economics theory will improve our current knowledge in economics.

13500717.value: We complete objectives 1 and 3 in research outcome 1. To complete objectives 2 and 4, we build two axiomatically robust smooth ambiguity models in research outcomes 2 and 4. We also use Choquet Expected Utility in research outcome 3 to achieve objectives 2 and 4.

13500717.label: Major findings and research outcome
13500717.value: 1. We provide a systematic treatment of a decision maker’s current payment for stochastic improvements in a two-period smooth ambiguity model. Our model disentangles intertemporal substitution, risk preference, and ambiguity preference. We determine the effect of changes in ambiguity aversion on the strength of the current willingness to pay. Our results are used to analyze two fundamental economics problems, namely, saving and prevention (self-insurance). We generalize the models in previous works and explore the effects of ambiguity aversion (see research outcome 1). 2. We establish three axiomatically founded smooth ambiguity models by relaxing the consistency axiom in Klibanoff, Marinacci, and Mukerji (2005) to the imprecise consistency axiom. The first model is able to accommodate the Ellsberg Paradox (Ellsberg 1961) without imposing different preferences in different stages and characterizes ambiguity attitudes via risk vulnerability (Gollier and Pratt 1996) and consistency imprecision. The second and third models recover Klibanoff, Marinacci, and Mukerji (2005)’s model as a special case (see research outcome 2). 3. We establish an axiomatically founded robust smooth ambiguity model by integrating an exogenously given background risk into the model of KMM. Our model provides a decision framework for Decision Makers who simultaneously face an ambiguous risk and a background risk. Moreover, our model addresses the question of whether uninsurable background risk will lead Decision Makers to behave in a less uncertainty-averse way (see research outcome 4). 4. We studie optimal demand of insurance coverage when insured has nonadditive subjective probability beliefs on loss uncertainty. By showing the equivalent conditions of Jensen inequality in Choquet Expected Utility framework, we not only provide the threshold of insurance premium whereby Mossin Theorem holds, but also explore the joint effect of both risk aversion and uncertainty aversion on optimal insurance demand(see research outcome 3). Objective 2 (70%) and Objective 4 (70%): We found it is not easy to extend the result to higher order stochastic dominance. So we build two new axiomatically robust smooth ambiguity models to study the issue. But we are still preparing these papers to be submitted to the top journals.

13500717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
13500717.value: The representations presented in this project show that the presence of a background risk is important to determine the degree of ambiguity aversion. For example, adding an unfair background risk to wealth makes risk vulnerable decision makers act in a less ambiguity-averse way, thereby decreasing the value of information that reduces ambiguity. Not taking the effect of background risks on ambiguity aversion into account may lead to incorrect predictions. It is interesting to observe how many results in the classic ambiguity aversion models extend to the background environments.

13500717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
13500717.value: Would the presence of background risk modify the decision makers’ ambiguity attitudes toward the endogenous prospect? Is it true that, e.g., a deterioration in the background risk will always reduce the degree of ambiguity aversion toward the controllable prospects? In this project, we propose several models to examine the above questions.

13500817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13500817.value: Shared leadership is an emergent team property resulting from the distribution of leadership functions and influence across multiple team members. Since shared leadership may address the limitations of singular leaders and perform multiple leadership functions more fully, it is gaining increased attention as a team leadership approach. Despite the rapidly growing attention to shared leadership, researchers are concerned that the current understanding of shared leadership may be seriously flawed. Although theories suggest that shared leadership is a dynamic process emerging through the interactions of team members, current research has mainly adopted the static approach and generated inconsistent results. Without an understanding of the dynamics of shared leadership, the current literature provides only limited insights into mechanisms and processes through which shared leadership influences team effectiveness. In the proposed study, we will build a time-sensitive model to improve shared leadership theory. We will develop our model based on entrepreneurial teams, which often face complex and uncertain tasks that demand efficient leadership and flexible adaptation. As development is a major task for entrepreneurial teams, this context will provide a good opportunity to examine the dynamics of shared leadership and its underlying mechanisms. Specifically, we will adopt a latent change score approach to explicitly examine a dynamic reciprocal relationship related to changes in shared leadership, transactive memory system, and team entrepreneurial passion. We propose that shared leadership will promote changes in a team’s transactive memory system and team entrepreneurial passion. These changes will in turn further fuel changes in shared leadership. The enhanced transactive memory system and team entrepreneurial passion will also mediate the effects of shared leadership on team entrepreneurial progress. To capture the mutual influence among team members, we will use a social network approach to measure shared leadership. This project is important for several reasons. First, it will provide novel insights into the development and effectiveness of shared leadership in entrepreneurial teams over time. Our shift from a static view to a dynamic view should also give stronger predictions and improved causal inferences. Second, we will identify the underlying mechanisms. This exploration will shed light on our understanding of how shared leadership influences team outcomes. Third, this study will lay a useful foundation for future research on shared leadership and entrepreneurial teams in Hong Kong and mainland China. 采用共享型领导的团队中，多名团队成员会共同承担领导的职能和影响力。由于这样的共享型领导方式能够更充分地发挥领导的各项职能，共享型领导在团队研究中受到了越来越多的关注，而目前的研究对共享性领导的理解依然有所不足。共享型领导在理论上是一个动态的过程，它通常藉由团队成员的互动过程产生，发展和变化。目前关于共享型领导的研究有许多不一致的发现，这很可能与当前多数学者所采用的静态的研究方式有关。 本研究意在通过建立一个时间敏感型的模型来推进共享型领导的理论发展。我们聚焦于初创团队这一研究对象，一是因为初创团队通常面临复杂而不确定的环境，因此初创团队是对有效的领导力有极高要求的研究对象；二是因为初创团队在团队结构和成员互动方式上会经历比较明显的发展阶段，因而有利于研究共享型领导方式的产生和发展。我们将采用基于潜变量变化分值模型方法来研究共享型领导的变化，以及它与团队的交互记忆系统的变化，团队创业激情的变化之间的互惠影响。我们认为，共享型领导会促进团队交互记忆系统的成熟和创业激情的增长，而这些变化又会反过来促进共享型领导的进一步发展。为了测量团队成员之间相互施加的领导力和影响，我们还采用了社会网络的方法对共享型领导进行测量。 本项目的重要性主要有三点。第一，它将会给共享型领导在创业团队中随着时间的发展和效果提供新的洞见。从静态到动态的研究模式的改变也会使我们的研究在支持因果推理上更进一步。第二，我们研究了共享型领导的作用机制。这可以帮助我们理解共享型领导是如何影响团队结果。第三，本研究将对基于中国内地和香港的创业团队研究提供更多的案例和洞见。

13500817.label: Realisation of objectives
13500817.value: Although the project was significantly influenced and postponed because of the pandemic, we managed to finish the project and achieve all objectives. Before the longitudinal data collection, we interviewed a number of entrepreneurs in business incubators to learn about their team structures, their daily activities, and their ideas about shared leadership in entrepreneurial teams. We familiarized ourselves with the procedures and potential challenges of the data collection in business incubators. We managed to survey the management teams of 95 entrepreneurial firms. Most of the entrepreneurial teams in the business incubators are at the stage of opportunity development with the intention to attract capital venturing. This setting helps us investigate the dynamics of shared leadership in a field setting. Moreover, we collected longitudinal data by tracking 165 student project teams (including EMBA, MBA, graduate, and undergraduate students) who attended a competitive team project. In this team project, each team operated a simulated company. The initial condition of the company was identical for all teams. In addition, we also collected longitudinal data by tracking 84 student project teams who attended another business simulation competition. Each team also operated a simulated company with the same initial condition. These two settings help us trace the development of shared leadership from team formation. Using these data, we managed to achieve all objectives of this research project. Based on part of the findings of this research project, we have organized a symposium entitled “The dynamics of shared leadership: New directions in research,” which will be presented at the 2022 Annual Meeting of the Academy of Management (see https://2022.aom.org/meetings/virtual/uqSED8CbTnyrfghq5). In this symposium, we will present two papers that are derived from this research project. Except for these two papers, we also have several other working papers derived from this project. We aim to publish these papers in top-tier journals in the following years. Below, we outline the objectives of this project and state how we achieved all these project objectives. First, we articulated the development of shared leadership in entrepreneurial teams over time. Through tracing the development of shared leadership since team formation, we investigated the development trajectory of shared leadership. Using latent growth curve modelling, we found that there was a positive developmental trajectory of shared leadership, suggesting that shared leadership developed over time. Thus, we demonstrated the temporal nature of shared leadership, and provided an explanation for how shared leadership develops over time in newly founded entrepreneurial teams. Second, we articulated why shared leadership in entrepreneurial teams may change over time by examining whether shared leadership develops in reciprocal relationships with a cognitive team property (i.e., team transactive memory system) and a team affective property (i.e., team entrepreneurial passion). Using latent change score modelling, we found that there was a dynamic reciprocal relationship related to change between shared leadership and team transactive memory system: shared leadership promoted changes in team transactive memory system; in turn, the changed team transactive memory system further fueled the change in shared leadership. However, we did not find a significant dynamic reciprocal relationship related to change between shared leadership and team entrepreneurial passion. In addition, we examined whether shared leadership influences entrepreneurial progress through team transactive memory system and team entrepreneurial passion. As expected, we found that shared leadership had a positive effect on team transactive memory system and team entrepreneurial passion. In turn, both team transactive memory system and team entrepreneurial passion positively influenced entrepreneurial progress. Third, we provided evidence for the effectiveness of shared leadership in entrepreneurial teams based on a dynamic approach. We found that the dynamics of shared leadership positively influenced the dynamics of entrepreneurial performance. Thus, shared leadership is a promising way to enhance entrepreneurial performance. Fourth, we developed a refined measure of shared leadership based on social network approach that captures both the configuration and content of shared leadership. Scholars have pondered on what is actually being shared in shared leadership. Without a clear and comprehensive understanding of “what is actually being shared,” the meaning of shared leadership remains vague. Drawing on functional leadership theory, we proposed a role-based approach to understand the sharing of leadership in venture management teams and developed a measure of role-based shared leadership. In this measure, we specified “leadership roles” as the content of shared leadership, and employed the social network approach to depicting the configuration of role-based shared leadership. This measure can capture both the configuration and content of shared leadership and has good validity.

13500817.label: Major findings and research outcome
13500817.value: Shared leadership is an emergent team property resulting from the distribution of leadership roles and influence across multiple team members. In this project, we investigate the dynamics of shared leadership in entrepreneurial teams. This research project has four major findings. First, as shown in the paper entitled “Understanding the trajectories of shared leadership development in entrepreneurial teams: A latent growth curve approach,” we found that shared leadership grew over time in newly founded teams since team formation. Therefore, this project foregrounds the temporal nature of shared leadership, and it helps us have a deeper understanding of how shared leadership develops over time in newly founded teams. Second, as shown in the paper entitled “The dynamics of shared leadership in entrepreneurial teams: A latent change score approach,” we examined a dynamic reciprocal relationship of shared leadership with team entrepreneurial passion and team transactive memory system. We found a dynamic reciprocal relationship related to change between shared leadership and team transactive memory system: shared leadership promoted changes in team transactive memory system; in turn, the changed team transactive memory system further fueled the change in shared leadership. Yet, we did not find a significant reciprocal relationship between shared leadership and team entrepreneurial passion. Third, we provided evidence for the effectiveness of shared leadership in entrepreneurial teams based on a dynamic approach. We found that the dynamics of shared leadership positively impacted the dynamics of entrepreneurial performance. In addition, we found that shared leadership had a positive influence on entrepreneurial performance through team transactive memory system and team entrepreneurial passion. Forth, we developed a refined measure of shared leadership. Existing shared leadership research tends to focus on the configuration of leadership ties without paying much attention to what kind of leadership ties are being shared. Yet, scholars ponder on what is actually being shared in shared leadership. Drawing on functional leadership theory, we proposed a role-based approach to understand the sharing of leadership in venture management teams and developed a measure of role-based shared leadership. This measure can capture both the configuration and content of shared leadership, and it has good validity.

13500817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
13500817.value: Based on the insights obtained from this project, we can further develop the research in three ways. First, we have advanced a refined measure of shared leadership and demonstrated its validity in the entrepreneurship setting. We will conduct a follow-up study to examine the predictive validity of this measure in other settings. Second, we have investigated the dynamics of shared leadership with team processes and emergent states. Given that many teams have a formal leader, we will conduct a follow-up study to investigate the role of formal team leaders in the dynamics of shared leadership. For example, will shared leadership emerges faster in teams with a humble leader? We have already found a data collection opportunity to test this idea. Third, we have investigated the dynamics of shared leadership in a “normal” context. Nevertheless, work teams inevitably face disruptive events (e.g., a crisis), which may impair team functions and effectiveness. Shared leadership might be a promising way to respond effectively after a disruptive event. Thus, it is theoretically and practically important to investigate whether and how shared leadership enables teams to “bounce back” more quickly from disruption events. We will conduct a follow-up study to examine this research question.

13500817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
13500817.value: In contrast to traditional top-down leadership approaches that focus on the leadership displayed by a designated leader, shared leadership emphasizes the collective enactment of leadership roles among team members, whereby team members take leadership roles in areas where they have expertise. Because shared leadership emerges through the interactive processes of team members, it is dynamic. In this project, we advance the research of shared leadership with a dynamic approach. Our findings foreground the dynamic nature of shared leadership and show that shared leadership develops over time in newly found entrepreneurial teams. Moreover, shared leadership has a reciprocal relationship with team transactive memory system. In addition, the dynamics of shared leadership further contribute to the dynamics of entrepreneurial team performance. This project has both important theoretical contributions and practical implications. It provides a better understanding of the dynamic nature of shared leadership and its underlying mechanisms in entrepreneurial teams, as well as contributes to the development of time-sensitive leadership theories in general and shared leadership theory in particular. Moreover, it also helps practitioners better understand and apply shared leadership to enhance performance in entrepreneurial teams.

13501017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13501017.value: Consumers today are frequently writing online product reviews on different websites across providers such as Amazon, TripAdvisor, and Yelp. Although some review websites simply ask consumers to describe their experience freely in a completely open-ended area, others may provide certain guidelines and instructions to direct consumers’ review behavior. One common practice, among many others, is requiring reviewers to provide both the pros and cons of their consumption experience. As we have learnt from the literature that a two-sided review can be perceived as either helpful or unhelpful, our primary interest is to understand how the review format plays a role in affecting the content of the review being written, and how this content impacts the reviewers’ subsequent behavior. More specifically, we aim to explore a potential bias in review behavior triggered by the pros-and-cons review format. We argue that this format can influence the decision to allocate a neutral aspect of an experience to the wrong category when the consumption experience is mostly positive (negative) across different aspects. In such a case, consumers may not find any negative (positive) aspects to fill the empty cons (pros) section and thus allocate a neutral aspect to the empty area. Such a desire to conform to the community norm of being cooperative, as a result, biases the review content and can subsequently influence the judgment of the rating score assignment. This proposed project attempts to contribute to the psychology literature by exploring the role of the sense of the community and the marketing literature by identifying a new source of biased review behavior that can be managed and avoided. We will conduct three lab experiments and an online empirical study to examine the proposed effects and the underlying mechanism. When consumers provide product reviews online, does the format of review structure affect their review behavior? In this research, we compare two online review formats, a structured pros-and-cons review vs. a non-structured open-ended review, and predict a biased review occurred for the structured pros-and-cons review. We predict that the presence of two fill-in areas (i.e., pros area and cons area) would encourage consumers to allocate some "neutral' experiences into these areas. We further propose a sense of community hypothesis to explain this cooperative misallocation behavior. 當消費者在網路上提供消費的經驗評論時, 評論的格式是否會影響他們的評論行為呢? 本研究比較兩種評論格式: 一個架構式的優缺點評論, 與一個無架構式的開放評論, 並預測優缺點評論會導致偏誤的評論行為. 我們的預測是, 呈現兩個需要填空的區域的時候 (也就是優點與缺點)會鼓勵消費者將某些中性的經驗也分類地放入這些區域. 我們也提出了一個社群感受度的假設來解釋這個偏誤的分類行為.

13501117.label: Realisation of objectives
13501117.value: The three objectives have been fully realized, although it has taken much longer time to finish the project as expected. This project has produced two outputs. The first is a paper examining intra-industry information transfer in China. We undertook this project, because we found that there is no prior study examining intra-industry information transfer in the context of emerging markets in general and China in specific. Existing studies have focused either on mature markets or used international data. As intra-industry information transfer is a sophisticated information acquisition behaviour that investors in emerging markets such as China may not have the ability and incentive to undertake, it is necessary for us to examine whether intra-industry information transfer exists in China and their salient characteristics before we could examine whether and how private information may influence the intra-industry information transfer. We thus started a project examining whether intra-industry information transfer exists in China and how the transfer (if any) has been shaped by the country’s institutional environment. We submitted the first version of our paper to the Journal of Banking and Finance on 21st June 2019. We have gone through three rounds of revisions, as one of the reviewers raised new questions in every round of his/her reviews. After three rounds of revisions that had taken us for nearly 2 years, the editor eventually indicated on 10th April 2021 that our manuscript had converged to publication. We have already submitted our fourth revision for another round of review. We are confident that we have addressed all the remaining issues raised by the reviewers and this paper could be accepted by JBF soon. After conducting literature review, data collection and cleaning, we started to examine how investors’ private information about firms may influence intra-industry information transfer and obtained some preliminary results in late 2019 (as we have scheduled in our proposal). However, the results were unexpected and opposite to what had been hypothesized in our proposal. According to the existing literature, both information-based and familiarity-based perspectives predict that information transfer is stronger for close non-announcing firms than distant non-announcing firms. However, we found that investors transfer more information to distant rather than close non-announcing firms. At the beginning, we were trapped by the existing information-based and familiarity-based perspectives and confine our focus to the question of how investors’ private information may influence their interpretation and transfer of the information as contained in corporate announcements. Instead of developing a new perspective, we tried very hard to refine our modelling and estimation methods to check whether our results are robust. More importantly, we conducted a lot of cross-sectional analyses by looking at different interaction effects in order to gain some insights on the unexpected results. Nevertheless, the results of the cross-sectional analyses were very confusing and very difficult to understand. In September 2020, we suddenly realized that there may be a new intra-industry information transfer channel that had been overlooked by the literature – the transfer of information via private information channel instead of induced by corporate announcements. As existing studies have focused on the transfer of information as induced by corporate announcements, the transfer of information via private information channel even in the absence of corporate announcements is something entirely new to the literature. Under this perspective, investors may transfer industry information by using their private information rather than rely on corporate announcements as an information source. As private information transfer is more likely when both announcing and non-announcing firms are located close to each other, this perspective predicts that investors will transfer less information as contained in corporate announcement to close peer firms than distant peer firms – the results that we previously failed to understand!! After we jumped out of the box, we immediately collected more data to conduct further cross-sectional analyses and obtained some significant results to support our new perspective. We finished a working paper and then presented it at JIAR Conference of AAA on 23 June 2021. Based on the feedback we received, we then conducted further analyses and finished a revised manuscript. The manuscript is now under review at the Journal of Accounting and Economics. In addition to the difficulty involved in coming up with a new perspective, the progress of the research has been adversely affected by the social unrest in Hong Kong and the pandemic. Our full-time RA decided to return to China after the outbreak of the social unrest. As we could not hire another RA in Hong Kong who are familiar with the data sources in China (especially the collection of data relating to the high-speed railways and media coverage) and potential RAs in China were reluctant to move to Hong Kong after the outbreak of the pandemic, we had to rely on virtual monitoring of RAs who had stationed in China to finish our project.

13501117.label: Major findings and research outcome
13501117.value: In the first the paper examining intra-industry information transfer in China, we find that investors in China transfer information between peer firms, with a stronger transfer when earnings forecasts are more accurate and credible, and when the investors of non-announcing firms are more sophisticated. We also find that the non–market-based resource allocation and entry restrictions in China discourage information transfer between firms. Overall, our results suggest that information transfer in China is constrained by institutional barriers. In the paper examining the effects of private information, we find that non-announcing firms’ investors react more strongly to announcing firms’ earnings forecasts if the firms are located far from the announcers, which suggests that investors’ private information on close firm pairs facilitates information transfer to close peer firms before the announcements and thus reduces the announcement-induced information transfer to close non-announcing firms. Further analyses show that the announcement-induced information transfer to distant non-announcing firms is weaker when the financial reporting quality of announcing firms is lower, when there is more media coverage, more analyst coverage and greater institutional ownership for the announcing firms. We also find that transportation improvement increases investors’ private information and reduces information transfer in the post-improvement period,

13501117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
13501117.value: This project has two major outputs. The first manuscript examines intra-industry information transfer in China, which is the first study to examine intra-industry transfer in the context of an emerging market. The results show that the intra-industry transfer in China has been shaped by the emerging markets' salient institutional environment, Thus, prior evidence obtained from mature markets cannot be directly generalized to emerging markets. This study highlights the role of institutional environment in influencing intra-industry information transfer - an insight which has not yet recognized by the existing literacture. The second manuscript examines how investors' private information on firms influence intra-industry transfer. The results suggest that investors can transfer information via private information channel, which weakens the information transfer through corporate announcements. As previous studies in the past four decades have focused on the information transfer as induced by corporate announcements, this study makes an important contribution to the literature. In addition to the newly documented private information channel, our study also calls for future research to investigate other possible information sources that may also trigger information transfer such as media coverage, analysts coverage, company visits, social interaction etc..

13501617.value: 消费者经常购买和拥有他们并不充分使用的产品。随着移动通信技术的广泛应用，消费者能够轻易地分享其闲置的产品，协同消费已经成为近年来的一个主要趋势。许多网站、在线社区和社交媒体平台帮助消费者在当地社区（有时甚至在各州或国家之间）分享各种产品和服务，例如：自行车（Spinlister），船只（Boatbound，GetMyBoat），汽车（RelayRides，Getaround），工作或停车位（Citizen Space，JustPark），乘车（Lyft，Uber，Zimride），短期租赁（Airbnb，Tujia），花园（Shared Earth，Landshare），服装，便携式工具/电器，电子产品和家居用品（FriendsWithThings，Neighborgoods）。事实证明，一些企业正在积极应对这一新趋势。例如，通用汽车公司与RelayRides合作，使车主更方便地出租其使用不足的支持OnStar的通用汽车，以通过授权租用者从智能手机远程解锁的功能来降低相应的成本（General Motors 2012）。宝马最近进入了美国汽车共享市场，并通过新推出的ReachNow汽车共享服务直接向消费者共享/租赁一定数量的汽车（Loizos 2016）。这些趋势自然产生了几个问题：企业应该何时进入产品共享市场？如果进入，企业应该如何在其主要市场和共享市场之间分配有限的产品？企业应如何最佳地调整销售价格？企业应该激励消费者进行产品分享吗？企业决策（是否进入共享市场，定价和产品分配）和企业利润如何受到消费者行为和运营因素的影响？ 为了解决这些研究问题，我们将采用以下分析框架。产品数量有限的公司需要在主要市场和共享市场之间分配产品，并确定其在主要市场的销售价格。然后，消费者决定是否从主要市场购买产品。消费者对产品的使用价值可能会在多个时期内变化。因此，在每个使用期，已经从主要市场购买产品的产品所有者决定自行使用产品还是在共享市场上将其出售；而没有购买产品的消费者决定是否从共享市场租用产品。需要注意的是，如果公司进入产品共享市场，消费者可以从公司或产品所有者租用产品。我们将通过分析上述多期多玩家博弈模型和对各种参数进行灵敏度分析来回答上面提出的研究问题。 这项研究将有助于企业实践者加深对如何参与产品共享市场的认识，并将影响企业的经营决策和盈利能力。这项研究还将为最近新出现的合作消费文献作出贡献，毕竟大多数现有研究集中在从概念上描绘共享这种现象而不是进行理论分析。据我们所知，这项课题是最早分析企业如何积极参与产品共享市场的一项研究。

13501617.label: Realisation of objectives
13501617.value: Objective 1: We characterize whether a firm should enter the product-sharing market, and how this decision depends on factors such as the efficiency of consumer-to-consumer and production cost. We analytically show that when consumer-to-consumer product sharing is highly efficient and the production cost is not very high, the firm will not enter the product-sharing market to provide the renting service; When consumer-to-consumer product sharing is medially efficient and the production cost is in a medium range, the firm will provide some units of products for renting, in which case the firm’s provided product renting and consumer-to-consumer product sharing will coexist in the product-sharing market; When consumer-to-consumer product sharing is lowly efficient or the production cost is very high, the firm will launch enough units of products for renting to rule out consumer-to-consumer product sharing (in expectation). Objective 2: We find that, with C2C product sharing in the market, the manufacturer’s provision of B2C rental services may not alter its optimal pricing in the retail market. This finding suggests that, to maximize the total profit from both the retail market and the rental market, it is more efficient for the manufacturer to adjust its quantity offered for rental rather than its retail price in the retail market. Meanwhile, in equilibrium, the manufacturer’s B2C rental service will lead to a lower market-clearing price in the sharing market. Objective 3: Depending on the C2C transaction efficiency and the total product usage period, the manufacturer’s offering of B2C rental services in the market may increase or decrease the equilibrium total number of units of the product in the market. On the one hand, the manufacturer’s rental service will cannibalize its retail sales, leading to fewer consumers buying the product; on the other hand, the manufacturer will offer some units of products for rental in the sharing market. That is, there is a tradeoff between the manufacturer’s retail sales and its direct offering of rental services in the market. Objective 4: When the C2C transaction is efficient and the manufacturer’s marginal cost of production is not very high, the manufacturer’s entry in the sharing market will reduce the manufacturer’s profit, the consumer surplus and the social welfare; otherwise, the manufacturer’s entry in the sharing market will increase the manufacturer’s profit, the consumer surplus and the social welfare.

13501617.label: Major findings and research outcome
13501617.value: We find that when the C2C transaction is efficient and the manufacturer’s marginal cost of production is not very high, the manufacturer will find it not optimal to offer its own rental services to consumers. In contrast, when the C2C transaction is not efficient or the manufacturer’s marginal cost of production is high, the manufacturer should offer enough units of the products for rental to squeeze out C2C sharing (in expectation). When the C2C transaction efficiency and the manufacturer’s marginal cost are both in the middle ranges, the manufacturer’s rental services and the C2C sharing will coexist, in which case the manufacturer’s entry in the product-sharing market may reduce the total number of units of the product in the whole market but increase the consumer surplus and the social welfare. This reduced number of products due to the manufacturer’s B2C rental service also suggests less environmental impact from production. Furthermore, we find that, to maximize the total profit from both the retail market and the sharing market, it may be more efficient for the manufacturer to adjust its quantity offered for rental rather than its retail price in the retail market, i.e., it may be best for the manufacturer to keep the same optimal retail price that it would choose in the absence of the sharing market, but use how much direct rental services to offer to respond to the C2C product sharing.

13501617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
13501617.value: First, we have assumed that the manufacturer’s involvement in the sharing market is through committing some fixed number of products to its rental service and let the market dictates the sharing prices. While this seems a reasonable approximation to some real-world markets, it may still be interesting to examine what happens if the manufacturer can directly set its rental prices with its rental units, rather than letting the sharing market clears. Second, our model has implicitly assumed an efficient sharing market that can perfectly match the supply and demand in the sharing market at a market-clearing price, where matched sharing transactions will occur with certainty. In reality, markets can have inefficiencies and uncertainties. For example, there can be some positive probability that not all of the manufacturer’s rental transactions will take place at the expected market-clearing price, for random reasons such as unexpected cancellation or unavailability due to severe weather or other factors. Third, this study has focused on a scenario where manufacturers enter the sharing market by providing their own rental services to try to reap the benefit of technology or platform-enabled sharing by consumers. In practice, manufacturers may have other means to participate in the sharing economy.

13501617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
13501617.value: Consumer-to-consumer (C2C) sharing has become an important part for the so-called “sharing economy.” The impact of C2C sharing on traditional firms can be very significant. Peer-to-peer product sharing platforms have also become very popular. Such sharing will enhance the consumers’ value of buying the products since they can generate some rental income during the time they do not use the products. Sharing can become a viable alternative for many consumers who have low or infrequent usage needs. Manufacturers of the products may lose some potential sales because of the C2C product sharing market. Some firms may be under pressure to cope with the cannibalization by the sharing market; some have proactively considered different options to influence or directly participate in the sharing market. Manufacturers have entered the sharing market by providing rental services to consumers. Note that these new rental/sharing services are very different from the traditional leasing options offered in the past. The manufacturers’ new sharing programs are similar to the C2C sharing, where the rental is very short-term and temporary compared with leasing. Our results would shed light on manufacturers' entry decision to the product-sharing market.

13600617.label: Project Objectives
13600617.value: Ample research has demonstrated that placebo analgesics can increase pain relief. Prior placebo studies have primarily focused on pain relief that occurs following the use of placebo analgesics. This project tests a novel hypothesis that merely possessing a placebo analgesic can benefit pain relief. To systematically demonstrate how merely possessing a placebo analgesic could contribute to pain reduction. To evaluate the application of the mere possession effect in placebo analgesia. To uncover the underlying mechanisms driving the effect.

13600617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13600617.value: 作為一種生存機制，人類神經系統使我們能夠經歷急性的短期身體疼痛，例如輕傷（如刮傷）或小手術（如拔除智慧齒）。鎮痛安慰劑的研究發現，患者在使用鎮痛安慰劑（假止痛藥）後彙報疼痛感減少。 以前的安慰劑研究主要集中研究人類在使用鎮痛安慰劑後的反應。然而，對於人在僅僅擁有（但未使用）鎮痛安慰劑時的反應則知之甚少。我們認為，人只要僅僅擁有鎮痛安慰劑（但仍未使用）已可減輕疼痛。我們進行了一個試驗來測試這個新穎的假設。我們要求參加者進行一項涉及實驗性疼痛的冷壓試驗。我們發現，相比並沒有擁有鎮痛安慰劑的參加者，那些僅僅擁有（但未使用）鎮痛安慰劑的參加者彙報較低的疼痛程度。這一發現令人鼓舞，並初步支持了"擁有效應"假設。 這個研究項目借鑒了社會心理學去了解人類的鎮痛體驗。我們提出三個問題。首先，只僅僅擁有鎮痛安慰劑能減輕身體疼痛嗎？第二，僅僅擁有鎮痛安慰劑實際意義是什麼？有多少過去記錄的安慰劑效應實際上是出自這種未確認的”擁有效應”呢？第三，是什麼機制驅動這”擁有效應”的？我們將進行兩項研究來回答這些問題。我們推測，只僅僅擁有鎮痛安慰劑足以引起由認知介導的積極期望（例如提高了自我效能以應對疼痛），導致疼痛感減輕。 這個研究項目建基在主研究員在社會心理學上的研究經驗，以及由兩位著名美國學者組成的研究小組：一名健康心理學家，具有應用社會心理學原理去理解安慰劑結果的專業知識;一名神經科學家，具有鎮痛和安慰劑機制專業知識。研究團隊擁有使用冷壓實驗的經驗，並曾在社會心理學，科學和臨床雜誌上發表文章。這個研究項目的成果對衛生專業人員和患者俱有實際意義。

13600617.label: Realisation of objectives
13600617.value: Our research team has achieved 100% of the research objectives. Below, we state the scope of investigation undertaken, and how the project objectives (objectives 1-4) are achieved. We had conducted three set of studies. In Study 1, we conducted two empirical experiments (Study 1a and Study 1b) and successfully demonstrated that merely possessing a placebo analgesic enhances placebo analgesia (achieved objectives 1-3) and we also examined the underlying mechanisms of this observed effect (achieved objective 4). To elaborate, we investigated the effect of merely possessing a placebo analgesic on pain outcomes in Study 1a and Study 1b. In Study 1a, we randomly assigned participants to either use a placebo analgesic, merely possess a placebo analgesic, possess a control object, and no possession. We found that healthy participants who merely possessed a placebo analgesic showed a higher pain threshold, longer pain tolerance, and lower pain intensity in a CPT compared to participants in the control conditions (i.e., those who did more possess any placebo analgesic, and those who possessed a pain-irrelevant control object). The most interesting finding is that these participants who merely possessed a placebo analgesic performed equally well as those who used the placebo analgesic. This suggests that mere possession of the placebo analgesic is useful to reduce pain and its analgesic effect is similar to actually applying the placebo analgesic (achieved objectives 1-3). While in Study 1a, participants who merely possessed the placebo analgesic were encouraged to anticipate the benefits of the possessed analgesic, in a follow up study (Study 1b), we did not allow participants to engage in such anticipation process. This is to investigate if the anticipation process is an underlying mechanism of the mere possession effect on placebo analgesia. We found that when participants were not allowed to anticipate the benefit of the placebo analgesic, those who merely possessed the placebo analgesic did not perform as well as those who merely possessed and used the placebo analgesic. This implies that the anticipation process or expectancy upon mere possession of a placebo analgesic is the underlying mechanism triggering the placebo analgesia (achieved objective 4). In Study 2, we conducted an empirical experiment and again successfully demonstrated that merely possessing a placebo analgesic enhances placebo analgesia (achieved objectives 1-3) and we also examined if prior pain experience affects the observed effect (achieved objective 4). To elaborate, we tested how the presence (vs. absence) of prior pain exposure would hinder participants’ engagement in the expectancy process upon mere possession of a placebo analgesic. We randomly assigned healthy participants to either the prior pain condition or no prior pain condition. Participants in both conditions were further randomized to possess either a placebo analgesic or a pain-irrelevant control object. We found that when participants did not have any experience of prior pain, those who merely possessed a placebo analgesic reported having a higher pain threshold and longer pain tolerance than participants who merely possessed a pain-irrelevant control object. And such mere possession effect was not found when participants were exposed to prior pain. In short, we found that merely possessing a placebo analgesic could reduce pain experiences (achieved objectives 1-3) under the condition when participants did not have relevant prior pain experience (achieved objective 4). In Study 3, we conducted an empirical experiment and successfully replicated the finding that merely possessing a placebo analgesic enhances placebo analgesia using a new experimental stimulus object (achieved objectives 1 to 3). We used a placebo oil instead of a placebo cream in our experiment. In addition, we further explored the nature of mere possession. We randomly assigned participants to either physically possess a tangle placebo analgesic vs. psychologically possess the placebo analgesic via a voucher vs. no possession. We found that placebo analgesia was achieved only when participants physically possessed a tangible placebo analgesic. The performance of participants did not differ regardless of whether they psychologically possessed a voucher for the placebo analgesic or without any possession. This shows that the nature of possession is an important factor determining the possession-based placebo analgesic effect (achieved objective 4). In short, we had conducted three bunches of empirically experiments and the four objectives are successfully achieved.

13600617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
13600617.value: Our research project presents novel findings and offers a novel perspective on the understanding of the placebo effect. Our findings have practical implications on potential pain intervention for clinicians and paradigm design for researchers of placebo study. The current research findings also inspire further research development. For example, would mere possession of placebo analgesic with side effect also induce a nocebo effect? What are the other factors (e.g., mediator, moderator) that affect the mere possession effect on placebo analgesia? This will be the future direction of this research line. Currently, a new GRF proposal is submitted aiming to investigate the possible mediator and moderator of this possession-based placebo analgesic effect. At the same time, pilot studies will be conducted to examine the possibility of the possession-based nocebo effect.

13600617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
13600617.value: The project presents an innovative finding that we do not need to actually use a placebo analgesic to achieve pain reduction, rather, under some circumstances, we could attain pain reduction by merely possessing a placebo analgesic. Our project has important theoretical as well as practical clinical significance. To elaborate, our project discovers that pain could be reduced via mere possession of a placebo analgesic, thus providing a possible alternative solution to alleviate physical pain. The project could inform health professionals and pain researchers about the possibility of setting up a possession intervention procedure, so as to enhance positive pain outcomes and pain management. For instance, clinicians and dentists could consider introducing a possession procedure prior to therapeutic treatment to reduce patients’ negative pain perception. Unlike traditional placebo procedure where the patients will actually consume the placebo, the possession procedure does not involve any actual consumption, the same placebo or resources could be re-used among different patients. This novel pain management procedure is cheap and cost-saving. Findings of the project could also be applied to other domains such as stress, fatigue, smoking and drinking.

13600717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13600717.value: Few authors have written more compellingly about political affairs than the British critic Rebecca West (1892-1983), yet today her political legacy is in the doldrums. Such deflation contrasts with the lively reception of West’s novels, literary criticism and travel writing. West's political writing extends in time from early twentieth century British feminism to the government of Margaret Thatcher. An inveterate traveller. she was also a prolific commentator on the culture and politics of the Balkans, Germany, the Soviet Union, the United States, South Africa and Mexico. This research aims to provide a comprehensive account of Rebecca West’s liberalism and thereby engage a fundamental dimension of her thought. It does so by investigating a series of arguments in which she explicitly assumed the persona of a liberal and, beyond that, by suggesting that we approach Rebecca West as a distinctive type of political liberal writer (as distinct from a political philosopher or political theorist). West’s liberalism grew out of a series of collisions with individuals, incidents and ideas that she believed menaced human liberty, responsibility and free expression. The research will identify these areas, map their common coordinates, and explore their continuing pertinence to current debates on such topics as spying and privacy, authority, political allegiance, ideology, the public and private, intellectuals and nationalism. This research builds on the PI’s previous work on canon formation, Hannah Arendt (a contrastive case), and the unmasking posture of much political criticism. Its outputs will be articles, a book, and pedagogic materials that encourage students of the cultural and political sciences to treat West as a major political thinker who speaks cogently to our era. 13600717.label: Realisation of objectives
13600717.value: I am grateful to the RGC for supporting financially this project on Rebecca West (RW) ARCHIVE VISITS A project of this kind, as my original application made clear, requires access to archives. Covid-19 severely disrupted my archival work. Before Covid materialized I made three archive visits, one to New York Public Library (for the Arthur Schlesinger papers which contain correspondence with RW, and some scathing commentary on her by some of AS’s interlocutors), another to the University of Tulsa (which is by far the largest of the RW archives) and a third to the University of Texas, Austin (for the A.D. Peters’ papers; Peters was RW’s literary agent). On the other hand, the visit to the University of British Columbia to work through the Time and Tide archive had to be aborted (library shut) and a return visit to Tulsa was prevented (library shut). I say “return visit” because the Tulsa archive is so rich that, in the time available to me, I was only able to work through about sixty per cent of the relevant materials. Return visits to archives, I should add, are common; I know that RW’s most important biographer, Carl Rollyson, returned twice (so three visits in all to Tulsa). All the same, the visits that did occur were useful. For instance, the New York Public Library visit formed the core of the materials I used for the TLS piece, and the article I sent to Thesis Eleven (decision pending) drew heavily on the Tulsa materials. TALKS I also gave two talks on RW that drew on the research: one at the University of Buckingham, the other at Wellesley College. Both were well received. I attach the posters in Section C. PROJECT TRUNCATED About half way through the project, once the impact of Covid-19 became clear, I realized that I would not be able to cover the span of RW’s ideas that I had originally intended to address. I therefore shaved down the project into one focused on her anti-Communism, the core of her political liberalism. Other topics were put into deep freeze: for instance, a study of her treatment of the Dreyfus case and the importance it assumed in England before and just after the First World War. PUBLICATIONS I describe my publishing strategy in Research Outcomes (below) and show how I overcame a general publication problem that arose out of the research. In this section, I would like to show how I overcame a specific publishing problem. Originally, I had sent an expanded version of my Wellesley College speech – “The Intelligent Liberalism of Rebecca West” - to Society, a journal that has published several of my articles and whose editor is a professor of sociology at Wellesley. What could go wrong? The article was accepted and queued. But then a new editor arrived on the scene. When my article did not appear, I wrote to him to ask of its status. He replied that he was not happy with the section on “Dervish Trials” which mentions the Brett Kavanaugh hearings; he wanted this piece taken out. I refused and withdrew the article. I sent it to the New English Review instead, a very conservative internet journal, and they accepted it within a couple of weeks. I would say that my experience of researching about and writing on RW is that while she considered herself to be “on the Left,” the new diversity-equity-inclusion Left does not like her. She is too free-spirited, too iconoclastic for this identity-politics Left. I actually mention this in the Wellesley speech. We’ll see how Thesis Eleven finds the piece I sent to them. In sum: I could not do everything I had first envisaged, but I believe that the RGC’s money has been well-spent; part of the sum has also been returned because of my inability to travel during Covid-19. With no teaching relief, but with some research assistance, I was able to make three archive visits pre-Covid, give two international talks, and publish five articles on RW drawn from the GRF research, and have another article (Thesis Eleven) that awaits a publication decision. All of the published articles were well received; meaning, that I received several appreciative emails from readers. The National Review article on RW’s analysis of Whittaker Chambers garnered a lot of attention from readers; my favourite email came from David Chambers, Whittaker Chambers’ grandson; he said that his father – Whittaker Chambers’s son – had told him that my National Review article on West and Chambers was outstanding. ---
