13603317.label: Project Objectives
13603317.value: To compare Hong Kong and UK experiences of the interface between Shakespeare performances live in theatres and Shakespeare performances ‘live’ in cinemas with attention to concepts such as mediativity, intermediality, reception theory and Shakespearean iconicity. To investigate empirically the nature and responses of Hong Kong and UK audiences to live transmission and captured-live performances of staged Shakespeare by professional theatre companies, with attention to socio-economic and gender-related factors. To theorise and conceptualise the aesthetics of the intermedial stage-to-screen transfer of Shakespeare plays, and explore the concepts and pragmatics of liveness (livestreaming) and mediatisation (captured live/ ‘pretend’ live). To strengthen existing research on theatre-in-cinema with specific reference to the Shakespeare creative industry worldwide, and to investigate issues surrounding the cultural relativism of celebrity status and name recognition in the contexts of Shakespeare live on stage and ‘live’ in cinema. 13603317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13603317.value: This proposed project will investigate a relatively new and under-researched topic: namely the interface between live stage performances of Shakespeare’s stage plays and simulcast and captured live (digitally broadcast) transmissions in cinemas. Theatre-film hybridity created by the remediation of performances of plays, operas and ballets on the cinema screen has captured the imagination of audiences worldwide, not least in Hong Kong with its historically Anglophone cultural connections. Since its inception in the first decade of the millennium this commercial practice - dubbed 'event cinema’, or ‘alternative content cinema’ - has flourished in Asia's self-styled 'World City'. Outside the US and the UK such putatively 'live' performances tend to be recorded and sometimes edited for the global market; however, in Hong Kong, as in other cities across the world, screenings of NT Live, RSC Live and Globe on Screen performances nevertheless appear to retain a 'virtual liveness’, raising fascinating ontological and phenomenological questions about the nature of 'liveness' and interpretations of ‘attendance’ and ‘presence’. A unique and central feature of the proposed study is its response to pertinent questions raised in Martin Barker’s pioneering work of cultural media criticism, Live to Your Local Cinema - The Remarkable Rise of Livecasting (2013). Barker’s study explores early US and UK. experiences in this burgeoning cultural-technological field. Adopting a wider, cross-cultural comparative/contrastive approach, the proposed project will investigate the aesthetics of and audience response to livecast Shakespeares in both UK and Hong Kong contexts as a parallel, comparative/contrastive study. This will be facilitated by linked research studies carried out in parallel and collaboratively by the Hong Kong-based Principal Investigator and the UK-based Co-Investigator. Specifically, we will conduct an empirical investigation into various aspects of the practice, including aesthetic/artistic criteria for audiences, knowledge of Shakespeare texts available to a second- or other-language public, cultural perceptions and participation and performer/author celebrity factors. In the Hong Kong-based part of the study we will explore questions concerning Chinese language subtitling, which is mandated under the city's 'trilingual, bi-literate' language policy. The study seeks to determine how screened Shakespearean theatre--in-cinema is being delivered, accessed and evaluated, and to assess these processes culturally and aesthetically. The outcomes of the study will comprise an independent critical report for the benefit of the various stakeholders and substantial journal articles related to the findings. 摘要 這項研究將探索一個相對較新的和未被研究的研究領域：即莎士比亞舞台劇的現場表演與聯播以及在電影院中捕獲的實時（數字廣播）傳輸之間的相互聯系。用電影屏幕來彌補戲劇、歌劇和芭蕾舞表演形式的不足，實現了電影和戲劇的混合，吸引了全球觀眾的想像力。這在香港這樣一個在歷史上有著英語文化關聯的地方表現得尤為明顯。雖然在美國和英國以外，這樣的“現場”表演往往被記錄下來，並有時候針對全球市場進行剪輯，但在香港，還有世界各地的其他城市，NT Live、RSC Live和Globe on Screen表演卻似乎保留了它們的“虛擬現場感”。這引起了一個迷人的本體論和現象學問題，即關於“現場感”的質量和對“出席”或“在場”的闡釋。本研究的香港部分將探索中文字幕的問題，這是由該城市的三語，雙文字語言政策規定的。這項研究旨在探求莎士比亞劇院在電影中是如何被傳播，訪問和評估的，並在文化和美學上進行衡量。其結果將包含一份獨立的批評報告，以便利益相關者和相關的重要期刊文獻從中得到啟發。

13603317.label: Realisation of objectives
13603317.value: 1. To compare Hong Kong and UK experiences of the interface between Shakespeare performances live in theatres and Shakespeare performances ‘live’ in cinemas with attention to concepts such as mediativity, intermediality, reception theory and Shakespearean iconicity. - This objective was addressed in Outputs 1, 3 and 4 which compared home reception in the U.K. for live-streamed productions and remoter access viewing in Hong Kong (my contribution) and other contexts (e.g. Japan, Italy, Brazil). It was also addressed in Output 2 (article under review) which looked in much greater detail at the Hong Kong context and the impact and significance of NTLive, RSC Live, etc. 2. To investigate empirically the nature and responses of Hong Kong and UK audiences to live transmission and captured-live performances of staged Shakespeare by professional theatre companies, with attention to socio-economic and gender-related factors. - This objective was achieved in Outputs 1, 2, 3 and 4 and to an extent in the-end-of-project report (Output 6) 3. To theorise and conceptualise the aesthetics of the intermedial stage-to-screen transfer of Shakespeare plays, and explore the concepts and pragmatics of liveness (livestreaming) and mediatisation (captured live/ ‘pretend’ live). - This objective was addressed in Outputs 1-3 and will continue to be explored and further developed in Output 5 4. To strengthen existing research on theatre-in-cinema with specific reference to the Shakespeare creative industry worldwide, and to investigate issues surrounding the cultural relativism of celebrity status and name recognition in the contexts of Shakespeare live on stage and ‘live’ in cinema. - This objective was addressed in Outputs 1 and 3 and will be further explored in the in-progress Output 5 5. To compare the findings of the above research in a process of critical, cross-cultural analysis and commentary, and to liaise with the various stakeholders in both Hong Kong and the UK to determine how best to make the findings relevant and available for market-survey and market-development purposes. - This objective represents the biggest challenge for the research project since Outputs 5 & 6 are ongoing, and it is extremely difficult to find a liaison person in the Hong Kong cinema industry in the least interested in engaging with researchers. This difficulty represents the most frustrating part of the scheme. Outreach to audiences are researchers in the U.K. is variable but much more common, while in Hong Kong it is virtually non-existent. Distributors and cinemas do not appear in the least interested in the nature and potential of their theatre-content event cinema, Shakespeare or otherwise. I had not anticipated this lack of interest or engagement when I proposed the study as a GRF and discussed it with potential collaborators. On reflection, this original goal may have been, at least to an extent, naive in the Hong Kong context, where email and phone enquiries to distributors and other parties involved in these cinema broadcasts met with either silence or apathy for the most part. 6. To analyse and document the theoretical and practical insights and implications provided by the work of Shakespearean directors and actors in the field, and to compare the findings with perceptions in Hong Kong through a global/local lens. - This objective remains a work in progress with Outputs 5 & 6 set to address the specific issues raised. 7. To produce a report on live-screened Shakespeare for publication/dissemination via relevant channels in both Hong Kong and the UK, to share the findings on a website, and to write two substantial journal articles and share the insights and findings obtained from the study at academic conferences and symposia. - Two earlier Shakespeare/ English Studies conferences in Belfast in early 2018 and in Cordoba in late 2018 proved good opportunities for trying out earlier findings and putting together drafts of work that came to fruition that year, or later in the case of the paper I have recently submitted to the journal 'Shakespeare'. The inaugural Shakespeare Drama Festival in Hong Kong in late 2020 run by director Tang Shu Wing with an associated conference (funding approved) will provide the perfect platform for launching the project report and disseminating it to multiple parties, including key stakeholders. It is hoped to do some 'live-capture' some of the productions of the cultural exchange and discuss both stage and screen manifestations. My panel at the Asia Shakespeare Association Conference, also toward the end of 2020, will provide further opportunity for academic exchange in the field and synergy in terms of of intercultural and intermedial work on Shakespeare on stage and on screen and on both simultaneously. My collaborative work with the Co-Investigator is evident in Outputs 1 and 3, while my own Hong Kong-specific initiative is represented by Output 2. Overview: Some of the initial project targets proved more achievable in terms of the outcomes than others, which are still in progress, e.g. objectives 5, 6 & 7, in particular. The effects of COVID-19 and other issues in Hong Kong added to the usual challenges of difficulties. Nevertheless, the scholarly exchange involved in the book project begun in 2017 around the same time that the GRF project was approved, and completed promptly in summer 2018 was extremely valuable, and quite cutting-edge in a rapidly changing research environment. The paper under review (Output 2) on presentist Shakespeare in the current Hong Kong situation is unique as a reception study, and the collaborative paper on Shakespeare and other event cinema from the perspective of mediation, distribution, commodification and new technology will be a significant deliverable from the project. It should be borne in mind that this was a fairly modest and small-scale project, even if it was originally designed along very ambitious lines. The scope of the project has increased in some areas, and admittedly been constrained in others. Nevertheless, I believe it offers great insights and a pioneering foundation for further critical investigation. Ideally, the findings included in the report ought to be of interest and benefit to the cultural industries involved in theatre broadcast and event cinema generally in both Hong Kong & the U.K.. At the same time, we recognise that consciousness-building and dissemination of critical ideas is a gradual process. Given the relatively short duration and modest size of the project, it has produced useful outcomes, and has either fully realised, or is on target to realise, the goals stated in the proposed GRF project.

13603317.label: Major findings and research outcome
13603317.value: The major findings of the research project are incorporated in publications to date, specifically in the book chapters in Shakespeare and the Live Theatre Broadcast Experience dealing with Hong Kong (myself) and London’s South Bank (the co-investigator) which present and compare reception in the U.K and in overseas contexts. In addition, new articles by us both on Shakespeare’s Screen Traffic in Hong Kong, and a decade of digital theatre broadcast from London, respectively, are forthcoming. They look at specific productions and their reception, including the move to online viewing and consumption in response to the coronavirus pandemic. The just-concluded report (Objective 7), which ought to interest stakeholders, incorporates useful findings and observations, although as I explain, it is much harder than originally envisioned in the project proposal to gain access to meaningful data, since the various companies do not wish to disseminate any such data. The findings suggest this form of theatre performance for remote viewing has the potential to be the most common form of access to performance, given increasingly prohibitive costs and impracticalities of world touring by international theatre companies. However, a more consistent approach to presentation, as well as promotion and publicity, has been lacking. The high number of Shakespeare productions in cinemas prior to and immediately after the Shakespeare Quatercentenary in 2016 was a major promotional tie-in, and, in a number of viewed productions, there was evidence of felicitously topical parallels with Hong Kong affairs in line with contemporary ‘presentist’ interpretations. As I argued the illusion of ‘nowness’ inherent in Shakespeare’s themes and subject matter can be seen as complementing the ‘nowness’ of the ‘live’--or in Hong Kong, captured-live--theatre broadcast events. There is a potentially wider audience for theatre broadcast in the city, as well as online streamed productions, but better coordination of publicity, better liaison with interested parties on the part of theatre and cinema companies involved, and better audience development represent the next stage, if this promising period of growth in theatre broadcast is to be sustained. My Co-Investigator, Professor Aebischer’s research in this area is influential, while my own has been the first related project in the Hong Kong context, and is therefore significant for researchers on remote experience of live theatre. I am working on a major academic paper exploring theatre broadcast provision in HK both in cinemas and streamed on line in order to extend knowledge and understanding in this field.

13603317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
13603317.value: The new collaborative paper in preparation entitled ‘The Three Hours Traffic of our Screens: Theatre Moves on Line’,focuses on the interface between theatre broadcast in cinema and the so-called ‘home theatre’ phenomenon. The aim is to publish a cutting-edge journal article reflecting on the rapid changes in the theatre broadcast creative industry and the remediation of theatrical content at the present time. A key area of focus in the extension of the research will be on the mixed-mode options for online and offline consumption, as well as for greater audience interaction. Predictive modifications of existing technology and methods of remediation for remote-access viewers will also be considered (please see attached outline). Another planned direction for the research is offered by the panel I am co-organising for the Asian Shakespeare Association’s biennial conference in Seoul in early November 2020 on the topic ‘Intermediality in Shakespeare - a good opportunity to work on a publishing project with contributions from participants. Future engagement with Prof Aebischer and John Wyver, the RSC Live broadcast producer and observation of film procedures at Stratford-upon-Avon and London are also planned for as soon as the practice of live recording of Shakespeare productions resumes when theatres re-open.

13603317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
13603317.value: Shakespeare in the 21st century retains the aura of dramatist and poet 'for all time' (Ben Jonson) and of 'Big-Time Shakespeare' (Bristol, 1996). The principal value of the research project to Hong Kong theatre- and cinema-goers, students of Shakespeare's plays and the public familiar with his name, if not his works specifically, is that it highlights an opportunity for wider audience engagement with Shakespeare through cinema. My work and the work of my co-Investigator in the U.K. trace the development of Shakespeare theatre broadcast at both ends of this production and reception continuum. For the Hong Kong side of the project I have discussed in a systematic way how specific Shakespeare plays have been transmitted to Hong Kong screens in the past seven years and shown how they can be interpreted in a way that is locally resonant for remote audiences. Since some of these productions are given so-called 'encore' (repeat) screenings, particularly on line during the COVID-19 theatre closures, local audiences have a greater opportunity to familiarise themselves with Shakespeare's plays in a more accessible way. My closing report makes useful recommendations for further development and suggestions for improved publicity and outreach strategies to facilitate better appreciation of Shakespeare screenings.

13603517.label: Realisation of objectives
13603517.value: In the proposal, one daily-diary study and two experimental studies were proposed to address the project objectives. We have successfully completed one daily-diary study and one experimental study which reveal the effects of valence and variation of mood on critical thinking performance as assessed by the Halpern Critical Thinking Assessment (HCTA) - a standard assessment tool consisting of open-ended and forced-choice questions. The findings of these studies have been written up in a manuscript titled Effects of Mood on Critical Thinking (Lun, Yeung, & Ku, under review). The first version of the manuscript has been reviewed by the journal Contemporary Educational Psychology. Comments from that review have been incorporated in the revised manuscript which is under review for the journal Thinking Skills and Creativity. Although only two of the three proposed studies could be successfully completed, the results of the two studies are sufficient to address the two project objectives. Therefore, we conclude that the project objectives have been fully achieved despite the discrepancies between the original proposal and final output. Below we will highlight the reasons behind these discrepancies, and the steps we have taken to address the challenges. Unforeseen Interruptions to Research and Dissemination Plans In the midterm report submitted in June 2019, we reported the completion of the daily-diary study and the preparation for the experimental studies. To ensure successful implementation of the mood-induction procedure, we conducted a few pilot studies using different measures of mood and mood-induction stimuli (i.e., music pieces and booster procedures) since the beginning of 2019. In September 2019, we began the experimental study which is reported in the manuscript under review. As the social unrest in Hong Kong unfolded at the time, we experienced increasing difficulty in recruiting research participants who would voluntarily take part in the study at the university. We completed data-collection for the experimental study by the end of October 2019. Three presentations based on the two completed studies have been prepared and scheduled for international conferences in May and July 20201. However, all presentations have been postponed due to the COVID-19 pandemic. To continue the project within the constraints of the pandemic, we adapted the third experimental study into a web-based study, which we preregistered with the Open Science Framework (Lun & Yeung, 2020)2. To ensure consistency across studies, we focused on collecting data from young adults with higher education background. Because of these requirements of participants, online data-collection has been difficult even with the assistance of a research company. When the pandemic situation in Hong Kong eased up slightly in the last quarter of 2020, we conducted the last round of data-collection on university campus. At the end, we collected data from 244 participants in this web-based study. Analysis of the data showed that mood-induction through Internet is not effective in inducing the intended mood changes. One possible reason for this lack of effect could be that participants had not paid full attention as they underwent the procedure on their own without the guidance of an experimenter. Therefore, the data from this web-based study are not included in the manuscript under review. Differences between Research Hypotheses and Findings The original hypotheses in this project included: Hypothesis 1. Positive mood predicts higher levels of critical thinking; negative mood predicts lower levels of critical thinking. Hypothesis 2. The detrimental effect of negative mood on all dimensions of critical thinking will be stronger with assessment by open-ended questions than by forced-choice questions. Hypothesis 3. Ruminative thought style will exacerbate the detrimental effect of negative mood on critical thinking. Hypothesis 4. Approach of affect will strengthen, whereas avoidance of affect will weaken, the effects of positive and negative moods on critical thinking. Results of the two completed studies did not fully support these hypotheses. The results of the daily-diary study showed that daily variation in positive mood positively predicted the overall score in critical thinking assessment, and the effect was more salient in forced-choice questions. The results of the experimental study showed that participants who received negative mood induction performed better in the HCTA compared to their counterparts who received positive mood induction. Individual differences in terms of ruminative thought style, approach for affect and avoidance of affect did not moderate the effects of valence or variation of mood on critical thinking either. An important insight we gained from analyzing and interpreting these findings is that daily average and variation in mood experiences are useful indicators of individual differences in emotional experiences. The findings of the daily-diary study can therefore serve to address research objective 2, viz., to examine the individual differences in the effects of moods on critical thinking. As the HCTA was used in both studies, the overall findings serve to address research objective 1, viz., to examine the effects of moods on the application of critical thinking in everyday scenarios. Application of Findings and Future Research These findings are not consistent with our original hypotheses, but the results provide important grounds for further research on the topic and ideas for future design of critical thinking instruction. Details about the results and related interpretations may be found in Section 6 of this report and the uploaded draft of the manuscript. In conducting the main studies in the proposal, we developed ideas about relevant application of the concept of critical thinking. For example, we applied the idea of critical thinking to understand the impact of popular psychology materials on lay persons. Specifically, using the concept of critical thinking, we showed that presenting both supportive and counter evidence about the effectiveness of popular self-help materials would alleviate the negative effects of such materials on people’s stigma about individuals suffering from depression (Yeung & Lun, 2020)3. This analysis demonstrated the importance of critical thinking in our everyday lives, and the findings formed part of the output of this research project. Other variables included in the project are being analyzed for additional submissions to peer-reviewed journals, such as the relations of social beliefs and language ability to critical thinking performance. The ideas generated from these analyses can potentially be expanded for future research projects. Conclusion Despite the challenges brought by unforeseen circumstances during the project, we addressed the two project objectives with two successfully completed studies. We also tested the feasibility of using web-based mood-induction procedures, although the findings were not promising. While the original research hypotheses were not fully supported by the data, the findings have inspired reconceptualization of individual differences in emotion and ideas for future research. 13603517.label: Major findings and research outcome
13603517.value: In two studies, we showed the effects of valence and variation of mood on college students’ performance in a standard assessment of critical thinking, namely, the Halpern Critical Thinking Assessment (HCTA) which consists of open-ended and forced-choice questions. The first study involved daily sampling of 191 college students’ mood for a week prior to assessment of their critical thinking performance using the HCTA. Results showed that daily variation in positive mood positively predicted critical thinking performance, and the effect was more salient in forced-choice questions. The second study adopted mood induction procedures to elicit positive or negative mood among 115 college students. Participants who experienced negative mood induction performed better in the HCTA than their counterparts who experienced positive mood induction. These findings showed that valence and variation of mood could influence critical thinking. The findings have important theoretical and practical implications. Theoretically, we found that daily measures of mood can be used to indicate individual differences in emotional experiences which influence critical thinking performance. Daily variation in positive mood may be interpreted as indicating a person’s readiness to detect benign situations in everyday life, which can benefit critical thinking performance. Contrary to our original hypotheses, we found that negative mood induction would lead to better performance in critical thinking. We noted that the negative mood induced was anxiety, which suggested that anxiety may enhance people’s performance in critical thinking tests. This counterintuitive finding provided important extension from past research based on the “broaden-and-build” theory (Fredrickson & Losada, 2005) which focused only on the benefits of positive emotion on thinking. Practically, these effects of valence and variation of mood on critical thinking performance have implications to the design of more effective critical thinking instruction. The findings suggest that responsiveness to positive-mood related signals and experience of anxiety may be leveraged to enhance critical thinking. To achieve this end, critical thinking instruction may include elements of emotion-regulation training. In addition to appropriate use of higher-order thinking skills, individuals may be trained to also use their subjective mood experiences as an additional source of information to facilitate the critical thinking process.

13603517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
13603517.value: A few limitations of the research have been identified, and the following suggested areas of future research may be considered. For example, different measures of critical thinking and mood may be used to improve the generalizability of the findings in future research. These points have been detailed in the manuscript under review. Through making presentations on these findings in seminars or conferences, the PI of the project will seek other opportunities to test these ideas in future research. The submitted manuscript included only the results related to the original project objectives. Other variables which were not the primary research focus in the original proposal will also be analyzed to improve our knowledge on the prediction of better critical thinking performance. Examples include the relations of language abilities and social beliefs to critical thinking. Based on the results of these analyses, further research on these secondary variables will be proposed. Additional analyses of the data generated from the web-based, mood-induction experiment will be conducted to identify the causes behind the null effect of online mood-induction. These analyses may help to improve the use of web-based experimental studies in future research.

13603517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
13603517.value: This research project examined the relationship between emotional experiences and critical thinking performances among university students. In a study which involved measures of students’ everyday mood experiences, we found that a person who experienced more daily variation in positive mood tended to perform better in critical thinking. In another experimental study, we found that students who were experimentally led to feel negative mood performed better in a test of critical thinking than those who were led to feel positive mood. These findings showed that both positive mood and negative mood could benefit critical thinking through different mechanisms, and emotional experiences could be used as a source of information which enhanced critical thinking performance. As the world becomes more complex due to increased information flow, critical thinking is an essential skill for all learners to acquire. The link between mood and critical thinking shown in this research suggests that we need to attend to the influences of emotional experiences on people’s ability to think critically. Critical thinking instruction should include elements of emotion-regulation so that students would learn to incorporate their own emotional experiences when they use critical thinking to address everyday problems.

14100917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14100917.value: Glaucoma is a serious, complex and progressive eye disease that can lead to narrowing of visual field and even irreversible blindness due to damage of retinal ganglion cells and loss of retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL). About 2% of the world’s population aged over 50 years is affected by glaucoma. Early glaucoma is usually asymptomatic, although early visual field and RNFL losses can be detected clinically. When progressed to the late stage, glaucoma patients can be suffering from “tunnel vision” or even total blindness. Elevation of intraocular pressure (IOP) is a major and so far the only modifiable factor for glaucoma and its progression. Clinically IOP can be controlled by IOP-lowering medications, laser and surgery. Unfortunately, the progression of glaucoma is inevitable despite adequate treatments. Thus, the identification of risk factors that can predict the progression of glaucoma is essential for planning the treatment for individual patients. In this study, we aim to identify genetic factors to predict the progression of visual field and RNFL in primary-open angle glaucoma (POAG), a major subtype of glaucoma. By the time of writing this proposal, we have recruited over 500 POAG patients who have been followed-up in glaucoma clinics for at least 3 years. Detailed clinical information has been and will be obtained from each patient every 4 months for at least 5 years, including visual acuity, IOP, visual field, RNFL and optic disc parameters. We have also recruited over 1000 normal control subjects who have given complete ophthalmic examinations. In a recent systematic review of glaucoma genetics, we have worked out the full list of gene markers associated with POAG. In this study, we will genotype all these gene markers, totally 124 single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in 63 genes, in all our glaucoma patients and controls. We will perform association analysis to identify the SNPs that are associated with glaucoma susceptibility. We shall analyze glaucoma progression in visual field and RNFL of each patient over the ≥5-year follow-up period, and perform regression analyses to determine the SNPs that are correlated with the progression of visual field change and RNRL loss in patients, which is the primary and ultimate outcome. The completion of this study will lead us to a group of genetic biomarkers to predict the development and progression of glaucoma. This is an important step toward precision medicine for glaucoma. 青光眼是一系列嚴重的，複雜的，以及終身性、進展性眼睛疾病。由於視網膜神經節細胞受損和視網膜神經纖維層變薄，青光眼會導致視野收窄和不可逆視力喪失。在全球50歲以上人口中，約2%人士患有青光眼。雖然在臨床中能檢測到早期的視野和視網膜神經纖維層受損，但早期青光眼并無明顯症狀，因此往往未能及早診斷。而當進展到後期時，青光眼病人會呈现“管狀視力”甚至徹底失明。眼內壓是影響青光眼進展的主要及唯一可調節的因素。在臨床應用中，眼壓通常可通過降眼压药物、激光以及手術治療得以控制。但即使充分控制眼壓，青光眼的進展依然無法避免。因此，發現及確定能預測青光眼進展惡化的危險因素對制定青光眼個人化治療十分重要。 本研究的目的是發現及確定能預測原發性開角型青光眼的視野和視網膜神經纖維層變化的基因標誌物。原發性開角型青光眼是最常見的青光眼類型。截至到目前，我們已經招募了超過500名已在青光眼臨床跟蹤至少三年的原發性開角型青光眼病人。每名病人在至少五年內中每四個月的詳細臨床信息，包括視敏度、眼壓、視野、視網膜神經纖維層及各視盤參數已被詳細記錄。同時，我們已招募超過1000名正常對照個體并完成全面的眼科檢測。在近期一篇的青光眼遺傳學系統性回顧中，我們匯總了之前發現的所有與原發性開角型青光眼的基因標記。在此研究中，我們將在所有的青光眼病人和正常对照個體中測試63個基因中一共124個單核苷酸多態性分型，通過關聯性分析確定與青光眼易感率相關的單核苷酸多態性分型。我們還會調查每名病人在五年間的視野和視網膜神經纖維層變化，以及進行迴歸分析測定與視野改變和視網膜神經纖維層受損進程相關的單核苷酸多態性分型，這是此項研究的主要目標及意義。 通過完成本研究，我們將會得出一組能預測青光眼發病及進展的基因標記物。這是邁向青光眼精準治療的關鍵一步。

14100917.label: Realisation of objectives
14100917.value: In this project, the 3 objectives have been achieved as planned under the support of this GRF grant. In our series of studies on the molecular genetics of primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) and the major clinical parameters of POAG, i.e., visual field (VF) and VF progression, and retinal nerve fibre layer (RNFL) thickness and the longitudinal changes of RNFL thickness, we realized that our study hypotheses, objectives and methodologies were reasonable and valid. The study was completed under the collaboration of glaucoma specialists (Co-Is: Tham CC, Leung CK), glaucoma imaging specialist (Co-I: Cheung CY), statistician (Co-I: Yu MC) and molecular geneticists (Co-I: Chen LJ, and the PI: Pang CP). This study is an excellent example of the identification of genetic biomarkers for a major eye disease, glaucoma, and its progression. We investigated the genetic associations of POAG, including normal tension glaucoma and high tension glaucoma in local Han Chinese on gene variants that we and other groups have newly identified as putative glaucoma genes especially in East Asians. a number of genes and variants with significant associations. The optineurin gene, OPTN, was identified to be a causative gene for normal tension glaucoma but was confirmed by us to be a susceptibility gene for open angle glaucoma in the Chinese population. In this project, we have identified specific coding variants in OPTN that can serve as a genetic marker for early onset normal tension glaucoma. The evidences have been published: He JN, Lu S, Chen LJ, Tam POS, Zhang BN, Leung CKS, Pang CP, Tham CCY, Chu WK. Coding Region Mutation Screening in Optineurin in Chinese Normal-Tension Glaucoma Patients. Dis Markers. 2019;2019:5820537. Long term followup of patients carrying these OPTN variants are underway. The CAVI and CAV2 genes were discovered by us and collaborators in an international consortium in 2010 (Thorleifsson G, Walters GB, Hewitt AW,.., Pang CP, .., Stefansson K. Common variants near CAV1 and CAV2 are associated with primary open-angle glaucoma. Nat Genet. 2010 Oct;42:906-9). In this project, we delineate the differential roles of sequence variants in the CAV1-CAV2 locus among Chinese and Japanese patients with normal tension glaucoma (NTG). It is notable that NTG is more common and serious in Japanese patients compared with Chinese and Caucasians. We have identified contributions by specific CAV1 alleles: Lu SY, Rong SS, Wu Z, Huang C, Matsushita K, Ng TK, Leung CKS, Kawashima R, Usui S, Tam POS, Tsujikawa M, Young AL, Zhang M, Wiggs JL, Nishida K, Tham CC, Pang CP, Chen LJ. Association of the CAV1-CAV2 locus with normal-tension glaucoma in Chinese and Japanese. Clin Exp Ophthalmol. 2020;48:658-65. The SIX1-SIX6 Locus was identified in Caucasian patients with Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma that affect glaucoma development. In this project, we conducted detailed genotype phenotype analysis in two Chinese cohorts, one in Hong Kong and one in Sichuan, and a Japanese cohort in Osaka. We have identified putative SIX6 SNPs affecting glaucoma progression: Lu SY, He ZZ, Xu JX, Yang C, Chen LJ, Gong B. Association of Polymorphisms at the SIX1-SIX6 locus with Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma. Invest Ophthalmol Vis Sci. 2019;60:2914-24. Association of the SIX6 locus with primary open angle glaucoma in southern Chinese and Japanese. Exp Eye Res. 2019 Mar;180:129-36. Long term follow up of these patients in their respective regions are in progress. Our gene mapping for POAG by the candidate gene approach has identified the FOXC1 locus to confer susceptibility to glaucoma more in Chinese than in Japan. A manuscript is in preparation for submission for publication. Further collaboration with the Sichuan group on mechanisms of glaucoma progression and genetic markers have led to the identification of mutations in the RAMP2 gene that contributes to glaucoma in the CRLR-cAMP axis: Gong B, Zhang H, Huang L, Chen Y, Shi Y, Tam PO, Zhu X, Huang Y, Lei B, Sundaresan P, Li X, Jiang L, Yang J, Lin Y, Lu F, Chen L, Li Y, Leung CK, Guo X, Zhang S, Huang G, Wu Y, Zhou T, Shuai P, Tham CC, Weisschuh N, Krishnadas SR, Mardin C, Reis A, Yang J, Zhang L, Zhou Y, Wang Z, Qu C, Shaw PX, Pang CP, Sun X, Zhu W, Li DY, Pasutto F, Yang Z. Mutant RAMP2 causes primary open-angle glaucoma via the CRLR-cAMP axis. Genet Med. 2019;21:2345-54. Intensive studies on RAMP2 properties and the CRLR-cAMP axis in human clinical study and an animal model are in progress. Long term glaucoma progress can be part of an aging process in relation to neurodegeneration. We are examining the molecular basis of cellular aging and have found the leukocyte telomere length affecting the development of normal tension glaucoma in Chinese patients. A manuscript is in preparation for submission for publication. Accordingly, we have established a molecular platform based on our new genetic findings for the longitudinal analysis of the genetic factors associated with the progression of glaucoma and its endophenotypes, visual field and retinal nerve fiber layer thickness. However, we found that the gene variants that are associated POAG development were not associated with POAG progression. This is likely due to the following reasons. First, since the patients have been under treatment by glaucoma specialists, their glaucoma progression rates are low. Therefore, the progression over 5 years could be too small to provide sufficient statistical power to show significant association. We will keep following all our patients, and will re-analyze their progression rates in 3 years and re-analyze the association. Second, the gene variants associated with POAG may not be also associated with its progression. This phenomenon is also seen in myopia, where some gene variants associated with myopia are not associated with myopia progression, as indicated in our other studies. To tackle this issue, we have planned to conducted larger-scale genetic analysis, i.e., genome-wide association study (GWAS), to identify novel genes and loci for glaucoma progression. The GWAS, with both cross-sectional and longitudinal components, will lead to the identification of novel genes and loci for POAG. By completing this project, we have provided new data enriching the growing understanding of the genetic architecture of POAG. Results of this study will pave the way to our further larger-scale genomic analysis of POAG and its progression.

14100917.label: Major findings and research outcome
14100917.value: In this project, we aimed to identify genetic markers for primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) and its major clinical parameters, i.e., visual field (VF) and VF progression, and retinal nerve fibre layer (RNFL) thickness and the longitudinal changes of RNFL thickness. We have analyzed the genetic associations of multiple gene variants with different subtypes of POAG (cross-sectional study) and POAG progression (longitudinal study). In the cross-sectional study, we have identified a variant (rs4236601) in the CAV1-CAV2 locus that were associated with normal tension glaucoma (NTG) in Chinese and Japanese. This is a novel finding since the CAV1-CAV2 locus was initially identified in high-tension POAG. Also, in the sequence analysis of the OPTN gene, we confirmed the association of the OPTN T34T variant with NTG, suggesting that OPTN is a susceptibility gene for NTG in Chinese. Moreover, a variant with amino acid change (I407T) was identified in NTG but not in controls, suggesting it could be a causative mutation for NTT, although further studies are warranted. In contrast, in our study of the SIX6 locus, we confirmed the association between two previously-reported SNPs in SIX6 (rs33912345 and rs10483727) and high-tension POAG (HTG). Also, a SNP, rs12436579, not associated with POAG before, was found to be associated with POAG in Chinese. In collaboration with an international consortium on exome sequencing and replications, we identified in pathogenic variants in receptor activity-modifying protein 2 (RAMP2) within three genetically diverse populations (Han Chinese, German, and Indian). Six heterozygous RAMP2 pathogenic variants (Glu39Asp, Glu54Lys, Phe103Ser, Asn113Lysfs*10, Glu143Lys, and Ser171Arg) were identified among 16 of 4763 POAG patients, whereas no variants were detected in any exon of RAMP2 in 10,953 control individuals, indicating RAMP2 as a novel gene for POAG. In these studies, we have identified new genes and variants for different subtypes of POAG, i.e., NTG and HTG. We then performed further analysis of the association of multiple variants in these genes and other selected genes stated in the proposal with VF and RNFL thickness, and their longitudinal changes (i.e., progression) over 5 years. However, we found that there was no significant association between the variants with VF and RNFL thickness in both cross-sectional and longitudinal data. Therefore, the genes and variants that we identified are likely to be genetic markers for the development of POAG, but not its progression. Further studies are warranted to identify the gene markers for POAG progression.

14100917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14100917.value: The present study has identified new genetic information on gene variants susceptible to development of glaucoma and molecular basis of aging leading ro neurodegeneration in glaucoma. This is an important foundation for our further research on the genetics of POAG. Glaucoma patients carrying specific alleles are in longterm follow up for their clinical course and association with disease progression. Although we have identified a group of new gene markers for POAG, these variants altogether contributed to less than 5% of the heritability of POAG in our population. Therefore, there are still a large amount of genes and variants to be identified in our population. Also, the gene variants that were included in this study, which were selected using a candidate gene approach, were not associated with POAG progression. Therefore, further genomic approaches, including genome-wide association study (GWAS), whole-exome sequencing (WES) and whole-genome sequencing (WGS), will be adopted in different study samples, i.e., unrelated and familial, to identify novel gene markers for POAG and POAG progression in our population. We are now conducting WGS study in POAG proband-parents trios aiming to identification of de novo gene variants for POAG.

14100917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14100917.value: Primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) is a leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide. It is characterized by typical patterns of visual field (VF) defects and retinal nerve fibre layer (RNFL) loss. Elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) is a major risk factor for POAG, mainly for high-tension glaucoma (HTG). In contrast, normal tension glaucoma (NTG) refers to the subgroup of POAG patients whose IOP falls within the normal range. Once occurred, the damages in POAG, mainly manifested in VF and RNFL thickness, are subjected to progression even under good IOP control. Therefore, it is important to identify biomarkers for the development and progression of POAG, with a view of early detection and intervention for patients at higher risk. In this study, we evaluated the roles of a group of gene variants in the genetic susceptibility of POAG in Chinese and other populations. We identified variants in the CAV1-CAV2, SIX6, OPTN and RAMP2 genes to be associated with POAG (HTG and/or NTG), suggesting that individuals carrying the risk alleles of the variants have additional risk of POAG development. We found no association of these variants with POAG progression. Therefore, further studies are warranted to identify additional polygene markers for POAG and its progression.

14101117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14101117.value: 近視眼是在香港乃至亞洲範圍內的流行病。誠然相比較於非近視的眼，近視患眼具有發展為青光眼-導致不可逆轉的盲疾的首位病因-的高風險，在近視患眼中偵測以及追蹤青光眼性的視神經損傷是一道難題。視乳頭旁萎縮以及歪曲的視盤構造經常妨礙對於視神經網膜邊緣的評估，而低色素的眼底像經常使得視神經纖維層的可見度變得迷糊。在近視眼中識別青光眼的疾病進展的水平目前仍不準確。對於這群病人何時開始或進一步增效降低眼內壓的治療在很大程度上還不清楚。發現能夠在有近視眼的青光眼病人中對進展性視神經病有指示性的生物標記來指導眼內壓降低療法來防治變盲是仍未實現的需求。 我們已經展示了在SDOCT中測得的在青光眼病人中的視神經纖維層厚度變薄的速率可以用來預測視野進行性變差。我們假設在近視眼青光眼病人中，由TPA分析得到的視神經纖維層厚度圖的速率來計算得出的視神經纖維層變薄的峰值速率是可以提示降眼內壓治療的。我們提議進行一個為期三年的前瞻性多中心研究計劃以3個月左右的時間間隔來跟蹤304個近視眼青光眼患者用以記錄每一次的視神經纖維層影像學以及視野測量數據。在18個月的時候，快速的進展者（表現出視神經纖維層峰值變化率大於或等於每年5微米的眼）將會被隨機分配到進一步降低眼內壓的20%組或繼續治療組。慢速的進展者/無進展者（表現出視神經纖維層峰值變化率小于每年5微米的眼）將會被以同樣的方式隨機分組。所有的患者都將被以大約每3個月一次的時間間隔繼續追蹤剩下的18個月。 首要目標是去比較在快速進展組和慢/無進展組中接受或沒接受進一步眼內壓治療的所有眼中表現出視野進行性變差的眼的比例是否有所不同。我們預計相對於慢/無進展組，在快速進展組中給予進一步的降眼內壓治療能夠更有效的降低視野進行性變差的發生頻率。 此研究計劃將對青光眼的處理產生深遠的影響包括不僅僅是引進了一個能夠監控近視眼中的青光眼病的有效的策略而且也建立了一個對於用視神經纖維層變薄速率來指導眼內壓降低療法的新規範。在治療方面針對那些有功能惡化風險的病人，這個新的規範將會減輕青光眼致盲的負荷，並且能優化健康護理系統內部的資源合理的再分配給那些具有最高級別的需求者。

14101117.label: Realisation of objectives
14101117.value: I. How and to what extent the project objectives have been achieved A. Protocol Revision We submitted an amendment (approved by RGC on 7 December 2017) to include a new objective to determine whether latanoprost or brinzolamide/brimonidine fixed combination, which are topical intraocular pressure (IOP)-lowering medications with purported neuroprotective effects, can slow glaucoma progression independent of IOP reduction by comparing the IOP levels and the rates of retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) thinning between the two IOP-lowering medications – Objective (4). In addition, the title of the project has been revised to “Measurement of the Rates of Retinal Nerve Fiber Layer Thinning to Guide Management of Glaucoma Patients" because the study did not limit the recruitment to myopic eyes (over 80% of Chinese patients with glaucoma are myopic) to allow inclusion of eyes with a wider range of axial length for investigation of its association with glaucoma progression (approved by RGC on 24 July 2019). B. Project objectives achieved and key findings We have completed objectives (4), (3), and (2) and the findings have been included in a full manuscript (uploaded in Part C, Research Output 1) for submission to Ophthalmology. Objective (4) – We showed that eyes treated with brinzolamide/brimonidine had a considerably faster rate of RNFL thinning than those treated with latanoprost (Fig.4) despite the fact that the IOP levels measured at 2-month intervals over 2 years were similar between the two treatment arms (Fig.3), suggesting that latanoprost, not brinzolamide/brimonidine, better preserved the RNFL independent of IOP levels. Our data support the feasibility of detecting a treatment effect in short term neuroprotection trials; treatment differences in neuroprotection trials can be uncovered using a structural outcome (Fig.5) when VF outcomes failed to show a difference (Fig.S4). Objective (3) – Taking all data into consideration (i.e., 182 eyes of 102 patients), the only risk factor for progressive RNFL/GCIPL thinning was IOP (Table S5). Axial length, CCT, age, and baseline MD were not associated with progressive RNFL thinning (P≥0.070). Since the rates of change of VF MD were insignificant in the latanoprost group and the brinzolamide/brimonidine group using intention-to-treat analysis (Table S3) or per-protocol analysis (Table S4), risk factor analysis for VF progression was not performed. Objective (2) – Eyes with progressive RNFL thinning defined by GPA or TPA (i.e., progressors) had a faster rate of MD decline (-0.28 dB/year, 95% CI: -0.60 to 0.04) compared with those without progressive RNFL thinning (i.e., non-progressors) although it only reached borderline statistically significance (P=0.086). Objective (1) – We were not able to complete the objective because the numbers of eyes detected with progressive RNFL thinning by GPA or TPA over 24 months (Phase I) were not sufficient for the randomization to additional IOP-lowering treatment or continued treatment in Phase II (12 months) (elaborated below). II. Reasons for under-achievements The failure to achieve Objective (1) largely stems from the small number eyes that showed progressive RNFL/GCIPL thinning at the end of Phase I (24 months). Over 2 years of follow-up, only 14 eyes developed progressive RNFL/GCIPL thinning by GPA (Fig.S3A) – 12 in the brinzolamide/brimonidine group and 2 in the latanoprost group by intention-to-treat analysis; 9 in the brinzolamide/brimonidine group and 2 in the latanoprost group by per-protocol analysis (3 eyes with progressive RNFL/GCIPL thinning were excluded from the per per-protocol analysis because of development of allergic conjunctivitis and medication switch). Using TPA, 15 eyes developed progressive RNFL-GCIPL thinning (RNFL and GCIPL were analyzed as one single layer); 10 in the brinzolamide/brimonidine group and 5 in the latanoprost group by intention-to-treat analysis; 8 in the brinzolamide/brimonidine group and 5 in the latanoprost group by per-protocol analysis (2 eyes with progressive RNFL/GCIPL thinning were excluded from the per per-protocol analysis because of development of allergic conjunctivitis and medication switch). Altogether, only 24 eyes from 20 patients developed progressive RNFL/GCIPL thinning by GPA or TPA. The relatively small proportion of eyes that developed progressive RNFL/GCIPL thinning (24/182 or 13.2%) can be related to the fact that the mean IOP at the baseline (before IOP-lowering treatment) were not high (Table 1) and the IOP was significantly decreased after the treatment of latanoprost or brinzolamide/brimonidine (Fig.3). Although we were not able to enroll 203 patients (the planned sample size with one eye to be included for a subject), which in part was attributed to the 2019-2020 social unrest in Hong Kong and the COVID-19 pandemic, we were able to include 182 eyes in the analysis. The current sample size had a statistical power of 73.7% to detect a treatment effect of at least a difference of 0.7 µm/year in the rates of RNFL thinning between the treatment groups, with adjustment for correlation between fellow eyes in a subject. III. Attempts to overcome problem To achieve Objective (1), we need to extend the study follow up to allow sufficient time for development of progressive RNFL/GCIPL thinning before randomization to additional IOP-lowering treatment or continued treatment. We have a high retention rate of our research patients despite significant clinical service disruptions during the COVID-19 outbreak (96.0% in the latanoprost group and 92.3% in the brinzolamide/brimonidine group) and we are seeking additional funding support to complete Objective (1) (the total GRF budget awarded for this project was only US$84,311). IV. Research Output In addition to the aforementioned study findings (uploaded in Part C, Research Output 1), we also developed a new algorithm (ROTA – retinal nerve fiber layer optical texture analysis) to improve the detection of RNFL defects in glaucoma using data collected from the funded study. The manuscript was uploaded in Part C, Research Output 2.

To determine whether latanoprost or brinzolamide/brimonidine fixed combination can slow glaucoma progression independent of IOP reduction by comparing the IOP levels and the rates of retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) thinning between the two IOP-lowering medications.

14101117.label: Major findings and research outcome
14101117.value: PURPOSE: To determine whether latanoprost or brinzolamide/brimonidine fixed combination, which are topical IOP-lowering medications with purported neuroprotective effects, would slow glaucoma progression independent of IOP reduction by comparing the IOP levels and the rates of retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) thinning between the two treatments, and investigate the risk factors for glaucoma progression. METHODS: In this multicenter, randomized, open-labelled, parallel-group trial, 182 eyes of 102 glaucoma patients newly diagnosed patients (n=71) or patients who received ≤1 medication (n=31) after washout were randomized to receive latanoprost (n=50) or brinzolamide/brimonidine (n=52) and followed at 2-month intervals for measurements of IOP, RNFL thickness and visual field (VF) sensitivity over 2 years. The IOP and the rates of disease progression were compared with intention-to-treat (ITT) and per-protocol (PP) analyses using linear mixed models. The primary outcome measures were the rate of change of RNFL thickness. The rates of change of VF mean deviation (MD), time to detection of progressive RNFL/ganglion cell inner plexiform (GCIPL) thinning, and time to detection of VF progression were also compared between treatment groups. RESULTS: The baseline mean IOP was 19.2mmHg (95% CI: 18.3-20.0) in the latanoprost group (87 eyes) and 19.2mmHg (18.2-20.1) in the brinzolamide/brimonidine group (95 eyes). The 2-year mean IOP was 16.4mmHg (15.8-17.0) and 16.9mmHg (16.3-17.6), respectively, by ITT analysis; and 16.4mmHg (15.8-17.0) and 17.4mmHg (16.5-18.3), respectively, by PP analysis. No significant differences in the 2-year IOP measurements were detected between treatment groups (P≤0.178). The rate of RNFL thinning was on average 0.52µm/year (0.06-0.99) (ITT) to 0.85µm/year (0.26-1.45) (PP) faster in the brinzolamide/brimonidine group than the latanoprost group. The hazard ratio of brinzolamide/brimonidine to latanoprost for time to progressive RNFL/GCIPL thinning by Guided Progression Analysis was 5.28 (1.06-26.28) by ITT analysis and 7.38 (1.57-34.75) by PP analysis. The only risk factor associated with progressive RNFL/GICPL thinning was IOP; axial length was not a risk factor. There was no significant difference in the rates of change of VF MD and the time to detection of VF progression between treatment groups. 24 patients developed brinzolamide/brimonidine-associated allergic conjunctivitis. CONCLUSIONS: Latanoprost better preserved the RNFL than brinzolamide/brimonidine at comparable levels of IOP in glaucoma patients. Detection of a neuroprotective effect over 2 years was feasible with RNFL measurements but not VF measurements.

14101117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14101117.value: We have a high retention rate of our research patients despite significant clinical service disruptions during the COVID-19 outbreak (96.0% in the latanoprost group and 92.3% in the brinzolamide/brimonidine group). We will seek additional funding support to extend the study follow up to allow additional time for development of progressive RNFL/GCIPL thinning before randomization to additional IOP-lowering treatment or continued treatment.

14101117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14101117.value: Although numerous experimental studies have demonstrated brinzolamide and brimonidine to be neuroprotective in promoting retinal ganglion cells survival in models of optic nerve degeneration and the Low-Pressure Glaucoma Study Group supported a visual field-preserving effect for brimonidine in patients with glaucoma, we showed that eyes treated with brinzolamide/brimonidine had a considerably faster rate of retinal nerve fiber layer thinning than those treated with latanoprost despite the fact that the intraocular pressure levels measured at 2-month intervals over 2 years were similar between the two treatment groups. Our study provides early evidence suggesting a neuroprotective effect of latanoprost for patients with glaucoma and underscores the values of retinal nerve fiber layer measurements in neuroprotection trials when visual field outcomes may not show a treatment difference.

14101917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14101917.value: 大腸癌是人類最常見的惡性腫瘤之一。大約40%的大腸癌攜帶KRAS突變，而KRAS突變是一種重要的致癌突變，能導致大腸癌細胞對靶向表皮生長因子受體的藥物產生抗藥性。迄今為止，臨床上仍缺少KRAS突變特異性靶向治療藥物。近來，本研究團隊利用全基因組shRNA篩選的方法發現基因SLC25A22對攜帶有KRAS和APC/CTNNB1雙突變的癌細胞具有選擇性致死作用，是一個非常有前景的大腸癌藥物治療新型靶點。敲低SLC25A22能選擇性抑制KRAS突變型大腸癌細胞的生長，但對KRAS野生型大腸癌細胞或正常結腸上皮細胞的生長則沒有影響。我們的前期結果還發現，敲低SLC25A22與常用大腸癌化療藥物——5-氟尿嘧啶（5-FU）能協同促進KRAS突變型大腸癌細胞凋亡。此外，動物體內實驗發現敲低SLC25A22並協同5-氟尿嘧啶能抑制裸鼠皮下移植瘤的生長，並且比單藥治療更有效。代謝組學分析顯示，敲低SLC25A22並協同5-氟尿嘧啶能調節氨基酸和核苷酸代謝，共同調節KRAS突變型大腸癌細胞的代謝應激誘導，從而觸發內質網應激（ER stress）引起的細胞凋亡。因此，我們推測敲低SLC25A22聯合5-氟尿嘧啶能有效靶向KRAS突變型大腸癌。為了評估該假設，我們提出三個具體目標：1）評價敲低SLC25A22與化療藥物在大腸癌體內的協同作用；2）闡明敲低SLC25A22與化療藥物對腫瘤代謝的作用和3）闡明內質網應激途徑是敲低SLC25A22和化療藥物之間協同作用的基礎。通過本研究完善KRAS突變型大腸癌的發病機制，確定SLC25A22作為KRAS突變型大腸癌新型靶標的重要臨床價值，為大腸癌的靶向藥物治療開闢了一條新道路。

14101917.label: Realisation of objectives
14101917.value: Objective #1: In this study, we have comprehensively characterized the effect of SLC25A22 in KRAS-mutant CRC. We have established a unique Apcmin-KrasG12D mice model with or without conditional SLC25A22 knockout, and assessed its effect on tumorigenesis. Knockout of SLC25A22 impaired CRC development in this model. Our studies in vitro showed that SLC25A22 expression is associated with cancer stemness. Because cancer stemness drives chemotherapeutic resistance, we investigated the effect of SLC25A22 loss plus chemotherapy, including cisplatin (DNA damaging), docetaxel (antimitotic), fluorouracil (antimetabolite), and doxorubicin (topoisomerase inhibitor) in KRAS-mutant CRC cells. We found that loss of SLC25A22 increased sensitivity of KRAS-mutant CRC cells to fluorouracil (5-FU). Finally, we have tested the effect of combining SLC25A22 with chemotherapy in vivo. We evaluated the effect of SLC25A22 depletion plus 5-FU in vivo using DLD1 xenografts in nude mice. In DLD1-shControl and DLD1-shSLC25A22 xenografts (approximately 150 mm3) were treated with vehicle (phosphate-buffered saline) or 5-FU (50 mg/kg, intraperitoneal, once per week). Either SLC25A22 depletion or 5-FU treatment suppressed tumor growth by ~50%. Remarkably, SLC25A22 depletion plus 5-FU substantially reduced tumor weight by >85% compared with single treatments. In line with decreased tumor growth, SLC25A22 depletion plus 5-FU inhibited cell proliferation to a greater extent than either treatment alone, as done by Ki67 staining by immunohistochemistry. Together, these data indicated that SLC25A22 is a promising molecular target that sensitizes KRAS-mutant CRC to chemotherapy. Objective #2: To probe the role of SLC25A22 in modulating chemotherapy efficacy via modulating tumor metabolism, we initially compared the metabolome of control and SLC25A22 knockout cells. We performed targeted metabolomic analysis using 13C--glutamine as a tracer. We demonstrated that SLC25A22 suppressed the metabolic flux into succinate, fumarate, and malate, leading to an increased ratio of α-KG to succinate, fumarate, malate. Interestingly, 5-FU treatment also increased the ratio of α-KG to succinate, fumarate, malate. These metabolic alterations are functionally relevant, as succinate rescued viability of SLC25A22 knockout cells. Altered α-KG to succinate ratio has key ramifications for activities of α-KG–dependent dioxygenases. TETs and JMJDs are 2 major classes of α-KG–dependent enzymes that play crucial roles in gene regulation by modulating DNA and histone demethylation, respectively. We next evaluated the role of TCA cycle intermediates on cell growth. Manipulation of α-KG to succinate ratio by exogenous supplementation of α-KG (1 mM) or succinate (1 mM) revealed that α-KG inhibited growth of KRAS-mutant CRC cells; while succinate promoted cell proliferation in KRAS-wild-type DKS8 cells, suggesting that the α-KG to succinate ratio may regulate cell growth. To validate this hypothesis, we treated SLC25A22 knockout cells with α-KG or succinate and determined cell survival. Consistently, succinate restored cell viability in SLC25A22 knockout cells, while α-KG inhibited cell growth. Together, our data showed that SLC25A22 is critical for replenishment of TCA cycle via glutamine and maintains a low α-KG to succinate ratio favourable for cell growth and tumorigenicity. The combination of SLC25A22 depletion plus 5-FU treatment also suppressed the ratio of α-KG to succinate, fumarate, malate, in addition to decreased levels of non-essential amino acids. Hence, the combined metabolic effect of SLC25A22 and 5-FU are mediated through modulation of the TCA cycle metabolites. Objective 3: We observed that the reduction in amino acids levels after combination treatment caused the induction of ER stress, as evidenced by increased protein expression of ER stress markers. We also investigated whether the altered α-KG-to-succinate ratio by SLC25A22 knockout had an effect of signalling transduction and chemoresistance. As mentioned above, α-KG to succinate ratio has key ramifications for activities, TETs and JMJDs, 2 major classes of α-KG–dependent enzymes that play crucial roles in gene regulation by modulating DNA and histone demethylation, respectively. In line with this notion, SLC25A22 knockout led to genome-wide reduction in DNA methylation and histone H3K4me3 mark. This was mechanistically linked to altered TCA cycle metabolites, as succinate supplementation reversed the effect of knockout of SLC25A22 on DNA and histone methylation. Next, genome-wide epigenetic array reveals promoter methylation and transcriptional silencing of tumour suppressive protocadherin gene cluster (PCDHαβγ) in KRAS-mutant CRC in a SLC25A22-dependent fashion. It has been reported previously that members of the PCDHαβγ family function as tumour suppressors through inhibition of WNT/β-catenin signalling. Hence, we examined the effect of SLC25A22 on WNT/β-catenin signalling. Indeed, knockout of SLC25A22 suppressed WNT/β-catenin signalling, as evidenced by luciferase reporter assay, nuclear active β-catenin expression and the expression of WNT targets. TET1/2/3 knockdown restored nuclear expression of active β-catenin in SLC25A22 knockout, thereby confirming the role of DNA demethylases in the control of WNT/β-catenin signalling downstream of SLC25A22. Apart from DNA methylation, histone methylation was also mediated by SLC25A22. SLC25A22 knockout induced the loss of H3K4 and H3K79 trimethylation, together with H3K27 and H3K36 dimethylation. H3K4me3 plays a crucial role in normal stem cell functions, cell fate determination and self-renewal of cancer stem cells (CSCs). We thus postulated that SLC25A22-induced H3K4me3 may be associated with genes involved in CRC stemness. Indeed, WNT-driven stemness markers, such as CD44 and LGR5, were depleted in SLC25A22 knockout cells, which is mediated in part by reduced H3K4me3 levels at their gene promoters. Finally, we found that the combination of DNA and histone methylation by SLC25A22 was required for the optimal expression of CSC markers, in particular for LGR5. To summarize, depletion of SLC25A22 suppressed CRC stemness and induced ER stress via modulating metabolism, which forms the basis for its synergy with 5-FU.

14101917.label: Major findings and research outcome
14101917.value: Mutations in the KRAS oncogene are highly prevalent in CRC and it drives colon carcinogenesis by synergizing with the APC/β-catenin signalling pathway. Moreover, KRAS mutations mediate resistance to anti-EGFR therapy. In our previous study (Gastroenterology, 2016), we showed that SLC25A22 as a synthetic lethal metabolic gene that selectively targets colon cancer cells harbouring concomitant mutations in KRAS and APC/β-catenin. In the continuation of this work, we expand our work to investigate: 1) the role of SLC25A22 in epigenetic modulation and cancer stemness; and 2) the potential therapeutic value of targeting glutamine metabolism for the treatment of KRAS mutant CRC. We showed that SLC25A22 is essential for epigenetic deregulation in KRAS-mutant CRC, which in turn, promotes cancer stemness. Moreover, knockout of SLC25A22 in CRC cells that express mutant KRAS increased their sensitivity to 5-fluorouacil, implying therapeutic implication for KRAS-mutant CRC. This project has been fruitful and has been published in Gastroenterology in 2020 [IF=22.68], with the PI as corresponding author. This work has also been presented in UEG week 2018 and the Digestive Disease Week 2019. The PI was awarded the Early-Stage Investigator Award in DDW2019 based on this project. Apart from this work, we have also investigated the role oncogenes in CRC, including RNF6 (Oncogene, 2021, co-first author, IF=9.84) and METTL3 (Gastroenterology, 2021, IF=22.68), and also published several review articles related to CRC (Oncogene, 2020, IF=9.84; Metabolites, 2021, IF=4.75; Seminars in Cancer Biology, 2019, IF=15.71). A total of 12 papers and 3 conferences were published based on this funding.

14101917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14101917.value: To further improve our understanding of SLC25A22 in KRAS-mutant CRC, we will open up collaborative work with other academic researchers to investigate the impact of SLC25A22 with our SLC25A22 knockout mice models. I have collaborated with researchers from the local and international institutions who has expertise with different aspects of oncology research. We will focus on other aspects of SLC25A22-mediated oncogenesis, including onco-immunology, therapeutics and biomarker development. For medium term plans, we will screen small molecules or antisense strategies to target SLC25A22 in APC/KRAS-mutant CRC. Based on our results, we will apply for further R&D grants and contracts available through a competitive basis. We will also engage pharmaceutical companies to gain access to proprietary drug/antisense libraries, which will be used to screen for potential drug candidates using our human primary organoids and mice models with knockout of SLC25A22. The promising inhibitors will be further optimized through liaising with pharmaceutical firms.

14101917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14101917.value: Nature of the project: Mutant KRAS promotes glutaminolysis, a process that uses steps from the tricarboxylic cycle to convert glutamine to α-ketoglutarate and other molecules, via glutaminase and solute carrier family 25 member 22 (SLC25A22). This results in inhibition of demethylases and epigenetic alterations in cells that increase proliferation and stem cell features. In colorectal cancer cells that express activated KRAS, SLC25A22 promotes accumulation of succinate, resulting in increased DNA methylation, activation of WNT signaling to β-catenin, increased expression of LGR5, proliferation, stem cell features, and resistance to 5-fluorouacil. Significance: Our work demonstrated that SLC25A22 as an actionable target in KRAS-mutant CRC. The combination of targeting SLC25A22 in conjunction with 5-fluorouacil, synergized to inhibit the growth of KRAS-mutant CRC in vitro and in vivo, thereby implying the potential role of SLC25A22 as a chemotherapy sensitizing target. Apart from its role in therapy, we showed that SLC25A22 as a specific biomarker that predicts poor survival in KRAS-mutant CRC. Value of the project: Strategies to disrupt SLC25A22 might be developed for the treatment of KRAS-mutant CRC. SLC25A22 might serve as a prognostic biomarker for KRAS-mutant CRC

14102417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14102417.value: 細胞自噬是真核細胞中自我吞噬的過程。它通過形成雙膜結構的自噬體，與液泡/溶酶體融合，使細胞質內的物質降解。膜融合過程對於自噬體的形成及其在液泡/溶酶體中的降解方面起著至關重要的作用。該過程涉及到不同的功能調節因子和自噬相關蛋白，以用於自噬體與內體或液泡/溶酶體的對接和融合等不同過程。目前研究表明，內體與自噬途徑存在關聯途徑，囊泡運輸機制和自噬相關蛋白之間有緊密相連。 膜系鏈（SNARE複合物）通過作為自噬體和內體/液泡膜之間的鏈接蛋白，參與對接和融合的過程。然而，大多數植物SNARE蛋白的作用和功能仍未被發現。因此，鑑定植物特異的SNARE蛋白在內體/液泡 - 自噬體形成和融合過程中的作用，將加深我們對植物自噬中膜融合的理解。 我們提出特定的SNARE蛋白複合物以及相關組分參與植物自噬程程中自噬體的融合和液泡降解的過程因此，我們研究目的是：1）鑑定與植物自噬過程相關的SNARE; 2 ）鑑定參與植物自噬過程的SNARE相關的調控因子。我們研究的長期目標是闡明植物內吞和自噬機制之間潛在的關聯機制。

14102417.label: Realisation of objectives
14102417.value: 1. Using transient expression in Arabidopsis protoplasts, we have screened and identified two Arabidopsis SNAREs VAMP724 and VAMP726 associated with the autophagosome during plant autophagy. Using a combination of genetic (single/double mutants and transgenic plants), cellular (e.g. 3D electron tomography and immunogold-TEM) and molecular approaches in transgenic Arabidopsis plants, we have demonstrated the roles of the two selective SNAREs VAMP724 and VAMP726 in regulating the autophagosome-vacuole fusion and also their association with the ATG9 in regulating the autophagosome formation in Arabidopsis plants. A manuscript is under review (see attached MS in Part C: Research Output). 2. We have also developed a systems-level algorithm to identify autophagy-related modules (ARMs) and verified selective newly identified regulators in plant autophagy. This novel finding has been published in The Plant Journal in 2021. 3. We have first demonstrated that the Arabidopsis AtSec62 involved in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-stress response and may function as an ER-phagy receptor in plants. This novel finding has been published in Journal of Integrative Plant Biology (JIPB) in 2020. 4. We have identified and shown that a plant-unique ROP8-Sec5 signaling axis regulates autophagy promotion under stress condition in plants. This new finding has been published in Molecular Plant in 2021. 5. We have identified and demonstrated that a plant-specific nexus of Sar1d-RabD2a regulated autophagosome biogenesis in plans. This novel finding has been published in PNAS in 2021. In conclusion, we have achieved all the original objectives in the research project successfully as demonstrated by the publication as well as the research findings summarized in this completion report. This RGC-funded project sheds light into the research about new unique regulators in regulation of the autophagy pathways in plants. This project has also nurtured several graduate students, and resulted in publications in prestigious international journals.

14102417.label: Major findings and research outcome
14102417.value: 1. We have demonstrated Sec62 as a regulator of a selective autophagic pathway the ER-phagy. The finding was published in Journal of Integrative Plant Biology in 2020. 2. We have developed an in-silico pridiction algorithm to identify autophagy-related proteins using Arabidopsis thaliana interactome data. The data was published in The Plant Journal in 2021. 3. We have identified a unique ROP signaling mechanism, which mediates developmental to autophagic transition under stress conditions in Arabidopsis. The data was published in Molecular Plant in 2021. 4. We have uncovered a novel role of a specific Sar1 homolog Sar1d in plant autophagy in concert with RabD2a. The data was published in The Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America in 2021. 5. We have identified autophagy-related SNAREs VAMP724 and VAMP726 and investigated their roles in regulating autophagy in Arabidopsis. The MS is under review. 6. We have highlighted and discussed recent findings on the interplay between endomembranes and autophagy in plants in a review article published in Current Opinion in Plant Biology in 2019. 7. We have summarized and discussed about the feasibility and the challenges in applying the most advanced techniques (e.g. 3D-ET, Cryo-FIB, and Cryo-ET) in visualizing the plant endomembrane system in a review article published in Plant Physiology in 2021. 8. With partially support from this project, we have also trained several excellent postgraduate students with outstanding research outputs as demonstrated by publications of their thesis work in a number of international journals.

14102417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14102417.value: Our studies have shed lights on the molecular mechanisms of selective SNAREs (e.g. VAMP724 and VAMP726) and other new regulators in mediating the formation of autophagosome, autophagosome-vacuole fusion, and crosstalk between autopagy and endomembrane in plants. These new findings expanded our knowledge towards the complexity and plasticity of plant autophagy, which will provide the basis for further study on the underlying mechanisms of new regulators in regulating the crosstalk between the autophagy pathway and endomembrane trafficking in plants using our recently established advanced EM-absed imaging techniques at nanometer resolution including the 3D-ET, Cryo-FIB, and Cryo-ET in combination with the advanced live-cell imaging systems such as Super-Resolution Microscopy (SRM) and Lattice Light Sheet Microscopy (LLSM), as well as the Correlative Light and Electron Microscopy (CLEM) that we have developed and demonstrated in plants.

14102417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14102417.value: This project identified and studied the underlying mechanisms of selective SNAREs and novel regulators in plant autophagy using a combination of molecular, cellular, genetic and biochemical approaches. Findings from this study have provided new insights into about the molecular machinery of new regulators in plant autophagy, and provided the basis for future study of crosstalk between autophagy and other trafficking pathways in plants.
