14103817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14103817.value: Our long-term goal is to characterize the alternate paths by mushroom-forming fungi to determine the cell fates and reproduction strategies. Our specific objectives are (1) Identify the specific RNA editing events of each developmental paths, namely, chlamydospore, sclerotium and fruiting body; (2) Examine the roles of fruiting-body-specific RNA editing events by experiments; (3) Characterize the dynamic transcriptional and post-transcriptional changes in 3 different developmental paths; and (4) Analyze in silico the transcriptome data from evolutionary perspectives. In fruiting body development of C. cinerea, many genes are differentially expressed at different developmental stages. Transcription factors (TFs) controls the differential expression of these genes. When transcription factors are expressed higher or lower in some stages than in other stages, they are considered to play regulatory roles. Several TFs are essential and differentially expressed in early stages of fruiting body development in the model mushroom Schizophyllum commune. However, orthologs of these TFs do not show similar expression profiles in C. cinerea and related fungi. This has been a major gap in our understanding of the regulation of mushroom development. Levels of gene transcripts and the proteins they encode are not only determined by expression, but also by post-transcriptional modification. Expression profile variations of TFs in different mushroom species reflect that post-transcriptional modification is important for the effective transcript levels of the TFs responding to environmental conditions. Mushroom formation is a programmed process in fungi, but the fungi also behave like prokaryotes in responding to environmental conditions such as light, temperature and nutrition to attenuate fruiting and diverge to alternate paths to form mitotic spores, sclerotium, or other structures. RNA post-transcriptional modification is likely to take part in these. We have observed RNA-editing in transcriptomic analyses of TFs during the development of C. cinerea. We hypothesize that RNA-editing is important in determining the developmental destinies of C. cinerea. We propose to characterize the developmental destinies in detail by deep RNA-seq. We will understand the details in genes, transcripts, RNA-editing events and alternative splicing events specific to C. cinerea developmental destinies, providing insights into cell differentiation and developmental biology of mushroom-forming fungi. 我們的長期目標是描繪蘑菇形成真菌用以確定細胞命運及繁殖策略的不同發育路徑。我們的具體目標是（1）辨定厚壁孢子，菌核和子實體這三個發育路徑的具體RNA編輯事件;（2）通過實驗研究子實體路徑特異性RNA編輯事件的作用; （3）表徵三種不同發育路徑的轉錄組和後轉錄的變化; （4）從進化角度分析轉錄組數據。在灰蓋鬼傘子實體發育中，許多基因在不同的發育階段有差異表達。轉錄因子（TFs）控制著這些基因的差異表達。當轉錄因子在某些階段表達高於或低於其他階段時，它們被認為是在發揮著調控作用。在模式菇类裂褶菌的子實體發育的早期階段，幾種TF是必需的和差異表達的。然而，這些TF的直向同源物在灰蓋鬼傘和相關真菌中并没有類似的表達趋势。這令我們了解蘑菇發育的規律還存在一個巨大的空白。基因轉錄本及其編碼的蛋白質的水平不僅通過表達而且通過後轉錄修飾來決定。不同蘑菇物種中TFs的表達趨勢不同，反映了後轉錄修飾對於響應環境條件變化的TF的有效轉錄本水平是非常重要的。蘑菇子實體形成是程序化的過程，但是真菌也像原核生物一樣，在響應光，溫度和營養等環境條件下表現出減弱出菇，並發散到其它發育路徑以形成無性孢子，菌核或其他結構。 RNA後轉錄修飾可能參與這些環境響應和發育路徑選擇。我們已經觀察到了在灰蓋鬼傘發育過程中TFs的轉錄本的RNA編輯。因而我們提出假說，RNA編輯在決定灰蓋鬼傘的發育路徑時有很重要的作用。我們計劃通過轉錄組深度測序，詳細描述不同發育路徑的轉錄組特征。我們將了解灰蓋鬼傘的不同發育路徑，及其特定的基因，轉錄本，RNA編輯事件以及可變剪切事件的細節，為蘑菇形成的細胞分化和發育生物學提供理論基礎。

14103817.label: Realisation of objectives
14103817.value: 1. We have carefully clarified the life history of Coprinopsis cinerea A43mut B43mut pab1-1 #326 towards different developmental path. By culturing under different combination of temperature and light conditions, we induced vegetative growth, oidiation, fruiting and sclerotia formation with good repeatability. We chose 6 representative developmental paths and stages, namely, vegetative mycelia, oidia, sclerotia, hyphal knots, fruiting body primordia, and young fruiting bodies. Samples of developing colonies and developed colonies (structures well formed) were collected in five biological replicates. Carbohydrate compounds, including glucose, trehalose, glycogen and beta-glucan, of all samples were assayed. RNA of developing colonies were sequenced by Illumina Hiseq 4000 platform. We developed the RNA editing sites calling pipeline, and further tested it with four published fungal datasets. To increase the reliability of editing calling, we collected DNA sample and performed whole genome re-sequencing on the same sequencing platform. RNA editing site calling was conducted as follows: (1) DNA/RNA-seq read alignment by Bowtie2/Hisat2; (2) reads duplication removal by Java package, Picard MarkDuplicates.jar; (3) read mapping blat correction by python script REDItoolBlatCorrection.py; (4) candidate site calling by REDItoolDnaRna.py. To minimise the false discovery rate, we navigated the RNA editing recovery rate and cut-off parameters. We finalised the following cut-offs: (i) to minimise the false discovery caused by sequencing and mapping error, the minimum reads quality and mapping quality of are set to 25 in both DNA and RNA, and multi hit reads are excluded; (ii) to ensure the significance of occurrence of editing events, at least 3 reads should support the variant, with the minimum frequency of 3% and minimum coverage of 10 reads; (iii) exclude positions with changes in DNA-seq to avoid false positive events resulted from genome variants; (iv) exclude positions near splice site within 4 bases to avoid the mismatch caused by misalignment of RNA; (v) to further minimise the false discovery rate, editing events should present in at least 2 biological samples of all samples of developmental paths dataset and meiosis dataset. We also profiled the functional and evolutionary features of RNA editing sites. The RNA editing sites were annotated to specific genes or intergenic regions. The RNA editing events tended to appear on genes that are evolutionarily old and under strong purifying selection, revealing the special roles of RNA editing on providing plasticity to the transcriptome. 2. We have validated an RNA editing site, scaffold_131:54938, by PCR amplification and Sanger sequencing. It showed a maximum of 70% editing frequency during hyphal knot formation, while low editing level in vegetative mycelia, oidia and sclerotia, and no RNA editing in primordia and young fruiting bodies. We found that scaffold_131:54938 was located at a hypothetical protein coding gene, and the editing caused synonymous changes to the amino acid sequence. We have validated that expression level of the gene was up-regulated in hyphal knots and sclerotia. We have tested other 70 RNA editing candidate sites, but we have not observed other positive RNA editing events by Sanger sequencing. The RNA editing level showed by in silico prediction was low, which raised difficulties to the experimental validation. The significance of RNA editing on fruiting body development can also be minor. Potential RNA editing mechanism was predicted and studied. We have identified three adenosine deaminases acting on tRNA (ADAT) homologs, but no adenosine deaminases acting on RNA (ADARs) homolog. Quantitative real-time PCR showed that the expression levels of ADATs were relatively low and not significantly different among different developmental stages. These findings explained the low RNA editing level and little fruiting-body-specific RNA editing events. 3. Gene expression profiles were analysed and differentially expressed genes were identified. A total of 10,082 genes were expressed in at least one developmental path. Taking gene expression levels in vegetative mycelium as references, 3962 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were recognised in the paths. They were assigned to 6 groups (3 paths with up- and down-regulation). Hyphal knot and sclerotia possessed many DEGs, with 1,142 and 2,065 up-regulated genes and 1,011 and 1,009 down-regulated genes, respectively. In oidia, only 175 genes were up-regulated, while 460 genes were down-regulated. 652 and 185 genes were sclerotia specifically up-regulated or down-regulated. We observed significant turn-over on gene expression level in carbohydrate metabolic pathway, as well as the content of different carbohydrate compounds. Functional annotation showed that DEGs were enriched in the energy production and conversion, and metabolic process of carbohydrate and secondary metabolites. These results indicated the major role of carbohydrate metabolism in developmental path differentiation. To understand the transcriptome of developmental paths differentiation with an evolutionary perspective, transcriptome age index (TAI) and transcriptome divergence index (TDI) was used to estimate the evolutionary age and selective pressure of each developmental path. Oidiation process expressed the evolutionarily oldest genes, followed by sclerotia. Vegetative mycelia and hyphal knots expressed the evolutionarily younger genes. The oidia transcriptome showed the strongest signal of purifying selection, and the hyphal knot showed the weakest. Accordingly, oidia is seen as the most conserved developmental path, whereas fruiting process is evolutionarily young and divergent. The highest expression ratio of old genes to young genes occurred in oidia, followed by mycelium and hyphal knot, and sclerotia had the lowest ratio of zero. Interestingly, this ranking coincided with the evaluation on growing environment, from the most temperate to the most stressful. All these results indicated that oidiation, the asexual reproductive process, seemed to occur in the common ancestor of Eukaryota and conserved in current living organisms; while fruiting, the sexual reproductive process, was highly specific and evolutionarily adaptive. The RNA editome in developmental paths differentiation of C. cinerea was very different from those Ascomycetes fungi. A total of 245 and 152 RNA editing sites were found during developmental paths differentiation and basidiospore formation. Most of them were in low editing frequency. Sclerotia have 64 specific RNA editing sites, while other paths and stages got around or below 10 specific sites. Most of the RNA editing events had editing levels < 20%, and the editing level remained constant and relatively low. All substitution types were found in C. cinerea, except A-to-U editing. T-to-C substitution took up over 55% of the editing events. In mycelia, hyphal knots, oidia and sclerotia, 107, 111, 101 and 171 editing sites were detected, respectively. Functional enrichment of the RNA editing sites of specific developmental paths was not significant. Editing effect analysis showed that 44.1% the RNA editing sites were annotated to the intergenic region and only 30.4% were in the coding sequence (CDS). A total of 13 and 48 RNA editing sites were located in 5’ UTR and 3’ UTR, respectively. 42 of 71 editing sites in CDS and 19 of 61 editing sites in UTR would affect RNA secondary structure. There was 52.7% of the RNA editing sites occurs in hairpin loop area of the RNA, which displayed the structural preference. Six editing sites could generate the splicing variants and transcript length variants. One RNA editing would cause pre-mature stop codon. Four editing containing genes only have single copy in the genome and all with unique function.

14103817.label: Major findings and research outcome
14103817.value: As a model of mushroom-forming fungus, the fruiting process of C. cinerea has been well studied physiologically and genetically. In this project, we monitored the early developmental process of three destinies, fruiting, oidiation and sclerotia formation, with the reference of vegetative mycelium. Carbohydrate assays and high-throughput sequencing results all indicate the essential role of carbon metabolic flux in fungal morphogenesis. Evolutionary transcriptome analysis revealed the origin and selection of dispersal and survival strategies of C. cinerea. The RNA editing events have been found and confirmed in all developmental paths. Most editing sites had the editing levels below 20%. The impact of RNA editing includes recoding protein sequences, generating alternative transcripts, changing milRNA-UTR interactions and regulating gene expression levels. RNA editing show preferences on genes that are old and under high purifying selection, revealing the special roles of RNA editing on providing plasticity to the transcriptome. These analytical results expand our understanding of the evolutionary process of life history, reproductive strategy and multicellularity development in fungi. Due to limited available genome resources, we used Oxford Nanopore MinION platform to re-sequence C. cinerea strain #326 and constructed a chromosome-level reference genome. The transcriptomes of different developmental paths provided evidence to the genome annotation. The new reference genome improved the sequence contiguity for 30-times. We uncovered 4.6 Mb high complexity sequences that were missed in the previous short-read constructed genome, and 2602 novel gene models. It contributes new genome resources and transcriptome profile to future studies. The research findings of this project has been published in three articles on Fungal Genetics and Biology, a top journal in Mycology, namely: (i) Carbon metabolism and transcriptome in developmental paths differentiation of a homokaryotic Coprinopsis cinerea strain (Cover story); (ii) Chromosome-level de novo assembly of Coprinopsis cinerea A43mut B43mut pab1-1 #326 and genetic variant identification of mutants using Nanopore MinION sequencing; (iii) Genome-wide mRNA and miRNA analysis in the early stages of germ tube outgrowth in Coprinopsis cinerea. These results were also included in two Ph. D theses.

14103817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14103817.value: We have profiled the transcriptomic and post-transcriptomic changes during developmental paths differentiation and validated the existence of RNA editing in C. cinerea. However, the RNA editome in C. cinerea was greatly different from previous reports in other fungi, by means of substitution types, editing level, stage and tissue preferences, and functional impacts. Further, the mechanism and evolution of RNA editing in fungi remains largely unknown. To have a better view on RNA editing in basidiomycetes and other fungi, we suggest building an RNA editing database using the RNA-seq data from the public platforms. Currently, more than 6,500 transcriptomes of 2,425 species are available in SRA database, which is quite a large amount to profile the occurrence and evolution of RNA editing in basidiomycetes. Correlation covariation analysis on the RNA editing levels and genes expression level would help to identify novel RNA editing enzymes. By analysing the conservative RNA editing containing genes, we shall uncover the long-term importance and selective advantages of RNA editing to fungi.

14103817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14103817.value: Coprinopsis cinerea is a widely used model species in fungal developmental and evolutionary studies. This project analysed the carbohydrate metabolism and gene expression regulation during the early differentiation process of vegetative mycelia, oidiation, fruiting and sclerotia formation. We emphasized the major role of carbohydrate metabolism in the selection of fungal developmental strategy. We confirmed the existence of RNA editing in C. cinerea, and analysed its role in transcriptional and post-transcriptional regulation. This is the first analysis and report in C. cinerea and in the Agaricales group. The evolutionary analysis reveals that all transcriptomes are under the purifying selection, and the more stressful the environment, the younger the transcriptome age. These analytical results expand our understanding of the evolutionary process of life history and reproductive strategy in fungi. The new chromosome-level reference genome provides important resource to the research community. Our RNA editing site calling pipeline and MinION-based fungal genomic analysis workflow have great plasticity and expandability and are applicable to other fungal studies. We will transfer the knowledge to the research on a larger group of fungi.

14105517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14105517.value: We, as human beings, are constantly exposed to environmental agents that cause damage and mutations in our DNA, which includes ultraviolet radiation from the sun and chemical released by cigarette smoke and pollutants. The cells in our body have developed a sophisticated system, known as the DNA damage response, to cope with these insults in order to protect our genetic material. Without this system, these ongoing DNA damage and mutations will eventually lead to the development of cancer. The enzyme ATM has an essential role in initiating and regulating the entire DNA damage response system, and therefore understanding how ATM precisely functions would offer the possibility of exploiting or manipulating its enzyme activity for cancer therapy or prevention. We will use an electron microscope to directly image ATM to gain information about how it works and how it cooperates with other cellular protein partners. Advances in electron microscope instrumentation provide an opportunity to see these structures at high resolution. Our work promises to give an unprecedented clear view of an important component of the biological system that safeguards our DNA. 我們作為人類，經常暴露於造成我們的DNA損傷和突變的環境因素，包括來自太陽的紫外線輻射和由香煙煙霧和污染物釋放的化學物質等。我們身體中的細胞已經開發出一種被稱為DNA損傷反應的複雜系統，以應對這些損傷和保護我們的遺傳物質。沒有這個系統，這些持續的DNA損傷和突變將最終導致癌症的發展。酶ATM在啟動和調節整個DNA損傷反應系統中起重要作用，因此了解ATM精確功能提供利用或操縱其酶活性用於癌症治療或預防的可能性。我們將使用電子顯微鏡直接映像ATM以獲得有關其工作原理以及如何與其他細胞蛋白質合作夥伴合作的信息。電子顯微鏡儀器的進步提供了以高分辨率看到這些結構的機會。我們的工作有望為保護我們的DNA的生物系統的重要組成部分提供前所未有清晰的觀點。

14105517.label: Major findings and research outcome
14105517.value: The DNA damage response is a well-orchestrated and tightly regulated process, and has been recently shown to induce cellular autophagy. Given the central role of autophagy in the DNA damage response, we have successfully determined the first structure of ATG9 to subnanometer resolution by using the technique of single-particle cryo-EM, providing insights into the molecular architecture of this membrane protein involved in both autophagy and the DNA damage response pathways. Combined with prediction of protein contacts using sequence co-evolutionary information, our study provides testable hypotheses for the molecular mechanism of autophagy progression regulated by ATG9. The results have been published. We have also made due acknowledgement for RGC's support in these endeavours. Lai LTF, Yu C, Wong JSK, Lo HS, Benlekbir S, Jiang L and Lau WCY. 14105517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14105517.value: Built upon our understanding of the structure of ATG9, we are continuing to study its to higher resolution and in complex with its adaptor and regulatory proteins using lipid nanodisc technology in order to gain detailed insights into its mechanism of action in the membrane. We are also exploring potential interactions between ATG9 and key components of the DNA damage response, and will determine structures of the resulting complexes. Furthermore, we will also explore the opportunity to develop small-molecule or peptide inhibitors based on the cryo-EM structures for targeting the recently identified DNA damage response-autophagy axis for the treatment of cancers.

14105517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14105517.value: Our work provided the first structural insights into the molecular architecture of a core autophagy machinery ATG9 as well as testable hypotheses for the molecular mechanism of autophagy progression. Our structure provides a solid basis for future structural studies of ATG9 in complex with various adaptor and regulatory proteins and in different catalytic intermediate states using cryo-EM, paving the way for the development of therapeutics for the treatment of various cancers through targeting the DNA damage response-autophagy axis.

14106117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14106117.value: Skeletal muscle has a remarkable ability to regenerate after injury owing to the muscle stem cell (also called satellite cell, SC) which normally lies quiescently beneath the muscle fiber. SC can quickly activate and proliferate following injury, then differentiate and fuse into myofiber; meanwhile a subset of SCs undergoes self-renewal and return to the quiescent state to replenish the adult stem cell pool. Each state of the myogenic lineage progression is orchestrated by complex regulatory networks of intrinsic and extrinsic factors/mechanisms. Disruption of the regulations may render their loss of ability to regenerate, contributing to muscle wasting conditions such as muscular dystrophy, cachexia, and sarcopenia that are prevalent in our society. As a recently discovered family of cellular regulators, long noncoding RNAs (>200nt non-protein coding RNAs, lncRNAs) are remarkably powerful, flexible, and pervasive in controlling major biological processes. However, despite efforts from our groups and others in the past few years, our understanding of lncRNA participation in SC activities remains largely elusive. Here we propose to study the function of a previously uncharacterized long non-coding RNA SAM (Sgt1 Associated Muscle lncRNA) in promoting the myogenic lineage progression. In the pilot study, knockdown of SAM in culture or knockout in a mouse model caused defect in SC proliferation; mechanistically it binds with Sgt1 co-chaperon protein to regulate kinetochore assembly during cell division. These preliminary results lead us to hypothesize that SAM plays important roles in SC functionality and muscle regeneration. Three aims were proposed in this project to (1) further elucidate the intrinsic defect of SC from SAM KO mice; (2) further dissect Sgt1 mediated mechanism of SAM functions in SC proliferation; (3) examine the effect of SAM deletion on dystrophic muscle and the effect of conditional deletion on muscle regeneration. Once completed, this study will uncover SAM as a novel regulator of SC function and muscle regeneration; it will thus enhance our knowledge foundation in the intrinsic regulatory mechanisms underlying skeletal muscle regeneration for future therapeutic development of treating muscle damages and diseases. 骨骼肌肌肉在受損後擁有很強的再生能力，這主要歸功於附著於骨骼肌纖維上的干細胞。這些細胞通常處於靜息狀態，但當肌肉受損時會迅速激活，增殖並分化形成新的肌纖維來修復受損肌肉。這個過程中的每一步都受到精密調控。作為最近發現的細胞調控因子，長非編碼RNA（> 200nt非蛋白​​質編碼RNA，lncRNA）在控制細胞中主要生物過程中的作用非常靈活和。然而我們對lncRNA在骨骼肌幹細胞中的調控並不十分了解。在該課題中，我們將研究lncRNA SAM促進骨骼肌幹細胞增殖的作用及其機制。在預實驗中，小鼠模型中SAM的敲除導致了骨骼肌幹細胞增殖的減慢;進一步研究表明它與Sgt1蛋白質可結合以調節細胞分裂過程中的著絲點形成。為進一步研究SAM的功能，本項目提出三個目標：（1）進一步闡明SAM KO小鼠中骨骼肌幹細胞的內在缺陷; （2）進一步刨析Sgt1/SAM介導的著絲點形成機制; （ 3）研究SAM缺失對骨骼肌肌肉再生的影響。一旦完成，這項研究將首次揭示SAM調且骨骼肌幹細胞增殖和骨骼肌再生的作用機理，這將增強我們對骨骼肌再生的認知，從而為將來治療肌肉損傷和疾病奠定理論基礎。

14106117.label: Realisation of objectives
14106117.value: In the original proposal we hypothesized that SAM plays important roles in SC functionality and muscle regeneration. Three specific aims/objectives are proposed and we are pleased to report that all 3 aims have been successfully implemented with favorable outcomes. AIM 1: To further elucidate the cell autonomous defects of SCs from SAM KO mice. We first found that within 30 h after isolation, the percentages of EdU+ and Pax7+ MyoD+ cells were reduced 36.62% and 17.91%, respectively in KO vs. WT, indicating a possible defect at the very early activation stage. Further assessing the differentiation ability, we found the percentage of MyoG+MyoD+ cells was increased (25.72%) in KO vs. WT SCs cultured for 3 days or myofiber-associated SCs cultured for the same period (19.87%). This was further substantiated by measuring the fusion index by MF20 staining after 2 days in DM; KO cells showed a higher fusion ability (2.7 fold) than WT cells, indicating SAM loss leads to an increased propensity for differentiation, which was consistent with the finding from. Lastly, the TUNEL assay did not detect differences in KO vs. WT cells cultured for 2 days, suggesting SAM loss may not have caused SC apoptosis. Altogether, the above results demonstrate that SAM deletion causes a delay in SC activation and proliferation but increases the propensity for precocious differentiation. AIM 2: To further dissect Sgt1 mediated mechanism of SAM action in SC cell division. To further ask how SAM association regulates Sugt1, we found that SAM depletion in SC did not alter the mRNA level of Sugt1 or its proper localization at kinetochores in prometaphase. Furthermore, it did not appear to alter the basal level of Sugt1 protein. However, treatment with a protein biosynthesis inhibitor, CHX, caused a marked decrease (31.4%) of Sugt1 protein in KO whereas only 18% in WT, suggesting lower stability of Sugt1 in KO cells. Consistently, in a 20 h long CHX chase experiment, the half-life of Sugt1 protein was reduced at a faster rate upon SAM knockdown, confirming SAM is required for maintaining the protein stability of Sugt1. Moreover, the decreased Sugt1 upon SAM depletion was blocked in the presence of a proteasome inhibitor, MG132, suggesting SAM may stabilize Sugt1 through preventing its ubiquitination. To further test this notion, HA-tagged ubiquitin protein was over expressed in Ctrl or shSAM MBs together with Sugt1 protein; we found an increased accumulation of poly-ubiquitinated Sugt1 in shSAM cells. Consistently, the stability of Sugt1 protein was rescued after restoring SAM expression in the presence of CHX without changing its RNA level. To examine if SAM stabilizing Sugt1 protein specifically occurs in MB cells, we found no decrease in Sugt1 level in primary hepatocytes isolated from WT vs. KO mouse with or without CHX treatment. Lastly, to further strengthen that SAM promotes MB proliferation through stabilizing Sugt1 protein, we found that overexpressing the WT or a stable mutant of Sugt1 (Sugt1-4A)12 fully rescued the deficient proliferation of SAM KO cells while over-expressing a highly unstable mutant of Sugt1 (Sugt1-4E)12 failed. Since Sugt1 is critical for proper kinetochore assembly during cell division10,41, we next tested whether SAM/Sugt1 together regulate SC proliferation through modulating kinetochore assembly. By staining chromosomes with DAPI, centromeres with ACA and spindles with α-Tubulin, in control cells, a robust spindle structure was preserved in metaphase cells, and bundles of microtubules were observed to terminate in kinetochores. In contrast, cells with Sugt1 knockdown exhibited disorganized spindle structures with multipolar spindles and fragmented spindle poles frequently observed. The above phenomena were also observed in C2C12 MBs when Sugt1 was decreased. Altogether, our data demonstrate Sugt1 is important for proper chromosomal alignment and spindle organization and thus timely mitotic division of MBs. Next, to demonstrate that SAM functions synergistically with Sugt1, we found SAM KO cells displayed evident defects in chromosome alignment and mitotic spindle formation. Again, this was also more frequently observed in C2C12 MBs with SAM knockdown vs. control cells, confirming SAM is needed for proper chromosomal alignment and mitotic division. To further determine if the above observed mitotic defects in SAM-depleted cells were due to kinetochore abnormalities, we examined kinetochore–microtubule (kt–mt) attachments under cold treatment considering the loss of cold stable kt–mt attachments is commonly used as an indicator of kinetochore defects43. WT and KO SCs were treated on ice for 10 min followed by α-Tubulin staining of microtubules; the fluorescence intensity was markedly decreased (20.76%) in KO vs. WT SCs, suggesting SAM loss led to increased instability of microtubules due to decreased kinetochores attaching. Consistently, when performed on C2C12, the same conclusion was reached; a reduced fluorescence intensity of microtubules was found in shSAM MBs under cold treatment. To further pinpoint the defect in kinetochore assembly upon SAM loss, we examined the localization of Mis12 complex, since it is known as a client of Hsp90-Sugt1 to be stabilized and targeted to the kinetochore. As expected, by IF a lower level of fluorescent signals of Dsn1 subunit was observed at the kinetochores in the mitotic KO vs. WT cells. We next examined the localization of Hec1 giving that as a so-called keystone complex Mis12 contributes to the localization of Ndc80 complex; interestingly, an over-accumulation of Hec1 kinetochore signals was detected in the KO vs. WT SCs. Similar phenomena were also observed in C2C12 MBs with decreased SAM knockdown despite the total level of Hec1 protein was largely unaltered. Altogether, the above results confirmed the importance of SAM/Sugt1 in the proper localization of kinetochore components. Lastly, to pinpoint it is the defective kinetochore assembly that mediates SAM KO phenotype, we found that knockdown of Dsn1 or Hec1 in SCs also delayed cell proliferation as assessed by a decreased percentage of EdU+ cells. AIM 3: To examine the effect of SAM deletion on dystrophic muscle and the effect of conditional deletion on muscle regeneration. To examine whether SAM loss may affect chronic injury-induced regeneration in DMD, we generated SAM; dystrophin double KO (dKO) mouse by crossing the SAM KO first mouse with mdx mouse. As expected, SAM expression was completely depleted in freshly sorted SCs of dKO vs. control (Ctrl) mdx mice. The dKO mouse displayed no overt difference from the Ctrl mouse with comparable body weight during the course of 27 weeks; TA and gastrocnemius (GAS) muscles also showed comparable weight at 8 weeks. However, when examined closely, smaller myofibers were more frequently observed in the TA muscles of 8 weeks old dKO mouse as measured by the cross-sectional area (CSA) of individual fiber (Fig. 3d). Moreover, histological examination revealed increased size of unrepaired areas (Fig. 3e), an increased number of eMyHC+ myofibers and increased infiltration of CD68+ macrophages in dKO mice, suggesting loss of SAM delays the muscle regeneration in limb muscles. Compared to limb muscles, mdx diaphragm (Dia) muscle is known to exhibit a more severe dystrophic phenotype manifested by fibrosis and fatty infiltration that worsens as mice age. Expectedly, the dKO mice at 6–8 months displayed the exacerbation of fibrosis as evidenced by increased Collagen I or Trichrome staining. Taken together, the above results suggest that loss of SAM aggravates dystrophic phenotype of mdx mice.

14106117.label: Major findings and research outcome
14106117.value: The functional study of lncRNAs in skeletal muscle satellite cells (SCs) remains at the infancy stage. Here we identify SAM (Sugt1 associated muscle) lncRNA that is enriched in the proliferating myoblasts. Global deletion of SAM has no overt effect on mice but impairs adult muscle regeneration following acute damage; it also exacerbates the chronic injury-induced dystrophic phenotype in mdx mice. Consistently, inducible deletion of SAM in SCs leads to deficiency in muscle regeneration. Further examination reveals that SAM loss results in a cell-autonomous defect in the proliferative expansion of myoblasts. Mechanistically, we find SAM interacts and stabilizes Sugt1, a co-chaperon protein key to kinetochore assembly during cell division. Loss of SAM or Sugt1 both disrupts kinetochore assembly in mitotic cells due to the mislocalization of two components: Dsn1 and Hec1. Altogether, our findings identify SAM as a regulator of SC proliferation through facilitating Sugt1 mediated kinetochore assembly during cell division. The findings have been published on Nat Commun. 2020 Jun 1;11(1):2725. A total of 10 publications have been generated with this funding acknowledged. We have also reported our findings on four international/local conferences and were well accepted by peer scientists from both fields of skeletal muscle regeneration and lncRNAs. Five PhD students and one Postdoc were trained under the support of this project. The leading person, Dr. Yuying Li, has landed an academic job at Shanghai Institute of Nutrition and Health, CAS as a Research Assistant Professor. Collaboration with an overseas group from UC Davis, USA was also established through the study.

14106117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14106117.value: Our study for the first time uncovers SAM as a novel regulator of SC function and muscle regeneration; it enhances our knowledge foundation in the intrinsic regulatory mechanisms underlying skeletal muscle regeneration for future therapeutic development of treating muscle damages and diseases. In the future, to further these findings, we plan to continue the investigation of Sugt1 in regulating SC activities. We speculate it has SAM independent functions in regulating SC activities, which thus warrants future efforts of investigation in the next chapter of the study. In addition, we also plan to continue to uncover other unknown lncRNAs that play key roles in regulating SC biology and explore their functional mechanisms.

14106117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14106117.value: Skeletal muscle is a form of striated muscle tissue which permits basic functions such as breathing and movement, accounting for ~40% of adult human body weight. Failure of skeletal muscle to develop prenatally leads to embryonic lethality, while the inability to repair or maintain skeletal muscle postnatally leads to a diminished quality of life and sometimes even death. Muscular dystrophy, cachexia, and sarcopenia are examples of deleterious muscle wasting conditions that are prevent in our society. Thus, the ability to regenerate diseased muscle has important medical implications. The cell responsible for muscle regeneration is the satellite cells (SC). The molecular mechanisms that integrate various extracellular signals and intrinsic control to establish the character of SCs during the regeneration are a matter of intense research. Here we have studied and for the first time revealed the function of SAM in promoting the regenerative capacity of SCs; it will thus enhance our knowledge foundation in the regulatory mechanisms underlying muscle regeneration for future therapeutic development of treating muscle damages and diseases.

14106717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14106717.value: Defecatory disorders affect 25% of the population, the incidence is rising and poses a major health care burden. Defecatory disorders are poorly diagnosed and treated. The lack of physiologically relevant and practical diagnostic tests for identifying the underlying mechanisms is a huge problem. Current diagnostic tests such as the balloon expulsion test, high-resolution anorectal manometry, defecography, and dynamic pelvic MRI are surrogates for the act of defecation and provide incomplete and often conflicting information. Not surprisingly results of these tests correlate poorly with symptoms and treatment outcomes. Our goal is to address the problem of mechanistic understanding of defecation in health and of defecatory disorders by using a novel electronic simulated stool, Fecobionics, a device for mapping the geometric and manometric profiles during defecation. Fecobionics has the consistency and shape of normal stools and it records pressures, distensibility, cross-sectional area and viscoelastic properties of the lumen and the walls. Our central hypothesis is that a novel, unique Fecobionics device that mimics natural defecation will provide new mechanistic insights regarding anorectal physiology when compared to current technology and facilitate development of new monitored home-based biofeedback treatments for these disorders. Our objectives are to address the significant gaps in knowledge and determine wirelessly and physiologically, the normal signatures of defecation in healthy subjects and in patients with chronic constipation. Our expected outcome is to characterize the normal and abnormal pressures, forces and topographic changes in the rectum and anal canal, during defecation in health and constipation, and to provide the ground work for developing biofeedback therapy for defecation disorders. The impact of our project is to test a safe, low cost, less invasive, low risk, radiation-free biomechatronics device and its ability to provide new knowledge and scientific basis for understanding defecation disorders and provide the knowledge-base for developing innovative biofeedback therapies that can be administered at home and monitored remotely by healthcare providers, thus improving diagnostic capabilities, treatment modalities and reduce costs of healthcare delivery. 大約25%的人群飽受排便功能障礙困擾，且這一情況並處上升趨勢，並為醫療保健帶來巨大負擔。目前排便功能異常診斷和治療上存在缺陷，其主要原因在於缺乏有效的生理檢測技術來探索其潛在生物機理。現有的排便功能檢測方法有：球囊排出法，高分辨率肛門直腸測壓法，排便造影術以及骨盆動態核磁共振成像法，但它們提供的信息不夠完整，不夠準確，因此導致不能真實地反映臨床症狀，影響治療效果。 我們設計該設備的目的在於從理解健康人士和排便障礙患者的生理機理上解決問題。該設備使用電子模擬排泄物(Fecobionics)來監測排便過程中的情況，並繪製相關的幾何壓力圖。該設備具有良好的連貫性，且能真實反映排泄物的形狀，所以可以很好地記錄肛門組織壁的相關壓力，擴張度，橫切面積和粘彈性。 相對於現有技術而言，我們的主要科學假設在於：新型而獨特的Fecobionics設備能夠很好地模擬自然排便過程，用全新的機械學視角來觀察肛門直腸的生理學特徵，此外該裝置還有利於家庭觀測反饋治療的發展。我們的目的是解決信息不對稱的鴻溝， 在無線技術和生理學技術基礎上測定健康人士和便秘患者的排便特徵。預期結果是希望揭示健康人士和便秘患者直腸和肛門內的壓力異常情況，以及力和形狀變化情況，更好的服務於排便障礙的生物反饋治療。該項目的優勢在於提供了一個安全，廉價，微創，低風險，無輻射的生物力學設備，對於更好理解排便障礙提供新的認識和科學依據，促進了適用於家庭和醫護控制監測的新型生物反饋治療技術的發展。故此也強化了診斷能力，豐富了治療手段，降低了醫療保健服務的成本。

14106917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14106917.value: 這項雙盲隨機試驗旨在將替代治療（前列腺素類似物和質子泵抑製劑[PPI]的聯合療法）與標準策略（PPI）進行比較，以預防患者的複發性潰瘍出血史特發性胃十二指腸潰瘍出血。 特發性胃十二指腸潰瘍出血是一種危及生命的疾病，全世界越來越重要。它常常導致復發性潰瘍出血和死亡率增加。目前，沒有有關預防這些患者復發性潰瘍出血的循證指南。由於在這些患者中經常觀察到胃酸性次氯酸鹽，單用PPI的酸抑制治療不能完全預防復發性潰瘍出血。 儘管PPI的療效不明確，但經常用於患有特發性胃十二指腸潰瘍出血史的患者，以預防復發性潰瘍出血。我們假設前列腺素類似物和PPI的聯合治療優於單獨的PPI，以預防特發性潰瘍出血史患者的複發性潰瘍出血。 這是一項為期兩年的雙盲，隨機對照試驗，米索前列醇與蘭索拉唑聯合單獨使用蘭索拉唑聯合治療患有特發性潰瘍出血史的患者。本研究將招募連續的特發性潰瘍出血患者。 246名患者的目標樣本量將以1：1的比例隨機分配，每天接受米索前列醇800微克24小時，聯合蘭索拉唑30毫克，每天一次，蘭索拉唑30毫克，每天一次。主要終點是複發性潰瘍出血。 這項研究將提供重要的一級證據來改變護理患有特發性潰瘍出血病史的醫生的臨床實踐。這將是首次隨機試驗，以比較米索前列醇聯合蘭索拉唑與蘭索拉唑單獨使用的功效，並將對臨床實踐產生影響。不幸的是，這個重要的臨床問題不是製藥公司的優先事項，因為結果可能不利於他們的產品。無論研究結果如何，這種行業獨立的臨床試驗將鼓勵衛生當局和國際指導委員會審查其對這一新興狀況的建議。

14106917.label: Major findings and research outcome
14106917.value: Lau LH, Ho KH, Chan FK, Cheong PK, Wong GL. Prevention of recurrent ulcer bleeding in patients with idiopathic gastroduodenal ulcer: misoprostol combined with lansoprazole versus lansoprazole alone: year 1 interim analysis of a double-blind randomized trial (NRT-MISO study). Gastroenterology 2021; 160(Supp 1):S62. DDW 2021 Abstract # 3521777 (Abstract selected for oral presentation in the Digestive Disease Week [DDW], 2021, the USA. Background & Aim: Patients with a history of idiopathic gastroduodenal ulcer bleeding, i.e. in the absence of Helicobacter pylori and drug history of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAID) and/or antiplatelet agents, have considerable risk of recurrence. Our previous randomized trial did not demonstrate any superiority of lansoprazole over famotidine for the prevention of rebleeding or endoscopic recurrence. We hypothesized that a combination of synthetic prostaglandin (misoprostol) and proton pump inhibitor (PPI, lansoprazole) is superior to PPI alone for prevention of recurrent ulcer bleeding in these patients. Methods: In this industry-independent, double-blind, randomized trial performed in a tertiary hospital in Hong Kong, we included patients with a history of idiopathic gastroduodenal ulcer bleeding. After confirmation of ulcer healing, an independent research staff randomly assigned patients in 1:1 ratio to receive 24 months of misoprostol 200micrograms four times daily combined with lansoprazole 30mg once daily, or placebo four times daily plus lansoprazole 30mg once daily. Both patients and investigators were blinded to the treatment allocation. The primary endpoint was recurrent gastroduodenal ulcer bleeding (defined as episodes of hematemesis, per-rectal bleeding and/or melena; or a drop in hemoglobin 2 g/dL; with endoscopic confirmation of ulcer and/or erosions) within 24 months. The secondary endpoints were any clinical gastrointestinal bleeding as defined according to the criteria stated above; and presence of recurrent peptic ulcer detected by the end-of-study endoscopy. The primary and secondary endpoints were analyzed in the intention-to-treat population. This study was registered in ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03675672). We reported the per-protocol blinded interim analysis of findings at Year 1. Results: Between March 2018 and November 2020, we enrolled a total of 121 patients, assigning 61 and 60 patients to each study group respectively. The cumulative incidence of reaching endpoints after 12 months was 0% (95%CI) in Arm A and 11.7% (95%CI) in Arm B (p= 0.003, crude hazard ratio, 95%CI; p=). Cumulative incidence of clinical gastrointestinal bleeding was 0% in Arm A and 5% in Arm B (p= 0.119). Endoscopic ulcer recurrence rate was 0% in Arm A and 3.3% in Arm B (p= 0.244). No treatment-related deaths occurred during the study period. There was no difference in the incidences grade 3-4 adverse events and serious adverse events in both treatment arms. Conclusions: The blinded interim analysis demonstrated a superiority of either combination therapy (misoprostol and lansoprazole) or PPI alone for the prevention of rebleeding and ulcer recurrence in patients with history of H. pylori–negative non-NSAID-related idiopathic gastroduodenal ulcers.

14108117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14108117.value: 肉質水果是人類和動物飲食的重要組成部分。隨著它們在不同的植物譜系中獨立演化，其成熟調控系統的多樣性在很大程度上是未知的。我們已經在不同的水果發育階段產生了10個肉質果實的初步DNA甲基化，開放的染色質和基因表達數據。我們建議使用比較基因組方法來研究果實成熟期間的表觀基因組動力學，以便全面了解其多樣化的調節系統。 我們使用甜瓜和香蕉轉錄因子的初步分析顯示，他們的成熟乙烯生產由不是MADS盒而是NAC和HB型轉錄因子控制，進一步證實了在不同植物物種中獨立演化的複雜調控系統的多樣性。因此，我們計劃使用這種煙草反式激活系統系統鑑定那些成熟調節因子，並進一步證實其生物學功能。

14108117.label: Realisation of objectives
14108117.value: We have successfully profiled the epigenome, transcriptome and chromatin accessibility changes during fruit development and ripening in different dry and fleshy fruit species. We have discovered 3 major routes for angiosperms to evolve the ethylene-dependent climacteric fruit ripening process, and the core genetic elements and epigenetic mechanisms for these are present in non-climacteric and even dry-fruited species. Eudicots with recent WGD like tomato, utilized their duplicated MADS to form a positive feedback loop with ethylene to regulate ripening, while eudicots without WGD repurposed the carpel senescence NAC. Banana has two positive feedback loops using both leaf senescence NAC and duplicated MADS, which enables it to bypass ethylene inhibitor treatment after ripening initiation. The findings have now been published in Nature Plants and Horticulture research.

14108117.label: Major findings and research outcome
14108117.value: Fleshy fruit is a classic example of convergent evolution and as they have developed independently multiple times in the history of the angiosperm, this already suggests that they could have evolved different mechanisms to achieve this. However, some of them, mainly those classified as climacteric fruits, utilize the same plant hormone ethylene to regulate ripening. Their ripening is associated with a burst of respiration, and most importantly, autocatalytic ethylene synthesis, which is necessary for ripening to initiate and progress. In all seven cases (tomato, apple, pear, melon, papaya, peach, and banana) that have been examined in the fruitENCODE project, the autocatalytic ethylene is produced by positive feedback loops formed between ethylene and the so-called “ripening TFs”. Many genes required for ripening are coupled directly to this autocatalytic feedback loop through these TFs, which are controlled by conserved tissue-specific H3K27me3 marks. We propose that evolving this strategy enable plants to control most if not all ripening genes through a few key TFs, which is efficient and could be of significant evolutionary advantage.

14108117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14108117.value: The lack of more diverse ripening circuits appears to suggest that the evolution of fruit ripening was constrained by some unknown factors, which could be the limited optimal signaling molecules and genetic and epigenetic materials in the carpel tissue. What we have observed might be the most optimized path(s) for plants to evolve a ripening fruit, which is to repurpose an existing carpel senescence gene, or use the duplicated floral organ identify genes. However, further investigations in more species are necessary in order to show whether other regulatory systems do exist.

14108117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14108117.value: The epigenome is an additional layer of heritable information superimposed on an organism’s DNA code. It is capable of maintaining cell-specific gene expression profiles and cell identities without the need of altering the DNA. An unknown cellular memory dictates the transition of a fruit from vegetative to reproductive growth and alters its responsiveness to the plant hormone ethylene. We found that timing of this transition coincides with a global epigenome reprograming targeting most gene promoters (DNA methylation) as well as genebody (H3K27me3). Our study suggest that evolution of ripening is constrained by limited hormone molecules and genetic and epigenetic materials, and whole-genome duplications have provided opportunities for plants to successfully circumvent these limitations.

14160817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14160817.value: Pyrrolizidine alkaloids (PAs) are widely present in plants and known to be toxic, especially hepatotoxic. PA poisoning is usually caused by the unaware consumption of PA-containing herbs/plants and PA-contaminated foodstuffs. Exposure to relatively high doses of PAs mainly causes acute hepatotoxicity, while, for relatively low-level PA exposure, acute hepatotoxic manifestations are often unapparent, but the resultant chronic diseases, such as liver cirrhosis, liver cancer and pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), may gradually develop. Unfortunately, due to the lack of specific and definitive diagnostic methods, the determination of whether these chronic diseases are directly caused, indirectly initiated, or exacerbated via PA exposure, is extremely challenging and currently unsatisfactory. Unlike acute hepaotoxicity, which is accompanied by obvious and characteristic syndromes, PA-induced chronic diseases have received little attention. For PA-induced PAH, current efforts are solely focusing on monocrotaline (MCT), a typical toxic PA. PAH is a life-threatening disease caused by various insults, such as MCT, with characteristics of progressive remodeling of the pulmonary vasculature and right heart failure at the late stage. Extensive studies have found that the biochemical mechanism initiating MCT-induced PAH involves the reactive metabolite (dehydro-PA) of MCT, which is generated in liver and can be transported into lung to interact with proteins. However, although it is well-established that all toxic PAs undergo the same hepatic metabolic activation to generate similar dehydro-PAs, it is unknown whether other toxic PAs also induce PAH. Nevertheless, two studies have demonstrated that several other PAs also caused pneumotoxicity in animals. Moreover, our preliminary data also revealed lung damage by retrorsine, another typical toxic PA, in rats. Although the available data are limited, they are supportive; together with the well-established common metabolic activation of different toxic PAs, it is reasonable to hypothesize that, in additional to hepatotoxicity, pneumotoxicity is also a common phenomenon for other toxic PAs. Therefore, considering the high risk of PA exposure from both PA-containing plant-derived natural products and PA-contaminated foodstuffs, it is significant and timely to study whether other toxic PAs can also produce pneumotoxicity. The present project aims to 1) systematically investigate potential pneumotoxicity of other representative PAs selected from different types and the disease progression of PA-induced pneumotoxicity; and 2) deliniate the common biochemical mechanisms that initiate the pneumotoxicity of different PAs. The results obtained will facilitate better understanding of PA-induced pulmonary diseases, and provide scientific evidences to enhance public awareness of the adverse effects/toxicities of PA exposure. 吡咯裡西啶類生物鹼（PA）廣泛存在於植物中，並可致多種毒性，尤其是肝毒性。PA中毒通常是由於服用含有PA的草藥或植物和PA污染的食物所致。攝入大劑量的PA會引起急性肝臟損傷，而長期攝入低劑量的PA雖無明顯的急性癥狀，但會逐步引起多種慢性毒性，如：肝硬化、肝癌和肺動脈高壓等。不幸的是，由於缺乏明確、特征的診斷方法，目前關於上述慢性病變是否由PA直接導致、間接引發或者協同其他因素進一步形成的研究仍十分有限，且極富挑戰。 不同於急性肝毒性具有明顯且特征性的臨床癥狀，PA引起慢性疾病的關註度較低。對於PA引起的肺動脈高壓，目前的研究僅局限於野百合鹼這一種有毒PA。肺動脈高壓是一種嚴重威脅生命的疾病，主要病理特征為進行性肺脈管重構，以及晚期的右心衰竭。該疾病可由多種因素誘發，比如野百合鹼。大量研究表明野百合鹼引起肺動脈高壓的生物化學機制包括：野百合鹼在肝臟中代謝激活並生成活性代謝產物（脫氢野百合鹼），此活性代謝產物可從肝臟中被轉運至肺部，並於肺部蛋白發生共價結合，形成吡咯-蛋白加合物從而引起肺毒性。實際上除了野百合鹼，所有有毒PA均會在肝臟種激活並形成類似的脫氢PA。然而，其他有毒PA是否也可引起肺動脈高壓卻很少有研究。目前，仅有兩篇報道提示其他PA可在實驗動物上導致肺部毒性。同時，我們的初步實驗也揭示：另一種毒性PA，倒千裏光鹼，也可以引起大鼠肺部損傷。盡管相關數據有限，但考慮到毒性PA在體內均有相同的代謝激活途徑，我們有理由假設：除了肝毒性，其他毒性PA亦可引起肺部損傷，這可能是毒性PA的共性。 因此，考慮到PA攝入的高風險性，例如通過攝入含PA植物衍生的天然產物以及被PA污染的食物，關於其他毒性PA是否亦可導致肺毒性的研究已十分迫切。因此本項目旨在系統地研究不同結構類型毒性PA的潛在肺毒性，以及他們引起肺毒性的病程進展，和闡明不同結構PA引起肺毒性的生化機制。預期取得的研究結果將有利於我們更好的理解PA引起的肺部疾病，並為公眾對PA引起毒副作用的認知提供科學依據。

14160817.label: Realisation of objectives
14160817.value: Pyrrolizidine alkaloids (PAs) are widely present in plants and known to be toxic, especially hepatotoxic. PA poisoning is usually caused by the unaware consumption of PA-containing herbs/plants and PA-contaminated foodstuffs. Exposure to relatively high doses of PAs mainly causes acute toxicity, in particular hepatotoxicity, while, for relatively low-level PA exposure, acute hepatotoxic manifestations are often unapparent, but the resultant chronic diseases, such as liver cirrhosis, liver cancer, and damage in other organs, such as lung toxicity may gradually develop. Unlike acute hepatotoxicity, which is accompanied by obvious and characteristic syndromes, PA-induced chronic diseases in different organs have received little attention. For PA-induced pneumotoxicity, only monocrotaline (MCT) has been studied. MCT causes pulmonary endothelial injury and vascular medial hypertrophy, eventually leading to pulmonary arterial hypertension and right ventricular failure. Although, the detailed mechanism underlying MCT-induced pneumotoxicity is unclear, the initial biochemical mechanism is suggested to be involved with the reactive metabolite (Dehydro-PA) of MCT, which is generated via metabolic activation mediated by cytochrome P450 enzymes (CYPs) and interacts with proteins to form pyrrole-protein adducts (PPAs) in the body. However, although all toxic PAs undergo the same metabolic activation to generate structurally similar Dehydro-PAs, it is unknown whether other PAs also induce pneumotoxicity. Therefore, we hypothesize that, in additional to hepatotoxicity, pneumotoxicity is also a common phenomenon of PAs. The present study aims to investigate whether other PAs can also induce pneumotoxicity and their underlying biochemical mechanisms with the following two objectives. To date, both objectives have been well accomplished. Objective 1—We firstly tested metabolic activation of four PAs of different types, namely monocrotaline (MCT), retrorsine (RTS) and riddelliine (RID) representing retronecine-type, and clivorine (CLI) representing otonecine-type, by in vitro study using rat liver or lung S9 incubation. All PAs produced PPAs significantly in rat liver S9 but negligible in lung S9 incubation, revealing that liver is the key organ responsible for metabolic activation generating Dehydro-PAs. Furthermore, using in vivo rat model, we tested organ toxicity of these four PAs plus two PAs: senecionine (SEN) and seneciphylline (SEP), which are present in herb Gynura segetum, a widely used PA-producing herb responsible for human PA poisonings in China. All six PAs induced pneumotoxicity in rats within 48 h after exposure. The results demonstrate that pneumotoxicity is a common phenomenon of PAs and the liver-derived Dehydro-PAs can move to the lungs and form PPAs, leading to pulmonary toxicity. Our findings have proved our hypothesis and confirmed that pneumotoxicity is also a common toxicity of PAs. Parts of our results have been reported in conferences and published (Paper 2 and Abstracts 1-2 in Part C). Objective 2—Using MCT, a pneumotoxic PA widely used to establish animal lung injury model, our study for delineating the mechanisms underlying PA-induced pneumotoxicity has been conducted in 3 different mice models, i.e. conditional deletion of the cytochrome P450 reductase (Cpr) gene and resultant tissue-selective ablation of CYPs activities to have 1) liver-speciﬁc Cpr-null mice model, 2) extrahepatic Cpr-low mice model, and 3) wild-type mice model. The results demonstrated that after oral exposure to MCT, liver-speciﬁc Cpr-null mice, but not extrahepatic Cpr-low mice, had signiﬁcantly lower level of PPAs in the serum, liver, and lungs compared with wild-type mice, while signiﬁcantly higher blood concentration of the intact MCT was fund in liver-speciﬁc Cpr-null mice compared to extrahepatic Cpr-low and wild-type mice. Furthermore, MCT-induced pneumotoxicity was observed in wild-type and extrahepatic Cpr-low mice but not liver-speciﬁc Cpr-null mice, and Dehydro-PAs of MCT have been confirmed to exist in the blood efflux from the hepatic veins of MCT-exposed rats. Our findings provide the first mode-of-action evidence in that hepatic CYPs are essential for the bioactivation of PAs to generate Dehydro-PAs, and Dehydro-PAs move along with blood circulation from the liver to the lungs and then covalently bind with functional proteins to form PPAs in the lungs causing pneumotoxicity. Similarly, using mice with tissue-selective ablation of CYPs activity, we also confirmed for the first time that hepatic CYPs, but not intestinal CYPs, were essential for metabolic bioactivation of PAs, and the liver-derived Dehydro-PAs were transported by bile into the intestine followed by the interaction with intestinal proteins to form PPAs leading to enterotoxicity. On the other hand, Dehydro-PAs circulating in the blood have been determined by the detection of pyrrole-GSH adducts via the addition of glutathione (GSH) into the blood to trap Dehydro-PAs. In addition, Dehydro-PAs (which are generated by metabolic activation mediated by hepatic CYPs in the liver) in blood circulation has been proved to be covalently bound to albumin and red blood cells (RBCs) to form pyrrole−albumin adducts and pyrrole−hemoglobin (Hb) adducts, respectively. Pyrrole−Hb adducts with remarkably high level in blood and long-life span have been developed as a suitable biomarker of PA exposure. Parts of these results have been reported in conferences and published (Papers 1, 3-4 and Abstracts 1, 3-5 in Part C). In addition, a few more manuscripts reporting our findings with detailed biochemical, histological, and pathological changes in PA-induced lung injury and the related molecular and biochemical mechanisms are currently under preparation.

14160817.label: Major findings and research outcome
14160817.value: Our findings for the first time provide solid evidence and comprehensive information on PA-induced pneumotoxicity. Firstly, by studying six well-known hepatotoxic PAs (including two PAs present in Gynura segetum, a widely used PA-containing herb responsible for human PA poisonings in China) representing retronecine-type and otonecine-type PAs in rat model, we discovered that all PAs caused lung injury evidenced by biochemical and histological examinations in all PA-treated rats. Further, using MCT as a representative PA to investigate PA-induced pneumotoxicity, impaired systemic oxygen-carrying capacity and hypoxia were found in PA-induced lung injury. Secondly, the liver, but not the lungs, was confirmed as the primary site of metabolic activation to form structurally similar reactive metabolites, Dehydro-PAs, of all tested PAs in both in vitro rat liver and lung S9 incubations and in vivo different mice models. Parts of the results have been reported in conferences and published (Paper 2 and Abstracts 1-2 in Part C). Thirdly, the mechanism underlying PA-induced pneumotoxicity has been delineated for the first time in that the formation of Dehydro-PAs by hepatic CYPs-mediated metabolic activation in the liver was the essential first step, followed by blood circulation of Dehydro-PAs from the liver to the lungs and then covalently bind with proteins to form PPAs in the lungs causing pneumotoxicity. Evidently, our results demonstrated that Dehydro-PAs were present in blood circulation, and transportation of Dehydro-PAs via blood circulation was a common phenomenon for all PAs and the initial biochemical mechanism of PA-induced pneumotoxicity. All results confirmed that both retronecine-type and otonecine-type PAs can commonly induce pneumotoxicity. Fourthly, the significant changes in morphology of RBCs due to their interaction with Dehydro-PAs to form pyrrole−Hb adducts and the resultant hypoxia were observed in PA-treated rats, demonstrating Dehydro-PAs-induced RBCs dysfunction. Fifthly, on the other hand, pyrrole−Hb adducts demonstrated significantly high concentration and long persistence in the blood, and thus, have been developed as a specific biomarker of PA exposure for clinical test. Sixthly, the first evidence of PA-induced enterotoxicity was also discovered due to the similar metabolic activation mediated by hepatic CYPs to form Dehydro-PAs followed by their transportation via bile into the intestine and then the formation of PPAs to exert enterotoxicity. Parts of the results have been reported in conferences and published (Papers 1, 3-4 and Abstracts 1-5 in Part C). Further, a few more manuscripts reporting the above-mentioned findings are currently under preparation for future publication.

14160817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14160817.value: Our findings for the first time provide a comprehensive information on PA-induced pneumotoxicity and demonstrate that such toxicity can be induced commonly by different PAs. Our findings extend the understanding of biochemical mechanism and pathogenesis of PA-induced pneumotoxicity. However, the detailed molecular mechanism underlying PA-induced pneumotoxicity has not been fully delineated, and therefore further in-depth mechanistic investigations are warranted to provide insight into the development of possible therapeutic strategies for prevention and treatment of PA-induced lung diseases. Furthermore, our identification of PPAs gives a novel insight for further understanding of molecular mechanism of PA-induced toxicities in different organs, and our developed pyrrole-Hb adducts as a specific biomarker of PA exposure is also worth to be further investigated on clinical samples to confirm its future applicable clinical test for the diagnosis of PA poisoning patients. In addition, our study confirms that PA-induced pneumotoxicity is a common phenomenon for different PAs, and thus reveals that there may be a potential risk of PA-induced toxicity, not only hepatoxicity but also pneumotoxicity, via consumption of PA-containing natural products and PA-contaminated foodstuffs in our daily life. Therefore, the public health education on avoiding intake of PA-containing herbs and/or dietary supplements for self-health care is warranted.

14160817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14160817.value: Pyrrolizidine alkaloids (PAs) are natural toxins widely present in ~3% flowering plants worldwide. Humans are readily exposed to PAs by ingestion of PA-containing herbal products, or PA-contaminated foodstuffs. PAs are well-known to cause liver toxicity with typical symptoms of hepatomegaly, jaundice, and ascites. Our new findings demonstrate that PAs can also cause lung toxicity with typical symptoms of pulmonary arterial hypertension and hypoxia, although the current knowledge on disease progression of PA-induced lung toxicity and potential therapeutic treatment is limited. Our findings for the first time delineate the initial biochemical mechanism of PA-induced lung toxicity via similar reactive metabolites, called Dehydro-PAs, generated from structurally different PAs in the liver. Dehydro-PAs move with blood circulation, bind with proteins in red blood cells (RBCs), and cause morphological changes and decrease oxygen carrying capability of RBCs, resulting in hypoxia. Dehydro-PAs also move from the liver to the lungs and then interact with proteins in the lungs to cause lung toxicity. Our studies demonstrate that PA-induced lung toxicity is a common phenomenon for different PAs, and thus, there may be a potential risk of PA-induced lung toxicity via consumption of PA-containing natural products and PA-contaminated foodstuffs in our daily life.

14160917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14160917.value: Distraction osteogenesis (DO) is a surgical technique applying controlled gradual traction to regenerate musculoskeletal tissues. During DO process bone is formed and remodeled rapidly with advanced angiogenesis and upregulated gene expressions. DO is now widely employed in the treatment of limb length discrepancy, nonunion, and bone defects. However, patients undergoing DO procedure often need to endure a long treatment duration for bone consolidation. Many methods have been studied to enhance bone consolidation, however, due to the high cost and complicated procedures, a few methods are widely accepted clinically. Simple and cost effective approaches to augment bone consolidation during DO and to shorten the treatment duration are still in great need. The use of biomaterials for augmenting bone formation is a promising approach, but the use of biomaterials in DO has not been well studied. We recently found that biomaterials combined with DO technique could significantly enhance bone formation/consolidation process and reduce the treatment duration. We hypothesize that the applications of implantable or injectable biomaterials during DO, may enhance bone formation and consolidation in DO procedure. The planned investigations in this proposal are: (1) Test the effects of physical shapes (solid vs. cylindrical form) of macroporous poly(ε-caprolactone)-β-tricalcium phosphate (PCL-β-TCP) scaffolds on bone formation during DO treatment in a rat femur bone defect model. (2) Test the use of hydrogel functionalized with N-cadherin mimetic peptide (N-cadherin hydrogel) with or without rat bone marrow derived MSCs (rBMSCs) on bone formation during DO treatment in a rat femur bone defect model. (3) Test the effects of applying injectable polycaprolactone (PCL) or hydroxyapatites (HA)-PCL microspheres at the bone regenerate site on bone consolidation in a rat DO model. This study will clarify whether the use of biomaterials in combination with DO technique would be a cost-effective method to enhance bone formation and consolidation. The findings will have translational potentials in that the combined use of HA-TCP or hydrogel based biomaterials together with DO procedure may significantly reduce the treatment time for larger bone segment defects; local injection of HA-PCL based microspheres could be a simple and effective approach to augment bone consolidation in DO treatment. 牽引成骨（DO）是一種應用受控逐漸牽引以再生肌肉骨骼組織的手術技術. 在DO過程中, 骨骼組織形成迅速，並伴有豐富的血管形成生和各種成骨基因表達上調. DO現在廣泛應用於治療肢體長度差異，不癒合和骨缺損. 然而, 進行DO手術的患者通常需要忍受長時間的外固定以等待新生骨的礦化. 許多現有的增強骨礦化方法, 由於成本高昂和程式複雜, 臨床上難以廣泛使用. 開發在DO期間增強骨礦化，縮短治療時間的簡單和有效的方法仍然是非常需要的. 使用生物材料來增加骨形成是一種有希望的方法, 但在DO中使用生物材料尚未得到很好的研究. 我們最近發現生物材料結合DO技術可以顯著增強骨形成/礦化過程, 可減少治療時間. 我們假設使用植入式或可注射生物材料在DO期間可以增強DO新生骨形成和礦化。本研究的目標是: （1）在大鼠股骨骨缺損和DO模型中, 測試大孔聚己內酯-β-磷酸三鈣（PCL-β-TCP）支架的形態（固體與中空圓柱形）對DO骨形成的影響.（2）在大鼠股骨骨缺損模型中，在DO治療期間，測試使用載有或不載有大鼠骨髓來源的間充質幹細胞, 複合N-鈣粘蛋白模擬肽功能化的水凝膠, 對骨形成和礦化的作用. （3）在大鼠DO模型中測試在骨再生部位應用可注射聚己內酯（PCL）或羥基磷灰石（HA –PCL）微球對骨礦化的影響.

14160917.label: Realisation of objectives
14160917.value: 1. Test the effects of physical shapes (solid vs. cylindrical form) of macroporous poly(ε-caprolactone)-β-tricalcium phosphate (PCL-β-TCP) scaffolds on bone formation during DO treatment in a rat femur bone defect model. β-tricalcium phosphate (β-TCP) was fabricated into no tubular, single tubular, or multi-tubular structure constructs. The microstructure of the three types of β-TCP constructs was determined by scanning electron microscope. Unilateral tibial osteotomy (1 cm in length) with an external distraction fixator was performed in each New Zealand White Rabbit. After acute shortening of 0.5 cm, the defect site was implanted with β-TCP constructs with no tubular, single tubular, or multi-tubular structure. Five days after osteotomy, the tibia was lengthened at 0.5 mm/12 h for 5 days. After 28 days of consolidation, the animals were subjected to X-ray imaging and then sacrificed. Bilateral tibial specimens were harvested for micro-computed tomography analysis, four-point bending mechanical test, and histology analysis. Results showed that similar appropriate pore sizes and interconnected pores could be found in all the three types of β-TCP constructs. 38 days after surgery, results showed that new bone formation was significantly promoted and mechanical properties were significantly enhanced in the animals implanted with multi-tubular constructs as well as single tubular constructs, comparing with those implanted with no tubular constructs. Furthermore, the animals implanted with multi-tubular constructs showed higher mechanical properties comparing with those implanted with single tubular ones. 2. Test the use of hydrogel functionalized with N-cadherin mimetic peptide with or without rat bone marrow derived MSCs (rBMSCs) on bone formation during DO treatment in a rat femur bone defect model. We have followed our previous published protocol and fabricated the N-cadherin hydrogel as planned. We have then carried out a pilot animal experiment to exam the effects of using N-cadherin hydrogel with or without rBMSCs during DO treatment in a rat DO model . The preliminary data showed that BMSCs adhered well on the hydrogel in cell culture. However, when applying the hydrogel in vivo, we observed inhibitory effects on bone formation during the DO process, which was unexpected and we concluded the hydrogel we have manufactured had inhibitory effects on bone formation, therefore we decided to use an alternative injectable gel as source to carry out the test. A bioactive injectable material (BIM) was developed to improve the outcome. Naturally-derived polymer (gelatin) composed of bioactive silicate-nanodisk (Laponite) was crosslinked with natural-origin genipin. The BIM features with a sustainable linear release of osteoinductive components (Mg, Li and Si ions) and linear biodegradability upon the gradual tensile loading during DO procedure. BIM promoted the proliferation and osteogenic differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) in vitro. By using rat DO model, single injection of MSCs-laden BIM during distraction phase could augment the healing quality as indicated by increased bone mineralization (by micro-CT and bone dynamic histomorphometry assessments), bone strength (by mechanical test) and blood vessels formation (by immunohistochemical staining). The special design of this novel injectable material together with co-injected MSCs, provides a novel strategy to reconstruct favorable microenvironment for bone regeneration, unreached by the traditional methods (using growth factors like BMP-2, VEGF with high cost and un-stability limitations), which provides insight into the development of a promising translatable biomaterial-enhanced distraction osteogenesis strategy. 3. Test the effects of applying injectable polycaprolactone (PCL) or hydroxyapatites (HA)-PCL microspheres at the bone regenerate site on bone consolidation in a rat DO model. Here, we investigated whether the application of polycaprolactone (PCL) and hydroxyapatite (HA) composite microspheres could enhance bone formation in DO. Pure PCL microspheres and composite PCL and 10% HA microspheres were synthesized. Bone mesenchymal stem cells isolated from green fluorescent protein rats (GFP-rBMSCs) were cultured with microspheres in a rotary bioreactor system. Scanning electron microscopy was used to examine the microstructures. Osteogenic differentiation of rBMSCs was confirmed. Moreover, PCL/HA (20 mg) and PCL (20 mg) were locally administered into the distraction gap in rat DO model towards to the end of distraction period. Imaging detection, mechanical and histological examinations were performed to assess the quality of 4-week regenerates. Results showed that the microspheres were of uniform size and monodisperse. After incubation with rBMSCs in culture, PCL/HA microspheres showed better ability of cell adhesion and osteogenic differentiation comparing to PCL microspheres. In vivo, bone volume/total tissue volume, bone mineral density, and mechanical properties of new callus were significantly higher in the PCL/HA group compared to PCL group. Histological analyses confirmed improved bone formation and vascularization in PCL/HA group. We presented an effective protocol for the generation of functionalized microspheres and demonstrated implantation of PCL/HA microspheres into the distraction regenerate could significantly enhance bone consolidation. Thus, application of PCL/HA composite microspheres may be a novel approach for promoting bone regeneration.

14160917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14160917.value: Distraction Osteogenesis (DO) is a widely used surgical procedure for limb lengthening, deformity correction, and management of segmental bone defects. However, delayed bone consolidation and resultant poor healing quality remains an unsolved clinical problem, which hampered the wider clinical application of DO. We have here developed a new type of biomaterials with a combination of physical and chemical cross-linked structures to be used to aid bone formation in DO. We carried out in vitro and in vivo tests, showed that these novel biomaterials together with the loaded bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs), could cooperatively enhance bone formation and improve bone quality during the consolidation phase of DO. The combined application of BMSCs and the biomaterials revealed synergistic effects in enhancing both angiogenesis and osteogenesis during DO, which may be a promising bioactive material-guided therapeutic approach in enhancing bone formation and consolidation in DO. For future development, we will seek collaboration to commercialize our biomaterials. We will continue to promote our findings of this study to wider publics and medical users, and seek for future clinical trails in Hong Kong and China.

14161017.label: Project Objectives
14161017.value: Detect and compare the prevalence of a full spectrum of HPV infection in the head and neck region with or without squamous cell carcinoma. We hypothesize that, besides of alpha high-risk papillomaviruses, certain types/species of beta- and gamma-papillomaviruses make contributions to the development of HNSCC. We will genotype and compare oral HPVs including α-, β- and γ-types in head and neck tissues using Next-Gen sequencing to assess the roles of HPV in the development of HNSCC. Interrogate the contributions of oral microbiome dysbiosis to (i) the infection and genotype of HPVs and (ii) the development of HNSCC. We hypothesize that oral microbiome or microbial gene compositions differs in risk of developing HPV-associated HNSCC. We will perform a metagenomics-wide association study and 16S rRNA gene sequencing to identify microbial metagenomics marker(s) related to HPV infection and HNSCC development. Characterize the human epigenetic changes of global and CpG site-specific methylation loci and TP53 mutation in the head and neck region and their association with (i) oral microbiome dysbiosis, (ii) HPV infection and (iii) HNSCC development. We hypothesize that host genomic DNA hyper- and hypo-methylation vary in the development of different groups of HNSCC and are a consequence of pathogenic microorganism perturbation. We will compare the genome-wide methylation profile between HNSCC and the adjacent normal tissue, and quantitate human genomic DNA CpG site-specific methylation and TP53 mutation to assess their relationships to oral microorganism dysbiosis and HNSCC development.

14161017.label: Realisation of objectives
14161017.value: Objective 1: Through the completion of this project, we have successfully recruited 166 patients with head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), including 106 oral cavity SCC, 24 larynx SCC, 15 oropharynx SCC, 13 hypopharynx SCC, and 8 others (3 nasal cavity SCC, 4 paranasal sinus, 1 metastasis). Tumor tissue, adjacent normal tissue, and oral rinse from HNSCC patients were collected. Meanwhile, we have recruited 59 patients with benign head and neck lesions for the collection of biopsy and oral rinse samples. No HPV DNA was detected in patients with benign head and neck lesions, while the overall prevalence of HPV infection in the surveyed HNSCC cohort was 15.7%, with variable infection rates highest in oropharynx (66.7%), followed by larynx (16.7%), nasal (12.5%), and oral cavity (10.4%). Univariable and multivariable factors analysis found that HPV infection was associated with non-oral cavity SCC subtype, a later N stage, and an improved disease-specific survival. We reported our findings in two international conferences, and one manuscript is under review: • Jason Y. K. Chan, Man Kit Cheung, Linlin Lan, Siaw Shi Boon, Robert D. Burk, Paul K. S. Chan, Zigui Chen. “The oral microbiota and HPV involvement in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma from an Asian cohort”. Under review. Objective 2: We optimized microbiota 16S rRNA gene PCR amplicon next-generation sequencing assays and bioinformatics pipelines, and have profiled the human oral microbiota in HNSCC. We compared the differentially abundant bacterial communities between tumor cases and controls, and found that oral microbiota dysbiosis was associated with HNSCC. Changes in composition and the relative abundance of oral microbes in HNSCC was also associated with cancer subtype, T stage, survival/relapse, HPV infection and smoking. A panel of discriminative bacteria genera was identified, including two bacterial genera (Fusobacterium and Peptostreptococcus) to be consistently increased in relative abundances both in HNSCC tumor tissues and oral rinses, whereas ten taxa (Streptococcus, Neisseria, Rothia, Actinomyces, Granulicatella, Oribacterium, Lautropia, Corynebacterium, Abiotrophia, and Cardiobacterium) were significantly decreased. These bacteria may serve as marker for cancer prediction and diagnostics, and may also have a potential in the pathogenesis of HNSCC. In specific, Fusobacterium is the most predominant pathogenetic bacteria in HNSCC, and was further associated with non-smoking, early T and N stages, and better 3-year disease-specific survival. The findings underscore the increased impact of oral microbiota dysbiosis in HNSCC patients lacking traditional risk factors. Understanding the complex interactions between oral microbiota, HPV infection and other risk factors will provide important insights into the pathogenesis of HNSCC for formulating better strategies of disease intervention and patient management. We also investigated the dynamics of the oral microbiome and associated patient outcomes following treatment of HNSCC. There was a significantly depressed alpha diversities of oral microbial communities observed in HNSCC oral rinse samples within the first 6 months post-surgery when compared to pre-surgery or healthy controls. Following treatment, eight oral bacterial genera showed a trend towards the restoration in the relative abundances that approximate healthy persons. The decreased relative abundance of three periodontal bacteria (Capnocytophaga, Prevotella 7, and Leptotrichia) and the increased relative abundance of two commensal bacteria (Streptococcus and Rothia) at 6 months post-surgery compared to pre-surgery showed a better 3-year disease-specific survival. Our findings indicate that the dynamics of the oral microbiome postsurgery are associated with patient treatment and outcomes, and may serve as potential biomarkers for patient management in HNSCC treatment. We reported our findings in five international conferences. Three papers have been published, and one manuscript is under review. • Chen Z, Hui PC, Hui M, Yeoh YK, Wong PY, Chan MCW, Wong MCS, Ng SC, Chan FKL, Chan PKS. “Impact of Preservation Method and 16S rRNA Hypervariable Region on Gut Microbiota Profiling.” mSystems 2019;4(1) doi: 10.1128/mSystems.00271-18. • Chan JYK, Ng CWK, Lan L, Fung S, Li JW, Cai L, Lei P, Mou Q, Meehan K, Lau EHL, Yeung Z, Chan KCA, Wong EWY, Chan PKS, Chen Z. “Restoration of the Oral Microbiota After Surgery for Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma Is Associated With Patient Outcomes.” Front Oncol 2021;11:737843. doi: 10.3389/fonc.2021.737843. • Cheung MK, Chan JYK, Wong MCS, Wong PY, Lei P, Cai L, Lan L, Ho WCS, Yeung ACM, Chan PKS, Chen Z. “Determinants and Interactions of Oral Bacterial and Fungal Microbiota in Healthy Chinese Adults.” Microbiol Spectr 2022;10(1):e0241021. doi: 10.1128/spectrum.02410-21. • Man Kit Cheung, Sylvia L. Y. Tong, Martin C. S. Wong, Jason Y. K. Chan, Margaret Ip, Mamie Hui, Christopher K. C. Lai, Rita W. Y. Ng, Wendy C. S. Ho, Apple C. M. Yeung, Paul K. S. Chan and Zigui Chen. “Extent of Oral-gut Transmission of Bacterial and Fungal Microbiota in Healthy Chinese Adults.” Under review. Objective 3: We hypothesize that host-microbiota maladaptation play an important role in the pathogenesis of HNSCC. Tumor and adjacent normal tissues from 89 oral cavity SCC (OSCC) patients without HPV infection were analyzed for mucosal bacterial community, host genome-wide transcriptome and DNA CpG methylation to profile the complex network between bacteria and host genetic/epigenetic events. Dysbiosis of the oral microbiota was observed in OSCC, with nine bacteria genera (Fusobacterium, Treponema 2, Selenomonas, Peptostreptococcus, Catonella, Johnsonella, Peptococcus, Paludibacteraceae F0058 and Clostridiales FamilyXIII UCG001) significantly enriched in tumor microenvironment. These tumor-enriched bacteria formed positive correlations with 362 up-regulated host genes that involved pathways related to cell adhesion, migration, division, signaling and proliferation. An integrative analysis between bacteria-transcriptome and bacteria-methylation found that thirty-two dysregulated host genes with inverse CpG methylation in their promoter regions, such as the tumor suppressor genes AOX1 and PITX1 and the oncogenes DBF4B and IRS1, were significantly associated with the enrichment of pathogenetic bacteria, implying a potential of bacteria colonization in gene expression, in part through epigenetic alterations. An in vitro model by co-culturing F. nucleatum into the healthy immortalized oral epithelial cell confirmed 27 up- and 16 down-regulated host genes, including LAMA3, INHBA and SNAI2, three hallmark genes of epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT), were associated with bacterial colonization, implying that F. nucleatum may contribute to cellular invasion via crosstalk with E-cadherin/b-catenin signaling, TNFa/NF-kB pathway and extracellular matrix remodeling in OSCC.
