14161017.label: Major findings and research outcome
14161017.value: This funded project has directly generated 4 peer-reviewed publications in international journals (mSystems, Cancers, Frontiers in Oncology, Microbiology Spectrum). Three manuscripts on HPV, microbiota, and host-microbiota interactions are under review. We have also reported our findings in 7 international conferences in fields of HPV, human microbiota, and cancer. Meanwhile, this project provided the training opportunities for one PhD and one MPhil postgraduate students. In addition, the PI and co-PIs have established collaborations with local and oversea scientists in field of oral cancer and human microbiota. • Using optimized next-generation sequencing HPV genotyping assays, we identified high HPV infection rate in oropharynx SCC. HPV infection in oropharynx SCC was linked to a later N stage and an improved disease-specific survival. • Oral microbiota dysbiosis was observed in HNSCC, with differentially abundant communities mainly associated with HNSCC subtype, T stage, survival/relapse, HPV infection and smoking. The findings underscore the increased impact of oral microbiota dysbiosis in HNSCC patients lacking traditional risk factors. • A taxonomically defined microbial consortium associated with HNSCC was identified that may have clinical potential regarding biomarkers for early detection or intervention. • We observed significant enrichment of pathogenic oral bacteria in HNSCC tumor microenvironment, suggesting that oral microbiota dysbiosis may play a role in the pathogenesis of HNSCC. • An integrative analysis between bacteria-transcriptome and bacteria-methylation found significant association between bacteria enrichment, host gene expression and DNA methylation, implying a potential of bacteria colonization in gene expression, in part through epigenetic alterations. • A bacterial co-culture cell model in vitro confirmed that F. nucleatum may contribute to cellular invasion via crosstalk with E-cadherin/b-catenin signaling, TNFa/NF-kB pathway and extracellular matrix remodelling in OSCC.

14161017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14161017.value: Although our work has characterized comprehensive interactions between human oral microbiota, host genetic and epigenetic events, HPV infection and other clinical variables contributing to the pathogenesis of HNSCC, most of findings reveal correlations but not causality of oral microbiota in HNSCC tumorigenesis. Further studies using in vivo and in vitro models will be helpful to identify specific microbiota-host connections underlying the mechanism. We will devote our efforts in these areas in the near future by applying for new fund and establishing new collaborations with multidisciplinary teams. Our ultimate goal is to fill in knowledge gaps on the host-microbiota interactions that underlie oncogenic mechanisms in oral cancer for formulating more effective preventative and interventional strategies to control this fatal cancer.

14161017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14161017.value: Head and neck cancer is the 6th leading cancer by incidence worldwide. There is no currently accepted screening test to detect premalignant conditions or HNSCC at an early stage, hence, the 5-year survival rate is poor, resulting in high mortality and morbidity rates. In this project, we applied multi-omics approaches to reveal a complex network between oral mucosal microbiota, host gene dysregulation, DNA methylation, HPV infection and other risk factors in the pathogenesis of oral cancer. We identified several bacteria significantly enriched in cancer. We found enriched functions related to various cancer-related pathways such as immune response and inflammation. We confirmed high-risk HPV infection in oropharynx SCC. These findings expand our understanding of host-microbiota interactions in HNSCC tumorigenesis, which provides important insights into genetic and functional basis as potential diagnostic markers and therapeutic targets for formulating more effective preventative and interventional strategies to control this morbid cancer.

14161317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14161317.value: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is among the top ten most common cancers in Hong Kong. For patients with recurrent or metastatic disease that are not amenable to local treatment such as radiotherapy or surgery, the prognosis is very poor and response to chemotherapy is not very durable for the majority of patients. Immunotherapy is a promising treatment for NPC because it is closely related to the Epstein Barr virus infection, and the ability of NPC cancer cells in evading the patient's host immune system is one of the cardinal features of NPC. Nivolumab is a highly promising form of immunotherapy, which is a fully human IgG antibody against the Programmed-cell death (PD-1) signaling pathway. Nivolumab belongs to a class of immune checkpoint inhibitors that have shown unprecedented responses in melanoma and durable responses in lung and head and neck (non-NPC) cancers. Our group and others have generated preclinical data which supported the development of the first phase II international, multicenter study of nivolumab in recurrent and metastatic NPC involving 45 oncology centers from Hong Kong, Singapore and USA. This study is an investigator-initiated study led by the Principal Investigator from CUHK, Brigette Ma in collaboration with the Mayo Clinic Phase II Consortium, and sponsored by the National Cancer Institute (NCI), Bethesda, USA. The study has completed enrollment and clinical responses have been observed. Blood and archived tumor samples have been prospectively collected from the enrolled patients as part of a planned correlative study on biomarkers of response to PD-1 inhibitor. With the recent discovery of some new genetic alterations based on the whole exome and genome analyses of NPC by some of our investigators, it is primetime to evaluate the prognostic and predictive utility of some key candidate biomarkers these samples. This study is a systematic evaluation of the most promising candidate biomarkers of response to PD-1 inhibitors, ranging from expression of T-cells and immune checkpoint mediators in the tumor and its microenvironment, plasma EBV DNA clearance, and selected genetic alterations in antigen presentation and interferon gamma receptor associated gene. Since the USA NCI’s sponsorship is restricted to providing only the study drug for the clinical trial and there is no funding for the correlative studies, we seek the RGC’s consideration for support for this important study. The evaluation of predictive markers for nivolumab has tremendous clinical significance in individualizing immunotherapy for patients with NPC or other cancers. 鼻咽癌是香港十大最常見癌症之一。復發性鼻咽癌的前景很差。來自香港中文大學的馬碧如教授成功率領和完成了一項首次及國際性的第II期臨床研究, 運用一種新的免疫治療, 稱Nivolumab (免疫檢查點抑製劑）。這個國際研究由美國國家癌症研究中心（National Cancer Institute, Bethesda, USA）贊助。本研究將調查幾種重要的生物標誌的臨床效用.

14162117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14162117.value: 目的: 這項研究目的在提供充分數據，以支持研發新一代安全及有效對抗人類乳頭狀瘤病毒（HPV）相關癌症的標靶治療，並增加對HPV癌蛋白E6如何通過Aurora B激酶驅動致癌作用的了解。 背景: 感染人乳頭狀瘤病毒是導致多種癌症（包括子宮頸癌，口咽癌，陰道癌，外陰癌和陰莖癌）的重要因素。雖然接種HPV疫苗可以預防HPV感染，但疫苗對某些HPV相關癌症（如口咽癌）的療效尚未得到證實。此外，實施大規模疫苗接種計劃的實際障礙仍難以解決。因此，研發更有效的標靶治療對於治療HPV相關癌症有著迫切的需要。 Aurora激酶已知在多種類型癌症的形成起了關鍵作用，最常見於結直腸癌和肺癌。過去報告顯示Aurora也可能導致HPV相關癌症，而我們的初步研究亦顯示，由高危HPV類型的E6癌蛋白與Aurora有密切關係，能導致癌變。鑑於現時只有極少量的Aurora抑制劑進入臨床試驗，若希望作進一步的臨床研究，並使其發展為更好的標靶治療，我們迫切需要去描述及深入了解Aurora在導致HPV相關癌症的角色作用。 研究方向: 為探索治療HPV相關癌症的新方法，本研究方案著重於兩種蛋白質–HPV-E6和Aurora激酶，及其二者與致癌作用的關係。這項研究期望能証實Aurora抑制劑或E6-Aurora B複合阻滯劑的安全性及治療HPV相關癌症的效用。這些數據將有助於提高患者的生存率，及能患者提供標靶治療的新選擇。

14162117.label: Realisation of objectives
14162117.value: All Objectives of this project were achieved. The followings are the key findings. Please refer to the attached manuscript for details of the experimental data and illustrations of the results. (1). Objective 1 - From in-vitro binding, co-immunoprecipitation, and immunofluorescence assays, we identified for the first time that Aurora kinase B is a genuine binding partner of E6-encoded by HPV16 and 18: - a) Aurora B activity was increased in HPV-positive cells: We examined total cell lysates from HeKa (HPV-null primary human keratinocytes), C33A (HPV-null human cervical cancer cells), HeLa (HPV18-positive cervical cancer cells) and CaSki (HPV16-positive cervical cancer cells), by western blotting. We observed a dramatic increase in the level of total AurB, as well as phosphorylated AurB in HPV-positive cells. The level of phosphorylated Aurora kinase A was unchanged, while the phospho-Aurora C levels were reduced in CaSki cells. - b) Aurora B expression correlated positively with HPVE6: This observation was confirmed by (i) Overexpression of HPV oncoproteins in HPV-null cells; and (ii) Depletion of HPV oncoproteins in HPV-positive cells. - c) AurB co-immunoprecipitated with HPVE6, but not HPVE7: We immunoprecipitated E6 and E7 from cell extracts using HA-conjugated agarose resin and examined the bound AurB via western blotting. AurB bound to HA-HPV16E6, but not to HA-HPV16E7. We also detected AurB bound to HA-HPV18E6 in HEK293 cells. The results indicate that AurB interacts with both E6-encoded HPV16 and 18 in HEK293 cells, but not with E7. - d) E6-encoded by HPV16 and 18 bound directly to AurB: The results were obtained from in vitro binding assay with GST-tagged E6 fusion proteins encoded by HPV16 or 18, and the bound AurB was detected via western blotting. - e) HPVE6 formed a complex with AurB in the nucleus: We examined the subcellular co-localisation of AurB and E6, using an immunofluorescence assay. We found that AurB co-localised with HPV16E6 in the nucleus. We also detected E6 co-localised with AurB in the prometaphase and telophase cells. (2). Objective 2 - We identified 10 amino acid residues at the C-terminus end of HPVE6, located in the close vicinity of E6-PBM, are important for AurB-E6 complex formation. Based on these findings, we collaborated with the International Centre of Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology (ICGEB), Italy to design 5 AurB-E6 blocking peptides, designated as P1 to P5. Among them, P2, bound to E6 most efficiently. However, P2 did not inhibit the AurB-E6 complex formation. We discovered that AZD1152, a potent Aurora kinase B inhibitor, can inhibit AurB-E6 complex formation. - a) AurB bound to E6 at the C-terminus of E6, independent of E6-PBM: Through Scansite, it was predicted that amino acid residues serine (S) 89, threonine (T) 140, S145 and S150 of HPV16E6 harboured AurB recognition motif; and these amino acid residues were mutated to Alanine (A). We observed that all the E6 mutants showed a reduced binding affinity to AurB. We also tested a mutant with deletion of the PDZ binding motif. These results indicate that AurB interacts directly with HPV16 and HPV18 E6 in an E6-PBM-independent manner. The amino acid residues at the C-terminus of HPV16E6 (140 – 150) were found to be most critical for the AurB-E6 complex formation. - b) E6 inhibited AurB kinase activity: We performed a sensitive luminescence-based ADP-GloTM kinase assay and found that in the presence of GST-16E6 fusion proteins, the AurB activity was reduced by more than half, and that binding of E6 to AurB, disregarding the affinity of binding of E6 to AurB, can reduce the AurB kinase activity. (3). Objective 3 - We discovered that AurB-E6 complex activated histone H3, elevated the Ras/MEK/ERK signaling axis, and increased hTERT protein level and its telomerase activity. - a) AurB-E6 complex formation did not disrupt histone phosphorylation: We ectopically expressed HA-tagged E6 and/or Flag-tagged AurB in C33A (HPV-null cervical cancer cells), and showed that AurB-E6 complex is involved in maintaining the phosphor-status of histone H3, particularly at S10 in C33A cells. - b) E6 did not perturb the function of AurB in regulating hTERT protein: An HPV-null U-2 OS (an osteosarcoma cell line that lacks hTERT expression) was used. We found co-expression of hTERT with AurB and E6 led to an increased hTERT expression by at least 4-folds when compared with the cells expressing hTERT alone. - c) The association of AurB and E6 led to increased telomerase activity: We performed a PCR-based TRAPeze telomerase detection assay and demonstrated that E6 does not perturb the function of AurB in regulating telomerase activity. More strikingly, we also observed that AurB and E6 overexpression was able to increase the basal level of telomerase. - d) AurB-E6 association increased Ras/MEK/ERK signalling cascade: We expressed hTERT alone, or co-expressed with HA-tagged 16E6 and/or Flag-tagged AurB in C33A cells. Intriguingly, when hTERT, AurB and E6 were co-expressed, the levels of Ras, MEK1/2 and ERK1/2 were comparable to that of the mock-transfected samples. In contrast, the expression of hTERT with either AurB or E6 reduced the expression of Ras/MEK/ERK cascade. (4). Objective 4 - As we observed that AZD1152 was able to inhibit AurB-E6 complex formation, instead of using AurB-E6 blocking peptides, we studied the effect of AZD1152. The treatment of AZD1152 led to an activation of the apoptotic pathway; and inhibition of telomerase activity, cell proliferation and tumour formation. - a) The levels of Aurora kinases activity, HPV oncoproteins and p53 protein: We first examined the effect of an Aurora B specific inhibitor (AZD1152) and pan-Aurora kinases inhibitor (Reversine, AMG900 and Tozasertib) on the expression of (1) phosphor- and total AurB; (2) HPV16E7; and (3) p53 (as a surrogate marker for E6 expression in HPV-positive cells). We observed that AZD1152 treatment reduced the protein levels of phosphor- and total AurB and HPV16E7; as well as increased level of p53 protein. - b) AurB-E6 blocking peptides did not disrupt AurB-E6 complex formation: We proposed to use peptides to disrupt the AurB-E6 complex formation. In collaboration with the International Centre for Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology (ICGEB), Italy, we synthesized 6 N-terminally labelled biotinylated peptides. The sequences of the peptides are as follow: Peptide 1: GNLLTQAIRQQYYK Peptide 2: KPIDVDRMYGTI Peptide 3: TIDSPKLEELFN Peptide 4: PAWASGNLLTQA Peptide 5: LTQAIRQQYYKP Peptide 6: YYKPIPVDRMYGY Since we did not observe inhibitory effect from these blocking peptides (P1-P6), whereas a dose-dependent inhibitory effect was observed for AZD1152. We further examined effects of AZ1152 and found that the treated cancer cells exhibited (i) reduced telomerase activity, (ii) activated apoptotic pathway, and (iii) suppressed cell proliferation. Further more, the anti-tumour effect of AZD1152 was observed in: (1) Organotypic raft culture: We grew C33A, HeLa and Caski cells in an organotypic raft culture. Treatment with 300 nM of AZD1152 reduced the thickness of all three cell lines. (2) HPV-athymic nude mice: We injected HeLa or immortalized primary baby rat kidney cells into the dorsal flank of 4–5 weeks old female athymic nude mice. We observed that the tumour volume reduced dramatically when treated with AZD1152. In summary, this project has identified a novel host-viral complex (AurB-E6) critical in the oncogenesis of HPV-associated cancers, thus opens a new target for anti-cancer drug development.

14162117.label: Major findings and research outcome
14162117.value: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is a major cause of human cancers. The HPV-encoded oncoproteins, E6 and E7, interact with a different subset of host proteins, leading to dysregulation of apoptotic, cell cycle and signaling pathways. In this study, we have identified for the first time that Aurora kinase B (AurB) as a bona fide interacting partner of E6. We systematically characterized the AurB-E6 complex formation and delineated its consequences in carcinogenesis by using a series of in vitro and cell-based assays. We also assessed the potential of Aurora kinase inhibitors in halting HPV-mediated carcinogenesis by using in vitro and in vivo models. Our data showed that AurB activity was elevated in a dose-dependent manner with E6 expression in HPV-positive cancer cells of different origins. As demonstrated by co-immunoprecipitation assays, AurB bound directly with E6, but remarkably not with E7. Using immunofluorescence assay, we located AurB-E6 complexes inside the nucleus, and were detected in the prometaphase and telophase; whereas no overlapped localization of E7 and AurB was observed. We further investigated the physical interaction and identified a stretch of amino acid residues located at the C-terminus of HPVE6 (140-150) were critical for complex formation with AurB; whereas the PDZ binding motif of E6 was not important. AurB-E6 complex formation led to reduced AurB kinase activity. Furthermore, AurB-E6 complex activated histone H3, elevated the Ras/MEK/ERK signaling axis, and increased hTERT protein level and its telomerase activity. On the other hand, AurB inhibition led to an activation of apoptotic pathway, and inhibition on telomerase activity, cell proliferation and tumour formation. In summary, this study dissected the molecular mechanism of how E6 recruits AurB to induce cell immortalization and proliferation, leading to the eventual cancer development. In the final part of this project, we demonstrated that treatment with an Aurora inhibitor, AZD1152, resulted in an anti-tumour effect on HPV-positive cancer cells. This finding opens a novel virus-specific target, i.e. AurB-E6 complex, for the development of specific therapy targeting HPV-associated cancers.

14162117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14162117.value: The findings of this project indicate that the host-virus complex "Aurora B-E6" plays an important role in maintaining cancer status. The data also demonstrate a potential of using Aurora inhibitors to treat HPV-associated cancers. At present, a successful targeted therapy for HPV-associated cancer is not available. Therefore, it is worthwhile to develop compounds that can specifically disrupt the complex "Aurora B-E6" to acheive a specific anti-tumor effect on HPV-associated cancers. At present, we are pursuing on this direction using computer-aided, cell-based and preclinical models.

14162117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14162117.value: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is an important cancer causing agent associated with cancers arise from the uterine cervix, oropharynx and anogenital areas. The ability of HPV to cause cancer is mainly contributed by viral proteins E6 and E7, which disturb the balance between “good” and “bad” proteins that play a critical role in suppressing and promoting cancer formation, respectively. In this study, we identified a “good” protein that turned into a “bad” protein in cancer cells, termed Aurora kinase B (AurB), which is a previously unrecognized interacting partner of E6. We also systematically characterize the interaction between AurB and E6 and excavated the mechanism of how E6 deployed AurB to promote cancer formation and cancer progression. Following this, we tested the efficacy of an anti-cancer agent, AZD1152, that specifically inhibits AurB function and is currently being investigated in clinical trials. We discovered that AZD1152 can reduce the amount of the viral E6 and E7 proteins, activate the intrinsic cell death program, and subsequently inhibit the progression to cancer formation. Our findings open a new direction for developing targeted therapy for HPV-associated cancers.

14162217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14162217.value: The primary objective in this study is to establish a list of host cellular proteins that mediate norovirus infection. Norovirus is one of the most common pathogens attributed to diarrheal diseases from unsafe food. It is also the primary cause of mortality among young children and adults in foodborne infections. Norovirus is not just a foodborne burden. In a recent meta-analysis, norovirus accounts for nearly one-fifth of all causes of (including person-to-person transmission) acute gastroenteritis in both sporadic and outbreak settings and affects all age groups. Undoubtedly, norovirus is of paramount public health concern in both developed and developing countries. Research efforts to better understand norovirus pathobiology will be necessary for targeted intervention. From Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus to Zika virus, efforts to identify host factors important for mediating virus infection has always been a research priority. Such information will shed light on potential therapeutic targets in antiviral intervention. Norovirus virus-host interaction studies have been hampered by the lack of a robust cell culture model in the past 20 years. Despite encouraging claims of human norovirus cultivation in three-dimensional cultures of intestinal epithelial cells and hematopoietic B cells, attempts to reproduce these findings have proved challenging. In 2016, norovirus has finally been successfully cultivated in a stem cell-derived three-dimensional human gut-like structure called enteroid or mini-gut. More importantly, the model has been reproduced by several leading norovirus laboratories. CRISPR, a natural RNA-guided mechanism in bacterial immune defense against foreign genetic materials, has recently been harnessed as a promising gene-editing tool nowadays. In virology, CRISPR has been used to identify host factors for flaviviruses in human cells with overriding advantages of almost perfect efficiency and minimal off-target effect. Here, we will take advantage of the availability of these two ground-breaking technologies to search for host factors that regulate human norovirus infection. In our proposed study, intestinal stem cells will be isolated from human duodenal biopsies and differentiated into mini-guts. Genome-wide genetic screening for host essential and restrictive factors will be performed on infected mini-guts by knockout CRISPR and gain-of-function CRISPR SAM, respectively. Shortlisted candidates will undergo preliminary functional validation in cell lines. These data will provide insights into potential therapeutic targets against norovirus infection. We will also open up enquiries on norovirus pathogenesis depending on the discovered host factors. 14162417.label: Realisation of objectives
14162417.value: 1. To validate the technique of PGS using NGS on embryo culture media stated in previous literature. We have completed the validation of NGS technique on embryo culture media (SCM) for the purpose of preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (PGT-A). The 24-chromosome screening using NGS technique on embryo culture media, trophectoderm biopsy and control culture medium were performed to confirm the reliability and accuracy of the technique of cell free DNA amplification, followed by using NGS (Veriseq, Illumina) on embryo culture media. We also established a new PGT-A protocol using an alternative semiconductor sequencing NGS platform, related work has been published in 2019 (PMID: 31498328). 2. To identify the source of cell free-DNA in the embryo culture media. Based on the TE results among the 116 embryos that had PGT-A results from both TE and SCM samples, as compared with PGT-A using TE. Our NiPGT-A results showed a high concordance of 73.3% (85/116) and 82.4% (89/108) on autosomal and sex chromosomes. We also noticed that there is maternal contamination from cumulus cells or polar body DNA. This work has been published (PMID: 31292818) 3. to validate the ploidy status from embryo culture media, trophectoderm biopsies, product-of-conception from miscarriages, fetal cord blood and placental tissue from live births. We have achieved this long term follow-up by studying patient with mosaic embryo transfer with postnatal confirmation by placental multiple biopsies. (PMID: 32825792). Our data suggested that (1) aneuploidy rescue might occur during embryonic development, in-line with the aneuploidy cell line depletion theory supported by a chimeric mouse study. Secondly, single biopsy employed in PGT-A might not precisely represent the true genetic constitution and level of mosaicism. 4. to correlate the clinical outcomes of pregnancy with the ploidy status on its corresponding embryo culture media As mentioned by objective 3, we have achieved this long term follow-up by studying patient with mosaic embryo transfer with postnatal confirmation by placental multiple biopsies. (PMID: 32825792).

14162417.label: Major findings and research outcome
14162417.value: Cell-free DNA found in spent culture medium (SCM) could provide ploidy information of an embryo as in invasive preimplantation genetic testing for Aneuploidy (PGT-A) from its trophectoderm (TE). Given its potential to reflect the comprehensive chromosomal profile of the whole embryo, more research based on clinical outcomes is required to determine if SCM could be a reliable selection tool in PGT-A. Apart from published a highly cited paper Yeung et al., 2019) Times Cited: 19 since 2019. Based on the data and research work from this RGC grant, we have validated the next generation sequencing based PGT-A platform and offer it as clinical laboratory test to support PGT-A in IVF units in Hong Kong. We have also granted the PGT-A license by the Hong Kong Human Reproductive Technology council.

14162417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14162417.value: Studies on non-invasive preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidies using spent culture media have been devoting effort to examining its concordance with invasive trophectoderm biopsies results. However, we demonstrated that ploidy calling by sequencing embryonic cell-free DNA in the spent culture medium is prone to maternal contamination from cumulus cells. Besides, the reagent expenses and turn-around time of sequencing increase the cost of each cycle. We are studying an alternative i.e. metabolomic profiling of spent culture medium by Raman spectroscopy followed by machine learning algorithm as a rapid and cost-efficient method which could potentially serve as an alternative to sequencing-based PGT-A approach. We have applied for HMRF grant

14162417.value: Our study demonstrated that cell-free DNA found in spent culture medium (SCM) could provide genetic information of an embryo. It reflect the comprehensive chromosomal profile of the whole embryo. We have validated this non-invasive preimplantation genetic testing for Aneuploidy (niPGT-A) for clinical use.

14162617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14162617.value: Respecting patients’ wishes about end-of-life (EOL) care is considered as an essential part of high quality medical care. Advance care planning (ACP) facilitates communication among the patient, their family/carers, and healthcare providers to enable a shared understanding on patient’s EOL care preferences before they become incapacity for decision making. Advance directive (AD) extends individual rights in health care decision-making that an individual can indicate the kinds of care they would prefer if their decision-making capacity is compromised. With the ageing population, more people are now living longer but with a worsening health. ACP should be promoted to frail elders because they are vulnerable to sudden deterioration triggered by minor stressful events and becoming mentally incompetent. Yet, the development of ACP in clinical practice has emerged only very slowly worldwide including Hong Kong even though it has been noted that the concept of planning ahead for future care was well accepted by patients. In addition, when discussion of EOL treatment options, it is unavoidable to use technical medical terms in an abstract, hypothetical way but these medical terms may not be understandable for laymen, especially those with limited health literacy. Elders usually have a lower level of health literacy may find it difficult to understand the content, and as a result, the treatment options for EOL care discussed in the ACP may not be well received. Nurses are at the best position to promote ACP because they have medical knowledge and have frequent contacts with patients in the community. This study aims to establish best practice in ACP and AD completion within the current Hong Kong framework for frail elders by testing a well designed and tested audio-visual means to overcome limitations in health literacy to support improved EOL planning with better ACP and more AD completion using a double-blinded randomized controlled trial. A total of 298 frail elders will be recruited and asked to nominate an informal carer if any to participate in the study. Subjects will then be randomized to the video-supported ACP programme or the health education program. It is hypothesized that more AD completion and occurrence of discussion regarding EOL care in patients at 6-months will be obtained in the video-supported ACP group. The results of the proposed study will shed light to the implementation of structured ACP programmes in routine healthcare service in response to the ongoing growth in the need for quality EOL care.

14162617.label: Realisation of objectives
14162617.value: We have encountered barriers during the implementation of the project in three aspects which had led to the premature termination of the trial when the funding period ended on 31 May 2022. The premature termination means we were unable to achieve the targeted sample size of 148. Since we had only recruited 105 subjects (i.e. 70.9%) in total, as a result, we could only achieved all the five objectives in partial. The following four major reasons contributed to the partial completion of the five objectives of the trial: 1. Delay in the start of subject recruitment There was a substantial delay in the start of subject recruitment of the project due to 3 important events: (1) We were advised by Dr Felix Chan, CMO of Grantham Hospital (GH) in Feb 2018 to start subject recruitment after the winter flu surge; (2) the PI moved to PolyU on 14 June 2018 due to contract end; (3) CUHK took 3.5 months to transfer the project account which was available at PolyU on 2 Oct 2018. To catch up, we had speeded up all the processes with appointments of three research personnel offered on 29 Nov 2018 and subject recruitment was then started on 17 Dec 2018 with the support from GH. 2. Difficulties of subjects recruitment during the COVID pandemic The overall recruitment process was smooth even during the social issue in the community between June and Dec 2019. However, due to the outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic in Jan 2020 and then restrictions of social activities in the community, leading to the cessation of all research activities in the two study hospitals. Since then, subject recruitment at the hospital setting were stopped. Later, due to the restrictions of social activities in the community, our project was totally suspended. Unfortunately, there was not much we could do when facing the COVID-19 pandemic. 3. Difficulties in intervention delivery and follow-up of subjects The social event in the community from June to Dec 2019 has induced difficulty to our home visits for intervention delivery. Then, the social distance restrictions due to the COVID-19 pandemic since March 2020 has led to the cessation of home-based face-to-face ACP discussion intervention delivery in the trial. Also, many patients and carers had indicated that they did not want to talk about this topic during this hard period of time. In addition, we found it was hard to conduct the follow-up surveys with the older adults via phone as they could not hear clearly. Our nurses continued to provide the treatment sessions for patients and their family member in both the ACP and control groups at their homes from June 2019 to early March 2020 by scheduling the dates avoiding the social events in the community from June to Dec 2019 and wearing a mask during the discussion session until early March 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic. After the launch of social restriction measures in the community in late March 2020, we have tried out alternative ways to deliver the intervention and conduct the follow-up surveys, including deliver the intervention and conduct the follow-ups via telephone or other online technologies such as Zoom. However, these strategies were failed because the older adult participants could not hear clearly on the phone and most of them (even their family members) did not know or did not have Zoom at that time. 4. Difficulties in signing AD One of the team members at GH who was responsible for signing AD has left GH in May 2018. In response, we have recruited a part-time private geriatrician to sign the AD with the patients who wishes to. However, we received comment regarding the travel and cost barriers to the clinic of the private geriatrician (in Central). Because of hiring the private geriatrician for signing AD, we had asked permission from HA to adapt their AD forms for the use in the current project as well as arrange the patients to sign the electronic medical record sharing system in order to sign the AD with the private geriatrician. To solve the barriers, we provided the transportation cost and accompany for AD signing in the private clinic. However, after the outbreak of the COVID-19, participants refused to sign the AD even they had expressed their willingness to do so.

14162617.label: Major findings and research outcome
14162617.value: We found no evidence of a difference in the proportion of patients who had signed an AD during the study period (3 [5.9%] of 51 patients in the ACP group vs 1 [1.9%] of 54 in the control group, odds ratio [OR] 3.31, 95% CI (0.33, 32.93). The result remained unchanged after adjusting for the effects of baseline FRAIL score and whether the patients had completed the allocated treatment (adjusted OR 3.32, 95% CI (0.33, 32.79)). For occurrence of EOL care discussion, no evidence of between-group differences at baseline (9.8% vs. 11.1%, p=0.827), 1-month (71.4% vs. 47.6%, p=0.116) and 6-month follow up (33.3% vs. 20.8%, p=0.362). Non-significant results remained after adjusting for the effect of baseline FRAIL score and whether the patients had completed the allocated treatments. (Publication 4) There was no significant difference between ACP (n=11) and Control (n=15) groups at the 3 time points on decision-making confidence, anxiety and depression of carers (p-value ranged from 0.388 – 0.979). MW tests showed that there was no statistical between-group differences on the changes of the three outcome variables from baseline to 1 month or 6 month follow-ups. Patients in the ACP group reported a higher QoC-EOL score at 1 month than those in the control group, with an estimated mean difference (95% CI) of 8.73 (1.16, 16.30) after controlling for the effects of baseline FRAIL score and whether the patients had received the allocated treatment in GEE analysis. No evidence of differences in the mean change in the SURE and ACP knowledge scores from baseline to 1 month and to 6 months in the two groups after controlling for the effect of baseline FRAIL score and whether they had received the allocated treatment. (Publication 4) Kappa statistic was used to assess the congruence of EOL care goal between patients and carers. In the whole sample, the agreement between patients and carers on EOL care goal at 3 time points were none to minimal. There were slight increases of agreement at 1-month (k< 0.39) and 6-month follow up (k< 0.26) when comparing to baseline (k<0.18). Kappa statistics by group and time were also none to minimal, however, the results were based on small sample sizes. Qualitative analysis describing experiences of failure when engaging in ACP conversations revealed three themes were identified: “Refraining from discussing end-of-life care”, “Remaining in the here and now”, and “Relinquishing responsibility over end-of-life care decision-making”. (Publication 3)

14162617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14162617.value: There are two key messages generated from this study regarding (1) the optimal time for ACP by creating the clinical relevance of ACP to patients and (2) the involvement of family members in ACP discussions by providing support family members in terms of ACP knowledge and in their roles as surrogate decision-makers in the Asian context. Two new projects based on these observations are funded: A new GRF project targeting palliative care patients and their family members is ongoing now. An internal project is funded to launch a community-based educational intervention for family members in order to shift ACP from a health issue to a normal conservation in the community.

14162617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14162617.value: We had conducted a parallel, double-blinded randomised controlled trial to examine the effect of video-supported nurse-led advance care planning (ACP) (n=51) as compared with a health education programme plus an ACP promotion leaflet (n=54) on end-of-life decision-making outcomes in older adults with frailty. The trial was terminated prematurely because of the COVID-19 pandemic and the end of the funding. The ACP group reported a higher but non-significant advance directive completion rate (5.9% vs 1.9%). No evidence of a difference in favourable outcomes of subjects receiving the video-supported, nurse-led ACP compared with those receiving active control. However, the results might have been confounded by high attrition, poor intervention completion and reduced sample size due to the early termination of the study. We identified three themes describing experiences of failure when engaging in ACP conversations: “Refraining from discussing end-of-life care”, “Remaining in the here and now”, and “Relinquishing responsibility over end-of-life care decision-making”. This RCT provides insights to the directions of future research for ACP in an Asian context. To engage more ACP participation, it is important to create clinical relevance for patients and to provide support to family members in their role as surrogate decision-makers.

14163317.label: Project Objectives
14163317.value: To characterize and investigate the regulatory mechanisms of np_9884 under diabetic conditions. This will be examined in vitro in Smad3 WT/KO cells including MEFs and mesangial cells and in vivo in Smad3WT/KO-db/db mice. To determine the pathogenic role and therapeutic potential of np_9884 in db/db mice by knocking down np_9884 from the diabetic kidney before and after the development of DN. To investigate the underlying mechanism by which np_9884 mediates T2DN via the MCP-1 dependent mechanism in vitro and in vivo. The interaction between np_9884 and MCP-1 under diabetic conditions will be determined by luciferase reporter assay and the regulatory role np_9884 in MCP-1 expression will be explored by gain-of-function and loss-of-function assays.

14163317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14163317.value: Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is a major complication of diabetes and is a leading cause of end-stage kidney disease. We recently found that Smad3 signaling is a central pathway leading to chronic kidney disease (CKD) and DN. Many inflammatory mediators including TGF-beta1, angiotensin II, AGE, and CRP can activate Smad3 via both TGF-beta1-dependent and independent mechanisms, however, precise mechanisms whereby Smad3 mediates DN remain unclear. By using the next generation sequencing, we recently identified a number of Smad3-dependent long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) in CKD. In this proposal, we tested these Smad3-dependent lncRNAs in type-2 DN (T2DN) in db/db mice and found that a novel lncRNA np_9884 was markedly upregulated in T2DN and was induced by TGF-beta1 and high glucose. We also found that there is a predicted Smad3 binding site in the np_9884 promoter and expression of np_9884 was tightly regulated by Smad3, but not Smad2 in response to TGF-beta1 and high glucose. Surprisingly, silencing np_9884 largely suppressed TGF-beta1 and AGE- induced MCP-1, but not collagen 1 expression in a mouse mesangial cell line, demonstrating a potential role for np_9884 in the pathogenesis of T2DN via a MCP-1 dependent mechanism. This is also supported by a predicted np_9884 biding site in the MCP-1 promoter. Based on these novel and exciting preliminary findings, we thus hypothesize that lncRNAs np_9884 may play a pathogenic role in T2DN and importantly, targeting np_9884 may represent as a novel and specific therapy for T2DN. We plan to examine this hypothesis by studying 3 specific aims. 1) We will first characterize and investigate the regulatory mechanisms of np_9884 under diabetic conditions in vitro in Smad3 WT/KO cells and in vivo in Smad3WT/KO-db/db mice. 2) We will then examine the pathogenic role and therapeutic potential of np_9884 in db/db mice by silencing np_9884 in the diabetic kidney before and after the development of DN. Finally, the underlying mechanism whereby np_9884 mediates T2DN via the MCP-1 dependent mechanism will be studied in vitro and in vivo. By completing this study, we expect to identify Smad3 as a key regulatory mechanism of np_9884 expression under diabetic conditions. Importantly, np_9884 is pathogenic in the development of T2DN and targeting np_9884 may represent a novel and specific therapy for T2DN. Finally, np_9884-may mediate T2DN via the MCP-1 dependent mechanism. Thus, outcomes from this study will be highly innovative and significant both scientifically and clinically. 糖尿病腎病是糖尿病的主要併發症，是終末期腎臟疾病的主要原因。我們最近發現Smad3信號傳導是導致糖尿病腎病的中心途徑。然而，Smad3介導糖尿病腎病精確機制仍不清楚。通過RNA測序，我們最近鑒定了許多Smad3依賴性長非編碼RNA（lncRNA）。發現新型的lncRNA np_9884在2型糖尿病腎病中顯著上調，np_9884啟動子中存在預測的Smad3結合位點，並且被Smad3嚴格調控。令人驚訝的是，沉默np_9884在很大程度上抑制TGF-β1和AGE-誘導的MCP-1，證明了np_9884通過MCP-1依賴性機制在2型糖尿病腎病發病機制中的潛在作用。基於這些新穎而令人興奮的初步發現，我們假設lncRNAs np_9884可能在2型糖尿病腎病中起致病作用。我們計畫通過研究3個具體目標來研究這一假設。 1）首先在Smad3 WT / KO細胞和Smad3WT / KO-db / db小鼠體內研究np_9884的調控機制。 2）然後，我們將通過在糖尿病腎臟中沉默np_9884來檢查np_9884在db / db小鼠中的致病作用和治療潛力。3）最後，將通過體外和體內研究np_9884-通過MCP-1依賴機制介導T2DN的潛在機制。 我們期望，Smad3為np_9884表達的關鍵調控機制。重要的是，np_9884是2型糖尿病腎病致病因素，靶向抑制np_9884可能是特異性治療2型糖尿病腎病新穎療法。最後，np_9884可能通過MCP-1依賴機制來引起2型糖尿病腎病。因此，本研究的結果將具有高度的創新性，科學性，和臨床意義。

14163317.label: Realisation of objectives
14163317.value: We have successfully completed all three project objectives as outlined above with several major findings as described below. 1. To characterize and investigate the regulatory mechanisms of np_9884 under diabetic conditions as stated in Specific Aim 1, we first examined LRNA9884 expression in the development of type-2 diabetic nephropathy (T2DN) in db/db mice. We found that LRNA9884 was significantly upregulated in the diabetic kidney of db/db mice preceding the onset of microalbuminuria and progression of diabetic renal injury, suggesting that upregulation of LRNA9884 may be pathogenic in the development of T2DN. We then examined the regulatory mechanisms of LRNA9884 under diabetic conditions in vitro and found that LRNA9884 was induced by high glucose and AGE under diabetic conditions via a Smad3-dependent mechanism as MEFs lacking Smad3 but not Smad2 were failed to upregulate LRNA9884 in response to AGE, revealing a Smad3-dependent mechanism in regulation of LRNA9884 expression under diabetic conditions. This was further confirmed in vivo by genetically deleting Smad3 gene from db/db mice to blunt upregulation of renal LRNA9884. In addition, we also discovered that Smad3 could bind the promoter region of LRNA9884 by ChIP assay. Deletion (Smad3-KO) or inhibition (SIS3) of Smad3 effectively blocked the AGE-induced LRNA9884 expression in MEF and mTEC in vitro. 2. We have very successfully completed the Specific Aim 2 studies and uncovered the pathogenic role of LRNA9884 in T2DN. Importantly, we also developed a novel therapeutic strategy for T2DN by targeting LRNA9884 in db/db mice. By using an ultrasound-microbubble delivery system, we have successfully knocked down LRNA9884 with shRNA from both kidneys of the db/db mice and found that treatment of shRNA effectively suppressed expression of renal LRNA9884 in db/db mice and significantly suppressed renal histological injury including glomerular matrix deposition and glomerulosclerosis and decreased microalbuminuria excretion and serum creatinine, without altering the type-2 diabetic phenotype including body weight and fasting blood glucose. These novel observations suggest that LRNA9884 promotes T2DN via a kidney-specific mechanism and demonstrate a pathogenic role and therapeutic potential for T2DN by targeting LRNA9884. 3. We have also completed the Specific Aim 3 and successfully identified that LRNA9884 mediated T2DN via an MCP-1 dependent mechanism in vivo and in vitro. This was supported by the findings: 1) there was a binding site of LRNA9884 on the promoter region of MCP-1 genomic sequence; 2) Overexpression of LRNA9884 significantly enhanced the transcription activity of MCP-1 via direct binding on its promoter region (pGL3-MCP-1-promoter), which was effectively prevented by deletion of the predicted LRNA9884 binding site on the MCP-1 promoter (pGL3-MCP-1-mutant) or the LRNA9884 full length sequence (pcDNA3.1-LRNA9884-2) in vitro; 3) in vivo shRNA-9884-treatment significantly reduced renal MCP and infiltrating macrophages. Interestingly, we also found that LNRA9884 can interact with NF-kB and regulate NF-kB-dependent inflammatory response. We thus extended the original aims to study the role of LNRA9884 in acute kidney injury via the NF-kB-driven macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) mechanism. Thus, targeting LRNA9884 could inhibit acute kidney injury. In conclusion, we have completed all the proposed studies as described in Specific Aim 1-3 and found that LNRA9884 is pathogenic in T2DN and is tightly regulated by Smad3 under diabetic conditions. We also identified that MCP-1 is a targeting gene of LNRA9884 and thus LNRA9884 mediates T2DN via the MCP-1-dependent mechanism. Importantly, we also provide strong evidence for the therapeutic potential for T2DN by targeting LRNA9884. Thus, inhibition of LNRA9884 may represent as an effective novel therapy for T2DN. All these results have been published in the Top rank of journals (Diabetes 2019 ;68:1485-1498; Front Physiol 2020 Oct 29;11:590027; and others as shown in the Part C Research Output). With the grant support, we also examined the regulatory role of Smad3 and Smad3-related lncRNAs in diabetic complications as well as the pathogenic role of macrophages and its inflammatory cytokines such as MIF and CRP in acute kidney and chronic kidney injury with several original publications and review papers as shown in the Research Output (Nat Rev Nephrol 2019 Mar;15(3):144-158; J Physiol 2018 Aug;596(16):3493-3503; Nephrology (Carlton) 2018 Oct;23 Suppl 4:50-52; Clin Sci (Lond) 2018 Jul 9;132(13):1403-1415; Mol Ther. 2018 Oct 3;26(10):2523-2532; J Cell Mol Med. 2019 Jun;23(6):3867-3877).

14163317.label: Major findings and research outcome
14163317.value: We have very successfully completed this project study with several major findings. 1. We found that LRNA9884 was significantly upregulated in the diabetic kidney of db/db mice preceding the onset of type-2 diabetic nephropathy (T2DN), suggesting that LRNA9884 may be pathogenic in T2DN. 2. In vitro, we also found that LRNA9884 was induced by high glucose and AGE via a Smad3-dependent mechanism as MEFs lacking Smad3 but not Smad2 were failed to upregulate LRNA9884 in response to AGE. This was further confirmed in vivo by genetically deleting Smad3 gene from db/db mice to blunt upregulation of renal LRNA9884. In addition, Smad3 could bind the promoter region of LRNA9884 by ChIP assay and deletion (Smad3-KO) or inhibition (SIS3) of Smad3 effectively blocked the AGE-induced LRNA9884 expression in MEF and mTEC in vitro. 3. Importantly, we uncovered the pathogenic role of LNNA9884 in T2DN and also developed a novel therapeutic strategy for T2DN by targeting LRNA9884. We found that specifically targeting renal LRNA9884 can block progressive renal injury in db/db mice without altering the type-2 diabetic phenotype including body weight and fasting blood glucose. These novel observations suggest that LRNA9884 promotes T2DN via a kidney-specific mechanism and demonstrate a pathogenic role and therapeutic potential for T2DN by targeting LRNA9884. 4. We also identified LRNA9884 mediated T2DN via an MCP-1 dependent mechanism in vivo and in vitro as a binding site of LRNA9884 was found in the promoter region of MCP-1 and overexpression of LRNA9884 significantly enhanced but silencing LRNA9884 inhibited the transcription activity of MCP-1 and macrophage infiltration in vitro and in vivo. All these results have been published in the top rank of diabetes journal (Diabetes 2019 ;68:1485-1498) and also in other biomedical journals as shown in the Part C Research Output. 5. Furthermore, we also found that LNRA9884 can also interact with NF-kB and regulate NF-kB-dependent macrophage migration inhibitor (MIF) mechanism. Thus, targeting LRNA9884 could inhibit acute kidney injury, which was also published in Front Physiol (2020 Oct 29;11:590027). With the grant support, we also extensively examined the regulator role of Smad3 in other lncRNA mediated kidney diseases including MIF and CRP in acute kidney and chronic kidney injury with several original publications and review papers as shown in the Research Output (Nat Rev Nephrol 2019; J Physiol 2018 ; Nephrology (Carlton) 2018; Clin Sci (Lond); Mol Ther. 2018; J Cell Mol Med 2019).

14163317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14163317.value: Based on the finding from this study that LRNA9884 mediates renal inflammation via the MCP-1-dependent mechanisms, it is highly possible that LRNA9884 may also play a pathogenic role in MCP-induced macrophage-dependent kidney diseases. This hypothesis has been rested in an acute kidney disease model and has resulted in the success of a Joint Science and Technology Innovation Action Plan of the Shanghai Science and Technology Commission, Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan Science and Technology Cooperation Project entitled "The mechanism by which LRNA9884 promotes acute kidney injury by releasing inflammation from macrophages". We believe that the novel findings of the role of LRNA9884 from diabetes could be further extended to other inflammatory diseases and will largely promote the collaborations locally and internationally.

14163317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14163317.value: In this study, we discovered that a long-coding RNA molecule called LRNA9884 is pathogenic in the development of type-2 diabetic nephropathy. Our study found that LRNA9884 is markedly increased in type-2 diabetic nephropathy and inhibition of kidney LRNA9884 could block diabetic kidney injury. We also uncovered the molecular mechanisms through which LRNA9884 is induced by a molecule called Smad3 and then to mediate diabetic nephropathy by inducing macrophage accumulation and activation via macrophage chemotactic protein-1. Most importantly, we developed a novel and effective therapy for type-2 diabetic nephropathy by targeting renal LRNA9884 as kidney-specifically silencing LRNA9884 was capable of blunting progressive diabetic kidney injury in a type-2 diabetic db/db mice. In conclusion, results from this study demonstrate a pathogenic role and therapeutic potential for diabetic kidney disease by targeting LRNA9884.

14163517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14163517.value: 青少年特發性脊柱側彎(AIS)是一組原因不明，機理複雜的脊柱側彎，主要發病于青少年女性。 流行病學調查顯示AIS在香港的發病率大約2-4%。 如若不予治療，側彎有可能進展至重度並引發心肺功能異常及其他併發症。 現有治療手段包括支具佩戴及矯正手術，均未能達到滿意的治療效果並有局限性。 文獻報導系統性低骨密度現象發生在AIS患者的整個骨成熟期，並與AIS疾病發生和進展有顯著關聯。 我們 透過高解析度肢體骨定量電腦掃描器，我們發現AIS患者的體積骨密度及皮質骨厚度的有下降的現象。 Wnt信號通路在脊柱的骨骼發育中扮演重要作用。 最近的研究發現其中的WNT16信號通過影響成骨細胞和破骨細胞的活性，調節皮質骨質量。我們發現帶有Wnt16缺陷的小鼠也有低皮質骨厚度和低骨密度的徵狀。 我們近期的基因型研究發現了AIS相關的WNT16突變位點和AIS骨組織中高表達水平的WNT16 基因。然而，WNT16的基因型與皮質骨表型的關係依舊未知。 另外，我們組的隨機對照臨床實驗表明低骨密度AIS病人用維生素D和鈣補劑可顯著升高皮質骨容量性骨密度和厚度，控制側彎進展。 我們假設 WNT16基因多態性及相關功能的改變通過調節成骨細胞和破骨細胞的相互作用影響骨形成和吸收，導致低皮質骨厚度和低容量性骨密度從而降低機械力強度，參與AIS疾病的發生和進展。 本研究將通過細胞和基因敲除小鼠模型評估維生素和鈣補劑作為治療方案，改變AIS病人異常的皮質骨表型的治療潛力。 本研究計畫將作為我們過去GRF研究項目（463113和14116415）的後續研究，增強我們對骨細胞及細胞間相互作用的理解，並推進維生素D 和 鈣補劑作為治療方案預防脊柱側彎發生及進展的進程。

14163817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14163817.value: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the leading causes of cancer-related death worldwide. In Asian countries, the incidence of CRC has been rising rapidly and CRC is the commonest cancer in Hong Kong. However, the mechanisms underlying CRC initiation and development remain elusive. We have recently performed whole-genome sequencing and gene expression analyses of human CRC samples. Notably, Ring Finger Protein 6 (RNF6), a member of RING family genes, is frequently overexpressed in CRC tumor tissues due to copy number gain. This was further affirmed in an independent validation series of CRC patients, which suggested RNF6 was frequently overexpressed (74%) in human CRC tumor samples compared with their adjacent non-tumor tissues and in 6 out of 7 CRC cell lines. Several RING family members have been shown to play important roles in cancer development, whilst the functional significance and clinical implication of RNF6 in human cancer are unclear. Our preliminary in vitro and in vivo functional studies supported a strong oncogenic role of RNF6 in CRC development, possibly through inducing the WNT/β-catenin signaling pathway via directly interacting with its repressor transducin-like enhancer protein 3 (TLE3), which induced the polyubiquitination of TLE3 and proteasome-dependent TLE3 degradation. This in turn activates β-catenin-mediated oncogenic signaling that drives CRC tumorigenesis. Collectively, we propose to investigate the role of RNF6 as a novel tumor-promoting gene which may link WNT/β-catenin signaling pathway via TLE3 to the malignant progression of CRC. In this application, we propose three specific objectives: 1) to characterize the oncogenic role of RNF6 in CRC using a unique conditional colon-specific RNF6 transgenic mouse model; 2) to investigate the mechanisms underlying the oncogenic role of RNF6 in the activation of Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway through interacting with TLE3; 3) to study the clinical significance of RNF6 in CRC patients. These research objectives will be tackled with a multidisciplinary approach combining biochemistry, genomics, molecular and cell biology, signaling pathway, protein-protein, protein-DNA interaction analyses and transgenic animal models. The new knowledge gained from this proposed study will provide insight into the role of RNF6 in CRC initiation and progression, advance our understanding of CRC molecular pathogenesis and facilitate early diagnosis and more effective therapeutic strategy for CRC patients. 結直腸癌（CRC）是世界範圍內癌症相關死亡的主要原因之一。在亞洲國家，CRC的發病率迅速上升，CRC為香港最常見的癌症。然而，CRC的發病機制發展仍然不清楚。我們最近進行了人類CRC樣本的全基因組測序和基因表達分析。值得注意的是，RING家族基因的成員，戒指蛋白6（RNF6）在CRC腫瘤中由於拷貝數增加爾呈現過表達。這在一系列CRC患者獨立樣本中得到進一步驗證和肯定，與其相鄰的非腫瘤組織相比較，RNF6在74％人類CRC腫瘤樣本過表達。雖然已經有幾個RING家庭成員在癌症發展中有重要作用， 但RNF6在人類癌症中的功能意義和臨床價值尚不清楚。我們前期的體外和體內功能研究支持RNF6在CRC發生發展中有強大的致癌作用，RNF6可能直接與與WNT /β-連環蛋白信號通路阻遏物轉導素樣增強子蛋白3（TLE3）結合，誘導TLE3的多聚泛素化和蛋白酶體依賴性TLE3降解，從而啟動驅動CRC腫瘤發生的β-連環蛋白介導的致癌信號傳導。 在這項研究中，我們提出三個具體目標：1）使用結直腸特異性RNF6轉基因小鼠模型研究RNF6在CRC中的致癌作用; 2）研究RNF6與TLE3相互作用，在Wnt /β-連環蛋白信號通路活化中的致癌作用機制; 3）研究RNF6在CRC患者中的臨床意義。這些研究目標將結合多學科方法來解決生物化學，基因組學，分子和細胞生物學，信號通路，蛋白質 - 蛋白質，蛋白質 - DNA相互作用分析和轉基因動物模型。從該研究中獲得的結果和新的知識，將提供對RNF6在CRC中的作用和機制的瞭解，提高我們對CRC分子發病機理的認識並促進CRC患者的早期診斷和更有效的治療策略。

14163817.label: Realisation of objectives
14163817.value: All the proposed objectives have been completed in this project, as outline in the proposal. Below we summarized the completion status of the key objectives. Objective #1: We have successfully generated RNF6 conditional, colon specific transgenic mice, and showed that colon-specific RNF6 overexpression promotes colorectal tumorigenesis, validating that RNF6 as a novel oncogenic factor in colorectal cancer (CRC). We have delineated the molecular mechanism of RNF6 in colorectal cancer by the evaluation of apoptosis and cell proliferation, demonstrating that RNF6 suppresses apoptosis and induces cell proliferation in colonic tumors. These experiments completed the proposed work in Objective #1. We encountered no problems in completing these aims. Objective #2: In this aim, we have elucidated the molecular mechanism of RNF6 by (a-b) its interaction with TLE3 and activation of WNT signaling; and (c) its transcriptional targets. In the first part, we have performed immunoprecipitation assay to confirm the direct interaction of RNF6 and TLE3. We showed that RNF6 mediated ubiquitination and its associated degradation of TLE3, which in turn, activated WNT signaling to promote CRC phenotypes. In the second part, we have performed integrative ChIP-seq and RNA-seq in cells overexpressing RNF6, leading to the novel identification of splicing factor 3b subunit 2 (SF3B2) as a downstream factor. Knockout and rescue studies confirmed SF3B2 as a target of RNF6-driven CRC. These experiments completed the proposed work in Objective #2. We encountered no problems in completing these aims. Objective #3: We have performed analysis of the role of RNF6 in clinical cohorts of CRC. We found that RNF6 is up-regulated in CRC and its overexpression is correlated with gene amplification. In addition, we demonstrated that RNF6 gene amplification, mRNA expression and protein expression expression are all correlated with poor survival of CRC patients in independent cohorts. Besides, our investigation showed that RNF6 as a factor involved in resistance to chemotherapeutic agents. As a consequence, targeting of RNF6 or its downstream target SF3B2 could sensitize CRC cells to the effects of chemotherapy. These experiments completed the proposed work in Objective #3. We encountered no problems in completing these aims.

14163817.label: Major findings and research outcome
14163817.value: 1. We identified Ring finger protein 6 (RNF6) as a novel oncogene in colorectal cancer. RNF6, a RING-domain E3 ubiquitin ligase, is upregulated in 73.5% (147/200) of patients with colorectal cancer and was positively associated with RNF6 gene amplification. Furthermore, RNF6 expression and its gene amplification were independent prognostic factors for poor outcome of patients with colorectal cancer, consistent with its protumorigenic function. 2. In vitro and in vivo studies demonstrated the oncogenic function of RNF6 in CRC cells. RNF6 promoted cell growth, cell-cycle progression, and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition in CRC cells in vitro. In xenograft mouse models, RNF6 promoted CRC tumor growth and lung metastasis. 3. We established a novel colon-specific RNF6 transgenic (tg) mice, and demonstrated that RNF6 overexpression accelerated colorectal carcinogenesis compared to wild-type littermates in a chemically induced CRC model. More RNF6 tg mice developed macroscopic tumors in colon compared to wild-type mice, with a higher frequency of dysplasia, tumor number and tumor burden. Supporting this, tumors from RNF6 tg mice also had increased cell proliferation and suppressed apoptosis. 4. In terms of molecular mechanism, we first investigation protein-protein interaction of RNF6. With co-immunoprecipitation and mass spectrometry, we identified TLE3, a WNT repressor, as a RNF6 binding protein. RNF6 mediates the ubiquitylation and degradation of TLE3, which in turn led to the recruitment of β-catenin to TCF4/LEF, triggering Wnt/β-catenin activation. 5. We further unravelled RNF6 could function as a transcription factor in promoting CRC. We performed integrated ChIP-seq and RNA-seq analysis to identify splicing factor 3b subunit 2 (SF3B2) as a potential downstream target of RNF6. RNF6 binds to the SF3B2 promoter and the overexpression of RNF6 activates SF3B2 expression in CRC cells and also in RNF6 tg mice. Restore of SF3B2 abrogated the function of RNF6, suggesting that SF3B2 is a functional downstream target of RNF6. 6. We identified SF3B2 as a therapeutic target for RNF6-overexpressing CRC. We found that RNF6 mediates drug resistance to chemotherapeutic agents. Targeting of RNF6-SF3B2 axis with SF3B2 inhibitor with pladienolide B suppressed the growth of CRC cells with RNF6 overexpression in vitro and in vivo. Moreover, the combination of 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) plus pladienolide B exerted synergistic effects in CRC with high RNF6 expression, leading to tumor regression in xenograft models. Hence, SF3B2 is an actionable target for CRC expressing RNF6. 7. In summary, our study identified RNF6 as a pivotal player in CRC and devised a therapeutic strategy to overcome RNF6-overexpressing CRC.

14163817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14163817.value: To further improve the mechanistic understanding of RNF6 in CRC, we will open up collaborative work with other academic researchers to investigate the effect of RNF6 transgenic expression on the tumor microenvironment in our newly established mice model. I have extensively collaborated with researchers from the local and international institutions who has expertise with different aspects of oncology research. We will focus on the effect of RNF6 on tumor immunology, tumor-associated fibroblasts, as well as the gut microbiome, in order to unravel multifaceted effect of RNF6 in contributing to colorectal tumorigenesis. Over the long term, we aim to develop small molecules or antisense strategy that could directly target RNF6 in CRC. Based on our findings, we will apply for further basic research as well as R&D grant opportunities through a competitive basis. We will engage pharmaceutical companies to gain access to proprietary drug/antisense libraries, which will be used to screen for potential drug candidates for RNF6 with our CRC cell models and transgenic mice model. These studies will lead to filing of patents and valuable intellectual properties. Ultimately, we hope that our discoveries will lead to novel treatments for CRC patients.

14163817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14163817.value: Nature of the project: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is the number one cancer in Hong Kong, and its incidence is rapidly rising over the past decade. However, the molecular mechanism of CRC is far from clear. In this study, we identified Ring Finger Protein 6 (RNF6) as a novel oncogenic factor in CRC. Using a series of in vitro and in vivo experiments, including RNF6 transgenic mice, we comprehensively documented the oncogenic properties of RNF in CRC. We also investigated the molecular mechanism of RNF6, and unravelled that its ubiquitin ligase as well as transcriptional activities both contribute to its oncogenic effect, respectively, via its targets TLE3 and SF3B2. Significance: We demonstrated that RNF6 as an actionable target in CRC. The combination of targeting RNF6-SF3B2 axis in conjunction with 5-fluorouacil, synergized to inhibit the growth of CRC in vitro and in vivo, thereby implying the potential role of RNF6 as a chemotherapy sensitizing target. RNF6 is a novel, independent prognostic factor that could predict CRC patient prognosis. Value of the project: Strategies to disrupt RNF6 and its related signalling might be developed for the treatment of CRC. RNF6 might serve as a prognostic biomarker for CRC

14163917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14163917.value: The seemingly well-mixed and diluted oceans contain substantial heterogeneity both at micro-spatial scale and across ocean provinces. This includes heterogeneous distribution of nutrients (e.g., nitrogen, phosphorus, iron) among ocean regions. Seawater also contains transient hotspots at nanometer to millimeter scales as a result of cell lysis, sloppy feeding, photosynthetic extracellular release, and other processes, giving rise to nutrient concentrations up to three orders of magnitude higher than bulk seawater. Oxygen is similarly not equally available, and several mesopelagic ocean waters (200-800 m) are depleted with oxygen. In addition, temperature and light are other important factors that determine marine microbial diversity. Members of the marine Roseobacter clade are a great model to investigate the microbial evolution and adaptation under heterogeneous conditions. Roseobacters are prevalent in various ocean habitats. They represent up to 20% of the bacterial cells in coastal environments and 5% in open ocean surface waters, and frequently dominate the bacterial community associated with marine phytoplankton, macroalgae, and invertebrates. Consistent with their phenotypic diversity, roseobacters are well known for their metabolic versatility. For instance, many clade members evolved genetic capabilities to acquire energy through utilization of light and oxidation of inorganic compounds, and also possess genetic machinery to allow for interaction with host. Moreover, their genome size differs by a factor of >2 and GC content vary from below 40% to 70%. Much of this diversity is likely a result of adaptation to the heterogeneous environments that they inhabit, and thus provides excellent genetic material for this study. This project aims to understand adaptive mechanisms of marine roseobacters under distinct environmental conditions at the genome content level. This includes genomic analyses of a Roseobacter lineage sampled from ocean provinces with distinct iron, nitrogen, and phosphorus concentrations, of three Roseobacter species each sampled from surface water and deep sea, of Roseobacter populations co-occurring on particles and ambient seawater, and of Roseobacter genomic changes under low oxygen conditions. To support these analyses, we have developed several relevant bioinformatic approaches, obtained a number of Roseobacter cultures and uncultivated single cells, and downloaded Tara Ocean and other global metagenomic data sets. We will leverage these resources to investigate the impact of marine pelagic habitat heterogeneity on genome content diversification among roseobacters. 我們周圍看似稀釋且均勻混合的海洋實則在微觀和宏觀空間尺度上均有很大的異質性。例如，不同海域中的營養物（例如，鐵、氮、磷）呈現異質分佈。另外，由於海洋病毒攻擊導致的細胞裂解、原生動物捕食、光合作用導致的細胞外釋放等過程，海水普遍還含有納米至毫米級的瞬態營養熱點，導致熱點微環境中的營養物濃度超過海水本底值達三個數量級之多。此外，不同水層中氧氣分佈的不均勻性，溫度和光照的異質性也是導致海洋微生物多樣性的主要因素。 海洋玫瑰桿菌是研究微生物在異質條件下進化和適應的模式微生物類群。玫瑰桿菌在各種典型的海洋生境中都很普遍。它們在沿海海水中可以佔到高達20％的細菌數，在開放的大洋表面水中佔達5％，並且在附着于海洋藻類和無脊椎動物的細菌群落中也經常占主導。與他們的表型多樣性一致，玫瑰桿菌具有龐大的代謝和遺傳多樣性。例如，許多玫瑰桿菌通過利用光能或者氧化低價臺的無機化合物以獲得能量，並且還攜帶着与其共生的海洋植物和動物相互作用的各種代謝途徑。此外，不同玫瑰桿菌的基因組大小差異可達2倍以上而它們的GC含量（代表基因組的鹼基組成的最重要的指標）從低於40％至70％不等。這些多樣性中的很大部分可能是由於適應其所居住的異質環境而產生的，因此為本研究提供了極好的材料。 本項目旨在了解在基因組內容水平上不同環境條件下海洋玫瑰桿菌的適應機制。申請人提出進行以下多方面的分析以實現目標，包括從具有不同鐵、氮、磷濃度的海域採集的玫瑰桿菌的比較基因組學分析，從表層海水和深海採集的玫瑰桿菌的比較基因組學分析，從海洋中廣泛存在的顆粒物表面和其周圍海水採集的玫瑰桿菌的比較基因組學分析，以及從海洋低氧區和普通攜氧海水採集的玫瑰桿菌的比較基因組學分析。目前，申請人團隊已經開發了幾種相關的生物信息學方法，獲得了許多玫瑰桿菌的純培養和未培養的單細胞，並下載了全球宏基因組序列的海量數據。申請人團隊將利用這些資源對海洋環境異質性造成的玫瑰桿菌基因組內容多樣化進行系統地研究。

14163917.label: Major findings and research outcome
14163917.value: Some marine habitats are well separated and known to differ in physicochemical conditions. One good example is stony corals, which contain three physicochemically different compartments: mucus, tissue and skeleton. We collected a Roseobacter population which is separated into two clades corresponding to coral mucus and skeleton, respectively. The two clades show many functional differences that match well with the distinct physicochemical parameters associated with each coral compartment, such as periodic anoxia in skeleton and differential presence of osmolyte compounds in mucus. We also notice that many marine niches are mixed and cryptic. In this case, we use reverse ecology approaches. In one study, we isolated a Roseobacter population from an undisturbed seawater sample which is known to contain numerous microspatial niches relevant to microbial activities. We demonstrate that this population is under ongoing speciation, and the microscale niches created by bacteria-phytoplankton interactions may drive its speciation. In another study, we isolated a Roseobacter population from intertidal sediments. It has diverged into two emerging populations, each harbouring a unique type of nitrate reductase for nitrate respiration and showing evidence of adaptation to niches with different oxygen concentrations and organic substrate compositions. Next, we provide a novel angle to link Roseobacter genome content diveristy with heterogeneous niche adaptation. Different from the common perspective on the importance of horizontal gene transfer in bacterial niche differentiation, we highlight the opposite process - gene loss. We collected and sequenced the genomes of 279 closely related Roseobacter isolates from a coral ecosystem and a brown algal ecosystem, which harbor distinct ecological niches but co-located in Hong Kong waters. Through comprehensive comparative genomic analysis and ancestral state reconstructions, we show a correlation between niche shifts and genome content changes through pseudogenization. Finally, I want to highlight our successful cultivation of a novel pelagic (water column dwelling) Roseobacter cluster, which we named ‘CHUG’. They consistently possess some of the smallest genomes (~2.5 Mb) among all known Roseobacters (averaged >4 Mb). A prominent feature is that CHUG members are vitamin B12 auxotrophs, which differs from other pelagic Roseobacter clusters. Analysis of a global metagenomic and metatranscriptomic data set show that while the relative abundance and activity of other pelagic Roseobacter clusters are correlated with chlorophyll a concentration (proxy for phytoplankton biomass), this correlation is not evident for CHUG. Our results indicate that CHUG have evolved a free-living lifestyle decoupled from phytoplankton, highlighting the niche differentiation between pelagic Roseobacter lineages.

14163917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14163917.value: With the support from this project, we demonstrated that water column, intertidal sediments, and corals are excellent marine habitats for studying Roseobacter ecology and evolution. A natural next step is to investigate i) the impact of geographic differences within each type of habitat on Roseobacter evolution, and ii) the connection between sympatric Roseobacter populations from different types of habitats. Future studies should also combine cultivation-based population ecology with culture-independent approaches, which puts the population-level findings in context of the microbial communities.

14163917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14163917.value: Members of the Roseobacter group are highly abundant in coastal environments, making up one in five cells in the water column and one in ten cells in the surface sediments. They are also among the most abundant bacterial lineages associated with marine algae and invertebrates. Their ecological success is supported by a highly diverse genetic repertoire and their ecologically relevant genes often show patchy distribution among related lineages. This suggests that Roseobacter members can easily adjust their genome content and metabolic potential during niche adaptation. In this project, we investigated Roseobacter adaptation to heterogeneous marine habitats primarily through population ecology. By comparing closely related isolates at both genomic and physiological levels, we are able to elucidate recent selective pressures on genome evolution mainly imposed by ecological factors. Using this population ecology approach, we identified the key ecological factors that drive Roseobacter evolution in marine water column, intertidal sediments, and corals. We also illustrated that gene loss through pseudogenization is an important mechanism during Roseobacter niche transition. Finally, we cultivated a novel pelagic Roseobacter lineage which has some of the smallest genomes among all known Roseobacter members and demonstrated that it occupies completely different niches than other known pelagic Roseobacter members.

14164617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14164617.value: Plants are continuously subjected to both biotic challenges (e.g. pathogens) and abiotic stresses (e.g. drought and salinity), and translational regulation provides a rapid and efficient way to cope with these stresses by manipulating the translation of pre-existing mRNAs into functional proteins. We have previously identified the YchF1 protein from rice (OsYchF1) that is a negative regulator of both plant defense and abiotic stress responses and its functions are modulated by the C2-domain protein OsGAP1. OsYchF1 is an unconventional GTPase that can bind to both ATP and GTP. We have also found that it can interact with rRNAs and ribosomal proteins. Ribosomes are the “macromolecular machine” for the translation process. Plants have a high degree of heterogeneity among ribosomal proteins, suggesting that “specialized ribosomes” may play a role in translational regulation, while ribosome-associated proteins may modulate the functions and compositions of ribosomes according to tissue types and growth conditions. We have found that variations in the YchF levels in plants led to significant changes in protein profiles, including the levels of ribosomal proteins. Taken together, we may be on the verge of discovering a relatively unknown mechanism of regulating stress responses in plants through translational regulation. In this proposal, we will study the effects of the Arabidopsis YchF1 on the profile of translating mRNAs by comparing the RNA-Sequencing and Ribosome-Sequencing data. The importance of its ATP-binding ability and its interactions with rRNAs on protein translation profiles will be investigated, by using the AtYchF1-G4’ mutant we previously developed that has lost the ATP-binding capacity, and by overexpressing the AtGAP1 protein that can block the binding between AtYchF1 and rRNAs. Proteomic data will be collected in parallel in order to facilitate the interpretation of RNA-sequencing data. This research will enhance our understanding of a novel translational regulation mechanism in plants. 植物不斷受到生物（例如病原體）和非生物的脅迫（如乾旱和鹽害），而蛋白質轉譯調控通過操縱預先存在的mRNA轉譯成為功能蛋白，對這些威脅作出迅速和有效的應對。我們以前已經確定了水稻YchF1蛋白（OsYchF1）是植物生物和非生物脅迫的負調節因子，其功能由C2結構域蛋白OsGAP1所調節。 OsYchF1是可以結合ATP和GTP的非常規GTP酶。我們也發現它可以與rRNA和核醣體蛋白互作。核醣體是蛋白質轉譯的 「大分子機械」。植物的核醣體蛋白之間存在很高程度的異質性，由此推論「特異性核醣體」可能在轉譯調控中發揮作用。根據植物組織類型和生長條件，核醣體相關蛋白可能調節核醣體的功能和組成。我們發現植物中YchF蛋白水平的改變會引起蛋白表達譜的顯著變化，其中包括核醣體蛋白的水平。基於這些觀察，我們可能正在發現一個植物在環境壓力中通過轉譯調節的新機理。在這項研究計劃中，我們會以通過比較RNA測序和核醣體測序的數據，研究擬南芥YchF1對轉譯中mRNA表達的影響。另一方面，通過利用我們以前開發的ATP結合能力缺失突變體AtYchF1-G4'，以及表達可阻斷AtYchF1和rRNAs結合的AtGAP1蛋白，我們會調查擬南芥YchF1的ATP及rRNAs結合能力，在蛋白質翻譯譜上的互作。為了幫助對RNA序列數據的解讀，我們會並行收集蛋白質組學數據。這項研究將會增強我們對植物中新型轉譯調控機制的理解。

14164817.value: 二型糖尿病是一種慢性代謝疾病表現為血糖升高和胰島素抵抗。高糖引起的內皮細胞功能障礙是引起糖尿病血管併發症和心腦腎靶器官損傷的主要原因。高糖能上調NF-kB，MAPK，JNK等細胞內信號通路增加氧自由基產生，同時減少內皮依賴性舒張因子和增加內皮依賴性收縮因子，共同引起內皮細胞損傷。YAP/TAZ通路是一個新發現的參與轉錄調控的分子，在發育，代謝，癌症等生理病理活動中有重要作用。特別是在心血管系統發育和動脈粥樣硬化中發揮關鍵作用，但是YAP/TAZ在糖尿病血管病變中的作用仍未明確。 我們提出的假說是在內皮細胞，高糖環境能激活YAP/TAZ，引起糖尿病和肥胖小鼠的內皮細胞炎症反應和內皮功能障礙，YAP/TAZ通過與BMP4通路和JNK通路的相互影響發揮作用。 為了驗證我們的假說，我們將先檢測在內皮細胞中高糖是否能激活YAP/TAZ，並通過YAP/TAZ增加氧自由基，減少一氧化氮生物利用率，促進內皮細胞炎症反應。第二，我們將檢測抑制YAP/TAZ是否能減少內皮細胞炎症反應和抑制高糖誘導的BMP4-JNK通路及其相關的促炎因子表達和內皮功能障礙。我們將進一步在瘦素受體敲除的糖尿病小鼠和高脂飲食誘導的肥胖小鼠觀察YAP/TAZ的活性，最後利用基因組編輯技術Cas9進行內皮細胞特異性敲低Yap，檢測抑制內皮細胞Yap表達是否能改善糖尿病與肥胖小鼠的內皮功能障礙和血管炎症反應，同時抑制BMP4-JNK通路的活性。我們也會研究現有藥物如他汀類和小分子藥物是否通過抑制YAP/TAZ改善糖尿病和肥胖小鼠的內皮功能障礙。 我們的研究主要探討YAP/TAZ通路在二型糖尿病血管病變中的新作用，並提出新的作用機制和YAP/TAZ與其他信號分子的相互作用，為開發針對YAP/TAZ通路的心血管疾病藥物提供理論依據。

14165217.label: Project Objectives
14165217.value: Aim 1: To further clarify the functional role of Jmjd1a and Jmjd2c in hMSC senescence. We will knockdown Jmjd1a or Jmjd2c expression by a Tet-inducible lentiviral- shRNA vector in hESC-derived MSCs at different time points during serial passaging. We will use this innovative model to further elucidate the function of Jmjd1a and Jmjd2c in the onset and/or maintenance of heterochromatin and cellular senescence. Aim 2: To elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying Jmjd1a/Jmjd2c-mediated regulation of heterochromatin reorganization. We will perform RNA-seq assays to compare gene expression profiles between MSCs with Jmjd1a or Jmjd2c overexpression and MSCs with Jmjd1a or Jmjd2c knockdown to define gene expression changes regulated by Jmjd1a or Jmjd2c. This will allow us to identify key centromere packaging and chromosome condensation genes involved in the MSC senescence. We will also perform biochemical studies, including imaging, CHIP-PCR and co-immunoprecipitation, to test our hypothesis that Jmjd1a/Jmjd2c regulates heterochromatin reorganization via two distinctive roles: their demethylase function through modulating H3K9 and their scaffold function through recruiting heterochromatin complex proteins. Aim 3: To evaluate the role of Jmjd1a in the aging process using Jmjd1a knockout mice. We will use Jmjd1a knockout mice in 129SVEV/C57BL/6 background to further evaluate the role of Jmjd1a in osteoporosis. In addition, small molecules targeting Jmjd1a will be tested for their therapeutic effects in osteoporotic mice in order to provide potential epigenetic targets for disease intervention.
