14169717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14169717.value: Aim: The aim of this project is to elucidate the function of the primate-specific microRNA-1202 in human dopaminergic (DA) neurons. Background: Many miRNAs are evolutionarily conserved whereas a small number of them are found only in primates. miR-1202 is a primate-specific miRNA that was previously revealed as being involved in major depression disorder (MDD). Moreover, the genomic locus where miR-1202 located on (6q25.3) is strongly associated with recurrent early-onset MDD and neurodevelopmental disorder. Our preliminary results, together with others, suggest that miR-1202 is brain-enriched and tightly regulated during DA neuron differentiation. Concomitant with this, we and others have also identified several genes related to neurotransmitter transport and neuronal differentiation (SYPL2, GRM4, LIF and LMX1A) as the targets of miR-1202. Therefore, we hypothesize that miR-1202 plays a unique role in DA neurogenesis to fine-tune the transcriptional network central to the dopamine-related phenotypes, which may account for the role of DA neurons in MDD and other neuropsychiatric disorders. Objectives: We propose to perform experiments to identify 1) the consequences for DA neuron differentiation of miR-1202 overexpression or inhibition; 2) the interacting targets of miR-1202 and their significance to DA neurons; 3) upstream regulators for miR-1202. Significance of the project: Our proposed study will advance our understanding of the regulatory small RNAs evolved in primates, as typified by miR-1202 in the neural system. It will enable us to delineate that part of the regulatory network in DA neurons that is unique to humans and other primates. This will lay the groundwork for further research with potential clinical benefits in the field of depression and other psychiatric disorders. 目標： 該項目的目的是闡明靈長類動物特有的microRNA-1202在人類多巴胺能（DA）神經元中的功能。 背景： 許多miRNA在進化上被保存下來，而少數miRNA僅在靈長類動物中出現。 miR-1202是被揭示為參與重度抑鬱症（MDD）的靈長類動物特有的miRNA。此外，miR-1202位於（6q25.3）上的基因組位點與復發性早發性MDD和神經發育障礙密切相關。我們的初步結果與其他的結果都表明miR-1202在DA神經元分化過程中是在大腦大量表達和被緊密調節的。與此同時，我們和其他人還鑑定了與神經遞質轉運和神經元分化相關的幾個基因（SYPL2，GRM4，LIF和LMX1A）作為miR-1202的靶標。因此，我們假設miR-1202在DA神經發生中起著獨特的作用，以微調多巴胺相關表型的中樞轉錄網絡，這可能解釋了DA神經元在MDD和其他神經精神障礙中的作用。 目標： 我們建議以實驗去確定1）miR-1202過表達或抑制對DA神經元分化的後果; 2）與miR-1202相互作用的靶標及其對DA神經元的重要性; 3）miR-1202的上游調節因子。 項目重要性： 我們提出的研究將提高我們對靈長類動物中的調控小RNA的理解，正如神經系統中miR-1202所代表的。這將使我們能夠描繪巴胺能神經元在人類和其他靈長類動物中獨有的調控網絡。為進一步研究抑鬱症和其他精神疾病奠定基礎，具有潛在的臨床益處。

14169717.label: Realisation of objectives
14169717.value: In this project, we proposed three objectives, as listed above. Objective 1 is to elucidate the role of miR-1202 in DA neuron differentiation. Before the submission of the research grant application, we first profiled miRNA expression during neuronal differentiation from induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSC) (Tu et al., 2018) (Research output #4). hsa-miR-1202 (miR-1202) was a candidate miRNA differentially expressed in dopaminergic (DA) neuronal culture but not in cortical neuronal culture. We additionally tested an inducible system for the expression of transgenes in DA neuronal cultures. Unexpectedly, we found that tetracycline such as doxycycline could mask the genuine effect of the transgene induced by doxycycline (Cao et al., 2019) (Research output #1). We therefore switched to a 3-dimentional midbrain-like organoid model for studying DA neuron differentiation. This brain organoid system not only could be used for studying loss-of-function of miR-1202, but also could be used for studying pathogen-host interaction, such as neuroinvasion of SARS-CoV-2 in the brain (Hou et al., 2022) (Research output #3). To elucidate the role of miR-1202 in DA neuron differentiation, we generated miR-1202 knockout (KO) cells in human pluripotent stem cells (hPSC). We generated three miR-1202 KO lines (two single cells derived KO and one mixed cells derived KO). We subsequently generated midbrain organoids using these KO lines and compared the results with the normal wild-type (WT) cells. Interestingly, we found that miR-1202 KO organoids grew into smaller size and lower weight, and the KO organoids contained less Ki-67+ (an active proliferation marker) cells. Consistent with the smaller size, more neuronal differentiation was observed, suggesting that miR-1202 loss promoted neuronal differentiation. We analyzed markers for DA neurons (FOXA2, OTX2, LMX1A, EN1, DDC and TH) by qPCR and immunofluorescent staining. Both analyses suggested that miR-1202 KO promoted DA differentiation by upregulation these marker genes. We also performed RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) to profile the transcriptomic changes when miR-1202 was deleted. Pathway enrichment analysis showed upregulations of biological processes in dopaminergic neurogenesis, nervous system development, regulation of neurotransmitter receptor activity and neuron differentiation. Besides, biological process in anterior/posterior pattern specification was significantly downregulated. We confirmed changes of critical markers by qPCR, immunofluorescent staining and Western blot. Furthermore, we confirmed the increase of dopamine level in the culture media by LC-MS. Together, these results supported our hypothesis that miR-1202 plays a role in the brain development, particular in the midbrain DA neurogenesis. We concluded that Objective 1 was 100% achieved. Objective 2 is to identify the downstream targets of miR-1202 and characterize their functions. To achieve this objective, we performed RNA pulldown-seq experiments to capture mRNAs that interact with miR-1202. By this method, 697 genes (the candidate genes) were identified to interact with miR-1202 mimics. However, only 13 candidate genes were found upregulated in miR-1202 KO cells. Further bioinformatics analysis revealed that only 5 candidate genes contained the predicted miR-1202 binding site at their UTR. These genes included POU3F2, ADCYAP1R1, TTYH1, DCLK2, and APC2. Among these genes, we focused on APC2 in the subsequent studies because only APC2 was enriched in the brain. We thus generated APC2 knockdown cells in miR-1202 KO hPSC because APC2 expression was increased in the KO cells. We generated midbrain organoid using these APC2 knockdown cells. As anticipated, APC2 knockdown resulted in attenuated DA neurogenesis. As APC2 is a negative regulator of the canonical WNT/b-catenin signaling pathway, the increased APC2 expression in miR-1202 KO organoids weakened WNT/b-catenin signaling and hence promoted midbrain DA neurogenesis. In APC2 knockdown cells, WNT/b-catenin signaling was enhanced, and therefore midbrain DA neurogenesis was inhibited. These results were consistent with other studies that WNT signaling plays temporally distinct roles in the early central nerve system and midbrain development (Mulligan and Cheyette, 2012). It is also reported that strong WNT/β-catenin signaling inhibits the differentiation of WNT/β-catenin responding mesodiencephalic DA (mdDA) progenitors into PITX3+ and TH+ mdDA neurons by repressing the Pitx3 in mice (Nouri et al., 2020). We concluded that Objective 2 was 100% achieved. Objective 3 is to identify the upstream regulator of miR-1202. To achieve this objective, we treated the midbrain organoids with antidepressant drugs citalopram and imipramine. As anticipated, miR-1202 expressions were increased by both drugs in both acute (24h treatment) and chronic (14d treatment) conditions. DA neurogenesis markers was decreased accordingly. Consistent with the increased miR-1202 expression, APC2 was decreased, suggesting that both miR-1202 and APC2 were responsive to the antidepressant treatments. Interestingly, we also found APC2 upregulation in postmortem brain tissues in patients with major depression disorder (MDD). Because citalopram and imipramine promote serotonin neurotransmitter retention, the treatments may stimulate serotonergic neurogenesis and suppress DA neurogenesis through miR-1202. We additionally treated organoids with L-DOPA, a dopamine precursor molecule used to treat patients with Parkinson disease. Surprisingly, acute treatment stimulated miR-1202 expression, whereas chronic treatment suppressed miR-1202 expression. Together, our results suggested that antidepressants such as citalopram and imipramine (and perhaps L-DOPA) are upstream regulators of miR-1202. Overall, we concluded that Objective 3 was 100% achieved. A manuscript titled “Primate-specific microRNA-1202 regulates dopaminergic neurogenesis by targeting APC2 and modulates WNT/b-catenin signaling pathway in midbrain organoid” has been prepared based on the results of the project (Long et al., manuscript under preparation) (Research output #5). Moreover, we also published a review paper on the use of stem cells for the therapy of Parkinson disease (Liu and Cheung, 2020) (Research output #2). References: Cao, D., Cheung, H.H., and Chan, W.Y. 14169717.label: Major findings and research outcome
14169717.value: The major findings from this project are summarized below: First, we employed an organoid model that permitted us to study the function of miR-1202 to mimic the developing brain. Through this model, we demonstrated that miR-1202 is upregulated in the developing brain organoids. We observed that miR-1202 KO repressed organoid growth and cell proliferation but promoted neuronal differentiation. Transcriptomic analysis showed the upregulation of dopaminergic neurogenesis in miR-1202 KO cells. Using the RNA pulldown-seq approach, we identified APC2 as the direct interacting target with miR-1202. APC2 expression is highly enriched in the brain and is a negative regulator of the canonical WNT signaling pathway. MiR-1202 suppressed APC2 through directly binding to its 3’UTR and thus loss of miR-1202 inhibited β-catenin signaling to modulate the DA neurogenesis. This effect was abrogated by knocking down APC2 in miR-1202 knockout cells. We also demonstrated that both miR-1202 and APC2 responded to antidepressants, implying a role of this regulatory axis in psychiatric disorders. In summary, we identified a previously unknown role of the primate specific miR-1202 in the brain development, which may serve as a determinant or modulator in switching the dopaminergic and serotonergic fates in the midbrain-hindbrain boundary.

14169717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14169717.value: Through this project, we have defined a role of the miR-1202 in the brain. That is, in the normal brain development, miR-1202 suppresses the midbrain dopamine phenotype and promotes hindbrain serotonin phenotype through regulating the APC2/WNT signaling axis. Loss of miR-1202 promotes DA neurogenesis while suppressing serotonergic differentiation. This explains the phenomenon that miR-1202 expression is decreased in patients with depression. Accordingly, antidepressant treatment stimulates miR-1202 and thus modulates serotonin phenotype. Although our results supported this hypothesis with phenotypic data such as the increased OTX2 expression and the decreased GBX2 expression when miR-1202 was deleted, an in vivo test in animals is still lacking. Because miR-1202 cannot be found in common laboratory mammals (e.g. mouse, rat and rabbit), in vivo test of miR-1202 is challenging. The future research can focus on a humanized animal model that allows in vivo tests of drugs on animals transplanted with human brain organoids. With such humanized animal model established, it will be highly interesting to test whether in vivo delivery of synthetic miR-1202 (e.g. through conjugated in nanoparticles) to the human brain cells will stimulate neurotransmitter synthesis. This allows further translational research on using miRNA as therapeutic drugs.

14169717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14169717.value: Our project studies a small regulatory molecule called microRNA (miR-1202) in the brain. As we cannot get access into human brain tissues, we employed human stem cells to generate brain-like tissues to study the function of this microRNA. We generated neurons in a self-organized 3D structures that mimics the normal development in mid-part of the brain. We deleted the microRNA in stem cells. We found that deletion of the microRNA made our neuron more easily to form dopaminergic neuron, which is essential for producing a neurotransmitter called dopamine. Through molecular studies, we found that miR-1202 controls a gene called APC2. This gene can control the brain development through changing the activity of an intracellular signaling called WNT. WNT is important in determining the regional identity in the developing brain, whether it should develop into the midbrain or the hindbrain. We further found that miR-1202 and APC2 levels are changed when neurons are exposed to antidepressant drugs. These results are significant because they suggest an explanation to patients who receive antidepressants drugs, and provide a molecular basis to what happens in the neural cells in the brain when the microRNA is dysregulated, and help to understand the psychiatric disorder.

14169817.label: Project Objectives
14169817.value: To examine whether sleep extension that occurs during holidays would lead to a reduction in BP in sleep deprived adolescents.
rows: To examine whether sleep extension that occurs during holidays would lead to a reduction in BP in sleep deprived adolescents.

14169817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14169817.value: Our research question is: Are changes in sleep duration that occur naturally over school holidays associated with changes in blood pressure (BP) in sleep-deprived adolescents? Sleep deprivation is one of the common, clinically important and potentially reversible health risks in modern society. A great proportion of local adolescents are getting less than the recommended hours of sleep during school term. Chronic sleep deprivation affects academic performance and neurocognitive function. Our group shows that short sleep duration is independently associated with elevated ambulatory BP in normal weight adolescents. Any BP abnormality in children and adolescents should be dealt with promptly to minimize future risks of adulthood hypertension and adverse cardiovascular events. Delaying school start time is a mean to increase sleep duration but in our locality such suggestion is met with resistance from parents, teachers and school bus companies. Adolescents tend to sleep compensate during school holidays, and the difference in the amount of sleep between school term and holiday can be up to 2-3 hours. In this study, we will take advantage of changes in sleep duration that occur during school holidays in adolescents who are sleep deprived (>6 months’ history of sleeping <8 hours per night during school term). We will monitor changes in ambulatory BP and sleep duration over a period of 3 weeks which consist of a week at school, followed by a week of holiday when natural sleep extension takes place, and then another week of school after the holiday. Sleep-wake cycle will be recorded throughout the whole study period with actigraphy and sleep diary. Twenty-four hour ambulatory BP monitoring will be performed on the same weekday during each study week, when salivary cortisol will also be collected. The primary outcome is difference in ambulatory BP parameters between school term and holiday. A control group without sleep deprivation (history of sleeping >8 hours per night) will also be studied concurrently. We hypothesize that changes in sleep duration are negatively associated with changes in BP. If this study confirms our hypothesis, sleep extension can be used as a relatively inexpensive and simple behavioural intervention in the management and prevention of blood pressure abnormalities. More importantly positive results from this project will provide background information on which government and local school policy can be based and altered for the betterment of our youths. 我們的研究問題是：睡眠缺乏的青少年在學校假期時的睡眠時 間變化與他們的血壓變化有關聯嗎？睡眠不足是現代社會常見 而重要卻又可能可逆轉的健康風險之一。在學期期間，大部份 本地青少年的睡眠時間都少於建議的睡眠時間。長期睡眠不足 會影響學業成績和神經認知功能。另外，我們的研究小組發現 正常體重的青少年的睡眠時間越短動態血壓就越高。兒童和青 少年的血壓異常應得到及時處理，才可減低他們成年後患上高 血壓和發生不良心血管事件的風險。延遲學校開課時間是增加 睡眠時間的一種有效方法，但這建議卻受到本地家長，教師和 校車公司的反對。青少年往往會在假期期間補眠，學期與休假 時的睡眠量可相差達2-3小時。在這項研究中，我們將觀察長期 睡眠不足的青少年（超過6個月於學期期間每晚睡眠少於8小時） 在假期期間發生的睡眠時間變化。我們會安排受試者進行三個 星期動態血壓和睡眠時間的監測，其中包括第一個星期在上學 期間、第二個星期在假期期間、以及第三個星期於假期後上學 期間進行。受試者每天的睡眠時間將會以腕部活動監視儀和睡 眠日記作記錄。他們亦會於每個研究週的同一個工作日進行24 小時動態血壓監測及收集唾液樣本作皮質醇測量。研究的主要 結果指標是學期和假期之間的動態血壓的差異。我們也會邀請 沒有睡眠缺乏的青少年（睡眠時間多於每晚8小時）加入對照 組同時進行監測。我們假設睡眠時間的變化與血壓的變化是負 相關的。如研究結果證實了我們的假設，睡眠延長將可用作管 理和預防高血壓，是一個相對便宜而簡單的的行為治療。更重 要的是，政府將可根據這項研究的結果以改變學校相關的政策 從而令我們的青少年有更好的成長。

14169817.label: Realisation of objectives
14169817.value: A total of 222 subjects underwent screening, of whom 14 were not eligible to participate due to being outside of our recruitment age range (n=1), obesity (n = 8), presence of sleep disorder (n = 3), failure to provide parental consent (n = 2). 208 subjects have consented to participate and took part in the study. Enrolled subjects were monitored in 3 weekly study periods that included two periods of 7-day school attendance and one period of 7-day school holiday. During each study period, subjects underwent sleep-wake pattern monitoring by actigraphy for at least 5 days, 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure (ABP) monitoring, and saliva sample collection for cortisol and cortisone level determination. A total of 77 subjects (37%) failed to complete the study protocol and were excluded from the study, of whom 41 (20%) refused to come back for a follow-up and 36 (17%) had less than 5 days of actigraphy data at one or more visits. The remaining 131 subjects completed the study protocol, of whom 109 were assigned to the school day-holiday-school day protocol, whereas 22 were assigned to the holiday-school day-school day sequence. Based on their screening questionnaire date, 66 and 45 of them were categorized into sleep-deprived (weekday time in bed <8h and self-perceived sleep insufficiency) and normal sleep (weekday time in bed ≥8h and self-perceived sufficient sleep) groups, respectively. The remaining 20 subjects were unable to be classified into either group. The sleep-deprived group was older (15.0±1.0 vs. 13.9±1.2, p<0.001) and had a more advanced Tanner stage [4(4 to 4) vs. 3(3 to4), p<0.001] than the normal sleep group. Their self-report time in bed was shorter than the normal sleep group during school days (391±55 vs. 511±31 min, p<0.001) but was similar during weekends and holidays. They were also sleepier (ESS; 10±4 vs. 8±4, p=0.003; PDSS; 17±4 vs. 13±5, p<0.001) than the normal sleep group. The sleep-deprived group had a greater increase in sleep duration during holidays, especially during weekdays (all p<0.01). The sleep-deprived group also had better sleep efficiency regardless of school days or holidays. They tended to have less decrease in sleep efficiency during holidays although the difference was not statistically significant (p>0.05). However, there were no significant between-group differences in the changes of any salivary cortisol and ambulatory BP outcomes. We expected that the increase in sleep duration from school days to holidays would be much greater for subjects with shorter sleep during weekdays. However, the preliminary analysis revealed that the mean difference between the sleep-deprived and normal sleep groups was only 44 minutes. Therefore, categorizing subjects into sleep-deprived and normal sleep groups is not a good way to investigate the effect of an increase in sleep duration on BP changes. To directly test for the effect of the change in sleep duration across holidays on the BP, a posthoc analysis was performed to directly test the effect of the change in sleep duration on BP outcomes. Subjects were divided into two groups based on their increase in weekday nocturnal sleep duration during holidays. Those who increased by <1.5 hours were grouped as a sleep stable group, whereas those who increased by ≥1.5 hours were grouped as a sleep extended group. The two groups were similar in terms of their age, sex, and body size. The sleep extended group had less weekday time in bed as reported in their screening questionnaire (417±69 vs. 462±70 min, p<0.001) and they also had higher sleepiness scores than the sleep stable group (PDSS; 17±5 vs 14±5, p=0.005), which might predispose to a greater sleep extension during the holiday. For the sleep duration data, the sleep extended group had a much greater increase in sleep duration during the holiday when compared to the stable sleep group. Moreover, the sleep extended group had a less reduction in sleep efficiency during the holiday when compared to the stable sleep group. For the salivary cortisol awakening response (CAR), there were no significant differences in the changes between the sleep extended and the stable sleep groups. For the BP outcomes, the sleep extended group had a greater drop in 24-hour SBP, 24-hour DBP, and wake DBP during holidays when compared to the stable sleep group. However, although there were significant drops in these parameters from school day 1 to holiday, no significant increases from holiday to school day 2 could be observed. (Table 1) Dr. Chun Ting Au, who is a Research Assistant Professor in the Department of Paediatrics was co-supervising the work of the research assistant and helped in the data analysis of this project. He presented part of the results at the World Sleep Congress and was awarded the Young Investigator Award.

14169817.label: Major findings and research outcome
14169817.value: To summarise, the sleep-deprived group had a greater increase in sleep duration than the normal sleep group during holidays. However, there were no significant differences in the changes of any ABP parameters between the sleep-deprived and the normal sleep groups. Post-hoc analysis was performed to compare the sleep extended group (weekday nocturnal sleep increased by ≥1.5h) to the sleep stable group (increased by <1.5h). The sleep extended group had a greater drop in 24-hour SBP, 24-hour DBP, and wake DBP during holidays when compared to the stable sleep group. The differences were unlikely to be attributed to the changes in cortisol during holidays because there were no significant differences in the changes in salivary cortisol awakening response between groups. These findings suggest a causal relationship between the extension of sleep duration and the reduction in blood pressure in adolescents, despite a small effect size.

14169817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14169817.value: Sleep extension achieved by modifying the lifestyle and sleep-wake pattern is a potentially useful intervention for a specific group of hypertensive patients with sleep deprivation. Further studies should examine the effect of sleep extension on these patients with a more standardized protocol of sleep extension, which may be achieved by gradually advancing the bedtime across weeks/months. Further studies should also examine the effect of sleep extension on the other cardiovascular outcomes or the health outcomes of other aspects. The interaction effects between sleep quantity, sleep quality, and various sleep disorders such as sleep-disordered breathing and insomnia on health outcomes are also interesting to explore. We are going to conduct a retrospective analysis of our sleep laboratory data to investigate the effect of sleep duration and sleep disorder on blood pressure as well as neurocognitive and behavioral outcomes. Besides, we are also planning to explore and verify the causal relationship between sleep duration and other health outcomes, including metabolic and neurocognitive function.

14169817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14169817.value: This study examined whether natural sleep extension during holidays would lead to a reduction in BP in sleep-deprived adolescents, with an observational study design involving 3 weekly study periods that included two periods of 7-day school attendance and 1 period of 7-day school holiday. During each study period, subjects had sleep monitoring for at least 5 days and 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure (ABP) monitoring on a weekday. A total of 131 non-obese healthy adolescents aged 12-16 years without sleep disorders were included, of whom 66 and 45 were categorized into Sleep Deprived (weekday time in bed <8h and self-perceived sleep insufficiency) and Normal Sleep (weekday time in bed ≥8h and self-perceived sufficient sleep) groups respectively. The former group had a greater increase in sleep duration during holidays. However, there were no significant between-group differences in the changes of any ambulatory BP outcomes. Further analysis dividing participants into sleep extended (weekday sleep extended by ≥1.5h) and stable sleep (weekday sleep extended by <1.5h) groups showed that the sleep extended group had a greater drop in 24-hour SBP, 24-hour DBP, and wake DBP during the holiday, suggesting a possible causal relationship between sleep extension and blood pressure reduction in adolescents.

14171217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14171217.value: The aim of this project is to identify and characterize circular RNAs with critical roles in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). PDAC is aggressive and the available therapies are ineffective. Though the roles of the key proteins such as KRas, p53, p16 and DPC4 in PDAC have been well documented, overall survival of patients has little improvement in the past 20 years. It is of urgent significance to identify novel diagnostic markers and therapeutic targets. Circular RNA (circRNA) is one class of non-coding RNAs that the 3' end of the exon links back to its 5' end, forming a circular structure. Emerging evidence suggests that circRNAs play important roles in various biological processes and even cancer development. However, the roles of circRNAs in PDAC remains largely unexplored. We have been attempting to identify circRNAs associated with PDAC. Using RNA sequencing followed by bioinformatics analysis, we identified 169 circRNAs which were differentially expressed in non-tumor human pancreatic ductal epithelial HPDE and PDAC cell lines. We selected the up-regulated circRNAs and characterized their unique circular structures. We validated that two circRNAs circGANAB and circRTN4 were significantly up-regulated in PDAC cell lines and primary tumor tissues. The roles of these two circRNAs have never been reported. Knock-down of these two circRNAs by siRNAs significantly inhibited PDAC cell growth. Knock-down of these two circRNAs also dramatically inhibited PDAC cell invasion in vitro. Bioinformatics analysis and luciferase reporter assay suggested that circGANAB may serve as a sponge for MiR-127-5p and miR-2355-5p, while circRTN4 may be a sponge for MiR-15a-5p, miR-16-5p and miR-497-5p. All these miRNAs have been shown to play tumor suppressive roles in PDAC. We further found that siRNAs targeting circGANAB and circRTN4 dramatically inhibited the expression of the miRNA targets Bcl-6, Biliverdin reductase B (BLVRB), Aldehyde Dehydrogenase 1 Family Member A3 (ALDH1A3) and vacuole membrane protein 1 (VMP-1), Bcl-2, Bmi-1 and FGFR. The oncogenic roles of these proteins in PDAC have been well documented. These preliminary data prompted us to believe that circGANAB and circRTN4 are actively involved in PDAC development. In this proposal, we intend to 1) characterize the functional roles of circGANAB and circRTN4; 2) delineate the mechanisms underlying circGANAB and circRTN4’s oncogenic roles; 3) investigate the clinical implication of circGANAB and circRTN4 in PDAC. Knowledge gained from this project will reveal the roles of circRNAs in PDAC and potentially lead to novel diagnostic markers and therapeutic targets. 本項目的目的是鑑定及研究對胰腺癌形成起重大作用的環狀RNA。胰腺癌是一種極具侵略性的癌症，而且現時缺乏有效的治療方法。雖然過去研究顯示KRas， p53， p16 及 DPC4對胰腺癌的形成起重大作用，但是整體存活率在這二十年間仍是十分低。因此，發展針對胰腺癌的新診斷及治療方法具有重要意義。環狀RNA (circRNA) 是一種非編碼RNA。它的3’端跟5’端連接，形成環狀。 愈來愈多的研究發現環狀RNA參與不同的生物過程，甚至影響癌症形成。不過，環狀RNA在胰腺癌形成中的功能仍未被發現。 在這次研究，我們通過RNA測序及生物訊息學的分析，發現了169個在胰腺癌細胞系中有差異表達的circRNA。我們選擇表達量有顯著的上調的circRNA，並在其他細胞系及病人組織樣本中驗證。當中，我們集中研究兩個circRNA: circGANAB 及circRTN4。敲低circGANAB 及circRTN4明顯地抑制癌細胞的生長及侵略性。生物訊息學的分析顯示circGANAB能作為microRNA miR-127-5p 及miR-2355-5p的海綿，而circRTN4則作為miR-15a-5p、miR-16-5p及miR-497-5p的海綿。研究顯示這些miRNAs抑壓不同癌症的發展。 此外，我們發現敲低circGANAB抑壓miR-127-5p 及miR-2355-5p 目標: Bcl-6、BLVRB、ALDH1A3及VMP-1的表達，而敲低circRTN4則抑壓miR-15a-5p、miR-16-5p及miR-497-5p目標: Bcl-2、Bmi-1 及 FGFR的表達。因此，我們的研究顯示circGANAB 及circRTN4 在胰腺癌形成中起重要作用。 在本項目，我們會繼續研究circGANAB 及circRTN4的其他功用，以及他們的生物機制。我們亦會在更多的病人組織樣本中研究circGANAB 及circRTN4在胰腺癌的重要性。這些研究能有助我們發展新的診斷及治療方法。

14171217.label: Realisation of objectives
14171217.value: All the project objectives have been achieved. CircRTN4 was upregulated in PDAC CircRNA sequencing was performed using non-tumor HPDE cell and PDAC PANC-1, SW1990 cells to identify circRNAs that play critical roles in PDAC. Among these dysregulated circRNAs, circRTN4 was significantly upregulated in PDAC cells. Also, we found that circRTN4 was significantly upregulated in 60% of the PDAC primary tumors (53 out of 88), while 18% of PDAC patients showed downregulated circRTN4 (16 out of 88), and 22% of PDAC patients showed unchanged circRTN4 (19 out of 88). Furthermore, we correlated circRTN4 expression level with clinical characteristics. We found that PDAC patients with liver metastasis had significantly upregulated circRTN4 expression level in their primary tumors , suggesting that the upregulated circRTN4 in PDAC primary tumors may involve in liver metastasis. Moreover, circRTN4 expression level was increased in male PDAC patients and patients aged 60 or above . In addition to PDAC, we found that circRTN4 was frequently upregulated in multiple cancers, including colorectal cancer, laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma, head-neck squamous cell Carcinoma, ovarian cancer, and kidney cancer. Collectively, these results suggested that the upregulated circRTN4 play important roles in PDAC. CircRTN4 promoted PDAC cell growth, migration and invasion in vitro To examine the functional roles of circRTN4 in PDAC, we used siRNAs which specifically targeted the back-splicing junction of circRTN4 without altering the expression of its parental RTN4 mRNA. CircRTN4 knockdown significantly inhibited PDAC cell growth and clonogenic ability. The suppression in cell growth was due to cell cycle arrest in G0-G1 phase and the induction of apoptosis. PDAC cell migration and invasion were also restrained after circRTN4 knockdown. In addition, circRTN4 knockdown by the lentiviral sh-circRTN4 vector inhibited cell growth, migration, and invasion in PDAC cells. On the other hand, circRTN4 overexpression in non-tumor HPDE cells significantly promoted cell growth, clonogenic ability and cell invasion. Collectively, our results demonstrated the importance of circRTN4 in promoting PDAC cell growth and invasion. CircRTN4 promoted PDAC tumor growth and liver metastasis in vivo To investigate the functional roles of circRTN4 in PDAC in vivo, mice xenograft model was generated by subcutaneous injection of CFPAC-1 sh-circRTN4 cells. CircRTN4 knockdown by shRNA significantly suppressed tumor growth. The decrease in cell proliferation marker Ki67 and anti-apoptotic protein Bcl-2 also indicated the inhibition of tumor growth by circRTN4 knockdown. Since in vitro studies revealed that circRTN4 promoted PDAC migration and invasion, we constructed a metastatic mice model through orthotopic injection of CFPAC-1 sh-circRTN4 cells to the pancreas. We found that circRTN4 knockdown inhibited PDAC metastasis to the liver. Collectively, our results suggested the functional importance of circRTN4 in promoting PDAC tumor growth and liver metastasis. CircRTN4 promoted lncRNA HOTTIP expression by sponging miR-497-5p We next investigated the detailed mechanism of circRTN4-mediated PDAC progression. CircRNAs frequently function as miRNA sponges in regulating gene expression, we investigated whether circRTN4 also functioned as a miRNA sponge in promoting PDAC progression. Bioinformatics analysis by TargetScan revealed the potential miRNA binding sites on circRTN4. To prove the circRTN4-miRNA interaction, luciferase assay using pmiR-circRTN4 reporter was performed after transfecting the miRNA mimics. Transfection of miR-497-5p mimics resulted in a reduction in luciferase activity. Conversely, mutating the miR-497-5p binding site of the pmiR-circRTN4 reporter could restore the luciferase activity. CircRTN4-miR-497-5p interaction was further validated by miRNA pull-down. Biotin-labelled miR-497-5p remarkably enriched circRTN4 in PANC-1 cells. These results suggested the interaction between circRTN4 and miR-497-5p in PDAC cells. We next studied the functional roles of circRTN4-miR-497-5p interaction in PDAC. We demonstrated that circRTN4 knockdown increased the expression of miR-497-5p, whereas transfecting miR-497-5p mimics did not alter the expression of circRTN4. Collectively, our results suggested that circRTN4 functioned as a sponge of miR-497-5p in PDAC cells. MiR-497-5p functions as a tumor suppressor in PDAC through targeting the oncogenic HOTTIP-HOXA13 pathway. Since circRTN4 acts as a sponge for miR-497-5p, we hypothesized that circRTN4 regulates HOTTIP-HOXA13 pathway via sponging miR-497-5p in PDAC. CircRTN4 knockdown significantly inhibited the expression of HOTTIP and HOXA13. Moreover, circRTN4 overexpression promoted the expression of HOTTIP and HOXA13 in HPDE cells. In addition, transfection of miR-497-5p mimics rescued the effects of circRTN4 on the expression of HOTTIP and HOXA13. Importantly, circRTN4 level was positively correlated to the upregulated HOTTIP level in PDAC primary tumors. These results suggested that circRTN4 functioned as a sponge of miR-497-5p to promote the expression of HOTTIP in PDAC. CircRTN4 stabilized RAB11FIP1 to promote EMT Although circRNAs-miRNAs interaction is the most reported roles of circRNAs in PDAC, many circRNAs are found to have much lower abundance than miRNAs. This suggests that circRNAs may have additional mechanisms in PDAC. Therefore, to further investigate the roles of circRTN4 in PDAC progression, we performed circRTN4-pull down to identify circRTN4-interacting proteins in PDAC cells. In vitro-transcribed circRTN4 functioned as a probe to pull down circRTN4-interacting proteins in PDAC cells. Mass-spectrometry analysis identified 99 proteins significantly enriched by circRTN4. In addition, analysis using the STRING database revealed 90 protein-protein interactions (PPI) for the circRTN4-interacting proteins. Gene ontology analysis also suggested the critical roles of circRTN4-interacting proteins in multiple biological processes, including cadherin binding, cell adhesion and translation initiation. Particularly, we found that circRTN4 interacted with RAB11FIP1, which plays important roles in promoting cell migration and invasion in cancers. CircRTN4-RAB11FIP1 interaction was further validated by RNA immunoprecipitation assay in PDAC cells. Bioinformatics analysis by PRIdictor also revealed the RAB11FIP1-binding site on circRTN4. Mutating the RAB11FIP1-binding site on circRTN4 significantly inhibited the circRTN4-RAB11FIP1 interaction in PANC-1 cells. These confirmed that circRTN4 interacted with RAB11FIP1 in PDAC cells. We then investigated the functions of this interaction in PDAC. We found that knockdown of circRTN4 downregulated the RAB11FIP1 expression, without affecting its mRNA level. Importantly, circRTN4 knockdown decreased the stability of RAB11FIP1 in PDAC cells. We then further investigated the detailed mechanism on how circRTN4 regulated the stability of RAB11FIP1. Previous study showed that ubiquitination at the Lysine578 (Lys578) residue of RAB11FIP1 is required for its degradation. Notably, we revealed the 3-Dimensional structure of circRTN4-RAB11FIP1 interaction by HDOCK, and found that circRTN4 blocked the ubiquitination site Lys578 on RAB11FIP1. Also, circRTN4 knockdown in PDAC cells promoted the ubiquitination of RAB11FIP1. Importantly, circRTN4 level was positively correlated to the RAB11FIP1 level in PDAC primary tumors. These suggested that circRTN4 interacted with RAB11FIP1 and enhanced the stability of RAB11FIP1 through inhibiting its ubiquitination in PDAC. RAB11FIP1 plays important roles in promoting cancer migration and invasion through regulating the expression of EMT-related proteins. Therefore, we hypothesized that circRTN4 stabilizes RAB11FIP1 in regulating EMT in PDAC. We demonstrated that circRTN4 knockdown inhibited the expression of N-cadherin in PDAC cells and mice tumors. Also, we found the differential expression of EMT-related transcription factors in circRTN4-depleted PDAC cells. CircRTN4 knockdown inhibited expression of transcription factors Slug, Snail Family Transcriptional Repressor 1 (Snai1), Twist Family BHLH Transcription Factor 1 (Twist) and Zinc Finger E-Box Binding Homeobox 1 (Zeb1). In addition, knockdown of RAB11FIP1 rescued the effects of circRTN4 on the expression of Slug, Snai1, Twist and Zeb1. Accordingly, we demonstrated that Slug, Snai1, Twist and Zeb1 were upregulated in PDAC primary tumors. A positive correlation was also found between Slug, Snai1, Twist, Zeb1 and circRTN4 expression. Taken together, our results suggested that circRTN4 stabilized RAB11FIP1 by blocking its ubiquitination to promote the expression of N-cadherin, Slug, Snai1, Twist and Zeb1 for EMT in PDAC.

14171217.label: Major findings and research outcome
14171217.value: Please refer to Part C for more details. 1. Identification of circRNAs in PDAC cells To identify the differentially expressed circRNAs in PDAC, we performed circRNA sequencing of nontumor HPDE and PDAC cells PANC1 and SW1990. In total, 17,158 circRNAs were identified in which 84% were exonic. To validate the results from circRNA sequencing and the clinical significances of the upregulated circRNAs, we measured the expressions of selected circRNAs in a panel of PDAC cells and primary tumors. circGANAB and circRTN4 were found with significant upregulation in PDAC cells, as well as PDAC primary tumors. 2. Characterization of circGANAB and circRTN4 Next, we examined the physical circular structures of circGANAB and circRTN4. Outward-facing divergent primer and inward-facing convergent primer were designed to validate the formation of circGANAB and circRTN4. Both primers amplified a product of expected size from cDNA, while only convergent primers resulted in an amplification from genomic DNA. The presence of back-splicing junction was confirmed by Sanger sequencing. 3. circGANAB and circRTN4 promotes cell growth and invasion in vitro To elucidate the functions of circGANAB and circRTN4 in PDAC, we employed siRNA, which specifically targeted the back-splicing junction of circFOXK2, without altering the expression of its parental gene. Knockdown of circGANAB and circRTN4 inhibited cell growth and clonogenic ability of PDAC cells. 4. circGANAB and circRTN4 promotes tumor growth and metastasis in vivo Knockdown of circGANAB and circRTN4 was also employed for in vivo study. Xenograft mice model was generated by subcutaneous injection of sh-circRNA CFPAC1 cells. Knockdown of circGANAB and circRTN4 by shRNA significantly inhibited tumor growth. Because results from in vitro experiments revealed that circGANAB and circRTN4 promoted PDAC cell migration and invasion, we constructed PDAC metastatic mice model through orthotopic injection of sh-circRNA CFPAC1 cells to the pancreas. Knockdown of circGANAB and circRTN4 inhibited the PDAC metastasis to liver. Our results found that that circGANAB and circRTN4 played critical roles in promoting PDAC growth and liver metastasis. Identification of circGANAB and circRTN4-interacting proteins Therefore, we next studied the importance of circRNA–protein interaction in PDAC. We in vitro transcribed circGANAB and circRTN4, which functioned as a probe to pull-down circGANAB and circRTN4-interacting proteins. CircRTN4 interacted with important epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT)- driver RAB11FIP1 to block its ubiquitination site. We found that circRTN4 knockdown promoted the degradation of RAB11FIP1 by increasing its ubiquitination. Also, circRTN4 knockdown inhibited the expression of RAB11FIP1-regulating EMT-markers Slug, Snai1, Twist, Zeb1 and N-cadherin in PDAC.

14171217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14171217.value: The effectiveness of current therapy for PDAC is extremely poor. The development of novel diagnosis and therapeutic targets is urgently needed. Being an important regulator of gene expression, circRNAs are believed to play vital roles in PDAC development. This study explored the oncogenic roles of circRNAs. Knowledge gained from this project revealed the roles of circRNAs in PDAC and will potentially lead to novel diagnostic markers and therapeutic targets.

14171217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14171217.value: The detailed biological functions of circular RNA (circRNA) are largely unexplored. Using circRNA sequencing, we identified 169 differentially expressed circRNAs in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) cells compared with nontumor human pancreatic ductal epithelial cells. Among them, circGANAB and circRTN4 were validated with significant upregulation in PDAC cells and primary tumors. circGANAB and circRTN4 promoted cell growth, migration, and invasion and was involved in cell-cycle progression and apoptosis.circGANAB and circRTN4 contained multiple miRNA binding sites, functioning miRNA sponge, which in turn promoted expression of ANK1, GDNF, and PAX6. A novel and highly specific circRNA-pulldown followed by mass spectrometry analysis identified circRNA-interacting proteins, which were involved in cell adhesion, mRNA splicing, and structural molecule activity. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that circGANAB and circRTN4 in complex with YBX1 and hnRNPK promotes expression of oncogenic proteins that contribute to PDAC progression. SIGNIFICANCE: This study reveals a prominent role for circRNAs in PDAC progression, suggesting that circRNAs might be novel diagnostic markers for PDAC.

To study the induction of surface CRT expression by tumor-reactive serum: Serum (antibodies) will be obtained from VPDT-cured mice. Its specificity in inducing CRT exposure will be tested with another mouse cell line 4T1. The tumor cell membrane protein recognized by the antibodies will be isolated by pull down assay and identified by mass spectrometry. To study the effect of BAM-SiPc on the surface CRT expression pathway: The effect of BAM-SiPc-PDT and tumor-reactive serum will be compared with that induced by the canonical CRT inducer Mitoxanthrone. The individual steps of the pathway, including oxidative stress, endoplasmic reticulum stress, caspase-8 activation, anterograde transport and exocytosis, will be evaluated one by one with specific pharmacological agents. To study the immunogenicity of surface CRT-expressing tumor cells: Bone marrow derived dendritic cells will be isolated and incubated with the BAM-SiPc-PDT- or serum (antibodies)-treated CT26 cells. The maturation of dendritic cells will be followed by measuring the levels of cytokines released with ELISA, and following the phenotypic/functional changes using flow cytometry.

14171717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14171717.value: In recent decades, accumulating evidence from both animal and clinical studies suggests that a sufficiently activated immune system could strongly augment various types of cancer treatment, including photodynamic therapy (PDT). Through the generation of reactive oxygen species, PDT eradicates tumors by triggering localized tumor cell damage, shutting down the tumor-innervating blood vessels and hence cutting off the oxygen and nutrient supplies to the tumor cells, and also inducing anti-tumor immunity. As most cancer patients die as a result of tumor metastasis and relapse rather than the localized tumor, the immunomodulatory aspect appears to be particularly important. Unfortunately, this is also the PDT area where we know least. In the last decade, we have been studying the anti-tumor properties of a number of novel photosensitizers that we have chemically synthesized, among them is BAM-SiPc, a silicon(IV) phthalocyanine derivative. Using the mouse CT26 tumor cells as the model system, in vitro photodynamic treatment with BAM-SiPc was shown to lead to the exposure of calreticulin, heat shock proteins 70 and 90, the damage associated molecular pattern in immunogenic cell death. Our preliminary data on the cell death mechanism suggested that it involved necroptosis, a regulated form of necrosis. Putting the observations together, it appears that necroptotic cell death could be immunogenic in nature, a topic that has not been hitherto examined in details. In in vivo BALB/c mouse study, with a vascular PDT (VPDT) regimen, BAM-SiPc could eradicate the tumor in about 70% of the tumor-bearing mice. More importantly, an anti-tumor immune response was triggered that could protect the mice against further re-challenge of the tumor cells. Serum obtained from the VPDT-cured mice could also effectively hinder tumor growth and protect the mice against further re-challenge in a T-cell dependent manner, suggesting the involvement of both humoral immunity and cell mediated immunity in the process. In the proposed study, the “immunogenic necroptosis” hypothesis will be examined in detail. The exact component of the serum from the VPDT-cured mice which possess immunomodulatory effect will be identified. Its action mechanism will also be investigated. The results obtained should provide insights on our basic understanding of the relationship between cell death and immune response as well as information on the therapeutic potential of BAM-SiPc in clinical application.

14171717.label: Realisation of objectives
14171717.value: Objective #1 To study immunogenic necroptosis in BAM-SiPc induced PDT: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) using the photosensitizer BAM-SiPc exerted a dose-dependent cytotoxic effect on the mouse colon CT26 tumor cells. To determine the type of cell death involved, different specific inhibitors were used. In the flow cytometric analysis with dual annexin V and PI stainings, the percentage of viable cells was significantly increased when the cells were incubated with the necroptosis inhibitor necrostatin-1 (RIPK1 inhibitor) but not zVAD-fmk (pan-caspase inhibitor) or deferoxamine (iron-chelator). The expression of various marker proteins involved in the necroptotic pathway was studied by Western blot analysis. It was found that the expressions of the cleaved form of caspase 8 and the cleaved form of RIPK3 were both reduced. The formation of the necroptotic complex RIPK1-RIPK3-MLKL was followed by a co-immunoprecipitation method. All the three proteins were present and could be detected by their respective antibodies only after PDT; RIPK1 and RIPK3 could be pulled down by using antibodies against MLKL. To study the “immunogenic” nature of the cell death, the expressions of damage associated molecular pattern (DAMP) and chemokines were followed. Both confocal microscopic and flow cytometric analyses showed an increased expression of calreticulin (CRT) on the cell surface. For the other DAMP, ERp57 and HSP90 were detected in the Western blot analysis of the cell membrane protein preparation whereas ATP and HMGB1 could be found in the culture medium after PDT. The activation of immune response was also demonstrated by the increase in the expression of different chemokines. Objective #2 To study the induction of surface CRT expression by tumor-reactive serum: The serum obtained from the PDT-cured mice could induce surface CRT expression in the CT26 cells, as demonstrated by both confocal microscopy and flow cytometry. The serum was also found to possess various immunomodulatory properties. In in vitro studies, it stimulated cytokine secretion of IL-6 and C-X-C motif chemokine ligands 1-3 in the CT26 cells through activation of the NF-κB and MAPK pathways. The complement protein C5a boosted in the serum was shown to be involved in the process by different assays, including the use of neutralizing anti-C5a antibody and recombinant C5a, the expression of its cell surface receptor CD88 as well as the effect of the CD88 antagonist W-54011. The serum could also induce CRT exposure on CT26 cells and activate dendritic cells, as shown by both phenotypic and functional markers. The serum contained CT26-targeting antibodies which, through the Fc region, induced macrophage engulfment of the tumor cells. In in vivo studies, inoculation of the serum-treated CT26 cells to mice showed a delayed tumor growth with leukocytes, particularly T cells, attracted into the tumor site. To examine the cell type specificity, 4T1 and EMT6 murine breast tumor cells were used. It was found that the induction effects of the serum obtained from the PDT-cured mice (originally inoculated with CT26 cells) was weaker on 4T1 cells, followed by EMT6 cells. Other biochemical characterization of the effects of the serum, for example, increase in chemokine level and resistance against re-challenge of tumor cells in the animal model, followed the same pattern. Based on these results, it appears that the tumor antigens on 4T1 cells, which might be more similar with those on CT26 cells, were being recognized to a larger extent than those of EMT6 cells. Attempts were made to identify the tumor cell surface antigens recognized by the tumor-reactive antibodies. Two approaches were used to obtain the protein sample. First, the membrane protein preparation was pre-immunoprecipitated using naïve mouse antibodies so that the non-specific proteins were trapped and removed through a Protein G column. The unbound protein was then re-immunoprecipitated with antibodies obtained from the PDT-cured mice. In the second approach, intact CT26 cells were first probed with the antibodies prior to cell lysis and immunoprecipitation. At the same time, the protein crosslinker [bis(sulfosuccinimidyl)suberate] was used to covalently link the bound antibodies with the antigens on intact cell. Tryptic digestion was then carried out in the presence of 5% octyl glucoside. Finally, the samples were ready for liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry analysis. Altogether, 14 proteins were identified from the various trials. Among them, 4 different known cancer antigens, viz. annexin A2, plexin-B2, cathepsin B and integrin alpha-V, and 3 different immune-related proteins, viz. H-2 class I histocompatibility antigen, serotransferrin and macrophage migration inhibitory factor, could be identified in the protein samples prepared by both approaches. Generation of antibodies recognizing these proteins after PDT may help in cancer eradication. For example, previous study has shown that using antibodies against the the tumor antigen annexin A2 could inhibit tumor cell proliferation in a mouse model. It is possible that the serum of PDT-cured mice also contained similar antibodies to inhibit CT26 tumor growth. Objective #3 To study the effect of BAM-SiPc on the surface CRT expression pathway: The surface CRT expression pathways were studied. In the chemotherapy-driven classical immunogenic cell death pathway, reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation is expected to induce endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress to cause PERK activation and eIF-2α phosphorylation. Caspase 8 will then be activated. As a result, CRT could be translocated from ER to Golgi and brought to the cell surface through phosphoinositide-3-kinase dependent exocytosis. In the present experiment, to study the translocation pathway of CRT, the expression level of different protein markers and also the effects of different inhibitors on surface CRT expression were examined. The pathways involved in CT26 cells after BAM-SiPc-PDT or incubation with the serum from PDT-cured mice were slightly different. For CT26 cells after BAM-SiPc-PDT, phosphorylation of PERK and eIF-2 occurred as shown by Western blot. However, with the addition of any one of the inhibitors of the pathway, including glutathione (oxidative stress), 16F16 (ERp57), GSK2606414 (PERK), salubrinal (eIF-2), Z-IETD-FMK (caspase 8), brefeldin A (ER to Golgi apparatus anterograde transport) and wortmannin and LY294002 (phosphoinositide-3-kinase dependent exocytosis), the surface expression of CRT was significantly reduced. Knockdown of PERK and caspase 8 alo showed a reduced expression of surface CRT. Such results confirmed that the translocation of CRT in the necroptotic cells initiated by BAM-SiPc-PDT follows the chemotherapy-driven classical immunogenic cell death pathway. However, for CT26 cells after incubation with the serum, CRT exposure required ERp57 and caspase 8 but was independent of ER to Golgi apparatus anterograde transport and phosphoinositide-3-kinase dependent exocytosis. Objective #4 To study the immunogenicity of surface CRT-expressing tumor cells: To study the immunogenic properties of BAM-SiPc-PDT- or serum-treated- CRT expressing CT26 cells, we examined their effects on bone marrow derived dendritic cells (BMDC). Bone marrow monocytes from BALB/c mice were isolated, cultured and differentiated into BMDC. After co-culture with BAM-SiPc-PDT- or serum- treated tumor cells, the relative expression of cell surface markers of BMDC, including CD80, CD86 and MHC II, was found to be significantly increased upon flow cytometry analysis, indicating the maturation of BMDC. In addition to phenotypic changes, functional stimulation of the BMDC can also be demonstrated by the increased production of cytokines, for example, IL-12 and interferon-gamma. The BMDC could also recognize and take up PDT-treated CT26 cells.

14171717.label: Major findings and research outcome
14171717.value: PDT is a clinically approved treatment for various types of cancer. Besides killing the tumor cells directly, PDT has also been reported to trigger anti-tumor immunity. In the present study, BAM-SiPc-based PDT was shown to induce immunogenic necroptotic cell death on CT26 murine colon tumor cells in vitro (Zhang et al., 2021). Upon treatment, different DAMP were exposed onto the cell surface or released from the cells. Among them, CRT was found to translocate to the cell membrane through a pathway similar to that in chemotherapy. The activation of immune response was demonstrated by an increase in the expression of different chemokines. The PDT-treated tumor cells could be recognized by dendritic cells which, as a result of the interaction, were activated both phenotypically (increase in matured dendritic cells surface marker) and functionally (release of cytokine) (Zhang et al., 2019). For in vivo studies, our previous results showed that BAM-SiPc-PDT could eradicate tumor in ~70% of tumor-bearing BALB/c mice and elicit an anti-tumor immune response. In the present study, the serum obtained from the PDT-cured mice was examined and found to possess various immunomodulatory properties (Zhang et al., in press). In in vitro studies, it stimulated cytokine secretions of IL-6 and CXCL 1-3 in CT26 cells through the NF-κB and MAPK pathways. The complement protein C5a boosted in the serum was shown to be involved in the process. The serum also induced CRT exposure on CT26 cells and activated dendritic cells. It contained CT26-targeting antibodies which, through the Fc region, induced macrophage engulfment of the tumor cells. In in vivo studies, inoculation of the serum-treated CT26 cells to mice demonstrated a retarded tumor growth with leukocytes, particularly T cells (both helper T cells and cytotoxic T cells), attracted to the tumor site. In addition, the PDT-cured mice also showed different degrees of resistance against challenge of other types of murine tumor cells, for example, the breast tumor 4T1 and EMT6 cells.

14171717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14171717.value: To strengthen the anti-tumor immunity induced by PDT, different approaches have been used. Knowing that immunogenic cell death is usually triggered by ER stress, we have synthesized an ER-localized photosensitizer by conjugating a BODIPY photosensitizer with the ER-targeting glibenclamide moiety (Zhou et al., 2018, J. Med. Chem. 61, 3952-3961) and are ready to examine its immunogenic effect. BAM-SiPc is a promising candidate for PDT. Unfortunately, one limitation is the lack of specificity. In this regard, we have synthesized an antibody-drug conjugate to target specifically the tumor cells. In that study, IR700, a hydrophilic photosensitizer, was conjugated to the humanized monoclonal antibody ARB102 which binds specifically cadherin-17, a cell surface marker highly expressed in gastrointestinal cancer. The results showed that photoimmunotherapy using the conjugate ARB102-IR700 could induce cell death in CDH17-positive tumor cells with high potency, while leaving the adjacent CDH17-negative cells unaffected in the co-cultured model. In vivo studies using the pancreatic adenocarcinoma AsPC-1 (CDH17-positive) xenograft tumor model in nude mice showed that ARB102-IR700 accumulated specifically in the tumor site and that PDT could inhibit tumor growth significantly (Lum et al., 2020, Mol. Pharm. 17, 3941-3951). Currently, we are studying the immune response generated from this tumor-targeting photosensitizer.

14171717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14171717.value: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) is a technique employing three non-toxic species, viz. photosensitizer, oxygen and light, to achieve cell death. Through the generation of ROS, PDT eradicates tumor by triggering localized tumor cell damage, shutting down the tumor-innervating blood vessels and also inducing anti-tumor immunity. As most cancer patients die as a result of tumor metastasis and relapse rather than the localized tumor, the immunomodulatory aspect of PDT appears to be particularly important. In the past fifteen years, we have synthesized a number of novel phthalocyanine-based photosensitizers with a long wavelength of activation and a high potency of generating ROS, among them is BAM-SiPc. In this study, we demonstrated that BAM-SiPc can not only kill the tumor cells with high potency, but the mode of cell death is also immunogenic in nature. Using the tumor-bearing mice as an animal model, BAM-SiPc-PDT could result in tumor regression. At the same time, it could stimulate anti-tumor immune responses and generate immunologic memory which helps to prevent cancer recurrence such that the PDT-cured mice could resist further rechallenge of the tumor cells. Moreover, the serum obtained from the cured mice also showed anti-tumor immunity and could help to act against the development of cancer.

14173017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14173017.value: AIM:The aim of the study is to determine whether the risk of metachronous advanced neoplasia increases if the surveillance interval is extended beyond the current recommendation of 3 years for high-risk subjects with advanced adenoma polyp at screening colonoscopy. BACKGROUND:With many countries initiating population colorectal cancer (CRC) screening, including Hong Kong, more robust guidance for surveillance interval is required to optimize the balance between clinical benefit and use of resources. The optimum surveillance interval after removal of advanced adenoma at screening colonoscopy remains unclear. The current recommendation of 3 years is based on data collected before widespread implementation of population screening programs and quality metrics in colonoscopy. These high-risk subjects are those most likely to benefit from surveillance and represent the majority of the demand in surveillance colonoscopies. We hypothesize that the risk of metachronous advanced neoplasia significantly increases if the surveillance interval is increased beyond 3 years for high-risk subjects. If this is true, our study’s findings will provide definitive evidence to support existing guidelines. Conversely, if our study shows that there is no significant increase in risk beyond the 3 years surveillance interval, then an extended surveillance interval such as 5 years is justified without exposing subjects to substantial risk STUDY DESIGN:Subjects stratified as high-risk after screening colonoscopy will be identified from the cohort of an existing territory wide CRC screening programme and open recruitment. High-risk subjects will be defined as those with adenomas 1 cm or greater, or with villous components (tubulovillous or villous), or with high-grade dysplasia, or ≥3 adenomas. Study design: A non-randomized prospective comparative study 3-year group: High-risk subjects with screening colonoscopy done in 2014-2016 will be eligible for 3-year surveillance colonoscopy in 2017-2019. Beyond 3 years group: High-risk subjects who have had a screening colonoscopy in the prior 3 years, but who have neither received nor are scheduled for a surveillance colonoscopy (either due to non-adherence or limited access to surveillance colonoscopy) will be eligible for surveillance colonoscopy in 2017-2019. Intervention: Conventional colonoscopy Analysis: Relative risk of metachronous advanced neoplasia detected at surveillance interval beyond 3 years as compared with surveillance interval of 3 years. POTENTIAL IMPACT OF STUDY: 1) This study’s results will either support or change international practice guidelines for surveillance interval in high-risk subjects. 2) This local data will be fundamental when population CRC screening starts in Hong Kong, 2016. 3) Early detection of metachronous advanced neoplasia will save lives and avert costs of treating colorectal cancer.

14173817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14173817.value: Many cellular phenotypes, such as various normal cell types in healthy individuals and many aberrant cell types in disease tissues, are shaped by DNA methylation. With the advent of high-throughput bisulfite sequencing and methylation array techniques, we can now produce methylation profiles of different cells and compare them to find differentially methylated regions (DMRs), which are genomic segments that show different methylation status across different cellular phenotypes. After DMRs associated with a disease or a developmental process are detected, they can later be combined with other genetic, epigenetic and environmental factors for causal modelling of disease or development. Since nearby CpG sites tend to share the same methylation status, differential methylation measured at region level should be more predictive and statistically powerful than at individual level. But because the CpG sites are unevenly distributed throughout the whole genome, so as the probes of methylation arrays, it is still challenging to account for such spatial correlation. Existing methods use either a window-based approach or a local smoothing approach, thus they not only need a lot of ad hoc tuning, but also are incapable of capturing the heterogeneous differential methylation pattern across the genome. We propose a probabilistic model for DMR identification based on either bisulfite sequencing data or array data from one or multiple paired samples, with or without extra unpaired samples. More specifically, we propose a non-homogeneous hidden Markov model to fit the observed methylation value sequences. This will allow us to model the differential methylation event, spatial correlation and the gene region effect jointly, thus we can achieve better performance. Both synthetic data and real data will be used to evaluate our method and compare with existing methods. A R/Bioconductor package will be produced for biomedical researchers to automatically detect DMRs of the whole genome without setting tuning parameters. As to our knowledge, this will be the first genome-wide probabilistic modelling of methylation data which adapts the spatial correlation to the spatial distance. 14173817.label: Realisation of objectives
14173817.value: All five objectives are fully achieved. For the first objective, we developed the non-homogeneous hidden Markov model with constrained multivariate Gaussian prior for the automatic detection of DMRs. For second objective, the Bayesian approach with an MCMC algorithm is used to infer the parameters and the hidden states, which correspond to the segmentation of the input sequence to DMR and non-DMR. The third objective is achieved by extensive simulation studies based on synthesized datasets, and comparison with existing approaches, including mehtylKit, DSS, HMMDM, etc. For the fourth objective, we extracted real methylation datasets from Gene Expression Omnibus for detail DMR analyses. The detected DMRs are largely supported by existing biomedical literature. For the fifth objective, we published our work and developed a R package called BSDMR and shared it freely online. We not only fulfilled all the above five objectives, but also extended the ideas from this project to other Bioinformatics problems and further investigated the statistical problems originated from this project, such as protein-DNA interaction and missing data imputation.

14173817.label: Major findings and research outcome
14173817.value: (Note: Journal papers listed in Part C/Section 8 are cited here according to their order in the table of Section 8) As planned by the project, we developed models and computing methods for detecting differentially methylated regions (DMRs) from paired methylation data. The main model is based on a non-homogeneous hidden Markov chain, and the main computing method is Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm [5]. We found that by incorporating the distances between neighboring CpG sites into the association modelling of neighboring hidden states, we can significantly increase the accuracy of DMR detection. This is also intuitive because of the molecular mechanism of methylation & de-methylation process. The methylation statuses of nearby sites tend to converted simultaneously. During the implementation of the project, related Bioinformatics and statistical problems and their applications are also explored. For example, at the very beginning, the difficulty of handling the missing data in this project led us to develop a more accurate data imputation method [1]. While checking the tumor sample, we realize that it might be polluted with neighboring healthy tumor, thus the purity is a concern for downstream analysis. Thus we investigated the problem of purity estimation for methylation data [2]. Note that the methylation data may be either real numbers from methylation array (although originally integers from imaging data) or counts of reads. The pre-processing and in-house analyses actually involve some general statistical or machine learning methods, but they often need to be tuned, thus producing some interesting side lines [3,4,6,7]. Also, the change of methylation status may be related to the binding and interaction between specific molecules and DNA, thus leading to some general binding and interaction analysis [8]. Finally, except for the most common methylation type that we mainly analyzed, we also studied some rare methylation type [9].

14173817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14173817.value: At the application side, the models and computing methods produced by this project can be applied to other paired sequence segmentation problems. In the new era of personalized medicine, more and more medical studies get both the disease sample and the control sample from same person. Such paired data provide cleaner signal for detecting the exact biomarker causing the specific disease of this person. Our new method can help on such cases. At the methodology side, more complex structures, such as family data, can be explored, e.g. using hierarchical hidden Markov models. We will continue developing HMM methods along this line.

14173817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14173817.value: With the need of targeting at the specific disease cause in the new era of personalized medicine, we may get both the disease sample and the control sample from same person for detail diagnosis. Such paired data provide cleaner signal for detecting the exact biomarker causing the specific disease of this person, but also cast a challenge for analysis. We develop a statistical inference method for such paired methylation data, which tells us one important level of information from DNA molecules. We outperformed existing methods in terms of the accuracy of detecting true differential methylation sites.

14173917.label: Realisation of objectives
14173917.value: Objectives 1 1. Long-term BPs treatment impaired fracture callus bridging, with paradoxically increased osteogenic potential of BMSC in a rat model of AFF. Zoledronate (ZOL), one of the most potent bisphosphonates, was injected to OVX rats. As a result, both high and low dose of ZOL were able to induce delayed fracture healing in OVX rats. We next injected ZOL at an even higher dose to non-OVX rats to recapitulate the potential side effect of BPs on fracture healing in a relatively short period. As a result, 3 months ZOL injection at such a high dose was able to induce a callus non-bridging rate as high as 94% at week 12 post-fracture, producing a more consistent phenotype of delayed union. To investigate potential alternations in the properties of osteoprogenitor cells in response to long-term BPs treatment, we isolated bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) from rats treated by 3 months of ZOL. BMSCs from AFF rats displayed with a significantly increased osteogenic potential as compared to control, consistent with clinical findings. 2. Non-united AFF animal fracture gap was aberrantly distributed with fibrosis tissue and persistent cartilage-like tissue Histologically, we observed two healing patterns of non-bridged callus in AFF rats. Twenty percentage of rats in AFF group displayed with complete fibrosis (without cartilage-like structure) in the fracture gap. Higher magnified images show that the gap was filled with fibrous tissue, enlarged vessels, and lymphocytes, indicating a feature similar with granulation tissue. These results indicate that BPs may lead to excessive fibrosis. The remaining 80% AFF rats present with persistent cartilage-like tissues at late stage of fracture healing, whereas the control group presented with successful endochondral ossification that resulted in bony union of the fracture gap. 3. ZOL prevented the clearance of collagen-secreting fibroblasts We first measured the fraction of fibroblasts in the soft callus. Flow cytometry showed a higher proportion of S100a4/Cd26 double-positive fibroblasts among all FCCs was found in ZOL group at 4 wpf as compared to the control group. At 12 wpf, these pathological fibroblasts were mostly cleared with concurrent bony union of the fracture callus in the control group, whereas ZOL-treated rats showed retention of these cells, consistent with histological findings. To resolve the genetic heterogeneity of the fibroblasts, we next performed single-cell mRNA sequence (scRNA-seq) of the unfractionated adherent FCCs. The results suggest that ZOL treatment may hamper the clearance of a distinct fibroblast cluster that is actively secreting collagen to prevent callus bridging. 4. ZOL promoted differentiation of myeloid progenitor cells into fibroblasts We postulated that ZOL might facilitate the transition of myeloid progenitor cells into fibroblasts. In support of this, the fraction of myeloid-derived fibroblasts in the control group decreased from 4 wpf to 12 wpf as indicated by scRNA-seq, and a similar trend was observed specifically for the collagen-secreting clusters. In ZOL group, however, the proportion of these Cd14-positive fibroblasts remained unchanged over time. Immunohistochemistry staining validated a continuous contribution of myeloid cells to the development of fibrosis. Of note, ZOL group contained a unique cluster of fibroblasts which was over-represented in categories associated with myeloid leukocytes migration/regulation on GO analysis, echoing the histological features of chronic inflammation. These inflammation-related fibroblasts were particularly enriched for myeloid marker Cd14 as well, suggesting a pathogenic role of bone marrow in the fracture non-union. Further, in vitro treatment of BMSCs from the control rats with ZOL also increased fibrogenic potential of the progenitor cells, supporting a direct effect of BPs on fibrotic changes. 5. Aberrant vessel formation and decreased CGRP expression were found in the fracture callus Computational tomography-based angiography and immunohistochemistry showed the vessel formation is dysregulated by ZOL treatment. At the same time, we found a significant reduction of CGRP expression in the callus of both human AFF specimens and our AFF animal model at early stage of fracture healing as compared to BPs naïve subjects. Objectives 2 1. Restoration of CGRP optimized ZOL-induced delayed fracture healing via preventing myeloid transformation of bone marrow stem cells. We daily percutaneously injected CGRP into the fracture gap of out AFF models. Both X-ray and CT result showed that local CGRP injection could enhance AFF healing by reducing the non-bridging rate, indicating that replenishing CGRP might be a promising strategy to treat AFF. Concurrently, fibrosis was decreased, suggesting CGRP effectively attenuated the formation of fibrous tissues potentially by acting on progenitor cells. scRNA-seq showed collagen-secreting fibroblasts in CGRP group were cleared, indicating that CGRP may decrease the production of the committed ECM-secreting fibroblasts or enhance their clearance. In addition, the reduction in fibroblasts number was due to inhibited transformation of myeloid-derived progenitor cells into the fibroblasts as indicated by scRNA-seq data and in vitro culture of BMSCs isolated from CGRP group rats. Collectively, CGRP may play an important role in preventing pathological differentiation and maintain stemness of progenitor cells. 2. Optimized fracture healing by magnesium-containing intramedullary nail (Mg-IMN) We applied Mg-IMN instead of stainless steel IMN (SS-IMN) to fix unilateral closed femoral fractures in rats with ZOL pre-treatment. As a result, Mg-IMN fixation effectively reduced fracture non-bridging rate compared to conventional SS-IMN to the same extent as CGRP injection did. These data support a beneficial role of Mg-IMN in facilitating fracture callus bridging of AFF animal model. Mg-IMN-treated rats displayed fewer fibrous tissues as well as optimized vessel structures in the fracture gap compared to ZOL group as shown by histology and flow cytometry, suggesting that degradation of Mg effectively mitigates ZOL-induced fibrosis and, as a consequent, possibly attenuates retention of abnormal fibrocartilages. An accelerated clearance of myeloid derived fibroblasts that might be responsible for aberrant fibrosis was also observed in Mg treated rats as suggested by scRNA-seq, validation on histology samples, and in vitro culture of BMSCs isolated from Mg-IMN treated rats. These data together denote that Mg-IMN prevents fibrogenic differentiation of myeloid cells via upregulating CGRP, resulting in optimized vessel formation and callus bridging. Objective 3 The major mechanism of Mg/CGRP-induced better healing outcome of AFFs was found to be the reduced myeloid transformation of bone marrow stem cells (results of Objective 2). The research questions of how BPs impact osteogenesis, angiogenesis, and CGRP has been studied in results of Objective 1, showing that BPs “paradoxically” increased osteogenesis of BMSCs and led to aberrant angiogenesis. The inhibitory effect of BPs on CGRP expression in the fracture callus, as shown in both human and animal AFF specimens, was found to be related to a direct inhibitory effect of BPs on CGRP gene expression in DRGs (our experimental data), and the reduced osteoclast activities, which is essential to innervation of CGRP-expressing periphery nerve fibers in fracture callus (J Clin Invest, 129 (2019) 1076–1093.). As for how CGRP enhanced angiogenesis, it was mainly mediated by the CGRP-induced reduction in collagen deposition because of reduced fibrotic transformation of myeloid cells. Notably, researchers from other groups also found that CGRP directly stimulated angiogenesis, the underlying mechanism of which is worth future further investigation.
