14176317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14176317.value: Crabs (infraorder Brachyura) constitute the largest group of decapod crustaceans, with over 7200 species known to-date. They are extremely diverse in morphology and ecology, with members inhabiting an extensive spectrum of environments including hydrothermal vents, the abyss, coral reefs, intertidal, freshwater, on land, in pitcher pants and bromeliads, as well as forming symbiotic association with many marine taxa. With their extremely diverse morphology and ecology, it is not surprising that many major questions pertaining to the evolutionary origin and relationships of crabs have yet to be resolved despite intensive research. In the past few decades, considerable effort has been devoted to resolve the brachyuran phylogeny at various taxonomic levels using morphological and molecular data. The studies suggest that the Brachyura represents an ancient rapid radiation, whereas most of the extant superfamilies and families radiated during the Cretaceous and Early Tertiary period. Unfortunately, phylogenetic signals for such ancient radiation in the current molecular datasets are easily muddled, causing many of the most important internal nodes regarding the interfamilial relationships to be poorly or even unresolved. Therefore, more new molecular data and methods are necessary to resolve these ambiguous relationships. Furthermore, the genetic mechanisms underlying the physiological innovations that allow crabs to reign in diverse habitats is poorly understood. However, the myriad of genomic data that would be required for such investigation has yet to be available. Recent advances in genome sequencing technology enable rapid acquisition of profuse sequence data of non-model organisms without prior knowledge of their genomes, hence allowing us to quickly identify hundreds or even thousands of informative markers for evolutionary studies. This study proposes to employ a transcriptomic approach to reconstruct the phylogeny of crabs with a major focus on interfamilial relationships. With strategic selection of about 80 species covering all brachyuran habitats, the study will shed light on the origin and transition of various ecological traits. The copious genomic information generated from this study will allow us, for the first time, to explore gene evolution in relation to novel habitats adaptations throughout the evolutionary history of crabs. 螃蟹（短尾下目）是十足甲殼類動物中最大的類群。目前已知的螃蟹物種已超過了7200個。他們在形態和生態學上是非常多樣化的，可居住於廣闊多變的環境中，包括深海，海底熱泉，珊瑚礁，潮間帶，淡水，陸地上，豬籠草裡和鳳梨叢中，並可與許多海洋類群形成共生關系。由於形態和生態上的高度多樣化，盡管研究者們多年來進行了深入的研究，然而螃蟹的起源和進化關系仍舊有許多重要的問題尚未得到解決。在過去幾十年中，研究者們致力於運用形態學和分子數據來揭示短尾下目中各個分類水平的系統發育史。這些研究表明，短尾下目代表了一種古老的快速輻射進化，其中大多數現存的超科和科都是在白堊紀和早第三紀期間輻射進化而來的。不幸的是，目前分子數據中這種古老輻射的系統發育信號極為混亂，導致許多連接不同科之間關系的重要內部節點很難或甚至完全未解決。因此，需要更多新的分子數據和方法來解決這些模糊的關系。此外，我們對於能令螃蟹廣泛適應不同棲息環境的生理創新及其遺傳進化機制也知之甚少。但這些研究所需的大量螃蟹基因組數據目前仍極為匱乏。幸而，基因組測序技術的最新進展使得在基因組先驗知識缺乏的情況下快速獲取非模式生物的大量測序數據成為可能，從而使我們能快速識別數百甚至數千個可用於進化研究的序列信息標記。 本研究提出採用轉錄組學方法來重構螃蟹的系統發育樹，主要側重於解決科間關系。通過策略性地選擇約80種覆蓋所有螃蟹棲息地的物種，本研究將揭示各種生態特徵的起源和轉變。這項研究所產生的豐富的基因組信息將使我們能首次於螃蟹進化史上探索與新生棲息地適應相關的基因進化。

14176317.label: Realisation of objectives
14176317.value: We have successfully reconstructed a robust family-level phylogeny of Brachyura using phylotranscriptomic approach (Objective 1). This is achieved by de novo transcriptome sequencing of 57 brachyuran species from 41 families of Brachyura. We analyzed these data together with the available data of Brachyura from NCBI SRA and altogether 68 species from 46 out of the total of 104 families (44%) were analyzed. Furthermore, we have also sequenced 10 selected markers from 93 out of the 104 brachyuran families to achieve the most comprehensive phylogeny to date. Given that interfamilial relationships among heterotremes are well resolved in our analyses but those within Thoracotremata remain obscure, our effort in the latter part of this project has been focused on Thoracotremata. In this analysis we included all thoracotreme families including the newly established family Leptograpsodidae. The results confirm the polyphyly of all three superfamilies with more than one family. And Camptandriidae, Dotillidae, and Xenophthalmidae are early diverged lineages in Thoracotremata. At family level, Macrophthalmidae and Varunidae are both non-monophyletic. Symbiosis between crabs and other marine macro-invertebrates evolved at least twice in Thoracotremata: one in Aphanodactylidae which is sister to Macrophthalidae and the other two symbiotic crab families Cryptochiridae and Pinnotheridae might share a common ancestor. Diversification rate analysis based on a time calibrated phylogenetic tree suggests an increased diversification rate in Sesarmidae compared to closely related families. Such shift in diversification rate suggests possible adaptive radiation upon mangal invasion and dietary shift to herbivory, allowing sesarmids to exploit new niche that other thoracotreme species can rarely utilize. For objective 2 on the evolution of genes and gene families underlying the physiological innovations associated with habitat types and lifestyles of brachyurans, we have curated and analyzed genes or gene families that are potentially involved in their adaptability to diverse habitats and lifestyles, such as osmoregulatory genes, chemosensory genes, genes encoding digestive enzymes, and crustacean hypoglycemic hormones responsible for molting regulation. For instance, we identified that endogenous glycoside hydrolases are associated with herbivory, and opsin gene number is related to the light environment which the animals inhabit. Positive selection analyses of osmoregulatory genes reveal that genes responsible for low-salinity adaptation are different between primary freshwater crabs and euryhaline crabs, with the former relying on upstream signaling transduction genes and the latter depending on downstream ion transport genes. Based on the above findings, functional genomics and physiological studies on some of these genes/families (which are beyond the scope of the present project) are in progress in our labs. We have completed transcriptome and proteomic analyses on the mud crab Scylla paramamosain acclimated to different salinities. Data from both approaches reveal that exposure to low salinity (5 ppt) resulted in upregulation of ion transport and energy metabolism associated genes, as well as early changes in gene expression for signal transduction and stress response. In contrast, exposure to high salinity (33 ppt) resulted in upregulation of genes related to amino acid metabolism, and amino acid transport genes were upregulated only at the early stage of acclimation to this salinity. Our study reveals contrasting mechanisms underlying osmoregulation and osmoconformation in the mud crab, and provides novel candidate genes for osmotic signal transduction, thereby providing insights on understanding the salinity adaptation mechanisms of brachyuran crabs. To conclude, a robust family-level phylogenetic tree of the brachyuran crabs has been constructed using phylotranscriptomic approach. The tree forms the basis for exploring the genetic basis of the adaptation of the crabs to different habitats and lifestyles. We have identified a number of genes/gene families that are potentially of importance in speciation and adaptive evolution of crabs. We also conducted salinity acclimation experiments on the mud crabs to identify genes underlying osmoregulation and osmoconformation.

14176317.label: Major findings and research outcome
14176317.value: As discussed in the Progress Report, we conducted phylotranscriptomic analysis on 30 brachyuran species from 22 families using 372 orthologs with the results published in Molecular Phylogenetics and Evolution. The phylogenetic analyses confirm the early divergence of primary freshwater crabs; yet in contrast to a previous hypothesis on their close relationship to Heterotremata, the freshwater crabs are sister to Thoracotremata and therefore the monophyly of Heterotremata was rejected. Further analyses including the almost half of the described families reveal recent origins for hydrothermal vent associated crab families Bythograeidae and Xenograpsidae and independent colonization to the vent habitat at least three times in the brachyuran crabs. These results have been presented in international and regional conferences (see section 9) and a manuscript is under preparation will be submitted soon. We have successfully resolved the phylogeny among all families of the thoracotreme crabs as discussed under section 5.3. These findings have been presented in the Mid-Year Meeting of the Crustacean Society 2019 (see section 9) and we are in the progress of preparing a manuscript on Thoracotremata phylogeny to be submitted later this year. The 372 carefully selected orthologs will serve as informative markers for future phylogenetic analyses of Brachyura. A number of genes and gene families were identified to be associated with herbivory, water depth, and salinity adaptation. Part of the above findings have been presented in the Evolution 2019 meeting (see section 9). In particular, we focused on salinity adaptation by conducting salinity acclimation experiments on the euryhaline crab Scylla paramamosain. The genes underlying osmoregulation were identified through the differential gene expression under different salinities. These results were presented in a regional conference and published in Scientific Reports (see section 8).

14176317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14176317.value: Dr. Tang Yuanyuan, one of the PhD graduates supported by the grant, worked on the composition of gut microbial communities in brachyuran crabs and other decapod crustaceans. Her results on the distinct communities in species from different habitats suggest that gut microbes may play a role in adaptation to these habitats. This line of research on the relationships between gut microbiota and habitat in decapod crustaceans has recently been funded by the Hong Kong Branch of the Southern Marine Science and Engineering Guangdong Laboratory (Guangzhou).

14176317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14176317.value: Crabs (infraorder Brachyura) constitute the largest group of decapod crustaceans, with over 7200 species known to-date. With their extremely diverse morphology and ecology, it is not surprising that many major questions pertaining to the evolutionary origin and relationships of crabs have yet to be resolved. The present study employs a transcriptomic approach to reconstruct the phylogeny of crabs with a major focus on interfamilial relationships. With new data from 57 species covering 44% of the families, the study sheds light on the origin and evolutionary history of this ecological important group of organisms that lays the foundation for the establishment of a reliable classification system of crabs. The copious genomic information generated from this study also allows us to identify several genes and gene families underlying adaptations of crabs to diverse habitats and lifestyles. Subsequent studies on these genetic mechanisms would enhance our understanding on speciation of crabs, and animals in general.

14176617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14176617.value: Ribosome inactivating proteins (RIPs) are RNA N-glycosidases that depurinate a specific adenine at the sarcin-ricin loop (SRL) of the large ribosomal RNA (23S rRNA/28S rRNA) in prokaryotic and eukaryotic ribosomes. They inhibit protein synthesis in cells and are promising anticancer, anti-HIV and anti-plant virus agents. In this study, we propose to isolate and characterize the corresponding protein and DNA sequences of nine unique RIPs from mushrooms, express and purify the proteins for functional studies. So far, two RIP candidates from Lyophyllum shimeji and Volvariella volvacea were preliminarily identified, respectively. After obtaining their protein and DNA sequence information, we have heterogeneously expressed and purified the recombinant mushroom RIPs and confirmed their N-glycosidase and RIP activities. Sequence comparison of these RIPs has shown that they are very different from the classical RIPs, suggesting that they exert a distinctive RNA N-glycosidase mechanism. Our further studies will focus on mapping the active sites or key catalytic residues responsible for N-glycosidase activities, testing their anti-tumor and anti-HIV activities in vivo or in vitro. Three mushroom RIPs with the most potent activities will be subject to in-depth characterization, including: (1) to elucidate the mechanism for N-glycosidase activity, (2) to characterize their efficacy on tumor and HIV-infected cells, (3) to carry out structural study. Our work will provide insights into new RNA N-glycosidase mechanism and the structure and function of this enzyme. Obtaining new RIPs will expand the portfolio of this family of proteins for different pharmacological and biotechnological applications. and assist in the future rational design of useful agents for these applications. 核糖體失活蛋白（RIP）是一類具有rRNA N-糖苷酶活性的毒性蛋白家族。這類蛋白能實現特異性地將位於原核或者真核生物的核糖體大亞基RNA（包括23S rRNA/28S rRNA）的高度保守的莖環結構（sarcin-ricin loop）上的特定腺嘌呤進行水解去除這個腺嘌呤。由於這類蛋白能抑制細胞中核糖體的蛋白質生物合成功能，越來越多的研究表明它是非常具有應用前景的抗腫瘤，抗HIV病毒，乃至抵禦植物病毒感染的藥物。本研究中，我們首先將從蘑菇中分離提取以鑒定得到天然核糖體失活蛋白的編碼基因和對應的蛋白質序列，通過重組表達的方法獲得重組的核糖體失活蛋白，並進行深入的結構和功能方面的研究。截止到目前為止，我們已經分離鑒定了兩個分別在本菇和草菇中的RIP蛋白。在獲得這兩個RIP蛋白的序列資訊之後，我們將這兩個蛋白進行了異源重組表達，並通過活性實驗確證了這兩個重組蛋白的rRNA N-糖苷酶反應活性。基於序列比對，我們發現這兩個核糖體失活蛋白與經典的核糖體失活蛋白確實存在者很大差異，這也暗示著其在反應機制上或許與經典的核糖體失活蛋白會存在者區別。我們接下來的研究，將會集中在定位其催化活性中心，找到參與催化反應的關鍵殘基；在體外細胞水平上，驗證這些蘑菇中的新型核糖體失活蛋白對腫瘤增生和病毒感染的抑制作用。對於更具有研究價值的RIP蛋白，我們會在多個層面進行深入研究鑒定，其中包括： (1)闡釋RNA N-糖苷酶活性的反應機理；(2) 這些蛋白的抗腫瘤和抗HIV病毒活性； (3)結構生物學研究。我們的研究，將為闡釋核糖體失活蛋白的RNA N-糖苷酶的反應機制提供新理論基礎，並將有助於未來對新型藥物設計，研發以及應用。

14176617.label: Realisation of objectives
14176617.value: 1) Purification and sequences determination of mushroom RIPs As stated in the research proposal, we set forth to study nine selected mushroom RIPs, which reported with potent N-glycosidase activity and protein synthesis inhibitory activity, or show unique characteristics compared with classical RIPs. Above all nine mushroom RIPs, Lyophyllin from L. shimeji, HmRIP from H. marmoreus, Volvarin from V. volvacea were successfully isolated from fresh mushroom samples. Its depurination activity and protein synthesis inhibitory activity were also confirmed. The isolation of Calcaelin from Calvatia caelata and Flammin, flammulin, velin and velutin from Flammulina velutipes were also taken. However, no depurination activity and protein synthesis inhibitory activity were found in the crude extracts. It might be due to the errors in the publications or the change of strains obtained from the market. For mushroom containing Lyophyllin, HmRIP and Volvatoxin A2, the fractions containing N-glycosidase activity were collected and checked for their purity by SDS-PAGE. MALDI-TOF-MS mass spectrometry analysis and N-terminal sequence determination were carried out to identify the protein. The determinations were also combined with NCBI blast, transcriptome and genome searching. 2) Purification of recombinant mushroom RIPs and their N-glycosidase and protein synthesis inhibitory activities As stated in mid-term report, the corresponding sequences were synthesized, and then were cloned into common vectors (pET28a His-Tag, 2BT His-Tag, 2GT GST-Tag, PMCSG19 MBP-Tag), then attempts were made to express the recombinant plasmids in BL21(DE3), BL21(DE3) PlysS, C43, and optimized the expression condition (temperature, IPTG concentration and additives). Unfortunately, most clones were expressed in inclusion bodies. Only a tiny amount of MBP-fused Lyophyllin can be purified, and the protein was easily degraded. Then an edited pRSETb (His5HKGn-tev-ABeta1-42 in pRSETb) with a fluorescent protein sequence was used as the vector, which apparently increased the yield and stability of the mushroom RIPs. The vector backbone is pRSETb from Invitrogen. The fluorescent protein was a monomeric green mutant of Orange Fluorescent Protein. 5* His tag was inserted into the plasmid for further purification. An optimal site for TEV protease was designed to remove the fused OFP-mutant tag. With the edited vector, Lyophyllin and Volvatoxin A2 were successfully expressed. The expression of HmRIP was still poor. According to the reported potencies of these three mushroom RIPs and in consideration of the expression difficulties, lyophyllin and VVA2 were selected to further study. To minimize the possible influences of protein tags and further improve the yield, Lyophyllin and VVA2 were cloned to pet28a vector with revised sequence and only 6*His tag. The final yields were improved. The depurination and RIP activity of recombinant lyophyllin were then confirmed by yeast ribosome based N-glycosidase assay and luciferase based cell-free translation inhibitory activity assay. However, recombinant VVA2 did not show the supposed RIP activity, which indicates the previous positive activity in crude extract might come from protein contamination. On the other hand, we found another enzymatic activity of VVA2, which is the nicking endonuclease activity. Both wild-type VVA2 from mushroom and recombinant VVA2 I82E/L86K showed nicking activity in need of Mg2+ and Mn2+ environment with ligatable end. A manuscript is being drafted. 3) Anti-cancer and anti-HIV properties of lyophyllin Recombinant lyophyllin shows anti-cancer potential in Hela, HapG2 and JAR cancer cell line (see listed paper in Part C). Lyophyllin also shows anti-HIV activity in HIV-1 infected C8166 cells tested by cytopathic effect (CPE) and Elisa (HIV-1 p24), with IC50 as 7.065±1.874μM and 8.250±2.531μM respectively. 4) Mapping catalytic sites and mechanism study on the structural basis of lyophyllin. Lyophyllin was found to resemble the peptidase M35 domain of peptidyl-Lys metalloendopeptidases. It was found that several amino acids in the zinc-binding motif of lyophyllin have orientation similar to the conserved amino acids in TCS active site cleft. According to the superposition of the hypothetic active site of lyophyllin and that of ribosome-inactivating protein trichosanthin (TCS), the E122, H121, Y137, and Y104 may be equivalent to E160, R163, Y70, and Y111 of TCS. To find the importance of these residues, several variants of lyophyllin were generated by site-direct mutagenesis. According to the activity changes of the variants, we propose a mechanism for the N-glycosidase activity of lyophyllin. The crystallization and structural studies of lyophyllin are in progress. The protein crystal we got shows about 4.6-angstrom resolution. Further revision of the protein construct and modification of crystallization conditions are under processing. 5) Objectives addressed We regard we have addressed 80% of the objective 3. We are still working on the cyrstal structure of lyophyllin. We have characterized the nuclease activity of VVA2 and a manuscript is being drafted. Owing to limitation of time, how VVA2 elucidates the nuclease activity has not yet been addressed.

14176617.label: Major findings and research outcome
14176617.value: 1) Study on lyophyllin (Article 1 in Part C) In this study, we set forth to reveal the identity of lyophyllin and characterize its ribosome-inactivating mechanism. We first elucidated the DNA and protein sequences of lyophyllin and found that it belongs to the peptidase M35 like superfamily. Recombinant lyophyllin shows a dose-dependent protein synthesis inhibitory activity. Zinc ion is not required for lyophyllin to elicit the N-glycosidase activity. We have generated a structural model of lyophyllin and it is not possible to align this model to the classical RIPs. However, the region on lyophyllin for zinc-binding can form a pocket for binding adenine. The orientation of amino acid Y104 and the zinc-binding residues E122, H121, and Y137 of lyophyllin in three dimensions highly resemble E160, R163, Y70, and Y111 of TCS. To find the importance of these residues, several variants of lyophyllin were generated. The depurination activity of E122A was drastically disrupted, and its RIP activity decreased by 836-fold. The RIP activities of Y137A and Y104A decreased about 245- and 9-fold respectively, showing the greater importance of the Y137. With the above observation, we propose a mechanism for the N-glycosidase activity of lyophyllin. H121 takes the role of R163 in TCS for protonating and breaking the N-glycosidase bond, and E122 takes the role of E160 for stabilizing the positively charged oxocarbenium ion and polarizing the attacking water molecule. Y137 and Y104 take the role of Y70 and Y111 in TCS for stacking the target adenine ring. 2) Study on VVA2 VVA2 (Volvatoxin A chain 2) is a cardiotoxic protein from Volvariella volvacea. The cytotoxicity of VVA2 is from its pore-forming activity. In this project, new activity of VVA2 as a nicking endonuclease was established. Wild-type VVA2 from mushroom Volvariella volvacea with high purity was found possessing nicking endonuclease activity in need of Mg2+ or Mn2+. Recombinant VVA2 variant I82E/L86K which lost its oligomerization activity shows stronger activity. The nicked pUC19 by re-VVA2 I82E/L86K left a ligatable end. Its performance at different time/pH/temperatures was studied. The catalytic sites of VVA2 and its nicking sites on the DNA vector are still being investigated. 3) Review articles on RIPs Two comprehensive reviews, one on the engineering of RIPs for improving the pharmacological properties (Article 2 in Part C) and another on trichosanthin (TCS), a classical RIP (Article 3 in Part C), have been published.

14176617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14176617.value: Further studies related to this topic include: 1) Crystal structure of lyophyllin will confirm its N-glycosidase mechanism on the structural basis. Structure of lyophyllin and together with analogues of its subtract such as adenine, adenosine, AMP, ATP can be made to reveal the interaction and reacting mode of lyophyllin as an N-glycosidase. 2) Lyophyllin is a protein of the M35 endopeptidase superfamily. It will be of interest to find if other proteins in this family also possess N-glycosidase activity, so as to increase the portfolio of N-glycosidases for pharmacological applications. 3) Nicking endonuclease activity of VVA2 needs further study. This includes the substrate specificity, reaction requirements and catalytic site of VVA2. We expect to publish an article on the findings later this year.

14176617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14176617.value: Most RIPs have been found in plants. In recent years, several RIPs have been found from mushrooms. Compared to classical RIPs, many of these RIPs have different N-terminal sequences and molecular weights. In this study, the encoding genes of two mushroom RIPs lyophyllin and Volvatoxin A chain 2 (VVA2) were identified and heterologous expressed in Escherichia coli. Lyophyllin is shown to be in the M35 endopeptidase superfamily. It has potent RIP and anti-tumor activities and there is a site in the protein with amino acids orienting in space like the catalytic site of classical RIPs. We have proposed the mechanism of action. Our work has first shown a protein in this distinct family having potent N-glycosidic activity. Heterologous expression of VVA2 did not show N-glycosidase activity. However, it is found to have nicking endonuclease activity. VVA2 is shown to better perform at 55℃ with Mg2+ or Mn2+ in the medium. The catalytic site of VVA2 and its nicking sites on DNA are being studied.

14176817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14176817.value: 這個研究計劃的目的是認識胚胎幹細胞分化出的心肌細胞（ESC-CMs）的功能特性和成熟過程。 胚胎幹細胞來自囊胚的內細胞團，能夠自我更新和擁有萬能的特性，這意味著它們可以無限地被培養，並有能力分化為體內所有的細胞類型，包括心肌。因此胚胎幹細胞是科學研究和未來治療應用極好的心肌細胞來源。能夠達致成功移植，移植的細胞必須生存，並與心臟的天然心肌在結構上和功能上整合。應用ESC-CMs於細胞治療法之前，我們必須更好地理解這些細胞的功能特性。 ESC-CMs是電活性的，它會產生出自發性的鈣瞬變和動作電位。這些是決定心肌細胞激發與收縮的聯結的重要因素。然而，我們尚未完全理解早期分化的心肌細胞是如何調控這些信號。我們最近的數據顯示，經典型瞬時受體電位通道7（TRPC7）表達於ESC-CMs。在分化初期，TRPC7位於M線附近。隨著ESC-CM進一步成熟，TRPC7位於M線和Z線附近（橫小管所在的地方）。TRPC7在心肌細胞中的功能作用從未被探索過。我們假設TRPC7調節ESC-CMs的鈣瞬變和動作電位。此外，TRPC7如何在ESC-CM中被調節也是未知的。已知的是，TRPC7在超表達系統中被環磷酸鳥苷依賴性蛋白激酶I（cGKI）磷酸化。另一方面，以前的研究表明，錨定蛋白B（ankryin B）將蛋白磷酸酶2A（PP2A）的B56α亞基導向心肌細胞的M線，而ankryin B也是自發性活性有關的離子通道和轉運蛋白的協調中心。因此，我們假設內源TRPC7在ESC-CMs被cGKI和PP2A-B56α的磷酸化和去磷酸化調節。此外，雖然α1-腎上腺素能導致ESC-CM的生理肥大或成熟，但TRPC7在該過程中是否具有任何作用是未知的。我們假設α1-腎上腺素能通過激活TRPC7來調節心肌肥大或成熟。這個研究計劃的總體目標是研究TRPC7是如何調控ESC-CMs的功能和成熟。我們會使用細胞生物學、分子生物學、電生理和遺傳操作技術以達致研究目標。 這研究將對TRPC7如何調控ESC-CMs的功能和成熟過程提供重要的信息。總括來說，本研究將對理解複雜的ESC-CMs的生物學和揭示ESC-CMs的治療潛力至關重要。

14176817.label: Realisation of objectives
14176817.value: Aim 1. To investigate if the canonical transient receptor potential isoform 7 (TRPC7) channels regulate the calcium transients and the action potentials of embryonic stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (ESC-CMs). By immunostaining and by western blot analysis, TRPC7 proteins were found to be expressed in ESC-CMs. To investigate the function of TRPC7 in ESC-CMs, TPRC7 was knocked down and overexpressed using adenoviral vectors (AdVs). AdV-CMV-BFP-U6-shTRPC7, and its respective control AdV-CMV-BFP-U6-shLuc were made for knockdown experiments, while AdV-CMV-TRPC7-CMV-BFP and its respective control AdV-CMV-MCS-CMV-BFP (‘MCS’ stands for ‘multiple cloning sites’) were made for overexpression experiments. These cells were then subjected to calcium transient (CaT) measurement using confocal microscopy. Knockdown of TRPC7 was found to decrease the frequency and increase the time-to-peak and decay constant of CaTs, while overexpression of TRPC7 exerted the opposite effects. These cells were also subjected to calcium spark measurement. Interestingly, knockdown of TRPC7 was found to decrease while overexpression of TRPC7 was found to increase the frequency of calcium sparks. In addition, these cells were also subjected to patch clamping under current clamp mode. Knockdown of TRPC7 was found to decrease the frequency and diastolic depolarization rate (DDR) of action potentials (APs), while overexpression of TRPC7 exerted the opposite effects. Indeed, our further investigation revealed the mechanisms through which TRPC7 regulates the automaticity of ESC-CMs. By confocal microscopy and whole-cell patch-clamping, TRPC7 was found to be positively associated with the activity of ryanodine receptor 2 (RyR2), sarco/endoplasmic reticulum calcium-ATPase (SERCA), and sodium-calcium exchanger (NCX) but not hyperpolarization-activated, cyclic nucleotide-gated channel (HCN), and inositol trisphosphate receptor (IP3R). By western blot analysis, we also found that knockdown or overexpression of TRPC7 did not alter the expression of HCN4, Cav1.3, Cav3.1, Cav3.2, IP3R1, RyR2, and SERCA but positively regulated the phosphorylation of RyR2 at S2814 and phospholamban (PLN) at T17. Taken together, our results showed that TRPC7 plays a positive role in determining the CaTs, calcium sparks and the APs of ESC-CMs and therefore positively regulates the automaticity of ESC-CMs. The underlying mechanisms are also elucidated in our study. Therefore, this aim was more than 100% achieved. Aim 2. To investigate if the post-translational modifications of TRPC7 regulates its structural role in developing cardiomyocytes. By immunocytochemistry, the subcellular localization of TRPC7 was found to translocate from cell periphery to M-line and finally to Z-line during the maturation of ESC-CMs. By western blotting, TRPC7 expression was found to increase as maturation occurred; this increase in expression was concomitant with an increase in the size of TRPC7 protein. Treatment of the proteins with PNGase F, an enzyme for removing N-glycosylation, confirmed that TRPC7 was N-glycosylated in ESC-CMs, and the glycosylation increased as maturation occurred. TRPC7 was knocked down in more mature ESC-CMs by AdVs as described in Aim 1. Intriguingly, immunostaining of the sarcomere protein alpha-actinin followed by confocal microscopy analysis revealed that sarcomeres were disassembled after TRPC7 knockdown in more mature ESC-CMs, suggesting TRPC7 may be involved in maintaining the stability of sarcomeres. Co-immunoprecipitation followed by mass spectrometry was employed to identify the interacting partners of TRPC7. Out of 231 identified proteins, nexilin, a novel Z-line protein, was a highly confident interacting partner of TRPC7. Previous study showed that nexilin helps to stabilize the structure of Z-lines in cardiomyocytes. We speculate that TRPC7 can assist to maintain the integrity of sarcomeres through the interaction with nexilin. Interestingly, N-glycosylated TRPC7 was found to physically associate with nexilin as revealed by co-immunoprecipitation followed by western blotting. By combining the prediction result from NetNGlyc and the typical topology of other TRPC channels, we speculated that there are two N-glycosylation sites (N418, N514) in TRPC7. Three glycosylation-deficient mutants, namely N418Q, N514Q and N418/514Q, were constructed by replacing asparagine (N) with glutamine (Q) at one or two potential N-glycosylation sites; they were then expressed in HEK 293T. Treatment of cell lysates or live cells by PNGase F and tunicamycin respectively, followed by immunoblotting analysis revealed that N418 and N514 are the only two N-glycosylation sites in TRPC7. Immunoblotting analysis also showed the reduction of protein expression when one or two N-glycosylation sites were mutated. Interestingly, reduced cell surface expression of TRPC7 was detected via immunocytochemistry when two N-glycosylation sites were simultaneously mutated. Our findings suggested that N-glycosylation may help TRPC7 to be targeted correctly on the plasma membrane and subsequently stabilize the structure of sarcomeres by strengthening the interaction of TRPC7 with Z-line protein nexilin. Taken together, TRPC7 has a structural role in ESC-CMs; it helps to stabilize the sarcomere of ESC-CMs. In addition, the post-translational modification N-glycosylation of TRPC7 helps with this structural role of TPRC7 by directing TRPC7 to plasma membrane where it can interact with the Z-line protein nexilin. We have also identified the N-glycosylation sites of TRPC7. Overall, this aim was more than 100% achieved. Aim 3. To investigate if TRPC7 channels mediate the maturation &/hypertrophy of ESC-CMs and if activation of alpha1-adrenergic receptor leads to the maturation &/hypertrophy of ESC-CMs through activating TRPC7. By calcium imaging, knockdown of TRPC7 in ESC-CMs was found to decrease the kinetics of CaTs (increase the time-to-peak and decay constant, and decrease the Vmax-upstroke and Vmax-decay of CaTs). On the other hand, overexpression of TRPC7 exerted the opposite effects and increased the kinetics of CaTs. In line with these results, TRPC7 knockdown decreased the activity of RyR2 and SERCA, while TRPC7 overexpression exerted the opposite effects. These results suggested that TRPC7 positively regulates maturation at functional level. In addition, TRPC7 knockdown was found to decrease the size of ESC-CMs, suggesting that TPRC7 positively regulates maturation at morphological level. Moreover, TRPC7 may be a positive regulator of physiological hypertrophy. Moreover, as mentioned in Aim 2, co-immunoprecipitation followed by mass spectrometry was employed to identify the interacting partners of TRPC7 and 231 interacting partners of TRPC7 were identified. When these genes were analyzed by Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) analysis, interestingly, many of these proteins were found to be involved in “dilated cardiomyopathy” pathway. Therefore, an additional information generated by this study was that TRPC7 may be involved in the regulation of cardiac diseases. While further investigation in these pathological pathways is beyond the scope of the present project, this opens up a new direction for further investigation of the pathological role of TRPC7. On the other hand, unlike what has been reported in neonatal mouse cardiomyocytes or human ESC-CMs, we did not observe any significant change in cell size when phenylephrine, an alpha1-adrenergic receptor agonist, was applied to ESC-CMs. In addition, as indicated in Aim 2, knockdown of TRPC7 in more mature ESC-CMs for longer run led to disassembly of sarcomere; this precludes us from further investigating if TRPC7 knockdown would reverse the effect of activation of alpha1-adrenergic receptor, if any. Altogether, TRPC7 positively regulates the maturation and the cell size of ESC-CMs. However, activation of alpha1-adrenergic receptor cannot lead to increase in cell size of ESC-CMs in our hand. This aim was 100% achieved.

14176817.label: Major findings and research outcome
14176817.value: Major findings of this project are listed below: i) TRPC7 is expressed in ESC-CMs and positively regulates the calcium transients and action potentials of ESC-CMs. It regulates the automaticity of ESC-CMs by increasing the activity of NCX, RyR2 and SERCA. ii) TRPC7 positively regulates the stability of sarcomere of ESC-CMs through its interaction with the Z-line protein nexilin. iii) TRPC7 is post-translationally modified by N-glycosylation at position N418 and N514. The N-glycosylation increases the expression of TRPC7 and directs the plasma membrane localization of TRPC7. iv) N-glycosylated TRPC7 interacts with nexilin and stabilizes the sarcomere structure of ESC-CMs. v) TRPC7 positively regulates the maturation and the cell size of ESC-CMs. vi) Many of the proteins that interact physically with TRPC7 were found to be involved in the “dilated cardiomyopathy” pathway as revealed by KEGG analysis. All results involving the role of TRPC7 in determining the calcium transients and action potentials of ESC-CMs, and the mechanisms underlying the role of TRPC7, were published in form of conference abstracts and in a full-length peer-reviewed research paper as documented in Part C. All results involving the structural role of TRPC7 in sarcomere stability and the post-translational modification of TRPC7 are packaged into another full-length research paper and the paper is under preparation. The manuscript is expected to be submitted at the beginning of 2021. Some results were also published in form of conference abstracts as documented in Part C. In addition, related review articles have been published as documented in Part C. The identification of 231 novel interacting partners of TRPC7 has also led to some potential future directions (please see section 6.2 below). All of the results generated in this whole project were reported in one PhD thesis (Dr. Xianji Liu of this thesis has already been graduated in year 2020), one MPhil thesis (Ms. Yanzhuo Zhou of this thesis has submitted her MPhil thesis in December 2021) and some final year project theses of undergraduate students. Therefore, this project has allowed the training of several postgraduate and undergraduate students.

14176817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14176817.value: In this project, co-immunoprecipitation followed by mass spectrometry was employed to identify the interacting partners of TRPC7. A total of 231 interacting partners of TRPC7 were identified. When these genes were analyzed by KEGG analysis, interestingly, many of these genes were found to be involved in six important pathways, including the “dilated cardiomyopathy” pathway. In the future, the role of TRPC7 in regulating cardiac diseased conditions and the underlying mechanisms would be investigated by in vitro cell model and in vivo animal model. In addition, the identified TRPC7 interacting proteins include ion channels located on the sarcoplasmic reticulum and on the plasma membrane. We speculate that TRPC7 may form a functional complex with these ion channels. Further investigation would be conducted to confirm that they are physically interacting with each other. Thereafter, molecular level and functional level studies will be conducted to investigate the physiological functions of the complex.

14176817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14176817.value: Embryonic stem cells (ESCs) can propagate indefinitely in culture and have the ability to give rise to all differentiated cell types in the body, including cardiomyocytes. ESCs can therefore be an excellent source of cardiomyocytes for research and future therapeutic applications. The functional and structural properties, as well as the maturation of these potential replacement cells must be better understood before such cells can be used for therapeutic purposes. Electrical signals, calcium signals and contractile function are involved in the important excitation-contraction coupling of cardiomyocytes. In this project, a combination of cell biology, molecular biology, electrophysiology and genetic manipulation techniques were employed. Canonical transient receptor potential isoform 7 (TRPC7) channels were found to be important for regulating the electrophysiology and calcium signals, for maintaining the sarcomere structure, and for regulating the maturation of ESC-derived cardiomyocytes. Detailed mechanisms of how TRPC7 channels exert their effects were also elucidated in this study. This project has generated novel and important information on the role of TRPC7 in regulating the functions, structure and the maturation of ESC-derived cardiomyocytes. Altogether, this project is crucial for understanding the complex biology of ESC-derived cardiomyocytes and is pivotal for revealing the therapeutic potentials of ESC-derived cardiomyocytes.

14177217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14177217.value: Macroautophagy, the major pathway for autophagy, involves the formation of a double membrane structure known as autophagosome that encircles cytoplasmic cargos, such as proteins or damaged organelles, and delivers them to the lysosomes/vacuoles for degradation. We have previously identified a novel regulator, SH3P2, of autophagosome biogenesis in Arabidopsis. We showed that SH3P2 is recruited to autophagosomes upon induction of autophagy, and is essential to the biogenesis of autophagosomes. Knock-down of AtSH3P2 was lethal in transgenic Arabidopsis. Noteworthy, we have identified a novel interaction between the SH3 domain of SH3P2 and ATG8. To date, the functional role of this interaction in the biogenesis of autophagosomes is not known. In this proposal, we will address the following questions: (1) how does SH3P2 interact with ATG8? (2) What is the functional role of such interaction. Taking advantages of the observation that ATG8 can only interact with SH3P2, but not with other homologs such as SH3P1 and SH3P3, we hypothesize that surface residues unique in SH3P2 should be involved in binding ATG8. We will perform alanine-scanning mutagenesis on these residues. Mutants of SH3P2 created will be tested for their interaction with ATG8, and their effects on autophagosome biogenesis in Arabidopsis. To better understand how SH3P2 interacts with ATG8, we propose to determine the structure of ATG8 in complex with the SH3 domain. To demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed NMR experiments, we have obtained good HSQC spectrum of Arabidopsis ATG8f. As autophagy plays important roles in many aspects of plant physiology (such as stress tolerance and plant-pathogen interactions), a better understanding on the plant autophagy mechanism may have applications in crops improvement in the future. 巨自噬為最廣泛存在的自噬途徑，它的發生始於形成雙層膜結構叫自噬小體，自噬小體會包圍著胞內貨物，比如蛋白，損壞的細胞器，把它們送到溶酶體或液泡，降解成小分子重新參與代謝。我們在前期研究發現了一個新的調控自噬小體發育的蛋白AtSH3P2。結果顯示，誘導自噬發生時AtSH3P2會被招募到自噬小體上，並且AtSH3P2對於自噬小體的形成是必需的。敲除AtSH3P2基因會令轉基因擬南芥幼苗致死。值得注意的是，我們發現了一個新的相互作用存在於AtSH3P2的SH3結構域同AtATG8之間。到目前為止，二者的相互作用在自噬小體發育過程中的作用尚不清楚。本計劃書提出了兩個問題：（1）AtSH3P2與 AtATG8如何相互作用？ （2）該相互作用如何調控自噬小體的發育？ AtSH3P家族在擬南芥中有三個同源體，其中只有AtSH3P2可以和AtATG8相互作用。氨基酸序列比對顯示AtSH3P2蛋白中存在一些與AtSH3P1和AtSH3P3不同的特殊序列，因此我們推測AtSH3P2中的特殊序列可能是AtATG8的結合位點。我們將突變這些可能的結合位點，並創建相應的突變體來測試這些突變是否會影響同AtATG8的相互作用，並觀察這些突變對自噬小體形成的影響。為了更清楚的理解AtSH3P2和AtATG8如何相互作用，我們將通過解析AtSH3P2的SH3結構域同AtATG8的複合體蛋白結構。目前我們得到的AtATG8 的HSQC圖譜證明了NMR實驗的可行性。自噬在很多生理過程例如植物逆境脅迫及病原體侵害防禦中發揮重要作用，因此對植物自噬途徑分子機制的研究對於農業發展應用意義重大。

14177217.label: Realisation of objectives
14177217.value: The main theme of this project is to understand how does autophagy adaptor protein SH3P2 interact with ATG8 (autophagy-related protein 8) and how the interaction affect autophagy in Arabidopsis. Most of the work described in this completion report has been reported in Sun et al. (2021) “Mechanistic insights into an atypical interaction between ATG8 and SH3P2 in Arabidopsis thaliana” Autophagy, published online ahead of print, https://doi.org/10.1080/15548627.2021.1976965. Unpublished results are reported in (Cheung et al. in preparation) attached with this report. We have performed in vitro GST pull down assay to test the specificity of SH3P2/ATG8 interaction. Recombinant SH3 domains of SH3P1, SH3P2 and SH3P3 were expressed in E. coli and loaded to GST resins pre-equilibrated with GST-tagged ATG8f. Our results showed that only the SH3 domain of SH3P2 (SH3P2-SH3), but not SH3P1-SH3 and SH3P3-SH3, was co-eluted with GST-ATG8f, suggesting ATG8 selectively interacts with SH3P2 (Fig. 1, Sun et al., 2021). We further showed that SH3P2 interacts with all isoforms (ATG8a-i) of ATG8 (Fig. S1, Sun et al., 2021). The SH3P2/ATG8 interaction in Arabidopsis was confirmed by the CNX recruitment assay (Fig. 1, Sun et al., 2021). Since only SH3P2, but not SH3P1 and SH3P3, can interact with ATG8, we hypothesize that residues that are unique in SH3P2 are responsible for binding ATG8f. To test this hypothesis, we created five double-substituted variants (L307A/F308A, H311A/G312A, D315A/V316A, S321A/T322A, Y350A/G351A) of SH3P2-SH3 and tested their interactions with ATG8f by GST pull-down assay (Fig. 1, Cheung et al., in preparation). Our results showed that substitutions of H311A/G312A, S321A/T322A and Y350A/G351A resulted in weaken interactions between SH3P2 and ATG8f. A sextuple variant combining all six substitutions were created and the H311A/G312A/S321A/T322A/Y350A/G351A variant did not interact with ATG8f according to the microscale thermophoresis assay (Fig. 1, Cheung et al., in preparation). As ATG8 is well-known for its interaction with the ATG8-interacting motif (AIM) with a consensus sequence of [W/F/Y]xx[L/I/V], we identified three AIM-like motifs in SH3P2-SH3: 310-YHGV-313, 325-YVVV-328, 350-YGYI-353. In vitro pull-down assay showed that ATG8f interacts with peptide sequence containing the YVVV motif, but not the YHGV and YGYI motifs (Fig. 2, Sun et al., 2021). Y325A/V328A substitution abolished the SH3P2-ATG8 interactions in co-immunoprecipitation, yeast-two hybrid and CNX recruitment assays, supporting the role of these two residues in the SH3P2-ATG8 interaction in Arabidopsis. To understand the structural basis of SH3P2/ATG8 specific interaction, we have determined the solution structure of Arabidopsis ATG8f by NMR spectroscopy (Fig. 3, Sun et al., 2021). We have expressed and purified 15N and 13C labelled samples of ATG8f and SH3P2-SH3 and assigned the backbone resonances ATG8f, SH3P2-SH3, ATG8f in complex with SH3P2-SH3 and with a canonical AIM from a selective autophagy adaptor protein, NBR1 (Fig. 2 and 3, Cheung et al., in preparation; Fig. S4, Sun et al., 2021). NMR titration experiments identified I22, Y26, R29, K47 and R68 around the W- and L-sites of ATG8f underwent large chemical shift changes upon binding the AIM of NBR1. Substitutions of these residues with acidic residues abolished NBR1/ATG8f interactions. In contrast, substitutions of Y26E/R29E, which abolished NBR1/ATG8 interaction, did not affect the SH3P2/ATG8 interactions in pull-down, co-immunoprecipitation and in vivo CNX recruitment assays (Fig. 5, Sun et al., 2021). These observation suggest SH3P2/ATG8 interaction is different from that between ATG8 and NBR1. Although we showed that ATG8 interacts with the peptide motif of 325-YVVV-328 of SH3P2, crafting this motif to SH3P1 and SH3P3 failed to promote interaction with ATG8 (Fig. 2, Sun et al., 2021). Taken together, ATG8 interacts with SH3P2 atypically and does not follow the rules of canonical AIM interaction. To gain structural insights into SH3P2/ATG8 interaction, we have modelled the structure of SH3P2/ATG8f complex using the program HDOCK (http://hdock.phys.hust.edu.cn/) with inputs of experimental evidence derived from NMR spectroscopy and site-directed mutagenesis analyses (Fig. 4, Cheung et al., in preparation). Consistent with mutagenesis data, SH3P2-SH3 binds mainly to residues around the L-site of ATG8f and such interaction requires proper 3D conformation of SH3P2-SH3. Since both SH3P2 and NBR1 can interact with ATG8, we next tested if they would compete for binding ATG8. To this end, we have purified recombinant ubiquitin-associated domains of NBR1 containing the AIM-motif (NBR1-UBA), SH3P2-SH3 and ATG8f and tested their interaction by analytical gel filtration (Fig. 4A, Sun et al., 2021). When ATG8f was mixed with SH3P2-SH3 and NBR1-UBA in a 2:1:1 molar ratio, ATG8f could form complexes with both SH3P2-SH3/ATG8f and NBR1-UBA. On the other hand, if ATG8f was mixed in a limited amount with the two proteins in a 1:1:1 ratio, majority of ATG8f formed complex with NBR1-UBA, suggesting NBR1 can outcompete with SH3P2 in forming a complex with ATG8. That NBR1 could outcompete with SH3P2 for ATG8 binding was also suggested by co-immunoprecipitation experiments using full length NBR1 and SH3P2 (Fig. 4B, Sun et al., 2021). To test how SH3P2/ATG8 interaction affects autophagy, we have created transgenic Arabidopsis expressing GFP-tagged SH3P2 and its ATG8-interaction-defective (Y325A/V328A) variant. The Y325A/V328A substitution disrupted the co-localization of SH3P2-GFP and mCherry-ATG8e in transgenic plants upon induction of authophagy by BTH treatment (Fig. 6B, Sun et al., 2021). This observation suggests that SH3P2/ATG8 interaction is important in the recruitment of SH3P2 to the autophagosomes. In addition, while co-treatment of BTH and ConcA induced the formation of autophagic bodies in transgenic plants expressing wild-type SH3P2-GFP, the formation of GFP-labelled autophagic bodies was significantly reduced in transgenic plants expressing Y325A/V328A variant of SH3P2-GFP (Fig. 6C, Sun et al., 2021). Taken together, our results support the essential role of SH3P2/ATG8 interaction in recruiting SH3P2 to the autophagosomes. This project is a close collaboration that combines the biochemical and structural approach of Wong’s group (PI) and plant cell biology approach of Jiang’s group (Co-I). Most of the biochemical and structural work was performed by Shuangli Sun, who was a PhD student of Wong’s group and the first author of the Autophagy paper (Sun et al., 2021). The corresponding author of the Autophagy paper, Xiaohong Zhuang, used to be a post-doctoral researcher in Jiang’s group when the project began but later became independent as an Assistant Professor. We believe we have achieved all objectives of the projects.

14177217.label: Major findings and research outcome
14177217.value: Through this project, we have combined biochemical, structural and plant cell biology approaches to understand how SH3P2 interacts with ATG8. Here is a summary of our major findings: 1. We have determined the solution structure of ATG8f. Structural comparison with the crystal structure of potato ATG8CL in complex with the AIM of a pathogen effector shows large conformational changes in residues (I22, Y26, R29, K47, V64 and R68) around the W- and L-sites of ATG8. 2. We have shown that ATG8 selectively interacts with the SH3 domain of SH3P2, but not with SH3P1 and SH3P3. By combining NMR spectroscopy, site-directed mutagenesis and modelling studies, we showed that residues in the loop between β1 and β2 of SH3P2 are responsible for interaction with ATG8. 3. We have shown that the interaction between ATG8 and SH3P2 is different from that between ATG8 and a canonical AIM from NBR1. We argued that the SH3P2/ATG8 interaction is atypical and does not follow the rules of canonical interaction with AIM for the following reasons: (i) The AIM-like motif (325-YVVV-328) is conserved in SH3P1, SH3P2 and SH3P3 but only SH3P2 interacts with ATG8; (ii) substitution in residues (e.g. Y26E/R29E) abolished NBR1/ATG8 interaction without affecting SH3P2/ATG8 interaction. Our results suggest proper 3D conformation of SH3P2 is important for SH3P2/ATG8 interaction. 4. Using transgenic plants expressing ATG8-interaction-defective variant (Y325A/V328A) of SH3P2, we have shown that the SH3P2/ATG8 is important for recruiting SH3P2 to the autophagosomes. Disturbing SH3P2/ATG8 impaired the recruitment of SH3P2 to the autophagosomes and to the autophagic bodies. 5. Our results provide an interesting observation that NBR1 can outcompete SH3P2 for ATG8 binding. When ATG8 is in excess, it can bind to both NBR1 and SH3P2. However, when ATG8 is limited, it preferentially forms complexes with NBR1 over SH3P2. Such preference in binding could play a role in switching of protein binding partner of ATG8 during different stages of autophagy – ATG8 recruits SH3P2 for the formation of autophagosomes but later switches to bind NBR1 in selective autophagy.

14177217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14177217.value: In addition to autophagy, SH3P2 has recently been implicated to play a role in endocytosis. Interestingly, we also showed that the SH3 domain of SH3P2 is responsible for interacting with Auxilin-like protein 2 (Sun et al., 2021). However, the 325-YVVV-328 motif of SH3P2 is not involved in binding Auxilin-like protein 2, suggesting the plasticity of SH3P2 in interacting with multiple protein binding partners in the endomembrane trafficking. It would be interesting to understand the structural basis of how SH3P2 interacts with Auxilin-like proteins in plants in the future.

14177217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14177217.value: Autophagy, or “self-eating”, is an essential process to eukaryotic cells. How SH3P2, a plant-specific autophagy adaptor protein, interacts with ATG8 of the autophagy machinery is not known. In this study, the researchers in this project combined biochemical, structural and plant cell biology approaches to understand how SH3P2 interacts with ATG8 and how such interaction play a role in autophagy in plant cells. They showed that the interaction between SH3P2 and ATG8 is atypical and is different from the interaction of ATG8 with a canonical ATG8-interacting motif found in a selective autophagy adaptor protein. Using transgenic plants, they showed that SH3P2/ATG8 interaction is essential in the recruitment of SH3P2 to the autophagosomes. Their work provides a mechanism where ATG8 can switch protein partners in different stages of autophagy.

14177317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14177317.value: Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) is an enveloped hepadnavirus that infects the liver. The replication of HBV in hepatocytes requires the packaging of the viral pregenomic RNA (pgRNA) and HBV DNA polymerase, which is also a reverse transcriptase, in a nucleocapsid formed by the Hepatitis B Virus core protein (HBVcp). Maturation of HBV occurs when the pgRNA is reverse transcribed into DNA and the nucleocapsid acquires an envelop at the ER. It has been shown that the C-terminal domain (CTD) of HBVcp requires to be phosphorylated during the encapsidation of the HBV pgRNA and DNA polymerase. SR Protein Kinases (SRPKs), a family of kinases that involves in the regulation of pre-mRNA splicing, have been suggested to be the cellular kinases that phosphorylate the HBVcp CTD. A recent model suggests that the binding of SRPKs to unphosphorylated HBVcp prevents self-assembly of the core protein and encapsidation of non-pregenomic RNA. Subsequent phosphorylation of HBVcp by SRPKs lowers their affinity and the binding of pgRNA to HBVcp displaces SRPKs, resulting in the final assembly of the nucleocapsid. We have previously illustrated that a SRPK-specific docking groove is important for the interaction and phosphorylation of different substrates including HBVcp. We now propose to further decipher the detailed molecular mechanisms of interaction and phosphorylation of HBVcp by SRPK2 using various biochemical and structural approaches. We will investigate if HBVcp contains multiple docking motifs that contribute to its multisite phosphorylation. To understand how SRPK2 interacts with free HBVcp and the viral capsid, we propose to determine the crystal structure of kinase-HBVcp complex and the cryo-EM structure of SRPK2-bound nucleocapsid. We will also study how the direct interaction between HBVcp and SRPK2 affects HBV replication in vivo. Our lab has recently identified a docking groove-targeting inhibitor that inhibits the binding and phosphorylation of substrates by SRPKs. Since HBVcp also binds to the docking groove, we will apply this inhibitor to test if it affects the replication of HBV. Together, our findings will significantly improve our understanding on how SRPK2 regulates HBVcp phosphorylation and subsequently affects capsid assembly. We will also provide information on the biological significance of SRPK2 in HBV life cycle. Although detailed studies and optimization of the inhibitor will be proposed elsewhere, this project will help to verify if SRPKs could serve as new targets for anti-HBV therapeutics and the structural information obtained may aid the development of a new class of antiviral drug. 乙型肝炎病毒（HBV）是一種包膜型嗜肝病毒，它在肝細胞中的複制需要病毒的前基因組RNA(pgRNA)和HBV DNA 聚合酶在乙型肝炎病毒核心蛋白(HBVcp)形成的核衣殼中組裝。因為HBV DNA聚合酶同時也是一種逆轉錄酶聚合酶, pgRNA會被反轉錄成DNA; 與此同時核衣殼在ER獲得包膜，令HBV變為成熟。 研究表明：HBV pgRNA和DNA聚合酶衣殼化期間，HBVcp的C末端結構域（CTD）需要被磷酸化。 SR蛋白激酶（SRPKs）是涉及前mRNA剪接調控的一類激酶，已經被認為是磷酸化HBVcp CTD的細胞激酶。最近的一個研究模型表明：SRPKs與未磷酸化的HBVcp結合能阻止核心蛋白的自組裝和非前基因組RNA的衣殼化。隨後HBVcp被SRPK磷酸化，降低了SRPK與HBVcp的親和力，使pgRNA代替SRPK與HBVcp的結合，導致核衣殼的組裝完成。 我們之前的研究已表明，SRPK特異性對接槽對於包括HBVcp在內的不同底物之間的相互作用和磷酸化作用非常重要。現在，我們建議運用各種生物化學和結構學方法進一步破譯SRPK2與HBVcp的相互作用和磷酸化作用的詳細分子機制。我們將探究HBVcp是否包含多個對其磷酸化作用的對接點。為了了解SRPK2如何與游離HBVcp和病毒衣殼的相互作用，我們要解出激酶 - HBVcp複合物的晶體結構和SRPK2結合衣殼體的cryo-EM結構。 HBVcp和SRPK2之間的直接相互作用如何影響HBV在體內復制也將被研究。我們實驗室最近已經發現一種對接槽靶向抑製劑，能夠抑制SRPK對底物的結合和磷酸化作用。由於HBVcp也與對接槽結合，因此我們將應用該抑製劑來測試它是否影響HBV的體內復制。 這個發現還將顯著提高我們對SRPK2如何調節HBVcp磷酸化及其隨後如何影響衣殼體裝配的認識。有關SRPK2在HBV生命週期中的生物學意義也將被闡釋。雖然抑製劑的詳細研究和優化將在別處提出，但該項目將有助於驗證SRPK是否可以作為抗HBV治療的新靶點，所獲得的結構信息可能有助於開發新一類抗病毒藥物。

14177317.label: Realisation of objectives
14177317.value: Objective 1. We have performed all assays in this objective in triplicates using a HBVcp mutant which Y132 was mutated to alanine (hereafter referred to as “Cp dimer”). We determined that SRPK2 phosphorylated Cp dimer at ~ 6 sites and among these, 1.6 ± 0.1 sites were phosphorylated in a partial processive manner (in which only a fraction of substrate molecules remain associated with the kinase after each turnover) under our start-trap condition. Point mutagenesis studies further confirmed that S157, S164, and S172 were the major sites while S170, S178, and S180 could also be phosphorylated by SRPK2. Together with the results that were reported in the mid-term report, all of our new results using Cp dimer were consistent with the notion that the docking groove of SRPK2 and the C-terminal arginine-rich domain (ARD) of HBV were critical for their interaction and phosphorylation. We had performed the crosslinking experiments as described in the proposal. We observed that Cp dimer(T147C) crosslinked with SRPK2 when there was no ATP or when ATP concentrations were low. Less crosslinked products had been observed when the concentrations of ATP increased. Cp dimer(S157C) crosslinked with SRPK2 in an ATP-independent manner. On the other hand, more crosslinked SRPK-Cp dimer(S170C) complex was observed when ATP was presented. Finally, Cp dimer(S178C) failed to crosslink with SRPK2 regardless of whether ATP was presented or not. These results suggested that SRPK2 preferentially interacted with the N-terminal region of the ARD prior to phosphorylation and the ARD slid along the docking groove in a N-to-C manner. Overall, the objective has been fully achieved. Objective 2 We have investigated whether SRPK2, as previously reported for SRPK1, gates HBV capsid assembly. We performed gel filtration chromatography using an active construct of SRPK2 (SRPK2∆S1) and wild-type core protein (CpWT) in the presence or absence of ATP. Our results showed that in the absence of ATP, all core proteins were trapped by SRPK2 to form heterodimeric complexes; whereas in the presence of ATP, a portion of core proteins, while remained bound with a small amount of SRPK2∆S1, were eluted at the void volume, suggesting that they had assembled into high molecular weight capsids. Negative staining electron microscopy showed that the void volume samples had assembled into spherical particles with diameters of ~35nm, which is the typical diameter of a T=4 HBV capsid, confirming that HBV capsids had been formed after phosphorylation. This suggested SRPK2, similar to SRPK1, gated the capsid assembly process by binding unphosphorylated HBVcp and kept the latter in a low oligomeric state. Phosphorylation of HBVcp by SRPK2 subsequently triggered the dissociation of the complex and subsequently allowed the formation of HBV capsids. We next repeated the experiment using SRPK2DM and showed that the mutant failed to form stable complex with CpWT and could not prevent capsid formation regardless of whether ATP is presented or not. Our results demonstrated that HBVcp binding via the docking groove was important for the SRPK2-gating mechanism. We have investigated the effects of SRPK2 knockout on HBV replication in vivo. We observed that knockout of SRPK2 resulted in a significant decrease of the nuclear cccDNA level but a small increase in the level of total intracellular pgRNA. On the other hand, the level of viral DNA in the medium decreased by half. Surprisingly, HBsAg level was found to be greatly elevated. The lowered levels of nuclear cccDNA and extracellular viral DNA suggested the knockout of SRPK2 had attenuated viral replication. We speculated that the elevated levels of intracellular pgRNA and extracellular HBsAg were the results of lowered pgRNA encapsidation efficiency in the absence of SRPK2 because unencapsidated pgRNA could not be converted to rcDNA, and thus was trapped intracellularly and in turn produce more free HBsAG via translation. We evaluated the efficiency of pgRNA encapsidation in SRPK2KO cells and found that it was lowered. We next tested whether the lowered encapsidation efficiency was the result of a lack of interaction or phosphorylation of HBVcp by SRPK2. Surprisingly, our results showed that both SRPK2DM and SRPK2KD (kinase-dead) mutant constructs could rescue the encapsidation efficiency to similar extents as the wild-type kinase. This suggested that besides the proposed “gating” mechanism, there might be alternative SRPK2-mediated mechanisms for pgRNA encapsidation that require either the interaction or phosphorylation of HBVcp alone in a non-mutually exclusive manner. During our study, we have attempted to knockout or knockdown SRPK1 in SRPK2KO HepG2 cells. However, the double knockout HepG2 cells were not viable and SRPK1 knockdown in SRPK2KO cells made them unsuitable for further transfection experiments. We have also attempted to study whether transient transfection of SRPK2DM or SRPK2KD in SRPK2KO HepG2 cells could rescue HBV replication. Yet, since we need to ascertain equivalent transfection of pHBV1.3D in these experiments, we co-transfected pEGFP to monitor the transfection efficiency and as a normalizer in our qRT-PCR. This detrimentally affected the transfection efficiency of SRPK2DM or SRPK2KD constructs, making further analysis unfeasible. Therefore, we reported our observations in the control and SRPK2KO cells only in our manuscript. We are currently testing how our peptide inhibitor and the ATP-competitive inhibitor SRPIN340 affect HBV replication. These experiments have been delayed significantly due to COVID-19 lockdown and lab closure. Nonetheless, we have mostly achieved the objective by providing strong evidence that the direct interaction between SRPK2 and HBVcp is important for HBV replication. Objective 3 We have determined the cryo-EM structures of the HBV capsid in its apo-form and in complex with SRPK2∆S1. When comparing the 3D reconstructions of the complex and capsid only, which were low-pass filtered to 10Å, ~30 extrusions were found on the twofold vertices of the complex reconstruction. We next performed focused classification and refinement. A class of 36624 subparticles was chosen for the subsequent masked 3D auto-refinement with C1 symmetry applied. A 12Å density map was reconstructed. The crystal structure of SRPK2 (PDB ID:2X7G) was fitted into the density map above the twofold vertex. The fitting result illustrated that whole kinase structure can be fitted into the density, leaving some extra density that is close to the disordered region of the crystal structure of SRPK2. The front of SRPK2 lays close to the opening at the twofold vertex. We also observed some densities extend through the twofold vertex to the capsid surface where SRPK2 is anchored. These densities likely represent the externalized C-terminal domain of HBVcp, which has been reported previously, for the binding of SRPK2. However, we were not able to reveal the details of the binding interface as our structure is limited by the low resolution. Nevertheless, we have confirmed and elucidated how SRPK2 interacts with HBV capsid. We have spent most of our efforts in determining the cryo-EM structures during the funding period. Although we have also invested tremendous efforts in optimizing the crystals of HBVcp in complex with an active fragment of SRPK2, we were not able to improve the crystal size nor diffraction quality. We are currently attempting to crystallize different constructs of HBVcp in complex with SRPK2. Overall, we have successfully achieved the objective by elucidating how SRPK2 binds to HBV capsid.

14177317.label: Major findings and research outcome
14177317.value: Members of the serine-arginine protein kinase (SRPK) family, SRPK1 and SRPK2, have been identified to phosphorylate the HBV core protein (HBVcp) and are important for pregenomic RNA encapsidation during viral nucleocapsid assembly. Among them, SRPK2 exhibits higher kinase activity towards HBVcp. In this study, we demonstrated SRPK2 utilizes a SRPK-specific docking groove to directly interact with the arginine-rich domain (ARD) of HBVcp to regulate its phosphorylation. We mapped six sites at the ARD that could be phosphorylated by SRPK2 and revealed that the kinase phosphorylates HBVcp at 1.6 sites in a partially processive manner. We also unveiled that SRPK2 binds to unphosphorylated HBVcp to prevent capsid assembly. Upon phosphorylation, most of the HBVcp dissociates from the kinases to form viral capsids. Cell-based experiments confirmed that SRPK2 is important for HBV replication by regulating the viral pregenome packaging. Finally, to elucidate the molecular mechanism of how SRPK2 interacts with HBVcp, we have determined a cryo-EM structure of HBV capsid in complex with SRPK2. The structure, together with our biochemical assays, reveals that ~30 molecules of SRPK2 decorate the surface of the viral capsid via a docking groove-ARD interaction. Together, our studies provide important insight on the molecular basis of how SRPK2 interacts with HBVcp and regulate HBV nucleocapsid formation. A manuscript describing the findings has been prepared. We are now awaiting the results of our inhibitor treatment of HBV-infected cells before submission. Cryo-EM maps for the HBV capsid, the SRPK2∆S1/HBV capsid complex, and the focused refine density map for SRPK2∆S1 bound on the HBV capsid have been deposited in PDB with the accession codes EMD-33553, EMD-33574, and EMD-33589, respectively.

14177317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14177317.value: There are several clinically available drugs to combat chronic HBV infection, which include formulations of alpha interferon to enhance the host antiviral response or nucleotide/nucleoside analogs that target the HBV DNA polymerase activity. However, alpha interferon treatment only achieve sustained virological response in approximately 35% of patients and all the drugs that target the HBV DNA polymerase have been reported to experience viral resistance due to mutations at their target sites. Therefore, there is a pressing need for novel antiviral therapeutic agents for HBV patients. Based on previous findings and our current work, SRPK2 represents an important host target for anti-HBV intervention. We have recently identified a SRPK-specific peptide inhibitor that can block the interaction between SRPK2 and its substrates including HBVcp. The molecular basis of how SRPK2 and HBVcp interact provides new insights to further optimize our inhibitor. We have a long-term plan to develop our inhibitor into a drug lead molecule and are collaborating with a chemistry group for such goal. We anticipate our inhibitor, by targeting cellular protein like SRPK2 instead of the viral ones, might be able to overcome the drug resistance problem that the current drug regimen is encountering.

14177317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14177317.value: Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) infection is a worldwide health problem that may lead to severe diseases such as liver cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. Current anti-HBV therapies cannot eradicate the virus from patients, therefore the identification of new therapeutic targets such as host cellular proteins involved in pathogenesis is needed. In this study, we have provided new insights on how SRPK2, a cellular kinase, plays an important role in the regulation of viral pregenome encapsidation and capsid formation during HBV replication. We also illustrated how a SRPK-specific docking groove regulates the interaction and phosphorylation of HBVcp by SRPK2, and in turn modulates the capsid assembly. Together, our findings have significantly improved our understanding on how SRPK2 regulates HBVcp phosphorylation and subsequently affects capsid assembly. Our work also suggests that SRPK2 could serve as new target for anti-HBV therapeutics. The information obtained provides invaluable information to design a new class of anti-viral inhibitors that could block the interaction between SRPK2 and HBVcp and subsequently HBV viral replication.

14177617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14177617.value: Despite extensive research in the past several decades, how plants sense soil drying is still a fundamental question in our understanding of plant drought tolerance. Simply, we do not know the initial molecular mechanism of sensing soil moisture and the activation of downstream adaptive traits. Classically, hydrotropism is coined for the differential growth of root towards high moisture gradient but the genetic basis of hydrotropism is largely unknown, although a couple of genes have been reported in the hydrotropic responses in Arabidopsis. Hydrotropic response is difficult to be dissected as other tropisms, particularly gravitropism, strongly interact with hydrotropism. We have observed an intriguing response that rice seed can sense moisture gradient (air humidity) even before root emergence during seed germination. Profuse hairs are developed from the surface of coleorhiza at near saturated humidity before root emergence, while low air humidity restricts the development of such hairs as well as root emergence and ultimately seed germination, even though the seeds are almost fully imbibed. Coleorhiza hairs are known to anchor germinating seeds in seedling establishment but our finding suggests that they function to sense appropriate moisture for the seed germination. This adaptive phenotype suggests that specific cell types may sense moisture around seed surface and develop hairs originated from epidermal cells of coleorhiza. Similarly, root hairs are initiated on the root surface, although coleorhiza hairs are initiated quicker, longer and denser in nature than root hairs. But are they the same? We, therefore, propose first of all to investigate if the root hair specific genes are also working in coleorhiza hairs too. Overexpression and knock-out/down lines of several root hair specific genes will be analyzed. This may confirm the specific identities of coleorhiza hair, as their developmental regulations may suggest specific genes and therefore, specific functions. For deep exploration of this adaptive phenotype and its genetic basis, we propose to screen for its rice mutants. Mutant screening can start from available mutant resources or induced by EMS mutagenesis. In addition to search for genes from mutants, we also propose to examine the spatio-temporal gene expressions of coleorhiza tissue using RNA sequencing to provide clues of the specific genes of this phenotype. Outcome of this research will reveal the key genes in coleorhiza hair induction and increase our understanding of how plants sense moisture gradient and activate downstream adaptive responses to soil drying. 植物如何感知土壤乾旱是植物抗旱性研究中一個基本問題，但多年來仍然沒有定論。根本原因是我們不知道植物是如何感知土壤濕度和如何啟動下游的基因表達。我們在研究中發現水稻在萌發過程中可以感知空氣濕度，然後才有胚根出現。如果空氣濕度接近飽和，胚芽鞘上可以生出許多的鞘毛。當空氣濕度低於飽和時，幾乎沒有鞘毛出現，雖然種子也已充分吸水。胚芽鞘毛雖然有在種子萌發過程中幫助幼苗出土的作用，但它們是如何能感知空氣濕度的還不知道。這顯然與根在向水性反應中感應土壤濕度有關聯。本研究首先研究胚芽鞘毛和根毛的產生有什麼不同和相同，然後尋找胚芽鞘毛產生的特有基因，並對它們的功能進行鑒定。

14177617.label: Realisation of objectives
14177617.value: Plant roots can sense soil drying by enhancing growth to chase the water in soil profile. How this physiological process operates, or hydrosensing, is a fundamental question in plant science for long time. We have observed an intriguing response that rice seed can sense moisture gradient, i.e. air humidity, even before root emergence during seed germination. Profuse hairs are developed from the surface of coleorhiza at near saturated humidity before root emergence. However, low air humidity restricts the development of such hairs as well as root emergence and ultimately seed germination, even though the seeds are almost fully imbibed. To understand the interesting plant adaptation mechanism and its genetic background involved, we have performed the following studies: We have found that rice embryos have unique ability to absorb water from atmospheric water vapour under partial caryopsis-soil contact conditions. To absorb atmospheric moisture, rice embryos develop profuse and highly elongated hairs on embryo surface. These hairs, classically known as coleorhiza hairs, develop only on the rice embryo surface exposed to humid air and submergence of embryo surface inhibits their development. Compared to root hair development, we observed almost all other developmental features of coleorhiza hairs are also significantly different from rice root hairs. However, we have identified that rice coleorhiza hair development is also regulated by the same gene named as ROOT HAIRLESS1 (RHL1) that causes severe short root hairs in rice. In addition to the genetic identification of coleorhiza hair development, we have also found the mechanism how rice caryopses manage to keep the hairs turgid in natural open environments as the hairs are highly sensitive to dry air exposure. Video-documented images show that the unique humid air-dependent coleorhiza hair development and their ability to absorb water from water vapor present in microsites or soil air provide rice exceptional advantages in germination and seedling establishment. Ultimately, coleorhiza hairs may have contributed to the ecological success of rice, and perhaps also the grass family plants, to germinate in the right humidity condition (Bin Rahman et al. 2021, submitted to Plant Physiology and under reviewing). Coleorhiza hairs are developed in germinating seeds of all Poaceae family members, root hair-like but developed from the coleorhiza epidermal cells. The major role of coleorhiza hair in seed germination involves facilitating water uptake and nutrient supply for seed germination. Genetic control and regulation pathways of of coleorhiza hair development are largely unknown. We first of all compared the transcriptome profiles of coleorhiza development in the two rice subspecies, japonica and Indica, to identify major differentially expressed genes (DEGs). DEGs in embryo samples from seeds with embryo in air (EIA) as compared to embryo from seeds completely covered by water (CBW) were enriched in water deprivation, abscisic acid (ABA) and auxin metabolism, carbohydrate catabolism and phosphorus metabolism in coleorhiza hairs in both cultivars. Up‑regulation of key metabolic genes in ABA, auxin and dehydrin and aquaporin genes may help maintain the basic development of coleorhiza hair in japonica and indica in EIA samples during both early and late stages. Additionally, DEGs involved in glutathione metabolism and carbon metabolism are upregulated while DEGs involved in amino acid and nucleotide sugar metabolism are downregulated in EIA suggesting induction of oxidative stress‑alleviating genes and less priority to primary metabolism (Song et al. 2021a). Coleorhiza hairs help seed germination and seedling establishment, which are crucial processes in rice production in terms of direct seeding. Seeds of Nipponbare were treated under two water conditions: in one, half of the seed surface was immersed in water and the other half was embryo side in air (EIA), and in the other, the whole seed was covered by water (CBW). Coleorhiza hairs formed only in EIA samples. Transcriptomics was used to identify the gene regulation during coleorhiza hair formation in EIA (vs. CBW) embryos and endosperm. Embryos displayed more transcriptome modulation even though smaller in size than the endosperm. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were enriched in both primary and secondary metabolism and showed changes in abscisic acid, auxin, jasmonic acid, and salicylic acid signatures. Metabolites enrichment data were positively correlated with gene expression changes in the affected metabolic functional pathways. The presence of shorter coleorhiza hairs in an OsRHL1 (Os06g0184000, a coleorhiza hair formation regulation candidate gene) knockout mutant suggested that root hair-associated DEGs share molecular regulators that control the formation of coleorhiza hairs (Song et al. 2021b). Cultivated rice is very different from its wild relatives. Domestication and human selection over the years have harvested many natural mutations. With such thinking and support of this project, we have come up with reviews to show the rice breeders how to make use of the naturally existing genetic resources. We first analyzed the distribution and population types of drought-and flood-tolerant rice accessions, synthesized recent progresses of flood and drought tolerance research, and proposed a hypothesis that the molecular mechanisms of both drought and flood tolerance may be regulated by cross-talked pathways and coexist in some native landraces in Southern Asia. Then we identified a shared geographic distribution pattern for these highly stress-tolerant accessions and pointed out that the majority of these tolerant accessions predominately originated from Southern Asia including Bangladesh, a centralized narrow geographic region (Rahman and Zhang 2018). We believe these reviews will make impact to the rice researchers and breeders.

14177617.label: Major findings and research outcome
14177617.value: We have found that rice embryo, also likely all grass embryos, have unique ability to absorb water from humid air to promote germination under partial caryopsis-soil contact conditions, by developing specialized hygro-adaptive hairs, the coleorhiza, on embryo surface, utilizing the same ROOT HAIRLESS1 (RHL1) that controls root hair development. Analysis of the transcriptome profiles of coleorhiza development in different rice subspecies or genotypes show that there are many differentially expressed genes (DEGs) when external humidity conditions are different. Abscisic acid and auxin metabolism, carbohydrate catabolism and phosphorus, dehydrin and aquaporin genes are all upregulated in response to reduced humidity. In addition, with analysis with genome information we have found that drought and flood tolerance may be regulated by cross-talked pathways and coexist in some native landraces in Southern Asia, where stress tolerant accessions should be exploited in rice breeding.

14177617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14177617.value: Plant adaptations to stressful environments, including the early seed germination and seedling establishment, are always the key research areas for plant stress physiology research and crop breeding. Here we have revealed an interesting mechanism showing how a geminating rice seed senses the external air humidity and proceeds the germination process. Detailed genetic analysis have shown the key genes involved in this kind ecological adaptation. We shall work with rice breeders for more natural variations of this phenotype and see if the genes and traits involved can be exploited for better seed germination and seedling establishment that is crucial in rice production. Rice production has moved to a less labor-intensive way and direct seeding is a way to do it. Rice cultivars with good germination strength and better seedling establishment should have advantages.

14177617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14177617.value: Plant roots can sense soil drying by enhancing growth to chase the water in soil profile. How this physiological process operates is a fundamental question for long time. We have observed an intriguing response that rice seed can sense moisture gradient (air humidity) even before root emergence during seed germination. Profuse hairs are developed from the surface of coleorhiza at near saturated humidity before root emergence, while low air humidity restricts the development of such hairs as well as root emergence and ultimately seed germination, even though the seeds are almost fully imbibed. Coleorhiza hairs are known to anchor germinating seeds in seedling establishment but our finding suggests that they function to sense appropriate moisture for the seed germination. We have found that same ROOT HAIRLESS1 (RHL1) gene that controls root hair development is involved in this adaptation response. This finding enhances our understanding of how plants sense moisture gradient and activate downstream adaptive responses to soil drying.
