14200117.value: 在過去的幾年中，網絡社區正在呼籲互聯網體系結構中的“根本變革”。傳統上，互聯網架構主要依靠以端對端原則為主體的以主機為中心的模式[25]和基於TCP的可靠和按順序交付。以主機為中心的模式為互聯網服務，可以輕鬆支持諸如電子郵件或網頁瀏覽等眾多傳統服務。 然而，隨著人們創建視頻/音頻廣播，大規模信息分發（例如軟件更新）或物聯網（IoT）通信等新服務，顯而易見的是，傳統的互聯網架構不能 隨著這些服務的用戶或設備的增加而擴大。特別是，這些新服務中的許多更“數據為中心”：用戶不關心數據的“位置”，而是信息本身。 以信息為中心的網絡（ICN）是一種新的互聯網架構，可以滿足這一迫切需求。 ICN允許用戶的移動性，間歇性的連接性以及數據原始位置的獨立性，以便用戶可以從各種網絡緩存中訪問相同的數據。 ICN架構倡導“緩存”作為其網絡底層的一部分，內容可以由不同的互聯網服務提供商（ISP）或內容分發網絡（CDN）的提供商機會地緩存。 這可以帶來顯著的優點，如帶寬節省，短時延和服務器卸載。 由於緩存在全球內容傳遞中的根本作用，如何有效利用和分配緩存資源成為重要的研究課題。 為了實現ICN的框架，一個關鍵的組件是緩存的設計。 雖然有各種緩存算法，但是如何設計可以適應不斷變化的對象的緩存算法的緩存算法，如何量化緩存算法到最優緩存算法的距離，以及如何在競爭的ISP之間分配分佈式緩存（或 可以提供緩存等差價格的CDN運營商？ 這些是我們在本研究計劃中尋求回答的基本問題。 本研究的目的是為ICN設計分佈式緩存算法提供“理論基礎”。特別是，我們將開發數學理論和模型，以不僅量化一系列緩存算法的性能指標，即緩存命中概率，而且我們還旨在量化緩存算法如何適應變化的“快速”對像在分佈式設置下的概率。這是必不可少的，因為有大量的互聯網對象，根據他們的類型，有些人可能會快速流行，改變時間尺度，而其他人的流行度變化時間縮短。了解緩存算法對時變流行度的適應性將有助於我們在不同ISP或運營商的CDN之間設計分佈式緩存分配。我們還旨在調查分佈式緩存的“網絡經濟學”：ISP或CDN的運營商應如何設置適當的價格以最大限度地提高收入？鑑於這些價格，內容提供商應如何在互聯網的不同位置分配緩存資源？最後，當一個對像在多個地方進行緩存時，應該如何路由流量，以減少信息傳遞的延遲，同時減少網絡瓶頸？ 本研究考慮了大型網絡設置中分佈式緩存的數學分析，算法設計，以及地理分佈式數據中心網絡分佈式緩存策略的系統設計與實現。 除了理論和數學分析之外，我們還計劃在我們在中大的數據中心測試中實施緩存算法，以及我們的研究合作夥伴的一些數據中心。

14200117.label: Major findings and research outcome
14200117.value: In this project, we have completed what we set out to do (and more). In particular, we have created new and novel mathematical models to understand distributed caching in information centric networks. We have also came up with the models to understand the interaction between network service providers, caching operators as well as users, in particular, for different high layer applications. We have also implemented some distributed caching protocols and some of these ideas have been picked up by some industry, e.g., Huawei and Tencent Inc. In addition, we have also achieved related works on information centric networks, including how to provide virtual network functions (VNFs), feasibility of network connectivity via internet exchange, and estimating traffic size and flow availability in information centric network design. We also proposed to provide some edge services via the Docker technologies so as to realize the caching services.

14200117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14200117.value: There are potential number of interesting research questions, for example: - How to perform dynamic GPU scheduling with Live Migration at the network edge? - How to organize payment for the distributed caching services? - How to understand the reputation of caching operators so that users can select the appropriate caching services. These questions are fundamental and they deserve to be examined via other research projects.

14200117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14200117.value: The importance of this research is to understand the technical issues, as well as the scalability of distributed caching service for the whole Internet. To enable such service, we proposed the mathematical models to help us to design and implement the network protocols so to realize such service. We also investigated various technologies to enable this service, such as virtual machines, docker services, as well as network topology and flow reliability estimation so that operators can provide better caching services to end users.

14200217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14200217.value: Networked control techniques can be used in many novel engineering applications, including telemedicine, remote control of unmanned ground or aerial vehicles, telerobotics, and real-time real-life online games. The communication network plays a central role in a networked control system. Traditional design usually relies on dedicated communication channels, which can guarantee low upper bounds on communication delay but is costly and not scalable. On the other hand, solutions based on open networks, such as the Internet, are scalable and much less expensive. However, it is difficult to control network delay on such networks. Fortunately, recent advances in networking technology have offered new directions for realizing real-time networked control systems over open networks. Development of standards for the 5th Generation Wireless System, popularization of Software Defined Networking, and the rapid growth of mega data centers with highly structured architectures are some of the important new trends that will benefit the development of time critical networked control applications on open networks. This project is motivated by these new trends. It aims to investigate fundamental properties of networked control systems over an open network and to introduce new design methodologies for these systems. When control signals are transmitted over a communication network with uncontrollable elements, there is a probability that they will be delivered after their expected arrival times and become unusable to the system actuators. These control signals can be regarded as lost packets. There have been extensive studies in the literature on the effect of lost packets for networked control systems. In this project, we build on these prior studies and introduce an integrated model that will allow us to examine dynamic system stability and network routing protocol in one single model. This in turn helps us investigate the relationship among issues such as stability, sampling time, control delay, and packet loss probability. There are two major tasks in this project. The first task is focused on understanding the fundamental relationship between control and communication design issues for a single networked control system. The second task formulates a network optimization problem involving multiple independent network control systems over an open network and aims to find its globally optimal solution. Results from these investigations will help engineers in their job to design better control algorithm for time critical applications over open networks. 網絡控制技術可以用於大量工程應用中，如遠距離醫學，無人地面駕駛或無人機，遙操作機器人技術和實時真人在線遊戲等。 通信網絡在網絡控制系統中起著核心作用。傳統的設計通常依賴於專用通信信道，該種信道雖然可以保證較低的通信延遲，但成本較高且可擴展性較差。另外一方面，基於開放式網絡（如因特網）的系統設計方案雖然具有可擴展性好以及成本低等優點，但是此類網絡的傳輸延遲無法得到有效保證。 網絡技術的最新進展為實現基於開放式網絡的實時網絡控制系統提供了一些新的可能性。第五代無線通信系統標準的發展，軟件定義網絡的普及以及大型數據中心網絡的高速發展將會在很大程度上推動實時網絡控制系統在開放式網絡中的應用。 在當前新的發展趨勢下，本項目旨在研究基於開放式網絡的網絡控制系統的基礎性質，並引入一些新的設計方法。 當控制信號在一個不可控的通信網絡中傳輸時，可能出現信號無法按照預期時間到達而失效的情況。這些沒有按時到達的控制信號可以被視為丟失的數據包。目前，已經有大量文獻研究了數據包丟失對網絡控制系統的影響。本項目將在已有研究的基礎上引入一個新的綜合模型去研究動態系統的穩定性和網絡路由協議之間的關系。這將進一步有助於了解穩定性，采樣時間，控制延遲，和數據包丟失幾率之間的關系。 本項目主要有兩項研究工作。第一項工作的研究目標是建立單一網絡控制系統中控制設計和網絡通信設計的相互關系。第二項工作是將多個網絡控制系統訂制為一個網絡優化問題，並嘗試找出一個全局最佳設計方案。本項目的研究成果將有助工程師在有實時限制的網絡控制應用中設計更優的控制算法。

14200217.label: Realisation of objectives
14200217.value: This project focuses on control systems that are remotely controlled over a communication network shared by multiple users in addition to the controller. These types of systems have many potential applications, including transportation, logistics, and manufacturing. The aim of our project is to understand how issues such as stability, sampling time, control delay, and packet loss probability are interrelated, so that one could derive efficient control design policies for such systems. There are two main tasks in the project. The first task is to investigate the fundamental relationship between control and communication design for a single networked control system. The second task aims to extend the investigation to multiple independent networked control systems sharing a common wireless communication network. Both tasks had been well completed and results were summarized and published over several papers. We provide details of the project work as follows. Many networked control systems rely on wireless communication channels for the transmission of control decisions, for example, in controlling unmanned aerial vehicles or unmanned ground vehicles. It is well known that the transmissions over such channels are susceptible to packet losses. As a preliminary investigation for the first task, we studied the stabilization control of a discrete time linear dynamical system, for which the control effect is affected by a multiplicative noise. The noise could be interpreted as representing packet loss or other random transmission noises. Some early results were published in a paper appearing in the Systems & Control Letters under the title, “Stabilization of Discrete Time Stochastic System with Input Delay and Control Dependent Noise”. (In our Mid-term progress report we explained why this paper has a first submission date before the formal project start date, Dec 1, 2017. To summarize the key points: Dr. Tan Cheng, who had independently studied discrete dynamical systems relevant to this research project was recruited to serve as a postdoctoral fellow for this project. In the summer of 2017, after learning about our integrated control research task, he realized that his work could be applied to networked control systems involving a wireless communication channel and he subsequently made adjustments to his research focus. A joint paper was readied by end of August 2017. After formally joining our project, Dr. Tan continued to make revisions on this paper. The finalized version was accepted around Nov 1, 2018, about 11 months after the start date of the project. ) Further generalization of this line of work was published in a paper in the IEEE Transactions on Control of Network Systems under the title “Feedback Stabilization of Uncertain Networked Control Systems over Delayed and Fading Channels”. Since data traffic for networked control applications have strict delay requirements, delay-constrained throughput is an important performance measure for such systems. We conducted a performance study of delay-constrained traffic throughput under various topology-transparent transmission scheduling schemes. The results were summarized in a paper entitled “Delay-Constrained Topology-Transparent Distributed Scheduling for MANETs”, which was published in the IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology. To complete the objective of the first task, we analyzed an integrated stabilization policy for a single networked control system. The dynamical system is remotely controlled over a shared communication network that allows multi-path routing, such as a Software Defined Network. We derived stabilization conditions for such a system involving parameters that come from the dynamical system as well as from the routing policy of the communication network. Results obtained were summarized in a paper, entitled “Integrated Stabilization Policy over Multipath Routing Enabled Network”, which was published in the IET Control Theory and Applications. (In our previous progress report, this paper was entitled as “Integrated Stabilization Policy over a software defined network”. The title change was in part prompted by one of the journal reviewers.) For the second task we focused on a networked control system consisting of multiple, dynamically independent control subsystems with shared transmission of control messages over a common wireless channel. We want to understand how the whole system can be stabilized under a joint control and message scheduling policy. We discovered that the stabilization of the whole system can be characterized jointly by the timely capacity region under the scheduling policy and the control stability region of the dynamical systems. Early results of the work were published in the 57th IEEE Conference on Decision Control, under the title, “On Stability Condition of Wireless Networked Control Systems under Joint Design of Control Policy and Network Scheduling Policy.” A more detailed version summarizing our results on this task is being reviewed for journal publication. The project involved the participation of a postdoctoral fellow, Dr. Tan Cheng, as well as PhD graduates of CUHK, Dr. Deng Lei and Dr. Yang Lin. Hence, the project supported the training of young researchers in the area.

14200217.label: Major findings and research outcome
14200217.value: We studied the stabilization of discrete time stochastic systems with input delay and control dependent noise, which is a general model of the project. For such systems, we proposed the necessary and sufficient stabilization conditions. A paper entitled, “Stabilization of Discrete Time Stochastic System with Input Delay and Control Dependent Noise’’ was published in the Systems & Control Letters. We studied the joint effect of plant uncertainty, transmission delay and fading channel on the stabilization of networked control systems (NCSs). For the general uncertain model, we derived the necessary and sufficient stabilization condition in terms of symmetric matrix homogeneous polynomials, which can be verified by LMI feasibility test. As an application, under the parallel transmission strategy (PTS), we further derived an explicit formula for computing the maximum allowable delay bound. Related results were summarized in a paper, “Feedback Stabilization of Uncertain Networked Control Systems over Delayed and Fading Channels”. The paper was published by the IEEE Transactions on Control of Network Systems. In the paper, “Integrated Stabilization Policy over Multipath Routing Enabled Network’’, we focused on the stabilization problem of the integrated sampled-data system over multipath routing enabled network, where each delivered signal in path suffers a random delay. By utilizing an event-driven strategy with a predefined application time, we reformulated the sampled-data model to the stochastic form and further derived a set of stabilization conditions. The paper was published by the IET Control Theory and Applications. In the paper, “Delay-Constrained Topology-Transparent Distributed Scheduling for MANETs”, we compared the performance for various topology-transparent transmission scheduling schemes, including TDMA, ALOHA, Galois Field Sequence and Combination Sequence. The paper was published by the IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology. In our project we introduced recent results on network scheduling policy into the analysis of wireless networked control systems (WNCSs). For such a WNCS consisting of N sub-systems sharing a common unreliable wireless channel, we characterized the stability condition under the joint design of the control policy and the network scheduling policy. The paper entitled, “On Stability Condition of Wireless Networked Control Systems under Joint Design of Control Policy and Network Scheduling Policy’’ was published in the 57th IEEE Conference on Decision Control. A final version has been submitted to the Information Sciences for publication.

14200217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14200217.value: The occurrence of networked control systems sharing a common communication network appears in many engineering applications. The joint control and message scheduling design to stabilize such a system poses a big challenge. Our project started to investigate this type of issues and obtained some preliminary results. Our work could be continued in several interesting directions. For example, in our second task, we only considered multiple, dynamically independent control systems. How could we design for inter-connected dynamically systems? Also, we only considered scheduling policies that do not depend on the dynamical states. For some applications, it may be necessary to involve the information of the dynamical states in the scheduling consideration. All such extension will lead to control systems with non-classical information structures, which is well known to be extremely challenging.

14200217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14200217.value: Networked control systems appear in many applications, such as real-time game and remote control of unmanned ground or aerial vehicles. To ensure the cost effectiveness of such systems, it is desirable to send arising control and observation data over a communication network that is shared by other users, including users who are not related with the controlled systems. In order to support controllability of the whole system, it is not sufficient to just consider how to control each individual dynamical subsystem alone. It is also important to consider how to schedule the control messages destining to the different subsystems. In this project, we try to build up our understanding on issues concerning joint design of controlling and scheduling for such systems.

14200417.label: Realisation of objectives
14200417.value: All three objectives have been met for this project, with some research outcomes extending beyond the original three objectives. Altogether, 8 journal publications and 2 conference publications are associated with this project (publications listed in Part C). This project also led to the training and successful graduation of four Ph.D. students. Furthermore, there has been collaborative research with three external parties (see Part C). With respect to objectives 1 and 2, we have succeeded in formulating and solving the problems associated with N-user rate-diverse broadcast with side information, including subchannel power allocation, source-user multi-rate allocation, and implementable channel code designs (using rateless codes). With respect to objective 3, we successfully implemented the rate-diverse broadcast system on a software-defined radio (USRP) platform, demonstrating the concept and validating the viability of the system. During the implementation process, we began to explore the use of IFDMA as a power-saving alternative to OFDMA. This new development led to two additional journal papers and served as the seed (preliminary results) for the successful application for an ITF grant (see Section 6.2 for more details). The research results associated with the objectives have been published in IEEE journals (more details in Section 6.1 and Section 6.2). Going beyond objectives 1, 2, and 3, we also studied other multiuser detection (MUD) and physical-layer network coding (PNC) systems. Both are highly related to the rate-diverse systems under study in this project. In IEEE conference paper [2] and IEEE journal [7] listed in Part C, we explored multiuser detection systems exploiting sparsity and massive-device scenarios (i.e., N users where N is large). In IEEE journal paper [6], we studied a NOMA MUD system. In IEEE Journal papers [2] and [8] listed in Part C, we studied PNC two-way relay systems. The communication set-up of the current project can be considered as the broadcast phase of an overall relay system. The Ph.D. students trained under this project also started to explore the use of machine learning techniques for wireless networking. These efforts led to IEEE conference paper [1] and IEEE journal paper [3] listed in Part C

14200417.label: Major findings and research outcome
14200417.value: For objectives 1 and 2, we found that the N-user rate-diverse wireless network coding problem can be formulated as a general rate allocation problem subject to constraints on side information and point-to-point channel capacities. Given this solution to the problem, we then realized the solution using rateless codes with encoding/decoding at the BS and the users. As for the power-allocation issue, we formulated an effective “mountain-leveling” as a joint rate and power-allocation method. Two key outcomes are 1) A novel algorithm for power and rate allocation. The algorithm also yields the theoretical achievable optimal sum rate of the system. 2) An approach that can achieve the optimal sum rate in practice. In particular, we give a simple scheme that employs only a single encoding-decoding mechanism for all subchannels in the broadband channel case, obviating the need for separate encoding-decoding mechanisms for different subchannels. As a result, the implementation complexity is much reduced. These results have been published in IEEE journal paper [1] listed in Part C. For objective 3, we successfully implemented the rate-diverse broadcast system on a software-defined radio (USRP) platform, demonstrating the concept and validating the viability of the system. In a real implemented system, we found that there are other aspects of the system that consume much power/energy beyond the power allocation issue addressed in objectives 1 and 2. IFDMA, as an alternative to OFDMA, has a much better PAPR profile that can lead to significant power saving on the transmitter side. Thus, we forayed into the use of IFDMA in our implemented system. In the course of doing so, we found that the conventional IFDMA FFT modules are much more complex than that of OFDMA FFT modules. We thus embarked on a mission to simplify the implementation of IFDMA FFT modules. That led to a discovery that by exploiting a certain correspondence between IFDMA FFT processing and the construct of the Cooley-Tukey FFT algorithm, we can significantly reduce the complexity of the IFDMA FFT modules. This work led to IEEE journal papers [4] and [5] listed in Part C. More importantly, the IFDMA work served as the preliminary results for the successful application for an ITF grant (see Section 6.2 for more details).

14200417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14200417.value: As mentioned in Section 6.1, the study of IFDMA as an offshoot of our implementation effort in objective 3 led to an important discovery that the implementation complexity of IFDMA can be much reduced by exploiting a certain structural property of the Cooley-Tukey FFT algorithm. Leveraging on these results, we applied for an ITF grant with the following targeted deliverables (abbreviated): Deliverable 1: To extend and strengthen the IFDMA innovation in journal paper [4] by adding “time” dimension to the wireless resource, whereby users are allocated different subcarriers in different time slots for transmission of their data. Deliverable 2: To implement the IFDMA innovation in journal paper [5] on software-defined radio (SDR) platforms for experimental investigation and validation. Deliverable 3: To implement our IFDMA innovations, including the background innovations and new innovations arising from Deliverables 1 and 2, on FPGA for realtime performance. The FPGA implementation will also give rise to valuable IP core for our IFDMA technologies. This ITF project, with an overall project cost of HK$3,629,850, has been approved and is currently ongoing.

14200417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14200417.value: This research is a comprehensive theoretical study and experimental validation of wireless rate-diverse broadcast with side information. Simultaneous transmissions of information from an access point (AP) to multiple terminals, referred to as the “broadcast channel problem”, was well studied. Much less so is the scenario under study by this project, where the terminals have side information, Situations like this abound in wireless networks. For example, for a two-terminal case with terminals A and B, terminal A may already have the message targeted for terminal B, and vice versa. The side information could have been acquired in prior transmissions by the AP: that is, terminal A could have overheard the message for B, and terminal B could have overheard the message for A, but neither of them acquired their own desired message. This research has brought forth a new wireless transmission paradigm that can significantly boost the throughput of future generation wireless networks, including 5G cellular networks and advanced Wi-Fi networks. Furthermore, this research led to the discovery of an IFDMA transceiver structure with much lower implementation complexity than the conventional IFDMA transceiver structure, paving the way to a more energy-efficient wireless communications system.

14200617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14200617.value: The last decade has witnessed a tremendous expansion of the research on various control problems of multi-agent systems. These control problems are motivated by such applications as the formation of mobile robots, multiple spacecraft attitude alignment, mobile sensor area coverage, control of electric power grids, and so on. By far, a variety of techniques have been developed, which are capable of handling such problems as consensus, rendezvous, flocking, cooperative output regulation problem for complex continuous-time multi-agent systems characterized by nonlinearity, uncertainty, time-delay, and switching network topology. In contrast, the research on the cooperative control of discrete-time multi-agent systems falls far behind its continuous counterpart. For example, under the jointly connected network topology, both the leaderless and the leader-following consensus problems of continuous-time multi-agent systems was solved for directed networks, while the solvability of the same problems for discrete-time multi-agent systems has been limited to undirected networks. As another example, the distributed observer for a continuous-time leader system can always be made asymptotically stable by sufficiently large observer gain, but this is not the case for a discrete-time leader system. The significant lag between the research status of continuous-time systems and discrete-time multi-agent systems are mainly attributed to two factors. First, the stability of the continuous-time switched systems has been thorough studied and thus are well understood, yet little has been done for the stability of discrete-time switched systems. Second, the high gain feedback control is an effective technique to stabilize a continuous-time linear system. However, this technique does not work for discrete-time systems because the stability region of discrete-time systems is a unit disk. Since, nowadays, almost all control laws are implemented in digital platforms, it is imperative to lay a solid foundation for the control of discrete-time multi-agent systems. Thus, in this project, we will first study the stability property for a class of discrete linear switched systems. The understanding of this problem will lead to the solvability of the two consensus problems for discrete-time multi-agent systems. Second, we will develop a discrete distributed observer for a discrete-time system. This discrete distributed observer will play a key role in synthesizing a distributed control law for solving the cooperative output regulation problem for discrete-time multi-agent systems. Finally, we will apply the cooperative output regulation problem to some practical problems in robotics, flight control, and networked manufacturing via digital control laws. 近十年來，有關多智能體系統的各種控制問題的研究迅猛擴展。這些控制問題由诸如移動機械人的編隊，多個航天器的姿態控制，移動傳感網絡的區域覆蓋，以及電網的控制等大量的实际应用所推动。到目前為止，已發展出各種能够處理由非線性，不確定性，時延和切換網絡拓撲所描述的複雜連續時間多智能體系統的趨同，蜂擁，群聚，協同輸出調節等問題。相比之下，有關離散時間多智能體系統的協同控制的研究遠遠落後於連續時間多智能體系統的相關研究。例如，在網絡拓撲是聯合連通的假定下，針對有向網絡的連續時間多智能體系統的無領導和有領導趨同問題都已經解決。然而對於離散時間多智能體系統，相同問題的可解性仍局限於無向網絡。又例如，連續時間領導者系統的分佈式觀測器總是可以通過選取充分大的觀測器增益來達到漸進穩定，但對離散時間領導者系統卻不是這種情況。連續時間多智能體系統和離散時間多智能體系統的研究現狀之間的顯著滯後主要歸因於兩個因素。其一，連續時間切換系統的穩定性已有深入研究，故已被很好地理解，但有關離散時間切換系統穩定性的研究還很少。其二，高增益反饋控制是鎮定連續時間線性系統的有效技術。然而，由於離散時間系統的穩定域是單位圓，該技術不適用於離散時間系統。考慮到現在幾乎所有的控制律都是在數字化平台上實現的，為離散時間多智能體的控制打下堅實的基礎就顯得尤為重要。因此，在本項目中，我們將首先研究一類離散時間線性切換系統的穩定性問題。對於該問題的理解將有助於離散時間多智能體系統的兩個趨同問題的解決。其次，我們將針對離散時間系統設計離散時間分佈式觀測器。該觀測器將在合成分佈式控制律以解決離散時間多智能體系統的協同輸出調節問題中發揮關鍵作用。最後，我們將通過數字化控制律將協同輸出調節問題應用於機械人，飛行控制和網絡化製造中的一些實際問題中。

14200617.value: The two objectives of the project are as follows: 1. Study the stability property for a class of discrete-time linear switched systems, and apply the theoretical results to solve the leader-following consensus problems for discrete-time multi-agent systems. 2. Establish the discrete distributed observer for discrete leader systems, and then develop a discrete distributed observer approach to the cooperative output regulation problem for discrete-time multi-agent systems. 14200617.label: Major findings and research outcome
14200617.value: The cooperative control of multi-agent systems has been one of the central control problems since the 2000. For the class of continuous-time systems, the research on the cooperative control has advanced from single-integrator systems to complex nonlinear uncertain systems subject to switching network topology. However, for the class of discrete-time systems, the research on the cooperative control falls far behind its continuous counterpart. By the time this project started, the results of the cooperative control of discrete-time multi-agent systems had been mainly limited to undirected or static networks. The first objective of this project is to study the stability property for a class of discrete-time linear switched systems, and apply the theoretical results to solve the leader-following consensus problems for discrete-time multi-agent systems. So far, we have successfully achieved this objective and the main findings are reported in Papers 1 and 2 attached. The first paper exactly achieved the first objective for the class of discrete-time linear multi-agent systems subject to directed static networks. The second paper further extended the results of the first paper to the class of discrete-time linear switched systems, and applied the theoretical results to solve the leader-following consensus problem for discrete-time multi-agent systems over jointly connected switching networks. The second objective is to establish the discrete distributed observer for discrete leader systems, and then develop a discrete distributed observer approach to the cooperative output regulation problem for discrete-time multi-agent systems. This objective has also been fully accomplished. The main findings have been reported in Papers 3 and 4 attached, Paper 3 has established the discrete distributed observer for discrete leader systems, and applied this discrete distributed observer approach to adaptive output tracking of linear discrete-time multi-agent systems, and Paper 4 further enhanced the stability result of Paper 3 and applied the result to solve the cooperative output regulation problem for discrete-time multi-agent systems over jointly connected switching networks. Moreover, we have further extended the scope of the investigation by publishing Paper 5 attached. So far, all results on the leader-following consensus problem of discrete-time multi-agent systems are limited to the case where the system matrix of the leader system does not contain exponentially unstable modes. Paper 5 has made a breakthrough by solving the discrete-time leader-following consensus over switching digraphs with general system modes, thus bridging the gap between the discrete-time multi-agent systems and the continuous -time multi-agent systems

14200617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14200617.value: Two potential expansions of the project are summarized as follows: 1. This project has focused on the class of discrete-time multi-agent systems. The extension of this project to sampled-data multi-agent systems is on-going. 2. In this project, we have established a discrete-time distributed observer for a known leader system. It is more interesting and more practical to establish a discrete-time distributed observer for an unknown leader system. This generalization is under way.

14200617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14200617.value: The cooperative control of multi-agent systems has been one of the central control problems since the 2000, and it includes but is not limited to such problems as consensus/synchronization, formation, cooperative output regulation, rendezvous, and flocking. For the class of continuous-time systems, the research on the cooperative control has advanced from single-integrator systems to complex nonlinear uncertain systems subject to switching network topology. However, for the class of discrete-time systems, the research on the cooperative control falls far behind its continuous counterpart. This project has bridged this gap by achieving the following two objectives: 1. Established the stability property for a class of discrete-time linear switched systems, and apply the theoretical results to solve the leader-following consensus problems for discrete-time multi-agent systems. 2. Developed the discrete distributed observer for discrete leader systems, and then solved the cooperative output regulation problem for discrete-time multi-agent systems by a discrete distributed observer approach. The outcome of this project can be applied to design digital control laws for complex systems such as mobile robots formation, attitude synchronization of spacecraft systems, coordinated control of power grids, distributed allocation of resources, and networked manufacturing.

14200817.label: Project Objectives
14200817.value: Design efficient solutions to evaluate multi-column filter-scan, multi-column sort, multi-column hash, and multi-column aggregation. They are the primitive operators to support WHERE, JOIN, GROUP BY, ORDER BY, and AGGREGATION (e.g., SUM) in SQL. 14200817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14200817.value: Main memory analytic databases are gaining ground rapidly because of the strong demand of real-time analytics and the increasing capability of housing terabytes of main memory in modern servers (e.g., Intel Xeon E7 v3 servers can support 12TB of RAM). Modern main-memory analytical databases are “column-stores”, with data tables physically stored in memory as sections of columns of data rather than as rows of data. Query processing in main-memory column-stores have been based on the “column-at-a-time” approach, i.e., a query is evaluated as a sequence of primitive operations (e.g., hashing, sorting) on individual attributes/columns, one at a time. With the advent of several key techniques such as SIMD-accelerated data processing, column encoding, and code generation, our preliminary work showed that a main-memory column-store can attain substantial performance improvement if it can support “multi-column-at-a-time” processing. Multi-column-at-a-time means a column-store processes multiple columns together instead of one by one. It is a novel query processing paradigm that opens up a much finer level of optimization (e.g., bytes from different columns can be processed together) for main-memory column-stores. In this project, we aim to pioneer the community’s first multi-column-at-a-time enabled main-memory column-store. We will develop novel solutions to enable various cross-column operations. We will also develop the cost model for each multi-column operation and design a new multi-column-aware query optimization algorithm. We plan to build an open-source prototype based on our research results and evaluate the query performance comprehensively. By making our project open-source, this project will yield not only significant scientific merit, but also high practical value. 多列同時表示列存儲一起處理多個列，而不是逐個處理。這是一種新穎的查詢處理範例，可以為主內存列存儲打開更精細的優化級別（例如，可以一起處理來自不同列的字節）。 在這個項目中，我們的目標是開創社區首個支持多列的主內存列存儲。我們將開發新的解決方案，以實現各種跨欄操作。我們還將為每個多列操作開發成本模型，並設計出一種新的多列感知查詢優化算法。我們計劃根據我們的研究成果構建一個開源原型，並綜合評估查詢性能。通過使項目開源，該項目不僅具有重大的科學價值，而且具有很高的實用價值。

14200817.label: Major findings and research outcome
14200817.value: The project has led to 3 journal and 6 conference publications. The project has also directly/partially supported 5 PhDs and 1 MPhil students. Specifically, the core technology developed has led to new hash implementations (Part C: Papers 8.1, 8.2, 9.2), a new memory index (Part C: Paper 8.3), and a new scan method (Part C: Paper 9.1). Furthermore, the applications of our developed techniques have extended beyond core databases on x86 CPU platform, e.g., machine-learning systems (Part C: Papers 9.3, 9.5), mobile devices that use ARM architecture (Part C: Paper 9.6), and streaming data (Part C: Paper 9.4). For example, stream data analytics has more stringent time requirement than traditional analytics, hence, the data processing part is fully memory-resident. In Paper 9.4, we leveraged the multi-column SIMD filter developed in this project to accelerate range queries on stream data.

14200917.label: Project Objectives
14200917.value: The PI plans to study when the optimal policy in a stochastic control problem with a non-standard objective function, such as mean-risk criteria and preference representations with probability weighting, is Markovian. The PI conjectures that the optimal policy is Markovian if the objective function depends only on the distributions of the control and state value at each fixed time and is quasi-convex in the distribution of the control and state processes. The PI plans to consider a mean-risk stochastic control problem in which the risk aversion degree of an agent can evolve in time. The PI attempts to find the dynamics of the agent’s risk aversion degree under which she is time consistent, i.e., under which the agent’s optimal policy set up today is also optimal at any future time. The PI attempts to conduct a survey study to elicit the dynamics of the risk aversion degree of a typical individual and thus to test whether the individual is time consistent. To this end, the PI plans to ask some undergraduates in the PI’s institution, who are well trained to understand the concepts of expected return and risk, to participate in the survey.

14200917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14200917.value: In a classical stochastic control problem, an agent attempts to maximize an objective function that is the expectation of the agent’s total reward in certain time period. To solve this problem, one applies the dynamic programming principle: at every future time, suppose the agent attempts to maximize the expectation of her rewards in the remaining time period. Then, the value functions of the agent at different times satisfy the so-called dynamic programming equation. By solving this equation, one can find the solution to the control problem at the very beginning. A direct consequence of the dynamic programming principle is that the optimal control is Markovian if the state process is a controlled Markovian process. Many stochastic control problems in operations research, however, have a non-standard objective function in that it is not the expectation of certain reward function, such as mean-risk criteria and preference representations that involve probability weighting in the literature on decision analysis. For such an objective function, the dynamic programming principle does not apply, so it is unclear whether the optimal control is Markovian. In the first part of this proposal, the PI attempts to answer this question. Such an answer is useful to understand the optimal policies in many control problems with non-standard objective functions. An agent is time consistent if the optimal control set up today is also optimal at any future time. It has been found recently that if an agent has a mean-variance objective function, which is a weighted average of the mean and variance of the state process at certain terminal time, and the degree of her risk aversion, which is represented by the weight of the variance in the objective function, does not change over time, then she is time inconsistent. It is unclear, however, whether the degree of risk aversion of a typical individual is constant over time and whether this individual is indeed time inconsistent. In the second proposal, the PI plans to consider a general mean-risk problem, in which the risk can be measured by the variance, VaR, or CVaR of the state process at some terminal time, and to find the dynamics of the degree of risk aversion with which the agent is time consistent. Furthermore, the PI plans to elicit the dynamics of the degree of risk aversion of a group of well-trained undergraduates so as to test whether a typical individual is time consistent. 在傳統隨機控制的問題中，一個經濟主體的目標通常設為最大化該主體在給定一段時間內所有可能得到的報酬的期望。要解決這類問題，一個常用的方法是動態規劃原理：在將來每個時刻，我們假設該主體最大化他在剩下時間內所有可能得到的報酬的期望，那麼該主體在不同時間所對應的價值函數滿足一個動態規劃方程。通過解出這個方程，我們從而能夠得到該經濟主體最開始考慮的隨機控制問題的解。動態規劃原理的一個直接推論就是如果描述控制問題的狀態過程是馬氏的，該主體的最優控制也一定是馬氏的。 在運籌學中的很多隨機控制問題中，經濟主體的目標函數不能表示成在給定一段時間內所有可能得到的報酬的期望，譬如均值-風險模型，概率扭曲模型等。在這種情況下，動態規劃原理不再適用，從而我們也無從得知當描述控制問題的狀態過程是馬氏的時候，該主體的最優控制是否也為馬氏的。在這個提案的第一部分，我們嘗試回答這個問題。這個問題的答案能夠幫助我們瞭解很多隨機控制問題的解的性質。 如果一個經濟主體在當前時刻選擇的最優策略在將來任何時候對於他也還是最優的，那麼我們稱該經濟主體是時間一致的，反之就是時間不一致的。先前的研究發現當一個經濟主體的目標函數是一個狀態過程在將來給定一個時間的均值和方差的加權平均，且該權重不隨時間變化時，這個經濟主體是時間不一致的。該權重度量了這個經濟主體的風險厭惡程度。然而，我們並不知道通常一個經濟主體的風險厭惡程度是否隨時間變化，從而並不能確定他是否確實是時間不一致的。在這個提案的第二部分，我們嘗試解決這個問題。具體來說，我們考慮一個一般的均值-風險優化問題，其中風險可以由方差，風險價值，或者條件風險價值來度量。我們希望找到一個使得經濟主體時間一致的風險厭惡程度的動態過程。然後，我們計劃通過實驗來測量人們風險厭惡程度真正的動態變化過程，從而確定人們實際上是否時間不一致。

14200917.label: Realisation of objectives
14200917.value: The first objective of the proposal is to study optimal policies in a stochastic control problem with a non-standard objective function, such as preference representations with probability weighting. The PI has achieved this objective by studying a stochastic control problem in which a gambler has the opportunity of taking bets in a casino repeatedly and decides when to exit the casino. The gambler’s preferences for the wealth at the exist time is represented by cumulative prospect theory, which involves probability weighting. The PI finds that the gambler can improve her preference value by taking randomized strategies because her preferences for the wealth is not quasi-concave in the distribution of the wealth. Then, the PI identifies conditions under which the gambler, asymptotically, adopts a loss-exit strategy, a gain-exit strategy, or a nonexit strategy. For a specific parameter setting when the utility function is piecewise power and the probability weighting functions are concave power, the PI derives the optimal strategy of the gambler in closed form whenever it exists, via solving an infinite-dimensional program. The above results lead to a paper published in the SIAM Journal on Control and Optimization, a leading journal in the area of stochastic control. See Research Output 8-5. The second and third objectives of the proposal are to study mean-risk portfolio selection problems and to identify individual’s dynamic risk aversion in the mean-risk framework. The PI has achieved these two objectives by two works. First, the PI considers a mean-variance problem in which an agent trades multiple stocks and a risk-free asset continuously in time. In contrast to the settings in the literature, the PI formulates the problem by setting a target of the expected terminal wealth that the agent wants to achieve and an objective of minimizing the variance of the terminal wealth. The PI identifies three reasonable dynamic models of the agent’s target for the expected terminal wealth, thus achieving the third objective in the proposal. The PI then shows under what dynamic model of risk aversion the agent is time consistent, and this achieves the second goal of the proposal. Finally, the PI shows that the agent is time inconsistent in general and thus proposes a new framework of addressing the issue of time-inconsistency. Using this general framework, the PI derives so-called intra-personal equilibrium strategies, which is a commonly used approach to addressing the issue of time-inconsistency. In particular, the PI finds that under a reasonable dynamic model of risk aversion, the agent’s strategy is to reduce stock holdings when she approaches the end of the investment horizon. This trading behavior is consistent with life-cycle investment that is commonly observed in retirement accounts. The above results lead to a paper published in Mathematics in Operations Research, a leading journal in the area of operations research. See Research Output 8-1. Second, the PI considers a portfolio selection problem in which an agent maximizes the preference value of her terminal wealth. The agent’s preferences are represented by a model that generalizes the so-called dual theory of choice under risk in the literature. This model is general enough to accommodate mean-risk models where risk is measured by value-at-risk, expected shortfall, and many others. The PI derives the optimal portfolio in closed form, thus achieving the second and third objectives of the proposal. The above results lead to a paper published in Operations Research Letters, a well-recognized journal in the area of operations research. See Research Output 8-3. In addition, when studying mean-risk problems in continuous time so as to address the second and third objectives, the PI encounters a new problem, namely how to define the notion of intra-personal equilibrium strategies properly. In a continuous-time setting, the existing notion of equilibrium strategies for time-inconsistent problems in the literature, referred to as weak equilibrium, is not fully aligned with the standard definition of equilibrium in game theory in that the agent may be willing to deviate from a given weak equilibrium strategy. To address this issue, there is a recent paper proposing the notion of strong equilibrium for an infinite-time stochastic control problem in which an agent can control the generator of a time-homogeneous, continuous-time, finite-state Markov chain at each time. The PI studies weak and strong equilibria in a general diffusion framework, provides necessary conditions for a strategy to be a strong equilibrium, and proves that strong equilibrium strategies do not exist for three investment and consumption problems. The PI also proposes a new notion of equilibrium strategies, referred to as regular equilibrium, shows that it implies weak equilibrium, provides a sufficient condition under which a weak equilibrium strategy becomes a regular equilibrium, and shows that this condition holds for many time-inconsistent problems. The above results lead to a paper published in the SIAM Journal on Control and Optimization, a leading journal in the area of stochastic control. See Research Output 8-2. Finally, in the course of addressing the second and third objectives, the PI identifies several issues that have not been identified in the literature of time inconsistency. The PI addresses these issues and at the same time reviews the recent development of studies on time-inconsistent problems. This leads to a survey paper published in the volume Stochastic Analysis, Filtering, and Stochastic Optimization. See Research Output 8-4.

14200917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14200917.value: First, we may consider dynamic mean-variance portfolio selection models with stochastic investment opportunities, such as stock prices with stochastic volatility. The results in Research Outputs 8-1 and 8-2 can be potentially useful to solve these models. Second, portfolio selection under preferences with probability weighting is in general difficult to solve due to time inconsistency caused by probability weighting. We may consider special preference models, such as quantile maximization, and we may derive intra-personal equilibrium portfolio strategies under these models. The results in Research Outputs 8-2, 8-4, and 8-5 can be potentially useful to achieve the above goal.

14200917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14200917.value: Expected utility theory, the classical model of individuals’ preferences under risk, cannot describe many commonly observed individuals’ behaviors under risk, such as the popularity of insurance contracts and lotteries. Alternative preference models have thus been proposed, and many of them involve probability weighting to capture individuals’ tendency of overweighting extreme outcomes, such as winning lotteries. When applied to dynamic decisions, preference models with probability weighting result in time inconsistency: a plan of actions to be taken in the future that is optimal for an agent today may not be optimal for the same agent in the future. Time inconsistency also arises from mean-risk criteria that strike a balance between growth and risk in a random environment. In this proposal, the PI has studied various decision problems with preference models involving probability weighting and with mean-risk criteria, and has successfully addressed the issue of time inconsistency and derived plans that can be consistently implemented by the agents. These results significantly advance our understanding of time inconsistency, and also have implications for guiding investment and avoiding pitfalls caused by time inconsistency.

To design the mathematical model that can solve multiple constraints in colorblind-sharable video synthesis.
To develop a set of efficient algorithms and tools that facilitates the colorblind-sharable video synthesis.

14201017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14201017.value: There are approximately 250 millions of human population suffer from various degrees of color vision deficiencies (CVD). Colorblind is the most severe case. While one can modify colors of the visual content to allow CVD to distinguish colors, this may completely change the original colors and is not desirable for sharing the recolored content to normal vision audiences. It is unavoidable to face the sharing scenarios, due to the vast amount of CVD. Unfortunately, current research on producing colorblind-sharable content is very limited. In this project, we propose to tackle the synthesis of colorblind-sharable video that can be simultaneously shared by both CVD and normal vision audiences. By utilizing the two visual experiences of common binocular displays (one wearing glasses and one without), we propose to synthesize a binocular video that can simultaneously provide two visual experiences, one for CVD (by wearing glasses) to enhance color distinguishability, and the other for normal visual audiences (without glasses) without aware of any changes in the original visual content. To achieve this goal, we need to satisfy multiple requirements simultaneously. Firstly, the resultant video must be temporal coherent to avoid flickering. Secondly, when viewed without wearing glasses, the average of the left and right frames has to be indistinguishable from the original one. Thirdly, when viewed with glasses, left and right frames are sufficiently different to enable CVD to distinguish colors (color distinguishability), and at the same time, not too different to trigger undesirable binocular rivalry (a visual discomfort that left and right views cannot be perceptually fused stably). Our major challenge in solving this problem is the simultaneous fulfillment of the temporal coherence, color preservation, color distinguishability, and binocular fusibility. We will formulate it as an optimization problem and solve these constraints simultaneously. In order to be applicable for real-life large-scale problem, we will also design a fast colorblind-sharable video synthesis algorithm. By solving the above research challenges, we believe the outcome (the knowledge, publications, and algorithms) from the proposed project should motivate further study along the direction of colorblind-sharable content synthesis, which is currently very scarce. Besides, the proposed colorblind-sharable video synthesis method should be directly applicable to TV industry and content providers, and ultimately benefits CVD people. Via the technology transfer, the proposed method shall provide a technological niche to the TV and entertainment industry in Hong Kong and mainland China. 全球大約有兩億五千萬人口患有不同程度的顏色視覺缺陷。色盲是其中最嚴重的一種。雖然可以通過改變視覺內容的顏色來讓顏色視覺缺陷者區分色彩，但這樣做可能會完全改變原始的顏色，當將變色後的內容共享給視覺正常者時，效果並不理想。而由於大量顏色視覺缺陷者的存在，這種共享視覺內容的場景是不可避免的。不幸的是，當前對色盲可共享內容生成的研究非常有限。 在這個項目中，我們計劃解決色盲可共享視頻生成的問題。生成的視頻可以同時被顏色視覺缺陷者和視覺正常者所分享。通過利用普通雙目顯示器的兩種視覺體驗（佩戴眼鏡與不佩戴眼鏡），我們計劃生成一個可以同時提供兩種視覺體驗的雙目視頻。一種提供給顏色視覺缺陷者（通過佩戴眼鏡），使他們的顏色區分度提高，另一種提供給視覺正常者（無需佩戴眼鏡），讓他們察覺不到我們在原始視覺內容上做的任何改變。為了達到這個目標，我們需要同時滿足幾個需求。第一，最終生成的視頻必須是時間相干的，從而避免閃爍。第二，當不佩戴眼鏡觀看時，左幀和右幀的均值必須令人無法將它同原本的幀區分開來。第三，當佩戴眼鏡觀看時，左幀和右幀必須足夠不同，以使得顏色視覺缺陷者可以區分顏色（顏色區分性），同時它們又不會太過不同而導致不理想的雙目對抗（一種左右眼看到的內容在視覺上不能融合成穩定影像的視覺不適）。我們在解決這個問題上面臨的主要挑戰是同時滿足時間相干性，顏色保持性，顏色區分性和雙目融合性。我們會把該問題公式化為一個最優化問題，並同時解決這些約束。為了適用於真實生活中的大規模問題，我們也會設計一個快速的色盲可共享視頻生成算法。 通過解決以上的研究挑戰，我們相信所提出項目的成果（相關知識，發表的論文和提出的算法）應當會激發當前非常缺乏的，在色盲可共享內容生成這個方向上的進一步研究。除此之外，所提出的色盲可共享視頻生成方法應當可以直接被電視產業和內容提供商所應用，並最終惠及顏色視覺缺陷者。通過技術轉化，所提出的方法將會為香港和中國內地的電視和娛樂產業提供一類針對特定市場範圍的技術產品。

14201017.label: Realisation of objectives
14201017.value: The ultimate goal of this project is to generate visual plausible colorblind-sharable videos that simultaneously maintain multiple constraints, including temporal coherence, color preservation, color distinguishability, and binocular fusibility. To simultaneously satisfy multiple constraints, we approached this problem via two approaches, one is the classical optimization approach, and the other is the deep learning approach. Instead of starting with the most challenging colorblind-sharable video synthesis, we first designed and developed optimization method and deep learning models for a closely related but relatively simpler problem, binocular tone mapping. It is also a problem that employs binocular single vision to reproduce the illusion of high dynamic range image display on standard low-dynamic-range binocular display. Since binocular tone mapping requires less constraints than that of colorblind-sharable video synthesis, it is a good starting point to develop our models and accumulate experience. We started by a still-picture version of binocular tone mapping problem. This simplified problem still requires the simultaneous satisfaction of binocular fusibility, contrast preservation and detail preservation. An initial objective function is designed and developed for synthesizing the pair of output images. It is solved by a classical iterative optimization approach. Satisfactory results are obtained and published in [J01]. This initial objective function enables us to synthesize colorblind-sharable video in the subsequent phase. We then solved the same problem with a deep learning approach, in order to cumulate experience in solving our image-pair synthesis problem. The same objective function can be adopted in the deep learning approach by providing sufficient training pairs. Our initial optimization method can naturally be used for generating the groundtruth samples for the training purpose. Comparable results are obtained with our trained convolutional neural networks (CNN), but the results can be generated in much faster speed. In the mean times, we also attempted multiple color synthesis problems with our CNN to accumulate more experience, and published in journal [J02][J03]. All these strengthen our confidence in approaching harder colorblind-sharable video synthesis problem with CNN. With the success of applying CNN to binocular tone mapping, we applied the CNN for colorblind-sharable image synthesis. This requires a reformulation of the objective function. While keeping the binocular fusability term, we introduced the color preservation term to ensure that normal vision audience unaware of the recoloring, and the binocular color distinguishability term to improve the color distinguishability for colorblind. Note that our output is a pair of images. Simultaneously generating two images with CNN may have a challenge that the two images may not consistent to each other. To solve this problem, we proposed to generate the difference image between the left and right images, instead of directly generating the image pairs. This approach ensures the best consistency. With this new formulation, we are able to synthesize the colorblind-sharable image pair, that allows the colorblind audiences to distinguish the color by wearing the binocular glasses, while the normal vision audiences without wearing the glasses observe no visual difference. We then extended the application from still image to video, by including a temporal coherence constraint. The first attempt to video is based on the optimization approach and we applied a blind filtering to smoothen the frames. This results in a conference paper published in [C01]. Flickering are nicely suppressed to produce significantly improved visual quality. However the computational time is long and the results are highly dependent on the random initialization. The next attempt to this problem is based on CNN. By introducing an additional temporal coherence term into the objective function and adopting a recurrent neural networks, we are able to generate smooth colorblind-shareable video in an end-to-end fashion. The generation time is almost interactive speed using the GPU few years ago. We believe real-time performance is achievable with the current faster GPU. Our result is published in IEEE Transactions on Computational Imaging [J05]. Although the results from the above recurrent neural networks are generally visual plausible, there exists occasional visual artifact of global color inconsistency. That is, the same input color is mapped to two different colors at two different spatial locations. After indepth investigation, we identified the fundamental causes of the problem is due to the local support nature of convolutional neural networks. Due to the limited size of receptor field and the lack of mechanism to constrain the color consistency over a long-range spatial distance, CNN by nature is hard to ensure such global color consistency. This motivates us to reformulate the problem from a different perspective. Instead of using CNN to directly generate the pixel colors, we proposed to utilize CNN to generate the parameters of a polynomial function that computes the final pixel color. In other words, an indirect color generation approach. The same polynomial function is used to generate the whole image instead of individual pixels. A single polynomial coefficient vector is applied to the whole image, this ensures the same input color will always map to the same output color and hence enforces the global color consistency. The major challenge is whether we can design and develop a recurrent neural networks that can generate the coefficients that fulfill the temporal coherence, color preservation, binocular fusability and binocular color distinguishability requirements in our objective function. After multiple intensive experiments, we finally achieved this and obtained high-quality results. We published this advanced approach in ACM Transactions on Graphics [J04].

14201017.label: Major findings and research outcome
14201017.value: Please refer to the field “Title” in research output section for the reference ID like [J01][J02],... 1. We started to tackle the multi-constraint problem with a closely related but relatively simpler problem of binocular tone mapping. An optimization approach is adopted to generate image pair that fed to our eyes separately to produce an illusion of displaying HDR on standard LDR binocular display. The work is published in journal, Computer Graphics Forum [J01]. 2. Next we extended the work from still picture to video by introducing an additional temporal coherence constraint. We attempted the colorblind sharable video synthesis problem with the classical optimization approach. A blind filtering method is applied to smoothen the result frames obtained in per-frame fashion. The result is visually plausible, and we published it in the International Conference on Cyberworlds [C01]. 3. However the computational time of the above approach is long and the result is sensitive to random initialization. To solve the above instability and low-speed performance, we solve the synthesis of colorblind-sharable video in an end-to-end fashion by solving the problem with a recurrent neural networks. Satisfactory results are obtained. We published it in IEEE Transactions on Computational Imaging [J05]. During our study, we also evaluated the capability of CNN in synthesizing colors using various CNN models for different applications, and published our works in ACM Transactions on Grahpics [J02][J03]. 4. While the results for our above CNN model is visually satisfactory and smooth, there exists visual artifact of global color consistency problem. The same input color may be mapped to two or more different colors at two or more spatial locations. The fundamental cause is the limited size of receptive field and the inability of our above model to constrain the color consistency in long-range distance. We then proposed to indirectly generate pixel colors to enforce the global color consistency. Instead of directly generating the pixel colors, we utilized the CNN to generate the coefficients of a polynomial function that generates the pixel color of the whole frame. Since the same coefficient vector is applied to the whole frame, this ensures the global color consistency problem is removed. This approach results in the state-of-the-art result in the field and we published it in top journal, ACM Transactions on Graphic [J04].

14201017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14201017.value: Further development: In this project, we designed and developed multiple methods (optimization-based and deep learning models) for synthesizing the colorblind-sharable video that can enhance the color distinguishability of colorblind audiences while maintaining the visual experience for normal visual audiences. To practically apply our methods to real-world applications, the trained CNN models may have to reduce in size to fit in memory-limited machines. Course of action: To fit in low-end machines, memory consumption has to be reduced. We plan to further design and develop information distillation framework for training more compact CNN models. Recent teacher-student framework is promising in this direction. This will be the primary method for our future development.

14201017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14201017.value: We proposed an AI-based solution to generate colorblind-sharable video that can enhance the color distinguishability of colorblind while sharable to normal visual audiences. By displaying the generated binocular video on standard binocular TV and wearing a stereoscopic glasses, the colorblind audiences can better distinguish color, while simultaneously sharing the same video content with the normal visual audience without wearing the stereoscopic glasses. The direct application of our techniques can be used for content generation of binocular TV broadcast, and real-time conversion of standard video to colorblind-friendly video (by displaying on a binocular display and wearing a stereoscopic glasses).

14201117.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14201117.value: 限價單市場對於低價高流動性股票的最優做市

14201117.label: Project Objectives
14201117.value: We will analyze the optimal quoting policy and the market conditions under which market making is profitable for large-tick stocks when there is no latency. We will take latency into account in market-making, investigate the optimal policy numerically, and identify structures in the optimal quoting strategies (if any). We will estimate our model using historical order book message data and study the value of relative latency for market makers.

We will take latency into account in market-making, investigate the optimal policy numerically, and identify structures in the optimal quoting strategies (if any).
We will estimate our model using historical order book message data and study the value of relative latency for market makers.

14201117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14201117.value: A market maker in a security market provides liquidity to other investors by quoting bids and offers, allowing investors to transact at almost any time during the trading hours. Hence, market makers play a crucial role in facilitating market efficiency and functioning. Traditionally, there are official market makers who have entered into contractual agreements with exchanges and they are under certain affirmative obligations to maintain a continuous two-sided market. With the popularity of order-driven markets in recent decades, market participants can simultaneously submit buy and sell limit orders and adopt market making as a class of high- frequency trading strategies. Several recent studies of quantitative finance have investigated the optimal quoting strategies of such unofficial market makers. However, few of these studies have focused on large-tick liquid stocks, or have considered the discrete nature of prices. Nor have they considered the latency experienced by market makers in trading. This project aims to study optimal market making for large-tick stocks in a limit order market, addressing these two issues. We will develop a new approach to establish structural results on the optimal quoting policy of market makers when there is no latency. Such structural results lead to efficient computation methods. Our approach innovatively combines a key concept known as the expected profit of a limit order in the market microstructure literature with dynamic programming methods. This will allow us to characterize the structures of the market maker’s optimal quoting policy, leading to efficient computation methods. We will also take latency into account and study the new problem of market making in the presence of latency. This will allow us to illustrate the qualitative differences between market making with and without latency. This proposed study will provide important insights into the effects of latency, quoting frequency and other factors in market making for large-tick liquid stocks. It will allow us to better understand the interplay between the reward and the risks a market maker may face, thereby elucidating their quoting and cancellation strategies. Moreover, latency indeed exists in practice (however low it is), so the proposed study will also provide market makers with practical information, enabling them to quote optimally in the presence of latency. This in turn will enable other investors to benefit from the additional liquidity such market makers provide. 摘要： 一個證券市場的做市商通過買賣報價向其他投資者提供流動性，允許投資者在交易時間內的幾乎任何時刻交易。因此，做市商在促進市場效率和運行方面扮演著關鍵角色。傳統上，有與交易所簽訂合同協議的官方做市商，它們在某些肯定的義務下去維持連續的雙邊市場。隨著近幾十年訂單驅動市場的流行，市場參與者可以同時提交買賣限價單，並且採用做市作為一類高頻交易策略。最近幾項關於量化金融的研究調查了這種非官方做市商的最優報價策略。然而，這些研究中很少有關注於低價高流動性的股票，或者考慮了價格的離散性質。他們也沒有考慮到做市商在交易中所經歷的延遲。 該項目旨在研究在限價單市場對於低價股票的最優做市，解決這兩個問題，我們將會制定一種新的方法來建立當沒有延遲時做市商最優報價策略的結構性結果。這種結構性結果導致高效的計算方法。我們的方法創新地結合了一個在市場微觀結構文獻中被稱為限價訂單預期利潤的關鍵概念與動態規劃方法。這將讓我們能夠描述做市商的最優報價策略的結構，從而產生高效的計算方法。我們還將考慮延遲並研究存在延遲下新的做市問題。這將使我們能夠說明在有無延遲下的做市的定性差異。 這項提出的研究將對延遲效應，報價頻率和其它低價高流動性股票的做市因素提供重要的見解。這將使我們能夠更好地理解做市商可能面臨的獎勵和風險之間的相互作用，從而闡明他們的報價和撤單策略。此外，在實際中確實存在延遲（不管延遲多低），所以提出的研究還將為做市商提供實用的信息，使他們能夠在存在延遲的情況下最佳地報價。這反過來也會使其他投資者受益於這些做市商提供的額外流動性。

14201117.label: Realisation of objectives
14201117.value: All the objectives have been achieved. We have analyzed the optimal market making strategy with or without latency. We have also provided explicit criteria for assessing the profitability of market making when there is latency, based on a characterization of the value of an order. Under our model, we show that a market maker can earn a positive expected profit if there are sufficient uninformed market orders hitting the market maker's limit orders compared with the rate of price jumps, and the trading horizon is sufficiently long. We have also used order book data to estimate model parameters and used the experiments to show that the latency can be an additional source of risk and latency impacts negatively the performance of market makers. We have also extended our study to estimate the value of an order using a Markov chain model. By combining with multi-armed bandit learning, we have used the order value to design effective order cancellation strategies which are critical for optimal market making.

14201117.label: Major findings and research outcome
14201117.value: 1. In Gao and Wang (2018) [Article 2 in Part C], we study the optimal market making strategy in the presence of latency. We characterize the value of an order, and provide explicit criteria for assessing the profitability of market making when there is latency. Our theoretical and numerical results suggest that latency can be an additional source of risk and latency impacts negatively the performance of market makers. 2. In Gao and Xu (2022) [Article 3 in Part C], we develop an order scoring model that quantifies the performance of a limit order before execution. We calibrate and validate the model using the historical order book data and backtesting simulations, and show that our model can perform well empirically. We also combine our model with multi-armed bandit learning to guide order cancellation decisions. 3. In Chen et al. (2018) [Article 1 in Part C], we study the multi-stage optimal order execution problems where hidden orders, limit orders and market orders can all be used. We obtain closed-form solutions to the dynamic programming problems, which provide insights on how market conditions impact the choice of order types. 4. Motivated by some of the non-convex optimisation problems that arise in previous research studies, in Gao et al. (2020) [Article 4 in Part C], we analyze two variants of Langevin dynamics for global optimziation. We show theoretically that non-reversible Langevin algorithms are more efficient to locate a local minimum as well as exploring the state space.

14201117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14201117.value: One interesting direction for future research is to study how more sophisticated reinforcement learning and/or deep learning approaches can be used in developing optimal market making and/or optimal execution strategies. We aim to study such problems in the future.

14201117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14201117.value: Designing optimal quoting strategies has been a great challenge for financial practitioners, partly due to the dynamic nature of the optimization problem and the latency involved in the trading processes. This research project studies the optimal market making strategy in the presence of latency, characterizes the value of a limit order, and uses multi-armed bandit learning algorithms to design order cancellation strategies. Our results provide important insights into the effects of latency and the role of order value in optimal market making for stocks in the electronic market. The optimal strategies and related tools developed in this project may also help financial practitioners to quote bids and asks optimally in the presence of latency.
