14201217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14201217.value: Visible light communication (VLC) provides distinct advantages over conventional radio-frequency wireless communications, including free license, enhanced physical security, and immunity to electromagnetic interference. Furthermore, the dual function of VLC, i.e., illumination and data communication, also contributes towards the all-important topic of energy-efficient ‘green communication’. Currently, visible light emitting diodes or lasers have been widely used for both indoor and outdoor illumination. This facilitates potential ubiquitous and seamless high-speed connectivity for users in various environments, including cubicle offices, shopping malls, and future smart homes. Despite the various advantages offered by VLC, there are still challenges for its practical implementation, including limited bandwidth, the high dependence on the line-of-sight link, and the support for multi-user access. In the literatures, single-user VLC systems have been widely investigated. However, the design of multi-user VLC systems, especially the spectrally-efficient multiple access schemes that support simultaneous high-speed and multi-user connectivity, is still limited and thus requires extensive research to unleash its ample potential. In this project, we will investigate VLC-based spectrally-efficient multiple access for future high-speed multi-user communications. Based on the expertise gained through our previous works on advanced signal processing, optical multiplexing networks and VLC systems, we will systematically investigate the multi-user VLC system, namely (1) the spectrally-efficient modulation formats and robust coding, (2) the multi-user interference mitigation, and (3) the corresponding multiple access schemes. The first one focuses on the modulation formats with high spectral efficiency to combat the limited modulation bandwidth of VLC systems and the coding schemes that are robust under different channel scenarios, so as to enhance the reliability of VLC for various applications. The second and third one investigate conceptual designs of multiple access schemes for the multi-user VLC systems, with an emphasis on the multi-user interference cancellation/mitigation. This project aims to identify the optimal solution for VLC systems to provide simultaneous high-speed and multi-user access, which is essential for the enlargement of the customer base and cost reduction before pushing VLC to commercialization. As a mega city with huge energy consumption and high demand for high-speed multiple access, Hong Kong has its inherent immediacy to develop energy-efficient high-speed VLC access systems. Therefore, this proposal is strategically important to Hong Kong and helps promote early-stage transfer of innovation to commercialization to improve its economic competitiveness. This project will also strengthen overseas collaboration with researchers in Taiwan, through which valuable feedbacks from its sound optoelectronic industry can be attained. 與傳統射頻無線通信相比，可見光通信具有保密性高，抗電子干擾等優勢。此外，可見光通信可同時提供照明和通信的雙重功能，因而可用於未來高效節能的“綠色通信”。目前，可見光LED或激光器已被廣泛放用於室內和室外照明，為利用可見光通信在包括辦公室、購物商場、智能家居等在內的不同應用場景下實現用戶的高速無線接入提供了可能。儘管可見光通信具有多種優點，目前將其用於實際通信系統中仍有許多挑戰，例如受限的系統帶寬、對直射通信鏈路的高依賴性以及多用戶接入。現有關於可見光通信的研究大多基於單用戶的情形，而針對多用戶可見光通信系統，尤其是有關高頻譜效率的多用戶接入方案方面的研究仍不多見，因而針對該課題的廣泛探討是對於可見光通信而言是必要的。 本項目旨在研究基於可見光通信的高頻譜效率的多址接入方案，進而實現高速的多用戶可見光通信。基於課題組此前關於先進信號處理，光接入網和可見光通信等課題的研究經驗，在本項目中，本項目將系統地研究多用戶可見光通信系統，涵蓋（1）高頻譜效率的調製格式、魯棒編碼以及（2）多用戶干擾消除技術以及相應的多用戶接入技術。前者主要研究高頻譜效率的調製格式以減輕低系統帶寬的影響，以及魯棒編碼以提升系統在不同信道情況下的可靠性。後者則主要研究有效的多用戶干擾消除或抑制技術，提供可行的可見光多用戶接入的系統方案。本項目旨在研究並驗證適用可見光通信系統的最優多用戶接入方案，該課題的成果可用於增加可見光通信系統的用戶數量以及降低系統成本，對於促進可見光通信技術向商業應用的轉化極為重要。 香港作為大型城市，所需能源消耗極高，對於高速的多用戶接入也有較高的需求，因而亟需研究和發展節能高速的可見光多用戶接入技術。因而本項目不僅符合香港的戰略需求，並且能夠促進創新技術向商用的轉化，進而提升香港的經濟競爭力。此外，本課題通過與海外學者的合作，也將能夠有效獲得和利用光電產業界的反饋。

14201217.label: Realisation of objectives
14201217.value: Objective 1 We have studied the system model to understand the VLC system with multiple users. We simulate the system with an arbitrary number of multiplexed users and comprehensively consider the visible light signal characteristics. We also propose a robust channel processor (RCP) for improving signal detection. • We first investigate the power allocation problem for the downlink of an orthogonal frequency division multiple (OFDM)-based non-orthogonal multiple access visible light communication (NOMA-VLC) system [1]. When formulating the sum-rate maximization problem, an arbitrary number of multiplexed users is considered. Moreover, both user-level and subcarrier-level power optimization are taken into account to improve the system performance. The corresponding theoretical analysis is presented, considering optimal decoding order and each user’s required signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR). Given a fixed power constraint on each OFDM subcarrier, we derive the optimal power ratio for an arbitrary number of multiplexed users in OFDM-NOMA VLC. • We also develop a multi-user VLC model [2] with careful consideration of the fairness between users, the frequency-selective property of the VLC channel, non-negativity of the optical signal, and the power constraint for human eye safety. The problem under the above physical constraints is formulated as a non-convex optimization problem and is solved by the genetic algorithm. • We then propose a robust channel processor (RCP) for improving signal detection [3]. As VLC is an intensity-modulation/direct-detection optical system, the transmitted signal must be real-valued. Compared to the conventional implementation of a real-valued FTN-NOFDM signal that requires analog or digital signal up-conversion, the proposed scheme adopts quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) formats and employs Hermitian symmetry to directly obtain a real-valued FTN-NOFDM signal in the baseband with reduced bandwidth requirement. Objective 2 After studying the system modeling, we developed efficient multi-user interference mitigation techniques that address the second objective. • In [3], though fractional discrete Fourier transform increases the spectral efficiency, it also induces non-orthogonality. Therefore, the information needs to be compensated using the proposed channel estimator. The hybrid iterative detection and fixed sphere decoding (ID-FSD) are proposed to eliminate the inherent inter-carrier interference (ICI). • We demonstrated a high-speed dual-band FTN-OFDM system over VLC [4]. Frequency domain overlapping between sub-bands is used to achieve FTN operation. Duobinary shaping and 2-tap maximum likelihood sequence detection (MLSD) are performed before the DFT operation of each band at the transmitter and after IDFT at the receiver, respectively, to reduce the inter-sub-band interference (ISBI). The optimal spectrum overlapping ratio is studied to balance the trade-off between the performance degradation induced by spectrum overlapping and performance improvement brought by avoiding high-frequency fading. • For the NOMA-OFDM VLC system [1][2], since multiple users are multiplexed on the same subcarrier, successive interference cancellation (SIC) was applied at the receiver side to eliminate the inter-user interference successfully. In [5], the interference induced by the bubble effect was investigated over a 2×2 MIMO underwater VLC system using multiple transmitters and multiple receivers for interference mitigation. Objective 3 We also proposed multiple access schemes such as power allocation algorithms and coding schemes to optimize the system throughput. Real-time experimental demonstrations of multiple users at data rates of gigabit/s were achieved. • We proposed and experimentally demonstrated OQAM-OFDM based MIMO-NOMA for multi-user VLC [6]. The power ratio, which is the key factor that affects the bit error rate (BER) performance of NOMA systems, is experimentally investigated. We showed that an aggregate data rate of 3.2 Gbit/s can be achieved with the optimized power ratio for a two-user 2×2 MIMO-NOMA VLC system. Experimental results show that significantly reduced BER can be achieved by the proposed scheme. • To resolve the issue of high-frequency fading induced error propagation in NOMA-based VLC, we propose and experimentally demonstrate the pairwise coding (PWC) based OFDM-NOMA VLC [7]. By resolving this severe issue with the proposed scheme, both users can achieve better BER performance. The performance improvement of PWC is attributed to the maximized signal space diversity by rotating the constellation, which is achieved by exchanging the real and imaginary components between different sub-channels. For the proposed PWC-based OFDM-NOMA VLC, the low-frequency subcarriers that have better signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions are paired with the high-frequency subcarriers (with worse SNRs). As a result, each pair of subcarriers can achieve similar transmission performance, and the high-frequency fading issue is effectively resolved. • We also propose and demonstrate a real-time software reconfigurable dynamic power-and-subcarrier allocation scheme for OFDM-NOMA in VLC systems [8][9]. With the help of the software-reconfigurable technique, the power ratios of different sub-bands can be dynamically adjusted according to the channel conditions, resulting in superior user fairness and optimal transmission performance. Moreover, the subcarrier number of each user can also be flexibly controlled to fulfill the corresponding capacity demands. • We demonstrated various multi-user VLC systems including a gigabit/s MIMO-OFDM visible light communications using CSI-free/dependent precoding techniques [10], a four-channel 4K video transmission over an underwater-air VLC channel [11], and an adaptive physical-layer network coding (APNC) for VLC-based two-way relay (TWR) networks [12]. 14201217.label: Major findings and research outcome
14201217.value: In this project, we investigated multiple access schemes for multi-user VLC systems. We proposed spectrally-efficient schemes with simulation and experimental demonstrations to improve overall throughputs for the multi-access in VLC systems. • System modeling of the multi-user VLC and simulation of the proposed resource allocation algorithms. We modeled the multi-user OFDM-NOMA system with an arbitrary number of total users and an arbitrary number of multiplexed users per subcarrier. Simulation results show that the proposed resource allocation algorithm exhibits a better overall system throughput as well as user fairness performance than the conventional schemes. The proposed robust channel processor for the mFrDFT-based FTN-NOFDM showed better performance than the previously proposed Joint Channel Equalization and Detection (JCED). • Experimental validation of the advanced coding and resource allocation schemes for user interference mitigation and performance optimization of multi-user VLC systems in the target applications. To improve the spectral efficiency of the limited bandwidth of typical VLC systems, we propose two non-orthogonal multi-user VLC schemes using FTN-DFT-S-OFDM and FTN-NOFDM. For the first scheme, we optimized the dual-band spectrum overlapping ratio and used duo-binary coding to reduce the interference. For the second scheme, we showed that with the proposed channel processor and the consequently accurate decision from ID-FSD, the capacity of the total system could be further improved. We also have proposed and demonstrated effective algorithms for multicarrier NOMA VLC systems. The results showed that the proposed algorithm is better than the traditional FPA and GRPA algorithms, especially for a smaller total number of subcarriers. In the 3-user scenario, the overall throughput and fairness of the proposed algorithm, compared with that of the conventional algorithm, can be improved. We also demonstrated a real-time OFDM-NOMA VLC system with software reconfigurable dynamic power-and-subcarrier allocation. A 1.84-Gbit/s real-time transmission with stable operation over several hours was achieved, wherein the BER is below the hard-decision forward error correction threshold. The proposed scheme is markedly adaptive to dynamic capacity demands while maintaining better user fairness and system flexibility and stability. We also successfully demonstrated a time-multiplexed four channels of 4K video transmission in real-time using the proposed scheme over a 3.6-m underwater and 8-m free-space channel. The above research findings were published on eight top conference papers and nine journal papers, including the Journal of Lightwave Technology, Photonics Technology Letters, and Optics Express. The experimental results provide high-quality scientific research and promote the transfer to practical applications.

14201217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14201217.value: For the interference mitigation system, the investigation of the real-time transmission performance can be conducted in the future. For computational complexity, the iteration operation in the interference mitigation algorithms could be further improved. For multi-user throughput improvement, the effect of bandwidth limitation, non-negative optical signal, peak power for the eye safety, and the additional QoS requirements on the complexity of the optimization algorithms can be analyzed. Moreover, we will investigate the issues of the impacts of various system setups, including location and shadowing effects. Joint optimization will be investigated based on the feedback of the experimental verification to derive the optimal solution for VLC-based high-speed multiple access. Moreover, the developed schemes can also be applied to different scenarios. Recently, underwater optical wireless communications have potential applications for underwater for the unique advantages over radio-frequency signals and acoustic communications and draw more and more attention. The critical environmental effects such as turbulence and bubble need to be considered. The study of user interference mitigation, resource allocation, and system performance optimization with environmental effects still requires further extensive research.

14201217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14201217.value: By modulating data on the widely deployed lighting infrastructures, it is possible to realize ubiquitous and seamless network connectivity. Visible light communications (VLC) that exhibit dual functionality have attracted considerable research interests in recent years. VLC inherently supports multiple access for multi-user scenarios as a wireless communication method. Compared to point-to-point systems, the challenge issues for multi-user VLC systems include mitigation of the multi-user interference and effective multiple access schemes that can optimize the system performance. In this project, we developed the multi-user VLC system model and proposed some novel multiple access schemes with high spectral efficiency for practical VLC systems by addressing the aforementioned two challenges. We have investigated the coding schemes to mitigate the multi-user interference in both frequency and spatial domains. We also conduct both numerical and experimental investigations to optimize the performance of developed schemes. We then demonstrated the first real-time software reconfigurable dynamic power-and-subcarrier allocation scheme for an OFDM-NOMA VLC system. Experimental results show that the proposed schemes can boost the throughput of the multi-user VLC system and meanwhile maintain the users’ fairness.

14201317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14201317.value: Aim of Project The aim of this project is to engineer and validate a miniaturized 3D cell culture platform for spheroid production and subsequently investigate the cellular and molecular characteristics of the generated spheroids. Project Background Tumors are three-dimensional (3D) tissues. However, limited by existing techniques, the mainstream of cancer research relies largely on two-dimensional (2D) culture models, which overlook many of the important complexities of tumors and the physiological factors characteristic to the in vivo tumors. Efforts to remove these obstacles have led to the development of 3D culture models, including the so-called spheroids that are close to living tissues. However, currently no system simultaneously satisfies all the clinical and scientific requests, including facile formation and cultivation, as well as systematic and standardized characterization of these in vitro generated spheroids. Brief Project Description To address this grand challenge, this proposal intends to establish a standalone platform incorporating the salient features of: (1) effective production and maintenance of uniform-sized tissue-like spheroids in double emulsions produced by microfluidics without the requirement of biomaterial scaffolds, and (2) generalized physical, chemical and biological characterizations on a built-in analytical station. Made possible by the planned technological advancement, this proposal subsequently aims to uncover the cellular and molecular characteristics of these in vitro-generated 3D spheroids, as well as the correlations to their drug responses. Significance of Project The developed in vivo-mimicking model is expected to bridge the gap between cell-based assays and animal studies, and to ultimately generate health benefits in personalized cancer treatment by offering a pre-animal tool to predict the chemoresponses of individual patients. The success of this proposal represents an important opportunity for us to stride ahead in the competitive landscape of cancer research. 腫瘤具有較為複雜的三維結構，然而，目前針對癌症的研究多是基於二維培養體系，因而忽略了許多體內腫瘤的複雜度及生理特性。近年來，三維細胞培養模型，如球型細胞聚團 (Spheroids) 等策略已被證實能更為真實的模擬腫瘤於體內的形貌及功能性。然而，現有生成球型細胞聚團的技術難以同時滿足當前科研及臨床上的需求，亦無法系統化地表徵體外培養的球型細胞聚團。 針對標準化培養球型細胞聚團，本研究旨在搭建一套創新的技術平台，具體研究內容包括：(1) 利用微流控的技術產生水包油包水之雙重微乳液 (Water-in-oil-in-water Double Emulsion)，有效地生成及培養大小一致的球型細胞聚團, 以及(2) 內建分析平台以同步研究球型細胞聚團的物理、化學及生物特性。此一技術上的推進預期能實現於體外培養均質的三維球型細胞聚團，並初步研究其細胞及分子分物上的表徵，為藥物篩選及所謂的個人化癌症治療(Personalized Cancer Treatment)提供準備。

14201317.label: Realisation of objectives
14201317.value: This project has developed a microfluidic-based double emulsion (DE) platform for both controlled production and sustained cultivation of spheroids, as well as for the on-chip characterization of the spheroids. During the project period, we have realized the proposed objectives as elaborated in the following: (A) Design and Fabrication of the Microfluidic Device A-1: Development of the droplet microfluidic platform for the production of double emulsions We have established the backbone technology of the microfluidic droplet generator, including the design, fabrication and surface functionalization of the device. Briefly, the microfluidic chips were designed based on the flow-focusing geometry. The water-in-oil (W/O) single emulsions were generated at the first cross-junction, while the single W/O emulsions were dispersed into the water phase at the second cross-junction, forming the water-in-oil-in-water DEs with a thin oil layer. The microfluidic device was fabricated by conventional soft lithography techniques based on polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS). More importantly, we have employed a novel strategy, taking advantages of the ‘airway resistance’, to selectively change the wettability of PDMS in a facile and robust manner. Our results have also demonstrated a well control over the size of generated DEs, thickness of the oil layer, and generation frequency. We have also optimized the oil layer thickness to enable small molecule and gas transport for sustained cell culture in the DEs. A-2: Demonstrate tumor spheroids cultivation in the double emulsions We have demonstrated the applicability of this approach for spheroid cultivation using two human colorectal carcinoma epithelial cell lines, Caco-2 and HT-29. The formation of spheroids with both cell types were initiated without additional supplement in the double emulsions. As a pioneering effort, the molecular characteristics of the DE generated spheroids were examined by the activities of human topoisomerase I (hTopI), the sole target of a clinically approved anticancer drug camptothecin. At the molecular level, enhanced hTopI activities were observed in the 3D culture models (both the proposed DEs and commercially available ultra-low attachment plate (ULAP)), when compared to the 2D culture, suggesting an altered differentiation level for the cells cultured in 3D. However, further analysis suggested that only the results obtained when analysing spheroids cultivated in DEs presented statistical significant difference to the results obtained when analysing cells grown in the 2D culture. This is mainly due to the group of DEs presented smaller errors compared to the ones obtained for ULAP groups. Collectively, these evidences suggest a change in the differentiation patterns when cells are clustered into spheroids. The small variations observed in DEs further support that DEs provide a homogeneous condition to cultivate 3D multicellular spheroids and the subsequent studies. A-3: Extend the double emulsion platform for organoids cultivation We have extended the developed platform to cultivate organoid-like structures in DEs and observed the accelerated formation of organoid-like structures compared with matrix-assisted assembly. As a model cell line, Calu-3 (Homo sapiens lung adenocarcinoma) were cultivated in a commercially available Matrigel and DEs. Lung tissue-like lumen structures were observed, indicating that an “organoid”-like structures were recreated in both culture formats, however, the Matrigel-produced organoids were relatively heterogeneous in size compared to the DEs. It is also important to note that the organoid-like structures in DEs were formed within 2 days of cultivation, as opposed to close to 5 days of cultivation in Matrigel. Additionally, as an indicator differentiating spheroids against cell aggregates, the circularity was observed increased in the DEs, suggesting the cells were self-organized into “spheroids” without additional supplement of biomatrices. These results have validated that the DEs provide enhanced size control to not only spheroid but also production of the organoid-like structures by having each emulsion as an individual cell incubator for spontaneous cell assembly. Furthermore, the organoid-like structures may be produced within a relatively shorten amount of time. Made possible by the uniformity of organoids offered by the DE platform, further investigations of these in vitro produced organoids in relation to their in vivo counterparts may become reliable and consistent. (B) Development of a Multifunctional On-Chip Spheroids Analytical Station B-1: Design and Fabrication of a Spheroid Trap It is noted that the analysis of spheroids is currently fragmented, mainly due to the lack of available tools and protocols. One important task of this project is set to develop an on-chip multifunctional analytical station capable of systematically investigating the spheroids at the “single-spheroid” level. We have developed a series of “emulsion trap” to allow the emulsions being trapped. The emulsion trap is able to localize individual spheroids for an in situ characterization, as well as to allow the modulation of microenvironments. This scanning array has the resolution down to “single-spheroids”, and allows analysis of the biological and physical characteristics of spheroids, before or after the treatment of anti-cancer drugs. B-2: Develop and Establish an Optical Detection Module for On-Chip Analysis We have developed a customized optical detection module to enable both of morphological investigation and fluorescent readout from each droplets. Briefly, the excitation (white light and 488-nm laser) was focused through an objective lens to excite the observation volume within the microfluidic device. The emission was then collected through the same objective, passed through a pinhole, and separated by appropriate dichroic mirrors and bandpass filters before being detected by independent photomultiplier tube photon multiplier photodiodes for each channel. Customized LabVIEW programs were used to communicate with a digital counter for data acquisition and analysis. (C) Characterization of the Generated Spheroids As an effort to prolong the investigation and to expand the capacity of in situ analysis of double emulsion-produced tumour spheroids, this project has developed a streamlined platform by combining the DE-based spheroid initiation and microwell culture, henceforth termed DE-Pretreated Microwell Culture (DEPMiC). After breaking the oil layers of DEs in the geometrically well-fitted microwells (the emulsion traps), the released spheroids have been observed proliferating and gradually exhibiting a circular morphology as spheroids cultured in existing 3D culture approaches. We have also custom-built a detection system to evaluate the drug responses from individual spheroids in an in situ manner, where the IC50 has been observed comparable with the drug sensitivity measured from tumour spheroids produced with patient-derived cancer-associated fibroblasts. It is of note that the DEMPiC produced spheroids do not express proteins of ZO-1 and β1-integrin distinctly around the cyst structures as shown in the counterparts produced by Matrigel, one of the most widely used 3D culture strategy. However, investigations by Raman spectroscopy have demonstrated that DEPMiC-produced spheroids present ordered lipid structures in apical membrane as opposed to the basal membrane, displaying similarities with those obtained from the Matrigel cultivation. While the finding is intriguing, further studies are necessary to rationalize why the elevated lipid ordering structure is established on the apical membrane for the DEPMiC-produced spheroids. Combining with a custom-built detection system, we have also demonstrated the possibility to follow the drug responses from individual spheroids in an in situ manner. Taken together, the streamlined DEPMiC platform developed in this GRF project has incorporated the features of: (1) effective initiation of uniform-sized multicellular spheroids by the pretreatment of DEs produced by microfluidics without the requirement of biomaterial scaffolds, (2) sustained maintenance and culture of the produced spheroids with facile removal of the oil confinement, (3) in situ characterizations of individual spheroids localized in microwells by a built-in analytical station.

14201317.label: Major findings and research outcome
14201317.value: This project has developed an integrated platform, based on microfluidics generated double emulsions, for spheroids formation, cultivation and in situ characterization. The microfluidics generated double emulsions have shown promising as a pretreatment to encourage spheroid initiation while culturing the produced spheroids in emulsion traps has made the localization of spheroids possible for subsequent in situ analysis. Without artificial scaffold, Calu-3 cells cultivated by the developed platform have exhibited organoid-like structures after one day of pretreatment in DEs and the circular morphology has resembled the phenomena observed in the Matrigel counterparts. Characterized by the microscopic observations and Raman spectroscopy, the cultivated spheroids in the developed platform have gathered elevated lipid ordering on the apical membrane, which is similar with those observed in the Matrigel counterparts. We have published the developed platform and findings in an article published in Microsystems & Nanoengineering (Impact Factor: 7.127, top 15% in the field of Instruments & Instrumentation, Research Output, Peer-Reviewed Publications #2), and in two conference papers (2018, Sino-Russian ASRTU Symposium on Advanced Materials and Processing Technology, Research Output, Recognized international conference #2 (presented); 2020, The 2nd International Workshop on Microfluidics for Hematology, Research Output, Recognized international conference #3 (accepted but the conference is postponed). As part of our collaborative effort with Prof. Wan Chao at the School of Biomedical Sciences in CUHK, we have developed a set of hydrogel based 3D culture approaches to recapitulate the configurations of tissues including bone and muscles. Combining tumor multicellular spheroids produced from this project and recapitulated tissues, the integrated platform is expected to be extended for the study of metastasis in the near future. The results and potential applications were presented in a conference paper (2018, The 22th International Conference on Miniaturized Systems for Chemistry and Life Sciences (MicroTAS), Research Output, Recognized international conference #1). As part of our effort on the detection platform, we worked with Prof. Thierry Blu at the Department of Electronic Engineering in CUHK, and developed an effective algorithm to estimate the point-spread function (PSF) in 3D wide-field fluorescence microscopy which is expected to significantly improve the deconvolution performance and assist the microscope calibration process. The principle of the developed PSF estimation approach is sufficiently flexible to be generalized non-spherical aberrations and other microscope modalities. The results was published in a journal article published in Optics Express (Impact Factor: 3.894, top 20% in the field of Optics, Research Output, Peer-Reviewed Publications #1).

14201317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14201317.value: Looking into further validations, integration and automation of the modules of DE generation, localization, and observations are expected to promote the application in a clinical setting. Lung cancer, together with other cancers, have been lingering public burdens for human health due to the notorious heterogeneity of tumours against therapeutic treatments. The presented DEPMiC platform is expected to serve as a scalable factory for the production of tumour spheroids, and yet a programmable bioreactor for long-term cultivation, microenvironmental regulation and drug efficacy testing. More importantly, the capability of DEPMiC to analyse individual spheroids may help advance our understanding of tumour heterogeneity and ultimately devising of personalized treatments. We will continue to work with our collaborators, Prof. Renee Wan Yi Chan at the Department of Paediatrics (CUHK) and Prof. Wan Chao at the School of Biomedical Sciences (CUHK), to promote our platform for clinical applications. From the education’s perspective, the PI has co-edited a textbook with Prof. Han-Sheng Chuang in the National Cheng Kung University, Taiwan. In line with the broader scope of this project, the textbook covers the state-of-art biosensing technology available for future personalized medical diagnostics (Advances in Biosensing Technology for Medical Diagnosis, Bentham Science Publishers, 2020 (ISBN-10: 9811464782)).

14201717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14201717.value: Reconfigurable and transformable assembly structures consist of component parts that can be re-used and re-assembled into different configurations for use in different scenarios. While this is a cost-effective and practical idea, designing these structures is nontrivial, since we need to consider not only the overall designs and component parts but also the geometric connections among the parts in every single configuration. This is a very challenging problem that the state-of-the-art methods cannot handle. In this research, we aim to innovate novel computational solutions to support the design and fabrication of reconfigurable and transformable assemblies. Altogether, we consider four tasks: i) co-analysis of input configuration designs to optimize the re-usability of parts and discover parts correspondence, parts reusability, and joint compatibility across configurations; ii) co-construction of joint networks over multiple configurations while respecting the constraints of parts correspondence and joint connections, as well as achieving multi-key mechanical interlocking; iii) modeling component parts transformation with hinges and optimizing the assembly structures with transformable parts; and iv) enhancing our results in various practical aspects: stability analysis, extensible assembly structures, and co-fabrication with multiple material. In summary, this project is built upon the knowledge learnt from the previous works of the PI on computing mechanical interlocking structures, as well as geometric modeling and analysis, most were published in top-tier flagship journals and conferences in graphics research. Through this project, the PI will continue to innovate and develop new research methods, and strive to produce high-quality results that can attain to top-tier research conferences and journals with his team and collaborators. 可重構和可變形的組裝結構是由可以重新使用和重新組裝成不同配置的組件所組成。雖然這是一個具有成本效益和實用性的想法，但是設計這些三維結構是極具有挑戰性的，因為我們不僅需要考慮整個配置的設計和結構，還要考慮每個配置中部件之間的幾何連接。這具挑戰性的問題，即使是現在最新的方法也無法解決。在這項研究中，我們將致力於研究創新的計算方案，以支持可重構和可變形組件的設計和製造。總括來說，我們將考慮四個任務：一）共同分析多個輸入配置的結構，辨認組件的對應，及優化組件的可重用性和配置之間的聯合兼容性; 二）在兼顧組件對應關節和關節連接的同時，共同構建多個配置的聯合網絡，以在多個配置上分別實現機械聯鎖; 三）研究如何使用鉸鏈建模組件，使配置的組裝結構達到可變形的目的; 和 四）在各種實踐方面增強我們的成果：穩定性分析，可擴展的組裝結構和與多種材料的共同製造。總而言之，這項目建立在已往的計算機械聯鎖結構的幾何建模與分析方面的知識基礎上，大部分是發表在頂級旗艦期刊和頂級圖形研究會議上。通過這項目，我們將不斷創新和開發新的研究方法，努力製作可達到一流研究會議和期刊的高質量研究成果。

14201717.label: Realisation of objectives
14201717.value: This project aims for developing computational methods to aid 3D designs and 3D fabrications related to reconfigurable 3D assemblies. In short, we have developed various computational methods on 3D fabrications and also learning-based methods that are related to 2D and 3D geometry analysis and processing. First, to construct 3D fabrication requires us not only to compute the 3D geometries of individual parts and their connections but also to respect 3D fabrication constraints related to the machine for creating the fabricated objects. Further, to construct reconfigurable structures, we need to create a common set of parts, such that the same set can be assembled into different forms for use in different situations. Designing these assemblies is a complex problem, since it requires a compatible decomposition of shapes with correspondence across forms, and a planning of well-matched joints to connect parts in each reconfigurable form. In [J01/C01], we design novel computational methods with three technical contributions. First, we formulate the compatible decomposition of reconfigurable structures as a weakly-constrained dissection problem and derive a solution based on the dynamic bipartite graph to construct common parts across multiple forms; particularly, we optimize the reuse of parts and preserve the geometric semantics over different reconfigurable forms. Second, we develop a joint connection graph to model the solution space of reconfigurable structures with part and joint compatibility across different reconfigurable forms. Third, we formulate the backward interlocking and multi-key interlocking models by iteratively planning the joints consistently over multiple reconfigurable forms. In this work, we also show the applicability of our approach by constructing reconfigurable furniture of various complexities, extend it with recursive connections to generate extensible and hierarchical structures, and create several results using 3D printing, 2D laser cutting, and woodworking. Further, in [J02/C02], we explore another form of wire-based 3D fabrication with the wire bending machine. Here, we design a population-based hybrid metaheuristic model, and design the join, bridge and split operators, such that we can refine the solution wire sets in the population; based on this model, we develop a fully automatic method that finds a small number of machine fabricable wires with minimal overlap to reproduce a wire sculpture design, demonstrate the efficiency of our method on a rich variety of models, and physically fabricate several of them. In [J03/C03], we explore the dissection puzzles, which is also a kind of reconfigurable assemblies; here, a dissection puzzle consists of a common set of puzzle pieces that can be assembled into multiple distinct forms. In this work, we design a new computational method to design steady 3D dissection puzzles; our method takes two voxelized shapes as inputs and dissects them into a common set of puzzle pieces, during which we allow slight modification of the inputs, preferably inside the shapes to preserve the external appearance. Particularly, we formulate a formal model of generalized interlocking for connecting pieces into a steady assembly using both their geometric arrangements and friction. Next, we start to explore deep learning approaches for geometry analysis and processing. In [J04/C04], we introduce the first neural optimization framework to solve a classical instance of the tiling problem. Our key idea is to is reformulate tiling as a graph problem by modeling candidate tile locations in the target shape as graph nodes and connectivity between tile locations as edges, such that object assembly becomes a graph node selection problem. Here, we design a graph convolutional neural network to progressively propagate and aggregate features over graph edges and predict tile placements for producing the assembly structure, and conducted various experiments on a variety of shapes to showcase the speed and versatility of our method. In [J05], we present a novel approach to learn and detect distinctive regions on 3D shapes by analyzing point sets sampled from 3D shapes and then formulating and training a deep neural network for an unsupervised shape clustering task to learn local and global features for distinguishing shapes with respect to a given shape set. In [J06], we present a deep normal filtering network to denoise 3D meshes by first capturing local geometry through local patches extracted from the mesh and then processing patches of facet normals to predict denoised facet normals on each patch for 3D reconstruction with feature preservation. In [J07], we present a new approach to recognizing vanishing points by developing a novel convolutional neural network architecture that generates geometric segmentation of varying orientations. In [C05,C07,C08,C09], we explore deep-learning-based methods for 3D geometry analysis and processing for upsampling 3D point clouds, for 3D instance segmentation, and for 3D data augmentation. Lastly, in [C06], we explore geometric structure analysis of floor plan layouts to recognizing the visual elements in the inputs, whereas in [C10], we learn to recognize 3D occlusion between objects and hand by designing and developing a novel neural network approach that directly predicts the occlusion.

14201717.label: Major findings and research outcome
14201717.value: In summary, this project produces 7 journal papers and 10 conference papers, including four papers in ACM Transactions on Graphics (TOG) and one in Eurographics (Computer Graphics Forum (CGF)), as well as several papers in CVPR and ICCV. Note that top-tier conferences such as SIGGRAPH/SIGGRAPH Asia and Eurographics publish the accepted papers in ACM TOG and CGF, respectively. First, we summarize major findings on 3D fabrication: - [J01]/[C01] presents novel computational methods for the design and construction of 3D reconfigurable assemblies: a dynamic bipartite graph to construct parts across multiple forms, a joint connection graph to model the solution space of reconfigurable assemblies, and the backward interlocking and multi-key interlocking models that iteratively plan the joints consistently over multiple forms. - [J02]/[C02] presents a fully automatic method with a population-based hybrid metaheuristic model and our designed join, bridge and split operators to automatically find few machine fabricable wires with minimal overlap to reproduce a wire sculpture design as a 3D shape abstraction. - [J03]/[C03] presents methods to create 3D dissection puzzles, such that a common set of 3D puzzle pieces constructed by our method can be assembled into distinct forms of different input 3D shapes. - [J04]/[C04] presents the first neural optimization framework to solve a classical instance of the tiling problem. Second, we summarize major findings on geometry analysis and computation: - [J05] presents a novel approach to learn and detect distinctive regions on 3D shapes by conducting the analysis on point sets sampled from 3D shapes and formulating a deep neural network for an unsupervised shape clustering task to learn local and global features. - [J06] presents a deep normal filtering network for denoising 3D meshes by capture local geometry in the form of patches and formulating an end-to-end network that directly predicts facet normals with a novel multi-scale feature embedding unit, a residual learning strategy to remove noise, and a deeply-supervised joint loss function. - [J07] presents a new approach to recognizing vanishing points by developing a novel convolutional neural network architecture that generates geometric segmentation of varying orientations. - [C05] proposes a GAN-based model with an up-down-up expansion unit in the generator with error feedback and self-correction, a self-attention unit to enhance the feature integration, and a compound loss with adversarial, uniform and reconstruction terms, for upsampling point features with better distribution uniformity. - [C06] explores geometric structure analysis of floor plan layouts to recognizing visual elements in the inputs. - [C07] presents PointAugment, a new auto-augmentation framework, that automatically optimizes and augments point cloud samples to enrich the data diversity when we train a downstream classification network. - [C08] presents a new end-to-end bottom-up architecture with a two-branch network to extract point features and predict semantic labels and offsets, specifically focused on better grouping the points by exploring the void space between 3D objects. - [C09] propose a novel disentanglement approach for the 3D point cloud upsampling task by formulating two cascaded sub-networks, i.e., a dense generator to infer a coarse but dense output that roughly describes the underlying surface and a spatial refiner further to fine-tune the coarse output by adjusting the location of each point. - [C10] presents a method that learns to recognize 3D occlusion between objects and hand by designing and developing a novel neural network approach that directly predicts the occlusion pattern.

14201717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14201717.value: This project produces a collection of computational methods for designing and constructing 3D reconfigurable assemblies. We formulate techniques such as the dynamic bipartite graph model for arranging common component parts across multiple reconfigurable forms, the joint connection graph to model the solution space of reconfigurable assemblies, and the backward interlocking and multi-key interlocking models for iteratively planning joints consistently over multiple reconfigurable forms. Besides, we demonstrated our reconfigurable results for designing some furniture models and 3D dissection puzzles, performed various evaluation experiments, and explored various forms of 3D fabrication, including laser cutting, wire bending, and wood cutting. Further, we also started to explore artificial intelligence for 3D geometry and develop some deep-learning-based methods for 3D point cloud analysis and processing. Besides, we also derived the first neural optimization approach that enables us to learn to solve a classical instance of the tiling problems by formulating tiling as a graph selection problem, such that our trained neural network can learn to produce a tiling by selecting nodes in a graph. In the end, we produced 10+ high-quality publications in leading international journals and conferences, with four in ACM Transactions on Graphics, a journal with highest impact factor in computer graphics research.

14201817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14201817.value: 目標 開發可用于檢測早期肝纖維化的可靠磁共振技術。 背景 慢性肝病是一個全球性的重大健康問題。肝纖維化是慢性肝病在早期階段的一個關鍵特徵。如果能早期發現肝纖維化，我們可以逆轉肝病以避免晚期並發症。目前，肝纖維化診斷的黃金標準是肝活檢。但是肝活檢是侵入性的並且有發病和死亡的風險。如今無創診斷工具越來越多地用於臨床實踐。但是，現有的非侵入性方法仍然有很大的局限性。目前有很大的臨床需要以改善非侵入性診斷技術以用於評估和監測肝纖維化。 一些動物和人體研究報告T1rho有潛力用於評估肝纖維化。T1rho在臨床實踐中具有優勢，因爲它不需要造影劑和額外的硬件。然而，當前的磁共振技術難以獲得穩定的T1rho肝臟測量。肝臟中豐富的血管，呼吸運動和由於比吸收率（SAR）提高所帶來的掃描時間增長都使得T1rho測量容易出錯。 項目介紹 在此提案中，我們的目標是克服上述挑戰，開發磁共振脈衝序列以達到快速和穩定、並具有優化黑血效果的T1rho定量肝臟成像。 通過減少脈衝序列的SAR，我們計劃在一個六秒的屏息内采集單層的肝臟T1rho定量圖像。我們會使用多個屏氣獲得多個層面的T1rho定量圖像。現有的肝纖維化評估成像的一個主要限制是炎症可以混淆測量結果。我們會開發脈衝序列以在一個10秒的屏氣内同時獲得T1rho和T2圖像。我們期望復合指標（1/T1rho -1/T2）能用來區分肝纖維化與炎症。我們會在被肝活檢確定有肝纖維化的病人群體中評估我們的磁共振脈衝序列。 項目意義 該項目將會提供檢測早期肝纖維化的診斷工具。這將會改善慢性肝病患者的臨床療效，並為進一步開發可用於其他目的的磁共振技術提供基礎。

14201817.value: We have completed the objectives in 100%. We have completed theoretical analysis based on MRI physics, MRI engineering, and pathology of liver fibrosis. We have implemented the prototype of our MRI pulse sequence in standard MRI scanners. Our MRI pulse sequence can achieve suppression of blood signal when measuring T1rho value. 14201817.label: Major findings and research outcome
14201817.value: 1. Liver fibrosis is characterized by collagen deposition in the liver. T1rho MRI is sensitive to the water content change associated with liver inflammation, but its sensitivity to the collagen change is low. 2. The composite metric R1rho – R2 is sensitive to chemical exchange effect. However, liver fibrosis causes minor change in chemical exchange effect. 3. Liver fibrosis cause significant changes in magnetization transfer effect due to collagen deposition. We developed a new technique based on off-resonance T1rho which is specific to detect such change based on magnetization transfer effect. We observed it has good diagnostic value for detecting liver fibrosis. 4. Suppression of blood signal in the liver is important. Our technique can significantly reduce the confounding effect from blood signal in quantitative MRI of the liver.

14201817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14201817.value: Chronic liver disease (CLD) is a major health problem worldwide. It is increasing in prevalence due to the growing epidemic of obesity, both alcoholic and non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, and chronic viral hepatitis. Globally, 1.5 billion people had CLD in 2017. CLD accounts for 2 million deaths worldwide each year, in addition to a high burden of disability and healthcare costs. Liver fibrosis is a key pathogenic and prognostic feature in most CLD. Liver biopsies are the current gold standard for the diagnosis of liver fibrosis. However, biopsies are invasive and subject to sampling errors and significant intra-and inter-observer variability. The existing non-invasive methods for diagnosis of liver fibrosis still have significant limitations, particularly for diagnosis of liver fibrosis at early stages. In this grant, we developed and investigated novel non-invasive MRI technologies for diagnosis of liver fibrosis. To make the measurements reliable, we developed methods to suppress the confounding signal from blood in the liver. To reduce influence from respiratory motion, we developed MRI technique so that the data can be acquired within a brief breath-hold. The preliminary clinical study demonstrated this technology has potential to detect early-stage liver fibrosis.

14202017.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14202017.value: 一般情形下推廣形信賴域子問題半定規劃（SDP）鬆弛的精准條件

14202017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14202017.value: While quadratically constrained quadratic programming (QCQP) formulation captures nonlinearity of the real world in its simple form, it still remains as a great challenge to the optimization community due to its nonconvexity. We investigate in this project generalized extended trust region subproblem (GETRS), an important subclass of QCQP. GETRS involves a nonconvex quadratic objective function, a nonconvex quadratic constraint and a set of linear constraints, and includes generalized trust region subproblem (GTRS) and extended trust region subproblem (ETRS) as its special cases. Our goal is to advance the state-of-the-art of GETRS, including GTRS and ETRS, in both theoretical and methodological aspects. It is always interesting to derive the exactness conditions under which a convex relaxation delivers an optimal solution of the primal problem. The exactness conditions of the semi-definite programming (SDP) relaxation of the GETRS still remain open due to i) the quadratic forms of the GETRS may not be simultaneously diagonalizable, and ii) the feasible region of the GETRS is no longer compact and the optimal solution may be unattainable in some cases. In this research, we will reformulate the SDP relaxation as a second-order-cone-programming (SOCP) relaxation using the canonical form developed in the PI's previous work. We will proceed to derive sufficient conditions to ensure an exact solution from the SOCP relaxation. Under such exactness conditions, we investigate further the attainableness under different assumptions. When expressing GTRS in its epigraph form, if we are able to identify the convex hull of the epigraph, we can find the exact solution. In this research, we will derive the convex hull of the intersection of a second order cone (SOC) and a quadratic under weaker conditions than the ones in the literature, which facilitates an identification of the convex hull of the intersection of two quadratic forms. We expect our technique to be used to derive SOCP reformulation for the GTRS under some easy-to-verify conditions. Practical implementations demand fast speed algorithms for solving the GTRS. As the GTRS has a non-compact feasible region and the objective value of GTRS is not always finite, no linear-time algorithm is available in the literature. Our preliminary research shows that, under some regular condition, we can restrict the feasible region to a compact neighborhood of an optimal solution within which the optimal value remains invariant (and finite). This finding will enable us to derive a linear-time algorithm for the GTRS under some mild conditions. 儘管二次約束二次規劃（QCQP）以其簡潔的形式描述客觀世界 的非線性本質，由於它的非凸性，QCQP仍然是最優化理論界面 對的一個棘手課題。本項目研究QCQP的一個重要子類（GETRS）， 即一般情形下推廣形信賴域子問題。 GETRS問題包含非凸二次形 目標函數，一個非凸二次形約束與一組線性約束。一般情形下的 信賴域子問題（GTRS）與推廣形信賴域子問題（ETRS）是 GETRS的兩個子類。我們的目標是推進GETRS（也包括GTRS與 ETRS）理論與演算法的研究前沿。 一個總是有趣的課題是找出精准條件，使得凸鬆弛的解同時給出 原問題的解。在目前，GETRS的半定規劃（SDP）鬆弛的精准條 件還未解決。其主要原因是由於兩個二次形可能不能同時對角化 及GETRS的可行域可能不緊或最優解不可達。在本研究中，利用 專案主持人以前在規範形方面的成果，我們會試圖將SDP鬆弛重 新寫成二階錐（SOCP）鬆弛的形式。我們其後將推導二階錐 （SOCP）鬆弛情況下的精准條件。在這些精准條件下，我們會 進一步研究不同假設下問題的可達性。 假設我們用Epigraph形式來表示GTRS， 如果我們能夠找出這一 Epigraph的凸包，我們也就能找到精確解。在一些比文獻中來的 弱的假設下，我們在本項目裡會先推導二階錐與二次形交集的凸 包，其後進一步推導兩個二次形交集的凸包。運用這一結果， 我們有信心在一些較容易檢驗的條件下，推導出GTRS的SOCP 鬆弛的等價描述。 在實際應用中求解GTRS常常需要快速演算法。因為GTRS可行 域非緊，不能保證GTRS目標值有界，所以文獻中還沒見到有線 性時間演算法。在我們的初步研究中發現，在一些正則條件下， 我們能限制可行域在最優解的鄰域，使得最優值在這鄰域中有 界且保持不變。這一發現將幫助我們，在一些溫和條件下，得 到GTRS的線性時間演算法。

14202117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14202117.value: Options market is a major component of today’s financial markets. A key issue in the options business is how to price and hedge various types of options. Starting with the celebrated works of Black, Scholes and Merton, option pricing models typically assume that the underlying asset price follows a continuous time Markov process with continuum state space. Despite few models in which option prices can be obtained in closed form, numerical approximations are often needed to price and hedge different types of options in practice. Continuous time Markov chain (CTMC) approximation is proposed recently for pricing several types of options, including European, barrier and Asian options. The idea is to approximate the continuous time Markov process with continuum state space in the model by a continuous time Markov chain that takes value in a discrete space. For the Markov chain model, the pricing problem can be solved in closed form using the matrix exponential. The Markov chain approximation method is very attractive in practice because it is applicable to general Markovian models, fast and accurate, and easy to implement. Although convergence of CTMC approximation for option pricing can be proved using standard weak convergence theory, the theoretically and practically important issue of convergence rate remains an open question. Financial payoffs do not have the required smoothness to apply standard results for convergence rate analysis, making the problem very challenging. In this project, we will develop an efficient algorithm based on CTMC approximation to price lookback options which are popular path-dependent options in the market. We also aim to solve the open problem on the convergence rate of CTMC approximation for diffusion models, which play a fundamental role in financial modeling. More specifically, we will establish sharp convergence rate for the price of European options and popular path-dependent options, as well as for the sensitivities of these options which are essential for hedging. Some smoothing techniques that can improve the convergence of CTMC approximation will also be analyzed and their effectiveness will be justified theoretically. The results achieved in this project will make a significant contribution to the theory and application of Markov chain approximation for option pricing and provide key insights into the best practice of this method in the options business. 期權市場是現代金融市場的一個重要組成部分。在期權業務中一個關鍵的問題是如何定價和對沖各種期權。從著名的Black, Scholes以及Merton的工作開始，期權定價模型通常假設基礎資產服從連續時間帶有連續狀態空間的馬氏過程。除了少數能夠有解析解的模型，現實中數值近似通常需要用來定價和對沖各種期權。 最近連續時間馬氏鏈近似的方法被用來定價各種期權，包括歐式，障礙式和亞式。這個方法的想法是用帶有連續時間離散狀態空間的馬氏鏈去逼近原模型中連續時間帶有連續狀態空間的馬氏過程。 對於馬氏鏈模型，定價問題可以用指數矩陣顯示的解出。馬氏鏈逼近的方法在實踐中很有吸引力，因爲它可以應用到一般的馬氏模型，準確且快速，同時容易編程實現。 儘管這個方法的收斂性可以用標準的弱收斂的辦法來證明，在理論和實踐中都非常重要的收斂速度問題仍未解決。金融中的收益函數沒有相應的光滑性去應用標準的關於收斂速度的分析。這使得該問題變得很有挑戰性。 在本課題中，我們會開發基於連續時間馬氏鏈逼近的算法去定價回溯期權。 這是市場中一種常見的路徑依賴期權。 我們同時希望對於擴散模型解決馬氏鏈逼近的收斂速度問題。該類模型是金融工程一類重要的基本模型。具體的講，我們會得到對於歐式以及一些路徑依賴期權的價格和對沖敏感度的收斂速度。我們也會分析一些能夠改進算法收斂性的光滑收斂的辦法， 並從理論上去證實他們的有效性。本課題得到的結果將為馬氏鏈定價對沖期權的研究做出重要的貢獻， 同時也為這個方法在現實中的最佳應用提供關鍵的指導。

14202117.label: Realisation of objectives
14202117.value: For objective 1, we have developed efficient algorithms for pricing European and American style lookback options based on continuous time Markov chain approximation. We have demonstrated the good performance of our algorithms under various popular financial models. See output 3 and 4. For objective 2, we've obtained sharp estimates of the convergence rate of continuous time Markov chain approximation for the prices of European, barrier and lookback options (the latter two are popular path-dependent options) under diffusion models. We've also developed sharp estimates of the convergence rate for option delta and gamma, which are important sensitivities for hedging these options. See output 1, 4 and 5. For objective 3, based on our convergence analysis, we've proposed principles for designing the grid of the Markov chain to achieve smooth second order convergence under diffusion models. This smoothing technique based on grid design would improve the general convergence rate of Markov chain approximation. We mathematically prove and numerically verify the effectiveness of this technique. We also analyze another smoothing technique called harmonic averaging and prove that it can improve the convergence rate for diffusion models with nonsmooth coefficients. See output 1 and 5. We've also gone beyond the original scope of the project to deal with other important problems using continuous time Markov chain approximation. (1) Parisian options are a class of complex path-dependent options. We've developed an efficient algorithm based on Markov chain approximation to price various types of Parisian options and obtained sharp estimate of its convergence rate for diffusion models. See output 6. (2) Diffusion models with a sticky boundary or a sticky interior point are natural tools for modelling some important financial phenomina, such as low interest rate and asset price stickiness. We've developed an efficient algorithm based on Markov chain approximation for computations under this type of models. The algorithm is applied to price bonds in a low interest rate model with stickiness to the lower bound of interest rates as well as European options in a geometric Brownian motion model with a sticky price level. We've also developed efficient simulation algorithms based on Markov chain approximation to simulate these models with sticky behavior. See outout 2 and 7.

14202117.label: Major findings and research outcome
14202117.value: 1. In output 1, we consider one-dimensional diffusion models with smooth coefficients and European and barrier options with nonsmooth payoffs. We mathematically prove that the convergence rate of continuous time Markov chain approximation is first order in general for the option price, delta and gamma. Based on the theoretical analysis, we propose principles for designing the Markov chain grid that are sufficient and necessary for achieving second order smooth convergence. Our grid design enables the Markov chain approximation method to price and hedge a large number of options with different strikes fast and accurately. In output 5, we consider a more challenging setting where the coefficients of the diffusion models can be nonsmooth in addition to nonsmooth payoffs. We also prove that the convergence rate is first order in general, but designing the grid properly or applying harmonic averaging to the nonsmooth coefficients can achieve second order convergence. These results allow the Markov chain approximation method to be efficient for solving important financial engineering problems like pricing occupuation time derivatives as well as bonds in short rate models with nonsmooth coefficients. 2. In output 4, we develop an efficient method for pricing various types of lookback options by combining Markov chain approximation with efficient numerical quadrature. In output 3, we consider lookback put options that can be exericsed early. These options can be converted to American style drawdown options for which we develop efficient algorithms based on Markov chain approximation. 3. In output 6, we develop an efficient algorithm based on Markov chain approximation to price various types of Parisian options and obtain sharp estimate of its convergence rate for diffusion models. Our method provides a unified approach to solve this challenging problem in a computationally efficient way. 4. In output 2, we consider one-dimensional diffusions with a sticky boundary or a sticky interior point. These models arise naturally in modeling some financial phenomena such as low interest rate environment and sticky price behavior. We develop an efficient Markov chain approximation scheme for these models and provide a sharp convergence rate estimate. We also use the scheme to simulate these processes for which the standard simulation method like Euler scheme completely fails. In output 7, we consider multidimensional diffusions with sticky boundaries and develop an efficient simulation scheme based on multidimensional Markov chain approximation. Results in output 6 and 7 are also reported in the PhD dissertation of my student Christian Meier.

14202117.value: 1. The project is focused on single asset options. We plan to extend the Markov chain approximation method to price and hedge some important two-asset options, such as spread options, double lookbacks and rainbow options. 2. The convergence rate analysis is done for diffusion models. We plan to develop sharp convergence rate estimates for models with jumps.

14202117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14202117.value: In financial markets, an important problem is how to price various types of options under sophisticated models that describe the random financial environment and manage the risk associated with these options. In this project, we develop fast and accurate algorithms for the pricing and risk management of some popular financial options based on Markov chain approximation. We also provide rigorous theoretical analysis of its convergence behavior. The outputs of the project equip financial institutions with computationally efficient tools to price and manage the risk in their options business.

14202217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14202217.value: The goal of this project is to develop a new framework which unifies visual representation learning and concept modeling through intelligent visual question answering (VQA). A new VQA system and a new question guided visual search engine will be developed from this framework. Deep learning has generated big impact on both computer vision and natural language processing. Its success heavily relies on large-scale training data and it faces challenges when many applications only have a small number of training samples. However, human beings have the capability of learning new concepts from a few samples, and they can also flexibly model new concepts by combining visual representations learned from existing concepts. Nowadays, with the fast growth of rich media on the web, social networks, and mobile devices, tens of thousands of new visual concepts emerge quickly in daily life. There is a need to break the limitations of existing deep learning frameworks on predefined visual concepts and large-scale training data. In the framework developed from this project, concepts and their relations are automatically discovered from visual question-answer pairs in natural language description. The process of free-style VQA keeps generating new concepts. Visual representations are automatically learned and matched with the discovered concepts with recurrent neural networks. On the top of that, a new Bayesian model is proposed to generate new concepts from common concepts and a few training samples, forming a structured visual concept system. This framework can significantly improve visual recognition on emerging concepts with small training data. Besides, a new VQA system will be developed from this framework. It answers human-raised questions regarding to visual content of images and also automatically generates meaningful questions regarding to visual content. As one of the broad range of applications, a question guided visual search engine based on the VQA system will be developed. It captures user intention by raising a series of questions intelligently. The outcome of this project will have substantial impact on computer vision and deep learning research both scientifically and practically. It targets on the fundamental challenges and makes computer vision systems an important step towards human visual perception and intelligence. It makes significant contributions to many computer vision applications with small training data and emerging concepts. The developed VQA system based on representation learning and concept modeling also has important applications to robotics, question guided image search and other fields. 本項目的目的是研究基於智能問答的新框架，該框架可以統一視覺表達學習和概念建模。我們還將基於該框架開發一個新的智能問答系統和一個新的問題指引的視覺搜索引擎。 深度學習在計算機視覺和自然語言處理領域都產生了巨大影響。它的成功極大依賴於大規模訓練，同時當許多應用只有小樣本時，它也面臨巨大的挑戰。然而人類具有從少量樣本中學習新概念的能力。他們也可以通過將從已有概念中學習得到的視覺特徵的表達進行組合，靈活地對新概念進行建模。現在隨著互聯網媒體，社交網絡和移動端設備的快速增長，成千上萬的新的視覺概念在生活中湧現。迫切需要打破現有深度學習框架對於預先定義的視覺概念和大規模訓練數據的限制。 本項目中研究的框架可以從自然語言描述的視覺問答對中自動發現概念以及概念之間的關係。自由式視覺問答的過程中，新概念會不斷產生。視覺表達是通過復發神經網絡自動學習得到並與發現的概念進行匹配。在此基礎之上，提出了一個新的貝葉斯模型，它可以從常見概念和小樣本中生成新的概念，進而形成一個結構化的視覺概念系統。它可以回答人們針對圖像視覺內容提出的問題，還可以自動生成關於視覺內容的有意義的問題。作為它的廣泛應用之一，我們會基於這個視覺問答系統研發一個問題引導的視覺搜索引擎。它能智能地提出一系列問題，進而捕捉用戶的意圖。 本項目的成果將會對計算機視覺和深度學習理論研究和實踐產生巨大影響。它使得計算機視覺系統向人類視覺和智能邁向重要一步。它對許多基於小樣本和新概念的計算機視覺的應用作出重要的貢獻。基於表達學習和概念建模研發的視覺問答系統在機器人，問題引導的圖像搜索和其它領域都有重要應用。

14202217.label: Realisation of objectives
14202217.value: All the objectives in this project have been realized successfully. (1) We have developed a novel framework for learning effective latent concept representations to unify visual and question features. Exploiting relationships between visual regions and question words have achieved great success in learning multi-modality features for Visual Question Answering (VQA). However, previous methods mostly model relations between individual visual regions and words, which are not enough to correctly answer the question. Answering a visual question requires understanding the summarizations of visual and language information. To learn latent concept representations for both images and questions, we proposed the Multi-modality Latent Interaction module (MLI). The proposed module encodes visuals and languages into a small number of latent concept representations, which can be considered as latent visual and language summarizations. The cross-modality relationships between the two modalities are modeled based on the latent concepts. The small number of latent representations to avoid modeling uninformative individual region-word relations. The cross-modality information between the latent summarizations are propagated to fuse valuable information from both modalities and are used to update the visual and word features. Such MLI modules can be stacked for several stages to model complex and latent relations between the two modalities and achieves highly competitive performance on public VQA benchmarks. (2) We have developed visual question answering systems based on representation learning and concept modeling. Another important aspect of VQA is to better fuse multi-modal information. We propose a novel method of dynamically fusing multi-modal features with intra- and inter-modality information flow, which alternatively pass dynamic information between and across the visual and language modalities. It can robustly capture the high-level interactions between language and vision domains, thus significantly improves the performance of visual question answering. We also show that the proposed dynamic intra-modality attention flow conditioned on the other modality can dynamically modulate the intramodality attention of the target modality, which is vital for multimodality feature fusion. Experimental evaluations on public benchmarks show that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art VQA performance. (3) We have developed a language-guided person image search algorithm. Person image retrieval is an important task that requires learning discriminative visual features for distinguishing different person identities. Diverse auxiliary information has been utilized to improve the visual feature learning. We proposed to exploit language descriptions and questions as additional training supervisions for effective visual features. Compared with other auxiliary information, descriptions and questions can describe a specific person from more compact and semantic visual aspects, thus is complementary to the pixel-level image data. Our method not only learns better global visual feature with the supervision of the overall description but also enforces semantic consistencies between local visual and linguistic features, which is achieved by building global and local image-language associations. The global image-language association is established according to the identity labels, while the local association is based upon the implicit correspondences between image regions and noun phrases. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of employing language as training supervisions with the two association schemes. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on p without utilizing any auxiliary information during testing and shows better performance than other joint embedding methods for the image-language association.

14202217.label: Major findings and research outcome
14202217.value: As research outcomes, 15 conference papers are published in CVPR, ECCV, ICCV, NeurlPS, which are premier conferences on computer vision and machine learning. In this project, we have proposed a series of algorithms for Visual Question Answering (VQA). In (Part C.8 No. 5), we propose an end-to-end unified framework, the Invertible Question Answering Network (iQAN), to leverage the complementary relations between questions and answers in images by jointly training the model on VQA and VQG tasks. After training, iQAN can take either questions or answers as input, then output the counterparts. Evaluated on the large-scale visual question answering datasets, our iQAN improves the VQA accuracy over the baselines. In (Part C.8 No. ), we proposed a novel Question-Guided Hybrid Convolution (QGHC) network for VQA. Question-guided kernels generated from the input question are designed to convolute with visual features for capturing the textual and visual relationship in the early stage. The question-guided convolution can tightly couple the textual and visual information but also introduce more parameters when learning kernels. The hybrid convolution can generate discriminative multi-modal features for effective VQA.In (Part C.8 No.16), we propose a novel Dynamic Fusion with Intra- and Inter-modality Attention Flow framework for efficient multi-modality feature fusion to accurately answer visual questions. Our DFAF framework integrates cross-modal self-attention and cross-modal co-attention mechanisms to achieve effective information flows within and between the image and language modalities. The multi-modal features can be effectively fused in the proposed framework. In (Part C.8 No.17), to model more complex cross-modality relations, we propose a novel Multi-modality Latent Interaction Network (MLIN) with MLI modules. The MLI module encodes question and image features into a small number of latent visual and question summarizaiton vectors. Original visual and word features would finally aggregate information from the updated latent summarizations using attention mechanisms to predict the correct answers. In (Part C.8 No. 8), we have also proposed other algorithms on using language descriptions as supervisions to help image-to-image search. We design a deep neural network to automatically associate related phrases and local visual features via the attention mechanism to improve the learning of image features. We have also developed algorithms for learning discriminative features for different computer vision tasks, including relation detection, person retrieval, 3D human pose estimation. The learned visual features can be transferred into language-related applications to achieve better performance.

14202217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14202217.value: In this project, we have developed a series of VQA systems, some of which can only utilize a small number of training samples. For future work, we will explore using much larger vision-language pre-trained models for improving the VQA performance. We will further study more advanced vision-language models that do not work only for the VQA task, but also simultaneously on a series of other vision-language tasks, such as image captioning, language-guided navigation, etc. Such obtained visual and linguistic features for the multiple tasks can also be improved via the multi-task learning. We plan to generalize such learned features to improve single-modal downstream vision and language tasks, including object detection, image segmentation, question answering, neural machine translation, etc.

14202217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14202217.value: The goal of this project is to develop a new framework which unifies visual representation learning and concept modeling for visual question answering (VQA). A series of new VQA systems and language-guided visual search engine were developed in this project. The proposed systems can automatically mine a series of concepts for better summarizing visual and question information to tackle the VQA tasks. Different techniques were proposed to better fuse the multi-modal information within the language and vision modalities. They are either new operators to better process the multi-modal information, or mechanisms to mine the underlying concepts for better information fusion. The developed VQA system based on representation learning and concept modeling also has important downstream applications to robotics, language-guided navigation and other fields.
