14202417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14202417.value: The aim of this project is to devise and implement a computer-aided detection method based on the deep convolutional neural network (CNN) structure and model compression techniques for real-time diagnosis of polyps during colonoscopy. Detection and classification of polyps are two major procedures in colorectal cancer diagnosis during colonoscopy. Early diagnosis enables resection of neoplastic polyps at an early stage before they develop into deep submucosal invasive cancer. However, the performance of optical diagnosis of small colorectal polyps varies among endoscopists. A computer-aided algorithm for objective polyp diagnosis during colonoscopy can assist endoscopists in diagnosing colon polyps. Towards this end, our team has recently developed algorithms based on the CNN structure and transfer learning technique to identify 2D images with polyps from short colonoscopy video clips, as well as to classify the polyps as hyperplasia and adenomatous with an accuracy of 86%. Nevertheless, it needs to be further substantiated whether the accuracy still holds good in real-time colonoscopy procedures with more complicated scenarios, e.g. with motion blur, interlacing artifact and bubble reflection. In particular, identifying polyps for diagnosis in these scenarios are challenging. Therefore, a polyp detection algorithm to assist endoscopists for real-time detection and classification of polyps during colonoscopy is needed. We propose to develop a 3D deep CNN model for polyp detection by making use of the spatial-temporal relationship among adjacent frames of a colonoscopy video to better discriminate frames with or without polyps. By coupling the compact deep CNN structure with novel model compression techniques, model parameters and computational complexity of the proposed CNN structure can be drastically reduced such that the data processing time can be reduced without comprising the detection accuracy. The proposed method is anticipated to integrate with the polyp classification algorithm to improve the effectiveness of colonoscopy in colorectal cancer prevention. 該項目旨在設計并實施一套基於深度卷積神經網絡（CNN）結構和模型壓縮技術的計算機輔助檢測方法，以用於在結腸鏡檢查期間對息肉进行實時診斷。 息肉的檢測和分類是在結腸鏡檢查期間對結直腸癌診斷的兩個重要步驟。早期診斷可以在息肉發展成深層粘膜下侵襲性癌症之前对腫瘤性息肉进行切除。然而，內鏡醫師依據光學方法對小型結直腸息肉的診斷準確性因人而異。一套可以对息肉进行客觀診斷的計算機輔助算法可以在內鏡醫師进行結腸鏡檢查时起到辅助作用。為此，我們的團隊最近開發了一套基於深度卷積神经網絡結構和轉移學習技術的算法，從短結腸鏡視頻中識別含有息肉的2D圖像，並將息肉分類為增生和腺瘤，精度达86％。然而，這套算法的精確度能否在實時結腸鏡檢查過程中，以及在更複雜的情況下，例如運動模糊，交錯假象和氣泡反射，依然保持良好需要进一步验证。特別地，在這些情況下識別息肉是具有挑戰性的。因此，需要一種息肉檢測算法來協助內窺鏡醫生在進行結腸鏡檢查時，对息肉进行實時檢測和分類。 我們提出的一个用於息肉檢測的3D深度卷積神经网络方法，通過利用結腸鏡視頻相鄰幀之間的时间-空间相关性，以更好地區分具有或不具有息肉的幀。通過將简洁型深度卷積神經網絡結構與新型模型壓縮技術相結合，可以大大減少提出的深度卷積神經網絡的模型參數和計算複雜度，從而可以在不损失檢測精度的情況下降低數據處理時間。提出的检测方法将與息肉分類算法相結合，以提高結腸鏡检查在結腸直腸癌預防中的有效性。

14202417.label: Realisation of objectives
14202417.value: 1. To build up an expert-labelled database on colonoscopy videos which reflect more complicated imaging situations during colonoscopy (e.g., motion blur, interlacing artefacts and bubble reflections) to facilitate more rigorous performance evaluation of polyp detection algorithms The system we developed is named AI-doscopist. The training and validation datasets to fine-tune AI-doscopist consisted of colonoscopy and non-medical images. The images were obtained from 7 databases around the world, including four public online colonoscopy databases, two private databases formed by colonoscopy images/videos from two local hospitals, and one non-medical database: 1) CVC-ColonDB, 2) CVC-ClinicDB, 3) ETIS-LaribDB, 4) AsuMayoDB, 5) CU-ColonDB, 6) ACP-ColonDB530, and 7) Selected Google Images. Details of the first five databases have been described in our previous studies. As most of the images in the previous five databases consisted of images with polyps, we constructed the sixth database from videos of colonoscopies collected from our Endoscopy Centre. To construct this database, written informed consents were obtained from patients before colonoscopy during June to October 2017. Excluding 19 patients with abnormality found but no biopsy taken, 133 patients with corrupted/missed videos, and 14 patients whose lesion cannot be labelled, 364 patients were included in this database, namely ACP-ColonDB530. Data from 220 patients were used for training and validation (ACP-ColonDB530-Train), while data from 144 patients (68.0±8.8 years old and 69 males) were used for testing (ACP-ColonDB530-Test). A total of 110 hours of colonoscopy videos were recorded from 364 patients by 7 endoscopists. The objects found in the colonoscopy images were classified into 13 categories, namely “Adenomatous Polyp”, “Hyperplastic Polyp”, “Other Polyp”, “Bleeding”, “Lumen”, “IC Valve”, “Normal Colon Structure”, “Instrument”, “Stool”, “Bubble”, “Artefact”, “Inside Colon Background”, and “Outside Colon Background”. The total length of the colonoscopy videos we collected for the training dataset were 57 hours. We included images with a polyp as much as possible (72,350 images). In order to maintain a relatively balanced ratio between images with and without a polyp, we randomly selected 116,250 images without a polyp for training. Most of these images were selected based on running the training dataset with an earlier version of AI-doscopist. “False Positives” were manually checked and re-labelled to other categories. “False Negatives” were confirmed and other non-polyp labels that can possibly affect the localization of the polyp were added in the same image. “True Negatives” were randomly selected for inclusion for training. The selection ratio is around 3.7%, which is a trade-off between acceptable performance, labelling efforts and time required for training. 2. To develop real-time algorithms based on 3D deep CNN for polyp detection during colonoscopy A novel regression-based Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) pipeline has been developed for polyp detection during colonoscopy. The proposed pipeline was constructed in two parts: 1) to learn the spatial features of colorectal polyps, a fast object detection algorithm named ResYOLO was pre-trained with a large non-medical image database and further fine-tuned with colonoscopic images extracted from videos; and 2) temporal information was incorporated via a tracker named Efficient Convolution Operators (ECO) for refining the detection results given by ResYOLO. The proposed algorithm achieved real-time detection with good trade-off between accuracy and processing speed, i.e. the method can accurately locate polyps in more frames and at a faster speed compared to existing methods. We evaluated the proposed model on different platforms. When the input image resolution was fixed at 608 × 608, the model ran at around 28 frames per second (fps) on a Nvidia GTX 1080Ti and at 37 fps on a Nvidia GTX 2080Ti. 3. To investigate the effectiveness of a transfer learning scheme for the 3D deep CNN model, i.e. pre-training with a large-scale non-medical video database and fine-tuning with the colonoscopy video database Due to the limitation in processing speed, 3D deep CNN model were not chosen for the system. Instead, spatial features were extracted by AI-doscopist using a 2D CNN and tracked using a temporal filter. The backbone network of AI-doscopist was first pre-trained with 1.2 million non-medical images collected from the public online database ImageNet. Additional learning using selected images from the aforementioned, combined databases were used to fine-tune AI-doscopist for 90 epochs, using stochastic gradient descent with a learning rate of 0.001, weight decay of 0.0005 and momentum of 0.9. All learned weights were monitored by the validation dataset to avoid overfitting. The learned weights that gave the highest sensitivity, given the specificity was over 0.9, when evaluated on the validation dataset were selected as the final model for testing. Moreover, different transfer learning scheme has been studied for topics related to AI-doscopist. Specifically, a multi-task recurrent neural network has been built to predict hospital mortality of patients from the critical care unit. The learnt weight has been transferred to predict mortality and need of therapeutic endoscopy in patients with an acute gastrointestinal bleeding, a common medical emergency worldwide. The possibility of transferring knowledge learnt by AI-doscopist to another endoscopy procedure (endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography) has also been studied. 4. To improve the time efficiency of the 3D deep model using structure such as SqueezeNet and model compression techniques for real time polyp detection Different CNN Structures have been evaluated for the real-time localization of colorectal polyps in edge computing devices, including devices with graphics processing units (GPU) and field programmable gate array (FPGA). Two deep network structures (Darknet19 and YOLO-Lite) and evaluate their accuracy and inference time for the localization of colorectal polyps. When evaluated on a public database, the deep network modified from Darknet19 (Darknet19-l4) achieved the best performance (sensitivity=88%, specificity=95%, and inference time=20ms). To conclude, deep networks designed for general object detection should be restructured in order to optimize their performance for localizing colorectal polyp in endoscopy videos. Nevertheless, based on the compression techniques implemented on the current edge computing devices, the sensitivity of polyp localization dropped below 90%, which is not ideal for a medical application. Thus, instead of using the compressed technique, dual-GPU systems have been set up for further study and testing. In one of our studies, 144 full colonoscopies have been evaluated. The image-based specificity of AI-doscopist was 93.3%. AI-doscopist were able to localise 124 out of 128 polyps (polyp-based sensitivity = 96.9%). Furthermore, after reviewing the suspected regions highlighted by AI-doscopist in a 102-patient cohort, an endoscopist has high confidence in recognizing four missed polyps in three patients who were not diagnosed with any lesion during their original colonoscopies. In summary, AI-doscopist can localise 96.9% of the polyps resected by the endoscopists. Furthermore, using the dual-GPU system, AI-doscopist was evaluated on another 57 videos (from 50 patients) of which no biopsy was taken during their endoscopy. AI-doscopist detected suspicious regions in only 12397 frames. In other words, amongst roughly 1,282,500 images (= 57 videos x 15 min/video x 60 min/sec x 25 frames/second), it highlighted only < 1% of the regions. On average, AI-doscopist highlighted suspicious regions for 8.7 seconds/colonoscopy in normal subjects.

14202417.label: Major findings and research outcome
14202417.value: The work has led to two journal papers, two book chapters, and three conference papers during the project period. Moreover, two more journal papers and several conferences papers related to the work of AI-doscopist have been prepared/under preparation. A spin-off company has been formed to possibly commercialize the work. Two dual-GPU systems have been setup to possibly localise colonic neoplasia in real-time during colonoscopy. AI-doscopist has been trained to localise 13 categories of objects in the colonoscopy images, namely “Adenomatous Polyp”, “Hyperplastic Polyp”, “Other Polyp”, “Bleeding”, “Lumen”, “IC Valve”, “Normal Colon Structure”, “Instrument”, “Stool”, “Bubble”, “Artefact”, “Inside Colon Background”, and “Outside Colon Background”. The CNN structure together with the features learnt for these classes can be further developed to extend the functions of AI-doscopist. The PI of this project has received several international recognitions for her work in this related area. She has been awarded Academic Early Career Achievement Award by IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society 2018 “for her contributions to wearable sensing and endoscopic surgery.” Moreover, she has been appointed as the Distinguished Lecturer (DL) by the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society (EMBS) during 2019-2020. The appointment is considered as a major Society recognition. The DL program aims to provide high quality speakers to the Biomedical Engineering Community. During her term of service, she has travelled to Portugal, South Korea, Malaysia, and different regions in China to deliver talks on AI-doscopist and related topics. Hundreds of students and researchers have benefited from the talks. Due to the outbreak of COVID-19, hosts from India and China have invited the candidate to virtual conferences that were held online in 2020, reaching out to over 6000 candidates in one incidence.

14202417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14202417.value: We have designed a deep-learning model, an “Artificial Intelligent Endoscopist (a.k.a. AI-doscopist)”, to localise colonic neoplasia during colonoscopy. AI-doscopist was pre-trained by 1.2 million non-medical images and fine-tuned by 291,090 colonoscopy and non-medical images. The colonoscopy images were obtained from 6 databases, where the colonoscopy images were classified into 13 categories and the polyps’ locations were marked image-by-image by the smallest bounding boxes. Seven categories of non-medical images, which were believed to share some common features with colorectal polyps, were downloaded from an online search engine. Written informed consent were obtained from 144 patients who underwent colonoscopy and their full colonoscopy videos were prospectively recorded for evaluation. A total of 128 suspicious lesions were resected or biopsied for histological confirmation. When evaluated image-by-image on the 144 full colonoscopies, the specificity of AI-doscopist was 93.3%. AI-doscopist were able to localise 124 out of 128 polyps (polyp-based sensitivity = 96.9%). Furthermore, after reviewing the suspected regions highlighted by AI-doscopist in a 102-patient cohort, an endoscopist has high confidence in recognizing 4 missed polyps in 3 patients who were not diagnosed with any lesion during their original colonoscopies. In summary, AI-doscopist can localise 96.9% of the polyps resected by the endoscopists. If AI-doscopist were to be used in real-time, it can potentially assist endoscopists in detecting one more patient with polyp in every 20-33 colonoscopies.

14202817.label: Realisation of objectives
14202817.value: Exhaust emissions from gasoline vehicles are one of the major contributors to aerosol particles observed in urban areas. It is well-known that these tiny particles are associated with air pollution, climate forcing, and adverse health effects. However, their toxicity and bioreactivity after atmospheric ageing are less constrained. The aim of the present study was to investigate the chemical and toxicological properties of fresh and aged particulate matter (PM) samples derived from gasoline exhaust emissions under different driving cycles. Vehicle testing was carried out on a 48-inch single roller chassis dynamometer (Mustang, USA) set up in the Jockey Club Heavy Vehicle Emission Testing and Research Centre (JCEC), Hong Kong. The tailpipe emissions from the vehicle were connected to a dilution tunnel and a constant volume sampling unit. Real-time concentrations of carbon monoxide (CO), carbon dioxide (CO2), nitrogen oxides (NOx) and total hydrocarbons (THC) were sampled near the end of the dilution tunnel. Fresh emitted aerosol samples were collected by Teflon filter and quartz filter from the dilution tunnel simultaneously. Then part of the diluted exhaust sample was then mixed with ozone and delivered into the Gothenburg Potential Aerosol Mass (PAM) flow reactor to simulate the atmospheric ageing of gasoline exhaust particles. Before entering the reactor, the diluted exhaust was mixed with ozone-containing zero air in a ratio of 1:1 in order to maintain a relatively stable temperature and humidity in the reactor. The main oxidant in PAM reactor is hydroxyl radical (OH), which is produced by the photolysis of externally supplied ozone and water vapor under UV radiation at 254 nm. The aged PM samples were collected simultaneously on a 47-mm quartz filter and a 47-mm Teflon membrane filter. In this study, five gasoline vehicles were recruited for the sampling campaign. All the recruited vehicles are currently in circulation in Hong Kong; they have similar sizes (from 1395 to 1600 kg), but different exhaust emission standards (two are Euro 3, one is Euro 4, and one is Euro 5). All vehicles are equipped with a three-way catalyst as aftertreatment device. Three driving tests were performed on each vehicle based on three driving cycles: the new European driving cycle (NEDC), idling cycle, and steady state cycle. The weight of PM sample collected on each pre-weighted filter were determined gravimetrically. Gravimetric analysis was then carried out by a microbalance (Satorius, Germany) with readability of 0.001 mg inside the same chamber. The organic carbon (OC) content, elemental carbon (EC) content were determined using a Desert Research Institute Model 2001 Thermal/Optical Carbon Analyzer with IMPROVE-A protocol. In total, 119 organic species were characterized in the present study, including 40 polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), 27 n-alkanes, 27 monocarboxylic acids, 8 alkenoic acids, 11 dicarboxylic acids, 3 aromatic acids and 3 engine emission (EE) markers. The non-polar organic compounds detected on the filter samples were directly analyzed via in-injection port thermal desorption-gas chromatography/mass spectrometry (TD-GC/MS). The polar organic compounds, including organic acids [i.e., 27 monocarboxylic acids, 11 dicarboxylic acids, 3 aromatic acids, and 3 EE markers], were analyzed using the solvent extraction (SE-GC/MS) method. The emission factors (EFs) of OC, EC, and individual chemicals were calculated in a fuel-based manner. The amount of fuel consumed in each driving cycle was estimated based on the total amount of CO2 emitted. The mass of OC, EC, or individual chemicals produced in each driving cycle was then normalized by the amount of fuel consumed. Cell experiments were conducted with PM samples collected from freshly emitted and photochemically aged gasoline vehicle emission to determine their cytotoxicity. Human lung alveolar epithelial (A549) cells were used to investigate the toxicity induced by PM. The A549 cells were exposed to PM for 24 h, and bioreactivity markers such as lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), reactive oxygen species (ROS), and interlukin-6 (IL-6) were examined. For the determination of ROS production, the cells were exposed to 2’,7’-dichlorodihydrofluorescein diacetate (DCFH-DA). The reaction between cell bound ROS and DCFH-DA produce the highly fluorescent 2’,7’-dichlorofluorescin (DCFH). The fluorescent intensity serves as the surrogate of ROS concentration and was measured by a Light Luminescence Plate Reader (VICTOR X, Waltham, MA, USA). The supernatants of the cell culture were used to determine the lactic dehydrogenase (LDH) and interlukin-6 (IL-6) released by the cell. The concentrations of LDH and IL-6 were determined by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) kit (BD Biosciences, CA, USA) according to manufacturer’s instructions. Inflammatory and oxidative responses were found after PM exposure, and the crucial organic compounds for the cell responses were also identified. Spearman’s rank correlation was used for the correlation analysis while the Kruskal-Wallis H test was employed to identify significant differences among datasets. All of the targets have been accomplished on schedule. The outcomes were published in peer-reviewed journals. More results will be anticipated and expected for further articles submissions in due course.

14202817.label: Major findings and research outcome
14202817.value: The emission factors (EFs) of PM, OC, and EC for all vehicles under the three tested driving cycles were determined. In general, in fresh PM samples, the idling cycle had the lowest EF, followed by steady state cycle, whereas the NEDC cycle generated the highest EF. A similar trend was observed in the fresh OC samples. The EFs of PM, OC and individual organic species have significantly increased after the fresh exhaust samples passed through the PAM reactor under all driving conditions and for all tested vehicles. This increase can be explained by the formation of secondary organic aerosol (SOA) in the PAM reactor, where the gaseous SOA precursors present in the fresh exhaust samples oxidized and condensed to particle-phase compounds. It can be observed that the dominating organic components of fresh and aged PM were n-alkane (carbon number 25 to 34) and PAH (four-ring PAHs) under all tests. Moreover, the weighing of o-PAH, dicarboxylic acid, and aromatic acid increased significantly in aged PM sample. In particular, a drastic increase in aromatic acid (e.g. phthalic acid) was observed in idling cycle tests. The high concentration of organic gases, e.g. benzene, toluene and xylenes, in the idling cycle provides a large number of precursors for the formation of SOA, ultimately resulting in a high concentration of oxidation products. It can be observed that under all driving conditions and for all vehicles, the levels of ROS in aged PM samples were higher than in fresh PM samples. This result clearly shows that aged or highly oxidized gasoline exhaust causes a more significant oxidation stress to human lung cells compared to its unoxidized form. In most cases, the IL-6 and LDH values were higher in the aged samples than in the fresh ones. Moderate to weak correlations were identified between chemical species (e.g. dicarboxylic acids and O-PAHs) and ROS levels in fresh PM samples, as well as between chemical species and LDH levels in aged samples. Stepwise regression analysis results suggested that n-alkane and alkenoic acid are the major contributors to the increase in LDH levels in fresh samples, while PAH and monocarboxylic acid the main factors causing the increase in LDH levels in aged samples. This study demonstrated that other than fresh emission, the aged organic compounds derived from gasoline vehicles play a critical role in PM-induced oxidative stress and inflammation in urban areas of Hong Kong.

14202817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14202817.value: The current study was focusing on the chemical characteristics of PM samples collected from fresh and aged gasoline exhaust under different driving cycles. The cytotoxicity caused by PM were investigated and compared. In the future, VOC emission from vehicles and their secondary organic aerosol formation mechanism by photo-oxidation reactions can be further studied. Moreover, it is important to compare the health effects triggered by different vehicle types, e.g. diesel vehicles, LPG vehicles etc. In this study, only organic components were identified, metals and inorganic fractions of PM were not resolved in details. Therefore, the detailed chemical compositions of fresh and aged PM from different vehicles types (e.g. diesel and LPG vehicles) can be investigated and compared, the results are important for the further air pollution control strategies in Hong Kong. In addition, human health effects could be studied based on the current results, such as the cardiovascular and pulmonary diseases. When PM inhaled by human, there will be a series of body reactions be triggered and spread to the whole body, which will finally trigger different disease, this is also important for the further studies on PM health researches.

14202817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14202817.value: Motor vehicles are one of the key air pollution sources in urban areas of Hong Kong. The health effects of vehicular exhaust have attracted many interests. However, these studies were limited to the primary emissions. This is inadequate since particulate and gaseous source emissions can undergo different transformations once emitted to the atmosphere. Therefore, reliable scientific data on the levels of the fresh and aged gasoline exhaust particles and their chemical compositions are essential to evaluate the potential effects on human health. In this study, we added to the literature the robust evidence of significant amount of SOA formed after oxidation of exhaust from gasoline vehicles. High loading of organic acids and oxygenated compounds were determined in aged aerosol. In general, the bioreactivity markers have higher values in the aged samples than in the fresh ones. Moderate to weak correlations were identified between chemical species and bioreactivity markers in PM samples. Further investigations are encouraged to understand the mechanisms behind the observed increase in bioreactivity during PM ageing. This study demonstrated that other than fresh emission, the aged organic compounds derived from gasoline vehicles play a critical role in PM-induced oxidative stress and inflammation in urban areas of Hong Kong.

14203417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14203417.value: Digital content generated around the world is growing in an increasing rate. Cloud storage business, now hosting petabytes of data, is expected to have double-digit annual growth rates in the coming years. As hard disk failures are commonplace events in a large-scale a distributed storage system, providing reliability and fault tolerance is one of the major missions of cloud storage service providers. Traditional erasure-correcting codes, such as Reed-Solomon codes, cannot cope with today's networked storage systems, because it is not designed for the purpose of repairing individual symbol in a codeword. Should a traditional erasure-correcting code be employed, the amount of network bandwidth required to repair the failed disks will occupy a significant portion of the total network resource. Reducing the overhead due to disk repairs is one of the major challenges in cloud storage. There are two classes of storage codes which can be repaired efficiently. The first one is called regenerating codes, and is built upon the premise that the amount of network traffics required to recover a lost storage node is optimized, with respect to a fundamental bound derived from network coding theory. The second one is called locally repairable codes, and is aimed at minimizing the number of nodes contacted during a repair process. We will focus on the second class in this project. The number of existing storage nodes we need to access during the repair of a failed disk is a system parameter called the locality. Erasure-correcting code with small locality is preferred in cloud storage systems, as it incurs fewer disturbances to other storage nodes during a repair process. The design of storage codes with small locality is an emerging research topic. Some existing code constructions and bounds on code parameters are available. The objective of this project is to devise fast decoding algorithms for this class of storage codes, and to come up with new storage codes that can be repaired efficiently. 雲端存儲業務預計在未來幾年將有兩位數的年度增長。由於硬盤故障是一個常常出現的事件，提供可靠性和容錯性是一個雲存儲服務提供商的主要任務。現時，有兩種新一代的編碼方法。第一種被稱為再生碼，第二種被稱為局部修碼。這個項目的目標是設計出有效和快速的解碼方案。

14203917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14203917.value: Since the beginning of this decade, the automatic manipulation of compliant objects has attracted a great deal of attention amongst many researchers in the robotics and automation community. This rising interest in automating the manipulation of soft objects comes from its many potential applications in various fields such as surgery (e.g. manipulating soft tissues and organs), food industry (shaping food materials), personal and home robotics (folding stretchable fabrics/clothes), manufacturing (assembling flexible parts), to name a few cases. However, despite the recent progress in soft robotics, the automatic manipulation of soft materials still remains an open research problem. The main difficulties that hamper the implementations of these types of dexterous manipulation tasks are: (1) the real-time estimation of the deformation properties of the unmodelled soft object, (2) the characterisation of the infinite-dimensional soft body as a compact feedback signal, and (3) the coordination of the robot's input motion with the feedback shape measurements of the manipulated object. Our goal in this project is precisely to provide a solution to these issues. Specifically, we aim to develop a new visual servoing methodology for robot manipulators to automatically deform soft objects into a desired target shapes. To perform these types of manipulation tasks, we will use an efficient vector representation (constructed with Fourier coefficients) of the object's feedback contour that is suitable for real-time computations and closed-loop control. To automatically deform the object into the desired shape, an adaptive model estimator that iteratively approximates the relation between the manipulators' input motion and the relative change of the shape vector will be developed. The estimated model will be used to coordinate the motion trajectories for each robot manipulator. Note that in contrast with most previous deformation controller, the new method that we propose in this project do not require to use artificial markers or special texture on the object's surface. The work proposed in this project, will be validated by conducting multiple experiments with robotic prototypes in our laboratory. The research outputs from this project will contribute to the technological advancements of robotics and automation in Hong Kong and the rest of the world. 自十年以來，自動化在機器人這個領域引起了許多研究人員中極大的關注。 有著很多可發展潛力的研究領域，軟體機器人的操縱亦開始興盛，大部份應用於手術（軟組織和器官操縱），食品工業（食品成型材料），個人和家庭機器人（織物/衣服折疊），製造（柔性部件組裝）等等。 然而，儘管軟機器人近年取得了進展，但在操縱方面仍然保著一個開放性的研究課題，仍存在一定的困難。現時主要困難包括（1）軟體變形特性的實時預測，（2）將軟體的特性用作反饋信號，（3）機器人經反饋操作後的輸入運動。 我們在這個項目中的目標正是為這些問題提供解決方案。 具體來說，我們目標是開發新的視覺伺服方法，令機器人以自動操作，將軟體變形成所需的目標形狀。 為了執行這些類型的操作，我們將使用適用於實時計算和閉合控制回路的反饋輪廓的向量表示。 為了自動將物體變形成所需的形狀，我們將開發一個可以反覆預算操縱輸入運動和形狀矢量的相對變化的自我適應預算模型. 。 預計模型將用於操作機器人的運動軌跡。與大多數以前的變形控制器相反，我們在本項目中提出的新方法不需要在物體表面上使用人造標記或特殊紋理。本項目提出的工作將通過實驗室中的機器人原型進行多次實驗來驗證。 該項目的研究成果將有助於香港和世界其他地區的機器人和自動化技術進步。

14203917.label: Realisation of objectives
14203917.value: Objective 1: The first critical problem in the automatic manipulation of deformable objects is the representation of the object's shape. Throughout the project, we have proposed many original approaches to numerically characterise the infinite-dimensional configuration of soft objects. To this end, we developed several original algorithms that use, periodic trigonometric functions, principal component analysis (PCA), autoencoding networks, parametric curves/surfaces, contour moments, 3D curvatures and centroids, etc. Our developed methodology enables to efficiently characterise soft object shapes with compact (i.e., small dimensional) feature vectors; This facilitates the implementation of the method in real-time. Objective 2. To guide the deformation actions of a soft object with visual feedback, we must first compute the sensorimotor model that relates the robot's input motions with the produced object's shape changes; Note that this model is typically unknown. To address this problem, we developed online algorithms to adaptively estimate this structure without requiring to do parametric identification (which is complicated to do in practice). Our new methods accomplish this e.g., by using adaptive gradient descent rules, multi-objective optimisation algorithms, self-organising maps, spiking and deep neural networks, to name a few of our new solutions. With our proposed methodology, robots can manipulate complex deformable objects in a completely unstructured manner (a valuable property for real-world applications). Objective 3. The high dimensionality of the soft object's configuration poses many complications to the planning of a manipulation task. In contrast with rigid objects, planning a "straight" deformation trajectory of a soft object (defined in shape space) may not necessarily result in feasible/realisable object configurations (i.e., some of these motions may not be connected). To deal with this critical issue, we developed a new methodology that computes connected shaping actions by calculating geodesic trajectories over a deformation manifold. Out novel strategy solves the long-standing problem of determining the feasibility of a shape servoing trajectory before the robot performs the motions. This approach can be easily extended to various dimensions and configurations (e.g., surfaces, cables, and volumes). Objective 4. The ultimate goal of this project is to develop automatic controls that enable robots to manipulate and deform soft objects into desired shapes. Throughout the project, we have made important contributions in the design of shape servoing control laws; Various automatic control schemes have been formulated using e.g., sliding modes, model predictive control, hierarchical action planning, and output feedback regulation. The closed-loop stability of these control methods has been rigorously analysed using Lyapunov theory. Objective 5. The performance of *all* of our control methods and algorithms has been thoroughly validated with experiments. For that, we developed an advanced experimental robotic platform composed of multiple manipulators and vision sensors. Several innovative cases of study were formulated and proposed, such as the autonomous packing of soft objects into compact boxes, the manipulation of visco-elastic phantom tissues into desired shapes, automatic routing of cables and ropes in constrained environments, autonomous cloth manipulation and folding, and the shaping of composite rigid-soft materials. These manipulation capabilities demonstrated the practical feasibility of all new theoretic control methods.

14203917.label: Major findings and research outcome
14203917.value: 1. Findings on Shape Representation. Before we started this research project, the common practice to represent the infinite-dimensional shape of compliant objects was to use simple features such as angles and positions. Through our investigations, we solved the problem of computing generic shape representations with compact feature vectors. In contrast with traditional ad-hoc approaches, our methodology enables us to characterise a broad range of materials (including composites) and geometries (1D, 2D, 3D), and does not require any special texture or surface markers (refer to Part C, journal papers [1], [5] [9], [12], [14], [15], [17]). 2. Findings on Adaptive Sensorimotor Models. Classical methods to control the interaction with deformable objects are based on the assumption that the object's model is known. In our project, we demonstrated how adaptive computational models can efficiently estimate this information from sensory data. For example, we developed methods based on spiking neural networks ([2], [4], [6], [13]), sliding window ([5], [9], [15], [16]), and Lyapunov theory ([3], [11], [17]). 3. Findings on Manifold-Based Planning. Our project also made substantial contributions to the problem of deformable motion/path planning of robotic manipulation tasks. The main idea behind our new planning approach is to compute incremental connected points over a curved surface (which may represent e.g. a high dimensional manifold). By doing this, we can ensure that a shaping task is conducted in a physically reasonable sequence of actions; This idea was formalised in [7]; It was also demonstrated in other cases of study in [8], [10], [18]. 4. Findings on Sensor-Based Control and Applications. This project has led to various important results in the area of visual shape servoing. Traditional approaches to performing these manipulation tasks typically assume ideal unconstrained environments (which largely differs from practice). In this project, we have developed new control techniques that enable robots to perform complex manipulation tasks composed of multiple sequential actions; The effectiveness of this new approach has been demonstrated in challenging applications such as autonomous handling of soft materials (see [1], [14], [16]). Our proposed control theory can cope with multiple physical constraints of the experimental platform, thus, it facilitates its implementation in the field, see [16]. We extensively published in the best journals in robotics and control, which led to: - 15 published journal papers (10 Q1 papers, 4 Q2 papers, and 1 Q3 paper) - 3 papers currently under review - 7 conference papers

14203917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14203917.value: Various key directions must be further explored in the robotic manipulation of deformable materials, such as the development of vision/tactile-based algorithms that can progressively estimate the mechanical properties of objects based on sensor observations; By doing this, robots can construct a richer (viz. physics-informed) representation of their deformable environment and thus better plan the task. Another open technical problem is the manipulation of rheological materials, as the majority of methods in the literature have been developed for elastic objects; The effective manipulation of these types of materials is critical to automate many important applications in human environments, e.g., food processing. Also, although great progress has been achieved toward the development of multi-action control strategies, the performance of current methods still cannot solve most deformable manipulation tasks in the real-world; Action planning represents a promising direction to deal with the current limted capacity. Finally, with the ubiquitous adoption of data-driven approaches for estimation and control, the availability of data is a clear problem; The development of efficient and realistic simulation environments that can be used to train these systems (e.g., following a sim-to-real approach) is a feasible solution that demands to be further explored.

14203917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14203917.value: In this project, we have developed new methodologies to manipulate deformable objects with robots. These types of soft object manipulation tasks are needed to automate many important applications in various industries. For example, our methods can enable robots to automatically interact with soft tissues in robotic surgery, fold fabrics and cloths in home environments, shape and handle food materials in food processing tasks, and assemble soft and compliant parts in manufacturing, to name a few cases. A key component of our new solution is the development of specialised algorithms that provide robots with more efficient ways to: (1) understand the geometry of deformable objects and (2) physically interact with them. With these algorithms, robots can represent complex shapes of objects by using simple visual feedback, and automatically deform them into desired configurations (a task seemingly performed by humans, but which is very difficult to automate with robots). The outcomes of this project represent a leap forward toward the use of robot manipulators in unstructured human environments, where the majority of objects have some degree of deformability; We expect that our methods will pave the way for robots to finally be integrated into service tasks in human societies.

14204017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14204017.value: Network operators rely on network measurement to characterize the statistics of network traffic for effective network management. However, network measurement remains a missing piece in today's software packet processing platforms, which have been widely deployed in enterprise and data center networks. Mainstream software switches only support basic measurement tools that provide coarse-grained measurement. How to achieve fine-grained network measurement remains largely unexplored. Sketch-based measurement has been widely studied in the literature in the context of traditional IP networks, and hence is expected to provide a promising way of enabling fine-grained network measurement for software packet processing. Sketches are compact data structures that can summarize every packet with fixed-size memory and bounded errors. Many sketch designs have been proposed for different types of measurement tasks on detecting anomalies and characterizing traffic statistics. However, contrary to conventional wisdom, the seamless deployment of sketch-based measurement in software packet processing is in fact non-trivial. Our analysis suggests that existing sketch-based measurement solutions, when implemented in software, incur substantial computational overhead and fail to achieve line-rate throughput. We observe that while sketches are simple data structures that perform lightweight operations with theoretical guarantees, putting them in actual measurement requires sophisticated extensions that add substantial computational overhead to the software packet processing pipeline. In this research, we propose to design and implement a robust sketch-based network measurement framework, whose primary goal is to achieve high performance even under unexpectedly high traffic load, while still collecting accurate measurement results for characterizing the global network view. Our earlier work proposes an initial measurement framework toward this primary goal. Specifically, the framework is designed to complement existing sketch-based measurement solutions, by offloading their processing burdens in the face of high traffic load to a separate data path that provides fast but slightly inaccurate measurement. The framework periodically merges results and recovers missing information from multiple software switches, so as to return highly accurate network-wide measurement. We have built a prototype to realize this main idea, and our testbed experiments suggest that the prototype can improve sketch processing performance for a wide variety of measurement tasks. Our findings open many important research directions, both from theoretical and applied perspectives, on how to achieve robust sketch-based measurement at scale. The contributions of this research will enable network operators to effectively manage large-scale software-centric enterprise and data center networks. 網絡運營商依靠網絡測量來作網絡流量統計，以實現有效的網絡管理。 然而，網絡測量仍然是當今軟件網絡數據處理平台中的一個缺陷， 主流軟件交換器僅支持提供粗粒度的基本測量工具，如何實現細粒度網絡測量仍然在很大程度上未被探索。 在傳統IP網絡的背景下，文獻中已經廣泛研究了略圖式網絡測量，因此略圖有望為軟件網絡數據處理提供一個可行的方法來實現細粒度網絡測量。略圖是一種簡潔的數據結構，可以在固定大小內存和有界錯誤的前提下總結所有網絡數據。文獻中已經有得多不同的略圖設計，用於檢測異常和表徵流量統計等不同類型的網絡測量任務。 但是，與我們的經驗相反，略圖式測量在軟件網絡數據處理中的無縫部署實際上是有難度的。我們的分析發現，現有的略圖式測量解決方案在軟件實現時會產生很太的計算開銷，並且無法實現網絡最大吞吐量。我們觀察到，雖然略圖能提供具有理論保證的輕量級操作，但如果將其置於實際測量中，其實需要很複雜的擴展，亦因此為軟件網絡數據處理增加了大量的計算開銷。 在本研究中，我們提出設計和實現一個穩健的略圖式網絡測量框架，其主要目標是即使在意外的高流量負載下也能實現高性能，同時可以收集精確的測量結果和全網絡特徵。我們早期的工作提出了一個初步測量框架來實現這一主要目標，它旨在補充現有略圖式的測量解決方案，通過其處理高流量的單獨數據路徑，提供快速但略微不准確的測量，然後再週期性地合併結果，並從多個軟件交換機中恢復丟失的信息，以返回高精度的全網測量。我們已經建立了一個原型來實現這個主要思想，我們的測試實驗表明，原型可以提高各種測量任務的略圖處理性能。 我們的研究結果從理論和應用的角度，開展了許多重要的研究方向，穩健的略圖式網絡測量。這項研究的貢獻將使網絡運營商能夠有效管理大型以軟件為中心的企業和數據中心網絡。

14204017.label: Realisation of objectives
14204017.value: Objective 1 [Theoretical guarantees]: We have three new sketch architectures for practical network measurement, namely SketchLearn [SIGCOMM’18], MV-Sketch [INFOCOM’19, ToN’20], and SpreadSketch [INFOCOM’20]. We conduct theoretical complexity analysis on memory usage, accuracy, and update overhead for sketch-based measurement solutions. SketchLearn is a novel sketch-based measurement framework that greatly relieves manual efforts on the parameter tuning. Its idea is to automatically infer the inherent statistical properties of sketches without relying on complicated model parameters. We formally analyze the theoretical properties of SketchLearn that it can accurately retrieve flow information. MV-Sketch is a fast and compact invertible sketch that supports the detection of heavy flows (e.g., heavy hitters and heavy changers) with small and static memory allocation, thereby significantly mitigating the memory access overhead in high-speed network monitoring. MV-Sketch tracks candidate heavy flows inside the sketch data structure via the idea of majority voting. We formally analyze MV-Sketch on its memory space complexity, update/detection time complexity, and detection accuracy. We also extensively evaluate MV-Sketch via trace-driven experiments. SpreadSketch is another fast and compact invertible sketch that supports superspreader detection in which superspreaders send a large number of distinct connections (unlike the heavy flow problem, each distinct connection can be a small flow). We formally show that SpreadSketch can accurately identify superspreaders and also provide accurate estimates of their numbers of distinct connections, in a network-wide setting. Our findings are published at SIGCOMM, INFOCOM, and IEEE/ACM Transactions on Networking, all of which are prestigious venues in computer networking research. Objective 2 [Hierarchical measurement]: Our work SketchLearn [SIGCOMM’18] allows arbitrary flowkey definitions, thereby making hierarchical network measurement viable. SketchLearn is designed as a multi-level sketch for per-bit tracking, and hence it can extract the traffic statistics for any combination of the packet fields of interest by examining the levels for the corresponding bits. To support hierarchical measurement, we can readily define the flowkeys as the network prefixes for the corresponding subnets of interest, such that all flows that belong to the same subnet can be aggregated as a whole in network measurement. Objective 3 [Storage management]: We propose a distributed streaming systems called AF-Stream [VLDBJ’19], which proposes a lightweight checkpointing design that mitigates the storage I/O overhead in sketch-based measurement and general streaming analytics. Our observation is that while checkpointing provides a mechanism for storing measurement results, its high I/O overhead inevitably degrades normal processing performance. We are currently looking into a tunable checkpointing design that mitigates the performance overhead of checkpointing while limiting the checkpointing errors. Our work is designed to be applicable for not only sketch-based measurement, but also for general streaming analytics. Objective 4 [Large-scale deployment]: We propose OmniMon, a network telemetry architecture that supports various network-wide measurement tasks while simultaneously achieving both resource efficiency and full accuracy (which often cannot be simultaneously achieved in state-of-the-art measurement solutions in the literature). OmniMon carefully exploits the collaboration among network entities for network measurement. It further addresses consistency in network-wide epoch synchronization and accountability in error-free packet loss inference. In addition, we also demonstrate the feasibility of deploying our proposed measurement solutions in hardware for the emerging programmable data networks. Our proposed systems, SketchLearn, MV-Sketch, SpreadSketch, and OmniMon have all been deployed and evaluated on P4-based hardware programmable switches.

14204017.label: Major findings and research outcome
14204017.value: (I) Invertible sketch constructions. We propose invertible sketches that can accurately return anomalies of interest from the sketch structure itself for network measurement. We propose a number of invertible sketch constructions: (i) SketchLearn [SIGCOMM’18], which can return flow information without limited configuration efforts, (ii) MV-Sketch [INFOCOM’19, ToN’20], which returns the heavy hitters and heavy changers, and (iii) SpreadSketch [INFOCOM’20], which returns the superspreaders. We formally prove the theoretical properties and space/time complexities of each proposed sketch construction. (ii) Architectural designs for network measurement. We propose the architectural designs for large-scale network measurement. We propose AF-Stream [VLDBJ’19], which supports fault-tolerant storage management in data stream processing, including sketch-based measurement and general streaming analytics. We propose OmniMon [SIGCOMM’20], a network telemetry architecture that supports various network-wide measurement tasks while simultaneously achieving both resource efficiency and full accuracy.

14204017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14204017.value: We believe that the use of sketches in network measurement still has many open issues. First, in-band network telemetry (INT) has been widely used for active network measurement. INT embeds network telemetry information on a per-packet, per-hop basis to accurately monitor the network information, but the embedding of network telemetry information can add substantial packet overhead. An open question is to leverage sketches to record INT information in a compact manner. Also, the emergence of P4-based programming networks has created new opportunities for supporting advanced network measurement. We have demonstrated the feasibility of deploying our proposed sketch-based measurement design in P4-based hardware programmable switches. We may further exploit other types of network measurement tasks to support more scalable and versatile network measurement.

14204017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14204017.value: Network operators rely on network measurement to characterize the statistics of network traffic for effective network management. Sketches are compact data structures that can summarize every packet with fixed-size memory and bounded errors. How to enable sketch-based measurement in a large-scale network-wide environment remains a non-trivial task. In this research, we propose to design and implement various sketch-based network measurement solutions for large-scale network-wide environments. Our proposed solutions support various network measurement tasks (e.g., the detection of heavy hitters, heavy changers, and superspreaders), backed by theoretical analysis and extensive evaluation in software and hardware. We have published a number of papers in prestigious conferences and journals on our findings; our prototypes have also been released as open-source software.

14204117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14204117.value: Cerebral small vessel disease (SVD) is commonly presented in elderly and is considered to be associated with cognitive decline, functional loss, and increased stroke risk. Automatic identification of the major manifestations of SVD, i.e. recent small subcortical infarcts, white matter hyperintensities, lacunes, perivascular spaces, and microbleeds, would significantly improve the objectiveness of the SVD diagnosis and prognosis. In this project, a semi-supervised deep learning approach will be proposed to automatically identify the major manifestations of SVD in multimodal brain MR images. The novelties of the proposed method are summarized as follows. Firstly, a tailor-designed multi-modal input data structure is proposed to fit the architecture of 3D fully convolutional neural network. Secondly, in order to reduce the false positive and improve the detection accuracy of SVDs, an innovative deep learning structure is proposed with a nearly symmetric network structure which is ideal for handling the semantic information and localization simultaneously. In order to quantify the size of SVD lesions, a two-stage SVDs segmentation method composed of two different 3D FCNs is proposed and a dynamic weights of loss scheme to address the unbalanced-class problem. Thirdly, a new semi-supervised deep learning approach is proposed to train both the annotated and unannotated medical images. To assess the accuracy of proposed deep learning approach quantitatively by comparing with ground-truth. The application of this new method will be demonstrated in clinical researches, i.e., exploring the relationship between lesions and symptom of SVD and using as quantitative biomarkers in drug trials. 腦小血管病作為一種常見的老年疾病，被認為與認知減退，功能損失和增加腦卒中風險有密切關係。自動識別新發皮層下小梗死、腦白質高信號、腔隙、血管周圍間隙和微出血等腦小血管病的主要表現，將為腦小血管病的診斷和預後提供客觀有效的保障。在本項目中，我們將提出一種半監督的深度學習方法，以自動識別多模態腦磁力共振圖像中腦小血管病的主要表現。首先，為適應3D全卷積神經網絡的架構(Fully Convolutional Neural Network, FCN)，我們提出了一種多模態數據輸入結構。其次，為了減少假陽性，提高檢測精度，我們提出了一種新的深度學習神經網絡結構，該結構以一種近乎對稱的網絡結構來同時處理語義信息和位置信息。為了準確量化腦小血管損傷，我們提出了一種包含兩個不同3D FCN的兩階段腦小血管病分割方法。最後，一種新的半監督深度學習方法被用來訓練帶標註和未標註的醫學圖像。並通過與人工標註結果對比，定量評估該方法的準確性。該新方法的提出將為臨床探索腦小血管病病灶與症狀之間的關係及藥物試驗提供客觀有效的量化標準。

14204117.label: Realisation of objectives
14204117.value: 1. To develop a novel deep learning based approach to identifying major SVD biomarkers in multi-modal MR images. In this research, we proposed a novel 3D fully convolutional and densely connected convolutional network (3D FC-DenseNet) to automatically segment the ischemic infarct in diffusion weighted imaging, which is one of the very common imaging biomarkers in small vessel disease. We integrated dense connectivity to boost information and gradient propagation within the deep 3D model, and optimize it with Dice objective function to tackle the severe class imbalance problem. By incorporating dense connectivity and Dice loss, the difficulty in training deep 3D CNN is effectively relieved, thus our model is able to outperform state-of-the-art 2D and 3D CNN methods on a variety of metrics. Our results showed a fast, accurate and robust performance, and good potential in clinical practices, and can serve as a preliminary step in a computer aided diagnosis system. 2. To enrich the deep learning methodology in multi-modal medical image computing research by proposing an innovative network structure. We also proposed novel functional connectome analysis approaches to investigate the functional brain organization changes of elderly. For example, we combined the advantage of k-means clustering and singular value decomposition (SVD), and propose a two-step singular value decomposition to capture the dynamic patterns of the time-varying functional connectivity. The proposed approach was then used to investigate diversity of the brain in normal aging. We also investigated the functional connectome similarity of long-term married couples in elderly. These functional connectome analysis approaches could be further used to evaluate the altered brain functions of patients with cerebral small vessel diseases. 3. To solve the problem of super unbalanced classes in segmentation by proposing a two-stage SVD lesion segmentation method. We studied the prediction performance of frequently utilized feature selection and classification methods in brain abnormality grading. The diagnostic performance of sixteen feature selection and fifteen classification methods were evaluated by using two different test modes: ten-fold cross-validation and percentage split. Balanced accuracy and area under the curve (AUC) of the receiver operating characteristic were used to evaluate prediction performance. In addition, the roles of the number of selected features, feature type, MRI modality, and tumor sub-region were compared to optimize the radiomics-based prediction. The results indicated that the combination of feature selection method L1 -based linear support vector machine (L1 -SVM) and classifier multi-layer perceptron (MLPC) achieved the best performance in the differentiation of GBM and LGG in both ten-fold cross validation (balanced accuracy:0.944, AUC:0.986) and percentage split (balanced accuracy:0.953, AUC:0.981). 4. To ensure the compatibility of the proposed method by designing a new semi-supervised 3D FCN structure, which can be trained on both annotated and unannotated medical images. An automatic brain extraction framework consisted of two FCN models, i.e., a shallow FCN and an extra deep multi-scale FCN (M-FCN) was proposed. The first shallow FCN rapidly located the brain and extracted the region of interest (ROI) containing the brain. Then, within the brain ROI, the M-FCN further refined the segmentation and produced the final brain mask by leveraging the multi-scale information and residual learning blocks. Dilated convolutional layers were employed in both FCNs to control the size of feature maps and increase the field of view. Eighty-eight 2D fetal MRIs were collected for experiments. We compared our method with the state-of-the-art methods on extracting fetal brains. It has been evaluated that our proposed framework outperformed the other methods in both fetal brain localization and segmentation tasks. With the pro- posed method, we located the fetal brain with an accuracy of 100%. The brain segmentation performance was measured based on the overlap between the automatic segmentations and the manual segmentations. Our proposed method achieved an average of 0.958 Dice score, 0.950 sensitivity rate, and 0.968 precision on the testing dataset. 5. To validate the effectiveness of proposed deep learning approach in clinical research and practice, the relationship between lesions and symptom of SVD will be explored and the comparison of biomarker quantities before and after drug treatment of SVD will be conducted. We compared our method with two kinds of current state-of-the-art 3D CNN models, i.e. VoxResNet and 3D U-ResNet, and demonstrated the efficacy of our model. The qualitative evaluation in challenging cases also showed our model achieves satisfactory segmentation results. In addition, we validated the proposed 3D FC-DenseNet approach on both in-house dataset and public multi-modal MRIs dataset (ISLES2015-SSIS from MICCAI challenge dataset). The results showed a very competitive performance of our model on various metrics (Dice similarity coefficient: 79.13%, lesionwise precision: 92.67%, and lesionwiseF1 score: 89.25%), and demonstrated the good potential of our model in clinical routines.

14204117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14204117.value: In this project, we investigated the automatic segmentation of major MR imaging manifestations of small vessel disease. We developed a series of deep learning methods and studied the related technical issues and clinical applications of these automatic methods. These methods will enable automatic generation of quantitative evidence of CSVD. With these objective evidences, better understanding of the underlying mechanism of CSVD could be achieved, which will further enable improved quality of clinical management of this very common brain abnormality in the aging population.

14204417.label: Project Objectives
14204417.value: Develop a new incremental sheet metal bending method based on the minimum energy principle and the model-less control. The method can bend a sheet metal plate step-by-step to form any 3D free-form part efficiently and accurately. Additionally, the entire operation is automated without human intervention. Investigate the formation and minimization of the residual stress of the part and accordingly, further optimize the presented incremental sheet metal bending method. This will further improve the part quality demanded by high-end applications such as building of submarines and LNG containers. Investigate the practical engineering issues such as the slip of the sheet metal plate and the trimming of the part after bending. This will pave the road for commercialization in the near future. Forest two Ph.D. students who will become the leading researchers with hands-on experience.

14204417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14204417.value: 3D free-form sheet metal bending is a common manufacturing process used in many heavy industries such as shipbuilding and making of chemical engineering equipment. The traditional method is the so-called line heating method, which is not only laborious but also inefficient and error-prone. There have been some attempts in developing automated methods including the multi-point forming method, the roll forming method and the laser forming method; however, the success has been limited. This proposal presents a new incremental bending method based on the minimum energy principle and the model-less control method. First, the part is approximated by a series of strips connected through virtual springs. Next, by applying the minimum energy principle, the pressing point and the supporting points are calculated for each strips. Then, the deformation of the strips and the effect of the springback are computed. Because of the variations of the sheet metal blanks (e.g., the material properties and the flatness) as well as the process conditions (e.g., the slip of the sheet metal plate), forming errors are inevitable. Thus, following the model-less control method, the errors are measured and compensated. The new method is being tested on a 50 KN custom-made incremental bending machine. For a sheet metal of 1000 x 800 x 5 mm, the average forming error is only 2.1 mm and the production time is just 18 min. Comparing to the existing methods, the new method has a number of advantages. First, using the minimum energy principle, it only bends where it needs to be bent and hence, is very efficient. Second, because of the minimum energy, it requires only a small machine and hence, is simple and reliable. Third, using the model-less control with vision-based feedback, it can compensate the forming error on-line and hence, is fast and precise. In the project, a number of theoretical and practical issues will be further investigated including the residual stress of the formed parts, the slip of the sheet metal plate and the trimming of the formed parts. Solving these problems will further improve the product quality and productivity paving the road to commercialization. Presently, 3D free-form sheet metal bending is a bottleneck problem in the industry. The presented research can solve this problem and hence, significantly advances the industry. The positive economic gain and societal influence will then follow. 3D自由曲面金屬板彎板成形是重工業（如造船及化學工程設備的製造）中常用的製造工藝。傳統的方法是人工的水火法,不僅費力,而且效率低下、容易出錯。近年來有一些自動化的嘗試,包括多點成形方法，多點滾壓成形方法和鐳射成形方法;然而,這些方法各有缺點。我們基於最小能量原理和無模型控制方法提出了一種新的步進彎曲方法。首先我們把金屬板材離散化成一系列由虛擬彈簧連接的樣條。接著用最小能量原理計算每個樣條的壓下點和支撐點。然後計算樣條的變形和回彈。由於金屬板材的差異（例如,材料特性和平坦度）以及工藝條件的差異（例如壓頭和支撐點的滑移之間的摩擦），成形誤差難以避免。因此我們按照無模型控制方法，對誤差進行測量和補償。我們在一台特製的50KN樣機上進行了測試。對於800x600x5 毫米的板材，平均成型誤差僅為1.2 毫米，生產時間僅為18分鐘。與現有方法相比,新方法具有多個優點：首先，它使用最小能量原理，僅彎曲需要彎曲的位置,因此非常高效。第二，由於能量最小,機床變得簡單可靠。第三，它使用基於視覺的回饋無模型控制,可以即時補償成形誤差，快速且準確。 在本研究中我們將進一步深入研究一系列理論和實踐問題,包括板材成形後的殘餘應力，成形零件的修整等。解決這些問題將進一步提高產品質量，從而實現商業化。目前3D自由曲面金屬板彎板成形是行業的一個瓶頸問題。本研究將解決這個問題，推動行業的發展。

14204417.label: Realisation of objectives
14204417.value: (1) Developed a new incremental sheet metal bending method based on the minimum energy principle and the model-less control method. The method would bend a sheet metal plate step by step to from any 3D free-form part efficiently and accurately. First we discretize the metal plate into a series of strips. After discretization, the metal plate could be descried by these strips. The strip number is determined by several aspects such as the shape, size and material of the metal plate. For a given plate, if its shape is complex, more strips should be discretized. For example, for a single curvature plate or variable curvature plate less strips are needed. For a saddle shape plate more strips are needed. The size of the plate also plays an important role. If the size is large more strips, of course, are needed. For each strip, the minimum energy principle is applied to calculate the punching and supporting positions. At each bending step, the shape error between the current strip and the designed shape is calculated. The current strip can be predicted mathematically or measured using computer vision. According to the minimum energy principle, the punching position is at the maximum point of the shape error, and the supporting position is at the minimum point of the shape error. The process repeats until the shape error is within the tolerance. In each bending step, the deformation is relatively small and hence Euler-Bernoulli beam theory is used to compute the bending. We have carried out a lot of experiments. Different kinds of 3D free-form metal plates have been manufactured such as simple curvature workpiece and variable curvature workpiece. One of the big advantages of the method is its low forming force. During the forming process, no blank holder is used. The metal plate is only bent to its designed shape. The bending force would be not very large compared with conventional incremental forming method, in which the sheet metal is stretched and bent locally. (2) Investigated the formation and the residual stress of the part. Since using of the minimum energy principle, the forming force is quite small at each bending step. We have used the finite element analysis to explore the bending procedure. The implicit algorithm was used to simulate the bending and its springback. The finite model was constructed by four-node shell element. The material model was selected as piece-wise linear isotropic plasticity model. Its stress-strain curve was measured by tensile test. The boundary condition was defined as the actual bending procedure. The stress around the bending strips was much larger than other areas. The punching force is relatively small. (3) Investigated the practical engineering application of the forming method. The method aims at making 3D free-form part. As in practical application like ship building industry, the huge metal plate is always welded by several relatively small pieces. The dimension accuracy along the edge of the metal plate would be a key aspect, which determines whether the plates can be welded together. We have manufactured a huge wall structure by 8 small pieces. Each of the small pieces is a variable curvature metal plate. Their shapes are different. The size of each plate is 900 × 700 mm. The two adjacent plates are welded by spot welding. It is noted that the surface of the wall is smooth enough. The curvature of the wall is also different along the surface. (4) Forest two Ph.D. students who will become the leading researchers with hands-on experience. Two Ph.D. students supported by this project have graduated from the Department of Mechanical and Automation Engineering in The Chinese University of Hong Kong. They are Dr. Dang Xiaobing and Dr Xie Fengran. In addition, another Mphil student Thomas Kowk supported by this project have graduated and received a PhD position in NUS with NGS scholarship.

14204417.label: Major findings and research outcome
14204417.value: In this research, a new incremental bending method to form 3D free-form metal plate is presented. The new method is a good use of the minimum energy principle. It gives several advantages over the existing methods. First, it is more flexible. The entire forming process is controlled by programming the positions of the punching tools and the supporting pillars. Second, it is cost-effective. Because of the use of the minimum energy principle, the required forming force is much smaller. Consequently, the machine can be much simpler and smaller, and the cost to build such a machine is much reduced. Third, because of low forming force, the forming process is efficient resulting in much reduced energy consumption and machine maintenance. The idea of Bending Limit Diagram (BLD) is introduced. BLD predicts whether a bending step can be carried out successfully. At each bending step, the bending operation should lie between the minimum bending ellipse and the maximum bending ellipse. If the bending operation is less than the minimum bending ellipse, only elastic bending exists and the plate would recover to its original shape after the bending punch. On the other hand, if the bending operation is beyond the maximum bending ellipse, plastic hinge would develop. This is particularly important for bending complex 3D free form plate, such as saddle shape plate and the bowl shape plate. BLD can also be used in various metal plate bending processes including the traditional line heating method. Extensive experiments have been carried out to test the new method. The tested 3D free form sheet metal can be divided into four kinds: the single curvature plate, the variable curvature plate, the saddle shape plate and the bowl shape plate . All the formed plates are of high quality with a smooth surface and no visible defects such as punching dimple and plastic hinge. For the single curvature plate and the variable curvature plate , the average operation time is about 20 minutes. For the saddle shape plate and the bowl shape plate, the average forming time is about 3 to 4 hours, as much smaller incremental steps are needed. The new method has a great potential for industrial applications. It is not only technically effective but also economically effective. It can solve the bottleneck problem of bending 3D free form metal plate and will benefit many heavy industry sectors, such as ship building, chemical process equipment building, and etc.

14204417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14204417.value: For industrial applications that requires large and thick metal pate, a much large machine is needed. Our team has designed a 6000 kN machine. It can only form a metal plate with the maximum size of 3000 × 2000 × 30 mm. In the ship manufacturing and other applications, much bigger metal plates would be needed to reduce the assembly. For practical applications, the consideration is the irregular shape metal plate. For example, an irregular metal plate may has a long edge in one side and a short side in the other side. In this case trimming will be necessary. There are two possible methods: bending - trimming and trimming - bending. The later could be more effective but create more challenges. For example, the effect of the supports and the models of the virtual springs. These issues would need to be investigated in the future.

14204417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14204417.value: Metal plate bending is a common manufacturing process applied in many industrial sectors such as shipbuilding, chemical engineering and shell structure construction. This project presents a new incremental bending method to form 3D free form metal plate. The new method has a number of advantages. First, because of the use of minimum energy principle, the bending force is minimized. As a result, the forming machine can be made much smaller and simpler. Additionally, the bending operation becomes much more efficient and stable. Second, using the BLD, one can predict the behavior of the bending operation and hence, avoid the forming defects, such as punching dimple and plastic hinge. Third, because of the use of the vision-based model-less control scheme, the forming error can be compensated online to achieve better workpiece quality. 3D free form metal plate bending is a bottleneck problem in industry. The new method can solve this problem. With further refinements, it is expected that the new method will be used in the shop floor in the near future bring in positive economic gain for the industry.

14204917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14204917.value: To fulfill the power-supply requirements for SoC designs, multi-supply-voltage approach is well adopted. The supply voltages can be simply generated by different dc-dc converters such as buck/boost converters, low-dropout regulator and charge-pump circuit. Conventional buck/boost converters are most acceptable due to their high power efficiency. However, the required external inductors enlarge the required PCB area and increase production cost. Single-inductor multiple-output buck-boost dc-dc converter is able to provide multiple step up/down output voltages with only one inductor. However, efficiency, as well as self- and cross-regulations among different output channels are major specifications to further improve. In this project, a dual-inductor multiple-output (DIMO) buck-boost dc-dc converter is proposed. The goal of this project is to improve the attenuation performance of cross-regulation, as well as to enhance the self-regulation by an auxiliary power stage with a much smaller inductor’s value for transient enhancement. 為了滿足SoC設計的電源要求，多電源電壓方式已被採用。電源電壓可以由不同的DC-DC轉換器，例如降壓/升壓轉換器、低壓差穩壓器和電荷泵電路，簡單地產生。傳統的降壓和升壓轉換器由於其高功率而是最可接受的。然而，所需的外部電感器卻增加了所需的PCB面積，並增加了生產成本。 單電感多輸出DC-DC電源轉換器只有一個電感來提供多個升壓/降壓輸出電壓。但是，不同輸出通道的自我和交規調節是進一步去改善的主要規範。在這個項目中提出了一種雙電感多輸出降壓/升壓型DC-DC轉換器。該項目的目標是利用較小的電感和輔助功率級來提升交規調節和自我調節。

14204917.label: Realisation of objectives
14204917.value: The project is completed successfully. All objectives have been achieved. The proposed DIMO buck-boost dc-dc converter is developed. One version is on PCB-level controlled by a FPGA board (Objective 1), and another version is implemented in TSMC 65-nm CMOS technology (Objective 2). For the DIMO buck-boost dc-dc converter on PCB-level, it is firstly designed using MATLAB and Simulink. Uncompensated transfer functions in z-domain are obtained via discrete-time modelling. Voltage and current compensators are designed in s-domain using bilinear transformation. Non-ideal factors such as quantization error, finite bit-length and time-delay are added into the Simulink model to verify the design. Control algorithm is then implemented with Verilog modules. Terasic DE1-SoC FPGA is chosen as the hardware controller. The Verilog code is compiled and synthesized using Quartus Prime without any timing violation for the designed Verilog modules. Verilog modules are verified using Co-Simulation as the interface between Simulink and ModelSim. The modules are programmed into DE1-SoC once their functionalities have been verified. High-side power switches are implemented using ON Semiconductor FDS6875, while low-side switches are implemented using ON Semiconductor FDS9926A. The drivers are implemented using Texas Instruments UCC27424D. Two pairs of RC-filter are placed on each side of the inductor to sense its current based on an estimated value of its DCR. The output of each filter is fed to an instrumentation amplifier implemented with Texas Instruments INA849 to amplify the differential signal in order to achieve a 1:1 I-to-V gain. The sensed inductor current is sent to a passive low-pass filter to drive an ADC for feedback control. The whole discrete current sensor is designed using PSpice for TI. Voltage at each output channel is sensed using resistive feedback network. Texas Instruments TLV272 in unity-gain configuration is used as buffer to drive the respective ADC with the sensed signal. All ADCs in this design are implemented using Texas Instruments ADS7884. The digitalized sensed output voltage along with the digitalized sensed inductor current are fed to the GPIO port of DE1-SoC as input signals for the controller. The obtained results reveal and verify the improvement of transient-response performance with the proposed structure. For the DIMO buck-boost dc-dc converter implemented in TSMC 65-nm CMOS technology, the master and salve stages use two inductors, which one is large (4.7uH) and the other is small (470nH), as proposed. The overall chip area is 2500um x 1000um. Two inductor current sensors are needed in this DIMO design (i.e., one for main stage and another for slave stage). Conventional sense-FET-based current sensor is adopted for the master power stage. Yet, its inherent problems are (1) loop performance variations in different loads, and (2) undesired glitches during mode transitions are not solved in the previously reported works. To solve these problems, a piecewise-linear adaptive-bias generator is proposed and implemented to suppress the variations in sensing loops, and the switching sequence is specially designed to achieve the continuous mode transition. When it comes to the slave stage, the previously mentioned senseFET method is not suitable for this high-speed operation. To solve this problem, an online-calibration hybrid current sensor, which combines the senseFET-based and integration-based current sensing methods, is designed. By integrating the voltage across the inductor, the proposed hybrid current sensor achieves accurate and continuous sensing without glitches during the switching transitions. The integration error is periodically calibrated by an assisted sense-FET-based current sensor, which operates at most thrice every 8 switching cycles and hence it does not need continuous operation of the power-hungry high gain-bandwidth amplifier. To achieve the digital control in this DIMO project, both the inductor currents (i.e., slave inductor and master inductor) and multiple output voltages are required to be sampled and converted to digital signals. In the previously reported works, parallel individual ADCs or single time-multiplexing ADC are utilized. Obviously, large die area and more power consumption are required if multiple independent ADCs are used. On the other hand, time-multiplexing ADC can only quantize the voltages once at a time sequentially, which greatly extends overall conversion time. Therefore, the delay in digital control loop is increased, which decreases the phase margin and worsen the stability. To overcome these limitations, a multi-phase time-interleaved ADC with single shared cycling delay line capable of simultaneous quantization for high-frequency digital-control single-inductor-multiple-output dc-dc converters is proposed. The ADC achieves the conversion by voltage-time conversion and time-digital-conversion. Benefited from the shared cycling delay line structure, 7-bit resolution for each channel is achieved with only 8 delay cells. Hence, the die area and mismatch among delay cells are reduced. Together with 2-phase time-interleaved mothed, the sample rate is doubled with no extra delay cells required. Moreover, simultaneous quantization for multi-channel is achieved by converting all sampled voltages into time domain with the common ramp signal in each phase. For Objective 3, the possibility to further increase switching frequency has been investigated. It is found that it is not a good solution to further improve transient responses by this approach. The main reason is due to the speed limitation of inductor-current sensor to extract the exact waveforms of the inductor currents at high frequency since the accuracy of the sensor is dramatically degraded at high frequency. In conclusion, we have proven that the proposed DIMO buck-boost dc-dc converter can enhance the self-regulation and reduce cross-regulation, when comparing to the conventional SIMO structure.
