14204917.label: Major findings and research outcome
14204917.value: The development of proposed DIMO structure requires advanced development of SIMO structure, inductor-current sensor, high-gain high-speed error amplifier, bootstrapped gate driver and internal regulation for digital controller. We have developed the afore-mentioned circuits and published the ideas and results. The details are listed below. We have developed a SIMO structure with a new control scheme to reduce cross- and self-regulation. The related works are “A Single-Inductor Multiple-Output Buck/Boost DC-DC Converter with Duty-Cycle and Control-Current Predictor” published in IEEE Transactions on Power Electronics, and “Single-Inductor Multiple-Output DC-DC Converter with Duty-Cycle-Constrained Comparator Control” published in Electronics Letters. We have developed several novel inductor-current sensor circuits. The related works are “Adaptive-Biased Sense-FET-Based Inductor-Current Sensor for 10-MHz Buck Converter” published in International Journal of Circuit Theory and Applications, “Full-Wave Sense-FET-Based Inductor-Current Sensor with Wide Dynamic Range for Buck Converters” published in IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems II, and one work published in IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits. For the development of high-gain high-speed error amplifier for control loop, the related work is “Bandwidth and Slew Rate Enhanced OTA with Sustainable Dynamic Bias” published in IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems II. Moreover, there are 3 works published in IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits. To reduce the on-resistance of power transistor with small size, N-MOSFET is used but a high gate voltage generated by bootstrapped gate drivers is required. Thus, we have conducted some research on charge pump to potentially develop a new bootstrapped gate driver. The related works are “A Dual-Power-Path Charge Pump for Solar-Energy Harvesting” published in International Journal of Circuit Theory and Applications and “Optimization of Charge Pump Based on Piecewise Modeling of Output-Voltage Ripple” published in Energies. The regulated supply for internal digital controller is generated by low-dropout regulators. We have developed several new structures. The related works are “Low-dropout Regulator with Dual Cross-coupled Current Mirrors” published in International Journal of Circuit Theory and Applications, “A Flipped-Voltage-Follower-Based Low-Dropout Regulator with Signal- and Transient-Current Boosting” published in Analog Integrated Circuits and Signal Processing, “A Hybrid Low-Dropout Regulator with Load Regulation Correction” published and “An Analog-Assisted Digital LDO With Dynamic-Biasing Asynchronous Comparator” accepted by IEEE Access. All designs have been verified by simulations and/or experimental results. They show significant performance improvements over conventional designs. In conclusion, 10 journal papers are published and 1 journal is accepted. Moreover, 5 conference papers are presented.

14204917.value: There is a possibility to use the bondwire and IC package’s mutual inductance effect to replace the small off-chip inductor used in the slave stage. However, the resistance of bondwire and IC package may cause additional conduction loss which degrades the overall efficiency of the dc-dc converter. To develop this research direction, more analyses on the generated inductance from different combinations of arrangement of bondwire and IC package are required. Moreover, the reliability and parameters' variations are two key issues needed to be addressed carefully.

14205117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14205117.value: Similarity of entities in graphs plays a key role in data analysis and mining. SimRank is a widely used and popular measurement to evaluate the similarity among the vertices. The idea behind is that similar objects are linked to objects that are similar. This is a recursive concept, since the neighboring similar objects are themselves linked to other similar objects, and so on. The base case is that an object is the most similar to itself. In real life applications, graphs not only grow in size, requiring fast and precise SimRank computation for large graphs, but also change and evolve continuously over time, demanding an efficient maintenance process to handle dynamic updates. In this project, we study a random walk based indexing approach to compute SimRank efficiently and accurately over large dynamic graphs. Our preliminary study shows that this approach has the potential to outperform the state-of-the-art static and dynamic SimRank algorithms for both static and dynamic graphs.

14205117.label: Realisation of objectives
14205117.value: The first objective is to propose a new approximation algorithm for SimRank with probabilistic guarantees that better match the expected user requirements with respect to dynamic graphs. We already proposed new approximate algorithms for this problem meeting this objective requirement. The second objective is to show experimental results on large datasets to illustrate the performance of the proposed methods. We already did experiments to illustrate the performance of the proposed methods.

14205117.label: Major findings and research outcome
14205117.value: The first objective is to propose a new approximation algorithm for SimRank with probabilistic guarantees that better match the expected user requirements with respect to dynamic graphs. There are different types of user requirements. One example is that the user would like to know the similarity between two entities based on not only the structural information but also the textual information of entities. We proposed efficient algorithms and published results in [C1, C2]. Another example is that the user would like to know the similarity between two entities when both the spatial information and the textual information of entities are known. We also proposed approximate algorithms and published results in [C3]. The third example is that the user would like to know the similarity between two entities when the user is asked with his/her preferences via some interactive questions, whose results were published in [C4, C6]. The fourth example is that the user would like to be interested in frequent entities only, whose results were published in [C5]. The fifth example is that the user would like to be interested in similarities between two images where images are particular examples of entities. We focused on this problem and proposed efficient methods, whose results could be found in [C7, C8]. The second objective is to show experimental results on large datasets to illustrate the performance of the proposed methods. All of the studies discussed before [C1-C8] were conducted with experiments on large datasets.

14205117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14205117.value: There are further developments of the research studied in this project. Since the problem studied in this project is to study the similarity between any two entities/users in graphs like social network analysis, it is expected that a lot of social network companies are interested in the results of this project. In addition, social network data (e.g., facebook data) becomes much larger nowadays. It is interesting to study how our proposed method could handle larger data in a distributed manner (e.g., cloud computing).

14205117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14205117.value: [Nature] Similarity of entities in graphs plays a key role in data analysis and mining. SimRank is a widely used and popular measurement to evaluate the similarity among the vertices. In this project, we study an efficient approach to compute SimRank efficiently and accurately over large dynamic graphs. [Significance and Values] SimRank is an important measure of object-to-object similarity. It involves a recursive definition that objects are similar when they are linked to similar objects. Such a measure is important for social network analysis, spam detection, data mining on graph data including the web and social networks, and collaborative filtering in recommender systems. Furthermore, the findings of our project are expected to promote considerably the community’s understanding of using SimRank, which, in turn, may lead to the discovery of new methodologies and even research areas.

14205217.label: Project Objectives
14205217.value: To establish a network theory for decoupling two coupled antennas as the foundation work for the "self-curing" decoupling scheme. With the theory, one can resolve two things: the locations of "acupuncture points" on coupled antennas for applying appropriate reactive decoupling loads; and the values of the reactive components at the points, with which the mutual coupling between two coupled antennas can be reduced significantly. To investigate the existence conditions for acupuncture points and required reactive loads for decoupling three most commonly used antenna forms, namely loop antennas, semi-loop antennas and microstrip patch antennas. In addition to satisfying the decoupling conditions, other antenna properties, such as bandwidth, radiation efficiency, and radiation patterns should be maintained or improved. To verify the proposed “self-curing” decoupling scheme and to demonstrate its impact to a MIMO wireless terminal in a multipath channel condition by two measures: a SCME channel model simulation platform for assessing the channel capacity of a MIMO system with MIMO antennas; and a measurement platform for data throughput of a smart phone equipped with a MIMO array antenna in PI’s MIMO OTA lab. In both theoretical and experimental verifications, a MIMO array antenna and its decoupled version using the proposed decoupling scheme will be designed, fabricated and measured for comparison.

14205217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14205217.value: Multiple antenna techniques are widely used in wireless communication systems. Two commonly used multiple antenna technologies are spatial diversity antenna technology and spatial multiplexing, or Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO), antenna technology. MIMO technology is a paramount means nowadays for LTE smart phones and Wi-Fi modules. Due to the compact volume of a mobile terminal, severe mutual couplings among the multiple antennas will impose a significant negative impact on the system performance and diminish the benefits brought by the multiple antenna technologies. Therefore, developing an effective decoupling technology that is easy to implement in a wireless terminal has become a very important issue in the wireless industry in recent years. Very recently, an astonishing “self-curing” decoupling phenomenon between two Inverted F Antennas (IFA) is discovered in PI’s group. An effective decoupling can be achieved by introducing a capacitive load at an “acupuncture point” (also called acupoint in Chinese medicine) of the shorting arm of each of the two coupled IFA antennas. It is called “self-curing” as there is no any physical inter-connection or a dummy antenna element between the coupled IFA antennas, nor defection on the ground plane as required in many existing decoupling methods. This proposed research will focus on systematic development of the “self-curing” decoupling concept and its applications to MIMO antenna arrays in various practical antenna forms, including loop antennas, semi-loop antennas, and microstrip patch antennas. The research covers the foundation theory for the new decoupling method, the practical implementations on real antenna forms for smart phones and system level assessment in a realistic channel model theoretically and experimentally. The new decoupling technique will possess the following unique features as compared to all the existing decoupling approaches: 1) No any interconnecting circuit or electromagnetic structure is required between coupled antennas; in other words, decoupling devices will be only affiliated to coupled antennas; 2) The antenna impedance matching bandwidth will be increased while the mutual coupling being reduced; 3) The decoupling device is a simple discrete component and occupies nearly no extra space; 4) The decoupling device is frequency insensitive and very suitable for low frequency applications; and 5) The decoupling scheme can be easily extended to dual band array antennas. 14205217.label: Realisation of objectives
14205217.value: Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) technology has been widely used in today’s wireless communication systems, from base stations to Wi-Fi modules and various mobile terminals such as smartphones and tablets. A key front-end module for adopting MIMO technology is to use multiple antennas at each end of the communication. By using multiple antennas, a MIMO system sends and receives more than one data signal streams simultaneously over the same radio channel by utilizing uncorrelated channel paths in a multipath environment. To accommodate the high demands of a high number of antennas on a smartphone, new design challenges must be confronted. One of the thorny issues is how to reduce the mutual coupling among tightly packed antennas that are attached to a compact circuit board, which is full of densely populated surface mounted electronic components. The self-curing decoupling technique is a brand new concept conceived and developed by the PI’s research group in antenna theory. The technique can effectively reduce the mutual coupling among closely co-located antennas for wireless terminals without introducing noticeably overhead. The technique is developed in two stages: In stage 1, the decoupling technique only solved the decoupling problem between Inverted F-antenna (IFA), which is the most popular antenna form for wireless terminals. With the self-curing decoupling technique, only a capacitive load on the shorting arm of each coupled IFA is required without connecting a circuitry or inserting a physical structure between the two coupled antennas. The capacitive load occupies very little space and is frequency insensitive therefore the decoupling technique is a very favorable choice for low frequency applications. Network analysis model is developed to mathematically justify the working mechanism and to provide a design guideline. Various practical cases of two IFAs sitting at different positions on the periphery of a PCB board are studied to validate the effectiveness of the technique. The experimental results show that with the decoupling technique significant improvements in the port isolation (from 10 dB to 20 dB), antenna correlation coefficient (from 0.25 to 0.05), multiplexing efficiency (from 46 % to 60 %) and above all the system throughput (1.2 dB and 0.8 dB power saving in UMi and UMa channels, respectively) can be obtained. In stage 2, the self-curing decoupling technique is substantially extended to decoupling of general form of MIMO antenna arrays in mobile terminals. Using the technique, the mutual coupling between antennas can be reduced by inlaying lumped element capacitors on the ground plane. The decoupling method does not require any physical connection or obstruction between coupled antennas. It has been theoretically and experimentally validated that the decoupling technique can be applied to IFAs, monopole antennas, loop antennas, and a MIMO array with mixed antenna types. The working mechanism of the self-curing decoupling method is revealed and justified through the partial element equivalent circuit model. 14205217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14205217.value: A new antenna technology called self-curing decoupling technique is proposed, theoretically developed and experimentally validated for decoupling of general form of MIMO antenna arrays in mobile terminals. Antenna forms include Inverted F Antennas (IFAs), monopole antennas, loop antennas, and a MIMO array with mixed antenna types. Using the technique, the mutual coupling between antennas can be reduced by inlaying lumped element capacitors on the ground plane. The decoupling method does not require any physical connection or obstruction between coupled antennas. The working mechanism of the self-curing decoupling method has been mathematically revealed and justified through the partial element equivalent circuit modeling. The experimental results show that significant improvements in port isolation (from 9 dB to 30 dB), total efficiency (from 53 % to 69 %), and above all, the system data throughput can be achieved. The significance of the research project is fourfold: (1) it developed an effective decoupling method for wireless terminals that is suitable for a wide range of antenna types, including IFAs, monopole antennas, and loop antennas, which are the most three commonly-used antenna forms for mobile terminals; (2) it attracted great attention from the industry; (3) it generates valuable Ips (two granted US patents and one pending Chinese patent); and (4) it trains a number of high caliber talent graduate students.

14205617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14205617.value: This project proposes to design and develop a natural language based interactive system to query large knowledge graphs effectively and efficiently. The continuously growing knowledge graphs, e.g., DBpedia, Yago, and IMDB, have attracted extensive attention, since more and more real-life data have been collected and maintained in a natural and intuitive way, i.e., using a triple (subject, predicate, object) to describe a fact. However, providing an easy and effective mechanism to access knowledge graphs is a very challenging problem. Although keyword search has achieved great success in retrieving the related web pages from millions of unstructured documents, it is not expressive enough to query structured knowledge graphs since only a small number of words are used to specify the query intention. At the other extreme, the structural query language, e.g., SPARQL and GraphQL, is highly expressive to retrieve data precisely, but it is very difficult for end users to use because (1) The structural query language has complicated syntax in general; and (2) A user is required to have sufficient knowledge about the underlying knowledge graph, that is, the structure of data, the vocabulary (entity, predicate, type) used within the knowledge graph, etc. This motivates us to design an easy-to-use system to query knowledge graphs effectively and efficiently. Recently, natural language has been used to query databases (including both relational data and graph data), as it provides a simple yet powerful way for users to describe the query intention. However, due to the inherent ambiguities of natural language, it is not an easy task for the machine to understand the input question precisely and generate the correct structural query. In our daily communication, if one person does not understand the meaning of a question, she will try to ask some questions back to the asker to make it clear. Enlightened by this interactive process, we propose to design a natural language based system that understands the query intention and performs query processing through interactions with users. Such a system will make it easy for end users to query knowledge graphs and acquire useful knowledge. It will also increase the usability of the existing huge knowledge graphs. 本項目計劃設計和開發一個用自然語言來查詢知識圖譜的交互系統。那些持續增長的知識圖譜，例如DBpedia、Yago和IMDB, 引起了很多關注，因為越來越多的真實生活中的數據在知識圖譜中以一種自然的方式被收集和管理，即是用三元組 (主語，謂詞，賓語) 的形式來描述一個事實。然而如何用一種簡單而有效的機制來訪問知識圖譜仍然是一個很有挑戰性的問題。儘管關鍵字查詢能夠成功地從數以百萬計的非結構化文檔中檢索相關的網頁，這一技術並不具有足夠的表達能力來查詢結構化的知識圖譜，這是因為關鍵字查詢只用很少的詞來表達查詢意圖。另一方面，結構化的查詢語言，例如SPARQL和GraphQL, 有很強的表達能力來精確地查詢數據，但是卻因為以下兩個原因很難被普通用戶使用: (1) 結構化的查詢語言通常有很複雜的語法; (2) 而且用戶需要對底層的知識圖譜有足夠的瞭解，包括它的結構以及所使用的詞彙 (實體、謂詞、類別) 等。這些因素促使我們開發一套易用、高效的系統來支持對知識圖譜的查詢。 近年來，自然語言因其能為普通的用戶提供一種簡單卻又強大的方式來描述查詢意圖，已經被用來查詢數據庫 (包括關係型數據庫和圖數據)。然而，由於自然語言本身所固有的歧義性，讓機器準確地理解所輸入的問題並生成正確的結構化查詢並不是一件容易的任務。在我們日常的交流中，如果一個人不明白另一個人所說的意思，她會通過反問一些問題的方式來弄清其中的意思。受到這個交互過程的啟發，我們設計一個通過與用戶交互的方式來理解查詢意圖並且進行查詢處理的自然語言問答系統。這個系統支持用戶非常容易地查詢知識圖譜從而獲取知識，同時也會提高現有的大規模知識圖譜的可用性。

14205617.label: Realisation of objectives
14205617.value: All project objectives have been achieved satisfactorily with rich and comprehensive research output. The realisation of each objective is described below. 1. We designed an interactive, user-friendly, general solution framework to effectively and efficiently query large knowledge graphs using natural language questions. The framework takes a natural language query from a user, and applies the following steps to find answers to the query: generating mapping phrases from the knowledge graph, building a basic graph pattern for the query, interacting with the user to eliminate ambiguity, and evaluating the structured query on the knowledge graph. 2. We built a dictionary of synonymous phrases from two well-known resources: WordNet and Wikipedia. We used the following mechanism to collect synonymous phrases: There is a special link "redirected from" between Wikipedia articles, which indicates that the entities refer to the identical one. Moreover, we can also extract the synonym based on some rules (e.g., "commonly known as", "abbreviated"). The constructed dictionary contains 2,506,368 groups of synonymous phrases. It becomes a very useful dictionary for the question answering task we studied; in addition, it can also benefit other tasks involving phrase understanding such as machine reading comprehension, text generation, and knowledge graph reasoning. 3. We evaluated the proposed solution on a real knowledge graph DBpedia. It is an open-domain knowledge base, which contains 21,205,271 vertices (6,653,242 entities, 381,425 concepts, and 14,170,604 literals) and 155,385,713 triples (i.e., edges). Our method can achieve an F-1 score of 0.81, compared with 0.42 by GAnswer and 0.61 by GATemplate, which are two state-of-the-art methods in the literature. Through the experimental study, we demonstrate the usefulness of our method. Carefully designed user studies confirm that casual users are able to query knowledge graphs effectively in practice.

14205617.label: Major findings and research outcome
14205617.value: The research outcome is as follows. Overall, there are 7 journal papers and 6 conference papers published from the research investigations in this project. 2 PhD students and 1 postdoctoral researcher were trained over the project duration. The major findings are, using natural language to query knowledge graph is an intuitive and user-friendly way. In contrast, structured query languages, such as SPARQL, are difficult to use due to its complex syntax, and keywords are simple but have a very limited expression ability. Although natural language question (NLQ) is promising on querying knowledge graphs, a huge challenge is how to understand the question clearly so as to translate the unstructured question into a structured query. In our solution, we designed a novel framework which applies the following steps to find answers to the query: generating mapping phrases from the knowledge graph, building a basic graph pattern for the query, interacting with the user to eliminate ambiguity, and evaluating the structured query on the knowledge graph. To reduce the interaction cost with users, we formalized an interaction problem and design an efficient strategy to solve the problem. To improve the efficiency, we proposed a query prefetch technique by exploiting the latency in the interactions with users. The research results have been published in CIKM Conference 2017 and Information Sciences 2019. In addition, we noticed the gap between unstructured natural language and structured data makes it challenging to build a system that supports using natural language to query large knowledge graphs. To address this problem, we proposed a novel systematic method to understand natural language questions by using a large number of binary templates rather than semantic parsers. We designed a low-cost approach that can build a huge number of templates automatically. To reduce the search space, we carefully devised an index to facilitate the online template decomposition. Moreover, we designed effective strategies to perform the two-level disambiguations (i.e., entity-level ambiguity and structure-level ambiguity) by considering the query semantics. This research result has been published in PVLDB 2018. Our other publications, e.g., those focusing on subgraph matching, subgraph counting, subgraph isomorphism are also related to the project as they are used as basic operations in the framework, i.e., subgraph matching between the structured query and the knowledge graph.

14205617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14205617.value: With the rapid evolution and growth of knowledge graph in various application fields, and the growing need of inquiry from users, we believe there will be more opportunities and challenges arising from this prosperous field. Thus there is a lot of potential for further investigation in this direction. Based on our current research findings and expertise, we can continue to address new challenges. As a particular example, we may incorporate users' past query log to identify the context and eliminate ambiguity. We may also ask for user feedback to the query results which can be used as supervised information to improve our question answering system. These are potential directions for further development.

14205617.value: The continuously growing knowledge graphs, e.g., DBpedia, Yago, and IMDB, contain rich information about real-world entities, facts and relationships between entities. This project proposes to design and develop a natural language based interactive system to query large knowledge graphs effectively and efficiently. With our designed solution, end users can use natural language to express their queries to knowledge graphs without the need to learn complex SPARQL syntax. The system can automatically understand the natural language questions and provide answers to the users. Such a system will make it easy for end users to query knowledge graphs and acquire useful knowledge. It will also increase the usability of the existing huge knowledge graphs.

14205717.value: 我們計劃研究一個新穎的算法框架來解決單純體結構矩陣分解問題（simplex-structured matrix factorization, SSMF）。SSMF 是一類結構矩陣分解問題 （structured matrix factorization, SMF），其係數向量被限制在單位單純體中。此問題及其相關技術已在不同領域的重要問題中得到了應用，例如遙感裡的高光譜分離，機器學習裡的文檔分類和主題發現等等。因此，無論是在算法還是理論上，理解 SSMF問題對解決廣泛的工程和科學問題都有著重大影響。目前相關研究主要集中在確定性 SSMF技術上，而我們關注的是一個更具挑戰性，但也更有潛力的統計框架。我們會先建立一個概率數據模型，並把現實存在的問題，如噪聲，異常，和多模數據行為等，納入模型之中。之後，再提出一個從統計估計理論上能有效解決 SSMF的隨機最大似然（maximum-likelihood, ML）框架。涉及的 ML問題是一個困難的隨機優化問題。我們會開發一套隨機優化方法來解決，並探討這個高性能 SSMF框架在應用方面能帶來多大的提升，特別是一些（需要更強大的技術才能取得滿意效果的）前沿問題。例如在高光譜成像中的多光譜數據融合和多時相數據分析，在線數據分類（ 如對於Twitter 和 Facebook上的帖子），和多路傳感器數據分析。我們還會通過統計性能分析來了解 SSMF的理論極限。這份 研究計劃結合了統計估計，隨機優化，和 SMF 的技術與應用，我們期望在實用性和理論性上都取得顯著性成果。整個研究將由三名相關領域的專家帶領（一名負責人和兩名協助者）。

14205717.label: Realisation of objectives
14205717.value: We met the project objectives with great success. Objective 1: We developed a probabilistic framework for simplex-structured matrix factorization (SSMF). Taking insight from probabilistic principal and independent component analyses, the framework developed is considerably different from the mainstream studies in the SSMF context. Our framework gives us a unique advantage in combating noise. Interestingly, our study led to elegant connections with some popularly used algorithms, namely, the simplex volume minimization algorithms in SSMF. Our study provided insights on why some famous algorithms can be resilient to noise, and on how we may improve the existing algorithms. Drawing the aforementioned connections greatly enriched our understanding of SSMF techniques. As research outcomes, we published two journal papers that examine the fundamental nature of our probabilistic framework. In addition, as the blessing of a probabilistic framework, our framework has the flexibility to deal with multi-modal data models, outlier noise models, nonlinear models and non-simplex models. The aforementioned models are considered challenging in the existing techniques. We successfully demonstrated these possibilities in 3 conference papers. Objective 2: We developed efficient stochastic approximation schemes for the problem of realizing our probabilistic framework. As a key result, we also devised the variational inference approximation (VIA) schemes for the realization. The VIA schemes allow us to tackle the realization problem with much better efficiency, and with reasonable approximation accuracies under low to moderate SNRs. The originality of the VIA schemes is high; to the best of our knowledge, it is the first time VIA is used to achieve SSMF. The VIA schemes play a significant role in our study, and open new possibilities for future research. Objective 3: The algorithms established in Objective 2 were applied to real hyperspectral imaging data and real word-document data. We were particularly successful with the hyperspectral imaging application. Using our algorithm, we were able to mitigate the effects of (unknown) outliers and variability effects with the data; even better, we can detect and identify the presence of those effects – which is useful in real applications. Objective 4: We carried out performance analysis by showing the identifiability of our probabilistic framework. As an important finding, we showed that the probabilistic framework is equipped with a powerful identifiability guarantee under the “big data” regime. The guarantee is unique to probabilistic approaches, and is not seen in the existing SSMF studies. The guarantee provides an implication that our probabilistic framework can effectively combat the noise effects; our empirical results support this view.

14205717.label: Major findings and research outcome
14205717.value: We established a probabilistic framework for SSMF. Our study led to significant fundamental findings. Our framework, named PRISM (probabilistic simplex component analysis) for short, principally differs from the majority of SSMF studies. It leverages on probabilistic techniques for latent variable analyses, which has lately drawn much interest due to the rise of machine learning. The fundamental merits of PRISM are that i) it is a principled approach to deal with noise, which often appears in real-life data; and ii) it has the flexibility to deal with complex models arising from real-life data. There are three main fundamental contributions with our study. First, we showed the theoretical identifiability of PRISM. Simply speaking, we showed that PRISM is a fundamentally sound framework – an important attribute practitioners want to know before they employ our framework. Second, we drew connections between PRISM and some famous existing algorithms for SSMF. Our study provided new explanations for the existing algorithms, and suggested new algorithm design guidelines. Third, we proposed variational inference approximation (VIA) schemes for the algorithmic realization of PRISM. VIA represents a major breakthrough in this project, allowing us to overcome a technical challenge on computations; and it greatly expands the practical utility of PRISM. Our study also demonstrated practical usefulness of PRISM, mainly with the application of hyperspectral imaging. Simply speaking, PRISM was empirically found an effective approach for dealing with noise and adversarial modeling error effects. The aforementioned findings led to two papers in prestigious journals and four papers in major conferences. - The journal paper titled “Probabilistic Simplex Component Analysis” is of very high quality, in the PI’s view. It laid the foundation of PRISM. - The sequel journal paper “SISAL Revisited” described how the famous algorithm of SISAL can actually be seen as an outcome of PRISM, and addressed some previously unanswered fundamental questions with SISAL. The study led to strikingly new insights to, and new understanding of, a famous algorithm in SSMF. - In our conference publications, we demonstrated the practical utility of PRISM in hyperspectral imaging and some other applications. For example, in “Robust Probabilistic Simplex Component Analysis”, we empirically illustrated how an outlier-robust variant of PRISM can effectively deal with the highly undesirable outlier effects in real hyperspectral imaging data.

14205717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14205717.value: We see great potential for future development. In recent machine learning research, there has been tremendous interest in deep unsupervised learning and deep latent variable analyses. The PI can foresee great opportunities for expanding PRISM (our framework) to engage with the aforementioned “hot” research trend. This is because PRISM has naturally strong ties with basic techniques in unsupervised statistical learning, from the point we proposed this research in 2018. Now, in 2022, we happen to find that the direction of PRISM aligns with the blooming machine learning theory research. Apart from machine learning, our study of PRISM has essentially built a new framework for SSMF. The PI hopes that this will have long-term impacts on SSMF research and its numerous signal processing applications. From a practical utility viewpoint, we still see many opportunities for PRISM to engage with the application of hyperspectral imaging; for example, we can modify PRISM to handle complex models and uncover interpretable results from real-life data.

14205717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14205717.value: Simplex-structured matrix factorization (SSMF) is an important class of problems in signal processing and data science. Researchers have found numerous applications for SSMF, such as blind unmixing of hyperspectral images in remote sensing (separating different materials we see in the image), blind unmixing in biomedical imaging (separating different parts of organs), audio separation (separating different speakers’ voices), and community detection and crowdsourcing in data science. In this project we established a new SSMF framework called PRISM. PRISM is considered quite different from the existing SSMF approaches. PRISM uses a probabilistic approach, and is powerful in its flexibility in handling increasingly complex phenomena in real-life applications. This project studied the fundamental nature of PRISM; e.g., on what we may gain from PRISM, compared to the existing studies. This project also studied the practical applications of PRISM, and we demonstrated how the flexibility of PRISM gave us advantages in practice, e.g., on resisting undesirable bad data (outlier) effects. The significance of this study lies in the fundamental side -- laying the foundation of a different SSMF framework to provide new perspectives and practical solutions to SSMF, and to enrich our basic understanding which may lead to deep and long-term scientific impacts.

14205817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14205817.value: The aim of this study is to develop cyclic loading resistant and cytocompatible guest-host hydrogels as carrier materials for cell-based cartilage therapies. Osteoarthritis (OA) is characterized by the progressive degradation of articular cartilage in articulating joints such as the knee joint. Cell-based (including stem cells) cartilage tissue engineering is a promising approach for cartilage repair. However, direct administration of cells to the cartilage defects often results in limited efficacy due to significant cell death in the harsh environment of diseased joints. Therefore, there exists a huge demand for effective scaffold biomaterials that afford physical anchorage and protection to the delivered stem cells to promote cartilage repair. Hydrogels provide a favorable 3D environment for the encapsulated cells and neocartilage formation. However, the inadequate mechanical properties of conventional hydrogels severely limit the application of hydrogels as the scaffold material for repairing articular cartilage, as it is routinely subjected to intense cyclic compressive loading of large deformation, high frequency, and non-resting nature. When subjected to such intense cyclic loading, previously developed mechanically robust hydrogels often fail to maintain their original mechanical properties due to inability to recover disrupted network structure. Incorporation of reversible physical crosslinking improves the resistance of hydrogels to cyclic loading, but this generally requires long resting time and external stimulations. Furthermore, none of the aforementioned hydrogels permit the encapsulation of cells into the hydrogels. These limitations preclude the application of such “fatigue resistant” hydrogels as a cell-laden biomaterial scaffold for reparing articular cartialge. This proposed study aims to develop cyclic loading resistant (CLR) supramolecular hydrogels that allow encapsulation of stem cells. We will develop a novel hybrid host-guest macromer consisting of biopolymer grafted with a newly designed βCD monomer via host guest complexation. The fast binding kinetics of host-guest complexation facilitates rapid recovery of hydrogels under cyclic loading. The polymer linker of optimized length in the βCD monomer provides the necessary elasticity for network recovery and enhances monomer polymerization efficiency without using cytotoxic monomers, thereby enabling cell encapsulation in the formed hydrogels. The reversible nature of host-guest crosslinking in hydrogels during cyclic loading will also be visually demonstrated by Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) experiments. The study will also evaluate the efficacy of the obtained hydrogels to support chondrogenesis of encapsulated hMSCs and cartilage repair in vivo. The findings from this project will promote the clinical translation of hydrogels for repairing injured soft tissues including cartilage, meniscus and intervertebral disc. 本研究的目的是開發抗循環負載和具有細胞相容性的超分子主客體水凝膠作為軟骨治療的細胞載體材料。 骨關節炎（OA）的特徵是關節軟骨逐漸退化。基於細胞的（包括幹細胞）軟骨組織工程是軟骨修復的有前途的方法。然而，由於細胞在病變關節的惡劣環境中過早大量死亡，導致療效有限。因此，急需開發有效的支架生物材料，用於保護干細胞以促進軟骨修復。 水凝膠為封裝的細胞和新軟骨形成提供了有利的3D環境。然而，常規水凝膠的機械性能不足嚴重限制了水凝膠作為修復關節軟骨的支架材料的的應用，因為它常規地經受大變形，高頻和非靜止性質的強烈的循環壓縮載荷。當經受這種強烈的循環加載時，先前開發的機械堅固的水凝膠通常由於不能恢復破壞的網絡結構而不能保持其原始的機械性能。引入可逆物理交聯可提高水凝膠對循環載荷的抵抗力，但這通常需要較長的休息時間和外部刺激。此外，上述水凝膠都不允許將細胞包封到水凝膠中。這些限制排除了使用這種“疲勞抗性”水凝膠作為細胞負載的生物材料支架用於修復關節軟骨。 這項提出的研究旨在開發允許幹細胞包封的抗循環負載超分子水凝膠。我們將開發一種新型的混合主客體大分子單體，其由通過主客體絡合物與新設計的環糊精單體接枝的生物聚合物組成。主客體絡合的快速結合動力學有助於在循環載荷下水凝膠的快速恢復。在環糊精單體中優化聚合物接頭的長度可為網絡恢復提供必要的彈性，並且在不使用細胞毒性單體的情況下提高單體聚合效率，從而使得能夠在形成的水凝膠中進行細胞包封。通過共振能量轉移實驗，可視化顯示循環載荷期間水凝膠中主客體交聯的可逆性質。該研究還將評估獲得的水凝膠支持包被的間充質幹細胞的軟骨形成和體內軟骨修復的功效。 該項目的結果將促進水凝膠的臨床轉化，可用於修復包括軟骨，半月板和椎間盤等受損的軟組織，。

14205817.label: Realisation of objectives
14205817.value: We have successfully completed all objective. In details, we fabricated novel supramolecular hydrogels by cross-linking supramolecular cross-linkers that were self-assembled from adamantane -grafted polymer (ADA-PEG-ADA) and mono-acrylated β-cyclodextrin monomer (mono-Ac-βCD). Compared with conventional covalently cross-linked hydrogels, these PEG-ADA hydrogels exhibit high deformability, excellent capacity to dissipate massive amounts of loading energy, and superior antifatigue property under excessive, ultrafast, and nonresting cyclic compression. The improvement of these mechanical properties results from the employment of the βCD-ADA host-guest complex as the cross-linker, which has a high binding constant and rapid binding kinetics. The PEG-ADA hydrogels can rapidly recover completely even under a high compression rate of up to 25% strain per second. The parametric analysis of the PEG-ADA hydrogels suggests that the gelation parameters can be modified to customize the hydrogel bulk properties to address the specific demands of different applications. The excellent water solubility of this supramolecular cross-linker eliminates the additional organic solvent typically required by conventional methods for host-guest hydrogel fabrication to dissolve the hydrophobic guest molecules. This is important for the biomedical applications of such hydrogels. The in vitro cell metabolism and viability tests showed that our PEG-ADA hydrogels are nontoxic to cells. By effectively dissipating loading energy and relaxing applied stress, the PEG-ADA hydrogel cushions significantly promoted the survival of the underlying myoblasts compared with the PEGDA hydrogels. Therefore, we believe that the PEG-ADA hydrogels are promising biomaterials for tissue repair and regeneration at loading-bearing sites. Our finding will provide valuable guidance on the design of prosthetic hydrogels for load-bearing implantation sites with surrounding mechanosensitive cells and tissues. We further developed another cyclic-loading resistant hydrogel named HGMC hydrogel based on the same strategy. The excellent stretchability of the HGMC hydrogels is shown by stretching it to around 17 times of its original length. Such excellent stretchability suggests that the polymer networks crosslinked by host-guest interactions can successfully dissipate the loading energy. The energy dissipating property was revealed by the hysteresis of the HGMC hydrogels under cyclic stretching. The recovery of the hydrogel mechanical properties was fast, as evidenced by the nearly identical loading-unloading curves of the original cycle and the second cycle after 10 seconds. This indicated the disruption and fast self-recovery of the original polymer networks due to the reversible multivalent host-guest interactions. We propose a mechanism for the excellent stretchability and self-recovery of the HGMC hydrogels as follows. While the initial stretching of the hydrogel extends the polymer chains between multivalent crosslinkers, further stretching induces the dissociation of some host-guest complexes and extension of the PAAm chains between neighboring host-guest complexes. The release of such temporary “looped defects” improves the stretchability of the hydrogels, and the residual host-guest complexes prevent the early fracture of the hydrogels. Upon removal of the large stretching, the conformational recovery of the extended PAAm chains and the re-association of the temporally ruptured host-guest complexes induce the fast recovery of the hydrogel mechanical properties. The reversible nature of the host-guest interactions contributing to the mechanical robustness of HGMC hydrogels were also revealed by the oscillatory frequency-sweep measurement. Firstly, the shear modulus of the hydrogels is frequency dependent, indicating the reversible nature of the host-guest crosslinks. Moreover, no gel-sol transition points indicated by the crossover of guest interactions usually showed the G’-G’’ crossover points within this frequency range due to their mechanical weakness and poor long-term stability. Meanwhile, the oscillatory amplitude sweeps revealed the ductility of the hydrogel matrix after swelling. They can withstand the large shear strain up to 10 % even though the polymer chains between multivalent crosslinkers were pre-extended by the swelling effect, indicating the important roles of temporal “looped defects” in improving the strechability of the HGMC hydrogels. Accordingly, the swollen HGMC hydrogels can still be stretched up to 4.5 times of its original length. Furthermore, the immediate and full recovery of the shear modulus of the hydrogels was also demonstrated by the step-strain time-sweep measurements.

14205817.label: Major findings and research outcome
14205817.value: Findings from this project show that supramolecular hydrogels based on the supramolecular cross-linkers can exhibit substantial deformability, excellent capacity to dissipate massive amounts of loading energy, and rapid full recovery during excessive, ultrafast, and non-resting cyclic compression. Furthermore, the energy dissipation capacity of supramolecular hydrogels can be regulated by changing the concentration, molecular weight and cross-linking density of polymer. We further showed that according to in vitro cell metabolism and viability tests, the energy-dissipating hydrogels are noncytotoxic and can significantly enhance cell survival under this deleterious mechanical insult compared with the conventional hydrogel. Therefore, such supramolecular hydrogels are promising prosthetic biomaterials for the repair and regeneration of load-bearing tissues. We further used multivalent supramolecular crosslinkers to reinforce the chemically crosslinked hydrogels, and we showed that the reversible supramolecular crosslinks can simultaneously tune the energy storage and dissipation properties of the hydrogels. The dually crosslinked hydrogels showed significantly improved mechanical strength, ductility, and self-recovery. Moreover, we carefully examined the individual contribution of the two crosslinking types to the overall mechanical properties of the hydrogels. Our finding revealed that the chemical crosslinks contributed mainly to the energy storage property, while the supramolecular crosslinks significantly contributed to both the energy storage and dissipation properties. Insights from this study may inspire us to develop more advanced hydrogel materials with well-tailored overall mechanical properties for a broad range of applications. We have published three peer-reviewed papers based on the findings from this project and train one PhD student from this project.

14205817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14205817.value: We believe that findings from this project provided valuable insights to developing mechanically robust and bioactivatable hydrogel matrix for biomedical applications, such as soft tissue prothesis, biomaterials scaffold, drug delivery vehicles. Supramolecular hydrogels are especially promising prosthetic biomaterials for the repair and regeneration of load-bearing tissues such as meniscus and intervertebral disc (IVD). We are now collaborating with orthopedic surgeons to develop hydrogels to repair herniated IVD and torn meniscus. We are also planning to do the pre-clinical biosafety tests with CNAS-accredited test centers for our developed hydrogels to push for further translation of hydrogel products in clinical applications

14205817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14205817.value: Biomimetic hydrogels with excellent biomechanical properties are promising biomaterials for diverse biomedical application due to their unique hydrated structures. One successful biomimetic strategy for facile construction of high-performance hydrogels is to incorporate reversible crosslinks as sacrificial bonds into chemical polymer networks. By mimicking the unfolding-refolding functions of the skeletal muscle protein titin, the reversible crosslinks can reinforce the otherwise weak and brittle hydrogels. However, the contribution of multivalent reversible crosslinks to the overall hydrogel mechanical properties has rarely been investigated. In this project we present the biomimetic hydrogels with multivalent host-guest interactions as reversible crosslinks, which provide not only energy storage capacity, but also elevated energy dissipation capacity to the dually crosslinked networks, therefore leading to the improved hydrogel ductility and tensile strength. Our results also reveal the manner of multivalent host-guest crosslinks contributing to the hydrogel mechanical properties, including gelation rate, energy storage and dissipation, tensile hysteresis, and fast spontaneous recovery. Such hydrogels are especially promising prosthetic biomaterials for the repair and regeneration of load-bearing tissues such as meniscus and intervertebral disc.

14205917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14205917.value: In recent years, bistable energy harvesting has attracted researchers' attention due to its high energy output and broadband performance. Bistable energy harvesters could be beneficial from large amplitude motion when undergoing high-energy orbit oscillations and significantly increase energy output to be harvested. Thus they could be effective across a broad-frequency bandwidth compared to linear energy harvesters. However, it is difficult for bistable energy harvesters to go into high-energy orbits under low-level excitations. Usually, low and high energy orbits coexist, while sensitive to initial conditions. To address these challenges, the impulsively-excited bistable energy harvester was proposed that impulsive force was initially applied to the bistable energy harvester so that it could jump into high-energy orbit. However, the practical implementation of impulsively-excited bistable energy harvester has not been fully realized and its mechanisms have not been investigated in depth. This proposed research is aimed to design new bistable energy harvesters adaptive to non-harmonic excitations such as human motions so that they can maintain high-energy orbit oscillations. A comprehensive model is needed to fully understand corresponding mechanisms and further improve energy harvesting performances. We propose an adaptive bistable energy harvester with flexible rotor and impact mass. This design converts input excitation into impact force, which excites the bistable energy harvester. The added flexible rotor, which is made of soft material, makes the energy harvester adaptive to different amplitudes and frequencies of excitations. As a result, high-energy output and broadband performance could be realized. Impact mechanics will be applied to develop a comprehensive model, which will be used to analyze the nonlinear dynamics. Parametric studies will be conducted to provide guidelines on improving energy harvesting performances. New performance metrics could be proposed to give a fair comparison among different bistable energy harvesters under non-harmonic excitations. Prototypes will be fabricated and tested under various excitations. 近年來，雙穩態能量收集技術由於其高能量輸出和寬頻性能，引起了研究者們的關注。雙穩態能量收集裝置能夠受益於高能軌道振盪下的大幅度運動，並顯著增加收集能量的輸出。因此，與線性能量收集裝置相比，它們可以在寬頻段下有效工作。然而，雙穩態能量收集裝置在低層次激勵下難以進入高能軌道。通常情況下，低能軌道和高能軌道共存，並且兩者對初始條件敏感。 為了應對這些挑戰，研究者們提出了衝擊激發的雙穩態能量收集裝置，其原理是最初將衝擊力施加到雙穩態能量收集裝置，以便使其能夠躍入高能軌道。然而，衝擊激發的雙穩態能量收集裝置的實際應用尚未完全實現，其機理也未被深入研究。我們提出的研究旨在設計能夠適應於人體運動之類的非諧波激勵的新型雙穩態能量收集裝置，以便使其能夠維持高能軌道振盪。為此需要一個綜合模型來全面理解相關的機理，並進一步提高能量收集性能。 我們提出了一種帶有柔性轉子和碰撞質量的適應性雙穩態能量收集裝置。該設計將輸入激勵轉換為碰撞力，來激勵雙穩態能量收集裝置。增加的由軟材料製成的柔性轉子，使得能量收集裝置適應於不同幅值和頻率的激勵。因此，此設計可以實現高能量輸出和寬頻性能。碰撞力學將被應用於開發一個能夠分析非線性動力學的綜合模型。我們將進行參數研究來提供改進能量收集性能的指導方針。我們將提出新的性能指標，以便在非諧波激勵下對不同雙穩態能量收集裝置進行公平的比較。我們將製造原型，並會在不同激勵下測試。

14205917.label: Realisation of objectives
14205917.value: We developed a comprehensive model of impact piezoelectric energy harvesting, which considers constitutive mechanisms of electromechanical model, Hertzian contact theory and Hunt-Crossley model of impact dissipation. We confirmed the implications of impact dissipation mechanism on the responses of impact piezoelectric energy harvesters. We proposed a method to test the impact piezoelectric energy harvester. The parameters in the model were identified and the responses of the impact piezoelectric energy harvester were measured with a high-speed camera. The developed model was experimentally validated so that it well predicts the responses of impact piezoelectric energy harvesters by considering impact dissipation mechanism. We nondimensionalized the developed model by choosing the scaling to zoom in impact process; zoom in impact dissipation; and emphasize the electromechanical coupling and energy harvesting performance. Parametric studies were conducted to analyze the implications of dimensionless parameters on energy distribution. The interesting findings are that the impact dissipation mechanism influences the impact energy, showing its implication on the dynamics of the whole system. The energy distribution fluctuates under different mass ratios, revealing the intrinsic nonlinearity of impact process. Both of these phenomena are the results of multiple impacts due to structural compliance. Plucking piezoelectric energy harvesters can convert sporadic motions into plucking force to excite vibration energy harvesters and achieve broadband performances. Though different kinds of plucking piezoelectric energy harvesters have been designed, the plucking mechanism is not well understood. The simplified models of plucking piezoelectric energy harvesting neglected the dynamic interaction between the plectrum and piezoelectric beam. We investigated the plucking mechanism and developed a comprehensive model of plucking piezoelectric energy harvesting. Parametric studies were conducted on the dimensionless model after choosing appropriate scaling. The influences of plucking velocity and overlap length on energy harvesting performance and energy conversion efficiency were discussed. The comprehensive model helped investigate the characteristics and guide the design of plucking piezoelectric energy harvesters. Incorporation of plucking up-conversion and bistable energy harvesting techniques can be solutions to enhance energy harvested from large-amplitude impulsive-type events. We designed an asymmetric plucking-based bistable energy harvester with rotary structure and plectrum, to convert the impulsive excitation to plucking force that helps the harvester jump into the high-energy orbit. Hertzian contact theory was employed to relate different oscillation modes with dynamic plucking force under variations of plucking velocity and overlap length. By considering the dynamic deformation and rotational angle of beam tip during vibration, geometrically dipole-dipole model was adopted to calculate the asymmetric magnetic force and study potential well in contrast to the symmetric configuration. With the fact that linear damping model often misses its physical essentials in bistable systems, nonlinear damping model was employed to account for the energy dissipation process. Experiments showed qualitative agreement with simulation results in terms of system responses and power output under different velocities, overlap lengths and load resistances. Parametric studies based on nondimensionalization were further conducted to investigate the mechanisms that control the energy characteristics of the system, thus providing a foundation to develop an optimal plucking bistable energy harvester. Energy harvesters, especially nonlinear systems with broad bandwidth, have made it possible for devices in IoT (Internet of Things) to extract energy from the ambient environment. However, due to the multistability feature of the nonlinear system, high and low energy orbits coexist in the nonlinear energy harvesting systems. We proposed the load perturbation method to attain the high-energy orbit of nonlinear energy harvesters. Simulation and experiments revealed that the load perturbation can stimulate high-energy orbit oscillation for both monostable and bistable systems. The power output can be amplified for multifold times. The perturbation requires only one switch without additional mechanical structures. Furthermore, this method consumes little energy so that no external electrical energy source is needed. The load perturbation method opens opportunities for wide applications of nonlinear energy harvesters. We reported a synergistic design by combining these two mechanisms toward a dual-effect broadband piezoelectric energy harvesting solution. We then investigated the piezoelectric energy harvesting system with mechanical and electrical nonlinearities and provided new insights. A smart energy harvester was proposed and investigated to target the negative work of ankle joint during normal walking and convert biomechanical energy into electricity to power electronic devices. One-way clutch was employed to ﬁlter the plantarﬂexion of ankle joint and mechanical switch array was used to disconnect the electrical load at swing phase, so that the harvester can accurately capture the negative of ankle joint. Mathematical model of the energy harvesting system was built to analyze the four-bar linkage mechanism and predict the power generation as well as efﬁciency of the system. A light weight prototype was fabricated to validate the performances of the proposed energy harvester. From the experimental results, the prototype can produce average power of 0.35W at walking speed of 4.9kmh−1, which is sufﬁcient to power most wearable electronic devices. The experiments also demonstrated that the proposed harvester can reduce metabolic expenditure of 0.8W with consequent cost of harvesting (COH) of −2.29. The result of reduction in metabolic expenditure was also supported by measuring the EMG signals of related muscles. We designed an electromagnetic generator with coaxial topology that efficiently captures the motion of arm swing to produce electricity for smart watches and wristbands. This electromagnetic generator integrates a coaxially-installed motion capture mechanism, a magnetic frequency-up converter and a power generation unit in a highly compact and flat space, allowing it to be embedded in smart watches and wristbands. The average power generation and normalized power density were 1.74 mW and 820.38 μW/cm3·Hz2, which are, respectively, more than 4 and 10 times that of previous works. Targeted for high-power density, we further proposed an inertial energy harvester without additional proof mass to efficiently scavenge the kinetic energy of human limb swing. They have great potential to sustainably power wearable sensors for the Internet of Things. We also introduced a tiny repulsive magnetic spring to improve the performance of a wrist-worn inertial energy harvester.

14205917.value: Significant results (17 journal papers and 7 conference papers) have been obtained from this completed project. The invention supported by this research won Gold Medal, International Exhibition of Inventions Geneva, 2021. One journal paper [J11] receives ASME Energy Harvesting Best Paper Award, 2021. Three PhD students were trained with their theses: M. J. Cai, “Kinetic Energy Harvesting from Human Limbs Swing Based on Electromagnetic Transducer,” Ph.D. Thesis, August 2020. Cai’s thesis also won Faculty Outstanding PhD Thesis Award 2020, at The Chinese University of Hong Kong. For the further development, embedded generators will be fully implemented toward self-powered smart watches and wristbands.

14205917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14205917.value: Bistable energy harvesters could be beneficial from large amplitude motion when undergoing high-energy orbit oscillations and significantly increase energy output to be harvested. However, it is difficult for bistable energy harvesters to go into high-energy orbits under low-level excitations. To address these challenges, the impulsively-excited bistable energy harvester was proposed that impulsive force was initially applied to the bistable energy harvester so that it could jump into high-energy orbit. In this research, the mechanism of impulsively-excited bistable energy harvester have been investigated in depth. Bistable energy harvester with flexible rotor and impact mass have also been considered. The input excitation is converted into impact force, which excites the bistable energy harvester. As a result, high-energy output and broadband performance could be realized. Impact mechanics has been applied to develop comprehensive models, which have been used to analyze the nonlinear dynamics. Parametric studies were conducted to fully understand the physical insights and provide guidelines on improving energy harvesting performances. Performance metrics were compared among different bistable energy harvesters under non-harmonic excitations. Several bistable energy harvesters subject to non-harmonic excitations such as human motions were designed. Prototypes will be fabricated and tested under various excitations.

14206117.label: Project Objectives
14206117.value: Investigate the source of margin procyclicality from the perspective of asset dynamics. This object is theoretical. It is to capture the persistence in volatility through self-exciting price dynamics. For models based on the GARCH setting, we will derive the associated conditional quantile processes and examine their serial dependence. If time permits, we will also explore persistence in jumps and examine models based on self-exciting point processes, in particular the Hawkes model. Investigate margin rules that are stable and resistant to procyclicality. It is to examine the ``through the cycle" margin rule we propose and quantify the degree of procyclicality by studying the gap between stable unconditional margin and risk-sensitive conditional margin. We will establish limiting laws of tail ratio between unconditional and conditional loss distribution, for both light-tailed and heavy-tailed GARCH innovations. We will also estimate models for a range of financial markets to demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposal, through which to highlight the limitations of existing approaches that regulators are proposing for limiting procyclicality. Investigate the probability of margin breaches. It is to provide theoretical guidance on how long a look-back period is needed to set adequate margin level that are resistant to procyclicality, given a particular margin rule. We will derive the critical time that characterizes the probability of margin breaches. For a set of representative asset classes, we will also use simulation to demonstrate the theoretical result's relevancy. Investigate the margin properties of nonlinear assets. This objective contains two components. The first one is to characterize the tail behavior of European style options, given a particular distribution of market risk factors. The second one is investigate how volatility persistence of the risk factors influences margin variations of a nonlinear asset. In particular, we will examine the limitations of sensitivity-based approach that regulators propose to margin non-centrally cleared derivatives. Besides research objectives, we plan to use this project to serve an educational purpose for Hong Kong. As a key international financial center, Hong Kong is exposed to external financial shocks, whose effects may be further exacerbated through the dollar pegging monetary channel. It is thus strategically important to provide state-of-the-art education to students and train them to be competent financial risk managers in the future. By involving students in the research process and by offering courses using materials developed out of this project, this educational purpose can be served.

14206117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14206117.value: We propose to study the procyclical properties of margin requirements in derivative markets. Margin requirements serve as a buffer against the transmission of losses through the financial system by protecting one party to a contract against default by the other party. As is often noted, collateral coverts counterparty risk into funding liquidity risk through margin call. If margins are based on risk-sensitive rules, however, financial markets can be unstable. Margin calls would occur at worst times when markets are in most stress. A sudden request of billion dollar liquidity is seismic for any bank. Procyclical margin therefore becomes a serious concern of regulators and international standard-setting bodies. What is the root cause of margin procyclicality? How to set rules to mitigate it? What are the chances a given margin level will be breached? Could margins of nonlinear assets be more procyclical than linear ones? These are the questions we plan to address in this proposal. At the center of our proposal is to realize that volatility persistence and the self-exciting nature of price changes cause extreme negative returns to be serially dependent, which in turn renders margin requirement procyclical. The alternative we propose is to set ``through the cycle" margin levels that are less sensitive to current conditions and therefore less prone to spikes at the onset of market stress. How much higher a stable margin requirement could be depends on how much heavier the unconditional tails of risk factors are, relative to their conditional counterparts. How much more collateral one party needs to raise than the other party depends on how asymmetric the contract's payoff function is. 保證金交易制度的核心功能是對交易雙方可能產生的損失施以緩衝，避免相互傳導。但保證金制度本身並不會降低對手方風險，它事實上是將潛在的對手方倒閉風險轉化成了追加保證金過程中的資金流動性風險。在現行的全球各市場保證金制度中，保證金的額度多與各種對瞬時風險敏感的風險度量掛鉤，這將會導致金融市場的不穩定。歷史經驗表明，追加保證金的事件多發於市場下行壓力極大的時候，而在這個時候要求金融機構去市場上融資來滿足追加的保證金要求，對任何金融機構來說都是雪上加霜，會加劇已經承壓的市場下行壓力。全球監管當局對這種 順週期特性已然非常擔憂。本課題就將著眼於研究衍生品市場中的這種保證金順週期特性。首先，這種順週期特性的本質原因是什麼？如何設置保證金規則讓保證金額度免於這種順週期的危害性？其次，對於股票債券這類線性損益的證券, 預設的保證金額度被突破的概率是什麼？最後，期權類的非線性權證的保證金是否會更加的順週期？我們的中心出發點是意識到資產價格的波動持久性和自激性是導致大幅度資產價格下挫具有時域上強相關性的核心原因。我們認為在價格動態過程的層面，這也是導致保證金的順週期特性的內在機理。基於此我們提出一種對資產實時損益不敏感的保證金制度。我們將研究在該制度下的保證金額度比現有製度高出多少。我們也將研究對於非線性權證，尤其是交易雙方收益不對稱情況下，雙方各自的順週期差異。

14206117.label: Major findings and research outcome
14206117.value: The major findings: 1. The growing use of margin requirements in over-the-counter derivative transactions reduces counterparty credit risk but may amplify shocks to the financial system through margin calls when volatility spikes. Our analysis yields two key insights: buffer required to offset procyclicality depends on the critical tail exponent of price change innovation, and the look-back period required to estimate the quantile accurately depends on the extremal index. Both of these parameters depend on the persistence and burstiness of volatility. 2. Our analysis highlights important trade-offs. Market participants want their margin obligations to reflect the risk in their portfolios, but tying margin too closely to current risk levels amplifies stress when volatility spikes. CCPs face a trade-off in their use of historical data: long look-back periods are required to capture periods of high and low volatility, but changes in markets can make older data less relevant. In calm markets, CCPs and industry regulators may be tempted to allow lower margin levels. Our analysis cautions against this temptation. Setting practical and prudent margin levels requires balancing the risk-sensitivity that comes from relying on conditional volatility and the stability that comes from unconditional margin levels. The research outcomes: 1. Journal paper: 1 paper published at the Management Science; 1 paper under review at Mathematics of Operations Research. 2. Book chapter: 1 book chapter published at the Risk Book Series "Margin in Derivative Trading". 3. Conference talks: 4 conference talks are given by the PI at venues such as the INFORMS Annual Meeting, SIAM Conference on Financial Mathematics & Engineering, etc. 4. Industrial impact: part of the research work is in collaboration of the US Department of Treasury, Office of Financial Research.

14206117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14206117.value: One related topic is the right mix of margin requirements and guarantee fund contributions at CCPs. Guarantee fund contributions change less often and are therefore less procyclical, but CCP clearing members generally prefer putting more of their overall contributions in the initial margin. A further important topic is a fine-grained analysis of how shocks in margin levels propagate through a network of CCPs and clearing members. A better understanding of the origins of shocks to market volatility and the consequences of spikes in margin levels should help shape margin requirements that balance concerns for risk-sensitivity and financial stability.

14206117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14206117.value: Margin requirements for derivative contracts serve as a buffer against the transmission of losses through the financial system by protecting one party to a contract against default by the other party. However, if margin levels are proportional to volatility, then a spike in volatility leads to potentially destabilizing margin calls in times of market stress. Risk-sensitive margin requirements are thus procyclical in the sense that they amplify shocks. We use a GARCH model of volatility and a combination of theoretical and empirical results to analyze how much higher margin levels need to be to avoid procyclicality while reducing counterparty credit risk. Our analysis compares the tail decay of conditional and unconditional loss distributions with comparable stable and risk-sensitive margin requirements. Greater persistence and burstiness in volatility leads to a slower decay in the tail of the unconditional distribution and a higher buffer needed to avoid procyclicality. The tail decay drives other measures of procyclicality as well. Our analysis points to important features of price time series that should inform “antiprocyclicality” measures but are missing from current rules.

14206317.label: Project Objectives
14206317.value: We will investigate theoretically and experimentally the mid-infrared (2.5–10.6 microns) light coupling and delivery in single-mode chalcogenide glass and silver halide fibers. With the free-space radiation from quantum cascade laser (QCL) or interband cascade laser (ICL) coupled into the single-mode fiber (SMF), the evanescent field can be generated by tapering the optical fiber using a custom-designed fiber tapering system. We will systematically exploit the influence of tapering parameters such as heating temperature, fiber material, fiber drawing speed and distance, on the geometric profiles of the fiber taper. We will design and experimentally investigate a mid-infrared evanescent-wave quartz-enhanced photoacoustic gas sensor. A quartz tuning fork will be employed to detect the photoacoustic wave generated by the tightly confined mid-infrared evanescent field with an extraordinarily compact optical configuration. We will examine the influence of the optical and geometrical characteristics of the microfiber, including the fiber material, the core diameter, fiber probe geometry, and probe length on the photoacoustic signal. We will also conduct a theoretical and experimental study of the influence of the laser modulation depth, gas pressure, and fiber microstructures on sensor performance. We will investigate theoretically and experimentally the photothermal effect in the mid-infrared hollow-core metal-coated fiber and the hollow-core photonic bandgap fiber. We will couple the free-space QCL/ICL radiation into the hollow-core fibers and measure the phase modulation information using the highly sensitive fiber-optic interferometry. We will develop a mid-infrared hollow-core fiber-based photothermal gas sensor and its prototype for sensitive detection of formaldehyde and nitrogen oxides. With the proposed sensor setup, we will investigate the following parameters that particularly affect sensor performance: 1) laser modulation frequency, depth, and gas pressure, 2) higher-order mode noise and phase compensator modulation parameters, and 3) intrinsic light attenuation along the fiber.
