14206317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14206317.value: The proposed project will aim to design, fabricate, and characterize novel types of photoacoustic and photothermal trace gas sensors based on mid-infrared optical fibers. Laser-based photothermal spectroscopy (PTS) and photoacoustic spectroscopy (PAS) relying on the detection of absorption-induced thermal or acoustic waves are two highly sensitive optical methods for trace gas detection. In conventional PTS and PAS, laser radiation is delivered to a gas sample as a free-space beam. Many spectroscopic applications require the photons to be delivered to the sample via optical fibers, to achieve remote interrogation, multiplexed multi-point detection, and a distributed sensor network. We recently developed a near-infrared evanescent-wave photoacoustic sensor by using a silica fiber tip, and demonstrated carbon monoxide detection at 2.3 microns with an excellent linear response. However, this technique has limited detection sensitivity due to its relatively weak evanescent-wave power and absorption strength in the near-infrared. The mid-infrared spectral window between 2.5 and 20 microns provides an opportunity for ultrasensitive gas detection because the fundamental bands of many molecules occur in this fingerprint spectral region. Mid-infrared spectroscopy has recently evolved into a significant sensing technique, due to the commercialization of mid-infrared light sources, waveguides, and detectors. Merging these light sources and fiber-optics with PAS and PTS, and thus exploiting new highly sensitive and flexible optical sensing methods, has not been fully researched. We propose to develop two types of novel mid-infrared gas sensors: 1) an evanescent-wave quartz-enhanced photoacoustic sensor using a solid-core microfiber, and 2) a photothermal interferometric sensor using a hollow-core fiber (HCF). We will theoretically and experimentally investigate the light coupling performance of the free-space radiation from quantum cascade lasers and interband cascade lasers into various types of mid-infrared fibers. Using the single-mode chalcogenide glass and silver halide fiber tapers fabricated with a custom-designed tapering apparatus, we will employ a quartz tuning fork to detect the evanescent-wave absorption that is tightly confined to the tapered region. We will examine experimentally the influence of microfiber geometry and laser modulation characteristics on sensor performance. The mid-infrared HCF-based photothermal gas sensor will be developed using a novel pump-probe configuration with the photothermal phase modulation detected by an all-fiber interferometer. We will investigate the effects of several key parameters such as laser modulation frequency and depth, gas pressure inside the hollow core, and higher-order mode noise of the HCF on detection sensitivity and the dynamic range. 本項目旨在設計、構建和測試基於中紅外光纖的新型光聲光譜和光熱光譜痕量氣體傳感器。激光光熱光譜（PTS）和光聲光譜（PAS）分別用來測量物質吸收激光能量引起的光熱效應和光聲效應，這兩種光譜技術可用於高靈敏痕量氣體檢測。傳統PTS或PAS測量時，激光光束是以空間光的形式打入氣體介質，然而很多光譜應用需要光束通過光纖導入待測物質，從而實現遠距離、分布式傳感以及復用多點測量。我們前期的工作研究了基於倏逝波的光聲光譜傳感器，該傳感器將拉錐光纖針尖和石英音叉耦合，可以探測倏逝波被氣體分子吸收時引發的聲波信號，並初步應用到一氧化碳的測量。但是，該方法采用吸收強度較弱的近紅外波段，且倏逝場強度較弱，因此傳感器的探測靈敏度受限。註意到許多氣體分子在中紅外波段（2.5-20微米）具有很強的吸收帶，該波段非常適用於超靈敏氣體檢測，隨著中紅外光源、波導技術和光電探測器的發展，中紅外光譜技術已經發展成為重要的氣體檢測方法。然而，將這些新型的中紅外光源和光波導與PAS/PTS技術結合，並充分利用各自的技術優勢，相關研究還沒有開展起來。我們計劃研究兩種新型的中紅外光纖氣體傳感技術：1）利用實芯微光纖倏逝波的石英增強光聲光譜法，和2）利用空芯光纖（HCF）的光熱幹涉測量法。我們將理論建模結合實驗論證將中紅外光源（如量子級聯激光器和帶間級聯激光器）耦合入多種類型光纖的方法和手段，在光纖拉錐機上實驗研究單模硫系玻璃光纖和鹵化銀多晶光纖的拉錐特性，並將該中紅外微光纖應用到石英增強光聲光譜探測，系統性研究微光纖結構和激光調制參數對氣體探測的影響。同時，我們將完成中紅外空芯光纖光熱氣體傳感器的設計和構建，並系統性研究一系列關鍵參數，如激光調制頻率和深度，氣體壓力，光纖高階模對傳感器探測極限和動態範圍的影響。

14206317.label: Realisation of objectives
14206317.value: All the research objectives have been achieved in the project period. We have made significant progresses in all respects of this project on experiments and modeling. Our research findings have resulted in 12 papers published in peer-reviewed journals such as Sensors and Actuators B, Optics Letters, and Journal of Lightwave Technology. Here we explain the essential technical methods and results. Objective 1: Investigate the mid-infrared light coupling and delivery in single-mode optical fibers. We have investigated the mid-infrared light coupling between quantum cascade lasers with single-mode glass fibers and hollow-core fibers. The free-space laser beam can be focused into these fibers by knowing the mode size and numerical aperture. By selecting the AR-coated aspheric lens for different wavelengths between 2.3 µm and 10.6 µm, we can generally achieve a coupling efficiency above 80%, which is sufficient for optical gas sensing applications. With the free-space mid-infrared radiation coupled into the solid-core fiber, we investigated the evanescent field generated by tapering the optical fiber. The multiphysics COMSOL simulation suggests that the fractional power of the evanescent-wave increases with the reduced diameter of the microfiber. At the target wavelength of 5.2 µm for nitric oxide detection, we can generate an evanescent field of >95% when the microfiber can be tapered to be ~ 1 µm. Based on the custom-design soft-glass fiber tapering system, we have obtained microfibers with a diameter of 3 µm by controlling the heating temperature and drawing speed. Such tapered mid-infrared microfibers can be further used for photoacoustic spectroscopy. Objective 2: Design and investigate the quartz-enhanced photoacoustic gas sensor. We designed and investigated photoacoustic gas sensors by integrating the quartz tuning fork or acoustic resonator with the mid-infrared microfiber to achieve sensitive gas detection. The fiber taper was inserted through two acoustic resonator tubes with the taper waist placed between the two prongs of the tuning fork. Such a fiber taper with an acoustic resonator eliminates the stray light emitting from the tapered region to reduce the optical noise. We employed different types of lasers such as quantum cascade lasers and interband cascade lasers for nitric oxide, formaldehyde and acetylene detection. These photoacoustic gas sensors demonstrated the sensitivity in ppm level. In order to further improve the detection sensitivity, we adopted an optical cavity to boost the intracavity power for photoacoustic detection. Note that the photoacoustic signal is directly proportional to the incident laser power. As a result, the detection sensitivity was improved by another two orders of magnitude, leading to the ultrasensitive gas detection at ppb level. To further enhance the detection sensitivity, we used a high-finesse (> 9000) optical cavity to build up the optical power. By placing a photoacoustic cell inside a 130-mm long optical cavity, we obtained an enhancement of more than two orders of magnitude, leading to the sensitive gas detection at ppb level. Objective 3: Investigate the photothermal effect in the mid-infrared hollow-core fiber. We investigated photothermal effects inside different types of mid-infrared hollow-core fibers by coupling both the pump radiation and the near-infrared probe beam into hollow-core fibers. The pump-laser induced phase modulation can be measured sensitively by a fiber-optic interferometry. The first type of hollow-core fiber we investigated was the hollow-core negative curvature fiber (HC-NCF). The 85-cm long HC-NCF has a core diameter of 40 μm surrounded by a single layer of eight nontouching capillaries. Each capillary has a diameter of 14 μm and a wall thickness of ∼3 μm. Such a novel microstructure forms a negative curvature because the surface normal vector of the core boundary is oppositely directed from the center. This special core boundary keeps the guided fundamental mode away from silica junctions where light attenuation and cladding modes are significant. The node-less cladding structure made of nontouching capillaries forms a free core boundary that eliminates additional optical losses. We demonstrated that a diode laser beam at 2.3 μm was transmitted through the HC-NCF with negligible loss by using a Keplerian telescope made of two convex lenses (focus length, 20 mm and 40 mm) with a pinhole placed at the focal point. Another HC-NCF consists of a single ring of six nontouching silica capillaries. The hollow core has an inner diameter of 65 μm inscribed by those capillaries with a diameter of 34 μm and a strut thickness of 0.69 μm. We demonstrated the mid-infrared light delivery near 3.6 μm using an interband cascade laser for such a HCF with a total length of 120 cm. Objective 4: Develop mid-infrared hollow-core fiber-based photothermal gas sensors. We developed mid-infrared photothermal gas sensors using HC-NCFs, which serve as a sensing arm in a fiber-optic Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI). The sensing arm consists of the HC-NCF, the pump and probe laser beams, as well as the gas cell to pressurize the sample gas into the hollow-core fiber. The probe laser beam and the free-space pump laser are coupled into the HC-NCF from its two ends. The reference arm is composed of a standard near-infrared single-mode fiber coiled around a piezoelectric transducer (PZT) acting as a phase compensator. With the servo-loop control, we can keep the MZI at quadrature. In particular, we demonstrated the photothermal CO detection in the silica HC-NCF. The photothermal effect in a 40-μm hollow core is induced by CO absorption at 2327 nm and detected by the MZI operating at 1533 nm. By using wavelength modulation spectroscopy, we obtained the noise equivalent concentration of 90 ppm. We systematically investigated the parameters that affected the photothermal sensing and found out the optimal modulation frequency, depth and gas pressure. Additionally, we demonstrated a new method of heterodyne interferometric photothermal gas sensing with a simplified sensor design and enhanced sensor stability. We used an interband cascade pump laser at 3.6 μm for nitrous oxide detection and a MZI with a 1.5 μm near-infrared probe laser. The probe laser was split into two beams, one transmitted through the hollow-core fiber and one frequency-shifted by using an acoustic-optic modulator. Both beams were recombined to generate a beat note signal, which was then demodulated by two cascaded lock-in amplifiers to extract the photothermal signal. This detection scheme eliminates the sophisticated opto-mechanical stabilization system and exhibits intrinsic immunity to the power fluctuation of the probe laser.

14206317.label: Major findings and research outcome
14206317.value: In this project, we studied photoacoustic and photothermal gas sensors using mid-infrared fibers. By selecting the coupling lenses, commercial quantum cascade lasers and interband cascade lasers can be coupled into solid-core glass fibers and hollow-core fibers with low coupling loss. We successfully coupled a distributed-feedback diode laser at 2.3 µm into a hollow-core negative curvature fiber (HC-NCF) with a length of 85 cm and a core diameter of 40 μm [Sensors and Actuators B: Chemical, 303]. We also investigated the coupling of a mid-infrared interband cascade laser at 3.6 µm into a silica HC-NCF and achieved a coupling efficiency of 66% and a fiber transmission loss of ~0.6 dB/m [Journal of Lightwave Technology, 38]. Regarding photoacoustic gas detection, we designed and investigated photoacoustic gas sensors by integrating the quartz tuning fork or acoustic resonator with the mid-infrared microfiber to achieve sensitive gas detection. We demonstrated rapid and sensitive detection of sulfur hexafluoride at 10.5 µm using a quantum cascade laser [Measurement Science & Technology, 31], as well as ultrasensitive detection of acetylene at 1.5 µm with a high-finesse cavity [Optics Letters, 44(8); Optics Letters, 45(5)]. Regarding photothermal gas detection, we successfully demonstrated mid-infrared photothermal gas sensors using a HC-NCF and a fiber-optic Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI). We demonstrated the first photothermal CO sensor using a HC-NCF, which features a typical structure of one ring cladding containing eight nontouching capillaries to form a negative curvature core surround. Based on wavelength modulation spectroscopy, we achieved a normalized noise equivalent absorption coefficient of 4.4×10-8 cm-1WHz-1/2 [Optics Letters, 44(16)]. Additionally, we demonstrated a new method of heterodyne interferometric photothermal gas sensing with a simplified sensor design and enhanced sensor stability [Sensors and Actuators B: Chemical, 346]. Besides the use of an interband cascade pump laser at 3.6 μm, the probe laser was split into two beams, one transmitted through the hollow-core fiber and one frequency-shifted by using an acoustic-optic modulator. Both beams were recombined to generate a beat note signal, which was then demodulated by two cascaded lock-in amplifiers to extract the photothermal signal. Finally, we applied these mid-infrared sensors for the sensitive detection of formaldehyde [Applied Optics, 57], CO [Optics and Laser Technology, 130], N2O [Sensors, 20], and NO [Journal of Physics D, 53].

14206317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14206317.value: With the completion of this project, we have demonstrated photoacoustic and photothermal trace gas detection using optical fibers. The merging of mid-infrared laser radiation and photothermal fiber-optic interferometry will lead to the realization of an optical sensor system with unprecedented detection sensitivity and compact sensor system. We will further spend more engineering efforts to make the sensor suitable for ultrasensitive, miniaturized, multiplexed multi-point detection, and cost-effective trace gas sensing. Particularly, we will seek funding support from Innovation and Technology Commission to develop a prototype for socially beneficial chemical and biological sensing, including air pollutant monitoring, and non-invasive disease diagnosis. By collaborating with industrial partners, we aim to realize the technology transfer of our new spectroscopic technique to the open market for commercialization.

14206317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14206317.value: Photoacoustic and photothermal spectroscopy in the mid-infrared spectral region provides a promising way of sensitive gas detection, which can be used for environmental monitoring, process control and biomedical diagnostics. For sensing applications in a harsh environment with significant safety concerns, fiber-optic gas sensors are often among the best solutions. Hence, this project studied the combination of photoacoustic and photothermal spectroscopic techniques with mid-infrared light sources and optical fibers for the next generation of trace gas sensors with unique performance levels. On the one hand, we designed and investigated photoacoustic gas sensors by integrating the quartz tuning fork or acoustic resonator with the microfiber to achieve sensitive gas detection. We demonstrated rapid and sensitive detection of different gases such as sulfur hexafluoride and acetylene at ppm or ppb level. On the other hand, we successfully demonstrated mid-infrared photothermal gas sensors using a novel type of hollow-core negative curvature fiber and a fiber-optic Mach-Zehnder interferometer. To reduce the sensor complexity, we reported a heterodyne interferometric photothermal gas sensing method that eliminates the sophisticated opto-mechanical stabilization system. In the long term, our proposed spectroscopic techniques will potentially enable the development of ultrasensitive, miniaturized, and multiplexed multi-point gas detection systems.

14206517.label: Project Objectives
14206517.value: Develop a random-access TPE microscope based on a digital micromirror device (DMD) and binary holography; demonstrate random-access scanning in space at the DMD pattern update rate, i.e., ~20 kHz. Develop multi-depth imaging and 3D programmable imaging plane functions in a custom-built laser scanning TPE microscope based on the DMD beam shaper. Develop parametric models to establish deterministic relationships between the design parameters and the performance of the DMD-based laser scanner (i.e., DMD beam shaper). Specifically, the model should predict the minimum step size, the maximum scanning range in the axial and lateral directions, as well as the point spread function at different depths for a DMD of given pixel size and number of pixels. Develop and implement sensorless adaptive optics methods on the DMD beam shaper based on modal wavefront sensing and quadratic optimization; identify the optimal basis modes and quality metrics to minimize aberration; achieve simultaneous beam scanning and wavefront correction with a single DMD. Develop parametric models to predict the performance (e.g., imaging resolution and penetration depth etc.) of simultaneous beam shaping and beam scanning using a DMD; validate the predicted results with experiments. 14206517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14206517.value: This proposal aims to develop (1) a random-access two-photon microscope and (2) real-time sensorless wavefront correction methods using a digital micromirror device (DMD) and binary holography to achieve enhanced imaging resolution and speed. To achieve the goals, binary hologram patterns will be designed and programmed to a DMD, which functions as a programmable binary mask, operating at 10s kHz. With angular dispersion of the femtosecond laser properly compensated, the DMD can rapidly update its patterns to simultaneously scan and shape the laser beam. Fast axial scanning and random-access imaging are highly desired functions in two-photon microscopy to achieve high-speed volumetric imaging. For neuronal imaging, random-access scanning is particularly important as it captures high-speed biological events, e.g., spiking of neural circuits, by maximizing the scanning time at selected regions. Conventional laser scanners either are limited by their scanning speeds, e.g., piezo-objective scanner (~10Hz), or compromise their imaging resolution in exchange for higher speeds, e.g., acousto-optic deflectors (AODs) (~10kHz). Although AOD-based scanners have been used in random-access imaging for their speeds, their minimum step size is ~10 µm which makes them unsuitable for continuous volumetric scanning. A random-access scanner that overcomes the aforementioned issues has yet to be developed. To realize simultaneous random-access laser scanning and wavefront correction, we propose a binary holography-based approach, where the DMD is used as binary masks to modulate the incident femtosecond laser wavefront. For scanning, the focal point can be arbitrarily positioned/scanned in space by using holographic patterns of spherical wavefronts with adjusted tilted phases. For wavefront correction, a sensorless adaptive scheme will be used, where a sequence of images will be collected at low exposure level; the aberration is then determined based on modal wavefront sensing and quadratic optimization, where the quality metric is total intensity. Optimal basis modes, e.g., Zernike polynomials, will be converted to binary holograms and superposed to the scanning holograms, realizing beam scanning and wavefront correction using a single DMD. Lastly, in vivo Ca2+ imaging on GaCamp6 labeled zebrafish will be performed to validate the microscope performance and study the neuronal signaling processes. This proposal develops the fundamental theories and optomechanical designs to create a new class of two-photon microscopes that realize continuous volumetric scanning, random-access imaging, and sensorless wavefront correction with a single DMD, generating impact in both engineering and medical fields. The binary holography-based beam shaping/scanning methods may be utilized in the fields of laser fabrication, enabling new high-throughput, high-resolution processes. 本項目旨在開發（1）隨機存取雙光子顯微鏡和（2）使用數字微鏡器件（DMD）和二值全息術的實時無傳感器波前校正方法，以實現增強的成像分辨率和速度。為了實現目標，二進制全息圖模式將被設計和編程到以10s kHz工作的作為可編程二進制掩碼的DMD。隨著飛秒激光的角度色散被適當地補償，DMD可以快速更新其圖案以同時掃描和成形激光束。 快速軸向掃描和隨機存取成像是雙光子顯微鏡中高度需要的功能，以實現高速體積成像。對於神經元成像，隨機訪問掃描特別重要，因為它通過最大化選定區域的掃描時間來捕獲高速生物事件，例如神經迴路尖峰。常規的激光掃描儀或者受其掃描速度的限制，例如壓電物鏡掃描器（〜10Hz），或者損害它們的成像分辨率以換取更高的速度，例如聲光偏轉器（AOD）（〜10kHz）。雖然基於AOD的掃描儀已經被用於隨機存取成像的速度，但它們的軸向解析度僅約10微米，這使得它們不適於連續體積掃描。克服上述問題的隨機存取掃描儀尚未開發。 為了實現同時的隨機存取激光掃描和波前校正，我們提出了一種二進制全息方法，其中DMD被用作二進制掩模來調製入射的飛秒激光波前。對於掃描，可以通過使用具有調整的傾斜相位的球面波前全息圖來任意地定位/掃描焦點。對於波前校正，將使用無傳感器自適應方案，其中將以低曝光水平收集圖像序列; 然後基於模態波前感測和二次優化來確定像差，其中質量度量是總強度。最佳基礎模式，例如Zernike多項式，將被轉換為二進制全息圖並疊加到掃描全息圖，使用單個DMD實現波束掃描和波前校正。最後，對GaCamp6標記的斑馬魚進行體內Ca2 +成像，以驗證顯微鏡的性能並研究神經元的信號傳導過程。 本項目開發了基礎理論和光機械設計，以創建一種新型的雙光子顯微鏡，可實現連續體積掃描，隨機存取成像以及單個DMD的無傳感器波前校正，從而在工程和醫療領域產生影響。基於二進制全息術的束成形/掃描方法可用於激光製造領域，從而實現新的高通量，高分辨率的工藝。

14206517.label: Realisation of objectives
14206517.value: All six project objectives have been fully realized. For Objective 1, we have developed a new class of two-photon microscope based on a digital micromirror device (DMD) and binary holography; specifically, the location, amplitude and phase of an incident femtosecond laser beam can be arbitrarily controlled by the designed hologram displayed on the DMD. By sweeping the different designed holograms in the DMD, 3D random-access scanning is realized at the DMD pattern rate, i.e., 22.7 kHz. The result is published in [1]. For Objective 2, by combining the DMD random-access scanner with a pair of galvo scanners, we realized multi-depth imaging and 3D programmable imaging plane functions in a custom-built two-photon excitation (TPE) microscope; the detailed design parameters and configurations of the microscope system is published in [2]. For Objective 3, we have developed parametric models that establish deterministic relationships between the design parameters and the performance of the DMD-based laser scanner. Based on the model, we have accurately predicted the minimum step size, maximum scanning range, as well as the point spread function at different depths in the work volume for a DMD of given pixel size and number of pixels with experimental verification; these results have been reported in [1, 2]. For Objective 4 & 5, we have successfully applied the sensorless adaptive optics (AO) algorithm to the DMD-based TPE microscope and developed parametric models to predict the system performance with experimental verification; in this case, the DMD is simultaneously used as deformable mirrors to modulate distorted wavefront and a fast scanner to maneuver the laser focus in a 3D space by designed binary holograms, i.e., the tilted phase and spherical wavefront control the lateral and axial position of the focus respectively. As such, aberration-free 3D imaging is realized by superposing the wavefront correction and 3D scanning holograms. Comparing with conventional AO devices and methods, the DMD system can apply optimal wavefront correction information to different imaging regions or even individual pixels without compromising the scanning speed and device resolution. The results have been published in [3,4]. For Objective 6, in vivo experiments on animals and cells have been performed via the DMD TPE microscope system to verify the performance. Most results have been published in [1-4]. In addition to the six objectives, by using the DMD, digital holography, and the combination of them, we have significantly extended the application of our method to other optical applications and systems, including a new ultrafast synchronization-free light sheet microscope, published in Optica [5]; random-access pump probe spectroscopy [6]; DMD and holography-enabled multi-channel surface plasmon resonance (SPR) sensing [7]; high-resolution light field microscopy [8]; multi-focus 3D microscopy based on Hi-Lo algorithm [9]; and a new fiber-optic sensing method for label-free DNA hybridization detection [10]. Develop multi-depth imaging and 3D programmable imaging plane functions in a custom-built laser scanning TPE microscope based on the DMD beam shaper.

Develop parametric models to establish deterministic relationships between the design parameters and the performance of the DMD-based laser scanner (i.e., DMD beam shaper). Specifically, the model should predict the minimum step size, the maximum scanning range in the axial and lateral directions, as well as the point spread function at different depths for a DMD of given pixel size and number of pixels.

Develop and implement sensorless adaptive optics methods on the DMD beam shaper based on modal wavefront sensing and quadratic optimization; identify the optimal basis modes and quality metrics to minimize aberration; achieve simultaneous beam scanning and wavefront correction with a single DMD.

Develop parametric models to predict the performance (e.g., imaging resolution and penetration depth etc.) of simultaneous beam shaping and beam scanning using a DMD; validate the predicted results with experiments.

Perform in vivo Ca2+ imaging on GaCamp6 labeled zebrafish to evaluate the performance of the random-access TPE microscope and wavefront correction algorithms and study the neuronal signaling processes.

14206517.label: Major findings and research outcome
14206517.value: In this project, we have successfully developed a new two-photon microscopy platform based on the DMD and digital holography, which is a revolutionary method to manipulate and control the laser focus at the DMD pattern rate, i.e., 22.7 kHz [1, 2]. This method effectively eliminates the need for mechanical scanners in a laser scanning microscope as well as many other optical systems that require mechanical scanners, e.g., galvanometric mirrors, polygonal scanners, piezoelectric scanners etc. Although some aberration will be introduced to the moving focus in the DMD work space, it is largely suppressed by the sensorless adaptive optics (AO) algorithm which is pre-calculated and superposed to the designed binary holograms, leading to aberration-free high-speed 3D imaging [3]. In other words, we use a single device, i.e., a low-cost DMD, to perform ultrafast 3D random-access scanning, beam shaping, and wavefront correction. In comparison, a conventional TPE microscope system would require multiple expensive components, e.g., acousto optic deflector (AOD), resonant galvo scanner, liquid crystal-based spatial light modulator, Shack-Hartmann sensor, to partially realize the new functions we have demonstrated. The results have generated good impact to the biophotonics community and many research groups have adopted our method to design new optical systems.

14206517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14206517.value: By superposing the designed binary holograms, the DMD optical scanner will be able to perform multi-focus scanning at 22.7 kHz. We have demonstrated the use of multiple laser foci to improve the imaging speed of a TPE microscope. (C. Wen, M. Ren, F. Feng, W. Chen, and S. Chen, “Compressive Sensing for Fast 3-D and Random-access Two-photon Microscopy,” Optics Letters, Vol. 44, No. 17, pp.4343-46, 2019.) In the future, we plan to apply the DMD laser scanner to laser fabrication and two-photon polymerization to enhance the fabrication resolution, accuracy of laser dose control, and throughput. We will also investigate the maximum number of laser foci that can be generated by the DMD and binary holography and how they can influence the laser focus quality due to discrete sampling errors via theoretical modelling and experiments.

14206517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14206517.value: In this project, we have successfully developed a new class of two-photon microscope based on the DMD and digital holography. The new microscope achieves substantially improved scanning/imaging speed (22.7 kHz), random-access scanning capability for optogenetics application, and improved resolution for in vivo deep tissue imaging, which generate significant impact to the field of biophotonics. The holography-based DMD scanner effectively eliminates the need for mechanical scanners in a laser scanning microscope as well as many other optical systems that require mechanical scanners, e.g., galvanometric mirrors, polygonal scanners, piezoelectric scanners etc. This means it can be readily applied to fields beyond imaging and microscopy, such as laser fabrication, 3D printing, optical metrology, and ultrafast spectroscopy.

14206717.label: Realisation of objectives
14206717.value: Objectives 1, 2 and 3 have been completed fully. Objectives 1 and 2. We have achieved an imaging speed of 6 frames per second using our prism design and compressed sensing algorithms. This was a breakthrough for THz imaging and was published in Nature Communications. There are also several news articles about it in both Chinese and English. Objective 3. We have developed a robust protocol for measuring healthy subjects which enables meaningful comparisons to be made between and within subjects. We investigated how contact pressure between the skin and the imaging window affects the rate of occlusion and customised pressure sensors with real time feedback so that consistent measurements of volunteers were made. Comparing healthy subjects 30seconds after the onset of occlusion gives a robust parameter for comparisons. Objective 4. Due to the covid-19 pandemic it has not been possible to do patient studies, however we have further developed our instrumentation to be able to do the first THz in vivo ellipsometry measurements of human skin (journal article 12) and this also was reported in the media.

14206717.label: Major findings and research outcome
14206717.value: 1. Real-time THz imaging with a single-pixel detector Nature Communications.. IF 12.1 (Journal (J) article 9) In this work we developed a single-pixel terahertz camera reaching 100 times faster acquisition than the previous state-of-the-art without adding any significant costs to the entire system or sacrificing the sub-picosecond temporal resolution needed for the most sought-after applications. The THz modulation was achieved by optically modulating our in-house THz silicon based modulator (detailed in journal article 7) with a digital micro-mirror device (DMD) and is a breakthrough for increasing the speed of THz imaging. Several press reports have been released about this work and the article was accessed over 2500 times within the first 10 weeks of publication (2640, 3rd Aug) It has now been downloaded nearly 10000 times (Nov 2021). 2. Exploiting Complementary Terahertz Ellipsometry Configurations to Probe the Hydration and Cellular Structure of Skin in vivo, Advanced Photonics Research. Nov 2020 (J 12). This paper demonstrates the first in vivo measurement of the THz birefringence of human skin. The proposed ellipsometer employs a unique two-prism system to obtain enriched spectral information from different incident angles and polarizations. This provides insightful quantitative information that cannot be non-invasively obtained by other techniques. The approach introduces a new functionality of terahertz as a structural-probing technique, rather than just a hydration-sensing tool, which is particularly promising for monitoring and treatment of skin conditions including skin cancer. The breakthrough achievements in this work will pave the way for THz technology to mature to reach such clinical applications. Moreover, the revolutionary characterization capability will further benefit numerous studies on materials with multiple unknown parameters arising from their complicated structure, thus impacting a wide range of applications in the future. 3. In vivo skin studies and application to skin treatments Having established that contact pressure affects the THz response (J1) and that occlusion is a useful parameter (J2), we then developed a robust measurement protocol (J5) and applied it to study existing treatments. In journal articles 3, 11 and 13, we apply our findings to evaluate skin products including scar treatments, transdermal drug delivery through micro/nano needles, and moisturisers.

14206717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14206717.value: This project shows great potential for further development – the imaging speeds have been significantly increased and measurement, algorithm and analysis techniques in place for applying the technology to different applications. The work is being continued by Professor Emma MacPherson, now at Warwick university, and there are plans to measure skin cancer patients in early 2022.

14206717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14206717.value: THz light is a million times lower energy than x-rays, so is safe for screening and diagnosis. In this project we have increased the speed of THz imaging to be 100 times faster than the state of the art, with a view to ultimately applying this to the detection of skin cancer. We have used the high sensitivity of THz light to water to probe the changes in skin caused by occlusion and have investigated how the THz reflectivity changes with contact pressure and occlusion duration. We have developed robust protocols and characterisation algorithms for measuring healthy skin to account for variables due to person-to-person variation and fluctuations in the THz system. In this way we have also studied and monitored the effects of different types of skin products to the skin.

14207017.value: 該項目旨在研究軟粘彈性環境下蝸牛式運動的有效性，基於此研發一種適用於消化道的仿蝸牛軟體機器人。 消化道是癌症高發區域。例如結腸直腸癌（CRC）發病率在香港排名第一，胃癌排名第六。早期篩查和早期治療是降低消化道相關癌症發病率和死亡率的有效方法。內窺鏡是目前胃腸道檢測及治療的金標準，其主要缺陷在於：患者耐受性差，需要鎮靜及存在穿孔風險一種舒適的篩查方法是非常有必要的，尤其是針對具有高發病率風險及低耐受性的老年人。膠囊內窺鏡存在無痛，無需鎮靜的優點。然而，現有的膠囊內窺鏡在消化道內缺少主動運動。這大大降低了其在檢測中的有效性。主動式膠囊內窺鏡的研究關鍵在於消化道內的有效運動模式。現有的膠囊內窺鏡主動運動模式包括爬行（蚯蚓式，腿狀，膨脹式，真空式）和游泳。爬行方法依賴於脹大/夾持腸壁以獲得足夠的固定，而腸壁會隨之一起膨脹，這極大地降低了效率。游泳的方式要求胃部充滿液體，然而液體會迅速排空。由此可見，這些方法並不是消化道內運動的最佳選擇。 在這項研究中，我們打算研究一種用於軟粘彈性環境的新型蝸牛狀運動方法。蝸牛可適應多種地形，包括軟粘彈性環境。它通過粘液粘附周圍環境，在柔軟的腹足內行成一列行波推動蝸牛運動。這種方式即便在倒置時也有效，而且不會損傷環境。因此，蝸牛狀運動是消化道內運動的一個潛在有效方式。為了驗證和評估其在消化道內的有效性，我們將開發一個模擬蝸牛運動的軟體機器人並在離體胃腸道樣本中進行實驗評估。 研究團隊在仿生機器人方面（包括軟機器人和醫療機器人）擁有多年的經驗，過往的工作受到國際同行認可。我們預計這項研究最終將衍生出一種舒適的消化道檢測裝置並促進大眾早期篩查和治療從而大大降低消化道癌症的發病率和死亡率。在該項目中研發的技術也將推動軟體機器人的研究工作。

14207017.label: Realisation of objectives
14207017.value: This project aims to study the snail-like locomotion in the soft viscoelastic environment and develop a soft snail-like robot that can crawl in these environments, e.g., the ex vivo pig intestine. It contains two main objectives and we have fully achieved these. The first objective is to understand the snail locomotion mechanism and develop a soft robot (snailBot) mimicking the snail locomotion, which includes: modelling the wet adhesive force generated by the mucus layer; modelling the prograde peristalsis locomotion of land snails both on rigid substrate and soft substrate; design and prototype a soft robot (snailBot) to mimic the prograde peristalsis locomotion. The second objective is to evaluate the efficacy of the snail-like locomotion in the soft viscoelastic environment experimentally, which include: evaluate the forward speed, and payload ability of the snailBot in the soft viscoelastic environment with different settings, including flat plan and inclined plan; ex vivo test of the snailBot in pig colon and stomach. Mucus is one of the important components in snail locomotion. The rheological property of the natural mucus demonstrates that the steady shear viscosity of the natural snail mucus will drop significantly once the shear stress reaches a yielding point. The mucus is modelled as a Bingham liquid. A synthetic mucus was developed in the lab. Two candidate gels are considered, including the Laponite RD and Carbopol. From the Lissajous curve and viscosity test comparisons, the Laponite RD could better mimic the snail natural mucus. Synthetic mucus with different concentrations were studied, including 3%, 5%, and 8%. The 3% Laponite RD solution shows good mobility and low viscosity. The 8% Laponite RD solution is gel-like and with little mobility. In the later study, 5% Laponite RD solution is used. The water in the mucus would evaporate. To keep the mobility, the mucus cannot be exposed in air for over 12 hours. When the mucus is smeared on the surface and the air is dry, the evaporation is faster. This explains why snails usually show up after rainy days. Another important component in the snail locomotion is the peristalsis underneath its soft pedal. This peristalsis can be modelled as a travelling wave, which can be controlled by the amplitude profile, wavelength, and frequency. There are two kinds of travelling waves, one is prograde and the other is retrograde. In the land snails, the prograde wave is adopted. To mimic the snail’s pedal wave, several kinds of snail robots were designed and developed with soft materials, e.g. EcoFlex 0010, EcoFlex 0030, Dragon skin, etc. The first snailBot contains four pneumatic chambers. An actuation system containing four solenoid valves and an Arduino control board was used to drive the snailBot. From this pilot work, we identified that EcoFlex 0010 is a better option than the other candidates for the soft pedal. However, we cannot use unified wall thickness for the air chambers as when the chamber is inflated, the wall will deform, and this would significantly reduce the pedal wave amplitude. On the other hand, to generate a smoother waveform, the number of chambers needs increase. Therefore, we developed a second snailBot. In this snailBot, eight air chambers are designed. To accommodate the control of eight air chambers, we developed another actuation system containing eight solenoid valves. These two snailbots are developed by one undergraduate student as pilot studies. Later, we recruited one postgraduate student and continued the study. In his study, three more snailBots were developed. In the previous two snailBots, the soft pedal shape is rectangular. This would increase the impedance during locomotion. Inspired by the snail pedal, we designed a third snailBot with a fusiform soft pedal. Also, the front part is with an inclined surface to reduce the impedance by the mucus. A dynamometer is used to measuring the wet adhesive force with the synthetic mucus. Results show that with the 5% Laponite RD, the normal force is 0.667 N and the shear force is 0.232 N. This normal force is strong enough to support the snailBot move on surfaces with different inclinations, including upside-down. The maximum velocities of this snailBot with 3%, 5% and 8% Laponite RD are 17 mm/min, 19mm/min, and 25mm/min respectively. This speed is attained at 1 Hz wave frequency and does not change significantly with surface incline angles. The snailBot’s performance is affected by the elasticity of the surface. When it moves on soft surface as thin silicon pad or pig intestine, the speed decrease. Its maximum speed is reduced to 8.5 mm/min with 5% Laponite RD at 0.75 Hz. To improve the speed of the snailBot, we designed a fourth version with a slim structure. This snailBot is 60 mm long with four bellow-type chambers. The weight is 4.2 g. With this design, the stroke of each cycle is increased and the friction along the moving direction is further reduced. To better regulate the airflow into the snailBot, a syringe-type actuation system was developed. This actuation system allows controlling the pressure as well as volume inside the air chambers. The maximum speed is 90 mm/min, which is 5 times faster than the previous one. As we all know that snails could not only move forward/backward, but also turn around. To realize this, we developed the fifth snailBot that is composed of two parallel chamber arrays like that in the fourth version. By the differential actuation of the two chamber arrays, the snailBot could turn around. Therefore, this snailBot has three gaits, including forward/backward, turning left, and turning right. To accommodate the motion control of this multi-gait snailBot, we developed a central patten generator (CPG) controller for the low-level control and a reinforced learning network for high-level control. A virtual environment is built based on the robot kinematics and the CPG controller to train the reinforced learning network. The Actor-critic Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) was used to train the agents. After training, once the target position on the surface is given, the snailBot could plan the quasi-optimal path and move towards the target automatically. The maximum speed of this multi-gait snailBot is 110 mm/min, which is comparable to the speed of colonoscope insertion, i.e., 104.2 mm/min.

14207017.label: Major findings and research outcome
14207017.value: This project investigated the bio-inspired locomotion in soft elastic environment and developed soft robots that could crawl in such environment. Particularly, a snail-like soft robot has been developed for locomotion inside the gastrointestinal tract. The snails can move effectively on various environment, including soft and elastic environment. They secret a layer of mucus to adhere themselves to the surface and then generate a travelling wave underneath to move on the mucus. In this project, at first, we studied the mucus and developed a mathematic model to describe its non-Newtonian behaviour. The mucus deformed elastically like a solid at first, once the stress reached the yielding value, the mucus behaves like a liquid with the stress dropped to a constant value. A synthetic mucus is developed with 5% Laponite RD and 95% water, which demonstrated a similar property of the snail mucus. To mimic the travelling wave, we designed and fabricated several soft snails by using silicon rubber, e.g., EcoFlex. In the first snail, it has an array of air chambers. By sequentially actuate the air chambers, both prograde and retrograde travelling waves can be generated. In the second snail robot, two arrays of air chambers are designed. This enabled the snail turning around. To control the air chambers, we developed two kinds of pneumatic systems. One is with solenoid pumps, which can well control the pressure but difficult to control the air volume inside the chamber. The other one is with syringe pumps, which forms a closed system and can better control the volume. A central pattern generator (CPG) based controller is developed to generate the control signal of the travelling wave. This low-level control mimics that existed in natural organisms. For the high-level control and motion planning, a reinforced learning method is used. The snail robot could move forward/backward and turn around on different surfaces, including rigid, soft, and elastic surfaces. By the wet adhesive force, the snail robot could also climb on inclined walls and even crawl up-side-down. The speed of the snail robot can reach 110 mm/min. The snail robot also demonstrated effective locomotion on ex vivo pig intestines. In addition to the snail robot, we also investigated other bio-inspired locomotion, such as earthworm-like locomotion in the soft tubular environment and fish-like locomotion in open watery environment. The results are published in top peer-reviewed journals and leading international robotics conferences as shown in part C.

14207017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14207017.value: Locomotion inside the soft and elastic environment is quite challenging, as the environment will deform largely during the interaction with the robot. The snail-like locomotion relies on the wet-adhesive force to adhere to the surface and use the travelling wave to propel the robot. It has excellent adaptability to various surface conditions. In the current pilot study, we well demonstrated that the snail-like locomotion is promising. However, there are still several challenges to be solved. The first is the synthesized mucus cannot fully mimic the natural mucus, therefore impairs the wet-adhesive force. These reflected in the yield strength and the transition time between liquid state and solid state. The second is the material for the robot development needs be further improved. The silicon rubber is soft, however it cannot full mimic the texture of the biological tissue. When the curvature of the surface is large, the robot cannot fully conform to the environment. This sacrifices part of the adhesive force and affects its locomotion efficiency. The third is functionality of the snail-like robot. In this pilot study, we haven’t explored the applications yet. In the future, the robot can be developed to perform various tasks, such as endoscopy and biopsy.

14207017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14207017.value: Diseases, particularly cancer, in the gastrointestinal (GI) tract is frequent. Early diagnosis and treatment are effective ways to improve the cure rate. To diagnose diseases, the prerequisite is to reach the region of interest inside the GI tract, which is soft, elastic, with large size variation, and full of mucus. Currently, there is no device/robot that can adapt to all these changes. Inspired by the snails, we developed a soft snail-like robot and explored its navigation in the GI tract environment for the first time. The fundamental principle of snail locomotion was studied, and a mathematical model was established for the mucus. Three snail-like robots, two actuation systems and a central patten generator-based controller were developed. Due to the wet-adhesive from the synthesized mucus, the developed snail-like robot could crawl through various surface conditions, including rigid/soft surfaces, dry/wet surfaces, curved/flat surfaces and horizontal/vertical/up-side-down surfaces. The robot could move forward/backward and turn around. The maximum speed is 110mm/min. It can also crawl on ex vivo pig intestine. With the support of this project, we trained two postgraduate students and provided research opportunity to two undergraduate students. The research results were published in leading journals and conferences in robotic field.

14207117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14207117.value: Conventional silicon microdisk resonators have quality factors (Q) typically limited to under a million because of the scattering of the whispering gallery modes by the roughness of the sidewalls at the circumference of the microdisk. In this project we propose to address this limitation by the development of wedge-shaped edge microdisk resonators with integrated waveguide directional couplers. Tapered fiber-coupled ultra-high Q silica wedge microdisk resonators, with Q factors of 875 million have previously been demonstrated in silica by photolithography and wet etching, but this approach has not yet been successfully applied for ultra-high Q silicon microdisk resonators. The dramatic enhancement in Purcell factor possible from microdisks which have ultra-high Q and small radii will enable efficient spontaneous four wave mixing and enhance the generation rate of quantum entangled signal and idler photons at multiple different optical frequency comb resonances. Silicon has two orders of magnitude larger Kerr nonlinearity than silica, and this combined with the smaller mode volumes made possible by the higher refractive index of silicon and the ultra-high Q potentially attainable with wedge-shaped edge silicon microdisk resonators may lead to better performance than possible with silica or hydex glass in the low pump-power regime for generating multiple entangled photons for integrated quantum photonics. In this project we shall design and develop the process for the fabrication of high Q wedge-shaped edge microdisk resonators for the generation of time-bin and frequency entangled states and the integrated photonic devices needed for wavelength filtering, and quantum interference measurements. We also propose to integrate waveguide grating couplers, bus waveguides for coupling light into and out of the resonators, wavelength filters, switches and delay line interferometers to enable the integrated measurement of the quantum interference between the multiple orders of entangled signal and idler photons created by spontaneous four wave mixing in the resonator. We shall optimize the optical dispersion of the silicon microdisk for efficient generation of nonlinear optical frequency combs and experimentally investigate how ultrahigh Q affects the time-bin entanglement among the different frequency lines of the optical frequency comb. Successful experimental realization of the ultra-high Q microdisk resonator will enable the generation of multiphoton time-bin and frequency entangled states and lead to integrated quantum systems which can generate and measure multiple-photon quantum entangled states. The proposed research is aimed at advancing the development of integrated silicon quantum photonics for applications in quantum communications and quantum computing. 本項目中，我們提出研發與波導方向藕合器集成在壹起 的楔形邊緣微盤諧振腔。 該微盤諧振腔具有超高Q因子和極小的半徑，能夠極大地增強 Purcell因子，從而可以實現高效自發四波混頻並提高位於 多個不同諧振光學頻率梳齒上 的量子糾纏信號光子與閑頻 光子對的產生速率。在本項目中，我們將設計並開發 用於產生時間糾纏與頻率糾纏態的高Q因子楔形邊緣 微盤諧振腔，且該諧振腔還可用於集成光子器件所需 的濾波器以及量子幹涉測量系統。我們將優化該矽基微盤 的光學色散特性，使其能夠高效產生非線性光學頻率梳， 並實驗研究超高Q因子對光學頻率梳中不同頻率線間 時間糾纏特性的影響。超高Q因子微盤諧振腔的成功 實現將為產生多光子時間糾纏與頻率糾纏態鋪平道路， 並有助於實現能夠產生並測量多光子量子糾纏態的集成 量子系統。

14207117.label: Realisation of objectives
14207117.value: Objective 1 - to design and fabricate ultra-high Q micro-resonators and integrate them with silicon waveguides and test the ultra-high Q micro-resonators Our research towards objective 1 included the following research activities: (i) We designed and engineered the optical dispersion of multimoded silicon microdisk resonators, with radius of 27.2microns and coupled to multimode silicon waveguides. The resonators supported high Q resonances with loaded Q of 262,000 for the outcoupled TE0 and 174000 and TE 1 modes. We studied the quantum interference between photon pairs of the same higher-order whispering gallery modes populated by spontaneous four-wave mixing in the micro-disk resonator: the photon pairs of the first two quasi-TE0 and quasi-TE1 radial modes was measured to have net visibilities of Vnet ∼ 98 ± 0.8% and Vnet ∼ 94 ± 2.6%, respectively. The results show the potential for achieving higher-dimensional quantum states using the higher-order radial modes of a micro-disk resonator coupled with an integrated waveguide. [J. OSA B 37, p.2231, Aug 2020] ; (ii) We designed and fabricated near zero total dispersion multimode ultra-high Q silicon ring resonators. The resonators had a measured loaded Q of 1.8 million. We showed that they could be used to produce many frequency comb lines with very modest input pump power of only 0.3mW. [Applied Physics Letters vol. 117 article 221103, August 2020]; (iii) We designed and fabricated silicon racetrack resonators which had ultrahigh loaded Q of about 2.8 million. For ultrahigh Q resonators, we discovered that coherent anti-stokes Raman scattering can lead to anti-stokes lasing when the input pump power was above 2.5mW, while Raman lasing at the Stokes wavelength could start with input pump powers as low as 0.3mW. [ACS Photonics vol 8 p. 3462, 2021] Objective 2 - To optimize the design and fabrication of the micro-resonators for spontaneous four wave mixing and generation of quantum entangled photons With our developing understanding of the strongly competing processes of Raman scattering in the silicon microresonators fabricated with a loaded Q > 1million (see previous paragraph on objective 1 results), our exploration of alternative strategies other than increasing Q, for improving the efficiency of resonators for efficient spontaneous four wave mixing came to prominence in this project. We obtained excellent results from (i) a collaborative work with Technical University of Eindhoven where we engineered the dispersion of indium phosphide membrane microring resonators on silicon wafers (the devices were fabricated at Eindhoven) and we showed the feasibility of exploiting the 1 order of magnitude higher third order nonlinearity (compared with silicon) of InP for use in highly efficient spontaneous four wave mixing for the generation of entangled photons. The InP microring resonators had modest loaded Q of 40,000-55,000 and we demonstrated the use of these InP microring resonators for highly efficient heralded single photon generation using only 47 microwatts (CW) pump power [J. of Optics vol. 21 article 115201, 2019] and generation of quantum entangled photons [ Applied Physics Letters vol. 114 article 021104, 2019]. These works were also included as part of an invited paper [Phys. Status Solidi A vol 217, article #1900606, 2020]. (ii) We also designed and integrated silicon microdisk resonators with Q ~85000 for the generation of correlated photons by spontaneous four wave mixing and demonstrated a spectral brightness of 48.4 million pairs/second/ square millwatt per GHz [CLEO 2019, paperSTh1H.2] (iii) In addition we also further explored the use of the near-zero dispersion silicon microring resonators for quantum frequency comb generation. Using the near-zero dispersion single mode silicon microring resonators, which had loaded Q of about 90,000, we observed the efficient generation of 12 optical frequency comb lines with a modest pump power of only 8.9mW. [J. of Optics vol 23, paper 10LT02, 2021]. Objective 3 : To design, fabricate and test the integrated silicon devices needed for the on-chip quantum interference measurements of the quantum entangled photons Our research activities towards objective 3 concentrated on the difficult problem of filtering out and removing the pump photons from the signal and idler photons produced by spontaneous four wave mixing. With extinction ratio of over 100dB being needed, this is one of the most challenging problems that must be solved to enable on-chip quantum interference measurements. Our research activities for objective 3 included (i) the design and fabrication of coupled resonator optical waveguide (CROW) optical filters which served to remove the pump photons. Our initial results in 2019 only achieved 60dB pump rejection and required the help of off-chip filter for the quantum correlation measurements [CLEO 2019, paperSTh1H.2] (ii) As the 60dB pump rejection obtained in 2019 work was insufficient to reject the pump photons, we improved the design of the spectral filters by using tunable second order CROW filters, where we designed two cascaded filters on a single chip and then cascaded two different chips in order to avoid the limitation of scattered pump photons which could produce a background pump photon level in a single chip solution at around -70dB (which can still be 30dB larger than the signal and idler photons). Using two 2nd order CROW filters on one chip and two 2nd order CROW filters on a separate chip (in order to remove the background pump photons) we achieved >110dB pump rejection [Optics Letters vol 45 p. 1289-1292, 2020]. We further improved the results to 112dB pump rejection by using two cascaded 2nd order CROW filter on one chip and only one CROW filter on the second chip [CLEO 2020, paper SM3O.2 ]. (ii) We further improved on the pump rejection on a single chip by using two CROW filters and we demonstrated the integration of the cascaded CROW filters with the thermal phase shifter to tune their bandwidth and resonance wavelength and spectrally match the wavelengths of the signal and idler quantum correlated photons produced by spontaneous four wave mixing in a long silicon waveguide. These second order integrated CROW filters produced 96dB pump rejection with the monolithically integrated source of quantum correlated photons on the silicon photonics platform [ Optics Letters, vol. 46, p.134-137, January 2021].

14207117.label: Major findings and research outcome
14207117.value: The proposed approach of using ultra-high Q microresonators is not necessarily the best approach for obtaining high spectral brightness sources of quantum correlated photons because of the presence of competing Raman lasing, and the increased difficulty of stabilizing the signal and idler output wavelengths in the presence of themo-optic nonlinearities. Although we succeeded in objective 1, and made resonators with loaded Q of over 3 million, our results showed that the ultrahigh Q resonators are unsuited for integrated quantum photonics, but instead they are extremely efficient for stimulated Raman scattering and making Raman lasers. We were surprised to observe both Stokes and Anti-Stokes Raman lasing output from the ultrahigh Q resonators [ACS Photonics vol 8 p. 3462, 2021] and we observed outputs of 12 different optical frequency comb lines from four wave mixing [J. of Optics vol 23, paper 10LT02, 2021]. We also showed that silicon microdisk resonators, supporting the resonances of different radial modes with loaded Q of about 140,000-260,000, could be used as sources of correlated photon pairs produced by spontaneous four wave mixing of the higher-order whispering gallery mode: the photon pairs of the first two quasi-TE0 and quasi-TE1 radial modes were measured to have net quantum interference visibility of Vnet ∼ 98 ± 0.8% and Vnet ∼ 94 ± 2.6%, respectively. These results show the potential for achieving higher-dimensional quantum states using the higher-order radial modes of a micro-disk resonator coupled with an integrated waveguide. [J. OSA B 37, p.2231, Aug 2020] The integration of III-V microring resonators offer an order of magnitude improvement in third order nonlinearity which could be used for efficient heralded single photon generation [J. of Optics vol. 21 article 115201, 2019] and the generation of quantum entangled photons [ Applied Physics Letters vol. 114 article 021104, 2019]. We designed and fabricated the second order CROW filters which could achieve 112dB pump rejection when two separate silicon photonic chips were used for the cascaded filters in order to reduce the background count of randomly scattered pump photons [CLEO 2020, paper SM3O.2 ]. We achieved over 96dB pump rejection, sufficient to remove the pump from the output of the long silicon waveguide producing the correlated photon pairs from spontaneous four wave mixing. [ Optics Letters, vol. 46, p.134-137, January 2021]. These works pave the way for the using silicon photonics as a monolithic platform for the generation and measurement of entangled photons.

14207117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14207117.value: There exists a huge potential to develop integrated quantum photonics for different practical applications, taking advantage of the extreme scalability possible on the silicon photonics platform. Some specific suggestions for further development include (i) development of integrated single photon detectors for monolithic integration of the sources of quantum entangled photons with the integrated filter developed in this project for a completely monolithoc solution for integrated quantum photonics (ii) development of integrated devices for generating high order quantum entangled photons (iii) Further development of the low scattering loss waveguides for use in monolithic integrated Franson interferometers with balanced losses despite the large differences in path lengths (and different scattering losses). (iv) Photonic circuit development for use of the integrated quantum entangled sources in quantum computing and quantum enhanced metrology.

14207117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14207117.value: This project employed the mature fabrication technologies developed for the silicon microelectronic industry, to make optical integrated circuits where the quantum nature of light can be exploited to produce quantum entangled biphoton states. We showed that it is possible to generate and filter the quantum light sources using the silicon photonic circuits and we advanced the state of the art in optical filters by which could have selectivity of 4 billion to one (96dB) in a single chip and 158 billion to 1 (112 dB) using two chips for rejecting the classical pump photons and leaving only the quantum entangled biphotons produced from the monolithically integrated silicon waveguides. Our work shows the practicality of using silicon photonic integrated circuits to build scalable quantum photonic circuits for applications in quantum computing and in quantum enhanced sensors.

14207517.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14207517.value: 固態鋰氧電池正極-電解質界面的模型系統研究：反應動力學、電極穩定性和衰減機理

14207517.label: Project Objectives
14207517.value: This project aims to generate the fundamental knowledge required for designing a stable and efficient solid-state Li-oxygen cathode-electrolyte interface. Specifically, we aim to (i) identify the sources of chemical instability, kinetic/transport losses, and cycling degradation mechanism of the solid-state carbon and carbon-free ruthenium (Ru) oxygen-cathodes and (ii) examine the effect of electrode surface modifications on the chemical/electrochemical reversibility at the solid-state cathode-electrolyte interfaces. The technical objectives subordinate to our overall objective are as follows: We will design and fabricate two levels of model electrode including dense thin-film electrode and particle-based film electrode to obtain in-depth intrinsic information on the factors responsible for combinatory effects. We select carbon and Ru as the model electrodes and lithium aluminium germanium phosphate (LAGP) as model solid electrolyte owing to their unique chemical/electrochemical stability/properties. We will modify the carbon model electrodes to investigate the effect of carbon surface functionalization (such as OH/COOH/fluorine) and/or plasma treatments (O2/Ar) on the chemical stability and electrochemical activity of a solid-state carbon-based oxygen-cathode on LAGP. We will modify the ruthenium model electrodes to investigate the effect of heat-treatment atmosphere (such as Ar, dry air) and/or plasma treatments (O2/Ar) on the chemical stability and electrochemical activity of solid-state ruthenium oxygen-cathode on LAGP. We will apply comprehensive electrochemical, microscopic and in situ spectroscopic techniques (such as online electrochemical mass spectroscopy, in situ ambient pressure XPS, in situ XRD) to study the proposed model electrode-electrolytes with systematically varied electrode area and triple-phase-boundary length to probe the reaction intermediates/products, transport/interfacial resistances, morphological evolutions and parasitic reactions of the solid-state Li-oxygen reactions.

14207517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14207517.value: 此研究項目計劃利用模型系統尋找固態鋰氧電池中正極-電解質界面的化學不穩定性、動力學/傳遞損失和循環衰減等問題的根源，並探究電極表面改性對反應效率和可逆性的影響。 鋰-空氣或鋰-氧氣電池因能量密度有望達到傳統鋰離子電池的2-5倍而掀起了相關研究的熱潮。然而鋰氧電池技術仍然受制於其不穩定性，即中間產物/終產物和液體電解質、碳電極之間的不穩定問題。電池在循環過程中會積累大量的副產物，嚴重影響性能。 利用固態陶瓷電解質取代易降解的液體電解質是一個能顯著減少副反應的可行方法。然而，直到現在，即使在低電流密度和容量的條件下，固態鋰-氧電池仍然只能提供有限的循環性能。碳/過氧化鋰、固態電解質/過氧化鋰、碳/固態電解質等界面可能存在的副反應和氧氣還原/析出反應緩慢的動力學特性均有可能是性能受限的原因。由於學界對固態鋰-氧電池中正極-電解質界面的化學不穩定性、動力學/傳遞損失和循環衰減等問題的根源仍知之甚少，固態鋰-氧電池的進一步發展仍然舉步維艱。 在這一研究項目中，我們將設計和製造模型電極 - 電解質系統，以獲得深層內在科学规律，解耦在固態鋰-氧電池正極-電解質界面有組合效應的各個過程。由於碳（C）具有極強實用性，釕（Ru）具有優異的催化活性，這裡我們選擇C和釕Ru作為兩個模型電極。同時基於磷酸鋁鋰（LAGP）在導電性，高電壓穩定性和大氣穩定性上具有很大的優勢，我們選擇LAGP作為電解質。我們將在緻密的LAGP固體電解質上製造兩個級別的模型電極，包括設計結構的緻密薄膜電極和顆粒基膜電極。我們的目標是（1）研究固態碳和無碳Ru電極的反應動力學，反應產物，化學反應活性和衰減機理，並與液體醚類解質進行比較; （2）研究碳表面改性（即表面官能化（OH / COOH /氟）和等離子體處理）對反應化學穩定性和電化學活性的影響; （3）研究無碳Ru正極的熱處理氣氛和等離子體處理對化學穩定性和電化學活性的影響。我們將使用具有系統變化電極面積和三相邊界長度的模型電極，以及常用的電化學手段（例如電化學阻抗譜），顯微和光譜技術（例如原位環境壓力X射線光電子能譜，在線電化學質譜法，原位X射線衍射）來探測在提出的锂-氧電極- 電解質體系裡的反應中間體/產物，傳遞/界面損失，形態演化和副反應。 通過該項目的研究，我們將更深入的了解鋰氧正極-電解質界面的基本過程，這些將對未來設計穩定高效的全固態鋰-氧電池提供指導。

14207517.label: Realisation of objectives
14207517.value: We fabricated model electrodes using dense thin-film and particle-based electrodes based on Ru-containing electrodes on the lithium aluminium germanium phosphate (LAGP) as model solid electrolyte. In addition to Ru, we also synthesize non-precious metal based metal oxide catalysts and compare with Ru based catalyst. We employed several design principles to design and fabricate the electrodes. We maximized three-phase-boundary (TPB) areas as they are the locations where the electrolyte (Li+ conducting phase), cathode (electron conducting phase) and oxygen gas (gas phase) meet. In addition, we control the porosity of the electrode as it determines the space for storing the solid product Li2O2. We then evaluate the chemical compatibility between cathode materials and the solid-state electrolyte. We minimized the interfacial resistance by constructing well-connected Li+ ion conducting channel and electron conducting networks. We optimized the porosity by adjusting the volume/mass ratios of the electrolyte powder to the pore formers. We control the pore sizes and pore size distributions of the backbone by tuning particle sizes and particle size distributions of the electrolyte powder and pore formers. We designed and synthesized a series of Cr2O3 catalysts with varying fraction of high-energy facet by introducing TiO2 inhibitor and examine the role of high-energy facet on Li-O2 oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity (Lu et al. Joule, 2018, 2, 8, 1511). We examined how the surface chemistry and functionalization of carbon affect the chemical stability and electrochemical activity of oxygen electrode on LAGP. We performed surface treatment and functionalization using different gas environment and revealed that the carbon consists of oxygen containing functional groups such as carbonyl (C=O) group acting as active reaction site for oxygen reduction reaction, which guide the future design and synthesis of stable carbon oxygen electrode for Li-oxygen batteries. We tested the carbon-free RuO2/LAGP solid-state Li-O2 batteries and revealed that that loading of the cathode/catalyst in the solid-state Li-O2 cells is a critical factor to improve the energy efficiency and discharge capacity and the electrical conductivity of the cathode is important for achieving high-performance solid-state Li-O2 cells. Accordingly, we further incorporated high-surface-area ketjen black carbon with RuO2 electrode onto the integrated LAGP solid-state electrolyte network and optimized its electrochemical performance. To investigate the electrochemical reaction and chemical evolution at Li-O2 reaction interface, we probed the reaction interface of the charge reaction, or oxygen evolution reaction (Li2O2-oxidaiton) in Li-O2 ¬single cell via isotope-labelled techniques combining time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (ToF-SIMS) and on-line electrochemical mass spectroscopy (OEMS) (Lu et al. Angew. Chem. Int. Ed., 2019, 58, 6962). We real-time monitor the gas consumption and evolution behavior during discharging and charging of Li-O2 cells using OEMS. The labelled 18O2 (outer layer) gas was firstly detected upon charging for both pure VC and Ru/VC electrode. No 16O2 (inner layer) evolution was detected for both cells before reaching one quarter of the capacity (~ 300 mAh gC-1). The 16O2 dominated the oxygen evolution at the late charging stage after started to evolve from 300 mAh gC-1. These observations provide direct evidence to show that oxygen is evolved from the Li2O2/electrolyte interface for both cells with and without Ru catalyst. In this process, the Li2O2 particles retain continuous contact with the catalyst/electrode, explaining why solid catalyst is effective in oxidizing solid Li2O2 without losing contact. This is consistent with our previous study showing that Li2O2-oxidation occurs in contact with the catalyst-electrode without losing contact to the catalyst. Furthermore, we developed in situ Li-O2 cells operating under ambient pressure X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (APXPS) to examine the change of surface chemistry of the electrode upon oxygen reduction reaction and oxygen evolution reaction. We revealed side reactions occurred during battery operating associated with carbonate formation, which suggests that effective electrode design should protect the carbon electrode from forming carbonate-containing species.

14207517.label: Major findings and research outcome
14207517.value: We evaluate the chemical compatibility between cathode materials and the solid-state electrolyte. We minimized the interfacial resistance by constructing well-connected Li+ ion conducting channel and electron conducting networks. We designed and synthesized non-precious metal oxide Cr2O3 catalysts with varying fraction of high-energy facets by introducing TiO2 inhibitor. We revealed that the Li-O2 OER activity increase with increasing fraction of high-energy facets. This suggests that the high activity of Cr2O3 can be attributed to stronger bonding with OER intermediate owing to the larger number of uncoordinated atoms. We demonstrated a highly active Cr2O3-based catalyst that shows much higher Li-O2 OER activity than the state-of-the-art precious metal Ru/VC catalyst with improved oxygen recovery efficiency and lower parasitic gas evolution. (Part C #1) We probed the reaction interface of the charge reaction, or oxygen evolution reaction (Li2O2-oxidaiton) in Li-O2 ¬single cell via isotope-labelled techniques combining time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (ToF-SIMS) and on-line electrochemical mass spectroscopy (OEMS). We demonstrate that oxygen loss during Li2O2 oxidation starts at the outer part, that is, the Li2O2/electrolyte interface, regardless of the catalyst, under the practical Li-O2 cell conditions. Our study offers critical insights into the OER mechanism of rechargeable Li-O2 batteries and the developed isotope labelling technique can be universally applied to reveal the reaction mechanism in other metal-air (Na/K-O2) batteries (Part C #4). We further revealed a strong solvent-controlled Li2O2-oxidation reaction mechanism. Preferential formation of soluble LiO2(sol) in the high-donicity solvents could account for low O2 evolution and severe CO2 evolution due to low chemical stability of soluble LiO2(sol) in the electrolyte. Our work offers new insights into resolving the discrepancy in the Li-O2 charging mechanism and designing strategies to achieve efficient and long-life Li-O2 batteries. (Part C #2). In addition to oxygen electrode, we address the issue of Li anode by exploiting biphenyl complex as the negative electrode, forming a metal-anode-free organic–O2 battery that demonstrated an unprecedented cycling stability of 3,000 cycles (average CE > 99.84%) at a high current density of 4.0 mA cm−2. The side products were estimated to be less than 0.3% of the total discharge product per cycle. Our work demonstrates that the long-term cyclability of the O2 cathode can be achieved by simultaneously exploiting the kinetically fast O2/KO2 redox, replacing the metal anode with a stable organic liquid anode and eliminating electrode crosstalk. This design knowledge can be applied to improve the cyclability of other alkali metal–oxygen batteries.

14207517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14207517.value: Future work on air electrode design to maximize cathode capacity and cell energy, reducing the ionic and interfacial resistances of the ion-conducting solid-state membrane and device engineering of full-cell assembling and production is critical to achieve a stable and practical oxygen batteries. To further probe the charging mechanism and charging reaction intermediates, more advanced in-situ techniques such as in-situ UV–vis and in-situ Raman should be applied to qualitatively probe the charging intermediate further provide a full picture of the OER mechanism. These in-situ techniques could provide real-time information regarding the Li2O2-decompostion upon charging which is more possibly to detect the highly unstable intermediate. In addition, more in-depth insights into the formation mechanism of singlet oxygen and approaches to prevent or stabilize singlet oxygen is an important direction to be developed. More in-situ, cross-validated technique combining the real cell operation condition should be used to achieve a comprehensive understanding of the OER interface and OER catalysis mechanism.

14207517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14207517.value: Lithium-air (Li-air) or Li-oxygen batteries have attracted intensive attention in recent years owing to their potential to provide higher gravimetric energy density than conventional Li-ion batteries. However, the Li-oxygen system suffers from a poor cycle life (<100 cycles), low rate capability and poor round-trip efficiency (65–70%). These disadvantages stem directly from scientific challenges, including sluggish discharge and charge reaction kinetics at the oxygen-electrode, and chemical instabilities between reaction intermediates, liquid electrolytes and carbon electrodes. In this project, we identified the sources of chemical irreversibility, kinetic/transport losses, and cycling degradation mechanism of the solid-state carbon and carbon-free ruthenium oxygen-electrodes, and revealed the effect of surface modifications on the chemical/electrochemical reversibility for solid-state Li-oxygen reactions. This project provides a deeper understanding of the fundamental processes of solid-state Li-oxygen cathode-electrolyte interfaces, and its findings will guide the future design of electrodes and electrolytes for stable and efficient solid-state Li-oxygen batteries.
