14207617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14207617.value: Stroke is a leading cause of long-term disabilities worldwide, commonly associated with abnormal muscle coordination and loss of dexterity. Recovery of hand and fingers functions is particularly demanding and challenging, since only around 38% of stroke patients regained some dexterity in their paretic arm at 6 months after stroke. Transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) had recently been shown having feasibility in modulating cortical excitability transiently during motor training in a noninvasive way. The findings support that tDCS and motor practice can positively promote post-stroke motor learning to improve upper-limb motor recovery after stroke. However, the promise of adjunctive stimulation shown in early clinical studies in which the effect of adjunctive stimulation in rehabilitation was positive when compared with rehabilitation delivered alone, could not be replicated in later and larger clinical trials. Optimization of tDCS protocols for stroke rehabilitation therefore becomes crucial. Researchers had recently developed high-definition tDCS (HD-tDCS), which is designed to have better spatial focality, greater influence on cortical excitability and longer lasting effect than conventional tDCS. HD-tDCS opens a new potential to facilitate the brain to relearn motor task after brain lesion, like stroke. The main challenge in applying HD-tDCS is finding the optimal stimulation area on the brain. The restoration of motor functional is highly depended on the remapping into the unimpaired motor-related areas away from the lesion site in the brain. Therefore, we will use neuroimaging techniques (magnetic resonance imaging, MRI and electroencephalography, EEG) and neurophysiological assessments (transcranial magnetic stimulation, TMS) which offer the advantages and capacity of identifying neural correlates of stimulation-induced behavioral gains and measuring interhemispheric imbalance and corticospinal excitability. The results are expected to better determine the optimal stimulation target brain area for HD-tDCS. Computational modeling of neuromodulation will also be developed to allow a detailed examination of tDCS-induced changes in brain activity and enable the visualization of how tDCS modulates ongoing brain activation. The optimized tDCS protocol over the target motor-related areas will be combined with exoskeleton robot hand training. A randomized controlled trial will be conducted with three groups of stroke patients: optimized HD-tDCS, conventional tDCS and sham HD-tDCS. A 10-session training will be provided to evaluate the effectiveness of transient modulation of cortical excitability through tDCS with clinical assessment scores. TMS, MRI and EEG evaluation will be conducted before and after training and at 3-month follow-up, to investigate tDCS-induced neuroplasticity and effects on hand motor function recovery. 中風是全球長期殘疾的主要原因，肌肉協調異常和喪失功能。恢復手和手指功能特別具有挑戰性，因為中風只有38％患者在6個月後恢復了一些靈活性。經顱直流刺激(tDCS)最近已顯示出在運動訓練期間暫時調節皮層興奮性的方式。研究結果支持tDCS和運動能夠積極促進中風後改善上肢功能。因此，中風康復的tDCS方案的優化變得至關重要。 研究人員最近開發了高分辨率tDCS（HD-tDCS），其設計具有更好的集中度，對皮質興奮性的影響更大，並且比常規tDCS具有更長的持久效果。 HD-tDCS開闢了一個新的潛力，以促進大腦在腦損傷之後重新學習，如中風。應用HD-tDCS的主要挑戰是在大腦上找到最佳的刺激位。運動功能的恢復依賴於未受損的運動相關區。因此，我們將使用神經成像技術（磁共振成像和腦電圖）和神經生理學評估（經顱磁刺激，TMS），測量大腦間不平衡和皮質脊髓興奮性的能力。還將開發計算建模，以便詳細檢查tDCS對腦活動的變化。 結合tDCS與外骨骼機器人手訓練， 將進行隨機對照試驗中風患者：HD-tDCS，常規tDCS和對照組。將提供10個課程培訓，TMS，MRI和EEG評估將在培訓前後進行，調查tDCS誘發的神經可塑性和對手功能恢復的影響。

14207617.label: Realisation of objectives
14207617.value: We have achieved all the project objectives with randomized, single-blinded, sham controlled crossover studies to show the effectiveness of the optimized tDCS. The first part of the project has been finished and published in IEEE transactions on Neural Systems and Rehabilitation Engineering. Eleven chronic stroke subjects who suffered from first-ever stroke, and with time since stroke more than 1 year, were recruited to join the high definition tDCS and isometric contraction experiments. Subjects were excluded if they had history of epilepsy, serious cognitive deficits, comprehensive aphasia, and/or metal implants. The first study was a randomized, single-blinded (subjects), sham controlled crossover study. Each subject randomly received three stimulation experiments (anode, cathode and sham) and with at least a one-week washout to prevent confusion effects between the sessions. Electroencephalography (EEG) signals were acquired for each subject following the international 10-20 system, with 64-channel Neuroscan amplifier (SynAmps2, Neuroscan Inc, Herndon, USA) at a sampling frequency of 1000 Hz. while four-channel Electromyography (EMG) was acquired using g.USBamp (g.tec Medical Engineering GmbH, Austria), EEG and EMG electrode impedances were kept under 5 kΩ and 10 kΩ respectively. HD-tDCS system included 1x1 DC stimulator (Soterix Medical, New York City, USA) to generate DC current and a 4x1 high-definition adaptor (Soterix Medical, New York City, USA) to split DC current. A 64-channel Quik-Cap EEG cap was combined with 5 sintered HD-tDCS Ag/AgCl electrodes by replacing the original EEG electrodes with specialized holders. The central stimulation electrode was placed in the ipsilesional motor cortex (C3/C4 according to the lesion side, 10-20 EEG system), and four ring return electrodes were placed around the central electrode. Bipolar EMG electrodes were carefully placed over extensor carpi radialis (ECR) muscles on the affected upper limb with inter-electrode distance at around 20mm. Four sessions of wrist isometric contraction tasks of affected arms were respectively conducted before HD-tDCS, and 10, 30, and 50 minutes after the end of 10 minutes 1mA HD-tDCS. Each isometric contraction session was around 10 minutes containing 5 contraction trials and 1-minute intermediate breaks, each trial lasted for 30 s. After each session, subjects rested until the next session. During the tasks and stimulation periods, subjects were asked to sit comfortably in a quiet radiofrequency-shielded room (Universal Shielding Corp., NY, USA), with their eyes open and fixed on the center screen in front of them, the upper limbs were placed on the table and subjects were asked to avoid large movement. The online EMG feedback system was used to ensure force stability was maintained to approximately 30% of their MVC. The second part of the project involved 25 chronic stroke subjects in our tDCS study. We acquired Functional MRI were acquired before and after stimulation, as a proxy to tDCS-induced neuromodulatory changes. Twelve subjects underwent 20 minutes of conventional tDCS whether as thirteen subjects underwent sham stimulation with the same duration, with anode and cathode placing on the ipsilesional primary motor cortex and contralesional supraorbital ridge, respectively. Whole-brain functional connectivity (FC) analysis was performed with the seed at ipsilesional primary motor cortex (M1) for both groups using resting-state fMRI. Functional connectivity and global efficiency modulation within the ipsilesional sensorimotor network were further explored. Seed-based FC analysis revealed significantly increased FC in surrounding areas of ipsilesional M1. Significant increase in average FC within ipsilesional hemisphere was only observed in the tDCS group (t(11)=2.57, p=0.026), but not in the sham group (t(12)=0.69, p=0.50). Furthermore, enhanced global efficiency was only found in the tDCS group (t(11)=2.30, p=0.042), but not in the sham group (t(12)=0.57, p=0.58). To further understand how tDCS influence neurophysiological changes of the brain, we developed an analytical approach using Finite Element Models, to investigate the tDCS-induced effects on our brain activity. - Realistic finite element models were constructed for all subjects using high resolution T1, T2 and diffusion-weighted Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI). Resulted volume conductor models were used to perform simulation of tDCS-induced electric field. Construction of head models and simulations were performed using SIMNIBS. To verify the use of individualized volume conductor models, we compared the electric field distribution on the primary motor cortex for all individuals. We identified that individual anatomical characteristics, such as stroke lesion distance to the cortex, affects the electric field delivered to the cortex. This justifies the use of individualized computation model, when studying the tDCS-effects. To understand how tDCS induces changes in these activities, we performed Partial Least Square Regression (PLSR) to identify brain regions in which the simulated electric field effects the most on neurophysiological changes of the brain. We identified a strong positive association between normal electric field components the motor cortex, to the increase in intra-hemispheric connectivity between motor networks. These findings justify the use of tDCS to influence on functional reorganization of the brain, in which strong electric field at primary motor cortex achieves better results. More studies will be performed to develop individualized tDCS protocol targeting specific ipsilesional motor networks. For stage three, we have conducted a preliminary randomized controlled trial to evaluate the training effectiveness of HD-tDCS. Eleven chronic stroke subjects (6 males, mean age=65.5±5.6 years) were recruited from the local community. The inclusion criteria were (1) first-ever stroke, (2) onset of stroke more than six months, (3) a single unilateral brain lesion, (4) sufficient cognitive function to understand instructions and perform tasks, and (5) no additional rehabilitation therapies applied to the subject. The subjects with a history of epilepsy, mental implants, and brain surgery would be excluded. The subjects were randomly allocated to the experimental group (6 subjects with HD-tDCS together with robot-hand training) and the sham group (5 subjects with sham HD-tDCS together with robot hand training). Motor functions of the paretic upper limbs for all stroke subjects were evaluated with Fugl–Meyer Assessment for upper extremity (FMA) and Action Research Arm Test (ARAT) before and after the training intervention. Each subject underwent ten sessions of robot-hand training, and each session had 30 minutes of training. Simultaneously, at the beginning of the first trial, experimental(optimized tDCS) or sham HD-tDCS will be applied to the subject for 20 minutes. The 2-mA current was used in the experimental group, but the current with 30-second ramp-up and ramp-down periods was adopted in the sham group. FMA score was used to evaluate the function of the whole upper limb, including fingers, wrist, elbow, and shoulder. Both experimental and sham groups showed a significant FMA increase before and after the training (Paired t-test, Experimental group: from 31.3±13.3 to 39.7±13.5, t(5)=6.250, p=0.002. Sham group: from 32.0±19.2 to 36.8±19.5, t(4)=12.829, p=0.001). However, the experimental group illustrated significant FMA improvement than the sham group (Independent t-test, Experimental group: 8.3±3.3. Sham group: 4.6±1.1. t(9)=2.418,p=0.039). ARAT score was more prone to assess the fine finger movements. Only the experimental group showed a significant ARAT increase before and after the training (Paired t-test, from 25.8±19 to 32.8±18.4,t(5)=3.796, p=0.013), which was not observed in the sham group. Meanwhile, a significant difference of ARAT improvement was also observed between these two groups (Independent t-test, Experimental group: 7.0±4.5. Sham group: 1.6±2.7. t(9)=2.336,p=0.044).

14207617.label: Major findings and research outcome
14207617.value: Repeated measures ANOVA with two factors, stimulation conditions (anode, cathode and sham) and session (Baseline, Post-10, Post-30, Post-50) was used to assess the modulation effects on the three measures in the broadband of interest and individual EEG bands. To explore the tDCS modulatory effects with the residual functional ability of stroke subjects. We found significant polarity-dependent HD-tDCS modulatory effect in peak of cortico-muscular coherence (CMC) in the broadband of interest (8-48 Hz). Repeated measures ANOVA was used to determine peak CMC modulation in the broadband of interest and individual bands with two factors, session (baseline, Post-10, Post-30, and Post-50) and stimulation condition (anode, cathode, and sham). For peak CMC in the broadband, we found a significant interaction of session*stimulation (p=0.003), but no significant effect of session (p=0.192). For intra-group comparisons of each stimulation condition, one-way ANOVA showed significant main effects of session in anode stimulation for broadband peak CMC (p=0.004), while post-hoc analysis shows significant difference between baseline and Post-10 session after anode HD-tDCS (p=0.004). There was no significant difference between baseline and Post-30. These results suggest that the offline modulation effects of anode HD-tDCS on stroke subjects did not last up to 30 minutes (Post-30 session), and cathode or sham stimulation did not induce significant changes along the time course. A significant Pearson Correlation was found between “broadband peak CMC change from baseline” and ARAT score for anode Post-10 session (r=0.771, p=0.005). Such results implied that anode HD-tDCS modulatory effects might relate to residual functional abilities of stroke subjects. Each subject underwent ten sessions of robot-hand training, and each session had 30 minutes of training. Simultaneously, at the beginning of the first trial, optimized or sham HD-tDCS will be applied to the subject for 20 minutes. Both optimized tDCS and sham groups showed a significant FMA increase before and after the training. The optimized tDCS group showed significant FMA improvement than the sham group. Only the experimental group showed a significant ARAT increase before and after the training, which was not observed in the sham group. Meanwhile, a significant difference of ARAT improvement was also observed between these two groups to show that the optimized tDCS has better effect in the neuroplasticity for stroke rehabilitation.

14207617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14207617.value: For the second and last research objectives mentioned, we would apply systematic finite element modeling and conduct practical clinical experiments for stroke patients. For finite element modeling (FEM) of tDCS, factors affecting electrical distribution in stroke brain would be explored first, a finite element model of tDCS on healthy subject would be built, afterwards, a finite element model of tDCS on stroke patients would be developed considering the effect of stroke lesion, based on the above models, we could compare the difference between the lesioned brain and healthy brain and determine the factors influencing electrical flow in stroke patients. Beyond that, an optimized tDCS therapy based on FEM would be probed to find the optimal method of tDCS on lesioned brain, the optimized tDCS suggests having better modulation effects. A randomized controlled trial study between optimized tDCS, conventional tDCS and sham tDCS together with robot-assisted training would be conducted to evaluate the training effectiveness, and to assess the short-term and long-term clinical and neurophysiological effects of the interventions.

14207617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14207617.value: In this project, we have validated the feasibility of adopting anodal tDCS to enhance the cortical excitability. Using EEG and fMRI, we have thoroughly investigated the lasting effects of anodal tDCS and the network-wise interaction modulation in the brain. With FEM models, optimized and individualized stimulation protocols could be designed. Furthermore, combining tDCS and robot-assisted hand training, the motor functional recovery of stroke subjects could be further promoted.

14207717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14207717.value: Quantum technologies, which utilize quantum phenomena such as entanglement and superposition, can have distinct advantages over the classical technologies. The realization of quantum technologies, however, is still a challenging task as the quantum phenomena are extremely sensitive to environment noises and fabrication imperfections. The exquisite control of quantum systems requires a precise calibration of the Hamiltonian that governs the dynamics of the system. This makes Hamiltonian estimation a crucial step for the realization of practical quantum technologies. The aim of this project is to develop systematic methods to obtain optimal adaptive feedback schemes that can lead to higher precision Hamiltonian estimation than conventional schemes. Typical Hamiltonian estimation is achieved by preparing some basis states and letting them evolve under the dynamics governed by the Hamiltonian for certain period of time. The Hamiltonian can then be estimated by making measurements on the output states. In such schemes, the dynamics are assumed to be fixed. However, in many practical experimental settings, additional controls can usually be used to adjust the dynamics for better estimation of the Hamiltonian. In the most general case, the controls can be designed based on the information gained from previous rounds of measurements, which forms the basis for adaptive feedback Hamiltonian estimation. So far optimal adaptive feedback schemes are only identified under the ideal unitary dynamics, however in real experiments environment noises and experimental imperfections are usually inevitable. In this project, we aim to develop systematic methods to obtain optimal adaptive feedback schemes in the presence of environment noises and control errors, which are crucial for practical implementations. Compared to the parallel scheme, another scheme that is commonly studied to improve the precision, the adaptive feedback scheme can not only potentially lead to higher precision but is also easier to implement on many current experimental systems. This is because adaptive feedback scheme can be potentially realized on small physical systems where high fidelity controls can now be routinely done while preparing large entangled states required by the parallel scheme is still very challenging. Our findings will not only broaden the horizon of Hamiltonian estimation research but will also have wide implications for various applications of Hamiltonian estimation, including quantum sensing, quantum imaging, and quantum metrology. 量子技術利用諸如糾纏和疊加的量子現象可以比古典技術有明顯的優勢。量子技術的實現仍然是一個具有挑戰性的任務，因為量子現像對環境噪音和製造缺陷是非常敏感的。量子現象的精密控制需要對系統動力學的哈密頓量有高精度的測量。這使哈密爾頓估計成為實現量子技術的關鍵一步。該項目的目的是開發系統的方法來獲得最佳適應性反饋方案導致比傳統方法更高精度的哈密頓量估計。 典型的哈密頓量估計是通過準備一些量子態並讓它們在由哈密頓量控制的動力過程中演化,然後可以通過對輸出狀態進行測量來估計。在這種方案中,動力過程是固定的。然而在許多實際的實驗設置中，通常可以使用控制來調整動力過程以更好地估計哈密頓量。在最常見的情況是可以根據從以前獲得的信息來設計控制,這些形成了自適應反饋哈密頓量估計的基礎。 到目前為止，最優的自適應反饋方案僅在理想的酉動力學下被確定，在實際環境中，環境噪聲和實驗缺陷通常都是必然存在的。在這個項目中，我們旨在開發系統的方法在存在環境噪聲和控制誤差的情況下來獲得最佳的自適應反饋方案，這對實際系統至關重要。自適應反饋方案不僅可能導致更高的精度，在許多當前的實驗系統中也更容易實現。

14208017.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14208017.value: 雲接入網絡中的具無線資源虛擬化的可擴展性研究

14208017.label: Project Objectives
14208017.value: User-centric radio resource allocation (RRA) with collaborative signal processing --- The centralized C-RAN architecture allows extremely flexible and aggressive frequency reuse across the whole system. In this task, we aim to design a global-optimal user-centric RRA scheme for an MVNO, where interference is managed by tight RRH coordination. Both fast- and slow-adaptive algorithms will be investigated for different application scenarios. Besides spectrum efficiency, we are interested in the scalability of algorithms, in the sense that the computational complexity does not grow drastically with the size of C-RAN. Radio resource quantification for MVNOs --- To facilitate RRV, MVNOs must quantify how much radio resources to require from the MNO, so that their users will receive satisfactory service. This amount heavily depends on user location distribution, service type, wireless channel condition, PHY-layer signal processing, and the RRA scheme adopted. Depending on the affordable complexity and procurement procedure, we investigate radio resource quantification at different time scales. In particular, we pursue optimal and simple solutions, so that the process of radio resource quantification is not resource intensive itself. Dynamic radio resource isolation and sharing among coexisting MVNOs --- Multiple MVNOs typically run different protocols and applications, and thus their signals would not be jointly processed for interference mitigation. This makes radio resource isolation and sharing crucial for multi MVNO coexistence. Due to the time-spatial reusability of radio resources, we will seek a critical understanding of the optimal balance between spectrum sharing and isolation among coexisting MVNOs.

14208017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14208017.value: 本項目旨在研究雲接入網絡中實現無線頻譜資源虛擬化的算法。介於近來雲接入網絡規模不斷增加，本項目著重探討算法的可擴展性，以使算法複雜度不隨網絡規模而急劇增加。 面對呈指數增加的無線移動網絡的吞吐量需求，無線網絡運營商正不斷地尋找適用於未來無線網絡的策略，以期在不增加網絡運營成本的基礎上大幅增加網絡容量。 網絡虛擬化被公認為可以實現這一目標的有效解決方案。雲接入網絡是一種通過雲計算，為基站功能虛擬化提供革命性平台的技術。近年來，雲接入網絡成為各大運營商和設備供應商重點投資的領域。其中亞太區亦成為雲接入網絡占有市場份額最大的區域。 與其他網路資源相比，無線頻譜資源虛擬化有其獨特的特性。這是因為頻譜資源的復用取決於終端傳輸功率、干擾消除能力、信干比要求等等。同時，雲接入網絡所擁有的大規模集中式處理能力，也為頻譜資源在不同的網絡虛擬運營商之間的共享、分割、及定制提供新的可能。本項目旨在從根本上探索在不同時間和協議架構層面上實現頻譜資源虛擬化的有效機制。具體而言，我們將著重研究以下三方面工作：1）以用戶為中心，具有全局干擾控制機制的網絡中頻譜最佳復用；2）基於用戶分佈及服務質量需求的頻譜網絡量化機制；2）多個共存的無線虛擬網絡運營商的最佳頻譜資源分割。

14208017.label: Realisation of objectives
14208017.value: The project objectives have all been fulfilled satisfactorily. In particular, we have comprehensively studied the virtualization of radio resources in cloud radio access networks (C-RAN). The project has led to numerous publications in top venues. Regarding the first objective, we studied user-centric radio resource allocation with cooperative signal processing of C-RAN base stations. In the hindsight, the work is highly relevant to the cell-free design proposed for 6G wireless networks. In CRAN, dense remote radio heads (RRHs) are centrally coordinated by a data center, where RRH cooperation can be configured flexibly on demand. Based on this feature, we develop a user-centric join transmission scheme, where a set of RRHs around a mobile user are configured as a small virtual cell. We derive the average user throughput in the downlink analytically. The result reveals the impact of important design parameters, such as RRH density, path-loss exponent, virtual cell size and the minimum separation distance between co-channel users. Regarding the second objective, we address the challenge of spectrum provisioning brought about by the uncertainty of mobile traffic and wireless channels. We propose a two-stage spectrum leasing framework, which allows an MVNO to acquire spectrum resources from both advance reservation and on-demand requests. To maximize the MVNO's surplus, we jointly optimize the amount of spectrum resources to lease in the two stages by taking into account the traffic distribution, random user locations, wireless channel fading, QoS requirements, and price differences. Regarding the third objective, we considered the spectrum allocation problem in virtualized CRANs with pricing and optimization approaches. Due to the highly self-interested nature of the Mobile Network Operator (MNO) and the Mobile Virtual Network Operators (MVNO), we formulate the spectrum allocation as a two-level problem, of which the upper level is a spectrum leasing problem and the lower level is an optimization problem of channel-allocation. To provide fast overall solution in large CRAN, we propose a low-complexity algorithm to solve the lower-level problem and two efficient algorithms to solve the upper-level problem in different cases. With the help of the predicted traffic and the proposed action refinement technique, the proposed DRL approach significantly outperforms the existing algorithms in terms of both power-saving and convergence time.

14208017.label: Major findings and research outcome
14208017.value: There are several major research outcomes from this work, leading to 17 referred journal publications and 10 referred conference publications. The detailed findings are as below. 1. We derived analytically the performance of user-centric joint transmission in a CRAN with a number of virtual cells. In contrast to previous works that assume constant RRH transmit power, we consider a total transmit power constraint for each user and assume that the power is optimally allocated to the RRHs in each virtual cell. Based on stochastic geometry models of RRHs, we explicitly explain the impact of RRH density and path-loss exponent on the user throughput. 2. We derived the optimal two-stage spectrum leasing scheme for an MVNO. In the first stage, i.e., advance reservation, the MVNO reserves a certain amount of spectrum resources for a long period of time, which usually covers hours or days. The decision is optimized according to the statistics of the user traffic and the on-demand price over the period. In the second stage, i.e., on-demand request, the MVNO decides whether to request an additional spectrum after observing the actual number and locations of users it needs to serve. The on-demand request changes with user arrivals, departures, and movements, and usually varies in a timescale of seconds. Then, in the timescale of milliseconds, the MVNO dynamically allocates the spectrum resources acquired from both advance reservation and on-demand to the users according to the fast channel fading. To maximize its profit, the MVNO jointly optimizes the operations in all three timescales. 3. We derived a pricing-based resource allocation scheme for virtualized CRAN (V-CRAN). We first formulate the resource allocation problem in a V-CRAN as a two-level non-cooperative pricing problem. The upper level corresponds to spectrum leasing from the MNO to MVNOs, where the MNO aims to find an optimal price that maximizes its revenue. In the lower level, we formulate the channel allocation problem between an MVNO and its users as a utility-surplus maximization problem. Then, under the non-cooperative pricing framework, we analyze the revenue behavior of the MNO in a parameterized utility function family. We find that different utility functions lead to radically distinct revenue behaviors with respect to the price. Accordingly, we propose efficient pricing algorithms to achieve optimal revenue. In particular, we identify a sufficient condition under which the upper-level spectrum leasing problem can be solved with guaranteed performance. Finally, by exploiting the network structure, we propose a low-complexity algorithm for the MVNO problem. (Remark: In the grant acknowledgment of the following research outputs, the project reference number 14208017 is misquoted as 14208107: Part C 8-1, 8-2, 8-4, 8-5, 8-6, 8-7, 8-14, 8-15, 9-9, 9-10)

14208017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14208017.value: In the future, we are going to study the application of machine learning in optimizing resource virtualization decisions. Our preliminary work in Section C 8-14 has studied a novel Deep Reinforcement learning-based BS Activation alGorithm (DRAG) to efficiently obtain SBS on/off scheduling decisions in large-scale HetNets. The proposed approach DRAG does not depend on the distributions of channel, traffic demand, user location, or the underlying resource allocation/scheduling mechanisms. In fact, it is purely data-driven and completely model-free. Moving forward, we plan to extend the study to complicated C-RAN systems with multiple MVNOs and realistic interference channels.

14208017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14208017.value: In light of the remarkable success of virtualization of wired networks, wireless network virtualization undoubtedly holds great promise to address the many challenges today’s mobile systems are facing. The focus of this project is on virtualizing the most precious and scarce resource in wireless systems, i.e., radio resources. Our research outputs in this project contribute greatly to the advancement the key enabling technologies for radio resource sharing, isolation, and customization in C-RAN, and consequently contribute to a new paradigm shift in the next-generation networked ICT.

14208117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14208117.value: 分析優化算法的收斂率乃是數值分析領域中一個重要課題。 最近的研究顯示實變函數論裏的 Lojasiewicz 不等式能夠用 來分析一大類優化算法的收斂性，而且不等式當中所謂的 Lojasiewicz 指數能推出算法的收斂率。可是到目前為止，對於 很多具應用背景的非凸優化問題的 Lojasiewicz 指數值，我們 並未掌握。本項目旨在斷定在機器學習和信號處理中所出現的 非凸優化問題的 Lojasiewicz 指數值，並由此去解釋不同一階優 化算法的優異收斂表現。

14208117.label: Realisation of objectives
14208117.value: To achieve Objective 1, we began by focusing on the problem of optimizing a quadratic matrix form over the Stiefel manifold--which includes the well-known principal component analysis (PCA) as a special case--and showing that any of its critical point has a Lojasiewicz exponent of 1/2. At the time the result was published, it expanded the very limited repertoire of manifold optimization problems for which the Lojasiewicz exponent can be explicitly determined. Moreover, it allows us to establish, in unified manner, the linear convergence of a large family of retraction-based line-search methods and a newly developed stochastic variance-reduced gradient method when applied to the problem. The techniques developed in this work form the basis of our later research on provably and practically efficient algorithms for l1-PCA, which is an outlier-resistant version of the classic PCA and has attracted considerable attention in the signal processing community. Next, we showed that certain popular smooth non-convex formulations of a phase retrieval problem and a low-rank matrix recovery problem possess a local error bound property, which can be used to deduce the Lojasiewicz exponent at certain critical points of the problems in question. Such a result allows us to establish the quadratic convergence of the cubic regularization method, which improves upon the decade-long sub-quadratic convergence result of Nesterov and Polyak. Lastly, we considered a non-smooth non-convex formulation of the robust matrix recovery problem and showed that under a standard generative model of the data, it not only is weakly convex but also possesses the sharpness property. The latter is akin to a Lojasiewicz-type growth condition and expands the limited repertoire of non-smooth non-convex optimization problems that are known to satisfy such a condition. Moreover, the result allows us to establish the linear convergence of the vanilla subgradient method with geometrically diminishing stepsize when applied to the problem. To achieve Objective 2, we proceeded in two directions. In the first direction, we took two fundamental problems in data science and signal processing, namely, robust subspace recovery and sparse dictionary learning, and showed that they can be formulated as the problem of optimizing a non-smooth function over the Stiefel manifold. Moreover, we showed that under standard generative models of the data, both the robust subspace recovery and sparse dictionary learning problems are weakly convex and satisfy the sharpness property. Consequently, we are able to show that a host of Riemannian subgradient-type methods will converge linearly when applied to these problems. It is worth noting that our work is the first to establish convergence rate guarantees for using Riemannian subgradient-type methods to optimize a class of non-smooth non-convex functions over the Stiefel manifold. In the second direction, we considered the problem of exact community recovery in stochastic block model (SBM), which has attracted much attention in the data science, information theory, signal processing, statistics, and theoretical computer science communities. The SBM is a random graph model that can generate graphs with community structures. We proposed a power-type method with spectral initialization to solve the exact community recovery problem. By characterizing the growth behavior of the maximum-likelihood (ML) function associated with the problem and developing a novel analysis of the spectral initialization method, we showed that our proposed method will, with high probability, exactly recover the ground-truth communities in $O(n log^2n / loglog n)$ time, which is currently the best in the literature.

14208117.label: Major findings and research outcome
14208117.value: The major findings of the project have already been summarized in Section 5.3 above. The research outcomes for Objective 1 have led to the publication of 3 journal articles---1 in Mathematical Programming and 2 in SIAM Journal on Optimization---while those for Objective 2 have led to the publication of another 2 journal articles---1 in Mathematical Programming and 1 in SIAM Journal on Optimization---and 1 conference article at the International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML). Both Mathematical Programming and SIAM Journal on Optimization are top-ranked journals in the field of mathematical optimization, while ICML is one of the top conferences in the field of machine learning. Besides the above publications, we have also published a review article in IEEE Signal Processing Magazine, which summarizes some of the contributions from this project and serves to disseminate our results to the research community. The IEEE Signal Processing Magazine is the premier publication of the IEEE Signal Processing Society.

14208117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14208117.value: The analysis techniques developed in this project can potentially be applied to tackle a broader set of problems. One direction, which has already been alluded to in Section 5.3, is to develop provably and practically efficient algorithms to solve outlier-resistant variants of the classic PCA problem. In fact, we have recently characterized the Lojasiewicz exponent of the so-called l1-PCA and developed the first algorithm with convergence rate guarantee for the problem. Currently, we are studying a rotationally invariant version of the l1-PCA, and it is expected that the outcomes from this project will play a crucial role. Another direction is to develop low-complexity algorithms for solving community detection problems. The power-type method mentioned in Section 5.3 is highly versatile and can be applied to a host of different problems. Currently, we are focusing on the problem of exact community recovery over signed graphs, and the techniques we developed in this project have shown great promise in obtaining exact recovery algorithms with near-linear complexity for the problem.

14208117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14208117.value: Modern applications in data science, machine learning, and signal processing often call for the solution of large-scale optimization problems. This has motivated the development of many lightweight solutions methods to tackle these problems. Nevertheless, our theoretical understanding of the performance of these methods is rather limited. In this project, we developed a broad set of analytic tools to study the crucial features of an optimization problem that allow for an efficient and effective algorithmic treatment. We then demonstrate the power of our tools by applying them to several representative problems in data science and machine learning and showing that they lead to state-of-the-art results. It is expected that the outcomes of this project will find many more applications and enhance our understanding of the types of problem structures that are amenable to efficient algorithmic treatment.

14208417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14208417.value: The objective of this project is to develop joint object detection and tracking systems based on deep neural networks. Multi-object detection and tracking are fundamental problems in computer vision. They have escalating demands in high-level vision applications, such as intelligent surveillance, autonomous driving, and video understanding. The proposed joint detection and tracking systems would significantly improve object tracking robustness and accuracy, and serve as important components for many vision-based applications. The problem of multi-object tracking was studied for decades, and most state-of-the-art methods adopt the tracking-by-detection strategy. Such a strategy treats object detection and object tracking as two independent problems and their relations were not thoroughly studied in a unified framework. A tracking system specifically designed for an object detector might have difficulties in handling detection results from another detector due to different data distributions of the detections. In addition, the spatial and semantic relations between different tracklets are usually modeled as optimization models that are difficult to optimize. On the other hand, deep neural networks including Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN) have achieved great success in object detection and video understanding. There are preliminary attempts on solving object detection and tracking problems by deep networks. However, they still treat detection and tracking as two independent problems. There was no existing work on joint object detection and tracking with deep neural networks. We propose deep CNN-RNN models to solve the detection and tracking problems jointly in a unified framework. The proposed deep neural networks consist of a CNN model for learning visual appearance of each video frame and a RNN model for capturing temporal relations between frames. To enable using CNN to process tracklets effectively and efficiently, we propose an innovative way of encoding tracklets into rectangle grids. The tracklet box locations are encoded as relative offsets to a set of default anchor boxes with different sizes and aspect ratios, which are well aligned across time. The learned convolution layers are able to capture spatial and semantic relationships between different tracklets. For online and offline object detection and tracking, two different types of CNN-RNN models are proposed to obtain robust and accurate results. The outcome of the project would significantly improve the performance of object detection and tracking in multiple applications. It also provides a new way of developing detection and tracking systems based on deep neural networks and would intrigue more research in this direction. 該項目的目標在於開發基於深度神經網絡的聯合物體檢測與跟踪系統。多物體的檢測和跟踪是計算機視覺裡的基礎問題，在一系列高級視覺應用中，如智能監控，自動駕駛，視頻理解中有著大量的需求。本項目中提出的聯合檢測和跟踪系統能夠夠極大的提升多物體跟踪的魯棒性與準確性，能夠用於許多視覺應用。多物體跟踪問題已經有幾十年的研究歷史，大多數較好的算法均採用了“基於檢測的跟踪”策略。這種策略將物體檢測與跟踪看作兩個獨立的問題進行解決，兩者之間的關係因此未能在一個整體的框架下進行詳盡的研究。由於不同的檢測數據分佈，一個針對某種物體檢測器的跟踪算法可能對與其他檢測器的結果不能擁有良好的性能。同時，不同跟踪軌跡之間空間與語義上的關係通常被建模為易於優化的模型。另一方面，近年來包括卷積神經網絡（CNN）和遞歸神經網絡（RNN）的深度學習技術在物體檢測與視頻理解中取得了極大的成功。已有一些將物體檢測與跟踪物體建模的深度網絡，但是它們仍然將檢測與跟踪看作兩個獨立問題，目前還沒有工作將物體的檢測與跟踪整合在一個深度神經網絡進行研究。本項目中，我們提出一種聯合解決檢測與跟踪問題的深度CNN-RNN模型，該模型包含一個學習視頻幀視覺特徵的卷積神經網絡，以及一個學習幀幀之間時序信息的遞歸神經網絡。為了使CNN高效和有效的處理跟踪軌跡，我們提出一種新穎的跟踪軌跡編碼方式，將跟踪軌跡編碼進在時序上對齊的方格中，跟踪軌跡被編碼成為相對於一系列不同長寬比和大小錨框的相對偏差。訓練的卷積層因此能夠有效的學習不同跟踪軌跡之間的空間與時間關係。針對在線和離線物體檢測與跟踪，我們提出了兩種不同的CNN-RNN模型。該項目的成果能夠極大的增強眾多應用中物體檢測與跟踪的性能，同時提出了一種新穎的基於深度神經網絡的物體檢測與跟踪方法，能夠帶動該方向更多的發展。

14208417.label: Realisation of objectives
14208417.value: All the objectives in this project have been realized successfully. (1) We have developed deep neural networks for joint object detection and tracking in videos. Multi-object tracking itself is a challenging problem. We observe that in existing MOT methods, individual objects' movements and inter-object relations are mostly modeled separately and relations between them are still manually tuned. In addition, inter-object relations are mostly modeled in a symmetric way, which we found is not an optimal setting. We propose a Deep Continuous Conditional Random Field (DCCRF) for solving the object detection and tracking problem in a track-by-detection manner. It consists of a unary term and an asymmetric pairwise term for modeling an energy function. The unary terms are modeled by a deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), which is trained to estimate each individual object’s displacement between consecutive time steps with each object’s visual appearance. It acts as the object detection with prior appearance. The asymmetric pairwise terms aim to tackle the problem caused by object occlusions, object misdetections and global camera motion. For two neighboring tracked trajectories, the pairwise influence is different along each direction to let the high-confidence trajectory assists the low-confidence one more. Based on such estimated object locations, a final visual-similarity CNN is proposed for generating the final detection association results. Extensive experiments on two public datasets show the effectiveness of our proposed joint detection and tracking framework. (2) We have developed different strategies for online and offline tracking. DCCRF mainly focuses on online object detection and tracking. However, it can be extended to offline tracking by modifying the unary terms to not only estimate object locations from two consecutive times but predicting and refine their locations from multiple previous and future frames. The unary terms and pairwise terms can be alternatively optimized to take advantage of both the temporal relations across different frames and spatial relations within each frame. We also mine a large number of street videos from the Internet and iteratively use previously estimated trajectories from the current-generation detection-tracking model to train a new detection-tracking model for the next generation. The detection and tracking performance can be significantly improved using the proposed learning scheme. (3) We have applied the studied joint object and tracking algorithms to vehicle detection and tracking. Our group has developed high-performance re-identification algorithms for robustly estimating inter-object similarities. By extending the trained vehicle re-identification models to serve as the initialization weights, the re-ID models can naturally be finetuned to better estimate the vehicle displacements in our DCCRF framework and thus significantly improve the accuracy of the unary terms.

14208417.label: Major findings and research outcome
14208417.value: As research outcomes, 1 journal paper on IEEE TCSVT and 14 conference papers are published. IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology is one of the top journals in video understanding and perception. CVPR, ECCV, ICCV, NeurlPS are the top conferences on computer vision and machine learning. In this project, we proposed DCCRF (Part C.8, No. 1) for joint object detection and tracking using deep neural networks. The proposed framework adopts novel unary terms and asymmetric pairwise terms, and models them as deep neural networks. They are modeled as deep Convolution Neural Networks, which are able to learn discriminative visual features for tracklet association. The asymmetric pairwise terms model inter-object relations in an asymmetric way, which encourage high-confidence tracklets to help correct errors of low-confidence tracklets and not to be affected by low-confidence ones much. The DCCRF is trained in an end-to-end manner for better adapting the influences of visual information as well as inter-object relations. For Learning discriminative person representations for joint multi-person tracking, In (Part C.9 No. 6), we observed that most of the current methods impose only local constraints for similarity learning. We proposed to incorporate constraints on large image groups by combining the CRF with deep neural networks. In (Part C.9, No. 3), we aim to tackle the problem of significant variation of person poses and viewing angles between person images. The spatial layout and correspondences between query person images are vital information for robustly estimating the pairwise similarities, which are ignored by most state-of-the-art methods. In (Part C.9, No. 4), we noticed that existing deep learning models are biased to capture too much relevance between background appearances of person images for learning person features, which hinders the deep learning models to learn effective visual features. In (Part C.9, No. 7), we also study the similarities among a group of gallery images with a similarity-guided graph neural network. In (Part C.9, No. 12), we try to mitigate the problem of large pose variation of person images. A Feature Distilling Generative Adversarial Network (FD-GAN) is proposed for learning identity-related and pose-unrelated representations. In (Part C.9, No. 5), we tried to learn person features from person video clips. Our approach divides long person sequences into multiple short video snippets and aggregates the top-ranked snippet similarities for sequence-similarity estimation. In summary, more discriminative feature representations are learned via training on person reID datasets and can be used to boost the detection-tracking accuraices.

14208417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14208417.value: In this project, we found that deep neural networks can well model multi-object relations and dynamics for tackling detection and tracking in a joint framework. The proposed pipeline introduces the novel asymmetric pairwise term, which can motivate future studies in related fields. We will further pursue the direction on joint detection and tracking with deep convolutional networks and the novel transformer networks. The obtained object trajectories by the current detection and tracking model, and also serve as strong supervisions for self-supervised algorithms to learn more discriminative visual features and tracking models.

14208417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14208417.value: The aim of this project is to develop deep neural networks for jointly tacking the problem of multi-object detection and tracking from videos. The proposed framework successfully achieves the proposed goal. The framework can well model inter-object relations and behaviors to improve the detection and tracking performance. The learned models can be well applied to different types of objects, such as pedestrians, vehicles, etc. We also developed a series of algorithms for learning discriminative visual features for person and vehicle tracking, which do not only improve tracking performances but also generalize to other related applications, such as person retrieval, fashion search, etc.

14208717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14208717.value: This proposal aims to develop a nanoscale PT-symmetric acoustic system based on coupled optomechanical cavities and experimentally investigate the physics of PT-symmetric acoustics at the nanoscale. The development of quantum mechanics is one of the most significant achievements in the 20th century. As is well known, a fundamental assumption in quantum mechanics states that a system’s Hamiltonian H must be Hermitian in order to obtain a real energy spectrum and ensure the probability conservation. This condition, however, is recently found to be sufficient but not necessary. Actually, Bender and Boettcher discovered in 1998 that a class of non-Hermitian Hamiltonians can also have real energy spectra under certain conditions, as long as they possess the so-called “parity‒time (PT) symmetry.” This remarkable finding not only has extended quantum mechanics from the real into the complex domain, but also has revolutionized many other branches of classical physics. Despite rapid theoretical development, the experiments on PT symmetry have progressed relatively slowly. To date, most experimental works have been focused in the optical and photonic domain. Due to its versatile applications in communication and signal processing, an acoustic system operating in the microwave-frequency regime with the idea of PT symmetry is highly desirable and remains to be developed. We will study the PT symmetry in acoustics at the nanoscale with a coupled cavity optomechanical system. We will fabricate on a silicon chip a pair of high-quality optoacoustic cavities which are coupled acoustically via thin connecting nanowires. We harness the optomechanical backaction effect to optically control the acoustic modes of the two cavities independently such that they experience balanced gain and loss. By varying the ratio between the gain/loss strength and the coupling strength, we expect to observe the PT-symmetry-related phenomena in such a coupled acoustic system. By exploring interesting physics phenomena in a completely new domain, this proposal has far-reaching significance to both fundamental research and some cutting-edge engineering applications. Fundamentally, the experimental results of this proposal will be used to test and verify the PT theories. New experimental results that are not supported by existing theories may stimulate further theoretical development. Technology-wise, better understanding of the physics of PT symmetry in nanoscale acoustic systems will lead to unprecedented engineering applications on a chip, such as mass sensing with extremely high sensitivity, unidirectional phonon transport, and highly efficient phonon lasers and amplifiers. 本項目旨在開發基於耦合光機械腔的納米PT對稱聲學系統，並通過實驗研究納米尺度PT對稱聲學的物理機制。 量子力學的發展是二十世紀最重要的成就之一。眾所周知，量子力學裏的一個基本假設規定一個系統的哈密爾頓量H必須具備厄米特性才能獲得實的能譜並確保概率守恒。然而，最近發現表明這一條件其實充分而非必要。事實上，Bender和Boettcher於1998年發現有一類非厄米的哈密爾頓量只要具備所謂的“宇稱時間（PT）反演對稱性”就可以在某些條件下也擁有實的能譜。這一偉大發現不僅將量子力學從實域拓展到復域，而且給經典物理的許多其它分支也帶來革命性的發展。盡管理論發展迅速，但PT對稱的實驗研究進展相對緩慢。到目前為止，多數實驗工作都集中在光學和光子學領域。鑒於其在通信和信號處理中的諸多應用，人們迫切需要開發具備PT對稱概念的微波頻段的聲學系統。 我們將利用耦合腔光機械系統來研究納米尺度的PT對稱聲學。我們將在矽片上制備一對高品質的光聲諧振腔，它們通過細納米線連接從而聲學上相互耦合。我們利用光機械反作用效應來用光學方法獨立地控制兩個腔的聲學模式，使得它們獲得平衡的增益和損耗。通過改變增益/損耗強度與耦合強度的比例，我們期望在此耦合聲學系統中觀察到PT對稱的相關現象。 通過探索一個全新領域中的有趣的物理現象，本項目對基礎研究和前沿工程應用具有深遠的意義。從根本上，本項目的實驗結果將用於測試和驗證PT理論。現有理論不支持的新的實驗結果可能會推動理論的進一步發展。在技術層面，更好地理解納米尺度聲學系統中PT對稱的物理問題將導致前所未有的基於芯片的工程應用，諸如具有極高靈敏度的質量傳感器、單向聲子傳輸以及高效聲子激光器和放大器。

14208717.label: Realisation of objectives
14208717.value: 1. (Objective 1) To design and fabricate a nanoscale cavity optomechanical device for studying PT-symmetric acoustics on a chip. We have fully achieved this objective by designing and fabricating several types of nanoscale cavity optomechanical devices for studying PT-symmetric acoustics on a chip. (1) We proposed and designed PT-symmetric optomechanical systems that consist of two or more mechanical resonators, where the damping rates of the mechanical resonators can be manipulated through the frequency and strength of the optical drive by using the cavity optomechanical effect [J11, C5]. The individual optomechanical resonator takes the form of optomechanical crystal nanobeam cavity, where the nanobeam can support high-Q mechanical modes that are colocalized with the optical modes to have strong optomechanical coupling. The mechanical mode can be designed at a frequency as high as 14.97 GHz, with the mechanical modal mass as small as 22.83 fg, and the optomechanical coupling rate as large as 1.26 MHz [C6]. Such nanoscale optomechanical cavities can be used in an optomechanical cavity array for studying PT-symmetric acoustics [J10, C4]. (2) We have also designed and fabricated a hybrid graphene/Si electro-optomechanical resonator system, which consists of two coupled microwheel mechanical resonators. One mechanical resonator is covered with graphene used for electromechanical actuation, and the other one is used for optomechanical detection [J9, C3]. Such a system can support high-Q optical resonances (Q ~ 10^6) in the telecommunication band. (3) We have also designed and fabricated suspended 2D optomechanical crystals on a silicon-nitride-on-insulator platform [J2, J3, J5]. Theses nanomechanical resonators exhibit strong second-order and third-order nonlinearities, and thus can be used for studying PT-symmetric acoustics and for realizing topological parametric phonon lasers [J6, C1]. 2. (Objective 2) To use optical methods to control the behaviors of the acoustic modes of the device. We have fully achieved this objective by theoretically proposing and experimentally demonstrating several optical methods for controlling the behaviors of the acoustic modes in cavity optomechanical devices. (1) In a system composed of two coupled optomechanical cavities, we manipulated the damping rates of the acoustic modes through the frequency and strength of the optical drive by using the heating or cooling effects in cavity optomechanics [J11, C5]. More generally, in a one-dimensional array of optomechanical cavities, we considered the parametric-squeezing interaction to engineer not only the band structure but also the dissipation rate of the acoustic waves, which is important in the study of PT-symmetric acoustics on a chip. We can fully control both the energy band diagram and the dissipation rate of the acoustic waves by the spatial distribution of the optomechanical coupling rate, such that the perturbed acoustic wave not only has a nonreciprocal group velocity but also experiences different dissipation rates when propagating in opposite directions [J10, C4]. (2) In a fiber-based optomechanical system, we slightly fused the cladding of the fiber to create a bottle-like microstructure, which forms optical and mechanical energy potentials for supporting high-quality optical probe modes and mechanical modes. The optical force of a modulated optical beam sent through the fiber can cause acoustic vibrations, which can be further amplified by the resonant mechanical modes [J4, J7]. (3) In a single-resonator optomechanical system, we broke the azimuthal symmetry of the resonator to construct a mechanical bound state in the continuum, which has high quality factor and is robust against structural variation. We experimentally achieved a mechanical Q factor of ~10^4 for the acoustic mode in the very high frequency band at room temperature [J8]. 3. (Objective 3) To perform low-noise optical and electrical measurements to characterize the PT-symmetry-related phenomena in the device. We have fully achieved this objective by performing optical and electrical measurements of the optomechanical devices and obtained the PT-symmetry-related results. (1) We measured an optomechanical microresonator, where two lossy mechanical modes interact with each other. We used optomechanical transduction method to characterize the intrinsic loss of the resonant mechanical modes as a function of the coupling strength. We found that the dissipation loss of one eigenmode is always high and that of the other eigenmode is always low, where the low-loss mode turns into a bound state in the continuum when its loss is at the lowest point [J8]. This is PT-symmetry-related phenomenon when the system is in the PT-broken phase. We further investigated the relationship between PT-symmetric systems and bound states in the continuum and elucidated that bound state in the continuum exists in PT-symmetric systems with appropriate design parameters [J1]. (2) We also measured double-wheel electro-optomechanical resonators, where the two mechanical modes in the two resonators are coupled with each other by using a connecting nanowire. Electrode was patterned on top of one resonator, which introduces a mechanical loss to one mechanical mode. Depending on the additionally introduced loss, the measured mechanical Q factor varies from several hundreds to ~1000 [J9, C3]. On the other hand, we experimentally demonstrated parametric phonon oscillators based on nonlinear nanoelectromechanical topological Dirac-vortex cavities. We obtained strong and variable mechanical gain by leveraging the strong squeezed interaction from the mechanical nonlinearity of an electro-optomechanical device [J6, C1].

14208717.label: Major findings and research outcome
14208717.value: The research outcome in the science aspect is shown as follows: (1) PT-symmetric acoustics by the optomechanical effect: Our simulation results of a PT-symmetric acoustic system by the cavity optomechanical effect show the interesting property of unidirectional reflection. These results may pave the way for the study of topological acoustics and phononic signal processing [J11, C5]. (2) Demonstration of PT-symmetry-related phenomena in a cavity optomechanical system: We experimentally realized and observed mechanical bound state in the continuum in an optomechanical microresonator [J8], which is a special state under the condition of PT symmetry [J1]. These results open a new way of obtaining high-Q micro- and nanomechanical resonators, which will inspire applications in areas of electromechanics, optomechanics, and quantum physics. (3) Unraveling the symmetry of optical force in a cavity optomechanical system: Our experimental investigation of the optical force inside a solid dielectric (optical fiber) showed that the optical force exerted by a Gaussian beam has distributions with the angular mode numbers of both 2 and 0, which cannot be explained by traditional theories. We suggested a modified Helmholtz theory to explain our experimental results. These results represent a fundamental leap forward in determining the correct form of optical force and will update the working principles of many applications involving optical force [J4]. (4) Discovery of a new degree of freedom in an electro-optomechanical system: We discovered an auxiliary orbital degree of freedom in topological insulators on a nanomechanical platform. We also realized an adiabatic transition between distinct topological edge states. These results introduce the orbital degree of freedom as an alternative means to manipulate the topological phase transition on an integrated platform [J2]. (5) Realization of parametric phonon oscillation in an electro-optomechanical system: We experimentally demonstrated a parametric phonon oscillator based on a nonlinear nanoelectromechanical Dirac-vortex cavity by harnessing the strong squeezed interactions. We found that the random frequency variation caused by fabrication disorders can effectively be suppressed by increasing the cavity size, while the free spectral range reduces at a much slower rate. These properties are advantages for realizing large-area single-mode phonon lasers on a chip [J6, C1]. The research outcome in the engineering aspect is shown as follows: (6) Coherent information processing with cavity optomechanics: We demonstrated coherent information transfer between two orthogonally propagating light beams of disparate wavelengths. Our scheme significantly simplifies the experimental implementation of coherent wavelength conversion and extends the operating bandwidth to that of an optical fiber, which will enable a broad range of coherent-optics-based applications such as optical sensing, spectroscopy, and communication [J7]. (7) Optical control of acoustic waves with cavity optomechanics: Our studies on the particle-conserving and particle-nonconserving photon–phonon interactions in an optomechanical cavity array produced the following findings: The particle-conserving term generates a synthetic gauge field for phonons, leading to an acoustic analog of quantum Hall effect, while the particle-nonconserving interaction strongly modifies the quantum vacuum of phonons, enabling control of the dissipation rate of phonons. Our strategy can be employed to construct novel acoustic devices which are robust against both backscattering and internal losses without additional engineering complexity [J10, C4].

14208717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14208717.value: In this project, we designed and fabricated nanoscale cavity optomechanical devices, used optical methods to control the behaviors of the acoustic modes of the devices, and experimentally obtained the PT-symmetry-related phenomena in the devices. Further development of the research can include the following aspects: (1) In the science aspect, this project has provided a platform for studying PT-symmetric acoustics. Those devices can be used not only for verifying the PT-symmetry theories but also for exploring exotic phenomena not yet discovered in the acoustic domain, e.g., unidirectional reflection, PT-synthetic phononic lattices, unidirectional acoustic transmission, etc. Our work can be further extended to study more complex PT-symmetric acoustic systems that combine PT symmetry with topological insulator, which is a hot topic in recent research. Since in this project we established a relationship between PT symmetry and bound state in the continuum, one can harness such bound states in the continuum for phonon trapping in micromechanical structures with dissipation channels to obtain long phonon lifetimes, which are desired in many micromechanical applications. (2) In the engineering aspect, this project has provided strategies to optically manipulate acoustic waves on a chip. Further developments in acoustic systems require small size and high working frequency, which can be achieved based on the investigated devices. The combination of PT symmetry and acoustics also leads to unprecedented applications. For example, PT-symmetric acoustic systems can be used for mass sensing with substantially enhanced sensitivity when working near the exceptional point. Topological phonon lasers and amplifiers can be used for active components in a phononic circuit with enhanced robustness. The combination of PT symmetry and nonlinear effects can be used for unidirectional acoustic transmission and for realizing acoustic isolators.

14208717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14208717.value: The development of quantum mechanics is one of the most significant achievements in the 20th century. A fundamental assumption in quantum mechanics states that a system’s Hamiltonian must be Hermitian to obtain a real energy spectrum and ensure probability conservation. This condition, however, is recently found to be sufficient but not necessary. Bender and Boettcher discovered that non-Hermitian Hamiltonians that satisfy a so-called PT symmetry can also have real energy spectra under certain conditions. Although this finding revolutionized many other branches of classical physics, nanoscale PT-symmetric acoustic systems operating in the microwave-frequency regime were illusive. In this project, we performed both theoretical and experimental studies of cavity optomechanical systems for studying nanoscale PT-symmetric acoustics on a chip. We designed and fabricated a series of high-quality optomechanical and electro-optomechanical devices including individual and coupled micromechanical resonators. We used optical approaches to control and detect the acoustic modes and observed the PT-symmetry-related phenomena. The results obtained in this project will contribute to both fundamental research of PT-symmetric acoustics and enable unprecedented on-chip applications, such as high-sensitivity mass sensors as well as robust phonon lasers and amplifiers.

14208817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14208817.value: 導致言語障礙的原因有很多，包括神經退化性疾病、中風、腦癱、創傷性腦損傷或腫瘤，言語障礙不僅會影響一個人日常生活言語交流，也影響個人身份的聲音表達。輔助性技術通常包括用生成的語音來代替病人的語音。這種語音生成技術被稱為語音輸出交流援助（VOCA）。它不僅需要支持用高質量語音去進行有效的交流，還要體現基於說話人原本聲音特質的說話人身份。實現個性化VOCA的方法有幾種：語音庫（Voice Banking）通過錄製大量來自病人的高質量語音來合成個性化的語音。但是如果在錄製時病人的言語已經有障礙了，這種方法的效果並不理想。障礙語音恢復利用語音轉換技術來把障礙語音轉換為正常語音。個性化文本到語音合成採用說話人自適應技術從說話人獨立模型生成目標說話人語音。這種方法要求較少的訓練數據，但是如果自適應數據里含有障礙言語特征，會導致生成障礙的語音。障礙言語特征需要從自適應數據或者合成數據中清除，這從根本上來說跟障礙言語恢復方法類似。我們提出用語音轉換來研發障礙語音恢復技術。我們將把精力集中與構音障礙上。構音障礙是言語障礙中最常見的，它跟神經系統損傷有關並且影響全球數百萬人。我們將設計基於深度學習的障礙語音恢復方法，這種方法跟現存方法相比具有兩個主要的優勢：（i）非常少的訓練數據量要求；（ii）聲學-語音學特征和說話人語音特征之間明確的模型分離 -- 這樣，目標說話人數據的構音發音元素就不會影響語音轉換的結果。我們會用能夠將說話人不同點歸一化的語音后驗概率譜（PPGs）來表示源說話人和目標說話人的聲學-語音學空間。我們將開發一個能夠同時對正常語音和構音障礙語音進行建模來得到PPGs的語音識別系統。我們將用少量的平行數據訓練一個基於深度雙向長期短期記憶的循環神經網絡（DBLSTM-RNN），它能在多說話人之間從構音障礙的PPGs轉換到正常發音的PPGs。將經轉換過的正常PPGs輸入到DBLSTM-RNN合成模型可以實現片段級的構音障礙語音到正常語音的恢復。我們將把模型增強到能夠修改音高和時長的超音級恢復。我們的研究成果將產出改良的個性化VOCAs，這將有助於眾多的構音障礙者，特別是中文構音障礙群體。

14208817.label: Realisation of objectives
14208817.value: Realization of Objectives: 1. Expand existing Chinese dysarthric speech corpus. While we have extended the Chinese dysarthric speech corpus following a previous collection, we have also devised a new approach that can leverage the use of a large amounts of normal speech. This approach is especially helpful given the difficulty of finding dysarthric individuals who agree to donate speech data through recording sessions. We are mindful that such recording sessions are often exhausting for our participants, due to their conditions. We proposed an approach that uses model-based speaker adaptation with limited dysarthric speech data to fine-tune a base model that has been pre-trained with large amounts of normal speech – and in this way obtains speaker-dependent models. The challenge is that there is statistical distribution mismatch between normal and dysarthric speech data, which limits the adaptation performance of the base model. We proposed to reinitialize the base model via meta-learning to obtain a better model initialization. The re-initialized model can acquire dysarthric speech knowledge and learns how to perform fast adaptation to previously unseen dysarthric speakers with improved performance. This work was published in IEEE ISCSLP 2021. 2. Dual modeling of dysarthric and normal speech in unified automatic speech recognition to build up the phonetic posteriorgram space for both speech types. We devised an approach that uses diffusion probabilistic models to recover mel spectrograms iteratively from Gaussian noise, conditioning on content, tone and loudness features. The content features are extracted as phonetic posteriorgrams (PPGs) using Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) from the signal. This work was published in IEEE ASRU 2021. 3. Develop voice conversion approach from dysarthric to normal speech, exploring either the segmental or suprasegmental level. • We first experimented with voice conversion (VC) and proposed a novel approach that can beyond one-to-one VC (i.e. one source speaker to one target speaker) to any-to-many VC. This converts a source speech signal from an arbitrary speaker to a target speaker appearing in the training set. Few any-to-many VC approaches have been reported in the literature. Our proposed approach achieves robust, non-parallel sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) VC. The novel approach concatenates a seq2seq phoneme recognizer and a multi-speaker duration informed attention network for synthesis. Extension is also made on this approach to enable support of any-to-any voice conversion. Thorough examinations including objective and subjective evaluations are conducted for this model in any-to-many, as well as any-to-any settings. This work is published in the IEEE/ACM Transactions 2021. • We have devised a novel end-to-end voice conversion (VC) framework that contains three components. First, a sequence-to-sequence text-to-speech (TTS) synthesizer is trained with transcribed normal speech. The text encoder of this trained TTS is leveraged as the “teacher” in a teacher-student framework using a knowledge distillation (KD) approach. In particular, we have used cross-modal KD by training a speech-encoder to extract appropriate linguistic representations from transcribed dysarthric speech. In this way, we have utilized the normal and dysarthric speech data for the first two components. The third component will effectuate voice conversion, as listed in the next project objective. This work was published in IEEE ICASSP 2020. • At the suprasegmental level, we focused on prosody. Given a speech encoder that generates robust phoneme embeddings from dysarthric speech, we proposed a prosody corrector that takes in phoneme embeddings to infer typical phoneme duration and pitch values. Then, a conversion model takes phoneme embeddings and typical prosody features as inputs to generate the converted speech, conditioned on the target deep speaker embedding that is learned via speaker encoder or speaker adaptation. Evaluation demonstrates significantly improved intelligibility after speech restoration. This work was published in INTERSPEECH 2021. • A further development of the idea of cross-modal knowledge transfer is to learn phoneme-like acoustic indices from mel-spectrograms in the content encoder, and transfer it to a lip-to-index network that takes as input a lip sequence and infers the index sequence of acoustic units. This can then be used in a video-to-speech synthesis system to convert silent videos to acoustic units for reconstructing accurate spoken content. This work is published in IEEE ICASSP 2022. 4. Develop the voice conversion methodology into a speech restoration framework Under the previous project objective, we described the first two components of our proposed end-to-end voice conversion (VC) framework. The third component is where the speech encoder trained with transcribed dysarthric speech is concatenated with the attention and decoder of the first TTS component to achieve dysarthric speech restoration. As mentioned above, this work was published in IEEE ICASSP 2020. In addition to restoring the speech to be normal-sounding, dysarthric speech restoration must also preserve the speaker’s identity. We have devised an approach whereby a speaker encoder (SE) is optimized for speaker verification in order to control the speaker identity. This is further enhanced for capturing the characteristics of dysarthric speakers that are previously unseen. To address this issue, we proposed a novel, multi-task learning strategy, using adversarial speaker adaptation (ASA). The primary task of ASA is to fine-tune the SE with the speech of the target dysarthric speaker to effectively capture identity-related information, and the secondary task applies adversarial training to avoid the incorporation of abnormal speaking patterns into the reconstructed speech, by regularizing the distribution of reconstructed speech to be close to that of reference speech with high quality. Experiments show that the proposed approach can achieve enhanced speaker similarity and comparable speech naturalness with a strong baseline approach. This work is published in IEEE ICASSP 2022. 5. Perform objective and subjective evaluation of speech restoration outputs. To verify the effectiveness of the proposed method to improve the quality of dysarthric speech, we conducted three subjective evaluation tests including two mean opinion score (MOS) tests and one by human speech recognition. 10 listeners are asked to conduct 5-scale MOS tests (1-bad, 2-poor, 3-fair, 4-good, 5-excellent) in terms of speech naturalness and content similarity between the converted (i.e. restored) speech and reference speech. We also obtained the reduction word error rates (WERs) of human speech recognition of the original dysarthric speech and the corresponding restored version. As mentioned above, this work was published in IEEE ICASSP 2020. Evaluation results reflect the effectiveness of the proposed approach in dysarthric speech reconstruction – through attainment of high degrees of naturalness and intelligibility, as well as significant reduction in WERs.

14208817.label: Major findings and research outcome
14208817.value: We have devised a novel end-to-end voice conversion (VC) framework for dysarthric speech reconstruction. The framework contains three components. First, a sequence-to-sequence text-to-speech (TTS) synthesizer is trained with transcribed normal speech. The text encoder of this trained TTS is leveraged as the “teacher” in a teacher-student framework using a knowledge distillation (KD) approach. In particular, we have used cross-modal KD by training a speech-encoder to extract appropriate linguistic representations from transcribed dysarthric speech. In this way, we have utilized the normal and dysarthric speech data for the first two components. The third component is where the speech encoder trained with transcribed dysarthric speech is concatenated with the attention and decoder of the first TTS component to achieve dysarthric speech restoration. Dysarthric speech reconstruction necessitates correction in prosody. Given a speech encoder that generates robust phoneme embeddings from dysarthric speech, we proposed a prosody corrector that can take in phoneme embeddings to infer typical phoneme duration and pitch values. Then, we devised a conversion model takes in phoneme embeddings and typical prosody features as inputs to generate the converted speech, conditioned on the target deep speaker embedding that is learned via speaker encoder or speaker adaptation. Evaluation demonstrates significantly improved intelligibility after speech restoration. In addition to restoring the speech to be normal-sounding, dysarthric speech restoration must also preserve the speaker’s identity. We have devised an approach whereby a speaker encoder (SE) is optimized for speaker verification in order to control the speaker identity. This is further enhanced for capturing the characteristics of dysarthric speakers that are previously unseen. To address this issue, we proposed a novel, multi-task learning strategy, using adversarial speaker adaptation (ASA). The primary task of ASA is to fine-tune the SE with the speech of the target dysarthric speaker to effectively capture identity-related information, and the secondary task applies adversarial training to avoid the incorporation of abnormal speaking patterns into the reconstructed speech, by regularizing the distribution of reconstructed speech to be close to that of reference speech with high quality. Experiments show that the proposed approach can achieve enhanced speaker similarity and comparable speech naturalness with a strong baseline approach.

14208817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14208817.value: The proposed framework of disordered speech reconstruction (DSR) has been demonstrated to be capable of automatically transforming disordered, dysarthric speech into normal-sounding speech. This transformed speech attains high levels of speech naturalness and intelligibility after voice reconstruction. Further development of this research may pursue the directions of adapting the framework for applicability to other languages and dialects, applicability to different levels of dysarthria (ranging from mild to moderate to severe), as well as applicability to other types of speech disorders aside from dysarthria.

14208817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14208817.value: Speech disorders impair a speaker’s capacity to produce normal speech. This project focuses on dysarthria, a speech disorder caused by neuromotor problems that lead to poor control of articulators. Dysarthric speech sounds labored, but the intelligibility is low. We aim to develop an approach for dysarthric speech reconstruction (DSR), which can automatically transform dysarthric speech into normal-sounding speech. We present an encoder-decoder framework that achieves DSR through solving three sub-problems: (1) Content restoration – where the approach leverages the mechanisms of text-to-speech synthesis in generating normal speech, as well as cross-modal knowledge distillation to adapt generation from textual input to dysarthric speech input. (2) Prosody correction – where the approach reconstructs phoneme durations and fundamental frequencies for normal speech output. (3) Speaker identity preservation – where the approach effectively captures identity-related information, but avoids incorporation of abnormal speaking patterns into the reconstructed speech. We have demonstrated that the proposed framework can achieve high degrees of speech naturalness and intelligibility in the reconstructed speech, while preserving the speaker’s identity in the signal. DSR technologies present great potential in enhancing the quality of life and social inclusion of individuals with speech disorders.
