14208917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14208917.value: As technology advances, there are more complex standard cells for power and performance consideration, and it is common to have standard cells of multi-row heights in a design. Complex cells with small single-row height will bring congestion problem, especially as the number of tracks per row has been steadily decreasing. In addition, single-row height cells in high performance systems may not be able to deliver sufficiently large current because of the small transistor sizes. The popularity of multi-bit flip flops (MBFF) to reduce power consumption and area will also lead to more multi-row height cells in a design. All these emergent challenges make it essential for a tool to be able to handle a significant number of multi-row height cells in the physical design flow and in placement in particular. However, traditional placers work with standard cells of uniform height and the cells are placed row-wise aligning with the power/ground rails. The placement of cells in each row can thus be performed quite independently. In the presence of multi-row height cells, placements between rows are no longer independent and power/ground alignment of cells of different heights imposes more constraints on the placement problem. With multi-row height cells, legalization and detailed placement becomes more complicated. However, there are not many previous works on detailed placement for multi-row height cells. On the other hand, as the process technology of semiconductor scales down to nanometers, the gap between the illuminating wavelength and the process node becomes bigger and lithography awareness has become an inevitable feature of a placer today. With the presence of multi-row height cells, layout decomposition becomes an even more challenging task since the coloring in one row will directly affect the colorings of many other rows. This cascading effect will make the move of even one single cell difficult and slow. In this proposal, we plan to research on this placement problem with multi-row height cells in order to develop a hybrid lithography aware detailed placement flow for designs with macros and standard cells of different heights. Continued semiconductor scaling will bring a rapid increase in circuit complexity and an advanced hybrid lithography aware placement technology to handle effectively multi-row height standard cells is urgently needed. The success of this project will definitely contribute to the VLSI CAD community and to the design of high performance microprocessors. 隨著科技的進步， 標準元件因能源和性能等考量而設計的更加複雜。現在在設計中使用多行高的標準元件是普遍的一種做法。由於每一行的磁軌數量顯著降低，只有單行高的標準元件會帶來電路擁塞問題。除此之外，由於晶體管體積太小，在高性能系統中單行高的元件可能不會有效的傳遞大量電流。而且為了減少能源消耗並縮小面積，多位觸發器的廣泛使用也推動著多行高的元件在設計中出現。由於這些新的挑戰的出現，如何更好的在設計中，尤其是在佈局中，處理明顯增多的多行高元件變得尤為重要。然而，傳統的佈局器只是處理統一高度的元件，它只是將元件放置到每一行，對齊電源線和地線。因此每一行的元件的佈局可以單獨處理。而多行高的元件的出現，行與行之間的佈局變得不在獨立，元件在不同高度下和電源線和地線的對齊的佈局有了更多的限制。因為多行高的元件，合法放置和細部擺放也變得更為複雜。然而並沒有很多前作來處理細部擺放中的多行高元件。 另一方面，隨著半導體行業科技節點到納米技術，光的波長和工藝節點的差距越來越大，佈局器不得不考慮光刻因素。由於多行元件的出現，在每一行的塗色會直接影響其他行的塗色，佈局的分解變得更又挑戰性。這種級聯的影響讓每個單個元件的移動更加困難和緩慢。在本提案中，我們計劃對此多行高的元件佈局進行研究，並對有巨型單元和不同高度的標準單元的設計來開發一個混合考慮光刻的細部擺放的流程。半導體尺寸不斷地減小使電路越來越複雜，現今更需要一個先進的混合光刻佈局技術來有效的處理多行高的標準單元。這個項目一定會給超大型整合電路帶來巨大的貢獻並給電路帶來更高的性能。

14208917.label: Realisation of objectives
14208917.value: In this project, we have studied two important issues related to detailed placement, the presence of multi-row height cells and hybrid lithography awareness. In sub-7nm technology, the gap between device size and metal pitches becomes larger and the number of routing tracks within a cell becomes smaller, and more standard cells are thus implemented with multi-row height. We studied this problem of detailed placement and legalisation in the presence of multi-row height cells, with an objective to remove overlaps while minimising displacement from the global placement solution, minimising wire length and maximising routability. We developed a fast and high-quality legalisation framework for standard cells with mixed cell heights, that out-performs the state-of-the-art works under the displacement objective. We designed a multi-threaded method called Multi-row Global Legalisation (MGL) that can insert a multi-row standard cell at an optimal position of a window with respect to its global placement position. An iterative bipartite graph matching method is applied to minimise the maximum displacement among a group of cells without creating additional violations. A min-cost flow (MCF) formulation of the fixed-row-and-fixed-order problem is developed to optimise displacement, with constraints on cell movements to avoid lithography aware Design Rule Check (DRC) violations like pin short and pin access. Our detailed placer optimises both the maximum and average displacement from the global placement solution. It considers fence constraints and lithography aware DRC constraints like edge spacing, pin access and short, minimising the number of violations. For the issue of hybrid lithography awareness, we studied the problem of co-optimisation of cell layout decomposition and multiple patterning lithography (MPL) aware detailed placement for designs with macros and standard cells. In the detailed placer we developed, different layout decompositions of the patterns inside a cell are represented by different colouring solutions, which can be enumerated very efficiently. The placement of a cell can then be incorporated with these decomposition decisions by an efficient MPL-aware compaction algorithm and an efficient MPL-aware legalisation method based on dynamic programming. As discussed above, our placer considers displacement constraint to minimise the total displacement from the global placement solution under hybrid lithography awareness.

14208917.label: Major findings and research outcome
14208917.value: The advancement in semiconductor technology shrinks feature size and boosts design constraints that lead to many new emergent problems in placement and routing. Multi-row height standard cells resolve the problem of lacking intra-cell routing resources but bring challenges to traditional placers. Increases in cell pin density and power mesh limits the number of pin access points for each pin, bringing challenges to lithography related Design Rule Check (DRC) satisfaction. The increasing number of multi-row height standard cells and the need to consider hybrid lithography issues are important concerns in physical design. In this project, we studied their impact on detailed placement and developed efficient methods to handle them during placement legalisation, detailed placement and routing (please refer to DAC2018, ASP-DAC 2019, ICCAD 2019, TCAD 2020 in section C). Detailed placement and routing are the "right" stages to handle these issues, and very effective methods can be developed and incorporated into a detailed placer or router to resolve potential lithography related problems that may occur during manufacturing further down the design and manufacturing flow. Our works on development of such detailed placer and router have confirmed on this.

14208917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14208917.value: There is a good potential of further development in the direction of considering lithography related issues in detailed placement and routing. Besides multiple patterning and hotspot detection, other lithography and Design Rule Check (DRC) related issues should be considered during detailed placement to provide a good placement solutions for the later designing steps. A good example is pin access, and it is beneficial to have a detailed placer that can consider pin access plans for the cells in the design, so that routing can be completed more easily without DRC violations. To achieve this, one needs to come up with a modelling that can capture the accessibility of the pins of a cell and its neighbouring cells so that the detailed placer can consider this additional metric besides other performance factors like displacement, wire length and routability.

14208917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14208917.value: As the technology in semiconductor advances, there are many new challenges to the design and manufacturing process. One example is the appearance of multi-row height standard cells. In the past, all the standard cells are of the same height to simplify the complicated design process. As technology advances, the minimum feature size decreases and circuit design becomes more complex, leading to the appearance of standard cells with different heights. Besides, new lithography technologies like multiple patterning, EUV, etc. are also needed to push forward the advancement. All these changes impact traditional detailed placement and routing in physical design and it is essential to study how detailed placement can take into account of these new issues to lead to successful manufacturing at the end. In this project, we studied this problem and developed a detailed placer that is lithography-aware and can handle multi-row height cells. Comparisons with other approaches have shown its superiority over previous works on the problem.

14209217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14209217.value: Imagine that you stand in front of a mirror and you request your artificial assistant to generate a desired outfit, e.g., “A white shirt, black trousers, with a yellow jacket”, for your special occasion. It then automatically synthesizes the right outfit and renders it to ‘replace’ the pyjamas you are currently wearing (Fig. 1). This project aims to develop the core deep generative framework and computer vision algorithms for fashion image generation. Image generation is an important and classic problem in computer vision and machine learning. Despite years of research, generating realistic and high-resolution images with fine structures remains an ill-posed question due to the difficulty in capturing the complex classes of different texture types and bridging the semantic gap between input space and real-world image. The problem is further compounded in fashion synthesis given the additional challenge of modelling abstract unstructured concepts of styles. In addition, the model needs to take various contextual information, e.g., wearer’s attributes (age, body size, gender) and text description (e.g., a casual blue T-shirt with logo), into consideration during the synthesis process. No solutions exist to resolve the aforementioned problems. In this proposal, we discuss plausible parametric models with the following novelties: i) We make the first attempt to decompose a complex generating process into multiple generative stages, each of which conditioned on the previous stage. Thanks to the decomposition, each stage becomes more manageable in terms of training and inference complexity. In addition, semantical constraints such as attributes and text can be integrated seamlessly between stages as conditioning variables. ii) We formulate a new competing generative adversarial framework to better capture rich textures in fashion. iii) We investigate a novel joint image generation and super-resolution framework through decomposition of multiple spectral components. The project is meaningful both practically and scientifically. In particular, it will lead to a variety of interesting applications, e.g., fashion synthesis, recognition, and retrieval. Its learned features can be exploited for fashion recognition and cloth detection. The project would also benefit existing research through inspiring new formulations for generative modeling and adversarial learning. Generative learning is useful for a number of downstream tasks such as classification, regression, visualization, and reinforcement learning. The algorithms are not limited to fashion but can be further expanded to other types of visual categories such as face and general images. 想像一下，你站在鏡子前面，要求你的人工智能助手為你設計一個你想像的衣服，例如“白襯衫，黑色長褲，黃色外套”。然後，它自動合成正確的時裝，並使其“更換“你目前穿著的睡衣。 這項目旨在開發時裝生成的核心深度學習生成框架和計算機視覺算法。圖像生成是計算機視覺和機器學習中重要和經典的問題。儘管經過多年的研究，由於難以為不同紋理類型建立模型，並彌補輸入空間與現實世界圖像之間的語義差距，因此生成具有精細結構的高分辨率圖像仍然是一個困難的問題。考慮到為抽象非結構化概念建模的挑戰，時裝圖像生成比一般圖像生成更為複雜。此外，模型需要在生成過程中考慮各種背景信息，例如佩戴者的屬性（年齡，身材，性別）和文本描述（例如，具有標誌的藍色T卹）。 在這個項目中，我們討論了具有以下方案：ⅰ）我們首先嘗試將複雜的生成過程分解成多個生成階段每個階段在培訓和推理複雜性方面變得更加易於管理另外，諸如屬性和文本之類的語義約束​​可以作為條件變量在階段之間無縫集成。ii）我們制定一個新的競爭性生成對抗框架，以更好地捕捉時尚的豐富紋理iii）我們研究新穎的聯合圖像生成和超分辨率框架。 這個項目將引領各種有趣的應用，例如時尚生成，識別和檢索。深度學習得到的表示可以用於時尚識別和衣服檢測。這項目有可能啟發新的生成建模和對抗學習方法生成。學習對於一些下游任務（如分類，回歸，可視化和強化學習）很有用。我們的算法不限於時尚生成，可以進一步擴展到其他的視覺類別。

14209217.label: Realisation of objectives
14209217.value: The work C1 realises objectives 1 and 2. In particular, we present a novel approach for the task of human pose transfer, which aims at synthesizing a new image of a person from an input image of that person and a target pose. Unlike existing methods, we propose to estimate dense and intrinsic 3D appearance flow to better guide the transfer of pixels between poses. We wish to generate the 3D flow from just the reference and target poses. Training a network for this purpose is non-trivial, especially when the annotations for 3D appearance flow are scarce by nature. We address this problem through a flow synthesis stage. This is achieved by fitting a 3D model to the given pose pair and project them back to the 2D plane to compute the dense appearance flow for training. The synthesized ground-truths are then used to train a feedforward network for efficient mapping from the input and target skeleton poses to the 3D appearance flow. With the appearance flow, we perform feature warping on the input image and generate a photorealistic image of the target pose. Extensive results on DeepFashion and Market-1501 datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach over existing methods. The work successfully demonstrate how fashion image generation can be decomposed into multiple stages of deep generative models. It also presents a new way to generate photo-realistic fashion images from different conditions. The work C8 facilitates objective 2 by providing better conditions to fashion generation. In particular, we focus in single-image 3D human recovery. The estimation of 3D model for in-the-wild images remains a formidable challenge. The reason lies in the fact that obtaining high-quality 3D annotations for in-the-wild images is an extremely hard task that consumes enormous amount of resources and manpower. To tackle this problem, previous methods adopt a hybrid training strategy that exploits multiple heterogeneous types of annotations including 3D and 2D while leaving the efficacy of each annotation not thoroughly investigated. In this work, we perform a comprehensive study on cost and effectiveness trade-off between different annotations. Specifically, we focus on the challenging task of in-the-wild 3D human recovery from single images when paired 3D annotations are not fully available. Through extensive experiments, we obtain several observations: 1) 3D annotations are efficient, whereas traditional 2D annotations such as 2D keypoints and body part segmentation are less competent in guiding 3D human recovery. 2) Dense Correspondence such as DensePose is effective. When there are no paired in-the-wild 3D annotations available, the model exploiting dense correspondence can achieve 92% of the performance compared to a model trained with paired 3D data. We show that incorporating dense correspondence into in-the-wild 3D human recovery is promising and competitive due to its high efficiency and relatively low annotating cost. The work C5 realises objective 3. We show that it is possible to recover textures faithful to semantic classes in texture generation. In particular, we only need to modulate features of a few intermediate layers in a single network conditioned on semantic segmentation probability maps. This is made possible through a novel Spatial Feature Transform (SFT) layer that generates affine transformation parameters for spatial-wise feature modulation. SFT layers can be trained end-to-end together with the SR network using the same loss function. During testing, it accepts an input image of arbitrary size and generates a high-resolution image with just a single forward pass conditioned on the categorical priors. Our final results show that an SR network equipped with SFT can generate more realistic and visually pleasing textures in comparison to state-of-the-art methods. The work C2 realises objective 4. In this work, we thoroughly study three key components of image super-resolution based on generative adversarial network – network architecture, adversarial loss and perceptual loss, and improve each of them to derive an Enhanced SRGAN (ESRGAN). In particular, we introduce the Residual-in-Residual Dense Block (RRDB) without batch normalization as the basic network building unit. Moreover, we borrow the idea from relativistic GAN to let the discriminator predict relative realness instead of the absolute value. Finally, we improve the perceptual loss by using the features before activation, which could provide stronger supervision for brightness consistency and texture recovery. Benefiting from these improvements, the proposed ESRGAN achieves consistently better visual quality with more realistic and natural textures than SRGAN and won the first place in the PIRM2018-SR Challenge (region 3) with the best perceptual index.

14209217.label: Major findings and research outcome
14209217.value: In this project, we found effective ways of generating and transferring textures. Major findings include a new pipeline of estimating dense and intrinsic 3D appearance flow to better guide the transfer of pixels between poses; a comprehensive study of different 3D annotations, which facilitate cost effective labelling of 3D models; a novel Spatial Feature Transform (SFT) layer that generates affine transformation parameters for spatial-wise feature modulation, which helps generating photorealistic textures faithful to the underlying semantic classes; and a new model architecture that can allow generation of fine details in super-resolution.

14209217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14209217.value: Our ongoing work include the following: i) to improve texture generation performance for fashion given different conditioning human poses and very fashion styles; ii) to improve the details in texture generation. To address the first problem, we are investigating alternative models such as variational auto-encoder and diffusion models. For the second problem, we are studying new technique to integrate generative priors into the network.

14209217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14209217.value: This project aims to develop the core deep generative framework and computer vision algorithms for fashion image generation. Image generation is an important and classic problem in computer vision and machine learning. Despite years of research, generating realistic and high-resolution images with fine structures remains an ill-posed question due to the difficulty in capturing the complex classes of different texture types and bridging the semantic gap between input space and real-world image. In this project, we study approaches to decompose a complex image generating process into easier and more manageable subtasks. We also investigate new priors, new architectures, and more effective conditions to help texture generation.

14209317.label: Project Objectives

In the realm of SPA applications in coding theory, one special focus will be on the analysis of spatially-coupled LDPC codes and LDPC convolutional codes, where we expect our technique not only to yield novel insights into the benefits of spatial coupling, but also to help in formulating efficient code design algorithms that yield codes with very good finite-length performance, i.e., low error floors for various classes of channels. Besides the point-to-point communication setting, we want to establish a pseudo-codeword-based theory towards characterizing and improving SPA-based coding schemes for channels like the relay channel, the interference channel, and beyond. Such results would not only be of fundamental combinatorial importance, but also advance methods like pattern maximum likelihood estimation that appear in data science.

14209317.label: Realisation of objectives
14209317.value: Four of my PhD students, one of my MPhil students, and one postdoc have worked on topics related to this project: (1) July X. Li (LI Xialu) (PhD, supported by this grant Sep. 2018 - Jan. 2021) (2) Michael X. Cao (CAO Xuan) (PhD, supported by this grant Sep. 2018 - Dec. 2018) (3) Charles Cao (CAO Haiwen) (PhD, supported by PGS, not supported by this grant) (4) Anthony Huang (HUANG Yuwen) (PhD, suppored by PGS, not supported by this grant) (5) Jacky Ng (NG Kit Shing) (MPhil, supported by this grant Jan. 2021 - May 2021) (6) Shashank Vatedka (postdoc, not supported by this grant) For all of the above students and the postdoc, I directly supervised their research by having individual weekly meetings, giving them advice on how to proceed, telling them about relevant papers, sometimes outlining potential solutions, sometimes proving results and writing computer programs myself, and giving guidance while writing papers. ------------------------------------------------- Contributions toward objectives (more details below): (1) July X. Li has mainly contributed to Objectives 2 and 3, and somewhat to Objective 1. (2) Michael X. Cao has mainly contributed to Objective 4. (3) Charles Cao has mainly contributed to Objective 2 and 3. (4) Anthony Huang has mainly contributed to Objectives 1 and 4 (5) Jacky Ng has mainly contributed to Objectives 4, and somewhat to Objective 1. (6) Shashank Vatedka has mainly contributed to Objective 4. -------------------------------------------------- The unifying theme of this project was to gain a better understanding of the sum-product algorithm (SPA) for various graphical models, in particular in the context of reliable communication and storage, and more generally in the context of classical and quantum information processing. A key tool were (topological) graph covers of the graphical model under consideration, as introduced in earlier work by Koetter and the PI. (On the side, the PI has been elevated to IEEE Fellow (class of 2021) "for contributions to graphical models for channel coding".) -------------------------------------------------- (1) July X. Li's main focus was on the construction and decoding of quantum stabilizer codes. (Such coding schemes will be needed for the reliable operation of future quantum computers.) She used insights gained from graph-cover-based pseudo-codewords to improve the finite-length performance of currently used SPA-based decoders. In particular, she introduced a two-stage decoder based on pseudo-codewords for quantum stabilizer cycle codes and quantum stabilizer color codes. The resulting decoder have local operations w.r.t. the underlying graphs, syndrome-weight-dependent computational complexity, and better decoding performance compared with previous approaches for these classes of codes. July worked also on quantum stabilizer codes over GF(4), i.e., over non-binary alphabets, and better understanding their properties. -------------------------------------------------- (2) Michael X. Cao's main focus was on characterizing the classical information rate of quantum channels with memory with the help of variations of the SPA. Here the SPA is not used for decoding, but for estimating the information rate of such channels. Moreover, he presented efficient algorithms for optimizing the information rate of so-called mismatched decoders that have low complexity. -------------------------------------------------- (3) Charles Cao's main focus was on spatially-coupled LDPC codes and afterwards on sparse regression codes. W.r.t. the first topic, he used graph-cover-based pseudo-codewords toward quantifying why spatially-coupled LDPC codes perform better than non-coupled LDPC codes. W.r.t. the second topic, he considered approximate message passing (AMP) decoding, which is a low-complexity approximation of the SPA, to sparse regression codes. In particular, he analyzed the finite-length behavior of such coding schemes and improved them by proposing novel design matrices (design matrices describe a sparse regression code), suitable outer codes for code concatenation, and decoding algorithms for the overall scheme. Finally, he studied sparse regression codes for multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) channel setups and proposed solutions to issues arising in this setup. -------------------------------------------------- (4) Anthony Huang's main focus was on understanding the approximation obtained by the SPA, known as the Bethe approximation, in the context of graphical models motivated by quantum information processing. For context: for graphical models, the partition sum (or partition function) Z is the sum of the global function over all configurations. For scenarios of interest, the partition sum is usually intractable and so one has to approximate it. In the context of classical information processing, Yedidia et al. defined the Bethe approximation Z_Bethe to the partition sum Z via the solution of an optimization problem and showed that fixed points of the SPA correspond to stationary points of the function appearing in the above-mentioned optimization problem. Later, the PI showed a combinatorial interpretation of Z_Bethe in terms of graph covers. While the expression of Z_Bethe in terms of an optimization problem is useful for numerical purposes, the latter result has proven beneficial for analytically relating the values of Z and Z_Bethe. Anthony investigated the generalization of the above results to graphical models motivated by quantum information processing. In particular, he analyzed if the combinatorial interpretation of Z_Bethe in terms of graph covers still holds. This is non-trivial because the proof technique that was used in the classical setup breaks down in the quantum setup. We were able to show that for certain classes of graphical models (which satisfy an easily checkable condition) the result still holds. In fact, based on numerical results, we conjecture that the result holds much more generally. An important ingredient of the proof was a graphical-model transform, which we called the symmetric subspace transform. This transform has strong similarities to the graphical-model transform in the proposal. While the latter was formulated for binary alphabets and covers of degree two (with potential for extensions), we were able to generalize the symmetric subspace transform to non-binary alphabets and higher-degree covers. In another research direction, Anthony considered the local marginal polytope associated with graphical models. For context: the local marginal polytope is the domain of the above optimization problem and collects all the relevant variable-based and function-based marginals for the graphical model under consideration. For most graphical models with cycles, the local marginal polytope is such that there are collections of marginals that cannot be written as marginals of a joint probability mass function. This is an important aspect when understanding and quantifying the suboptimality of the SPA. As we discovered, interestingly enough, the same mathematical structures appear when trying to understand the benefits of entanglement in quantum information processing (cf. Bell's inequalities). -------------------------------------------------- (5) Jacky Ng's main focus was on qualitatively and quantitatively characterizing the Bethe approximation of the permanent of a non-negative, square matrix. The permanent of a non-negative, square matrix is one of the most prototypical (weighted) counting problems in theoretical computer science and appears naturally in many information processing scenarios. In this context, the Bethe approximation of the permanent obtained via the SPA is known as the Bethe permanent. A technique introduced by the PI in 2016 for analyzing the Bethe approximation, which was one of the pillars of this grant proposal, was successfully used to analyze the Bethe permanent for certain classes of matrix families. -------------------------------------------------- (6) Shashank Vatedka's main focus was also the approximation of the permanent for non-negative matrices. However, he introduced a novel graphical model, i.e., a graphical model that is different than the traditionally used graphical model for approximating the permanent via the SPA. He studied the resulting Bethe approximation and showed that for some classes of matrices, with a slight increase in computational complexity compared with the traditionally used graphical model, better approximation guarantees can be given. -------------------------------------------------- Some of the insights gained in the above research have be weaved into my post-graduate course IERG5200 (Channel Coding and Modulation) in Spring 2020 and Spring 2022 and my post-graduate course IERG6120 (Quantum Information Processing) in Spring 2021. -------------------------------------------------- Concerning Objectives 1-3, where I indicated 90% completion: this is due to slightly more focus being spent on Objective 4 than originally planned. (This refocusing is not due to fundamental problems, but due to pursuing the most promising directions based on the capabilities of the students and postdocs.)

14209317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14209317.value: Potential research directions based on the obtained result include the following. -------------------------------------------------- Extension of the results that were obtained by Anthony Huang. We want to show that in the quantum setup the combinatorial characterization of the Bethe approximation of the partition sum holds more generally than we were able to prove so far. At the same time, we want to search for counter-examples (we do not have a counter-example so far), which would show limitations to the generality of the conjecture. -------------------------------------------------- Extension of the results that were obtained by Jacky Ng. Let M be some subset of the set of square matrices with non-negative entries. An interesting optimization problem is the following: arg max_{A in M} perm(A), where perm(A) is the permanent of A. We want to investigate for which sets of matrices M we can replace the above optimization problem by arg max_{A in M} perm_B(A), where perm_B(A) represents the Bethe permanent of A, such that arg max_{A in M} perm_B(A) approximates arg max_{A in M} perm(A) well in some suitable sense. Empirically, it works well for various sets of matrices M, but we would like to better understand this observation analytically. --------------------------------------------------

14209317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14209317.value: Various important information processing tasks can be expressed as message-passing iterative (MPI) algorithms operating on some suitable graphical models. For example, reliable data communication in the recent 5G telecommunications standard is achieved with the help of low-density parity-check codes, where the checks that are imposed by the code are expressed in terms of a graphical model and where decoding is achieved by running an MPI algorithm on this graphical model. The aim of this project was to enhance our understanding of MPI algorithms in existing and novel applications. Building on earlier work by the PI, a key technique were so-called (topological) graph covers of the graphical model under consideration, in particular pseudo-codewords induced by graph covers. Pseudo-codewords can be used to characterize and quantify the suboptimality of MPI algorithm compared with (usually intractable) maximum-likelihood-based schemes. In a particular research direction, we used pseudo-codewords to characterize the suboptimality of stabilizer quantum code decoders (such schemes will be needed for the reliable operation of future quantum computers) and then also employed pseudo-codewords to enhance the performance of MPI decoders.

14209417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14209417.value: In the past years random local functions have emerged as a foundational object in the unstruc- tured world of symmetric-key cryptography, shedding light on the computational complexity of primitives such as pseudorandom generators and collision-resistant hash functions. These results were enabled by rigorous studies of the security in the regime where the output length is significantly longer than the input length. Current methods do not yield much insight about hardness in the setting where the input and output length are roughly equal. We propose to examine this setting using both empirical and theoretical tools. A reasonable objective is to relate the observed hardness in inverting instances to the geometry of the solution space, leveraging methods developed to analyze satisfiability of random k-CNF formulas. Random local functions have so far had limited impact is in the construction of pseudorandom functions, the workhorse of symmetric-key cryptography. We consider two specific families of proposed constructions and propose specific criteria for testing their security. We believe that this line of work may be influential beyond cryptography and shed further light on hardness of learning and proving circuit lower bounds for specific computational models, including boolean formulas and small-depth circuits with parity gates. 過去幾年，隨機局部函數已經成為對稱密鑰加密領域的非結構化世界中的基礎對象，揭示了如偽隨機函數及抗衝突雜湊函數等密碼學基元的計算複雜度。這些安全性的嚴格研究結果都基於輸出長度明顯長於輸入長度的設置。 在輸入和輸出長度大致相同的設置中，當前的方法對計算難度沒有太多了解。我們建議使用實驗和理論工具來研究這個設置。合理的目標是把觀察所得的反演實例的難度，與解空間的幾何聯繫起來，加以利用分析隨機合取範式可滿足性所用的方法。 到目前為止，隨機局部函數對於構造作為對稱密鑰加密骨幹的偽隨機函數的影響有限。我們研究兩個具體構造家族的建議，並提出測試其安全性的具體準則。我們相信這一系列研究的影響範圍超越密碼學，進一步揭示學習的難度，並為特定的計算模型（包括布爾方程式及具有奇偶檢驗門的小深度電路）提供電路複雜度的下限。

14209417.label: Realisation of objectives
14209417.value: The second objective of the project is to formalize security criteria for the security of ad-hoc pseudorandom function (PRF) constructions. The works in this project as well as works by others influenced by it have now adopted small-bias aganist linear tests, high degree as GF(2) polynomials, and high rational degree as necessary criteria for any candidate PRFs to satisfy. Moreover these criteria were met for the boolean formula size measure in the work “Small bias requires large formulas” that was realized as part of this project, leading to progress on the third objective. The work “Exploring Crypto Dark Matter ” by Boneh, Ishai, Passelegue, and Sahai carried out a similar analysis for the case of weak pseudorandom functions computed by ACC circuits (bounded depth circuits with MOD2 and MOD3 gates), attesting to the influence of the ideas introduced by this project. While further improvements in this direction may be possible (it is not yet clear what is the minimal model in which weak pseudorandom functions can be realized) we consider the third objective to have been largely accomplished. Regarding the first objective, a direct analysis of the “computational hardness threshold” for random local functions is still out of reach for current techniques. We found that some algorithmic results (e.g., “Strongly refuting random CSPs below the spectral threshold” by Raghavendra, Rao, and Schramm) indicate that there may not be a sharp threshold at which inversion of random local functions becomes computationally intractable, but the time complexity of inversion depends smoothly on the output length of the relevant function. This project carried out a thorough a precise analysis for the related question of randomness extraction from a general model of adversarial dice. In this setting a rich behavior was uncovered that depends on the probability distribution of the dice in question. Another work that arose from the ideas in this project addresses the natural problem of partitioning a function over multiple inputs into almost-independent parts. This was inspired by and found applications to variance reduction in reinforcement learning. While not directly related to the objectives, the idea of analyzing the bias of the relevant function (via generalized Fourier decomposition) played a crucial role in the result.

14209417.label: Major findings and research outcome
14209417.value: The main insight of the project is that in the absence of reductions of well-established hard problems, well-defined pseudorandomness criteria such as small-bias and high rational degree are reliable indicators of cryptographic hardness of pseudorandom functions. These can be used as a guiding design principle when the objective is to optimize for a specific complexity measure such as formula size. This project was carried out for pseudorandom functions in the work “Small bias requires large formulas”. Since the completion of the project statistical-computational gaps for statistical inference problems have been discovered to be a ubiquitous phenomenon in learning theory. This project uncovered the existence of such gaps for specific cryptographic functions. While fully explaining the hardness is still out of reach for current techniques, the project demonstrated that complete analyses can be carried out in the related setting of extractors from “generalized Santha-Vazirani” sources representing collections of biased dice. As a byproduct it was demonstrated that the pseudorandomness notion of small-bias has additional algorithmic applications to computing approximate decompositions of functions over product spaces into direct sums.

14209417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14209417.value: Constructions of local pseudorandom generators have recently found application in constructing indistinguishability obfuscation schemes, a very powerful cryptographic primitive. For that application it is important to obtain a favorable tradeoff between the degree d of the predicate specifying the pseudorandom generator and the output length m. It is known that m can be at most n^{d/2} but it is still open if this is in general achievable. Proving small-bias of the construction could be a tractable first step.

14209417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14209417.value: The established methodology for proving the security of cryptographic constructions (which underlie the security and privacy of much internet communication) is to argue that if the construction can be broken, then some well-known mathematical problem that has resisted decades of attempts can be solved. Despite great successes in the past such methods have found limited application to new proposals. The findings in this project support the use of specific tests to argue the security of more modern constructions with wider applicability. While such tests do not imply security in general they have proven effective in diversifying the existing toolkit of cryptographic primitives, some of which have found use in designing new protocols for secure computation.

14209517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14209517.value: Optical frequency comb source has found wide applications in optical metrology, precision spectroscopy, optical communications, optical signal processing, and microwave photonics. Key characteristics of a comb source include the operating spectral range and bandwidth, comb spacing, spacing tunability, comb flatness, optical signal-to-noise ratio, accuracy, and stability. Unfortunately, most commercial comb sources cannot match the requirements for applications such as wideband optical communications and signal processing. The limited comb spacing, spacing tunability, and noise performance are some of the constraints. In this proposal, we investigate a new and versatile technique to generate low-noise, widely spaced and tunable optical combs using readily available RF and optoelectronic components operating at relatively low frequencies. The common approaches to generate a frequency comb include the coupling of a continuous-wave or a mode-locked laser to a micro-resonator, or a mode-locked laser to a nonlinear optical medium. By contrast, our method is based on a cavity-less approach through external modulation. Apart from offering flexible carrier frequencies and comb spacing, the cavity-less approach exhibits improved comb quality since mode-locked laser pulses are usually initiated from noise, suffering from amplified spontaneous emission noise, supermode noise from harmonic mode-locking, drift of the center wavelength and phase instability. A key challenge of the cavity-less approach is the requirement of high-frequency electronic/optoelectronic equipment and components including the RF source, modulator drivers, and optical modulators in generating widely spaced frequency combs. In this proposal, we investigate a new approach using the fractional temporal Talbot effect for repetition rate multiplication of laser pulses by up to a factor of ten. Tunability of the multiplication rate is allowed through phase or intensity modulation of the input pulses without changing the fiber dispersion. The multiplied output is used to modulate another continuous wave laser through cross-phase modulation in a highly nonlinear fiber. Hence, the input pulses with a narrow optical frequency spacing can be used to generate spectral components at a multiplied frequency. Also, phase fluctuations in the input pulse train are removed. The comb generation will be enhanced by four-wave mixing among the spectral components. We will characterize the comb bandwidth, optical carrier to noise power ratio, comb flatness, and demonstrate wide tunability of the comb spacing using low-frequency optical modulation. Furthermore, we will investigate applications of our comb source in spectrally efficient optical communications with advanced modulation formats, as well as microwave photonic signal processing including polychromatic parametric sampling and radio frequency channelization. 光頻梳源在光學計量，精密光譜，光通信，光信號處理和微波光子中得到廣泛應用。光頻梳源的關鍵特性包括工作光譜範圍和帶寬，梳形間距，間距可調性，梳狀平坦度，光信噪比，準確性和穩定性。 然而，大多數商業光頻梳源不能滿足寬帶光通信和信號處理等應用的要求。 有限的梳形間距，間距可調性和噪聲性能是其中所存在的一些限制。 在這份提議書中，我們研究一種通用的新技術， 通過使用在較低頻率下工作的現成的射頻和光電子元件從而產生低噪聲，寬間距和可調諧的光頻梳源。 產生頻率梳的常見方法包括將連續波或鎖模激光器耦合到微諧振器或將鎖模激光器耦合進非線性光學介質。相比之下，我們的方法是基於一種利用外部調製的無腔的設計。除了提供載波頻率和梳狀間距可調的靈活性，這種無腔的方法還展現出頻率梳質量的提升，因為鎖模激光脈衝通常由噪聲引發，其性能往往會受到放大的自發發射噪聲，諧波模式鎖定的超模噪聲，中心波長漂移和相位不穩定的影響。在產生寬間隔頻率梳中，這種無腔的方法存在一個關鍵挑戰，就是對高頻電子/光電設備及部件包括射頻源，調製器驅動器和光調製器的需求。在這份提議書中，我們研究一種新的方法，通過時域分數Talbot效應來提高激光脈衝重複頻率達十倍。在不改變所用光纖的色散情況下，可通過對輸入脈衝的相位或強度調製從而實現激光脈衝重複頻率的可調。通過交叉相位調製效應，速率倍增的輸出脈衝在高度非線性光纖中用於調製另一束連續波激光。憑藉這種方法，窄光頻間隔的輸入脈衝可以用於產生以倍增速率為間隔的光譜分量。並且，輸入脈衝串中的相位波動會被去除。頻率梳的產生通過光譜分量之間的四波混頻效應得到增強。我們將表徵梳狀帶寬，光載波與噪聲功率比，梳狀平坦度，並使用低頻率的光學調製來展示梳形間距在廣範圍內的可調性。此外，我們還將探究這種頻率梳在進階調製格式的光譜高效光通信，以及微波光子信號處理中多色參量採樣和射頻信道化方面的應用。

14209517.label: Realisation of objectives
14209517.value: 1. To generate low-noise, widely spaced optical frequency combs at 50 GHz and 100 GHz using comb pitch multiplication by the fractional temporal Talbot effect together with cross phase modulation and to characterize the comb performance We experimentally demonstrate a new approach for the generation of widely spaced flexible optical frequency combs in a highly nonlinear fiber (HNLF) using relatively low-speed components [J1]. A cavity-less 10-GHz optical pulse source is passively multiplied up to ~50 GHz via the fractional temporal Talbot effect. The repetition rate multiplied pulse train then propagates in an HNLF together with a continuous-wave probe laser to achieve comb spacing multiplication through cross-phase modulation (XPM). Numerical study shows that the timing jitter of the initial 10-GHz optical pulse induces insignificant excess phase noise at high frequency offset relative to the optical comb lines, which favors a low phase noise wideband frequency comb generation. The spectral widths of 5 comb lines (the central line, the 5th and the 10th lines on both upper and lower frequency bands) have been experimentally characterized by the delayed self-heterodyne interferometric technique. Well-preserved linewidth quality has been obtained. Instead of relying on a HNLF, we also demonstrated the generation of frequency combs using XPM in a silicon waveguide fabricated on a CMOS-compatible integration platform [J8, C8, C9]. Optical frequency combs with spacings ranging from 140 to 200 GHz have been successfully generated with a maximum carrier-to-noise suppression ratio of ~45 dB [J8]. Other methods of producing and modulating optical frequency combs have been demonstrated using multi-wavelength single sideband generation [J4] and wavelength multicast approaches [J7, C5] 2. To achieve programmable spacing in the comb source by low-frequency intensity or phase modulation of the input optical pulses prior to comb pitch multiplication A programmable pulse-rate multiplier has been demonstrated for the generation of optical frequency combs with tunable spectral spacing [J1]. The multiplier provides an energy-efficient way for pulse-rate multiplication through electro-optic phase modulation followed by the temporal Talbot effect. In the demonstration, we multiply the rate of a 9.91-GHz optical pulse train by different factors of 3, 4, and 5. Subsequently, the multiplied pulses are applied to generate frequency combs spaced at 29.73, 39.64, and 49.55 GHz, respectively. We also numerically investigate the influence of the deviation in modulation patterns on the suppression of the undesirable secondary comb peaks. Our study is extended towards applying the scheme for the generation of programmable microwave waveforms through optical envelope detection. This is made possible by using the temporal Talbot effect to achieve discrete Fourier transform of the modulated optical pulse trains [C1, C3, C4]. With the use of joint amplitude and phase modulation, additional flexibility has been realized in the generation of arbitrary microwave waveforms [J5]. Programmability in the frequency comb spacing has also been demonstrated on the silicon photonic platform [C8]. Several other programmable approaches have been realized including the use of an optical processor to control the required dispersion [J8], the application of programmable binary modulation coefficients on a Mach-Zehnder modulator [J9], and the use of multi-wavelength nonlinear Bragg scattering for flexible frequency tone generation [J4]. 3. To modulate the comb source for spectrally efficient communications with an aggregate data rate approaching Tb/s, to achieve high-speed polychromatic parametric sampling, and to investigate photonic channelization of RF receivers As described in the proposal, we have generated 50-GHz spaced frequency comb using the temporal Talbot effect and cross-phase modulation. We then applied individual modulation to the central 11 comb lines by Nyquist-shaped 32 GBaud 16 quadratic-amplitude modulation signals, demonstrating the applicability of the comb source in providing optical carriers to achieve an aggregate data rate over Tb/s. We also perform study on carrier regeneration for a frequency comb based WDM system [J2]. This was demonstrated with 7 × 16 Gbaud QPSK data channels with 25 GHz spacing and a fiber transmission distance of 80 km. The work enables self-homodyne detection for communication systems adopting signals in advanced modulation formats. Besides, we have investigated frequency comb based Kramers-Kronig (KK) direct detection transmission links with 5x10 Gbaud QPSK/16-QAM channels [C2]. The frequency combs at the transmitter and receiver are locked by regenerating an optical carrier from a single sideband signal. We have also successfully applied self-seeded stimulated Brillouin scattering to improve the performance of KK detection for frequency comb based single-sideband signals. By virtue of low-carrier-to-signal power ratio (CSPR) transmission and high-CSPR detection, our proposed scheme effectively advances system performance by reducing propagation-induced distortion while maintaining the minimum phase condition [J6, C7]. Modulation of single-sideband signals has been achieved in a programmable optical frequency comb generated from dual-stage four-wave mixing, offering an attractive alternative approach to reach a high aggregate data rate [J4]. Polychromatic sampling has been demonstrated using temporal lenticular lens realized with electro-optic modulation and group velocity dispersion [J3, C6]. A parallel architecture based on time-interleaved sampling was used to increase the effective sampling rate. A 20 Gbit/s NRZ data pattern was copied to 4 different wavelengths to achieve an aggregate sampling rate of 80 GSample/s for signal reconstruction. Timing jitter of the sampling pulses was measured to be 26.8 fs. The effective number of bits was determined to decrease gradually from 4.2 to 3.5 over the frequency range of 40 – 80 GHz. We also developed a photonic technique to generate programmable microwave waveforms by temporal Talbot processing of an optical pulse train. The generation is realized by real-time Fourier transform of the modulation coefficients applied to an amplitude or IQ modulator before the dispersion medium [J5, C3, C4]. Our scheme offers potential benefits for diverse applications in optical and microwave signal processing.

14209517.label: Major findings and research outcome
14209517.value: Following our proposed plan, we have achieved the objectives of generating low-noise, widely spaced optical frequency combs, developing effective techniques for tuning the frequency spacing of the comb source, and applying the frequency comb in optical communications and RF photonics. Frequency combs with spacings that varied from 10 GHz to 200 GHz have been demonstrated. These combs were generated by first multiplying the repetition rate of an input optical pulse train using temporal Talbot processing in a dispersion medium, followed by cross phase modulation in a nonlinear optical medium. In our work, we have used a dispersive fiber and/or an optical processor to realize the optical dispersion. The nonlinear processing has been performed in either a highly nonlinear fiber or a silicon waveguide [J1, J8-9, C8-9]. Programmability of the repetition rate multiplication factor and hence the frequency comb spacing has been realized by applying electro-optic phase or intensity modulation to the input pulse train, leading to high-quality frequency combs with a carrier-to-noise ratio as high as 45 dB. Applications of the frequency combs in optical communications and RF photonics have been investigated. By modulating the frequency combs with advanced modulation formats including QPSK and 16-QAM, we have demonstrated the generation of high-data-rate coherent optical signals. The signals have been successfully transmitted over 80-km fiber and detected at the receiver. Carrier regeneration that supports self-homodyne detection has been adopted [J2, J6, C2, C7]. For the applications in RF photonics, we demonstrated multi-channel time and wavelength-interleaved optical sampling, effectively increasing the overall sampling rate by a factor equal to the number of channels [J3, C6]. Programmable microwave waveform generation has also been realized by amplitude and phase modulation of the optical pulse trains together with temporal Talbot processing [J5, C1, C3-4]. The scheme offers a significant reduction in the required bandwidth of the electronic devices and system in generating the waveforms.

14209517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14209517.value: In the course of carrying out the research project, we have identified two important areas that deserve further investigation. The first area is related to the choice of the primary laser source in generating the optical frequency comb. Since the phase noise of the generated comb lines is mainly limited by that of the input laser, it is crucial to look into how different lasers will affect the phase noise property of the frequency comb. Therefore, we have collaborated with the Changchun Institute of Optics, Fine Mechanics and Physics of the Chinese Academy of Sciences on applying their semiconductor lasers for optical frequency comb generation and characterization. A joint proposal was submitted and was funded for 1 million RMB in 2022. Another area that deserves attention is regeneration of the programmable optical frequency comb at the receiver. This process is of much significance in simplifying the required digital signal processing for compensating the frequency offset between the transmitter comb and the receiver comb. We have prepared another GRF project to investigate the possible solutions. The proposal was funded for an amount of HKD 673,470 for three years starting from January 1, 2020.

14209517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14209517.value: Nowadays, lasers have been widely used in optical communications, optical sensing, precision measurement, and in different consumer electronics. There are however limitations in their applications in meeting the demand of optical bandwidth, resolution, and processing performance. An effective way to extend the capability of the lasers is to use them to generate a coherent frequency comb of optical carriers. Compared to a set of discrete lasers at different wavelengths, a frequency comb offers simplicity in the electrical and optical control, programmability in the frequency spacing, and intrinsic coherence among the optical carriers. In this proposal, we have successfully generated programmable and widely spaced optical frequency combs by making use of combined linear and nonlinear optical processing techniques. The combs have been characterized and applied in different optical communication systems to increase the overall data rate of transmission. Also, the combs have been used in RF photonic systems for high-speed waveform sampling and programmable microwave waveform generation. Our research findings shed light on using optical frequency combs to enhance the capability of the laser sources for potential new applications.

14210117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14210117.value: Robot assisted surgery is greatly favored in many clinical surgical operation procedures because of its advantages in smaller incisions, less blood loss, and faster recovery, among others. Tracking system is the soul of robot assisted surgery. With the help of tracking system, surgical robot can find the relative pose relationship amongst medical images, surgical instruments and lesions, and then compensate the drawbacks of the traditional operation procedures that depend heavily on the experience of the surgeon and the direct sight view. In the past decades, various tracking systems have been developed for robotic surgery. In general, they can be classified into several categories, including mechanical tracking system, optical tracking system, magnetic tracking system, etc. Among these tracking systems, optical tracking system has been the “gold standard” for traditional open surgeries, and magnetic tracking system has been used in minimally-invasive surgeries. Nevertheless, information loss is a common problem in the widely adopted surgical tracking systems, which is characterized by missing versatility, occlusion and broken information feed, and accuracy instability in its localization algorithms. In this proposal, we plan to tackle the information loss problem of the surgical tracking systems and provide a versatile solution for both open and minimally-invasive surgeries. The main approach is to solve three identified underlining theoretical problems, namely adaptive multi-modality localization strategy, modeling method and improvement scheme for localization accuracy with corrupted data, and the mechanism investigation and compensation design for information loss during surgical procedures. The objectives of this proposed research are to set up a theoretical framework for the prediction, prevention and compensation of the information loss problems in robotic surgery and to develop an integrated optical-electromagnetic localization system with high accuracy, occlusion free, and improved versatility for robot assisted surgery applications. In specific, the developed system integrates the optical tracking system and the electro-magnetic tracking system to provide a versatile solution for both open and minimally-invasive surgeries. In this context, an adaptive and robust data fusion strategy that provides accurate tracking results and intelligently switching mechanisms between different surgical scenarios will be developed. To solve the information loss problem, we will focus on the compensation strategy and the associated technologies in both optical and electro-magnetic tracking systems. Consequently, the developed system will actively avoid obstacles that block the line-of-sight for the optical sub-system and resist signal data corruption for the electro-magnetic sub-system to achieve an optimal hybrid tracking system for robot assisted surgical procedures. 機器人輔助手術醫療已逐漸成為病人和醫生的首選。與傳統手術相比較，它有非常顯著的優點，比如手術刀口的創傷面小，手術過程失血少，以及術後病人恢復快等等。而在機器人輔助手術系統中，手術器械相對於病人的身體組織部位的精準定位、跟蹤和導航系統又是其靈魂，因為它是替代醫生在傳統手術中直視創傷面和手術器械的唯一替代。在各類機械、光學和電磁定位、跟蹤和導航技術中，光學定位、跟蹤和導航被認為是其黃金標準。但光學遮擋和信息傳送不穩定成為光學定位、跟蹤和導航系統的最大缺陷。本項目旨在針對光學定位、跟蹤和導航系統的缺陷，提出一種外部多攝頭光學，內部微小型電磁混合式定位、跟蹤和導航系統。這套系統適用於傳統和微創手術，並結合外部多攝像頭冗余以及微創電子冗余機制，實現可靠、穩定的機器人輔助手術系統的定位、跟蹤和導航系統，以助於提高醫療治理水平，更好的服務大眾。

14210117.label: Realisation of objectives
14210117.value: We have accomplished all four objectives of the project. We have developed a novel surgical tracking system capable of compensating for the information loss during the surgery. The detailed achievements are as follows: (1) We designed a new type of optical-magnetic fusion target. Above the target, there are four arranged optical spheres with a pattern. An electromagnetic tracking coil is placed at the lower end of the target. The position and direction relationship between the optical spheres and the electromagnetic coil is fixed and known. (2) We proposed an adaptive fusion algorithm. According to the design of the target and the pose constraint relationship, we defined the local coordinate system of the target. When both the optical and the electromagnetic systems are working normally, the target pose is calculated through the optimization of the two pose constraints. When the optical spheres are occluded, the electromagnetic coil is used to calculate the target pose, and further calculate the optical ball position. Then the pose is compared with the visible spheres to correct the positioning result. When electromagnetic interference occurs, the optical spheres are used to calculate the target's pose. (3) When magnetic interference occurs in the electromagnetic system, the optical spheres are used to calculate the target pose, and then the electromagnetic coil pose is further calculated. The theoretical induction magnetic field information is calculated according to the coil pose. Compared with the actual induction magnetic field signal, we can determine the interference mode. Then the result can determine the interference source and realize decoupling and separation.

14210117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action

14210117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14210117.value: To enhance the accuracy of the surgery, the tracking system has been the indispensable assistive component of robotic surgery. With the help of a tracking system, the surgical robot can find the relative pose relationship amongst medical images, surgical instruments, and lesions, and compensates the drawbacks of the traditional operation which depends heavily on the surgeon's experience and sight. Due to the innate physical constraints of each tracking system, no single tracking method can handle both open surgery and minimally-invasive surgery in different procedures. This project proposed to develop a versatile system that predicts, prevents, and compensates for the information loss problem in the traditional systems with high accuracy and robustness.

14210217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14210217.value: 我們見證着信息爆炸。將龐大信息的存取外判到雲端變得流行。雲也提供額外其他服務，例如版本控制和協作編輯。不幸的是，使用雲端亦帶出安全考量，如近十年的眾多數據外洩事件。一個自然的解決方案是使用加密來保護外包數據的機密性。然而，這不允許如搜索等有用的操作。 可搜索加密（SE）允許對已加密數據進行查詢 。通過由私鑰生成的令牌，令牌所支持的特定查詢無需解密。現有研究已提出一系列在兩個主要模式下 的SE方案。在對稱可搜索加密（SSE）中，數據編寫者和數據所有者必須共享相同的密鑰。雖然這限制了可搜索加密的應用，但SSE方案通常性能非常高，其中一些已達到最佳效果，即搜索複雜度與在匹配結果數量呈線性關係。另一方面，公鑰可搜索加密（PKSE）方案支持多編者，且編者不需要具有數據所有者的私鑰。 PKSE通常由諸如雙線性配對的數論工具構成，比SE慢。更重要的是，因缺少全局索引，PKSE令牌僅用於測試單個密文 。因此，PKSE需要線性的徹底掃描，這是一個眾所周知的，似乎是本質上的弱點。 在這個計劃中，我們研究一個基於實際動機的問題---如何將通用SSE方案升級到其公鑰版本。我們的第一種方法稱為非對稱可搜索加密（ASE），它是一種利用編者註冊的新方法。我們的第二種方法稱為混合可搜索加密（HSE），將線性掃描限制在更小的關鍵字空間。我們的研究將正式定義這些框架及其相應的安全要求。我們還將嚴密分析擬提出的方案的安全性。 提出的方法造成一些新及具挑戰性的問題，在理論和實踐層面都是很重要的。 首先，受到ASE建設的啟發，我們發現了在“基於身份的加密”（IBE）和“忘卻式隨機存取機”（ORAM）的領域中兩個新的未解决的問題。 這兩個概念本身是很有趣的，並不限於雲的應用。 解決這些問題可能會促進我們對各個領域的理解。 第二，為了在HSE中提供搜索的額外靈活性，我們提出了一種需要新的密碼學工具，其顯著特點在於可減少對於任何編者子集創建的密文進行搜索的令牌大小。 此項目的成功不僅完全解鎖可搜索加密技術的潛力，而且推動了應用密碼學領域的發展，為保護雲計算或分佈式系統提供了有用的基礎。

14210217.label: Realisation of objectives
14210217.value: ** Objective 1: Reason for 99% achievement: We have been aiming only top-tier conferences but a result proposing a new notion is highly dependent on the background and taste of reviewers. At the time of writing, we submitted it to Usenix Security 2023. The competition for such a top-tier conference is fierce, but we are confident that this result can end up in a good place since it is an improvement to our Objective 4 (already accepted by Usenix Security 2022). a. We renamed it to delegatable searchable encryption (DSE) to better capture the core enabler, i.e., multiple writers and readers only need to obtain a one-time delegation of the corresponding update or search token for a particular keyword. b. The security requirements have been rigorously defined via a simulation-based definition. While it is typical for searchable symmetric encryption (SSE), there is only a single writer and a single reader in SSE. Corrupted writers in DSE can even compromise the *privacy* of data contributed by honest writers. Moreover, corrupted writers in DSE can also compromise the data integrity, i.e., a reader fails to obtain the search result corresponding to other honest updates. Moreover, DSE features two kinds of leakage profiles depending on whether the server is corrupt. Note that the case for an honest server is not necessarily weaker than that for a corrupt server because it might have a more confined leakage. c. We have also tailor-made a new building block called shiftable multi-recipient encryption. For functionality, it should feature homomorphism. For simulated-based security, it should be non-committing. While the scheme design is relatively simple, the security analysis is highly non-trivial since existing non-committing designs destroy any homomorphic property. ** Objective 2: Reason for 70% achievement: This objective is for the ultimate goal -- multi-writer searchable encryption. We moved our focus from studying theoretical foundations to more practically-relevant research. The original goal of achieving the strongest security level in theory partially contributes to the prior rejection of our result for Objective 1 since the resulting construction is not efficient. We proposed two related IBE notions for Objective 1 and 4 respectively with other IBE-related contributions. In short, we made independent achievements. a. While anonymous identity-based encryption (IBE) is equivalent to public-key searchable encryption, and the initial ideas in the proposal are worth pursuing, we eventually moved our focus. One of the reasons is that while the results for our other objectives do have some "theory" component, especially for Objective 3, we found that a theoretical treatment of the building block might dilute the focus and even hinder the performance of the resulting systems, which is also the ultimate goal of this project: practical multi-writer searchable encryption. Concretely, our initial solution for Objective 1 is based on the intended result here and that of Objective 3: multi-user oblivious RAM (MCORAM). However, even if we used a more efficient but "security-downgraded" MCORAM, the resulting instantiation is not that welcomed by reviewers (also explains why the result for Objective 1 is still under submission). b. We do have some preliminary results for Objective 2, but it takes quite some effort to make it a standalone paper if it has been taken out of the "context" here. Hence it is not written up as a complete draft. c-i. For the public-key searchable encryption sub-component needed by our two main systems. We still made some achievements. For Objective 1, we explicitly formulate non-committing identity-based encryption, where the non-committing properties apply to both the recipient-identity and the message. c-ii. We have also proposed a new notion of identity-based encryption, which we call identity-coupling key-aggregate encryption. This is one of the two essential building blocks for Objective 4, which has been accepted by Usenix Security 2022. d. Meanwhile, our team has many other related results for extended notions of IBE, particularly, certificateless encryption and access control encryption. While these papers were written independently of the searchable encryption motivation and these notions might look orthogonal, there are direct connections. d-i. In [CTRSA19], we argue that structure-preserving IBE (without any extra restriction) is impossible to achieve. The next best thing we have is structure-preserving certificateless encryption (SP-CLE). The SP property is known to be helpful in efficient zero-knowledge proof (ZKP) of the ciphertext. In DSE (Objective 1), we skip that part for integrity since it could be considered outside of the encrypted index, but a strengthened notion would require such a ZKP. SP-CLE still works in DSE since it expects delegation from the data owner anyway (in contrast to IBE, which needs encryption to be just dependent on a short master public key). d-ii. Access control encryption (ACE) is compatible with DSE since both of them are based on access control, and ACE is also outsider-recipient-anonymous. Holistically, we thus consider this objective to be partially achieved. As usual, we will continue to work on that one way or another. ** Objective 3: The result has been published by AsiaCrypt 2020. We have formulated this new notion, proposed new homomorphic-encryption-related techniques, and proposed two constructions in particular. Nevertheless, the single-server one relies on fully-homomorphic encryption (some lower-bound results have been established before our work). The multi-server results do not quite match with the usual application of searchable encryption that assumes a single server. Interestingly, this theoretical work has attracted a "practical" follow-up in NDSS 2022: "Titanium: A Metadata-Hiding File-Sharing System with Malicious Security." ** Objective 4: The result has been accepted by Usenix Security 2022. We have formulated this new notion, proposed two cryptographic building blocks to achieve it, including identity-coupling key-aggregate encryption mentioned above. This is the first multi-writer searchable encryption scheme in the literature that features both forward privacy and a sublinear number of symmetric-key operations for search complexity, a practically-motivated problem but remained unsolved for two decades since the birth of the first searchable encryption.

14210217.label: Major findings and research outcome
14210217.value: Our major findings include those directly contributing to our objectives. i. [UsenixSecurity23 Submission] We proposed delegatable searchable encryption. Compared to our prior result [UsenixSecurity22], it achieves the regular notion of forward privacy via our new notion of shiftable multi-recipient encryption, which is compatible with our hybrid searchable encryption technique [UsenixSecurity22] too. ii. Part 5.3 described the connections of the following three papers with our two notions of multi-writer searchable encryption. [CTRSA19] We proposed the first structure-preserving certificateless encryption. Its original motivation is a new group signature notion with certified limited opening. [SP21, ACNS21] We proposed two access control encryption constructions that feature arbitrary policy, constant-ciphertext, and efficiency. Prior results either require heavy primitives such as indistinguishability obfuscation or randomized functional encryptoin or require exponentially-long ciphertext. iii. [AsiaCrypt20] We proposed multi-client oblivious RAM (MCORAM) with poly-logarithmic communication in both single-server and multi-server models. This solves the open problem of whether MCORAM (with obliviousness maintained when fellow clients are corrupted) can match the upper bound complexity of single-client ORAM (where corruption does not exist). iv. [UsenixSecurity22] We proposed hybrid searchable encryption, the first result since the birth of searchable encryption two decades ago that features sublinear search complexity and forward privacy in the multi-writer setting. The prior solution is either single-writer (symmetric searchable encryption) or has linear search complexity (public-key searchable encryption). v. Our findings also include other searchable encryption notions. The papers were not written under the multi-writer context but served as an improved building block to be upgraded with our two multi-writer techniques. [PETS22]: We proposed a generic upgrade of any (inverted-index) dynamic SSE to support range queries. We also attacked a scheme in ESORICS'18. [DASFAA20] We proposed structured encryption (a generalized notion of searchable encryption) for skyline queries that only uses a "minimal" trusted execution environment such as Intel SGX (with less than 128M of memory). Prior systems are inefficient for their heavier cryptographic techniques. [DBSEC21] We proposed a simple storage-saving structure for volume hiding encrypted multi-map, generalizing keyword SSE in the data structure. Prior schemes require more complicated techniques in design and more storage in practice. vi. Finally, the fund of this project also aids in other cryptography research of our group briefly summarized below. [TDSC21]: We achieved secure deduplication for updatable files encrypted by independent "writers." [WPES18]: We achieved secure matching of two encrypted sets, returning whether their overlapping is larger than a threshold while revealing nothing else.

14210217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14210217.value: 1. [UsenixSecurity22] has already attracted attention before its official conference presentation. The PI has been invited to give a talk at Brown University virtually (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R2AWcpJDa38), and also invited to attend a workshop co-located with Crypto'22 (http://esl.cs.brown.edu/tpes). One way or another, the PI would try to discuss future research with other top-notch researchers. 2. The core of both multi-writer searchable encryption schemes is compatible with the popular inverted index design. There are many potential extensions; some are discussed in [Usenix Security 2022]. We will continue to explore those. 3. Variants of identity-coupling key-aggregate encryption (e.g., with better security but with arguably unavoidable less efficiency) are also proposed. The security notion of anonymous ciphertext stems from the PhD thesis of the PI, and we will revisit it. 4. The objectives of this project belong to the bigger topic of processing encrypted data. During this project, the PI has been invited to give keynote talks [SCC19, FCS18] or submit a (co-authored) position paper [NSS18] on related topics. 5. We also made fundamental contributions to cryptography [PKC19, AsiaCrypt18]. 6. Lastly, the project also aids in training research intern/students who worked on blockchain [ACISP19], cryptocurrency [ICDCS21, CCS19], and payment applications [ACSAC21].

14210217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14210217.value: Outsourcing vast amounts of information to cloud computing services is prevalent. Unfortunately, considering the numerous data breaches of the past decade, using the cloud comes with security concerns. Searchable encryption enables the efficient retrieval of encrypted data. Nevertheless, secure and efficient multi-writer searchable encryption remains hardly unexplored. The core challenge is that different writers should be able to write independently, but they are not trustworthy to be granted the same secret key as in traditional single-user searchable encryption. Furthermore, when the storage server is also untrusted, it is unclear how the writers can collaboratively establish an index of related files in an encrypted form without learning "too much" of other writers' data. This proposal explores two paradigms of achieving these seemingly conflicting requirements: hybrid searchable encryption and delegatable searchable encryption. The former uses time information as a basis to confine searchability and "coordinate" the writers. The latter takes a different approach by requiring the database owner to perform one-time delegation of writing (and reading) access rights for different keywords. Both schemes remain secure against collusion among the server and writers while searching is much faster than the known approach of scanning all encrypted files. These lead to various contributions to cryptography.

14210517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14210517.value: When a laser beam is tightly focused in an aqueous medium, the rapid change in optical intensity across the focal spot may result in a restoring force on any transparent object within a short distance. First reported by Askin in 80’s, the so-called optical trapping phenomenon has been widely used for remote manipulation of live cells in life sciences. The laser power threshold is typically in several tens of mW, which sometimes results in structural damages in the trapped object because of absorption. Recent development in nanoscale confinement of photons by means of surface plasmons has led to the realisation of plasmonic nano-optical tweezers (PNOTs) with power threshold substantially reduced to sub-mW regime. Since the excitation of plasmons still requires a focused laser spot, which has a diameter in microns, one has to rely on the nanoscale intensity modulation associated with localised hot-spots found in the metallic nanostructure. Since the operation of optical tweezers relies primarily on intensity variations within a focused laser beam, the trapping range is always limited to several microns. Clearly this is not ideal, particularly when the target objects are in very low concentration levels. Until now, all reported cases of nano/microscale trapping are based on the use of photons. Other means of trap excitation, such as those due to thermophoresis, electrophoresis and flow-induced pressure, particularly in the nanoscale are yet to be explored and utilised. This project proposes to develop a new type of nano-optical tweezers with the specific aim to achieve very large trapping range. The idea is to first use photon-free tweezers based on thermophoretic effects from local temperature gradient field. Such tweezers can be customised to increase trapping range through a trap-and-transfer process and convective flow directed to a central trapping site. Once the target objects are transferred to a region small enough for optical trapping, plasmonic excitation takes over and the trapped objects will be steered to the final hot-spot. Ultimately, the device has the capability to grab target objects from a long distance and bring them to the final nano-optical trapping site for user’s analysis. Specifically, the project scope covers two components: (i) development of hybrid long-range nano-optical tweezers and their arrays by combining the nanoscale precision from PNOTs and the long-range photon-free trapping capability from microscale electric thermal heaters (METHs); (ii) in-depth investigation of physical forces that contribute to the observed trapping phenomenon excited by temperate gradient. 激光束緊密地聚焦在水性介質中時，焦斑上的光強度的快速變化可能導致在短距離內的任何透明物體上的恢復力。 80年代由Askin首先報導，光學光阱現像已被廣泛應用於遠程操縱生命科學中的活細胞。激光功率閾值通常為幾十mW，這有時導致由於吸收而導致光阱被俘物體的結構損傷。通過表面等離子體激元在納米尺度限制光子中的最新發展已經導致實現等離子體激元納米光鑷（PNOT），功率閾值大大降低到亞水平。由於等離子體激元的激發仍然需要具有微米直徑的聚焦激光光斑，所以必須依賴於與在金屬納米結構中發現的局部熱點相關的納米級強度調製。由於光學鑷子的操作主要依賴於聚焦激光束內的強度變化，光阱範圍總是被限制在幾微米。顯然，這不是理想的，特別是當目標物體濃度非常低時。到目前為止，所有報告的納米/微量光阱都是基於光子的使用。鑷子激發的其他手段，例如由於熱泳，電泳和流動誘發的壓力，特別是在納米尺度，尚待探索和利用。 這項目建議開發一種新型的納米光鑷，其目的是實現非常大的捕集範圍。這個想法是首先使用基於局部溫度梯度場的熱泳效應的無光子鑷子。這種鑷子可以定制，以通過陷阱 - 轉移過程和指向捕集位點的對流來增加捕獲範圍。一旦將目標物體轉移到足夠小的光學捕獲區域，等離激元激發將被接管，被俘物體將被引導到最終的熱點。最終，該設備具有從遠距離抓取目標物體的能力，並將其帶到最終的納米光阱位置進行用戶分析。 具體來說，項目範圍涵蓋兩個部分：（i）通過結合PNOT的納米級精度和微電子熱電加熱器（METHs）的遠距離無光子俘獲能力，開發混合遠程納米光鑷及其陣列， ; （ii）深入研究有助於觀察到溫帶梯度激發的俘獲現象的物理力量。

14210517.label: Realisation of objectives
14210517.value: Through this project we have developed a new all-in-one platform that can perform detection of a target DNA sequence through from a single cell by first trapping the cell into a micro-well, followed lysing of the cell with localised heating using a focused laser beam and finally iso-thermal amplification of the target DNA sequence with modulation and scanning of the laser beam. The micro-heating effect is generated through highly efficient absorption of optical radiation by resonant surface plasmons. We have performed numerical calculation of the temperature profile surrounding the hot-spot where the focused laser beam interacts with gold nano-islands deposited on the bottom of the micro-well arrays. Our results suggest that because of localised heating in the micron scale, cell lysis occurred very rapidly. Also, the total laser power required for producing the expected DNA amplification is as low as 9.2mW. We have also demonstrated a new trap-and-transfer device using electrically excited micro-heater arrays. The best experimental resolution was around 3 microns due to the presence of Brownian motions. The fabrication process, microfluidic designs and new knowledge in surface plasmon resonance absorption of this work have inspired the inception of several new research ideas, namely, ultrahigh sensitivity surface plasmon resonance biosensor based on absorption singularity, digital-mirror-device (DMD) based 2-dimensional surface plasmon resonance biosensors arrays, fibre-based biosensor using plasmon scattering effects in gold nano-island coated cladding, surface plasmon-assisted zinc oxide nano-tetrapod gas sensor and droplet-based centrifugal microfluidics. Overall, we have achieved all objectives of this project and the results have led to the publication of 8 journal publications.This project has also funded the training of one PhD graduate. Two new research projects (Innovation & Technology Fund, and General Research Fund) have used the results generated from the project for their supporting data.
