14210517.label: Major findings and research outcome
14210517.value: 1) Experimental demonstration of a novel resonant surface plasmon absorption induced micro-heating strategy for trapping of biological samples. By sequentially adjusting the power level and spatial location of the excitation laser beam, one can further use this platform for conducting trapping and lysing of a target single cell, as well as detection of a DNA sequence through an iso-thermal nucleic acid amplification process. (Journal Publication#1) 2) Detail analysis of the possible physics behind the trapping phenomenon suggests that a thermophoresis is operation. The micro-heater induced 3-dimensional temperature field results in an asymmetric diffusive flow of ionic molecules, which in turn leads to mechanical forces that pull the target object to the higher temperature region, hence the final trapping effect. We have successfully demonstrated a photon-free trapping device based on purely electrical heating, and subsequently used this effect for performing “trap-and-transfer” cell manipulation. (Journal Publication#2) 3) This project has inspired the demonstration of an ultrahigh sensitivity surface plasmon resonance biosensor based on absorption singularity. (Journal Publication#3) 4) Experience collected through this project has been used in the demonstration of a digital-mirror-device (DMD) based 2-dimensional surface plasmon resonance biosensor array. (Journal Publication#4) 5) Some project results have been used as supporting data for a recently funded project that aims to the develop a fibre-based biosensor using plasmon scattering effects in gold nano-island coated cladding. (Innovation & Technology Fund project). 6) The light-induced local heating phenomenon has led to the demonstration of a surface plasmon-assisted zinc oxide nano-tetrapod gas sensor. (Journal Publication#6) 7) The fabrication strategy developed through this project has contributed to the demonstration of droplet-based centrifugal microfluidics.(Journal Publication#7) 8) Resources provided through this project has enabled the publication of three review publications on the topic of surface plasmon resonance imaging sensors, microfluidic whispering gallery mode optical sensors and thermodynamic perspectives on liquid–liquid droplet reactors for biochemical applications. ((Journal Publications#5, #8 and #9)

14210517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14210517.value: As noted from the publications generated through this project, localised heating associated with either surface plasmon absorption or electrically excited micro-heater offers a versatile alternative for producing trapping effects. In particular the electrically excited approach has the potential for achieving 2-dimensional trap-and-transfer, with which target objects, e.g. single cells, can be manipulated on a surface through sequential switching the elements in 2-dimensional grid of micro-heaters. The fabrication process of such devices is completed compatible with conventional thin film lithographic processes. The results of this project has provided the foundation for the development of purely electrically excited trapping and manipulation of small objects such as bacteria, microbes and other cellular species. We are currently exploring the possibility of integrating such micro-heaters in microfluidic devices for performing accurate manipulation of biological samples.

14210617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14210617.value: Single photon imaging sensors (photomultiplier tubes, single photon avalanche diods) permit low intensity/fast acquisition of binary images. The sensor values obtained (either 0 or 1) follow a Bernoulli distribution whose parameter (the probability of getting 1) is in direct relation to the intensity of light hitting the sensor. Hence, imaging amounts to reconstructing this probability from the binary sensor values. Quite a number of medical imaging modalities could benefit from such a low intensity imaging, in particular nuclear imaging modalities (scintigraphy, SPECT and PET), but also low-dose Computed Tomography. We propose to perform this reconstruction by expressing the restoration algorithm as a linear combination of elementary (non-linear) processings (LET---``Linear Expansion of Thresholds''), and by minimizing an estimate of the mean-square error (MSE) between the restoration result and the original (unknown) image. One of the key issues that we plan to solve in this project is to identify a statistical estimate of this MSE. We also plan to address the problem of identifying a good LET-basis for processing binary images, in particular for an accurate representation of edges. Finally, since the relation between the pixel value probabilities and the image may be modelized by a linear transform, we also plan to propose a full restoration scheme, encompassing the inversion of this linear transformation. 單光子成像傳感器（比如光電倍增管，單光子雪崩二極管）能夠獲取低亮度或者快速採集的二值圖像。傳感器數值（0或1）服從伯努利分佈，其參數（得到1的概率）與擊中傳感器的光的強度直接相關。因此，單光子成像相當於從二值傳感器數值中重建出這個概率。有相當多的醫學影像能夠受益於這種低強度成像，尤其是核成像模式（比如閃爍掃描，單光子發射計算機化斷層顯像（SPECT）和正電子發射斷層顯像（PET）），還有低劑量的計算機斷層掃描成像(CT)。 我們提出通過將恢復算法表示為一系列基本（非線性）處理過程（LET, 閾值的線性擴張）的線性組合，同時最小化恢復結果和原始未知圖像之間均方誤差（MSE）的一個估計來進行重建。此項目中，其中一個我們打算解決的關鍵問題是確定這個均方誤差的統計性估計；此外，我們也計劃解決確定一個適合處理二值圖像的基本過程（LET-basis）的問題，尤其是對於圖像邊緣的準確表達；最後，由於像素值概率和圖像之間的關係可以通過線性變換來建模，我們還計劃提出一個包含該線性變換的逆變換的完整的恢復方案。

14210617.label: Realisation of objectives
14210617.value: Objective 1 As indicated in the midterm report, we have been able to find the theoretical expression of an unbiased risk estimate for binary probability laws. In order to perform efficiently this calculation for images of reasonable size, we realized that it was necessary to find an approximation of this expression. We investigated variants of this unbiased risk estimate based on, e.g., Total-Variation minimization (conference paper #2) and General Cross-Validation (conference paper #1). Unfortunately, it appeared that the approximation formula that we had developed was not close enough to the actual value of the binary risk estimate, which implied that the denoising process obtained by optimizing this estimate was not sufficiently close to the ideal process. For this reason, we had to continue using the Poisson Unbiased Risk Estimate (PURE, for denoising and deconvolution) and the blur-PURE version (for blind deconvolution) developed in the journal paper #1 in an application to fluorescence microscopy. Objectives 2 and 3 We had already started to address these two objectives in the midterm report, using essentially earlier approaches to build LET (Linear Expansion of Thresholds) for denoising and deconvolution (see Journal #1 and conference paper #3). Developing further an intuition that was sketched in the conference paper #4, we have identified (journal paper #2) the optimal linear representation that allows to denoise arbitrary image patterns, independently of their orientation. We coined this representation "Fourier-Argand" due to the rotation covariance inherited from the use of complex numbers (Argand) and the expansion in powers of the complex exponential of the rotation angle (Fourier). This linear expansion of non-linear operations was demonstrated to be extremely robust with regards to noise, in particular the severe inaccuracies that arise from binary noise. It is also maximally flexible: outlining of edges is achieved by expanding the step function in the Fourier-Argand representation (which is calculated exactly in journal paper #2), outlining of arbitrary patterns is achieved by using the Radon transform, a DFT and the inverse of the Radon transform. We believe that journal paper #2 has a large potential for impact, and we are sharing our Matlab code on our website (see demo page at http://www.ee.cuhk.edu.hk/~tblu/FourierArgand/). Objective 4 We have successfully implemented an L1 regularization (i.e., Total Variation in that case, since our goal was to retrieve sharp transitions in images) for which the regularization parameter is selected based on an unbiased risk estimate (conference papers #2 and #5). We were able to demonstrate the superior performance of this selection by comparing with the standard choice.

14210617.label: Major findings and research outcome
14210617.value: The findings of this projects have been twofold: First finding: we were able to successfully demonstrate the existence of an unbiased risk estimate for binary noise (Bernoulli distribution), that can be used like the previous unbiased risk estimators (e.g., SURE and PURE) in image restoration problems. Second finding, and this is the most significant outcome of this project, is the (orientation-friendly) Fourier-Argand representation of patterns which opens the path to image restoration based on patterns to recognize, independently of orientation. This could be particularly useful for cryo-Electron Microscopy (cryo-EM) image reconstruction, for which individual pixels show an extremely low count of electrons (distribution can be modelized accurately as binomial or, in the limit, Bernoulli). The link between this representation and the Radon transform indicates that it could be a natural representation for images that are acquired through tomographic projection; e.g., slices in a Computed Tomography (CT) X-ray scanner, in tomographic Transmission Electron Microscopy.

14210617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14210617.value: The Fourier-Argand representation appears to be an adequate approach to analyse the images obtained in Cryo-EM where large instances of same protein/virus are captured in different, unknown orientations: the ability of the representation to factor out the "orientation" part of the object imaged allows to reformulate the image reconstruction problem algebraically as a matrix factorisation problem. For this, however, it will be necessary to devise a 3-dimensional update of this representation, involving spherical harmonic functions. The very impressive ability of the Fourier-Argand representation of edges to extract edges out of extremely noisy images (e.g., for a Peak Signal to Noise Ratio as low as -10 dB) is an indication that the basic bricks of the representation are suitable for building a basis of thresholds for image restoration. A new PhD student is currently working on these aspects. To investigate further the effects of binary noise on the reconstruction of patterns, we have recently purchased a single-photon counting camera which can also provide the time delay between the arrival of two photons, and will provide us with real binary images.

14210617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14210617.value: Microscopes that are designed to images biomolecules (RNA, DNA, proteins) and viruses are based on counting electrons one by one (e.g., Cryogenic Electron Microscopy, whose inventors were awarded the 2017 Nobel prize in chemistry), the randomness of which results in a very noisy image. This project is about the optimal prediction of the pixelwise probabilities that underly these counts to restore biologically meaningful images. To this end, a statistical estimate of the goodness-of-fit of any restoration process is identified and, even more significantly, optimal orientation-independent feature representations based on a linear expansion on a "Fourier-Argand" basis are developed. The Fourier-Argand representation is particularly well-structured for tomographic reconstruction problems (e.g., X-ray CT) and will continue to be investigated in these contexts.

14210717.label: Project Objectives
14210717.value: Framework Design for Performance and Reliability Management of Mobile-Cloud Computing This task aims to design a framework for performance and reliability management of mobile-cloud computing. Despite the wide prevalence of the mobile-cloud computing paradigm, there is a lack of tools capable of providing end-to-end performance and reliability management. We aim to provide app providers with a general framework that involves techniques and tools from the mobile side to the cloud side. To handle the high complexity and the large scale of mobile-cloud computing, we will also investigate the novel use of data-driven approaches to address these unique challenges where traditional techniques are inapplicable. Mobile-Side Performance and Reliability Management This task aims to investigate techniques to manage mobile-side performance and reliability problems. Firstly, we will explore data mining techniques to automatically identify app issues from the large number of user reviews, which directly convey users’ feedback on mobile apps. Secondly, we will profile runtime data of mobile apps, which are important to monitor app execution, and perform postmortem analysis when failures happen. Finally, based on the profiled data during continuous testing, we will develop techniques to analyze such data and detect potential performance bugs. Cloud-Side Performance and Reliability Management This task aims to investigate techniques to manage cloud-side performance and reliability problems. To be specific, we will first investigate bug localization via automatically mapping bug reports to source code. Then, we will study how to diagnose system failures via automated log analysis in the cloud. Finally, we will dig into performance issues and mine system metrics data to detect performance anomalies.

14210717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14210717.value: Aim: To develop an end to end framework for detecting performance and reliability issues in mobile-cloud computing. Background: Mobile applications (apps) have become widely pervasive in daily life. Many of these apps are built in the mobile-cloud computing paradigm, where providers employ cloud computing to deliver their online applications to mobile users. This can benefit app providers with quick development, easy operation, and low maintenance costs. In this way, many startup companies and individual developers can afford to develop and provision their own apps. Reliability and performance, which directly affect user experience, are important to the successful delivery of mobile apps. Any app crash or performance issue can lead to user dissatisfaction and lower user ratings, and finally result in revenue loss. Timely detection of performance and reliability issues is essential to facilitate immediate remediation. However, unlike traditional software systems, there exists a set of new challenges in mobile-cloud computing. Firstly, the types of mobile devices and operating system (OS) versions vary widely; therefore it is difficult to cover all environment settings during lab testing. Secondly, the use of cloud platforms, coupled with the interaction with a large number of mobile devices, leads to rapid growth of the complexity and scale of the whole system. Both of these factors magnify the difficulty in managing app performance and reliability. Consequently, app providers need an end-to-end framework to help detect performance and reliability issues, which is currently lacking. Project Description: First we will design a framework for mobile-cloud computing, building on our previous research outcomes and employing our collaboration with industrial partners. We will then develop procedures and tools for performance and reliability management on both mobile side and cloud side. After testing our approaches on Microsoft and Huawei's platforms and datasets, we will finally pull all the work together into an open-source toolkit which we will publish, along with a set of datasets to enable other researchers to reproduce our results and conduct further research in this field. Significance of Project: This project will provide app developers with a framework and toolkit that will enable them to maintain better reliability and high performance of their apps, thus benefiting both the app developers and their customers. It will also put into the public domain not only the results of our research, but real datasets which will enable further research in this field. Both these outputs will be of major benefit to the development of mobile-cloud computing. 手機上的應用程序在我們日常生活中被廣泛的使用。很多這樣的應用程序是基於移動雲計算的模式構建。在這種模式下，應用程序提供商使用雲計算來向移動端的用戶提供在線應用程序。這可以使應用程序提供商享有快速開發、簡化操作、低維護成本的便利。這樣，許多創業公司和個人開發商都有能力開發和提供自己的應用程序。可靠性和性能可以直接影響用戶體驗，所以它們對於移動應用程序的成功運轉至關重要。任何應用程序崩潰或性能問題都可能導致用戶不滿意，並降低用戶打分，最終導致收入損失。及時檢測性能和可靠性問題對於即時修復至關重要。然而，與傳統的軟件系統不同，移動雲計算中存在一系列新的挑戰。首先，移動設備和操作系統的版本類型差異很大。因此，在實驗室測試期間難以測試所有的環境設置。其次，雲平臺的使用加上與大量移動設備的交互，導致整個系統的複雜性和規模快速增長。這兩個因素加大了管理移動應用程序性能和可靠性的難度。因此，應用程序供應商需要一個目前缺乏的端到端的框架來幫助檢測性能和可靠性問題。該項目將基於我們現有的研究成果設計一個移動雲計算框架，並利用我們與工業界合作夥伴的合作。然後，我們將在移動端和雲端開發性能和可靠性管理的程序和工具。在微軟和華為的平臺及數據集上測試了我們在的方法後，我們最終會將所有工作匯總到一個我們將要發佈的開源工具包中。我們還將發佈一組數據集，使其他研究人員能夠重現我們的結果並進一步研究這個領域。項目將為應用程序開發人員提供一個框架和工具包，使其能夠更好的保持應用程序的可靠性和高性能，從而使應用程序開發人員及其客戶受益。我們不僅將把研究結果投入公共領域，而且還將發佈能推動這個研究領域的真實數據集。這兩項產出都對移動雲計算的發展有很大的好處。

14210717.label: Realisation of objectives
14210717.value: All the objectives stated in this project have been either completely achieved or exceedingly achieved. We designed a general framework for performance and reliability management of mobile-cloud computing, which involves techniques and tools from the mobile side to the cloud side. To handle the high complexity and the large scale of mobile-cloud computing, we investigated the novel use of data-driven approaches to address these unique challenges where traditional techniques are inapplicable. For the mobile side, we proposed several algorithms to automatically identify app issues from a large number of user reviews. We also developed techniques to analyze the runtime data of mobile apps and detect potential performance bugs. For the cloud side, we investigated bug localization by linking bug reports to source code. Moreover, we performed performance anomaly detection and system failure diagnosis by leveraging different system monitoring data such as logs and metrics. Overall, to achieve the project objectives, a number of machine learning and data mining algorithms have been designed and deployed into real-world mobile-cloud computing systems. Some algorithms and datasets have been published to facilitate future studies in the field.

14210717.label: Major findings and research outcome
14210717.value: In total, seven journal papers and 43 conference papers are published, covering the project’s objectives in various aspects. These publications all acknowledge the support of this grant. We describe the resulting outcomes as follows. (We use [C1] label to refer to conference publication [1], and [J1] label to refer to journal publication [1], etc.) The first objective aims to design a framework for performance and reliability management of mobile-cloud computing. The framework should involve techniques and tools from the mobile side to the cloud side. To this end, we started from understanding users’ experience on the mobile side from the perspective of advertisements' performance costs [J7]. Then, on the cloud side, we conducted a comprehensive study of the reliability issues of cloud systems [C43]. We summarized important challenges towards achieving efficient cloud reliability management and proposed a complete framework to boost the effectiveness of service incident management. Researchers and practitioners can gain a deep understanding about cloud reliability management and design more dedicated algorithms. The second objective investigates techniques to manage mobile-side performance and reliability problems. We tried to understand the semantic meaning of user app reviews by proposing a series of text comprehension algorithms [C6, C14, C15]. We extracted key insights from app reviews [C2] and identified emerging app issues [C4]. We also explored the feasibility of generating app review response automatically [J6, C18]. This is important for the efficiency of mobile-side reliability management. Moreover, we proposed a visualization-oriented learning algorithm to detect text-layout bugs in mobile apps [C42], which are an important and common type of bugs in mobile apps. The third objective focuses on cloud-side performance and reliability problems. To enable the mapping between bug reports and app source code, we proposed a code retrieval model based on semantic dependency learning [J5]. Log analysis is important for the reliability of mobile-cloud computing as logs are often the only available data recording a system’s runtime details during failures. Thus, we conducted a series of studies covering different stages of log analysis. For example, we developed and released a toolset for automated log parsing [C10], which serves as the very first step of many downstream log mining tasks. To identify impactful service system problems, we combined logs and KPIs (Key Performance Indicators) to detect service performance violations [C1]. Moreover, we studied log compression problem, which is an important means to deal with the extreme large volume of log data produced by today’s mobile-cloud computing paradigms. Besides performance issue detection, we also tried to improve the performance by designing a more cost-effective cloud service function scheduler [C24], which is achieved by leveraging the dependencies of service functions. The fourth objective focuses on realization and dataset publication. We implemented the aforementioned techniques and conducted comprehensive experiments. We also maintain a public repository on GitHub, i.e., LogPAI (https://github.com/logpai), to share the source code and data relating to log analysis to promote related research.

14210717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14210717.value: We have successfully achieved all objectives stated in our project, where a comprehensive framework for performance and reliability management of mobile-cloud computing has been established and well-evaluated. For future research, we can design and implement an easy-to-use toolkit that contains the algorithms facilitating the performance and reliability management of mobile-cloud systems. Besides mobile-cloud computing, we can extend the developed framework in a systematic and comprehensive way such that it can be applicable to more general cloud computing systems. For example, we can collect heterogeneous monitoring data generated by cloud systems, e.g., system metrics, logs, system topologies, alerts, incidents. These data characterize the health states of online service systems from different perspectives, based on which operations engineers can monitor their performance and reliability. This topic is called Artificial Intelligence for IT Operations (AIOps) and many academic and industrial efforts have been devoted to it. We have initiated a project called IT Operations Powered by AI (OpsPAI, https://github.com/OpsPAI) and started to develop techniques under the topics of anomaly detection, root cause analysis, incident management, causal machine learning (ML) for AIOps, auto-remediation, ML platforms for AIOps, etc.

14210717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14210717.value: We investigated the performance and reliability management of mobile-cloud computing for both mobile side and cloud side via modeling and exploiting platform-generated big data. We performed various tasks such as emerging app issue identification, text-layout bug detection in mobile apps, log-based anomaly detection, cost-effective service function scheduling, etc. Various machine learning and data mining techniques are proposed and employed, such as clustering, correlation mining, topic modeling, deep neural network models, etc. Design and implementation for the proposed techniques were provided, and empirical experimentation was extensively conducted. The research outcomes can bring new insights and practical application for systematic reliability engineering of modern mobile-cloud computing systems.

14210917.label: Project Objectives
14210917.value: To develop processing methods for preparation of 2D/3D OLHP structures with well controlled 2D layer coverage and thickness. To identify (i) suitable 2D and 3D OLHP combinations and (ii) optimal 2D layer thickness to render the 2D/3D OLHP structures highly stable and efficient in charge generation and extraction. To understand (i) how moisture resistance and thermal photostability vary with the different organic cations in the 2D layer, and (ii) how charge transport occurs through the 2D/3D interface. To develop new hole transport layers (HTLs) based on metal oxide-based hybrid inorganic materials or metal oxide/carbon nanocomposites. The new HTLs will have much improved stability and charge extraction properties as compared to the current ones used in PSCs. Through a systematic material and device characterization, to establish a comprehensive model to describe the key factors that lead to performance and stability improvement through material and interface engineering.

14210917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14210917.value: The objective of the proposed research is to develop highly efficient perovskite solar cells with long-term stability through material and interface engineering. Specifically, we will bond an ultrathin two-dimensional (2D) organolead halide perovskite (OLHP) layer on top of a three-dimensional (3D) OLHP light absorbing layer to improve the air stability and thermal photostability of the 3D OLHP. The stability of the entire solar cell structure will be further enhanced by the use of new hole transport layers based on hybrid inorganic materials and metal oxide/carbon nanocomposites. Clean energy, especially solar energy, is crucial for solving energy and environmental crises. Among various photovoltaic materials, OLHPs are particularly promising because of their low fabrication costs and rapidly improving power conversion efficiency (PCE), currently greater than 22%. However, current 3D OLHPs have poor moisture resistance and thermal photostability, in particular for the organolead mixed bromide-iodide perovskites that are widely researched for tandem cell applications. Equally, the commonly used doped organic hole transport layer (HTL) materials have also been shown to degrade under heat and light stress. Such stability issues largely limit the practical applications, as long-term stability is always desired by the end users. We propose to address the instability problem of perovskite solar cells through new material design and interface engineering. First, we will develop new thin film structures by bonding an unltrathin 2D OLHP layer with 3D OLHP. Within this design, the high photovoltaic efficiency is assured by the 3D OLHP while the high moisture resistance is enabled by the 2D OLHP. More importantly, the 2D OLHP is bonded to the 3D OLHP via ion coordination and hydrogen bonding, thus enabling the 2D layer to passivate the non-stoichiometric defect sites on the 3D OLHP surface. (Note that the defects are a main source for light-induced thermal decomposition.) Second, instead of employing the commonly used doped organic HTLs or single-layer inorganic HTLs in the perovskite solar cells, we will develop new HTLs based on hybrid inorganic materials or metal oxide/carbon nanocomposites to ensure high charge extraction efficiency and good stability. The proposed research will generate valuable material design principles that can be used in varies perovskite solar cells to enable high efficiency and good stability. The bonded 2D/3D OLHP structure and the hybrid HTLs may also find applications in other devices such as light emitting diodes. 清潔能源，特別是太陽能，被視為解決能源及環境問題的重要手段。在諸多種光伏材料當中，有機鉛鹵化物鈣鈦礦備受關注，源於其低成本製造工藝和快速提高的能量轉換效率，目前為止最高能量轉換效率已超過22%。但是，現在的三維鈣鈦礦材料受限於其較差的耐濕性和光熱穩定性，特別是碘溴混合鈣鈦礦。同時，現時常用的有機空穴傳輸層在光熱的作用下很容易退化。以上的穩定性問題都會限制鈣鈦礦的實際應用。因此，本專案旨在通過材料及介面工程研究來實現高效並長期穩定的鈣鈦礦太陽能電池。一方面，我們通過設計新型的鈣鈦礦材料及介面優化來解決鈣鈦礦本身的不穩定性問題。通過在三維鈣鈦礦材料上面覆蓋一層很薄的二維鈣鈦礦的方法，來提高其耐濕性。更重要的是，二維鈣鈦礦還可以與三維的通過離子配位和氫鍵作用連在一起，使其可以鈍化三維鈣鈦礦表面的缺陷，從而提高鈣鈦礦材料本身的光熱穩定性。另一方面，我們不使用常規的有機空穴傳輸層，而是引進無機材料，例如金屬氧化物和碳材料的複合材料來改善空穴的提取效率以及整體的穩定性。該項目的研究將提出適用於各種鈣鈦礦材料的有價值的材料設計原理，以實現高效率長期穩定的鈣鈦礦太陽能電池。同時，二維三維連接的鈣鈦礦結構已經混合的空穴傳輸層可適用於其他應用，如發光二極體。

14210917.label: Realisation of objectives
14210917.value: We have achieved the project objectives and developed several material and interface approaches to realize high efficiency and stable perovskite solar cells: Firstly, we developed a two-step sequential deposition method to enable simultaneous incorporation of alkali cations (e.g., Cs+ and Rb+) and large organic cations (such as benzylammonium (BA+)) into formamidinium (FA+)-based perovskite thin films and subsequent formation of 2D/3D organic-inorganic hybrid perovskite (OIHP) structures. It is found that the formation of the 2D surface layer is promoted by the presence of alkali cations, which also alters the surface crystal facet the 3D perovskite, allowing for suppression of surface facets associated with deep traps. Through composition optimization, the solar cells based on the perovskite system demonstrate a high power conversion efficiency (PCE) of up to 22.5%. More importantly, the perovskite films demonstrated superior resistance to humidity and photo-thermal stress, and the perovskite-based devices (without encapsulation) retained over 95% of the initial efficiency after exposure to air (humidity level: 60–65%) for 2 months. Secondly, we have developed a highly reproducible approach for incorporating guanidinium (GA+) in the FA-based perovskites for further enhancing the stability of the 3D perovskite lattice. The key factor to this approach is the simultaneous incorporation of small amounts of Cs+ and Br−, which synergistically enhance the incorporation of GA+ into the perovskite lattice. Once GA+ cation is successfully incorporated, it binds the surrounding halides more tightly than FA+ does, and therefore improves the structural stability and increases the formation energy of halide vacancies. Accordingly, the GA-modified perovskite films show a significant increase in carrier lifetime and the thermal-photostability. Thirdly, we extended our study to wide-bandgap perovskites (WBHPs), which are critical for tandem solar cell applications. Specifically, we focused on the use of precursor additives and introduced Pb(SCN)2 to assist perovskite crystallization and FAX (X = I and Br) for grain boundary healing. Our results suggest the synergistic effects of the precursor additive in enhancing film crystallinity and grain size, reducing impurity and passivating grain boundaries. As a result, we demonstrated a series of high performance solar cells based on WBHPs. The average open-circuit voltage (Voc) of the solar cells increases monotonically with the increasing bandgap, from (1.223 ± 0.014) V for bandgap of 1.72 eV to (1.254 ± 0.019) V, (1.272 ± 0.019) V, and (1.286 ± 0.017) V for 1.79 eV, 1.86 eV, and 1.93 eV, respectively. The loss-in-potential of these cells is lowest among the reported values for the same bandgap range. Fourthly, we also explored new hole-transport layers (HTLs) and developed a sol-gel method to fabricate NiLiOx-based HTLs. The electronic properties of the HTLs can be tuned by not only the Li doping concentration but also the annealing temperature and UV ozone treatment, which concertedly modulate the doping concentration of the HTL as well as inducing surface dipole to facilitate hole extraction. It is found that the perovskite solar cells (PSCs) with the NiLiOx HTL exhibit greatly improved photo-thermal stability compared to the PSCs using common organic HTLs, with the former exhibiting a T70 (retention of 70% of the initial PCE) of more than 180 hours at 85°C in humid air while the latter showing a lifetime of 17 hours under the same condition. Through all these studies, we have established a comprehensive understanding of the relations between the material bulk and interface properties and the device performances and stability.

14210917.label: Major findings and research outcome
14210917.value: Firstly, we developed a sequential deposition method for incorporating alkali cations (e.g., Cs+) and benzylammonium (BA+) cations into formamidinium lead iodide-based perovskite (FAPbI3) thin films for highly efficient and stable PSCs. By combining experimental characterization and theoretical calculations, we demonstrate the concerted effects of alkali and BA+ cations in improving the crystallinity, orientational growth and surface stabilization. We showed that the method can be used to create a BAPbI4-dominant 2D surface layer on the 3D perovskite lattice as well as promoting the preferred orientation of defect-free (1 0 0) facets. The optimized PSCs demonstrate a high PCE of up to 22.5% as well as superior resistance to humidity and photo-thermal stress, retaining 95% of the initial efficiency after exposure to humid air for 2 months without encapsulation. (Publication #1). Secondly, we theoretically and experimentally investigated the viability of substituting FA+ cations in FAPbI3 by guanidinium (GA+) cations, while stabilizing the structure by a controlled amount of Cs+ and Br− substituting FA+ and I− ions respectively, without negatively affecting the optical properties of the original compound. Through this study, we demonstrated PSCs with a stabilized power output (SPO)/Voc of 20.5%/1.229 V, which are among the highest values reported in MA-free perovskites at the time of the study. (Publication #2). Thirdly, we demonstrated a composition tuning approach to address the commonly seen photo-instability and large Voc loss issues in wide bandgap (WB) PSCs. Using mixed halide perovskites, with a varied bandgap from 1.72 to 1.93 eV, as the model system we have illustrated how precursor additive Pb(SCN)2 should be matched with a proper ratio of FAX (I and Br) to realize large grains with defect-healed grain boundaries. The optimized WB PSCs show good photostability at both room-temperature and elevated temperature. The champion Voc/SPO reaches 1.244 V/18.60%, 1.284 V/16.51%, 1.296 V/15.01%, and 1.312 V/14.35% at the bandgap of 1.79 eV, 1.86 eV, and 1.93 eV, respectively. The loss-in-potential of these cells is lowest among the reported values for the same bandgap range. (Publication #3). Extending from these studies, we have further explored the use of the material strategies in perovskite light-emitting diodes (Publication #4), analyzed the potential application of PSCs in self-powered flexible devices (Publication #5) and conducted a review on integrated quantum dot/photonic structures for various optoelectronic device applications (Publication #6).

14210917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14210917.value: The findings in composition tuning and structure engineering can be extended to other perovskite devices such as perovskite light-emitting diodes and perovskite photodetectors. We have already initiated a few projects along this direction. Considering the rapid development of the perovskite PV industry, we will be also be actively seeking for opportunities to transfer our technologies to the industry.

14210917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14210917.value: Photovoltaic technologies play a critical role in achieving renewable electricity and zero-carbon emission. This project was devoted to the research of perovskite solar cells (PSCs), a photovoltaic technology that combines the advantages of low fabrication cost, high power conversion efficiency, and fast energy-payback time. In particular, we conducted a series of studies to explore how the stability of PSCs could be improved via composition tuning and structure engineering of the bulk and surface of the perovskite absorber and how these material modifications fundamentally influence the electronic properties of the perovskites and PSCs. Several device fabrication protocols have been developed and demonstrated both high efficiency and substantially improved stability as compared to previous reports. The new material designs and fundamental understandings provided by this project may enable a step forward for commercializing PSCs and thus impact the solar energy and other semiconductor industries.

14300117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14300117.value: This project aims to advance the notion of structural quantum criticality via thermodynamic, transport and spectroscopic measurements of high quality single crystals. The concept of a structural quantum phase transition in correlated electron systems has recently gained attention. In the cases where the phase transition remains continuous at the zero temperature limit, a structural quantum critical point can be realized. In this project, we will adopt a dual-track approach. On one hand, we will perform microscopic studies to investigate the role of phonons, electrons and the interaction between the two in the context of structural quantum criticality for systems with a well-established phase diagram. Systems such as the Remeika phase (Ca,Sr)3Rh4Sn13 and (Ca,Sr)3Ir4Sn13 fall into this category. On the other hand, we plan to develop new single crystals of other material systems that feature a thermally driven continuous structural phase transition. Hydrostatic pressure or chemical substitution will be employed to tune the structural transition temperature of the newly available crystals to exploit the structural degree of freedom. We believe the joint Hong Kong-Kyoto team is in an advantageous position to carry out this project owing to our extensive experience in this class of materials, our well-established capability to investigate correlated electron under multiple extreme conditions, and our track record in the growth of high quality single crystals. The results obtained from this project will enable a deeper understanding of structural quantum phase transitions and quantum criticality, allowing a well-informed comparison with the case of magnetic quantum criticality that is widely discussed in correlated electron and superconductivity research. 本研究計劃的目標是透過對高品質單晶進行熱力學、傳輸性及能譜測定，來深化對結構量子臨界的了解。最近，在關聯電子系統中，結構量子相變的概念引來不少注目。其中在零度極限條件下仍保持連續性的相變裡，我們可以觀察到結構量子臨界點。在本計劃裡，我們會使用雙軌策略。一方面，我們會進行微觀研究，以了解在已知相圖系統中，聲子、電子及兩者之間的相互作用在結構量子相變所擔任的角色。系統如Remeika相(Ca,Sr)3Rh4Sn13與(Ca,Sr)3Ir4Sn13就是屬於這一類系統。另一方面，我們計劃開發其他材料的新單晶，而這些材料都具備熱驅動的連續性結構相變。靜水壓力和化學置換會被用來改變新單晶的結構相變溫度，以研究結構自由度。我們相信香港-京都聯合團隊在實行本計劃上處於有利位置，因為我們擁有研究相關材料的豐富經驗，在多重極端狀態下研究關聯電子系統的能力，以及製造高品質單晶的良好紀錄。本研究導出的結果可以加深我們對結構量子相變和量子臨界的了解，從而令我們可以與在關聯電子系統及超導體研究中已被廣泛討論的磁性量子臨界進行更具體詳細的比較。

14300217.label: Realisation of objectives
14300217.value: 1. We synthesized a series of linear N-heteroarenes as well as linear arenes containing four-membered rings, and characterized them using different techniques including single-crystal X-ray crystallography. 2. We designed a hoop-shaped N-heteroarene, which is a structurally defined fragment of N-doped carbon nanotubes, and synthesized its synthetic precursor, a tetraepoxy nanobox consisting of tetraazapentacene and pyrene subunits. This nanobox was identified with single-crystal X-ray crystallography and formation of the hoop-shaped N-heteroarene was observed with mass spectroscopy. 3. We studied the electronic structures, supramolecular assemblies and stability of the linear N-heteroarenes as well as linear arenes containing four-membered rings in relation to their applications as organic semiconductors. 4. We fabricated and characterized field effect transistors of the linear N-heteroarenes as well as linear arenes containing four-membered rings, and investigated relationship between molecular/supramolecular structures and device performance. In particular, a tetrachloro derivative of tetraazapentacene in solution-processed OFETs exhibited electron mobility of 14.9 ± 4.9 cm2/Vs with a maximum value of 27.8 cm2/Vs, which set a new record for n-channel OFETs. 5. We briefly studied a phenazine-pyrene tetraepoxy nanobelt to form complexes with transition metal ions.

14300217.label: Major findings and research outcome
14300217.value: We studied two linear polycyclic N-heteroaromatic frameworks, namely, cyclobuta[1,2-b:3,4-b']diphenazine (CBDP) and indolo[3,2-b]carbazole, by synthesizing new derivatives of them and investigating their interesting electronic structures, in particular, aromaticity and antiaromaticiy. New n-type organic semiconductors were developed on the basis of these molecules and relationship between their molecular packing and semiconductor properties were studied. These results were reported in Publications 1 and 5 (Part C) We developed high-performance n-type organic semiconductors on the basis of chlorinated tetraazapentacenes, which were originally planned as precursors for synthesis of the proposed N-Heteroarenes containing four-membered rings. It is found that substitution of tetraazapentacene with different numbers of fluorine and chlorine substituents enables fine-tuning of the frontier molecular orbitals, molecular vibrations, and π–π stacking for n-type organic semiconductors. In collaboration with Prof. Ai-Min Ren (Jilin University), we also conducted computational studies on the relationships between molecular structure, crystal structure and charge transport. The tetrachloro derivative (4Cl-TAP) in solution-processed thin-film transistors exhibited electron mobility of 14.9 ± 4.9 cm2/Vs with a maximum value of 27.8 cm2/Vs, which set a new record for n-channel organic field-effect transistors (OFETs). This work was reported in Publication 2 (Part C). We further studied interface engineering of the OFETs of 4Cl-TAP with a self-assembled monolayer of 12-o-carboranyldodecylphosphonic acid on alumina. It was found that the assembled dipoles of o-carborane at the semiconductor–dielectric interface enabled ambipolar charge transport in the solution-processed thin films of 4Cl-TAP. This result was recently reported in Publication 6 (Part C). We expanded the scope of this project to p-type organic semiconductors on the basis of linear arenes containing four-membered rings. We synthesized new derivatives of bisnaphtho-[2′,3′:3,4]cyclobut[1,2-b:1′,2′-i]anthracene (BNCBA), and studied the relationship between their molecular packing in crystals and semiconductor properties. All of these BNCBA derivatives functioned as p-type semiconductors in solution-processed OFETs, and the tetrahexyl derivative exhibited a field effect mobility as high as 2.9 cm2/Vs. This work was reported in Publication 3 (Part C). We designed a hoop-shaped N-heteroarene, which is a structurally defined fragment of N-doped carbon nanotubes, and attempted to synthesize it. As its synthetic precursor, a tetraepoxy nanobox consisting of tetraazapentacene and pyrene subunits was successfully synthesized and identified with single-crystal X-ray crystallography. Formation of the hoop-shaped N-heteroarene was observed with mass spectroscopy. This work was reported in Publication 4 (Part C), which was highlighted by Synfacts, 2020, 16, 279.

14300217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14300217.value: The tetrachloro-tetraazapentacene developed through this project is one of the best n-type organic semiconductor so far for organic field effect transistors. We plan to further explore its application in organic electronic devices in collaboration with other researchers and use it to address important questions in organic semiconductor physics. In this project, we investigated extension of N-heteroacenes through a four-membered ring. On the basis of this concept, we plan to further explore extension of N-heteroacenes through an eight-membered ring for new organic semiconductors with enhanced charge transport and solubility.

14300217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14300217.value: With the financial support from this General Research Fund, we explored synthesis and applications of new linear and hoop-shaped polycyclic N-heteroaromatic frameworks. On the basis of linear N-heteroarenes, we developed a series of organic semiconductors, fabricated organic electronic devices, and studied structure-property relationship for organic semiconductor materials. In particular, the tetrachloro tetraazapentacene derivative in solution-processed thin-film transistors exhibited record-high electron mobility for n-channel organic field-effect transistors. This project has led to six peer-reviewed publications on top journals of chemistry and materials science. The results of this project were also presented at three international and national conferences. Moreover, two PhD students received training from this project

14300317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14300317.value: Accretion-Induced Collapse (AIC) is the collapse of a white dwarf (WD), which reaches its Chandrasekhar limit by accreting mass from its companion red giant star in a single-degenerate system, or another WD in a double-degenerate system. Depending on the accretion rate and its mass, a WD can explode as a Type-Ia supernova (SNIa) or undergo AIC. In particular, if the central density of a WD is high enough for electron capture before the onset of SNIa explosion, the resulting loss of the supporting electron degeneracy pressure triggers the AIC of the WD to a proto-neutron star together with a collapse-driven supernova. Despite a huge amount of gravitational energy released during the collapse, most energy is lost by neutrino emission rather than electromagnetic signals, and so AIC forms sub-luminous and peculiar objects, much dimmer than SNIa. So far, no direct observation of AIC has been made. We propose to model the hydrodynamics of AIC and calculate its gravitational-wave and neutrino emissions. We will study the effects of nuclear matter equation of state (EOS), possible quark-gluon deconfinement phase transition and dark matter admixture on AIC. By predicting the electromagnetic, gravitaitonal wave and neutrino signals, our results will help to search for AIC and constrain models of dark matter and/or nuclear matter EOS.

14300317.label: Realisation of objectives
14300317.value: Objective 1. Modify an existing Newtonian hydrodynamics code to model AIC: (100% achieved) We modified our hydrodynamics code, which was originally designed to model SNe Ia. First, for the initial model, we set up a white dwarf (WD) with or without admixed DM in hydrostatic equilibrium. We assume the WD to have a uniform temperature at 0.01 or 0.1 MeV. We also tried using a more realistic temperature profile. For a rotating WD, we followed [Hachisu86] to generate the rotating WDs self-consistently. Second, due to the compactness of the final protoneutron star (PNS), the previous implementation of Newtonian Gravity will be less accurate. Therefore, we use an approximation proposed in [Marek06], the Case A formula based on the Tolman–Oppenheimer–Volkoff (TOV) extension of the hydrostatic equilibrium equation. Third, to include the electron capture process which is essential for triggering the collapse, we applied the parameterized electron capture scheme first proposed in [Liebendoerfer05]. These have all been implemented in the hydrodynamics code. Objective 2. Calculate the neutrino signals from AIC: (100% achieved) We have implemented the isotropic diffusion source approximation (IDSA) proposed in [Liebendoerfer09] to follow the neutrino transport in AICs. We have calculated the neutrino signals for non-rotating AIC, which are similar to those from Core-Collapse Supernovae (CCSNe). For rotating AICs, we find some correlation between neutrino signals and gravitational-wave signals. We have published a paper in The Astrophysical Journal based on these results [Zha19]. Objective 3. Calculate the gravitational wave signals from AIC: (100% achieved) We carried out axisymmetric hydrodynamical simulations of AIC of dark matter (DM) admixed rotating WDs and their burst gravitational wave (GW) signals. For initial WD models with the same central density, the admixed DM is found to delay the plunge and bounce phases of AIC, and decrease the central density and mass of the proto-neutron star (PNS) produced. The bounce time, central density, and PNS mass, generally depend on two parameters, the admixed DM mass M_DM, and the ratio between rotational kinetic and gravitational energies of the inner core at bounce βic,b. The emitted GWs have generic waveform shapes and the variation of their amplitudes h+ show a degeneracy on βic,b and M_DM. We found that the ratios between the GW amplitude peaks around bounce allow breaking the degeneracy and extraction of both βic,b and M_DM. Even within the uncertainties of the nuclear matter equation of state, a DM core ≥ 0.03 M⊙ can be inferred. We also discuss possible DM effects on the GW signals emitted by PNS g-mode oscillations. GW may boost the possibility for the detection of AIC, as well as open a new window in the indirect detection of DM. These results have been published in the Astrophysical Journal [Zha19]. Objective 4. Study effects of nuclear matter equation of state on AIC: (100% achieved) To understand the effect of nuclear matter EOS on the bounce dynamics, we use three EOS’s, the SFHo EOS [Steiner13], HShen EOS [HShen], and LS220 EOS [LS220]. We choose these EOS’s because they are used extensively in the literature. We show that the production of lowered NS mass from DM admixed WD is a robust result with respect to the nuclear matter EOS. This result has been published in the Astrophysical Journal [Leung19]. Objective 5. Study effects of dark matter accretion on AIC: (100% achieved) For non-rotating initial WD models with the same central density, we study the effects of a static, compact dark matter (DM) admixed core on the collapse and bounce dynamics and properties of the PNS, with DM mass ~ 0.01 M⊙. We show that increasing the admixed DM mass generally leads to slower collapse and smaller PNS mass. Our results, therefore, imply that the accretion-induced collapse of dark matter admixed white dwarfs can produce low-mass NS, comparable to that of the low-mass pulsar J0453+1559. This result has been published in the Astrophysical Journal [Leung19]. For rotating models, the bounce time, central density, and PNS mass, generally depend on two parameters, the admixed DM mass M_DM, and the ratio between rotational kinetic and gravitational energies of the inner core at bounce βic,b. The emitted GWs have generic waveform shapes and the variation of their amplitudes h+ show a degeneracy on βic,b and MDM. We found that the ratios between the GW amplitude peaks around bounce allow breaking the degeneracy and extraction of both βic,b and MDM. Even within the uncertainties of the nuclear matter equation of state, a DM core ≥ 0:03 M⊙ can be inferred. We also discuss possible DM effects on the GW signals emitted by PNS g-mode oscillations. GW may boost the possibility for the detection of AIC, as well as open a new window in the indirect detection of DM. These results have been published in the Astrophysical Journal [Zha19]. Objective 6. Study effects of a quark-gluon phase transition on AIC: (100% achieved) We study the consequences of a quark-gluon phase transition (PT) in a nonrotating core-collapse supernova with axisymmetric hydrodynamic simulations. We find that the PT leads to the collapse of the proto compact star (PCS) and results in a loud burst of GWs. The amplitude of this GW burst is ∼30 times larger than the postbounce GW signal normally found for nonrotating CCSN. It shows a broad peak at high frequencies (∼2500–4000 Hz) in the spectrum, has a duration of 5 ms, and carries ∼3 orders of magnitude more energy than the other episodes. Also, the peak frequency of the PCS oscillation increases dramatically after the PT-induced collapse. In addition to a second neutrino burst, the GW signal, if detected by the ground-based GW detectors, is decisive evidence of the first-order QCD PT inside CCSNe and provides key information about the structure and dynamics of the PCS. The result has been published in Physical Review Letters [Zha20]. 14300317.label: Major findings and research outcome
14300317.value: The quantum chromodynamics (QCD) phase transition in core-collapse supernovae has been examined for the first time, using state-of-the-art multi-dimensional supernova simulations and unique imprints of such a phase transition on the emitted gravitational-wave and neutrino signals have been detected. The findings have been reported in a paper selected as Editors’ Suggestion in the Physical Review Letters, a top physics journal. Future detection of such a gravitational-wave signal, coincident with a burst of neutrinos, will provide strong evidence for the transformation of supernova core matter into quarks and gluons. Such detection will greatly promote scientists’ understanding of supernovae. We performed hydrodynamical simulations of accretion-induced collapse (AIC) of dark matter (DM) admixed rotating and non-rotating white dwarfs (WD) and their burst gravitational wave (GW) signals. Using spherically symmetric hydrodynamics simulations, we follow the collapse of a massive WD core triggered by electron capture, until the formation of a proto-neutron star (PNS). We show that increasing the admixed DM mass generally leads to a slower collapse and smaller PNS mass, down to about 1.0 ⊙. Our results suggest that the accretion-induced collapse of DM admixed WDs can produce low-mass neutron stars (NSs), such as the observed low-mass pulsar J0453+1559, which cannot be obtained by conventional NS formation path by core-collapse supernovae. For rotating models, we found that even within the uncertainties of the nuclear matter equation of state, a DM core can be inferred if its mass is greater than 0.03⊙. GWs may boost the possibility for the detection of AIC, as well as open a new window into the indirect detection of DM.

14300317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14300317.value: 1. Our promising results studying the gravitational-wave signals of the quark-gluon phase transition in core-collapse supernovae can be extended to other equations of state to test for potential sensitivity to the details of the quark-gluon phase transition. 2. Our study of the effects of dark matter accretion on AIC should be extended to consider dynamic dark matter and dependence on dark matter particle mass. In particular, simulation of AICof DM-admixed rotating white dwarfs with an extended dark matter component should be carried out with their gravitational-wave signals predicted. It will also be interesting to investigate the remnant compact stars produced.

14300317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14300317.value: We performed hydrodynamic simulations of the collapse of a stellar core at its death and calculate its gravitational wave and neutrino emissions. Through such calculations, we predicted signatures for a possible quark-gluon deconfinement phase transition and dark matter admixture in such an event. By predicting the electromagnetic, gravitational wave, and neutrino signals, our results help to search for accretion-induced collapses of white dwarfs, quark-gluon phase transition in stellar core collapses. Our results also open a new window into the indirect detection of astrophysical dark matter.

14300617.label: Project Objectives
14300617.value: Receiver Deniability for Broadcast Channels: For our first task, we propose to fully characterize the capacity region for general broadcast channels. Prior work has been able to only give an achievability for degraded broadcast channels. Sub-linear throughput: Noting that non-zero rates of transmitter deniability are impossible for channels such as Binary Symmetric Channels and Gaussian channels, we pose a natural question: is a sub-linear throughput still possible? (in a similar vein as covert communication, where a throughput of O(sqrt{n}) is possible over n channel uses. Bi-deniable communication: As the next step, we propose to extend the study of deniable communication to the setting of bi-deniability. In addition to the reliability requirement as earlier, both Alice and Bob are summoned by Judy to produce the message without coordinating with each other (unlike the previous setting where only one party is summoned in any given round). Interactive Protocols: In the Information Theoretic Secrecy setting, it is well known that interaction between Alice and Bob can increase the capacity. In our setting, however, interaction can be both a boon as well as drawback. On one hand, interactive protocols allow Alice and Bob to potentially transmit at a higher rate if full secrecy is desired. On the other hand, if the feedback channel from Bob to Alice is noisier than the channel from Bob to Judy, Alice's ability to produce a message that is consistent with the forward transmissions as well as feedback transmissions is compromised. We propose to start with simple models to understand the effect of interaction on deniable communication. Covert protocols: In scenarios where even the presence of {em any} communication is suspicious, the strongest guarantee on deniable communication corresponds to simultaneously demanding covertness and plausible deniability. As our next task, we aim to characterize the capacity for various problem settings when covertness and deniability are simultaneously demanded. Efficient code constructions: We propose to come up with efficient code constructions for our problem in various settings. In addition to demanding efficient encoding and decoding, a key challenge here is to also come up with an efficient faking procedure. Computationally bounded eavesdroppers: While in our discussion so far, we have focused our attention on purely information theoretic notions of deniability, there are several models that lie in between information theoretic and cryptographic formulations of deniability. One interesting model that we propose to examine is a public key setting where communication takes place over a broadcast channel where the eavesdropper may have a better channel than Bob, but is computationally bounded.

14300617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14300617.value: In this project, we propose examine the notion of plausible deniability from an information theoretic viewpoint. Simply stated, plausible deniability refers to the property that someone in possession of a confidential message may respond with an innocuous looking message if forced to divulge it by a forceful party. In the proposal, we consider several communication problems where plausible deniability is desirable. The general framework for our study is a broadcast channel with an intended receiver and an eavesdropper. The transmitter and the receiver wish to communicate the reliably over this channel while ensuring that if one of them is summoned by the eavesdropper, then they have the ability to produce a fake message or codeword that appears plausible given the eavesdropper’s side information. Inspired by the notion of deniable encryption in cryptography, preliminary work on this problem has already been performed by the PI in a 2016 paper. We note that there are many open question that are still to be answered. In particular, we argue that the ability to confuse the eavesdropper, the ability to be covert about the transmission, and the ability to collude in a distributed manner are key ingredients in a general framework for deniable communication. We aim to examine the information theoretic capacity of several variations on this setting and also address several computational angles to these problems — namely code constructions and capacity computation when either the legitimate parties or the eavesdropper are computationally bounded. We also note rather intriguing connections to covert communications — specifically, it appears that codes for covert communications are good starting points for coming up with codes for deniable communication in some cases. 在此項目中，我們將從信息論 的層面探究“合理否認性 (plausible deniability)”這一概念。簡單地說，“合理否認性”指的是如果某人擁有機密的消息 (message) 而且被強迫提供給一個強力機構，那麼他/她能夠用一個看起來無害的消息來混淆該強力機構。在該研究計劃中，我們將會研究幾個需要用到“合理否認性”這個性質的通信問題。本項研究的通用框架是一個廣播信道 (broadcast channel)，其中包含一個接收者 和一個竊聽者。發送者 和接收者希望利用這個信道進行可靠的 通信，同時保證如果其中一方被竊聽者傳喚，被傳喚的一方有能力製造一個假的、但是對於擁有邊信息 (side information) 的竊聽者來說看起來是合理的消息或碼字 (codeword)。 本項目負責人受到密碼學中“可否認加密 (deniable encryption)”的啟發，於2016年的一篇論文中對信息論領域中的“合理否認性”這一概念進行了初步的研究。與此同時，我們注意到目前此方面的研究工作依然存在著許多尚未解決的問題。特別地，我們論證“使竊聽者混淆的能力”、“使通信隱蔽的能力”、以及“發送者和接收者進行分佈式共謀的能力”是在該通用框架中進行“可合理否認的通信”的關鍵要素。 我們的目標是從信息論的角度分析該框架下幾個不同模型的容量 (capacity)，此外我們也會從計算複雜度的角度對該問題進行探討 — 在發送者接收者或竊聽者有計算能力限制的情況下如何構建碼 (codes) 以及計算容量。此外，“合理否認性”與“隱蔽通信 (covert communication)”之間的聯繫同樣引人注目 — 確切的說，隱蔽通信中所用到的碼可以很大程度上啟發我們如何為“可合理否認的通信”設計和構建一套行之有效的碼。

14300617.label: Realisation of objectives
14300617.value: Over the course of this project significant progress was made on understanding the fundamentals of various aspects of deniability. Specifically, the PI and his collaborators were able to construct covert and deniable communication schemes that worked despite jamming by an active adversary, design schemes that could operate over a large class of channels with differential eavesdropping ability by the adversary, obtain fundamental limits of such types of communication, and design computationally efficient schemes that met information-theoretic bounds.

14300617.label: Major findings and research outcome
14300617.value: As noted above, in the course of this project, the PI and his collaborators were able to derive fundamental bounds on the limits of covert/stealthy/deniable communication (and combinations thereof) in a variety of settings. For instance, in the paper "Covert Communication over Adversarially Jammed Channels", we were able to design schemes that were robust to jamming by an active adversary, while being simultaneously covert. In "Covert Communication With Polynomial Computational Complexity" and "Undetectable Radios: Covert Communication under Spectral Mask Constraints" we were able to design computationally efficient schemes in a variety of communication settings (over DMCs, and over wireless communication systems). In "Stealthy Communication Over Adversarially Jammed Multipath Networks " we derived stealthy (deniable) communication schemes, and also derived fundamental limits of such schemes.

14300617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14300617.value: The results obtained above in simple point-to-point settings set the stage for examining covert/deniable communication in a variety of adversarila network communication settings. For instance, Co-PI Mayank Bakshi is currently examining multiple-access Byzantine communication schemes, including settings in which adversary localization can be instantiated. Extending our results to general network settings containing some legitimate communicating parties, and some adversaries, is of interest. The techniques developed in the course of this project show promise in terms of extending analysis in these directions.

14300617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14300617.value: The desire to communicate is innate in humanity, but it can come at a cost, if such communication is observed by a party that has the power to harm the communicating authorities. In such scenarios, where even the fact of communication can be dangerous, one must carefully design communication schemes that are either covert (sound like random noise to an eavesdropper), or deniable (can reasonably be explained away in terms of "innocent" communication). In this project we used mathematics to explore the fundamental limits of when such communication is possible, and also designed communication schemes in a variety of scenarios (such as wireless and/or wired communication).

14300717.label: Project Objectives
14300717.value: BSDVIs and non-local PVIs: to extend the unique existence result of the solutions from backward stochastic dynamics (BSD) to backward stochastic dynamical variational inequalities (BSDVIs), we shall conquer this by adopting Yosida approximation as in Pardoux and Rascanu (1998). Though the connection between BSDs, under the Brownian setting, with a particular class of non-local PDEs was first indicated in Liang, Lyons and Qian (2011), the complete analytic derivation was not apparent there, and we shall first supplement with a thorough analysis with a new proof; to this end, some novelty is required in rewriting the assumptions for the BSDs with more analytic favour, so that an appropriate interpretation for the general mapping of square integrable martingales in the BSD can be expressed in terms of a non-local term in the PDE. We then extend this result to the variational case which links the solutions of BSDVIs with the weak solution of a certain type of non-linear and non-local parabolic variational inequalities, which are hardly treated by any common analytic methods. Well-posedness of a broad class of non-Lipschitz BSDEs of non-quadratic growth: apart from one or two recent major works, optimal intertemporal pension/mutual fund management problem remains untouched mainly because of the unusual nature of the respective non-prevalent and non-linear parabolic partial differential equations governing the primal and dual values functions making the determination, via the traditional PDE approach, of their classical nature extremely inconvenient. Instead, we adopt a probabilistic approach to resolve this general problem by derving a non-trivial class of non-Lipschitz BSDEs yet not of quadratic growth. Though the standard iterative approach is not applicable due to imbalance of moments over the course of derivation of apriori estimates, we aim to develop a novel approach which involves a tricky use of Malliavin Calculus. In particular, we note that the solution pairs of the original BSDEs have their own Malliavin derivatives which in turn satisfy another more regular BSDE, based on which a new and better behaved iteration solution scheme can be constructed for their Malliavin derivatives. Our expected result also serves a definite example that uniform continuity of the drift function is not necessary for unique solution in contrast with the claim in Jia (2008). Further numerical approximations will be investigated via a combined method of cubature and Fourier-cosine techniques. H-FBSDEs, abstract stochastic control and Master equations: we plan to extend our recent precise discovery of linking the abstract ``deterministic'' control theory with the solvability of first order Mean Field Master equations to that between the abstract stochastic control and second order Mean Field Master equations. To realize this, we aim to generalise the general existence theory from the Euclidean setting to Hilbert space-valued FBSDEs under the nondegenerate case. A hybrid of probabilistic and PDE methods will be developed to extend the usual maximum principle in PDE theory as found in Ladyzhenskaja et al. (1988) from the Euclidean framework to a certain one, but with more probabilistic favour, over the infinite dimensional Hilbert space, with which the smooth pasting of consecutive local solutions could become definite so as to form the unique ultimate global solution.

14300717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14300717.value: 自Bismut（1973）以後, 作為數學研究領域最重要的學科之一, 後向隨機微分方程（BSDEs）和前向隨機微分方程（FBSDEs）的理論得到了廣泛​​研究及應用。到目前為止, 大部份研究都集中在標準條件及布朗系統下的擴展. 然而，這個數學分支仍然有著其活力，並存在許多艱深的問題。 現項目旨在解決BSDE和FBSDEs中的一些長久未解問題。首先，我們將BSD的解決方案擴展到BSD變分不等式（BSDVI）。然後，我們將通過我們提出的概率方法將BSDVI的解與一些非局部和非線性拋物線變分不等式的弱解相連結; 這些不等式幾乎不能被任何通用的分析方法所處理。其次，優化跨期養老金或共同基金管理問題是當今金融中最具挑戰性的問題之一。經過一些初步的嘗試，可通過引入一種利用Malliavin微積分的新穎方法以解決一類相關但非普遍的BSDEs, 他們既不有Lipschitz性質也沒有二次增長性. 最後，我們最近發現抽象的“確定性”控制理論與一階平均場主方程的可解性之間的微妙聯繫，我們計劃擴展此理論到相對的希爾伯特空間中的抽象隨機控制理論與二階平均場主方程之間的可能連結. 我們的整體研究目標將通過以下研究課題來實現：隨機分析，偏微分方程，Malliavin微積分和平均場理論。 我們預期的結果應該是（1）提供BSDE和FBSDE理論中一些長期難解問題的完整解決方案及在基金管理和平均理論中的應用; （2）豐富了平均場理論統一性的技術; （3）為一些非規範的BSDE解決方案建立一個系統的技術並開發有效的數值近似方案.

14300817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14300817.value: 這個項目的目標是研究三角範疇（更準確地說是3-Calabi-Yau和Fukaya範疇）上的Bridgeland穩定條件。研究的動機來源於： 1.物理弦論中對Dirichlet物體的研究，特別是Douglas的Pi穩定的研究。 2. Bridgeland-Smith的聯系了代數幾何與動力系統的研究。 3. Kontsevich的同調鏡像的研究。 4. Fomin-Zelevinsky的簇代數理論。 我們計劃調查以下內容： 1. 曲面上的3-Calabi-Yau範疇的穩定空間與其上二次微分的模空間的關系。 2. 導出Fukaya範疇和拓撲Fukaya範疇的關系。 3. 簇理論中帶勢箭圖的辮子群的推廣及表示。

14300917.label: Project Objectives
14300917.value: The first goal is to study multi-dimensional transonic shock patterns in general variable nozzles. In particular, we will continue our investigations on the solvability of the Courant-Friedrichs transonic shock problem in a general de Laval nozzle which aims to find a transonic shock wave which turns a supersonic flow into a subsonic one with a given suitable large pressure at the exit of the nozzle. Despite the recent substantial progress (especially for the two-dimensional case), almost all the previous well-posedness results depend crucially on the fact that the transonic waves are small perturbations of a given background solution whose uniqueness and properties can be characterized easily, which thus requires special geometry of the nozzle. For general nozzles, this remains open. We will focus on the case that the nozzle is a small but generic perturbation of a finite flat nozzle in which the background transonic shock wave can be arbitrarily located. Thus all the previous ideas fail here. We will look for a new approach to determine the location of the transonic shock for the perturbed problem in terms of the geometry of the nozzle and the exit pressure. The next objective is to study the well-posedness of the finite subsonic jet problem for steady compressible flows through a finite duct with variable sections. The 2-dimensional problem can be stated as: Given a finite nozzle with variable solid walls, incoming flow angle at the inlet, mass flux m, and ambient pressure $P_e$, can one find a compact continuous curve connecting the two exit point of the nozzle wall through which the pressure of the subsonic flow coming from the nozzle reaches the given ambient pressure $P_e$. In contrast to the previous studies on subsonic jet flows where the jets are all free streamlines which go to infinity, here for the finite subsonic jet problem, the jets may not be purely streamlines so that the well-known variational approach due to Alt-Caffarelli-Friedman cannot be applied here and new ideas and techniques are required to deal this class of free boundaries. We will first concentrate on the 2-dimensional irrotiational steady subsonic flows with simple nozzles. Another main objective is to continue our study on the well-posedness and structure of continuous steady transonic flows in a variable duct. Due to the strong degeneracy and possible singularities near a sonic state for the steady compressible Euler system, the well-posedness of smooth transonic flows may not be possible in general as shown by the structural instability of Taylor type smooth transonic flows in a de Laval nozzle by Morawetz and the singular subsonic-sonic solutions in a straight converging nozzle by Wang-Xin. However, recently, the PI and his collaborator have established rigorously the well-posedness of local smooth Meyer type irrotational steady transonic flows for a class of 2-dimensional suitably flat de Laval nozzles. Furthermore, the supersonic smooth extension of this local transonic flow in the expansion part of the nozzle has been established also. Yet, how to extend the local Meyer type transonic flow in the convergent part by a subsonic solution remains open. The main difficulties lie in that there is no a background solution for this quasilinear equation which is strong degenerate at the sonic state. We will focus on this problem. Furthermore, we will plan also to study similar problems for high space dimensions and flows with non-zero vorticity. In particular, we will study the global well-posedness of steady sonic-supersonic smooth flows in 3-dimensional expansive nozzles.
