14300917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14300917.value: The steady compressible Euler system is one of the most important nonlinear partial differential equations which are mixed-type, have strong nonlinearity, and may change types with degeneracies. Many important wave phenomena in fluid dynamics are governed by the Euler system and its variants. The analysis of this system in the multi-dimensional setting is of great importance not only in mathematical theory but also in applications such as aero-dynamics. However, due to the great complexities, strong nonlinearities and degeneracies, and possible changes of types, the studies on this system give rise to many challenging open problems in the area of nonlinear partial differential equations. The other difficulties include discontinuities such as shock wave and vortex sheets, free boundaries such as jets and sonic curves, and complicated nonlinear boundary conditions. Such features appear in the studies of some interesting steady flow patterns associated with flows through ducts with variable sections which have important applications in aero-dynamics. In this project, we plan to study rigorously some basic wave patterns for steady compressible flows in general ducts with variable sections, to investigate the existence, uniqueness (or non-uniqueness), stability, and the qualitative structure of solutions for such problems, and to develop methods and techniques to study nonlinear boundary or free boundary problems for general mixed-type partial differential equations which may change types and have degeneracies. The focus of the project will be: the well-posedness of transonic shock waves in a finite nozzle with given receiver pressure; well-posedness and behavior of finite subsonic jets flows from a nozzle; and global existence of smooth subsonic-sonic flows, Meyer type transonic flows, and sonic-supersonic flows in multi-dimensional variable nozzles. These studies may lead to resolution of some well-known open problems in the area.

14300917.label: Realisation of objectives
14300917.value: With the main support of RGC grant 14300917, the PI has achieved the objectives of this project: The first goal in the multi-dimensional transonic shock patterns has been achieved fully. Indeed, we have established the theory of the existence of transonic shock solutions to the 2-dimensional steady Euler system in an almost flat nozzle which is a generic perturbation of a flat one under physical boundary conditions proposed by Courant-Friedrichs. This is achieved by finding a sufficient condition in terms of the geometry of the nozzle and the given exit pressure which ensure the well-posedness theory of an elaborately designed linear free boundary value problem. Then the nonlinear free boundary is solved by an iteration scheme based on the linearized solution. In particular, we have shown that if the nozzle is either strictly expanding or contracting, then there exists a transonic shock solution with one transonic shock front, while for a general nozzle with both expanding and contracting portions, the transonic shock problem has more than one solution with a given exit pressure, which yields the instability of the unperturbed normal shock solution under general perturbations of the nozzle geometry and show how this instability may behave. These results have been reported in [9] which has been published at CPAM. For the higher dimensional transonic shock problem, we have shown the structural stability of the transonic shock problem for 3-dimensional axisymmetric nozzles. The major difficulties are the swirl and corner singularities due to the interactions of the shock with the boundaries. We have overcome these difficulties by introducing a new invertible modified Lagrangian transformation, which could be useful for other similar problems. These results have been published in SIMA [6]. Furthermore we have found some new and interesting wave patterns containing transonic shocks due to the angular velocity for the steady inviscid compressible flows with cylindrical symmetry. Indeed, besides the well-known supersonic-subsonic shocks as appeared in divergent nozzles without angular velocity, there exist also supersonic-supersonic shocks with downstream flows containing smooth transonic flows and supersonic-sonic shock solution where shock and sonic state conicoid, which are completely new and interesting and published in [18]. Next, we have achieved the goal in studying the well-posedness of the finite subsonic jet problems for steady compressible flows and related problems. First, we have solved the finite subsonic jet problem completely, and shown that for any two-dimensional finitely long convergent nozzle with straight solid wall and given surrounding pressure and incoming mass flux, there exists an optimal interval on the length of the nozzle such that there exists a unique subsonic flow with the giving incoming flux satisfying the properties that the flow velocity is normal at the inlet, and the pressure of the flow at the downstream free boundary is the given surrounding pressure. The optimal regularities and structures of the flow can be obtained. These have been published in [5]. Furthermore, we have found recently the relationship between finite jet and the infinite jet, which cannot be obtained by the variational approach used previously by others. We also established the existence, uniqueness, and stability of subsonic flows past an airfoil with a vortex line at the trailing edge. The vortex line attached at the trailing edge is a contact discontinuity for the steady compressible Euler equations and is treated as a free boundary. The main difficulties for the analysis of such an important wave pattern in the Prandtl’s lifting line theory are due to the fitting of the vortex line with the airfoil at the trailing edge and the possible subtle instability of the vortex line at the far fields. We have overcome these difficulties by finding suitable weights and barrier functions. These results have been published in [19]. The third objective on studies of continuous steady transonic flows has been also fully achieved. First, we have established a satisfactory theory for the global well-posedness of smooth transonic flows of Meyer type whose sonic points are all exceptional in a class of 2-dimensional nozzles. The necessity of the flatness of the nozzle at the throat of the nozzle for such transonic flows has been proved. Although the local existence and the supersonic extension problems have been established by the PI and his collaborator earlier, yet how to obtain the global subsonic extension of the Meyer type transonic flow has been difficult open problem. We have reduced this into studying general well-posedness and locations of sonic points for general subsonic-sonic flows in a general 2-dimensional nozzle, and solved this problem completely by showing that there exists a critical value depending only on the length and the geometry of the nozzle such that the flow is sonic on the whole throat if the height of the nozzle is not greater than this critical value and the sonic points must lie on the wall if otherwise. Furthermore, we proved that critical height is positive if and only if the nozzle is suitably flat near the throat. In particular, this theory implies a necessary and sufficient condition on the subsonic extension of Meyer-type transonic flows whose sonic points are all exceptional in de Laval nozzles. This is a first result in this direction and has been published in [13]. Next, the PI has achieved some deep understanding on continuous transonic flows with non-zero angular velocity and vorticity by studying the structural stability of smooth cylindrical symmetric spiral flows under both cylindrical and axisymmetric perturbations. We established the structural stability in both the class of cylindrical and axisymmetric smooth spiral transonic solutions with non-zero angular velocity and vorticity by overcoming the difficulties that sonic points of the flow are non-exceptional and non-characteristically degenerate. The key elements of our analysis are to use the deformation-curl decomposition for the steady Euler equations developed by the PI and Weng earlier and to find appropriate multipliers for the second order mixed type equations which are crucial to identify suitable boundary conditions and to yield the stability estimates. These results have been published in [17].

14300917.label: Major findings and research outcome
14300917.value: By achieving the major objectives of the project, the PI and his collaborators have made the following significant progress on the analysis of some important wave patterns for the multi-dimensional steady compressible Euler equations: (1) On transonic flows with shocks: We have established the theory of the existence of transonic shock solutions to the 2-dimensional steady Euler equations in an almost flat nozzle (which is a generic perturbation of a flat one) under physical boundary conditions proposed by Courant-Friedrichs by developing a new scheme based on a linear free boundary value problem and found some new phenomena on the instability effects of the geometry of the nozzle. We have also proved the structural stability of the transonic-shock in 3-dimensional axisymmetric nozzles by introducing a new invertible modified Lagrangian transformations which enables us to overcome the major difficulties due to swirl and corner singularities from the interactions of the shock with the wall of the nozzle. Furthermore, we have also found some new interesting steady transonic flow patterns containing shocks for spiral flows without physical boundaries, such as transonic flows with supersonic shocks and supersonic-sonic shock flows. These results have been published in top research journals, see [9, 6, 18]. (2) On subsonic jets and vortex lines: We have formulated and solved the finite subsonic jets from a 2-dimensional convergent nozzle with straight walls for given incoming flux and surrounding pressure. Furthermore, regularity and dependence on the length of the finite nozzle and incoming flux have been obtained which lay foundation to study the infinite subject jet problem and the degenerate case of subsonic-sonic jet problems which are free boundary problems for degenerate nonlinear elliptic equations. We have also proved the first result on subsonic flows past a thin airfoil with a vortex lie at the trailing edge. This yield the first structure stability result on the steady contact discontinuity. These results have been published at [5, 19]. (3) On continuous transonic flows: We have developed a complete theory for the global well-posedness of smooth irrotational isentropic transonic flows of Meyer type whose sonic points are all exceptional for a class of 2-dimensional finite nozzles, in particular, we have found a necessary and sufficient condition for the subsonic extension of any local Meyer type transonic flows. Furthermore, we have also established the structural stability of a class of smooth cylindrical symmetric spiral flows under both cylindrical and axisymmetric perturbations. The methods developed by us for this can be used to overcome the difficulties due to that the sonic curve may contain non-exceptional points and may be degenerate in other problems. These results have been published in [13, 17]. (4) Other related results: Besides the main results described above, the PI has also obtained significant results on vacuum dynamics for viscous and heat conductive compressible fluids, interface motions for magnetohydrodynamics, and asymptotic stability of elementary waves under periodic perturbations. These results have been published in [12, 3, 16, 1, 2, 8, 11, 15, 14, 4, 7].

14300917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14300917.value: The theories and methods developed in this project may lead to many significant open problems in the studies of the important multi-dimensional compressible Euler equations, such as the Courant-Friedrich’s transonic shock problem for 3-dimensional de Laval nozzles, the infinite long subsonic-sonic jet problems; the mathematical analysis of the Prandtl’s lifting line theory and structural stability of 3-dimensional contact discontinuities; and general existence of Meyer-type transonic flow with non-exceptional sonic points and non-zero vorticities, etc. The ideas and techniques developed in this project may share light on such problems. These may also lead to some deeper understanding of the general theory for mixed-type nonlinear partial differential equations.

14300917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14300917.value: In this project, we have studied rigorously some basic wave patterns for the steady multi-dimensional compressible flows either in general ducts with variable sections, or around an airfoil, or without physical boundaries, established the existence, uniqueness (and/or non-uniqueness), structural stability, and qualitative structure of solutions to such problems; and developed some new methods and techniques to study these well-known difficult nonlinear boundary or free boundary problems. In particular, 2-dimensional theory for both smooth transonic flows and transonic flows with socks has been achieved, and important understanding on subsonic jet flows and subsonic flows around an airfoil with a vortex line at the trailing edge has been obtained. These studies have resolved some long standing difficult problems and will share light on studies of general nonlinear mixed-type partial differential equations.

14301017.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14301017.value: 分形集合之生成迭代函數係統與仿射嵌入

14301017.label: Project Objectives
14301017.value: It is proposed to study the structure of the collection of generating IFSs of self-similar sets and self-affine sets. A key part of this investigation is to study the self-embeddings of these fractal sets under similarity or affine maps. Furthermore, it is proposed to characterize those self-similar and self-affine sets of which all the generating IFSs can be derived from a specific IFS by simple iterations. In the literature, there have been some partial results on the generating IFSs of special self-similar sets. Our main focus will be laid on general self-similar sets and certain self-affine sets. It is proposed to study the problem when a self-similar set can be embedded into another self-similar sets under an affine map. Some necessary arithmetic conditions have been obtained in the literature for a broad class of self-similar sets. We aim to provide possible criterion for determining whether one self-similar set can be affinely embedded into another one, at least for some special class of self-similar sets. It is proposed to characterize the smooth manifolds (for instance, analytic curves and algebraic surfaces) in the Euclidean spaces that contain a non-trivial self-affine set.

14301017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301017.value: 上世紀七十年代中期，Mandelbrot引入了分形的概念， 並用它來描述自然界幾何對象（如雲彩，樹木，岩石， 山峰，海岸線，星空，宇宙等）的不規則性與復雜性。從那之後， 分形的想法已被廣泛地應用到自然科學，工程，經濟，金融等諸多領域。 許多當代藝術家也將這一想法用來創作許多前人所未見的美麗畫卷。分形也自然地出現在數學的很多分支， 包括幾何，動力系統，數論，調和分析與概率。 在數學上， 迭代函數係統是生成分形的基本辦法之一。具體而言， 一個函數迭代系統（IFS）由有限個壓縮映射構成。通過反复迭代，我們得到一個分形集，稱之為該IFS的吸引子。 儘管每一個IFS生成唯一的吸引子，不同的IFS也可能具有相同的吸引子。 在該研究計劃中， 我們將分析刻畫分形集的可能生成函數迭代系統。特別的，我們希望刻畫從分形集到自身的壓縮仿射映射。與之關聯的是，我們將研究分形的嵌入問題。具體而言，我們將研究一個分形集何是否能被嵌入到某一給定的分形集或光滑流形。 這些研究將加深我們對分形幾何的進一步理解。

14301017.label: Realisation of objectives
14301017.value: One of the main objectives of this project is to study the structure of the generating IFSs of a given self similar or self-affine set. For this purpose, we need to investigate the invariant scales of the underlying fractal sets, that is, the possible similarities or affine mappings that map a given fractal set into itself. In our investigation, we focus our studies on the following two classes of fractal sets: (1) total disconnected self-similar sets in R^d satisfying the strong separation condition (SSC) or the open set condition (OSC); (2) a special class of planar self-affine sets called Bedford-McMullen carpets. In Case (1), we succeed in showing that the semigroup of generating IFSs of any self-similar set satisfying the SSC is finitely generated, meanwhile, the semigroup of generating IFSs of a self-similar set satisfying the OSC is only countably generated. The proof is based on a kind of blow-up argument, and a recent result of Deng and Wang on the discreteness of the similar self maps of totally disconnected self-similar Cantor sets satisfying the OSC. We also construct some concrete examples of self-similar Cantor sets satisfying the OSC, of which the semi-group of the generating IFSs is not finitely generated. This shows that different separation conditions on self-similar sets will lead to different properties for the generating structure. In Case (2), we show that under mild assumptions, each affine mapping that maps a Bedford-McMullen (BM) carpet into itself is a diagonal mapping, and the diagonal entries are logarithmically commensurable to the dilation ratios for the BM carpets. Moreover we are able to classify all such affine embeddings of BM carpets. In our approach we need to apply different techniques from number theory, zoom-in dynamics. In particular we apply some recent results achieved by by Meng Wu and Pablo Shmerkin on intersections of non-commensurable Cantor sets. In this project we also investigate the geometry of self-similar and self-affine fractals. We call such a fractal is arithmetically thick if the n-th arithmetic sum of this fractal set has a non-empty interior. We prove that all self-similar sets in R^d and all planar self-affine sets are always arithmetically thick provided they are not contained in a hyperplane. Similarly we prove such results hold for higher dimensional self-affine sets under mild irreducibility assumptions. In our approach we use different tools from zoom-in dynamics and complex analysis. We also investigate the dimensional properties of attractors of nonlinear iterated function systems. We introduce a generalized transversality condition for a parametrized family of IFSs and show that the dimension of their attractors is equal to its singularity dimension (which is the zero point of a certain pressure function). Moreover, we are able to verify this condition for some upper-triangular nonlinear IFSs. This work significantly extends and generalises the early results of Falconer, Solomyak, Jordan, Pollicott and Simon on typical self-affine sets and measures. Another objective of the project is to study the smooth curves and manifolds which may contain a non-trivial self-affine subsets. Along this direction we investigate all the analytic curves and more generally, analytic manifolds. We succeed in classifying all such manifolds that may contain a non-trivial self-affine subsets. In our approach we mainly use the ideas and techniques in complex analysis. Overall we have achieved the major parts (around 95%) of our original objectives. A further understanding of the generating IFSs and affine embeddings of more general self-affine sets is expected. The difficulty comes from the geometry of higher dimensional non-diagonal self-affine sets. This might be achieved by further extending the methods developed in this project as well as by using some ideas of the recent developments of the dimension theory of self-affine sets and measures, and we hope to check this possible approach in the further investigations.

14301017.label: Major findings and research outcome
14301017.value: In [1] we investigate the algebraic structure of similar self-embeddings of totally disconnected self-similar sets. The focus is on totally disconnected self-similar sets which satisfy the strong separation condition (SSC) or more generally, the so-called weak separation condition (WSC). We prove that the semigroup of the self-embeddings is finitely generated when the SSC holds, and countably generated if the WSC holds. Further examples are provided to show that under the WSC, the semigroup of the self-embeddings may be not finitely generated. In [2] we investigate the arithmetic sums of fractal sets in the Euclidean spaces. The main question is to determine whether a given fractal set is arithmetically thick. Here a set E is said to be arithmetically thick if there is an integer n such that the n-th arithmetic sum of E has non-empty interior. As our main results, we show that all self-similar sets, all self-conformal sets, all planar self-affine sets are arithmetically thick if they are not contained in a hyperplane. These results strongly depend on the self-similarity or self-affinity of the involved fractal sets. Moreover we introduce the notion of thickness for compact sets in high dimensions and prove that every set of positive thickness is arithmetically thick. In [3] we investigate the dimensions of the attractors of nonlinear iterated function systems. We introduce a generalized transversality condition (GTC) for parameterized families of C1 IFSs, and show that if the GTC is satisfied, then the dimensions of the IFS attractor is equal to its singularity dimension. Moreover, we verify the GTC for some parameterized families of C^1 IFSs on R^d. In [4] concrete examples of self-similar sets in R^d are constructed to show that their s-dimensional Hausdorff measures can be arbitrarily close to the s-power of their diameters, where s stands for the Hausdorff dimension. In [5] we investigate the generating IFSs of self-similar sets. We prove the following rigidity result: if a self-similar set is generated by an homogeneous IFS which satisfies the open set condition but not the strong separation condition, then this self-similar set can not be generated by any IFS satisfying the SSC. In [6] we successfully determine all the affine embeddings of a class of planar self-affine sets called Bedford-McMullen carpets. Moreover in a paper in preparation, we are able to characterise all the 2-dimensional analytic manifolds which contain a non-trivial self-affine subsets.

14301017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14301017.value: 1. To investigate the affine self-maps of general self-affine sets satisfying certain irreducibility and proximality assumptions. 2. To further investigate the algebraic manifolds with dimension greater than 2 that may contain a self-affine subsets.

14301017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14301017.value: In mathematics, iterated function systems are a basic scheme to generate fractal sets. Formally, an iterated function system (IFS) consists of a finite set of contractive transformations. By repeatedly iterating these transformations, one obtains a fractal set, which is called the attractor of the IFS. A fractal set may be generated by many different IFSs. In this project, we investigate the algebraic structure of the possible IFSs that generate a given fractal set, and prove some rigidity properties for these generating IFSs. Moreover we successfully determine all the affine self-embeddings of a class of planar self-affine fractals, and classify all the two dimensional analytic manifolds that may contain a non-trivial self-affine subset. Besides we obtain some geometric and dimensional properties for the attractors of iterated function systems. These investigations will lead to a better understanding of the theory of IFSs and the algebraic and geometric structure of fractal sets.

14301117.value: 特殊同樂群流形的幾何

14301117.label: Project Objectives
14301117.value: Constructions of TQFT type structures for special geometry. Further our understanding of geometric cycles in manifolds with special holonomy. Study the geometry of Calabi-Yau fourfolds.
rows: Constructions of TQFT type structures for special geometry.
Further our understanding of geometric cycles in manifolds with special holonomy.
Study the geometry of Calabi-Yau fourfolds.

14301117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301117.value: The PI proposes to study special geometry, especially the Topological Quantum Field Theory type structures associated to these spaces. The dimensions of these spaces are 8, 7 and 6 and they are Spin(7)-manifolds, G2-manifolds and Calabi-Yau threefolds respectively. The underlying geometric cycles in these spaces include Donaldson-Thomas bundles, coassociative submanifolds coupled with ASD connections, complex Lagrangian submanifolds and so on. These TQFT type structures can be viewed as coming from an infinite dimensional complex Morse theory as introduced by Gaiotto-Moore-Witten. 硏究者建議繼續研究特殊幾何，特別是有關這些空間的拓撲量子場理論類型結構與這些空間相關聯。 這些空間的維數是8,7和6，它們分别是Spin（7）流形，G2-流形 和三維卡拉比空間。這些空間的幾何構造包括Donaldson-Thomas 叢, coassociative子流形和ASD連絡，複Lagrangian子流形等。 這些TQFT類型的結構可以看作是來自無限維度由 Gaiotto-Moore-Witten引入的複Morse理論。

14301117.label: Realisation of objectives
14301117.value: For objective 1, the PI has achieved it by obtaining categorical duality which gives a duality structure as part of the Rozansky-Witten TQFT under hyperkahler flops. There are a number of new results on quantization of Kahler manifolds which would be very useful for future studies of TQFT structure as well. For objective 2, the PI has achieved it for various types of geometric cycles. These include cycles in octonion spaces in the joint work with Chen and Huang; Lagrangian branes under cyclic symmetries in joint work with Chow; complex branes under categorical duality in joint work with Jiang. For objective 3, geometry of Calabi-Yau fourfolds, as well as arbitrary dimension, has been careful stuides in various joint works with Chan, Chow, Ma and Young. We obtained detailed description of moduli spaces of Maurer-Cantan solution, relating them to scattering diagrams and their refined generalization. This is a foundational work to understand mirror symmetry from large structure limit.

14301117.label: Major findings and research outcome
14301117.value: In the paper 'Geometry of the Maurer-Cartan equation near degenerate Calabi-Yau varieites' with Chan and Ma, given a degenerate Calabi-Yau variety, we construct an almost differential dgBV algebra. Assuming Hodge-to-de Rham degeneracy and a local condition that guarantees freeness of the Hodge bundle, we prove a unobstructedness theorem for smoothing of singular Calabi-Yau varieties. We also demonstrate how our construction yields a logarithmic Frobenius manifold structure on a formal neighborhood of X in the extended moduli space by applying the technique of Barannikov-Kontsevich. In the paper 'Refined scattering diagrams and theta functions from asymptotic analysis of Maurer-Cartan equations' with Ma and Young, we further develop the asymptotic analytic approach to the study of scattering diagrams by analyzing the asymptotic behavior of Maurer-Cartan elements of a differential graded Lie algebra constructed from a (not-necessarily tropical) monoid-graded Lie algebra. This allows us to give a combinatorial description of Hall algebra theta functions for acyclic quivers with non-degenerate skew-symmetrized Euler forms. In the paper 'Twisted cyclic group actions on Fukaya categories and mirror symmetry' with Chow, we construct a Z/2n-action on its Fukaya category and a Zn-action on the local models of its moduli of Lagrangian branes if X has Fano index n. In the series of papers 'A geometric construction of representations of the Berezin-Toeplitz quantization' , 'Bargmann-Fock sheaves on Kähler manifolds', 'Quantization of Kahler manifolds', 'Kapranov's L_infinity structure, Fedosov's star products, and 1-loop exact BV quantizations on Kahler manifolds','Geometric quantization and quantum moment maps on coadjoint orbits and Kähler-Einstein manifolds' with Chan, Li and Ma, we developed deformation quantization and geometric quantization by generalizing Fedosov and BV approach. In the paper 'Embeddings from noncompact symmetric spaces to their compact duals' with Chen and Huang, every compact symmetric space M admits a dual noncompact symmetric space Mˇ. When M is a generalized Grassmannian, we can view Mˇ as a open submanifold of it consisting of space-like subspaces. Motivated from this, we study the embeddings from noncompact symmetric spaces to their compact duals, including space-like embedding for generalized Grassmannians, Borel embedding for Hermitian symmetric spaces and the generalized embedding for symmetric R-spaces. We will compare these embeddings and describe their images using cut loci.

14301117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14301117.value: New techniques and tools developed to study the Maurer-Cartan equation will be useful for further understanding of many moduli problems in geometry.

14301117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14301117.value: This research project has obtained a detailed description of Maurer-Cartan equation near degeneration which is important in the study of Calabi-Yau geometry. Moreover, new mathematical perspectives for quantizations has been established.

14301317.label: Project Objectives
14301317.value: Investigate various topological phenomena of spatial graphs (e.g., knotting, linking, slicing, etc.). Study the topological symmetry group of spatial graphs. Develop and introduce new tools (e.g., Heegaard Floer homology) to the theory of spatial graph.

14301317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301317.value: While knot theory is the study of an embedded circle in the space, the theory of spatial graphs is the study of embedded graphs in the space. This is a field placing between graph theory and topology and has drawn increasing attentions among researchers in nearby fields. Its impact has even extended to the field of molecular chemistry. In this project, we concentrate on answering three questions about graphs, namely: When is a graph knotted? When is a graph slice? When is a graph symmetric? Answers to these questions are not only considered important progress in the theory of spatial graphs, but also leads to interesting applications in molecular chemistry. To approach these questions, we either refine or generalize existing methods (such as Conway-Gordon type theorems and rigidity theorems), or we develop new tools for studying spatial graphs (such as Heegaard Floer homology). Having witnessed profound influence of Heegaard Floer theory on knot theory, we hope that it will exert a similar magnitude of impact on spatial graph theory. 相對紐結理論研究空間中的嵌入圈，空間圖理論是對空間中嵌入圖的研究。這是在圖論和拓撲之間的一個交叉領域，並已得到附近的領域的研究人員越來越多的關注。其影響甚至擴展到分子化學領域。 在這個項目中，我們集中精力回答有關圖形的三個問題，即：圖形何時打結？什麼時候是圖片？什麼時候圖形對稱？對這些問題的回答不僅在空間圖的理論上被認為是重要的進展，而且也會在分子化學中產生有趣的應用。 為了解決這些問題，我們改進或推廣現有的方法（如Conway-Gordon類型定理和剛度定理），同時發展用於研究空間圖的新工具（如Heegaard Floer homology）。目睹了Heegaard Floer理論對紐結理論的深刻影響，我們希望它對空間圖理論產生相似的影響。

14301317.label: Realisation of objectives
14301317.value: All objectives were thoroughly investigated and achieved partly by the 5 publications of the PI. The biggest achievement is the paper by the PI and his collaborator which set up a rigorous foundation of the classical Alexander polynomial invariant for spatial graph and addressed the first and second objectives of the project. Due to Covid-19, there have been some delays of completing the third objective, in the sense that the PI has not yet published a journal paper on the "Heegaard Floer homology" of graphs. Nonetheless, a sketch of the main ideas and results has been collected and reported in RIMS Kôkyûroku with the title "Heegaard Floer complexes of a trivalent graph defined on two Heegaard diagrams".

14301317.label: Major findings and research outcome
14301317.value: The PI published 4 research papers and 1 conference proceeding, and also trained a master student, Man Kit Kung, who also wrote an unpublished manuscript on the topic. Among all research outcome, the joint paper “An Alexander polynomial for MOY graphs” with Prof. Bao Yuanyuan from University of Tokyo published in Selecta Math. is the most important piece of work that laid a solid foundation of the classical Alexander polynomial invariant for spatial graphs. We defined the Alexander invariant combinatorially using a "Kauffman state" type formulation, and we discovered that such an invariant contains many interesting geometric and combinatoric information of the graphs, including an obstruction to the planarity and a counting of the spanning trees. The invariant is shown to satisfy (and conversely being determined) by a series of MOY-type relations. This enables us to further prove the equivalence of our Alexander invariant to Viro's version, which was defined via quantum invariant.

14301317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14301317.value: We expect plenty of follow-up work in the coming years: essentially, we can revisit all classical Alexander invariant results in the past 100 years and then try to extend them to our version of Alexander invariants for graphs. More specifically, we may reformulate the invariants in different ways (geometrically via spanning/Seifert surfaces, by grid diagram, using spanning tree methods, etc.), then relate the invariant to various geometric/combinatorial properties of graphs (planarity, chirality, symmetry, genus, crossing number, spanning trees, etc.), and finally study the categorification of the graphs. In particular, we expect to finish a paper on grid diagram and another paper on Heegaard Floer homology very shortly - probably by the summer of 2023.

14301317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14301317.value: The spatial graph theory can be viewed as an intersection of the two main research areas in math, namely, the graph theory in combinatorics and the knot theory in topology. It is also an ideal tool to model the structure and various phenomena in molecular chemistry and biology. In Layman's language, what we have achieved in this project is to introduce the most important invariant in the 100-year history of knot theory to the study of spatial graphs, which hopefully opens up a window for new exciting development in spatial graph theory. There are likely many common properties between the knot/link and graph cases, but we also expect certain unique features for the graph Alexander polynomial only, which makes this a fascinating topic to explore.

14301417.label: Project Objectives
14301417.value: Improve the voltage sensitivity of RhoVRs (Rhodamine voltage reporters). Our previous MD simulations of VoltageFluor dyes revealed their orientation in lipid bilayers, based on which a series of new VF dyes have been designed, where the molecules' long axes become better aligned with the membrane normal through the addition of a second sulfonate group. These newly designed molecules include disulfoVF2.2(OMe).Cl, the most sensitive VoltageFluor dye developed to date. Building upon these results, we plan to investigate the membrane orientation of RhoVRs, a set of red-shifted, voltage-sensitive dyes based on tetramethylrhodamine. Chemical modifications that render RhoVRs better aligned with the membrane normal will be first examined by MD simulations and then tested in our collaborator's lab, in order to develop the next-generation RhoVRs with enhanced voltage sensitivity. Evaluate the influence of cholesterol on the distribution of voltage-sensitive dyes. The membranes of mammalian cells are known to contain a significant amount of cholesterol, while the exact phospholipid:cholesterol ratio varies among cell types and among different organelles in a single cell. Our previous MD simulations have revealed that VF dyes become better aligned with the membrane normal upon insertion into a mixed POPC:cholesterol (2:1) bilayer. Given this result and the uneven content of cholesterol in cellular membranes, we plan to evaluate, via free energy calculations, the influence of cholesterol on a voltage-sensitive dye's distribution, i.e., whether a given dye prefers a certain type of lipid environment. Along with the analysis of dye orientation, these calculations will provide a mechanistic understanding of physical principles governing the distribution of fluorescent voltage-sensitive dyes in biological membranes.

14301417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301417.value: Compared with traditional patch-clamp methodology, fluorescent voltage-sensitive dyes based on small molecules offer a high-throughput, non-invasive alternative to the interrogation of electrical activity in a cell. Ideally, these dye molecules should localize to the plasma membrane, offer sub-millisecond response time, and present high voltage sensitivity with little or no disruption to normal cellular function. Fluorescent voltage-sensitive dyes based on photoinduced electron transfer (PeT) mechanism, such as the VoltageFluor (VF) dyes, are a group of newly developed voltage sensors that meet the above criteria. However, despite their successful applications on a range of biological systems, a rational design scheme remains elusive, due in part to our incomplete understanding of physical principles governing their performance in a lipid membrane. We have recently combined computer simulations with our collaborator's experiments in the investigation and optimization of first-generation VF dyes. Through multiple replicas of molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and the corresponding experiments, we established the close link between the voltage sensitivity of a VF dye and its tilt angle in a lipid membrane. This result led to the development of disulfoVF2.2(OMe).Cl, the most sensitive VoltageFluor dye found to date. Building upon the above work, we propose to systematically investigate the interactions of VF dyes as well as the red-shifted, rhodamine-based voltage sensors (RhoVRs) with lipid membranes. Our goal is to understand how such interactions can be exploited to improve both the voltage sensitivity and brightness of these fluorescent dyes. To this end, we will conduct MD simulations and free energy calculations to measure the orientation of the dye molecules in a membrane, compute their membrane binding affinity, and evaluate whether/how their distribution is influenced by the cholesterol content in their lipid environment. These computational efforts will be complemented by chemical synthesis and fluorescence experiments conducted by our collaborator. Together, we expect that the proposed work not only will lead to the development of next-generation VF dyes and RhoVRs, but also will help establish a general, rational design scheme for PeT-based fluorescent voltage-sensitive dyes. 相比傳統的膜片鉗技術，可感知膜電壓的螢光小分子具有高通量、非侵入的特點，因而更適用於檢測細胞內的膜電壓變化。基於PeT（光敏電子傳送）的螢光小分子染料是一類新近研究出的膜電壓感受器。最近，我們同實驗合作者一起優化了一類這樣的染料，即VoltageFluor (VF)分子。通過將分子動力學模擬和實驗結合，我們發現了disulfoVF2.2(OMe).Cl, 迄今為止具有最高的電壓敏感度的VF染料。立足於這項工作，我們計劃系統性的研究VF染料與細胞磷脂膜的相互作用，以闡明這類作用可以如何被利用來優化染料的電壓敏感度和亮度。為了達到這一目標，我們將進行分子動力學模擬和自由能計算，測定染料在細胞膜中的朝向，並計算它們的分布是如何被磷脂膜中膽固醇的含量所影響的。除了VF染料以外，我們也將研究另一類基於rhodamine的膜電壓感受小分子RhoVR。這些研究將為基於PeT的壓敏螢光小分子的設計提供基礎。

14301417.label: Realisation of objectives
14301417.value: We have realized 80% of objective 1 and 100% of objective 2 as listed in section 5.2. Specifically, with regard to objective 1, as mentioned in our mid-term progress report, we first examined isoVF, one of the latest family members of the VoltageFluor dyes. Along with our experimental collaborator, we investigated its membrane orientation as well as its membrane binding affinity. This part of the work has been submitted and attached to this report. Next, we turned to the originally proposed RhoVR dyes. We have completed simulations of five members of this voltage reporter family, where we investigated their orientation through multiple replicas of 500-ns MD trajectories. We are currently preparing for 'mutant' RhoVR simulations, where we will modify the dyes artificially to examine the resulting changes in their membrane orientation. This set of calculations will allow us to complete the remaining 20% of proposed objective 1. The reason that this objective was not 100% achieved in the project duration is due to the additional study on isoVF dye, which, as noted in our mid-term progress report, represented a latest addition to the VF family. We proceeded with the original objective 1 after we finished the work on isoVF and we expect that all related work on objective 1 will be completed within a year. With regard to objective 2, we have finished all the proposed free energy calculations of VF dyes within different lipid membranes. This part of the work has been summarized and we plan to submit the draft (also attached to this report) within a couple of months.

14301417.label: Major findings and research outcome
14301417.value: Through the work summarized in section 5.3, we thoroughly investigated the originally proposed RhoVR voltage reporters as well as isoVF, one of the latest VoltageFluor dyes developed in our experimental collaborator's group. Our simulations revealed the distinct orientations of these fluorescent dye molecules within various lipid environment and quantified their differential binding affinity to membranes with or without cholesterol. Our work has resulted in one joint manuscript with our collaborator (submitted), one simulation manuscript to be submitted. We expect that a third manuscript will be produced within the next year. Through this project, we have trained/been training two Mphil students (one graduated in 2019 and one expected to graduate in 2022).

14301417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14301417.value: We are currently preparing more calculations on RhoVRs to examine how structural modifications affect their membrane orientation. This part of the work will allow us to accomplish the remaining 20% of the proposed objective 1, which we expect to complete within one year. Recently, our collaborator has demonstrated the distinct membrane permeabilities of RhoVRs, which grant some members of this family the unique ability to tag mitochondria and provide voltage sensing for these intracellular organelles. We therefore plan to expand our study to the membrane permeability of RhoVRs, which we believe has the potential to be developed into an independent project on its own.

14301417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14301417.value: Voltage measurement with small fluorescent indicators is a valuable tool to decipher complex dynamics in electrically excitable cells. However, the design of molecular wire-based probes based on photo-induced electron transfer (PeT) mechanism remains a considerable challenge, due in part to our incomplete understanding of the physical properties governing the voltage sensitivity and membrane affinity of these probes. Through aggregated multi-microsecond molecular dynamics simulations and free energy calculations, we systematically investigated the difference in orientation and membrane binding affinity of the voltage-sensing VoltageFluor (VFdyes) as well as the Rhodamine voltage reporters (RhoVRs). Our results indicate that the symmetry of the molecular scaffold and the strength of hydrophilic chemical groups of a given dye dominates its orientation and membrane binding affinity, respectively. Our work not only provides a mechanistic understanding of physical principles governing the voltage sensitivity, fluorescence brightness and local distribution of existing dyes, but also shed light onto future rational design of PeT-based fluorescent voltage sensors in general.

14301517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301517.value: In this project the PI plans to study the Ricci flow and Kahler-Ricci flow with possible unbounded curvature. The PI also plans to study the preservation of certain curvature properties without assuming the curvature being bounded. The PI plans to investigate if the results on Kahler-Ricci flow can be applied to understand the complex structures of the manifolds. The PI wants to study static metrics on noncompact asymptotically flat or asymptotically hyperbolic manifolds and on compact manifolds with boundary. The PI plans to understand static metric on an asymptotical end and on an asymptotically hyperbolic manifold with an inner boundary. The PI also plans to understand compact static manifolds with boundary without assuming that the manifolds are conformally flat. The PI plans to study various functionals on compact manifolds with boundary which may be related to various definition of quasilocal masses. 在這個計畫中主研究員計畫研究在可能無界曲率的流形的Ricci流 和 Kahler-Ricci流。主研究員還計畫研究某些曲率特性的維持而 不假定曲率是有界的。主研究員計畫研究Kahler-Ricci流的結果 是否可用於理解流形的複結構。 主研究員要研究非緊漸近平坦或漸近雙曲流形和帶邊界緊流形的 靜態度量。主研究員計畫瞭解漸近平坦端和有內部邊界漸近雙曲 流形上的漸靜態度量。主研究員還計畫瞭解在不假定流形是共形 平坦的緊湊帶邊界的靜態流形。主研究員計畫研究帶邊界緊流形 上可能與各種准局域質量有關的各種泛函。

14301517.label: Realisation of objectives
14301517.value: Objective 1: People use Ricci flow or Kahler-Ricci flow to study structure of manifolds is the flow may give more information after t>0. Usually one cannot expect an initial metric to have bounded curvature. Then previous methods do not work. Lee and the PI tried to construct Kahler-Ricci flow on noncompact manifold with nonnegative bisectional curvature. We use some sort of compact exhaustion by conformally change the metric in compact sets, and the resulting metric will only be Hermitian. The first step is to construct solution of the Chern-Ricci flow which will be Kahler-Ricci flow on the set where the initial metric is Kahler. Lee and the PI obtain a criteria for the existence of Chern-Ricci flows which generalize some previous results. In order to obtain limit when we let the compact sets exhaust the manifold, Lee and the PI are able to obtain some local estimates of the curvature under the condition that the initial metric is non-collapsing and has nonnegative bisectional curvature. With this estimates we can obtain solution on each compact set on a fixed time interval so that the curvature is bounded by c/t and then take limit. We show that we still have nonnegative bisectional curvature for t>0. If the initial metric has maximal volume growth, then the deformed metric still has maximal volume growth. Together with a previous result by Chau and the PI, this gives a proof that a complete noncompact Kahler manifold with nonnegative bisectional curvature and with maximal volume growth is biholomorphic to the complex Euclidean space This last result on the complex structure of the manifold is also obtained by Gang Liu using different method. To extend the method on curvature estimates above, Lee and the PI obtained some local maximum principles for certain elliptic operators along the Ricci flow with curvature being bounded by c/t. One of which was originally obtained by Hochard. We then get some lower bound of certain curvatures assuming the curvatures of the initial metric have some lower bound. Using these, we studied Kahler-Ricci flow with initial data with orthogonal bisectional curvature and Ricci curvature bounded from below and with non-collapsing condition. We use the previous method and results on the construction of Chern-Ricci flow. Lee and the PI are then construct Kahler-Ricci flow under the above conditions. This is similar to the pyramid solution of Ricci flow in the Riemannian case as studied by Simon-Topping and others. We apply the result on the complex structure of Gromov-Hausdorff limit of a sequence of Kahler manifolds. The problem of smooth structure of Gromov-Hausdorff limit in the Riemannian case has been studied by many people including Simon-Topping, Bamler-Cabezas-Rivas and Wilking , Lai and McLeod-Topping. People are interested to understand conditions for Kahler manifolds (compact or complete noncompact) to support a Kahler-Einstein metrics in terms of Ricci curvature and holomorphic sectional curvature. PI and his co-authors (Huang, Lee, Tong) obtained sufficient conditions of existence of Chern-Ricci flow or more generally the corresponding potential flows on a noncompact complex manifold without assuming the initial metric is complete or have bounded curvature. In fact, we consider initial data which only a nonnegative (not necessarily positive) real (1,1) form for the potential flows. Condition that the potential flow will give Chern-Ricci flow is given. Condition for the Chern-Ricci flow will converge to a Kahler-Einstein metric after renormalization is given. Roughly speaking, the condition is to say that the Ricci form is negative as a class. In terms of holomorphic sectional curvatures, PI and his co-authors proved that if a complete Kahler metric g with bounded gradient with respect to and uniformly equivalent to another is uniformly equivalent to a complete Kahler metric with holomorphic sectional curvature being bounded above by a negative constant, then the Kahler-Ricci flow will exist for all time and converge to a Kahler-Einstein metric after renormalization. The results are related to the existence of Kahler-Einstein metrics on strictly pseudo-convex bounded domain (by Cheng-Yau) and on complete Kahler manifolds with bounded curvatures and negative holomorphic sectional curvature by Wu-Yau and others. Objective 2: For a compact manifold with smooth boundary, one would like to know the interplay between the scalar curvature and the boundary behaviour. Previously, Shi and the PI have proved that in dimension 3, if the scalar curvature is nonnegative and the boundary satisfies two conditions: (i) each connected component has positive mean curvature; (ii) each connected component has positive Gaussian curvature, then the Brown-York quasi-local mass is nonnegative and is zero if and only if the manifold is a domain in R^3. The Brown-York quasi local mass is 1/8π times the total mean curvature of the boundary subtracted from the total mean curvature of the surface when isometrically embedded in R^3. The embedding exists and unique by (ii). In this project, Shi and the PI proved the same results by assuming the mean curvature is nonnegative and the Gaussian curvature is quasi-positive. In the case of positive mean curvature, one may use the so-called quasi-spherical metric by Bartnik. If the mean curvature is only nonnegative, then one cannot use this method. Instead, one has to use a careful conformal change of metric to get the nonnegativity of the Brown-York mass. The rigidity part is more subtle. In case of positive mean curvature, some monotonicity property of the quasi-spherical metric will give rigidity more easily. In case the mean curvature is only nonnegative, we have to construct a suitable inverse mean curvature flow and show that the level sets near a chosen point has zero Hawking mass and then show that the metric is flat near the chosen point. Mantoulidis, Miao and the PI studied asymptotically flat three manifolds with compact boundary and with nonnegative scalar curvature and with positive mean curvature. In the proof of the Riemannian Penrose inequality, Bray proved that the capacity of the boundary is bounded by the ADM mass of manifold (assuming there is only one end). We obtained an upper bound of twice of the capacity in terms of 1/8π of the total mean curvature plus a quantity introduced by Mantoulidis, Miao. The quantity is on a pair (S,g): a compact surface (not necessarily connected) and a metric on the surface. The quantity is to measure how large the total mean curvature of this pair so that it can be fill-in by a three manifold with nonnegative scalar curvature and positive mean curvature. The quantity is motivated by the study of Brown-York mass and the notion of Bartnik mass. If the above mentioned inequality becomes an equality and the boundary consists of only topological spheres, then the manifold must be that part of the Schwarzschild manifold exterior to a coordinate sphere. In the process of the study, we need to consider non-smooth fill-in which may be independent interest. With Wan, the PI studied solutions of the vacuum Einstein equation on three dimensional spacetime with compact Cauchy surface with genus at least 2, under the constant mean curvature spatially harmonic gauge. We reproved a result of Moncrief on the parametrization of the Teichmuller space by those solutions by a careful study of a Monge-Ampere type equation. These are the works realizing the two objectives of the project.

14301517.label: Major findings and research outcome
14301517.value: All references are in section 8. In [6 ] , Shi and the PI proved that if $M$ is a compact manifold with boundary, and $g$ is a metric on $M$ with nonnegative scalar curvature so that the boundary has nonnegative (instead of positive) mean curvature and each component of the boundary has quasi-positive (instead of positive) Gaussian curvature, then the Brown-York mass of each component is nonnegative and if one of them is zero, then the boundary is connected and $M$ is isometric to a domain in $R^3$ which is topologically a ball. In [3], Mantoulidis, Miao and the PI obtained new inequalities between the boundary capacity of an asymptotically flat 3-manifold with nonnegative scalar curvature and boundary quantities that relate to quasi-local mass including the Brown–York mass and another quasi-local mass quantity on a surface introduced by Mantoulidis and Miao which is closely related the concept of Bartnik quasi-local mass. By a careful study of a Monge–Amp`ere type equation introduced by Moncrief In [8], Wan and the PI obtained another proof of a result of Monchrief on the parametrization of the Teichm¨uller space of surface with genus larger than 1 by solutions of the Einstien equation in three dimensional spacetime . In [1 ], Lee and the PI constructed Kahler-Ricci flow with initial data with nonnegative bisectional curvature which is non-collapsing, without assuming the curvature is bounded. We then gave another proof a special case on a uniformization conjecture of Yau. In [ 2], we proved that along a complete Kahler-Ricci flow, the nonnegativity of bisectional curvature is preserved assuming that the curvature is bounded by c/t, for example. We obtained some local maximum principles in [9 ] for certain elliptic operators along the Ricci flow with curvature being bounded by c/t. One of which was originally obtained by Hochard. Using these, in [7] we studied Kahler-Ricci flow with initial data with orthogonal bisectional curvature and Ricci curvature bounded from below and with non-collapsing condition. We concluded that the Gromov-Haussdorff limit of a sequence of Kahler manifolds with the above properties supports a Kahler metric. In [4, 5], the PI and his co-authors studied the short time, long time existence and convergence of Chern-Ricci flow on noncompact Hermitian manifolds without assuming the curvature of the initial data is bounded. Kahler-Einstein metrics with negative Ricci curvature are obtained under suitable conditions.

14301517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14301517.value: Since we know how to construct Kahler-Ricci flow initial metric with nonnegative bisectional curvature for a short time under a noncollapsing condition , one would like to understand about long time existence and behavior. This is related to Yau’s uniformization conjecture without assuming maximal volume growth. On the other hand, there are other kinds of curvature conditions which are of interest. Instead of working on Ricci curvature and holmorphic sectional curvature, one may consider the interpolation of them, e.g. the k-Ricci curvature. People are working in this direction and one would like to know more. Recently many activities on the structure and classification of manifolds in terms of scalar curvature. In the study, non-smooth metric may arise naturally as in the proof of the positivity of Brown-York mass. An outstanding question is whether a non-smooth metric will actually be smooth under certain conditions. This is one of the possible direction of research. On the other hand, one would like to understand whether the results in the project on manifolds with nonnegative scalar curvature can be extended to the case that the scalar curvature is bounded from below. This may be related to the study of asymptotically hyperbolic space.

14301717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301717.value: Mild, catalytic hydrogenolysis of aliphatic carbon-carbon bonds with water as the transfer hydrogenating agent will be investigated at low temperatures using newly designed, more efficient iridium porphyrin based catalysts to provide energy rich fuels and valuable chemicals from simple hydrocarbons. The use of non-combustible and readily available water eliminates the use and handling of highly explosive, difficult to store and transport hydrogen gas. The understanding of selective bond cleavages gained from selective cleavage of the weaker carbon-carbon bonds than stronger carbon-hydrogen bonds is of fundamental importanct. The proposed catalysis couples two very challenging processes of water splitting and aliphatic carbon-carbon bond cleavages to give hydrogen enriched organics as well as value added chemicals. This proposal aims to provide a novel method for chemicals in economically more attractive ways. 研究銥卟啉催化劑在低溫下進行新型催化脂肪族碳 - 碳鍵與水的氫化反應,以提供能源豐富的燃料 -簡單的碳氫 和的有價值的化合品. 這氫化反應使用不燃的和易於使用的水, 消除了高度爆炸性氫氣的使用和避免處理,儲存和運輸氫氣. 從對選擇性斷裂更弱的碳 - 碳比碳氫化學鍵的理解 是非常重要的.這個建議計劃的催化 水分解和脂肪族碳 - 碳鍵組合裂解是極其挑戰性的化學反應, 為了經濟上更有吸引力的方式提供富氫的有機物和增值化學品.

14301717.label: Realisation of objectives
14301717.value: With respect to the project objectives as per original application: (1) A series of new di-iridium(III) porphyrin alkyl complexes containing meta- and para-xylyl diether linkers were successfully synthesized, and their reactivity towards hydrogenolysis of the carbon(sp3)-carbon(sp3) sigma-bonds of [2.2]paracyclophane substrate using water as a hydrogen source was examined in this research work. These di-iridium(III) porphyrin complexes exhibited catalytic reactivity for hydrogenolysis of [2.2]paracyclophane, yielding the corresponding hydrogenolysis products. (2) A series of meta- and para-diamide-linked di-iridium(III) porphyrin alkyl complexes were also synthesized in this work. Their reactivity towards hydrogenolysis of the carbon-carbon sigma-bonds of [2.2]paracyclophane was also examined and compared with that of the xylyl diether-linked counterparts (3) We have also examined the carbon-carbon activation of substituted cyclopropanes using an iridium(III) porphyrin hydride complex as a pre-catalyst. Cyclopropane substrates containing substituents of different electronic and steric properties were investigated, and a mechanism of the carbon-carbon activation was proposed. (4) In order to further explore the reactivity of group 9 metal complexes towards activation of C-E (E = H, C, N, O or halogens) bonds, we have also examined the reactivity of methyl rhodium(III) porphyrin complex with various substituted benzoic acids with isopropyl alcohol being the hydrogen source. Difficulty encountered in this work: A major obstacle that we encountered in the present research project is the worldwide lockdown due to the pandemic situation in the past few years. This led to long and frequent down-time of major instruments (NMR spectrometers, mass spectrometers and X-ray diffractometers), which are fundamental for characterization of various products in our studies. Besides, most of the conferences and meetings related to the present research area were either cancelled or postponed in the past few years. These conferences and meetings are important platforms for us to interact and exchange ideas with our peers.

14301717.label: Major findings and research outcome
14301717.value: Carbon-carbon bond activation is a challenging topic as compared with carbon-hydrogen bond activation. There are only few examples on carbon-carbon bond activation of unstrained and unfunctionalized hydrocarbons. Moreover, the use of water as a hydrogen source for hydrogenolysis reactions is also an attractive research topic which has enormous potential for future development. In this research project, we have investigated hydrogenolysis of carbon-carbon sigma-bonds of alkanes catalyzed by iridium(III) porphyrin complexes. A series of new di-iridium(III) porphyrins complexes containing semi-rigid meta- and para-xylyl diether and diamide linkers have been designed and successfully synthesized. These di-iridium(III) porphyrins complexes exhibited catalytic activity towards hydrogenolysis of unfunctionalized [2.2]paracyclophane alkane substrate with water as a hydrogen source. A mechanism for the hydrogenolysis reactions has been proposed based on results of a mechanistic study in this work. It is remarkable to note that the present di-iridium(III) porphyrin system exhibited a faster hydrogenolysis reactivity, as compared with the rates of the corresponding mononuclear iridium(III) porphyrins as well as rhodium porphyrin systems. This may be attributed to (i) a stronger iridium-carbon bond formed in the carbon-carbon activation step of the catalytic cycle, and (ii) formation of an energetically more favorable diporphyrin-substrate complex due to the presence of a semi-rigid linker between the two iridium porphyrin moieties. Results of our findings have been reported in an article published in New Journal of Chemistry, vol. 43, pp. 3656 (2019). In the course of examining carbon-carbon bond activation by metalloporphyrins with water and isopropanol and various promoting additives, we have discovered the carbon-oxygen C(=O)-O activation of carboxylic acid additives by metalloporphyrins. It was found that methyl rhodium(III) porphyrin complex Rh(ttp)Me, in the presence of isopropanol as a mild reductant, could activate the carbon-oxygen C(=O)-O bond of various carboxylic acid substrates and generate the corresponding rhodium porphyrin acyl complexes. A detailed mechanistic study on these carbon-oxygen C(=O)-O activation reactions has also been carried out. Our study led to a new synthetic route for rhodium(III) porphyrin acyl complexes, which are generally difficult to prepare. Results of these findings have been reported in Organometallics, vol. 40, pp. 3733 (2021).

14301717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14301717.value: Results of the present research work have shown that the di-iridium(III) porphyrins are viable catalysts for hydrogenolysis of aliphatic carbon-carbon bonds. These prompted us to carry out further investigations on carbon-carbon bond activation by the di-iridium porphyrin system through modifying (i) the length of the linker group, and (ii) the steric and electronic properties of the porphyrin system. It is expected that these modifications may allow us to tune the reactivity of the di-iridium porphyrin based catalysts towards activation of carbon-carbon bonds. Activation of the carbon-carbon bonds of other unfunctionalized alkane substrates, such as cyclopropanes and cyclohexadienes, would also be explored. Besides, the reactivity of the di-porphyrin system towards activation of the carbon-oxygen C(=O)-O bond of acyl groups is also an interesting study worthy of exploration.

14301717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14301717.value: Carbon-carbon bond activation is a fundamental but important topic in synthetic chemistry which can provide new routes for preparation of various chemicals. However, carbon-carbon bond activation is also a challenging topic as compared with carbon-hydrogen bond activation. The present research project focused on hydrogenolysis of aliphatic carbon-carbon bonds of an unfunctionalized alkane with water using iridium(III) porphyrin-based catalysts. A series of new di-iridium(III) porphyrins complexes containing semi-rigid meta- and para-xylyl diether and diamide linkers have been designed and successfully synthesized. These di-iridium(III) porphyrins complexes exhibited catalytic activity towards hydrogenolysis of unfunctionalized [2.2]paracyclophane alkane substrate with water as a hydrogen source. A mechanism for the hydrogenolysis reactions has been proposed based on the results of a mechanistic study. The use of non-combustible, earth-abundant water as a hydrogen source instead of the explosive hydrogen gas for hydrogenolysis of carbon-carbon bonds is remarkable. We hope the results of the present research work can pave the way for our future study on carbon-carbon bond activation of various organic substrates using water as a hydrogen source.

14302317.label: Project Objectives
14302317.value: To investigate the global heat transport modification by polymer additives in turbulent RBC for Wi>1. 14302317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302317.value: Polymer-induced drag reduction (DR) in wall-bounded turbulent flows has been studied extensively since its discovery more than 70 years ago. Compared with DR, experimental studies of polymer additives on turbulent heat transport are rather limited, partially due to the fact that, in a typical laboratory experiment, weak fluctuating velocity in thermally driven turbulence cannot stretch polymers appreciably, i.e. the Weissenberg number (the ratio of polymer relaxation time to the Kolmogorov time of the turbulent flow) is much smaller than one. In the proposed project, we will conduct a systematic experimental study of the heat transport modification by polymer additives and its mechanism in a regime with large Wi. The experiments will be conducted in an idealized model system for thermally driven turbulent flows, the Rayleigh-Bénard convection (RBC). In this project a combination of approaches will be used to achieve large Wi. Firstly, a large molecular weight (Mw) polymer, Polyacrylamide (PAM) with Mw=18 million, dissolved into water with 1% sodium chloride by weight will be used. The addition of salt in the solution should significantly increases the relaxation time of PAM. The strong negative temperature dependence of PAM also allows us to increase polymer relaxation time (2.6 s at 20 oC) and thus large Wi. Secondly, we will carry out experiments in convection cells with rough surfaces. By operating the rough convection cell at a lower mean temperature of the bulk fluid and over the Rayleigh number range from 2×108 to 5×1010, we can achieve Wi from 0.8 to 11.2, which significantly extends the Wi range when compared with previous experiments (Wi < 0.1). The global heat transport modification by polymer additives will be studied as a function of polymer concentration c and Wi. The changes in the boundary layer, and the influences on the emission rate and coherency of thermal plumes by polymer additives will be directly measured. The local heat transport and energy dissipation rate in the cell center will also be studied. The obtained results will help to elucidate the mechanisms of heat transport in the presence of polymer additives in thermally driven turbulence. From a practical point of view, the measured properties of c- and Wi-dependence of heat transport enhancement should also be useful for real applications. 70多年前，人們發現高分子聚合物可以用來減小管道/槽道流中的流動阻力。這一現象被稱為高分子聚合物引起的流動減阻。到目前為止，很多研究都致力於理解高分子聚合物流動減阻的機理。和高分子聚合物引起的流動減阻相比較，高分子聚合物對熱驅動湍流影響的實驗研究就比較少了。主要的原因在於，在一般的熱驅動湍流中，相對較弱的速度漲落較難拉伸高分子聚合物。這個拉伸的程度可以用一個無量綱的Weissenberg數Wi來衡量。這裡的Wi數定義為高分子聚合物弛豫時間和熱湍流的Kolmogorov時間的比值。當Wi>1時，高分子聚合物和湍流有比較強的相互作用。在一般的熱驅動湍流中Wi遠小於1。在該項目中，通過一些特殊的實驗設計，我們將在Wi>1的區間里，系統地研究高分子聚合物對熱驅動湍流的影響。我們的實驗將在熱驅動湍流的標準模型瑞利-伯納德對流（Rayleigh-Bénard convection, RBC）中展開。 從Wi數的定義不難看出，不管是增加高分子聚合物的弛豫時間還是減小湍流的Kolmogorov時間都可以增加Wi數。這兩種途徑都將在這個項目中採用。其次為了減小湍流的Kolmogorov時間，我們將在對流槽的上下表面引入粗糙元素。結合這兩個方法，在瑞利數（RBC的控制參數）2×108 到5×1010的區間內，我們可以使Wi數從0.8變到11。 和以前的實驗中達到的Wi~0.1相比較，我們能達到的Wi數遠大於之前的實驗。我們將系統地測量高分子聚合物濃度以及Wi數對熱湍流傳熱效率的影響。我們將直接測量高分子聚合物引起的邊界層變化以及其對熱羽流相干性的影響。 該項目的研究成果將有助於人們理解高分子聚合物影響熱對流傳熱的機制。實驗中得到的傳熱效率與Wi數和高分子聚合物濃度的關係，也可以在實際中得到應用。

14302317.label: Realisation of objectives
14302317.value: 1. We studied the effect of polymer concentration c on the viscosity of the polyacrylamide (PAM) solution in the presence of salt. The polymer PAM was dissolved into 1% (by weight) NaCl aqueous solution. We measured the viscosity of the polymer solution with NaCl for c changed from 0 ppm to 200 ppm at temperature 20 oC. 2. We measured heat transport modification by polymer additives in a Rayleigh-Benard (RB) convection system with c changed from 0 ppm to 200 ppm. The experiment was carried out in RB cell with rough surfaces. The roughness elements were in the form of squared latticed pyramids with a roughness parameter λ=1.9. Here λ=h/d with h=8 mm is the height of the roughness elements and d=4.2 mm is the roughness base width. 3. We also studied the effects of roughness parameter λ on the heat transport modification by polymer additives. We varied λ from 1.0 to 8.0. We made systematic measurement of the boundary layer properties, such as its profiles and thickness as functions of the polymer concentration, salt concentration and the surface roughness parameter. In addition, we measured the global velocity field measurement and how it depends on the concentration of polymer additives and system control parameters such as the polymer concentration, surface roughness and the Rayleigh number.

14302317.label: Major findings and research outcome
14302317.value: 1. We found that for c< 20 ppm, the change of the viscosity compared with pure water is smaller than 2%. For c larger than 20 ppm, the viscosity increases gradually with c and it reaches 150% that of pure water for c=200 ppm. 2. We found that the global heat transport can be enhanced with polymer additives. A maximum heat transport enhancement of 4% compared with the Newtonian case was observed for c=18 ppm. For c<=18 ppm, the heat transport increases with c. But it starts to decrease with c for c>18 ppm. The heat transport behavior with polymer additives, characterized by the Nusselt number Nu, can be expressed by Nu(c)=3.2*log(106c)+178.2 for c<=18 ppm and Nu(c)=-2.3e5c+191.5 for 18 ppm <=c<=200 ppm. The enhanced heat transport for c<=18 ppm is probably due to the enhanced coherency of thermal plumes, which will be investigated in detail in the next phase of the project. As the solution viscosity increase with c for c>20 ppm, the reduction of Nu for c>18 ppm is largely due to the stabilization of the boundary layer by polymer additives. 3. We found that except for the case of λ=1.9, the heat transport in other values of λ all decreases with polymer additive. As the heat transport in Newtonian fluids for different values of λ are in different regimes, such a λ-dependence of the heat transport modification by polymer may be correlated with the spatial distribution of energy dissipation rates and thermal variance dissipation rate for convection cells with different λ. Some of the results have been published in refereed journals, some are still under preparation.

14302317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14302317.value: A potential future study would be to use polymers with much larger molecular weight than used in the present study, which will be a challenging task.

14302317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14302317.value: Heat transfer, such as cooling of electronic devices, is a fundamental industrial process and have very broad applications in engineering and industry. This study found that a small amount of polymer additives can potentially enhance heat transfer in the bulk of a convective fluid flow, which could be useful in certain engineering situations.
