14302617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302617.value: This project continues the PI's study of SYZ transforms and their geometric applications. The Homological Mirror Symmetry (HMS) conjecture was a categorical formulation of mirror symmetry proposed by the Fields Medalist Maxim Kontsevich in 1994. It attempts at explaining the powerful and mysterious mirror symmetry phenomenon for a pair of mirror Calabi-Yau manifolds as an equivalence between the Fukaya category on one side and the derived category of coherent sheaves on the other side, which are algebraic objects describing different types of geometry on the two sides. On the other hand, in 1996, Strominger, Yau and Zaslow proposed a much more geometric framework to explain the relation between a mirror pair of Calabi-Yau manifolds. The SYZ conjecture, named after its authors, suggests that mirror symmetry is essentially a geometric Fourier transform and a mirror pair admits fiberwise dual Lagrangian torus fibrations to the same base. In a previous project, the PI employed the SYZ framework and constructed explicit SYZ transforms to realize the equivalences predicted by HMS. This provides a geometric and concrete understanding of the HMS conjecture, which was usually proved by separate computations on the two sides. This project is a continuation of the above one, and our main aim is to explore further and deeper applications of SYZ transforms in mirror symmetry and geometry in general. There are several main objectives in this project. The first and most immediate goal is to extend our results obtained in the previous project to higher dimensions. There are various difficulties including the search for a good construction of suitable Lagrangian submanifolds and proving a powerful enough generation result. Another, probably more important, goal is to explore geometric applications of the principle “HMS is realized by SYZ”. As HMS is topological while SYZ is much more geometric in nature, we expect that more refined geometric information can be extracted from this principle. As an instance, we plan to apply it to problems in geometric quantization. Finally, we aim at working out how geometric structures are being interchanged by SYZ transforms, and possible digging out new geometric structures or new applications to geometric problems. We plan to explore how SYZ transforms can be applied to study the deformation theory on the A-side, the correspondence between special Lagrangian submanifolds and the solutions of the deformed Hermitian-Yang-Mills equation, and so on. 本項目將繼續PI對SYZ變換及其幾何應用的研究。 同源鏡對稱（HMS）猜想是由菲爾茲獎得主Maxim Kontsevich在1994年提出的對鏡對稱的一個代數和範疇描述。它試圖將一對鏡像Calabi-Yau流形之間的強大而神秘的鏡對稱現象解釋為一方的Fukaya範疇（辛幾何）與另一方的凝聚層的導出範疇之間的等價關係，這些範疇是兩側不同類型幾何的代數描述。 另一方面，1996年，Strominger，Yau和Zaslow提出了一個更加幾何的框架來解釋一對Calabi-Yau流形之間的鏡對稱現象。 SYZ猜想以其作者命名，它斷言鏡對稱本質上是一個幾何傅立葉變換。 在以前的項目中，PI採用SYZ猜想的框架，構建了具體的SYZ變換來實現HMS猜想所預言的等價關係。這提供了對HMS猜想的幾何和具體的理解，有別於以往通常由兩側的單獨計算所得出的證明。 這個項目是上述的延續，我們的主要目的是探索SYZ變換在鏡對稱和幾何中的更深入的應用。這個項目有幾個主要目標。第一個也是最直接的目標是將我們在上一個項目中獲得的成果擴展到更高的維數。 另一個可能更重要的目標是探索“HMS由SYZ實現”這個原理的幾何應用。由於HMS是拓撲的，而SYZ本質上更具有幾何性質，所以我們期望從這個原理可以提取出更精細的幾何信息。例如，我們計劃將其應用於幾何量化中的問題。 最後，我們將集中研究幾何結構如何通過SYZ變換進行互換，以致發現新的幾何結構或新的幾何應用。我們計劃探索如何應用SYZ變換來研究辛幾何的形變理論，以及特殊拉格朗日子流形與變形Hermitian-Yang-Mills方程的解的對應等問題。

14302617.label: Realisation of objectives
14302617.value: The first objective of this project was to apply SYZ transforms to study the geometry of the Homological Mirror Symmetry conjecture. In the previous project (RGC Ref No 400213), the PI and collaborators have constructed and applied geometric Fourier-Mukai—type functors for toric Calabi-Yau 2- and 3-folds. These realize the equivalence between the derived category of coherent sheaves on a toric Calabi-Yau manifold and the Fukaya category of its mirror, as asserted in Kontsevich's Homological Mirror Symmetry conjecture. As applications, we provided the first complete computation of the wrapped Fukaya category of a six-dimensional Liouville domain, which is neither a product of lower dimensional manifolds nor a cotangent bundle, and obtained new results on Bridgeland stability conditions on Fukaya categories of six-dimensional symplectic manifolds. In fact, the above geometric Fourier-Mukai—type functors were constructed explicitly only on Lagrangian sections of SYZ fibrations, which are mirror to holomorphic line bundles on the toric Calabi-Yau manifold. This was sufficient for our purpose because in those cases Lagrangian sections do split generate the wrapped Fukaya category. However, this may not be the case in higher dimensions or outside the toric world. This is one of the motivations for initiating the study of SYZ transforms for Lagrangian multi-sections in the current project. In a joint work with Suen, the PI studied SYZ transforms of Lagrangian multi-sections in a semi-flat Lagrangian torus fibration (or SYZ fibration). Our starting point was an investigation on the relation between Lagrangian surgery of a pair of straight lines in a symplectic 2-torus and extension of holomorphic vector bundles over the mirror elliptic curve, via the SYZ transform for immersed Lagrangian multi-sections. This study led to a new notion of equivalence between objects in the immersed Fukaya category of a general compact symplectic manifold, under which the immersed Floer cohomology is invariant; in particular, we gave an answer to a question of Akaho-Joyce. Furthermore, we proved, under some additional assumptions, that this new equivalence is mirror to isomorphism between holomorphic vector bundles over the dual torus fibration via the SYZ transform. The second objective of this project was to explore geometric consequences of the principle “HMS is realized by SYZ”. In another joint work with Suen, the PI applied the guiding principle “HMS is realized by SYZ” to solve the so-called “invariance of polarization” problem in geometric quantization. In geometric quantization, one needs to choose a polarization on a prequantized symplectic manifold in order to define the quantum Hilbert space, which is constructed as the space of polarized sections. The “invariance of polarization” problem is asking whether the quantum Hilbert space is independent of such a choice. We observe that, in the case of a semi-flat Calabi-Yau manifold equipped with a semi-flat Lagrangian torus fibration, where we have both a natural complex polarization and a natural real polarization, applying the SYZ transform twice produces a canonical identification between the space of real polarized sections and that of complex polarized sections. In this way, we gave a new method to solve the “invariance of polarization” problem in two cases: 1) semi-flat Lagrangian torus fibrations over complete compact integral affine manifolds, and 2) projective toric manifolds. The third objective of this project was to investigate the precise correspondence between geometric structures via SYZ transforms and seek possible geometric applications. In a joint work with Suen and Ma, we initiated the study of the reconstruction problem for higher rank vector bundles over Calabi-Yau manifolds. More precisely, we restrict ourselves to the two-dimensional setting. We introduced the notion of tropical Lagrangian multi-sections over a two-dimensional integral affine manifold with singularities, and used them to study the reconstruction problem for higher rank locally free sheaves over Calabi-Yau surfaces. This study was based on the algebraic framework for smoothing degenerate Calabi-Yau varieties and pairs developed in earlier joint works of the PI with Leung and Ma. The main advantage of this approach is that now we can go beyond the semi-flat case and allow SYZ fibrations to admit singular fibers. The price to pay is that now we cannot expect very explicit constructions of the functors; the moral is that explicit correspondences via SYZ transforms can only be seen in the large structure limits. Nevertheless, we were still able to find some easily checkable combinatorial conditions which can guarantee smoothability of a pair consisting of a locally free sheaf over a maximally degenerate Calabi-Yau surface coming from some tropical Lagrangian multi-sections. We expect that, under the same conditions, these tropical Lagrangian multi-sections should arise as certain “tropical limits” of genuine Lagrangian multi-sections on the mirror side. Also, there should be more concrete correspondence between the geometric properties/structures on the two sides. We plan to address these problems in a subsequent project.

Investigate the precise correspondence between geometric structures via SYZ transforms and seek possible geometric applications.

14302617.label: Major findings and research outcome
14302617.value: The first major finding in this project is the rich geometry provided by SYZ transforms of Lagrangian multi-sections. On the one hand, this is not surprising because Lagrangian multi-sections are mirror to higher rank holomorphic vector bundles, which are known to have very rich structures and play many important roles in numerous different subjects in geometry. On the other hand, using SYZ transforms, we saw in this project how one can extract very useful geometric information from the correspondence between Lagrangian multi-sections and their mirrors. Our results illustrate how SYZ transforms can help to reveal delicate information hidden in the HMS equivalences, and even structures which are beyond the reach of HMS. The second major finding is the way how SYZ transforms could be applied to geometric problems that are outside the realm of mirror symmetry. In this project we showed how this can lead to a solution of the “invariance of polarization” problem in geometric quantization. This is indeed quite natural because Kähler geometry, or more precisely Calabi-Yau geometry, is a common starting point for mirror symmetry and geometric quantization. Our results have opened up an entirely new direction about the relation between mirror symmetry and quantization. We expect to see further and deeper results along this direction, as well as more applications in other contexts. The third major finding is the incorporation of the algebraic framework for smoothing degenerate Calabi-Yau varieties developed earlier by the PI with Leung and Ma with the geometry of SYZ transforms. In this project, we showed how that framework can be applied to construct smoothable locally free sheaves over maximally degenerate Calabi-Yau surfaces from tropical Lagrangian multi-sections over two-dimensional integral affine manifolds with singularities. The latter are expected to arise as tropical limits of genuine Lagrangian multi-sections on the mirror side. The correspondence between locally free sheaves over maximally degenerate Calabi-Yau surfaces and tropical Lagrangian multi-sections can be understood by SYZ transforms, and by combining with smoothing techniques, we can establish geometric correspondences in mirror symmetry even when the SYZ fibrations admit singular fibers.

14302617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14302617.value: This project has led to many future research directions. We would first like to further investigate the relation between mirror symmetry and quantization. Indeed, the PI has initiated another series of works with Leung and Li about using geometric methods to study quantization of Kähler manifolds. We hope to link these with the work reported here in future projects. Another direction is to continue our study of the smoothing problem for degenerate pairs. One question is to find a proper formulation of the deformation problem. From examples and special cases, we know that one should specify certain extra structures on the locally free sheaves (analogous to log structures on degenerate Calabi-Yau varieties) in order to get a well-behaved deformation problem. This problem will be taken up in another project. On the other hand, we also plan to explore the analogue of scattering diagrams in the case of pairs. Recall that consistent scattering diagrams play a key role in the solution of the reconstruction problem by Kontsevich-Soibelman and Gross-Siebert. It is natural to ask if these tropical objects have analogues in the case of pairs. We plan to study this problem in the near future.

14302617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14302617.value: Mirror symmetry is a highly nontrivial and mysterious duality between the symplectic geometry of a space and the complex geometry of a completely different space. It was discovered by string theorists in the early 1990s. It has led to numerous surprising and deep mathematical conjectures. Since its discovery, mathematicians have been working very hard to try to understand the mechanism of mirror symmetry. A breakthrough came in 1996 when Strominger, Yau and Zaslow proposed that mirror symmetry should be understood as a geometric Fourier-type transform. Lying at the heart of the SYZ conjecture is the role played by quantum corrections, which is the key to explain the miraculous power of mirror symmetry. This research project studied the constructions and applications of the aforementioned geometric Fourier-type transforms, known as SYZ transforms. We showed how one could use these transforms to understand the correspondences between geometric structures on the mirror spaces. Our results have shed new light on the geometry of mirror symmetry. We have also demonstrated how our new techniques can be applied to problems that lie even beyond the realm of mirror symmetry.

14302817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302817.value: We aim to develop the global well-posedness theory of the Boltzmann equation for initial data which are allowed to have large oscillations around global Maxwellians. We first treat the Cauchy problem either in the whole space and in the periodic box, and then deal with the initial-boundary value problem on general bounded domains. We take into account the general intermolecular potentials under the Grad's angular cutoff assumption including the full range of hard and soft cases. For the IBVP, we consider different types of boundary conditions, including diffuse reflection or specular reflection or their convex combination Maxwell boundary. The Boltzmann equation is fundamental for describing the motion of the rarefied gas in the collisional kinetic theory. The global well-posedness is one of the basic problems in the mathematical analysis of such integro-differential evolution equation with the interplay between free transportation and collision relaxation. For general large initial data, after the original studies by Carleman and Arkeryd in the spatially homogeneous setting, the renormalized global inhomogeneous solution was first constructed by DiPerna and Lions, and uniqueness of such solutions has remained unknown. A well-established regime for global existence is that initial data are in the small neighborhood of vacuum or equilibrium states. Particularly, since the pioneering work by Ukai, perturbative solutions around global Maxwellians have been extensively studied by Guo and many others. Indeed, the oscillations of those solutions need to be small enough due to the nonlinear feature of Boltzmann collisions, and thus vacuum is not initially allowed. How to remove such restriction in order to treat more general initial data is our concern of the project. We expect to develop new mathematical estimates to realize the global dynamics of the Boltzmann equation for a class of initial data which are close to global Maxwellians in an integrable space but can still have large oscillations. Moreover, we expect the current project to shed some light on the connections between different kinds of global existence theories for the fully nonlinear Boltzmann equation. 本項目旨在發展帶大振盪初值的玻爾茲曼方程的整體適定性理論。我們首先處理全空間或週期域上的柯西問題，然後考察一般有界域上的初邊值問題。我們考慮帶角截斷的廣泛的分子間相互作用位勢，包括所有硬的和軟的情形。對於初邊值問題，我們考慮不同類型的邊界條件，包括漫反射、鏡面反射或它們的凸組合麥克斯韋邊界。 玻爾茲曼方程乃碰撞動理學中描述稀薄氣體運動的基礎。對於這類具有自由運輸和碰撞鬆弛兩者相互作用的積分微分發展方程，整體適定性是其數學分析中的一個基本問題。對於一般的大的初始值，在Carleman和Arkeryd研究了空間齊次解之後，非齊次方程的重整化整體解首先是由DiPerna和Lions構造的，但這類解的唯一性仍未知。對於比較完善的非齊次整體存在性理論，一個框架是初值處於真空或平衡態的小鄰域內。特別地，自Ukai的開創性工作之後，在整體麥克斯韋附近的擾動解已得到Guo和許多其他學者的廣泛研究。事實上，基於玻爾茲曼碰撞算子的非線性，方程整體解的振盪通常需要足夠小，並且初值也通常不允許含有真空，如何移除這種限制從而處理更廣泛的初值是本項目研究的出發點。我們期望考慮一類在可積空間中靠近整體麥克斯韋分佈但仍能有大的振盪的初值，通過發展新的數學估計建立新的玻爾茲曼方程的整體適定性理論。同時, 我們也期望本項目能對非線性玻爾茲曼方程的不同類型的整體存在性理論之間的聯繫提供一些理解。

14302817.label: Realisation of objectives
14302817.value: The first objective is to justify the large-time behavior of solutions to the Cauchy problem with large-amplitude initial data in the case of the whole space, particularly for soft potentials. In an early work "Global Well-Posedness of the Boltzmann Equation with Large Amplitude Initial Data" [Arch. Rational Mech. Anal. 225 (2017)], we first started to introduce a class of large-amplitude global solutions to the cutoff Boltzmann equation in torus or in the whole space where the collision kernel can be either hard or soft potentials in the full range. The main observation is that smallness of solutions in an integrable function space may propagate in time so that the solutions are still allowed to have concentration in space variables and hence the large-amplitude becomes possible. There are two kinds of ways to treat the propagation of space integrability. One is to use the usual power-law function space and the other, more realistic and more useful, is to use the relative entropy of solutions with respect to global Maxwellians. For the latter, the relative entropy is small globally in time and for the former, the power-law norm, for instance, energy norm, is small up to any finite time. Such general strategy has proved to be very useful for understanding the global large-amplitude dynamics of the Boltzmann equation in other physical situations. To proceed the project, we firstly focus on the Boltzmann equation in bounded domains. Our first research work concerns the motion of rarefied gases in a bounded domain governed by the angular cutoff Boltzmann equation with diffuse reflection boundary. As the project planned to handle, we mainly study the effect of soft intermolecular interaction upon the long-time dynamics of solutions to the corresponding initial boundary value problem in the case when non-isothermal wall temperature occurs. Specifically, we are devoted to proving the existence and dynamical stability of stationary solutions whenever the boundary temperature has suitably small variations around a positive constant. For the proof of existence, we introduce a new mild formulation of solutions to the steady boundary-value problem along the speeded backward bicharacteristics, and develop the uniform estimates on approximate solutions in the energy norm and the supremum norm. Such mild formulation proves to be useful for treating the steady problem with soft potentials even over unbounded domains. In showing the dynamical stability, a new point is that we can obtain the sub-exponential time-decay rate in the supremum norm without losing any velocity weight, which is actually quite different from the classical results by Caflisch for the torus domain and essentially due to the diffuse reflection boundary and the boundedness of the domain. To consider the large time behavior of solutions to the Boltzmann equation for soft potentials in the whole space, we focus on the asymptotics toward non-trivial rarefaction waves with macroscopic fluid quantities determined by the Euler solutions. In the meantime, we consider the physically more realistic collision kernel, that's the long-range interaction with angular singularity exposing the velocity diffusion. As the first step, we study the case of the Landau equation with Coulomb potentials because the analogous results for the non-cutoff Boltzmann can be obtained in a similar way. Indeed, we constructed the global smooth solutions to the three-dimensional Landau equation with a self-consistent force near one-dimensional local Maxwellians corresponding to the rarefaction waves of the Euler system. Furthermore, we obtained the convergence rate in the vanishing Knudsen number of the solutions to the large-time asymptotic rarefaction waves. The main difficulties in analysis arise from velocity singularity and diffusion of the collision operator. To overcome them, we make use of the Burnett function, the Navier-Stokes dissipation mechanism basing on the macro-micro decomposition, and the combined energy method in terms of perturbations around global and local Maxwellians. We remark that it is very interesting to further extend those works to the situation where the solutions around the asymptotic wave patterns may have large-amplitude. Independent of the above directions, we have also explored a class of large-amplitude solutions to the Boltzmann equation with the total energy increasing to infinity as time goes to infinity. For the problem, we consider the spatially homogeneous Boltzmann equation in the Maxwell molecule case with a constant shearing force. Physically it has been observed that the temperature of the system must tend to infinity exponentially in time due to the shearing motion. We develop a rigorous mathematical analysis to justify the self-similar asymptotics of solutions when the shear strength is small enough. The second objective of this project is to extend the result on the diffuse reflection boundary to other types of boundary conditions including the specular reflection and the Maxwell boundary for both hard and soft potentials. For this objective, in a recent preprint "The Boltzmann equation with large-amplitude initial data and specular reflection boundary condition", we have studied the Boltzmann equation with cutoff hard potentials. We constructed the unique global solution converging with an exponential rate in large time to global Maxwellians not only for the specular reflection boundary condition with the bounded convex smooth domain but also for a class of large amplitude initial data where the supremum norm with a suitable velocity weight can be arbitrarily large but the relative entropy need to be small. A key point in the proof is to introduce a delicate nonlinear iterative process of estimating the gain term basing on the triple Duhamel iteration along the linearized dynamics. In the classical bootstrap argument by Guo for the specular reflection boundary condition, it is crucial to derive the nondegeneracy condition except for some small regions in phase space, when the double Duhamel iteration is applied. However, it is hard to obtain such condition because of the complicated trajectory form. In an early work by Kim and Lee, the main idea was to introduce the triple Duhamel iteration for ensuring another kind of the nondegeneracy condition. Such condition can be verified using some idea of the geometric decomposition of particle trajectory, so a unique global mild solution can be constructed and converges exponentially to zero in large time when initial data is small enough in the velocity-weighted supremum norm. This strongly implies that one may need to perform the Duhamel iteration thrice to make a proper change of variables and bound it by the power-law norm so that the large-amplitude solutions can be expected. However, one cannot directly make use of the same idea as in the diffuse reflection boundary case. In particular, the previous Gronwall argument fails. To overcome the difficulty, we have developed a new nonlinear iteration procedure to close the a priori estimates under the smallness of relative entropy.

14302817.label: Major findings and research outcome
14302817.value: 1. We have made an extensive study of the Boltzmann equation in bounded domains with diffuse reflection boundary conditions, see the research papers including items No. 1, No. 2 and No. 7 in Section 8 of Part C. We can treat three physical situations: a) The wall temperature is variable; b) The wall temperature can be time-periodic near a constant; c) The rarefied gas is contained between two infinite parallel plates with opposite velocities along the tangent direction. In those situations, we established the global existence and large time behavior of solutions to the IBVP on the Boltzmann equation. In particular, in the article No. 1, we have fully explored the effect of soft potentials on the global dynamics with an extra consideration that solutions can be of large-amplitude. 2. We have studied the large-amplitude solutions to the Boltzmann equation in bounded domains with specular reflection boundary conditions, see the research paper Item No. 6 in Section 8 of Part C. We developed a new iteration procedure to treat the nonlinear estimates and obtained the global existence of solutions. Note that the problem is much harder for specular reflection than in case of diffuse reflection since solutions expose more singular behavior in the former case. 3. We have further studied the effect of soft interactions on the global dynamics near some non-trivial asymptotic profiles such as rarefaction waves, see the research papers including Items No. 3 and No. 4 in Section 8 of Part C. We focused on the long range interaction with angular singularity. In particular, we studied the Landau equation with Coulomb potentials as the first step so that the analogous results could be expected for the Boltzmann equation without cutoff. 4. We have studied a class of global solutions to the spatially homogeneous Boltzmann equation that admit a finite kinetic energy tending to infinity with an exponential rate, see the research paper Item No. 5 in Section 8 of Part C. Such solutions turn out to be in non equilibrium states and of large amplitude in temperature. We proved the self-similar asymptotics of smooth solutions when the shear strength is small enough.

14302817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14302817.value: Regarding the large-amplitude global solutions around global Maxwellians, it is still challenging to treat the mixed Maxwell boundary condition although we have resolved the problem in either diffuse reflection or specular reflection. More importantly, it is extremely interesting to explore the global existence of large-amplitude solutions in other kinds of situations, such as the angular non-cutoff and the function space involves only the integrability in both space and velocity variables in order to understand the uniqueness of solutions with large data by DiPerna and Lions. In the meantime, it is expected that the method and techniques this project developed could be adopted to deal with other kinetic models for large-amplitude solutions, for instance, it is interesting to consider this problem on the Vlasov-Poisson-Boltzmann system for which a self-consistent force appears and this makes the analysis more subtle.

14302817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14302817.value: The global well-posedness for the Boltzmann equation is one of the basic problems in kinetic theory. For general large initial data, the renormalized global inhomogeneous solution was first constructed by DiPerna and Lions with uniqueness unknown so far. A well-established regime for global existence is that initial data are in the small neighborhood of equilibrium states due to the pioneering work by Ukai. Indeed, the oscillations of those solutions are required to be small enough. How to remove such restriction in order to treat more general initial data is our concern of the project. We have developed new mathematical estimates to realize the global dynamics of the Boltzmann equation for a class of initial data which are close to global Maxwellians in an integrable space but can still have large oscillations. It is expected that the current project can shed some light on the connections between different kinds of global existence theories for the fully nonlinear Boltzmann equation.

14302917.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14302917.value: 關於俱全向或水平粘性而無任何擴散本構方程之弱解及強解

14302917.label: Project Objectives
14302917.value: One of the main objectives of this project is to establish the global existence of weak solutions to the PEs with full or horizontal viscosity but without any diffusivity. In the real atmospheric dynamics, due to the existence of discontinuous waves, the solutions are not necessary to be regular enough, and thus mathematically one has to deal with the PEs with weak initial data, while weak solutions are those that can exist globally under the most weak conditions on the initial data. The other main objective of this project is to establish the local and global well-posedness of strong solutions to the PEs with full viscosity but without any diffusivity. To identify if heat conduction is necessary or not for globally stabilizing the flow of the oceanic and atmospheric dynamics, one has to look for such solutions that enjoy both existence and uniqueness, while strong solutions are those that meet both. We will also pay attentions to the conditions as weak as possible on the initial data, under which the uniqueness holds.

14302917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302917.value: The core models for the large-scale atmospheric and oceanic dynamics are the primitive equations (PEs), which are derived from the Navier-Stokes equations by applying the Boussinesq and hydrostatic approximations. Physically, for the large-scale ocean and atmosphere, the strong horizonal turbulence creates the eddy viscosity in the horizontal direction, which leads to the PEs with horizontal viscosity. It has been known that the PEs with full or horizontal viscosity and full or either horizontal or vertical viscosity are globally well-posed, as long as the initial data is appropriately regular; however, it is still unknown if the PEs with full or horizontal viscosity but without any diffusivity are globally well-posed. In this project, we propose to study some basic problems on the PEs with full or horizontal viscosity but without any diffusivity. We will focus on two problems: one is the global existence of weak solutions, and the other one is the local and global well-posedness of strong solutions. 本構方程組是大尺度大氣海洋動力學模型中的核心組成部分。它是通過對Navier-Stokes方程組作Boussinesq逼近以及靜水力學逼近而得到。物理上，由於大氣中存在著的水平方向上的強湍流混合會對空氣產生水平粘滯效應，我們通常考慮的本構方程組含有水平粘滯項。現有的文獻已經證明，帶全向或水平粘滯項的本構方程組是整體適定的，只要方程組中還帶有水平或豎直方向的熱擴散項；然而，對帶全向或水平粘滯項，而無任何擴散項的本構方程組而言，我們仍不清楚它是否整體適定。在本研究計劃中，我們將對帶全向或者水平粘滯項，而無任何擴散項的本構方程進行研究。我們將主要考慮兩個問題：（一）弱解的整體存在性；（二）強解的局部或整體存在唯一性。

The other main objective of this project is to establish the local and global well-posedness of strong solutions to the PEs with full viscosity but without any diffusivity. To identify if heat conduction is necessary or not for globally stabilizing the flow of the oceanic and atmospheric dynamics, one has to look for such solutions that enjoy both existence and uniqueness, while strong solutions are those that meet both. We will also pay attentions to the conditions as weak as possible on the initial data, under which the uniqueness holds.

14302917.label: Major findings and research outcome
14302917.value: (i) Rigorously justified the convergence from the Navier-Stokes equations to the primitive equations, in both the isotropic and anisotropic settings. In particular, this proves that the hydrostatic balance is an accurate approximation for the large scale oceanic flow, from the mathematical point of view. It turns out that for both cases, the convergences are strong though with different convergence rates. It is discovered that there are essential differences between the isotropic case and the anisotropic case at the following aspects: (i) sharp contrasting to what we expected, the convergence rate in the anisotropic case does not approach the rate in the isotropic case, when the anisotropic parameter approaches isotropic value; (ii) in the isotropic case, the convergence can be globally in time or in other words uniformly in all time, while in the isotropic case, the convergence depends also in time, thought the strong convergence holds up to any finite time. These results have been published in JMPA [1]. (ii) As a byproduct of strong convergences stated in the above, for both the isotropic and anisotropic cases, it is discovered that if the aspect ratio is sufficiently, then the local strong solutions to the scaled Navier-Stokes equations are actually globally in time. This is also reported in [1]. (iii) Established the global well-posedness of strong solutions to the primitive equations that with horizontal viscosity and vertical diffusivity. Some a priori estimates independent of the diffusivity and being finite up to any finite time were also achieved. Established the global well-posedness of z-weak solutions to the primitive equations that with full viscosities but with only horizontal diffusivity. This extensively weaken the regularity assumptions on the initial data required in the previous work. These results have been published in [10, 11]. (iv) Established the local and global well-posedness of strong solutions with arbitrary large initial data to the full compressible Navier-Stokes equations with or without heat conductivity, and if considering the Cauchy problem and if the initial density contains vacuum at the far fields only with a decaying rate not more than 1/x^2, then the entropy can be uniformly bounded up to any finite time. In the one-dimensional case, the initial data can be arbitrary large, while for the multidimensional case, one needs the smallness on some quantities of the initial data. These results have been published in Advance in Math. and CPAM [2, 13]. (v) Some related problems have been solved successfully. These include global qualitative behavior of compressible Navier-Stokes equation, transonic flows in general nozzles, vacuum dynamics jet flows, and interface problems for both viscous incompressible and incompressible inviscid resistive magneto-hydrodynamics, and transonic shocks. Some important problems such as Meyer type smooth transonic flow in a De Naval nozzle and Courant-Friedrich transonic shocks in a 2-dimensional general nozzle have been established. We also give the first global existence of plasma-vacuum interface for inviscid impressible MHD with resistivity. These results have been published in [3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 12, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22].

14302917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14302917.value: The outcomes of this project will be the basis to study the coupled system of the primitive equations with the moisture system for the large scale atmospheric dynamics.

14302917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14302917.value: The research of this project indicates by giving rigorous mathematical proofs that the hydrostatic balance is a accurate approximation in the practice use of the geophysics, as long as we work on the horizontal large scale oceanic or atmospheric dynamics.

14303017.label: Project Objectives
14303017.value: To establish a novel semiparametric HMLVM for analyzing multivariate longitudinal data with latent variables. The proposed model comprises two major components. The first component is a semiparametric continuation-ratio logit transition model for investigating how potential covariates linearly or functionally influence the probabilities of transition from one hidden state to another. The second component is a conditional latent variable model that includes a measurement equation for characterizing latent variables through multiple observed indicators and a nonparametric structural equation for examining the functional effects of the explanatory observable and latent variables on the outcome latent variables. Several useful extensions of the proposed model will also be developed to cope with the circumstances wherein missingness exist or the number of latent variables and their indicators are unknown. To develop novel and sound statistical methods for estimation and model/variable selection. Bayesian approaches, coupled with Bayesian versions of penalized splines, linear basis expansions, and Lasso-type procedures, as well as various efficient sampling schemes, will be developed to conduct the statistical inference. Moreover, we will explore feasible and computationally efficient procedures to determine the number of hidden states in the proposed model. To develop efficient computer programs for producing accurate results and post these programs onto freely available websites for general use. We will try our best to make the codes user-friendly through freely available software, such as R. To apply the developed methodologies in the analysis of real datasets relevant to Hong Kong and elsewhere.

14303017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14303017.value: Hidden Markov models (HMMs) describe the relationship between two stochastic processes: an observed process and an unobservable finite-state transition process. Owing to their modeling dynamic heterogeneity, HMMs are widely used to analyze heterogeneous longitudinal data. Early developments in HMMs mainly focused on parametric models. One problem of parametric modeling is that its limited flexibility can cause important features, such as functional associations among variables, to be missed. A more comprehensive approach is to model such associations in a nonparametric manner. However, no existing work addresses functional associations in the HMM framework. Moreover, existing HMMs often assume that each variable is fully observable despite the existence of latent variables that are indirectly observable and should be characterized by multiple indicators from different perspectives. Given the popularity of such latent variables in medical, behavioral, social, and psychological research settings, investigating a longitudinally observed process with latent variables and its dynamic heterogeneity is both of scientific interest from a methodological standpoint and of practical value in real applications. Nevertheless, available works in this direction are very limited and restricted only to parametric models with the maximum likelihood (ML) analysis. Owing to the huge challenge confronting ML-based procedures in estimating the nonparametric functions of latent variables, developing sound Bayesian inference methods for the aforementioned advancement becomes necessary and important. To the best of our knowledge, this study is the first to introduce nonparametric modeling together with latent variables into HMMs and conduct a full Bayesian analysis in the HMM framework. This study aims to develop semiparametric hidden Markov latent variable models for the analysis of multivariate longitudinal data with latent variables. The models comprise two major components. The first component is a semiparametric transition model for investigating how potential covariates linearly or functionally influence the probabilities of transitioning from one hidden state to another. The second component is a semiparametric conditional latent variable model that includes a parametric measurement equation for characterizing latent variables through multiple observed indicators, as well as a nonparametric structural equation for examining the functional effects of explanatory observable and latent variables on the outcome latent variables. Several useful extensions are also considered, and Bayesian methods for estimation and model selection are developed. Efficient and user-friendly computer programs are likewise developed to produce statistical results. These computer programs will be made freely available for practitioners. 14303017.label: Realisation of objectives
14303017.value: We have fully achieved the project objectives specified in the proposal: 1. We have established novel semiparametric HMLVMs for analyzing multivariate longitudinal data with latent variables. The proposed model comprises two major components. The first component is a semiparametric continuation-ratio logit transition model for investigating how potential covariates linearly or functionally influence transition probabilities from one hidden state to another. The second component is a conditional latent variable model that includes a measurement equation for characterizing latent variables through multiple observed indicators and a nonparametric structural equation for examining the functional effects of the explanatory observable and latent variables on the outcome latent variables. In addition, several useful extensions of the proposed model have been developed to cope with the circumstances wherein missingness exists or the number of latent variables and their indicators are unknown. The objective in Item 1 of Section 5.2 (related to the model establishment) is fully achieved. 2. We have developed novel and sound statistical methods for estimation and model/variable selection. Bayesian approaches, coupled with Bayesian versions of penalized splines, linear basis expansions, and Lasso-type procedures, as well as various efficient sampling schemes, have been developed to conduct the statistical inference. Moreover, we have developed feasible and computationally efficient procedures to determine the number of hidden states in the proposed model. The objectives in Item 2 of Section 5.2 (related to inference methodology) are fully achieved. 3. We have developed efficient computer programs for producing accurate results and posted these programs onto freely available websites for general use and made the codes user-friendly through freely available software, such as R, Rcpp, and Python. The objectives in Item 3 of Section 5.2 (related to computer programs) are fully achieved. 4. We have applied the developed methodologies to analyze many real datasets relevant to Hong Kong and elsewhere. The real-life applications include, but are not limited to, (1) type 2 diabetes and its complications data collected by the Prince of Wales Hospital at the Chinese University of Hong Kong, (2) the Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative data, (3) drug abuse data collected by the UCLA drug abuse center, (4) the medical cost study data for chronic heart failure patients from the University of Virginia Health System, (5) bladder tumor data, (6) studies on the National Longitudinal Surveys of Youth in the US, (7) financial and business datasets, and (8) Chinese air pollution and meteorological dataset. The objectives in Item 4 of Section 5.2 (related to applications) are fully achieved.

14303017.label: Major findings and research outcome
14303017.value: Our major findings and research outcomes are represented by 15 publications (see “Research outputs” in Section 8 of Part C). Specifically, 1. We have established novel semiparametric hidden Markov latent variable models (HMLVMs) to analyze multivariate longitudinal data with latent variables, such as hidden Markov structural equation models for multivariate longitudinal data, Bayesian semiparametric HMMs, and HMLVMs with an unknown number of hidden states. Please refer to Items 1, 3, 4, 7, and 8 in Section 8. In addition, we have developed many useful extensions of the proposed model to cope with complex circumstances. In particular, we have extended the proposed model to continuous-time HMMs to deal with continuously and irregularly collected multivariate longitudinal data, two-part HMMs to accommodate semicontinuous longitudinal data, HMMs with missing responses and/or covariates, quantile HMMs, HMMs with unknown numbers of hidden states and latent variables, and functional concurrent HMMs. Please refer to Items 1, 6, 7, 8, 9, and 15 in Section 8. 2. We have developed novel and sound statistical methods for estimation and model/variable selection. In particular, we have developed various Bayesian and frequentist techniques for nonparametric approximation and variable selection in the HMM framework, including penalized splines, linear basis expansions, and Lasso-type procedures. Please refer to Items 2, 4, 5, 8, 11, 12, 13, 14, and 15 in Section 8. In addition, we have proposed feasible and computationally efficient procedures to determine the number of hidden states and important risk factors. Please refer to Items 6, 8, and 11. 3. We have developed efficient computer programs for producing accurate results. All the computer codes have been published or provided on websites that are freely accessible to practitioners (see the corresponding papers in Section 8). 4. We have applied the developed methodologies to analyze many real datasets relevant to Hong Kong and elsewhere. 14303017.value: The models considered in this project can be extended to incorporate functional data. Although such an extension is out of this project's scope, we have considered this vital extension and submitted a paper to a prestigious international journal "Statistics and Computing." 14303017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14303017.value: Hidden Markov models (HMMs) describe the relationship between two stochastic processes: an observed process and an unobservable finite-state transition process. Early developments in HMMs mainly focused on parametric models and assumed that each variable is fully observable and the number of hidden states is known. This project proposed a semiparametric hidden Markov latent variable model and its various extensions to analyze complex multivariate longitudinal data with latent variables. Compared with the conventional HMMs, the newly proposed model and its variants can reveal functional interrelationships among longitudinal variables and accommodate different types of complex data. The models considered in this project are original and applicable to various problems in medical, behavioral, social, and psychological research settings. The novel methods developed in this project have addressed the most challenging issues in the HMM framework, such as nonparametric modeling, the presence of missing data, and order and variable selection, and thus contribute significantly to the field of complex longitudinal data analysis. The applications of the developed methodologies have produced important findings and new insights into vital problems in different research areas. A total of 15 publications in international journals represent the primary outputs. Some extensions of the proposed methods beyond the project objectives have also been considered.

14303317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14303317.value: 少體問題在很多不同能量尺度的物理體系中都是很普遍的，包括核物理，生物物理以及原子分子物理。普遍來講，即便對看似簡單的有相互作用的三體問題，解析解已經很難得到，但Efimov效應是一個特例。在三個粒子的體系中，當每兩個粒子間的相互作用都接近共振時，系統中會有無窮序列的被稱之為Efimov三聚體的三體束縛態，而且，這些束縛態的能量和尺寸都呈嚴格的對數關係，即對每一個Efimov三聚體，總會有另外一個大一定的因子的Efimov三聚體存在。Efimov在1970年就預言了這一效應，但直到2006年才在冷原子體系中第一次觀測到。 在本課題中，我們計劃利用相互作用可調的銣原子和鈉原子的超冷混合物研究異核三體Efimov效應並研究將Efimov效應擴展到異核四體問題。對這些問題的研究目前尚處於早期，特別是異核的四體問題還沒有實驗數據，而理論上還有很多的爭議，我們的實驗將提供釐清這些問題的依據。我們的實驗工作將在一套現有的平台上進行，而且目前已經觀測到了一些初步的結果。我們相信這一工作不僅對理解冷原子體系中的少體問題有很大幫助，也會為將Efimov效應擴展到其他體系從而對整個少體問題的發展提供重要的提示。

14303317.label: Realisation of objectives
14303317.value: The main purpose of this project is to investigate few-body physics with an ultracold Na and Rb Bose-Bose quantum gas mixture. Although the few-body problems have been studied in ultracold systems for a while, the special case of heteronuclear Bose-Bose mixture with imbalanced masses has not been investigated carefully. This project is based on the previous works supported by RGC in which we have successfully prepared the double Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) mixture of Na and Rb with tunable interactions. There are four objectives in this project. All of them have been successfully addressed. Based on these investigations, several papers have been published or are under review. 1. Technical improvement of the apparatus: Since most of the interesting few-body features, including the 3-atom Efimov resonate, the atom-dimer resonance and the dimer-dimer resonance, are scattering length, thus magnetic field dependent, it is very import to make the B field as stable as possible. In our previous setup, the field stability is ~10 mG at 350 G. When the B field is tuned to near resonance, the B field noise will induce a large scattering length fluctuation. To mitigate this problem, we developed a new magnetic field control system which reduced the instability to 1 mG at 350 G. In this system, a high precision voltage, a 20-bit DAC and a low-noise feedback circuit are used. Previously, the ultracold atomic mixture was co-trapped by a crossed-beam 1070 nm optical dipole trap. At this wavelength, the trap frequencies of Na and Rb are different by about 10%. As a result, the gravity causes some differential sag which separates the center of mass of the two clouds. At large positive scattering lengths, the repulsive interaction further pushes the two clouds away from each other and diminishes the signal. The problem was solved by transferring the atoms to a 946 nm laser trap after the evaporative cooling in the 1070 nm trap. At 946 nm, the two atomic species have the same trap frequencies and the same gravity sag. Their COMs always locate at the same position. Since a commercial 946 nm laser is too expensive (~ 30,000 USD), we had to build the laser by ourselves with a tapered amplifier. 2. Dimer-dimer resonance: After the technical improvements, we continued the investigation on the dimer-dimer collisions as showed as preliminary results in the proposal. We mapped out the dimer-dimer resonance more carefully and confirmed the absence of 3-body loss. In addition, we also studied the collisional energy dependence by tuning the temperature of the dimer samples. It was found that the collision rates are non-universal near the dimer-dimer resonance. Our results represent the first systematic study of the collisions between heteronuclear Feshbach molecules. The observation and characterization of the dimer-dimer resonance will provide great help in understanding the 4-body system of different masses. A paper is published in Phys. Rev. A 100, 042706 (2019). 3. High-field detection of Feshbach molecules: For probing the dimer-dimer resonance in situ, we developed a new way of detecting the Feshbach molecules. This method relies on photodissociation and the subsequent detection of the Na and/or Rb fragments. To this end, we first carried out a spectroscopic investigation on the photodissociation path and found the Na 5p3/2 is a better excited-state dissociation limit. We calibrated the heating issue induced by the near threshold dissociation process and developed a reliable protocol to extract both the number and temperature of the molecular sample. This work was published in Phys. Rev. A 102, 043327(2020) . 4. Precise calibration of the Feshbach resonance: For many of the few- and many-body investigations, to perform a rigorous comparison between experiment and theory, it is necessary to know the conversion between magnetic field and scattering length precisely. In the aforementioned studies, we have noticed the calibration of the 347.64 Feshbach resonance parameters is not accurate enough. In this work, we carried out a high precision calibration of this resonance by measuring the binding energy of the Feshbach molecules. Combined with the coupled channel calculation, we obtained a new and more accurate calibration of this Feshbach resonance. In addition, we also observed 10 more s-wave resonances which may find applications in future investigations. We wrote up a paper for this work which is now under review. 5. Three- and four-body resonances: We also searched for 3-body and 4-body collision resonances between Na and Rb atoms. With the improved magnetic field stability and resolution, we were able to reach within 20 mG of the 347.64 G resonance or Na-Rb scattering length more than -10,000a0. However, even in this region, we didn’t observe any Efimov features. This was understood from our theoretical collaborator Prof. Blume’s modeling. Due to the relatively small mass ratio between Rb and Na, even the favored first RbRbNa 3-body Efimov resonance will occur at very large scattering length. To observe this, we thus need samples with temperature <50 nK to extend the window of universality. On the other hand, according to the calculation, a 4-body resonance could happen within the range already covered in the experiment, but we didn’t observe it either. The reason of this is still not clear. 6. We have not finished the trimer binding energy mapping as planned. In the original plan, we will use RF association of atom + Feshbach molecule to create trimers. However, the trimer signal was not observed so far. We have not figured out the exact reason, but most probably, this has to do with the weak coupling between the trimer and the atom + dimer. As the RF intensity is limited, if the transition is too weak, it will become non-observable. Due to time limitation, we decided to leave this part to the further. 7. Other works: Using the double BEC of Na and Rb atoms, we observed the Na-Rb quantum droplet formation when the Na-Rb scattering length is tuned to negative values near the mean-field collapsing region. We also measured the gas to droplet phase transition diagram. This work has just been accepted by Physical Review Research.

14303317.label: Major findings and research outcome
14303317.value: 1. Resonant scattering between weakly bound NaRb Feshbach molecules. This resonance is caused by the crossing of the energy of two NaRb Feshbach molecules with a four-body tetramer. Near this resonance, we also observed the non-Wigner threshold law dependence on temperatures which we attributed to the near resonant effect. This work has been published in Physical Review A 100,042706(2019). 2. Detection of NaRb Feshbach molecules by photodissociation. We developed a method to detect the Feshbach molecule without having to lower the high magnetic field. This capability will enable us to probe molecular dynamics in real time. This work was published in Phys. Rev. A 102, 043327(2020). 3. Measuring of the Feshbach molecule binding energy. We measured the binding energy of Feshbach molecules by the dissociation method. Based on this, we performed a precise calibration of the parameters for the 347.64 G Feshbach resonance. A paper based on this work has been submitted to Physical Review A. 4. Creation of Na-Rb quantum droplet. With the help of the Feshbach resonance, we tune the interspecies interaction between Na and Rb to values negative enough so that the double BEC should collapse in the mean-field picture. Instead, we observed the Na-Rb quantum droplet as a manifestation of the beyond mean-field Lee-Huang-Yang effect. A paper based on this work has been accepted by Physical Review Research.

Especially, influences of the intraspecies interactions should be included in the picture.

14303317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14303317.value: The few-body problem is ubiquitous in many physical systems of vastly different energy scales, ranging from nuclear systems, bio-physics systems to atomic and molecular systems. It is well known that, already for the seemingly simple system of three quantum particles, analytical solutions for few-body problems are hard to obtain except for a few special cases, such as the prominent three-body Efimov effect in the limit of strong two-body interactions. The Efimov effect predicts an infinite series of three-body bound state called Efimov trimers which follow a logarithmic scale invariance, i.e., for each Efimov trimer, there will be another one larger by a scaling factor determined only by the mass ratio of the three particles. Interestingly, although the Efimov effect was originally proposed for the nuclear system, the first experimental observation was on ultracold atoms, which have since become the primary platform for investigating the Efimov effect. In this project, we studied experimentally the heteronuclear three-body Efimov effect and its extension to the heteronuclear four-body processes in an ultracold sodium and rubidium mixture with tunable inter-species interactions. Especially, we observed a dimer-dimer resonance which is caused by a Feshbach like resonance with a 4-body Efimov-like state. Furthermore, together with our theoretical collaborators, we gained a detailed understanding on the 3-body heavy-heavy-light 3-body and 4-body problem of Bose-Bose mixtures. Our work will help to extend the Efimov framework to the Bose-Bose system with imbalanced masses and will deepen our understanding toward a more broad range of few-body problems.

14303417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14303417.value: 石冰川是山地系統的一個重要組成部分，影響高山地貌、水文、和氣候。當山地冰川正在不斷消融的情況下，石冰川的影響很可能越來越顯著。儘管石冰川在中國西部分佈廣泛，但近二十多年來都缺少一個系統的研究。這個空白限制我們對中國區域內多年動土有一個全面理解。 該研究將利用遙感手段來全面研究中國西部主要山脈內石冰川的運動和動力學。我們的研究區域包括天山、崑崙山、唐古拉山、念青唐古拉、和橫斷山脈。我們把合成孔徑雷達干涉和光學影像結合來識別活動的石冰川並且將它們編目。基於該編目，我們可以定量分析石冰川發育的地形和氣候環境，並評估它們對地貌的影響。我們還將選取個別石冰川來研究它們的運動特徵在時間和空間的變化，並和附近冰川作比較。 該研究將填補中國石冰川研究的空白，完善目前國內外關於多年凍土和冰川的研究。該工作將提供為研究中國山地冰凍圈的一個重要的基本信息，有助於未來長期監測和全區域評估多年凍土在氣候暖化下的變化。

14303417.label: Realisation of objectives
14303417.value: This research project combines the Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar measurements of surface motion and optical imagery to identify active rock glaciers in western China and compile an inventory to describe their occurrence and key kinematic characteristics. Objective 1: Compile an inventory of active rock glaciers in western China by a combined use of InSAR and optical images. (1) Together with the International Permafrost Association Action Group on Rock glacier inventories and kinematics, we have defined a working standard for identifying rock glaciers and related periglacial landforms based on morphological features. These practical guidelines have served as the foundation for inventorying exercises of our kind for the global community. (2) Following the method laid out in the proposal, we have compiled an inventory of active rock glaciers and related periglacial landforms in the West Kunlun Mountain and Poiqu Basin by the combined use of Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) and Google Earth images. We have also quantified the surface velocities of each mapped rock glacier using InSAR. (3) We have also developed a deep-learning-based method that can automatically identify and delineate rock glaciers from remote sensing imagery. Applying such an innovative method to Sentinel-2 and PlanetScope images, we have compiled inventories of rock glaciers in five major mountain ranges across the Tibetan Plateau, including the West Kunlun Mountain, Hunza River Basin, Poiqu, Daxue Mountain, and Nyainqêntanglha Mountains. Objective 2: Conduct multi-temporal remote sensing analysis using both InSAR and optical images to quantify the spatio-temporal changes of movement at selected rock glaciers. (1) We have conducted a comprehensive analysis of the dynamics and runout hazard of a low-angle valley glacier in the East Kunlun Mountains. The changes in morphology, terminus position, and surface elevation of the glacier between 1975 and 2021 were characterized by a stereo-image pair from the historical KH-9 spy satellite, six digital elevation models, and 11 high-resolution PlanetScope images. With a combined analysis of the geomorphic, climatic, and hydrologic conditions of the glacier, we suggest that the flow of the glacier tongue is mainly controlled by the glacier geometry. (2) We have carried out detailed remote sensing and field investigations on the Jingxian Valley periglacial landforms and elucidated their mixing nature of debris-mantled-slope-connected rock glaciers and gelifluction process occurring on the surface as small-scale and discrete events. (3) We have developed an empirical rheological model that links a rock glacier’s surface movement to its ice contents. Our model takes input data, including surface velocities obtained from InSAR measurements, planar shape, and surface slope angle, and is calibrated and validated using observational data from the Chilean Andes and Swiss Alps. We have applied the model to infer the ice content of five rock glaciers in the Khumbu and Lhotse Valleys in northeastern Nepal.

14303417.label: Major findings and research outcome
14303417.value: The project has produced five research papers, one Ph.D. thesis, and 11 conference papers. Please refer to Part C for detailed information. Our major findings are summarized below. Hu et al. (2021) conducted a case study on a puzzling landform near the Kunlun Pass. We employed InSAR to quantify the spatial-temporal variations of the creeping velocities. Based on the kinematic and geomorphic characteristics, we identified the landform as a debris-mantled-slope-connected rock glacier, with gelifluction processes occurring on the surface as small-scale and discrete events. In a paper submitted to Remote Sensing of Environment, we developed a deep-learning-based method for a region-wide, extensive delineation of rock glaciers from Sentinel-2 images to inventory the landforms that were previously missed in the InSAR-based identification. Considering the geomorphologic context, we inferred that the glacier – debris-covered glacier – rock glacier transition is currently inactive due to the abnormal mass gain of glaciers in the region. Wang et al. (2021) employed multi-sensor satellite data, including optical images and digital elevation models derived from spy satellites, Planet and Google Earth, to characterize the morphological changes and dynamics of a low-angle valley glacier near the Kunlun Pass in the past 40 years. The observed changes in the frontal positions, surface elevations and flow velocities suggested that the glacier undergone slow surge-like processes. We also estimated the potential runout distance if a failure of the glacier tongue were to occur in the future and suggested that the avalanche of the whole glacier could easily reach the Qinghai-Tibet railway. In a paper submitted to Geografiska Annaler, we compiled a rock glacier inventory for the Poiqu River basin, Central Himalaya. The mapping was conducted using very high-resolution Pléiades imagery and digital elevation model and imagery available from Google Earth. Rock glaciers were classified either as active or inactive based on InSAR. Our results reveal 370 rock glaciers including 148 active and 222 inactive ones. We found nine rock glaciers damming lakes, three of which could be potentially dangerous. In a paper submitted to The Cryosphere, we estimated the potential water storage of rock glaciers situated by developing a velocity-constrained rheological model to infer their ice contents. The velocity constraints applied to the model were derived from InSAR measurements. The inferred ice fraction of the rock glaciers in Khumbu Valley is about 71%. The total amount of water stored in rock glaciers could be ~10 billion m3 over the Nepalese Himalayas.

14303417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14303417.value: 1. Further development and application of deep-learning methods for automated delineation of rock glaciers. As it has become increasingly labor-intensive and time-consuming to manually identify rock glaciers over vast mountain regions, state-of-the-art deep-learn methods used in computer vision can be adopted for remote sensing tasks of this kind. Building on our successful case studies, we developed a research proposal and were funded by the RGC to pursue this direction. 2. Estimating ice content of rock glaciers. Little is known about the amount of ground ice stored as permafrost and in rock glaciers in western China. We will improve the surface-velocity-constrained numerical model previously developed for the Khumbu Valley rock glaciers for estimating the ice content of rock glaciers over Tibet. We will further evaluate the hydrological significance of active rock glaciers in a warming climate. We have secured an internal seed fund from the CUHK–University of Exeter Joint Centre for Environmental Sustainability & Resilience and will apply RGC funding to pursue this direction.

14303417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14303417.value: Rock glaciers are ice-debris landforms widely distributed in the mountainous periglacial realm worldwide. This project uses satellite remote sensing and deep learning to measure the surface kinematics of rock glaciers and identify their locations and boundaries over the major mountain ranges in Tibet. Our extensive efforts inventoried 369, 513, 649, 370, and 284 rock glaciers in the West Kunlun Mountains, Hunza River Basin, Western Nyainqêntanglha, Poiqu Basin, and Daxue Mountain, respectively, having filled major knowledge gaps about the number and spatial distribution of these landforms in western China. Furthermore, through quantification of kinematic and geomorphological characteristics, we solved a long-standing puzzle about the type of a periglacial landform in the Kunlun Mountain, which is classified as a debris-mantled-slope-connected rock glacier. We estimated rock glacier ice contents from a rheological model and surface velocity measurements. The outcome of this project improves the knowledge of rock glaciers and the permafrost environment in the fast-warming western China.

14303817.label: Realisation of objectives
14303817.value: The central object of investigation in this proposal is Carleson's operator. Its importance lies in the fact that it is one of the simplest modulation invariant operators in harmonic analysis, and the powerful tools developed to tackle this modulation invariance has since flourished into a sub-field called time-frequency (or wave packet) analysis. In our investigation, we are especially interested in the polynomial Carleson operator, the Radon-type Carleson operator, and the Stein-Wainger operator. We manage to prove sharp variation-norm estimates for certain oscillatory integrals related to Carleson’s theorem. Bounds for the corresponding maximal operators were first proven by Stein and Wainger. Our estimates are sharp in the range of exponents, up to endpoints. Such variation-norm estimates have applications to discrete analogues and ergodic theory. The proof made use of various local smoothing and square function estimates for the solution of the Schrodinger equation. The paper above also found applications in discrete harmonic analysis, such as an alternative proof of an earlier result of Krause and Lacey. We also investigate the maximal operators associated with families of Hilbert transforms along non-flat homogeneous curves. 14303817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14303817.value: In 1966, L. Carleson proved a celebrated theorem about pointwise convergence of Fourier series. This result can be reformulated in terms of the boundedness of the so-called Carleson's operator. In our project, we provide some sharp estimations (including the variational norms and Lp norms) on several variants of Carleson's operator (in particular those that involve features of Radon transforms, and certain polynomial phases), by developing techniques in oscillatory integrals and time-frequency analysis. We also provide a short and elementary proof of the l^2 decoupling inequality for some curves. The techniques we developed in this project would pave a way towards a better understanding of wave packet analysis in higher dimensions, and be applicable to other related problems.

14303917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14303917.value: In this proposal we aim to build hydrogel based artificial cells capable of long-live protein expression. We will demonstrate that the artificial cells support synthetic gene networks. We will illustrate the application of the artificial cells by constructing an mRNA biosensor. First, the polyacrylamide hydrogel particles will be prepared in microfluidic devices with uniform size in the range of tens of micrometers. The artificial cells will then be prepared by loading and confining the multiple enzymatic components for protein expression. With the continuous supply of the feeding solution containing the energy source, nutrients, and the DNA template, we expect the artificial cells to be capable of long-live protein expression. Secondly, we will integrate synthetic gene networks in the artificial cells to achieve auto-regulated protein expression. The artificial cells supporting synthetic gene networks will be a useful medium for the safe deployment of engineered gene circuits beyond the constraints of an in vivo environment. Positive feedback and negative feedback auto-regulation of protein expression will be implemented in the artificial cells. 14303917.label: Realisation of objectives
14303917.value: The first objective has been fully realized. We constructed the artificial cells by immobilizing the cell-free transcription and translation proteinaceous factors on the polymer backbone of the hydrogel particles and encapsulating the plasmid template and ribosome inside the hydrogel. The cell-free transcription and translation components remained inside the artificial cells while the feeding nutrients, expression products, and byproducts freely diffused into and out of the artificial cells. By continuously feeding the artificial cells with the nutrients and energy, the protein expression in the artificial cells remained stable for 28 days. The long-lived expression of the artificial cells paves the way in the further work such as the protein expression regulation and gene networks inside the hydrogel-based artificial cells. The second objective has been fully realized. Using the hydrogel-based artificial cells, we built several gene networks. First, we tried simple gene expression regulation based on the lac operon. IPTG was used to regulate the gene expression level inside the artificial cells. The protein expression level changed according to the IPTG concentration in the surrounding buffer. Secondly, the gene oscillator was demonstrated inside the artificial cells. The oscillator was achieved by the negative feedback between the lacI protein and the lac operator. The gene oscillators made the artificial cells capable of the biological rhythm. The third objective has been fully realized. We built more complex gene networks in the hydrogel-based artificial cells for the sensor application. The DNA aptamers were used to form DNA-mRNA complex in the artificial cells and impede the translation of the signaling protein. The mRNA could be released when the analytes bound to the DNA aptamers, then the translation started again. The single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNP) was also used to regulate the protein expression. The wild type and mutant type showed different toehold-mediated strand-displacement efficiency, which led to the difference in the mRNA release level. Accordingly, by measuring the translation level of the signaling protein, the nucleotide mutation in the samples was detected. The sensor has high specificity and sensitivity due to the usage of the aptamer-mRNA complex and the efficient protein synthesis in the hydrogel microparticles.

14303917.label: Major findings and research outcome
14303917.value: We designed and constructed hydrogel-based artificial cells capable of long-lived protein expression (X. Zhou, H. Wu, M. Cui, S. N. Lai, B. Zheng, Chem. Sci., 2018, 9, 4275). We achieved the regulation of protein expression in the cell-mimic particles by the usage of lac operon. The cell-mimic particles quickly responded to the concentration change of isopropyl β-D-1-thiogalactopyranoside (IPTG) in the feeding buffer to regulate the mCherry expression level. We also constructed an in vitro genetic oscillator in the cell-mimic particles. Protein LacI provided a negative feedback to the expression of both LacI itself and eGFP, and the expression level change of eGFP presented an oscillation. We then improved the hydrogel-based artificial cells by replacing the Ni-NTA agent with DNA aptamer in the hydrogel, which made the hydrogel more biocompatible (S.N. Lai, X. Zhou, X. Ouyang, H. Zhou, Y. Liang, J. Xia, B. Zheng, ACS Synth. Biol., 2020, 9, 76). The resulting artificial cells also showed capability of long-lived protein expression and regulation of protein synthesis. Utilizing the hydrogel-based artificial cells, we constructed biosensors for the detection of various biomolecules such as thrombin. In the biosensor, the DNA aptamer and mRNA complex recognized the target biomolecule and altered the synthesis yield of signaling protein. Based on such concept, we built two new types of chemiresistive electronic nose for the detection of volatile organic compounds (B. Liu, Y. Huang, K. WL Kam, W.-F. Cheung, N. Zhao, B. Zheng, Biosens. Bioelectron.: X, 2019, 1, 100016; B. Liu, X. Wu, K. WL Kam, W.-F. Cheung, B. Zheng ACS Sensors, 2019, 4, 3051). One students obtained her PhD for her work on this project. Xiaoyu Zhou synthesized the hydrogel microparticles and constructed the artificial cells in the hydrogel. She further demonstrated protein synthesis regulation and genetic circuit in the hydrogel-based artificial cells. Her research work won her the Best Student Poster award in 2018 Gordon conference on Biointerface Science. Research collaboration has been established based on the research works. We are collaborating with Professor Yohei Yokobayashi of the Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology. Professor Yokobayashi is an expert in nucleic acid chemistry. We are working on developing new biosensors using the hydrogel-based artificial cells.

14303917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14303917.value: With the long-lived and efficient protein synthesis, the hydrogel-based artificial cells support the gene regulation and gene circuit engineering. We plan to further our research work on the hydrogel-based artificial cells in the following aspects: (1) The hydrogel-based artificial cells provide a powerful platform for biosensors such as toehold-based sensors for viruses; (2) We will utilize the hydrogel-based artificial cells as the model cells in the research of cell–cell communication such as biofilm disruption; (3) The hydrogel used in the project provides a new matrix for enzyme immobilization and protection, which substantially extended the lifetime of the enzyme for the purpose of metabolic engineering; (4) With a coating of a lipid bilayer, the cell-mimic particles provide a potential starting point to the construction of new artificial cells and drug delivery vehicles.

14303917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14303917.value: In this project we designed and constructed hydrogel microparticles capable of protein synthesis. The hydrogel microparticles has no membrane, facilitating continuous uptake of nutrients and release of the protein and waste products. As a result, the hydrogel microparticles can continuously and efficiently synthesize proteins for more than 28 days while the traditional membrane encapsulation based artificial cells can maintain the protein synthesis for at most three days. The long lifetime of hydrogel microparticles allows us to integrate more functions. By designing and implementing appropriate genetic circuit, we achieved the regulation of protein synthesis in the hydrogel microparticles by controlling the concentration of regulating molecules in the nutrient solution. We also demonstrated genetic oscillation in the hydrogel microparticles, i.e., the yield of the protein would oscillate with time. Such genetic oscillator provides a useful model for studying the natural oscillators in cells. Based on the hydrogel microparticles we constructed a sensor that can detect the target molecules through interactions with a nucleic acid complex. Fluorescence signal was produced as a result of the interaction. The sensor has high specificity and sensitivity due to the usage of the nucleic acid complex and the efficient protein synthesis in the hydrogel microparticles.
