14304017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14304017.value: Many systems of interest in physics and systems biology consist of a large number of interacting components. Such systems can be represented as networks with the components known as nodes. The collective behavior of a network arises from the interactions of the nodes. When two nodes interact, they are said to be connected or linked to one another. For a biological network, knowing the information of such connectivity of the network provides insights for understanding the functionality of the network. It is often difficult to directly measure the network structure but relatively easy to measure the dynamics of the nodes. Reconstructing a network from dynamics is a longstanding challenge in network research that has great impact to many topics in systems biology. Recently, we have successfully developed a reconstruction method for directed networks that require only time-series measurements of the nodes. Our method gives accurate results for a variety of networks with different nonlinear dynamics and coupling and also for a physiologically realistic model of interacting neurons. Synchronized bursts are a prominent property of many in-vitro neuronal cultures, which is essential for various phenomena in neuroscience but their complex dynamics are not yet understood. In this project, we propose to study the relation of network structure and the bursting dynamics in cultured neuronal networks using our model and the state-of-the-art multi-electrode array experimental measurements from our collaborators. In realistic situations, one often encounters the problem of incomplete data in that some of the nodes are unknown or measurements from some of the nodes are missing. We will address this challenging problem of network reconstruction from incomplete data and our objective is to find out the conditions for which the links among the measured nodes can be reconstructed from the available measurements. Furthermore, we will extend our approach to study the reconstruction of metabolic networks and aim to develop a method that has better performance than existing ones. 很多物理學及生物學系統是由大量相互影響的基本部份組成。這類系統可以表示為網絡​​， 基本部份為網絡的節點​， 而基本部份之問的相互作用則為節點之間的連結。​​一個​網絡的整體行爲由個別節點的相互作用所​​​導致。所以，知曉一個生物學網絡各個節點的連結狀況，即其網絡結構，可以幫助我們去理解這個網絡的功能性質。一般之言，要直接測量一個網络的結構是非常困難的，但是量度各個節點的動力學訊息則相對容易。故此，網絡硏究的一個長期挑戰便是如何從動力學訊息重構網絡的結構，而這些研究結果將會對系統生物學有重大影響。最近我們成功建立了一個只需知道各個節點的動力學訊息，即其時間序列，便可重構網絡的方法。對不同結構和不同非線性動力學的網絡，包括一個描述神經細胞相互作用的模型，我們的方法都能給出相對準確的網絡重構結果。同步爆發(synchronized bursts)是體外神經細胞培養(in-vitro neuronal cultures)的一個突出性質，並且與神經科學中種種現象有密切的關係，可是我們今天仍未能明白同步爆發的複雜動態。在此次研究計劃，我們將利用上述我們所建立的網絡重構方法去分析由我們硏究夥伴運用多電極陣列所量度的實驗數據，從而探討體外神經細胞培養爆發現象和相應網絡結構的關係。此外，在處理實際問題時，我們經常會遇到資料不全的難題，如網絡有未知的節點或欠缺某些節點的動力學訊息。在此研究計劃我們亦將致力解決從不完全資料重構網絡的難題。最後，我們會硏究重構代謝網絡，嘗試找出比現存做法更有效和準確的方法。

14304017.label: Realisation of objectives
14304017.value: By using a model class of bidirectional networks with nonlinear dynamics and diffusive-like coupling that are subjected to a Gaussian white noise, we have derived analytical results that explain the effects of incomplete data or hidden nodes, nodes that are unknown or whose measurements are unavailable, on the reconstruction of bidirectional networks. Our results show that when the hidden nodes are not preferentially linked to the measured nodes in any manner, the presence of hidden nodes would have little effects on the reconstruction of the links among the measured nodes and this is true even when the hidden nodes outnumber the measured nodes. When the hidden nodes are preferentially linked to the measured nodes, the accuracy of the reconstruction results would deteriorate but useful information can still be uncovered. We have verified our theoretical results and their implications using numerical simulations and our numerical studies indicate that our results and analytical understanding can apply more generally even to some systems beyond the model class of networks studied. Thus, we have fully achieved objective 1. We have exceeded objective 2. Estimating connectivity of neuronal cultures from voltage measurements recorded by multi-electrode array (MEA) is a great challenge. Existing methods commonly make use of the cross-correlation of spiking events detected in MEA voltage recordings to estimate the functional connectivity. As statistical correlation can arise from indirect influences, extensive efforts have been spent to optimize the performance of such methods based on spike cross-correlation. We have adopted a different approach. We have modeled the neuronal culture as a stochastic dynamical system and applied a method that we have previously developed [Ching and Tam, Phys. Rev. E 95, 010301(R), 2017] to estimate the effective connectivity that describes direct interactions between the nodes. This method makes use of a relation between the time-lagged covariance and equal-time covariance of the dynamics recorded by the whole voltage time series. Applying a theoretical method to estimate real-world networks from experimental measurements is non-trivial since imperfections of real-world situations pose additional difficulties. We have overcome the various difficulties and successfully reconstructed the effective connectivity. The effective connectivity obtained reproduces various reported features of cortical regions in rats and monkeys and has similar network properties as the chemical synaptic network of the nematode C. elegans. These findings support that the effective connectivity that we have reconstructed can capture the general properties of synaptic connections in neuronal networks. We have further shown that our results can better reveal relationships between network structure and spiking dynamics than the functional connectivity estimated from the same sets of measurements using an existing method based on cross-correlation of spiking events. By performing numerical simulations of networks of spiking neurons using the reconstructed effective connectivity, we have gained insights on the possible effects of bicuculline, a drug that blocks the receptors of inhibitory neurotransmitter GABA, on the spiking and bursting activities of neuronal networks. Our simulation results suggest a heterogeneity in the action of bicuculline and such heterogeneous effect has indeed been reported in a rat hippocampal neuronal network. Furthermore, by comparing the dynamics of networks with the reconstructed connectivity and networks with modified network properties, we are able to conclude that a long-tail distribution of the average synaptic weights of outgoing links is the crucial feature that gives rise to bursting dynamics in neuronal networks. Metabolic networks comprise the chemical reactions of metabolism and the regulatory interactions that guide these reactions. They are often modeled by a set of differential equations which govern the time evolution of the concentration of the metabolites. Some studies model metabolism processes based on the Lotka-Volterra model of population dynamics. For such models, our method for reconstructing directed networks from dynamics can be directly applied to obtain accurate results. However, Lotka-Volterra model is not well-suited to model biochemical systems because the dynamics of Lotka-Volterra model is incompatible with basic functionalities of pathways of enzymatic reactions. Instead, biochemical systems theory is a better mathematical modelling framework for biochemical systems, in which biochemical processes are represented using power-law expansions in the variables of the system. For metabolic networks modeled by biochemical systems theory, we have found that our approach cannot capture influx and efflux metabolic pathways or links with the same kinetic orders. These results imply that our approach does not lead to methods that can perform better than existing methods for reconstructing metabolic networks and this achieved objective 3.

14304017.label: Major findings and research outcome
14304017.value: Hidden nodes, nodes that are unknown or whose measurements are unavailable, are common in real-world problems. For a model class of bidirectional networks, we have derived analytical results showing that corrections occur in the reconstruction result of a potential link between two measured nodes when these measured nodes are connected via a path of hidden nodes. The size of the corrections are determined by the number of paths of hidden nodes connecting the two measured nodes, the coupling strength of the links, and the strength of the hidden nodes in these paths (publication 1). We have shown how to adopt a method that we have previously developed to reveal the effective connectivity of neuronal cultures from multi-electrode array (MEA) recordings (publication 3). Definite dependencies of the average synaptic strengths of excitatory incoming and outgoing links on the number of detected spikes are found in our estimated effective connectivity but not in the functional connectivity estimated from the same sets of MEA recording using existing method based on cross-correlation of spikes. Thus, we have demonstrated that our results can better reveal relationships between network structure and dynamics for neuronal cultures (publication 3). Using numerical simulations of networks of spiking neurons, we have shown that neurons in a network respond differently to changes in inhibitory synaptic weights. This suggests that activity-dependent modification of synaptic strength does not necessarily generate a positive feedback on the dynamics of neurons connected in a network and thus synaptic plasticity does not necessarily lead to unstable runaway synaptic dynamics in neuronal networks (publication 2). It has been found that bicuculline, a drug that blocks the receptors of inhibitory neurotransmitter GABA, has a heterogeneous effect on firing rate in a rat hippocampal neuronal network. Our simulation results thus shed light on the heterogeneous effects of bicuculline when its blocking action is crudely modeled as a decrease in the magnitudes of all inhibitory synaptic weights (publication 2). The reconstructed networks from MEA recordings have biologically realistic long-tailed distributions of average synaptic weights. By comparing the dynamics of these networks and those of networks with modified properties, we have shown that a long-tail distribution of the average synaptic weights of the outgoing links is the crucial feature that gives rise to bursting dynamics in neuronal networks and determines the overall response of the whole network to changes in synaptic strength (publication 2).

14304017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14304017.value: We have shown that the neuronal networks that we have reconstructed can reproduce various known features of cortical regions in rats and monkeys and are thus biologically realistic and can better reveal relationships between network structure and dynamics. Our numerical simulations of networks of spiking neurons using the reconstructed effective connectivity have revealed heterogenous responses of the neurons to changes in inhibitory synaptic weights. This unexpected result has interesting implications on the stability issue in synaptic plasticity, a property of the brain that is proposed to play a fundamental role in learning and memory. Our simulations have further shown that specific network property gives rise to bursting dynamics and determines the overall response to changes in synaptic weights. Understanding fully the relationships between network structure and dynamics as well as network structure and function and the stability of synaptic plasticity will be interesting problems to be explored in future studies. To follow up on these further developments, we plan to carry out a systematic numerical study of networks of spiking neurons using particularly the biologically realistic effective connectivity that we have reconstructed to address the various questions of interest. We have already submitted a new RGC GRF project proposal.

14304017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14304017.value: Networks are systems that consist of many interacting components. Knowing the network structure, which depicts the connectivity or interactions among the components or nodes, is crucial for understanding the dynamics and functions of the systems. A grand challenge is to reconstruct the network structure from measurements of the nodes. Our project has addressed this challenge. First, we have derived theoretical results that advance our understanding of how hidden nodes, nodes that are unknown or whose measurements are unavailable, affect the reconstruction of bidirectional networks. Our results show that when the hidden nodes are not preferentially linked to the measured nodes in any manner, they would have little effects on the reconstruction of links among the measured nodes and this is true even when the hidden nodes outnumber the measured nodes. Second, we have successfully reconstructed networks of cultured cortical neurons from experimental measurements recorded by a multi-electrode array. These networks can reproduce various features of cortical regions in monkeys and rats and better reveal relationships between network structure and spiking dynamics than networks obtained using existing methods based on statistical correlations. These networks, with biologically realistic properties, will allow us to gain insights on the organizing principles of neuronal networks.

14304117.value: 本項目從理論上研究在強太赫茲場下半導體中高階邊帶產生和高次諧波產生過程中的非阿貝爾貝利相位的效應。 超強激光下原子中的極端非線性光學，例如高次諧波產生，可以用來研究強場物理和經典-量子過渡，也給諸如飛秒光學和相干X射線頻譜學等前沿技術提供了基礎。最近在半導體中發現的高階邊帶產生和高次諧波產生提供了一個研究極端非線性光學的新的平台。半導體極端非線性光學蘊含豐富的物理有待研究。其中一項就是貝利相位—在強太赫茲場驅動下，半導體中電子在動量空間的運動會伴隨內部態（包括軌道態和自旋態）的絕熱變化，因而帶來一個額外的量子相位，即貝利相位。此前本項目負責人發現阿貝爾貝利相位（發生於單個能帶情形）會影響邊帶發生的偏振。最近，本項目負責人和實驗合作者更發現源於非阿貝爾貝利相位可能導致邊帶發生中非平凡的偏振依賴。更豐富的物理現象仍待研究。 在此，我們將系統研究非阿貝爾貝利相位在半導體量子阱中高階邊帶產生及半導體體材料中高次諧波產生的物理效應。有光激發時，量子阱中電子空穴對被幾十 kV/cm場強的太赫茲場驅動可以產生高階邊帶產生；在體材料中幾MV/cm強的太赫茲場更可以直接產生高次諧波。在這些過程中，電子空穴都可以伴隨累積非阿貝爾貝利相位。我們將深入研究此相位對高次諧波及高階邊帶的偏振的影響，以及它們對激發光和太赫茲場偏振的依賴關係。我們亦會研究脈衝激發條件下的物理效應，以期直接測量量子軌道的相位。 本研究將有助深化對固體材料中強場物理的理解也可望啟發新的超快光電器件應用。

14304117.label: Realisation of objectives
14304117.value: We have addressed Objective 1 by the following works. We have formulated a general theory of Berry phase in nonlinear optical systems. In particular, we discovered a new type of singularity of Berry curvatures, which, unlike monopole singularities, resembles a critical surface of quantum phase transitions, in nonlinear quantum systems. Such a phenomenon does not exists in linear optical systems. The paper is under review. We worked together with the experimental collaborator (CoI M. Sherwin) in studying the effect of Berry phases in THz sideband generation in semiconductor quantum wells and apply to to measure the spinor wavefunctions in the energy bands in semiconductors. We discovered an interesting quantum interference effect caused by the non-Abelian phases of quantum trajectories in the re-collision of electron-hole pairs in semiconductors under strong THz driven. Such effects lead to strong dependence of the THz sideband generation on the polarizations of both the excitation and emission. Furthermore, we realized that the superradiance masing of Floquet states is profoundly related to the sideband generation and proposed to study the THz sideband generation in gain medium such as population-inverted semiconductors. This would lead to new directions in the field of superradiance masing and THz sideband generation. Objective 2 was addressed with the following works. We have formulated a general theory of Berry phases of higher spins (relevant to hole spins and exciton spins in semiconductors) using the Majorana star representation. Such a representation provide an intuitive, geometrical understanding of the relatively more complicated structures of Berry phases of higher spins. Through this picture, we discovered a link between the Berry phases of higher spins and quantum entanglement in symmetric states of multiple qubits that are used to form the higher spins. This study forms a basis for studying the Berry phases of holes and exciton wavefunctions, which are higher spinors. We established a quantum interferometry method for measuring the quantum phases of quantum trajectories in recollisions of electron-hole pairs in semiconductors under strong THz driving. Unlike recollisions of electrons and ions in the high-harmonic generation in atoms and molecules, the THz sideband generation involves electron-hole pairs which are virtual particles and can be excited at selected times. Therefore, we come up with a scheme of using two or more lasers to excite the electron-hole pairs in semiconductors under strong THz driving. The electron-hole pairs then follow different quantum trajectories and recollide to emit THz sidebands. The interference between different quantum trajectories, which resembles the AB effect in real space, results in oscillating strengths of the sidebands as functions of the sideband order. Therefore, the phase, and in particular the Berry phases of the quantum trajectories, can be measured. This provide a unique method to differentiate quantum pathways from classical trajectories and a new control handle of THz sideband generation.

14304117.label: Major findings and research outcome
14304117.value: We discovered that the Berry phases in nonlinear optical systems have characteristic differences from those in linear quantum systems. In particular, the singularities in Berry curvature fields of linear quantum systems resemble the monopoles of gauge fields, but those in nonlinear optical systems resemble the critical surfaces of quantum phase transitions. We have proposed schemes for observing such effects. We studied the effects of Berry phases in the THz sideband generation in semiconductors and discovered the strong dependence of the sideband intensities on the polarizations of the excitations and emissions. We propose to use these effects to measure the spinor wavefunctions of Bloch electrons and holes in semiconductors. We formulated a general theory on representing the geometric phases in higher spins using the Majorana constellations and discovered a connection between the quantum entanglement in the symmetric states of qubits that form the higher spin and the geometric phases. We discovered quantum interference between quantum trajectories of electron-hole pairs in semiconductors driven by strong THz field and the oscillation of sideband generation due to the quantum interference. Therefore, we propose a scheme to measure the quantum phases and Berry phases of the quantum trajectories, which has not been possible in recollisions in atoms and molecules. We propose to use this quantum interference to modulate and control the intensities of the sideband generation, which could have applications in optical communication. We found that there is a profound link between three different optical phenomena, superradiance masing in Floquet systems under periodic driving, high-order THz sideband generation in systems under strong AC driving, and QASER (proposed by Scully) in high frequency in coherent quantum systems driven by low-frequency field. We pointed out this perspective a commentary paper published in Science (2021).

14304117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14304117.value: In this project we found that there is a profound link between three different optical phenomena, superradiance masing in Floquet systems under periodic driving, high-order THz sideband generation in systems under strong AC driving, and QASER (proposed by Scully) in high frequency in coherent quantum systems driven by low-frequency field. In the future, it is of great interest to study the THz sideband generation in gain media under strong AC driving. That would lead interesting strong-field physics and new lasers as well as new applications.

14304117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14304117.value: When a semiconductor is excited by a laser, a pair of virtual particles called electron and hole can be excited and their recombination leads to light emission. When the semiconductor is irradiated by a strong AC field, the AC electric field would drive the electron and hole, inducing large kinetic energy of these virtual particles. When the electron and hole pair re-collide, they would emit light at frequencies separated from the excitation laser frequency by integer multiples of the AC field frequency. This phenomenon is called sideband generation. The motion of the electron-hole pairs under the Ac driving is almost like classical motion following the Newtonian laws but the trajectories are quantum in that they have phases and can interfere like waves. We find the quantum interference between quantum trajectories leads to troughs and peaks in the sideband generation. Such interference effect is due to the different phases between different quantum trajectories. We can use this phenomenon to measure the phases and in particular the Berry phases (a geometric phase similar to the rotation one experiences when they walk uprightly along a close path on a curved surface like the earth sphere).

14304217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14304217.value: A large number of scientific applications is based on the mathematical understanding and numerical simulation of acoustic and elastic waves; examples include the design of sound absorbing walls, reconstruction of images or seismic exploration. The simulation of wave propagation in heterogeneous media is particularly important for the detection of material defects or anomalies; important applications include clinical diagnostics or seismic imaging. Predictions or reconstructions of the material behaviour, which are the key to the above applications, require the numerical solution of wave equations. For an accurate simulation, the computational method needs to have a large enough degrees of freedom to resolve the heterogeneities. On the other hand, in order to obtain an efficient numerical process, the degrees of freedom cannot be too large. For materials with scale separation, there are upscaled or homogenized computational models of moderate sizes that are able to represent the fine scale features. However, for very general heterogeneous media, it is challenging to construct a computational method defined on a coarse scale, which does not necessarily resolve all fine scale features. The proposed research develops a class of multiscale methods for the simulations of wave propagation in heterogeneous media. The novelties of the work are the discretization in space-time grids and the approximation of the solution by space-time multiscale basis and test functions. Existing multiscale approaches are based only on the spatial operator, and do not consider the interaction with the time variable. However, for wave propagation, especially in highly heterogeneous media, the interaction of the spatial heterogeneities and the propagation of solutions in time are strongly related. Therefore, the incorporation of space-time features in the construction of multiscale methods is essential for an efficient upscaling of the wave operator. In this regard, our proposed space-time approach, which has not been investigated in literature, will provide a new insight and a significant advance in the field. In addition, our discretization is based on the recently developed generalized multiscale finite element methods and the local orthogonal decomposition, which are proven to be successful in a number of multiscale problems. These methods are complementary to each other, and we will construct novel multiscale methods on space-time grids by using the ideas from both methods, with the aim of producing a stable and efficient multiscale framework for the solutions of the wave equation in heterogeneous media. 大量的科學應用是基於聲波和彈性波的數學理解和數值模擬; 例如吸聲牆的設計，圖像的重建或地震勘探。異質介質中波傳播的模擬對材料缺陷或異常的檢測特別重要;重要的應用包括臨床診斷或地震成像。材料行為的預測或重建是上述應用的關鍵，需要波動方程的數值解。對於精確的模擬，計算方法需要具有足夠大的自由度來解決異質性。另一方面，為了獲得有效的數值處理，自由度不能太大。對於具有刻度分離的材料，具有能夠表示精細尺度特徵的均勻計算模型。然而，對於非常一般的異構介質來說，構建在粗略尺度上定義的計算方法是困難的。 我們的研究開發了一類用於異質介質中波傳播模擬的多尺度方法。工作的創新之處在於時空網格的離散化以及時空多尺度基礎和測試功能的解決方案近似。現有的多尺度方法僅基於空間算子，不考慮與時間變量的交互。然而，對於波傳播，特別是在高度異質介質中，空間異質性與解的傳播在時間上的相互作用是相關的。因此，在構建多尺度方法時併入時空特徵對於波動算子的有效升級至關重要。在這方面，我們提出的空間時間方法尚未在文獻中進行調查，將為該領域提供新的見解和重大進展。此外，我們的離散化是基於最近開發的廣義多尺度有限元方法和局部正交分解，這被證明在許多多尺度問題中是成功的。這些方法是相互補充的，我們將通過使用這兩種方法的想法來構建時空網格的新穎多尺度方法，目的是為異質介質中波動方程的解決方案提供一個穩定和有效的多尺度框架。

14304217.label: Realisation of objectives
14304217.value: The objectives are fully achieved. In particular, we have developed new multiscale basis functions for wave equations in heterogeneous media. We have also performed convergence analysis of our methods. The basis functions are based on some local energy minimization problems. The resulting basis functions have fast decay property, and can therefore be computed efficiently. The convergence of the method depends only on the coarse grid size, and is independent of the scales of the media. The resulting method has shown to give excellent performance for wave problems arising from real applications.

14304217.label: Major findings and research outcome
14304217.value: The project has developed several advances in multiscale wave simulations. The problem is challenging especially for the case of heterogenous media. In order to obtain an efficient method, one has to perform some type of model reduction. It is the goal of this project to achieve these goals. The project has led to some very general methodology for the construction of multiscale basis functions for wave simulations. In addition, some mathematical theories are developed to validate the methods. Also, extensive numerical tests are performed to show the power of the proposed methods.

14304217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14304217.value: There are certainly rooms for development. For example, in many real applications, one has to perform coupled problems. That is, the model consists of several model components, and wave equation is one of them. In order to develop efficient methods, one has to develop carefully basis functions. This is certainly a very important direction for future exploration.

14304217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14304217.value: The project has developed some efficient model reduction for wave simulations. Many applications involve the solution of wave equations in heterogeneous media. In the project, we have designed some new methods for solve the equations efficiently. The method is based on finding some local dominant modes of solutions, as using them as basis functions. The resulting method can solve the problems ten to hundred times faster than traditional methods.

14304417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14304417.value: 這項提案將旨在開發使用未活化的環丙烷來模擬未活化的烯烴用於由路易斯鹼催化的各種親電鹵化反應中。環丙烷已知具有高的環張力。環丙烷中低效的軌道重疊意味著它具有三個彎曲的鍵，它們各自具有顯著程度的鍵特性。因此，環丙烷的反應性類似於C = C雙鍵的反應性。活化環丙烷（即供體 - 受體環丙烷）的開環反應在過去幾十年中引起了有機化學家的廣泛關注，這些反應（在分子內和分子間反應方面）已經有很好的文獻記錄。然而，因為需要特定取代基（吸電子基團和給電子基團），環丙基底物的規模相對有限。形成鮮明對比的是，由於反應活性和區域選擇性差，未活化環丙烷的開環反應仍然是一個鮮被開發的領域和強大的挑戰，而所得到的產物對於藥物化學和有機合成非常有用。理論上，環丙烷的反應化學性質與烯烴的相似，應適用於親電鹵化反應。 通過路易斯鹼催化可以實現烯烴底物的高效和區域選擇性親電鹵化。最近，我們的團隊在烯烴的催化親電鹵代環化的發展以及將這些反應應用於藥物合成方面取得了重大進展。例如，我們使用我們的方法合成了由默克公司上市的口服活性抗真菌藥物泊沙康唑（Noxafil）的關鍵中間體（J. Am. Chem. Soc., 2014, 136, 5627–5630）。此外，我們最近的研究已經證明，環丙基甲基酰胺（Org. Lett., 2015, 17, 2444–4947）和環丙基羧酸（Adv. Synth. Catal., 2016, 358, 1719–1724）可以模擬它們的烯烴對應物用於路易斯鹼性硫化物催化的親電溴化反應。 在這個提案中，我們計劃進一步探索使用未活化環丙烷模擬未活化烯烴用於各種鹵化反應中。一個重要的研究方向將是探討各種親核試劑在分子內和分子間反應中的應用。我們將對路易斯鹼催化的各種環丙烷衍生物的有機轉化進行系統的研究。一旦開發，這些方法將潛在地用於合成在製藥工業中重要的有價值的中間體。

14304517.label: Project Objectives
14304517.value: We shall formulate several important inverse problems of our interest into nonlinear nonconvex and nonsmooth minimization systems by combining a regularization term with a specially designed penalty term that takes care of some a priori knowledge of the unknown parameters to recover in the inverse problems. We shall study the finite element discretizations of the regularized nonlinear, nonconvex and nonsmooth minimization systems from Objective 1, and the convergence and stability of the finite element solutions to the continuous regularized solutions. We will derive and analyse the a posteriori error estimates of the finite element solutions to the regularized minimization systems from Objective 2 and construct adaptive finite element methods based on the error estimates. We will run a large number of numerical simulations for the new finite element methods to verify their performance. Using these numerical results, we shall improve the finite element methods.

14304517.value: 本研究的目標是構造和分析一些求解不適定反問題的自適應數值方法。 這些反問題是通過使用某些測量數據去重構數學模型中的一些未知但非常重要的物理參數。 分析和求解這些反問題的主要困難在於重構這些係數時關於測量誤差的數學不穩定性。求解反問題的一個有效和流行的方法是應用某些正規化策略將它們轉化成為數學上穩定的優化系統。由於偏微分方程模型中的待識別參數在很多實際應用中是不連續的，或者在兩種非均勻介質的交介面上有大的跳躍，因此， 在將這些反問題轉化成為穩定的優化系統時非常有必要引入非光滑正 則化項。而且待識別參數通常會有一些具體的先驗資訊，例如稀疏性質，因此引入的正規化項需要更好的與這些具體的性質相吻合以便於得到更加理想的解。這將會導致需要求解帶有一些偏微分方程約束的高度非線性、非凸並且非光滑的優化問題。 鑒於偏微分方程模型中的這些不連續（可能高度不連續）的係數，線性有限元方法是離散這些高度 非線性優化系統的最自然的選擇，因為任何更高階的有限元方法不能得到更高的精度。 對於有限元離散，我們需要首先構造一個合適的有限元網格去求解這些在偏微分方程約束下的非線性優化系統。由於係數的不連續性的位置是未知的，我們將通常採用均勻網格。 但是，這些偏微分方程模型中的不連續係數使得線性有限元方法在這些均勻網格上只能得到很差的收斂性。自適應有限元方法可以自動捕捉這些待識別係數的不連續位置並且改善網格，使得形成的非線性優化系統的有限元解將以近似最優的速度收斂到問題的真解。 但是，自適應有限元方法還沒有被用於求解非光滑正規化的反問題。 所以在本研究中，我們將構造並且分析一些有效的自適應有限元，用於求解一些偏微分方程中具有代表性的不適定的非光滑正規化的線性與非線性反問題。

14304517.label: Realisation of objectives
14304517.value: We are very happy to declare that we have achieved all the Objectives in this RGC project. Whenever an inverse problem is solved numerically, which is the main Objectives of the RGC project, the first crucial step is to collect sufficient physical measurement data. But it is a fundamental mathematical issue to find out the amount of data that is required to ensure the unique solution of an inverse problem. We studied in depth this fundamental mathematical and physical issue for inverse electromagnetic medium scattering problems in [1] and for acoustic inverse scattering problems with physical impedance media in [3][6]. We discovered that for some physically important scenarios, the knowledge of the far-field pattern incited by only one or two incoming wave fields are sufficient to uniquely determine the shape and impedance property of a penetrable or impenetrable scatterer of special geometries. Using these fundamental results, the unique reconstruction can be established to the corresponding inverse problems with non-smooth normal derivatives or impedance parameters at the scattering interface. These mathematical investigations provide an insightful guidance for practitioners to collect the desired amount of the measurement data, for which the inverse electromagnetic or acoustic scattering problems are ensured to have stable and effective numerical reconstructions. In addition, the theoretical analyses indicate clearly how to make full use of irregular or non-smooth regularizations or geometries of physical objects in numerical solutions. As proposed in the Objectives, a very important regularization approach for solving inverse problems is to formulate the inverse problems into some nonlinear, nonconvex and nonsmooth minimizations, by combining a special regularization strategy. But these regularized minimizations must be mathematically stable in order for any stable numerical solutions. The verification of stability of the regularizations is challenging to most inverse problems. We investigated this stability issue for general elliptic and parabolic inverse problems of recovering the unknown radiativity [9]. We successfully verified variational source conditions for these highly ill-posed inverse problems, and worked out the specific convergence rates for the Tikhonov regularization approach. The analyses are very general and can be extended to some other important classes of inverse problems. As we know from above, inverse problems are often formulated into nonlinear, nonconvex and nonsmooth minimizations by combining a special regularization strategy that takes care of a priori knowledge of unknown physical parameters. These minimizations are solved mostly by iterative optimization methods with certain effective preconditioning techniques. And each iteration of these optimization solvers is to solve 2 or 3 forward model problems involved. So an efficient solver for any inverse problem relies on the availability of efficient and stable numerical methods for the corresponding forward model systems. These important issues were investigated deeply in the works [4][7] [10]. First, we analysed adaptive finite element methods for solving elliptic curl-curl variational inequalities of second kind in [4], for solving quasilinear H(curl)-elliptic problems in [7] and for solving time-harmonic Maxwell problems in [10]. Then we derived a posteriori error estimators based on an elegant combination of the Moreau-Yosida regularization and the edge elements of first family [4][7]. We further proposed adaptive finite element algorithms and established their convergence, reliability and efficiency. Using these results, we established the strong convergence of the edge element solutions that are produced by the adaptive finite element algorithms. We have carried out many numerical experiments that are able to clearly show the robustness and effectiveness of the new adaptive finite element algorithms, particularly when the algorithms were applied to solve a challenging variational inequality problem arising from the high-temperature superconductivity [4], a quasilinear H(curl)-elliptic problem [7] and a time-harmonic Maxwell problem [10]. We studied a highly ill-posed inverse problem associated with an eddy current model mathematically and numerically in [11]. The ill-posedness of the inverse problem was first investigated. By making use of nonradiating source conditions, we demonstrated the regularity of the tangential trace of the true solution on the boundary. This justified our mathematical formulation of the inverse problem. With these results, we formulated the inverse problem as a nonlinear optimization problem with an appropriate regularization. In order to effectively solve the nonlinear nonconvex constrained optimization, we introduced a feasible Lagrangian and its discrete variant. By means of the gradient of the objective functional, a nonlinear conjugate gradient method was formulated for solving the optimization system, with its step sizes updated very effectively by a quadratic approximation of the objective function, and a Sobolev gradient is incorporated to accelerate the iterative process. Many numerical experiments were provided to demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed mathematical formulation and numerical reconstruction algorithm, especially the robust recovery of the locations and sizes of separated inclusions in the noisy case. In many applications of inverse problems, multiple inhomogeneous inclusions arising from two different physical parameters may be involved, and very limited boundary Cauchy data are available associated with one or two measurement events, to which most existing methods do not apply. We investigated a class of elliptic inverse problems for these challenging physical scenarios in [6]. We proposed a new fast, stable and highly parallelable direct sampling method (DSM) for the simultaneous reconstruction process. Two groups of probing and index functions are constructed, and their desired properties are constructed. In order to identify and decouple the multiple inhomogeneous inclusions of different physical nature, we introduced a new concept of mutually almost orthogonality property that generalizes the important concept of almost orthogonality property in classical DSMs for inhomogeneous inclusions of same physical nature. With the help of this new concept, we developed a reliable strategy to distinguish two different types of inhomogeneous inclusions with noisy data collected at one or two measurement event. We further improved the decoupling effect by choosing an appropriate boundary influx. Many numerical experiments were presented to illustrate the robustness and efficiency of the proposed method. Stochastic gradient descent algorithm (SGD) has been widely applied for solving many challenging problems, including some important inverse problems. But there is still no mathematical understanding of the effectiveness and robustness of SGD for inverse problems. We made a systematic investigation of this important issue through this RGC project and filled in this big gap. We first analyzed the regularizing property of SGD for the numerical solution of a class of linear and nonlinear ill-posed inverse problems in Hilbert spaces in [5][8]. At each step of the iteration, SGD randomly chooses one equation from the system to obtain an unbiased stochastic estimate of the gradient and then performs a descent step with the estimated gradient. It is highly scalable to the problem size and holds significant potential for solving large-scale inverse problems. Under some reasonable conditions, we established the regularizing property and the saturation phenomenon of SGD for a priori stopping rules and then analysed the convergence rates. All the forward models involved in this RGC project could be extended to fractional type PDE models. We carried out a systematic study of the stability, especially the optimal decay rates, of the solutions to several important numerical schemes for solving general fractional ODEs in [2]. These have provided constructive guidance for numerical solutions of inverse fractional type PDEs.

14304517.label: Major findings and research outcome
14304517.value: We list the major findings and research outcome below, with more detailed introduction of these findings and outcome as well as their background and significance given in Section 5.3. We studied in depth the fundamental mathematical and physical identifiability of inverse electromagnetic scattering problems [1] and of acoustic inverse impedance scattering problems [3][6]. We proved far-field pattern incited by only one or two incoming fields is sufficient to uniquely determine the shape and impedance property of a penetrable or impenetrable scatterer of special geometries. We investigated the stability issue of the widely used nonlinear, nonconvex and nonsmooth optimizations for general elliptic and parabolic inverse problems of recovering distributed fluxes [2] and radiativity [9]. We verified variational source conditions for these inverse problems, and worked out convergence rates of the Tikhonov regularization approach. How to solve nonlinear, nonconvex and nonsmooth minimizations is crucial to an effective solution of an inverse problem. We analysed adaptive finite element methods for elliptic curl-curl variational inequalities [4], for quasilinear problems [7] and for time-harmonic Maxwell problems [10]. We proposed and analysed adaptive finite element algorithms as well as their convergence, reliability and efficiency. We studied a highly ill-posed inverse eddy current problem in [11], its ill-posedness and mathematical formulation. We proposed and analysed a feasible Lagrangian and its discrete variant as well as an effective nonlinear conjugate gradient method. We investigated a class of elliptic inverse problems [6] for the scenarios with multiple inhomogeneous inclusions arising from two different physical parameters and data. We proposed a fast, stable and highly parallelable direct sampling method, and developed a reliable strategy to distinguish two different types of inhomogeneous inclusions. We made a systematic investigation of the effectiveness and robustness of the widely used stochastic gradient descent algorithm (SGD) for inverse problems. We analyzed the regularizing property of SGD for the numerical solution of a class of linear and nonlinear ill-posed inverse problems in Hilbert spaces in [5][8], and established the regularizing property and the saturation phenomenon of SGD for a priori stopping rules and then analysed the convergence rates. We carried out a systematic study of the stability, especially the optimal decay rates, of the solutions to several important numerical schemes for solving general fractional ODEs in [12]. We have carried out many numerical experiments to demonstrate the robustness and effectiveness of all the newly proposed methods in this project.

We proved far-field pattern incited by only one or two incoming fields is sufficient to uniquely determine the shape and impedance property of a penetrable or impenetrable scatterer of special geometries. It is physically and mathematical important how to remove the geometrical conditions assumed in the current theory. We investigated the stability issue of the widely used nonlinear, nonconvex and nonsmooth optimizations for general elliptic and parabolic inverse problems of recovering radiativity [9]. We verified variational source conditions for these inverse problems, and worked out convergence rates of the Tikhonov regularization approach. It is practically important how to extend this stability theory and results to more nonlinear inverse problems. We studied a highly ill-posed inverse eddy current problem in [11], its ill-posedness and mathematical formulation. We proposed and analysed a feasible Lagrangian and its discrete variant as well as an effective nonlinear conjugate gradient method. It is practically important to study how the method and results can be extended to other nonlinear inverse problems.

14304517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14304517.value: In many applications, it is required to recover unknown important physical parameters in mathematical models of partial differential equations (PDEs), by using certain physical data. These problems are challenging to analyze mathematically and to solve numerically. The major difficulty lies in mathematical instability of physical parameters with respect to data noise. A popular mathematical approach is to transform inverse problems to some mathematically stabilized systems by some regularization strategies. As the identifying physical parameters in the PDEs from most applications are discontinuous, or even have large jumps across the interfaces between two different inhomogeneous media, it is desirable and necessary to introduce some nonsmooth regularizations in mathematical formulations of an inverse problem. This results in highly nonlinear, nonconvex and nonsmooth minimization systems to solve. Adaptive finite element method is a very effective approach for solving direct PDE problems, by automatically capturing and refining the meshes around the locations of discontinuities of the solutions so that the resulting solutions converge optimally. But adaptive methods have still not been studied for inverse problems with non-smooth regularizations. We developed and analyzed several efficient adaptive methods for solving a couple of representative ill-posed linear and nonlinear inverse problems of PDEs by non-smooth regularizations.

14304817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14304817.value: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) is an alternative cancer treatment that is non-invasive with minimal side-effects. The key chemical component in PDT is the photosensitizer, which can be activated by light. In the presence of oxygen, it converts oxygen into singlet oxygen and other reactive oxygen species that cause cytotoxicity and damage the cancer cells. The current limitation of PDT is that the photosensitizer itself is unable to distinguish friend or foe that causes non-specific phototoxicity. Moreover, it can be carried by other proteins and go around our circulation that leads to hyper-photosensitive and inflammation when exposing to light. Peptides have been a popular targeting unit to conjugate onto photosensitizer in the recent years because of their high binding affinity and specificity towards proteinaceous targets. Although the peptides show improved selectivity towards tumor, the peptides are quickly degraded in the circulation followed by renal clearance. Therefore, they are not ideal to use in the body. One of the best methods is to join the terminuses of the peptides together to form a ring structure. Accumulated evidence showed that such cyclized structures can significantly enhance enzymatic stability as well as binding affinity. Thus far, different research groups have used cyclic RGD peptide to target integrin-expressing cancers with the photosensitizer and showed significant improve on binding affinity and stability. Besides, RGD, there are hundreds of other cancer-specific peptides that can bind to cancers with high selectivity. However, the synthesis of other cyclic peptides and conjugation onto photosensitizer has posted synthetic challenges to researchers, which requires extensive optimization and displaying low successful rate. In this proposal, we are bridging the recently developed technologies in peptide ligation and bioconjugation with the PDT research. We aim to develop one-pot, robust, and universal methods to cyclize different peptides and at the same time, conjugated onto the photosensitizer (phthalocyanine) to form the cyclic peptide-phthalocyanine conjugates. Colon cancer is one of the most common diagnosed cancers, and it is the third leading cause of death in the US. Surgery is now the only treatment for colon cancer. Therefore, a good photosensitizer is needed to bring the PDT into the clinics, replacing the invasive surgery procedures. By using our methods, we will synthesize a series of colon cancer-targeting cyclic peptide-photosensitizer conjugates for in vitro and in vivo characterization. Potential candidates will be identified and proceed to details pre-clinical studies. 光動力療法（PDT）是非侵入性的替代癌症治療，副作用較小。 PDT中的關鍵化學成分是光敏劑，可以通過光激活。在氧的存在下，它將氧轉化為單線態氧和其他引起細胞毒性並破壞癌細胞的活性氧物質。目前PDT的局限性在於光敏劑本身無法區分正常和癌細胞而造成光毒性。此外，它可以由其他蛋白質攜帶，並到我們的循環系統，導致光敏炎症。近年來，多肽已經成為常用的靶向單元，以在光敏劑上結合。雖然肽顯示改善的對腫瘤的選擇性，但是多肽在循環系統中快速降解。因此，它們不適合身體使用。方法之一是將多肽的末端連接在一起形成環結構，這種環化結構可以顯著增強對的酶穩定性。到目前為止，不同的研究組已經使用環狀RGD肽來靶向整合素表達癌症與光敏劑，並顯示出顯著改善結合親和力和穩定性。此外，RGD還有數百種可以高選擇性結合癌症的癌細胞特異性肽。我們希望通過PDT研究來彌補最近開發的肽連接和生物共軛技術，目的是開發簡單和通用的方法來環化不同的多肽，同時結合到光敏劑（酞菁）以形成環狀肽 - 酞菁綴合物。 結腸癌是最常見的診斷性癌症之一，它是美國第三大死因。手術現在是結腸癌唯一的治療方法。因此，我們希望光敏劑將PDT可以引入診所，取代侵入性手術。通過使用我們的方法，我們將合成一系列結腸癌靶向的環肽 - 光敏劑綴合物用於體外和體內表徵。

14304817.label: Realisation of objectives
14304817.value: Realization of objectives Summery: All the objectives listed in the proposal have been achieved. Besides the objectives listed in the proposal, we also demonstrated that our novel methods could be extended to other photosensitizers and peptides to target not only colon cancer but also different types of cancers and exhibited anticancer effects during photodynamic therapy.[1-2] We also extended our methodology to antibacterial applications. The results showed that our methods could efficiently cyclize an antibacterial peptide and conjugate a phthalocyanine for chemo-photodynamic therapy against both Gram-positive and negative bacteria as well as clinical MRSA strains.[3] The details of achievements were listed below. Objective 1: To develop methodologies for one-pot peptide cyclization and phthalocyanine conjugation by using different types of chemical peptide ligations and bioconjugation approaches. This objective was achieved by using our novel designed linker that contains bifunctional moieties, which contains a 1,3-dibenzylbromide and a bioconjugation functional group including azide for strain-promoted azide-alkyne cycloaddition reaction, and cyclopentadiene for Diels-Alder reaction with maleimide.[1-3] We have been using the linkers to conjugate phthalocyanine, and BODIPY photosensitizers for anticancer and antibacterial photodynamic therapy. We have also cyclized a collection of peptides by our linkers to enhance the stability and targeting efficiency, which includes colon EGFR-targeting peptide (CMYIEALDKYAC) [1], integrin-targeting peptides(CRGDfC and GRCTFRGDLMQLCYPD), and cancer-targeting peptide (CPIEDRPMC),[2] and antibacterial peptide (RRLCRIVWVIRVCRR) [3]. All the peptides were cyclized with over 80 % yield, and the conjugation with photosensitizers is also highly effective. Thus, all the data demonstrated that our novel one-pot peptide cyclization and photosensitizer conjugation reaction could be used as a general method for drug design and synthesis. Objective 2: To apply the methods in the preparation of a series colon cancer-targeting cyclic peptide-phthalocyanine conjugates. We have been using our novel method to design a colon cancer-targeting cyclic peptide-phthalocyanine conjugates. Colon EGFR-targeting peptide (CMYIEALDKYAC), integrin-targeting peptides (GRCTFRGDLMQLCYPD) were conjugated to a phthalocyanine and BODIPY through a bifunctional linker that contains a cyclopentadiene and 1,3-dibenzylbromide and strain-promoted azide-alkyne cycloaddition reaction. The synthesis of the two compounds using our novel method demonstrated satisfying yield and simplicity. [1,2] Objective 3: To characterize the physical properties and PDT efficiency of novel conjugates including singlet oxygen generation and the fluorescence properties. All the novel peptide-photosensitizer conjugates that synthesized by our novel method have been carefully characterized. Details can be found in each supporting information of our publications. [1-3] Objective 4: To investigate the enzymatic stability and in vitro cancer-binding activities of different cyclic structures of peptide-phthalocyanine conjugates and well as their linear counterparts. The serum stability of EGFR-targeting peptide-phthalocyanine conjugate has been completed. The results showed that the half-life of the linear peptide was only 17 min while the cyclized peptide was remained intact after 2 h incubation. In vitro experiment also showed that our designed peptide-phthalocyanine conjugates could selectively bind to colon cancer cells, including HT29 and HCT116. Confocal images and flow cytometry data were obtained. [1] Objective 5: To conduct in vivo imaging and PDT on xenograft mice model with potential candidates identified from the in vitro assays. We have successfully conducted in vivo mice xenograft model to demonstrate the in vivo targeting ability of the cyclic peptide-phthalocyanine conjugates. The data suggested that the compound can be retained at the tumor site via in vivo imaging. Photodynamic therapy was conducted, and the results showed that after administration of the compound with light irradiation, tumor regression was observed. [1] Reference: 1. Chu et al. J. Med. Chem. 2021, 64, 2064. 2. Chu et al. Chem. Commun. 2020, 56, 11941. 3. Chu et al. Adv. Therap. 2020, 4, 2000204.

14304917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14304917.value: 不同於經典的傅里葉方法，斯坦因方法是確認極限方布以及 逼近速度的有效工具。它不僅適用於獨立隨機變量同時也適合 處理相依隨機變量。在過去的二十多年，斯坦因方法在正態與 非正態逼近方面取得了重大的進展，特別是通過可交換對方法 給出了確認極限分佈的具體步驟，以及相應的絕對誤差和相對 誤差。斯坦因方法成功地應用於解決隨機矩陣理論統計物理和 數論等領域眾多問題。本項目的主要目的是進一步發展完善斯坦 因方法及其在不同領域的應用， 特別要解決各種具有挑戰性的 未決問題，比如獨立隨機變量函數的極限問題， Ising模型與 黎曼猜測之間的關系。

14304917.label: Realisation of objectives
14304917.value: NOTE: This project was transferred from the former PI: Q.M. Shao to current PI: X. Fang. Z.S. Zhang was a former Ph.D. student of the former PI. L. Luo and S. H. Liu were Ph.D. students jointly supervised by both PIs. REALISATION OF OBJECTIVE 1: The first objective of this project is to develop Stein’s method for Cramer type moderation deviations, especially for unbounded exchangeable pairs. We have successfully achieved the objective. In particular: 1.1 In Shao, Zhang, Zhang (2021, Annals of Applied Probability), we established Cramer type moderate deviation theorem for normal and nonnormal approximations via a general Stein identity which includes exchangeable pair approach as a special case. 1.2 In Zhang (2021, under review), he obtained a more general result, especially for unbounded exchangeable pairs. 1.3 In Liu and Zhang (2021, under review), they used a new recursive approach to obtain Cramer type moderate deviations via a general Stein identity which includes unbounded exchangeable pairs as a special case. 1.4 In Fang, Luo and Shao (2020, Bernoulli), we obtained a refined Cramer type moderate deviation theorem for sums of local statistics partially using the exchangeable pair approach. REALISATION OF OBJECTIVE 2: The second objective of the project is to obtain Berry-Esseen bounds for general functions of independent random variables. We have successfully achieved the objective. In particular: 2.1 In Shao and Zhang (2019, Annals of Probability), we have established the Berry-Esseen bounds of normal of nonnormal approximation for unbounded exchangeable pairs. 2.2 In Shao and Zhang (2021, in preparation), we have successfully solved the problem for general function of independent random variables. REALISATION OF OBJECTIVE 3: The third objective of this project is to explore applications to statistical mechanics models. We have largely achieved the objective. In particular: 3.1 In Shao and Zhang (2019, Annals of Probability), we obtained a Berry-Esseen bound for a general Curie-Weiss model. 3.2 In Shao, Zhang and Zhang (2021, Annals of Applied Probability), we obtained a Cramer type moderate deviation theorem for the general Curie-Weiss model. 3.3 In Zhang (2021, under review), he obtained a Cramer type moderate deviation theorem applicable to statistical mechanics models where spins can take unbounded values. We have also identified a connection between the Ising model and the Riemann hypothesis. While a rigorous treatment requires more work, we don’t see any major difficulty.

14304917.label: Major findings and research outcome
14304917.value: The Berry-Esseen bound measures the absolute error of distribution approximation, while the Cramer moderate deviation theorem quantifies the relative error. These are two main topics in this project. In Shao and Zhang (2019, Annals of Probability), we have established the Berry-Esseen bounds of normal of nonnormal approximation for unbounded exchangeable pairs. As an application, we obtained a Berry-Esseen bound for a general Curie-Weiss model. In Shao, Zhang and Zhang (2021, Annals of Applied Probability), we established Cramer type moderate deviation theorem for normal and nonnormal approximations via a general Stein identity which includes exchangeable pair approach as a special case. As an application, we obtained a Cramer type moderate deviation theorem for the general Curie-Weiss model. In Zhang (2021, under review), he obtained a more general result, especially for unbounded exchangeable pairs, which is applicable to statistical mechanics models where spins can take unbounded values. In Liu and Zhang (2021, under review), they used a new recursive approach to obtain Cramer type moderate deviations via a general Stein identity which includes unbounded exchangeable pairs as a special case. In Fang, Luo and Shao (2020, Bernoulli), we obtained a refined Cramer type moderate deviation theorem for sums of local statistics partially using the exchangeable pair approach. Other related work includes: (i) a sufficient condition for self-normalized central limit theorem (for general independent random variables) which is conjectured to be necessary (Shao (2018)), (ii) self-normalized Cramer-type moderate deviation theorems for functionals of Markov chain (Feng and Shao (2020)), (iii) self-normalized moderate deviations for random walk in random scenery (Feng, Shao and Zeitouni (2019)), (iv) a Berry-Esseen bound in the high-dimensional central limit theorem (Fang and Koike (2020)), (v) new error bounds in multivariate normal approximations via exchangeable pairs with applications to Wishart matrices and fourth moment theorems (Fang and Koike (2021)), (vi) an error bound in Gaussian process approximation for locally dependent random walks (Fang et al. (2021)).

14304917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14304917.value: Several problems are left open by this project, in particular, regarding multivariate and high-dimensional approximations. (i) Moderate deviations in chi-square approximations. Motivated by chi-square tests, when a random vector W is asymptotically standard normal, it is desirable to obtain a relative error bound on the approximation of P(|W|>r), where | | denotes the Euclidean norm. However, such a bound is only known for the independent case. With the recent development of Stein’s method for Cramer type moderate deviations, we can deal with sums of locally dependent random vectors and multivariate U-statistics, which are most relevant for statistical applications. We are currently investigating improved relative error in chi-square approximations with skewness correction. (ii) Open problems in high-dimensional central limit theorem. High-dimensional CLT is a relatively new topic, but has already attracted researchers from the fields of probability, statistics, and econometrics. Thus, I believe the next few decades will see high-dimensional CLT become an extremely fruitful and exciting area of research. Notably, two fundamental questions in high-dimensional CLT remain open, one regarding the optimal Berry-Essen bound and the other regarding self-normalized high-dimensional CLT.

14304917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14304917.value: Stein’s method is a powerful tool for establishing distributional approximation results and providing the accuracy to the approximation at the same time. It works not only for independent random variables but also for dependent random variables. This project further develops Stein’s method regarding both absolute error and relative error of distributional approximations. We have successfully established the Berry-Esseen bounds of normal and nonnormal approximation for unbounded exchangeable pairs and general functionals of independent random variables. We have also established Cramer type moderate deviation theorem for normal and nonnormal approximations via a general Stein identity which includes exchangeable pair approach as a special case. Using a new recursive approach, we have successfully removed a very restrictive boundedness condition imposed in the literature of Stein’s method for Cramer type moderate deviations. As an application, we have obtained a Berry-Esseen bound and a Cramer type moderate deviation theorem for a general Curie-Weiss model. We expect these new developments of Stein’s method will enrich the asymptotic theory in probability and large sample theory in statistics and provide a powerful tool to applications in various areas.

14305017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14305017.value: Carboranes, a class of carbon-boron molecular clusters, can be viewed as three-dimensional heterocyclic, analogues of benzene. They are finding many applications in coordination/organometallic chemistry as versatile ligands, in medicine as boron neutron capture therapy agents and in supramolecular design/nanomaterials as useful building blocks. All this has recently drawn considerable attention to carborane chemistry. However, the exceptionally thermal and chemical stabilities as well as 3D structures of carboranes make their derivatization difficult, thus limiting the application scope. The development of an efficient and general methodology to functionalize carboranes would be a major advance. In general, cage C-H derivatization can be achieved via deprotonation as the C-H proton is weakly acidic (pKa ~23). In contrast, functionalizing cage B-H bonds selectively is more challenging, owing to the relatively weak polarization of B-H bonds and the similarity of ten B-H vertices, and has been little explored. Very recently, we have reported a carboxylic group-directed, palladium-catalyzed regioselective dehydrocoupling of cage B-H with the sp C-H of terminal alkynes which led to the efficient synthesis of a variety of cage B(4)-alkynylated o-carboranes (Chem. Sci. 2016, 7, 5838). Inspired by this preliminary result, we plan, in this proposal, to combine activation of cage B-H with organic C-H to develop new methodologies for selective functionalization of o-carboranes via dehydrocoupling of cage B-H with C-H and then extend it to other X-H bonds (X = B, O, N, S). The advantages of this strategy are threefold: 1) prefunctionalized reagents are not required, making the method more atom economical and less wasteful; 2) complicated multi-step syntheses can be simplified to a straightforward one-pot process; 3) high functional group tolerance is expected. The project will result in the synthesis of a new class of cage boron functionalized carboranes with potential applications in many areas. Reaction mechanism elucidation is an intrinsic part of this proposal, hence the results will certainly enhance our fundamental understanding of transition metal catalyzed selective dehydrocoupling reactions, which in turn would shed light on how to more generally control selectivity in dehydrogenative cross-coupling reactions. 碳硼烷是一類由碳和硼原子組成的簇合物，被認為是苯環的三維結構類似物。碳硼烷衍生物在配位化學，醫藥和材料等領域具有特殊應用，因而受到了廣泛的關注。但是，碳硼烷特殊的穩定性和三維結構使得它們很難被官能團化。同弱酸性的碳硼烷碳氫鍵相比，選擇性地活化極性較弱的硼氫鍵更具挑戰。碳硼烷有十個處於相似化學環境的硼氫鍵，這使得獲取化學選擇性變得非常困難。最近，我們課題組報導了羧基導向的金屬鈀催化的選擇性碳硼烷硼氫鍵和端炔碳氫鍵的脫氫偶聯反應。基於這一結果，我們計劃將碳硼烷硼氫鍵活化和有機碳氫鍵/雜原子氫鍵活化結合起來，發展一系列新的脫氫偶聯的方法來修飾碳硼烷。這些新的方法將擁有以下三個優點：1）不需要預先修飾過的化學試劑，有更好的原子經濟性和更少的污染；2）複雜的多步反應能夠被簡化至一步法製備； 3）擁有更好的官能團耐受性和底物適應性。可以預見的是，這個研究將會產生一系列新的存在潛在應用的碳硼烷衍生物。反應機理的研究也是我們的一個重要目標。這個研究的結果將會提升我們對交叉脫氫偶聯反應本質的理解，從而幫助我們調控此類反應的選擇性。

14305017.label: Realisation of objectives
14305017.value: Carboranes, a class of carbon-boron molecular clusters, can be viewed as three-dimensional heterocyclics, analogues of benzene. They are finding many applications in coordination/ organometallic chemistry as versatile ligands, in medicine as boron neutron capture therapy agents and in supramolecular design/nanomaterials as useful building blocks. All this has recently drawn considerable attention to carborane chemistry. However, the exceptional thermal and chemical stable 3D structures of carboranes make their derivatization difficult, limiting their scope. The development of an efficient and general technique to functionalize carboranes would be a major advance. In general, cage C-H derivatization can be achieved via deprotonation as the C-H proton is weakly acidic (pKa ~23). In contrast functionalizing cage B-H bonds selectively is more challenging, owing to the relatively weak polarization of B-H bond and the similarity of the ten B-H vertices, and has been little explored. We have previously reported a carboxylic group-directed, palladium-catalyzed regioselective dehydrocoupling of cage B-H with the sp C-H of terminal alkynes for the synthesis of a variety of cage B(4)-alkynylated o-carboranes. Inspired by this preliminary result, we plan, in this proposal, to combine activation of cage B-H with organic C-H to develop new techniques for selective functionalization of o-carboranes via dehydrocoupling of cage B-H with C-H and then extend it to other X-H bonds (X = B, O, N). During the course of our study on imine-guided cage B-H activation, we accidently discovered a Rh-catalyzed cascade reaction of carboranyl N-4-chlorophenylimine with 2-butenone to generate the unexpected C,B-substituted o-carborane-fused tricyclic, in which one cage B-H and one sp2 C-H bonds were activated, companied with the construction of three new B-C and C-C bonds. After the optimization of the reaction conditions, we developed a regioselective and efficient Rh(III)-catalyzed cascade cyclization of carboranyl N-arylimines with vinyl ketones, leading to the facile synthesis of a wide variety of C,B-substituted carborane-fused N-polyheterocycles in high yields, which cannot be prepared by any other methods. In a simple one-pot process, cage B-H and aryl C-H bonds are activated compatibly along with the formation of three new B-C and C-C bonds. This work represents the first example of transition metal catalyzed cascade one-pot construction of polycycles in carborane chemistry, which may also provide useful reference for crafting the quinoline framework in organic synthesis. Another straightforward and efficient B-H/C-H dehydrocoupling of o-carborane with (hetero)arenes has been developed, resulting in a wide range of nitrogen-containing (hetero)aryl carborane derivatives for potential applications in medicinal chemistry and materials science. This work represents a rare example of carboxyl and pyridine directing groups co-guided dehydrogenative cross-coupling, which features a very broad substrate scope with a high tolerance of various functional groups. This work can also provide valuable references for controlling chemoselectivity in dehydrocoupling reactions via mixed directing-group strategy. We extended such a dehydrocoupling protocol to build B-N bond. Subsequently, A straightforward and efficient Ir-catalyzed cascade B-H/C-H and B-H/N-H dehydrocoupling has been achieved, leading to the facile synthesis of previously unavailable carborano-isoquinolinone derivatives in high yields with excellent regioselectivity from readily available carboranyl carboxylic acid and benzamide in a simple one-pot process. A series of α-carboranyl benzamides is also selectively prepared by tuning reaction conditions, suggesting that B-H/C-H dehydrocoupling occurs preferentially over B-H/N-H one. The traceless carboxylic acid directing group assists the first B-H activation and is in-situ removed after B-C cross-coupling. This work not only offers valuable references for the control of regioselectivity and chemoselectivity in cascade and dehydrocoupling reactions, but also provides a general and versatile method to prepare a wide variety of carborane-featuring functional molecules. In addition, a straightforward and efficient iridium-catalyzed dehydrogenative cross-coupling between o-carboranes and ammonia gas was achieved, leading to facile synthesis of a series of 3-NH2-o-carboranes. This new protocol allows chemical-oxidant-free B-H/N-H dehydrocoupling and generates H2 gas as the sole byproduct. This work not only opens up a new pathway for direct, efficient, and regioselective B-H amination of o-carboranes but also offers a valuable reference for organic C-H amination with NH3. We further extended such a dehydrocoupling protocol to build B-O bond. Accordingly, a regioselective and efficient Ir-catalyzed cascade B-H/C-H and B-H/O-H dehydrogenative cross-coupling has been achieved, resulting in the facile synthesis of unprecedented carborano-coumarin derivatives in high yields with excellent regioselectivity from readily available carboranyl carboxylic acid with benzoic acid in a simple one-pot process. By tuning reaction conditions, a series of B(4)-arylated o-carboranes were also selectively prepared, indicating that B-H/C-H dehydrocoupling happened preferentially over B-H/O-H dehydrocoupling. Moreover, the results of control experiments proved that both oxidants and the traceless directing group -COOH were essential for the cascade cyclization. This work not only provides a tunable platform for the synthesis of a large collection of functionalized carborane derivatives, which are otherwise unavailable or quite difficult to be prepared, but also provides valuable reference on the control of regioselectivity and chemoselectivity in cascade dehydrogenative cross-coupling reactions. Another Pd-catalyzed intramolecular dehydrogenative coupling of cage BH and phenol OH for the convenient construction of B–O bonds has also been achieved, leading to a series of 1,3- and 1,4-o-carboranobenzoxaborole derivatives in high yields. This represents a new route to carborane-fused polyheterocycles that otherwise are inaccessible by other means. On the other hand, a regioselective palladium-catalyzed formal OH/BH dehydrogenative cross-coupling reactions was achieved for the regioselective construction of o-carborane-fused oxaboroles through oxidative annulation of 1-hydroxy-o-carborane with internal alkynes. The reaction was compatible with a broad substrate scope including diaryl or alkyl aryl acetylenes with a variety of substituents. Further ring-closure reaction of the resultant products gave a new class of carborane-fused large π conjugated systems for potential applications in organic materials. In summary, all research objectives in the proposal have been accomplished. We have developed a toolbox for the construction of cage B-C/N/O bonds in a catalytic manner via dehydrogenative cross-coupling reactions. Such reactions represent one of the most straightforward and effective methods in synthetic chemistry with high atom economy and bond-forming efficiency, as non-prefunctionalized reagents are employed as coupling partners.

14305017.label: Major findings and research outcome
14305017.value: (1) Development of transition metal catalyzed selective dehydrocoupling of cage B-H with organic CH bond for the construction of B-C bond in the functionalization of carboranes (Pubs. #1-#5, #10 and #11). The following new methods have been developed: (1) a Rh-catalyzed cascade reaction of carboranyl N-4-chlorophenylimine with 2-butenone was achieved to generate the unexpected C,B-substituted o-carborane-fused tricyclic, in which one cage B-H and one sp2 C-H bonds were activated, companied with the construction of three new B-C and C-C bonds, (2) a straightforward and efficient B-H/C(sp2)-H dehydrocoupling of o-carborane with (hetero)arenes was developed, resulting in a wide range of nitrogen-containing (hetero)aryl carborane derivatives via mixed a directing-group strategy, and (3) a Cu-catalyzed B-H/C(sp)-H dehydrocoupling of o-carborane with terminal alkynes was developed to prepare a new class of B(4)-alkynylated o-carboranes. (2) Development of transition metal catalyzed selective dehydrocoupling of cage B-H with NH bond for the construction of B-N bond in the functionalization of carboranes (Pubs. #6 and #13). A straightforward and efficient Ir-catalyzed cascade B-H/C-H and B-H/N-H dehydrocoupling has been achieved, leading to the facile synthesis of previously unavailable carborano-isoquinolinone derivatives in high yields with excellent regioselectivity from readily available carboranyl carboxylic acid and benzamide in a simple one-pot process. On the other hand, a very efficient iridium-catalyzed dehydrogenative cross-coupling between o-carboranes and ammonia gas has also been achieved, leading to facile synthesis of a series of 3-NH2-o-carboranes. This new protocol allows chemical-oxidant-free B-H/N-H dehydrocoupling and generates H2 gas as the sole byproduct. (3) Development of transition metal catalyzed selective dehydrocoupling of cage B-H with OH bond for the construction of B-O bond in the functionalization of carboranes (Pubs. #7, #8 and #12). A regioselective and efficient Ir-catalyzed cascade B-H/C-H and B-H/O-H dehydrogenative cross-coupling has been achieved, resulting in the facile synthesis of unprecedented carborano-coumarin derivatives in high yields with excellent regioselectivity from readily available carboranyl carboxylic acid with benzoic acid in a simple one-pot process. Another Pd-catalyzed intramolecular dehydrogenative coupling of cage BH and phenol OH for the convenient construction of B–O bonds has also been achieved, leading to a series of 1,3- and 1,4-o-carboranobenzoxaborole derivatives in high yields. In summary, this original work has resulted in 13 peer-reviewed articles published in international chemistry journals including J. Am. Chem. Soc. (x 3), Chem. Commun. (x 1), Chem. Eur. J. (x1), Chem. Sci. (x 1), Sci. China Chem. (x 1), Dalton Trans. (x 2), Chin. J. Chem. (x 2), Organometallics (x 1) and Chem. Soc. Rev. (x 1). PI was invited to give two keynote and one invited lectures at international conferences. Two PhD students have been trained with one being awarded HKPFS.

14305017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14305017.value: Carboranes, a class of carbon-boron molecular clusters, can be viewed as three-dimensional analogues of benzene. They are finding many applications in coordination/ organometallic chemistry as versatile ligands, in medicine as boron neutron capture therapy agents and in supramolecular design/nanomaterials as useful building blocks. All this has recently drawn considerable attention to carborane chemistry. However, the exceptional thermal and chemical stable 3D structures of carboranes make their derivatization difficult, limiting their scope. The development of an efficient and general technique to functionalize carboranes would be a major advance. In this project, we combine activation of cage B-H with organic C-H to develop new methodologies for catalytic selective functionalization of o-carboranes via dehydrocoupling of cage B-H with C-H and then extend it to other X-H bonds (X = B, O, N). Such a dehydrocoupling strategy represents one of the most straightforward and effective methods in synthetic chemistry with high atom economy and bond-forming efficiency, as non-prefunctionalized reagents are employed as coupling partners. Accordingly, a large class of new functionalized carborane molecules with exo cage B-C/O/N bond(s) has been synthesized in high yields with excellent regioselectivity in a catalytic manner. They may find applications in materials and medicine.

14305117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14305117.value: Carboranes, three-dimensional relatives of benzene, are a class of boron hydride clusters in which one or more BH vertices are replaced by CH units. Due to their unique steric/electronic properties, functional carboranes are now finding a broad range of applications encompassing materials, polymers, catalysis, organometallic/coordination chemistry and more. As a result, increasing efforts have been directed towards the area of carborane functionalization. Compared to the relatively well-developed methods for cage carbon functionalization of carboranes, selective cage boron functionalization of carboranes, however, still represents a challenging task. We recently demonstrated that by utilizing visible-light-mediated photocatalysis, selective cage B(3) (hetero)arylation can be achieved efficiently via a boron-centered carboranyl radical (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed., 2016, 55, 3166). This preliminary result suggests that, comparing with traditional methods, cage boron-functionalization of carboranes can be realized under very mild reaction conditions (metal-, base-, ligands-free, room temperature). In this proposal, we plan to systematically expand this reaction to other synthetically useful transformations for the preparation of a wide variety of functionalized carboranes containing cage B-X bonds (X = C(sp3/sp2/sp), O, N, S, P, and halogen) via the intermediacy of the boron-centered carboranyl radicals. Reaction mechanism elucidation is an intrinsic part of this proposal. Comparison of the similarities and differences between such non-classical boron-centered carboranyl radicals with classical boryl radicals is also an interesting topic. It is anticipated that this research will provide a new toolbox for cage boron-functionalization of carborane derivatives and enhance our fundamental understanding of the reaction chemistry of boron-centered carboranyl radicals.
