14305117.label: Realisation of objectives
14305117.value: Carboranes are finding a broad range of applications encompassing materials, polymers, catalysis, organometallic/coordination chemistry and more. As a result, increasing efforts have been directed towards the area of carborane functionalization. In this project, we have developed new methods for the functionalization of carboranes via the intermediacy of the boron-centered carboranyl radicals. We reported the preliminary results that, in the presence of visible-light and organic dye photocatalyst, the boron-centered carboranyl radical was efficiently produced from 3-diazonium-o-carborane tetrafluoroborate. We then developed a visible-light-promoted cage B-thiazolylation of o-carborane via the intermediacy of cage boron centered carboranyl radical. In the presence of 1 mol% Ir photosensitizer, treatment of carboranyl diazonium salt with 1-isocyano-2-(methylthio)benzene under the irradiation of blue LED in CH3CN at room temperature afforded the cyclized product B(3)-thiazolylated o-carborane in 89% isolated yield. No reaction was observed without the addition of either Ir-photocatalyst or blue LED, suggesting their crucial roles. A total of 22 substrates were examined. Unfortunately, Hong Kong’s 2019 social unrest, followed by COVID-19 pandemic and new regulations on chemical substances made the delivery of NH3 gas to Hong Kong impossible in the past 3 years. Since NH3 gas is an essential reagent for the preparation of 3-diazonium-o-carborane tetrafluoroborate, the lack of NH3 gas results in the incompletion of the aforementioned work, which also makes the other related works very difficult to perform. We will complete this work when NH3 gas becomes available in Hong Kong. We then have to find other methods to generate boron-centered carboranyl radicals. After many attempts, we found that under the irradiation of blue LED light, single-electron-transfer (SET) from the excited metal complex to iodo-o-carboranes can efficiently generate the desired boron-centered carboranyl radicals. Such SET strategy offers a brand new entry into carboranyl radicals. These radicals can be efficiently trapped by a variety of (hetero)arenes to give a class of (hetero)arylated o-carboranes in high yields. Accordingly, we developed a general method to efficiently generate a class of boron-centered carboranyl radicals at the B(3)-, B(4)- and B(9)-positions via a visible-light excited Pd(0)/Pd(I) pathway using iodo-o-carboranes as the starting materials. These hypervalent boron-centered radicals exhibit different electrophilicity, and follow the trend B(3) > B(4) > B(9). They serve as useful intermediates for the synthesis of a wide range of cage B-(hetero)arylated o-carboranes under very mild conditions at room temperature. This work not only offers an alternative method for the generation of boron-centered carboranyl radicals, but also demonstrates that photoexcited Pd catalysis can result in a new reactivity mode for palladium-catalyzed functionalization of boron clusters. Having achieved the aforementioned visible-light excited Pd(0)/Pd(I) strategy for the generation of carboranyl radicals, we then wondered if base metals such as Ni could undergo such a single-electron transfer (SET) process for the generation of boron-centered carboranyl radicals. After many attempts, we developed a visible-light-promoted abstraction of iodine atom from iodo-o-carboranes by Ni(I) species to generate hypervalent boron-centered carboranyl radicals at different cage vertices B(3), B(4) and B(9). They exhibit diverse reactivity patterns towards (hetero)arenes, leading to a wide range of (mono-/di-)(hetero)arylated o-carboranes at room temperature. This work not only opens up new avenues for the vertex-specific functionalization of boron clusters by merging photochemistry with Ni catalysis, but also provides valuable reference for the generation of other boryl radicals via SET process. We then extended our research to include the chemistry of carbon-centered carboranyl radicals. Homolytic cleavage of cage C-I bond under UV light irradiation results in the formation of carbon-centered carboranyl radical which can be efficiently trapped by alkenes and terminal alkynes. This represents a very promising approach for clean, efficient, transition-metal-free and cheap synthesis of a large class of 1-alkenyl-o-carboranes, 1-alkynyl-o-carboranes and o-carborane-fused cyclics. As this reaction does not require strong bases, photocatalysts and high temperatures, it has a broad substrate scope. The mechanistic studies indicate that the reaction proceeds via the radical process. The isolation of carborane-fused spiro product suggests that the reaction involves the formation of a spiro radical species. This work represents significant advances over the known methods for the synthesis of 1-alkynyl-o-carboranes, and also sets a very good example for the functionalization of boron clusters using photochemistry. In summary, we have developed new strategies for the generation of boron-centered carboranyl radicals at the B(3)-, B(4)-, and B(9)-positions via visible-light promoted SET from excited transition metal complexes to iodo-o-carboranes, or for the generation of carbon-centered carboranyl radical via homolytic cleavage of cage C-I bond under UV light irradiation. These open-shell reactive radicals can react with a variety of organic compounds for the preparation of a large class of cage B- or cage C-functionalized o-carboranes under mild conditions with high yields.

14305117.label: Major findings and research outcome
14305117.value: (1) Development of Visible-Light-Promoted Nickel-Catalyzed Cross-Coupling of Iodocarboranes with (Hetero)Arenes via Boron-Centered Carboranyl Radicals (Pub. #6). A general strategy for the generation of hypervalent boron-centered carboranyl radicals at the B(3), B(4) and B(9) positions has been developed for the first time via visible-light-promoted iodine atom abstraction from iodo-o-carboranes by low-valent nickel complex. These radicals react with various (hetero)arenes to afford a wide range of cage B-arylated carborane derivatives at room temperature in very good to excellent yields with a broad substrate scope. Their electrophilicities are dependent on the vertex charges of the cage and follow the order B(3) > B(4) > B(9). Both visible light and nickel catalyst are proved critical to the generation of boron-centered carboranyl radicals. The involvement of boron radicals is supported by control experiments. A reaction mechanism associated with these reactions is also proposed. This strategy offers a new protocol for the generation of boron-centered carboranyl radicals at the selected boron vertex, leading to a facile synthesis of a large class of cage boron substituted carborane molecules. (2) Development of Visible-Light-Induced Palladium-Catalyzed Cross-Coupling of Iodocarboranes with (Hetero)Arenes via Boron-Centered Carboranyl Radicals (Pub. #7). This work describes a general method for the efficient generation of a class of boron-centered carboranyl radicals at the B(3)-, B(4)- and B(9)-positions via a visible-light excited Pd(0)/Pd(I) pathway using readily available iodo-o-carboranes as the starting materials. They are useful intermediates for the synthesis of a variety of cage B-(hetero)arylated o-carboranes at room temperature. The associated reaction mechanism is also proposed on the basis of control experiments. (3) Development of Transition-Metal-Free UV Light Promoted Cross-Coupling Reaction of Iodocarboranes with Terminal Alkynes via Carbon-Centered Carboranyl Radicals: Synthesis of 1-Alkynyl-o-Carboranes and Carborane-Fused Cyclics (Pub. #2). A transition-metal-free coupling protocol between iodocarboranes and terminal alkynes enabled by light at room temperature has been developed, leading to the synthesis of a variety of 1-alkynyl-o-carboranes. Moreover, following this strategy, the introduction of 1-I-3-aryl-o-carboranes or 1-I-2-aryl-o-carboranes results in the formation of o-carborane-fused cyclics. Interestingly, when 1-I-3-(p-R-C6H4)-o-carboranes are chosen as coupling partners, unexpected R-group migration products are also isolated. Based on the results of control experiments and isolation of the key intermediates, a possible reaction mechanism is then proposed, involving the formation of spiro radical species. (4) Development of Transition-Metal-Free UV Light Promoted Cross-Coupling Reaction of Iodocarboranes with Unactivated Alkenes via Carbon-Centered Carboranyl Radicals (Pub. #4). A synthetic method to alkenylated-o-carboranes via photoalkenylation of iodocarboranes with unactivated alkenes has been achieved. This strategy features a transition-metal-free protocol, light-promoted reaction with mild reaction condition, broad substrate scope and good functional group tolerance. Control experiments suggest that the reaction may involve the cage C-centered radical species. In summary, this original work has resulted in 7 peer-reviewed articles published in international chemistry journals including J. Am. Chem. Soc. (x 2), Chem. Sci. (x 1), Dalton Trans. (x 1), Chin. J. Chem. (x 1), Chem. Soc. Rev. (x 1) and Org. Lett (x 1, under review). PI was invited to give one plenary, one keynote and two invited lectures at international conferences. Three PhD students have been trained and graduated.

However, the exceptional thermal and chemical stable 3D structures of carboranes make their derivatization difficult, limiting their application scope. In this project, we have developed new strategies for the generation of boron-centered carboranyl radicals at the B(3)-, B(4)-, and B(9)-positions via visible-light promoted single electron transfer from excited transition metal complexes to iodo-o-carboranes, or for the generation of carbon-centered carboranyl radical via homolytic cleavage of cage C-I bond under UV light irradiation. These open-shell reactive radicals can react with a variety of organic compounds for the preparation of a large class of cage B- or cage C-functionalized o-carboranes under mild conditions with high yields. These functionalized o-carboranes may find applications in materials and medicine.

14305317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14305317.value: 這項提出的工作的目的是使用鹵素鍵化合物作為有機催化劑來開發有效的鹵化反應。 不飽和化合物的鹵化反應是一個重要的有機基礎轉化。所得的鹵代產物是廣泛出現在製藥工業和材料化學中的有用分子模塊。金屬路易斯酸經常用作各種鹵化反應中的催化劑，但是這種催化方法通常具有低的官能團耐受性。 路易斯鹼性有機催化劑被認為是金屬催化劑更環保的替代物, 並已經被用於一系列親電鹵化反應中。我們的研究小組多年來一直從事路易斯鹼性有機催化劑的研究工作（例如，Yeung, Y.-Y. et al. J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2014, 136, 5627; Chem. Commun. 2013, 49, 7985) 。雖然路易斯鹼催化的條件溫和，反應的官能團相容性較高，但在其他底物的鹵化反應中相對地無效。 鹵素鍵化合物是一類新興的有機催化劑。鹵素鍵化合物中鹵素原子的缺電子sigma-孔可以作為“有機”路易斯酸。雖然鹵素鍵催化劑已經在一些反應中被應用，但是它們在親電鹵化反應中的應用尚未被研究。 在最近未發表的研究工作中，我們已經認識到單官能鹵鍵有機催化劑可以催化一系列親電鹵環化反應，包括鹵碳環化，鹵內酯化和鹵醚化反應。此外，我們將鹵素鍵元素併入手性雙功能體系中。所得氨基鹵鍵雙官能手性有機催化劑可以促進不對稱的鹵內酯化反應，並具有明顯的對映選擇性。基於這些初步結果，在本文提出的工作中，我們計劃進一步探討鹵素鍵有機催化劑在各種親電鹵化反應中的應用。預計此新開發的催化方案可以成為有機合成中的有力工具。

14305317.label: Realisation of objectives
14305317.value: 1. Prepare a series of mono- and bi-functional halogen-bond organocatalysts At the initial stage of the project, a series of halogen bond organocatalysts were prepared according to the literature or modified literature procedures. Iodine was used as the halogen bond donor atom. Various electron-withdrawing substituents such as pyridinium and imidzaolium cations were used to enhance the strength of the halogen bond donors. Typically, iodopyridines and iodoimidazoles were alkylated to give the corresponding iodopyridinium and iodoimidazolium salts. Alternatively, the synthesis could be achieved by treating imidazolium chloride salts with sodium hydride followed by the addition of molecular iodine. Weakly coordinating counter anions such as triflate were used to minimize the poisoning effect on the halogen bond donors. Bifunctional halogen-bond organocatalysts were prepared by incorporating halogen bond donors into bifunctional catalyst scaffolds such as amino alcohols. Halogen bond catalysts with other halogen atoms such as bromine and chlorine were also prepared in order to study the effect of halogen bond in catalysis. 2. Examine the performance of the halogen-bond organocatalysts in various intra- and intermolecular electrophilic halogenation reactions. The halogen bond catalysts were used in some catalytic reactions. Their catalytic performances were examined. Parameters such as reaction time, temperature, solvent, and concentration were evaluated. Two types of reactions were testified: electrophilic halo-carbocyclization and nucleophilic addition to N-acylimminium ions. Halogen bond catalyzed halocarbocyclization Evaluation of the catalyst performance in the bromocyclization of N-cinnamyl sulfonamide was conducted using N-bromoamides as the halogen sources. It was found that iodopyridinium and iodoimidazolium halogen bond catalysts gave appreciable conversions. Structural analogue that bears no iodine could not catalyze the reaction, which further highlights the role of the iodine atom. Replacing the iodine atom in catalyst with bromine or chlorine atom gradually decreased the catalytic performance, which could be attributed to their weaker XB strength due to the lower polarizability of the halogen bond donor atom. Pentafluoroiodobenzene that bears multiple electron-withdrawing substituents still returned negligible conversion. In addition, a dramatic drop in the reaction efficiency was observed when the iodopyridinium was replaced by the neutral halogen bond catalyst 4-iodopyridine. These results suggest that the cationic character of iodopyridinium might play a crucial role in enhancing the electron-withdrawing property and the halogen bond strength in the organocatalytic halogenation process. It was noticed that the cyclization of N-cinnamyl sulfonamide could not be achieved efficiently by other organocatalysts such as hydrogen-bond catalysts, Lewis bases, Brønsted bases, Brønsted acids, which clearly demonstrated the unique role of halogen bond organocatalyst in halogenation reaction. Next, the substrate scope was examined. In general, the halocarbocyclization of N-cinnamyl sulfonamides proceeded smoothly to give the desired tetrahydroquinolines in good efficiency, excellent diastereoselectivity (dr > 99:1) and regioselectivity (endocyclization). Bromocarbocyclization of O-phenyl cinnamyl ethers that could give rise to valuable chromane building blocks was also examined. To our delight, the XB-catalyzed carbocyclization of O-phenyl cinnamyl ethers was applicable to substrates with electron-rich or electron-deficient substituent at the phenol ether or the cinnamyl chain. An interesting phenomenon was observed during the mechanistic investigation; when we monitored the halogen bond-catalyzed bromocarbocyclization of N-cinnamyl sulfonamide by time-dependent 1H NMR experiment, unexpectedly, it was realized that the reaction progress fits a sigmodal curve, which suggests that an autocatalytic component might exist in the reaction system. Next, a more detailed investigation was conducted aiming at identifying the species that caused the autocatalytic behavior. Among the products/by-products that could be generated from the reaction, it was found that the addition of stoichiometric amount of 5,5-dimethylhydantoin (DMH) or mono-N-bromo-5,5-dimethylhydantoin (MBDMH) as an additive could greatly accelerate the bromocarbocyclization of N-cinnamyl sulfonamide. On the basis of the mechanistic studies, we rationalize that the halogen bond organocatalyst might coordinate with the carbonyl group of DBDMH to enhance the electrophilicity of the Br for the bromination reaction. In addition, we speculate that DMH or MBDMH, which would be generated after each of the reaction cycle, might interact with the halogen bond-hydantoin anion to give a more reactive intermediate. The reaction rate would increase at the later stage of the reaction since the concentration of DMH and MBDMH would increase in accordance to the reaction progress. Nucleophilic addition to N-acylimminium ions N-acylimminium ions (NAI) are an important class of synthetic intermediates in organic synthesis. This class of reactive intermediates can be transformed into a wide spectrum of useful products through reactions with various nucleophiles such as indoles, malonates and silyl enol ether. We hypothesized that halogen bond could serve as a mild and organocatalytic protocol for the environmentally-benign generation of NAI with high functional group compatibility with diverse class of nucleophiles. At the outset of our investigation, N,O-aminal and allyltrimethylsilane were employed as the reaction partners. TMSCl was used as an activator that could convert N,O-aminal into the corresponding preactivated N-acylimminium chloride. We reasoned that the chloride anion could interact with halogen bond catalyst to undergo anion-metathesis and give the highly reactive N-acylimminium triflate, which could be subsequently attacked by nucleophile to furnish the allylation product. It was realized that the reaction proceeded smoothly in the presence of iodoimidazolium halogen bond catalyst with triflate or hexafluoroantimonate counter-anion as the catalyst. In contrast, the catalyst with tetrafluoroborate as the anion gave no reaction. These results highlighted the intrigued anion-dependence of catalytic effect in halogen bond catalysis. We speculate that the tetrafluoroborate might act as a fluoride source that might poison the halogen bond donor. The catalytic effect completely diminished when replacing the iodine atom in catalyst with hydrogen, indicating the crucial role of the halogen bond donor in this catalytic transformation. The reaction was also found to be sensitive to the bulkiness of the catalyst substituent. With the optimized catalyst in hand, various kinds of silyl-nucleophiles were subjected to the evaluation. In general, the desired products were obtained in good yield and diastereoselectivity. Other than silyl nucleophiles, different electron-rich aromatics, including acid sensitive arenes (thiophene, furan, pyrrole) alkoxybenzenes and indoles were also studied. The regioselectivity and chemical yields were generally excellent. When phenols were employed as the nucleophilic partners, the C-attack products was furnished exclusively. 1,3-dicarbonyl compound was also able to deliver the desired C-attack product. The reaction was found to be compatible with substrates that are absent of the aryl moiety. In addition, the reaction was readily scalable and the product was still obtained in quantitative yield when the reaction was conducted at 1 mmol scale. In addition, the halogen bond catalyst could be recycled quantitatively and reused in the new rounds of reactions without diminishment of catalytic performance, which was not readily achievable using moisture sensitive Lewis acids. Further experimentations indicated that achieving the reaction with both high yield and dr is not a trivial task. For instance, Lewis acids [Ti(OiPr)4, Cu(CH3CN)4BF4, AuOTf, Zn(OTf)2], Brønsted acid (TfOH), and dihydrogen bond catalyst (Schreiner’s thiourea) gave either low efficiency or low d.r.. In sharp contrast, the iodoimidazolium catalysts with various counter-anions furnished the desired product in good yield and dr. 3. Publication of the results in world-class peer-reviewed international journals Under this project, two high-impact publications (1 Angew. Chem. Int. Ed., 1 Org. Lett.) were produced. In addition, a manuscript about bifunctional halogen bond catalysis is underway. The detail appears in Part C. Overall, all objectives have been fully realized and a summary of the major research outcomes is shown below.

14305317.label: Major findings and research outcome
14305317.value: 1. A halogen-bond catalyzed bromocarbocyclization has been developed (Part C, output 1). N-methyl 4-iodopyridinium triflate is used as the halogen-bond organocatalyst. The soft Lewis acid nature of halogen bond catalyst allows the bromocarbocyclization of N-cinnamyl sulfonamides and O¬-cinnamyl phenyl ethers to proceed smoothly in high chemoselectivity and regioselectivity. The reactions proceed smoothly in high chemoselectivity and regioselectivity. The resulting heterocyclic products are useful building blocks of pharmaceuticals. The halogen handles on the products can be manipulated easily to give valuable derivatives. This research represents the first example of proof-of-concept of halogen-bond organocatalyst-promoted electrophilic halogenation. Mechanistic study suggests the autocatalytic nature of this reaction. 2. N-acylimminium ions are an important class of synthetic intermediates to produce diverse products upon treatment with different nucleophiles. Most of the reported catalytic protocol involved moisture-sensitive Lewis acids or transition metal. In this piece of research, we developed an organocatalytic version by using halogen-bond catalyst as mild Lewis acid through anion-abstraction strategy (Part C, output 2). N,O¬-aminals were used as substrates to generate N-acylimminium ions selectivity through in situ activating strategy with TMSCl and anion-binding catalysis. The mechanistic studies pointed out that the halogen-bonding catalyst served as an anion-binder. A wide range of C-nucleophiles were compatible with the reaction and the desired products were obtained in good yield and selectivity. 3. In our preliminary study, it was found that halogen bond catalysis, halogen bond donors with chiral counter-anion could act as chiral catalysts in asymmetric synthesis. Chiral BINOL-phosphate anion and achiral halogen bond cation were used in the study. It was realized that the catalytic system gave better ee than that of the reaction with BINOL-phosphoric acid alone. This result provides an opportunity for the asymmetric catalysis by tuning the halogen bond donors with cationic substituents.

14305317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14305317.value: Lewis acid catalysis is widely applied in various catalytic transformations. While there are already a number of Lewis acids have been developed, many of them are moisture-sensitive. Halogen bond catalysts can be considered as milder alternatives of Lewis acids. Their steric and electronic demands can be altered easily by changing the substituents. Since iodine-based halogen bond catalysts can be considered as soft Lewis acids, they are potentially useful in chemoselective transformations. Indeed, it was shown in our study that the bromination happened at the olefins instead of the arenes while many existing catalytic methods (e.g. Lewis base catalysis) preferentially brominate arenes. In addition, based on our study it was found that a halogen bond donor with a chiral counter-anion is useful in asymmetric catalytic reaction. In future, we will further explore the applications of halogen bond catalysis in other chemo and/or stereoselective reactions.

14305317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14305317.value: Many chemical manufacturing processes are energy- and atom-inefficient, leading to the generation of significant amount of wastes and emissions. To meet the growing demand on energy for the global economy, it becomes more important than ever to look for green alternatives of energy-efficient processes. However, the current state of technology lags behind the schedule to meet the international targets. Small molecule catalysts are considered as nanoscale molecular machines that can provide control in various transformations at molecular level. Catalysis underpins many industries as over 90% of chemicals produced rely on the use of a catalyst to certain extent. It is obvious that catalytic processes play a key role in improving air and water quality, reduce energy consumption and emission, and offer solutions to long-term sustainable energy and environmental protection. In the current project, we have developed a number of useful catalytic protocols based on halogen bond. Our work on the novel catalysis provides a very useful tool for various transformations. In addition, organocatalysis is mild and metal-free, which are attractive features to the manufacturing sectors. The research endeavor results in the synthesis of a wide range of useful building blocks for various medicinal and chemical applications.

14305417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14305417.value: Energy crisis and environmental pollution are the two pressing challenges for the human beings. Among various widely-used methods to solve these issues, photocatalysis is considered as one of the most promising techniques. This method is driven by sunlight to decompose pollutant molecules for environmental remediation, to split water for hydrogen production, or to reduce CO2 for valuable fuels. An easy-prepared and high efficient photocatalyst is crucial for the photocatalysis. However, the conventional metal oxide photocatalysts suffer from lower charge separation efficiency, narrow-spectrum-photo response, and possible secondary pollution. Red phosphorus, with the advantages of earth abundant, low cost and low toxic, can be used as a new efficient photocatalyst for various photocatalytic applications. The potential of red phosphorus has been demonstrated by our recent record breaking photo-activity towards the hydrogen evolution in the family of elemental photocatalysts. Besides, red phosphorus shows superior stability during the photocatalytic process. However, due to its low conductivity and fast charge recombination, the potential of the red phosphorus has not been fully realized. As a newly-discovered elemental photocatalyst, crystalline red phosphorus and its composites are still rarely reported. Thus, this proposal aims to prepare various novel photocatalysts of red phosphorus based composites by using the widespread phosphorus as raw materials. Herein, the photo(electro)chemical property of the red phosphorus will be optimized by controlling their lattice structure via non-metal ions doping (such as B, S). Besides, their performance is expected to be enhanced via combination of red phosphorus and other functional materials like graphene or g-C3N4. The products will be investigated as photocatalysts for hydrogen evolution and environmental remediation. 能源危機和環境污染是目前人類面臨的兩個主要挑戰。在解決這兩個問題的方法中，光催化技術被認為是最有前途的。光催化技術可以通過太陽能來實現降解污染物和分解水產氫。合成一種能簡單製備的，有高活性的光催化劑是這種技術的關鍵。但是，傳統的金屬氧化物光催化劑存在電荷傳輸效率低，窄光譜回應和容易產生二次污染等問題。紅磷是一種廣泛存在的，低成本和低毒性的新型高效光催化劑。我們最近的研究中發現，紅磷光催化劑的活性在目前已報導過的元素光催化劑中是最高的。而且，紅磷在光催化的過程中表現出很好的穩定性。但因為它低的導電性和容易複合的光生電荷，紅磷在光催化中的潛力還沒有充分開發出來。作為一種新發現的元素光催化劑，結晶相的紅磷和它的複合物還很少被報導。所以，本研究計畫主要目的是製備一種新型的結晶相的基於紅磷的元素光催化劑。本研究計畫中，通過製備結晶相的紅磷和非金屬離子（像硼，硫）摻雜的紅磷，我們期待可以提高紅磷在光催化和光電催化中的性能。同時，通過紅磷和其它功能性材料的複合，比如石墨烯和氮化碳等，我們期待能製備高效的紅磷光催化劑。我們的產品期待能應用在在光催化產氫和環境污染等方面。

14305417.label: Realisation of objectives
14305417.value: At the early stage of the project, we confirmed that highly crystalline red phosphorus could be prepared by a simple thermal vapor deposition. Amorphous red phosphorus powders were placed in a quartz capsule. The powders were heated to 550 °C at 5 °C per minute, held for 2 h, cooled to 300 °C (holding temperature) at 2 °C per minute and held for 10 h, and finally cool to room temperature at 2 °C per minute. After the thermal treatment, the crystallized red P was washed with D.I. water and ethanol. A series of red P-based were prepared including coupling with bismuth (see the first publication attached) and reduced graphene oxide (see the second publication attached). Some of these new materials were fabricated into a photoelectrode for photoelectrochemical water splitting. Mechanisms for the enhanced activities were proposed as shown in the attached publications.

14305417.value: By adding bismuth nanoproplets in the synthesis of crystalline red P microbelts, we achieved excellent charge polarization Electrons accumulate at the two ends of the microbelts which become negatively charged, while the middle section is positive. In an aqueous solution, the PMBs can trigger water reduction to produce hydrogen at their negative-charged ends. Compared with where charge carriers are randomly distributed, the highly-polarized PMBs exhibit ten times enhancement in photocatalytic hydrogen production. An explanation for this interesting light-induced polarization effect is provided based on experimental results and theoretical calculations. Our findings may shed new light on the future development of high-efficiency P-based photocatalytic devices and systems. Details are availble in the first publication. We synthesized a red P/RGO (reduced graphene oxide) composite in a one-step ampoule chemical vapor deposition synthesis that formed a conducive interface between the red P photocatalyst and the RGO acceptor for efficient interfacial charge transport. As substantiated through photoelectrochemical characterization and ultrafast (femtoseconds) transient absorption spectroscopy, the interfacing with RGO provided a rapid pathway for the photocharges in red P to be interfacially separated, thereby circumventing the slower the charge trapping process. As a result, up to a sevenfold increase in the photocatalytic hydrogen production rate (apparent quantum yield = 3.1% at 650 nm) was obtained for the red P/RGO relative to the pristine red P. Details are shown in the second publication.

14305417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14305417.value: It would be worthwhile to explore the potential of the new red P-based photocatalysts for carbon dioxide reduction, ammonia synthesis and hydrogon peroxide formation.

14305417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14305417.value: Among various methods for solving energy and environmental problems, photocatalysis is considered as one of the most promising techniques. We have developed two new classes of easy-prepared and high efficient red phosphorus-based photocatalysts in this project. The first one contains bismuth to achieve excellent charge isolation for enhanced photocatalytic activity. The second one is coupled with a conductive substrate for improved charge transport. These new approaches may revolutionize the design of future photocatalysts for large-scale applications.

14305517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14305517.value: 本計劃的主要目標是為多元時間序列的長期漸近方差矩陣發展一個穩健, 統計與運算有效的估計量. 長期漸近方差矩陣, 是時間序列的樣本平均數之漸近共變異數矩陣. 它是用於統計程序中標準化的重要工具, 常用於建構時間序列迴歸系數的置信區間, 變點分析, 馬可夫鏈蒙地卡羅法的收歛診斷等. 長期漸近方差矩陣的應用, 在很多領域如統計學, 計量經濟學, 電腦科學及運籌學均受到一定重視. 近年, 高頻率或高維度的時間序列數據十分常見. 所以, 遞歸估計與 高維度的長期漸近方差矩陣估計也是重要的研究方向. 作為檢定統計量中標準化的量, 長期漸近方差矩陣極需準確與穩健的估計來控制統計程序的偏差. 但是, 即使在單元的時候, 有效地估計長期漸近方差值已很具挑戰性. 通常, 長期漸近矩陣方差是用自我共變異函數的加權總和來估計的. 這些加權一般取決於稱為核的函數形. 而每個核都需要指定一個頻寛用來控制自我共變異函數的遲延期數. 實用上, 我們要找出最優的頻寛使得長期漸近方差矩陣估計的均方誤差為最小. 但是, 這樣的估計方法有兩個缺點. 首先, 尋找最優頻寛時有一循環問題. 具體來說, 對於所有核, 最優的頻寛都與長期漸近方差矩陣—即我們要估計的數值有關. 其實, 最優的頻寛更與另一更難估計的, 與數據相依的平滑度參數有關. 所以, 最優的長期漸近方差矩陣估計是實際上不能算出的. 第二, 即使較平滑的核 會有更少 偏差和更快的收歛速度, 但這結果只對弱相關性的時間序列有效. 雖然相關性強度的估計對核的階數(核的平滑度)非常重要, 現有文獻並沒有有系統的方法來應付此問題. 順帶一題, 長期漸近方差矩陣也可透過子抽樣/重抽樣 來估計, 但此等方法需要選取數據集區的長度. 而選取最優的數據集區遇上的困難基本上與選取最優的核階數的困難相同. 要克服上述問題, 及向最優的長期漸近方差矩陣估計方法邁進一步, 我們提出一套新類型的核, 而它的最優頻寛不會與本身長期漸近方差矩陣的數值及平滑參數有關. 所以, 這避閧了困難的頻寛選擇問題. 我們推測, 在特定之相關強度的時間序列中, 我們提出的長期漸近方差矩陣估計量的風險為常數. 所以, 這估計量為大中取小最佳. 此外, 我們將嘗試以創新的方法, 以估計量的誤差作多元解析度分解, 來克服選擇核階數的問題 . 透過此方法, 我們可以比較不同核的估計量之有限樣本均方誤差. 我們推測以此選出的核階數在有限樣本中將有最佳的 L2表現. 為了滿足大數據分析的需求, 我們還考慮將以上提出之估算法推廣到遞歸和高維度的情況. 這研究將會得出一個統計與運算有效的長期漸近方差矩陣估計量. 此計劃提出的估計量適用於普遍的相關隨機過程, 高維度和海量的數據, 將在大數據年代為各個科研領域的研究員和從業者提供統計推論的有效工具.

14305517.label: Major findings and research outcome
14305517.value: In this project, we introduce a novel concept of converging kernels for constructing time-average variance constant (TAVC) estimators. Specifically, the class of converging kernel functions is designed to be dependent on the bandwidth so that the unknown parameters in the squared-bias and variance term can be factored out. Consequently, the optimal bandwidths can be computed easily, and most importantly, are free of unknown parameters. We obtain the precise convergence rate of the mean squared error of the estimator and prove that the new estimator has a constant risk asymptotically. We also developed practical implementations for choosing the optimal kernel over the class of convergence kernels. Extensive simulation studies are conducted to demonstrate the promising performance of the proposed estimator compared to existing estimators.

14305517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14305517.value: It is worth considering generalizations to functional data since massive data sets in the form of functional data are increasingly popular in the big data era.

14305517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14305517.value: Time-average variance constant (TAVC), or long-run variance, is the limiting variance of a statistic that has the form of an average of some quantities over time. TAVC is important in many hypothesis testing problems since it usually appears as a standardizing term in the formulation of test statistics. However, the estimation of TAVC is difficult: existing estimators require a choice of bandwidth, but the optimal choices of bandwidth of all existing estimators depend on the TAVC itself and another unknown parameter which is very difficult to estimate. Thus, the optimal estimation of TAVC is unachievable. In this project, we introduce a novel concept of converging kernels for constructing time-average variance constant (TAVC) estimators. Specifically, the class of converging kernel functions is carefully designed to be dependent on the bandwidth so that the unknown parameters in the squared-bias and variance term can be factored out. Consequently, the optimal bandwidths can be computed easily, and most importantly, are free of unknown parameters.

14305617.label: Realisation of objectives
14305617.value: We conducted a variety of investigations targeting the project objectives and successfully completed all proposed objectives, including deployment of two linear dense arrays across the Chenghai Fault (CHF), deriving high-resolution tomographic structure across the dense array, and deriving temporal changes in the Binchuan region using the nearby airgun source. One Mphil and two PhD students participated in the project and were trained in various aspects in data processing and interpretation. Two postdoctoral fellows were partially supported by this project to work on imaging the fault zone and deriving temporal changes of subsurface structure, respectively. Relevant results have been presented in international conferences and/or published in peer-reviewed journals. From January 2018 to February 2018, we deployed two linear dense arrays across two segments of the CHF with a small inter-station spacing, ~40 m. One profile was 8 km in length and consisted of 125 seismometers, across the southern portion of the CHF. The other one had 80 seismometers and was ~3 km in length across the northern segment of the CHF. The three-component seismometers were equipped with all-in-one unit of sensors, with a response band from 5 s to 100 Hz. To our best knowledge, our Binchuan dense array was the first one using such number of three-component instruments to illuminate fault zone structures. The acquired waveform data had been submitted to the data center of China Earthquake Experimental Site, through which all interested users can access the data. As such, the objective No. 1 had been completed. Using the acquired dense array data, we first conducted ambient noise tomography to obtain the S-wave velocity structure. The results revealed a 3.4 km wide low velocity zone (LVZ) in which the velocity was reduced by 50 percent and 40 percent compared to the NW side and SE side of the LVZ. The LVZ extended to ~1.5 km in depth, which was independently confirmed by teleseismic P-wave and S-wave arrivals. This was the first time to find such a wide LVZ along a continental fault. The results were published in Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth (JGR), addressing the objective 2. Furthermore, we developed a new dense-array-based inversion method to obtain high-resolution fault zone structure using teleseismic receiver functions, by identifying and utilizing coherent travel times of converted waves and their multiples. The inversion results suggested that the depth of the LVZ beneath the CHF extended to ~1.1 km, shallower but more robust than the above result from ambient noise tomography. The average V_p/V_s ratio and V_p of the LVZ were ~2.08 and 0.91 km/s, respectively. The results were also published in JGR, which completely addressed the objective 2 together with the above JGR paper. The presence of such a wide LVZ posed a great challenge to seismic hazard assessment since ground motions could be significantly amplified and prolonged. We thus investigated seismic site response based on local and teleseismic earthquakes recorded by the dense array. In addition to finding clear amplified peak ground velocity (PGV), we found that the ground motion measures at the dense array can provide independent constraints to the LVZ structure, such as the width and depth extent. By incorporating P and S waves of teleseismic earthquakes, we further analyzed the relative ground motion in the frequency domain. The horizontal amplitude spectra from 0.2 to 2 Hz at stations inside the LVZ were ~20 times as large as those outside, and a more localized zone (~500 m wide) enclosing the fault surface trace was characterized by broader frequency bands and larger amplification. Such results are under review for JGR presently, and have further extended our original objectives. To investigate temporal changes of subsurface structure, we derived seasonal changes in travel times of body waves excited by the air gun. After correcting the timing issues of airgun waveforms, we observed a ~5% increasement in the summer for all stations. We also conducted ambient noise cross-correlation to investigate arrival time changes of coda waves, which showed ~0.1% changes and a different seasonal trend. Although the changes from the airgun and noise cross correlation represented different material properties (P and S waves, respectively), such large contrast in their amplitudes raised a significant question of whether the airgun source itself affected the changes in travel times. We then applied a water-level deconvolution method to remove the source effect, but we still observed clear seasonal variation in the dominant frequency of P waves, indicating that deconvolution cannot completely remove the source effect. By comparing the seasonal changes of P-wave travel times and water level fluctuation in the reservoir where the airgun source is located, we concluded that the water level fluctuation affected airgun excitation, leading to the observed ~5% travel time change. Such results were published in Remote Sensing. In addition to the seasonal changes, we also derived daily variations using airgun waveforms that were excited within one month when the water level did not change much. Clear diurnal and sub-diurnal patterns were observed, which correlated the best with variation in air temperature. Such subsurface changes were attributed to thermoelastic strain corresponding to the temperature, which had been suggested to be capable of penetrating into ground for more than a few kilometers. Such findings demonstrate that we had to carefully inspect and remove the effects of atmospheric forcing before we may derive tectonic signature associated with earthquake process. The results are under review for Seismological Research Letters. As such, we have addressed the objective No. 3.

14305617.label: Major findings and research outcome
14305617.value: We deployed a dense array with a large aperture (8 km) across the Chenghai fault with intermediate-period three-component instruments, first of its kind among many other arrays across fault zones. Based on the dense array record, we obtained high-resolution low velocity structure along the Chenghai fault, which is 3.4 km in width (Yang et al., 2020 JGR). We also developed a new method using the coherent converted waves and multiples to constrain the depth extent of the LVZ (Jiang et al., 2021 JGR), which can be applied in broader settings such as deriving shallow subsurface structure in sedimentary basin from dense array recordings. Furthermore, we characterized the site amplification of ground motions generated by local and teleseismic earthquakes using the dense array data. As anticipated, ground motions were amplified within the low velocity fault zone. However, the new finding is that such pattern of ground motion amplification can help identify high-resolution low velocity zone structure (Song and Yang, 2021 JGR under review). In addition to the high-resolution structure, we also derived subsurface structural changes using the nearby airgun source. Using a short-term high quality airgun data, we found clear diurnal and sub-diurnal patterns of travel time changes, which correlated the best with variation in air temperature (Luan et al., 2021 SRL under review). Considering the long-term changes, we found that the water level change in the water reservoir played crucial roles in travel time changes derived from the airgun source (Liu et al., 2021 Remote Sensing). Although we tried to remove the source effects by deconvolving the waveform from the nearest station, such approach can not completely remove the source effects, which were subjected to water level changes.

14305617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14305617.value: The profound effects of water level fluctuation on seasonal variation of travel times from airgun waveforms pose the question how to reliably remove the source effects. In addition, how to remove the effects from atmospheric forcing (air temperature and pressure) remains challenging. The latter can be conducted by comparing data inside and outside the low velocity fault zone, because the atmosphere induced travel time changes are supposed identical for stations in a short distance. However, effects of interseismic fault motion (although slowly) should be different for stations in and out of the fault zone. Thus it is hopeful to observe different patterns of changes in travel times for stations. Furthermore, our deployment of the dense arrays with intermediate period enables developing new methods that were commonly used in broadband seismology, such as receiver functions. Waveform modeling from advanced methods can be further applied on such data with broader frequency content than previously used short-period sensors.

14305617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14305617.value: Properties of seismogenic faults, including the structure of the damaged fault zones, play significant roles in earthquake generation, rupture propagation and termination. Furthermore, the structure of the damaged fault zones may change over time, and such temporal change may serve as a proxy to understand fault zone healing and stress variation in the crust. Therefore, high-resolution imaging of the fault zone structure and its temporal changes is of critical significance to advance our understanding of earthquake physics and thus of better seismic hazard preparation and mitigation. Using the newly deployed dense arrays, we obtained high-resolution low velocity structure of the Chenghai fault and developed new methods to constrain the depth extent and lateral variation of the fault zone structure. By analyzing the waveform generated from the nearby airgun source, we also derived daily and annual subsurface structural changes. The results highlight the necessity of future work to carefully remove source effects of airgun when deriving the long-term structural changes, as well as to separate the impact of atmospheric forcing on subsurface variation.

14305717.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14305717.value: 包含雙極擴散的恒星生成數值模擬

14305717.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14305717.value: Dr Leung, Po Kin Prof WANG, Hsiang-hsu

14305717.label: Project Objectives
14305717.value: We have started developing Scorpio, a numerical code dedicated to astronomical magnetohydrodynamic simulations with AD. The code has recently passed all the standard 2-D tests and AD tests with flying colors (see Methodology). We will develop Scorpio into a 3-D code equipped with the option of Adaptive-Mesh-Refinement (AMR). We will install Scorpio on Tienhe2 and perform the first 3-D 2-fluid “cloud to core” simulation with gravity, turbulence, magnetic fields and AD without any approximation. Ion/neutral turbulent velocity fields from the diffused regions in “2” will be compared with recent (Tang, Li & Lee 2016) and future turbulent AD (TAD) observations to help interpret the data. Ion/neutral contraction velocity fields from the bounded regions in “2” will be studied and simulated observation of these regions will be performed to search for new signatures of gravitational-contraction AD (GAD). AMR will be turned on to study the impact of AD on the “core to disk” process.

14305717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14305717.value: Magnetic fields (B-fields) are ubiquitous in the Milky Way, and are believed to play various important roles in converting galactic gas into stars (Li et al. 2014). In most state-of-the-art analysis and numerical simulations, gas and B-fields are treated as perfectly coupled. However, ambipolar diffusion (AD), the decoupling between gas flows and B-fields, is theoretically predicted (e.g. Oishi et al. 2006; Li & Houde 2008; Tilley & Balsara 2010; Xu et al. 2015), and is thought to have critical impacts on various stages of star formation, from damping cloud turbulence (e.g. Burge et al. 2016) to inducing cloud core collapse (Shu et al. 1999; Mouschovias 1976) and releasing the “magnetic brake” for protostellar disk formation (Li et al. 2011). In the past, there have been two main obstacles to the improvement of numerical simulations to involve realistic AD. First, AD is very expensive to simulate. Second, observational evidence both for and against the existence of AD has been extremely difficult to obtain and the validity of existing observations has been hotly disputed (Li & Houde 2008; Crutcher et al. 2009; Mouschovias & Tassis 2009; Li et al. 2014). However, the situation has been changed recently. The world’s fastest supercomputer, Tianhe-2 ("Milky Way 2"), which is able to carry out AD simulations at a reasonable speed and cost, was installed in Guangzhou in 2013. Recently, our group also discovered the first direct observational evidence of AD. This discovery has greatly increased our eagerness to develop realistic AD simulations. In this proposal, we will demonstrate this recent discovery, its background and a how a two-fluid AD code can help to develop future observing strategies. We will then use Scorpio, a two-fluid magnetohydrodynamic code we are presently developing, to simulate AD on Tianhe-2. The exploitation of modern supercomputing capabilities should enable us to amass opportunities hitherto unavailable to researchers, and should enable us to develop realistic AD simulations which will help to resolve the vexed question of the effects of AD in star formation. 磁場在銀河中無所不在，並且可能對恒星生成有重要影響。絕大多數的恆星生成數值模擬都假設磁場與氣體完全耦合，但這是為了節省運算時間，並不符合理論與觀測結果。以往，這種假設是必須的，因為計算機不足以應付描述磁場與氣體分離（雙極擴散）所需的運算。但現今的計算機（例如天河二號）已具備此運算能力。再者，雙極擴散的觀測非常困難，以往都只能間接觀測。本組最近發現的直接證據加強了在模擬中加入雙極擴散的必要性。本計劃的目的就是發展出一個能精確模擬雙極擴散的程式。

14306117.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14306117.value: 基於金剛石色心的磁光成像用於探測疾病相關的生物礦物質

14306117.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14306117.value: Prof Jörg, Wrachtrup Prof Li, Quan

14306117.label: Project Objectives
14306117.value: Setting up a wide-field quantum diamond microscopy. The developed wide-field microscopy will enable quantum sensing through an ensemble of NV centers (in diamond substrate) in a large field-of-view (~ 100×100 µm2). We will adopt the total internal reflection fluorescence (TIRF) mode for current study, avoiding phototoxicity which is crucial for bio-related sample. Developing the optimized quantum sensing protocol based on NV spin relaxometry. The quantum sensing will be realized by quantifying the NV spin relaxation time T1 determined by surrounding spin noise (e.g., iron biominerals). We will optimize the NV spin relaxometry measurements aiming at an enhanced T1 contrast and improved sensitivity. Monitoring in-situ formation of mimicked iron biominerals in microfluidics. The most representative beta-amyloid peptide (associated with neurodegenerative disease) will be decorated on the surface of diamond substrate, treated with ferrihydrite (Fe3+ ions) solution as a function of incubation time. Using the methods developed in this project, we will monitor the in situ formation of mimicked iron biominerals in detail. We will perform the corresponding measurements in a microfluidic channel, which allows us to precisely control local environments. Demonstration of in vitro magneto-optical imaging of iron biominerals. By seeding in vitro model PC12 rat pheocromocytoma cell on top of diamond substrate, we will stimulate the neuronal differentiations and the developments of neuritic plaques associated with iron biominerals. As a proof-of-the-principle demonstration, we will monitor the spatial-temporal evolution of iron biominerals in cultured model cells.

14306117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14306117.value: 金剛石中的氮空穴色心逐漸成為一種重要的常溫常壓下的納米尺度磁場探測器，其探測靈敏度能到~nTHz-1/2 並且同時擁有納米尺度的空間解析度。這種色心擁有很好的光穩定性和生物相容性，因而使得它們非常適合生物醫學方面的應用。近期通過測量氮空穴色心的自旋弛豫時間，專案主持人和他的合作者們已經實現了各種金屬離子在微流腔中的量化磁自旋成像。 這些成果激發我們進一步去發展基於氮空穴色心的量子探測技術，用來原位的研究和疾病有關聯的磁性生物礦物質。 順磁鐵離子已經被發現是人腦裡最富集的過渡金屬元素。鐵離子會在某些大腦區域高度富集，這被高度懷疑和許多神經退行性疾病有關聯。儘管如此，探測此種生物相關的鐵離子還是有一定的困難，特別在生理環境中的亞細胞尺度下。因此現在迫切需要發展有用的方法，使得其能用來即時監測生物相關的鐵離子，保證有最好的表現在綜合考慮視場大小，探測靈敏度，空間解析度和生物相容性上。 這個專案的目標是發展基於金剛石中的氮空穴色心的成像和探測方法，來驗證它在量化探測生物相關的鐵離子的可行性。基於寬場顯微探測方案，我們將建立擁有100×100 µm2的量子金剛石顯微鏡。通過優化氮空穴色心的自旋弛豫測量，我們將獲得在衍射極限限制的最小探測體積內(410×410×20 nm3)幾十個鐵原子的探測靈敏度。通過當前的量子探測方案，我們會盡力去演示即時監測在微流腔內或者細胞內的鐵離子。 當前的項目將會給研究神經退行性疾病提供一種有用的工具。過程中獲得的經驗將會非常有益於發展生物相關的先進量子探測技術。

14306117.label: Realisation of objectives
14306117.value: We have conducted a series of investigations targeting the project objectives and have almost completed all objectives as originally proposed in the project, including the construction of widefield quantum microscope; developing optimized quantum sensing schemes for proposed study; evaluating in model system and application in cell experiments. The above results on objectives 1-3 have been published in a few papers as attached; and the preliminary work on objective 4 has been published in a conference proceeding paper (there is another one under review in Angewandte Chemie; and one in preparation for publication). Two Ph.D. graduate students were trained and involved in this project, and one research assistant was partially supported by the project. Furthermore, we have scheduled regular meetings with our collaborators to discuss the progress, and PI has visited Co-I Wrachtrup's group in Germany for once to discuss the project.

14306117.label: Major findings and research outcome
14306117.value: The major findings and research outcome from this project are in several aspects: publications, patents, researchers training and collaborations with academia and beyond. A total of at least 12 journal publications have been produced from this project (10 published, 1 in revision and 1 in preparation). We have systematically studied the literature about bio-orientated quantum sensing, and summarized our understanding in a review article [ACS Sensors, 6, 2077-2107 (2021)]. In addition, one US provisional patent has also been filed on this method (US provisional patent Application No. 63/109,956 (PCT Application No. PCT/CN2021/125267).). We have reconsidered the quantum nanosensors, and found the way to purify those materials which remains a challenging task. These results have been published in ACS Applied Nano Materials, 4, 9223-9230 (2021). We also found the ways to pattern those nanosensors for our planned experiments, and those results got published in Advanced Science, in press, 2021 (https://doi.org/10.1002/advs.202103598). In addition, one US provisional patent has also been filed on this technology development (Application No. 63/236,411). To enable the proposed bio-application of developed quantum sensing, we have investigated the cellular behaviors of neuron cells firstly. These results got published in Frontiers in Bioengineering and Biotechnology, 8, 621777 (2020) and Journal of The Royal Society Interface, 17, 20200331 (2020). We have achieved quantitative imaging of magnetic labelled cells in culture using our developed NV relaxation sensing scheme, and the preliminary results got published in a conference proceeding (“Development of a Wide-field Quantum Diamond Microscope for Imaging Dynamics of Cell Adhesion”, Quantum Information and Measurement VI 2021). Furthermore, we managed to monitor the dynamic process of magnetic labelled cell changes using our development, and the corresponding results are being reviewed (under review in Angewandte Chemie) and being prepared for publication. By carrying out this research project, we have established strong collaborations with international partners including both academic and industrial experts. Based on the developed wide-field quantum diamond microscope, we have been working with Prof. Qiang Wei (College of Polymer Science & Engineering, Sichuan University), Prof. Joachim Spatz (Max Planck Institute for Medical Research, Germany) and Dr. Yuan Lin (Department of Mechanical Engineering, The University of Hong Kong) to develop diamond molecular tension microscopy for studying cellular traction forces. In addition, we have also been working together with local industrial partner, Master Dynamic (a major high-tech company especially in precision diamond manufacturer) to apply quantum sensing for authenticity of diamond jewellery (successfully awarded one ITF project).

14306117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14306117.value: We noticed that the performance of our developed widefield quantum sensing microscope could be improved in terms of spatial and temporal resolution, and we do have some initial ideas to tackle those issues. For instance, it is possible to improve the resolution by introducing some proper super-resolution technique which has no interference with quantum sensing protocol. Also, it is feasible to revolutionize the imaging sensor in order to gain a much higher temporal resolution. The demonstrated bio-applications in current project remains in an early stage, and we will continue with the direction of applying quantum sensing techniques for investigating the transition metal ions associated with neurodegenerative diseases.

14306117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14306117.value: Paramagnetic iron ions in magnetite biominerals have been found to be the most abundant transition metals in human brain, being highly suspected to associate with many neurodegenerative disorders. In current project, we aim to develop a novel imaging and sensing platform based on the diamond-based quantum technologies, in order to obtain the “real-time tracking” of those iron biominerals. The developed method will give us the best combination of field-of-view, sensitivity, spatial resolution and biocompatibility. Our development enables a feasible method to measure the spatial/temporal evolution of iron species, and thus provides information relevant to the understanding of the role of iron in neurodegenerative disorders.

14306217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14306217.value: 在電磁場理論裡面，BORN-INFELD 理論提出的主要動機就是解決經典麥克斯韋理論裡面能量無窮大的問題。為了能夠同時保証經典電磁理論裡面關於龐加萊群和外爾群的不變性，BORN和INFELD引進了他們的非線性電磁理論。並且成功証明了有限能量電粒子的存在性。最近他們的理論被証明允許存在多個不同的電粒子。基於上面提到的一些工作，我們在這個項目裡面將要考慮BORN-INFELD理論和HIGG理論的結合以期待能夠得到帶電磁極子的存在性。同時我們也希望驗証從BORN-INFELD 理論到經典麥克斯韋理論的有效性。通過有效性的研究，我們能夠更清楚的了解磁極子和帶渦旋粒子之間的相互作用。這個項目的研究還能幫助我們理解弦理論裡面其他類似的模型。並且吸引一些物理學家的興趣。

14306217.label: Realisation of objectives
14306217.value: This project is devoted to studying semilinear elliptic equations arising from Born-Infeld theory. In general, such equations also have applications in various other physical systems, e.g. Poisson-Nernst-Planck equation, Poisson-Boltzmann equation and Keller-Segel equation. In this project, I have finished the items 1, 3, 4 and 5 listed in the objectives. Basically, I have constructed solutions to the self-dual Born-Infeld-Higgs equation and solutions to the self-dual Born-Infeld gauged harmonic map equations with singularities, via the method that we call Born-Infeld approach. Different from previous works, my results include singularities with fractional order. Not just for the previous mentioned models, we also extended our approach to dealing with more general equations and several non-local semilinear elliptic equations with exponential nonlinearities. In this direction, we have solved a long-standing open problem on the Debye layer phenomenon in Poisson-Boltzmann equation. Before our work, the Debye layer phenomenon has only been considered in 1D. However, we extended to studying the higher dimensional case and discovered a novel formula to calculate the limiting electric potential as the thickness of the layer becomes small. This is the first work that includes both singularities and Debye layer in the Poisson-Boltzmann equation. For the general semilinear elliptic equations (not just Poisson-Boltzmann equation), the asymptotic behavior of solutions near singularities are also considered. Meanwhile, by taking the so-called Born-Infeld parameter to infinity, we also recover the Maxwell-Higgs model from the Born-Infeld one, which has long been accepted in physics. In this project, I have not too much time to study the non-Bogomol'nyi regime. So far, the results that we have obtained is still near the Bogomol'nyi regime, even though we can consider in some sense non-Bogomol'nyi regime. Our method is still limited to the implicit function theorem. The results are not satisfactory. We are still engaging to extending our results to cover all the situations beyond the Bogomol'nyi regime, not just near the Bogomol'nyi regime. Besides the above mentioned results, the project also has some unexpected outcomes that I want to explain at this moment. In a paper with Chia-Yu Hsieh, we also considered the dynamical stability of the singular solutions to some non-local semilinear elliptic equations with exponential nonlinearities, in terms of the Poisson-Nernst-Planck (PNP for short) equation. We show that the 2D PNP equation has an equilibrium state with prescribed singularities. Moreover, we also show that such equilibrium solution is dynamically stable. This is the first work in the PNP equation where the system can have finitely many point singularities. Without singularities, Biler et al have already studied the dynamical stability of the equilibrium solutions to the PNP equation. In our work, we include singularities. Please be noted that, with the singularities, the dynamical system becomes extremely difficult since the system is singular/degenerate near the singularities. Our work extended the method of Biler to the current case with singularities. The work is now submitted for publication in a peer-reviewed journal. On the other hand, Chia-Yu and I also considered the Keller-Segel equation and its long-time behavior. Note that equilibrium state of Keller-Segel satisfies a semilinear elliptic equation with exponential nonlinearity. This equation is quite similar to the Poisson-Boltzmann equation with different sign. For a long time, the asymptotic behavior of the Keller-Segel equation was studied only in 2D with solutions having finite free energy. In a joint work with Chia-Yu Hsieh, we have dropped the assumptions on the finiteness of free energy and proved the global stability results of the Keller-Segel equation in 2D. We also considered the long-time behavior of Keller-Segel equation in higher dimensional case. This work is also submitted for publication in a peer-reviewed journal. In a word, this project is successful. Not only it gives a systematic approach, which we call Born-Infeld approach, to construct singular solutions to a class of semilinear elliptic equations with exponential nonlinearities, it also provides some dynamical stability results to the PNP equation and Keller-Segel equation, which indicate that the static solutions that we construct are indeed stable dynamically in many physical systems, not just linearly stable with respect to some linearized operators.

14306217.label: Major findings and research outcome
14306217.value: 1. Reference 1 of Part C is devoted to introducing a systematic method for constructing singular solutions to some semilinear elliptic equations with exponential nonlinearities. The method is called Born-Infeld approach, which originates from the nonlinear electro-magnetic field theory due to Born and Infeld. In this work, we invent a shrinking hole argument which indicates that finitely many holes with the size carefully prescribed will eventually shrink to the prescribed singularities as the Born-Infeld parameter tends to infinity. With different prescribed orders at different singularities, the size the the holes are different. Technically speaking, our method relies on the work of Crandall-Rabinowitz-Tartar for a Dirichlet problem with a singular nonlinearity. More than theirs, since we have order constraint for each singularity, the size of the holes cannot be arbitrary. So we introduce a novel inverse problem so that we can determine the size of the holes in terms of the orders prescribed at singularities. This is the first work up to our knowledge that the inverse problem method is used to construct singular solutions of semilinear elliptic equations. 2. Reference 2 in Part C. In this work, we consider Poisson-Boltzmann equation in arbitrary dimensions. This is a non-local semilinear elliptic equations with exponential nonlinearity. The Poisson-Boltzmann equation is satisfied by equilibrium solutions of the Poisson-Nernst-Planck equation. The inverse problem method that we have introduced before can be used to prove the existence of singular solutions to the Poisson-Boltzmann equation. Moreover, in this work, we also addressed the so-called Debye layer phenomenon. It is the first time that we include both Debye layer and point singularities in the Poisson-Boltzmann equation. The major contribution in this work is the resolution of a long-standing open problem on determining the limiting electric potential while the thickness of the Debye layer tends to 0. Before our work, the Debye layer problem has only been considered in 1D without any singularities. We completely solve the problem in any dimensions by providing a novel formula to calculate the limiting electric potential in terms of the Dirichlet data prescribed on the boundary. Surprising, the formula only depends on the Dirichlet data prescribed. The point singularities and their orders have no influence on the limiting electric potential. The removability of singularities are also shown when the physical dimension is greater than or equal to 3.

14306217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14306217.value: As we have discussed before, in higher dimensions, usually point singularities are removable. In the future, we want to extend to studying singularities with more complicated geometry, e.g. curved singularities. More generally, we can study the singular solutions to the semilinear elliptic equation with exponential nonlinearity whose singularities are of codimension 2. We also want to study the dynamical stabilities of these singular solutions in some physical systems, e.g. Keller-Segel equation and Poisson-Nernst-Planck equation. In recent decades, the Keller-Segel equation and Poisson-Nernst-Planck equation are also coupled with fluid described by the Navier-Stokes equation. We also want to address the influences of singularities on the background fluid and vice versa.

14306217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14306217.value: Equilibrium states of many dynamical systems are governed by nonlinear elliptic partial differential equations. Solutions of nonlinear elliptic partial differential equations can let us know the long-time behaviors of various dynamical systems. Singularities are usually coupled into a dynamical system with roles of point charges, vortices/anti-vortices, monopoles, filaments, impurities etc. In this project, I successful couple singularities into solutions of a class of nonlinear elliptic equations arising in electro-magnetic theory, polymer science, electron interactions in semiconductors and biology. Successfully completing the project not only builds up several novel mathematical methods for solving elliptic partial differential equations, but also provides both quantitative and qualitative descriptions on various phenomena in physical and biological systems with singularities. The methods introduced in the current project can be applied in the future to more complicated and realistic models.

14306317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14306317.value: SUMOylation是指一種發生在細胞內的天然蛋白質的化學反應。在這個過程中，一個10 kDa的小泛素樣修飾物（SUMO）蛋白通過一系列酶反應共價連接到各種其他蛋白質，這提供了一個動態，快速和可逆的方式來調節蛋白質定位、活性和穩定性的方法。最近的進展將SUMO化與神經變性疾病，癌症和心力衰竭的發病機制相關聯。因此，了解這種反應的控制和調控以及SUMO化機制中涉及的成分將有助於揭示這些疾病的潛在致病機制，並可能導致新的治療方案。 儘管SUMOylation的研究已有長足發展，但我們對SUMOylation的理解仍然落後於其他領域。特別是SUMO化學工具遠遠不夠。例如，SUMO修飾的蛋白質的識別取決於特異性結合SUMO蛋白的抗體。然而，由於抗體和SUMO之間的結合相互作用的可逆性質，在這個過程中存在固有的問題：難以區分共價SUMO連接的蛋白質與那些與它們結合併共同沉澱在一起的蛋白質（但不直接與SUMO共價連接）。共價SUMO反應性探針在這種情況下具有優於抗體的優點，因為共價固定可以耐受嚴格的洗滌步驟，其從真正的SUMO化蛋白質中除去共沉澱的結合物。 我們實驗室已經合成了可以選擇性地，特異性地並且共價地與復合蛋白質組中的蛋白質反應的化學探針。例如，基於“接近誘導”半胱氨酸和酪氨酸特異性反應，我們合成了可以與細胞內的蛋白質結合結構域（包括PDZ，SH2和SH3）共價反應的多肽。這些肽探針與目標蛋白質顯示出無與倫比的特異性。在這個課題中，我們設計賴氨酸特異性反應，並首先在SH3-肽相互作用中，然後在SUMO-肽相互作用中進行驗證。這些初步結果為SUMO反應肽鋪平了道路。化學工具的進步往往帶動生物學的突破。我們的工作不僅擴大了特異性生物交聯反應，而且還將通過引入與現有技術相容的新工具，進一步拓展蛋白質SUMO化的研究領域。

14306317.label: Realisation of objectives
14306317.value: Both objectives have been successfully realized. (1) We have significantly advanced lysine-selective conjugation reactions. (2) We designed peptides inhibitors of SUMOylating enzymes, including SUMO4. In addition, we have extended the scope of this project and discovered that bacterial infection significantly affects SUMOylation in the host cells. The SUMOylation probes, including SUMO-reactive peptides that we developed in this project and the SUMO4 inhibitors, prove to be powerful tools to investigate how bacterial infection alters the signal transduction in the host cells, which may lead to continued funding supports. The center of this project is the development of site-selective lysine reactions. Site-selective lysine reactions are challenging because of the difficulty of identifying one lysine residue among many in the same protein. With the funding support from this project, we developed several site-selective lysine reactions by screening different amine-reactive groups fluorodinitrobenzene, isothiocyanate, and phenyl ester reactions, and have validated the site-specific targeting of the ε-amino group of one single lysine in natural proteins that contain multiple lysine residues by carefully choosing the reactive group and the length of linker. The reactions were examined first on model proteins and then on a set of ubiquitin-like proteins, including SUMO. A group of peptide-binding proteins Crk SH3 has been used as the model protein. Based on the crystal structure of Crk SH3 bound with the peptide ligand, we synthesized a covalently reactive peptide which proved to react with Crk SH3 at the cysteine residue with high efficiency through the reactive group fluorodinitrobenzene (FDNB). We found although Csk SH3 contains 9 lysine residues, only Lys43 reacted with the FDNB group of the peptide, which proved the site selectivity. The lysine reaction on SUMO is more challenging because the 11 lysine residues are closely clustered around the peptide binding site in SUMO. Next, we then designed lysine reactive peptides based on a SUMO-binding peptide and observed a 1:1 covalent addition of SUMO and the reactive peptide. We also confirmed that the reaction happens only at a single Lys of SUMO but not other Lys residues. We also screened different reactive groups, including FDNB, carboxyl ester, dialdehyde moiety, and NCS group. We observed that most of the reactive groups except dialdehyde benzene support a specific and efficient lysine reaction. Till now, we have succeeded in the development of SUMO-specific reactive peptides as probes for SUMO-related protein modification. Next, we convert the SUMO-reactive peptide into probes for SUMOlyated proteins. Adding a bioorthogonal reactive group at the end of the SUMO-reactive peptides gives these peptides a reactive handle for further derivatization. For example, we installed an alkyne at the reactive peptide (the peptide is then a bifunctional peptide with a lysine-reactive moiety and a click site); covalent lysine reaction then attaches the alkyne on a single site of the protein. We can further functionalize through the alkyne with chemical groups such as biotin, allowing us to pull down SUMOylated proteins with high efficiency for proteomic identification. Alkyne-modified proteins can also be detected in SDS-PAGE through the click reaction. Reactive peptides to study the mechanism of protein SUMOylation have also been developed. As the SUMO protein is attached to the host proteins through its C-terminus, the C-terminal functionalization of peptides or proteins becomes an important task. Accessing C-terminally modified peptides, however, is difficult because solid-phase peptide synthesis starts from a covalent anchor of the C-terminus of the peptide, followed by N-terminal conjugation and extension. We developed on-resin multicomponent reactions Passerini and Ugi reactions to synthesize C-terminally photocaged peptide acids and peptide amides. The C-terminally nitroveratryl-caged peptides can be photolyzed to give amides with electrophiles. These peptides with C-terminal electrophiles will react with SUMO-related enzymes via the active cysteine residues. Traditionally C-terminally modified peptides can only be accessed by laborious and lengthy in-solution synthesis with fully protected peptides. Our methods are unique in that the regular Rink MBHA amide resin is first converted to the isocyanide resin in a single-step reaction. In the on-resin Ugi reaction, Fmoc-amino acid, isocyanide resin, 6-nitroveratrylaldehyde, and 2,4-dimethoxybenzylamine as an amine donor are then condensed in a single step to load the Fmoc-amino acid onto the resin via a photolabile linker. This reaction is highly efficient with non-detectable racemization. More importantly, a variety of amine donors can be used. Using D-, and L- histidine as an example, we showed that this procedure does not incur racemization. Furthermore, the compatibility of this method with all the 20 amino acids was confirmed. Lastly, we showcased the applicability of these methods by synthesizing short head-to-tail cyclized peptides via intramolecular click reaction. Two papers have been published. These works armed the development of inhibitors for SUMOylating enzymes with new tools. A second strategy to devise peptide inhibitors for the cysteine enzymes (SUMOylating enzymes all exert their function through an active site cysteine) is to synthesize peptides with C-terminal Dha or propargyl group. We developed a method of converting a cysteine residue to Dha using dibromo butane. Although the Dha does not perfectly align with the C-terminus of the peptide ligand, we observe that peptides with Dha at the C-terminus can effectively block the activity of cysteine enzymes. In another approach, we activated the C-terminal carboxylic acid of the fully protected peptides with DIC/HOBt and propargylamine and installed the propargyl group at the C-terminus of the peptide in solution. Although the synthesis involves in-solution manipulation, the propargyl peptide can inhibit the cysteine enzyme. Therefore they are also valuable peptide inhibitors for SUMOylating or deSUMOylating enzymes. Besides harnessing peptides as the inhibitors of SUMO-related enzymes, we also utilized sortase-mediated ligation to synthesize SUMO analog proteins with C-terminal modified electrophiles to react with SUMO-related cysteine enzymes. Comparing peptides as inhibitors with proteins, protein inhibitors will bind with the enzyme with higher affinity, thereby resulting in higher inhibition activity. Equipped with these new peptide tools, we are able to explore how protein SUMOylation changes in various cellular processes. One of the important events is the bacterial infection, whether SUMOylation in cell changes in association with bacterial infection remains elusive. We explored an epithelial cell infection model and found that the infection of pathogenic bacteria elicits a pronounced shift in the SUMOylation pattern in mammalian cells. This work then demonstrates a new chemical-biological approach to studying protein post-translational modifications. It also illustrates how the development of chemistry may contribute to advancing knowledge in biology, using SUMOylation as one example. The site-specific protein reactions will be a valuable tool to elucidate new biological pathways in the cells. Beyond protein SUMOylation, this strategy is also applicable to other protein reactions such as autophagy and may stimulate the area of drug development in the long run. Taken together, we have been successfully fulfilled both objectives.

14306317.label: Major findings and research outcome
14306317.value: Site-selective lysine reactions in a multi-lysine protein have been realized by harnessing proximal reactivity. We have solved a significant challenge in protein labeling reactions. Through controlling the spatial organization of reactive groups in the context of protein-peptide interacting complex, we can tune the lysine reaction specifically at a single lysine residue without reacting with other lysines. This method renders a selective SUMO-reactive peptide. Synthetic methods of C-terminal modified peptides have been established. For cysteine enzymes that recognize and modify the C-terminus of the protein substrates, access to C-terminally modified peptides and proteins is valuable but difficult. We developed two new on-resin multi-component reactions to synthesize C-terminally modified peptides. New peptide-based SUMOylation studying tools have been devised. SUMO-reactive peptides can selectively and covalently recognize SUMO and SUMOylated proteins from the cell lysate. They are can be further functionalized with bioorthogonal reactive handles for selective labeling and protein pull-down separation, thereby paving the role for the subsequent proteomic identification of the SUMOylated proteins in cells. On another note, peptides with C-terminal electrophiles are effective inhibitors for SUMOylation-related cysteine enzymes. They can be used to perturb the normal function of the SUMOylation enzymes and thereby probe the function of protein SUMOylation under normal or diseased states. Several papers have been published to report the results above. This work was also reported in international conferences as invited talks. A total of four Ph.D. students received training under this project, and two have graduated with a Ph.D. degree during the period.

14306317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14306317.value: The new reactions we developed in this project have potential uses in other systems. The site-selective lysine reactions can be used to modify valuable protein therapeutics such as monoclonal antibodies and therapeutic enzymes. The peptide-based SUMOylation probes or interferers can be used to study the change of SUMOylation patterns under certain disease states. For example, we and others have discovered that SUMOyation changes during the course of bacterial infection. How such an effect happens during the process and how SUMOylation is associated with the bacterial infection still remains elusive. But our peptide-based SUMOylation probes or interferers are valuable tools in these studies. Based on these proof-of-principle results, we are exploring the use of our peptide tools in the study of bacterial infection. We have discovered significant changes in the SUMOylation states and patterns during infection. We will apply for grant supports to deepen this study and optimize our tools through collaboration with biomedical scientists. Eventually, these endeavors may lead to druggable targets in the protein SUMOylation pathway as a new therapeutic option.

14306317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14306317.value: SUMOylation is a protein reaction that naturally happens inside cells. This protein reaction regulates important functions of the cell and thereby is a research focus. Using various designs of peptides, we can effectively probe the SUMOylation process of a cell. This research will lead to a better understanding of the bacterial infection process, provides hints whether key regulators, substrates, or enzymes in the SUMOylation pathway can be drug targets, and may eventually lead to new therapeutics for the treatment of diseases such as infection and others.
