14306417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14306417.value: The aim of this project is to develop Bayesian methods for graph-valued regression, which studies how graph structures change with covariates. Graphical models characterize the dependence structures among a set of random variables, and they are widely applied in various scientific domains such as economics, sociology, and genomics. One motivating example is the gene regulatory network, which describes the collaboration among genes and is crucial for understanding biological diversity and disease mechanisms. It is especially critical to learn how the gene regulatory network varies across different tissue types, age groups, and disease categories. Nevertheless, despite the large body of literature on learning graphs from observed data, statistical methods for graph-valued regression are lacking. Early proposed methods must first partition the space of covariates and then separately learn graphs on each portion of the data, resulting in unstable estimators and a loss of interpretability for the covariates. Recent emerging methods on the joint modeling of multiple graphical models can be viewed as a special case of graph-valued regression with the covariate being univariate and categorical. However, they cannot handle continuous covariates, let alone multiple covariates and more complicated data structures. In this project, we propose a novel Bayesian framework for graph-valued regression. Our proposed model can easily interpret the effects of covariates on each edge of the graph, handle all types of covariates, and borrow strength across the whole covariate space to improve edge detection. Moreover, the Bayesian paradigm automatically entails the capacity of incorporating domain-expert information into the prior, providing a full set of statistical inference, and generalizing to more complex hierarchical models. In particular, we will extend the Bayesian graph-valued regression to a longitudinal setting as motivated by the application to gene regulatory networks. To conduct posterior inference for the proposed model, we will develop highly efficient parallel Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithms and provide them as a freely available software package. The proposed model and inference methods will make profound contributions to graphical modeling, longitudinal data analysis, statistical computing and parallel programming. The application to gene regulatory networks will greatly deepen our understanding of genomics, help tackle Hong-Kong-related disease problems, and ultimately improve human health. 圖值回歸研究圖的結構如何隨協變量變化。本項目旨在開髮用於圖值回歸的貝葉斯方法。 圖模型刻畫一組隨機變量之間的依賴關係並廣泛應用於經濟學、社會學和基因組學等各個科學領域。基因調控網絡是一個典型的圖模型例子。它描述了基因之間的協作關係。理解基因調控網絡對於了解生物多樣性和疾病機制至關重要，尤其是我們需要了解基因調控網絡如何在不同組織類型、年齡組和疾病類別之間變化。 然而雖然從觀察數據中學習圖模型的文獻很多，但是圖值回歸的統計方法仍然十分缺乏。早期提出的方法必須首先將協變量的空間進行劃分，然後在每一個部分上單獨學習一個圖模型。這樣的方法導致估計很不穩定同時也無法解釋協變量的作用。最近出現的同時估計多個圖模型的方法可以被看作是圖值回歸當協變量是分類數據時的一種特殊情況。但是這些方法不能處理連續協變量，更不用說多元協變量和更複雜的數據結構的情況。 在這個項目中，我們提出了一種用於圖值回歸的新貝葉斯框架。我們提出的模型可以輕鬆地解釋協變量對圖中每條邊的影響、處理各種類型的協變量、並藉用整個協變量空間的信息來提高對邊估計的準確度。此外，貝葉斯框架自動具有將專家知識加入先驗分佈的能力、提供了一整套統計推斷並可被推廣到更複雜的層次模型。特別地，受到基因調控網絡應用的啟發，我們將貝葉斯圖值回歸擴展到縱向數據。為了進行後驗統計推斷，我們將開發高效的並行馬爾科夫鏈蒙特卡羅算法並將其開發成一個免費的軟件包。 本項目提出的模型和推斷方法將對圖模型、縱向數據分析、統計計算和並行計算做出重要的貢獻。基因調控網絡的應用將大大加深我們對基因組學的認識、幫助解決與香港相關的疾病問題並最終改善人類健康。

14306417.label: Realisation of objectives
14306417.value: We have fully achieved the objectives of the proposal. The reference number is indexed according to the references listed in Part C. We have developed a Bayesian framework to study how the graphical structures change with covariates [4]. Our method is able to handle not only categorical but also continuous covariates. We developed two Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithms to conduct statistical inference and parallelized the algorithm, one based on reversible jump MCMC [4] and another on a birth-death Markov process [5]. We provide our algorithms publicly available at https://github.com/becky7b29/BRUG and https://github.com/Anguscgm/BRUG_BDMCMC, respectively. We applied our algorithm to study how the gene regulatory networks vary with age and gender using gene expression data collected by the Genotype-Tissue Expression (GTEx) project. In particular, we studied a pathway related to neurodegenerative diseases. Compared to the single dense network learned by GLASSO, our proposed method shows deeper insights into the gene regulatory network. In our original proposal, we proposed to use the reversible jump MCMC to perform the posterior inference following Wang and Li’s approach in estimating a single Gaussian graphical model for all the samples (Electronic Journal of Statistics, 2012). Nevertheless, the algorithm turns out to be slow. During the implementation of the project, we found the birth-death process based algorithm by Mohammadi and Wit (Bayesian Analysis, 2015) for estimating a single Gaussian graphical model for all the samples. Following the same philosophy, we construct a birth-death process based MCMC algorithm to perform posterior inference for our Bayesian graph-valued regression. We mathematically prove that the stationary distribution of our proposed algorithm is the posterior distribution of our Bayesian graph-valued regression. Moreover, we also developed Bayesian methods to characterize the dependence among multivariate mixed type variables, including survival outcomes and continuous outcomes [2]. In addition to studying gene regulatory networks based on expression data, we also constructed regulatory networks for ChIP-seq data which measure transcription factor binding to DNAs [3]. Motivated by teasing the heterogeneity for graphical structures, we also developed statistical methods to learn the heterogeneity for microbiome data [1].

14306417.label: Major findings and research outcome
14306417.value: In scientific domains such as economics, sociology and biology, people are always interested in the dependence structure among a set of variables, which can often be represented by a graphical model. There has been active research on estimating a single Gaussian graphical model for a set of samples. However, when there exists heterogeneity among the samples, learning a single graphical model for all of the samples can lead to many spurious edges. The existing methods on joint modeling of multiple graphical models allow graphical structures to change with univariate, categorical covariates. However, they cannot handle continuous covariates, let alone multiple covariates. The early proposed frequentist approach to linking multiple covariates to graphical structures must first partition the space of covariates and then separately learn graphs on each portion of the data, resulting in unstable estimators and a loss of interpretability for the covariates. In this project, we develop a novel Bayesian framework to study how the graphical structures change with covariates for Gaussian graphical models. Our proposed method can handle all types of covariates, borrow strength across the whole covariate space to improve edge detection, and provide direct interpretation for effects of covariates on each edge of the graph. We develop two parallel Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm to conduct posterior inference. Simulation studies show that our proposed reversible jump MCMC algorithm outperforms GLASSO, the Joint Graphical Lasso (JGL) and the frequentist’s Graph-Valued Regression. We applied the proposed method to gene expression data, and the analyses show that gene regulatory networks do vary across different types of covariates such as age and disease categories [4]. We further developed a birth-death process based MCMC algorithm to perform posterior inference of our proposed Bayesian graph-valued regression [5]. The birth-death MCMC algorithm is much faster than the reversible-jump MCMC. We have also developed Bayesian methods that built upon latent factor models that further study the dependence among mixed type of variables, including survival outcome and continuous variables [2]. When processing gene expression data for constructing gene regulatory networks, we found huge sample heterogeneity due to technical artifacts and biological variability. The method we used to handle the sample heterogeneity for gene expression data further motivated us to develop a statistical method to separate the technical artifacts and biological heterogeneity for microbiome data [1]. In addition to constructing regulatory networks with gene expression data, we also constructed regulatory networks for transcription factor binding data [3]. Both types of regulatory networks have greatly deepened our understandings of gene regulation mechanism.

14306417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14306417.value: We will further perform systematic and extensive simulation studies to compare the two proposed MCMC algorithms for the inference of Bayesian graph-valued regression. In the current project, we applied the proposed method to analyze an important gene pathway for neurodegenerative diseases. In the future, we can apply the proposed method to systematically survey all the know pathways to build a database which show how gene regulatory networks vary with different covariates such as age and gender. Such a database can greatly deepen our understandings of the gene regulation mechanism and serve as an important resource for the scientific community. Moreover, built upon the current framework, we can further develop statistical methods to study how the dependence structures among multivariate time series change with covariates of interest, which can help reveal the associations between the dependence structures among different stock prices and macroeconomic indices such as CPIs and GDPs.

14306417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14306417.value: Graphical structures are often used to characterize the dependence structures among a set of random variables. For example, the gene regulatory network represents the dependence among expression levels of different genes. However, there is a lack of research on how the graphical structures can change with covariates. For instance, despite the large body of literature devoted to learning gene regulatory networks, little is known about how gene regulatory networks change with age and gender. This project provides a solid statistical framework to learn the relationship between graphical structures and covariates of interests. The scientific discovery from this project greatly deepens our understanding of gene regulatory networks and disease mechanism. The statistical methods developed in this project opens door to research on how the dependence structures among a set of features are associated with another set of features, which can be applied to many problems in economics, sociology, biology and medicine.

14306617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14306617.value: 多重乳液或雙重乳液是一種液滴穩定存在於另一液滴中的分級多相體系，主要包含水包油包水(W/O/W)和油包水包油(O/W/O)兩種類型。多重乳液中的內部分散液滴和外層液相通過另一中間相分隔開來。基於這種結構，多重乳液在食品工業領域廣泛用於封裝敏感性營養物質或香料，提高油脂氧化穩定性，以及構建低熱量和減脂食品。 儘管多重乳液在食品科學中具有巨大的應用潛力，然而其製備方法複雜，且維持長效結構穩定性也極具挑戰。多數情況下，多重乳液的形成是通過組合使用親脂性和親水性的乳化劑，並採用兩步乳化過程而實現。這種多步驟生產路徑非常複雜，且二次乳化通常會破壞內液相，從而造成封裝成分的流失。此外，由於滲透梯度的出現和乳化劑在油水界面形成的夾層膜較薄，內液相與外液相之間由熱力學驅動的擴散交換可導致內部液滴發生溶脹或收縮，隨即引發中間薄液層破裂，最終造成複乳結構不穩定。 當前，以微米和納米尺度膠體粒子穩定的乳液和泡沫成為食品配製研究中一個活躍的領域。膠體粒子穩定的乳液也稱為皮克林(Pickering)乳液，憑藉不可逆的界面吸附，出色的穩定性以及可再生性，皮克林乳液相比於傳統表面活性劑穩定的乳液顯示出更多的優越性。近期，我們已經證明，自主設計的混合高分子刷修飾的表面絨毛狀粒子和具有環境響應性的離子型微凝膠粒子均可用作皮克林乳液的穩定劑，並能夠通過一步法形成多重乳液。而且，許多不同種類的蛋白質(如酪蛋白和乳清蛋白)和多醣可用於製備微凝膠粒子。因此，本項目計劃深入研究一步法製備皮克林複乳的機理以及探索多重乳液在食品工業中的應用潛力。我們將著重從以下幾個方面進行研究： (1) 以自主設計的離子型微凝膠粒子為穩定劑製備複乳並研究一步法製備多重乳液的形成機理； (2) 通過調控組分和加工過程的變量來調節和研究皮克林多重乳液的穩定性和結構； (3) 設計和合成食品級蛋白質微凝膠粒子作為新型膠體配料用於一步法製備多重乳液過程中的穩定劑； (4) 研究和評價蛋白質微凝膠粒子穩定的多重乳液在食品配方設計中的封裝效率，封裝穩定性，釋放行為以及抗氧化能力。 許多我們喜愛的加工食品都是基於乳液的形式，如蛋黃醬，沙拉味調料，人造黃油，巧克力，慕斯，冰淇淋。W/O/W型多重乳液在低卡路里和減脂食品的構建方面是一個極有希望的嘗試方向。然而受限於複雜的製備過程和乳液穩定性問題，多重乳液的應用並未在食品工業領域廣泛展開。本項目有望解決這些問題並促使複乳在食品工業中廣泛推廣和應用，為大眾打造更加健康的食品產品。

14306617.label: Realisation of objectives
14306617.value: There are four objectives in this project and the details of the realization related to each objective are as follows: 1. To prepare multiple emulsions stabilized by engineered ionic microgel particles and examine the mechanism of their one-step formation. We have synthesized a series of engineered ionic microgels for stabilizing water-in-oil-in-water (w/o/w) multiple emulsions. With 1-vinylimidazole (VIM) introduced as comonomer, the poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) (PNIPAM)-based microgel exhibited superb amphiphilicity and formed multiple emulsions in a single-step route. By comparison, when using methacrylic acid (MMA) as comonomer, the commonly observed single oil-in-water (o/w) emulsion will be obtained. The amphiphilicity of PNIPMA-co-VIM microgel was accounted for as the acid-base interaction between VIM and silicon oil. Considering the similarities between microgels and biopolymers, we anticipated that the amphiphilic microgel could be used to design amphiphilic edible particles, which can be applied to foods, delivery and cosmetics. Advanced emulsion technology and structural design principles were also utilized to create the micro-scale egg-like structured multiple emulsions (10-100 μm). In particular, a w/o/w multiple emulsion was formulated using natural materials found in eggs (lecithin, oleic acid, and albumin) to create the egg yolk/egg white structure. Then, a CaCO3 “eggshell” was fabricated in situ to stabilize the outer oil-water interface. A potential mechanism for the formation of such egg-like structure was proposed. 2. To tune and investigate the stability and structure of the resulting Pickering multiple emulsions by adjusting compositional and processing variables. For both as-prepared PNIPAM-co-MAA and PNIPAM-co-VIM microgels, we found that they were readily adsorbed onto the oil−water interface, while the latter gave a lower interfacial tension. Like most amphiphilic emulsifiers, tuning the homogenization conditions also affects the obtained emulsions. We examined the effects of microgel concentration and oil fractions on emulsion properties. It turned out that a good multiple emulsion could be obtained at a high microgel particle concentration (>0.1%, w/v) and a mediate oil fraction (0.3−0.5). Otherwise, phase inversion might occur. We also tested the versatility of PNIPAM-co-VIM microgels with different edible oils and multiple emulsions were obtained as well, which hopefully would shed some light on designing biopolymer-based microgels for food-grade multiple emulsions. For the micro-scale egg-like structured emulsions, the stability of the W/O/W droplets during storage was evaluated. We found that the stability could be improved by forming a fat crystal network inside the oil phase by cooling the system below the melting point of the oleic acid and/or by neutralization of the pH by adding NaOH. These micro-scale egg-like structured multiple emulsions may be useful for encapsulating and protecting hydrophobic and hydrophilic bioactive substances. Moreover, they could easily be incorporated into functional foods designed to improve human health and wellness. 3. To design and synthesize food-grade protein microgel particles as a new class of colloidal ingredients for the stabilization of multiple emulsions produced in a single-step process. Sodium caseinate (NaCas), which is derived from casein has been prepared as the sole emulsifier to formulate emulsions. NaCas is an intrinsically disordered proteins (IDP) with unique open conformation. Another attractive feature is the intrinsically present of the specific phosphorylation-site motifs, such as [-(Ser(P)-)3 (Glu-)2] of NaCas. The hydrolysis leads to casein phosphopeptide (CPP) which could be used as a vehicle for ions capture, providing theoretical support for strong salt tolerance formation and resulting in nearly infinite cyclability that has never been observed in any protein-stabilized emulsions. We demonstrated that NaCas can be universally applied to stabilize many other kinds of oils, including toluene, benzene and dichloromethane, and the resultant emulsions could be switched on or off through the regulation of the pH value within one minute under stirring. Zein nanoparticles (ZNPs) and starch nanocrystals (SNCs) were prepared and characterized as well as used as the particular emulsifiers to formulate emulsions. A novel Pickering emulsion synergistically stabilized by ZNPs and SNCs was successfully prepared. The investigation into the stabilization mechanism reveals that the ultra-stability of the emulsions is a result of the oriented assembly of two individual particles at the oil/water (o/w) interface. Such a unique structure endows Pickering emulsions with ultrastability against coalescence under different stresses such as high-speed centrifugation, pH change and heat. This study provides an excellent example of the preparation of the Pickering emulsions stabilized by natural binary particles. We also developed a high internal phase emulsion (HIPE)-based w/o/w multiple emulsion system. Zein nanoparticles and soybean lecithin were found to have a synergistic effect in stabilization — using both natural emulsifiers together resulted in the formation of w/o/w double-emulsions with improved stability, which was further confirmed by the interfacial tension and rheology of zein- and/or lecithin-laden oil-water interfaces. It turns out lecithin contributes to the strong surface elasticity of the interfacial films while zein nanoparticles support the formation of the lecithin layer. 4. To investigate and evaluate the encapsulation efficiency, encapsulation stability, release behavior and oxidation stability of protein microgel-stabilized multiple emulsions in food formulations.. The micro-scale egg-like structured multiple emulsions have been used to encapsulate, protect, and deliver bioactive agents. We investigated the influence of temperature and pH on the stability of the multiple emulsions. Oleic acid is known to form crystalline networks at temperatures below its melting point (14 °C). This phenomenon may account for the increase in stability of the multiple emulsions that was observed when they were stored in a refrigerator at 4 °C. Similarly, the stability of the multiple emulsions could be improved by controlling the pH. The results showed that the structure of multiple emulsions remained intact when stored under neutral or weakly alkaline conditions, with no obvious demulsification even after 1 month of storage. The release behaviors study suggested that cargo-loaded water droplets were released from the oil droplets during storage. Under acidic conditions, the oleic acid should be fully protonated due to the high H+ concentration, which leads to a higher hydrophobicity of the oil phase inside the oil droplets, which slowed down the expulsion of the cargo-loaded water droplets compared to under neutral conditions. The slower release rate of the cargo-loaded water droplets from the acidified multiple emulsions at 4 °C than at 25 °C can be attributed to the crystallization of the oleic acid at the lower temperature. As a result, the movement of the cargo-loaded water droplets through the oil phase in the oil droplets was reduced. Normally, food-grade emulsions are o/w or w/o emulsions. A w/o emulsion can effectively protect the encapsulated actives by the oily layer, but this kind of emulsion may have an unpleasant taste in the mouth because the continuous phase is oil liquid. Our developed water-in-squalane-in-water multiple emulsion system solves this problem by introducing an outermost aqueous phase. To verify the potential of the w/o/w multiple emulsion as a delivery system, we conducted digestion experiments in simulated gastric fluid. Upon being delivered to the stomach, although the outermost aqueous phase may be destroyed by the gastric juice, the remaining w/o emulsion can still protect the inner nutrients, ensuring a more successful delivery to the intestine. The simulated digestion results demonstrated in our study show that the inner w/o morphology remains intact after 120 min digestion in the simulated gastric juice.

14306617.label: Major findings and research outcome
14306617.value: This research project has been successfully accomplished by our group. A series of engineered microgel particles and protein particles were synthesized and characterized so as to the production of food emulsions, in which their encapsulation properties, release behavior and oxidative stability were examined. This project has generated a total of 15 high-quality publications in the colloidal science and food chemistry fields and trained 2 PhD and 1 MPhil students. The main findings are summarized as follows: 1. We presented the synthesis and characterization of Poly(N-isopropylacrylamide)-co-methacrylic acid (PNIPAM-co-MAA) based multi-responsive soft microgel particles employed as ‘‘smart emulsifiers” for controlled stabilization and breakage of the Pickering emulsions (J. Colloid Interf. Sci. 2019). 2. We report an easy procedure for the preparation of a poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) PNIPAM-based microgel which can stabilize water-in-oil-in-water (w/o/w) multiple emulsions in one step (Langmuir, 2021). 3. We developed a robust pH-responsive oil-in-water (o/w) emulsion prepared by using pure sodium caseinate (NaCas) as the particulate emulsifier. We found that stabilization and destabilization of the obtained NaCas-stabilized emulsion can be unprecedentedly triggered by simply tuning the pH value of the solution and that this cyclability maintained over 100 cycles (Chem. Sci. 2020). 4. Ultra-stable emulsions synergistically stabilized by zein nanoparticles and starch nanocrystals were successfully prepared and the stabilization is ascribed to the double-layer shell of binary particles. The as-prepared emulsions showed unprecedented stability against centrifugation up to 20 000g and against environmental stresses such as pH change and high temperature (Chem. Commun 2020). 5. We produced food-grade microcarriers that mimic many of the structural and functional properties of egg cells. The biomimic egg-structured multiple emulsions developed in this study were used as microcarriers to encapsulate, protect, and release valuable nutrients in functional foods designed to improve human health and performance (ACS Appl. Bio. Mater 2021). 6. We developed a w/o/w high internal phase multiple emulsion based on all-natural materials, including the oil phase, aqueous phase, and stabilizers, which will open up a new and healthy platform for nutraceutical delivery and cosmetics (Food Hydrocolloids 2021).

14306617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14306617.value: In this project, multiple emulsions stabilized by engineered microgel particles have been successfully produced. Based on advances in understanding the physical behavior of microgels at the oil/water interfaces, we extended our study to the production of food emulsions using protein microgel particles as the Pickering emulsifiers and evaluated their encapsulation properties, release behavior and oxidative stability. Since the developed multiple emulsion systems are based on all-natural materials, including the oil phase, aqueous phase, and stabilizers, they should be very useful for encapsulation and controlled release for both hydrophobic and hydrophilic bioactive substances. However, more in vitro and in vivo studies will be needed in different conditions in order to turn this kind of edible emulsions to serve as a novel nutritional agent and carriers for personal care and healthcare applications.

14306617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14306617.value: Obesity has become a world-wide crisis as a result of chronic energy imbalance: people intake too many calories but do not take enough exercise. This causes social problems such as employment opportunities and leads to many health risks such as cardiovascular disease, diabetes and strokes. Accordingly, the food industry is seeking to produce foods that are acceptable in terms of their performance, but contain less fat. Many food products that we consume on a daily basis, such as milk, salad dressing and butter, are formulations based on emulsions. The replacement of conventional oil-water (o/w) emulsions by multiple emulsions, particularly water-oil-water (w/o/w) type emulsions, has long been considered as a promising strategy to reduce the fat content of food products. Practical applications, for example in low-fat yogurt and model cheeses, have been proposed, however multiple emulsions are much more difficult to prepare and characterize than simple emulsions, and they may be less stable. In this project, multiple emulsions stabilized by engineered protein particles have been successfully produced and their formation mechanism have been examined. The discovery of this research will promote the replacement of conventional surfactants by edible protein particles and help develop healthier emulsions for incorporation in everyday foods.

14306817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14306817.value: Maxwell’s equations possess an inherent symmetry, where the electric and magnetic fields play an equivalent role in free-space light propagation. However, for natural materials, their dielectric permittivities are usually very different from that in vacuum, while the magnetic permeabilities are close to its free-space value at optical frequencies. This explains why the interaction of a material with the magnetic field of light is usually much weaker than that with the electric field. Materials that can support strong magnetic resonance in the optical region (visible and near-infrared) are hardly found in nature. However, magnetic resonances are generally required for designing metamaterials, which offer a number of breakthrough technologies, such as negative refraction, optical cloaking, miniaturized superlensing, and electromagnetically induced transparency for slowing and stopping light. Tremendous efforts have been made to synthesize noble metal nanoparticles, because of their extraordinary localized surface plasmon resonance, which can interact strongly with light. So far, a majority of metal nanoparticles only possess electric plasmon resonances. Few metal nanoparticles or nanostructures can support magnetic plasmon resonances. A pioneering type is split-ring resonators, which were designed to provide a magnetic response at microwave frequencies in 1999. Magnetic resonances were also achieved in various complicated plasmonic nanostructures. These different nanostructures supporting magnetic plasmon generally suffer from several disadvantages: (1) Magnetic plasmon has rarely been achieved on individual metal nanoparticles. (2) Complicated nanostructures often lead to increases in size, cost and energy loss. (3) Complicated nanostructures are usually difficult to be assembled with other nanomaterials to study the interactions of magnetic plasmon with various optical processes. (4) The reported nanostructures have mainly been fabricated by physical methods, which are tedious, low throughput, and often cause severe plasmon damping. Here we propose (1) the synthesis of colloidal metal nanostructures supporting strong magnetic plasmon resonance, and (2) the study of magnetic plasmon-based coupling as well as (3) the interactions between magnetic plasmon and magnetic dipole transition. We will focus on highly asymmetric Au nanocups and split nanorings. We foresee that the success of this project will lead to the production of high-quality colloidal Au nanocups and nanorings supporting strong and energy-variable magnetic plasmon resonance at low cost. Moreover, the unique geometries of Au nanocups and nanorings will offer unprecedented opportunities for studying the interactions of magnetic plasmon resonance with other optical processes, which will greatly contribute to the understanding of magnetic plasmon resonances and their interactions at the nanoscale. 麥克斯韋方程組具有内在的對稱性，使得電場與磁場在真空環境下的光傳播中扮演著同等重要的角色。然而，天然材料的介電系數在介質和真空環境中存在很大的差異，但在光頻段它們通常具備與真空相近的磁導率。這一現象解釋了爲什麽材料與磁場的相互作用通常弱於它們與電場的相互作用。也正因如此，在自然界中很難發現能夠在可見光及近紅外範圍內支援強磁性共振的天然材料。 然而，研發而成的超材料通常具備磁共振特性，用以提供許多突破性的技術，比如負折射、光學隱身、小型超透鏡和用以減慢光綫乃至停止光綫的電磁感應透明等。由于其出眾的表面等離激元共振性能，貴金屬納米顆粒可以與光進行強烈的相互作用，因此人們在貴金屬納米顆粒的合成方面做出了巨大的努力。迄今爲止，大多數的納米顆粒只具備電等離激元共振特性，但很少有金屬納米顆粒或是納米結構可以支持磁等離激元共振。1999年，一種開口諧振環開創性的被用來產生微波頻段上的磁響應。之後，許多可以支持磁等離激元共振的複雜的納米結構被相繼開發出來。但是，這些具備磁等離激元共振特性的不同納米結構一般存在以下缺點：(1)單個納米顆粒很難產生磁性等離激元共振；(2)複雜的納米結構通常會導致尺寸、成本以及能量損失的提升；（3）複雜的納米結構由於通常很難與其它納米材料進行組裝，因此阻礙了其被應用於研究磁性等離激元共振與其他光學過程的相互作用；(4)之前所報導過的納米結構主要是通過物理方法製備的，所用的方法耗時長且產量低，並且通常會造成很强的等離激元阻尼。 因此，我們計劃(1)製備可以支持強的磁等離激元共振的膠體金屬納米結構，並(2)研究基於磁等離激元共振之間的耦合作用，以及(3)磁等離激元共振和磁偶極子轉換間相互作用。我們將會集中研究高度不對稱的金納米杯以及納米開口環。我們預計這一項目將會成功幫助我們生產低成本、高質量的以及具有共振能量可控的強磁等離激元共振的金納米杯以及金納米開口環膠體。此外，金納米杯和納米開口環的獨特形貌將會為我們研究磁等離激元共振與其他光學過程的相互作用提供寶貴的機會，並將會對理解磁等離激元共振以及它們在納米尺度的相互耦合作用作出重大貢獻。

14306817.label: Realisation of objectives
14306817.value: All of the 4 objectives were fulfilled in this project. The first objective is to synthesize colloidal gold nanostructures with strong magnetic plasmon resonance. We developed chemical methods for the synthesis of gold nanocups with strong magnetic resonance and control of their geometrical parameters (overall size, opening size, cavity depth) (ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces 2019). As a result, the strength and wavelength of the magnetic resonance can be adjusted. We also synthesized gold nanorings through a combination of multiple overgrowth and etching steps (Small 2019). The goal of the synthesis of the nanorings was to further open a slit to give split nanorings, which have been shown by others to exhibit strong magnetic plasmon resonance. Although we tried different methods to open a slit on the nanoring, we did not succeed. We further prepared zirconia nanospheres by aerosol spray. The zirconia nanospheres exhibit both electric and magnetic Mie resonance modes (Advanced Optical Materials 2021). Although the Mie resonance modes associated with dielectric nanoparticles are different from plasmon resonance modes, they have the advantage of reduced loss and are suitable for some niche applications. The second objective is to study and understand the geometrical parameters that affect the characteristics of the magnetic plasmon resonance (resonance wavelength, absorption/scattering cross-sections, linewidth, resonance strength relative to electric plasmon) of the colloidal gold nanostructures. The overall size (100-230 nm), the opening size (10-120 nm), and the cavity depth of gold nanocups were systematically varied during synthesis by combining overgrowth with mild etching (ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces 2019). Their effects on the intensity and wavelength of the magnetic resonance mode were investigated. The magnetic plasmon wavelength was tunable from 600 to 900 nm. The outer diameter, the inner diameter (40-90 nm), and the thickness (30-50 nm) of gold nanorings were also systematically varied by choosing circular gold nanodisks of different diameters and thicknesses (Small 2019). The electric field enhancement contours of the gold nanorings with different thicknesses were simulated. The substrate effect on the far-field scattering properties of the gold nanorings were also studied (ACS Materials Letters 2020). The in-plane and out-of-plane plasmon modes of the gold nanorings deposited on metallic films can be excited in varying proportions, which are dependent on the incidence angle of light, producing distinct, and controllable far-field scattering plasmonic colors. Moreover, largely enhanced second-harmonic generation (SHG) was observed on the gold nanocups (Nano Letters 2019). The most efficient SHG was experimentally observed on the gold nanocups with a particular cavity depth. The maximal SHG can be attributed to the joint action of the optimized magnetic plasmon resonance and the “lightning-rod effect” of the gold nanocups. Interesting SHG and third-harmonic generation (THG) properties were also observed on hollow gold nanostars that were synthesized in a similar manner to the gold nanocups (ACS Nano 2020). The third objective is to study and understand the plasmon coupling behaviors between the magnetic plasmon of the colloidal gold nanostructures and the electric plasmon of gold nanospheres. We tried to assemble together the gold nanocups and gold nanospheres, where the gold nanosphere was selectively positioned inside or outside the cavity of the gold nanocup. However, this experiment was not successful. It was challenging to construct the assembled structures out of the gold nanocups and nanospheres in solutions. We next tried to assemble the gold nanocups and gold nanoplates on substrates. In this experiment, the pre-synthesized gold nanoplates were first deposited on a substrate. They lied flat on the substrate. Dithiol molecules were then attached on the gold nanoplates. The substrate carrying the gold nanoplates was subsequently immersed in a solution containing the gold nanocups. In this way, the heterodimers were formed from the gold nanoplates and nanocups. We aimed to realize forward scattering and suppress backward scattering by aligning the magnetic dipole plasmon resonance of the nanocup perpendicular to the electric dipole plasmon resonance of the nanoplate. Many heterodimers were measured, where the nanocups were positioned on top of and beside the nanoplate. However, no conclusive results were obtained from this experiment. On the other hand, the gold nanorings were assembled with gold nanospheres to give heterodimers in sphere-in-ring and sphere-on-ring configurations on substrates (Small 2019). The sphere-in-ring heterodimers exhibited the interesting feature of plasmonic Fano resonance upon the excitation of the dark quadrupolar plasmon mode of the gold nanorings. The zirconia nanospheres were assembled with gold nanospheres to give heterodimers (Advanced Optical Materials 2021). The scattering signals of the heterodimers were approximately the sum of the contributions from the individual components. Furthermore, plasmon-induced toroidal resonances and anapole states were demonstrated in a simple structure, which was made of gold nanoplates deposited on a gold film through a dielectric spacer (Advanced Optical Materials 2020). Our studies revealed that the observed toroidal resonances were originated from the higher-order cavity modes, which can further interfere with the dipolar antenna mode to generate the anapole states. The cavity modes were strongly dependent on the lateral size of the nanoplate, offering a straightforward method for altering the anapole excitation at optical frequencies. In contrast to the excitation of the toroidal resonances and the anapole states at small spacer thicknesses, the structure with a thick dielectric spacer was found to support the plasmon-induced magnetic resonance with a narrow linewidth. Our findings provided a simple and practical platform for generating strong magnetic resonance in metallic nanostructures. The fourth objective is to study and understand the interaction behaviors between the magnetic plasmon of the colloidal gold nanostructures and the magnetic dipole transitions of lanthanide-doped upconversion nanocrystals. We indeed synthesized lanthanide nanoparticles and tried to assemble the lanthanide nanoparticles with the gold nanocups, where the position of the lanthanide nanoparticles could be controlled. However, we could not obtain well-defined heterostructures out of the lanthanide nanoparticles and the gold nanocups. There was either no assembly or random aggregates were formed. We therefore synthesized dielectric zirconia nanospheres by aerosol spray (Advanced Optical Materials 2021). These dielectric nanospheres were found to support strong magnetic Mie resonances. Europium ions with magnetic dipole transitions were doped inside the zirconia nanospheres. In contrast to previous structures where magnetic dipole emitters were positioned outside dielectric nanoresonators, our structure offered an unprecedented opportunity for the light emitters to access the strong magnetic field within the dielectric nanoresonator. This unique architecture allowed the magnetic emission from the doped europium ions to be effectively manipulated. Moreover, in the heterostructures made of gold nanospheres and the europium-doped zirconia spheres, the electric dipole emissions of the europium ions were enhanced strongly by the plasmon resonance of the gold nanospheres, while the magnetic dipole emission was weakly affected, suggesting much weaker interaction between the magnetic dipole transition and the electric resonance.

14306817.label: Major findings and research outcome
14306817.value: There are 4 findings that are closely related to this project. First, the synthetic control of gold nanocups with strong magnetic plasmon resonance is developed (ACS of Applied Materials and Interfaces 2019). Second, the synthesis of gold nanorings is developed (Small 2019). Their interactions with gold nanospheres and substrates are understood (ACS Materials Letters 2020). These nanorings can potentially be made into split nanorings, which exhibit strong magnetic plasmon resonance. Third, the gold nanocups are found to exhibit superior nonlinear optical properties (Nano Letters 2019 and ACS Nano 2020). Fourth, Eu-doped zirconia spheres are synthesized. The spheres exhibit both electric and magnetic resonance modes. The magnetic resonance mode is found to enhance the emission of the magnetic dipole transitions in europium ions. In addition to the major, closely related findings mentioned above, we also made discoveries that are related to the topic of the project loosely. First, the vertical alignment of gold nanoplates on substrate is realized, and their molecular sensitivities are elucidated (Nanoscale 2018 and The Journal of Physical Chemistry C 2019). Second, chemical and electrochemical switching of Fano resonance and plasmonic colors are demonstrated (Nanoscale 2019 and ACS of Applied Materials and Interfaces 2020). Third, color routing is realized on single silver nanorods (Light: Science and Applications 2019). Fourth, three-dimensional plasmonic color lasering printing is demonstrated with transparent polymer matrixes with embedded gold nanodisks (Advanced Optical Materials 2020). Fifth, a versatile electrochemical approach is developed for coating conductive polymers on noble metal nanocrystals (Nanoscale 2020). Sixth, long gold nanonails are synthesized to enhance molecular infrared light absorption (Nanoscale Horizons 2020). We published 20 papers with the support from this grant. 17 are research articles, and 3 are invited review articles. They are on Accounts of Chemical Research, ACS of Applied Materials and Interfaces (2), ACS Materials Letters, ACS Nano, Advanced Optical Materials (4), Chemical Science, Light: Science and Applications, Nano Letters, Nano-Micro Letters, Nanoscale (4), Scientia Sinica Physica, Mechanica & Astronomica, Small, and The Journal of Physical Chemistry C. Most of these journals are mainstream ones. We were invited to present our research results. 9 invited talks with topics related to this project were given in regional and international conferences. Moreover, two PhD students were trained during this project. One was in physics and the other one was in materials science and engineering.

14306817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14306817.value: We discovered that circular gold nanodisks can produce strong magnetic plasmon resonance when they are deposited on gold films and separated by a dielectric layer of 5 to 10 nm in thickness. The magnetic plasmon resonance peak produced by such nanostructures is much narrower and stronger than that exhibited by gold nanocups. The magnetic plasmon resonance wavelength can be tuned by varying the diameter of the nanodisk and the thickness of the dielectric layer. Moreover, the nanodisk-based structures are much easier to fabricate than gold nanocups. The nanodisk-based structures therefore provide a great opportunity for studying the interactions of magnetic plasmon resonance with other electromagnetic effects. We are going to insert two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenide (TMDC) monolayers in the structures and study the coupling between the magnetic plasmon resonance and the 2D excitons and the effect of the interaction on the emission behaviors of the 2D excitons. 2D TMDC monolayers possess rich excitons (bright excitons, dark excitons, trions). The 2D excitons also exhibit chiroptical properties. They have numerical applications in optics, optoelectronics, and quantum information processing. The nanodisk-based structures are particularly suitable for the manipulation of the various excitons and their emissions in 2D TMDC monolayers.

14306817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14306817.value: This project is devoted to nanoparticles with strong magnetic resonance. It includes the synthesis of such nanoparticles, understanding the properties of the magnetic resonance, and study of the interactions between magnetic resonance and other electromagnetic effects. The study of magnetic resonance is of both fundamental and technological importance. Light waves always carry both electric and magnetic fields. Although the electric field of light plays a dominant role in the optical range, the magnetic field is always existent. Moreover, magnetic resonance can bring negative permeabilities, which, together with electric resonance, can lead to the creation of various metamaterials and metadevices, such as ultrathin lenses and superior holograms. Therefore, the synthesis of nanoparticles with strong magnetic resonance and understanding of their magnetic resonance properties and behaviors are highly desired. In this project, gold nanocups with strong magnetic plasmon resonance has been synthesized. Their geometrical parameters, including the overall size, opening size, and depth, can all be synthetically varied, and so are their magnetic plasmon resonance properties. The nanocups have been found to exhibit superior nonlinear optical performances. The magnetic resonance can enhance magnetic dipole emissions. These results will be very useful for developing magnetic-resonance-enabled metamaterials and metadevices.

14306917.value: Design and implement algorithms for the extraction and analysis of homeomorphic deformations. 14306917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14306917.value: 形變在現實世界中很常見。理解幾何形狀的變形模式在計算機視覺，醫學成像和計算機圖形學等各個領域都有重要的應用。例如，在醫學圖像分析中，分析心臟運動對於心臟病分析至關重要。因此，形變分析的需求不斷增加，我們有必要開發準確有效的工具來研究形變。在這個項目中，我們的目標是為各種形變分析問題開發數學算法。 本研究主要分為兩部分。在研究的第一部分，我們有興趣開發有效的數學算法進行形變分析。我們將考慮幾個形變分析問題。首先，現實世界中的形狀變形通常是非確定性的，這涉及不確定性和隨機性。因此，在實際應用中我們需要分析隨機形變的模型。在這個項目中，我們將研究使用具有隨機係數的橢圓偏微分方程來分析隨機性形變的可能性。 其次，異常變形的提取在許多應用中是非常重要，尤其是醫學成像。其挑戰性在於形狀變形通常是由正常和異常變形部分組成，故此，我們需要設計數學算法，將異常形變與正常形變分開。第三，我們將研究根據形狀信息和不同區域的形變類型，從單一圖像中提取形狀的多尺度變形模式，形變的多尺度提取對形狀分析特別重要 。在這個項目中，我們將研究一個優化模型，將Beltrami係數的小波分解與分割模型結合起來，以提取多尺度變形分解。最後，現實世界應用中的一些形變可能是非同構的。為了分析這種形變，我們將開發數學模型來描述和分析非同構形變。 接下來，在我們研究的第二部分，我們有興趣將所提出的算法應用於醫學圖像分析，圖像處理和計算機圖形學中。 我們將使用多尺度變形提取算法來恢復氣流失真圖像。我們亦會應用提取異常形變的算法來研究病人的心臟運動。用於分析非確定性形變的模型也可以進一步應用於心髒病分析 。對於計算機圖形的應用，我們將應用分析非同構形變的數學模型來描述衣服形變。

14306917.label: Realisation of objectives
14306917.value: In this project, we have proposed several objectives. The ultimate goal is to develop mathematical models for deformation analysis and explore their applications. The developed models are then applied to various deformation analysis problems for real-world applications. The PI has tackled each proposed problems successfully. Details are as follows. Objective 1: Our first objective is to design and implement algorithms for the extraction and analysis of homeomorphic deformations. The PI has successfully achieved this goal. There are several tasks involved in this objective. Below, we describe in detail what we have achieved for each tasks. Firstly, the PI has successfully developed a mathematical model to analyze deformation patterns with randomness. Deformation analysis is crucial in many applications, especially in medical image analysis. Analyzing the deformation pattern of anatomical structures provides important information for disease analysis. With degraded images, getting a deterministic solution of the deformation is challenging. In some cases, there may also be multiple solutions with different probabilities. As such, it is important to analyze the probability distribution of deformations, given data information with uncertainty. In this project, we have successfully developed a framework to tackle this task. The basic idea is to use computational Quasiconformal (QC) Teichmuller theories to parameterize the space of deformations with the Beltrami coefficients. A distribution over the space of special features, called the QC features, can be computed and applied for deformation analysis. Extensive experiments have been carried out on both synthetic data and real medical images, which demonstrate the efficacy of the developed framework. The developed framework is applicable to many practical uses, such as the classification of shapes and longitudinal deformations with multiple modes. In addition, we have further extended the framework that can classify corrupted medical images, of which their deformation patterns are non-deterministic. Secondly, another task in this objective is to extract abnormal deformation from a deforming shape. One application is to detect abnormal deformations of a cardiac motion for heart disease analysis. For this goal, the PI has successfully developed a model based on the low-rank and sparse decomposition of a deformation represented by the Beltrami coefficient. The low rank part of the Beltrami coefficient captures the global (normal and regular) motion of the deformation, whereas the sparse part captures the sudden abnormal deformation. In this project, we have successfully developed an effective numerical algorithm to solve the low rank and sparse decomposition. Effective optimization algorithm has been developed. The method has been tested extensively on both synthetic and real data, which demonstrate the efficacy of the method. The developed method has also been applied to medical imaging to detect abnormal deformation of a cardiac motion for heart disease analysis. Finally, we have developed methods to extract deformation patterns with priori information about the initial shape of the object and the deformation types at different regions. This can be applied to shape analysis as well as restoration of turbulence-distorted video. The task involves two components: first, we need to identify the deformation types of a particular problem; second, we need to develop a mathematical model to extract multiscale deformation based on the priori information about the geometry and deformation type of the deforming object. For this purpose, we have developed a machine-learning technique to learn the deformation types of turbulence-distorted video sequence based on deep neural network. The results are very encouraging and show that our developed method can effectively extract the deformation type. Given priori information about the geometry of the deforming object, we have developed a mathematical model to extract deformation. The method can extract deformations given a partial convexity constraint on the object. The experimental results demonstrated that the developed method is very effective for extracting deformation of a convex object. By considering the Fourier/Wavelet components, this approach can also be successfully used to extract deformation pattern of various scales with priori shape information. Objective 2: Our second objective is to develop a mathematical model to describe and analyze non-homeomorphic deformations. In real-world applications, deformations can be non-homeomorphic. For instance, the deformation of clothes may comprise of foldings, which is non-homeomorphic. In this project, we have successfully developed a mathematical model to describe non-homeomorphic deformations using the alternating Beltrami coefficient (ABC). Each non-homeomorphic deformation with foldings can be described by the ABC. The relationship between the non-homeomorphic deformation and the corresponding ABC is given by a partial differential equation, called the alternating Beltrami’s equation. The PDE has been carefully studied and numerical algorithms have been developed to solve the alternating Beltrami’s equation. The challenge lies in the fact that singularities occur on the folding lines/curves. To solve the problem, we have developed an effective approach that partitions domain into orientation-preserving and orientation-reversing regions and considers the variational formulation on each region. A second order PDE with suitable Neumann conditions on the folding lines can be derived. With that, the non-homeomorphic deformations can be effectively described by ABC (which measures the local geometric distortion) and can be efficiently reconstructed by solving the second order PDE. Experimental results demonstrated our developed method is very efficient and accurate. The method can also handle folding curves. Another challenge is that the folding pattern of a non-homeomorphic deformation is often partially known due to occlusions in real situations. In this situation, we need to develop a mathematical model to simultaneously determine the folding pattern as well as the folding map. For this purpose, we have developed a mathematical model and a numerical algorithm to solve the problem. The basic idea of the algorithm is an iterative scheme to simultaneously adjust the folding pattern and the folding map that converges to the final optimal solution. Experimental results show that our developed method can effectively handle folding map problem with significant missing information about the folding pattern. Objective 3: Our third objective is to apply the developed algorithms to image processing, medical image analysis and computer graphics. The PI has successfully accomplished this task. In this project, we have analyzed the effectiveness of using our developed shape analysis algorithms for different practical deformation analysis problems. More specifically, the proposed algorithms have been applied to study the deformation pattern of turbulence-distorted images, with which the restoration of the turbulence-distorted images can be done. The deformation analysis model to extract abnormal deformation components has also been successfully applied to deformation analysis of cardiac motions in medical image analysis. The developed models to describe and extract the non-homeomorphic deformations can also been used for the simulation of cloth deformation for virtual humans in computer graphics.

14306917.label: Major findings and research outcome
14306917.value: In this project, we have developed various mathematical models for deformation analysis, which have resulted in 5 published papers and 1 submitted papers (under revision). Details are as follows. (1) Deformation Analysis with Uncertainties: To analyze the deformation pattern with uncertainties, we have developed a new framework based on Quasiconformal theories [5,6]. The distribution of the Beltrami Fourier Descriptors are used to represent the distribution of deformations. With that, the classification of shapes and longitudinal deformations with multiple modes can be carried out. (2) Low-rank and sparse decomposition of a deformation: To extract abnormal deformation from a deforming shape, we have developed a mathematical model based on the low-rank and sparse decomposition of the Beltrami coefficients [4]. The low-rank part effectively represents the normal deformation pattern while the abnormal component is extracted as the sparse part. Effective optimization algorithm has been developed to solve the proposed model. (3) Extract deformation patterns with priori shape information: We have developed a model to extract deformation patterns with priori information about the initial shape of the object and the deformation types at different regions [3]. The method can also be incorporated with the Fourier/wavelet decomposition to extract deformation pattern of various scales with priori shape information. A machine-learning technique has also been developed to learn the deformation types of turbulence-distorted video sequence [2]. (4) Numerical solver for alternating Beltrami’s equation: To describe the non-homeomorphic deformation (branched folded map), we have developed a framework to represent the mapping using the alternating Beltrami coefficient [1]. The branched folded map satisfies the alternating Beltrami’s equation. An efficient numerical solver for the alternating Beltrami’s equation has been developed. (5) Mathematical model for determining the folding patterns: The folding pattern of a non-homeomorphic deformation is often partially known due to occlusions in real situations. To solve this problem, an iterative scheme has been developed to simultaneously adjust the folding pattern and the folding map that converges to the final optimal solution [1].

14306917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14306917.value: There are several areas for further development of the research: (1) For the determination of the folding pattern of a branched folded map, extra priori information is necessary if the occluded region is large. If some geometric information is known, this information can be used. A possible future direction is to explore how the priori geometric information can be integrated into the developed mathematical model to determine the folding pattern of a branched folded map with large occlusion. (2) The mathematical model to extract deformation patterns with priori shape information can be combined with machine learning techniques. Using deep learning methods, the shape feature can be learnt. The energy functional used in our developed model can be utilized as a loss function to train a deep neural network to extract deformation pattern using a deep learning framework. (3) The low rank and sparse decomposition of a deformation pattern can separate a deformation into different important components. These components capture different information about the deformation. The idea can be incorporated into the deep neural network of some deep-learning based framework for image registration problems for better performance. It should be an interesting direction, which is worthwhile to explore.

14306917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14306917.value: In this project, the main goal is to develop mathematical models for deformation analysis and explore their applications. We have explored two research directions: 1. Design and implement effective mathematical algorithms for deformation analysis and 2. Applications of the algorithms to practical problems. We have successfully developed and implemented mathematical models for the above two goals. For deformation analysis, we have developed a new framework to analyze deformation pattern with uncertainties. Using the low-rank and sparse decomposition of the Beltrami coefficient, a mathematical model has been developed to extract abnormal deformation from a deforming shape. Besides, we have developed a model to extract deformation patterns with priori information about the initial shape of the object and the deformation types at different regions. Finally, mathematical algorithms have been developed to analyze the non-homeomorphic deformations, called the branched folded maps. The developed algorithms have shown to be useful in various practical applications As for the second part of the project, we have explored the applications of proposed algorithms for practical uses. These include: the restoration of turbulence-distorted images, deformation analysis of cardiac motions in medical image analysis and the simulation of cloth deformation for virtual humans in computer graphics.

14307117.label: Realisation of objectives
14307117.value: In this research project, we have carried out an exploratory study on the coordination properties of a heteroatom-stabilized methanide ligand system towards divalent lanthanide metals. Methanide anions of the general formula [CRR'R"]– (R, R', R" = H or organic substituents) are prototypical alkyl ligands, yet thermally stable and structurally authenticated lanthanide(II) methanide complexes are rare because they are generally difficult to prepare and isolate. With respect to the project objectives as per original application: (1) A series of new alkali metal (Li+, Na+ and K+) complexes derived from monoanionic methanide ligand [CH(iPr2P–BH3)(C9H6N-2)]– were successfully synthesized in this work. Introduction of a diisopropylphosphinoyl substituent in our ligand system can enhance the stability of the methanide anion, whilst the 2-quinoyl group can provide an additional donor site resulting in the formation of metal methanide complexes with diversified structures. All of the compounds were fully characterized by NMR spectroscopy, elemental analysis and single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis. (2) Europium(II) and ytterbium(II) methanide complexes were successfully synthesized by metathesis reaction of the appropriate lanthanide diiodide LnI2(THF)2 (Ln = Eu, Yb) with 2 molar equivalents of the potassium reagent [K(18-crown-6)2[CH(iPr2P–BH3)(C9H6N-2)]2]n in THF. An X-ray diffraction analysis revealed that the Yb(II) complex had a mononuclear structure in which two anionic [CH(iPr2P–BH3)(C9H6N-2)]– ligands were loosely coordinating to the Yb(II) ion through agnostic-type Yb…H-B interactions. To the best of our knowledge, this structural feature has not been reported in organo-lanthanide(II) chemistry. Both Eu(II) and Yb(II) complexes were highly reactive and extremely sensitive to air and moisture. Besides, the weak lanthanide(II)-anionic ligand interactions rendered their isolation and characterization difficult to carry out. Unfortunately, attempts to prepare the most reducing Sm(II) derivative have not been successful. (3) Organo-lanthanide(II) complexes are strong one-electron reductants. We have explored the reactivity of the present Eu(II) and Yb(II) complexes with several organic substrates, including elemental iodine, diphenyl dichalcogenide PhEEPh (E = S, Se) and diazobenzene. It was expected that these reactions would lead to generation of the corresponding lanthanide(III) complexes. Unfortunately, attempts to isolate the desired products suitable for X-ray diffraction studies were unsuccessful, despite our effort devoted to screen appropriate reaction conditions for the reactions (e.g. screening of appropriate solvent systems and addition of appropriate ancillary donor ligands). In order to further explore the chemistry of our lanthanide(II) complexes, we have also prepared a series of alkaline earth metal (Mg2+, Ca2+, Sr2+, Ba2+) complexes of the [CH(iPr2P–BH3)(C9H6N-2)]– ligand for structural and reactivity comparison. It was noted that the structures and reactivity of heavier alkaline metal complexes are similar to those of their lanthanide(II) metal counterparts due to their similar metal ionic radii (for CN = 6: Ca2+ 100 pm, Yb2+ 102 pm, Sr2+ 118 pm, Eu2+ 117 pm) and hardness of the metal ions. All of the group 2 metal complexes were fully characterized by NMR spectroscopy, elemental analysis and X-ray crystallography. These complexes exhibited diversified structures with the methanide ligand bonding to the metal(II) centers in various coordination modes. (4) Besides, we have also examined the chemistry of heavier group 14 complexes derived from the present [CH(iPr2P–BH3)(C9H6N-2)]–methanide anion. Sn(II) and Ge(II) complexes were prepared by reactions of an appropriate metal dichloride with two molar equivalents of the lithium salt of the [CH(iPr2P–BH3)(C9H6N-2)]– ligand. Subsequent reduction of the latter Ge(II) complex with potassium metal led to isolation of a novel, mixed-valent homo-catenated [Ge(II)Ge(I)Ge(I)Ge(II)] complex. These interesting results will set a stage for our future investigation on the coordination chemistry of the present methanide system with the main-group elements.

14307117.label: Major findings and research outcome
14307117.value: Lanthanide(II) alkyl complexes are rarely reported in the literature. In the present research work, we have carried out an exploratory study on the coordination chemistry of the monoanionic, 2-quinolyl-linked (boranophosphorano)methanide ligand [CH(iPr2P–BH3)(C9H6N-2)]– with lanthanide(II) metal ions. Regarding the ligand design, the diisopropylphosphinoyl substituent can enhance the stability of the methanide anion, whilst the 2-quinolyl group can provide an additional donor site resulting in the formation of metal methanide complexes with diversified structures. Major findings of this work include: (1) A series of organo-alkali metal (Li+, Na+, K+) complexes derived from the [CH(iPr2P–BH3)(C9H6N-2)]– methanide ligand were successfully prepared and structurally characterized. The [CH(iPr2P–BH3)(C9H6N-2)]– ligand exhibited a "flexible" coordination behavior, forming metal complexes with diversified structures. The potassium complex exhibited an unusual one-dimensional polymeric structure, in which the anionic [(iPr2P–BH3)CH(C9H6N–2)]– ligand is loosely coordinating to the potassium ion via agostic-type K…H-B as well as eta2-arene interactions. Structurally well characterized organo-sodium and -potassium complexes of methanide ligands are rare. (2) Europium(II) and ytterbium(II) complexes derived from the [(iPr2P–BH3)CH(C9H6N–2)]– methanide ligand were successfully prepared. An X-ray diffraction analysis showed that the Yb(II) complex exhibited an unusual structure in which two [(iPr2P–BH3)CH(C9H6N–2)]– ligands were loosely coordinating to the Yb(II) cation through weak agnostic-type Yb(II)…H-B interactions, whilst the anionic charge was believed to delocalize onto the quinolyl nitrogen atom of the ligand. Unexpectedly, neither Yb(II)-carbon nor Yb(II)-nitrogen bonds were observed. To the best of our knowledge, this type of metal-alkyl interaction involving only loosely bound Ln(II)…H-B interactions has not been reported in organolanthanide(II) chemistry. (3) In addition, a series of alkaline earth metal (Mg2+, Ca2+, Sr2+ and Ba2+) complexes supported by the [(iPr2P–BH3)CH(C9H6N–2)]– ligand were successfully synthesized for comparison with the structures and reactivity of the lanthanide(II) counterparts. (4) Results of this study have demonstrated that the [(iPr2P–BH3)CH(C9H6N–2)]– ligand can exhibit variable coordination modes and form metal complexes with diversified structures. It can coordinate to the metal ions via exclusively its quinolyl nitrogen atom or through agostic-type M···H–B interactions. It can also coordinate to the metal ions via both the quinolyl nitrogen atom and the BH3 group. The modes of coordination depend on the ionic size of the metals as well as the ancillary donor ligands used (T.-H. Choi, W.-P. Leung, H. K. Lee and Y.-C. Chan, manuscript submitted and under review).

14307117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14307117.value: The successful synthesis of a series of groups 1 and 2, as well as lanthanide(II) complexes with interesting structures in this work prompted us to extend our study to other main group elements. Recently, there has been renewed interest in the chemistry of organo-main group complexes in a goal to achieve transition-metal free catalysis (European Journal of Inorganic Chemistry, Special collection: Main Group Catalysis.). Towards this direction, we have recently carried out an initial study on the coordination chemistry of the [CH(iPr2P–BH3)(C9H6N-2)]– methanide ligand with heavier group 14 metals, and a novel, mixed-valent, homo-catenated [Ge(II)Ge(I)Ge(I)Ge(II)] complex has been isolated (T.-H. Choi, W.-P. Leung and H. K. Lee, manuscript in preparation.). Therefore, it is worth to carry out a detailed investigation on the coordination chemistry of the [CH(iPr2P–BH3)(C9H6N-2)]–ligand with the whole series of heavier group 14 elements. It is worth to note that the electronic properties of the present methanide ligand can be tunable through introduction of various electron-donating or -withdrawing substituents. One would expect to observe a new series of heavier group 14 metal complexes with tunable reactivity.

14307117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14307117.value: Divalent lanthanide alkyl complexes are rarely reported in the literature. Structural and reactivity studies on lanthanide(II) alkyl complexes remain a challenging topic worthy of investigation. The present research project focused on the coordination chemistry of a monoanionic, heteroatom-stabilized methanide ligand, [CH(iPr2P–BH3)(C9H6N-2)]–, with lanthanide(II) metal ions. It is worth to note that methanide anions of the general formula [CRR'R"]– (R, R', R" = H or organic substituents) are prototypical alkyl ligands, yet thermally stable and structurally authenticated methanide complexes are difficult to prepare and isolate. The presence of a diisopropylphosphinoyl substituent in our ligand system can enhance the stability of the methanide anion, whilst the 2-quinoyl group can provide an additional donor site resulting in the formation of metal methanide complexes with diversified structures. Using the [CH(iPr2P–BH3)(C9H6N-2)]– methanide ligand, we have successfully synthesized a series of groups 1 and 2 as well as lanthanide(II) complexes in this work. The structures of the potassium and ytterbium(II) complexes are remarkable as similar structural features have not been reported in the literature. Results of our study have demonstrated that the [CH(iPr2P–BH3)(C9H6N-2)]– ligand could exhibit “flexible” coordination modes, depending on the metal ionic radii and the ancillary donor ligands being used.

14307317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14307317.value: On July 4, 2012, the ATLAS and the CMS collaborations at CERN (the European Organization for Nuclear Physics), announced the discovery of a particle compatible with the Standard Model Higgs boson in the analysis proton-proton collisions produced by the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). The discovery was followed by detailed studies of this particle, which demonstrated that it is indeed a scalar particle, as predicted by the Brout-Englert-Higgs mechanism. Among other awards, the discovery was recognized with the High Energy and Particle Physics Prize 2013 of the European Physical Society, awarded to the ATLAS and CMS collaborations, and the 2013 Nobel Prize in Physics, awarded to Professors Peter Higgs and Francois Englert. After an extended shut-down period for maintenance and upgrades, the LHC has re-started operations with a collision energy of 13 TeV, which is significantly higher than the energy used for the discovery (up to 8 TeV), and will collect a much larger data sample. The current data-taking period, customarily called “Run II”, will allow detailed measurements of the properties of the Higgs boson, and will make it possible to search for exotic decays of this particle, forbidden by (or strongly suppressed within) the Standard Model. Hong Kong institutions, building over the solid foundation provided by the success of the Daya Bay Reactor Experiment, have created the Joint Consortium for Fundamental Physics in Hong Kong (JCFP). In June of 2014, the JCFP was accepted as a member of the ATLAS Experimental Collaboration. Hong Kong researchers and students are actively involved in the analysis of data from Run II of the LHC. The JCFP collaborates with the ATLAS Muon Spectrometer Project, Higgs studies and Exotic Physics searches, and has adopted a number of responsibilities within the ATLAS collaboration. The goal of this project is to strengthen the participation of the JCFP in the ATLAS Experiment at CERN through work on the following areas: 1. Search for exotic decays of the Higgs boson; in particular in lepton-flavor violating decays. 2. Tuning and enhancement of muon identification algorithms in the ATLAS Collaboration. These areas are designed to avoid overlap with the objectives of the JCFP proposals and, to the maximum extent possible, to complement them to build a complete and solid physics program from Hong Kong institutions, with a significant impact and a long-term contribution to LHC Physics.

14307317.label: Realisation of objectives
14307317.value: All objectives were achieved. Details on each one are given below. Objective 1. Search for exotic decays of the Higgs boson; in particular, in lepton-flavor violating decays (e-mu, e-tau, mu-tau). The search for phenomena beyond the predictions of the Standard Model of Particle Physics (SM) is one of the main goals of the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) research program at CERN. One possible sign of such phenomena is lepton flavor violation (LFV) in decays of the Higgs boson [ATL12, CMS12]. LFV is predicted by several beyond-SM theories as, for example, extensions of the Higgs sector or warped extra dimensions [AHR13, AGA09, ALB09]. Before the period covered by this project, our team had already become an active participant in the study of the Higgs boson, and in searches for new high-mass resonances decaying into lepton flavor violating final states, first using only the e-mu channel [LFV15] and later all three possible LFV channels (e-mu, e-tau, mu-tau) [LFV16, LFV18]. This project allowed us to build upon that experience to become one of the main contributors in ATLAS to the search for LFV decays of the Higgs boson [RO1, RO2], where we have studied the impact of adding new signal regions to the analysis to enhance the sensitivity of the study in events where the Higgs boson is likely to have been produced through vector-boson-fusion (VBF). We designed these regions for both the leptonic and the hadronic decays of the tau leptons, which yielded an increase of about 10% in the significance of both channels. We also implemented a multivariate analysis (MVA) to study the VBF region for the hadronic decays of the tau leptons. The MVA was based on Boosted Decision Trees (BDT); we optimized the parameters of the BDT’s used and achieved a higher statistical significance than the corresponding cut-based analysis (CBA). We performed the statistical analysis of both the CBA (based on the distribution of the collinear mass of the tau and the lepton), and the BDT (based on the BDT score distribution), to study the significances, limits, and nuisance parameter rankings, as well as the behaviour of the systematic uncertainties. The results of this analysis were approved by the ATLAS Collaboration to be made public at the Conference on Flavor Physics and CP Violation (FPCP 2019) in Victoria BC, Canada [DEM19], and at the Large Hadron Collider Physics Conference 2019 in Puebla, Mexico [DEL19]. With 36.1 fb-1 of pp data, no significant excesses over the SM predictions were observed; consequently, upper limits on the lepton-flavor-violating branching ratios were set. The observed (expected) 95% CL upper limits are 0.47% (0.34%) and 0.28% (0.37%) for H to e-tau and H to mu-tau, respectively. These results were published in an ATLAS report [RO1] and in Physics Letters B [RO2]. Subsequently, the ATLAS collaboration has accumulated a total integrated luminosity of 139 fb-1 of pp collision data which is being used for the next iteration of the analysis. We have continued to improve the sensitivity of the analysis, refined the estimations of the fake backgrounds and reevaluated the main systematic uncertainties. Objective 2. Tuning and enhancement of muon identification algorithms in the ATLAS Collaboration. Before the beginning of this project, in collaboration with the ATLAS Muon Combined Performance group, we studied and characterized the performance of the two algorithms used in ATLAS to identify muons using only tracking and calorimeter information. Based on those studies, we were able to modify and improve both algorithms. In this project, we explored the use of multivariate analysis techniques not contained in the ATLAS software; we developed tools to convert files from the format used by the CERN software framework to formats readable by machine learning tools (specifically TensorFlow [ABA15], Keras [CHO15] and PyTorch [PAS17]), to interface the ATLAS data with machine learning techniques that use novel signal extraction methods to improve algorithm performance. We explored the use of boosted decision trees and deep neural networks, as well as refinements in the neural network architectures and activation functions, to take advantage of the different detector sensitivities available in different pseudorapidity and energy regions. Objective 3. Train Hong Kong students and postdocs for research in the forefront of fundamental physics. One postdoctoral research associate, three PhD students (Kevin Kwok, Michael Chu and Minlin Wu), and three undergraduate students (Yik Kwan Chan, Kyle Lau and Siu Yin Fung) have worked on the project. This has allowed them to benefit from the close interaction with colleagues from other ATLAS institutions (located both in Hong Kong and overseas), from learning several of the tools used for research in High Energy Physics, and from working with recent data and Monte Carlo simulation from the Large Hadron Collider, on searches and measurements at the energy frontier. 14307317.label: Major findings and research outcome
14307317.value: A search is performed for the potential decays of the Higgs boson into different-flavor dilepton pairs (eμ, eτ or μτ), using 36.1/fb of proton-proton collision data at √s=13TeV collected in 2015–2016 by the ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider. No excesses over the Standard Model predictions are observed. Lower limits at the 95% confidence level are placed on the cross section times branching ratio of these states. Further studies were carried out using the full run 2 sample to increase the sensitivity of the analysis when a larger dataset becomes available.

14307317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14307317.value: An extended use of machine learning techniques may yield a larger sensitivity, especially in the mass regions where the expected standard model backgrounds are much larger than the potential signals. Also, the use of different classifiers for different backgrounds, later combined into a single test statistic, has yielded promising preliminary results that can be further explored. Regarding the muon identification algorithms, particle information provided by the New Small Wheel, recently installed in the ATLAS detector, should be included into the machine learning systems used to identify muon candidates.

14307317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14307317.value: This research project contributes to our understanding of the fundamental processes of Nature on two fronts: (a) searching for phenomena that is not expected in our current theories, and (b) improve the particle reconstruction tools used to study high-energy particle collisions. These objectives are pursued through the analysis of proton-proton collisions at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) at CERN in Geneva, Switzerland. There, protons travel almost at the speed of light; when they collide, they can transform into any particle allowed by the laws of Nature. Our current description of these laws (the “Standard Model”, or SM) provides very precise predictions for the possible outcomes of these collisions, but we know that the SM is incomplete, so we are making a systematic search for phenomena not contained in it. We aim specifically to (a) search for the possible decay of the Higgs boson, discovered in 2012, into two different kinds of leptons (which are charged elementary matter particles that do not feel the strong nuclear force), and (b) improve the methods used to identify and reconstruct the muons that are produced in high-energy particle collisions at the Large Hadron Collider.
