14308017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14308017.value: Weather and climate extremes can cause tremendous economic and human losses to the society. Some of these extreme events, such as heat waves and heavy rainfall episodes, are becoming more frequent because of human-induced global warming. However, traditionally it has been challenging to establish a linkage between specific weather extremes and climate change, not to say to communicate such information with the general public. The emerging science of event attribution allows one to assess how anthropogenic activities might affect these extremes, based on a scientific and robust methodology. It involves the comparison between a model world with human influence on climate, to a hypothetical one without human effects, and infers the extent to which global warming changes the severity and frequency of extreme weather events. Indeed the extreme rain rates over Hong Kong have been increasing in recent years. Currently it is not clear how man-made climate change and urbanization might affect the characteristics of intense rainfall over the highly urbanized Pearl River Delta (PRD). In this study, we will carry out attribution analyses and evaluate the importance of these anthropogenic influences on extreme precipitation in the region. To provide realistic and fine-definition representation of intense rainfall processes and the urban environment, an atmospheric model at the 1km x 1km resolution will be used to downscale climate change simulations from global models. Results from this project will enhance our scientific understanding of extreme rainfall episodes in this region. Ultimately this will inform adaptation strategies to high-impact weather and will provide invaluable insights for planning future resilience under a warming climate. 極端天氣可帶來巨大的經濟和人為損失。由於全球變暖，其中一些事件如熱浪和強降雨變得越來越頻繁。然而，建立特定極端天氣事件和氣候變化之間的聯繫是一個極具挑戰性的工作。目前我們還不清楚人為氣候變化和城市化會如何影響珠江三角地區強降雨特徵。在本研究中，我們將運用具有精細分辨率的大氣模型來模擬江三角地區極端降水情況，並進行歸因分析以評估它們的重要性。這個項目的結果將增強我們對該地區極端天氣事件的了解，並為全球變暖背景下之未來環境規劃提供參考。

14308017.label: Realisation of objectives
14308017.value: The two objectives of this project have been achieved by applying the pseudo global warming (PGW) approach in the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model. We first successfully setup the WRF model at a cloud-resolving spatial resolution of 2 km x 2 km for the PRD area. Attribution was carried out by reversing the PGW method. This was done by forcing the model with factual as well as “counterfactual” initial and boundary conditions separately. The latter conditions, representing a natural climate with no anthropogenic activities, were inferred from the difference between historical and “historical natural” runs from the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 5 (CMIP5) models. Human influences on PRD rainfall extremes can then be evaluated by comparing the two sets of experiments. We identified 215 extreme events during 1998-2018 affecting Hong Kong as well as the PRD region, with daily rainfall reaching the 95th percentile. Based on WRF’s performance in reproducing these events, eventually we selected 40 episodes (23 cases from May to September (hereafter MJJAS) and 17 in non-MJJAS periods) for attribution analysis. Using the above mentioned method, we quantitatively assessed changes in extreme precipitation frequency and intensity attributable to anthropogenic activities. The seasonal dependence of human impacts on, as well as the thermodynamic versus dynamic contributions to these rainfall changes, were examined. Furthermore, we conducted case studies of two remarkable extreme events from different seasons: the record-breaking wintertime rainstorm in December 2013, as well as the pre-monsoon heavy rainfall case in May 2016. Results show a location-dependent rainfall response to human influences and its main causes have been elaborated.

14308017.label: Major findings and research outcome
14308017.value: The attribution of multiple events indicate that the near-surface temperature over PRD has increased by 0.9-1.1 deg C in MJJAS and 0.6-0.8 deg C in non-MJJAS season. Due to such anthropogenic warming, the intensity of extreme daily rainfall (> 95th percentile) increased by 8%-9.5% (~CC scaling) in MJJAS and 12.4% at most (larger than CC scaling) in non-MJJAS season. Moisture-related thermodynamic effects on rainfall change in the two seasons are similar, while dynamic effects differ according to the season. Changes in MJJAS are related to stronger low-level southerly winds and the dominance of stronger ascents and descents. Larger increments in non-MJJAS rainfall are attributable to the strengthened regional low-level wind convergence. For the record-breaking winter event in 2013, human activities resulted in the 4-day mean rainfall increase according to CC scaling, but increase in 95th and 99th percentile extreme rainfall is much greater than CC prediction. It is noteworthy that human-caused dynamic effects can further exacerbate the thermodynamic-driven rainfall increase. The former is likely related to of enhanced land-sea thermal contrast, favouring anomalous southerly winds under human-related climate warming. However, for the pre-monsoon rainfall in 2016, human-induced thermodynamic anomalies led to over 70% reduction in this pre-monsoon rainfall over eastern PRD and 25%-40% increases in the west for about 0.9 deg C of warming. This is due to changes in relative humidity and convection inhabitation by human activities. Some of the rainfall reductions, however, are mitigated by human-caused dynamic effects induced by anomalous southerly winds.

14308017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14308017.value: 1) Attribution of sub-daily rainfall extremes: This study focused on daily rainfall extremes. Short-duration or sub-daily rainfall extremes are also important as they can cause flash flooding. However, there is limited modelling evidence of variations in sub-daily extremes under a anthropogenic climate. The same PGW method can be used for attribution of sub-daily heavy rainfall-derived floods to various forcing. 2) Attribution of TC-induced rainfall: Observational records have found that the probability and proportion of major TC intensities has increased over the past four decades (Kossin et al., 2020), which cannot be explained by natural variability alone (Bhatia et al., 2019). A high-resolution regional model can be utilized to reduce these uncertainties, and attribution analysis of TC-caused extreme rainfall and the physical mechanisms involved will be examined in the future work.

14308017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14308017.value: This research quantifies human influences on extreme precipitation in PRD using numerical model simulations. We have also investigated the physical mechanisms leading to heavy rainfall variations, such as wind circulation changes and atmospheric moisture abundance, in relation to human activities. Besides, case studies for difference seasons expand our knowledge of how the impacts of human-induced warming on PRD precipitation depends on the season when extreme rainfall occurs. Overall, this work constitutes significant advance in understanding global warming effects on PRD rainfall and ultimately provides invaluable insights in coping with climate risks in the area.

14308217.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14308217.value: 低質量行星附近原行星盤中氣體和塵埃的動力學

14308217.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14308217.value: Dr Gu, Pin-Gao Prof Yen, Chien-Chang

14308217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14308217.value: Circumplanetary disc (CPD) may play a role in the process of planet formation. As a protoplanet as heavy as a few Earth mass orbiting around a young Sun-like star at the Jupiter radius, a cirumplanetary disc may form and deeply embedded in the natal protoplanetary disc, which is assumed to be isothermal and inviscid. As a result, the flow pattern around the protoplanet is fully three-dimensional and nonlinear (Wang+ 2014). The gas inside the Bondi radius is not gravitationally bound to the protoplanet and constantly replenished. Similar flow pattern is also found for sub-Earth mass protoplanets (Ormel+ 2015). The replenishment of planet atmosphere may have the following dynamical and thermal impacts on the protoplanet that will be addressed in the project. First, since the gaseous CPD is no longer gravitationally bound to the protoplanet, any persistent asymmetry of the CPD with respect to the protoplanet may have an impact on the planet migration. Second, dust grains and pebbles are only partially coupled to the gas, it will be very interesting to see how those solid materials evolve and enrich the gaseous envelope. Third, more realistic cooling and heating phenomenon due to the grain growth and pebbles accretion should be properly modeled for the atmosphere. Fourth, we shall seek the conditions under which a protoplanet of a few Earth mass may continue to accrete mass. In this project, global, 3D, non-isothermal numerical simulations will be performed to address these questions for embedded protoplanets.

14500117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14500117.value: 該項目旨在研究漲跌停板制度對股票市場中傳染行為的影響。我們計劃使用深圳股票交易所專有的日內價格和帳戶級別數據，研究漲跌停是否存在傳染現象，並分析潛在的傳染渠道。 我們首先記錄大量股票在同一天接連漲停或跌停的現象。我們假設這些行為是傳染導致的，並設計測試這一假設。我們通過關注傳染作為“超過人們對經濟基本面預期的相關性”（貝卡爾特，哈維，和吳，2005年）來識別這種效應。具體而言，我們檢查後繼達到漲跌停股票的回報是否在隨後的交易日更有可能逆轉。 儘管我們觀察到漲停板和跌停板都存在傳染現象，但我們相信它們各自的傳染機制是不同的。我們提出“注意力溢出效應”解釋漲停板的傳染機制。漲停板股票受到投資者的關注，但10％的限價限制其後續交易。投資者的注意力傳播到相關股票。我們計劃測試這些相關股票是否傾向於也漲到漲停板，並檢查他們隨後的逆轉模式。我們利用帳戶級別的數據進一步檢驗跟隨漲停的投資者是否更有可能蒙受損失。 關於跌停板的傳染，我們建議利用流動性渠道來解釋。如果槓桿投資者不能維持他們保證金賬戶，槓桿投資者將被迫清算其資產。因為流動性交易的影響，清算往往發生在跌停出現的情況。一系列的清算導致跌停板的傳染現象。我們通過檢查投資者交易和帳戶信息來檢驗這個假設。流動性較低的股票或者高槓桿投資者持有的股票更可能會觸及跌停板。 該項目建議將傳染作為漲跌停板規則的一種新的破壞性機制。與現有的關於個人股價變動的文獻相比，我們的項目強調價格限制規則在系統脆弱性和市場不穩定性中的作用。

14500617.label: Major findings and research outcome
14500617.value: We build our empirical setting with three preliminary steps to support the effects of the EAWA ban on hiring foreigners on foreign-worker-dependent institutions. First, we show that TARP institutions complied strictly with the EAWA, because their applications for H-1B visas to sponsor foreign workers dropped to zero throughout the period in which the restriction was in effect. At the same time, companies not receiving government aid did not experience such a drop in H-1B-visa applications, which suggests that the Great Recession in itself can barely explain the drop in foreign hiring by companies subject to the H-1B visa restriction (Figure~ ef{fig:BankH1BFig}). Second, we show that, during the period in which the EAWA was in effect, companies that hired more STEM workers in the period 2004---2006 experienced a 20\% drop in H-1B-visa renewals for STEM workers relative to all foreign workers, suggesting that the EAWA restrictions hit the hiring of specialized STEM workers substantially. Third, after controlling for a set of observable job characteristics, our visa-level analysis suggests that TARP firms were 21.3\% less likely to apply for H1-B visas to sponsor STEM jobs than other jobs both during and after the foreign hiring restrictions. Overall, these results suggest that the EAWA hiring restriction was a material obstacle for firms to hire foreigners, and especially high-skilled STEM workers. We next document that, during the EAWA period, STEM-dependent institutions reduced their patenting activity in terms of both filing patents (extensive margin) and the number of patents filed (intensive margin). The economic magnitude of these effects is sizable: A one-standard-deviation increase in our measure of STEM dependence, which we define in detail below, reduces the probability of patent filling during the EAWA period by 3.6 percentage points, which is about 27.7% of the sample mean. Interestingly, the largest drop in patent filing by STEM-dependent companies arose in the area of financial technology (FinTech). Crucially, we find that once the EAWA ban on hiring foreign workers was lifted, STEM-dependent institutions started to hire foreigners as well as file FinTech patents again.

14500617.value: We presented the paper at the American Finance Association 2021 and the discussant pointed some important issues for us to address. We are going to revise the paper and submit it out to top journals.

14500617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14500617.value: Banning financial institutions from hiring high-skilled foreign nationals reduces their ability to produce cutting-edge FinTech innovation. We document this fact focusing on the Employ American Workers Act (EAWA), which banned financial institutions in the Troubled Asset Relief Program (TARP) from hiring any foreign nationals under an H-1B visa until the full repayment of TARP funding. We exploit the differential timing in which banks were subject to the EAWA, irrespective of when they entered TARP, to document that the ban did not only neutralize foreign hires but also reduced the quantity of FinTech patents filed after controlling for bank-level observables. The drop in patenting in strategic areas such as business methods, cybersecurity and fintech services dropped more for institutions that used to hire a higher share of STEM workers on H-1B visas before the EAWA. After the ban was lift, affected banks started to hire foreign STEM workers and to produce more FinTech innovation.

14500917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14500917.value: Hot money refers to funds that actively seek short-term returns in the international capital market. The Chinese government has imposed strict capital controls on foreign exchange. One of the main purposes of such controls is to deter hot money flows, insulating the Chinese capital market from the volatility of the global financial markets. However, despite the government’s tight regulation, it has been widely reported that overseas speculators can still channel large amounts of hot money into and out of China. The goal of this proposal is to explore the international trade channels to understand the mechanism through which hot money can bypass government regulation. As the flow of hot money is often illicit, an empirical study is difficult, if not impossible. Previous studies have estimated hot money flows by calculating the changes in the country’s balance sheet (e.g., Prasad and Wei, 2007). Instead of studying hot money flows using macroeconomic data, we will adopt a micro approach to the topic by studying the misinvoicing of international trade by foreign-invested firms. We will take advantage of a comprehensive transaction-level dataset from Chinese Customs that covers the universe of import and export transactions occurring between 2000 and 2006. In our sample period, a massive inflow of hot money into China due to the increasing expectation of a RMB appreciation provides an opportunity to study the misinvoicing behavior of multinationals. Expecting the RMB to appreciate in the future, a multinational wanting to move hot money into China could have either over-reported the export price or under-reported the import price when its Chinese subsidiaries traded with its overseas affiliates. Our empirical methodology will focus on two wedges in the data. The first wedge is the price difference between related-party and arm’s-length transactions. We will use this price wedge to measure the size of misinvoicing. The second wedge is the difference between the RMB spot exchange rate and the forward exchange rate. The exchange rate wedge reflects the profitability or motivation of the hot money flow. If the RMB is expected to appreciate, we expect a positive correlation between the exchange rate wedge and the price wedge, even after controlling for the usual suspected correlates, such as the differences in corporate income tax rates, interest rates, and other factors. Based on our transaction-level empirical results, we will further estimate the total aggregate-level hot money inflow, tax gain or loss, and overstated value of trade surplus. 熱錢指的是國際資本市場上積極尋求短期回報的資金。中國政府對外匯一直嚴加管制，其主要目的之一就是防止國際熱錢的進出，以保護國內資本市場不受國際市場波動的影響。雖然政府採取了各種管制措施，媒體卻經常報導大量的國際熱錢仍然可以自由流入或流出中國。本項目就是要研究國際熱錢如何利用國際貿易的渠道規避中國政府的外匯管制。由於這一類的國際熱錢往往非法，這給實證研究帶來了很多困難。文獻中已有的研究主要通過國際收支平衡表的變化來估算國際熱錢的規模。在本項目中我們使用微觀研究方法，而不是過去研究經常使用的宏觀研究方法。我們研究的是外資企業在國際貿易交易時假報貨值的行為。我們的數據來自中國海關交易層面的數據庫，它包括了2000年至2006年中國的所有進出口貿易。恰好在這個時間段，外界普遍預期人民幣將會升值，於是大量國際熱錢通過外資企業的假報貨值流入中國企圖獲利。外資企業在與境外關聯企業交易時，可以通過高報出口貨值或者低報進口貨值的方式，達到將境外資金轉入中國的目的。我們的實證方法主要利用兩個價格差。第一個價格差是外資企業與關聯企業交易和非關聯企業交易的價格差，它可以衡量假報貨值的程度。第二個價格差是人民幣即期匯率和遠期匯率的價格差，這個匯率差表示國際熱錢利用匯率套利的動機。如果預期人民幣升值，那麼交易的價格差應該和匯率差之間存在正向關係。即使我們同時控制了其他的因素如企業所得稅的差異和利率的差異，這種正相關也應該存在。因此，基於以上交易層面的實證研究，我們可以估算宏觀層面的熱錢總規模，以及由此帶來的總稅收變化和虛假國際貿易順差的規模。

14500917.label: Realisation of objectives
14500917.value: The first objective is fully achieved. We first show that multinational firms in China often set different prices for inter-firm and intra-firm transactions. Then our regressions provide evidence that the price wedge is correlated with the expectation of RMB appreciation. Such correlation is also statistically significant. These results are reported in Table 2 to Table 5 in the paper. The second objective is fully achieved. Based on the estimation results in this paper, we did a simple back-of-envelope calculation of the total amount of hot money flow due to the exchange rate motivation of misinvoicing. The results are shown in Figure 4 of the paper. The estimated hot money flow is largest during 2005-2007 and 2011-2013. In 2007 for example, net hot money inflow due to exchange rate motivation is estimated to be USD 16.8 billion. It also implies that China’s total exports were over-stated by the same amount. The third objective is not fully achieved. Although we did not explicitly write down a mathematical model, we verbally discussed the relationship of variables in the paper. First, the correlation between the price wedge and the exchange rate wedge is simple and straightforward in our setting. We feel that writing a complicated model will only add limited value. Second, in the paper we discussed the effect of potential punishment by the government on firms’ misinvoicing decisions. The implication is that we should expect to see more misinvoicing activities in the trade of differentiated goods than homogeneous goods. This is because when the tax authority applies the principle of comparable uncontrolled prices (CUP), for the differentiated goods, it is more difficult to find a benchmark price to catch the misinvoicing activities. Third, it is possible that the multinational firms may even manipulate the prices of arms-length trade if reducing the gap between the related-party and arms-length trade can lower the risk of being caught by the tax authority. This scenario is complicated and is fully modelled in Cristea and Nguyen (2016). We didn't write our own model, but we cited their paper when we discussed the alternative measure of the price wedge.

14500917.label: Major findings and research outcome
14500917.value: China liberalized its current account in 1996, allowing RMB to be convertible for international trade transactions. Yet, its capital account remains tightly regulated. As a result, international funds cannot move into or out of China freely. One of the main purposes of such capital control is to stop the hot money flow and insulate China from the fluctuations of the international financial market. However, this unique institutional setting allows multinational firms to bypass the restriction of capital control by over or under report the prices of their import or export transactions when they trade with overseas affiliates. Thus, the capital control can be ineffective when facing the misinvoicing (or transfer pricing) behavior of the multinationals. In this project, we provide evidence of hot money flow in response to the expectation of the RMB appreciation. We use transaction level data from Chinese customs that covers the universe of all import and export activities in China between 2000 and 2015. To obtain the information of multinational firms’ country of origin, we merge the customs data with a foreign invested firm database of Ministry of Commerce. From our empirical analyses, we find that multinational firms frequently manipulate their export prices when trading with the related-party customers, as compared to arms-length customers. We then calculate the price wedge by taking the difference between these two types of prices. To measure the expectation of the RMB appreciation, we define the exchange rate wedge as the difference between RMB spot rate and forward rate. We also use the forecast RMB exchange rate from over 100 financial institutions in order to check the robustness of the main estimates. Our regression analyses indicate that the price wedge has a positive and statistically significant relationship with the exchange rate wedge. We interpret this result as the evidence that multinational firms over-report their export price in related-party transactions when they expect RMB to appreciate. Moreover, we also find that the multinational firms are more likely to engage in misinvoicing if the export products are differentiated goods. This is because tax authorities impose fines and other punishments on misinvoicing activities. Unlike homogeneous goods that usually have a reference price, the exports of differentiated goods are more difficult for the tax authority to monitor. Based on these regression results, we estimate that between 2000 and 2015, each year about USD 10-20 billion hot money flowed into China out of the exchange rate motivation.

14500917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14500917.value: In current study, we rely on a proxy variable of the related-party transactions. In the future, we can better study the hot money transfer if we can directly observe the related-party transactions in the data. Another follow-up research will be the consequences of the capital control policy when it is weakened by the misinvoicing.

14500917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14500917.value: Chinese government has imposed strict capital control that basically prohibits the cross-border financial transactions. Yet it allows the RMB to be convertible for import and export transactions. This unique institutional setting allows multinational firms to bypass the restriction of the capital control. Despite the capital control, since the early 2000s, there has been a large inflow of international hot money that tried to profit from the RMB appreciation. A common practice of transferring funds is that the multinational firms manipulate their import or export prices when trading with their own overseas affiliates. This project provides micro evidence for the trade misinvoicing (or transfer pricing) using a transaction-level international trade data reported by the Chinese government. We find that even for the same goods, multinational firms often set different prices when trading with the overseas affiliates, as compared to the unrelated customers. Such misinvoicing behavior correlates with the market expectation of RMB appreciation. We also show that misinvoicing is more likely to take place when the products traded are differentiated goods, the firms are wholly foreign owned, and the destination countries are tax havens.

14501317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14501317.value: How do people respond to uncertainty? Suppose you can work on a task for a reward. What do you do if you can receive one of the following rewards upon completion: a certain reward of HK$100, a certain reward of HK$200, or an uncertain reward of either HK$100 or HK$200? Previous literature presents a paradox. Gneezy, List, and Wu (2006) document a strong “uncertainty-aversion” effect, in which the response to an uncertain reward (HK$100 or $200) is even less positive than the response to a certain low reward (HK$100). Meanwhile, we document a strong “uncertainty-loving” effect, in which the response to an uncertain reward (HK$100 or $200) is even more positive than the response to a certain high reward (HK$200; Shen, Fishbach, and Hsee 2015). Both effects are striking, but the paradox between the two is even more so. How can two opposite anomalies exist at the same time? In this research, we suggest that they actually do not happen at the same time. Strong uncertainty-aversion occurs before one engages in the activity, or “in-prospect,” while strong uncertainty-loving occurs when one engages in the activity, or “in-process.” Thus, the mode in which decisions are made, in-prospect versus in-process, moderates the effect of this incentive uncertainty. We examine both strong uncertainty-aversion and strong uncertainty-loving effects on the same magnitude and in the same decision task and demonstrate the crucial role of the decision mode on uncertainty incentives in both the lab and the field. Moreover, we propose a continuity hypothesis that explains this intriguing reversal: a single in-process decision differs from a series of isolated in-prospect decisions because the latter group lacks continuity, and continuous engagement in an activity over time brings out extra “process” utility. This hypothesis is expected to be a simple but parsimonious explanation for the preference reversals about risk on other fundamental issues, such as value and time. Theoretically, our research is the first to exam both extreme uncertainty-loving and extreme uncertainty-aversion together on the same magnitude. Our newly proposed theory, the continuity hypothesis, is expected to be a simple and parsimonious explanation for many decision making anomalies. Practically, our research offers insight for policymakers, marketers, and other regulators on how to utilize uncertainty when designing incentives. 決策連續性假說：再論結果不確定性的激勵效應 在不同決策階段，人面對不確定結果的反應大相徑庭。即使在同一個決策情境中、面對同一個不確定可能性，決策者既有可能表現出極端化風險規避(Gneezy, List, and Wu 2006)，也有可能表現出極端化風險喜好(Shen, Fishbach, and Hsee 2015)。本研究就此駁論展開深入探索，提出決策連續性在不同決策模式中的重要性，致力於精確預測人的風險反應式。具體來說，本研究提出人在事先期待、未進入狀態階段易風險規避，但在實際體驗、進入狀態階段易風險喜好。比如說，在選擇簽訂勞動合同階段（事先期待、未進入狀態），人不喜歡帶有不確定性的激勵機制。然而，當人 履行勞動合約、真正工作階段（實際體驗、進入狀態），人其實很享受不確定性，會為止更加賣力工作。本研究旨在：其一，統一文獻上看似相互矛盾的決策現象，並實證這些現象實質上相輔相成，歸於同一理論基礎（決策連續性假說）；其二，探索具體生活場景中這一新理論的操作性；其三，解釋該決策理論的背後邏輯和文獻基礎；最後，構建系統性知識框架，為未來的進一步探索搭造平台。

14501317.label: Realisation of objectives
14501317.value: All research objectives have been successfully and fully achieved. We wish to note that this project is well recognized internationally, and the PI has been invited to present this project at over a dozen of top schools in the world and the most prestigious international conferences in the academic field. At the same time, much of the project developments was inspired by audience at different stages of this project. Especially, audience at Stanford GSB's marketing seminar and reviewers at Management Science were particularly helpful on shaping our thoughts on Objectives 3 and 4. Although the manuscript was rejected later in the advanced round where the review team experienced a personnel change, unfortunately, the editor reinforced the significance of our project and encouraged us to continue the pursue. We are determined to make a bigger impact after the pandemic. Related to Objective 1, we developed a related paper, "As A Wage Increases, Do People Work More or Less?", where we explore how people respond to wage changes that are transitory (application period uncertain; e.g., a price surge that may be gone at any point) and permanent (application period certain). This paper finds that how the wage change is communicated affects work supply decisions. If the wage change is personalized (e.g., from now on, you can work the same 20 hours to make $900 instead of $600), workers don't show a difference in work supply between transitory and permanent wage changes. But when the wage frame is its default formate (e.g., $20 per hour), workers showed a preference of seizing the opportunity to make money at the price of their leisure. This paper is under advanced review at Management Science.

14501317.label: Major findings and research outcome
14501317.value: Judgment and decision-making research has documented a wide spectrum of risk preferences, ranging from extreme risk aversion to extreme risk seeking. How can people display both risk aversion and risk seeking? The present research offers an answer to this puzzle. To do so, it distinguishes between two types of decisions: decisions in prospect (those made at one time point prior to a task) and decisions in process (those made continuously throughout the task). Three incentive-compatible experiments (total N = 2,891) find that the opposite risk preferences do exist but, crucially, not in the same circumstances: people display risk aversion in prospect and risk seeking in process. For example, when workers were asked to decide in prospect whether to work for a specific payment scheme, fewer chose to work for an uncertain payment than for a certain payment, and the workers promised the uncertain payment expected that they would quit earlier. Once engaged in the task and hence in process, however, workers worked longer for the uncertain payment even when it was strictly financially worse than the certain payment. In other words, uncertain incentives are not attractive in prospect but are motivating in process. This research aims to make three contributions: (a) to identify an important distinction—in prospect versus in process—for the decision-making literature; (b) to use this distinction to reconcile the two opposing risk preferences, risk aversion and risk seeking; and (c) to reveal the hidden value of uncertain incentives for managerial decision making.

14501317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14501317.value: With the support of the RGC grant, we have finished all the empirical and conceptual work. It was based on the Management Science's feedback that we combined two papers into one manuscript. Although that manuscript as demanded did not survive the review process, we learned a lot from the reviewers' comments. Benefiting from this rejection, now it is possible for us to form two research manuscripts that potentially turn into two journal publications and optimize the impact of this RGC-funded research project. Thought the research progress was greatly slowed down by the pandemic, we strive to publish the newly shaped manuscripts at the earliest possible. While working on the this project, the PI developed a related paper with Prof. Samual Hirshman at the Norwegian School of Economics, "As A Wage Increases, Do People Work More or Less?", which is currently under advanced review at Management Science. This project also seeded new exciting collaborations between the PI and researchers at Stanford University (Prof. Erika Plambeck), UC San Diego (Profs On Amir and Danqi Luo), UC Berkeley (Prof. Przemyslaw Jeziorski), and Norwegian School of Economics (Prof. Samuel Hirshman) on various research topics related to this project.

14502117.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14502117.value: 用情景思考理论来预测选择的情景依赖性: 基于不同方法的实证研究

14502117.label: Project Objectives
14502117.value: First, we investigate the necessary and sufficient conditions underlying the emergence of the compromise effect. Second, we develop and estimate a structural econometric model to estimate the effect size of contextual deliberation as a general mechanism for context dependent choices.
rows: First, we investigate the necessary and sufficient conditions underlying the emergence of the compromise effect.
Second, we develop and estimate a structural econometric model to estimate the effect size of contextual deliberation as a general mechanism for context dependent choices.

14502117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14502117.value: Classical economic theories assume that choices are rational and independent of other options in the choice set. However, numerous studies demonstrate that choices between two options may be systematically influenced by the presence or value of other options. One well-known example of context-dependent choices is the compromise effect, i.e., an option can become relatively more attractive when it is an intermediate option in a choice set. Such abnormal phenomena have typically been interpreted as evidence of irrational decision making. However, our previous research suggests that theory of contextual deliberation can reconcile rationality with context dependence. We address two sets of research issues in this proposed project. First, we will identify the complete chain of factors that, as predicted by the theory of contextual deliberation, collectively determine whether or not the compromise effect would emerge. That is, we will examine the necessary and sufficient conditions that would turn on and off the compromise effect in an arbitrary scenario. We plan to run laboratory experiments to test some predictions that relate to the role of these conditions. In particular, in this proposed project we will examine whether the compromise effect can be moderated by cognitive load, presentation order, and temporal separation of choice tasks. More importantly, we will evaluate whether subjects’ prior belief on attribute importance can help us predict whether and when the compromise effect would arise. In addition, we will employ neural experiments to test whether brain activities can help predict the emergence of the compromise effect. With the increasing sophistication of neurophysiological technologies, we will be able to record the timing, location, and intensity of brain activities before, during and after the decision making process. These additional data represent more precise measures of deliberation, which can be used, as complement to the behavioral experiments, to examine the robustness of the proposition that contextual deliberation drives the compromise effect. Second, we plan to develop and estimate a structural econometric model to explicitly incorporate deliberation in context-dependent choices. The proposed econometric model will recover the process of how the deliberation decision can be optimally made to improve the subsequent decision of which alternative to choose. Estimating this model will allow us to answer some important questions that cannot be addressed by controlled experiments. For example, what is the cost of deliberation? What is the effect size of deliberation in influencing context-dependent choices? How do context-dependent choices respond to changes in the decision makers' utility information? 传统经济学理论假设选择行为是理性的，不随选择情景而变化。但是，大量的研究表明，选择行为可能会受到其它选项的影响。受情景影响的选择行为（context-dependent choice）的一个著名的例子是折中效应：中间选项可能会比其它选项更有吸引力。这个现象通常被解读为非理性决策。然而，我们之前的研究提出了一个新的情景思考理论（theory of contextual deliberation），可以解释选择的理性和情景依赖性之间的有机统一。 在本计划中我们主要研究两组问题。第一，基于情景思考理论的预测，我们致力于找到折中效应是否会出现的决定因素。也就是说，我们将研究折中效应在一般情况下会出现或者不出现的充分和必要条件。我们将用行为实验来检测与这些条件所起的作用相关的预测。具体而言，我们将研究折中效应的强弱是否会受到认知超负荷，呈现顺序以及选择任务的隔离等因素的影响。更重要的，我们将评估实验参与者关于选项属性的相对重要性的认知是否能预测折中效应的出现。 另外，我们将用神经实验的方法来检测是否大脑的活动能帮助我们预测折中效应的出现。随着神经生理学技术的日益发展，我们可以记录大脑活动在决策之前，之中以及之后的时间，位置以及强度。这些额外的数据能对思考（deliberation）的强度进行更精确的测量，可以用来作为行为实验的补充，进一步检测情景思考是否折中效应出现的内在驱动机制。 第二，我们计划提出一个结构性经济计量模型，并对该模型的参数进行实证估计，以研究情景思考在选择的情景依赖性中所起的作用。该经济计量模型将具体的考虑思考本身的决策过程是如何做出的，以及思考怎么样能帮助改进选择的质量。对该模型的参数进行实证估计将帮助我们回答一些行为实验无法回答的问题。比如，思考的成本是什么？思考对于选择的情景依赖性的影响到底是多大？依赖情景的选择具体怎么样随着决策者的效用信息而变化？

14502117.label: Realisation of objectives
14502117.value: First, to “investigate the necessary and sufficient conditions underlying the emergence of the compromise effect,” we have identified a potential cause in standard experiments that may confound the emergence or absence of the compromise effect. We hypothesize that the presentation order of the options in a commonly-conducted experimental setting may influence the relative choice of the options, which is termed as the “contextual order effect” or the “presentation order effect”. We also formally develop a mathematical model of sequential search with costly recall to endogenize order-dependent choices. As a result, the compromise effect may be either strengthen or diluted by the presentation order effect. To examine the hypothesis, we have run two large experiments to test the extent to which the order effects are context dependent and the extent to which they may moderate the magnitude of the compromise effect. We have finished the theoretical development and the empirical analysis on the presentation-order effect. We report the results in the working paper titled “When Presentation Order Affects Choice.” Regarding the second objective on “develop and estimate a structural econometric model to estimate the effect size of contextual deliberation as a general mechanism for context dependent choices,” we had some change in our original plan and expectation. Basically, as we investigated our first research objective, we shifted our main theoretical focus from contextual deliberation to sequential search with costly recall, in driving context-dependent choices (in general) and the compromise effect (in particular). This shift is based on the results of the experiments we run and also on the comments and feedback we received from other colleagues. Therefore, instead of developing and estimating a structural econometric model of contextual deliberation, we decided to run controlled experiments to test the role of costly recall in sequential search. Essentially, we divided our plan to test experimentally how our newly developed theory can account for the compromise effect. The first part is to assess the extent to which the presentation order can moderate the compromise effect, and the second part is to examine the underlying process for the presentation-order effect by manipulating the search and the recall costs of the decision-making process. We have made substantial progress on the first part, as mentioned above for the first research objective. The second part is work in progress, which will be followed up as we publish the paper based on the first-part research.

14502117.label: Major findings and research outcome
14502117.value: We conducted two controlled experiments to examine the emergence and the nature of order-dependent choices, in standard settings of compromise effect. The first is a Mturk study in each of twenty categories of commonly seen products or services, and the second is a lab experiment of incentive-based choices between simple lotteries. For each choice set (of two or three options), we considered all possible sequences to order the options. The experiments yield findings that are consistent with context-dependent order effects. First, the impacts of positions can vary qualitatively across alternatives. Second, the relative advantage of positions varied substantially across the binary and the trinary choice sets. When an additional option was added to the choice set, the advantageous position changed from the first to the middle one for the Mturk participants, and the strong disadvantage of the prominent position became evidently much weaker and often nonsignificant in the lottery experiment. Third, we observe substantial heterogeneity in the sign and the significance of the order effects along other dimensions (e.g., categories, probabilities/stakes). We find the compromise effect was evidently stronger in the Mturk experiment than in the lottery experiment. Moreover, importantly, we obtain some evidence that the relative strengthen of the compromise effect can be explained by the presentation order. In particular, in the Murk experiment where we observe the compromise effect, we also document a strong middle-position effect. In comparison, in the lottery experiment in which the compromise effect was often weak or nonsignificant, we do not observe a stronger tendency to choose the option in the middle position either. We develop an ordered-search model to account for the contextual order effects. We consider the problem of choosing among alternatives that are searched sequentially and revisited with a recall cost. We show that a higher recall cost can yield two countervailing effects on the likelihood to favor earlier versus latter options. We present conditions under which the interaction of the search and the recall effects may endogenously generate different types of position-dependent choice. First, the prominent position need not always boost choice probability and either the middle or the last position can be beneficial. Second, the number of options in the choice set may qualitatively influence the relative advantage of positions. That is, a position can be beneficial in the choice between two alternatives but become disadvantageous for a trinary choice set, and vice versa. Third, the influence of presentation order in trinary choice sets is generally complicated and context dependent.

14502117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14502117.value: There are several directions to further develop the research. The most related one is to formally tease out the presentation order and the compromise effects. What proportion of the choice behavior can be explained by each factor? Can the compromise effect be still significant after we move the middle-position effect in the Mturk study, and can we recover the compromise effect after we remove the diluting effect of the preference for the non-middle position in the lottery experiment? Another direction would be to formally test the role of the search and the recall costs in driving the presentation order effect. We will conduct controlled experiments to manipulate the subjects’ cost of sampling an additional option and/or the cost of revisiting a previously sampled option. This would allow us to test our theory as an explanation for the presentation order effect and the compromise effect. It would be interesting to study implications of costly recall for the supply side and for market equilibrium. We can extend our model to consider price competition between firms. Alternatively, one can consider other types of search, either random or ordered. Another direction is to consider endogenous search order when recall is costly.

14502117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14502117.value: It has been observed that people may exhibit the so-called compromise effect. They appear to prefer the option with intermediate attribute values (e.g., price, quality). Nevertheless, in previous studies the options’ physical order (on a computer screen) typically coincides with their attribute order, i.e., the option with intermediate attributes is positioned in the middle of the other two options. Therefore, the compromise effect need not be driven by a preference for the middle attributes, but by a tendency to choose the option in the middle option. Conversely, the compromise effect may be absent when people prefer not to choose the middle-positioned option. Our research seeks to test whether the emergence or absence of the compromise effect can be explained by the presentation order effect. We run two large experiments and find evidence for our hypothesis. That is, the compromise effect can be strengthened or diluted, depending on whether people tend to prefer the middle potion. In addition, we develop a formal theoretical model of sequential search with costly recall to explain why and when people may be more likely to prefer a given position. That is, the (forward or backward) consideration of an options involve a sampling or cognition cost. This theory can also be used to explicate other context-dependent choice.

14502217.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14502217.value: 滬港通內地投資者對市場的影響

14502217.label: Project Objectives
14502217.value: To examine whether Mainland Chinese Investors contribute information or noises under Shanghai-Hong Kong Stock Connect
rows: To examine whether Mainland Chinese Investors contribute information or noises under Shanghai-Hong Kong Stock Connect

14502217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14502217.value: The launch of Shanghai-Hong Kong Stock Connect in 2014 represents an important milestone in the development of China’s capital market. Through Shanghai-Hong Kong Stock Connect, investors in Hong Kong can buy shares from the Shanghai stock market and vice versa for investors in Shanghai, based on an approved list of stocks and are subject to an aggregate capital quota on a daily and annual basis. In the proposed study, we will examine the effect of the participation of southbound investors (i.e. investors from Shanghai who trade in the Hong Kong stock market) on the market efficiency. It is widely suspected that after Stock Connect was implemented, that there was a surge of volatility in the Hong Kong stock market. This has been attributed to the idea that Mainland Chinese retail investors are speculative traders. We therefore examine whether the southbound trades contain any information or simply cause noises. First, we will compare the volatility of Hong Kong stocks before and after the implementation of Stock Connect, and investigate whether there was a surge of volatility in the stocks eligible under Stock Connect. Second, to examine whether these stocks exhibited more price reversals, we will check whether their variance ratios increase after Stock Connect. Third, we will infer the information content of southbound trades from their stock return predictability. And fourth, we will examine the bivariate relationship between the net purchase of southbound investors and the A-H share premium to see whether southbound trading reduced A-H price differentials. To our best knowledge, this project will be the first to conduct a comprehensive analysis of the effect of the Shanghai-Hong Kong Stock Connect program. The results of this project will be relevant for understanding the effect of further liberalization of China’s capital market. 2014年啓動的滬港通是中國資本市場發展的重要里程碑，透過滬港通，香港投資者可以買賣上海證券交易所上市的合資格公司股票；同時，上海投資者亦可以買賣香港聯合交易所上市的合資格公司股票，惟雙方均實行累積總額度及每日額度管理。本項目將研究南向交易投資者（即於香港股票市場投資的上海投資者）的參與對市場效率的影響。由於中國大陸零售投資者一般被認為是投機交易者，因此投資者廣泛認為在實行滬港通後，香港股市的波動性將會激增。我們將研究南向交易有否包含任何信息或只是市場噪音。首先，我們會比較滬港通實施前後香港股市的波動性，再檢視合資格公司股票價格波動性有否遽增。第二，我們將檢視實施滬港通後股價的變異數比率(Variance ratio) 有否增加，以確定這些股票是否出現更多的價格反轉（price reversal)。第三，我們將從股票回報的可預測性(predictability)推斷南向交易的信息內容。第四，我們將研究南向投資者的淨購買與A-H股溢價之間的雙向關係，從而得知南向交易有否減低A-H股的價格差異。據我們所知，本項目將是首個以滬港通對市場影響作全面分析的研究，結果將有助於了解進一步開放中國資本市場的影響。

14502217.label: Realisation of objectives
14502217.value: The objective of the project has been realized. The major objective of the project is to examine whether Mainland investors contribute information or noises under Shanghai-Hong Kong Stock Connect. Our results show that both northbound trades and southbound trades significantly and positively predict returns of connected Shanghai and Hong Kong stocks, respectively, suggesting that cross-border flows are informed. Northbound aggregate net purchase can predict returns of Shanghai stocks on both daily and weekly basis, while lagged values of southbound aggregate net purchase can predict returns of Hong Kong stocks on daily basis only. Therefore, Mainland investors contribute information, through southbound trades, although this only appears at daily intervals. In contrast, Hong Kong/international investors contribute information, through northbound trades, at both daily and weekly intervals. In addition, we find that the launch of Stock Connect has an asymmetric effect on the volatility-volume relationship for connected stocks. While there is a positive relationship between lagged southbound volume and absolute returns of connected stocks in Hong Kong, there is a negative relationship between lagged northbound volume and absolute returns of connected stocks in Shanghai. This suggests that Mainland investors will also contribute volatility (positively), via southbound volume, to the Hong Kong stock market. On the other hand, Hong Kong/international investors will help to reduce volatility, via northbound volume, in the Shangahi stock market.

14502217.label: Major findings and research outcome
14502217.value: This paper examines the effects of bi-directional cross-border equity flows on stock returns, volatility and valuation differential using the unique Stock Connect program in China as a natural experiment. Via Stock Connect, investors from Hong Kong (mainland China) can trade qualified stocks listed in Shanghai (Hong Kong). We find that southbound (northbound) investors net purchases predict returns of Hong Kong (Shanghai) stocks. However, southbound and northbound trades exhibit asymmetry in volatility-volume relationship; there is a positive (negative) relationship between lagged southbound (northbound) volume and volatility of connected stocks in Hong Kong (Shanghai). Southbound investors net purchase is positively related to lagged AH share price premium for dual-listed stocks and such trades reduces future valuation differential. Our study shows that stock market integration facilitates information sharing and narrow valuation differential across previously segmented markets. But the effects of stock market integration depend importantly on local market environments such as investor clienteles.

14502217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14502217.value: The project has been focused on the period around the introduction of Stock Connect in 2014. Further studies can look at the relationship in more recent years.

14502217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14502217.value: The Stock Connect program is introduced in 2014 in linking up Shanghai and Hong Kong stock market. It should be noted that the investor clienteles in the Hong Kong and Shanghai stock market are quite different. While Hong Kong is characterized by the presence of institutional investors who are more sophisticated and trade on fundamentals, the Mainland stock market is dominated by retail investors who are less sophisticated and trade mostly on speculation. However, due to the sheer size of Mainland investors, they can exert an important influence on the Hong Kong stock market. Indeed, our results show that both northbound trades and southbound trades can positively predict returns of connected Shanghai and Hong Kong stocks, respectively, suggesting that the cross-border flows contain information. However, the information content in northbound trades is higher than in southbound trades. We find that the launch of Stock Connect has an asymmetric effect on the volatility-volume relationship for connected stocks. While there is a positive relationship between volatility and volume of connected stocks in Hong Kong, there is a negative relationship in the case of connected stocks in Shanghai. Therefore, the trades of retail investors from Mainland China and trades of institutional investors from Hong Kong create different volatility-volume relationship.

14502517.value: 他人對消費者情感體驗的影響

14502517.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14502517.value: Prof Sengupta, Jaideep Prof Wan, Echo Wen

14502517.label: Project Objectives
14502517.value: To investigate whether knowing others are having an enjoyable experience will increase or decrease consumers’ own reactions to that experience. To investigate whether consumers might evaluate an ad differently when they watch it in public versus in private and whether culture might moderate the above effect. To investigate whether consumers will be more influenced by others' attitude toward a brand if they communicate with others about their view of the brand than if not.
rows: To investigate whether knowing others are having an enjoyable experience will increase or decrease consumers’ own reactions to that experience.
To investigate whether consumers might evaluate an ad differently when they watch it in public versus in private and whether culture might moderate the above effect.
To investigate whether consumers will be more influenced by others' attitude toward a brand if they communicate with others about their view of the brand than if not.

14502517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14502517.value: Consumers often experience positive or negative feelings when they consume products or watch advertisements. This research examines whether and why consumers’ emotional reactions might be influenced by other people. For example, suppose a consumer sees a post on Facebook showing others currently having an enjoyable experience such as eating ice cream. Will this consumer react to the same experience more or less favorably than if he or she does not see this message? As another example, suppose a consumer uses a smartphone in public areas such as on the train or airplane to watch an emotional ad. Will that consumer, particularly an Asian consumer, react to the ad differently than if he or she had watched it at home? Our research aims to investigate these issues in order to provide insight into the broader question of how social influence affects emotion-laden experiences. First, following up from the initial example above, we will investigate whether simply knowing that others are enjoying an experience influences consumers’ projected reactions to that experience. Two opposing possibilities exist. On the one hand, consumers might imagine how others will feel about the experience and might mentally simulate such positive emotions in their own minds, leading them to react to the experience more favorably than they otherwise would. On the other hand, knowing that others are enjoying an experience might make consumers feel envious of those others, especially if they want to have the same experience but cannot. The first half of our investigation seeks to delineate and test a contingency based theoretical framework to identify conditions under which of these opposing effects will obtain. Second, we will investigate whether consumers might evaluate an emotional ad differently if they watch it in public versus in private. We posit that if an ad elicits strong emotions such as excitement or sadness, Asian consumers, who are socialized to inhibit emotional reactions, will want to avoid expressing such emotions in pubic. Because inhibiting emotional expression is often cognitively effortful, consumers might feel uncomfortable when they watch such an ad. Consequently, they will evaluate the ad less favorably than if they watch it in private. Our research will examine these possibilities and also identify theoretically-derived boundary conditions.

14502517.label: Realisation of objectives
14502517.value: Project: “The Effect of Sharing an Experience on Consumers’ Reaction toward It” Two projects examined objective 1. In the first project, we found that consumers tend to find an experience more enjoyable if they share it with their friends than if not. In study 1, we found that when participants watched the same video as the person sitting next to them (i.e., their neighbor), they found the video more interesting if they had (vs. did not have) a close relationship with that person. However, if they watched a different video from the one their neighbor watched, they found the video less interesting if they had (vs. did not have) a close relationship with their neighbor. In study 2, we found that when participants and their neighbor watched the same video sequentially, the participants who watched the video first tended to find it more enjoyable than those who watched it second. We believe that those who watched the video first might have had a more intense reaction to the video because they simulated the feelings their neighbor would experience when watching the video. In study 3, we asked participants to watch a funny video and then either shared the link to the video with another person we paired with them or not. We found that participants evaluated the video more favorably if they shared the video with another partner than if not. This effect was mediated by the extent of their imagination about the reaction of their partner. In study 4, we replicated the findings of Study 3 and showed that the effect was mitigated when participants were told that they would share the video to their partner later. We are writing up this paper to be submitted to a journal. In the second project, we examined whether sharing product usage experience associated with females may lead males to change their decision making. In particular, we predict that sharing an incidental product usage experience can produce an assimilative effect, whereby the user takes the perspective of the dissociative group, and changes their self-evaluations and behaviors to be more in line with those of the dissociative group. These ideas are tested in the specific context of men using pink products that are typically associated with women. Across a set of studies, we find support for the basic proposition that incidental usage of pink products causes men to think of themselves as being more feminine, and also aligns their behaviour with that of women in the domain of financial decision-making. This paper is under review at Journal of Consumer Research. Projects: “The Face is the Index of the Mind: Predicting Individuals’ Self-Construal from Their Facial Expressions” Two projects examined objective 2. In the proposal, we suggest that Asian consumers may react to an ad more negatively if it elicits extreme emotion than if not, and this effect is more evident when they watch it in a public (vs. private) context. This is because Asian consumers, who typically have interdependent self-construal, may avoid expressing extreme emotions in public. To test this assumption, we conducted several studies showing that participants are less likely to make an extreme facial expression if they have an interdependent self-construal than an independent self-construal. Six studies examined our assumptions. Studies 1-3 examined a bidirectional causal relationship between individuals’ self-construals and the extremity of their emotional expressions. Study 1 provided evidence that priming participants with different types of self-construal can influence the extremity of their emotional expressions. A second study (Studies 2A and 2B) found that inducing people to manifest an extreme facial expression activated an independent social orientation and influenced their performance on tasks that reflect this orientation. Study 3 examined marketing implications of these findings. Studies 4 and 5 investigated whether people’s facial expressions are an indicator of their chronic social orientation. Study 4 showed that the facial expressions of students who were told to smile for a group photograph predicted both their self-construal and judgments that were presumably influenced by this construal. Study 5 showed that social orientation can only be inferred from emotional expression that people make in a public context but not in a private context. In these studies, the effects of individuals’ facial expression were reflected not only in measures of their social orientation but also in judgments and behavioral decisions that this orientation is likely to influence. This paper was accepted by European Journal of Marketing. In addition to this project, we also worked on another project that is relevant to the relationship with facial expression and mood repair. Engaging in an enjoyable activity is often effective in reducing or eliminating a negative mood. However, imagining this activity before deciding whether to perform it can decrease unhappy people’s willingness to engage in it. The facial expression that accompanies a negative mood (and the muscles activated by the expression) can conflict with the expression that is elicited by imagining the performance of an enjoyable activity, evoking subjective feelings of difficulty of imagining it. Unhappy people misattribute these feelings of difficulty to the enjoyable activity itself, decreasing their desire to engage in the activity. We conducted seven studies to examine those assumptions. This paper was published in Journal of Personality and Social Psychology. Project: “Just Talk About It: How Can Communication Enhance Social Influence on Brand Attitude?” One project examined objective 3. We examined whether simply communicating to others about one’s view of a brand can make one more susceptible to others’ preexisting attitudes toward that brand. We posited that consumers might have a goal of receiving positive feedback from their audience during social communication. Consequently, they might generate messages that fit with the audience’s preexisting attitude toward a brand when sharing their own view of the brand with that audience. Consumers’ own attitude toward the brand may thus be influenced by the messages they generate without their awareness of it. Five experiments examined these possibilities. Experiment 1 tested the basic effect of how the communication of brand influenced consumers’ own attitude toward the brand to be consistent with that of their audience. Experiment 2 tested the robustness of the effect found in Experiment 1 using a scenario that is more similar to real life situation. Experiment 3 investigated the marketing implications of our effect to show whether marketers can influence consumers by making consumer talk to them. Experiment 4 and 5 distinguished between the conscious and unconscious processes that drove our effect. This paper was under the 2nd round review at Journal of Experimental Psychology: Applied.

To investigate whether consumers might evaluate an ad differently when they watch it in public versus in private and whether culture might moderate the above effect.

14502517.label: Major findings and research outcome
14502517.value: The first project found that consumers tend to find an experience more enjoyable if they share it with their friends than if not. This effect occurred because they tend to simulate the experience in their mind when they share it with their friends. We observed that the effect was stronger when consumers had the experience before than after their friends and was stronger when consumers already shared the experience than when they are told that they would share the experience later. The second project found evidence for the basic effect, showing that men’s sharing experience associated with females such as using a pink product induced them to not only subsequently rate themselves as being more feminine, but also heightened their financial risk-aversion. We also showed that a salient threat to males’ gender identity militated against their willingness to take the perspective of females, and attenuated the effect of incidental usage on males’ risk-taking tendency. The third project suggests that self-construal may affect consumers' reaction toward extreme emotions and that this effect was more evident in a public context than in a private context. The studies provide support for a bidirectional causal relationship between individuals’ self construals and the extremity of their emotional expressions. They show that people’s general social orientation could predict the spontaneous facial expressions that they manifest in their daily lives. The forth project suggests that the facial expression that accompanies a negative mood (and the muscles activated by the expression) can conflict with the expression that is elicited by imagining the performance of an enjoyable activity, evoking subjective feelings of difficulty of imagining it. Unhappy people misattribute these feelings of difficulty to the enjoyable activity itself, decreasing their desire to engage in the activity. Seven studies demonstrated the role of these metacognitive experiences and their implications for research on affect regulation. The fifth project shows that because consumers have a goal of receiving positive feedback from the audience during communication, they might generate messages that fit with the audience’s preexisting attitude toward a brand when sharing their own view of the brand with the audience. As a result, consumers’ own attitude toward the brand may be influenced by the messages they generate. However, we also suggest that although this effect can occur when consumers generate messages either consciously or unconsciously, these two processes might have different consequences for consumer’s attitude persistence.

14502517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14502517.value: We will continue to work on the first and the fifth projects to complete them. Future research can be done to examine the following issues: (1) show more evidence for the role of mental simulation on the enjoyment of an experience; (2) show more evidence for the effect of culture rather than self-construal may affect consumers' reaction toward extreme emotions; (3) show more evidence for the unconscious process that underlies the effect of communication on consumers' own attitude toward a brand.

14502517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14502517.value: The first project suggests that consumers should share their experiences with their friends so that they might feel more enjoyable about their experiences. The second project suggests that sharing an experience associated with females may influence males' self identity and their decision making. The third and forth projects suggest that consumers' cognitive thoughts or feelings may be correlated with their facial expressions. For example, consumers with interdependent self-construal may respond to extreme emotions more negatively than those with independent self-construal. Consumers who feel sad may induce frown-like expressions that may affect their mood-repair motivation. The fifth project examines how consumers will be more influenced by others' attitude toward a brand if they communicate with others about their view of the brand than if not. We found that consumers might be more adapted to others' attitude during communication and may adjust their attitude toward the brand.

14503117.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14503117.value: 從投資刺激到增長疲軟

14503117.label: Project Objectives
14503117.value: Develop the concept of growth fatigue and use China as an example to illustrate the importance of the concept. Develop a new framework that is general enough to accommodate a rich variety of cross-sectional and time-series relationship between investment and growth. Establish conditions under which investment stimulation may lead to growth fatigue. Estimate the model to back out the magnitude and persistence of policy shocks that promote investment but distort resource allocation. Evaluate quantitatively the welfare consequences of the stimulus policies.

Develop a new framework that is general enough to accommodate a rich variety of cross-sectional and time-series relationship between investment and growth. Establish conditions under which investment stimulation may lead to growth fatigue.
Estimate the model to back out the magnitude and persistence of policy shocks that promote investment but distort resource allocation.
Evaluate quantitatively the welfare consequences of the stimulus policies.

14503117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14503117.value: We aim to understand the mechanism under which investment stimulation may end up with “growth fatigue”, a phenomenon that is referred to as the co-existence of high investment and weak growth. We first document a set of stylized facts from China, where growth fatigue has been present since the so-called four trillion Yuan stimulus package in 2008-10. Perhaps the most striking finding is the vanishing of the positive cross-sectional and time-series correlation between investment and growth, one of the most robust empirical regularities in economics. The standard growth accounting will simply attribute growth fatigue to low aggregate TFP growth, without explaining why. We will develop a new quantitative framework by investigating persistent policy distortions and their effects on aggregate TFP growth. Based on a much simplified version of the framework, we have established necessary conditions for investment stimulation to cause growth fatigue. Roughly speaking, policy shocks that aim to boost investment will have to be sufficiently (i) distortionary; (ii) big or persistent. These conditions seem to fit well the narratives and facts about China’s stimulus policies in 2008-10. Moreover, we have also found some preliminary empirical evidence supporting the mechanism in our model. We will use the model to identify and estimate the magnitude and persistence of China’s stimulus policies and, then, to evaluate their welfare consequence. The focus will be on the trade-off between gains from short-term growth and losses from long-term stagnation. 本項研究旨在理解投資激勵政策可能導致增長疲軟的內在機制。我們首先報告一組來自中國在2009年之後的特徵事實，說明這種增長疲軟的現象的確在現實中存在。最重要的發現是原本非常穩健的投資和增長之間的正相關性正在中國逐漸消失。我們將發展一個全新的數量分析框架來分析這一現象。

14503117.label: Realisation of objectives
14503117.value: Objective 1: Develop the concept of growth fatigue and use China as an example to illustrate the importance of the concept. The recent fast-growing literature on misallocation has shown that distortions can significantly reduce the level of output. However, the main challenge is to show how distortion can affect economic growth, which is the goal of this project. After four years’ work, we have now developed “growth fatigue” to a more specific concept of R&D misallocation, which we believe is at the root of cross-country long-run growth differences. The concept of R&D misallocation is formally analyzed in the paper “From Imitation to Innovation: Where Is All that Chinese R&D Going?”, which is now under R&R at Econometrica (a very positive decision letter is attached). We use China as an example as planned, where R&D investment increased dramatically but economic growth (especially aggregate productivity growth) has been slowing down. We construct a dynamic equilibrium model of endogenous technical change where firms’ investments are distorted. Using a model estimated by the Chinese firm data, we show that R&D misallocation can cause “growth fatigue”, i.e., substantial decline in long-run growth rate. Objective 2: Develop a new framework that is general enough to accommodate a rich variety of cross-sectional and time-series relationship between investment and growth. We construct a dynamic equilibrium model of endogenous technical change where firms are heterogenous in productivity and distortions. The state of firms' productivity determines the comparative advantage of the two alternative strategies, imitation and innovation. The further the firm is from the technology frontier, the more likely it is to succeed in learning through random interactions. Conversely, for firms close to the technology frontier, the scope for imitating other firms is limited, and they must break new ground in order to improve their technology. The investment decision is also affected by other firm characteristics, most notably, labor and capital market distortions (wedges). If distortions are big enough, more investment would reduce long-run productivity growth, which is exactly a manifestation of “growth fatigue”. Objective 3: Estimate the model to back out the magnitude and persistence of policy shocks that promote investment but distort resource allocation. We propose a structural estimation method exploiting the stationary equilibrium of the dynamic model. We estimate the model using the Simulated Method of Moments (SMM) by targeting moments of the empirical distribution of R&D and productivity growth that are salient in the theory. In our main application, we use data from manufacturing firms in mainland China in the period 2007-12. We are motivated by the observation that in recent years, the rapid economic growth in China has been accompanied by a boom in R&D expenditure and growing emphasis by the government on innovation We proxy the strategy of firms by their R&D investment behavior on the extensive margin and regard firms making R&D investments as innovators and firms not making R&D investments as imitators. We first show that the predictions of the theory conform with a set of cross-sectional data moments about the behavior and performance of Chinese firms. Then, we estimate the model. A parsimonious model fits the data reasonably well. Next, we extend the model to allow for heterogeneity across firms in R&D costs. We interpret these firm-specific "R&D wedges" as R&D subsidies and allow them to be correlated with firm-level TFP. The estimated pattern is suggestive of an active industrial policy, which is arguably a salient feature of China. The richer models with R&D wedge heterogeneity fit the target moments very accurately. Finally, we also explore an extension in which some Chinese firms may respond to fiscal incentives by fudging R&D expenditure, that is, relabeling part of their operational expenditure as R&D, in order to cash in on generous public subsidies. This model predicts that R&D investment is overestimated in the data. We study the success of the theory in predicting a set of nontargeted moments. We first show that the estimated model generates conditional correlations that closely match the coefficients on key covariates in nonstructural linear regressions whose dependent variables are (i) the determinants of the probability of firms to engage in R&D; and (ii) the determinants of TFP growth rates. Second, the theory bears predictions about the (stationary) TFP distribution and the endogenous TFP growth rate. We find that the estimated model replicates well the TFP distribution in the data, with both left and right Pareto tails that are quantitatively close to those observed in the data. Moreover, the theory predicts an annual TFP growth rate for the median firm of 3.8%, which is the same as in the data for China from 2007--12. In an extension, we re-estimate the model using plant-level data from Taiwan, for which census data about R&D investments are also available. Taiwan is a natural comparison for mainland China, not only because of its geographic and cultural proximity, but also because of the structural similarities between the two economies. In both cases, economic development has been led by the manufacturing sector, first through the growth of low value-added industries and later through a transition to a higher level of technological sophistication (e.g., electronics and semiconductors). Both economies still have today a relatively large manufacturing sector accounting for about 30% of the respective GDPs. The results for Taiwan are qualitatively similar to those obtained for China, although both the productivity of R&D and the rate of technology diffusion appear to be higher for Taiwanese firms. Objective 4: Evaluate quantitatively the welfare consequences of the stimulus policies We consider a reduction in misallocation, as measured by the variance of output wedges. We measure these wedges using the standard empirical methodology in the literature. We find that misallocation is an important drag on TFP for China. In our paper, static output wedges affect the decision to invest in R&D and the dynamics of TFP distribution. Firms' R&D investments are motivated by the desire to improve productivity, which in turn increases future profits. This decision is subject to a classic appropriability problem: a positive output wedge reduces the gains associated with a future TFP increase. A negative wedge has the opposite effect. In an undistorted economy, the level of TFP is the main driver of the decision to invest in R&D: firms with high TFP invest in R&D while firms with low TFP find imitation to be a more attractive strategy because the probability of improving technology through random interaction is higher. Thus, R&D is highly correlated with TFP. The presence of heterogenous output wedges lowers this correlation because the decision to invest in R&D is driven more by the wedge and less by TFP--or, identically, a firms' size matters more than a firm's TFP. We find that halving the variance of output wedges has a large permanent effect on TFP growth. In the benchmark model, annual TFP growth increases from 3.8% to 5.1%.

14503117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14503117.value: From a methodological perspective, this project represents one the first attempts to estimate models of R&D misallocation using firm-level data. The theoretical and empirical methods developed by the project can be applied to many other economies. An obvious next candidate is the US, where R&D misallocation could be much less severe than that in China. The investigation can shed lights on the fundamental differences between US and China in the factors that determine their long-run economic performance.

14503117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14503117.value: China's R&D investment increased dramatically in the past decade but its economic growth (especially aggregate productivity growth) was slowing down. The recent fast-growing literature on misallocation has shown that distortions can significantly reduce the level of output. However, the main challenge is to show how distortion can affect economic growth, which is the goal of this project. We construct a model of firm dynamics with heterogenous productivity and distortions. The productivity distribution evolves endogenously as the result of the decisions of firms seeking to upgrade their productivity over time. Firms can adopt two strategies toward that end: imitation and innovation. The theory bears predictions about the evolution of the productivity distribution. We structurally estimate the stationary state of the dynamic model targeting moments of the empirical distribution of R&D and TFP growth in China during the period 2007--2012. The estimated model fits the Chinese data well. We compare the estimates with those obtained using data for Taiwan and find the results to be robust. We perform counterfactuals to study the effect of alternative policies. We find large effects of R&D misallocation on long-run growth.

14503317.value: 關於一些非綫性時間序列模型依時性加總之研究

14503317.label: Project Objectives
14503317.value: To review the literature on the recent developments in nonlinear time-series modeling and the temporal aggregation of linear and nonlinear time-series models. To derive the mathematical links between basic nonlinear time-series models and their corresponding temporally aggregated processes. Three classes of nonlinear basic models will be considered (i) Markov-switching Gaussian (MSG) models, (ii) bilinear (BL) models, and (iii) self-exciting threshold autoregressive (SETAR) models. To carry out Monte Carlo experiments to study the effects of temporal aggregation on three selected SETAR-type nonlinearity tests. To extend the results obtained for the temporal aggregation of flow variables to the systematic sampling of stock variables.
