We will investigate whether selective exposure to online materials and the agreeableness, openness, and neuroticism personality traits will moderate the effect of intergenerational discrepancies in values on such family conflict;
We will investigate whether family conflict over political issues will predict important outcomes including life satisfaction, family satisfaction, and political attitude polarization;
We will investigate whether Age and constructive response style will moderate the effects of family conflict on the aforementioned outcomes.

14603117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14603117.value: Politics-related tension has been growing in Hong Kong. One notable incident was the “Occupy Central” Movement (or the “Umbrella Revolution”) in late 2014. Local families with members belonging to both pro-Occupy-Central and anti-Occupy-Central camps were reported to have experienced weakened family relationships, and some even sought family-counseling services. Public discourse has called for research on family conflict over political issues. Research in family dynamics has revealed political issues as a unique domain of intergenerational conflict. However, there is limited research on parent-child conflict over political issues. To fill this gap and to address local concerns, we propose a comprehensive model that captures some antecedents and consequences of conflict over political issues between parents and children. Drawing from the literature on family process, political psychology, personality, lifespan development, positive psychology, and communication, our model advances that parent-child value discrepancy brings about family conflict over political issues, which in turn leads to lower levels of life satisfaction and family satisfaction, and more polarized political attitudes for both parents and children. Moreover, we expect that personality traits of agreeableness and openness attenuate the impact of value discrepancy on family conflict, while neuroticism strengthens such associations. Furthermore, the relation between value discrepancy and family conflict should be stronger among those with selective online exposure. Regarding the associations between family conflict and its consequences, we argue that age and response style are the moderators. For instance, the negative impact of conflict on the satisfaction measures should be stronger for parents than for children. Such negative impact should also be stronger for those with a parent/child adopting a destructive, rather than constructive, communication style. To demonstrate the temporally causal relations among these variables, we propose a two-wave longitudinal design. Moreover, we will collect dyadic data and examine inter-influences between a parent and his/her child. Our model will advance existing knowledge of family processes related to politics, a hugely understudied area. In terms of practical implications, our investigation scrutinizes the impact of family conflict over political issues - a lingering social concern that has yet been addressed scientifically. It also delineates roles of important factors such as online behavior and constructive response style in the mechanism of family conflict. To promote the welfare of families with intense conflicts due to political issues, educators/counselors may target on modifying online behavior and reinforcing constructive response style. The proposed study bears significant conceptual and applied implications.

14603217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14603217.value: 來自世界各地的政策制定者都對醫療界別的採購事宜擔憂。為了了解醫療界別與企業之間的貪污行為，在這項研究中，我們專注於一種垂直限制，限制轉售價格（RPM），RPM是上游和下游企業之間的協議，限制下游公司銷售給客戶的價格。RPM不僅已經在醫療界別使用，而且在學術界和法庭上也特別有爭議。 美國法院可以接受的有利於競爭的理由是，RPM有助於防止那些不提供客戶服務（如銷售點服務）的下游公司的所謂搭便車行爲。關於用RPM的理由，不涉及搭便車行爲的理由是有爭議的。 除了Mao and Ng (2016)以外，沒有研究提出使用RPM但不涉及來自下游公司的服務的有利競爭性的理由。然而，Mao and Ng (2016)的模型並沒有提交貪污問題。在RPM的訴訟中沒有提交過貪污。 RPM可以僅僅是用於在貪污市場中競爭的工具嗎？ 醫療界別的採購團隊並不總是為了其機構的利益而採取行動的。與採購貪污相關的機構問題從未明確地出現在經濟學模型内，我們認為RPM是解決採購貪污這類代理問題的工具。 我們採取調查和理論方法。我們的動機來自中國第一個私人反壟斷訴訟Rainbow v. Johnson & Johnson。我們的解釋是，Johnson & Johnson（J&J）如何使用RPM來幫助其分銷商賣貨給醫院。官方的法庭文件根本沒有提到採購貪污問題，但有研究認為中國醫療界別貪污問題的是猖獗的。我們透過這個案例的材料，對醫院採購進行徹底的文獻綜述，特別關注貪污行為和專門針對中國的醫療界別。我們還調查了J&J的其他相關訴訟。其業務遍及全球，美國政府因為J&J在希臘，波蘭，羅馬尼亞和伊拉克的貪污行為而提出起訴。最後，我們與相關的衛生部門人員進行面談。 我們的理論方法旨在建立RPM經濟學模型，明確地說明採購貪污的可能性和採購團隊的行爲。該模型會將我們提出的理論（在提案中概述）形式化，將RPM視為上游公司用於幫助下游公司在賣貨給客戶時的策略。 什麼時候RPM應該被起訴，什麼時候應該被允許RPM呢？我們的經濟學模型旨找尋RPM是一種有利於競爭的策略的條件;條件可以幫助法院判斷使用RPM對市場的可能損壞。

14603217.label: Realisation of objectives
14603217.value: Two completed papers, one under submission at a journal (``Maximum Resale Price Maintenance and Services.'') and the other is at the final stage of polishing soon ready to be submitted (``Resale Price Maintenance in a Corruptible Market'') come out of this project. From now on, I will use the short-form RPM. The project's 7 objectives are all realized and documented in ``RPM in a Corruptible Market.'' The research requires reading many legal cases to find relevant applications of our theory. Kim-sau and I looked for cases where the supply chains have 2 features: [1] Dealers don't compete with one another, and [2] Dealers' services cannot increase manufacturer's own product sales. Our motivating example of ``RPM in a Corruptible Market'' is Johnson & Johnson's use of minimum RPM to sell suturing products to Chinese hospitals. Its dealers weren't competing with one another as exclusive territories were granted to them. There was also a debate in court concerning whether the dealers' services were important in making the hospitals buy Johnson & Johnson's suturing products. We came across another landmark RPM case: State Oil v. Khan 1997. The 2 features exist, namely, gas stations under State Oil's brand (which is Union 76) were far apart (i.e., dealers aren't competing) and it is hard to find any significant services that would boost gas sales. What distinguishes this case from Johnson & Johnson's, however, is that this is a case concerning maximum RPM. The question is whether the theory we developed in ``RPM in a Corruptible Market'' can also explain State Oil v. Khan. After much thought, we think our theory is inapplicable. It requires another theory. We therefore build one that concerns the idea that gas stations don't want to just profit from selling gas, but they have much interest in selling gas buyers convenience store items. As such, another RPM theory revolving around cross-sales is developed, crystalized into ``Maximum RPM and Services.'' Comparing the models in these two papers, one can find similar theoretical structure, equilibrium concepts, and conditions for RPM. The rest of this section concentrates on ``RPM in a Corruptible Market.'' [1] Derive a model of RPM without services but with corruption (100%) ``RPM in a Corruptible Market'' gives the simplest possible model we can think of to explain minimum resale price maintenance (RPM) used by Johnson and Johnson when it sells medical consumables to hospitals through dealers. Apart from the 2 features mentioned above, the customers the dealers have to satisfy are procurement teams, not the hospitals. They are not end-users but agents of the hospitals using other people's money for products used on others. Under this setting, corruption naturally emerges. The dealers' need to bribe the procurement teams motivates the manufacturer to take bribery costs into consideration. It is because they are merely one form of distribution costs. The lower the distribution costs, the more profit the manufacturer's supply chain can realize. Our model shows how this particular setting motives the manufacturer to use minimum RPM. [2] Explicitly account for the incentives of the procurement teams in a corruptible market (100%) To procurement teams, buying reasonable products at reasonable prices on behalf of the hospitals is what they want. The least they want is for the hospitals to suspect their transactions. Hospitals must audit them from time to time. But with thousands of medical inputs, they can't do it all the time. What triggers an audit is what procurement teams care about. Two things stand out: the price the hospital pays, and the price other hospitals pay for the same item. The logic is that if the price the other hospitals pay is high, it looks as if their own price is more reasonable. If the price is reasonable, then there is less urge for the hospital to audit the team. Therefore, even if dealers aren't competing, the price one dealer charges to a hospital can have a ``cover-up'' effect on the procurement team of the other hospital. But dealers will not take such a ``cover-up'' effect of their own pricing into account, and that results in their charging too low a price to their respective hospitals. The manufacturer of course wants to correct this by using minimum RPM to push their prices right back up. [3] Derive conditions under which RPM is pro-competitive (100%) Under our theory, RPM allows the manufacturer to make more money at the expense of hospitals that overpay medical inputs. Therefore, we find no condition under our theory for which RPM is pro-competitive. This is a new undesirable effect never articulated in the RPM literature. [4] Inform the court the conditions under which RPM is likely to be pro-competitive (100%) Our theory therefore informs the court that whenever they suspect dealers sell to agents rather than end-users, they have one more concern for the undesirable effect of RPM. RPM appears to make the agents ``safer,'' which ultimately translates to their principals paying a higher price than if RPM is banned. [5] Enhance our knowledge on how firms sell to hospitals (100%) Putting ourselves in the shoes of procurement teams, we should note that they will be sensitive to not just the price they authorize their own hospitals to pay, but they also care about the prices that other hospitals (even if they are far away) pay. RPM used by the manufacturer helps its dealers to sell to procurement teams by minimizing price variability across hospitals. Procurement teams are ``sold'' a sense of safety as low price variability probably makes it less likely for their hospitals to audit their transactions. The supply-side response to procurement teams' concerns of getting caught being corrupt is new to the literature. Our theory doesn't just study RPM, but to try to get a sense of the extent to which hospitals' overpayment of inputs can be severe without seeing any price variability across hospitals. [6] Indirectly help detect possible corruption areas (100%) When RPM is extensively used in products that those who make the purchase decisions are not end-users and they are using other people's money, it is a red-flag. Under our theory, RPM can facilitate corruption by making it less detectable. Therefore, checking if RPM is covered for certain products indirectly hints to the regulators where corruption more likely occurs. [7] Help formulate anti-corruption policies (100%) Our theory helps formulate anti-corruption policies by emphasizing that regulators cannot rely just on price variability of the same/similar inputs across hospitals. Once this is taken as a corruption proxy, the supply-side will respond to it. Using RPM to mask corruption is one such response. We also call for a serious attempt by regulators to think of coordinating across hospitals in banning inputs covered by RPM. We derive a strategic game in the Appendix of our paper that shows it is reasonable for individual hospitals to fail to ban RPM even if they can costlessly observe whether certain inputs are covered by RPM or not. It calls for coordination across hospitals, which probably can be facilitated by regulatory agencies.

14603217.label: Major findings and research outcome
14603217.value: Two completed papers: ``Maximum Resale Price Maintenance and Services'' and ``Resale Price Maintenance in a Corruptible Market'' come out of this project. They contribute to both theory and policy. [1]Theory: The existing literature almost always motivate RPM theoretically using intra-brand competition, i.e., dealers carrying the same product compete with one another. Although not all, many major RPM theories are also motivated by dealers' services, such as those along the lines of Telser (1960). We give two theories, one explaining minimum and the other maximum RPM, that do not depend on these two usual driving forces. In explaining minimum RPM, we rely on a setting of corruptible agents; such a setting is not uncommon. Other than hospital procurement, we at least have found another 2000 European RPM case concerning school procurement featuring similar market setting. In explaining maximum RPM, we rely on a setting where dealers not only can profit from selling the manufacturer's products, they can also profit from cross-selling customers coming for the manufacturer's other other products that the manufacturer does not supply. Gas is one prime example where gas buyers can buy a coffee at a station. According to the industry report, it is the coffee sales that stations rely on rather than the thin gas profit margin. As far as we read, none has proposed using cross-selling to explain maximum RPM. [2]Policy: When a court faces an RPM case, our theory calls for one practice. The court should ask: ``Who the dealers sell to?'' Are their customers end-users? Or are they agents using other people's money? How likely is corruption? Does RPM play a role in facilitating corruption? On the other hand, price variability across hospitals for same/similar inputs has been extensively used in anti-corruption programs. In ``RPM in a Corruptible Market,'' we document many of these programs around the world. Our theory, however, casts doubt on them. The key is that the supply-side will respond to regulators' focus of price variability. RPM is one tool they can use to iron-out price variability. While price variability is low, it does not mean corruption is absent. As far as administratively practical, hospitals should ban RPM covered products. This is difficult as procurement teams lack incentives to report which products are under RPM. Some coordination is probably needed as our game theoretic analysis shows that lacking coordination, hospitals can fail to ban RPM even if they can.

14603217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14603217.value: Our theory gives one reason why hospitals overpay for medical inputs. There is another plausible supply-side response to anti-corruption measures that jacks up the prices hospitals pay for inputs. Kim-sau and I have in mind another hidden perverse incentive: manufacturers may deliberately differentiate their products unnecessarily. Doing so allows them to tell hospitals' procurement teams: ``Look! Our product is one of a kind. Nowhere your boss can find similar products to compare the price you pay.'' The result will be the existence of unnecessarily differentiated products for the sake of making it ``safe'' for procurement teams to buy them at high prices. The teams feel ``safe'' because their bosses are less capable of finding similar products in the market to reference for to get a sense of what a reasonable price should be. This is analogous to a Salop (1979)'s result of inefficient over-differentiation. We have a hunch that this is a more serious problem than using resale price maintenance to jack up the prices hospitals pay for medical inputs. Because it involves expensive R&D. Our literature search finds no one mentioning about this problem. In the future, we will look for anecdotal evidence first to gauge this problem.

14603217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14603217.value: Many manufacturers were sued for controlling their dealers' prices. These lawsuits beg the question of why. Despite many existing explanations, scholars haven't given one in scenarios where dealers don't compete and their services do not help sell the manufacturers' products. One such scenario is when Johnson and Johnson disallowed its dealers to discount its suturing products when selling to hospitals. This project gives an explanation by putting ourselves in the shoes of the customers dealers have to please, namely, procurement teams. As they use other people's money to buy products for others, corruption likely creeps in. Dealers will bribe them for sales. Procurement teams would worry if other hospitals pay a low price. If others do, the hospitals will likely audit them. One way the manufacturer facilitates its dealers' sales is to disallow all dealers to discount. Doing so reassuring procurement teams that their hospitals will not audit them because no hospital pays a low price. This result is significant because in facilitating dealers' sales, the manufacturer increase profit at the expense of hospitals: they overpay for medical inputs. Ironing out price variability across hospitals also makes it more difficult to detect procurement corruption.

14603617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14603617.value: 在高密度城市，由於室內居住環境擠逼，城市綠地應被視為長者生活空間的延伸。具良好設計的城市綠地能促進積極樂頤年並改善長者的生活質素。擬議研究旨在了解長者對於城市綠地的看法、偏好及使用情況，以及城市綠地對長者的健康和生活質素的影響，以便就在高密度城市中規劃和設計長者友善的城市綠地提出見解。 研究顯示，長者在不同城市環境下，對市區綠化空間的看法、偏好及使用情況有很大差異。因此，設計師在設計城市綠地時必須考慮到這些差異。大部分的現存研究在低至中密度城市中進行，而高密度居住環境的研究甚為少見。此外，雖然已經證實長者對於城市綠地的看法和偏好與其使用模式有莫大關連，卻甚少考慮到與健康和生活質素的關係。 在香港這樣的高密度城市，長者對於城市綠地的看法、偏好和使用情況受到城市綠地不足所限制。這些空間的特質包括距離近、尺寸零散、空間狹窄和設計元素混合。因此，為了解決長者在提倡積極樂頤年下對城市綠地的需求，優化這些特質相當重要。 擬議研究旨在達致以下幾點：(1) 對香港高密度居住環境的典型社區裡的城市綠地進行現場審查，選取研究地點；(2) 對長者進行問卷調查，以取得有關該區的城市綠地的看法、偏好和使用情況，並據現有的SF12v2健康調查了解其健康狀況；(3) 統計分析感知價值、偏好和使用模式，並判斷它們與長者健康狀況的關係；(4) 根據上述結果，研發良好的設計規範，並為從事城市規劃和設計的持份者訂定循證為本的城市綠地的設計準則。 對於香港的城市規劃師和設計師而言，香港規劃標準與準則是一份重要文件。然而，該文件只提供了設計城市綠地方面的定量信息。擬議研究的結果能夠通過提供有關長者對城市綠地的看法、偏好和使用情況，改進香港規劃標準與準則。在香港以外，本研究亦就為促進積極樂頤年提供良好城市綠地方面，增進對世衞的全球老年友好城市建設指南的了解。

14603617.label: Realisation of objectives
14603617.value: Pilot study was conducted in urban green spaces in Hong Kong and Tainan during winter 2016, in collaboration with National Cheng Kung University. Site audits were carried out by a team formed by students from architecture, landscape architecture and social science. The audits offered first-hand information on the existing design of UGS and use patterns of older visitors, with a total of 118 and 99 responses obtained respectively. The questionnaire was then refined based on the responses obtained in the pilot study. The subsequent round of survey was conducted in 22 study areas covering urban green spaces in public housing estates, street parks, district parks. The interviews were carried out during the hours of 0800-1100 and 1400-1600 on weekdays. As from observations, older adults are much more likely to be present in the UGS during these periods of day, and there is a greater percentage of older adult visitors to the UGS on weekdays than in weekends. The questionnaire used in the pilot study was developed from validated questionnaires from previous studies (adjusted to fit the objectives of this study) and self-designed questions. Questions in the pilot study focused on the following aspects: 1) subjective assessment of the quality and characteristics of UGS, 2) usage pattern of UGS, 3) self-reported health status using Short Form-12v2 Health Survey (SF12v2), and 4) socio-demographic information. For the second-round survey, the questionnaire used was modified and extended to obtain more specific information about the design features of UGS. Based on the first-round survey and site audits, sub-scales were also added for the following topics: 1) accessibility of the UGS, 2) activity in different types of UGS, 3) preferences for UGS, 4) design aspects related to aesthetic quality, 5) aspects associated with perceived safety. Binomial logistic regression was conducted to examine how much the types of UGS and perceived environmental quality explains the frequency of visit and duration of stay. Two cut-off values were used in the frequency of visit (i.e. more than once a week, and everyday) in order to examine the threshold of how frequent older adults visited the UGS is significantly associated with the perceived quality of UGS. For duration of stay, the cut-off values are “more than one hour” and “half a day”. Respondents with missing data were excluded from the statistical analysis. ANOVA test was conducted to determine whether there are significant differences in perceived environmental quality between the types of UGS. Post-hoc Tukey’s test was also conducted to determine pairs of UGS types which are significantly different in scores of perceived environmental qualities. The statistical analysis was conducted using IBM SPSS Version 22. Binomial logistic regression was also used to investigate the relationship between the usage and perceived qualities of UGS, and self-rated health conditions of the respondents, i.e. the physical component summary (PCS) and mental component summary (MCS) scores of the SF12v2 health survey. Three models, consisting of different combinations of independent variables, were used. Model 1 adjusted for the usage pattern of UGS including frequency of visit and duration of stay while Model 2 adjusted for the perceived qualities of the UGS. Model 3 adjusted for both sets of variables in order to examine any potential interactions between the usage and perception of UGS. All models were adjusted for socio-demographic conditions of the respondents, including sex, age, education, and living arrangement.

14603617.label: Major findings and research outcome
14603617.value: The present study aims to investigate the inter-relationships between older adults’ perception and usage of UGS, as well as how the perception and usage of UGS are related to older adults’ self-rated health in three different types of UGS in Hong Kong, namely green spaces in public housing estates, street parks and district parks. Binomial logistic regression shows that perceived proximity to UGS is associated with frequency of visit and duration of stay. Longer exposure to UGS is also associated with better perceived physical and mental well-being. Influences on usage of UGS, however, is not limited to physical attributes of the space. Design and management of UGS can take into account the results of this research, to create a better environment for elderly in high density area. Perceived qualities of UGS were different across the types of UGS. District parks were significantly different from the other two types of UGS due to their sizes and locations, as they are generally larger in size and distant from residential areas. Maintenance and cleanliness were found to be different between urban parks and public housing estates because urban parks were managed by Leisure and Cultural Services Department which has a more frequent maintenance and cleaning schedule while UGS in public housing estates were managed by Housing Department which is responsible for the entire public housing estates in general. The methodology of the present study was also applied in Tainan. Results were published in International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health. The questionnaire surveys conducted in both Hong Kong and Tainan showed that the duration of visits to UGS was positively associated with “mental health” and “social functioning”, two subscales evaluating health-related quality of life in SF 12v2. Moderation analysis indicated that such correlation was especially significant in women and those with low social support and social capital. A positive relationship was found between the “physical health” subscale and perceived safety in UGS. This relationship was stronger among older adults living alone. Furthermore, colour of the plants and maintenance condition of UGS were significant aspects affecting the subjective assessment of aesthetic quality. Behavioural pattern of older adults also varied across different types of urban green spaces due to the maintenance level of such spaces and the demographic background of the community investigated.

14603617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14603617.value: The findings of this study are limited by the fact that the survey was conducted in the period when there were relatively more older adults in the UGS in order to obtain a higher response rate. Since there were many older adults in the UGS, it is possible to acquire a biased sample towards those enjoy socializing with others in UGS, and less likely to interview those prefer a quiet environment in the UGS. In the future, the surveys can be conducted in collaboration with local NGOs to cover elderly people with disabilities or those who are difficult to go outdoors. Telephone survey is also possible if the survey can be adapted to such means. Another limitation concerns the self-reported nature of SF12v2. Respondents might inaccurately estimate their health or reluctant to reveal their genuine health status to the interviewers. In addition, the survey was conducted in outdoor spaces and older adults who do not or less frequently visit were not covered. Findings may not be readily applied to this group of older adults. A larger sample size, especially in street and urban parks, would provide more reliable results in certain aspects and have a more balanced socio-demographic profile of the respondents.

14603617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14603617.value: This project explored how elderly perceive and use urban green space in high density cities and its relationship with their physical and mental health. It adopted a combination of questionnaire survey and site audit to obtain both objective and subjective data. As shown by the data, there are large variations in elderly’s perception in three different types of green spaces. Elderly people mostly enjoy large parks with multiple facilities than small spaces along the street and within their residing estate. Statistical analyses showed that staying longer in urban green space is related to better perceived physical and mental well-being. Among various features of the space, perceived proximity is related to both visiting frequency and staying duration. It implies that planner should focus on providing green space that are within comfortable walking distance from elderly’s home, even in very compact city environment.

14604117.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14604117.value: 中國的環境抗爭：對其演變及政治地理的測繪與分析

14604117.label: Project Objectives
14604117.value: To construct a database of environmental protest events in China between 2007 and 2017. To test partially contradictory hypotheses derived from case studies, to gauge the evolution of environmental contention, and to better ascertain factors that drive the apparent acceleration of environmental conflict in China. To engage broader scholarly debates on the repertoire of contention in China, environmental contention in comparative perspective, and environmental justice. To drive forward the methodological discussion on using newly available data on protests and other events that technological and political change in China has made available in recent years. To provide the domestic and international communities of scholars, journalists, policy-makers, and environmental activists with evidence on the evolution and political geography of environmental protest that does not yet exist. To use environmental contention as a window for observing the process of putting China on a more environmentally sustainable trajectory.

14604117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14604117.value: This research will examine the evolution and political geography of contention in one of the most dynamic and critical domains of state-society relations in China: the environment. Environmental concerns have not only emerged among the most potent drivers of protest. Some environmental protests also have developed public-spirited characteristics that depart substantially from the dominant form of moral economy protests in China. Although scholars have contributed intriguing case studies on this phenomenon and provided conjectures, to date the field is characterized by a glaring absence of systematic evidence. Next to nothing is known about even the most basic descriptive characteristics of environmental protests (in particular, the distribution of events over space and time). Likewise, their contextual conditions and driving forces remain not well understood. This project aims to fill this gap. It will collect data on environmental protest between 2007 and 2017 from a wide range of media sources and systematically code and analyze it in line with standards developed in protest event analysis. This evidence will be combined with community-level socio-economic and pollution statistics, as well as interviews with Chinese activists and policy researchers. The project will examine key attributes of environmental mobilization, state responses, and their evolution over time. It will provide new insights on whether novel forms of action such as preventive resistance, multi-stage contention, or the mobilization of broad communities for public goods are spreading. It will further study the spatial distribution of protests and diffusion patterns, and generate knowledge on the links between socio-economic and environmental context on the one hand, and the inclination to mobilize and the attributes of protests on the other. It will thereby increase the understanding on what is driving the seemingly proliferating propensity for environmental activism. Theoretically, the evidence will provide new leverage to engage broader scholarly discussions on the evolution of popular protest in China, comparative environmental contention, and environmental justice. Methodologically, it will help to drive forward the understanding of newly available news media sources for studying protests and other public events in China. Practically, it will provide not yet available evidence about the evolution of environmental politics in China to scholars, policy makers, and the public. The research will be carried out between 1st September 2017 and 31st August 2020. It is expected to produce several articles in peer-reviewed academic journals. 中國的環境抗爭：對其演變及政治地理的測繪與分析 本項研究旨在對中國環境抗爭的歷史演變和政治地理進行分析。選題的意義在於環境抗爭能夠集中反映當代中國國家與社會關係的急劇變化。 環境問題不僅是容易引發群體性事件的導火索，而且在一定程度上也培育了公共精神，從而與中國當前占主流的道德經濟型抗爭大相徑庭。儘管一些學者對一些環境抗爭的案例進行了很好的分析，也提出了猜想，但迄今為止，基於系統性證據的分析尚屬空白，即便是最基本的描述性統計分析比如環境抗爭在空間和時間上的分佈也不存在。當然，學界對產生環境抗爭的社會經濟背景和驅動因素也缺乏了解。 為了填補這個學術空白，本研究將系統性地收集由2007年至2017年關於環境抗爭的媒體報導，以抗爭事件分析的標準方法為基礎構建一套編碼系統，對收集的數據進行系統性的編碼和分析。在此基礎上，本研究將進行數據多源整合，將以上實證資料與社區的社會經濟數據、環境污染統計數據、中國社會活動家和政策研究人員的訪談數據進行整合分析。分析結果可以幫助了解是否出現了新興的環境抗爭模式，比如預防性抵禦、多階段抗爭、公共物品供給的大眾傳播和動員。此外，本項目將建立以下兩個二維分析模型：社會經濟條件-環境狀況、動員的傾向性-環境抗爭的特徵，推進環境抗爭的空間分佈及擴散模型的研究，並分析公眾環境抗爭傾向性不斷提高的動因所在。 本項目將會為以下理論研究做出貢獻：中國公眾抗爭的演化進程、比較環境抗爭、環境正義。在方法論上，本項目能夠為學者、政策制定者、公眾提供當前稀缺的環境政治演變過程的基本數據，並探索以媒體報導和大數據為分析對象的跨學科研究方法。 本項目的研究成果將會向高質量的同行評議的學術期刊投稿。

14604117.label: Realisation of objectives
14604117.value: To construct a database of environmental protest events in China between 2007 and 2017 (objective #1 and #5), we developed a data collection protocol which covers (1) possible data sources, (2) approaches adopted for identifying keywords related to environmental protest events, (3) test results on different combinations of keywords, and (4) steps to be taken for collecting news articles. Details of the data collection protocol are available in Appendix 1. Objective #1 has been fully realized. Table 1 summarizes the results of data collection. Table 1. Collection of news articles related to environmental protest events in China, 2013-2017 WiseNews CNKI 2013 8,884 9,341 2014 8,002 9,777 2015 5,390 9.296 2016 4,559 7,636 2017 3,630 9,136 To achieve objective #2 and #4, we collected and classified environmental protest cases from Wickedonna, complemented with news articles from WiseNews and CNKI. To be able to identify environmental news and to construct case profiles, we built the coodbook. By training three coders and comparing inter-coder differences in coding results, we refined and finalized the codebook. The cookbook was for constructing variables that can capture both the demographic information and patterns of evolvement of the protest events. Appendix 2 provides detailed information on the methodology for variable construction and measurement. In the era of the rapid development of computational social science that incorporates natural language processing and machine learning, we have also attempted to construct a set of training data to build algorithm for classifying news articles by focus issue, size of group activity, actor, strategies adopted for legitimizing the contention / gaining support / mobilizing the public, and outcome. Unfortunately, professionals who are equipped with such skills are under high demand. After being interviewed for the job, the candidates got to know more details about the project and they decided not to join because they considered the topic politically sensitive. Thus, objective #2 and #4 are 90% realized because the level of methodological advancement has not reached automated classification and pattern recognition for textual analysis. To achieve objective #3 and #5, both literature review and empirical analysis have been performed. It is rather labor intensive and time consuming to manually process the large amount of news articles. But hiring research support staff has become very difficult facing the social unrest and the outbreak of coronavirus, besides the development in Hong Kong’s legal system. Alternatively, we supported research degree students and requested them to work on the project, while they still need to spend much time on their doctoral studies. In this context, the progress on data analysis and manuscript writing was less than desirable. Furthermore, the project was under tremendous pressure in the changed legal system in Hong Kong. In this context, the project team has to take extra care to follow the advice from the authority and not to formally publish anything on environmental protests in China. Thus, objective #3 and #5 are only 80% realized, considering both articles published on institutional changes in the environmental governance system in China are not strictly on environmental protest cases. Appendix 3 and 4 are the journal publications. To achieve objective #6, we have been studying the institutional changes in China’s environmental governance carefully. Environmental contentions can be reflected in both the state-society and central-local relationships. By working on this project, we have successfully analyzed environmental contention in air quality monitoring, environmental enforcement, and the centralization reform by prefectural level cities in China. Besides the journal articles, Appendix 5 is a detailed study on the centralization reform. The knowledge gained advances our understanding of the institutional changes that put China on a more environmentally sustainable trajectory. Thus, objective #6 is 100% realized.

14604117.label: Major findings and research outcome
14604117.value: This project has focused on the driving forces and outcomes of institutional changes in China’s environmental governance. Facing the rising civil society and increasing social demand for a cleaner environment, China has updated its ambient air quality standards. However, the implementation and enforcement of the air quality standards cannot be taken for granted. Environmental contention still exists in the central-local relations in China. The project investigates the principal-agent problem in acquiring air quality monitoring data through the government hierarchy in China and uses Shandong as a case study for illustrating how it is addressed by resorting to a market approach. Adopting transaction cost economics perspective, we analyzed contractual hazards in both relying on the hierarchy and the market. We found the Shandong provincial environmental protection bureau has specified eligibility criteria and crafted contract terms that can reduce the risk of being held up resulted from asset specificity, increase efficiency, improve observability of both input and output quality, and induce accountability by enforceable rewards and sanctions. The lessons learned contribute to the literature on multi-level environmental governance and are useful for institution building for achieving sustainable development in China and beyond (Appendix 3). Furthermore, by comparing with other Asian countries, the project evaluates the outcomes and institutional changes in selected countries related to substantive environmental issues such as air pollution, water quality, municipal solid waste, transport, land use, and climate change. By synthesizing the main research issues, methodology and findings of the growing literature on the region, we highlight the trends in environmental governance and gaps in policy and research. Despite the efforts made, there are still remaining environmental governance challenges to be addressed by both the academics and practitioners in Asia (Appendix 4).

14604117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14604117.value: The project offers an opportunity for both methodological exploration and issue finding. In the future, the project can be extended along the following two lines. In terms of research focus, it is clear that collaboration also plays an extremely role to bring about the institutional changes in China’s environmental governance. Thus, the PI will design a project that would also collect cases on collaborative efforts in addressing sustainability challenges, beyond environmental contentions, which only partially contribute to the institutional changes. Furthermore, the PI has started to learn CiteSpace, ORA-Lite, Gephi, VOSviewer and python for conducting computerized bibliometric and textual analyses. In this way, it would become less labor intensive or time consuming to process a large amount of documents for case analysis.

14604117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14604117.value: Because of the size of its population and economy, good environmental governance in China is fundamental not only for the well-being of the country’s population but also for the health of the planet. This project focuses on the driving forces and outcomes of institutional changes in China’s environmental governance. Environmental contentions drive institutional change, which are reflected in both the state-society and central-local relationships. The project has successfully analyzed environmental contentions in air quality monitoring and environmental enforcement, as well as the resulted centralization reform in China. The research findings highlight the importance of contractual design for aligning the interests of different parties, improving the data quality, increasing efficiency and accountability of environmental monitoring and enforcement in China. The lessons learned contribute to the literature on multi-level environmental governance and are useful for institution building for achieving sustainable development in China and beyond.

14604817.label: Realisation of objectives
14604817.value: The 4 project objectives were fully achieved. To carry out this project, we employed a design-based research (DBR) methodological approach which consisted of 2 iterative research rounds, namely RR1 and RR2 (with iterative stages of Design, Enact, Analyse, and Redesign; 1 cycle per year). As of the original plan, this DBR was conducted in the context of formal curriculum learning and teaching of LS (Liberal Studies) in different school settings in Hong Kong. There were 9 participating secondary schools at the 3 different academic bands (upper, average and lower), involving a total of 9 LS teachers and 610 Secondary-5 (Grade-11) students. The background of the 9 recruited teachers was similar; each had a bachelor of education degree and 5 to 6 years of LS teaching experience. >> Design In accordance with the formal learning and teaching context of LS, FIBER (Flipped Issue-Based Enquiry Ride) was preliminarily constructed as a 6-phase pedagogic framework to integrate flipped learning and social enquiry learning [PRE-LESSON, lower-order learning: Phases of Connection, Comprehension, and Expression; IN-LESSON, higher-order learning: Phases of Exploration, Construction and Reflection]. At the beginning of the Design stage, we conducted individual training of flipped learning and FIBER for the 9 teachers. To get themselves more familiarised with this pedagogic framework before the Enact stage in RR1, the teachers piloted experimenting on the implementation FIBER in their own Secondary-4 classes. After that, each of them was assigned a social enquiry module in the LS curricular theme of “Society and the Environment.” We further went through with him/ her the FIBER resource set previously developed for the assigned module. All resource sets were reviewed by a research advisory panel which was composed of educators from local universities, experienced LS teachers from non-participating secondary schools and curriculum development officers. >> Enact At RR1’s Enact stage (i.e., the first year), in each school, the teacher implemented FIBER to facilitate a Secondary-5 class to study the assigned module. In this round, there were a total of 307 student participants from the 9 schools [Band-A students: 107; Band-B students: 105; Band-C students: 95]. At RR2’s Enact stage (i.e., the second year), in each school, the teacher implemented FIBER with the incorporation of the new teacher facilitation practices formulated at the Redesign stage (see below) to facilitate another Secondary-5 class to study the same assigned module. In this round, there were a total of 303 student participants from the 9 schools [Band-A students: 106; Band-B students: 103; Band-C students: 94]. In RR2, we deliberately requested the teacher to select a class that was comparable with the participating class in RR1, in terms of academic performance. We cross-checked that there was no significant difference (p > 0.05) between the LS school-based examination mean scores of the 2 classes respectively prior to their participation at the Enact stages in RR1 and RR2. Combining RR1’s and RR’s subjects, the total number of student participants in the entire DBR was 610. During the Enact stages in RR1 and RR2, apart from in-class observation in each school, we conducted out-of-class research data collection work, including teacher reflective think-aloud gathering, just-in-time and purposive student/ teacher interviews, as well as LMS access-log gathering. >> Analyse At the Analyse stages in RR1 and RR2, in each school, we administered a knowledge test to the students. The test questions were developed in accordance with the recent LS public examination questions pertaining to the social enquiry module that they had studied at the Enact stages of RR1 and RR2. All questions were scrutinised by the same research advisory panel which had been set up for reviewing the previously developed FIBER resources. Every completed and collected test paper in RR1 and RR2 was individually marked by 2 experienced LS teachers respectively from 2 non-participating schools. The Kappa values of the interrater reliability in RR1 and RR2 were respectively 0.92 and 0.91. Moreover, in each school, in RR1 and RR2, we conducted in-depth, semi-structured student interviews for probing into their learning experience with FIBER. We employed layering and interrelating approaches to analysing the collected interview data to triangulate and explain the knowledge test results. At RR1’s Analyse stage, we revealed a number of problems arising from the implementation of FIBER during RR1’s Enact stage, impeding the students’ flipped social enquiry learning process. Some of the problems generically happened in all schools across the 3 academic bands, while the others uniquely happened in the schools at a particular academic band. >> Redesign Three teacher groups were formed to work on the optimisation of FIBER by addressing the problems revealed in RR1. The 3 teachers at the same schools’ academic band were grouped together, e.g., the 3 Band-A teachers joined the Band-A teacher group, and so on. Through face-to-face and Apple® FaceTime online meetings, as well as other online tools (e.g., emails and WhatsApp® group chats), we discussed the findings obtained in RR1 in each teacher group and collaborate with them to formulate possible interventions for improving/ enhancing the implementation of FIBER in their own schools. Specifically, we aimed to derive new teacher facilitation practices for tackling the identified problems. All these newly derived practices were enacted by the teachers in the Band-A, Band-B, and Band-C schools at RR2’s Enact stage. Difficulties and Solutions: The main problem that the team encountered in this project happened in Fall 2019 (i.e., at RR2’s Enact stage). Owing to the social/ political issues arising in Hong Kong in the second half of 2019, the original teaching implementation schedule of some participating schools in the fall semester of 2019 was largely affected. Eventually, some teaching implementations had to be moved to December 2019 and January 2020. Fortunately, before the outbreak of COVID-19 in Hong Kong (early February 2020), the teaching implementation work, as well as the knowledge test, in each school was completed. After that, we made use of Zoom® as a video-conferencing tool to conduct the post-implementation data collection work online (mainly the student interviews) during the COVID-19 school suspension in Spring 2020.

14604817.label: Major findings and research outcome
14604817.value: At RR1’s Design stage of the DBR, in the experiment on the 9 teachers’ pilot implementation of FIBER and the comparison with the conventional social enquiry learning approach, it was showed that FIBER had significantly positive pedagogic effects on the upper, average, and lower academic students, with small to medium effect sizes [as documented in our AERA conference paper (2019) and our ILE journal paper (2019)]. After the Enact and Analyse stages in RR1, it was revealed that a number of problems arising from the implementation of FIBER, impeding the students’ flipped social enquiry learning process. Some of the problems generically happened in all schools across the 3 academic bands, while the others uniquely happened in the schools at a particular academic band. All these problems are summarised in Table 1 in our ICCE conference paper (2019) and recapped in Appendix A in our CAE journal paper (under review). Specific new teacher facilitation practices [see Table 2 in our CAE journal paper (under review)] for tackling these “generic” and “unique” problems were developed at the Redesign stage in RR2 and enacted by the teachers in the Band-A, Band-B, and Band-C schools at the Enact stage in RR2. According to the quantitative analysis (and the qualitative triangulation) of comparing the students’ performance across the 3 academic bands at the Enact stages in RR1 and RR2, the new teacher facilitation practices which were respectively enacted in Band-A, Band-B, and Band-C schools in RR2 functioned to mitigate the “generic” and “unique” problems and significantly advance the pedagogic effectiveness of FIBER, with medium to large effect sizes [as documented in our AERA conference paper (2021)]. Grounded on the results of this DBR project, 6 teacher facilitation principles for optimising the process of students’ flipped social enquiry learning were proposed [as documented in our CAE journal paper (under review)] : Principle 1: Projecting “teacher presence” onto pre-lesson individual learning; Principle 2: Rectifying misconceptions before in-lesson peer learning; Principle 3: Allowing competence-based autonomy in flipped formative and summative learning tasks; Principle 4: Incorporating necessitated in-class technical scaffolds; Principle 5: Empowering student leaders to moderate in-lesson peer learning; and Principle 6: Integrating contextual-based pedagogic elements into flipped learning The present work provides the field with (i) strong empirical evidence for supporting wider adoption of FIBER in LS and (ii) new insights into developing adequate teacher facilitation strategies when adopting flipped learning in social humanities education and upon different formal schooling settings.

14604817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14604817.value: Although the teacher facilitation practices and principles developed in this DBR are more specific to LS and secondary education, flipped learning researchers can make use of the developed as a basis to further derive particular “flipped” practices and principles for other SHE subjects (e.g., geography, history, economics, and religious studies) and different educational sectors (e.g., primary schools, colleges and universities). In addition, we suggest gamifying the out-of-class part of FIBER so as to further promote students’ motivation and engagement in accomplishing the pre-lesson learning tasks. In fact, we have already done some pilot work pertaining to this initiative. Grounding on Lee et al.’s educational-gamification framework (composed of 3 core gamification design constructs: cognitive, emotional and social), we conceptually proposed how to infuse the gamified learning elements into the “pre-lesson homework” of FIBER [see our DiGRA conference paper (2019)]. More recently, we have conducted a small-scale empirical pilot study on the proposed in which we initially obtained some positive results [see our ISET conference paper (2021)]. Certainly, more in-depth work with a larger scale is needed to further examine the pedagogic effectiveness of “Gamified FIBER” (G-FIBER) across different academic bands and in different schooling settings.

14604817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14604817.value: In recent years, flipped learning has been regarded as a salient instructional approach in school education. Although there have been considerable studies about adopting flipped learning in STEM-related education and language education, research into harnessing this approach in social humanities education (SHE) remains in its infancy. Flipped Issue-Based Enquiry Ride (FIBER) is a pedagogic integration of flipped learning and social enquiry learning that we developed for SHE. In this research, harnessing FIBER as an initial pedagogic framework, we designed, enacted and evaluated what and how teachers could do in order to optimise the process of high-, middle, and low academic-achieving students’ flipped social enquiry learning. Besides the formulated practices, we also derived 6 teacher facilitation principles for flipped social enquiry learning: (i) projecting “teacher presence” onto pre-lesson individual learning, (ii) rectifying misconceptions before in-lesson peer learning, (iii) allowing competence-based autonomy in flipped formative and summative learning tasks, (iv) incorporating necessitated in-class technical scaffolds, (v) empowering student leaders to moderate in-lesson peer learning, and (vi) integrating contextual-based pedagogic elements into flipped learning. The present work provides both researchers and educators with new insights into developing adequate teacher facilitation strategies when adopting flipped learning in SHE and in different schooling settings.

14605617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14605617.value: Tai Chi (TC) is a type of traditional Chinese exercises that are widely practiced particularly by middle-aged and elderly people to maintain or improve health. As a mind-body exercise, TC exercise has extra cognitive component than common physical exercise, besides common physical exercise component. As for cognitive components, it is suggested to include mental relaxation and cognitive activity that circulates "Qi" within the body when practicing. However, it was not known that whether TC demonstrates more significant mental calmness and more "Qi"-related mental activity than other types of aerobic exercise such as walking. Another research questions arises that whether extra cognitive component of TC could bring about additional mental health benefits than those without cognitive component. Furthermore, it is interesting to know whether proficiency level of TC practitioners correlates with the cognitive characteristics during performance and the mental health status of them. A few years ago we compared the cardiovascular (CV) health effect and metabolic demand between TC and walking, and found that both exercise training for 3 months yielded similar CV health effects but TC elicited much lower energy demand and exercise intensity. We speculate that the significant CV health effects with lower metabolic demand from TC may attribute to the additional cognitive component such as mental relaxation or "Qi"-related mental activity. For mental health benefits of TC, up to date, few trials conducted the comparisons with those benefits from walking and among TC practitioners at different proficiency levels. The previous findings to some extent supported that TC may have more benefits on mental health than walking and TC masters gain more mental health benefits than beginners. However, key drawbacks existed in those studies which seriously affect the interpretation of the results, such as short intervention duration, incomparable dropout rate, adoption of measurements non-specifically related to the TC cognitive components, or no report about other potential factors affecting mental health. This project will design two exploratory trials to clarify the research questions. The first trial, with a randomized controlled design, will longitudinally compare the 12-weeks training effects between TC and walking in terms of their cognitive characteristics during performance as well as chronic effects in apparently healthy adults. Secondly, a cross-sectional trial will compare the cognitive characteristics and the mental health among TC practitioners with different proficiency levels. Clarification of the research questions will be useful for TC practitioners to optimize the TC performance to achieve maximum health benefits. 太極拳（TC）是中國和老年人特別廣泛使用的一種中國傳統保健運動，用於維護或改善健康。作為身體鍛煉，TC運動除了常見的招式動作部分外，還具有比普通體育運動更多的認知成分。對於認知部分，實踐中有人建議是關於體內循環“氣”的精神放鬆和認知活動。然而， TC是否比其他類型的有氧運動如走路表現出更為顯著的心理平靜和更多的“氣”相關的心理活動，卻是未研究部份。另外還有一個研究問題是，TC的額外的認知成分是否能夠比沒有認知成分的精神健康益處更多。此外，有興趣的是了解TC實習者的熟練水平是否與表現中的認知特徵以及心理健康狀況相關。幾年前，我們比較了心血管（CV）的健康影響和TC與走路之間的代謝需求，發現運動訓練3個月產生與走路類似的CV健康影響，但TC卻祗需用更低的能量需求和運動強度。我們推測，來自TC的較低代謝需求的顯著的CV健康影響可能歸因於額外的認知成分，如精神放鬆或“氣”相關的心理活動。對於TC的心理健康益處，到目前為止，很少有試驗與不同熟練水平的人士在走路和TC進行了比較。以前的發現在某種程度上支持TC可能比步行和TC在心理健康方面有更多的益處，比初學者獲得更多的精神健康益處。然而，過往研究的主要缺點，包括干預訓練時間短，退出率高，採用與TC認知成分非特異性相關的測量，或沒有關於影響心理健康的其他潛在因素的報告。本研究項目將設計兩項探索性試驗，以澄清研究問題。第一次試驗，採用隨機對照設計，將縱向比較TC和步行之間的12週訓練效果，在表現過程中的認知特徵以及在健康成年人中的慢性影響。其次，橫斷面試驗將比較具有不同熟練程度的TC從業者的認知特徵和心理健康。澄清研究問題將有助於TC從業者優化TC性能以達到最大的健康效益。

14605617.label: Realisation of objectives
14605617.value: The first objective of this study was to compare the cognitive characteristics of Tai Chi and walking exercises in generally healthy middle-aged adults. This objective has been fully achieved from the data collection in the randomized controlled trial. One hundred and two participants were randomly allocated in a 1:1:1 ratio to control group (age: 51±9.7yrs, female: n=24), brisk walking group (age: 54±6.8yrs, female: n=25), and Tai Chi (age: 52±7.1 yrs, female: n=23) group. The cognitive characteristics of Tai Chi and brisk walking exercise were compared before and after the 3-month intervention. The cognitive characteristics were measured by the Trial Making Test (executive function), the Chinese version of Ray’s Auditory Verbal Learning Test (verbal memory), the Stroop Test (cognitive interference and selective attention), and the N-back Test (working memory). Our results showed that three months of Tai Chi improved the completion time in Trail Making Test (list A and B) and response time in N-back Test. In contrast, we observed that three months of brisk walking exercise did not induce any beneficial effect on cognitive function. The second objective is to compare the effectiveness of a 12-week training on mental health between Tai Chi and walking exercises in generally healthy middle-aged adults. This objective has been fully achieved from the data collection in the randomized controlled trial mentioned in objective#1. We have compared the mental health of Tai Chi and brisk walking exercise before and after the 3-month intervention. Mental health was measured by the Profile of Mood States (POMS) questionnaire. We found that Tai Chi alleviated the overall mood state, tension, depression, anger, fatigue, and confusion at the post-intervention (3-month) and follow-up (6-month) assessments compared with the control group. However, no improvement was observed in all mood states after three months of brisk walking exercise. The third objective is to compare cognitive characteristics of Tai Chi exercise among Tai Chi practitioners at different proficiency levels. To achieve this objective, we have recruited 39 participants (age: 67.3±5.5) with varying years of Tai Chi experience: 1) Novice (<1 year of Tai Chi experience; age: 68.4±3.4, n=13), 2) Master (10-30 years of Tai Chi experience; age: 66.5±7.5, n=15), and 3) Top Master (>30 years of Tai Chi experience; age: 67.0±4.7,n=11). The cognitive characteristics were assessed by the Trail Making Test and the Chinese version of Ray’s Auditory Verbal Learning Test. Our results showed that participants in the top master group performed better in Trail Making Test than the novices group participants. However, no group difference was observed in Ray’s Auditory Verbal Learning Test. The fourth objective is to compare the mental health of different proficient Tai Chi practitioners. This objective has been achieved from the data collection in the cross-sectional study mentioned in objective#3. We have compared the mental health among the participants with different Tai Chi experiences. Mental health was assessed by the POMS questionnaire, with a higher score indicating a higher level of negative mood. Our results showed that participants in the master group have lower scores in global mood state, tension, anger, and confusion than those in the novices group. We also observed a trend of lower fatigue (p=0.09) and confusion (p=0.07) scores in the top master group compared with the novices group.

14605617.label: Major findings and research outcome
14605617.value: In Part I of the project, a randomized controlled trial was conducted to compare the effectiveness of Tai Chi (TC) for improving cognitive function, mental health, and physical health among healthy middle-aged adults versus walking (WALK) and control (CON) groups. Out of 129 initial participants, 85 completed the pre-, post-, and follow-up assessments (n=26, 32, 27, respectively). Two-way repeated measure ANCOVA (age and gender as covariates) revealed significant interaction effects in multiple mood states, including total mood score (p<0.001), tension (p<0.001), depression (p<0.001), anger (p<0.001), fatigue (p<0.01), and confusion (p<0.001). The post-hoc analysis found that TC group exhibited significantly lower mood states (p<0.05) than CON at post- and follow-up assessments. Significant interactions were observed in the Trail Making Test (list A and B) and response time in the N-back test (0-back and 2-back). Post-hoc analysis revealed that the TC demonstrated significantly faster (p<0.05) than CON at post-intervention in both measurements. Significant interaction effect in the Trail Making Test (list B) was found only between pre- and post-intervention. The Trail Making Test (list B) tended to be reduced in TC as compared to CON (p=0.07) and WALK (p=0.09). In part II of this project, another 39 age-matched TC practitioners (age: 67.3±5.5) with different years of TC proficiency: Novices (<1 year; age: 68.4±3.4, n=13), Masters (10-30 years; age: 66.5±7.5, n=15), and Top Masters (>30 years; age: 67.0±4.7, n=11); were recruited in the cross-sectional comparison. Results revealed that the Masters scored lower in global mood state, tension, anger, and confusion than Novices. The trends of lower fatigue (p=0.09) and confusion (p=0.07) were found in Top Masters compared with the Novices. The top master performed better in Trail Making Test than the novices. No group difference was observed in Ray’s Auditory Verbal Learning Test. Remark: Two peer-reviewed publications were generated: a review article and a conference abstract. In the review article, we apologized that the RGC funding support was not acknowledged due to the negligence of our post-doc fellow who handled the communication with the journal editor. By the time the article was published, our post-doc fellow had left the University already, and we were not able (or too late) to follow up with the editor about the funding acknowledgement For the conference abstract, the RGC funding was acknowledged during the conference presentation (see attached pdf).

14605617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14605617.value: Our results from the randomized controlled trial and cross-section study suggested that Tai Chi has more health benefits on mood and some cognitive domains (i.e., executive function and working memory) than aerobic exercise. However, the current evidence is only limited to healthy middle-aged adults. The effect of Tai Chi on patients with a mood disorder or cognitive decline remains unknown. It is warranted to conduct a long-term, large-scale study to confirm the favorable effects of Tai Chi on other clinical population (depression, anxiety, bipolar disorder, mild cognitive impairment, or dementia).

14605617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14605617.value: This project contains a randomized controlled trial and a cross-sectional study. Our randomized controlled trial revealed that three months of Tai Chi intervention significantly improved cognitive function (i.e., executive function and working memory) and mood state (i.e., global mood states, tension, depression, anger, fatigue, and confusion) in healthy middle-aged adults. Therefore, compared with aerobic exercise (i.e., brisk walking), mind-body exercise (i.e., Tai Chi) demonstrated a better training effect on cognitive function and mental health. Furthermore, our cross-sectional study showed that participants with 10 to 30 years of Tai Chi experience have better mood states (i.e., global mood states, tension, anger, and confusion) than participants with less than one year of Tai Chi experience. We also find that participants with more than 30 years of Tai Chi experience have better executive function than those with less than one year of Tai Chi experience. In conclusion, our results demonstrated that Tai Chi effectively improves cognitive function and mental health among middle-aged adults. Additional research is needed to verify the effects of Tai Chi among the population with cognitive decline and mental disorders.

14605717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14605717.value: 目的 妄想指即使出現矛盾的證據亦不會改變的錯誤信念。據統計，25-64％的普通人群存在非臨床程度的妄想觀念，且情況隨時間發展起伏不定。本研究項目之目的是探討妄想觀念如何隨時間而發展，並探索與妄想發展相關的風險因素。 項目背景 早期有關妄想的研究大多聚焦在精神病患者身上，他們已出現了精神上的痛苦和一系列神經認知功能障礙。因此，研究妄想形成的最佳時機是精神病發病前，亦即妄想症狀產生之前。其次，以前的研究主要集中於精神病的發展軌跡，並假設精神病症狀有著相似的演變。然而，這說法未必正確。妄想包括三個可以互相區分，並且不會同時變化的層面（即其確定性、其情緒困擾性、及其揮之不去的程度），三者分別與不同的風險因素相關聯。理論上，一些心理機制導致妄想思維的形成，當中推理偏見和妄想的確定性，擔憂的過程與妄想的其情緒困擾性／揮之不去的程度之間皆存在特定的關係。這項研究將考慮到妄想的多維性質，並檢驗以下假設：上述心理機制將區分哪些人士的妄想將持續發展至嚴重程度，甚至可能導致思覺失調的出現；哪些人士的妄想觀念將維持在非臨床水平，不會繼續惡化。 項目簡述 基線樣本將包含1,420名無個人和家族精神病史的成年人。被抽樣而且有妄想經歷的人士（即在妄想量表中至少有一種妄想觀念）將被跟進18個月（N = 355）。我們將於基線，6個月，12個月和18個月量度三個妄想層面（確定性、情緒困擾性、及揮之不去的程度），並使用潛在類別分析 (latent class analysis) 確定其各自的軌跡。我們假設三個妄想維度在18個月內的發展軌跡與機能和情緒轉變有關。更重要的是，我們預測基線時間的推理偏見將可預測妄想確定性的變化，而基線時間的擔憂過程將能預測妄想的情緒困擾性和揮之不去程度的變化。 項目重要性 如果本研究能夠證明所假設的心理機制在妄想形成過程中的作用，由於前人的研究已經證明針對這些機制的干預措施有效，這項研究將有極大的可能促進妄想的早期識別和預防。

14605717.label: Realisation of objectives
14605717.value: Objective 1: This study consisted of a screening phase and a longitudinal phase. The screening phase involved an online survey of a large community-based young adult sample. A subsample entered the longitudinal phase, which consisted of four assessment timepoints (baseline, 6 months, 12 months, and 18 months). As proposed, the research team recruited young adults from the general population of Hong Kong via various sources. The majority of the sample was recruited via Qualtrics market research panel service (stratified by age, district of residence, and education level). We also sampled via advertising in public places, educational institutions, and social media (e.g. Facebook and Instagram). Individuals who reported a current or previous psychiatric disorder were excluded. The resultant sample consisted of 2595 participants at the screening phase. Among the screened participants, 2187 (84.3%) endorsed at least one delusional ideation and provided a pool of participants for random selection into the longitudinal phase. This high prevalence rate added to the existing literature that delusional ideation is commonly experienced by non-patients in the general community. As proposed, we selected around 355 participants for the longitudinal study, and the sample sizes for each assessment timepoint were as follows: Baseline (n = 356), 6 months (n = 341), 12 months (n = 354), and 18 months (n = 343). We adopted a 2-step validity check procedure. After removing invalid responses, a total of 352, 338, 329, and 330 responses remained at the four timepoints respectively. Based on previous studies that supported delusional dimensions as distinct, we performed latent class growth analyses (LCGA) on the three dimensions separately. For each of the three dimensions (conviction, distress, and preoccupation), four-group linear models were identified respectively – high stable (Class 1), moderate stable (Class 2), moderate decreasing (Class 3), and low stable (Class 4). Class composition appears to be more comparable between the distress and preoccupation models, but more distinct for the conviction model. Although our community-based sample did not yield an increasing group, it was intriguing that among the 356 participants who endorsed at least one delusional ideation at baseline, the majority belonged to the high stable or moderate stable classes on the three dimensions (Conviction: 81.5%; Distress: 61.2%; Preoccupation: 72.8%). Objective 2: Levels of emotional and functional outcomes were compared across classes within the same dimension using the three-step approach described in Bolck et al (2004). Overall, for each of the three LCGA models, the four respective classes differed significantly on the emotional and functional outcomes at 18 months. Seven out of nine pairwise comparisons revealed the same pattern of differences, where Class 1 had the worst outcomes, followed by Class 2, and then Classes 3 and 4 which did not differ between each other. In other words, the high/moderate stable classes exhibited significantly worse emotional and functional outcomes at 18 months than the other two classes. Within the class that was ‘high stable’ on conviction, 35.2% and 34.4% were at least moderately depressed and anxious respectively. Within the class that was ‘high stable’ on distress, 38.2% and 46.9% were at least moderately depressed and anxious respectively. Within the class that was ‘high stable’ on preoccupation, 55.2% and 43.6% were at least moderately depressed and anxious respectively. These classes also displayed a level of functional impairment greater than Andrews et al (2009)’s clinical norm scores. This is consistent with previous evidence that, despite a lack of a psychiatric diagnosis, individuals experiencing delusional ideation are subject to distress and functional impairment (Kelleher et al., 2015; Navarro-Mateu et al., 2017). Objective 3: Hypotheses 3 and 4 were tested by multinomial logistic regression with latent classes as dependent variables and baseline cognitive and affective processes as independent variables using Vermunt’s (2010) 3-step approach. Hypothesis 3 was partially supported. Reasoning biases (belief inflexibility and jumping-to-conclusions [JTC] biases) were measured at baseline. Although there was a trend for belief flexibility to be reduced in the persistently deluded groups, the group differences did not reach statistical significance. The finding that Classes 1 and 2 (within the Conviction model) had a milder jumping-to-conclusions bias than Class 4 is even counter-intuitive. However, such differences would not survive correction for multiple testing. Secondly, although there is robust evidence for extreme JTC bias among patients with delusions (McLean et al., 2016; So et al., 2016), whether delusion-prone individuals also share the same bias is less consistent. Therefore, it remains a possibility that while an extreme JTC bias may be linked to the presence of clinical delusions, there may not be a linear relationship between JTC and delusionality along the symptomatic continuum. Objective 4: Hypothesis 4 was supported. Worry and meta-worry were measured at baseline. Within each LCGA model, the Class 3 (moderate decreasing) represented a recovering group who was particularly interesting, as it was closer to Class 2 (moderate stable) at the beginning but closer to Class 4 (low stable) at the end of the study period. What differentiates Class 3 from Class 2 would, therefore, be of clinical significance. In particular, Classes 2 and 3 in the Distress model differed on worry and meta-worry, with the moderate stable class exhibiting more worry and meta-worry at baseline than the moderate decreasing class. In fact, worry and meta-worry systematically differentiated the decreasing/recovering groups from the persistently deluded groups across all three LCGA models. Therefore, even though delusional dimensions are conceptually separable and emerge as distinct in factor analyses (Kendler et al., 1983; Sharp et al., 1996), they are nonetheless inter-related, and interventions targeting worry-related processes are likely to lead to reduction across multiple dimensions of delusional ideation (Foster et al., 2010; Freeman et al., 2015). In sum, the project was fully completed, and all objectives have been achieved. The above results have been presented in conferences and written up as a journal article which is under review by Journal of Psychopathology and Clinical Science (formerly Journal of Abnormal Psychology).

14605717.label: Major findings and research outcome
14605717.value: Background It has been argued that what differentiates delusional ideation from full-blown delusions (indicating need for care) is not the number of beliefs, but the experiential dimensions such as conviction, distress, and preoccupation. However, how these dimensions evolve over time and affect outcomes is under-researched. While delusional conviction and distress are associated with reasoning biases and worry respectively in clinical samples, how these processes predict trajectories of delusional dimensions in the general population remains unclear. Method Young adults (age 18-30) were screened for delusional ideation on the Peters et al. Delusions Inventory. Participants with at least one delusional ideation were randomly selected for a 4-wave assessment (6-month apart). Trajectories of delusional dimensions were separately identified by latent class growth analyses, then compared on baseline levels of jumping-to-conclusions bias, belief inflexibility, worry, and meta-worry. Results The longitudinal sample consisted of 356 individuals (drawn from a community sample of 2187). For each of the three dimensions (conviction, distress, and preoccupation), four-group linear models were identified – high stable, moderate stable, moderate decreasing, and low stable. The high/moderate stable groups exhibited worse emotional and functional outcomes at 18 months than the other two groups. Worry and meta-worry predicted group differences, and notably differentiated the moderate decreasing groups from the moderate stable groups. Contrary to hypothesis, jumping to conclusions bias was milder in the high/moderate stable groups than the low stable group for conviction. Conclusions Distinct trajectories of delusional dimensions were predicted by worry and meta-worry. Differences between the decreasing and stable groups carried clinical implications.

14605717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14605717.value: Apart from the main objectives, we also addressed other research questions concerning loneliness and psychosis using the baseline data only. Three journal articles have been completed (1 published, 1 accepted, and 1 under review). With the longitudinal trajectories of delusional ideation being identified, we can conduct a follow-up study on putative psychological mechanisms comparing these groups, through methods such as experience sampling or experimental induction. Alternatively, psychological interventions targeting worry can be tested on the individuals who are prone to delusional conviction, distress, or preoccupation.

14605717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14605717.value: As the presence and worsening of delusional ideation substantially increases the risk for subsequent incidence of clinical psychosis, comparing the improving and worsening trajectories of delusional ideation at the non-clinical stage informs our understanding of delusional formation. This project followed 356 young adults (drawn from a pool of 2595 participants) for a period of 18 months. We found that endorsement of a delusional ideation is common. A substantial proportion of these individuals reported a stably high level of conviction, distress, or preoccupation associated with delusional ideations over time, which typically led to emotional disturbances and functional impairment. Therefore, it is imperative that early detection and intervention is in place for these individuals even though a full-blown psychiatric disorder has not yet emerged. We also found that the longitudinal trajectories were differentiated by worry and meta-worry, i.e. with the stable group exhibiting more worry and meta-worry than the decreasing/improving group. As persistence of delusional ideation was predicted by a tendency to worry, psychological intervention targeting worry processes may be helpful in curtailing the maintenance of delusional ideation in non-clinical individuals.

14605817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14605817.value: The aim of this research project is to better understand global information flows, in particular to what extent they are constrained by borders on the internet, by analyzing how internet platforms manage the internet including its relationship with governments, the myriad of laws and regulations seeking to control the internet, as well as its relationship with its users. The internet has led to a revolution in free expression. Critical is the global and borderless character of the internet, realizing to a large extent Article 19’s ideal of a world where: “Everyone has the right to freedom of opinion and expression; this right includes freedom to hold opinions without interference and to seek, receive and impart information and ideas through any media and regardless of frontiers.” However, governments around the world are ramping up their efforts to control what information can enter or exit their borders. These efforts go beyond traditional censorship, and include regulations such as internet jurisdiction, data protection, data localization and intermediary liability. At the same time, the enforcement of these regulations often depends on how the internet platforms decide to engage with them. This project asks: How do the global internet platforms strategically manage and make sense of the internet landscape, including its relationship with various governments, the laws, regulations and trade agreements seeking to control information flows and what implications, as well as its relationship with its users? What implications does the way internet platforms practice their craft have for the free flow of information? For example, how do the global internet platforms decide where to localize and which local law to comply with? This project sees the major internet platforms as critical agents in the shaping of the future of the open and global internet. Treating free expression and the open internet as a process and dynamics of political economy implies that this process can be influenced and shaped. More importantly, this framework highlights the importance of state and market actors and their relationship in the negotiation and contestation of the future of the open internet and free expression. 這項研究旨在加深了解全球信息流動，著眼點是互聯網世界裡的邊界對信息流動的限制程度。研究途徑是分析互聯網平台管理互聯網的方式，包括它們怎樣管理跟政府、跟企圖控制互聯網的法律和法規、以及跟用家的關係。 互聯網為言論自由帶來革命，關鍵在於互聯網覆蓋全球和無邊界的特質。互聯網很大程度地實現了《世界人權宣言》第十九條的理想世界：「人人有權享受主張和發表意見的自由；此項權利包括持有主張而不受干涉的自由，和通過任何媒介和不論國界尋求、接受和傳遞消息和思想的自由。」可是，世界各國的政府正加大力度控制信息進出它們的邊界，著力點不限於傳統審查，還包括例如互聯網管轄權、資料保障、資料在地化、中介責任等法規。同時，互聯網平台怎樣看待這些法規，也影響著法規的執行。 這項研究尋求解答：在各政府、法律、法規、貿易協議等等企圖控制互聯網的情況下，全球互聯網平台採用甚麼策略去理解及管理互聯網內的地理環境呢？ 這對用家層面帶來怎樣的影響呢？互聯網平台的應對手段對信息的自由流動又帶來怎樣的影響呢？例如，全球互聯網平台怎樣決定在哪裡進行在地化、以及遵守哪裡的本地法律呢？ 這項研究計劃把主要互聯網平台視為關鍵能動者，關係著全球開放式互聯網的未來。在政治經濟學的框架下，把言論自由和開放式互聯網視作一種過程和互動關係，意味著這個過程是可以被影響和塑造的。更重要的是，這個框架能突顯國家和市場的重要角色，以及它們在談判及角力場上的關係，為開放式互聯網及言論自由帶來一個怎樣的未來。
