14616617.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14616617.value: 食品及飲用水安全危機中的公眾風險感知、制度信任及危機傳播

14616617.label: Project Objectives
14616617.value: To theorize a comparative model of Chinese crisis communication, risk, and institutional trust to understand how crises in three Chinese societies reach resolution. To illustrate the interaction of public and organizational perspectives during food-safety crises and to reveal any gaps between them. To reveal Hong Kong’s native CCS and to develop practical guidelines for both government regulators and crisis managers in private sector.
rows: To theorize a comparative model of Chinese crisis communication, risk, and institutional trust to understand how crises in three Chinese societies reach resolution.
To illustrate the interaction of public and organizational perspectives during food-safety crises and to reveal any gaps between them.
To reveal Hong Kong’s native CCS and to develop practical guidelines for both government regulators and crisis managers in private sector.

14616617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14616617.value: In the past two decades, food-safety crises have increased public risk concern and weakened public trust in official policies in Greater Chinese societies. Such crises range from contaminated infant milk powder, rotten McDonald’s burger, to recent lead-contaminated water crises. More citizens have expressed widespread concern over food safety, especially for crises that threaten the vulnerable group of younger generation. The three Chinese societies have seen not only a disturbance of public institutional trust in the food industry but doubts about institutional competence and regulatory credibility. Beck (1992) and Fukuyama (1995) attribute high-risk, low-trust societies like modern Mainland China with weak potential for effective communications. The general Chinese public gradually lost institutional trust not only in the food products at the heart of a particular crisis but also in the media, government, and even society as a whole. The following questions merit examination but have received relatively little research: How do Chinese publics in each of the region perceive food-related risk? To what extent is trust at different levels (the targeted organization, central government, regulatory, and media) and of various dimensions expressed by the Chinese publics? How do the Chinese authorities and organizations respond to crises? How do Chinese the publics perceive these organizations’ communications practices? What gaps of perceived crisis communications, if any, exist between publics and organizations in a Chinese context? What are the relative predictive powers of perception, institutional trust, and crisis response in terms of risk acceptance/aversion? Against this background, this study proposes to conduct public polls and thematic analysis of organizational CCS, in order to depict the interrelations and impacts of risk perception, institutional trust, and crisis responses on public attitudes of risk acceptance/aversion in three Chinese societies situated under different legal, political and media systems. The comparative approach is empirically grounded on the notion of three models of media and politics developed by Hallin and Mancini (2004). This study would compare the data collected from Mainland China as a case of “polarized political model” (Sparks, 2006), from Hong Kong as a “democratic corporatist model,” and from Taiwan as a “liberal model.” In a nutshell, this study aims to (1) advance theoretical development in the study of risk, institutional trust, and crisis communication; (2) enhance cultural and contextual sensitivity; (3) revitalize a holistic methodological approach in crisis communication scholarship; (4) and provide practical crisis communication guidelines to public policy-makers and local businesses. 近年來，食品安全危機在大中華地區引起公眾廣泛的風險意識，並削弱了公眾對制度的信任。從毒奶粉事件、麥當勞食品過期，以至最近的食水含鉛危機，公眾對於食品及飲用水的安全更為關注，尤其擔心相關危機為弱勢及年輕一代所帶來的風險。在三個華人社會 (香港、中國內地、台灣) ，公眾不但對飲食業的信心下降，更質疑相關監管機構及制度的能力及可信性。因此，本研究旨於： 1. 建構一個華人比較危機傳播、風險及制度信任的理論模型，了解三個華人社會中的危機如何得以解決； 2. 分析食品及飲用水安全危機中的公眾及組織互動，探究當中是否存在漏洞； 3. 為香港本地的政府監管機構及企業的危機管理者提出可行的危機傳播策略及實際的風險管理建議。

14616617.label: Realisation of objectives
14616617.value: During the research period, all three objectives were achieved. 1. Theorize a comparative model of Chinese crisis communication, risk, and institutional trust to understand crisis resolution in three Chinese societies. In order to model crisis/risk communication and institutional trust, the PI constructed a Trust-Risk-Behavior Framework by adopting the Causal Chain model. In order to construct a theoretical framework, PI and the research team first identified several key concepts: institutional trust (ability, benevolence, and integrity), risk perception (cognitive and affective), risk acceptance and behavioral intention (use intention and word-of-mouth intention). In this study, we targeted three Chinese societies: Hong Kong, Taiwan, and Mainland China. To test the proposed framework, researchers conducted online surveys in these regions. Results were as follows: 1) institutional trust significantly predicts risk perception, risk acceptance, and behavioral intention; 2) risk perception and risk acceptance mediate institutional trust and behavioral intention; 3) the mediation effect of risk acceptance is stronger than the mediation effect of risk perception. This theoretical framework could benefit decision makers and strengthen policies. Moreover, the research project is cross-regional by design in an effort to illuminate the distinct crisis-management styles among three Chinese societies and equip practitioners in Hong Kong, Taiwan, and mainland China with the cultural sensitivity necessary for navigating crisis events in Chinese regions outside of their own. 2. Illustrate the interaction of public and organizational perspectives during food-safety crises and reveal any gaps between them. An overall picture of the crisis/risk communication scenarios in three Chinese societies emerged from this study’s examination of the interplay between public and organizational perspectives. This advances discussion of effective crisis/risk communication strategies when communicating with the public. A multiple case-study model was adopted (Huang, Choy, Wang, & Lu, 2019). Incorporating perspectives from Situational Crisis Communication Theory (SCCT) (Coombs, 1995; 2007) and the IDEA model (Sellnow et al., 2015), this study proposed a multiple stakeholder perspective incorporating different social actors’ risk and crisis narratives. We extended organization-centric crisis communication theories by accounting for social interaction between governmental crisis-response strategies and the risk and crisis narratives of non-governmental stakeholders. Specifically, this study investigated distinct types of risk and crisis narratives as depicted in different online media platforms (microblogs, news media, and search engines). 3. Reveal Crisis Communicative Strategy (CCS) native to Hong Kong and develop practical guidelines for both government regulators and corporate crisis managers. Through thematic analysis of official press releases and social media posts about imported food from Fukushima, we found that government agencies in Hong Kong and Taiwan communicated directly with the public, while officials in mainland China targeted local governments and industry. We identified institutional trust as the most important antecedent for predicting the public’s behaviour. This suggests that more research should be conducted on trust management. While risk perception typically depends on specific issues, institutional trust is specific to organizations. Therefore government agencies and corporations facing crises should not simply focus on the risk or crisis at hand but should cultivate institutional trust continuously with public constituencies in order to mitigate the impacts of crises that have not yet occurred. Moreover, we conducted a semantic analysis that identified two instructional strategies: explanation-focused buffering strategy and personalization-focused bridging strategy. The former significantly heightened cognitive risk perception and reduced affective risk perception, while personalization-focused bridging strategy sustained risk acceptance and behavioural intentions. Therefore instructional messaging should be tailored to regulatory organizations’ communication strategies and goals. In addition to these three objectives, the PI expanded the research and has been conducting a study on risk/health communication in the context of COVID-19 using the GRF project as a baseline. The COVID-19 research, which also focuses on three Chinese societies, confirmed the importance of institutional trust in risk communication. Preliminary results illustrated that trust in government can predict COVID-19 vaccination intention. This generated policy suggestions to counter COVID-19 vaccine hesitancy (see https://bit.ly/3xwzLFC for more details) that have been reported on by several Hong Kong media outlets such as Headline Daily, Apple Daily, BBC News, Sing Tao Daily, Wen Wei Po, etc. To conclude, this project provides a theoretical model for crisis/risk communication as well as practical guidelines for government regulators and corporate crisis managers. Foremost, this project outlines the importance of institutional trust in crisis/risk communication. Further, the study was conducted in three Chinese societies (i.e., Mainland China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan), thereby strengthening and cross-validating the findings. To realize the research objectives, two cases were initially identified: tainted food imported from Fukushima and Changchun Changsheng Bio-technology Company’s substandard vaccine. After an extensive literature review on crisis/risk communication, we adopted several theories and models for this study, including the IDEA model (Sellnow et al., 2015), the Causal Chain model (Earle, 2010; Siegrist, 1999), and the Dual-Process model of risk perception (Slovic & Peters, 2006). Then we constructed a conceptual model and tested it with case studies, thematic analysis, semantic analysis, and online surveys. We also expanded the research context to traffic accidents to further consolidate prior findings. Concrete deliverables include: -One journal paper published in Journal of Public Management (Chinese journal, CSSCI listed; Impact Factor: 7.410) -Six manuscripts have been submitted to SSCI journals and are currently under review, two of which have recently received Revise & Resubmit requests. -Five recognized international conference papers presented at the International Communication Association Annual Conference and the International Association for Media and Communication Research Annual Conference.

14616617.label: Major findings and research outcome
14616617.value: 1. Institutional trust plays an important antecedent role in risk/crisis communication outcomes by shaping the public’s risk perception, risk acceptance, and behavioral intention. 2. Issue politicization moderates institutional trust and risk perception/acceptance. 3. Media representations of risk and crisis issues vary across three Chinese societies. 4. Different strategies demonstrated differential impacts on risk perception and acceptance. Researchers studied several crisis/risk contexts to provide a stronger framework and suggestions for governmental and private sector decision makers. Through a combination of thematic analysis and quantitative methods (semantic analysis, online surveys, and online experiments), crisis/risk communication strategies in three Chinese societies were identified. This project generated theoretical and practical improvements for crisis/risk communication effectiveness (Huang, Choy, Wang, & Lu, 2019; Huang, Wang, Fong, & Wu, 2019). Adopting Causal Chain (Earle, 2010; Siegrist, 1999) and Dual-Process models of risk perception (Slovic and Peters, 2006), researchers for this study explored relationships among institutional trust, risk perception, risk acceptance, and behavioural intention in two health-related contexts (food imported from Fukushima and a substandard vaccine). Institutional trust demonstrated both direct and indirect effects on behavioural intention through risk perception and risk acceptance. Additionally, institutional trust more strongly predicted cognitive risk perception than affective risk perception. The mediation effect of risk acceptance was stronger than that of risk perception, confirming the importance of institutional trust in predicting risk assessment (Huang, Fong, Wang, & Wu, 2019; Huang, Wang, Fong, & Wu, under review). Fong, Huang, Wang, & Wu (2019) reinforced the importance of institutional trust in their examination of how interaction between perceived politicization and institutional trust influenced risk assessment in the context of nuclear contamination. Contradictory crisis interpretations proposed by political actors with various self-interests tend to confuse public constituents. The more trustworthy an institution is (in terms of ability, benevolence and integrity), the more likely publics will rely on its official interpretations in the midst of conflicting information. Wang & Huang (under review) conducted semantic network analysis of mass media and online searches to illuminate the crisis/risk understanding gap between scientific experts and the public during a food-safety crisis. This study found that media representations of the Fukushima food imports crisis differed across media sources and socio-political contexts (in Hong Kong, Taiwan, and mainland China), contextual factors that also affected public opinion. Regulatory authorities might use such findings to inform food-safety decisions, while corporate and civic PR efforts might develop more context-sensitive approaches to crisis management.

14616617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14616617.value: The PI will continue to focus on the field of crisis/risk communication, particularly the analysis of institutional trust and risk perception during public health emergencies. The conceptual framework and findings of this GRF project provide a helpful departure point for further validity tests within the context of the COVID-19 pandemic. Second, the PI identified a number of underexplored questions. For instance, the GRF project revealed that institutional trust is a multifaceted concept that plays a critical role in crisis/risk communication. A potential study might explore which dimensions of institutional trust are more influential in shaping behavioural intentions. Further, the PI has identified a need for a comprehensive index to measure societal trust levels. Methodologically, this GRF study relied on self-reported data (e.g., online surveys). Use of larger and different data sets could provide opportunities for elaboration and cross-validation of these ideas in the PI’s future research activity. To make these future research opportunities a reality, the PI has applied for several competitive external research grants seeking funding. Moreover, the PI has been planning to submit a new proposal for this year’s GRF application.

14616617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14616617.value: Crisis and risk are increasingly ubiquitous worldwide. Decision makers struggle with how best to effectively mitigate emerging crises and effectively communicate with the public about them. Although much research on crisis communication exists, Chinese societies are rarely studied. This research project focused on three Chinese societies (i.e., Hong Kong, Taiwan, and mainland China) and two public health crises (Fukushima food imports and distribution of a substandard vaccine). Researchers constructed a comparative framework containing institutional trust, risk perception, risk acceptance, and behavioural intention. Institutional trust was found to be the most powerful factor contributing to public compliance. By unfolding the relationship between and among these key variables, researchers suggest possible modifications to policy and regulatory strategies in both the public and private sectors.

14616917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14616917.value: Innovation plays a critical role in sustainable economic growth and social development, and frame-breaking innovations often result from cross-disciplinary collaborations. Nonetheless, collaborations across disciplines are difficult because each discipline has its established culture. Success in cross-disciplinary collaborations requires knowledge workers to cross cultural boundaries. As such, based on our past research and the recent advances in cultural psychology theories, we propose that having a polyculturalist mindset can promote cross-disciplinary collaborations, both in terms of the innovation outcomes measured in terms of originality and feasibility, and in terms of quality of collaboration. A polyculturalist mindset is the tendency to view a discipline as a continually evolving tradition through constant interactions with other disciplines. In contrast, having a culturalist mindset, or the tendency to view a discipline as independent and historically stable intellectual tradition can hinder the development of cross-disciplinary collaborations. We propose a series of 4 studies to systematically answer two questions. First, What are the consequences of activating the polyculturalist or culturalist mindset on both the innovation outcomes and the quality of collaboration in cross-disciplinary teams? Second, Will having a polyculturalist mindset benefit creative performance only when the situation favors interdisciplinary collaboration or will its benefits be most pronounced when the situational support for interdisciplinary research is relatively weak. 突破性的創新在可持續經濟增長和社會發展中起著至關鍵的作用。突破性的創新往往是跨學科合作的結果。然而，跨學科的合作是困難的，因為每個學科都有其既定的文化。跨學科合作的成功取決於參與者對跨越文化界限的能力。因此，根據我們以往的研究和文化心理學理論的最新進展，我們認為，具有多元文化主義思想的人，無論是在創意成果或與隊員合作質量上，都有良好成果。多元文化觀念通過與其他學科的不斷互動，將學科視為不斷發展的傳統。相反，具有文化主義思想的人， 往往會將學科視為獨立的知識傳統。這樣的概念會阻礙跨學科合作的發展。 我們提出一系列四項研究來有系統地回答兩個問題。首先，在跨學科團隊的創新成果和合作質量上激活多元文化主義或文化主義思想的後果會是怎樣？第二，多元文化主義會在什麼時候發揮最大益處？是當機制支持相對弱時或機制支持相對強時其效應會顯著？

14617117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14617117.value: 二十世紀三十年代，國民政府推行了一系列的計劃，藉此統一政權、帶動經濟和加強愛國情懷，其中的計劃包括新生活運動和東南交通的建設。遊覽中國名勝被視為愛國的活動，可以體現和實踐「生活藝術化」。此時，經濟民族主義和國族建構等議題被納入旅遊產業的論述。在這過程中傳統山水美學和藝術表述備受重視，更被視為最適合表現中國名勝的視覺語言。本研究建基於大量的原始材料，包括繪畫、照片、地方志、山志、旅遊指南、雜誌及報紙，藉此討論旅遊產業與名勝的視覺表述之間密不可分的關係。本計劃分為兩部份。第一部份研究民國時期被視為是中國東南最具代表性的名勝黃山、雁蕩山和天台山，以及重構名勝商品化和國族化的過程；第二部份分析大量與名勝相關的視覺材料，藉此深入了解視覺文化在建構國族和名勝進程中所扮演的重要角色。

14617517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14617517.value: The relations between peasants and the government have changed dramatically in the reform-era China. Peasants have routinely mounted collective protests to make claims to the government. Why do some collective protests demonstrate strong solidarity while others suffer a severe tendency toward fragmentation and mistrust? This project will account for the variations in the solidarity and trust among peasants in collective actions. A central hypothesis in this project is that the micro-structure of contention has a significant impact on the variation in group solidarity and trust. Micro-structure of contention refers to the number and types of actors in the collective bargaining and the types of resources involved in the contention. I posit that protesters are more likely to maintain strong solidarity and trust in direct contention between a social group and the government with few other actors or divisible material resources involved. For example, peasant protests on excessive burdens often witnessed strong solidarity and trust. This is partly because in such protests peasants directly made claims to the government and focused their claims on government responsibilities. With a combination of in-depth interviews and surveys conducted in ten selected villages in Hunan province, the project will examine the tendency toward fragmentation and the trust between protest leaders and rank-and-file villagers. Case studies will pay considerable attention to the mechanisms for solidarity and trust to change. Solidarity and trust among protesters often have a tremendous impact on the trajectory and outcomes of the collective actions. This project can therefore help to answer several fundamental questions about the regime stability in China: how does the state maintain political domination over peasants in China? How and to what extent are peasant interests accommodated in the political system? Will peasant protests evolved into regime-threatening movements? The project will not only shed light on the changing state-peasant relations in China, but also improve the conceptualization and theorization on popular collective action among a variety of social groups in China. Although studies on popular contention in China have been growing very fast in recent years, few of them have examined the variation in the dynamics and patterns of mass mobilization and government response. This project will fill this gap. The project will also contribute to general theories on social movements and contentious politics by looking into how micro-level group-specific political opportunities may shape the dynamics and patterns of popular mobilization, and uncovering mechanisms of mobilization and demobilization. 改革開放以來中國政府和農民的關係發生了巨大變化。農民經常通過集體行動與政府博弈。為什麼他們有時候能保持高度團結而有時候卻為內部分裂和相互猜忌所困呢？本研究項目將對這些差異進行解釋。 本計劃的一個基本假定就是政府民眾之間博弈的微環境會影響民眾動員時的團結和相互信任。具體而言，微環境指參與博弈的成員的數量和性質以及他們所影響到的資源。例如，農民為過重的稅負抗爭時，鬥爭對象集中於地方幹部而依賴於中央或上級權威，從而形成“三明治”式的博弈結構。這種條件下較容易保持團結。而他們為徵地或環境污染等問題抗爭時，不僅針對地方幹部，而且還要與開發商或污染企業做鬥爭，會面臨更多的分化的壓力。 本項目包括在湖南等地進行的田野調查，將結合問卷調查和深度訪談，並結合個案分析和比較研究，尤其注重揭示集體行動中信任與團結程度發生變化的條件和機制。信任和團結是民眾動員過程中的重要方面，影響到集體行動對於社會穩定和政策調整的效果。本研究不僅有助於深化理解和解釋政府民眾之間的博弈，對於抗爭性政治的社會科學理論也將做出貢獻。對於中國抗爭性政治的研究近年來取得了很大進展，但是對於不同政府民眾互動模式的差異及其成因的解釋較為薄弱。本研究將有助於填補這一空白。

14617517.label: Realisation of objectives
14617517.value: All the objectives of this project have been achieved. Through extensive field research in multiple locations, I have acquired rich qualitative and quantitative data on social protests staged by peasants and other social groups such as state workers. The project sheds light on three important aspects of state-society interactions in China. First, it provides a better account for the dynamics of mobilization by peasants on a variety of important issues, such as land taking, environment pollution, excessive fees and taxes. In particular, it highlights the role of village leaders in brokering the interactions between peasants and local governments. Second, by comparing the mobilization by peasants and other social groups, the project improves our understanding of the issue of government corruption in facilitating and constraining social protests in China. Third, the project explores the basic patterns of state response to different types of popular contention. In particular, it sheds light on how the Chinese government has used systematically different strategies to cope with non-civic and civic activism in China. The findings were presented in two international conferences and attracted plenty of attention from scholars on Chinese politics and contentious politics in general. They have been submitted to leading journals in the field.

14617517.label: Major findings and research outcome
14617517.value: The research project has yielded three important findings regarding how political order has been maintained in China in the reform era. First, by examining the role of village leaders in contentious and non-contentious bargaining between peasants and the government, the project underscores how grassroots elites brokered the peasant-government relations. Consequently, policy implementation and law enforcement in the countryside has become more flexible and moderate, and the bargaining relationship between peasants and the government more constructive. Second, the project reveals an oft-overlooked role of the issue of government corruption. Corruption has not only created grievances and therefore incentives for ordinary people to stage protests, but also the momentum of mobilization. As a officially certified issue on which ordinary people can make claim to the government, corruption has often worked as a pivoting issue to sustain the solidarity among protesters. Third, by comparing peasant protests, on the one hand, and feminist protests, on the other, the project contends that the Chinese government has often systematically differentiated civic and non-civic activism. In particularly, the government tends to take a more polarized approach toward civic activism in China.

14617517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14617517.value: This project mainly focuses on the dynamics and solidarity in collective action staged by peasants and other social groups on their private interests. While it touches on the mobilization processes and mechanisms in civic activism, further studies are needed to extend the research to protest movements on public interests. I am applying for a new grant on civic activism in China.

14617517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14617517.value: This project tackles the puzzle why some collective protests in China featured boarder solidarity and stronger dynamic than others. It also sheds light on the question of how regime stability has been maintained in the reform era. As one of the first projects to examine the micro-processes and mechanisms that impact on the dynamics and solidarity in mobilization by peasants and other social groups, this projects reveals the role of grassroots elites in brokering the interactions between peasants and the government and also illuminates how corruption has worked as an issue to sustain solidarity in a protest community. The project has also made an original argument about the differentiation strategies by the Chinese government to cope with civic and non-civic activism.

14617717.label: Realisation of objectives
14617717.value: All project objectives have been achieved. To address the objectives, we compiled a longitudinal dataset containing detailed information on the health lifestyle and socioeconomic conditions spanning 25 year, using data from the Chinese Health and Nutrition Survey. Four papers have been developed. Below we detail how the project objectives were addressed. 1. Document the extent of social gradient in health lifestyle in transitional China, by systematically and rigorously examining an extensive array of health behavior and multiple dimensions of social stratification from childhood to old age The first paper focuses on social disparities in smoking in China, which has not been systematically examined before. This paper is the first to identify diverging trends in smoking in men with different education levels among the post-1980 cohorts; for high-education men, smoking participation consistently declined, but for low-education men, the decline stopped and even reversed. The stagnation in the decline in overall smoking rate since 2010 was mostly due to the stalling of the decline of smoking among low-education men in the most recent cohorts. The diverging trends were a continuation of a general trend in expanding educational gaps in smoking that emerged in the cohorts born after 1960. These findings have important implications for both population health and health disparities. This paper has been presented at a number of conferences and invited talks and is now under review at the International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health. The second paper focuses on an aspect of socioeconomic conditions that is unique to China and has rarely been examined in the study of health lifestyle, which is state sector employment. Using individual-level fixed-effects model, we found that working in the state sector increases men’s drinking frequencies in regions where the marketization level is relatively low. These findings provide evidence for a workplace drinking culture that is unique to the Chinese social context. This paper not only identifies an under-studied social determinant of drinking behavior, but also contributes to an emerging area of study that emphasizes the role of culture in influencing health behavior. The findings also have implications for designing interventions that discourage heavy drinking. We have finished the manuscript and will submit it to a journal within a month. The findings have been presented at this year’s annual conference of the International Chinese Sociological Association. The third paper seeks to assess the social gradient of the health lifestyle, rather than separate health behaviors. Based on the premise that health lifestyle encompasses multiple health behaviors such as diet, smoking, drinking and physical activities and that there is overlapping among different health behaviors, we used latent transition analysis, a relatively novel method, to identify three types of health lifestyle and patterns of changes in health lifestyle during the 25 years of study period. We then examined how baseline socioeconomic conditions are linked to patterns of changes in health lifestyle during the follow-up period. This analysis allows us to examine a composite measure of health lifestyle, which is more efficient than analyzing individual health behaviors and also helps identify previously unknown disparities in health lifestyle. We have finished the statistical analyses and the manuscript is under preparation. We plan to submit the manuscript in two months. 2. Assess the extent to which intergenerational transmission mediates the relationship between socioeconomic relationships and health lifestyle, and whether intergeneration transmission amplifies the social gradient in health lifestyle We conducted analysis assessing how intergenerational transmission of health behavior contributes to the genesis of the social gradient of health lifestyle among children and adolescents. Our analysis first shows that parental body weight and level of physical activities are correlated with children/ adolescents’ body weight and level of physical activities. But this intergenerational transmission of body weight or physical activities do not mediate the relationship between socioeconomic conditions and the two health behaviors among children, mainly because socioeconomic conditions are not linked to the correlation between parental and children’s body weight and physical activities. So the analysis does not offer support to the hypothesis implied in the second objective. Beyond body weight and physical activities, other health behaviors we are concerned with had very low prevalence rates (very few children or adolescents smoked or drank alcohol). We therefore cannot clearly measure intergenerational transmission of these health behavior among children and adolescents. In theory, we can also examine how intergenerational transmission of health behavior contributes to the social gradient of health lifestyle among adults. However, because of the study design, although CHNS spanned 25 years, very few individuals were followed from childhood to adulthood. It is therefore almost impossible to determine how parental health behavior during the formative years of the offspring affects the health behavior of the offspring in adulthood. So we cannot reliably identify intergenerational transmission of health behavior among the adults, which limits our abilities to assess the role of intergenerational transmission of health behavior in social gradient of health lifestyle among adults. We have explored other longitudinal household surveys in China but have not found suitable data sources. 3. Examine the peer effects on health lifestyle in China and assess the extent to which peer effects contribute to the social gradient in health lifestyle To accomplish this objective, we first assess the peer effects on health lifestyle. For rural villages, we constructed indicators of peer health behavior by aggregating the health behavior of other villagers. We then applied a two-step model to estimate the effects of peer health behavior on individuals’ health behavior, accounting for possible endogeneity. However, our analysis found little consistent relationship between peer health behavior and villagers’ health behavior and provided little evidence for peer effects on health lifestyle. Since we have not identified peer effects, we did not go on to examine how peer effects contribute to the social gradient in health lifestyle. The exploration of peer effects, on the other hand, led us to develop the fourth paper, on how the rate of rural-to-urban migration in the village, above and beyond the migration experience in villagers’ immediate households, is connected to the health lifestyle, in particular, drinking behavior and diet, of individual villagers. It is possible that migrants in the villagers’ social environment brought back new ideas about risk and health behavior, which in turn, shapes the villagers’ own health lifestyle. The contextual migration rate can be conceived as a type of peer effects. Moreover, this paper is also related to the first objective. The urban/rural divide has been an important aspect of social stratification in China. This paper illustrates how the health lifestyle of rural residents changed as the urban/rural divide became blurred and more porous. The data analysis has been completed and the manuscript is under preparation. To sum, the findings of this project center on uncovering new patterns of social disparities in health lifestyle and changes in the social disparities. On the other hand, we have not found much evidence for the role of social transmission in the genesis of social gradient in health lifestyle, despite our best efforts, partly due to data limitations. Finally, a PhD student of the PI has been trained in this project. The second and third papers are chapters in her thesis. The fourth paper was developed in collaboration with the student.

14617717.label: Major findings and research outcome
14617717.value: The findings of this project center on uncovering new patterns of social disparities in health lifestyle and patterns of changes in the social disparities. First, we developed a composite measure of health lifestyle and assessed the social gradient in the composite measure, rather than focusing on separate health behavior, as typically has been done in previous research. Based on the premise that health lifestyle encompasses a number of health behaviors such as diet, smoking, drinking and physical activities and that there is overlapping among different health behaviors, we used latent transition analysis, a relatively novel method, and identified three types of health lifestyle: the healthy (avoiding risk behaviors and adopting healthy behaviors), the unhealthy (adopting risk behaviors and avoiding healthy behaviors) and the urbanized (avoiding smoking and drinking but mostly sedentary and adopting an unhealthy diet). We then assessed patterns of changes in health lifestyle during the 25 years of study period, and examined how baseline socioeconomic conditions to the patterns of changes in health lifestyle during the follow-up period. We found that socially and economically disadvantaged individuals were less likely to stay in or transit to the healthy lifestyle during the follow-up period, indicating a widening of socioeconomic gaps in practicing healthful lifestyle. Second, we also examined a specific health behavior that is important to population in China but has not been systematically studied in the research on social disparities in health, namely smoking. Our analysis is the first to identify diverging trends in smoking in men with different education levels among the post-1980 cohorts; for high-education men, smoking participation consistently declined, but for low-education men, the decline stopped and even reversed. The stagnation in the decline in overall smoking rate since 2010 was mostly due to the stalling of the decline of smoking among low-education men in the most recent cohorts. The diverging trends were a continuation of a general trend in expanding educational gaps in smoking that emerged in the cohorts born after 1960. These findings have important implications for both population health and health disparities. Third, we assessed aspects of social stratification that are under-studied in the research on health disparities but are important and unique to the Chinese social context. We first examined state sector employment. Using individual-level fixed-effects model, we found that working in the state sector increases men’s drinking frequencies in regions where the marketization level is relatively low. Moreover, men’s positions in the organizational hierarchy of their workplaces also affect their drinking behavior. These findings provide evidence for a workplace drinking culture that is unique to the Chinese social context. This paper not only identifies an under-studied social determinant of drinking behavior, but also contributes to an emerging area of study that emphasizes the role of culture in influencing health behavior. The findings also have implications for designing interventions that discourage heavy drinking. We also investigated contextual rate of rural-to-urban migration in a village affects the health lifestyle of individual villagers. The urban/rural divide has been an important aspect of social stratification in China. This paper illustrates how the health lifestyle of rural residents changed as the urban/rural divide was becoming blurred and more porous.

14617717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14617717.value: The findings of this project contribute to our understanding of patterns of social disparities in health lifestyle in contemporary China. But how these disparities are formed still remain largely unclear. In this project, we assessed two types of social transmission as possible mechanisms but were unable to provide clear supporting evidence. This project examined individuals’ health lifestyle over the life course and suggested that the adoption of health and risk behaviors typically take place during late teens and early twenties, which were times of important life course transitions, such as going to college, entering the labor market and getting married. Risk behaviors, educational attainment and labor market outcomes interact with one another during early adulthood. How family background and social context shaped these outcomes and the complex interaction among them in China are unclear and is an important future direction of research for me. I have already started to work with a PhD student of mine to examine how family socioeconomic background interact with people’s educational trajectories to influence their adoption of health lifestyle.

14617717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14617717.value: The health lifestyle of the Chinese population has shifted during the recent decades, which partially contributed to a quick rise in the burden of chronic diseases. Although past research has examined some aspects of the relationship between socioeconomic conditions and health lifestyle in China, much remains to be understood. This project focuses on the social gradient in health lifestyle in contemporary China and aims to provide a thorough and rigorous assessment of social stratification of health lifestyle. Furthermore, this project will investigate how social gradient in health lifestyle is formed by focusing on the role of social transmission We used data from a national longitudinal survey spanning 25 years from 1991 to 2015. This project uncovered new patterns of social gradient in health lifestyle and patterns of changes in the social gradient. The findings generally identified widening socioeconomic gaps in health lifestyle, which has important implications for future health disparities and for targeting policy interventions. On the other hand, we have not found much evidence for the role of social transmission in the genesis of social gradient in health lifestyle, despite our best efforts. Future research needs to assess the mechanisms of social disparities in health lifestyle.

14617817.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14617817.value: 儀式、皇權和逾度的美學：重探乾隆朝的宮廷大戲

14617817.label: Project Objectives
14617817.value: To explain the carefully designed representation of imperial power in the “grand plays” of the Qianlong court; To examine to what extent Emperor Qianlong’s Manchu identity influenced the composition and presentation of “grand plays” at court; To explore the interrelationships among these “grand plays”, Emperor Qianlong’s idea of rule, doctrine of loyalty, and his own image-building; To exemplify “the aesthetics of excess” as “spectacle of rule” in “grand plays” at the court of Qianlong; To evaluate the impact of ritual and “excessive” elements in court drama on literati's dramatic composition in eighteenth-century China.

To examine to what extent Emperor Qianlong’s Manchu identity influenced the composition and presentation of “grand plays” at court;

14617817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14617817.value: In eighteenth-century China, during the Qianlong reign (1736-1795), the emperor dictated the construction of three three-tiered stages and the composition of five “grand plays”. Each play includes a total of 240 scenes set on earth, in Heaven or Hell and divided into 10 long books and took 10 days to perform. Based on popular drama “Mulian Rescues His Mother”, and fiction “Journey to the West”, “The Romance of the Three Kingdoms”, “The Water Margin”, and “The Meritorious Book of the Gods”, these refashioned grand plays were characterized by what I call “the aesthetics of excess”, which notably deviates from the principle of “zhonghe” or decorum honored in ancient Han-Chinese tradition. In the last book of the grand play based on “The Water Margin” for example, Song Jiang is shown suffering from severe punishment in Hell not just once but four times with excessive and realistic detail. In another grand play based on “The Three Kingdoms”, nine scenes from Scene 216 onwards are unnecessary from traditional dramatic aesthetic perspective. What meanings did such “excess” have? Did the court’s dramatic aesthetics result from the carefully designed representation of imperial power? How closely were the “grand plays” related to the Qianlong Emperor’s idea of rule and doctrine of loyalty and obedience? In the numerous newly-added episodes of military combats in these plays, can we detect Emperor Qianlong’s insistence on Manchu identity and self-image building? These are some of the issues that scholars of Qing court drama have not yet fully or systematically explored; hence the focal points of my research. By examining the ritual beginnings and endings, the refashioning of the source materials, the repetition and digression in plot, the supernatural elements in battle scenes, the employment of mannequins and mechanisms for physical torture, as well as the recurring theme of retribution in all of the five “grand plays”, I expect to shed new light on court drama and the politics of culture in the Qianlong era. My findings will in turn deepen our understanding of Qing literature as well as Qianlong’s awareness of political instability and historical change. The outcome of this research will be two to four published scholarly articles and presentations at international academic conferences on Qing art, culture, drama, history and literature. In the meantime, I will share my research with students in my undergraduate class and graduate seminar in order to broaden their horizons in classical Chinese drama. 本計劃擬在前人文獻研究的基礎上，以「皇權」、「文治」為主導觀點，對乾隆宮廷大戲予以整體觀照，與清史研究對話；尤其關注乾隆朝宮廷大戲所表現出的「逾度的美學」之政治意涵。通過對文本以及物質（例如宮廷戲台）的細部分析，論證景觀 (spectacle) 與統治 (rule) 的關係，戲劇如何展現與象徵帝國皇權，滿清的民族特性與民族認同如何藉此表現，乾隆如何自我塑造統治形象，而最後宮廷大戲又透過何種機制影響中國文人的戲劇創作。《勸善金科》《昇平寶筏》《封神天榜》《鼎峙春秋》和《忠義璇圖》等五部大戲的編撰與三座三層大戲臺的建造，個人以為是乾隆「文治」大業的重要部分。深具儀典意義的宮廷大戲表演，雖從傳統小說戲曲取材，但表現內容與形式與歷史現實、皇權意識關連密切，意在彰顯威服四海、懷柔遠人、皇權至高無上的大清帝王威嚴，建構聖君形象，強化一統天下的王朝印記。

14617817.label: Realisation of objectives
14617817.value: 由於計劃的研究對象是乾隆朝的五部宮廷大戲：《勸善金科》、《昇平寶筏》、《封神天榜》、《鼎峙春秋》和《忠義璇圖》，每部長達十本240齣，它們所依據的長篇小說和戲曲、所涉及的製作背景如滿人的宗教信仰、乾隆帝的政治觀念、軍事活動，以及宮廷戲臺、服裝砌末的使用等等，都頗為複雜，需要花費大量時間閱讀多種一手材料（例如御製詩文集）融會貫通，難度超出預期，因此，計劃進行至今，我僅正式出版了三篇學術論文，另外完成了一篇論文初稿。 在已刊登的論文中有兩篇曾在美國和內地共四次不同的學術會議上發表。這三篇論文分別針對我稱之為乾隆宮廷大戲的「逾度的美學」風格、宮廷大戲中的帝王形象塑造與皇權呈現，以及清代宮廷戲曲文獻與演劇研究的成果與展望，這三個我認為尤其重要的研究議題做出論述。那篇接近完成的論文初稿，則處理宮廷大戲所體現的滿洲身份認同問題，可與「新清史」研究對話。有鑑於此，在上列五項計劃目標之中，前四項我都可算是順利達成了。唯有第五項目標，我雖已收集了一些零星的材料足以證明宮廷大戲對十八世紀文人戲曲創作的影響，但尚未形成嚴謹的學術性觀點。此為我計劃執行之不足之處。 對於一位計劃評審人曾建議我以專書作為計劃成果事，我念茲在茲，希望今年七月底退休之後，能夠專心一意從事此本專書的寫作。此書的撰寫，因今年春季，我在研究所開設「乾隆宮廷大戲研究」的新課，與十六位中國古典文學、古代文獻和現代文學的博碩生一起，共同探討了上述《勸善金科》等五部大戲的內涵及其相關議題和研究，而有了更為周延的準備與更多元的思考面向。我期望能在兩年內完成此本專書的寫作。

14617817.label: Major findings and research outcome
14617817.value: 本計劃以皇權、文治、兼羅今古為主導觀點，對乾隆宮廷大戲予以整體觀照，尤其關注乾隆朝宮廷大戲所表現出的「逾度的美學」之政治意涵。 計劃從2017年至今，個人的思索研究從未間斷，目前已正式發表的學術論文有三篇，重要的發現如下： （一）關於詞臣張照和《勸善金科》的研究，論證出宗教戲劇（目連救母）在宮廷的政治轉向，並指出《勸善金科》具有樹立一代「王朝戲劇」範型的意義，包括內容方面，描繪了乾隆治下聖君仁政、盛世昇平、八蠻王朝貢的帝國理想；形式方面，在舞臺布景、演員穿戴與大小砌末的設計與運用上，亦呈現出乾隆宫廷以其人力物力之盛、所開啓的戲曲「逾度的美學」風格。（見華瑋：〈儀式、皇權與逾度的美學——重探乾隆宫廷大戲《勸善金科》〉） （二）關於大戲製作與皇權、時事和戲臺的關係，筆者以存世版本眾多的《昇平寶筏》為例，說明了乾隆一代，同名之宮廷大戲會因應時事、君主、戲臺建築由一層到三層的發展而被改編。此劇情節雖源自《西遊記》小說、戲曲，編者卻有意地擴寫、重塑其中的唐太宗角色，以歷史上的「貞觀之治」，作為展示當今聖人御世，「昭代昇平」的重要渠道，藉此向乾隆皇帝及其文治武功致敬。比起乾隆初年張照編纂的「大阪本」，《古本戲曲叢刊九集》所收之《昇平寶筏》（「九集本」）出現了更宏大的排場、更多的神佛人物，也以更令人驚奇的視聽效果，意圖強化此劇所著力表現的頌聖內容。而全劇最後一卷，利用「太宗征頡利」戰事與眾仙護駕、地獄大赦、天界祝頌等盛大場面，將玄奘師徒西天取經事之焦點，一半轉移至唐太宗故事上。有關「九集本」的製作時間，筆者提出很有可能是在乾隆五十七年（1792）平定廓爾喀之後，與弘曆以詩文、圖像記其「十全武功」大約同時。（見華瑋、劉美宜：〈「舊編的唐家貞觀，新演的昭代昇平」：論乾隆宮廷大戲《昇平寶筏》中之唐太宗與皇權〉） （三）關於清代宮廷戲曲文獻與演劇研究的回顧與前瞻，筆者與指導的博士，在綜述前人研究成果後，舉出以下四个方面進行了論述，認為這些在清代宮廷演劇研究上，具有重要的開拓性意義：1. 儀式、民俗與政治：宮廷演劇的「大戲節戲」；2. 日常演戲的審美趣味：崑弋折子戲的宮廷面貌；3. 建築與文本：三層大戲臺與宮廷大戲的創編；4. 政治與美學：宮廷大戲的「逾度的美學」。（見胡光明、華瑋〈清代宮廷戲曲文獻與演劇研究：成果與展望〉）

14617817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14617817.value: （一）清代戲曲研究隨著《全清戲曲》的出版計劃，日益重要；宮廷戲曲作為清代戲曲的重要組成部分，業已受到中外學界的關注。承上所述，筆者將完成計劃專書的寫作（包括深入探討宮廷大戲如何影響十八世紀文人之戲曲創作）。而寫作期間，定會留意清代戲曲研究的最新成果，與之對話，以進一步開拓本計劃的研究視野。 （二）筆者已受邀參加深圳大學高志忠教授2020年度國家社會科學基金重大項目：〈清代宮廷戲劇史科匯編與文獻文物研究〉，負責子課題〈海外藏清宮戲曲文獻搜集整理與研究〉，此將有助於筆者將研究計劃進一步擴展，至海外所藏文獻，且不限於乾隆一代，也不僅限於宮廷「大戲」。

14617817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14617817.value: In eighteenth-century China, during the Qianlong reign (1736-1795), the emperor dictated the construction of three-tiered stages and the composition of five “grand plays”. These refashioned grand plays were characterized by what I call “the aesthetics of excess”, which notably deviates from the principle of “zhonghe” or decorum honoured in ancient Han-Chinese tradition. By examining the ritual beginnings and endings, the refashioning of the source materials, the repetition and digression in plot, the supernatural elements in battle scenes, the employment of mannequins and mechanisms for physical torture, as well as the recurring theme of retribution in all of the five “grand plays”, I have shed new light on court drama and the politics of culture in the Qianlong era. I have published three papers and finished the draft of another paper. And perhaps more significantly, I have taught a seminar to 16 postgraduates on the topic of my current research. From their oral presentations and term papers, I believe this course was a success. Finally, I expect to complete a book on the basis of my research in two years to contribute further to our understanding of Qing court culture as well as Emperor Qianlong’s idea of sovereignty.

14620117.value: 此比較研究旨在獲得對於高等教育中新興的國際化論述、新自由主義下的教育語言政策、以及在兩個政治及社會經濟環境截然不同的城市-香港和上海-中大學教職工和學生的語言意識形態及行為三者之間的動態交互的情景化理解。本研究採用社會語言學中的尺度理論(scale)(Blommaert, 2007; Canagarajah, 2016) 探究高等教育的國際化進程、前景與挑戰。本研究將仔細考慮國際上的探討如何塑造本地的政策及語言行為，後者如何對前者進行重新協商，以及在本地語言行為中新的關係及認同如何產生。 近期研究表明，雖然關於國際化的論述對教育目標已有樂觀的構想，但是在課程銜接、教學語言、評估標準和語言文化多樣性的本意之間的矛盾關係方面仍然有緊張甚至衝突產生(Fabricius, Mortensen, & Haberland, 2016)。在香港和中國大陸兩個亞太地區政治和社會經濟環境截然不同的重要經濟體的高等教育中雖然皆有促進學生和教職工群體多樣化和流動、課程同質化及國際研究合作的措施，但是卻鮮少有研究去探尋大學教職工和學生的生活體驗、他們如何構建自身身份認同、以及如何通過語言行為進行正當性協商。 本研究將使用個案研究及跨案例比較分析的研究方法，意在獲得對於一個深植於其所處環境的複雜現象的深入探究。一系列研究技術將用於數據收集，其中包括： 1）線下田野調查，包括採訪、文件審查、觀察以及語言交互記錄；2）線上田野調查，包括在社交平台上對參與者進行觀察和交流，例如上海的參與者使用的微博，香港參與者使用的臉書。這些研究方法使得研究者可以深入研究在高等教育國際化背景下，機構的語言政策、不同利益相關者（例如教職工和學生）、語言意識形態和行為的微妙的實時互動和互相關聯。這些方法在通過多源數據對數據進行核對和驗證方面十分必要，另外也有利於提高研究結果的豐富性、有效性，以及對研究結論進行外推和推廣的可能性(Hammersley, 2005)。 鑒於高等教育國際化的複雜性和語境依賴性，此比較研究將通過揭示高等教育國際化、語言和課程的統一、語言和文化多樣性三方面之間的相互作用促進相關文獻的發展。此外，本研究也將對其中的語言意識形態、不平等、以及身份認同等問題進行進一步探討。通過理解大學教職員工和學生面臨的挑戰和確定他們需求，此研究課題將為研究者和教育工作者提供一個信息資料庫用於發展切實可行的、資源配置高效的、資源分佈合理的語言政策。

14620117.label: Realisation of objectives
14620117.value: Objective 1 (100%) Explore the dynamic relationship between language-in-education policy, language ideology, and practices within the global discourse of internationalization In Jun 2018, the Co-I, Dr. Kristine Horner, travelled to Hong Kong and had fruitful exchanges with the PI. Dr. Horner offered helpful comments and provided theoretical insights in explaining the complex relationship between language-in-education policy and language ideologies within the context of internationalization. Dr. Horner also gave a seminar entitled as “Multilingual education, language politics and social (in)equality in Luxembourg” on June 5th, 2018. The seminar produced critical theoretical critiques of existing language policies, which were incorporated into the theoretical framework of the present project. The PI and the research team also conducted intensive literature review of existing studies in three directions: 1. The prevailing language policies that promote internationalization in mainland China and Hong Kong; 2. The effects of these language policies on both teachers and students; 3. The major theoretical perspectives that have been applied to the field of language-in-education policy. This literature review guides us to further comprehend our research contexts and participants. The findings have been published: Gu, M., & Lee, J. C-K. (2019). "They lost internationalization in pursuit of internationalization": Students' language practices and identity construction in a Cross-disciplinary EMI programme in a university in China. Higher Education, 78(3,) 389-405. Objective 2 (100%) Identify challenges and possibilities for staff and students for drawing from diversity as resource to shape practices in internationalization of higher education Data have been collected from in-depth interviews with international undergraduate students and university staff in Hong Kong and Shanghai. Altogether, the team has conducted in-depth interviews with around 26 international students in three universities in Shanghai, and 12 international students from two universities in Hong Kong. The research team have also interviewed 50 local and mainland Chinese students in five universities in Hong Kong. The team also conducted individual, in-depth interviews with over 20 universities professors with different subject backgrounds. This large-scale interview study yielded several major themes related to Objective 2 of this project: 1. The practice of super diversity provided the international students with their new networks in their academic and social lives, whereas challenges with regard to Chinese language learning and academic study produced unexpected amount of workload; 2. The university staff exercised strong agency and flexibility in their teaching practice and curriculum planning within the larger implementation process of the local and national language policies. The challenges they encountered differ in terms of their university policies, workplace cultures, and personal experiences. This has led to the following publications: Gu, M. (2021). Identity Construction and Scale Making of Migrant University Students in Multilingual Settings: A Scalar Analysis. International Journal of Bilingual Education and Bilingualism, 24 (3), 357-372. Objective 3 (100%) Identify knowledge, values, skills, and institutional policy support that enable staff and students to negotiate tensions and conflicts, and create new meaning and values to avoid marginalization and inequality To meet Objective 3, in addition to the large-scale interview project mentioned above, we also conducted an ethnographic-like study via a series of classroom observation and informal talks with both the staff and students. Rich qualitative data were collected to understand the knowledge, values, skills, and institutional policy support from multiple levels of the linguistic, academic and social lives of both staff and students. We conducted an ethnographic-like study to provide a close multimodal conversation analysis of the interaction between a Chinese instructor and an international student in a music classroom in an international university adopting English medium in China. We call for an expanded conceptualization of communicative competence in intercultural (classroom) interaction in international higher education, which moves beyond the linguistic-centered view and incorporates the value of spatial repertoires in generating individuals’ situated ‘language ability’ for achieving communicative, teaching and learning goals. This has led to the following publications: Ou, W., & Gu, M. (2021). Competence Beyond Language: Translanguaging and Spatial Repertoire in Teacher-student Interaction in a Music Classroom in an International Chinese University. International Journal of Bilingual Education and Bilingualism. Objective 4 (100%) Compare the language policy implementation, language ideologies, and language practices in two contexts, and identify the underlying political social and ideological reasons The research activities mentioned in Objective 1, 2, and 3 were relevant to Objective 4. In the current stage, informed by the research findings, the research team is working on a research proposal to explore the social and ideological forces that influence the language policy implementation, language ideologies, and practices in the different educational contexts. Furthermore, a qualitative study has been done to explore how a cohort of Chinese university teachers navigated their EMI instructional settings. Instead of reducing EMI into an English-only space, the findings show that the teachers constructed EMI as three major spaces, including a space for drawing upon local experiences as spatial resources, a space for redeﬁning internationalisation, and a space for translingual pedagogy practice. The findings lend further support to refute the monolingual bias in EMI practice and call for attention to how EMI teachers can act as agents in reconstructing EMI instructional settings as spaces for multilingual and multimodal meaning making. The findings have been published: Gu, M., Li., Z., & Jiang, L. (2021). Navigating the instructional settings of EMI: A spatial perspective on university teachers’ experiences. Journal of Multilingual and Multicultural Development. Gu, M., Guo, X., & Lee, C-K, J. (2019). The interplay between ethnic identity and academic identity construction among South Asian students in Hong Kong tertiary education. Higher Education, 78(6), 1109-1127. Objective 5 (100%) Offer a resource package to develop measures that will allow feasible, efficient, and just working and learning opportunities and effects in internationalized universities, while maintaining individual institutions’ linguistic and cultural uniqueness This objective has been fully achieved. First, it would be desirable to make further adaptation of curricula and materials with consideration of the learning styles of local students, the local pedagogical strategies, and localized sociocultural and linguistic factors could be taken into consideration. Furthermore, resources—such as training programs for teaching with EMI and various teaching strategies— need to be provided to develop academic staff proficient in English, content knowledge, and pedagogy. Second, the findings suggest that multilingual teachers and students should be provided with more space and autonomy to include spatial repertoires in meaning making. For such purpose, training workshops or programmes that target at translingual awareness and spatial competence development can be designed and offered to teachers and students. Teachers and students can be invited to use English as a spatial resource and consider how English can be used together with other languages and resources for more productive and agentive meaning makings. This would require policy makers, teachers, and students to develop a more flexible language ideology and to resist reducing EMI to an English only space. Last, pedagogically, grammar teaching and communicative teaching approaches may not meet the requirements of learners in the rapidly-changing spaces of international mobility and globalization. It would be meaningful to enable students to utilize their language repertoires to negotiate scales and norms, and to invoke new scales to make them more inclusive and hybrid. In this sense, so-called ‘non-standard’ linguistic and cultural backgrounds can be seen as resources in translocal spaces, rather than being marginalized or othered.

14620117.label: Major findings and research outcome
14620117.value: • The findings indicate that internationalization in higher education, despite its ideologically motivated nature, may produce curricular homogeneity but also creates a heterogeneous context of cultures and values and promotes critical understanding of internationalization, globalization, and diversity among students. • It is found that the teachers were able to capitalise on their spatial repertoires for alternative ways of meaning making in their EMI classrooms. Instead of reducing EMI into an English-only space, the findings show that the teachers constructed EMI as three major spaces, including a space for drawing upon local experiences as spatial resources, a space for redeﬁning internationalisation, and a space for translingual pedagogy practice. • The findings suggest that (re)scaling practices of the students are beyond hierarchically-ordered indexical regularities, but develop and change as a shifting category, and can be considered a construct that allows for negotiation and creation of meanings. The participants show their agentiveness in defining a translocal space that advocates hybridity to their advantage. • The findings indicate that the non-Chinese university students in Hong Kong figured out ways in which to interact with the outer world and set up new roles and spaces (i.e., a heritage community with more positive social image). • The findings illustrate how diverse resources beyond the official language of instruction congregated at a particular time in the classroom, interacted with one another and worked collaboratively to allow the participants to communicate smoothly and accomplish the teaching/learning tasks efficiently. 14620117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14620117.value: Informed by the research findings from this GRF project on the interplay of language-in-education policy, language ideology and linguistic practices within discourse of internationalization in higher education, further research can be conducted to explore the impact of EMI programs on university students' intercultural competence, intercultural citizenship, language learning, and content learning; and investigate the moderating and mediating effects of demographics, academic performance, perceptions towards EMI, teachers’ instructional strategies, and uses of language(s).

14620117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14620117.value: Theoretically, this study has 1) contributed to the area with the findings of how rescaling practices were continuously in play, and norms were re-constructed by language users under the force or influence of political, social, economic, and interpersonal factors; 2) shed light on the interplay between the emergence of discourses of internationalization in higher education and the local language ideologies and practices held by teachers and students within classroom context; 3) explored the legitimacy of languages other than English in academia in the global process of internationalization; thus 4) provided further support to refute the monolingual bias in EMI practice and call for attention to how EMI teachers can act as agents in reconstructing EMI instructional settings as spaces for multilingual and multimodal meaning making. Practically, the research findings have important implications for language-in-education policy, EMI programmes and EMI teaching in internationalized higher institutions, and for developing measures for feasible, efficient, and just working and learning opportunities and effects in internationalized universities.

14620817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14620817.value: The collapse of some prominent corporations, caused by management misappropriations, has generated a considerable amount of attention to corporate governance in the business literature. The general theme that has emerged advocates a separation of managerial control from ownership, the executive being required to report to a governing board comprising representatives of shareholders. However the majority of studies have focused solely the effect of board composition (input) on board effectiveness (output). Embedded in the input/output approach is the belief that the board can capitalise on members’ expertise, provided it meets the legislative composition requirements, based on the assumption that the board is a homogeneous unit with engaged members committedly and competently discharging their duties. This approach underestimates the importance of personal and organizational factors affecting members’ performance on boards. The effectiveness of a board is contingent on its ability to stimulate meaningful discussion, resolve conflicts, and coordinate members' expertise. In boards in which there is lack of a hierarchical structure to hold members accountable for their performance, the engagement of members is a particularly essential concern. The concept of “engagement”, relating an individual to a group, embraces both affective and behavioural dispositions; engaged members are willing to put additional effort, both physical and mental, into board activities. This study suggests adding two interrelated elements namely "board-processes" and "member-engagement" as mediating variables to the input/output link. A model depicting the causal relationships among these constructs will be developed using a quantitative methodology. Further, the depth of engagement felt by individuals is considered to be contingent on the experience they have gained from “board-processes” during their tenure. To understand this developmental process, personal interviews with selected members will be used; and these qualitative findings will be validated in a subsequent quantitative survey. Integrating the findings, this study will not only expand the literature, but also provide insights for enhancing school governance. The study will be situated in Hong Kong where the introduction of governance reform in the education field has been met with hesitation; the policy was viewed more as an intrusion into school sponsoring bodies’ authority to manage schools than an initiative for school improvement. An understanding of the interplay between group processes and members' dispositions under a contentious context will add a new dimension to governance study. It is both timely and necessary to review the effectiveness of the new policy to schools with the support of both theories and empirical evidence. 由於不適當的管理而引致部份優質企業瓦解的情況，已引起社會對企業管治的關注。社會現時普遍提倡「管理權」和「擁有權」兩權分立，行政人員需向由股東代表組成的管治委員會報告。然而，大多數的硏究焦點只集中討論負責管治的董事局的組成（投入）對企業效能（輸出)的影響。 企業植入投入/輸出的方式建基於於一個信念：假設董事局為一自主個體及各成員均盡職履行職務，只要符合法定組成要求，董事局便可將其成員的專長資本化。可是，此低估了個人及機構因素對成員在董事局表現的影響。董事局的成效在於能長久刺激有意義的討論、解決矛盾及整合成員的專長。在缺乏分層結構的董事局中，要維持成員盡責的表現，重點在於成員的投入參與。投入參與的概念，將個人聯繫至團隊，包括其情感及行為的意向。投入參與的成員，無論在物質和精神方面，均願意花費額外的精力投入董事會的活動。 這個硏究建議增加兩個相關的元素，分別是「董事局過程」及「成員投入參與」作為連結投入/輸出的促成變數，描述了這些以量化原則構成其發展的因果關係。再者，投入參與的深度之個人觀感被認為是從「董事會過程」中的工作經驗所獲得。為了解此發展過程，本研究將揀選有關成員將作個人訪問，其質性結果會以其後的量化調查所驗證。結合各調查的發現，本硏究將擴大文獻的參考及深化社會對學校管治的見解。 本研究將在一個教育管治改革遇到阻礙的地方--香港進行，其有關的政策被視為對贊助團體的學校管理之干預而非對改善學校管理的誘因。在此一具爭議的背景下，團體過程及個人意向的相互作用，將對管治的硏究賦予新的廣寬度。在理論及實證的支持下，檢討新政策對學校的效能是及時和必需的。

14620817.label: Major findings and research outcome
14620817.value: This study introduced the concepts of “engagement” and “board processes” to understand school boards drawing on the business literature. “Board processes” depicts the collective manifestations of board activities whereas “engagement” represents an individual’s commitment towards the board process. Our qualitative data with 42 informants saw a different engagement pattern between members appointed by the school sponsoring bodies (SSB-appointed) non-SSB-appointed members representing the constituencies of teachers, parents, alumni and independent body. In general, SSB-appointed members demonstrated a higher level of engagement. Based on our data set, we identified two main factors influencing non-SSB-appointed members' degree of participation in boards, namely their perception of being an advocate of the respective constituency and their perceived openness of the board to divergent views. The former was related to the constituency representative election method, and the latter was affected by members’ demographic background. The more competitive the election process was, the more committed the winning candidate felt answerable to the expectations of their constituency. More active members were more likely with higher educational attainment. A typology depicting four types of board participation was developed, using the two factors. The four types are: committed, supervised, nominal, and frustrated. Members with a stronger sense of being an advocate of the respective constituency were considered either committed participation or frustrated participation, depending on their perceived openness of the boards to divergent views. Committed participation was seen in open-minded boards whereas frustrated participation in conservative boards. Members with a weak sense of being an advocate of the respective constituency manifested in supervised participation or nominal participation; the former was observed in open-minded boards whereas the latter in conservative ones. Committed participating boards were most effective whereas nominal boards the least. The effectiveness of board processes was found to be contingent on the power-relationship pattern between the principal and the supervisor. Three patterns were identified: supervisor-dominated board, principal-dominated, and collaborative. The findings suggested that collaborative boards were more effective in formulating feasible and flexible school strategies. A model describing the effect of members’ engagement and board processes on board effectiveness was successfully developed based on our quantitative data administered to 315 board members. The following hypotheses were supported: 1: "members’ self-efficacy" has a positive effect on the board processes. 2: "members’ self-efficacy" has a positive effect on their engagement. 3: "Board processes" has a positive effect on board effectiveness 4. "Members’ engagement" has a positive effect on board effectiveness

14620817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14620817.value: The results point to the importance of the provision of professional development to school superintendents, in the areas of their value, knowledge and skills. It is evident in the findings that some of the superintendents do not have a good understanding of the educational issues and are often make decisions from a business perspective without realising the far-reaching effects of the decisions on student development. Their working relationship between the principals is also an area worth further study.

14620817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14620817.value: The findings confirm the importance of board meeting process and members’ engagement to its effectiveness. The leadership style of the school supervisor (superintendent) affects the quality of the boards’ deliberations and decisions. Cases in which the supervisors and principals worked collaboratively in setting meeting agenda and holding meeting were found to be more efficient and effective. In addition, a more efficient meeting was associated with a well organized agenda in which a separation of matters for reporting and matters for discussions was seen. The contribution of the parent representative and teacher representative is found to be marginalized in the study; they often take a passive role in board deliberations. The effect is more pronounced in schools with students of a lower socio-economic status background. Board members’ degree of engagement is related to their perception of the roles and responsibilities entrusted on them by the school governing bodies; it is developed from the practices adopted by the schools in calling meetings. More engagement is seen in members who believe that their contribution is valued by the school and that good secretariat assistance is provided. The logistic meeting arrangements and the format of minutes have an impact on members’ engagement.

15101217.value: The principal objectives of this study are to compare the effectiveness of four rehabilitation programmes that use (1) MT with TENS, (2) sham-MT with TENS, (3) MT with placebo-TENS and (3) control training, respectively, in addition to standardised task-oriented walking training, in improving muscle strength, motor control, co-ordination of the legs, walking performance, functional mobility and community integration in stroke survivors. Within the period of July 2018 and November 2021, 124 patients with chronic stroke were recruited for screening. Total 100 patients were recruited to participate in the program. There was no significant difference among the 4 groups at baseline. One hundred (100%), 90 (90%), 82 (82%) and 68 (68%) subjects completing the baseline, mid-intervention, post-intervention and 3-month follow-up assessment, respectively. No adverse incident occurred in this study. The duration of the study was extended, and the drop-out rate at 3-month was relatively high (32%). It was because of the campus closure due to social movement in 2021, several waves of pandemic from 2021-2022.

15101217.label: Major findings and research outcome
15101217.value: This is 4-arm single-blind randomized controlled trial. Total 124 subjects were screened and 100 were included in the study between July 2018 and November 2021. One hundred subjects were randomly allocated to MT+TENS, sham-MT+TENS, MT+placebo-TENS and control groups. All subjects were assessed with Fugl-Meyer Assessment of Lower Extremity (FMA-LE), paretic ankle dorsiflexion and plantarflexion strength, 10-meter walk test (10MWT), Timed Up and Go Test (TUG), lower extremity motor coordination test (LEMOCOT) and community integration measure (CIM) at baseline, after 10 sessions (mid-intervention), after 20 sessions (post-intervention) and 3-month follow-up after intervention ended. Several major findings has been identified in our study. First, the Linear Mixed Model (LMM) revealed a between-group effect in FMA-LE scores, indicating that MT+TENS group showed significant greater improvement of FMA-LE scores than the other 3 groups between baseline and post-intervention (sham-MT+TENS: mean difference=1.10, p=0.011; MT+placebo-TENS: mean difference=1.00, p=0.020; control: mean difference=1.15, p=0.012), and such improvement could be maintained in the 3-month follow-up. Secondly, the MT+TENS showed significant within-group improvement in FMA-LE score, paretic side ankle dorsiflexion and plantarflexion strength and the non-paretic side LEMOCOT score at post-intervention, and the effect was maintained at follow-up assessment. Thirdly, the sham-MT+TENS group showed significant within-group improvement in FMA-LE score, paretic ankle plantarflexion strength, paretic and non-paretic side LEMOCOT score at post-intervention. Only the improvement of FMA-LE score and non-paretic side LEMOCOT score was maintained at follow-up assessment. Fourthly, the MT+placebo-TENS group showed significant within-group improvement in FMA-LE score and non-paretic side LEMOCOT score at post-intervention, and only the improvement of FMA-LE score was maintained at follow-up assessment. In conclusion, the MT+TENS group is superior to sham-MT+TENS, MT+placebo-TENS, and control groups to improve the lower limb motor function in people with stroke. The manuscript reporting the findings of the randomized controlled trial is under preparation. In addition to the randomized controlled trial, the standardization procedure and psychometric properties of other related physical tests on lower limb motor functions were explored with the support of the funding. Those assessment included Maximal Step Length test, Survey of Activities and Fear of Falling, Short-form Physiological Profile Assessment, long distance corridor walk test, falls risks for older people in the community screening tool, and Trail Walking Test. Based on the results of these studies, 7 manuscripts have been published in international peer-reviewed journals. Our findings has also been presented in 2 international conferences.

15101217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15101217.value: Results of our research project demonstrated that the MT+TENS is superior to sham-MT+TENS, MT+placebo-TENS, and control to improve the lower limb motor function (FMA-LE) in people with stroke. The neurophysiological mechanism, however, had not been investigated in the current study. Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (TMS) and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) can be used to evaluate the cortical excitability of the related motor cortex in response to the cutaneous somatosensory stimulation and/or visual stimulation from MT. Using TMS, it would be feasible to evaluate the differences of neurophysiological response to TENS and MT in patients with chronic stroke. Further understanding of the neurophysiological mechanisms could help to identify the optimal dosage (eg, stimulation intensity and intervention duration) of TENS stimulation, and optimal protocol in conducting MT in stroke rehabilitation. The current study recruited patient with chronic stroke (i.e., 1 year post stroke). However, the period of between 3 to 12 weeks post-stroke is the ?golden? time period which showed the greatest motor cortical reorganization and motor recovery following stroke. Thus, we speculate that greater treatment effects could be obtained if applying MT+TENS over this ?golden? time period. Further study on patients 3 to 12 weeks post-stroke is warranted.

15101217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15101217.value: Transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS) and mirror therapy (MT), have been reported to be the effective supplementary intervention to enhance the physical training in improving the motor function in people with stroke. Mirror therapy (MT) required the people with stroke to attempt synchronous bilateral hand movements while observing the mirror reflection of their non-paretic limb in the position of their paretic limb. MT and TENS can activate the motor cortex via the somatosensory and visual input, respectively. It is reasonable to hypothesize that TENS combined with MT can augment the effect of physical training in improving the lower limb motor function in people with stroke. The aim of this study is to investigate whether MT+TENS is superior to sham-MT+TENS, MT+placebo-TENS and control in improving the lower limb motor function in people with stroke. Results of our randomized controlled trial demonstrated that the 20 sessions of MT+TENS is superior to sham-MT+TENS, MT+placebo-TENS, and control to improve the lower limb motor function (FMA-LE) in people with stroke in 100 people with stroke.

15101517.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15101517.value: 针对Beclin 2的生物化学和结构研究以阐明其在细胞自噬和GPCR转运中的不同功能

15101517.label: Project Objectives
15101517.value: Biochemical and structural study of the Beclin 2 CC domain to confirm its oligomeric state and metastability for Atg14L/UVRAG interaction The Beclin 2 CC domain is the binding site for Atg14L and UVRAG, two “primary” modulators of the Beclin 2-Vps34 complex. We will carry out biochemical characterization of the Beclin 2 CC domain to confirm its homodimeric metastable state. We also plan to determine its structure to delineate the molecular mechanism of its “imperfect” dimer interface. Our preliminary data has confirmed its homodimeric state and metastability. Structure determination is currently underway. Comparison of the Beclin 2-Atg14L and Beclin 2-UVRAG interactions through biochemical and structural characterizations to delineate their distinct binding modes We aim to confirm that Beclin 2 binds to Atg14L with higher affinity than UVRAG, in contrast to Beclin 1’s stronger binding to UVRAG. We will first characterize the binding affinities of the Beclin 2-Atg14L/UVRAG interactions by in vitro ITC and in vivo Co-IP. We also plan to solve the structures of the Beclin 2-Atg14L/UVRAG coiled coil complexes to delineate their distinct binding modes. Biochemical mapping of the GASP1-binding motif within Beclin 2 The Beclin 2-GASP1 interaction involves the N-terminal region of Beclin 2 and the C-terminal Armadillo Repeat (AR) domain of GASP1. To map the GASP1-binding motif within Beclin 2, a series of short constructs systematically scanning through the Beclin 2 N-terminal region will be generated and their binding to GASP1 AR domain will be tested by in vitro pull-down assay. Structure-based functional study on how competitive recruitment of Beclin 2 by Atg14L or GASP1 coordinates Beclin 2-mediated autophagy and GPCR trafficking Using the biochemical and structural data of Objectives 1-3 as guidance, we will generate three groups of Beclin 2 constructs to either disrupt or strengthen the Beclin 2-Atg14L interaction (termed “Atg14L-Loss” and “Atg14L-Gain” respectively) or to disrupt the Beclin 2-GASP1 interaction (termed “GASP1-Loss”). The impact of these mutations on Beclin 2-mediated autophagy and GPCR trafficking will be investigated by transfecting them into a Beclin 2 knockout cell line and assessing the relevant activities by standard assays.
