15105117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15105117.value: Glaucoma is the leading cause of irreversible blindness in the world. It is called the “sneak thief of sight” because the vision loss is insidious, painless and without warning. Frequently, patients are alerted to their condition only at a very late stage of disease. The cause of vision loss is attributed to retinal ganglion cell death secondary to high intraocular pressure. In a normal eye, a healthy intraocular pressure is maintained by a dynamic balance between aqueous humor production (inflow) and drainage of aqueous humor (outflow). This delicate balance can be changed by pharmaceuticals such as corticosteroids. Corticosteroids are frequently used as medication for treating eye inflammations. However, it causes an undesirable intraocular pressure elevation which is clinically known as corticosteroid-induced ocular hypertension (CIH). Glaucoma is frequent resulted if CIH is left untreated. Increase in aqueous humor outflow resistance is thought to be the cause of intraocular pressure increase in CIH. Intuitively, decreasing the outflow resistance is pivotal in treating glaucoma. Tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) is a novel and potent agent that could reduce outflow resistance in CIH and also lower the intraocular pressure in human. It is thought to breakdown collagens at the trabecular meshwork (TM) which is the main site of outflow resistance, by an unknown mechanism. We propose, first of all, to study the differential protein expressions of TM of the sheep CIH model by novel proteomic analysis with or without tPA treatment. The protein data will depict biological pathways that are altered in CIH and by tPA. With this information, we can zoom into specific biological pathways and molecule(s) and devise physiological study to validate their roles in CIH. These data will not only help understand the underlying mechanism of CIH and tPA’s action, but also form the scientific basis for future anti-glaucoma treatment. 青光眼是目前世界范围内不可逆盲的首要原因。它被称为“视力的小偷”，因为视力丧失过程是悄然、无痛、毫无征兆的。通常情况下，患者只有在疾病的极晚期才会被发现。视力丧失的原因是继发于高眼压损害的视网膜神经节细胞死亡。在正常情况下，眼内压由房水产生（流入）和房水引流（流出）之间的动态平衡来维持。这种微妙的平衡可以被药物如皮质类固醇打破。皮质类固醇通常被用作治疗眼部炎症的抗炎药物。然而，它可以引起眼内压升高，临床上被称为皮质类固醇诱发的高眼压症（CIH）。如果CIH未经及时治疗，就有可能发展成为青光眼。其原因可能是由于小梁网（TM）的结构变化引起的房水流出阻力的增加引起眼内压增高。了解CIH的发病机制可能有助于揭示青光眼的潜在发病机制。降低房水流出阻力一直是抗青光眼治疗的重点研究方向之一，但迄今尚无突破性进展。组织纤维蛋白溶酶原激活剂（tPA）是一种新颖有效的药物，可以降低CIH中的房水流出阻力，从而降低眼内压。一般认为其可以在TM上分解胶原蛋白，从而导致房水流出阻力降低的，但确切的机制仍不清楚。我们考虑通过最新的蛋白质组学分析研究绵羊CIH模型TM的tPA治疗差异蛋白表达。这种方法的优势在于它可以提供蛋白质组最全面的覆盖。数据进一步进行通路分析和生理学研究，可以揭示tPA作用于CIH的潜在机制。结果将有助于发现新的青光眼治疗方法。

15105117.label: Realisation of objectives
15105117.value: Objective 1 In order to establish an ocular hypertensive model in guinea pigs using corticosteroid, we tried different ways to administer the dexamethasone (DEX). We have modified the protocols and would like to have a more robust and sustained hypertensive effect. We modified the composition of injection by adding 1% of carboxymethyl cellulose into 5% DEX so as to increase its viscosity. Then we administered the DEX mixture via subconjunctival injection twice per week to mimic the extended release of DEX into the eyes. IOPs were monitored every 2 days for 6 weeks. The difference between treated and control eyes were calculated (IOD, treated minus control IOP). IOPs in treated eye were significantly increased (mean IOD: 7.14 ± 4.21 mmHg, n = 5). Animals were then sacrificed, and their trabecular meshwork tissues were extracted for proteomic analysis after IOP measurement. This objective has been achieved completely. Objective 2 We have studied differential protein expression of human trabecular meshwork (TM) with corticosteroid using high-resolution mass spectra (SWATH-MS), and further to confirm the targets using targeted based high-resolution multiple reaction monitoring (MRMHR) using a hybrid quadrupole-time-of-flight mass spectrometer. Quantitative proteomics revealed 20 differentially expressed proteins (p-value ≤ 0.05 and fold-change ≥ 1.5 or ≤ 0.67) between normal and corticosteroid treated TM tissue. These included connective tissue growth factor (CTGF) and thrombospondin-1 (THBS1), two proteins previously implicated in ocular hypertension, glaucoma, and the transforming growth factor-β pathway. In order to study the effect of corticosteroid on guinea pig’s TM cells, we used the proteomic approach to profile and identify differentially proteins. Quantitative proteomics revealed 108 differentially expressed proteins (p-value ≤ 0.05 and fold-change ≥1.3 or ≤ 0.77.). These included transforming growth factor beta (TGFβ) and transforming growth factor beta-1-induced transcript 1 protein. Both proteins were increased by corticosteroid by 1.31 and 1.5 folds, respectively. TGFβ has been shown to cause IOP elevation. Multiple proteins that were found to play different roles in ocular hypertension and glaucoma pathogenesis previously were also identified in this study. This objective has been achieved completely. Objective 3 We have also studied the effect of tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) on corticosteroid-induced hypertensive (CIH) eyes in guinea pigs. As mentioned previously, ocular hypertension in guinea pigs was induced by sub-conjunctival injection 5% DEX on both eyes. After 6 weeks of DEX injection, IOPs increased to 22.9 ± 2.2 mmHg (mean ± SD) and 23.1 ± 2.8 mmHg (mean ± SD) on both eyes respectively. tPA was then injected into the treated eyes while PBS was used to inject into contralateral eyes. The average inter-ocular difference (IOD, treated minus control IOP) of IOP between 2 eyes was, at day 0 of injection, - 0.2 ± 0.8 mmHg (mean ± SD) while it to - 6.7 ± 1.6 mmHg (mean ± SD) after 2 days of tPA treatment. IOPs of the tPA-treated eyes were lower than the contralateral eyes. This observation showed that tPA could reduce the IOP in 2 days after corticosteroid-induced ocular hypertension. The result indicated that tPA may be a novel anti-glaucoma drug in the future. Trabecular meshwork tissue in both eyes of the guinea pigs were then collected for proteomic analysis after IOP measurement. Eight differentially expressed proteins (p-value ≤ 0.05 and fold-change ≥1.3 or ≤ 0.77) were identified. Among them, phospholipid scramblase was found to be regulated by tPA in CIH TM tissue of guinea pigs. It was found that phospholipid scramblase activity was regulated in a genome-wide association study of glaucoma subjects. It is thus plausible that phospholipid scramblase activity is important in the transcytotic movement of aqueous humour across the TM. With the help of pathway analysis, specific pathways are mapped and investigated based on the differential protein expressions revealed and further illustrated in objective 5 below. This objective has been achieved completely. Objective 4 This objective has been achieved partially. There were three main reasons for the delay of progress. Firstly, due to the social unrest from late 2019 onward, the campus, including all the laboratories have been closed for two months. Still, our researchers had great difficulties in getting to work during and after the unrest. The progress of experiments and lab activities were completely stopped and slowed in picking up afterwards. Secondly, the recent novel coronavirus infection and lockdown has further delayed and disrupted our work. In this difficult time, the routine maintenance work of the key equipment (Quadrupole Time-of-Flight TripleTOF® 6600 mass spectrometer, SCIEX) for this project was suspended which is crucial in ensuring accuracy in protein analysis, and this has further hindered resumption of work. Thirdly, the plan of using guinea pigs did not work again due to the shortage of animal source in Hong Kong. We have planned to perform work in PolyU Shenzhen Research Institute in which guinea pigs are available. However, due to the border closure, the project was suspended. In the meanwhile, we used human TM cells and C57BL/6J mice to validate the differentially proteins on outflow facility. Two of the identified proteins, connective tissue growth factor (CTGF) and thrombospondin-1 (THBS1), were confirmed by RT-PCR after DEX-treatment. This result is consistent with our early result published in Journal of Proteome Research (Shan, S. W. et al. Journal of Proteome Research 16, 3753-3765, (2017)). Furthermore, we found that THBS1 antagonist leucine–serine–lysine–leucine triggered a dose‐dependent increase in outflow facility in ex vivo mouse eyes (71.2% increase at 50 μM). This result was published in Journal of Cellular Physiology (Shan S. W. et al. Journal of Cellular Physiology 1-13, (2021)). This publication was possible because of the outcome of the present project (paper attached). It was most unfortunate the project was negative impacted due to the closing down of the PolyU over the period of social unrest and then Covid-19 lockdown. While we are able to cover the loss time and complete nearly all of the objectives, we are currently still at the stage of writing up manuscript for publication. With the completed objectives and the good results obtained, we are confident that publications will be forthcoming soon. This objective has been achieved partially. Objective 5 Biological pathways involved in modulating aqueous outflow in both the human TM and corticosteroid- induced ocular hypertensive guinea pigs were further studied by bioinformatics and pathway analysis. The differential protein expression profile of hTM cells were investigated after corticosteroid treatment. Further analysis using the online PANTHER classification system were performed and seven molecular functions were classified. They included “binding”, “catalytic activity”, “structural molecule activity”, “enzyme regulator activity”, “receptor activity”, “transporter activity”, and “translation regulator activity”. Of the 8 proteins with significantly altered expression in dexamethasone and dexamethasone + tPA groups, iPATHWAY software analysis revealed the involvement of 5 major biological processes: the “phospholipid scrambling,” “galactose metabolic process,” “peptidyl-threonine dephosphorylation,” “regulation of membrane lipid distribution,” and “cholesterol homeostasis”. Phospholipid scramblase activity was also found to be regulated in a genome-wide association study of glaucoma subjects. This metabolic activity plays a crucial role in lipid translocation that drives endocytosis and exocytosis of micro-vesicles. It is thus possible that phospholipid scramblase activity is important in the transcytotic movement of aqueous humour across the TM. This objective has been achieved completely.

The difference between treated and control eyes were calculated (IOD, treated minus control IOP). IOPs in treated eye were significantly increased (mean IOD: 7.14 ± 4.21 mmHg, n = 5). 15105117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15105117.value: Our results revealed how tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) might reduce the IOP in corticosteroid-induced ocular hypertension (CIH) animal model, and the molecular mechanisms underlying. In particular, the corticosteroid leads to IOP elevation in guinea pigs and alters the TGFβ-associated molecules and ECM proteins, while tPA could reduce IOP in CIH guinea pigs. It will be important to characterize the related molecular changes at the TM. We profiled the protein expressions of CIH guinea pig’s TM with and without tPA treatment. We proposed to further valid the potential molecules using targeted based approach (high-resolution multiple reaction monitoring, MRM-HR) in these animal models or cultured human trabecular meshwork cells. Their signalling pathways can be extensively studied using various pathway analysis and bioinformatics methods. Ultimately, we will be able to construct a comprehensive or system biology understanding on the mechanism of blockage of anterior drainage system as well as the pathogenesis of glaucoma. Moreover, we will also be able to validate the effect of those potential proteins on IOP regulation in guinea pigs.

15105117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15105117.value: Glaucoma is a sight threatening disease that is frequently associated with a high intraocular pressure (IOP) which is known to be caused by the blockage of the anterior drainage system. This project studied the reaction of tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) on corticosteroid-induced ocular hypertension (CIH) and glaucoma using a guinea pig animal model. Ocular hypertension was successfully induced in guinea pigs by corticosteroids for 6 weeks. Excitingly, tPA was found to be significantly reduced the IOP in CIH guinea pig’s eyes. Our results revealed that tPA can also regulate multiple differentially expressed proteins too. Furthermore, our result will inform new clinical study to assess the development of a novel therapeutic drug in patients with glaucoma.

15106417.label: Realisation of objectives
15106417.value: Realisation of objectives Our proposal aims to investigate the roles and mechanisms of RUVBL2 in the regulation of NFAT5-mediated gene expression. The proposal is consisted of the following objectives: 1.Establishment of RUVBL2-overexpressing or -knockout cell models and substantiation of the functional role of RUVBL2 in Nos2 expression. 2.Characterization of the interaction between RUVBL2 and NFAT5 –domain mapping and functional significance. 3.Elucidation of the signaling pathway leading to RUVBL2/NFAT5 activation. 4.Functional role of RUVBL2 in transcriptional and epigenetic regulation of Nos2 expression. Realization of the objectives: Objective 1 was considered 100% realized. We have successfully achieved RUVBL2 knockdown in RAW 264.6 macrophages and in HeLa cells via transfecting cells with siRNAs. Using these knockdown cells we have characterized the role of RUVBL2 in innate immune response of macrophages (gene expressions, cytokine production, bactericidal activity, and epigenetic regulations)(ref 1), and in the regulation of NFAT5 nuclear export2. In particular, we conducted in-depth study on the role of RUVLB2 in LPS-induced Nos2 expression. We further showed that RUVBL2 regulates H3K4me3 epigenetic modification at Nos2 promoter, which plays an essential role in Nos2 expression. We further showed that pharmacological inhibition of RUVBL2 elicited similar effect as RUVLB2 siRNA in the regulation of Nos2 expression. More importantly, we showed that LPS-induced response in human primary macrophages are similarly regulated by RUVBL2, suggesting that our findings can be extended to human settings. Objective 2 was considered 100% realized. Despite that RUVBL2 is crucial for LPS-induced innate immune response of macrophages, our findings suggested that it did not act through NFAT5. Nevertheless, we provided unequivocal evidence that RUVBL2 regulates NFAT5 nuclear export under hypotonicity, using proteomic analysis, co-immunoprecipitation, in vitro pull-down, and functional studies2. Depletion of RUVBL2 significantly inhibited NFAT5 nuclear export under hypotonicity. We further mapped the protein domains on NFAT5 requires for its interaction with RUVBL2, and showed that the Auxiliary Export Domain (AED) of NFAT5 is essential2, consistent with the nuclear export function played by this domain. Together, we made a novel discovery that RUVBL2 mediates hypotonic NFAT5 nuclear export under hypotonicity via direct interaction (ref 2) . Objective 3 was considered 100% realized. We have conducted rescue experiments by ectopically express siRNA-resistant wild type or ATPase-deficient RUVBL2 mutant in RUVBL2-expressing cells, and determined its effect on the inhibition of NFAT5 nucleocytoplasmic trafficking. We found that while RUVBL2 is essential for NFAT5 nucleocytoplasmic trafficking, the ATPase domain did not play a role in the process. It is because in the rescue experiments the activity mediated by the wild type RUVBL2 did not differed from that of the ATPase-deficient mutant (ref 2). On the other hand, we showed that LPS induced rapid phosphorylation of JNK, ERK, AKT, and p38, degradation of IkappaB, and phosphorylation of STAT1. Pharmacological inhibitor of RUVBL2 did not inhibit the activation of these signaling molecules, suggesting that RUVBL2 did not play a role in the LPS signaling pathway (ref 2). Objective 4 was considered 100% realized. Despite that inhibition of RUVBL2 inhibited expression of proinflammatory genes, we showed it did not exert its role via the inactivation of NF-kappaB1, a well-known transcription factor responsible for the process. As LPS-induced activation of proinflammatory response requires the removal of the repressive H4K20me3 histone mark, we analyzed the role of RUVBL2 in the process and showed that LPS-induced removal of H4K20me3 does not require RUVBL2. However, another histone mark, H3K4me3, which will be enriched at the transcriptional start site of pro-inflammatory genes and was found to be associated with gene activation, was significantly reduced by the addition of the RUVBL2 inhibitor. Moreover, despite that the activation of NF-kappaB was not altered by RUVLB2 inhibition, we showed that the association of p50 to the enhancer of selected pro-inflammatory genes, including Il6, were comprised by the addition of RUVBL2 inhibitor (ref 1). Collectively, we discovered a novel functional role of RUVBL2 in the regulation of histone modifications that are required for pro-inflammatory gene expression. Reference 1. 15106417.label: Major findings and research outcome
15106417.value: Macrophages play an important role in the host defence mechanism. In response to infection, macrophages activate a genetic program of pro-inﬂammatory response to kill any invading pathogen, and initiate an adaptive immune response. We have identiﬁed RUVBL2 - an ATP-binding protein belonging to the AAA+ (ATPase associated with diverse cellular activities) superfamily of ATPases - as a novel regulator in pro-inﬂammatory response of macrophages. Gene knockdown of Ruvbl2, or pharmacological inhibition of RUVBL1/2 activity, compromises type-2 nitric oxide synthase (Nos2) gene expression, nitric oxide production and anti-bacterial activity of mouse macrophages in response to lipopolysaccharides (LPS). RUVBL1/2 inhibitor similarly inhibits pro-inﬂammatory response in human monocytes, suggesting functional conservation of RUVBL1/2 in humans. Transcriptome analysis further revealed that major LPS-induced proinﬂammatory pathways in macrophages are regulated in a RUVBL1/2-dependent manner. Furthermore, RUVBL1/2 inhibition signiﬁcantly reduced the level of histone H3K4me3 at the promoter region of Nos2 and Il6, two prototypical pro-inﬂammatory genes, and diminished the recruitment of NF-kappaB to the corresponding enhancers. Our study reveals RUVBL1/2 as an integral component of macrophage pro-inﬂammatory responses through epigenetic regulations, and the therapeutic potentials of RUVBL1/2 inhibitors in the treatment of diseases caused by aberrant activation of proinﬂammatory pathways. On the other hand, extracellular tonicity has been implicated a role in macrophages-mediate innate immunity through NFAT5 regulation. We further showed that RUVBL2 plays a novel functional role in the regulation of NFAT5 activity through regulating its nuclear export under hypotonicity. Our findings have identified an unconventional tonicity-dependent nuclear trafficking pathway for the regulation of NFAT5-depenent gene expressions. Together these findings offer an opportunity for the development of novel RUVBL2 strategies that are potentially useful for the treatment of immune diseases.

15106417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15106417.value: Our discovery regarding the functional role of RUVBL2 in proinflammatory gene induction and nucleocytoplasmic trafficking of NFAT5 are novel and have significant impact to our understanding on the regulation of innate immunity. Our findings also suggested RUVBL2 as a key molecules that may bridge tonicity-dependent gene regulations and innate immune responses. Our discovery also opened up a new direction in the study of how innate immunity can be controlled via fine tuning the activity of RUVBL2. We have already shown, in cell culture models, that RUVBL2 is a potential drug target for regulating proinflammatory gene expressions. Over-activation of innate immune response may contribute to different diseases such as sepsis and inflammatory bowel disease. Therefore, the next phase of the work will be to determine the efficacy of potential RUVBL2 inhibitors in alleviating these diseases in vivo. Animal models of these diseases will be set up. On the other hand, at present there are only a few RUVBL2 inhibitors available in the market. Therefore, new RUVBL2 inhibitors will be developed by rational drug design approach, and their efficacy will be determined by cell and animal models.

15106417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15106417.value: Macrophages play important role in host defence mechanism. In response to infection, macrophages activate a genetic program of pro-inflammatory response to kill any invading pathogen, and initiate adaptive immune response. We have identified RUVBL2, an ATP-binding protein belonging to the AAA+ (ATPase associated with diverse cellular activities) superfamily of ATPases, as a novel regulator in pro-inflammatory response of macrophages. 15200817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15200817.value: 大氣污染影響氣候變化、危害人類健康，是一個全球性挑戰。航運業對於維持全球經濟增長具有至關重要作用。然而，航運業產生了大量的廢氣。根據世界海事組織估計，航運廢氣每年至少導致八萬人死亡。死亡原因主要歸結為航運業大量採用高硫的化石燃料，這些化石燃料產生的硫氧化物占全球總的硫氧化物的10%至15%。世界海事組織對航運大氣污染問題嚴重關注，制定了排放控制區以降低航運的硫氧化物排放。船舶在排放控制區內航行時，必須採用硫含量不超過0.1%的低硫油，禁止採用傳統的硫含量可達3.5%的高硫油。低硫油價格高昂，因此航運公司運營的船舶在排放控制區內減速航行並改變航行路線以控制燃油成本。航運公司的這些措施會導致二氧化碳排放增加，極端情況下可增加10%。但是，已有文獻中並沒有關於如何解決制定排放控制區帶來二氧化碳排放增加的問題。 香港將於2019年同中央政府一同實施排放控制區。香港海運港口局一直致力於制定可持續的環保政策以增強香港作為世界航運中心的地位。本課題的目標是為排放控制區管理者提供一套指南以降低航運的硫氧化物和二氧化碳排放。本課題將建立一個博弈論模型，其中排放控制區管理者首先做出管理決策，然後航運公司根據排放控制的規定優化運營管理以降低成本。排放控制區管理者做決策時需要考慮航運公司可能採取的應對措施。本課題在理論和實踐兩個方面都有一定的價值。本課題的完成將為排放控制區管理者提供可持續航運的管理建議、增進對排放控制區政策下管理者與航運公司博弈的理解、用真實資料以香港為例做案例分析。本課題提出的方法和建議將有助於應對全球氣候變化帶來的威脅。

15200817.label: Realisation of objectives
15200817.value: With the joint effort of all participants, the three objectives of this project have been realized on time. To achieve Objective 1, we have proposed Stackelberg game models to develop effective policies for ECA regulators to minimize the sulfur oxide emissions and carbon dioxide emissions from sailing legs to and from the port. Study that investigates voyage-dependent ECA policies has been conducted. The decisions of two players, namely the ECA regulator and the shipping company, are integrated into our model, which considers the sulfur oxide emissions and carbon dioxide emissions simultaneously. Playing as the leader in the game, the regulator enacts sulfur limit on the marine fuel used on board and sailing speed and designs sailing path for the voyage to minimize the social cost (company cost, sulfur oxide cost, carbon dioxide cost). Playing as the follower, the shipping company that operates the considered voyage optimizes the sailing schedule to minimize its fuel cost (recorded as company cost). After thorough analysis, the optimal ECA policies under various policy combinations and shipping company’s operation optimization plans are obtained. The comparisons between the case of our ECA policies (sulfur limit, sailing speed limit, sailing path guidance) and the cases without and with current ECA policies (only sulfur limit) validate the new policies we proposed. It is revealed that optimizing sulfur limit and sailing path or optimizing sulfur limit, speed limit, and sailing path yield equivalent or lower social cost than traditional ECA policies when the total sailing time on the voyage is predetermined, which represents the short-term operation optimization of the shipping company. When the shipping company is going to make long-term operation optimization, which includes the design of total sailing time on the voyage, the new ECA policies also perform better than the traditional one. Especially, optimizing sulfur limit, speed limit, and sailing path simultaneously leads to lower social cost than any other policy combinations in this scenario. Based on this study, it turns out that considering the responses of the voyage operator, optimizing sulfur limit, sailing speed limit, and sailing path simultaneously can further reduce total social cost than traditional ECA policies, especially when the long-term design of the total voyage sailing time is taken into account. Our model and analysis validate that the new ECA policies are more effective in minimizing the total social cost while both sulfur oxide emissions and carbon dioxide emissions are considered, and therefore the new policies are better choice for the ECA regulators. Based on the results of phase 1, we extended the analysis and modeling of Objective 1 to consider carbon dioxide emissions from shipping routes that comprise several ports. Multiple studies have been conducted to verify the ECA policies under different scenarios. Two studies were conducted to show the response of shipping companies, namely the route operators, to the traditional ECA regulations. One is a study regarding the route and speed optimization problem for liner ships under the ECA policies. Standing at the point of a liner shipping company, a bi-objective model was proposed to minimize the fuel cost and the total sulfur oxide emissions from the route. Although the study was conducted from the shipping company’s perspective, the sulfur emissions, which is one of the ECA regulator’s main concerns, is taken into account as the second objective. Results of numerical experiments indicate that facing the sulfur limit within ECA, the shipping company will reoptimize its sailing speed to reduce the fuel cost, which will increase the sulfur dioxide emissions. The other study addresses a holistic liner shipping service planning problem considering the effect of ECAs. In addition to the sailing speed and path optimization in the previous study, ship type selection, fleet deployment and schedule design are also integrated into a three-stage model, which was then solved by a nesting algorithm framework originally proposed. Extensive numerical experiments reveal that, in liner service operation optimization, taking the effect of ECA into consideration can reduce over 2% of costs, which is a large amount considering the several billions’ annual total costs. Furthermore, approximately 90% of cost savings are obtained from speed optimization, and the rest are obtained from path optimization. The third study investigates the schedule design for liner services under vessel speed reduction incentive programs (VSRIPs), which provide dockage refund for ships that attend the program voluntarily and obey the sailing speed limits in the proximity to ports. A mixed-integer nonlinear mathematical model was developed for the minimization of the total cost, consisting of fuel cost, as well as operating cost, minus dockage refunds. Numerical experiments based on real sailing routes show that with the help of dockage refund policy, VSRIPs become attractive to sailing route operators. We also investigated the integrated impact of multiple emission reduction policies, namely sulfur emission regulations, carbon tax, and VSRIPs, on the operation optimization of a shipping company with multiple liner shipping routes. Given the emission reduction measures, the shipping company decides how many ships should be deployed on each route and how to design sailing path and speed for each leg. A mixed-integer non-linear programming model was presented to minimize the total cost of all routes, i.e., fuel cost, carbon tax, and fixed cost, minus dockage refund from VSRIPs. We proposed tailored method based on model properties and a dynamic programming approach to solve the problem. It is shown that considering three emission reduction measures can save more than 0.5% of the total cost, in which over 0.4% is obtained by considering ECA regulations. This study provides useful suggestions for the liner shipping service operation and help the shipping company to reduce the total cost under multiple emission policies. These studies yield managerial insights for shipping company in liner shipping route operation optimization and marine regulators in shipping emission reduction policy design. In the third phase, we conducted a case study and analyzed the effect of China’s potential domestic emission control area (DECA), which includes Hong Kong, with 0.1% sulfur limit. Guidelines for minimizing sulfur oxide and carbon dioxide emissions were formulated for DECA regulators (i.e., Ministry of Transport of China and Marine Departments of Hong Kong and Macau SAR). Various routes were considered, and their operation decisions were analyzed to yield instructive conclusions on the shipping companies’ behavior pattern. Since the water area of this DECA is very small, based on our analysis, a large majority of ships will bypass the DECA and make a detour, which will increase the total emissions and therefore undermining the sulfur dioxide reduction effect of the DECA. The decision of whether to bypass or not depends on a series of parameters. It is shown that, ships deployed on a route would bypass the DECA when distance between the two ports is long, the ratio of the price of low sulfur fuel and that of high sulfur fuel is high and the required time for fuel switching is long. As a result, we suggest that on-site investigations of ship operators regarding the aforementioned factors must be conducted before the sulfur DECA is established. The findings in our study are useful for DECA regulators to assess the sulfur emission reduction effectiveness and the effects on ship operations before the DECAs are established.

15200817.label: Major findings and research outcome
15200817.value: Stackelberg game models were developed to identify effective ECA policies to minimize the sulfur oxide emissions and carbon dioxide emissions from sailing legs to and from the port. We obtained the optimal ECA policies under various policy combinations and the corresponding operation decisions of shipping companies. Theoretically, we proved that the new ECA policies are more effective for the total social cost minimization while both sulfur oxide emissions and carbon dioxide emissions are considered. We have proposed a bi-objective model to investigate the route and speed optimization problem for liner ships under the ECA policies, minimizing the fuel cost and the total sulfur oxide emissions from the route. Results show that the shipping company’s optimization on sailing speed will increase the sulfur oxide emissions. We then addressed a holistic liner shipping service planning problem considering ship type selection, fleet deployment and schedule design as well as the sailing speed and path optimization, under the effect of ECAs. The three-stage model originally proposed was then solved by the tailored nesting algorithm framework. It turns out that: i) taking the effect of ECA into consideration can reduce over 2% of operating costs; ii) 90% of cost savings are obtained from speed optimization; iii) homogeneous fleet in one route is more economical. We further investigated the schedule design for liner services under VSRIPs. The results obtained through the mixed-integer nonlinear mathematical model, the enumerative algorithm, and the piecewise-linear approximation algorithm prove that with the help of dockage refund policy, VSRIPs become attractive to sailing route operators. Based on the above work, we investigated the integrated impact of multiple emission reduction policies, namely sulfur emission regulations, carbon tax, and VSRIPs, on the operation optimization of a shipping company and demonstrated that the most effective way of reducing emissions is obtained by considering the three emission reduction measures in the design of ECA regulations. We conducted a case study and analyzed the effect of China’s potential DECA, which includes Hong Kong. Conclusions on the shipping companies’ behavior pattern facing the DECA were obtained. This phase verifies the necessity of on-site investigations for ECA regulators to assess the sulfur emission reduction effectiveness and the effects on ship operations.

15200817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15200817.value: The first is joint optimization of emission policies among various ECAs. Currently, international shipping routes constitute the majority of maritime transportation, and they always visit ports located in various ECAs. As a result, the optimization of such shipping routes depends on the regulations of all the related ECAs. Compared with optimizing policies of different ECAs separately, the joint optimization will yield a more effective ECA regulation design. To investigate the joint optimization problem, a multilevel model that integrates the decision of the ECA level and the shipping company level will be developed. A tailored algorithm is required to handle the multilevel structure and convert it into single level. The second is to include more emission reduction methods. In this project, shipping companies can adopt fuel switching or sulfur scrubber to obey the ECA regulations. In practice, there are other methods available to achieve the goal, e.g., using alternative fuels. Considering more emission reduction methods will expand the coverage of the problem discussed. Including other emission reduction methods will increase the complexity of the models because more decision variables and constraints need to be included. Although the framework of the problem may not change a lot, more efficient algorithms are required.

15200817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15200817.value: Ship emissions are one of the main concerns of the maritime industry. Being an international maritime center, Hong Kong advocates formulating environmentally conscious and sustainable policies, e.g., emission control areas (ECAs). However, under ECA regulations, shipping companies tend to reoptimize shipping routes to minimize their operating cost, which will increase the sulfur oxide and carbon dioxide emissions out of ECAs. Thus, the sulfur emission reduction effectiveness of ECAs will be undermined, and the total carbon dioxide emissions from the route may increase. To alleviate these side effects, this research project investigated the ECA regulation design problem with the aim to minimize the sulfur oxide and carbon dioxide emissions, considering the responses of shipping companies. We have verified the side effects of shipping companies’ responses. Multiple studies regarding the shipping route operation optimization problem considering various emission policies were conducted, and the optimal solutions provide instructive suggestions for shipping companies. Moreover, we conducted the case study and analyzed the effect of China’s potential domestic ECA, which includes Hong Kong. Based on the shipping companies’ behavior pattern, we proposed constructive suggestions for the on-site investigations for ECA regulators to assess the sulfur emission reduction effectiveness and the effects on ship operations.

15200917.label: Major findings and research outcome
15200917.value: Hybridization of triboelectric and piezoelectric effects in textile structures has been studied in this project aiming at real applications of self-powered and maintenance-free sensing networks. The following key questions have been answered: Both additive or subtractive effects can be found in hybridized TENG and PENG in a cascaded structure. with respect to the individual effects. Two individual bridge rectification circuits are necessary to avoid the cancellation effect due to the output phase difference between TENG and PENG. By theoretical analysis, we have derived the theoretical limits of the output power and energy conversion efficiency by individual TENG and PENG unit, then the cascaded hybrid generator in terms of materials, device structural parameters and operating conditions. We investigated materials synthesis and optimization processes. Next, we conducted a study on device structural design, fabrication and testing of the individual components of hybrid generators, that is, the piezoelectric and triboelectric generator units, connectors and separators, as well as harvesting circuits. We then designed, fabricated and tested hybrid generators of selected structures integrating the individual components together. The performance of the hybrid generators was compared with those of the individual units. In parallel, theoretical modeling and numeric simulation were carried out with corresponding experimental verification. Three original and innovative outcomes have been achieved: high-performance, flexible and long-lasting piezoelectric, triboelectric and electrode materials; hybrid textile-based nanogenerators with 0.1 mWs/cm2 power output, satisfactory energy conversion efficiency and excellent durability; and verified theoretical models to predict the performance of individual generator units and the hybrid generators.

15200917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15200917.value: The modeling work sheds new light on the mechanisms and predicts the ways to optimize the materials, structural design and connections of textile-based hybrid generators for intended applications. The novel hybrid generators demonstrated the average power of 0.1 mW/cm2, representing one-orders-of-magnitude improvement to be used in some real portable or wearable microelectronic systems. We will pursue further applications of the results in real wearable system applications.

15200917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15200917.value: In this project, three original and innovative outcomes have been achieved: high-performance, flexible and long-lasting piezoelectric, triboelectric and electrode materials; hybrid textile based nanogenerators with 0.1 mWs/cm2 power output, satisfactory energy conversion efficiency and excellent durability; and verified theoretical models to predict the performance of individual generator units and the hybrid generators. The work sheds new light on the mechanisms and the ways to develop textile-based hybrid generators for self-powered sensing, portable and wearable applications of microelectronics. The novel hybrid generators can be applied in some real portable or wearable microelectronic systems. The textile energy harvesting systems added new members to the family of smart textiles, provide a green and renewable energy source, enable better communication, convenience and mobility for humans, and add abundant values to the industry.

15201017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15201017.value: Viscoelastic pipelines, such as PVC (polyvinyl chloride) and HDPE (high-density polyethylene), have been increasingly used in urban water supply systems (UWSS) worldwide due to their advantages of easy construction and management as well as economic investment. For example, in Hong Kong, over 30% of total length of water supply pipelines (fresh and salt water systems) is made of viscoelastic materials. In the literature, transient (highly unsteady) flows, which occur routinely in UWSS due to daily system operations and accidental events, have been widely studied for elastic pipes (e.g., metallic and concrete), but transient flow behaviors in viscoelastic pipes are so far not well understood. Such situations demonstrate clearly the practical necessity and importance of investigating transient flows and the induced wave propagation in viscoelastic pipelines. Recent experimental and numerical studies have evidenced the complex influences of pipe viscoelasticity on transient flow behaviors and wave propagation. However, there has not yet been reliable and holistic viscoelastic model for reproducing accurately and interpreting physically transient flows in viscoelastic pipelines. With current knowledge gap, the innovative transient-based leak detection methods, which are found to be efficient and non-intrusive technologies, have only been developed for elastic pipelines. Therefore, an in-depth study of transient waves in viscoelastic pipelines is important and necessary to better transient flow analysis for UWSS, which is the scope of this project. This project aims to investigate transient flow behaviors and wave propagation in viscoelastic pipelines, with achieving objectives to: (1) understand the physical mechanism on the influences of pipe viscoelasticity to transient responses in both time and frequency domains; (2) develop a holistic viscoelastic model so as to improve transient flow modelling and analysis in viscoelastic pipelines; and (3) explore key factors and relationships for governing the interactions of transient responses, viscoelastic properties and system conditions. The methods of experimental tests and numerical simulations as well as parametric analysis are adopted for investigation. The achievements of this project are useful to fill the existing gap of theory and practice on transient-viscoelasticity interactions in viscoelastic pipelines. The novel deliverables of this research will include: (1) extensive laboratory experimental program for investigating systematically transient flow behaviors in viscoelastic pipes (PVC and HDPE); (2) holistic viscoelastic model for accurate transient simulations in viscoelastic pipelines; and (3) key factors/relationships governing transient-viscoelasticity interactions. This project will make scientific advances in the understanding, modelling and analysis of complex transient flows in viscoelastic pipelines in UWSS. 粘彈性管道（如PVC管、HDPE管等）因其具有投資節省、施工容易、管理便捷等方面的優勢，現已廣泛應用於世界各地的城市供水系統。在香港，粘彈性管道占城市供水管道（食水和海水）總長度的30%以上。由於系統日常操作以及偶發事故，城市供水系統之中時常出現瞬變流現象；目前，已有大量文獻針對彈性管道（如金屬管、混凝土管等）中的瞬變流現象進行研究，然而，粘彈性管道中瞬變流的流動特性卻鮮為人知。基於此，開展粘彈性管道中的瞬變流特性以及其引發得水力波的研究，具有很高的重要性和必要性。 最近的實驗和數值研究證實，粘彈性管道對瞬變流的流動以及水力波的傳播特性有著極其複雜的影響。然而，目前還沒有一個全面可靠的粘彈性數學模型，可以在物理上準確的重現並解釋粘彈性管道中的瞬變流流動過程。由於這個知識空白的存在，基於瞬變流的管道漏損點檢測技術，目前僅能應用於彈性管道。因此，更深入的研究粘彈性管道中的瞬變流水力波，對城市供水管道中的瞬變流分析至關重要。 本項目致力於研究粘彈性管道中的瞬變流的流動以及水力波的傳播特性，具體內容為：（1）在時間域和頻率域內，理解粘彈性管道對瞬態響應影響的物理機理；（2）開發一個全面的粘彈性數學模型，以便提高粘彈性管道中瞬變流模擬及分析的精度；（3）探究瞬態響應、粘彈性及系統條件之間，存在的主要影響因素及其之間的關係。本研究將採用實驗測試、數值模擬及參數分析等方式。本項目將會填補關於粘彈性管道中瞬變流的理論及實踐空白。 為此，本研究創新性的成果將包括：（1）針對粘彈性管道中瞬變流的流動特性，開展廣泛的系統性實驗研究；（2）為了提高粘彈性管道中瞬變流模擬的精確度，開發一個全面的粘彈性數學模型；（3）探究影響瞬變流-粘彈性管道之間作用機理的主要參數及其之間的關係。本研究將會推進對粘彈性管道中瞬變流的模擬、分析及理解。

15201017.label: Realisation of objectives
15201017.value: All the objectives listed in section 5.2 have been well achieved during this project period. Meanwhile, the research outputs and findings from this project will be useful to provide insights to future research direction that continues this significant work, as well as offer implications to practical applications regarding the transient pipe flow modeling and pipeline diagnosis. (1) the numerical models were established by coupling the water hammer models and viscoelastic K-V models which were then applied to simulate transient flows in plastic/viscoelastic pipes under various conditions. The results obtained are reasonable and useful to this application field, which have been published in top journals in this field, such as Mechanical Systems and Signal Processing (MSSP), ASCE Journal of Hydraulic Engineering and so on (which can refer to the outputs in Part C). (2) a laboratory experimental test system was designed and set up for transient pipe flows in different viscoelastic pipes (HDPE/PVC), under the collaborations with the Co-I (Prof. Bruno Brunone) in Italy. The pressure data have been secured by the high-resolution transducers (with a sampling frequency of 1kHz), which could be stored and treated by the equipped computer and software (embedded software for the transducers). Before its application, thorough calibrations have been performed on this system based on the benchmark cases from the references. Afterwards, the obtained data were used for validating and verifying the established numerical models, as well as for systematic analysis for this project. (3) based on the validated numerical models and established experimental system, various application cases were carried out for data integration and analysis, so as to provide the fundamental understanding and practical application of transient wave behaviors and wave-fluid-pipe interaction mechanisms. Meanwhile, the developed model and experimental test data from this project have been well packaged for future use. (4) all the key results and findings from this project have been published on the important journals in this field as well as presented in the professional conferences in the community. The details refer to the outputs in Part C of this report. With these research activities and outputs/achievements, the objectives of this project have been well achieved (100%) during the project period.

15201017.label: Major findings and research outcome
15201017.value: This project has been achieved to investigate the transient wave behaviors and wave-fluid-pipe interaction mechanisms in viscoelastic pipes in urban water supply systems (UWSSs), with aims to: (a) understand the physical mechanism of the influences of pipe-wall viscoelasticity to transient responses in both time and frequency domains through extensive experimental data analysis; (b) explore a holistic viscoelastic model so as to improve transient flow modelling and analysis in viscoelastic pipes. The developed model is then calibrated and validated by experimental data obtained in this project; and (c) examine the key factors affecting the transient-viscoelasticity interactions under different system and flow conditions (including pipe scales, initial flows, pipe-wall materials and initial transient generations). With achieving these objectives, the main findings mainly include: (1) development of effective numerical models by coupling the efficient transient/waterhammer model and viscoelastic pipe material model (K-V model), with great improvement for the computational efficiency & accuracy for transient flows in plastic pipes under different flow and system conditions; (2) establishment of a laboratory experimental system for extensive tests, under close collaboration with the Co-I (Prof. Bruno Brunone) in Italy, for calibrating and validating the effectiveness and accuracy of the developed numerical model under different test flow scenarios and system configuration conditions; (3) applications of the validated model to transient viscoelastic pipe flows so as to examine the key influence factors and relationships governing transient wave-fluid-pipe interactions and wave propagation process in different viscoelastic pipelines. Based on these results and findings, the main outcomes of this research can be summarized as follows: (i) in total 15 journal papers have been published in key/top journals directly from this project through broad collaborations with local and overseas research groups (see details in Part C), which have provided substantial progress on this topic in this community. (ii) the results and findings have also been presented in front of peers and experts in this field in the international conferences and workshops, so as to gain essential feedback and connections with other research groups. In this regard, 2 conference papers were generated and included in the conference proceedings (details given in Part C). Note that due to pandemic situations in recent 2 years, only these 2 conference papers were produced in the initial stage of the project period (e.g., 2018-2019). (iii) 1 PhD student and 2 Research Assistants have been successfully trained/graduated (or going to graduate soon) during the project period, and seven undergraduate students (2 part-time student assistants and 4 final year project students) have been educated through participating this research project, which is also one of key objectives and outcomes for this project (i.e., young generation education and training purpose). (iv) various external collaborations have been carried out through the research plans of this project, which has led to both international and national connections on this research topic. More details on the publication outputs, young research students training and external collaborations can be found in the Part C of this report.

15201017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15201017.value: As stated in the objectives in Section 5 and achievements in Section 6.1, all the key objectives and planned tasks of this project have been well achieved. Through the implementation process of this project, it has been also found that further development of this research can be performed for future work, including (but not limited to): (1) more complex viscoelastic pipeline systems such as pipe networks can be tested and applied for understanding further the complicated mechanism of extreme transient phenomena such as transient wave-fluid-pipe interaction and process; (2) more complex surrounding conditions in urban water supply systems can be considered and included in the modeling and testing process of this project, such as buried conditions (soil and water), surface loading and traffic influences, as well as elevation variations of pipelines. To extend such research work, it will involve more practical factors and urban conditions, which requires more collaboration with local government department and authorities so as to gain enough geographical and hydrological/hydraulic information. To this end, an engineering R&D project and/or technology transfer project may be more suitable to continue and extend the results and findings of current project to more realistic and practical systems.

15201017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15201017.value: In current urban water supply systems (UWSS), pipelines are encountering many different problems that may affect the system function and operation. Meanwhile, plastic/viscoelastic pipes such as PVC (polyvinyl chloride) and HDPE (high-density polyethylene), have been increasingly used in UWSS, because of their advantages of convenient construction and management as well as economic investment for engineering applications. In this context, understanding and investigating the influences of the widely used viscoelastic pipes to flow dynamics may have great benefits to the industries and cities in both social and economic aspects. To this end, this project investigates transient flow behaviors and wave-fluid-pipe interaction mechanisms in viscoelastic pipelines, so as to enhance both theoretical development and engineering applications in this field. This project has been well achieved under the planned objectives and tasks, under the close collaborations with the PI and Co-I, as well as the research student and staff involved in this project. Specifically, effective numerical models and rigorous experiment tests are developed applied for this investigation. The results and findings obtained from this project are helpful to further development of transient theory and thus will be useful to effective management of UWSSs in Hong Kong and other cities in the world.

15201317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15201317.value: 大多數優化問題都是NP難的。如果可以等指數時間，我們可能會得到中等大小的實例的最優解；否則我們就只能接受次優解。在P不等於NP這個前提下，演算法設計者的工作分為兩個方向，讓演算法運行更快，和得到更好的解。相應的，精確演算法和近似演算法在過去幾十年一直是演算法研究領域的核心。 不管我們如何努力，對有些問題我們都沒法找到比間單枚舉更快的精確演算法，或者比某些間單演算法更好的近似。各種復雜性猜想因此被提出，例如，對精確演算法的指數時間假設（Exponential Time Hypothesis）和對近似演算法的唯一遊戲猜想（Unique Games Conjecture）。一旦這兩種思路都無法取得進展，一個自然的想法是聯合它們得到新的演算法，它們的運行時間在近似演算法和精確演算法之間，而得到的近似解比任何多項式時間近似演算法都要好。 在過去十年，這個研究方向得到不同研究者群體越來越多的註意。但他們的焦點或多或少放在那些（某種意義上）既難解又難近似的問題上，因此幾乎所有的已知結果都是負面結果。本項目則要考慮那些“相對容易”的問題，研究它們的演算法和難度。 滿足這個條件的最著名問題可能是樹寬（treewidth）和路寬（pathwidth）的計算了。很多圖問題在“像樹的圖”上變得容易得多，而度量一個圖是否像一個樹的一個度量就是樹寬，因此它的計算在很多地方至關重要。樹寬問題沒有已知的常數比近似，但如果樹寬很小，我們也可以在線性時間把它計算出來。盡管我們現在只能用指數時間才能得到3的近似比，基於P不等於NP或者唯一遊戲猜想，我們並不能排除多項式時間的1.00001近似演算法。我們計劃重新研究樹寬的結構和它的計算與相關問題的關系，以期找到更好的下界。 我們還會考慮幾個圖劃分問題，目標是更好的亞指數時間近似演算法， 和幾個圖修改問題，目標是更好的近似演算法上下界。

15201317.label: Realisation of objectives
15201317.value: There were several widely used heuristics for the minimum fill-in problem [George1973 and Lipton, Rose, and Tarjan 1979]. Based on them, Agrawal, Klein, and Ravi [FOCS 1990] developed the first approximation algorithm for the problem. The objective function they used is the number of nonzero elements in the matrix after elimination. An approximation algorithm using the number of fill-ins as the objective function was only presented by Natanzon, Shamir, and Sharan in 1998. These two versions are incomparable to each other in terms of approximation. Parameterized algorithms for the problem were first studied by Kaplan, Shamir, and Tarjan [FOCS 1994]. Hardness results of this problem are surprisingly scarce, and the few known ones either are weak or have to use nonstandard complexity conjectures. The only inapproximability result by Wu et al.~[IJCAI'15}] applies to only the first objective function and is grounded on the Small Set Expansion Conjecture. The only nontrivial parameterized lower bounds, by Bliznets et al. [SODA 2016], include a very weak one based on the Exponential Time Hypothesis and a strong one based on the hardness of subexponential-time approximation of the minimum bisection problem on regular graphs. Reductions for fine-grained complexity need to prevent the graph or the parameter of the reduced instance from increasing too much. All the previous lower bounds are based on the reduction of Yannakakis. His reduction consists of five steps, namely, max-2 extsc{sat}, maximum cut, optimal linear arrangement, and chain completion, before eventually minimum fill-in. For the prospect of deriving tight lower bounds on the minimum fill-in problem, the main obstacles lie in step~3, from maximum cut to optimal linear arrangement, and step~4, from optimal linear arrangement to chain completion. In the original version of the reduction, step 3 blows up an n-vertex graph to an n^4-vertex graph. The selection of four in the exponent turns out to be for the convenience of presentation, and any constant greater than three would suffice. Step 4 then blows up the graph size by another quadratic factor. Therefore, one can only derive very weak lower bounds from these reductions. Instead of further improving these reductions or finding alternatives, we start from scratch and devise an entirely new reduction from the vertex cover problem, which turns out to be surprisingly simple. The reduction we discovered can be easily turned into a linear reduction. Our proof is surprisingly simple. The minimum fill-in problem is an edge modification problem. An edge modification problem asks whether one can apply at most k edge modifications to a graph to make it satisfy certain properties. In particular, we look for sublinear kernels, which implies subexponential-time algorithms. We proposed the Label-And-Reduce technique and applied it to produce the first sublinear kernel for an edge modification problem. We are also concerned with the fine-grained complexity of graph modification problems in general. For hereditary properties, a classic result of Lewis and Yannakakis [1980] states that all the vertex deletion problems are either NP-hard or trivial. In contrast, the picture for edge modification problems is far murkier. Though having produced fruitful concrete results, earlier efforts for edge deletion problems shed little light on a systematic answer, and it was noted that such a generalization is difficult to obtain. A basic and ostensibly simple case of graph modification problems is to make the graph H-free for some fixed graph H. The complexity of this special case has been satisfactorily answered for vertex deletion problems, at least in the asymptotic sense. Even restricted to this very simple case, edge modification problems remain elusive. Significant efforts have been devoted to an ongoing program that tries to answer these questions in a systematic way, and promising progress has been reported in the literature. An ongoing program aims at understanding the compressibility of H-free edge modification problems for general H. Contrary to the early expectations, only for a few graphs H polynomial kernels exist for H-free edge modification problems. Apart from the trivial cases, these graphs H are very small, consisting of at most five vertices. The focus is thus on graphs of order four and five. We attack the diamond graph and the paw graph. We made novel observations on the maximal cliques of diamond--free graphs and paw-free graphs. We use these observations to develop polynomial kernels for edge modification problems toward them. Packing problems make one of the most important families of problems in combinatorial optimization. One example is H-packing for a fixed graph H, i.e., to find the maximum number of vertex-disjoint copies of H from a graph G. It is trivial when H consists of a single vertex, and it is the well-known maximum matching problem, which can be solved in polynomial time when H is an edge. The problem can be easily reduced to the maximum matching problem when each component of H has at most two vertices. The smallest H on which the H-packing problem is NP-complete is P2, the graph on three vertices and two edges. The P2-packing problem is thus a natural starting point for investigating H-packing problems in general and has been extensively studied. We again take a kernelization approach. For this problem, a ck-vertex kernel, provided that it satisfies certain properties, would imply an approximation algorithm of ratio c/3. Since we aim for an approximation ratio of 4/3, we need a 4k-vertex kernel. The independent set problem is one of the most important problems in combinatorial optimization. Its study inspired the perfect graph theory. After proving the polyhedral characterization of perfect graphs in the 1970s, Chvatal defined t-perfect graphs. The long efforts of characterizing t-perfect graphs started immediately, but embarrassingly, even a working conjecture on it is still missing after nearly 50 years. Unlike perfect graphs, t-perfect graphs are not closed under substitution or complementation. Benchetrit has obtained a full characterization of t-perfection with respect to substitution in his Ph.D. thesis. We attempt to understand t-perfection with respect to complementation. We also try to derive more subclasses of t-perfect graphs. These results would imply better approximation algorithms for the independent set problem.

15201317.label: Major findings and research outcome
15201317.value: For both versions of the classic minimum fill-in problem, we exclude the existence of polynomial time approximation schemes assuming that P does not equal NP. We also exclude the existence of subexponential-time approximation schemes for them, assuming the Exponential Time Hypothesis. Our results also imply an almost-tight lower bound for parameterized algorithms for this problem. Behind these results is a new reduction from vertex cover, which might be of its own interest: all previous reductions for similar problems are from some kind of graph layout problems. (I&C'20) We produced kernelization algorithms for several edge modification problems. Our sublinear kernel for the clique + independent set deletion problem is the first sublinear kernel for such problems. Our linear-vertex kernel for starforest deletion is optimal under ETH (Algorithmica'23). We presented a 2k-vertex kernel for cluster edge deletion, a linear-vertex kernel for split completion/deletion, and a quadratic-vertex kernel for trivially perfect completion (IPEC'21; Algorithmica'23). For H-free editing problems, we presented polynomial kernels for edge modification problems toward diamond-free graphs (Algorithmica'22) and paw-free graphs (TCS'21). They are an essential step toward a complete dichotomy of the compressibility of H-free editing. We presented a 5k-vertex kernel for the P2-packing problem. Our algorithm implies an approximation algorithm of ratio 5/3 for the same problem. Our improvement, although modest, is a solid step toward the ultimate goal of this line of research. (TCS'22) We characterized minimally t-imperfect graphs with respect to complementation. There are five pairs of graphs that are both minimally t-imperfect and 20 self-complementary graphs that are t-perfect, with orders of at most nine. We identified all the minimally t-imperfect graphs that are fork-free and proved that all the fork-free t-perfect graphs can be colored with four colors and are strongly t-perfect. We show that the following end vertex problems cannot be solved in subexponential time assuming ETH: LDFS and MCS on bipartite graphs (IPL'22) and MCS on weakly chordal graphs (Algorithmica'23). Further, we developed a recognition algorithm for unit interval graphs and interval graphs (SOSA'21). We presented a characterization for a subclass of interval graphs, namely the paired threshold graphs, and used the characterization to develop the first linear-time recognition algorithm for this subclass (WG'20).

15201317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15201317.value: The most important course of action is to understand sublinear kernels further. On the one hand, we develop more sublinear kernels. On the other hand, we show that some problems cannot have sublinear kernels. We need to correlate this topic with other complexity results. Another topic is to derive a tight lower bound for the interval completion problem, another edge modification problem with important applications in sparse matrix computation. Again, the only reduction for the problem was from Yannakakis, which blows up the instance too much. We need a new reduction that preserves the instance size. Last, we will continue the study of the graph parameters treewidth and pathwidth. New structural observations are required to pinpoint their complexity better.

15201317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15201317.value: A business needs to make quantitative decisions every day. Usually, it is neither necessary nor practicable to have mathematically optimal solutions. For example, how many salesmen for a city? In other words, we are satisfied with an approximation. The greater the cost is, we need better approximations, e.g., how many fire stations Hong Kong needs. Contrary to intuition, there are barriers to approximation: one needs significantly more time for an approximation better than a barrier. Traditionally, the boundary for tractability was polynomial time. With modern technology, we may allow moderate superpolynomial time. There are two sides to studying in this direction, developing better algorithms and proving higher barriers. The first one is self-explanatory. We also work on the second one. For example, we prove that the known algorithms for a classic matrix problem, which is universal in engineering computation, are essentially optimal. These negative results do not help computation itself, but it is important. On the one hand, it helps us better understand the problem in theory. On the other hand, it saves us the futile attempts to find theoretically better algorithms: we should focus on heuristics instead.

15201617.value: 集成電路中的晶體管密度不斷增長導致了其功耗不斷增大，進一步引起了對集成電路的性能與可靠性的挑戰。降低功耗的其中一個辦法是減小晶體管的操作電壓，因為功耗是與電壓的平方成正比。對於矽基的金屬氧化物半導體晶體管，其亞閾值斜率的理論極限是60 mV/dec，減小亞閾值斜率則取決於輸運因子或者體因子。使用鐵電材料作為柵介質可以表現出負電容和對柵壓的放大，這樣可以減小輸運因子。基於氧化鉿的鐵電與反鐵電材料有著較大的鐵電極化，高擊穿電壓，寬禁帶，並且兼容於目前的半導體工藝。另外一方面，二維層狀材料沒有懸掛鍵，這樣可以減少通常存在於三維半導體的表面態和缺陷態。使用超薄的二維材料也可以增加靜電控制並減小體因子。 在本項研究題目中，我們提出結合負電容的氧化鉿介質和二維半導體溝道來實現低功耗的晶體管。首先，我們將使用原子層沈積技術來制備鐵電或者反鐵電的氧化鉿材料來取代傳統的介質材料。我們將進一步研究厚度，晶粒大小以及退火條件對負電容的影響。其次，我們將在氧化鉿上制備二維材料電子器件，實現低電壓的晶體管。並且用不同的二維半導體材料制備p型和n型的晶體管。

15201617.label: Major findings and research outcome
15201617.value: We have successfully developed process flow for depositing ferroelectric HfZrO2 using atomic-level deposition techniques. The HZO film was deposited by ALD on p++ silicon (100) substrate at 180℃, using tetrakis (dimethylamido) hafnium as Hf source, tetrakis (dimethylamido) zirconium as Zr source, and H2O as oxidant. The HfOx and ZrOx were deposited sequentially with 1:1 ratio. Then 2-6 nm AlOx capping layer was deposited by ALD in-situ for capacitance matching, using trimethylaluminium and H2O as sources. The substrate was undergone 450 ℃ rapid thermal annealing (RTA) for 1 min in N2 to crystallize the HZO. Then few-layer MoS2 (3.6 – 4.8 nm) was mechanically exfoliated onto the substrate, followed by Au S/D electrode patterning and deposition. We also adopt high-resolution cross section TEM image to clearly reveal the structure of the HZO/AlOx/MoS2 stack with clean interfaces. The HZO layer is highly crystalline from the TEM and electron diffraction pattern. The polarization vs. electric field of the HZO film suggests ferroelectric behavior after 450 ℃ RTA, which is further confirmed by single-point polarization force microscope (PFM) P-E and butterfly loops We demonstrate room-temperature n-type MoS2 negative-capacitance FET (NCFET) on 4 nm AlOx/20 nm HZO and a normal FET on 25 nm AlOx, with the same channel length of 1.7 μm. The NCFET device maintains an average steep slope of 52 mV/dec (3 orders of ID) and 54 mV/dec (5 orders of ID) in forward and reverse sweeps respectively, while the normal FET has a minimum SS of 162 mV/dec. In addition, the off-state current of the NCFET devices (10-14 A/μm) is consistently lower than that of the normal FET. We also show p-type WSe2 NCFET with van der Waals contact. The device exhibits minimum forward SSforward = 44 mV/dec and reverse SSreverse = 18 mV/dec. The drain current can be modulated by 5x104 within 220 mV, which is among the smallest in published NCFETs, especially for p-type FET. We have published these research results in high impact journals, including Science Advances, Advanced Functional Materials.

15201617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15201617.value: To further reduce the power consumption of nanoscale field-effect transistors, we try to develop a device structure without the use of dielectrics. We demonstrate a low-temperature process to transfer metal gate to 2D MoS2 for the high-quality interface. By excluding extrinsic doping to MoS2 and increasing contact distance, the high–barrier height Pt-MoS2 Schottky junction replaces the commonly used MOS capacitor and eliminates the use of gate dielectrics. The MoS2 transferred metal gate (TMG) FETs exhibit sub-1 V operation voltage and a subthreshold slope close to thermal limit (60 mV/dec), owing to intrinsically high junction capacitance and the high-quality interface. The TMG and back gate enable logic functions in a single transistor with small footprint.

15201617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15201617.value: The density of transistors in integrated circuits (ICs) continues to increase, resulting in increased power consumption. This increase in power consumption also poses serious challenges to the performance and reliability of ICs. One way to reduce power consumption is to decrease the operation voltage of an individual transistor, because its power consumption is proportional to the square of the voltage. In this work, we choose negative capacitance stack as gate dielectrics to effectively reduce operation voltage, and select unltrathin two-dimensional semiconductors as channel materials for efficiently electrostatic control. Our research results clearly demonstrate that the operation voltage and the power consumption of the device are significantly reduced. The value of this research resides in the experimental realization of a NC device by integrating the atomic-level deposition of HfZrO2 and ultrathin 2D semiconductors. This work will represent progress toward 2D technology being a viable extension to high-performance Si CMOS technology.

15201717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15201717.value: Analyses of vibration and sound radiation of structures are important for many engineering applications. With the advent of modern design and manufacturing technologies in developing artificially engineered structures, exemplified by acoustic metamaterials, functional graded materials, periodic/lattice structures and acoustic black hole structures etc., unprecedented demand on simulation and analysis tools emerges that existing methods can hardly cope with. Exhibiting the common feature of having either their material or geometrical property variation across the structure, described as the Space-Dependent Structural Inhomogeneity (SDSI) in this proposal, this type of structures creates eminent technical challenges which are mainly twofold: one is the need for reaching higher frequencies with shorter wavelengths due to the lattice effect of the structure, and the other one is the space-dependent wavelength variations due to the inhomogeneous structural properties. In a more general context, these are also the bottle-necking problems that await solutions in general vibroacoustic simulation problems. Motivated by this and inspired by our preliminary work using wavelets in tackling acoustic cavity and 1D vibration problems, this study aims at establishing a general wavelet-decomposed Rayleigh-Ritz framework to deal with a 2D structure with space-dependent inhomogeneous properties, by capitalizing on a number of unique features of the wavelets. With the help of the developed models, underlying physics, specific to the structural inhomogeneity will also be explored. The outcome of the project is expected to guide the design and materialization of a new class of lightweight and high performance structures with unique artificially engineered vibroacoustic properties, in view of applications to a wide range of industrial, domestic or consumer products relevant to Hong Kong and beyond. From the scientific research viewpoint, the problem under investigation is fundamental and generic in nature, which may have significant scientific value for advancing the state-of-the-art in vibration and noise control engineering. 具有空間相關非均勻性的結構在工程具有廣泛的應用。點型結構包括皺起結構，帶孔結構以及聲學黑洞結構等等。此類結構的特點在於其波場及波數在結構空間分佈不均勻，因此對此類結構的模擬及分析帶來極大的挑戰。除此原因之外，波長分布的不均勻性也在結構上同時產生超音區及亞音區，對於結構噪音的產生帶來了新的問題。此課題著眼於對此類問題的解決，為其模擬及分析建立一套完整的方法， 以便為此類結構的降振降噪提供有效的解決方法。

15201717.label: Realisation of objectives
15201717.value: All objectives of the projects have been systematically addressed and realized. Research activities carried out, in relation to the research objectives are summarized as follows: 1). To establish a Wavelet-based Rayleigh-Ritz framework for vibration and sound radiation simulations of a planner structure, validated against some selected academic cases. Towards this objective, typical structures, involving Space-Dependent Structural Inhomogeneity (SDSI), namely an acoustic black hole plate, are taken as representative cases. More specifically, a 2-D semi-analytical model for the vibration and sound radiation analyses of a typical SDSI structure, namely an Acoustic Black Hole plate was established. The proposed model, along with the associated wavelet-based solution procedure, is intended to overcome major technical difficulties which are specific to SDSI structures: the non-uniform wavelength distribution and ABH-induced wave compressions at the high frequency range in a realistic structure of finite size. Under the general Rayleigh-Ritz framework, Daubechies wavelet (DW) scaling functions are chosen as the admissible functions to decompose the transverse displacement of the plate with ABH indentations. Vibration and sound radiation analyses are carried out with results compared with those obtained by the FEM as well experiments. It is shown that the model allows an accurate prediction of various vibration and sound radiation parameters and a realistic description of the typical ABH phenomena. ABH plates are shown to exhibit a reduced sound radiation efficiency as compared with their flat counterpart. Numerical simulations on the investigated configuration show an increase in the sound radiation efficiency due to the added stiffness effect of damping layers. Sound radiation efficiency along with the transonic boundary changes is scrutinized and quantified. Finally, visualization of the supersonic acoustic intensity and radiation allows identifying the effective sound radiation regions of ABH plates and their relationship with the transonic boundaries at different frequencies. This part of the work has been published in a series of papers in Journal of the Acoustical Society of America, Journal of Sound and vibration. 2). To extend the above model to structures containing space-dependent geometrical inhomogeneity with single/multiple/lattice elements. The above proposed modelling methodology has been applied to complex structures with extension to both periodic structures and SDSI structures at higher frequencies. SDSI structures with multiple/lattice ABH are extensively investigated. The targeted application is the creation of band gaps in periodic ABH structures for energy insulation, as well as noise radiation reduction applications. This part of work has resulted in a number of publications in JSV, JASA and MSSP as detailed in the research outcome section. Meanwhile, the vibro-acoustic modelling in the mid-to-high frequency range is investigated. This is a bottle necking problem for the so-called SDSI structures, since it is very difficult to deal with the wavenumber matching among different systems at higher frequencies. In this part of the work, a Condensed Transfer Function (CTF) approach is developed to tackle this problem. It is demonstrated that the calculation efficiency of the CTF method can be greatly increased by properly selecting the Condensation Functions (CFs) and exploiting their physical characteristics. In particular, owing to their spatial wavy features, the complex exponential functions can better match the structural wavelength variations so that the velocity on the plate-cavity interface can be described by using a much reduced CF set as compared with the gate functions which are widely used in the previous works. Numerical results show a piece-wise convergence behavior of the calculation which is further exploited for establishing a criterion for the truncation of the CFs. The proposed criterion allows the determination of a sub-set of the CFs for any prescribed frequency band for the calculation of the system response in a progressive and piece-wise manner, resulting in a great increase in the computational efficiency. This lays the foundation for the inclusion of the wavelet-based model developed in 1) into this general modelling platform. The outcome of this part of research has been published in the Journal of Sound and Vibration. Towards the same objective, a new PUFEM modeling method, particularly conducive to the handling of the SDSI structures, has also been established, with two papers published in IJAM and JSV, respectively. 3). To explore the underlying physics due to the SDSI-related wave-length variations. All the above studies shed lights on the underlying physics governing the SDSI, especially the wave-length variation behavior of the structures and its impact on physical process such as energy concentration, wave slowing-down and well as transformation of supersonic structural wave components to the benefit of sound radiation reduction. These findings inspire the design and numerous applications as reported in Objective 4) below. 4). To apply to some selected SDSI problems such as structures with cut-outs or structures with embedded acoustic black hole features. The above studies allow the exploration of a few important applications as briefly summarized as follows: a) The aforementioned studies inspired the design of light-weight structures with special wave (both structural and acoustic) manipulation capabilities. This includes the design of a plate with tunneled ABH cells with inner cut-outs, which show both directional and complete band gaps. Meanwhile, investigations on the vibration and sound radiation of a finite plate with four ABH cells show that, apart from the expected ABH-induced benefit at high frequencies with damping treatment, it is also possible to draw acoustic benefit in the low frequency range, which is far below the characteristic frequency of the structure. b) The work resulted in the design of add-on vibration devices, operating like a dynamic absorber for broad-band vibration reductions, in both 1D and 2D configurations. c) Based on the space-dependent structural inhomogeneity, various periodic lattices have been proposed, shower superior vibration insulation capabilities, with great industrial application promise.
