15201717.label: Major findings and research outcome
15201717.value: 1). SDSI structures, while creating challenges to conventional modelling and analysis methods, provide a vast space for the exploration of new and exciting applications. Some of these issues and possibilities are clearly shown by the present study. 2). Semi-analytical modeling based on Rayleigh-Ritz, though classical, show vitality through the use of wavelet base functions, to effectively handle SDSI and ABH structures in middle-to-low frequency ranges. The exceptional fitting capability of the wavelets are the assets to accommodate the space-varying features of the SDSI structures. 3). Wit the further improvement brought about by the Condensed Transfer Function (CTF) and FUFEM approaches, a rather complete set of modelling tools is now available to deal with SDSI structures. 4). SDSI structures with cut-outs, especially caved ABH cells, offer rich physics to be explored. Upon proper design as illustrated through double-layer, periodic ABH beams and plates, the designed structures offer exceptional and controllable bandgap properties, which would be exploited for the benefit of vibration insulation and sound radiation mitigations of structures. 5). The slow-wave phenomenon, created by the SDSI and ABH features, enable a transformation of supersonic structural component to subsonic, thus reducing the sound radiation efficiency of the structure and entail reduced sound radiation. Meanwhile, light-weight structural design can be materialized. 6). Benefiting from the rich dynamic and energy trapping features of the ABH structures, effective vibrations absorbers could be realized as an add-on component. Meanwhile, this can also offer the opportunity to achieve effective energy harvesting. More technical conclusions are summarized in the published papers.

15201717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15201717.value: Through four years of research on SDSI and ABH research, our group is now regarded as one of the most active research groups in the vibration and acoustic area. Apart from the academic reputation gained out of this effort, we have successfully attracted strong interest from a number of companies, who decided to support our research through collaborative/consulting projects, which shows the huge application potentials of the technology. This include our on-going collaborations with Midea Ltd, one of the largest houseware products in China. The company is interested in exploring the technology for conceiving better and sound-proofing products. On-going collaboration is taking place with more opportunities to be materialized. The potential application of the technology goes way beyond this. In fact, vibration and noise reduction based on SDSI and ABH technology start to flourish in recent years, with significant impact in many application areas ranging from mechanical, civil, aeronautical and naval engineering. We’ll explore these opportunities in years to come.

15201717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15201717.value: Vibration and sound radiation of structures are important issues for many engineering applications. With the advent of modern design and manufacturing technologies in developing artificially engineered structures, unprecedented demand on simulation and analysis tools emerges that existing methods can hardly cope with. As a result of material or geometrical property variation, described as the Space-Dependent Structural Inhomogeneity (SDSI), this type of structures creates eminent technical challenges while offering enormous opportunities for new design and applications. Motivated by this, this study aims at establishing advanced modelling techniques to deal with a structure with space-dependent inhomogeneous properties and explore the underlying physics for better structural design such as new class of lightweight and high performance structures with unique and artificially engineered vibroacoustic properties, in view of applications to a wide range of industrial, domestic or consumer products relevant to Hong Kong and beyond. 15202117.label: Realisation of objectives
15202117.value: Fabrication of hierarchical micro/nanostructures is a complex cutting process, in which the mechanical machining technique plays a crucial role. Therefore, the development of the machining technique is important. This project aims to develop an innovative μ-n-M4 based mechanical machining technique to flexibly generate complex hierarchical micro/nanostructures and promote potential applications of such structures. For objective (i) of this project, a novel tri-axial piezo-actuated mechanism with delta configuration was developed, and the hybrid theoretical model regarding the input/output stiffness and system natural frequency was established. The closed-loop based nano-sculpturing was conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of the developed mechanical machining technique for micro/nano-cutting. To control the high frequency in nano-level accuracy tertiary motion system, a PID controller was manually tuned for the motion control along each direction. To better monitor the cutting process and have an accurate control of the free displacement related to the actuation voltage, a force estimation strategy was proposed based on the fractional order hysteresis model, when subjecting to any given actuation voltages. The system response was decomposed into a basic linear component and a nonlinear hysteresis component. The experimental results demonstrated the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed model for the mechatronic system (objective (ii)). To facilitate the optimization of machining parameters before ultraprecision machining, a numerical simulation algorithm was developed by considering the three-dimensional geometric shape of cutting tool, cutting motion trajectory, and the elastic recovery of workpiece material. The experimental results validated the ﬂexibility and accuracy of the proposed algorithm (objective (iii)). As a whole, all the objectives of this project have been fully achieved. Eleven papers have been published in top SCI refereed journals, which five of them have been published in Grade A journals such as International Journal of Precision Engineering and Manufacturing-Green Technology, Optics express, and International Journal of Mechanical Sciences.

15202117.label: Major findings and research outcome
15202117.value: Hierarchical micro/nanostructures offer inconceivable impacts on various advanced fields, such as optics, tribology, water manipulation and antibacterial. Fabrication of functional micro/nanostructures with high efficiency and surface quality has become a research focus. In this project, an innovative μ-n-M4 based mechanical machining technique was developed for flexible generation of complex hierarchical micro/nanostructures. Major findings and research outcomes are summarized as follows: (1) In this project, a tri-axial piezo-actuated mechanism with delta configuration was developed. A Pareto front based multi-objective optimization was conducted to optimize dimensional parameters for the mechanism and an optimized prototype was produced for principal demonstration. Performance test showed that around 12.5 micrometer stroke and 3.5 kHz natural frequency were achieved for each direction. A PID controller was manually tuned for motion control along each direction for nano-cutting (Zhu et al., 2021). Micro-/nanostructured surfaces were successfully sculptured with different shapes. To monitor the cutting process, a self-sensing strategy for external force was developed for the piezo-actuated compliant systems without force sensors. (2) This project investigated a four-axial cooperation using three-axial linear motions and one rotary motion to generate hierarchical micro/nanostructured surfaces for micro/nanofluidic applications. A numerical model was developed with consideration of tool shape and motion kinematics to predict the surface topography. A variety of hierarchically structured micro/nanostructures were machined (Sun et al., 2019; Yip and To, 2020; Tong et al., 2020). A quasi-elliptical tool servo method using dual-axial fast servo motions (YZ) was developed to obtain consistent surface quality with high accuracy and low roughness (Du et al., 2021). (3) This project explored the material removal behavior during the complex micro/nanostructures cutting process, a theoretical cutting force model was developed by considering material property, tool geometry, and motion kinematics (Sun et al., 2019). The experimental results showed a good agreement between the estimated and practical cutting force. (4) This project also investigated the applications of micro/nanostructures in optics (Sun et al., 2020; Du et al., 2021), water droplet control and state characterization (Cheng et al., 2020), and corrosion reduction (Fu et al., 2020). A two-degree-of-freedom vibration generator with high bandwidth and high output stiffness was designed and theoretically analyzed for fabricating periodic saw-tooth-like micro/nanostructures that induce structural color (Du et al., 2021), which could be potentially applied for anti-counterfeiting. As a whole, the results of this project have been disseminated through publications in top international journals. Eleven journal papers have been published and one PhD student was trained.

15202117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15202117.value: Hierarchical micro/nanostructures are increasingly used in a range of modern industries, including biological, mechanical, tribological, optical, antibacterial components, data storage, etc. Due to the dimension limitations of natural single-crystal diamond cutting tool, micro/nanostructured surfaces with a high height-to-spacing ratio are still challenging. Currently, photolithography and deep etching are promising methods to fabricate such structures, but the fabrication efficiency is unsatisfactory. In the future, novel machining techniques should be developed to improve fabrication efficiency. On the other hand, applications of hierarchical micro/nanostructures, especially in water droplet self-propulsion, needs to be further studied. Generally, a droplet deposited on a micro/nanostructured surface tends to move in directions that reduce surface energy. However, the control of droplet motion needs to be further explored. The self-propulsion mechanism also needs to be theoretically analyzed. In the future study, high-speed camera and computational fluid dynamics simulation will be employed to overcome these challenges, opening a new avenue for micro/nano structure-induced liquid transport and emerging applications, such as microfluidics design, heat transfer, and smart liquid sorting.

15202117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15202117.value: Hierarchical micro/nanostructures with various functions are drawing ever-increasing attention due to their unique capacity to modify the surface characteristics. However, how to fabricate them efficiently still remains challenging. Therefore, to develop an innovative μ-n-M4 based mechanical machining technique for generating complex hierarchical micro/nanostructures is of great significance. In this project, a tri-axial piezo-actuated machining system was developed. Its working frequency can be up to 3.5kHz and its stroke has 12.5 micrometers. A control method was designed to monitor the cutting motion. Considering the three-dimensional geometric shape of cutting tool, cutting motion trajectory, and the elastic recovery of workpiece material, a numerical simulation algorithm was then developed to predict the surface topography. This project also established a theoretical cutting force model to explore the material removal behavior in micro/nano machining. Different kinds of micro/nanostructures were fabricated using the developed machining system. The structural color, as an interesting application of these structures, was also investigated in this project.

15202217.label: Realisation of objectives
15202217.value: Objective 1: To propose a new fabric defect detection theory and algorithm based on a novel deep vision information learning mechanism and algorithm to achieve the robustness of defect detection To realise Objective 1, a hybrid model based on deep convolutional neural networks (CNN) and weighted double-low-rank decomposition (WDLRD) methods have been successfully developed in this project. Thus, this objective has been fully achieved. Most of the traditional fabric defect detection works are based on auto-correlation function, local binary pattern, Fourier transform, wavelet transform and neural networks. As these methods are used to detect defects at image level, it is difficult to locate defects accurately. Therefore, they are limited to a specific type of fabric structure and thus it is the key reason that they cannot be extended to other fabric types with different structures. The hybrid model based on deep convolutional neural networks (CNN) and a variational autoencoder have been developed to release this limitation and improve the defect detection accuracy. Instead of using the original pixel value as input by the existing autoencoding based methods, CNNs are employed for image texture feature extraction and the variational autoencoder for features representation. Different with most current CNN based fabric defect detection methods that need large scale of labeled defect database, only defect-free samples are required for the training by the proposed model, which make it easy to use in practice due to fabric defect samples are labor-consuming to collect and mark. The proposed model on a public fabric dataset has been validated and experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the show that the proposed CNN technique. Recently, many methods based on low-rank representation have been proposed for fabric defect detection. Most of them relax the low-rank decomposition problem to a nuclear norm minimization (NNM) problem to pursue the convexity of the objective function. When solving the standard NNM problem, matrix singular values have to be treated equally. This, however, would be impractical in the scenario of fabric defect detection as the matrix singular values have clear physical meanings, and thus they should be treated differently. A weighted double-low-rank decomposition (WDLRD) method has been developed for improving the fabric defect detection accuracy, which is the first time that a weighted double-low-rank technique is applied to fabric inspection. Different from existing low-rank based defect detection methods, the proposed method can preserve the most important/distinguishing characteristics of a fabric image by treating the matrix singular values differently via assigning different weights. In addition, the proposed method locates defect regions based on the assumption that the defect-free and defective regions of a fabric image are usually composed of homogeneous objects that have a high correlation, and thus, they can both considered as low rank (i.e. double-low rank). By using such technique, the unnecessary information of the fabric image can be removed while the most important components that are corresponding to larger matrix singular values in both defect free and defective regions can be preserved. Objective 2: To propose a new multi-class hash coding-based classification framework for fabric defect images for improving the performance of defect classification such that defects can be analysed and classified on a real-time basis Most of the existing fabric defect detection methods based on deep learning focus on locating the defective regions of given images and they do not consider the defect categories. Actually, recognizing the categories of defects is important in real application in textile production as it can help to trace back to the source of causing the problem. On the other hand, the calculation during the training and testing processes is based on continuous values in previous deep learning models, which is more time-consuming than that based on binary codes. Therefore, it is necessary to develop an efficient method that can identify the categories of the fabric defects and at the same time reduce the computing time in the testing stage. To realise Objective 2, a deep hashing model has been developed to obtain concentrated and compact binary codes for efficient fabric defect classification in this project. The model is less time-consuming than existing methods as the calculation is based on binary codes instead of continuous values in both the training and testing stages. The hashing loss function of the model incorporates the projection matrix together with pointwise similarity-preserving to improve the accuracy of defect classification and simultaneously preserve the discriminability of the hashing code. Thus, this objective has been fully achieved.

15202217.label: Major findings and research outcome
15202217.value: Robustness of Fabric Defect Detection: To achieve the robustness of defect detection, two methods have been successfully developed, namely convolutional neural network (CNN) based fabric defect detection method, and weighted double-low-rank decomposition method (WDLRD). In the CNN method, the detection of fabric defects is considered as the problem of binary classification and the neural network with multi-convolution layers has been designed to extract the discriminated features for defect detection. In the WDLRD method, the matrix singular values is treated differently by assigning different weights. Thus, the most important/distinguishing characteristics of a fabric image can be preserved. WDLRD considers a defective fabric image being decomposed to two low-rank matrices, i.e., low-rank defect-free matrix and low-rank defect matrix, as the defect-free and defective regions are usually composed of homogeneous objects that have a high correlation. Experimental results on various textile defect image databases show that both CNN and WDLRD obtain better performance than state-of-the-art methods in locating the defective regions on fabric images. Two refereed papers have been published. For details, please refer to Part C: Research Output section (Nos. 1 and 2). Improvement of Fabric Defect Classification: To improve the performance of defect classification, two fabric defect classification methods have been successfully developed. The first method is deep hashing learning method which can learn high-level representation from the automatic observations of the input images instead of using handcrafted features and can recognize the categories of the defects for various fabric pattern and textures instead of only locating defects on specific patterns. The proposed method can learn compact binary codes for efficient defect classification as the calculation of binary codes is more efficient than that of the continuous values. Another method is CNN with Variational Autoencoder method. In the training step, normal defect-free images are segmented into patches and then fed to the model for fine-tuning the parameters. In the testing step, the trained model is used to slide on the original image and rebuild a new image. The differences between the original image and rebuilt image can be considered for defect detection after thresholding and morphology processing. These two methods have been validated on patterned fabric dataset. The experimental results demonstrate that both methods can achieve outstanding performance in terms of classification accuracy and efficiency on detecting various types of fabric defect images. Two refereed papers have been accepted for publication. For details, please refer to Part C: Research Output section (Nos. 3 and 4). Technology Transfer: A device embedded with the above algorithms, named "WiseEye" has been developed. A license has been granted to a textile manufacturing company for their practical use. WiseEye has been integrated with their weaving machines on detecting woven fabric with solid colours on real time basis during the weaving process.

15202217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15202217.value: On the basis of developed convolutional neural network (CNN) based fabric defect detection method, weighted double-low-rank decomposition method (WDLRD) and deep hashing algorithms and techniques brought by this project, a system prototype named “WiseEye” has been developed. The WiseEye, which can be integrated with the weaving machine, can automatically and instantly locate the defects with over 90% inspection accuracy and measure their sizes on common types of woven fabrics with plain and twill weaving structures and solid colours in the weaving process. The aforementioned defect detection and classification algorithms will be further enhanced and extended from inspecting woven solid colored fabric to stripe and plaid patterned woven fabrics and knitted fabrics. Apart from the algorithm enhancement, current WiseEye which can only detect defects on woven fabric to cope with the weaving speed during the weaving process, will be further enhanced for high speed inspection with at least 60 metres per minute for finished woven and knitted fabric inspection and can be commercialized for practical use in the industry.

15202217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15202217.value: Fabric inspection is a vital step for assuring the quality of fabric used for making up apparel products in the textile and apparel industry. Undetected fabric defects moving through the product assembly system cause many problems, which in turn increase the overall manufacturing cost. The conventional inspection through visual checking, which is commonly used in the industry, suffers from limitations such as low detection accuracy and efficiency. Although recent rapid developments in computer vision technology have brought new methods for fabric defect detection, their limitations still hinder the effectiveness and efficiency of defect detection. In this research, a hybrid model based on deep convolutional neural networks and weighted double-low-rank decomposition methods have been successfully developed to achieve the robustness of defect detection. As classifying types of defects is crucial in real application to help production management for identifying the causes of defect and improving the fabric quality, a novel multi-class hash coding-based classification framework on a real-time basis has also been successfully developed for effectively and automatically classifying the type of fabric defects. The defect detection and classification techniques brought by this project can successfully address the limitations and constraints of existing fabric defect detection algorithms and techniques, enabling the development of an automated system with a high level of inspection effectiveness and efficiency, in terms of high detection accuracy and low false fallout.

15202417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15202417.value: The advancement in structural health monitoring technology has been evolving from monitoring-based diagnosis to monitoring-based prognosis. While vibration-based methods using fast-varying structural response data (e.g. acceleration) have enjoyed thriving developments for structural health diagnosis over the past decades, a methodological framework suitable for handling both slow-varying structural response data (e.g. strain and displacement) and fast-varying structural response data in time series is more favourable for structural health prognosis. This proposal is aimed at developing a unified framework for estimation and forecasting of structural health in connection with slow-varying and fast-varying time series monitoring data. In recognising their flexibility, state space models consisting in observation equation and system equation will be formulated in terms of dynamic linear model and its extensions in the Bayesian context to underpin the desired methodological framework. The dynamic linear model is an elegant system approach to handling time series data from a Bayesian perspective. In contrast to classical autoregressive and moving average (ARMA) models which rest on stationarity, the dynamic linear model in the Bayesian context accommodates both stationary and non-stationary time series data. It is able to directly capture features of time series data, such as trend, seasonality, and regression effects. More importantly, the dynamic linear model allows for the description of temporary or permanent shifts in time series parameters that occur abruptly, which is necessary for outlier and damage detection in structural health monitoring paradigm. While uncertainty is inevitable in time series monitoring data and in forecasts based on time series data, the Bayesian approach provides a perfect tool for representing the uncertainty in time series models and quantifying the uncertainty in forecasts in line with time series data. The Bayesian calculation of complex systems has become tractable since the advent of Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods. In this research project, generic dynamic linear models in the Bayesian context will first be developed which enable the representation and forecast of both slow-varying and fast-varying structural response time series data, catering for the description of trend, seasonality, and regression effects. Then, in the Bayesian forecasting and dynamic modelling context, methods for detecting outliers and detecting changes in parameter regimes will be developed for application to structural health monitoring. Field monitoring data from an instrumented bridge and from an in-service high-speed train will be applied for examining the forecast accuracy and verifying the outlier and damage/defect detection and distinction capabilities. 本研究项目首先在贝叶斯框架下发展可以描述和预测慢变与快变结构响应时间序列数据的通用动力线性模型。该模型同时适应于描述趋势、季节性变化及回归效应。然后，在贝叶斯预测和动态建模的架构下，将开发适用于结构健康监测的异常值和参数状态变化的识别方法。最后，从装有传感器系统的桥梁和高速列车中采集的在线监测数据将被用于检验上述模型与方法的预测精度以及异常值和损伤/缺陷的检测与区分能力。

15202417.label: Realisation of objectives
15202417.value: Objective 1: A Bayesian framework has been developed for modelling and forecasting of slow- and fast-varying structural responses in time domain, which enables the probabilistic forecasting of structural responses and bears a strong capability of modeling non-stationary dynamic processes. State space models consisting in observation equation and system equation was formulated in the context of Bayesian dynamic linear model (BDLM) to underpin the methodological framework. The proposed method works in the following way: it updates beliefs by multiplying the prior distribution by the likelihood which is formulated once new data is available. As a result, the posterior distribution combines the information before the current data (current time step) through the prior distribution and the information in the current data through the likelihood function. As the analytical solution to the BDLM is intractable, the Gibbs sampler, one of the Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithms, was incorporated to compute the posterior distributions of the prediction and forecasting errors. A Bayesian variational inference approach based on the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence was also developed for approximate solution. Specific to the online condition assessment of in-service high-speed trains based on acceleration monitoring, the measured dynamic responses at train cabins were first processed to elicit a ride comfort index sequence. Then the developed method was implemented on the ride comfort index sequence for outlier detection and change detection. By integrating the Bayesian forecasting approach with time series analysis, one-step forecasting probability density functions (PDFs) can be obtained before proceeding to the next observation. The change detection is conducted by comparing the current model and an alternative model. While the Gibbs sampler was adopted to obtain approximate solutions in the proposed method, a variational Bayesian learning (VBL) approach was also explored with the purpose of improving computational efficiency. By introducing the entropy concept, the solution of the posterior probability can be obtained by minimizing the KL distance between the target distribution and a randomly proposed function as an optimization problem. As such, the approximate solution to the joint posterior can be pursued by approximating it by a two-factor variational distribution. Thus, the KL divergence becomes the critical measurement in VBL that allows directly drawing the distributions from intractable hidden variables models, instead of the drawn samples in the MCMC algorithms. In this project, the VBL algorithm was not only applied to calculate the joint posterior (Objective 1), but also used in handling input-dependent noise by the variational heteroscedastic Gaussian process (Objective 2). Objective 2: A modeling approach enabling explicit expressions of trend, cyclical, seasonal and regression effects was developed and incorporated into BDLM. As such, the enhanced BDLM accommodates both stationary and non-stationary time series data and delineates the time-dependent structural strain response through invoking different hidden components, such as overall trend, seasonal/cyclical and regressive components. A Bayesian algorithm embedding model class selection was proposed for probabilistic forecasting of time-dependent structural response given structural health monitoring (SHM) data. The innovation of the proposed algorithm is that, in order to appropriately determine the response components (trend, seasonal/cyclical and regression components) and their combinations, Bayesian model class selection (BMCS) was embedded into the modeling process of BDLM, by which the optimal model with most appropriate components and their order was elicited to characterize the time series of structural response, thus enabling concurrently model class selection and probabilistic forecasts in a real-time manner. This method also provides an effective way for incorporating newly observed time-variant data into the model for structural response prediction. In common Bayesian probabilistic approaches for SHM data-based modeling, diagnosis and prognosis, standard uniform or Gaussian distribution noise is assumed throughout the input space. However, in real-world SHM data, this assumption can be unrealistic, because of its unique heteroscedastic uncertainty induced by dynamic loading, electromagnetic pr environmental interference, daily operation activities, etc. To deal with this issue, the variational heteroscedastic Gaussian process (VHGP) approach using variational Bayesian and Gaussian approximation was proposed for SHM data modeling, data uncertainty estimation, and data forecasting. Objective 3: A damage detection methodology based on the enhanced BDLM was developed to detect potential defects and structural damage in a real-time manner, which incorporates logics for prognosis, potential outlier detection, identification of change occurrence (change-point detection), and damage extent and uncertainty quantification. The BDLM is considered as a tool for time series analysis, while Bayesian forecasting is executed to enable the calculation of one-step ahead forecast distribution. The change-point detection is performed by checking the current observation against the routine model (forecast distribution generated by the BDLM) and against an alternative model. The detection rule is that if the alternative model better fits the actual observation, a potential change is signaled. Whether such an observation is an outlier or the beginning of a genuine change (change-point), three metrics (Bayes factor, maximum cumulative Bayes factor, and run length) are performed for further identification. Once the change-point is confirmed, Bayesian hypothesis testing is conducted for damage extent assessment and uncertainty quantification. Objective 4: An on-board sensing system has been installed on an in-service high-speed train to collect a variety of monitoring data during routine operation. With the measured acceleration responses, the proposed Bayesian framework for time series inference and forecasting (given in Objective 1) was applied to conduct a probabilistic assessment of the train condition. Two metrics, Bayes factor and cumulative Bayes factor, were adopted respectively for outlier detection and change detection. The effectiveness of the proposed method was testified. The proposed approach for explicit representation and extraction of trend, cyclical, seasonal and regression effects (given in Objective 2) has been experimentally verified by using strain monitoring data collected from a cable-stayed bridge. By verification in terms of three model performance metrics, the following observations were obtained: (i) the BDLM taking account of all three components of trend, seasonal (cyclical), and regression concurrently achieves more accurate strain response predictions than the models with fewer components; (ii) the errors and uncertainty of forecast strain response become larger as the prediction horizon increases. An online SHM system has been developed for continuously monitoring the lateral deformation of rail track slabs by deploying an array of FBG bending gauges. With the monitoring data from this system, the performance of the proposed VHGP approach (given in Objective 2) for data modeling, monitoring data uncertainty estimation and data forecasting was verified. It was shown that the VHGP framework yields more robust regression results, and the estimated confidence level can better depict the heteroscedastic variances of the noise in SHM data. The real-time damage detection methodology based on the enhanced BDLM (given in Objective 3) has been verified by using strain monitoring data acquired by fiber Bragg grating sensors affixed on the bogies of an in-service high-speed train. Since the train wheels were lathed (lathing is a process to make wheels perfectly rounded) during the monitoring period, the recorded data contain information in line with two different states (before lathing and after lathing). The wheels can be considered as potentially unhealthy (defective) before lathing and as healthy after lathing. The strain monitoring data collected from the bogies before and after wheel lathing were used to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. In the cases addressed, wheel defects were successfully identified, validating the effectiveness of the proposed method.

15202417.label: Major findings and research outcome
15202417.value: 1. A technique that integrates Bayesian forecasting with time series analysis was developed for probabilistic assessment of the condition of in-service high-speed trains based on acceleration monitoring of car-bodies. The measured acceleration responses at train cabins are processed by the Sperling operator to elicit ride comfort index sequence. In terms of the ride comfort index sequence, the dynamic linear model (DLM) and Bayesian forecasting approach for time series are integrated for outlier detection and change detection of in-service trains (Journal Paper No. 1). 2. A fiber Bragg grating (FBG)-based track-side monitoring system for online detection of wheel tread defects was developed. The sensing system uses two FBG strain gauge arrays mounted on the rail foot, measuring the dynamic strains of paired rails excited by passing wheelsets. A defect detection algorithm was developed for using the online-monitored rail responses to identify potential wheel tread defects (Journal Paper No. 2). A patent entitled “An angular transducer based on fiber Bragg grating technology” was filed. 3. A variational heteroscedastic Gaussian process (VHGP) approach was developed which enables the treatment of input-dependent noise, uncertainty qualification, and forecasting of structural health monitoring data. It is demonstrated that the VHGP framework yields more robust regression results and the estimated confidence level can better depict the heteroscedastic variances of noise contained in monitoring data (Journal Paper No. 4). 4. A methodology for real-time defect detection of high-speed train wheels using on-board dynamic stress monitoring and Bayesian forecasting was developed. It embraces logics for (i) prognosis, (ii) potential outlier detection, (iii) identification of change occurrence (change-point detection), and (iv) quantification of damage extent and uncertainty (Journal Paper No. 6). 5. A Bayesian modeling approach embedding model class selection was proposed for forecast of real-time structural strain responses of long-span bridges, which enables the probabilistic forecasting of structural strain responses and bears a strong capability of modeling the underlying non-stationary dynamic process. As opposed to the classical time series models, the proposed modeling method accommodates both stationary and non-stationary time series data and delineates the time-dependent structural strain response through invoking different hidden components such as overall trend, seasonal (cyclical), and regressive components (Journal Paper No. 7). 6. A new sequential sampling method termed coherence-entropy strategy was proposed for polynomial chaos expansion (PCE) modeling. It comprises two sampling strategies, coherence-optimal sampling and Bayesian experimental design, and takes advantage of input and output information simultaneously (Journal Paper No. 8).

15202417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15202417.value: The proposed BDLM-based online structural damage detection method has been applied for structural damage/condition diagnosis and prognosis of in-service high-speed trains and long-span bridges in this project. In addition to structural condition assessment, it can be extended for real-time malfunction detection of controlling systems. For example, the PI is now extending the BDLM-based method for malfunction detection of the suspension controllers of maglev trains during in-service operation, with the data collected by a track-side online monitoring system. The BDLM-based method can be further combined with Echo State Networks (ESNs), Neural Ordinary Differential Equations (NODEs), and Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) for time-domain anomaly detection of nonlinear dynamic systems. The newly emerging physics-informed machine learning methods enable encoding/embedding physical law/knowledge of dynamic systems of concern in terms of ordinary differential equations or linear/nonlinear partial differential equations into deep neural networks, greatly facilitate the solution to forward and inverse problems with needing no labeled data or a few sets of observation data. the PI is now developing NODE-based and PINN-based methods for response solution and parameter identification of linear/nonlinear dynamic systems which can be described by ordinary differential equations, linear/nonlinear partial differential equations and integro-differential equations.

15202417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15202417.value: Despite the continuous evolution and development in the field of structural health monitoring (SHM), interpreting the huge amount of monitoring data from an SHM system to obtain useful information on structural conditions remains a challenge. Furthermore, due to the complexity of structures, measurement noise, inherent uncertainties in measured data and analytical methods, precise models which reflect the actual structural systems are difficult to create. This project developed novel model-free data-interpretation methodologies within the Bayesian framework for structural health evaluation and prediction, especially a methodological framework for structural condition prognosis and damage detection based on Bayesian dynamical linear model (BDLM). BDLM performs well in modeling the time-dependent responses of structures subject to external effects by superposing generic components, including baseline response, seasonal component, and regression component. In contrast to classical time series models, BDLM does not require the data series to be stationary and can provide structural response prediction along with their associated confidence interval to account for the response dynamics and uncertainty. Moreover, the state space method directly contains a model error term, which makes the analysis more robust to misspecification of the model. The effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method are illustrated and validated using real-world monitoring data.

15202717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15202717.value: High value-added complex surfaces containing multi-scale surface features are growing in importance in many fields including advanced optics,bio-medical, aviation,power generation,etc. However,there is still a lack of methodology to govern the measurement process to realize the automatic and intelligent measurement of complex surfaces with traceability. This project aims to develop a Deep Gaussian Process-based Bayesian Inference System (DGP-BIS) for the realization of automatic and intelligent measurement and characterization of complex surfaces on multi-sensor instruments. The DGP-BIS will make use of the Deep Gaussian Process(DGP) as the mathematical foundation to develop a Bayesian Inference engine (BIE) for analysis and modelling of various complex geometric features by designing multi-layer Gaussian process models with full Bayesian treatment. The DGP-BIE will include two core functions including multi-feature classification and multi-dataset regression. Multi-feature classification will automatically extract and classify the geometric features of the measured surfaces from the corresponding designed surfaces to produce an appropriate initial measurement setup and sampling strategy based on the DGP classifier. A class database will be established based on the prior knowledge of the sensor characteristics and the cumulated measurement experience to train the DGP classifier. By taking the initial sampling strategy as input, multi-dataset regression will be used to fuse the datasets obtained from different sensors to form a unique representation of the measured surface based on a DGP regression model. An on-line sampling strategy will be adapted automatically by taking into account the uncertainty of the DGP model as a critical sampling criterion to achieve the required measurement specifications. Scale-decomposition,feature segmentation or pattern analysis will be undertaken to characterize the quality of the machined surfaces. The statistical nature of the DGP-BIS combined with various powerful covariance kernel functions makes the system capable of being generalized for different kinds of complex surfaces and will give credibility to the classification and regression models which will be used as critical criteria to perform intelligent measurement via consecutive learning of the measured surfaces. The research attempts to address the deficiency and limitations of traditional methods which are more susceptible to the geometry of the surface being measured. The DGP-BIS will be integrated into modern measurement instruments to improve both the efficiency and accuracy when measuring complex surfaces. The successful development of the DGP-BIS will not only provide a breakthrough for measuring and characterizing complex surfaces but also contribute significantly to the future development of the next generation of advanced surfaces in precision engineering. 包含多尺度表面特徵的高附加值複雜表面在許多應用場合都具有日趨重要的地位，如在先進光學，生物醫學，航空航天，發電系統等等。然而，目前正缺少一個可以充分指導測量過程以實現自動化和智能化測量以及可追溯性測量的測量系統。因此，本項目以開發一個基於深度高斯過程貝葉斯推理的智能表面測量系統（DGP-BIS）為目標，開發一個可以實現自動化測量，智能化測量以及表徵多尺度複雜表面的多傳感器測量設備。 DGP-BIS系統將使用深度高斯過程（DGP）作為數學基礎，通過設計一個具有完備貝葉斯處理的多層高斯過程模型為作可適用於多種複雜幾何特徵的分析和建模模型，進而開發一個貝葉斯推理引擎（BIE）。此貝葉斯推理引擎（GDP-BIE）包括兩個核心功能，分別是多特徵分類功能和多數據回歸功能。其中多特徵分類功能將會基於深度高斯過程分類器自動對所測量的相應設計表面的幾何特徵進行分解和分類，從而生成一個合適的初始測量參數設定和採樣策略。 建基於先驗知識的傳感器測量特性和累積的測量經驗，本系統將會建立一個分類數據庫以訓練深度高斯過程（DGP）分類器。把初始採樣數據作為輸入，並使用多數據回歸對來自於不同傳感器的數據進行數據融合，將會得到一組基於深度高斯過程（DGP）回歸模型，從而可以得到對待測表面進行表徵的唯一數據。本系統將會建立一個自動考慮深度高斯過程（GDP）模型中預測的測量不確定度的在線採樣策略，從而達到所要求的測量指標。在本系統中，尺度分解，特徵分類和及圖樣分析將會作為表徵加工表面質量的方法。本DGP-BIS系統的統計學特性配合多種功能強大的協方差內核函數使本系統既可以適用於具有不同特徵的複雜表面，也可以確保分類和回歸模型的準確性，使其成為可以通過對待測表面的連續學習以實現智能化測量的關鍵因素。 本研究項目嘗試解決傳統測量方法中容易受表面幾何特徵影響的不足和限制。 DGP-BIS系統將會集成到現代測量設備當中以提高測量複雜表面時的測量效率和測量精度。本DGP-BIS系統的成功建立不但提供一個測量和表徵複雜表面的新的突破，而且對新一代精密工程中的先進表面的開發具有舉足輕重的貢獻。

15202717.label: Realisation of objectives
15202717.value: Complex surfaces containing multi-scale surface features are widely used for the design and manufacture of precision moulds, as well as critical components for automotive and aerospace, biomedical, entertainment and geographical data processing applications. They possess specific properties at different scales for the realization of specific functionalities, and require multi-scale measurement and characterization, which create a lot of challenges for governing the measurement process to realize the automatic and intelligent measurement of complex surfaces with traceability on multisensory instruments, which is hindering the further development and application of these surfaces. As a result, this research aims to develop a Deep Gaussian Process-based Bayesian Inference System (DGP-BIS) to meet the demand for the measurement and characterization of complex surfaces on multi-sensor metrology systems (Objective 3). To achieve the objectives, a study of the characteristics of the state-of-the-art precision measurement sensors for a wide variety of complex surface features has been conducted (Objective 1). To facilitate the modelling and classification of complex surfaces by taking into account the associated measurement errors, a hierarchical information-based characterization method for multiscale structured surfaces has been developed whichmakes use of a priori information of the multiscale surface and a hierarchical segmentation–registration (HSR) algorithm to firstly divide the measurement dataset into segments, which are then registered with the designed geometry of the microstructure. The registered information is used to reconstruct the large-scale topography. Multiple scales of surface information are decomposed hierarchically by the HSR algorithm (Objective 2). To fully characterize the quality of the machined surface, a deep learning characterization method (DLCM) based on a detail-aware dilated convolutional neural network (DDCNN) has been developed. (Objective 2). In this project, a prototype of a Deep Gaussian process-based Bayesian inference (DGPBI) system has been developed. The Gaussian process has been used as the mathematical foundation to establish a plausible inference model to aid the measurement process via multi-feature classification and multi-dataset regression (Objective 3). Multi-feature classification extracts and classifies the geometric features of the measured surfaces at different scales to design an appropriate composite covariance kernel and corresponding initial sampling strategy. Multi-dataset regression takes the designed covariance kernel as the input to fuse the multi-sensor measured datasets with the Gaussian process model (Objective 2). Research work has been conducted on the integration of the DGPBSI system on a multi-sensor instrument. A substantial amount of experimental research studies concerning performance evaluation and enhancement have been undertaken to evaluate and verify the performance of the DGPBI system in the realization of automatic and intelligent surface metrology (Objective 4).

15202717.label: Major findings and research outcome
15202717.value: In this project, a study of the variety of geometric characteristics of the measured surfaces (Conference Paper 1 and Journal paper 3) and various covariance kernel functions has been conducted. Different kernel functions can be selected to study different kinds of surfaces in accordance with the characteristics (Journal Paper 2). In order to model and classify complex surfaces by taking into account the associated measurement errors, a hierarchical information-based characterization method for multiscale structured surfaces has been developed (Journal Paper 1). In addition to the measurement errors on the workpiece, surface defects adversely affect the surface quality of the workpieces. To fully characterize the quality of the machined surface, a deep learning characterization method (DLCM) based on a detail-aware dilated convolutional neural network (DDCNN) has been developed for the characterization of different scales and types of surface defects found on the machined surfaces (Journal Papers 4 to 6). Hence, a Deep Gaussian process-based Bayesian inference system (DGPBIS) has been developed which is mainly composed of four modules, including preprocessing, multi-feature classification, multi-dataset regression, and surface characterization. The DGPBIS considers the surface measurement as a consecutive learning process and makes use of the Gaussian process to model the process. A prototype DGPBIS has been successfully integrated on a Multi-Sensor Instrument and a series of experiments have been conducted for the realization of the intelligent measurement of multiscale complex surfaces (Journal paper 2). The results show that the performance of the multi-sensor instrument has been dramatically improved in terms of measurement efficiency while maintaining the measurement accuracy at a safe level. Up to present, one PhD student has been trained. She has submitted a draft thesis and is expected to graduate at the end of 2022. Six refereed journal papers have been published and one refereed conference paper has been presented to disseminate the research results of the project.

15202717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15202717.value: Some suggestions for potential future work are given below: (i) The present study provides new insights into the realization of intelligent measurement of complex surfaces. However, one of the problems of Gaussian Process (GP) modelling is the high computation complexity which requires a huge amount of time for the computation to complete when a large volume of data is involved in the inference process. Potential future work is suggested for the implementation of approximated GP inference with the aid of a graphics processing unit (GPU) for practical use of the proposed method especially in regard to manipulating vision-based measurement datasets. (ii) The Industry 4.0 has proposed a new initiative for in-situ and/or in-process production measurement in manufacturing environments. This poses new research challenges for high dynamic range measurement for complex surfaces that can cover a larger scale with credible accuracy and production measurement in manufacturing environments which demand high speed and robust in-situ and/or in-process surface measurement, especially when the workpiece is large and repositioning error is unacceptable. Further work can be done by embedding the Deep Gaussian process-based Bayesian inference system (DGPBIS) in on-machine multi-sensor measurement systems to release the in-situ and/or in-process intelligent measurement of complex surfaces in manufacturing environments.

15202717.value: High value-added complex surfaces containing multi-scale surface features are growing in importance in many fields including advanced optics, bio-medical, aviation, power generation, etc. However, there is still a lack of methodology for governing the measurement process to realize the automatic and intelligent measurement of complex surfaces. In this project, a Deep Gaussian Process-based Bayesian Inference System (DGPBIS) has been developed for the realization of automatic and intelligent measurement and characterization of complex surfaces on multi-sensor instruments. The DGPBIS makes use of the Deep Gaussian Process (DGP) as the mathematical foundation to develop a Bayesian Inference engine for the analysis and modelling of various complex geometric features by designing multi-layer Gaussian process models with full Bayesian treatment. The DGPBIS is integrated into modern measurement multi-sensor instruments to improve both the efficiency and accuracy when measuring complex surfaces. 15202817.value: 收益率不確定情況下的最優停時問題

15202817.label: Project Objectives
15202817.value: In studying financial decision-making models, it is important to take the inevitable presence of modeling uncertainties and information incompleteness into consideration. There have been surprisingly few attempts to tackle financial optimal stopping models under incomplete information. This project aims to study several financial optimal stopping models, all under incomplete information. The first problem is the optimal redeeming problem of stock loans. We plan to adopt the free boundary theory in PDE to tackle the problem. Numerical scheme to compute the optimal solution will be provided if no explicit or closed-form solution is available. The second problem is the mean-variance hedging problem. This problem (and the following two) promise to be very hard, with the main difficulty arising from the presence of the running maximum process. We will first endeavor to rewrite the problem into a standard one in terms of some suitable observable Markov state process and then adopt classical methods to solve the problem. The third problem is the optimal tracking problem of the maximum hitting time. We plan to rewrite the problem as a standard one in terms of some suitable observable Markov state process and then study it by standard methods. The fourth problem is the expected utility maximizing model and the relative error minimizing model. We will first endeavor to rewrite the problem into a standard one via an application of the law of total expectation, then tackle the latter by classical methods.

rows: In studying financial decision-making models, it is important to take the inevitable presence of modeling uncertainties and information incompleteness into consideration. There have been surprisingly few attempts to tackle financial optimal stopping models under incomplete information. This project aims to study several financial optimal stopping models, all under incomplete information.

The first problem is the optimal redeeming problem of stock loans. We plan to adopt the free boundary theory in PDE to tackle the problem. Numerical scheme to compute the optimal solution will be provided if no explicit or closed-form solution is available.

The second problem is the mean-variance hedging problem. This problem (and the following two) promise to be very hard, with the main difficulty arising from the presence of the running maximum process. We will first endeavor to rewrite the problem into a standard one in terms of some suitable observable Markov state process and then adopt classical methods to solve the problem.

The third problem is the optimal tracking problem of the maximum hitting time. We plan to rewrite the problem as a standard one in terms of some suitable observable Markov state process and then study it by standard methods.

The fourth problem is the expected utility maximizing model and the relative error minimizing model. We will first endeavor to rewrite the problem into a standard one via an application of the law of total expectation, then tackle the latter by classical methods.

15202817.label: Major findings and research outcome
15202817.value: We have got many important outcomes from this project. For instance, in the paper titled "Mean-variance portfolio selection under partial information with drift uncertainty" we studied a mean-variance portfolio selection problem under partial information with drift uncertainty. The problem is completely solved by solving a related backward stochastic differential equation (BSDE). More importantly, we proposed an efficient numerical scheme to solve the BSDE and compute the optimal portfolio, making our theoretic results can be applied to practical problems immediately. In this process, we used very deep results in Malliavin calculus. We think this paper has made great theoretical and practical contributions. In another paper titled "Optimal redeeming strategy of stock loans under drift uncertainty", we studied stock loan pricing problem under drift uncertainty. Because one has to estimate the market trends when making decisions, the related Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman equation turns out to be of a degenerate parabolic type, which is very hard to obtain its regularity using the standard approach, making the problem different from the existing models. To overcome the difficulty, we introduced delicate probabilistic and functional analysis method to prove the regularity of the value function and derive the optimal strategies. We have a very important financial finding that one should use significantly different strategies in the bull and bear trends. We have published several papers in the highly respected journals in the fields, such as "Mathematics of Operations Research'', "SIAM Journal on Financial Mathematics'', "Quantitative Finance" and "Mathematical Finance''. These published papers are listed in the final report. Meanwhile, we have been invited to delivery talks in several important world leading international conferences such as "The 10th World Congress of the Bachelier Finance Society", "SIAM Conference on Control and Its Applications'', "The Six Asian Quantitative Finance Conference (AQFC)" and "The Seventh Asian Quantitative Finance Conference". Our results have attracted many attentions from the audience. The PI is honored to be awarded the Distinguished Keynote Speaker at the AQFC 2018. Moreover, two PhD candidates have joined the project and accomplished parts of the work. They will continue the research along the research direction proposed by the present project.

15202817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15202817.value: More and more people have realized the importance of market uncertainties in daily operation and risk control, especially with the rapid spread of global pandemic coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19). Therefore it becomes more urgent than before to study how to investment and control risk when faced such market uncertainties. This is a very rapid growth research area and many problems remain open to study. We have PhD students to continue the study. We also hope the the RGC will support a following project along this research direction.

15202817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15202817.value: Financial market is very complicate; nobody knows the further market status, so has to face market uncertainties when making decisions. This project studied several financial models under market uncertainties. It made both theoretical and practical contributions, and its findings can guide people's investment and reduce trading risks in daily operations.

15203117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15203117.value: 中國在2015年佔全球排放量的38％，與美國並列為排放量最大的排放國之一。面對批評，中國近年以平衡人類、自然和經濟發展為宗旨，對其環境治理體系作為生態文明建設的一部分進行改革。舊有的目標導向體系在實施10年後證明不足，因此消除舊有制度成為改革環境治理體系的關鍵之一。新制度鼓勵企業加強在環境保護方面的透明度和責任感。其中，環境透明度涉及披露和報告企業在環境保護方面所作的功夫和表現，但一般企業僅報告法定內容以符合法規。企業環境透明化的進展緩慢，是文學和實踐對環境透明化在環境保護和經濟成效方面的了解甚少所致，而這未知數的出現是因為缺乏環境透明度方面的知識。這些方面對於判斷傳播的環境信息、方式、數量以及向誰，以獲取由環境透明化所得的理想回報而言至關重要。 由於服裝行業的各個供應鏈階段均消耗大量能源和化學物質，並排放有毒廢物，因此這項研究對於污染力强的服裝行業尤其重要。為解決這個迫切的課題，本研究從環境透明度的四個方面探討信息傳播：（1）環境信息在組織溝通渠道的涵蓋率（即環境信息透明水平）、（2）環境信息類型（即環境信息多樣性）、（3）傳播環境信息的利益相關者的類型（即環境信息廣泛性）、以及（4）環境信息的詳細度（即環境信息深度）。我們建議在理論發展和實證研究上驗證出一個理論模型來調查環境信息透明度在環境和經濟方面的潛在影響。這項研究將會從以上四方面的成效提供實證和管理建議，從而幫助企業加強環境透明度，而不僅僅局限於法律遵從和企業社會責任報告的環境披露。這些調查結果將有助於決策者制定政策並建立鼓勵機制，促進企業加強環境透明度，以改善香港和中國服裝業的生態環境和經濟發展。

15203517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15203517.value: Recent advances in medical imaging and surgery technology have made minimally invasive partial nephrectomy (PN) an attractive alternative to radical nephrectomy (RN) for a large number of patients. Evidence has demonstrated that PN can significantly decrease chronic kidney diseases and cardiovascular events compared with RN, especially for patients with small renal tumors. However, nowadays it is still quite difficult for surgeons to precisely excise the tumor with a thin negative margin and meanwhile avoid warm ischemia in the complicated surgical environment, which are two critical factors for the success of a PN. In this project, we aim at developing a set of innovative technologies that facilitate the precise planning and intraoperative guidance of minimally invasive PN in order to greatly improve both oncological and functional outcomes of PN. Although several PN planning systems have been developed, they are incapable of making the precise planning of many advanced yet challenging PN strategies, such as selective clamping of segmental arteries, super-selective clamping of tumor-specific artery branches, and zero-ischemia PN without clamping. These techniques require surgeons to thoroughly grasp the complex surgical anatomy, identify the location and vascularity of the tumor, and recognize the optimal surgical path, which are all laborious and painful tasks using existing tools. To meet these challenges, we shall first propose a novel deep convolutional neural network (DCNN) equipped with probabilistic graphics models and skip connections to precisely delineate the kidney parenchyma and the tumor, which facilitates to exactly identify the tumor-parenchyma interface for precise excision. Then, we shall propose a new multi-level and fine-grained recurrent neural network (RNN) to segment renal vasculature from bi- or tri-phasic 3D CT Images. Based on the segmented results, we shall build a 3D surgical anatomy environment by developing depth- and shape-aware visualization models to clearly exhibit the complicated surgical anatomy for precise planning of advanced PN strategies. We shall also develop a novel interactive physically-based model for the alignment of preoperative data with intraoperative data for accurate and interactive intraoperative guidance, and hence help surgeons exactly track the kidney, the margin of the tumor and the critical anatomical landmarks during the surgery. In summary, this is a joint project with a strong interdisciplinary team including experts in medical image processing, virtual reality, visualization, urological oncology and minimally invasive kidney surgery. The proposed techniques are anticipated to strengthen PN planning and operation, as well as advance the research on computer-assisted minimally invasive surgery.

15203517.label: Major findings and research outcome
15203517.value: The major findings and research outcomes can be summarized in four aspects, which reflect the four research objectives of the project. First, we propose a set of novel deep learning models for medical image segmentation. We develop a non-local context-guided 3D U-Net to automatically segment kidney and tumor from CT images [C2], which is an essential prerequisite to developing the proposed system. To address the challenge of insufficiency of training data, we further propose a set of novel computation- and data-efficient methodologies, including learning 3D features with 2D CNNs via surface projection [C3], unsupervised learning with adversarial redrawing [C4], and selective learning from external data [C10]. These algorithms and their variants have also been used in other medical image analysis tasks [J1, J3, J5-J7, J14, C8-C9, C11-C13], demonstrating their generalization capability. We further propose new domain adaptation approaches [J4, C1] to improve the performance of cross-modality segmentation. Second, we develop a set of geometric modeling and optimization algorithms to facilitate the detail-aware visualization of these segmented models. We propose a robust DGP-based discontinuity preservation approach for surface reconstruction [C6], a geometry and learning co-supported normal estimation method [C5] for noise reduction, an adaptive graph convolution for mesh/cloud points processing [C7], and a data-driven geometry-aware mesh denoising and optimization approach [J8-J9]. Based on these fundamental algorithms, we develop a detail-aware visualization method, which has been patented in both US and Mainland China (see attachment). Third, for both the segmentation and visualization algorithms, we design a set of new schemes to accelerate their computation speed based on the characteristics of GPUs. For example, we propose a memory-efficient method to accelerate the non-local context-guided 3D U-Net [C2] and an adaptive graph convolution for rapid mesh/cloud points analysis [C7]. These acceleration algorithms make these models be capable of performing complex natural scene analysis [J11, J14], as well as other detection and classification tasks [J2, J12-J13, J15, C12, C14]. Fourth, based on the above-mentioned techniques, we have developed a prototype for precise planning and intraoperative guidance of partial nephrectomy and conducted experiments to validate its effectiveness. In the future, we plan to, based on the proposed algorithms and the prototype, apply for ITF and/or HMRF grants, to further improve them and evaluate them on more clinical data. As promised in the proposal, the proposed techniques are general enough to be used in the development of other computer-assisted intervention systems [J8, J16-17].

15203517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15203517.value: We do have a comprehensive plan for further development. First, we plan to validate the proposed system and the algorithms on more clinical data collected from more hospitals. Based on the feedback of the extensive validation, we shall further optimize the system and the algorithms. We plan to apply for an ITF/HMRF grant to conduct this downstream research and development. Second, in the development of the project, we recognize that in order to make our algorithms to be widely harnessed in clinical practice and generate larger impacts, we should further enhance two kinds of research. First, we should address some fundamental theoretical and empirical problems to improve the generalization, robustness, and interpretation capability of these AI models. Second, we should work more closely with clinical collaborators to design and conduct more stringent validation to demonstrate their clinical effectiveness, such as large-scale randomized control trials (RCTs). The cost of these studies may exceed the range of GRF. We plan to apply for some large collaborative grants, such as CRF and RIF, to achieve these significant and impactful objectives. Third, we shall also actively seek collaboration opportunities with relevant companies in these fields to promote and commercialize our outputs.

15203517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15203517.value: The central purpose of the project is to develop a set of novel medical image segmentation, geometric modeling, and visualization techniques to facilitate the development of a computer-assisted system for precise partial nephrectomy (PN). The significance and value of this project are embodied in the following three aspects. First, we proposed a set of novel deep learning models for medical image segmentation, which is an essential prerequisite for the development of computer-assisted intervention systems. Existing models cannot sufficiently address this challenging task owing to (1) the limited training data, (2) the limited computational resources, and (3) the complicated anatomical characteristics. The models generated from this project can largely meet these challenges and achieve better performance than state-of-the-art approaches. Second, we propose a set of novel geometric modeling and visualization methods to reconstruct 3D models and visualize them, which is another key task in computer-assisted intervention systems. Compared with traditional methods, we introduce many advanced AI models in this task and achieve remarkable performance improvement. Finally, we developed a prototype for precise PN and conducted experiments to validate its effectiveness. Most of the proposed techniques are general enough to be applied to develop other similar computer-assisted interventions systems.
