15203617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15203617.value: Text summarization aims to automatically produce a concise and well-organized summary that conveys the most important information in original document(s). It is a crucial technique to support efficient access of information, especially in the era of information overload. The current state-of-the-art summarization approaches are extraction-based, which select salient sentences from source document(s) and concatenate them directly as a summary. These approaches guarantee to produce a summary with good grammatical sentences. However, coherence is problematic especially when summary sentences are extracted from different documents. Moreover, non-essential and redundant information in selected sentences are quite common. Although sentence compression might help, it often causes further readability issue. An ideal way to summarize is to create new sentences with good readability and coherence to reformulate the salient information in source document(s). This process resembles human summarization strategies and is known to be challenging for machines. It requires sophisticated techniques for natural language understanding and generation, which themselves are growing fields. Previously, only a limited number of knowledge-driven approaches are developed in specific domains and with hand-crafted templates/rules. In contrast to extraction-based approaches, research efforts along this line are referred to as generation-based approaches. The challenge of generation-based summarization deserves renewed attention with remarkable success of deep learning and neural network applications in machine translation and response generation lately. The goal of this project is to develop data-driven neural network models for generation-based summarization by exploring their potentials for content representation, abstraction and text generation. We devote to design effective network architectures to seamlessly connect language understanding and language generation models, and to exploit novel collaborative mechanisms to “teach” machines to “read/understand”, “summarize” documents and “write” summaries. In particular, our research focuses on the following fundamental but under-researched issues: (1) how to leverage the hierarchical structure of a document and the prior knowledge of a language to adequately model semantics of words, sentences and documents; (2) how to devise domain-independent learning strategies to identify the focus of attention in documents; and (3) how to utilize the identified key information to create readable sentences, and coordinate document-level, sentence-level content planning to generate coherent multi-sentence summaries. While this project aims to develop innovative neural network solutions to generation-based summarization, our research achievements are valuable for the applications beyond summarization that also heavily rely on language understanding and generation, and will eventually contribute to the development of intelligent machines that have effective language communication skills. 文本摘要旨在自動生成簡明扼要的摘要以傳達原始文檔中的核心信息，是信息超載時代支持信息有效訪問的關鍵技術之一。目前最普遍的摘要方法是基於提取的方法，即從源文檔中選擇重要句子，將其按照一定顺序連接起來作為摘要。这种方法能夠保證摘要句子的語法正確性但卻存在一致性和连贯性問題，特別是當從不同文檔中提取摘要句子時問題更為突出。此外，所選句子中包含非必要和冗餘信息的情況也非常普遍。雖然后续的句子壓縮技术可在一定程度上缓解冗余问题，但往往會導致更多的可讀性問題。 理想化的方法是构造新句子，重新編寫源文檔中的核心信息，並保證良好的可讀性和一致性。這個策略符合人工摘要過程，但是對於機器來說却及具挑戰，依赖于自然語言理解和自然語生成的複雜技術，而這些技術本身還處在成長階段。因此，這方面的研究成果相對而言比較有限，且基本上是在特定領域中的、基於手工製作模板/規則的知識驅動方法。與基於提取的方法相比，沿著该方向的研究工作被稱為基於生成的方法。最近深度學習和神經網絡在機器翻譯和对话系统的應用中所取得的顯著成功，使得生成式摘要的研究重新受到關注。 該項目的目標是通過探索語意內容抽象表示和文本生成的潛力，開發為生成式摘要服務的數據驅動神經網絡模型。我們致力於設計有效的網絡架構，無縫連接語言理解和語言生成模型，並利用新穎的協作機制“教”機器“閱讀/理解”、“總結”文檔和“撰寫”摘要。我們的研究重點將針對以下關鍵問題：（1）如何利用文檔的層次結構和語言的先驗知識來充分表達單詞、句子和文檔的語義。（2）如何設計不依賴領域的學習策略，以確定文檔中的關注焦點。（3）如何利用識別的關鍵信息來創建可讀性好的句子，並協調文檔級別的句子之間的內容規劃，以生成連貫的多話句摘要。 雖然該項目旨在開發創新穎神經網絡解決方案來實現生成式摘要，我們的研究成果對於摘要之外的其他在依賴於語言理解和生成的應用也是非常有價值的，最終將有助於为開發具有有效語言溝通能力的智能機器提供技術支持。

15203617.label: Realisation of objectives
15203617.value: The project “Exploring Neural Network Models for Generation-based Text Summarization” was proposed in October 2016, funded in June 2017, commenced in January 2018, and competed in June 2021. The main research objectives of this project were to (1) design neural network architecture to integrate document understanding and summarization generation; (2) explore mechanisms to support machine learning of neural summarization; (3) develop learning strategies and algorithms for practical applications, and (4) enhance the language quality of generated summaries with knowledge augmentation. With the efforts of several PhD students, research associates and research assistants, these targets were smoothly and successfully completed. Since the proposal was submitted to RGC in 2016, the research on generation-based text summarization has been rapidly developed. The neural sequence-to-sequence (S2S) (aka. encoder-decoder) framework equipped with the copy and the attention mechanisms has become the de facto standard setup. Based upon the S2S summarization framework, two main research issues must be addressed are (1) how to identify the most important information to be included in the summary (i.e., what to write) and (2) how to generate grammatical sentence(s) to express the selected information (i.e., how to write). Our researches were mainly developed along these two directions. Content Selection: What to Write Considering copying and rewriting (e.g., using paraphrases) are two writing styles when humans summarize, we proposed a novel S2S model to fuse a copy decoder and a rewrite decoder to mimic human summarization behaviors. While the copy decoder picks up the most important information (i.e., keywords) from the source text by finding the positions to be copied based on an attention model, the rewrite decoder on the other hand restricts the generation output within a small yet highly relevant vocabulary according to the source text. To combine the two decoders and determine the final output, we developed a predictor to predict when to copy or rewrite. The decoder is responsible for fusing the important words copied from different positions in the source text. However, without any regulation the fused summaries often misrepresent the original meaning and hence produce fake facts. We argued that an effective summarization model should copy facts rather than simply copying unrelated individual words. To avoid generating fake facts in a summary, we leveraged open information extraction and dependency parsing technologies to extract actual fact descriptions from the source text. The dual-attention S2S framework was proposed to force generation conditioned on both the source text and the extracted fact descriptions. We also developed a tool to automatically evaluate faithfulness of generated summaries. We also explored the ways to make better use of the keyword information in the source text. The copy mechanism is essentially the attention mechanism, which is expected to give a higher weight (i.e., the learned probability) to a more important word. With the attention mechanism, content selection is performed over the hidden states of an encoder. As such, the key content which is most contributed to the summary is not directly and sufficiently reflected in the S2S model. To address this issue, we proposed a multi-task learning framework to enhance summary content selection with key word classification. The classification task helped obtain word embeddings that better represent word saliences in the summarization task. Considering the source text is often composed of a series of related events, we further proposed to represent the facts in the source text as a structured graph so that the relevant fact components could be connected together. Consequently, we were required to advance the S2S generation models applied in our earlier work to the graph-to-sequence (G2S) generation models. We verified the proposed approaches on extractive summarization first by extracting fact-level semantic units and introducing a hierarchical structure to incorporate the multi-level of granularities of the text into BERT with a hierarchical graph mask. This allowed us to combine BERT’s ability in natural language understanding and the structural information without increasing the scale of the model. Then we moved on and used the document fact graph to guide abstractive summarization. Note that not all content in the fact graph is necessary for summarization, we constructed focal graphs, i.e., a set of sub-graphs representing critical facts, to capture the salient information. To model global relationships among focal graphs, we developed a graph fusion mechanism to synthesize multiple focal graphs via representation fusion. In addition, we introduced a novel training objective based on contrastive graph learning to further enhance the representations of focal graphs after fusion. Utilizing both document and fused focal graph representations, we adopted a self-attention based transformer decoder to generate the summary. Content Expression: How to Write While state-of-the-art S2S models provide a viable solution to generation-based text summarization, these models face significant challenges when generating both semantically and syntactically correct summaries. Traditional summary generation approaches heavily relied on human carefully designed domain-specific templates. The core functions of these approaches were to extract summary-worth information and filled in hand-crafted templates with the extracted information. Inspired by traditional template-based approaches, we proposed to select existing human summaries as soft templates to guide the S2S generation model. To this end, we adopted a popular information retrieval tool to retrieve proper summaries as candidate templates. Then, we extended the S2S framework to jointly conduct context-based template re-ranking and template-aware summary generation. We call this model 3R model, representing retrieving, re-ranking and rewriting. Text generation necessarily depends on language models. In essence, the decoder in a S2S model has two roles. One corresponds to summarization, i.e., to copy and fuse different parts in the source text using the attention mechanism. The other corresponds to text generation, i.e., to function like a language model. We have explored potential solutions to incorporate external language knowledge to augment linguistic quality of text generation with the believe that incorporating the external language model releases the burden of the internal (decoder) language model by taking more care of language fluency and this consequently enables the decoder to focus more on jointly learning both summary content selection and text generation. Sentence fusion is a conditional generation task that merges several related sentences into a coherent one, which can be deemed as a summary sentence. The importance of sentence fusion has long been recognized by the communities in natural language generation, especially in text summarization. We explored the effective sentence fusion method in the context of text summarization and proposed to build a fact graph from the input sentences to effectively capture and organize related facts in a structured way and use the constructed fact graph to guide sentence fusion. In addition to make use of the attention over the content of sentences and graph nodes, we further developed a graph flow attention mechanism to control the fusion process via the graph structure. Additional efforts were also made to improve text generation models, including the development of variational autoregressive decoders and the joint modeling of duality of the encoder and decoder tasks. In overall, the main goals of this project were completely achieved. Some research results have been published in top conferences (with RGC funding acknowledgments) in natural language processing (ACL, EMNLP and COLING) and artificial intelligence (AAAI). A few other research efforts have been reported in the papers submitted to the top conferences.

15203617.label: Major findings and research outcome
15203617.value: In this project, two closely related research issues were addressed. They are how to identify the most important information to be included in the summary and how to generate grammatical sentence(s) to express the selected information. The main research outcomes are summarized as follows. Content Selection: What to Write With focus on content selection, we were the first to recognize and explain the summary faithfulness problem with the existing neural summarization models in the literature. We argued that without any regulation the fused summaries often misrepresent the original meaning and hence produce fake facts. To alleviate this problem, we leveraged information extraction and dependency parsing technologies to extract actual fact descriptions from the source text. The proposed fact-aware neural abstractive summarization model was published in AAAI’2018. Considering the source text is often composed of a series of related events, we proposed to represent the facts in the source text as a structured graph so that relevant fact components could be connected together. Consequently, the sequence-to-sequence generation models applied in our earlier work were advanced to the graph-to-sequence generation models. The relevant research results were published in COLING’2020, EMNLP’2021 or submitted to CIKM’2021. We also explored the ways to make better use of the key information in the source text via a multi-task learning framework to enhance summary content selection with keyword classification. It was submitted to EMNLP’2019. Content Expression: How to Write Generating natural language text is a fundamental issue in neural summarization. During this project period, pre-trained large language models were not yet available. Inspired by traditional template-based approaches, we proposed to select existing human summaries as soft templates to guide sequence-to-sequence generation models. This work was quite successful and its details could be found in ACL’2018. Meanwhile, we have also explored the potential solutions to incorporate external language knowledge to augment linguistic quality of text generation. The findings were submitted to EMNLP’2019. The importance of sentence fusion has long been recognized by the communities in natural language generation, especially in text summarization. Based on the fact graph constructed from the source text, we developed a graph attention mechanism to control the fusion process via the graph structure. The work was published in EMNLP’2021. Additional efforts were also made to improve text generation models, including the development of variational autoregressive decoders and the joint modeling of duality of the encoder and decoder tasks. The relevant research achievements were published in EMNLP’2018 and ACL’2019. Moreover, the advanced deep learning algorithms such as contrastive learning and prompt learning were also studied recently to enhance generation models, which were just submitted to EMNLP’2022. At the end, we would like to mention that the research progress was more or less affected by the worldwide COVID disease outbreaks. Research assistants, associates and students could not come to Hong Kong in time. Although we have tried hard and finally managed to complete all objectives, some of the research outcomes haven’t had a chance to publish yet. It is our commitment to ensure that all these research results will be published sometimes in the future.

15203617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15203617.value: On the occasion of the boom of deep learning and neural network technologies, we had a very good chance in this project to explore and investigate neural models for generation-based text summarization, which brought great challenges to neural network models for understanding and generating natural language text. Through the joint efforts from all the researchers in this area, the achieved research results were visible. The experience gained from his project allowed us to well understand the potentials of neural technologies and at the same time the limitations of them. While neural summarization models have been able to make very good short summaries that include one or two sentences, they are incapable of generate long summaries with multiple sentences. The coherence and the consistency problems are still there. We noticed that the problems with long text generation are not unique for summarization. They are also applicable to the scenarios of data-to-text generation, review generation and story generation, etc. For long text generation, content planning is even more important than text generation. We would like to further extend our current work and explore the Plan-and-Write paradigm that takes into account of both sentence ordering and sentence generation issues in the future.

15203817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15203817.value: Space heating used to be a luxury in residential buildings in Hong Kong, but has become common in the last ten years. This is attributed to the fast development of reversible room air-conditioners (RACs) which use only one third as much energy as a gas or electric heater. But for subtropical Hong Kong where summer cooling demand is always higher than the winter heating demand, reversible RACs only operate at low part load conditions in winter to become less energy efficient. To restore the full load efficiency, the best solution is to utilize the “surplus” heating capacity for other household uses. The ordinary gas or electric water heater is energy inefficient and thus it is natural to propose utilizing the “surplus” heating capacity for water heating for further energy savings. The PI has recently completed successful research into the feasible use of heat recovery RAC for combined space cooling and water heating in summer. It was found that enough hot water can be produced virtually free as long as space cooling is in demand. Based on previous research results, it will be perfect if the heat recovery RAC, is replaced by a reversible unit, which can be utilized for combined space and water heating in winter. As such, water heating requirement can be fulfilled by a reversible RAC all year-around. The use of a reversible RAC for combined space and water heating is a novel concept. It requires careful consideration of measures which enable parallel operation of the two end-uses so that sufficient hot water can be produced without compromising the space heating and energy saving objectives. But given the highly variable operating conditions and use patterns of RACs in residential buildings, whether or not the objectives can be achieved is subject to how appropriately the reversible RAC is designed, integrated and controlled. In this proposed research, a physics-based dynamic model will be established for performance predictions of the major components and for designing an advanced closed-loop controller. A model-based supervisory control strategy developed on this basis will be used for maximizing the reversible RAC’s overall energy efficiency, while fulfilling both the space and water heating requirements. Laboratory experiments will be carried out for validating the established dynamic model and examining the efficacy of the proposed control strategy. The energy benefits associated with its widespread deployment in Hong Kong will also be estimated.

15203817.label: Realisation of objectives
15203817.value: The proposed research is a pilot study of the potential use of the reversible room air-conditioner (RAC) for combined space and water heating in residential buildings in subtropical regions (abbreviated as the RRAC). Related studies have focused only on single end-use. There has been virtually no mention of their parallel operation in fulfilling both space and water heating requirements. The configuration of the proposed RRAC consists of a compressor, an indoor unit, an outdoor unit, a water heating coil immersed in a hot water storage tank, a group of flow valves (2-way, 3-way and 4-way), and two expansion valves. For the successful application of the proposed RRAC, the major concerns are (1) how RRAC must be positioned to achieve the desired thermal comfort and better energy efficiency,(2) how the RRAC must be configured to fulfil both space and water heating objectives, and (3) the economic viability of the proposed technology. To address concern (1), a bedroom carefully selected from a typical public housing estate in Hong Kong was used to identify the preferred positioning strategy for thermal comfort and energy efficiency. Experimental measurements, market survey, CFD simulations, EnergyPlus simulations and statistical analyse were employed for the investigations. In the investigations, considering that conventional air diffusion performance index (ADPI) is not an ideal performance indicator for thermal comfort analysis especially for bedroom environments and for heating mode, revised ADPIs were developed. Based on the revised ADPIs, it was found that should higher ADPI (>96.8%) be needed, the RRAC should be installed at a higher level (1.86m) and on the longer side of the bedroom. Further, considering number of RRACs in use in Hong Kong itself can be over 5 million, the energy performance for different positioning strategies for RRACs were investigated. In the investigations, heating and cooling physics-based coil models for positioning the RRAC at low level, which are in absence in literature, were developed. Based on the developed models, energy simulations were conducted. It was found that positioning the RRAC at low level could result in an average energy saving of 34.2 % and 15% for cooling and heating modes respectively, as compared to positioning at high level. To address concern (2), a representative housing estate in Hong Kong consisting of 12,800 residential units was selected for a whole building hour-by-hour energy analysis, aiming to quantify the magnitude of the “surplus” space heating capacity for individual units’ heating demand. This was done using actual equipment performance data, realistic building characteristics, and local climatic conditions. While for the DHW heating demand, reference was made to previous study results on bathing habits of residents in Hong Kong. Detailed supply and demand analysis was carried out to assess the potential use of the proposed technology. It was found that for successful use of the technology, it is necessary to configure the RRAC with a storage tank, and the storage tank must be designed with a minimum heat transfer efficacy of 0.04. An energy and environmental assessment on the proposed technology was also conducted. It was found that the annual heating electricity use of a household can be reduced by 60.1% to 65.4% on average associated with the adoption of the proposed RRAC. A widespread use of the technology has the potential to reduce 7.7% (equivalent to 1,305.6 GWh) of the Hong Kong residential energy consumption and 744,192 t of CO2e emissions. To address concern (3), the tolerable capital cost (TCC) approach was adopted for economic viability analysis. To enhance the robustness of the analysis, a range of electricity price escalation rates (2%, 4% and 6%) and interest rates (3%, 5% and 7%) were considered to address their uncertainties. It was found that the average TCC for individual residential units ranges from HK$983 to HK$11,490 depending on the household size. It was also recommended that government subsidy or incentive programs may be required to promote the technology in the Hong Kong residential market. The total TCC for introducing the technology into all public housing in Hong Kong was found between HK$2.02 billion and HK$6.10 billion depending on the electricity price, interest rate and assumed payback period. The results of this study confirmed the feasible use of RRACs for combined space and DHW heating from thermal comfort, energy, environmental and economic perspectives.

15203817.label: Major findings and research outcome
15203817.value: Residential buildings represent a dominant source of energy consumption in most subtropical cities. To enhance the energy performance of this sector, the use of reversible room air-conditioners (RRACs) for combined space heating and domestic hot water (DHW) production is proposed. Room air-conditioners (RACs) are typically placed at overhead level for cooling of residential environments because this offers better air distribution performance and thermal comfort. However, for the proposed RRACs, they comprise both cooling and heating modes. Whether the same practice of locating RACs at overhead level should continue for air distribution, thermal comfort and energy performance were investigated. As a preliminary enquiry, a bedroom carefully selected from a typical public housing estate in Hong Kong was used to identify the preferred positioning strategy. Experimental measurements, market survey, CFD simulations, EnergyPlus simulations and statistical analyse were employed for the investigations. Considering that conventional air diffusion performance index (ADPI) is not an ideal performance indicator for thermal comfort analysis especially for bedroom environments and for heating mode, revised ADPIs were developed. Based on the revised ADPIs, it was found that should higher ADPI (>96.8%) be needed, the RRAC should be installed at a higher level (1.86m) and on the longer side of the bedroom. Considering number of RRACs in use in Hong Kong itself is over 5 million, the energy performance for different positioning strategies for RRACs were investigated. In the investigations, heating and cooling physics-based coil models for positioning the RRAC at low level, which are in absence in literature, were developed. Based on the developed models, energy simulations were conducted. It was found that positioning the RRAC at low level could result in an average energy saving of 34.2 % and 15% for cooling and heating modes respectively, as compared to positioning at high level. Other than positioning strategy, in order to assess the techno-economic feasibility of the proposed initiative, a representative housing estate in Hong Kong consisting of 12,800 residential units was selected for an extensive simulation study. Results confirmed the technical viability of the proposed system. It was found that the technology has the potential to reduce 7.7% of Hong Kong residential energy consumption and 744,192 t of CO2e emissions. The tolerable capital cost (TCC) approach was adopted for economic viability analysis. The average TCC for individual residential units was found ranging from HK$983 to HK$11,490 depending on the household size, electricity price, and economic settings.

15203817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15203817.value: A prototype can be developed for experimental investigations of the proposed technology. Upon experimental investigations, a detailed mathematical model, which is capable of evaluating the dynamic performance of the proposed RRAC under time-varying conditions, can be developed. The availability of the model can overcome the inherent shortcoming associated with experimental investigations, which can only provide discrete performance evaluations.

15203817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15203817.value: Residential buildings represent a predominant source of energy consumption in most subtropical cities. To enhance the energy performance of this sector, the use of reversible room air-conditioners (RRACs) for combined space heating and domestic hot water (DHW) production is proposed. The idea arises from the fact that in subtropical regions RRACs sized for cooling always have excessive heating capacities to allow a parallel production of DHW. To facilitate the wide application of the proposed technology, this study investigated into its positioning strategies, energy efficiency, technical viability, and economic performance. The results confirm the techno-economic feasibility of the proposed technology and opens a new way for residential energy savings in Hong Kong and elsewhere in the subtropical.

15204717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15204717.value: Many dome structures are shallow with small slopes to allow water drainage and prevention of water ponding during heavy rain, which induce additional loads. These structures are commonly cladded by glass panels to provide an aesthetic appearance and architecture. This structural form is welcomed in society and has been widely used as roofs and covers for unobstructed areas like train stations and swimming pools. The use of tapering sections not only makes the structure more economical by reducing the weight of the steel material, but it also makes the dome more aesthetics. With technology in computer aided drafting (CAD) in fabrication and automatic welding of tapering fabricated sections, production of space frames and non-prismatic members can be done economically and reliably to date, as seen in a project competed by the proposer in Figure 1 in appendix of this proposal. Although effective length method of design is still common in practice, advanced analysis has become popular in many national steel design codes and it represents a conflict between practice and technology. Advanced or direct analysis has been recommended in many national steel design codes. The method allows for geometric and material non-linearities under static and dynamic loads and effective length is not required to be assumed in the design process. However, these works are mostly devoted to conventional building frames and little work was done on single layer dome structures widely used in city commercial complex, aircraft hangar and stadia. The use of this better design method is particularly important for shallow domes which are prone to snap-through buckling. Collapse of a shallow dome in Netherland on 7th July 2011 during heavy snow, and recently on 2nd May 2016 in City University as seen in Figure 2 in Appendix of this proposal in Hong Kong showed the danger of this structural form. This project will improve the design and progressive collapse could also be prevented. The method for limit state design has been applied to design of a number of building frames and detailed in Chapter 6 of the steel code in Hong Kong, of which the proposer is the first principal consultant that he has experience in putting new theory to practice (see http://www.bd.gov.hk/english/documents/index_crlist.html ). This projects aims to formulate a practical advanced analysis method for design of domes made of tapering members prone to snap-through buckling which is not well covered in many design codes. 衆多穹頂結構的頂部都具有輕微的傾斜度以便於排水， 爲避免雨水在暴雨中過度積聚以產生額外荷載。爲了 美觀及建築要求，這類屋頂結構通常以玻璃面板覆蓋。 這類結構深受歡迎，常作爲屋頂結構用于火車站和游 泳池等空曠區域。在這類結構中采用變截面桿件不但 減小材料使用和更爲經濟，并可讓屋頂結構更爲美觀。 伴隨著電腦輔助設計技術及自動化焊接技術的發展， 現今已經可大規模製作和使用變截面桿件，并且經濟 和可靠。正如本計劃書附錄1中的圖片所示，為申請 人參與和完成的項目，其中大量使用變節目桿件。 雖然在目前工程實踐中仍然采用有效長度設計法，在許 多國家鋼結構設計規範中，已包含高等分析法。可見工 程實踐和科技發展之間存在矛盾。很多國家鋼結構設計 規范都推薦使用高等或者直接分析設計法。該方法允許 在靜力和動力作用下，直接模擬幾何和材料非綫性，并 且在設計過程中無需假設有效長度。但是，大部分研究 都主要針對常規建築結構，儘管單層穹頂結構在城市中 廣汎使用，如商場、停機庫和體育館等，但對於這類結 構的高等分析研究仍然非常有限。采用高等分析的另一 重要好處是更好的設計淺穹頂結構，以避免其發生跳躍 失穩。例如荷蘭的一個淺穹頂在2011年7月7日在大 雪下發生坍塌，還有香港城市大學的屋頂在2016年5月 的倒塌（如附錄中圖片2所示），可見這類結構若發 生倒塌的危險性。該項目可以改進這類結構設計，以避免發 生類似的坍塌。極限設計方法已經廣汎應用在大量建築結 構中，并且在香港鋼結構設計規範的第六章中有詳細描述， 而本項目申請人為本規範的第一主要顧問 (見http://www.bd.gov.hk/english/documents/index_crlist.html) ，有充分的經驗將新理論運用於實踐。許多設計規范并無包 含避免淺穹頂發生跳躍失穩的設計方法，本項目將對由變截 面桿件構建的淺穹頂結構，提出具有實用性的高等分析法。

15204917.value: 復雜實時任務系統之高效分析

15204917.label: Project Objectives
15204917.value: To study highly efficient techniques to analyze schedulability of complex real-time task systems modeled as timed automata. To develop a novel framework based on task-centric compositional analysis and busy-period oriented workload quantification and address technical challenges within this framework, including defining proper workload abstractions and performing precise yet efficient analysis on both the task and system level. To understand the difference and relation between the models, abstractions and techniques of the two areas, real-time scheduling and model-checking, and gain a better understanding the strength and limitation of each. To bridge, integrate and even unify them for new theories and techniques for real-time system modeling and analysis. To understand the influence of different models on the accuracy of the system modeling and analysis. To study the tradeoff between the precision loss in the modeling and analysis phases under different modeling/analysis frameworks. To validate the proposed approaches by tool implementation and evaluation with both synthetic task systems and realistic cast studies.

15204917.value: 計算機系統與正在愈加緊密地整合入周圍的物理環境中。為了匹配物理世界固有的動態規律，計算需要具備實時性。許多實時系統是安全關鍵性的，其時間約束必須在所有情況之下都得到保障。提供此保障的一種有效方式是對系統進行形式化建模，並在此基礎上證明其時間正確性。 實時系統建模與分析方面之研究主要在兩個領域內開展：實時調度與模型檢測。兩個領域在過去的幾十年裡都取得了重大成就，但也都存在固有之局限性。在實時調度中，系統被描述成抽像程度較高的模型（如周期性任務模型）。盡管這些模型能夠被高效地分析，它們往往因過於簡單而無法對復雜系統進行建模。相比之下，模型檢測使用表達能力很強的建模語言（如時間自動機），其分析問題復雜度通常非常高，因此在實際使用中受限於其低下的分析效率。隨著現代實時系統的規模和復雜度的快速提升，上述局限性變得更加顯著。 本項目之目標為探索解決上述兩個領域局限性的新方法，在提供類似於模型檢測中表達能力很強的建模語言的同時，又具有與實時調度方法相似的高分析效率。確切地說，我們將使用廣為人知的時間自動機作為建模語言，並研究如何對建模成時間自動機網絡的系統進行高效的可調度性分析。我們提出一個新的分析方法框架，該框架與基於狀態空間搜索的模型檢測分析方法有本質的不同。其中，我們的方法具有以下顯著的特點： （1）以任務為中心的組合分析。模型檢測方法對全部的自動機組件求笛卡爾集，這通常會導致組合爆炸。相比之下，我們的方法首先分析每個單獨的任務，然後將任務級信息進行組合來進行系統級分析。這兩個步驟進行迭代，從而對分析結果逐漸進行精煉以控制分析精度。 （2）量化的負載分析。模型檢查方法通過（顯式地或隱式地）在狀態空間中搜索對應於截止期錯失的壞狀態來進行可調度性分析。相比之下，我們的方法通過定量計算截止期錯失可能發生的某些特定時間區間（即所謂的忙碌期）內系統的負載總量來分析可調度性。 我們的方法面臨許多技術挑戰，其中包括定義適合的負載抽像，高效地從復雜的時間自動機模型中計算出任務負載，處理任務間的依賴關系以及在系統級分析中維持精確度。為了解決這些問題，我們將利用實時調度和模型檢測兩個領域中各自獨立發展而來的成功思想和技術。本項目的終極目標是理解兩個領域中所使用的模型、抽像與技術的關系。通過對它們進行連接、整合乃至統一，本項目期望開拓一個新的研究前沿，為復雜和大規模實時系統的設計提供更好的支撐。

15204917.label: Realisation of objectives
15204917.value: The project objectives are achieved. During the project, we studied efficient analysis techniques of several graph-based real-time task models with different features. The analysis techniques are based on the preliminary idea presented in the proposal, but with significant extensions on the techniques of computing demand of workload and composing them into system-level analysis. Through the study, we gained a deep understanding on the difference and relation between the models, abstractions and techniques of real-time scheduling and model-checking, and the influence of different models on the accuracy of the system modeling and analysis. We also have implemented the developed techniques and evaluated them with both synthetic task systems and realistic case studies.

15204917.label: Major findings and research outcome
15204917.value: In this paper, we aim to exploit the possibility of applying efficient analysis techniques rooted in real-time scheduling theory to analysis of real-time task systems modeled by several expressive graph-based task models, and eventually apply and extend these techniques to the very expressive model timed automata with tasks (TAT) as reported in [31]. We develop efficient techniques to analyze the feasibility of TAT-based task models (i.e., whether all tasks can meet their deadlines on single-processor) using demand bound functions (DBF), a widely used workload abstraction in real-time scheduling theory. Our proposed analysis method has a pseudo-polynomial time complexity if the number of clocks used to model each task is bounded by a constant, which is much lower than the exponential complexity of the traditional model-checking based analysis approach (also assuming the number of clocks is bounded by a constant). We apply dynamic programming techniques to implement the DBF-based analysis framework, and propose state space pruning techniques to accelerate the analysis process. Experimental results show that our techniques can model complex real-time systems accurately and analyze them very efficiently. We also worked on applying the expressive models and the efficient analysis techniques to realistic case studies.

15204917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15204917.value: We will consider to extend the work on applying the expressive models and the efficient analysis techniques to realistic case studies. In particular, the computing system of autonomous driving systems is a very complex real-time system which do not have a solid theoretical foundation for analysis. We will consider to apply and extend the results of this project to model and analyze the computing system of autonomous driving systems and validate the methodology framework together with our industry partners.

15204917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15204917.value: Computing systems are more and more closely integrated into the physical environment. In order to match the inherent dynamics of the physical world, computing must be performed in real-time. Many real-time systems are safe-critical, where timing constraints must be respected under any circumstance. Research on modeling and analysis of real-time systems has been done in two areas: real-time scheduling and model-checking, both of which have some inherent limitations. In real-time scheduling, systems are described with abstract models, which although can be analyzed efficiently, are often too simple to represent complex systems. By contrast, model-checking uses expressive modeling languages (e.g., timed automata), the analysis problems of which are typically very expensive, and its practical usage is limited by the low analysis efficiency. In this project, we investigated a new approach to address the limitations of both areas, providing expressive modeling languages as in model-checking and high analysis efficiency as in real-time scheduling at the same time. More specifically, we use the well-known timed automata as the modeling language, and study how to efficiently analyze the schedulability of systems modeled as timed automata networks. We propose an analysis framework that is fundamentally different from the model-checking based analysis that searches over the resulting state-space.

15205617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15205617.value: Ultrasound is widely used to view internal organs in the human body. It is also applied extensively in engineering to find defects in mechanical components. In both cases sound is used because it penetrates through optically opaque objects. Optics is, nevertheless, very useful for the detection of sound waves and one of the most common methods is the so-called optical resonator. This device deforms very slightly due to the mechanical pressure imposed by the sound wave, this change in dimension is detected by the optical beam and converted to a variation in the amount of light reflected from the unit. Optical detection is very valuable because it is both highly sensitive and there is no need for wires or electrical contact; this means that one can measure the signals remotely. It also means that it is possible to measure many points simultaneously without complicated wiring and interference between different channels. The present project will develop novel ultrasound detectors with greatly improved sensitivity. The reason for this increased sensitivity is related to the so-called Q which indicates how well a structure stores energy. High Q means that it stores energy for a long time with small losses, this in, turn, leads to great sensitivity. In a normal resonator the light is reflected backwards and forward with metallic mirrors, even the best mirrors lose energy on reflection so the Q degrades leading to a reduction in sensitivity. People have used so-called dielectric mirrors but these require large numbers of layers. our approach involves a diffraction grating, which we will make with a simple stamping process, this allows two different waves to travel, when they reach the end of the structure they will interfere with each other to give very strong reflections hence very high Q values. These make very compact and efficient devices. There is more! The high sensitivity is very useful when we have weak signals, but when the signals are strong the detector saturates (you cannot weigh a car on kitchen scales!). It turns out that the rich behaviour of these resonators has some regions where the response is much less sensitive where we can measure the large signals. We can therefore measure over an unprecedented range of signal strengths, something not possible with existing technology. There will also be other applications of these sensors to detect biological molecules and we will also investigate the potential in this area. 超声波检测在对人体内器官的成像方面有广泛的应用，在工程上也使用其来探测机械部件中的缺陷。在以上两例中，声波由于其可以穿透光学不透明的物体而被采用。然而，光学方法却是一个非常好的检测超声波的工具，其中最常用的就是光学谐振腔。整个谐振腔会随着声波带来的压强而发生弹性形变，弹性形变会引起谐振腔谐振位置的改变从而改变谐振腔反射的光强度。由于其灵敏度非常高，而且不需要接触，也就意味着可以远程的测量信号强度，使得光学检测方法非常有价值。这也意味着同时进行多点测量而不需要复杂的接线或者消除不同信道之间的干扰。这个项目会研发一种全新的大幅度提升灵敏度的超声波检测装置。大幅度提升灵敏度的原因是大幅提升了可以反映装置储能能力的品质因数。高的品质因数意味着装置可以在同样时间储存同样的能量而损失较小。反过来，这也就实现了高的灵敏度。在一个传统的谐振腔中，光在两个金属镜面之间来回反射，而最好的金属面也会损失能量，也就会因为品质因数下降，从而降低灵敏度。如果采用绝缘镜面则会需要很多层来实现目标。我们的方法采用了一层衍射光栅（可以通过简单的压印方法制得），这层光栅只允许两个不同的波通过，而他们到达装置后端时，会互相发生干涉而产生一个很强的反射信号，也就产生了一个很高的品质因数。这是一个非常微型和有效率的装置。不仅如此，一般来说，高的灵敏度装置对于弱信号来说非常有优势，而当信号特别强，信号就会超过装置的动态范围而引起测量误差（就比如不能用厨房的秤来称汽车）。而我们的装置中，由于这些谐振腔中的丰富的特性，谐振峰中有很多的不同的灵敏度，我们可以采用低灵敏度的部分测量大信号。于是我们可以测量的信号强度范围十分的广泛，现时还没有装置可以达到的广泛。这个光学谐振腔也有很多其他的应用比如用于检测生物分子等等，我们也会对这方面进行研究。

15205817.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15205817.value: 基於新型三饋無刷永磁發電機的獨立風能AC/DC供電系統的研究

15205817.label: Project Objectives
15205817.value: A triply-fed PM machine based stand-alone wind power generation systems for DC and AC energy supply will be developed. Aiming to realize the simultaneous and individual AC/DC supply, winding switching technology which can flexible control the winding split and combination, is proposed. To keep the DC voltage constant over a wide speed range, winding phase shifting strategy which can online control the phase angular difference of the power windings, is proposed. The important design parameters will be optimized and the topology having the best overall performances will be constructed and extensively tested to verify the design concept against theoretical analysis and numerical method simulations.

15205817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15205817.value: 此項目研究目的是為偏遠或者獨立社區, 研發下一代提供混合AC/DC能量供應的獨立風力發電系統。此系統特點是用單一電機實現恆定的 DC電壓和具有恆壓恆頻的AC電能供應。本項目研究的電機具有靈活的繞組分配和組合功能以及先進的繞組相位控制策略，從而可以滿足孤立社區的恆定交流電壓/頻率的要求，從而消除昂貴的大容量電力電子轉換器件。 到目前為止，仍有近15億人口或超過世界人口的五分之一生活在偏遠地區，無法享受穩定電力供應，因為延伸電網到這些農村或島嶼的經濟代價是昂貴的。獨立風力發電系統可以有效解決這個問題。然而，隨著DC負載，能量存貯，及電源系統發展的多元化，如果將DC技術整合到現有的AC發電系統中將會是成本節約和提高能量利用效率的一個很好的策略。。因此，獨立的DC/AC電源供電系統已經成為趨勢。在未來研究中，如何為混合交直流電系統設計有效的風力發電機已被納入議程。在這個項目中，我們提出一種新型的三相饋無刷永磁發電機，來滿足混合DC/AC電源供電系統中的具有挑戰性要求。 三饋無刷PM發電機是PI提出的一種新型的電機設計概念。這種特殊的風力發電機是基於雙向通量調制理論設計而成。它具有很多優點。首先，基於無刷永磁電機的三相供電發電系統具有高效率和高可靠性，而其轉矩密度以及功率密度都有提高。其次，采用繞組開關控制策略，繞組分合組合控制可以實現同時或單獨的交流和直流能量供應的要求。第三，根據在線相移的控制策略，電壓可以在寬風速範圍內保持恆定。 擬建風力發電機設計符合以下要求：轉矩（0-60 Nm），轉速（〜150 rpm），體積（<9000 cm3），效率（92-94％）。此項目提出的電機設計的標准包括定子 設計（優化槽形，最佳槽/極對數組合），轉子設計（優化PM和磁通調制段形狀，磁通路徑優化，磁芯損耗最小化，可靠的機械設計的轉子結構）和相關的繞組切換和相移控制策略將進行徹底調查。 PI和她的團隊在電機設計和應用方面擁有豐富的研究經驗。繞組相移方法用於寬範圍電壓/頻率調節的設計以及繞組切換策略是具有很高的創新型，將其應用於獨立風力發電系統中提供混合AC / DC供電研究具有極大的挑戰性和重要性。

15205817.label: Realisation of objectives
15205817.value: Aiming to improve the electricity accessibility to remote communities as well as mitigate environmental pollutions problems, wind energy based isolated power generation technologies are under rapid development. Nowadays, more and more dc loads, dc energy storage systems have emerged in the regional power systems. DC technologies have started to be integrated into existing AC systems step by step, which leads to the emergence of hybrid AC/DC power supply system. At present, stand-alone wind power generators designed for AC supply application have been comprehensively studied but brushless permanent magnet generator designed particularly for integrated DC/AC supply is very limited. The stand-alone brushless PM wind power generation system with simplified power conversion circuit, which can supply simultaneous or individual DC and AC energy is the main objective of this project. We successfully realized the following objectives: 1) A triply-fed PM machine based stand-alone wind power generation systems for DC and AC energy supply has be developed. In the following paper, a new parameter identification method of a dual-rotor triply-fed PM flux-modulation machine based on an adaptive differential evolution algorithm is investigated. Y. Mao, S. Niu and Y. Yang, “A new parameter identification method of a dual-rotor flux-modulation machine based on an adaptive differential evolution algorithm” IET renewable power generation, 6 July 2021, v. 15, no. 9, p. 1888-1897. With the wide applications of dual-rotor flux-modulation machines for the growing wind power generations, research activities for the control of dual-rotor flux-modulation machines are intensified in recent years. Most of the existing control schemes are based on indirect measurements of the d-axis inductance, the q-axis inductance and the stator resistance to achieve high torque density and low torque ripple for the dual-rotor flux modulation machines. However, conventional measurements of the d-axis inductance, the q-axis inductance and the stator resistance may suffer from (i) low accuracy and (ii) addi tional sensor costs. To this end, an adaptive differential evolution algorithm is proposed to identify the machine parameters by considering the magnetic saturation and cross-coupling issue at low rotational speed of dual-rotor flux-modulation machines. Finite element analysis is adopted in simulation to preliminarily monitor the actual machine parameter values based on the length and cross section area of the conductor and inductance matrix com putation. Both simulation and experimental results reveal that the adopted adaptive differ ential evolution algorithm can identify the three parameters more steadily and accurately than the conventional genetic algorithm 2) Aiming to realize the simultaneous and individual AC/DC supply, winding switching technology which can flexible control the winding split and combination, has been investigated. To keep the DC voltage constant over a wide speed range, winding phase shifting strategy which can online control the phase angular difference of the power windings, has been developed. Winding switching technology has been mainly investigated in the following paper. J. Jiang, X. Zhang, X. Zhao and S. Niu, "A Novel Winding Switching Control Strategy for AC/DC Hybrid-Excited Wind Power Generator," in IEEE Transactions on Magnetics, vol. 57, no. 6, pp. 1-4, June 2021, Art no. 8700204, doi: 10.1109/TMAG.2021.3074926. Winding switching strategy has been used to extend speed range of the machine. In this article, a novel winding switching strategy is proposed to improve the flux-weakening capability of a hybrid-excited reluctance machine (HERM). The key is that in low-speed operation, the primary and the secondary windings are connected in series and serve as armature winding to maximize output voltage while in high-speed operation, the secondary winding is switched to dc excitation winding to realize variable speed constant voltage output. The machine configuration, operation principle with dual excitation sources, winding switching concept, and manipulation circuit are illustrated in detail. Then the electromagnetic characteristics of HERM in different operation status are investigated. Finally, the variable speed constant voltage output of wind power generation system resorting to winding switching as well as dc excitation regulation is verified with Maxwell/Simplorer cosimulation. 3) The important design parameters have be optimized and the topology having the best overall performances have been constructed and extensively tested to verify the design concept against theoretical analysis and numerical method simulations. The machine design and optimization have been mainly investigated in the following paper. Q. Lin, S. Niu, H, Wu and W. Fu, “Design and optimisation of a bidirectional flux modulation machine for AC and DC power supplies” IET renewable power generation, 6 July 2021, v. 15, no. 9, p. 1996-2006. This study proposes a novel power supply system that utilises wind power to produce AC and DC power. The wind energy captured by the system can be increased with the design of dual wind blades, and thus the Cp will be increased. In addition, with dual stator windings, AC and DC power can be produced simultaneously, and electrical isolation can be realised. The organisation of this study is as follows. The composition of the system will be introduced first. Then, the generator and its operation principles and the design guidelines will be introduced. The magnetic field and the induced voltage of the proposed generator will be analysed theoretically. In the third part, the design optimisation of the machine is conducted. The combinations of stator slots, outer rotor pole pairs, and inner rotor pole pairs will be investigated first. Then, the machine with preferable performances will be selected out for further optimisation. The simulation results of the proposed generator including magnetic field, induced AC voltage, and rectified DC voltage will be shown. In the fourth section, a prototype of the proposed machine is made and the experiment results validate the effectiveness of the design. A special designed generator based on bidirectional flux modulation effect is the key part of the proposed power supply system. The novel power system has a compact structure since the proposed generator has two electric port. There are three essential points that make the proposed system outstanding. One is the contra-rotating rotors, which will cluster wind power even under low wind speed. Second one is the dual armature winding structure, which will provide AC and DC power simultaneously. There are two electric port in the proposed generator. One port can produce AC power to the non-sensitive resistive load. The other can provide AC power with different frequency to the rectifier to obtain DC power. The induced voltage due to flux modulation effect can be used to offer AC power, and the induced voltage due to the outer rotor can be used to offer DC power. The voltage frequency of two sets windings is different. The last one is the air gap flux rotation speed amplification due to flux modulation effect. Time stepping finite element method is used to analyse the dynamic performance of the proposed machine.

15206517.label: Project Objectives
15206517.value: To understand the morphological and biomechanical differences between a normal foot and a hallux valgus foot; To investigate the biomechanical effects of intrinsic factors (bone deformities, ligament and/or tendon weakness) and extrinsic factors (shoe support) on the progression of hallux valgus; and To provide biomechanical data on the effectiveness of orthotic interventions and surgical treatments for hallux valgus.

15206517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15206517.value: Deformities or defects of the foot are relatively common and can have a significant impact on a person’s quality of life. Hallux valgus is a frequently-observed deformity which causes joint pain and increases the risk of falling. Etiological studies have been published on this condition but overall fail to reach a consensus on its origin. Orthotics may be offered for pain relief, but it is questionable whether this method of intervention can hinder further deterioration of the foot. Surgical intervention can correct the deformity and offer relatively longer-lasting relief. However, the incidence of surgical complications, recurrence and post-operative outcomes rely heavily on surgical protocols. There is insufficient quantitative data available to support the choice of one treatment method over another. In this study, based on our previous research into the biomechanics of normal foot, a series of experimental studies will be conducted to better understand the hallux valgus condition, and a comprehensive computational platform will be developed to model the pathomechanics of a hallux valgus foot and to provide biomechanical information for evaluating the effectiveness of various clinical treatment methods. Gait analyses, plantar pressure and shear stress measurements will be conducted to acquire kinematic and kinetic information during standing and walking. A musculoskeletal model will be used to estimate corresponding joint and muscles forces. Finite element models of an entire hallux valgus foot will be developed with detailed anatomical structures. The model will be validated through comparison with experimental measurements of the model subject. Inadequate foot support, such as when wearing high-heeled shoes, has been charged with imposing excessive loading on the first ray and excessive valgus moments on the first tarsometatarsal joint, which can potentially progress an already deteriorating deformity. As such, the effects of heel height as well as typical surgical and orthotic interventions will be evaluated using the validated finite element model. Parametric analyses will be conducted on the designs and protocols of the interventions. The parameters of interest include these geometrical and load-transfer parameters reflect the immediate effects of realignment on the entire foot. The outcome of this study can provide critical biomechanical information on the pathomechanics of hallux valgus, which is often difficult to assess with experimental studies. A concise biomechanical evaluation of common interventions will provide evidence-based guidance to physicians for selecting suitable treatment methods. 15206517.label: Realisation of objectives
15206517.value: 1. The reconstruction of finite element model from a hallux valgus patient that considered patient-specific structural variation was completed. The model was reconstructed from magnetic resonance images from a representative and typical mild hallux valgus patient featuring thirty bone segments embedded in a volume of encapsulated bulk tissue with the phalanges and sesamoids detailed and segmented. 2. Gait study and analysis was conducted on the model subjects. Lower limb kinematics, kinetics and plantar pressure distribution of the model subjects performing self-preferred speed walking was acquired. The participant walked in three conditions, including barefoot walking and walking with two kinds of toe spacers. For each condition, five walking trials were performed to ensure repeatability. Data including the joint angles, moments, power of the ankle, knee and hip joints, as well as the regional peak and time-integral of the plantar pressure were processed for each condition and trial. 3. Based on the input from the in vivo experiments, the muscle forces were predicted using an open source musculoskeletal model system. The muscles forces of the foot-shank segments, including triceps surae (tendon Achilles), tibialis anterior, tibialis posterior, fibularis longus, fibular brevis, extensor and flexor hallucis and digitorium longus, etc, were predicted. 4. Using the input from the in vivo experiments and musculoskeletal model, a baseline simulation was conducted. The predicted plantar pressure distribution was compared to the measured plantar pressure distribution for validation. The model and simulation settings were optimized and ready for subsequent analysis. 5. Three proposed intrinsic factors were examined and simulated to investigate their relationship with potential deterioration of hallux valgus. The three intrinsic factors were generalized ligament laxity, laxity of the deep transverse metatarsal ligament and the laxity of the medial metatarsosesamoid ligament. The independent factors were facilitated by the reduction of stiffness on the dedicated ligaments, while a sensitivity test on the degree of reduction was also conducted. The outcome measures and evaluation metrics were the metatarsus primus varus angle and the hallux valgus angle between the baseline and the laxity states; the load bearing ratio between the medial and lateral metatarsals, and the direction of load of the first ray. The simulation and data analysis has been completed.

15206517.label: Major findings and research outcome
15206517.value: In this study, we reconstructed a finite element model of a hallux valgus foot from a patient and drove the simulation by gait analysis, and musculoskeletal model (muscle estimation) from the model participant. While the model was validated by plantar pressure measurement of the model participant, a parametric analysis was conducted to examine the influence of levels of generalized ligament laxity on the biomechanical responses of the foot, in which the laxity was mimicked by impoverishing the stiffness of the ligaments. Our simulation study reported that generalized ligament laxity deteriorated hallux valgus by impairing the loadbearing capacity of the first metatarsal, inducing higher deforming force, moment and malalignment at the first metatarsophalangeal joint. There were significant increases of hallux valgus angle at second peak instants, and the intermetatarsal angle at all examined instants. The maximum von mises stress of the first metatarsal was significantly lower for the laxity case compared to the intact condition. The joint force direction for the metatarsophalangeal and metatarsocuneiform joints was lateralized with significant increases of abduction moment. Besides, the deforming moment formed a deteriorating vicious cycle between hallux valgus and forefoot abduction and may result in secondary foot problems, such as flatfoot. However, the metatarsocuneiform joint did not show a worsening trend possibly due to the overriding forefoot abduction. Controlling the deforming load shall be prioritized over the correction of angles to mitigate deterioration or recurrence after surgery.

15206517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15206517.value: This study will focus on gaining a solid biomechanical understanding of hallux valgus and the progression of the deformity. This study will develop a platform which integrates experimental and computational data to address this clinical problem. The findings of this project will provide additional biomechanical evidence to support the selection of appropriate conservative and surgical interventions for treating hallux valgus. Future studies may consider investigating the extrinsic and intrinsic mechanical causes of hallux valgus and how they interact resulting in the progression of the deformity. For example, the consideration of a high-heeled shoe gait with different heel heights and tightened toe-box on the interaction with generalized ligament laxity. It would be beneficial to know on how to adjust the shank curve or arch support of the high-heeled shoe that could reduce the progression risks of hallux valgus.

15206517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15206517.value: Generalized ligament laxity may deteriorate hallux valgus and influence surgical decisions but is difficult to evaluate because of multiple risk factors. In this study, we aimed to evaluate the isolated influence of generalized ligament laxity on the deterioration using computer simulation (finite element analysis). We reconstructed a foot model from a mild hallux valgus participant and conducted gait analyses to drive the simulation. Different levels of laxity were mimicked by impoverishing ligament stiffness in the simulation. Our results showed that hallux valgus with generalized ligament laxity impaired the load-carrying capacity of the foot’s first column, and deforming load could result in further malalignment at the metatarsophalangeal joint. The high level of forefoot abduction was alarming. The correction of deforming load shall be as important as correcting the malalignment in the deformity. The significance of this research lies in its potential to identify the biomechanical consequence of the aggravating factor (generalized ligament laxity) on hallux valgus and provide evidence to initiate future intervention design from a biomechanical point of perspective.

15206617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15206617.value: Flash-based SSD RAID Arrays (SSAs) are increasingly being deployed in data centers. Compared with HDD (Hard Disk Drive) arrays, SSAs can drastically enhance IO performance and density, and reduce power, cooling, rack space. Nevertheless, SSAs suffer aging issues. Specially, an SSD has the limited endurance and needs to be replaced when it reaches to its lifetime. Although several studies have been conducted to address this disadvantage, effective mechanisms and techniques are still urgently needed for two critical problems, namely, extending the lifespan of SSAs and reducing the reconstruction time under heavy workloads. We will focus on investigating these in this project. To optimize the lifespan of SSAs, we will for the first time apply approximate storage via the interplay of RAID and SSD controllers. With approximate storage, bad blocks that contain pages with uncorrectable errors can be reused to store approximate data that can tolerate more errors. By doing this, our preliminary studies demonstrate that we can extend the endurance of NAND flash by more than 6 times, thereby providing huge potentials for significantly extending the lifespan of SSAs. However, to exploit approximate storage in SSAs, we need new mechanisms and techniques to coordinate RAID and SSD controllers and manage both approximate and ordinary data, which will be investigated in this project. The RAID reconstruction time of SSAs due to a disk failure can be greatly reduced when there are no or light IO workloads with new technology such as Distributed RAID from IBM. However, with heavy workloads, RAID controllers are fully occupied and cannot efficiently process reconstruction tasks, so it still takes too long (e.g. more than 10 hours for a 4 TB disk) to complete data reconstruction with intensive host inputs/outputs. In this project, we will for the first time utilize the computing power of SSDs, so reconstruction tasks can be processed in a distributed manner. We will study how to efficiently schedule reconstruction tasks so they can be efficiently performed in SSDs. The failure model of SSAs and proactive reconstruction with predictive scheduling and early data migration will be investigated as well. The proposed research will facilitate data intensive computing systems such as data centers to most effectively utilize SSAs. As big data applications, such as real-time data analytics, play an essential role in international business, trade and finance, this project is particularly important for Hong Kong. 閃存固態盤陣列在數據中心中得到越來越多的部署。 與硬盤陣列相比，固態盤陣列極大地提高了IO性能 和存儲密度，並減少了能耗、 散熱和機架佔用空間。 然而，固態盤陣列存在老化問題，也就是，因固態 盤有限定的使用壽命，一旦達到壽命就需要被替換。 因而急需更加有效的機制和技術以延長固態盤陣列 的壽命和減少在重負載下的重構時間。本課題將針 對這兩個問題進行研究。 為了延長固態盤陣列的壽命，我們將首次利用RAID 和SSD的交互作用在近似存儲基礎上開展研究。利 用近似儲存，固態盤中包含不可修復錯誤的壞塊可 以被再次利用來存儲有一定錯誤容忍度的近似數據。 我們的初步研究表明，基於此技術，NAND閃存的 壽命可以延長超過6倍，這為大幅度延長固態盤陣 列的壽命提供了有力的支撐。在本課題中，我們將 研究在固態盤陣列中應用近似存儲所需的新的機制 和技術，來協調RAID和SSD控制器有效地管理常規 數據和近似數據。 在沒有負載或輕負載情況下，新的技術比如IBM的 分布式RAID，可以大幅度減少RAID固態盤陣列中 單個設備故障的重構時間。然而，在重負載下，因 為RAID控制器處於高負荷狀態，無法高效的處理重 構任務，這就導致了在重負載下數據重構工作需要 很長的時間（比如需要超過10小時來完成一個4TB 的硬盤重構）。在本課題中，我們將首次利用固態 盤的計算能力，使得重構工作能夠以分布式的形式 在固態盤上進行處理。我們將研究如何高效的調度 重構工作以有效地減少重構時間。此外，我們也會 研究固態盤陣列的故障模型，並開發基於可預測調 度和早期數據遷移的主動式重構技術。 本課題的研究將會促進諸如數據中心的數據密集型 計算系統更好地利用固態盤陣列。大數據分析、 應用在國際商務、貿易和金融中起著關鍵作用， 因此本課題對於香港有著特別意義。

15206617.label: Realisation of objectives
15206617.value: The project has been going very well, and all objectives have been 100% achieved. With the support of this fund, one PhD student (HAN, Lei) at HK PolyU was recruited and passed his defense in March 2019; two PhD students (WANG, Tiany and WANG, Zhiqi) at CUHK, partially supported by this grant, were enrolled in August 2019 and are expected to graduated in July 2023. One undergraduate student (SHANG, Siqi) at CUHK, was recruited to conduct undergraduate research and graduated in 2021. In total, 4 journal papers and 4 conference papers have been published. Objective 1 has been 100% achieved. For Objective 1, our research was carried out from the following two aspects: (1) Approximate Storage: In [C1, J3], we apply approximate storage via the interplay of RAID and SSD controllers to optimize the lifespan of SSD arrays. Our basic idea is to reuse faulty blocks (those contain pages with uncorrectable errors) to store approximate data (which can tolerate more errors). By relaxing the integrity of ﬂash blocks, we observed that the endurance of NAND ﬂash memory can be significantly boosted, thereby providing huge potentials to significantly extend the lifetime of SSDs. Based on this observation, we propose an efficient space management scheme for data allocation and FTL (Flash Translation Layer) strategies by coordinating the interplay of RAID and SSD controllers to optimize the lifetime of SSD arrays. We implement a prototype, called FreeRAID, based on an SSD array simulator. Our experiments show that we can significantly increase the lifetime by up to 2.17× compared with conventional SSD-based RAID arrays. Moreover, in [C4, J4], an FTL, called Rebirth-FTL, has been proposed to effectively manage approximate space and normal space with approximate storage in NAND flash systems. (2) Shingled Magnetic Recording (SMR): SMR has huge potential to significantly increase the disk capacity and reduce the cost of RAID so we also investigated effective techniques to optimize SMR disks. In [J2], we address the hot-data write-back effect. Due to write constraints, SMR disks prohibit random writes. To solve this, current solutions utilize a persistent cache to change random writes to sequential ones. By doing this, nevertheless, the hot-data write-back effect will be triggered which inevitably incurs extra read-modify-write operations. We propose a cache management scheme called Dual-buffer to manage the overall SMR space, by which the persistent cache is partitioned into the persistent buffer and the filter buffer. It leaves hot data in the filter buffer and moves cold data back to the SMR disk so that the hot data write-back effect can be alleviated. Since the persistent cache may contain a large amount of valid data, Dual-buffer also presents a prediction-based dynamic configuration strategy so hot data can be cached as much as possible. We conducted a series of experiments with synthetic traces. Experimental results show that our Dual-buffer scheme can shorten the average response time by 51.66% on average and reduce the total number of read-modify-write operations by 98.76% on average compared to the previous work. Moreover, in [C2], we address optimizing read-modify-writes (RMWs) that greatly challenge the management of SMR disks. Specifically, we for the first time propose a decentralized approach called Tiler to manage the SMR disks by dividing the physical space into small autonomous regions (ARs). Each AR can manage its space allocation, address mapping and cleaning independently. By managing these ARs, Tiler is capable of partitioning a centralized-large-scale cleaning into self-contained-small-scale cleaning. In this design, Tiler not only limits cleaning inside an AR but also eliminates the need of over-provisioned buffer as well as RMWs. Our experimental results show that Tiler can shorten the overall system average response time by up to 47% and improve the space utilization by up to 1.32X. Objective 2 has been 100% achieved. For Objective 2, we have conducted our research from the following two aspects: (1) SSD optimization. In [J1], we studied the reliability issue caused by power failure. As power failure may occur at any time and result in data loss, crash recovery becomes vitally important in NAND flash storage systems. To solve this, we propose a scheme called DCR (Deterministic Crash Recovery) that adopts a deterministic approach for crash recovery in NAND flash storage systems. The basic idea is to exploit the determinism of FTLs and reproduce events that happened between the last checkpoint and the crash point during crash recovery. Different from existing approaches that need to scan the whole flash memory chip, DCR can recover the system more efficiently by only checking a limited number of blocks based on deterministic FTL operations. We have implemented DCR in an FTL and compared it with the previous works. Experimental results show that DCR can greatly reduce the recovery time and guarantee the consistency of FTL metadata after recovery. Moreover, in [C1, J3], how to accelerate reconstruction with approximate storage has been discussed. (2) NVDIMM-based Heterogeneous Storage: In [C3], we propose a holistic solution to address several important and challenging issues in storage data management in light of emerging NVDIMM-based architecture, namely, new performance modeling, NVDIMM-based migration, and architectural support for NVDIMMs on migration optimization. In particular, a novel NVDIMM-based heterogeneous storage performance model is proposed to effectively address bus contention issues caused by placing NVDIMMs on the memory bus. We also develop an NVDIMM-based lazy migration scheme to effectively minimize adverse effects caused by memory traffic interferences during storage data management processes. Finally, the NVDIMM-based architectural support for migration optimization is proposed to increase channel parallelism in the destination NVDIMMs and bypass buffer caches in the source NVDIMMs, so that the impact of memory traffic can be alleviated. We present detailed evaluation and analysis to quantify how well our techniques can enhance the I/O performances of big workloads via efficient heterogeneous storage hierarchy management. Our experimental results show that overall the proposed techniques yield up to 98% performance improvement over the state-of-the-art techniques. Objective 3 has been 100% achieved. For Objective 3, we have developed various experimental platforms to evaluate the proposed techniques and mechanisms. Specifically, in [C1, J3], we evaluated FreeRAID via a trace-driven simulator, and compare its performance with that of conventional RAID and FTL schemes. FreeRAID is developed based on the heavily-modified existing flash simulator to implement RAID schemes and components. In [C2, J2], our evaluation is based on a simulator to emulate a Seagate ST8000AS0011 8TB SMR disk. In [J1, C4, J4], the proposed FTLs have been implemented on the ARM-based embedded boards with NAND flash storage. In [C3], we evaluate the proposed technique by utilizing Marssx86, DRAMSim2 and NANDFlashSim, in which Marssx86 is a cycle-accurate full-system simulator that uses PTLsim for CPU simulation on top of the QEMU emulator, DRAMSim2 is a cycle-accurate simulator of the main-memory system, and NANDFlashSim is a NAND flash simulator.

With approximate storage, bad blocks that contain pages with uncorrectable errors can be reused to store approximate data that can tolerate more errors. Thus, the lifespan of SSAs can be greatly enhanced. Moreover, with approximate storage, we study how to utilize the computing power of SSDs to accelerate reconstruction tasks in a distributed manner. In summary, the proposed research can facilitate data intensive computing systems such as data centers to most effectively utilize SSAs.

15206717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15206717.value: 在各種結構和機器中，振動是不可避免的，會影響設備精度，降低使用壽命，甚至造成系統損傷。長時間操作振動機械，會給操作者帶來職業疾病。 儘管振動控制已經研究了很多年，實際工程實踐中仍然有很多挑戰性工作，比如性能和可靠性可操作性以及價格的矛盾。本課題旨在通過一類仿生X型結構，研究有效的被動振動控制方法，探索非線性在振動控制中的有效利用，從而建立一套有效的高性能的被動的通過仿生X型結構實現非線性振動控制的新方法。

15206717.label: Realisation of objectives
15206717.value: 1. To explore the potential benefits of the nonlinear stiffness and damping characteristics of various X-shaped structures in vibration control; Passive low-cost high-efficiency in-situ adjustable stiffness systems have not yet been well explored, due to uncertain and unexpected nonlinear behavior within materials and structures, difficulty or limitations in manufacturing or implementation, and various demanding requirements. To address these challenges, we present an efficient stiffness-manipulation method using a flexible and compact X-shaped structure (or mechanism). The resulting nonlinear stiffness systems can be conveniently realized and are capable for achieving various desired stiffness (positive, negative, zero or quasi-zero, multi-stable-equilibria). The inherent nonlinearity of such nonlinear stiffness systems is completely controllable and predictable with simple and reliable mathematical modelling, compared to many other metal materials or foldable mechanisms/structures. Due to the advantages of linkage mechanisms, the X-shaped structure (or mechanism) approach offers superior in-situ adjustability which can be easily achieved via various and simple pre-extension/distance/length/height adjustable mechanisms in practical mechanical designs. The stiffness-manipulation methods demonstrated in this study have also advantages including simplicity and efficiency in manufacturing and assembly, high-quality nonlinearity control and in-situ adjustability, and low-cost part production, without stability issues, manufacturing difficulty and strict material restriction, leading to revolutionary or upgrading technologies to existing engineering systems. 2. To explore applications of the X-shaped structures (such as typical nonlinear absorbers/isolators, energy harvesters, and/or anti-vibration exoskeleton for manipulating heavy-duty jackhammers) with benchmark design, prototyping and testing. To demonstrate the capability of this stiffness manipulation method, a series of application case studies are conducted with prototypes for validation. These results include: (1) a tunable and enlarged quasi-zero or zero stiffness passive vibration isolation platform, with a resonant frequency around 1 Hz in the prototype testing subject to small or large vibration excitation for a given payload; (2) the vibration isolation platform can be designed into a small cube (X-cube) of 10 cm in length and width in the prototype (working height about several cm dependent on the payload) and of capability to be even smaller; (3) a quasi-zero-gravity lifting platform, which can be tuned to be close to zero in a large displacement region, a lifting platform with quasi-zero-gravity property can therefore be readily created and demonstrated; (4) a novel X-shaped absorber of demonstrative performance with respect to traditional one; (5) A novel tracked robot was designed and tested successfully, which has a special X-shaped structure based suspension system such that the robot is more stable when passing rough grounds; (6) A novel sensor system was created based on the X-shaped structure, which is the first one allowing us to measure the absolute vibration displacement of a moving platform accurately; (7) The X-shaped structures can be successfully applied to energy harvesting to significantly improve the energy harvesting efficiency at low frequency and also in a broad frequency band with several prototypes developed. Many other applications can be explored with more innovative technologies to be produced. ITF projects and industrial funded projects would be applied as follow-up R&D activities.

15206717.label: Major findings and research outcome
15206717.value: A desired structural or material stiffness is critical in many engineering systems for structural stability, vibration control, energy saving and manipulation efficiency. However, passive low-cost high-efficiency in-situ adjustable stiffness systems have not yet been well explored, due to uncertain and unexpected nonlinear behavior within materials and structures, difficulty or limitations in manufacturing or implementation, and various demanding requirements. To address these challenges, we present an efficient stiffness-manipulation method using a flexible and compact X-shaped structure (or mechanism). The resulting nonlinear stiffness systems can be conveniently realized and are capable for achieving various desired stiffness (positive, negative, zero or quasi-zero, multi-stable-equilibria). The inherent nonlinearity of such nonlinear stiffness systems is completely controllable and predictable with simple and reliable mathematical modelling, compared to many other metal materials or foldable mechanisms/structures. Due to the advantages of linkage mechanisms, the X-shaped structure (or mechanism) approach offers superior in-situ adjustability which can be easily achieved via various and simple pre-extension/distance/length/height adjustable mechanisms in practical mechanical designs. The stiffness-manipulation methods demonstrated in this study have also advantages including simplicity and efficiency in manufacturing and assembly, high-quality nonlinearity control and in-situ adjustability, and low-cost part production, without stability issues, manufacturing difficulty and strict material restriction, leading to revolutionary or upgrading technologies to existing engineering systems. Theoretical analysis and experimental validation (or case studies) demonstrate the advantages, effectiveness, and great potential of this new approach for exploiting nonlinearities in various engineering applications.

15206717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15206717.value: More X-shaped structures and mechanisms will be studied which have been demonstrated a successful and effective approach to most engineering practice for vibration control. Large grant for industrial applications will be done later with industrial partners.

15206717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15206717.value: In structures and machines, vibration is usually unexpected, which may incur downgrade of instrument accuracy, reduction of operating life, and even destructive damage to systems or human body. Prolonged exposure of human body to vibration may incur serious and invertible occupational diseases such as vibration white fingers. Although vibration control has been studied for many years, there are still a lot of challenging issues related to performance, cost, reliability and easiness of implementation. This project is to explore effective passive vibration control via an X-shaped structural design, to explore purposely nonlinear benefits within structures or geometric relations, and thus to establish efficient and effective analysis and design methods. To these objectives, a very specially-featured structure name as the X-shaped structure is therefore focused in this project. To the best of our knowledge, the X-shaped structures and variants have never been explored as “a source” of beneficial nonlinear stiffness and damping in vibration control (except the preliminary results done by us). The X-shaped structures can provide very tunable stiffness and damping characteristics and are fairly flexible and low-cost for practical application, and thus potentially provide an ideal and innovative solutions to the vibration control problems in a purely passive (cheaper) manner.
