15208217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15208217.value: The inductive power transfer (IPT) system utilizing non-radiative varying magnetic fields to transmit energy efficiently and safely has found many applications in electrical vehicle (EV) charging, home appliances, underwater or mine lighting, biomedical implants, etc. Compared with conventional plug-in systems, IPT systems realize isolation electrically and mechanically, and save cables and sockets to be operated conveniently even in harsh environments. Specifically, in EV charging, the IPT primary supply can be buried underneath the existing parking lots that saves the space for charging stations. Moreover, IPT can realize on-the-road powering of electric vehicle and charging of its battery so that both the capacity and charging time of a battery could be reduced or eliminated. The direct power to the wheel of an EV can greatly improve power efficiency by reducing the loss in power cycles of the intermediate battery storage. Energy can be stored to and retrieved from a shielded system which is nearly impossible without the IPT technology. Similar advantages apply for biomedical implants. However, the constantly varying distance vertically, laterally and longitudinally between the IPT primary supply windings and the secondary pick-up windings is one of the most important obstacles that prevents the development of the next generation IPT systems. The electrical property of this IPT transformer behaves as a pair of varying inductances with a varying coupling coefficient. At a specific coupling coefficient, the IPT transformer can be compensated with external reactive elements and operated efficiently at a particular load and a particular frequency. This optimized operating point deviates a lot for a slight variation of inductances and coupling coefficient. The variations can effectively be overcome by a design with an appropriate adaptive feedback control. The main difficulty is that the coupling coefficient is varying and it is difficult to be measured or predicted during operation, making the control algorithm complicated and slow. This research attempts to solve this problem from the aspects of circuit topology configuration and control method design. The success of this research can help the practical applications of the IPT technology. 利用非輻射變化磁場，高效安全地傳輸能量的感應功率傳輸（IPT）系統已經應用在電動車輛（EV）充電，家用電器，水下或礦山照明，和生物醫學植入物等等。與傳統有插頭系統比較，IPT系統實現了電氣和機械隔離不需要電纜和插座，並且即使在惡劣的環境中也能夠方便地使用。具體來說，在EV充電中，IPT主電源可以埋在現有的停車場下面，從而節省了充電站的空間。此外，IPT可以實現行駛中電動汽車的供電及其電池的充電，從而可以減少或消除電池的容量和充電時間。通過減少充放電池的電力週期的損失，EV到車輪的直接電力功率效率可以大大提高。能量可以被存儲到屏蔽系統並從其獲取，在沒有IPT技術的情況下這幾乎是不可能。類似的優點適用於生物醫學植入物。然而，IPT主電源繞組和次級繞組之間的垂直，橫向和縱向上的不斷變化的距離是防止下一代IPT系統發展的最重要的障礙之一。該IPT變壓器的電氣特性表現為一對具有變化耦合係數的變化電感。在特定的耦合係數下，IPT變壓器可以用外部無功元件進行補償，並在特定負載和特定頻率下有效地工作。該優化的工作點對於電感和耦合係數的輕微變化而產生的偏差會很大。通過具有適當的自適應反饋控制的設計可以有效地克服這些變化。主要的困難是耦合係數變化，在運行中難以測量或預測，使控制算法複雜而緩慢。本研究試圖從電路拓撲結構和控制方法設計的角度解決這個問題。這項研究的成功可以幫助IPT技術的實際應用。

15208717.label: Project Objectives
15208717.value: To crystallize perovskite thin films for high-performance PSCs using different laser wavelengths and scanning conditions。 To improve the device efficiency and stability by compositional engineering of the perovskites under laser annealing. To obtain fundamental understanding of the laser-induced crystallization of perovskite grains.

To improve the device efficiency and stability by compositional engineering of the perovskites under laser annealing.
To obtain fundamental understanding of the laser-induced crystallization of perovskite grains.

15208717.label: Realisation of objectives
15208717.value: Objective 1: To crystallize perovskite thin films for high-performance PSCs using different laser wavelengths and scanning conditions. Perovskite films have been annealed under laser with three 405 nm, 450 nm and 660 nm. We found that 450 nm laser led to the largest average grain size of ~476 nm. We consider that this effect can be attributed to the different light absorption coefficients of the perovskite films at different wavelengths. It is noteworthy that the absorbance ratio of the two absorption spectra changes with the light wavelength and peaks at around 450 nm. Therefore, the 450 nm laser can induce the biggest temperature gradient on grain boundaries in perovskite films and provide the largest growth driving force for the perovskite seeds in the as-deposited film. We have studied the influence of scanning speed and laser output power on the morphology of the perovskite films. For the fixed power (150 mW) of the laser, the grain size increased with the decrease of scanning speed and then decreased when the speed was less than 25 mm/min. We found that the surface temperature increased with the decrease of scanning speed and the largest grain size was obtained when the central temperature was 100 C. For a fixed scanning speed of 25 mm/min, the crystallinity increased with the increase of output power and then decreased when the power was over 150 mW. The corresponding surface temperature as a function of output power was also obtained. Both experiments indicated that the maximum grain size was achieved at the central temperature of 100 C, which is consistent with the condition required by a thermal annealing process. Objective 2: To improve the device efficiency and stability by compositional engineering of the perovskites under laser annealing. In addition to the MAPbI3-based PSCs, (CsPbI3)0.05(FAPbI3)0.95-(MAPbBr3)0.05 mixed PSCs were also prepared by using laser annealing approach. The as-deposited mixed perovskite films were annealed by scanning laser beams with wavelengths of 405 nm, 450 nm or 660 nm. The surface temperature distribution of the mixed perovskite film was monitored by the infrared thermal imager. We then prepared mixed PSCs with the same device structure. The device performance was then optimized by controlling the laser power. Under the optimum conditions, we found that the maximum surface temperatures of the perovskite films are all close to 150 C (equal to the optimum thermal-annealing temperature of the control device). Similarly, only a very small area of the perovskite film surface near the beam center shows relatively high temperature, while the surface temperature of the other part of the film is close to the room temperature. The maximum heating rate is about 100 C/s, which cannot be achieved by a normal thermal annealing method. The device efficiency was improved from 20.98% to 21.50% when the composition was changed from MAPbI3 to (CsPbI3)0.05(FAPbI3)0.95-(MAPbBr3)0.05 mixed perovskite. Objective 3: To obtain fundamental understanding of the laser-induced crystallization of perovskite grains. The laser-annealed perovskite films demonstrate larger grain sizes than thermal-annealed samples, which can be attributed to the temperature gradient generated between perovskite seeds and the amorphous components around them due to different light absorption coefficients of the two phases. Under optimum conditions, the average PCE of the devices is relatively improved for about 20% in comparison with the control devices prepared by thermal annealing. By using a linear laser beam, large-area devices can be prepared with a high speed, which paves a way for the mass production of PSCs at a low temperature. To gain a deeper insight into the nature of the outstanding photovoltaic performance of the PSCs prepared by laser-annealing approach, we performed steady-state and time-resolved photoluminescence (PL) measurements of the perovskite films prepared at different conditions. The perovskite films for PL measurements were fabricated on pure glass substrates without FTO layers. It is notable that the optimized laser-annealed perovskite film exhibited more than three-fold increase in PL intensity relative to that of the thermal annealed film. Meanwhile, the PL peak demonstrated a slight blue shift from 768 nm (thermal-annealing) to 766 nm (laser-annealing). The enhanced PL intensity and the blue-shifted PL peak stem from the decreased bulk defect density in the perovskite absorber, which can lead to reduced charge recombination. To analyze the dynamics of the charge recombination in the perovskite films, time-resolved PL decay measurements were also performed. The PL decay processes for thermal-annealed and laser-annealed perovskite films were measured. A much slower PL decay can be found in the laser-annealed film. The decay curves were fitted with a biexponential function: Y = A1 exp(t/t1) +A2 exp(t/t2). The fast decay lifetime (t1) was attributed to the nonradiative recombination in the region with high-density defects such as the film surface, while the slow decay lifetime (t2) was ascribed to the recombination in the region with lower density of defects. The laser-annealed perovskite film displayed the two decay lifetimes of t1 = 51.9 ns and t2 = 193.6 ns. In contrast, the thermal-annealed film exhibited much shorter lifetimes: t1 = 17.3 ns and t2 = 45.6 ns. The longer PL lifetimes of the laser-annealed perovskite films imply the decreased concentrations of defects and traps, which can result in an increased short circuit current and a higher open-circuit voltage of a PSC.

15208717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15208717.value: Perovskite solar cells have attracted much attention recently due to their high efficiency, low cost and convenient fabrication processes. Perovskite films are normally prepared by thermal annealing for a long period of time (about 1 hour), which is time and energy consuming and incompatible with low-temperature fabrication required by certain devices such as flexible solar cells on plastic substrates. In this work, we demonstrate an ultrafast perovskite annealing strategy by scanning a laser spot on the film surface with a speed of tens of millimeter per minute. The fast scanning of the laser spot on the perovskite surface induces high temperature gradient in the perovskite film, which can accelerate the growth of perovskite grains in a short period of time (only several second) while the substrate is maintained at the room temperature. The resultant devices show high efficiency (over 21%) and good stability due to the high quality of the perovskite films under laser annealing. More importantly, this fast annealing approach can be used in the fabrication of large-area perovskite solar cells by utilizing linear laser. Therefore, the ultrafast laser scanning method is a promising technique for the mass production of perovskite solar cells with low cost.

15208817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15208817.value: Cooling energy demand in buildings is mounting, especially in subtropical climate regions. Unlike commercial premises, cooling energy consumption in the residential sector is mainly subject to occupant behaviour. Even though several simulation programs and mathematical expressions are available for cooling energy prediction, these tools are either too sophisticated for layman usage or inefficient for large-scale projects including regional public housing developments. This work will use an artificial neural network (ANN) model to simulate the cooling energy demands in public housing developments. The influencing factors and the potential for energy saving strategies relating to cooling in the public housing sector in Hong Kong will be evaluated. Hong Kong public housing units will be surveyed to identify the housing characteristics, occupant thermal expectations and air-conditioning usage patterns for model improvement and validation purposes. The improved model will be capable of assessing the cooling energy saving potential of public housing with respect to building layouts, materials, climate and set-point temperature variations. The model flexibility can be extended to allow a probabilistic input based on hourly occupancy rates and air-conditioning schedules. Such probabilistic input is not available for any existing energy simulation tool. In addition, a hands-on cooling energy calculator will be established, designed for laymen to understand and achieve energy savings. Given relevant building, weather and occupant data, the proposed hybrid model will be applicable to other countries and regions for local residential cooling demand forecasts in general. 建築物冷卻能源的需求日漸增加，特別是在香港這些亞熱帶氣候地區。住宅的製冷能源消耗受制於居民的行為，與商業大廈的自動化控制有所不同。雖然現時有幾種模擬程式和數學模型可用於預測冷卻能源的需求量，但這些工具對於外行人而言算是太複雜。這些程式和模型的效率亦並不足以應付大型建築項目如區域性公共住房開發等的需求。這項研究將使用人工神經網絡（ANN）模型來模擬公共居住房屋的冷卻能源需求，並評估香港公營房屋製冷能源消耗的影響因素及節能策略的發展潛力。研究團隊將調查香港公屋單位的房屋特徵，住客對溫度的期望以及空調使用習慣，以用作模型驗證和改良。ANN模型將能夠評估公共房屋中的建築設計佈局、建築材料、氣候與溫度設定點的相對變化等方面的製冷能源節能潛力。模型具有靈活性，容許輸入每小時空間佔用率和空調使用時間表這兩項機會率來計算出製冷能源需求量，以此提升模型準確度。現時尚未有模擬程式能融合機會率作模擬用途。另外，這項研究亦會建立一個簡便的冷卻能源計算機。這計算機是特別為外行人士而設計，讓他們更了解製冷能源消耗和達到節能目標。只要有著相關的建築、天氣和住客數據，上述的ANN模型將適用於其他國家和地區的住宅冷卻能源需求預測。

15208817.label: Realisation of objectives
15208817.value: Objective 1 A database was developed based on literature search and a new field survey conducted in extreme living environments such as very small residential units (about 200 residents). Data were classified into 3 groups: building design, environmental conditions and control and usage. These parameters are significant contributors to building envelope heat gain and their ranges in value was extracted from current design practice, standards, open literature data and government housing statistics. Measurement of household environmental conditions, air-conditioning electricity, and subjective survey on indoor environmental quality (IEQ) include thermal comfort data were conducted. Thermal condition behaviours were also recorded, i.e. adjusting air conditioning unit controls, clothing, windows, opening/closing, use of fans. Tenants were asked to vote for their thermal comfort sensation and acceptance in hourly basis with respect to the location of measurement. According to the data collected from very small residential units which includes thermal, basic indoor air quality (IAQ), visual and aural comfort, it demonstrated that the overall IEQ acceptance of these units was different from the one given for general residential building environments. Results showed that they were more sensitive to warmth and operative temperature change. A small variation of thermal acceptance suggested that they had already developed certain degree of tolerance to hot conditions. The adaptation to the reality of a hot environment was also reflected in the overall IEQ acceptance. It is believed that very small space residents have developed tolerance and adaptation to an unchangeable reality, changing environmental conditions does not necessarily alter their acceptance of individual IEQ aspects and overall IEQ (1 SCI paper was published in Indoor Built and Environment; The result was presented in CIB World Building Congress 2019). To address the above difference in IEQ responses, an open acceptance model for IEQ was established, which is a discrete probabilistic acceptance model free from assumptions of regression and is flexible to a diverse range of IEQ parameters. Thus, it is a concluding model to various published IEQ expressions in the past two decades. Model estimate of occupant acceptance is valid for published measurement results in different working and living environments such as residential, institution and offices with a unity correlation coefficient. The acceptance framework is adopted as an assessment for green healthcare buildings and the efforts of site measurement works could be reduced (1 SCI paper was published in Building and Environment). This project also revealed the importance of long-term indoor environment monitoring in maintaining an acceptable and pleasant living environment. Therefore, in addition to the proposed objectives, a low-cost user-friendly IEQ calculator and wireless IAQ sensing network for real-time IAQ monitoring were developed for environmental monitoring. The results were presented in Indoor Air 2018 and Indoor Air 2020. Objective 2 Based on the database collected, an artificial neural network (ANN) cooling energy simulation model was developed to evaluate the building energy cooling. A new electricity tariff and rebate scheme was also proposed to enhance and encourage cooling energy savings during the summer months. The per–area cooling energy consumption for the public housing sector during the summer months was benchmarked using a 5–star rating system to the determine its incentive level on the proposed tariff list. Under the proposed scheme, 5–star households will get a higher rebate rate while those with a star only will not receive any rebate. For the same amount of energy reduced, the application example demonstrated that the proposed scheme can save money as much as two times more than the existing scheme. The result was presented in ICAE2019: The 11th International Conference on Applied Energy. Objective 3 Cooling energy prediction in residential buildings is often complex and influenced by building features. Physical models, data-driven approaches, and hybrid methods have been used to predict energy consumption within a building. A physical model predicts energy consumption by considering a building’s physical property as well as its associated characteristics. It is generally computationally time-consuming, requires expertise to achieve high prediction performance and is infeasible for city scale energy predictions. On the other hand, a data-driven approach, specifically ANN, is capable to process highly non-linear multivariate inter relationships that exists in building energy analysis and it depends solely on the historical data to provide prediction of building energy performance. However, prediction performance of these models relies heavily on the database of input-output relationships. Coupling of these two methods presents the possibilities to overcome the individual shortcomings, which proved to be more time efficient and predicts accurately by reducing the computational complexities of traditional physical models. To improve cooling energy usage prediction for public housing, a hybrid grey box model was developed to predict the cooling energy consumption of residential housing in Hong Kong with different combinations of building physical characteristics and operational conditions. With the database developed previously, building energy consumption was first simulated using EP with various combination of building material properties and apartment layouts. The simulated results were pre-processed and then fed into MATLAB for ANN training. The hybrid simulation model can analyze the impacts of building materials, construction solutions, and indoor-outdoor temperature variations on the cooling energy consumed in apartments. (1 SCI paper was published in Energies). Objective 4 To consolidate the linkage between professional research analysis and layman energy saving actions, a Bayesian updating framework for IEQ acceptance model was developed, which updates the subjective-objective relationship of IEQ model. Bayesian IEQ acceptance model provides a systematic approach to related additional survey data to current belief. With selected target sample size and acceptable error, statistical significances of data are considered and incorporated into Bayesian analysis. Updating of IEQ prediction model can be achieved even with a small quantity of field data from a similar environment. Bayesian IEQ acceptance model can be a useful tool for indoor environmental design with a selection of target sample size and acceptable error based on managerial decision, corresponding energy saving actions can therefore be put forward to enhance sustainable building operation while maintaining acceptable indoor environment. (1 SCI paper was published in Intelligent Buildings International). Additionally, discrepancy between thermal comfort prediction and actual thermal sensation and satisfaction was identified through literature search. The mismatch creates a gap between expected thermal condition and engineering norm estimated by prediction model, therefore wasting building cooling energy. A practical solution was proposed to improve the reliability of thermal comfort predictions. Two Bayesian updating protocols were put forward to systemically update current thermal comfort beliefs with openly available field data. The updated model can be a practical tool for modelling thermal comfort using existing models and field survey data, therefore reducing the cooling energy wastage. (1 SCI paper was published in Journal of Building Engineering). Research into thermal comfort in sleeping environment is limited. Linkage between thermal satisfaction and sleep quality had not been identified, however it greatly affects the energy consumption in residential buildings. To enhance the awareness and understanding of the effect of sleeping environment on sleep quality, the relationship between thermal environment, sleeping thermal sensation, thermal satisfaction and sleep quality in a university dorm in Hong Kong was investigated. This work presents a great energy saving potential in residential environment during sleep while maintaining satisfied thermal sensation and good sleep quality. (1 SCI paper was published in Building and Environment).

15208817.label: Major findings and research outcome
15208817.value: In this project, a database of building design, environmental conditions, and control and usage for Hong Kong residential buildings was developed. Details of various living environments including number of apartments per floor, apartment floor area, total external wall and external window area, opaque wall U-value, window U-value, window shading coefficient, vertical shading angle, azimuth angle and the numbers of each block type were collected. Besides, field study was conducted in very small residential units in Hong Kong to collected IEQ data. Results showed that occupants had developed tolerance to hot conditions and adaptation to the reality of a hot environment. The adaptation suggests some energy saving potential in living environment. The data presented in the database are important for identifying the air-conditioning operational patterns of public housing residents for the ANN model developed and for other related research in the future. With the database established, a hybrid grey box model that combines physical model and data-driven model, an EP-ANN model for cooling energy consumption prediction was developed. The results showed that using low thermal conductivity building materials for windows and external walls can reduce the annual cooling energy consumption by up to 8.19%, and decreasing the window-to-wall ratio from 80% to 40% can give annual cooling energy savings of up to 18%. Moreover, significant net annual cooling energy savings of 13.65% can be achieved by changing the indoor set-point temperature from 24 °C to 26 °C. To consolidate the layman understanding on home environment and cooling energy consumption, an open IEQ model and a Bayesian updating framework for IEQ model were proposed. The models provide a robust tool for predicting the environmental acceptance and to identify energy saving potential. Sleeping thermal comfort study was also conducted. Results showed existing sleeping thermal sensation prediction models overestimated the thermal sensation and underestimated the neutral temperature, both thermally satisfied students and students with neutral thermal sensation had significantly higher self-assessed sleep quality, suggesting that sleep quality was largely influenced by thermal comfort, and sleeping thermal environment can be maintained at a higher temperature than predicted by models. Lastly, to encourage energy saving behaviour, a new electricity tariff and rebate scheme using a 5-star rating system was proposed to enhance the existing scheme in Hong Kong and promote cooling energy savings during the summer months.

15208817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15208817.value: This project revealed the effects of psychological, physical and behavioural adaptation on IEQ and thermal comfort acceptance, which gave us insight into enhancing the energy saving potential in residential environments by expanding the range of acceptable environmental conditions through adjustment and education. The effect of tolerance and adaption to environmental conditions on energy saving has yet to be investigated, which may provide useful strategies for enhancing building sustainable development. To such end, further IEQ field data collection shall be conducted in a range of living environments from poor to luxury, covering occupants with diverse socio-economic and educational backgrounds, and different degree of environmental awareness. The effect of occupant’s background on IEQ acceptance and expectation can then be quantified and modelled, which can be included as input parameters for cooling energy consumption in ANN model. Moreover, the effect of sustainable education on behavioural changes, especially on reduction in cooling energy consumption, can also be investigated through longitudinal study. Together, more comprehensive cooling energy saving program can be formulated to enhance residential building sustainability in Hong Kong.

15208817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15208817.value: This project aims at enhancing the capability of cooling energy consumption prediction using a hybrid grey box model that combines physical model and data-driven model. An EP-ANN (EnergyPlus™-Artificial Neural Network) model for cooling energy consumption prediction was developed, which encompasses the benefits of both approaches of less historical data requirement and enhanced computational speed. This model optimizes the prediction power and therefore provides an alternative tool for building designers to simulate the building cooling consumption using fewer parameters than conventional energy simulation programs. It is also useful for researchers and engineering professionals to conduct large scale cooling energy simulation in planning and design of sustainable public housing projects. To enhance public awareness and understanding of cooling energy consumption, indoor environmental quality and sleeping thermal comfort field studies were conducted in living environment. Results suggest that existing prediction models cannot reflect the effect of adaptation and toleration on environmental acceptance, therefore overestimate the environmental conditions to achieve satisfaction. Wider range of condition is in fact being accepted, therefore larger energy saving potential can be achieved through appropriate behavioural adjustment, psychological adaptation and proper sustainability education.

15209217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15209217.value: Every year, several billion tons of asphalt mixtures are produced worldwide for pavement construction. The binder in asphalt mixtures, asphalt, is a colloidal system where asphaltenes are the main solid phase suspended in a liquid medium. Asphalt is susceptible to oxidative ageing. The ageing process causes additional asphaltene formation, which is the driving force behind the deterioration of many asphalt properties. However, not all asphaltenes are created equal: Some are more harmful than others. Recent research has revealed different types of asphaltenes at nanoscale. In particular, needle-shaped crystalline asphaltenes are developed in asphalts from certain crude oil sources after ageing. Compared with other asphaltene types, the needle-shaped asphaltenes theoretically have more detrimental effects on asphalt durability and recyclability. These asphaltenes may be the culprit affecting those asphalts that are particularly vulnerable to ageing. The research proposes an in-depth investigation of the needle-shaped asphaltenes, including their effects on performance-related asphalt properties and asphalt recyclability, the prediction of their formation likelihood in non-aged asphalts and of their existence in aged asphalts, methods for controlling their development in non-aged asphalts and decomposing them in aged asphalts. At least 15 types of asphalts from different sources around the world will be studied. Asphaltenes in the aged asphalts will be examined using Transmission Electron Microscopy and analyzed by an image analysis program developed for this study. The effects of the needle-shaped asphaltenes on asphalt viscosity, ductility, shear modulus, micro-mechanical bond strength, and thermal cracking potential will be examined, while their effects on asphalt recyclability will be assessed through their influences on aged asphalt diffusion. Asphalt “fingerprint” traits will be constructed using asphalt fraction analysis results and infrared spectra of the different fractions. The “fingerprint” traits will be used to predict the formation likelihood of the needle-shaped asphaltenes in non-aged asphalts. Similar traits will be used to predict the existence of such asphaltenes in aged asphalts. Three classes of modifiers will be evaluated for their effectiveness in preventing the formation of the needle-shaped asphaltenes, including antioxidants, surfactants/polymers, and rejuvenators. Two strategies will be tested to decompose such asphaltenes, including temperature and rejuvenator based approaches. The anticipated research outcomes include: (1) scientific insights into the fundamental mechanisms of asphalt performance differences after ageing, (2) new methods for selecting ageing-resistant asphalts and evaluating the recyclability of aged asphalts, (3) more effective asphalt modification and recycling methods. The outcomes will contribute to the overall improvement of the durability and recycling effectiveness of asphalt pavements. 每年世界範圍內瀝青路面施工消耗了數十億噸的瀝青混合料。瀝青混合料中的粘合劑--瀝青是一種膠態體系，其中瀝青質是懸浮在液體介質中的固相。瀝青易氧化老化。老化過程產生了更多的瀝青質，這是許多瀝青性能劣化的驅動力。 然而，並不是所有的瀝青質都產生相同的危害。最近納米級的研究揭示了不同類型的瀝青質。來自某些原油來源的瀝青容易產生針狀結晶瀝青質。與其他瀝青質類型相比，針狀瀝青質理論上對瀝青耐久性和可回收性有較大的不利影響。這些瀝青質可能是影響那些特別容易老化的瀝青的罪魁禍首。 本課題將對針狀瀝青質做深入研究，包括其對性能相關的瀝青性能和瀝青回用性的影響、形成可能性的預測、控制其產生的方法、以及在老化瀝青中分解的方法。 本課題將研究世界各地多種不同來源的瀝青，使用透射電子顯微鏡檢查老化瀝青中的瀝青質，並通過圖像分析的程序進行分析。本課題將研究針狀瀝青質對瀝青的粘度，延展性，剪切模量，等性能的影響。 本課題將使用瀝青四組分分析結果和不同餾分的紅外光譜，構建瀝青“指紋”性狀。 “指紋”特徵將用於預測未老化瀝青中針狀瀝青質的形成可能性。本課題將使用類似的特徵來預測老化瀝青中此類瀝青質的存在。 本課題將評估三類改性劑的有效性，以防止針狀瀝青質的形成，包括抗氧化劑，表面活性劑/聚合物和復原劑。本課題將以兩種方法測試針狀瀝青質的穩定性，包括溫度和再生劑等。 預期的研究成果包括：（1）老化後瀝青性能差異的基本科學理論，（2）選擇耐老化瀝青的新方法和評估老化瀝青的可回收性，（3）更有效的瀝青改性和回收方法。結果將有助於整體提高瀝青路面的耐久性和回收效率。

15209217.label: Realisation of objectives
15209217.value: The principal investigator would like to thank the RGC panel members for providing us the opportunity to implement this project. This research focuses on the fundamental physicochemical properties of bitumen and some breakthrough research findings are made. With supports from RGC and other stakeholders such as Hong Kong Highways Department, Hong Kong Polytechnic University, and the paving industry in Hong Kong, the project has been satisfactorily completed. All the original proposed objectives have been successfully achieved. Fundamental and significant findings have been made based on this project. The realisation of objectives is explained as follows. Objective one: To quantify the effects of the needle-shaped asphaltenes on performance-related asphalt properties. We have made significant findings on relating the needle-shaped asphaltenes to the performance-related asphalt properties. Asphalt binders from different sources were used for investigation. The asphaltene contents of the binders were determined, and the zero-shear viscosities (ZSVs) of the binders and their maltene phases were tested at different temperatures. The size of asphaltenes in the asphalt binders was examined and approximately quantified with the assistance of scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) and image analysis. Note that solvent was not used in sample preparation; therefore, asphaltene microstructures in the STEM images represent the true states of observable asphaltenes in asphalt binders. It was found that asphaltene content and ZSV can well explain most of the commonly reported engineering properties of asphalt binders, including ZSV, dynamic viscosity, rutting parameter, fatigue parameter, phase angle, crossover frequency, Glover-Rowe (G-R) parameters, etc. However, asphaltene content cannot explain the fatigue performance of asphalt binders, for which the quantity of large-size (needle-shaped) asphaltene microstructures plays the most critical role. Objective two: To identify the impacts of such asphaltenes on the diffusion effectiveness of aged asphalts. The realistic structure of asphalt at the microscopic level, although of great value to researchers and practitioners, has not been thoroughly and quantitatively examined. This study characterized twelve asphalt samples of various origins and aging states by fraction analysis, scanning transmission electron microscope (STEM), and gel permeation chromatography (GPC). Asphaltene microstructures greater than 10 nm in STEM images were evaluated by their coverage areas, the longest dimensions, and aspect ratios. Smaller asphalt microstructures and molecules were evaluated by the overall distributions of GPC chromatograms and the proportions in different size ranges. Combined information from fraction analysis, STEM image analysis, and GPC results reveals the realistic distributions of microstructures and molecules in asphalt at the molecular level and nanoscale. After understanding the realistic structure of asphalt, the impacts of such asphaltenes on the diffusion effectiveness can be theoretically and experimentally determined. Objective three: To predict the formation probability of such asphaltenes in non-aged asphalts and their existence in aged asphalts; In this part of the study, we examined the formation probability of such (large, needle-shaped) asphaltenes. The chemical properties of asphalt binders were analyzed, including the oxygenated functional groups and Corbett fractions. Aging conditions were found to affect the generated aging products. Some asphalt binders were found to be more resistant to oxidative aging than others, and sulfur in asphalt binder appears to play an important role. Generally, the abundance of large-size, needle-shaped asphaltenes is associated with asphaltene content. Objective four: To identify the thermal and chemical stability of such asphaltenes towards effective asphalt recycling. In this part of the study, the stability of asphaltenes was investigated from the perspective of asphalt recycling. The study found that the asphaltene structure was quite stable, in spite of different rejuvenators used to break down the asphaltene particles. Nevertheless, some changes in asphaltene size can be detected after the treatment of rejuvenators. The overall changes in asphaltene size can be observed by using scanning transmission electron microscope (STEM) and a patented method developed in this study. The overall size changes can also be evaluated through asphalt binder’s relaxation spectrum. Overall, the research objectives are realised through well-planned experiments, theoretical and methodological developments. The research findings from the experiments are reported in several published papers.

15209217.label: Major findings and research outcome
15209217.value: The realistic structure of asphalt binder (bitumen) at the microscopic level, although of great value to researchers and practitioners, has not been thoroughly and quantitatively examined before. This research aimed to reveal the fundamental structure of asphalt binder (bitumen), with focus on the characteristics and influences of large-size, needle-shaped asphaltenes in asphalt binder. We have made the following major findings through this study: (1) Asphaltene microstructures embedded in asphalt binders are revealed for the first time. (2) The size and shape of asphaltene microstructures are found to be dependent on asphalt source and aging states. (3) The 3D morphology and toughness of asphaltene microstructures are determined. (4) Realistic distributions of asphaltene microstructures and molecules in asphalt binder are characterized. (5) Evolutions of asphaltene microstructures and molecular size of bitumen in aging are identified. (6) Connections between the hierarchical structure of bitumen and its properties are established. We found that nearly all of the commonly concerned engineering properties of asphalt binder can be well predicted through: maltene viscosity, and content and size of asphaltenes. (7) In particular, asphalt binders’ fatigue performance is related to asphaltene size and maltene ZSV. (8) Effective use of Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectrogram to differentiate contaminants in asphalt binder is proposed. (9) Some asphalt binders are more resistant to oxidative ageing than others, and sulphur appears to play an important role. This research has led to the following major research outcomes: (1) A patent is developed to analyze the microscopic nature of asphalt binder. This patent is critically important in asphalt binder study in the present study and in future studies. (2) Models are established between asphalt binders’ fundamental physicochemical properties and their engineering properties. (3) The morphologies and mechanical properties of asphaltene particles, which are the driving factor for asphalt binder property variations, are characterized through atomic force microscopy. (4) New methods to analyze the hierarchical structure of asphalt binders in aging and rejuvenation; (5) Significant scientific findings on the nature of asphalt binder, especially its changes in aging and rejuvenation; (6) Through the comparisons of chemical products produced through natural aging and artificial aging, proper aging treatment methods are recommended. (7) The disadvantages of using surface feature (bee structure) of asphalt binder to predict its properties are clearly demonstrated.

15209217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15209217.value: This study, for the first time, clearly reveals the fundamental structure of bitumen (asphalt binder) from the sub-nano to nano scale. Many engineering properties of asphalt binder are found to be determined by the fundamental structure. The findings from this study pave the way for future research and engineering practices. In the future, we can use the methods developed in this research to model and predict the fracture process and healing process of asphalt binder. We can use the methods developed in this study to treat asphalt binder so that it more realistically reflects the true aging conditions in the field. The methods developed in this study can also help select the more durable asphalt binder and evaluate the rejuvenation effectiveness of recycled asphalt. The developed patent can also help study the microscopic nature of various modified asphalt binders.

15209217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15209217.value: Asphalt binder, often used interchangeably with the term “bitumen” or sometimes just called “asphalt”, is an engineering material widely used in pavements, roof shingles, and waterproofing membranes. Early use of naturally occurring asphalt dates back to over 180,000 years ago. Most asphalt today, however, is derived from the petroleum distillation process. About 100 million tons of asphalt is produced globally every year. Production of asphalt and asphalt-containing materials and construction activities using such materials have significant impacts on finance, energy consumption, and green-house gas (GHG) emissions. Asphalt degradation is a leading factor for the deterioration of highways, roofs, and other infrastructures. Therefore, improving asphalt durability would help save costs, preserve non-renewable resources, and conserve the environment. Despite its importance, the mechanism of asphalt failure is not well understood. Through this research, the fundamental mechanisms of asphalt property variation and failure are revealed. New methods are developed to analyze asphalt binder at the microscopic level. Such new methods not only deepen our understanding on this important material, they also help us select and develop more durable asphalt materials.

15209517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15209517.value: In many large cities in Asia, such as Bangkok and Hong Kong, public transit network undoubtedly plays an important role for our daily travel. Due to the limited spaces of Hong Kong road network, over 90% of the 14 million daily trips are made by various public transit modes (e.g. road-based double-deck bus and public light bus, and non-road-based exclusive Mass Transit Railway). Under the densely populated environment, there is an increasing need of Hong Kong residents for efficient and reliable multi-modal public transit services particularly in congested urban areas with travel time uncertainties. In this project, the first-order and second-order statistical properties of the transit passenger travel times are investigated to model the space-time accessibility in multi-modal public transit networks with uncertainties due to recurrent demand fluctuation and non-recurrent heavy rainfall or unpredictable incident. Transit network design is widely recognized as an effective way for improving various transit services. Although transit network design problems have long been extensively studied, most of these existing studies looked for economic benefit of the transit service operators, and considered only time and cost-related attributes as explanatory variables of transit service quality particularly for long-term strategic planning. Little attention has been given to the space-time accessibility in congested networks with travel time uncertainties for long-term transit network design problem. To fill this gap, this project examines the transit network design problem from the viewpoint of reliability-based accessibility by public transit services. To this end, the concept of public transit accessibility is extended to investigate the ability to reach destinations or activity locations of the transit passengers in multi-modal transit networks while the effects of travel time uncertainties and crowding discomfort penalties due to adverse weather and/or traffic incidents will be considered in this project to assess the passenger on-time arrival probability to the selected destination by various transit modes. This project proposes to develop advanced analytical models and algorithms for maximizing the accessibility in multi-modal public transit network under uncertainty. The outputs of the proposed models consist of the optimal reliable path and mode choices in public transit network, accessible space-time service areas by multi-modal transit services, and the optimal transit network design schemes in terms of transit routing and stop location, transit vehicle frequency and transit fare by route. The proposed study has the potential to help authorities to make strategic policies for improving the efficiency and reliability of public transit services.

15209517.label: Realisation of objectives
15209517.value: As far as the project objective 1 is concerned, a novel reliable path finding algorithm was proposed for a stochastic road network with uncertainty in travel times while simultaneously taking account both electric vehicle energy and efficiency (see publication no. (2)). A bi-objective programming model was formulated to maximize the on-time arrival reliability and vehicle energy-efficiency in a path finding problem. Numerical examples were carried out to demonstrate the applicability of the proposed algorithm. This reliability-based path finding algorithm can be further extended to the design of electric bus system. On the basis of this proposed algorithm, a reliability-based transit assignment model was developed for schedule-based networks with uncertainties in transit schedule and travel demand (see publication no. (12)). A new concept of reliable effective travel cost was introduced to deal with the reliability of both travel cost and boarding in schedule-based transit networks. In connection to the project objective 2, the effects of travel time uncertainty on accessibility to public service were investigated with consideration of multi-modal transportation network topology and on-time arrival probability by time of day (see publication no. (10)). Travel behaviors of passengers to access a facility was analyzed for evaluation of the location/place-based accessibility. The results of the case study reveal the dynamic impacts of travel time uncertainty on accessibility coverage area by mode and on-time arrival probability across time of day. In addition, new location/place-based accessibility measures were proposed with consideration of space-time effects for evaluating accessibility dynamic. The new measures extended the conventional location/place-based measures with the space-time utility perspective (see publication nos. (1), (8) and (11)). In this new approach, the accessibility of a location within the study area can be evaluated by the space-time utility in terms of activity duration, travel time and facility attractiveness. Apart from location/place-based accessibility, the impacts of travel time uncertainty on the equity of individual accessibility were studied. Two reliability-based individual accessibility measures were proposed to generalize traditional individual accessibility measures by explicitly considering various individuals’ reliability constraints in face of travel time uncertainty (see publication no. (9)). The proposed measures were further applied to quantify travel time uncertainty impacts on the equity of individual accessibility to shopping services (see publication no. (4)). Understanding activity-travel choice patterns are also important for long-term multi-modal transit network design. A novel household-oriented activity-based mixed-equilibrium model was thus proposed for estimating individual and household activity-travel choices in multimodal transportation networks with interactions between private car and public transit modes (see publication no. (6)). Feeder transport to transit stations was also considered in the multi-modal transit network design. The relationship between the access travel time estimation and the accessibility of different travel modes to high speed railway station was studied (see publication no. (5)). The results can help to better understand how the accessibility of the feeder transport changes at different time periods. With respect to the project objectives 2 and 3, a new accessibility-based discrete network design model was proposed to maximize the accessibility in determining the optimal network design scheme with use of the above proposed location/place-based accessibility measures (see publication no. (3)). The proposed model was formulated as a bi-level programming problem, in which the upper-level was to maximize commonly used gravity-based accessibility subject to the construction budget constraint, and the lower level was formulated as an elastic-demand user equivalent model. Numerical examples were conducted to illustrate the merits of the proposed model. Case study will also be carried out to demonstrate the applicability of the proposed model in practice. In addition, another bi-level programming model was proposed for optimizing time-dependent transit line headways and fares in a multi-modal transit network from the activity-based space-time accessibility perspective (see publication no. (7)). In the upper level, transit line headways and fares are optimized by time of day to maximize the network-wide activity-based space-time accessibility. At the lower level, an activity-based network equilibrium model is adapted to provide the resultant activity-travel patterns as reactions to the upper level decision. Crowding discomforts both in vehicles and at activity locations are taken into account for long-term transit planning. A super-network platform was adapted to simultaneously consider individuals’ activity choices and travel choices so that individuals’ accessibility to various activities and travels can be measured in a unified framework. A case study on a simplified multi-modal transit network in Hong Kong selected area was carried out to highlight the performance of the proposed activity-based space-time accessibility measure and the bi-level programming model.

15209517.label: Major findings and research outcome
15209517.value: Regarding the project objective 1, a bi-objective model was proposed for finding the optimal reliable energy-efficient path in road networks with uncertainty in travel times (see publication (2)). The proposed model accounts for both the on-time arrival probability and the correlated link travel times in a stochastic road network. The proposed algorithm overcomes the infeasibility of the traditional path finding algorithms for reliable shortest path problems. In additional, a reliability-based transit assignment model was proposed for schedule-based networks with uncertainties in transit schedule and travel demand (see publication no. (12)). A concept of reliable effective travel cost was introduced to capture the risk-aversion behavior of passengers in response to the reliability of transit routes. The proposed model can be used to evaluate the route choice behavior of risk-adverse passengers, as well as the quality and reliability of transit service, which can help for the design of transit networks. With respect to the project objective 2, both location/place-based and individual accessibilities were studied. The effects of travel time uncertainty on accessibility to public service were investigated with consideration of multi-modal transportation network topology and on-time arrival probability by time of day (see publication no. (10)). Space-time utility in terms of activity duration, travel time and facility attractiveness were also considered for evaluating the accessibility of a location (see publication nos. (1), (8) and (11)). The results of the case studies indicated that the proposed measures are able to capture the temporal variation of location/place-based accessibility at different times of day. In addition, the impacts of travel time uncertainty on the equity of individual accessibility were examined (see publication nos. (4) and (9)). The results of the case study show that travel time uncertainties have more severe impacts on disadvantaged people with a lower accessibility level, and exaggerate the overall accessibility inequity among all people groups. Based on the proposed accessibility measures, two bi-level programming models were proposed for long-term multi-modal transit network design (see publication nos. (3) and (7)). Moreover, feeder services to transit stations (see publication no. (5)) and activity-travel choices in multimodal transportation networks (see publication no. (6)) were studied, which could help for multimodal public transit network design. In connection to the project objective 3, case studies were conducted to demonstrate the applicability of the proposed accessibility-based network design model in practice. The proposed model maximizes the total system accessibility in determining the optimal network design scheme (see publication no. (3)). The numerical results show that the proposed model could generate a better network design scheme with better performance than that of the conventional models using total system travel time and consumer surplus. Another case study on a simplified multi-modal transit network in Hong Kong selected area was carried out to highlight the performance of the proposed activity-based space-time accessibility measure and the bi-level programming model for optimizing time-dependent transit line headways and fares in a multi-modal transit network from the activity-based space-time accessibility perspective (see publication no. (7)). It was demonstrated from the case study that the proposed model provides a useful tool for estimating the time-varying profile of the activity-based space-time accessibility in multi-modal transit networks over time of day, and can be used to evaluate various transit operating schemes at the strategic planning level.

15209517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15209517.value: In this project, various accessibility measures were proposed to evaluate the accessibility in multi-model transit network. However, the impacts of socio-economic factors (such as car ownership and household structure) on the daily activity-travel pattern choice and the accessibility by different groups of individual have not been studied. In further research, relevant personal socio-economic characteristics should be incorporated into individual accessibility studies to provide deeper insights on how the travel time uncertainties affect accessibility of different people groups, particularly those individuals with disadvantaged socio-economic conditions. In addition, there is a need to examine different levels of accessibility considering socio-economic factors so that the impacts of different transit operating strategies can be examined in the long-term multi-modal transit network design.

15209517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15209517.value: Transit network design is widely recognized as an effective way for improving various transit services. This project investigates the transit network design problem from the viewpoint of reliability-based accessibility by public transit services. The concept of public transit accessibility has been extended to examine the ability to reach destinations or activity locations of the transit passengers in multi-modal transit networks while the effects of travel time uncertainties and crowding discomfort penalties due to adverse weather and/or traffic incidents are considered to assess the passenger on-time arrival probability to the selected destination by various transit modes. In this project, various accessibility measures have been proposed. Advanced optimization models and solution algorithms have been developed for maximizing these accessibility measures in multi-modal public transit network under uncertainty. The results of the project have potential to help authorities to make strategic planning for improving the efficiency and reliability of public transit services.

15209617.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15209617.value: 新興智能電力分佈系統中的多變換器互動分岔分析

15209617.label: Project Objectives
15209617.value: The first objective is to develop a modeling approach that effectively describes the input characteristics of power sources and the driving characteristics of various kinds of loads including downstream converters, as well as characteristics of power converters that are designed to work with the various types of input and load terminations. For SPECIFIC systems, this will end up with models that allow the systems' dynamics to be conveniently revealed by analytical study and simulations. A multiple operation model, for instance, can be used to treat the uncertain input power characteristics of photovoltaic terminations, as has been successfully used before. Based on the models developed under the first objective, combined with extensive simulations and experiments, analysis of the dynamics of interacting converter systems will be conducted. Since no small-signal model assumption is used, the analysis involves a systematic plan of simulation and experiments using specific models that are derived for the specific practical set of interacting converters in question. The focus is on identifying the key set of parameters that affects stability, and the ways in which the system loses stability upon variation of some selected parameters. Finally we will consolidate and re-organize key findings in a design-oriented form that can be used for practical design of power distribution systems involving the choice of parameter ranges that would guarantee stability of operation. Design charts will be generated in multiple parameter spaces that will clearly provide convenient visual interpretation of the effects of varying key parameters on the stability and dynamics of the interacting systems.

15209617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15209617.value: This is a resubmission of a proposal submitted last year. Clarifications are provided in Part-II-7 to address the concerns of the reviewers. A preliminary work by the PI in studying interacting converters along this direction was awarded the Best Paper Prize (Second Place) 2015 by the IEEE Transactions on Power Electronics. Another paper by the PI in modeling large-scale power network using a network modeling approach was reported by the highly selective IEEEXplore Innovation Spotlight (only a few selected each month from over 3 million publications in IEEEXplore) in December 2015. This encourages the PI to resubmit this proposal and also proves the relevance of this proposal to future power distribution development. The rapid development of solid-state lightings and the overwhelming demand for DC power consumed by computers, electronics, battery chargers, etc. have defined the future path of development of power distribution at the user level towards DC distribution. The variable voltage level and multiple operating modes will necessitate the design of power converters interfacing the various terminations and sources to cater for a range of operating conditions and maintain stability under various practical conditions. The problem is complex because power sources and terminations are no longer adequately described by voltage or current sources and resistive loads. Furthermore, power converters converting AC-to-DC, DC-to-DC, etc., will be interacting with one another through the local and main power grids. Design methods based on conventional standalone converter models are not expected to describe the correct dynamics and predict precise stability conditions. This project will conduct in-depth study of the dynamics and stability of emerging smart power distribution systems which involve interactions of power converters connecting AC, DC and other interfaces with terminations and sources which are nonlinear and complex in nature. The properties of these terminations cannot be treated as simple impedances like resistors or reactive elements. For instance, solid-state lightings and solar panels are hardly voltage sources. The first task is to develop a modelling approach that includes the essential input characteristics of power sources and the driving characteristics of various loads including downstream converters. The second problem is to study the stability of interacting converters and identify parameters that affect stability in such systems. The final task is to consolidate and re-organize key findings in a design-oriented form that can facilitate design of power distribution systems involving the choice of parameter ranges that would guarantee stability of operation. 這項目就新興智能電力分佈系統中的多個變換器的互動所產生的穩定性問題進行深入研究。電力分佈系統包括AC、DC和其他非線性能源及複雜終端介面。複雜的終端特徵實際上不能以一般阻抗代表，如電阻性和反擊性阻抗。例如：固體狀態照明元件及光伏元件皆非簡單的電壓源，故需要用針對性的模型方法處理。此項目的首要任務是發展一套模型方法，有效描述各種電力源的輸入特徵和下游變換器的驅動特徵。第二任務是研究多個變換器在耦合互動時產生的穩定性問題，以及找出影系統穩定性的響關鍵參數。最後，此項目簡化及重組有關穩定性的結果，以面向設計的形式表達，直接促進智能電力分佈系統的參數設計，務求保障整體系統的穩定運作。

15209617.label: Major findings and research outcome
15209617.value: In the mid-term report, we presented some key results focusing on the specific downstream converters characteristics, which were performed specifically to address a reviewer's key comment raised in the proposal review stage. This turned out to be extremely helpful for us in targeting our research to important applications, and we made an in-depth study of the current-source driving applications, and the study was extended to multiple output high voltage ratio applications as specific circuits for applying the modeling method. The grid-interaction was then studied in this specific application scenario. On this topic, we produced two journal papers, one emphasizing the current-source driving downstream converter models and the other on grid connection requiring power factor correction. One of the key aspects of our work is that we applied general analytical methods without making small-signal assumptions. We studied the power grid, leading to a useful practical procedure for detecting cascading failure. This work was presented by IEEE ISCAS to be held in May 2019, which was selected for co-publication in an IEEE Transactions. In the second stage of the project, the dynamical interaction of converters connected to a power grid was the main problem was investigated. Our study has generated very fruitful outcomes, and we precisely identified the major cause underlying the instability in typical grid-interacting converters, which was the nonlinear operation of the phase-locked loop in the controller. The operation of this essential component and the mechanism leading to instability were thoroughly investigated and summarized in an IEEE Transactions paper. Furthermore, the interaction of converters was studied in a variety of connected systems, including the very popular DC distribution which is a typical downstream configuration interfacing with the final consumer loads. The various instability phenomena were put in a design-oriented form, as promised in the original proposal, for ease of use by practitioners. The results were presented in another IEEE Transactions paper. Our final stage of work has gone further into the grid addressing a much higher level problem, which was related to the robustness of a power network and the possible methods for restoring a power network undergoing cascading failure in practice. This work may be considered an extension arising from this project to future topics of research, and we specifically identified the potential problems associated with the increasingly complex interconnected power grid and the threats imposed on its safe operation and restoration from failure. Another paper was published in an IEEE journal.

15209617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15209617.value: As the modern power grid rapidly evolves, the converters connected to the power have provided essential functions but at the same time posed threats to stability and robustness of operation. The project has laid a good foundation for the future continual investigation of the power electronics penetrated power grid, which is expected to have an even bigger impact on the research development of power distribution infrastructure. At the time of reporting, the PI has been funded a new GRF project which precisely extends the current project beyond converter interaction and moves further into the complex network structure of future power grids. Thus, the results of this project will offer important insights from the circuit and dynamical system level, and we will develop new techniques to deal with the complex problems at the network level, like cascading failure, cyber attacks, and the impact of increasing use of renewable sources.

15209617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15209617.value: Our society has depended on the safe, stable and robust operation of the key infrastructures. One of these infrastructures is the power generation and distribution network which has increasingly deployed power electronics converters. The interaction of the many converters via the power network is unavoidable, and the result has profound influence on the stability and safe operation of the power network and local distribution networks. This project has made a systematic attempt in studying the dynamical interaction of power electronics converters. We focused on a few specific types of interconnected systems that were commonly used in practice, and the results generated from this project have uncovered some important instability phenomena and offered clear explanations of the mechanisms responsible for the commonly seen instability phenomena. The study itself has involved sophisticated mathematical techniques and the results generated were put in design-oriented forms that can be conveniently used by engineers to choose appropriate parameters and control methods in order to ensure safe and robust power conversion functions. Our future work will consider the effects of network topology and design parameters on the robust operation of the future smart power generation and distribution network.

15209917.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15209917.value: 基於IGZO TFT的高性能柔性壓力傳感器

15209917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15209917.value: Recently, there is a rising demand for high-performance pressure sensors due to the rapid developments in touch displays and artificial skin for mobile, prosthetic and robotic applications. Although the existing pressure sensors can register changes in signals to the applied pressure, they have some disadvantages such as complicated and expensive manufacturing procedure, poor stability and repeatability, limited sensitivity, bulky size, and high power consumption. Moreover, these sensors are unsuitable for applications demanding high mechanical flexibility and large-area coverage. Because of these limitations, a novel flexible pressure sensor based on indium-gallium-zinc-oxide (IGZO) thin-film transistor (TFT) and compressible capacitor is proposed. IGZO TFT-based pressure sensors can offer appealing advantages such as simple, low-cost and low-temperature fabrication, multi-parameter response, flexibility, lightweight, large-area sensing, high transparency and uniformity, easily integrated into an electronic circuit and direct transduction. However, before they can be put into practical applications, there are still several features such as operating voltage, sensitivity, stability and reliability needed to be improved. The performance of sensors based on IGZO TFT depends largely on the characteristics of the dielectric, the IGZO/dielectric interface and the gate electrode. Therefore, the main aim of this project is to investigate the structure of the sensor and its preparation methods, and optimize the processing conditions for the dielectric, IGZO film and gate electrode of the device so that a low-voltage, sensitive, stable, reliable and flexible IGZO TFT-based pressure sensors can be produced. Our approach is to (i) use new materials with high dielectric constant as the dielectric layer inside the IGZO TFT sensors to achieve low operating voltage and high current drive; (ii) passivate the dielectric by low-temperature nitridation, fluorination and/or adding a high-k interlayer between the high-k dielectric and the IGZO layer to improve stability, sensitivity and response time; (iii) passivate the traps in the IGZO film with a view to providing a high-quality dielectric-IGZO system to enhance sensing performance; and (iv) develop suitable gate electrode materials for flexible vacuum tape substrate for enhancing long-term stability and reliability of the sensors. 最近，由於應用在手機，假肢和機器人的觸摸顯示和人造皮膚的快速發展，對高性能壓力傳感器的需求不斷增長。雖然現有的壓力傳感器可以將施加的壓力記錄到信號的變化上，但是它們具有一些缺點，例如製造過程複雜和昂貴，穩定性和可重複性差，靈敏度有限，體積大，功耗大。此外，這些傳感器不適合要求高機械靈活性和大面積覆蓋的應用。由於這些限制，提出了一種基於銦鎵鋅氧化物（IGZO）薄膜晶體管（TFT）和可壓縮電容器的新穎的柔性壓力傳感器。 IGZO TFT型壓力傳感器可以提供吸引人的優勢如簡單，低成本和低溫製造，多參數響應，靈活性，輕便，大面積感測，高透明度和均勻性，易於集成到電子電路中，並直接轉導。然而，在實際應用之前，還需要改進工作電壓，靈敏度，穩定性和可靠性等幾個特性。基於IGZO TFT的傳感器的性能在很大程度上取決於電介質，IGZO/介質界面和柵電極的特性。因此，本項目的主要目的是研究傳感器的結構及其製備方法，優化器件的電介質，IGZO膜和柵電極的處理條件，使低壓，靈敏，穩定，可靠並且靈活的基於IGZO TFT的壓力傳感器可以製造。我們的方法是（i）使用具有高介電常數的新材料作為IGZO TFT傳感器內的電介質層，以實現低工作電壓和高電流驅動; （ii）通過在高k電介質和IGZO層之間的低溫氮化，氟化和/或添加高k夾層來鈍化電介質，以提高穩定性，靈敏度和響應時間; （iii）鈍化IGZO膜中的陷阱，以提供高質量的介電IGZO系統以增強感測性能;和（iv）開發用於柔性真空帶基板的合適的柵電極材料，以增強傳感器的長期穩定性和可靠性。

15210017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15210017.value: The finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method is an intuitive and powerful analysis technique to solve electromagnetic (EM) problems in the time domain. This numerical method has been successfully applied to analyze electromagnetic phenomena associated with bio-electromagnetic models, waveguide models, and printed circuit boards with lumped electric elements. This method has also been applied to analyze lightning transients in electric power systems and lightning protection systems. The FDTD method has the advantages of broadband field simulation, less memory space, easy implementation of parallel computing and others. Thin wire models have been proposed recently to model thin round conductors. With this technique the FDTD method has been extended to solve fast transients in wire structures found in power systems, railway systems, telecommunication systems as well as lightning protection systems. Note that the thin-wire models cannot be used to represent lossy wires with arbitrary cross sections. It has, therefore, only a limited value in the application of lightning surge analysis in practical wire structures, which consist of long power/signal line and cables, structural steel and others. This project aims at developing extended and stable thin-wire models to represent practical and lossy wire structures for lightning surge analysis. The physical effects of practical conductors will be taken into account, such as conductor loss, skin effect, proximity effect, ferromagnetism, arbitrary cross section and others. The extended thin wire models are constructed by embedding equivalent circuit models and analytical formulas for non-linear characteristic curves into the classical FDTD mesh. This approach allows for the construction of a detailed wire model to be contained within a coarse FDTD mesh, and can reduce computational time and computing resources significantly with good computation accuracy. The simulation stability is maintained by adopting a hybrid implicit-explicit method. The proposed modeling method can be applied to the evaluation of lightning surges in overhead lines, towers and power and signal cables inside and outside buildings. The results could be used to design effective lightning protection measures and select most appropriate protective devices. The extended thin-wire model proposed in this project can extend the range of FDTD applications to other types of transient analysis in wire structures made of thin lossy conductors. 有限差分時域 (FDTD) 方法是一種既直觀而又強大的數時域有限差分法(FDTD)是一種直觀且強大的數值分析技術，廣泛地應用於時域電磁分析。電力系統和防雷保護系統中的雷電暫態分析即是此數值計算方法的成功應用領域之一。它具有寬頻帶響應、消耗內存少、易於實現並行運算等優點。 近來有學者構建出FDTD細線模型來模擬細圓導體。通過這項技術，時域有限差分法可以進一步求解電力系統線狀導體中的快速瞬變過程。然而現有的技術不能模擬具有任意形狀且有損的導線。因此，時域有限差分法在如長電源/信號線、電纜、鋼結構等的實際導線結構中，雷電浪湧分析的價值有限。 該專案旨在開發一個拓展的FDTD細線模型，用來分析在實際及有損線結構中的雷電浪湧。該專案將考慮導體的各種物理特性。拓展細線模型將通過在經典時域差分網格中嵌入和解析等效電路模型來實現。此方法能把精細的線模型構建在稀疏的 FDTD 網格上，從而在保證合理的計算精度前提下，大大減少計算時間、節省計算資源。這種建模方法可以廣泛應用於評估建築物內外的架空線、鐵塔、電源電纜和信號電纜。其運算結果可用來設計有效的防雷保護措施、選擇最適當的保護裝置。此外，拓展細線模型也可以應用于其它领域有关細薄有損導體的脈衝分析。

15210017.label: Realisation of objectives
15210017.value: The objectives of this project have been achieved generally. (a) The extended FDTD thin-wire models have been developed for conductors with arbitrary cross-sections for lightning surge analysis by taking into account electromagnetic effects. The EM field near long conductors is described using a single constant correction factor, which can be obtained with the charge simulation method (CSM) numerically. The conductor loss is expressed as a single internal impedance which is calculated with an equivalent circuit method (ECM). The frequency-dependent parameters are considered in the time-domain simulation. The constant correction factors and internal impedances need to be only calculated once prior to the FDTD updating iteration. In the FDTD working volume, the EM field associated with a long conductor can be divided into three parts: 1) the EM field inside the conductor, 2) the EM field between the conductor surface and the closed FDTD surface of adjacent cells, and 3) the EM field outside the closed FDTD cell surface. The 1st part of the EM field, the EM field inside the conductor, can be described with a lumped internal impedance Z_int. The voltage drop, caused by the internal impedance along the long conductor, is presented in the FDTD region as a series of longitudinal E field components convolutionally in time-domain simulations. The 3rd part of the EM field is located at least ∆l away from the conductor, where its distribution is similar to that generated from a circular conductor. This region is discretized with the FDTD mesh, and the EM field is evaluated with the normal FDTD updating iterations automatically. The 2nd part of the EM field lies between the conductor surface and the closed surface of the FDTD cells. Although the EM field distribution here is irregular because of its irregular cross-section, the E field on the closed-cell surface is similar to that generated from a circular conductor. An equivalent circular conductor then is proposed to substitute the non-circular conductor. (b) The computation instability associated with the use of the extended thin-wire models in lightning surge analysis has been investigated. The computational stability of the extended thin wire model is enhanced with a multi-conductor cable stabilizing technique (MCST) using a 1D spatial low-pass filter. When the FDTD cell size is set to be one-tenth, sometimes one-hundredth of the simulated wavelength, high-frequency spatial harmonics are observed in FDTD simulations. In most cases, these components behave like high-frequency noises superimposed on the actual results. In the simulation with the thin-wire model for multi-core structures, it is found that the high-frequency spatial harmonics in the vicinity of the multi-conductor structure could grow exponentially and lead to calculation collapse. The MCST eliminates high-frequency spatial harmonics of the surface E field on thin wire conductors in the conductor region to reduce the potential risk of instability. Since the high-frequency spatial harmonics are usually weakly excited in the FDTD simulation, the simulation accuracy will not be compromised by doing so. During each updating cycle, a spatial series of surface E fields on each thin wire conductor can be transformed into the spectral domain by the Discrete Fourier Transform. Then high-frequency spatial harmonics can be eliminated completely with an one-dimensional (1D) spatial low-pass filter in the spectral domain. Once the surface E field is modified, it can be transformed back to the space domain with the Inverse Discrete Fourier Transform (IDFT). Note the Fourier transformations included in the MCST are operated only for surface E field on the sheath conductors (1D conductor domain), not for E fields in the entire 3D FDTD domain. The simulation time and memory space are barely increased. (c) The extended thin-wire models have been validated analytically and numerically. the characteristic impedance, loss of long conductors, and time-domain waveforms, evaluated by the proposed thin-wire model, are compared with the CSM, the transmission line theory (TLT), and the traditional FDTD method. Six different cross-sectional shapes of the conductor are selected for comparison, i.e., rectangular shape, L shape, T shape, H shape, U shape, and cruciform. According to the simulation results of the characteristic impedance of lossless conductors calculated by the proposed thin-wire model and the CSM, the average and maximum errors are 0.61% and 1.35%. Good agreements are observed. This indicates that the characteristic impedance of the proposed thin-wire model for lossless conductors with irregular cross-sections is accurate. The current amplitudes along the conductor are calculated with the proposed thin wire model and TLT. It is observed that the current amplitude decreases to around 70% of the original amplitude at a distance of 500 m in all cases. The average and maximum relative errors of the amplitudes are respectively 0.96% and 2.66%. This indicates that the proposed thin-wire model can simulate the frequency-dependent conductor loss with satisfactory accuracy. The time-domain waveforms calculated with the proposed model are compared with the one calculated by the traditional FDTD. It is observed that the current waveforms match well. The maximum relative errors of the proposed thin-wire model with 5 mm and 10 mm cell sizes are 2.15% and 2.96%. Compared to the traditional FDTD method, the proposed thin-wire model with 5/10 mm cell sizes saves 99.71%/ 99.93% of simulation time, and 74.27%/80.78% memory space. It is shown that the proposed thin-wire model can simulate current waveforms in the time domain accurately with high computational efficiency. The proposed thin-wire model is applied for lightning transient analysis in an electrified railway system. An axle counter is installed at the trackside between two masts to determine the occupation of this railway block. The signal is transmitted to a control station via a signal cable. The cabinet is bonded via a conductor to the track. Surge protective devices (SPDs) are installed between the signal port and the ground in the cabinet. It is found that one SPD in the cabinet is broken in a thunderstorm. The lightning surge current in the SPD then is analyzed with the proposed thin wire model. It is found that the lightning current in the surge protective device has a relatively long duration. Under a 1/200 μs lightning return stroke terminated on the track-side mast, track-side devices such as axle counters could be possibly damaged. Removing the bonding point near the axle counter and reducing the distance between the signal cable and rail tracks can reduce the surge current amplitude effectively. A more suitable MOV is also recommended based on the simulation results.
