15210017.label: Major findings and research outcome
15210017.value: A stable extended FDTD thin-wire model for lossy wire structures with irregular cross-sections was proposed in this project. The irregular EM field distribution in the vicinity of such conductors was taken into account by adopting one simple constant correction factor. The constant correction factor was evaluated with the CSM numerically. The conductor loss, as well as the ferromagnetic effect, was modeled using frequency-dependent internal impedance, which was calculated using an ECM. Both the correction factors and internal impedances were only calculated once before the FDTD updating iteration [J1, J3]. The FDTD model for inclined conductors also was developed in [J2]. A stabilizing technique with a 1D spatial low-pass filter was proposed to maintain computational stability in the thin-wire model [J3]. The proposed model was validated analytically and numerically for the conductors with six different cross-sectional shapes. Other types of conductors, such as coaxial multiple-layer cables and multiple coaxial cables, were addressed, and the models were presented in [J4, J5]. In this project, a complete set of thin-wire models have been developed for modeling various wire structures found in practice. In addition, a simulation procedure for integrating FDTD models and SPICE models was provided in [8] for field-to-circuit coupling simulation. The proposed thin-wire models have been applied to solve practical engineering problems in the power industry. In [J4-J5], lightning transients on underground power cables were evaluated to reveal the insulation stress under lightning. In [J1, J3, C1], a procedure was developed for evaluating lightning transients in railway traction power supply systems and trackside signaling systems. The mechanism of device damage was analyzed, and recommendations were provided, in terms of device selection, earthing and bonding strategies, etc. The FDTD models also were applied in lightning surge analysis in photovoltaic (PV) systems and others [J6, J9, C2]. The effect of grounding arrangement of PV systems and others [J7] was investigated, and design guidelines were provided for effective lightning protection. Numerical instability was found in the simulation during indirect lightning, and a holistic approach was developed in [J6] for solving this problem.

15210017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15210017.value: Thin wire models for a single thin wire conductor in the FDTD domain have been investigated in this project, including updating equations, algorithms, stability issues, validations, and applications. It is found that the arrangement of wire conductors may be more complicated than a single conductor in some cases. For instance, the electromagnetic shielding mesh, which is widely used in building structures, consists of multiple crossing thin wire conductors. If the shielding mesh is simulated by using the existing thin wire models, the computation time could be unacceptable. A more comprehensive model considering various thin wire structures should be developed in the future.

15210117.value: 的士提供了門到門的按需出行服務，在大都市居民日常通勤出行中扮演著重要角色。目前的士行業的運營，一方面，空車兜圈攬客，白白佔用道路資源，消耗燃油和司機的時間；另一方面，乘客在某些區域或時段的出行需求沒能得到快速回應甚至需要花費很長的等待時間。這種供、需不匹配的現象長期以來困擾著計程車行業的從業者及管理部門。解決這個問題仍然面臨著交通擁堵帶來的網路不確定性、供、需的不確定性和時空不平衡等難題。隨著大数据時代的到來，智慧手機、GPS導航等移動設備的普及，為估計乘客用車需求和車輛的時空分佈，從而為解決上述供需不平衡導致的的士運營難題帶來了新的機遇。本研究首先通過跨域数据來檢測音樂會、遊行示威和展覽等會極大影響出行需求的社會事件。如果發現社會事件, 首先確定相關的擁擠點。每個點都被視為一個小網路。然後, 研究每個小網路內的動態旅客出行需求，建立一個區域常規社會行為動力學的概率模型, 描述了區域內沒有發生社會事件的客流概率和發生異常社會事件的客流。為預測由社會事件引起的短期旅客出行需求, 設計了一個滾動預測方法。根據需求預測和動態交通狀況, 提出了線上計程車調度的滾動時域框架。在每個滾動時域內, 根據需求預測結果作為不確定輸入, 以隨機的即時計程車服務供給和預設的乘客滿意度為約束條件, 提出並解決魯棒車輛調度問題。 該專案的最終目標是設計一個理論上可行且可實用的框架。因此, 該專案將與香港和泰國的計程車行業合作夥伴建立強有力的合作關係, 並基於實際数据和現有的士調度系統開展研究。該項目將受益于項目主持人及主要參與人在香港和泰國開展此類項目的實際經驗,確保研發的系統的可行性和實用性。

15210617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15210617.value: In buildings in the tropics and sub-tropics, the controls of both indoor air temperature and humidity are equally important. In small- to medium-scale buildings such as residences, direct expansion (DX) based air conditioning (A/C) systems are widely used for the control of indoor thermal environment because they are compact in volume, high in energy efficiency and low in operation and maintenance costs. However, to simultaneously control indoor air temperature and humidity using DX AC systems is a great challenge. While the application of variable speed (VS) technology to DX AC systems can help achieve simultaneous control over indoor air temperature and humidity, due to the reduced total supply air flow rate in order to have a lower evaporating temperature and thus a greater moisture removal capacity, two problems are created: the total output cooling capacity is reduced and a poorer indoor air velocity distribution adversely affects indoor thermal comfort for occupants. In this proposed project, to mitigate the two problems a novel DX based A/C system having a two-sectioned cooling coil (TS-DXAC) is proposed and its inherent operational characteristics in terms of the relationships between its output total cooling capacity (TCC) and equipment sensible heat ratio (E SHR) will be studied for different designs and operational conditions, primarily by simulation supplemented by experiments. The evaporator in the proposed TS-DXAC system will have two parallel-connected sections operating at two different evaporating temperatures, and a constant total supply air flow rate passing through the entire two-sectioned evaporator will be maintained for enhanced output cooling and dehumidification capacity and improved indoor air velocity distribution. The successful carrying out of the proposed project will help achieve better thermal comfort for occupants, improved indoor air quality (IAQ) and reduced energy use through enhanced indoor humidity control, by using the proposed TS-DXAC systems in small- to medium- scale buildings in the tropics and sub-tropics. The long-term significance of the proposed project is its contribution to sustainability by reducing the energy use for air conditioning in buildings while improving the thermal comfort of building occupants, and to the advancement of DX A/C technology. While the project outcomes are expected to be applicable to all tropical and sub-tropical climates, they will be particularly useful to Hong Kong where DX A/C systems are widely used and control over the indoor thermal environment using DX A/C systems has always been a great challenge. 在熱帶和亞熱帶地區的建築中，對室內溫度和濕度的控制是同等重要的。在住宅樓等中小型建築，由於直膨式空調系統體積小，能效高，運行和維護費用低，它被廣泛用於控制室內熱環境。但是直膨式空調系統很難同時控制室內溫濕度。儘管應用變頻技術於直膨式空調系統可以實現同時控制室內溫濕度，但是為了降低蒸發溫度和提高除濕效果而降低的總送風量會造成的兩個問題：一是減少了總輸出製冷量，二是造成了室內較差的風速分佈，進而影響人體熱舒適。 為了緩解以上兩個問題，本研究課題提出了一種新型的帶有雙冷卻盤管直膨空調系統。在各種設計和運行工況下，其總輸出製冷量和顯熱比的關係等包含在內的內在運行特性通過模擬輔以實驗的方法進行研究。在此次提出的帶有雙冷卻盤管直膨空調系統的蒸發器中，兩段相互連接的平行的盤管運行在不同的蒸發溫度，而經過雙冷卻盤管蒸發器的總送風量將維持不變，這是為了提高輸出製冷量，除濕能力以及改善室內風速分佈。 提出這種新型空調系統的意義在於它可以有利於提高熱帶和亞熱帶地區中小型建築的室內人體熱舒適，室內空氣品質同時減少因濕度控制而產生的能耗。從長遠角度來看，這種空調系統因能耗低熱舒適性好從而將會為可持續發展做出貢獻，促進對直膨式空調系統的發展。另外，此次課題的科研成果可以用於熱帶和亞熱帶氣候，尤其對直膨空調系統一直廣泛存在但對熱環境卻沒有良好控制策略的香港非常適用。

15211217.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15211217.value: 具有視野適應性解碼器的3D全景視頻編碼和轉碼

15211217.label: Project Objectives
15211217.value: So far, the intra-frame coding techniques in 3D holoscopic/LF videos have widely been investigated in the literature, and current inter-frame coding techniques are mainly designed for 2D videos. However, these techniques are not suitable for 3D holoscopic/LF video due its distinct repetitive patterns among micro-images. Therefore, one of the objectives in this proposal is focusing on designing a new low-complexity motion estimation strategy to exploit the repetitive patterns in inter-frame coding for 3D holoscopic videos. Although the 3D holoscopic coding scheme can achieve significant coding gains, transmitting the entire LF data might induce obstruction because the user requires waiting until the whole bitstream arrives before it can be visualized. It is independent on users’ preferences, requirements, and the type of interaction the user prefers doing. This motivates us to introduce the new concept of FoV adaptability for this purpose. Therefore, another objective of this proposal is to adopt this FoV adaptability into the completely new 3D holoscopic coding framework with the consideration of both coding and transcoding efficiency. The transcoding process will introduce high processing complexity unavoidably. Due to this fact, compressed-domain transcoding will be the approach in this study. Results of our preliminary study show that degree of uniformity of motion vectors is reduced, which is not in favor of the compressed-domain transcoding process. Although the proposed motion estimation strategy using the repetitive patterns among micro-images can already increase the motion vector uniformity during encoding, it is not sufficient for efficient transcoding. In respond such challenge further, we will explore a new joint coding and transcoding mechanism by making use of structural information of the LF information in order to determine the optimized motion vectors for both coding and transcoding process.

15211217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15211217.value: 隨著三維（3D）視頻技術不斷發展，人們可以擁有更加身臨其境的觀看體驗。如今，3D視頻技術的應用不僅局限於劇院，它對於家庭娛樂變得也越來越有趣。然而，在家庭中3D視頻的要求與在戲劇場景中截然不同。在劇院中，佩戴特殊3D眼鏡的觀眾需要在指定的一段時間內坐在椅子充分關注電影。而在客廳環境中，長時間地佩戴特殊眼鏡會導致眼睛疲勞和頭痛。對無眼鏡並且無疲勞3D視頻的獲取和顯示系統的研究一直在迅速發展。與立體顯示系統相比，3D光場攝像機和顯示器的最新進展是將3D可視化在平滑運動視差和廣視野（FoV）方面向前推進的關鍵步驟。光場（LF）3D顯示器能夠將視頻像全景圖一樣顯示給多個無眼鏡並且自由移動的觀眾。通過將微透鏡陣列（MLA）放置在高分辨率的傳感器之前，LF /全息視頻由每個微透鏡中的場景的空間和角度信息組成，並且產生大量複雜的數據。因此，JPEG和MPEG已經建立了相關的工作組來發展LF /全景圖像和視頻編碼的標準化。然而，觀看自由是以解碼器的複雜度和具有豐富視點的視頻數據量為代價的。由於能夠顯示多達數百個視角的完整的FoV LF顯示器是非常昂貴的，預期只有少數客戶端或顯示器能夠解碼所有視點。在這種情況下，3D全景視頻服務器應該具有從LF壓縮比特流中提取子視點集的能力。實際上，文獻中還沒有3D全景視頻系統的FoV適應性過程的研究。在此研究中，我們將探討一種具有FoV適應性的新型3D全景視頻編碼和轉碼方案，並對一些相關技術進行調查，以實現所需組件並解決這些具有挑戰性的問題。

15211217.label: Realisation of objectives
15211217.value: Objective 1: To evaluate the proposed idea, we have first implemented the new motion compensated prediction framework in Light Field Coding (LFC). Our work investigated a possible trend in the near future of performing LFC by exploring the repetitive patterns among micro-images in both intra/inter-frame coding for 3D holoscopic/LF video. After the investigation, we designed a new LFC model using Screen Content Coding (SCC) to encode LF video based on LF video characteristics. The adoption of SCC is due to the reason that SCC is a recently developed extension profile of High Efficiency Video Coding (HEVC), and Intra block copy (IBC) mode is a new coding mode to find the repeating patterns such as text and graphics in computer screen content (SC). With the image characteristics that there are plentiful repeating patterns within the LF videos, the SCC encoder can be an encoder for encoding LF videos as well. However, there are many assumptions or constraints that are based on the SC video characteristics in SCC, which limit the coding performance of LF videos. Thereby, we also contrived a new LFC model in the SCC encoder to further boost the coding efficiency for LF videos. With modifications, our proposed SCC encoder is still definitely conformed to the standard, which means that the bitstreams, encoded by our SCC encoder, are decodable by the standard SCC decoder without any modifications. On top of our new LFC model, we also developed a fast IBC search to reduce the complexity. It is also noted that our proposed LFC model facilitates generating the SCC conformed bitstream such that a user equipped with an SCC decoder can decode the bitstream. This approach provides a short-term solution in an effort to LF video compression. As compared with the recent development of LF image compression which is non-conformed bitstream with the current standards, our approach can achieve a more reasonable increase in both encoding and decoding complexities. To exploit the repetitive patterns among micro-image (MI) for motion estimation, we then designed a motion estimation algorithm using multiple search windows (SWs) based on the MI structure. Instead of using the traditional single and large SW, a number of small SWs are adopted for motion estimation due to the repetitive patterns among Mis. It can be observed that the best motion vector is usually around the multiple of the MI resolution. Our result shows that the complexity can be reduced to about 25% on average of the original ME with large SW while the rate-distortion loss is smaller than 0.06dB on average. Objective 2: Light Field is a collection of light rays, with their spatial information and, critically, the angular path of those light rays resulting in an LF image. The basic way to render a viewpoint image from the LF image in which the size of MI is Nx x Ny is based on the patch. The patch with the fixed size of nx x ny is selected from each MI. The viewpoint image is rendered by tiling the selected patch together. Different viewpoint images can be chosen by varying the relative position of the patch within the MI. Field-of-view (FoV) is an important parameter of any 3D display technology, which refers to the emission range of a display screen. Different selection of light rays generates three hierarchical FoV levels. Including all light rays represent the full FoV and it corresponds to the whole LF image. If only central light rays are considered, a narrow FoV at the center (FoV(C)), corresponding to the reduced resolution of the LF image is created. FoV(C) can be widened to FoV(W) if the boundary light rays are also included. The concept of the proposed FoV adaptability is to extract hierarchical subsets with various FoV from the LF raw data. In other words, the FoV of the LF image can grow from the center to the border patches in each MI. This FoV adaptability is extremely helpful to the 3D holoscopic video system that multiple end-users can extract a different subset of the LF raw data to be transmitted and displayed. It provides the flexibility to meet different LF display architectures that have been so far demonstrated to support various FoV capabilities. With the limited FoV LF 3D display always happening at any given time for a single user, the concept of FoV adaptability, and the relationship between the light rays and the LF images, firstly suggested in this work, allow the reductions in bandwidth requirement and the decoder complexity for a reduced LF data after transcoding. In our study, we proved that transcoding the entire LF image to the reduced set of the LF image is a smart solution. Our new 3D holoscopic coding/transcoding framework are tailor-made to FoV adaptability in 3D holoscopic video, for extracting the desired set of the LF images from the entire LF image based on the information of the unique 3D holoscopic video structure. Objective 3: During the transcoding into the LF compressed bitstream with the desired FoV, the straightforward approach to generating a reduced set of LF pixel data is to first decode the video, extracting appropriate pixels in the desired viewpoints in the pixel domain, and then re-encode it by exhaustively looking for the new structure similarity (SS) vectors and motion vectors in the reduced spatial resolution LF data. Although the multiple SW motion estimation proposed in 3D holoscopic video coding can achieve complexity savings, the motion re-estimation process in 3D-HVT is still very time consuming. During the transcoding into the LF compressed bitstream with the desired FoV, a compressed-domain or information re-using approach is adopted in the proposed 3D-HVT. All the transcoding works proposed in the literature have been done for reduced spatial resolution transcoding in which pixel subsampling is to employ a fixed chessboard pattern. This work successfully implemented a temporal/spatial reduced resolution transcoding algorithm. Nonetheless, the reduced spatial resolution LF data is not in a fixed chessboard pattern. Instead, it is composed of a sparse set of patches from different EIs. No algorithm in the literature, so far, has been proposed to deal with this special reduced-resolution for 3D-HVT. In this study, we proposed the joint coding and transcoding mechanism to reduced-resolution transcoding with a sparse set of patches. The joint coding and transcoding mechanism makes use of structural information of LF information to determine the optimal motion vectors for both coding and transcoding processes.

15211217.label: Major findings and research outcome
15211217.value: 3D holoscopic videos captured by LF cameras bring viewers with the real 3D sensations of scenes. Its future success in the consumer market relies not only on technological advances but also on the flexibility of the encoding format on 3D contents that are adaptive to a wide range of different applications. For scenarios with limited decoder capability or reduced transmission bandwidth, just a subset of the viewpoints can be decoded by the client. In this research, the server is designed to offer the adaptation functionality to support this. To do so, the flexible bitstream adaptation process can be done at the server where only the sub-bitstreams with less bandwidth and desired by the client are transmitted, and other irrelevant views are discarded. After bitstream transcoding, the sub-bitstreams must be decodable by heterogeneous LF 3D-displays. Efficient holoscopic video coding is the key factor for the success of these applications. Recent studies give much attention to 3D holoscopic video, more specific to intra-frame coding. Only very limited works proposed to realize inter-frame coding and the adaptation process of LF data streams. Therefore, in this research, we have studied the use of a completely new motion estimation strategy for inter-frame 3D holoscopic video coding and transcoding techniques to facilitate flexible FoV selection from the LF data streams. For this, an individual transcoding unit in the server serves an individual user, who can request specific 3D video with the desired FoV. In the literature, there were two major works for scalable 3D holosopic video coding schemes in intra-frame only. One approach is to use a three-layer 3D holoscopic scalable coding architecture. A single 2D view for 2D display in the base layer, a stereo-pair for stereoscopic displays, and full 3D holoscopic video for LF displays. Another approach is a three-layer scheme. From the first to second layers, spatial scalability is provided, and from the second to third layers, quality scalability. In theory, the proposed 3D-HVT scheme is a fine granularity approach in terms of FoV, and only one LF compressed bitstream needed to be stored. In the conclusion to this research study, we designed joint coding and transcoding mechanism in order to achieve good trade-off among coding efficiency, complexity and FoV adaptability for 3D holosopoic videos. This is a very fruitful direction for further investigation in 3D holoscopic videos. As a result, six journal papers and two conference papers have been published in this project.

15211217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15211217.value: The introduction of FoV adaptability into the transcoding is brand new concept. Efficient coding/transcoding of these data is crucial for the success of these applications. Consequently, the new JPEG PLENO and the third phase of Free-viewpoint TV initiatives aiming at free navigation and full parallax 3D video applications are developing various new standards for this purpose. We expect the work in the standard organization will adopt new coding/transcoding tools in the future standard with the support of FoV adaptability. In our plan, we will also plan to make a comparative study with the new tools with FoV adaptability. When the performance of the proposed framework with individual techniques is proved to be better than the future approaches in the coding standardization activities. The core techniques in this research will be submitted to JVET for their consideration and possible inclusion in future video coding standards. Therefore, in the long term, we should participate in JVET meetings to promote our techniques in future video coding standards. Our present study will have a remarkable long-term and significant impact on the advancement of future 3D holoscopic video coding technology.

15211217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15211217.value: 3D-video technologies become increasingly interesting for home entertainment where wearing special glasses in a living room environment causes eyestrain after prolonged watching. Light field (LF) 3D displays are capable of showing the video to multiple glasses-freely moving audiences. By placing the microlens array in front of the high-resolution sensor, the LF/holoscopic video consists of spatial and angular information of the scene in each microlens resulting in a massive amount of complex data. However, the viewing freedom comes at the expense of the decoder’s complexity and the amount of data with rich viewpoints. It is expected that only a small number of displays can decode all viewpoints since a full field-of-view LF display, which can display up to hundreds of views, is very expensive. So, a 3D holoscopic video server should have the capability of extracting a sub-set of viewpoints from an LF compressed bitstream. There has a limited study on this FoV adaptation process of 3D holoscopic video. This research designed a joint coding/transcoding framework for 3D holoscopics contents which not only be of great value to theoretical studies but can also lay down a solid foundation for the future 3D video system, where the only subset of FoV with less bandwidth and desired by the client is sent.

15211317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15211317.value: Optical communication system serves as the backbone of modern Internet and provides ultra-wide bandwidth for data communication. Optical fiber is indispensable transmission medium due to its ultralow loss. However, major functional elements of optical communication systems including lasers, modulators, and photo-detectors are still discrete components. The light has to be coupled between the discrete functional elements with the transmission fibers, resulting in high coupling loss, low-energy efficiency, and high complexity. It will be great if the functions of these elements can be realized by the fiber itself, which will lead to integrated all-fiber optical communication system as future “information highway”. An optical modulator is one of key elements in fiber optic communication systems. Different kinds of waveguide-based optical modulators have been proposed and fabricated. Generally the light has to be coupled into the modulator from the fiber and then coupled out again to the fiber. It will be a breakthrough to demonstrate modulation function in fiber itself and realize high-speed all-fiber modulator in optical communication systems. In this project, we propose to demonstrate graphene-assisted all-fiber modulator and optimize its system performance. As a two-dimensional (2D) honeycomb lattice monolayer, graphene was widely studied since its controllable carrier doping, fast carrier relaxation time, and highly compatible integration. However, both modulation depth and transmittance are limited for the modulators based on discrete waveguides with graphene. We propose to demonstrate all-fiber electro-optical (EO) intensity modulator by applying electrical voltage to D-shape fiber coated with graphene and improve modulation depth and transmittance. Another scheme for intensity modulation is converted from phase modulation induced in graphene-coated fiber by interferometer. However, the conversion by traditional Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) is bulky and unstable. We will explore our novel in-fiber miniaturized modal interferometer (MMI) graphene-assisted structure to convert the phase modulation to stable intensity modulation. We will also use partly side-etched or D-shape fiber Bragg grating (FBG) covered with graphene to create tunable offset optical filter based on the photo-induced refractive index change, and integrate it with our modulator in the same fiber to improve the generated data quality. We have demonstrated digital signal processing (DSP) techniques combined with optical filter for optimizing regular optical communication systems. Here we will test our all-fiber modulator with optical filter in high-speed system (up to 100-Gbit/s), and develop DSP techniques including pre-code and equalizer to improve the performance further, which can be the first detailed study on system level for graphene-assisted all-fiber modulator. 光通信系統作為現代互聯網的骨幹，為數據通信提供超寬帶寬。光纖由於超低損耗而成為不可或缺的傳輸介質。然而，光通信系統的主要功能元件（包括激光器，調製器和光電檢測器）仍然是分立元件。光必須在傳輸光纖與分立功能元件之間耦合，造成高耦合損耗，低能量效率和高複雜性。如果這些元件的功能可以通過光纖本身實現，將可建立基於全光纖通信系統的未來“信息高速公路”。光調製器是光纖通信系統的關鍵元件之一。目前廣泛使用的是基於波導的分立光學調製器。光必須從光纖耦合到調製器中，然後再次耦合到光纖。在光纖通信系統中使光纖本身具備調製功能，實現高速全光纖調製器將是一個突破。 在這個項目中，我們將實現石墨烯輔助的全光纖調製器並優化其系統性能。作為二維（2D）材料，石墨烯由於其可控的載流子摻雜，快速載流子弛豫時間和高度兼容性而被廣泛研究。然而，基於石墨烯的離散波導調製器，調製深度和透射率都受到限制。我們建議通過對塗有石墨烯的D型光纖施加電壓來實現全光電光（EO）強度調製器，並提高調製深度和透射率。另一種方案是通過干涉儀在石墨烯塗覆的光纖中將相位調製轉為強度調製。然而，傳統的馬赫曾德爾干涉儀（MZI）尺寸大且不穩定。我們將探索石墨烯輔助的新型光纖微型模間干涉儀（MMI）結構，將相位調製轉換為穩定的強度調製。我們還將使用由石墨烯覆蓋的部分側蝕或D型光纖布拉格光柵（FBG），實現可調的偏移光學濾波器，並將其與我們的調製器集成在同一光纖中，以提高產生的數據質量。我們將在高速系統中測試帶有光濾波器的全光纖調製器，並開發數字信號處理（DSP）技術，包括預代碼和均衡器，以進一步提高性能，對石墨烯輔助的全光纖調製器進行首次詳細的系統層面的研究。

15211317.label: Realisation of objectives
15211317.value: All objectives set out in the original proposal have been thoroughly studied and achieved. As for the detailed progress, we have fully achieved objectives 1, 2 and 3 by the mid of year 2019, objectives 4, 5 and 6 by the end of year 2020, and objective 7 by the mid of 2021, respectively. For objectives 1, 2 and 3, we study the all-optical light modulator based on tapered fiber which is also successfully achieved in our experiment. The fiber tapering is realized by mechanical stretching under the circumstances of H2 and O2 heating. The thermal heating process gives rise to the melt of fiber structure and various fiber tapers can be achieved through mechanical stretching with different speeds. Firstly, the generator of H2 and O2 is turned on until the H2 concentration reached a certain value. The H2 and O2 can be transferred to the fiber tapering machine through transporting pipeline for further utilization. The tapering machine is controlled by a personal computer which can regulate the parameters of the fiber tapering process, such as moving distance, moving speed, preheating time, etc. The tapering machine is initialized before the start of the fiber tapering experiment to find the precise position of fiber holders. Then the single-mode fiber is pre-processed by removing the protection layer and then the processed fiber is located on the fiber holders of the fiber tapering machine. After the setting of tapering parameters on the computer, the fiber tapering process is started. The heating tip moves towards the processed fiber and give the preheating around 5 s. Afterward, the two fiber holders move slowly in opposite directions until reaching the setting position. From the user interface of the fiber tapering machine software, we can see that various parameters can be adjusted to control the shape of the produced fiber taper. Among these parameters, the preheating time, the moving speed and distance of the fiber holders (in red circles) are extremely important for shaping the tapered fiber. With repetitive trials and multiple tuning of the three parameters, the preheating time of 5 s, moving speed of 20 mm/min and the moving distance of 18 mm are selected to generate the fiber taper with proper diameter and cone shape. For the normal SMF, the diameter is around 125 μm and the fiber diameter is decreased to about 3~5 μm after the process of fiber tapering. The graphene nanoflakes are purchased from Xianfeng Nanomaterials Technology Company (XFNANO). The diameter of the nanoflakes is around 5 μm and the average thickness is about 3 nm. The graphene nanoflakes are dispersed in deionized water and then the graphene solution was processed by ultrasonic for 1 hour to disperse the nanoflakes as much as possible. After that, by using the drop-cast method, the graphene nanoflakes can be attached to the tapered fiber. For objective 4, 5 and 6, we make deep and systematic study on the performance of the proposed light modulator. The relationship between input power and output power through the pure microfiber and graphene-coated microfiber is investigated, respectively. It can be found that with the increase of input power from 5 mW to 30 mW, the output power shows corresponding rising. The transmittance is measured to be around 75% before graphene coating and 40% after graphene coating. The difference can be attributed to the light absorption of graphene nanoflakes. It should be noted that with different tapering shapes of microfibers and graphene coating conditions, the light transmittance through the fiber taper will change accordingly. Based on our trials, the insert loss of the proposed light modulator can range from 4 dB to 20 dB. The spectrum is recorded from 1500 nm to 1660 nm, and it can be seen that the laser energy is mainly centralized in the range of 1540 nm to 1640 nm. Thus, based on the transmission spectrum, a filter of 1530 nm is utilized for filtering the femtosecond laser energy. In addition, a strong signal peak can be found in the recorded oscillogram of the femtosecond laser which is induced by the femtosecond laser pulse. We study the influence of input light on the output signals received from the oscilloscope. We find that the rising of pumping laser energy gives rise to a small change of the base energy, but only results in the enhancement of peak amplitude. In addition, the introduction of CW laser has a great impact on the base energy and the amplitude of the peak signal shows a very slight change. We thus concluded that the amplitude of peak signal can only be influenced by femtosecond laser and the base energy of the output signal completely depends on the CW laser. The optical filter is the indispensable optical component that is used to eliminate experimental errors by removing the pumping laser. As the bandwidth of the femtosecond laser is much wider than that of the CW laser applied in the experiment, the filtering of the femtosecond laser can be easily realized by choosing the proper bandpass filter. The bandpass filters of 1550 nm and 1530 nm are selected to compare both of the output signals. Based on the experimental results, the 1550 nm filter cannot remove all of the pumping energy. However, when the 1530 nm filter is utilized, most of the pumping laser is successfully filtered from the output signals. Based on this, the transmitted signal emitted from CW laser source can be detected with slight disturbance of the femtosecond laser. In our experiment, the energy of the CW laser is set to be 10 mW and 20 mW, respectively. At 10 mW laser energy, no obvious signal peak can be found which can be attributed to the light absorption of CW laser. Further, when the energy of the CW laser is increased to 20 mW, a strong signal peak appears in the oscillogram. It is noted that the pumping energy is maintained the same only with the change of CW laser energy. Thus, the signal peak can be attributed to the femtosecond laser pumping. The femtosecond laser will pump the electrons from ground state to excited state so that part of the CW laser can transmit through the graphene-coated fiber taper and be collected by the PD at the receiving end. The measured response time is about 0.4 ns, indicating the potential for optical signal processing with a bandwidth up to 2.5 GHz. For objective 7, we have studied and developed the algorithms to improve the performance of the proposed modulator. Due to the COVID-19 special period, our experimental conditions are significantly limited because the travel constraints between Hong Kong and mainland China so we could not take full advantage of the equipment on both sides. Nevertheless, we still achieve all objectives and conduct some research beyond the original targets such as applying the developed fiber devices and systems for sensing and monitoring applications. We published 18 journal papers and 6 conference papers in total and graduated 2 PhD students supported by this project.

15211317.label: Major findings and research outcome
15211317.value: (1) The down-tapered single-mode fiber is successfully fabricated and the graphene nanoflakes are attached to the tapered fiber. By using the pumping of the femtosecond laser, the saturated absorption of graphene can be realized. And then the signal light can transmit through the graphene coat and be collected by the photodiode at the receiving end. The measured response time of the fabricated light modulator is about 0.4 ns, indicating the potential for optical signal processing with a bandwidth up to 2.5 GHz. By proper coding of the pumping laser, the modulation of signal light can be successfully realized. (2) Variable optical attenuation and optical modulation are essential operations in integrated photonic circuits. A new graphene plasmonic gap waveguide structure, which possesses the functions of variable optical attenuator and modulator are proposed and numerically investigated. The propagation and attenuation modes of the structure can be realized by tuning the gate voltage. The result shows that it can achieve great modulation depth per micrometre and the working frequency range of 8 THz or more for the variable optical attenuator and the modulator. It also has the advantages of high tolerance, large attenuation range and modulation depth, wide bandwidth and high integration without crosstalk, which would be promising for highly integrated optical circuits. (3) Beyond the original objectives, the all-fiber sensor based on hollow-core Bragg fiber has been successfully created in our work which displays excellent performance on sensing such as human breath monitoring. The response time of the proposed sensor is around 0.15 s which enables the rapid and precise recording of breath signals. The applied distance between fiber sensor and the human face is also investigated to reveal its influences on sensing results. Moreover, the hollow-core Bragg fiber sensor proves strong insensitivity to temperature and curvature variation, which demonstrates its reliable sensing performance in different application environments. (4) Beyond the original objectives, the Mach-Zehnder interferometer fiber sensor based on ring core fiber structure is successfully achieved. The experiments on temperature and refractive index (RI) sensing are conducted and dual demodulation of temperature and RI is realized. The maximum sensitivity of temperature sensing is 69 pm/℃ and that of RI sensing reaches 182.07 dB/RIU and -31.44 nm/RIU with the intensity and wavelength demodulation methods, respectively. The proposed MZI sensor has advantages of cost-effective source, ease of fabrication and high sensitivity for both temperature and RI sensing.

15211317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15211317.value: Further research of our developed fiber devices and systems assisted with 2-dimentional (2D) materials can be conducted. Moreover, a key point of 2D materials based optical modulator is to control the light-material interaction in a fast and accurate way. Metasurfaces, consisting of periodic sub-wavelength structures, have shown good properties to confine light in a small volume with ultra-high intensity, which can greatly enhance the light-material interaction. Therefore, the metasurfaces equipped with 2D materials provide new ways to design optical modulators. In our recent work, a silver-silicon-silver (Ag-Si-Ag) structure is found to mainly form a magnetic dipole in the near-infrared wavelength band when illuminated by a plane wave. Since most of the electric field is confined in the Si layer in an in-plane direction, the light-graphene interaction can be greatly enhanced. When apply the gate voltage on the graphene, the chemical potential of the graphene can be changed. Then, the surface conductivity of graphene will vary with the chemical potential. Hence, the total resonance condition of the graphene-assisted metasurface can be tuned. In the future work, we will try to fabricate this graphene-assisted metasurface and then test the modulation speed and the extinction ratio.

15211317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15211317.value: In our work, different fiber devices with specifically designed structures have been successfully fabricated. It displays good performance on various applications of for communication and sensing. Based on the proposed fiber structures, light modulation can be realized through tuning light interference which can be stably excited through the specifically structured fiber. The all-optical light modulator with down-tapered single-mode fibers (SMFs) structure assisted with graphene is proposed and demonstrated in this work. The performances of the proposed and successfully fabricated light modulator are studied and improved. The experimental results demonstrate a feasible method for all-optical light modulation with a down-tapered fiber structure assisted with graphene nanoflakes. The measured response time is up to 0.4 ns, indicating the potential for optical signal processing with the bandwidth of up to 2.5 GHz. We demonstrate a feasible method for all-optical light modulation with a down-tapered fiber structure assisted with graphene nanoflakes and the research will play a very important part in the optical communication system to simplify the optical components and realize all-fiber light modulation. Beyond that, we also applied our developed fiber devices and systems for sensing of temperature, humidity, refractive index, curvature, and human breath.

15212217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15212217.value: Many urban cities are experiencing fast growth due to rapid urbanization. In 2008, the world’s urban population outpaced the rural population for the first time. By 2030, twice as many people will live in cities than in 1970. This shift in population requires meticulous transport planning in order to meet the travel needs of these fast-growing urbanized cities. Current practice in transport planning procedures, which were mostly developed by North America and the United Kingdom, are inadequate for modeling the combination of changing demographics, land use development, and rapid transport infrastructure development in urban cities. On the other hand, the state-of-the-art, activity-based travel demand forecasting procedure is too data intensive and time-consuming for planning applications in growing urban cities. In addition, traditional transport planning assessment is based on mobility-oriented analysis, which tends to emphasize on the private motorized transport mode (i.e., personal automobiles). However, most urban cities have a multi-modal transport system that emphasizes public transport more than private transport. In Hong Kong, over 90% of daily trips are made using multiple public transport modes. This requires a fundamental change in how problems are defined and solutions evaluated. Hence, a paradigm shift is needed by moving from mobility-based planning to accessibility-based planning, which focuses on people and their travel behaviors in multi-modal transport networks. This proposal aims to build an integrated path flow estimator (PFE) analysis framework as an alternate travel demand forecasting methodology that can address the weaknesses of traditional transport planning in a consistent manner, while acknowledging the difficulties of developing an activity-based travel demand model in fast-growing urban cities. In addition, this new PFE analysis framework will advance the state of knowledge by incorporating state-of-the-art discrete choice models for estimating and forecasting travel demand for both public and private transport modes and mixed trips involving more than one mode, as well as assessing people-based accessibility in a multi-modal transport network. To show proof of concept, case studies using Hong Kong and Shanghai will be conducted to test the integrated PFE analysis framework. The proposed methodology is particularly relevant to Hong Kong and urban cities in Mainland China, which are subject to very rapid changes in land development and high growth in transport infrastructure construction. It has the potential to help transport planners and policymakers evaluate the accessibility of multi-modal transport networks such that cost-effective strategies can be developed to accommodate the growing travel needs of rapid urbanization. 快速的城市化进程导致很多城市的人口急速膨胀。2008年，世界上城市人口首次超过了农村人口；预计到2030年，城市人口将是1970年的2倍。这种人口转移需要精细化的交通规划，以满足快速发展的城市化进程带来的巨大交通需求。当前主流的交通规划方法，主要是由北美和英国开发的，不能够对城市的人口变化、土地开发及快速的交通基础设施建设进行整体建模。另一方面，当前最先进的基于活动的交通需求预测方法不仅依赖于大量的数据，而且进行大规模的规划模型求解时需要耗费巨大的时间。此外，传统的交通规划评估主要研究小汽车出行模式。然而，很多城市拥有一个多模式的交通系统，且公共交通往往比私人交通更得到城市管理者的重视。在香港，超过90%的日常出行由多模式的公共交通系统承担。这就需要从根本上重新定义交通规划所面对的问题和解决途径。因此，交通规划需要一种新的范式转型，由基于个体机动性的规划转向基于可达性的规划，更加强调出行个体本身及其在多模式网络中的出行行为。 本项目试图构建一个一体化的路径流量估计模型分析框架，该框架可以作为一种新的交通需求预测方法，一方面克服传统交通规划模型在一致性方面的缺陷，另一方面也避免在快速发展的城市中难以构建基于活动的交通需求模型的困难。此外，这一新的路径估计模型分析框架将结合前沿的离散选择模型进行交通需求估计和预测（包括公共交通方式、私人交通方式和组合交通方式等），同时对多模式交通网络中基于人的可达性进行评估。为了验证所提出的一体化路径流量估计分析框架，将以香港和上海进行案例分析。本项目所提出的方法可以适用于香港和中国大陆的城市，因为这些城市不仅土地利用变化快，而且交通基础设施建设迅猛。该方法可以帮助交通规划师及政策制定者评估多模式交通网络的可达性和制定经济高效的策略，以适应快速城市化带来的不断增长的交通需求。

15212217.label: Realisation of objectives
15212217.value: Objective 1 is to develop the PFE framework for estimating travel demands at different spatial levels of the multi-modal transportation network. Specifically, the existing PFE model is extended: (1) to consider more transport modes, such as major public transit modes; (2) to consider more choice dimensions; (3) to take advantage from emerging sources of data in real-world transportation networks. As for extension (1), an integrated PFE model is developed using the hyperpath size formulation, which specifically considers the frequency-based public transit services and integrates multiple emerging data sources. This work has been published in Transportation Research Part E (Paper 1) and presented in two conference papers (i.e., paper C1 at the 22nd Hong Kong Society of Transportation Studies Conference (HKSTS), December 9-11, 2017, Hong Kong, China; paper C2 at the 23rd HKSTS Conference, December 8-10, 2018, Hong Kong, China). On this basis, Paper 2 further considers the strategy-based transit demand assignment (published in European Journal of Operational Research). Paper 3 further developed a combined travel demand model to investigate mode choice and route choice in the congested multi-modal transportation network (published in the journal of Transportation Research Record). As for extension (2), Paper 4 proposed a model to consider three classes of travelers with different attitudes to cycling and incorporate the safety and air quality concerns of cyclers in addition to travel distance (published in International Journal of Sustainable Transportation). Paper 5 developed a system dynamics approach to investigate the influence of a range of microscopic AV user behaviors and their interaction with external environment, such as infrastructure installation, policy sentiment, and law enforcement (published in Transportation Research Part C). Several other studies have been carried out for extension (3) to investigate some specific choice dimensions of individuals on the travel demand pattern, including the stochastic route choice with environmental-oriented guidance from the advanced traveler information system (Paper 6 published in Sustainability), the joint activity-travel choices made by different types of households (Paper 7 published in Transportation Research Part B), and the joint residential location and route choice (paper C3 presented at the 24th HKSTS Conference, December 14-16, 2019, Hong Kong, China). An integrated data-driven approach has also been proposed for the simultaneous estimation of the four travel choice dimensions with multiple data sources (see paper C4 presented at the 14th International Conference of Eastern Asia Society for Transportation Studies (EASTS), September 12-15, 2021, Hiroshima, Japan). Objective 2 is to advance the PFE models which were extensively developed based on the traditional multinomial logit (MNL) travel choice model. Two issues exist in the MNL model: (1) the similarity issue, i.e., the ignoration of correlations among alternatives in different choice dimensions, and (2) the heterogeneity issue, i.e., the inadequacy to model alternatives with distinct magnitudes of travel utility. Extended logit models have been applied to address the first issue (similarity issue), including the path-size logit model (Papers 2,3,4,5,8) and the paired combinatorial logit model (paper C5 presented at the 98th Transportation Research Board (TRB) Annual Meeting, January 13-17, 2019, Washington D.C., USA) that account for the effect of path overlapping on route choice, the cross-nested logit model to consider mode similarity in mode choice (Paper 3), and the Dogit model for capturing the captivity of travelers in mode choice (Paper 8 published in Transportation Research Part A). The effect of the second issue (heterogeneity issue) on travel choice is empirically investigated in Paper 9 (published in Travel Behavior and Society). Paper 10 provide a thorough discussion on the properties of weibit-based models and illustrates its theoretical derivation and advantages compared with the logit-based models (published in the Journal of Choice Modelling). Several extended weibit models have also been developed to address both similarity and heterogeneity issues together, and applied in equilibrium demand models (i.e., paper C6 presented at the 98th TRB Annual Meeting, January 13-17, 2019, Washington D.C., USA; and paper C7 presented at the 25th HKSTS Conference: Sustainable Mobility, December 9-10, 2021, Hong Kong, China). Papers 11 and 12 (both published in Transportmetrica A) further investigated the theoretical properties of weibit-based models with respect to its application in travel demand modeling. The analysis of paradox problem can provide valuable insights for the planning and operation of transportation network (see Paper 13 published in Transportation Research Part B). Paper 14 developed a mixed itinerary-size weibit model to consider both heterogeneity in traveler’s perception and overlapping in rail trip itinerary for modeling the itinerary choice in railway networks (published in Transportmetrica A). Paper 15 (published in Sustainability) applied the weibit choice model in the travel choice within a multi-modal network with park & ride facilities. Objective 3 is to develop a network-based approach for evaluating the accessibility measures of individual modes and collective modes while consistent with the state-of-art choice models developed in Objective 2. The limitations of the logsum-based accessibility measure derived from the traditional logit choice model are empirically investigated in a real-world road network, and it is necessary to incorporate advanced choice models in the accessibility studies (see Paper 16 provided in the interim report). A case study extracted from the Hong Kong multi-modal network is conducted to show the application of the proposed approach for accessibility assessment in different planning scenarios. This work (conference paper C8) has been presented at the 14th International Conference of EASTS, September 12-15, 2021, Hiroshima, Japan. Paper 17 further developed a combined travel demand model for applying the proposed measure to accessibility and vulnerability assessment in congested multi-modal transportation network (published in Multimodal Transportation). Objective 4 is to implement the proposed framework and conduct case studies to demonstrate the proof of concept. An advanced Barzilai-Borwein (BB) step size determination scheme has been incorporated to accelerate the state-of-art gradient-based algorithm for solving the equilibrium travel demand model in road networks with both additive and non-additive path costs (see Paper 18 published in European Journal of Operational Research and Paper 19 published in Computers & Operations Research). The advanced gradient-based solution algorithms have also been extended for the combined travel demand models in the multi-modal network (see Paper 20 published in Journal of Advanced Transportation and paper C9 presented at the 22nd HKSTS Conference, December 9-11, 2017, Hong Kong, China). Cases studies have been conducted in various real-world networks, including the network Winnipeg, Canada (papers 2,4,11,16,18,19), the Jiangning district in Nanjing, China (paper 3), Seoul, Korea (papers 8,20), subnetwork of Harbin, China (paper 13), Chiang Mai, Thailand (Paper 15), subnetwork of Hong Kong (papers 17, C8), and the Chicago sketch network (Paper 18). The travel demand model was also applied to the network capacity analysis with integration of a new type of OD-level service quality constraint and the emerging big data analytics (see Paper 21 published in Transportation). Conference paper C10 further conducted post-analysis of the proposed modeling framework, including the sensitivity analysis and the uncertainty analysis (presented at the 23rd HKSTS Conference, December 8-10, 2018, Hong Kong, China).

15212217.label: Major findings and research outcome
15212217.value: The major research outcomes of this research project are the development, implementation, and post-analysis of the integrated PFE modeling framework which estimates the multi-level travel demand incorporating both travel choice behavior and data sources associated with a variety of transport services in the multi-modal network. Specifically, the outcomes include developments of transit-oriented PFE models (Papers 1-3) and travel demand models with emerging mode and technologies (Papers 4-7); development, analysis, and application of advanced travel choice models customized for the multi-modal network (Papers 8-15); accessibility measurement based on the PFE with advanced choice models (Papers 16-17); network capacity analysis based on the PFE modeling framework (Paper 21); and the development of advanced solution algorithms for the proposed PFE models. All of the abovementioned research out comes have been published in SCI journals. The major findings are: (1) The PFE model is flexible to incorporate multiple modes and multiple data sources for enhancing the quality of travel demand estimation. Various advanced travel choice models can also be flexibly integrated to improve model performance and interpretability while ensuring the application of efficient solution algorithms. (2) The extended weibit choice models are suitable to naturally address the issues embedded in commonly used logit models, including the consideration of heterogenous travel utility scales and the similarity among travel alternatives, including spatial correlation, mode similarity, path overlapping at different choice dimensions in the multi-modal transportation network. (3) The traditional logsum-based accessibility measure is also limited owing to the issues embedded in the traditional logit-based choice models, which will negatively affect the outcomes of accessibility and vulnerability analyses for the multi-modal network. Such limitations can be inherently addressed by the utility-based accessibility measure derived from weibit-based choice models while remaining consistent with the random utility theory.

15212217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15212217.value: Estimating and predicting the travel demand pattern in multi-modal transportation networks are imperative but difficult tasks for transportation planning and operation. This research aims to fulfill this gap by extending the flexible PFE model to account for varying transport services, emerging data sources, and complex travel choice behaviors in the multi-modal demand analysis. Results from this research project are encouraging and accepted in the international research communities. It would be interesting and worthwhile to further the research development to consider more emerging travel modes in the demand estimation, such as electric vehicles, connected and autonomous vehicles, ridesharing, and customized bus. The proposed research can also be extended to take advantage of various emerging data sources in the era of big data, e.g., the CCTV data, WiFi data, smartcard data, etc. Another useful extension would be developing and adapting more types of advanced choice models that are customized for specific infrastructures or operations, such as the electric vehicle charging facilities, metro line extensions, shared parking services, and road tolling schemes. These extensions will have broader impacts on improving the planning, design, and operations for the multi-modal transportation system in densely populated mega cities like Hong Kong.

15212217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15212217.value: PFE is a traffic observer that is flexible to incorporate multiple data sources for estimating and predicting the travel demands at different spatial levels. However, existing PFE models are developed mainly aiming at the private car in road networks, which is inadequate for application in congested cities with highly developed transit modes like Hong Kong. This research makes an initial effort to extend the PFE framework to consider the service characteristics of various transit and private modes and incorporate emerging sources of transit flow data, which enables the analysis of travel demand pattern in the multi-modal transportation network. Specifically, a variety of advanced travel choice models have been developed and adapted in the PFE framework to capture the complex travel behaviors at different choice dimensions, including activity choice, residential location choice, destination choice, mode choice, and route choice. Efficient state-of-art solution algorithms are developed and customized to facilitate implementation of the proposed PFE models in real-world case studies. The model outcomes can provide high-quality estimates of multi-level travel demand and the model post-analysis can provide accessibility and capacity assessment of multi-modal network. The results can be used to support urban and transportation planning in transit-oriented mega cities like Hong Kong.

15212317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15212317.value: 木質纖維素生物質主要由纖維素、半纖維素與木質素等三種天然化合物所構成。這些物質在植物細胞壁中形成一種三維的立體結構。纖維素纖維是一種由氫鍵連結的結晶/非結晶結構隨機交錯的長鏈狀多糖類聚合物。這些纖維進一步由半纖維素連結成束並被複雜且隨機鍵結的木質素結構黏合並包覆在內。各種以物理、化學與生物基礎的生物煉製方法在近年間大量被研發來分解細胞壁並有效地提取不同的化合物來產生高價產品。現今最常見的生物質降解技術是將生物質混合酸、鹼或其他化學物質並加熱至攝氏165至220度的熱化學處理方法為主流。處理過後的底物再輔以酶進行水解以提出各種醣類與其他產物。預處理和水解之優化條件(如溫度與pH)不同，導致生物轉化流程的優化變得極為複雜且成本極高。針對此一問題本研究團隊提出了以綠色溶劑的預處理方法進行生物質轉化。天然深共溶溶劑是一種由有機代謝物質以特定比例調製而成的低價液體溶劑。這類溶劑因其低健康風險與環境友好的特性已迅速成為化學製程中極具吸引力的一種材料，並有極佳機會用於低溫(小於攝氏100度)生物質降解上。由於學界對各種天然深共溶溶劑對預處理與水解的影響仍未有全盤的了解，有必較進行進一步的研究。在本計畫中天然深共溶溶劑將會首先應用於由細胞壁提出的天然纖維素之處理，並輔以反溶劑進行纖維素之重建及水解。我們會建立一種快速篩檢的流程對不同溶劑配方對各種木質生物質結構的效率進行量測。新設計的共溶溶劑將首先應用在模型物的降解上以了解反應機理與影響因子對反應動力的影響。協同溶劑或輔助化學藥劑將首先應用於木質素模型物在新溶劑中之降解。結合各種實驗結果此一溶劑系統將被應用在處理木質生物質之降解，並測試其對酶解反應的影響。最後，完整的反應系統將會在實驗室規模的反應器中進行測試。本計畫所建立的研究方法與成果結合新一代生物煉製技術與永續廢棄物經營理念希冀能對今日高等教育與科學研究提出貢獻。

To quantify the impacts of selected key parameters affecting the solubility of key plant cell wall components in different NDESs Hildebrand solubility theory was first applied to evaluate the ChCl/alchohols natural deep eutectic solvent (NDES), which suggested that 1,4-BDO had a smaller relative energy difference (RED) with lignin than other alcohols, implying a higher lignin dissolution capability of this organosolv pretreatment. In this study, we prepared various types of lignin from NDESs and diols pretreated Eucalyptus; and the composition and structure of the obtained lignin were investigated via chemical composition analysis and several types of nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) analyses. The potential advantages of the pretreatment process over monohydric alcohol pretreatments to fractionate reactive lignin and achieve high enzymatic sugar release were clarified. The Hansen solubility parameters were calculated to clarify the solvent power dissociating the lignin. Thermodynamics requires that the free energy of mixing must be zero or negative for the solution process to occur. Hildebrand and Scott pointed out that the solubility parameter should be considered as a free energy parameter. Solubility parameters are derived from the energy required to convert a liquid to a gas, which directly reflects the degree of dispersion forces, permanent dipole-permanent dipole forces, and hydrogen bonding hold to molecules of the liquid. Based on Hansen solubility theory, the relationships between lignin yields of different solvent systems and their corresponding solubility parameters (i.e., RED) were estimated to analyze the effects of lignin solubility capacity on the lignin fractionation yield of the solvents. The results indicated proper relationship between REDs and lignin yields for the selected solvents, with and without addition of ChCl. However, lignin yields of acid pretreatment with EG, 1,3-PG and 1,4-BDO were much higher than the predicted value. Therefore, more detailed analysis of the change of lignin physicochemical structures during acid pretreatments with EtOH and 1,4-BDO. In addition to the findings presented here, more research outputs have been published in Research Output items 8-1,5 and 9-1,2,4. 2. To investigate the mechanisms of substrate decomposition toward a complete dissolution of targeted waste derived lignocellulosic biomass using selected NDESs The chemical compositions of eucalyptus before and after pretreatment was determined according to the procedures established by the standard method of National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NERL). The hydrolyzed monomeric sugar units were quantified via high-performance liquid chromatography equipped with CHO-782 Transgenomic column; and acid insoluble lignin content was calculated gravimetrically. Different high boiling point alcohols, including EG, 1,3-PG, 1,4-BDO and glycerol were employed to investigate the effects of delignification versus the solubility parameters of the solvents on the delignification efficiencies. ChCl, the most common and inexpensive HBA of NDESs, was used to catalyze the biomass fractionation process, and ethanol was selected as a control to compare with NDESs. Dilute sulfuric acid was also used to catalyze organosolv pretreatments as it is an inexpensive strong acid that can be neutralized easily. The solvent systems of EtOH, EG, 1,3-PG, 1,4-BDO and glycerol with or without ChCl or acid were selected as comparisons to analyze the effects of catalysis on lignin fractionation efficiency. The results indicated that the addition of ChCl had only little effect on lignin fractionation while addition of sulfuric acid greatly improved the efficiency lignin fractionation. Woody biomass is physically larger, structurally stronger and denser, and has higher lignin content than agricultural biomass. As a result, some pretreatment methods had limited effectiveness on woody biomass. While lignin was subjected to depolymerized into small fractions during acidic conditions, which facile the dissolution of lignin in pretreatment solvent. In addition, two-dimensional heteronuclear single quantum coherence (HSQC) NMR analyses were conducted to determine the molecular-scale structure of lignin samples. beta-O-4, beta-5, and beta-beta were the dominant interunit linkages. A unique signal was discovered in the HSQC spectra of 1,4-BDO pretreated lignin, which indicated the presence of 1,4-BDO related functional group on the alpha position of beta-O-4 linkage. During acid-based pretreatments, the departure of a leaving group by an SN1 process from the alpha position of beta-O-4 linkage leads to the formation of a reactive benzylic carbocation intermediate. It was reported that S lignin features a higher level of readily cleavable beta-O-4 linkages, leading to dissociated lignin at lower molecular weight. 1,4-BDO pretreatment seems to be more powerful to remove S units than EtOH pretreatment, leading to a lower proportion of S lignin units remaining after 1,4-BDO pretreatment. Approximately 10% of beta-5 and 2% of beta-beta were detected in all lignin samples, indicating that organosolv did not impact these inter-unit linkages in comparison with DA lignin. More detailed findings are presented in Research Output items 8-3,8,&9. 3. To investigate the compatibility of residual NDESs with cellulase and the use of stabilizing agents for supporting the synergistic effects of solvents and enzyme Residual lignins (DA-S, EtOH-S, and 1,4-BDO-S) were prepared and purified according to a modified procedure. The pretreated eucalyptus was hydrolyzed by cellulase at a 2% (w/v) solid loading in 50mM sodium citrate buffer (pH = 4.8), 50 °C, 150 rpm for 72 h. Enzyme loading was set at 40 FPU/g substrate to convert most of the carbohydrates. After hydrolysis, the lignin residues were recovered by centrifugation and rinsed three times with distilled water. The crude lignin was then incubated overnight at 37 °C in 50 mM phosphate buffer (pH=7) with 1 U/mL Pronase. After filtration, the solid residues were extracted twice with 96% (v/v) dioxane/water mixture at room temperature for 48 h. The extracts were combined, rotary evaporated, and freeze-dried to obtain residual lignin for further analysis. Organosolv soluble lignins (i.e., EtOH-L and 1,4 BDO-L) were isolated from the liquid product. Three volumes of water were added into the pretreatment spent liquor and the precipitated lignin was rinsed with water to remove soluble impurities. The purified lignin was freeze-dried under vacuum for 24 h and stored in desiccators before analysis. To characterize the unique feature of the 1,4-BDO-L lignin, a 0.10 g lignin sample was extracted with 10 mL ethanol for 24 h. The extract was rotary-evaporated and freeze-dried to obtain EtOH-extract lignin, and the solid residue after the ethanol extraction was freeze-dried to obtain EtOH-insoluble lignin. Organosolv soluble lignin from the other pretreatments in this work was prepared as described above. More details of the studies have been presented in Research Output items 8-4,6,7 and 9-3,5,6. 4. To develop a low-temperature “one-pot” process to convert lignocellulose into monosaccharides and value-added lignin products An integrated biorefinery process was designed and investigated using pentanol-water biphasic pretreatment to simultaneously produce reactive lignin as well as a carbohydrate pulp which was amenable to bioethanol production. Pentanol is almost immiscible with water which can facilitate more efficient solvent recovery to physically separate hemicellulose and lignin. The results showed that the proposed biphasic pretreatment yielded 70.3% lignin dissolution in the organic phase while leaving cellulose as an insoluble solids. Simultaneous saccharification and fermentation resulted in 92.2% cellulose digestibility and ethanol yield of 0.41 g/g-glucan. In addition, biphasic pretreatment also preserved 42.5% of reactive beta-aryl ether linkages in fractionated lignin, which is higher than ethanosolv pretreatment (31.1%). The overall energy balance showed that the biphasic process yielded net positive energy of 1.1 MJ/kg-wood which was much higher than the dilute acid (-0.16 MJ/kg) and ethanosolv (-1.6 MJ/kg) processes. More details refer to Research Output items 8-10.

15212317.label: Major findings and research outcome
15212317.value: Alcohols can act as nucleophiles and react with the intermediate to form alpha-esterified lignin. As 1,4-BDO contains two hydroxyl groups, the unreacted hydroxyl group introduced a hydroxyl tail at the alpha position of the 1,4-BDO lignin. The inability to directly observe EtOH related alpha esterified signal in aliphatic regions of HSQC NMR spectra was possibly due to the absence of hydroxyl tail on EtOH esterified lignin and overlapping of signals from other interunit linkages of the lignin. The pretreated lignin demonstrated its major aromatic compositions consisting of S and G units for hardwood species. Condensed lignin was not observed in organosolv pretreated lignin, indicating that both EtOH and 1,4-BDO alleviated lignin condensation. In addition, most of the interunit linkages were absent in the NMR spectra of soluble lignin samples, implying significant degradation of lignins during organosolv pretreatments. Meanwhile, a kinetic model was developed to incorporate dynamic enzyme adsorption and product inhibition parameters into hydrolysis simulation. The enzyme adsorption coefficients obtained from Langmuir isotherm were fed dynamically into first order kinetics for simulating the equilibrium enzyme adsorption in hydrolysis. A fractal and product inhibition kinetics was introduced and successfully applied to improve the simulation accuracy on adsorbed enzyme and glucose concentrations at different enzyme loadings, lignin contents, and in the presence of Bovine Serum Albumin (BSA) and lysozyme. The model provided numerical proof quantifying the beneficial effects of both additives, which improved the hydrolysis rate by reducing the non-productive adsorption of enzyme on lignin. The hydrolysis rate coefficient and fractal exponent both increased with increasing enzyme loadings, and lignin inhibition exhibited with increasing fractal exponent. Compared to BSA, addition of lysozyme exhibited higher hydrolysis rates, which was reflected in the larger hydrolysis rate coefficients and smaller fractal exponents in the simulation. The model provides new insights to support process development, control, and optimization.

15212317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15212317.value: Aromatic compounds are important fuels and key chemical precursors for organic synthesis, however the current aromatics market are mainly relying on fossil resources which will eventually contribute to carbon emissions. Lignin has been recognized as a drop-in substitution to conventional aromatics, with its values gradually realized after tremendous research efforts recently. Advances of various biorefinery techniques is needed to facilitate the development of a possible lignin economics while overcoming the remaining challenging for lignin valorization. Continuous studies are needed to further explore lignin structures and the potential functions of lignin related chemical structures. Actions on development of lignin-first pretreatment, catalytic lignin depolymerization, and the high value products with possible benchmark with modern aromatics shall be our next research targets. Possible retrofit of conventional petroleum refinery for lignin products may be promoted and hopefully paving a way to progressively migrate the industry towards carbon neutrality.

15212317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15212317.value: Overall, the findings of this project have resulted fully or partially with acknowledgement in 9 journal publications, 6 conference presentations, and 3 PhD student trained or in training (refer to Part C for more details). This study aims to explore the potential of an innovative pretreatment solvent/reagent to isolate lignin without sacrificing its integrity. Organosolv pulping with diols (e.g., 1,4-BDO) implied it an effective delignification solvent for woods. However, this solvent system has never been applied in biorefinery for lignin valorization, of which particular attention have been paid on increasing the value of dissolved lignin structures. During conventional pretreatment process, cleavage of alpha-ether linkage of lignin forms a resonance stabilized benzyl carbocation, resulting in unfavorable condensation or lignin damage reactions. The pretreatment approach developed in this study offers a never-published reaction pathway to fractionate a new reactive lignin in a biorefinery. We found that diols could act as nucleophiles quenching the resonance stabilized benzyl carbocation and formed alpha-etherified lignin with hydroxyl tail. The hydroxyl tails (i.e., aliphatic hydroxyl group) improve the solubility of lignin in diols, preserving the beta-O-4 linkage in lignin residue for future lignin valorization, which significantly increase the potential market value of the final products.

15212417.label: Project Objectives
15212417.value: To develop a new research framework, whereby to quantitatively characterize and monitor pitting-type damage (with massive, disorderedly clustered craters and cracks); To hierarchically ally linear with nonlinear features of guided ultrasonic waves (GUWs), whereby to break through a bottleneck of GUW-based inspection when attempting to evaluate multitudinous damage disorderedly scattered within a single inspection area; To achieve insight into the mechanism of interlacing energy shift and cumulative energy transfer of GUWs when interacting with pitting damage, using theoretical analysis, modeling, and experiment; and To experimentally validate the proposed framework, using space structures with pitting craters.

15212417.label: Realisation of objectives
15212417.value: In this project, four objectives have been proposed, and all of them have been fully accomplished by the end of this project. Pervasive but insidious, pitting corrosion is a form of localized corrosion in engineering assets exposed to corrosive environments (e.g., ship hulls or offshore platforms). Possibly initiated by surface defect or damage in protective coating, pitting corrosion has a formation mechanism similar to that of crevice corrosion, but is more detrimental. Motivated by this, this proposed research aspired to a new framework to characterize disorderedly clustered pitting damage quantitatively and precisely, by hierarchically allying linear with nonlinear guided ultrasonic wave (GUW) features. From fundamental study to engineering applications, this research embraced in-depth analytical investigation, dedicated modeling, and intensive experiment. This completed GRF project included mainly the following aspects: (1) developed a new research framework, whereby to quantitatively characterize and monitor pitting-type damage (with massive, disorderedly clustered craters and cracks); (2) hierarchically allied linear with nonlinear features of guided ultrasonic waves (GUWs), whereby to break through a bottleneck of GUW-based inspection when attempting to evaluate multitudinous damage disorderedly scattered within a single inspection area; (3) achieved insight into the mechanism of interlacing energy shift and cumulative energy transfer of GUWs when interacting with pitting damage, using theoretical analysis, modeling, and experiment; and (4) experimentally validated the proposed framework, using real-world maritime structures with pitting corrosion and space structures with pitting craters. Fundamental investigations were first carried out. From fundamental research to application-oriented implementation, this proposed research has reached its expectation, ending up with an innovative yet practical SHM framework for pitting-type damage characterization. In conclusion, all the proposed research objectives have been successfully and fully accomplished.

15212417.label: Major findings and research outcome
15212417.value: Pitting-type damage, from pitting corrosion in maritime structures through debris-cloud-induced craters in space shielding layers to electrical pitting in bearings, is a sort of material degradation and structural lesion in engineering assets. Common but insidious, it typically features hundreds of clustered, localized craters and cracks disorderedly scattered over a wide area. Evaluation of this specific type of damage is far beyond the detectability of conventional approaches using guided ultrasonic waves (GUWs), because the large number of craters and cracks within the pitted area cause highly complex, mutually-interfering wave scattering, making signal interpretation a daunting task. This has created a clear impasse to GUW-based inspection when used to detect pitting damage, let alone the quantitative characterization of a pitted area. With this motivation, a new research framework has been developed via this GRF project, which has demonstrated capability of quantitatively characterizing pitting-type damage. The research outputs are expected to enhance safety, drive down exorbitant maintenance costs, and extend residual service life of ageing assets. From fundamental research to real-world application-oriented implementation, this proposed research has made contribution to the development of a new structural health monitoring framework for pitting-type damage in ageing engineering assets, and most importantly, to break through a bottleneck of GUW-based detection when extended to quantitative evaluation of multitudinous damage disorderedly scattered within a single inspection region. Benefiting from in-depth fundamental interrogation and intensive experiment, this proposed research has reached some very important conclusions and achieved significant findings and outcomes which can benefit relevant students in future. For scientific research, the research outcomes arising from this GRF project will break through some technical bottlenecks of GUW-based approaches when attempting to evaluate multifarious damage within a single inspection area; for real-world engineering, the developed framework will be conducive to enhancing safety, driving down exorbitant maintenance costs, and extending residual service life of ageing assets. A number of high-level publications have been arising from this research project, including 30 papers in top-tier SCI journals, along with another 6 papers in the international conference proceedings (see Part C).

15212417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15212417.value: All the proposed objectives have been well achieved, and in the meantime the team has also identified some potential directions along which deeper and broader research could be expanded. All work has been done in the laboratory, with mock-up structures. The team is now proactively coordinating with industrial partners, to seek opportunity to validate this technique in real engineering world.

15212517.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15212517.value: 集现场监测和高级计算于一体的桥梁温度作用实时研究

15212517.label: Project Objectives
15212517.value: To establish a real-time platform that integrates 3D modeling, global heat transfer analysis, structural analysis, and structural field monitoring; To obtain the global temperature distribution of bridges by combining the numerical heat transfer analysis and field monitoring via the Kalman filtering technique; To investigate the temperature-induced responses of bridges from the structural analysis.
rows: To establish a real-time platform that integrates 3D modeling, global heat transfer analysis, structural analysis, and structural field monitoring;
To obtain the global temperature distribution of bridges by combining the numerical heat transfer analysis and field monitoring via the Kalman filtering technique;
To investigate the temperature-induced responses of bridges from the structural analysis.

15212517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15212517.value: 温度是桥梁的一种主要荷载，比如香港青马大桥的长期监测系统发现该桥跨中最大年竖向位移可达2.2米。与此同时，桥梁也承受较大的风荷载和交通荷载。如何将温度荷载与其它荷载分离是当前一个主要的研究课题和难题。尽管桥梁的温度作用已经研究了几十年，一般方法是将桥梁的各个构件（比如桥塔、桥面）分开处理，每个构件单独简化为一个二维或三维有限元模型，分别进行热传导计算。各构件得到的温度场综合起来输入到结构的整体三维有限元模型中，从而计算桥梁结构在温度荷载作用下的响应。 上述“分而治之”的策略有两个主要缺陷：1）该过程需要大量的人工干预，计算效率低；因此只能分析几个时间点的温度作用，而不是连续的实时的分析。2）桥梁各个构件的温度可能不是均匀分布的，采用局部的二维或三维有限元模型不能准确地描述整座桥梁的温度分布，造成计算结果不够准确。 为了解决上述问题，本项目将以一个实际的人行桥为例，通过现场监测和先进的数值计算方法高效地、准确地、实时地研究桥梁的温度作用。该桥梁位于香港理工大学校园内，目前正在施工并装有健康监测系统。本项目将以该桥梁为一个试验平台，开展如下方面的研究： 1. 在建筑信息模型（BIM）的基础上建立一个一体化的平台，将三维模型、结构整体热传导分析、结构分析和结构监测有机结合起来。 2. 基于BIM建立详细的结构三维整体有限元模型，该模型包括桥梁结构所有构件及其详细的几何信息，使得结构热传导分析和结构力学分析使用相同的网格划分。 3. 在任意时刻对桥梁整体结构进行三维热传导分析，得到桥梁的温度分布。根据现场实时监测的温度结果，用卡尔曼滤波方法，得到更为准确的桥梁温度分布。 4. 将得到的温度分布自动输入到桥梁的同一个整体有限元模型中进行结构力学分析，计算结构在温度荷载作用下的位移和应变。 上述步骤可以实时连续地完成，从而实时监测桥梁的温度作用。本项目的完成将更好地了解桥梁的温度作用，准确地将温度荷载与其它荷载分离，从而对评估结构在不同荷载作用下的性能。

15212517.label: Realisation of objectives
15212517.value: 1) The present project uses a footbridge at the Hong Kong Polytechnic University campus as the test bed. A real-time construction monitoring system was designed and implemented by the PI. This system consists of 61 sensors of ten types. They monitor three categories of parameters: loadings (wind, pedestrian, and temperature), bridge responses (displacement, strain or stress, and acceleration), and environmental factors (air temperature, humidity, rain, and solar radiation). A global finite element model has been established, in which a virtual sun was generated and the angles between the sun and surface of each structural element were calculated. This enables the heat radiation on each element can be obtained, the heat-transfer analysis of the entire structure to be conducted, and consequently, the 3D temperature distribution of the entire bridge is calculated in real-time efficiently. This is the first such study in the area to obtain the global 3D temperature distribution of a bridge, as previous studies can obtain the 2D temperature distribution or 3D temperature distribution of components only. 2) A multi-rate Kalman filtering technique was developed to estimate the more accurate temperature distribution of bridges by combining the numerical heat transfer analysis results and field monitoring counterparts. The calculated temperature was in very good agreement with the field monitoring results. 3) The strain and displacement of key components of the bridge are also monitored in real-time. On the other hand, the temperature data obtained in the above step are directly input to the same finite element model for structural analysis without any modification of the mesh. The temperature-induced strain and displacement of the bridge are then calculated. The results show that the two sets of data are in a very good agreement, which verifies the accuracy and efficiency of the finite element model and the platform. The global finite element model then provides the strain (and stress) and displacement of the entire bridge. The monitored and calculated stresses and displacement of the structural components have provided the actual safety status of the bridge during the operational stage. The integration of field monitoring and advanced computational techniques leads to a better understanding of the temperature behavior of bridges and condition assessment under varying temperature conditions.
