15212517.label: Major findings and research outcome
15212517.value: Under the support of the grant, one software system has been established; three refereed journal papers have been published; one PhD student is educated (he submitted his thesis in April 2022 and may have the oral exam at the end of June or July). The main findings and outcomes of the project include: 1) A health monitoring platform has been established for research and education purposes. A touch screen system with real-time data is shown in the PolyU campus. A web system is also available at http://polyucee.hk/ceyxia/footbridge/index.html (for security reasons, the real-time data is not available online). 2) An efficient global 3D heat-transfer analysis technique for bridges has been developed for the first time worldwide, which enables the temperature distribution of the entire structure and temperature-induced structural responses can be calculated in real-time efficiently. A journal paper has been published in Structural Control and Health Monitoring. The other one is under preparation and will be submitted to Structural Control and Health Monitoring. 3) The uncertainties of bridge variables were studied using the polynomial chaos expansion technique. One paper was published in the top journal Mechanical Systems and Signal Processing. The temperature-induced displacement of expansion joints of bridges was studied and published in Structural Control and Health Monitoring.

15212517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15212517.value: An analytical solution for temperature-induced bridge will be studied. The results will be compared with the field monitoring and numerical simulation results.

15212517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15212517.value: Varying temperature is one of the major loads of bridges. Conventional techniques adopt a 2D or local 3D model only, which cannot calculate the detailed temperature distribution, and thus they cannot capture the accurate temperature actions on bridges. The present project develops a global 3D approach to study the temperature behaviours of bridges by utilizing a footbridge on the PolyU campus as a test bed. Two main outputs have been achieved: 1) An efficient global 3D heat-transfer analysis technique for bridges has been developed for the first time worldwide, which enables the temperature distribution of the entire structure and temperature-induced structural responses can be calculated in real-time efficiently during the operational stage; 2) An interactive software platform has been established to summarize the configuration and function of the SHM system, provide real-time measurement data, present numerical simulation results of the footbridge under pedestrians, temperature, winds, and earthquakes, and introduce fundamental knowledge in bridges, sensors, and surveying. It integrates research, teaching, and public education.

15212617.label: Project Objectives
15212617.value: Develop strongly performing exact algorithms for the single-echelon, two-echelon, stochastic-demand, and multi-commodity models, respectively. 15212617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15212617.value: Business-to-business companies often differentiate the services provided to their business customers (hereinafter referred to as “retailers”) even if they demand the same product. These differentiated services can be viewed as a set of service options, varying in supply lead-times, pricing strategies, after-sales terms, etc. Both the demand of a retailer and the profitability of serving the retailer depend on by which option the retailer is served. Thus, any attempt to maximize profit should take into consideration the decision of service options. This project integrates the service decision with distribution network design so as to maximize the total profit of the entire network. To the best of our knowledge, it is among the first endeavors to design a supply chain network providing customized services, especially in the two-echelon and/or stochastic-demand settings. More specifically, we jointly optimize the location of distribution centers (DCs), the allocation of retailers to DCs, the inventory decision of the network, and the selection of a service option for each served retailer. Our first two models, i.e., the single- and two-echelon models, focus on retailers facing deterministic demands of a single commodity. The single-echelon model only considers the inventory decisions at the DCs, whereas the two-echelon model also takes account of the inventory decisions of the retailers, which models a Vendor Managed Inventory system or a network where the DCs and the retailers belong to the same company. These models are then extended to allow for stochastic demands and multiple commodities. All the proposed models are obviously computationally challenging. To find their optimal solutions efficiently, we plan to employ iterative approaches such as cutting-plane and branch-and-price, each iteration of which requires solving a subproblem. The subproblems of our models turn out to be new combinatorial optimization problems that are of interest by themselves. Some of the subproblems have been shown to be polynomial-time solvable in our preliminary results. In this project, we will further improve the algorithms for these subproblems and develop polynomial-time algorithms for the others. Extensive numerical studies will be conducted to ensure that the practical size instances can be solved to optimality within moderate time. For large-scale problems, we will develop polynomial-time approximation algorithms, ideally with constant-factor worst-case performance guarantees, to obtain close-to-optimal solutions. This project will also use numerical and, if possible, analytical methods to understand the impact of service differentiation on the optimal network profit and configuration. 从事企业对企业（B2B）业务的公司往往对需求相同产品的不同企业客户（以下简称“零售商”）提供差异化的服务。这些差异化服务可以被看作是一系列在交货时间，定价策略，售后条款等方面有所区别的服务选项。零售商的需求以及服务该零售商的获利情况均取决于用来服务该零售商的选项。因此，我们必须优化对零售商采用的服务选项以增加盈利。 本项目将服务决策与分销网络设计相结合，从而最大化网络总利润。据我们所知，这是对提供定制服务的供应链网络设计，尤其是在二梯队和/或随机需求环境中，的首创性研究之一。具体来说，我们同时优化了分销中心的选址，零售商到分销中心的分配，网络库存决策，以及对所服务的各零售商采用的服务选项。我们的前两个模型，即单梯队和二梯队模型，主要考虑零售商对单一商品的确定性需求。单梯队模型侧重于分销中心的库存决策。二梯队模型在此基础上兼顾了零售商的库存决策。该模型适用于供货商管理库存（VMI）系统或分销中心和零售商同属一家公司的供应链网络。我们还对单梯队和二梯队模型进行拓展从而考虑随机需求和多种商品的情况。 上述所有模型在数值求解方面都具有相当的挑战性。为了有效地找到最优解，我们计划采用如切平面或分支定价等迭代算法。此类算法的难点在于解决每次迭代中必须求解的子问题。这些子问题本身也是有潜在应用价值的组合优化新问题。我们的初步结果已证明一些子问题是多项式时间可解。本项目将进一步改进这些子问题的算法，并针对其它子问题开发多项式时间算法。我们将通过大量的数值研究以确保实际规模的算例可以在适度的时间内解决。对于大规模问题，我们将开发多项式时间的近似算法以获得接近最优的解决方案，并预计能求得算法在最差情况下的常数比性能保证。本项目还将通过数值方法并尽可能地应用解析方法来研究服务差异化对网络最大利润和最优配置的影响。

15212617.label: Realisation of objectives
15212617.value: The project objectives have been fully achieved. The details are provided as follows: 1. Exact algorithm. This project studies distribution network design with service differentiation. In particular, we consider four types of models. (i) The single-echelon model considers the case that the retailers demand a single commodity at constant rates. For each retailer, the demand rate, the unit selling price, and the unit cost to serve the retailer can all depend on the service option used to serve this retailer, which can be interpreted as, e.g., how long it takes to fulfill an order, whether a high or low pricing strategy is adopted, and which product warranty and after-sales maintenance policy is offered. An integer program with a nonlinear objective function is formulated to maximize the network-wide profit by jointly determining the location of distribution centers (DCs), the assignment of retailers to DCs, the inventory decision of the DCs, and the service option used to serve each retailer. (ii) The two-echelon model also considers the single-commodity setting with constant demand rate. However, each open DC is responsible for the inventory replenishment of not only itself but also its assigned retailers so that the demands at the retailers can be satisfied without shortage. Therefore, we need to incorporate in our objective function a two-echelon inventory related cost for each open DC. (iii) The stochastic-demand models allow the service-dependent demand at each retailer to be stochastic. In this case, each open DC needs to hold a sufficient amount of safety stocks, which is determined by the set of retailers it serves and which service option is used to serve each retailer, so as to meet a target service level. We generalize both the single- and two-echelon models to this stochastic setting by introducing a term representing the safety stock holding cost for each DC. (iv) We also consider the multi-commodity counterparts of the single- and two-echelon models. In this case, each retailer may demand multiple commodities and the demand, price, and unit cost for each commodity can all depend on the service option. All our models inherit the NP-hardness of the facility location problem. To tackle the computational challenges, we first study the structural properties of the objective functions of the proposed models. For the single- and two-echelon models, we show that the profit function for a DC to serve a set of retailers, which corresponds to the nonlinear terms in the objective function, is supermodular in the set of retailers. For the stochastic-demand and multi-commodity models, although the profit function may not be supermodular, we can decompose this function into a small number of components that are supermodular in certain binary decision variables. These observations motivate us to study a general minimization problem whose objective function contains components submodular in binary decision variables. We show that the submodular components in the objective function can be linearized by adding an exponential number of linear constraints, which are referred to as polymatroid inequalities in the literature. This leads to a cutting plane approach to solve the original minimization problem, which is referred to as the polymatroid cutting plane approach. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first time that the polymatroid cutting plane approach is proved to be an exact algorithm. We further show that the separation problems in each iteration of the polymatroid cutting plane approach can be solved by evaluating the submodular components in the original objective function for a polynomial number of times. This result suggests that the proposed models can be solved by the polymatroid cutting plane approach as long as we can efficiently evaluate the supermodular components in their objective functions. We then develop polynomial-time evaluation algorithms for these components based on their specific structural properties. As a result, we can use the polymatroid cutting plane approach to solve all the proposed models and the separation problems in each cutting plane iteration can be solved in a polynomial time. Extensive numerical studies have been conducted to validate that practical scale instances of the proposed models can be solve by the proposed algorithms within moderate computational time. 2. Approximation algorithm. We have developed greedy algorithms for all the proposed models. In each of the greedy algorithms, the retailers are added to the network iteratively. In every iteration, among all possible (i,S) pairs, where i represents a (potential) DC and S is a subset of retailers that have yet to be assigned to any DC, we choose the pair (i*,S*) with the highest marginal profit. The retailers in S* are then assigned to DC i*. The algorithm terminates when the marginal profit is zero. The key of the greedy algorithms is to identify the pair (i*,S*) with the highest marginal profit. For the single- and two-echelon models, we show that this can be done in a polynomial time and hence the corresponding greedy algorithms are also polynomial-time. For the stochastic-demand and multiple-commodity models, a line search is required to find the optimal pair. Nevertheless, we have validated numerically that the greedy algorithms can solve large scale instances efficiently. We have also conducted extensive numerical experiments to validate the effectiveness of the greedy algorithms. For small and moderate scale instances, the solutions returned by the greedy algorithms are compared with the optimal solutions. The numerical results suggest that the greedy algorithms are close to optimal. For large scale instances where the cutting plane approach cannot return an optimal solution in a reasonable amount of time, the benchmark is set to the optimal solution of the corresponding network design model where the service option for a DC to serve a retailer is fixed to the one maximizing the difference between the expected revenue and the expected linear cost. The greedy algorithms are capable of providing solutions with substantially higher profits than the benchmark. 3. Benefit of service differentiation and its impact on network configuration. For each of the proposed models, we have generated different instances by varying the number of service options for each DC to serve a retailer. For each instance, two network design models are solved to optimality. One is the proposed model with service differentiation. The other is a counterpart with a fixed service option for each pair of DC and retailer. In particular, the service option for a DC to serve a retailer is set to the one maximizing the difference between the expected revenue and the expected linear cost. Through comparing the solutions of these two models, we have gained insights on the benefit of service differentiation and its impact on network configuration. In particular, it is revealed that significant profit improvement can be achieved by the integrated decision of service options and network design.

15212617.label: Major findings and research outcome
15212617.value: This project has led to 2 papers published in INFORMS Journal on Computing (Li et al., 2020 and Ni et al., 2021), 1 PhD thesis (Li, 2020), 4 presentations in international conferences, and 3 seminar talks at Nanyang Technological University, Southeast University, and Beijing Institute of Technology, respectively. Furthermore, we are preparing the following working paper, which will be soon submitted for peer review at INFORMS Journal on Computing: Li, N., Shu, J., Song, M., and Zhai, Y. 2021. Location-Inventory Network Design Optimization with Service Differentiation. Working paper. The Hong Kong Polytechnic University. The major findings of this project are summarized as follows (see Li, 2020 and Li et al., 2021). - For the single- and two-echelon models, the profit function for a DC to serve a set of retailers is supermodular in the set of retailers and can be evaluated in a polynomial time. For the stochastic-demand and multi-commodity models, although the profit function for a DC to serve a set of retailers is not supermodular in general, we identify supermodular components in the objective function, which can also be evaluated in a polynomial time. - To develop exact algorithms for the proposed models, we study a general minimization problem whose objective function contains components submodular in binary decision variables. We prove that the submodular components in the objective function can be linearized by adding an exponential number of linear polymatroid inequalities. Based on this result, a cutting plane approach is developed to find the optimal solution for each of the proposed models. The separation problem in each iteration of the cutting plane algorithm can be solved in a polynomial time. Through extensive numerical experiences, we show that the proposed cutting plane algorithm is capable of solving practical scale instances within moderate computational time. Furthermore, it is also demonstrated that considering service differentiation could significantly improve the profit of the entire network. - A greedy algorithm is proposed to find heuristic solutions for each of the proposed models. For the single- and two-echelon models, the greedy algorithms are shown to be polynomial-time. Through numerical comparison with the exact algorithm and the counterpart without considering service decisions, we demonstrate that the greedy algorithms can obtain close-to-optimal solutions. For the stochastic-demand and multi-commodity models, the efficiency and effectiveness of the greedy algorithms are both validated through extensive numerical studies.

15212617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15212617.value: As in the literature of location-inventory models without service differentiation, the models proposed in this project can be extended in various ways to capture more practical considerations. For example, we can consider capacity restrictions at DCs, routing costs from DCs to retailers, more general non-convex non-concave facility costs incurred at DCs, and supply chain networks with more than two echelons. Furthermore, the project focuses on a company serving its business customers. This particular company is assumed to take a lead in deciding the differentiated services offered to the customers. This setting is rather common in the business-to-business environment, especially for those dominant equipment manufacturers. However, in the business-to-customer environment, a company usually offers a set of service options to its customers, e.g., one- and two-year warranties. Each individual customer then decides which option to choose. The aggregated demand of the DC is determined by how customers respond to the set of service options offered by the DC. This observation can lead to an interesting extension of our model, which would further enrich the supply chain network design literature by adding a new dimension, i.e., customer choices, to the existing models.

15212617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15212617.value: Business-to-business companies often differentiate the services provided to their business customers (hereinafter referred to as “retailers”) even if they demand the same product. These differentiated services can be viewed as a set of service options, varying in supply lead-times, pricing strategies, after-sales terms, etc., which have a considerable impact on both the demand of a retailer and the profitability of serving the retailer. This project integrates the service decision with distribution network design so as to maximize the total profit of the entire network. More specifically, we jointly optimize the location of distribution centers (DCs), the allocation of retailers to DCs, the inventory decision of the network, and the selection of a service option for each served retailer. In particular, we propose the single- and two-echelon models in the single-commodity deterministic-demand setting, and then extend these models to allow for stochastic demands and multiple commodities. All the proposed models are computationally challenging. We develop exact algorithms to solve practical size instances within moderate time. For large-scale instances, efficient approximation algorithms are developed to obtain close-to-optimal solutions. Extensive numerical studies demonstrate that the integrated decision of service differentiation and network design can significantly improve the network profit.

15212717.label: Realisation of objectives
15212717.value: In relation to Objective 1, we have successfully developed a planar polarization rotator using a nematic liquid crystal waveguide, which is subject to a gradient electric field in parallel to the waveguide substrate plane. The fabricated polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) device has demonstrated the electrically controlled polarization rotation at a switching time of 70 ms and a propagation loss of 9 dB/cm at 532 nm. The unique features such as planar form, electric control, and soft material allow the integration into planar lightwave circuits and flexible photonics. In relation to Objective 2, we have proposed a compact planar optofluidic optical switch based on electro-optic (EO) waveguides in nematic liquid crystal (NLC). Each device consists of two portions: the NLC EO waveguides for 1 × 2 switching and the fixed NLC-core waveguides to support subsequent beam paths of the lead-in/lead-out process or the bending process. With numerical simulations, a sample design of 8 × 8 OXC is analyzed and optimized, which provides the predicted broadband performance as approximately 8.0 dB maximum on-chip insertion loss, –45.9 dB cross-talk and 16 ms switching time in the footprint of 2 mm × 2 mm. The loss reduction and the switching speed-up issues are also discussed, with the expected 5.5 dB maximum on-chip insertion loss and 1 ms switching time. The proposed OXC switch is new in the working principle using both electric-field reconfigurable NLC waveguides and fixed NLC core waveguides, and can leverage the liquid-crystal on silicon fabrication. In relation to Objective 3, we have presented the device design and performance analysis of a novel design of planar optical cross-connect (OXC) using nematic liquid crystal (NLC) waveguides. It employs N × N switching matrix in cross-bar fabric. In each unit cell, the input light is set in either the transverse electric (TE) mode or the transverse magnetic (TM) mode by electrically reorienting the NLC in the waveguide. The light then enters a passive waveguide and is routed to different paths depending on the polarization state (TE/TM mode). A sample device of 8 × 8 OXC is analyzed for performance estimation, which predicts a maximum on-chip insertion loss of 3 dB, an average cross-talk of −40 dB, ~1 ms switching time, and 2 mm × 2 mm footprint. The proposed OXC is unique in the switching mechanism of polarization dependent routing and allows non-blocking switching with high compactness and broad bandwidth, making it highly potential for optical circuit switching in data centers and optical communication networks.

A sample design of 8 × 8 OXC provides the predicted broadband performance as ~8.0 dB maximum on-chip insertion loss, –45.9 dB cross-talk and 16 ms switching time in the footprint of 2 mm × 2 mm. The proposed OXC switch is new in the working principle using both electric-field reconfigurable NLC waveguides and fixed NLCcore waveguides, and can leverage the liquid-crystal on silicon fabrication. The results were published in a journal paper in IEEE Photonics Journal in 2018. (3) We have presented the device design and performance analysis of a novel design of planar optical cross-connect (OXC) using nematic liquid crystal (NLC) waveguides. It employs N × N switching matrix in cross-bar fabric. A sample device of 8 × 8 OXC predicts a maximum on-chip insertion loss of 3 dB, an average cross-talk of −40 dB, ~1 ms switching time, and 2 mm × 2 mm footprint. The proposed OXC is unique in the switching mechanism of polarization dependent routing and allows non-blocking switching with high compactness and broad bandwidth. The results were published in another journal paper in Optics Express in 2018, and also produced a China Invention Patents (CN107688250B) on 03 July 2020. (4) We have reported an electrically reconfigurable optofluidic lens with two air–liquid (silicone oil) interfaces actuated by dielectrophoretic (DEP) force. The focal length can be tuned from −0.5 mm to infinite to +0.5 mm. In the experiment, the lens achieves an ƒ number of 0.91 while consuming only 6.7 nJ per circle. Its wide tunability, low power consumption and easy operation make it suitable for light manipulation in microfluidic networks. The results were published in a journal paper in Lab on a Chip in 2018. (5) We have presented an electrically generated optical waveguide formed in a z-cut single-crystal lithium-niobate (LN) thin film by the electro-optic effect. When a voltage applied to patterned electrodes, the extraordinary refractive index (RI) of the LN film is increased to act as the waveguide core. Such a waveguide can be made to exist or disappear by turning on or off the applied voltage. A straight waveguide and an S-bend waveguide with an RI contrast of ∼0.004 are generated at a voltage of 200 V. It can be used to form ultrafast (switching time ~ 1 ns) reconfigurable OXCs. The results were published in a journal paper in Optics Express in 2020. Research outputs (1) Published 5 journal articles and 4 conference papers (including 2 invited talks and 1 keynote talk). (2) Filed 3 patents. (3) Obtained 1 international technical award from IOO International Society. 15212717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15212717.value: Further studies will be conducted to design and fabricate large-port number OXC using lithium niobate on insulator (LNOI) substrate. It is expected to improve the switching speed to the scale of 1 ns and allows to integrate with other passive & active photonic components on a single chip. In addition, wafer bonding of photonic components of different materials (e.g., LNOI, MgF2, SiO2, Si, InP, etc.) will be investigated for heterogeneous integration of multiple photonic components into an on-chip system.

15212717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15212717.value: Telecommunication networks and data centers are facing an explosively increasing data traffic due to the rapid growth of smart phone apps and online services, but their switching and routing still rely on the optical-electronic-optical (OEO) conversion and becomes the bottleneck of overall bandwidth. Optical crossconnect (OXC) eliminates the OEC conversion by directly connects multiple optical inputs and multiple optical outputs, but the developed OXCs have limits in various aspects. This project has presented 3 designs of non-blocking planar OXCs based on a new polarization switching method using nematic liquid crystal (NLC) waveguides. It produced 4 journal papers, 3 China patents and 1 technical award. The project results facilitates low-cost, low-power, durable, compact, non-blocking, scalable OXC systems for next-generation telecommunication systems and data centers.

15212817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15212817.value: Linear and continuous piecewise linear vector optimization have been extensively studied and applied to various decision-making problems in economics, management science and engineering. The construction theory of solution sets of vector optimization problem in the case of finite dimension spaces with the polyhedron ordering cone has played a key role in the development of its theory and applications. It is well recognized that continuous piecewise linearity is still very restrictive in both theory and application. Practical problems of piecewise linear functions include transaction costs in finance and sparse nature of the decision variables in statistics and compress sensing. Here by a piecewise linear function we mean a not necessarily continuous one. It is worth noting that the study of piecewise linear, in particular vector, optimization problems is very limited and immature. Therefore there is a need to establish a unified and in-depth theory for piecewise linear vector optimization problems. In this project, we will study the fully piecewise linear vector optimization problem, that is, both objective and constraint functions can be piecewise linear. We will first explore the solution structures of the piecewise linear vector optimization problem in general Banach spaces and apply them to develop weak sharp minima for linear vector optimization problems and to explore the corresponding finite terminate rule for some piecewise linear vector optimization algorithms. On the other hand, in establishing mathematical models of practical problems, one often adopts piecewise linear functions as objectives and constraint functions, and these piecewise linear functions are determined by only finitely many available test data. However all test data obtained are not perfectly ideal. In general, the gap between the ideal data with the ``test" data is unavoidable. In view of this, we will consider some stability issues when the objective and/or constraint functions undergo small perturbations.

15213117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15213117.value: This research project aims to study the impact of variance and probability of the predicted flight arrival delay on the reliability of Crew Pairing (CP) in short-haul flight networks. CP defines the itinerary, which is constructed by a set of duties/flights with sit-time and rest period governed by the aviation regulations. In reality, flight delay causes not only inconvenience to passengers, but also economic loss to airlines (~US$25 billion in 2014). Accordingly, many researchers are working on reducing the impact of flight delay by adding a buffer time for absorption. Consequently, predicting flight delay for buffer time becomes the key issue. Nowadays, although forecasting with big data creates more accurate predictions, it is rare that flight delay can be predicted precisely without deviation because uncertainties are inevitable. However, many studies use only the expected value of flight delay in the CP calculation without considering the effect of its variance on the reliability of the CP formed. However, expected value alone cannot reflect the variance of the prediction error. Because of the CP problem characteristics, an earlier flight arrival does not mean it creates more buffer time to the following flights as every flight has scheduled departure time. However, if a flight arrives later than expected, the CP may become infeasible because of the potential overtime working. It is strictly prohibited according to aviation regulations. This problem has not been studied in the existing literature. This impact is more severe in short-haul flights because the number of flights served by a crew per day/week is relatively higher. Accordingly, this research project aims to demonstrate the significance of considering the variance and probability of the predicted flight arrival delay in short-haul CP and propose a new optimization methodology for it. The research questions encountered are i) the estimation of the variance and probability of flight delay extending from the existing prediction methods, and ii) the huge problem complexity of short-haul flight networks. Accordingly, an estimation approach, a new model of column generation, and a new solution approach have to be developed. With the variance and probability of flight arrival delay obtained, the robustness of CP can be truly maximized. Nevertheless, airlines can calculate which flight connection and itinerary may have a higher risk with probability values indicated. Moreover, airlines can assign reserve crews as needed rather than purely by experience. Therefore, this project provides significant benefits to airlines, passengers, and crews. 本研究項目旨在針對在短途航班網絡，所預測航班到達延誤的變異及可能性對於‘空勤組員組合’可靠性的影響進行課題研究。‘空勤組員組合’明確定義了由一整套在航空法規框架內所規定時間及休息週期的值勤/航班所構成的航空行程。事實上，航班延誤不僅對旅客造成不便，而且會給航空公司帶來經濟損失（在2014年相關經濟損失高達250億美金）。鑑於此，許多研究學者都在致力於研究通過增加緩衝時間加以吸納以降低航班延誤造成的影響。因此，對需要增加緩衝時間的航班延誤預測成為非常關鍵的問題。目前，儘管通過大數據能創造更精準的預測預報，但由於不可避免的不確定性，對於航班延誤完全無誤差的精確預測非常稀缺。然而，在‘空勤組員組合’的計算中，許多研究只運用了航班延誤的期望值，並未考慮對其差異對所構成‘空勤組員組合’的可靠性造成的影響。而且，期望值本身無法反映預測失誤的差異。由於‘空勤組員組合’問題的特性，提前抵達的航班並不意味著它能為後續航班提供緩衝時間，因為每一個航班都有其計劃好的起飛時間。但是如果一個航班的抵達晚於計劃時間，那麼由其造成的潛在加班工作則可能導致其‘空勤組員組合’無法繼續工作。相關情況在航空法規中明令禁止。這個問題在已有的文獻中並未被充分研究。這種現像對於短途航班影響更甚，因為在短途航班中，空勤組員每天/週所承擔的服務工作量相對更高。鑑於此，本研究項目旨在闡釋在短途航班的‘空勤組員組合’中考慮所預測航班到達延誤的變異及可能性的重要意義，並為此專門構建新的優化研究方法論。所承載的研究問題包括：1. 基於現有預測方法所延伸的對於航班延誤差異和可能性的估算。 2. 短途航班網絡其問題巨大的複雜性。因此，新的估算方法、新的列生成算法模型以及新解決方案的生成途徑都需要被研發。如果能得出航班到達延誤的變異及可能性，‘空勤組員組合’的穩健性將會被實際最大化。然而，航空公司可以計算得出所預示具有更高風險可能值的航班對接和航空行程。此外，航空公司可以指派實際所需的後備空勤組員，而不僅是單憑經驗。因此，此項目能為航空公司、旅客和空勤組員帶來意義重大的收益。

15213717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15213717.value: Nowadays, using personal information to gain access to remote services has become a daily activities in Hong Kong. Recent security leaks have raised the concern that our personal information is vulnerable to identity theft. The major issue is that most of these services still rely on user names and passwords for authentication. As personal information can be easily compromised through social engineering attacks, these traditional approaches are insufficient to safeguard the security of remote services. The recent advances in machine learning has made voice biometrics commercially viable. With voice biometrics, a criminal trying to impersonate a legitimate user can be identified while he/she is speaking to the system. To incorporate voice biometrics into remote services, it is important to ensure that recognition accuracy can still be maintained even if the users are speaking in an adverse environment that the system has not encountered during training. Adverseness can be caused by background noise, reverberation, bad microphones, and poor communication channels. The prevalent utterance representation (i-vectors) and scoring method (PLDA) rely on linear models to summarize the spectral characteristics of speech and to marginalize out any nuisance variability not related to speaker recognition. Our previous studies have suggested that when there is a severe mismatch between the training and test conditions or when the nuisance variability is too severe, a linear model may not be sufficient. We advocate that the relationship between the latent variables and the observed variables may not be linear. To relax this linearity assumption, we propose incorporating speaker labels into the learning algorithm of variational autoencoders (VAE), which effectively combines variational Bayesian learning and deep learning to model any complex relationships between the observed vectors and latent variables. To adapt the VAE to a new environment, we propose a new semi-supervised learning algorithm in which some of the hidden nodes in the VAE are used as stochastic indicator variables to guide the adaptation. We also question on the suitability of the linearity assumption of the i-vector representation and introduce a variational utterance representation that can model more complex distributions of acoustic features. The proposed VAE will be evaluated on the latest NIST SRE dataset. The proposed work is the first to leverage semi-supervised deep learning, Bayesian learning and their combinations for speaker verification. It will also push speaker modeling, score computation, and utterance representations in speaker verification beyond the prevalent linear models. 最近幾年，用個人信息來獲取遠程服務已經在香港相當普及。然而最近的安全漏洞事件引起了我們對個人信息安全的擔憂。主要的問題在於這些服務已然依賴於用戶名的密碼進行驗證。由於個人信息易於被策劃攻擊，這些傳統的方法不足以來保障遠程服務的安全。機器學習最近的進展讓語音生物識別已可在商業層面上運用。通過語音生物識別技術，在通話過程中遠程系統可以識別出企圖冒充真正用戶的犯罪份子。 要將語音生物技術結合到遠程服務中，非常重要的壹點是保證識別的精度，即便用戶是在訓練中沒有遇到的不利的環境中。不利環境可能是由於背景噪音，混響，質量差的麥克風和不良信道。如今先進普遍的語音表示（i向量）和評分法（PLDA）都依賴於線性模型來總結語音的頻譜特征，並且邊際化於說話人身份無關的滋擾變化。我們之前的研究成果表明，當訓練與測試條件之間存在嚴重不匹配時，線性模型可能不合適。我們認為隱形變量和觀測變量之間的關系可能不是線性的。為了放寬線性的假設，我們提出將說話人身份信息納入到變分自動編碼器（variational auto-encoder）的學習算法中，該算法高效得結合了變分貝葉斯學習和深度學習來模擬隱形變量和觀測變量之間的復雜關系。 為了讓VAE適用於新的環境，我們提出壹個新的半監督學習算法，在這個算法中部分隱形節點被用來作為隨機指標變量來指導適應。我們還對i向量的線形假設提出了質疑，並引入了更符合復雜的聲學特征的變分（variational）語句表示。 我們所提出的VAE將在最新的NIST SRE數據集上進行評估。該工作是第壹個試圖結合半監督深度學習，貝葉斯學習來進行說話人識別。其能推動說話人模擬，分數計算和語句表示在人聲識別到先所流行的線形模型之上。

15213717.label: Realisation of objectives
15213717.value: 100% of Objective 1 has been achieved. We have proposed an information-maximized variational domain adversarial neural network (InfoVDANN) that incorporates an InfoVAE into domain adversarial training (DAT) to reduce domain mismatch and simultaneously meet the Gaussianity requirement of the PLDA backend. Specifically, DAT is applied to produce speaker discriminative and domain-invariant features, while the InfoVAE performs variational regularization on the embedded features so that they follow a Gaussian distribution. Another benefit of the InfoVAE is that it avoids posterior collapse in VAEs by preserving the mutual information between the embedded features and the training set so that extra speaker information can be retained in the features. The results of Objective 1 have been published in the top journal in our field: IEEE/ACM Transactions on Audio, Speech, and Language Processing. Preliminary results of this journal paper have been published in top conferences in speech, such as ICASSP and Interspeech. 100% of Objective 2 has been achieved. Most pooling methods in state-of-the-art speaker embedding networks are implemented in the temporal domain. However, due to the high non-stationarity in the feature maps produced from the last frame-level layer, it is not advantageous to use the global statistics (e.g., means and standard deviations) of the temporal feature maps as aggregated embeddings. This motivates us to explore stationary spectral representations and perform aggregation in the spectral domain. Specifically, we have proposed attentive short-time spectral pooling (attentive STSP) from a Fourier perspective to exploit the local stationarity of the feature maps. In the attentive STSP, for each utterance, we compute the spectral representations through a weighted average of the windowed segments within each spectrogram by attention weights and aggregate their lowest spectral components to form the speaker embedding. Because most of the feature map energy is concentrated in the low-frequency region of the spectral domain, attentive STSP facilitates the information aggregation by retaining the low spectral components only. The results of Objective 2 have been published in the top journal in our field: IEEE/ACM Transactions on Audio, Speech, and Language Processing. Preliminary results of this journal paper have been published in top conferences in speech, such as ICASSP and Interspeech. We have also successfully trained a Ph.D. student in this project. The student has graduated in Feb. 2022 with two journal papers and 4 conference papers.

15213717.label: Major findings and research outcome
15213717.value: Deploying speaker verification systems to adverse acoustic environments faces a number of challenges. First, today’s SV systems rely on the condition that the training and test data share the same distribution. Once this condition is violated, domain mismatch will occur. The problem will be exacerbated when the speaker embeddings violate the Gaussianity constraint. Second, because the temporal feature maps produced by the last frame-level layer are highly non-stationary, it is not desirable to use their global statistics as speaker embeddings. Third, current speaker embedding networks do not have any mechanisms to let the frame-level information flow directly into the embeddings layer, causing information loss in the pooling layer. This project has developed three strategies to address the above challenges. First, to jointly address domain mismatch and the Gaussianity requirement of probabilistic linear discriminant analysis (PLDA) models, we proposed a variational domain adversarial learning framework with two specialized networks: variational domain adversarial neural network (VDANN) and information-maximized VDANN (InfoVDANN). Both networks leverage domain adversarial training to produce speaker discriminative and domain-invariant embeddings and apply variational autoencoders (VAEs) to perform Gaussian regularization. The InfoVDANN, in particular, avoids posterior collapse in VDANNs by preserving the mutual information (MI) between the domain-invariant embeddings and the speaker embeddings. Second, to mitigate the effect of non-stationarity in the temporal feature maps, we proposed short-time spectral pooling (STSP) and attentive STSP to transform the temporal feature maps into the spectral domain through short-time Fourier transform (STFT). The zero- and low-frequency components are retained to preserve speaker information. A segment-level attention mechanism is designed to produce spectral representations with fewer variations, which results in better robustness to the non-stationary effect in the feature maps. Third, to allow information in the frame-level layers to flow directly to the speaker embedding layer, MI-enhanced training based on a semi-supervised deep InfoMax (DIM) framework is proposed. Because the dimensionality of the frame-level features is much larger than that of the speaker embeddings, we proposed to squeeze the frame-level features via global pooling before MI estimation. The proposed method, called squeeze-DIM, effectively balances the dimension between the frame-level features and the speaker embeddings. We found that the VDANN and InfoVDANN outperform the DANN baseline, indicating the effectiveness of Gaussian regularization and MI maximization. We also found that applying segment-level attention and leveraging low spectral components of temporal feature maps can produce discriminative speaker embeddings. Finally, we demonstrated that the squeeze operation facilitates MI maximization.

15213717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15213717.value: Our VAE assumes that the prior distribution follows a standard Gaussian. One limitation of this assumption is that posterior collapse may occur while training the VAE. Another adverse effect is that the latent variables can only capture single modal information if their prior is a normal distribution. A possible improvement is to apply a Gaussian mixture model to increase the encoding capacity of the latent features and make the domain transfer more continuous for complicated adaptation. We found that performing aggregation in the spectral domain is more robust against the non-stationarity in the convolutional feature maps than applying temporal aggregation. Nevertheless, STFT is a simple time-frequency transform that cannot achieve good temporal and spectral resolutions simultaneously. Therefore, we may try advanced time-frequency analysis tools such as wavelet analysis to transform the temporal feature maps to the spectral domain, so that better time-frequency details can be captured during utterance-level aggregation. We may extend the MI-enhanced training by performing dense squeeze-DIM regularizations on the speaker embeddings. Rather than maximizing the MI between the feature maps from a single convolutional layer and the speaker embeddings, we may simultaneously feed the frame-level information from multiple convolutional layers to the embeddings.

15214417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15214417.value: To promote environmental protection and achieving sustainable development, it is highly desirable to recycle construction and demolition waste (C&D) and to reduce GHG emissions through sustainable strategies. However, direct reusing of recycled aggregates from C&D waste has shortcomings because of the inferior properties of recycled aggregates, largely due to the presence of a porous layer of attached old cement mortar on the recycled aggregates. In order to efficiently facilitate resources recycling, ways to improve the quality of recycled aggregates have attracted much research interest. In recent years, adopting the accelerated carbonation technique to improve the quality of recycled aggregates has been investigated by a number of researchers. Utilizing the carbonation behaviour of recycled cement based waste materials to enhance their properties has an additional benefit to sequestrate CO2 from GHGs. Previous experimental studies indicated that after a period of accelerated carbonation, the physical and mechanical properties of the recycled aggregates were improved. Generally, this is believed to be related to the formation of calcium carbonates from the common hydration products of cement leading to the densification of the porous structure in the old cement mortar of the recycled aggregates. The improved microstructure of the recycled aggregates would also have significant influence on the properties of the new concrete prepared with the carbonated recycled aggregate. This is particular important in the interfacial transition zone between the old mortar of the recycled aggregate and the new mortars in the new concrete. The extent of such improvement would be related to the degree of carbonation of the old hydrated cement products. But contrasting results have been reported on the benefits of using the accelerated carbonation technique. Therefore, it would be of significant research interest to assess the influence of the different degrees of carbonation and the associated change of chemical phases in the recycled aggregates after carbonation on the micro- and macro-mechanical properties of the new concrete. The proposed study will be a joint effort between HK PolyU and EPFL of Switzerland and will comprise a comprehensive laboratory studies, using a range of advanced microstructure techniques to reveal the fundamental mechanisms on how accelerated carbonation affect or improve the micro and macro structural properties of recycled aggregate concrete. Practical guidelines will be also developed to facilitate the use of the accelerated carbonation technique. 隨著環保意識的宣傳和人們環保意識的加強，世界上許多國家高度重視廢棄混凝土作為有用資源的再生利用，並採用環保方式降低混凝土溫室氣體的排放。然而再生混凝土骨料存在一些內在缺陷（孔隙率大、吸水率高等），使得它在再生利用中受到限制。探索有效的、實用的和環保的再生混凝土骨料強化手段，將有助於改善再生混凝土的性能。近幾年，利用加速碳化手段改善再生混凝土骨料性能已經受到關注。再生混凝土骨料的加速碳化可以達到：溫室氣體二氧化碳的捕獲與封存和再生混凝土骨料的強化。由於混凝土含有豐富的鈣質和矽酸鹽，會與CO2 反應，形成的碳酸鈣填充微觀孔隙，使得微觀結構更加緻密。碳化再生骨料製作混凝土的性能得到明顯的改善，特別在微觀界面過渡區。鑒於此，有必要深入研究加速碳化後碳化程度對再生混凝土骨料化學組成的影響，以及对再生骨料和再生混凝土在宏觀和微觀上性能的改善機理，並建立兩者之間的聯繫。此研究合作項目將由香港理工大學和洛桑聯邦理工學院共同執行與完成。並利用兩所大學的水泥基材料先進實驗設備，揭示再生骨料碳化程度對再生混凝土在宏觀和微觀性能上的影響，此項研究將會更有意義地推廣應用加速碳化手段改善再生混凝土的性能。

15214417.label: Major findings and research outcome
15214417.value: Carbonation treatment is a promising option to enhance recycled concrete aggregate (RCA) quality and eventually improve concrete performance. This study investigated the multi-scale mechanical properties of calcium silicate hydrates (C-S-H) in a mature alite paste subjected to accelerated carbonation treatment by testing macro compressive strength, microhardness and nanoindentation. The results show that, carbonation treatment resulted in a heterogeneous distribution of carbonation products in the alite sample. Reinforcement of C-S-H by the randomly precipitated calcite and aragonite crystals prevailed over the nano-structural and compositional alteration of C-S-H induced by carbonation, leading to an increase of nano-indentation modulus at the edge of the sample. Also, the microhardness at the edge zone was markedly higher than that at the core of the carbonated sample. The carbonated peripheral zone with improved nano-scale modulus and microhardness was likely serving as a “hard shell”, contributing to the improved macro compressive strength. The new insights into the multi-scale mechanical properties of carbonated C-S-H contribute to further understanding of the enhanced properties of RCA after carbonation treatment

15214417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15214417.value: It was found that carbonation treatment can also be applied to recycled fine aggregates including waste concrete powder. This is particularly useful for the recycling industry and the recycled fine powder is normally disposed of without any application. Further research will be carried out on this aspect.

15214417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15214417.value: Reusing recycled aggregates in cement and concrete products is an effective option to manage these wastes. However, due to its inferior quality and varying nature, recycled aggregates are still restricted only to non-structural applications. Carbonation reactions are known to be able to densify the matrix of old concrete and also cause rapid hardening of fresh cementitious materials. This study employed a CO2 curing process to enhance the properties of recycled aggregate concrete products. Experimental results showed that properties of recycled concrete aggregate and eco-concrete blocks were enhanced after CO2 curing process; mechanical and durable performance was also improved for the concrete prepared with CO2 -treated recycled aggregate. Furthermore, there is a great potential of CO2 sequestration by recycled aggregate concrete products. The life cycle assessment results indicated that the production of concrete and concrete blocks with recycled materials using CO2 treatment are environmentally sustainable resulting in reduced greenhouse gas emissions and lower non-renewable energy consumption

15214517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15214517.value: Prefabricated concrete sandwich walls (PCSWs), composed of two concrete wythes and a thermal insulation layer in between, have been widely used as a complete building envelope. To achieve sufficient composite action of PCSWs, connectors are often used to connect the two wythes. Traditionally such connectors were made of steel bars/trusses or solid concrete. Due to the thermal bridge effect, recently these have been replaced to a large extent by fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP) composites that have high strength but low thermal conductivity. Clearly, the structural performance of FRP-connected PCSWs depends strongly on the mechanical properties of the two wythes and the performance of the connectors. Extensive studies have been carried out on the capacity of FRP shear connectors which are generally available in solid bar, plate or grid form. In recent studies conducted by our research group, tubular FRP connectors were found to perform better than the corresponding existing systems, particularly in terms of connector stiffness. In addition, a new type of ultra-high performance fiber-reinforced cementitious composite (UHP-FRCC) featuring strain-hardening and multiple-cracking characteristics, has also been developed. In addition to its high compressive strength (> 120MPa), the new UHP-FRCC has a tensile strength and an elongation of 20MPa and 8.7%, respectively, is predicted to have an excellent energy absorption ability. This project will aim to develop a new type of FRP-connected PCSW system for potential use in high-rise buildings in seismic regions. It comprises: (1) two wythes of UHP-FRCC; (2) a tubular glass FRP (GFRP) connector; and (3) a layer of rigid foam for thermal insulation. Besides direct shear tests and out-of-plane bending tests that are frequently conducted to evaluate the capacity of connectors and the degree of composite action of PCSWs, lateral reversed cyclic loading tests will be applied to the proposed PCSW system to achieve a fundamental understanding of their in-plane behavior, which so far has been little understood. The proposed FRP-connected UHP-FRCC sandwich wall system will inherit all of the advantages of existing PCSWs, such as good quality control, fast construction and high energy efficiency, and is also expected to be more durable, lighter, stiffer, strong in shear and thus ductile. It has great potential for use as ductile shear walls for high-rise buildings in seismic regions, which meets an urgent socio-economic need of industrialized and energy efficient buildings in Hong Kong, mainland China and many other parts of the world. 預製混凝土三明治墻（PCSW）由内外墻體以及中間保溫層組成，該結構形式已經被廣汎應用于建築的圍護體系中。為達到内外墻體的組合效應，通常需要有傳力鍵來連接内外墻體。傳統的傳力鍵主要是由鋼筋或者混凝土塊體來承擔。由於熱橋效應的存在，近年來，纖維增强樹脂複合材料（FRP）由於其具有高强及低熱傳導的特性，已被作爲剪力鍵廣汎應用于PCSW的製造中。顯然，PCSW的結構性能取決于内外墻的力學性能以及剪力鍵的性能。 已有研究已經就筋、板、或柵格形式的FRP剪力鍵開展了大量的研究，申請者的研究小組最近發明了一種新型的管狀FRP傳力鍵，並證明了其優異的力學性能（尤其是剛度性能）。此外申請者的研究小組也開發了一種新型的超高性能纖維增强水泥基複合材料（UHP-FRCC），其抗壓强度120MPa以上，而相應的抗拉强度及斷裂應變分別可達20MPa及8.7%，具有出色的延性耗能能力。 本研究項目旨在開發一種新型的基於FRP剪力鍵的PCSW系統（FRP-UFSW），作爲剪力墻在地震區域的高層結構中使用。該系統以上述管狀FRP傳力鍵連接UHP-FRCC内外墻體，墻體之間用剛性發泡材料實現保溫作用。將對管狀FRP傳力鍵的直剪性能、UHP-FRCC三明治板的面外抗彎性能以及面内重複載荷下的抗剪性能進行深入研究。所建議的FRP-UFSW系統將繼承已有PCSW系統更輕質、高强、耐久、延性，並順應香港、中國大陸以及世界其它地區的建築工業化社會經濟需求，有望在工程中得到廣汎應用。

15214517.label: Realisation of objectives
15214517.value: 1. Objective 1 has been realized through a combined experimental and finite element modeling program Three kinds of glass fiber reinforced polymer (GFRP) connector, including a flat plate, a corrugated plate, and a hexagonal tube connector were investigated for potential use in the precast concrete sandwich panel (PCSP). In-plane direct shear tests were conducted to evaluate the performance of the connectors based on a typical push-out configuration (i.e., three concrete wythes linked with connectors and two rigid foam layers in between). Twenty-five specimens were tested, and shear force vs. relative slip relationships and failure modes of all types of connectors were compared and discussed in detail. Meanwhile, finite element (FE) analysis was conducted to reproduce the test results. All three types of GFRP connectors were found to exhibit a progressive failure manner; the corrugated plate connector achieved higher deformability than the flat plate connector, particularly when the GFRP laminate thickness was small; and the hexagonal tube connector exhibited similar behavior along with two orthogonal directions, making them well suited for use as two-way connectors. The developed FE model was able to reasonably predict the peak shear load and stiffness of all types of connectors based on comparisons with the test results. 2. Objective 2 has also been realized through a combined experimental and finite element modeling program. Eight PCSPs were fabricated and evaluated their flexural performance through four points bending test to understand their out-of-plane bending behaviors. The experimental parameters included connector type (plate-type and hexagonal tubular), connector spacing (300 and 525 mm), reinforcement type (basalt FRP reinforcement and steel reinforcement) and reinforcement ratio (0.30% and 0.43%). The load vs. mid-span deflection relationships, crack patterns, failure modes, reinforcement strain development relationships, and degrees of composite action of the panels were investigated in detail. In addition, two-dimensional (2D) finite element (FE) analysis was conducted to reproduce the test results and to facilitate a better understanding of the panel’s performance, particularly the connector’s behavior at different loading stages. It was concluded that a higher degree of composite action in the panels can be achieved through the use of FRP tubular connectors, besides, all the FRP tubular connectors can retain their load transfer capacities at the ultimate limit state owning to their ductile failure behavior. (3) Objective 3 has been realized through a combined experimental study and analytical modeling. Ten PCSPs were prefabricated and subjected to concentric axial loading. The primary test variables included the slenderness ratio of the wall panel (i.e., the effective height to total sectional thickness ratio), longitudinal spacing of connectors, and the ratio of the wythe thickness to the insulation layer thickness of the wall panel. The load-deflection relationships, failure modes, and load-strain relationships were carefully investigated. All the wall panels failed by crushing of concrete. The connectors were subjected to axial force, transverse shear, and bending in order to allow two wythes to deform together. The axial load capacity of the wall panel was reduced by 26% as the slenderness ratio varied from 8 to 17. The spacing of FRP connectors was found to have a marginal impact on the axial load capacity because of the existence of capping beams at the end of panels. An increase in the insulation thickness while keeping the wythe thickness constant resulted in a significant rise in the ultimate axial load in the case of panels having a higher slenderness ratio. A theoretical second-order analysis was performed to predict the ultimate axial load of equivalently assumed solid wall panels, and the predicted results were compared with the experimental ones. In addition, 6 more PSCPS were prefabricated and tested to study the effect of load-eccentricity. It was found that the axial load capacities of the eccentrically loaded PCSPs subject to load eccentricity-to-sectional thickness ratios of 0.15, 0.45, and 0.63 were reduced by 35%, 75%, and 85% (average of the load capacity values for the slender and squat SWPs), respectively, compared to their counterpart concentrically loaded SWPs. A second-order theoretical analysis was also conducted to obtain the axial load-moment interaction curves of equivalently assumed sections, and the outcomes were compared with the experimental ones to validate the modeling.

15214517.label: Major findings and research outcome
15214517.value: The project involves a substantial amount of experimental tests and finite element/analytical modeling work, leading to the following major findings and research outcomes: (1) Ultra-high-performance cementitious composites with both ultra-high tensile/compressive strength and ductility have been successfully developed (refer to Journal papers 2 and 3 in Part 3) (2) A new type of FRP connector was proposed and an in-depth understanding of their shear-load slip behavior has been achieved (refer to Journal paper 1 and "other impact" in Part 3). (3) An thorough understanding of the degree of composite action in the GFRP connector-enabled PCSPs has been achieved through the out-of-plane bending tests and finite element analyses, which have provided a solid foundation for the safety and serviceability design of the PCSPs under the out-of-plane bending load (refer to Journal papers 4 in Part 3). (4) The models for predicting the loading-carry capacity of GFRP connector-enabled PCSPs under concentric and eccentric loadings have been established and validated by experimental results (refer to Journal papers 5 and 6 in Part 3).

15214517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15214517.value: The PI's team will be investigating the structural responses of the GFRP connector-enabled PCSPs subjected to a combined constant axial load and reversed cyclic lateral load. It is expected that a full set of knowledge will be established to facilitate the practical design of the GFRP connector-enabled PCSPs in terms of safety and serviceability. The PI will attempt to reflect the research outcomes into the code of practice development of the composite PCSP system and promote its applications in engineering practice.

15214517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15214517.value: Prefabricated concrete sandwich walls (PCSWs), composed of two concrete wythes and a thermal insulation layer in between, have been widely used as a complete building envelope. To achieve sufficient composite action of PCSWs, connectors are often used to connect the two wythes. Traditionally such connectors were made of steel bars/trusses or solid concrete. Due to the thermal bridge effect, these have recently been replaced largely by fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP) composites with high strength but low thermal conductivity. Clearly, the structural performance of FRP-connected PCSWs depends strongly on the mechanical properties of the two wythes and the performance of the connectors. In this project, an extensive experimental program has been conducted to investigate the shear stress transfer behavior of a newly developed tubular GFRP connector and the structural performance of ultra-high-performance concrete sandwich walls with the tubular GFRP connector under out-of-plane bending, in-plane axial loading, and combined axial-bending loads. The outcomes from the projects will be helpful for promoting the use of the prefabricated PCSWs as ductile and energy-efficient shear walls for high-rise buildings in seismic regions, which meets an urgent socio-economic need in Hong Kong, mainland China and many other parts of the world.

15215117.label: Project Objectives

rows: To develop GNSS receiver algorithms that precisely estimate movements of slopes using GNSS reflected signals;
To carry out experiments to examine the performance of the proposed slope monitoring system

15215117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15215117.value: 本项目提出一种利用GNSS反射信号用与滑坡监测的心方法。本系统利用两个GNSS天线接收从滑坡反射的GNSS信号。应用相关原理，当滑坡发生运动时，两接收天线的载波相位差将发生变化。本项目将开发基于两种不同的相关原理的相关算法，并通过实验进行验证。

15215117.label: Realisation of objectives
15215117.value: The use of Global Navigation Satellite System Reflectometry (GNSS-R) as an opportunity for remote sensing applications has drawn increasing attention in recent years. A variety of applications have been developed and can be generally characterized into two groups: the non-geometrical applications such as sea state monitoring and biomass monitoring, which are usually focusing on the amplitude or the power of the reflected signals; the geometrical applications such as sea level monitoring and snow depth monitoring, which are focusing on the range difference between the direct and reflected signals, and centimeter level accuracy has been achieved through these applications. The idea of using GNSS-R for deformation monitoring is inspired by the remarkable achievement of the GNSS-R geometrical applications. Diversified equipment and technologies are available nowadays to fulfill the deformation monitoring tasks, such as onsite monitoring (i.e., GNSS, leveling, and tilt sensor) and offsite monitoring (i.e., photogrammetry, Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR), microwave radar and Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR)). To realize the application of deformation monitoring using GNSS-R technology, the measurement of sub-centimeter accuracy is desired. Moreover, various deformation situations, such as kinematic and quasi static deformation, require differently to the monitoring methods. Towards this goal, the ranging accuracy of GNSS-R needs to be improved, and different monitoring approaches need to be developed for various deformation cases. If done, this new application possesses the advantages of low labor-consuming and low time-consuming considering the remote working mode. In view of the other methods like II photogrammetry, InSAR, or LiDAR, the benefits of applying the GNSS-R approach rest in lower expense, easy implementation and higher update rate. Aiming at this purpose, this project devotes the investigation on the feasibility of using GNSS-R for deformation monitoring. Three different algorithms, which suit continuous, discontinuous and relative deformation monitoring cases, have been proposed in this project. Sub-centimetre level accuracy has been achieved through various experiments. To maximize the availability of implementing this application, the proposed approaches can be adopted to both software-defined radio (SDR) receiver and commercial GNSS receiver, which will lower the barrier of using GNSS-R technology. The suitability of the GNSS-R technology has been analyzed to evaluate the practicability of the proposed methods in terms of different types of reflecting surfaces, monitoring distances and the deformation period.

15215117.label: Major findings and research outcome
15215117.value: This project developed new algorithms for monitoring slope movements using GNSS signals reflected from the slope surface. Two methods investigated. The first method utilizes a GNSS software receiver, which enables to record the GNSS IF signals. Using GNSS loop tracking method, we are able to estimate the phase differences between the direct and reflected GNSS signals, so that the range differences can be estimated. The second method utilizes one commercial GNSS receiver with two antennas, the direct and reflected GNSS signals are mixed an antenna side. Then the signal-to-noise ratio outputs from the GNSS receiver are used to estimate the time delay. Extended experiments have been carried out and results show both methods can achieve sub-centimetre accuracy for the deformation monitoring of the slope. Also, algorithms for estimate the position of the reflected points are developed.

15215117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15215117.value: This project has demonstrated that GNSS reflected signals can be used for slope deformation monitoring first time in the world. The further research should be concentrated on 1) testing the performance in different environments ; 2) developing reliable products for engineering application, particularly in the locations where is different to install monitoring systems on the slopes; 3) improving the computation efficiency to make it a real-time processing system. We will try to contact the GNSS manufacturers to see the chances for further development of the technology developed in this project into commercial products.

15215117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15215117.value: Slope stability monitoring is an important method for reducing the potential nature disasters. Currently, large number of technologies have been developed, including on-site monitoring (i.e. installing GNSS receiver on the slope) and offset monitoring (i.e INSAR technology). Most existing GNSS monitoring method installs GNSS receivers on the slope to estimating the coordinate changes on the points on a slope. In this project, we developed a GNSS slope monitoring system to remotely monitoring the slope movement (i.e. more than 500 m away from a slope). Two new algorithms are developed for different GNSS receiver types. The experiments demonstrates that the accuracy of sub-centimetre level of deformation can be monitored by this new technology. This will allow to monitor the slope movement remotely, which can used to monitoring the active slopes where the installations of equipment are difficult.

15215517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15215517.value: Quality health services entail not only competent healthcare professionals but also effective management of the underpinning facilities. Such facilities management (FM) services include soft-side services such as cleaning and those on the hard side, e.g. engineering services. Researchers have proposed certain assessment models for healthcare facilities and some have developed performance indicators for the facilities. In recent years, the Investigators completed a study on the outsourcing of hospital engineering services, developed a model for evaluation of input, delivery and output of FM services, and established an assessment scheme for engineering facilities in commercial buildings. Based on such groundwork, a five-stage research study that aims to develop a method for systematic evaluation of hospital FM performance is proposed. In Stage 1, a comprehensive literature review will be carried out to identify measures for assessing FM performance of hospital buildings. The performance measures will be grouped into different types (e.g. safety, financial, etc.) and categorized by different phases of the FM service delivery process and different levels of an FM organization. In Stage 2, a focus group meeting involving representatives of owners, FM contractors and users of hospital buildings will be convened to review the usefulness of the identified measures. Based on the then selected measures, a questionnaire survey will be designed in Stage 3 for distribution to FM professionals. Their responses will enable shortlisting of key performance indicators (KPIs). In Stage 4, a second focus group meeting will be convened to examine any interdependencies between the KPIs, from which a network diagram showing the relationships between the KPIs will be constructed for processing by the analytic network process (ANP), which is a multi-criteria decision analysis technique. Face-to-face interviews, in two parts, will be held with FM professionals in Stage 5. Responses during the first part will be processed by the ANP software to yield importance weightings for the KPIs and hence a performance scoring scheme will be devised. For the second part, actual hospital FM performance data will be assembled in order to determine the KPIs’ performance scores, thus demonstrating the scheme’s applicability to hospital buildings. Correlations between importance and performance for each type of FM service will be analyzed to unveil their fundamental relationships. To complete the development of the intended evaluation method, the outcome performance of the FM services will be examined against their input cost to reveal the holistic performance of the services. 設施管理水平是除醫生的專業性和競爭力之外，決定醫療服務質量的另一核心因素。醫療設施管理不僅涉及諸如樓宇清潔等“軟”的方面，也包括對工程設備的保養與維修等“硬”的方面 。過往已有學者提出一些用於評估醫療設施管理的模型或指標。項目組也於近年來完成了多項相關工作，包括研究承包型醫療設施服務的績效表現； 建立用於評價輸入，工程交付，和設施管理產出的模型；以及制定用於商業樓宇的設施管理服務評價機制。基於這些成果，項目組在本項目中將致力於構建一個可系統性、全面地評價醫院樓宇設施管理績效的方法。 本項目擬包含五個階段。第一階段以了解現有的醫院設施管理績效量度指標為目的，進行全面的文獻綜述研究。所總結的指標將進一步歸納為“安全”、“財務”等組別， 並按其適用的階段和組織等級進行分類。第二階段為焦點小組討論——業主，設施管理承包商，醫療服務使用人士將被邀請來審閱上階段所總結的度量指標。根據焦點小組的意見，項目組將於第三階段設計以設施管理專業人士為對象的調查問卷。通過分析問卷結果，項目組將確立醫院樓宇設施管理的關鍵績效指標（KPIs）。 項目組將於第四階段組織第二次焦點小組討論，以分析所得各KPIs間的相關性。討論的結果將通過一種多準則決策分析方法——網絡分析法（ANP）——進行處理，從而以直觀的網絡圖示形式來展示各KPI間的復雜關系。本項目的最終階段包括兩部分面對面訪談。第一部分訪談的目標是得出設施管理專業人士對以前階段所得KPIs的反饋。訪談結果將在ANP軟件中處理，以計算各KPIs的權重。項目組可據此構建評價醫院樓宇設施管理績效的評分機制。第二部分訪談將得到一些案例醫院的設施管理績效的數據，項目組將結合該數據來展示所構建的評分機制的可實施性。本項目可揭示各項醫院設施管理服務的重要性和之間的聯系。在考量各項管理績效的同時，項目組也將充分考慮其所對應的投入，從而完善和拓展所構建的評分機制的全面性。

15215517.label: Realisation of objectives
15215517.value: Adding to the literature search done in preparing this study, further effort was made upon commencement of the study to review any new, relevant publications. The literature review process identified measures that are applicable for assessing the FM performance of hospital buildings. The identified measures were grouped into different aspects and, with reference to the process-hierarchy model, they were classified by FM services delivery process and FM organization hierarchical level [i.e. Objective 1]. Based on the above findings, a series of questions were designed for use in a focus group meeting in order to examine and confirm the usefulness of the above measures in real-world applications. Hospital FM professionals were invited to participate in this meeting, with the Investigators of this study serving as facilitators. Upon deliberations and obtaining the consensus of the participants, the identified measures, after modifications and adjustments, were consolidated. These measures, subsequently, formed the basis for designing a survey questionnaire. The questionnaire was pilot-tested and then refined before dissemination in full swing to solicit opinions of the FM professionals. To ensure that only quality data would be analysed, the survey responses were scrutinized in a screening process. Those with incomplete data provided were discarded. The remaining 103 responses, with all the required fields of the questionnaire completed, were taken for analysis. Then, detailed statistical analyses were conducted, and the responses on the importance levels were processed to determine the mean value and rank of each of the performance indicators listed in the questionnaire. Those with relatively high importance levels were shortlisted as key performance indicators (KPIs) for use in the evaluation method [i.e. Objective 2]. A second focus group meeting was convened. All being veterans and holding positions such as senior hospital facilities manager and hospital facilities manager, the focus group experts were highly experienced with hospital FM work. The meeting, with an interim comfort break in the middle, was held for one and half hours. Upon commencement, all the meeting participants were informed of the research aim and objectives. In addition to the ethics approval given by the Human Subjects Review Committee of the principal investigator’s institution, informed consent was obtained and the participants were given assurances that a strict ethical protocol would be adhered to: specifically, confidentiality and anonymity of participants was assured. Then, the study team showed a relationship diagram of the selected indicators, briefed the participants about the interdependencies and influences between the indicators, and invited them to express their opinions and discuss the information shared with them. The discussion comprised two parts: 1) whether each of the performance indicators should be included in the subsequent analysis; and 2) the influences between the indicators and their performance categories. Referring to the relationship diagram, a series of comparisons between the indicators and/or their respective performance categories are needed to determine their importance weightings according to the Analytic Network Process (ANP) method. For this comparison purpose, the study team explained some comparison examples to the participants before asking them to make comparisons on the items being studied. The responses for such comparisons given by each of the focus group experts were recorded and immediately input to the SuperDecision software. Among all of the pairwise comparisons, the largest matrix was 3-by-3, for which the allowable consistency ratio is 0.05. Whenever a computed consistency ratio exceeded this acceptable limit, the respective participant was requested to reconsider the response given and adjust the corresponding comparison judgment. This step repeated until the computed consistency fell within the acceptable limit. Based on the computed importance weightings pertaining to each of the focus group experts, the average weighting of each performance category (i.e. physical, environmental, financial and safety) was calculated. Likewise, the average weighting of each KPI in its own category was calculated. Upon determination of the weightings, a performance scoring scheme was devised for each building studied [i.e. Objective 3]. After obtaining the above-mentioned weightings, interviews were held with the experts to collect FM record data for scoring each of the KPIs. In total, data from 20 hospitals were gathered, which included: facilities maintenance work orders; operational incidents and statutory orders served by government departments; energy consumption and carbon emissions; and O&M and energy costs of the hospital buildings. The data fell into two types: percentage data and numeric data. For percentage data where the KPI’s possible performance levels lie within a bounded scale (e.g. ‘availability of lift service’, which ranges from 0 to 100%), the actual value of the record data was taken as the performance score. For KPIs whose best performance levels are some target values (e.g. ‘actual costs within budgeted costs’), the best performance is attained when the actual level hits the budgeted level. Conversely, a budget overrun shows failure in financial control. Ergo, two scenarios were considered in determining the performance score of KPIs of this type: (A) the actual data value was taken as the performance score of the KPI if the data value is below or equal to the target value; and (B) the difference between the actual data value and the target value was considered in calculating the performance score if the data value exceeds the target value. For numeric data where the KPI’s possible performance levels are not bounded by definite limits (e.g. ‘No. of incidents’, which ranges from zero to virtually an unlimited value), one of the following two methods was used for the determining the performance score for the concerned KPI. In cases where the lower the KPI value, the better the performance level: the actual data value was normalized with respect to the best performance data value (i.e. minimum value among the sample data) and the worst performance data value (i.e. maximum value among the sample data). The performance score of the KPI was then calculated. Likewise, in cases where the higher the KPI value, the better the performance level: the actual data value was normalized with respect to the best and the worst performance data values, and the performance score of the KPI was calculated. The normalized values of individual performance measures was taken as their performance scores for input to the performance scoring scheme, thus demonstrating the applicability of the scheme [i.e. Objective 4]. The importance weightings and performance levels of the FM services obtained from the above stages were plotted on an importance-performance matrix to show if any of the eight possible perception tendencies exists. Such findings contributed to the fundamental understanding of the correlations between importance and performance of FM services. And the performance levels of individual services trades over different time periods were plotted against the corresponding input costs to show any changes in the performance footprints of the services. These findings, interpreted with the aid of a cost-performance matrix, are useful for internal performance benchmarking. In order to complete the evaluation for the FM services, the overall performance score of the services were processed to yield a normalized overall performance score, which serves as an external performance benchmarking index, enabling fair performance comparisons to be made across the same type of hospitals. Combining the above findings, the correlations between importance and performance of FM services, and the holistic FM performance of the hospital buildings were revealed [i.e. Objective 5].
