15215517.label: Major findings and research outcome
15215517.value: An extensive literature review, which forms the fundamental part of this multi-stage research project, identified 61 indicators that are applicable to assessing the FM performance of hospital buildings. The phase-hierarchy model was proved useful for mapping the performance indicators for hospital buildings. The mapping results informed clearly which phase(s) of services delivery and which hierarchical level(s) the hospital FM performance indicators belong to. This approach can be taken in future (e.g. for studies on other types of buildings) when it is necessary to classify indicators for performance evaluation purposes. Through a focus group study, 18 KPIs were shortlisted, covering four aspects, namely, “physical”, “safety”, “environment” and “financial”. These KPIs serve as a basis for designing a subsequent questionnaire survey. The survey results, showing the importance levels of the indicators, were taken for review in a second focus group meeting. After deliberations and adjustments, eventually, ten KPIs were selected as optimal for use in the intended performance evaluation model. Developed from this optimal set of KPIs and the application of the ANP method, the performance evaluation model established in this present study is novel in the context of hospital FM. The KPIs’ practicality in real-world hospital buildings was verified by the focus group experts. Unlike traditional studies where assumptions or simulations were made to assign scores for the KPIs, this present study’s research team managed to obtain real performance data that were retrieved from empirical FM records and used such data to score the KPIs. A key finding from this process was the classification of two data types: data with bounded values, and data with unbounded values. Another important finding was the identification of different scenarios where the score of a KPI is higher (or lower) when the respective performance data value is higher (or lower) than the target KPI value. In handling these different scenarios and the two data types, the robust calculation method devised was useful for obtaining the FMP score, which reflects the overall FM performance of the hospital. Overall, a rigorous and pragmatic scheme has been developed for evaluation of hospital FM services. The scheme has been proved useful for assessing not only the FM performance of individual hospital buildings but can also be applied for comparing the performances of different hospital buildings.

15215517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15215517.value: While measures had been taken in this study to ensure the data quality and reliability, further studies of this kind should endeavour to enlarge the sample of responses such that the results of analysis could be generalized. As the model was established based on the group of hospitals investigated in Hong Kong, in future the model can be taken to conduct similar FM research work on other hospitals. When more evaluation results of this kind are available, both internal and external performance benchmarking can be made for hospitals, for the betterment of the healthcare sector. Following the approach of this study can also establish similar performance evaluation models for managing the facilities in other types of buildings or infrastructures. With the increased applications of smart technology, further work can be taken to develop a web platform that collects, process, analyse data of the relevant FM systems. When such a platform is established, the FM performances of the respective buildings can be readily evaluated in an automatic manner. The evaluation results are potentially useful for identifying how FM services could be continuously improved for the needs and well-being and their end-users.

15215517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15215517.value: Before this study, a credible method for systematic assessment of hospital FM performance was not available. To address this problem, this study was initiated. Upon developing the intended FM performance evaluation method, the applicability of the method to hospital buildings was tested using empirical hospital FM performance data. Besides this originality, the study is novel in that it investigated the existence of any correlation between importance and performance of FM services. The method can track changes in the performance footprints of individual FM services over time. The results of the study are instrumental to the pursuit of effective FM services for hospital buildings, not only in Hong Kong but also elsewhere around the world. The study methodology, data analysis processes and the findings can serve as useful reference for similar research in other disciplines. In particular, the result of the applicability of the developed method in evaluating hospital FM services and the findings on the correlations between importance and performance of the services provide important, fundamental information for future research. As such, the study will have long-term, influential impacts on both practice and research.

15215617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15215617.value: This investigation aims to explore the mechanisms by which the properties of fibroin fibers (FFs), i.e. silk in this study, could be chemically modified to improve specific aspects of performance (e.g. wet strength and antiseptic power). The investigation will enable us to: extract important information about photo-redox initiated polymerization, crosslink chemistry and toughening mechanism, and explore fundamental principles of photocatalytic engineering and biopolymer-enhancing technologies. We propose a study of new technique to enhance FFs with guanidine-containing double network (DN) structure, which will be synthesized through photocatalytic dual reactions under visible light at room temperature for the first time. This finely tuned DN structure will realize improved wet strength and permanent antibacterial surface, and enable us to explore the intrinsic toughening mechanism and the wide possibility of photo processing. This novel photocatalytic approach is applicable to a variety of compounds and extendable to many fields beyond textile industry. It can promote the advancement of wide areas such as biopolymer functionalization, health care technique, and sustainable photo energy exploitation. 本研究旨在探索通過化學修飾蠶絲絲素來提高其特定性能，尤其 是濕強度和抗菌能力。它能提煉出關於光氧化/還原引發聚合，交 聯化學與增韌機理的重要資訊，揭示光催化工程和生物大分子改 性的基本原理。 我們計畫首次應用室溫可見光催化雙反應，開發含胍基的雙網路 結構改性絲素。這一可控的雙網路結構可以實現提高的濕強度和 長久的抗菌表面，並揭示材料內在的增韌機理和光加工的廣泛適 用性。這一光催化方法可用於多種化合物和紡織業以外的多個領 域，還可以促進生物材料功能化，健康護理技術和可持續的光能 利用的發展。

15215617.label: Realisation of objectives
15215617.value: (1) To investigate the photo-crosslinking of fibroin fibers (FFs) in relaxed / stretched states, identify the efficiency of photo-crosslink, and characterize the changes in their crystallinity and mechanical properties in dry / wet states. Solid fibroin fibers (FFs) were directly cross-linked by employing a ruthenium-mediated redox pair under visible light at room temperature for the first time. The chemical cross-link through dityrosine connection was confirmed by Fouriertransform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, fluorescence spectra, and a solubility test. The resultant cross-link density of fibers was calculated based on their swelling ratio evaluation in LiBr solution. Further applying stretch to the fibers during irradiation increased the fiber strength to higher values. The break stress and Young’s modulus of photo-cross-linked 15% stretch FFs reached a 60−90% increase in comparison to the original FFs in dry and wet conditions. This work was published in ACS Biomater. Sci. Eng. 2022, 8, 484−492. Based on our experience in photochemistry of polymers, we were also invited to contribute a review paper to a journal editor. We reviewed different photo-initiation approaches for the dityrosine crosslink formation, which contributes to improving mechanical property and stability of polymers, especially for the bio-tissues in most insects. The photo manipulation on tyrosine units provides a path for the formation of dityrosine bonding and shows unique superiority to other chemical approaches. It was published in Journal of Materials Science & Technology 63 (2021) 182–191. Thus, this objective was fully achieved. (2) To design guanidine-containing polymers initiated by visible light at room temperature, analyze the photo-initiation and polymerization kinetics of vinyl monomers in aqueous solutions, and explore the dependence of bactericidal efficacy on guanidine contents. Bactericidal polymers were synthesized via free-radical polymerization from butyl acrylate (BA) and glycidyl methacrylate (GMA) mixtures (molar ratio = 10:1 ~ 2:1), with photo-initiator Irgacure 2959 or riboflavin (1 w/v%) under UV light (360–365 nm, 20 W) or white light (20 W). The prepared copolymer P(BA-GMA) was purified, and further modified with ethylenediamine (EDA) in dry THF. Resultant copolymer was functionalized with 1H-pyrazole-1-carboxamidine hydrochloride (HPC) and N,N-diisopropyl ethylamine (DIPEA) at room temperature. Purified via dialysis and freeze drying, the guanidine-containing polymers were confirmed in structure with NMR and FTIR characterizations. These guanidine-containing polymers were tested against bacteria Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) and Escherichia coli (E. coli), and confirmed as efficient bactericidal molecules according to the shaking dispersion method (standard ASTM E2149). Its minimum effective concentration is as low as 0.03 mg/mL. This part of work was prepared into a manuscript (Antimicrobial Silks with Integrated Guanidine-containing Polymers via In-situ Photosynthesis). Thus, this objective was fully achieved. (3) To create double networks (DN) in FFs through photosynthesis, clarify the resultant two networks in their distribution and ratio, and explore the effects of DN structure on FF crystallinity and mechanical properties in dry / wet states. Robust silk fibroin fibers (FFs) with double networks (DN) were produced via swelling with monomers and in-situ photo-polymerization, together with photo-crosslinking of fibroin chains. The obtained DN FFs exhibited improved mechanical properties in both dry and wet states, and enhanced alkali resistance. Based on this fast photo-initiated synthesis and DN strengthening mechanism, the silk fibers are expected to be extended to wider structural applications that require high durability and mechanical resilience. It has been prepared into a manuscript (Photosynthesis of Robust Silk Fibroin Fibers with Double Network Structures). DN fibers were also fabricated from ketone-containing polymers and iota-carrageenan, in which dynamic covalent crosslinking of acylhydrazone chemistry and supramolecular helix coordination were explored. Parental DN hydrogels were wet-spun into macroscopic fibers with controlled drawing ratios, which demonstrated high strength of 1.35 MPa and toughness of 1.22 MJ/m3. Highly efficient self-healing performances were observed in hydrogel fibers and their bulk specimens. These fibers achieved rapid and near-complete healing, via the reversible acylhydrazone chemistry and helix coordination manipulated by pH and temperature, respective. They also supported shape memory and repetitive actuating function, with potential application in smart devices. This work was published in Gels 2022, 8, 101. Through combining silk fibroin and hydrogel into double-layer fibers, solar energy storage function was achieved. Long-lasting phosphorescent phosphor (i.e. 492 nm) and fluorescent Ag2S quantum dots (QDs) were incorporated into the core−sheath fibroin fibers, and realized solar energy storage in core and continuous near-infrared emission on shell. Up to 13.5 % of the 993 nm NIR radiation passed through porcine epidermis of 0.25 mm thickness. This work has shed new light on the fabrication of self-warming fiber, which is anticipated to be applied in various fields such as continuous warming textiles and wearable phototherapy devices. This work was published in ACS Materials Lett. 2020, 2, 801−807. The above DN structure inspired us to explore its possible usage in electric energy storage. We introduced a single-Zn-ion conducting hydrogel electrolyte (SIHE), P(ICZn-AAm), synthesized from iota carrageenan (IC) and acrylamide (AAm). The SIHE manifests single Zn2+ conductivity via the abundant sulfates fixed on the IC polymer backbone, delivering a high Zn2+ transference number of 0.93. It also exhibits outstanding ionic conductivity of 2.15 × 10−3 S cm−1 at room temperature. This DN gel electrolyte led to stable Zn striping/plating performance along with a homogenous and smooth Zn deposition layer on the electrode. The passivation of Zn anode was effectively prohibited due to the lack of free anions in the electrolyte. The practical performance of the SIHE is further investigated with Zn−V2O5 batteries, which showed a stable capacity of 271.6 mA h g−1 over 150 cycles at 2 C and 127.5 mA h g−1 over 500 cycles at 5 C. This work was published in ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2021, 13, 30594−30602. Thus, this objective was fully achieved. (4) To investigate the photosynthesis of DN in braided silk sutures with additional chromatic sensor, evaluate the changes in their braiding structure and mechanical properties, and assess their bacteria sensing, antibacterial efficacy and cytotoxicity. Braided silk sutures were wound on PTFE framework and immersed in 6% CaCl2 solution in methanol for swelling, then immersed in precursors (monomer BA and GMA, photo-initiator Irgacure 2959 / riboflavin, crosslinker BDDMA) for exchange. The sutures were exposed to UV light / white light for polymerization. The resultant P(BA-GMA) on sutures were further reacted with EDA, HPC and DIPEA to obtain guanidine groups. The guanidinized suture presented improved tensile property (by over 50% in dry & wet states) and promising bactericidal activity against S. aureus and E. coli (according to modified AATCC-100 standard). When the sutures were further modified with guanidine derived diacetylene (GDDA) under UV light, PDA coating was formed on surface. These PDA coated sutures demonstrated color change from blue to red in contact with bacteria (S. aureus and E. coli), and reliable compatibility with keratinocytes and erythrocytes. This part of work will be organized into a manuscript (Photosynthesis of Bactericidal and Sensing Silk Sutures with Double Network Inside). Thus, this objective was fully achieved.

15215617.label: Major findings and research outcome
15215617.value: In this project, double network was successfully established via photosynthesis approach in silk filaments and sutures, which greatly improved the filament tensile strength and toughness, together with mechanical stability in wet environment. Additionally, guanidine group and guanidine derived diacetylene were proved highly effective as bactericidal group and chromatic sensing reagents respectively, through their incorporation in the double network and bioassay against typical bacteria on sutures. The modified silk sutures were also proved compatible with human skin application. Through adjusting the double network chemical structures, self-healing and shape memory actuating gel filaments were also obtained based on dynamic bonding and helix coordination. The double network was also synthesized via other approaches and integrated with additional functional components into core-sheath filaments and battery electrolytes, which presented essential and versatile photonic and electronic functions. A Chinese patent was applied based on our invention on the Water stimulated contraction fabrics and bandages and their preparation methods (ZL202110040649.6, filed: 13-Jan-2021). Totally, this project has produced 5 published papers, 3 manuscripts in preparation and submission, 1 patent, 5 conference papers, 2 PhD theses (refer to Section C).

15215617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15215617.value: Besides the photosynthesis of double network in silk fiber and suture, the double network was also utilized in core-sheath filaments and battery electrolytes to realize photonic and electronic functions. The photosynthesis approach will be further explored for the modification / functionalization of other biopolymers and fibrous assemblies.

15215617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15215617.value: This project explored the photo-redox initiated polymerization, crosslink chemistry and toughening mechanism, and clarified fundamental principles of photocatalytic engineering and biopolymer-enhancing technologies. In detail, we developed a new technique to enhance FFs with guanidine-containing double network (DN) structure, which was synthesized through photocatalytic dual reactions under visible light at room temperature for the first time. This finely tuned DN structure realized improved wet strength and permanent antibacterial surface, and enabled us to explore the intrinsic toughening mechanism and the wide possibility of photo processing. This novel photocatalytic approach is applicable to a variety of compounds and extendable to many fields beyond textile industry. It may promote the advancement of wide areas such as biopolymer functionalization, health care technique, and sustainable photo energy exploitation.

15216117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15216117.value: The invention of the digital camera has given people the privilege of capturing the world in pictures, and the proliferated use of smartphone devices enables these pictures to be shared conveniently with the world. Image data, with diverse visual and semantic content, is growing exponentially every day in volume. This enables computer vision community to progress rapidly in content-based research studies, especially in areas relating to human and clothing recognition. On the other hand, precise human modelling technology has advanced rapidly in recent years in computer graphics domain, in which a digital 3D human model can now be reconstructed from front- and side-view photographs of a subject with known standard pose. The resulting digital human models have accurate size and shape appearance, comparable to scanned models. Extending from this precise human modelling technology, we will investigate in this project the recognition of size and shape information by reconstructing subjects’ 3D human body models in arbitrary poses from still images of limited-views. In addition to somatotype recognition, this project will also analyse the subjects’ style preference by mining fine-grained clothing attributes from input images by exploiting state-of-the-art deep learning technologies, namely human parsing, pose recovery and attribute modelling. By analysing abundant data of clothing style and somatotype recognition, it provides the fertile ground for future work on personalised recommendations and context-aware advertisement. The technology has vast potential for application in e-commerce sector, enhancing customer satisfactory of online shoppers, also lowering the return rate of online shopped clothes. 本項目研究基於圖像的體型分析及識別技術，是透過重構真實場景的圖像中的用戶3D人體模型的前沿技術。本項目擬利用最先進的深度學習技術從真實場景的圖像中挖掘用戶的服裝各樣屬性，從而分析其喜好的服式風格。通過上述方法從圖像中所獲取用戶的體型呎碼的信息以及所挖掘的服裝款式、風格、形狀等屬性可用於研究個人化推薦算法應用於服裝電子商務，為用戶提供個人化的服裝推薦，以減少退貨次數並改善用戶體驗的目的。

15216117.label: Realisation of objectives
15216117.value: A total of 4 research objectives are defined in this research project, including deep learning based technology and network structure, clothing and human parsing, pose estimation, as well as visual features extraction and learning. These research objectives have been achieved in the project, in which new deep learning-based methods have been developed for human and clothing parsing, pose estimation, and multi-task learning of both parsing and pose estimation, as well as visual image feature processing and understanding. These methods and models have been experimentally verified to be effective in comparison of the state-of-the-art methods. These human parsing and pose estimation methods have been developed into various applications for body size and shape analysis, body skin surface variation in dynamic poses, and fashion recommendations. 9 journal publications/submissions have been generated from this project, some of these are under review and 3 are published. In addition, 6 conference publications are generated from this research. One PhD student is trained; although the student was admitted to the project late, about mid of the project, she mainly focused on the research objective 4 and has 3 conference publications and 2 journal submission under preparation in total. Another PhD student was partially supported by this project and she had one conference publication with best paper award and 2 journal submission under preparation.

15216817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15216817.value: Distributed optical fibre sensing systems have potential application in many application fields such as monitoring of large civil structures, transportation, energy and security systems. Since they allow the measurement of sensing parameter over the range of tens or even hundreds kilometers with a spatial resolution down to a meter, it can easily be used to replace hundreds of thousands conventional sensors. However, in order to expand their application ranges, the performance of the sensors in terms of sensing range, spatial resolution, accuracy of measurement parameters have to be further improved. Much research has been carried out in these aspects, the focuses have been on Brillouin optical domain analyzer(BOTDA) for temperature and strain measurement and phase optical time domain reflectrometer (phase OTDR) for vibration measurement. In the proposed study, we will look at the possibility of system performance improvement through introducing wavelength and spatial dimensions into system design. Both new system configuration and new sensing fibre design will be investigated. In particular, we will study BOTDA system based on wavelength multiplexed pump and wavelength multiplexed probe for reducing nonlocal effect and for reducing measurement time. We will investigate the use of few mode fibre in phase OTDR system for enhancing signal to noise ratio of the detected signal. We will investigate the use of two new few mode fibre designs in the study of few mode fibre based BOTDA and dynamic grating based sensing system. Through system study and fibre optimization, system performance improvement is expected to be obtained. The proposed study is expected to make good contribution to the development of future distributed sensing systems. 分布式光纤传感系统在很多应用领域都有很好的应用前景。由于可用于在几十到上百公里小于米级分辨率的信号感测，它可用于代替几十万个常规传感器。为进一步增加它的应用领域， 我们需要增强传感器的测量距离，空间分辨率和测量精度。在此研究项目中， 我们希望利用空间及波长复用技术来提高系统性能。我们将考虑新型系统结构及新性传感光纤设计。通过研究我们希望能大大增加分布式传感系统的应用领域。

15216817.label: Realisation of objectives
15216817.value: All the objectives have been realized successfully. In particular, we proposed and investigated a novel in-fiber spatially integrated Michelson interferometer based on weakly coupled multicore fiber (MCF) for vibration sensing. The compact interferometer is constructed by using two separate cores of the MCF, where the fiber end is cleaved in order to generate strong Fresnel reflection, and independent light coupling between the cores of MCF and the single mode fibers (SMFs) is enabled by the fan- in coupler. Broad vibration frequency response range up to 12 kHz has been achieved. The unique sensor structure provides some extraordinary merits, including ultra-compact size, high mechanical strength, high sensitivity and temperature insensitivity. We propose and demonstrate a multicore fiber (MCF) based space-division multiplexed (SDM) Φ-OTDR and Mach–Zehnder interferometer (MZI) hybrid sensor, enabling truly uninterrupted distributed vibration sensing with broad vibration frequency response range and high spatial resolution. By taking advantage of highly integrated multiple spatial cores offered by an MCF, Φ- OTDR implemented in one of the cores is used to locate the vibration. Meanwhile, an MZI is constructed using another two parallel spatial cores with sufficient continuous-wave optical power from a coherent narrow linewidth laser, which is used to retrieve the vibration frequency by processing the acquired interference signal. Compared with the single mode fiber based hybrid systems, the proposed SDM configuration allows implementation of Φ-OTDR and MZI independently without any crosstalk between them. Consequently it offers many unique advantages, such as simple data processing procedure, good signal-to-noise ratio of the demodulated vibration frequency spectrum, no frequency dead zone, and single-end access. A multipath distributed acoustic sensing system based on phase-sensitive optical time-domain reflectometry (Φ-OTDR) and frequency division multiplexing (FDM) technique has been investigated. This enables simultaneously monitoring of multipath vibration with flexible functionality. Using wavelength and spatial diversity, we have successfully solved the fading problem associated with Φ-OTDR systems.

15216817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15216817.value: The research work enabled us to implement distributed optical fibre sensing systems with improved system performance. we will try to implement some of the research findings in realtime hardware and explore its application in different application areas.

15216817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15216817.value: Optical fibre can be used to implement a distribute sensing system to measure temperature, strain and vibration over tens of kilometers. With spatial resolution often in the range of meters, a single piece of optical fibre is equivalent to tens of thousand of distributed sensor. Additional advantages include immunity to electromagnetic interference, remote sensing and the ability to be used in harsh environment. A widely used distributed sensing system is vibration sensing. However, its performance is often limited by variation in other environment parameter and poor signal to noise ratio due to fading. It also has limited frequency response for long range sensing. In the project, through the use of spatial division, common mode signal has been rejected to enable better system performance. It also enables multi-parameter discrimination as well as extended frequency range. Using wavelength(frequency) multiplexing, fading problem can also be solved. The work carried out in the project helped to improve system performance fo distributed optical fibre sensing systems and should allow more innovative applications to be explored.

15216917.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15216917.value: 基於二硫化鉬/石墨烯量子點的復合納米系統用於影像引導的腫瘤幹細胞靶向光治療

15216917.label: Project Objectives
15216917.value: Aim 1: Synthesis and characterization of near-infrared GQDs and MoS2 nanosheet. Near-infrared GQDs will be synthesized with a solvothermal approach by co-doping of nitrogen and sulfur elements. The synthesis conditions will be optimized to achieve GQDs with strong adsorption/emission in NIR window and good singlet oxygen generation. Nanosized MoS2-PEG will be synthesized by an ultrasonic exploration approach from bulk MoS2. The photothermal heating property of MoS2-PEG nanosheet will be explored. Aim 2: Establishment of hybrid MoS2/GQD based phototherapy platform. The hybrid system will be established with near-infrared GQD and MoS2 nanosheet, linking by a cleavable linker at intracellular environment. Near-infrared GQD will be conjugated with nucleus-targeting molecule and MoS2 nanosheets will be conjugated with cancer stem cell targeting molecules for dual targeting purpose. The fluorescence quenching efficiency of this MoS2/GQD system will be explored to achieve optimal phototoxicity silence. Aim 3: Testing of the hybrid MoS2/GQD system in solutions. The formed hybrid nanosystem will be evaluated for fluorescence quenching, inhibitory characteristics of singlet oxygen generation, and photo-stability in extracellular fluids under laser irradiation. The fluorescence recovery and activation of singlet oxygen generation in intracellular solution with reductant glutathione (GSH)/acid environment will also be evaluated. Finally, the photothermal heating properties of the hybrid nanosystem in solutions will also be evaluated. Aim 4: In vitro testing of the hybrid MoS2/GQD imaging guided phototherapy for targeting skin cancer stem cells (CSCs). The dual-targeting efficiency will be compared between MoS2/GQD systems 1) with/without CSCs-targeting molecules, 2) with/without nucleus-targeting molecules and 3) reduction/acid cleavable bonds. To analyze the synergetic phototherapy effect, cell viability experiments of CSCs treated with only GQDs, only MoS2 nanosheet and MoS2/GQD systems after laser irradiation will be compared. The control experiments with common skin cancer cells and normal skin cells will also be performed.

15216917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15216917.value: 越來越多的研究結果表明，治療後腫瘤的復發往往與腫瘤幹細胞(cancer stem cells, CSCs)的抗藥性和自我更新性有關，其對於傳統的治療方式(放療和化療)均具有顯著的抗性。因此，亟需發展以CSCs為靶向的新型腫瘤治療方法用於腫瘤的有效治療，長期防止腫瘤的復發。在新近出現的治療方式中，具有非侵入式治療、副作用少和毒性低等優點的光治療方式, 光動力療法(photodynamic therapy, PDT)和光熱治療(photothermal therapy, PTT)，是潛在的替代治療方式。將PDT和PTT整合到一個平臺是增強光治療方式效果的新趨勢。然而，目前復合型的光治療平臺通常都是將有機PDT物質負載到無機PTT載體上，其具有一定的局限性，如PDT物質在生物環境中穩定性差，PDT物質在與PTT載體直接接觸後產生單線氧的產生下降，不具有定位能力等。因此，發展基於無機材料，穩定性高、生物兼容性好和對於目標CSCs選擇性光活化的復合型PDT-PTT平臺至關重要。 在本項目中，我們計劃構建一種基於二硫化鉬/石墨烯量子點(MoS2/GQDs)二維納米復合物，以CSC為目標的光治療納米系統，其具有熒光成像、CSCs和CSCs細胞核雙定位、腫瘤細胞內環境選擇性光活化PDT物質和更高的光治療效率等優點。在MoS2/GQDs納米復合物中，近紅外的GQDs作為成像探針和光動力學治療物質，MoS2納米片作為熒光猝滅體和光熱治療物質，以可通過還原作用或酸處理裂解的連接子實現的MoS2和GQDs連接。分別在MoS2納米片和GQDs上偶聯CSCs定位分子和細胞核定位分子，實現雙定位功能。當納米復合物進入腫瘤幹細胞後，細胞內環境高濃度的還原性物質谷胱甘肽或較低的pH值將破壞MoS2納米片和GQD之間的連接，從而使GQDs遠離MoS2納米片表面，恢復GQDs的熒光信號，活化光動力學功能。具有細胞核定位分子的GQDs定位並富集在細胞核內用於細胞核的定位治療。基於以上機理，本項目中構建的MoS2/GQDs納米復合物探針將用於皮膚腫瘤細胞的體外成像和光治療研究，這種基於無機二維納米復合物的探針可能作為一種具有生物兼容性好、穩定性高、雙定位、選擇性光活化和光治療效率高等優點，近紅外成像引導的光治療平臺。

15216917.label: Realisation of objectives
15216917.value: During the whole project period, all the 4 objectives have been realized. 1) Near-infrared GQDs were synthesized with a solvothermal approach by co-doping of nitrogen and sulfur elements. It was demonstrated the nitrogen and sulfur element doping could shift the emission spectra from blue emission to green and even red emission. It has been demonstrated that the quantum yield of GQDs could be improved by passivation with PEG. Various surface functional groups including amine and carboxyl groups could be grafted on surface for further functionalization. The photothermal properties of GQDs were characterized by thermal imaging camera. The singlet oxygen generation capability of GQDs were characterized by singlet oxygen sensor green assay (SOSG). The synthesized NIR GQDs showed both good photothermal and photodynamic properties under NIR 600nm and 808 nm irradiation. Nanosized MoS2-PEG was synthesized by an ultrasonic exploration approach from bulk MoS2. After PEGlation and sonication, the size of MoS2 nanosheets could be reduced to tens of nanometers. 2) Various hybrid systems were established with different nanomaterials including near-infrared GQD, MoS2 nanosheet, MOF materials, and nanodroplets. The combination of various components was realized by chemical bonding, pi-pi interaction and electrostatic interaction. The hybrid nanotherapy system included various components with multifunctions of multi-modality imaging, targeting molecules, surfaced molecule and therapy reagents. The hybrid nanosystems showed multi-modality imaging capability of fluorescence imaging, MRI imaging, photoacoustic imaging etc. The multimodality imaging could combine the advantages of single modality imaging for accurate diagnostics. The hybrid nanosystems were also functionalized with tumor targeting molecules, which could target tumor cells with specificity. The synthesized hybrid nanosystems with multiple therapy capabilities including photothermal therapy, photodynamic therapy and chemical therapy could enhance the therapy effect. 3) Various hybrid systems were tested in solutions for fluorescence quenching, photo-safety, photo-stability in extracellular fluids under laser irradiation. The emission spectra and adsorption spectra of the hybrid nanosystems were measured and compared with single components. The hybrid nanosystems were put in PBS solutions with various pH values/with bovine serum albumin (BSA) to test the stability in various physiological environment. The photothermal effect of the hybrid nanosystems was characterized by thermal imaging camera and compared with those of single components under various concentrations and various power density of laser irradiation. The singlet oxygen generation capability was characterized by singlet oxygen sensor green assay (SOSG) and compared with those of single components. The multi-modality imaging capability of the hybrid nanosystems were also tested in solution for fluorescence imaging, MRI imaging, photoacoustic imaging. 4) Both in vitro and in vivo testing of the hybrid imaging guided tumor phototherapy were realized. In vitro experiments were firstly performed with tumor cell model. We used 3D soft fibrin gels for caner stem cell selection. Quantitative RT-PCR and western blotting were used to characterize the characteristic biomarkers of cancer stem cells to confirm the cancer stem cells. The targeting capability of hybrid nanosystems were confirmed by the cellular uptake of hybrid nanosystems. The combinational therapy effects of various groups were evaluated in the tumor cell models and confirmed that the combinational therapy approach can significantly improve the therapy effects. Finally, in vivo animal experiments were performed to demonstrate the in vivo multimodality imaging for tumor target imaging. The combinational therapy effects of various groups were evaluated in the tumor animal modals and confirmed that the combinational therapy approach can significantly improve the therapy effects and decrease side effects.

The fluorescence recovery and activation of singlet oxygen generation in intracellular solution with reductant glutathione (GSH)/acid environment will also be evaluated. Finally, the photothermal heating properties of the hybrid nanosystem in solutions will also be evaluated.

In vitro testing of the hybrid GQD imaging guided phototherapy for targeting skin cancer stem cells (CSCs). The dual-targeting efficiency will be compared between GQD hybrid systems 1) with/without CSCs-targeting molecules, 2) with/without nucleus-targeting molecules and 3) reduction/acid cleavable bonds. To analyze the synergetic phototherapy effect, cell viability experiments of CSCs treated with only GQDs, only MoS2 nanosheet and MoS2/GQD systems after laser irradiation will be compared. The control experiments with common skin cancer cells and normal skin cells will also be performed.

15216917.label: Major findings and research outcome
15216917.value: We developed nitrogen-doped graphene quantum dots (GQDs) based nanosystem for cancer stem cell (CSC) targeting and therapy (Refer to Acta Biomaterials, 135, 493-505, 2021 in Part C). Here, we report that breast CSCs exhibit much lower stiffness but considerably higher uptake of nitrogen-doped graphene quantum dots (N-GQDs) than bulk tumor cells. Our findings unveil a new mechanism by which low cellular stiffness can be harnessed in nanoparticle-based strategies for specific CSC elimination, opening a new paradigm of cancer mechanomedicine. We also developed an O2 self-supplying catalytic nanoagent, based on tannic acid (TA)-Fe(III) coordination complexes-coated perfluorooctyl bromide (PFOB) nanodroplets with lactate oxidases (LOX) loading (PFOB@TA-Fe(III)-LOX, PTFL), for cascade metabolic-chemodynamic tumor therapy (CDT) by dual-depletion of lactate and ATP with hydroxyl • OH radicals generation (Refer to Advanced Science, 8, 2102595, 2021 in Part C). This multifunctional nanoagent may provide new insight for targeting abnormal tumor metabolism with the combination of CDT to achieve a synergistic therapeutic effect. We also developed a hybrid microbubble-based theranostic platform for dual-modality ultrasound (US) and enhanced photoacoustic (PA) imaging-guided synergistic tumor therapy by combining starvation therapy, low-temperature photothermal therapy (PTT), and hypoxia-activated therapy (Refer to Journal of Materials Chemistry B, 9, 9358-9369, 2021 in Part C). Through dual-modality US/PA imaging monitoring, PDA–PVAMBs@GOx with long-term retention (∼7 days) combined with PTT and TPZ significantly inhibited the growth of solid tumors with minimum systemic side effects, which might be a powerful tool for effective tumor treatment. To enhance the photodynamic therapy effect, we propose to fabricate porous metal organic framework (MOF) nanostructure which can function as GQDs carrier due to its porous structure. We have developed a size-controlled synthesis method for the synthesis of porous Zn-MOF-74 nanostructure and finished the characterization (Figure 3a,b) which showed good crystallinity and porosity. The related work has been published in (ACS Appl. Nano Mater., 1(7), 3747–3753, 2018. In Part C). We also developed a NIR-II driven MOF-based hybrid nanosystem (AIPH/PDA@CuS/ZIF-8) for hybrid photothermal (PTT)/photodynamic (PDT)/ and chemodynamic (CDT) combined tumor therapy (Refer to Journal of Nanobiotechnology, 19, 265, 2021 in Part C). The tumors could be completely eradicated after 14 days of treatment due to the prominent therapeutic effects of PTT/PDT/CDT. Finally, we extended the photothermal therapy idea from cancer therapy to osteoarthritis therapy and developed a molybdenum disulfide nanosheet-coated gold nanorods (MoS2‑AuNR) hybrid system for osteoarthritis pain targeted imaging and medication (Refer to ACS Nano, 15, 11711−11723, 2021 in Part C).

15216917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15216917.value: The further development of imaging guided combinational phototherapy will combine the latest concept of immunotherapy. Photothermal and photydynimic therapy can not only directly kill tumor cells but also can generate immunogenic cell death (ICD) molecules which can lead to the maturation of DC cells as well as activating T cells finally. The activated T cells will be used for further cancer immunotherapy. The idea of photo-induced immunotherapy will be the potential direction after completing this project. This photoinduced immunotherapy is expected to increase the tumor therapy efficiency with less side effects.

15216917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15216917.value: Accumulating evidence has suggested that cancer recurrence after treatment is often related to drug resistance and self-renewal properties of cancer stem cells (CSCs), which have been demonstrated to be markedly resistant to conventional therapeutic approaches including radiotherapy and chemotherapy. Therefore, CSCs-targeted therapy with new cancer therapeutic approaches is of urgent need for efficient cancer treatment and long-lasting prevention of cancer recurrence. In this project, we developed various hybrid nanosystems by combining multi-modality imaging guidance and multiple therapy approaches including photothermal(PTT), photodynamic (PDT) and other therapy approaches to achieve better therapy effect with less side effects.

15217317.label: Project Objectives
15217317.value: Novel designs of multimode PCFs will be developed in which the number of modes, type of modes, nonlinear coupling constants between modes, and mode properties can be controlled. We will vary the PCF parameters such as the index profile, arrangement of the air holes, the diameters of the air hole, the pitch size, etc. Modeling of nonlinear light propagation in multimode PCFs will be carried out using the appropriate theoretical and modeling tools which include nonlinear partial differential equations, coupled-mode equations, variational analysis, and the finite-difference-time-domain (FDTD) method. Fundamental spatiotemporal dynamics: we will carry out explorative studies to discover novel nonlinear phenomena including multisolitons using the multimode PCFs designed. Fabrication of PCFs and experiments: The multimode PCF designs developed will be fabricated using the in-house PCF drawing tower. Experimental studies will be carried out to study the spatiotemporal dynamics of light propagation in the PCF multimode fibers. The experimental results will be compared with the modeling results for further optimization of the fiber designs.

15217317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15217317.value: In the last five decades, extensive research has been carried out on optical fibers as a platform for fundamental study of nonlinear dynamics. Much of these efforts have been focused on single mode fibers because of their simplicity, which allow careful investigation of the interplay between the linear dispersive effects and nonlinearities leading to fundamental advances in diverse areas including soliton dynamics, supercontinuum generation, and mode-locked lasers. The modal degree of freedom offered by multimode fibers promise even more fertile ground than single mode fibers for novel nonlinear dynamical phenomena and applications. However, investigations of multimode fibers are hampered by their intrinsic complexity. In addition to each mode having its own dispersion and nonlinear characteristics, nonlinear coupling among the modes render the problem intractable when the number of modes is large. Nonlinear dynamical studies carried out on multimode fibers to date typically utilized commercially available graded index multimode fibers and focused on the lower order zero angular momentum modes. Thus the observed dynamics are similar to that of single-mode fibers. The full potential of multimode fibers remains to be explored. While a comprehensive study of nonlinear light propagation in multimode fibers is not possible, significant advances can still be achieved through an integrated research program combining multimode fiber designs, modelling, simulation, and experiments. In this project, we propose to utilize the design degree of freedom in photonic crystal fibers (PCFs) to develop multimode PCFs with specific properties targeted for three areas, they are multimode solitons, supercontinuum generation, and mode-locked lasers. The three areas are chosen because each emphasizes different properties of the multimode fibers. We will adopt two complementary approaches to determine the PCF designs for each area. The first is to start with a PCF design, and investigate its propagation characteristics using the relevant theoretical model. The second is to start with an idealized model of PCFs, and then develop the PCF designs that are described by the models. In either approach, we will limit the number of modes to less than 10, and focus on higher order modes such as the optical vortex modes. The multimode PCF designs developed will then be fabricated using our in-house PCF drawing tower and their properties characterized. Experiments in each area of focus will be carried out on these multimode PCFs. The experimental results will be compared with the simulations results, and then used to modify the PCF design. 近五十年來，光纖中的非線性動力學得到廣泛的研究。不過大部分研究都集中在單模光纖上，因為它只有一個傳輸模式，系統簡單，易於建模。基於這種簡單的系統模型，人們詳細研究了線性的色散效應和非線性效應之間的相互作用，在包括孤子動力學，超連續譜產生和鎖模激光在內的不同領域都取得了重要的成果。對於新的非線性動力學現象和應用而言，多模光纖提供的模式自由度使它比單模光纖可以支持更加豐富的現象。然而，多模光纖的研究受到其固有的複雜性的阻礙。除了每個模式獨有的色散和非線性特徵之外，當模式數量大時，模式之間的非線性耦合使問題變得難以求解。迄今為止，對多模光纖進行的非線性動力學研究通常使用漸變折射率多模光纖，並集中在低階零角動量模式上，因此觀察到的動力學類似於單模光纖。多模光纖的全部潛力尚待探索。 雖然不可能對多模光纖中的完整非線性光傳播進行系統性研究，但通過結合多模光纖設計，建模，模擬和實驗的綜合研究，仍然可以取得顯著成果。在這個項目中，我們提出利用光子晶體光纖（PCF）的設計自由度，在多模孤子，超連續譜產生和鎖模激光器三個領域來研究特定的多模PCF。選擇這三個領域是因為每個領域都利用了多模光纖的不同特性。我們將採用兩種互補的方法來研究每個領域的PCF設計。第一種是從PCF設計開始，並使用相關的理論模型來研究其傳播特徵。第二個是從PCF的理想化模型開始，然後開發由模型描述的PCF設計。在任一方法中，我們將模式的數量限制為小於10，並且關注高階模式，例如光旋轉角動量模式。然後將使用理工大學的PCF拉絲塔來製造設計的多模PCF。我們將在這些多模PCF上進行每個重點領域的實驗，實驗結果將與模擬結果進行比較，然後用於優化PCF設計。

15217317.label: Realisation of objectives
15217317.value: All four Objectives have been achieved. The following are brief discussions of the achievement and the research output. A. Deep-ultraviolet second-harmonic generation using few mode photonic crystal fiber. We experimentally demonstrate, for the first time, deep-UV SH generations (SHGs) by combining degenerate four-wave mixing (FWM) and surface nonlinearity polarization in an in-house designed and fabricated air-silica photonic crystal fiber (PCF). The solid-core PCF is fabricated from purified silica material with the refractive index of ~1.46 by the stack and draw technique. The core diameter (D) and relative air-hole size (d/Λ) for the PCF in the cladding region are 2.91 μm and 0.85, respectively. Because of the large d/Λ, three guided-modes can be supported in the fiber core, but we only focus on the characteristics of the fundamental and SH modes. We calculated effective refractive indices of the fundamental and SH modes considered, and derived the group-velocity dispersion curve of the fundamental mode from the effective refractive index, which agrees well with the measured values by pulse time-delay method. When femtosecond pump pulses with average input power of 650 mW and center wavelength of 810, 820, 830, and 840 nm are coupled into the normal dispersion region close to the zero-dispersion wavelength of the fundamental mode of the PCF, the anti-Stokes waves induced by degenerate FWM process are tunable from 669 to 612 nm. Then, they serve as the secondary pump, and deep-UV SHs are generated within the wavelength range of 334.5 to 306 nm as a result of surface nonlinearity polarization at the core-cladding interface of the PCF. The physical mechanism of the SHGs is confirmed by studying the dependences of the output power of the SHs on the PCF length and time. We have also established a theoretical model to analyze the SHGs. (Journal Output item 1 in Section 8 of Part C below). B. Discrete-ultraviolet generation by cascaded intermodal FWM using multimode photonic crystal fiber. We have also demonstrated experimentally, for the first time to the best of our knowledge, discrete ultraviolet (UV) wavelength generation by cascaded intermodal FWM when femtosecond pump pulses at 800 nm are launched into the deeply normal dispersion region of the fundamental guided mode of a multimode photonic crystal fiber (MPCF). For pump pulses at average input powers of P_av = 450, 550, and 650 mW, the first anti-Stokes waves are generated at the visible wavelength of 538.1 nm through intermodal phase matching between the fundamental and second-order guided mode of the MPCF. The first anti-Stokes waves generated then serve as the secondary pump for the next intermodal FWM process. The second anti-Stokes waves in the form of the third-order guided mode are generated at the UV wavelength of 375.8 nm. The maximum output power is above 10 mW for P_av = 650 mW. We also confirm that the influences of fiber bending and intermodal walk-offs on the cascaded intermodal FWM-based frequency conversion process are negligible. (Journal Output item 2 in Section 8 of Part C below). We note that the Journal Output items 1 and 2 form part of the output of the current project even though they were published before the start day of the project as the papers are the outcome of the on-going investigation on the proposal submitted in November 2016. C. All-fiber cylindrical vector beam laser. We demonstrated an all-fiber laser generating cylindrical vector beams (CVBs) with high efficiency and low threshold. The laser cavity consists of a long-period fiber grating (LPFG) acting as a transverse mode converter. The LPFG has a high coupling efficiency of over 99% in a working bandwidth of ∼8 nm around the resonant wavelength of 1548 nm. The fiber laser operates at 1547.95 nm with a narrow 30 dB spectral width of 0.18 nm and a side-mode suppression ratio (SMSR) of more than 56 dB. The features of high coupling efficiency, narrow spectrum, no parasitic oscillation, and no residual pump ensure the high mode purities of 98.12% and 98.33% for the radially and azimuthally polarized beams, respectively. The laser output power is 72 mW when the absorbed pump power is 225 mW, the threshold is as low as 24.5 mW, and the slope efficiency is as high as 35.41%. It is worth mentioning that the quantum efficiency of YDF is higher than that of EDF. So, we are certain that when this scheme is applied to 1.0 μm band with YDF as gain medium, the slope efficiency will be further enhanced. There is no doubt that this approach can be extended to pulsed fiber laser operation with Q-switching and mode-locking techniques. This all-laser laser will likely find applications in areas such as high-power CVB and orbital angular momentum (OAM) laser beam generation as well as in mode division multiplexing systems. (Journal Output item 3 in Section 8 of Part C below). One of the co-authors, Dr. Feng Li, is part of the PI’s research team. Even though the PI initiated and guided the research work, he did not consider his intellectual contribution is sufficient to warrant co-authorship in the publication. D. Mid-Infrared Supercontinuum and Frequency Comb Generations by Different Optical Modes in a Multimode Chalcogenide Strip Waveguide We numerically investigate the mid-infrared (MIR) supercontinuum (SC) generations with the three optical modes (TE_00, TE_10, and TE_20) in a multimode chalcogenide (As_2Se_3) strip waveguide. The waveguide structure is engineered to ensure that the pump pulses are propagated in the normal dispersion regions of the three optical modes considered. Highly coherent and octave-spanning MIR SCs are generated when the optimized pump pulse with 80-fs pulse duration, 3-kW peak power, and 3-m center wavelength is used. Moreover, the nonlinear dynamics of the SC generation are numerically analyzed. Finally, the SC-based frequency combs are numerically demonstrated when a pulse train with a repetition rate of 50 MHz is used as the pump source and launched into the multimode As_2Se_3-based strip waveguide. It is believed that the generated MIR SC and SC-based frequency comb sources have important applications in biophotonics, metrology, and sensing. (Journal Output item 5 in Section 8 of Part C below). E. Output by the investigation team on objectives not mentioned in the project proposal. Polarization-insensitive modulation is desirable for high-capacity on-chip optical interconnects. We propose a hybrid graphene-silicon-based polarization-insensitive electro-absorption modulator (EAM) with high-modulation efficiency and ultra-broad bandwidth. The hybrid graphene-silicon waveguide is formed by leveraging multi-deposited and multi-transferred methods to enable light interaction with graphene layers in its intense field distribution region instead of the commonly used weak cladding region, thus resulting in enhanced light–graphene interaction. By optimizing the dimensions of all hybrid graphene-silicon waveguide layers, polarization-insensitive modulation is achieved with a modulation efficiency (ME) of ~1.11 dB/μm for both polarizations (ME discrepancy < 0.006 dB/μm), which outperforms that of previous reports. Based on this excellent modulation performance, we designed a hybrid graphene-silicon-based EAM with a length of only 20 microns. The modulation depth (MD) and insertion loss obtained were higher than 22 dB and lower than 0.23 dB at 1.55 μm, respectively, for both polarizations. Meanwhile, its allowable bandwidth can exceed 300 nm by keeping MD more than 20 dB and MD discrepancy less than 2 dB, simultaneously, and its electrical properties were also analyzed. (Journal Output 4 in Section 8 of Part C below).

15217317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15217317.value: The current project only scratches the surface in the investigation on the multimode nonlinear optics in photonic crystal fibers (PCFs). Because of the cut in the research funding from the requested amount of the original proposal, two of the objectives in the original proposal have been dropped. They are (1) the development of mode-locked lasers to study the effect of spatial mode content on the mode-locking dynamics of fiber laser cavity comprised of multimode PCF, and (2) the fabrication of PCFs and experiments on the PCF designed in the first four objectives. Thus, the obvious next step on further development is to pursue the above two omitted objectives based on the results obtained in this project. Furthermore, novel and more sophisticated designs of the multimode PCFs to study the fundamental spatiotemporal dynamics including propagation of multisolitons, supercontinuum generation, and mode-locked lasers should be continued to be investigated. The novel multimode PCF designs developed should then be fabricated. Experimental studies are to be carried out and compared with the modeling results for further optimization of the multimode PCF designs.

15217317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15217317.value: Recently, there is a surge in interests in multimode fibers triggered by the push to utilize spatial division multiplexing to increase the data transmission rate in optical fiber communication systems. By its very nature, multimode fibers allow higher power transmission than single mode fibers. More important, the interaction of tens, even hundreds of propagation modes make multimode fibers fertile ground of nonlinear dynamics that promises novel and complex nonlinear phenomena and possible means to engineer and control physical processes such as supercontinuum generation and lasers. The spatial structure of the higher order modes such as the optical vortex modes, opens up a new total new dimension for exploration. In this project, we experimentally demonstrated, for the first time, deep ultraviolet second harmonics generations by combining degenerate four-wave mixing and surface nonlinearity polarization in an in-house designed and fabricated air-silica photonic crystal fiber. We have demonstrated experimentally, also for the first time, discrete ultraviolet wavelength generation by cascaded intermodal four-wave mixing. Then we demonstrated an all-fiber laser generating optical vortex beams with high efficiency and low threshold. Finally, we numerically investigate the mid-infrared supercontinuum generations with the three optical modes in a multimode chalcogenide strip waveguide.

15217417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15217417.value: Dealloying is the selective dissolution of one or more active elemental components of an alloy in corrosive solutions. It can be a key failure mechanism for engineering structures such as those in power plants and aging aircraft. It was found that the dealloying of binary alloys can result in the formation of porous metals with porous size ranging from a few nanometers to a few tens of micrometers. This has attracted significant attention for applications in catalysis, electrochemical supercapacitors, sensing and actuation, bone tissue engineering, mass and/or heat transport, high-temperature templates/scaffolds, radiation damage-tolerant materials, and battery electrodes in recent years. Unlike the extensive experimental achievements in creating porous metals by dealloying, progress in the theoretical modeling of the formation and evolution of 3D porous metal structures during dealloying is very limited, which hinders the understanding and prediction of the behavior of porous metals. This project will aim to develop a theoretical modeling framework for the formation and evolution of porous metals during dealloying, using phase-field methodology (PFM), a mesoscale modeling method that has advanced significantly over the past two decades. The research team has over 15 years of PFM modeling experience and will collaborate with experimentalists in this project. Combining with the modeling methods at the macro and atomistic scales, the project will deliver important tools for the mechanistic understanding and design of advanced porous metals, and for predicting the behavior of porous metals in engineering environments. 去合金化是选择性地将一种或多种合金的活性元素组分溶解在腐蚀性溶液中。这一直是工程结构（如发电厂和飞机等）的关键失效机制。研究人员发现二元合金的去合金化可导致多孔金属的形成，多孔尺寸范围从几纳米到几十微米。近年来，这些多孔金属在催化，电化学超级电容器，传感和致动，骨组织工程，质量和/或热传递，高温模板/支架，耐辐射损伤材料和电池电极中的应用引起了极大的关注。与通过去合金化创造多孔金属的广泛实验成果不同，对去合金化过程中3D多孔金属结构的形成和演化的理论建模进展非常有限，这阻碍了对多孔金属的形成与行为的理解和预测。本项目旨在采用相位场法（PFM）开发一种理论建模框架，用于理解和预测在去合金化过程中多孔金属的形成和演化。PFM是一种在过去二十年获得显着进步的细观尺度理论模拟方法。本研究团队拥有超过15年的PFM理论模拟经验，并将与实验人员合作。结合宏观和原子尺度的模拟方法，该项目将为去合金化机理研究和设计先进的多孔金属、以及预测工程环境中多孔金属的行为提供重要理论工具。

15217417.label: Realisation of objectives
15217417.value: Chemical dealloying beckons researchers both for scientific interest in corrosion failure of metallic materials and for the fabrication of nanoporous materials that have versatile applications due to their ultra-high surface area. Empirically, nanoporous structure evolves by the corrosion of less noble elements coupled with the rearrangement of more noble elements in the alloys. However, how topologically complex porous structures form and how environmental and material factors affect the dealloying kinetics are still unknown. This project developed a comprehensive model that provides a powerful tool to tailor made nanoporous metallic structures under chemical and electrochemical dealloying. All objectives are realized and some additional factors were investigated. Objective 1: A multiphase-field model based on a nucleation-growth mechanism is developed to understand and predict this behavior of Au–Ag alloy. The nucleation of the porous phase is controlled by a noise term, which is scaled by the phase transformation driving force to account for the heterogeneous nucleation. At the growth stage of the porous structure, the model focuses on two major interface-related processes: corrosion of the less-noble element (Ag) and surface diffusion of the more-noble element (Au). The parameters affecting the interface processes, such as the chemical acid concentration, initial alloy composition, and surface diffusion coefficient, are demonstrated to be the key factors controlling the morphology evolution of the dealloyed structure, which mirrors the experimentally observed behaviors. We also demonstrate the capability of this model to determine the content thresholds (parting limits) for porous structure formation, and to simulate the dealloying of two-phase composite and precursor with the presence of defects. Objective 2: Porous metal structures formed by electrochemical dealloying are extensively studied for the various applications that required high surface area. Here, a comprehensive multiphase-field model considering the electrochemical reaction, bulk and surface diffusion, ion transport, applied electropotential and charge conservation is developed to simulate microstructural pattern formation during the electrochemical dealloying process of binary alloys. The governing equations for the alloy-porous clusters-electrolyte system account for the electrochemical reaction rate and classical nucleation theory. The fundamentals of how the electropotential and precursor composition affect the dealloyed structure are naturally revealed by the governing equations. Moreover, we demonstrate that the proposed model enables the creation of bimodal porous metals with a hierarchical structure through the chemical dealloying of dual-phase Al-Au alloy.

15217417.label: Major findings and research outcome
15217417.value: In this study, a multiphase-field model based on a nucleation-growth mechanism is developed to understand and predict this behavior of Au–Ag alloy. The nucleation of the porous phase is controlled by a noise term, which is scaled by the phase transformation driving force to account for the heterogeneous nucleation. At the growth stage of the porous structure, the model focuses on two major interface-related processes: corrosion of the less noble element (Ag) and surface diffusion of the more noble element (Au). The simulation results demonstrate that the interplay between the Ag dissolution and Au diffusion determines the dealloying kinetics and morphology of the porous structure. The parameters affecting the interface processes, such as the chemical acid concentration, initial alloy composition, and surface diffusion coefficient, are demonstrated to be the key factors controlling the morphology evolution of the dealloyed structure, which mirrors the experimentally observed behaviors. We also demonstrate the capability of this model to determine the content thresholds (parting limits) for porous structure formation, and to simulate the dealloying of two-phase composite and precursor with the presence of defects. Porous metal structures formed by electrochemical dealloying are extensively studied for the various applications that required high surface area. Here, a comprehensive multiphase-field model considering the electrochemical reaction, bulk and surface diffusion, ion transport, applied electropotential and charge conservation is developed to simulate microstructural pattern formation during the electrochemical dealloying process of binary alloys. The governing equations for the alloy-porous clusters-electrolyte system account for the electrochemical reaction rate and classical nucleation theory. The simulation results imply that the electrochemical dealloying of Ag-Au is dominated by the coupling of the electrochemical reaction of Ag and surface diffusion of Au. The fundamentals of how the electropotential and precursor composition affect the dealloyed structure are naturally revealed by the governing equations. Moreover, we demonstrate that the proposed model enables the creation of bimodal porous metals with a hierarchical structure through the chemical dealloying of dual-phase Al-Au alloy.

15217417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15217417.value: The developed framework can be further applied to study other evolution processes such as nanostructure self-assembly under multiple physical fields.

15217417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15217417.value: Chemical and/or electrochemical dealloying is the selective dissolution of one or more active elemental components of an alloy in corrosive solutions. It was found in recent years that the dealloying of binary alloys can result in the formation of porous metals with porous size ranging from a few nanometers to a few tens of micrometers. This has attracted significant attention for applications in catalysis, electrochemical supercapacitors, sensing and actuation, bone tissue engineering, mass and/or heat transport, high-temperature templates/scaffolds, radiation damage-tolerant materials, and battery electrodes. However, the progress in the theoretical modeling of the formation and evolution of 3D porous metal structures during dealloying is very limited, which hinders the understanding and prediction of the behavior of porous metals. This project was aimed to develop a theoretical modeling framework using phase-field methodology. This theoretical framework includes (1) for the first time to incorporate thermo-nucleation theory for heterogeneous nucleation of new solid phase at the metal-electrolyte interfaces; (2) to construct multi-phase-field model to describe morphology evolution of more than 3 different phases; (3) to examine various environmental/testing/theoretical conditions on characteristics of porous structure formation.

15217917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15217917.value: 交通運輸電氣化在減低化石燃料消耗和溫室氣體排放、以致實現生態交通和生態城市中，扮演著越來越重要的角色。要實現交通運輸電氣化、尤其是地面運輸電氣化的最大關鍵在於純電動車能否全面取代數十億輛傳統汽油車，這些汽油車所消耗的化石燃料佔了全球的34%，而它們的二氧化碳排放量更高達世界的40%。然而，目前最先進的可充电電池、即鋰離子電池，也只能把純電動車的驅動範圍提升至汽油車的三分之一左右，嚴重阻礙了純電動車的廣泛使用。 鋰氧電池巧妙地利用了大自然中最輕的鋰金屬作為陽極和第四輕的氧氣體作為陰極，自2009年以來一直被譽為可充電電池的「聖杯」。在放充電過程中，這個鋰氧組合在陰極表面分別進行可逆轉的氧還原反應和氧析出反應，能夠激發高出鋰離子電池3至5倍的實際比能，從而允許純電動車提升到與汽油車相近的驅動範圍。雖然鋰氧電池極具吸引力，但今天的它卻尚未準備好登上舞台的黄金时间，最大的障礙是一種名為「過氧化鋰」(Li2O2)的電絕緣放電產物在氧還原反應期間積聚在多孔陰極有限的表面上，由於在氧還原反應的積聚速度遠比在氧析出反應的分解速度快，導致多孔陰極快速鈍化、氧還原和析出反應以及電池循環壽命快速下降。 本研究針對實現長壽命可充電鋰氧電池，提出了一種新穎、有前途、有利於氧還原和析出反應、名為核/殼納米囊組裝中空結構(Core-Shell Nanocapsule-Assembled Hollow Architectures, CSNC@HA)的催化陰極材料。這種CSNC@HA催化陰極材料創新地結合了納米顆粒催化劑和有缺陷單層碳的強大優勢，形成了核/殼結構納米囊作為構件，继而組裝出具有大量電催化活性表面位點和高電子電導率的納米至微米尺度的三維中空結構(例如中空球體、中空籠等)，以增強和穩定氧還原和析出反應對Li2O2的鈍化。碳殼的固有缺陷和薄形態同時確保了氧的住处，允許了電催化，促進了電子傳導，並保護了催化納米顆粒核心免受粉碎和聚合。首先，我們將設計和合成各種有趣的CSNC@HA，並對其物理化學特性進行評估。然後，我們將製備CSNC@HA催化陰極和鋰氧測試電池，並通過操作、原位和非原位方法研究其電催化活性和穩定性。接著，我們將建立電化學放充電電壓與電容量模型，分析所觀察到的電催化活性和穩定性，以揭示根本的氧還原和析出反應機制。最後，我們將根據已優化/有特色的陰極/電池設計去展示和驗證具有特徵/特性的鋰氧電池原型。

15217917.label: Realisation of objectives
15217917.value: Although the project has experienced dramatic challenges from the 2019–20 Protests and the COVID-19 pandemic, it has been managed adequately in that all the three project objectives have been fully achieved with “7” journal publications and “2” journal submissions as the direct output, all with acknowledgment of the RGC funding. In addition, an MPhil student has been trained in the project period and graduated in September 2021. Two high-talented BEng students have been selected to gain research experience under “Provision of Research Experience for Undergraduate Students” during their final-year project period. An extensive research collaboration network has been established, both locally and non-locally. The scope of realization of the project objectives is summarized as follows: (1) In line with the project objectives 1–3 and following our initiative work and findings already stated in the proposal, Mn3O4 nanocapsule-assembled 3D mesoporous hollow nanocages were designed and synthesized as an emerging electrocatalyst for enabling novel electrocatalytic cathodes and their rechargeable Li–O2 batteries (LOBs) via a facile template-assisted growth process. The physicochemical properties and formation mechanism of the Mn3O4 hollow nanocages were studied, and the 3D mesoporous hollow nanocage morphology was formed by the loose agglomeration of many crystalline Mn3O4 nanoparticles of 25 nm mean diameter, giving a large mean diameter of 250 nm and a high specific surface area of 90.65 m2/g. The Mn3O4 hollow nanocages were combined with highly conductive Ketjenblack C to form novel electrocatalytic cathodes in nonaqueous LOB cells having a Li anode, a Whatman glass microfiber separator, and a LiTFSI/TEGDME electrolyte. An investigation into the electrocatalytic activity and stability of the LOB cells revealed a high and stable reversible restrained specific capacity of 600 mAh/g at a specific current of 400 mA/g even after 50 discharge–charge cycles due to the stabilization of O2 reduction reaction (ORR) and O2 evolution reaction (OER) during the discharge and charge processes by the presence of the good amount of Mn electrocatalytically active surface sites in the Mn3O4 hollow nanocages. An analysis of dead LOB cells was performed to understand how this hollow nanocage architecture provided a pathway for better diffusion of reactants and products, how it prevented the blockage of pores from solid-insulating Li2O2, and how it improved the cyclic stability of the LOB cells. The results have been published in “Nanomaterials” (Journal Paper #1). (2) Besides increasing the specific surface area of electrocatalysts for better stabilizing ORR–OER, the findings in (1) indicated the equal importance of simultaneously enhancing the electrocatalysts’ electronic conductivity for improving Li-ion and electron transports as well as improving their anti-pulverization ability for minimizing electrode material loss during ORR–OER. Accordingly, core@shell nanoarchitectures were proposed as new generation electrocatalysts. Because of the existence of magnetism in many metal and transition-metal-oxide ordinary electrocatalysts, there were unexplanatory crucial concerns about how an electromagnetic field could induce electromagnetism in the electrocatalysts and how it could affect the electrocatalytic activities and stabilities of the resulting cathodes and their LOB cells. A special research effort was put into the study of the electromagnetic properties of the core@shell nanoarchitectures in addition to their physiochemical properties and electrocatalytic performance. Therefore, six characteristic types of nanoarchitectured electrocatalysts were developed and analyzed to obtain an improved insight into the scientific and technological know-how. These included: (a) Ni@SiO2@PANI hexagonal nanoflakes with specific magnetization and polarization orientations; (b) Fe2B@C nanocapsules decorated with Fe@C nanocapsules; (c) Co3O4@LDH nanowire@nanosheet 3D networks on Ni foams; (d) FeSn2@onion-like C nanocapsules; (e) Graphene/MXene 3D porous hydrogels; and (f) C fibers with pyridinic-N-rich C layer modification and LDH nanosheet decoration. The results of (a) – (e) have been published in “Materials & Design” (Journal Paper #2), “IEEE Transactions on Magnetics” (Journal Paper #3), “Dalton Transactions” (Journal Paper #4), “Catalysts” (Journal Paper #5), and “APL Materials” (Journal Paper #6), while that of (f) submitted to the “Journal of Materials Science & Technology” (Journal Paper #7). (3) With the improved scientific and technological know-how acquired in (1) and (2), an advanced type of bifunctional electrocatalysts featuring core@shell-structured hierarchically porous MnO/CoMn2O4@N–C nanorods with interstitially decorated CoMn2O4 nanoparticles were synthesized via one-step carbonization of the metal–organic framework (MOF)-coated α˗manganese oxide (α-MnO2@ZIF-67) nanorods to exhibit a MnO nanorod core with CoMn2O4 nanoparticle interstitial decoration, both coated by an N-doped C (N–C) conductive shell. The MnO core rendered Mn active sites and O2 vacancies; the CoMn2O4 interstitial decoration gave additional Mn, Co active sites and enhanced the bifunctional electrocatalytic ORR–OER; the N–C shell increased electronic conductivity, hierarchical porosity, specific surface area, and protected the core and interstitial decoration against Li2O2 passivation. The MnO/CoMn2O4@N–C nanorods were evaluated as a novel bifunctional electrocatalytic cathode for LOB cells to improve the bifunctionality, specific discharge capacity, and cyclability of α˗MnO2 nanorod cathode-based LOB cells. The improved structural features allowed the MnO/CoMn2O4@N–C nanorod cathode-based LOB cells to exhibit superior full specific discharge capacity of 8,625 mAh/g and cyclability of 48 discharge–charge cycles at 200 mA/g specific current and 2,000 mAh/g limited specific discharge capacity compared to their α˗MnO2 nanorod counterparts. An ORR–OER mechanism was proposed to describe the interesting formation of particle- and film-type Li2O2 deposits at different cycles for the MnO/CoMn2O4@N–C nanorod cathodes. Such MOF-derived, interstitial nanoparticle-decorated nanoarchitectures can lead to high-performance tunable bifunctional electrocatalysts and energy storages. The results have been published in “Electrochimica” (Journal Paper #8). (4) Following the success in (3), another advanced type of bifunctional electrocatalysts featuring core@shell-structured mesoporous Mn3O4@C multi-hollow microspheres were synthesized via facial templateless synthesis of hybrid manganese oxide nanoparticle MnO2/Mn2O3 hollow microcages followed by one-step carbonization of the glucose-coated MnO2/Mn2O3 hollow microcages. The Mn3O4 multi-hollow microspherical core provided increased open paths for Li-ion and O2 mass transports. The C thin layered shell enhanced electronic conductivity for Li-ion and electron transports and protected the core from pulverization loss during ORR–OER. The Mn3O4@C multi-hollow microsphere cathode-based LOB cells exhibited outstanding initial specific discharge capacity of 3,677 mAh/g and cyclability of 66 discharge–charge cycles at 200 mA/g specific current and 500 mAh/g limited specific capacity, which were twice more than those of the MnO2/Mn2O3 hollow microcage cathode-based LOB cells. The postmortem investigations revealed the existence of higher reversible stability and stronger electrocatalytic activity in the Mn3O4@C multi-hollow microsphere cathode-based LOB cells. The density functional theory (DFT) calculations found higher adsorption energy for O2, LiO2, and Li2O2 on the surface of the Mn3O4@C multi-hollow microspheres than on the MnO2/Mn2O3 hollow microcages, leading to more favorable ORR activity. The results have been submitted to the “Journal of Materials Science & Technology” (Journal Paper #9).

15217917.label: Major findings and research outcome
15217917.value: A total of “9” good journal papers (7 published, 2 submitted) have been directly produced from this project [Part C: 8] to properly address the three project objectives [Part B: 5.2]. An MPhil student has been successfully trained and graduated [Part C: 10]. Two BEng students have been selected to gain research experience under “Provision of Research Experience for Undergraduate Students” [Part C: 11]. A solid research collaboration network has been effectively built [Part C: 11]. The major findings and research outcome are summarized as follows with reference to Part C: 8: (1) Journal Paper #1: This paper describes the design, synthesis, evaluation, and analysis of an emerging electrocatalyst of Mn3O4 nanocapsule-assembled 3D mesoporous hollow nanocages for enabling novel electrocatalytic cathodes and their rechargeable LOBs. It also gives the details of the physicochemical properties and formation mechanism of the Mn3O4 hollow nanocages, followed by an investigation into the electrocatalytic activity and stability of the LOB cells and a postmortem study of the dead cells to understand the underlying ORR–OER mechanisms. (2) Journal Papers #2 to #7: These 6 papers report the fundamental studies of 6 characteristically different nanoarchitectured electrocatalysts to obtain an improved scientific and technological know-how in simultaneously increasing their specific surface area for improving ORR–OER stabilization, their electronic conductivity for enhancing Li-ion and electron transports, and their anti-pulverization ability for minimizing electrode material loss during ORR–OER. A special research effort is put to study the influence of electromagnetic fields on the electromagnetic properties in addition to their physiochemical properties and electrocatalytic performance. (3) Journal Paper #8: With the improved scientific and technological know-how obtained in (1) and (2), this paper reports an advanced type of bifunctional electrocatalysts, featuring hierarchically porous MnO/CoMn2O4@N–C nanorods with CoMn2O4 nanoparticle interstitial decoration in the MnO@N–C core@shell structure, to improve the bifunctionality, specific discharge capacity, and cyclability in existing α˗MnO2 electrocatalytic cathodes and their LOB cells. A postmortem characterization is performed and an ORR–OER mechanism is proposed to elucidate the interesting formation of particle- and film-type Li2O2 deposits at different cycles. (4) Journal Paper #9: Following the success in (3), this paper discloses another advanced type of bifunctional electrocatalysts featuring core@shell-structured mesoporous Mn3O4@C multi-hollow microspheres. A postmortem investigation reveals superhigh reversible stability and electrocatalytic activity. The density functional theory (DFT) calculations show superhigh surface adsorption energy for O2, LiO2, and Li2O2, confirming the experimental observations and the presence of more favorable ORR activity.

15217917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15217917.value: The operation of LOBs is based on the reversible ORR–OER on the electrocatalytic cathode surface on discharge and charge, respectively, so the key issue in today’s LOBs is to develop energetically stable electrocatalysts and their cathodes to enhance and stabilize ORR–OER for simultaneously high specific capacity (and energy), low discharge–charge overpotentials, and long cycle life. It has been clearly shown in the present project that the critical obstacle to development is the rapid passivation of cathodes and hence the deterioration of ORR–OER by faster accumulating solid-insulating Li2O2 on their limited surface areas during ORR on discharge than decomposing Li2O2 during OER on charge. Considering also the importance of electrocatalytic stability, electronic conductivity, and structural stability, an “ideal” cathode should have five preconditions: (1) Large surface area for O2 accommodation and Li2O2 accumulation without passivation; (2) Suitable electrocatalyst for making ORR–OER energetically stable; (3) High electronic conductivity for improving Li-ion and electron transports; (4) Strong anti-pulverization ability for minimizing electrode material loss; and (5) Strong anti-aggregation ability for maximizing electrocatalytically active surface sites. In fact, this project aims to develop such an advanced class of electrocatalysts and their “ideal” cathodes for enabling long-life rechargeable LOBs. There exists great room for further development from materials and electrodes to devices and systems.

15217917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15217917.value: Studies on the design, synthesis, evaluation, and analysis of an advanced and emerging class of ORR–OER favorable electrocatalysts, featuring 1D to 3D core@shell porous hollow architectures, are carried out in this project to provide substantial amounts of electrocatalytically active surface sites and high electronic conductivity for enhancing and stabilizing ORR–OER against Li2O2 passivation as well as to protect the electrocatalytic core from pulverization and aggregation. Various experimental and computational methods are established to design and synthesize the electrocatalysts, evaluate their physicochemical properties, prepare their electrocatalytic cathodes and LOB test cells, study the electrocatalytic activities and stabilities, and reveal the underlying ORR–OER mechanisms. The research output of this project, including the nurtured research personals, the SCI journal publications, the scientific and technological know-how, the invented/developed materials, devices, and processes, etc., will serve as good references for the related communities. They are also likely to strengthen our research profile and find international markets and/or collaborations.
