15218017.label: Project Objectives
15218017.value: Improvement of the ray theory based EIWG model. A ray theory based EIWG model mainly consists of two parts: derivation of the reflection coefficient of the ionosphere, and determination of the transfer function for waves from source to receiver. In existing models, the reflection coefficient is derived based on the ODE method. The transform function is based on terms of phase integration along the wave path, wave diffraction of the ionosphere, and several window functions. Different treatments of these two parts may lead to different model accuracy. In this study, the transfer function may be modified by introducing such as the ionospheric focusing factor and transmitter and receiver factors to improve the model accuracy. The reflection coefficient may be based on the transfer matrix method. Coding and evaluation of the model. Verification of the model may be done in two ways. One is to simulate lightning sferics with presumed ionosphere parameters for different locations at different distances and times. Then the results may be compared with those in literature to check the model’s effectiveness. Another way is to apply the model to a specific lightning stroke to check the model accuracy, such as a rocket-triggered lightning stroke or a lightning stroke to tall tower, where the lightning currents and the corresponding sferics are recorded. Observation of Lightning Sferics. Observations of lightning sferics require specially designed antennas that can sense lightning VLF/LF waves at distances up to 1000 km. To do this, in collaboration with the University of Science and Technology of China, a Lightning Sferic Detection Network (LSDN) was firstly put in operation in 2012 in central China. Currently, the network consists of a central data analyzer and 6 stations separated at about 200 km, covering a from (115.5° E, 29.5°N) to (118.5°E, 33.5°N). It will be further updated to detect lightning sferics more efficiently. Application of the model to LSDN. After validation, the model may be implemented at the central data analyzer of LSDN to monitor the spatial and temporal variations of the lower ionosphere during thunderstorm season. For the same lightning stroke, its sferics may arrive at several LSDN stations through different paths, making it possible to monitor simultaneously the ionosphere state at different locations. Relationship between the ionosphere and various earth and space events. Successful application of the model to LSDN may produce huge data of the ionosphere state. The spatial and temporal properties of ionosphere state may be related to various earth and space events, which may lead to early warning of these events.

15218017.label: Realisation of objectives
15218017.value: This project aims to make improvements on the accuracy of the existing ray-theory-based model for studying the lightning electromagnetic pulse (LEMP) propagating in earth-ionosphere-waveguide (RT-EIWG), so that the model can perform a high resemblance to lightning sferics in both day and night times. There are five core tasks: (1) Improve the existing ray theory based EIWG model by introducing a modified transform function taking account the ionospheric focusing factor and the transmitting and receiving antenna factors; (2) Validate the improved model by both simulation and comparison with observation; (3) Carry out observations of lightning sferics in collaboration with the University of Science and Technology of China (USTC)by using with its Lightning Sferic Detection Network (LSDN) located in central China; (4) Apply the improved RT-EIWG model to LSDN to monitor the spatial and temporal variations of the lower ionosphere during thunderstorm season; (5) investigate the relationship between the ionosphere and various earth and space events by using the model developed and the data observed. To achieve these tasks, starting from January of 2018 to June of 2021, we have been carried our continuously field observations and numerous lightning data have been obtained and analyzed with the proposed model. Specifically, (a) Firstly, to improve the ray-theory-based EIWG model we proposed previously, further modifications has been made to increase its accuracy in modeling the lightning sferic in a broader frequency band and a larger distance range. The modification included two aspects: a new incident angle finding technique and a novel method for deriving the high-order hop series. To verify the effectiveness of this modified model, a comparative study of the model with its previous version and the full-wave finite-difference-time-domain model was carried out. The results showed that this modified model did better than its previous version and was in close agreement with the full-wave finite-difference-time-domain method in modeling the lightning sferic in frequencies bands lower to 3, 5, and 7 kHz for distances up to 500, 800, and 1,000 km, respectively. With these efforts, we have achieved 100% of Tasks (1) & (2). Details of these works were published in Journal of Geophysical Research-Atmosphere and presented at ICAE2018 respectively [Z. Qin, M. Chen, Steven A. Cummer, Y. Du, F. Lu. A ray-theory-based earth-ionosphere waveguide model for lightning sferics study and its comparison with the full-wave finite difference time domain model. XVI Int. Conf. on Atmos. Electricity (ICAE2018), 17-22 June 2018, Nara, Japan; Z. Qin, S. A. Cummer, M. Chen, F. Lyu, Y.-p. Du, (2019). A comparative study of the ray theory model with the finite difference time domain model for lightning sferic transmission in Earth‐ionosphere waveguide. Journal of Geophysical Research: Atmospheres, 124, 3335–3349. https://doi.org/10.1029/2018JD029440.] (b) Secondarily, to conduct lightning serferics, in collaboration with the USTC, we have obtained large number of lightning sferics in association with the distinct type of lightning events – NBEs with LSDN. With the method retrieving the virtual reflection height of the lower ionosphere we proposed and the NBEs data in two thunderstorms, variations of the lower ionosphere reflection height during sunset and sunrise time have been obtained and analyzed. With these efforts, we have achieved 100% of Tasks (3) & (4). Details of these works were published in Chinese Journal of Geophysics [F. Liu, Z. Qin, B. Zhu, M. Ma, M. Chen, P. Shen (2018). Observations of ionospheric D layer fluctuations during sunrise and sunset by using time domain waveforms of lightning narrow bipolar events. Chinese J. Geophys., 61(2), 484-493, https://doi.org/10.6038/cjg2018k0658.] (c) Thirdly, to look insight how the thunderstorm interacts with the upper atmosphere and lower ionosphere via a lightning discharge; we have analyzed a sequence of seven blue bolts emanating from an active thunderstorm over Lake Taihu in China. The analyses provided the first compelling evidence that the blue lightning bolts were closely related to NBEs of negative polarity inside the parent thunderstorms. This work enriched the insight of the relationship between the lower ionosphere, the blue bolts and the ordinary lightning discharges. With this effort, we have achieved 50% of Tasks (5). Details of the results were published in Geophysical Research Letter [F. Liu, B. Zhu, G. Lu, Z. Qin, … , M. Chen, et al. (2018). Observations of blue discharges associated with negative narrow bipolar events in active deep convection. Geophysical Research Letters, 45. https://doi.org/10.1002/2017GL076207.] (d) Lastly, to investigate how a lightning discharge pose impact on the ionosphere, we have statistically analyzed the skywave features of thousands of negative cloud-to-ground lightning strokes in southern China. It was found that skywave features of a lightning sferic are closely related to its source intensity. Every lightning stroke, regardless of intensity, has an impact on both daytime and nighttime lower ionosphere. Variations with increasing lightning intensity show a higher reflectivity from nighttime ionosphere but a larger time delay from daytime ionosphere. This suggests that there exists a direct and fast nonlinear coupling between lightning discharge and lower ionosphere, making the ionospheric response to a lightning discharge dependent of the lightning intensity. With this effort, we have achieved 100% of Tasks (5). Details of the results were published in Geophysical Research Letter [Qin, Z., Chen, M., Lyu, F., Cummer, S. A., Gao, Y., Liu, F., et al. (2020). Prima facie evidence of the fast impact of a lightning stroke on the lower ionosphere. Geophysical Research Letters, 47, e2020GL090274. https://doi.org/10.1029/2020GL090274.]

15218017.label: Major findings and research outcome
15218017.value: Firstly, we have succeeded in further modification of the RT-EIWG model we proposed previously, which have increased its accuracy in modeling the lightning sferic in a broader frequency band and a larger distance range. The modification included two aspects: a new incident angle finding technique and a novel method for deriving the high-order hop series. A comparative study with the full-wave finite-difference-time-domain model showed that this modified model did better than its previous version and was in close agreement with the full-wave finite-difference-time-domain method in modeling the lightning sferic in frequencies bands lower to 3, 5, and 7 kHz for distances up to 500, 800, and 1,000 km, respectively. (Ref.: Journal paper No. 3, https://doi.org/10.1029/2018JD029440). Secondly, the sferics of lightning NBEs data in two thunderstorms we observed, the variations of the lower ionosphere reflection height during sunset and sunrise time have been obtained and analyzed. The results showed that it is potential to monitor the lower ionosphere using not only the NBEs but also other type lightning sferics in real-time if a more accurate model is available. (Ref.: Journal paper No. 2, https://doi.org/10.6038/cjg2018k0658). Beside, a sequence of seven blue bolts emanating from an active thunderstorm have been were observed and analyzed with our proposed model. This work provided the first compelling evidence that the blue lightning bolts were closely associated with NBEs of negative polarity inside the parent thunderstorms. Detection of NBEs might provide a convenient approach to monitor the occurrence of blue bolts as the electrical coupling between thunderstorms and the lower ionosphere. (Ref.: Journal paper No.1, https://doi.org/10.1002/2017GL076207). Thirdly, we have statistically analyzed the skywave features of thousands of negative cloud-to-ground lightning strokes in southern China. The results show that skywave features of a lightning sferic are closely related to its source intensity. Every lightning stroke, regardless of intensity, has an impact on both daytime and nighttime lower ionosphere. Variations with increasing lightning intensity show a higher reflectivity from nighttime ionosphere but a larger time delay from daytime ionosphere. This suggests that there exists a direct and fast nonlinear coupling between lightning discharge and lower ionosphere, making the ionospheric response to a lightning discharge dependent of the lightning intensity. (Ref.: Journal paper No.4, https://doi.org/10.1029/2020GL090274).

15218017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15218017.value: By this project, we have proposed and demonstrated an accurate ray-theory-based (RT) earth-ionosphere-waveguide (EIWG) model. This model makes the lightning sferic an efficient tool to probe the lower ionosphere during both daytime and nighttime. The model may be used to detect not only the variation of electron densities of the ionosphere, but also the anomalous variation of geomagnetic field and neutral particle precipitation of the ionosphere. Furthermore, the variation of the ionosphere may be related to various earth and space events for forecast and mitigation of the event-related hazards. In addition, by the analysis of skywave features of thousands of cloud-to-ground lightning discharges, we found that every lightning stroke, regardless of intensity, has a fast impact on the lower ionosphere. Variations with increasing lightning intensity show a higher reflectivity from nighttime ionosphere but a larger time delay from daytime ionosphere. This suggests that there exists a direct and fast nonlinear coupling between lightning discharge and lower ionosphere.

15218017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15218017.value: The ionosphere may response to various earth and space activities like solar X-ray flux, earthquakes, and thunderstorms. Monitoring of the ionosphere is an important issue in earth and space science. Traditional technique for probing the ionosphere is to emit a series of pulse at different frequencies to the ionosphere and receives the reflections, which due to weak return signal level and background noise has a difficulty in probing the lower ionosphere where the electron density is extremely low. On the other side, lightning emits strong electromagnetic pulse at very low frequency and low frequency bands. By this project, we have proposed and demonstrated an accurate ray-theory-based-earth-ionosphere-waveguide model that makes the lightning sferic an efficient tool to probe the lower ionosphere during both daytime and night-time. The model can be used to detect not only the variation of electron densities of the ionosphere but also the anomalous variation of geomagnetic field and neutral particle precipitation of the ionosphere. Furthermore, the variation of the ionosphere can be related to various earth and space events for forecast and mitigation of the event-related hazard.

15218417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15218417.value: 空氣濕度過大嚴重影響人們的生活環境以及建築物材料的質 量，必須採用適當的除濕措施對空氣進行除濕處理以保證室內空 氣濕度符合要求。 冷凝除濕是目前較為常用的除濕技術，但該技術存在能耗過 大等問題。溶液除濕是近年來興起的新除濕技術，該技術具有環 保、能耗低等優點。 溶液除濕過程是復雜的傳熱傳質過程，傳質的驅動力為空氣 中水蒸氣分壓與除濕溶液表面飽和蒸汽壓之差。除濕劑採用臭化 鋰、氯化鋰等無機鹽或三甘醇等醇類物質。內冷型板式除濕器是 新穎的溶液除濕器，具有效率高等優點，但也存在著由於除濕劑 液膜收縮或破斷導致有效氣液接觸面積減小以及液滴攜帶等缺點 。本項目主要針對這些問題，提出採用二氧化鈦超親水塗層的方 案改善除濕器表面的潤濕特性，增大有效氣液接觸面積從而提高 除濕效率。研究結果表明二氧化鈦塗層可以有效地增大溶液的潤 濕面積從而提高了除濕器的除濕效率。

15218417.label: Realisation of objectives
15218417.value: For objective 1, the solid-liquid interaction effect between desiccant and plate surface was fully studied and the targets were well achieved. A 3D CFD simulation model was developed to study the factors that are correlated with the liquid desiccant dehumidification performance of a falling film dehumidifier. It was shown that smaller contact angles of desiccant corresponded to better wettability of falling film and dehumidification performance. Therefore, the super-hydrophilic coating could be applied on the plate surface to improve the wettability for better dehumidification performance. The effect of different surface properties on dehumidification performance was investigated. It was founded that surface wettability contributed positively to both wetting area of falling film and dehumidification performance. A novel semi-empirical correlation considering the surface free energy for mass transfer coefficient was developed based on aforementioned findings. Publication directly arising from this objective: Dong, C., Lu, L., & Wen, T. (2018). Investigating dehumidification performance of solar-assisted liquid desiccant dehumidifiers considering different surface properties. Energy, 164, 978-994. Tao, W., Yimo, L., & Lin, L. (2019). A novel 3D simulation model for investigating liquid desiccant dehumidification performance based on CFD technology. Applied energy, 240, 486-498. For objective 2, experimental studies were carried out to validate the findings in objective 1. The experimental results indicated that surface wettability demonstrated positive effect on dehumidification performance by increasing wetting area and reducing falling film thickness, which is consistent with the conclusions in objective 1. Experiments for testing the performance of plate liquid desiccant dehumidifier (PLDD) were also conducted. By comparing the experimental data with the CFD simulation results, it was shown that the 3D CFD model can reflect the inhomogeneous behavior of flow dehumidification from the falling film shrinkage on the dehumidifier, which was missing in traditional 2D models. Moreover, we developed several novel desiccants based on our findings in objectives 1 and 2. The first desiccant was a mixed liquid developed with LiCl, hydroxyethyl urea, and water. The experiment results showed that regeneration rate and the effectiveness of the new mixed solution both show slight improvement over conventional LiCl solution and empirical correlations in this study can provide meaningful guidance for the design of both regenerators and LDCSs. The second desiccant was a novel LiCl/H2O-MWNTs nanofluid, which is developed for falling film dehumidifier. The experimental data indicated that by adding MWNTs to LiCl solution, the dehumidification rate can be increased by over 25%, the wetting areas were increase, and the film thickness was notably reduced. Further, long-term operation performance of PLDD was investigated. We developed a novel mixed liquid desiccant, for which the corrodibility is much smaller than traditional desiccant, and as a result, it showed great potentials in improving the long-term performance of PLDD. Publication directly arising from this objective: Wen, T., Lu, L., Li, M., & Zhong, H. (2018). Comparative study of the regeneration characteristics of LiCl and a new mixed liquid desiccant solution. For objective 3, based on the findings of Objectives 1-2, a novel heat and mass transfer mathematical model for solid-liquid interaction in PLDD was developed. For the first time, we considered film shrinkage shape and vapor condensation in internally cooled liquid desiccant dehumidification. Moreover, we proposed a new Sherwood number correlation based on our experimental data. The novel mathematical model showed a high prediction accuracy by comparing the numerical results by the model and the experimental data, and it can well predict the desiccant flow patterns. Beyond the proposed objectives, we were pushing forward real applications of our current studies. we conducted review studies on the CFD technology on analyzing falling film heat/mass exchangers and on the fundamentals and investigations of falling film dehumidification/absorption refrigeration, which provided a comprehensive and meaningful guidance for the CFD simulation in various industry application fields. We conducted CFD simulation of liquid desiccant dehumidifier performance with different plates. It was suggested that the liquid film waves can significantly increase the contact area between the moist air and liquid desiccant, and the ribbed plate can significantly enhance dehumidification performance of PLDD. Last, the findings in the project were extended to other cross field including ground source heat pump and radiative cooling technologies, which involve sloid-liquid interaction, and heat and mass transfer. 15218417.label: Major findings and research outcome
15218417.value: In this project, the solid-liquid interaction effect in plate liquid desiccant dehumidifier was studied and the according heat and mass transfer enhancement methods were investigated. Some key findings and outputs are summarized as follows: On the aspect of theoretical study, a novel heat and mass transfer model considering solid-liquid interaction in PLDD was developed, in which we considered the effect of film shrinkage shape and vapor condensation. A novel semi-empirical correlation considering the surface free energy for mass transfer coefficient was developed. On the aspect of numerical study, a 3D CFD simulation model was developed to study the factors that are correlated with the liquid desiccant dehumidification performance of a falling film dehumidifier. It was revealed that the heat and mass transfer performance in PLDD was correlated with factors including surface free energy, surface wettability, contact angle, film thickness, air humidity and velocity, solution temperature and centration, etc. The effect of each factor on dehumidification performance was individually studied. It was founded that the application of bilayer superhydrophilic coating could improve the wettability and reduce the film thickness, and as a result the efficiency of the PLDD can be improved. On the aspect of experimental study, the findings and conclusions via theoretical and numerical studies were validated. A new Sherwood number correlation for the solid-liquid interaction in PLDD was proposed based on our experimental data. Three different formulae of liquid desiccant were developed. All of them have shown great advantages respectively in increasing regeneration rate and the effectiveness, increasing dehumidification rate, and decreasing corrodibility compared with traditional desiccants. Abundant research outcomes have been directly arisen from the present project. Totally, 14 high-quality journal papers have been published (please refer to Part C for the detailed information of these published papers), which include the journals of Applied Energy, Building and Environment, International journal of Heat and Mass et al. One PhD student was also supported by this project.

15218417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15218417.value: Heat and mass transfer involving solid-liquid interaction for PLDD was fully investigated in this project. Nevertheless, the surface fluctuation resulted from the liquid-gas interaction is also a significant factor for the modeling of falling film, which is rarely considered in present studies. The future study can be carried out to develop more accurate simulation model to clearly predict the surface waves and fluctuations. In our experiments, we observed that there exist both latent heat transfer in terms of phase change and sensible heat transfer in terms of convection in the phase interface. However, no study is found to explore the influence of convection on the whole transfer process even though it may only account for a very small proportion. Besides, the surface for the falling film flow is always treated as constant temperature constant heat flux. In the future, we aim to reflect these actual boundaries during simulation and conduct experiments for comparison. Most previous CFD simulations only concern the one-way mass transfer in falling film components. The reverse heat and mass transfer processed in PLDD should be investigated in the future study.

15218417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15218417.value: The heat and mass transfer mechanism in plate liquid desiccant dehumidifier (PLDD) is a complicated process for the reason that it involves interactions between different phases and can be influenced by many factors including plate surface characteristics, fluid velocity, desiccant concentration, etc. In this research, we successfully developed more accurate theoretical and CFD models compared to previous studies. We improved the performance of PLDD with the application of bilayer super-hydrophilic coating. We investigated and evaluated the factors that could influence the performance of heat and mass transfer in PLDD by both numerical and experimental studies. Based on our findings, we developed three desiccants that exhibit significant improvements in regeneration rate, effectiveness, and long-term performance. We conducted review works and summarized present studies on CFD technologies, and offered a comprehensive and meaningful guidance for the desiccant dehumidifier in various industry application fields. Further, we extended the conclusions and findings in this project to other cross-filed including CO2 absorption technologies, absorption cooling, radiative cooling, and ground source heat pump.

15218517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15218517.value: Renewable energy is crucial for sustainable economic development and environmental protection. Within all the renewable energy resources, solar energy plays a key role in solving the terawatt (TW) energy challenge the world is facing today, because of the abundance and ultimate environmental friendly nature. The pursuit of cost-effective and high performance solar photovoltaic technologies has attracted tremendous effort in the academic and industrial world, particularly in the past two decades. As a new solar cell technology, solution processed organic photovoltaic cells (OPVs) have distinct advantages in materials abundancy, low cost, roll-to-roll compatible fabrication, flexible, light weight form factor, tunable color and transparency etc. Significant progress in OPV has been achieved in the past decade, with the power conversion efficiency improved from 1-2% to 10-11% (single junction). The PI has been one of the leading researchers in the field. However, only a few preliminary publications reported to date touched on the surface of the MOST important limiting factor of OPV today – the photovoltage loss. The understanding and approaches to overcome the large loss is very far from reality at present stage. Based on the rich OPV research experience, we believe we are potentially at the edge of a breakthrough that finally address a missing piece that inhibit the fully potential of OPV technology. The objectives of the research are developing novel materials and approaches to significantly reducing the photovoltage loss in OPV devices. We propose two major directions to achieve our objectives – (1) new small molecule donors with (a) enlarged molecular dipole moment via main-chain, side-chain design, and (b) incorporate hetero/heavy atoms in the molecule structure; (2) introducing micro/nanostructure quasi-ordered bulk heterojunction (QO-BHJ) device concept to significantly reduce the donor/acceptor interface recombination to lower the photovoltage loss in OPV. The newly discovered high performance non-fullerene acceptors will also be incorporated into the project, and custom interface engineering will be investigated to pursue high efficiency. The success of the proposed research will provide critical information for the OPV research, offer guidance in material and device design, and enhance the overall solar cell performance to new milestone (13-15%). The proposed research represents a new front for OPV research, which integrates chemistry, physics and material science to generate new perspectives in science and offer solutions to challenging issues in renewable energy. It will also offer a broad spectrum of research and educational opportunities for students and postdocs. 可再生能源對於可持續經濟發展和環境保護至關重要。在所有可再生能源資源中，因為其能量豐富和最終的環保性質，太陽能在解決世界今天面臨的特瓦（TW）级能源挑戰方面發揮了關鍵作用。近二十年來，追求低成本和高性能的太陽能光伏技術已經引起了在學術界和工業界的巨大关注和研究发展。作為新型太陽能電池技術，溶液法制备處理的有機光伏電池（OPV）有其材料豐富，成本低，卷對卷兼容製造，靈活，重量輕，可調顏色和透明度等方面具有明顯的優勢。在過去十年中，OPV已有顯著進步，電力轉換效率從1-2％已提高到10-11％（單结电池） 本项目主持人也是該領域的世界領先研究員之一。然而，到目前為止僅有少數文章報導了OPV今天面臨的重要限制因素 - 光电压損耗的研究。克服光电压巨大損失的研究和解决方法还非常初步，與現階段的現實相差甚遠。基於豐富的OPV研究經驗，我們相信我們可能處於科技突破的邊緣，本研究计划的成功最終将解決一個阻礙OPV技術潛力的缺失部分。 本研究的目的是開發新的材料和方法來顯著降低OPV器件的光電壓損耗。我們提出兩個主要方向來實現我們的目標 - （1）新的小分子给體 - 在分子結構中引入雜/重原子; （2）引入微/納米結構準有序體異質結（QO-BHJ）器件概念，以顯著降低給体/受體界面複合，降低OPV中的光電壓損耗。新發現的高性能非富勒烯受体分子也將納入項目，并通过精心设计的界面工程進一步实现高效率有机太阳能电池。本研究计划的成果將為OPV研究提供重要信息，為材料和器件設計提供指導，並进一步提升整體有机太陽能電池效率到新的里程碑（13-15％）。本研究计划代表了OPV研究新的前沿，它將化學，物理和材料科學的研究进行整合并產生新的科技生长点，並為可再生能源中的挑戰性問題提供解決方案。本计划還將為學生和博士後提供廣泛的研究和教育機會。

The core of the proposal is reducing Voc loss to enhance device efficiency. The two objectives are: (1) new materials design, and (2) new device structure. We have synthesized quite a few new wideband polymers and small molecules, and explored ternary OPV concepts, including nano-morphology tuning and smart materials combinations – both polymer OSC and all small molecule OSCs. The progress covers objective 1 are fully accomplished. In objective 2, we successfully go beyond traditional bulk heterojunction (BHJ) OSC architecture, and achieved novel Graded BHJ (G-BHJ) solar cells with enhanced efficiency and processibility. This work has been published on Nature Communications, and moreover, the new structure has clear advantages in further OSC device structure manipulation, fabrication, and even photodetector/sensing devices with reduced dark current. We have started new research in these new fronts, inspired by the research output of this GRF project The Voc loss goal of 0.55 eV was almost reached in the midterm report, with the Voc loss 0.55eV in our publication (1 below). The achieved 10.8% solar cell efficiency is below the project target of 13%. In 2020, we achieved polymer OSCs with efficiency over 16%, and small molecule OSCs of 14.7% efficiency already. In 2021, we boosted the OSC performance to 17.5%, and most recently 18.9%. In addition to high efficiency, these works in deed demonstrated lowered Voc Loss that just slightly above 0.5 eV. The impact of this project research will also significantly help the development of unique solar applications including flexible, wearable, transparent and colorful solar energy harvesting devices. We have been working hard in the past 12 months after the completion of this GRF proposal, continuously advancing the OSC technology. We are developing new morphology manipulation approaches, new materials - both active layer and interfacial layer, and novel electrodes for transparent OSCs. We have excelled beyond the GRF results by achieving (1) certified 19% OSC, and (2) record efficiency and FOM - Light Utilization Efficiency (LUE) in transparent OSCs (under review). 15218517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15218517.value: Energy is one of the greatest challenges our Planet is facing, and so is environmental sustainability. Today, over 85% of the world energy requirements comes from non-renewable fossil fuels – oil, coal, with concealed consequences on health and the environment - the greenhouse gas emissions, climate change and environmental pollution. Moreover, the global energy demand is predicted to double by 2050, therefore, technology progress through engineer novel materials to provide efficient and sustainable energy is imperative. Solar energy is the ultimate renewable energy source due to its abundance and clean manner. However, wider implementation of the solar energy harvesting is hampered by the cost of the solar cells and installation. Printable solar cells like Organic polymer solar cells (OPVs) have the potential for lower cost solar energy generation and easier installation, as well as new application areas such as flexible/portable PV for portable electronics, building integrated PV & transparent window etc. In this GRF project, we successfully delivered all the objectives and achieved high efficiency printable solar cells reaching ~19% (well above the 13% goal). New materials, new semiconductor layer formation control and new device process are the key to the success. The GRF project further inspired our new exploration leading to ~24% perovskite solar cells. More exciting results towards 20% printable OSC, and >15% transparent OSCs are highly expected in the near future and will contribute to our life.

15219217.label: Project Objectives
15219217.value: Contactless to contact based fingerprint matching: The key objective of this project is to develop fundamental operators and algorithms for accurate matching of fingerprints when images from the same fingers are acquired using contact-based and contactless fingerprint sensors. Novel algorithms to significantly enhance interoperability of contactless fingerprint images will incorporate (a) significantly increased useful fingerprint image area by correcting perspective distortion; (b) valleys, in addition to ridges, that bring additional information; and (c) significantly advanced capabilities for detecting/correcting the fingerprint deformations. Identification and matching of contactless biometrics features under known imaging setups: A key objective of this project is to identify discriminant feature descriptors that can be efficiently recovered from a single 2D image acquired under known contactless imaging setup. Projective nature of real-world contactless imaging setups will be thoroughly investigated to develop novel feature descriptors and efficient matching strategies.

15219217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15219217.value: 为了有效保护国家边界安全以及合理支持国家电子政务项目，各界相关人士已经开发构建了包含数十亿张接触式指纹图像的大型数据库。这些数据通过传统的生物识别传感器获取，例如通过手指滚动或者按压采样器表面（由玻璃或者聚合物构成），但是由于皮肤的形变，滑动，表面的污迹以及采样器表面残留指纹印记的影响，导致获得的图像质量不高，无法用于准确有效的指纹信息验证。非接触式的指纹采集系统的出现为上述问题提供了有效的解决方案。由于非接触性指纹图像中含有更丰富的个人信息，这种基于非接触性生物特征识别的指纹采集系统将很有可能提供更加准确有效的个人识别。 然而这种非接触式生物识别技术的应用却存在以下几个方面的障碍：1）缺乏能够将非接触式指纹图像与接触式指纹图像精确匹配的数据库和2）缺乏准确模拟人体皮肤的模型，从而准确有效地恢复匹配非接触式生物特征。本项目的目标是突破非接触生物识别技术中的障碍，以实现其在现实生活中更快更好的应用。 本项目的主要目标有以下三个方面：（1）通过深入探究不同生物感知系统的特性差异，设计和研发一项基础技术，用于增强非接触式指纹识别技术与已有接触式指纹数据库的互操作能力。无接触式指纹图像中细节特征的扭曲主要来源于视角的扭曲。开发先进的模型技术来检测和矫正这种扭曲不仅可以提高非接触式指纹与接触式指纹图像的匹配精度，同时还可以增强二者之间的互操作性。（2）人体皮肤是一种透光材料，具有多重散射和镜面反射的特性，而线性成像模型并不足以模拟人体皮肤的特性。因此本项目的另一大挑战是设计创新的理论模型，准确模拟人体皮肤的特性，进而有效地从2D非接触式指纹图像中恢复得到丰富的生物特征。（3）最后，传统生物识别的图像描述子无法恢复得到识别对象的表面形状信息，主要因为它们缺乏对部署的非接触式成像模型的考虑。本项目计划研发这样一种图像描述子，通过充分考虑2D成像的投影性质，从而实现更加准确，更加快速的个人识别。 我们的初步实验取到了很好的效果，验证了该项目的潜力和可行性。其中，在非接触式生物识别技术方面的突破对于该项目的成功至关重要。本项目出现地非常及时，将大大提高新兴非接触式生物识别技术的准确性以及可接受程度，从而在民生以及医学领域中得到更好的应用。

15219217.label: Major findings and research outcome
15219217.value: This research project has developed novel algorithms for more accurate contactless fingerprint and cross-fingerprint matching capabilities. A key finding from this research relates to the need for accurate estimation of the presented fingers during contactless fingerprint identification. In this context this research introduced a three-stage pose compensation framework, based on the ellipsoid model, to address the pose-invariant contactless fingerprint identification problem. Another finding from this project relates to the extraction of minutiae features from contactless fingerprints and a new approach introduced from this research suggests that a deep network-based method can robustly recover contactless minutiae as compared to conventional methods available in the existing literature. Research from this project has also enabled the most accurate contactless-to-contact-based fingerprint identification using a specially designed network and a loss to train such a network. Our research effort to recover 3d feature descriptors, using a localized difference of surface normal computations, was quite successful to advance biometric identification capabilities and is another important finding from this research. One of the other key findings from this project related to the uniqueness of 3D finger knuckle features and this can be exploited to enable highly accurate contactless finger-based personal identification. The use of surface normal vectors, instead of recovering the depth information using computationally complex operations, can offer an efficient alternative for contactless 3D finger-knuckle pattern matching. Extraction of surface key points is another simplified alternative to match 3D fingers using their knuckle patterns. It is highly desirable to characterize the uniqueness of 3D finger knuckle patterns or estimate the probability that two persons can have substantially similar 3D finger knuckle patterns in a given population. Our research has revealed that the probability of false random correspondence for 3D finger knuckle patterns is very small, which indicates high uniqueness in the finger knuckle patterns, and this probability is much smaller than estimated for the popular fingerprints in the existing literature.

15219217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15219217.value: During the last few years, there has been increasing demand for contactless fingerprint identification capabilities, especially due to the hygienic concerns emerging from the pandemic like COVID-19. This project has significantly enhanced the contactless and contactless-to-contact-based fingerprint identification capabilities available today. However, the achievable performance and error rates are still below the expectations for their actual deployment in any large-scale real-world applications. Therefore, there is a need for further research in this area. One of the key challenges in advancing contactless fingerprint identification capabilities is the lack of availability of large-scale public databases in the public domain and such sharing is further challenged by privacy concerns and recent government regulations. Therefore, further extension of this research should develop novel capabilities to synthesize multi-view contactless fingerprint databases, and along with the precise minutiae of ground truth. We will submit a new research proposal that is built from the strengths of achievements from this research and addresses open research problems to achieve a significant reduction in the error rates to enable wide deployment of contactless fingerprint-based identification.

15219217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15219217.value: Millions of contact-based fingerprint images have been acquired and routinely used for e-governance applications and to protect national borders. These databases have been acquired using legacy fingerprint sensors when the users are required to press their fingers against the sensing surface. Contactless fingerprint systems have emerged to provide improved hygiene and address other limitations of contact-based fingerprint systems. This project has introduced significant advances in realizing such highly accurate contactless fingerprint identification capabilities. This project developed new theoretical models to estimate the pose of presented contactless fingerprints and developed algorithms to utilize pose compensation mechanisms to significantly enhance contactless fingerprint match accuracy available today. Advanced capabilities to recover 3d features from contactless finger images acquired under a fixed and known illumination, is a significant advancement towards realizing the development of contactless 3D fingerprint identification using a single 2D fingerprint image in near future. This research project also introduced advanced capabilities to recover and match ancillary biometric features from contactless fingers. In this context, for the first time, the reconstruction of 3D finger knuckle patterns and the capabilities to match them accurately for biometric identification was introduced in this project. This project also presented a theoretical estimation of the uniqueness of 3D finger knuckle patterns for the human population.

15219517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15219517.value: The recent rapid development of high-speed rail (HSR) in Northeast Asia and other parts of the world has caused more dynamics in the air transport sector. As being claimed to be greener than air transport and able to mitigate airport congestion, HSR has been advocated by many policy makers to substitute air transport in short-haul markets so as to feed airlines’ long-haul or international routes. However, as adding frequency is important in the competition between scheduled transportation services, the entry of HSR may cause more flights and hence more emissions in certain air routes. In addition, airport congestion mitigation may not be achieved since HSR can expand an airport’s catchment while increasing the overlap of catchment areas with other airports. The consequent intensified airport competition may enhance large airports’ attractiveness and result in more congestion at these airports. This study models the competition and cooperation between airlines and HSR and examines the potential impacts on air transport due to the entry of HSR. A series of analytical models will be built by incorporating important features ignored in the air-HSR interaction literature, such as heterogeneous passenger values of time, the role of price competition, HSR catchment expansion effects, airport competition and airlines’ competition in offering more destinations from their hub airports. The objective of these models is to theoretically analyze the competition, welfare and environment impacts of introducing HSR. Numerical simulations based on real life cases will be conducted to validate the theoretical predictions. As the HSR network evolves, its network structure as well as individual airports’ location within the HSR network change over time. This could have differential impacts and implications on individual airports’ competitiveness. Such potential network-related impacts will be explored empirically by applying the complex network theories and regression analysis in comparing three HSR networks in Northeast Asian countries, namely China, Japan and South Korea. 近年來，高速鐵路（高鐵）在東北亞和世界其他地區快速發展，給航空業帶來了更多變數。高鐵被認為比飛機更綠色環保並且可以減輕機場的交通擁擠。因此，許多政策制定者推崇用高鐵來替代飛機以完成短途線路的旅客運輸並且為航空公司的長途和國際航線提供接駁服務。然而，提供定期服務的兩種交通模式往往會通過增加班次來競爭，所以高鐵的介入可能會使得航空公司在某些航線增加航班的次數，從而增加溫室氣體排放。此外，高鐵未必能有效減輕機場擁擠。這是因為，高鐵的運營能夠擴大機場的客源範圍，導致鄰近機場的服務範圍相重疊，增加機場間的競爭。在這樣的競爭中，對乘客來說，大型樞紐機場可能比小機場更有吸引力，使得大機場變得更加擁擠。本研究模擬航空公司和高鐵的競爭與合作。我們將通過建立一系列的理論模型，把被文獻忽視的幾個重要特徵納入對航空與高鐵互動關係的研究。這些特徵包括乘客的時間價值差異，價格競爭，高鐵的機場客源擴大效應，機場競爭，航空公司利用樞紐機場增加航點等。通過這些模型，我們首先從理論上分析開通高鐵對競爭、社會福利及環境的影響。然後，將基於現實案例進行數值模擬，從而驗證理論預測。由於高鐵變得更加網絡化，我們將探索高鐵的網絡結構以及個體機場在高鐵網絡中的位置是否會影響機場的競爭力。為達到這一目的，我們將運用複雜網絡理論和回歸分析對中國，日本和韓國三個不同的高鐵網絡經行實證分析和比較。

15219517.label: Realisation of objectives
15219517.value: All the project objectives have been very well achieved. The detailed information about each objective is provided below. Objective 1: We constructed game-theoretic models of airline-HSR duopolistic competition to theoretically demonstrate and explain how and why air traffic may increase or decrease after the entry of HSR. The base case involves a city-pair market without catchment expansion. We first replicated the findings from the literature (i.e. both air fare and air traffic would drop after HSR entry) by assuming quantity competition, a common assumption in the literature. Then, we derived new findings that air traffic may increase or decrease while air fare will drop by assuming differentiated price competition. We further demonstrated that airline’s perceived demand function under price competition leads to the mixed equilibrium outcomes. We also proved mathematically that such air traffic increase is associated with the rail-air travel time difference. The base case model was then extended to incorporate a network of three cities such that HSR can feed traffic from the third city to the air route, a case of catchment expansion by using air-HSR intermodal service. This extension adds complexity to the issue and provides much richer results. For example, we showed that in addition to the substitution effect mentioned above, air traffic might increase while air fare might increase if the HSR feeding effect (complementary effect) is sufficiently strong. Our model provides a way to explain and reconcile mixed empirical findings and hence provides a better understanding on air-rail interaction than the other theoretical models in the literature. Objective 2: Following the new theoretical model developed in Objective 1, we empirically tested our theoretical prediction and quantified the impacts of HSR entry on air fare, air traffic and carbon emissions in the context of China. We used route-level air flight data extracted from OAG schedule analyzer and IATA Airport Intelligence Services database and HSR-related data from China’s HSR timetables. The main purpose of the empirical estimation is to show how air fare adjustment channels the possible increase in air traffic, despite the entry of a competing HSR service. The econometric specification includes a series of three equations. The first equation uses route-level air passenger number as the dependent variable and a set of dummies indicating different levels of rail-air travel time difference (TTD dummies), air fare, and number of HSR feeding cities as main variable of interest, together with other control variables. The second equation removes the air fare from the first equation. The third equation uses air fare as the dependent variable while rail-air travel time difference and number of HSR feeding cities as independent variables. The difference of the estimated coefficients of HSR-related variables between the first and second equations can be considered as the evidence that air fare adjustment plays a role in HSR’s impact on air traffic. The amount of HSR-induced air traffic impact via the change of air fare could be quantified by using the coefficients in the first and third equations. After estimating the equations with our data, we found that the coefficients of TTD dummies in the traffic equation are substantially reduced after controlling for air fare, suggesting that a large amount of air traffic change discovered in the literature is contributed by the adjustment in air fare, which is entirely ignored in the literature. In general, we found post-entry airfare reduction mitigates the negative impact of HSR on air traffic by half on routes with TTD around 3-5 hours and leads to an increase in air traffic on routes with TTD around 5-9 hours. We also found air-HSR intermodal service is another major booster of air traffic. We then explored the heterogeneous impacts stemmed from pre-entry competition intensity. Using the estimated models, we quantified the changes in air flights’ CO2 emissions and the amount of emission changes driven by airfare adjustment, and then decomposed the total air flights’ emission changes into three sources, i.e. competition effect, feeding effect and long-term effect. However, due to the unavailability of HSR traffic and price data as well as route-level operating cost data, we are not able to provide an overall assessment of welfare and CO2 emission impacts by summing up the emissions and welfare generated from both air transport and HSR. Objective 3: We first refined the measures of an airport city’s location in the HSR network. While the traditional approach is based on railway infrastructure data, we used HSR service timetable data. This allows us using daily service frequency and generalized travel time to develop weighted degree, betweenness and harmonic centralities to measure, respectively, a city’s connectivity, transitivity and accessibility. Using these new centrality indicators, we conducted two empirical studies with a panel data from China and Japan. In the first study, we regressed airport-level domestic, international and total passenger traffic on HSR connectivity, HSR accessibility, linkage between airport and HSR stations as well as a number of interactive terms. We identified different results between hub and non-hub airports, as a clue for potential air traffic redistribution effect of HSR. The main finding is that airport traffic does not necessarily reduce and the traffic inequality between hub and non-hub airports can be enlarged after the development of HSR, implying that HSR could worsen the congestion at large and busy airports. Unlike the case in Japan, good airport-HSR station connection seems ineffective in helping non-hub airports in China to grow traffic and alleviate congestion at busy airports. In the second study, we evaluated the impacts on airports’ technical efficiency by adopting both the standard two-stage Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) and double bootstrap method, and then evaluated the effects of HSR on airport labor productivity. We found that HSR connectivity and accessibility relate to a decline in airport efficiency. In China, air-HSR intermodal service associates with an improvement in airport efficiency, but the locational advantage of HSR station relative to airports associates with a decline in airport efficiency. Objective 4: We provided detailed policy discussion in each major output (in the form of journal articles) of the above three research objectives. In addition, combining our findings from these objectives and a thorough literature survey, we derived a clearer picture on major findings and issues related to the impacts of HSR on air transport, environment and regional economic development, and then came up with a policy paper. In the paper, we provide in-depth discussion on how HSR can affect airport congestion and redistribute air traffic, its unclear role in mitigating or raising inequality in economic development, as well as various issues which should not be ignored when arguing for HSR’s effectiveness of reducing emissions. Inspired by the findings that HSR development could increase regional disparity in airport traffic and economic development, we assessed the disparity of HSR development among cities in different regions, of different sizes, and in different megalopolises by calculating Theil’s T indices on centrality measures developed under objective 3. This study sheds light on the regional disparity from the viewpoint of provision of HSR services and pave the way for a better understanding of the HSR impact on regional economy and echoed our findings on HSR’s impact on airports.

15219517.label: Major findings and research outcome
15219517.value: The project generated several major findings and six research papers among which five have already been published. First, we show the idea of cutting air traffic and reducing CO2 emissions by developing HSR and introducing air-HSR competition may not be as promising as expected, esp. when the HSR network provides long HSR rides. When introducing new HSR services, policy makers should consider rail-air travel time difference, pre-entry market power of airlines and HSR’s feeding effects. Another highlighted finding is the importance of understanding airlines’ reaction in ticket price and its mediation effects on air traffic. We developed two papers with these findings. Gu and Wan (2020), which is published in Transport Policy, developed the theoretical models and propositions. Then, Gu and Wan (2022) tested these theoretical predictions with data from China and provided more comprehensive assessment and policy discussion on the impacts on air traffic, air fare and CO2 emissions. This second paper was submitted to Transportation Research Part A and is now under revision for the second-round review. Second, we question the claim that HSR can mitigate congestion at busy airports and improve airport productivity. Rather, we find a possible increase in congestion at busy airports together with an increased difficulty of small airports to attract traffic and recover their costs. While air-HSR integration may boost airport efficiency, it is not effective in diverting air traffic from congested airports to less congested regional airports. These findings generated two papers. Liu et al. (2019), which is published in Transportation Research Part A, contains the findings about the impact on airport traffic and congestion. Liu, Wan and Zhang (2021) covers findings about the impact on airport efficiency and is published in Transport Policy. Third, applying the modified centrality measures in objective 3, we find in China small/medium-sized cities not belonging to any major city cluster are further lagged behind in HSR development. Plus, non-core cities are increasingly relying on core cities to access other regions. This finding echoes the view that HSR could worsen regional disparity and forms another paper, i.e. Liu, Wan and Zhang (2020) published in Transportation Research Part A. Finally, combining findings from objective 3 and extensive literature review, Zhang, Wan and Yang (2019), which has been published in Transport Policy, provides well-rounded discussion on policy and environmental issues associated with air-HSR competition, spatial redistribution of airport traffic, and HSR’s impacts on economic development.

15219517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15219517.value: Due to the unavailability of HSR traffic and price data as well as route-level operating cost data, our empirical analysis focuses on the reactions of air transport, such as how air traffic, air fare, airport productivity and CO2 emissions of airlines changed due to the development of HSR. This issue also makes it impossible to provide an overall assessment of welfare and emission impacts of HSR as welfare and emission reduction due to reduced air traffic could be captured (fully or partially) by the growth of HSR traffic due to the substitution effect. Moreover, even if HSR traffic data is available, it is not straightforward to merely investigate HSR and air transport without considering other ground modes, such as conventional rails. Thus, there is room for further study on these aspects in the future.

15219517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15219517.value: As being claimed to be greener than air transport and able to mitigate airport congestion, HSR has been advocated by many policy makers to substitute air transport in short-haul markets so as to feed airlines’ long-haul or international routes. However, it is unknown whether such claimed benefit of HSR can be realized as the reaction of air transport to HSR’s entry is not straightforward. An increase in air traffic was observed in certain air routes after the entry of HSR, implying a potential increase in emissions in those cases. In addition, HSR can expand an airport’s catchment and enhance large airports’ attractiveness, resulting in more congestion at busy airports. In this project, to derive theories to explain the mixed empirical findings in the literature, we built analytical models which incorporate important features ignored in the air-HSR interaction literature. These theories were then tested with real-life data. We provided scientific evidence that the development of HSR can increase the disparity between large and small airports in China, making the former more congested. Besides, CO2 emissions from airlines in our sampled routes can increase due to HSR’s feeding and air fare reduction.

15219917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15219917.value: Recent on-demand services, such as Uber and GoGoVan in Hong Kong, provide a platform for users to request services on the spot and for suppliers to meet such demand. Uber, for example, allows its users to call for taxies on demand through mobile apps. The demand is dispatched by Uber to the drivers, who decide whether or not to accept them. If multiple drivers are willing to serve, the order will be assigned to one of them according to pre-established policies. Future energy systems can also be considered as on-demand services, as multiple suppliers, including power stations, energy stores, and mobile charging stations, compete to satisfy energy demand from their customers. In this project, we study the fundamental problem of demand dispatching in these emerging on-demand services, with the objective of maximizing supplier profits and saving user costs. Our research is novel in both the problem itself and the proposed solution approach. To the best of our knowledge, no work on demand dispatching has been reported in the specific context of on-demand services. In traditional supply and demand systems, the service directly assigns a request to a particular supplier, and assumes that the supplier must accept it. In on-demand services, in contrast, the suppliers are autonomous in deciding whether to accept the request, and a request is usually dispatched to multiple suppliers in order to be answered in a shorter period of time or with a lower cost. Also, both the demand and supplies vary over space and time. We need to address these new challenges for on-demand services. In this project, we will design scheduling policies and dispatching algorithms that optimize user costs and supplier profits. Due to the autonomy of the suppliers, traditional optimization approaches are no longer applicable. We will propose an alternative data-driven approach, the upshot of which is that the time-varying pattern of the supply-demand distribution and the pattern of suppliers in accepting user demand can be automatically predicted using historical service data, and such predictions will be used by our online algorithms to optimize demand dispatching in terms of response times and service costs. One highlight of this project is its focus on real-world scenarios in the GoGoVan system, an online logistic platform providing shipping services to customers in Hong Kong. This project will deliver both theoretical advances beyond existing work in the academic literature, and practical values with a tangible impact in the on-demand service industry. 近年來，包括Uber和GoGoVan在內的新興按需服務提供了一個平台。通過該平台上，用戶可以即時發出服務請求，服務提供者則可以滿足這些服務請求。例如，Uber用戶可以通過移動應用程式呼叫按需的出租車服務。Uber將這些訂單需求分配給司機，由司機決定是否接受所分配的訂單。當多個司機願意接受訂單時，訂單則根據預定義的策略進行分配。未來的能源系統也可以視為按需服務，包括發電廠、能源商店和移動充電站在內的服務提供者共同競爭滿足客戶的能源需求。 在本項目中，我們將研究這些新興按需服務中最基本的分配問題，旨在最大化服務提供者的收益，同時為用戶節省開銷。項目的新穎性體現在問題本身和所提出的解決方案。 據我們所知，目前還沒有針對按需服務這一特定領域中需求分配的研究。在傳統的供需系統中，服務需求直接指派給特定的服務提供者，並假定服務提供者必須接受該分配。在按需服務中，服務提供者則可以自主決定是否接受分配的服務請求。通常，為了確保服務請求可以在短時間內或者以較小的開銷被響應，服務請求將被同時分配給多個服務提供者。 在本項目中，我們將設計調度策略和分配算法，從而優化用戶的開銷和服務提供者的收益。由于服務提供者具有自主性，傳統的優化方法難以適用。因此，我們提供了數據驅動的方法，旨在利用曆史服務數據發掘供需分布的時變模式和服務提供者接受用戶請求的行為模式，進而利用這些知識優化需求分配中的響應時間和服務開銷。 本項目的亮點之一在于著眼于真實的應用場景，即GoGoVan系統。GoGoVan是一個位于香港的物流平台，為用戶提供貨物運輸服務。本項目的研究將實現對現有研究工作的理論創新，並對按需服務産業産生實質性的影響。

15219917.label: Realisation of objectives
15219917.value: We have finished the main objectives listed in the proposal, which is elaborated as below. For the 1st objective, i.e., “to investigate and study the new requirements of demand dispatching for on-demand services; especially to identify the challenges arising from the autonomy of suppliers and dynamic demands and supplies, to develop new system models and to formulate new problems”, we have deeply investigated the new requirements of demand dispatching for on-demand services, and reviewed the related studies. The challenges arising from the autonomy of suppliers and dynamic demands and supplies have also been identified. We have developed new system models to provide an effective solution to on-demand order dispatching and formulate multiple new problems arising from on-demand services, including demand prediction, driver behavior pattern discovery, and many-to-many order dispatching. The outputs of these studies have been published in [J2019a][J2019b]. The 2nd and 3rd objectives aim to develop new methods for analyzing historical data, discover the supplier's response patterns to the demands and the patterns of the demand and supplies' variation, and design algorithms that use the patterns for the optimization of the demand dispatching. To achieve this end, we made achievements in four aspects, i.e., embedded feature learning, dynamic demand prediction, driver behavior pattern discovery and reinforcement learning-based order dispatching. (1) Embedded feature learning: One critical task for data-driven approaches is to learn good representations, i.e., features, for data from different sources. The learned features are then used for training decision making models. Therefore, we proposed different feature learning techniques [J2020a][ C2018a][C2018b][C2018c] to effectively learn representative features from those data sets that are related to the studied issues. First, to learn feature representations for nodes in network data (e.g., road network), we propose to embed not only the network structure, but also the interaction content within which each interaction arises. Second, we proposed a new method to learn low-dimensional and dense representations for data records, which can reduce the complexity of learning models. Third, to address cold-start issue, we propose to learn application-specific similarity metrics by proposing a weighted formulation of metric learning model. (2) Dynamic demand prediction: On-demand services usually face the dilemma of demand-supply imbalance, meaning that the spatial distributions of orders and drivers are imbalanced. Due to such imbalance, much supply resource is wasted while a considerable amount of order demand cannot be met in time. To address this dilemma, knowing the unmet demand in near future is of high importance for service providers because they can dispatch their vehicles in advance to alleviate the impending demand-supply imbalance. Therefore, we develop a general framework for predicting the unmet demand in future time slots[J2019b]. Under this framework, we extract both static and dynamic urban features relevant to unmet demand from datasets in multiple domains. Then, multiple prediction models are trained to predict unmet demand by using the extracted features. As demonstrated via experiments, the proposed framework can predict unmet demand in on-demand services effectively and flexibly. In addition, for the total demand prediction, we proposed a data driven approach for demand inference[J2020b]. We first estimate the demands in some regions and time intervals from a small number of observed historical orders directly, and then use them as seeds to infer the region-level order demands of an entire city. Specifically, we formulate this problem as a matrix completion task by modelling the demand as a matrix whose two dimensions are time intervals of a day and regions of a city respectively. We also incorporate the spatial-temporal correlations and some constraints into a joint optimization framework. According to experimental evaluation, the proposed model achieves good performance in predicting demand. (3) Driver behavior pattern discovery: With a good understanding of driver behavior, we can dispatch orders based on drivers’ preferences, thus reducing the order cancel rate. To this end, we aim to predict how long it will take for one order to be accepted by certain drivers. Concretely, the order response time on current day is predicted by fusing data from order history and driver historical locations. We propose Coupled Sparse Matrix Factorization (CSMF) to deal with the heterogeneous fusion and data sparsity challenges. CSMF jointly learns from multiple heterogeneous sparse data through the proposed weight setting mechanism therein. Compared with various baseline methods via experiments on real-world datasets, our approach achieves much better performance. The performance of multiple variants of the proposed method is also presented to show the effectiveness of each component. (4) Reinforcement learning-based order dispatching: The demands for on-demand services are usually dispatched to suppliers round by round, and suppliers have autonomy to decide whether to accept demands or not. Existing approaches dispatch a demand to multiple suppliers in each round, while a supplier can only receive one demand. However, by using these approaches, pended demands cannot be fully dispatched in a round specially when suppliers are not enough, and thus need to wait for many rounds to be dispatched, leading to long response time. In this work, we propose a many-to-many demand dispatching model[J2019a]. The novelty of the model is that a supplier could receive multiple demands in a round, such that the demand has high chance to be dispatched and answered within short time. More specifically, we first learn the probability distribution function of the response rime of a supplier to a given demand, by considering the features of both the demand and the supplier. Taking the learned results as input, our model generates an optimal matching between the demands and suppliers to minimize the overall response time of the demands via solving an optimization problem. Experiments on real-world datasets show that our model is better than the start-of-art models in terms of successful acceptance rate and response time. (5) Other achievements: We also studied user’s behavior and urban traffic which have big impacts on demand dispatching[J2018][C2018d][C2020]. For user’s behavior, we proposed a group detection system to discover those users that are of high probability to be in one group. With this technique, we can design more informed ride-sharing mechanisms. For urban traffic prediction, we propose a network-scale deep traffic prediction model called GCGAN[C2019] by combining adversarial training and graph CNN. To fully capture the spatial correlations among the road segments of a transportation network, we propose to apply a graph convolution network (GCN) in both generator and discriminator of GCGAN for feature learning. With a better prediction for traffic, we can optimize the route planning for drivers and improve the efficiency of order serving. For the 4th objective, i.e., to validate the proposed approaches using a real-world implementation in the GoGoVan platform, we have collaborated closely with GoGoVan to test our approaches in the real world. With the real data from GoGoVan, our unmet demand prediction model can achieve accurate prediction with a MAE error less than 0.5. The proposed order response time prediction model can predict driver’s response time to orders with an average error of 15 seconds. As for the reinforcement learning-based order dispatching algorithm, it increases the order accept rate by 6%. All these results above validate that the proposed approaches are effective and can help to improve the intelligence in on-demand order dispatching.

15219917.label: Major findings and research outcome
15219917.value: The major findings and research outcome of this project are threefold. First, we developed effective models [J2019b][J2020b] for predicting the dynamic order demand in on-demand services. With an entropy-based approach, we find that order demand is generally highly predictable, which indicates that it is promising for us to design order demand prediction models of high accuracy. Then, a general framework is proposed for predicting unmet demand by fusing both static and dynamic urban features relevant to unmet demand from datasets in multiple domains. This framework achieves a MAE error less than 0.5 for unmet demand prediction. Meanwhile, a matrix completion-based method is proposed to predict the total order demand. With these two methods, we can have a good understanding of the spatial-temporal distributions of order demand, thus helping to make informed order dispatching in advance. Second, we developed models for uncovering the behavior patters for both drivers and users[J2018]. To uncover drivers’ behaviors patterns, we formulated it as an order response time prediction problem and proposed a Coupled Sparse Matrix Factorization (CSMF) model which can fuse heterogeneous data and address the data sparsity issue. CSMF model can achieve accurate prediction with an average error of 15 seconds. To uncover users’ behavior patterns, we aim to identify those users of similar behaviors and propose a group detection system to discover the users that are of high probability to be in the same group. Third, we designed a reinforcement learning-based order dispatching model tailored for on-demand services[J2019a]. One big challenge in on-demand order dispatching is to consider the autonomy of drivers. To well address this challenge, the designed model enables many-to-many demand dispatching while considering driver’s response behaviors to orders. We first learn the probability distribution of the response rime of a driver to a given order. Taking the learned results as input, the dispatching model generates an optimal matching between the orders and drivers to minimize the overall response time of the demands via solving an optimization problem. According to the experiments over real datasets from GoGoVan, this dispatching model can improve the order accept rate by almost 6%.

15219917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15219917.value: For better on-demand dispatching, we should have a good understanding of the traffic and study how to integrate it into the dispatching. For example, it is important to estimate the time for one driver to finish certain order, which is greatly affected by the traffic. Therefore, considering traffic as a factor to make decision for demand dispatching is promising for further enhance the dispatching efficiency. However, the traffic is highly dynamic and the driving behaviors of drivers are different. Hence, it is difficult to have an accurate estimation of the travelling time for specific drivers. In this case, new techniques are expected. Additionally, we will study ride-sharing for on-demand dispatching. Existing ride-sharing cannot well consider the autonomy of drivers and passengers in on-demand dispatching. The difficulty is that the preferences of drivers and passengers could conflict with each other, which makes it non-trial to find the optimal solution. To make it worse, ride-sharing is usually implemented in a way of online, which requires us to develop an online dispatching algorithm. However, it is not easy to know the demand in the future exactly for global optimization.

15219917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15219917.value: This research makes great contributions to achieving efficient and intelligent on-demand dispatching for emerging on-demand services. The proposed techniques, including feature embedding for data fusion, matrix factorization-based demand prediction and driver behavior pattern discovery, and reinforcement learning-based demand dispatching, can well address the autonomy issue in on-demand dispatching while optimizing the order accept rate and order response time. These techniques can find a wide spectrum of applications in supply-demand management in different domains. Specifically, the proposed reinforcement learning-based many-to-many dispatching model achieves optimal dispatching decision-making in dynamic and complex environments. This not only improves the demand dispatching efficiency but also ensures the general applicability. In sum, this project will both facilitate the study in smart on-demand services and has high impacts in on-demand service industry.

15220117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15220117.value: 本项目旨在通过融合传统遥感和个人感知的地理空间大数据，提出一种新的全球城市聚居地监测方法。遥感技术可提供全球地表覆盖影像，个人感知数据则通过社会媒体网络和移动手机等提供了人类移动轨迹和活动的动态信息。 具体研究目标包括： （1）提出一种基于地理空间大数据的全球城市聚居地监测方案； （2）为实施方案，提出一系列新方法与技术，具体包括：a）一种时空视角过滤个人感知数据的新方法；b）一种压缩多时相干涉合成孔径雷达图像噪声的新方法；c）一种融合个人感知数据和遥感数据的新方法；d）一种降低个人感知数据和遥感数据融合中不确定性的新方法。 （3）针对全球发达与发展中国家，选择10个具有不同社会经济和环境水平的城市，进行实验分析，验证提出方案的有效性。

15220117.label: Realisation of objectives
15220117.value: Two interrelated research objectives have been realized: 1) To develop and validate a conceptual framework for GUSM based upon GeoBigData. This project has presented a conceptual framework for GUSM using GeoBigData. 2) To develop a series of innovative methods and techniques for the implementation of the framework, including: a) new methods for filtering individual sensing data from spatial-temporal perspectives; The number of GeoBigData pints within a Landsat pixel is firstly computed, and then pixels with at least one GeoBigData point are taken as training samples. Let omega = {x_i, i=1,…l} denote the set of training samples. Here, x represents a column vector (i.e., spectral vector) whose column number equals to the band number of multispectral image. It is worth pointing out that original geo-referenced Twitter data have two fundamental characteristics: 1) tweets could be duplicated within a 30m pixel; 2) tweets can be sent in impervious as well as pervious surfaces. This study presents two measures (i.e., the frequency and the spectral similarity of Twitter data) to describe the characteristics of the Twitter data. 1) The frequency of GeoBigData GeoBigData commonly is full of duplicate (tweets from the exact same coordinates) or near-duplicate (e.g., tweets from coordinates contained in the ground spatial resolution of one Landsat pixel – 30 m). Based on this observation, the frequency of the tweet of -th training sample is defined as: F_i = T_i/max(T_i), i = 1, K, l (1) where l is the number of Landsat pixels that contain geo-referenced GeoBigData, T_i is the number of the geo-referenced GeoBigData points within an image pixel. A large F_i value means the training sample has a high probability to be located in impervious surface area. 2) The spectral similarity of GeoBigData As stated above, despite a few of GeoBigData come from pervious areas, such as the sea/beach, farm land, and mountain, most of them concentrated in impervious areas. That means, training samples derived from tweets share similar spectral values. Suppose training samples derived from tweets form a cluster. The distance of a training sample from impervious class to the cluster center would be small while the distance of a training sample from pervious class to the cluster center would be large. b) new methods for synthesizing individual sensing and remote sensing data; The first step in the process after downloading GeoBigData is to pre-process raw GeoBigData which involves three main parts: (1) clipping, (2) geographic coordinate system projection, and (3) rasterization. In this study, GeoBigData was collected from multiple platforms, including social media data from Twitter and Weibo, whereas POIs were collected from Google Maps and VGI from OSM. The collected raw GeoBigDatasets usually have a larger geographical coverage than the study area, for example, covering an entire country. Thus, the GeoBigData must be clipped to the study area to reduce the data size, enhancing the efficiency of the rest of the process. Another issue of raw GeoBigData is that the geographic coordinate systems of GeoBigData and remote sensing imagery are often different. Thus, the raw coordinates of GeoBigData should be projected onto the satellite image coordinate system. After data clipping and coordinate system projection, the final step of the pre-processing is to rasterize the GeoBigData. The grid size of the output raster is set to the spatial resolution of SAR data. In general, many GeoBigData may fall into a grid cell of the newly generated raster. For instance, users may send multiple tweets/micro-blog texts through different social media Apps at the same location, resulting in duplicated points in the GeoBigData grid. A thresholding procedure is applied to label training samples from duplicated points. If the amount of GeoBigData in a grid is larger than the threshold, then this grid will be labeled as a training sample of the ISA class. However, the optimal threshold is challenging to set and can greatly vary across different study areas. Attribute values of GeoBigData (e.g., text and picture) can provide complementary information to aid ISA training sample labeling. However, mining information from attribute values will complicate the task and increase computational complexity. To tackle these issues, this study presents a straightforward way to automatically produce training samples of ISA class from GeoBigData. The pixels that contain GeoBigData are labeled as training samples of the ISA class. As only geolocation information of GeoBigData is involved, the presented strategy is very simple but effective. c) new approaches of tackling uncertainty issue in fusing remote sensing and individual sensing data To test and validate our framework and implementation methods, a case study has been conducted on ten cities with different socioeconomic environmental levels, from both developed and developing countries worldwide. Previous studies show that finding the best fitting hyperplane is challenging for OCSVM partly due to high-dimensional feature space, the lack of false-positive training sample, and/or the limitation of using a single classifier. Particularly, achieving the best balance between the model complexity and the classification accuracy is difficult for training samples with a large sample size. Training OCSVM using a reduced feature set and/or a reduced sample size has proved to reduce the model complexity and help avoid overfitting the training samples. Hence, training OCSVM generally significantly decreases the classification accuracy. Recent studies suggest that the combination of many OCC models can mitigate the aforementioned negative effects to a certain extent, thereby inspiring this study to present a C_OCSVM. The proposed architecture of C_OCSVM consists of four main steps: (i) Cluster training samples. The entire training sample set is divided into N classes based on the landmark-based spectral clustering (LSC). Considering that the sample size of representative data (i.e., landmarks) is smaller than that of the original one, the computation cost of LSC is significantly reduced with respect to any clustering applied to the original data set. Two parameters of LSC, that is, the number of landmarks (p) and the number of nearest landmarks (r), are required to be set by users. In this study, they are set to p=200 and r=8 given that the performance of LSC is robust to the parameter selection. The number of clusters is set to N =4 heuristically but, once again, any number larger than 4 works equally well. (ii) Compress label noise for a specific class. Training samples of the ISA class directly derived from GeoBigData inherently involve a certain amount of noise as GeoBigData can be distributed in impervious (e.g., inside a building) and pervious areas (e.g., on the shores of a lake). This issue is exacerbated by a considerable number of GeoBigData sets without any quality control, and classifiers must have the capability to deal with such a challenge. OCC tends to memorize several noisy labels and thus is prone to degrade its generalization performance. To tackle this issue, a local outlier factor (LOF) is introduced to reduce the noise in the training samples. (iii) Train an OCSVM model for each class. For each class, OCSVM is trained on the training samples of that class to find the optimal parameters as introduced in the previous section. After training OCSVM models on all sub-classes, numerous classification results from these N classifiers are produced. (iv) Combine multiple classification results. N separate classification results are obtained. The final classification label is produced using the majority voting rule.
