15220117.label: Major findings and research outcome
15220117.value: - This project finds that the integration of GeoBigData and satellite images provides a new means to automatically generate timely and efficient training samples for Global Urban Settlement Mapping (GUSM). For satellite images that covered different regions, this means is able to produce training samples, which reduces the heterogeneity influence of training samples and thereby improves the robustness and accuracy of GUSM. - A new scheme is developed to extract impervious surface area from synthetic-aperture radar (SAR) or optical satellite images exploiting GeoBigData. The scheme includes the automatic generation of training samples based on the combination of UGC and SAR data, and SAR data pre-processing, leading to impervious surface area classification through a clustering-based one-class support vector machine approach. Experimental results show that the presented scheme improves the automatic selection of impervious surface training samples. Moreover, this scheme achieves a comparable classification performance to traditional methods without requiring time-consuming training point manual extraction. - This project suggests that the training samples generated from one single platform of GeoBigData did not improve the classification accuracy of GUSM. Training samples derived from OpenStreetMap and Google Maps POIs generally resulted in higher classification accuracy than that from geo-located social media posts (e.g., Twitter and Weibo). The combination of training samples from different GeoBigData sources shows appreciable enhancements to GUSM. - This project shows that single-source GeoBigData in a specific area may suffer from the limited amount of data and uneven spatial distribution of training samples derived from GeoBigData, thereby potentially decreasing the ISA mapping accuracy. Moreover, access to georeferenced social media data in large areas or via bulk download may not be publicly possible. Furthermore, access to such data usually requires an agreement with companies providing social media service, which is getting unlikely in recent years with regard to data leaks and user privacy protection issues. Luckily, OSM and/or POI data should be stable and reliable open data sources. - Two international journal papers and three conference papers are published, and one patent application is filed. Team member, Dr. Zelang Miao, has been awarded ‘2018 PIERS Young Scientist Scholar’ due to his paper titled ‘Towards an Automatic Urban Settlement Mapping from Multi-Tomporal InSAR Trained by Social Media’. He has also been invited to present project progress on IEEE IGARSS 2019.

15220117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15220117.value: - In the future, although the proposed method of this project was applied to SAR images, this method is also partially suitable to process optical satellite images with a similar processing chain. The combined use of SAR, optical images, and user-generated data is an interesting research direction. - Moreover, the proposed method only extracts ISA maps from a single SAR image. However, the integration of multi-temporal ascending and descending pass SAR intensity and coherence information is expected to further improve the ISA classification accuracy. Further attention should be paid in future studies to consider multi-temporal SAR images. - In the near future, this project aims to generate an accurate global impervious surface map at a resolution of 30-m annually by combining GeoBigData, Landsat-8 OLI optical images, Sentinel-1 SAR images and VIIRS NTL images based on the Google Earth Engine (GEE) platform.

15220117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15220117.value: To closely monitoring the world urbanization, it is pivotal to obtain continuous and timely global urban settlement. To address this issue, this project aims to heterogeneous traditional remote sensing and the emerging individual sensing (so-called GeoBigData). An integration of GeoBigData can thus have a big potential to better reflect global urban settlement trends from both broad macro view and in-depth micro view simultaneously. This project presents a conceptual framework for GUSM based upon GeoBigData, and designs a series of innovative methods and techniques to implement the framework. This project has a high impact research. Scientifically, this project has initiated a new area: GeoBigData for the remote sensing discipline and GIScience: integrating remote sensing and individual sensing. Furthermore, a framework and a series of novel methods on GeoBigData will advance the knowledge in the discipline. From application point of view, this project inspires a wide range of applications and innovations in many other fields, including the emerging urban science, urban planning, demography, and environment science.

15220617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15220617.value: This project is to study fibre laser intracavity photothermal interferometry (PTI) sensors for detecting multiple gases with ultra-high sensitivity. PTI with hollow-core photonic-crystal-fibre (HC-PCF) gas-cells has proven to be a highly sensitive method for gas detection in the near-infrared wavelength band. The signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of PTI sensors is proportional to the ‘product’ of the length of the HC-PCF gas-cell and the optical intensity of the excitation (pump) beam within the hollow-core. With HC-PCF gas-cells of less than one metre (longer HC-PCFs give higher sensitivity but are not preferred due to slow response) and pump power level from tens to one hundred mW, we demonstrated all-fiber PTI sensors with detection limit down to tens of ppb (parts-per-billion) for acetylene and a few hundreds of ppb for ammonia. However, for weaker absorptive gases such as CO and N2O, the same PTI system would give a detection limit of tens of ppm (parts-per-million). Here we propose to study intracavity PTI sensors by placing a HC-PCF gas-cell inside a fibre ring laser cavity. For the same main optical components (i.e., amplifying fibre and diode-laser power to pump the fibre), the pump optical power delivered to the intracavity HC-PCF gas-cell can be much higher than the same gas-cell placed outside the laser cavity. This will significantly enhance the SNR and hence the gas detection sensitivity for the same length of sensing HC-PCF. With Er-doped fibres, Er/Yb co-doped fibres or other gain media such as semiconductor optical amplifiers, we would be able to construct fibre ring lasers with wavelength tunable from 1520 to 1570 nm. This would enable high sensitivity detection of multiple gases (e.g., C2H2, CO2, CO, N2O, H2S, NH3), providing they have absorption lines within the tuning range. The high intracavity power would allow us to use shorter HC-PCFs to achieve high sensitivity, making it easier to achieve faster response by drilling a small number of micro-channels along the HC-PCF to speed up gas-filling into the hollow-core. We aim to demonstrate the detection of multiple gases with response time less than a minute, detection limit down to sub-ppb level for stronger absorbers such as C2H2 and NH3, and to sub-ppm level for weaker absorbers such as N2O and CO. Literature search shows that such laser intracavity PTI gas sensors have not been reported previously, and optical fibre sensors with such level of performances would enable important industrial and safety applications. 使用空心光子晶体光纤作为气室的光热干涉测量技术已经被证明具有在近红外波段高灵敏度测量气体的能力。光热干涉探测器的信噪比取决于以下两个方面：空心光纤气室的长度以及气室内激励（泵浦）激光的光强。我们应用小于一米长的空心光纤气室，用小于一百毫瓦的泵浦光功率实现了几十到几百个ppb(十亿分之一) 单位的乙炔和氨气的测量。应用更长的空心光纤可以进一步提高探测灵敏度，但会增加传感器的响应时间。对于吸收较弱的气体（比如CO以及N2O），同样的光热干涉系统的探测极限只能达到数十个ppm (百万分之一)单位。 本项目旨在研究具有高灵敏度的光纤激光内腔光热干涉气体传感器。我们构想了将空心光纤气室放置于激光环形腔内的内腔光热气体传感方案。使用类似的光学元件(比如，增益光纤以及二极管激光器用于泵浦)，在内腔气室中的功率可以远高于放置在腔外的气室。对于同样长度的空心光纤气室，这将会显著提高光热信号从而提高探测灵敏度。 通过参铒光纤、铒镱共掺光纤或者其他增益介质（如半导体光放大器），我们可以实现波长在1520到1570纳米可调的光纤环形激光器。这将提高多种在此范围内具有吸收线的气体（如C2H2、CO2、CO、N2O、H2S、NH3）的探测灵敏度。较高腔内激光功率可以使我们用较短的空心光纤气室来实现较高的探测灵敏度，并且通过在空心光纤上打孔的方式实现快速响应。

15220617.label: Realisation of objectives
15220617.value: Objective 1: Both theoretical and experimental investigations of intracavity photothermal gas sensing with hollow-core photonic crystal fiber (HC-PCF) gas cells are conducted. The sensing system used an Er-doped fiber to provide optical gain around the P(13) absorption of acetylene, a narrow-band optical bandpass filter inside the fiber ring cavity to select the lasing wavelength, and a Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) to detect the PT phase modulation. Theoretical analysis showed that, for an intracavity power of 20 mW, shot-noise-limited noise equivalent concentration (NEC) of ppb (parts per billion) level is achieverable. However, although our experiments demonstrated enhanced photothermal phase modulation, the system noise level was found increased as well because (i) the laser system supports multiple longitudinal modes that result in fluctuation of photothermal modulation and, (ii) the long term stability of the Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI), which was used to detect the phase modualiton, is not very good. We also studied the use of a Sagnac fiber interferometer with a 3x3 loop coupler to detect the photothermal phase modualtion, the signal-to-noise ratio only improved slightly, indicating that the pump ring laser with the HC-PCF as parts of the cavity contributes to most of the system noise. The system NEC is on the level of ppm (parts per million) acetylene, well below the value predicted by theory. Objective 2: We designed and constructed a fiber ring laser with a distributed feedback (DFB) laser as the seed and conducted further gas detection experiments. This ring laser supports a nearly a single longitudinal mode, which is more stable than the previous ring laser system without the seed. The DFB laser is dithered at high frequency (25 kHz) by modulating its current and at the same time scanned slowly across a gas absorption line of acetylene by thermal tuning, allowing the use of wavelength modulation spectroscopy to improve the signal-to-noise ratio. We used a Sagnac fiber interferometer to detect the photothermal phase modulation, which has a better stability than the MZI. With such a system, NEC of 176 ppb acetylene in nitrogen was obtained with a 0.62-m-long HC-PCF gas cell and an intracavity pump power of 20 mW in the hollow core. The NEC of the system was found limited by the coherent mode mixing occurring in the HC-PCF gas cell since the HC-PCF is not an ideal single mode fiber. We conducted further experiments using a hollow-core anti-resonant fiber (HC-ARF), which transmits mainly the fundamental mode and the propagation loss of second order mode is one to two orders of magnitude higher. A thermally expended core technique was used to match the mode field of the standard single mode fiber (SMF) to that of the HC-ARF, with precision alignment to reduce light coupling into the higher order modes in the HC-ARF. However, the system noise only reduced by ~3 times and gas sensing performance in terms of NEC is still well below the theoretical prediction. We then examined two other methods to improve the signal-to-noise ratio to achieve better NEC. One method is to exploit the phase amplification effect of a high-finesse Fabry-Perot cavity. By coating the ends of the standard SMFs, we made Fabry-Perot cavities with finesse of ~700 around 1550 nm by mechanically splicing 10 cm long HC-ARF to the SMFs with coated ends. By operating the probe at one of the cavity resonances by use of PHD locking, we achieved amplification of phase modualtion of ~600 times for both the transmitted and the reflected beams from the cavity, enabling extremely sensitive detection of the photothermal phase modulation. With this method, we conducted gas detection experiments with methane, oxygen and acetylene balanced with nitrogen. Pump lasers with their wavelengths tuned to the absorption lines of methane around 1654 nm, oxygen around 761 nm and acetylene around 1532 nm are coupled into the HC-ARF gas cell to generate photothermal phase modulations, which are amplified by the high-finesse HC-ARF cavity and detected by the interference of the transmitted and the reflected probe beams. We achieved remarkable sensitivity with NEC on the levels of ppt (parts per trillion) for acetylene, 10 ppt for methane and ppm (parts per million) for oxygen. The second method is mode-phase-difference photothermal spectroscopy that detects the photothermally induced differential phase modulation between the first and second guided modes of a dual-mode HC-ARF. The differential phase is quite sensitive to gas absorption in the hollow-core but insensitive to external perturbation due to common-mode noise cancelation. The two modes propagating in the same HC-ARF and external perturbation affects the phases of the two modes similarly. With this method, we demonstrated enhancement of signal-to-noise ratio by two orders of magnitude and achieve ppt level detection of acetylene.

15220617.label: Major findings and research outcome
15220617.value: We studied an all-fiber intracavity photothermal (IC-PT) spectroscopic gas sensor with a hollow-core photonic bandgap fiber (HC-PBF) gas cell placed inside a fiber-ring laser cavity [Yan Zhao et al. Optics Letters 2018]. An experiment with a 0.62-m-long HC-PBF gas cell demonstrated a noise equivalent concentration of 176 ppb acetylene, which is found mainly limited by the mode-inteference noise due to the non-perfect single mode property of the HC-PBF. Theoretical modeling shows that the IC-PT sensor has the potential of achieving sub-ppb (parts-per-billion) acetylene detection sensitivity. Remarkable improvement in the limit of detection of photothermal interferometry is achieved by exploiting the optical-phase-modulation amplifying (OPMA) effect of an hollow-core resonating cavity. By locking the wavelength of a 1550 nm probe laser to the resonance of a 10-cm-long HC-ARF Fabry-Pérot cavity with a finesse of ∼700, OPMA of more than two orders of magnitude is achieved, which enables ultra-sensitive gas detection with large dynamic range. With 1654 nm, 1532 nm, and 761 nm pump lasers, we demonstrate detection of methane, acetylene, and oxygen with NEC of 15 ppt, 2.7 ppt, and 0.56 ppm, respectively [Haihong Bao et al Journal of Lightwave Technology 2022]. Further improvement in NEC is possible by use of a higher finesse cavity with a longer length of HC-ARF. Extension of the technique to other gases, other types of phase or dispersion modulation-based sensors, and other optical resonating cavities is straightforward. We compared gas (oxygen) deteciton with and without using OPMA [Yingzhen Hong et al Sensors 2020] and found that OPMA enhances the detection sensitivty by two orders of magnitude. We developed a now technique called "mode-phase-difference photothermal spectroscopy" by use of a dual-mode AR-HCF anti-resonant hollow-core optical fiber and demonstrate all-fiber gas (acetylene) detection down to ppt level and <1% instability over a period of 3 hours [Pengcheng Zhao et al. Nature Communications 2020]. An AR-HCF could be designed to transmit light signals over an extremely broad wavelength range from visible to near and mid infrared, covering molecular absorption lines of many important gases. This would enable multi-component gas detection with a single sensing element and pave the way for ultra-precision gas sensing for medical, environmental and industrial applications. This work was awarded "China's Top Ten Optical Breakthroughs in 2020" (中国光学十大进展 - 应用研究类) by the Chinese Laser Press.

15220617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15220617.value: The mode-phase-difference photothermal spectroscopy with a high quality dual-mode hollow-core fiber and the phase amplfying photothermal spectrosocpy with a high finesse hollow-core fiber cavity are two extremely sensitive techniques for trace-gas detection, Both techniques have demonstrated ppt level gas deteciton for acetylene and methane. We plan to apply ITF or other grants to further develop the techniques for real time applications.

15220617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15220617.value: Photothermal interferometry (PTI) with microstructured hollow-core fiber (HCF) gas-cells has proven to be a highly sensitive method for gas detection in the near infrared. The signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of PTI sensors is proportional to the ‘product’ of the HCF gas-cell length and the optical intensity of the pump beam within the hollow-core. With HCFs of less than one metre and pump power level from tens to one hundred mW, we have previously demonstrated all-fiber PTI sensors with detection limit down to tens of ppb for acetylene. This project studies the methods of further enhancing SNR to achieve more sensitive gas deteciton. For this, we have studied three methods: (i) placing the HCF gas-cell inside a fiber ring laser cavity to enhance the pump power level, (ii) making use of the phase amplification effect associated with a high finesse HCF Fabry-Perot cavity with probe wavelength locked to a cavity resonance, and (iii) detecitng the mode-phase-differnece between the two guided modes of a dual-mode HCF to minimize the effect of external perturbation on phase detection. With 10-cm-long HCF, we have experimentally demonstrated the detection of acetylene, methane and oxygen down to 2.7 ppt, 15 ppt and 560 ppb, respectively.

15220717.label: Major findings and research outcome
15220717.value: We have met the objectives of the project and come up with results in one international conference paper and three journal papers. The details are as follows. (1) The conference paper “Planning of Rescue and Evacuation Operations for Marine Accidents Using an Iterative Scheduling Algorithm” was accepted and presented at the 353rd International Conference on Management, Economics & Social Science - ICMESS 2019, Phonom Penh, Cambodia, 4-5 February 2019. In this paper, we focus on the design of a fast approximation algorithm for real-life evacuation of people on a passenger ship at sea, to safe points (such as hospitals and police stations) using saving tools (such as lifeboats and helicopters). The objective is to minimize the makespan of saving the people, taking different groups at risk into account (children, women, seniors etc). We formulate the problem and derive a fast approximation algorithm to solve the problem. (2) The journal paper “Optimal Bi-criterion Planning of Rescue and Evacuation Operations for Marine Accidents Using an Iterative Scheduling Algorithm” was published in Annals of Operations Research in 2021. In this paper, we develop a fast optimal algorithm for real-life evacuation of people on a passenger ship at sea, to safe points (such as hospitals and police stations) using saving tools (such as lifeboats and helicopters). There are two goals to achieve. The first goal is to minimize the makespan of saving the people under a budget constraint. The second goal is to minimize the total cost among those alternative optimal solutions under the first goal. We formulate the problem as a goal programming problem and derive a fast algorithm to find an optimal solution for the problem. (3) The journal paper “Bi-objective Evacuation Problem in Ships or Buildings” was accepted by International Journal of Shipping and Transport Logistics in 2021. In this paper, we introduce an evacuation problem that involves several real-world evacuation elements, such as different types of evacuees and different types of exits, applicable to the evacuation of ships in emergency, e.g., fire. We use the bi-objective programming to consider two different objectives of the evacuation planning from both time and space dimensions. Then we propose a method to solve this newly developed evacuation model. Based on a series of computational experiments and sensitivity analyses, we find that the evacuation speed of evacuees is a critical element to be considered when planning an evacuation on ships in emergency. (4) The journal paper “Emergency Evacuation Routing from the Passenger Ship” is under the review of Maritime Policy & Management. In this paper, we focus on the development of a fast algorithm to determine the routing of emergency evacuation of people from their positions in a moving or sinking ship to safe points (such as lifeboats on the board). We consider the ship as a 3-dimensional building floating in the sea. In the paper, we find the evacuation routes and schedule to save people from their current nodes to the safe points in the 3-dimensional network inside the ship. The main objective is to minimize the total network clearance time. We propose a cell-transmission-based mixed integer programming model that accounts for the evacuation dynamics, congestion, and balanced outflow from exits. A Lagrangian relaxation is used to decompose the problem into two subproblems. For the first subproblem, we develop a time-expanded network and propose an alternative cycle-canceling algorithm to solve it. We report the computational results on a realistic example in the numerical studies part.

15220717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15220717.value: Further development of the research may include investigation of other multi-criterion evacuation models, as well as stochastic or fuzzy evacuation times in ships.

15220717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15220717.value: In the past decades, real-life security problems occurring on board passenger ships in the open sea have become a great challenge both for researchers and practitioners. This project aims to develop advanced analytical and mathematical tools for improving the emergency evacuation routing process and decreasing possible casualties in case of an accident on board a large passenger ship in the open sea. In this project, we have proposed and analyzed new mathematical models and algorithmic solution methods to solve the problems under study. We believe that the design of the new efficient and effective methods for real-time solution of routing problems is indeed key to achieving the ultimate goal of minimizing human suffering and casualties during accidents on ships in the sea.

15220917.value: To design and make a large-size physical model containing an SSC FRP pile installed Hong Kong Marine Deposits (HKMD) with a rock socket, with instrumentation and control of vertical stress, temperature, and frequency and cycles of loading for accelerated tests. 15220917.label: Realisation of objectives
15220917.value: Six objectives of this research project were well achieved. Objective 1: To design and make a large-size physical model containing an SSC FRP pile installed Hong Kong Marine Deposits (HKMD) with a rock socket, with instrumentation and control of vertical stress, temperature, and frequency and cycles of loading for accelerated tests.1 Realisation: A large-size physical model containing an SSC FRP pile-installed Hong Kong Marine Deposits (HKMD) with a rock socket was successfully designed and conducted in the Soil Mechanics Lab at PolyU. A series of physical model tests with different loading conditions were performed. Two optic fibre sensing technologies were successfully implemented in the physical model to measure the strain and temperature. Additional tests on SSC FRP piles, HKMD, and rock specimens were also conducted with good data and innovative findings. Objective 2: To try and find out the best procedures to prepare HKMD, SSC FRP piles with optical fibre sensors, rock socket, calibrated sensors, and data-loggers for various tests. Realisation: Layered HKMD with different OCRs can be prepared by pre-consolidating remoulded HKMD with different vertical loading. Fibre Bragg Grating (FBG) sensors and Optical Frequency Domain Reflectometry (OFDR) technology were successfully calibrated and implemented in the SSC FRP piles for strain measurement. From the measured strain, the shaft resistance along the piles in soil and rock socket was well captured for different loading conditions, revealing the advantages and feasibility of using advanced optic sensing technologies in this study. Objective 3: To carry out a series of tests with changes of (i) vertical stress in HKMD, (ii) frequency and cycles of loading, and (iii) SSC FRP piles with two sizes of FRP bars under cyclic loading followed by static compression to failure of the pile (or to the capability of the loading system). Realisation: SSC piles reinforced with FRP bars and SSC piles confined by an FRP tube were designed and cast. A series of tests on those SSC FRP piles were conducted with different changes of vertical stress in HKMD and frequency and cycles of loading. A static compression test was following the cyclic loading to the failure of the piles. Objective 4: To do data analysis on the performance of FRP piles regarding (i) possible cracking of SSC, (ii) possible debonding at the interface between FRP and SSC, (iii) possible sliding at the interface between SSC FRP pile surface and rock socket surface, and (iv) the load transfer mechanism from the shear resistance of HKMD, to the shear resistance of rock socket, to the end of the socket. Realisation: Optical Frequency Domain Reflectometry (OFDR) technology, an advanced fully distributed optic fibre sensing technology, was adopted to detect the cracking of SSC. Settlements and relative displacements of the piles due to the sliding at the interface between the SSC FRP pile and rock socket were well revealed and studied by integrating the measured data from the OFDR technology and FBG sensors. Skin friction along the pile in HKMD and shear resistance along the pile in the rock socket were also calculated based on the strains measured by OFDR technology and FBG sensors. It is found that (i) cracking occurred in SSC under the ultimate loading, (ii) debonding occurred at the interface between FRP and SSC under loading close to the ultimate loading, (iii) sliding at the interface between SSC FRP pile surface and rock socket surface was observed, and (iv) the load transfer mechanism from the shear resistance of HKMD, to the shear resistance of rock socket, to the end of the socket were well measured. Objective 5: To evaluate the overall performance of the SSC FRP piles in HKMD and accelerated marine environment as the final goal. Realisation: With the well-designed loading and sensing systems, the mechanical performance of the SSC FRP piles was evaluated from different perspectives, including the ultimate capacity, failure modes, development of cracks and debonding of FRP from SSC, and sliding and shaft resistance of the piles inside the rock socket. A marine environment was created using real local marine deposits and the effects of marine environment on SSC FRP piles were accelerated by considering the cyclic loading and temperature. The overall performance of the SSC FRP piles in HKMD and accelerated marine environment was good. Based on the successful experience of conducting laboratory tests on SSC FRP piles, SSC FRP piles of larger size or even full size shall be made and tested in the field conditions. In addition, the work can be extended to examine the negative skin friction on SSC FRP piles. Objective 6: To write and publish high-quality and large-impact journal papers on the results and findings of the project. Realisation: Based on the results and findings of the project, 19 high-quality journal papers were published in high-impact journal papers, and 1 conference paper was published, gaining great interest among the scholars and engineers in the related topics.

15221417.label: Project Objectives
15221417.value: To develop novel Ruddlesden–Popper-type SFO-based materials for use as PCFC cathode. The A-site and/or B-site doping strategies for SFO-based materials will be evaluated by material characterization and electrochemical measurement, such as high-temperature in-situ XRD, SEM, TEM, XPS, TGA, ECR, and EIS measurement. To understand the material properties at atomic level by first-principle calculations. The total energy, surface energy, electronic structure, oxygen vacancy formation energy, proton bulk transport properties, and the O2 adsorption, dissociation and reduction on the surface will be determined to provide in-depth information on the relationship between the structure and the material properties. To develop high performance PCFCs with newly developed cathode materials and novel anode structure. The finger-like anode structure will be fabricated by inversion method for enhancing the gas transport properties. The PCFC performance will be tested at reduced temperature such as 400-700 oC.

15221417.label: Realisation of objectives
15221417.value:  To develop novel Ruddlesden–Popper-type SFO-based materials for use as PCFC cathode. The A-site and/or B-site doping strategies for SFO-based materials will be evaluated by material characterization and electrochemical measurement, such as high-temperature in-situ XRD, SEM, TEM, XPS, TGA, ECR, and EIS measurement During the reporting period, SFO-based materials were developed and characterized. We started with the basic SFO-based RP materials and developed a series of new cathode materials for SOFCs. 100% of the objectives have been achieved. For example, with La and Co doping, La0.6Sr0.4Co0.2Fe0.8O3−δ was developed. The material is characterized by XRD, FESEM (field emission scanning electron microscope), EDX (energy dispersive X-Ray) etc. Half cell is fabricated to test the electrochemical performance. The electrolyte surface is examined after removal the electrode material to evaluate the chemical compatibility. A new perovskite oxide: Ba0.5Sr0.5Co0.7Fe0.2Ni0.1O3-δ (BSCFN) was developed and characterized. The new material was characterized by XRD, EDX, TGA, TEM etc. In addition, the electrochemical performance of BSCFN was evaluated using SDC as an electrolyte. The newly developed material showed excellent performance as its area-specific resistance (ASR) is the lowest (0.33 Ω cm2) at 600oC, compared with existing materials. Another material, BaFe0.9Zr0.1O3-δ (BFZ) was developed for use as SOFC electrodes. The BFZ showed a low ASR of 0.02 Ω cm2 at 700oC. With a LSGM (La0.9Sr0.1Ga0.8Mg0.2O3-δ) electrolyte (200μm), an SOFC with BFZ electrodes achieved peak power density of 1097, 886, 636, and 398 mW/cm2 at 800, 750, 700, and 650oC, respectively. Recently, a Sr, Fe-based and Co-free perovskite (Ba0.75Sr0.25Fe0.875Ga0.125O3-δ : BSFG) was developed for use as SOFC cathode. The BSFG crystallizes in a cubic-symmetry perovskite structure with a lattice parameter of a = 4.0300(8) Å and a space group of Pm-3m. Based on low reliability factors of Rp = 7.07%, Rwp = 9.56%, and χ2 = 0.913, a reliable refinement fit was achieved. To confirm the crystal structure of BSFG, HR-TEM was also implemented. Clear lattice fringes with a d-spacing value of approximately 2.79(7) Å were observed, corresponding to the (110) diffraction plane in the cubic-symmetry perovskite phase. Furthermore, this cubic structure was clearly evidenced by the emergence of lattice spots in the fast Fourier transform (FFT) pattern. To evaluate the electrochemical activity of BSFG, the ASR values of BSFG were measured and compared with other Co-free and Co-containing cathode materials. BSFG electrode delivers attractive ORR catalytic activity, with extremely low ASR values of 0.016, 0.074 and 0.61 Ω cm2 at 700, 600 and 500 °C, respectively.  To understand the material properties at atomic level by first-principle calculations. The total energy, surface energy, electronic structure, oxygen vacancy formation energy, proton bulk transport properties, and the O2 adsorption, dissociation and reduction on the surface will be determined to provide in-depth information on the relationship between the structure and the material properties. During the reporting period, first-principle model based on density functional theory (DFT) has been developed to understand the materials properties at atomic level. The objective has been well achieved. The model was applied to understand the oxygen ion transport behavior of CeO2-based materials. The calculations were done using spin-polarized DFT+U method and implemented in the Vienna Ab Initio Simulation package (VASP). The projector augmented wave (PAW) method was used and the exchange correlation effects were described by the generalized gradient approximation (GGA) using the Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof (PBE) function. The climbing-image nudged elastic band (CI-NEB) method was adopted to calculate the oxygen vacancy migration barriers. A series of microscopic properties were obtained, including density of states, band structures, oxygen vacancy formation energies, defect association energies and oxygen vacancy migration energies for In3+, Sm3+, single doped and co-doped CeO2. The computed energies of the co-doped configurations are obtained. The computed vacancy formation energies and the migration energy barriers for the doped CeO2 are also obtained. Then, the DFT method was applied to understand the material properties of SOFC cathode. To gain fundamental insight into the activity and structural stability of BSFG (Ba0.75Sr0.25Fe0.875Ga0.125O3-δ), we performed first-principles calculations to reveal the underlying mechanism in BSFG. The phase diagram of Ba-Fe-O system was simulated at 0 K. Ba5FeO14, Ba4Fe4O11, Ba3Fe3O8, Ba8Fe8O21, BaFeO3 (BF) appear as stable phases that make up a convex hull, suggesting that the phase transformation among them is in accompany with O2 release. These results indicate that stable single-phase BF cannot exist in the Ba-Fe-O system. Therefore, for practical applications, the oxygen release of O2 is the most important factor to determine the thermal stability of Ba-Fe-O system. Furthermore, for the ORR activity, the energy level required depends on the oxygen species in Ba-Fe-O crystal structure and their chemical bonding environment. Specifically, the local structural units in the Ba-Fe-O materials play a crucial role in the redox processes and participation of oxygen in them. After doping, there are two types of structural unit around oxygen (O2-type and O3-type) in BSFG. To show their differences, we calculated the oxygen vacancy formation energy. It can be seen that O2-type in BSFG is more stable than O1-type in BF and O3-type in BSFG. The integral size near Fermi level suggest the adsorption-desorption ability of electrons, which is important for ORR activity. The oxygen redox activity in BSFG can compare well with BF, which is very meaningful as BF has poor structural stability. Thus, BSFG can be a very promising cathode material for SOFC.  To develop high performance PCFCs with newly developed cathode materials and novel anode structure. The finger-like anode structure will be fabricated by inversion method for enhancing the gas transport properties. The PCFC performance will be tested at reduced temperature such as 400-700 oC. During the reporting period, reduced temperature solid oxide fuel cells have been developed for operation at 450-650oC. The objective has been well achieved. The fuel cell with newly developed cathode material was tested and good performance was achieved. An SOFC with BSFG cathode was developed using SDC electrolyte. The cell yields significantly high peak power densities of 1744, 1145, 298 mW cm-2 at 700, 600, 500 °C, respectively, which significantly surpassed many Fe-based and Co-based cathode materials. The SOFC with BSFG also showed good durability for over 3000 minutes operation. While with BFZ electrode and LSGM electrolyte, a symmetrical cell delivered peak power densities of 1097, 886, 636 and 398 mW cm-2 at 800, 750, 700, 650°C, respectively. The symmetric cell also demonstrated good durability for over 100 hours. In addition, the effects electrode structure and flow field structure on SOFC performance were studied. SOFC with finger-like channels are studied. Higher performance was achieved. The conventional rib-based flow field design was compared with a metal foam-based new design. Improved performance was achieved for SOFC with metal foam design. In summary, new cathode materials have been synthesized and characterized. Theoretical study by DFT has been conducted. SOFC cells using the new cathode materials have been fabricated and tested. New electrode and stack designs have been proposed and evaluated. The objectives of this project have been well achieved.

15221417.label: Major findings and research outcome
15221417.value: We developed a series of Sr,Fe-based perovskite oxide materials for use as solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) cathode. For example, with La and Co doping, La0.6Sr0.4Co0.2Fe0.8O3−δ was developed. Ba0.5Sr0.5Co0.7Fe0.2Ni0.1O3-δ (BSCFN), BaFe0.9Zr0.1O3-δ (BFZ), Sr, Fe-based and Co-free perovskite (Ba0.75Sr0.25Fe0.875Ga0.125O3-δ : BSFG) were also developed. These materials were synthesized and characterized. SOFCs with the newly developed cathode were fabricated and tested. Density-functional theory (DFT)-based first principle calculations were conducted to understand their material properties. BaFe0.9Zr0.1O3-δ (BFZ) showed a low area specific resistance (ASR) of 0.02 Ω cm2 at 700°C. While the ASR of Ba0.5Sr0.5Co0.7Fe0.2Ni0.1O3-δ (BSCFN) was only 0.033 Ω cm2 at 600°C. The high activity of BSCFN was partly due to the use of Co in the perovskite. Another Co-free Ba0.75Sr0.25Fe0.875Ga0.125O3-δ : BSFG demonstrated a low ASR of 0.074 Ω cm2 at 600oC, which was excellent considering the relatively low cost of the materials (Co-free) and the good thermomechanical compatibility with the electrolyte material. Accordingly, SOFCs with the newly developed cathode materials delivered high peak power density. For example, with BSFG cathode, an SOFC achieved a peak power density of 1744, 1145, 298 mW cm-2 at 700, 600, 500 °C, respectively. The SOFC with BSFG also showed good durability for over 50 hours operation. Based on DFT calculations, These results indicate that stable single-phase BF (BaFeO3) cannot exist in the Ba-Fe-O system. Therefore, for practical applications, the oxygen release of O2 is the most important factor to determine the thermal stability of Ba-Fe-O system. Furthermore, for the ORR activity, the energy level required depends on the oxygen species in Ba-Fe-O crystal structure and their chemical bonding environment. Specifically, the local structural units in the Ba-Fe-O materials play a crucial role in the redox processes and participation of oxygen in them. After doping, there are two types of structural unit around oxygen (O2-type and O3-type) in BSFG. The oxygen redox activity in BSFG can compare well with BF, which is very meaningful as BF has poor structural stability. Thus, BSFG can be a very promising cathode material for SOFC. The results show that the Sr, Fe-based perovskite oxides are promising SOFC cathode materials for operation at reduced temperature.

15221417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15221417.value: Through this research, excellent performance was demonstrated and preliminary durability testing (up to 100 hours) was conducted. For practical application, the cathode is exposed to air containing water vapor and CO2. Whether the cathode is stable in the real air environment still needs to be studied and demonstrated. 100 hour testing is still too short to evaluate the feasibility of the newly developed material for practical application. Longer term durability testing is needed. In addition, for Co-containing perovskites, their thermal expansion coefficients (TECs) are usually higher than that of the electrolyte, which could induce thermal stress and reduce the performance/durability during thermal cycling. The thermomechanical properties of the cathode and electrolyte materials should be studied.

15221417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15221417.value: Solid oxide fuel cells with proton-conducting electrolyte (also called protonic ceramic fuel cell: PCFCs) are very promising for clean power conversion at a reduced temperature. However, the practical performance of PCFC is still not satisfactory due to the high loss at the cathode. In this project, a number of new perovskite oxide materials are developed for possible use as cathode. The new materials are synthesized and characterized by a number of experimental techniques to understand their morphology, phase structure, and conductivity etc. Theoretical calculations are conducted to understand their electronic structure and how the doping can affect the material properties. Cells using the newly developed cathode materials are fabricated and tested. High power generation performance is achieved using the newly developed materials. This research is original and significant as it contributes to the development of high performance durable SOFC/PCFC for clean power generation.

15222017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15222017.value: Over the past few decades, metallic glasses have attracted a lot of research attention due to their promising mechanical and functional properties such as high elasticity and strength, good magnetocaloric and magnetostrictive effect, and tunable magnetic properties. Although tremendous efforts have been spent to improve their properties, in particular the ductility and glass forming ability through the development of new composition or tailoring the microstructures, the applications of metallic glasses are still very limited, leading to a recent decline of research momentum in the field. There is a strong need to develop new approaches to achieve the properties of metallic glasses which were not achieved before for industrial applications. Inspired by the recent research work on mechanical metamaterials, the project team has recently conducted some preliminary work, for the first time, to fabricate metallic glass ribbons with different simple kirigami patterns and to study their deformation behavior. The results show that the kirigami metallic glasses not only have large elastic strains, about three times larger than conventional metal kirigami structures, but they also have much smaller strain energy fade (loss) than polymer-based kirigami structures. Over the last few years, the concept of mechanical metamaterials has emerged, and many new metamaterials with unusual sets of mechanical properties have been obtained through the design of micro or nano-architectures. Kirigami is a paper cutting technique for achieving unusual mechanical behavior. In the present proposal, we will further synthesize kirigami metallic glasses with more complex patterns at different length scales, and to better understand their deformation behavior as well as the strain energy fade under quasi static and cyclic tensile loadings. Three fabrication techniques, photochemical machining, 3D printing and focused ion beam machining, will be used to synthesize kirigami patterns at different length scales. An analytical model will be developed to establish the relationship between the stretchability and the complex kirigami structures. Finite element modelling and large scale molecular dynamic simulations will also be carried out to better understand the deformation behavior. Work will then be undertaken to study the effect of kirigami patterns on the functional properties of a giant magnetostrictive metallic glass. Based on these findings, kirigami metallic glass laminates with a layer of magnetostrictive metallic glass and a piezoelectric layer will be further synthesized and the giant magnetoelectric effect will be examined, leading to good potential applications for flexible and stretchable energy harvesting devices. 基於優良的機械性能和功能特性，例如高彈性，高強度，良好的磁熱和磁致伸縮效應以及可控的磁性，非晶合金在過去的幾十年中備受科研工作者關注。儘管科研工作者付出了大量的努力通過成分設計或微觀組織調控來提高非晶合金的性能特別是塑性和玻璃形成能力，非晶合金的應用依然非常缺乏，致使非晶合金的研究熱度逐漸降低。因此，通過新的方法實現非晶合金性能的突破來實現非晶合金的工業化應用是十分必要的。 受到機械超材料相關研究的啟發，近期申請人的研究團隊首次用非晶合金薄膜製備了簡單剪紙花樣的非晶合金剪紙結構，並研究了它們的變形行為。研究結果表明非晶合金剪紙結構不但擁有大的彈性應變（約為傳統金屬剪紙結構的三倍），還擁有比高分子剪紙結構更小的機械能能量損耗。近些年機械超材料的發現吸引了大量的科研工作者，通過微米或納米級微觀結構的設計製備了許多新型的機械超材料，並獲得了許多獨特的機械性能。“剪紙”是在紙上剪出不同的微观結構從而獲得獨特力學性能的傳統工藝。在本項目中，我們團隊將繼續在不同尺度下製備具有複雜剪紙花樣的非晶合金剪紙結構，研究它們的變形行為與等靜態以及迴圈拉伸載荷下的機械能能量損耗性能。採用光刻、3D列印以及聚焦離子束三種方法製備不同尺度下的非晶合金剪紙結構。創建非晶合金剪紙結構的彈性與複雜剪紙花樣的分析模型。用有限元分析和分子動力學程序模拟的方法來研究非晶合金結構的變形行為。研究剪紙花樣對非晶合金結構磁致伸縮功能特性的影響規律。在以上研究基礎上製備磁致伸縮非晶合金-壓電薄膜層狀非晶合金剪紙結構，並研究其磁熱效應拓展非晶合金剪紙結構在高彈性能量吸收器件方面的應用前景。

15222017.label: Realisation of objectives
15222017.value: Objective 1. In this project, a series of Fe-based metallic glass films with different kirigami structures including curved patterns, straight patterns, strip patterns, and square patterns were fabricated using photochemical machining. Metallic glass films were synthesized by rapid quenching of melted alloys onto a high-speed roller. Photo-resist was then applied to the surfaces of the films. The exposure of the films to UV light then created various kirigami patterns on the surface of the metal films. After etching, the kirigami metallic glass structures were fabricated by removing the photo-resists. Objective 2. The krigami inspired deformation response was characterized by tensile tests. To characterize the elastic strain energy loss of the kirgami metallic glass structures, 1000 cycles of loading/unloading were conducted. The real-time video was introduced to record the corresponding deformation features of the kirigami metallic glasses. In-situ and ex-situ methods were combined to characterize the deformation behaviour of kirigami metallic glasses. The structures and the stress-concentration regions of the kirigami metallic glasses after deformation were also examined. Objective 3. The effect of cut-distances, curved elements and circle-shaped node-cuts of the kirigami patterns on the stretchability and elasticity of kirigami MGs was investigated. Three deformation stages of the kirigami MGs were characterized. The excellent elastic performance of the MGs is associated with the second stage of deformation, where out-of-plane bending and rotation of the struts play a dominant role. The super elastic performance is mainly attributed to the elastic bending of the kirigami elements, and the bending energy of kirigami elements is found to be in good agreement with the stretchability of the samples with different kirigami patterns. Objective 4. A beam deflection mechanism was proposed for the analyses of the transition during the elastic deformation stage. The intensity of force concentration that gives a prediction of the relationship between the fracture force and the kirigami geometric size was also introduced in the analyses of plastic deformation behaviour. Furthermore, the critical force prediction model at the micrometer scale, which was verified by the experimental kirigami response of the scaled samples, was proposed. Based on the theoretical models, the relationships between the intrinsic materials properties and the external geometric parameters, and the size effect in the kirigami metallic glasses were revealed. Objective 5. Tb55Co30Fe15 metallic glass ribbons with good glass formability and a giant reversible magnetostriction were fabricated by injecting the melt of the metallic glass to a rotating copper roller under the protection of pure Ar. Their magnetic properties, magnetostriction and strain-magnetic properties of the ribbons were characterized. With the introduction of kirigami patterns on the ribbons, their magnetostrictive properties, and the strain-magnetic properties were further investigated and compared with those without kirigami patterns.

15222017.label: Major findings and research outcome
15222017.value: In this project, a series of kirigami patterns were designed for both Fe-based metallic glasses. The krigami patterns of the Fe-based metallic glasses vary in cut distances, curved elements, and node cut. By tailing the kirigami patterns, the kirigami metallic glass exhibited programmable super elasticity with values larger than 277%. A highly stretchable kirigami metallic glass (MG) structure with ultra-small strain energy loss during cyclic loading was developed. Less than 3% of strain energy loss is achieved after 1000 loading/unloading cycles, which is much smaller than the Kapton or nanocomposites-based kirigami structures. The underlying deformation mechanisms for these metallic glasses were analyzed. The super elastic performance is mainly attributed to the elastic bending of the kirigami units rather than rigid deformation. The research reveals the deformation mechanism of the kirigami metallic materials and the entitled "Programmable super elastic kirigami metallic glasses" was published in Materials and Design. Ten scaled krigami patterns are prepared. The size effect was found in the mechanical response of the kirigami samples. To further study the size effect and the origin of kirigami response of the kirigami structures, the beam deflection theory and the force concentration mechanism was developed in the analyses. Based on the beam deflection theory, the study reveals the elastic buckling deformation of the krigami metallic glasses and develops a critical force prediction model. Based on the force concentration theory, the study reveals the local force distribution on the kirigami patterns in the out-of-plane rigid plastic deformation stage and predicts the nominal ultimate force. The kirigami-inspired fracture force model is firstly proposed. The predictions of the model are in good agreement with the experimental data. Based on these findings, a journal paper entitled "Critical transition in the shape morphing of kirigami metallic glass" was published in Journal of Materials Science & Technology. Three different orders of pattern levels were architected for kirigami structures for both square and strip units. The relationship between the degree of freedom and the mechanical response of the hierarchical metallic glasses is studied. It was found that a high degree of freedom contributes to the large stretchability of kirigami metallic glasses. The high-order kirigami metallic glasses that possess a high degree of freedom show large stretchability. And the square kirigami samples with a high degree of freedom show large stretchability than strip kirigami samples with a low degree of freedom at the same hierarchical level. Based on the findings, a journal paper entitled "Architected hierarchical kirigami metallic glass with programmable stretchability" was published in AIP Advances.

15222017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15222017.value: The present project revealed that kirigami patterns are an important factor affecting the stretchability and functional properties of kirigami metallic glass. It is of significance to better understand the underlying magnetostriction mechanisms of the kirigami-inspired structures and to further enhance the magnetostrictive property of kirigami metallic glasses for industry applications. New research funding will be applied in due course to support these research work.

15222017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15222017.value: Over the past few decades, metallic glasses have attracted a lot of research attention due to their promising mechanical properties such as high elasticity and strength. However, their poor room temperature ductility has hindered their applications. This project applied the paper cutting technique, Kirigami to architect external structures and improve the stretchability of metallic glasses. By optimizing kirigami patterns, designed MGs approached a large stretchability of 277%, and an ultra-small strain energy loss of less than 3% after 1000 loading cycles was obtained. Based on the beam deflection theory, the elastic buckling behavior of kirigami metallic glass was manifested and a critical force prediction model was developed. Moreover, a force concentration parameter was introduced in the rigid-plastic deformation stage, predicting the nominal ultimate force. The kirigami-inspired fracture force was firstly proposed. The findings of the models are in good agreement with the experimental data. The results open up a new window for developing metallic metamaterials with superior mechanical properties. The kirigami MGs can also be used as substrates for a wide range of stretchable optoelectronic/electronic devices/sensors to maintain stable functionality within a longer cycle life.

15222217.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15222217.value: 用高頻地基和空基GNSS監測數據研究熱帶氣旋對GNSS信號質量的影響

15222217.label: Project Objectives
15222217.value: The goal of this research is to investigate the impact of tropical cyclones, a newly recognized error source for GNSS in tropical regions, on GNSS signal quality by using high-rate ground- and space-based GNSS monitoring observations. The aim is to enhance our understanding of GNSS error source and to improve GNSS positioning accuracy and reliability during TC impacts. More specifically, this project will achieve the following objectives: (1) Evaluating and characterizing GNSS signal quality under the impact of TC of various intensities, using a suite of parameters including GNSS carrier phase cycle slip occurrence rate, measurement noise level, rate of total electron contents (ROT) index (ROTI), and GNSS positioning accuracy. It will represent the first investigation in the GNSS community to study the impact of TC on GNSS signal quality. Numerical analyses of various parameters characterizing GNSS signal quality will be conducted for a few TC. (2) Developing a novel algorithm to evaluate GNSS noise levels for both pseudorange and carrier phase measurements using only one single GNSS receiver. This is different from the traditional noise evaluation method of using two receivers at a short- or zero-baseline. This new algorithm is fundamental for all data analysis in the GNSS community. (3) Generating new knowledge of the relationship between the severity of GNSS signal quality degradation and the intensity of TC through the analysis of some historical TC data and ground- and space-based GNSS data. The new knowledge gained from this project will for the first time provide a valuable guideline for high-precision GNSS users/applications to assess the risk and impact during the passage of TC.

15222217.label: Realisation of objectives
15222217.value: To achieve the first objective (objective completed 100%), we investigated the ionosphere-related parameters based on GPS observations collected at three Hong Kong GNSS monitoring network stations (HKOH, HKPC, and HKST) and one ionospheric scintillation monitoring receiver (ISMR) station in the south of Hong Kong during TC events. The parameters are the scintillation index (S4), cycle slips (CS), and total electron contents rate (TECR). We utilized the well-performed and reliable algorithm developed by previous researchers to calculate these parameters. Then, we comprehensively demonstrated the TC impact on GNSS signals quality in the case of TC Usagi in 2013. The results suggest that GNSS signals are largely contaminated by the TC event. Specifically, the ionospheric scintillation events on the second day after the TC’s landfall increased suddenly from 40 to 500 (around 12 times). Correspondingly, the cycle slips on GNSS measurements occurred more frequently (around 4 times the average value of 80), and the GNSS-derived TECR value had a substantial standard deviation (around 3 times the normal value of 0.5 TECU/sec) (project research output: Yu and Liu 2021a). Furthermore, we found that the large observation noise shares a consistent distribution in the temporal and spatial domains. The anomalies of the detected parameters (S4, CS, and TECR) occurred during the period from 12:00 UT to 18:00 UT on the second day after the TC’s landfall. We pinpointed the ionospheric pierce point (IPP) locations of the irregularities on the assumed ionospheric single layer with an altitude of 450 km from the Earth’s surface and found that they had the same positions on the ionospheric layer for the same GPS satellites of G04, G05, G14, G15, G21, G24, and G29. On the other hand, the contaminated GNSS measurements reflected that the ionospheric in the upper atmosphere were indirectly affected by the convection in the lower atmosphere. To facilitate the space weather research, we proposed a reconstructed vertical total electron (VTEC) observation (HeVTEC). It is defined as follows: VTECnew(i) = {VTECi(s) | s is the satellite with the maximum elevation at the epoch i} where i is the epoch number; s is the GPS satellite with the maximum elevation angle at the epoch i. The proposed VTEC observation can help to detect the ionospheric disturbance above a given GNSS station on the Earth. For instance, we observed obvious ionospheric disturbances during the TC Hato event via analyzing the reconstructed VTEC time series based on GPS measurements collected at the HKSC station in Hong Kong. The results show that the daily maximum of HeVTEC soared from 30 TECU to 62 TECU during the 2017 TC Hato. We also found that the VTEC spatial gradients above the landfall area increased by around 50% and 200% in the north-to-south and west-to-east directions, respectively. Furthermore, most ionospheric disturbances on the TC landfall day occurred in the northwest of Hong Kong, along the TC moving direction (project research output: Yu et al. 2021). Regarding GNSS positioning accuracy during TC event, we used different positioning software, e.g. Bernese 5.2, RTKLIB, and self-developed software, to assess the GPS performance in the precise point positioning (PPP) and relative positioning modes during the TC event. The results suggest that the contaminated GPS signals led to poor positioning performance on the second day after the landfall of the TC Usagi 2013. For the PPP mode, the degradation of positioning performance on the TC-impacted day was ~ 138%, ~ 181%, and ~ 460% in the east (root mean square (RMS) of positioning errors 0.050 m), north (RMS 0.045 m), and up (RMS 0.185 m), respectively, compared with RMS of 0.021 m in the east, 0.016 m in the north, and 0.033 m in the up on normal days. For the relative positioning mode, the positioning errors in the east (RMS 0.134 m) and north (RMS 0.118 m) directions were ~ 7.1 and ~ 7.9 times the average RMS 0.019 m in the east and 0.015 m in the north. The positioning errors in the up (RMS 0.513 m) component on the TC-impacted day were ~ 12.2 times larger than the RMS of 0.042 m on normal days. Following the research work of the first objective, in the second objective (objective completed 100%) we analyzed the post residuals of the positioning errors on GPS pseudo-range and carrier phase measurements in the PPP and relative modes during the TC event of Usagi in 2013. The results show that large post residuals of the positioning results occurred in the present of irregularity of ionosphere-related parameters (12:00 UT – 18:00 UT). For instance, the standard deviation of the post residuals of G05 satellite increased from 0.1 m to 1.8 m on pseudorange measurements and from 0.003 m to 0.015 m on carrier phase measurements when the ionospheric disturbance occurred during 12:00 UT -14:00 UT on the second day after the TC landfall. Similar conclusions can be drawn for the relative positioning mode. For example, the standard deviation of the post residuals of G02 satellite increased from 0.1 m to 1.0 m on pseudorange measurements and from 0.010 m to 0.015 m on carrier phase measurements, at 12:00 UT on the second day after the TC landfall. In terms of the third objective (objective completed 100%), the relationship between the signal degradation and the TC intensities has been extensively and carefully investigated. To get a comprehensive view of how the GPS performance is affected by the severe convection, we investigated the performance of GPS positioning application in Taiwan and Hong Kong regions, which are located near the trajectory of the TC Hato event. In the Hong Kong region, the RMS of positioning errors in the 3D component suddenly increased at a rate of ~9.86 mm/h within seven hours (00:00 UT and 07:00 UT on August 22, 2017) on the TC landfall day. In comparison, the TC swiped Taiwan for more than one day, and the RMS of positioning errors gradually climbed at a rate of 1.2 mm/h. Furthermore, the peak RMS (156.5 mm) on the TC-impacted day is more than 3 times the average RMS on the non-TC-impacted days (44.2 mm) (project research output: Yu and Liu 2021b). We also get a deep insight into the positioning result when the TC Hato hit the Hong Kong region. Interestingly, we found that the positioning errors varied with a period of 2-5 hours during the TC landfall phase. Then, we further investigated the extra data (weather radar image) and drew a conclusion that the periodical variation in the positioning error was caused by the rainbands near the TC center (project research output: Yu and Liu 2021c). In short, this project has achieved all of the three proposed project objectives successfully. One PhD student has been successfully trained and he completed his oral examination in November 2022. The PI and his research team have gained and shared with the research community the new knowledge regarding how to probe the tropical cyclones using the powerful GNSS tool and how the tropical cyclones impact on the GNSS observations. The new knowledge generated from this project shed new light for the research community on the monitoring of tropical cyclones using a new tool from a viewpoint different from traditional ones. It also sets an excellent foundation for the PI to continue future research in this direction.

The aim is to enhance our understanding of GNSS error source and to improve GNSS positioning accuracy and reliability during TC impacts. More specifically, this project will achieve the following objectives: (1) Evaluating and characterizing GNSS signal quality under the impact of TC of various intensities, using a suite of parameters including GNSS carrier phase cycle slip occurrence rate, measurement noise level, rate of total electron contents (ROT) index (ROTI), and GNSS positioning accuracy. It will represent the first investigation in the GNSS community to study the impact of TC on GNSS signal quality. Numerical analyses of various parameters characterizing GNSS signal quality will be conducted for a few TC.

(2) Developing a novel algorithm to evaluate GNSS noise levels for both pseudorange and carrier phase measurements using only one single GNSS receiver. This is different from the traditional noise evaluation method of using two receivers at a short- or zero-baseline. This new algorithm is fundamental for all data analysis in the GNSS community.

(3) Generating new knowledge of the relationship between the severity of GNSS signal quality degradation and the intensity of TC through the analysis of some historical TC data and ground- and space-based GNSS data. The new knowledge gained from this project will for the first time provide a valuable guideline for high-precision GNSS users/applications to assess the risk and impact during the passage of TC.

15222217.label: Major findings and research outcome
15222217.value: 6.1 Major findings and research outcome a. The TC-surrounding PWV over different ocean basins is changing its normal properties under the context of global climate changes. The PWV content within 600 km from TC center shows a significant increasing trend (0.72 kg·m-2·decade-1 on average over different basins) from 2008 to 2020. The PWV spatial gradient near TC center increased by 45% and 35% over the eastern and western North Pacific Ocean and decreased by 42% over the South India Ocean during the period. In terms of the PWV spatial gradient distribution, the gradient in the TC’s western side is around 2.34 times as large as the one in the eastern side. b. The PWV temporal and spatial evolutions over the coastal regions (Hong Kong and Taiwan) were investigated based on the GNSS-derived and ERA5-derived PWV data in the case of TC Hato in 2017. The results suggested that the TC-concentrated PWV started to invade the landfall regions with a distance of 500-700 km. During the landfall phase, the PWV content above the landfall area reached up to 75 kg·m-2, which was around 50 kg·m-2 in the normal weather condition, and the PWV spatial gradient almost doubled from 1.0 to 1.9 (Hong Kong) and 4.7 to 10.6 (Taiwan). Furthermore, the PWV variation featured a period of 2-5 hours, which stems from the strip structure of the rainband. c. The ionospheric irregularities during the TC landfall phase (Hato in 2017) were observed in the west of Hong Kong by analyzing the reconstructed VTEC time series (HeVTEC). In details, the maximum HeVTEC above Hong Kong doubled from 30 TECU to 62 TECU on the TC landfall day. With respect to the VTEC under the normal condition, the VTEC mean bias soared from 5 TECU to 20 TECU on the landfall day. d. The GNSS signal and data quality was adversely affected during the TC events. The ionospheric scintillation events during the Usagi 2013 event rocketed from 40 to 500 (around 12 times). Correspondingly, the cycle slips in GNSS measurements occurred much more frequently (around 4 times), and the GNSS-derived TECR value had a substantial increase in standard deviation (around 3 times). The contaminated GNSS measurements resulted in a poor GNSS positioning performance. On average, the positioning errors during the TC period (Usagi 2013 and Hato 2017) increased by 200%. Additionally, the positioning results varied with a period of 2-5 hours, which was caused by the same periodical variation of PWV.

15222217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15222217.value: 6.2 Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action This research work attempts to explore the linkage between tropospheric tropical cyclone events, ionospheric disturbances, and GNSS performance. This is an exciting, complex topic for which many new potential work can be further explored. a. The scope of research work can be extended to worldwide TC events over a much longer historical TC event chain. Currently, the number of TC events studied in our research work is still limited and the study area is focused in Hong Kong. It is definitely worthwhile to study the global TC events over a long period of time based on the historical TC and GNSS observation data. Thus a more comprehensive global understanding of the complex relationship among tropospheric tropical cyclone events, ionospheric disturbances, and GNSS performance can be reached. b. The research work also can be further improved via introducing multi-source observation data. In this project, the observation data are primarily derived from GNSS. To further explore the TC, different types of observation instruments can be used to complement the GNSS. c. Hopefully functional formulae can be developed in the future to precisely locate the TC and even predict how the TC will evolve.

15222217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15222217.value: 7 The Layman’s Summary Tropical cyclone is a destructive hazard to the lives and properties over coastal cities. The global casualty toll caused by the TC event was estimated to approximate 8,000 every year, and the financial losses were around US$ 26 billion. Moreover, these numbers are still increasing due to global warming. The increasing sea surface temperature (SST) provides much more energy for the TC genesis and leads to a new era of the TC climatology. Motivated by the harsh situation, we proposed a research topic to investigate the TC impacts in Hong Kong region using the GNSS technique. The major contributions can be summarized as the follows: a. We quantified the TC-surrounding PWV trend over different ocean basins from 2008 and 2020 for the first time. This work can help us numerically understand the exact impact of global warming on the TC’s ability to concentrate water vapor. b. We presented the exact evolution of PWV near coastal cities during the TC landfall phase. This can guide us to do a good preparation for the TC’s invasion. c. We provided evidence to show the coupling between lower and upper atmospheric activities. This can help us further understand the dynamics of the atmosphere during TC events.

15222317.label: Project Objectives
15222317.value: Discover the original sensitive operations in hardened apps. We will devise a novel learning-based mechanism to recognize the original operations from hardened apps. Then, we will propose new mechanisms to explore the sensitive operations after locating the private data. Recognize the sensitive operations from apps' text data. We will design new algorithms to accurately identify the sensitive operations and the corresponding constraints from apps' privacy policies and descriptions. Then, we will propose novel algorithms to correctly recognize the sensitive operations reported in users' comments. Identify the unexpected sensitive operations. We will design new tools to automatically identify the unexpected sensitive operations. It is worth noting that this project will not examine the issues in the area of human computer interaction, such as how to organize and visualize the information for effectively informing users.

15222317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15222317.value: 智能手机常包含大量需要保护的隐私信息。与此同时，这些信息被各种移动应用所觊觎。虽然不少隐私防护方法被提出，它们有如下的不足。首先，虽然这些方法可以发现并禁止访问隐私信息的操作，但这并不能辅助用户做出正确的隐私决策，因为合法的应用也会需要执行这种操作。此外，最新的应用加固技术将阻止这些方法来对应用进行分析。其次，虽然最近一些方法提出从应用的文本数据中提取信息来提醒用户非预期的应用行为，但是这些方法有大量的误报率和漏报率。本项目将研发一个创新的框架，通过分析多个信息源来揭示移动应用中的非预期敏感行为。在这个研究中，我们将解决一系列具有挑战的难题，包括从加固的移动应用中识别敏感行为，从文本数据中识别敏感行为及约束等。我们将基于之前在移动应用分析和文本处理的经验来研发新的方法及系统。这个项目将对移动隐私保护提供新的理论基础和实用系统，如（1）监控和分析加固应用的系统；（2）从应用的文本数据中推测敏感行为及其约束条件的工具。本研究将帮助用户更好的分析和理解加固的移动应用以及相关的文本信息。

15222317.label: Realisation of objectives
15222317.value: We have realized the three objectives. 1. Discover the original sensitive operations in hardened apps. We have proposed a set of new approaches to discover the original sensitive operations in hardened apps. First, we designed new methods and developed practical tools to reveal the original apps’ operations. We first performed cross-layer monitoring for the Android new runtime and developed PackerGrind for recovering the Dex code from the hardened apps. The corresponding paper entitled “PackerGrind: An Adaptive Unpacking System for Android Apps” was accepted by IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering(TSE). We also proposed a novel hardware-assisted approach named Happer that leverages ARM ETM and other hardward features to perform cross-layer monitoring and recover the hidden Dex files. Different from existing studies, Happer can evade the anti-analysis and self-protection mechanisms of packed apps and effectively retrieve all the hidden Dex data and assemble them into a valid Dex. Moreover, it can select proper unpacking strategies according to the observed packing behaviors of packed apps, and it can be easily extended to cover new packing behaviors. The corresponding paper entitled “Happer: Unpacking Android Apps via a Hardware-Assisted Approach” appeared in IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy 2021. We further proposed a novel approach to conduct the first systematic study on VMP-based hardening services and recover the code protected by such packing services. We demystify the VM-based packers under three different scenarios. Since almost all existing commercial packing services are publicly accessible, we first investigate whether the VM-protected code can be recovered with the help of our training apps. Moreover, we investigate whether the semantics of the VM-protected code can be recovered if the training apps and the target apps are packed by the different versions of packers. Furthermore, we investigate whether the semantics of the VM-protected code can be recovered if we cannot access any packer to build the training apps. The corresponding paper entitled “Parema: An Unpacking Framework for Demystifying VM-Based Android Packers” appeared in ACM SIGSOFT International Symposium on Software Testing and Analysis (ISSTA) 2022. Furthermore, we have conducted concolic execution on apps for exploring the sensitive operations and the methodology appeared in the paper entitled “PERDICE: Towards Discovering Software Inefficiencies Leading to Cache Misses and Branch Mispredictions”, which appeared in IEEE Annual Computer Software and Applications Conference (COMPSAC) 2018. We have also located the private data from three sources including sensitive APIs and the content providers using sensitive URIs, user inputs through app UI, and apps’ privacy policies and user comments. We locate the text labels by dynamically exploring all UI components and handle those dynamically generated UI components. The technique was used in our paper entitled “MadDroid: Characterizing and Detecting Devious Ad Contents for Android Apps”, which appeared in WWW 2020. We further explore how UI components can be manipulated so that existing UI analysis methods may fail to handle them. The corresponding paper entitled "UI Obfuscation and Its Effects on Automated UI Analysis for Android Apps" appeared in IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering (ASE) 2020. 2. Recognize the sensitive operations from apps' text data. We proposed new approaches to determine the sensitive operations and the constraints from apps’ privacy policies and the descriptions. When analyzing apps’ privacy policies, we designed a new approach to identify the constraints under which the sensitive operations will be performed along with the purposes and/or reasons of collecting sensitive information. Moreover, we proposed a new approach to construct patterns for locating sentences mentioning sensitive operations and designed a new pattern selection algorithm based on random walks to filter out irrelevant patterns. Besides studying apps’ privacy policies, we enhanced the state-of-the-art tool AutoCog to examine apps’ descriptions. The corresponding paper entitled “PPChecker: Towards Accessing the Trustworthiness of Android Apps' Privacy Policies” was accepted by TSE. We have proposed new approaches to analyze user comments for spotting the sensitive operations from user comments. These new approaches lead to three papers. One paper entitled “CHAMP: Characterizing Undesired App Behaviors from User Comments based on Market Policies” appeared in ICSE 2021, where we proposed a novel approach that adopts text mining and NLP techniques to extract semantic rules and classifies comments into 26 pre-defined types of undesired behaviors. Another paper entitled “Where2Change: Change Request Localization for App Reviews” was accepted by TSE, where we leveraged NLP techniques to extract information of sensitive operations from user comments. The third paper entitled “Towards Automatically Localizing Function Errors in Mobile Apps with User Reviews” was submitted to TSE and is under major revision. In this paper, we further exploit the context information in user comments and correlate the comments and bytecode through their semantic meanings. Since there may be lots of user comments for some apps and it would cost lots of time to go through all comments, we proposed a novel approach that utilizes historical reviews to suggest the time when most of the useful information appears in reviews of a certain version. The corresponding paper entitled “STRE: An Automated Approach to Suggesting App Developers When to Stop Reading Reviews” was submitted to TSE and is under major revision. 3. Identify the unexpected sensitive operations and create privacy notes. We designed novel approaches and developed new tools to automatically identify the unexpected sensitive operations and generate clear and detailed privacy notes. For example, we found that inappropriate use of Application Performance Management libraries for apps can cause privacy leaks. The corresponding paper entitled “A Systematical Study on Application Performance Management Libraries for Apps” was accepted by TSE. We also observed that many apps are using third-party libraries with vulnerabilities that could be exploited by attackers to collect private information. The corresponding paper entitled “ATVHunter: Reliable Version Detection of Third-Party Libraries for Vulnerability Identification in Android Apps” appeared in ICSE 2021 and received ACM SIGSOFT Distinguished Paper Award. Moreover, we identified the limitations of existing tools for discovering third-party libraries from apps. The corresponding paper entitled “A Systematic Assessment on Android Third-party Library Detection Tools” was accepted by TSE. We further developed a taxonomy for existing studies on third-party libraries in Android apps and pointed out the research directions in a paper entitled “Research on Third-Party Libraries in Android Apps: A Taxonomy and Systematic Literature Review”, which was accepted by TSE. We also revealed that the vulnerabilities in Android system may be exploited by attackers to collect user information. For example, we found that the vulnerabilities in the App links can be exploited by attackers to launch various attacks for collecting users’ information, and the corresponding paper entitled “All Your App Links Are Belong to Us: Understanding the Threats of Instant Apps Based Attacks” appeared in ACM Joint European Software Engineering Conference and Symposium on the Foundations of Software Engineering (ESEC/FSE) 2020. We also revealed that adversaries can conduct resource race attack (RRAttack) to capture the sensitive information in the camera view, and the corresponding paper entitled “Resource Race Attacks on Android” appeared in IEEE International Conference on Software Analysis, Evolution and Reengineering (SANER) 2020. Moreover, we have conducted user studies on the effectiveness of our new approaches and the experimental results show that the privacy notes generated by our tool can help user recognize more privacy-related behaviors and increase their awareness of privacy issues.
