15222317.label: Major findings and research outcome
15222317.value: We found that it is challenging to discover the original sensitive operations in hardened apps because they usually adopt various anti-analysis and bytecode-hiding techniques. To address these challenges, we first propose PackerGrind, an adaptive unpacking system for recovering the hidden Dex data, and then design Happer, the first hardware-based unpacker that can circumvent the anti-analysis techniques adopted by hardened apps and collect the hidden Dex data effectively. However, these systems cannot handle VM-based packing mechanisms that replace the original Dalvik bytecode with customized. Hence, we proposed Parema, the first system for unpacking VM-protected apps and conducted the first systematic study on VM-based hardening services. We also designed novel approaches and developed practical tools for analyzing Android apps, such as parallelized conclic execution, advanced UI analysis and obfuscation techniques. Moreover, we designed new approaches to recognize the sensitive operations from apps' text data, such as their privacy policies and descriptions, user comments, market policies and regulations, etc. It is challenging to examine the text data because they are written in natural languages. We developed new approaches to successfully extract important information from text data and map it to bytecode. By doing so, we can identify the inconsistency between the privacy policy and description of an app and its implementation, discover the compliance issues between an app’s privacy policy/bytecode and market policies/regulations, and locate various issues in an app’s implementation according to user comments. Based on the information collected from several sources, we designed novel approaches to automatically identify the unexpected sensitive operations and generate clear and detailed privacy notes. We found that many apps use vulnerable third-party libraries that could be exploited by attackers to collect private information, the inappropriate use of APM libraries for apps can cause privacy leaks, and the vulnerabilities in Android system may be exploited by attackers to collect user information. Moreover, the privacy notes generated by us can help user recognize more privacy-related behaviors and increase their awareness of privacy issues. In this project, we have published 6 papers in the prestigious journal IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering and 13 papers in top conferences like IEEE S&P/ICSE/FSE/ASE/ISSTA/WWW and received one ACM SIGSOFT Distinguished Paper Award. Two journal paper submitted to IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering are under major revision. We trained two Ph.D. students, one M.Sc. student, and several undergraduate students. Moreover, we have been collaborating with the researchers in several universities on this research.

15222317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15222317.value: Although we designed and developed novel tools to discover the original sensitive operations in hardened apps, the hardening services are evolving and will adopt new techniques to prevent the hidden bytecode from being recovered. Hence, one direction for further development of this research is to explore the design space of packing techniques and develop robust approaches to recover the bytecode hidden by mobile malware. As we focus on Android apps in this project, one direction is to develop techniques and tools for inspecting iOS apps, because they have not been systematically investigated due to the lack of effective analysis tools. Since the text data of apps is also evolving, another direction for further development of this research is to design advanced NLP techniques to understand the meaning of text data in a more accurate and efficient manner. Moreover, as we just study text data in English in this project, one direction is to develop NLP-based approaches to analyze the text data in other languages. As adversaries are adopt more stealthy methods to collect application-specific private information, another promising direction is to develop efficient methods and tools to identify and track such information and inform users if their privacy is invaded.

15222317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15222317.value: Being an indispensable part of our daily lives, smartphones usually contain lots of private data whose privacy should be well protected. Unfortunately, both malware and legitimate apps may collect such data without users’ full awareness. The situation becomes worse on Android, because it is the target of the majority of mobile malware and not all Android apps have passed through a rigorous app review process, let alone the difficulty for normal users to understand the permissions and apps’ privacy policies and the challenges for security analyst to discover the sensitive operations in hardened apps. In this project, we developed new techniques to correctly identify sensitive operations of hardened apps, and proposed new algorithms to effectively and efficiently analyze privacy policies, descriptions and user comments. Moreover, our approaches can identify the unexpected sensitive operations by capturing the contradictions among the operations discovered from hardened apps, the operations inferred from apps’ text data, and the operations reported by other users, discover private information leakage via apps and their embedded third-party libraries, and generate clear and detailed privacy notes to help app users recognize more privacy-related behaviors and increase their awareness of privacy issues.

15223017.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15223017.value: 沉積物對香港半自然河流的棲息地復收實驗和數值調查

15223017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15223017.value: Rivers always attracts human settlements as they provide a variety of fluvial ecosystem benefits in terms of water supply, navigation, irrigation, power generation, flood discharge, waste discharge, landscape, recreational opportunities and habitats for economically important fisheries etc. (Poff et al., 2003). The inherent complexity in the relationship between abiotic and biotic ecosystem functions constitutes a challenge in understanding the functionality of fluvial ecosystems (Wohl et al., 2007). In Hong Kong, in order to mitigate flooding hazards, many rivers that pass through urban areas have been trained into concrete channels with straight, wide and deep configurations. Although a few local rivers, such as Tung Chung River, have not been extensively channelized and are still in semi-natural condition, from an ecological perspective, the original river habitat has been severely abused by channelization. There are different aspects to assess the health of a river, including the abiotic part - sediment transport ability, water depth, flow velocity, bed morphology, floodplain and riparian zone health as well as the biotic parts - aquatic vegetation, fishes, benthic macroinvertebrate, water birds and so on. It is believed that a successful river restoration is indispensable from the consideration of sediment transport. Either sediment in excess or sediment in deficit in a river system is likely to have some fundamental impact on the process and form of rivers, leading to the degradation of ecosystems. There exists a knowledge gap in river restoration that is the integration of sediment transport and river ecological restoration. Some studies on fish spawning sites take the physical-biota relationships into consideration and have made significant advancement on simulating flow conditions and sediment transport behavior for fish habitats. In this project, research effort will be aimed at modifying the water flow and sediment regime according to the aquatic habitat requirement in order to attract local fish and macroinvertebrate back to some semi-natural river sections in the lowland areas in Hong Kong where the rivers meet the sea. Experimental and numerical modeling methods will be employed to investigate and determine suitable aquatic habitat conditions. It is one of the goals in the present research to make use of the research results to develop a useful guideline for future channel restoration design for semi-natural rivers which are deserved to be protected due to their high biodiversity. 河流總是吸引人類住區，因為它們在供水，導航，灌溉，發電，洪水排放，廢物排放，景觀，娛樂和經濟，漁的棲息地等方面提供了各種各樣的河流生態系統優勢。 非生物和生物生態系統功能之間關係的內在復雜性在理解河流生態系統的功能方面構成了一個挑戰。 在香港，為了減輕淹水危害，經過城市的許多河流已經被訓練成具有直線，廣泛和深度配置的具體渠道。 雖然一些當地的河流，如東涌河，尚未廣泛渠道化，仍處於半自然狀態，但從生態的角度來看，原始的河流棲息地受到渠道化的嚴重濫用。 在這個項目中，研究工作將旨在改變水流和沈積物根據水生棲息地要求，將本地魚類和大型無脊椎動物吸引回到半自然河段的低緯地區。 將採用實驗和數值模擬方法來研究和確定適宜的水生棲息地條件。 本研究的目標之一是利用研究成果為自然河流的未來渠道復收設計製定有用的指導方針，從而其生物多樣性可高度受到保護。

15223117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15223117.value: High-strength steel materials are constructional steel materials with yield strengths ranging from 690 to 960 N/mm2, and they are readily produced in many countries at affordable prices recently. Many engineers believe adoption of these steel materials will lead to a major advancement in structural engineering as there will be fundamental changes to the ways super high-rise buildings and long span bridges are being constructed. New structural forms will then become not only technically feasible, but also financially viable. Despite high structural advantages offered by high-strength steel materials, there are challenges to promote wide adoption of these steel materials in construction. One of the key concerns is limited deformation ductility of these steel materials and their welded sections as their elongation limits at fracture in standard tensile tests are found to be smaller than those of commonly used steel materials. As modern seismic resistant design always assumes that all structural steel members and systems possess a high degree of ductility, it is essential to provide experimental evidence to demonstrate adequacy of ductility in these steel materials. Alternatively, complementary design rules for effective use of these steel materials and their welded connections under cyclic loads should be developed (Bjorhovde, 2015). In this project, it is proposed to conduct three comprehensive experimental investigations to establish adequacy of welded connections and weldments of high-strength steel materials for application in seismic resistant design. Data analysis on test results of these investigations will be performed to establish hysteretic behaviour of high-strength steel welded sections and weldments under i) axial forces only, ii) shear forces only, and iii) various combinations of co-existing axial and shear forces. More importantly, effects of heat inputs onto the hysteretic behaviour of these welded connections and joints will also be assessed thoroughly. Key findings of the project will be highly relevant to structural engineers in Hong Kong as they are often required to perform seismic resistant design on high-rise buildings in major cities in the Region. Despite deflection control is critical in many high-rise buildings, the use of high-strength steel materials is able to reduce member sizes, and thus increase usable floor areas, in particular in lower floors. Moreover, application of high-strength steel materials to columns in upper floors will facilitate construction as these columns will be smaller in size and lighter in weight for lifting and erection at height, when compared with those commonly used steel materials. 高强钢是屈服强度为690到960 N/mm2的建筑钢材。近期，许多国家已经能够生产出质优价廉的高强钢钢材。很多工程师认为采用高强钢会使高层建筑和大跨度桥梁的施工方式发生根本的改变，从而促进结构工程领域的重大进步。因此，新型结构形式将变得同时在技术上和经济上可行。 虽然高强钢在结构性能上有显著优势，唯其在建筑行业的广泛推广应用，仍面临着诸多的挑战。其中最关键的问题是高强钢材以及其焊接截面的延性较小。以往的标准拉伸试验表明，高强钢钢材和焊接截面的断后延伸率小于普通钢材。而由于现代的结构抗震设计通常假设所有结构构件和结构体系都具有高度延性，因此，提供实验证据，证明高强钢具有充足延性是非常必要的。另外，应当针对高强钢的有效使用及其焊接截面在循环荷载作用下的性能，发展补充的设计规范。 本课题旨在通过进行三项综合性的实验研究，证明高强钢的焊接截面及焊接件的性能足以应用于抗震设计。通过对实验结果进行数据分析，得到高强钢焊接截面和焊接件在i)轴力作用，ii)剪力作用，iii)不同的轴力和剪力组合共同作用下的滞回性能。更重要的是，焊接热输入量对截面和焊接节点滞回性能的影响也将被充分研究。 本课题的研究成果将对香港的结构工程业界产生重要的影响，因为涉及足中国内地主要城市的高层建筑抗震设计时，抗震性能需要被充分考虑进去。尽管在高层建筑中挠度控制是至关重要的一环，但是使用高强钢可以减小构件尺寸，进而增大使用面积，特别是对低楼层适用。此外，与常用钢柱相比，高强钢柱的尺寸小，重量轻。如果将它应用在高层柱构件上，则能够极大地方便高处吊装和安装施工。

15223117.label: Realisation of objectives
15223117.value: This project aims to investigate experimentally the structural response of high strength S690 welded sections under various cyclic loading conditions. Hence, a series of experimental investigations into i) coupons of welded sections under axial deformations, and ii) welded joints between tubular sections under in-plane bending were conducted, and details of these tests were reported as follows: i) Coupons of welded sections under axial deformations for Objective 1 A total of 32 cyclic tests were carried out under two different cyclic protocols with various combinations of target strains ε_T and loading frequencies f_L, as reported in Paper 2. Particular focus was given to assessing key structural response related to the cyclic tests, including: i) strength deteriorations, ii) numbers of effective cycles completed before fracture, and iii) hysteretic energy dissipation densities. The main structural response parameters for the S690 welded sections subjected to cumulative cyclic loading were quantified and compared with those of the unwelded S690 steel plate counterparts which were reported in Paper 1. A number of important conclusions can be drawn from this study: a) In general, Cyclic Protocol CT, in which constant strain amplitude cycles are applied up to fracture, is significantly more demanding when compared with the more gradual Cyclic Protocol NL. Whilst the former is considered an overly severe representation of seismic loading, it can be used as an effective approach for assessing the inelastic cyclic response of the S690 welded sections in comparison with that of the S690 steel plates. b) Cyclic softening in the hysteretic loops of the coupons of the S690 welded sections under Cyclic Protocol CT were evident. The corresponding numbers of cycles completed before fracture, n_c, for the S690 welded sections were found to be typically only half or even one third of those for the S690 steels. Hence, the structural response of the S690 steel plates was shown to deteriorate more significantly after welding under various cyclic actions. c) Deteriorations in both the strength and the energy dissipation performance of the S690 welded sections under accumulated cyclic deformations according to Cyclic Protocol CT were more severe than those of the S690 steel plates. These deteriorations were readily quantified in terms of the numbers of effective cycles completed before fracture, the strength adjustment factors and the hysteretic energy dissipation densities. d) The coupons of the S690 welded sections under Cyclic Protocol NL were able to complete 20 cycles at a target strain ε_T of ±5.0%. When the target strain ε_T was increased to ±7.5%, the coupons of the welded sections failed prematurely. Hence, a ± 5.0% strain might be considered as the strain limit of the S690 steel plates and their welded sections in seismic resistant design. The test results showed that there was always a significant deterioration in the strengths of both the S690 steel plates and the S690 welded sections when the cycle numbers increased, with such reductions being more pronounced under large target strains. In terms of ductility, the number of effective cycles to fracture, n_c, for the S690 welded sections were shown to be considerably smaller than that for the S690 steel plates, typically by a factor of 2 to 3. Moreover, the hysteretic energy dissipation densities of the S690 welded sections, E_WS, were found to be only 0.41 to 0.47 of those of the S690 steel plates, E_SP. Overall, the experimental assessments and discussions presented in this study provide detailed insights into the structural response of S690 welded sections in steel structures under earthquake attacks, and emphasize the importance of going beyond monotonic tensile tests in quantifying ductility for seismic resistant design. The results also provide novel experimental data that can be used in calibrating detailed numerical cyclic models, as well as offer quantified information that can be used for determining ductility criteria for use in assessment and design procedures. ii) Welded joints between tubular sections under brace in-plane bending for Objectives 2 and 3 In Paper 3, a comprehensive investigation into the structural behaviour of T-joints between high strength S690 cold-formed tubular sections (CFTS) under lateral forces acting onto the braces, i.e. under in-plane bending, and deformation characteristics of these T-joints under both monotonic and cyclic actions were examined experimentally. It should be noted that deformation characteristics of these T-joints under both monotonic and cyclic actions were captured in carefully executed experiments, and then, analyzed rationally. The following conclusions are drawn: a) The T-joints between S690 CFTS under monotonic brace in-plane bending, i.e. Joints M-T1 and M-T2, are found to fail at large deformations with a fracture in the heat-affected zones of the braces in the vicinity of the welded brace/chord junctions. The maximum lateral displacements of these T-joints are found to exceed the lateral displacement corresponding to 5% principal strains in the joints. b) It should be noted that the T-joints between S690 CFTS under cyclic brace in-plane bending, i.e. Joints C-T3 and C-T4, and Joints C-T5 and C-T6, are also found to have a failure similar those of Joints M-T1 and M-T2 mentioned above. Hence, the sudden fracture does not pose any adverse effect on these joints as their resistances have been fully mobilized well before the occurrence of the fracture. c) In general, welding-induced residual stresses along the welded brace/chord junctions are found to have limited effects onto the structural behaviour of these T-joints under brace in-plane bending, in particular, both the moment resistances and the ductility. Consequently, the effects of welding onto the structural behaviour of these T-joints are shown to be significantly less pronounced than generally anticipated, provided that the welding processes and parameters have been properly controlled. Overall, the experimental investigations presented in this study provide detailed insights into the structural response of T-joints between S690 cold-formed tubular sections in steel structures under earthquake attacks. It is demonstrated that these T-joints possess a high degree of cyclic ductility under two different loading protocols, and they are able to response with sufficiently large deformations. The results also provide novel experimental data that can be used in calibrating detailed numerical cyclic models, as well as offer quantified information that can be used for determining ductility criteria for use in assessment and design procedures. In short, these experiments examine the structural responses of the high strength S690 welded sections and joints under seismic actions which are complementary to many similar investigations.

15223117.label: Major findings and research outcome
15223117.value: Despite of excellent high strength to self-weight ratios of the S690 steels, when compared with the S355 steels, there is a widespread concern regarding the ductility of the S690 steels. It is generally considered that the ductility of the S690 steels is significantly lower than that of the S355 steels – this is the general understandings the authors attempt to investigate. A systematic experimental investigation into the cyclic deformation characteristics of both the S355 and the S690 steels under different loading protocols is presented in Paper 1. It is found that: i. Contrary to the general understandings on the ductility of both the S355 and the S690 steels, the cyclic deformation characteristics of both steels are demonstrated to be the same under Loading Protocol V under varying target strains ! ii. The cyclic deformation characteristics of the S690 steels are demonstrated to be inferior to that of the S355 steels under Loading Protocol C with a target strain εm at ±2.5% and f = 0.1 and 1.0 Hz. This agrees with the general understandings. iii. Interestingly, the cyclic deformation characteristics of the S690 steels are demonstrated to be superior to that of the S355 steels under Loading Protocol C with target strains εm at ±5.0, ±7.5 and ±10%, and f = 0.1 and 1.0 Hz. This is contrary once again to the general understandings ! In Paper 2, the cyclic deformation characteristics of the S690 steel plates and their welded sections are examined, and it is found that there are certain deteriorations in both resistances and ductility, depending on the loading protocols. Nevertheless, the cyclic ductility of the S690 welded sections is shown to be sufficient. It is further demonstrated in Paper 3 that the T-joints between S690 cold-formed tubular sections possess a high degree of cyclic ductility, and they are able to response with sufficiently large deformations. Consequently, the experimental evidence allows the international research community for structural engineering and modern steel construction technology to appreciate that the high strength S690 steels do have a good ductility under both monotonic and cyclic actions. Moreover, the findings of this experimental investigation highlight the importance of establishing ductility requirements and cyclic deformation characteristics for the high strength S690 steels in accordance with specifically designed cyclic tests rather than relying solely on conventional monotonic tensile tests.

15223117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15223117.value: The experimental investigation should be further extended to examine cyclic deformation characteristics of typical welded sections of the S355 and the S690 steels having different welding procedures as follows: i) welded sections with different q under cyclic axial deformations; and ii) welded joints with different q under cyclic bending. Systematic experiments should be carried out to assess their structural behaviour, and their cyclic deformation characteristics should be analyzed according to different parameters to register their cyclic ductility. Through an integrated numerical modelling approach developed by the PI, advanced three-dimensional finite element models of the S690 CFTS with solid elements should be established. With a proper definition of weld collars at the brace/chord junctions of the T-joints between the S690 CFTS with different diameters and thicknesses, these models are readily adopted to perform a heat transfer analysis, a thermomechanical analysis and a structural analysis sequentially with compatible element types and meshes. Hence, the effects of the welding-induced residual stresses at the welded brace/chord junctions onto the structural behaviour of these T-joints should then be readily assessed. These models will be able to provide additional insights to the cyclic deformation characteristics of these welded sections and joints under cyclic actions.

15223117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15223117.value: Despite of excellent high strength to self-weight ratios of the S690 steels, when compared with the S355 steels, there is a widespread concern regarding the ductility of the S690 steels. It is generally considered that the ductility of the S690 steels is significantly lower than that of the S355 steels. Through a number of systematic experimental investigations into the cyclic deformation characteristics of both the S355 and the S690 steels and their welded sections and joints, it is shown that contrary to the general understandings on the ductility of the S690 steels, the S690 steels are shown to possess a high level of cyclic ductility. Moreover, both their welded sections and welded joints are shown to have a high degree of cyclic ductility that they are able to response with sufficiently large deformations. The experimental evidence allows the international research community for structural engineering and modern steel construction technology to appreciate that the S690 steel structures do have a good ductility under both monotonic and cyclic actions, when they are properly designed and fabricated. Moreover, it is important to establish ductility requirements for the S690 steels using specifically designed cyclic tests rather than relying solely on conventional monotonic tensile tests.

15223217.value: 在一些突發的地質災害（如山體滑坡和地陷等）發生之前，地面經常有一個變形過程。如果這些變形信號可以足夠早地被檢測到，它們可以用作警報信號，以決定是否採取進一步的行動，包括展開深入現場調查以更好地理解發生的問題或將人員從現場撤離。然而，以足夠的空間分辨率和準確度測量如香港這樣的通常很微小，而且被植被覆蓋的大範圍地面的變形是一項具有挑戰性的任務。 該項目旨在進一步推進乾涉合成孔徑雷達（InSAR）技術，並將其與全球導航衛星系統（GNSS）觀測結合起來以研究香港的地面變形。要開發的創新技術對於今後在香港和其他許多地方研究地質災害應該起到重要作用。研究還將提高對香港地面整體變形的時空特點的理解。結果還將有助於理解香港的構造活動和識別地質災害潛在的發生地點。 眾所周知，香港可用的土地面積非常有限，很多建築物和基礎設施建在陡峭的斜坡上或非常接近斜坡。因此，山體滑坡一直是香港的一個突出問題。此外，香港大面積填海造地，以創造更多的可用土地。填海得到的土地通常會經歷很長一段時間的沉降，可能對建在土地之上或之下的建築物和基礎設施造成損害。地面沉降與垂直地質構造運動以及海平面上升相結合可以大大增加海水入侵和發生洪水的機會。香港已經有大量的地面塌陷事件，造成生命損失，交通混亂和公眾關注。頻繁進行整個香港的地面變形測量將能夠及早發現與地質災害相關的變形信號，以便採取及時的行動，減低災害所造成的損失。 研究成果將有助於InSAR這一重要的空間大地測量技術的發展，並更好地了解香港的地面變形。更重要的是，開發的技術和方法對減少地質災害的損害，挽救生命將起到重要的作用。這個研究結果具有在香港和世界許多其他地方（如地質災害每年造成巨大損失的中國內地）廣泛使用。因此，該項目具有重要的學術和應用價值。

15223217.label: Major findings and research outcome
15223217.value: Objective 1: Better understand the performance of InSAR technology under various conditions when it is applied to study territory wide ground deformation in Hong Kong. The performance of InSAR (Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar) technology under the various atmospheric and site conditions has been studied extensively in the project. It has been found that the technology could work reasonably well in general in most urban and lightly vegetated areas in Hong Kong but it almost did not work at all in the heavily vegetated areas despite the best data processing algorithms were applied (e.g., Bilal et al., 2018; Wu et al., 2019; Ali et al., 2021; Zhang et al., 2021b (Output No. 10); 2021c (Output No. 11)). More research efforts are still needed to further enhance its capabilities to apply it to monitor the deformation of some other parts of Hong Kong. Objective 2: Further develop InSAR technology so that it can be used more effectively in studying ground deformation related to geohazards. We have further developed the capabilities of InSAR technology in the project to make it more effective in studying ground deformation related to geohazards in Hong Kong (e.g., Zhang et al., 2018; Liang et al., 2019; Yang et al., 2020; Zhang et al., 2021a (Output No. 6); 2021c (Output No. 11)), the integration of SAR data from multiple satellites (e.g., Zhang et al., 2021b (Output No. 10); Wu et al., 2021), a more advanced method for better coherent point selection (e.g., Wu et al., 2019), and analysis of the quality of InSAR products (Yang et al., 2020). Objective 3: Study spatiotemporal features of ground deformation in Hong Kong based on all existing and new SAR and GNSS data and assess potential geohazards based on the results. We have studied the ground and structural deformation of Hong Kong extensively (e.g., Qin et al., 2018; Wu et al., 2020; Qin et al., 2019; Wu et al., 2021). For example, we studied with InSAR technology the ground and structural deformation in To Kwa Wan caused by the construction of a new MTR line (Wu et al., 2021). We also built up a deformation history of the Hong Kong International Airport over the past two decades (since its operation) (Wu et al., 2020).

15223217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15223217.value: We have found that InSAR technology worked reasonably well in most urban and lightly vegetated areas in Hong Kong but it almost did not work at all in the heavily vegetated areas despite the best data processing algorithms were applied. Therefore, more research efforts are still needed to further enhance its capabilities in order to apply it to monitor the deformation of some other parts of Hong Kong. The efforts may include development of both new radar sensors (e.g., longer wavelengths and shorter revisit time) and new data analysis algorithms. We have planned some further research targeting to extend the capabilities of InSAR so that it can work under challenging site conditions such as heavily vegetated areas.

15223217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15223217.value: Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) is one of the most powerful spaceborne Earth observation technologies. We have studied extensively the performance of the technology under the various atmospheric and site conditions in Hong Kong. We have also further developed the capabilities of the technology to make it more effective in studying ground deformation related to geohazards in Hong Kong. The development includes better understanding and mitigation of the impacts of atmospheric effects on radar signals when the signals travel through the atmosphere, integration of SAR data from multiple satellites, a more advanced method for better coherent point selection, and analysis of the quality of InSAR products. The research outcome has contributed significantly to the development of InSAR technology and our capabilities to better monitor and understand the deformation of the Earth surface.

15223417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15223417.value: Deteriorating air quality and slow progress in meeting greenhouse gas emission reduction targets are major environmental issues in Hong Kong. As one of the significant pollution and emission sources, heavy construction equipment, powered by diesel engines, emit toxic pollutants including CO, NOx, HC, particulate matter, as well as CO2. Recent regulations on emission compliance for non-road mobile machinery are mainly targeted at equipment newly imported to Hong Kong. Complete replacement of the current stock of 11,300 units working on construction sites will take many years due to their long service lives, if no environment regulations are imposed. How to provide incentives to equipment owners and take regulatory measures to encourage the adoption of emission reduction technologies and the earlier phase-out of in-use equipment, while not escalating contractor’s financial burdens, is a pressing issue in Hong Kong and worldwide. Although there is a consensus agreeing the “carrot and stick” approach to reduce the transition period toward a greener equipment fleet, currently there are no financial models guiding the makers of environmental policy and contractors, which cater for the interests of both the public and equipment stakeholders. A life cycle cost (LCC) analysis model for construction equipment which also allows for environmental policy effects is proposed as the outcome of this research. Environmental policy variables, both the one-off grants/tax exemption for the adoption of emission reduction technologies, or the pollution charge/carbon tax levied on emissions or fuel, based on the polluter-pays principle, will be integrated with the classic LCC analysis model for quantitative numerical analyses. Three models, a deterministic model, a stochastic model, and a computer-based time series model, will be studied to determine the effects of different environmental policy variables. For equipment of different conditions, the levels of impact of various environmental policy scenarios, on equipment LCC and equipment economic life, will be evaluated. Through this research, the interrelationships between equipment conditions, economic conditions, the financial impact of environmental incentives and regulations, technology costs, life cycle costs, and the economic life of representative construction equipment will all be uncovered and presented. The research will make theoretical contributions to the body of knowledge by integrating environmental policy and regulation effects into the classic construction equipment LCC analysis. From a practical point of view, the research will provide guidance to both policy makers and equipment owners, helping them to make informed decisions concerning equipment retrofitting and replacement in relation to emissions reductions. 香港的空氣質量日漸惡化而且政府在達到溫室氣體減排目標方面進度緩慢。由於大多使用柴油發動機，重型施工設備是其中一個顯著的汙染及溫室氣體排放源，排放的有毒的汙染物包括一氧化碳、氮化物、碳氫化合物、微顆粒及二氧化碳等。而香港最近的非道路機械設備排放規管主要針對新進口的施工設備。如果不考慮環境影響，香港目前在地盤使用的11,300臺設備如果徹底更換將需要很多年。 如何給設備擁有者提供誘因但同時采取措施鼓勵使用減排技術並使得當前設備盡快退出使用時又不給承包商帶來沈重的經濟負擔是香港及全世界面臨的急迫問題。盡管大家有一致公認應該采用激勵及懲罰措施以縮短過度到低排放設備的時間，但是目前沒有可供決策者和承包商使用的經濟模型，以綜合考慮公眾及設備使用者的利益。 本研究致力於構建考慮環境政策影響的建築施工設備的生命周期成本模型。把環境決策因素包括使用減排技術的一次性獎勵或減稅，及根據燃料汙染及碳排放收費與傳統的施工設備生命周期模型相結合進行定量分析。本研究擬使用靜態模型和動態模型確定不同環境決策因素對設備生命周期的影響。結合不同設備狀況、不同環境決策因素的間接成本水平，對施工設備基於生命周期的成本及經濟壽命進行系統研究。 本研究將揭示設備狀況，經濟環境因素，環境調控的間接收益成本，減排技術成本，及有代表性的施工設備的生命周期成本及經濟適用壽命之間的相互關系。在理論方面，本研究結合環境政策及措施改進傳統施工設備聲明周期模型，在實踐方面，研究給決策者和設備擁有者在進行與施工設備排放有關的更新改造時提供決策支持。

15223417.label: Realisation of objectives
15223417.value: 1. Propose a construction equipment life cycle cost analysis model which includes costs/benefits deriving from environmental incentives, environmental charges, and the adoption of low emission technologies. A comparison between a deterministic model, a stochastic model, and a computer-based time series model will be conducted. Data collection is the most dauting task in the research project, as the data are from the different sources. Detailed equipment emissions data and information on retrofitting technologies are mainly collected from sources of US EPA, California Air Resources Board, European Environment Agency, International Council on Clean Transportation (ICCT), DieselNet, an online Engine & Emission Technology source, and the emission reduction technology manufacturers and service providers, etc. Different methods of calculating construction equipment emissions during their operations are studied with comparison of advantages and disadvantages. The major types of diesel engine retrofitting technologies are identified with their cost data, technical suitability, and limitations. Data on air pollutions and their economic effects in Hong Kong are collected from the research works in HKU and CUHK. Interviews and focus group meetings were held with Chun Wo Construction and Engineering Ltd, a large general contractor in Hong Kong, for data collection and equipment life cycle management. Data were collected on the contractor’s construction equipment operations, equipment site use, and equipment conditions for dump trucks, wheel loaders, excavators etc. Case study is conducted on equipment replacement and diesel emission reductions based on the equipment data provided by Chun Wo. Statistical equipment replacement models are created in excel for some categories of selected equipment with and without environmental effects (penalty from surcharges for emissions and reduced operation costs due to tax exemptions and government one-off incentive for equipment upgrading). Oracle Crystal Ball tool was used to generate distributions and random data for Monte Carlo simulation modeling, of some equipment and conditional variables including maintenance and repairs, fuel consumption, fuel price, etc. Time series modeling of the equipment emissions was also conducted using SQL server data mining module with satisfactory results. 2. Determine the impact of different environmental policies on life cycle costs and the economic life of construction equipment of different types, engine tiers, and ages, under different economic conditions. The optimum range values for environmental policy variables, and how to prioritize equipment replacement for different policy and economic scenarios will be studied. A comprehensive study was made on the equipment environmental policies in the world with focus on the policy and practice in advanced economies such as USA, EU, Japan, etc. A in-depth review and analysis was conducted to compare different policy instruments in global contexts and identify the critical factors which impact on the decisions of equipment regulations and control for environmental protection. The identified factors and variables are then used for quantitative analysis of social and environmental conditions on equipment replacement or retrofitting for emissions reduction. A series of equipment replacement models are developed with focused study on the effects of government incentive policies, i.e. how the government incentive policies change the contractor’s decisions in equipment replacement or retrofitting with the most cost-effective approach. Responsibility sharing between the government and equipment owners is studied to determine the percentage of subsidies enticing the contractors to switch to low emission technologies. Different types of equipment are compared in policy effects and found that equipment engine sizes , equipment utilization rates, and engine tiers are important factors in equipment replacement with government policy supports. Research modelling and analysis indicates that incentive-based approaches are transparent, scientific, and more practical than command-and-control approaches in pollution reduction considering the competitive nature and low profit margin in construction industry. EPD provided the NRMM registration database in Hong Kong for our study. An interview was conducted with Air Policy Group of EPD to seek the views of the government on emission reductions of NRMM, current practice, and emission control policies. Equipment data from EPD are used to study the equipment emissions reduction in group wise approach and their expert views validated our policy findings in terms of practicality for implementation. 3. Develop a computer tool for life cycle cost analysis with environmental effects integrated, to facilitate the decision making of the environmental policy makers and the construction equipment owners. Microsoft Excel is used as a development environment with the use of its features such as random number generation, data table, pivot table and pivot chart, basic visual interface and VBA macro programming. Different types of equipment replacement models are created in Microsoft Excel, with automated calculations of life cycle costs and graphic display of trends, key points of interests with input of equipment fixed and variable costs, environmental variables, as well as policy variables. Different types of equipment, for examples, excavators, truck cranes, loaders, power pack for piling works, of different tier and horsepower range values are studied. The Microsoft Excel is also used to develop a tool for calculating the total amount of different types of pollutant emissions of equipment in a fleet, for examples, fleet owned by a contractor, for equipment replacement or retrofitting decision.

15223417.label: Major findings and research outcome
15223417.value: The following major findings and research outcomes are produced from this research project: (1) A compressive review and analysis of policy instruments has been conducted for addressing the severe problem of extensive construction equipment emissions (CEE) by governments around the world. Advanced and developing-economy promoters with distinctive background and constraints present differences in the development of CEE reduction policy instruments. A comprehensive and thorough investigation is made into the evolving trends, lessons, and accumulated experiences in the development of CEE reduction policy instruments. Three groups of policy instruments are identified, including the mandatory administration policy instrument (PI-A), the economic incentive policy instrument (PI-B), and the voluntary participation policy instrument (PI-C). Comparative analysis of CEE reduction policy instruments is conducted between advanced and developing-economy promoters. The results show that both advanced and developing-economy promoters overwhelmingly prefer to adopt PIAs. Developing-economy promoters may not have sufficient resources for implementing PI-Bs and PI-Cs. Advanced economy promoters have devoted more efforts to developing PI-Bs and PICs. It is suggested that a mixture of PI-As, PI-Bs and PI-Cs works better, and policy instruments should be selected considering the context of promoters. This part of policy research is aimed to promote experience-sharing between policymakers and provide them with significant insights for formulating more effective CEE reduction policy instruments. (2) Quantitative optimization models are proposed for determining subsidy levels to accelerate the replacement of in-use construction equipment for emission reduction. The models integrate emission reduction targets of the government and life cycle cost of construction equipment to calculate the reduced service life of an item of construction for early replacement. With the proposed integrated life cycle models, the economic life of construction equipment and its corresponding equivalent uniform annual cost (EUAC) can be determined by using a traditional life cycle cost analysis model. Optimal subsidy levels can be obtained on the basis that the subsidized EUAC of a piece of construction equipment over its shortened service life is not more than that over its normal economic life. (3) A responsibility-sharing subsidy policy modelling approach is proposed to determine the optimum subsidy level of the government and the responsibility of contractors, in the role of equipment owners, in order to minimize the overall cost per ton of emissions equivalent reduced, i.e. the most cost effective decision for equipment replacement or retrofitting. Through a case study on a fleet of excavators of a general contractor in Hong Kong, a subsidy level in the range of HK $14,800 to HK$16,096 per ton of emissions equivalent reduced is recommended, with the responsibility of emissions reduction borne by the government from 92% to 100% and the contractor from 0% to 8%. The percentages of subsidies are similar to the US subsidy levels such as Carl Moyer program for off-road emissions reduction in California. (4) Computer tools are created in Microsoft excel spreadsheets with integration of equipment emissions data, decision variables, and reports in the form of graphs, tables, and optimal decisions.

15223417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15223417.value: The research works conducted in this project can be extended to a public policy research project. With quantitative modelling of Nonroad machineries in the current inventory of Hong Kong, it is possible to identify and prioritize the equipment groups in replacement and retrofitting. Both government spending and costs of equipment owners can be justified with transparent and informed decisions to reduce the local air pollution in Hong Kong with the most cost-effective approach. Another future trend is electrification of construction equipment, which also involves investment and environmental effects, a progressive strategy can be formulated to replace these in-service high emitting equipment with clean technology substitutes. The PI will further explore related research and policy study through other funding sources.

15223417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15223417.value: Construction equipment used for civil and infrastructure projects is usually powered by diesel engines which emit harmful exhaust pollutants including PM, NOx, CO, and HC contributing to lung cancer, respiratory and cardiovascular illness, and premature deaths of people affected. Equipment life cycle modelling with integration of environmental effects is studied with government regulations and incentive policies. A series of models are constructed with case study on the fleet of Hong Kong Contractors to explore the quantitative relationships between equipment conditions, market conditions, government incentive (subsidies and pollution charges) policies, etc. The updated engine retrofitting technologies are reviewed and studied with the proposed life cycle model in terms of their effects, cost effectiveness, and technology limitations. Recommendations are made on the cost-effective strategies of the government to reduce emissions of Nonroad equipment, government subsidy policies to accelerate equipment replacement or retrofitting, contractor’s responsibilities, use of optimization models to balance the government emission reduction target settings, government spending, as well as the contractor’s willingness to pay. A number of interviews and focus-group meetings were conducted with the contractors, Environmental Protection Department, to validate the findings of the research and practical applications in construction industry of Hong Kong.

15223517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15223517.value: 為了船隻航行安全，航道需要保持足夠的深度，海洋底泥需要定期進行挖掘清淤。然而，人類活動和污水排放導致在河口沿岸地區的底泥受到重金屬和持續性有機物的污染。在香港，每年挖起的大量海洋底泥被傾倒在密封的海洋填埋設施（2015年大約有1.29 Mm3），這造成了高昂的成本，也給環境帶來了長久的負擔。隨著公眾環保意識提升，現有的填滿方式和擴建工程是不可持續的。在全球，只有少於1%的挖起的底泥被回收利用， 因此開發一個創新的底泥處理技術顯得極為緊迫。 本項目的目標是開發一種環保且增值的方式來回收被污染的海底泥製成地磚，並應用於建築工業中。我們創新地結合普通矽酸鹽水泥（OPC）和低碳的氧化鎂水泥（MOC）用來製備底泥地磚，可以充分發揮兩種材料的優勢，並克服各自的缺點。我們的初步實驗已經證實了在合適的配比和養護條件下，這種二元水泥與污染物具有優異的兼容性，能夠提高二氧化碳的固定，提供較高的機械強度。因此，我們所提出的方法能夠克服各種來自底泥的不利影響，如孔隙率高、硬化滯後、和耐久性低。為了生產高性能的底泥地磚，操作條件、OPC與MOC的比例、底泥與粘合劑的比例都需要進一步優化，並與本地和國際上的地磚應用標準（人行道和行車道）進行比較。 底泥地磚的性能將會從機械強度、物理性質、污染物淋出性、和環境耐久性等方面根據相關的標准進行全面評估。將進行微觀分析、光譜分析、和熱重分析等實驗來揭示二元水泥的水化機理和微觀結構特徵。用添加磷酸鹽和二氧化碳養護的方法來改善底泥表面的水化作用。引入再生骨料、孔隙堵塞劑、和聚合物乳化劑等方法來改善微觀結構。這些實驗成果會給海洋底泥的資源化利用提供一個科學基礎。 我們會驗證本創新技術對不同底泥的技術可行性，經濟可行性。並對其進行生命週期評價，與傳統的填埋方式進行比較。因此，本項目意在構建一個綠色的新一代的回收理念和技術，並激勵社會各界認識海洋底泥的價值，促進香港的循環經濟和可持續發展。

15223517.label: Realisation of objectives
15223517.value: Dredging is a regular maintenance for navigation in harbours and water channels; however, disposal of dredged sediment poses environmental liability and leads to shortfall of disposal facilities. This study demonstrated an innovative approach to transform contaminated sediment into eco-friendly sediment blocks by applying binary cement and CO2 curing. The binary use of magnesium oxide cement (MOC) and ordinary Portland cement (OPC) with air curing improved the compatibility of heavy metals and cement by provision of sufficient magnesium hydrates for metal sequestration. However, an introduction of MOC weakened compressive strength and increased water absorption of sediment blocks. Therefore, 1-d CO2 curing was employed to transform soluble magnesium hydrate into stable carbonates, and densify the microstructure and reduce the porosity from 18.5% to 16.9%, which enabled a substantial enhancement in strength (2.8 times) as well as carbon sequestration (3.98 wt%) in 40% MOC sample. A subsequent 7-d air curing with moisturizing facilitated continuous carbonation and rehydration of binary cement, resulting in a deeper carbonation and higher strength by the provision of additional nucleation sites of reactive magnesium oxide. Although accelerated carbonation had an adverse influence on metal immobilization in OPC sample due to pH decrease, it provided synergistic interaction with binary cement samples due to sufficient hydrates and pH buffering capacity. This study developed a novel and green remediation method for contaminated sediment using stabilization/solidification with calcium-rich/low-calcium industrial by-products and CO2 utilization. The hydration products were evaluated by quantitative X-ray diffraction analysis and thermogravimetric analysis. The incorporation of calcium carbide residue (CCR) facilitated hydration reaction and provided relatively high 7-d strength. In contrast, the addition of Class-F pulverized fly ash (PFA) and ground granulated blast furnace slag (GGBS) was beneficial to the 28-d strength development due to supplementary pozzolanic and hydration reactions. The employment of 1-d CO2 curing was found to promote strength development (98%) and carbon sequestration (4.3wt%), while additional 7-d air curing facilitated cement rehydration and further carbonation in the sediment blocks. The leachability tests indicated that all studied binders, especially CCR binder, effectively immobilized contaminants in the sediments. The calcium-rich CCR and GGBS were regarded as promising candidates for augmenting the efficacy of CO2 curing, whereas GGBS samples could be applicable as ecopaving blocks in view of their superior 28-d strength. Transforming contaminated sediment into value-added construction materials using low-carbon MgO cement is a sustainable option; however, the weak mechanical strength and unreliable water solubility of MgO cement restrict its practical engineering applications. This study elucidates the potential role of industrial Si-rich minerals in the performance enhancement of MgO-based products via the promotion of magnesium silicate hydrate (M-SH) gel formation. Quantitative X-ray diffraction and 29Si nuclear magnetic resonance analyses indicated that compositions and crystallinities of the Si-rich minerals significantly influence the formation and polymerisation of the M-S-H gel. Pulverised fly ash was found to be a promising Si-rich mineral for generating polymeric M-S-H gel, whereas incinerated sewage sludge ash samples demonstrated a low degree of polymerisation, and the use of glass powder samples gave a low yield of M-S-H. The formation of M-S-H gel enhanced the compressive strength and water resistance (strength retention after water immersion). Further experiments demonstrated that Si-modified MgO cement can transform dredged sediment into fill materials with satisfactory mechanical properties and contaminant immobilisation. This research intended to explore the efficacy of wood waste biochar as a green admixture and assess the influence of different physico-chemical properties of dredged sediments on the mechanical performance of cement-based sediment products. X-ray diffraction and porosimetry analysis reflected that particle size distribution of sediments determined the pore structure formation and strength development. Thermal and calorimetry analyses showed that biochar incorporation slightly enhanced the cement hydration reaction, while its relatively large and brittle particles induced microcracks and weakened the strength of sediment products. Nevertheless, biochar addition enhanced immobilization of potentially toxic elements and organic contaminants, rendering the sediment products more environmentally acceptable. This study proposes a low-carbon, cement-free, clay-based approach for simultaneous S/S of As and Pb in contaminated sediment, and accordingly elucidates the chemical interactions between alkali-activated clay binders and potentially toxic elements. Quantitative X-ray diffraction and 27Al nuclear magnetic resonance analyses indicated that the addition of lime effectively activated the hydration of kaolinite clay, and the presence of limestone further enhanced the polymerization of hydrates. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy showed that approximately 19% of As[III] was oxidized to As[V] in the alkali-activated clay system, which reduced toxicity and facilitated immobilization of As. During the cement-free S/S process, As and Pb consumed Ca(OH)2 and precipitated as Ca3(AsO4)2·4H2O and Pb3(NO3)(OH)5, respectively, accounting for the low leachability of As (7.0%) and Pb (5.4%). However, the reduced amount of Ca(OH)2 decreased the degree of hydration of clay minerals, and the pH buffering capacity of the contaminated soil hindered the pH increase. Sufficient dosage of lime was required for ensuring satisfactory solidification and contaminant immobilization of the clay-based S/S products. The leachability of As and Pb in high-Ca S/S treated soil samples was reduced by 96.2% and 98.8%, respectively. This study proposed a sustainable stabilization/solidification (S/S) of As-contaminated sediment via novel valorization of red mud waste, blast furnace slag and calcined clay mineral, which were selected to mitigate the increased leaching of As under alkaline environment of S/S treatment. Quantitative X-ray diffraction and thermogravimetric analyses illustrated that stable Ca-As complexes (e.g., Ca5(AsO4)3OH) could be formed at the expense of Ca(OH)2 consumption, which inevitably hindered the hydration process and S/S efficiency. The 29Si nuclear magnetic resonance analysis revealed that incorporation of metakaolin for As immobilization resulted in a low degree of hydration and polymerization, whereas addition of red mud promoted Fe-As complexation and demonstrated excellent compatibility with As. Transmission electron microscopy and elemental mapping further confirmed the precipitation of crystalline Ca-As and amorphous Fe-As compounds. Therefore, red mud-incorporated S/S binder achieved the highest efficiency of As immobilization (99.9%), which proved to be applicable for both in-situ and ex-situ S/S of As-contaminated sediment. Proper management of hazardous materials arouses widespread environmental concerns due to its enormous ecological and health impacts. The development of green stabilization/solidification (S/S) technology for resourceful utilization of hazardous materials, as well as the immobilization of potentially toxic elements is of great scientific interests. Cement-based S/S is often considered a low-cost and highly efficient technology, but the environmental sustainability of a broad spectrum of S/S technologies has yet to be evaluated. Therefore, this study assessed the environmental sustainability of S/S technologies for managing two common types of hazardous wastes, i.e., contaminated marine sediment and municipal solid waste incineration fly ash (MIFA) by using life cycle assessment (LCA). The LCA results identified the most preferable S/S technology in each strategy. In particular, Scenario 1 (mixture of sediment with a small percentage of ordinary Portland cement and incinerated sewage sludge ash) of Strategy 1 (use as fill materials) would be the preferred option, as it reduces about 54% and 70% global warming potential compared to those of Scenarios 2 and 3, respectively. The results can serve as a decision support for the practical application of the environmentally friendly S/S technology for sustainable remediation.

15223517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15223517.value: • Contaminated sediment could be recycled into pedestrian and vehicle paving blocks. • Magnesium oxide cement reduced metal leachability and compressive strength. • Binary cement exhibited higher strength and carbon sequestration with CO2 curing. • CO2 curing improved porous structure and relieved undesirable Ca/Mg complexation. • Additional moisturizing and air curing enabled further carbonation and rehydration. • Dredged sediment was valorized into eco-friendly construction products. • Contaminants disturbed hydrates formation and adversely influenced qualities. • Tailored mixture designs and press method enhanced product properties. • Trace elements and organic contaminants were effectively immobilized. • Recycling sediment into paving blocks was the most profitable option. • Dredged sediment could be recycled into value-added construction products. • Particle size distribution of sediments determined strength of sediment products. • Biochar incorporation had a beneficial effect on cement hydration reaction. • Yet biochar addition may incur micro-crack and reduce mechanical strength. • Biochar immobilized contaminants and promoted environmental acceptability.

15223517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15223517.value: This study proposed a low-carbon and environmentally friendly approach to recycle contaminated sediment into paving blocks using binary cement and accelerated carbonation. Compared to single cement, binary cement with MOC exhibited a larger extent of CO2 sequestration and strength enhancement during CO2 curing. The use of alternative cement could enhance the metal immobilization and reduce the leachability of sediment blocks. Selected waste materials such as ground granulated blast-furnace slag, incinerated sewage sludge ash, and recycled glass could be used as partial substitute of binder or aggregate to promote waste recycling and environmental sustainability. The proposed treatment effectively immobilized various contaminants in the sediment-based products and fulfilled the acceptance criteria on leachability for on-site reuse. Cost-benefit assessment suggested that production of paving blocks achieved the highest potential profits, whereas production of fill material had an advantage in saving the most of disposal fee. Wood waste biochar incorporation had a beneficial effect on cement hydration, but for the studied particle size it may incur micro-crack and strength degradation. For practical applications, the S/S mixtures should be prudently designed in consideration of the variability of contamination level, particle size distribution, and water content of sediments.

15223617.label: Realisation of objectives
15223617.value: Barium titanate-based perovskite oxides Ba1-xCaxTi1-yZryO3 are one of the most important ferroelectric materials which have been widely investigated and used in various applications. The ferroelectric properties of the oxides are strongly dependent on the compositions such as Ca. For examples, the piezoelectric coefficient of Ba0.85Ca0.15Ti0.9Zr0.1O3 (i.e., BCTZ-85) reaches a very high value of 420 pC/N while the oxide Ba0.15Ca0.85Ti0.9Zr0.1O3 (i.e., BCTZ-15) becomes non-ferroelectric. In this work, via doping 2 mol% Pr3+ as luminescent centres, not only elastic-mechanoluminescence (EML) but also electroluminescence (EL) and photoluminescence luminescence (PL) can be realized in the oxides (in the form of composite with an epoxy matrix). The mechanism as well as the luminescence responses have been investigated in detail. Unlike most of the studies which mainly reported red EL emissions in Pr-doped (Ba,Ca)TiO3 perovskite oxides, we have successfully realized blue EL emission in BCTZ-85/PDMS composites as well as intense red EL emission in BCTZ-85 bulk ceramics. The blue emission corresponds to the 3P1 -> 3H4 transition of Pr3+ whereas the red one corresponds to the 1D2 -> 3H4 transition. Based on other experimental evidences such as PL and photoluminescence excitation spectra as well as thermoluminescence glow curves, a schematic energy level diagram has been established for elucidating the possible mechanisms of the observed EL emissions. Shallow and deep electrons traps are identified. It has been suggested that the electrons trapped in the shallow traps can be released by the external electric field and then accelerated by the induced piezoelectric electric field to become hot electrons for impacting and exciting Pr3+. Owing to the cross-relaxations through the 4f5d levels and Pr-to-metal charge transfer state, the excited electrons of Pr3+ are de-excited non-radiatively to the 1D2 state to produce the red observed in the bulk ceramics. For the composites, a large local deformation of the ceramic particles embedded in the soft PDMS matrix will be produced by the converse piezoelectric effect, which in turn causes a bending of the conduction band and then a considerable downwards shift of the 4f5d levels from the conduction band. As a result, the electrons in the deep traps can be released and excited to the 4f5d levels, which then relax non-radiatively to the 3PJ levels for producing the blue emission. As there is no overlap of the 4f5d levels and CB, the cross-relaxation through the Pr-to-metal CTS is hindered, which also facilitates the blue emission. We have also realized red EML emission in Pr-doped BCTZ-15 and Pr-doped Ba0.1Ca0.9TiO3 (BCT-10) composites. BCTZ-15 is a diphase system containing Pr-doped Ba0.93Ca0.07Ti0.2Zr0.8 grains embedded in Pr-doped Ba0.1Ca0.9TiO3. As both BCTZ-15 (including the two phases) and BCT-10 are non-ferroelectric, the well-accepted piezoelectrically-induced EML model developed for the well-known EML perovskite oxide Pr-doped Ba0.7Ca0.3TiO3 is not applicable for the EML emissions observed in this work. As compared to BCT-15, the EML intensity of BCTZ-15 decreases slower and exhibits a longer lifetime after each replenishment by UV radiation. Electron traps are ascertained as the key element for exhibiting the EML response, and a model based on electron tunnelling mechanism has been adopted for elucidating the response. Based on the thermoluminescence measurements, it has been shown that the electrons trapped in the traps cannot be easily released by thermal energy at room temperature. On the other hand, during the elastic deformation, the distance between the electron traps and luminescent centers become shortened, and thus allowing the trapped electrons to tunnel to the luminescent centers for emitting photons. As the number of trapped electrons decreases after the tunnelling, the EML intensity decreases with time. However, the EML intensity can be largely recovered by irradiation with UV which can replenish the trapped electrons. As evidenced by the thermoluminescence glow curves, the electrons trapped in BCTZ-15 are more in number and deeper in energy levels as compared to BCT-10. This should be attributed to the substitution of Zr for Ti, which has been shown to can enhance the afterglow. Based on the good properties, barium titanate-based perovskite oxide Ba0.9Ca0.1Ti0.975Fe0.025O3 has also been developed and fabricated in the form flexible film on a mica substrate. Our results have revealed that the band gap of the film can be reversibly and continuously tuned by an elastic mechanical strain. A large mechanical strain of 0.85% can be introduced into the ferroelectric active layer, leading to a reduction in the band gap of 0.38 eV. It has been shown that the strong dependence of the optical band gap on mechanical bending mainly arises from the strain-induced modification of Fe-O bond. Because of the superior mechanical property of mica, the flexible film also exhibits excellent anti-fatigue characteristics over 103 bending cycles. Such a precise control of the band gap is crucial for lead-free ferroelectrics in the application of high-performance optical devices.

15223617.label: Major findings and research outcome
15223617.value: Barium titanate-based perovskite oxides Ba1-xCaxTi1-yZryO3 with strong elastic-mechanoluminescence (EML) and electroluminescence (EL) have been developed, and the associated mechanisms have been investigated in detail. After the doping of Pr3+ as the luminescent centers, calcium-rich perovskite oxide, i.e., Ba0.15Ca0.85Ti0.9Zr0.1O3 (BCTZ-15) can exhibit strong and long-lasting EML. Owing to the low solubility, the oxide contains two phases, i.e., Ba0.93Ca0.07Ti0.2Zr0.8 and Ba0.1Ca0.9TiO3, both of which are non-ferroelectric, clearly indicating that the EML emission should not be related to the piezoelectricity. Charged defects (e.g., [PrCa]o) which can entrap electrons at a relatively deep depth have been identified as crucial elements for providing EML emissions. A tunnelling mechanism has been adopted for elucidating the emissions. During the elastic deformation, the distance between the charge traps and luminescent centers become shortened, and thus allowing the trapped electrons to be released and tunnel to the luminescent centers for emitting photons. The emission is similar to that arisen from photoluminescence, i.e., the 1D2 -> 3H4 transition of Pr3+. Our results have also revealed that the partial substitution of Zr for Ti can increase the charge traps as well as the trap depth, and then enhance the EML intensity and the lifetime. Barium-rich perovskite oxide Ba0.85Ca0.15Ti0.9Zr0.1O3 (BCTZ-85) has also been fabricated. After the doping of Pr3+ as the luminescent centers, blue and red electroluminescence (EL) have been observed, which are attributed to the excellent piezoelectric properties of the oxide as well as the charged defects. Corresponding models have been established for elucidating the possible mechanisms. Intense red EL emission observed in BCTZ-85 bulk ceramics is attributed to electrons entrapped in the shallow traps, which are released by the external electric field and accelerated by the induced piezoelectric electric field to impact and excite Pr3+ for emitting photons (corresponding to the 1D2 -> 3H4 transition). On the other hand, blue EL emission is observed in BCTZ-85 composites. A large local deformation of the ceramic particles embedded in the soft PDMS matrix will be produced by the converse piezoelectric effect, which in turn causes a bending of the conduction band and then a considerable downwards shift of the 4f5d levels from the conduction band. As a result, the electrons in the deep traps can be released and excited to the 4f5d levels, which then relax non-radiatively to the 3PJ levels for producing the blue emission (corresponding to the 3P1 -> 3H4 transition). Barium-rich perovskite oxide Ba0.9Ca0.1Ti0.975Fe0.025O3 thin film has also been fabricated on mica substrates. Owing to the flexibility provided by the substrate, the film exhibits a mechanical strain-driven continuous and reversible tuning of bandgap.

15223617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15223617.value: Barium titanate-based perovskite oxides with strong elastic-mechanoluminescence (EML) and electroluminescence (EL) should find potential in various applications such as real-time stress sensing, imaging, lighting and display. Based on the inter-relationships between the compositions, doping agents, charged traps and ferroelectricity, as well as the mechanism models established in this work, other perovskite oxides with strong EML can be developed for practical applications.

15223617.value: Barium titanate-based perovskite oxides Ba1-xCaxTi1-yZryO3 with strong elastic-mechanoluminescence (EML) and electroluminescence (EL) have been developed, and the associated mechanisms have been investigated. Charged defects which can entrap electrons at a relatively deep depth have been identified as crucial elements for providing EML and EL emissions, while the ferroelectricity determined by the composition may affect the emission mechanisms. Calcium-rich non-ferroelectric perovskite oxide Ba0.15Ca0.85Ti0.9Zr0.1O3 can exhibit strong and long-lasting red EML emission. The piezoelectric electric field can accelerate the electrons released by the external electric field to excite the luminescent centers to exhibit red EL emission. When the oxide (in the form of ceramic particles) embedded in a soft PDMS matrix, a large local deformation will be produced by the converse piezoelectric effect, which in turn causes a bending of the conduction band. As a result, the electrons in the deep traps can be released to excite the luminescent centers for producing the blue EL.

15224017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15224017.value: One of the key activities in airports is assigning flights to parking positions called “gates”, at which ground services are provided and passengers board or leave the aircraft. Due to the dramatic growth in air traffic, it is vital that airports utilize their gates in the best way possible. In particular, it is estimated that the Hong Kong International Airport’s capacity will be reached around 2020, and the additional capacity of its third runway (to be completed in 2024) will be exhausted around 2030. This project aims to investigate a new approach to optimizing airport flight gate assignments in situations where, due to uncertain disruptions such as flight tardiness, actual flight arrival time and ground service time are unknown in advance. When disruptions occur, costly catastrophic delay or reassignment of flights may be needed to restore gate assignments. Therefore, it is vital that gate assignments are robust to uncertainty, with the total cost, including the recovery cost, minimized. The project is motivated by a major deficiency in previous approaches to optimizing flight gate assignments under uncertainty. In these approaches, the recovery cost is estimated without taking into account the recovery actions used. As a result, the estimated values may deviate significantly from the actual recovery costs, and a gate assignment based on such can be highly suboptimal. To overcome this deficiency, we propose investigating a new “recoverable” approach, taking into account recovery actions for different disruptions. We essentially need to solve a multi-period optimization problem where uncertainty is revealed progressively. The recovery cost at each period is modeled as an outcome of optimization over recovery actions, which is much more rigorous than the previous approaches. The problem is challenging, having many interesting variants for applications with different recovery costs, recovery actions, and overall objectives. To solve the problem and its variants, we will develop effective solution methods and optimization techniques, including to: derive mathematical models effective for analysis, identify non-trivial cases easy to solve, and develop algorithms of practical usefulness for hard cases. The outcome of the project is promising, as our new idea has been proved feasible in a preliminary study, from which effective models, tractable cases, and new algorithms have been obtained for several variants of the problem. The success of the project will significantly enrich the literature on flight gate assignments, contribute to new optimization methods and techniques, and open up fresh directions leading to interesting topics and useful results.

15224017.label: Realisation of objectives
15224017.value: Since the commencement of the project on January 1, 2018, we have conducted the following research activities to achieve all the project objectives by 100%: 1. We have followed the idea in the proposal to formulate a conflict robust resource assignment problem, for its application in airport gate assignment under uncertainty. The problem considers decisions on the assignment of resources (or gates) to events (or flights) and the decisions on recovery from conflicts of events due to uncertainty. We propose an optimization model to measure the conflicts caused by the uncertainty and formulate the conflict-robust resource assignment into a combinatorial robust optimization model. This has contributed to the achievement of Objectives 1 and 2. 2. We have studied and reformulated the optimization model for conflict measurement. We formally define the notion of ``crossings"--a crossing occurs when the actual completion time of service surpasses the scheduled start time of the succeeding service that uses the same resource. We prove some structural properties of the model, which reveals that under down-monotone properties, the worst-case number of crossings is identical to the worst-case number of conflicts. Based on the properties, we reformulate the model as an integer linear programming (ILP) model. We then analyze its linear programming relaxation and prove that the optimal objective value for the relaxation is close to the optimal solution to the ILP model. With this property, we reformulate the optimization model for the measurement of events’ conflict as a single-parametric optimization model. This has contributed to the achievement of Objective 2. 3. Based on the reformulation of the model for the conflict measurement, we develop three solution methods to solving the conflict-robust resource assignment problem. (i) The first is by direct search, as the objective function can be decomposed into two components, one is the cost for assignment, and the other is the cost for recovery. (ii) The second is by iterative row generation, which is based on an epi-graph reformulation of the conflict-robust resource assignment problem. (iii) The third is based on a transformation from the robust counterpart to the nominal problem. This has contributed to the achievement of Objective 2. 4. We have identified a tractable case of the problem and also studied a more general setting of the problem. For the tractable case, where resources are identical, only three basic constraints are taken into account in the resource assignment. Based on the third solution method newly developed, we have shown that this special case can be solved to asymptotically optimum in polynomial time. For the more complicated setting of the conflict-robust resource assignment problems faced in the flight gate assignment, where passengers’ walking distances are taken into account, we develop an exact algorithm as well as a heuristic. This has contributed to the achievement of Objectives 3 and 4. 5. We have also developed a distributionally robust optimization model with an ambiguity set of down-monotone uncertainty distributions. Our results derived for the robust optimization model are extended to a distributionally robust optimization model for the resource assignment problem. We have developed a distributionally-shrunken sample average approximation method to synthesize and combine the benefits of the data-driven solution approach and data-free solution approach to solve the distributionally robust optimization model. This has contributed to the achievement of Objectives 2 and 3. 6. We have conducted extensive experiments to examine our newly proposed optimization models and solution methods. For test instances, we have collected flight data from an airport and another available data source, including a data set on flights of the San Fransisco airport. We have implemented some benchmark methods known in the literature, including those based on graph-coloring models, as well as those based on buffer optimization models. Our experiments have shown that our new methods outperform these benchmark methods for the flight gate assignment. The results have also demonstrated the effectiveness of our robust optimization solution methods based on the “crossing” optimization. It has shown that our distributionally-shrunken SAA approach is able to outperform the arctangent model and SAA model in reducing actual conflicts. Our study provides the first theoretical justification for the use of distributionally robust optimization models in crossing minimization to control for the number of conflicts in the resource assignment problem. This has contributed to the achievement of Objective 4. 7. We have implemented our newly proposed model and solution methods. The models and solution methods implemented provide an optimization engine that can be used to improve gate assignments for airports. This has contributed to the achievement of Objective 5. 8. In addition to the basic flight gate assignment problem, we find that there are many other more complicated optimization problems that can be formulated as a robust resource assignment problem. We extend our studies to (1) tackle another challenging practical transportation problem, and to (2) study a general combinatorial robust optimization problem: 8a. For (1), we have formulated the liner service transportation problem with demand uncertainties as a two-stage robust optimization problem, where the first stage determines the selection of carriers, and the second stage, which is similar to the robust gate assignment problem, determines the recovery decisions that allocate cargos to the selected carriers’ decisions. The new problem is also a multi-period optimization problem. This has contributed to the achievement of Objectives 1 and 2. 8b. For (1), we have followed our solution approach developed for the gate assignment problem to reformulate the robust optimization model, so as to develop a constraint generation method to solve the liner service procurement problem with demand uncertainties. The numerical experiments show that our proposed models and solution method can help shippers to effectively optimize their liner service procurement decisions by utilizing liner service schedules. The success in extending our work on the robust gate assignment problem to the liner service transportation problem has demonstrated a great potential of our recoverable robust optimization approach in solving challenging practical optimization problems with uncertainties. This has contributed to the achievement of Objectives 3 and 4. 8c. For (2), we have studied a general combinatorial robust optimization problem with uncertain parameters, which generalizes the robust flight gate assignment problem and incorporates a challenging chance constraint to avoid risks such as extensive conflicts of flights in flight gate assignment. The combinatorial robust optimization counterpart is formulated based on some newly proposed upper bounds for the violation probability of the chance constraint. This has contributed to the achievement of Objective 1 and Objective 2. 8d. For (2), we have derived an exact bound for the violation probability under constant densities, in which all the underlying uncertainties follow uniform distributions. Under general distributions, with a minimum first-order dominance constant approximation for the densities and the exact upper bound for violation probability under constant densities, we develop two upper bounds under general densities, which lead to various robust counterparts in forms of combinatorial robust optimization. We have then developed some new solution methods by transforming the robust counterparts into several deterministic binary programs or even nominal problems. The proposed method has been shown to have theoretical and numerical advantages over other existing methods. This has contributed to the achievement of Objectives 3 and 4.
