15224017.label: Major findings and research outcome
15224017.value: For the robust airport gate assignment problem, we have completed a paper, titled “Conflict-Robust Resource Assignment Problem: The Role of Down-Monotone Ambiguity Set”, which is under review in Manufacturing & Service Operations Management. We have the following major findings and research outcomes: 1. We formally define the notion of ``crossings"--a crossing occurs when the actual completion time of service surpasses the scheduled start time of the succeeding service that uses the same resource. 2. We find that under down-monotone properties, the worst-case number of crossings is identical to the worst-case number of conflicts in the distributionally robust optimization (DRO) models with down-monotone uncertainty distributions. 3. We propose a distributionally-shrunken sample average approximation model to synthesize and combine the benefits of the data-driven approach and data-free approach. 4. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our solution method on the San Fransisco airport gate assignment problem using public data available, and the experimental results show that our approach is able to outperform other existing approaches in reducing actual conflicts. We have extended our results from the study on the robust airport gate assignment problem to a robust liner service procurement problem and a general combinatorial robust optimization problem, which are presented in two papers, with one titled “Optimal Global Liner Service Procurement by Utilizing Liner Service Schedules” published in Production and Operations Management, and the other titled “A Non-parametric Robust Optimization Approach for Chance Constrained Knapsack Problem ” under preparation for submission to Mathematical Programming. We have the following major findings and research outcomes: 1. We formulate the liner service procurement problem with demand uncertainty as a two-stage recoverable robust optimization problem, which, similar to the robust gate assignment problem, involves multiple periods. As the two-stage robust optimization problem is challenging to solve, we derive some novel reformulations that enable us to develop an effective constraint generation solution method. Results from experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in helping shippers to optimize their liner service procurement decisions. 2. We formulate the general combinatorial robust optimization problem as a chance-constrained problem, which generalizes the robust flight gate assignment problem to avoid risks. We have derived an exact bound for the violation probability under constant densities, and two upper bounds under general densities. We have developed solution methods by transforming the robust counterparts into deterministic binary programs or even nominal problems, which have theoretical and numerical advantages over existing methods.

15224017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15224017.value: For the robust airport gate assignment problem, an interesting topic for future research is to investigate for various ambiguity sets as to whether the equivalence of conflicts and crossings with respect to the worst-case delay realization still holds. If it does, we can further investigate how to reformulate and solve the problem under these ambiguity sets. This study reveals the equivalence of conflicts and crossings, with respect to the worst-case delay realization, which can also be employed in situations where service schedules need to be optimized together with resource assignments. Due to this, our modeling and solution approach can be applied to solving a broader class of problems, such as the port berth allocation problem in which the scheduled berthing starting and completion times need to be determined for each incoming vessel, together with the assignment of berths at the port. For the application to the liner service procurement problem, our recovery robust optimization models and solution method can be extended to incorporate the uncertainty of transit times in addition to demands. However, the formulations of the two-stage robust optimization problem will contain many more decision variables and constraints, so more efficient solution methods need to be developed in the future.

15224017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15224017.value: One of the key activities in airports is assigning flights to parking positions called “gates”, at which ground services are provided and passengers board or leave the aircraft. It is vital that airports utilize their gates in the best way possible. In this project we investigate how to optimize the resource assignment problem under uncertainty for its application to the airport flight gate assignment. We propose a new “recoverable” robust optimization approach, considering recovery actions and solving a multi-period optimization problem, where uncertainty is revealed progressively. We formally define the notion of ``crossings"--a crossing occurs when the actual completion time of a service surpasses the scheduled start time of the succeeding service that uses the same resource. We find that the worst-case number of crossings is identical to the worst-case number of conflicts in resource assignment under the distributionally robust optimization models with down-monotone uncertainty distributions. We develop a distributionally-shrunken sample average approximation model to synthesize and combine the benefits of data-driven approach and data-free approach, which is shown to outperform other approaches. Part of our solution methods have been extended to other combinatorial robust optimization problems, including the liner service procurement problem and the robust knapsack problem.

15224317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15224317.value: Buses and cars share the road space in almost every city of medium-size or above. Their frequent interactions often lower the speeds of both modes, and add to the congestion of the mixed-traffic network. Segregation of the two modes can be inefficient too; for example, dedicating a lane to bus use only will reduce the capacity for serving cars, and may result in long car queues at busy intersections. Present strategies and designs for prioritizing buses and for increasing car capacities are by and large applied to limited cases. Moreover, these two types of strategies and designs are never integrated to improve bus and car operations concurrently. We therefore propose to develop efficient and general models for analytically estimating the delays and capacities of bimodal traffic, first for a larger set of design and strategy options at the intersection level, and then for a smaller subset of efficient strategies at the arterial level. The models will be developed using kinematic wave theory for the intersection level, and variational theory for the arterial level. We will mainly focus on a class of strategies that use mid-block pre-signals for both, increasing cars’ discharge capacities and reducing bus delays. Our main goal is to identify for a wide range of operating parameters, the designs and strategies that achieve the best performance of bimodal traffic (e.g., the minimum person delay). The analytical models will be calibrated and verified by a simulation model to be developed in-house, and field data collected by unmanned aerial vehicles. The proposed project will be fruitful upon successful completion. For example, the models will furnish new and more efficient designs and strategies for wider ranges of real-world cases. The variational-theory-based arterial models for bimodal traffic will contribute to the frontier of traffic flow theories, and can be used as a key building block for arterial signal optimization. The practical contributions and implications will be huge too, given the ubiquitous presence of bimodal traffic over the world, and that our project has a significant component of case studies using high-quality field data. The expected project outcomes will also shed light on future developments of more advanced bimodal traffic theories and opportunities for further integration and collaboration with the industry. 在許多城市，道路交通主要由公共巴士與私家車組成。這兩種車輛混合行駛時的相互作用往往造成道路行駛速度的降低和塞車的加重。隔離兩種車輛的措施也往往帶來很大負面作用；例如，巴士專線（bus lane）會導致私家車能用的車道減少，從而可能在繁忙路口造成更長的車龍。目前所採用的巴士優先策略和提高社會車輛通行能力的策略都只適用於有限的情形，且這兩種策略往往互相矛盾，從未被組合起來以期同時改善巴士與私家車的通行狀態。 因此，我們計劃研發高效率且普遍適用的數學模型，用以計算受交通燈控制的單個路口和整條城市幹線（arterial）上的巴士與私家車交通的延誤與通行能力。模型的研發將基於運動波理論（kinematic wave theory）和該理論的變分法表述（variational theory of kinematic waves），并利用計算機仿真和實地採集的數據進行校準。我們將利用該模型探討在各種情形下如何利用安置在路段中間的預信號（pre-signal）結合巴士優先行車燈號（bus signal priority）以實現同時改善私家車通行能力和減少巴士延誤的目的，并力圖取得最優的設計與控制方案。 本研究項目預期將取得豐碩的成果。我們建立的模型將可用於改進實際城市道路的設計與混合交通流的控制策略；基於運動波理論的變分法表述的城市道路交通預測模型將推進交通流理論領域的前沿研究，并可作為幹線交通燈配時最優化問題的解決工具。在本項目成果的基礎上將可能研發更為先進的城市道路混合交通流理論。

15224317.label: Realisation of objectives
15224317.value: Objective 1: Develop analytical models using KW theory for estimating bimodal delays and capacity at a signalized intersection for various pre-signal and bus priority settings. We have developed kinematic wave theory (KWT) models for estimating bus delay and car capacity at a signalized intersection for the following scenarios: (i) integrating a mid-block pre-signal with transit signal priority (TSP) of green extension; (ii) integrating a pre-signal with dynamic TSP scheme; and (iii) integrating a pre-signal with special TSP for a 2-lane intersection approach. We obtain Pareto improvements for both buses and cars in most cases examined. Objective 2: Develop efficient numerical schemes using VT for estimating bimodal delays and throughput flows in a signalized arterial with various pre-signal and bus priority settings. We have developed models using VT theory to calculate the traffic states, queue lengths, and vehicle delays for a signalized intersection approach, and for a signalized arterial. Objective 3: Verify the bimodal traffic flow models via simulation. The KWT models and VT models are verified via simulations developed in-house via the cell transmission model and the car-following model. Objective 4: Apply the models to real sites of busy intersections and/or arterials; verify and calibrate the models using field data; and identify suggestions of improvement measures and practical guidelines. We have developed and tested Bayesian methods to estimate traffic states at real-world multimodal intersections (e.g. queue length, inflow, etc.). Our method is proved to have good accuracy.

15224317.label: Major findings and research outcome
15224317.value: We find a novel design involving a mid-block pre-signal, a dedicated bus lane, and a TSP (green extension) scheme can benefit both car and bus traffic substantially. A journal paper has been published on Transportation Research Part C. We find converting the dedicated bus lane to an intermittent lane and incorporating a dynamic choice of the optimal TSP scheme can further improve the car capacity and reduce the bus delay. A journal paper is near completion. We find variational theory can be applied to intersection approaches with conflicting traffic streams. A journal paper is under preparation. We develop a Bayesian method to more accurately predict traffic states and queue lengths in an intersection approach. A journal paper has been published on Transportation Research Part C.

15224317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15224317.value: The project can be extended in two ways. First, develop commercial software to implement the VT method for fast calculation of traffic states in an urban road network. We may apply for an ITF project to conduct this extension. Second, further examine the deficiencies of the KWT and VT methods as compared to the real traffic, and explore ways to improve these efficient methods. We may apply for another GRF project to conduct this extension.

15224317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15224317.value: A bus carries many more passengers than a private car. Thus, urban transportation systems should prioritize the bus traffic, especially at signalized intersections where buses often experience delays. We develop strategies that can prioritize buses without damaging the car traffic. Specifically, with the assistance of pre-signals and an intermittent bus lane, a bus approaching a signalized intersection can do so without being impeded by car queues. At the intersection, most buses will receive bus signal priority so that they can discharge into the intersection with no or little delay. We develop computationally efficient models using advanced theories like the kinematic wave theory and the variational theory. Results are verified via simulation. Our methods can be commercialized by developing software for the fast calculation and prediction of urban traffic network states. They can also assist traffic managers to determine the efficient bus priority measures.

15300017.label: Project Objectives
15300017.value: We will develop efficient smoothing quadratic regularization methods and cubic regularization methods with block coordinate descent techniques for solving partially separable nonsmooth, nonconvex minimization problems. These methods can be used in parallel computing environment. We will establish comprehensive theoretical results on convergence rate and complexity bounds for regularization methods to solve partially separable nonsmooth nonconvex optimization problems. We will derive innovative first order and second order necessary conditions and sufficient conditions for local minimizers of partially separable constrained nonsmooth, nonconvex optimization problems. We will explore more theoretical properties of smoothing functions for a sum of nonsmooth functions, such as the gradient consistency regarding subdifferentials and directional derivatives. We will extensively test the proposed regularization methods and compare them with the existing methods in terms of speed, accuracy, robustness and complexity. Real data from biology, finance and transportation will be used to test the efficiency of the new theory and algorithms.

15300017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15300017.value: Partially separable nonsmooth optimization problems have numerous important applications in biology, finance, imaging sciences and signal processing. Many mathematical and statistical models in data science are formed as constrained optimization problems where objective functions are partially separable, nonsmooth, nonconvex, and constraint sets are convex. A function is called partially separable if it can be written as a sum of element functions that depend only on subsets of the components of the variable. Partial separability generalizes separability and block separability. Partially separable smooth optimization problems have been studied for more than twenty years and extensively used in some popular software packages and testing environment for nonlinear optimization problems. Using the partially separable nature of the objective function, we can develop efficient regularization methods, especially when the size of the problem is large. Recently, with rapid increase of the size of optimization problems, splitting methods and subspace methods have attracted considerable attention, which use certain separable structure of the problems to develop algorithms in parallel computing environments. However, in contrast with well-developed algorithms and comprehensive complexity analysis for partially separable smooth problems or separable nonsmooth convex optimization, little algorithmic and theoretical results for partially separable nonsmooth, nonconvex constrained optimization are known. This project aims to develop innovative theories and efficient regularization methods for partially separable nonsmooth, nonconvex, or non-Lipschitz optimization problems arising from various important applications in data science. We will establish novel concepts and theory for constructing effective quadratic or cubic regularization concerning sparse approximation. In particular, we will use smoothing and subspace approximations based on the special structure of the partially separable functions, and derive comprehensive complexity analysis of regularization methods that include smoothing structured trust region methods and block coordinate descent methods. Simulation studies will be conducted to evaluate proposed methods and compare them with existing methods in terms of speed, accuracy and robustness. Real data from financial markets, genomic research and transportation research will be used to demonstrate the applications of the new theory and methods. The outcomes of this project will have a long-term and significant impact, because partially separable nonsmooth, nonconvex optimization problems arise naturally from many applications in data science and urgently need efficient methods for implementation. The new regularization methods for partially separable nonsmooth optimization with worst-case complexity bounds and convergence rate will attract attention from the international scientific community through excellent collaboration with world leading researchers and publications in leading journals and conferences. 部分可分的非光滑優化問題在生物、金融、圖像科學和信號處理中有著大量而重要的應用。在數據科學中，很多數學和統計學模型也被建模為目標函數是部分可分、非光滑、非凸甚至非Lipschitz連續但約束集合是閉凸集的約束優化問題。 部分可分性是指一个函数可以写成多个子函数的和，并且每个子函数中的变量只是原函数的变量的一部分。部分可分性為可分性和分塊可分性的推廣。 关于部分可分的光滑优化问题的研究已有20多年的历史，并且被广泛地应用于非线性优化问题的求解软件和检验链接库中。利用目标函数的部分可分性质可以改进正则化方法，特别是针对于大规模优化问题。最近，由于优化问题的求解规模迅速增加，在并行计算盛行的环境下，利用问题的可分结构设计的分裂算法和子空间方法受到了人们的广泛重视。 相對而言，關于部分可分的光滑優化問題和可分的非光滑凸優化問題的算法和計算複雜度分析已較為成熟，然而，對于部分可分的非光滑非凸約束優化的算法和理論結果卻寥寥無幾。 本項目的主要目的是針對部分可分的非光滑、非凸、非Lipschitz優化問題建立新穎的理論結果和有效的正則化方法。所研究的優化模型均來自于數據科學中各種重要的應用問題。我們將針對稀疏優化問題，提出新穎的概念和理論並用于建立有效的二次和三次正則化方法，分析其收斂速率和一致性。具體來說，我們將基于部分可分函數的特殊結構設計光滑化方法和子空間方法，給出具有光滑化結構的信賴域方法和分塊坐標下降法在內的正則化方法的複雜性分析。數值實驗將被用于衡量各種方法並用于和已存在的方法進行計算速度、精度和魯棒性等方面的比較。同時，在數值實驗中，本項目將采用來自金融市場、基因研究和交通等領域的真實數據，以此來展示新的理論和方法在這些問題中地應用效果。進一步，我們還將正則化方法應用于圖像科學、信號處理和變量選擇等重要應用領域的問題中。 由于部分可分的非光滑非凸約束優化問題來源于數據科學的重要應用並迫切需要有效的求解算法，本項目的研究成果將有著長期而重要的影響。本項目將與國際科學界的領軍人物就部分可分的非光滑約束優化問題的新的正則化方法、算法的最壞複雜性界和收斂速率等問題展開良好的合作,並通過在國際頂級期刊和會議上發表學術論文以得到國際科學界的關注和認可。

15300117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15300117.value: Multifunctional polycyclic molecules with nitrogen- and oxygen-containing functional groups are commonly found in biologically active natural products and pharmaceuticals. Efficient construction of polycyclic compounds from simple and readily available starting materials remains a significant challenge in organic chemistry. By catalytic activation of strategically positioned functionalities, simple organic molecules can be converted into structurally diverse polycyclic molecules using one-pot cascade reaction sequences and further transformed to complex molecular structures in high efficiency and selectivity by subsequent synthetic elaborations. In this proposal, we plan to explore the novel synthetic utilities of gold, silver, and visible light photoredox catalysis for selective organic transformation reactions and site-specific bioconjugation of peptides and proteins in aqueous medium. We aim to employ propargylamine-based 1,6-diynes with m-CPBA followed by silver catalysis to afford quaternary isoxazolinium salts as the cycloisomerization products. We propose to develop an efficient cascade iodination/cyclization of propargylamine-based 1,6-diynes for the synthesis of novel quaternary ammonium salts bearing vinyl iodide and alkyne/allene moieties with high regio- and chemoselectivity. In addition, we will develop novel visible light-gold catalysis for the synthesis of fluorescent quinolizinium salts. Notably, the newly synthesized fluorescent quinolizinium salts will be used as visible light photoredox catalysts for organic synthesis. Through mechanistic studies, we plan to investigate the reaction pathways of these novel organic transformation reactions. Bioconjugation is an important interdisciplinary research area between Chemistry and Biology facilitating the studies of complex biological systems. In particular, site-specific modification of biomolecules provides an appealing tool for the development of biopharmaceuticals. On the basis of our track record in catalysis and bioconjugation research, we propose to develop N-terminal modification of peptides and proteins by pyridinium salt formation and gold(III) catalyzed three-component coupling reaction. The success of this project would have a great impact on the research areas of Organic Chemistry, Protein Science, and Chemical Biology.

15300117.label: Realisation of objectives
15300117.value: [1] Novel Cascade Cyclization of Propargylamine-based 1,6-Diynes Cascade cyclization is of growing importance for the synthesis of complex molecules as it reduces synthetic steps and improves cost- and time-efficiency. In this project, we have developed a novel iodine-mediated cascade cyclization of propargylamine-based 1,6-diynes to construct spiro 1H-isoindoliums. Different functional groups were compatible under the optimized reaction conditions, giving the corresponding products in up to 94% yields. Upon treatment with triethylamine, the alkyne moieties of 1H-isoindoliums were smoothly transformed to the corresponding allenes. Allenes have long been recognized as a very important class of compounds with unique structural features and reactivity and utilized in the synthesis of numerous biologically active compounds and pharmaceuticals. To the best of our knowledge, the synthesis of this class of electron-deficient allenes has not been reported. Further to the above studies, we have also synthesized a new class of quaternary oxazinium salts by treatment of propargylamine-based 1,6-diynes with m‐CPBA (1.1 equiv.) followed by AgNO3 (10 mol%) in THF at 0 °C to room temperature for 1 h. Structurally diverse propargylamine‐based 1,6‐diynes bearing different functional groups were compatible with the reaction, giving products in 32‐60% yields. To our knowledge, this transformation has not been reported in literature. We envision that the new class of quaternary oxazinium salts would also serve as interesting building blocks for construction of molecules with diverse functionality. Site-selective modification of peptides and proteins has been recognized as a powerful tool for biological studies and development of targeted therapeutics. As reported in the above section, we have developed efficient synthesis of 1H-isoindoliums through a facile and novel cascade iodination/cyclization reaction of propargylamine‐based 1,6‐diynes. Upon treatment with a base, the alkyne moiety of 1H-isoindoliums could be further transformed to allenes. Using the isoindolium‐based electron‐deficient allenes, we have developed an efficient and chemoselective cysteine modification of peptides and proteins. Cysteine-containing peptides can be selectively modified to afford the corresponding bioconjugates in good conversions. With the optimized reaction conditions, a cysteine-containing protein (BSA) could be efficiently and selectively labelled with high functional group compatibility. The above works have led to a paper published in Org. Biomol. Chem., 2022, 20, 3755–3762 and a manuscript under preparation. [2] Dual Gold and Visible Light Photoredox Catalysis for the Synthesis of Fluorescent Quinolizinium Salts Quinolizinium salts were found in many natural products with diverse bioactivities, and quinolizinium salts could be used as organic dyes (fluorophores) and DNA intercalators in DNA-targeting drugs. In this project, we have developed visible light-gold catalysis for the synthesis of fluorescent quinolizinium salts with application studies. Quinoliziniums were prepared by treatment of quinoline-substituted aryl diazonium and electron-deficient alkyne containing phenyl ethynyl trimethylsilane with Ph3PAuCl (10 mol%) under irradiation of blue LEDs for 16 h. Electron-deficient alkyne-linked quinoliziniums were also prepared using the same method. Both alkynoic ketones and alkynoic amides were isolated in up to 49% yield. The photophysical properties of the electron-deficient alkyne linked quinoliziniums were then measured by UV/Vis and fluorescence spectroscopies in dichloromethane. The results showed that the maximum absorption was in the visible light region (405–445 nm) and the maximum emission was between 478–555 nm, with quantum yield of up to 0.22. The molar absorptivity of these compounds was up to 15,700 M-1 cm-1. We found that the electron-deficient alkyne-containing quinoliziniums were useful reagents for cysteine-selective modification of peptides and proteins with up to 99% conversion. The present method was successfully applied on selective modification of proteins, including a therapeutic protein (BCArg). The resulting cationic quinolizinium-modified BCArg have comparable enzymatic activities and anticancer efficacies to those of the unmodified one. Formaldehyde is an abundant contaminant in food and environments causing various diseases. Thus, the development of fast, simple, and selective formaldehyde detection is of great interest. Based on the above dual gold and visible light photoredox catalysis, we have developed novel quinolizinium-based fluorescent probes featuring a 2-aza-Cope rearrangement reaction and showed high selectivity to formaldehyde by fluorescence emission shift. We successfully reduced the detection time by increasing the bulkiness of the homoallylic moiety. The probes were applied to detect formaldehyde in aqueous solution, serum, and paper format. In the presence of formaldehyde, the fluorescent probes showed the blue shift of fluorescence emission from 495 to 481 nm in which the fluorescence colour changed from green to blue as observed by naked eyes. Remarkably, we have demonstrated that the incorporation of geminal dimethyl substituents to the homoallylic amine moiety reduced the formaldehyde detection time to 15 min which showed extremely fast response to formaldehyde comparing with other 2-aza-Cope-based fluorescent probes. Apart from dual gold and visible light photoredox catalysis, we have developed visible light-mediated copper-catalyzed cis-difunctionalization of terminal alkynes for the synthesis of quinolinizinium compounds with up to 85% yields. Interestingly, during the mechanistic study of this reaction, a new class of cyclometalated copper(I) complex was discovered. The complex consisted of four coordination sites occupied by two 2,2'-(2,2'-biphenyldiyl)dipyridine ligands with a pseudo tetrahedral geometry. To the best of our knowledge, the structure of the copper(I) complex has not been reported in literatures. The above works have led to two published papers (1) RSC Adv., 2022, 12, 6248–6254 and (2) RSC Adv., 2022, 12, 11543–11547 and a manuscript under preparation. [3] N-Terminal Modification of Peptides and Proteins by using 2-Ethynylbenzaldehydes Site-selective chemical modification of peptides and proteins has become an emerging research field in chemical biology, which allows the production of well-defined bioconjugates for biological studies and drug development. Although a number of bioconjugation reactions for specific amino acid modification have been developed in the past decade, due to the prevalence of multiple targeted residues on protein surface, only a few of them are amenable to give single-site modification. Targeting the N-terminus of peptides and proteins is a promising strategy to achieve single-site modification as a single chain protein contains only one N-terminal residue in its sequence and it is mostly solvent exposed for functionalization. Thus, development of an efficient N-terminal modification method will not only be an important direction for site-selective protein bioconjugation but also provide a chemical biology approach to study the biological functions of the protein N-terminus. We have developed a novel N-terminal selective modification of peptides and proteins by using 2-ethynylbenzaldehydes (2-EBA) via the formation of isoquinoliniums to produce well-defined bioconjugates. After reaction screening with a series of 2-EBA, excellent N-terminal selectivity is achieved by the reaction in slightly acidic phosphate-buffered saline using 2-EBA with electron-donating substituents. Selective modification of a library of peptides XSKFR (X = either one of 20 natural amino acids) by 2-ethynyl-4-hydroxy-5-methoxybenzaldehyde results in good-to-excellent N-terminal selectivity in peptides (up to >99:1). Lysozyme, ribonuclease A and a therapeutic recombinant Bacillus caldovelox arginase (BCArg) are N-terminally modified using alkyne- and fluorescein-linked 2-EBA. Alkyne-linked BCArg is further modified by rhodamine azide via copper(I)-catalyzed [3 + 2] cycloaddition indicating that the reaction has high functional group compatibility. Moreover, the BCArg modified by 2-ethynyl-5-methoxybenzaldehyde exhibits comparable activity in enzymatic and cytotoxic assays with the unmodified one. The above work has led to a paper published in Communications Chemistry, 2020, 3(1), 67.

15300117.label: Major findings and research outcome
15300117.value: Cascade cyclization is important for the synthesis of complex organic molecules by reducing synthetic steps and improving cost- and time-efficiency. We have developed a novel iodine-mediated cascade cyclization of propargylamine-based 1,6-diynes to synthesize spiro 1H-isoindoliums. Different functional groups were compatible, giving the corresponding products in up to 94% yields. Upon treatment with triethylamine, the alkyne moieties of the 1H-isoindoliums were transformed to the corresponding allenes. In addition, a new class of quaternary oxazinium salts was synthesized by treatment of propargylamine-based 1,6-diynes with m‐CPBA followed by AgNO3. Using the isoindolium-based electron-deficient allenes, we have developed an efficient and chemoselective cysteine modification of peptides and proteins in good conversions. A cysteine-containing protein (BSA) could be efficiently and selectively labelled with high functional group compatibility. Visible light photoredox catalysis has been demonstrated as a novel approach for selective transformations of organic molecules. We have developed dual gold and visible light photoredox catalysis for efficient synthesis of fluorescent quinolizinium salts. A variety of quinolizinium salts has been prepared by treatment of quinoline-substituted aryl diazoniums and electron-deficient alkynes containing phenyl ethynyl trimethylsilane with a catalytic amount of Ph3PAuCl under irradiation of blue LEDs. The functionalized fluorescent quinolizinium salts achieved cysteine-selective modification of peptides and proteins with up to 99% conversion. Selective modification a therapeutic protein (BCArg) was achieved, and the resulting quinolizinium-modified BCArg has comparable enzymatic activities and anticancer efficacies to those of the unmodified one. In addition, we have developed novel quinolizinium-based fluorescent formaldehyde probes featuring a 2-aza-Cope rearrangement reaction. Furthermore, we have developed a new visible light-mediated copper-catalyzed cis-difunctionalization of terminal alkynes for the synthesis of quinolinizinium compounds with up to 85% yields. Interestingly, a new class of cyclometalated copper(I) complex was discovered. Targeting the N-terminus of peptides and proteins is a promising bioconjugation strategy to achieve single-site modification. We have developed a novel N-terminal selective modification of peptides and proteins by using 2-ethynylbenzaldehydes (2-EBA) via the formation of isoquinoliniums. Excellent N-terminal selectivity was achieved by the reaction in slightly acidic phosphate-buffered saline using 2-EBA with electron-donating substituents. Selective modification of a library of peptides XSKFR (X = either one of 20 natural amino acids) by 2-ethynyl-4-hydroxy-5-methoxybenzaldehyde results in good-to-excellent N-terminal selectivity in peptides (up to >99:1). A therapeutic recombinant protein (BCArg) was N-terminally modified using alkyne- and fluorescein-linked 2-EBA. Interestingly, the modified BCArg exhibited comparable activity in enzymatic and cytotoxic assays with the unmodified one.

15300117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15300117.value: We have developed novel cascade cyclization strategies for efficient synthesis of new classes of structurally diverse spiro 1H-isoindoliums, electron deficient allenes, and electron deficient alkynes from propargylamine-based 1,6-diynes. We will conduct further synthetic elaboration of these compounds to construct structurally complicated organic molecules. We have found that the isoindolium‐based electron‐deficient allenes achieved chemoselective cysteine modification of peptides and proteins. We will develop multifunctional bioconjugation reagents by installing biophysical probes to these electron‐deficient allenes and to expand the scope of them in chemoselective bioconjugation reactions of different types of peptides and proteins. We have developed dual gold/copper visible light photoredox catalysis for the synthesis of novel quinolizinium salts. We will further expand the scope of these photoredox catalysis to construct structurally diverse quinolizinium salts. Built on the successful application studies on bioconjugation and fluorescent formaldehyde detection, we aim to design and synthesize different fluorescent quinolizinium-based bioconjugation reagents and fluorescent probes. We have demonstrated that 2-ethynylbenzaldehydes (2-EBA) achieved excellent N-terminal selectivity in bioconjugation via the formation of isoquinoliniums. We plan to develop the isoquinolinium moiety as a novel bioorthogonal handle for further modification to assemble multifunctional bioconjugates. We intend to conduct further biological investigations for the N-terminal modified therapeutic recombinant protein (BCArg).

15300117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15300117.value: Multifunctional polycyclic organic molecules with nitrogen- and oxygen-containing functional groups are commonly found in biologically active natural products and pharmaceuticals. By using novel catalytic and selective organic transformations, simple organic molecules can be converted into structurally diverse polycyclic molecules using cascade reaction sequences and further transformed to complex molecular structures with diverse applications. In this project, we have employed propargylamine-based 1,6-diynes as the starting materials to synthesize structurally diverse electron-deficient alkynes and allenes by cascade reaction sequences and conducted application studies on chemoselective bioconjugation of peptides and proteins. In addition, we have developed dual gold/copper visible light photoredox catalysis for the synthesis of novel fluorescent quinolizinium salts. Given their interesting fluorescent properties, we have developed the fluorescent quinolizinium compounds as fluorescent reagents for bioconjugation and fluorescent probes for formaldehyde detection. We have developed a novel N-terminal selective modification of peptides and proteins by using 2-ethynylbenzaldehydes (2-EBA) via the formation of isoquinoliniums. A therapeutic recombinant protein (BCArg) was N-terminally modified using alkyne- and fluorescein-linked 2-EBA. This project has demonstrated the importance of research on advanced chemical synthesis to provide novel functional molecules contributing to the diverse applications on organic synthesis, fluorescent probes development and selective bioconjugation of peptides and proteins.

15300217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15300217.value: Transition metal N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) complexes, renowned for their strong sigma donating properties and strong metal-carbon bond, have received great attention in catalysis and materials science over the past decades. However, application study of metal-NHC complexes, other than the aforementioned areas, is rarely explored. Recently, we demonstrated that significant improvement in photocatalytic performance has been achieved by using photostable iridium bis(NHC) complexes as photocatalysts (Chem. Sci., 2016, 7, 3123). Encouraged by our previous work, in this project, we aim to develop photostable NHC analogues of bipyridine(bpy) which would combine the rich redox and photochemical properties of bpy and at the same time retain the strong sigma donating and strong M-C bond properties of NHC. A library of metal-NHC complexes with different excited state properties and structural diversity will be developed. Different spectroscopic techniques including resonance Raman spectroscopy, ultrafast time-resolved measurement and density functional theory calculation will be performed to characterize the excited states originated from the metal-NHC complexes. We will also develop metal-NHC complexes as strong photooxidants and photoreductants with tunable excited redox potentials for excited state electron transfer reactions. We envision that new applications of the metal-NHC complexes could be emerged via the creation of a tool box of luminescent metal-NHC complexes with diverse structures, functions and tunable excited state properties. 15300417.value: 非局部相場方程指數差分格式的穩定性分析及誤差估計

15300417.label: Project Objectives
15300417.value: The spatial convolution is computationally the most expensive part of the simulation of nonlocal phase field equations. We will provide a highly efficient implementation for the computation of the spatial convolution under the Fourier spectral discretization in space. We will provide a new linear convex splitting of the energy, develop a linear semi-implicit scheme, and prove the unconditional energy stability and unique solvability of the derived scheme. Based on the linear convex splitting, ETD schemes will be constructed in combination with the Fourier spectral spatial discretization. The energy stability and error estimates of the purposed ETD schemes will be proved rigorously. We will apply our proposed numerical methods on the numerical simulations of phase field crystal equations, which has the nonlocal correlation function in the energy functional.

15300417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15300417.value: This project focuses on a family of exponential differencing time (ETD) schemes for the nonlocal phase field equations, such as the nonlocal Cahn-Hilliard equation, arising in material science. There are more and more literatures on the numerical methods of the nonlocal phase field equations, while few works are devoted to the studies on the energy stability. The energy stable method has been popular and effective approach for the numerical studies of the classical (local) phase field equations, so it is highly desirable to explore its application on the nonlocal models. There exist nonlocal terms, reflecting the long-range interactions in a nonlocal system, involving a convolution in the spatial domain, which usually leads a great many of calculations. Thus, it is meaningful to reduce the computational cost by more efficient numerical methods. Since, as the gradient flows, the solutions to the nonlocal phase field equations decrease the energy along the time, numerical methods preserving such property of energy decay laws are highly useful in simulating physically reliable dynamics of the system. The goal of this project is to develop a family of efficient energy stable ETD schemes for the simulations of the nonlocal phase field equations. The main contribution of this project includes the energy stability and error estimates for a class of ETD schemes for the nonlocal phase field equations. The equation will be decomposed into linear and nonlinear parts based on the stabilized splitting form. The ETD schemes are a set of explicit time-marching algorithms, which solve the linear part exactly and approximate the nonlinear part by numerical integrations with any desired temporal accuracy. We will discretize the spatial domain by Fourier spectral approximation to take advantage of the high accuracy of spectral methods. The computational cost of the convolution can be reduced to that of the ordinary product by using the fast Fourier transform, which is one of the key advantages of our numerical methods. The proposed algorithms are more efficient than some existing methods because of the explicit temporal integration in combination with the fast spatial transform technique. We will prove for the ETD schemes the unconditional energy stability independent on the time step size. In addition, the error estimates of the proposed ETD schemes are also investigated. 本項目集中研究材料科學中非局部相場方程，例如非局部Cahn-Hilliard方程，的一類指數差分格式。越來越多的文獻中出現關於非局部相場方程的數值方法研究，但是關於能量穩定性的研究卻很少。能量穩定性方法在是一種在研究傳統（局部）相場方程中廣泛使用並且非常有效的數值方法，所以探索它在非局部相場方程中的應用是十分必要的。非局部相場方程中的非局部相用來反應 非局部系統中的長程作用，它包含空間上的卷積，通常這將帶來巨大的計算量。因此，用更加高效的數值方法來降低計算量是有意義的。作為梯度流，非局部相場方程的解隨時間能量遞減，所以為了模擬非局部系統物理可信的動力學行為，保持能量衰減的數值方法是十分有用的。 本項目的目標是發展數值模擬非局部相場方程的一類高效能量穩定性的指數差分格式。項目的主要貢獻在於研究非局部相場方程一類指數差分格式的能量穩定性和誤差估計。所研究的方程將基於穩定化的分裂格式被分解為線性和非線性兩部分。指數差分格式是一類顯式時間遞進算法，它解析求解線性部分，運用數值積分公式可以近似求解非線性部分達到任意階時間精度。我們將在空間上用傅裏葉譜逼近，以此來利用譜方法的高階精度。使用快速傅裏葉變換，卷積的計算量將會被降低到和普通乘積一樣，這是我們數值方法的關鍵優勢。我們發展的算法比現有的方法更加高效，因為我們在時間方向使用顯式積分，在空間方向使用快速傅裏葉變換技巧。我們將證明指數差分格式不依賴於時間步長的能量穩定性性質。並且，指數差分格式的誤差估計也將被研究。

15300417.label: Realisation of objectives
15300417.value: The objectives of this project have been achieved successfully. Under the support of this GRF grant, we have developed several energy stable numerical schemes, including ETD schemes, for the nonlocal phase field equations. The stability and convergence of the proposed numerical schemes have been analyzed. The characteristic properties of the solution, -e.g. the energy decay property, the gradient bound of the solution, have been conserved in numerical simulations. The proposed numerical schemes can be used to solve different phase field equations.

15300417.label: Major findings and research outcome
15300417.value: In this project, we have studied the stability and convergence of some high order efficient numerical schemes for some nonlocal phase field equations. The major findings and research outcome are as follows: 1. In [Cheng, Qiao, Wang, JSC, 2019], we have developed a third order accurate exponential time differencing (ETD) numerical scheme for the no-slope-selection (NSS) equation of the epitaxial thin film growth model, with Fourier pseudo-spectral discretization in space. A linear splitting is applied to the physical model, and an ETD-based multistep approximation is used for time integration of the corresponding equation. A third order accurate Douglas-Dupont regularization term is added in the numerical scheme. A careful Fourier eigenvalue analysis results in the energy stability in a modified version, and a theoretical justification of the stabilization coefficient becomes available. As a result of this energy stability analysis, a uniform in time bound of the numerical energy is obtained. The proposed stability analysis method can be used for other phase field equations. The extension to nonlocal phase field equations is straightforward. 2. In [Liu, Qiao, IMANA, 2020], We establish an optimal strong convergence rate of a fully discrete numerical scheme for second-order parabolic stochastic partial differential equations with monotone drifts, including the stochastic Allen–Cahn equation, driven by an additive space-time white noise. A strong convergence rate of the proposed fully discrete scheme is obtained. 3. In [Li, Qiao, Wang, Math Comp. 2021], we provide a detailed convergence analysis for a first order stabilized linear semi-implicit numerical scheme for the nonlocal Cahn–Hilliard equation, which follows from consistency and stability estimates for the numerical error function. Taking the view that the numerical solution is indeed the exact solution with a perturbation, the error function is L-infinity bounded uniformly under a loose constraint of the time step size, which then leads to the uniform maximum-norm bound of the numerical solution. The proposed analysis method can be applied in the stability analysis on the ETD schemes for nonlocal phase field equations. 4. In [Fan, Qiao, Sun, JCS2020; Qiao, Zhang, NMTMA2021; Liu, Qiao, Zhang, SISC2021], we have applied developed energy stable numerical schemes in the simulation of diffusive interface models of Peng-Robinson equation of state for isothermal compositional grading by gravity and image segmentations. Some superiorities of the nonlocal models have been observed in the simulations.

15300417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15300417.value: Further development of this research is to solve other nonlinear partial differential equations with nonlocal diffusion terms with ETD solvers. Other high order methods, such as BDF schemes, will also be studied for nonlocal systems. The applications of the numerical schemes proposed in this project will be further studied for image segmentation problems and inpainting problems.

15300417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15300417.value: The nonlocal phase field models have attracted more and more attentions in many physical and chemical applications on phase separation of multi-component mixtures. Their numerical simulations have become highly important in engineering. This project focuses on high order energy stable numerical schemes, such as exponential differencing time (ETD) schemes, for the nonlocal phase field equations. We have developed several high order efficient energy stable numerical schemes for some nonlocal phase field equations, e.g., nonlocal Cahn-Hilliard equations. The stability analysis and error estimates of these schemes have been given theoretically and demonstrated numerically. Successfully simulations have been conducted on different applications, such as stochastic phase field equations, diffusive interface models of Peng-Robinson equation of state for isothermal compositional grading by gravity, image segmentation, etc.

15300517.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15300517.value: 大規模優化問題算法的收斂速度分析

15300517.label: Project Objectives
15300517.value: Analyze the local convergence rate of popular first-order methods such as the proximal gradient algorithm and the Douglas-Rachford splitting method on commonly used (possibly nonconvex) optimization models by explicitly estimating the KL exponent of the model. Approaches include explicit derivation for some simpler models, and developing various calculus rules to deduce the exponent of a new model from old models with known exponents. The outcomes can provide guidelines for the design of new algorithms and the construction of new models in various applications. Examine the role KL exponents play in the analysis of classical optimization algorithms such as Newton's method and the augmented Lagrangian method. The tools developed will likely lead to convergence results that are based on more relaxed assumptions than those available in the literature.

15300517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15300517.value: In this proposal, the PI and his coworkers will study the local convergence behavior of popular first-order methods for solving optimization models commonly encountered in applications such as compressed sensing and statistical machine learning. The models considered can be either convex or nonconvex, and are typically presented in large scale. In the literature, the analysis of local convergence rate of first-order methods for convex models is largely based on the error bound condition, while that for nonconvex models is mainly centered around the Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz (KL) exponent. Though the error bound condition has been extensively studied with a lot of concrete examples known to satisfy it, the KL exponent of many important optimization models remains unknown. In this project, based on the recent work by the PI and the co-I, we further investigate the KL exponents by developing new calculus rules to deduce the KL exponents of new optimization models from those whose KL exponents are known. We will also explore the applicability of the KL property in analyzing some classical optimization algorithms. The knowledge of KL exponents is central to the analysis of local convergence rate of first-order methods, and can provide guidelines for the design of new algorithms and the proposal of new models in various applications. 本項目將研究一階優化算法的局部收斂速度。一階優化算法常用作求解壓縮感應及機器學習等應用中的大規模凸或非凸優化問題，而誤差界與Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz (ＫＬ) 指數則分別用於分析一階優化算法求解凸及非凸問題時的收斂速度。雖然已知很多模型滿足誤差界條件，但一些常用模型的ＫＬ指數仍為未知。本項目將致力研究ＫＬ指數的運算法則，以用作計算新模型的ＫＬ指數。我們亦會研究如何利用ＫＬ指數分析傳統優化算法的收斂速度。ＫＬ指數對分析一階優化算法的收斂速度尤為重要，了解ＫＬ指數將有利於設計新的優化模型及算法。

15300517.label: Realisation of objectives
15300517.value: One of the goals of this project is to develop rules to determine explicit Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz (KL) exponents, by either developing so-called calculus rules for general models or direct computation techniques for simple models. In this regard, we studied in “Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz exponent via inf-projection” how the KL exponent behaves under the classical and ubiquitous operation “inf-projection”, and derived various new KL exponent results for models whose KL exponents were previously unknown. This includes a large sub-class of semidefinite-programming (SDP) representable functions, many so-called C2 cone reducible functions, Bregman envelope functions, and some difference-of-convex functions, etc. This is a significant generalization of our previous results, which studied how KL exponent behaves upon taking the minimum of finitely many functions, and formed a significant portion of the PhD thesis of the graduate student of the PI, Dr Peiran Yu (graduated in August 2021). This work was presented in various seminars including the Tutte seminar in Department of Combinatorics and Optimization in University of Waterloo, during a visit of the PI there, supported under this funding. Besides, in the paper “Convergence rate analysis of a sequential convex programming method with line search for a class of constrained difference-of-convex optimization problems”, we derived a calculus rule for deducing the KL exponent of the extended objective of a convex optimization problem with smooth inequality constraints from its Lagrangian, under suitable assumptions. This result enables us to deduce a KL exponent of ½ for model problems such as noisy basis pursuit, and hence the algorithm studied in the paper is linearly convergent when applied to solving such models. In addition, in the paper “A subgradient-based approach for finding the maximum feasible subsystem with respect to a set”, we directly computed the KL exponent of a certain formulation of the maximum feasible subsystem problem, under suitable assumptions such as convexity of the sets involved. In summary, we have derived new calculus rules for deducing KL exponents (and successfully derived KL exponents that were previously unknown), and deduced in some special settings the KL exponent of the model of interest directly based on the problem structure. The other aim of the project is to examine the role KL exponent plays in some classical optimization algorithm. In “Convergence rate analysis of a sequential convex programming method with line search for a class of constrained difference-of-convex optimization problems”, we studied how to deduce convergence rate of a variant of the moving-balls-approximation (MBA) algorithm under KL-type assumptions on some suitable potential functions. The MBA algorithm is a special instance of the classical difference-of-convex algorithm (DCA) applied to constrained optimization problems. Our variant is able to handle nonsmoothness in the objective and admits a flexible line-search scheme for empirical acceleration. In the general setting, in order to make use of the KL exponent for analyzing convergence rate, we constructed a new potential function and imposed KL assumptions on such function. Our work provides the first theoretical guarantee that such an algorithm is linearly convergent when applied to application problems such as basis pursuit with noise. This work was presented in the 64th annual meeting of the Australian Mathematical Society in December 2020 (Zoom conference). It formed part of the PhD thesis of the PI’s student, Dr Peiran Yu. Moreover, in “A refined convergence analysis of pDCAe with applications to simultaneous sparse recovery and outlier detection”, we studied the role KL exponents play in the convergence analysis of pDCAe, another variant of the classical DCA. In this work, we performed our convergence analysis based on a newly constructed potential function, which allowed us to remove a differentiability assumption that was needed in a previous work concerning pDCAe. This significantly enhances the applicability of our convergence theory and allows us to conclude that pDCAe is linearly convergent when applied to compressed sensing problems with Gaussian noise regularized by the sum of the k smallest entries (in magnitude). In summary, we have studied how KL exponent can be used (via constructing suitable potential functions) for analyzing convergence of some classical optimization algorithms.

15300517.label: Major findings and research outcome
15300517.value: Four journal papers are published as research outcome of this project. The first paper is “A refined convergence analysis of pDCAe with applications to simultaneous sparse recovery and outlier detection”, which was already reported in the midterm progress report. This paper considers pDCAe, a variant of the classical DCA, and establishes convergent rate of pDCAe under mild assumptions while allowing the concave part to remain nonsmooth. The second paper is “A subgradient-based approach for finding the maximum feasible subsystem with respect to a set”, which studies the important problem of identifying maximum feasible subsystems. We developed a new formulation and proposed a new algorithm for solving it. Convergence of the new algorithm was analyzed under suitable KL-type assumptions. The third paper is “Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz exponent via inf-projection”, which studies the effect of inf-projection on KL exponents. Using this new calculus rule, we were able to deduce KL exponents for a large class of functions whose KL exponents were previously unknown. This includes many SDP representable functions and some nonconvex functions that can be written as inf-projections. Knowledge on KL exponents has direct implications on the rate of convergence when first-order methods are applied to solving these models. The fourth paper is “Convergence rate analysis of a sequential convex programming method with line search for a class of constrained difference-of-convex optimization problems”, which contains one calculus rule that deduces the KL exponent of an extended objective from that of its Lagrangian function. We also established the convergence rate of a variant of MBA algorithm under suitable KL-type assumptions. Results in “Convergence rate analysis of a sequential convex programming method with line search for a class of constrained difference-of-convex optimization problems” were presented at the 64th annual meeting of the Australian Mathematical Society in December 2020 (Zoom conference). Some preliminary results on KL exponents were also presented in the 23rd International Symposium on Mathematical Programming and the 29th European Conference on Operational Research, both held in July 2018, under the talk(s) “Iteratively reweighted l1 algorithms with extrapolation”. Finally, Results in “Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz exponent via inf-projection” was presented in the Tutte seminar in Department of Combinatorics and Optimization in University of Waterloo in June 2019.

15300517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15300517.value: There are several avenues for potential further development. For instance, the KL exponents of many optimization models such as some general conic optimization problems are still unknown. Moreover, the connection between KL-type convergence analysis and projection-free algorithms (such as Frank-Wolfe algorithm) is still unclear. These are possible venues for future research.

15300517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15300517.value: The PI and his coworkers analyzed the local convergence rate of some first-order methods and studied Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz (KL) exponents for optimization models and some associated potential functions that arise in contemporary applications such as compressed sensing. KL exponents are key notions that govern the convergence rate of various first-order methods for large-scale problems. On the one hand, we developed calculus rules for obtaining explicit KL exponents of functions based on some of its constituent functions whose KL exponents were known. This enables us to deduce linear (fast) convergence of some popular first-order methods for applications such as noisy basis pursuit. On the other hand, we examined the role of KL exponents in analyzing convergence rate of some variants of the classical difference-of-convex algorithm. The methodology developed in this project enhances the state-of-the-art understanding of convergence rate analysis of first-order methods, and sheds new light on the design of fast optimization algorithms.

15300717.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15300717.value: 高阶马尔科夫链, 转移概率张量与随机张量

15300717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15300717.value: In this project, we plan to make a comprehensive study on higher order Markov chains, transition probability tensors and stochastic tensors. We will study general conditions for existence of positive solution of the fixed point problem for transition probability tensors, and general contract mapping conditions for this fixed point problem. We will investigate convergence conditions for the higher order Markov chain itself. We will define cyclic limiting probability distributions of higher order Markov chains, study the uniqueness conditions for such cyclic limiting probability distributions, and convergence of higher order Markov chains to such cyclic limiting probability distributions. We will also introduce doubly stochastic tensors based upon both transition probability tensors and stochastic tensors, and discuss the Birkhoff-Von Neumann theorem for them, and their applications such as the three index assignment problem. 此项目计划广泛研究高阶马尔科夫链, 转移概率张量与随机张量. 我们将研究关于转移概率张量不动点问题正解存在性的一般条件以及此不动点问题的一般性压缩影像条件. 我们将考察高阶马尔科夫链本身的收敛性条件. 定义高阶马尔科夫链的循环概率分布，并研究这种分布的唯一性条件和高阶马尔科夫链收敛到这种循环概率分布的条件. 我们也将引入在转移概率张量与随机张量这两种张量基础上的双重随机张量，并讨论关于它们的伯克霍夫-冯诺依曼定理以及在诸如三维任务分配等问题上的应用.

15300817.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15300817.value: 分数阶时间演化方程的高精度数值逼近

15300817.label: Project Objectives
15300817.value: For general smooth initial data and smooth source term (right-hand side of the equation), direct discretisation of the fractional-order time derivative generally yields only first-order accuracy in time in solving fractional evolution PDEs, due to the nonsmoothness of the solution near the initial time t = 0. Several papers have been devoted to improving the accuracy to higher order. With uniform step sizes, the accuracy of the numerical solutions is limited to second order or lower in the literature. In this project, we shall develop high-order accurate time-stepping methods for approximating the nonsmooth solutions of fractional evolution PDEs, by modifying the source term at a finite number of starting steps and then discretising the fractional time derivative with the convolution quadrature (CQ). The proposed method will improve the accuracy of the numerical solutions to high order while minimizing the number of steps of modifications of the source term. For nonlinear fractional evolution PDEs, existing numerical methods are limited to second-order accuracy, requiring very strong compatibility conditions on the nonlinear source term. We shall propose high-order time-stepping methods for solving nonlinear fractional evolution PDEs without imposing compatibility conditions on the source term, under the natural regularity of the solution, and apply the proposed high-order methods to solve nonlinear fractional evolution PDEs from physics and engineering. We shall present rigorous analysis for the stability and convergence of the numerical solutions of nonlinear problems. In contrast with the existing work, which often requires Lipschitz continuity of the nonlinear terms with respect to the unknown solution, we shall consider more general nonlinearities of physical interest by utilizing the maximal regularity of discretised fractional equations, which may be used to control very strong nonlinear terms that may not be Lipschitz continuous. An l^p version of discrete Grönwall’s inequality for fractional time derivatives will be introduced, which is particularly convenient for the analysis of nonlinear problems by using the maximal regularity approach. For stochastic time-fractional PDEs, both the underlying stochastic process and the fractional differentiation lead to low regularity of the solution. Hence, numerical approximation of such problems is very challenging. We shall propose efficient numerical methods for solving nonlinear stochastic time-fractional PDEs subject to space-time white noise, and prove the sharp-order accuracy of the proposed numerical method. Higher-order discretization methods will also be considered, which are particularly important for solving some nonlinear stochastic PDEs of physical interest in two- and three-dimensional spaces.

15300817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15300817.value: The solutions of fractional-order evolution partial differential equations (PDEs) often exhibit weak singularity at the initial time even if the source term and initial data are sufficiently smooth, due to the possible incompatibility between the source term and the initial data in practical computation. High-order accurate numerical approximation of such nonsmooth solutions is very challenging. In this project, we shall propose high-order time discretization methods, with uniform step sizes, for solving fractional-order evolution PDEs with possibly nonsmooth solutions, and extend such methods to solving nonlinear problems of physical interest. In contrast with existing work, we shall consider more general nonlinear problems without imposing the Lipschitz continuity assumption on the nonlinearities, by using the discrete maximal regularity of time stepping schemes established recently. Rigorous numerical analysis of the stability and convergence of the numerical solutions will be carried out for both linear and nonlinear problems, and extensive numerical experiments will be provided to support the theoretical results. Besides deterministic problems, we shall also develop efficient numerical methods for solving nonlinear stochastic time-fractional PDEs and apply the proposed numerical methods for solving nonlinear physical PDEs subject to space-time white noise. 在實際計算中，分數階時間演化型偏微分方程的初始值和右端項即使充分光也通常在初始時刻不相容，這就導致分數階時間演化型偏微分方程的解在初始時刻通常帶有弱奇異性。這類帶有弱奇異性的非光滑解的高精度數值逼近具有很大的挑戰性。在本項目中，我們提出一系列使用均勻時間步長的高精度時間離散方法來求解分數階時間演化型偏微分方程, 並進一步把這些方法推廣到非線性問題。與以往的工作相比，我們在不假設非線性項的 Lipschitz 連續性的情況下，通過使用離散的最大正則性來分析更一般的非線性問題。我們將為數值解的穩定性和收斂性提供嚴格的數值分析，並提供大量的數值算例來支持我們的理論分析結果。除確定性問題之外，我們也將為帶有時空白噪聲的隨機分數階方程發展有效的數值解法，並將用於求解有物理背景的方程。

Several papers have been devoted to improving the accuracy to higher order. With uniform step sizes, the accuracy of the numerical solutions is limited to second order or lower in the literature. In this project, we have developed high-order accurate time-stepping methods for approximating the nonsmooth solutions of fractional evolution PDEs, by modifying the source term at a finite number of starting steps and then discretising the fractional time derivative with the convolution quadrature (CQ). The proposed method improves the accuracy of the numerical solutions to high order while minimizing the number of steps of modifications of the source term.

For nonlinear fractional evolution PDEs, existing numerical methods are limited to second-order accuracy, requiring very strong compatibility conditions on the nonlinear source term. We have proposed high-order time-stepping methods for solving nonlinear fractional evolution PDEs without imposing compatibility conditions on the source term, under the natural regularity of the solution, and apply the proposed high-order methods to solve nonlinear fractional evolution PDEs from physics and engineering. But analysis of the schemes have not been finished.

We presented rigorous analysis for the stability and convergence of the numerical solutions of nonlinear problems with relatively smooth initial data. An l^p version of discrete Grönwall’s inequality for fractional time derivatives has been introduced, which is particularly convenient for the analysis of nonlinear problems by using the maximal regularity approach. Error estimate is done by using discrete maximal regularity of the numerical solutions. As applications of the maximal regularity approach, we established error estimates for an optimal control problem and first-order convergence of numerical solutions to fractional evolution equation with time-dependent coefficients.

For stochastic time-fractional PDEs, both the underlying stochastic process and the fractional differentiation lead to low regularity of the solution. Hence, numerical approximation of such problems is very challenging. We have proposed efficient numerical methods for solving linear stochastic time-fractional PDEs subject to space-time white noise, and have proved the sharp-order accuracy of the proposed numerical method.

15301017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15301017.value: Architectural fabric structures are of growing interest in modern architecture, due to their elegant design, high translucency, low construction cost and high flexibility. However, current architextiles have poor solar-heat-shielding ability (SHSA), so the temperature inside architectural fabric structures is significantly affected by the outer environment. To make it thermally comfortable, the costs of an adequate cooling system are huge, and it has limited applications in tropical areas such as Hong Kong. To address this problem, we propose to investigate a bionic finishing process, involving the first exploration into mimicking the micro-hair array of the Saharan silver ant (SSAnt) to enhance the SHSA of architextiles. Last year, the leading journal ‘Science’ published an investigation into the novel cooling mechanism of the SSAnt, which enables it to survive the scorching desert heat. The SSAnt has a reflective micro-hair array, which improves SHSA by: 1) acting like an array of optical prisms to reflect most of the incoming solar heat away from the body; 2) increasing the thermal emissivity for effective body heat disposal via radiation. These findings have inspired our idea of developing a bionic finishing process to enhance the SHSA of architextiles. Our proposed bionic finishing process will duplicate the micro-hair array of the SSAnt on polyester fabric by synthesising a horizontally aligned ZnO branched micro-rod (BMR) membrane and coating the fabric with it. The finishing process will involve three main steps: 1) synthesising ZnO BMR as the artificial micro-hair via the hydrothermal method; 2) producing the horizontally aligned ZnO BMR membrane via solution blending and the stretch-film method; 3) coating the fabric surface with the membrane via lamination as a reflective micro-hair array. Finally, the SHSA and other properties of the finished fabric will be characterised via the relevant standard test methods and a field test. This project will be significant for academia and industry in a number of ways. It represents the first attempt to develop a bionic finishing process based on the micro-hair array of the SSAnt, so the intention is to publish the obtained results in leading journals such as ‘Nature Materials’ and ‘Advanced Materials’. Our bionic finishing method can produce architextiles with high SHSA at low cost, and can thus increase the viability of architectural fabric structure in Hong Kong, and will be of high economic value in the textile industry. 建築織物具有優雅的設計、輕薄、低建造成本和高靈活性的特點，使其在當今建築市場中的應用日益增加。然而，目前建築織物的太陽能热屏蔽能力較差，所以建築織物內的溫度容易受外界環境的影響。為了維持舒適的溫度，冷卻系統需長期運行，由此造成很高的使用成本。因此，在類似香港這種熱帶地區較少採用建築織物。 2015年，權威學術期刊《科學》發表了一篇有關撒哈拉銀蟻冷卻系統的研究論文，研究指出該系統使撒哈拉銀蟻可以在酷熱的沙漠中生存。撒哈拉銀蟻冷卻系統的關鍵部分是其表面具有一層排列緊密細微的毛髮纖維，此毛髮纖維具有很強的熱反射能力，可極大地增強對太陽能的热屏蔽能力。此毛髮纖維的結構和光學棱鏡的原理非常相似，能夠反射大部分射向身體的太陽熱能，並透過輻射有效地把身體的熱能排出。這個發現激發了我們應用仿生技術研發具有太阳能热屏蔽能力的創新建築織物的想法。 我們將利用仿生技術研發類似撒哈拉銀蟻表面毛髮的細微纖維結構列並將此結構製造到滌綸織物上，即把整齊排列好的氧化鋅細微棒所做的薄膜利用塗層整理技術加工到織物表面。整個研發可分為三個主要部分：（1）透過水熱法合成具有毛髮細微纖維結構的氧化鋅細微棒；（2）透過混合溶液製造出氧化鋅細微棒薄膜，並把薄膜均勻地拉長；（3）透過層壓技術把薄膜塗層到織物表面，使織物產生具有熱反射的能力。最後，對所加工的織物進行相關的標準測試以評估其對太陽能热屏蔽能力。 這個研究項目在學術上和工業應用上將具有許多重要意義。根據撒哈拉銀蟻毛髮的細微纖維排列結構作為研究基礎，仿生研發具有太阳能热屏蔽能力的新型建築織物，預期將獲得顯著的热屏蔽效果，并將把研發成果投稿到一些權威學術期刊中，例如《自然-材料科學》和《先進材料》。我們的仿生技術將能夠以低成本生產具有高效太陽能热屏蔽能力的新型建築織物，從而提高建築織物在香港建築市場的應用并同時為紡織工業創造新的經濟增長點。

15301017.label: Realisation of objectives
15301017.value: Achievements to objective 1: We have successfully synthesized ZnO microrod as the artificial SSAnt microhair via hydrothermal method, modified from the method of Pimentel et. al. Zinc(II) chloride (ZnCl2), Triton X-100, aluminium isopropoxide (C9H21O3Al) and sodium hydroxide (NaOH) were used as precursors. In a typical synthesis, 0.037 mol of ZnCl2 and 0.00185 mol of aluminium isopropoxide was dissolved in 100 ml of deionized water and NaOH was then added under constant stirring until a concentration of 8 M was reached, yielding a transparent solution (solution A). Solution B was prepared by dissolving 30 mL of Triton X-100 in 900 mL of deionized water. 118 mL of solution A and 882 mL of solution B were mixed in 1 L glass bottle. The mixture was kept at 100℃ for 5 hours. The white precipitate was obtained via centrifugation. The resulted ZnO microrod is weighed about 1.4 g (molar yield = ~46.5%). It was washed with deionized water and ethanol under ultrasonic for several times to remove unreacted chemicals and then recollected via centrifugation. It is finally dried in air at 60℃ for 4 hours. The SEM image shows that our sample has a rod shape. The surface of the sample is very smooth and no separate Al2O3 solid forms on the microrod surface. The EDS results show that the Al is evenly distributed within the ZnO microrod. As a result, it is believed that Al is uniformly doped in the ZnO microrod. The diameter of the Al doped ZnO microrod was about 0.8-2.6 um while its length was about 10-40 um. The XRD spectrum shows that ZnO is in Wurtzite structure. It has strong peaks, implying that it has a high crystallinity. The (100) and (101) crystalline plane are considerably dominant compared to all other diffraction peaks. No peak of Al2O3 is detected in the spectrum. Achievements to objective 2: We have successfully synthesized a horizontally aligned ZnO BMR membrane. It contains three major components: Dimethylpolysiloxane binder, thinner and Al doped ZnO microrod. During the preparation process of the coating agent, 5 g of Al doped ZnO microrod is placed in 7 ml of silicone oil. They are mixed with vigorous stirring and are then dispersed with ultrasonic disperser to form a stable pigment paste. The pigment paste is then mixed with liquid silicone rubber in the mass ratio of paste: ELASTOSIL® LR 6200 A : ELASTOSIL® LR 6200 B = 2: 5: 5. The coating agent is finally placed in vacuum to remove the trapped bubbles. Polypropylene film is used as the release paper. The coating agent is applied on the polypropylene film and spread with Meyer rod. To adjust the thickness of the coating, we use plastic tape as a spacer to lift up the Meyer rod. By curing at 100-130℃, a silicone coating with aligned microrod is obtained. The alignment distribution of the Al doped ZnO microrod within the coating is studied with OrientationJ. The alignment distribution can be well fitted with Lorentzian function. The full width at half maximum is measured to be 16.7o. Achievements to objective 3: We have successfully duplicated the micro-hair array of the Saharan silver ant (SSAnt) on polyester fabric by coating the horizontally aligned ZnO BMR membrane on the fabric surface via lamination. Adhesive (ELASTOSIL® LR 6200 A/B) is applied on the silicone coating and a PET fabric is placed above it. Via hot press, silicone coating is attached on the PET fabric. The polypropylene film is finally removed so that a PET fabric with aligned microrod coating is obtained. The treatment provides a white, reflective coating on the PET fabric coated with microrod. The coating is very flexible and can be bended easily without damaging the coating. Mass increase by 111% after the treatment. In other word, the mass of original PET fabric is 262 g/m2 while mass of treated fabric is 554 g/m2. Pigment density on the fabric was calculated to be 0.46 g/m2. The SEM image of the cross-section of coated fabric shows that the average thickness of the fabric at the compression force of 6 g is measured to be 0.557 mm, with the standard derivation of 0.0151 mm, while the thickness of the uncoated fabric is 0.5 mm. The thickness of the coated is 0.0542 mm. The optical properties of the samples are measured via UV/Vis/NIR spectrometry. The transmittance in visible light and near IR range of fabric decreases about 10% after coating the microrod. This optical property is also observed in SSAnt micro-hair structure and can effectively shield off the sunlight. Meanwhile, UPF value is calculated to be 4872.05 and is significantly higher than that of commercial summer protective garment, which is about 50. Achievements to objective 4: We standardised the SHSA of the finished fabric by conducting the lab test. The Solar Heat Gain Coefficient (SHGC) is the fraction of incident solar radiation admitted through the fabric, both directly transmitted and absorbed and subsequently released inward. SHGC of the treated fabric is 0.29 while that of the original PET fabric is 0.39. Ratio = (0.74:1). This implies that our treatment can significantly improve the solar heat shielding ability. In order to obtain repeatable results of solar heat shielding ability, an in-lab solar heat shielding test was developed. Solar simulator (94081a Oriel Sol1A Class ABB) with AM 1.5 G irradiation was used as the light source. The plastic box was used to prevent temperature fluctuation caused by air convection. The fabric sample was placed above the plastic box to shield the solar light. The thermometer (AT4208 Applent, test range: -200℃---1300℃, accuracy: ±0.2℃) had 8 ribbon-type hot junction thermocouples (0.3 mm in diameter, K-type). Four thermocouples were sent into the case and touch with the bottom surface to measure the temperature inside casing. When black foam is selected as the ground material, ground temperature under PET fabric coated with the microrod, original PET fabric, PET fabric coated with silicone rubber (PDMS) and glass sheet are 54.9℃, 64.8℃, 64.7℃ and 107.8℃ respectively after 1 h exposure. The ground temperature under PET fabric coated with the ZnO microrod is up to 10℃ lower than that under PET fabric and PET fabric coated with silicone rubber (PDMS), and up to 53℃ lower than that under glass sheet. When brick is selected as the ground material, ground temperature under PET fabric coated with the ZnO microrod, original PET fabric, PET fabric coated with silicone rubber (PDMS) and glass sheet are 38.9℃, 43.2℃, 43.2℃ and 57.1℃ respectively after 1 h exposure. The ground temperature under PET fabric coated with the ZnO microrod is up to 4℃ lower than that under PET fabric and PET fabric coated with silicone rubber (PDMS), and up to 18℃ lower than that under glass sheet. Both results imply the treated fabric shows superior solar heat shielding ability in various conditions.

15301017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15301017.value: The current work developed a bionic coating technology that mimics the micro-hair arrays of Saharan Silver Ant (SSAnt) on the architextiles to enhance their solar heat shielding capability. To do so, the Al-ZnO microrods were synthesized via hydrothermal method and coated on the polyester fabrics in parallelly aligned way by a Meyer rod coating. The fabric properties coated with microrods were investigated with various tests. An outdoor solar exposure test was conducted to measure the solar heat shielding capability of the coated fabric. The diameter of the synthesized Al-ZnO microrods are about 0.8 - 2.6 um and have a length of about 10 - 40 um, which are similar in size to the SSAnt micro-hairs. The coated microrods are parallelly aligned along the fabric warp direction. The solar heat gain coefficient of the coated fabric is 23% lower than the original polyester fabric. The coated fabric has no degradation after exposed in simulated sunlight for 1440 hours. Under sunlight, the ground temperature covered by the microrods coated fabric is about 10℃ lower than that of covered by the original Polyester fabric.

15301317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15301317.value: Abstract In the development of future cancer drugs and therapies it is imperative to understand the molecular processes underlying tumor initiation and progression. Many key factors involved in these processes have been identified based on cell culture and transplantation experiments, but their relevance for tumor formation and disease progression in the living organism is often unclear. The SOX family (2, 4, 8, 9, 10, 11, 17) is part of the high mobility group proteins (HMG) being able to bind to DNA and plays a critical role in self-renewal and tumor propagation, such as in liver cancer, (liver CSCs), hence the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms regulated by the SOX family is an important link to tumor initiation and cell division. Unlike SOX2, SOX9 is unique in the fact that it is not involved in certain normal cell functions, such as for normal melanocyte stem cell function, the formation of hyperplastic lesions, and melanoma initiation. Hence, this makes it an important biomarker for studying some processes in tumorigenesis and oncology. To date, the complete crystal structure of SOX9, a transcriptional factor localized in the nucleus, is unknown, only the HMG domain is known, therefore, to our knowledge, no peptides or small chemicals compounds have been especially designed to bind specifically to SOX9. Our key goals here are to develop a probe that can be used to elucidate the initiation and proliferation mechanisms involving SOX9 and its functions in the cellular cycle. We also hope to optimize the probes for the development of multi-modal imaging agents – in vitro/in vivo via various imaging methods, and also in parallel create a dual function where the probe can produce some inhibitory function. To achieve this we hope to incorporate different peptides to enhance their target specificity. We propose to systematically develop several multi-modal complexes as fast responsive peptide based probes for targeting and monitoring the progression of the cellular cycle in various types of cancer cells.
