15301717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15301717.value: Practical systems for quantum information processing are all inevitably influenced by their environments in the form of heat, electron, and radiation baths. They are thus in principle open quantum systems. Understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of open quantum systems with a continuum of uncontrollable environmental degrees of freedom is a rapidly growing topic, which is important to quantum optics, quantum information processing and quantum transport. The essential quantum features of quantum devices, such as quantum coherence and interference, are often ruined by environmental noises. Suppressing decoherence and restoring quantum properties pose critical challenges to quantum technologies. Due to rapid developments in experimental techniques on atomic, artificial atomic systems and nanoscale solid systems with ever stronger system-environment interactions and environmental memory capabilities, conventional tools for open quantum systems, such as Lindblad master equation and Bloch-Redfield master equation, may not be able to accurately predict the dynamics. More generally, the Born and Markov approximations are becoming increasingly inapplicable. Under these approximations, evaluating the effectiveness of for example quantum control strategies may lead to unreliable conclusions. It is becoming highly desirable to pursue more accurate non-Markovian formalisms. The quantum-state-diffusion (QSD) equation is one of the most promising approaches for the accurate or exact solution of the non-Markovian dynamics of open quantum systems even with strong system-environment interactions. We propose to further develop and apply this approach as well as related methods to quantitatively investigate the non-Markovian dynamics of both free and controlled open quantum systems. We will consider potentially useful systems of current interest such as a superconducting qubit coupled to a coplanar-waveguide resonator. Cases with or without coupling to external bosonic baths will be considered. Decoherence suppression approaches including nonperturbative leakage elimination operators based on external repeated fast pulses will be accurately studied. Processes such as adiabatic passage, quantum state transfer, geometric phase-based quantum computation and high-speed quantum gate will be critically examined. 用于量子信息处理的真实量子系统都不可避免地遭受到周围环境的影响，比如热噪声，电噪声和辐射噪声。因此这些真实的量子物理体系原则上来说都是开放量子系统。当环境拥有多个连续不可调控自由度的时候，理解开放体系的非平衡动力学行为对量子光学，量子信息处理和量子输运来说显得尤为重要，所以这个方向的相关研究正在快速崛起。由于量子器件的量子特性总是会受到环境的破坏，如量子相干性和量子干涉性，因此如何抑制退相干和还原量子特性对已存在的量子技术提出了重大挑战。 对于原子、人工原子体系和纳米量级的固态体系而言，它们不仅能够与具有强大记忆能力的外界环境发生强相互作用，而且目前研究这些体系的相关实验手段也在快速发展，因此传统的研究开放系统工具可能不能够准确或严格地预测体系的动力学行为，如Lindblad主方程和Bloch-Redfield主方程。更一般性地说，波恩近似和马尔可夫近似的正确性正在逐渐地失效。在这两种近似条件下，对量子调控方法有效性的评估可能会导致出不可靠的结论。 因此科学家们正在强烈呼吁，希望能够找到一种更加准确的研究开放系统的非马尔可夫动力学方法。量子态扩散方程是目前研究开放系统中最具有潜力的方法之一，这种方法能够对开放系统的非马尔可夫动力学行为进行精确或严格求解，同样也适用于体系与环境有着强耦合的开放系统。我们进一步发展了量子态扩散方程的方法并且把这种方法以及与其相关的方法运用到量化研究不可调控和可调控的开放系统的非马尔可夫动力学。我们将会研究一些目前大家认为具有潜在用处、感兴趣的具体系统，如超导量子比特与共面波导谐振腔耦合系统。我们也会考虑系统与外界玻色环境发生作用和不发生相互作用这两种情况。我们也可以精确地研究抑制退相干方法中的非微扰泄漏消除算符，这种算符是基于外界不断反复的快速脉冲基础上建立的。我们也将利用量子态扩散方程严格地检验一些具体的物理过程，如绝热过程、量子态传送、几何相量子计算和高速量子门。

15301717.label: Realisation of objectives
15301717.value: All project objectives are completed. We have studied dynamical decoupling as a quantum control strategy. It aims at suppressing quantum decoherence by adopting the popular philosophy that the disorder in the unitary evolution of the open quantum system caused by environmental noises should be neutralized by a sequence of ordered or well-designed external operations acting on the system. We find in two-level and three-level atomic systems that a non-Markovian relaxation or dissipation process can be suppressed by a Markovian dephasing noise. In a related context, to suppress impact of environmental noise in coherent quantum phase slip systems, we have proposed a design consisting of multiple nanowire junctions to realize a phase-slip flux qubit. It can enhance the effective rate of collective quantum phase slips. Furthermore, we demonstrate how to couple two such devices via a mutual inductance. This is potentially useful for quantum gate operations. These complete objectives 1 and 2. We have proposed a coupled atom-cavity system which can attain controllable coherent perfect absorption. It does not require a strong coupling. The proposed system exhibits bistable behaviors, with bistable patterns switchable between conventional and unconventional shapes. The operation point of the perfect absorption can be tuned to be inside or outside the bistable regime. It can also be located at the upper or the lower stable branch or even the unstable branch of the bistable hysteresis loop. We also studied a quantum phase transition property of a cavity magnonic system as controlled by a parametric field. This results at a rich phase diagram, including the parity-symmetric phase, parity-symmetry-broken phase, and bistable phase. When increasing the drive strength beyond a critical threshold, the cavity magnonic system undergoes either a first- or second-order nonequilibrium quantum phase transition from the parity-symmetric phase with microscopic excitations to the parity-symmetry-broken phase with macroscopic excitations, depending on the parameters of the system. These complete objective 3.

15301717.label: Major findings and research outcome
15301717.value: For improved control of phase-slip superconducting flux qubit by introducing an array of Josephson junctions, we have proposed a design consisting of multiple nanowire junctions to realize a phase-slip flux qubit. It admits good controllability provided by gate voltages applied on superconducting islands separating nanowire junctions. In addition, the gates and junctions can be identical to or distinct from each other, leading to symmetric and asymmetric setups. We find that the asymmetry can improve the performance of the proposed device by minimizing the sensitivity to charge noise in the islands compared with the symmetric case. In particular, it can enhance the effective rate of collective quantum phase slips. Furthermore, we have demonstrated how to couple two such devices via a mutual inductance for possible quantum gate operations. An important quantum phenomenon useful for quantum control is coherent perfect absorption. This is studied in a two-level atom weakly coupled to a cavity embedded with a second-order nonlinear crystal. Under coherent perfect absorption conditions, the system behaves as a two-level system coupled to a cavity with a tunable effective bandwidth. The output field intensity exhibits a bistability. By tuning system parameters such as the frequency detuning of a two-level atom from the input driving field, the coefficient of the nonlinearity crystal and its relative phase, the bistable pattern can be switched from conventional to unconventional shapes or vice versa. The operation point can be switched between two stable branches. Our study provides a way to realize future optical devices utilizing coherent perfect absorption in the weak-coupling regime. We have proposed an experimentally feasible scheme to engineer the nonequilibrium quantum phase transition in a parametrically driven cavity magnonic system containing the spin ensemble in a ferrimagnetic yttrium iron garnet (YIG) sphere. By investigating its steady state in the presence of decoherence, we obtain the steady-state phase diagram of the system. With appropriate parameters, it is found that the cavity magnonic system can undergo both first- and second-order quantum phase transition by just varying the drive-field strength. Our scheme is implementable in a quantum circuit consisting of these elements using the parametric drive.

15301717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15301717.value: The cavity magnonic systems studied in part of this work are of particular interest because of its good experimental relevance. We plan to submit a research proposal to further investigate the quantum dynamics and controls in these systems.

15301717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15301717.value: Coherent phase slip in a superconducting wire attracts much attention because phase-slip junctions can form qubits which are robust against charge noise. Its realization represents a significant experimental challenge. We have proposed a design consisting of multiple nanowire junctions to realize a phase-slip flux qubit. It admits good tunability and can enhance the effective rate of collective quantum phase slips. When coupling two such devices via a mutual inductance, it is potentially useful for quantum gate operations. We have studied a two-level atom weakly coupled to a cavity embedded with a second-order nonlinear crystal. It can be tuned into a coherent perfect absorption regime, which is the reverse of laser emission process. Our system can potentially be applied to realize optical devices such as optical switches in the weakly coupled regime. In additional, focusing on a cavity magnonic system with quantized magnetization, a parity-symmetry-breaking quantum phase transition is predicted. Our work provides an alternate way to engineer quantum phase transition in a hybrid quantum system containing the spin ensemble in a ferri- or ferromagnetic material with strong exchange interactions.

15301917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15301917.value: Novel approaches to the manipulation of the flow of light in periodic structures has drawn great interest in recent decades. In particular, the restriction of light to flow in only one direction but not the reversed way could be useful for reducing optical signal losses significantly. This type of non-reciprocal one-way optical waveguides are not easy to realize because of the strong requirement on broken symmetries and their non-trivial topological nature. As a non-reciprocal device, compact optical isolator is also useful for improving the operation stability of compact lasers and its role in photonics can be considered similar to a diode in electronics. As a result of the fast development of photonic technology, the demand for compact non-reciprocal devices is increasing. However, the complexity of novel designs of non-reciprocal devices, such as two-dimensional non-reciprocal photonic crystals and photonic metasurfaces, requires much theoretical support. So far, a complete theory for the designs of these non-reciprocal devices are still lacking. For example, the theoretical limit on the thickness and bandwidth of a one-way filter based on magnetization is still unanswered. In this proposal, we plan to study novel non-reciprocal photon modes on two-dimensional surfaces where topological band theory may not apply due to the limited thickness of materials. The photonic surfaces to be considered include metasurfaces and artificial structures made of novel two-dimensional materials such as graphene and single-layer transition metal dichalcogenides and interface between two thin domains. We have already discovered an unconventional surface mode which requires further investigation on its consequences. We plan to analyze the roles of spatial-temporal symmetries and the eigen-response of the photonic bands in these ultra-thin systems. In the final stage of this project, we will try to use our developed theories to predict the theoretical limits for the thickness and bandwidth of linear non-reciprocal devices. 於週期性結構中對光進行操縱的新方法在近幾十年來引起了極大的興趣。當中，限制光僅在一個方向上流動可能有效地降低光信號損耗。基於對稱性破壞及其非平凡拓撲性質的強烈要求，這種類型的非互逆單向光波導並不容易被實現。作為非互逆器件，微型光隔離器也可用於改善微型激光器的操作穩定性，並且其在光子學中的作用可以被認為類似於電子學中的二極管。由於光子學技術的快速發展，對微型非互逆器件的需求正在增加。然而，對於二維不可逆光子晶體和光子元表面之類的非互逆器件的新穎設計，由於其複雜性，還需要很多理論支持。到目前為止，設計這些非互逆器件的完整理論仍然非常缺乏。例如，基於磁化的單向濾波器的厚度和帶寬的理論極限仍然沒有得到解決。我們計劃研究在二維表面的新穎非互逆光子模式。由於材料的厚度有限，拓撲帶理論可能不適用。研究的光子表面包括由新穎的二維材料組成的表面和人造結構的界面。我們已經發現了一種非常規的表面模式，需要對其後果進行進一步研究。我們計劃分析這些超薄系統中時空對稱性和特徵反應。在這個項目的最後階段，我們將嘗試利用我們開發的理論來預測線性非互逆器件的厚度和帶寬的極限。

15301917.value: All four objectives have been achieved. The eigen-response theory have been successfully applied to reciprocal-breaking materials such as gyromagnetic materials (Objective 1). Related results on extinction cross sections and transmission have been published in Refs. [1,2,4,6]. Spatial-temporal symmetry analysis has been extended to non-reciprocal photonic surfaces (Objective 2), with publication in Ref. [1]. [5]. For artificial photonic surfaces made of Yttrium Iron Garnet (YIG, a typical reciprocity breaking material), we have studied metasurface designs which can provide opposite one-way transmission at two distinct frequencies. 15301917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15301917.value: The development of new photonic technologies requires new designs of compact devices for controlling the flow of light. Non-reciprocal devices such as optical isolators are key elements for improving the operation stability of compact lasers and their roles in photonics can be as important as diodes in electronics. Compact designs of these devices are lacking because of the strong material requirements as well as failures due to lack of theoretical understanding. Our theories and the predictions of novel non-reciprocal surfaces have provided much clearer guidance on the thin-slab and/or broadband designs.

15302017.label: Project Objectives
15302017.value: Broadband fs time-resolved spectroscopy experiments will be done to study selected N1-methylated Cyt and derivatives in solvents of different properties. This work is aimed to probe directly the spectra, dynamics, and effect of solvent on excited states involved in the deactivation processes. The result will provide direct evidence for unveiling deactivation pathway and to help clearly identify the molecular cause due to N1 substitution on the nonradiative dynamics. Broadband fs time-resolved and steady-state spectroscopy will be used to study selected C5-methylated Cyt and derivatives. The works is proposed to provide for the first time excited state spectra, dynamics, and decay pathways signature to these recently recognized important base systems. The work is also aimed to examine solvent and substitution effect and to characterize excited states for not only the bases in their neutral form but also protonated or deprotonated form(s) relevant to the physiological condition. Steady-state and fs broadband time-resolved spectroscopy experiments will be done to characterize N4-methylated Cyt derivatives in solvent of varied polarity and H-bonding capacity. This work is aimed to provide the hitherto unknown but much needed information on the dynamics, electronic and structural nature of excited states for deactivation of these important molecules. The work is proposed to also explore effect of solvent and to elucidate presence or not of excited state intramolecular charge transfer (ESICT) and how the overall deactivation can be affected by microscopic solvent condition and mono- vs di-methylation of N4 in these derivatives. Systematic fs time-resolved and steady-state spectroscopy experiments will be done to study N6-methylated Ade derivatives with the purpose to monitor directly temporal evolution of excited state spectra and to determine dynamics and pathways of the deactivation processes. This work is proposed to also inspect effects of solvent and N6 substitution with an emphasis to resolve current uncertainty on the dynamic origin, role of solvent, and competing of ESICT with other decay channels for the excitation deactivation. Taking together the results from objective (1) - (4) will enrich greatly the current knowledge on photo-physics of nucleobase and derivatives; it will also contribute significantly to the understanding of structure-property relationship. This will help identify the key structural and environmental factor responsible for the extraordinarily high photo-stability of the canonical nucleobases. This will also make possible to evaluate photo-stability and propensity to photo-damage for the several minor bases that play important roles in epigenetic gene regulations and the onset of cancer.

15302017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15302017.value: 核酸甲基化對於維持基因組穩定性及多種生物過程的正常運作至關重要。甲基化通常發生在核酸四個鹼基中胞嘧啶和腺嘌呤的位置，進而形成相應的稀有鹼基。在各種稀有鹼基中，胞嘧啶的C5和N4甲基化及腺嘌呤N6甲基化而產生的稀有鹼基最為重要，在表觀遺傳學、基因調控、和疾病的產生，包括紫外光誘發的皮膚癌的形成等，皆發揮關鍵作用。因此，了解這些稀有鹼基的激發態過程是詮釋核酸光穩定性和光損傷的重要組成部分。已有大量的關於正常鹼基的激發態研究表明，其卓越的光穩定性源自於其激發態分子具有高效的非輻射躍遷通道和超短的激發態壽命。但目前對稀有鹼基的激發態了解甚少，這方面的工作是核鹼基激發態研究的難點。這主要是由於稀有鹼基激發態固有的複雜性。一方面，其激發態衰變發生在極快速的時間尺度上；另一方面，其衰變過程可能受各種因素，尤其是取代基效應和溶劑微環境等條件的影響。為了解決這一難題，我們提出利用先進的超快寬帶時間分辨光譜並結合穩態光譜方法，對多種稀有甲基化鹼基及其衍生物進行系統研究。研究的體系包括：胞嘧啶的N1衍生物，被稱為第五鹼基的胞嘧啶C5甲基化衍生物，最近才被發現的、被稱之為第六至第八鹼基的胞嘧啶衍生物、胞嘧啶N4環外甲基化衍生物，及腺嘌呤N6環外甲基化衍生物等，在不同性質的溶劑環境中的激發態光譜和衰變行為。本研究的目的在於為表徵所選稀有鹼基激發態的失活通道和時間尺度提供直接的實驗證據。研究結果將揭示鹼基甲基化及溶劑效應對其激發態動力學和非輻射躍遷機理的調控與影響。這將有助於從分子水平了解導致核酸光穩定性和光損傷的關鍵結構性和微環境因素。本研究的成功實施和完成將提供新的、重要的實驗結果，進而極大地豐富人們對鹼基激發態和其結構與性質內在關係的了解和認識。

15302017.label: Realisation of objectives
15302017.value: For objective 1: 100% achieved We have performed femtosecond time-resolved spectroscopic investigation where we combined femtosecond time-resolved fluorescence (fs-TRF) and femtosecond transient absorption (fs-TA) experiments on selected N1-methylated Cyt and derivatives in solvents of different properties. The spectra and dynamics properties of the excited-states involved in the deactivation processes as well as solvent effects are studied. For objective 2: 90% achieved We have performed an integrated spectroscopic investigation where we combined steady-state absorption and fluorescence, fs-TRF and fs-TA experiments on selected C5-methylated Cyt and derivatives. These results have been used to examine solvent and substitution effect and to characterize excited states for the protonated and deprotonated forms of Cyt and derivatives. For objective 3: 90% achieved We have performed an integrated spectroscopic investigation where we combined steady-state absorption and fluorescence, fs-TRF and fs-TA experiments on selected N4-methylated Cyt derivatives in solvent of varied polarity and H-bonding capacity. These results have been used to explore excited state intramolecular charge transfer (ESICT) and solvent effect in the excited-states of these derivatives. For objective 4: 100% achieved We have performed an integrated spectroscopic investigation where we combined fs time-resolved and steady-state spectroscopy experiments on selected N6-methylated Ade derivatives. These results have been used to determine the deactivation processes of excited state and to inspect the dynamic origin, role of solvent, and competing of ESICT with other decay channels for the excitation deactivation. For objective 5: 95% achieved By performing the investigations to achieve the objectives 1 to 4 above, we have obtained useful information on the photophysics of the selected nucleobase derivatives and on the key structural and environmental factor responsible for the extraordinarily high photo-stability of the canonical nucleobases.

15302017.label: Major findings and research outcome
15302017.value: We have conducted most of the experiments planned in this project. Through these measurements, expected evidences have been obtained for addressing most of the questions posed in the proposal. Our study shows that of 2’-Deoxy-5-formylcytidine (5fodCyd) after excitation at 267 nm forms the 1ππ* excited state with extremely low fluorescence quantum yield due to mixing with the lower energy closely lying 1nπ* state. The major non-radiative deactivation occurs in two steps including decay from the 1ππ* state to 1nπ* state with ~0.6 ps following by transformation of the nπ* state into the triplet state through intersystem crossing (ISC) at an ultrafast rate of ~1.7 ps. The time constants of the two procedures are excitation wavelength dependent, being ~2.3-2.5 ps and ~35.8-51 ps, respectively, with the excitation at 285 nm and 300 nm. This notable feature, according to the varying temperature measurement, is caused due to the existence of energy barriers for the transitions of 1ππ* state to 1nπ* state and from the 1nπ* state to the triplet state for ISC. Our study also unveils that the stability of methylated cytosine i-motif (iM) increases when using cacodylate buffer at acidic pH. Stability enhancement varies from location of methylation, decreasing from the core to the edge of iM close to the loop and further from single loop to double loop. The lowest Tm was recorded in 9CM under neutral pH condition, which possibly owing to the steric hindrance at this position destabilized the y flexible iM formed under the physiological pH condition. For hyper-methylated cytosine sequence, higher thermal stability was obtained when methylation occurred at the pairing cytosines. However, extensive methylation at the successive stacking cytosines lead to distortion of iM structure and reduce its thermal stability. Our study also reveals significance of protonation and a solvent environment in altering the excited state dynamics of Ado. This shows that AdoH+ features a bi-exponential dynamics occurring at the sub-picosecond and nanosecond timescales corresponding, respectively, to the decay of syn-N3 and syn-N1 formed by excited state tautomerization of the syn-N3 conformer. Our study also provides a possible mechanism for the conformation change of the N6-methylated Ade family after absorbing energy and the nucleobase can remain reactive, triplet state, for a long time after the relaxation, suggesting that N6-methylated Ade family loses the stability of Ade and therefore causes the oncogene related property.

15302017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15302017.value: Based on the outcome of this project, further research will be attempted to perform more combined fs-TRF and fs-TA experiments to directly probe the dynamics and spectra of the excited-states for more methylated cytosine oligomeric DNAs.

15302017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15302017.value: Nucleobases, the building blocks of genetic materials, absorb strongly UV irradiation creating electronically excited states that are crucial to the photo-stability and propensity towards photo-damage of DNAs. Apart from the canonical nucleobases, genomic DNAs contain minor bases induced by process like DNA methylation which is essential for a wide range of biological processes. Following the research plan suggested in the proposal, some methylated cytosine and methylated adenine compounds were investigated using femtosecond time-resolved fluorescence, femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy and steady-state method. The results help establish an overall description of excited state cascades for the compounds and new insight into role of microscopic solvation in affecting the deactivation processes and regulating the course and relative efficiencies of elementary steps for the photo-stability and probable photo-damages. The outcomes of this project have led to several publications in top international journals. The research grant allows training of several students, at both the undergraduate and post graduated levels.

15302317.label: Project Objectives
15302317.value: To develop ligand-promoted directing group-free regioselective arene amidations: We will prepare palladium(II)-amide complexes supported by chelating strong sigma-donor ligands and examine their reactions with oxidizing agents for synthesis of defined Pd(IV)-amide complexes. The reactivities of the palladium complexes for regioselective arene palladation and C-N bond forming reductive elimination will be examined. To develop ligand-controlled regioselective meta-C-H amidations of arenes: We would examine the formation of Pd(IV) complexes containing a nitrogen donor tethered with hydrogen bonding donor motifs. The tethers with optimal conformational properties will be designed so as to direct the arene palladation to some meta-C-H bonds.

15302317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15302317.value: Regioselective functionalization of unactivated C-H bonds by molecular catalysts is a promising approach for developing atom-economical and step-efficient organic synthesis. Catalytic C-H bond amidations by reactive metal-nitrene complexes have been extensively investigated. Despite some impressive achievements by this approach, the metal-nitrene complexes would preferentially react with the most reactive tertiary C-H bonds, rather than the secondary C-H bonds and primary C-H bonds. This has inevitably limited the application scope of this technology. Aiming to develop a general carbon-nitrogen bond forming platform, we focus our effort on developing late transition metal catalysts for activating arene and aliphatic C-H bonds to form reactive organometallic complexes, followed by the C-N bond coupling reactions with a variety of nitrogen reagents. This project is to develop catalytic C-H amidation reactions, where the selectivity is controlled by the ligands' / catalysts' properties. In this regard, we recently investigated the directing group-free arene amidation reaction catalyzed by a palladium(II) acetate complex of N-heterocyclic carbene ligand (2.6-diisopropylphenyl imidazolidin-2-ylidene; IPr). Treating trifluorotoluene and phthalimide with PhI(OAc)2 as oxidant, meta-selective amidation product was obtained preferentially in 50% yield. The amidation was initiated by the palladium(II)-phthalimide formation. The meta-selective arene amidation was probably mediated by a reactive amidopalladium(IV) complex. Prompted by this finding, we envision to develop catalytic regioselective arene C-H amidation reactions by designing metallacyclic amidopalladium(IV) complexes. Equipped with strong sigma-donors, the metallacyclic ligands should stabilize reactive organopalladium(IV) complexes, thereby favoring effective arene C-H amidation at mild conditions. It is plausible to design chiral metallacyclic amidopalladium complexes to effect desymmetrization of diarylmethylamines by enantioselective C-H amidation reactions. Our study would focus on chiral bidentate ligands with the backbones composed of chiral amino acids scaffolds. The chiral ligands can be modified to suit the steric and electronic demands of different enantioselective coupling reactions of interest. To achieve a broader reaction scope, we would study the reaction of amidopalladium(II) complexes with hydroxylamines, which feature a weak N-O bond. It is noteworthy that hydroxylamines can be prepared in situ by reacting amines with oxidizing agents. Oxidative N-O bond addition by amidopalladium(II) would afford reactive organopalladium(IV) complexes, which would exhibit favorable C-H bond coupling reactivity. Our approach to ligand-enabled cross coupling technology is based upon modulating the reactivity of organopalladium(II) complexes, and this approach is less susceptible to deactivation of the electrophilic Pd center. The successful completion of this project would open a new avenue for ligand-enabled Pd C-H cross coupling catalysis. 通過分子催化的手段對惰性碳氫鍵進行選擇性功能化是發展原子經濟性及步驟經濟性有機合成的有效方法。其中，利用金屬-乃春配合物對碳氫鍵進行催化酰胺化已得到廣泛關注。目前，儘管在該方面已經取得顯著成果，然而，當底物分子中存在多種碳氫鍵時，乃春配合物優先與活性較高的三級碳氫鍵反應，而不與二級及一級碳氫鍵反應。這樣就不可避免的限制了該方法的應用範圍。為了發展一種具有普適性的碳氮鍵構建策略，我們致力於開發後過渡金屬催化劑來活化芳香及脂肪碳氫鍵，形成高活性金屬有機配合物，然後通過這些金屬有機配合物與含氮試劑的偶聯來構建碳氮鍵 本項目旨在發展一系列碳氫鍵催化酰胺化反應，通過調控配體或催化劑的性質來控制反應選擇性。為此，我們以氮雜環卡賓（1,3-diisopropylphenyl imidazolidine-2-ylidene; IPr）與醋酸鈀配位的鈀（II）配合物為催化劑，對無導向基條件下芳烴的酰胺化反應進行研究。以醋酸碘苯（PhI(OAc)2）為氧化劑，以三氟甲苯和鄰苯二甲酰亞胺為模版底物進行反應，能夠以50%收率選擇性得到間位酰胺化產物。該酰胺化過程由鄰苯二甲酰亞胺-鈀（II）配合物的生成所啟動，芳環上間位選擇性酰胺化可能是通過高活性的胺基鈀（IV）配合物促進實現。基於該發現，我們設想通過設計合成環金屬化胺基鈀（IV）配合物，發展一系列芳環碳氫鍵的選擇性催化酰胺化反應。具有強σ-給電子能力的環金屬化配體可以穩定高活性的有機金屬鈀（IV）配合物，從而可在溫和條件下實現芳環碳氫鍵的酰胺化反應。在此基礎上，進一步通過設計合成手性環金屬化有機鈀配合物對碳氫鍵進行非對映選擇性酰胺化，從而實現二芳基甲醇的去對稱化也是合理可行的。本課題在前期工作基礎上，聚焦於含軸手性二芳基骨架的手性雙齒配體的設計和製備，通過對配體進行修飾來調節其位阻及電子性質，使其滿足不同非對映選擇性偶聯反應的要求。 為拓展該反應的適用範圍，我們嘗試將胺基鈀（II）配合物與含弱氮氧鍵的羥胺進行反應。眾所周知，羥胺可通過胺與過氧化物的反應制得。我們設想通過氮氧鍵對胺基鈀（II）的氧化加成可生成高活性的有機鈀（IV）配合物，該配合物對碳氫鍵偶聯表現出高反應活性。同時實現脂肪碳氫鍵的區域及非對映選擇性胺基化反應是另一個更具挑戰性的目標。在脂肪碳氫鍵的功能化反應中，由於有機鈀（II）中間體容易進行ß-氫消除而得不到目標產物，因此有機鈀（IV）配合物的參與將有望實現具有廣闊應用前景的脂肪碳氫鍵偶聯反應。

15302317.label: Realisation of objectives
15302317.value: This project initially aims to develop direct arene amination/amidation with electrophilic Pd(II) complexes. This approach is based on the polarizable nature of the arene pi-bonding that favors coordination of the Pd(II) ion for bringing about the heterolytic C–H bond cleavages via the concerted metalation deprotonation pathway. We obtained some success in this respect. However, the reaction scope remains limited as high temperature needed for the amidation also caused substantial side reactions, and extensive decomposition of the aminating reagents was observed and low-yielding of the products results. Our protocol is more practical for more electron-rich arenes, which would react faster at milder conditions. We performed some screening exercises on the ligands for the Pd-catalyzed arene amidation, and some electrophilic amidation reagents were also examined. To our disappointment, no appreciable improvement was achieved in bringing about a more productive transformation, and the scope remained rather limited to electron-rich arenes. To realize the research objectives of this project, we turned our attention to the reactive Ru-carbonylnitrene chemistry. With dioxazolones as electrophilic aminating agents, we achieved regiocontrolled direct C–H amidation using structurally defined [(cymene)Ru] complexes as catalysts. Noted that carbonylnitrenes are highly reactive and prone to undergo Curtius-type rearrangement, our first task is to identify the ligand sets for the Ru center for facile nitrene C–H insertion with the Curtius-type rearrangement being suppressed. As discussed in the later section, we have successfully achieved gamma-selective C(sp3)–H amidation regioselectively. With the use of chiral diamine ligands, the optically enriched gamma-lactams were prepared in up to 95 %ee. Detailed substrate scope studies were performed, and we found that the C–N bond coupling reaction occurred regioselectively at the gamma-C–H bond, alkene, and alkyne linkages are entirely tolerated. In general, the gamma-lactams containing aryl, vinyl, and acetylenic groups can be prepared by the Ru-catalyzed cyclization of the dioxazolones. It should be noted that the classical dirhodium(II,II) carboxylates catalysts suffer from poor chemoselectivity. We later extended the Ru-catalyzed carbonylnitrene reactions to direct arene functionalization to synthesize dihydroquinolinones. With [(cymene)Ru(proline)Cl] as the catalyst, cyclization of dioxazolones to form dihydroquinolinones in remarkable yields and regioselectivity. The dihydroquinolinones formation is mediated by direct nitrene insertion to the arene at the ipso carbon resulting in the spirolactam formation. The spirolactams then undergo either 1,2-C–C or C–N migration to give the dihydroquinolinones product. The spirolactam intermediates have been trapped using some phenol-substituted dioxazolones. With these phenol-substituted substrates, kinetically favorable deprotonation of the -OH group has preceded the skeletal migration, and thereby the spirolactams have been isolated and structurally characterized. We have tested several ligands other than proline for the arene amidation. For instance, 8-hydroxyquinoline and 8-aminoquinoline serve as effective ligands to support the Ru-catalyzed arene amidation. However, the Ru complex bearing the 1,2-diphenylethylene-1,2-diamine ligand is ineffective for the arene amidation. With [(cymene)Ru(proline)Cl] as a catalyst, amidation at the arene group was achieved exclusively, even in the presence of aliphatic C–H bonds. Compared to the diphenylethylene-1,2-diamine ligands, the use of proline enabled chemoselective arene amidation, rather than the aliphatic C–H amidation. The dihydroquinolines products were formed in excellent yields, and the arene amidation reaction can be scaled-up for practical application. We consider that effective regio- and chemoselective amidation would be an advantage for developing sustainable pharmaceutical production. Compared to the technologies based on notable metals, the use of earth-abundant first row metal for catalytic amidation would be an advancement to the field. Amides are prevalent scaffolds in many medicinal products and bioactive compounds. The conventional carboxylic acid and amine coupling require the use of a coupling agent (e.g. carbodiimides), which is often wasteful and atom-uneconomical. Here we successfully employ alkenes as substrates and dioxazolones as nitrogen reagents for the amide bond formation. With Ni(ClO4)2 as catalyst and 2,9-dibutyl-phenanthroline as ligand, the alkenes undergo hydroamidation to give anti-Markovnikov linear amides in excellent yields and regioselectivity. Other diamine ligands such as simple phenanthroline were examined and failed to display comparable results. An extensive substrate scope study has been conducted, over 90 examples were successfully achieved. The successful scope covers both the dioxazolones and the alkenes; structures with diverse electronic and steric properties have been included. Examples also include motifs of selected natural products (e.g. cholesterol, estrone, lithocholic acid) and medicinal scaffolds (e.g. ibuprofen, naproxen, gemfibrozil). Computational and experimental studies have been performed to delineate the origin of the anti-Markonikov linear selectivity. We concluded that Ni(II)-alkyl complexes be the resting state of the reaction, and its subsequent reaction with dioxazolones to form Ni(II)-alkyl-nitrene should be rate-determining. Noted that the Ni(II)-alkyl complexes would undergo reversible beta-hydride elimination to form a mixture of linear and branched Ni(II)-alkyl complexes. The use of 2,9-dibutylphenathroline seems to favor the equilibrium toward the linear Ni(II)-alkyl complexes, which would then react with the dioxazolones irreversibly to afford the linear amide product. The regioselectivity is under Curtin-Hammett equilibrium controlled. Apart from dioxazolones as the C–N coupling reagents, we are interested to explore diazo compounds as C–N bond coupling partners. We also explored the photocatalytic approach for C(sp3)–N bond formation based on radical coupling with diazoacetate. The radical is derived from photoredox reduction of the NHPI esters, which can be easily prepared in large diversity. This reaction is inspired by the classical nucleophilic alkylation using reactive alkyl-lithium reagents. The success of this project establishes an easier operational protocol for the alkylation of diazo compounds. The reaction took place at very mild conditions with the use of yellow light, which is less energetic than the common blue-light irradiation. The substrate scope study covers extensively on both the diazo esters and the NHPI esters, and highly diverse alkyl hydrazones have been successfully prepared with remarkable functional group tolerance. In conclusion, all the objectives listed in this project have been fulfilled.

15302317.label: Major findings and research outcome
15302317.value: [1] Based on our earlier success on the [(cymene)Ru]-catalyzed intramolecular nitrene C(sp3)–H amidation by decomposition of dioxazolones, we extended this chemistry to arene C–H amidation to afford dihydroquinolinones. Analogous to the case of aliphatic C–H amidation, facile nitrene formation occurred with [(cymene)Ru(proline)Cl] as catalyst without any isocyanate due to Curtius-type rearrangement was detected. Notably, the diphenylethylene-1,2-diamine ligands were ineffective for the catalytic nitrene arene amidation. Analogous to proline, 8-hydroxyquinoline and 8-aminoquinoline were effective for the catalytic reaction. [2] The mechanism of the dihydroquinolinone formation has been investigated. With reactive Ru-nitrene being the intermediate, the reaction is initiated by electrophilic nitrene attack at the ipso carbon to form a spirolactam. The spirolactam intermediate has been isolated and structurally characterized. Subsequent to the spirolactam formation, 1,2-C–C / C–N migration would take place to furnish the dihydroquinolinone products. Our catalytic reactions can be readily adapted to late-stage functionalization for the synthesis of anticancer compounds. This study has been published in Organic Letters. [3] Our next goal is to develop regioselective amide formation by hydroamidation of alkenes using dioxazolones as reagents. Due to pi-conjugation, NiH-mediated hydrometallation of aromatic alkenes or 1,3-dienes would proceed by Markovnikov regioselectivity. However, the analogous hydrometallation of aliphatic alkenes is known to be non-regioselective, affording both Markovnikov and anti-Markovnikov products. In this study, we employed pinacolborane as the hydride source, Ni(II) perchlorate as catalyst, 2,9-di-n-butyl-phenanthroline as ligand and dioxazolones as the reagent, anti-Markovnikov hydroamidation of simple alkenes has been achieved with linear-to-branch ratio > 20:1. The mechanism has been studied experimentally and computationally, and the regioselectivity is likely to be controlled under the Curtin-Hammett model, in which the more energetically favorable Ni(II)-alkyl complex would react faster with the dioxazolones to form the major product amides. This work has been submitted to ACS Catalysis, and the revised manuscript is under consideration for publication. [4] A metal-free photocatalytic protocol has been developed with diazoesters as the nitrogen source, and structurally and functionally diverse alkyl hydrazones can be obtained in good yields. Under yellow LED irradiation, the Rose Bengal would undergo photoinduced single electron reduction by the Hantzch ester. The rose Bengal anion radical then undergo single electron transfer to NHPI esters to generate alkylcarboradicals for coupling with the diazoesters to furnish the alkyl hydrazones. This work has been published in Organic Letters. [5] Since our work on the photocatalytic C–N coupling was published, we received an invitation from Prof. Paul Knochel for submitting a review article to Synthesis. The review article has been published in Synthesis.

15302317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15302317.value: Catalytic C–N bond formation is among the most popular reactions practiced in academics and industries. The catalytic protocols that forge C–N bonds are particularly important since catalyst-controlled (through the judicious choice of ligands) would modulate the selectivity of the coupling reaction. The use of inexpensive ruthenium and nickel catalysts is attractive for potential synthetic applications in the industries. It is feasible to undertake a more in-depth study on the catalyst decomposition pathways during the catalysis. By so doing, some unwanted side reactions would be identified and later be shut down through proper ligand design. Through ligand structure optimization, more robust catalysts that exhibit high catalyst turnovers with controllable selectivity can be developed. This is particularly promising for ruthenium and nickel because they are known to have rich coordination chemistry encompassing diverse ligand donor sets. Further development of the current reactions to enantioselective C–N bond coupling is clearly conceivable. To assess the feasibility, we performed the Ru-catalyzed nitrene arene amidation using optically enriched proline ligand, we found that the product dihydroquinolinones was obtained in 30 %ee. Further screening of available chiral ligand scaffolds is ongoing.

15302317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15302317.value: This project established metal-catalyzed and metal-free conditions for C–N bond formation, either through metal-nitrene or carboradical coupling manifolds. In this project, we showed that the metal-nitrene reactivity can be modulated to selectively functionalize either C(sp3)–H bonds or C(aryl)–H bonds with careful choice of the auxiliary ligands. The successful development of catalytic C–N bond coupling reactions by the nitrene and carboradical pathways permits flexibility in designing synthetic routes in industrial applications. Considering that C–N bond formation is one of the most practiced chemical reactions in industries, our protocols developed in this project allow direct functionalization of aryl C–H bonds and C(sp3)–H bonds. Our protocols developed here would enable direct functionalization of insert C–H for the regiocontrolled synthesis of aromatic and aliphatic amines.

15302717.label: Project Objectives
15302717.value: To prepare epitaxial bilayers of ferromagnetic (FM)/antiferromagnetic (AF) manganites and investigate their exchange bias behaviour. Primarily, La0.7Sr0.3MnO3 will be used as FM, while SrMnO3 and BiFeO3 will be used as AF. To explore the influence of electric field on the exchange bias behaviour of FM/AF bilayers, by applying an external electric field to the bilayer structure via an ionic liquid in a field-effect device geometry. To investigate the effect of electric field on the exchange bias behaviour of FM/AF bilayers, as applied in form of multiple pulses across a ferroelectric copolymer dielectric in a field-effect geometry.

15302717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15302717.value: Exchange bias effect occurs at ferromagnet/antiferromagnet interfaces, and bears the signature behaviour of shifted hysteresis loops from zero field position. The phenomenon is a heated research topic for various reasons. Being an important component in giant magnetoresistive devices, the effect provides a mechanism for locking ferromagnetic layers and allows the exhibition of antiparallel alignment of magnetic electrodes, an important criteria for many spintronic applications. Scientifically, the phenomenon itself has rich physics for investigations, and numerous theoretical and experimental studies have been performed to tackle the problem. For active regulation of device performances, it is desirable to have means of modulating the exchange bias behaviour, ideally at isothermal conditions. In this proposal, we attempt to regulate the exchange bias effect in epitaxial perovskite oxide bilayers by external electric field, and two approaches will be attempted. Firstly, ionic liquid gating of antiferromagnetic layer will be used to regulate the carrier concentration level in the material, which indirectly changes the magnetic behaviour of the antiferromagnet and changes the bias effect. Alternatively, low-amplitude voltage pulses applied across ferroelectric copolymer dielectric gate were found to change the properties of manganite films significantly, and the strategy will be adapted for electrical modulation of the antiferromagnetic layer and hence the exchange bias behaviour. The successful implementation of the project will provide additional means of regulating the performances of spintronic devices, and can provide information for future design of sensors and high-density memory devices. 交換偏置效應普遍發生於鐵磁/反鐵磁體界面，其主要表徵為從零外加磁場偏移的磁滯行為。作為自旋電子器件的重要組成部分，交換偏置效應能有效鎖定磁化方向，並有利於展示反平行磁極排列，是作為獲得巨磁阻效應的先決條件。在科學上，交換偏置現象本身也是一個重要的物理課題，於理論和實驗層面皆被廣泛研究。其中，於固態情況（特別是等溫情況下）主動調節交換偏置，能大大增強所製作器件的性能。 本研究嘗試通過外部電場以調節外延鈣鈦礦氧化雙層膜，並達致調控交換偏差效應。首先，我們會利用離子液體控制反鐵磁層的載體濃度水平，間接地改變其磁性行為及偏置效應。此外，我們發現施加在鐵電共聚物電介質的低電壓脈衝能有效改變亞錳酸鹽膜的性質，並可應用於反鐵磁層（交換偏壓行為）的電場調控。本項目的成功將可提供更多方法調節自旋電子設備的性能，並能應用於未來的傳感器和高密度存儲器件之設計。

15302717.label: Realisation of objectives
15302717.value: The current project aims at solid-state modulation of exchange bias systems with electric field. Specifically, (La,Sr)MnO3 (LSMO) perovskite manganite films and bilayers were deposited on lattice matching substrates. In the LSMO system, a rich phase diagram of magnetism can be achieved depending on the level of Sr doping in the parent LaMnO3 (LMO) compound. The combination of ferromagnetic (FM)-phase LSMO (FM-LSMO) and antiferromagnetic (AF)-phase LSMO (AF-LSMO) would lead to exchange bias (EB) effect, a phenomenon characterized by the shifted magnetic hysteresis from zero magnetic field and an enhanced coercivity. Given the sensitivity of the LSMO system towards oxygen vacancies, this project intended to induce modulation of EB effect in such bilayer FM-LSMO/AF-LSMO system through electrochemical generation/depletion of oxygen vacancies in the AF-LSMO layer. A summary of achievements made in this project, as in correspondence to the project objectives, are summarized as follows. Objective 1: Central to the current project was the preparation of FM-LSMO/AF-LSMO bilayers which can demonstrate EB effect. Ideally one should have a good control on the perovskite oxide heterostructures with atomically precise interfaces. Normally, metallic La0.7Sr0.3MnO3 is used as the FM layer since it has a relative high Currie temperature. However, magnetic properties of antiferromagnetic (La,Sr)MnO3 thin films were seldom reported, let alone using them as the pinning layer. At the beginning of the project, we established EB in FM-LSMO/AF-LSMO, using La0.35Sr0.65MnO3 as AF-LSMO and La0.7Sr0.3MnO3 as FM-LSMO. The structural compatibility between AF-LSMO and FM-LSMO allowed the epitaxial growth of heterostructures with sharp interfaces. To further modulate the microstructural and magnetic properties of AF-LSMO (which can be reflected viaEB), the AF-LSMO growth temperature was varied. This study offered a handle to modify the exchange bias effect, and shedded light on the magnetic properties of AF-LSMO layer under different AF-LSMO growth conditions. Results of this study was published in Publication 2 of Research Output (Part C of the report). Meanwhile, it was found that single-layered LMO films also showed EB behaviour. Despite being an AF in bulk, LMO films are often reported to exhibit weak ferromagnetism. In particular, LMO were deposited at low oxygen pressure on SrTiO3 single crystal substrates were found to show enhancement EB effect as compared with oxygen stoichiometric films. The impact of lattice matching with the substrates, and the thickness of LMO films, were also investigated. Results of this study were listed in Publication 1 of the Research Outputs. Given the close relation between the LMO system with LSMO, single layer LMO films were also adopted for the study of electric modulation of EB effect. Objective 2: A common approach for solid-state electrical magnetism modulation is through the use of ionic liquid (IL). In this project, IL was deployed to control the magnetism in LMO films. High-quality epitaxial LMO thin films exhibiting EB were deposited by pulsed laser deposition method at low oxygen pressure. By using IL gating, the out-of-plane lattice constant, structure disorders, Mn oxidation state, and magnetic properties of LMO thin films were regulated. The enhanced EB and restrained ferromagnetism in LMO suggested that +2V IL gating suppressed Mn3+ - O - Mn2+ double exchange interaction and enriched the AF phase. We speculated that the enhanced AF phase originate through the structure transition from pseudo cubic to tetragonal phase due to oxygen vacancies. Results of this work were presented in Publication 5 of Research Output. IL gating was also used in FM-LSMO/AF-LSMO bilayers. Sign reversal of EB was observed in the bilayers with the application of gating across IL. The change of antiferromagnetic ordering in AF-LSMO could be viewed by EB in the bilayers. To trace the evolution of interfacial AF ordering (including tailoring of EB field and sign crossover temperature) under different polarity IL gating process, high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADFSTEM) and electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) were performed. Quantitative STEM-EELS results suggested that the modulation of AF-LSMO was due to the creation and annihilation of oxygen vacancies in AF-LSMO, leading to the evolution of AF domains and defects. Results of the work are presented in Publication 7 of research output. Objective 3: In a previous GRF project, the PI investigated magnetism modulation in single FM-LSMO using a field-effect device geometry, with ferroelectric copolymer P(VDF-TrFE) as gate dielectric. It was realized that the application of small-magnitude gate pulse chains (which is smaller than the ferroelectric coercive field) across the copolymer gate would lead to substantial modulation of FM-LSMO magnetism (e.g. shifting of Curie point). We therefore further adopted the technique for modulating EB in LMO and bilayer systems. To start with, we attempted to establish the origin of magnetism modulation in FM-LSMO through the gate pulsing technique. We attributed the observations to electric field-induced oxygen vacancy accumulation/depletion in the FM-LSMO layer upon the application of pulse chains, which was supported by surface-sensitive-characterization techniques (X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and X-ray magnetic circular dichroism). These techniques not only unveiled the electrochemical nature of the mechanism but also established a direct correlation between oxygen vacancies created and subsequent changes to the valence states of Mn ions in LSMO. The results were presented in Publication 4 in the Project Output. Another important issue is the validity of the technique in modulating the AF-LSMO. To confirm the possibility of such a scenario, we investigated low-voltage pulse modulation of AF-LSMO thin films. Positive voltage pulses were found to increase the resistance of the films at low temperatures, which was ascribed to the oxygen vacancies induced by positive voltage pulses. This effect was supported by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) results. While positive pulses can induce significant changes in the AF-LSMO, negative pulsing showed little impact and is consistent with oxygen vacancy related process observed in various electrochemical reaction systems. These results were presented in Work 3 of Research Output. Finally, we prepared fully strained AF-LSMO/FM-LSMO bilayers with observable EB effect and prepared them into field-effect devices. By using electrical transport measurement, in-situ regulation of EB was realized via applying low-voltage pulses across the ferroelectric copolymer gate. Various microstructural and spectroscopic techniques (XPS, STEM and EELS) revealed that the control of EB in AF-LSMO/FM-LSMO bilayer mainly resulted in modulation of antiferromagnetism in AF-LSMO layer, due to creation/annihilation of oxygen vacancy in AF-LSMO layer. This work showed promises for low electric field regulation of antiferromagnetic spintronics. Results of the work are submitted and is included in Publication 6 of Research output. In summary, all the objectives in this work were fully addressed.

15302717.label: Major findings and research outcome
15302717.value: 1. Exchange bias (EB) effect was established in bilayers of (La,Sr)MnO3 with constituent layers possessing different Sr doping levels (thus achieving either ferromagnetism or antiferromagnetism). Optimal deposition conditions was established to maximize the observed exchanged bias effect (Publication 2, Part C) 2. (EB) was also observed in single-layer LaMnO3 (LMO) films. In particular, low oxygen pressure favoured the exhibition of EB and coercivity enhancement. The impact of substrates and film thickness on EB of LMO films were also investigated. (Publication 1, Part C). 3. The impact of field effect modulation in single-layer epitaxial FM-LSMO and AF-LSMO upon repeated gate pulsing were examined, using a general field-effect device geometry, with a ferroelectric copolymer as the gate dielectric. The magnitude of gate pulses applied were much lower than the corecive field of the ferroelectric, and hence remnant polarization is not expected. In general, positive gate pulsing was found to induce oxygen vacancies in the films, which could be detected through changes of Mn valance states in the films. Such a change would be accompanied by changes of electrical resistance and magnetism of films. On the contrary, little impact was observed due to the application of negative gate pulse chains. (Publications 3 & 4, Part C) 4. Such low-voltage pulsing scheme was then applied across FM-LSMO/AF-LSMO bilayers. By using electrical transport measurement, in-situ regulation of EB was realized via applying small magnitude, positive-voltage pulses across the copolymer gate. XPS, STEM and EELS techniques revealed that the control of EB in AF-LSMO/FM-LSMO bilayer mainly resulted in modulation of antiferromagnetism in AF-LSMO layer due to creation/annihilation of oxygen vacancy in AF-LSMO layer. (Publication 6, Part C). 5. Ionic liquid was also deployed in the modulation of EB in either FM-LSMO/AF-LSMO bilayers and LMO single-layered films, suggesting the possibility of regulating the antiferromagnetic phases and (indirectly) adjusting the EB effect (Publications 7 and 5)

15302717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15302717.value: - Oxygen vacancies can greatly change the crystal structure and symmetry of AF-LSMO. Indeed recent reports on perovskite films have shown superstructures in perovskites oxides that are sensitive to oxygen content. But the exact roles of the oxygen vacancies in crystal structure and the associated change is still not resolved. The magnetic structure and magnetism of this kind of structure is still an open question. - A clear phase change from pseudocubic to orthorhombic symmetry has been observed in LMO thin films after creating oxygen vacancies. How do the oxygen vacancies change the symmetry from pseudocubic to orthorhombic, and whether the orthorhombic phase the end of such transitions, are worth investigating. - In this work, all the systems investigated were low temperature AF insulator. A perovskite oxide system with room-temperature antiferromagnetism and sensitive to oxygen pressure would be appealing for application purposes.

15302717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15302717.value: In this work, we attempted to regulate the exchange bias effect in epitaxial perovskite oxide bilayers by external electric field. Two approaches were adopted. Firstly, ionic liquid gating of antiferromagnetic layer was used to regulate the oxygen vacancy in the antiferromanget, which changes the magnetic behaviour of the material and hene the bias effect. Alternatively, low-amplitude voltage pulses applied across ferroelectric copolymer gate were found to change the properties of manganite films significantly, and the strategy was adapted for electrical modulation of the antiferromagnetic layer and hence the exchange bias effect. The successful implementation of the project will provide additional means of regulating the performances of spintronic devices, and can provide information for future design of sensors and high-density memory devices.

15303117.label: Major findings and research outcome
15303117.value: Boundary layer driven by bacterial chemotaxis is a prominent phenomenon observed in the experiment, but no analytical results have been developed to rigorously show that the chemotaxis models can generate stable boundary layer solutions. The research outputs in this project provided first-hand results to justify that singular chemotaxis models can generate boundary layers when appropriate boundary conditions (i.e. Zero-flux and Dirichlet boundary conditions) are prescribed. These analytical results not only support the hypotheses made in the experiment, but also open a new research direction. Prior to our research works, there are no results on the study of boundary layer solutions for chemotaxis models.

15303117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15303117.value: The mathematical techniques developed in our works like the Cole-Hopf transformation resolving the logarithmic singularity and taking anti-derivative technique will help to conduct further researches on the chemotaxis models with physical boundary conditions. In particular these methods will provide effective ways to overcome the deficiency of solutions regularity due to the lower-order boundary regularity. Our research results provide a framework to study the boundary layer solutions of the chemotaxis-fluid models in the future.

15303117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15303117.value: In order to absorb more fresh airs for survival, the bacteria in the water will accumulate at the air-water interface along which a thin layer along was formed, which was a prominent experimental observation. How to use mathematical models to justify this hypothesized mechanism for the boundary layer formation driven by the bacterial chemotaxis remained unsolved. This research project partially solves this open problem by showing that the chemotaxis models without fluid subject to suitable boundary conditions do generate boundary-layer solutions which can potentially interpret the phenomenon observed in the experiment.

15303317.label: Project Objectives
15303317.value: To design and synthesize two-dimensional (2D) mono- and few-atomic-layer chalcogenides with ferroelectric phases. To observe ferroelectricity in the synthesized chalcogenides and to realize robust room-temperature ferroelectric ultrathin layers and vdW heterostructures. To establish the relationship between the structural properties of the 2D layers and their ferroelectric characteristics, and to understand physical mechanism behind the observations by combining theoretical calculations and experiments. To demonstrate ferroelectric chalcogenide layer based proof-of-concept devices (e.g., ferroelectric tunnel junction) operated at room-temperature.
rows: To design and synthesize two-dimensional (2D) mono- and few-atomic-layer chalcogenides with ferroelectric phases.
To observe ferroelectricity in the synthesized chalcogenides and to realize robust room-temperature ferroelectric ultrathin layers and vdW heterostructures.

To establish the relationship between the structural properties of the 2D layers and their ferroelectric characteristics, and to understand physical mechanism behind the observations by combining theoretical calculations and experiments.
To demonstrate ferroelectric chalcogenide layer based proof-of-concept devices (e.g., ferroelectric tunnel junction) operated at room-temperature.

15303317.label: Realisation of objectives
15303317.value: 1. In order to achieve the objective 1, we have designed our experiments to synthesize ferroelectric two-dimensional (2D) mono- and few-atomic-layer chalcogenides possessing a variety of crystal structure, composition and phases. Particularly, ultrathin van der Waals (vdW) α-In2Se3 and unexploited MoTe2 distorted 1T (d1T) phase down to the atomic monolayer limit have successfully been prepared. Regarding the synthesis, we have mainly employed fabrication methods of mechanical exfoliation (ME), laser processing for phase transformation, and vapor deposition techniques including molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) and chemical vapor deposition (CVD). As typical examples, the 2D MoTe2 nanosheets have been prepared using ME followed by laser process. Furthermore, monolayer MoTe2 films were deposited on highly oriented pyrolytic graphite (HOPG) and SiC substrates from Mo and Te sources by MBE. To ensure the stoichiometry and crystallinity of epitaxial MoTe2 film, the latter (Te) was set a few tens to hundred times that of Mo. The growth temperature was ranged between 250 and 400 °C. Prior to MoTe2 deposition, the substrate was thoroughly degassed in the ultra-high vacuum chamber and flashed up to 600 °C. In addition, we also used CVD to deposit large-area layers suitable for device applications. The In2Se3 samples by CVD were grown on mica substrates and then transferred onto SiO2 substrates by wet transfer techniques. Specifically, the 2D In2Se3 nanoflakes were grown on flexible mica substrates through CVD method. Se and In2O3 powders were used as the precursors with 10% H2/Ar mix gas as the carrier gas. The precursors were placed at separate quartz boats and the Se source was placed in the upstream. The Se and In2O3 powders were heated to 300 and 660 oC, respectively, and the temperature was held for 40 min in atmospheric pressure with carrier gas flowing at ~30 sccm. The 2D In2Se3 nanoflakes were deposited on the mica substrates placed above the In2O3 powders. After the deposition process, the CVD furnace was cooled down naturally to room-temperature. 2. To achieve the objective 2, piezoelectric force microscopy (PFM) measurements have been employed to study on the ferroelectric properties of the synthesized samples. The tests were carried out on a commercial atomic force microscope (Asylum Research MFP-3D), where a tip was driven with an ac voltage (Vac = 0.5–2 V) under the tip-sample contact resonant frequency (~350 kHz). Hysteresis loops were collected in the DART (dual a.c. resonance tracking) mode. PFM images were taken in single frequency or dual frequency resonance tracking mode. In addition, vector PFM was also performed by imaging the in-plane signal. In addition, ultrathin grown In2Se3 nanosheets were also exfoliated from bulk α-In2Se3 crystal onto Pt substrate for the PFM characterization. The PFM images, single-point off-field phase and amplitude hysteresis loops were obtained. The high-temperature single point off-field switching hysteresis loops were collected in DART-PFM mode with a polyheater equipped. We have used the technique to observe the robust ferroelectricity of α-phase In2Se3 from room-temperature to high-temperature. 3. To achieve the objective 3, we have measured various structural properties and deepen our knowledge of material’s properties (phase, non-centrosymmetry, layer number, crystallinity, orientation, etc.) and their relations with the observed ferroelectric characteristics (hysteresis profile, switching polarization, Curie temperature, domain, etc.) by combining theoretical calculations and experiments. Specifically, the Raman spectra of samples were measured by Raman spectroscopy (Horiba, HR800) using a laser excitation source with the wavelength of 488 nm and the spot size of 1 μm. Microstructures and chemical compositions were examined by transmission electron microscope (TEM, JEOL JEM 2100F) equipped with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX). The cross-sectional TEM specimen was prepared by applying FIB (JEOL JIB-4500) milling and lift-off technique. The cross-sectional atomic structure was characterized in a JEOL JEM-ARM300F with STEM aberration corrector operated. The chemical composition of samples was measured using XPS (Thermol Escalab 250Xi, Al Kα radiation). A Ti:sapphire femtosecond laser with the wavelength of 990 nm was used to examine the second-harmonic generation (SHG) signals of samples. We attempt to understand physical mechanism behind the observations by combining theoretical calculations and experiments. First-principles calculations of the electronic structure, phonon dispersion were performed within DFT as implemented in the plane-wave pseudopotential code VASP. In order to understand physical mechanism behind the observed phenomena, we investigated the origin of ferroelectricity as well as the phase transition temperatures of the layers which are of great importance to determine material’s usefulness in a variety of applications. 4. To achieve the objective 4, we used the robust 2D ferroelectric layers to demonstrate proof-of-concept devices including ferroelectric tunneling junction (FTJ) and multifunctional ferroelectric optoelectronic synapse. For FTJ device, the I-V curve of the device was measured by CAFM. The two polarization directions stand for the ON and OFF states of the device and the I-V curve is highly nonlinear in the ON and OFF states. To construct ferroelectric layered α-In2Se3/GaSe heterojunctions, α-In2Se3 nanosheets were placed on the source and drain electrodes, and then GaSe nanosheets were transferred to connect α-In2Se3 channels and gate electrodes, the fabrication processes were performed by a dry transfer system equipped with a microscope. Electrical characteristics were measured by Keithley 4200 in quiet mode. A waveform generator (Keithley 3390) was applied to produce light pulses. The power density of LED and lasers were calibrated by a power meter (Sanwa). Regarding the neural network simulations of the device, the program code was written in Python and combined with the neuron cores provided by the crosssim platform. The program ran under Spyder, a free integrated development environment (IDE). 5. In summary, we have fully achieved the four objectives of the project. Particularly, 7 high-quality papers are published with acknowledgements of this project. Among them, 2 papers are published in Nature Communications (one paper “Room-temperature ferroelectricity in MoTe2 down to the atomic monolayer limit” (2019, PI is sole corresponding author) is listed as ESI “Highly Cited Paper”, times cited: 126 (Google Scholar), 100 (WoS) as of 8 December 2021). Other papers are published in prominent SCI journals such as Adv. Funct. Mater., Nano Energy, Nano Research and so on. One postgraduate student IO Weng-Fu financially supported by the GRF grant has been trained in the project period. The student has published international journal paper in Nano Research as the first author, and Adv. Funct. Mater. as co-author. Because of her good record in her MPhil study on this project, Miss IO was awarded prestigious Hong Kong PhD Fellowship (2021/22) and continued her research in the PI’s group. To disseminate our results, the PI has given 5 plenary or invited talks in the recognized international conferences and our works contributed to this field have attracted much attention.

15303317.label: Major findings and research outcome
15303317.value: 1. We found that ferroelectric phases in 2D mono- and few-atomic-layer chalcogenides can be formed by phase transition from 2H to the distorted 1T (d1T) phase in MoTe2. In order to achieve the goal, the as-prepared MoTe2 nanosheets can be processed by a laser with 488 nm laser power of 2–20 mW for 10–300 s. Compared to ME, vapor deposition technique is found to exhibit the merits of synthesizing 2D ferroelectric layers with controllable layer numbers, reproducibility and wafer-scale. The detailed processing parameters can be tuned and optimized by considering varied vapor pressure and melting points of each metal element involved. (see: Part C: Journal 1,4,5,6, Conference 2,5). 2. PFM measurement is proved to be a powerful technique to study on the ferroelectric properties of the synthesized samples by considering that these samples are ultrathin ferroelectric and conventional ferroelectric analyzer is not applicable to the measurements in this project. Simultaneously, the I-V curves of the devices can be measured by CAFM at room temperature to characterize the electrical transport characteristics. Importantly, observation of room-temperature ferroelectricity in 2D layers down to the atomic monolayer limit can be achieved by using the technique. (see: Part C: Journal 1,2,3,4, Conference 1,3). 3. We observe robust room-temperature out-of-plane ferroelectricity in the thinnest monolayer MoTe2 with unexploited distorted 1T (d1T) phase. By combining theoretical study with experiments, we found that a few Te atoms move towards the Mo plane in the out of-plane direction by around 0.06 nm while the others largely remain still, which is consistent with the atomic structure model optimized from DFT calculations. Such trimerized structure with vertical atomic displacement of Te causes spontaneous polarization. The phase switching behaviors and ferroelectric domains of In2Se3 from room-temperature to high-temperature (200 oC) are first demonstrated. (see: Part C: Journal 1,4,7, Conference 1,4). 4. We found that the ON/OFF resistance ratio of the ultrathin FTJ device can reach up to 1000. The I-V curves measured on different devices present good reproducibility. A multi-terminal hybrid memtransistor can be fabricated, combining the concepts of both memristor and field effect transistor (FET) with ultrathin chalcogenide layers and van der Waals heterostructures as the active semiconductor layer. A novel multifunctional device based on ferroelectric α-In2Se3/GaSe vdW heterojunctions has been demonstrated to mimic the entire human visual system at the single device level. All devices achieved can operate at room-temperature. (see: Part C: Journal 1,2,5,7, Conference 1,4,5).

15303317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15303317.value: In this project, representative robust room-temperature ferroelectric ultrathin chalcogenide layers and vdW heterostructures have been made by both ME and vapor deposition methods. Firstly, we believe that more kinds of 2D ferroelectric layers and heterostructures with different formula and crystal phases can be developed followed by our techniques. Since the ultrathin layered ferroelectric and ferroelectric device approaching to the ultimate limit is demonstrated in this project, the discovery of ferroelectricity in monolayer 2D materials will facilitate further exploration of fundamental physics of ferroelectrics at the nanoscale and open up new possibilities for promising applications. Secondly, first-principles calculations of the electronic structure, phonon dispersion were performed within DFT as implemented in the plane-wave pseudopotential code VASP. It is possible to employ more modeling method to handle complex structure with ferroelectric phases, leading to understanding additional factors such as ferroelectric phase transition and domain. Lastly, we have demonstrated typical proof-of-concept devices using the ferroelectric chalcogenide layers. Based on the achieved results, there is a great potential to develop artificial intelligent devices that mimic biological neural behaviors such as synaptic short-term plasticity and long-term plasticity when developing further ferroelectric layered devices for efficiently processing complex information and simplifying the design of systems.

15303317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15303317.value: Ferroelectricity has found a wide range of applications. Currently, technological progress has pushed increasingly miniaturized devices and systems, stimulating an intense search for ultrathin ferroelectric materials as fertile ground for new physics and applications. In this project, we have employed fabrication methods of mechanical exfoliation, laser processing for phase transition and vapor deposition techniques to synthesize two-dimensional (2D) mono- and few-atomic-layer chalcogenides. The prepared layers possess a variety of crystal structure, composition and phase. Importantly, we observed room-temperature ferroelectricity in the synthesized layers down to the atomically thin limit. Physical mechanism behind the observed phenomenon is understood by combining various characterizations and theoretical calculations. The origin of the ferroelectricity in the chalcogenides results from the spontaneous symmetry breaking due to the relative atomic displacements of different atoms. Moreover, we demonstrate proof-of-concept devices including ferroelectric tunneling junction and multifunctional ferroelectric synapse using the robust 2D ferroelectric layers. High ON/OFF resistance ratio is achieved in the devices based on van der Waals heterostructures. Our works broaden the functionalities of 2D layered materials, which can take conventional ferroelectric devices to the 2D limit. The research project provides insights into promising applications, such as nanoelectronic, optoelectronic, smart sensing and nano energy devices.
