15303417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15303417.value: Recent research attention has been focused on the use of plasmonic nanostructures to enhance the nonlinear frequency conversion efficiency of metals in sub-diffraction-limited volumes. For example, enhanced second- and third-harmonic generation (S/THG) of light has been demonstrated in a single plasmonic nanocavity consisting of a metal nanoparticle separated from a metal film by a nanometer-thick self-assembled molecular monolayer or a dielectric oxide layer. So far, the S/THG efficiency in such a plasmonic nanocavity can be controlled only in a passive manner, namely, through simply adjusting the particle-film gap distance by changing the molecular length or the oxide film thickness. Conversely, active control such as electrical, optical and electrochemical modulation of the nonlinear optical phenomena in plasmonic structures remains relatively unexplored. Realization of active control in nonlinear plasmonics is of essential importance for photonics applications, particularly for optical signal and information processing. Additionally, it remains unclear whether the particle-film contact area has a substantial effect on the nonlinear emission efficiency of the plasmonic nanocavity. The aim of the proposed research is to realize all-optical control of the nonlinear emissions in an individual plasmonic molecular nanocavity. The nanocavity consists of a single gold nanoparticle (nanosphere, nanorod, or nanocube) separated from a gold mirror by a self-assembled monolayer of photoactive molecules, a hybrid platform of metal nanophotonics and molecular electronics. Here the photoconductive path at the particle-film junction can be optically triggered in a fast and repeatable manner, leading to an all-optical modulation of the effective dielectric environment of the junction and so for the linear and nonlinear optical properties of the nanocavity. The all-optical control of the linear plasmonic response is expected to manifest itself by a significant blueshift in the bonding dipolar plasmon (BDP) resonance and possible appearance of a low-energy tunneling charge transfer plasmon (tCTP) resonance upon switching on the conductive path under ultraviolet-light illumination; The system will recover to its initial state upon silencing the conductive junction with visible-light illumination. Thus, by setting the fundamental femtosecond excitation wavelength at the BDP (tCTP) resonance, one can optically modulate the emission intensity of ultraviolet-visible SHG (THG) through plasmonic on- or off-resonance enhancement. The project will be carried out in collaboration with Prof. Peter Nordlander at Rice University (US), and his team will be responsible for theoretical understanding of the light-induced charge transfer across the conductive junction that serves as the physical mechanism for the plasmon resonance tuning of the nanocavity. 利用表面等離激元納米結構在亞衍射極限內增強金屬的非線性頻率轉化效率已經成為當前納米光子學研究的熱點。比如，研究發現由薄膜耦合金屬納米顆粒構成的單個表面等離激元納米腔展現出增強的二次和三次諧波發射。然而，目前的研究只能被動地控制這種表面等離激元納米腔的諧波發射，也就是通過直接改變薄膜-顆粒之間的分子長度或者氧化層厚度。相反，表面等離激元納米結構中非線性光學現象的主動調控研究相對較少，包括電學、光學和電化學調控。實現非線性表面等離激元的主動調控對納米光子學中光學信號和信息處理極其重要。此外，目前的研究還沒有完全理解在單個表面等離激納米腔中薄膜-顆粒接觸面積對其非線性發射效率的影響。 此建議研究的目標是實現單個表面等離激元分子納米腔中非線性發射的全光調控。這種納米腔是通過把單個金納米顆粒（納米球和納米棒）用光敏分子連接在一個金薄膜鏡面上，組成一個金屬納米光子學和分子電子學的雜化納米結構。薄膜-顆粒納米結間的光電導通道可以被入射光快速、重復地觸發，從而全光調制納米結中的有效介電環境和線性/非線性光學特性。用紫外光照射開啟納米腔的導電通道會使綁定偶極等離激元共振藍移，並伴隨著可能在低能區域出現的隧穿電荷轉移等離激元模式；用可見光照射關閉納米腔的導電通道可以恢復系統的原本狀態。因此，把基頻的飛秒激發脈沖波長設定在納米腔的綁定偶極等離激元共振波長處，可以通過光觸發的共振和非共振等離激元增強來全光調控系統在紫外-可見區的二次和三次諧波產生。此研究會和美國萊斯大學的Peter Nordlander教授合作，他的研究團隊負責理論理解納米腔中光誘發電荷轉移對表面等離激元共振的調制。

15303417.label: Realisation of objectives
15303417.value: We have fully addressed and achieved the proposed project objectives by undertaking the planned research activities, with details summarized as follows. Results achieved (1) We have successfully prepared plasmonic molecular nanocavities by either linking single gold nanospheres to a gold thin film or connecting a gold nanosphere core to a gold shell with self-assembled nanometer-thick photo-inactive, photoactive or conductive molecules (objective 1), and applied single-particle dark-field scattering imaging and micro-spectroscopy to characterize their structural morphology and molecular conductivity dependent linear optical properties (objective 2) as well as all-optical control of the cavity’s plasmon resonance frequencies (objective 3). To achieve the above-described project objectives, we have fabricated three types of plasmonic molecular nanocavities, namely (1) plasmonic particle-on-film nanocavities through linking gold nanospheres onto a thin gold film with a self-assembled photo-inactive molecule (CTAB), (2) plasmonic core-molecule-shell nanocavities through bridging a gold nanosphere core to a gold shell with a self-assembled monolayer of length-varied conductive molecules, and (3) plasmonic particle-on-film nanocavities through linking gold nanospheres onto a thin gold film with a self-assembled photoactive host-guest molecular system. To investigate the effects of molecular conductivity, junction length and contact area in the plasmon resonance shift, we have deliberately (1) used the photo-inactive molecule – CTAB, three types of length-varied conductive molecules – BDT, BPDT, and TPDT, and the photoactive host-guest molecular system – the guest molecule diarylethene embedded into the host molecule thiol-β-CD, and (2) compared the plasmonic responses of zero-dimensional gold sphere-on-film nanocavities and three-dimensional gold core-molecule-shell nanocavities, i.e. changing the nanoparticle shape from sphere to core-shell. We have then used a commercial UV-Vis spectrometer and our home-built single-particle dark-field scattering imaging and micro-spectroscopy to measure their structural morphology, junction length and molecular conductivity dependent absorption and scattering spectra. In the meanwhile, we have performed full-wave electrodynamics simulations on these plasmonic molecular nanocavity systems in order to fully understand their near-field and far-field optical properties. On the one hand, we have observed from single-particle dark-field scattering measurements that the CTAB-assembled plasmonic particle-on-film nanocavities exhibited two pronounced scattering peaks at around 560 nm and 850 nm. Our full-wave electromagnetic simulation results reveal that these two plasmonic modes originate from the near-field interaction between the localized surface plasmon (LSP) of the gold nanosphere and its induced image in the gold film (forming a plasmonic virtual nanoparticle dimer), which results in a prominent vertical bonding dipolar mode at a wavelength of 850 nm and a weaker, horizontal bonding dipolar mode at a shorter wavelength. Objective 1 addressed and achieved. On the other hand, we have observed from high-resolution transmission electron microscope imaging characterizations that the three types of plasmonic gold core-molecule-gold-shell nanocavities with self-assembled monolayers of length-varied conductive molecules – BDT, BPDT, and TPDT have core-shell gap distances varying from 0.7 to 0.9 and 1.5 nm. We have further observed from UV-Vis spectroscopy measurements that the three plasmonic molecular nanocavities all exhibit only one absorption peak in the visible range with a slight shift of a few nanometers, consistent with our earlier full-wave electromagnetic simulation results based on a quantum conductance corrected model (although being inconsistent with the prediction by a classical electromagnetic model). Objective 2 addressed and achieved. Finally, we have observed from single-particle dark-field scattering measurements that the host-guest molecular complex plasmonic metal particle-on-film nanocavities exhibit reversible optical tuning of their scattering peaks under alternative illumination of ultraviolet (UV) and visible light, which induces reversible photo-isomerization of the guest molecule thiol-β-CD. Such photo-switchable plasmonic response has been verified by the light-triggered switching of the correlated UV-Vis absorption and surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) spectra of the host molecule. Objective 3 addressed and achieved. (2) We have successfully realized all-optical active and passive control of SHG and two-photon photoluminescence (TPL) signals in the three types of plasmonic molecular nanocavities (objective 4), and also made comparative analysis of our experimental results with theoretical calculations to reveal the physiochemical mechanism governing the light-triggered-photoconductivity based linear and nonlinear plasmon tuning (objective 5). To achieve the abovementioned project objectives, we have performed single-particle nonlinear spectroscopy on the three-types of plasmonic molecular nanocavities in correlation with their linear scattering or absorption spectroscopic results. On the one hand, we have measured SHG and TPL signals of single CTAB-assembled gold nanosphere-on-gold film cavities and gold nanosphere dimers. By carrying out excitation-wavelength-dependent and excitation/detection-polarization-resolved nonlinear spectroscopy on both types of cavities, we have surprisingly found that the former structure exhibits a much stronger surface SHG signal intensity than the latter, even comparable to its bulk TPL signal intensity. Theoretical analysis coupled with full-wave electromagnetic simulations reveal that the significantly enhanced surface SHG be attributed to the light-induced electromagnetic asymmetry in the gold sphere-CTAB-gold film nanogap junction, which efficiently suppresses the cancelling of locally generated SHG fields and the SH emission is further amplified through preferential coupling to the bright, bonding dipolar resonance mode of the nanocavity. On the other hand, in the aspect of nonlinear emission modulation, we have realized passive control of TPL signals in the plasmonic gold core-molecule-gold shell nanocavities. We have observed that the TPL emission spectral response of each nanocavity has a very similar spectral profile as the corresponding scattering spectrum with a peak cantered at around 540 nm and a full-width half maximum of about 150 nm, indicating a radiative de-excitation of the localized surface plasmons induced by two-photon absorption. Importantly, the excitation wavelength dependence of integrated TPL signals reveals several maxima in the excitation wavelength range from 700 nm to 800 nm. Our theoretical calculations have revealed that the TPL response of such conductive plasmonic junctions is closely related to the near-field enhancement inside the metal regions, and can be strongly affected by the electron transport through the embedded conductive molecules. TPL excitation spectroscopy results for the three plasmonic molecular junctions (with 0.7, 0.9 and 1.5 nm junction widths) have shown no perceivable contribution from their low-energy plasmon modes. We have well explained these TPL results by a quantum-corrected model, assuming significant conductance for the self-assembled molecular layers and thus efficient charge transport through the junctions. Objective 4 addressed and achieved. Finally, in the aspect of all-optical active control of nonlinear emission, we have realized photoswitching of SHG signals in the plasmonic particle-on-film nanocavities sandwiched assembled by a self-assembled photoactive host-guest molecular system. In experiment, by switching the molecular junction to the “on” state under UV light illumination, we have observed that the SHG emission intensity from such a single photoconductive plasmonic nanocavity is enhanced nearly by an order of magnitude compared to that of the original structure; by switching the molecular junction to the “off” state under visible light illumination, the SHG signal intensity is quenched to the same level as that of the original structure before the UV light illumination. A manuscript reporting these results is currently under review with Nano Letters (2022). Objective 5 addressed and achieved.

15303417.label: Major findings and research outcome
15303417.value: Major findings and research outcome of this GRF research project are summarized in the following 6 aspects. (1) The vertical dipolar mode in a CTAB-assembled plasmonic particle-on-film nanocavity features a strong electromagnetic field enhancement in the gap region with the dominant electric field component oriented in the vertical direction. On resonance, the maximum field enhancement in this extremely small gap reaches approximately 300, resulting in a second-harmonic generation (SHG) excitation rate enhancement up to 90,000-fold. Indeed, this leads to a far-field SHG conversion efficiency of up to 3.56x10-7 W−1, two orders of magnitude higher than for complex double-resonant plasmonic nanostructures or simple gold nanosphere dimers (Nature Communications 2021, 12, 4326, item 3 in Section 8 of Part C). (2) Molecular conductivity can quench the long-wavelength bonding dipolar plasmon mode in conductive molecule assembled 3D plasmonic core-shell nanocavities, consistent with our quantum conductance corrected model based full-wave electromagnetic simulation results. Importantly, we have explored the charge transport mechanism by investigating the junction width dependent TPL intensity under a given excitation wavelength, contributing to the field of molecular electronic plasmonics by opening up a new avenue for studying quantum charge transport in molecular junctions by nonlinear optical spectroscopy (Nanophotonics 2021, 10 (9), 4326, item 4 in Section 8 of Part C). (3) Light-triggered photoconduction modulation of a host-guest molecular complex system leads to reversible tuning of plasmon resonance in a photoactive plasmonic molecular nanocavity. Both SERS and SHG emission signals from such nanocavity can be actively tuned through light-triggered conductance switching, enabling tremendous flexibilities in designing plasmonic molecular nanocavities and manipulating their optical properties (a manuscript under review with Nano Letters 2022, item 6 in Section 8 of Part C). (4) We have implemented topology optimization to inversely design a metallic nanoparticle dimer with the goal of optimizing the near-field enhancement factor in its sub-10 nm gap. By optimizing the material layout within a given design space, the topology optimization algorithm results in a plasmonic nano-dimer of two heart-shaped particles having both convex and concave features, which exhibits a larger near-field enhancement in the nanogap than inversely designed bowtie- and disk-shaped nano-dimers and hence the largest TPL signals under fs laser excitation (Advanced Functional Materials 2020, 30 (23), 2000642, item 1 in Section 8 of Part C). (5) Inspired by the above results on all-optical control of plasmon-enhanced nonlinear emissions, we have further demonstrated the application of nonlinear SHG and TPL signals in mapping the magnetic and electric field Intensities of incident light beams. Briefly, we demonstrate a simple and straightforward method to exclusively map the magnetic field intensity distribution of light with single spherical silicon (Si) nanoparticles or the electric field intensity distribution of light with single spherical gold nanoparticles. We exploit the nonlinear optical emission properties of single Si and gold nanoparticles and show that such nonlinear electric (gold) and magnetic (Si) nanoprobes enable direct mapping of the intensity distribution profiles of unknown electric or magnetic fields with arbitrary electromagnetic structures (Nano Letters 2021, 21 (6), 2453-2460, item 5 in Section 8 of Part C). (6) In the metatronic paradigm, we have proposed a displacement current based circuit model to reproduce the resonance spectral details of a series of optical nano-circuits comprising plasmonic oligomers with varied structural symmetries and retrieve many hidden physical quantities associated with their optical responses. These metatronic circuits allow us to predict spectral engineering of the oligomers with reduced geometric symmetry and examine subgroup decomposition of several plasmonic quadrumers, revealing a close correlation between the metatronic circuitry and strongly coupled plasmonic oligomers (ACS Photonics 2021, 8 (1), 166-174, item 2 in Section 8 of Part C).

15303417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15303417.value: While carrying out this GRF research project, we have come up with a new experimental idea about exploiting quantum tunneling through an ultrathin plasmonic molecular nano-junction to produce and enhance optical high-harmonic generation. This experimental idea is inspired and grounded on two elegant theoretical publications, namely (1) D. C. Marinica et al., Quantum Plasmonics: Nonlinear Effects in the Field Enhancement of a Plasmonic Nanoparticle Dimer, Nano Letters 12 (3), 1333 (2012), and (2) J. W. Haus et al., Nonlinear quantum tunneling effects in nanoplasmonic environments: two-photon absorption and harmonic generation, Journal of Optical Society America A 31, A13 (2013). Based on this new idea and some preliminary results, the PI has developed and submitted an ANR-RGC Joint Research Scheme grant in 2020. In the new proposal, will investigate both experimentally and theoretically quantum tunneling enhanced optical harmonic generation in rationally designed plasmonic nano-junctions as functions of tunneling barrier, incident power and incident/detection polarizations at the single nanostructure level. We will reveal the critical dimension at which the quantum size effects must be fully considered in all nanophotonic systems, with an ultimate aim of distinguishing the interplay between classical field enhancement and quantum tunneling effects in the optical harmonic generation of quantum-sized plasmonic systems. In the long term, we hope that our study could open up new avenues for nonlinear optics and nanoplasmonics, and also shed light on research fields such as quantum transport and molecular electronics.

15303417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15303417.value: Plasmonic nanostructures have long been used to enhance the nonlinear frequency conversion efficiency of metals in sub-diffraction-limited volumes. For example, enhanced second- and third-harmonic generation (S/THG) of light has been demonstrated in a variety of plasmonic nanocavities. However, the S/THG efficiency in such nanocavities have so far been controlled only in a passive manner; active control such as electrical, optical and electrochemical modulation of the nonlinear optical phenomena in plasmonic structures remains relatively unexplored, which is of critical importance for photonic applications such as optical signal and information processing. Through carrying out this project, we have achieved both passive modulation and active control of SHG and TPL in plasmonic molecular nanocavities. On the one hand, we have discovered the light-induced electromagnetic asymmetry in a symmetry-broken plasmonic particle-on-film nanocavity separated by a self-assembled photo-inactive molecular monolayer and observed significantly enhanced SHG and TPL in comparison to a symmetric plasmonic nanosphere dimer. On the other hand, we have demonstrated molecular conductivity dependent TPL signals in 3D plasmonic core-shell nanocavities assembled by conductive molecules, consistent with our quantum conductance corrected model based full-wave electromagnetic simulation results. Finally, we have realized reversible photoswitching of plasmon resonance tuning and corresponding SHG in a host-guest molecular system assembled plasmonic particle-on-film nanocavity through light-triggered photoconduction modulation. Our results will enable tremendous flexibilities in designing plasmonic molecular nanocavities and manipulating their optical properties at the interface with molecular electronics.

15303517.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15303517.value: 海量數據的自助法統計推斷

15303517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15303517.value: Technological advances in data collection are increasing the availability of massive datasets. These datasets bring both opportunities and new challenges to statisticians. We focus on using the bootstrap to assessing the precision of estimators and construct inferential procedures. The bootstrap is a general, automatic and powerful method that computes measures of accuracy for estimators, such as the bias, variance and confidence intervals. However, traditional bootstrap algorithms become computationally infeasible for massive datasets even with modern cloud storage and computing architectures. Newly proposed methods, such as the bag of little bootstraps (Kleiner et al., 2014) and the subsampled double bootstrap (Sengupta et al., 2016), address these issues but still have some drawbacks when applied to a range of estimators in statistics. We propose several general bootstrap procedures to efficiently quantify the accuracy of estimators for massive datasets in the framework of supervised learning, including linear regression models, generalized linear models and mixed-effects models. These procedures have many appealing features. First, in linear models or generalized linear models, by incorporating leverage scores into the bootstrap, the empirical distributions obtained by bootstrapping can stabilize faster and reduce the computational burden, especially when the design matrix has very non-uniform leverage scores. Second, incorporating stratification produces a bootstrap that is well-suited for the case in which the relationship between the response and predictors is nonlinear and makes the bootstrap procedure more robust. Third, the proposed procedure provides general and computationally feasible ways to eliminate model selection discontinuities and validly assess the precision of estimators after model selection for massive datasets. In all, the proposed methods will be scalable, easily implemented on modern parallel and distributed computing platforms and extremely useful for solving practical problems with the massive datasets. 數據收集方面的技術進步正使得海量數據變得越來越普遍。這些海量數據給統計學家帶來了機遇和新的挑戰。基於自助法的思想，我們主要研究評估估計量精確度等統計推斷過程。自助法是一種通用的，自動的，強大的主要用來計算估計量精度的方法，如評價估計量的偏差，方差和置信區間。然而，傳統的自助法即使在現代雲存儲和計算體系結構下，也因為過於繁重的計算量，無法有效的用來評估基於海量數據的估計量的精度。 一些新提出的方法，例如bag of little bootstraps（Kleiner et al.，2014）和subsampled double bootstrap（Sengupta等人，2016），可以在一定程度上解決一些問題，但是，當我們把這些方法用到一些估計量的時候， 仍然有一些不足之處。 在有監督學習的框架下，我們提出了幾種一般的自助法過程，這些方法可以有效地量化海量數據的估計量，包括線性回歸模型、廣義線性模型和混合效應模型。這些方法有許多吸引人的特點。首先，在線性模型或廣義線性模型中，通過將槓桿得分引入自助法，可以使得估計量的經驗分布更快地穩定並減少計算負擔，特別是當設計矩陣具有非常不均勻的槓桿得分時。第二，通過結合分層技術，當響應變量和自變量之間有非線性關係時，自助法過程可以更加的穩健。第三， 我們擬提出一個通用的，且計算可行的方法可以減少模型選擇的不連續性，有效的得到模型選擇之後估計量的精度。總之，我們所提出的方法具有可擴展性，且易於在現代分布式計算平台上實現，可以有效的解決海量數據的統計建模問題。

15303917.label: Realisation of objectives
15303917.value: (i) To prepare high-quality and thickness-controllable a-BP thin films. Amorphous black phosphorus (a-BP) thin films were prepared by pulsed laser deposition (PLD). A BP crystal was used as a target with a substrate temperature of 150 C. The thickness of a-BP thin films can be tuned from 2 to 10 nm. We demonstrated the growth of highly crystalline ultrathin BP on the centimetre scale by adjusting the PLD conditions and using the mica substrates. The work has been published in Nature Materials. We have also successfully grown BP crystals using the chemical vapor transport method. The BP crystals can serve as a precursor in the PLD for large-area ultrathin BP films. Furthermore, we could also grow violet phosphorus (VP), another allotrope of phosphorus, by the chemical vapor transport method. We have also investigated the optical properties of VP. The synthesis of BP crystals has led to the fabrication of BP quantum dots. In turn, the BP quantum dots was found to be an effective catalyst for Li-S batteries. The work has been published in Nature Communications. (ii) To fabricate and characterize top-gate and dual-gate a-BP field effect transistors We have developed various approaches to fabricate stable field-effect transistors (FETs) with a capping layer. The bottom gate a-BP FETs using Si as substrate was prepared with hole mobility ranging from 10 to 100 cm2/Vs. Furthermore, we fabricated large-scale top-gated field-effect transistor arrays on crystalline BP films. FET arrays were prepared to verify the electrical performance of the as-grown BP. Benefiting from the considerable crystalline size of the as-grown BP, we fabricated FETs using hard-mask-based electron-beam deposition technology, allowing easy construction of electric devices while avoiding possible contamination or oxidation. The 10-nm-Pd/40-nm-Au multilayers were used as electrodes. Among all the BP samples, the optimal field-effect electrical transport properties were obtained at a thickness of ~5 nm, and the carrier mobility reached up to 213 and 617 cm2 V-1 s-1 at 295 and 250 K, respectively. Such electrical performances are comparable to those of exfoliated or CVD-grown BP-based FETs of similar thickness. (iii) To explore the optoelectronic properties of a-BP/MoS2 heterostructure. Heterostructures of a-BP/WS2 were prepared. Samples composed of 2 nm a-BP and a monolayer WS2 obtained by mechanical exfoliation were fabricated by dry transfer. Photoluminescence measurements revealed that photocarriers excited in WS2 of the heterostructure transfer to a-BP, in the form of either energy or charge transfer, on a time scale shorter than the exciton lifetime in WS2. (iv) To study the charge transfer dynamics in a-BP/MoS2 heterostructure. Transient absorption measurements further indicate that holes can efficiently transfer from WS2 to a-BP. However, interlayer electron transfer in either direction was found to be absent. The lack of electron transfer from amorphous black phosphorus to WS2 is attributed to the localized electronic states in the amorphous semiconductor. Furthermore, we show that a hexagonal BN bilayer can effectively change the hole transfer process. The results establish a-BP as a building block for van der Waals heterostructures, provide new information for understanding interlayer charge transfer, and allow electrical connections to amorphous materials by van der Waals interfaces. As WS2 exhibits stronger photoluminescence than MoS2, the charge dynamic is also stronger. A paper has been published on the topic in collaboration with Professor Zhao from the University of Kansas.

15303917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15303917.value: The PLD technique is promising for preparing large-scale two-dimensional materials, including amorphous and highly crystalline BP films. Our results pave the way for further developing BP-based wafer-scale devices with potential applications in the information industry. The CVT method can also prepare a wide range of layered materials for further exploration.

15303917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15303917.value: BP has attracted tremendous attention all over the world due to its electronic, optical, and catalytic properties. However, the controllable large-scale growth of few-layer BP films has been a long-standing major problem, and it hinders the further development and practical applications of BP. This project has demonstrated that centimeter-scale BP can be fabricated using pulsed laser deposition (PLD). The device quality of the PLD-grown BP films is comparable with the mechanically exfoliated BP. During the course of the project, amorphous-BP and violet phosphorus were also prepared and investigated. The works open up the possibility of developing phosphorus-based electronic and optoelectronic devices, especially scalable integrated device arrays and information systems.

15304117.label: Realisation of objectives
15304117.value: In this project, the conformations and dynamics of a class B metallo-β-lactamase NDM-1 upon binding three inhibitors, i.e., L-captorial, Ebselen and aspergillomarasmine A, with different mechanisms of action, have been investigated by mass spectrometry, as proposed. Although the social incidents and pandemic in Hong Kong during the project period caused some delays in some of the experiments, the proposed objectives of this project have been fully achieved, and even additional studies on the inhibition of NDM-1 by Ebselen and L-captopril through molecular modelling and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation have been performed for this project. 1. Study of NDM-1 β-lactamase and its complexes with inhibitors by ESI-MS NDM-1 was expressed, purified, and characterized by electrospray ionization mass spectrometry (ESI-MS). The denaturing ESI-MS results confirmed the successful production of NDM-1. A minor species with an extra mass of 178 Da, corresponding to α-N-6-phosphogluconoylation of N-terminal His-tag of NDM-1, was also found, which is normally presumed to have little impact on the study under the experimental conditions. Native ESI-MS results showed that two molar equivalents of zinc were bound to NDM-1 which existed as a monomer in the ammonium acetate solutions. The complexes with L-captopril studied by both denaturing and native ESI-MS suggested a stoichiometry of one molar equivalent non-covalent binding between NDM-1 and L-captopril, and both zinc ions were retained on NDM-1 upon the binding. In contrast, it was found that Ebselen covalently bound NDM-1 with one zinc stripped from the active sites while AMA sequestered the two zinc ions from the active sites. Therefore, ESI-MS study revealed that NDM-1 was inhibited by L-captopril, Ebselen and AMA via three different mechanisms of action, i.e., acting simultaneously on zinc ions and key amino acids, acting on cysteine only, and acting on zinc ions only, respectively. 2. Study of NDM-1 β-lactamase and its complex with L-captopril by HDX-MS The conformational dynamics of NDM-1 was investigated in its free and bound state with L-captopril by hydrogen/deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS). The overall conformation of NDM-1 was more protected from HDX upon the binding, indicating a more compact and rigid structure after non-covalently binding to L-captopril. Major conformational changes occurred in the active-site loops that are ligated to zinc ions. Other regions that are proximal to the active pocket, especially for the loop region connecting β10 and α3 (known as L10) and its C-terminal helix α4, were more protected from HDX. Interestingly, a loop region connecting β6 and β7 also became more compact in the bound state with L-captopril while this change was not observed in the crystal structures (PDB IDs: 3spu and 4exs). 3. Study of NDM-1 β-lactamase and its complex with Ebselen by HDX-MS The conformational dynamics of NDM-1 was investigated in its free and bound state with Ebselen by HDX-MS. The structural perturbation of NDM-1 upon Ebselen incubation was opposite for the L3 and L10 regions versus other regions along the sequence. L3 and L10 displayed significant protection while the loop connecting α3 and β11 was deprotected. In contrast to the results for L-captopril inhibition, the active-site loops were all deprotected after AMA treatment. Besides, the loop connecting β6 and β7 and the C-terminal helix α4 were both deprotected. These results indicated a looser conformation of NDM-1 in the inhibited state. Such changes are consistent with the modification of Cys208 and also the substitution of an active zinc ion that ligates to active-site amino acids, i.e., Asp124, Cys208 and His250. 4. Study of NDM-1 β-lactamase and its complex with AMA by HDX-MS The conformational dynamics of NDM-1 was investigated before and after AMA incubation by HDX-MS. Mild conformational changes were observed when one zinc ion was stripped from the active pocket. The most significant change was found at the loop 203-209 containing the ligating residue Cys208. Our results provided strong evidence that only the zinc ion ligated with Cys208 was sequestered by AMA. This zinc ion was reported to have a lower binding affinity than the other one, and thus it was more easily dissociated from the active sites. 5. Study of NDM-1 β-lactamase with molecular modelling and MD simulation The active sites containing zinc ions were constructed via MCPB.py, i.e., a python-based metal center parameter builder. The force field was built for the simulation of metallo-protein employing a bonded model approach. MD simulations were performed with the prepared force field to obtain the dynamics of NDM-1 in its native state (PDB ID: 3spu) and inhibitor-bound states. The starting structure of the complex of L-captopril and NDM-1 was adopted from PDB (PDB ID: 4exs). However, no crystal structure of the complex of Ebselen and NDM-1 was available, and thus it was prepared by molecular docking. Two top-ranking conformations were found in the covalent docking with AutoDock. Both structures were subjected to MD simulation to further optimize the orientations and to correlate with the HDX results. One promising structure was selected and represented as the first optimized model for the complex of Ebselen and NDM-1. In summary, NDM-1 β-lactamase and its interactions with the three inhibitors were investigated with mass spectrometry and computation modelling. Conformational aspects for the inhibition of NDM-1 via different mechanisms of action were concluded. For the first time the apparent differences in the active sites and loop regions were revealed for these inhibitors. Detailed molecular model helped further illustration on the conformational dynamics of NDM-1 upon the inhibition.

15304117.label: Major findings and research outcome
15304117.value: 1. An overall more compact conformation for NDM-1 inhibited with L-captopril Our HDX-MS study revealed significantly reduced dynamics of the loop regions that coordinated to zinc ions after L-captopril occupies the active pocket. This conformational change not only blocked the substrate recognition but also paralyzed the two zinc ions. Besides, two binding interactions, i.e., hydrophobically interacting with Loop3 and hydrogen bonding to N220 in Loop10, were reflected by more protected HDX in these loop regions. The restricted plasticity of these two loops could suppress the turn-over during the catalysis. In addition, the loop L8 connecting β6 and β7 displayed a substantial change in HDX, revealing an allosteric change overlooked in other studies. This loop also presented highest deuterium uptake throughout the sequence, indicating its potential role in modulation of the structure and activity. Our finding was strongly coupled with the evolution of NDM-1 where 50% of the clinical variants have a common point mutation M154L on this loop. 2. An overall more flexible conformation for NDM-1 inhibited by Ebselen or AMA HDX-MS revealed significant deprotection effects on the loops containing C208 and D124. Interestingly, the loop L8 displayed a more flexible conformation on the contrary to that of L-captopril inhibition. Deprotection of the loop region connecting α3 and β11 was found and predominantly contributed by R234, reflecting a less ordered helical structure that could impact the dynamics of the C-terminus. HDX-MS presented an overall deprotected profile for intact NDM-1 upon inhibition by Ebselen. An obvious deprotection effect in the loop connecting α3 and β11 and C-terminal α4 indicated a more flexible C-terminus of NDM-1 upon the inhibition. Interestingly, Loop10 displayed a more compact conformation highly similar to that in the L-captopril bound state, presumably due to the hydrophobic interaction with the phenyl group of Ebselen modified C208, as reflected by the docking results. 3. Computational modelling provided information supporting to HDX-MS Two top ranked models displayed opposite orientations of the phenyl group in the active pocket. Our HDX-MS results corelated well with the orientation in which the phenyl group pointed towards the hydrophobic residues in Loop10 region, reflecting by a protected conformation. In summary, our study is the first one to provide comprehensive insights into the conformations and dynamics of NDM-1 under inhibited states with three representative inhibitors. These findings provided deep insights into the inhibition of NDM-1 β-lactamase and crucial evidence for the design of novel inhibitors.

15304117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15304117.value: This study focused on the impact of different inhibitors on a clinically prevalent metallo-β-lactamase NDM-1. An intriguing finding was the potential role of loop8 connecting β6 and β7 in the modulation of the activity of NDM-1. Other threatening NDM variants with a very common substitution (M154L) on loop8, e.g., NDM-4, 5, 7, 8, 12, 13, 15 and 17, can be studied along with L-captopril which caused substantial conformational change in this loop. Inhibitory effects of L-captopril towards NDM variants can be characterized by mass spectrometry and thus infer the evolution of the inhibitor resistance. On the other hand, these variants have shown different zinc affinities and thus confer various resistance towards inhibitors (e.g., AMA and its derivatives) based on zinc sequestering. It would be interesting to reveal the selectivity of these inhibitors in suppression of metallo-β-lactamases. Furthermore, when paired with different types of β-lactam antibiotics, AMA displayed antibiotic dependent efficacy towards metallo-β-lactamases. Further understanding on such phenomenon will provide basic guideline for rational design of β-lactam/inhibitor combination. This study also highlighted the powerful role of mass spectrometry in understanding the mechanism of action of the inhibitors and optimizing the design of the inhibitors.

15304117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15304117.value: NDM-type metallo-β-lactamases have attracted great attentions due to their resistance towards almost all the β-lactam antibiotics while effective inhibitors have not been available yet. Understanding the mechanisms of action of potential inhibitors is urgently desired for the rational inhibitor design. In this study, three representative inhibitors undergoing different mechanisms of action were investigated by mass spectrometry and computational modelling. Our HDX-MS results revealed an overall more compact conformation upon inhibition by L-captopril while a more flexible conformation upon inhibition by AMA or Ebselen. Specifically, the active-site loops were protected after occupation of L-captopril in the active pocket while were deprotected after zinc displacement by Ebselen or AMA. Unexpectedly, the loop connecting β6 and β7 displayed a pronounced conformational change upon the inhibitions. A common substitution M154L on this loop has been discovered for half of the natural variants of NDM-1, indicating a prevalent pathway in evolution. Our finding for the first time reveals the structural role of this loop in the modulation of the activity of NDM-1. These findings proved the powerful role of mass spectrometry in understanding of the mechanism of inhibition for NDM-1 and providing novel insights in allosteric changes that are overlooked by other techniques.

15304417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15304417.value: Isothermal nucleic acid amplification techniques have received increasing attention in central and clinical laboratories as well as decentralized settings for accurate and ultrasensitive detection of pathogens such as viruses and bacteria. These isothermal techniques have the advantages of simple temperature control and short reaction time compared with the current gold standard of polymerase chain reaction (thermocycling-based amplification of specific target sequence). The ability to monitor the progress of the amplification reaction in real-time, typically by incorporating organic fluorophores into the reaction mixture, eliminates additional detection time and enables quantification over a wide dynamic range. Fluorescent semiconductor nanocrystals (quantum dots) have proven to be promising substitutes for organic fluorophores by virtue of their superior brightness and photostability. Efforts have been made to couple quantum dot fluorescent detection probe with isothermal amplification, however, almost all platforms involved modifying quantum dots with target-specific oligonucleotide sequences (complementary to target/amplified sequences) via special attachment chemistries. Apart from laborious, time-consuming, and costly preparation, different oligonucleotide-modified quantum dot probes are needed for different targets. This proposed project aims to develop a first-of-its-kind real-time isothermal amplification assay platform based on a universal quantum dot probe (i.e., without the attachment of oligonucleotide). Specifically, this is based on a previously unreported phenomenon that cysteamine-modified quantum dots are dispersed in a negative loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) sample (without target DNA sequence) but precipitated in a positive LAMP sample (with target DNA sequence). We will investigate the effects of the LAMP reaction components (both reactants and products) on the dispersion/precipitation of the cysteamine-modified quantum dots and thus reveal the underlying mechanism. We will explore the generic applicability of this mechanism to other isothermal amplification reactions, other types of nanomaterials with cysteamine modification, as well as other modifications (amine-containing). We will apply the assay scheme for avian influenza virus detection (field samples). We will demonstrate real-time assay by using a simple and hand-held home-made device. The successful development of a real-time isothermal amplification platform based on a universal quantum dot probe will bring huge benefits to food safety control, environment surveillance, and medical diagnostics, especially in resource-limited laboratories and on-site/point-of-care settings. This project will also provide important insights into the interactions between different surface-modified nanomaterials and isothermal amplification reaction components, which can guide the design of future nanomaterials for in vitro and in vivo applications. 核酸等溫擴增技術近年來受到越來越多的關注，特別是在中心實驗室、臨床實驗室和分散實驗室裡被用於對病毒和細菌等病原體的精確和超敏感檢測。與目前的標準聚合酶鏈式反應（對特定靶序列的熱迴圈擴增）技術相比，這些等溫技術具有簡單溫度控制、短反應時間等優點。通常通過將有機螢光物質摻入反應混合物中以實現在較寬動態範圍內對核酸擴增反應進程的即時定量監測，這就大大省去了額外的檢測時間。螢光半導體納米晶體（量子點）憑藉其優越的亮度和光穩定性已被證明是有機螢光物質的有前途的替代品。目前雖然已經有研究將量子點螢光檢測探針與核酸等溫擴增技術相結合，但是幾乎所有的設計都涉及通過特殊的化學附著方法將目標特異性寡核苷酸序列（與靶/擴增序列互補）修飾到量子點表面。這種設計除了費力、耗時和需要昂貴的製備過程等缺點之外，不同的靶標還需要不同的寡核苷酸修飾的量子點探針。該專案旨在開發首個基於通用量子點探針（即不附加寡核苷酸）的即時核酸等溫擴增監測平臺。具體來說，我們發現半胱胺修飾的量子點能夠分散在陰性環介導等溫擴增（LAMP）樣品（無目標DNA序列）中，但是卻在陽性LAMP樣品（具有靶DNA序列）中形成沉澱，並且這一發現尚未被報導過。我們將進一步研究LAMP反應組分（反應物和產物）對半胱胺修飾的量子點的分散/沉澱的影響，從而揭示其潛在的反應機理，並且探討這種機理對其它等溫擴增反應、其它類型的具有半胱胺修飾的納米材料以及其它修飾（含胺）的一般適用性，將這種監測方法具體應用於對禽流感病毒的檢測（現場樣本），並且通過使用簡單的掌上型自製設備來演示即時監測。這種基於通用量子點探針的即時核酸等溫擴增平臺的成功研發將為食品安全控制、環境監測和醫療診斷帶來巨大的效益，特別是對資源有限的實驗室和現場而言。另外，該項目還將為不同的表面改性納米材料和等溫擴增反應組分之間的相互作用提供新的重要發現，這些將有利於指導未來納米材料在體外和體內應用的設計。

Then we will consider the convergence of the mini-batching scheme enhanced by Polyak-Ruppert averaging.

15304917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15304917.value: In recent years, more and more data mining problems emerging from both scientific research and industrial applications concern data sets with big size. To effectively retrieve pattern from big data, distributed learning scheme and online algorithms are widely applied and extensively studied. We propose to study a new mini-batching scheme for promoting the convergence of online algorithms. In the proposed scheme, the batch size provides a flexible control on the trade-off between computational complexity and convergence speed for different application scenarios. Using the error decomposition method we developed recently, we will study the convergence of mini-batching online algorithms, both in expectation and with confidence. We will study the sparse enhancing regularization for mini-batching, with the target of relaxing the space restriction of kernel-based online algorithms. The other scheme we propose to study is the Polyak-Ruppert averaging. Using the analysis we developed recently, we propose to study the strong and weak convergence of the averaging scheme for the randomized Kaczmarz algorithm in high dimensional spaces, and the application of averaging to promoting the convergence of mini-batching. 近年來，不論從科學研究還是工業應用的實踐中，都湧現出不少牽涉大規模數據的數據挖掘問題。為了有效地從大數據中提取模式，分布式學習算法和在線學習算法被廣泛使用和深入研究。為提高在線算法的收斂速度，我們計劃研究一類新的小批次迭代框架。在此框架下，對於不同的應用問題，小批次的大小提供了一種協調計算復雜度和收斂速度的良好工具。利用我們最近發展出的誤差分解方法，我們計劃研究小批次框架的期望意義下和高置信度意義下的收斂性。為了緩解基於核方法的在線學習算法對存儲空間的要求，我們計劃研究可以增強小批次框架稀疏性的正則化方法。我們計劃研究Polyak-Ruppert平均算法。使用我們最近發展出來的分析方法，我們計劃研究在高維空間中平均技術應用於隨機Kaczmarz算法的強收斂及弱收斂速度，以及平均技術在提高小批次算法收斂速度上的作用

15304917.label: Realisation of objectives
15304917.value: The proposed project objectives have been successfully achieved. In the work [1], we proposed and analyzed an algorithm LESS (Learning with Empirical feature-based Summary statistics from Semi-supervised data). By adopting unlabeled data, empirical features, and summary statistics, LESS provides a protocol to communicate data without directly releasing private and sensitive information. The design of LESS assumes the access to sufficient unlabeled data that have no privacy issues (for example, those generated by sampling the estimated density function, or those already gone to the public domain). Empirical features are computed with these unlabeled data, and are used to encode training data as summary statistics. Empirical features are passed to the holders of training data, where summary statistics are computed and passed to the computing center. Releasing summary statistics instead of raw data helps to protect private information. In the computing center, the predicted function is computed as a linear combination of empirical features, and is shipped out for prediction purpose. The selection of empirical features serves as a trade-off between prediction precision and the protection of privacy. We derived the convergence rate, which matches the minimax optimal learning rate for all the kernel-based learning algorithms. The analysis removes the requirement of minimum sub-sample size of each single data source. While this requirement is often assumed in many recent papers on distributed learning, it restricts the application of algorithms to the privacy-sensitive scenarios. In the scenarios of restricted computing resources (one of the most important motivation of online learning), LESS is a one-pass online learning algorithm which accumulates summary statistics with low computational complexity. More importantly, LESS achieves a big breakthrough of the traditional distributed or mini-batch online algorithm, that is, while maintaining the minimax optimal convergence rate, LESS does not restrict batch size. So, it is absolutely OK for some of the mini batches to be very large, while some others very small, and all the batches are made full use of (in the sense of achieving the optimal convergence rate). The online mini-batch iteration is symmetric, that is, the output function does not depend on the order the training sample batches are processed. With the help of summary statistics, the requirement of storage in the typical kernel-based online learning algorithms is relaxed. In the work [2], we studied the pairwise learning problem with pointwise kernel. The application scenarios include score-based ranking and non-linear metric learning. The relations between the reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces generated by pointwise kernel and pairwise kernel are studied. The convergence rate of the obtained pairwise learning algorithm is derived. The minimax optimal learning rate is derived. The gap between our upper bound and minimax optimal lower bound is only the logarithm of sample size. Although [2] does not directly adopt online setting, the analysis of hypothesis space could be trivially applied to improve the analysis of online pairwise learning problems well studied in the literature. In [3], we studied online algorithms for functional data learning problems. Reproducing kernel Hilbert space is adopted as the hypothesis space. We derived convergence rates for the expected excess prediction risk under both online and finite-horizon settings of step-sizes respectively. It is well understood that nontrivial uniform convergence rates for the estimation task depend on the regularity of the slope function. Surprisingly, the convergence rates we derived for the prediction task can assume no regularity from slope. Our analysis revealed the intrinsic difference between the estimation task and the prediction task in functional data learning. The algorithm studied [3] is a special form of randomized Kaczmarz algorithm applied to functional data learning in Hilbert spaces. Convergence rates were derived that are comparable to batch learning schemes studied in the literature. In [4], we studied multiple waves of Canadian Population Census data (1981–2016). We first used multiple imputation to normalize the data into pseudo five-year age intervals. Then, we adopt hierarchical age-period-cohort (HAPC) logistic regression models to analyze home-ownership in Canada. Using best linear unbiased predictors (BLUPs), HAPC models treat age as an individual-level fixed effect, while treating period and cohort effects as population-level, cross-classified random effects. The hierarchical modeling not only circumvents the collinearity problem of temporal effects but also allows social scientists to consider individual-level variations along with population-level clusters such as survey periods and birth cohorts. To identify local anomalies in home-ownership trends, we used structural change analysis proposed by Bai and Perron (1998) to detect potential structural breaks in time series. Because of the large size of data, this research is an ideal application of online algorithms.

15304917.label: Major findings and research outcome
15304917.value: In [1], we proposed a summary statistic-based learning algorithm LESS (Learning with Empirical feature-based Summary statistics from Semi-supervised data). The algorithm first generates a set of empirical features (in terms of kernel functions) from unlabeled data. The features are then circulated to different sources of data, where summary statistics are computed. The values of the statistics, instead of the original data which contain private information, are collected for computing predicted function. LESS is designed to make use of unlabeled data and do distributed or mini-batch online learning. LESS reduces the exposure of private information, achieves minimax optimal convergence rate, and is designed perfectly suitable to handle batches with very different sizes. LESS [1] suggests that the weights of the Polyak-Ruppert averaging should be designed to cope with the iteration. The best possible weight design should entitle each mini batch a weight proportional to its size. In [2], we studied the pairwise learning problem by constructing the pairwise reproducing kernel through pointwise kernel. We characterize the resulted pairwise function hypothesis space in terms of the pointwise kernel employed. The convergence rate of the obtained pairwise learning algorithm is derived. The minimax optimal learning rate is derived. The gap between our upper bound and minimax optimal lower bound is only the logarithm of sample size. In [3], we studied reproducing kernel-based online learning algorithms for functional data, and derived convergence rates for the expected excess prediction risk under both online and ﬁnite-horizon settings of step-sizes respectively. The results in this paper show that with a properly selected reproducing kernel, it is possible to learn the predictor (in a specific convergence rate) without assuming any regularity of the slope function. We therefore verified that the regularity requirement on the slope function is an intrinsic difference between the prediction problem and the estimation problem in functional data learning. In [4], we studied multiple waves of Canadian Population Census data (1981–2016) for identifying local anomalies in home-ownership trends. To make best use of data, the multiple imputation technique was adopted to normalize the data into pseudo five-year age intervals. Hierarchical age-period-cohort (HAPC) logistic regression models, combined with structural change analysis are adopted. This is an application research and several demographic observations are obtained from the analysis of real data.

15304917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15304917.value: The convergence analysis of randomized Kaczmarz algorithm for functional linear regression problems we studied in [3] could be further extended to capacity-dependent convergence analysis. Better convergence rates are also expected by integrating the Polyak-Ruppert averaging technique. The summary statistic-based learning algorithm LESS we developed in [1] could be further applied to functional data learning, where an artificial random noise could be added to the summary statistics for better privacy protection. We propose to continue the research for more outcomes.

15304917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15304917.value: This project studies several reproducing kernel-based machine learning algorithms. First, we designed a new learning algorithm based on summary statistics. This algorithm aims to process data that contain private information and are held in batches of different sizes by different sources. Our algorithm does not collect data directly, but just collect summary statistics to reduce the exposure of private information. Our mathematical analysis shows that our designed algorithm achieves the best possible performance in terms of convergence speed. Second, we studied pointwise kernel-based pairwise learning algorithms, of which the applications cover ranking, metric learning, and classification. By characterizing the pairwise reproducing kernel in terms of pointwise kernel, near optimal convergence rates are derived. Third, we study kernel-based online algorithm for functional data learning, which is a special case of randomized Kaczmarz algorithms. We showed that it is possible to learn the predictor without assuming any regularity of the slope function. We therefore verified that the regularity requirement on the slope function is an intrinsic difference between the prediction problem and the estimation problem in functional data learning. We also extended the research to the analysis of real data and the application of structural change analysis for demographic research.

15305117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15305117.value: One of the great scientific challenges in the twenty-first century is undoubtedly energy storage and conversion. There is an increasing need for considering environmental concerns and energy security as well as important breakthroughs in battery or supercapacitor science and technology to meet the needs of modern society. Supercapacitors (SCs), also called electrochemical capacitors, which bridge the gap between conventional dielectric capacitors and batteries in terms of both energy and power densities, are currently attracting intensive attention in the scientific community because they can provide energy density higher by orders of magnitude than dielectric capacitors, and greater power density and longer cycling ability than batteries. Accordingly, SCs have had an important role in complementing or replacing batteries in electrical energy storage and harvesting applications, when high power delivery or uptake is needed. SCs store energy using either ion adsorption (as in electrochemical double layer capacitors, EDLC) or fast surface redox reactions (as in pseudocapacitors). Carbon materials with high surface area generally display EDLC behavior, whereas transition metal oxides or conducting organic polymers exhibit typical pseudocapacitive behavior. In general, the specific capacitances of pseudocapacitors are much higher than those of carbon materials based on the EDLC mechanism. Conducting conjugated organic polymers are one important type of electrode materials for pseudocapacitors due to their large capacitance, good electronic conductivity, low cost, ease of synthesis and flexibility. While an increasing effort has also gone into developing SCs based on porous metal-organic frameworks recently, the use of metal-containing conductive polymers as electrode materials in SC applications is still rarely explored, despite the advantages such as the wide structural diversity, rich redox chemistry and intermolecular/supramolecular interactions made possible by the metallic elements in these metallopolymers. In this proposal, we initiate a new project of developing a new family of electrically conducting and electroactive metal-containing polymers of one and two dimensions (1D and 2D) for high-performance SC applications. In the presence of redox-active transition metal chromophores, these metallo-organic systems should have several redox states with good control of their electrical conductivity, thereby improving the pseudocapacitance. This would facilitate charge/discharge processes and enhance the energy densities of the SC devices. The multiple electrochemical events of these metallated polymers can be fine-tuned through chemical control of the redox-active metallic segments and topologies. The present work will provide a new avenue to a new class of advanced supercapacitor electrode materials for high-power energy storage. 能源存儲、轉化是二十一世紀面臨的巨大科學挑戰之一。隨著環境和能源安全問題日益凸顯，人們對能源存儲轉化的要求越來越高。近年來，電池或超級電容器快速發展，取得了一系列重大突破，逐漸成為能源領域研究的焦點。超級電容器又稱為電化學電容器，有效融合了傳統電解質電容器和電池，不僅可以提供比電容器更高的能量密度，還表現出比電池更高的功率及更好循環使用性能。超級電容器在電能存儲中可以有效的填補電池的缺陷，在輸送或攝取高功率領域發揮了重要的作用。超級電容器中常見的電化學雙層電容器和贗電容器，分別通過離子吸附和表面快速氧化還原進行能量存儲。具有高表面積的碳材料通常是基於電化學雙層電容器的機理，而過度金屬氧化物或導電聚合物表現出贗電容特性。贗電容器的比電容通常遠遠高於基於碳材料的電化學雙層電容器。導電性共軛有機聚合物易於合成和加工，是一種重要類型的贗電容器電極材料，其電容量大、電導率高、成本低。基於多孔性金屬有機骨架的超級電容器材料已經被廣泛的研究，但是導電金屬聚合物在這一領域仍比較罕見。金屬聚合物結構多樣，具有優異的氧化還原性能，而且金屬中心易於形成分子間相互作用或超分子作用。基於此，我們擬開發一系列具有導電性和電化學活性的一維、二維金屬聚合物，並將其用於制備高性能超級電容器。金屬有機體系中引入具有氧化還原活性的過渡金屬基團後，通常具有幾種氧化還原狀態，而且可以很好的控制其導電性，從而提高贗電容器的性能。這將有助於充電/放電過程並增強SC器件的能量密度。這類金屬聚合物的多重電化學特性可以通過控制氧化還原活性的金屬片段和拓撲結構進行精細調控。這項工作將為開發高功率儲能的新型超級電容器電極材料提供一條新的途徑。

15305117.label: Major findings and research outcome
15305117.value: A new series of metallopolymers and related metal complexes were synthesized (papers 1-13) as supercapacitor electrode materials. First, we demonstrate the preparation of pseudocapacitive electrodes by inkjet printing cobalt-bis(terpyridyl) complexes as pseudocapacitive additives on laser induced graphene films. The substrate temperature during inkjet printing can effectively tune the morphology of the pseudocapacitive additives. Under optimum conditions, the capacitance of the pseudocapacitive electrodes was enhanced by 75 times over pristine graphene films. This approach can also be employed for the deposition of other functional materials via inkjet printing (paper 1). A general one-step solid-state pyrolysis method was developed to synthesize multihierarchical porous carbon using bio-wastes as precursors and potassium ferrate as the pore-forming agent. This method is superior to the traditional two-step or multi-step method due to its simple procedure, low cost, little pollution and time-saving features. The multiple pore-forming effect derived from potassium ferrate is responsible for this multi-hierarchical porous structure. The resulting porous carbon was used to fabricate symmetrical supercapacitors, exhibiting specific capacitances of 291.2 F g-1 at 1 A g-1 and 240.1 F g-1 at 10 A g-1, and exceptional cyclic stability with 93.2% capacitance retention over 100,000 cycles (paper 11). New free-standing and binder-free ferrocene-containing polymer-coated carbonaceous electrodes were also fabricated which exhibited morphologies with cauliflower-like units consisting of open-top spheres at the micrometer scale. The highest areal specific capacitance of 2.97 F cm-2 for the electrodes surpasses those for almost all the flexible and binder-free supercapacitor electrodes reported. Two all-solid-state symmetric supercapacitor devices were assembled, and the flexible one exhibited ultrahigh capacitance (1.35 F cm-2), extraordinary cycling performance (88% retention after 15,000 cycles) and excellent mechanical stability. Both maximum energy densities (over 0.37 mW h cm-2) and maximum power densities (22.4 mW cm-2) of the devices are superior to those of all flexible all-solid-state symmetric devices reported and these values also stand out among the non-flexible ones (paper 13). We were invited to write a review and a book on the relevant topic (outputs 12, 14). Numerous bottom-up 2D metal-complex nanosheets were prepared by coordination of the multifunctional ligands and metal ions. Interface-assisted synthesis provides a facile method to generate few-layer/multi-layer nanosheets. These materials showed sheet morphology and uniform composition. They present large size domains and good mechanical strength (papers 5-8, 10). Using different electroactive ligands and metal ions, these 2D polymers are expected to show rich electroactivity and stable redox process for future supercapacitor fabrication.

15305117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15305117.value: The following areas of research work can be further developed in the future: (1) Extension of the work to other metal and ligand chromophores as well as those redox-active 2D metallopolymers aforementioned which can be anticipated to show improved supercapacitive properties. (2) Enhancement of the performance of the supercapacitor devices by structural and device engineering.

15305117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15305117.value: Metal-organic compounds, including molecular complexes and coordination polymers, have attracted much attention as electrode materials in supercapacitors owing to their large surface area, high porosity, tailorable pore size, controllable structure, good electrochemical reversibility, and abundant active sites. A series of conductive metal-containing polymers (both 1D and 2D) with redox-active sites have been prepared which represent a new class of electrode materials for supercapacitors. The spectroscopic, photophysical, thermal, structural and redox properties of these new metallopolymers were investigated in detail and the effect of metallation was also studied. Furthermore, selected metallopolymers were shown to exhibit attractive supercapacitive effect useful for the energy storage application. The as-prepared electrodes combine the advantages of pseudocapacitor electrode materials from metal–organic compounds and conductive polymers as well as electrical double-layer capacitor electrode materials from carbon fibers without involving composite formation. The present work fills in a relatively under-explored area of supercapacitor electrodes derived from conducting metallopolymers and would thus provide a new impetus to the creation of some technologically useful materials and systems for storing energy.

15305217.label: Realisation of objectives
15305217.value: Objective 1: Expression, purification, and characterization of FtsQ, FtsB and FtsL. His-tagged periplasmic and full-length Fts-proteins were (co-)expressed and (co-)purified according to the methods reported by the previous literature from Marjolein Glas and Adrien Boes. In brief, free and the corresponding Fts-protein complexes were (co-)expressed in E. coli BL21 (DE3) or C43 (DE3) harboring the transformed plasmid(s). The co-purifications were achieved using the His-tagged FtsB or FtsBp as bait. Bacteria were first grown in LB medium with ampicillin at 37 C for 12 h. The culture was then diluted into 2xTY medium (with ampicillin) in a 1:50 volume ratio and then incubated at 37 C. Once the OD600 reached 0.8, the expression was induced by a final concentration of 1 mM β-D-1 thiogalactopyranoside (IPTG) at 16 C for 14 h. Cells were collected by centrifugation followed by resuspension with protease inhibitor cocktail (cOmplete™, Sigma Aldrich) in lysis buffer and lysed by the cell disruptor (TS2, Constant system LTD). Different lysis buffers were used for the periplasmic protein FtsQp/Bp/Lp (50 mM sodium phosphate pH 8.0, 300 mM NaCl, 10 mM imidazole, 10 mM dithiothreitol (DTT), and 1 mM phenylmethylsulphonyl fluoride (PMSF)) and the full-length FtsQ/B/L proteins (50 mM Tris-HCL pH 7.5, 50 mM NaCl). The debris was then removed by centrifugation (2 hours, 10864 x g, 4 C). The FtsQp/Bp/Lp proteins in the acquired supernatant were directly purified in the next step. For the membrane-bound FtsQ/B/L proteins, supernatants were recovered and subjected to an additional ultra-centrifugation step (1 hour, 276,900 x g, 4 C). The membrane proteins were then collected in pellets and extracted by agitation in solubilizing buffer (50 mM HEPES, pH 7.5, 500 mM NaCl, 10%(v/v) glycerol, 30 mM n-dodecyl-β-D-maltopyranoside (DDM)) for further purification. Target proteins from both constructs were purified by Ni-NTA agarose resins (Qiagen). Individual proteins and protein complexes were (co-)purified by imidazole in a stepwise concentration: of 20 mM, 140 mM, 200 mM, and 400 mM. Protein purities and their molecular weights were analyzed by standard SDS-PAGE and LC-MS. Amicon (Merck) was used to concentrate and buffer exchange the purified periplasmic proteins (50 mM ammonium acetate) and the full-length protein (50 mM HEPES, pH 7.5, 300 mM NaCl, 1 mM DDM). All buffer used for the full-length proteins was supplemented with 1 mM DDM to warrant the micelle formation with a critical minimum concentration (CMC) of 0.17 mM. In the original objective, we aimed at the expression of the periplasmic regions of FtsQ, FtsB and FtsL only. But during our study, we achieved to express both the periplasmic regions and full length of all three proteins. As FtsQ, FtsB and FtsL are bitopic transmembrane proteins, the expression of full length proteins are much difficult but eventually we were able to obtain the full length proteins with high purity. Objective 2: To study the protein-protein interaction and conformational change in these bacterial cell division proteins by H/D exchange mass spectrometry Hydrogen/deuterium exchange mass spectrometry was conducted with a Waters Synapt G2-Si Mass Spectrometer equipped with an automated HDX manager (Leap technologies). Deuterium labeling was performed by adding 5 µL of protein sample (40 µM) to 95 µL of deuterium buffer (pD 7.0, 50 mM potassium phosphate in 99.9 % D2O). Proteins were deuterated at room temperature in selected on-exchange periods. After each interval, the exchange reaction was quenched by transferring the deuterated sample to a quenching buffer (pH 2.5, 50 mM potassium phosphate) in a 1:1 volume ratio that was kept at 0 °C. A 50 µL portion of the quenched sample was injected immediately into UPLC-MS. Proteins were first digested online, followed by 3 min of concentrating and desalting at the guard column (ACQUITY UPLC BEH C18 VanGuard Pre-column, 130 Å, 1.7 µm, 2.1 mm x 5 mm). The digested peptides were then separated through the C18 reverse-phase analytical column (ACQUITY UPLC BEH C18 Column, 130 Å, 1.7 µm, 1 mm x 100 mm) using 10 to 95 % water: acetonitrile (with 0.1 % (v/v) formic acid) solvent gradient. The peptides were separated and eluted with a solvent gradient of 0 to 0.5 min: 92 % A/ 8 % B; 0.5 to 10 min: 92 % A/ 8 % B to 40 % A/ 60 % B; 10 min to 10.5 min: 40 % A/ 60% B to 5% A/ 95 % B; 10.5 min to 13.5 min: 5 % A/ 95 % B, where solvent A was H2O with 0.1 % formic acid and solvent B was acetonitrile with 0.1% formic acid. The solvent flow rate was 60 µL/min. To minimize back exchange, except for the pepsin column (Waters EnzymateTM BEH Pepsin Column, 300 Å, 5 µm, 2.1 mm x 30 mm) was kept at room temperature, all parts of the Acquity UPLC M-Class dual-pump LC system were placed in a 0 °C chamber. The eluted peptides were analyzed with the mass spectrometer (MSE data acquisition mode) using leucine enkephalin for internal mass calibration. The mass spectrometer conditions were: 3 kV capillary voltage, 150 °C source temperature, 350 °C desolvation temperature, 600 L/h of desolvation gas flow, and 6.5 bar nebulizer gas flow. The mass spectrometer was operated in MSe mode with a 0.3 second scan time. The trap collision energy was ramped with a 6 V lower energy acquisition and 15 to 35 V for high energy acquisition. Three technical replicates were performed for each HDX time point. Six column volume of pepsin wash solution (1.5 M guanidine hydrochloride/ acetonitrile/ formic acid in 4.0/ 95.2/ 0.8 % (v/v)) was injected to clean the pepsin column, and the same solvent gradient was used subsequently to remove the residual peptides in the C18 column after each sample injection. Peptide peak assignment was performed by the ProteinLynx Global Server (PLGS, version 3.0.2, Waters) with the primary sequence of the target proteins. Only the peptide that matched the following criteria were processed: PLGS score > 6, precursor ion (MH+) mass error < 10 ppm, and the number of product ions per amino acid > 0.33. The HDX-MS data of the free and complexed Fts-proteins were processed by the DynamX (Version 3.0.0, Waters) software, and the results were manually inspected. An E coli proteome (GCF_012978145.1) database was used to validate the peptide assignment. The reference mass of each peptide was generated by the same HDX-MS procedure while replacing all the D2O with deionized water. There is no bimodal distribution in the analyzed peptides. The average deviation of the deuterium uptake was below 0.1 Da. Back exchange level was estimated to be an average rate of 50% by analyzing fully deuterated peptides and was not corrected when carrying out comparisons of deuterium uptake. The results of HDX-MS study on the protein-protein interaction and conformational change of FtsQ, FtsB and FtsL are summarized in item 8 (journal publication) under Part C Research Outputs of this report.

15305217.label: Major findings and research outcome
15305217.value: FtsQBL is a transmembrane protein complex in the divisome of Escherichia coli that plays a critical role in regulating divisions. Although extensive efforts have been made to investigate the interactions between the three involved proteins: FtsQ, FtsB, and FtsL, the detailed interaction mechanism is still poorly understood. In this study, hydrogen-deuterium-exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS) was used to investigate these full-length proteins and complexes purified in the detergent DDM. The structural dynamic changes and the related binding interfaces within the complexes were dissected. Our HDX data reveal that the FtsB and FtsL interact at both the periplasmic and transmembrane regions to form a stable complex. Part of the periplasmic region of FtsB underwent significant conformational changes. With the help of modeling, our results reveal that the FtsBL complexation may bring the respective constriction control domains (CCDs) close together. When FtsBL adopts a coiled-coil structure, the CCDs are fixed at a vertical position relative to the membrane surface. Thus, this conformational change in the FtsBL complexation may be essential for interacting with other divisomal proteins. In the FtsQBL complex, intriguingly, only FtsB interacts with FtsQ at its C-terminal region and stiffens a large area of the β-domain in FtsQ. Furthermore, the connection between the α- and β-domains in FtsQ is also strengthened in the complex. Overall, the present study provides important experimental evidence on the local interactions between the full-length FtsB, FtsL, and FtsQ and valuable insights into the roles of FtsQBL complexation in regulating the divisome activity. The results have been accepted for publication in Journal of Biological Chemistry (item 8 in Part C)

15305217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15305217.value: As the FtsQBL complex is believed to be a switch in regulating the divisome activity, further study on how the protein complex interacts with E. coli PBP1b (the protein that is responsible for peptidoglycan synthesis) would shed light on how FtsQBL functions to regulate peptidoglycan synthesis. This can be achieved by studying the interaction of FtsQBL with PBP1b through a combination of different techniques, such as H/D exchange mass spectrometry and cryo-electron microscopy. The role of other bacterial cell division proteins like FtsN and CPoB in the interaction between FtsQBL and PBP1b should also be studied with similar techniques to get a better picture on how the conformation of FTsQBL changes in the presence of FtsN and CPoB which will affect its interaction with PBP1b.

15305217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15305217.value: Antibiotic resistance is a serious worldwide health threatening problem. There is an urgent need to develop new antibiotics based on new chemical structures and new drug targets. Proteins that are involved in bacterial cell division are potential drug targets in the development of new antibiotics. The FtsQBL protein complex is an important protein complex in regulating bacterial cell division. Understanding how FtsQBLworks in bacterial cytokinesis is important both for advancement of knowledge and application in antibiotic development. Interruption of the functions of FtsQBL will lead to failure in bacterial division. In particular, knowledge on how FtsQBL interacts with other proteins during cell division and the conformational changes in association with its functions will provide insight on the development of small molecules as inhibitors of the protein complex. This study unveils the conformational change of FtsQBL by hydrogen/deuterium exchange mass spectrometry. The results of this project provides useful information on how FtsQBL functions in bacterial cytokinesis and the information will guide the future development of FtsQBL inhibitors as new antibiotics

15500917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15500917.value: Although there are many on-going debates on the effects of the emerging accommodation sharing services, there is limited empirical research on the gains of destinations where these services are offered. We plan to investigate how the entry of accommodation sharing services into a market influences tourist flow and satisfaction in major destinations in China. We will exploit a set of natural experiments that are the staggered rollouts of two major accommodation sharing services in China between 2011 and 2015. Using the difference-in-difference econometric strategy, we will estimate the effect of the accommodation sharing services on tourist flow and satisfaction. Drawing on millions of online observations captured from accommodation sharing and destination review platforms, this study is the first attempt to use large online datasets to rigorously measure whether accommodation sharing services have generated tourism benefits for destinations. The findings are expected to contribute to the understanding of the fast growth in visitor numbers and improved destination experience of accommodation sharing. These findings will not only have implications for the on-going debates on how the sharing economy might enhance or hinder destination tourism development, they also may generate policy suggestions by revealing the mechanisms through which accommodation sharing services influence tourists’ experiences. The insights obtained from the study could also help the industries affected by the sharing economy to form useful business strategies with a view to enhancing their competitiveness. More importantly, the research findings could inform policymakers who wish to regulate this emerging sector within the service industry. 儘管有關新興的住宿共享服務的影響有許多持續的討論，其對目的地之好處的實證研究仍然有限。研究隊伍計劃調查住宿共享服務進入市場的情況如何影響中國主要目的地的旅客流量和滿意度。研究員將進行一系列自然實驗，即2011至2015年期間中國兩大住宿共享服務的交錯推出，利用差中差計量經濟學，評估住宿共享服務對旅客流量及滿意度的影響。本研究將從住宿共享和目的地評論平台取得在線觀測資料，是首個嘗試使用大型在線數據來測量住宿共享服務是否為目的地帶來旅遊收益的研究。研究結果將有助瞭解旅客量的增長和改善目的地體驗。調查結果不僅牽動共享經濟如何增強或阻礙目的地旅遊發展的持續辯論，並通過揭示住宿共享服務對旅客體驗的影響來提供政策建議。研究見解亦有助共享經濟下的行業制訂有用的商業策略，以提高競爭力。更重要的是，研究結果可供決策者參考。

15500917.label: Realisation of objectives
15500917.value: All five research objectives have been achieved after the completion of the study. Regarding objectives 1-5, the empirical findings of this study identify a positive spillover effect of the entry of accommodation sharing on the neighboring attractions in a destination. In particular, using the difference-in-differences estimations with two-way fixed effects, we quantify a 15.4% increase in an attraction’s popularity after the entry of accommodation sharing (Objective 1). By comparing different service providers, the study examines that this positive spillover effect is reduced when the density of commercially operated properties is higher (Objective 3). The use of various specifications allows us to cross-check the robustness of the estimation results (Objective 5). The temporal increase and geographical diffusion of the entry effect of accommodation sharing are identified (Objective 2). The pre-treatment heterogeneity is estimated using a relative time model to check its parallel trends assumption (Objective 4).
