15500917.label: Major findings and research outcome
15500917.value: Following the rapid proliferation of accommodation sharing and its consequences, this study provides a comprehensive analysis of the impact of accommodation sharing. This is the first study to identify and quantify the positive horizontal spillover of the entry of accommodation sharing services on tourist attractions. In the context of accommodation sharing, this study further determines the heterogeneous impact of private hosts (e.g., peers who share vacant space) and commercial hosts (hosts with formal business licenses) on tourist attractions. Expanding existing studies of the influence of a new disruptive business model on a long-established industry, we address connectivity and interdependency between multiple tourism service sectors. In particular, the difference-in-differences estimates of the relationship between the entry and non-entry of accommodation-sharing services cast light on intra-industry dynamics in hospitality and tourism. This study provides useful information for policy formulation by revealing the mechanisms underpinning how accommodation sharing services influence tourism industries in a destination region. Furthermore, exploring how different types of hosts facilitate such an impact offers insights into specific strategies for marketing operations in accommodation sharing. The research has resulted in two top-tier journal publications and two conference papers.

15500917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15500917.value: Given the research findings of this project, further examination of the spillover effects on various tourism and hospitality sectors are highly encouraged. This study extends the academic debates about the positive spillovers of the sharing economy beyond the ongoing arguments focused mainly on its negative impacts. This study examines a horizontal spillover in two key tourism service suppliers that are geographically adjacent to each other. This empirical evidence can help to initiate the development of spillover and spatial interaction theory that can be used to delineate the negative and positive spillover effects of other peer-to-peer sharing businesses on various tourism-related industries. Future studies could also look at the horizontal spillover effects of new entrants on other destinations than China. The current project focused on the impacts of the peer-to-peer accommodation sharing on the suppliers of tourism products/services. Future research could investigate the impacts of peer-to-peer accommodation sharing on the behavior of consumers or vice versa. In fact, the research team has already submitted another GRF proposal (2020/2021) with the main focus on identifying the factors that may affect senior residents’ choice of the peer-to-peer sharing accommodations, which extends the current research in this direction.

15500917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15500917.value: Although there are many on-going debates on the effects of the emerging accommodation sharing services, there is limited empirical research on the gains of destinations where these services are offered. This research investigates how the entry of accommodation sharing services influences tourist flows and satisfaction in major destination attractions using the difference-in-difference modeling strategy. It exploits a set of natural experiments that are the staggered rollouts of two major accommodation sharing services in Beijing between 2013 and 2017. Drawing on millions of online observations captured from accommodation sharing and destination review platforms, this study is the first attempt to use large online datasets to measure the benefits of accommodation sharing services for tourist destinations. The findings contribute to the understanding of the spillover effects of the accommodation sharing on the tourism activities in destinations. Not only do the research findings have important research implications for the on-going debates related to the sharing accommodation sector and its influence on the destination economy, they also provide useful policy suggestions for destination management in terms of revealing the mechanisms through which accommodation sharing services influence tourists’ experiences. More importantly, the research findings could inform policymakers who wish to regulate this emerging sector within the service industry.

15501017.value: 一個重要的財務研究題目為調查股票回報波動是由現金流和/或貼現率消息驅動的。現有的證據仍是不確定的。早期的結果表明貼現率新聞的重要性，這激發了強調貼現率風險的資產定價模式（例如，Campbell和Cochrane 1999）。相比之下，Chen，Da, 和Zhao（2013）發現，分析師盈利預測推斷的現金流量消息可能佔所有股票價格變化的很大一部分。他們的研究結果支持強調現金流風險的資產定價模型（例如，Bansal和Yaron 2004）。 我們提出的研究評估了基於分析師的方法的結論在多大程度上受到分析師預測中可預測的錯誤的影響。例如，如果看漲的投資者情緒推動了分析師的預測和股票價格，那麼基於分析師的現金流新聞就會顯示出股價走勢。但與基本面支持的真實現金流新聞不同，這種情緒驅動的“現金流量新聞”受到投資者過度樂觀的推動，並且往往不能完全實現。因此，由看漲情緒驅動的分析師現金流新聞的組成部分將預測未來股票收益低點 - 就像低貼現率將導致同期股價高漲，但未來回報低。知道股票價格受到這種情緒驅動的“現金流量新聞”驅動，其實並不支持像Bansal和Yaron（2004）等模型，因為這些模型的現金流量預期不包含可預測的預測誤差。 Hribar和McInnis（2012），So（2013）以及 Mao 和 Wei（2014年，2016年）顯示，可預測的分析師預測錯誤影響股票收益，而Arif和Lee（2014年），Huang，Jiang，Tu, and Zhou（2015）顯示，這些錯誤也與總體股價的時間序列變化有關。我們評估這些研究發現的有偏差的現金流量預測是否也影响整體股票的收益波動。

15501017.label: Realisation of objectives
15501017.value: We have used various firm characteristics and their interactions with investor sentiment to predict analyst forecast biases, mutual fund portfolio holdings, as well as cross-sectional and time-series variations in stock returns. These variations in stock returns are then decomposed into cash flow and discount rate components, and are used to evaluate the importance of expectation biases and investor sentiment in explaining stock return variations. The evaluation of the extent to which stock price variations reflects future earnings information is closely related to a growing literature on "stock price informativeness" (see references below), with some analyses for Objective 3 still ongoing—in order to compare my results to this literature. 15501017.label: Major findings and research outcome
15501017.value: Both discount rate movements and investor sentiment are found to impact stock price variations. In relation to investor sentiment, Chue and Mian (2021) find that investor sentiment affects the degree of institutional investors' active stock selection, challenging the conventional view that it is only the preponderance of retail investors during high sentiment periods that allows sentiment to influence asset prices. In relation to discount rate, Chue and Xu (2021) find that the cash component of aggregate profits contain discount rate information not found in other known predictors of the equity premium, including aggregate investor sentiment. We also find that this positive predictive relationship between aggregate cash profits and stock returns is related to the term structure of interest rates, and that cash profits forecast higher aggregate risks—as proxied by aggregate market volatility and average correlation of firm-level stock returns. In all, aggregate cash-based operating profits contain unique discount rate information, indicating that accounting data is informative at the macroeconomic level. Finally, Chue (2021) finds that the stock prices of companies with high capital investment tend to be more informative for future earnings. This finding contrasts with a large body of research that tries to explain firms' investment decisions from a behavioral perspective, which concludes that companies with higher investment expenditure suffer from greater mispricing.

15501017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15501017.value: We plan to show that our finding of a positive relationship between capital investment and price informativeness is robust to the new measure developed by Davila and Parlatore (2021). We also plan to use our methodology to evaluate the impact of investor sentiment on stock price informativeness. This exercise serves as a quantitative assessment of sentiment on investor welfare. Even though investor sentiment has been widely attributed as an important source of stock market fluctuations, an evaluation of its overall impact on welfare is still lacking.

15501017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15501017.value: Investor sentiment has received much attention, from researchers and practitioners alike, as a potential explanation of stock price movements. We show that the impact of sentiment can show up in unexpected places, and yet be over-rated in others. On the former, Chue and Mian (2021) find that even professional fund managers are sentiment-prone—challenging the conventional view that it is only the preponderance of retail investors during high sentiment periods that allows sentiment to influence asset prices. On the latter, Chue and Xu (2021) show that aggregate cash profits contain discount rate information—related to the term structure of interest rates and different measures of market risks—that outperform various sentiment measures as predictors of the overall stock market. In the cross section, Chue (2021) shows that the stock prices of firms that have higher capital investments are found to reflect a larger fraction of all inter-firm variations in future earnings. This result suggests that the conclusion reached by a large body of behavioral research—that it is sentiment that drives companies' investment decisions—may be premature.

15501217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15501217.value: Omni-channel drives the next wave of supply chain evolution, but retailers are still struggling in their omni-channel adoption. The manager’s main concern is that they are not convinced that omni-channel can indeed be profitable, given the tremendous effort to transition from traditional operations to this new business model. What differs omni-channel operations from multi-channel operations is that online and offline channels are managed as an integrated organization, instead of as independent organizations competing for resources. The objective of this project is to understand the impacts of omni-channel on supply chain operations and restructuring. We propose to investigate those issues that have practical relevance and academic interest. Specifically, we are interested in how firms can better serve customers with new channel adoption and restructure supply chains to more responsively match supply up with changing demands. Importantly, we want to identify the hurdles to omni-channel success. An in-depth understanding of the interaction between bricks-and-mortar stores and online channels is helpful to provide concrete insights. We analyze representative supply chains with omni-channel adoption as a strategic option. By capturing the omni-channel features that have a broad appeal, our exploration is based on the customers’ utility-driven channel selection for demand generation and the firms’ demand fulfillment by restructuring their relationships with suppliers. The retailing industry is a pivotal service sector and has a substantial impact on the economy. Overall retailing in Hong Kong SAR has seen a decline in 2016 that extends the trend starting in 2015. Among the contributing factors, intensified regional competition, worsened economy and increasingly entangled geo-political environments are notable ones. Traditional operations are outdated. Non-store retailing is now on the horizon. With a high level of mobile penetration and interconnectedness, customers increasingly rely on omni-channel to search for information and finalize transactions. This offers retailers a golden opportunity to strengthen competitiveness and seek growth by tailoring their supply chains to fit the changing market condition in a more responsible and responsive way. We look into the fundamental features of omni-channel, its design and operations, by pining on customer behavior and supplier involvement. The findings are expected to provide guidance for retailers to adopt omni-channel to reach customers and manage channel integration for demand generation and fulfillment. 15501217.label: Realisation of objectives
15501217.value: This project was motivated by the fast development of e-commerce that has pushed firms online, giving rise to the prevalent omni-channel operations. The co-existence of online and offline channels has become the new engine of growth, driving the new wave of supply chain re-engineering. Omni-channel operations differ critically from traditional multi-channel operations in that online and offline channels are managed as an integrated organization. By contrast, firms in the traditional multi-channel structure operate channels as separate entities and expect each of them to optimize its own performance. Online channel has long been managed separately without being integrated into the bricks-and-mortar business model, unavoidably leading to internal competition for resources and hurting overall efficiencies. This is destined to change as supply chains in the new age of AI and data analytics have turned to be centric to consumers, who expect to search and purchase products across a variety of channels in a timely manner. This calls for the rise of omni-channel that has at its core the intricate integration across channels for demand generation and fulfillment. In this project, we have taken a few chosen perspectives to investigate the impact of omni-channel, with the changes in supply chain structure and the means of interactions it ushers in, on the firms’ operations, information flow, consumer behavior, and market efficiency. The general objectives are to address the latest issues that revolve around omni-channel adoption, including how firms adapt operations and information policies to better serve customers with new channel adoption, how consumers react to the changes in channel structure and operations policies, and the resulting effects on consumer surplus and social welfare. An in-depth understanding of the interactions between bricks-and-mortar store and online channel is pivotal to addressing these issues. Since the commencement of this project, we have exerted substantial efforts to develop a general model framework, which houses a variety of industry structures including channel structure, market competition mode and information structure, and work on the various aspects to investigate the targeted issues to great detail. Our focus in this analytical investigation is on the strategic effects of omni-channel adoption by the firms on their operations and information interactions, attending to the consumers’ utility-driven response in practical environments. The results from this project reveal how a supply chain system can adapt itself to the changing business environment, through a series of rational actions taken by constituent members, and the effects on the profit performance of its constituent members in absolute and relative terms. The main objectives of the project have been achieved. An important finding stemming from our research is that the latest trend in omni-channel adoption, through its impact on the operations and information interactions among firms, has a critical effect of facilitating information sharing in supply chains to enhance system-wide information transparency. Channel competition structure, mode of market selling and signal structure are crucial factors influencing the scale of this effect. On the path to reach this finding, we have successfully addressed a decade-long issue in the study of incentive-driven information sharing. Specifically, we show that firms holding private demand information have an incentive to truthfully share private information with other firms, instead of engaging in the intricate signalling and inference processes. We believe that this result will have a substantial impact in the community, to encourage further efforts into the research on information sharing. Our research also reveals that the firms engaging in the new business model have an incentive to adopt pricing and stocking strategies that they would not consider in the traditional business model. Moreover, our results clearly indicate the roadmap whereby firms should follow to adapt their strategies to the new model. Despite the flexibility that the firms can gain in managing operations and information interactions, circumstances exist in which firms are trapped into the well-known Prisoner’s Dilemma type of situation to adopt inferior strategies and are thus suffer worsened profit performance. These results yield actionable guidance for firms to optimize the means to manage information and operations in the new era. In the process of working on this project, we frequently consulted senior and experienced scholars in the relevant fields for their comments on our progress. We delivered presentations based on research findings in international conferences and at invited research seminars hosted by a variety of institutions, and received valuable feedback from colleagues, which have helped us to strengthen the scope and substance of the work. The research findings have been documented into working papers and published in peer-reviewed journals. The two articles that were fully funded by this project, i.e., they were completed, submitted for review, accepted, and published in the project period (Jan 1, 2018 – June 30, 2020) have been attached to this report. Based on the progress that we have made thus far, we have exerted efforts to extend the scope of research by including more participants and adding more practical features into the general model framework. We expect fruitful outputs from all these dedicated efforts.

15501217.label: Major findings and research outcome
15501217.value: Our research findings have been documented into working papers and published in peer-reviewered journals. Two publications were fully funded by this project. One paper, published in Operations Research Letters (Vol 47, 305-310) under title “Direct selling by suppliers improves system-wide information flow”, initiates a pioneering effort to explore the impact of omni-channel migration on information flow. In a bilateral monopoly selling to a market with uncertain demand, the retailer has a demand signal. The supplier can, in addition to the traditional channel, implement a direct channel, gaining access to market information as well. As the supplier and retailer have demand information useful for updating the forecast of market conditions, they can acquire signals from each other. We demonstrate that the supplier's direct selling improves information flow to realize system-wide transparency, but it has mixed profit implications. In the process, we establish an important finding: firms have an incentive to make private demand signals fully inferable by each other.; this result resolves the decade-long debate on how firms manage private signals and is expected to have a far-fetching impact. This work paves the way for two other papers, currently in the late stage of review, which extend the study to more general settings. The other paper studies operations initiatives in an omni-channel environment, where consumers gain timely information of prices and inventory availability at retailers and switch among them to finalize purchases. Prior to knowing the actual market size, retailers choose stocking quantities before prices under prestocking but adopt the reverse sequence under prepricing. After actual market size is realized, each customer chooses to purchase from a retailer to maximize utility. Each retailer satisfies local demand up to availability. A customer with unmet demand at the local retailer may continue to visit the other retailer, termed customer switching. We find that, in the presence of customer switching, product value and market condition are crucial to whether and how retailers adapt strategies. Retailers can adopt differential strategies, whereby the retailer that overprices the other stocks more as well. Customer switching can also trap the retailers into a Prisoner's Dilemma type of situation to price low and stock less. Compared to prepricing, prestocking weakens retailers’ incentive for strategic divergence but enables them to profit more when market conditions are optimistic. This paper was published in Production and Operations Management (Vol 29, 6, 1381-1396) under title “The bright and dark sides of customer switching”.

15501217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15501217.value: The progress made in the project drives us to explore other relevant issues pertaining to information flow and operations interactions embedded in general omni-channel frameworks. Along one direction, we investigate the appropriate sequence whereby the supplier, with an online presence, establishes vertical information interactions with a group of retailers who compete in selling substitutable products to the market, and study the sustainability of system-wide information transparency. Along another direction, we study horizontal subcontracting between retailers who source from the same supplier but engage in dual-channel operations. The main issues are when and what to subcontract from one another, and which channel to deploy subcontracted resources to. The complete results are expected to be useful for guiding contracting procedures under suitable market conditions in practice. Moreover, we are in the process of further integrating operations and information initiatives to study their strategic interplay in improving system performance in omni-channel environments, by drawing in more participants and adding more practical features into the investigating framework. The progress has been smooth and we are confident of pushing this research to further depth and producing fruitful outputs.

15501217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15501217.value: Motivated by the increasingly prevalent omni-channel operations amid the development of e-commerce that has moved firms online in addition to selling through traditional channels, we have engaged in a systematic exploration of the effects on operations and information interactions among supply chain firms alongside the impact on consumers and society. On one hand, omni-channel operations enable firms to reach consumers through more channels, gaining access to more timely information and flexibly allocating resources between channels. On the other hand, it grants more convenience to consumers in searching for product information and finalize purchases. Our research finds that this trend has a critical role in facilitating information flow among supply chain partners to enhance system-wide information transparency. This justifies the fast development of information infrastructure (i.e., blockchain) dedicated to facilitating information sharing and data analytics. Moreover, it grants firms more flexibility in managing competitive instruments such as prices and inventory availability, enticing them to engage in the strategies they would forgo in the traditional business model. Nevertheless, it is likely that firms are harmed by their omni-channel adoption by being trapped to adopt inferior strategies. We suggest concrete policies that guide firms to adapt to the new business model.

15502917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15502917.value: Today with the rapid growth of information technology and the popularity of social media, a consumer can easily obtain the product information through the posted reviews and ratings. And such reviews/ratings heavily influence their purchase decisions. Thus, more and more firms now rely on word of mouth marketing to advocate their products since this option is not only effective but also cost-saving. However, a consumer's quality evaluation inevitably involves behavioral factors such as reference-dependent preference and loss aversion that can be influenced by the seller's information disclosure strategy. In addition, a firm's own information disclosure decision is inevitably affected by the rival firm's information disclosure decision. Therefore, it remains unclear (1) to which extent such word of mouth marketing is effective when there exists market competition, (2) under which scenarios the firm shall withhold its quality information and rely on the consumer's word of mouth to advocate its products when facing loss-averse consumers, and (3) under which scenarios the firm shall disclose its own quality. In this project, we are going to investigate the above questions by explicitly investigating how consumer loss aversion and market competition affect a firm's information disclosure strategy. We plan to first consider a duopoly setting where two firms sell products to reference-dependent and loss-averse consumers that hold prior beliefs about firms' quality via online reviews/ratings. We first ignore the horizontal reference effect (where the consumer would take the product quality of the rival firm as a reference point) and derive the firms' optimal pricing and consumers' purchasing decisions under four scenarios depending on whether each firm discloses or withholds its private quality information. A comparison of the firms' profits and consumer surplus across the above four scenarios can help us answer the above research questions. We then need to extend the above analyses to incorporate the horizontal reference effect and to consider a two-period setting with the consumer post-consumption quality evaluations to re-examine the above questions. 随着信息技术的飞速发展和社交媒体的流行，消费者可以轻松地通过消费者评论/评分获取产品信息。这些评论/评分严重影响了消费者的购买决定。 因此，因为口碑营销即有效又节约成本，越来越多的企业现在依赖口碑营销来推销他们的产品。 消费者对产品的评价不可避免地受到其行为因素的影响。而消费者的参考点依赖偏好和损失规避行为可能受到企业信息披露策略的影响。此外，一个企业自身的信息披露决策也受到其竞争对手信息披露决策的影响。当市场存在竞争的情况下，目前还不清楚：口碑营销到底有多有效；在面临损失规避型消费者时，企业应该在什么情况下不披露其质量信息而依赖口碑营销来推销他们的产品；企业又应该在什么情况下披露其质量信息。 在这个研究项目中，我们将具体研究消费者损失规避行为和市场竞争如何影响企业的信息披露策略。我们考虑双寡头垄断下企业向有参考点依赖偏好和损失规避的消费者销售其产品。消费者通过网上的评论/评分对企业产品有一个先验认知。根据各个企业是否进行信息披露，我们进一步研究企业的定价决策和消费者的购买行为。通过对比不同情况下企业的利润和消费者盈余，我们可以探讨企业应该在什么时候进行信息披露。

15502917.label: Realisation of objectives
15502917.value: All the five objectives have been achieved. This research project focuses on the firms’ information disclosure strategies in an information age with loss-averse customers. We aim to examine how consumers’ reference-dependent and loss-averse behavior affects the firms’ information disclosure strategy. We have considered that firms are selling products to the reference-dependent loss-averse consumers. We have constructed game-theoretical models to derive consumers' reference-dependent and loss-averse utilities and their purchasing decisions depending on whether the firms withhold or disclose their private quality information. Through backward induction, we have derived the firm’s optimal retail pricing decision depending on whether the firm withholds or discloses the private quality information under both monopoly and duopoly settings. We then compared the equilibria associated with the monopoly and duopoly settings to examine how market competition and consumer loss aversion affect the consumer surplus, the firms' profitability and their information withholding/disclosing decisions. We show that competition and consumer loss aversion can actually benefit the firms and consumers. The firm’s disclosure incentive is much lower in a competition context than that when the firm is a monopoly. In other words, horizontal competition induces firms to withhold more private quality information. We further considered a scenario where the firms under horizontal competition may share their quality information with each other before launching their products into the market. The firms are asymmetry in the sense that one firm may have the high quality while the other has the low quality. Consumers can confirm the timing of firms’ disclosure decisions before the firms make the disclosure decisions. Upon observing the firms’ information disclosure behavior, a horizontal reference effect then arises. We show that horizontal information sharing between the competing firms, which leads to the horizontal reference effect in deriving the consumers’ reference dependent quality expectations, dramatically impacts the equilibrium disclosure strategies. Now, the firm that has the ex-post low quality never discloses his quality information, while he may disclose such information when the firms do not share their private quality information upfront. This is because horizontal information sharing alters the consumer quality speculation process. It facilitates the consumer to better infer the firms' product quality after observing their disclosure behaviors. When the firms do not share their quality information, the consumer believes that each firm's disclosure decision is independent and her quality expectation towards the firm that withholds his information would converge to a fixed point. However, when the firms share their quality information, firms' disclosure decisions are now dependent on their observed quality levels in the sense that they are correlated. The consumer then can take the disclosed quality level as a benchmark to further infer the quality level of the firm that withholds his information. Thus, only the ex-post high-quality firm has the incentive to disclose his quality when firms share their information upfront. We have also considered a two-period setting where consumers arrive sequentially and are reference dependent with respect to product quality. The early adopters post their subjective post-consumption reviews, which are observable by the followers. Consumers may be naive or sophisticated, depending on whether they can make rational inferences from the firm's disclosure behavior and an experienced consumer's quality review. We show that when consumers are naive, the firm can strategically withhold high quality information and disclose low quality information to boost the reference-dependent early adopter's subjective quality review, which in turn enhances the follower's quality expectation and allows the firm to extract more surplus in the second period. However, when consumers are sophisticated, it is difficult for the firm to enhance their quality expectations by designing his disclosure strategy to manipulate the early adopter's quality review. The firm discloses all the quality information to consumers. When the market contains both naive and sophisticated consumers, the firm is able to withhold relatively low quality information in advance. In such a situation, the firm exclusively serves naive customers in the first period by charging a high retail price. We further consider a setting where the firm is a service provider. Sophisticated customers are well-informed of service-related information, including service quality and reward, and decide whether to join the firm’s service or balk strategically, whereas naive customers do not have such information and rely on online rating information to make such decisions. We demonstrate that under certain conditions a service provider can increase its profitability by simply `dancing' its price, that is, replacing the static pricing strategy with a high-low cyclic pricing strategy. Based on the finding in this research project, we have completed three academic papers which are listed as follows: F. Huang, P. Guo and Y. Wang. Cyclic Pricing When Customers Queue with Rating Information. Production and Operations Management, 28, 2471-2485, 2019. X. Guan, Y. Wang, Z. Yi and Y. Chen. Inducing Consumer Online Reviews via Disclosure. Production and Operations Management, 29(8), 1956-1971, 2020. X. Guan and Y. Wang. Quality Disclosure in a Competitive Environment with Consumer’s Elation and Disappointment. Omega, 2021, accepted and available online. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.omega.2021.102586.

15502917.label: Major findings and research outcome
15502917.value: The PI has trained one PhD student, worked with two postdoctoral fellows, and presented the research work at three conferences and several universities. Three research papers are generated, with two published on Production and Operations Management, a flagship UT-Dallas FT journal, and one accepted by Omega (high impact factor: 7.084). Our main findings are as follows: In a business setting, consumers often arrive sequentially and are reference-dependent towards product quality. Under a two-period setting, we show that when consumers are naïve/myopic, the seller/firm can strategically withhold high quality information and disclose low quality information to boost the reference-dependent early adopter's subjective quality review, which in turn enhances the follower's quality expectation. However, when consumers are sophisticated, the seller discloses all the quality information to consumers. When the market contains both naive and sophisticated consumers, the seller is able to withhold relatively low quality information in advance. The related results have been published on Production and Operations Management; See Part C (8) Item 1. When the firm does not disclose their quality information, naive customers do not have such information and rely on buyer-generated information to make their decisions. In a service firm system, we demonstrate that under certain conditions a service provider firm can increase its profitability by simply `dancing' its price, that is, replacing the static pricing strategy with a high-low cyclic pricing strategy when certain customers are review-dependent to disclose his quality information. The related results have been published on Production and Operations Management; See Part C (8) Item 2. Loss-averse consumers generate psychological feelings of elation or disappointment when the perceived product quality exceeds or falls short of their initial expectations. We show that both psychological disappointment and elation can induce the firm(s) to disclose more quality information than that when the consumer is fully rational. However, firm competition mitigates the firms’ information disclosure incentive. In a monopoly setting, the increase of the magnitude of disappointment always undermines the firm's profit while the increase of the magnitude of elation may hurt the firm's profitability. In contrast, in a duopoly setting, the increase of the magnitude of disappointment and/or elation always improves the firm's profitability. Such improvement can be further enhanced when the competing firms share their quality information upfront before making their disclosure decisions (which leads to a horizontal reference effect). The related results have been published online with Omega; See Part C (8) Item 3.

15502917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15502917.value: There are some related research topics that are worth exploring. For example, conducting some empirical analysis to verify our analytical results could be an interesting direction for further study. Also, we notice that recently, some e-commerce platforms help the firms to disclose quality information for the products sold on it, such as labelling the product as certified by the platform. What happens when the firm’s business partner, the e-commerce platform is willing to engage in quality information disclosure? Motivated by the observed business practice, we have just started another related research project to study who shall be responsible for quality information disclosure, the firm or the e-commerce platform, and under what conditions.

15502917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15502917.value: Consumers often exhibit reference-dependent preference and are loss-averse, that can cause consumer disappointment (elation) when the product quality is below (above) their expectation. Undoubtedly, a consumer's quality evaluation is inevitably influenced by the firms’ information disclosure strategies, by her type (whether she is sophisticated or naïve), and by her reference-dependent preference. We show that under certain situations, the firm can take advantage of consumer reference dependent preference to withhold its quality information, which can help boost consumer’s perceived quality level and make the firm better off. When more customers are naïve, it becomes more likely for the firms to withhold information and rely on the consumers’ review/ratings (word of mouth) to propagate their quality. We further show that market competition does not necessarily hurt the firm when their customers are loss averse. That is, loss aversion can actually benefit firms in a competitive market. Moreover, the collaborative cooperation between firms via horizontal information sharing can further enhance firm profitability with loss averse consumers. Also, we show the commonly adopted high-low cyclic pricing strategy are actually the optimal pricing strategy when taking customer review into account.

15503517.label: Project Objectives
15503517.value: To comprehensively examine whether security analysts exploit well-documented stock return anomalies and generate recommendations consistent with the return predictability of these anomalies around the world. To evaluate the asset pricing implications when analyst recommendations agree or disagree with anomaly prescriptions. In particular, we investigate whether analyst disagreement defies or amplifies the return predictability of anomalies. To further examine whether our results are pervasive around the world, whether there exists cross-country variation, and whether the strength of our results are associated with country-level institutional environments.

15503517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15503517.value: Security analysts serve an important information intermediary role in financial markets. They collect, process, and disseminate fundamental information, which helps improve market efficiency. Previous studies documents that the stock market reacts strongly when analysts revise their earnings forecasts or change their recommendations. Since analysts are rewarded by the accuracy of their earnings forecasts and superior stock picking ability, they should have strong incentives to make use of all available information. Many cross-sectional return anomalies have been discovered in the past 40 years. If analysts are truly sophisticated and informed, they should exploit such well-known sources of return predictability. The objective of this proposal is to examine the relation between analyst recommendations and return anomalies around the world. I test whether analysts’ recommendations are consistent with firm relative valuation suggested by anomalies. The “sophisticated analyst” view assumes that analysts are sophisticated, informed, and unbiased, and predicts that analysts should produce more favorable recommendations for stocks in the long-leg of anomalies. The “biased analyst” view assumes that analysts are biased and are driven by different incentives, and predicts either no or a negative relation. I consider well-known 11 anomalies suggested by Stambaugh, Yu, and Yuan (2012). I first look at the level and the change of recommendations during the anomaly formation period for long- and short-legs of anomalies separately. However, analysts’ recommendation during the anomaly formation period itself is not sufficient to distinguish between the two hypotheses. Analysts may have superior information such that even their recommendations are contradictory to anomaly prescriptions, their recommended stocks can still outperform. I then examine anomaly returns when analyst recommendations confirm or contradict anomaly signals. The “biased analyst” hypothesis predicts that anomaly returns should be more pronounced when analysts disagree with anomaly prescriptions, whereas the “sophisticated analyst” hypothesis predicts the opposite. Our preliminary result for the U.S. supports the biased analyst hypothesis. I further examine whether our preliminary U.S. results are pervasive across countries and whether the strength of our results are related to country-level institutional environments. The findings of this project should be useful and of great interest to regulators around the world who want to know whether analysts improve or impede market efficiency. Moreover, investors can also benefit from our findings to improve their portfolio performance by taking into account analysts’ stock recommendations when forming their trading strategies based on existing anomalies. 證券分析師在金融市場中扮演重要信息的中介角色。他們收集，處理和傳播基本信息，有助於提高資本市場效率。以前的研究證明，當分析師修改其盈利預測或改變其股票推薦建議時，股市反應強烈。由於分析師的盈利預測的準確性和優良的股票選擇能力得到回報，他們應該有強大的動機來利用所有可用的信息。 過去40年來，已經發現了許多橫斷面股票回報異常現象。如果分析師真正有閱歷和知情，他們應該利用這種眾所周知的回報可預測性。本研究計劃的目的是檢驗分析師股票推薦建議與世界各地股票回報異常之間的關係。我測試分析師的建議是否與回報異常建議的相對估值一致。"複雜分析師”的觀點認為，分析師是有閱歷的，知情的和不偏不倚的，並預測，分析師應該對長倉回報異常的股票產生更有利的建議。“偏見分析師”的觀點認為，分析師有偏見並受不同的激勵所驅動，並且預測其關係不會存在或者是負的。 我將以Stambaugh，Yu和Yuan（2012）所提出的眾所周知的11個股票回報異常變量做為基礎。我首先分析回報異常變量長倉和短倉形成期間的建議程度和變化。然而，分析師在回報異常變量形成期間的建議本身不足以區分這兩個假設。分析師可能會有優越的信息，即使他們的建議與回報異常變量處方相矛盾，他們推薦的股票仍然可以跑贏大市。然後，我將檢驗，當分析師的建議是確認或抵觸回報異常變量信號時，其股票回報異常變量的回報。“偏見分析師”假設預測，當分析師不同意回報異常變量處方時，異常回報應該更明顯，而“複雜分析師”假設則預測其結果相反。我們對美國的初步結果支持偏見分析師假設。我將進一步研究美國的初步結果是否在世界各國普遍存在，我們結果的強弱是否與一個國家的制度和環境有關。 這個研究項目的發現應該對世界各地的監管機構感興趣，並希望了解分析師是否能夠改善或阻礙市場效率。此外，投資者還可以從我們的研究結果中獲益，通過考慮分析師的股票建議，根據現有的回報異常情況形成交易策略，從而提高投資組合的表現。

15503517.label: Realisation of objectives
15503517.value: The major objectives of this project are (i) to examine whether security analyst recommendations are consistent with the return predictability of well-known anomalies around the world; (ii) to evaluate the asset pricing implications when analyst recommendations agree or disagree with anomaly prescriptions; and (iii) to investigate the results extend to the international setting and whether there is a cross-country difference. We find that the results in the U.S. are contrary to the common view that analysts are sophisticated information intermediaries who help improve market efficiency. Specifically, when analysts make more favorable recommendations to stocks classified as overvalued, these stocks tend to have particularly large negative abnormal returns in the future. Moreover, analysts whose recommendations are more aligned with anomaly signals are more skilled and elicit greater recommendation announcement returns. Our results suggest that analysts’ biased recommendations could be a source of market frictions that impede the efficient correction of mispricing. For the international samples (Asian, Europe, Developed, and Emerging) except Japan we find anomaly returns on the two mispricing factors (MGMT and PERF) are consistent with those from the U.S. that a trading strategy by longing underpriced stocks and shorting overpriced stocks earn highly significant abnormal returns. Moreover, we also find that the U.S. findings that analyst recommendations tend to be inconsistent with the mispricing prescription for the MGMT anomaly but to be consistent with the mispricing prescription for the PERF anomaly extend to all international samples including Japan. In contrast, we do not find any evidence consistent with the U.S. finding that when analysts make more favorable recommendations to stocks classified as overvalued, these stocks tend to have particularly large negative abnormal returns in the future. In another paper, I study the long-term shareholder returns in the global stock market and find that the top-performing 2.4% of firms account for all of the net global stock market wealth creation from 1990 to December 2020 that outside the U.S., the ratio is even lower with only 1.41% of firms accounting for all of the net wealth creation. The results are summarized in two papers and one summary report. The paper on “Security analysts and capital market anomalies” has been published at Journal of Financial Economics (2020) and presented in many international academic conferences (the 2018 Financial Management Association Meeting (FMA) in San Diego, the 2019 Asian Bureau of Finance and Economics Research (ABFER) conference in Singapore, and the 2019 Conference on Pacific Basin Finance, Economics, Accounting, and Management (PBFEAM) in Taipei). This paper was the Finalist for the Best Paper Award in Investment at the 2018 FMA meeting. The paper on “Long-term shareholder returns: Evidence from 64,000 global stocks” is currently under review at Financial Analysts Journal as a monograph. The outcomes of the project have clearly demonstrated that the project objectives have been successfully achieved.

Summary: We document that the majority, 55.2% of U.S. stocks and 57.4% of non-U.S. stocks, underperform one-month U.S. Treasury bills in terms of compound returns over the full sample. Due to lack of meaningful finding and at the same time a competing working paper by Azevedo and Müller (2020) finding similar results, we only summarize our major finding without writing up a complete paper.

15503517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15503517.value: Many studies find that financial analyst stock recommendations contain valuable information in the short run. Meanwhile, studies also find that institutional investors tend to trade stocks contradictory to mispricing prescriptions. In this project, we show that in the U.S., those highly overpriced stocks with the most favorable analyst recommendation tend to underperform substantially in the long run (i.e., one year), but it is not the case outside the U.S. It would be potentially interesting to examine whether the interaction effect of security analyst recommendations and mispricing extends to the bond market or the options market.

15503517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15503517.value: Do not take analyst stock recommendations for granted at least in the U.S. We find that analysts tend to give more favorable consensus recommendations to stocks classified as overvalued, and, more importantly, these stocks subsequently tend to have particularly negative abnormal returns. Fortunately, we do not find similar results for stock market outside the U.S. More importantly, we find that shareholder wealth creation is concentrated in less than 2.4% in the global market, especially outside the U.S. (less than 1.41%). The results strongly suggest that only a handful of stocks contribute the total wealth creation for investors and that it is much better for investors to invest in a basket of stocks such as the S&P 500 index fund in the U.S. or the Hang Seng index fund in Hong Kong.

15503817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15503817.value: 資訊科技投資已成爲美國公司的資本開支的最大組成部分 (Mithas et al. 2011) 。有研究指出，它更新迅速，日新月異，並且具有高度的不確定性 (例如 , Dewan et al. 2007, Brynjolfsson 2013) 。 同時 ，資訊科技也是日益重要 ，因爲它可支援企業的各種領域 ，為企業 提供種競爭優勢 ，並使新的商業模式成為可能。因此 ，了解管理人員和董事如何進行資訊科技投資決策十分關鍵。在這項研究提案中 ，我們研究管理人員和董事的社會網絡是否以及如何影響資訊科技投資和投資績效。 鑑於資訊科技 投資複雜而充滿活力，社交網絡（例如共同的社會俱樂部成員資格 , 以及過去教育、之前建立的工作關係）可能有助有關資訊科技知識的傳播 (例如 , Young 2009) 。 透過社交網路，關於最新技術開發，安裝，使用的經驗可以在技術嫺熟的高階主管之間傳播。 同一社交網路中的信任感較強，他們可以分享關於資訊科技投資成本與效益的方方面面。 正如先前的文獻所描述的，社交網絡作爲一項分享知識和經驗的重要渠道 ，可用來提高商業決定的有效性 (Ellison and Fudenberg 1995) 。資訊科技投資的性質表明 ， 社會網絡可以產生重大的影響 。但現有的文獻並沒有深入研究這個問題 , 也許是因爲缺乏高管社交網絡和企業資訊科技方面的大規模數據用於實証研究。 我們將使用 BoardEx 資料庫的社交網路及Harte-Hanks的電腦資訊情報 ( CI ) 數據庫回答如下三個問題 : 1 。社交網絡對資訊科技投資量的影響 : 是否會影響資訊科技投資而導致他們的資訊科技投資量類似? 2 。社交網絡對資訊科技投資回報的影響 : 社會網絡是否會影響公司的資訊科技投資回報? 3 。與資訊科技有關的背景和經驗 : 高管與資訊科技有關的背景和經驗是否增加社交網絡對資訊科技投資量以及投資回報的影響?

15503917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15503917.value: Consumers may incur switching costs if they switch suppliers, which creates consumer stickiness and gives the incumbent suppliers market power to charge a higher price. We extend the analysis of switching costs to competition between big-N and non-big-N auditors. Since investors perceive big-N auditors as having higher reputation and quality, an auditee incurs a cost of switching downward from a big-N to a non-big-N auditor by delivering investors a negative signal about financial statement credibility. Likewise, an auditee enjoys a benefit of switching upward from a non-big-N to a big-N auditor by delivering a positive signal. As such, auditees’ downward switching costs (upward switching benefits) increase (decrease) their stickiness with big-N (non-big-N) auditors and gives the big-N auditors market power. This proposal outlines a theoretical framework incorporating an auditee’s cost and benefit of auditor switch derived from a signaling game into a switching cost model for audit fee determination. Preliminary analytical results show that: the audit fee differential between a big-N and a non-big-N auditors equals their production cost (i.e., quality) difference plus the auditee’s switching cost and benefit; the switching cost and benefit increase with the auditee’s pre-switch earnings quality; the big-N auditor’s market power increases with the switching cost and benefit; and, the equilibrium distribution of auditees between the two types of auditors depends on the levels of the auditees’ switching costs and benefits. Using U.S. data of auditor switches, auditees’ switching costs and benefits will be estimated at the individual auditee level. Empirical tests will be conducted for implications from the theoretical model. The estimated switching costs and benefits will be used to project the probability of unfavorable post-switch audit outcomes. This study brings the switching costs analysis from the field of economics into the growing literature on audit market competition. It offers a new perspective to explain the significant audit fee differential between big-N and non-big-N auditors and helps explain the nature of competition between the two types of auditors. By comparing auditees in terms of their switching costs, switching benefits, and patterns of auditor switches, our approach is applicable by regulators, auditors, and investors in identifying auditees facing high risks of unfavorable audit outcomes (e.g. qualified audit opinions). Moreover, this study contributes to richer switching costs analysis because the large and detailed dataset on auditor switches allows extensive individual-level investigations on consumer and supplier behavior in the presence of switching costs. 聘請一間大核數師公司反映被審計單位的財務報表的可信性。換句話說，大核數師公司不僅提供審計服務，而且還為其客戶執行信號功能。本研究的目標是：（1）理論上對大核數師公司執行信號功能的審計費用的“信號溢價”的確定進行建模，（2）用實際審計師切換數據實證估計均衡信號溢價，（3）實證調查信號溢價與被審計單位的轉換前收益質量之間的關係。經濟學的轉換成本文獻表明，從大核數師公司轉向小核數師公司的總轉換成本有兩個部分：交易成本和負效用。負效用是由於轉換為小核數師公司的負面信號引起的，所以它必須等於被審計方願意支付的最大金額（即信號溢價) 以避免這樣一個負信號。具有良好私人信息的被審核單位比不良私人信息單位願意支付更高的信號溢價，因為後者的審計結果不太有利。這樣可以確保招聘大核數師公司所提供的積極信號對投資者來說是可信的。在均衡情況下，大核數師公司與小核數師公司之間的審計費用差額有兩個組成部分 - 審計成本差異(反映了質量差異)，以及大核數師公司收取的信號溢價。這項提出的研究將是文獻中首先直接估計大核數師公司的信號功能的均衡價格（即“信號溢價”）。轉換核數師公司前的收益質量越高，被審計單位願意為投資者提供良好信號的信號溢價越高。因此，信號溢價與轉換核數師公司前的收益質量成反比。本研究將經濟學領域的轉換成本分析納入審計市場競爭日益增長的文獻。 它提供了一個新的視角來解釋大和小核數師公司之間的重大審計費用差異，並有助於解釋兩種審計師公司之間的競爭性質。 通過比較被審計單位的轉換成本，轉換效益和審計師轉換模式，我們的方法適用於監管機構，審計師和投資者識別面臨高風險的不利審計結果。 此外，這項研究有助於更加豐富的轉換供應商的成本分析，因為審計師公司轉換上的大量和詳細的數據集允許在轉換成本的情況下對消費者和供應商行為進行廣泛的單位層面調查。

15503917.label: Realisation of objectives
15503917.value: 1. The PI has constructed a theoretical model that incorporates an auditee’s cost and benefit of auditor switch derived from a signaling game into a switching cost model. The model determines the audit fee differential between big-N and non-big-N auditors and extends the analysis of switching costs to competition between big-N and non-big-N auditors. An auditee incurs a cost of switching from a big-N to a non-big-N auditor because such a downward auditor switch reduces the creditability of the auditee’s financial statement and delivers a negative signal to investors. Likewise, an auditee enjoys a benefit of switching from a nonbig-N to a big-N auditor because such an upward auditor switch improves credibility and delivers a positive signal. As such, auditees’ downward switching costs (upward switching benefits) increase (decrease) their stickiness with big-N (non-big-N) auditors and gives the big-N auditors market power. Both types of auditors take auditees’ switching costs and benefits into consideration when they set audit fees, which partly explains why the audit fees charged by big-N auditors are so much higher than those by their non-big-N counterparts. 2. The PI and Co-Is have collected data from AuditAnalytics and Compstat for empirically estimating the costs and benefits arising from auditor switches at the individual auditee level. The two alternative methods, namely, non-parametric data envelopment analysis (DEA) and stochastic frontier analysis (SFA), gave similar results. 3. The PI and Co-Is have conducted empirical tests on the implications of the theoretical model. The overall results are consistent with the theoretical model that there is a positive signalling cost embedded in a big-N auditor's fee. 4. The PI and Co-Is have investigated the relationship between the estimated signalling costs and post-switch financial report quality. The findings are consistent with expectation.

15503917.label: Major findings and research outcome
15503917.value: This project is focused on the signaling function performed by large auditors in signaling an auditee’s financial report quality to investors. Large auditors, the so-called ‘big-N auditors’, generally charge substantially higher audit fees than do small auditors, although all auditors presumably follow the same auditing standards and requirements. If auditees with high (low) financial report quality voluntarily select big-N (non-big-N) auditors, the big-N auditors would charge higher audit fees than the non-big-N auditors because the former not only devote more resources to each audit engagement but also convey a positive signal about the auditees’ financial report quality. This project theoretically models the competition between big-N and non-big-N auditors and formulates the negative signal of a downward auditor switch from a big-N to a non-big-N auditor as a switching cost. This switching cost indicates the maximum signaling cost an auditee is willing to incur to hire a big-N auditor. In equilibrium, the fee differential between a big-N and a non-big-N auditor has two components: the difference in audit cost between the two types of auditor, which reflects their difference in audit accuracy, and the signaling cost of hiring the big-N auditor. Our empirical analysis considers not only audit fees but also non-audit fees because auditees are likely to take both into consideration when they make decisions on switching auditors. Our empirical findings show that auditees with higher financial report quality are willing to pay a higher signaling cost, and that non-audit fees embed a larger signaling cost component than audit fees do. Using data on audit fees and auditor switches at the individual auditee level, this study directly estimates the magnitude of each sample auditee’s signaling cost associated with hiring a large auditor. Our empirical findings suggest that for auditees incurring a positive signaling cost, the mean signaling cost is approximately 6.88% and 16.57% of a large auditor’s audit fee and total fee, respectively, where the total fee is the audit fee plus non-audit fee. Our findings also show that when facing market pressure on audit fees, large auditors tend to embed a larger signaling cost component in non-audit fees than they do in audit fees. Specifically, a large auditor collects approximately 70% of the total signaling cost from non-audit fees and the remaining 30% from audit fees. Moreover, auditees with higher financial report quality are willing to pay a higher signaling cost to signal their financial report quality to investors.

15503917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15503917.value: The theoretical and empirical analyses can be extended to policy analysis, e.g., competition policy in the audit market.

15503917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15503917.value: We considered the competition between large and small auditors and analytically shows that the fee differential between them consists of their audit cost difference and the signaling cost of hiring the former. The negative signal associated with a downward auditor switch is a switching cost. Large auditors therefore cannot compete with small auditors if the former perform no signaling function. The analytical model is empirically estimated to show the magnitude of the signaling cost embedded in a large auditor’s audit and non-audit fees. Findings suggest that non-audit fees contain a larger signaling cost component than audit fees do. Moreover, auditees with higher financial report quality are willing to pay a higher signaling cost to signal their financial report quality.

15504617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15504617.value: Despite the increasing prevalence of the formation and termination of brand alliances in today’s business world, research related to this topic is somewhat unilateral. Past research on brand alliance has mostly focused on the reasons leading to the formation and termination of brand alliances and how they influence firms’ strategies and operations. What is largely missing from this literature is the perception of these brand alliance formations and terminations from the consumer’s perspective. To fill this gap, in the current research, we look at how consumers react to the formation and termination of brand alliances. Specifically, drawing on the recent marketing and psychology literature on brand anthropomorphism, we explore how consumers respond to anthropomorphized brand alliances. Considering both literature on brand anthropomorphism and interpersonal norm, in the current research we hypothesize that consumers will have more positive reactions toward the formation of a brand alliance but more negative reactions toward the termination of a brand alliance, if the brand alliance is anthropomorphized. We further predict that relationship orientation, alliance length, alliance status symmetry, and dimensions of anthropomorphism will moderate the proposed effect. The current research will contribute to the emerging literature on brand alliance, brand anthropomorphism, and customer-brand relationships. It should also have significant implications for marketing practitioners, and help companies strategically manage their communication to consumers. 近年來品牌之間戰略聯盟的興起和終止日趨頻繁。以往相關研究大多著重於研究品牌聯盟興起和終止對於商家策略與運轉的影響。有別於此，在本研究中我們測試將品牌聯盟的興起和終止擬人化是否對消費者行為造成影響。基於品牌和產品擬人化的研究，我們提出消費者會對擬人化的品牌聯盟興起有更正面的態度，而會對擬人化的品牌聯盟終止有更負面的態度。這個現象將會進一步受到品牌關係定位，聯盟時間長度，品牌地位差距，以及品牌擬人化的維度等因素的影響。本研究將不僅增進我們對品牌聯盟，品牌擬人化，和消費者品牌關係的瞭解，而且對廣大商家和市場營銷從業人員具有顯著的實踐意義。

15504617.label: Realisation of objectives
15504617.value: The objectives of this project have been largely completed. Through a series of studies, we investigate how consumers react to the formation and termination of brand alliances. Specifically, we find that consumers have more positive reactions toward the formation of a brand alliance but more negative reactions toward the termination of a brand alliance, if the brand alliance is anthropomorphised. We further find that factors such as power symmetry and alliance length moderate the observed effect. A paper based on this project has been submitted to the Journal of Consumer Research (JCR), and received a revision invitation. In addition, several other related papers partially supported by the grant have been published on top-tier academic journals. For example, one paper has been published on the Journal of Consumer Research (JCR), and the other has been published on the Journal of Personality and Social Psychology (JPSP), both are top-tier journals in the field of marketing and psychology. A third paper has been published on the Journal of Association for Consumer Research (JACR).

15504617.label: Major findings and research outcome
15504617.value: Four papers are yielded from this project with a general focus of the role of psychological factors in consumer judgment and decision making. In the focal paper, we look at how consumers react to the formation and termination of brand alliances. We found that consumers have more positive reactions toward the formation of a brand alliance but more negative reactions toward the termination of a brand alliance, if the brand alliance is anthropomorphised. We further find that factors such as power symmetry and alliance length moderate the observed effect. A paper based on this project has been submitted to the Journal of Consumer Research (JCR), and received a revision invitation. A second paper, published in 2019 on the Journal of Consumer Research (JCR), examines how consumers react to range marketing offers. Eight studies show that reminders of resource scarcity induce a promotion orientation among consumers, which consequently increases consumers’ favorability toward range marketing offers. This effect is found to strengthen when the range of the offer becomes wider, and to weaken when the range offer cannot provide a better-than-reference outcome. A third paper, published in 2019 on the Journal of Personality and Social Psychology (JPSP), examines when and why a threat to self-image influences saving intentions. Data from a set of seven studies, comprising a large-scale survey and 6 experiments, show that when individuals experience a self-image threat, they generate negative expectations about their future. Consequently, these individuals show a greater propensity to save money compared with non-threatened individuals. It’s further observed that the relationship between self-image threat and saving intentions is attenuated under the following conditions: (a) when individuals are induced to adopt positive future expectations; (b) when individuals perceive themselves as having abundant social connections, a perception that buffers their anxiety about the future; or (c) when individuals’ attention is directed, through self-affirmation, to important aspects of their lives that are irrelevant to the threat. The fourth paper, published in 2018 on the Journal of the Association for Consumer Research (JACR), examines how and why consumers’ social relationships influence their attitudes toward probabilistic selling. Four experiments reveal that socially excluded consumers exhibit less favorable attitudes toward probabilistic selling than do their peers who do not feel excluded. This effect is mediated by a thwarted sense of personal control following social exclusion, and the effect diminishes when vivid information about the probabilistic offer is provided.

15504617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15504617.value: As may be evident from the above section, this project is productive and there is great potential for further development of this research. My first priority is to push the brand alliance working paper through the review process and hopefully publish it in the following year. I also plan to further extend findings of some of these published papers and develop new research projects accordingly.

15504617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15504617.value: Despite the increasing prevalence of the formation and termination of brand alliances in today’s business world, research related to this topic is somewhat unilateral. Past research on brand alliance has mostly focused on the reasons leading to the formation and termination of brand alliances and how they influence firms’ strategies and operations. What is largely missing from this literature is the perception of these brand alliance formations and terminations from the consumer’s perspective. To fill this gap, in the current research, we look at how consumers react to the formation and termination of brand alliances. Specifically, drawing on the recent marketing and psychology literature on brand anthropomorphism, we explore how consumers respond to anthropomorphized brand alliances. Adding to both literature on brand anthropomorphism and interpersonal norm, in the current research we find that consumers have more positive reactions toward the formation of a brand alliance but more negative reactions toward the termination of a brand alliance, if the brand alliance is anthropomorphised. We further find that factors such as power symmetry and alliance length moderate the observed effect. The current research contributes to the emerging literature on brand alliance, brand anthropomorphism, and customer-brand relationships. It also has significant implications for marketing practitioners, and help companies strategically manage their communication to consumers.

15505117.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15505117.value: 經濟不確定性與有條件保守會計準則的環球實研究

15505117.label: Project Objectives
15505117.value: To examine the relation between economic uncertainty and conditional accounting conservatism around the world. To investigate how investor protection affects the relation between economic uncertainty and conditional accounting conservatism across countries.
rows: To examine the relation between economic uncertainty and conditional accounting conservatism around the world.
To investigate how investor protection affects the relation between economic uncertainty and conditional accounting conservatism across countries.

15505117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15505117.value: Conditional accounting conservatism, the differential verifiability required for recognition of economic gains versus economic losses, has been a common phenomenon for years. Prior literature has documented that conditional conservatism is mainly generated by contracting, litigation, regulation, and taxation. Recently, a growing literature has explored how differences in institutions and financial structures affect conditional conservatism across countries. The international evidence is in general consistent with the above four explanations of conditional conservatism. A novel feature of this proposal is our investigation of the influence of economic uncertainty on conditional conservatism. Economic uncertainty is naturally a fundamental factor underlying the incentives for financial reporting. For instance, Concepts Statement No. 2, FASB (1980) describes conservatism as a “prudent reaction to uncertainty.” We hypothesize that economic uncertainty increases conditional conservatism. We use a newly developed index on economic policy uncertainty as a measure for economic uncertainty. This index is based on newspaper coverage frequency and it is available for 16 countries including the United States. We conduct our analyses in two stages. First, we examine how economic uncertainty influences conditional conservatism in the U.S. We start our analysis from the U.S. because previous studies mainly focused on this country. We construct country-year measures on conditional conservatism and examine its co-movement with economic uncertainty over time. In the second stage, we extend our analysis to an international setting. Institutions are developed to resolve uncertainty and some institutions are better in reducing economic uncertainty than others. We focus on how a country’s investor protection affects the relation between economic uncertainty and conditional conservatism. We make two contributions. First, we document the relation between economic uncertainty and conditional conservatism around the world. Second, we show how investor protection affects the relation between economic uncertainty and conditional conservatism across countries. Our findings will be useful for researchers in economics and accounting. Our results can also benefit the governments around the world to understand how increases in economic uncertainty affect managers’ decisions such as financial reporting quality. 有條件保守會計準則意指對確認公司經濟收益及損失的會計準則的鬆緊。過往研究指出此鬆緊度與公司契約﹑訴訟風險﹑公司規則及稅制有關。因此不同國家的制度及金融結構會影響該國的有條件保守會計準則。本研究指出一個國家的有條件保守會計準亦受到該國的經濟不確定性影響。當經濟不確定性愈大，會計準則將會愈保守。此研究將會覆蓋十六個國家，當中包括美國及中國。

15506317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15506317.value: Venture capital firms provide equity financing for technology-intensive private companies. They can successfully exit their investments if their portfolio companies have IPOs or are acquired by other companies. The emergence of a secondary market makes it possible for venture capital firms to trade their illiquid shares of private companies, thus providing a third option of exit. We believe that a secondary market will not only affect the returns on venture capital funds and the way they invest, but also serve as a mechanism to uncover the underlying value of their portfolio companies and have an overall positive impact on the venture capital industry. Since the secondary market for venture capital investments emerged in the early 2000s, it has developed at unprecedented speed. However, such phenomenon receives little attention from scholars. The biggest hurdle is the lack of comprehensive data on secondary market transactions. In this proposal, we will take up this challenge and build a comprehensive dataset on secondary venture capital transactions by integrating major databases and hand-collected data. We will then empirically investigate which firms tend to participate in the secondary market and how they perform. We propose that the networks and stage specialization of venture capital firms can have a significant impact on their tendency to participate in the secondary market and the performance of secondary investments. Lastly, we will extend our analysis by relating venture capital firms’ secondary market investments to their network positions and long-term performance. We believe that our research on the secondary market for venture capital investments has the potential to make multiple contributions to the literature. First, we will build a comprehensive dataset on the secondary market for venture capital transactions. Second, our study on the participants and performance of the secondary venture capital market will be new to the literature. Third, we will extend the existing literature on social networks by documenting the role of networks in providing liquidity for network partners. Fourth, our research will provide new insights to the study on the performance of venture capital firms which mainly focuses on IPOs and acquisitions of the portfolio companies. 风险投资公司为科技密集型的私营企业提供股权融资。如果他们的投资组合中的公司上市，或者被其他公司收购的话，他们能够成功的退出投资。二级市场的出现使得风险投资企业能够交易那些流动性很低的私营企业的股份。这成为风险投资公司的第三种退出方式。我们相信这种二级市场不但会影响风险投资基金的回报率和投资方式，而且可以作为一种揭示他们的投资组合中的公司的内在价值的机制，在风险投资行业有积极的整体影响。 自从风险投资的二级市场在2000年左右出现后，它以史无前例的速度发展。然而，这种现象却没有得到研究人员的广泛关注。最大的困难在于缺乏有关二级市场交易的综合数据。在这份研究计划中，我们将解决这个问题。通过结合主要的数据库和手动收集的数据，我们将建立一个有关风险投资二级交易的综合的数据库。然后，我们将实证调查哪些公司会倾向于参与二级市场，以及他们是如何运作的。我们认为，风险投资公司的网络和阶段专业化在他们参与二级市场的意愿以及他们在二级市场的投资表现上有巨大的影响。最后，我们将延伸我们的研究，来分析风险投资公司的二级市场的投资和这些公司在网络中的地位以及长期表现的关系。 我们相信我们有关风险投资的二级市场的研究对文献有多重贡献。第一，我们建立了一个有关风险投资交易的二级市场的综合数据库。第二，我们对二级风险投资市场的参与者和表现的研究是过去的文献中没有的。第三，通过证明社交网络在为参与者提供流动性方面的作用，我们拓展了现有的关于社交网络的文献。第四，目前对风险投资公司的表现的研究主要关注于投资组合中的公司的上市和被收购， 而我们的研究提供了新的见解。

15506417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15506417.value: With an aging population, health care resources are becoming increasingly limited. Governments in many countries are faced with steeply rising health care costs, and patients are experiencing excessively long waiting times. Doctor-shopping behavior among patients, defined as visiting multiple medical practitioners during a single illness episode without referrals, makes the situation even worse. Doctor-shopping behavior is very common in many health care systems. For example, in Hong Kong, the rate of doctor shopping was reported to be as high as 40% in public outpatient clinics (Lo et al., 1994). Repeated consultations and examinations cause unnecessary costs and congestion for health care systems. It is widely believed that cognitive dissonance on certain illness between patients and medical practitioners is the main reason for doctor-shopping behavior by patients. In the proposed project, we aim to comprehensively study doctor shopping with regard to patients and medical practitioners. We plan to capture the doctor-shopping behavior of patients by applying Bayes' rule and derive the numbers of doctor-shopping times for different types of patients. The proposed model can capture the dynamic updating process of patients' illness perceptions after obtaining multiple diagnoses from different doctors. We will also investigate how patients' doctor-shopping times change according to the patient type, which will be classified according to their prior illness perception and diagnostic quality, which will be captured by type I and type II errors in the diagnostic process. With regard to medical practitioners, we will investigate the appropriate length of time they should spend on a diagnosis. We assume the following: the shorter time a medical practitioner spends with patients, the more ambiguity on illness perception and the greater the doctor-shopping rate. A long queue might push doctors to work faster by reducing the consultation time with patients, which can increase the patients' doctor-shopping rate, and, in turn, increase the workload on the health care system. The proposed project aims to study the optimal decision making by doctors regarding service times under both revenue-maximization and welfare-maximization objectives and conduct a comparison between the optimal decisions under these two objectives. Other than the aforementioned objectives, the proposed project also aims to explore the role of pricing in reducing the doctor-shopping rate, as price not only affects doctor-shopping costs but also changes the financial incentives for medical practitioners to adjust their service rates. The outcome of this research can shed light on doctor-shopping behavior and methods to reduce the problem. 随着人口老龄化， 医疗资源变得越发紧张。 政府对上升的医疗成本以及病人们漫长的等待时间束手无策。 病人的医生寻找行为， 定义为在病人对同一个病患来求诊多个医生， 令这个状况恶化。 例如， 香港公立系统的医生寻找行为比例多达40%。 重复求诊和检测浪费了宝贵的医疗资源。 病人和大夫对疾病的认知差异导致了病人的医生寻找行为。 本研究致力于寻求病人的多次求诊的基本动机， 并在次基础上考虑医生的就诊时间和定价方面的决策。本研究计划用贝叶斯推断法来对病人的多次就诊行为来建模。 该模型可以将大夫诊断中的第一类和第二类错误的概率进行定量化。 本研究最后要研究医疗提供者的诊断时间长度的决策。 时间太短不利于病人理解自己的疾病状况， 从而导致更多的医生寻找行为， 这种行为反过来又导致系统更加拥挤。 因此， 从社会福利最大化角度， 存在最优的诊断时间决策。

15506417.label: Realisation of objectives
15506417.value: The five objectives are fully achieved. The details are listed as follows. Objective 1. To formulate patients' doctor-shopping strategies by adopting the Bayes' rule. This is well achieved, and I have adopted an economics utility model to capture patients’ perception on their illness and use Bayesian updating mechanism to allow them to update their beliefs based on diagnosis results in the doctor-shopping process. Objective 2: To understand how doctor-shopping behaviour affects the workload of medical practitioners using a queueing model. This is fully achieved. I have used queueing network to model the equilibrium customer choice among different doctors and derive the equilibrium behaviour of the system. Objective 3: To conduct a sensitivity analysis of doctor-shopping times with respect to patient type (captured by the patient's perception of prior illnesses) and the quality of the diagnostic process (captured by type I and II errors). This is fully achieved. I found that the diagnosis accuracy plays a key role in determining the effect of doctor shopping on social welfare. Objective 4: To investigate the influence of the service time (i.e., time spend on the consultation and diagnosis) on doctor-shopping rates. This is fully achieved. With the queueing model, the system congestion is captured by the expected waiting time in the queueing system. Customers take such cost into consideration and make decision based on their overall utility. When the service time is long, the system is very congested which reduces the doctor-shopping rate. Objective 5: To investigate the influence of optimal pricing decisions by the medical practitioner on doctor-shopping behavior. This is fully achieved. Using a high price can determine doctor-shopping behaviour. In a more general model with uninformed customers who follow online rating information, I found that the manager can even use cyclic pricing (change price to be high or low periodically) can help to increase their profit.

For example, when customers do doctor-shopping, they look at the rating of doctors online and pick up one. 15506417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15506417.value: When a patient's illness perception is inconsistent with a doctor's diagnosis, she may seek opinions from multiple doctors without referrals, a behavior called doctor shopping. Shall such behavior be encouraged or discouraged? This is an important question for the healthcare regulators. In this project, we model and derive patients’ optimal doctor shopping decisions. After each visit, patients update their beliefs about their health status following the Bayes’ rule. Our main finding is that the patients’ doctor shopping decisions are critically affected by the diagnosis accuracy, the relative value of identifying a severely ill patient, and the cost per visit. We find that allowing patients to conduct doctor shopping exacerbates the system congestion (congestion effect), but it can help those patients who have decided to join obtain a higher reward (reward effect). The key finding is that there exists a diagnosis accuracy threshold above which allowing doctor shopping incurs a welfare loss and below which allowing doctor shopping improves welfare. Our results provide strong insights on understanding why doctor shopping should be encouraged for the critical illness such as breast cancer.

15507117.value: 金融的一个核心问题是股票流动性是否有实际影响。股票流动性有实际影响的一个潜在渠道是, 股票流动性可能会降低公司的资本成本, 因为理论表明, 在似是而非的假设下, 投资者预期持有更多流动性股票的回报率会较低, 这就形成了流动资金溢价的概念。对流动性溢价概念的实证有效性进行了巨大的努力。然而, 投资者的预期回报是观测的。因此, 所有的实证研究都利用未来实现的回报作为预期回报的代表。现有的实证研究普遍发现股票流动性与未来实现收益之间存在负相关关系。人们倾向于解释股票流动性与未来实现收益之间的负相关关系, 作为流动性溢价概念的佐证。 我们认为, 由于两个原因, 我们无法从股票流动性与未来实现收益之间的估计关系中得出流动性溢价概念的经验有效性的确定性推论。第一个原因是, 未来实现回报的一个可衡量的组成部分反映了对事前错误定价的修正。未来实现收益的错误定价修正部分与预期收益无关。第二个原因是股票流动性和错误定价 (即低估或高估) 的程度是负相关的。因此, 股票流动性与未来实现收益的估计关系, 可以说反映了股票流动性与投资者预期收益的关系, 以及股票流动性与未来实现收益的错误定价修正分量之间的关系。 股票流动性与被低估 (高估) 股票未来实现收益的错误定价修正部分有关, 因为较高的股票流动性与较低的事前低估 (高估) 有关。股票流动性与未来实现收益的错误定价校正部分之间的关系表明了一个可测试的假设。即股票流动性与未来实现收益之间的估计关系随着比较高估的观测值进入估计样本而增加。 在这项研究中, 我们尝试使用包括美国数据在内的国际数据来检验假说。如果我们发现与假设相符的证据, 我们就会知道, 股票流动性与未来实现收益之间的估计关系, 是对股票流动性与预期收益之间关系的潜在偏颇估计。此外, 如果我们发现, 股票流动性和未来实现的回报率之间的估计关系, 从消极到积极的, 当我们移动的估计从一个样本相对较低估的观察对于一个比较高估的样本, 我们知道, 股票流动性与未来实现收益的错误定价修正分量的关系, 超过了股票流动性与预期收益之间的关系。因此, 我们知道, 我们没有办法从股票流动性与未来实现收益的经验关系中推断出流动性溢价概念的实证有效性
