15507217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15507217.value: Customers and suppliers have strong economic links. A customer's disclosure often contains material information about its suppliers' business performance and prospects. Leuz and Wysocki (2016) call for research into market-wide effects of disclosure and reporting activities. Existing research in this area focuses on information spillover effects of earnings announcement, restatements, and misreporting. Externalities on the disclosure choice of management forecasts is relatively unexplored. This study aims to test whether and how customers’ disclosures (both mandatory and voluntary) affect its suppliers’ management forecasts. Specifically, we ask the following questions. Does a customer’s disclosure have any impact on the disclosure choice of its suppliers' management forecasts? Would a customer’s disclosure affect the accuracy or value relevance of its suppliers’ management forecasts? How would a supplier's management forecasts be different if all of its major customers are government entities? Customers' disclosures may affect a supplier's management forecasts for at least two reasons. First, management forecasts can reduce information asymmetry among investors. If customers' disclosures stimulate private information collection, information asymmetry among investors will increase because of investor heterogeneity, which could prompt the supplier's management to issue forecasts. Second, if customer's disclosures contain bad news, a supplier's management have incentives to quickly incorporate the negative information into its earnings forecasts. By doing so, they can attribute bad performance to external factors and avoid potential litigations against dissatisfying investors. If suppliers issue management forecasts in response to customers' disclosures, the latter is likely to affect suppliers' forecasts in several ways. We expect that a supplier's management forecast is more precise, more accurate, and less value relevant if it closely follows a major customer's disclosure. In addition, while publicly listed firms are required to report their performance to outside investors periodically, government entities are not subject to such disclosure requirements. We compare the suppliers whose major customers include public firms with the suppliers whose major customers are government entities only. We expect the first group’s management forecasts to be more precise, more accurate, and less value relevant than the second group’s forecasts. This study will provide new empirical evidence on the externalities of corporate disclosure along the supply chain. It builds on the extensive literature of management earnings forecasts and contributes to the emerging literature on the effects of corporate disclosure on managerial behavior. Though we analyze the U.S. data in this study, the findings will have implications for regulators and investors in other countries. 供應商和客戶之間有著緊密相連的商業關系。客戶的信息披露往往包含有關供應商的經營活動和前景的實質性內容。Leuz和Wysocki (2016)呼吁學術界更多地關注和研究信息披露對整個市場的影響。這個領域的研究集中在盈利公告，修正公告以及披露錯誤的溢出效應。這些信息披露如何影響管理層的盈利預測還沒有研究過。 這個研究項目著眼於檢驗客戶的披露（無論是監管要求的和自發的）如何影響供應商的管理層盈利預測。具體而言，我們希望回答以下問題。客戶的披露是否影響供應商的管理層盈利預測的方式？客戶的披露是否影響供應商的管理層盈利預測的准確性和相關性？隻為政府供貨的供應商在管理層盈利預測是否有所不同？ 客戶的信息披露會影響供應商的管理層盈利預測有兩方面的原因。第一，管理層的盈利預測能夠降低投資者之間的信息不對稱性。如果客戶的信息披露促使投資者去收集更多的信息，由於投資者收集和分析信息的能力各不相同，他們之間的信息不對稱性會進一步增加。這種情況下，管理層可以通過盈利預測來緩解這種不對稱性。第二，如果客戶的信息披露包含負面的消息，供應商的管理層可以通過盈利預測來告知投資者這一負面消息將如何影響公司的盈利。這樣做能夠幫助管理層將負面影響歸咎於外部因素，從而降低被不滿的投資者起訴的風險。 對於供應商在客戶披露信息之后發布的管理層盈利預測，我們做出以下假設。緊隨在客戶的信息披露之后的盈利預測會有更高的精度，更接近實際的盈利，但是對供應商的股票價格的影響相對較小。此外，上市公司必須定期向外部投資者發布業績報告，而政府部門則沒有這樣的要求。我們比較兩類供應商，一類是有上市公司為主要客戶的供應商，另一類是隻為政府供貨的供應商。我們的假設是第一類的盈利預測會比第二類的盈利預測有更高的精度，更接近實際的盈利，但是對股票價格的影響相對較小。 這個研究項目將對信息披露在供應鏈公司之間的溢出效應提供新的實証結果。本項目建立於對管理層盈利預測的大量研究的基礎之上，與信息披露如何影響管理層的行為這一新興領域密切相關。雖然我們計劃用美國的數據進行研究，我們相信研究結果對其它國家的市場監管者和投資者都會有借鑒價值。

15507217.label: Realisation of objectives
15507217.value: For research objective #2, we examine whether and how the type of a major customer, specifically, government entities versus exchange-listed companies, affects the properties of a supplier's management earnings forecasts. We posit that business transactions with government entities have unique features that improve the quality of government suppliers’ management earnings forecasts. First, unlike corporations, government entities are much less likely to default or declare bankruptcy. They tend to offer longer-term procurement contracts, which lowers the risk of switching suppliers. When the uncertainty about future customer demand is low, suppliers are able to plan and undertake customer-specific investments more efficiently. Second, firms contracting with government customers tend to face less competition in the product market and generate a large portion of their revenues from non-competitive procurement contracts. Third, government agencies follow a standard procurement process regulated by the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) and require comprehensive information to assess whether a supplier has adequate financial resources to deliver the goods and services as expected. In order to meet the information demand by government procurement, government suppliers are likely to have a more efficient internal information process. We collected supplier-customer relationship data from the Compustat Segment database. The Financial Accounting Standards Board’s (FASB) new segment reporting standard was issued in June 1997 and became effective for financial statements for periods beginning after December 15, 1997. Hence, we begin our sample period from the fiscal year ending in 1998. The database classifies each customer into seven categories: ‘GOVDOM’, ‘GOVSTATE’, ‘GOVLOC’, ‘COMPANY’, ‘GEOREG’, ‘MARKET’, and ‘GOVFRN’. We classify a supplier as corporate supplier if the firm reports only sales to major customers in the ‘COMPANY’ category in three years consecutively. We classify a supplier as government supplier if the firm reports only sales to major customers in the ‘GOVDOM’, ‘GOVSTATE’ and ‘GOVLOC’ categories in three years consecutively. We obtained management forecasts of quarterly earnings from the IBES Earnings Guidance database. For each management earnings forecast (MEF), we calculated its precision, accuracy, and price impact. We followed prior studies to measure forecast precision as the negative of the difference between the upper and the lower end of a range forecast, scaled by the beginning-of-quarter stock price, or zero for a point forecast. We measured forecast accuracy by the absolute forecast error, that is, the absolute value of the difference between actual earnings and the forecast value, scaled by the beginning-of-quarter stock price. For a range forecast, the forecast value is equal to its midpoint. We measured the price impact by the market adjusted cumulative abnormal returns in the four-day [-2, 1] window around the forecast release day (i.e., day 0). In addition, we measured the information content in a management forecast by the difference between the forecast value and the median of analysts’ earnings forecasts as of the day prior to the release of the management forecast. We obtained analyst forecasts from the IBES Detailed Analyst Forecast database. Our empirical results show that firms whose major customers are government entities (i.e., government suppliers) issue more precise and more accurate management earnings forecasts than firms whose major customers are public companies (i.e., corporate suppliers). Moreover, when managers disclose negative information to the market, earnings forecasts issued by government suppliers have greater price impact than those issued by corporate suppliers. Overall, our results support that government entities being a major customer positively influence the quality of a supplier firm's voluntary disclosure. The findings are published in the journal paper by Cheng, Huang, and Zhang (2020). For research objectives #1 and #3, after we collected the data and did some preliminary analysis, we encountered the difficulty that few suppliers issue management earnings forecasts within the first two weeks after customers' earnings announcements or management earnings forecasts. Suppliers often issue management earnings forecasts before their own earnings announcements rather than in response to customers' mandatory or voluntary disclosure. Because the sample of suppliers' management earnings forecasts within the first two weeks after their customers' mandatory or voluntary disclosure is small, we decided to use the data we collected to study how customers' earnings announcements influence investors expectation of suppliers' future volatility in the equity option market. While a large literature has examined many topics on volatility, there is lack of empirical evidence on how information about one stock’s future volatility is transferred to other related stocks. The supply chain setting offers an ideal setting to study the effect of cross-firm volatility information transfer because customers and suppliers are closely related. Earnings announcements may have a different impact on the expected volatility of stock return in the short term (i.e. the short-term expected volatility), the expected volatility of stock return in the long term (i.e., the long-term expected volatility), and the expected volatility of the stock return in a time window with a starting point in the future (i.e., the forward expected volatility), respectively. We show analytically that while the change of the short-term and long-term expected volatility is subject to a negative bias, the change of the forward expected volatility is an unbiased measure of the new volatility information. To empirically quantify the changes in the short-term, long-term, and forward expected volatilities after earnings announcement, we apply the model free implied volatility (MFIV) method. MFIV is derived from multiple option prices across a wide range of strike prices, which is important in our study because stock price reaction to earnings announcements may cause an at-the-money option to become out-of-the-money or in-the-money after the announcement. We start our empirical analysis by examining the changes in the short-term, long-term, and forward expected volatilities of both the announcing customers and its suppliers around the customers’ earnings announcement. We find that the short-term expected volatility, on average, drops substantially for the announcing customers, but experiences a small increase for the suppliers. The forward expected volatility, on average, remains almost the same for both the announcing customers and its suppliers. We investigate the effect of volatility information transfer from customers’ earnings announcement to suppliers by estimating the regression models with the change of a supplier’s short-term, long-term, or forward expected volatility being the dependent variable. The key independent variables are the changes of the announcing customer’s short-term, long-term, and forward expected volatility. We include the contemporary change of the VIX index to control for the market-wide volatility factor and the event-window stock returns of both the announcing customer and its supplier to control for the effect of stock return spillover. We find that the change of the customer’s forward (short-term) volatility has a positive and significant coefficient in the regression model of its supplier’s forward (short-term) volatility. We also examine how the effect of volatility information transfer varies with the strength of the economic link between a customer and its suppliers. We use three measures to quantify the customer-supplier economic link: the sales to a customer as the percentage of the supplier’s total sales, the correlation coefficient of their daily stock returns, and the correlation coefficient of their squared daily stock returns. Subsample analysis shows that the effect is stronger when the customer and its supplier are more closely related. The findings are reported in the working paper by Huang, Li, and Zhang (2021), which is under review in Management Science.

15507217.label: Major findings and research outcome
15507217.value: The paper we have published in Frontiers of Business Research in China, i.e., Cheng, Huang, and Zhang (2020) examines whether customer base composition in the U.S., i.e., whether a firm’s major customers comprise of government entities or publicly traded companies, affects the properties of supplier’s management earnings forecasts. We find that firms whose major customers are government entities (i.e., government suppliers) issue more precise and more accurate management earnings forecasts than firms whose major customers are public companies (i.e., corporate suppliers). Moreover, when managers disclose negative information to the market, earnings forecasts issued by government suppliers have greater price impact than those issued by corporate suppliers. Our empirical results show that government entities being a major customer have a positive effect on the quality of a supplier firm's voluntary disclosure. The paper we have written and is currently under review in Management Science, i.e., Huang, Li, and Zhang (2021) investigates whether and how information about one stock’s future volatility is transferred to other related stocks along the supply chain. The supply chain setting offers an ideal setting to study the effect of cross-firm volatility information transfer because customers and suppliers are closely related. Earnings announcements may have a different impact on the expected volatility of stock return in the short term (i.e. the short-term expected volatility), the expected volatility of stock return in the long term (i.e., the long-term expected volatility), and the expected volatility of the stock return in a time window with a starting point in the future (i.e., the forward expected volatility), respectively. We show analytically how the changes of the long-term, short-term, and forward expected volatilities after an earnings announcement are related. We find that while the change of the short-term and long-term expected volatility is subject to the negative bias that is caused by the inflated volatility of the announcement day stock return, the change of the forward expected volatility is an unbiased measure of the new volatility information. Empirically, we find that, on average, the announcing firms’ short-term expected volatility decreases substantially after earnings announcements, while the change of their forward expected volatility is close to zero. Regression analysis shows that the change of the announcing firm’s short-term (forward) volatility has a positive and significant effect on the change of its supply chain partner’s short-term (forward) volatility. The effect is economically meaningful and becomes stronger if customers and suppliers are more closely related.

15507217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15507217.value: Our first study shows how firms with different type of major customers exhibit different properties in the information they voluntarily disclose to the capital market. The recent literature document evidence on managerial self-interests that influence the issuance and quality of management earnings forecasts. For example, managers guide investor expectations, time the issuance of management forecasts strategically, and bundle management forecasts with earnings announcements. Further research is required to explore whether contracting with government entities helps to alleviate the influence of such self-centered managerial motives on management earnings forecasts. In our second study on the effect of volatility information transfer along the supply chain, we point out that earnings announcements may have a different impact on the short-term, long-term, and forward expected volatility, respectively. We show analytically how the changes of the long-term, short-term, and forward expected volatilities after an earnings announcement are related. We find that while the change of the short-term and long-term expected volatility is subject to a negative bias, the change of the forward expected volatility is an unbiased measure of the new volatility information. We intend to continue with this line of research to study volatility information transfer across stocks around other important corporate events.

15507217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15507217.value: With the financial support of the research project No. 15507217, we completed two studies in the supply chain setting. The first study contributes to our understanding of the influence of government entities being a major customer on their suppliers. Previous studies show that the U.S. federal government spending constitutes about 20% of the U.S. GDP in the past four decades and that government customers account for 33.3% of their suppliers' total sales. We find there is a positive impact of major government customers on the quality of their suppliers' management earnings forecasts. The potential channel of this effect is that contracting with the government improves a supplier's internal information process. The second study empirically investigates how corporate customers’ quarterly earnings announcements affect their suppliers’ expected volatility, and vice versa. Prior studies mainly focus on the stock return spillover effect. There is lack of empirical evidence on how information about one stock’s future volatility is transferred to other related stocks. We document evidence on the effect of volatility information transfer both upstream and downstream along the supply chain. Moreover, our research methodology can be extended to studying volatility information transfer across stocks around other important corporate events.

15507617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15507617.value: This project aims to provide evidence on the causal impact of limited attention on investors’ processing of earnings information. An important feature of this study is the setting of breaking news as a source of plausibly exogenous variation in investor attention. A growing literature in finance and accounting studies how investors’ attention affects their information processing in the financial markets. Using Google searches during the IPO filing period to measure retail investor attention to IPO firms, Da, Engelberg, and Gao (2011) find that high levels of such searches are related both to higher initial returns and to more long-term underperformance. Liu, Sherman, and Zhang (2014) suggest that media coverage is more likely to be a measure of institutional investors’ attention and find that pre-IPO media coverage of an IPO firm is positively related to the stock’s long-term value, liquidity, analyst coverage, and institutional investor ownership. In understanding the evidence on the impact of investor attention, a matter of critical importance is the source of the variation in investor attention. In order to draw causal interpretations, ideally one needs to have a significant portion of the variation in investor attention to be plausibly exogenous (Tetlock, 2014). One source of such exogenous variation in investor attention, initially proposed by Liu, Sherman, and Zhang (2014) and further corroborated by studies such as Bajo, Chemmanur, Simonyan, Tehranian (2016) and Chemmanur, Krishnan, and Yu (2016), is the special news reports (breaking news) broadcast on the three U.S. television networks (ABC, NBC, and CBS). In general, these news reports were about exogenous events that drew investors’ attention away the financial markets. For example, in the year of 1981, regular television programming was interrupted by many specials because of the Iran hostages, the assassination of Anwar Sadat, and the attempted assassinations of the Pope and Ronald Reagan. In this project, using the breaking news as a plausibly exogenous source of investor attention, we will provide evidence on how investors react to corporate earnings announcements. We predict that, as investor attention is diverted by breaking news, the stock market will be relatively slow in processing information and therefore will underreact to earnings announcement. We also hypothesize that such under-reaction driven by breaking news will be more pronounced if the breaking news is more eye-catching, if the location of the breaking news event is close to a financial center, or if the firm announcing earnings is relatively small. 該項目旨在提供有關注意力因果影響的證據投資者處理收益信息。這項研究的一個重要特徵是將突發新聞設定為投資者合理外生變化的來源注意。 財務和會計研究方面日益增長的文獻如何影響投資者的注意力他們在金融市場的信息處理。在此期間使用Google搜索首次公開招股時間來衡量零售投資者對IPO公司的關注，Da et al.（2011）發現，高水平的這種搜索與較高的初始度相關回報和更長期的表現不佳。Liu et al.（2014）建議媒體報導更有可能成為機構投資者的衡量標準注意並發現上市前媒體對IPO公司的報導正面相關股票的長期價值，流動性，分析師覆蓋面和機構投資者所有權。 在理解有關投資者關注影響的證據方面，至關重要重要性是投資者關注的變化的根源。為了畫因果解釋，理想情況下，需要有很大的變化投資者註意合理的外生（Tetlock，2014）。這樣的一個來源投資者關注的外生變化，由Liu et al.(2014)提出，並進一步證實了Bajo et al.（2016）和Chemmanur et al.（2016年）都是特別的新聞報導（ABC，NBC和CBS）在美國三大電視台（美國廣播公司，NBC和CBS）上播出（最新消息）。一般來說，這些新聞報導涉及外部事件，注意金融市場。例如，在1981年，定期由於伊朗人質，電視節目被許多特別節目打斷，暗殺安瓦爾·薩達特，以及暗殺了教皇和羅納德·裡根 在這個項目中，將突發新聞作為投資者的外生來源注意，我們將提供投資者如何對企業盈利做出反應的證據公告。我們預測，隨著投資者的注意力被突發新聞所轉移，因此，加工信息的股票市場將會相對較慢盈利公告反應不力。我們也假設這種不足的反應如果突發新聞更加眼光，推動突發新聞更加顯著，如果突發新聞事件的位置靠近金融中心，或者如果該公司宣布盈利相對較小。

15507617.label: Realisation of objectives
15507617.value: The objective of research project has been full realized. We have conducted corresponding analyses. The analyses have been incorporated into the paper titled “The Role of Stock Returns in CEO Performance Evaluation: A New Interpretation”, co-authored with Sudarshan Jayaraman (Wesray Professor of Business Administration, University of Rochester, U.S.A.), Joanna S. Wu (Susanna and Evans Y. Lam Professor of Business Administration, University of Rochester, U.S.A.), and Xiaoxu Ling (former PhD student at Hong Kong Polytechnic University). The paper is currently under Revise & Resubmit at The Accounting Review (A* journal, included in UTD journal list). In this paper, we show that institutional investor attention has a causal impact on corporate policies. Specifically, we show that, when institutional investor attention is abnormally low due to exogenous shocks that are unrelated to their stock portfolio firms, they pay less effort in monitoring their stock portfolio firms, which results a lower efficiency in the compensation policies at these firms. The measure of the efficiency of compensation policies, which is also newly developed in the paper, is the sensitivity of CEO compensation to fundamental information-based stock returns relative to other stock returns. To measure fundament information-based stock returns, we utilize the Capital IQ’s Key Developments database and identify the dates of events that are both related to corporate fundamentals and under the control of the management; we calculate cumulative stock return over short windows around such events. Overall, in a large sample of CEO compensation, we show that, in the absence of institutional investor attention shock, the sensitivity of CEO compensation to fundamental information-based stock returns is significantly higher than that to other stock returns. In contrast, when institutional investor attention is low due to exogenous shocks, the sensitivity of CEO compensation to fundamental information-based stock returns is no longer higher than that to other stock returns, i.e., the compensation weight is the same irrespective of the nature and relevance of the different components of stock return performance. Thus, our analyses suggest that institutional investor attention affects their monitoring efficiency, which in turn affects the efficiency of CEO compensation contracting. This paper contributes to the literatures on investor attention, investor monitoring efficiency, and compensation contracting. Our findings will also be interesting to financial market investors, corporate governance activists, and regulatory agencies.

15509117.value: 公司能否打破投资者对于股价52周高点的锚定偏差?

15509117.label: Project Objectives
15509117.value: We plan to examine our conjecture that the 52-week high anchoring bias motivates firms to split their stocks. Our conjecture predicts that firms whose stock prices rise to near their 52-week highs are more likely to split their stocks, and that, prior to stock splits, firms suffer from the 52-week high anchoring bias. We propose to test our conjecture that stock splits, which attract new investors and induce more information production, can mitigate the anchoring bias. That is, the anchoring bias would be less severe in the post-split period than in the pre-split period. We expect to see that, in general, the market is more efficient in the post-split period than in the pre-split period. Consequently, we expect that post-split stock prices are more informative in reflecting firms’ earnings information than their pre-split counterparts.

15509117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15509117.value: When a firm’s stock price rises to its past 52-week high, investors may perceive it as having reflected available information and relatively “overvalued.” This perception may make investors reluctant to buy the stock (even if the firm has good prospects), and cause its price to sluggishly adjust to new information. Indeed, George and Hwang (2004) show that investors tend to anchor stocks’ 52-week highs in making investment decisions, and that the anchoring bias leads to undervaluation that persists for some time. George, Hwang, and Li (2015) and Birru (2015) further find that the nearness of stock prices to their past 52-week highs induces underreaction to earnings announcements, causing the post-earnings announcement drifts (PEAD). These studies highlight the formidable role of the anchoring bias in affecting the stock price behavior. The question we are interested in is: How would good firms whose stock prices have risen to near their past 52-week highs deal with the anchoring bias? While they may disclose more information, the effect could be limited because their investors may perceive that the information was already impounded into the stock prices. Alternatively, we conjecture that, to overcome the undervaluation problem induced by the anchoring bias, good firms may split their stocks to attract new investors and induce more information production about their fundamental values. According to Brennan and Hughes (1991), brokerage houses have incentives to produce research reports on firms with low share prices because the brokerage commission rates are inversely related to share prices. By increasing the number of shares outstanding, a stock split automatically lowers the stock price level and induces more analyst coverage on the firm, revealing more information to investors. Chemmanur et al. (2014) test this information production theory and find that, indeed, stock splits induce brokerage firms to produce more information, and that institutional investors obtain the produced information and become better informed about the fundamental values of the split firms. While undervalued firms have incentives to induce more information production, the literature has not identified what may cause split firms to be undervalued. We conjecture that the anchoring bias may play an important role in causing the undervaluation associated with split firms. Thus, we propose to test our conjecture that the 52-week high anchoring bias motivates firms to split their stocks. This conjecture may help resolve the puzzle why firms split their stocks. 当一个公司股价攀升至过去52周高点的时候，投资者可能会认为该股价已经反应现有信息并且相对的被高估了。这种看法会使投资者犹豫是否购买该股票（即使该公司有很高的前景）， 进而导致股价对新信息的调整变得缓慢。事实上，George and Hwang (2004) 确实发现投资者在进行投资决策时倾向于锚定股价的52周高点，而且此锚定偏差会使股价低估持续一段时间。George, Hwang, and Li (2015) 和 Birru (2015) 进一步发现股价接近52周高点会引发投资者对盈余宣告的不充分反应，造成盈余惯性。这些研究凸显了锚定偏差在影响股价行为上的强大作用。我们所感兴趣的问题则是： 当股价攀升到52周高点的时候，优质公司如何应对锚定偏差？ 尽管这些优质公司可能会披露更多的信息，但是这样做的效果是有限的，因为这些公司的投资者会认为信息已经都反应到了股价中。我们推测还有另外一种可能。为了克服锚定偏差引发的价值低估问题，优质的公司会分割股票来吸引新的投资者进而引起更多关于基本面信息的创造。 根据Brennan and Hughes (1991)，因为经纪佣金率跟股价成反向关系，所以证券经纪商有动机去生产关于低股价公司的研究报告。通过增加股票的数量，股票分割自动的降低股价水平进而引起更多分析师关注，揭露更多信息给投资者。Chemmanur et al. (2014) 检验了信息创造理论并且发现股票分割确实引起证券经纪商创造更多的信息，并且机构投资者获得了创造的信息进而对股票分割公司的基本面价值变得更加了解。尽管被低估的公司有动机去引发更多的信息创造，但是文献并没有发现什么会导致股票分割公司被低估。我们推测锚定偏差会对股票分割公司被低估起到重要作用。 因此，我们计划检验我们的推测（i）52周高点的锚定偏差会激励公司分割股票且（ii）股票分割创造的信息会使股票分割的公司缓解投资者52周高点的锚定偏差。

15509117.label: Realisation of objectives
15509117.value: I am pleased to report we have completed the three objectives. For the first objective, we collected a sample of 11,623 stock splits from the Center for Research in Security Prices (CRSP) database with a declaration date between 1962 and 2017, and find evidence that the 52-week high anchoring bias motivates U.S. firms to split their stocks. Consistent with our conjecture, our findings show that firms whose stock prices rise to near their 52-week highs are more likely to split their stocks. Furthermore, using the mispricing score of Stambaugh, Yu, and Yuan (2015), we find that among firms subject to investors’ 52-week high anchoring bias, those with higher profitability but greater undervaluation are more likely to split their stocks. This result helps explain why the market tends to react positively to split announcements (e.g., Grinblatt, Masulis, and Titman, 1984). For the second objective, we first verify the presumption that stock splits attract market attention and induce information production by showing that EDGAR downloads, analyst coverage, and the number of analyst reports all increase following stock splits by firms with stock prices near their 52-week highs. This result provides the prerequisite for stock splits to be useful in resolving the undervaluation problems induced by investors’ 52-week high anchoring bias. Moreover, firms that choose to split their stocks when their stock prices are near their 52-week highs are more undervalued than their non-split counterparts before the split. We also find evidence that the undervaluation associated with anchoring bias gradually disappears after stock splits. Thus, by attracting new investors and inducing more information production, stock splits mitigate the 52-week-high anchoring bias. Consistent with the third objective, we find that the likelihood of stock splits increases with CEO wealth-performance sensitivity, and firms’ investment-price sensitivity increases after stock splits. Specifically, Jayaraman and Milbourn (2012) argue that “when stock prices are more informative to investors in the market, they are also assumed to be more informative about the manager’s actions and thus more useful for contracting purposes.” Their argument implies that when anchoring bias distorts stock prices, it reduces the effectiveness of using equity-based compensation to incentivize managers. Hence, we expect more firms with a higher CEO wealth-performance sensitivity to split their stocks when their price nears the 52-week high, and we find consistent results. Moreover, increased investor attention and greater information production concerning the split firms should make their stock prices more informative. Improved price informativeness could lead to better corporate resource allocation via managerial learning from the stock market (see, e.g., Subrahmanyam and Titman, 2001; Chen, Goldstein, and Jiang, 2007). As expected, we observe an increase in investment sensitivity to stock price following stock splits for firms subject to investors’ 52-week high anchoring bias. Collectively, our findings suggest that firms have incentives to use stock splits to correct the price distortion induced by investors’ 52-week high anchoring bias and enhance the informational role of stock prices.

15509117.label: Major findings and research outcome
15509117.value: I am glad to report that this project has generated a working paper, "Behavioral Bias, Distorted Stock Prices, and Stock Splits." Here are the summary of the major findings: Studies show that investors’ anchoring bias associated with past 52-week highs of firms’ stock prices leads to undervaluation. We propose that the resulting price distortion misguides managerial incentives and resource allocation, and motivates managers to split stocks (to induce more analyst coverage and attract more investors). Indeed, we find that firms are more likely to split stocks when subject to the anchoring bias, especially when having higher profitability but undervalued. Furthermore, the likelihood of stock splits increases with CEO wealth-performance sensitivity, and firms’ investment-price sensitivity increases after stock splits. Our findings provide a rationale and managerial incentives for stock splits.

15509117.value: We have received comments and suggestions after presenting at two conferences and submitting to top finance journals. We are revising the working paper to incorporated the comments and suggestions, and will get it published in a good academic journal.

15509117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15509117.value: Several well-known firms, including Apple, Tesla, and Nvidia, recently announced to split their stocks, raising public interest in the age-old debate of why firms split their stocks. While many theories have been proposed in the literature, in practice the split announcements generally indicate that stock splits are intended to make stock ownership accessible to a wider base of investors. In this study, we offer a new perspective on the debate by showing that firms can split their shares to correct undervaluation and price distortion caused by investors’ behavioral biases.

15509217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15509217.value: Many U.S. companies disclose non-GAAP financial measures. Managers suggest that these disclosures are useful while the media continues criticizing managers’ self-interest motives. To improve the credibility of such disclosures, SEC issued Regulation G (effective March, 2003) to require firms to provide a reconciliation between the disclosed non-GAAP financial measures and the most directly comparable GAAP financial measures. This regulation at first reduced the number of firms that reported non-GAAP financial measures; however, studies report that the non-GAAP financial measures have increased significantly in recent years. An interesting phenomenon is that firms differ significantly in their disclosure details ranging from a few lines to a full set of financial statements for reconciliation. In providing reconciliation disclosures when firms choose to report non-GAAP earnings, managers have to make decisions on the details of reconciliation. More disclosures can be costly and can be risky. However, more disclosures can also be beneficial. I will investigate two competing hypotheses. First, detailed disclosures could be informative, especially if the market’s demand for such information is high (the informative disclosure hypothesis). Second, detailed disclosures can be opportunistic; as firms have to comply with Regulation G and provide reconciliation information, they can choose to provide more information to “window-dress” the credibility of the non-GAAP information (the opportunistic disclosure hypothesis). I will first develop measures of total non-GAAP disclosures in the 8-K filings and then evaluate the relation between these measures and market return variations. Previous research investigating usefulness of non-GAAP earnings examines how the market responds to the reported non-GAAP earnings; however, this methodology cannot be applied to the total non-GAAP disclosures. I propose two market-based measures: price asynchronicity and future price crash risk. Price asynchronicity (a firm-specific information measure) tests if the market responds more to voluminous disclosures. Future price crash risk (resulted from past over-valuation due to bad news hoarding) tests if previous voluminous non-GAAP disclosures were informative or opportunistic. I will also add control variables and use the propensity score matching method to control for endogeneity. Cross-sectional analyses based on management incentive and information uncertainty will also be conducted to corroborate my findings. My proposal shall shed light on the role of non-GAAP disclosures in the capital market which can help regulators and standard setters in evaluating the regulations and standards regarding these disclosures.

15600717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15600717.value: General fatigue with non-specific causes is prevalent among frail older people. Although the evidence suggests that general fatigue is a strong indicator of rapid ageing, leading to frailty and disability, general fatigue is under-recognized and under-treated in gerontological care. Exercise and Behavioural Change Enhancement (BCE) have been shown to be effective at improving disease-induced fatigue, but their effect on general fatigue among frail older people is not known. This project aims to investigate the effects of an individualized exercise programme with and without BCE strategies for community-dwelling frail older people with general fatigue, so as to reduce their fatigue and improve their physical endurance, exercise self-efficacy, and habitual physical activity, while reducing their symptoms of frailty. In this three-arm, single-blinded, cluster-randomized controlled trial, 285 community-dwelling older people with general fatigue will be recruited from twelve district community health centres. Each centre will be randomized to one of the three study groups: the combined (COMB) group, receiving the 16-week combined intervention consisting of individualized exercise training and BCE programmes plus two booster sessions at 2 and 6 months after the programme; the exercise (EXER) group, receiving exercise training and health talks only; or the control group, receiving health talks only. Participants from each centre will be placed in their centre’s corresponding group to avoid ‘contamination’ effects across participants. We hypothesize that the COMB group will achieve a significantly greater reduction in fatigue and a greater improvement in their physical endurance, exercise self-efficacy, and habitual physical activity, and a significantly greater reduction in their frailty symptoms, when compared with the EXER and control groups at 1 week and 6 and 12 months after completing the interventions. Semi-structured focus group interviews with 30 COMB participants (4-6 per group) will be conducted after the first post-test. Content analysis of the interview data will be used to identify the participants' perceptions of the benefits, weaknesses, and difficulties of participation/adherence in the combed intervention, and the therapeutic components of the combined interventions. Based on the intention-to-treat principle, A mixed-effects modelling technique will be used to compare changes in all of outcome variables at the three post-tests between the three groups, followed by the Helmert contrasts test (if any outcome results are found to be significant). This study will be a pioneering interventional study on how general fatigue among frail older people can be managed and how fatigue-related frailty can be prevented. 本研究旨在評估個人化運動計劃伴隨 “增進行為改善策略”對在社區生活的體弱長者改善一般疲倦徵狀之成效 體弱長者在沒有明顯原因下出現疲倦徵狀的情況普遍。雖然有研究指出疲倦症狀是迅速衰老的重要先兆，甚至會導致衰弱和殘疾， 但長者照顧服務並未有辨識及治療疲倦徵狀的措施。 有研究顯示，運動伴隨“增進行為改善策略”能有效改善疾病引致的疲倦。 但是，用於改善衰老長者疲倦徵狀的成效仍然未知。本研究旨在探討在有否加入”增進行為改善增進策略”的情況下，個別化運動計劃對出現疲倦症狀的長者於減少老年衰弱的徵狀之成效， 從而減少其疲倦徵狀以及改善他們的體能、運動自信心和持續運動量。 此研究是包含三個研究組別 ，採用單盲及集群隨機對照試驗的方法，從12個社區健康機構中邀請了285個出現疲倦症狀的長者參與是次研究。每間機構會被隨機分配為三個研究組別的其中一組：一．個人化運動訓練伴隨“增進行為改善策略”組別；二． 運動組別（接受運動訓練和健康講座）；三．控制組（健康講座）。計劃為期16星期，個人化運動訓練伴隨“增進行為改善策略”會組別分別會在計劃結束後的兩個月和六個月後各有一節改進活動。 研究假設在完成此計劃後的首個星期、 六個月和十二個月後，個人化運動訓練伴隨 “行為改善增進策略”組別相比其餘兩組，能顯著減少疲倦徵狀以及改善長者的體能、運動自信心和持續運動量，以及改善老年衰弱的徵狀。在第一次評估後，研究人員將與30位研究參與者進行訪談，隨後進行內容分析以了解參與者對於是次接受個人化運動訓練“增進行為改善策略”的介入計劃所感受的得著、弱點、參與計劃時所遇到的困難，以及介入計劃的治療元素。 此研究將會是開創性的介入研究計劃以幫助管理衰老長者的疲倦徵狀及如何預防與疲倦徵狀相關的衰老情況。

15600717.label: Realisation of objectives
15600717.value: Project objectives achievement The objectives of this project have been completely achieved, as evidenced by the completion of a cluster-randomised controlled trial in 21 local community centres for older adults. We recruited 184 participants from February 2018 to April 2020. As a one-year follow-up was required to evaluate the possible sustainable effects, we completed the collecting of all data in April 2021. The findings support the view that the combined (COME) intervention with individualised exercise training and the Behavioural Change Enhancement (BCE) programme had significantly better immediate and sustainable effects (6 and 12 months) on reducing fatigue in frail older adults than exercise training or health talks alone (Objective 1). Significantly better immediate effects on the secondary outcomes (i.e., the participants' physical endurance, exercise self-efficacy, physical activity levels, and frailty status) were observed in the COMB intervention and the exercise training groups alone than in the control group. The performance of the COMB intervention and exercise training alone on most of the secondary outcomes was similar, as no significant differences between these two intervention groups could be found for most of the measurements at different time points (Objective 2). To attain Objective 3, we conducted four semi-structured interviews (n=26) and the survey (n=46) with the participants from the COMB group immediately after the completion of the intervention for participants from the COMB group. Four themes were synthesised from the data: 1) Overall perceptions of the COMB intervention were good and practical; 2) Barriers to participating in the COME intervention were mainly related to sometimes feeling unwell both physically and psychologically; 3) Facilitators for implementing the COMB intervention included receiving supportive compliments from the interventionist, gaining peer support, and formulating a specific, measurable, achievable, realistic, and time-based (SMART) action plan to follow the exercise goal; 4) Suggestions for improving the programme included cancelling the task of keeping a daily exercise record because it was troublesome, increasing the duration of the programme, and others. In addition, the findings from the survey were mostly positive. The majority of the participants agreed that the strategies used in the BCE programme were helpful to them. All of the participants stated that they would recommend this programme to other older adults with the same problems. In conclusion, the COMB programme was acceptable to the frail older people with fatigue, although most of them claimed that keeping daily exercise records was the most challenging part of the intervention. Besides attaining the three study objectives, an intervention protocol for the combined intervention was tested and published. The protocol includes a design for behavioural change strategies guided by behavioural change model that was tested and found to be effective (i.e., the Health Action Process Approach [HAPA] model), given alongside an exercise programme. In addition, teaching materials for training participants in different intervention groups were developed and validated. This combined intervention is led by the behavioural change model and informed by evidence. It is also tailor-made to manage frail older people with fatigue. With the availability of the intervention protocol and all teaching materials, the intervention can easily be adopted in community settings as there is no need to rely on sophisticated equipment or skills. Difficulties encountered during the project and their solutions Due to the frequent incidents of social unrest in 2019 and the covid-19 pandemic that began in January 2020, all local community centres were closed and older adults were reluctant to join any social events. The research team experienced a huge challenge in recruiting participants for the study. Therefore, the sample size was only about 60% of the size calculated in the proposal. We therefore extended our invitation to as many community centres as possible. In fact, we sent out our invitation to all government-funded community centres for older people (n=211) in Hong Kong by email and followed up with a telephone call. In the end, only 21 centres accepted the invitation to join the study. We also encountered another challenge in completing outcome measurements at different times, particularly for the data collection period of between 2019 and 2020 Due to the closure of the community centres at that time, we could not collect any data there. To minimise the missing data, we immediately changed the data collection method from face-to-face to telephone interviews. We immediately developed the telephone interview guide to train the outcome assessors to ensure that all outcome assessments could be conducted in a consistent manner. For the physical assessments, such as handgrip strength, the get-up-and-go-test, and others, we had no choice but to conduct face-to-face assessments. To minimise the missing data, whenever the participants agreed, we visited their homes to conduct the physical assessment. With the assistance of the community centres, most agreed to this arrangement. However, this arrangement was very disruptive to our original plan and strained the human resources of our research team because the intention had been to handle more participants at the same time. Also, because of these unforeseeable events, the attrition rates were 14.1%, 18.5%, and 14.5% at T1 (immediately post-intervention) and increased to 28.1%, 32.3%, and 41.8% at T3 (at the 12-month follow up) in the COMB, EXER, and control groups, respectively.

15600717.label: Major findings and research outcome
15600717.value: Major finding 1: The findings support the view that the combined intervention had a more significant immediate and sustainable effect on reducing fatigue in frail older people than pure exercise training or health education. However, the effects of the combined intervention and pure exercise training on most of the secondary outcomes were similar, although both intervention groups performed better than the control group, who received only the health talks. Major finding 2: The qualitative interviews and survey findings show that this combined intervention is welcomed by frail older people with fatigue. This combined intervention has great potential to be sustainably implemented in community settings, as evidenced by the fact that our team has already implemented this programme in 21 community centres. One non-governmental organisation that operates 10 community centres has adopted this programme and recommends it to their members. The research outcomes based on this project: A study protocol has been published in the journal Physical Therapy [Impact factor: 3.043]. A manuscript reporting the main findings of the clinical trial has already been submitted to European Review of Ageing and Physical Activity [Impact factor: 3.878]. An abstract for oral communication has been submitted to International Conference on Frailty & Sarcopenia Research, April 20-22, 2022, Boston, MA, USA. Two animations to introduce frailty and its management has been developed and used to educate the general public.

15600717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15600717.value: The following are potential areas for further development after this clinical trial: 1. The intervention in this project can be revised to offer an interactive game environment combining live action, games, and an award system. This can make the exercise training more interesting than traditional exercise training, thereby enhancing engagement. This interactive preform can also be used to deliver different effective behavioural change techniques to reduce human contact with the participants and reduce staff costs but provide a more sustainable effect. 2. To eliminate the task of having participants keep daily exercise records, our team has been piloting the use of electronic activity trackers. This kind of tracker can provide feedback and display activity counts to participants. The feedback includes multiple charts, social comparisons, and indicators of progress towards individual goals. Activity trackers show promise as a medium for implementing behavioural change strategies. Based on the findings of this study, we are running a pilot study to investigate the feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary effects of an exercise programme plus a WAT intervention to increase physical activity levels in frail or pre-frail older people. If the results are promising, we will apply for an external grant to support a full-scale clinical trial.

15600717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15600717.value: Ageing-induced fatigue is common among older people, potentially leading to other adverse outcomes such as frailty unless properly managed. Currently, no evidence-based intervention is available to address this problem. This study evaluated the effects of an exercise with Behavioural Change Enhancement (BCE) programme for older adults with fatigue, compared with those receiving an exercise programme only and health talks only. 184 participants (mean age: 79.1) were recruited from 21 community centres. They were randomised to either: the COMB group (n=64) receiving 16 weeks of exercise training plus the BCE programme, the EXER group (n=65) receiving exercise training and health talks, or the control group (n=55) receiving only health talks. Fatigue levels were assessed at baseline, immediately, 6 months, and 12 months post-intervention. The results indicated a significantly greater reduction in fatigue levels in the COMB group than in the control or EXER groups immediately and at 6 and 12 months post-intervention. No significant difference was found between the fatigue levels of the EXER group and the control group at any time point. In conclusion, better immediate and sustainable effects on reducing fatigue in frail older adults were seen with the COMB intervention than with exercise training or health talks alone.

15601617.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15601617.value: 中國職校中新一代勞工的性別化過程

15601617.label: Project Objectives
15601617.value: To critically review how market transition and globalisation reshape gender hierarchies and ideologies in reformed China by focusing on how they shape gendered institutions, relationships, identities, and experiences of women and men. To explore the lived experiences and everyday practices of the younger generation of female and male workers at the intersection of neoliberal market values and traditional patriarchal values as a reflection of the complex dynamics of class and gender relations in educational and working environments. To examine the gendering of learning, training and working experiences among female and male students in both formal and informal curriculums of vocational education, and its relations to gender ideologies and identities in the process of crafting selves in social institutions. To shed light on future feminist movements in the areas of education and employment by bringing new gender knowledge about young people’s school-to-work transitions and the gendering processes of work, training, and employment in post-reform China.

15601617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15601617.value: 中國在毛澤東時期用了“婦女撐起半邊天”這個口號，鼓吹男女性在生活的所有領域取得平等。雖然許多的相關措施並沒有得到落實，中國女性的確進入了一個新時代，在教育、婚姻、就業等各方面都得到了長足的改進，意味其在一定程度上通過社會主義演變獲得了社會地位的"解放"。然而，從改革開放時代開始，社會主義婦女運動又發生了新的變化。男女分工、 性別角色、乃至兩性形象都在學術界和社會上引起激烈辯論並被重新定義。女性主義研究的新趨勢集中在身體、女性化、消費身份等議題，但鮮有探討教育中的性別化情況，以及其對社會上的性別角色、兩性形象、男女生就業及工作，以及基本經濟權利的影響。我們的研究正希望填補這個空缺。 近年來，越來越多的初中畢業生進入城市的中等職業教育體系。這些男女學生在找到製造業和服務業的工作前，一般都先在職業學校接受教育和培訓。不同於一般的學術教育，職業教育是專門面向勞動市場，為學生未來就業做好準備。我們會在城市裡的職校，通過長期觀察和深度訪談，瞭解現有的兩性關係如何影響職校學生，對其學習經驗、生活習慣、就業策略等有何影響。通過性別和階級再造的視角，我們的研究問題包括: 新一代的男女工人在新的市場秩序中將面對什麼不同的機遇與困難？這些年青男女會如何回應，現有社會的兩性關係和勞動市場的性別秩序又有何面貌？

15601617.label: Realisation of objectives
15601617.value: During the project period, our project team had made eleven field trips, lasting from 6 to 15 days, to Shenzhen and Zhuhai (Southern China), and Hangzhou (Eastern China), the two major and original research sites of the project. In addition, we had made four explorative but extended field trips (lasting from 2 to 3 weeks) in Guizhou and Gansu provinces to understand the schooling and transitional experiences of young vocational school students in less developed regions of China. Information about the students’ enrolment in different programs in 8 vocational schools are collected (3 from Southern China, 3 from Eastern China, and 2 from Western China). Our team has successfully interviewed principals, teachers, students and graduates in the vocational schools to obtain detailed information about the gender-related recruitment policies, the structure and design of programs in vocational schools, and the ways their programs respond to the changes of local and national labour markets. Ethnographic works in Hangzhou ran between early 2018 and late 2019. Data relating to the gendering processes in vocational schools and sites of internships were collected from students, interns, graduates of various types of programs and in terms of their gender compositions. We have successfully interviewed over 130 students at their vocational schools (75 females and 57 males), with 52 of them having been re-interviewed during their internships, part-time work, and even after their graduation. Through purposeful sampling, about one-third of our informants enrolled and studied in “gender-non-conforming” programs (e.g. female students in Advanced Industry and Robotic Process Automation, male students in Accounting, Hotel and Tourism), while less than one-third among them had chance to get training or employment that related to their fields of study. For those who enrolled in “gender-conforming” programs, more than three quarters of them were assigned internships in related fields and more than half of them stayed in the field after graduation. Rich qualitative data related to students’ educational choice, parents’ expectations, learning and training experiences inside and outside schools, their dreams, concerns, reflections, and struggles during schooling, internship, and employment were collected through interviews and numerous informal chats during fieldwork. Through comparing female and male students’ strategies of securing a proper and stable employment in an increasingly competitive urban labour market, we have revealed the complex dynamics of gender relations in reformed China under the influence of both neoliberal market values and traditional patriarchal values. Their gender subject making is torn among forces of state, market, school, and individual desire during their years of vocational training and school-to-work transitions. In the mid-2018, our team were invited to pay a short visit to two vocational colleges that are located in the relatively poor regions in the Guizhou and Gansu provinces. We decided to have another extended period of fieldwork in the Western China at the end of 2018 to further explore the young gendered stories from less urbanized areas to diversify the existing works that are mainly done in urban areas of eastern China. During the two trips, our team interviewed 48 students (20 females and 28 males) in the college in Guizhou and 73 students (49 females and 24 males) in the college in Gansu. Based on the educational decisions and the life-planning of the rural students, we tried to explore their meaning of self-development and achievement through vocational training – the new education opportunity only available to this generation of rural youth. Focusing on the young women’s strategies for economic empowerment and self-development, we identify a new form of empowered gender subjectivity highly connected to their strong desire to become valuable daughters for their natal patrilineal families. The development and construction of this identity is only possible under the rapid expansion of vocational education and labour market and the emergence of individualistic values among rural youth. In urban China, to further confirm the ways the market transition and the development of globalized knowledge economy reshaping gender hierarchies and ideologies in China, and further review their impact on gendered institutions, relationships, identities, and experiences of women and men, we have organized fieldwork in Shenzhen, a newly developed leading national, if not global, technology hub. Since late 2018, we were able to identify the vocational colleges that specialized on Information Technology and Electronic Commerce in Shenzhen and Zhuhai, and collected background information from the school principals and teachers. Field work in the two cities was arranged and started in April 2019 but ended in June of the same year. Although we had already gained permissions to contact student interns who are working outside schools for their internships and had arranged visits to their workplace dormitories with the teachers responsible for the internships, all the planned research activities were suspended by the vocational colleges. We were told that because of the social incidents in Hong Kong, they were forbidden to host any research work from overseas (including Hong Kong) institutions. Later in 2020, research work in mainland China had been fully halted due to the coronavirus pandemic. All scheduled and rescheduled field visits in vocational schools and internship sites were cancelled. Faced with all the unexpected unfavourable situations in Hong Kong and the mainland, our team adopted alternative data collection strategies since November 2020. Without any help from vocational schools, we tried to contact the previous informants to arrange some group- or individual- online interviews. We successfully recruited 34 vocational school students from previous in-depth interviews in Zhuhai. We also re-interviewed 30 interns and graduates from Hangzhou, 22 from Guizhou and another 29 from Gansu. We also kept in touch with many of them via social media sites QQ and WeChat. Through investigation on their training experiences and employment status after graduation, the changes of their aspirations due to the difficulties faced and opportunities offered in the labour market, their daily interactions with colleagues from different gender, age, educational and training experiences, we have evaluated the gendering processes of work, training, and employment in post-reform China. Also, through a systemic analysis of the (changed) aspirations, with the job opportunities and occupational attainments among vocational school students of different gender, we have discovered how the identity formation of the future generation of Chinese labour is highly related to the interactions of class hierarchies and gender ideologies. Although these makeup measures have made substantial contributions to the project, they cannot fully compensate for the lack of opportunities for doing ethnographic studies in the field sites. For the further advancement of Chinese capital and industry, labor-intensive manufacturing is turning toward scientific innovation for sustainable economic growth, and vocational schools are regarded as crucial sites of cultivating this new generation of Chinese workers. We found the emerging image of a proper labourer is an “innovative brain” equipped with a high level of technical knowledge and strong operating skills for the new economies—a natural attachment to the hegemonic masculinity for achieving it. This macro-level study informs us of the interactions between vocational education and employment under the impact of hegemonic gender discourse and structure in present-day China. It also explains how individual girls’ and boys’ decisions and behaviour during their education transitions are shaped by the larger social and economic structure.

15601617.label: Major findings and research outcome
15601617.value: This research project examines how the larger structural, political, and cultural forces impact on students’ learning and training experiences in vocational schools that prepare them as a future generation of Chinese worker. Due to the existing inequalities in the education system, students with rural background, especially females, are overrepresented in short-cycle programs in vocational colleges. Although vocational education has a lower status than academic education, it provides them the chance to receive higher education that previous generation of rural populations did not enjoy. The emergence of individualistic values also allows the young generation of Chinese rural women to have freedom in their individualized planning for future development and construction of their identities. While investigating the young women’s strategies for economic empowerment and self-development, we identify a new form of empowered gender subjectivity highly connected to their strong desire to become valuable daughters for their natal patrilineal families. This empowered agency, however, does not necessarily challenge the gender structure of the labor market and the primary caregiving role of women in the family. These findings have been presented in the conference paper “The Persistence of Gendered choices of Education and Occupation among Chinese Young Women”, and are further illustrated and discussed in the accepted journal paper entitled “Being a Valuable Daughter in a Rural Family: The Relational Identity and Empowered Gender Subjectivities of Female Vocational College Students”. Further, the project demonstrates the conflictual roles of state, market, school, and individual desire in the future workers’ subject formation during their years of vocational training. Vocational school students have to negotiate in between the different demands of the masculinised national project, the marketable value of femininity, the call for flexibility and entrepreneurship in global youth culture, and individual aspirations of independence and self-actualization. These findings have been discussed in the paper entitled “Clashing Gender in Vocational Education: State, Market and School in Subject Making of Female and Male Workers in China”, presented in a conference paper “From Gender Egalitarianism to Gender Essentialism: The New Generation of Working Class in Post-Reform China”, and further elaborated in a paper under preparation for journal publication “Doing Gender in Vocational School: Training experiences of female students in male-dominated fields”. The former paper has been submitted to the journal “positions: asia critique” for review in September 2021. But due to the pandemic and the changes of their peer-review system, the reviewing process has been substantially delayed and prolonged.

15601617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15601617.value: The potential for further development of this project is rich. Based on the data we collected at the later stage of the project, vocational school students and graduates are under a great pressure of economic and employment insecurity due to the economic recession. The expansion of service and manufacturing sectors in China have been dampened by the pandemic and hostile global trade environment over the past few years. Millions of companies are shutting down, laying off workers, and slashing wages to get though these difficult times. Given that the market situation and labour conditions are found to be classed and gendered in this project, it is worthwhile to explore the gendered strategies of the vocational school students used to cope with the economic downturn during their school-to-work and family transitions. We have stayed in touch with our informants, hopefully we will be able to have further investigation on the stated issue in Mainland China when normal travel is resumed.

15601617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15601617.value: Since the market reform, an expansion of labour market and an increasingly accessible higher education system appear to offer young women and men abundant employment opportunities. Even girls from disadvantaged families or with rural background now have chances to receive vocational training before employment. These developments lead this new generation of Chinese youths to feel that they have more power and freedom in having more choices in education and labour market. This project however finds the persistent gendered divisions in the educational field of young students in the vocational track which leads them to gendered career paths. Being influenced by various factors like the development of industries, availability of work opportunities, expectations from friends and families, and self-evaluation, we find the young women and young men continue to choose and take on feminine and masculine types of work according to their genders after their vocational higher education. The opportunities of additional training and schooling have not changed their trajectories to a conventional career path that matches with their gender identity. Young women graduates continue to cluster in the service sector and young men work in male-dominated manufacturing occupations.

15602017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15602017.value: 很少人會質疑真實及可理解輸入對語言習得的重要性。可是， 在眾多的網上視頻中，針對每位英語學習者的整體英語 、詞彙水平及聽覺信息加工能力，找尋出可理解的輸入殊不容易。最近，我們發展出一套電腦程式，用來估算每一套附字幕網上視頻的語速及詞彙覆蓋率。克服了自動化評估視頻用語難度這個技術挑戰後，下一步我們需要了解語速及詞彙覆蓋率對第二語言聆聽理解的影響。本計劃將會是解決在網上視頻中尋找個人化、可理解輸入這個難題的關鍵。 本對照實驗旨在測試語速及詞彙覆蓋率對第二語言聆聽理解的影響。一百位英語學習者將參加一項實驗，負責重複及翻譯語速、詞彙覆蓋率及長度各異的句子。在線性混合效果模型(linear mixed-effects model)分析中，兩項句子重複及翻譯任務的得分為結果變量，語速、詞彙覆蓋率及兩者之相互作用(interaction)為固定效應，受試者之整體英語 、聽覺信息加工能力及句子長度為共變量，受試者及試題為隨機效應。所得的最佳模型可以解答以下兩條問題： 一、在排除受試者之整體英語 、聽覺信息加工能力及句子長度的影響後，語速、詞彙覆蓋率及兩者之相互作用如何影響第二語言聆聽理解? 二、不同英語水平之學習者需要甚麼語速及詞彙覆蓋率才能充份理解第二語言聆聽內容? 本計劃為首個針對語速、詞彙覆蓋率及其相互作用、在排除受試者之整體英語及聽覺信息加工能力方差後，對第二語言聆聽理解影響的研究。解答問題一，將加深我們對第二語言聆聽理解影響因素的認識，有助老師預備適合每位學生第二語言能力的輸入。解答問題二，則可以為日後相關第二語言聆聽研究提供語速及詞彙覆蓋率的參考值。現時文獻中並沒有實證有效的同類指引。最後， 本計劃產生的語速及詞彙覆蓋率參考值將被應用到電腦輔助語言學習系統的開發，該系統能針對每位英語學習者的語言能力，自動搜尋及推薦合適的網上視頻，讓廣大英語學習者能在芸芸的視頻中，找到個人化、可理解的輸入。

15602017.label: Realisation of objectives
15602017.value: This project aimed to facilitate computer-assisted vocabulary learning by helping language learners find online videos matching their proficiency level and verbal processing ability. Previously, we (Lin, 2016a, 2016b, 2016c, 2021) developed a computer tool to estimate the speech rate and word density unknown to a learner in any subtitled internet media (e.g., YouTube). While the technical challenge of automatically evaluating the difficulty of internet media language has been overcome, the controlled experiment conducted in this project allowed exploration of the effects of speech rate and unknown word density on L2 listening comprehension. The findings have informed and improved the algorithm used by our computer tool to recommend videos to learners. To accomplish the objectives, a controlled experiment using a multivariate and within-subjects design was conducted, requiring 87 local EFL learners to complete a sentence repetition task and a sentence translation task. Eighty utterances taken from an authentic one-hour BBC documentary on the discovery of painkillers were divided into two comparable lists of 40. Each included a range of utterances with different speech rates and numbers of difficult words. The repetition task required subjects to repeat the utterances verbatim, with their performance rated in terms of accuracy of meaning, syntax, vocabulary, morphology and pronunciation. The translation task required subjects to translate the sentences into their L1 within 5 seconds of listening. Performance was again rated in terms of coherence, cohesion, accuracy and omission of propositions. Subjects also completed: an auditory lexical decision task, testing their recognition of the phonological form and their semantic knowledge of the words from the 80 utterances; a serial non-word repetition task measuring phonological short-term memory capacity; a cloze test to assess their L2 English proficiency; a vocabulary size test measuring L2 English vocabulary size and a background questionnaire. To achieve objective 1, performance in the repetition and translation tasks was recoded into a binary outcome variable (i.e., pass/fail) and analysed using generalised linear-mixed effects models with by-subject and by-sentence random intercepts. To achieve objective 2, the estimates of the best-fitting generalised mixed-effect model were examined. This model could calculate the chance of adequate listening comprehension given a certain proficiency level after partialling out the effect of other variables. Adequate is defined as a meaning score above 3 out of 6 in the repetition task with 0 omission of propositions in the translation task.

15602017.label: Major findings and research outcome
15602017.value: The project had 3 major findings. Firstly, it developed a generalised linear mixed-effects model for L2 listening comprehension taking into account both textual factors and individual differences. In the best-fitting model, the statistically significant predictors were number of unknown words in an utterance, duration of the utterance, task type (repetition/translation), vocabulary size test score and cloze test score. Speech rate of the utterance, serial non-word repetition score and the interaction between speech rate and number of unknown words in the utterance were non-significant. Secondly, it revealed how much each factor affected successful listening comprehension. More specifically, concerning the variable number of unknown words in the utterance, for every 1 unknown word in the utterance, there was a decrease of approximately 45% in the odds of passing. This observation corroborates the descriptive statistical findings: The chances of successfully repeating or translating an utterance when there was only one unknown word were 28.7% and 50.4% respectively. When the number of unknown words increased to 2, this dropped significantly, to 18.4% and 42.6%, respectively. It was unlikely for learners to correctly repeat or or translate an utterance when there were three or more unknown words. The effects of the other four significant predictors are as follows: - Every 1 second increase in the duration of the utterance was associated with a 57% decrease in the odds of passing. - When the task switched to translation from repetition, the odds of passing increased drastically: by 734%. - For every 1 unit (i.e., 10.94 points) increase in the vocabulary size test score, there was a 71% increase in the odds of passing. - For every 1 unit (i.e., 7.43) increase in the cloze test score, there was a 42% increase in the odds of passing. Thirdly, the project found poor knowledge of (the phonological form of) words as a key obstacle to local EFL learners’ listening comprehension. In the 137-item auditory lexical decision task, the learners failed to recognise over 50% of the words from the 80 utterances. The majority (82.5%) of these unknown words were still not recognised when presented visually. The learners’ inability to recognise and recall (the phonological form of) the words became apparent in the repetition task. Our model has ruled out poor phonological short-term memory capacity as a reason for poor repetition task performance.

15602017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15602017.value: The statistical model developed in this study will significantly improve our computer tool’s ability to help learners find online videos matching their L2 proficiency and verbal processing abilities. Following its next major update, our tool will recommend YouTube videos to learners based on their performance in the vocabulary size test and cloze test. As we found that the number of unknown words significantly predicted L2 comprehension, we plan to add a new function so the tool will test and score users’ auditory recognition of English words from videos they have previously watched. Such information could further improve the tool’s ability to help learners find suitable videos. Our experimental evidence shows how local EFL learners’ poor vocabulary knowledge and poor recognition of the pronunciation of words hindered their L2 listening comprehension and vocabulary learning from spoken input. Looking ahead, research is needed to strengthen learners’ memories of the phonological forms of English words. Changes to the local EFL curriculum are also recommended, to substantially increase their vocabulary sizes.

15602017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15602017.value: This project investigated factors affecting L2 listening comprehension. In the controlled experiment, 87 local EFL university students completed a sentence repetition task and a sentence translation task, both measuring L2 listening comprehension. Their performance was analysed using generalised linear mixed-effects models. The best-fitting model identified 5 significant predictors of listening comprehension: number of unknown words in an utterance (measured using an auditory lexical decision task), duration of the utterance, task type (repetition or translation), vocabulary size (measured by a vocabulary size test) and L2 proficiency (measured using a cloze test).The speech rate of the utterance, phonological short-term memory capacity (measured using a serial non-word repetition task) and the interaction between speech rate and the number of unknown words in the utterance were non-significant. Results from the auditory lexical decision task revealed the extent of the learners’ problems with recognising the phonological forms of words and their limited L2 vocabulary size. Few studies before this have developed a model of L2 listening comprehension taking into account multiple textual factors and individual differences. This model will be applied in our vocabulary learning tool’s next major update so that YouTube videos are recommended based on users’ vocabulary size and cloze test scores.
