15602417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15602417.value: Overparenting generally refers to the inappropriate parenting styles and strategies that parents use in order to “ensure” the accomplishment and happiness of their children by actively intruding into their children’s lives and removing the problems and difficulties that parents may anticipate. Overparenting has become an emergent parenting style in global and local contexts, and it catches the attention of mass media and the public. Separation-individuation theory incorporated with family systems theories argue that overparenting prohibits adolescents from self-differentiation and autonomy, which contributes to psychosocial immaturity and maladjustment of adolescents. Besides, social learning theory posits that parents who exercise overparenting may model their children’s behaviours of using forceful actions to achieve success, dominance of control and manipulation as well as a sense of entitlement, superiority and perfection which would eventually promote the development of narcissistic traits among adolescents. Against this background, this study aims at examining the relationships between overparenting and psychosocial developmental outcomes (narcissistic traits, empathy and positive youth development attributes) of Chinese adolescents in Hong Kong over time. Specifically, the study attempts to: 1) examine the concurrent and longitudinal influences of overparenting on psychosocial development (narcissistic traits, empathy and positive youth development attributes) among a sample of Chinese adolescents in Hong Kong; 2) investigate the differences between paternal and maternal overparenting characteristics perceived by adolescents over time; and 3) assess how perceived paternal and maternal overparenting interact to influence psychosocial development of adolescents over time. A 3-year longitudinal study will be conducted in the study. A sample of N = 1,900 adolescents studying in Secondary One (Grade 7) in Hong Kong will be recruited through multi-stage stratified cluster sampling method, with geographical location and school banding as the main stratifying factors. Adolescents will be invited to fill out a questionnaire containing measures of perceived paternal and maternal overparenting, narcissism, empathy and positive youth development attributes. Three waves of data will be collected, with an interval of one year in between them. This study fills a distinct conceptual gap in the literature and it is a pioneering scientific study to examine the relationships between overparenting and psychosocial development of adolescents in the Chinese contexts. The study will enrich our understanding on emerging styles of Chinese parenting, which will provide important insights for the study of adolescence, the family as well as family social work. 過度管教意旨父母透過不適當的管教模式，包括替子女解決預見的問題和困難，積極干預子女的生活，以『確保』子女的幸福及未來成就 (Segrin et al., 2012)。過度管教成為香港以至國際上冒起的親職管教模式，並吸引傳媒及公眾的關注。根據家庭系統理論 （Bowen, 1993），過度管教碍礙青少年從親子關係中分離出來，為他們帶來不成熟的身心發展的及社會適應上的困難 (Grotevant & Cooper, 1986)。另一方面，根據社會學習理論 （Bandura, 1997），子女透過模仿父母過度管教的行為，採取控制和操縱手段達致成功，強調優越感、完美主意及權利擁有權，形成青少年的自戀性格。 在這種背景下，這項研究旨在剖析過度管教及青少年身心社交發展(自戀性格、同理心及正向身心社交發展構念)之間的關係。研究目的包括： 1) 了解過度管教對青少年身心社交發展(自戀性格、同理心及正向身心社交發展構念)的影響； 2）檢視父親和母親過度管教隨著時間改變而產生的變異；及 3) 評估父親過度管教和母親過度管教之間的相互效應如何影響青少年的身心社交發展。 是項研究為一項長達三年之追蹤研究，以問卷形式跟進受訪者之看法。是項研究會邀請1,900 位在香港就讀中一(第七級)之青少年參與，透過分層多階段整群抽樣調查(Multistage stratified cluster sampling)形式進行，以學校地域及成績類別為抽樣條件。青少年會被邀請填寫一份問卷，內容包括父親和母親的過度管教、自戀性格、同理心及正向身心社交發展構念等量表。資料搜集會於三年內分三次進行，每次資料搜集相隔為一年。這項研究有助補足在社會科學文獻上就有關華人社會過度管教及青少年身心社交發展課題之縫隙，並加深我們對過度管教模式的認識，為青少年研究、家庭研究及家庭社會工作帶來重要的啟示。

15602417.label: Realisation of objectives
15602417.value: Overparenting refers to the inappropriate parenting styles and strategies that parents exercise to “ensure” the accomplishment and happiness of their children by actively intruding into their children’s lives and removing the problems and difficulties that parents may anticipate (Segrin et al., 2012). While this emerging parenting style catches the attention of mass media and the public, research on overparenting is in its infancy, particularly in the Chinese context. Moreover, longitudinal studies on overparenting and adolescent developmental outcomes over time are severely lacking. As such, this study aimed at examining the relationships between overparenting and psychosocial developmental outcomes of adolescents in Hong Kong over time. Originally, 21 secondary schools participated in the study at Time 1, of which 19 secondary schools were mainly for Chinese, whereas the other two schools were for non-Chinese students. The data collection was smooth in Times 1 and 2. However, we faced various difficulties in data collection at Time 3 because of the outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic, when school suspension and learn-at-home arrangement were widely arranged. Changes of principals and school personnel further created hurdles to the study. Two non-Chinese secondary schools withdrew from the study as many students left Hong Kong because of the pandemic. Moreover, five secondary schools withdrew from the study, with three schools failed to arrange data collection during the pandemic, and two schools changed the major school personnel. We finally had 14 secondary school completing data collection for all three waves. The data collection of Time 3 completed in August, 2021. After matching, there were 1,074 respondents filling out the questionnaires at all three time points. The sample was large enough to perform statistical analyses. Attrition analyses of students from 14 schools were performed. Logistic regression analyses were performed to assess whether demographic characteristics and the studied variables at Time 1 (T1) were associated with sample attrition (dropout = 0, retention = 1). Results showed that more girls and adolescents from intact families retained in the study. However, the associations of all studied variables at T1 with sample retention were non-significant, suggesting that there was a random dropout of the respondents. Regarding the demographic characteristics of 1,074 respondents, 685 (63.8%) were girls. The mean age was 12.66 (SD = .80) at T1. A majority of respondents came from intact families (n = 1082; 74.0%), while 315 (21.6%) respondents coming from non-intact families. 292 (20.0%) respondents were recipients of Comprehensive Social Security Assistance. The objectives are generally achieved. For Objective 1 (i.e., to examine the concurrent and longitudinal influences of overparenting on the psychosocial development of Chinese adolescents residing in Hong Kong), we performed correlational analyses to examine the concurrent associations between paternal and maternal overparenting with adolescent developmental outcomes, and multivariate LGC modelling analyses to examine the effects of the initial points (intercepts) and changes (slope) of overparenting on the changes (slope) of adolescent growth parameters, including narcissism, empathy and positive youth development. Results showed that while paternal overparenting was consistently and positively associated with adolescent narcissism, positive youth development and life satisfaction, maternal overparenting was positively associated adolescent narcissism, anxiety and depression. Two papers were published based on the findings. Findings from multivariate LGC modelling analyses further indicated that the initial level (intercept) and trajectory (slope) of paternal overparenting predicted the rate of change of adolescents’ narcissistic behavior. Moreover, the trajectory (slope) of maternal overparenting also predicted the rate of change of adolescent narcissism. However, the initial level (intercept) and trajectory (slope) of paternal and maternal overparenting did not predict the outcomes of positive youth development, empathy, life satisfaction, depression and anxiety, respectively. Interestingly, when we introduced father-child conflict and mother-child conflict into the tested model as intervening variables, results from cross-lagged model analyses indicated that mother-child conflict mediated the relationship between maternal overparenting and adolescent anxiety over time. A reverse association of prior adolescent anxiety with subsequent maternal overparenting via mother-child conflict was also identified. This reverse relationship also occurred when positive youth development and life satisfaction served as predictors, respectively. Moreover, father-child conflict mediated the relationship between paternal overparenting and adolescent life satisfaction. Two papers were published based on the findings. For Objective 2 (i.e., to investigate differences between paternal and maternal overparenting characteristics perceived by adolescents over time), we performed repeated measure - ANOVA to examine the difference between paternal and maternal overparenting over time. Adolescents reported higher levels of maternal overparenting than paternal overparenting. The results showed that both paternal and maternal overparenting declined over time. However, there is no significant difference between paternal and maternal overparenting over time. Regarding Objective 3 (i.e., to assess how perceived paternal and maternal overparenting interact to influence different psychosocial developmental outcomes of adolescents over time), we examined the interaction effect of paternal and maternal overparenting at T1 on adolescent developmental outcomes/wellbeing at T3, after controlling for adolescent gender and adolescent developmental outcomes/wellbeing at T2. Results from structural equation modelling showed that the interaction term of paternal and maternal overparenting did not predict adolescent narcissism, empathy, positive youth development, life satisfaction and anxiety. However, paternal overparenting marginally strengthened the prediction of maternal overparenting and adolescent depression over time. Our study has further achieved the following outcomes: • We validated the Chinese Overparenting Scale using the Time 1 sample. The measurement showed excellent internal consistency and factorial validity. A peer-reviewed journal paper was published based on the findings. • We collected data of a sample of 1,074 respondents who had filled out the questionnaire at three time points. To the best of my knowledge, the study is pioneering in examining the longitudinal effects of overparenting on developmental outcomes of adolescents in Chinese as well as global contexts. • Four peer-reviewed journal papers were published based on the analyses. • We disseminated the reports to each participating school each year after data collection and analyses. • We disseminated the findings in different social work subjects, including “Youth and Social Work” in Bachelor of Arts in Social Work, “Advanced Social Work Theory and Practice II” in Master of Social Work, “Adolescent Development and Family Systems” in Master of Arts in Family Education and Family Therapy, and “Advanced Family-Centred Social Work: Theory, Practice and Research” in Doctor of Social Work. • The study helped to put forth on future development overparenting research in Hong Kong and Chinese contexts. The PI has been awarded by the General Research Fund, the Research Grants Council to conduct a research project entitled “Parenting Perfectionism and Overparenting among Chinese Parents in Hong Kong” in 2022-2024. The study has several merits. First, the study filled the research gaps in examining overparenting and adolescent developmental outcomes in the Chinese context. Validated indigenous measurement of overparenting was used in the study. Second, while a major of studies selected emerging adults as the study sample, this study chose young adolescents as the targets of study, which provides important insights on the impacts of overparenting on adolescent psychosocial development during early adolescence. Third, the study was a longitudinal one with three conservative time points. The study enables more advanced statistical analyses on examining the changes of overparenting over time and how initial point and trajectories of overparenting might affect trajectories of adolescent development. Fourth, a large sample of 1,074 respondents ensures the robustness of the study.

15602417.label: Major findings and research outcome
15602417.value: This study examined the relationships between overparenting and psychosocial developmental outcomes (narcissistic traits, empathy and positive youth development attributes) of adolescents in Hong Kong over time. There are some important findings in the study. First, the study indicated that while paternal overparenting was consistently and positively associated with adolescent narcissism, positive youth development and life satisfaction, maternal overparenting was positively associated adolescent narcissism, anxiety and depression. Two peer-reviewed journal papers were published based on the findings. Second, results from multivariate LGC modelling analyses further indicated that the initial level (intercept) and trajectory (slope) of paternal overparenting predicted the rate of change (slope) of adolescents’ narcissistic behavior, with Estimate = .021, S.E. = .009 (p < .05) and Estimate = .088, S.E. = .031 (p < .01), respectively. Moreover, the trajectory (slope) of maternal overparenting also predicted the rate of change (slope) of adolescent narcissism, (Estimate = .095, S.E. = .044, p < .05). Third, results from cross-lagged model analyses indicated that mother-child conflict mediated the relationship between maternal overparenting and adolescent anxiety over time. Besides, a reverse association of prior adolescent anxiety with subsequent maternal overparenting via mother-child conflict was also identified. Two peer-reviewed journal papers were published based on the findings. Moreover, this reverse relationship also occurred when positive youth development and life satisfaction served as predictors, respectively. In addition, father-child conflict mediated the relationship between paternal overparenting and adolescent life satisfaction. Fourth, results from repeated measure - ANOVA showed that both paternal and maternal overparenting showed a decline over time (F = 17.906, p < .001). However, there was no significant difference between paternal and maternal overparenting over time (F = .72, p > .05). Fifth, we validated the Chinese Overparenting Scales using the Time 1 sample. The measurement showed excellent internal consistency and factorial validity. A paper was published based on the findings. Sixth, the findings had been disseminated to the participating schools. Moreover, the findings were presented in different social work subjects Bachelor of Arts in Social Work, Master of Social Work, Master of Arts in Family Education and Family Therapy and Doctor of Social Work programmes. Lastly, the study helped to put forth on future development overparenting research in Hong Kong and Chinese context. The PI has been awarded by the General Research Fund, the Research Grants Council to conduct a research project entitled “Parenting Perfectionism and Overparenting among Chinese Parents in Hong Kong” in 2022-2024.

15602417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15602417.value: The study provides important insights on the impacts of overparenting on adolescent developmental outcomes over time in Chinese families in Hong Kong. There is a need to disseminate the findings to school personnel of secondary schools and social workers of non-governmental organizations. Parent educational programmes may be designed and conducted to let parents understand the impacts of overparenting and how they can nurture their children without overparenting them. Besides, it is important to let the public understand the impacts of overparenting. Dissemination of the findings via mass media will be useful for parents and the public to reflect on their parenting styles. Further study on overparenting is important. Indeed, parents who exercise overparenting have good intention to ensure happiness and future success of their children, though they are over-involved and become intrusive in their children’s lives. Future study on examining the antecedents of overparenting is essential to attenuate the trend and reduce the adverse effects of overparenting on adolescents. The PI has been awarded by the General Research Fund, the Research Grants Council to conduct a research project entitled “Parenting Perfectionism and Overparenting among Chinese Parents in Hong Kong” in 2022-2024, which is regarded as a continuation of overparenting research.

15602417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15602417.value: The research project was a three-wave longitudinal study examining the relationships between overparenting and developmental outcomes of adolescents in Hong Kong over time. A sample of 1,074 junior secondary school students in Hong Kong joined the study. The findings indicated that while paternal overparenting was consistently and positively associated with adolescent narcissism, positive youth development and life satisfaction, maternal overparenting was positively associated adolescent narcissism, anxiety and depression. Besides, the initial level and trajectory of paternal overparenting predicted the rate of change of adolescents’ narcissistic behavior respectively. The trajectory of maternal overparenting also predicted the rate of change of adolescent narcissism. Moreover, the results indicated that mother-child conflict mediated the relationship between maternal overparenting and adolescent anxiety over time. A reverse association of prior adolescent anxiety with subsequent maternal overparenting via mother-child conflict was also identified. Furthermore, both paternal and maternal overparenting showed a decline over time. However, there was no significant difference between paternal and maternal overparenting over time. This study sheds new light on understanding the long-term impacts of overparenting on developmental outcomes of Chinese adolescents in early adolescence, which contributes to the development of Chinese socialization models in the modern era.

15603017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15603017.value: 據估計，每10個社區生活的老年人中就有一個遭受某種形式的虐待或忽視，在近90％的案件中，肇事者是受害者的家庭成員（National Council of Aging, 2015）。虐待不僅影響長者的身體和精神健康，更與長者的死亡風險有莫大關係（Dong et al，2011）。鑑於其影響，一些理論嘗試解釋虐老成因。這些理論包括照顧者壓力模式，其重點是照顧環境中的壓力；社會交換理論，提出肇事者和長者之間的不公平的社會交換導致虐待；社會學習理論，這表明虐待是從體驗或見證家庭暴力學習所得；和個人動態，其重點是照顧者的脆弱性。然而，大多數對虐老的研究僅僅依賴於受害者的報告，測試這些理論所提出的因素的實證研究，結果也不一致。此外，大多數測試虐老風險因素的文獻都使用了單一的理論和有限數量的因素。這些理論也沒有充分解決預防虐老的因素，亦沒有探討理論上“會虐老的照顧者”事實上不會虐待老年人 。 這項研究的目標是確定虐待老年成人的照顧者的風險模式。 這是第一個使用生態框架，結合照顧者壓力模型，社會學習理論，社會交換理論，個人動態，和其他預防虐老的因素來檢查虐老風險因素的研究。 這種模型將有助於識別虐老相關的潛在因素。 這將有助於解決先前研究中不一致的發現，包括不同理論產生的假設。 這模型也將試圖解決照顧者的個人和社會資源的緩衝效應。 這將有助於全面了解老年人的虐待，提供更有效和有針對性的預防和干預措施。 數據將從600名在香港的老年人提供照顧家庭照顧者收集。數據包括個人層面的數據，照顧者的特徵（負擔，依賴性，家庭暴力的童年經歷，神經質個性，上癮和賭博行為，照顧自我效能，韌性，社會支持），關係和被照顧者的特徵（健康狀況，自我照顧能力，依賴性），護理環境（親屬關係，持續時間和護理類型），社區支持（正式和非正式援助）以及照料者的虐待行為。虐待將被分為不同的群體（身體虐待，心理虐待，財務虐待和忽視）。假設不同類型的虐待將相互關聯，但每個都將有不同的風險模式。多標度回歸分析和結構方程模型將用於確定各種因素對虐待的各自貢獻以及不同類型的虐待之間的關聯。

15603017.label: Realisation of objectives
15603017.value: The present study aims to explore the risk and protective factors of abuse on older adults by family caregivers. A cross-sectional survey was conducted on a purposive sample of 600 family caregivers of community-dwelling older adults in Hong Kong (mean age=71.04, female=67.2%). Caregivers responded to a structured interview which consist of elder abuse behaviors, caregiver burden, care recipients’ agitated behaviours, caregiver resilience, self-efficacy, social support, and basic demographic characteristics. Analyses identified distnct risk and protetcive factors for elder abuse as well as different profiles of caregivers with varying degree of vulnerablity for committing elder abuse. Our findings provde critical insights in factors associated with elder abuse and inform relevant service development.

15603017.label: Major findings and research outcome
15603017.value: Hierarchical linear regression analysis was conducted to determine the respective conrtibution of various factors to elder abuse. Caregiver resilience was predictive of lower levels of verbal abuse, physical abuse, injury, and financial exploitation but not potentially harmful behaviour. Social support was independent with all forms of elder abuse, while self-efficacy predicted greater physical abuse after controlling for other confounding variables. Caregiver burden and agitated behaviours by care recipients remained significant risk factors in the final models when protective factors were considered. Base on the latent profile analysis, we also identified a typology of 3 distinctive caregiver profiles: (a) non-vulnerable caregivers; (b) isolated, vulnerable caregivers; and (c) traumatised, vulnerable caregivers. Isolated and traumatised caregivers reported greater risk factors related to elder mistreatment: They had higher levels of caregiver stress and burden, lower levels of social support and resilience, greater neurotic personality orientation and problematic gambling behaviour, and more severe childhood traumatic experiences. The two groups also display significantly higher level of abusive behaviors than non-vulnerable caregivers. Study findings have been disseminated in the form of conference presentations, journal and book chapter publications, as well as seminars for undergraduate students.

15603017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15603017.value: Our results suggest that promoting caregiver resiience and social support has great potential for preventing elder abuse. While conventional research focuses on risk factors for elder abuse, further research should take a more positive approach and look into ways to strengthen caregiver resilience.

15603017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15603017.value: Elder abuse negatively impact older persons, their families and the society. Efforts are needed to prevent and intervene elder abuse cases. Information on factors leading to abuse is thus of critical importance in informing service design and delivery. This study identified risk and protective factors for elder abuse by family caregivers. We found that high level of caregiver stress and care recipient agitated behaviors are risk factors for elder abuse, whereas social support, resilience and self efficacy serve protective functions and lower risk of abuse. Apart from helping caregivers to cope with the burden and stress, we proposed that prevention and intervention should target at promoting caregivers' resilience, self efficacy, and social support.

15603517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15603517.value: 現實生活中的重要決策通常要考慮多方面因素，並需要考慮許多不同的選擇，即大環境決策。然而，早期的腦神經科學模型主要是通過簡單決策的實驗而發展出來。這些實驗中，人們可以通過仔細查看每個選項，並對所有選項進行全面比較來作出決策。這些過程涉及的腦區一般包括額葉皮層 ventromedial prefrontal cortex (vmPFC) 和頂葉皮層posterior parietal cortex (PPC)。一般認為這些簡單決策的腦神機制可應用在大環境中的決策。然而，由於大腦的認知能力有局限性，將這些簡單決策的機制推展到具有大量選項的決策時可能是不合適的。因此，在抽取重要信息來進行有效率的決策時，應該需要額外的腦神經機制。 在這項研究中，我們提出了一個雙重選擇策略框架，以了解在大環境中的決策。首先，早期選擇策略涉及一種類似野外覓食類的過程，其中需要考慮在環境中抽樣新選項的成本和效益。當採集新信息的成本較高時，這種機制尤為重要。當目前的選項預期比環境中未知的選項更好時，採樣過程將會停止。我們預計與覓食決策相關的扣帶皮層 dorsal anterior cingulate cortex (dACC) 會負責這種早期選擇策略。第二，在晚期選擇策略中，環境中所有選項己經採樣。但是，只有一部分選項將被重視和主導決策。當採集新信息的成本較低和己知的選項較多時，這種機制特別重要。我們預計晚期選擇策略涉及處理決策信息的額葉皮層 lateral prefrontal cortex (lPFC)。這種雙重選擇框架得到了本計劃書中的眼動數據支持。 我們會設計一項決策任務，當中參與者需要在不同採樣成本的情況下在大量選項之間作出決策。 我們的建議包括兩個實驗。 實驗一，我們將使用功能磁共振造影（fMRI）來測試早期和晚期選擇策略的腦神經機制。 實驗二，我們將使用經顱直流刺激（tDCS）來測試實驗一中的腦區與決策的因果關係。

15603517.label: Realisation of objectives
15603517.value: Objective 1: To test the Dual-Selection Framework (Early-Selection Strategy and Late-Selection Strategy) for decision making in large environments. This objective is the primary objective, whereas Objectives 2-4 are the sub-objectives under this. This project has already generated three manuscripts to address the issue of decision making in large environments, including one published in Cerebral Cortex (impact factor=5.375), one published in Behavioural Pharmacology (impact factor=2.206), and one preprint archived at Research Square. In addition, there is a fourth manuscript that is currently under preparation. In brief, we have provided evidence supporting the Dual-Selection Framework using a combination of eye tracking, functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and non-invasive neurostimulation with human participants. We found that the lateral prefrontal cortex (lPFC), posterior parietal cortex (PPC) and anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) have dissociable roles in selecting choice information. Objective 2: To demonstrate that whether Early-Selection Strategy or Late-Selection Strategy is predominantly employed depends on the cost of sampling information. In the Behavioural Pharmacology paper, we describe that the ACC encodes the sampling cost and that influences whether an agent will select an effortful course of action to obtain large rewards during decision making. In the preprint manuscript, we also reported that the ACC encodes the amount of cost invested in the past for sampling information and its influence on determining whether further information is sampled in the expense of additional cost. Objective 3: To investigate the roles of vmPFC/PPC, dACC and lPFC in decision making using neuroimaging and to test whether these brain regions are predominately involved in simple decision making, Early-Selection Strategy and Late-Selection Strategy respectively. In a fMRI experiment, we found that vmPFC is involved in comparing option values during decision making. We found that both PPC and ACC are related to Early-Selection of choice information. However, the two regions differ by encoding difference choice information – the PPC encodes information related to choice uncertainty, whereas the ACC encodes information related to choice switching. Finally, the lPFC is related to the filtering of choice information in during a late-selection process. Objective 4: To demonstrate the causal roles of the neural regions for decision making in large environments using neurostimulation methods. This was achieved by performing neurostimulation that targeted at lPFC and PPC. The causal role of the neural regions during decision making are reported in the Cerebral Cortex paper and the preprint manuscript.

15603517.label: Major findings and research outcome
15603517.value: This research has generated two publications (Chau et al., Behavioural Pharmacology, 2018; Woo et al., Cerebral Cortex, 2021), one preprint manuscript (archived at Research Square, currently reviewed at eLife), one manuscript in preparation, two conference abstracts and one science exhibition booth at the Hong Kong Laureate Forum. This project has also successfully trained one MPhil student, Cristian Giron, who graduated in the summer of 2020. We provided evidence supporting the dual-selection framework of obtaining choice information in large environments. In the Behavioural Pharmacology paper, we explained the dissociable roles of multiple neural regions in decision making. This involves the ventromedial prefrontal cortex (vmPFC) that encodes signals for value comparisons between options and the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) that encodes the cost for obtaining choice information and executing the choice. In the Cerebral Cortex paper, we focused more specifically on the causal roles of lateral prefrontal cortex (lPFC) and posterior parietal cortex (PPC) on selecting choice information, especially in large environments with many options. This was achieved by conducting a combination of eye tracking and neurostimulation in human participants. We found that the lPFC has a specific role in filtering out choice irrelevant information, especially when people had to choose between many options. In contrast, the PPC has a specific role in value-based spatial selection. In the preprint manuscript, we further investigate the role of PPC in value and information encoding. Previous studies suggested that in large environments when there are multiple options, the neural signals related to the value of the options can interfere each other. It has been suggested this interference is mediated via the PPC. Hence, this study tested notion by involving an experiment that used a similar approach as in the Cerebral Cortex paper – performing eye tracking and neurostimulation in human participants. We found that when the PPC activity was disrupted using neurostimulation, the interference between options was also attenuated. Finally, in the manuscript in preparation, we examined the roles of vmPFC, ACC and PPC on decision making in large environments in a single neuroimaging experiments. We found that vmPFC is involved in simple decision making. We found that both PPC and ACC are related to Early-Selection of choice information. However, the two regions differ by encoding difference choice information – the PPC encodes information related to choice uncertainty, whereas the ACC encodes information related to choice switching.

15603517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15603517.value: This research has inspired a new research idea that investigate neural mechanisms of decision making between multiple environments. I have written a research proposal about this new idea and it has been supported by the General Research Fund in 2019.

15603517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15603517.value: Important decisions in real lives are often multifaceted and require people to consider between many different options i.e. a large environment. However, early models of decision neuroscience were predominantly developed by studies that employed simple decision making paradigms with only a few options. Due to the limited cognitive capacity of the brain, it might be inappropriate to extend these models to describe real life decision making that involves large number of options. Hence, efficient decision making should involve neural mechanisms for selecting the most relevant information for making a choice. In this project, we propose a Dual-Selection Framework that describes decision making in large environments involves multiple strategies to obtain choice information. This was tested by performing a series of experiments that involved eye tracking, neurostimulation, and brain imaging. We found that vmPFC is involved in comparing option values during decision making. We found that both PPC and ACC are related to Early-Selection of choice information. However, the two regions differ by encoding difference choice information – the PPC encodes information related to choice uncertainty, whereas the ACC encodes information related to choice switching. Finally, the lPFC is related to the filtering of choice information in during a late-selection process.

15605017.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15605017.value: 保護環境及拯救生命: 中國的環境獎項能否減少企業營運風險？

15605017.label: Project Objectives
15605017.value: Using major environmental awards at the national level as a proxy, we estimate the effectiveness of excellent environmental management in reducing operational risks in China, including environmental casualties and violations of environmental regulations. By adopting propensity-score matching and difference-in-difference analysis of closely related firms, we seek to quantify the effectiveness of environmental awards in reducing the number of casualties in environmental accidents, translating to potential saving in human lives. We postulate and verify if the efficacy of environmental awards in reducing environmental casualties and regulatory violations is strengthened when firms simultaneously possess a positive CSR attitude, improve environmental disclosures, and enhance operational capability. More generally, we explore the factors that will make corporate environmental initiatives more effective in operational risk reduction.

15605017.label: Realisation of objectives
15605017.value: We believe that the three objectives of this research have been fully realized. Following the suggestions of the reviewers, we focused on environmental accreditation systems of ISO 14001, instead of general environmental awards in China. We investigate the impact of ISO 14001 adoption on operational risks as proxied by regulatory violations and casualties, and the moderating roles of government monitor and slack resources. Existing OM literature mainly evaluates the outcomes of environmental initiatives from an efficiency perspective. Nevertheless, it is less understood how environmental initiative could contribute to the well-being of people. We collected data from multiple sources and used propensity-score matching and difference-in-difference analysis to draw the causal influence of ISO 14001 on operational risks. As such, we estimated the quantitative impact of environmental management systems adoption on operational risks, while controlling for selection bias and endogeneity. We also conducted the triple-difference model to examine the moderating impacts of government monitor and slack resources. Finally, a series of robustness tests and extension analysis were conducted to ensure that the results are reliable. This study shows that environmental accreditations in China significantly decrease operational risks. For firms that receive government monitor, the impact of environmental accreditations on casualties is strengthened. For firms with more slack resources, the impact of ISO 14001 adoption on regulatory violations is weakened. Traditionally, researchers in OM tend to focus on efficiency and economic benefits, but hidden behind these visible measures are the burdens to the environment and human beings. We examined the relationship between ISO 14001 adoption and operational risk, bringing considerations for people’s well-being into sharp focus. We further examined the impact of ISO 14001 adoption on operating risks and sales growth, and the moderating effects of certification time and industrial pollution level. Low financial risk and high sales growth are indicators for a firm’s resilience performance. Following the signaling theory, we proposed that environmental accreditations demonstrate a firm’s credibility and capability to its shareholders and customers, thus mitigating operating risk and enhancing sales growth. We employed propensity-score matching and difference-in-difference models to test the hypotheses and then conducted robustness tests. The findings suggest that environmental accreditations lead to paradoxical outcomes: it decreases financial risks and attenuates market growth simultaneously. Early certification exacerbates the paradox by reducing more financial risk and diminishing more market growth. Adoption of firms in high-polluting industries alleviates the paradoxical outcome by decreasing more financial risk and harming less market growth. We provided empirical evidence for whether it pays to adopt corporate environmental initiatives. Based on the signaling theory, we resolved a puzzle about the impact of environmental accreditations on financial risk and sales growth. Financial risk refers to the idiosyncratic volatility of stock returns. The higher the financial risk, the more uncertain shareholders perceive about a firm’s future financial stability. Sales growth, on the other hand, stands for a firm’s potential to grow and prosper, indicating its full exploitation of existing resources and abundant opportunities. Low financial risk and high sales growth signify a firm’s long-term and stable development. Investigating this relationship helps understand the potential and long-term influence of ISO 14001 adoption. We linked corporate environmental initiatives to risk outcomes, including financial and operational risk, bridging the gap between environmental and risk management. Risk management has been a popular topic in recent years. A high level of operational risk incurs tremendous financial loss, damages firm reputation, and requires substantial costs to recover. Similarly, a high level of financial risk impairs a firm’s stability of cash flow and weakens the anticipation of future development. By scrutinizing the relationship between ISO 14001 adoption and risk, the research contributes to the literature in risk management. In short, our study enriches empirical studies about Chinese firms’ environmental initiatives. Due to the lack of existing database about environmental management, there is a scarcity of research using secondary data. Most studies in the past adopted survey-based studies, leading to common method bias and endogeneity concerns. Moreover, cross-sectional data in the past provided no evidence on possible causal relationships. We collected data from multiple sources and formed a unique secondary database, which could be used to establish causal relationships.

15605017.label: Major findings and research outcome
15605017.value: We believe that our findings are very significant to the literature. First, this study unveils a previously under-researched outcome of environmental initiatives. As mentioned above, we focused environmental accreditations of ISO 14001, instead of general environmental awards in China. Previous research has indicated that ISO 14001 adoption could improve environmental and financial performance, but there has been little research focusing on operational risk. This study shows that ISO 14001 adoption significantly decreases operational risks. For firms that receive government monitor, the impact of ISO 14001 adoption on casualties is strengthened. For firms with more slack resources, the impact of ISO 14001 adoption on regulatory violations is weakened. We consider the risk of regulatory violations and environmental casualties as two proxies of operational risks and demonstrates that saving the environment can save lives. The people-oriented mindset stresses on identifying the external social impact of firm practices. We suggest that in future operations management research, more attention should be paid to hidden costs (i.e., impact on people, environment, and society) beyond economics and efficiency considerations. Our findings further suggest that ISO 14001 adoption reduces financial risk while harming sales growth, implying a trade-off between promoting buffering and enabling capabilities. Reducing financial risk is vital for stable development such that firms may focus on core technology, conduct innovative activities, and win competitive advantages in highly turbulent environments (Luo and Bhattacharya, 2009; Lam, 2018). However, rapid growth and sustained stability can be opposing objectives in implementing ISO 14001. Managers should find a balance in maximizing benefits, based on the needs of the firm. Start-up firms seeking rapid expansion should be cautious about obtaining ISO 14001 certification. The requirements for ISO 14001 can involve much effort, and the standard management system may hinder firms’ search for resources and opportunities. In contrast, for firms pursuing stability, ISO 14001 adoption can aid in systematically improving processes and gaining support from shareholders. Especially as some medium- or large-sized firms reached a bottleneck in regard to market expansion, adopting ISO 14001 would be beneficial for their long-term stability. Furthermore, managers may fundamentally resolve the trade-off between maintaining stability and boosting growth, and to this end they could search for alternative environmental management instruments. (2009), "The Debate over Doing Good: Corporate Social Performance, Strategic Marketing Levers, and Firm-Idiosyncratic Risk", Journal of Marketing, Vol. 73 No. 6, pp. 198-213.

15605017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15605017.value: There are some potentials for further development of this research. First, in examining the relationship between environmental initiatives and performance, we adopted ISO 14001 certification as the proxy. Other possible proxies include environmental innovation, supply chain environmental management, and environmental information disclosure. Different types of environmental initiatives may lead to inconsistent results. Previous research found that investors have different reactions to environmental practices related to products and processes; another previous research found that self-disclosed and third-party certified environmental practices lead to different abnormal stock returns. Therefore, it is necessary to explore the difference between different types of environmental initiatives. Second, we used regulatory violations and casualties as proxies for operational risk. Since there is no available database, the variables can only be formed by self-search, which suffers from subjectivity in the screening process. Future studies may try to develop other proxies for operational risk. At the same time, it is an urgent need to promote information disclosure of Chinese firms and establish databases for academic research. Third, we included government monitor and slack resources as moderators from the perspective of institutional theory and resource-based view. We further adopted the certification time and industrial pollution level as a moderator from the perspective of signal theory. Future research can further expand the scope of moderating variables from corresponding theoretical perspectives, such as media exposure, operational capabilities, industry complexity, and market uncertainty. Also, since the research is based on Chinese firms, more Chinese unique features can be considered, such as political connection and legal unprotectability. Overall, we suggest that in future operations management research, more attention should be paid to hidden costs (i.e., impact on people, environment, and society) beyond economics and efficiency considerations.

15606317.label: Project Objectives
15606317.value: The study aims to use prospective design to test the intervention effects of perspective-taking reappraisals. Based on positive findings of our pilot studies, we test a comprehensive 12-week Connecting Through Caregiving (CTC) intervention involving the following components: relational insight, self-awareness, empathetic understanding balancing self-care and caring for others and negotiating action plans. The CTC program will be evaluated against a Basic Skill Building (BSB) as active control in two-arm randomized controlled trial of 12 weeks of intervention. Participants in each group receive a total of approximately 12 hours of training through 2 home visits, 2 group sessions and 8 telephone-administered sessions. Measures are obtained at baseline Weeks 1 (baseline), 6 and 12 (post-intervention) with a follow-up at Week 24. We test whether, as compared to those in BSB, CTC participants would show greater progress with the primary outcomes in terms of decreased levels of depressive symptoms and enhanced psychological well-being. We test whether, as compared to those in BSB, CTC participants would show greater progress with the secondary outcomes (enhanced social support, reduced levels in blood pressure and intergeneration ambivalence for caregivers and decrease in behavioral problems for care recipients and associated decreased caregiver’s distress). We examine the possible mediation effects of perspective taking strategies on intervention with regard to the primary outcomes. We examine whether caregivers with higher levels of initial burden will benefit more from CTC.

15606317.label: Realisation of objectives
15606317.value: The study aims to use prospective design to test the intervention effects of perspective-taking reappraisals. Based on positive findings of our pilot studies, we test a comprehensive 12-week Connecting Through Caregiving (CTC) intervention involving the following components: relational insight, self-awareness, empathetic understanding balancing self-care and caring for others and negotiating action plans. The CTC program will be evaluated against a Basic Skill Building (BSB) as active control in two-arm randomized controlled trial of 12 weeks of intervention. Measures are obtained at baseline Weeks 1 (baseline), 6 and 12 (post-intervention) with a follow-up at Week 24. The objectives listed above were all fulfilled. In the interim report, we have informed and sorted approval to conduct the RCT with clustered randomized controlled in order to facilitate the organization of the meetings for the participants in the centres. Within the RCT research framework, we have improved our research design in the actual implementation process. We also found out that if we recruited participants of both conditions in the same center, we could not prevent the participants from sharing information. The risk involved the control group participants inadvertently being exposed to the intervention which they were not supposed to be involved in. Thus contamination bias can potentially minimize the difference in outcomes between the two groups. We have conducted a Cluster RCT to minimize contamination bias. The project has been completed through randomized cluster control trial. Eighteen community centers were involved. A total of 191 adult caregiver participants were recruited. 91 completed CTC and 81 completed BSB. The attrition rate for both groups were about 11%. There were no significant differences between the 2 groups in terms of relationship with care-recipients (mostly daughters), education (both secondary and tertiary), occupation (mostly full-time). Most of the care recipients across the two groups mostly females in their seventies with moderate dementia and attending community centers. The framework of the intervention protocols were based on Au et al. (2020 & 2019): 1) Au, A., Lai, D. W. L., Biggs, S., Cheng, S.-T., Haapala-Biggs, I., Chow, A., & Gallagher-Thompson, D. (2020). Perspective-taking interventions for intergenerational caregivers of Alzheimer's diseases: A randomized controlled trial. Research on Social Work Practice, 30(3), 306-319. doi: 10.1177/1049731519864165 2) Au, A., Yip, H. M., Lai, S., Ngai, S., Cheng, S. T., Losada, A., Thompson, L. & Gallagher-Thompson, D. (2019) Telephone-based Behavioral Activation Intervention for Dementia Family Caregivers: Outcomes and Mediation Effect of a Randomized Controlled Trial. Patient Education and Counseling. 102, 2049-59, 30: 306-19. doi:10.1016/j.pec.2019.06.009 The final version of the intervention protocol and questionnaire had incorporated comments and suggestions from with an interdisciplinary team with expertise in counseling, social work and clinical psychology. The objectives of the project were judged to be well-realized. Results obtained provided empirical support for an intervention model incorporating the facilitation of self-awareness and empathetic insight. The present study contributes to the literature by highlighting the importance of perspective-taking reappraisals to take into account the balance of self-care and caring for others and provides evidence that perspective-taking reappraisal.

15606317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15606317.value: In terms of implications for practice, the CTC project has successfully engaged social service agencies to promote the program and recruit caregivers in need to join the intervention and complete research-based evaluations. Trained professionals delivered the program with interdisciplinary collaboration with expertise in counseling, social work and clinical psychology. This work contributes to the recent initiatives to promote the health and social work collaboration to enhance support for dementia in Hong Kong. As interdisciplinary collaboration and training is needed for dealing with the needs of AD familiar caregivers, the present intervention has the potential of further contributing to the training of professionals across disciplines to sustain the care of AD caregivers in the community. We have trained some staff at the community centres to implement the program and run the groups. Some NGOs (e.g. Hong Kong Family Welfare Society) have been give details of the protocol. We are also planning for collaboration with countries where community or public services are just developing and the demand for family caregiving is high due to collectivistic concerns. An abstract submission has been made to the British Geriatrics Society Conference to be held later this year.

15606317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15606317.value: Purpose: The present study examined the effects of perspective-taking intervention in the context of intergenerational caregiving. Method: One-hundred seventy-two adult child caregivers of persons living with Alzheimer’s disease (AD) were randomized into two twelve-week interventions: 1) Connecting through Caregiving with intergenerational perspective-taking reappraisals (CTC: 91 participants) and 2) Basic Skill Building (BSB: 81participants). The CTC intervention focused on perspective-taking reappraisals aiming to promote balance between self-care and caring of others: 1) connecting with self through enhancing self-awareness, 2) connecting with the care-recipient and 3) connecting with others who can help. Results: In terms of primary outcomes, as compared to the BSB group, the CTC group reported significantly higher increase greater reductions in depressive symptoms and higher levels of psychological well-being. For the secondary outcomes, the CTC group scored higher in emotional and instrumental support and also lower levels of perceived presence and reaction to behavioral and memory problems of the care recipient. Perspective-taking was found to mediate between intervention effects and reduction of depressive symptoms of the caregiver. Discussion: The results provided evidence for the efficacy of the CTC program. The present findings can be relevant to countries where the demand for family caregiving is high due to collectivistic concerns.

15606617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15606617.value: The proposed study is a new and original one aiming primarily to enable hospitality industry practitioners to handle negative online reviews more effectively, and to enrich the existing literature discussing the linguistics of hotel management’s responses to such reviews – termed the ‘review response genre’ in this proposal. To achieve these aims, the study will explore first the moves (i.e. components) present and the sequence in which they are presented, and second the linguistic strategies hotel management uses to manage rapport with the readers of the review responses and to persuade them to (re)purchase the hospitality services. The data comprises hotel management’s responses to the negative online reviews accessible and downloadable freely from TripAdvisor, transcribed interviews with the hospitality practitioners responsible for writing the responses, and written feedback from reviewers – those customers posting the negative comments on TripAdvisor. Methodological triangulation will be used to increase the reliability and validity of the proposed study. Qualitative content analyses will lead to the identification of first, moves like Acknowledging Problem and Expressing Feelings (e.g. happiness and regret); second, rapport management strategies (e.g. management of the reviewers’ face wants when agreeing with the reviewers, and management of the reviewers’ interactional goal by offering an apology or explanation); and third, metadiscourse used in the hotel management’s persuasive attempts. Quantitative statistical analysis will reveal the relationship between star-rating of hotels and the pattern of use of moves and metadiscourse in the genre. This original study is significant as it can (1) provide hospitality practitioners with a set of linguistic resources and suggestions for responding to negative online reviews in a way which would probably lead to service recovery and increased business; (2) increase the explanatory power of the genre theory and the metadiscourse construct; (3) inform the design of the syllabus and teaching of English for specific purposes; and (4) make methodological advancement through demonstrating the adoption of mixed methods in researching the review response genre. 該研究是全新而又原創的，主要目的是讓酒店行業的從業者能夠更有效得處理網上的負面評論，亦能夠豐富現存的著作對酒店從業者對此類評論的回應的語言研究，我們稱之為“評論回應文體”。 為了達到這些目的，本研究將首先探索它所呈現的話步（moves），例如成分組件，和它們所呈現的順序。其次，會探索酒店行業管理者處理與讀者關係并說服他們（再次）購買酒店服務時所採用的語言策略。 研究數據由幾部分構成： 可在貓途鷹（TripAdvisor）網站上免費下載的酒店管理者對網上的負面評價的回應，對負責回應評論的酒店管理者採訪的轉錄，以及顧客在網站上發佈的書面反饋。本研究將會使用三角交叉檢視法（Methodological triangulation）， 來提高該研究可靠性和有效性。定性的內容分析將可以鑒定出：1）承認問題和表達情感的話步，例如高興或遺憾；2）處理關係的策略，例如因顧忌評價者的面子而作出的對其評價的認同，和通過道歉或解釋以達到互動的目的；3）酒店行業管理者在說服過程中使用的元話語。定量統計分析將可顯示出酒店的評級與其使用這種話步和元話語的模式之間的關係。 這個原創的研究具有重大的意義，因為它可以1）為酒店行業提供一套語言材料及建議去應對網上的負面評價，為其服務補救及增加業務提供可能性；2）增加文體理論和元話語概念的解釋力；3）為教學大綱的制定和為專門用途英語的教學提供資料；4）通過採用多種混合方法的研究方式，取得方法論上的提升。

15606617.label: Realisation of objectives
15606617.value: Objective 1: Fully achieved The move structures of the genre have been identified – there are a total of 11 moves, with three being obligatory and the other eight optional. The rapport management strategies have been identified – managers enhanced and challenged rapport with dissatisfied customers by managing the latter’s face wants, sociality rights and obligations, and interactional goals with the obligatory and/or optional moves. The persuasive strategies employed by hotel management have also been identified – managers made appeals to rationality, credibility and character, and emotions with metadiscourse. Objective 2: Fully achieved Statistically significant differences between managerial responses written by hotels of different ratings in terms of the move structures, rapport management (through the strategic use of moves), and persuasion strategies (through the use of metadiscourse) were found. Objective 3: Fully achieved The genre theory and the interpersonal model of metadiscourse were drawn upon successfully in the study. Objective 4: Fully achieved Three types of data were collected – managerial responses downloaded from TripAdvisor, questionnaire responses collected from experienced travellers, and interview responses collected from hotels managers who were actually responsible for writing responses to online reviews. These data were analysed quantitatively and qualitatively.

15606617.label: Major findings and research outcome
15606617.value: (a) Move structures (please see Items 8.1, 8.6 & 9.1) (i) Three obligatory and eight optional moves were identified: • Obligatory: Expressing Feeling and Wish, Thanking Reviewer, and Acknowledging Problem • Optional: Self-promoting, Continuing Relationship, Denying Problem, Recognizing Reviewer’s/Comment’s Value, Greeting, Offering Assistance, Agreeing with Reviewer, and Accusing Reviewer (ii) Order of appearance The most common order of appearance of the obligatory moves was Thanking Reviewer > Acknowledging Problem/Expressing Feeling and Wish > Expressing Feeling and Wish (b) Rapport management (please see Items 8.2, 8.3, 8.4, 8.5, 8.6, 9.2, 9.5 & 9.6) The moves identified were shown to either enhance or challenge rapport, as shown below: (i) Rapport-enhancing moves • Enhancing face: Thanking Reviewer; Acknowledging Problem (Empathizing); Recognizing Reviewer’s/Comment’s Value; Agreeing with Reviewer • Fulfilling sociality rights and obligations: Expressing Feeling & Wish; Continuing Relationship; Greeting; Agreeing with Reviewer; Offering Assistance • Facilitating achievement of readers’ interactional goals: Acknowledging Problem (Apologizing, Explaining Cause of Problem, and Rectifying Problem) (ii) Rappport-challenging moves • Threatening face: Self-promoting; Denying Problem; Accusing Reviewer • Ignoring sociality rights and obligations: Self-promoting • Ignoring achievement of readers’ interactional goals: Self-promoting; Denying Problem (c) Persuasion (please see Items 8.1, 8.3, 8.6, 9.1, 9.3, 9.5 & 9.6) (i) Persuasive attempts were made by appealing to logos, ethos, and pathos with metadiscourse: • Appeals to rationality (i.e. logos) were made using transitions, frame markers, endophoric markers, and code glosses; • Appeals to credibility and characters (i.e. ethos) were made using hedges, boosters, and a combination of hedges, boosters, and self-mentions; • Appeals to emotions (i.e. pathos) were made using attitude markers, engagement markers, hedges, and a combination of self-mentions and attitude markers. (ii) The review response genre shows a characteristic pattern of use of metadiscourse, distinguishing itself from other genres that have been studied extensively from a metadiscourse perspective (the genres of research articles, university textbooks, policy documents, and workplace request emails). It has comparatively less interactive metadiscourse but more interactional metadiscourse. (d) Distinguishing features of management responses written by hotels of different star-ratings (please see Items 8.6, 9.3 & 9.5) (i) Managers of 4- or 5-star hotels included in their responses seven moves more often than those of 2- or 3-star ones: Expressing Feeling and Wish, Thanking Reviewer, Acknowledging Problem, Self-promoting, Continuing Relationship, Recognizing Reviewer’s / Comment’s Value, Greeting, and Offering Assistance. (ii) Managers of 4- or 5-star hotels enhanced rapport with dissatisfied customers more often than those of 2- or 3-star hotels. (iii) Managers of 2- or 3-star hotels used metadiscourse more often than 4- or 5-star ones, in particular attitude markers, self mentions, and engagement markers.

15606617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15606617.value: The research can be extended to other key industries that are also receiving online reviews and are thus subject to public scrutiny. A pilot study can be conducted investigating the management responses to negative reviews provided by dissatisfied customers of the car industry (e.g. Tesla), telecommunications industry (e.g. CSL), and paid entertainment industry (e.g. cable TV). These industries have witnessed a rapid growth and popularity worldwide on the one hand, and received an increasing number of complaints on the other. The way the leading companies/enterprises of these key industries addressed negative reviews and handled complaints can be studied from a linguistic perspective.

15606617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15606617.value: The research project studied hotel management responses to negative online reviews posted by dissatisfied customers on one of the most popular travel-related websites, TripAdvisor. It conducted a multi-perspective analysis of authentic management responses to negative reviews, questionnaire responses given by frequent travellers with experience using TripAdvisor, and opinions of hotel managers tasked with responding to negative online reviews. The study has obtained findings that are important to the hotel industry and the academia: (1) the structure (the components and their sequence of appearance) of the management responses; (2) the strategies hotel managers used in improving their harmonious relationships with their dissatisfied customers; (3) the strategies managers used in persuading the readers of their responses to (re)purchase accommodations services from their hotels; and (4) the language features of the responses produced by hotels of different star-ratings. Hotel managers will have access to useful linguistics resources and ideas that can help them write effective responses to achieve service recovery. The academia can benefit in two ways. First, the existing literature on service recovery and online managerial responses will be enriched. Second, English courses for students majoring in hotel management can enrich their syllabus by making reference to the findings.

15607217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15607217.value: Relative Clause has been intensely investigated in language typology, acquisition and processing for decades. Cantonese relative clauses have word order properties that are distinctly rare across languages of the world. Given its special word order properties, Cantonese is an important language in debates regarding acquisition and processing of RCs, because it allows researchers to tease apart predictions regarding the relative complexity of subject versus object relative clauses. Despite its importance, to date there has been very little published research on the acquisition and processing of Cantonese relative clauses. This project deals with a classical observation from the literature that young children often find object relatives hard to process, while subject relatives are easier. The project aims to address the following important issues that have not been significantly addressed in the literature. First, why are object relative clauses not always harder than subject relative clauses for Cantonese children? Second, how do structural versus linear influences compete and vary in strength in the course of a child’s language development, which could give rise to possible variations in subject-object processing preference as children grow older? Third, why do we consistently observe individual differences in asymmetry patterns in Cantonese that are more variable than in European languages like English? Fourth, what is the nature and source of difficulty for processing Cantonese object relative clauses? Our proposed project links experimental psycholinguistics and structurally and functionally oriented perspectives in the study of relative clause processing in child and adult Cantonese. We use experimental methods involving eye-tracking, elicited production and elicited imitation, as well as a longitudinal study that yield both online and offline data to analyze children’s comprehension and production of relative clauses. The project also incorporates a novel within-subjects design to capture developmental changes in the same group of children. We will document patterns of subject-object asymmetry in Cantonese relative clause processing across a range of relativisation strategies; and examine their relation to (i) intervention or competition effects, in light of structurally-oriented theories like relativized minimality and functionally-oriented theories like the competition model; (ii) structural versus linear effects; and (iii) individual differences. The project findings will lay necessary groundwork for future Cantonese studies on clinical populations such as children with Specific Language Impairment. The complementary expertise of the research team will ensure wide dissemination of our findings not only for language acquisition and processing research, but also for research on language typology and morphosyntax.

15607217.label: Realisation of objectives
15607217.value: To better contextualize the report, Principal Investigator(PI) wishes to first outline the 3 major challenges and the solutions, before elaborating on realization of the project objectives (POs). 1. Limited funding to run a three-year longitudinal project Since the funding was substantially cut to half (original funding requested: HK$734,212; funding granted HK$359,600 plus university matching fund: HK$ 35,960), it was insufficient to fully fund a PhD student for three years, as originally planned. To save money while still being able to achieve the POs, PI had the following solutions: (i) recruited a promising RA who later won the RGC-Hong Kong PhD Fellowship to develop this research project and extend it to Cantonese-speaking children with and without Developmental Language Disorder (DLD) under PI’s supervision; and (ii) recruited another half-time RA and 17 part-time student helpers to assist with data collection and coding, and 9 BA students and 1 master-degree student in Speech Therapy (MST) to use subsets of the data for their final-year/capstone research projects under PI’s supervision. 2. Subject recruitment Another challenge was that it has taken us longer than expected to recruit as many as 90 three-year-olds and each child needs to be tested in multiple sessions (as many as 10) to complete all tasks at one age level. This challenge was overcome after having approached more than 20 kindergartens- in the end, 7 kindergartens were willing to take part, allowing us to achieve the original goal of recruiting 90 three-year-olds. 3. Testing disruptions due to social unrest and COVID This project experienced multiple hiccups in testing due to social unrest in 2019, PolyU campus and schools closure, and then COVID-disruptions since 2020. Moreover, one major method (the referent selection eye tracking task) requires in-person testing and cannot resort to online testing. PI had the following solutions: (i) in times when in-person testing were not feasible, PI supervised the research personnel to conduct 2 corpus studies on 78 Cantonese-speaking children to address POs 1, 2 and 4 using naturalistic speech samples; (ii) in times when kindergartens were closed and parents of kindergarten children were reluctant to let their child take part in in-person testing, but parents of primary-school children were less reluctant for in-person testing, PI supervised the research personnel to test 66 Cantonese-speaking primary schoolers with and without DLD to address POs 1, 2 and 4 using production and offline/online comprehension experimental data; and (iii) PI seized certain time slots when parents of kindergarteners were more willing to continue with in-person testing and when our student helpers were available to conduct the testing in the midst of also catching up with their other coursework requirements within their packed weekly schedules. Although these solutions were very tedious to implement, PI is thankful to report the following positive outcomes. Project Objectives (POs) 1, 2, 4 were fully addressed. Specifically: PO1 related to elucidating subject-object asymmetry in Cantonese RC comprehension and production was addressed in Publication 1 (see Part C) using elicited production data, Publication 2 using naturalistic speech data, Publication 3 using offline and online comprehension data, Publication 4 using elicited imitation data, and Publications 5 and 6 using longitudinal data of comprehension and production respectively. Moreover, PO1 related to the structuralist notion of intervention was addressed Publications 5 and 6, while PO1 related to the functionalist notion of competition was addressed in Publications 1, 3 and 4. PO2 related to the dynamic change of subject-object asymmetry in RC processing in the course of a child’s development and how effects of the structural, linear and other functional factors impact on preference in production and comprehension were addressed in Publication 2 based on naturalistic speech data and Publications 5 and 6 based on the longitudinal experimental datasets in comprehension and production. PO4 related to evaluating current theories/hypotheses against new empirical evidence was addressed in every publication. Theoretically, the project incorporated the typological perspective that Cantonese, being one of the best-known Sinitic languages in addition to Mandarin, offers a good opportunity to test some opposing predictions from emergentism versus structurally-oriented perspectives in the acquisition of subject-RCs versus object-RCs. In addition, given the multi-functionality of Cantonese classifiers that resemble the neighboring Southern Sinitic languages and Miao-Yao languages more than Mandarin, Cantonese offers a unique opportunity to discuss the role of function in the acquisition of RCs and its related constructions, where a functionalist approach to language is a major feature of emergentism. Moreover, the project also incorporated the typological perspective that Cantonese is an attributive clause language, as a conceptual motivation to examine the acquisition of conventional RCs and their related noun modifying clause constructions. The new findings also bear on the long-standing debate of domain-specific versus domain-general theories of language acquisition and DLD. Furthermore, the findings addressed the applicability of NPAH perspectives in a Chinese and East Asian language context, where the new data did not align with the predictions based on NPAH, and were better accounted for by domain-general perspectives. PO3, related to examining the predictive validity of working memory in accounting for individual differences was only 70% achieved at this point. To address PO3, PI has a paper-in-preparation titled “Individual differences in Cantonese-speaking children's competence with object and subject relative clauses: contrasting different theoretical perspectives”. The paper aims to examine the nature of difficulty in processing Cantonese object- and subject-RCs in children; and to examine the predictive validity of working memory in accounting for individual differences in Cantonese-speaking children. The 3-year-olds’ data were analyzed but nothing interesting came out likely because of their low accuracy in general. The multiple disruptions in testing due to social unrest and COVID have caused the research team taking much longer than planned: we could finally transcribe, code and input all the longitudinal experimental data at data points aged 3, 4 and 5 only in April 2022. The research team also needs more time to identify the best statistical models for this longitudinal dataset and to match with the conceptual framing. PI hopes to finalize the statistical analyses and theoretical interpretations and write up the findings for journal submission in the coming months. The following hypotheses would be tested: (i) Nature of difficulty with Cantonese ORCs: If the source of difficulty with ORCs stems from structural intervention, we would expect that children’s competence with other structures that also involve object A-bar dependencies and structural intervention (e.g. object topicalization and object focalization structures in Cantonese) will be the strongest predictor accounting for individual differences in ORC processing. By contrast, if perspective shift is the primary determinant for ORC difficulty, we would expect that cognitive abilities that involve perspective shift like executive functioning and backward digit span would be the strongest predictors accounting for individual differences in ORC processing. On the other hand, if conventional RCs (SRCs and ORCs alike) are a subtype of a general noun modifying clause construction (NMCC) that is semantically-pragmatically governed in Chinese, one could hypothesize based on this typological perspective that children’s competence with gapless RCs may be the strongest predictor accounting for individual differences in ORC (and SRC) processing. (ii) Nature of difficulty with Cantonese SRCs: If Cantonese SRCs are challenging to process due to having to resolve a longer dependency between the head noun and the missing argument, children’s forward digit span measures might predict their performance with Cantonese SRCs.

To examine the predictive validity of working memory in accounting for individual differences;
To evaluate current theories/hypotheses against new empirical evidence.

15607217.label: Major findings and research outcome
15607217.value: Despite the multiple challenges mentioned in 5.3, this project has been tremendously blessed with the following outcomes. - The project generated valuable datasets that cover naturalistic speech production, offline and online experimental comprehension, elicited production, elicited imitation, pre-school and school-aged children, children with Typical Development (TD) and children with Developmental Language Disorder (DLD), different RC types (subject, object, indirect object, oblique, genitive), different RC strategies (classifier, GE, hybrid), different RC conditions (with similar vs dissimilar NPs). - The major findings document robust variations at different levels: (i) variations in subject-object asymmetry between comprehension and production and between sentence conditions with similar vs dissimilar NPs in the same children, and variations in subject-object asymmetry that changed across ages in a longitudinal design, which- collectively- point towards a lack of robust subject-over-object RC advantage; (ii) variations between RC types that suggest a reverse ranking of difficulty inconsistent with the Noun Phrase Accessibility Hierarchy(NPAH); (iii) variations between RC strategies consistent with some input frequency effects; and (iv) variations between children with TD and DLD that challenge predictions from the structurally-oriented accounts, while the domain-general emergentist approach offers a better explanation. - These findings are empirically and theoretically significant in many ways. Empirically, these novel comprehensive data and the experimental manipulations are an empirical first not only in the Chinese TD and DLD literature but also the East Asian languages TD and DLD literature. Theoretically, the findings incorporate the typological perspective that Cantonese is an attributive clause language, as a conceptual motivation to examine the acquisition of conventional RCs and their related noun modifying clause constructions. The findings also bear on the long-standing debate of domain-specific versus domain-general theories of language acquisition and DLD, and address the applicability of NPAH perspectives in a Chinese and East Asian language context, where the findings do not align with the predictions based on NPAH, and instead are better explained by domain-general perspectives. - The project has generated these promising outputs and impacts: at least 6 publications in high-impact journals/publishers in linguistics/psychology as of now (1 published, 1 accepted subject to minor revisions, 2 in-preparation with full manuscripts attached that are close to ready for submission, 2 in-preparation with abstracts attached), 2 international major conference presentations, 10 BA/MST student research projects, 17 BA/MST student assistants and 2 RAs trained, 1 RGC-Hong Kong PhD Fellowship and 1 RGC-Postgraduate Students Conference/Seminar Grants as synergistic outcomes (see Part C for details).

15607217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15607217.value: The project findings consistently align with a domain-general account of acquisition. While this project has considered typological properties that affect experience-based factors and form-function pairings, the role of cognitive factors, despite their important status within the emergentist-constructivist framework, in predicting children’s complex sentence performance can be examined in greater depth in future research. Individual differences in cognitive abilities such as working memory and statistical learning skills have been a recent line of research in the context of RC acquisition. Given the reported limitations in working memory capacities and statistical learning skills in children with DLD in the cross-linguistic literature, future research could investigate whether/how individual differences in these cognitive abilities predict children’s competence with RCs in Cantonese DLD. One specific follow-up is that PI has collected some pilot data on measures of working memory span and executive functioning abilities in our sample of children with and without DLD. Given the online findings suggesting a generally slower processing speed observed in DLD children relative to their age-matched TD peers, it is theoretically interesting to examine whether there are differences/similarities in whether/how these cognitive abilities predict children’s RC performance in each group. This follow up will be pursued in the coming months.

15607217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15607217.value: This project is significant in promoting research on Chinese language acquisition and disorders with the following characteristics: (i) research integrating interdisciplinary and cross-linguistic perspectives, considering how language-specific properties of Cantonese interact with our language acquisition mechanisms to impact on acquisition outcomes; (ii) collaborations with local and overseas internationally leading research universities/institutes; and (iii) research disseminated in international major publication outlets and conferences. Specifically, this project studied the acquisition of an important grammatical construction, relative clause, in Chinese languages, because Chinese languages such as Cantonese present certain linguistic properties that are cross-linguistically distinctly rare, and these special properties provide important opportunities to tease apart predictions of theories in ways that investigating most European languages do not allow. The project has generated these promising outputs and impacts: at least 6 publications in high-impact journals/publishers in linguistics/psychology as of now (1 published, 1 accepted subject to minor revisions, 2 in-preparation with full manuscripts attached that are close to ready for submission, 2 in-preparation with abstracts attached), 2 international major conference presentations, 10 BA/MST student research projects, 17 BA/MST student assistants and 2 RAs trained, 1 RGC-Hong Kong PhD Fellowship and 1 RGC-Postgraduate Students Conference/Seminar Grants as synergistic outcomes (see Part C for details).

15609617.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15609617.value: 應有之惡？——早期中古中國的戰爭與暴力

15609617.label: Project Objectives
15609617.value: To attain a broad understanding of the history of violence in early medieval China. To trace the changing nature and notions of military violence in early medieval China. To analyze the pervasive impact of military violence on early medieval Chinese society, culture, and political systems. To provide a basis for a comparative study of violence and warfare with other regions and periods in a world historical context. To prepare for the writing of a monograph which will investigate the development of concepts of violence and their application in the military, social, legal and political aspects of life in early medieval China.

To provide a basis for a comparative study of violence and warfare with other regions and periods in a world historical context.
