15609617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15609617.value: This project aims to study the relationship between violence and warfare and their impact on society and culture in early medieval China, a period that ran from the late second to early seventh centuries AD., also known in Chinese history as the Era of Disunity. While violence is manifested in different ways and formats, such as combat, legal punishments, animal hunts, religious rituals, games, and crime, this study focuses on the exercise of violence in warfare, which, as the most organized form of violence, is generally the largest in scale and most devastating in effect. Its impact on various aspects of human society is therefore also pervasive and far-reaching. Besides, warfare always entails components of other categories of violence, which guarantees it as a primary subject of violence studies to start with. The period under study was notorious for its incessant warfare. With the frequent rise and fall of polities and armed clashes between various regional and ethnic groups, violence became an everyday part of the lives of many people. Through the examination of textual and material evidence, and the incorporation of historical, sociological, and archaeological analyses, this project attempts to arrive at a broad understanding of how people in early medieval China conceptualized, justified, and deployed violence in warfare, in which circumstances and to what purposes did they resort to war? What justification did they use for their action? In what ways were people’s lives affected by violence and warfare? By studying the perception and the application of military violence of the people in medieval China and the evolution of their attitude towards related issues, the project gives us a glimpse of the early medieval worldview and provides references for further research on other topics, such as conflict, power, political order, social norms, and religious beliefs of the period. The problem of widespread application of military violence, whether legitimate or illegitimate, that faces modern societies is not unique. While this study focuses on early medieval China, it also asks the perennial and universal questions of how, why, and when people used military violence and what arguments they summoned to justify it. It will not only shed new light on the fields of early medieval China and Chinese military history, but will also be of value to scholars of ancient and medieval European history, world history, military history, historical sociology, and anthropology. 應有之惡？——早期中古中國的戰爭與暴力 自後漢 (25-220) 中央政權崩潰至於隋唐統一帝國重建之間的近四個世紀，在帝國的廢墟上，不同的政權更迭頻繁。這段在傳統史籍中被稱為魏晉南北朝的時代，其留給後人的一貫形象為分裂割據、戰禍不息，而且族群衝突嚴重，而戰爭在當中扮演了非常重要的角色。政權之興往往由於戰爭，其亡也源於戰爭。過去的研究雖然都肯定了戰爭在該時段歷史演變中的作用，特別是破壞與負面的作用，但對於戰爭與其背後的暴力觀念的關係、暴力觀與戰爭形式的互動關係，以及戰爭、暴力與當時社會和族群軍事化的歷程之間的關係則未見有深入探討。本研究計劃即希望在這些方面，提供新角度以理解早期中古中國的歷史發展、戰爭對當時社會的影響、時人的暴力觀，以及中華帝國從早期到中古模式的轉變等等課題。同時，也希望對於從世界史角度比較和理解中古時期不同文明的暴力觀有所貢獻。

15609617.label: Realisation of objectives
15609617.value: The two publications of this project, namely “Warfare” in _Routledge Handbook of Early Chinese History_ and “Violence and Warfare in Early Imperial China,” in _The Cambridge World History of Violence, Volume I: The Prehistoric and Ancient Worlds_, have become important reference for understanding the history of violence and warfare in early and early medieval China, thereby having realized the first three objectives. My conference presentations and invited lectures during the period of the project have also contributed to the realization of those objectives. In addition, both mentioned publications have provided brief comparisons between ancient China and Greco-Roman culture of violence and warfare, which serve the basis for further comparative study. As for Objective 5, I have been working on a monograph, tentatively naming, _War, State and Society in Ancient China—From the Classical Age to the Early Medieval Period_, which will be the first book-length study on the topic when it is completed.

15609617.label: Major findings and research outcome
15609617.value: By tracing the changing nature and notions of military violence and analyzing the pervasive impact of military violence on society, culture, and political systems, the publications, conference papers, and invited lectures produced by this project have given the readers and audience a broad understanding of the history of violence in early and early medieval China, which as a subject has long been overlooked. It demonstrated that how violence, especially military violence, shaped state organizations and everyday life during early imperial and early medieval China. It also provides a basis for further comparative study on the topic in a world historical context.

15609617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15609617.value: On the basis of this project, I have been working on a monograph. Blending cultural, military, political, and social history, the book aims to offer an up-to-date, authoritative, and comprehensive analysis of the interrelationships among war, state, and society in the Chinese realm from earliest times until the end of the sixth century AD. Warfare and violence will constitute the main thread that runs through the book and binds together a broad range of topics: military campaigns, command structures, weapon systems, troop types, institutions of recruitment and training, military logistics, strategy and tactics, military thought, perceptions of war, cultural responses to military conquests, civil-military relations, political and military cultures, and daily lives of common soldiers, as well as military interactions and diplomatic relations between Chinese empires and their Eurasian neighbors over time. By offering a descriptive and analytical panorama of the developments in warfare and the military in relation to contemporary social and political structures, as well as culture, this book assesses the function of war as a dynamic in the processes of the integration and fragmentation of the imperial realm and examines how war both shaped and was shaped by culture, politics, and society in classical and early medieval China.

15609617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15609617.value: This project aims to show that war and violence were essential features to ancient Chinese civilization as far as the earliest historical records inform. Military violence was in fact at the core of the formation of early states and empires, bringing prosperity and glory to the ruling elites, but it was also the only devastating force apart from natural disasters that could release horrific violence to destroy families, communities, and states, showing apocalyptic scenarios to those who were caught in it. The preparation for, engagement in, and prevention of war thus constituted crucial concerns in ancient Chinese state and society.

16100017.label: Realisation of objectives
16100017.value: To unravel the role of TRIP13 in SAC activation, maintenance, and inactivation. This aim has been achieved. To elucidate the function of TRIP13 in SAC, we developed a conditional gene inactivation system by integrating the tetracycline-controlled promoter system and the auxin-inducible degron (AID) system in conjunction with CRISPR Cas9-mediated disruption of the endogenous locus. The rapid and tight conditional depletion of TRIP13 in different phases of cell cycle uncovered an antagonistic function of TRIP13 in SAC activation and inactivation during interphase and mitosis. With prolonged inactivation of TRIP13, we did not notice the significant changes in cell cycle progression. Interestingly, we found that nocodazole (NOC), a spindle poison, was unable to trap the TRIP13-deficient cells in mitosis, with an inactive SAC. In fact, we and other groups have observed previously, depletion of TRIP13 resulted in an accumulation of p31comet, the MAD2 binding protein that is capable of blocking the SAC activation. One explanation for the inactive SAC after the loss of TRIP13 can be the over-compensation of the accumulated p31comet. Therefore, we generated AID-TRIP13-expressing cells in the KO background of TRIP13 and p31comet. The cells were still unable to be blocked in mitosis with NOC, indicating that p31comet was not the cause of the SAC activation failure. To better understand the temporal relationship of SAC activation failure to the loss of TRIP13 protein, we performed a time-course experiment to determine when the loss of functional SAC occurred after the TRIP13 degradation. With cell cycle synchronization, the formation of the MCC was unaffected immediately after the complete loss of TRIP13. Importantly, this occurred before all O-MAD2 was converted to C-MAD2. The SAC only became impaired about one to two cell cycles upon TRIP13 was removed, correlating with the depletion of O-MAD2. Our data indicate that the TRIP13 is required for SAC activation by maintaining the O-MAD2 before mitosis. Using a similar setup, we investigated the role of TRIP13 in SAC maintenance, and found that mitotic slippage occurred only marginally slower when TRIP13 was absent. Since p31comet is the adaptor protein of TRIP13 in MCC dissociation and the ability to promote SAC inactivation, we further investigated the role of TRIP13 in the p31comet controlled mitotic exit. Ectopic expression of either WT or a mutant p31comet unable to bind TRIP13 (p31(PK)) could induce rapid mitotic slippage. By contrast, a mutant unable to bind MAD2 (p31(QF)) did not promote mitotic slippage. To investigate the p31comet mutants at a more physiological level, we generated the stable cell lines with expression of exogenous p31comet, p31(PK), or p31(QF) at levels comparable to endogenous p31comet in the p31 knockout background. KO of p31comet resulted in a delay in mitotic slippage, while p31comet or p31(PK) restored the normal rate of mitotic slippage, p31(QF)-expressing cells underwent delayed mitotic slippage similarly as p31KO cells. The data suggested that p31comet normally promotes mitotic slippage through a TRIP13-indepenent mechanism. Given the essential role of TRIP13 in converting C-MAD2 to O-MAD2, it can play a key role in inactivating the SAC to facilitate mitotic exit. But as the SAC requires the O-MAD2 to be activated, it was previously impossible to show that TRIP13 is involved in SAC inactivation during mitotic exit. The auxin-dependent degron system allowed us to inactivate TRIP13 after mitotic block and investigate the role of TRIP13 specifically in mitotic exit. Interestingly, we found that the degradation of TRIP13 during mitosis merely delayed mitotic exit. This suggested that TRIP13 is not the sole mechanism for SAC inactivation. To define the function of MAD2 conformation equilibrium in SAC and to understand the molecular basis of why C-MAD2 alone is insufficient to support the SAC. These objectives have been completed. A perplexing finding is that, although both TRIP13KO and MAD2KO lacked a functional SAC, they displayed a different degree of chromosomal instability during unperturbed mitosis. The detrimental effects on proliferation were consistent in the previously reported knockout mice study, while Mad2-knockout mice are embryonic lethal, Trip13-knockout mice are born at a relatively normal ratio. We speculate that, although TRIP13KO cells are incapable of regenerating O-MAD2, there is enough O-MAD2 from the newly synthesized MAD2 for the SAC to facilitate the unperturbed mitosis. To test this hypothesis, we first increased the production of MAD2 via ectopic expression of MAD2 cDNA. Since MAD2 is first produced in O-form, the increased MAD2 synthesis resulted in the surged level of O-MAD2 in the TRIP13KO background. More importantly, the increase in the O-MAD2 can restore the MAD2-CDC20 complexes and SAC-mediated mitotic arrest in TRIP13 KO background. Furthermore, neither expression of C-MAD2 or O-MAD2 locked mutant could rescue the CDC20 binding, and SAC defects caused by MAD2 and TRIP13 knockout, therefore, suggested the dynamic conformation change in MAD2 is indispensable to the SAC function. Taken together, in the condition of limited O-MAD2 and excessive C-MAD2 as in TRIP13KO, the unperturbed mitosis can still be supported by the limited amount of O-MAD2, but during prolonged mitosis upon spindle poison treatment, the limited O-MAD2 will be converted to C-MAD2 during the formation of MCC. Cells will run out of O-MAD2, and mitotic slippage will be triggered. Interestingly, the cells with limited O-MAD2 survive and proliferate similar to WT cells under normal culture conditions, but the cells with limited O-MAD2 does not respond to the mild chromosome instability as induced by the low dose of spindle poison and leads to the poor survival in the long term. To investigate the role of TRIP13 and MAD2 conformation equilibrium in normal and cancer cells. The role of TRIP13 and MAD2 conformation equilibrium in cancer cells were done but the works in normal cells were incomplete. We have confirmed our finding in several different cancer cell lines originated from different tissue including liver, cervical, ovarian and colon cancer. TRIP13 is dispensable for survival and proliferation in cancer cells but with mild degree of chromosome instability. Although the expression of MAD2, p31comet, and TRIP13 is varied in different cancer cell lines, the depletion of TRIP13 resulted to the significant increase in p31comet expression and the shift of MAD2 equilibrium from limited C-MAD2 to excessive C-MAD2. In contrast, overexpression of TRIP13 has marginal effect on the MAD2 conformation equilibrium and SAC function. We originally proposed to investigate the TRIP13-p31comet-MAD2 axis in normal cells, but we failed to generate the TRIP13 depletion cells in the RPE1. We have tested the originally proposed knockin to the endogenous locus approach, but we cannot obtain a clone with the knockin to both alleles. We also tested the conditional inactivation approach, which we have successfully used in cancer cell lines, but we cannot obtain the knockout of both allele of TRIP13. In addition to RPE-1, we have also tested in another normal cell, IMR-90 immortalized by hTERT, but the results were also unsatisfactory. Nevertheless, we have tested the overexpression of TRIP13 in RPE-1 and IMR90, the effect in mitotic length, the MAD2-conformation equilibrium, SAC sensitivity and mitotic slippage were not obvious, as we observed in cancer cells. Taken together, the increase in TRIP13 expression does not affect the MAD2 equilibrium and SAC in both normal and cancer cells, while the loss of TRIP13 results to significantly change of MAD2 equilibrium and SAC function in cancer cells.

16100017.label: Major findings and research outcome
16100017.value: Characterizing the functions of cell cycle control genes requires tight and rapid inducible gene inactivation. We have developed a system to avoid the drawbacks of current conditional depletion approaches include slow responses and incomplete depletion. We demonstrated that by integrating the tetracycline-controlled promoter system and the auxin-inducible degron (AID) system together, AID-tagged proteins can be down regulated more efficiently than individual technology alone. When used in conjunction with CRISPR Cas9-mediated disruption of the endogenous locus, the system facilitates the analysis of gene function by allowing rapid and tight conditional depletion. The materials and methods have been first published in Cell Cycle and the upgraded system allowed the single-step generation by the incorporation of the transposon-mediated integration have been published in Molecular Biology of the Cell. Importantly, the conditional TRIP13 inactivation cell lines generated was the useful reagents for later part of studies requiring rapid and tight suppression of gene expression in mammalian cells. With the proposed conditional gene inactivation system, the role of TRIP13 in SAC activation, maintenance, and inactivation was characterized. With precise synchronization, we found that after AID-TRIP13 was targeted to degradation, spindle poison nocodazole could still trap the TRIP13-deficient cells in mitosis with normal level of MCC, suggesting that TRIP13 was not directly involved in the MCC formation. We found that the major role of TRIP13 in SAC is to maintain the O-MAD2 equilibrium for MCC formation. Importantly, the equilibrium of O/C-MAD2 and the level of p31comet are the determining factor in controlling SAC activation and mitotic slippage. This part of works has been published in Cell Reports and Oncogene. TRIP13 depleted cells do not have a functional SAC, however the proliferation and survival of TRIP13 KO cells are normal. While the knockout of MAD2-binding protein p31comet strengthened the SAC and promoted cell death, TRIP13 KO had the opposite effect of triggering mitotic slippage. Mitotic slippage prevented immediate mitotic cell death caused by spindle poisons but reduced long-term survival. In either mitotic slippage or mitotic exit with missegregated chromosomes, cell death occurred only after one cell cycle following mitotic exit and increased progressively during subsequent cell cycles. The specific temporal patterns of cell death after mitotic exit with weakened SAC after TRIP13 KO may reconcile the contradictory results from many previous studies. This part of works has been published in Cell Death and Disease.

16100017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16100017.value: The knowledge generated from this project extended our understanding of TRIP13 in controlling MAD2 in SAC. REV7, another HORMA family member like MAD2, has recently been found to be regulated by p31comet and TRIP13 in DNA repair signaling together with the Shieldin-complex. A more comprehensive understanding of TRIP13 in both SAC and DNA damage repair can provide a clear picture in explaining why TRIP13 is remarkably overexpressed in many types of cancer. To this end, with the reagents developed in this project, the preliminary data of TRIP13 in maintaining REV7 conformation equilibrium and the relationship to the DNA repair pathways will be generated and used to build the hypothesis to explain the role of TRIP13 in cancer. Apart from the TRIP13/MAD2 knowledge, the project has built the novel system for rapid gene conditional inactivation. The system is widely used in many of our other mechanistic studies in cell line model. We plan to further develop the cell line system along with mice xenograft for validation of the gene target as therapeutic target in cancer treatment.

16100017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16100017.value: SAC is a mechanism to protect the stability of the genome by safeguard the separation of genetic materials evenly during cell division. MAD2 is crucial for the SAC function, and it can be existed in two conformations, the closed-conformation C-MAD2 and the open-conformation O-MAD2. An enzyme named TRIP13 can catalyze the conformational change of C-MAD2 to O-MAD2. We confirmed that TRIP13 is essential in maintaining the proper ratio of C-MAD2 to O-MAD2. Although C-MAD2 is the functional effector of SAC, TRIP13-knockout cells express exclusively in C-MAD2 but at the same time are defective in SAC. Using the conditional degradation system, we found that TRIP13 is not directly involved in SAC activation but is likely to support SAC activation via providing O-MAD2. Moreover, we found that TRIP13-mediated C-MAD2 to O-MAD2 is not essential to SAC inactivation. Taken together, the data generated in this project provide further insight to the current SAC template model as well as addressing how MAD2 conformation change affects the SAC activity before and during mitosis. As the target of some of the most useful anticancer drugs such as Taxol, we now know that the MAD2 equilibrium but not the level of TRIP13 affects the response to Taxol in cells.

16100417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16100417.value: 周期蛋白 A(Cyclin A) 是細胞周期中的重要調節組件。有異於周期蛋白的其他​成員，周期蛋白 A在DNA 合成期和有絲分裂期中都有著其功能。周期蛋白 A在DNA 合成期中的復制起始點激發和預防基因組再復制上的功能已經有十分清晰。但是，周期蛋白 A是如何促進有絲分裂期還有待研究，而在這個研究課題上，如何區分因為功能喪失後在DNA 合成期的突變型是一個不易解決的挑戰。通過基因組編輯與可誘導選擇性降解技術，周期蛋白 A可在特定的細胞周期時間滅活，使我們能夠解決很多關於周期蛋白 A在人類細胞上的問題。這些問題包括周期蛋白 A在正常細胞與癌細胞中的作用和周期蛋白 A在人類胚胎干細胞上多能性維持及分化上的功能。我們計劃以蛋白質組學方法去探索周期蛋白 A相關的信號通路組成部分，從而全面理解周期蛋白 A在G2期和有絲分裂期中的功能。另外，基於周期蛋白 A是在DNA損傷後重新發動有絲分裂的必要原素，我們計劃進一步了解周期蛋白 A在DNA損傷檢驗點恢復的上的角色。本項目將延伸科學界對周期蛋白 A的認識，同時亦因爲周期蛋白 A在正常細胞與癌細胞的細胞分裂過程和基因組穩定性上有著重要的作用，這些知識對人類健康與疾病會有深遠的影響。

16100417.label: Realisation of objectives
16100417.value: Our first objective is to generate conditional knockout cyclin A cell lines and study the functions of cyclin A in different parts of the cell cycle. Characterizing the functions of essential cell cycle control genes such as cyclin A requires tight and rapid inducible gene inactivation. Given that the drawbacks of current conditional depletion approaches include slow responses and incomplete depletion, we first developed a novel system by integrating the tetracycline-controlled promoter system and the auxin-inducible degron (AID) system together. We demonstrated that the AID-tagged proteins can be downregulated more efficiently than the individual technology alone (Ng et al., 2019). When used in conjunction with CRISPR-Cas9-mediated disruption of the endogenous cyclin A locus, this system facilitates the analysis of cyclin A by allowing rapid and tight conditional depletion. We have subsequently re-designed the plasmids so that they could be integrated into the genome with high efficiency using the Sleeping Beauty transposase. This allowed one-step multiplex generation of cell lines containing all the elements required for Tet-Off and AID-coupled regulation and CRISPR-mediated knockout. Moreover, multiple genes could be simultaneously or sequentially targeted, allowing inducible inactivation of multiple genes. These resources enable highly efficient generation of conditional gene silencing cell lines to facilitate functional studies of essential genes. This method is published in Mol. Biol. Cell (Yeung et al., 2021). We have deposited the vectors constructed developed in both studies to Addgene (https://www.addgene.org/Randy_Poon/), which should be useful for other researchers in studies requiring rapid and tight suppression of gene expression in mammalian cells. Using the developed degron-mediated conditional knockout cyclin A, we have characterized the effects of cyclin A depletion in several cancer cell lines (including HeLa and HCT116). Using highly synchronized cells and the rapid removal of cyclin A of the system, we found that in addition to its accepted role in S phase progression, cyclin A is also critical for G2–M control. Interestingly, the effects of cyclin A appeared to depend on cell density – cell cycle arrest was particularly pronounced at relatively low cell densities. Moreover, we found that cyclin A also played a role in mitotic slippage. We have reported the initial characterization of a system used to promote mitotic slippage (without using chemicals) and the study of cell fates following mitotic slippage using live-cell imaging (Zeng et al., 2019). Using the same setup for the conditional cyclin A knockout cells, we now found that mitotic slippage was accelerated in the absence of cyclin A. These data suggested that cyclin A may be responsible for some of the mitotic phosphorylation require to maintain the cells in mitosis during prolonged mitotic block. Transcriptome sequencing of synchronized G2 cells revealed that transcriptional targets of FOXM1 are the major downregulated genes in the absence of cyclin A. This work is now being prepared for publication. Whether the roles of cyclin A we discovered above are specific to cancer cells was investigated by comparing the role of cyclin A in cancer cells and normal cells (Objective 2). We used the same tools to generate conditional knockout cyclin A cell lines in the normal RPE1 cells. However, clones that contained comparable levels of cyclin A after depletion as in HeLa cells (less than 1% relative to the endogenous cyclin A before KO) was difficult to be isolated. This differ from a related study in which we were able to generate conditional KO cell lines in HeLa and RPE1 for CDK1 and CDK2 (the CDK partners of cyclin A). We confirmed that CDK1 assumes the role of G1-S CDK in the absence of CDK2. Unexpectedly, CDK1 deficiency does not prevent mitotic entry. Nonetheless, inadequate phosphorylation of mitotic substrates by noncanonical cyclin B-CDK2 complexes does not allow progression beyond metaphase and underscores deleterious late mitotic events including the uncoupling of anaphase A and B and cytokinesis. Elevation of CDK2 to a level similar to CDK1 overcomes the mitotic defects caused by CDK1 deficiency, indicating that the relatively low concentration of CDK2 accounts for the defective anaphase. Collectively, these results revealed that the difference between G2-M and G1-S CDKs in human cells is essentially quantitative. Importantly, our data also indicated that CDK2 can compensate CDK1 activity in cancer cells but not in normal RPE1 cells. This work is now published in Cell Reports (Lau et al., 2021). Whether the mitotic cyclin A and cyclin B behave similarly as the CDKs is an important question. We found that the differences between the mitotic cyclins are also in part quantitative. Overexpression of cyclin A in a cyclin B-deficient background can drive cells into mitosis normally, suggesting that the two mitotic cyclins do not have fundamentally different properties (e.g. substrate specificity) in driving mitosis. This study is now under preparation for publication. A more impressive cell cycle arrest in the absence of cyclin A was found during DNA damage checkpoint recovery (Objective 3). Checkpoint-arrested cells can continue the cell cycle and enter mitosis after the DNA is repaired. Alternatively, chemical inhibitors of the checkpoint such as inhibitors of CHK1 (CHK1i) or WEE1 (WEE1i) can uncouple the checkpoint, forcing cells into mitosis. We found that both types of checkpoint recovery were delayed in the absence of cyclin A. Furthermore, PLK1 was also required for checkpoint recovery. With conditional KO cell lines for cyclin A and PLK1 (as well as PLK1’s activators Aurora A and Bora), we are currently trying to understand how cyclin A and PLK1 contributes to the activation of cyclin B during checkpoint recovery.

16100417.label: Major findings and research outcome
16100417.value: We have developed Sleeping Beauty transposon-based vectors for expressing auxin-inducible degron (AID)-tagged genes under the regulation of a tetracycline-controlled promoter (Ng et al., 2019; Yeung et al., 2021). The dual transcriptional and degron-mediated post-translational regulation allows rapid and tight silencing of protein expression in mammalian cells. We demonstrated that both non-essential and essential genes such as those involved in mitotic slippage (Zeng et al., 2019), cyclin A and its CDK partners could be targeted in human cell lines using a one-step transfection method. Using this methodology, we found that the difference between G2-M and G1-S CDKs in human cells is essentially quantitative (Lau et al., 2021). Likewise, there seems to be no fundamental differences between cyclin A and cyclin B in terms of mitosis-promoting activity. Loss of cyclin A delayed G2 phase in unperturbed cell cycle and recovery from the G2 DNA damage checkpoint independent on its S phase functions. One of the major pathways downstream of cyclin A for G2–M transition is FOXM1.

16100417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16100417.value: • Understand the relationship between cyclin A and the AURK–Bora–PLK1 axis in driving cells into mitosis in both unperturbed cell cycle and following DNA damage recovery. Revaluation of these critical pathways can be achieved using a combination of chemical inhibitors and conditional KO cell lines. • Develop a more robust conditional gene-On/Off system to study essential genes, especially for normal REP1 cells. RPE1 appears to require a tighter gene-Off system than the current available technology. We are developing several alternative degrons coupled with promoter control for REP1.

16100417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16100417.value: The cell cycle is choreographed by an evolutionarily conserved engine composed of a family of protein kinases called cyclin-dependent kinases (CDKs) and their partners called cyclins. As CDK pathways are entirely rewired in human cancer, the precise relationship between different CDKs in cancer cells remains ambiguous. We have developed Sleeping Beauty transposon-based vectors for expressing auxin-inducible degron (AID)-tagged genes under the regulation of a tetracycline-controlled promoter. The dual transcriptional and degron-mediated post-translational regulation allows rapid and tight silencing of protein expression in mammalian cells. We demonstrated that both non-essential and essential genes such as those involved in mitotic slippage, cyclin A and its CDK partners could be targeted in human cell lines using a one-step transfection method. Using this methodology, we found that the difference between G2-M and G1-S CDKs in human cells is essentially quantitative. Likewise, there seems to be no fundamental differences between cyclin A and cyclin B in terms of mitosis-promoting activity. Loss of cyclin A delayed G2 phase in unperturbed cell cycle and recovery from the G2 DNA damage checkpoint independent on its S phase functions. One of the major pathways downstream of cyclin A for G2–M transition is FOXM1. Collectively, these results revealed that the difference between G2-M and G1-S cyclins and CDKs in human cells is essentially quantitative.

16100517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16100517.value: Ankyrin-R/B/G (分別由 ANK1/2/3基因編碼) 與 β-spectrins (由 SPTBs 基因群編碼) 在許多特定的細胞膜功能區發揮關鍵作用。在紅細胞，肌肉細胞和神經細胞等細胞中，它們共同參與定向及轉運多種跨膜蛋白（包括細胞黏附份子，跨膜轉運蛋白和離子通道蛋白等），並將其整合成功能特定的微膜結構域。ankyrin 和β-spectrin 各亞型之間在體內有直接且特異性的配對結合特性，例如：ankyrin-B 結合 βII-spectrin, ankyrin-G 結合 βIV-spectrin, 以及 ankyrin-R 結合 βI-spectrin。這種特異性的配對結合使得結合ankyrin 的膜蛋白（如離子通道和跨膜受體）能夠被連接到規則且間歇性排列的細胞膜骨架結構上，從而行使其相對應的正常生理功能，例如控制心肌細胞的心率搏動信號以及控制神經細胞的動作電位的強度和頻率。ankyrin 和 spectrin 編碼基因的突變會導致包括遺傳性球形紅血球增多症、心律失常、運動共濟失調, 以及多種精神系統疾病在內的一系列嚴重人類疾病。儘管多種相關硏究已經進行了數十年，但是迄今為止關於ankyrin與spectrin 特異性結合的份子機理仍然有待探索與瞭解。 在此，我們計劃闡明ankyrin 與spectrin各種亞型之間特異性配對結合的生物化學及結構生物學基礎。我們在先期研究中已經發現，在各個ankyrin亞型上，位於spectrin結合結構域（ZU5-ZU5-UPA 串聯結構域）氨基端上游的一小段氨基酸序列可以極大地促進ankyrin與spectrin 結合的強度及特異性。重要的是，這段氨基酸序列在物種間的進化上極其保守，但是在各個ankyrin亞型之中又有所不同，這顯示了它可作為特異性調節序列的潛在能力。我們將首先通過詳盡的生物化學和生物物理學等實驗來界定ankyrin/spectrin的特異性配對結合情況，並且嘗試通過X-射線晶體學方法解析ankyrin各亞型（包含上述小段氨基酸序列和ZU5-ZU5-UPA 串聯結構域）及與其配對的spectrin 的複合物結構。我們將會使用來源於轉基因老鼠中的海馬神經細胞的體外培養實驗來驗證我們從生物化學和結構生物學硏究中所獲得的發現。在這種轉基因老鼠中，其內源性的ANK3基因外顯子22和23兩端被插入了兩個loxP重組結合位點，因此可以通過將內源性的ANK3 基因替換為帶有各種人為設計的突變的ANK3基因來進行ankyrin與spectrin的特異性結合測試。此項硏究的結果將直接有助於理解ankyrin/spectrin 複合物的生理功能基礎以及ANKs 和SPTBs基因突變導致多種人類疾病背後的份子機理。

16100517.label: Major findings and research outcome
16100517.value: Ankyrins (encoded by ANK1/2/3 corresponding to Ankyrin-R/B/G or AnkR/B/G), via binding to spectrins, connect plasma membranes with actin cytoskeleton to maintain mechanical strengths and to modulate excitabilities of diverse cells such as neurons, muscle cells, and erythrocytes. Cellular and genetic evidences suggest that each isoform of ankyrins pairs with a specific β-spectrin in discrete subcellular membrane microdomains for distinct functions, although the molecular mechanisms underlying such ankyrin/β-spectrin pairings are unknown. During the study, we discover that a conserved and short extension N-terminal to the ZU5N-ZU5C-UPA tandem (exZZU) is critical for each ankyrin to bind to β-spectrins with high affinities. Structures of AnkB/G exZZU in complex with spectrin repeats13-15 of β2/β4-spectrins solved here reveal that the extension sequence of exZZU forms an additional β-strand contributing to the structural stability and enhanced affinity of each ZU5N/spectrin repeat interaction. The complex structures further reveal that the UPA domain of exZZU directly participates in spectrin binding. Formation of the exZZU supramodule juxtaposes the ZU5N and UPA domains for simultaneous interacting with spectrin repeats 14 and 15. However, our biochemical and structural investigations indicate that the direct and strong interactions between ankyrins and β-spectrins do not appear to determine their pairing specificities. Therefore, there likely exists additional mechanism(s) for modulating functional pairings between ankyrins and β-spectrins in cells. This research was published in J Mol Biol in 2020 (Paper 3 in Part C). Giant ankyrin-B (gAnkB) is a 440-kD neurospecific ankyrin-B isoform and a high-confidence target for autism mutations. gAnkB suppresses axon branching through coordination of cortical microtubules, and autism-related mutation of gAnkB results in ectopic neuronal connectivity. We identified a bipartite motif from gAnkB, which bundles and avidly binds to microtubules in vitro. This motif is composed of a module of 15 tandem repeats followed by a short, conserved fragment also found in giant ankyrin-G (BG-box). Combination of these two parts synergistically increases microtubule-binding avidity. Transfection of astrocytes (which lack gAnkB) with WT gAnkB resulted in prominent bundling of microtubules, which did not occur with mutant gAnkB with impaired microtubule-binding activity. Similarly, rescue of gAnkB-deficient neurons with WT gAnkB suppressed axonal branching and invasion of EB3-tagged microtubules into filopodia, which did not occur with the same mutant gAnkB. Together, these findings demonstrate that gAnkB suppresses axon collateral branching and prevents microtubule invasion of nascent axon branches through direct interaction with microtubules. This research was published in 2020 in J Cell Biol (paper 4 in Part C).

16100517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16100517.value: Our research has suggested that there likely exists additional mechanism(s) for modulating functional pairings between ankyrins and β-spectrins in cells. This is a direction for future studies. Additionally, our study has indicated that interactions between giant ankyrins and microtubules likely play critical roles in determining how giant ankyrins function in axonal polarity and function. This is another future research direction.

16100517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16100517.value: The ankyrin/spectrin complex is an essential and universal scaffold connecting membrane microdomains with actin cytoskeleton in all animal cells. In these membrane microdomains, the ankyrin/spectrin complex play roles such as firing action potentials in neuron, controlling heart beating, regulating insulin metabolism, maintaining red blood cell structure and stability, etc. Impairments of the interactions between ankyrins and spectrins cause numerous human diseases (e.g. cardiac arrhythmia, psychiatric disorders, spherocytosis, to name a few). Unmatched with their vital functions in cells and tissues, our understanding of the interaction between ankyrins and spectrins are rather scarce. Our study in this manuscript aims to understand the mechanistic basis underlying the interaction between ankyrins and spectrins and to dissect how specific ankyrin/spectrin pairings exist in distinct cellular microdomains. Via extensive structural and biochemical investigations, we discovered that a small extension N-terminal to the ZU5-ZU5-UPA tandem (also known as the spectrin binding domain of ankyrin) plays a vital role for the stable complex formation between ankyrins and spectrins. Importantly, this N-terminal extension is subject to a switch-based regulation via insertion of a mini-exon in ankyrins. In addition to understanding the molecular basis governing the stable ankyrin/spectrin complex formation, our study will become a foundation for future functional studies various ankyrin/spectrin interactions in different tissues in animals including humans.

16101517.label: Realisation of objectives
16101517.value: 1. Characterization of PaxBP1-null mice and PaxBP1-null MuSC. To investigate the role of Paxbp1 in vivo, we first generated a Paxbp1 floxed mouse line and crossed it with Pax7-Cre mouse line to delete Paxbp1 in Pax7 expressing cells during embryonic development. Strikingly, while the number of mouse pups with other genotypes followed expected the mendelian ratio, no Paxbp1 KO pups were identified. This piece of data suggests Paxbp1 is essential during embryo development. To study the function of Paxbp1 in adult MuSCs, we generated a tamoxifen inducible, MuSC-specific Paxbp1 KO mouse line by crossing Paxbp1-flox/flox mice with Pax7-CreER mice. Paxbp1 was deleted in adult MuSCs by tamoxifen injection in adult mice. The functions of Paxbp1-null MuSCs were examined by in vivo muscle regeneration assays following cardiotoxin-induced muscle injury. Importantly, loss of Paxbp1 in MuSCs completely abolished muscle regeneration. 30 days post injury, while muscle regeneration was already completed in control heterozygous mice, no signs of new muscle fiber formation were observed in KO mice. Instead, excessive fat infiltration occurred as a result of failed muscle repair. To examine the property of Paxbp1-null MuSCs, we first isolated MuSCs from control and KO mice by flow cytometry and cultured them in the presence of EdU. 48 hours post isolation, more than 80% of control MuSCs already entered S phase as evidenced by EdU incorporation, while EdU incorporation was barely observed in KO MuSCs. Instead, KO MuSCs underwent apoptosis. Thus, our data demonstrated that Paxbp1 plays key roles in the cell cycle reentry and survival of adult MuSCs upon activation. 2. Investigating the role of PaxBP1 in regulation of MuSC in vivo To investigate the role Paxbp1 in MuSCs in vivo, we deleted Paxbp1 in adult MuSCs by tamoxifen injection and assayed functions of MuSCs. Loss of Paxbp1 severely impaired functions of MuSCs as evidenced by the complete abolishment of muscle regeneration. Unlike Pax7, Paxbp1 was not required for the maintenance of quiescent MuSC pool as the size of the MuSC pool was comparable between control and KO mice even at 5 months post Paxbp1 deletion. As the FACS-isolated Paxbp1-null MuSCs could not re-enter the cell cycle in culture, we then examined whether Paxbp1 was required for the cell cycle reentry of MuSCs in vivo. We injured TA muscles in both heterozygous control and KO mice followed by EdU injection to label MuSCs that re-entered the cell cycle in vivo. MuSCs were then isolated by FACS at 2.5 or 3.5 days post injury and subjected to EdU staining. While 30% and 60% of control MuSCs were EdU+ at 2.5 and 3.5 days post injury respectively, EdU incorporation was barely detected in KO MuSCs at either time point. Collectively, our data demonstrated Paxbp1 is absolutely required for the cell cycle reentry of MuSCs in vivo. 3. Mechanistic studies of the role of PaxBP1 in MuSC To understand the mechanisms by which Paxbp1 regulates MuSCs functions, we performed RNA-seq using MuSCs freshly isolated from heterozygous control and KO mice at 1 day post injury. Compared to control MuSCs, multiple cell cycle related genes including those involved in the G1/S transition and E2F targets were drastically repressed in KO MuSCs with a concomitant strong induction of many P53 target genes. Interestingly, many genes implicated in multiple metabolic pathways including glycolysis, TCA cycle and oxidative phosphorylation were greatly reduced in mutant MuSCs, suggesting that Paxbp1 regulates the metabolic reprogramming of MuSCs during quiescence exit. We further confirmed that both glycolysis and mitochondria respiration were impaired in KO MuSCs using the Seahorse-based cell mito stress test assays. Moreover, mitochondria biogenesis was also impaired in mutant MuSCs. A careful examination of MuSCs by live cell imaging revealed that the cell growth before cell cycle entry was severely impaired in the absence of Paxbp1. Consistently, the activity of mTORC1, the master regulator of metabolism and cell growth, was also inhibited in Paxbp1 KO MuSCs. Of note, our data suggested a two-tier activation of the mTORC1 activity during quiescence exit of MuSC and both waves are essential for cell cycle reentry. While the first tier of mTORC1 induction is p110a (PI3K)-dependent and does not require Paxbp1, the second wave of mTORC1 induction is regulated by Paxbp1 and required for metabolic reprogramming and cell growth before cell cycle reentry. Mechanistically, Paxbp1 controls mTORC1 activity via a redox-dependent mechanism and P53. Loss of Paxbp1 triggers aberrant accumulation of ROS in mutant cells, which then activated P53 activity and suppressed mTORC1 activation. Sesn2 and Ddit4, two well-established P53 targets known to inhibit mTORC1, were strongly induced in Paxbp1 mutant MuSCs. Importantly, ROS scavenging in mutant MuSCs partially restored cell cycle re-entry defects. Altogether, our data indicates that Paxbp1 maintains the cellular redox states during early activation and is required for cell growth before cell cycle reentry. 4. Identification of PaxBP1-interacting proteins The difference in the phenotypes of Paxbp1 and Pax7 KO MuSCs prompted us to look for more binding partners of Paxbp1. We performed yeast a two-hybrid screening using full-length Paxbp1 as bait. As Paxbp1 is predominantly expressed in the nucleus, we focused on nuclear hits among our candidate lists and among which we identified Nfe2l2 (NRF2), a master regulator of ROS scavenging and cellular detoxification. We further confirmed the binding between Paxbp1 and Nfe2l via co-immunoprecipitation. Previous reports showed that loss of Nfe2l2 impaired MuSC function and muscle regeneration. Many targets of Nfe2l2 are antioxidant genes and they were significantly reduced in mutant MuSCs. This is consistent with upregulation of ROS in mutant MuSCs. At present, it remains unclear how Paxbp1 regulates NRF2. More detailed mechanistic and functional studies should be carried out in the future to address such a question.

16101517.label: Major findings and research outcome
16101517.value: Adult mouse muscle satellite cells (MuSCs) are quiescent. Upon acute muscle injury, MuSCs exit quiescence, reenter the cell cycle to proliferate and self-renew, and then differentiate and fuse to drive muscle regeneration. However, it remains poorly understood how MuSCs transition from quiescence to the cycling state. We recently showed that PI3K critically controls an early activation checkpoint by permitting MuSC to exit quiescence. Here, we showed that Paxbp1 controls another key checkpoint during this critical transition. Deletion of Paxbp1 in adult quiescent MuSCs prevented them from reentering the cell cycle upon injury, resulting in a total regeneration failure. Unlike Pax7, Paxbp1 is not required for the quiescence maintenance of MuSCs. Instead, it is critically required for the metabolic reprogramming, cell growth and survival during quiescence exit. Mechanistically, we found an abnormal elevation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) in Paxbp1- null MuSCs, which enhanced p53 activity and impaired the mTORC1 signaling. Deliberate ROS reduction partially rescued the cell- cycle reentry defect in mutant MuSCs. Our study reveals that Paxbp1 regulates a late cell-growth checkpoint essential for quiescent MuSCs to reenter the cell cycle upon activation.

16101517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16101517.value: 1. Our work provided the first functional characterization of Paxbp1 in vivo and revealed an essential role of Paxbp1 during quiescence exit of adult MuSCs. We demonstrated that Paxbp1 is required for cell growth before cell cycle reentry. However, it remains unclear whether Paxbp1 functions in subsequent steps of muscle regeneration including myoblast proliferation and differentiation due to the failure of the activated MuSCs to re-enter the cell cycle and their subsequent cell death. Deletion of Paxbp1 in MuSCs at later stages using other Cre lines like Myod-CreER or Myog-CreER will help answer such questions. As Paxbp1 is broadly expressed in multiple tissues and cell types, it would also be interesting to test whether its role in cell growth regulation is also conserved in other quiescent stem cells (e.g., HSC, HFSC and NSC) upon their activation. 2. In addition, we showed that Paxbp1 regulates cellular redox states, probably through its interaction with NRF2. It remains unclear how Paxbp1 regulates NRF2. Previously we demonstrated that Paxbp1 could function as an adaptor protein linking a transcription factor (e.g., Pax7) with H3K4 histone methyltransferases (HMT). It would be worthwhile to explore whether Paxbp1 regulates the functions of NRF2 in a similar manner. A good starting point would be performing a H3K4me3 ChIP-seq in both control and Paxbp1-null MuSCs and then examining whether there are changes in the H3K4Me3 peaks around known NRF2 binding sites. 3. Our data suggest that the functions of Paxbp1 in proliferating myoblasts and quiescent MuSCs are different. The comparison of Paxbp1 target genes in these two contexts would provide more insights into the functions of Paxbp1 in proliferating myoblasts.

16101517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16101517.value: Adult muscle stem cells (MuSCs) exist in a unique dormant (or quiescent) state. Upon muscle injury, these dormant MuSCs wake up followed by their transition into the cycling (or dividing) myoblasts. These dividing myoblasts then differentiate and fuse with each other to form new muscles. It remains unclear how the initial wakeup (or activation) process is regulated in MuSCs upon muscle injury. Our previous work showed that PI3K, a lipid kinase, regulates a critical early activation checkpoint that determines whether MuSC can exit the dormant state. Our current work revealed that Paxbp1, a poorly-studied nuclear protein, regulates a distinct late activation checkpoint indispensable for the dormant MuSC to transition to the cycling state. Specific deletion of the Paxbp1 gene in adult MuSCs impaired the late stage of cell growth and caused cell death in Paxbp1-null MuSCs, which prevented their transition into the cycling state and resulted in a complete failure in injury-induced muscle regeneration. As Paxbp1 is broadly expressed in multiple tissues in mouse and is highly conserved in other animal species and humans, our Paxbp1 knockout mouse model will be very useful in elucidating its functions in other tissues and will also shed light on its functions in other species.

16101717.label: Project Objectives
16101717.value: To investigate the mechanism of GAS2L1 action in centrosome disjunction We hypothesize that GAS2L1 mediates the centriole attachment of microtubules and actin filaments, which provide forces required for centrosome dynamics and disjunction. First, we will examine whether alteration of GAS2L1 expression (knockdown and overexpression) affects the attachment of microtubules and actin filaments to the centrioles. Second, we will test whether microtubule and actin cytoskeletons are required for GAS2L1-mediated centrosome disjunction by using microtubule- and F-actin-depolymerizing agents. Third, we will investigate whether the binding of F-actin, microtubules, and EB1/3 is required for the GAS2L1 function. GAS2L1 mutants that are devoid of actin-, microtubule-, or EB1/3-binding activities will be generated and tested for the complementation of GAS2L1 knockdown or knockout. In the assays, centrosome dynamics and disjunction will be measured. Overall, the above assays will reveal the actions of GAS2L1 on centrosomes. To analyze GAS2L1 phosphorylation during the cell cycle To obtain GAS2L1 phosphorylation profiles, the protein will be immunoaffinity isolated from HeLa cells that are synchronized in interphase and in mitosis. After identification of the phosphorylation sites using mass spectrometry, we will compare the interphase and mitotic phosphorylation profiles to reveal the cell cycle-dependent phosphorylation events. In addition, we will analyze the sequences and domain structures that harbor the phosphorylation sites. The above analyses will predict the functional relevance of the phosphorylation events and the candidate kinases that mediate the phosphorylation. Moreover, we will test whether Plk1 and Nek2A catalyze GAS2L1 phosphorylation. To characterize in vivo phosphorylation, we will generate site- and phosphorylation state-specific antibodies for GAS2L1. The antibodies will be used to examine the spatiotemporal patterns of GAS2L1 phosphorylation. The phosphorylation characterization will help understanding the regulation of GAS2L1 actions. To explore the effects of GAS2L1 phosphorylation on centrosome disjunction The biological effects of identified GAS2L1 phosphorylation will be investigated by using a mutational approach. The impacts of the phosphomimetic and nonphosphorylatable mutations of the identified phosphorylation sites will be assessed in the rescue experiments of GAS2L1 knockdown or knockout. We will examine the mutational effects on the function of GAS2L1 in centrosome dynamics and disjunction. Moreover, the mutations may affect various GAS2L1 properties, including subcellular localization (e.g., localization at centrosomes and microtubule and actin cytoskeletons) and microtubule-, F-actin-, and EB1/3-binding activities. These activities will be tested in cell-based and in vitro assays. We anticipate that the above functional assays will inform the biological relevance of GAS2L1 phosphorylation.

16101717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16101717.value: 探索形成兩極紡錘體過程中中心體分離的新機制 動物細胞內的微管隨著細胞分裂週期進程而重組，微管在細胞分裂間期會以中心體為中心、並呈放射狀；在細胞有絲分裂期，微管形成兩極紡錘體。在每個分裂週期中，中心體在S期復制，復制後的中心體由連接蛋白連接、並持續至有絲分裂期。進入有絲分裂期，復制後的中心體會移至細胞兩端、並最終形成紡錘極體，以致組成紡錘體。中心體的及時分開至細胞兩端對正常紡錘體的形成、以及染色體的准確分離至關重要。然而，中心體的分開過程由一系列事件調控，其中包括已復制的中心體在G2晚期的分離，這些事件的控制機理至今尚不清楚。 本實驗室一直專注於研究中心體和其他微管組織中心對微管的調控機制。GAS2L1是一種微管和肌動蛋白絲結合蛋白，其基因表達在急性骨髓性白血病中發現被抑制。我們近期的研究揭示GAS2L1定位於中心體內成熟中心粒的近端，並在中心體的動態及分離中擔負不可或缺的角色。過量表達GAS2L1誘導中心體在細胞分裂週期進程中過早分離，此分離過程需要Plk1和Nek2A，這是兩個被証實在中心體分離中有重要功能的有絲分裂期的激酶。此外，GAS2L1也被發現進行有絲分裂期的磷酸化。基於這些發現，我們假設GAS2L1是微管和肌動蛋白絲在中心體上的附著位點，而這些微管和肌動蛋白絲被認為施加作用力、以達致中心體的動態及分離，我們並相信GAS2L1的這項功能是受磷酸化調控。本研究計劃書專注以下研究：（1）研究GAS2L1在中心體分離中的功能和機制，（2）分析GAS2L1在細胞分裂週期中的磷酸化狀態，（3）探索GAS2L1磷酸化對中心體分離的影響。這些研究將揭示一種全新的、並由GAS2L1及其結合的細胞骨架主導的中心體動態和分離機制。 總體而言，我們擬議的研究不僅將揭示一項未知的GAS2L1功能，而且還開闢了對中心體動力學和分離態的嶄新探索方向。鑑於中心體在整個細胞分裂週期中對組織微管起著關鍵作用，這項研究工作將有助增加我們對多種倚賴於微管的細胞活動的了解。急性骨髓性白血病是一種與基因組不穩定性相關的癌症，而在這種疾病中GAS2L1的表達會被抑制，本研究也從而會加深我們對誘發基因組不穩定性和癌症的分子機理的理解。

16101717.label: Realisation of objectives
16101717.value: Objective #1. To investigate the mechanism of GAS2L1 action in centrosome disjunction We have fulfilled this objective by identifying the mechanism by which GAS2L1 participates in centrosome disjunction and therefore in the assembly of bipolar spindles. GAS2L1 is a microtubule- and actin-binding protein and contains a calponin-homology (CH) domain and a GAS2-related (GAR) domain, which are responsible for F-actin- and microtubule-binding activities, respectively. We found that GAS2L1 functions in centrosome dynamics and disjunction by attaching F-actin and microtubules to the proximal end of mature centrioles. We generated the GAS2L1-knockout lines of hTERT RPE-1 cells by using the CRISPR/Cas9 system and used these GAS2L1-knockout cells to assess the physiological functions of GAS2L1. The GAS2L1-knockout cells showed significant defects in centrosome separation: ~22% of the G2 cells, which were identified by positive staining of CENP-F, contained split centrosomes (d > 2µm, d refers to inter-centrosome distance hereafter), compared with ~53% of the G2-phase parental hTERT RPE-1 cells. Time-lapse microscopy showed much reduced motility of the centrosomes in the GAS2L1-knockout cells, compared with those in the parental cells. These results are in agreement with those obtained from RNAi-mediated silencing of GAS2L1 expression. Timely centrosome disjunction facilitates proper spindle formation and thus chromosome segregation. We tested whether GAS2L1 is involved in mitotic spindle assembly and chromosome segregation. In metaphase GAS2L1-knockout cells, a bipolar spindle frequently formed with altered geometry: the pole-to-pole spindle axis was not oriented perpendicular to the metaphase plate. We measured the angle of the spindle axis to the metaphase plate and found that in ~92% of normal hTERT RPE-1 cells with spindle angle > 85°; and the proportion dropped to ~45% in GAS2L1-knockout cells. We also observed a higher incidence of chromosome segregation defects, such as chromosome bridges and lagging chromosomes, in anaphase GAS2L1-knockout cells than that in parental hTERT RPE-1 cells (~18% and ~5% for the GAS2L1-knockout and parental cells, respectively). Therefore, GAS2L1 is indispensable for proper spindle assembly and chromosome segregation. Objective #2. To analyze GAS2L1 phosphorylation during the cell cycle We have fulfilled this objective by revealing the cell cycle-dependent phosphorylation of GAS2L1 and by identifying the protein kinase that catalyze the phosphorylation in late G2 phase and mitosis. GAS2L1 displays cell-cycle dependent phosphorylation with hyperphosphorylation found in late G2 and mitosis. Mass spectrometry-based approaches were used to identify the mitotic phosphorylation sites. After mitotic arrest of GFP-GAS2L1-expressing cells, the hyperphosphorylated GAS2L1 protein was isolated by anti-GFP immunoprecipitation and then resolved using SDS-PAGE. Peptides were then extracted from phosphorylated GFP-GAS2L1 and were analyzed using mass spectrometry coupled with reverse-phase liquid chromatography. The obtained tandem mass spectra were subject to searches by using the MASCOT search engine for protein and phosphorylation site identification. By comparing the mass-spectrometric results of interphase and mitotic GAS2L1, we found that GAS2L1 phosphorylation was drastically induced during mitosis at 12 residues and 5 of the residues are clustered in the short region 352–360 (Ser352, Ser355, Ser357, Ser358, and Ser360) of GAS2L1. Next, we analyzed the function of the clustered phosphorylation on GAS2L1. We substituted all five residues of Ser352, Ser355, Ser357, Ser358, and Ser360 with Asp to generate the phosphomimetic mutant (5D) or with Ala to create the nonphosphorylatable mutant (5A). The mutants and the wildtype GAS2L1 were overexpressed in cells to examine their effects on centrosome separation. Our result showed that the overexpression of the wildtype and the 5D mutant of GAS2L1 efficiently induced centrosome separation, but the expression of the 5A mutant induced centrosome separation at a drastically attenuated activity. Furthermore, we mutated the five Ser residues individually to Asp or Ala and tested the effects of the single mutations. The mutant S352D showed a strong centrosome-splitting activity similar to that of the 5D mutant. In contrast, the S352A mutation lowered the centrosome-splitting activity of GAS2L1 to the same extent as the 5A mutant. Overall, the mutational analyses concluded that Ser352 phosphorylation is essential to stimulate the centrosome-separating activity of GAS2L1. Given the role of Ser352 phosphorylation, we searched for kinases that phosphorylate GAS2L1 at Ser352. The serine/threonine-protein kinase Nek2 (NIMA-related kinase 2) has been known to play a key role in G2/M to promote centrosome disjunction and bipolar spindle assembly. Therefore, we carried out assays to test whether Nek2A phosphorylates GAS2L1 at Ser352 and we obtained the following results. First, we detected the physical interaction between Nek2A and GAS2L1. By coexpressing GAS2L1 and Nek2A in cells followed by a pulldown assay, we found that Nek2A was readily detected in the pull-down of expressed GAS2L1, but not in the control pull-down. Therefore, Nek2A interacts with GAS2L1 specifically. Second, we performed an in vitro phosphorylation reaction of GAS2L1 by recombinant Nek2A and we detected a phosphorylation-dependent mobility upshift of GAS2L1 on SDS-PAGE. The upshift band was also stained by an antibody specifically recognizing Ser352-phosphorylated GAS2L1. Taken together, Nek2A is the kinase to phosphorylate GAS2L1 at Ser352. Objective #3. To explore the effects of GAS2L1 phosphorylation on centrosome disjunction We have fulfilled this objective by demonstrating the role of GAS2L1 phosphorylation in its physiological functions on centrosome disjunction. We generated a gas2l1-knockout cell line and stably expressed wildtype GAS2L1 or the mutants S352A and S352D in the gas2l1−/− cells at close-to-endogenous levels. In contrast to the parental line, the gas2l1−/− line clearly showed defects in centrosome disjunction in late-G2 cells. In the gas2l1−/− cells, a close-to-endogenous level expression of the wildtype or the S352D mutant of GAS2L1 restored centrosome separation to the same extent as in the parental line. The S352A expression did not rescue the disjunction defect in gas2l1−/− cells. These results confirmed that the Ser352 phosphorylation of GAS2L1 is required for centrosome disjunction during late G2 of the cell cycle. Timely centrosome separation before mitotic entry facilitates proper spindle formation and subsequent chromosome segregation during mitosis. To analyze the role of Ser352 phosphorylation in mitosis, we performed time-lapse imaging through G2 and mitosis on parental, gas2l1−/− cells, and gas2l1−/− cells expressing GFP-tagged wildtype GAS2L1 and the Ser352 mutants. We found that centrosome disjunction was markedly delayed in gas2l1−/− cells and S352A-expressing gas2l1−/− cells than in the parental cells and in gas2l1−/− cells expressing S352D GAS2L1. The gas2l1−/− cells and S352A-expressing gas2l1−/− also have a longer mitosis duration with chromosome mis-segregation events more frequently observed in anaphase, compared with parental cells and S352D-expressing gas2l1−/− cells. Overall, Ser352 phosphorylation of GAS2L1 is required to ensure timely centrosome separation and promotes the fidelity of chromosome segregation. Next, we asked whether the defective chromosome segregation observed after the inhibition of Ser352 phosphorylation is attributed to the defect in mitotic spindle assembly. The geometry of mitotic spindle was analysed in metaphase cells, and we found that the bipolar spindle frequently formed with defective geometry in gas2l1−/− cells and S352A-expressing gas2l1−/− cells during metaphase, compared with the symmetrical spindles observed in parental cells, wildtype GFP-GAS2L1-, and S352D-expressing gas2l1−/− cells. Therefore, timely centrosome separation facilitated by Ser352 phosphorylation of GAS2L1 is required for symmetrical spindle assembly to promote accurate chromosome segregation.

16101717.label: Major findings and research outcome
16101717.value: In animal cells, the centrosome is the principal microtubule-organizing center. During mitosis, centrosomes are incorporated into spindle poles to organize mitotic spindle for accurate chromosome segregation and maintenance of genome stability. Therefore, the separation of the duplicated centrosomes before mitosis is the prerequisite for the formation of mitotic spindle. GAS2L1 is an F-actin- and microtubule-binding protein that localizes to mature centrioles. We demonstrated that GAS2L1 functions in centrosome disjunction during late G2 by attaching microtubules and F-actin to the proximal end of mature centrioles. These cytoskeletons are considered to exert the forces that drive the centrosomes apart. We showed that GAS2L1 is regulated by an autoinhibitory mechanism that controls its F-actin- and microtubule-binding activities, and further that the autoinhibition is relieved by a site-specific GAS2L1 phosphorylation that occurs in late G2 and is catalyzed by Nek2A. GAS2L1 contains a calponin-homology (CH) domain and a GAS2-related (GAR) domain, which bind to F-actin and microtubules, respectively, and we showed that the CH and GAR domains bind directly to each other and that the binding inhibits the functions of both domains. To trigger centrosome disjunction in late G2, GAS2L1 is phosphorylated at Ser352, with the phosphorylation being mediated by Nek2A, and the phosphorylation relieves the GAS2L1 autoinhibition by disrupting the interaction between the CH and GAR domains, which then promotes the attachment of the cytoskeletons to the centrioles and thereby facilitates centrosome disjunction. Furthermore, GAS2L1 phosphorylation at Ser352 is required for centrosome disjunction occurring in late G2 and thus for proper spindle assembly and faithful chromosome segregation. We dissected the roles of the two Nek2A-mediated events, the removal of GAS2L1 autoinhibition and the disassembly of the centrosome linker, in centrosome disjunction, and we demonstrated that both actions of Nek2A are required to drive the disjunction: neither action alone is sufficient to separate the centrosomes. To conclude, our findings delineated the complex Nek2A-mediated mechanism underlying centrosome disjunction. Overall, we not only revealed the regulation of GAS2L1, which is a key player in centrosome motility and separation, but also presented a unified mechanism by which Nek2A mediates centrosome disjunction. Our findings and insights related to the mechanism of centrosome disjunction are crucial for understanding the process of bipolar spindle assembly and chromosome segregation, which are essential for maintaining genome and chromosome stability.

16101717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16101717.value: CH domains usually occur in tandem for effective F-actin binding. However, GAS2L1 contains a single CH domain that displays a robust F-actin-binding activity. We plan to investigate the mechanism by which GAS2L1 regulates actin organization in cells. We have found that GAS2L1 promotes the bundling of actin filaments in cells and in vitro by its amino-terminal CH domain. This F-actin–bundling activity of GAS2L1 promotes stress fibers formation, maturation of focal adhesions, and F-actin stability against drug-induced depolymerization. Furthermore, the CH domain of GAS2L1 dimerizes, which is inhibited by binding to the GAR domain. Overall, this work will reveal the functions of GAS2L1 on actin cytoskeletal organization and defines the role of CH domain in bundling F-actin. As a result, it will provide unprecedented insight into various cellular events involving CH domains.

16101717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16101717.value: Accurate chromosome segregation in mitosis requires the assembly of a bipolar spindle apparatus, which contains a centrosome at each spindle pole to organize spindle microtubules; this pulls and segregates the chromosomes into two daughter cells during mitosis. Timely separation of the centrosomes is critical for the formation of bipolar spindles and for subsequent accurate chromosome segregation. Defects in centrosome separation are highly associated with chromosome instability and cancers; however, the precise mechanism of centrosome separation remains unclear. We identified GAS2L1, an actin- and microtubule-binding protein, as a centriole-associated protein that is crucially involved in centrosome disjunction. We demonstrated that the centrosomal GAS2L1-tethered cytoskeletons and the centrosome linker play opposing roles in maintaining centrosome cohesion and in centrosome disjunction. Furthermore, the mitotic kinase Nek2 phosphorylates GAS2L1 to remove an autoinhibitory interaction between the actin- and the microtubule-binding domains, and that this phosphorylation event plays a key role in centrosome disjunction. Our work revealed a previously unidentified disjunction mechanism mediated by GAS2L1 and the regulation of GAS2L1’s function at centrosomes. These findings and insights are crucial for understanding the process of bipolar spindle assembly and chromosome segregation, which are essential for maintaining genome stability and preventing uncontrolled proliferation that leads to cancers.

16101917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16101917.value: 微生物固氮是指固氮菌通過體內固氮酶的作用將大氣中的氮（N2）還原成氨，是一個具有重要意義的生物過程 。普遍認為固氮菌所固定的氮素（diazotroph derived nitrogen ，DDN）是通過異養和自養生物吸收，繼而被浮游動物攝食後釋放出溶解態的氮而進入食物網的物質循環中。原生動物是浮游植物最主要的攝食者，因此它們在DDN釋放到水體的過程中起着重要的作用，但是目前尚未有相關研究探討原生動物對固氮藍細菌的攝食壓力。在本課題中，我們將利用在浮游動物攝食方面十多年豐富的研究經驗，並結合生物分子技術（qPCR)來研究南中國海由原生動物攝食所導致的不同種類的單細胞固氮藍細菌（UCDs)的死亡率。初步的研究和現有數據表明，目前已知的所有UCDs子系均能在南中國海發現，因此南中國海是研究本課題的理想海域。本研究有助於闡明下行控制因素對UCDs的分佈和種群動態變化的影響。另外，由於UCDs採用時間分隔的方式將固碳和固氮過程分離——白天進行光合作用固碳，晚上進行固氮，以防止固氮酶被氧氣破壞；另外，由於固氮酶需要大量的能量還原N2， 因此與其他非固氮菌相比，UCDs的C:N值晝夜差異較大。因此我們認為，原生動物為了抵消攝食非固氮餌料引起的化學計量不平衡，可能偏好具有較低C:N值的固氮菌。為了驗證該假說，我們將進行室內培養實驗，喂食原生動物不同晝夜時段的（不同C:N值)固氮和非固氮藻所組成的混合餌料。此研究將首次測定由攝食導致的不同種類的UCDs的死亡率；並探討原生動物是否選擇性攝食UCDs（與個體大小相近的非固氮藻混合時）。研究UCDs和微型浮游動物的營養級聯關係，以及它們在控制UCDs和其他浮游生物分佈和組成所起的作用，有助於我們瞭解海洋生態系統N和C的生物地質化學循環的複雜性。

16101917.label: Realisation of objectives
16101917.value: We conducted both laboratory and field study to address the two objectives. I believe the two objectives are well achieved. Laboratorial experiment about the protistal grazing selectivity on a major marine UCD In this study, considering that prey with low carbon to nitrogen (C:N) ratio is more nutritious and it could influence the grazing behaviour of predator (Shannon et al., 2007), we hypothesized that Crocosphaera watsonii (a major marine UCD) is selectively grazed by microzooplankton when it is fixing nitrogen. To test this hypothesis, we first measured the diel variation of cellular C:N ratio of C. watsonii and Chlorella autotrophica (a non-diazotrophic unicellular microalga with a similar size to C. watsonii). Then, a mixed diet consisting of C. watsonii and C. autotrophica (1:1) was supplied to four species of marine protists (Oxyrrhis marina, Euplotes sp., Scuticociliate sp. and Lepidodinium sp.) during daytime and nighttime, respectively. We found that both C. watsonii and C. autotrophica showed a diel pattern of C:N ratio that increased during daytime and decreased during nighttime, while the magnitude of the diel variation was much greater in C. watsonii. C. watsonii was found to enhance respiration for creating an oxygen depleted condition for nitrogen fixation at nighttime (Dron et al., 2012), which lead to a great decrease in C:N ratio during nighttime. Although different grazers showed specific preferences for different preys, all the tested grazers increased grazing rate and selectivity on C. watsonii when the latter was fixing nitrogen at night. In particular, O. marina, a widely distributed free-living protist in marine ecosystems, whose grazing behaviour closely followed the changes in C:N ratio over time. It changed from preferring C. autotrophica during daytime to preferring C. watsonii during nighttime. These results suggested that the UCD became more nutritious (inferred by C:N ratio) and thus a preferred prey for microzooplankton grazers when it fixes N2, which implies the importance of UCD as a N source of the microzooplankton in the nitrogen-limited oceanic waters. This work was published in journal Frontiers in Marine Science (Deng et al., 2020). Estimation of grazing impact on UCDs in marine ecosystems We used a combination of dilution experiment and quantitative PCR to estimate the grazing impact on the major UCDs in the marine ecosystems. The dilution experiment is a technique that estimates the instantaneous growth rate and grazing mortality rate of the marine phytoplanktons that are overlapping in size with their microzooplankton grazers (Landry and Hassett, 1982). In our studies, we conducted the dilution experiments under ambient and nutrient enriched condition (20M nitrate and silicate; 1.25M phosphate) to study the influence of nutrient availability to the overall phytoplankton community and UCDs. We used an optimised protocol with high recovery rate to extract the DNA samples collected from the dilution experiments, in which the UCDs were quantified with their specific TaqMan assays. Based on our result, the estimated apparent growth rates of the UCDs in the duplicate bottles of the dilution experiments were highly consistent with each other, suggested that our approach can be used to estimate the growth and grazing rates of the UCDs concisely. We investigated the growth and grazing mortality of the UCDs with this approach in the western Bering Sea. The marine BNF was earlier thought to be only occurring in warm and oligotrophic oceans, while recent study demonstrated that BNF is conducted by the UCDs (UCYN-A groups) in polar waters (Harding et al., 2018). Nevertheless, the environmental determinants and ecological functioning of the UCDs in the cold waters are still unclear. In this study, we have found a hotspot of UCYN-A groups (UCYN-A1 and UCYN-A2/3/4) in a high-iron-low-nitrate water in the western Bering Sea. UCYN-A1 (1-3m) is relatively smaller in size than the known species of UCYN-A2/3/4 (4-10m) (Farnelid et al., 2016). Statistical analyses suggested that the abundances of UCYN-A groups were mainly determined by the concentration of dissolved iron (mainly from riverine input in the studied region). As estimated by the dilution experiments, we found that both the instantaneous growth and grazing mortality rates of the UCYN-A groups were significantly higher than that of the overall phytoplankton community (Figure 1). And the rates of UCYN-A1 (small group) were higher than that of UCYN-A2/3/4 (large group). The growth rates of overall phytoplankton community increased in the nutrient enriched incubations, while the UCYN-A groups showed opposite patterns, suggested that the UCDs can take advantages over the other phytoplanktons in the nitrate-deplete condition in the studied region. In addition, the growth of the UCYN-A groups were almost balanced by their mortality caused by the microzooplankton grazing, indicated that the biomass of UCYN-A groups were turned over quickly although they are rare compared to other phytoplanktons (Figure 1). These findings suggested that the UCDs were selectively grazed by the microzooplankton grazers and could play an important role in the nitrogen cycle in the studied area. Our findings will provide important contribution to understanding the determinants of and grazing impact on the UCDs in the ocean. We are currently revising a manuscript about this study, which will be submitted very soon. Besides this work, we have also quantified and compared the growth and grazing mortality rates of the major UCDs (i.e., UCYN-A, UCYN-B and UCYN-C) at different water depths in the South China Sea; and we also observed the high biomass turnover rates of the UCDs. We will write a manuscript about this study as well. Figure 1. 16101917.label: Major findings and research outcome
16101917.value: In this project, we used both laboratorial cultural experiments and field observations to unravel the grazing impact on marine unicellular cyanobacterial diazotrophs (UCDs). For laboratorial experiment, we found that Crocosphaera watsonii, a major model organism of marine UCD, was more preferred by protistal grazers when it was fixing nitrogen and became more nutritious (lower in C:N ratio) during nighttime. In field observation, we found a hotspot of UCYN-A groups (major marine UCDs) in a high-iron-low-nitrate water in the western Bering Sea. By combining the classical dilution experiment and molecular technique (i.e. quantitative PCR), we have successfully estimated the instantaneous growth and grazing mortality rates of the UCYN-A groups in the western Bering Sea. The UCYN-A groups were more actively growing and grazed by microzooplankton grazers compared to the overall phytoplankton community; and the growth of the UCYN-A groups was mostly balanced by their grazing mortality that caused by the microzooplanktons (i.e. with high biomass turnover rates). Moreover, we also observed variations of the growth and grazing mortality rates among different groups of UCYN-A. All these findings suggested that the UCDs are actively grazed and more preferred by microzooplanktons in marine ecosystem, playing a crucial role in the marine nitrogen and carbon cycling. On the other hand, given that the grazing impact on UCDs are largely unknown in the field, our rate measurement dataset can serve as important basis for estimating the dynamics of UCDs and nitrogen cycle in biogeochemical models. The laboratorial study has been published in the journal Frontier in Marine Science (Deng et al., 2020). We are preparing a manuscript regarding the field work in the western Bering Sea, which will be submitted very soon. Furthermore, we have also conducted some studies related to marine diazotrophs with the support of this funding. We have conducted field surveys to unravel the determinants and ecophysiologies of the marine diazotrophs at multiple scales. We have identified the importance of physical forcing like boundary current, mesoscale eddies and wind-driven coastal upwelling in controlling the dynamics of the diazotrophs (Cheung et al., 2019; Cheung et al., 2020). Moreover, we have also used multi-stressors cultural experiment to demonstrate that warming can relieve the phosphorus-limitation in a major UCD (under review). In addition, a number of studies related to marine microbial ecology were also partially supported by this funding (a total of 14 papers acknowledged this grant).

16101917.value: This is a topic deserves a lot of further study. One of the extension of this project is that we have established a collaboration with scientists in the Scripps Institute of Oceanography, University of California San Diego, to participate in a research cruise in Eastern Indian Ocean (west of Australia) in early next year (It was scheduled in last year, but postponed twice due to COVID-19 pandemic. We will study the species specific growth and grazing rate of different types of diazotrophs, as well as other important cyanobacteria groups using molecular techniques.

16101917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16101917.value: Ocean contributes about half of the global primary production, but a large area of the (sub)tropic ocean is nutrient (particularly nitrogen) limited. Some cyanobacteria can fix nitrogen gas and produce ammonium (called diazotrophs), which can not only support their own growth, but also reaches the food web for other heterotrophic and autotrophic plankton. Protozoan zooplankton are the major grazers of phytoplankton, and are therefore a major player in the processes that release diazotroph derived nitrogen to the water column, but their grazing impact on unicellular cyanobacterial diazotrophs (UCDs) has never been investigated. In this project, we use molecular technology (qPCR), to study the taxon-specific grazing mortality of different phylotypes of UCDs. This may help to elucidate the possible role of top-down control in the distribution patterns and population dynamics of different groups of UCDs. Understanding the trophic interaction between UCDs and micrograzers and their role in regulating the composition and distribution of UCDs and other planktonic organisms will help us to understand the complexity of the biogeochemical cycling of nitrogen and carbon in the oceanic ecosystems.
