16102317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16102317.value: As the most abundant photosynthetic organisms on Earth, the unicellular cyanobacteria Prochlorococcus and Synechococcus contribute to ~50% of primary production in the world’s oceans. About 15% of marine cyanobacteria are estimated to be infected by viruses (cyanophages) at any given time and a variety of dissolved organic matter (DOM) can be released after cell lysis. Traditionally, marine DOM is thought to be consumed primarily by heterotrophic bacteria. Recently, field studies suggest that Prochlorococcus and Synechococcus can take up organic nutrients, including amino acids. However, the impact of viral lysis products on cyanobacteria has not been studied. In our preliminary experiments, we added viral lysis products to Prochlorococcus strain MIT9313 and studied its transcriptomic response using RNA-seq. We found that the transcript abundances of many tRNA genes increased and we hypothesize that free amino acids in viral lysis products may be responsible for this transcriptional response. We systemically tested 20 amino acids and found for the first time that several amino acids can be used as the sole N source for Prochlorococcus MIT9313 while some inhibited its growth. Our transcriptomic study also showed that the transcript abundances of many photosynthesis genes and Calvin cycle genes decreased. We hypothesize that photosynthesis of Prochlorococcus may be inhibited by viral lysis products. In our proposed work, we plan to test our hypotheses in three aspects: transcriptomic response, key components in viral lysis products, and physiological effects on the uninfected cells. We will first generate viral lysis products from more host-phage pairs and determine which cellular pathways of Prochlorococcus are affected by all the DOM sources and which are affected by a specific source. Next, we will measure the concentrations of intracellular and extracellular free amino acids of infected cells and analyze the transcriptomic response of Prochlorococcus to different amino acids. Finally, we will measure the photosynthetic efficiency, carbon fixation rate, and ATP content of Prochlorococcus MIT9313 cells after addition of viral lysis products. We will also study the infection kinetics of cyanophages to test whether viral lysis products stimulate or reduce cyanophage infection. Our work will give us new insights into how cyanophages affect the composition of marine DOM and how viral lysis products feeds back to affect the physiology of the uninfected host cells. The research proposed here will deepen our understanding of the role of cyanobacteria and cyanophages in carbon cycling in the marine ecosystem. 單細胞藍細菌原綠球藻和聚球藻大約貢獻了海洋初級生產總量的50%，是世界上數量最為龐大的光合作用生物。侵染藍細菌的噬菌體也在海洋中廣泛分布，其侵染的藍細菌約占海洋中藍細菌總量的15%。噬菌體侵染最終會導致細菌的裂解並釋放出子代噬菌體和細胞內的有機營養物質。已有實驗表明原綠球藻和聚球藻可以吸收氨基酸等有機營養但噬菌體裂解產物對細菌的影響尚待研究。在預實驗中，我們分析了原綠球藻在添加噬菌體裂解產物後的轉錄組差異。結果表明噬菌體裂解產物會導致細菌氨酰tRNA合成酶基因表達水平的提高以及光合作用相關基因表達水平的降低。基於預實驗的結果，本研究將通過測量細胞的生理指標以衡量噬菌體裂解產物對細菌代謝的影響，並進一步探究噬菌體裂解產物的添加對噬菌體和細菌相互作用的影響以及噬菌體代謝產物中的成分。針對藍細菌及其噬菌體互作的研究將加深我們對藍細菌及其噬菌體對海洋中物質能量循環的影響的認識。

16102317.label: Realisation of objectives
16102317.value: We have been able to fully achieve all the three objectives of the proposal. In Objective 1, we employed RNA-seq to analyze the transcriptomes of Prochlorococcus MIT9313 cells taken at 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 24, 48, and 72 h after amendments with the seven lysates or the growth medium (control). By normalizing gene expression levels to those of the control cultures, differentially expressed genes were identified as early as 0.5 h and their numbers varied among different DOM amendments (Liu and Zeng, attached in Part C). To resolve the biological functions of these differentially expressed genes, we grouped them into functional categories. Other than genes of unknown function, the most abundant functional category was translation and the second most abundant was energy metabolism (Liu and Zeng, attached in Part C). Genes related to nitrogen (N) metabolism were also abundant (Liu and Zeng, attached in Part C). Genes in these three categories were highly represented in the cultures amended with the seven lysates, indicating that translation, energy metabolism, and N metabolism of Prochlorococcus were affected by the seven lysates. Besides the common responses, some genes were differentially expressed in response to a specific lysate. We compared the transcriptional responses of Prochlorococcus MIT9313 to different lysates by normalizing the transcripts in one DOM amendment to those in another (Liu and Zeng, attached in Part C). First, we compared lysates generated from the same host by different phages. Normalized to ProDOM, there were more than one thousand genes differentially expressed in ProPSS2DOM and ProSyn19DOM, respectively. However, when ProPSS2DOM was normalized to ProSyn19DOM, there were only two genes with significantly increased transcripts (PMT2490 and PMT2717, both of unknown function). Similarly, when SynSyn19DOM was normalized to SynSShM2DOM, there were only one gene with significantly increased transcripts (PMT2634, unknown function) and one gene with significantly decreased transcripts (urease subunit gene ureA). Together, our data suggested that the DOM compounds released by different phages from the same host strain are similar, but are different from those released by sonication (ProDOM and SynDOM). Second, we compared lysates generated from different hosts by the same phage. When ProSyn19DOM was normalized to SynSyn19DOM, 305 differentially expressed genes were identified, which is less than 50% of the number of differentially expressed genes between ProDOM and SynDOM. This suggested that phage infection can homogenize the DOM composition of different host strains. Third, when SynSShM2DOM was normalized to SynSShM2ϕDOM, 300 differentially expressed genes were identified. This might be due to the different sized filters used to prepare these two lysates and hence the different DOM compounds in them. The results generated from Objective 1 have been written as a manuscript, which is attached in Part C and will be further revised for submission in summer 2021. In Objective 2, we first measured the intracellular free dissolved amino acids after Prochlorococcus MIT9313 was infected by cyanophage P-SS2, which takes ~12 h for one infection cycle. Aspartic acid, glutamic acid, asparagine, and tyrosine were the most abundant free dissolved amino acids in Prochlorococcus MIT9313 cells that we can reliably quantify. At the end of infection (12 h), their concentrations in the infected cells were all higher than those in the uninfected cells (Liu and Zeng, attached in Part C), which might result in more free dissolved amino acids in phage lysates. Consistent with this hypothesis, we found that the concentrations of total combined amino acids in vDOM (>10 kDa dissolved protein fraction after protease digestion) were much higher than those of the natural seawater-based Pro99 growth medium. We also studied the transcriptional responses of Prochlorococcus cells to different amino acids (Fang et al. 2019 Environmental Microbiology). After vDOM addition, 31 out of 43 tRNA genes showed increased transcript abundances. Not much is known about the transcriptional regulation of tRNA genes in cyanobacteria, but in E. coli cells tRNA abundances increased after amino acids were added (Dong et al., 1996). The tRNA aminoacylation level (charging level) in E. coli is also positively correlated with amino acid concentrations in the growth medium (Dittmar et al., 2005). To test whether amino acids can increase the tRNA abundances, we added glycine to Prochlorococcus MIT9313 and used quantitative reverse transcription PCR (RT-qPCR) to detect the transcript levels of tRNA-Gly1. Glycine did not affect the growth rate of Prochlorococcus MIT9313; however, similar to vDOM, glycine addition increased the transcript abundances of tRNA-Gly1, suggesting that amino acids are one of the compounds in vDOM that affected the expression of tRNA genes. To test whether tRNA genes can be responsive to non-cognate amino acids, we added aspartic acid and found that this non-cognate amino acid can also increase the transcript abundances of tRNA-Gly1 while did not change the growth rate of Prochlorococcus MIT9313. Moreover, we found that addition of glycine and aspartic acid can decrease the transcript abundances of ribosomal protein genes. In Objective 3, we investigated whether viral lysis products affect the photosynthesis and respiration of Prochlorococcus (Fang et al. 2019 Environmental Microbiology). For photosynthesis, we measured the maximum photochemical quantum yield (Fv/Fm) of PSII, which reveals the potential ability of PSII to transform absorbed photons to chemical energy. Fv/Fm of Prochlorococcus MIT9313 decreased by ~3% from 24 h after vDOM addition. Despite the slight decrease of Fv/Fm, the carbon fixation rate of Prochlorococcus cells decreased by ~16% after vDOM addition. In contrast to photosynthesis, the respiration of Prochlorococcus MIT9313 cells was transiently enhanced by ~51% at 12 h after vDOM addition. Similar to vDOM, glycine slightly reduced the Fv/Fm of Prochlorococcus cells by ~2%. However, glycine reduced the carbon fixation rate by ~32% and increased the respiration by up to ~108% at 72 h. The more significant effects of glycine than vDOM on respiration and carbon fixation rate might be due to the higher DOM concentration of glycine. Although Prochlorococcus has been shown to take up amino acids (Zubkov et al., 2003; Mary et al., 2008; Gomez-Pereira et al., 2013; Bjorkman et al., 2015), as far as we know, our study showed for the first time that amino acids can reduce the carbon fixation of Prochlorococcus. With decreased carbon fixation and increased respiration, Prochlorococcus was supposed to accumulate less organic carbon and in that case its growth should have been inhibited. However, our results showed that Prochlorococcus MIT9313 maintained its growth rate after vDOM and glycine addition. One plausible explanation is that Prochlorococcus assimilates DOM compounds, which is consistent with the expression of tRNA genes and is also consistent with the ability of Prochlorococcus to assimilate organic compounds.

16102317.label: Major findings and research outcome
16102317.value: Marine phytoplankton contribute to about one half of global primary production, and a significant proportion of their photosynthetically fixed organic carbon is released after viral infection as dissolved organic matter (DOM). This DOM pool is known to be consumed by heterotrophic microorganisms; however, its bioavailability to the uninfected co-occurring phytoplankton remains largely unknown. In this research project, we conducted transcriptomic analysis and biochemical assays to study the utilization of viral lysis products by the unicellular cyanobacterium Prochlorococcus, which is the most abundant photosynthetic organism on Earth. While Prochlorococcus growth was not affected by viral lysates (without infectious phage particles), its tRNA and ribosomal protein genes were differentially expressed, which was partially caused by amino acids. Our transcriptomic data also suggested that viral lysates inhibited the photosynthesis while enhanced the respiration of Prochlorococcus. Indeed, after addition of viral lysates to Prochlorococcus cells, the maximum photochemical efficiency of photosystem II and CO2 fixation decreased while the respiration rate increased. Furthermore, the extracellular media of Prochlorococcus showed lysozyme activity that can be induced by viral lysates. This inducible lysozyme activity might enable Prochlorococcus to degrade cell wall peptidoglycan of infected cyanobacteria into amino acids, which have been shown to be assimilated by Prochlorococcus. One of the highest positive fold-changes was observed for the 6S RNA, a non-coding RNA functioning as a global transcriptional regulator in bacteria. The high level of 6S RNA might be responsible for some of the observed transcriptional responses. Taken together, our results revealed the transcriptional regulation of Prochlorococcus in response to viral lysis products and suggested its metabolic potential to utilize organic N compounds. Our project has resulted in one publication (Fang et al. 2019 Environmental Microbiology) and one manuscript that will be submitted in summer 2021 (Liu and Zeng, attached in Part C). One Ph.D. student and one M.Phil. student have been trained during this project.

16102317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16102317.value: Our project revealed the transcriptional responses of Prochlorococcus to DOM and suggested that the a non-coding RNA 6S RNA may function as a global transcriptional regulator. We plan to further study the function of 6S RNA using in vivo and in vitro assays. Our project also showed that DOM inhibits the photosynthesis of Prochlorococcus. We plan to study the molecular mechanism of the inhibitory effects of DOM on photosynthetic pathways.

16102317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16102317.value: Photosynthetic microorganisms called phytoplankton are abundant in the oceans and contribute to about one half of global CO2 fixation. Phytoplankton are frequently infected by viruses and after infection their organic carbon is released into the ocean as dissolved organic matter (DOM). Marine DOM is important for the marine food web because it supports the growth of heterotrophic microorganisms. However, the impact of marine DOM on the uninfected phytoplankton is largely unknown. Our project showed that viral lysis products inhibit the photosynthesis of the marine cyanobacterium Prochlorococcus. We also found that Prochlorococcus can regulate its gene expression differentially in response to different DOM sources. Since Prochlorococcus is the most abundant photosynthetic organism on Earth, its utilization of marine DOM may affect carbon cycling in the world’s oceans.

16102417.value: 通過基因篩選現已經在哺乳動物中發現纖連蛋白富亮氨酸跨膜蛋白（Fibronectin leucine-rich transmembrane proteins, FLRTs）家族中共有三個成員， FLRT1,FLRT2,FLRT3, 並且已有研究證明FLRTs在細胞粘附以及信號通路傳到中起到重要作用。儘管已有研究發現FLRT3突變可能同病人耳聾有某種關聯，但是對於FLRT1-3在聽覺中的作用還是了解甚少。近來，我們的實驗數據表明FLRT1和FLRT3與被認為有可能是聽毛細胞中的機械傳導通道TMC1有相互作用，並且可以被TMC1下調表達。隨後我們還發現FLRT1和FLRT3在聽毛細胞中均有表達但位置有所不同：FLRT1位於聽毛細胞体的頂部區域而FLRT3 位於聽毛的踝連接處。當在聽毛細胞中敲減FLRT1的表達時會損壞靜聽毛的梯式排列。通過這些實驗結果我們認為FLRT1和FLRT3有可能在聽毛的形成和維持中起到重要作用並且進一步影響聽毛細胞中機械傳導通道的功能。 FLRT1和FLRT3 在聽毛細胞中的表達和功能通過與TMC1的相互作用而被TMC1所調控。為了驗證這一假設，我們將通過（1）檢測FLRT1在形成和維持聽毛結構以及毛細胞機械傳導中的作用。 （2）檢測FLRT3 在形成和維持踝連以及毛細胞機械傳導中的作用。 （3）研究FLRT1，FLRT3 與TMC1結構及功能上的相互作用。 聽毛的發育和維持對聽毛細胞的機械傳導過程起到重要的作用。我們對FLRT1和FLRT3在聽毛細胞中的功能及其與TMC1結構和功能的相互作用上的研究將不僅對聽覺中聲音機械傳導過程中的重要蛋白TMC1 的功能得到進一步的理解，而且還能對機械傳導複合體的作用得到更深入和廣泛的認識。

16102617.label: Realisation of objectives
16102617.value: We and others have previously showed that neuronal apoptosis contributes to the attraction of microglial precursors to colonize the brain, especially the optic tectum region in the developing zebrafish brain. However, we noticed that the migration of microglial precursors from their birth-place to the proximal brain regions is independent of neuronal apoptosis, indicating the existence of alternative mechanisms regulating this process. To address this issue, we took advantage of the zebrafish for its accessible in vivo imaging and genetic manipulation to further elucidate that microglia colonization is also regulated by Il34-Csf1ra pathway. Our key results are as follows. 1. Because the migration of microglial precursors to the proximal brain region was unaffected in the Tg(Xla.Tubb:bcl-2) transgenic fish, in which neuronal apoptosis was inhibited, we therefore conducted a careful re-examination of the microglia colonization in all CNS compartments of Tg(Xla.Tubb:bcl-2) embryos. We surprisingly found that microglia deficiency was drastic in the optic tectum but not significant in the forebrain and tegmentum. These data indicate that both the migration of microglial precursors to the proximal brain region and their subsequent colonization in the forebrain and tegmentum are independent of neuronal apoptosis. 2. We then went on to search for the possible mechanisms complementing neuronal apoptosis for microglia colonization, and identified that csf1ra deficiency led to severe defect in microglia colonization, indicating that csf1ra signaling may play a role in the migration of microglial precursors. 3. To further dissect the role of csf1ra pathway in the migration of microglial precursors, we turned to the three potential ligands for csf1ra, namely csf1a, csf1b and il34. We found that il34 was expressed at highest level among the three genes in the developing zebrafish brain. To directly assay their functions in vivo, we generated three mutant lines deficient in the respective genes. Consistent with the highest expression in the brain, il34 deficiency, but not csf1a and csf1b, resulted in significant decrease of microglia in a dosage-dependent manner. Through time-lapse imaging, we showed that primitive macrophages, presumably microglial precursors, were both developmentally and functionally normal but failed to effectively colonize the anterior head region, indicating a direct role of il34 in the migration of microglial precursors. 4. To provide further evidence for the function of the three ligands, we performed gain-of-function assays by generating three neuronal-specific overexpression transgenic lines using the Xla.Tubb promoter. Only il34, but not csf1a and csf1b overexpression embryos, exhibited a dramatic increase of microglia. Through time-lapse imaging, we showed that the massive CNS-infiltrating macrophages in Tg(Xla.Tubb:il34) embryos were at least partly resulted from direct migration. We further showed that the effects of il34 overexpression purely depended on Csf1ra and the enforced expression of csf1ra in neutrophils, another kind of immune cells that normally do not invade the CNS, drove their ectopic CNS colonization, establishing that il34-csf1ra pathway is sufficient for the migration of microglia precursors. 5. Finally, we reconstructed the model for microglia colonization in zebrafish. We found that il34-csf1ra pathway and neuronal apoptosis function in this process independently. Microglial precursors are first attracted to the proximal brain region through the activation of il34-csf1ra pathway; subsequently, these two pathways synergistically orchestrate the colonization of microglia in different CNS compartments. This study shows that Il34-csf1ra signaling and neuronal apoptosis synergistically orchestrate the colonization of microglia in early zebrafish development. Microglia play important roles in tissue clearance, immune defense, as well as the proper development and function of the neural networks. Yet, the cellular and molecular basis underlying these versatile functional states of microglia is not fully understood. Recent single-cell studies in human microglia revealed possible heterogeneity, but it remains obscure whether this asserted heterogeneity represents simply different states of microglia or distinct subpopulations. In our study, we identified two ontogenically distinct microglial populations in zebrafish and comprehensively characterized their differences in cellular phenotypes, origins, transcriptome profiles, and functions. Our key results are as follows. 1. Two distinct microglial populations exist in the zebrafish brain. The predominant population (~80%) are widely distributed and amoeboid in morphology. The other population (~20%) are enriched in the white matter and ramified in morphology. They also differ in their dependency on the CSF1R (colony-stimulating factor 1 receptor) signaling and developmental origin. 2. We established a TgBAC(ccl34b.1:eGFP) transgenic line that labels only the amoeboid but not ramified microglia. Transcriptome profiling showed that both populations express microglia/macrophage signature genes but also display substantial differences, indicating their functional diversification. 3. To further explore their cellular phenotypes, we performed acute brain slice culture and phagocytosis assay. Results showed that the ccl34b.1+ amoeboid microglia are highly mobile and phagocytotic, whereas the ccl34b.1- ramified microglia are less mobile and possess relatively low phagocytotic capability. 4. Finally, in an in vivo CNS bacterial infection model, though only the ccl34b.1+ microglia migrated to the infection site and actively phagocytosed the bacteria, transcriptomic profiling showed that the ccl34b.1- microglia also responded by secreting chemokines, which presumably play a role in the recruitment of T cells and myeloid cells from periphery. We concluded that the ccl34b.1+ microglia play major roles in tissue clearance and the ccl34b.1- microglia secrete immune regulators to modulate the inflammation. We hence designated the ccl34b.1+ and ccl34b.1- populations as phagocytotic and regulatory microglia, respectively. This study sheds light on the functional diversification of microglia, providing ideal models to study the contribution of different roles of microglia to CNS homeostasis and pathology.

16102617.label: Major findings and research outcome
16102617.value: Microglia are the major immune cells in the central nervous system (CNS), and they are involved in diverse biological processes, including immune defense, neural development, neural function, and neuroinflammation. Born in peripheral hematopoietic tissues, microglial precursors colonize the CNS during early embryogenesis and maintain themselves thereafter. However, the mechanism underlying this colonization process remains elusive. We have found that microglial precursors, which are born in the peripheral hematopoietic tissue are attracted to the brain by brain-derived interleukin 34 (il34) and its receptor colony-stimulating factor 1 receptor a (csf1ra). In both il34- and csf1ra-deficient zebrafish larva, embryonic macrophages fail to migrate to anterior head and colonize the CNS, but their initial development and colonization to peripheral tissues remain largely unaffected. Activation of Il34-Csf1ra pathway is sufficient to attract embryonic macrophage to the CNS independent of neuronal apoptosis. Our study shows that cytokine signaling pathway orchestrate the colonization of microglia in early zebrafish development. This work was published in Development Cell 46:552-563, 2018. The versatile functions of microglia have long been thought to attribute to the heterogeneity of microglia. Recent studies revealed possible heterogeneity in human but not murine microglia, yet a firm demonstration linking microglial heterogeneity to functional phenotypes remains scarce. We have identified two distinct microglial populations in adult zebrafish that differ in morphology, distribution, development, and function. The predominant population – phagocytotic microglia is broadly distributed, amoeboid in shape, highly mobile and phagocytotic. The other white matter-enriched population, termed regulatory microglia, possesses ramified protrusions but has limited mobility and phagocytosis capability. Their functional differences are further supported by distinct transcriptomes and responses to bacterial infection, where phagocytotic microglia function in tissue clearance and regulatory microglia release immune regulators. Our study sheds light on the heterogeneity and functional diversification of microglia. This work was recently published in Science Advances 6:eabd1160, 2020.

16102617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16102617.value: Microglia are mononuclear macrophages of the central nervous system (CNS). Recent studies have shown that in addition to functioning as the immune cells to maintain homeostasis of the brain, microglia are also actively involved in the regulation of neurogenesis and neural activity in the developing and adult CNS. The importance of microglia is exemplified by their engagement in various neurodegenerative disorders, such as Multiple Sclerosis, Autism, Alzheimer and Parkinson diseases. Our studies reveal the mechanism orchestrating the colonization of microglia in the CNS and uncover the heterogeneity and functional diversification of microglia. We believe that these findings may offer new therapeutic opportunities for the treatment of associated human diseases.

16102717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16102717.value: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is the most prevalent form of dementia and is characterized by the deposition of amyloid-beta (Aβ) plaques and neurofibrillary tangles in the brain. Synaptic dysfunction, which disrupts vulnerable memory-related networks, precedes neuronal degeneration and hippocampal atrophy during AD progression. We previously demonstrated that activation of a postsynaptic G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR), melanocortin-4 receptor (MC4R), restores the synaptic functions and plasticity in the hippocampus of APP/PS1 mice, a transgenic mouse model that exhibits AD pathologies. While soluble Aβ peptide oligomer is believed to be the major agent causing synaptic impairment during AD progression, our preliminary findings suggest that MC4R activation reduces the levels of Aβ in APP/PS1 mice. In contrast, blockade of MC4R signaling in the hippocampus of APP/PS1 mice exacerbates amyloid accumulation in the brain. Thus, in the study proposed herein, we will examine the roles of MC4R signaling on Aβ level and deposition. We will also examine whether activation of hippocampal MC4R signaling can restore neuronal network activity, which is critical for learning and memory, in APP/PS1 mice. We will demonstrate the beneficial effect of MC4R activation on memory performance in these mice using a battery of behavioral tests. Finally, we will examine the molecular mechanisms that underlie the action of pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC)/MC4R signaling in hippocampal neurons in AD. The proposed study aims to demonstrate the functional roles of hippocampal POMC/MC4R signaling in Aβ metabolism and neuronal network function in AD, which may help identify new targets for drug development.

16102717.label: Realisation of objectives
16102717.value: This work demonstrates that melanocortin 4 receptor (MC4R) plays an important role in the hippocampus, where it maintains and modulates synaptic plasticity; synaptic plasticity dysfunction is a key signature of Alzheimer’s disease (AD). AD is among the most common neurodegenerative disorders and is presented with a lack of existing disease-modifying treatment. It represents a devastating disease with progression characterized by the deterioration of memory and cognitive functions, neuroinflammation, and the accumulation of β–amyloid (Aβ) and neurofibrillary tangles termed “hyperphosphorylated tau protein” in the brain. These maladies together lead to dysfunctions in neurons and the resident brain immune glial cells, including microglia and astrocytes. Neuropeptides govern diverse pathophysiological processes and represent key players in AD pathogenesis, regulating synaptic functions, glial cell functions and amyloid pathology. The melanocortin receptors (MCRs), a family of G protein-coupled receptor and its ligands, proopiomelanocortin (POMC)-derived neuropeptide, have been implicated in the homeostatic process modulating synaptic functions in the hippocampus. While disruption of this hippocampal microcircuit exacerbated synaptic impairment in the APP/PS1 transgenic mouse model of AD, POMC overexpression or enhancement of MC4R signaling in the hippocampus rescues the synaptic plasticity deficits. Furthermore, peripheral administration of a synthetic melanocortin analogue in AD transgenic mouse models resulted in reduction in Aβ deposition and neuronal loss. However, the effect of melanocortin signaling on the multiple neurodegenerative signatures of AD, particularly the glial activation and inflammatory shift underlying AD pathogenesis, remains to be examined. In this study, we investigated the therapeutic potentials of MCR activation in AD through understanding the molecular and cellular basis of the beneficial actions of their activation in the central nervous system. In this study, we examined whether and how MCR activation exerts beneficial effects on AD pathophysiology. We showed that MCR activation mediated by the central administration of its agonist D-Tyr MTII (D-Tyr), via osmotic pump installation for 28 days, reduces Aβ level and its deposition in APP/PS1 transgenic mice. In parallel, D-Tyr restored the otherwise deficit synaptic plasticity in the hippocampus of these mice, as indicated by improved LTP (long-term potentiation). Significantly, overexpressing the MCR agonist produced by POMC in the hippocampus also led to substantial reduction in Aβ accumulation, a hallmark of AD pathology. Further, MCR activation reduces global neuroinflammation, particularly in the hippocampus, reverting the elevated transcription of major inflammatory factors Il1β, Il6, Icam1, and the glial markers Aif1 and Gfap. In addition, MCR stimulation alleviates astrocytic activation especially in the hippocampus. Intriguingly, MCR activation in APP/PS1 mice led to the drastic reduction of the neurotoxic A1 subtype of reactive astrocytes, which is the major astrocytic subtype that mediates astrocytic toxicity in AD. Concordant with the understanding that A1 neurotoxic astrocytes are induced by classically activated neuroinflammatory microglia, MCR activation is demonstrated to reduce the activation of microglia but enhances their recruitment to amyloid plaques. As amyloid plaque deposition is determined by the process of Aβ synthesis and clearance, and microglia have well-established roles in facilitating amyloid clearance, it is worthwhile to further examine the enhanced engagement between the microglia and amyloid plaques. Collectively, our findings support the beneficial actions of MCR activation and their molecular basis in AD pathogenesis. As delineated above, MCR activation has been demonstrated to exert multiple beneficial effects in the hippocampus of APP/PS1 mice, including the rescue of synaptic plasticity impairment, the reduction of Aβ accumulation, and restoration of glial cell homeostasis. In order to examine the molecular basis for the observed alterations induced by promoted hippocampal melanocortin signaling, we performed transcriptome analysis on hippocampal slices from APP/PS1 mice directly subjected to D-Tyr treatment for MCR activation. We demonstrated that D-Tyr administration led to the significant differential expression of 339 genes in the hippocampal slices, among which 141 were upregulated while 198 downregulated. Intriguingly, such D-Tyr–directed transcriptomic regulations in APP/PS1 mice showed distinctive negative correlation with the transcriptomic changes in APP/PS1 mice relative to WT controls. In other words, the differentially expressed genes identified showed resembling expression levels and pattern between the D-Tyr-treated APP/PS1 mice and the untreated WT mice. These results suggest that the D-Tyr-induced regulation of molecular phenotypes in the hippocampus partially restored the transcriptomic signature of APP/PS1 mice to that of the WT mice. Further validation of the reverted expression levels was attained using quantitative RT-PCR for specific genes, including Itgam and Aif1, which are associated with microglial activation. Substantially, the significant upregulation of these transcripts in the hippocampal slices from APP/PS1 mice was abolished upon D-Tyr treatment. Accordingly, we also verified that D-Tyr administration mitigated the perturbed transcriptional changes in the pro-inflammatory cytokine Il6 and the astrocyte marker Gfap in APP/PS1 mice. In light of the functional implications offered by D-Tyr-induced restoration of the transcriptomic signatures in APP/PS1 mice, we performed pathway analysis to decipher the molecular pathways involved in MCR actions. Annotation of the differentially expressed genes identified using both Gene Ontology and protein–protein interaction analyses demonstrated that the D-Tyr-upregulated genes were primarily associated with homeostatic processes and responses to heat, unfolded protein, TGF-β (transforming growth factor-beta), topologically incorrect proteins, and stress. Meanwhile, the D-Tyr-downregulated genes were associated with the regulation of metabolic processes, protein modification processes, macromolecule localization, histone modification, rRNA processing, cellular respiration, and microglial activation. On that account, the diverse molecular events directed and promoted by the enhanced melanocortin signaling may provide insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying the observed shifts in glial reactivity and restoration of hippocampal homeostasis. In sum, activation of the melanocortin system exerts beneficial effect on multiple functional aspects in AD condition and offers a potential target for therapeutic interventions in AD.

16102717.label: Major findings and research outcome
16102717.value: Based on our previous work which showed the implication of MCRs, particularly MC4R, in the homeostatic process modulating synaptic functions, we set out to investigate the potential benefits of MCR activation in AD pathology in this study. In APP/PS1 transgenic mice, we demonstrate that MCR activation mediated by the central administration of its agonist D-Tyr MTII substantially reduces Aβ accumulation in both the hippocampus and cortex of the brain, while alleviating global inflammation and astrocytic activation in a brain region-specific manner, particularly prominent in the hippocampus. MCR activation prominently reduces the A1 subtype of reactive astrocytes, which is considered a key source of astrocytic neurotoxicity in AD. Concordantly, MCR activation suppresses microglial activation, while enhancing their association with amyloid plaques. The blunted activation of microglia may contribute to the reduction in the neurotoxic phenotypes of astrocytes. Importantly, transcriptome analysis reveals the downregulated expression of genes involved in microglial activation in D-Tyr–treated hippocampal slices, indicating that MCR activation restores the impaired homeostatic processes and microglial reactivity in the hippocampus in APP/PS1 mice. These findings suggest that microglia are one of the major cell targets that mediate how melanocortin/MCR signaling alleviates the pathological features of AD. Collectively, our findings demonstrate the potential of MCR signaling as therapeutic target for AD. Considering that current therapeutic approaches for AD merely provide symptomatic relief, there is an urgent need for new curative treatments targeting disease modification. The restoration of hippocampal synaptic plasticity, which forms the basis of learning and memory, is a possible target for therapeutic intervention. Meanwhile, replenishment of POMC/MC4R signaling has been demonstrated to rescue synaptic plasticity impairment. In addition to neuronal functions, we showed in this study that melanocortin/MCR replenishment alleviates the activation of microglia and astrocytes, thereby restoring cellular homeostasis, rendering MCRs and their agonists attractive targets for AD therapeutic development. In sum, activation of the melanocortin system exerts beneficial effect on multiple functional aspects in AD condition and offers a potential target for therapeutic interventions in AD. The efforts of a few undergraduate students conduced to the findings generated in this work. Mr. Han CAO provided technical assistance in the preparation of drugs and central administration procedures. Mr. YIP Man Shun offered kind help in the identification and quantification of amyloid plaque. Miss LIU Sze Kei assisted in the quantification and analysis of microglia and astrocytes. Lastly, Miss YIP Fung Ting, Carina engaged in the transcriptomic analysis of the effects of D-Tyr treatment in acute hippocampal slices. Their excellent assistance was pivotal to the fruition of this project.

16102717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16102717.value: In this study, we showed that melanocortin signaling involving MCRs plays an important role in the hippocampus in AD, where it modulates and restores synaptic plasticity as well as alleviates AD pathologies in AD transgenic mouse models. To further explore the therapeutic potentials of the MCR system in AD, it is crucial to characterize the spatiotemporal expression profile of MCRs in AD progression. Among different MCRs, while MC3R is predominantly expressed in the hypothalamus, MC4R is widely distributed throughout the brain, with prominent expression across the hypothalamus and hippocampus formation. In addition to neurons, MC4R expression is identified in microglia and astrocytes. Cell-type-specific knockout of MCR(s) in AD mouse models may facilitate the dissection of the cellular mechanisms underlying the beneficial action of the melanocortin system. As such, further work that expands our understanding of the cellular and molecular basis of α-MSH/MCR signaling in the hippocampus will be invaluable for exploring their therapeutic potential as a treatment paradigm for AD.

16102717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16102717.value: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a devastating neurodegenerative disease and the most common cause of dementia, characterized by the deterioration of memory and cognitive functions, neuroinflammation, and the accumulation of harmful species in the brain, such as β–amyloid (Aβ). These maladies together lead to dysfunctions in neurons and the resident brain immune cells termed glia, including microglia and astrocytes. There are no effective intervention strategies against AD to date, while existing drugs for the disease can only provide transient effects on symptom alleviation. In this study, we showed that AD pathologies can be alleviated through the activation of melanocortin signaling, which is a diverse biological system involving a family of melanocortin receptors (MCRs). Significantly, activation of the MCRs in the brain ameliorates Aβ deposition and glial activation, hallmarks of AD pathology, in an AD transgenic mouse model. Also, we showed that administration of the MCR agonist, D-Tyr, reduces amyloid burden in both the hippocampus and cortex of the brain, while decreasing global neuroinflammation and activation of astrocytes and microglia. Further transcriptome analysis also revealed the downregulation of genes involved in microglial activation in D-Tyr–treated hippocampal slices. Our findings suggest the potential of MCR signaling as therapeutic target for AD.

16102817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16102817.value: In the past 20 years, epigenetic modifications have taken center stage when studying gene regulation. These chemical changes on DNA or its associated histone proteins regulate the activity of DNA sequences without altering the underlying genetic code. The amalgamation of these and other marks across the genome forms the epigenome. The interdependence of various epigenetic marks is an intriguing aspect in deciphering the complexity of the epigenome and in turn general transcriptional regulation. Aside from the epigenome, recent studies have found that 3-dimensional (3D) organization of the genome within the nucleus plays an important role in regulating transcription. Chromatin is segmented into spatial domains where interactions are frequent. The nuclear localization of a given sequence can influence the activity. Moreover, genetic mutations that affect the 3D interaction of DNA sequences were shown to lead to human diseases. Incorporating the spatial organization of DNA is rapidly becoming a crucial factor in studying transcriptional regulation. However, the role of the epigenome on nuclear architecture remains unclear. In this study, we aim to elucidate the role of a histone modifying enzyme, G9a, on the epigenome and the 3D organization of the nucleus. We will first delineate the molecular mechanism behind epigenomic changes that occur in mouse embryonic stem cells depleted of G9a. The proposed experiments clarify the interdependent nature of two distinct epigenetic modifications. Furthermore, we aim to study the 3D chromatin conformational changes that occur in G9a depleted cells. Employing an integrative approach, we aim to understand how the epigenome affects the spatial organization of the nucleus. Taken together, the results of this study have implications in both furthering the fundamental understanding of transcriptional control and also molecular changes that occur in a range of diseases. 過去二十年，表觀遺傳修飾成為研究基因調控的關鍵領域。表觀遺傳修飾是在DNA或相關組織蛋白質上所作的微細化學修飾, 不會改變原有DNA序列，但能夠調控基因的轉錄狀態。多款不同的表觀遺傳修飾形成表觀基因組。拆解表觀基因組和一般轉錄的調節機制時，表觀遺傳標記的相互依賴性，尤其引人入勝。 除表觀基因組之外，最近研究發現細胞核內基因組的三維（3D）組織在調節轉錄中起著重要的作用。染色質佔用核內特定空間領域，並且互動頻繁。特定序列的核定位能影響該序列的活動。研究亦曾顯示，影響三維空間互動的基因突變，會為人類帶來疾病。故此，鑽研基因轉錄調控時，DNA的空間組織便更為重要。然而，表觀基因組在核結構上的作用仍未有定論。 這項研究的目標，是要闡明組蛋白修飾酶G9a對表觀基因組和細胞核內3D組織的作用。首先，老鼠胚胎幹細胞在剔除G9a後，將導致表觀基因組變化。我們將把這個分子機制加以描繪。兩種不同的表觀遺傳修飾之間所表現的連結，將得到詳細表述。此外，我們也將探討細胞核內3D染色質構像，在剔除G9a後所產生的變化。整合各方資料，我們希望了解表觀基因組如何影響細胞核內的空間組織。綜上所述，本研究將拓展我們對轉錄調控機制的根本認識，以及疾病中所見的分子變化。

16102817.label: Realisation of objectives
16102817.value: Objective 1: Characterizing epigenomic changes in G9a-depleted mouse ES cells The role of G9a in embryonic development has been long established. This histone methyltransferase is known to deposit histone 3 lysine 9 mono- and di-methylation (H3K9me2) to mediate transcriptional repression. Previous studies have also suggested that DNA methylation is also dependent on the activities of G9a. However, the molecular mechanism remains unclear. Therefore, to elucidate how G9a regulates DNA methylation maintenance, we investigated the epigenomic changes in mouse embryonic stem cell (mESC) lines that are depleted of G9a or harbor a catalytically inactive version of the enzyme. Consistent with previous reports, we found that G9a mutant mESCs show a global loss of DNA methylation. This dramatic effect on the epigenome was not restricted to specific genomic features and not related to H3K9me2 inhibition of DNA demethylating enzymes. Intriguingly, we discovered that while the catalytic activity of G9a is required for the maintaining DNA methylation, it is not dependent on H3K9me2. Our data shows that G9a methylated the Lig1 protein, which is a key co-factor for DNA methyltransferase 1 (Dnmt1) to carry out its function. Taken together, our results revealed a novel mechanism by which G9a regulates the epigenome in mESCs. These findings were published in the journal Cell Reports. Objective 2: Delineating the molecular function of H3K9 di-methylation To delineate the molecular functions of H3K9me2 in mESCs, we conducted a variety of different epigenomic assays including ChIP-seq, RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, and Hi-C in G9a mutant mESC lines. Our integrative analyses uncovered several previously unknown functions of G9a and H3K9me2. Firstly, we found that G9a functions in both catalytically dependent and independent manners to transcriptionally silence retrotransposon elements. A proportion of these de-repressed elements generate chimeric transcripts with near by protein coding genes, which can alter their coding potentials. Furthermore, G9a form distinct complexes with other epigenetic modifying proteins to silence putative cis-regulatory elements by maintaining chromatin compaction. Finally, we discovered that G9a prevents aberrant CTCF and cohesin binding at particular retrotransposons. This role is important to maintain chromatin loops and topologically associated domain boundaries. Taken together, our study discovered several important and unappreciated functions of G9a and H3K9me2. These findings were published in the journal Cell Reports and has led to a follow up study, which is currently under review.

16102817.label: Major findings and research outcome
16102817.value: In objective 1, we aimed to study how G9a regulates the epigenome of mESCs. We generated the first truly CpG resolution, genome-wide whole genome bisulfite sequencing datasets of G9a knockout, G9a/GLP double knockout, and G9a catalytic mutant mESCs. We found that upon G9a deletion, mESCs lose DNA methylation on a global level. This DNA hypomethylation occurs across the whole genome and is not restricted to any genomic features. Interestingly, this change is dependent of G9a’s catalytic activity but not its histone methyltransferase activity. We found much of the hypomethylation occurs outside of regions marked by H3K9me2. This is likely because G9a has non-histone protein targets, such as Lig1, which functions to maintain DNA methylation. For objective 2, we focused on understanding the function of G9a and H3K9me2. We carried out integrative analysis of multi-modal epigenomic assays. We conducted ChIP-seq, RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, and Hi-C experiments, which measure different aspects of the epigenome. We found a variety of chromatin state changes, both associated with and independent of G9a’s catalytic activity. These loci are co-enriched with distinct chromatin modifiers and are putative cis-regulatory elements. We also observed that in mESCs that lack either G9a or H3K9me2, subsets of retrotransposons are de-repressed and generates chimeric transcript with neighboring genes. These elements affect function of the gene by altering its open reading frames. It should be noted that analysis of retrotransposons in next generation sequencing data typically suffers from poor mappability. As these elements exist in many identical copies in the genome, they contribute to the majority of multiple alignment reads. To circumvent this problem, we developed a custom iterative mapping pipeline to “rescue” multi-aligned reads about retrotransposon subfamilies. This pipeline has proven useful in other independent studies. Finally, we found that global chromatin conformation, on the level of topologically associated domains and compartment A/B, is unaffected in the absence of G9a. This is surprising as G9a deposits H3K9me2 across 40% of the genome. However, TAD and compartment definitions remain constant in the various mutant lines we investigated. Intriguingly, we found that G9a/H3K9me2 in wildtype mESCs function to block CTCF and cohesin binding at particular sites. As a result, G9a mutant cells gain 3D chromatin interactions that are associated with weakening of TAD boundaries. All the above findings were published in a manuscript in the journal Cell Reports and have been presented at multiple international meetings.

16102817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16102817.value: We demonstrated how G9a regulates the epigenome, transcriptome, and 3D chromatin structures in mESCs. In this study, we discovered that ground-state pluripotency genes were upregulated in G9a mutant mESCs. The dysregulation of these genes is associated with the formation of a novel super-enhancer element, which arose from disruption of existing chromatin structures. This result may in part explain the reason that G9a mutant mESCs are unable to effectively exit pluripotency even upon experimental induction of differentiation. In a follow-up study, we are applying genome engineering to investigate this role of G9a. Secondly, given that G9a is co-enriched with Setdb1, another histone methyltransferase, we asked if Setdb1 has similar functions in maintaining 3D chromatin structures. Our analysis revealed that Setdb1 functions independently of G9a to regulate chromatin loops. Similar to G9a, Setdb1 deposits H3K9me3 to block CTCF binding. However, these sites are distinct to those defined in G9a mutants. A manuscript describing this work is currently under review. Finally, the bioinformatic pipeline for analyzing retrotransposons has been of interest to many researchers in the field and have led to several collaborations. We have applied this pipeline in other studies, including one which was recently published in Journal of Neuroscience.

16102817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16102817.value: Epigenetic modifications have recently taken center stage when studying gene regulation. These chemical changes on DNA or its associated histone proteins regulate the activity of DNA sequences without altering the underlying genetic code. Together, these and other marks across the genome forms the epigenome. The interdependence of various epigenetic marks is an important aspect in deciphering the epigenome and general transcriptional regulation. In addition, recent studies have found that 3-dimensional (3D) organization of the genome within the nucleus plays an important role in transcriptional control. Chromatin is segmented into spatial domains where interactions are frequent. The nuclear localization of a given sequence can influence the activity. Moreover, genetic mutations that affect the 3D interaction of DNA sequences were shown to lead to human diseases. Incorporating the spatial organization of DNA is rapidly becoming a crucial factor in studying transcriptional regulation. However, the role of the epigenome on nuclear architecture remains unclear. In this study, we employed state-of-the-art approaches to elucidate the impact of a histone modifying enzyme, G9a, on the epigenome and the 3D nuclear organization. We discovered that G9a functions in distinct ways to regulate the “openness” of chromatin segments, which in turn influences gene expression and spatial interactions.

16103017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16103017.value: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a form of dementia characterized by memory loss and other cognitive impairments. There is currently no effective treatment or cure. Emerging evidence shows that neuroinflammation is a major factor in AD pathogenesis along with the deposition of amyloid-beta (Aβ) peptides and the formation of neurofibrillary tangles. During AD progression, Aβ deposition alters brain homeostasis, leading to the activation of the innate immune system. Our previous finding demonstrated that interleukin (IL)-33 signaling is impaired in patients with mild cognitive impairment; these individuals have an increased risk of developing AD. In transgenic mouse model that exhibits AD pathologies, IL-33 administration rescues synaptic plasticity impairment and reduces Aβ levels through microglial activation. To unravel IL-33–mediated mechanisms in the pathogenesis of AD, we conducted a transcriptome analysis of IL-33–treated APP/PS1 mice. While the transcript levels of several immune-related genes were increased in APP/PS1 mouse brains, IL-33 administration abolished this aberrant increase, in particular osteopontin (OPN). Nonetheless, the role of this cytokine in AD pathology and its involvement in IL-33 signaling are unclear. In the proposed study, we will examine the regulation of OPN expression in AD transgenic mouse brains and the regulation of OPN signaling by IL-33. Furthermore, we will examine the role of OPN in AD progression and the underlying mechanisms. First, we will examine the changes of the expression level of OPN transcripts and proteins in brains of different AD transgenic model mice. We will then determine which neural cell types specifically express OPN. Our preliminary data suggest that OPN is significantly elevated in microglia in APP/PS1 mouse brains. Therefore, we will study the role of induced OPN expression in AD progression, in particular, its effects on synaptic dysfunctions and Aβ pathology. Finally, we will explore the molecular pathways underlying the action of OPN in AD. We will examine the transcriptome signature of the OPN+ (OPN-expressing) and OPN− microglia in APP/PS1 mouse brains. The findings of the proposed study will advance our understanding of the role of OPN in AD pathogenesis and the molecular basis of OPN signaling, providing insights in the development of new AD therapies targeting specific inflammatory pathways.

16103017.label: Realisation of objectives
16103017.value: We have fully achieved our project objectives. Below is a summary of our key findings. Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a major type of dementia and is highly prevalent among aged people. Patients with AD experience progressive atrophy of cortical and subcortical structures, memory loss, and cognitive impairment. Because its precise pathophysiological mechanisms remain unclear, AD has no effective treatment. The hallmarks of AD are amyloid plaque deposits, neurofibrillary tangles, and neuroinflammation. Current research is focused on identifying AD biomarkers and/or mechanisms that underlie AD progression. Accordingly, osteopontin (OPN) is an inflammatory cytokine that is upregulated in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) in AD patients. Furthermore, OPN levels in the CSF and plasma of newly diagnosed AD patients are higher than those in chronic AD patients, suggesting that OPN might play a role in early AD progression. Our laboratory has demonstrated that interleukin-33 (IL-33) administration alleviates AD-associated synaptic defects and cognitive dysfunctions in APP/PS1 mice, an AD transgenic mouse model. Transcriptome analysis of the APP/PS1 mouse brain revealed that IL-33 administration abolishes the aberrant increase in OPN transcript level (Spp1). Nevertheless, the role of OPN in AD pathology has not been thoroughly investigated. Therefore, to better understand how the immune responses of neural cells contribute to AD pathogenesis, we are investigating the roles of OPN in AD pathology. In this project, we first examined the spatiotemporal regulation of OPN in the cerebrum in young adult APP/PS1 mice (4 months old; the age stage at which amyloid deposition has not yet developed and synaptic functions are normal) and middle-aged APP/PS1 mice (12–13 months old; the age stage at which amyloid pathology, synaptic dysfunction, and cognitive impairment are severe). We observed that Spp1 transcript expression was relatively stable in both age stages in the cerebral cortices of wild-type (WT) mice. There was no significant change of the Spp1 transcript in the cerebral cortices of 4-month-old APP/PS1 mice when compared with age-matched WT mice. At 12 months, the Spp1 transcript level increased significantly (by 3-fold) in 12-month-old APP/PS1 mice as compared with age-matched WT mice. Consistently, ELISA revealed that the OPN protein level was three times greater in the cerebral cortices of 13-month-old APP/PS1 mice than in age-matched WT mice. We further characterized the cellular expression of OPN in 12-month-old mouse brains by immunohistochemical analysis. In both WT and APP/PS1 mice, OPN was constantly expressed in GABAergic neurons from the thalamic reticular nucleus and was occasionally detected in the cerebral cortex. We did not observe OPN in other neural cells in the cerebral cortex in WT mice, whereas OPN was expressed in a subpopulation of microglia in the cerebral cortex in APP/PS1 mice. Notably, most OPN+ microglia were associated with amyloid plaques. Detailed morphological analysis showed that compared to OPN− microglia, OPN+ microglia near amyloid plaques had a significantly larger soma area and a higher activation index. Consistently, OPN+ microglia exhibited higher phagocytic capacity compared with OPN− microglia near amyloid plaques, as demonstrated by the upregulation of CD68, a phagocytic marker, in OPN+ microglia. These results suggest that OPN+ microglia play a pathological role in AD progression (Chuang el al., in preparation). The functions of microglia can be elucidated based on their transcriptome signature. To examine the roles of OPN+ microglia in AD, we performed single nuclei transcriptome analysis in the forebrains of APP/PS1 mice. We identiﬁed microglia clusters, including homeostatic microglia and diseased-associated microglia (DAM) subtypes, based on transcriptome signatures by unsupervised clustering of 15,041 microglia (CD11b+ cells) using the t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE) algorithm. We found that the Spp1 transcript was enriched in DAMs known to be amyloid-beta (Aβ)-plaque-associated for barrier formation or phagocytosis (Lau et al., 2020a). To further examine the role of OPN in AD pathology, we intracerebroventricularly injected IL-33 into the brains of APP/PS1 mice. We collected the forebrains 2 days later and then performed single nuclei transcriptome analysis. IL-33 mediated the transcriptome reprogramming in a speciﬁc subpopulation of DAM, which we termed “IL-33RMs.” This IL-33RM subpopulation maintained the expression of DAM signature genes including Spp1, while restoring the expression of homeostatic signature genes such as the Cap1, Fcrls, and Sft2d1 genes. Further characterization showed that enriched genes in IL-33RMs are associated with angiogenesis (e.g., Vegfa), antigen presentation (e.g., H2-Aa and H2-Eb1), and endocytosis (e.g., Axl and Ctse), highlighting their roles in phagocytic response. We performed a Search Tool for the Retrieval of Interacting Genes/Proteins (STRING) analysis of the genes enriched in IL-33RMs, including Spp1, Axl, C3, Ciita, H2-Ab1, Ptgs2, and Vefga, which further revealed that these genes belong to an interconnected gene network that co-regulates pathways in chemotaxis, cell motility, and endocytosis regulation as determined by Gene Ontology (GO) analysis. These highlighted pathways further support the notion that IL-33RMs adopt phenotypes characterized by enhanced chemotaxis and phagocytosis (Lau et al., 2020a). Immunohistochemical analysis confirmed that, while only a few IL-33RMs were found in the cerebral cortex in APP/PS1 mice, IL-33 injection signiﬁcantly increased (by 10%) the proportion of IL-33RMs in the cerebral cortex in APP/PS1 mice. Most of the IL-33RMs were associated with Aβ plaques in the cerebral cortex. To determine whether IL-33RMs mediate Aβ phagocytosis in APP/PS1 mice, we examined their Aβ uptake in vivo by injecting mice with methoxy-X04 (MeX04; a brain-penetrant Aβ dye) followed by ﬂow cytometry. In naive APP/PS1 mice, the IL-33RMs only accounted for ~15% of Aβ phagocytic microglia (i.e., MeX04+ CD11b+ cells), whereas IL-33 injection increased the proportion to ~60%. Furthermore, in IL-33-injected APP/PS1 mice, the IL-33RMs exhibited increased Aβ phagocytic capacity as indicated by a higher mean ﬂuorescence intensity of MeX04 than that in IL-33RMs. In addition, IL-33RMs had higher CD68+ lysosomal content than MHC-II-microglia in both IL-33-injected and naive APP/PS1 mice as shown by immunohistochemical analysis. These ﬁndings demonstrate that IL-33RMs possess a higher Aβ phagocytic capacity than that of the other microglial subpopulations. Given that IL-33RMs is enriched with the Spp1 transcript, and OPN+ microglia have a higher content of CD68, OPN may play a role in regulating microglial phagocytic capacity. (Lau et al., 2020a). Beside exhibiting functional roles in its expressing cells, OPN is also a secreted cytokine that exerts inflammatory responses. As OPN is also increased in the CSF and plasma of newly diagnosed AD patients, it may play a role in mediating neuroinflammation in AD progression. To further understand the pathological roles of OPN in AD progression, we further characterized which neural cell types OPN may act on to initiate the inflammatory response. We also examined the cellular expression of its receptor, CD44, in the cerebrums of APP/PS1 mice by immunohistochemical analysis. We did not detect CD44 in the cerebrums of 12-month-old WT mice. However, CD44 was significantly induced in the astrocytes located in the cerebral cortices of age-matched APP/PS1 mice. Our previous study demonstrated that intraperitoneal injection of IL-33 for 2 consecutive days decreased the Spp1 transcript level in the cerebral cortices of 12-month-old APP/PS1 mice compared with age-matched untreated mice. We also found that IL-33 downregulates the Cd44 mRNA level. In AD, the crosstalk between microglia and astrocytes plays a critical role in mediating neuroinflammation and amyloid pathology. Thus, the OPN/CD44 signaling pathway present in the microglia–astrocytes axis suggests this signaling pathway is involved in mediating the pathogenesis of AD (Chuang el al., in preparation).

16103017.label: Major findings and research outcome
16103017.value: This study aimed to characterize the spatiotemporal regulation of OPN expression in the brains of AD transgenic model mice at different ages and explore the role of OPN in AD pathogenesis. Our major findings and research outcomes are as follows: • The transcript (Spp1) and protein of OPN expression are induced in the brains of AD model mice, and OPN-expressed microglia are associated with amyloid pathology: Real-time PCR analysis and ELISA demonstrated that the mRNA and protein of OPN are significantly increased in the brains of middle-aged APP/PS1 mice, the age stage in which amyloid pathology and cognitive impairment are severe. Immunohistochemical analysis showed that OPN was induced in a microglial subpopulation associated with amyloid plaques in the cerebral cortex in APP/PS1 mice. Single nuclei transcriptome analysis of the forebrain in APP/PS1 mice further demonstrated that the Spp1 transcript was enriched in diseased-associated microglia (DAM) subtypes (Chuang et al., in preparation; Lau et al., 2020). • IL-33 transcriptionally reprograms a subpopulation of DAMs known as IL-33RMs with enriched Spp1 expression: To understand how OPN signaling is involved in AD pathogenesis, we performed a transcriptome analysis of IL-33-treated brains of APP/PS1 mice. IL-33 administration into these mice mediated the transcriptome reprogramming in a speciﬁc subpopulation of DAM (IL-33RMs). We found that IL-33RMs were enriched with the Spp1 transcript. Gene Ontology (GO) analysis of IL-33RM transcriptomes suggests this microglial subtype is involved in chemotaxis, cell motility, and endocytosis regulation. Immunohistochemical analysis showed that IL-33RMs localize around amyloid plaques (Lau et al., 2020), demonstrating that OPN-expressed microglia play a critical role in regulating amyloid pathology. • OPN-expressed IL-33RMs have enhanced Aβ phagocytic activity: IL-33-treated APP/PS1 mice exhibit reduced severity of amyloid plaques. Collectively, in vivo imaging, immunohistochemical analysis, and flow cytometry analyses of IL-33-treated APP/PS1 mice revealed that microglia have enhanced chemotactic activity and Aβ phagocytic activity. This finding suggests that OPN-expressed microglia impact amyloid pathology via modulating the functional state of microglia in chemotaxis and phagocytosis (Chuang et al., in preparation; Lau et al., 2020). • Determination of the OPN/CD44 signaling axis between microglia and astrocytes in APP/PS1 mice: To understand how OPN signaling is involved in AD pathogenesis, we characterized the cellular expression of OPN receptors in APP/PS1 mouse brains. We found a very low signal of CD44 in WT mice but observed a significant increased expression of CD44 in activated astrocytes in the brains of APP/PS1 mice. These findings suggest that the OPN/CD44 signaling axis present between microglia and astrocytes mediates neuroinflammation (Chuang et al., in preparation). • The efforts of a few undergraduate students conduced to the findings generated in this work. Miss LIU Sze Kei offered kind help in performing ELISA assay for determining OPN level in mouse brains. Mr. YIP Man Shun assisted in the immunohistochemical staining and imaging of OPN-expressed microglia and amyloid plaques in brain sections of APP/PS1 mice. Lastly, Miss YIP Fung Ting, Carina engaged in the transcriptomic analysis of in cerebral microglia of APP/PS1 mice. Their excellent assistance was pivotal to the fruition of this project.

16103017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16103017.value: Our current findings demonstrate that OPN-expressed microglia are associated with amyloid pathology in AD. We found that OPN transcript and proteins are induced in a subpopulation of an AD-microglia subtype known as DAM. Moreover, these OPN-expressed microglia show enhanced chemotactic and Aβ phagocytic activity in response to IL-33 stimulation. Thus, OPN-expressed microglia may play critical roles in ameliorating amyloid pathology in AD and may be a potential target for AD therapeutic development. Therefore, further studies are required to determine the regulatory mechanisms of OPN expression in this microglial subpopulation. To delineate how the Spp1 transcript is regulated in the DAM subtype in AD, the epigenetic signature of OPN+ and OPN− microglia in APP/PS1 mice can be determined by performing ATAC-seq (assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing). Moreover, we identified an OPN/CD44 signaling axis between microglia and astrocytes in the brains of APP/PS1 mice. Given that astrocytes are the key contributors for generating inflammatory factors in the brain, it is critical to determine how this signaling axis contributes to the mediation of neuroinflammation in AD progression. To achieve this, CD44 expression can be specifically knocked down in astrocytes in the brains of APP/PS1 mice, followed by the characterization of how blocking OPN-downstream signaling in astrocytes modulates the expression of inflammatory factors in the brain and contributes to the various pathological changes in AD. Taken together, our current findings can help expand our knowledge about the mechanistic roles of OPN signaling in AD, making OPN a potential target for AD therapeutic development.

16103017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16103017.value: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is the most prevalent form of aged-related dementia. Its multifactorial nature and unclear pathological mechanisms are the 2 main reasons of why an effective treatment for AD has not been developed. Meanwhile, osteopontin (OPN) is a multifunctional cytokine as well as an adhesion molecule that is critical for mediating both innate and adaptive immune responses in the peripheral nervous system. Multiple studies show that OPN expression is deregulated in the brains of AD patients. However, it is unclear what neural cell types express OPN in AD and how OPN contributes to AD development. Herein, we demonstrate that OPN is induced in a subpopulation of AD-microglia and that the localization of OPN-expressed microglia is associated with amyloid-beta (Aβ) pathology, a key characteristic of AD. Further analysis shows that in AD model mice, OPN-expressed microglia are involved in modulating Aβ pathology by altering their Aβ-clearance activity in response to IL-33 stimulation. Taken together, our findings support that OPN signaling is one of the major mechanisms underlying the functional transition of AD-microglia and provide insights on manipulating AD-microglia as a potential treatment target for AD.

16103317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16103317.value: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is the most common type of late-onset neurodegenerative disease. After the failure of dozens of clinical trials, the field has begun to accept the fact that AD is a more complex disease than can be explained solely by the deposition of β-amyloid or hyperphosphoyrlated tau. This has increased the need to identify new pathways for therapeutic intervention. Wnt signaling is crucial for normal brain functioning and impaired signaling is associated with late onset AD. Currently, the majority of studies on Wnt signaling are focused on nerve cells with much less known about its potential roles in non-neuronal cells such as astrocytes. We have been drawn to the astrocyte population both because they offer primary metabolic support to neurons and because they are subjected to the same AD microenvironment during disease progression. As Wnt signaling regulates cellular fuel metabolism, and perturbed cerebral glucose metabolism is an invariant pathological feature of AD, we hypothesize that Wnt normally regulates fuel metabolism in astrocytes and failure of this support function contributes heavily to the symptoms of AD. Our preliminary findings suggest that the Wnt/Lrp5/mTor/Akt axis, but not the canonical β-catenin-dependent axis, is the primary Wnt pathway in astrocytic glucose metabolism. We also found that the Wnt antagonist Dkk1, which is upregulated in AD brains, switches Wnt signaling from the mTor/Akt axis to the Ca2+/PCP/Nfat and Jnk/Ap1 axes. This initiates a pro-inflammatory reprogramming of astrocytes. Our first goal is to evaluate the metabolic kinetics and immunocytokine profiles of astrocytes in the presence or absence of Wnt-Lrp5 signaling, and to perform in-depth analyses on the downstream pathways in charge of programming the immuno-metabolomic features of astrocytes. In vivo, we will investigate how Dkk1 modulates Wnt signaling and monitor the corresponding changes in the properties of astrocytes with mouse models of AD. Finally, we will evaluate the therapeutic potential of various antibodies of Dkk1 or other small molecule inhibitors to rescue Wnt-Lrp5 signaling and function of astrocytes. Our long term goal will be to develop these interventions as potential therapeutics to fight against AD. 在種種晚年期病發的神經退化疾病中，阿爾茨海默氏症是最常見一種。在經歷過多次大型臨床試驗失敗後，有關研究人員及專家開始認同此病症的病理成因比傳統所認為的β類澱粉和過度磷酸化Tau蛋白沉積理論更為複雜。因此，我們認為從新的角度找出此病症的分子病理機制對藥物及治療的研發極為重要。 Wnt訊息傳遞路徑有助維持大腦的正常功能，而不少研究已指出有關信號的減弱和變異對促進阿爾茨海默氏症的形成有著密切的關係。直到目前為止，大部份有關Wnt訊息傳遞路徑的研究都集中在神經元上；至於有關訊息對大腦其他種類細胞的影響，如星形膠質細胞，則未曾作出深入的研究。我們的研究團隊對星形膠質細胞極感興趣，是由於星形膠質細胞的主要功能是給神經元提供各樣燃料代謝產物；同時，星形膠質細胞是大腦裡數量最多的細胞，他們亦會跟神經元一樣，在發病的大腦裡受其微觀環境因素的影響。 由於Wnt訊息傳遞路徑可調控細胞的燃料代謝作用，加上有報告曾指出大腦的葡萄糖代謝功能失效是阿爾茨海默氏症的恆常病理特徵。因此，我們推測正常的Wnt訊息傳遞路徑有助調控星形膠質細胞對神經元提供燃料代謝物的功能，而這功能的缺失則會引發出阿爾茨海默氏症的相關症狀。我們從初步研究數據中找出調控星形膠質細胞葡萄糖代謝支援作用的Wnt訊息傳遞的路徑是Wnt/Lrp5/mTor/Akt，而不是典型Wnt/Beta-catenin傳遞路徑 。我們也發現Wnt訊息傳遞路徑拮抗劑Dkk1的表達量不但在阿爾茨海默氏症的大腦裡有所提升，而且它把星形膠質細胞Wnt訊息傳遞的路徑從mTor/Akt改變成Ca2+/PCP/Nfat 和Jnk/Ap1。繼而，這種下游訊息的切換則啟動了星形膠質細胞的活化和炎症反應。 在計劃書中，我們有三個研究目標：第一是評估Wnt/Lrp5通路對星形膠質細胞燃料代謝動力學和炎症分泌物質譜的影響，及深入研究主導這兩大作用的下游分子通路。第二是，我們會利用跟阿爾茨海默氏症相關的小鼠模型進行以上的分析，以肯定有關現像和疾病的關聯性。最後，我們會評估那些針對Dkk1的中和性抗體和小分子抑製劑能否調整病態星形膠質細胞的功能。長遠來說，我們希望這研究能為阿爾茨海默氏症的分子病理及治療研發帶入新的元素。

16103317.label: Realisation of objectives
16103317.value: Overview: The major finding of this project is accepted in Advanced Science [IF=15.84] where the PI serves as the first and sole corresponding author of the paper. Two of her PhD students, Miss Jacquelyne Ka-Li Sun and Mr. Tsun-Ming Lau are serving as co-authors on the paper. All objectives of the proposal have been achieved. In the following description, key findings will be described. For further details, please refer to the manuscript in the attachment (Part C). Reminder on deviations approved in the previous report: In the previous report, we raised out that LRP6, instead of LRP5, are more abundantly expressed in astrocytes. This deviation is accepted by the panel. Therefore, all descriptions below are based on LRP6 findings in astrocytes. Findings related to objective 1 1. LRP6 controls the metabolic landscape in astrocytes Hinted from the existing associations present between LRP6 mutations and a spectrum of metabolic disorders, we revealed that LRP6-mediated Wnt signalling modulates the metabolic landscape of these cells. With the LRP6-/- astrocytes harvested from astrocyte-specific conditional knockout mice, global metabolite profiling and qPCR mini-array on all KEGG metabolic genes analyses revealed that LRP6 loss resulted in fuel metabolism re-programming in astrocytes, causing a shifting of fuel dependence from glucose (i.e. glycolysis) towards amino acids, in particular glutamine (Q) and branched chain amino acids (BCAAs). 2. LRP6-dependent and independent Wnt downstream signalling axes regulate the bimodal switch of metabolic network in astrocytes With multiple assays, including high-throughput ELISA-based antibody assays and other validation assays including immunofluorescence analyses and Western blotting analyses, these investigations revealed that the PI3K-AKT-mTORC1 axis is the dominant downstream signalling pathway of LRP6-mediated signalling, and this signalling axis governs the glycolytic capacities. LRP6 is a Wnt co-receptor, in its absence Wnt may trigger coreceptor-independent signalling pathway. With the same set of experimental strategies, Ca2+-PKC-NFAT axis is turned on instead in the absence of LRP6. This switching, results in loss of mTORC1-driving glycolytic capacity; while simultaneously induces a number of NFAT-downstream targets that take part in mitochondrial glutaminolysis and BCAAs catabolism; leading to Q and BCAAs dependence. Together, these findings indicated that LRP6 serves as a bimodal switch that modulates Wnt-dependent metabolic landscape in astrocytes. Findings related to objective 2 1. Loss of LRP6 signalling results in astrogliosis DKK1 is a Wnt signalling antagonist functions by promoting the endocytosis of LRP6. This effect mimics the switching of Wnt downstream signalling resulted from direct LRP6 knockdown. Elevated expression levels of DKK1 is found in both brain cortex tissues harvested from human late-onset Alzheimer’s disease (LOAD) patients and in aged AD-mouse models, supporting the relevance of astrocytic Wnt-LRP6-mediated signalling during LOAD pathogenesis. The concept of metabolic reprogramming acting as an adaptive mechanism in facilitating phenotyping changes and functional properties of a cellular system has been well-established. In concordance with this, we found that the morphologies of LRP6-deficient astrocytes resemble reactive astrocgliosis; this could be a result of activated NFAT—a classic transcription factor of immune response; as well as a consequence of aberrant amino acid catabolism. One of these consequences is the induction of urea cycle genes and urea excretion from these cells. Urea cycle metabolism is uncommonly found in the brain under physiological condition; therefore, we believe this is a feedback mechanism for coping the enhanced ammonia stresses caused by amino acid catabolism encountered by the astrocytes. 2. Loss of LRP6 signalling in astrocytes impairs neuronal synaptogenesis; leading to neurodegeneration, cognitive and memory decline in mice Previous studies have suggested DKK1 is liked to neurodegeneration and LOAD. Here we offer a new insight on how it may affect cells other than neurons in the brain and contribute to disease pathogenesis. As mentioned above, DKK1 hampers LRP6-dependent Wnt signaling in astrocytes, and hence results in metabolic dependence on Q and BCAAs in these cells. Since both Q and BCAAs are also physiological metabolic precursors that normally delivered from astrocytes to neurons for neurotransmitter recycling and biosynthesis; with astrocytes consume them as fuel when LRP6-dependent signalling is hampered this limit their availabilities to neurons. Without efficient neurotransmitter recycling and biosynthesis, this results in synaptic deficits and electrophysiological functional decline in neurons. Consequently, these cellular defects manifest as cognitive and memory deficits in vivo. Together, these finding reveals how cross talks between proteins and metabolites abundance affects normal functioning of the brain, offering new insights on how metabolic disturbance contributes to accelerated brain function decline and dementia. Findings related to objective 3 (A) Antagonizing DKK1 improves functions in AD-mice, but other LOAD-risk factors in human may impair LRP6-mediated Wnt signalling as well As mentioned above, Wnt antagonist DKK1 level is upregulated brain cortical tissues of AD-mouse model (e.g. 6-month 3xTg). By stereotaxic injection of a small molecule inhibitor against DKK1 (WAY-262611) into such area, this yielded improvements in both short-term and spatial working memory in these mice. But consider that in human, other known LOAD genetic risk factors may also affect the LRP6 function as well. For instance, individuals harbouring the APOE-E4 allele would express APOE4 protein which can hamper the recycling of LRP6-containing vesicles back to the surface membrane; or individuals who have LRP6 LOAD-associated SNP (rs1012672) could suffer from reduced LRP6 expression in the prefrontal cortex. All these factors could result in diminished surface availability of LRP6, hence hence the fidelity of Wnt-LRP6 signalling axis. (B) Intranasal administration of glutamine and BCAAs improves brain physiology and functions Despite various risk factors could lead to diminished LRP6 surface availability among different individuals, the downstream metabolic consequence as a result of losing Wnt-LRP6 signalling upstream, were however similar. Because of that, we would opt for a downstream targeting approach. From our analyses, we reasoned that compromised brain functions as a result of LRP6 signalling loss are likely a direct result of insufficient Q and BCAAs availability to neurons. Targeted supplementation of these metabolites in quantities equivalent to difference found between normal and astrocyte-specific LRP6-deficient brain samples was therefore performed through the intranasal route which allowed direct brain delivery and avoidance of any unexpected degradation in the body system. Upon targeted nutrient supplementation, brain tissues of astrocyte-specific LRP6-deficient mice revealed alleviated astrogliosis, better neuronal dendritic morphologies and synaptic functions. These animals also regain better performance in memory-related tasks than the vehicle controls. Together our findings reflected that the objectives of this project are properly achieved.

16103317.label: Major findings and research outcome
16103317.value: Major findings: 1. LRP6 is a unique Wnt coreceptor on astrocytes, serving as a bimodal switch that modulates their metabolic landscape. 2. The Wnt-LRP6 mediated mTOR-AKT axis is essential for sustaining glucose metabolism. In its absence, as a result of Wnt antagonist DKK1 action; APOE4 interference on LRP6 recycling or LRP6-knockdown, Wnt switches to activate the LRP6-independent Ca2+-PKC-NFAT axis, resulting in a transcription network that favours glutamine (Q) and branched chain amino acid (BCAAs) catabolism over glucose metabolism. 3. Exhaustion of these raw materials (Q+BCAAs) essential for neurotransmitter biosynthesis and recycling results in compromised synaptic, cognitive and memory functions, priming for early changes that are frequently found in LOAD. 4. In addition to traditional drug therapies (e.g. DKK1 inhibitors), our findings also highlight that intranasal supplementation of glutamine and BCAAs is effective in preserving neuronal integrity and brain functions, proposing a nutrient-based alternative medicine method for delaying cognitive decline when LRP6 cell surface levels and functions are suboptimal.
