16103317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16103317.value: In this project, we demonstrated that the altered brain metabolic balance can potentially be circumvented by short-term intranasal glutamine and branched chain amino acids (BCAAs) supplementation, even if the altered cellular metabolism could be secondary to pre-existing genetic or other events during the pathogenesis of LOAD. Studies on specific modulation of amino acids and other metabolites in diet has indeed shown promise for improving markers of aging and longevity, with our findings this could be potentially adopted for pathological brain aging and early LOAD management. Intranasal spray formulation and development could be an area of applicational research, such as intranasal cobalamin (Vit.B12) or and insulin sprays for direct delivery into the brain. Amino acids are natural nitrogen carriers, our result revealed that adaption of amino acid catabolism results in induction of ureagenesis in astrocytes, serving as a feedback mechanism coping with the increased ammonia stress. This is therefore associated with elevated urea excretion to the peripheral circulation; potentially being a new biomarker for early diagnosis. Future evaluation on blood urea contents can be performed in individuals with mild cognitive impairment and those harbouring APOE4 allele(s) to address if this is a reliable marker of early pathogenesis.

16103317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16103317.value: This study revealed new insights on metabolic roles of brain Wnt signalling, with important implications in early pathogenesis of LOAD. We revealed that LRP6-mediated Wnt signalling in astrocytes is governing the metabolic landscape in these cells. Integrated metabolomics and transcriptomics analyses revealed extensive metabolic reprogramming occurred when LRP6 is lost, switching from glycolytic to glutamine and branched chain amino acids (BCAAs)-dependence. The aberrant exhaustion of these amino acids, which are raw materials for neurotransmitter biosynthesis and recycling, results in compromised synaptic functions. While the fidelity of LRP6-mediated signalling could be hampered by DKK1—a Wnt signalling antagonist; other important factors may contribute to inhibition as well, such as the presence of APOE4 allele that hampers LRP6 recycling and the LRP6 LOAD-associated SNP (rs1012672) which diminishes LRP6 expression directly. This hinted that targeting DKK1 alone (as proposed) is unlikely to achieve maximal results when other factors are present. Coping with that, we devised a downstream targeting approach as these upstream variants would lead to the same downstream metabolic consequences. We highlighted that intranasal supplementation of glutamine and BCAAs directly is effective in preserving the neuronal integrity and brain functions, suggesting a nutrient-based alternative medicine method for delaying cognitive and memory decline.

16103517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16103517.value: We propose to construct a polymer-peptide hybrid hydrogel as a new smart material responsive to ultrasound trigger. This hydrogel will consist of polymer chains crosslinked by self-assembling peptide nanostructures. Ultrasound energy will be used to trigger the change of supramolecular conformation of peptide assemblies, which will then lead to changes in the macroscopic properties of hydrogel, such as the crosslinking density of the network, erosion profile, and mechanical strength. As self-assembling peptide nanostructures result from an interplay of non-covalent interactions, such as hydrogen bonding, pi-pi stacking and electrostatic interaction, the same sequence can display various ways of hierarchical ordering and morphologies. Perturbation by ultrasound will shift the peptide assemblies from one equilibrium state to another, by either kinetic trap and thermodynamic control. By using different self-assembling peptides as crosslinks, we expect that it is possible to use ultrasound to trigger a spectrum of different responses in hydrogel. We will explore the mechanism by varying ultrasound parameters to explore the thermal and non-thermal effects, including the influence of frequency, intensity and extent cavitation. Potential application of this new material in pulsatile drug release will be investigated. 此提案目的是要創造一種由聚合物和多肰合成並能感應超聲波的智能水凝膠，這新材料由聚合物鏈和自組多肰交聯而成。通過超聲波刺激，多肰組合的超分子構象會產生變化，以致改變水凝膠的宏觀特性,包括交聯密度丶侵蝕情況和機械強度等。由於自組多肰的納米結構源於多種非共價的相互作用，如氫鍵丶pi-pi 堆積和靜電作用，相同的肰序列也能展示不同的分級秩序和形態，而超聲波的擾動可以透過動力或熱力的控制將多肰組合從一平衝狀態轉移至另一平衝狀態。利用不同的自組多肰作交聯，便能造岀對超聲波產生各種形式反應的水凝膠。我們會通過改變超聲波的頻率丶強度和氣穴作用，探索控制材料反應的熱力與非熱力之機制，並研究水凝膠用於間歇性藥物釋放的可能性。

16103517.label: Realisation of objectives
16103517.value: Firstly, a model self-assembling peptide (original peptide, OP) and concomitant histidine-substituted self-assembling peptide (F20H) were used to examine the feasibility of utilizing external stimuli to control the assembly and disassembly of self-assembling peptides. Both pH and ultrasound were found to be employable in controlling the assembly and disassembly kinetics, thereby constructing a double-stimuli-triggered model self-assembling system. Additionally, the disassembly of model self-assembling peptide OP, could be significantly enhanced by single substitution from phenylalanine (F) to histidine (H). Next, possibility of controlling peptidic hybrid hydrogel crosslinker using controlled ultrasound as external stimuli was investigated. Here, amyloid-like β-sheet forming self-assembling peptide (SAP) was utilized to fabricate peptidic ‘nanomillipede’, which consists of worm-like nanoscale ‘body’ and cysteine-terminated peptidic ‘legs’. The nanomillipede crosslinker was treated using ultrasound for specific time and the result indicates satisfying linear length control of crosslinkers. Moving on, nanomillipedes with different length were used to crosslink the vinyl sulfone (VS) modified dextran to form mechanically tuneable hybrid hydrogels. Unique properties are conferred to the hybrid system. The nanoscale anisotropic millipede-like geometry, reversible intermolecular interactions within nanomillipede, and thiol (SH) crosslinking sites on nanomillipedes provide shear-thinning property, self-healing property and soft tissue-mimicking mechanical strength, respectively. This previous work has significance in clarifying the relationship between microscopic crosslinker properties (especially size and geometry) and macroscopic hybrid hydrogel properties, where little investigation has been carried out. When self-assembly peptide fibers are used as crosslinks of hydrogel, the gel exhibits self-healing upon mechanical disruption. On one hand, this prevents the weakening of hydrogel hampering the achievement of pulsatile release from the gel. On the other hand, this property may be useful for other applications such as tissue repair and wound healing. Inspired by above results on mechanically tuneable hybrid hydrogels of vinylsulfone-decorated polysaccharide and cysteine terminated-peptides, we explored the effect of ultrasound on the assemblies formed by disordered protein mimicking polymer–oligopeptide hybrid (IPH). IPH forms micron size artificial membraneless organelles (AMLOs) under physiological conditions through liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS). Size of the AMLOs could be reduced by ultrasound application while the liquid nature of AMLOs remained unaffected. It was clear that mechanical perturbation modified AMLOs even in the absence of thermal effect. We next tested our hypothesis that ultrasound could trigger the release of biological cargo molecules from AMLO. Due to the positive charge of AMLO, we chose to investigate DNA as the biological cargo. Opposing the hypothesis, around 5-fold DNA enrichment was observed upon sonication, while AMLOs evolved from its liquid phase into solid phase forming gel like assemblies. Next, we examined RNA as the biological cargo. Lower enrichment of RNA in AMLOs was observed and the liquid nature was maintained upon sonication independent of the N/P ratio. In the experiments of studying cargo recruitment kinetics of ultrasound treatment, recruitment reached a plateau within sonication time of 15 minutes for both RNA and DNA without significant change in total volume. Furthermore, higher cargo recruitment was reported with higher mechanical indexes (higher intensity at 40 kHZ). We speculated that aromatic groups of nucleic acids and the peptide on IPH rearrange during sonication inducing a conformational change such that more nucleic acids could be recruited into assemblies. This explanation is consistent with the literature on ultrasound induced gelation. As explained above, we found that ultrasound was not suitable as a trigger to release cargo from AMLO, and therefore objective 5 could not be realized as planned. Nevertheless, the discovery opened up a new possibility to deliver bioreactor into cells using ultrasound, as detailed in section 6.2.

16103517.label: Major findings and research outcome
16103517.value: Ultrasound effect on two bioinspired polymer-peptide hybrid materials, namely hydrogel and liquid condensate (artificial membraneless organelles, AMLO), were studied. Under the investigation on hydrogel, length of peptide crosslinker can be readily modulated by ultrasound treatment, which in turn influence the mechanical strength, self-healing and shear-thinning properties of hybrid hydrogels. All these features endow this new hybrid hydrogel with promise as a new biomaterial platform for expanding the application as artificial scaffold in tissue engineering. For the AMLOs, two scenarios as AMLO alone and AMLO loaded with nucleic acids were studied for changes in cargo loading and releasing behaviours. AMLO itself found to be change its molecular arrangement by mechanical stimulation of ultrasound, while its highly dynamic nature buffered noticeable changes of the materials’ overall identity. However, possibly due to a strong adjustment of pi-pi stacking interactions, AMLOs loaded with DNA formed distinct gel-like assemblies abandoning its liquid phase. Furthermore, the acoustic cavitation effect may induce conformational changes, leading to improvements in the nucleic acid recruitment. Overall, results demonstrate the use of ultrasound in manipulating the assembly-disassembly and non-covalent interactions of two polymer-peptide assemblies.

16103517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16103517.value: As ultrasound is effective for enriching nucleic acids in the liquid-like polymer-peptide assemblies, it can enhance the functionality of the polymer-peptide assemblies as artificial membraneless organelles (AMLO). We propose to use AMLO as a deliverable "reactor", in which biochemical reactions involving nucleic acids take place at higher rate. Ultrasound will be used to serve two purposes: 1) increase the permeability of cell membrane to allow intracellular delivery of AMLO; 2) increase the concentration of nucleic acids and other reactants within AMLO during sonication, not only to increase the carrier's payload but to facilitate the subsequent release of cargo.

16103517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16103517.value: The project has investigated the use of ultrasound to influence the behavior of biomaterials by exploring the mechanical effect of ultrasound on the conformation of self-assembling peptides attached to a polymer backbone. We were able to construct self-healing hydrogels whose mehcanical strength could be tuned using ultrasound. This approach can find relevant applications in tissue engineering scaffold. Separately, polymer-peptides were designed to assemble into liquid droplets, for which ultrasound could enrich the loading of nucleic acids. Further experiments can be conducted to explore this approach for intracellular delivery of reactions involving nucleic acids.

16103817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16103817.value: The oscillation of cytoplasmic calcium concentration (or called calcium spike) serves as a universal and versatile second messenger in plant cells to control numerous cellular events in response to both developmental cues and environmental factors. However, the mechanistic and the mode of action of calcium ion signaling in plant responses still remains to be an enigma. To decipher the information coded in the calcium spikes, more than 250 calcium-binding proteins (CBPs) from Arabidopsis have been proposed to serve as calcium ion sensors. These CBPs undergo conformational changes upon calcium-binding, and consequently interact with downstream effectors to elicit precise cellular responses. Calmodulins (CaMs) and CaM-like proteins (CMLs), calcium-dependent protein kinases (CDPKs) and calcineurin B-like proteins (CBLs) are responsible for decoding calcium-binding events into both kinase/phosphatase activities and protein-protein interactions, leading to the ultimate regulation of downstream target proteins and subsequent cellular responses. Since all plants are exposed to gravitational field on earth, the gravitational force constantly elicits a mechanical signal in plant cells, which regulates plant morphogenesis, growth and development. Past plant cell biology studies have revealed that gravistimulation by reorientation of whole Arabidopsis seedlings is able to trigger biphasic spikes of calcium ions. The initial and the second spike peaks at 4 and 40 seconds, respectively, following 180-degree reorientation of whole plant. Each of these two calcium signatures may be translated into a unique phosphor-relay network and a distinct profile of protein phosphorylation. In this proposal, we plan to perform quantitative phosphoproteomics at 15 and 40 seconds of gravistimulation, respectively, to identify protein phosphorylation profile changes in both CBPs and their interacting proteins unique to each of the two calcium spikes. In combination with kinase assays, reverse genetics, cell biology studies and epistatic analysis, our approach intends to provide new insights into the calcium spike-specific phosphor-relay signaling pathways and to build comprehensive models of phosphor-relay networks for the gravitropic response. 细胞液中的钙离子浓度变化(或称为钙密码，或钙指纹，或钙峰值)是一种普遍存在的和通用的第二信使。它在植物细胞中可以控制无数的细胞活动以致响应不同的发育的和环境的因素信号的应答。 然而, 植物对机械力诱导的钙离子信号是如何反应的仍然是个谜。 传递钙峰值的信息密码的钙耦合蛋白质(CBP) 有超过250 之多。它们在拟南芥中可作为钙离子密码传感器。 这些 CBP 经过与钙耦合导致构象变化并与下游的影响因子如钙调素和钙依赖激酶(CDPKs) 组成级联反应导致下游靶蛋白质互作及其后的及联反应。 因为所有的植物都生长在重力场中，持续不断的重力机械信号调节植物细胞活动和植物组织的形成、增长和发育。 过去的植物细胞生物学研究表明由 180度调转整个拟南芥幼苗，重力会诱导钙离子双相脉冲。初次和第二次尖峰峰值分别在 4 和 40秒钟。 这两个补钙指纹可以转化为一种独特的磷酸化传递网络。 在这项建议书中, 我们计划要通过行定量 磷酸化蛋白质组学 在 15 和 40 秒两个 时间点寻找两个钙尖峰信号特异的钙耦合蛋白质（CBP）和与它们的相关的钙依赖激酶(CDPKs)蛋白 及其底物。 并进行激酶测定、反向遗传学、细胞生物学研究和分析表观遗传。 我们采取的方法拟提供有关钙离子双相脉冲中钙峰特异的磷酸化网络，信号通路并构建全面的重力信号传递网络通道。

The hybrid plants’ genotypes have been confirmed (Figure 2). The force-induced calcium oscillation in the hybrid transgenic plant has been monitored and measured by a CCD camera (Figure 3). 5.3.2. A gravistimulation machine has also been built as planned (Figure 4). The automatic re-orientation clinorotation machine has been designed to re-orient adult Arabidopsis plant of 4 - 8 cm long inflorescence. To capture the 20 sec- and 50 sec-specific gravistimulated phosphoproteomes from Arabidopsis, we gravistimulated Aeq/LUC Arabidopsis plants using the clinostat (Figure 4) for 20 sec and 50 sec, respectively. The multiple inversions (6.5 to 7 rounds) within 20 sec allowed plants to induce higher level of phosphorylation on proteins followed by the immediate frozen of force-stimulated plants in liquid nitrogen. The control plants were harvested and frozen in liquid nitrogen without rotation treatment. This pair of plants were mixed together as a single biological replicate. For the 50 sec gravistimulated plants, we also used clinostat to rotate a whole set of plants for multiple rounds and kept the plants at the upside-up position at the end of 20 sec of rotation. while the other group of plants were kept at the upside-down position for additional 30 sec. 5.3.3. As compared to the newly developed dimethyl labelling-based quantitative PTM proteomics protocol (Liu et al., 2018), we eventually decided to first try the SILIA-based 4C quantitative phosphoproteomics onto 150 sec gravistimulation-altered protein phosphosites in Arabidopsis. By 4C PTM proteomics (Figure 5), we found 13 gravistimulated protein groups include cytoskeleton structural proteins like Chloroplast Unusual Positioning1 (CHUP1), Patellin3 (PATL3), and Plastid Movement Impaired2 (PMI2), as well as the blue light receptor Phototropin1 (PHOT1, Yang et al., 2020). These 15N-labeled adult plants was re-oriented 180-degree for multiple times (6.5) up to 20 sec as described above (Figure 4), and the aerial organs of Arabidopsis were harvested for proteomic analysis. Similarly, we applied the 50 sec gravistimulation onto Aeq/LUC transgenics to harvest the second calcium spike-specific phosphoproteins. A total of 6 pairs of plant groups were harvested for each time point and frozen immediately in liquid nitrogen. 5.3.4. The mixings of 14N-coded with 15N-coded tissues with a ratio of 1 to 1.1 generated 3 pairs of differentially labelled and mixed tissues (F1, F2, F3, R1, R2 and R3). In order to identify phosphoproteins specific to 20 sec and 50 sec cytoplasmic calcium concentration spikes, the labelled and gravistimulation-treated (Figure 4 and 5) tissues from each time point were mixed together (Figure 6). The total cellular proteins were isolated quickly from the mixtures of frozen plant tissues in a protein-denaturing solution containing 8 M of urea. The phosphoproteins from 2 x 6 mixed tissues were extracted through salt gradient centrifugation and subsequently proteolytically digested into phosphopeptides. The phosphopeptides from each of mixing samples were enriched via TiO2 and Fe3+IMAC columns (Figure 7) and fractionated on SCX columns. Around 10 – 20 fractions of phosphopeptides were prepared from each mixing replicate for LC-MS analysis (Figure 5 - 7). We normally obtained about 10 µg of 80 - 90% pure phosphopeptides from a gram of 14N/15N-coded tissue mixture. 5.3.5. These phosphopeptides (or PTM peptides) were analyzed using LC-MS/MS machines provided by both UCSF proteomics services and Stanford Carnegie Institute MS services. The MASCOT search engine was used for the initial identification of phosphopeptides from mass spectrometry (MS)- data while SQUA-N, and/or SILIAMASS2.0 quantitation software were used for quantitation of phosposphopeptides to identify 20 sec- and 50 sec-specific phosphopeptides and phosphoproteins (Figure 8). New antibodies were raised against numerous force-related phosphosites of phosphoproteins, such as S155 of ZAC8, S605 of CPK1, S107 and S167 of TREPH2, and S108 of SEC14 (Figure 12). 5.3.7. Molecular biological studies were performed on newly selected phosphoproteins. The first round of biological study of these phosphoproteins genes included 18 single mutants generated via T-DNA insertion and 7 double mutants generated through both CRISPR genome editing and genetic crossing (Figure 13, 14, 15). Single mutant cpk1 and double mutants, cpk1cpk2 (Figure 13, 14) and phot1phot2 (Figure 15) were among those mutants assayed for growth and gravitropism phenotypes. The functional role of PHOT1 in gravitropic response was further confirmed with gravicurvature measurement in the darkness of both the loss-of-function double mutant phot1phot2 and its complementary transgenic plant PHOT1/phot1phot2 (Figure 15). 5.3.8. 16103817.value: In this proposed project, we have developed dimethyl labeling-based quantitative PTM proteomics protocol (Liu et al., 2018; Moradi et al., 2021) although we eventually decided to first apply the SILIA-based 4C quantitative phosphoproteomics onto 150 sec gravistimulation-altered protein phosphosites in Arabidopsis (Wang et al., 2018; Yang et al., 2020). Preliminary proteomic quantitation of these two sets of phosphopeptide groups revealed that there were 14 and 22 phosphopeptide groups identified as significantly regulated phosphoprotein groups (SRP) for 20 sec and 50 sec of gravistimulated plants, respectively. We have defined the gravity regulated phosphoproteins collectively as GREPHs. Several of these Grephs have been classified into membrane protein such as TREPH2, kinase such as MKK1 and CPK1, vesicle trafficking proteins such as Sec8, filamental protein such as KAC1 as well as ion channel proteins such as ACA8 and transcription factor like TPR1. To confirm the authenticity of newly identified phosphosites associated with the calcium spikes, the synthetic peptides and phosphoproteins containing these newly identified putative phosphosites were analysed using the Western blots and dot blots with the phosphosite-specific antibodies. The preliminary reverse genetic and molecular biological studies of 25 putative gravity-related phosphoproteins genes identified from the three phosphoproteomics experiments showed that CPK1, MKK1, and PHOT1 kinases auto-phosphorylate themselves and might phosphorylate other protein substrates, suggesting that these phosphoproteins might play a role in transducing gravity force-specific calcium spike signals down to protein phosphorylation.

16103817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16103817.value: These research activities have laid a foundation for the follow-up molecular and cellular biology and reverse genetic studies on many potentially important and putative gravity force signaling-related proteins. Further genetic screening of single and double mutants of Grephs will help discover plant gravity force sensors and more putative gravity force signaling components and help us to build complex signaling network underlying plant gravitropism. The antibodies produced will be used to study the dynamic changes in phosphorylation status of some phosphoproteins across several time points of gravistimulation. These immunoblotting studies of gravistimulated plants will provide information about the responsiveness of protein phosphorylation to gravistimulation signals and will define the gravity force signaling components.

16103817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16103817.value: Plant gravitropism is a fundamental response of plant to the earthly gravitational force. Interestingly, this response has two cytoplasmic calcium spikes following a 180-degree inversion of whole plants. To decipher the rich signaling information which the biphasic calcium signatures encode, our integrated multidisciplinary proteomic approach starts from the SIML-based quantitative PTM proteomics to identify likely protein candidates to the subsequent follow-up reverse genetic screens and biochemical study of gravistimulated dynamic changes in protein phosphorylation. The high-throughput phosphoproteomics integrates with the biological functional validations to map out the important early stage signaling components in the gravity sensing networks of plant gravitropism. This work will help us to understand the molecular basis underlying the plant gravitropism. The outcome of this study may help us to breed super-productive crops for feeding billions of people around the world. Someday, these discoveries may help us colonize either the moon or Mars where planet gravity strength is weak for crop plant growth.

16104517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16104517.value: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a neurodegenerative disorder common in the elderly. Our understanding of PD has been improved substantially by the study of genes that are linked to familial PD. One such gene is α-synuclein (α-syn) which is a major component of Lewy bodies (LBs), the classic pathological hallmark of PD. It is widely accepted that the aggregation of α-syn and formation of LBs are crucial elements in the pathogenesis of PD. However, how aggregation of α-syn can induce the formation of LBs or can affect cellular function and survival is poorly understood. Although α-syn and its familial PD linked mutants (A30P, E46K, A53T and H50Q) have an increased tendency to aggregate, a robust α-syn aggregation model is still lacking. In order to address this issue, we have previously modified α-syn to increase its tendency to aggregate 20-fold by attaching a 17 amino acid CL1 peptide to its C-terminus. In this cellular study, we showed that this increased propensity in α-syn aggregation with the attachment of CL1 enhanced cell death and formation of LB-like protein aggregates. With the use of an adenoviral expression system, we found that CL1 α-syn enhanced the degeneration of dopaminergic neurons associated with the formation of the LB-like α-syn aggregates in mice, suggesting that enhanced α-syn aggregation is a major contributor to neurodegeneration in PD. These results demonstrate that CL1 α-syn can be a valuable tool in studying how α-syn aggregation contributes to PD. In this resubmission, we have revised our proposal to address all the suggestions from the reviewers and have also provided new preliminary data supporting our proposed mouse model. We propose in this study to establish a novel transgenic mouse model based on our previous findings by selectively expressing WT or mutant α-syn with or without CL1 in dopaminergic neurons. The long term goal of this study is to establish a robust alpha-syn aggregation transgenic animal model to study the role of alpha-syn aggregation in the formation of LBs and neurodegeneration in PD. This study will contribute significantly to the development of PD therapies that target alpha-syn aggregation. 帕金森氏病（Parkinson’s disease, PD）是一種常發於老年群體的神經退行性紊亂疾病。現已知的關於帕金森氏病的研究更多集中在與家族性遺傳帕金森病相關的基因，其中之一就是α核突觸蛋白（α-synuclein, α-syn），並作為路易氏體（Lewy Bodies, LBs）的主要成分，而路易氏體則是帕金森氏病典型的病理特徵。現在多被人廣泛所接受的帕金森氏病發病機制的主要因素，是α核突觸蛋白的聚集和路易氏體的形成。然而，關於α核突觸蛋白的聚集是如何誘發路易氏體的形成和如何影響細胞功能和存活始終未能明晰。盡管α核突觸蛋白及其與家族遺傳性帕金森氏病相關的突變體（A30P, E46K, A53T和H50Q）都有較高的聚集傾向，然而仍舊缺少一個顯著的α核突觸蛋白聚集模型。為了闡明這個問題，在初期，我們通過修飾構建，在α核突觸蛋白鏈C末端添加一個由17個氨基酸組成的短肽CL1，使其傾向性聚集增加了20倍。 在細胞層面的研究中， 我們發現在α核突觸蛋白添加CL1短肽之后，這種蛋白聚集的傾向性增加會增加細胞的死亡和類路易氏體的蛋白聚集。通過利用腺病毒表達體系，我們發現CL1 α-syn在小鼠腦內表達能夠增加多巴胺神經元的退行性凋亡，並伴隨形成路易氏體α核突觸蛋白聚集，由此表明了增加的α核突觸蛋白聚集是帕金森病神經退行性的主要促導因素。以上這些結果証明了CL1 α-syn可以作為我們研究α核突觸蛋白的聚集是如何引發帕金森氏病的有利工具。所以基於之前的發現，我們在本項研究中提出，通過選擇性在多巴胺神經元內表達野生型α核突觸蛋白及其突變體，和表達修飾後帶有CL1短肽的野生型α核突觸蛋白及其突變體，建立不同的新的轉基因小鼠模型。研究的長遠目標是建立一個α核突觸蛋白顯著聚集的轉基因動物模型，用來研究α核突觸蛋白在路易氏體形成和神經退行性帕金森氏病中的作用。本項研究將會在帕金森氏病針對α核突觸蛋白的治療中有重要作用。

16104517.label: Realisation of objectives
16104517.value: 1. We had generated transgenic mouse lines that could conditionally express high levels of WT α-syn with or without CL1 specifically in selected neuronal population. We first explored the most effective ways to activate cre in the TH creERT2 mice with the 4-HT treatment. In order to achieve this more efficiency, we acquired a reporter mice R2R-brainbow 2.1 transgenic mice (Snippert, et.al., 2013) and then crossed that with the creERT2 mice. The offsprings from this cross were aged to 3 months and then treated with different schemes of 4-HT injection. The effective excision induced by cre would be indicated by the expression of different florescent proteins in the brain stem. We had tested extensively with different schemes of 4-HT and found that the creERT2 was not effective in activating the expression of the florescent proteins in the mice. We therefore acquired another mouse line, the DAT cre mice, and crossed this line with the R2R-brainbow 2.1 transgenic mice. After three months we sacrificed the offsprings of this crossed and found the DAT cre could effectively activate the expression of florescent proteins in brain stem. We therefore decided to use this DAT cre mice instead. We than proceed to established crossing our transgenic mouse lines to the DAT cre mouse lines. We found that crossing of our transgenic mouse lines with the DAT cre mouse line resulted in the expression of WT α-syn with or without CL1 specifically in the dopaminergic neurons. We then proceeded to determine if expression of WT α-syn with or without CL1 specifically in the dopaminergic neurons would affect neuronal cell death in the dopaminergic neurons in associated with the behavior deficit in an age-dependent manner. 2. To determine how early and late stage expression of WT or WT-CL1 α-syn would affect dopaminergic neuronal survival, the process of α-syn aggregation and movement dysfunction, we generated control or mice expressing WT or WT-CL1 α-syn by crossing our transgenic mice with the DAT cre mice. We generated mouse cohort that we could perform movement assessment at the age of 3, 6, 9 and 12 months. At each time point after movement assessment, we sacrificed the mice and perform neuronal counting and immunohistochemistry. From our movement assessment study, we found that both expression of WT or WT-CL1 α-syn resulted in an age-dependent progressive movement dysfunction. In addition, we also observed that this movement dysfunction was associated with the age-dependent reduction of dopaminergic neurons along with the observed movement dysfunction. More interestingly, when we assessed the number and size of the α-syn positive aggregates in the dopaminergic neurons, we found that although the numbers of α-syn positive aggregates reduced along with aging in mice expressing WT or WT-CL1 α-syn, the size of the aggregates were increasing along with aging. These observations strongly suggested that small α-syn aggregates could progressively convert to larger aggregates especially accumulated in the perinuclear region as observed. This provide a potential mechanism of how Lewy bodies are form in the pathogenesis of PD.

16104517.label: Major findings and research outcome
16104517.value: From our proposal, we proposed to establish a novel mouse transgenic model by expressing WT or WT-CL1 α-syn specifically in the dopaminergic neurons to extend our previous study of how α-syn aggregation could contribute to the PD pathogenesis. We have now established a robust novel mouse PD models that can express WT or WT-CL1 α-syn specifically in different type of neurons in the brain. One of the major findings in this project is that expression of WT or WT-CL1 α-syn specifically in the dopaminergic neurons is enough to induce dopaminergic neuronal loss and movement dysfunction. These results provide another strong support that movement dysfunction in PD patients is specifically linked to the demised of the dopaminergic neurons along with aging in related to the abnormal accumulation of α-syn. Another major finding from our study is that the formation of α-syn-positive aggregates along with aging is a progressive process in which it start with the accumulation of small cytosolic aggregates and then follow by a more prominent perinuclear larger aggregates as observed in aged mice expressing WT or WT-CL1 α-syn. These results provide a potential mechanism of how Lewy bodies are form in PD patients. Our study also provides a model that can study how α-syn expression could post toxicity to different neurons such as dementia with Lewy bodies, frontotemporal dementia in contrast to that in PD.

16104517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16104517.value: Aging, increased expression of α-syn and α-syn aggregation are known to be the major contributing factors to the pathogenesis of Parkinson’s disease (PD). From our study, we have established a novel mouse model that will facilitate the understanding of the pathogenic mechanism behind these factors. This novel α-syn transgenic model is particular useful in the study of different synucleinopathies. For instance, it is not known why in PD, dopaminergic neurons are more vulnerable to α-syn aggregation whereas in other degenerative disorder such as dementia with Lewy bodies, other neurons are affected more. With our novel α-syn transgenic model, we plan to further study how WT or WT-CL1 α-syn can affect the survival of different neurons in related to different disorders such as dementia with Lewy bodies, frontotemporal dementia in contrast to that in PD

16104517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16104517.value: In this study, we have developed a novel mouse model to study how abnormal expression and processing of a Parkinson’s disease related protein, α-synuclein, can contribute to pathogenesis of Parkinson disease. We have further followed how the process of aging could affect the movement dysfunction in associated with the demise of dopaminergic neurons and abnormal accumulation of the disease-causing α-synuclein protein aggregates. Our new mouse model will provide a novel tool to study the mechanism behind the pathogenesis of PD which could lead to the development of new therapeutic strategies for this neurodegenerative disorder.

16104617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16104617.value: 真核生物DNA複製的解旋酶CMG複合物由11個蛋白因子構成，包括作為其催化核心的MCM2-7，以及 輔助因子Cdc45和GINS（Psf1,2,3和Sld5）。 CMG解旋酶在復制起位點的組裝和激活，在細胞體內被嚴格調控。在細胞週期的G1期， 兩個MCM2-7複合物被組裝 到DNA複製起始位點上，形成MCM雙六聚體（DH）。此時，MCM DH的解旋酶活性還未被激活 。隨著細胞進入S期，兩種激酶（DDK和S-CDK）和多種解旋酶激活因子共同作用，將Cdc45和 GINS依次組裝到MCM2-7 DH上，形成穩定的CMG二聚體起始復合物（pre-IC）。隨後，pre-IC被轉化成兩個活躍的CMG解旋酶，其沿著相反的方向進行DNA雙鏈的解鏈活動 。 Mcm10在激活 CMG活性的過程中發揮重要作用；有研究指出，其作用可能是通過促進MCM2-7 DH的分離。最近的體外重構DNA複製過程的研究，在很大程度上揭示了CMG解旋酶的組裝和激活過程中關鍵事件的分子順序。然而， 此過程中各個生物蛋白因子潛在的分子機制仍然很不清楚 ；其中一個主要的原因是 相關過程中生物大分子的高分辨率結構非常缺乏。 在本項目中，我們將提取體內組裝的pre-IC，以研究其冷凍電鏡的高分辨率結構，從而了解CMG解旋酶體內組裝和激活的分子機理。這項研究的結果將為DNA複製起始的調節提供有價值的見解，特別是關於CMG解旋酶的組裝和激活的體內機制。

16104617.label: Major findings and research outcome
16104617.value: In eukaryotes, DNA replication is initiated from multiple sites along each chromosome. The assembly and activation of the replicative helicases are tightly regulated. This process begins with the formation of an inactive head-to-head MCM double hexamer (DH) at replication origin. Upon entry into S phase, the MCM DH is further transformed into two active CMG helicases. In this study, we successfully purified and/or assembled several large replication complexes that are involved in this activation process and successfully determined their high-resolution structures using cryo-EM. The information derived from these structures has significantly advanced our understanding of helicase activation (Adv Exp Med Biol 2018; Nat Commun 2022) as well as the regulation of the activity of CMG helicase (manuscripts submitted and in preparation).

16104617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16104617.value: This research laid a solid foundation for us to further characterise the regulation of replication initiation in both yeast and human.

16104617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16104617.value: DNA replication is initiated from hundreds or even thousands of origins distributed along chromosomes. Every initiation event is strictly controlled to ensure faithful genome duplication during each cell division cycle. Mis-regulation of replication initiation can cause dire consequences such as tumorigenesis. It is important to understand the mechanisms regulating this process. Central to this regulation is the assembly of a replication machinery called replicative helicase which unzips the duplex DNA to generate DNA template for DNA synthesis. In this study, we made use of the cutting-edge cryo electron microscopy to image the replicative helicase and determined their relevant high-resolution structures. Seeing is believing. With the solved structures, we now have a picture of how they work.

16104917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16104917.value: In eukaryotic cells, genomic DNA is tightly packaged into a chromatin structure. A basic nucleosome is composed of a histone octamer that is wrapped by 147 base pairs DNA. The octamer comprises two copies of each of the core histones—H2A, H2B, H3, and H4. In addition to core histones, the linker histone H1 binds to adjacent canonical histone octamer region and helps form the chromatin. Chromatin structure, histone post-translational modifications, and histone variants regulate several biological functions such as DNA replication, DNA repair, and transcription. Among the aforementioned histones, H4 is considered to be the only one without histone variants. We identified and characterized a new histone H4 variant, H4G. H4G is only present in primates and shows 85% identity with canonical H4. H4G localizes in the cellular nucleolus and we have detected its expression specifically in breast cancer cell lines. 16104917.label: Realisation of objectives
16104917.value: To establish the functional role of the novel histone variant H4G, we performed a series of follow-up experiments. Our findings were presented in several conferences and are published in several papers (see list of publications for details). Aim 1 Histone variants are known to affect nucleosomal stability. These effects on nucleosome stability underlie their functions in processes such as transcription and DNA repair (1). The H4G N-terminal tail amino acid sequence was found to be different from that of canonical H4, which directly interacts with H2A (2). Hence, the different functions of H4G when compared to canonical H4 may be a direct result of their sequence differences, which likely manifests itself through altered nucleosome stability. Therefore, we analyzed the stability of reconstituted nucleosomes consisting of this variant with the 601 nucleosome positioning sequence as DNA template. However, during the preparatory stage, we noticed that the recombinant expression of H4G protein alone is very poor. This was likely caused by the high hydrophobicity of its alpha-helix 3 domain and this issue was later solved by the addition of GST-tag. GST-H4 and GST-H4G appear to be capable of forming nucleosomes, however SDS-PAGE of the reconstituted complexes revealed that, while nucleosome assembled with GST-H4 contains the expected stoichiometric amounts of core histones, complexes reconstituted with H4G do not. This demonstrates that H4G cannot form a stable nucleosome using the regular salt-dialysis method. As we discovered that H4G strongly interacts with the nucleolar histone chaperone NPM1, the possibility exists where H4G might be able to form nucleosomes in the presence of this histone chaperone. NPM1 has been well studied to act as a histone chaperone to assist the deposition of nucleosomes in vitro (3). In the absence of histone chaperones, when histones and DNA are mixed together under in vitro condition, they form large aggregates that do not enter the gel (4). In contrast, if core histones are preincubated with increasing amounts of NPM1, free DNA and nucleosome bands can be detected where the amount of free DNA decreases and nucleosomes increase in a NPM1-dose-dependent manner. However, with the exception of some tetrasome-like bands, no apparent nucleosome bands were observed when a mixture of histones containing His-SUMO-H4G was used. These results clearly indicate that H4G is either unable to form a nucleosome in vitro in the presence of NPM1 chaperone, or the nucleosome or nucleosome-like-structure that formed is highly unstable. Moreover, we decided to conduct FRAP assays using MCF7 cells that had been transfected with GFP-tagged or mCherry-tagged proteins. Interestingly, the FRAP recovery of GFP-tagged H4G in nucleoli was very fast for a histone, with a fluorescence recovery half time (t1/2) of less than 20 s. While this was slower than free GFP itself, this result indicates that H4G is not stably associated with the chromatin in nucleoli. Therefore, it is very likely that H4G is released on the nucleolar chromatin by NPM1 and forms temporary nucleosome-like-structure, which then dissociates quickly. Aim 2 In eukaryotic cells, rDNA transcription occurs in the nucleolus (5). We treated H4G-transfected MCF7 cells with low concentration of actinomycin D, which primarily inhibits transcription by RNA polymerase I (6), and observed that the nucleolar localization of H4G was lost with H4G becoming dispersed throughout the nucleus. In contrast, in non-transfected control cells, the addition of actinomycin D did not change the localization of H4. H4G localization did not change when H4G-transfected MCF7 cells were treated with rapamycin, an mTOR signaling inhibitor. mTOR signaling has been shown to regulate the synthesis of ribosome components, pre-rRNA, and 5S rRNA without affecting rDNA transcription (7). Taken together, these results suggest that the nucleolar localization of H4G may be dependent on ongoing rDNA transcription. For further analysis, we produced several H4G knockout (KO) and knockout-rescue MCF7 cell lines through CRISPR-Cas9 technique. We found that, in H4GKO cells, the amount of total rRNA production was reduced. And the amount of rRNA in the H4G rescue lines was restored to the amount observed in the WT MCF7 line. These data indicate that H4G promotes the bulk transcription of rDNA. We also found that protein synthesis rates were reduced by approximately 10% in H4GKO cells in comparison with WT cell. Moreover, the overall cell cycle was significantly delayed in the H4GKO cells, a likely consequence of their dampened protein synthesis. The observed cell cycle delay may either be linked to the reduced amounts of rRNA and the decrease of the protein synthesis speed or the decrease of the restarting efficiency from G0/G1. Moreover, to investigate the growth effects of H4G in vivo, xenografts of NOG mice using WT MCF7, MCF7-H4GKO3 and MCF7-H4GKO9 cells were created. This xenograft experiment showed that both H4GKO lines generated tumors with sizes half of that by WT MCF7 cells. These results suggest that H4G has a positive role in promoting rDNA transcription, protein synthesis and cell growth. Aim 3: We first checked h4g expression levels in several cultured cell lines. We found that the overall h4g expression is low compared to canonical histone H4 genes: HIST1H4d (h4d) and HIST1H4e (h4e). In general, the h4g gene is expressed in breast cancer cell lines at low levels, which is consistent with the expression data from public database (The Human Protein Atlas). Notably, the expressions of h4g in breast cancer cell lines, including MCF7, LCC1, and LCC2 cells were higher than the expressions of h4g in the noncancerous breast epithelial cell line, MCF10A; or the embryonic kidney cell line, HEK293T. To confirm the presence of H4G at the protein level, we have also conducted a LC-MS proteomic analysis of MCF7 cell which positively identified peptides specific to H4G. Next, we checked the expression profile of h4g using a human cancer survey cDNA panel (ORIGENE) containing eight different types of tumors (breast, colon, kidney, liver, lung, ovary, prostate, and thyroid). The results showed that although the baseline expressions of h4g are varying among normal tissues , it is elevated in colon cancer and significantly upregulated in breast cancer tissue compared to normal tissue control. Finally, we evaluated the association between the expression of h4g and breast cancer progression using a human breast cancer cDNA panel (ORIGENE). Importantly, we discovered that the h4g expression level was progressively increased as tumors progressed to more advanced stages. The expression of canonical h4d and h4e were also increased in breast cancer patients, however the observed fold-changes are comparatively insignificant to that of h4g. Reference 1. 16104917.label: Major findings and research outcome
16104917.value: Histone variants, present in various cell types and tissues, are known to exhibit different functions. For example, histone H3.3 and H2A.Z are both involved in gene expression regulation, whereas H2A.X is a specific variant that responds to DNA double-strand breaks. In this project, we characterized H4G, a novel hominidae-specific histone H4 variant. H4G expression was found in a variety of cell lines and it is particularly overexpressed in the tissues of breast cancer patients. H4G was found to localize primarily to the nucleoli of the cell nucleus. This localization was controlled by the interaction between the alpha helix 3 domain of H4G and the histone chaperone Nucleophosmin 1 (NPM1). In addition, we found that the nucleolar localizing H4G increases rRNA levels, protein synthesis rates, and cell cycle progression. Furthermore, micrococcal nuclease digestion of H4G-containing nucleosomes reconstituted in vitro indicated that H4G destabilizes the nucleosome, which may serve to alter nucleolar chromatin in a way that enhances rDNA transcription in breast cancer tissues. Further study shows that H4G is not incorporated into the nucleolar chromatin even with the chaperoning assistance of NPM1 both in vitro and in vivo. Instead, H4G may interfere with the histone chaperone activity of NPM1 and alters the nucleolar chromatin configuration. Taken together, these results suggest that H4G expression alters nucleolar chromatin and enhances rRNA transcription in breast cancer cells.

16104917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16104917.value: We have characterized a novel histone variant, H4G. We discovered the enhanced expression of H4G in breast cancer patients. We have investigated how H4G is localized in nucleolar, and how the nucleolar localization of H4G affects the cell. Regarding the interaction between H4G and NPM1, since NPM1 is known to possess a multitude of cellular functions, one potential direction is to explore whether the effect of H4G on NPM1 extends beyond mere histone-chaperoning in both normal and cancer cells. Also, since we established the link between the over-expression of H4G with breast cancer progression, it would be potentially rewarding to see if H4G can serve as a breast cancer early detection marker and therapeutic target. Finally, with the method established in this study, we could look into the characterization of other histone variants that are involved in other similar cellular processes. The future studies of breast cancer related genes using our established methods would help us better understand their functions and potentially develop more effective targeted therapies.

16104917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16104917.value: In eukaryotic cells, the genomic DNA is tightly packed into the chromatin. Many histone variants are present in different location and stages, and have distinct functions from their canonical counterparts. We characterized a hominidae-specific histone H4 variant, H4G. The expression of H4G is very limited in normal tissues and its expression was increased in breast cancer patients in a stage-dependent manner. H4G primarily localized in nucleoli through its interaction with NPM1, which is a nucleolar histone chaperone. In addition, we demonstrated that the amounts of rRNA and protein synthesis rate were reduced in H4G knockout (KO) cells. Interestingly, we found that H4G is not stably incorporated into the nucleoli chromatin even with the chaperoning assistance by NPM1. On the contrary, the nucleoli chromatin in H4G KO cells was more compact than the WT nucleoli chromatin and they exhibits diminished growth characteristics. Taken together, these results suggest that H4G may open the nucleolar chromatin and enhances rRNA transcription, which ultimately drives breast cancer growth and progression.

16200117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16200117.value: Endocrine disruptors (EDs) may interfere with the human and wildlife immune systems and are causing increasing public concern. The discharge of treated sewage effluent has been suggested as one of the major sources of EDs in natural water bodies, because conventional treatment technologies are unable to remove EDs efficiently. Meanwhile, despite the wide use of chlorination for pathogen disinfection in sewage treatment works (STWs), the formation of toxic disinfection byproducts (DBPs) has become a challenging issue in sewage treatment nowadays. Recently, separate studies have shown that photocatalysts based on nitrogen-doped TiO2 (N-doped TiO2) could potentially be used for ED photodegradation and pathogen disinfection under visible light irradiation. However, N-doped TiO2 generally requires different modifications to achieve an efficient removal of EDs or pathogens. There is currently a lack of technology that is specifically designed for simultaneous ED removal and pathogen disinfection efficiently in sewage treatment. Moreover, separating photocatalyst nanoparticles after sewage treatment is difficult and represents another major obstacle to their application in real sewage treatment. This proposed project aims to develop a unique, photocatalytic technology based on N-doped TiO2. This technology will possess the dual functions of ED photodegradation and pathogen disinfection which will be activated by visible light. Core/shell-structured N-doped TiO2@SiO2@Fe3O4 nanoparticles will be prepared, and the photocatalysts will be synthesized using different approaches for combining the three components, silver (Ag), reduced graphene oxide (rGO) and N-doped TiO2@SiO2@Fe3O4, to form three kinds of magnetic photocatalysts. They are (i) rGO/Ag|N-codoped TiO2@SiO2@Fe3O4, (ii) Ag loading on rGO/N-doped TiO2@SiO2@Fe3O4, and (iii) Ag/rGO loading on N-doped TiO2@SiO2@Fe3O4. The synthesized photocatalysts will then be characterized by various solid-state technologies (e.g. SEM, TEM, BET and VSM). Their removal efficiency and magnetic separability in synthetic water will be systematically studied. Meanwhile, the effects of water matrices will also be considered. The mechanisms of ED and pathogen removal in sewage will be investigated. Furthermore, a prototype study will be conducted to examine the magnetic separability and reusability of the photocatalysts in real sewage samples using a patented prototype reactor. The effect of light intensity will also be tested. This advanced technology has great potential to replace chlorination as a single-step treatment process for simultaneous ED and pathogen removal in STWs by using novel visible-light-driven magnetic photocatalysts. To our best knowledge, there is currently no similar technology developed and available in the market of sewage treatment in Hong Kong and other regions. 內分泌干擾物會對人體和動物免疫系統造成干擾，引起公眾社會對這類物質的關注。傳統污水處理技術並不能有效去除內分泌干擾物，處理後排放的污水是自然水體中內分泌干擾物的主要來源之一。同時，污水處理廠普遍利用氯消毒，期間形成的氯消毒副產物是當前污水處理的一個問題。近期研究顯示，氮摻雜二氧化鈦（N-doped TiO2）在可見光下能光催化降解內分泌干擾物並有殺菌效果，但須對氮摻雜二氧化鈦進行改性修飾。目前還沒有一項技術同時針對污水處理過程中內分泌干擾物的去除與殺菌功效。此外，由於納米光催化劑難以從污水中分離，也限制了這項技術的實際應用。 本項目旨在開發一種新穎的以氮摻雜二氧化鈦為基礎的光催化技術。這項技術能利用可見光同時達到內分泌干擾物的光催化降解與殺菌兩個目的。首先製備出核殼結構的N-doped TiO2@SiO2@Fe3O4納米顆粒，再通過不同合成方法把銀（Ag）、還原石墨烯（rGO）和N-TiO2@SiO2@Fe3O4納米顆粒結合在一起，得到三種磁性光催化劑，分別是(i) rGO/Ag|N-codoped TiO2@SiO2@Fe3O4, (ii) Ag loading on rGO/N-doped TiO2@SiO2@Fe3O4,和(iii) Ag/rGO loading on N-doped TiO2@SiO2@Fe3O4。 本项目將會通過不同技術手段(如SEM, TEM, BET和VSM)對合成出來的催化劑進行表徵，也將系統研究催化劑在合成水樣中對內分泌干擾物的去除與殺菌效果，以及催化劑在水中的分離效果，同時考慮水質影響，研究內分泌干擾物及病菌去除機理。此外，會利用獲得專利的原型反應器來研究催化劑在真實污水樣品中的磁分離效果與重複使用的去除效率，同時研究光照強度影響。此先進技術具有替代氯消毒的巨大潛力，利用磁性可見光催化劑，能在污水處理過程中一步到位，同時去除內分泌干擾物與病菌。據瞭解，目前還沒有類似技術得到開發或應用於香港及其他地區的污水處理市場。

16200117.label: Realisation of objectives
16200117.value: The project was smooth and the four research objectives were met as expected. In this study, N-doped TiO2-based photocatalysts were developed for pathogen (E. coli) removal and degradation of ED: bisphenol A (BPA, a representative ED) under solar irradiation. Ag and reduced graphene oxide (RGO) were used to improve the performance of the photocatalysts. A visible-light-absorbing and magnetically separable photocatalyst Ag/Fe,N-TiO2/Fe3O4@SiO2 (AgFeNTFS) through a multi-step method was successfully developed by codoping Fe and N in the TiO2-based component, Ag deposition and equipping the Fe3O4@SiO2 magnetic core. The photocatalyst was used for the photocatalytic disinfection of E. coli and degradation of BPA in synthetic water and real sewage. AgFeNTFS exhibited good performance in the separate disinfection of E. coli and degradation of BPA under visible light irradiation. The mechanisms of BPA removal and disinfection of bacteria were investigated. The reactive species generation and the BPA degradation intermediates in synthetic water were studied. •O2- and H2O2 were the dominant reactive species in photocatalytic disinfection process. Another type of N-doped TiO2 based photocatalyst RGO/Fe,N-TiO2/Fe3O4@SiO2 (RGOFeNTFS) was developed and investigated for its disinfection performance under simulated solar light. It initiates photocatalytic reaction under solar irradiation, and shows high efficiency in disinfection of E. coli. Photocatalytic disinfection treatment is a process of interaction between the activated photocatalytic materials and the sewage. Other than the photocatalyst, the sewage characteristics also affect the photocatalytic disinfection efficiency. As discussed in the photocatalytic disinfection of different types of sewage, the sewage characteristics (organic matter, suspended solids, inorganic ions, pH and DO level) are involved in the variation of disinfection performances using RGOFeNTFS. Therefore, the effects of the sewage characteristics on the photocatalytic disinfection were evaluated. Prototype experiments were performed to understand the practical applicability of the photocatalysts under the real treatment condition. Different types of sewage samples collected in HK local STWs were used for the photocatalytic disinfection to evaluate the potential of the technology using the N-doped TiO2-based photocatalysts. A solar simulator was used as the light source to mimic the solar irradiation which is the driven energy of photocatalysis in this study. Moreover, the photocatalytic disinfection of bacteria and degradation of BPA were performed in real sewage. In real sewage under visible light using AgFeNTFS, a 3-log reduction of E. coli was achieved in the sewage using AgFeNTFS after 90 min of photocatalytic reaction, the treated sewage could meet with the local disinfection discharge standard. Meanwhile, BPA in the sewage solution could be simultaneous completely removed. After 3 cycles of simultaneous photocatalytic reaction, AgFeNTFS still retained its photocatalytic activity and demonstrated no obvious change in the XRD pattern, indicating a good reusability of the photocatalyst in real sewage. Sewage characteristics have major effects on photocatalytic disinfection. As the low-salinity sewage samples have better water quality than the high-salinity sewage samples, low-salinity sewage has higher potential for the photocatalytic disinfection treatment using RGOFeNTFS under solar irradiation. Organic matter (presented in TOC), suspended matter (presented in turbidity), pH and DO level are found to significantly influence the photocatalytic disinfection performance. Furthermore, the impacts of photocatalyst and treated sewage on phytoplankton are determined by monitoring the phytoplankton density, and further predicting their potential impacts on the ecosystem. The negligible effects RGOFeNTFS on phytoplankton, which supports the ecosystem as the base of aquatic food webs, indicate the non-toxicity photocatalyst to the ecosystem, demonstrating that photocatalytic disinfection of sewage using RGOFeNTFS (<=3 g/L) is feasible without unfavorably influencing the water body. Another innovative technology using a ternary BiVO4/Ag/g-C3N4 composite, constructed by photodeposition and hydrothermal reactions, was developed for disinfection of sewage. The Ag in the BiVO4/Ag/g-C3N4 composite promoted the interfacial electron transfer, effectively suppressed the recombination of e−–h+ pairs, and boosted the reactive species generation during the photocatalytic process. It achieves 6.5-log E. coli inactivation in 60 min. BiVO4/Ag/g-C3N4. Generally, reactive species such as e−, h+, •O2−, •OH, and H2O2 are generated and are involved in bacterial inactivation in the photocatalytic disinfection process. To investigate the dominant species in the photocatalytic E. coli inactivation by BiVO4/Ag/g-C3N4, the reactive species scavenging experiments were conducted. The results demonstrated that h+ and •O2− followed by H2O2 played important roles in photocatalytic bacterial inactivation by BiVO4/Ag/g-C3N4. In addition, to investigate the practical disinfection, the photocatalytic disinfection by BiVO4/Ag/g-C3N4 in a secondary sewage effluent sample was undertaken and the effects of sewage components i.e. suspended solids, inorganic ions and dissolved NOM on the disinfection activity were explored in depth.

16200117.label: Major findings and research outcome
16200117.value: AgFeNTFS exhibited good performance in the individual disinfection of E. coli and degradation of BPA under visible light irradiation. In the individual process, a 6.3-log reduction in cell density of E. coli was achieved and BPA (2 mg/L) was completely removed by AgFeNTFS in the separated photocatalytic processes within 120 min. In the simultaneous process, the disinfection of E. coli was not affected by the presence of BPA, but the degradation of BPA was dropped by 10%. The disinfection reaction and degradation of BPA have similar dominant reactive species of •O2- and H2O2. In addition, after 90 min of photocatalytic reaction using AgFeNTFS under visible light, the treated sewage could meet with the local disinfection discharge standard. In the treated sewage, no detectable bacteria regrowth was detected after the recovery period of 24 h or 48 h of keeping in dark at room temperature, indicating the irreversible disinfection of E. coli by AgFeNTFS. The magnetic AgFeNTFS showed good reusability over three cycles. After three cycles of simultaneous photocatalytic reaction in real sewage, AgFeNTFS still retained its photocatalytic activity and stable crystalline structure, showing a good reusability. Using RGOFeNTFS under solar irradiation, around 20 min and 45 min of photocatalytic disinfection are required for low-salinity sewage samples to meet the discharge standard, and no bacterial regrowth has been observed in the treated sewage after 48 h. However, treatment of high-salinity sewage with poorer water quality remains a challenge according to relatively long reaction time and low disinfection efficiency. Organic matter (presented in TOC), suspended matter (presented in turbidity), pH and DO level are found to significantly influence the photocatalytic disinfection performance. Multivalent ions such as Ca2+, Mg2+, SO42- have more significant adverse effects than monovalent ions (Na+, K+, Cl- and NO3-) on the photocatalytic disinfection of low-salinity sewage after secondary biological treatment, but not on low-salinity sewage after tertiary treatment. RGOFeNTFS shows good reusability over three cycles for photocatalytic disinfection of low-salinity sewage samples (both tertiary and secondary) under simulated solar light irradiation. In the toxicity assessment using phytoplankton in seawater as an indicator, RGOFeNTFS (of 3 g/L) and the treated low-salinity sewage (both after tertiary and secondary treatment) demonstrate insignificant adverse effects on the ecosystem. The innovative ternary BiVO4/Ag/g-C3N4 composite also provides rapid disinfection of E. coli in real sewage sample, and indicates stable efficiency in cycling tests with dominant reactive species of h+ and •O2− followed by H2O2 for disinfection reaction.

16200117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16200117.value: As the N-doped TiO2-based photocatalysts showing potential for sewage treatment, it exhibits significance of extending the research to engineering application. It is promising to apply the photocatalysts in a scale-up test. A continuous reactor for disinfection of sewage is proposed to be designed and used for further development of the research, and hence evaluating the technology driven by solar energy for sewage treatment. And applying the N-doped TiO2-based photocatalysts in different STWs will benefits the assessment of the technology for practical use.

16200117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16200117.value: Pathogens and endocrine disruptiors (EDs) in sewage are growing concerns in sewage treatment, because of their adverse impacts on human being and wildlife. Conventional treatment methods have drawbacks such as inefficient removal, non-sustainable, and generation of toxic by-products. Photocatalysis is an effective and green technology for simultaneous disinfection of pathogens and removal of EDs in sewage. In addition, employing the single-step photocatalysis process to tackle the issues of pathogens and EDs could be cost-effective and space saving. This study developed three types of TiO2-based photocatalysts for disinfection of pathogens and removal of EDs. The photocatalysts are active under visible light and solar light irradiation, and able to be effectively separated from treat sewage after reaction due to their magnetic property. The photocatalysts effectively inactivate pathogens and remove EDs simultaneously from sewage, and retain the performance in real sewage after three cycles of reaction without significant structural change, exhibiting good reusability and high potential in sewage treatment. Moreover, according to the toxicity assessment, the photocatalytically treated sewage is non-toxic to the environment and the technology is safe. From this study, photocatalysis using the TiO2-based photocatalysts is a promising technology for disinfection and removal of EDs in sewage treatment.

16200317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16200317.value: Standard algorithmic analysis considers a worst-case scenario and gives an upper bound on the running time. Although the bound is guaranteed to hold, it can often be pessimistic. Input into a specific application may exhibit a particular pattern, that is unknown a priori, but that it can be exploited to speed up processing. A self-improving algorithm starts with a training phase that tunes its computation to the hidden distribution of input instances. The advantage is that the expected running time of the algorithm after the training phase can be smaller than the best worst-case bound. Nevertheless, self-improving algorithms are known only for a few one- or two-dimensional problems, including sorting, two-dimensional convex hulls, two-dimensional Delaunay triangulations, and two-dimensional maxima. Self-improving algorithms are needed for fundamental problems such as convex hulls, Delaunay triangulations and Voronoi diagrams in higher dimensions. Also, current self-improving algorithms disallow any dependence among the input items. Removing this restrictive assumption will broaden the applicability of self-improving algorithms. 分析算法時, 我們通常假設最壞情況, 來為運行時間得出一個上限。雖然這能保證上限不會被超越，但分析結果往往較為悲觀。某些應用的輸入可能呈現特定的模式，就算模式是未知的，還是可以利用它來加速運算。自我改進算法先用一些輸入來調整運算程序，使之更適合輸入內隱藏的特定模式。優點是在調整階段後，預期的運行時間可能遠低於最壞情況下得出的上限。然而，自我改進算法僅用於幾個一維或二維問題，包括排序丶二維凸包丶二維Delaunay三角剖分和二維最大值。我們需要為諸如高維凸包丶Delaunay三角剖分和Voronoi圖等基本問題設計自我改進算法。此外，目前的自我改進算法不允許輸入項之間有任何依賴。若能消除這限制, 將可提高自我改進算法的使用。

16200317.label: Realisation of objectives
16200317.value: We have realized the objectives of the project. We have obtained a collection of self-improving algorithms for sorting, Delaunay triangulation, and Voronoi diagrams. For sorting n items, we obtained the first set of algorithms that go beyond the product distribution model. A key feature of the product distribution model is that each input item is drawn from a distribution independently. This lack of dependence is uncommon. Our first extension assumes that there are some hidden parameters that follow a product distribution, and that multiple input items may depend linearly on the same hidden random parameter. Our second extension introduces mutual dependence by allowing the input distribution to be a hidden mixture of m product distribution. We obtain expected running times that are close to the information-theoretic lower bound after a training phase that runs in polynomial time. Let H be the output entropy. In the first extension, the expected running time is O(n/eps + H/eps) for any eps in the range (0,1) which matches the information-theoretic lower bound; the training phase runs in O(n^2*(log n)^3) time. In the second case, the expected running time is O((n*log m)/eps + H/eps), and the training phase runs in O(mn*(log mn)^2 + m^eps * n^{1+eps} * log (mn) ) time. The above expected running time bounds hold with probability at least 1 – 1/n. Subsequently, we remove the restriction to linear dependence, and we also extend the result to Delaunay triangulation in two dimensions. For sorting, we no longer require any specific formulations of the input items as functions of the hidden parameters; we only assume that each hidden function has O(1) extrema and two such functions have equal values at O(1) parameter values. In the training phase, our algorithm automatically learns the partition of the input items according to the hidden random parameter that they depend on. After spending O(n^3) time in the training phase, we can sort in O(n + H) expected time with probability at least 1 – 1/n. We extended the result to Delaunay triangulation as well. Delaunay triangulation has found numerous applications in mesh generation for numerical simulation, curve reconstruction, the construction of Voronoi diagrams, etc. As long as the coordinates of each input point are determined by some hidden bivariate polynomials of a fixed degree on hidden, two-dimensional random parameters, the training phase can automatically partition the input points according to the hidden random parameters that they depend on. After spending a polynomial time in the training phase, we can construct the Delaunay triangulation in O(n*alpha(n) + H) expected time with probability at least 1 – 1/n, where alpha(n) is the extremely slowly growing inverse Ackermann function. That is, we nearly match the information-theoretic lower bound. Recently, we extended our result to the computation of Voronoi diagrams under convex distance functions. Convex distance functions are generalizations of the Euclidean metric, and they have been studied extensively in the context of Voronoi diagram computation due the application in the motion planning of convex planar robots among obstacles. We allow the input distribution to be a hidden mixture of m product distributions. As long as m = o(sqrt{n}) and each product distribution has a probability of Omega(1/n) being chosen for generating an input instance, our algorithm can compute the Voronoi diagram in O((n*log m)/eps + n*2^{O(log^*n)}/eps + H/eps) expected time with probability at least 1 – 1/n, after spending O(mn*(log mn)^{O(1)} + m^eps * n^{1+eps} * log (mn)) time in the training phase. Note that 2^{O(log^* n)} grows extremely slowly. In the Euclidean case, the expected running time improves to O((n*log m)/eps + H/eps). So far, self-improving algorithms can be viewed as the study of algorithms that approach the optimal time complexity according to a fine-grained measure. Another important direction that researchers have considered is designing output-sensitive algorithms so that the running time is in tune with the actual output size instead of the worst-case output size. An open question is designing output-sensitive algorithms in high dimensions so that the fixed overhead (which is independent of the output size) is significantly less than Theta(n^2) where n is the number of input points. Very recently, we discover that it is possible to do so in fixed dimensions in the setting of self-improving algorithms. In particular, we believe that one can obtain an expected running time of O(n+f) times a polynomial in log n, where f is the output size. The time complexity of the training phase is n^{O(d)}. Due to the connection between convex hull in d+1 dimensions and Voronoi diagram and Delaunay triangulation in d dimensions, it means that we also have self-improving, output-sensitive algorithms for Voronoi diagrams and Delaunay triangulations in high dimensions. We are preparing a manuscript on this result.

16200617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16200617.value: There has been a substantial amount of work on the optimal control of various inventory systems over the last few decades. For most inventory problems with a single state variable, structures of optimal decisions can be obtained. Inventory problems with higher dimensional state spaces, the focus of this project, arise when it is necessary to keep track of a series of events in order to make optimal decisions. For instance, to make an optimal ordering and clearance decision in a perishable inventory problem, the age distribution of the on-hand inventory needs to be known. To make optimal ordering decisions in a lost-sales inventory system with a positive ordering lead time, it is essential to track both the outstanding orders and the on-hand inventory. The longer the lifetime or ordering lead time for the above examples, respectively, the higher the dimension of the state space is. Absent a fixed ordering cost, complete characterization of optimal solutions has been successful for many inventory problems through the establishment of submodularity, multi-modularity, or L-natural-convexity of the cost functions. With a fixed ordering cost, successful characterization of optimal decisions is almost impossible when the dimension of the state space exceeds two. Regardless of whether an optimal structure is known or not, since the optimal decisions are probably state-dependent and complex, computing an optimal policy is notoriously hard due to the curse of dimensionality. A common approach is to develop heuristic policies based on a partial or complete characterization of the optimal structures of the problems. In this project, we will approach such problems from a new angle by exploring their asymptotic behavior. Since the behavior of many complex systems is predictable in an asymptotic regime, very simple heuristic policies can be asymptotically optimal and work well for the original problems under mild conditions. Our preliminary research suggests that, as long as the demand is moderate or not too small, a perishable inventory system can be managed in a similar way to a non-perishable one. Such an insight is very encouraging as it may lead to much simpler management procedures for some highly complex inventory systems than any of the existing heuristic policies. While asymptotic analysis is widely used to study complex queueing systems, it has seen few applications in inventory systems, which have their distinctive features. Thus, seeking simple and asymptotically optimal policies for complex inventory systems may require the development of new methodologies. 过去几十年间已经有不少的工作集中在库存系统的最优控制策略上。 对于大部分的一元状态变量的库存问题, 已有最优策略的结构化结果。 高维库存问题, 也是本项目的重心, 会随之出现如果最优策略必须基于一系列的事件而不是单个变量。比如, 为了得到易腐产品的最优订货和清货策略, 我们需要知道当前所有库存的剩余寿命的分布。在带lead time的需求流失库存系统中, 最优策略依赖于当前的库存量以及已经下单尚未到达的库存量。 在以上例子中, 产品的最大寿命或者lead time越大, 相应的状态空间维度越高。 没有固定订货成本的前提下,很多库存问题可以通过建立成本函数的submodu- larity, submodularity, multi-modularity 或者 L-natural-convexity 这些性质来得到最 优策略的完全刻画。但是如果有固定订货成本的情况下, 状态空间的维度一旦超出2, 这种方法几乎就会失效。不论最优决策的结构能否解出, 由于当前最优行为取决于当前的高维状态(通常依赖关系很复杂), 计算最优策略很难实现, 也就是著名的维数灾难 (curse of dimensionality)。一个通常的做法是基于问题的一些结构化结果提出经验策略。 在本项目中, 我们会从一个新的角度研究这类问题, 也就是探讨渐进的行为。 由于很多复杂系统的行为在渐进的领域会变得可预测, 在很弱的条件之下, 很多时候非常简单的经验策略会收到很好的效果同时也是渐进最优的。我们初步的研究表明, 只要需求不是太小的情况下, 一个易腐库存系统可以近似看成一个非易腐库存系统来管理。这种洞察非常的振奋人心, 因为它可能导致一些比现有策略更简单的方法能很好的管理非常复杂的库存系统。虽然渐进分析在排队论中已经应用的非常广泛, 它在库存系统中的应用还不多,部分归因于后者与排队系统的截然不同的性质。这也对我们探索简单同时满足渐进最优策略提出了新的挑战。

16200617.label: Realisation of objectives
16200617.value: We have successfully accomplished all the objectives and produced a high quality paper published in Production and Operations Management. Inventory problems have a long history and there has been a substantial amount of work on the optimal control of various inventory systems. The problems that suffer the curse of dimensionality are known to be difficult ones and there had been a lot of attempts in this long history. Absent a fixed ordering cost, complete characterization of optimal solutions has been successful for many inventory problems through the establishment of submodularity, multi-modularity, or L-natural-convexity of the cost functions. With a fixed ordering cost, successful characterization of optimal decisions is almost impossible when the dimension of the state space exceeds two. Regardless of whether an optimal structure is known or not, since the optimal decisions are probably state-dependent and complex, computing an optimal policy is notoriously hard due to the curse of dimensionality. A common approach is to develop heuristic policies based on a partial or complete characterization of the optimal structures of the problems. We approached perishable inventory problems, which requires to keep track of the age distribution of the on-hand inventory and is difficult when the lifetime is long, from a new angle by exploring their asymptotic behavior. Since the behavior of many complex systems is predictable in an asymptotic regime, very simple heuristic policies can be asymptotically optimal and work well for the original problems under mild conditions. Such an insight is very encouraging as it leads to much simpler management procedures for some highly complex inventory systems than any of the existing heuristic policies. While asymptotic analysis is widely used to study complex queueing systems, it has seen few applications in inventory systems, which have their distinctive features. Indeed, our analysis revealed interesting insights into the circumstances under which perishability is negligible. This intuition not only leads to the construction of our simple policies, but also helps to establish theoretical performance bounds on the proposed policies. The bounds vanish asymptotically as the market size becomes large and clearly specify a required size for our policies to achieve any given optimality gap. Numerical studies suggest that our policies can work well even for small-to-medium-sized systems and achieve comparable performance to existing heuristic polices.

16200617.label: Major findings and research outcome
16200617.value: It is well known that perishable inventory problems are difficult to optimize due to curse of dimensionality and even heuristic ordering and clearance policies involve solving complicated equations or optimization problems. Inspired by the asymptotic behavior of perishable inventory systems, we consider two simple policies that ignore clearance except at the very beginning of the planning horizon and order up to the mean demand (called a fluid-based policy) as well as a newsvendor type of solution (called a newsvendor type of policy). We provide analytical performance bounds for the policies which vanish as the size of the system increases, implying asymptotic optimality of the policies and also providing lower bounds of the market size to achieve any desired performance. Numerical experiments show that these policies work reasonably well even for small-to-medium-sized systems, suggesting that managing perishable inventory systems with reasonably large market sizes may be just as simple as managing non-perishable ones. In addition, it is observed that when the lifetime is small (L = 2) or the demand distribution has a high coefficient of variations (e.g., hyper-exponential), the performance of our policies deteriorates. Designing simple polices in such circumstances remains an open problem. Given that analytical and tight bounds on the performance of heuristic policies are rarely established in the perishable inventory literature, our research makes a significant contribution to both the existing literature and practice.

16200617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16200617.value: The significance of this paper is that we showed that there are ways to deal with problems with long known difficulties due to curse of dimensionality. One is to attack the problems head on by exploring their hidden properties (which requires sophisticated mathematical skills and patience) and the other is to look at the problems from different angles. These methodologies have the potential to be applied to a broad set of problems in inventory management or other planning/decision problems that suffer curse of dimensionality. We expect to encounter such problems in different applications and apply what we learned to advance new research.

16200617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16200617.value: Inventory problems with higher dimensional state spaces arise when it is necessary to keep track of a series of events in order to make optimal decisions, e.g., the age distribution of the on-hand inventory in a perishable inventory problem and both the outstanding orders and the on-hand inventory in a lost-sales inventory system with a positive ordering lead time. The longer the lifetime or ordering lead time for the above examples, respectively, the higher the dimension of the state space is. This RGC grant leads to a high quality paper published in Production and Operations Management. Our analysis revealed insights into the circumstances under which perishability is negligible, which leads to the construction of and helps establish theoretical performance bounds on simple policies. The bounds vanish asymptotically as the market size becomes large and clearly specify a required size for our policies to achieve any given optimality gap. Numerical studies suggest that our policies can work well even for small-to-medium-sized systems and achieve comparable performance to existing heuristic polices.
