16200717.label: Realisation of objectives
16200717.value: During the undertaking of this project, we have achieved what was listed in the objectives. We have screened and synthesized hierarchically porous non-precious iron-nitrogen-carbon-based electrocatalyst to increase the accessible active sites for oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in alkaline medium. We found a low overpotential of 357 mV was achieved at a high current density of 100 mA/cm2 for OER of the FeNGC-T catalyst (N-doped graphitic carbon with Fe atoms prepared by the Co template method). The multistep chronopotentiometric curves measured with the current density varying from 32 to 75 mA/cm2 (7 mA/cm2 per 500 s) can remain unchanged within 500 s for all steps of the FeNGC-T catalyst, which proved that the well-definable liquid, gas and electron transport passages have been formed within the hierarchically porous structures. We have also developed a core-shell structured catalyst with NiCo2O4 nanowires as the core and MnOx nanoflakes as the shell and deposited on a stainless steel mesh, and applied in anion exchange membrane (AEM) electrolyzer. In addition, a mathematical model coupling two-phase flow and the electrochemical reaction was developed to study the transport of water and the generation of gas bubbles inside the porous microporous layer (MPL) and gas diffusion layer (GDL). Different geometrical structures of MPL and GDL with varied geometrical parameters, including fiber diameter, fiber orientation, and porosity, were reconstructed. Aside from the geometric structure, the wettability of the MPL and GDL was also investigated. All the theoretical investigations have been verified by the experimental results. By taking advantage of the optimized electrolyzer, a high performance AEM electrolyzer has been demonstrated, which can be operated at a high current density of 200 mA cm−2 with a low overpotential of about 500 mV and stably run for 100 h without significant degradation

16200717.label: Major findings and research outcome
16200717.value: With the support of the present RGC grant, we have made significant contributions to the development of patterned electrode structures of electrolyzers and the study of the mass transport in electrolyzers. The results obtained in this project have been published in two peer-reviewed papers, as listed in Sections 8, and presented in a recognized international conference, as listed in Sections 9. The major findings are summarized as follows: We have developed a novel protocol for synthesis of N-doped hierarchically porous graphite carbon catalysts with single Fe atoms by pyrolyzing the mesoporous Fe-polydopamine precursor, which is prepared by one-step of polymerization of a Co-template-embedded dopamine. The as-prepared catalyst exhibits a specific surface area of as high as 1229.3 m2g-1 and demonstrates an extraordinarily high OER activity in the alkaline electrolyte; this strategy also allows the formation of hierarchically porous structures, which can provide well-definable liquid, gas and electron transport passages. We have visualized the gas bubble transport in GDLs to study the effects of the GDL geometry on the two-phase flow in electrolyzers. The results showed that gas is easy to accumulate foam-based GDL as compared to felt-based GDLs. The wettability of the MPL and GDL was also investigated. The result indicated that increasing the PTFE loading in the GDL and introducing carbon nanotubes in MPL could decrease bubble accumulation in GDLs, which greatly enhanced the stability of AEM electrolyzers. With the developed numerical model, the water and gas bubble transport behavior inside the porous media is studied. It is found that the MPL layer with a high porosity facilitates the formation of gas bubbles and effectively removes them from the catalyst layer. Compared with the random fibrous structure of GDL, the simulation indicates that aligned structure reduces the water transport resistance. By varying hydrophobicity of MPL and GDL, it is found that higher hydrophobicity is favored to ensure a balanced gas-liquid transport inside the porous media. With the knowledge attained from the above model, we combined different impacting parameters and studied the synergetic effect of the geometric structure and hydrophobicity in the gas-liquid two-phase flow. The numerical simulation reveals that a hydrophobic GDL with a large porosity combining a hydrophobic MPL with reduced tortuosity is favored in the gas-liquid two-phase flow.

16200717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16200717.value: The present project has primarily focused on the development of patterned electrode structure for AEM electrolyzer and the study of inherently coupled two-phase mass transfer/electrochemical reactions in the electrolyzer. The outcome of this project have deepened our fundamental understanding of electrocatalyst design and two-phase mass transport in the nano-structured electrodes of AEM electrolyzer and provided the needed information for the performance boost of AEM electrolyzer with longer lifetime in the low-cost production of clean hydrogen.

16200717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16200717.value: Solar and wind energy are two of the largest sustainable sources of carbon-free power, but the electricity obtained from solar photovoltaics and wind turbines is intermittent and scattered, and thus unreliable. One of the most promising solutions to this problem is to employ large-scale energy storage to separate electricity generation and use. Electrolysis of water is a promising option for such large-scale and long-term storage, using hydrogen as the storage medium. Recently, anion exchange membrane electrolyzer has been developed to address the cost issue related to its counterpart, proton exchange membrane electrolyzer. The rational design of an efficient electrode with high electroactivity and excellent stability is a critical challenge for anion exchange membrane electrolyzer. In this project, we developed patterned electrode structure for the electrolyzer, with which inherently coupled two-phase mass transfer/electrochemical reactions in the patterned electrode structure were studied. We have optimized the present design and achieved a high performance and stable electrolyzer, which shows promising applications in large-scale energy storage.

16201017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16201017.value: Intracellular delivery of drug molecules, proteins, and genetic materials is in high demand in many areas: gene therapy and reprogramming, tissue engineering, and regenerative medicine. This challenging procedure has to overcome the cellular membrane, a few nanometers thick impermeable barrier that allows restricted access to the cytosol. Reversible permeabilization of the cell membrane to exogenous materials has been addressed through a variety of methods: (1) viral vectors, which are very efficient but pose a high risk of inflammation and cancer-causing mutagenesis; (2) chemical helpers, which avoid such issues but usually only become effective at high cytotoxicity levels; (3) physical methods, which are more benign and can breach the cell membrane by inducing transient pores via microinjection, gold particle bombardment, electroporation (electrostatic pressure), optoporation (laser irradiation) and sonoporation (acoustic pressure). Electroporation, in particular, has found broad interest and scales well with miniaturization. Miniaturization mitigates the need to choose between high delivery efficiency and high cell viability encountered in bulk electroporation. This is achieved by establishing a low-voltage activation via a focused electric field directed at a tiny spot and also by ensuring a rapid cell recovery with a highly localized perturbation on the cell membrane. A low-voltage activation reduces adverse effects arising from electrochemical reactions, gas bubble formation, pH variations, and Joule heating. Nevertheless, with scaling comes the issue of low throughput, which is exacerbated by the use of thin-film surface microelectrodes that inevitably limit the flow chamber height and thus cell handling capacity. Moreover, despite the progress made in delivery efficiency and cell viability, many cells are still found either harmed or untreated. This proposal aims to address these concerns through novel robust microsystems that take advantage of unique microfabrication processes. First, we propose a design featuring bulk microelectrodes for effective electroporation of cells and enhanced throughput. The design will additionally implement in situ separation of treated cells from those harmed or untreated through dielectrophoretic railing of cells, a novel concept that we have introduced recently. Second, we propose to demonstrate a high-throughput precision delivery via nanochannel electroporation based on integrated glass nanocapillaries that we demonstrated using a standard semiconductor fabrication process without involving any costly low-throughput lithography. Third and last, we propose a new intracellular delivery method, which is mechanical in nature and less often studied in miniaturized platforms. This high-throughput approach exposes cells to a controlled shear in a viscous solution by running them through a series of point constrictions. 細胞內轉運，如藥物分子、蛋白質和遺傳物質的胞內遞送，在基因治療與程式重組、組織工程、再生醫學等許多領域都有著極大的需求。這一過程的難點在於轉運的物質必須要穿透一層僅有幾個納米厚度卻非完全通透的細胞膜，這層細胞膜對允許進入細胞的物質具有限制與選擇性。目前已經有多種技術被應用於可逆性增強細胞膜對外來遞送物質的通透性，如：（1）病毒載體，這項技術十分高效，卻有較大機會引起炎症和誘發癌症；（2）化學輔助，這類技術雖然避免了使用病毒載體帶來的風險，但其發揮效應的濃度往往對細胞具有較高毒性；（3）物理方法，這項技術包含了多種在細胞膜上引入暫時性孔通道的方法，並且對細胞傷害也更小，這些方法包括微注射、粒子槍（如金粒子）、電穿孔（靜電力）、光穿孔（激光輻射）和聲致穿孔（聲壓）等。 電穿孔這一獨特的細胞內轉運技術已經吸引了廣泛關注並且可以靈活適用於小型化器件。小型化電穿孔器件在一定程度上改善了大型電穿孔設備對於高轉運效率與高細胞活性不可兼得的缺陷。這一改善得益於通過點聚焦電場形成的低電壓刺激，並且通過對細胞膜高度局部化的作用來保證細胞的快速恢復。低電壓刺激能夠有效地減小如電化學反應、氣泡形成、酸鹼度變化和焦耳熱等一系列負面效應。然而，與小型化隨之而來的問題是較低的樣品通量。這一問題在使用薄膜微電極時尤為突出，這種電極對器件腔體高度的固有限制減小了其可操作細胞的數量。此外，儘管電穿孔技術能夠在一定程度上改善轉運效率與細胞活性，但仍然有相當數量的細胞會受到損害或是沒有被有效穿孔。 這項研究提案旨在利用獨特的微加工工藝製造新型可靠的微系統來解決上述問題。首先，我們提出一種具有三維微電極的器件設計，該器件可以實現高通量且有效的電穿孔。此外，基於我們最近提出的介電泳細胞滑動概念，這一設計還會在同一器件中額外實現對有效穿孔細胞與損傷細胞或未穿孔細胞的分選。第二，我們計畫實現一種基於納米通道電穿孔的高通量、精准細胞內轉運器件，該器件採用我們早前展示的集成玻璃納米毛細管製造技術，這項技術可以通過標準半導體工藝實現納米通道而無需借助任何高成本低通量的高等光刻技術。最後，我們提出一個全新的機械細胞內輸運方法，此類方法目前在小型化系統中的應用研究仍然很少。這一方法通過使具有特定粘度的細胞懸浮液穿過連續的超薄微孔而使得細胞暴露在可控的剪力場中，進而實現高通量且有效的細胞內轉運。

16201017.label: Realisation of objectives
16201017.value: Objective 1 concerned a flow-through electroporation microsystem in which successfully treated viable cells can be railed along physical tracks (bulk microelectrode sidewalls) and thereby isolated from non-viable cells based on the combined effect of dielectrophoresis and hydrodynamic drag. We first studied dielectrophoretic railing of viable cells along bulk microelectrode sidewalls as this was a novel concept that had never been reported before. This required bulk microelectrodes with a special sidewall contour to act as physical tracks. We have developed such microelectrodes using doped silicon substrate by tailoring plasma etch profile. We successfully demonstrated cell railing under the combined effect of dielectrophoresis and hydrodynamic drag (Lab Chip 2018, 18, 3760). We identified the railing efficiency, as high as >95%, against the activation voltage and flow rate. We also applied the technique to dielectrophoretic cell sorting and have reported the collection efficiency of about 86% for both target (HCT116) and non-target cells (K562). We then investigated whether cell railing itself can induce transient membrane pores. We performed cell railing in the presence of 3 kDa dextran as a model cargo molecule. The collected cells showed no noticeable intake of dextran suggesting that neither dielectrophoretic activation nor mechanical contact with the electrodes during railing induced sizeable membrane pores. They also showed the necessity for an additional electrical activation for poration, which we delivered in the form of sinewave voltage bursts superimposed on the background dielectrophoretic activation. We observed efficient and uniform delivery of 3 kDa dextran into railing cells with the dose delivered being proportional with the number of voltage bursts applied. We investigated the delivery rate against various burst parameters. Importantly, we observed railing cells that were losing viability (diminishing in the expression of viability dye) escaped from railing and resulted in the collection of transfected cells with an increased viability fraction. We have reported our results in recent conferences (microTAS, Palm Spring, 2021; Transducers, Virtual, 2021) and recently filed a US provisional patent. We are now summarizing our extended results in a peer-reviewed journal submission. Objective 2 concerned a single-cell nanoelectroporation array microsystem based on integrated glass nanocapillaries and centrifugal cell docking. The integrated glass nanocapillaries are of an in-plane type featuring a cylindrical profile defined by thermal reflow of a doped glass layer on silicon; the process renders the need for advanced lithography redundant. Each nanocapillary connects a dedicated chamber filled with a buffer containing the material to be delivered (dextran) and a chamber filled with cell suspension and shared by all the nanocapillaries. A major challenge we encountered was the accessibility of the nanocapillary openings to cell docking. The nanocapillary openings were situated next to the chamber top or bottom, rendering them inaccessible to cells due to the corner effect. We successfully distanced the nanocapillary openings from bottom corner by etching chambers further into the silicon substrate. However, we faced major obstacles when distancing them from top corner. We tried to address that by replacing flat polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) cover with a structured PDMS similarly featuring chambers. However, this required the top and bottom chambers to be precisely aligned before bonding PDMS cover and silicon substrate to avoid reintroducing a top corner or leakage path between the chambers. This was not an easy task as the alignment had to be performed manually and it required a precision dictated by the length of the nanocapillaries, which had to be kept short (50 um or less) to limit the voltage requirement. This difficulty led to a very low yield and those few successfully aligned failed during operation likely because of high voltage electroporation pulses causing the bonding interface to break down. The novelty in our proposed research rested upon the use of integrated glass nanocapillaries for target application and thus abandoning the proposed microsystem was not a viable option. To move forward, we have characterized the glass nanocapillaries for ion concentration polarization which has never been reported before for such one-dimensional nanochannels. We have summarized our findings in a peer-reviewed journal article (Analytical Chemistry, 2020, 92, 1252). Meanwhile, we investigated the possibility of cell poration and transfection by railing/sliding cells along tubing sidewalls under centrifugal forces, an innovative idea inspired by our railing device in the project. The results indicated that this physical mechanism is ineffective for achieving cell poration based on the intake of 3 kDa dextran molecules although we observed some level of success with the intake of small molecule propidium iodide. Objective 3 has been achieved without encountering any major issue. It concerned a flow-through mechanoporation microsystem based on shear pulses exerted through point constrictions. Point constrictions are of a semiround geometry and cells passing through point constrictions become squeezed in both dimensions (the width and depth). This is unlike cells subjected to conventional rectangular constrictions and squeezed only in one dimension (the width). Moreover, point constrictions are highly localized (hence the term “point”) and accordingly introduce a very little backpressure to the system, which is a silicon-glass platform. The constrictions are situated in cascade along an array of channels. We have determined the influence of the constriction size and count as well as treatment pressure on the cytosolic delivery performance through flow-cytometric analyses of HCT116 cells treated using dextran as model molecules. We have also determined delivery efficiency and cell viability data from three other cell lines: NIH 3T3, HEK293, and MDCK. Moreover, we have demonstrated the versatility of the platform on the delivery of proteins (tubulin antibodies) as well as sequence-specific small interfering RNA (siRNA in transient gene knockdown). Interestingly, we have discovered that target proteins in some cells exhibit a non-diffusive (punctuated) pattern raising the plausibility of mechanisms other than transient membrane pores. It could be that rapid deformation of cell membrane promotes endocytotic uptake of molecules. Indeed, endocytosis is known to play a crucial role for the uptake of large dextran (155 and 500 kDa) in cells treated with ultrasound-driven microbubbles (Meijering et al., Circ. Res., 2009). We have also noticed localized cytosolic staining in some cells treated in the presence of 500 kDa dextran, clearly suggesting endocytosis. Endocytosis as a possible mechanism of cytosolic delivery has not been reported for rectangular constrictions, which makes our report the first account. We have achieved reasonable efficiency for delivering relatively small molecules (e.g., 3 kDa dextran, proteins, siRNA). However, our attempts to use point constrictions to transfect HCT116 cells with labeled or naked plasmids (gWIZ-GFP, 5757 bp) have failed to return detectable delivery or gene expression (3 bar). We have expected this based on the delivery of large dextran molecules (500 kDa) and the passive nature of the delivery relying on diffusion alone to drive molecules through transient membrane pores; the membrane diffusivity is the rate limiting and estimated to be 4 orders of magnitude smaller than the buffer diffusivity according to 70 kDa dextran results obtained with rectangular constrictions (Sharei et al., PNAS, 2013). Moreover, it was recently shown that plasmids cannot be delivered using rectangular constrictions unless a downstream electric field is applied to assist plasmid crossing the disrupted membrane (Ding et al., Nat. Biomed. Eng., 2017). A similar strategy can be adopted here to facilitate the plasmid delivery. We have summarized our findings in a peer-reviewed journal article (Analytical Chemistry, 2018, 90, 1836).

16201017.label: Major findings and research outcome
16201017.value: A major outcome of this project concerns the development of a flow-through mechanoporation microsystem based on shear pulses exerted through single-cell point constrictions (see Publication 1; Section 8; Part C). Our results indicate that an effective cell treatment and cytosolic delivery through point constrictions requires lower supply pressure than through rectangular constrictions of a comparable size. Additionally, our results suggest that a long constriction may not be necessary for the success of cytosolic delivery through rapid cell deformation. The contraction and relaxation a cell undergoes when entering and leaving a point constriction could essentially fulfill the extent of rapid cell deformation required by this cytosolic delivery method. A further project outcome concerns the development of a flow-through microsystem supporting a dielectrophoretic cell railing (Publication 2; Section 8; Part C) and effective electroporation of railing cells (Publications 1 and 2; Section 9; Part C). We also witnessed railing cells that were losing viability escaped from railing and resulted in the collection of transfected cells with an increased viability fraction. The microsystem features silicon bulk microelectrodes with a novel architecture as physical tracks along which cells can rail under the combined effect of dielectrophoresis and hydrodynamic drag. We first characterized the cell railing behavior against various design and experimental parameters and demonstrated flow-through dielectrophoretic cell sorting (Publication 2; Section 8; Part C). Subsequently, we have demonstrated the microsystem for flow-through cell electroporation by superimposing voltage bursts on background dielectrophoretic activation (Publications 1 and 2; Section 9; Part C). The microsystem proposed here for single-cell nanoelectroporation based on integrated glass nanocapillaries and centrifugal cell docking faced some difficulties in fabrication and experiments. Instead, we characterized the integrated nanocapillaries for ion concentration polarization (Publication 3; Section 8; Part C). During our experiments, we also made a serendipitous discovery concerning ordered surface crack patterns in fluidic microchannels which we have reported in a Communication (Publication 4; Section 8; Part C). The students hired for the project also contributed to the development of a chip calorimeter (Publication 5; Section 8; Part C) and the preparation of a review article on point-of-care PCR tests for COVID-19 pandemic (Publication 6; Section 8; Part C). The project led to the training of three MPhil and two PhD students (Section 10, Part C) in addition to the filing of a US provisional patent (Section 11, Part C). Further details of our results are given in Section 5.3, Part B.

16201017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16201017.value: Mechanoporation of cells undergoing rapid membrane deformation through point constrictions allows effective cytosolic delivery of small molecules but fails to deliver relatively large molecules such as plasmids. This is also true for rectangular constrictions because mechanoporation relies on a passive delivery mechanism (diffusion of molecules through transient membrane pores). For further development, a mild electric field can be applied to facilitate large molecules to cross cell membrane following rapid membrane deformation and permeabilization. This strategy has been demonstrated for rectangular constrictions using microelectrodes integrated at the constriction downstream. A similar approach can be implemented here. Alternatively, point constrictions can be turned into microelectrodes as they are defined in silicon. Further development may also target applications. For instance, the microsystem demonstrated here for cell railing and electroporation also supports cell sorting. Using the microsystem, cell electroporation and sorting can be realized concurrently; target cells undergo electroporation while being sorted from non-target cells which travel at a distance from microelectrodes and thus leave the microsystem unaffected (untreated). The microsystem can be applied for the cytosolic delivery of the materials involved in the powerful gene-editing tool known as CRISPR-Cas9 which stands for clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats and CRISPR-associated protein 9.

16201017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16201017.value: The delivery of drug molecules, proteins, and genetic materials into cells is crucial in many fields from gene therapy and reprogramming to tissue engineering and regenerative medicine. This challenging procedure must breach the cellular membrane, which is an impermeable barrier, while maintaining cell viability. Reversible permeabilization of the cell membrane to external materials is typically realized through chemical helpers or viral vectors, which may lead to either cytotoxicity or inflammation and cancer-causing mutagenesis. In comparison, physical methods are relatively benign, and can induce membrane transient pores under mechanical or electrical disturbances. The project demonstrated two novel microsystems that take advantage of physical methods to breach cell membrane for the cytosolic delivery of molecules: (1) a flow-through electroporation microsystem in which target cells receive electroshocks and become transiently permeable to molecules while railing along bulk microelectrodes under dielectrophoretic forces and hydrodynamic drag; and (2) a flow-through mechanoporation microsystem in which cells become transiently permeable to molecules as a result of their rapid membrane deformation under shear pulses exerted through single-cell point constrictions. Such microsystems for high-throughput cell transfection have gained further significance with the invention of CRISPR-Cas9, the new ground-breaking gene editing tool, which received the 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

16201417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16201417.value: The control of stochastic systems driven by Brownian motions has been a popular research area for decades since Brownian motions serve as a good proxy to model the randomness in the real world. The applications of such stochastic control problems range from finance, inventory management, and manufacturing. The basic setting of such control problems is that a system is driven by a random source modeled using a Brownian motion. We can control the system by making adjustments to either increase or decrease the content at some cost. There is also a holding cost depending on the amount of the content, structured to incur higher cost when there is either too much or too little content. The central idea behind the optimal control of such systems is to combat the randomness and takes a long-term view so that the total cost over a planning horizon is minimized. This is implemented by breaking the problem into smaller ones on shorter horizons, and solving it iteratively. The iterative structure and the randomness make solving such problems extremely challenging. In this project, we propose to study a more difficult situation where there is a lead time before the adjustments are effective. This delay effect makes it difficult even to describe the system dynamics since we need a high dimensional descriptor to record all the past adjustments which have been initiated but have not yet become effective. The requirement for a high dimensional space combined with the iterative structure and randomness requires further development of the existing methodology to solve the proposed problems. We plan to divide the study into two general cases, depending on whether a fixed cost is needed to initiate an adjustment. Without a fixed cost, we will show that the optimal value function has a useful property called L-natural convexity and utilize this property to construct an optimal control policy. If there is a fixed cost, we will construct a lower bound for the value function, and identify a control region which will lead to an optimal control policy. For both cases, we also plan to see whether a simple and easy-to-implement policy can be near optimal when the lead time becomes large since this is the case where computational complexity becomes overwhelmingly large and a simple policy is needed for practical applications. We are also interested in quantifying the optimality gap for the simple policy. 由布朗运动驱动的随机系统的控制问题是数十年来的热门研究领域，因为布朗运动是对现实世界中随机性的一个很好的模拟。这种随机控制问题的应用范围包括金融，库存管理和制造管理。 这类控制问题假定系统的库存由一个服从布朗运动的随机源驱动。我们可以增加或减少库存，这样的调整需要付出相应的成本。同时还要支付取决于当前的库存水平的持有成本，当库存水平太多高或太低时，会导致更高的持有成本。分析这类系统的核心思想是结合随机性和长期规划，力图使得在一段规划的时间内总成本达到最小。具体通过将这段规划的时间分成许多份较小的时间片段，再在每段时间分片上，反复迭代求解来实现的。也因此，迭代结构和随机性使得解决这些问题变得非常具有挑战性。 在这个项目中，我们研究一个更加困难的情况，那就是增加或减少库存并不是马上生效，而是有一段延迟时间。由于我们需要一个高维空间来记录所有已经做出但尚未生效的调整，所以这种延迟效应使得描述系统的动态变化都变得十分困难。想让处理迭代和随机性的方法适用于高维空间里，需要进一步发展现有的方法来解决所提出的问题。我们计划将研究分为两类情况，取决于变化库存所付出的成本是否包含一个固定成本。当没有固定成本时，我们将证明最优策略下的成本函数具有一种称为L-natural凸的性质，并利用该性质找到最优控制策略。如果存在固定成本，我们将给出最优策略下的成本函数的下限，并随之确定将被实施控制的状态空间。对于这两种情况，我们还计划看看当增加或减少库存的延迟时间变长时，是否有一种简单且易实施的近似最优策略，使得它得到的总成本非常接近最佳策略得到的总成本。因为最优解的计算复杂度变得压倒性的巨大，同时简单的策略更容易实施也更贴近实际。我们也有兴趣量化近似最优策略和最优策略之间的差距。

16201417.label: Realisation of objectives
16201417.value: Most of the objectives have been achieved with great success in Paper #2 (see Section 8 of the report), which provides a theoretical framework for optimal control with Brownian input. At any time, one may increase or decrease the content at a cost proportional to the amount of adjustment. A decrease of the content takes effect immediately, while an increase is realized after a fixed lead time. Holding costs are incurred continuously over time and are a convex function of the content. The objective is to find a control policy that minimizes the expected present value of the total costs. Because of the positive lead time for upward adjustments, the state of the system is a function on [0,l], a high dimensional object. We first extend the concept of L-natural-convexity to function spaces and establish such convexity of the optimal cost function, achieving objective 1. We then derive various properties of the cost function and identify the structure of the optimal policy as a state-dependent two-sided reflection mapping making the minimum amount of adjustment necessary to keep the system states within a certain region, achieving objectives 2, 4 and 5. The paper developed a theoretical advancement for achieving objecitve 6. In paper #1, we unify all the mainstream analyses for fluid models of many-server systems with general service and patience time distribution. In particular, due to the generality of our theoretical framework, we are able to extend the analysis to allow time varying arrivals. Papers #3 and #7 developed nice policies for handling multi-class customers in a many-server queueing setting by theoretically analyzing the asymptotic behavior of fluid models for many-server queues. The analytical framework we developed is both mature in theory and applications. In this way, we have achieved objective 7. Move over, to demonstrate the applicability of our method, we also apply our analytical framework to supply chain and inventory in papers #5 and #6, respectively. Paper #5 studied and extended model online demand fulfillment in a class of networks with limited flexibility. Paper #6 developed a novel policy to manage perishable inventory, again a high-dimensional dynamic programming problem. Moreover, paper #4 developed a dynamic policy for controlling a state-dependent processing-sharing service system whose performance depends on the number of customers it serves. In this way, we have enhanced the achievement of objectives 3, 4, and 6. Achieving the objectives was not an easy task. It took tremendous effort from myself and several of my PhD students. All of them have already graduated. One became an assistant professor at Nanjing University School of Business upon completing a post-doc with me, one became an assistant professor at the School of Data Science at CUHK(Shenzhen), one become an assistant professor in Fudan University after a year of post-doc at Columbia University. Another PdD student got a nice job offer from Alibaba, working on supply chain projects which share the similar theoretical challenges, and one got a job offer from Huawei Consumer Business Group. The papers produced in this project were much improved by hiring research assistants and communicating with top researchers in the field. The grant allowed me to have English editors improve the exposition of all my papers. The travels made possible by this grant also enable me to collaborate extensively with my collaborators and consultant around the world, and present the research outcomes in major conferences and workshops.

16201417.label: Major findings and research outcome
16201417.value: This project lead to significant development in both theory and application. Papers 1, 2, and 4 developed a framework and necessary theory to support it. All papers are motivated by practical applications such as service centers, and applied the framework to obtain insightful results as well as practically implantable near-optimal policies. The major findings of this project are as follows: Paper #1 unify two mainstream methods of analyzing fluid models, and even extend such analysis to allow time-varying input. Paper #3 provide a theoretical framework for optimal control with Brownian input. Paper #3 and #7 provide a effective and easy-to-implement policies for solving the routing and staffing of a multi-class service networks with different customer classes. Paper #4 studies approximations and control of a processor sharing (PS) server where the service rate depends on the number of jobs occupying the server. Paper #5 extend a well know nice property from the classical long chain model to more general network structure. It shows that a little bit flexibility goes a long way. Paper #6 design a simple policy for managing perishable inventory and prove its asymptotic optimality when the size of the system becomes large.

16201417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16201417.value: In this project, we have solved several major research challenges completely. For example, we develop a theoretical framework to analyze stochastic control with high-dimensional system states. We also applied our method to several models that are widely used in many real applications. In this way, there should not be much left to do in the scope of proposed research. This project has excellent potential for future research in applications. We only demonstrate the application of the theory we develop in a number of applications in manufacturing, service and inventory. However, there shall be many more models motivated by other applications, such as those in sharing economy, which shares a similar intricacy and challenge. For example, ride hailing such as Didi and Uber (or more general business models in the emerging sharing economy such as bike sharing), systems can be modeled as a multi-server system with high dimensional system states. The method we develop can be applied or at least shed some light in terms of how to solve if not directly applicable.

16201417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16201417.value: This project demonstrated both theoretical and application significance. On the theoretical side, we advanced the state of art of analyzing the difficult yet widely used Brownian control problem with high-dimensional system states. We are also able to extend our study to multi-server queueing network models by developing a framework for both fluid and diffusion approximations. We demonstrate the applicability of our theoretical analysis by solving challenging problems motivated by real applications in emerging areas. Many of these models are new in the research literature and have their distinctive features, necessitating the development of new methods. Beyond the development of new methods, we have obtained operational insights into many real applications. For example, we propose easy-to-implement and optimal staffing and control policies for service centers with multiple customer classes, an important application in modern society. The Brownian control problem with lead time is motivated by the real challenge in modern manufacturing, which allows deep customization while ordering. The online fulfillment paper demonstrates that a little of flexibility goes a long way for manufacturing and supply chain models.

16202217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16202217.value: Securing safe potable water to protect public health from exposure to contaminants is always one of the most important tasks in sustaining societal development. The task is however becoming more difficult to accomplish due to water shortage and its continuing quality deterioration. This highlights the increasing need in using less pristine water and even reclaimed water containing recalcitrant emerging micropollutants as the source. This challenge demands advanced treatment for the abatement of the contaminants. UV-based advanced oxidation processes (AOPs), which rely on photolysis of precursor oxidants such as peroxide and chlorine using conventional mercury UV lamps to produce highly reactive radical species, have passed several tests and pilot trials along with implementation of the UV/peroxide AOPs in real-world practice. However, the conventional lamps have short lifetimes and low energy efficiencies, contain toxic mercury, and are fragile and oversized. UV light emitting diodes (UV-LEDs), which are mercury-free sources of monochromatic UV radiation, are potential alternatives and regarded as the most promising UV light source. UV-LEDs are robust, compact and instant on-and-off. By 2020, the wall plug efficiency and lifetimes of UV-LEDs are predicted to increase to more than 75% and 20,000 hours, respectively, with a price drop of 40%. More interestingly, UV-LEDs provide versatility in emitting light at any designated wavelength. The versatility facilitates easy matching of their emission spectra with the absorption and/or quantum yield maxima of any specific precursor oxidant/pollutant to enhance its photo-reaction. However, the fundamentals of this wavelength overlap phenomenon have not yet been established. Moreover, the achievable wall plug efficacy of UV-LEDs decreases significantly with decreasing wavelengths. Thus, despite the eventual UV-LED dominance as the primary light source in all UV processes, coping with these inherent reduced efficiencies at low wavelengths requires a timely buildup of fundamental knowledge necessary for the design, selection and operation of UV-LED-driven AOPs. In this project, we intend to establish the fundamentals of the UV-LED/chlor(am)ine AOPs with emphases on wavelength-dependent chlor(am)ine photolysis and its effects on radical/ozone yields and degradation of selected micropollutants. These fundamentals, consolidated together the impacts of different aqueous constituents on the AOPs, will be used to investigate and demonstrate two realistic application cases: direct potable water reuse and drinking water treatment. A critical understanding of the wavelength-dependent radical/ozone concentration profiles and subsequent pollutant degradation efficiencies will allow recommendation of strategies to maximize UV-LED/chlor(am)ine AOPs in safeguarding potable water. 為保護公眾健康免受污染物的影响，保護飲用水水質安全始終是維護社會發展最重要的任務之一。然而，由於水源短缺和持續的水質惡化，這項工作變得越來越難。這使得減少使用原始水源，甚至使用含有難降解新興微量污染物的回用水的需求正在日益增加。這個挑戰促使我們開發先進的處理技術來降解污染物。基於紫外線的高級氧化工藝，主要依靠使用傳統汞紫外燈照射前體氧化劑（如過氧化氫和氯）， 產生高活性的自由基，去降解污染物。這些工藝已經通過了多項測試和試點試驗，其中紫外／過氧化氫高級氧化工藝更是在現實生活中得以應用。然而，傳統的紫外燈具有壽命短，能源效率低，含有毒性汞，易碎且尺寸過大等問題。紫外發光二極管是無汞源的單色紫外線輻射裝置，是傳統紫外燈的潛在替代品，並被認為是最有希望的紫外線光源。 紫外發光二極管具有耐用，尺寸小並可以即時開關等特點。截止到2020年，紫外發光二極管的能源轉化效率和壽命預計會分別增加75％和達到20,000小時，同時價格將會下降40％。更有趣的是，紫外發光二極管可以在任何指定的波長下發光。這可以實現紫外發光二極管的發射光譜與任何特定前體氧化劑或污染物的吸收光譜或量子產率最大值之間的簡單匹配，以增強光反應的效率。然而，這種光譜重疊現象的基本原理尚未建立。此外，紫外發光二極管的能源轉化效率會隨著波長的減小而顯著降低。因此，儘管所有基於紫外線的工藝最終都將會以紫外發光二極管作為主要光源，但是對於其固有的低波長下低效率的特點，我們有必要了解掌握更多的基本原理，以供於指導紫外發光二極管驅動的高級氧化工藝的設計，選擇和運行。在本項目中，我們打算開發一種新的紫外發光二極管／氯（或氯胺）的工藝，並著重研究紫外光的波長是如何影響 氯或氯胺的光解，自由基或臭氧的生成，以及對所選擇的微量污染物的降解。這些即將建立的基本原理，連同對於水中各種常見組分如何影響高級氧化工藝的研究結果，將會在兩個現實的案例中得以應用：直接飲用水再利用和常規飲用水處理。對於波長影響的自由基/臭氧濃度分佈和污染物降解效率的關鍵理解，將會對如何最大限度地發揮紫外發光二極管／氯（或氯胺）工藝的效率和保護飲用水水質安全提出寶貴建議。

16202217.label: Realisation of objectives
16202217.value: Objective 1 of this project was completed. Tests were designed to investigate the wavelength- and pH-dependency on chlor(am)ine photolysis and subsequent radical formation. Briefly, a testing solution of 5-mL was buffered at a particular pH, spiked with sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl) or monochloramine (NH2Cl) or dichloramine (NHCl2) stock solution to give an initial chlor(am)ine concentration of 100 µM, and then exposed to monochromatic UV-LED light at one of the fice wavelengths (255, 265, 285, 300, and 365 nm) each time. Samples were collected at pre-determined time intervals and subjected to the measurement of residual chlor(am)ine concentrations. Tests were also conducted in a similar manner with 10-µM nitrobenzene, benzoic acid, and 1,4-dimethoxybenzene coexisting as probing compounds to investigate the wavelength-dependency on radical generation from chlor(am)ine photolysis. It was found that the photodecay rates of free chlorine, monochloramine, and dichloramine were highly wavelength-dependent, mainly due to the wavelength-dependent molar absorption coefficients, instead of the apparent and innate quantum yields. A model that incorporated the chlor(am)ine photodecay rate constants, quantum yields, and molar absorption coefficients was established, validated, and then used to predict the chlor(am)ine photodecay rate at any wavelength (255–365 nm) and pH (5–10). The model can be used to well describe the wavelength- and concentration-dependency of chlor(am)ine photolysis. The findings provide the fundamental information in selecting UV-LEDs with specific wavelength for enhancing/optimizing chlor(am)ine photodecay and/or its radical generation at different pHs in real-world applications. Two journal papers summarizing the results of chlorine and chloramine photolysis have been published in Water Research in 2018 and Environmental Science and Technology in 2020, respectively. The wavelength-dependency on chlor(am)ine photolysis, along with the fundamentals and applications of UV-LEDs in water treatment, have also been reviewed and published in the IUVA News in 2018. The major findings relevant to this objective have been formulated to one conference paper and presented at the IWA LET Conference in May 2018. Objective 2 was completed. Tests were conducted to investigate the degradation kinetics and mechanisms of different micropollutants (nitrobenzene, carbamazepine, benzoic acid, 1,4-dimethoxybenzene, caffeine, bisphenol A, and diclofenac) in the UV-LED/chlor(am)ine process. Briefly, a 100 µM-chlor(am)ine-containing testing solution of 5-mL was buffered at a particular pH, spiked with one of the seven micropollutants at an initial concentration of 5 µM, and then exposed to monochromatic UV-LED light at one of the five wavelengths each time. Samples were collected at pre-determined time intervals, quenched and subjected to the measurement of residual micropollutant concentrations. The experimental results suggested that the degradation of the micropollutant depended on the structure of the micropollutants. For example, the degradation of bisphenol A was dominantly contributed by chlorination, while that of diclofenac was majorly contributed by direct UV photolysis at 285 nm. The degradation of other micropollutants was mainly contributed by radicals that were generated from chlor(am)ine photolysis, e.g., nitrobenzene degradation was solely contributed by hydroxyl radicals, and the degradation of benzoic acid, carbamazepine, 1,4-dimethoxybenzene, and caffeine was mainly due to the reactive chlorine species. The micropollutant degradation was also found to be highly wavelength- and pH-dependent, because the UV absorption of the micropollutants and chlor(am)ine are both wavelength-dependent, and pH affected the speciation of chlor(am)ine as well as the radical concentrations. The findings have been formulated to a journal paper published in Water Research in 2020. The findings were also summarized in four conference papers and presented at the IWA 11th Micropol & Ecohazard Conference in October 2019, the 2nd International Institute of Environmental Science (IIES) Graduate Students Forum in November 2018, the 4th National Conference on Water Treatment and Reuse of China in August 2020, and the IWA Digital World Water Congress in May 2021. Objective 3 was completed. Tests were designed and conducted to investigate the degradation kinetics of the selected micropollutants in real drinking water (e.g., tap water) and RO permeate (e.g., real wastewater secondary effluent polished by lab-scale microfiltration plus RO), in order to evaluate the potentials of UV-LED/chlor(am)ine AOP for drinking water treatment and potable water reuse. Compared to that in the synthetic water, the degradation of the tested micropollutants were inhibited to some extents in the tap water, due to the radical scavenging of the water matrix components (e.g., dissolved organic matter, bicarbonate and chloride etc.). In RO permeate, the degradation of nitrobenzene was enhanced, which was mainly due to the higher hydroxyl radical concentration at lower pH (pH shifted from 7.5 to 6.5 after RO). The degradation of other micropollutants was hindered due to the reduced RCS concentrations and radical scavenging. As a comparison, the fate of micropollutants in the LPUV-driven UV/chlorine AOP was also studied, and the findings were summarized to a journal paper published in Environmental Science: Water Research & Technology in 2018 and a conference paper presented at the 4th International Forum on Asian Water Environment Technology in December 2021. Tests were also conducted to evaluate the byproduct formation from the NOM-containing water after the treatment of UV-LED/chlor(am)ine AOP. Compared to chlor(am)ination alone, higher concentrations of the known DBPs (i.e., volatile DBPs and HAAs) and total organic chlorine (TOCl) were formed in the UV-LED/chlor(am)ine process at the five tested wavelengths and three pHs (i.e., pH 6, 7 and 8) in the synthetic drinking water containing NOM. TOCl formation was positively correlated with the decrease of the aromaticity and humic acid-like moieties of NOM. Cl• was found to contribute more significantly than HO• on the changes to NOM spectroscopic properties as well as on the TOCl formation. The findings were summarized in a conference paper and presented at the IWA 2nd Disinfection and Disinfection By-products Conference in May 2018. It was also found that the by-product formation was reduced and the degradation of micropollutants was enhanced simultaneously by adding persulfate into the UV-LED/chlorine AOP, which was mainly due to the transformation of halogen radicals (e.g., RCS) to non-halogen radicals (e.g., hydroxyl radicals and sulfate radicals) by adding persulfate. The findings have been formulated to a conference paper and presented in the IUVA World Congress in Feb 2019. The established fundamentals of UV-LED-based chlor(am)ine photolysis were also extended and applied in understanding the photochemistry of UV-LED photolysis of chlorine dioxide. It was found that compared to the well-documented UVC254/chlorine AOP, the UVA365/ClO2 AOP produced similar levels of reactive species at similar oxidant dosages but was much less pH-dependent and required much lower energy input, with much lower formation of chloro-organic byproducts and marginal formation of chlorite and chlorate. The findings were formulated to a journal paper published in Environmental Science and Technology in 2022 and a conference paper presented at the IUVA Americas Conference in March 2020.

16202217.label: Major findings and research outcome
16202217.value: The fundamentals of UV-LED-based chlor(am)ine photolysis and reactive species formation were established and applied to optimize the micropollutant degradation by the UV-LED-driven AOPs. The photodecay rates of chlor(am)ines were highly wavelength-dependent, mainly due to the wavelength-dependent molar absorption coefficients, instead of the apparent and innate quantum yields (Journal papers #1, #3 and #4). A model that incorporated the chlor(am)ine photodecay rate constants, quantum yields, and molar absorption coefficients to predict the chlor(am)ine photodecay rate at any wavelength and pH was established and validated (Conference paper #2). The research enables selecting UV-LEDs with specific wavelength for enhancing/optimizing chlor(am)ine photodecay and/or its radical generation in real-world applications (Conference paper #4 and #7). The pathways responsible for degradation of selected emerging micropollutants in the UV-LED/chlor(am)ine AOPs at different wavelengths were disclosed and the wavelength-dependent structure-reactivity correlations were established. The degradation highly depended on the structure of the micropollutants, the UV wavelength and the pH (Journal paper #5), because the UV absorption of the micropollutants and chlor(am)ine are structure-, wavelength-, and pH-dependent (Conference paper #5 and #8). The mechanisms of byproduct formation in the UV-LED/chlor(am)ine AOPs were elucidated. Cl• was found to contribute more significantly than HO• on the changes to NOM spectroscopic properties as well as TOCl formation (Conference paper #1). The byproduct formation was reduced and the degradation of micropollutants was enhanced by adding persulfate into the UV-LED/chlor(am)ine AOPs, by transformating halogen radicals to hydroxyl radicals and sulfate radicals (Conference paper #3). The fundemanls were extended to two applications: direct potable water reuse and drinking water treatment. UV light at longer wavelength is more suitable for photo-dechlor(am)ination of chlorine in swimming pools and pollutant degradation by the UV/chlorine AOP at neutral and alkaline pH. The UV light at shorter wavelength is more suitable for the chlorine photodecay and micropollutant degradation by the UV/chlorine AOP at acidic pH (e.g., RO permeate) (Journal paper #2). The UV-LEDs at longer wavelengths appear to represent promising alternatives to conventional mercury lamps for photodegradation NHCl2 and initiating NHCl2/UV AOPs (Conference paper #9). It was also found that compared to the UVC254/chlorine AOP, the UVA365/ClO2 AOP produced similar levels of reactive species at similar oxidant dosages but was much less pH-dependent and required much lower energy input, with much lower formation of chloro-organic byproducts and marginal formation of chlorite and chlorate (Journal paper #6 and Conference paper #6). One Ph.D. student was trained.

16202217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16202217.value: In this project, we observed that amino radicals generated from chloramine photolysis are less reactive than HO•/RCS toward micropollutants, but they can react with dissolved oxygen to form other reactive nitrogen species (e.g., NO• and NO2•). Moreover, the formation of nitrogenous byproducts is of particular concern. Futher investigation can be conducted to disclose the roles of different reactive nitrogen species on micropollutant degradation and byproduct formation. This study established cutting-edge techniques to modeling the photodecay rates and radical genenration from chlor(am)ine photolysis at different UV wavelengths and pHs. These approaches can be applied to illustrate how advanced treatment processes, not limited to the UV/chlor(am)ine AOP, generate reactive species under different operational conditions. Considering that UVA radiation sources (e.g., UVA-LEDs) are of high energy efficiency, the UVA/ClO2 AOP is practically promising for micropollutant abatement in water and wastewater treatment. We will seek for additional funding opportunities to better understand the UVA/ClO2 AOP and explore its potential applications.

16202217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16202217.value: The effective control of micropollutants is rapidly becoming a key priority in securing safe potable water. UV-based advanced oxidation process (AOP) are effective in micropollutant abatement but their real-world applications are limited by the intrinsic disadvantages of conventional UV lamps. In this study, we proposed to use the next-generation UV radiation sources (UV-LEDs) to drive the highly efficient UV/chlor(am)ine AOPs for micropollutant abatement in drinking water treatment and potable water reuse. We determined the chlor(am)ine photodecay rates and radical concentrations generated under different UV wavelength and pH conditions. We used the experimentally collected data to establish mathematical models to predict the chlor(am)ine photodecay rate and radical generation at any other untested wavelengths and pHs. The findings provide the fundamental information in selecting UV-LEDs with specific wavelength for enhancing and optimizing chlor(am)ine photodecay and its radical generation in the treatment of micropollutants in drinking water, swimming pool water, and reclaimed water. We also investigated and disclosed how the micropollutants with different chemical structures were degraded by the UV-LED/chlor(am)ine AOPs at different wavelengths, whether and how the byproducts were formed during the micropollutant degradation, and how to effectively control the undesired byproducts in real engineering applications.

16202317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16202317.value: The external memory (EM) model had been the dominating computation model for massive data until the late 2000's. It models the situation where data cannot fit into internal memory, thus has to reside in external memory (hard disks). As technology advances, the current trend is to use a cluster of interconnected machines with sufficient main memory combined, so that computation would not have to rely on rotating hard disks, which are mechanical devices that are inherently slow. This has led to many people into claiming that EM algorithms are no longer relevant. Recently, Koutris et al. proved a simulation result that any BSP algorithm (BSP is a computation model that abstracts main memory based cluster computing) can be simulated by the EM model. This is an interesting result, but not very useful as we know much more about EM than the BSP. In this project, we plan to investigate the inverse simulation and convert existing EM algorithms to the BSP. If this project is successful, we will be able to re-utilize the 30 years' research efforts on EM algorithms in today's main memory computing systems, at least in principle. 外存计算模型直到2000年前都是海量数据计算的主导计算理论模型。然而，随着技术进步，如今的海量计算更加经常的是在一个计算机集群上进行。一个集群经常有上百台机器，其内存总量超过数据总量，使得外存不在被需要。这令很多人认为外存计算模型将不再相关。 最近，Koutris等人发现任何一个BSP算法(BSP是集群计算的一个理论模型)可以转换为一个外存算法。这是一个很有意思的结果，可是并没有太多的实际价值，因为我们对于外存算法的认识要远远超过BSP算法，而且将来更有实际价值的BSP算法。在此项目中，我们计划研究如何将外存算法转化为BSP算法，这一结果会让我们对外存算法30年的研究结果重新利用起来。

16202317.label: Realisation of objectives
16202317.value: 1. We have extended the external memory model into a parallel version, and have studied its relationship with the BSP model, which is a popular model for handling massive datasets in parallel. Through this investigation, we have developed many general techniques and tools for converting EM algorithms to the BSP model. 2. We have successfully developed BSP algorithms for three broad classes of problems using techniques designed above: (1) We have developed a BSP algorithm for processing similarity joins. (2) We have developed a sparse matrix multiplication algorithm, and have generalized it to handle join-aggregate queries in the BSP model. (3) We have developed distributed/parallel query evaluation algorithms under the multi-party secure computation model, which can be considered as a secure version of the BSP model.

16202317.label: Major findings and research outcome
16202317.value: By exploiting the relationship between the external memory model and the BSP model, we have achieved the following research findings: (1) We have developed a sparse matrix multiplication algorithm, and have generalized it to handle join-aggregate queries in the BSP model. The importance of matrix multiplication is without double, while join-aggregate queries are very commonly seen in many complicated analytical queries. The new algorithms allow us to process these queries more efficiently in a BSP system. The paper has been published in PODS 2020. (2) We have further considered a secure version of the BSP, where the communication between parties go through insecure channels. We have developed query evaluation algorithms in this model for a broad class of queries. The paper has been published in SIGMOD 2020.

16202317.value: Some of the results above (e.g., (2)) are only theoretical. We plan to investigate their practicality in the future.

16202317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16202317.value: The external memory (EM) model had been the dominating computation model for massive data until the late 2000's. It models the situation where data cannot fit into internal memory, thus has to reside in external memory (hard disks). As technology advances, the current trend is to use a cluster of interconnected machines with sufficient main memory combined, so that computation would not have to rely on rotating hard disks, which are mechanical devices that are inherently slow. This has led to many people into claiming that EM algorithms are no longer relevant. In this project, we have investigated the relationship between the EM model and the BSP model, and have been able to convert many EM algorithms to the BSP model, so that they still work well in today's main memory computing systems.

16202517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16202517.value: A thermal diode is a device in which thermal transport along a specific axis depends on the sign of the temperature gradient or heat current. They are of interest due to their extensive applications in solar-thermal systems, micro/nano-electronic cooling, energy saving for buildings, etc. However, one drawback of the thermal diode, to be addressed in order to be practically useful for most engineering systems, is its low value of diodicity. This proposed study will aim to enhance the diodicity of thermal diodes by improving the forward thermal conductivity using both nanofluids and electrostatic effects and reducing the reverse thermal conductivity using electrostatic effects. Some prior studies have shown that a thin coating-layer formed by nanoparticles suspended in a nanofluid has a key effect on the thermal enhancement for diode heat pipes. On average, thermal performance enhancement can reach 50% using nanofluids in heat pipes due to the improvement in surface wettability and a reduction in thermal resistance. Additionally, an electrostatic field not only can increase the jumping height of coalescing droplets (i.e. creating a larger vapor space), but also enhance the heat transfer capability during condensation/evaporation. Our preliminary results show that the forward and reverse thermal conductivity of a thermal diode can be enhanced and reduced by 180% and 70% respectively when the vapor space is increased from 1.5 mm to 7.5 mm, leading to an 830% enhancement in diodicity compared to the case without the electrostatic effect. However, a number of academic challenges need to be addressed since the influence of electrostatic charging on coalescence-induced jumping droplets has been rarely studied, and the physical phenomenon regarding the enhancement in diodicity by applying the electrostatic effects is unclear. This study will develop two mathematical models and verified them by experiment. The first model will represent the effect of electrostatic charge on the jumping height of coalescing droplets; the second will predict the forward and reverse thermal conductivity of a thermal diode using nanofluids and the electrostatic effects. Based on the models, the electrostatic-assisted and nanofluid-based phase change thermal diode will be designed, built and experimentally tested. Finally, a novel solar-thermal power system using the developed thermal diode will be fabricated and its energy efficiency will be examined. This research will not only reveal the impact of an electrostatic field on coalescence-induced jumping droplets and the related thermal characteristics of thermal diodes, but also steer new development of solar-thermal power systems.

16202517.label: Realisation of objectives
16202517.value: To achieve Objective 1 a comprehensive study of jumping water droplets on superhydrophobic surfaces with electric fields has been conducted experimentally and theoretically. The jumping dynamic of the water droplet was recorded by an experimental setup which consisted of a superhydrophobic plate, copper plate, positive electrode, negative electrode, etc. The jumping height and jumping angle, were also observed in the experiment. For the jumping dynamic of the droplet, it is found that when the electrical charge approaches its threshold value, the droplet is slightly elongated and starts to form an elliptical shape, showing a tendency to depart from the surface even though the bottom of the droplet is pinned down to the surface. Besides, a theoretical model has also been developed to investigate different forces of the droplet, namely, gravitation force, inertia, electrostatic force and drag force with different droplet sizes. The computed forces are compared to the forces found in the experiment and the simulated results are consistent with the experimental results. Last, the jumping height with different droplet sizes can be used to develop a heat transfer model to evaluate the forward and reverse thermal conductivities of the thermal diode at the next Objective. For Objective 2, a heat transfer model has been developed first using the idea of the thermal circuit. In the forward mode of the thermal diode, the conductive, convective, and droplet heat transfers are mainly considered to form thermal resistances, while in the reverse mode, the conductive heat transfer is the major contributor to the thermal resistance. The forward and reverse effective thermal conductivities of the thermal diode are then computed at different hot side temperatures of the thermal diode. Next, a thermal diode was fabricated and the experiments were conducted under different conditions to measure the forward and reverse effective thermal conductivities of the thermal diode to verify the model. The numerical and experimental results of the effective thermal conductivity of the thermal diode are well-matched. It is found that when the hot side temperature of the thermal diode increases, the effective thermal conductivity in the forward mode of the thermal diode is also increased due to the enhanced buoyancy effects in the fluid and gas regions. Next, the thermal rectification ratio of the thermal diode is determined, and it is defined as the ratio of the difference between the forward and reverse effective thermal conductivities to the reverse effective thermal conductivity of the thermal diode. It is found that the thermal rectification ratio of the thermal diode increases with an increase of the hot side temperature of the thermal diode, with a thermal rectification ratio of 0.8 at 45 ºC of the hot side temperature, reaching 1.4 at 70 ºC of the hot side temperature. Regarding the thermal conductivity using different nanofluids, an investigation of various hybrid nanofluids has also been conducted experimentally and theoretically. The hybrid nanofluids, including Cu-Al2O3 with different mixing ratios were prepared and their thermal conductivities with different concentration of the nanoparticles were predicted by the developed model. It should be noted that the effective thermal conductivity of hybrid nanofluids increases linearly with the suspended particle concentration, and most importantly, it can be well-estimated by the model. The effective thermal conductivity, density and specific heat capacity of the hybrid nanofluids changing along with time were also investigated. For Objective 3, the optimized electrostatic-assisted and nanofluid-based phase change thermal diode was fabricated with the thermal diode consististing of a heat source, a nanostructured superhydrophilic surface, a nanostructured superhydrophobic surface, a heat sink and gaskets as the thermal insulation between the nanostructured superhydrophilic surface and the nanostructured superhydrophobic surface. The effective thermal conductivities of the thermal diode in the forward mode and the reverse mode under different electric voltages (0, 25 V and 50 V) and orientations (gravitational and anti-gravitational) were examined. In the anti-gravitational direction, the effective thermal conductivity decreased with an increase in the hot-side temperature. For the gravitational direction, the effective thermal conductivity increased with an increase in the temperature of the heat source. In the reverse mode, the electric field did not influence the performance of the phase-change thermal diode because the heat transfer occurred through thermal conduction at the copper plates and the gasket. It is found that the effective thermal conductivity in the reverse mode slightly increases with an increase in the hot-side temperature and the average effective thermal conductivity in the reverse mode is 0.063 W/m-K. Also, the estimated average effective thermal conductivity in the reverse mode is approximately 0.072 W/m-K, which is in line with the experimental results. Regarding the thermal rectification ratio, it is found that the thermal rectification ratio of the thermal diode increases with an increase in temperature difference at the hot side and cold side of the thermal diode, and the thermal rectification increases with the electric field. The maximum thermal rectification ratio of the thermal diode in the gravitational direction is 375 at the temperature difference of 8 ºC and at the electrical voltage of 50 V. It should be noted that the thermal rectification ratio of the thermal diode outperforms the counterparts in the literature where the thermal rectification ratio usually ranges from 1 to 250. Objective 4 is to study the feasibility and to test the energy efficiency of some potential applications using the thermal diode. This is achieved by determining the cooling performance and energy efficiency of a solar powered adsorption cooling system equipped with the thermal diode. Specifically, an experiment to measure the water condensation of different surfaces, including the nanostructured superhydrophilic surface, the nanostructured superhydrophilic–zeolite 13X adsorbent composite surface, the nanostructured superhydrophobic surface, the superhydrophobic–zeolite 13X adsorbent surface and plain copper surface, in the thermal diode used for adsorption cooling systems was conducted in an environmental chamber controlling different humidity levels. The results show that the condensation rate increased as the surface temperature of the thermal diode decreased. The condensation rate of the superhydrophobic–zeolite 13X adsorbent surface was found to be the largest, followed by the nanostructured superhydrophilic–zeolite 13X adsorbent composite surface, the nanostructured superhydrophobic surface, the nanostructured superhydrophilic surface and the plain copper surface. Next, a theoretical model considering the heat and mass transfer in different parts of the solar powered adsorption cooling system was developed that incorporated thermal diodes with the superhydrophobic–zeolite 13X adsorbent surface. Subsequently, experiments were conducted to investigate the coefficient of performance (COP) and specific cooling power (SCP) of the adsorption cooling system with the thermal diode, and the results were used to verify the developed theoretical model. The developed model was also employed to study the COP and SCP of the solar powered adsorption cooling system under different operational conditions. The optimized hot water inlet temperature, cooling water inlet temperature and adsorption/desorption phase time are 90 ºC, 13 ºC, and 600 s. It was found that after using the thermal diode utilizing the superhydrophobic–zeolite 13X adsorbent surface in the condenser of the solar-assisted adsorption cooling system in the optimized condition, an estimated SCP of 231.4 W/kg and COP of 0.317 were achieved, showing an improvement of 25% and 10%, respectively, compared with that of the solar powered adsorption cooling system using the thermal diode without any treatment.

16202517.label: Major findings and research outcome
16202517.value: A mathematical model describing the electrostatic charging of coalescing droplets jumping from a superhydrophobic surface was developed. The model considered the effect of the charge on the jumping height [Item 2 in table in Part C], and experiments to study the jumping height of the electrostatic charged coalescing droplets were also conducted. The experimental results were used to verify the model. The study found that the electric field can enhance the jumping height due to a significant increase in the electrostatic force. With the electric field applied, the maximum jumping height is over three times higher than those without using the electric field [Item 3 in table in Part C]. Subsequently, a heat transfer model to estimate the forward and reverse thermal conductivities of the electrostatic-assisted and nanofluid-based phase change thermal diode was developed. The nanoparticle concentration, vapor space, electric field, etc. were taken into account in the heat transfer model. A thermal diode was also built and the experiment to study the effective thermal conductivity of the thermal diode was conducted to verify the heat transfer model. It is found that the effective thermal conductivity of the nanofluid increased with the particle concentration [Items 7 and 8 in table in Part C] and the effective thermal conductivity of the thermal diode increased with the water to air volume ratio [Item 9 in table in Part C]. After that, the thermal diode was then optimized using the developed models. The optimized thermal diode was then fabricated and tested experimentally under different conditions, such as various thermal diode orientations. The results showed that in the forward mode of the thermal diode, the effective thermal conductivity was enhanced as the temperature difference between the hot side and cold side of the thermal diode increased. Besides, a larger electric field applied to the thermal diode can result in a higher effective thermal conductivity. In the reverse mode of the thermal diode, there was insignificant change in the effective thermal conductivity under different conditions, such as electric field [Item 6 in table in Part C]. Finally, the thermal diode was integrated to a solar powered adsorption cooling system and the feasibility of using the thermal diode in the adsorption cooling system was studied. It was found that the coefficient of performance of the adsorption cooling system with the thermal diode can be enhanced by about 10% [Item 4 in table in Part C].

16202517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16202517.value: In the project, a heat transfer model to estimate the forward and reverse thermal conductivities of an electrostatic-assisted and nanofluid-based phase change thermal diode was developed and the effective thermal conductivity of the thermal diode was studied experimentally. To further improve the effective thermal conductivity of the thermal diode, it is proposed to use hybrid nanofluid which is a blend of two kinds of nanoparticles in a base fluid that is expected to possess better effective thermal conductivity and stability, comparing to single nanofluid. However, the fundamental understanding of the hybrid nanofluid has not been well-studied, hindering its applications. Additionally, it is proposed that a biphilic surface (i.e. a new nanostructured surface) will be adopted in the thermal diode. The biphilic surface is a combination of a hydrophilic surface and a hydrophobic surface that can both increase the water condensation and jumping height of jumping droplets. Specifically, the biphilic surface used at the cold side of the thermal diode can improve its effective thermal conductivity and thermal rectification. However, the fundaments of the water jumping on a biphilic surface has not been well-studied, so this could be a future research direction in relation to the study of thermal diodes.

16202517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16202517.value: In this study, an electrostatic assisted and nanofluid-based thermal diode, which is a device with two terminals, allowing heat to flow in one direction and preventing heat flow in the other direction, has been designed, optimized and developed. A mathematical model to estimate the jumping height of water droplets and a heat transfer model to compute the effective thermal conductivity of the thermal diode have been established to optimize the thermal performance of the thermal diodes, including the designed parameters of the electric field strength, concentration of the nanofluid, temperature supply to the thermal diode, etc. Next, the optimized thermal diode was identified, then fabricated before completing the thermal performance test. The thermal rectification performance (i.e. 325) of the optimized thermal diode outperforms the counterparts in the literature (i.e. the thermal rectification from 1-250). Last, the optimized thermal diode was integrated with a solar powered cooling system for a feasibility study. The experimental result showed that the energy efficiency performance of the cooling system equipped with the optimized thermal diode was enhanced by at least 10% compared to the system without using the thermal diode. Overall, the proposed thermal diodes can effectively improve the thermal performance of different thermal systems.

16202917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16202917.value: Android是受歡迎的移動操作系統，支持數百萬個應用。然而，Android生態系統的沉重分裂引起了各種Android版本和設備之間應用程序兼容性的一些主要擔憂。在具有不兼容的Android版本或硬件驅動程序的設備上運行時，應用程序會出現意外的行為，甚至無法運行。為了解決這些兼容性問題，開發人員需要分析Android版本和設備型號的那些組合可能導致意外的行為並相應地自定義代碼。現有研究報告說，Android兼容性問題是普遍的：通常發現用戶評論抱怨應用程序在其設備上或系統更新後無效。造成這種現象的四個原因。首先，Android生態系統是分散的，使兼容性分析變得昂貴。在超過24,000個不同的設備型號上部署了超過50種Android版本，具有不同的硬件和驅動程序。兼容性問題可能來自於這些的任何組合，但在實踐中，開發人員只能靠這些組合的一小部分來測試他們的應用程序。第二，Android兼容性問題沒有很好的記錄。開發人員主要從經驗或非結構化的討論中了解問題。第三，隨著新的Android版本和設備型號的發布，新的問題不斷出現。很難通過不同的非結構化來源及時跟踪這些問題。最後，沒有相關的自動化工具。 我們建議使用大數據在三個維度上解決兼容性問題：問題表徵，知識庫構建和工具自動化。為了提高對兼容性問題的分散理解，我們將進行實證研究，以基於代碼存儲庫和2000多個開源Android應用程序的問題跟踪系統來表徵問題，構建兼容性問題的知識庫。由於這些問題隨著新版本的Android版本，庫和設備模型的發布而發生變化，因此我們可以通過使用人群數據開發代碼挖掘框架來自動識別新出現的問題，並根據需要更新知識庫。我們將開發自動化技術和工具，以幫助檢測和修補Android應用程序中的兼容性問題。我們將使用流行的真實世界的Android應用程序評估我們的方法。 Android應用開發是中國和香港信息產業的重要組成部分。本項目開發的知識庫和工具將提高開發人員的生產力。他們還將通過解決開發新產品時的兼容性問題來惠及移動設備供應商。

16202917.label: Realisation of objectives
16202917.value: We have fully achieved the three stated objectives by carrying out the following research activities. Objective 1: The heavily fragmented Android ecosystem has induced various compatibility issues in Android apps. We made empirical studies whether compatibilities issues arise from callback APIs in Android apps and how these apps respond to events induced by incompatible callback APIs. We examined Android documentations and conducted an empirical study on 100 real-world callback compatibility issues to investigate how these issues were induced by callback API evolutions. Based on our empirical findings, we have proposed a graph-based model to capture the control flow inconsistencies caused by API evolutions on how callback APIs are invoked in response to various events. We also extended our empirical studies to cover those hybrid Android apps with web browser capabilities. We found that the interaction between an app’s native code and web code induces new types of bugs, referred to as WebView-induced bugs, in Android apps. Our study identified new characteristics of these bugs. In addition, we also studied the issues induced by conflicts induced by the compatibilities across different versions of third-party libraries. Four patterns of such compatibilities were identified. These patterns allow for future systematic studies of such compatibilities. The above findings were disseminated at three top-tier research venues [Conference-3,4,5]. We followed up these findings with further real-world compatibility issues collected from five popular open-source Android apps. We interviewed Android practitioners and conducted an online survey to gain insights from real practices. We also made attempts to collect and analyze resource leakages occurring in Android apps since some of those leakages may arise from compatibilities across API levels and devices [Journal-2]. During the process of analyzing the root causes of compatibility issues, we often needed to locate from the old program versions the bug-inducing commits that introduced bugs repaired later by a fixing commit. We found that the process of locating bug-inducing commits has not been well-supported by existing methodologies. We conducted an exploratory study of the problem and disseminated our finding at a top-tier research venue [Conference-9]. Objective 2: We commenced our study to develop a framework after submission of proposal. We studied the high false positive rates of popular static analysis tools available in Android studio for the detection of software defects, including compatibility issues. A novel technique was developed to effectively reduce the false positive rates by augmenting the detected issues with user reviews and knowledge graph. We also developed techniques to further reduce false positive warnings based on failure clustering by means of crash points and crash origins. We developed a methodology to help developers locate their earlier code changes that are accountable for a given software issue. Automated detection techniques for compatibility issues arising from Android callback APIs and hybrid Android apps were developed. An automated technique was proposed to fix detected program issues. The results were disseminated at four top-tier research conferences [Conference-1,2,3,4]. We mined these issues by exploring the search space in three dimensions: device models, Android OS versions, and Android APIs. We will address two challenges. First, the issues arising from device models, evolve quickly with the frequent release of new device models to the market. Second, new issues are mostly undocumented. We developed a technique that automatically learns API-device correlations of FIC issues from existing Android apps. The technique extracts and prioritizes API-device correlations from a given corpus of Android apps. The result was disseminated at a top-tier research conference [Conference-1]. Besides Android apps, we also explored the detection of compatibility issues across Java projects [Conference-7], API libraries [Conference-8], and API documentation [Journal-1]. Objective 3: We implemented tool supports of our techniques and released our collected representative real-world Android applications as well as evaluation results to the public. The URLs of our publicly accessible project web sites were published. We evaluated our technique with large-scale open-source Android apps and evaluated if it can detect compatibility and uncover previously unknown issues.
