16202917.label: Major findings and research outcome
16202917.value: This project led to the training of 3 research students, publication of 12 top-tier research articles and 5 public project repositories at GitHub. The student, Ming Wen (2019 graduate), is an associate professor at Huazhong University of Science and Technology. Another student, Lili Wei (2020 graduate), is a postdoc supported by the RGC Postdoctoral Fellowship award. In recognition of her outstanding research, she received PhD fellowships from Google and Microsoft Research Asia. A feature interview of her by HKUST is available at https://seng.hkust.edu.hk/news/20191031/leveraging-computer-science-turn-imagination-reality. She will join McGill University as an assistant professor. The student, Hang Xu (2021 graduate), is a technical staff member at Tencent. The research artifact submitted to ICSE 2019 received the ACM SIGSOFT Distinguished Artifact award. We summarize major findings as follows. - Compatibility issues are not documented as the Android framework developers are likely unaware of them. These issues escape most of the unit tests. Another property of these issues is that they keep evolving. It means issues that have been detected in previous Android framework versions may no longer be applicable to the current or future Android framework versions. [Conference-2, 5] - API documentation are often outdated. The documentation may not accurately describe the behavior of the corresponding implementation. [Journal-1] - Compatibility issues can be broadly categorized into device non-specific and device specific. The former are issues that arise from the core Android framework components. They occur across different device models. It means that the fix to an issue can be applied to many device models. The latter are issues that arise from the components customized by Android device vendors. It means that the fix to an issue is applicable only to specific device models. [Conference-5] - The control flows of Android apps are largely driven by WebView and the protocols that govern how callback APIs are invoked in response to various events. These WebView and callback APIs evolve along with the Android framework, resulting in many compatibility issues. [Conference-2, 3] - Compatibility issues are often introduced by various vendors when they customize the Android implementation for their products. Such device specific issues are hard because most vendors do not publish such issues. App developers need to execute their applications on such device models to realize the issues. Motivated by the difficulties, we propose a mining technique to automatically extract the possible compatibility fixes from the latest obfuscated APK distribution of the close-source apps. These fixes are then be abstracted into common device specific compatibility patterns, which can then be applied to detect related compatibility issues in other apps. [Conference-6] - Many of the issues in Android apps result in resource leaks, which escape the code checking and testing by their developers. [Journal-2]

16202917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16202917.value: Android fragmentation is an outstanding problem intrinsic to the Android ecosystem. Our project laid the foundation work on the characterization and detection of the compatibility issues induced by Android fragmentation. This project mainly focused on the issues occurring at Java apps. Recently, apps are built using multiple platforms, including XML for graphical user interface rendering and WebView for web content rendering, in addition to Java. A promising extension of the work is to extend compatibility issues to apps built on top of multiple platforms. Another interesting direction is to explore the automation of repair for these issues. A major challenge is to work out the best repair strategy when multiple platforms are involved. Indeed, compatibility issues are not restricted to the Android ecosystem. We also found the issues are also pervasive in Java, Python, Go and Python ecosystems. A possible direction is to transfer the methodology developed in this project to the detection of compatibility issues in other ecosystems, including the emerging ones that support the development of artificial intelligence applications.

16202917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16202917.value: An Android app that works on a particular Android version and device model may no longer work when users deploy the app on another Android version or device model. This is because the support by the underlying Android framework varies across Android versions and device models. In most cases, app developers rarely have the resources to test their apps on all active Android versions and all major device models before releasing their apps. Indeed, such compatibility issues escape most unit tests and undocumented. In addition, they keep evolving as the upgrade of Android versions and device models. Addressing the compatibility issues is a well-known hard problem in the Android community. In this project, we conducted a systematic study, including interviews with experienced Android app developers, to characterize the form of these compatibility issues and the patterns by which the issues can be effectively detected. We developed the first benchmark dataset on Android compatibility issues and initiated five GitHub projects. The research findings were disseminated by 12 top-tier research articles. Three research students were trained.

16203317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16203317.value: 量子糾纏態曾被愛因斯坦描述為“幽靈般的超距作用”，是一個困擾科學家的抽象而又神秘的概念。儘管其本質仍撲朔迷離，實驗上卻證實並展示了量子糾纏態應用於量子隱形傳輸及量子計算，無論從速度還是保密度上都遠超傳統通信方式的巨大前景。而量子糾纏態的製備是實現量子通信的第一步。 許多微粒系統可用於實現糾纏態的製備，例如光子。研究者利用體光學非線性晶體成功製備出在偏振、路徑、時間等自由度糾纏的光子對，但體晶體的應用使得光學體系龐大而不穩定。在過去的十幾年裡，世界各地的研究組開始研發微米尺度的集成量子光學晶片，用於量子通信及量子資訊處理。集成量子光學平臺結構緊湊，與作為傳輸系統的光纖相容，且系統相對穩定。然而片上量子糾纏態的製備仍是個難題。 氮化矽（SiN）材料與成熟的互補金屬氧化物半導體（CMOS）納米製造工藝相容，是集成量子光學的潛在材料平臺。相較於矽材料，氮化矽具有較低的線性和非線性吸收。相較於二氧化矽，氮化矽有較高的折射率，能提供更好的光學限制和導波作用，並且具有更高的運用于自發四波混頻（SFWM）的三階非線性效應。許多研究組展示了氮化矽波導的超低光學損耗，並實現了高品質的應用於線性、非線性及量子光學中的氮化矽微腔。 在本項目的研究中，我們將充分利用CMOS相容的氮化矽材料平臺製備光子糾纏態。光子糾纏態在氮化矽諧振腔中通過自發四波混頻效應產生，產生的兩個光子態以不可分割的方式疊加。片上高效的偏振糾纏態光子製備依然是個技術難題。我們將研發低光學損耗、色散調控的氮化矽波導耦合微盤諧振腔，作為片上偏振及路徑糾纏態製備的基本結構單元。我們計畫進一步利用上述基本結構，實現同時在偏振和路徑自由度糾纏的多重光子糾纏態。

16203317.label: Realisation of objectives
16203317.value: We realized 70% of Objective 1. We experimentally demonstrated polarization-entanglement generation using integrated waveguides and whispering-gallery (WG) microring resonators on the Si3N4 platform. Our measurements revealed the generation of polarization-entangled photon-pairs with moderate visibilities of 65% ~ 84%. We also experimentally investigated path-entanglement generation using an WG microring resonator integrated with a waveguide-interferometer. Our experimental research work spanned the scope of (a) photonic device and circuit design, (b) theoretical and numerical modeling, (c) nanofabrication at the university’s cleanroom, (d) characterization of the heralded single-photon sources and (e) of the entangled photon-pairs by count-correlation measurements. However, as we have not succeeded in demonstrating path-entanglement, we have not attempted Objective 2 on hyper-entanglement, which imposes simultaneously realizing both polarization- and path-entanglement. Here, we highlight our key project achievements with a focus on realizing polarization-entanglement. We briefly discuss problems encountered with experimentally investigating path-entanglement and outline attempts implemented to address the problems. a. Photonic device and circuit design To generate polarization-entangled photon-pairs in an isotropic third-order nonlinear Si3N4 integrated photonic chip, we adopted our original proposed approach to generate by spontaneous four-wave-mixing (SFWM) photon-pairs that are colinearly polarized with the pump wave and are indistinguishable between two orthogonal polarization states. The generated polarization-entangled signal and idler photons are simultaneously transverse-electric (TE)- and transverse-magnetic (TM)-polarized. We note that in a single waveguide or resonator, the TE- and TM-polarized modes of the same mode order generally exhibit polarization-dependent waveguide group or effective refractive indices. The orthogonally polarized modes are generally distinguishable and thus do not enable polarization-entangled states. Except by attempting an ideal symmetric waveguide cross-section that supports degenerate orthogonally polarized modes, we believe it is not practical to generate in a single nonlinear waveguide or resonator nearly degenerate TE- and TM-polarized photon-pairs to enable polarization-entangled states. We circumvented such a fundamental constraint by waveguide-coupling two separately dispersion- and resonance-tailored (and actively fine-tuned) WG microring resonators. The two resonators exhibit nearly degenerate TE- and TM-polarized resonances (within the spectrally overlapping resonance linewidths) between the two resonators. We simultaneously pumped the two resonators at a nearly degenerate TE- and TM-polarized microring resonance wavelength by a 45o-linearly polarized laser. b. Theoretical and numerical modeling To generate SFWM in Si3N4 microring resonators, we require a waveguide cross-sectional design to attain near-zero (or slightly anomalous) dispersion to satisfy the phase-matching condition for efficient photon-pair generation. We numerically studied the waveguide dispersion of Si3N4 microring resonators by examining the waveguide height and width using the finite-element method. We adopted a 3.5µm-thick SiO2 under-cladding layer and a 1µm-thick SiO2 upper-cladding layer to provide good optical confinement. Our simulation results suggested that a Si3N4 film thickness exceeding 850 nm enables a near-zero or slightly anomalous dispersion with a pump wavelength around 1550 nm for both TE- and TM-polarized modes. A waveguide width of wider than 1.2 µm enables a slightly anomalous dispersion. c. Nanofabrication process developments We successfully developed a complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS)-compatible, wafer-scale subtractive fabrication process (see patent applications). We adopted a single-run low-pressure chemical vapor deposition to obtain Si3N4 films with a thickness of exceeding 850 nm. To avoid the stress-induced cracks in thick Si3N4 films (> 400 nm), we introduced a dense stress-release pattern on the under-cladding layer that helps release the stress and locally stops the propagation of the cracks (initiated from the wafer rim). d. Measuring heralded single-photon sources We first characterized the second-order correlation at a zero time-delay gH(2)(0) of heralded single-photons generated from the waveguide-coupled WG microring resonator upon various pump powers. Our measured gH(2)(0) for each pump power was below 0.087 indicating a good heralded single-photon source. To our knowledge, we demonstrated the lowest gH(2)(0) of 0.008 ± 0.003 in the Si3N4 photonic chip platform upon a pump power of ~ 0.47 mW. e. Measuring polarization-entangled photon-pairs To experimentally demonstrate the generation of polarization-entanglement, we must project the generated state to various polarization bases and measure the correlation between the two single photons. We first characterized the generated state in the TE and TM polarization bases. We observed coincidence counts with the two polarization analyzers set as both horizontal or both vertical polarizations while we observed no coincidence counts with the two analyzers set as one horizontal and the other vertical. We further verified the polarization-entanglement state by varying the angle of one analyzer while we fixed the other analyzer. The measured coincidence counts showed a theoretically expected sinusoidal variation with the polarization angle difference between the two single photons. Our measured visibilities were 65% ~ 84% reflecting a moderate purity of the polarization-entangled state. f. Problems encountered with experimentally investigating path-entanglement Path-entanglement requires the ambiguity of generating photon-pairs without the possibility of revealing the “which-path” information. Following our original proposal, we leveraged the same dispersion-engineered WG microring resonator and pumped simultaneously along clockwise (CW) and counter-clockwise (CCW) directions to generate photon-pairs in two indistinguishable paths. However, we have yet identified a fundamental mechanism that can generate a pure path-entangled state from the CW-CCW travelling photon-pairs. Despite this, we attempted initial designs essentially following our original proposal. The initial circuit designed for experimentally investigating path-entanglement comprised the path- entanglement source and an on-chip Mach-Zehnder interferometer with two long spiral waveguides integrated with a metal microheater for measuring the relative spatial phase angle between the path-entangled states. During the characterization, we further encountered the possible spontaneous Raman noise photons or extra photon-pairs generated along the long spiral waveguides. We also encountered fabrication issues with our metal deposition (sputtering) process, which did not yield a good enough metal surface. g. Attempts we implemented to address the problems To further explore the fundamental concept of generating path-entanglement on a chip, we are continuing to systematically characterize the generated output states from the single CW-CCW-pumped Si3N4 microring resonator and to investigate possible mechanisms to attain path-entanglement first by means of a free-space experimental setup for multiphoton interference. To minimize the spontaneously generated photon noise, we are optimizing the circuit design by integrating an on-chip wavelength-division-multiplexing filter circuit to reject the residual pump photons after the microring source. We also realized that we did not have enough control on-chip test patterns or interferometer circuits for design optimization and to experimentally test our hypothesis on fundamental mechanisms. The failure of fabricating an on-chip metal-based microheater also limited our experimental characterization of the spatial phase angle. We are currently redesigning a photomask with new circuit designs and control patterns addressing the aforementioned issues.

The generated polarization-entangled state exhibits a moderate visibility of 65% ~ 84%. 2. 16203317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16203317.value: Beside the on-going attempts to address the problems encountered, we will continue to explore characterization methods to fully characterize the polarization-entangled states unfolding their polarization states and relative phase angles. We will enhance our quantum measurement setup by stabilizing the pump laser amplitude and phase using a free-space Pound-Drever-Hall locking scheme. We will also optimize the collection efficiencies of the generated signal and idler photons. We will be more ready to experimentally investigate the originally proposed hyper-entanglement upon further addressing the fundamental mechanisms and characterizations of both the polarization- and path-entanglement on a chip. The realization of hyper-entanglement on a chip, along with further manipulation of multiphoton interference on or off a chip, will pave the way towards various quantum technologies including quantum metrology and sensing.

16203317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16203317.value: Quantum entanglement as a fundamental correlation generated between quantum systems and particles such as photons and electrons is at the heart of manipulating quantum information towards emerging quantum technologies, including quantum computing, communications, metrology and sensing. Photons are particularly promising quantum particles for carrying quantum information over long distances in free space or in optical fibers and for generating entanglement over different degrees of freedom such as polarizations and traveling paths. In this project period, we experimentally demonstrated generating polarization-entangled photon-pairs on a silicon nitride photonic chip. The silicon-based material platform exhibits a good third-order optical nonlinearity while allowing us to leverage the conventional silicon microelectronics fabrication technology. Specifically, we successfully designed, fabricated and experimentally demonstrated a nonlinear and quantum photonic circuit comprising a single waveguide coupled with two dispersion-and resonance-tailored micrometer-sized ring-resonators to attain nearly degenerate orthogonally polarized photon-pair sources for generating polarization-entanglement. This on-chip polarization-entangled photon-pair source will be a useful step towards exploring other degrees of entanglement on a chip, including path-entanglement or simultaneously polarization- and path-entanglement on a chip. These will enable new integrated photonics building blocks for further exploring large-scale manipulation of quantum information for next-generation supercomputing, fundamentally secure communications and cryptography, precision metrology and sensing.

16203417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16203417.value: In pressurized conduits such as water supply lines and pumped drainage systems, defects may occur during construction, or develop with operation and age. Defects include partially blocked/closed valves, changes in wall thickness due to bio-films, corrosion, tuberculation, material spalling and deposition. These defects cause higher pumping costs due to increased energy loss and deterioration in chemical and physical quality of the fluid. Transient-based defect detection methods (TBDDM) have been actively researched for nearly 20 years and are known to be economical detection methods capable of covering large areas of pipe systems quickly. In prior research, the PI used TBDDM to derive relationships linking shifted fundamental frequencies to blockage properties and showed that these relationships can be used to identify blockages once fundamental wave frequencies of the pipe system are physically measured. The PI’s group demonstrated that (i) this wave-shift methodology, while promising, is computationally onerous, and (ii) that the current inverse technique for blockage identification is ill posed (non-unique). The proposed work program overcomes impediments (i) and (ii). This goal will be accomplished using in-depth physical and mathematical analysis combined with laboratory and field experiments. Recent research by the PI and collaborators, found that an essential factor for improving success and accuracy of TBDDM, at least for the case of pipe blockage, is to understand the phenomenon of wave frequency shifts in the fundamental (resonant) frequencies of the pipe system caused by blockages and to prove that the maximum and minimum frequency shifts are due to the physics of Bragg resonance. Therefore, part A of the research will analyze the pressure, velocity and energy of each wave mode and the dispersion relations that link the fundamental wave frequencies of the blocked pipe systems to the unknown properties of the blockages (i.e., their number, size and location), investigate the phenomena of Bragg resonance and derive the corresponding Bragg resonance conditions. Part B of the research uses the insights developed in part A to develop efficient and robust blockage identification equations based on Bragg resonance conditions. Such conditions provide explicit relations between maximum shift, minimum shift and the location and size of blockage. Therefore, no optimization is required. As a result, a large reduction in computational time should be achieved and, at the same time, the problem of uniqueness in the identification solution will be addressed.

16203417.label: Realisation of objectives
16203417.value: The objectives were fully realized. Most models usually assume blockages to have a idealized geometric shape (i.e. the blocked section is a pipe of smaller diameter than the original). Such idealized blockage forms raise identification issues such as nonuniqueness, nonconvergence, and computational inefficiencies. We studied most realistic shaped blockage in various forms and developed a robust area reconstruction method to image such blockages. The method is based on designing an input that satisfy a prescribed system response (i.e. valve stroking concept). The proposed area reconstruction method was compared with other area reconstruction methods as well as with a regular blockage detection method. It was shown that the proposed method requires less information than other methods, in the sense that it needs only a single time measurement of desired duration and does not require (a priori) knowledge of the system boundaries. Moreover, the proposed method makes no assumptions regarding the number of blockages or their shapes. This results in higher accuracy and makes the proposed method more practical. The robustness and accuracy of the method was experimentally tested and validated. Moreover, we have implemented this method for solving the cross-sectional pipe area from boundary measurements in a tree network with one inaccessible end using reconstructive algorithm. This is equivalent to reconstructing the first order perturbation to a wave equation on a quantum graph from boundary measurements at all network ends except one. The method presented here is based on a time reversal boundary control method originally presented by Sondhi and Gopinath for one dimensional problem and later by Oksanen to higher dimensional manifolds. The algorithm is local, so is applicable to complicated networks if we are interested only in a part isomorphic to a tree. Moreover, the numerical implementation requires only one matrix inversion or least squares minimization per discretization point in the physical network. We presented a theoretical solution existence proof along with a step-by-step algorithm and a numerical validation. The developed method was found to lose accuracy when applied to blockage detected in visco-elastic (HDPE) pipes. For this reason, we studied and derived a mathematical relation between the damped and undamped waves propagating in a fluid-filled pipe. The damping considered is caused by the steady and un- steady friction and the pipe wall visco-elasticity. The derived relation is solved so that the idealized undamped pressure wave signal is obtained from the measured damped pressure signal. Physically, the proposed transformation is an amplification operation that adds back the energy that was lost due to the damping. This means that measurement errors will also be amplified under the transformation, making the problem ill-posed. The truncated singular value decomposition method is used to regularize the transformation. Both numerical and laboratory experiments are conducted to show the validity of this transformation. The results show that the transformation can accurately predict the shape and size of the reflections that were distorted due to the wave dissipation and dispersion.

16203417.label: Major findings and research outcome
16203417.value: • A pipeline blockage detection tool based on area reconstruction method is developed. • A transformation between damped and undamped waves is developed which compensates for the damping in a real system such as friction and visco-elastic pipes effect. Such transformation allows high resolution of defect detection because the damped high frequency waves are restored. • The derived area reconstruction method is extended to identify mixed-type defects (e.g. multiple blockages and leaks) in a pipe network. To the best of our knowledge, this was the first transient-based method capable to identify multiple mixed defects. • A reconstructive algorithm is applied to implement the derived area-reconstruction method to identify defects in a tree network where measurements are required at all external boundaries except for one. • High frequency wave propagation in an elastic pipe is studied whereby analytical solution for a general class of elastic pipes is derived and the wave propagation is simulated.

16203417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16203417.value: The successful completion allowed the PI to write a NSFC/RGC joint proposal (submitted in February 2021) to develop a high-frequency-wave (HFW) based pipeline defect detection scheme, by which one can identify their types, locations, and severities with super-resolution. The proposed work will (i) investigate the physical mechanism of HFW interaction with leakage, blockage, cavitation, and corrosion, and (ii) propose a signal processing method of mode decomposition to decouple the measured signal, which is a complex mixture of incident waves with multiple paths and their reflections, into separate resonant modes, so that the features of defects can be largely enhanced. These objectives will be accomplished using in depth physical and mathematical analysis informed and confirmed by laboratory and field experiments. The proposed theoretical investigation comprises (i) the derivation of the normal-mode solution of the wave equation and solve the dispersion relation for pipe systems with leakage, blockage, cavitation, and corrosion, respectively, and (ii) propose an inverse scattering scheme designed specifically for the pipe HFW data, by which one can classify, localize, and reconstruct leakage, irregular-shaped blockage, cavitation, and corrosion.

16203417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16203417.value: Blockages are ubiquitous and common in pressurized water systems due to air intrusion (the air content of UWSS around the world ranges from 2% to 10%), material deposition, tubercles (rust), scales, plaque, bio-fouling and inadvertently throttled inline valves. These blockages result in waste of energy and financial resources, reduced carrying capacity and increased potential for contamination. In addition, air blockages lead to poor system performance, instability and a potential for unsafe system operation. Other applications in which blockages commonly develop with the conduit?s age include pressurized drainage and disposal systems, crude oil lines, arterial systems, vocal tracts and hearing canals. Transient-based methods offer an efficient and low-cost diagnostic technique for assessing the internal condition of pipelines so that timely and appropriate remedies can be implemented. However, there are two key problems that limit the applicability of such methods in practice: (i) the computational time to solve for the properties of the blockages grows exponentially with time with the number of blockages, and (ii) the presence of trigonometric functions in the identification equation makes the search for a unique solution difficult. This project fully addressed these long standing impediments.

16203817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16203817.value: The project tackles key challenges in the understanding, assessment and attenuation of environmental noise produced by propulsive units on future hybrid and/or electric powered aircraft, and contributes towards achieving noise targets in aviation and towards mitigating environmental noise problems. Aerodynamic noise poses a health hazard to society in general, and particularly to communities near airports and high-speed transport routes. To minimize toxic gas emissions, increase efficiency, and to reduce noise impact, new aircraft configurations, e.g. blended wings, and new propulsive units, such as hybrid and electric powered fans/rotors/contra-rotating rotors (CROR) are being considered. These developments will have an impact on Hong Kong. The rotors bring new noise physics, which must be understood before effective designs can be proposed. For example, part of the rotors may operate in an oncoming turbulent boundary layer that develops on the blended wing surface, unlike conventional rotor powered aircraft on which the propulsive units operate in a “clean” and “uniform” airstream. The new noise sources could include non-uniform flow effects, and possess a rich tonal and broadband content due to the turbulent and non-uniform flow. Shortfalls and gaps in our understanding exist. Several deficiencies in the current ability to measure and to model the noise are identified. These are related to our current understanding of fan noise due to anisotropic turbulence ingestion by a rotary system, and partial turbulence ingestion by a rotatory system that is a significant source of engine installation noise. The current mathematical formulation to project noise into the far-field for assessment is also found to be inadequate with gusts or turbulence present on integral surfaces. We plan to conduct a multi-disciplinary study that builds on the team’s expertise and past R&D efforts in aeroacoustics, aircraft noise, materials, and manufacturing sciences. The study will include developing new computational aeroacoustic methods to build a model of rotor noise in a non-uniform turbulent stream, a new mathematical formulation to project noise into the far-field for environmental assessment, and accompanying collaborative aeroacoustic wind tunnel tests to provide validation databases. New experimental and computational tests are proposed in order to fill in the vital knowledge gaps, and to provide useful experimental databases. The new computational aeroacoustics methods will include key developments in high-order moving meshes and far-field noise estimation methods. 螺旋槳葉片的前緣噪音是渦扇發動機的主要噪聲源。本項目將針對此類噪音問題進行研究，提升對其的理解與預測能力。其研究成果也將在風力渦輪機、螺旋槳和轉子的噪音問題上發揮重要作用。對於未來在航空領域的降噪達標和噪音緩解，研究此噪聲源並設法降低其影響是至關重要的一步。此項目申請中指出了一些前緣噪音問題研究中現有模型和測試手段的缺陷，其主要有：在有攻角工況下測試的精度有限，單個翼型葉片上游區域的測試精確度不足，未考慮跨音速和超音速效應的作用，以及未考慮串聯結構中翼型葉片的幾何外形等。爲了彌補上述工況中的缺陷，此項目提出了利用實驗和計算相結合的方法進行研究，建立有效的實驗數據庫，為之後的研究與方法提供驗證依據。試驗測試和數值計算將分別使用香港科技大學現有的先進靜音風洞和已經被成功應用在此類問題求解上的氣動聲學解算器開展研究。

16203817.label: Realisation of objectives
16203817.value: The objectives listed in the proposal have been achieved by using computational, theoretical, and experimental studies. The research outcome has been published in reputed journals, including Journal of Fluid Mechanics, Proceedings of the Royal Society A, Journal of Sound and Vibration, The Journal of Acoustical Society of America, etc., and been presented at international conferences. A PhD student was supported, who successfully graduated in the year 2021. For the objectives, a summary of the achievements is given below. 1. We have investigated the effect of streamwise velocity components on noise generation in non-uniform flows. The theoretical analysis suggested that the interaction with the non-uniform flow can contribute to the noise produced in the upstream direction. The theoretical model also acts as a correction to Amiet's model for turbulence-airfoil interaction, making the results in the upstream direction more accurate. 2. We have developed new sound extrapolation methods to compute the noise radiation to the far-field using off-body integration surfaces. Two methods were developed, and both are based on the new acoustic analogy formulations of in-homogeneous convective wave equations. The first approach is based on filtering out the vortical wave based on its divergence-free property, and it was successfully applied to the turbulence-blade interaction noise problems. The other method is to apply a convection operator to the turbulent fluctuations, effectively removing the non-acoustic components based on Taylor's approximations. The operation leads to a third-order acoustic analogy formulation. The efforts led to both numerical methodologies and the theoretical development of understanding the noise generation mechanisms in turbulent flows. 3. In this project, we have developed an efficient and higher-order sliding mesh method for computational aeroacoustics. The key idea is to introduce a steady buffer zone region with uniform grid distribution, at the cost of some storage expense, at the interface of the regions with relative motion. High-order interpolation methods are employed to get the flow variable information transferred. The method has been applied for the simulations of complex rotor-stator configurations, and the blockage effect of the blade arrays is quantitatively investigated. 4. In this project, we have measured the turbulence properties, including the mean flow distribution, intensity variation, 2-point statistics in the wake region of different turbulence grids in the anechoic wind tunnel at HKUST. The measurement is mainly based on the hot-wire, and the frequency-wavenumber property is investigated. The influence of geometry and installation location of the turbulence grid was extensively investigated. Also, we have investigated the source strength and location of the airfoil-turbulence interaction noise source using phased microphones. The extended database can be used in future studies related to this topic.

16203817.label: Major findings and research outcome
16203817.value: 1. An analytical model was developed to account for the interaction of anisotropic turbulence with non-uniform mean flow, which can produce noise mainly in the upstream direction. The research outcome led to an analytical correction to the classical theory of airfoil-turbulence interaction noise based on the assumption of a flat plate in uniform mean flow. 2. An analytical model was developed to compute the noise generation in cascade, a typical configuration in the aero-engines. 3. Innovate sound extrapolation methods were developed to compute the noise distribution at far-field observers in turbulent flows. The methods were based on the development of new acoustic analogy theories. 4. An efficient and high-order sliding mesh method was developed for computational aeroacoustics, and it has been employed for different practical applications.

16203817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16203817.value: 1. The new acoustic analogy theories can be for the analysis of turbulence-induced noise sources in complex flow conditions. The study can enhance our understanding of the noise generation mechanisms. 2. The sliding mesh method can be combined with other numerical techniques such as immersed boundary methods for more challenging problems. 3. More theoretical models and experiments can be developed to consider the turbulence-blade interaction in arbitrary directions. Also, it will be challenging and interesting to consider the interaction noise with varying flow properties in the three-dimensional space.

16203817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16203817.value: This work considers the noise generation when complex flows are impinging to rigid surfaces. The problem is challenging because of our limited understanding of the flow motion and how sound is generated. Also, we need to develop methods to allow for efficient and accurate predictions, which rely on numerical simulations using supercomputers and theoretical modelling. In this work, we developed methods that can simulate the problems with moving objectives, such as the rotor blades in the aero-engines. We can use the information in a small region to compute the noise properties at any locations we are interested in. The work can help quickly and accurately assess the noise properties of the moving objects in complex flows and thus allow us to develop low-noise designs and optimizations.

16203917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16203917.value: Crowding occurs frequently in most cities, and it occasionally results in serious injuries and fatalities. To enhance the safety and service quality of urban rail transit (URT) systems it is crucial to understand the variations in passenger flow and crowding. With the development of information and sensing technology, it has become increasingly common to embed sensors and smart components in URT systems. The big data they generate contain rich information about passenger flow and crowding, and provide a good opportunity to improve the safety and service quality of urban rail transit systems. However, due to the high volume and great variety of the datasets, as well as the unique characteristics of different rail transit systems, existing data analytic techniques cannot always be applied for the inferencing of passenger crowding. This proposed research aims to establish an analytical framework appropriate to the massive datasets generated by URT systems. It will be suitable for modeling, predicting, monitoring and controlling the crowdedness of URT systems. In particular, we propose to develop solutions for (1) modeling the inflow and outflow of the passengers along each route and deriving an early warning scheme for passenger flow surges; (2) understanding and visualizing the level of crowding in a URT system by combining passenger flow information with information about a network’s structure; and (3) fusing entry and exit timestamp data and other sources of information to further forecasting. This work will be carried out using simulated data with the local urban rail services corporation as a test bed. Practically, this study will deliver a set of tools which will facilitate statistical learning from the massive data generated by various URT systems. From an academic standpoint the study will tackle a series of challenging research problems which will advance the understanding of statistical learning, modeling, and monitoring using large sets of heterogeneous data. The results should inspire the solution of similar problems in data-rich environments, especially those involving interconnected network systems in smart city development. 大多數城市頻繁發生擁擠，偶爾造成嚴重傷亡事故。為提高城市軌道交通（URT）的安全和服務質量，系統了解乘客流量和擁擠的變化至關重要。隨著信息和傳感技術的發展，越來越多在URT系統中嵌入傳感器和智能部件的通用技術。他們生成的大量數據包含有關客流和擁擠的豐富信息，並提供一個 提高城市軌道交通系統安全和服務質量的好機會。然而，由於數據量的大量和多樣性，以及獨特的不同軌道交通系統的特點，現有的數據分析技術並不總是適用於乘客擁擠的推論。這項提出的研究旨在建立適合於URT系統生成的大量數據集的分析框架。它將適合建模，預測，監控和控制URT系統的擁擠。特別是，我們提出製定解決方案（1）模擬每個乘客的流入和流出制定旅客流量預警方案;和（2）通過結合理解和可視化URT系統中的擁擠水平有關網絡結構信息的客流信息。這項工作將利用當地城市軌道交通公司的模擬數據作為試驗台進行。實際上，這項研究將提供一套工具促進各種URT系統生成的海量數據的統計學習。從學術的角度來看，這項研究將會解決一系列具有挑戰性的研究 這將導致使用大量異構數據的統計學習，建模和監控的理解。結果應該啟發在數據豐富的環境中解決類似的問題，特別是涉及智能城市發展的互聯網絡系統。

16203917.label: Realisation of objectives
16203917.value: We have completed the first objective to model the inflow and outflow of passengers and derive an early warning scheme. We start by developing statistical learning and monitoring schemes for change detection and early warning. In particular, a spatial-adaptive sampling procedure for online monitoring of big data streams, and a robust CUSUM scheme with a weighted likelihood ratio to monitor an overdispersed Poisson process have been published in related journals. Some general statistical monitoring and change detection procedures have also been developed, such as a control scheme for monitoring process covariance matrices with more variables than observations, and adaptive monitoring of multimodal data. We have also completed the second objective to understand the level of crowding using the passenger flow information. More specifically, a diagnostic procedure for high-dimensional data streams via missed discovery rate control was developed. The PI has also constructed a time-warped sparse non-negative factorization scheme for functional data analysis. We have been invited to present the research results at international conferences, such as INFORMS conference in Nov 2018 in Phoenix.

We have one Ph.D. student trained, who is working in Huawei as a data scientist now. We also had a deep discussion with the MTR operations department to seek further research and development based on this research, and they all showed vital interests.

16203917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16203917.value: Practically, this study delivered a set of tools that facilitate statistical learning from the massive data generated by various URT systems. From an academic standpoint, the study tackles a series of challenging research problems that advance understanding statistical learning, modeling, and monitoring using large sets of heterogeneous data. The research results, especially on process monitoring and change detection of URT, may inspire the solution of similar problems in data-rich environments, including those involving interconnected network systems in smart city development. The PI will seek further funding for further research and development in this direction.

16203917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16203917.value: Crowding frequently occurs in most cities, and it occasionally results in severe injuries and fatalities. To enhance the safety and service quality of urban rail transit (URT) systems, it is crucial to understand the variations in passenger flow and crowding. With the development of information and sensing technology, it has become increasingly common to embed sensors and smart components in URT systems. The big data they generate contains rich information about passenger flow and crowding and provides an excellent opportunity to improve the safety and quality of urban rail transit systems. However, due to the high volume and great variety of the datasets and the unique characteristics of different rail transit systems, existing data analytic techniques cannot always be applied for the inferencing of passenger crowding. This proposed research aims to establish an analytical framework appropriate to the massive datasets generated by URT systems. It will be suitable for modeling, predicting, monitoring, and controlling the crowdedness of URT systems. The research results should inspire the solution of similar problems in data-rich environments, especially those involving interconnected network systems in smart city development.

16204117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16204117.value: To succeed in the knowledge economy, it is increasingly important for firms to update their products and prices as technology and costs change, as competitor's offerings change, and as consumers' preferences change. This problem is relevant to both manufacturing firms, such as computer companies, and to service firms, such as hotels and airlines. To support the design and pricing of products and services it is critical to understand consumer demand, and this requires building discrete choice models the data well. Assuming a tested and validated choice model, the design and pricing of products can take place at several levels depending on the levers under management control. At the operational level, products and prices are taken as given, and the optimization problem is limited to finding the subset of products to make available for sale. This is known as the assortment optimization problem and it is at the core of hotel and airline revenue management practices. Assortment optimization problems are also commonly encountered in e-commerce. At a more strategic level, firms have the ability to design and price new products, to redesign, re-price, or remove existing products, and may allow part or all of the product attributes to be specified by consumers (mass customization). In this study we propose to fit choice models to data, and to incorporate them into a design and pricing model featuring the assortment problem as a special case. We have very promising preliminary results for the celebrated and widely used multinomial logit (MNL) choice model. Our design provides the highest profits to the firm, and simultaneously the highest consumer surplus among all other optimally priced designs with the same number of products. Our goal is to extend our work to other choice models that may have a better fit to data than the MNL. In particular, we intend to study the mixed MNL model, the nested logit model (NL), and rational inattention models (RIMs). In addition, we propose to study issues related to consumer surplus, mass customization, bundling and unbundling, negotiations, the pricing of ancillary services, and the presence of fixed costs. Our work will be of enormous value to manufacturing firms that build products to stock, to service firms that build services to order, and to both brick and mortar and e-commerce retail firms that order and price an assortment of products. 隨著科技進步，生產成本改變，競爭者策略更新以及消費者喜好變動，即時優化企業產品線設計和定價起著舉足輕重的作用。這個問題不僅僅和制造業息息相關，對服務行業也是重中之重。 解決此問題的關鍵首先在於建立消費者選擇模型來描述消費者需求。在給定消費者選擇模型下，產品線設計及定價就分為幾個層面：戰術層面上，企業可以在給定產品線和價格基礎上做產品線組合優化；戰略層面上，企業可以根據消費者喜好重新設計產品以及價格，或者改變部分配置來為客戶做大規模訂制。 本項目重點研究如何利用消費者選擇模型預測新產品需求，以及在給定模型下如何優化產品線設計和價格。初始結果顯示前景非常可觀：在經典的 Multinomial Logit模型下，我們給出了簡便易行的最優算法。並且我們發現，最優產品線不但能給企業帶來最大利潤，同時也能給消費者帶來最大剩余利益。 我們下一步的目標是把該問題拓展到更廣泛消費者選擇模型上，比如說多市場的Multinomial Logit模型，Nested Logit模型，以及理性疏忽模型。此外，我們還要研究繼而引發的一系列相關問題，如消費者剩余利益優化，大規模定制，產品打包和拆分，買賣雙方議價，以及輔助服務定價等問題。我們的工作將會給制造商和服務商創造巨大價值。

16204117.label: Major findings and research outcome
16204117.value: We were able to solve the longstanding problem of dynamic non-linear pricing problem. More precisely, we consider a finite-horizon, finite-capacity dynamic pricing model where consumers may purchase multiple units of the same product. We present three models that differ in their complexity and revenue potential. The dynamic nonlinear pricing (DNP) model allows the seller to dynamically selecting a price for each bundle size. The dynamic linear pricing model restricts the seller to dynamically select a unit price for all bundle sizes. There can be a significant revenue gap between the two models, but the additional revenues require a nonlinear policy that may be more challenging to implement. This motivates the study of dynamic block pricing as an intermediate pricing model where prices are linear within each block. A heuristic for this last model provides almost as much revenue as DNP. This paper appeared in Operations Research Volume 68 in 2020. Although an earlier version of this paper was submitted prior to the grant, the grant allows us to complete this project that supports pricing in general and in particular for product design. We propose one of the first models of “product framing” and pricing. Product framing refers to the way consumer choice is influenced by how the products are framed or displayed. We derive algorithms with guaranteed performance relative to an optimal algorithm under reasonable assumptions. Our algorithms are fast and easy to implement. This paper appeared in Operations Research in 2020. Although this paper was submitted before the grant was funded, we used funds from the grant to do the revision of the paper. We were able to solve the nonparameteric pricing problems with customer covariates. As personalized pricing analytics is becoming an essential tool in retailing. Upon observing the personalized information of each arriving customer, the firm needs to set a price accordingly based on the covariates, such as income, education background, and past purchasing history, to extract more revenue. This paper appeared in Operations Research Vol, 969 in 2021. In addition, we have nearly completed an ambitious project to integrate all our knowledge into the product design and pricing problem. The output is the last chapter of the Ph.D. thesis of Zhudong Tang which was judged excellent by the committee. This will soon be submitted as a paper to Operations Research,

16204117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16204117.value: There are still room for expanding on objectives 3 and 4 and my Ph.D. student Zhudong Tang will stay as a post-doc to explore this possibilities. In particular, he will complete some of the computational results and submit the final paper to Operations Research in the spring of 2022.

16204117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16204117.value: After this grant we have a much clearer understanding of the issues that are involved in designing and pricing products. These issues range from how consumers select, base on product attributes, price and consumer covariates, including a comparison of linear versus non-linear pricing and the depth of the product line. In product line design and pricing problems, we can optimize expected revenue over both prices and product configurations.We focus on three commonly used Basic Attraction Models (BAM): Multinomial Logit (MNL), Multiplicative Competitive Interaction (MCI), and the Linear model. We consider finite elasticity family and linearly compensate choice models. We develop a fully polynomial time approximation scheme. Moreover, the problem is polynomial solvable by the k-shortest path algorithm if product's valuation can be linearly compensated by the price. For multiple segments customers, a special case that customers are differentiated only with respect to the no-purchase alternative is investigated.

16204517.label: Project Objectives
16204517.value: To examine the morphology, size, and spatial distribution of nanoparticles exsolved from A-site-deficient perovskites in various configurations as a function of temperature, partial gas pressures and applied bias. To distinguish the features and mechanism of nanoparticle egress driven by chemical reduction in hydrogen and electrochemical polarization and to identify how the particles’ features impact the materials' activity. To model the mechanism of nanoparticle growth. The models will consider the effects and dynamics of diffusion and drift of various elements in the perovskites, the kinetics of the metal’s reduction from the bulk to nanoparticles, and the mechanical interaction of the particles with the material. 16204517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16204517.value: 排放到大气中的二氧化碳所造成的全球变暖已成为人类面临的最关键的问题之一。为了解决这一问题，高效的能量转换和存储技术迫切需要。固体氧化物电化学电池（SOC）是一种最有希望提供高效率和低排放温室气体的系统。 SOC是可逆的，因为它们既可以作为燃料电池也可以作为电解池工作。在前一种模式下，它们可以比基于燃烧的系统更有效地发电。而作为电解池，它们可以从水中产生氢和氧，产生完全可持续的燃料，并以化学能的形式有效地转化和储存。虽然前景广阔，但SOC技术的大规模部署仍然需要开发稳定且高活性的电极材料。 最近，一些研究使用了A位缺陷的钙钛矿氧化物作为高效的SOC电极。这些氧化物在氢气氛中高温（例如900℃）处理数十小时后，能够直接从大块材料中产生（析出）所需金属的纳米颗粒。这样的纳米颗粒可以显着增强SOC的活性，并且由于它们被锚定到材料上而特别稳定。最近发表的工作也表明，通过适当地向SOC施加电势，纳米颗粒的成核和生长可以加速到几分钟。此外，这种纳米颗粒具有更好的覆盖面积和更强的活性。虽然许多新材料已经开发了出来，但是纳米颗粒成核和生长的机制仍然没有被理解，特别是电驱动纳米颗粒析出的机制。而这种机制的理解至关重要，它可以允许对影响SOC性能的纳米颗粒的性质做出控制，诸如尺寸和分布。 我们提出的研究将侧重于弥合这一知识上的空白，并理解化学驱动和电化学驱动的析出机制。为了达到这一目标，我们需要开发由实验支持的高级建模。研究小组将首先着重研究一种材料，并进行实验以确定析出后纳米颗粒的形态，尺寸，分布和机械应变。通过一系列原位和非原位表征，我们将能够通过化学驱动或电场驱动的析出来区分在纳米颗粒生产期间发生的化学和物理过程。数据将用于校准模型，从而定量分析所涉及的纳米颗粒生长过程。我们还将研究其电化学响应以表征纳米颗粒对SOC的性能和稳定性的影响。最后，我们将执行从头模拟，以了解在纳米颗粒析出期间发生的原子尺度过程。 总之，在这项工作中，我们将致力于通过借助实验支持的专用模型来阐明化学驱动和电化学驱动的析出机理。对其的理解将能够更好地控制析出过程，最终研发出更加优良的SOC。

16204517.label: Realisation of objectives
16204517.value: Regarding objective 1, A-site deficient perovskites were reduced in hydrogen to exsolve metallic nanoparticles. The particles, composed of elements in the B-site, especially Ni, grew with a patterned nucleation distribution, caused by the energy difference of the heterogeneous structure and the anisotropic nature of the material. Therefore, their size depends on processing temperature and time, as well as hydrogen concentration. In particular, a decreased growth rate is correlated to an increase in the reduction time, and the growth rate is also related to the reduction atmosphere. As for objective 2, we observed that the mechanism of the exsolution process is based on four different steps, including diffusion, reduction, nucleation, and growth. the reduced materials showed a considerable increase in their electrochemical catalytic activity. Regarding objective 3, our DFT study on the energetics of Ni segregation in SrTiO3-based perovskites shows that Ni preferentially segregates toward the (100)-oriented and SrTiO-terminated surfaces. This suggests that Ni nanoparticles exsolution is promoted by the presence of A-site and O-site vacancies. Furthermore, first-principles calculations show that atomic substitution affects particle exsolution. In particular, it was observed that A-site substitution of Sr2+ with La3+ hinders exsolution, while B-site substitution of Ti4+ with non-metal elements, such as Si or P promotes it. The calculations were supported by experiments, which showed increased nanoparticle exsolution upon non-metal doping. In addition, surface analysis suggests that exsolution is promoted by the reduction of Ni to a lower oxidation state. As for objective 4, the computational models were fitted with the experimental data. Both the size-related micro-mechanical constraints and limited Ni amount were key factors in determining the growth rate of particles. However, these are not the only factors affecting exsolution. In fact, as already outlined above, the electrochemical activity can be maximized by tailoring A-site deficiency and B-site non-metal substitution. All objectives were fulfilled. As it is quite difficult to convey the study outcomes without the aid of pictures, part C expands on the above findings and their relationship to the objectives.

16204517.label: Major findings and research outcome
16204517.value: This work unveiled the potential of exsolution as a method to egress uniformly distributed metallic nanoparticles from perovskites. With the main focus on Ni nanoparticle production, we observed that: 1) Exsolution is favored by the reduction in hydrogen of A-site- and oxygen-deficient perovskites. 2) Regarding SrTiO3-δ-based perovskites, A-site substitution of Sr with La decreased the exsolution of Ni. 3) Introducing non-metals, such as P and Si, as B-site dopants increases the Ni nanoparticle egress. The surface analysis of the oxidation state of Ni after P and Si doping suggests that non-metal doping reduces the oxidation state of Ni, and for this reason, facilitates its exolution in nanoparticle. 4) While temperature, exposure time, and atmosphere composition can be adjusted to optimize Ni exsolution, nanoparticle formation is unavoidably limited by strain, Ni availability, and diffusion. 5) Because of their spherical shape and specific composition, Ni-metal nanoparticles could be identified by scanning electron miscoscopy (see micrographs in Part C). Interestingly, the egressed particles formed regular patterns on the surface of materials, suggesting that nucleation occurs preferably at grain boundaries. All points are further detailed in Part C.

16204517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16204517.value: The current state-of-the-art on exsolution led to examining various parent oxide materials and different combinations of metal nanoparticles. However, more research is necessary to unlock the full potential of exsolution. For example, the exsolution process has mainly been used to improve the performance of anodes (or fuel electrodes) of fuel cells. Still, there are no studies on the advantages of also having exsolved nanoparticles on cathodes. The presence of these particles at such highly oxidizing conditions may cause an inversion of the process and consequent reincorporation of the metal nanoparticles into the main structure. Finding a way to stabilize exsolved nanoparticles in cathodes at high temperatures could be the new frontier of this technology. At the same time, the development of novel low-temperature PCFC may enable the use of this technology as part of steam-free air electrodes.

16204517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16204517.value: The work investigates the mechanisms behind exsolution, a process that triggers the formation of metallic nanoparticles on ceramic materials. Such nanoparticles have been shown to improve the performance of many devices, including car catalysts used for pollution control, fuel cells, and electrolyzers. Being able to control the growth of these particles allows us to produce better functionalities. This project investigated Ni nanoparticle growth specific to perovskite oxides used in solid oxide fuel cells. In particular, we studied composition optimization to generate the nanoparticles more easily and the mechanism underpinning nanoparticle growth, including factors limiting it and growth patterns. This research project is extremely valuable because optimizing exsolution through the lens of fundamental science allows fabricating composite nanomaterials with controlled catalyst density, size, and stability. It is expected that the catalysis and green power production industries will benefit from the fundamental insight developed in this project.

16204817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16204817.value: The spillage and leakage of crude oil, which is essentially a mixture of liquid hydrocarbons, have induced serious soil contamination all over the world. For instance, it is reported that oil pollution contributes to about 24% of ground contamination in Europe. The oil contamination not only induces serious damage to the environment, but also affects the performance of civil engineering structures. As revealed by a recent study, the measured bearing capacity of a pile foundation reduced by 60% when the oil content in soil was increased from zero to 6%. Up to now, it is a great challenge for geotechnical researchers and engineers to predict the influence of oil contamination on the performance of civil engineering structures. This is because previous studies for oil-contaminated soil mainly focused on oil permeability for predicting the infiltration and migration of oil. There is a lack of study on the oil-water-air-solid (OWAS) interaction and its influence on the mechanical behaviour including small strain stiffness and shear strength, which are crucial for analyzing the serviceability and ultimate limit states of civil engineering structures, respectively. The proposed project will address and tackle this challenge through laboratory element testing and theoretical modelling, where the framework of unsaturated soil (an air-water-solid soil system) mechanics will be considered and extended for the OWAS interaction. In the laboratory testing, a novel multi-phase triaxial apparatus allowing for independent control of triaxial stress states as well as pore air, water and oil pressures will be developed. With the unique capability of stress and pore pressure control, the OWAS interaction and its influence on stiffness-strain relation at small strains, dilatancy and shear strength of oil-contaminated soil will be investigated. Effects of stress, suctions associated with air-oil, oil-water and air-water interfaces and strain rate will be considered. Based on the new experimental results, an advanced constitutive model will be developed for oil-contaminated soil with consideration of strain rate effects. In contrast with conventional unsaturated soil models using air-water suction, the new one will also consider air-oil and oil-water suctions. The success of this project will, no doubt, improve our fundamental understanding and modelling of complex hydro-mechanical behaviour of oil-contaminated soil. The new test results and theoretical model obtained from the proposed project will assist researchers and engineers to improve the analysis of civil engineering structures in oil-contaminated land, and also provide a basis for future studies of other multi-phase porous material. 石油的洩漏和排放在全球範圍內造成了嚴重的土地污染，例如在歐洲24%受污染的土地是由石油造成。石油污染不僅對生態環境造成巨大破壞，而且也影響周邊土木工程建築物的服役性能。最近一項研究發现，當土體含油量從零增加到6％時，樁基的承載力降低了60％。迄立至今，準確預測石油污染對土木工程建築物服役性能的影響對岩土工程研究人員和工程師是一個巨大的挑戰。主要原因在於針對石油污染土體的研究工作主要集中於石油在土體内的遷移規律，對油-水-空氣-土顆粒之間的相互作用缺乏完善認識。石油污染對土體小應變模量（用於分析正常使用極限狀態）和剪切強度（用於分析承載能力極限狀態）的影響規律亦尚未明確。 本項目將展開室內試驗和理論建模研究油-水-空氣-土顆粒四相系統的水力學性質，重點包括细粒土的持水和持油能力、應力-應變關係曲線、剪切模量隨應變衰減曲線和剪切強度。將開發一種新的多相三軸設備，以實現對三軸應力狀態、孔隙氣壓力、水壓力和油壓力的獨立控制，從而控制空氣-油、空氣-水和油-水交界面的吸力，揭示各吸力對土體水力學性質的影響規律。基於新的實驗結果，建立並驗證新的本構模型，創新地考慮空氣-油和油-水交界面的吸力效應，並考慮應變速率對剪切模量和強度的影響。本項目的成功無疑將提升我們對石油污染土體水力學性質的認知和理論模擬水平，有助於研究人員和工程師改進對石油污染土地中土木工程建築物服役性能的分析，為今後研究其他多相多孔材料提供参考。

16204817.label: Realisation of objectives
16204817.value: All of the objectives have been achieved through the following activities along with the original plan: (1) Several new apparatuses including a novel multi-phase triaxial apparatus were developed. This multi-phase triaxial apparatus imposes pore air pressure, pore oil pressure and pore water pressure inside unsaturated soils independently, so it is able to control the air-water suction, air-oil suction and oil-water suction of oil-contaminated soils simultaneously. As far as the research team members are aware, this is the first apparatus able to control stress and three suctions of a specimen. (2) Extensive tests were carried out to investigate the hydro-mechanical behaviour of both oil-contaminated and clean unsaturated soils, including the water retention curve, oil retention curve, compressibility, shear strength and dilatancy. (3) Several theoretical model were developed for unsaturated soils with/without oil contamination. (4) One of the theoretical models was implemented in a finite difference code. Parametric studies were carried out using the new code to improve the understanding of light non-aqueous phase liquid (LNAPL) in the vadose zone.

16204817.label: Major findings and research outcome
16204817.value: Key findings and outcome related to Objective 1: A multi-phase triaxial apparatus was developed, as explained in Section 5.3. (Reference: Journal paper 11 in the list shown below) Key findings and outcome related to Objective 2: A soil generally has a smaller retention capacity for silicone oil than that for the water, mainly because of the smaller interfacial tension of air-oil interface. For coarse-grained soil, its oil retention curve can be estimated from the water retention curve by applying a scaling factor, equal to the ratio of air-water interfacial tension to air-oil interfacial tension. For fine-grained soil, the scaling concept could be used to unify the water and oil retention curves, but the scaling factor should not be simply assumed to a ratio of interfacial tensions. This is because the oil contamination affects the micro-structure of soil, like the degree of aggregation. (References: Journal papers 1, 3, 10 and 11 in the list shown below) Key findings and outcome related to Objectives 3 and 4: The shear behaviour of OS and WS are very different, where OS and WS denote soil specimens partially saturated with oil and water respectively. The residual friction angle of OS is 30% larger than that of WS. The former structure includes more particle contacts than the latter one. When the degree of water saturation decreases, the dilatancy, peak friction angle and apparent cohesion of WS increase substantially because of the strengthen effects of air-water suction on soil skeleton. In contrast, the degree of oil saturation has minuscule effects on these variables, mainly because OS has a low oil retention ability and the air-oil suction. (References: Journal papers 2, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8 in the list shown below) Key findings and outcome related to Objective 5: With an aim to predict the coupled oil/water flow and soil deformation, several hydro-mechanical constitutive models for unsaturated soils were developed. In particular, a new mathematical model was developed for light non-aqueous phase liquid (LNAPL)-contaminated soils considering porosity effects on hydraulic properties of soils, including the retention behaviour and permeability function of LNAPL and water. The newly developed model was implemented using the finite difference method and then verified by the results of a centrifuge test. (References: Journal papers 1, 9 and 10; more models could be published in the next one or two years)

16204817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16204817.value: The coupled water and LNAPL flows and their influence on ground response are very important and complicated. The current project mainly focusses on the hydro-mechanical behaviour of oil-contaminated unsaturated soils, with some simplifications (a) Diffusion and dispersion among different phases and LNAPL partitioning are neglected; (b) The biodegradation of LNAPL is negligible for the time period under investigation; (c) Phase change between liquid water and vapour water is not considered. To further improve the understanding, a more comprehensive and multi-disciplinary study is urgently needed. A PhD student trained in this project plans to work on these problems as a postdoctoral fellow.

16204817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16204817.value: Soil contamination induced by oil spillage and leakage is a serious global problem. The infiltration and mitigation of oil would induce serious damage to the environment and also impose adverse impacts on the surrounding civil engineering structures. Up to now, it is still a great challenge for geotechnical researchers and engineers to predict the performance of civil engineering structures founded in oil-contaminated land. With an attempt to address this challenge, advanced testing and theoretical modelling were carried out in this project. The framework for unsaturated soil mechanics was extended in both experimental and theoretical studies. In the laboratory testing, a novel multi-phase triaxial apparatus was developed and adopted to investigate the water and oil retention, compressibility and strength behaviour of oil-contaminated soil. Based on new experimental results obtained from this proposed project, novel theoretical models for multi-phase soil system were developed to capture effects of stress, suctions associated with the air-water, air-oil, and oil-water interfaces. The new test results and theoretical model from this project can assist researchers and engineers to analyse the influence of oil contamination on the serviceability and ultimate limit states of civil engineering structures.

16205117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16205117.value: Uncertain graphs are prevalent in several applications including communications systems, biological databases and social networks. The ever increasing size of the underlying data renders both graph storage and query processing extremely expensive. Sparsification has often been used to reduce the size of deterministic graphs by maintaining only the important edges. For uncertain graphs, sparsification has important additional benefits: since the entropy of sparsified graphs is much lower than that of the original, query processing based on Monte Carlo sampling becomes significantly faster as it requires a fraction of the samples. Moreover, the sampling process is more efficient as its cost is analogous to the number of edges. Despite its importance, there is no previous work on uncertain graph sparsification. Furthermore, adaptation of deterministic sparsification methods fails in the uncertain setting. To overcome this problem, we plan to investigate sparsification techniques aimed explicitly at uncertain graphs. The proposed methods reduce the number of edges and redistribute their probabilities in order to decrease the graph size, while preserving its underlying structure. The resulting graph can be used to efficiently and accurately approximate any query and mining tasks on the original graph. Specifically, the goals of the project is to (i) explore properties of uncertain graphs to be captured by sparsification; (ii) design and implement efficient algorithms that preserve the intended properties and can be applied to the large uncertain graphs commonly found in practice; (iii) evaluate the proposed techniques with real data in a variety of query processing and data mining tasks. 不确定图被广泛应用于通信系统、生物数据库和社交网络等领域中。这些领域不断增长的潜在数据规模使得图的存储和基于图的查询处理代价高昂。通过保留关键的边，稀疏化算法已常常被用于减小确定图的规模。对于不确定图，稀疏化具有重要的增益：由于经稀疏化图的熵远远小于原图的熵，基于蒙特卡罗抽样的查询处理因需要更少的抽样而显著加快。而且，抽样过程也变得更高效，因其复杂度和边的数目近似。尽管如此重要，目前并没有关于不确定图稀疏化的研究。此外，确定图的稀疏化方法并不适用于不确定图。 为了解决这个问题，我们提出了首个针对不确定图的稀疏化框架。我们提出的方案通过减少边的数量和改变边的概率，在降低图的规模的同时保留了图的基本结构。所生成的图能替代原图，对任何查询或挖掘任务进行高效而准确的近似处理。具体来说，这个项目的目标包括：(i) 探究稀疏化需要保留的不确定图的性质。(ii) 设计并实现能保留这些性质并且适用于现实应用中出现的大规模不确定图的算法。(iii) 通过基于真实数据的不同查询处理以及数据挖掘任务来测试所设计的算法。

16205117.label: Realisation of objectives
16205117.value: Given a graph G = (V,E) and a parameter alpha in the range (0, 1), sparsification generates a graph G', which contains a fraction alpha of the edges. Although the problem is well studied for deterministic graphs, there is no previous work on uncertain graphs, where each edge is associated with a probability. In this setting, G' should preserve the structural properties of G and have less entropy, so that it could be used to efficiently approximate the result of a wide range of queries on G. We first propose a novel framework of uncertain graph sparsification with entropy reduction. Then, we design algorithms that reduce the number of edges and tune the probability of the remaining ones to preserve crucial properties. We experimentally demonstrate that the sparsified graphs are effective for a variety of common tasks including shortest path distance, reliability, page rank etc. As a second step, we deal with collective influence maximization in social networks, which are naturally modelled as uncertain graphs. The goal is to select a seed set of users, for each product, that maximizes the collective exposure for a set of products. To capture the competing diffusion processes, we introduce an Awareness-to-Influence model: in the first phase, awareness about each product propagates in the social graph unhindered by other competing products. In the second phase, a user adopts the most preferred product among those encountered in the awareness phase. To compute the seed sets, we propose a game-theoretic framework that views the various products as agents, which compete for influence in the social graph and selfishly select their individual strategy. In the following, we elaborate on the project outcomes, starting with sparsification algorithms. A prevalent goal in deterministic graph sparsification is preservation of the cut sizes. The notion of a cut can be extended naturally to uncertain graphs. In this case, the expected size of a cut is the sum of the probabilities of the edges involved in the cut. The absolute discrepancy of a vertex set S in a sparsified graph G' is the difference of S's expected cut size in G' to its expected cut size in G. Our work aims at cut-preserving sparsified graphs, or, equivalently, at minimizing discrepancy. The exponential number of cuts renders their exhaustive enumeration intractable. To overcome this, we target cuts of sets S with cardinality up to an input value k. The proposed framework starts with an initialization step that generates a connected unweighted, deterministic graph G* out of the input uncertain graph. G* can be thought of as a backbone that ensures that connectivity is preserved in the resulting sparsified graph. We first compute a maximum spanning tree of the uncertain graph, where the probabilities act as weights. Then, we remove the tree edges from G and insert them to G*. This process is repeated until G* contains the desired fraction alpha of edges. Then, two different techniques operate on G* in order to produce the sparsified graph, namely Gradient Descent Backbone (GDB) and Expectation Maximization Degree (EMD). GDB performs gradient descent, only updating the edge probabilities of the backbone graph, without inserting or removing edges. Therefore, it is sensitive to the choice of G*. On the other hand, EMD modifies both the edges and their probabilities. It is inspired by Expectation-Maximization, an iterative optimization framework that estimates two sets of interdependent unknown parameters. In our case, EMD estimates the: i) the set of edges in the sparsified graph and ii) their probabilities. Both GDB and EMD minimize discrepancy and entropy. Observe that the two objectives are not independent because, since the sparsified graph has fewer edges, it is likely to have lower entropy as well. Minimization of discrepancy refers to the quality of the sparsified graph, while entropy reduction relates to the efficiency of query processing. Indeed as shown in our experimental evaluation with multiple real uncertain graphs (see Journal 1 and conference publications), the proposed techniques capture well the structural properties of the input uncertain graph. The preservation of structural properties leads to accurate results for various queries with different characteristics. Moreover, reducing the entropy of the uncertain graph diminishes the processing time, as considerably fewer samples are required for accurate query estimation. As opposed to the proposed methods, techniques based on deterministic sparsification usually fail, in terms of result quality and variance. GDB is faster than EMD, which however produces more accurate query results. Nevertheless, compared to the high cost most queries, both methods are fast and therefore applicable to large uncertain graphs commonly found in several applications. Regarding influence maximization, a social network can be thought of as uncertain graph, where an edge weight corresponds to the probability that a user influences another. For our setting, we assume that the owner of multiple competing products is interested in their joint diffusion in the underlying social network. For example, an e-shop promoting various laptop models may wish to find seed sets of influencers for each model so that the total influence of all products is maximized. We consider that the owner has a budget for each product, which refers to the maximum number of seeds for that product. Users may have different weights for different products, which signify their importance. For instance, users whose profile or demographic characteristics match the advertised product have high weights. To capture the diffusion of the competing products we adopt an awareness-to-influence (AtI) model, which separates awareness and influence. AtI assumes that the influence of each product diffuses independently in the underlying social graph during the awareness phase. A user may thus become aware of several products, but in the end s/he adopts only one of them in the subsequent influence phase. Since influence maximization is NP-Hard for most diffusion models, even for a single product, most methods are approximate. We show that AtI possesses monotonicity and submodularity, two properties that enable approximate solutions with tight quality guarantees. Furthermore, we cast the problem as a game, where products compete for influence in the social graph. To compute the seed sets, we introduce GCW, a monotone utility game with bounded price of anarchy that falls under the important class of monotone utility games. Based on that, we prove that a single round of best-response dynamics can produce high quality solutions. To evaluate the practical effectiveness of our approach we evaluate it on numerous social networks (see Journal 2), capturing different problem characteristics. As there is no previous work, we use as benchmark a method where each products selects its seedset without considering the competition. The proposed GCW significantly extends the total influence compared to the baseline algorithm, especially in the presence of numerous competing products with big budgets. Moreover, since a single round of best responses suffices to reach high quality solutions, the proposed framework is applicable to large graphs.
