16205117.label: Major findings and research outcome
16205117.value: An uncertain (also called probabilistic) graph is interpreted as the set of all possible deterministic graphs (i.e., worlds), each defined on a subset of the edges. Exact processing necessitates query evaluation on all possible worlds and aggregation of the partial results, which is prohibitive due to the exponential number of worlds. Thus, most techniques provide approximate results by applying Monte-Carlo sampling on a random subset of possible worlds. However, even this is very expensive, because it requires numerous samples for accurate query estimation. In order to tackle the high cost, in this project, we develop techniques for uncertain graph sparsification. The proposed techniques first generate a backbone graph that preserves the connectivity of the original, and then refine it in order to capture well the structural graph properties. Sparsification yields significant benefits in execution time because the cost of sampling is linear to the number of edges. Moreover, the required number of samples is proportional to the graphs entropy, which is lower in sparsified graphs. Finally, sparsification reduces the storage cost, and facilitates visualization of complex networks. In addition, we design methods for collective influence maximization in uncertain graphs. Influence maximization is a fundamental task in social network analysis. Typically, it aims at selecting a set of seeds for the network that influences the maximum number of individuals. Motivated by practical applications, we focus on a variant, where the owner of multiple competing products wishes to select seeds for each product so that the collective influence across all products is maximized. To capture the competing diffusion processes, we introduce an Awareness-to-Influence (AtI) model. In the first phase, awareness about each product propagates in the social graph unhindered by other competing products. In the second phase, a user adopts the most preferred product among those encountered in the awareness phase. To compute the seed sets, we propose GCW, a game-theoretic framework that views the various products as agents, which compete for influence in the social graph and selfishly select their individual strategy. We show that AtI exhibits monotonicity and submodularity; importantly, GCW is a monotone utility game. The properties enable the development of an efficient best response algorithm, with quality guarantees on the collective utility.

16205117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16205117.value: Research directions for further development on sparsification methods involve refinement techniques that can be applied, as an extra step, on the sparsified graph produced by the proposed algorithms. For instance, a local search algorithm could saturate the edge probabilities uniformly, in order to minimize the expected degree error of each node. Another direction involves sparsification without an explicit parameter alpha: instead, the goal would be to generate the uncertain graph with the minimum amount of edges that preserves a set of structural properties. Moreover, we intend to investigate sparsification of multigraphs and weighted uncertain graphs. Regarding influence maximization on uncertain graphs, in addition to best response dynamics, it would be interesting to explore alternative algorithmic frameworks, including local search and dynamic programming.

16205117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16205117.value: Graphs constitute an expressive data representation paradigm used to describe entities (vertices) and their relationships (edges) in a wide range of applications. Sometimes the existence of the relationship between two entities is uncertain due to various reasons. In such cases, the data can be modeled as an uncertain graph, whose edges are labeled with a probability of existence. For instance, in social networks, the edge probability may denote the influence of a user on another. Most query processing tasks on uncertain graphs are computationally intensive and involve approximation methods based on extensive sampling. In order to diminish the high cost, we develop sparsification techniques that reduce the number of edges, and re-distribute their probabilities so that structural graph properties are preserved. Furthermore, we propose diffusion processes that maximize the influence for a set of competing products in social networks, represented as uncertain graphs. The effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed techniques is demonstrated through comprehensive evaluation with large, real-life, uncertain graphs.

16205217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16205217.value: Since the advent of option trading, many path-dependent options whose payoffs rely in various ways on the whole path of the underlying asset price process have been created to serve different purposes of hedging, arbitrage, and speculation in financial markets. Due to their versatility and popularity, the related pricing problems have received much attention from both practitioners and researchers throughout the world, including Hong Kong -- one of the most influential international financial centers. Discrete barrier options and Bermudan options are among the most popular path-dependent options actively traded in various financial markets. Although there are numerous studies relating to the pricing of them under one-dimensional option pricing models such as the Black-Scholes model and exponential Levy models, only a few publications deal with multidimensional option pricing models, which can, however, account for the complex multiple random sources inherent in the underlying asset price structures better than one-dimensional models can. In this project, we will propose an accurate and efficient Hilbert transform approach to pricing both discrete (single or double) barrier options and Bermudan options under a rich class of multidimensional models -- regime-switching exponential Levy models and regime-switching exponential Levy models with stochastic volatility/intensity (in each regime the asset price follows an exponential Levy model with stochastic volatility/intensity). This rich class of models includes many popular option pricing models such as stochastic volatility models (e.g., Heston model and Bates model), various exponential Levy models with stochastic volatility/intensity (e.g., Kou's model with stochastic volatility/intensity), and regime-switching stochastic volatility models (e.g., regime-switching Heston or Bates model). One appealing feature of the Hilbert transform method is that it is highly accurate and efficient usually with exponential decay discretization and truncation errors. More specifically, we will take the following three steps to complete the project. (1). Under regime-switching exponential Levy models, we intend to derive backward recursions in Fourier space for discrete barrier and Bermudan option pricing. (2) Under regime-switching exponential Levy models, we will attempt to develop accurate and fast pricing algorithms to implement these two recursions based on the celebrated sinc expansion approximation method proposed by Feng and Linetsky (2008, 2009). (3) We plan to develop Hilbert-CTMC-combined pricing methods for discrete barrier and Bermudan options under regime-switching exponential Levy models with stochastic volatility/intensity by first transforming these models into regime-switching exponential Levy models through CTMC approximation and twofold regime-switching integration and then applying the Hilbert transform approach developed above to the transformed models. 自期权交易开始以来，金融市场上出现了许多路径依赖期权，它们的支付函数以不同的方式依赖于资产价格的路径，能够在金融市场上服务于对冲，套利和投机等不同的目的。这些路径依赖期权功能多样，在金融市场上广受欢迎，相关的期权定价问题受到全世界学术界和工业界的普遍关注，包括香港 -- 最有影响力的国际金融中心之一。 离散观测的障碍期权和百慕大期权是两种非常流行的路径依赖期权，在各种金融市场上都有大量交易。虽然有许多论文在一维期权定价模型下研究它们的定价问题，比如Black-Scholes模型和指数Levy模型，但是只有少数论文考虑多维期权定价模型。然而，相比于一维模型，多维模型能够更好的描述资产价格里固有的多个随机因素。 在该研究项目中，我们将提出一个准确快速的希尔伯特变换方法对资产价格服从一大类多维模型 -- 具有体制转换的指数Levy模型和具有体制转换及随机波动率/强度的指数Levy模型（在每一个体制下，资产价格服从一个具有随机波动率/强度的指数Levy模型） -- 的离散观测的（单边或双边）障碍期权和百慕大期权进行定价。这一大类模型包含很多流行的期权定价模型，比如随机波动率模型（例如Heston模型和Bates模型），各种具有随机波动率/强度的指数Levy模型（例如具有随机波动率/强度的Kou模型），以及具有体制转换的随机波动率模型（例如具有体制转换的Heston模型和Bates模型）。这种希尔伯特变换方法的一个具有吸引力的特征是它非常准确和快速，通常具有指数衰减的离散误差和截断误差。 更具体地说，我们将通过以下三个步骤来完成该研究项目。 (1) 在具有体制转换的指数Levy模型下，我们计划推导出关于离散观测的障碍期权价格和百慕大期权价格在傅里叶空间上的倒向递推公式。(2) 在具有体制转换的指数Levy模型下，我们将尝试利用Feng和Linetsky （2008，2009）提出的著名的sinc展开近似方法对(1)中得到的两个倒向递推公式进行求解，从而给出这两种期权的准确快速的定价算法。(3) 在具有体制转换及随机波动率/强度的指数Levy模型下，我们计划给出一种结合希尔伯特变换和CTMC逼近的定价方法对离散观测的障碍期权和百慕大期权进行定价。首先，我们准备通过CTMC逼近和双层体制转换的整合把这种模型转化成具有体制转换的指数Levy模型。然后用之前已经给出的希尔伯特变换方法对转化后的具有体制转换的指数Levy模型上的离散观测的障碍期权和百慕大期权进行定价。

16205217.label: Realisation of objectives
16205217.value: In this project, I have achieved the project objectives by developing a Hilbert transform approach to pricing discrete barrier options and Bermudan options under various multidimensional option pricing models. More specifically, we have proposed a unified Hilbert transform method to price discrete barrier options, Bermudan options, and discrete lookback options under a rich class of multidimensional option pricing models with closed-form partial Fourier transforms, which includes various regime-switching exponential Levy models, stochastic volatility models with/without Levy jumps, and time-changed Levy models as special cases. We first derive the respective backward recursions in state space for the prices of these three types of path-dependent options under these multidimensional models. An important step is that we obtain double backward recursions in state space for the discrete lookback option price by overcoming the difficulty of nonexistence of valid damping factors via a decomposition technique. Then we construct their respective Hilbert transform based backward recursions in Fourier space in a unified way by taking advantage of the closed-form partial Fourier transforms of these multidimensional models and derive the pricing formulas of these three types of path-dependent options in terms of the solutions to their respective backward recursions in Fourier space. Numerical pricing algorithms for these three types of path-dependent options based on the accurate and efficient computations of Hilbert transforms and Fourier inversion have been developed. Numerical experiments indicate that our pricing algorithms are accurate and efficient under a wide range of multidimensional option pricing models. Moreover, a Hilbert transform approach combined with Malliavin calculus based expansions has been proposed to pricing various types of discrete barrier options under multidimensional jump diffusion models with multifactor stochastic volatility. More specifically, we first employ the Malliavin calculus based expansion techniques to express the discrete barrier option price as an asymptotic expansion. Then we construct a sequence of backward recursions in state space each corresponding to the computation of one term in the derived asymptotic expansion and manage to express each backward recursion in state space in terms of double convolutions. Finally, a Hilbert transform based backward recursion in Fourier space is established for each backward recursion in state space, and the pricing formula of the discrete barrier option is then obtained in terms of the solutions to these backward recursions in Fourier space. A numerical pricing algorithm has been developed to implement the pricing formula, and numerical results have demonstrated its high accuracy and efficiency under a broad range of multidimensional option pricing models. In addition, we have also investigated the decomposition of first passage probabilities via transform inversion, and the obtained results are potentially useful in the hedging of many path-dependent options.

16205217.label: Major findings and research outcome
16205217.value: Major findings and research outcome of this project are detailed as follows. A unified Hilbert transform approach has been developed to pricing discrete barrier options, Bermudan options, and discrete lookback options under a rich class of multidimensional option pricing models, which includes various regime-switching exponential Levy models, stochastic volatility models with/without Levy jumps, and time-changed Levy models as special cases. This is made possible mainly because we have obtained the respective backward recursions in state space for the prices of these path-dependent options under these multidimensional models and have also established the corresponding Hilbert transform based backward recursions in Fourier space in a unified way. Accurate and efficient pricing algorithms based on Hilbert transforms and Fourier inversion have been developed to compute the prices of these path-dependent options numerically. Moreover, we have proposed a Hilbert transform method combined with Malliavin calculus based expansions to price various types of discrete barrier options under multidimensional jump diffusion models with multifactor stochastic volatility by deriving an asymptotic expansion for the discrete barrier option price and by constructing a sequence of Hilbert transform based backward recursions in Fourier space for computing different terms of the asymptotic expansion. In addition, some decomposition results for first passage probabilities have also been derived via transform inversion and can be potentially used for the study of the hedging of many path-dependent options.

16205217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16205217.value: In this project, we have proposed a Hilbert transform method combined with Malliavin calculus based expansions to price discrete barrier options under multidimensional jump diffusion models with multifactor stochastic volatility. Potential future research problems might include the development of a similar pricing method that combines Hilbert transforms with Malliavin calculus based expansions for discrete lookback options. This problem is quite different due to the different payoffs of discrete lookback options. A potential approach might be to develop a recursive expansion pricing method by using Malliavin calculus to derive an asymptotic expansion for the discrete lookback option price and by establishing a sequence of convolution based backward recursions in state space and Hilbert transform based backward recursions in Fourier space for computing the asymptotic expansion.

16205217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16205217.value: Option pricing has been a fundamentally significant research topic in finance. Discrete barrier options, Bermudan options, and discrete lookback options are among the most important path-dependent options in the derivatives market. However, it is very challenging to price them accurately and efficiently under multidimensional option pricing models. In this project, we have proposed a unified Hilbert transform approach to pricing all of them under a rich class of multidimensional models that includes various regime-switching exponential Levy models, stochastic volatility models with/without Levy jumps, and time-changed Levy models as special cases. Moreover, a Hilbert transform method combined with Malliavin calculus based expansions has also been developed to price discrete barrier options under multidimensional jump diffusion models with multifactor stochastic volatility. Numerical results indicate that our pricing methods are accurate and efficient. Theoretically, to the best of our knowledge, we provide one of the first approaches to pricing discrete barrier options, Bermudan options, and discrete lookback options in a unified way under multidimensional models. In practice, our research offers accurate and efficient methods for pricing these path-dependent options under multidimensional models, thereby helping market participants to make better financial decisions.

16205317.value: 渦扇航空發動機的葉輪機械，如風扇和壓氣機葉片等，在高速旋轉時所産生的模態噪聲會誘發聲腔共振從而影響葉片使 用壽命，還會輻射到遠場影響適航認證。基于傳聲器陣列的氣動噪聲測試能直觀揭示相關物理 機制、評估和改進葉輪機械設計，是當前航空發動機研發中的重要測試工具之一。我們會結合理論模型、數值模擬和實驗研究，彼此依託、循序漸進，發展航空發動機的旋轉機械噪聲測試方法和測試系統。具體來說，本項目將針對旋轉部件氣動噪聲的氣動特征，發展關鍵實驗技術、設計和製造測試系統實驗台。首先計畫從小波分析和壓縮感知兩個新技術招手，擴展傳統波束形成方法，從而發展高速旋轉葉片的實時噪聲源成像技術；其次是繼續發展我們前期的Wiener-Hopf方法，發展安裝聲襯後的噪聲成像和模態提取測試能力；第三是設計測試陣列儀器、並完善引導 性風扇噪聲測試台，加入聲襯模塊和背景流動模擬能力，驗證和演示所開發的新試驗技術。

16205317.label: Realisation of objectives
16205317.value: We have developed two different types of testing methods for azimuthal mode detection of duct acoustics, one new method for radial mode detection, and conducted some guiding studies of testing methods for duct health monitoring, all based on inverse scattering and sensor arrays. Next, we have developed numerical simulations based on the in-house linearized Euler solver to verify and validate the proposed testing methods in the presence of stationary and low Mach number background flows, respectively. Finally, we have designed and established a duct acoustic testing rig in the anechoic wind tunnel facility at HKUST to experimentally verify and demonstrate the developed testing methods. All the above realizations have led to a series of publications and details can be found below in this report.

16205317.label: Major findings and research outcome
16205317.value: A series of compressive sensing methods have been considered and developed to surpass the sampling limitation imposed by the classical Shannon-Nyquist sampling theorem. Both the azimuthal and radial mode detection problems have been considered and the proposed compressive-sensing-based methods have been developed and, then, examined in numerical simulations and experiments. The tests and examinations have shown that reasonably good accuracy can be achieved with a significantly reduced number of sensors by using the proposed compressive-sensing-based methods. Besides, the proposed method is more advantageous in terms of the performance and flexibility in the arrangement of the sensors. Next, an experimental demonstration testing platform has been designed and established at HKUST. The rig consists of a spinning mode synthesizer, a couple of microphone arrays, and the enclosed sections. The first is for the purpose of simulating aircraft engine fan noise at various frequencies and spatial modes. The second is for the mode detection task. The third can be connected to a wind tunnel to accommodate and, thereafter, to study the effects of background flows. A lined section can be included in future works to further study liner (acoustic absorber) design and the corresponding mode testing methods. Besides, to study the possible defect scenarios, the enclosed duct has been modified to simulate hole/intrusion cases.

16205317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16205317.value: Some of the guiding studies about the array design strategy and the associated optimization method have been conducted to showcase the potential applications of the new testing method. On top of the numerical simulations, the idea of the fan noise health monitoring has been conceptually demonstrated in the wind tunnel tests, by taking account of possible accidental scenarios such as foreign body intrusions. Under such circumstances, it has been observed that remarkable changes appear in the azimuthal mode spectrum from the fan noise, which can be used to infer the health status of aircraft engine fan assembly, which should be possible for practical engine setups. To fully study the potential of this concept, we need to design more test set-ups and discuss them with field engineers.

16205317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16205317.value: In this work, we have developed a couple of new experimental methods for noise testings of duct acoustics. The potential applications can be found in aircraft engine. The research combines the compressive sensing method, which is an emerging theoretical method in information technology, and classical testing methods in aerospace engineering in general and aeroacoustics in particular. The proposed new methods from our group have received very positive feedbacks from the community and industry. For example, the recent works from the groups in France and Germany cited our works. Moreover, the recent work from the mainland, which received more than 20M RMB research funding, exactly follows our research work (according to their most recent AIAA publications). Overall, our work shall help the design, development and evaluation of silent aircraft aeroengines.

16205517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16205517.value: The miniaturization of electronic devices and electric power systems drives the search for new materials for energy storage and thermal management that enable more efficient storage and management of the electricity and heat generated from those systems. Polymer composites with functional fillers are excellent candidates because of their low density, good processability and tunable functional properties. In particular, polymer composites with exceptionally high thermal conductivities (TCs) but ultra-low electrical conductivities (ECs) are of potential interest to a number of emerging applications, such as thermal interface materials (TIMs) and high-temperature polymer dielectrics. However, designing such composites is a challenging task since the increase in TCs usually accompanies the increase in ECs, and previous numerous attempts have shown only limited success. To tackle such challenges, we propose to develop highly thermally conductive and electrically insulating polymer composites containing hybrid fillers of graphene and boron nitride (BN) sheets, in an effort to fully exploit the exceptional TCs of graphene and ultra-low ECs of BN sheets, chosen from a myriad of emerging two dimensional (2D) materials. Both the mono- or few-layer graphene oxide (GO) and BN sheets with large lateral sizes and aspect ratios will be prepared using an intercalation-thermal expansion-exfoliation process established in our lab. GO and BN sheets will be simultaneously reduced and functionalized to improve the intrinsic TCs of reduced GO (rGO) and facilitate chemical bonding between rGO and BN. A novel bidirectional freeze-casting technique will be used to fabricate highly-aligned graphene-BN aerogels for TIM applications. The aerogel walls containing BN sheets chemically crosslinked with rGO will provide continuous pathway for phonon transport while effectively blocking the electron tunneling between conductive rGO sheets. In addition, layered graphene/BN/graphene composites will be fabricated by two-step deposition and planar stacking for high-temperature dielectric applications. The highly aligned graphene/BN/graphene sandwich will form numerous nano-capacitors that provide excellent dielectric constant and dielectric strength, while the BN sheets are expected to isolate the graphene to suppress the electron tunneling and the associated dielectric loss. The excellent TCs arising from the aligned graphene and BN sheets are also expected to improve the dielectric properties under high-temperature conditions by dissipating the heat generated due to dielectric loss. The material system developed in this project will have a wide range of emerging applications, such as thermal management of wearable electronics, converters for electric vehicles and aerospace power electronics. 電子器件和電力系統的微型化極大推動了具有更加高效地存儲電能和耗散熱量功能的新型儲能材料與熱耗散材料的研究。因為具有密度低，加工性能良好，以及功能特性可控等優勢，功能性填充物高分子複合材料是此類新型材料的絕佳選擇。特別是具有優異的導熱性能但是超低的導電性能的高分子複合材料，他們很有希望被應用在很多新興領域中，例如熱界面材料和高溫介電高分子材料。然而，設計此種複合材料具有很大的難度，因為通常來說材料的導電性能會隨著導熱性能的提高而提高，之前很多的嘗試因而也鮮有成功。為了解決以上的問題，我們提出了應用石墨烯和氮化硼這兩種非常有應用前景的二維材料的混合物作為填充物來製備具有導熱絕緣性能的高分子複合材料，以充分利用石墨烯的優異導熱性能和氮化硼的超低導電性能。我們將應用自己研發的插層-熱膨脹-剝離的製備工藝來製備具有大橫向尺寸以及縱橫比的單層和多層的氧化石墨烯和氮化硼片層。氧化石墨烯和氮化硼的片層將同時被還原以及官能團化，以提高還原氧化石墨烯的導熱性，並且促進還原氧化石墨稀和氮化硼之間的化學鍵結。一種創新的雙向冷凍鑄造工藝將會被用來製造具有高度取向結構的石墨烯-氮化硼氣凝膠，以將其應用在熱界面材料中。由化學交聯的氮化硼與還原氧化石墨烯構成的氣凝膠孔壁將會為聲子傳輸提供連續的通道，并同時有效地阻擋導電的還原氧化石墨烯之間的電子隧道效應。另外，兩步沉積和平面疊加的方法將被用於製造層狀的石墨烯/氮化硼/石墨烯複合材料，以應用在高溫介電材料中。這種高度取向的石墨烯/氮化硼/石墨烯三明治結構將會形成大量納米尺度的電容器，使得材料具有優異的介電常數和介電強度。同時，氮化硼片層可以將石墨烯分離開來，以降低電子隧道效應，從而降低介電損耗。由於具有高度取向的石墨烯和氮化硼的結構，此種材料的導熱性能將會非常高，可以有效耗散由於介電損耗產生的熱量，使得其很有希望被作為高溫環境下的介電材料。本項目研發的材料體系將會有非常廣泛的應用前景，例如可穿戴電子產品中的熱耗散材料，電動汽車中的整流器，以及航天動力電子設備。

16205517.label: Realisation of objectives
16205517.value: Significant progress has been made in realization of the objectives, producing many original results published in high-impact journals. The efforts made to achieve the objectives are summarized below. Objective 1: To develop methods to synthesize mono- or few-layer h-BN sheets in aqueous solution with large lateral sizes and high aspect ratios Two methods have been developed to synthesis mono- or few-layer h-BN sheets using urea-assisted ball milling and NaOH-assisted liquid phase exfoliation. First, a urea assisted ball milling method was developed to synthesis hexagonal-boron nitride (h-BN) nanosheets. The application of urea was effective in assisting exfoliation and protecting the BN nanosheets from excessive mechanical damage to their lattice structure. The thickness and size of h-BN nanosheets are measured by atomic force microscope (AFM) height profiles, achieving an average diameter of 0.39 μm and an average layer number of 3.9. The high crystalline quality of h-BN nanosheets is confirmed by typical hexagonal spot patterns, XRD patterns and FTIR spectra. (J1, J8) Second, a three-step exfoliation method comprising “pre-treatment–intercalation–exfoliation” was developed to achieve large-area, ultrathin sheets. The h-BN precursors consisted of thick, large BN platelets, which became thinner after pre-treatment with Brønsted acid and more flexible with NaOH intercalation. After microwave-assisted exfoliation at 600 W for 60 s, ultrathin BN nanosheets with lateral sizes of over 1 µm were achieved, as confirmed by the scanning electron microscopy (SEM) image. The microwave power of 600 W used for exfoliation was chosen to avoid excessive damage so that large lateral sizes were maintained. The AFM image further confirmed BN nanosheets with a large lateral size of ≈ 2 µm and a thickness ranging 4–14 nm. The rough surface morphology as a result of wrinkles attests to the flexibility of BN nanosheets because of their high aspect ratios. (C1, J3) Objective 2: To fabricate highly aligned graphene-BN aerogels and their polymer composites with high TCs and low ECs by bidirectional freeze-casting for TIM and high-temperature dielectric applications The effect of graphene and BN orientation on the thermal conductivity of polymer composites was examined first. A thorough investigation was carried out to probe the different methods used to achieve aligned graphene and BN in polymer composites. Compared with other techniques, the freeze-casting strategy is capable of controlling the spatial arrangement and orientation of thermally conductive fillers, leading to rich microstructures encompassing isotropic, cellular, lamellar, and radial structures for the rational design of electron and heat conduction pathways, giving rise to generally higher TC of composites at similar filler loadings for thermal management and dielectric applications. (J7, J9) Graphene aerogel (GA)/poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) composites with a highly aligned porous structure are produced by simultaneous unidirectional freeze casting. A new two-step process was developed to apply insulating barriers between the aligned networks to avoid direct contacts between the neighboring conductive skeletons. The resulting composites coated with barriers exhibited exceptional insulating properties for a low EC of 10–5 S m–1. (C2) The highly-aligned structure also endowed the composites with improved mechanical properties. (C3) Pure graphene web/polymer composite was fabricated by a versatile chemical vapor deposition technique. The continuous high-quality in-plane graphene network led to exceptional electrical and thermal conductivities of 50 S cm-1 and 8.8Wm-1K-1, respectively, ideal for TIM applications. (J2) BN aerogels were fabricated by a solvent-assisted directional freeze-casting method with a tailored alignment channel structure. The acetone in the PVA suspension enlarges the cell walls to suppress the shrinkage, giving rise to a lower density and a higher porosity. The aligned structure brought about significant anisotropic TCs of the BN aerogels with the TC in the alignment direction being more than two times higher than that in the transverse direction. (J8) Graphene/BN/graphene microlaminates were fabricated using a novel, two-step bidirectional freeze casting process. It is found that the microlaminates of hybrid composites can fully exploit the high thermal conductivities of both BN nanosheets and graphene, as well as the excellent dielectric properties of BN nanosheets. The obtained microlaminate composites consisting of alternating rGO and h-BN nanosheets embedded in a polyurethane (PU) matrix delivered a remarkable dielectric constant of 1084 with a low dielectric loss of 0.091 and low EC of ~ 10-8 S/cm at 1 kHz. By virtue of synergy arising from both the rGO−PU layers with a high dielectric constant and the BN−PU barrier layers with a high dielectric strength, the microlaminate composites presented a maximum energy density of 22.7 J/cm3, 44 folds of the neat rGO−PU composite acting alone, ideal for dielectric applications. (J1) Objective 3: To fabricate polymer composites containing sandwich-structured graphene/BN/graphene sheets with high TCs, high k, low dielectric loss and high Eb for high-temperature dielectric applications To understand the effect of filler structures and orientations on the TCs of composites, we critically reviewed the TCs of composites containing 2D fillers of different structures. The high in-plane TCs of graphene and BN nanosheets (BNNS) can be fully utilized when they are aligned to afford excellent thermal dissipation in the alignment direction. (J4) In order to find the most suitable technique to fabricate the highly aligned structures with sandwich-structured rGO/BN/rGO layers, we systematically reviewed the state-of-the-art strategies to rationally assemble the 2D nanofillers into bulk composites. (J5) We developed a new sequential bidirectional freeze-casting (BFC) technique to rational assemble 2D BNNS and rGO sheets into distinctively separated, highly aligned laminates within the PI matrix. The alternating layers of BNNS-PI and rGO-PI composites formed numerous micro-capacitors where the conductive rGO-PI layers significantly improved the dielectric constant, while the insulating BNNS-PI layers blocked the tunneling of electrons, to the benefit of high breakdown strengths. The distinctively separated rGO and BNNS layers in the highly aligned structure synergistically contributed to high thermal conductivities of nanocomposites. Therefore, the hybrid architecture with optimized filler contents gave rise to multifunctional properties, including a high dielectric constant (~579), a low dielectric loss (0.25), a high thermal conductivity (1.49 W m-1 K-1) and a moderate breakdown strength (74.4 MV m-1), resulting in a dielectric material with a high energy density (14.2 J cm-3) and an excellent thermal management capability. (J3) Objective 4: To formulate a model(s) to understand the phonon transport in BN-graphene/polymer composites using molecular dynamics simulations The experimental results indicate that the micro-sandwich composites containing distinctively separated rGO and BNNS layers showed ~ 50 % higher thermal conductivities than those with walls made of randomly mixed rGO and BNNS. To understand the synergistic effect of the micro-sandwich structure, we carried out a series of molecular dynamics simulations to scrutinize the thermal transports across different interfaces, including BNNS/BNNS (B/B), graphene/graphene (G/G) and graphene/BNNS (G/B) interfaces. The interfacial thermal conductance (ITC) at homogeneous interfaces, i.e., G/G and B/B interfaces were about 84 and 61 % higher than that of the heterogeneous interface, i.e., G/B interface. Further probe into the vibrational power spectra suggests that the two layers across G/B interface showed distinctively different VPS with little overlapping area under the curves, whereas almost identical VPS were observed for the two layers consisting of either G/G or B/B combination. This means that better phonon vibrational couplings were achieved between the two layers with identical structures than those with heterogenous compositions, thus giving rise to higher ITCs in the former. (J3, J6)

16205517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16205517.value: Based on the findings from this project, future work will be focused on the following aspects. (i) Further improving the TC by surface modification. Surface modification of graphene and BN by introducing functional groups is effective in improving the thermal transport between the fillers and matrix in dispersed composites. However, it is not clear if surface modification will benefit the TC of 3D network composites. The effect of functionalization of graphene and BN on the intrinsic and interfacial thermal conduction will be investigated to understand their effects on the TCs of composites. (ii) Large-scale fabrication techniques based on freeze-casting. The current technique by using a single cold source can only achieve a short freezing distance, resulting in small samples with limited sizes. To scale up the freeze-casting technique, novel fabrication techniques will be developed by using a moving cold source to allow continuous freezing of samples over a long distance. (iii) Other potential applications by exploring the highly aligned structures. In addition to TIM and dielectric applications, the unique alignment structures of graphene and BN aerogels will be further explored for other emerging applications such as thermal insulation, radiative cooling, and solar-thermal conversion by optimizing the microstructures.

16205517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16205517.value: The miniaturization of electronic devices and electric power systems drives the search for new materials for energy storage and thermal management that enable more efficient storage and management of the electricity and heat generated from those systems. This project aims to develop polymer composites containing two-dimensional (2D) nanofillers with exceptionally high thermal conductivities (TCs) but ultra-low electrical conductivities (ECs) for thermal interface materials (TIMs) and polymer dielectrics. Large-size boron nitride and graphene sheets have been synthesized by ball milling and NaOH assisted exfoliation, which are further assembled into aerogels with highly aligned cell walls by the freeze-casting technique. In particular, a sequential freeze-casting technique is developed to rational assemble 2D boron nitride and graphene sheets into distinctively separated, highly aligned laminates within the polymer matrix. The alternating layers of boron nitride and graphene formed numerous micro-capacitors, synergistically contributing to high dielectric constant, low dielectric loss, and high TCs of nanocomposites. The material system developed in this project will have a wide range of emerging applications, such as thermal management of wearable electronics, converters for electric vehicles, and aerospace power electronics.

16205617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16205617.value: Free-form surfaces are widely used in the design of products with high and strict precision requirements, such as turbines and blisks, high precision lenses, biomedical components, etc. For purpose of error analysis in quality control and model reconstruction in reverse engineering, the geometric information of free-from surfaces should be retrieved both precisely and efficiently. For free-form surface inspection, the most accurate and effective way is by means of a Coordinate Measuring Machine (CMM). Traditionally, the inspection is carried out on a three-axis CMM where a series of discretized points are firstly sampled on the design surface and then inspected in a point-by-point manner. Due to this discontinuous and manual nature, the inspection efficiency is extremely low, often taking hours or even days for large-size parts. To address this problem, a novel five-axis sweep scanning technology has been developed recently. Instead of working in a point-by-point manner, the probe of the five-axis inspection machine constantly touches the surface and sweeps on it continuously in the inspection process, thus tremendously reducing the operation time. However, currently the planning of the five-axis sweep scanning path still depends heavily on human intervention. More critically, the existing five-axis sweep scanning path planning methods, in both academia and industry, rely solely on the geometry of the surface, without considering the unique kinematic and dynamic properties of the five-axis inspection machine itself. As a result, the capabilities of the five-axis inspection machine are often severely under-utilized and the inspection efficiency cannot be guaranteed. To overcome the above problem, an automatic five-axis sweep scanning path planning system for free-form surfaces will be developed in this project. By analyzing the unique kinematical configuration of the five-axis inspection machine, the critical factors that affect the inspection efficiency are first recognized and, based on the findings, two machine-based continuous five-axis sweep scanning path generation methods are proposed, both of which aim at reducing the kinematical loading on the inspection machine’s bottleneck axes, thus improving the overall inspection efficiency. Afterwards, for the already generated sweep scanning path, an optimal scheduling algorithm will be developed that strives to assign the maximum sweep speed under the kinematic and dynamic constraints of the machine, with the inspection accuracy upheld. The final developed system is expected to significantly outperform the current five-axis sweep scanning path planning methods in the level of automation, streamlining of operation, and the most of all the efficiency.

16205617.label: Major findings and research outcome
16205617.value: By carefully designing the stylus orientation and the tip point trajectory adaptive to the shape of the part-to-inspect and the kinematics of the five-axis inspection machine, the thus planned sweeping path is able to tremendously reduce the total inspection time while upholding the required inspection accuracy. The algorithm developed from this project has achieved this task. In our both computation and physical inspection tests, against some leading benchmarks, our sweeping scanning inspection path reduced the total inspection time by as much as 80%. To validate the developed sweep scanning path generation method from the project, the PC contacted the Northwestern Polytechnical University (西北工业大学) in China and tested the method in several of their industrial projects of blade inspection. The test results confirm the superiority of our method over some leading commercial sweep scanning path generation software systems in terms of (significantly) reducing the total inspection time while upholding the same inspection accuracy.

16205617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16205617.value: 1. Our developed algorithm is a general algorithm, which means it applies to an arbitrary shape of part. However, for some special shapes, e.g., a barrel shape, perhaps a better and specific sweeping scanning path could be devised, which requires a target analysis of the specific shape. 2. Currently, the global collision avoidance is very limited in our solution, which can be extended.

16205617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16205617.value: For quality control of a machined part, measurement of the part's geometry is extremely important. The traditional 3-axis or 3+2-axis CMM (coordinated measuring machine) technique has been the dominant means for this task. As both of them are point-wise processes, i.e., the probe needs to slowly approach the inspection point, makes contact at the point (thus acquiring its XYZ coordinates), and then finally retracts back to a safety position, and considering there are typically thousands or tens of thousands of points to inspect, it usually takes very long time to complete a CMM inspection process (e.g., longer than 24 hours to inspect a blade of 1m long). 5-axis sweeping scanning CMM inspection is an emerging technology which allows the probe to continuously change its orientation and lets the tip point of the stylus keep contact with the surface of part and sweep on it. As a result, the slow approach-contact-retract operation is removed, and the total inspection time is tremendously reduced (by 90% or more). However, as the CMM now is five-axis, how to automatically plan a sweeping scanning path is much more difficult. The goal of this project is exactly to develop such an algorithm.

16205717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16205717.value: The Thick Film Copper technology which is simpler and more environmental friendly has started to replace photolithography on Direct Bonded Copper to fabricate interconnects for power electronics. The interconnect patterns are directly deposited as tracks or films on a substrate by screen or stencil printing process using a thick film copper paste. After sintering, the conductive copper thick film is formed on the substrate. However, a high temperature (>900 °C) is required for sintering a film printed with a copper micro-flakes paste, while film cracking might occur if the paste is made up of copper nanoparticles. In this proposed research, a thick film conductive paste using a mixture of copper micro-flakes and nanoparticles will be developed to ameliorate the problems mentioned above. It is expected that the film printed with the paste containing bimodal particles could be sintered at a much lower temperature and the presence of flakes could suppress the formation of cracks during sintering. 傳統的光刻技術已經開始被厚膜銅技術所取代，並應用於高電流電子板制作中。原理是通過使用厚膜銅漿用絲網印刷方法將電路圖案直接印刷在基材上，再經過燒結或焙燒，在基板上形成導電銅厚膜。 然而，如果只用微米大小的銅顆粒作填料，燒結將需要非常高溫（> 900℃）；如果只用納米銅顆粒作填料則可以大大降低燒結時所需的溫度，但容易使厚膜銅破裂。 在此研究中，我們將開發一種含有微米和納米銅顆粒的厚膜導電膏，以改善上述問題。 目標是使用含有雙峰分佈顆粒的銅漿印刷的薄膜後，可以在低溫度下燒結，並且在可以抑制燒結過程中的形成裂縫 。

16205717.label: Realisation of objectives
16205717.value: All the project objectives were achieved. In this project, a low sintering temperature conductive paste for thick film printing was developed and the corresponding sintering behavior was studied. Thick film printing typically starts from preparing a conductive paste from its components, which involves the dispersion of the solid content (conductive fillers and adhesive elements) in the organic vehicle with additives (dispersants, rheology modifiers, and others); screen printing of the conductive paste on the target substrate; drying the wet film; and curing or sintering it afterwards. The physical properties of the paste will change throughout the screening printing processes and therefore the product must satisfy completely different sets of attributes. To satisfy these product attributes, we should select the paste formulation, such as the selection of component materials, and their corresponding amount; and the processing conditions, such as the screen-printing, drying and sintering conditions, carefully. However, as these parameters are highly interrelated, it is not easy to adjust a product attribute without affecting others. To have a proper understanding of the relationships between the parameters and the target product attributes; and translate these qualitative product attributes into quantitative produce specifications that can be used in the formulation process, quality function deployments (QFDs) are usually employed. We developed screen-printable conductive paste with compositions exhibited as follows. Composition of the formulated conductive paste Components Chemicals Mass percent (wt%) Conductive fillers Copper particles 85 Additive Rheology modifier 5 Adhesion elements Glass Frits 4 Solvent alpha-terpineol 6 The copper fillers with desired particle size, the rheology modifier, glass frits and alpha-terpineol were mixed overnight at a desired composition. Alumina substrates were ultrasonic cleaned in acetone for 30 min and dried at room temperature. The formulated copper pastes were printed on the substrates through a 325-mesh polyimide screen with a circular pattern (ø16mm). The printed film was dried in the tube furnace under the nitrogen atmosphere at 150 °C for 40 min and then sintered with the desired temperature profile. After the cooling to room temperature, the thick film was retrieved from the tube furnace and store in a vacuum desiccator, ready for further characterization. The particle size and morphology of purchased copper powders were observed by scanning transmission microscope, while synthesized copper nanoparticles were observed by transmission electron microscope. Thermogravimetry analysis (TGA) and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) characterization of the copper conductive paste and the copper nanoparticles were carried out under a nitrogen atmosphere at a heating rate of 5 °C/ min from 25 to 400 °C and 25 to 600 °C, respectively. The cross-section and top view images of the sintered copper film were obtained through scanning transmission microscope Energy-Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy to observe the structure of the sintered film. By using procedure and experimental method as mention above, the effect with different size of filler on the quality of the conductive film were first studied. A bimodal paste with both copper nanoparticle and microparticle was further formulated. By adjusting the ratio of copper nanoparticle and microparticle, the structure of sintered film can be manipulated and then gain optimized performance. The effect of glass frits on the paste were further reviewed and studied. Finally, the effect of sintering profile and thickness on the film quality were studied.

16205717.label: Major findings and research outcome
16205717.value: In this project, a low sintering temperature conductive paste for thick film printing was developed and the corresponding sintering behavior was studied. First, candidates for the bimodal size copper filler were selected. Microsized copper powder were formulated and sintered at 500˚C and 950˚C for 60 min at a heating rate of 15˚C/min. By measuring the electrical performance of the sintered film and characterizing using SEM/TEM, it was found that 10 µm copper powder remained loose powders at both sintering temperatures which was not further considered. 1 µm and 0.1 µm copper paste were both well-sintered at 950˚C and exhibited similar volume resistivity at both peak temperatures. However, compared with 1 µm film at 500˚C, 0.1 µm powder would aggregate and might lead to cracks on the film. Therefore, 1 µm copper powder was chosen as micro-sized copper filler in the bimodal paste. Next, the effect of the mass ratio of micro-to-nano sized particles on the film conductivity was studied. Copper film containing bimodal fillers with micro-to-nano sized particle mass ratio of 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5 and 3 were prepared and sintered at 500˚C for 60 min at a heating rate of 15˚C/min. The optimal mass ratio was 2 (66.7 wt% of micro-sized copper powder in copper filler) with the lowest volume resistivity of 6.27×10-8 Ω·m. This optimal formulation would be further studied. The sintering time of the optimal formulation of bimodal copper paste was investigated. Various sintering time was investigated and the volume resistivity to sintering time plot showed that sintering at peak temperature for 10 min could help enhance the final performance of the sintered film which was 4.43×10-8 Ω·m in volume resistivity. Finally, bimodal copper pastes with glass frits were studied. All the other variable remained unchanged during paste preparation, printing and heating. It can be found that with the help of glass frits, especially the TeO2-V2O5 based glass frits, the adhesion strength of the sintered copper film was enhanced at the expense of a minor volume resistivity increase from 4.43×10-8 Ω·m to 9.10×10-8 Ω·m.

16205717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16205717.value: 6.2 Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action In this project an optimal mass ratio of micro-to-nano copper particles and an optimal sintering profile were found. However, a more specific mass ratio can be investigated to further increase the packing density of green film and conductivity of sintered copper film. Also, heating rate before baking and sintering and the peak temperature can be studied to make the heating profile of the bimodal copper paste complete. More glass frits should be studied to figure out the function of each component and effectiveness of each type of glass frits. The peak temperature should be lowered to around 400˚C so that flash sintering can be applied on the bimodal copper thick paste. Besides the X-cut test, quantified test such as tensile test and shear strength test should also be carried out. Also, to expand the application, a modification on the bimodal paste should be deployed to be compatible with more types of substrates such as silicon for solar cell, aluminum nitride for powder devices or even polymer for flexible circuits.

16205717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16205717.value: Copper conductive paste is a promising material in electronic device market than silver or noble metal paste for its high conductivity and solderability as well as low electro-migration and cost. However, the harsh sintering conditions such as high temperature and inert atmosphere limit the application of copper paste from further commercialization. In this project, copper thick film paste is developed via utilizing proposed bimodal size distribution of copper as metal filler to reduce the sintering temperature. A temperature profile and glass frits additives are also studied to optimize the heating process and enhance the copper film electrical and mechanical performance. A bimodal paste with Ø50 nm and Ø2 μm at 33.3wt% of copper nanoparticles have the best performance where the sheet resistance reached 2.82 mΩ/□ at 25 μm thickness.

16206217.label: Project Objectives
16206217.value: To analyse the initiation and progression of hillslope erosion, sliding and debris flows during a rainstorm based on historic landslide records in Hong Kong from 1924 to 2014; To develop an integrated numerical model to simulate the initiation and progression of rain-induced hillslope erosion and debris flows; To predict likely hillslope erosion, landslide and debris flow hazards as basis for engineering design in the Hong Kong context.

16206217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16206217.value: A large rainstorm can trigger more than 2,000 hillslope washout failures, landslides and debris flows in Hong Kong. During a rainstorm, a part of the rainwater infiltrates into the hillslope and triggers landslides due to either the generation of positive pore-water pressure or the loss of soil suction. The excess rainwater becomes surface runoff, causing severe erosion of the slope surface and washout failures. The surface erosion will also steepen the slope and promote sliding failures. The detached materials from erosion or slope failures may mix with the runoff water and develop into a hillslope debris flow. While rain-induced landslides have been studied extensively, how slope surface erosion and debris flows are initiated on a hillslope during a rainstorm is less understood. Are the triggering rainfall thresholds for hillslope erosion, sliding and debris flows the same? Is their progression at the same pace? How do the magnitudes of the separate hillslope hazards increase with rainfall intensity? These questions must be answered in developing landslide mitigation strategies. The primary objective of this research project is to analyse the initiation and progression of surface erosion and debris flows on a hillslope during a rainstorm. The objective will be achieved through three research tasks. In Task 1, how hillslope erosion, sliding and debris flows developed in numerous past large storms in Hong Kong will be examined and empirical rainfall thresholds for these hillslope hazards will be developed based on a database of over 20,000 landslides in Hong Kong during the period of 1924-2014. Given the basic understanding attained from Task 1, an integrated numerical model will be developed in Task 2 to simulate the initiation and progression of rain-induced hillslope erosion and debris flows. A mathematical model developed by the PI and his co-workers will be extended to enable simulation of the initiation and progression of the hillslope hazards. In Task 3, the numerical code will be validated using well-controlled centrifuge models, and applied to simulate likely hillslope hazards in the Hong Kong context to assist in developing strategies for landslide risk mitigation. Breakthroughs will be made in the simulation of the initiation of slope erosion and debris flows by modelling transport of landslide and erosion masses in a physically-based manner. The research outcomes will also provide a theoretical basis for addressing the increasing hillslope erosion and debris flow problems in Hong Kong as storms become more frequent. 在香港，一場暴雨可誘發2000多處坡面沖蝕、滑坡和泥石流災害。在降雨過程中，部分雨水入滲到地下而引起土體強度降低和坡體失穩。地面徑流又導致坡面沖蝕，使坡面坡度增加而加劇坡體失穩。滑坡和沖蝕的土體在地面徑流作用下進而演變為泥石流。目前對滑坡機理研究較多，但對坡面沖蝕和泥石流的啟動規律卻知之甚少，對沖蝕、滑坡和泥石流這三個物理過程的啟動雨量和發展規律更缺乏認識。本科研課題的主要目的，就是分析研究坡面沖蝕和泥石流的啟動及發展規律。本課題分為三個子題。在子題1中，將根據香港1924-2014三十年間記錄到的20000多滑坡泥石流案例，研究沖蝕、滑坡和泥石流的實際發生情況和經驗規律。在子題2中，將突破目前單災害過程模擬的現狀，開發出模擬沖蝕、滑坡和泥石流全過程的數值模型和計算程式。在子體3中，將利用該全過程數值模型預測香港在多種暴雨情景中可能發生的沖蝕和滑坡泥石流災害過程，為制定香港的防災減災措施提供科學依據。

16206217.label: Realisation of objectives
16206217.value: (1) Analysis of the initiation and progression of hillslope erosion, sliding and debris flows during a rainstorm based on historic landslide records in Hong Kong from 1924 to 2014 The initiation and magnitudes of historic open hillslope landslides and channelized debris flows in Hong Kong are assessed based on the Enhanced Natural Terrain Landslide Inventory (ENTLI) from 1924 to 2014. The statistical distributions of both the open hillslope landslides and channelized debris flows are established. Correlations between maximum rolling rainfall and landslide frequency, scar area and volume are derived. The rainfall intensity-duration thresholds are proposed for identifying the likely rainfall conditions that initiate natural terrain debris flows of certain numbers and magnitudes. The progression of open hillslope landslides and channelized debris flows is also examined. The controlling topographic and geologic factors for travel distances are identified. Correlations among the horizontal travel distances, volumes and fall heights of landslides are established. The surficial materials have great impacts on landslide mobility, especially for channelized debris flows. The travel distances of channelized debris flows are enlarged significantly on colluvium lands, compared with those on weathered mantles. These findings can be used to design proper landslide prevention measures for hillslopes in different topographic and geologic conditions. Based on the ENTLI landslide database, as well as the topographic, geological, and rainfall data, five machine learning algorithms, including logistic regression, support vector machine, random forest, boosting method and convolutional neural network, are further utilized to identify various types of past landslides. Through a case study of Lantau Island, it is found that the convolutional neural network achieves an identification accuracy of 92.5% on recent landslides and outperforms other algorithms due to its strengths in feature extraction and multi-dimensional data processing. By using machine learning techniques, the proposed landslide identification method shows outstanding robustness and great potential in tackling the landslide identification problem. Representative outputs: [1] Gao, L., Zhang, L.M., Cheung, R.W.M. (2018). Relationships between natural terrain landslide magnitudes and triggering rainfall based on a large landslide inventory in Hong Kong. Landslides, 15(4), 727-740. [2] Wang, H.J., Zhang, L.M., Yin, K.S., Luo, H.Y., Li, J.H. (2021). Landslide identification using machine learning. Geoscience Frontiers, 12(1), 351-364. (2) Development of an integrated numerical model to simulate the initiation and progression of rain-induced hillslope erosion and debris flows Landslides and debris flows often occur in succession on a hillslope during a rainstorm. Numerical modelling of the integrated process of the initiation and progression of rain-induced hillslope landslides, erosion, and debris flows is challenging. Previous studies often assume an input debris flow input hydrograph and then simulate the subsequent flow process. In this project, a novel integrated numerical model, EDDA 2.0, is developed to simulate the whole process of debris-flow initiation, motion, entrainment, deposition and property changes. Two debris-flow initiation mechanisms (i.e., bed erosion and transformation from landslides) are considered. The integrated model consists of a digital terrain module, a rainfall module, an infiltration module, an overland flow module, a slope stability module, a surface erosion module, a debris flow dynamics module and a deposition module. Once debris flows are initiated, the motion of the flowing mixture is analysed through the debris flow dynamics module. Material entrainment may occur along the flow path, incorporating solid materials from additional slope failures and surface erosion. The model is unique in that it simulates the whole process of rain-induced debris flow evolution and two physical initiation mechanisms. Previous two-step analysis with an assumed inflow hydrograph and an inflow location can now be conducted at one go scientifically without subjective assumptions. The integrated model provides a powerful tool for simulating the initiation and progression of rain-induced hillslope erosion and debris flows. The underground drainage network plays an important role in urban flood control, because most of urban surface is impervious so that the rainwater is retained on the surface and becomes surface flow. Surface flow and drainage flow can exchange through drainage inlets, and the landslides and debris flows may block drainage inlets to a certain degree. An underground drainage flow module is further developed and integrated in EDDA 2.0 to consider the drainage network in the urban environment. A case study of North Lantau Highway debris flood indicates that the drainage inlet works well before it is blocked; the role of drainage system becomes limited when it is blocked by landslides, and the flooding time becomes much longer with significantly increased maximum flood depth. Representative outputs: [1] Shen, P., Zhang, L.M., Chen, H.X., Fan, R.L. (2018). EDDA 2.0: integrated simulation of debris flow initiation and dynamics considering two initiation mechanisms. Geoscientific Model Development, 11(7), 2841-2856. [2] Zhou, S.Y. (2020). Numerical Simulation of Multi Hazard Interactions and Stress Testing of Landslide Risks in Hong Kong under Extreme Storms. HKUST PhD Thesis. (3) Prediction of likely hillslope erosion, landslide and debris flow hazards as basis for engineering design in the Hong Kong context Debris flows can cause severe loss of human lives and damage to properties, especially on densely populated hilly terrains. A large number of debris flows can occur in a large storm, but conventional methods only analyse individual debris flows one by one. The EDDA model can overcome this difficulty and predict likely debris flow clusters. In this project, likely landslide and debris flow clusters on Hong Kong Island were examined considering extreme rainstorms under the influence of climate change. Slope stability analysis is conducted to predict unstable cells and landslide deposition areas. Clusters of debris flows initiating from these landslides are then simulated considering hillslope erosion. The models are validated with historical debris flows triggered by the rainstorm in 2008. Finally, debris flow clusters under three reference extreme rainstorms (i.e., 44%, 65% and 85% of the 24-h probable maximum precipitation) are predicted. The travel distance, maximum flow depth and velocity, total volume, and affected area become much larger with the increase of storm magnitude, and the consequences when initiating at the landslide scars are much severer than those when initiating at the deposition areas, as the potential energy of the debris flows initiating at the landslide scars are larger. Material entrainment can significantly magnify the debris flow volume and destructive power. It is important to evaluate the performance of existing entrainment models in debris flow hazard analysis. Three widely used entrainment models, including the Iverson-Ouyang model, the linear erosion model, and the linear Mohr-Coulomb model, are evaluated using EDDA 2.0. The Tsing Shan debris flow in 1990 in Hong Kong is used as a benchmark to compare the three models. Although some parameters are determined empirically, all these models can be used for debris flow hazard analysis in Hong Kong with similar conditions. Representative outputs: [1] Zhou, S.Y., Gao, L., Zhang, L.M. (2019). Predicting debris-flow clusters under extreme rainstorms: a case study on Hong Kong Island. Bulletin of Engineering Geology and the Environment, 78(8), 5775-5794. [2] Shen, P., Zhang, L.M., Wong, H.F., Peng, D.L., Zhou, S.Y., Zhang, S., Chen, C. (2020). Debris flow enlargement from entrainment: A case study for comparison of three entrainment models. Engineering Geology, 270, 105581.

16206217.label: Major findings and research outcome
16206217.value: (1) A novel integrated cell-based numerical model, EDDA 2.0, is developed to simulate the whole evolution process of rain-induced debris-flow initiation, motion, entrainment, deposition and property changes with consideration of two debris-flow initiation mechanisms (i.e., bed erosion and transformation from landslides) (Shen et al., 2018). It provides a powerful tool for simulating the initiation and progression of rain-induced hillslope erosion and debris flows. Previous two-stage analysis is no longer required. (2) An underground drainage flow module is developed and integrated in the numerical model, EDDA 2.0, to consider the drainage network in the urban environment, in which the complicated hazard interaction between landslides/debris flows and floods can be properly incorporated (Zhou, 2020). It provides a powerful tool for multi-hazard risk assessment in the urban environment. (3) The performance of three entrainment models for debris flow hazard analysis is compared through a case study of Tsing Shan debris flow (Shen et al., 2020). Although some parameters are determined empirically, all these models can be used for debris flow hazard analysis in Hong Kong with similar conditions. (4) The initiation and magnitudes of historic open hillslope landslides and channelized debris flows in Hong Kong are assessed based on the Enhanced Natural Terrain Landslide Inventory (ENTLI) from 1924 to 2014. Statistical models are established to analyse the initiation and progression of open hillslope landslides and channelized debris flows, considering landslide characteristics (i.e., landslide occurrence, scar area, volume, travel distance, and fall height), topographic and geologic factors, and maximum rolling rainfall (Gao et al., 2018). (5) Various machine learning and deep learning techniques are developed to identify past landslides from a digital terrain model, among which the deep convolutional neural network is found to be the most promising model to tackle the landslide identification problem (Wang et al., 2021). (6) A physically-based stress testing is conducted to predict likely landslide and debris flow clusters on Hong Kong Island considering extreme rainstorms under the influence of climate change (Zhou et al., 2019). The results serve as a basis for the engineering design of landslide prevention and mitigation measures. (7) The outcomes of this project form the basis for two major research awards: Guangdong Province Natural Science Award (first class) 2020 and Sichuan Province Science and Technology Award (second class) 2018.

16206217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16206217.value: It is a challenging task to predict the location and magnitude of landslides timely for warning and engineering design purposes. Although the developed numerical model provides insights into the initiation and progression of different types of landslides under extreme rainstorms, the computation costs make it difficult to be used for real-time landslide warning. The emerging machine learning techniques are an attractive potential solution to rapid landslide prediction for their powerful ability to model complex systems and high computational efficiency after training. A course of action for landslide prediction with machine learning techniques is proposed as follows: (1) Automated landslide mapping: Machine learning methods need to be developed to automatically delineate landslide sources and trails from aerial photos and satellite images. This will greatly enhance the update frequency of the existing landslide inventory in Hong Kong. (2) Landslide prediction model design, training and validation: Machine learning models will be designed, trained using historical landslide records for predicting landslide locations and sizes. Model errors will be quantified through validation. (3) Ensemble prediction: The machine learning models should be extended to give ensemble predictions for considering the uncertainties in input rainfall and model errors.

16206217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16206217.value: Landslides are one of the major natural hazards in Hong Kong due to the hilly terrain and the subtropical monsoonal weather settings. Different types of landslides are associated with distinctly different initiation mechanisms and movement behaviour, hence require different mitigation measures. Understanding how different types of landslides are triggered and evolve under a rainstorm is vital for developing effective landslide mitigation strategies. This research project advances our knowledge on the initiation and progression of different types of landslides from a qualitative level to a quantitative level by providing new quantitative evidence and developing a novel numerical model, EDDA 2.0. The relationships between extreme rainfall and the number and magnitude of landslides for various types of landslides are quantified by analysing the historical landslide records in Hong Kong in the period of 1924-2014. With this new model, the whole process of the initiation and progression of various types of landslides can be analysed in one go, instead of in two steps in previous studies. The developed numerical model is applied to predict the number and scale of landslides under extreme rainstorms in Hong Kong. The predicted results form a basis for planning and designing landslide mitigation measures in Hong Kong.

16206317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16206317.value: With increasing demand, parking spaces have become a vital part of urban living and efficient parking management has become more important. In many metropolises, it is often the case that finding a parking slot in downtown areas often constitutes an appreciable fraction of the total travel time due to lack of available parking spaces and the parking fees may well exceed the total vehicle operating costs. It is also a fact that a massive number of private parking slots are available during daytime in nearby residential compounds because those residents drive their cars to work. Thanks to the emerging platform economy enabled by the fast-growing mobile apps in our daily life, parking pains can be relieved from one peer to another. By making vacant private parking slots publicly available to drivers in need through an e-parking platform, shared parking not only allows the owner to earn additional income but also helps alleviate the shortage of parking spaces. While private parking sharing has already become a reality, relevant research is rather limited. This appears to be another case where academic research lags behind developments in the industry. We thus propose this project to address the pressing research need imposed by such emerging parking innovations initiated by the industry. We shall focus on the economic analysis and modeling of the pricing strategies of e-parking platforms in a two-sided parking sharing market, which have a great impact on the size of the two pools: the private car park owners who are willing to rent out their parking slots and the public users who prefer to utilize private parking slots. The first part of the project will develop the demand/supply and matching functions of the two-sided parking sharing market, and then determine the pricing strategies of the monopoly situation with a single e-parking platform acting as an agent or intermediary. The second part will consider the pricing competition in a duopoly scenario of e-parking platforms and will examine the efficiency of competition. The third part will determine the pricing strategies under hybrid modes of private shared parking and general public parking. Sharing private parking slots benefits the community by providing additional parking spaces without the city having to build more parking slots; it also benefits private slot owners by monetizing their existing assets at almost zero cost. Therefore, the proposed research deals with an emerging issue of great importance in both theory and practice. 随着停车需求的不断增长，停车已经成为了城市生活的重要组成部分。这种背景下，如何有效的利用停车位显得尤为重要。在许多大城市中，我们发现正是因为停车位数量有限而且停车费用过高，许多车主在市中心寻找停车位的过程中会造成额外的拥堵，这会使得原本拥挤的交通路况变得更加糟糕。与此同时，我们发现由于业主的出行，许多市区附近住宅的私家停车位暂时的闲置了下来。考虑到如今平台经济的出现和手机应用程序的迅速发展，停车难的烦恼能够被共享停车这一新兴事物所减轻。通过电子停车平台让暂时闲置的私家停车位对公众开放，共享停车不仅能使得私家车位的业主有额外的收入，而且还能有效的解决停车位短缺的问题。 尽管私家停车位的共享已经出现，但是关于这方面的研究还很有限，这也是因为产业的发展先于学术研究。因此，我们提出了这个课题来研究这个新型的停车问题。我们将专注于对停车平台在双边市场下如何定价的分析和建模。这将对两类人有重要的影响：1. 收购价格将决定愿意共享他们私家停车位的业主的数量；2. 销售价格将决定愿意来私家停车位停车的社会车辆的数量。 课题的第一部分将会在双边市场下建立一个供给和需求的匹配模型，然后在单一平台作为转销商和中介的情况下分别分析出能最大化平台收益的双边定价策略。第二部分将着重考虑在双平台竞争的情况下的价格策略以及竞争给平台用户带来的影响。第三部分，我们将把分享私家停车位和路边停车位结合在一起分析怎样定价会使得整个系统的花费最小化。 私家停车位的分享在已经有限的土地资源上开拓了额外的停车位来满足许多车主的停车需求，这样使得城市不必去建造更多的停车位来占用土地，同时私家车位的业主也可以把他们暂时闲置的资源转化为收入供他们使用，这将对整个社会起到积极的作用。因此，这个课题对于理论研究和实际应用有着重要的意义。

It focused on the economic analysis and modeling of the pricing strategies of e-parking platforms in a two-sided parking sharing market, which have a great impact on the size of the two pools: the private car park owners who are willing to rent out their parking slots and the public users who prefer to utilize private parking slots. Specifically, we developed the demand/supply and matching functions of the two-sided parking sharing market, and determined the pricing strategies of the monopoly situation with a single e-parking platform acting as an agent or intermediary. We also examined the pricing competition in a duopoly scenario of e-parking platforms and investigated the efficiency of competition. The pricing strategies under hybrid modes of private shared parking and general public parking were also studied. The findings from this projects answered the following questions which are of great importance in both theory and practice: 1) how does sharing private parking benefit the community by providing additional parking spaces without the city having to build more parking slots; 2) how does sharing private parking benefits private slot owners by monetizing their existing assets at almost zero cost.
