16206417.label: Realisation of objectives
16206417.value: Data-parallel computing frameworks, such as MapReduce and Spark, are serving as important foundations for big data processing in shared clusters. They help to accelerate the processing of large datasets by dividing a job into multiple tasks, and distributing them to different machines (called worker nodes) in a cluster for parallel execution. Each job involves multiple computation stages and tasks in a downstream stage have to wait for intermediate results produced from their upstream stages. In MapReduce, for example, intermediate results need to be transferred from mapper tasks to reducer tasks often with large volumes of data, referred as a shuffle phase. Such high-volume data transfers significantly affect job completion times. Although Spark reduces the amount of traffic shuffled between different stages through in-memory caching, jobs running on Spark still spend significant portion of their runtime on the shuffle phase. The above problem is further complicated by the fact that communication in data-parallel applications now widely follows the bulk-synchronous parallel (BSP) model, in which a collection of parallel flows, termed coflow, is responsible for transferring intermediate data between a group of machines. The unique feature is that a coflow completes only when all its parallel flows belonging to the same coflow have completed. In a shared cluster, a large number of co-existing coflows from different users and applications contend for the limited network bandwidth. Consequently, a network scheduler needs to schedule contending coflows to attain optimal performance towards fast completion (e.g., minimizing the coflow completion time) while providing service isolation among different coflows by means of fair sharing. This project focuses on the design of network-aware scheduling and resource allocation strategies for big data processing and analytic applications. The objective is to schedule tasks in a shared cluster with network awareness to improve both individual job performance and overall system resource utilization. The design of our network-aware scheduler is based on two key observations. First, a production cluster hosts many data-parallel frameworks, running a mix of different types of jobs such as background batch jobs and interactive query jobs, even on a common dataset. In such a production environment, the network transfer time become a critical contributing factor to the job completion time. Second, the optimal performance (i.e., minimizing average coflow completion time or CCT) and service isolation (i.e., fairness between different jobs) have long been considered as conflicting objectives that are difficult to achieve simultaneously. How to incorporate network transfer time into a job scheduler turns out to be a challenging problem. On one hand, existing cluster schedulers either only considers computation resources (such as CPU), or addresses network transfer time with a sole focus on network bandwidth resources. Without proper coordination, such isolated resource allocation strategies often lead to poor resource utilization. On the other hand, multi-resource scheduling policies have the potential in handling resource allocations across multiple types. However, in production clusters and data-parallel frameworks, there are several practical limitations making it difficult to apply (1) it may not be feasible to obtain prior knowledge of the resource demands in analytics jobs, background or interactive, as resource demands are not specified in job descriptions; (2) existing multi-resource scheduling strategies are typically designed with a clean and new approach, engineered to completely replace the current data-parallel frameworks. In another word, they cannot be utilized in existing data-parallel frameworks. In this project, we examine the fundamental workload characteristics in a shared cluster. We design and implement a network-aware task scheduler that complements and improves current scheduling policies in existing data-parallel frameworks, with a coordinated emphasis on both computation and network resources when scheduling decisions are made (Task 1). We evaluation the performance of the proposed scheduling algorithm through rigorous analysis under different traffic scenario (Task 2). Our emphasis is to rectify the resource imbalance by scheduling computation-intensive tasks (with data locality) on the same CPU core as network-intensive tasks (without data locality), within the same executor process are managed by existing data-parallel frameworks. In addition, we design a priority-based strategy to select the best-suited candidate when multiple computation-intensive tasks compete for an idle CPU core hosting a network-intensive task. One highlight of our solution is that the proposed scheduler is designed as a plugin to existing data-parallel frameworks, which co-exists with existing two-tier resource managers in traditional data-parallel frameworks. Thus, this remains transparent to applications, and requires no modifications to existing programming interfaces. We further design task scheduling algorithms with the objective of achieving different degrees of tradeoff between critical performance metrics (Task 3). More specifically, there are commonly two fundamental requirements in a network scheduler for contending coflows to attain optimal performance towards fast completion while providing service isolation between coflows by means of fair network sharing. However, simultaneously achieving optimal performance and service isolation are not feasible. In practice, one category of cluster schedulers settles for minimizing the average coflow completion time (CCT) as the primary objective. The idea is to preferentially prioritize “small” coflows over “large” ones, hence minimizing the average CCT. However, such an approach is incapable of providing service isolation. The other category of schedulers turns to fair sharing to provide optimal isolation between coflows. These schedulers allocate each coflow a fair share of the network bandwidth, isolating the completion of each coflow with a predictable CCT. However, such fair schedulers cannot explicitly optimize performance and fall short of minimizing average CCT. In fact, performance (i.e., minimizing average CCT) and fairness (i.e., service isolation) have long been considered as conflicting objectives that cannot be achieved simultaneously, We design and implement a new network scheduler, which can minimize the average CCT without compromising performance isolation guarantee. This achieves the best of two sides by preferentially scheduling coflows in ascending order of their CCTs under a fair networking sharing scheme. We implemented our proposed network-aware scheduler in Spark, and extensively evaluated in testbeds ranging from a few to over a hundred worker nodes on Linode under a diverse range of workloads (Task 4). We show that it significantly improves CPU utilization in the cluster and mitigates the lack of balance when multiple resources are involved. For our proposed coflow scheduler, we conducted extensive evaluation with the performance-optimal and isolation-optimal schedulers through both trace-driven simulations and EC2 deployment over a large cluster. The results demonstrate that it can reduce the average CCT by 1.8x without delaying a single coflow when compared with the isolation-optimal scheduler, and even outperforms the performance-optimal scheduler by 9%.

16206417.label: Major findings and research outcome
16206417.value: We started by investigating the main problems in existing cluster schedulers, in which they either focused only on computation resources or network resources, but not both. Due to lack of coordination, these isolated resource allocation strategies can easily lead to poor resource utilization. For instance, if only a network-intensive job is assigned to a CPU, the CPU core would mostly remain idle, and data transfer over a network becomes the performance bottleneck. This essentially requires a multi-resource scheduling policies that take both computation and network resources into account, as jobs require both resources to complete. We designed and implemented a novel network-aware task scheduler that complements and improves the state-of-the-art scheduling policies with a coordinated emphasis on both computation and network resources when scheduling decisions are made. Specifically, the proposed scheduler actively examines resource imbalance and categorically schedules computation-intensive and communication-intensive tasks. The task allocation problem was formulated into an optimization problem, which can be solved with polynomial-time approximation algorithms. We implemented our scheduler on top of Spark 1.4.0 as a scheduling plugin using Scala programming language, which co-exists well with the two-tier cluster managers in existing data-parallel frameworks. We examined the challenges associated with simultaneously achieving optimal performance and service isolation for coflows. We demonstrated that performance optimality (i.e., minimizing average CCT) and fairness (i.e., service isolation) posed a set of conflicting objectives. This motivated us to consider navigating the tradeoff between them. Our key insight is to preferentially serve coflows following their completion order in a fair allocation manner. More specifically, fairness only needs to be preserved when coflows complete. Thus, by tracking the completion order in a fair allocation scheme, a scheduler likely provides an equivalent long-term isolation between users and applications. We proposed and implemented Utopia, which allocates bandwidth to coflow towards the maximum progress. Through analysis and evaluation, it is shown that Utopia provides provable isolation guarantee while achieving the performance optimality in term of minimizing the CCT. When compared to a fair allocation scheme, each coflow completes within a constant delay. We implemented the proposed schedulers in testbeds and over public cloud Amazon EC2. We conducted extensive experiments under different a variety of workloads. The results conclusively demonstrated the performance improvement in reducing job completion times, better resource utilization and guarantee in performance isolation.

16206417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16206417.value: Cluster scheduler is no doubt one of the most critical components in data-parallel frameworks. Our focus in this project is the design of network-aware schedulers for improving resource utilization and for achieving performance optimality under various tradeoff such as fairness. In practice, however, there are many other factors that may come into play. Resource utilization in a cluster highly depends on the inter-framework resource allocation policy in cluster managers. Our design is largely based on the existing two-level cluster manager. It has been argued, however, this lacks sufficient resource visibility, and instead, a shared-state and optimistic concurrency approach can be adopted. Our proposed scheduler can be extended to shared-state cluster managers, in which it can help determine how to select computation-intensive tasks to share resources. Another fundamental limitation worth further investigation is that the multi-resource scheduling in theory only deals with offline job scheduling by leveraging complicated graph or combinatoric algorithms. Such approaches are not applicable in the online scheduling scenario since the demand for network and computation resources cannot be quantified in advance. We are exploring some new theories and approaches (e.g., reinforcement learning technique) to achieve better cluster scheduling performance.

16206417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16206417.value: Data-parallel computing frameworks are essential building blocks for big data analytic jobs in shared clusters. They assist to accelerate the processing of large datasets by dividing a job into multiple tasks, and by distributing them to machines across the cluster for parallel execution. The concept of coflow, referred as a collection of parallel flows for transferring intermediate data between a group of machines, becomes crucial for communications in data-parallel applications. Thus, it is increasingly important to design network schedulers which balance a complex set of resources such as computation, storage and network while ensuring the performance optimality of individual application. The significance of this project and its outcomes are primarily two-folded: (1) we propose a network-aware task scheduler with a coordinated emphasis on computation and network. It predicts and resolves the imbalance in utilizing computation and network resources while categorically distinguishing resource allocation for computation-intensive and network-intensive tasks. (2) We design and implement a coflow scheduler that simultaneously optimizes performance while providing provable isolation guarantee. Specifically, we demonstrate that it is capable of reducing the average CCT dramatically, while still guaranteeing that no coflow will be delayed beyond a constant time than its CCT in a fair scheme.

16206517.label: Project Objectives
16206517.value: Summary-based symbolic execution Summaries are a common technique in static analysis to address scalability of large software systems. We will borrow this idea to speed up symbolic execution using large computational clusters. The idea is to extract symbolic constraints involving the input parameters as well as heap variables. These symbolic formulae capture the effects of computation and can be conservatively estimated via static analysis prior to the execution. At the same time, we will simultaneously validate these summaries in parallel to further increase the preciseness of the constraints. This will greatly reduce redundancy in conventional symbolic execution and enable a high degree of parallelism in performing symbolic execution based on computing clusters. Weakest precondition extraction for efficient inlining of summaries Summaries are a good idea for preprocessing functions and parallelizing symbolic execution. However, conventional use of summaries still incurs a significant overhead because of the non-selective inlining of summaries. We observed that specific execution states can invalidate subsets of the preconditions of the whole or a part of the summary. We will formulate a predicate-cover problem by building a logic lattice to establish a hierarchical structure of the weakest precondition on both the entire procedure and basic blocks. The goal is to terminate the symbolic execution of the procedure as early as we can, to dramatically speed up the whole execution. Evaluation over commercial tools and industrial strength systems We will evaluate our system using the output from commercial tools and quantify both the quality and the performance using industrial strength, open-source software systems. We will also build a testing oracle for evaluating the verification correctness by examining bug fix histories of these systems.

rows: Summary-based symbolic execution Summaries are a common technique in static analysis to address scalability of large software systems. We will borrow this idea to speed up symbolic execution using large computational clusters. The idea is to extract symbolic constraints involving the input parameters as well as heap variables. These symbolic formulae capture the effects of computation and can be conservatively estimated via static analysis prior to the execution. At the same time, we will simultaneously validate these summaries in parallel to further increase the preciseness of the constraints. This will greatly reduce redundancy in conventional symbolic execution and enable a high degree of parallelism in performing symbolic execution based on computing clusters.

Weakest precondition extraction for efficient inlining of summaries Summaries are a good idea for preprocessing functions and parallelizing symbolic execution. However, conventional use of summaries still incurs a significant overhead because of the non-selective inlining of summaries. We observed that specific execution states can invalidate subsets of the preconditions of the whole or a part of the summary. We will formulate a predicate-cover problem by building a logic lattice to establish a hierarchical structure of the weakest precondition on both the entire procedure and basic blocks. The goal is to terminate the symbolic execution of the procedure as early as we can, to dramatically speed up the whole execution.

Evaluation over commercial tools and industrial strength systems We will evaluate our system using the output from commercial tools and quantify both the quality and the performance using industrial strength, open-source software systems. We will also build a testing oracle for evaluating the verification correctness by examining bug fix histories of these systems.

16206517.label: Major findings and research outcome
16206517.value: We have successfully completed the objectives by, first, developing a new summary method, different from the conventional design, that computes, solves, and caches many path conditions, in our design, the SMT solver no longer works separately to check the satisfiability of path conditions, but works together with the sparse analysis on its linear-sized program inter- mediate representation (IR), which is known as the program dependence graph. Our key insight is that program dependence graph and path condition are allotropes, which means that, although they are in different forms, they encode the same program information, i.e., the control dependence and the data dependence. Secondly, we have developed a framework of bottom-up data flow analysis that breaks the limits of function boundaries, so that functions having calling dependence can be analyzed in parallel. As a result, we can achieve much higher parallelism than the conventional parallel design of bottom-up analysis. Our key insight is that many analysis tasks of a caller function only depend on partial analysis results of its callee functions. Thus, the analysis of the caller function can start before the analyses of its callee functions complete. Therefore, our basic idea is to partition the analysis task of a function into multiple sub-tasks, so that we can pipeline the sub-tasks to generate function summaries. Each finding is reported in a top conference publication.

16206517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16206517.value: The work in this project on how to handle summaries in a novel and modular way paves the way for an even larger scale design by handling static analysis in a distributed manner. This allows the use of cloud-scale resources be efficiently coordinated to carry out ultra-large scale analysis. We plan to further study the algorithmic impact and believe the experience in building summaries will be of significant value.

16206517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16206517.value: The nature of the project is to improve the capability of existing automated tools to find software errors by leveraging more compact representations of the intermediate data and decoupled representations to enable parallelism. The significance is that we are the first to address the compactness and the fine-granular treatment of the intermediate representations so that tools can be scaled to handle large scale software systems. The value is to enable automated bug finding for software systems in the modern setting and benefit industrial scale users of these tools.

16206617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16206617.value: In computational fluid dynamics, the second-order methods are generally robust and reliable, and they are routinely employed in the practical computations. In recent decades, there have been continuous interests and efforts on the development of higher-order schemes. In the applications, such as direct numerical simulation of complex wave interactions, large eddy simulation of turbulent flows, and computational aeroacoustics, the higher order methods have significant potential than typical second order schemes. For engineering applications, due to complicated geometry the construction of higher order schemes on the unstructured meshes becomes extremely demanding. For higher-order finite volume schemes, the use of large stencil for spatial reconstruction has become the bottleneck in the application of higher order methods on unstructured meshes. Due to the large reconstruction stencil, more memory is needed to store the coefficients associated with the cells and much computational time has been spent on the searching of the distributed stencils. In the parallel computing, a large amount of data need to be transferred at the interface between partitions, which leads to the deterioration of parallel efficiency. Thus, the development of higher-order compact finite volume methods with the same stencil as the second-order scheme becomes demanding. The aim of this proposal is to develop a fourth- and fifth-order compact gas-kinetic schemes on both structured and unstructured meshes. In the past years, the gas-kinetic scheme has been developed systematically for the Euler and Navier-Stokes solutions, and has been successfully applied for the continuum flow simulations from nearly incompressible to hypersonic viscous and heat conducting flows. Compared with the Rieman solver-based finite volume methods, the gas-kinetic solver has distinguishable advantages. First, it is based on a higher-order space-time coupled evolution model for the flux evaluation. Second, it has the multi-dimensional property with the account of both normal and tangential derivatives of the flow variables around a cell interface. Third, instead of solving hyperbolic-parabolic type Navier-Stokes equations, the gas-kinetic scheme is based on a physical process of hyperbolic particle transport with local particle collision, which solves viscous and heat conducting flow in unstructured meshes without explicitly discretizing the dissipative terms. This also provides a theoretical basis for the possible construction of higher-order compact schemes. The development of accurate, robust, and efficient higher-order compact Navier-Stokes flow solver is the frontier of current computational fluid dynamics. This project seeks an alternative way, along with other massive research effort, to design such a higher-order scheme. 在计算流体力学中，二阶格式具有较好的稳定性和鲁棒性，并且 广泛被应用于实际数值模拟中。最近数十年，发展更高阶格式 始终是学科发展的一个重要方向。高阶格式对复杂波系传播的 直接数值模拟问题，湍流的大涡模拟问题，以及计算气动声学 等问题上，较之传统二阶格式有着显著的优势和巨大的潜力。 然而，在实际工程问题上，被模拟对象往往有着较为复杂的 几何外形。 因此，构建一类实用的基于非结构网格的高阶格式 就显得尤其重要。对于基于有限体积框架的高阶格式来说， 传统的空间重构方法需要较大的模板。这成为其应用到 非结构网格上的一大瓶颈。 其主要原因为：大模板需要 更多内存消耗来存储几何信息；搜索模板上所有单元的信息 需要大量的计算时间；在并行计算中，各个区块之间的信息 传递也变得更为复杂和耗时，并行效率也会下降。 因此， 发展与二阶格式拥有相同模板的新型紧致高阶格式就变得尤为 重要。本课题的主要目的是发展一类基于结构网格和 非结构网格的四阶及五阶紧致气体动理学格式。近年来， 基于欧拉方程和纳维斯托克斯问题的气体动理学格式被不断的 发展和完善，并且在从不可压连续气体流动模拟至高超声速 气动加热模拟上均得到了成功的应用。和基于传统黎曼求解器 的有限体积方法相比，气体动理学格式有着如下优势。 首先，在通量演化过程中，气体动理学格式基于的是更高阶的 时空耦合演化模型。其次，它具有内在的多维特性，界面处 的气体法向和切向分布效应可以被考虑到通量演化中去。 第三，不同于数值求解双曲-抛物型的纳维斯托克斯方程的 传统求解器，气体动理学格式是基于统计物理力学模型， 从而可以自然地描述气体粒子传输和碰撞的过程。并且， 该求解过程无需将粘性项和热传导项分离求解，更加符合 物理本质，也更利于在非结构网格上的重构。上述几点均为 发展高阶在非结构网格上的紧致气体动理学格式提供了 坚实的理论基础。发展高精度，强健且高效的高级紧致 纳维斯托克斯求解器是计算流体力学的前沿方向。 本项目试图另辟蹊径，利用气体动理格式的优势来设计 对可压缩流体的新型高阶算法。

16206617.label: Realisation of objectives
16206617.value: In this project, a class of compact higher-order gas-kinetic schemes (GKS) with spectral-like resolution have been developed. Based on the high-order gas evolution model, both the flux function and conservative flow variables in GKS can be evaluated explicitly from the time-accurate gas distribution function at a cell interface. As a result, inside each control volume both the cell-averaged flow variables and their cell-averaged gradients can be updated within each time step. The flow variable update and slope update are coming from the same physical solution at the cell interface. This strategy is based on the time accurate solution at a cell interface, which is very special to GKS, and it cannot be achieved by the conventional Riemann problem-based flow solvers due to its time-independent interface flux functions and flow variables. Instead, to update the slopes in the Riemann-solver based schemes, such as HWENO, there are additional governing equations for slopes or equivalent degrees of freedom inside each cell, which may not be physically valid. In GKS, only a single time accurate gas evolution model is needed at the cell interface for updating cell averaged flow variables through interface fluxes and updating the cell averaged slopes through the interface flow variables. Based on both cell averaged values and their slopes, compact schemes up to 8th-order accuracy have been developed. As analysed in this papers, the local linear compact reconstruction without limiter can achieve a spectral-like resolution at large wavenumber than the well-established compact scheme of Lele with globally coupled flow variables and their derivatives. For nonlinear gas dynamic evolution, to avoid spurious oscillation in discontinuous region, the above compact linear reconstruction from the symmetric stencil can be divided into sub-stencils and apply a biased nonlinear WENO-Z reconstruction. Consequently, discontinuous solutions can be captured through the compact WENO-type nonlinear reconstruction. In GKS, the time evolution solution of the gas distribution function at a cell interface is based on an integral solution of the kinetic model equation, which covers a physical process from an initial non-equilibrium state to a final equilibrium one. Since the initial non-equilibrium state is obtained based on the nonlinear WENO-Z reconstruction, and the equilibrium state is basically constructed from the linear symmetric reconstruction, the GKS evolution models unifies the nonlinear and linear reconstructions in a gas relaxation process in the determination of a time-dependent gas distribution function. This property gives GKS great advantages in capturing both discontinuous shock waves and the linear aero-acoustic waves in a single computation due to its dynamical adaptation of non-equilibrium and equilibrium states in different flow regions. This dynamically adaptive model helps to solve a long-lasting problem in the development of high-order schemes about the choices of the linear and nonlinear reconstructions. Compared with discontinuous Galerkin (DG) scheme, the current compact GKS uses the same local and compact stencil, achieves the high-order accuracy, uses a much larger time step, has the same robustness as a 2nd-order scheme, and gets accurate solutions in both shock and smooth regions without introducing trouble cell and additional limiting process. The nonlinear reconstruction in the compact GKS is solely based on the WENO-Z technique. At the same time, the current scheme solves the Navier-Stokes equations automatically due to combined inviscid and viscous flux terms from a single time evolution gas distribution function at a cell interface. Due to the use of multi-stage multi-derivative (MSMD) time-stepping technique, for achieving a 4th-order time accuracy, the current scheme uses only two stages instead of four in the traditional Runge-Kutta method. As a result, the current GKS becomes much more efficient than the corresponding same order DG method. A variety of numerical tests are presented to validate the compact high-order GKS. The scheme presents a state-of-art numerical solutions under a wide range of flow conditions, i.e., strong shock discontinuity, shear instability, aero-acoustic wave propagation, and NS solutions. It promotes the development of high-order scheme to a new level of maturity. The success of the current scheme crucially depends on the high-order gas evolution model, which cannot be achieved by any other approach once the 1st-order Riemann flux function is still used in the development of high-order numerical algorithms. A compact high-order GKS for 3-D flow simulation is constructed as well. The compact third-order GKS in 3-D shows similar resolution as the fifth-order gas-kinetic scheme with the noncompact WENO reconstruction. The scheme has been constructed on both structured and unstructured mesh with complex geometry. The computations, such as the flow passing through a space vehicle, have been successfully conducted from subsonic to hypersonic flow speed.

16206617.label: Major findings and research outcome
16206617.value: Computational fluid dynamics is a direct modelling of physical laws in a discretized space. Through this study, we fully realize the correct way to develop numerical schemes for the compressible flow simulation. The basic physical laws include the mass, momentum and energy conservations, physically consistent transport process, and similar domain of dependence and influence between the physical reality and the numerical representation. Therefore, a physically reasonable numerical scheme must be a compact one which involves the closest neighbouring cells within the domain of dependence for the solution update under a CFL number (∼ 1). In the construction of explicit high-order compact scheme, sub-cell flow distributions or the equivalent degree of freedoms beyond the cell averaged flow variables must be evolved and updated, such as the gradients of the flow variables inside each control volume. High-order dynamic process has to be modelled on the scales of cell size and time step. In the study, we know how to provide reliable cell averaged flow variables and their gradients for the compact data reconstruction, and construct evolution process with discontinuous time-dependent flow variables across a cell interface. At the same time, with the consideration of a discontinuous time accurate flux function at a cell interface, nonlinear temporal limiter for the flux function in time has been designed as well. The direct modelling unifies the nonlinear limiters in both space for the data reconstruction and time for the time dependent flux transport. The equivalent treatment of space and time makes the scheme be super robust and accurate for the compressible flow simulation. At the same time, the high-order compact scheme can use a large CFL number (∼ 0.8) in flow computation, even in the hypersonic flow simulation. Under the direct modelling framework, as an example, the high-order compact gas-kinetic scheme (GKS) has been constructed and used in the engineering applications.

16206617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16206617.value: The compact gas-kinetic scheme developed through this project shows significant improvement in terms of robustness, accuracy, and efficiency in comparison with the previous high-order schemes for the flow simulations. For example, a third-order compact gas-kinetic scheme (GKS) on unstructured tetrahedral mesh has been constructed for the compressible Euler and Navier-Stokes flow simulations. Due to the time dependent gas distribution function at a cell interface, both cell-averaged flow variables and their cell-averaged gradients can be evolved. As a result, the reconstruction can be done using von Neumann neighbouring cells. Benefiting from the evolved cell-averaged slopes, on tetrahedral mesh the GKS is linearly stable from a compact third-order smooth reconstruction with a large CFL number. At the same time, the high-order wall boundary treatment can be obtained by combining the constrained least-square technique and the WENO procedure. The scheme can be used to simulate both inviscid and viscous flows at low and high speed with complex geometry. At the current stage, the scheme has been used in the flow simulation of 3D flying vehicles, turbulence, and multiscale transports.

16206617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16206617.value: Flow simulations are needed in the study of a wide spectrum of disciplines in science and engineering, such as gas dynamics, acoustics, geophysics, and biomechanics, to name but a few. The development of numerical scheme plays a critical role in modelling and studying the phenomena. This project is about the development of high-order compact scheme for the simulation of inviscid and viscous flows in three-dimensional geometry. Many fundamental ideas have been obtained in the process of algorithm development, such as the updates of both cell averaged flow variables and their slopes and the introduction of nonlinear limiter in time evolution. The scheme developed has been used in the computations of compressible gas dynamics and applied in aerodynamics, shock waves, astrophysics, and ocean hydraulics. Many other challenging problems can be tackled as well using the high-order compact scheme, such as aeroacoustics and denotative waves.

16207017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16207017.value: Reversible structural phase transformation underlies the basic function of shape memory alloys with extensive biomedical applications such as coronary stents and orthodontic arch wires. However, emerging energy-related applications such as micro-actuation, caloric-cooling and energy conversion demand the functional properties having multimillion cycle repeatability of the transformation. Even the most successful shape memory alloy Nitinol provides ~25 MJ/m3 one-way work output in the first cycle of stress-induced phase transformation, but cannot sustain more than a few tens of cycles. The large hysteresis and the significant functional degradation accumulated upon transformation cycles strongly limit energy-related applications of these alloys. Recently, the PI and her collaborators have theorized that both hysteresis and reversibility in shape memory alloys depend strongly on lattice compatibility at phase interfaces. We showed that conditions of compatibility dominate the macroscopic properties of transformable materials at both centimeter and micron scales. These conditions are expressed as properties of the transformation stretch tensor, and are sensitive to the lattice parameters and symmetries. Tuning structural parameters provides a well-defined route to design new materials with desirable properties, but currently this is a slow and laborious process, and, despite a lot of work, only few materials have been found to closely satisfy these conditions. Nevertheless, they all exhibit unprecedented repeatability even under multimillions transformation cycles. The process would be speeded up immensely by a suite of algorithms integrated with real-time structural characterization tools for the high throughout development of transformable materials, by which low-hysteresis and low-fatigue shape memory alloys can be achieved simultaneously based on theories of lattice compatibility. The key task is to integrate the theoretical methods seamlessly with the characterization tools, so that the critical measures of compatibility are an immediate output. Besides incorporating state-of-the-art theoretical results, screening of potential candidates can be vastly accelerated by exploiting similarities between known alloys based on data mining and machine learning algorithms. Our proposed suite of algorithms includes methods for 1) determination of the full transformation stretch tensor and transformation pathway between two crystalline structures of arbitrary symmetry, 2) examination of compatibility conditions, 3) prediction of compatible microstructures at the measured parameters and 4) the development of a data-centric platform of transformable materials for smart screening. To support the algorithms, we will also build an advanced structural characterization system that measures the full stretch tensor and transformation pathway for a structural phase transformation and quantifies the in-situ lattice distortion during phase transformation. 在一定条件下形状记忆合金会发生可逆相变，这一特性赋予了形状记忆合金一些独特的功 能，使其被广泛应用于各个领域:在生物医学领域，形态记忆合金能用作血管支架和牙齿矫 形丝;在微机电系统和能量转化领域，形状记忆合金能用以制备微致动器、微传送器和热力 能量转化器等。这些新兴应用都要求材料具有优异的疲劳性能—经历数百万次相变循环而性 能不退化。 然而，即使是目前最成功的形状记忆合金--镍钛的合金，其应力诱导相变的第一 个循环中的单程输出功也仅约为 25MJ/m3，而且在数十个循环后就急速衰减。正是由于相变 循环过程中累积的严重滞后行为和功能退化问题，形状记忆合金的应用收到了很大的限制。 近年来，项目申请人及其团队研究发现了形状记忆合金滞后行为和可逆性与材料相界面的结 果相容性有很大的关系。研究表明，相界面的相容性对厘米和毫米尺度的材料的宏观力学行 为有很大的影响。而相界面的相容性则由相变拉伸张量决定，并且对晶格常数和晶体结构对 称性非常敏感。这个发现为通过调节结构参数以开发设计新的形状记忆合金提供了重要的指 导。然而，这一过程进展较为缓慢并且需要大量的实验工作，并且到目前而言为止，也仅有 少数几种材料能接近满足优异相界面相容性的条件。值得庆幸的是，这些材料都表现出了杰 出的记忆疲劳性能--即使经历数百万次相变循环性仍不失效。 为了能研发出兼具低滞后和耐疲劳特点的形态记忆合金，大大缩减上述过程所需的时间，我 们基于晶格相容性理论，提出一套整合了为形状记忆合金特别设计的实时材料表征工具的算 法系统。这一项目的核心在于理论分析与表征工具无缝连接以快速得到材料界面相容性的准 确测量。除了利用了最新的理论研究成果，这套系统内含已知材料的数据库，当研发出新材 料时，能快速有效地筛选出有潜力的材料并基于数据挖掘和机器学习技术分析它们的相同 点。我们所提出的这套算法体系包含了以下方面:1. 材料的相变拉伸张量和考虑任意晶体 结构和对称性的相变路径测量与计算;2. 相界面相容性的检测;3. 基于已测参数的相容细 观结构的预测;4. 用以智能筛选材料的相变材料数据库。 为了实现这套算法体系，我们将 进一步建立和完善一套能测量相变材料拉伸张量和相变路径并定量算得晶体变形量的结构 表征实验系统。

16207017.label: Major findings and research outcome
16207017.value: Upon the completion of this project, we have built the crystallographic data of phase-transforming materials by which we implemented a data-driven approach for index-free X-ray analysis. We have integrated the cofactor conditions with the crystallographic data for rational material development, and developed a suite of algorithms for determination of transformation mechanisms and discovered new transformation pathways and involution twin domains in traditional shape memory alloys. This underlies a new design strategy for transforming materials to achieve high transformability with ultra-high fatigue resistance.

16207017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16207017.value: By using the python packages such as Pystructrans, Canon and Monet, we can immensely screen and develop new transforming alloys/oxides with maximum achievable functionality and minimum functional/structural degradation. Further development can be carried out for the machine-learning models on derivative crystal structures with application to smart actuation, and solid-state cooling.

16207017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16207017.value: The research underlies the necessary algorithms for mathematical design of new phase-transforming materials. Without long trial-test-correction development period, this research opens a new avenue to discover new functional alloys/oxides with desirable properties and long functional life.

16207417.label: Major findings and research outcome
16207417.value: In this project, scaling effects on the coupled thermo-mechanical behaviour of energy pile were first investigated in the geotechnical centrifuge facility in HKUST. It is found that consistent results are obtained at centrifuge tests carried out 28g, 40g and 56g, where g is the Earth’s acceleration. It is evident that the scaling effects due to particle size on centrifuge modelling of floating energy piles with the ratio of D/d50 larger than 92 can be ignored. This finding is vital for physical modelling of energy foundations in future. Due to intended operational needs of energy foundations or by accident, cyclic non-symmetrical thermal loads may be applied to floating energy pile groups and piled rafts founded in soft clays. The thermo-mechanical interaction among non-symmetrical thermally loaded piles with 3D pile spacing, D is the diameter of each pile, was first investigated. Moreover, the effects of different pile spacings (3D or 5D) were also studied. In addition, an advanced thermo-hydro-mechanical (THM) bounding surface model developed by the PI and co-I was implemented in a finite element (FE) code to investigate the THM interactions of energy piled foundation three dimensionally. The new FE code was verified by centrifuge model tests. Consistent results were obtained. Systematic numerical parametric studies were then carried out to devise design guidelines and recommendations. The thermally induced irreversible ratchetting settlement and tilting of the elevated pile group, ceased in less than 20 heating and cooling cycles, but still exceeded the serviceability and ultimate limit state criteria set by the European design guidelines (i.e., EN 1997-1:2004). The observed irreversible pile-foundation settlement is attributed to the accumulation of contractive volumetric strain in the soil surrounding energy piles, lowering the horizontal stress and hence reducing the shaft resistance. To compensate for the reduced shaft resistance, a downward transfer of load takes place, resulting in an increase in base resistance. The thermally induced excess pore water pressure, which cannot dissipate completely during typical heating and cooling cycles. The energy piled raft similarly settled but to a much smaller extent than did the elevated group. It is found that the thermally induced irreversible s ratchetting settlement and tilting in a 5D-pile group are 200% and 300% smaller than those in a 3D group, respectively. It is recommended that an energy piled raft with 5D pile spacing, instead of an elevated energy pile group, should be used for design of energy foundations in soft clays.

16207417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16207417.value: Although some fundamental findings and high quality physical data have been obtained from this project, a systematic full-scale field trials should be recommended.

16207417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16207417.value: There is an increasing interest and use of energy foundation worldwide. As far as the PI and co-I are aware, all previous studies have focused on single energy piles and pile groups subjected to symmetrical thermal loads, although it is quite common to have energy pile groups stressed by non-symmetrical thermal loads. In this project, cyclic non-symmetrical thermal loads acting on energy pile groups and piled rafts founded were investigated three-dimensionally by carrying physical model tests at elevated gravity in a centrifuge and by using a state-of-the-art theoretical soil model. The thermo-mechanical interaction among non-symmetrical thermally loaded piles is understood. The thermally induced irreversible ratchetting settlement and tilting of the elevated pile group, ceased in less than 20 heating and cooling cycles. To compensate for the reduced shaft resistance, a downward transfer of load takes place, resulting in an increase in base resistance of pile group and piled raft. It is found that the thermally induced irreversible s ratchetting settlement and tilting in a 5D-pile group are much smaller than those in a 3D group, respectively. It is therefore recommended that an energy piled raft with 5D pile spacing should be used for design of energy foundations.

16207617.value: 在動態場景中針對基於事件的社交網絡的有效事件參與者規劃

16207617.label: Project Objectives
16207617.value: We aim to predict the participants who are most likely to join an event. We will study the key factors that a user would consider, such as the content of an event, the trustworthiness of its organizers and the social relationships between participants. We then propose to model the problem as a game to analyze which users are most likely to join an event and hence better predict participation at different events. We plan to develop an incremental event arrangement solution that is suitable for dynamic environments. Specifically, we will address the problem that in dynamic environments, information of events may be updated and hence event arrangements for users may need to be updated accordingly. We suggest that an incremental solution will be able to fulfill this requirement. We propose to develop our framework such that it can learn users' interests when making online arrangements. We will study a novel strategy that allows users to give feedback on the events that have been arranged for them which then learns users' interests. We will model the problem as a Multi-Armed Bandit (MAB) problem that can make appropriate long-term arrangements. We plan to implement a prototype system that will integrate the key technical solutions to effective event-planning for EBSNs.

16207617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16207617.value: The prevalence of Web 2.0 and the Online-to-Offline (O2O) marketing model has led to a boom of online event-based social networks (EBSNs) such as Plancast, Meetup and Eventbrite. With the popularity of EBSNs, there has been growing research interest in the effective and strategic management of event organization and participation. Unlike recommender systems, which focus on the interests of one particular party, recent works have been exploring global strategies for event management that can satisfy both event organizers and event participants. However, existing works have mainly focused on offline use of EBSNs when proposing strategies to facilitate event organization. That is, full information of events and users has been known before arranging events and the arrangements have been conducted offline for the available users and events. However, in the real world, users often log in to EBSN platforms online, register for events on a first-come, first-served basis, and information of events and requirements of users can get updated in real time. In this project, we propose to develop a general framework for effective event-planning that considers the dynamic changes of events in EBSN applications. Specifically, the framework will allow for the following key issues: 1) prediction of participants most likely to join an event; 2) incremental event arrangement in a dynamic environment; and 3) feedback-based event arrangement that learns users' interests in online scenarios. We further plan to implement a prototype system that will integrate three key technical solutions to effective event-planning. The results from this project will not only provide a stronger theoretical foundation for event-planning research but also practical guidance for building such a framework in industry. Web 2.0和線上離線（O2O）營銷模式的普及已經導致社交事件網絡（EBSN）如Plancast，Meetup和 Eventbrite在線上急速發展。隨著EBSN的普及，越來越多的研究致力於對事件組織和參與的有效和戰略管理。不像推薦系統，側重於一個特定的興趣. 最近的研究一直在探索可以同時滿足事件組織者和活動參與者的全面的事件管理策略。但現有的工作主要集中在離線使用EBSN時，促進事件組織的策略。在這些工作中， 事件和用戶的完整信息在安排事件之前就已經知道了， 這樣，可用事件和用戶的安排就可以離線進行安排。然而， 在現實世界中，用戶經常在線登錄EBSN平臺，以先到先得的原則註冊一個活動。同時， 用戶的要求和事件的信息是實時更新的。 在這個項目中，考慮到EBSN應用程序中事件是動態變化, 我們將研發一個有效的事件規劃框架。具體來說，研發的框架將解決以下的關鍵問題：1）預測參與者最有可能加入一個活動; 2）在動態環境中做增量的事件安排;和3）在基於反饋的事件安排中在線學習用戶的興趣。我們進一步計劃開發一個將三個關鍵技術整合的事件規劃原型系統。這個項目的研發結果不僅只為事件規劃研究提供了更強的理論基礎， 同時它要給出在行業中建立這樣一個框架的實際指導。

16207617.label: Major findings and research outcome
16207617.value: In this project, to achieve the first objective, we study the problem of event modeling on social media. By proposing the models for capturing events on social media including their contents and social relationships between participants, we develop effective and efficient algorithms to recommend social events to the users [J1, C15]. For the second objective, we focus on the incremental event arrangement problem in a dynamic environment and its related applications. Specifically, we investigate the vehicle dispatching problem in dynamic car-hailing [C12], the dynamic pricing problem in the crowdsourcing market to motivate worker participation [C10, C1, C17], and the multi-worker planning problem in a dynamic crowdsourcing environment [C4, C9]. As for the third objective, we first study how to effectively model and predict the user's behavior when making event arrangements [C14, C7]. Then, we propose a framework to properly plan events based on users' interests learned from social networks [J2]. Besides, we also study the user-event matching problem by considering the spatial-temporal constraints [C18]. To achieve the last objective, we implement a general-purpose user-event recommender system [J2], which integrates the key techniques achieved in Objective 1--3. Through extensive experiments, we demonstrate that our prototype can achieve fast and reliable user-event planning on both real and synthetic datasets. Besides the aforementioned major findings, we also study other data-driven problems related to task assignment, location-based social network (LBSN), bidding, and advertising [J3, J4, C2, C3, C5, C6, C8, C9, C11-13, C16, C19-33].

16207617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16207617.value: The proposed techniques of this project can be applied to general-purpose user-centered recommendation applications (e.g., car-hailing, parcel delivery, smart routing, etc.). Our future work aims at designing effective and efficient large-scale user-event recommendation systems using noisy and incomplete data.

16207617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16207617.value: Event-based social networks (EBSNs), such as Meetup and Plancast, have recently gained a lot of attraction as they allow users to create and join offline social events. To enhance user experience, EBSN platforms are expected to assist users in making suitable and personalized plans so that they can participate in a range of different social events. In this project, we tackle major technical challenges of the existing EBSN solutions. First, we design novel models to depict and predict user's interest in different events. Second, we study the key techniques to handle the user-event planning problem in a highly dynamic environment. Third, we investigate and design recommendation and incentive mechanisms to enhance user experience. By integrating the key techniques, we implement a user-event matching system prototype. Based on extensive experiments on both real and synthetic datasets, our prototype is shown to be both effective and efficient.

16207717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16207717.value: Chemical processes may be divided into two types: continuous and batch. In a batch process, a sequence of activities is performed on a single or multiple pieces of equipment in a defined order to yield a finished product. The process is repeated to produce more of the same product. Batch processes are widely used to manufacture specialty chemicals, electronic materials, polymers, and pharmaceutical products. Compared to continuous processes, batch processes typically occupy only a small amount of space. Thus batch processes are particularly well suited to regions like Hong Kong. Injection molding, a polymer processing process that is important to Hong Kong’s manufacturing business, is an example of a batch process. Precision control of a batch process is necessary for process performance and quality. The control of a batch process is lagging behind that of a continuous process. Recently, we have proposed technologies to improve the control performance of a batch process not only along the time direction but also along the batch direction in a so-called 2D time control frame. But before we can take full advantage of 2D control, a proper process dynamic model must be identified. This proposed project will develop methods for identifying batch process models by exploring batch process repetitiveness. 化学过程可分为连续式和批次式两种。在批处理过程中，在一个或多个设备中以一个确定的顺序执行一系列活动以生成成品。重复这个过程以产生更多相同的产品。批次过程广泛应用于特种化学品、电子、高分子材料、医药产品的生产。与连续过程相比，这种过程通常是紧凑的，占用的空间很小， 特别适合像香港这样的地区。批次过程的精确控制是保证过程性能和质量的必要条件。批次过程控制发展滞后于连续过程。最近，申请小组提出了批次二维控制不仅在时间方向上而且在沿批次方向可以提高控制性能。为了充分发挥二维控制的优势，需要建立合适的过程动力学模型。本项目旨在通过探索批处理过程的重复性来研究过程模型识别方法的发展。开发的方法将进行测试，以改善注塑控制。

16207717.label: Realisation of objectives
16207717.value: This project focuses on the development of modeling methods for batch process (objective 1) and demonstrate the application (objective 2). We used injection molding and battery management system charge-and-discharge operation as a typical batch process. The objectives have been realized in full. Batch process is common to have a model for one condition, eg one type of battery or one combination of injection mold and molding machine, the challenge is that when the process switches to a new condition, eg a new type of battery or a new mold and machine combination for a new molded part manufacturing, the original model developed based process data for the previous case is no longer valid for the new case optimization and/or control, we need to quickly develop the model for the new situation. In this project, based on the nature of process, specifically by exploring similarity between the batches of the same condition and large similarity between processes of different conditions, we have developed various model methods for migrating the model of the previous cases to a new case. For battery aging or state estimation, we developed model migration based on neural network structure, model migration based on Bayesian monte carol simulation, and model migrations by considering uncertainties. We also treated a batch process as a time-batch two-dimensional system for modeling, for example, we used 2D filtering, 2D run-to-run, and 2D optimal learning model for the modeling of a batch process. With batch processes running concurrently, we treat each process as an agent, information from these multiple agents may be shared for the enhancement of individual model of each process, an inter-argent learning framework for modeling this concurrent running batch processes has been proposed and demonstrated for a mass manufacturing scenario where many similar injection molding machines are operated in parallel. Beside modeling batch process dynamics, the end quality of batch operation is also essential, several methods for such a purpose have been proposed, for example, batch-end quality modeling by data-driven method, quality prediction by wavelet denoising OSC-SVM-PLS. A compressive review on various learning-based model predictive controls has also been conducted for batch process during this study. All these methods proposed have been tested to be effective for exemplar batch process of battery or injection molding. The modeling accuracy, efficiency, and validity are all demonstrated on these two processes. A series of quality publications have been resulted in such journals of IEEE Transactions, Applied Energy, Industrial & Engineering Chemistry Research, etc. The application of the proposed modeling or estimation methods have resulted one US and four Chinese patent applications.

16207717.label: Major findings and research outcome
16207717.value: A series of data-driven modelling methods have been proposed based on the findings of batch process nature discovered or explored in this investigation with applications to battery management or injection molding as a typical batch process. The following batch process findings for data-driven modelling have been made where publication in Part C is referred as JX or CX for journal or Conference paper X. (1) A batch process can be efficiently represented in a two time dimensional (2D) system, a traditionally time (t) index and batch (k) index, for the enhancement of model learning across these time indexes for more efficient model development for dynamics(J11, J14), state (J5), quality (J2), control(J3, 11, 14), monitoring and optimisation (J1 & C1). (2) Process similarity may be explored for building model under different conditions. The model developed for an existing condition may be migrated efficiently to a new condition to save modelling time, effort and costs. Model migration methods have been developed and applied for the prediction of battery ageing based on particle filtering (J4), based on neural network (J6), and based on Monte Carlo Simulation (J7). Model migration method has also been developed for modelling battery states such as power capability (J8), health (J12), power (J13), and incremental capacity (J9). (3) Information from concurrently running processes in parallel can be shared for developing modelling and control methods for enhanced performance. In this connection, each process may be treated as an agent and a multi-agent learning framework is developed for model development (J11).

16207717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16207717.value: The findings by exploring batch process nature have been proven to be effective for building efficient models. The current application have been limited to battery management and injection molding, these findings should be equally useful to other batch processes. Development wise, we plan to promote our methods for further applications and license our patented methods for real industrial applications. Academically, we will continue to expand the advancement of model migration and 2D modelling for further control and optimization research.

16207717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16207717.value: Batch process is a widely used manufacturing process where operation is repeated numerous times under a condition before running under a different condition for the manufacturing of a different product. This RGC project finds that good repeatability between runs and reasonable repeatability among different product processes and these repeatability can be explored for developing model efficiently. Two modelling frameworks were developed. One is to represent a batch process as a time-and-batch two time dimensional system for between runs modelling, called 2D modelling, and the other is to migrate the model for an existing product to a new one, called model migration. These two modelling frameworks allow engineers and researchers to model batch process efferently for the estimation, monitoring, control and optimization.

16207817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16207817.value: Many aerosol removal systems encounter difficulty in removing submicron particles, especially in the range of 0.1-1 micron. Densely packed fibre filters are capable of removing some of them, but such filters are expensive to maintain due to the low capacity and frequent replacement requirement. Aerodynamic air cleaners, such as the cyclone, have a longer lifetime and are lower in cost and easier to maintain, but they also face the problem of low removal efficiency for submicron particles. It would be beneficial to find a simple and economical way to enhance their efficiency. It is well-known that roughness in the micrometer-scale could increase the particle deposition rate while certain wind tunnel experiments have revealed that a patterned structure (in the millimeter-scale) on the surface of the wall can also enhance the deposition. However, there has been a lack of studies on the effect of a patterned micro-structure on the deposition rate reported in the literature. Since the smallest turbulence scale can go down to the micrometer level, it is expected that if the patterned structure also goes down to the micro-scale, interaction between the turbulence and the structured pattern will be manifested and the deposition could be further enhanced. Existing aerodynamic air cleaners would become more energy and material efficient than packed fibre filters by the enhancement of micro-structured surfaces. To develop this technology, understanding the particle dynamics and testing in realistic applications is crucial. This project will start with identification and selection of potential structures for the deposition enhancement by large eddy simulation. Then, a number of micro-structured surfaces from simple 2D ribs to complicated 3D structures with different geometrical dimensions will be fabricated and investigated by a series of experiments. An empirical formula for deposition rate for different micro-structures will be developed. It will be further improved by another set of experiments in a curved air duct and in a cyclic flow for more complicated flow fields existing in current air cleaning systems. The findings will help to optimize the dimensions of the micro-structures for maximum deposition enhancement. The feasibility of applying this optimized surface to some existing aerosol removal systems will also be studied by evaluating the performance of the enhanced systems in different operating conditions. This proposed project will enhance knowledge of particle dynamics in turbulence, and the findings will also determine a new direction for the development of aerosol removal systems based on patterned micro-structure. 許多氣溶膠去除系統在去除亞微米顆粒方面遇到困難，特別是在0.1-1微米的範圍內。密集纖維過濾器能夠去除其中的一些，但是由於容量低和更換頻繁，這種過濾器的維護成本高昂。利用空氣動力學原理的空氣淨化器，如旋風分離器，壽命更長、成本更低、易於維護，但也面臨亞微米顆粒去除效率低的問題。若找到一種簡單而經濟的方法來提高其效率，則益處可觀。眾所周知，微米級的粗糙度可以增加顆粒沉積速率，而某些風洞實驗已經揭示了壁表面上的圖案化結構（在毫米級）也可以增強沉積。然而，微米級的圖案化結構對沉積速率的影響的研究一直缺乏。由於最小的湍流尺度可以下降到微米級，因此如果圖案化結構也下降到微米級的尺度，則湍流與結構化圖案之間的相互作用，預期可以進一步提高沉積速率。通過改變現有的空氣動力學原理的空氣淨化器的表面結構，該類淨化器將變得比纖維過濾器，在能量和材料方面更加有效率。要開發這種技術，了解粒子動力學及在現實應用中測試是為至關重要。本項目先通過大渦數值模擬計算從而識別和選擇能增強沉積效果的潛在圖案化結構。然後，通過製作一系列的壁表面，從簡單的二維圖案化結構到具有不同幾何尺寸的複雜三維結構，並對其進行實驗，從而建立不同微結構沉積速率的經驗公式。接著，通過另一組在彎曲風道中的實驗，以及模擬當前空氣淨化系統中存在的更複雜的流場，進一步改進公式的實際應用效果。這些發現將有助於優化微結構的尺寸以實現最大的沉積增強。最後，將這種優化的表面安裝於一些現有的空氣淨化器中，並在不同的操作條件下作性能測試，以了解本技術的應用效果。這個項目，將提升我們對湍流中粒子動力學的知識，這些研究結果也將為氣溶膠去除系統的研究開創新的方向。

16207817.label: Realisation of objectives
16207817.value: The overall objectives have been achieved. The effects of micro-structured surfaces on particle deposition enhancement in turbulent flows and in a chamber were studied. A particle deposition velocity model was developed based on experimental and numerical approaches. The optimized geometrical dimensions, shape and spacing of the micro-structure were developed to enhance particle deposition. The particle removal system assisted by the micro-structures on surfaces was developed and tested under different operation conditions. Some key results are shown below. The semi-circular micro-structured surfaces with different pitch-to-height ratios were designed and the effect on particle deposition enhancement was investigated. Numerical simulation with near-wall correlations was employed to study particle deposition on the semi-circular structured surface in a fully developed turbulent channel flow. The flow fields around surfaces structures were simulated in a two-dimensional channel flow by using the Reynolds stress model, corrected by turbulence velocity fluctuation in the wall-normal direction. The particle trajectory was solved by using Lagrangian particle tracking. The particle deposition efficiency and flow mechanism induced by modification of surface structures were analyzed. It was found that the submicron particles firstly follow the recirculation flow to the middle of the cavity. Then, the entrainment traps the submicron particles at the near-wall boundary layers. As particles enter the distance less than two wall units from the surface, they collide with the surface under the Brownian motion effect. The highest particle deposition enhancement occurs at the range of submicron (0.1 mm to 1 mm) compared with ultrafine and micron particles. The highest efficiency ratio reaches 1137 in the semi-circular structured surfaces at the pitch-to-height ratio of 3. This study indicated that surface patterned structures can greatly enhance the submicron deposition efficiency. Different forms of surface patterns inspired by nature were designed and parametric studies were performed to enhance deposition efficiency in a turbulent channel flow. The parametric studies comprised three different aspects: geometry of the patterned surface, pitch-to-height ratio, and particle size. Particle deposition enhancement by various patterned surfaces (rectangular, triangular, semi-circular and open circular) were investigated by numerical simulation. The numerical simulation results were compared and validated with the experimental deposition velocity. The variance of the particle deposition velocity followed a “V” curve for a smooth channel in the size range of 0.01 μm to 8 μm. When the patterned surface had been added into the turbulent flow, the “V” curves of particle deposition were dramatically weakened. This was because the particle deposition at the submicron range had a much higher deposition enhancement (nearly 1000) compared with ultrafine and micron-sized particles. The enhancement ratio at ultrafine and micron-sized particles was below 10 times. When different pitch-to-height ratios (p/e=3, 4, 5 and 6) were considered for the open-circular surface, the p/e of 3 had the best particle deposition enhancement. Although the patterned surface was proven to have higher particle deposition velocity compared with smooth channels, the pressure drop increased at the same time. An overall performance in terms of efficiency index of the different patterned surfaces had been compared to indicate the best shape to be used in the air cleaners. The semi-circular shape achieved the highest efficiency index compared with other patterned surfaces for different p/e. A maximum deposition enhancement of 5009 can be reached at the p/e of 4 for the semi-circular patterns and a maximum efficiency index of 1137 at the p/e of 3 was obtained by considering the deposition enhancement as well as pressure drop increase. This study indicated that the semi-circular surface pattern with the p/e of 4 should be recommended to enhance the overall performance of particle removal devices, especially for submicron particles. Parametric studies were also conducted to enhance deposition efficiency in a chamber environment with forced air circulation. Different shapes (triangular, rectangular, semi-circular convex and semi-circular concave ribbed structures) and p/e values of patterned structures were studied. Particle sizes ranging from 0.3 μm to 5 μm in diameter were tested. Particle image velocimetry (PIV) technique was employed to characterize the flow pattern immediately above the surface structures and analyze the deposition mechanism of particles on patterned surface. It was found that for submicron particles, deposition velocity was increased by the patterned microstructures, and triangular-ribbed surfaces achieved the highest deposition velocity, which was 10 times higher than that on a non-patterned surface. For micron particles, it was found that deposition velocity was lower than that of a non-patterned surface. The results showed that particle deposition was not always enhanced by roughness, and it was possible to be reduced by a suitable length scale of patterned structures. The enhancement or reduction effect gradually vanished with the increasing p/e ratio. A semi-mathematical model was then developed to predict the particle deposition velocity on different pitch-to-height ratios of a microstructure surface. The particle deposition was commonly modeled by the mass flux to the wall and the mass flux can be modeled by the particle deposition velocity divided by the bulk concentration of particles. The geometrical dimensions of the patterned structures were from tens to hundreds of micrometers and were characterized by a number of parameters including the height, the pitch, and the shape factor of the rib. The boundary layer existed in three modes of transport of particles including eddy diffusion, Brownian motion and gravitational settling. A mathematical equation was proposed to describe the general form of the non-dimensional deposition velocity in the boundary layer plus an inertial-interception effect for the microstructure surface. The factors of surface roughness, gravitational settling, dimensionless shape factor, and deposition locations were considered. The predicted deposition velocity was then compared with experimental results. The results showed that the semi-mathematical equation had a good agreement with the experimental data under different pitch-to-height ratios. The semi-mathematical model was also extended to different sized particles. The non-dimensional deposition velocity calculated by the semi-mathematical model and numerical model followed a similar trend from ultrafine particles to micron-sized particles. The proposed semi-mathematical model can help design the micropatterns of the surface to achieve maximum particle deposition efficiency. An air cleaning technique aiming at submicron particles by means of installing patterned surfaces on the walls of ventilation ducts was proposed. A feasibility study of applying semicircular patterned surfaces as an air cleaning technique in ventilation ducts was conducted in comparison with the HEPA filter. The effect of patterned surfaces on particle deposition was numerically studied which was validated with a particle deposition experiment. A wind tunnel experiment was carried out to quantify the particle deposition on the semicircular micropatterns for a wide range of heights. Numerical results showed that the semicircular pattern height of 500 µm with the p/e of 10 had 8.58 times enhancement of the energy efficiency compared with a high-efficiency particulate air filter. The results indicated that adding surface micropatterns to ventilation ducting for submicron particle deposition was a possible energy-efficient air cleaning technique for practical usage. However, patterned surfaces also cause pressure resistance to the duct. The overall performance combined with deposition enhancement and increase of pressure drop in the HEPA filter was 50.79. Therefore, we suggest using the semicircular height of 500 µm at the p/e value of 10, which has the highest efficiency index at 435.90.

16207817.label: Major findings and research outcome
16207817.value: The patterned surfaces were fabricated and the effect on particle deposition enhancement was investigated. It was found that for the patterned surfaces in the turbulent flow, the “V” curve of particle deposition was dramatically weakened (Xu et al. 2020). The deposition enhancement for submicron particles was nearly 1000 times, while the enhancement ratio at ultrafine and micro-sized particles was below 10 times. The flow field near the surface patterns was then numerically and experimentally characterized (Xu et al. 2020; Zhong et al. 2021). It was found that the submicron particles firstly follow the recirculation flow to the middle of the cavity. Then the entrainment by turbulence kinetic energy trapped the submicron particles at the near-wall boundary layers. As particles entered the distance less than two wall units from the surface, they collided with the surface under the Brownian motion effect. As the pitch-to-height ratio (p/e) increased, the ratio of deposition velocity downstream to the deposition velocity upstream increased. An overall performance in terms of efficiency index of different patterned surface was then compared to indicate the best shape to be used in the air cleaners. The semi-circular shape achieved the highest efficiency index compared with other patterned surfaces for different p/e (Xu et al. 2020). A maximum deposition enhancement of 5009 can be reached at the p/e of 4 for the semi-circular patterns and a maximum efficiency index of 1137 at the p/e of 3 was obtained by considering the deposition enhancement as well as pressure drop increase. A semi-mathematical model was then developed to predict particle deposition velocity on different p/e of a microstructure surface (Xu’s PhD thesis). The non-dimensional deposition velocity calculated by the semi-mathematical model and numerical model followed a similar trend from ultrafine particles to micron-sized particles. A feasibility study of applying semicircular patterned surfaces as an air cleaning technique in ventilation ducts was conducted in comparison with the HEPA filter (Xu et al. 2020). The effect of patterned surfaces on particle deposition was numerically studied which was validated with a particle deposition experiment. It was found that the semicircular pattern height of 500 µm with the p/e of 10 had 8.58 times enhancement of the energy efficiency compared with a high-efficiency particulate air filter. The results indicated that adding surface micropatterns to ventilation ducting for submicron particle deposition was a possible energy-efficient air cleaning technique for practical usage.

16207817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16207817.value: This project focused on the vortex generation by the micro-to-millimeter scale patterns, which were much larger than the particle size. Smaller roughness elements on the surface in the same scale as the submicron particles were not considered. The turbophoresis force for the smaller roughness elements on the surface in the particle trajectory equation could be studied in the future. Moreover, in this work, the aerosol deposition on the photopolymer resin material was tested. The patterned surface was hydrophilic. Therefore, this research supposed that particle did not resuspend from the surfaces. Other hydrophobic patterned surfaces and aerosol with weaker adhesive forces could be examined in the future because they may be more susceptible to detach from the surface. Possible resuspension of particles are valuable to be investigated. In the real applicable cases, the area of patterned surface will be much larger than our fabricated devices for laboratory usage. The patterned surface in the ventilation ducts should be cleaned easily and reused frequently in order to save the maintenance budget in the ventilation system. Further studies about maintenance issues and comparison of the costs of usage of the patterned surface and the HEPA filter in ventilation ducts are necessary for commercialization purpose.

16207817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16207817.value: Many aerosol removal systems encounter difficulty in removing submicron particles, especially in the range of 0.1-1 micron. Densely packed fibre filters are capable of removing some of them, but such filters are expensive to maintain due to the low capacity and frequent replacement requirement. Aerodynamic air cleaners such as the cyclones which have a longer lifetime and are lower in cost and easier to maintain, but they also face the problem of low removal efficiency for submicron particles. It is well known that a millimeter-scale roughness or patterned structure could increase the particle deposition rate. Since the smallest turbulence scale can go down to the micrometer level, it is expected that a micro-scale patterned structure interacting with the turbulence could further enhance the submicron particle deposition. This project carries out step-by-step experimental and numerical analysis to study particle deposition on patterned surfaces. Patterned surfaces with different shapes and pitch-to-height ratios were investigated. It is found that surface patterned structures in the semi-circular shape can greatly enhance submicron deposition efficiency with few thousand times of that for smooth surface. The findings enhance our knowledge on submicron particle deposition and help improve the efficiency of aerosol removal systems based on patterned micro-structure.
