16207917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16207917.value: 近年来，随着我们的基础设施高度依赖于各类电子系统，系统的安全问题已经变得越来越重要。要解决系统安全问题，不仅需要开发针对现有威胁的保护性策略，更需要对新出现的攻击进行识别与建模。针对这些方面的需求，本提案分析硬件以及底层软件中可能被攻击者修改用以破坏系统安全的未规范功能，并提出相应的方法来检测这些恶意修改。 由于一个设计规范可以通过很多（甚至无穷多）不同的方式得以实现，未规范的功能是硬件以及软件设计过程中常见的副产品。传统的验证方法和指标专注于回答的问题是：该设计能否正确地实现规范的功能？而本提案要解决的问题是：除了实现规范的功能外，该设计是否会引起恶意功能？芯片中的恶意功能通常叫做硬件木马。 当前的研究中，木马一般被认为会直接影响规范的功能。而为了保证木马的隐蔽性以及确保其在系统测试或运行中不被激活，木马的触发都需要极端的条件。而本提案要解决的木马只在信号表现未有任何规范的周期内对设计信号进行修改，即该类木马不需要设定触发条件。该类木马不会与规范的功能发生冲突，也不会被已有的验证方法或者木马检测方法检测出。考虑到已有研究证明该类木马能够泄露敏感的设计信息，充分表征该类木马所构成的威胁并提出高效可行的检测办法是势在必行的。 本提案中，我们首次提出一种能够检测未规范功能中木马的方法，而该方法并不需要提前定义未规范功能中的正常行为。只要未规范功能能够被具体标识，我们即可开发一种自动的分析方法，以识别那些容易被嵌入木马的未规范功能。该方法能够广泛应用于不同抽象层次而不需要先验的特殊设计知识。 与此同时，我们将人工检测几类重要的设计类别，诸如通用处理器，FPGA比特流以及模拟传感器，以此证明在此类设计中木马攻击的可行性。由于本提案中的检测方法只针对未规范功能，我们也将直接给出未规范功能的描述与定义。此外，本提案也将重点研究硬件/软件边界处（指令集架构和设备驱动程序代码）的未规范功能，以防止软件攻击与硬件木马相结合。考虑到无论系统是否包含软件、纯数位电路、模拟电路或者这些部件的结合，系统实现过程中都广泛存在着的未规范功能，本提案中我们采用整体分析法来解决系统安全问题，而不是只针对特定的平台。

16207917.label: Realisation of objectives
16207917.value: Overall, we have achieved the vast majority of our target objectives. Some of the results are very promising, exceeded our initial expectations, and have been well received by the industry and the scientific community, evident by the multiple keynote and invited talk invitations to the PI for presenting the results in major conferences and scientific forums. For the execution of this project, the first two objectives were pursued through our idea of detecting Trojans in unspecified functionality by solving satisfiability problems: For modern complex designs it is impossible to fully specify design behavior, and only feasible to verify functionally meaningful scenarios. Hardware Trojans modifying only unspecified functionality are not possible to detect using existing verification methodologies and Trojan detection strategies. Through this research, we have successfully devised a detection methodology for these Trojans by 1) precisely defining “suspicious” unspecified functionality in terms of information leakage, and 2) formulating detection as a satisfiability problem that can take advantage of the recent advances in both boolean and satisfiability modulo theory (SMT) solvers. Our detection procedure, which is automatic, can be followed using a wide variety of tools and techniques, and we give specifics for Trojan detection using 1) data-flow graph analysis and SMT solving, and 2) equivalence checking, meaning our method is applicable to both register-transfer-level (RTL) and gate-level designs. We demonstrated our automated detection methodology to multiple publically available designs and successfully and efficiently detect Trojan-infected versions of both designs. The inserted Trojans process information leaked through the bus interface, exploiting the fact that bus protocols only partially specify signal behavior. Our methodology is the first to provide an atomated detection mechanism for this Trojan type. The last three objectives were pursued through characterizing unspecified functionality by mining simulation traces. Unspecified design functionality can be modified by Hardware Trojans to leak information. Techniques developed by this project are capable of detecting these Trojans, but require that unspecified functionality already be characterized which was a major limitation. To address this limitation, we showed previously the potential of using “mutation testing” to uncover testbench holes and highlight unspecified functionality, but such as technique requires tedious manual analysis of undetected faults to gain useful insight. In pursuing these objectives, we provide the missing link required to fully automate characterization of unspecified functionality and can formally prove the absence of Trojans. As a result, we developed an approach to mine simulation traces generated during mutation testing to produce assertions characterizing verification holes or unspecified functionality. These assertions can be fed directly to Trojan detection methods making securing unspecified functionality a completely automated process. Our trace mining technique is able to identify unspecified functionality in several widely used IP cores and verify and confirm that the functionality is benign, while flagging the same functionality in a Trojan-infected version of the design. As stated before, we have achieved the vast majority of our target objectives. The only missing portion is the coverage to device drivers and some analog functionality because of the lack of access to the device driver code and some analog IP blocks due to commercial confidentiality. I believe such missing elements are minor and do not affect the major goals and achievements of the main results.

16207917.label: Major findings and research outcome
16207917.value: In addition to the two key findings summarized in paragraphs 2 and 3 of Section 5.3, the following are two additional major results along with key findings: 1. Detecting Hardware Trojans in Unspecified JTAG Functionality: In this study we focused on Trojans in unspecified JTAG functionality, which has not been investigated before. Widely implemented standards such as IEEE 1149.1 (JTAG) and P1687 (iJTAG) standards are essential in providing improved chip and board testability, but it has been demonstrated that undocumented or poorly obfuscated scan and debug instructions can be exploited by hackers to undermine system security. Out-of-spec JTAG functionality can be inserted accidentally or with malicious intent. This study developed a technique capable of detecting anomalous JTAG instructions not present in the specification using commercial formal equivalence checking tools. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our technique by characterizing the entire JTAG instruction set space for the publicly available open source design OpenSPARC T2 benchmark in a completely automated manner. A full-length, peer-reviewed paper on this has been published in 2018 International Test Conference (ITC), the premier conference in hardware testing. 2. Evaluating Assertion Set Completeness to Expose Hardware Trojans and Verification Blindspots. Determining the quality and completeness of the verification infrastructure, including design assertions, is a challenging but important problem which is further complicated by the potential inclusion of extra malicious functionality hiding in unspecified design behavior. Existing testbench and assertion set completeness metrics do not handle unspecified functionality securely, and existing Trojan detection techniques targeting analysis of unspecified behavior miss the opportunity to use the assertion set to characterize unspecified and unverified conditions. In this project, we developed solutions successfully overcoming both of these shortcomings. Our solutions overcome such problems by mining simulation trace data and assertion coverage to find unverified conditions then use formal methods to differentiate benign unspecified behavior from verification blindspots and malicious functionality. We analyzed a couple of practical designs and demonstrated that our method successfully uncovers verification blindspots masking actual design bugs and potentially malicious behavior and detects information leakage Trojans inserted in both designs. A full-length, peer-reviewed paper on this has been published in 2019 Design, Automation and Test in Europe (DATE), the major European event on electronic design and design automation.

16207917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16207917.value: Because unspecified functionality in modern chip design, the key target of this study, is by nature unknown, there is still much work to be done in fully exploring the scope of the Trojan threat in this space beyond what has been developed in this project. Future work includes exploration of unspecified functionality at higher levels of design abstraction such as SystemC and TLM, as well as developing more “hardware information flow analysis” tools to analyze security specifications and verify them accordingly. This study offered some foundation for security-aware Electronic Design Automation (EDA) or Computer-Aided Design (CAD), and should be extended to be part of the tool chain whereas the commercial design for security and validation solutions can be robustly offered.

16207917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16207917.value: In this project we have addressed the threat of Hardware Trojans in unspecified design Functionality in hardware chips. Due to the complexity of modern chips, a design specification usually only defines a small fraction of behavior. Traditional verification techniques only focus on ensuring the correctness of specified behavior, meaning any modifications or bugs (malicious or accidental) only affecting unspecified functionality will likely go undetected. Addressing this Trojan type requires a fundamentally different approach from both existing Trojan detection and hardware verification methods. In this project, we developed such an approach to address this critical hardware security issue. In this project, we first illustrated how this verification hole allows an attacker with the ability to modify the design to stealthily undermine the security of a system. Furthermore, by viewing security as an extension of the verification problem we successfully developed a suite of methods which both detect Trojans and increase confidence in the correctness of specified design functionality. These techniques include a Trojan prevention methodology, a method capable of identifying dangerous unspecified functionality, and a methodology which inspects this dangerous unspecified functionality for the existence of Trojans.

16208117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16208117.value: 摘要：相比現有的無線系統，預計未來的無線通信技術將有高達1000倍的性能提升。這些技術不僅可以提供比如多媒體的傳統傳送服務，而且還可以用作機器對機器控制的關鍵系統，並且作為物聯網（IoT）的主要骨幹。然而，現有的系統技術如正交頻域復用接入（OFDMA）在提高無線系統性能方面幾乎已達到了極限。因此，業界正在考慮採用新穎的方法來提供更強的性能，而這些新穎的方法多圍繞天線範疇。這包括大規模的多輸入多輸出（MIMO），其中將在基站使用數百個天線，並使用高於18吉赫（18GHz）的毫米波系統，同時，手機裝置需配備緊湊，可控波束及高增益的天線。此外，還考慮了其他天線技術，包括移動裝置上的多個天線使用，運用具有緊湊型高增益天線的微微小區以及用於在物聯網中應用的無線能量傳輸的天線。然而，滿足這些要求的天線設計變得越來越具有挑戰性，這不是依靠天線工程師的設計直觀，而是迫切需要天線改進分析的設計方法。 為了滿足這種天線設計挑戰，我們希望將特徵模式理論（TCM）應用於下一代無線通信像素天線的分析和設計。TCM作為緊湊型天線設計的基礎分析工具正在重新出現，因此，天線設計的 “藝術” 可以通過增強的分析和理解得到補充。TCM可以幫助估算結構的基本諧振模式，從而提供關於特定結構的天線帶寬，工作頻率，端口和模式的基本限制信息。這使得天線設計者能夠創建接近TCM所發現的限制的饋送機制。此外，TCM還可以啟發對結構的修改或將重不被考慮的天線設計變為可能。在這裡提出的研究計劃中，我們打算通過開發高效的計算技術，分析和優化工具以及通過原型驗證來探索使用TCM進行像素天線的分析和設計。這項研究的長期意義在於，它可導致開發符合未來無線通信系統要求的天線新方法和設計。

16208117.label: Realisation of objectives
16208117.value: Both objectives have been met fully. This research has provided new insights for us on how to use the Theory of Characteristic Modes (TCM) for designing antennas and several publications have resulted from it. The first objective has involved the application of TCM to the design of pixel antennas. The breakthrough that we made in this work was using the N-port version of TCM. This allowed us to efficiently apply TCM to the design of pixel antennas which can be thought of as N-port loaded structures. By applying TCM to the pixel antennas we could perform their design and optimization on the TCM modes directly without considering the feed network and feed location. This allowed us to find the fundamental performance limits of the pixel geometry. After the pixel geometry was optimized we could then determine the feed locations as a second process. This is the first time these techniques have been utilized with TCM and pixel antennas and the work is published [J1]. These results also led us to develop more types of approaches to the design of pixel antennas and these have also been published [J7]. The second objective led us to design some innovative antennas based on TCM. By analyzing one of our previous antenna designs by using TCM we were able to extract one extra degree of freedom to allow 3 ports with orthogonal parts and low coupling to be co-located. This has led us to journal publications [J2] and extensions [J5,C1]. The work is important because it can be utilized in basestation massive MIMO antennas to reduce their size by 50%. It also helped us design antennas using TCM [J3]. In addition to this work the N-port TCM approach developed for pixel antennas also allowed us to take a fresh look at the design of ESPAR antennas. One of the bottle necks in these designs has been obtaining the necessary feed settings to produce orthogonal patterns. Until now only specific geometries could be handled. Our work on applying TCM to ESPAR has opened up the design of ESPAR antennas to any geometry [J4]. In addition we have also generalized this approach [J6] that is extremely flexible and can be applied to other publications as well.

16208117.label: Major findings and research outcome
16208117.value: Summarizing the details from section 5.3 three main break throughs were made as follows: 1) The utilization of the theory of characteristic modes (TCMs) in the design of pixel antennas by applying its N-port form. This allowed us to optimize the design from a fundamental perspective without considering feeds [J1]. 2) The application of N-port TCM to the design of ESPAR antennas. This has allowed the finding of orthogonal radiation patterns for any configuration of ESPAR antenna [J4,J6]. 3) Utilizing TCM to find more radiation modes allowing compact antenna elements for compact massive MIMO antennas. Space saving is up to 50% [J3,J5].

16208117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16208117.value: One interesting extension of this work could be to electromagnetic information theory (EIT). TCM provides for a natural decomposition of radiated fields into modes. This conveniently allows multiple input multiple output (MIMO) antenna systems to be analyzed using electromagnetics linking information with it. That is we may be able to design antennas that directly maximize channel capacity and reach the theoretical bounds on size.

16208117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16208117.value: This research considers looking at radio frequency radiation from the perspective of natural resonant modes and is known as analysis by the theory of characteristic modes (TCM). Using these natural resonant modes allows us to consider antenna design from a fundamental perspective in order to optimize their performance. Using this approach we have developed basestation antennas for 5G systems (massive MIMO antennas) that are 50% smaller than conventional techniques. In addition we have been able to enhance the design of other types of antennas known as pixel antennas and parasitic antennas. The work has been written up into 7 journal papers.

16208517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16208517.value: The objective of this project is to study the resilience of cyber-physical systems (CPSs), focusing on scenarios where cyber attack may occur and attackers have only partial information on the systems. Cyber attacks CPSs have attracted a rapidly growing number of researches. Most existing literature results assume that the attackers have complete a priori knowledge of the operating systems and/or full disruption/disclosure resources. In practice, however, there are many cases in which the attackers only have partial information on the systems and/or limited attack power. Two problems naturally arise: how the attackers with partial information can deteriorate system performance and what efficient and resilient countermeasures the system managers should take. We aim to provide answers to these two problems in this project. Under the assumption that the attacker has complete model knowledge and can listen to every transmitted packet, the interactive way between the system and the attacker can be formulated as a game with fully observable states. While for attackers with limited model knowledge or partial disclosure resources, a game with partially observable states is required, which is much more challenging to analyze. Also, the attacker that has non-perfect a priori model knowledge might infer the model knowledge by its attack actions using learning techniques. Motivated by these observations, we propose to develop a systematic approach to study CPSs under limited attacks, on which few studies have been done so far, based on reinforcement learning, stochastic game theory with asymmetric information and information theory. We shall develop novel theories to achieve better control/estimation system performance and increase system's resilience to cyber attacks, thus making a genuine contribution to the fast developing field of CPSs. 這個項目的目的是研究物理信息系統抵禦攻擊的能力, 特別集中考慮系統攻擊者對系統的了解不齊全的情況。物理信息系統的攻擊已引起廣泛關注。在這題目上現有文獻的大部分都假設攻擊者掌握系統運作的所有信息抑或能對系統作出無限制的干擾。但是，在大部份實際情況中，攻擊者只有系統的部份信息並設有攻擊能力的限制。此假設帶出兩個問題：從攻擊的角度，一個對系統一知半解的攻擊者能如何破壞系統？從系統的角度，應如何有效地對付攻擊？我們希望藉這個項目能夠解答以上的問題。 如果假設攻擊者對系統完全了解，包括知道系統發的信息包裹，我們可以用完全可觀察的博弈理論來描述攻擊和系統的互動。但是在攻擊者的知識和能力受限之下，我們需要用具有更高挑戰性的部分可觀察的博奕論來做分析。在這假設之下，攻擊者能夠不斷更新對系統的認識。所以，我們提議從信息理論，隨機博奕論和強化學習的途徑研究受有限攻擊的物理信息系統。所研發出的新理論將有助于優化系統參數估計, 提高控制系統的性能表現, 以及加增系統對攻擊的防禦性, 從而對物理信息系統的研究有較大貢獻。

16208517.label: Realisation of objectives
16208517.value: We have made excellent progress with this funding. Following the original objectives of the project, we have successfully investigated cyber-physical system security from a game-theoretic and learning point of view. For a number of different application scenarios such as remote estimation and networked control, we evaluated the system performance under typical cyber attacks (including reset attack, event-based stealthy attack, eavesdropping attack, etc.). We proposed novel state estimation, intrusion detection and control algorithms as counter-measures to these attacks. We further analyzed the security and system performance tradeoff. In addition to the original objectives, we have successfully applied the developed tools to other areas such as privacy-preserving consensus, efficient sensor scheduling, etc. The results are fruitful which are summarized and published in 7 leading prestigious international journals (five published in the IEEE-TAC and one in Automatica) and 3 leading international conferences. Two PhD students are trained during the project period.

16208517.label: Major findings and research outcome
16208517.value: We have conducted a full-spectrum and thorough study of cyber-physical systems security from a game-theoretic point of view with applications to remote estimation, multisensor filtering, consensus, multi-agent systems, etc. We have fully met the original project objectives and achieved more which is beyond our expectation. A number of novel CPS security problems have been formulated such as reset attacks, event-based stealthy attacks, and eavesdropping attacks. In addition, corresponding novel system defense mechanisms have been proposed to make the system resilient to cyber attacks. The main research outcomes include publications in 7 leading international journals and 3 leading international conferences as well as training of two PhD students.

16208517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16208517.value: The research outcomes are fruitful and paved the way for a number of exciting future research directions including extensions to general nonlinear systems security, other types of cyber-attacks, better tradeoff analysis, applications to multi-agents systems and IoT, etc.

16208517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16208517.value: We provided a thorough analysis of the system performance under malicious attacks and proposed corresponding effective well-designed countermeasures using game-theoretic and learning approaches. Some novel security-aware control frameworks are proposed which are critical in helping enhance our understanding of critical security issues arise in CPSs. These results will not only enrich the theoretical results in cyber-physical security but also contribute to their practical applications, for example, they would be of major strategic relevance to local industries which use CPSs in a networked environment that may encounter malicious attacks, or in autonomous vehicles where without proper security protections, they could become killers on the road.

16208617.value: 無線傳感器網絡（WSN）推動了物聯網（IoT），尤其是貼近人們生活的以人為中心的物聯網的快速發展。在這些應用中，射頻收發機消耗了遠程傳感器節點的高達90%的功率。為了延長工作壽命，我們希望收發機有更好的能量效率。能量採集技術促進了無處不在的無線傳感器網絡的發展。然而，採集到的能量例如太陽能和熱電能只能提供低電壓。為了提高系統的整體效率，我們應該開發一種超低電壓超低功率的設計。 超低電壓超低功率設計涉及到功率和包括線性、頻譜效率、抗干擾能力、靈敏度在內的諸多參數的重要權衡。超低電壓設計的主要挑戰在於有限的電壓餘量和退化的晶體管截止頻率fT。各種架構和新穎的設計已經被探索過來優化這種權衡。 本課題的目的是實現用於以人為中心的物聯網的超低電壓超低功率無線收發機。實際應用包括娛樂和健康護理。通信範圍從體內到人的周圍不等。根據通信距離和靈敏度的要求，我們提出不同的架構和電路設計來最大化能量效率並仍然滿足系統的各項指標。

16208617.label: Major findings and research outcome
16208617.value: • Magnetic tuning techniques were proposed for both coarse tuning or fine tuning for low-voltage low-power oscillators to achieve ultra-wide frequency tuning range and low phase noise without a need for varactors with low quality factor Q at high frequencies. The techniques were demonstrated and published in the IEEE Custom Integrated Circuits Conference in April 2019. • A harmonic-extraction technique was proposed to enhance the amplitude and the phase noise of LC oscillators at the third-harmonic frequency. By leveraging this technique, a cascaded injection-locked local oscillator (LO) generator is proposed, which consists of a fundamental voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) and a millimeter-wave (mm-wave) injection-locked frequency multiplier (ILFM). The work was first published in the IEEE Asian Solid-State Circuits Conference in November 2019 and later was invited to be expanded for publications in the IEEE Transactions on Microwave Theory and Techniques (TMTT) in July 2020, which is one of the top journals in the research area. • Finally, a novel frequency synthesizer was successfully proposed, which consisted of a radio-frequency subsampling phase-locked loop (SS-PLL) with injection-locked frequency multipliers (ILFMs) and a mixer for frequency extension. Enhanced third-harmonic and fourth-harmonic-extraction techniques were proposed for the ILFMs with different multiplication ratios. In addition, a frequency-tracking loop (FTL) with automatic frequency and amplitude calibration was embedded for the ILFMs. Moreover, a distributed bias technique was employed to improve the linearity of the wideband magnetic-tuning oscillator. All the blocks were designed and integrated to achieve a fully-integrated synthesizer demonstrated with the state-of-the-art performance. The work was first published in the IEEE Very-Large-Scale-Integration Circuits Symposium (VLSI) in June 2019 and later invited to be expanded for publication in the the IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits (JSSC) in April 2020, which is the most prestigious journal in the area of IC design.

16208617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16208617.value: With 5G technologies becoming available and deployable, it would be useful to apply the proposed design techniques to achieve high performance at millimeter-wave frequencies of 60GHz and beyond. In addition, the performance in terms of power consumption and size/cost would also be much improved if more advanced CMOS processes either 40nm or 28nm minimum feature sizes) are used instead of 65nm processes.

16208617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16208617.value: The research project has contributed significantly to the advancement of the state-of-the-art performance in the field of wireless radios for internet-of-things in terms of high integration and high performance while not only operating at higher frequencies for higher data rates but also consuming less power for longer battery life and occupying a smaller chip area for lower cost.

16208917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16208917.value: Modern portfolio theory, pioneered by Harry Markowitz in the 1950s, has revolutionized the finance world. Prior to that, people made investments mainly based on their expertise or experience. The appearance of modern portfolio theory laid the foundations and shaped investment into a mathematical and systematical activity. Without exaggeration, it is one of the pillars of modern finance and investing. Interestingly, there is a strong mathematical connection between Markowitz mean-variance portfolio design in finance and filter/beamforming design in wireless communication systems. This allows the application of methodologies from wireless communications to financial engineering and vice-versa. Besides modern portfolio theory, many other investment strategies have also been proposed for different goals. Index tracking attempts to follow the market index based on the efficient market assumption. Kelly's strategy tries to maximize the wealth growth rate of a long-term investment. Risk parity aims at distributing the overall risk of the portfolio equally among assets for risk diversification or equalization. Statistical arbitrage is a contrarian strategy based on forming a synthetic asset independent of the market and then benefiting from its random oscillations, essentially trading the residual noise. From the perspective of optimization, investment strategies, including those mentioned above, can be mathematically formulated as optimization problems. This is nontrivial, however, and the difficulty can be summarized into two issues. The first one is how to formulate the portfolio problem properly so that the designed portfolio behaves as expected and delivers in the financial markets. The second one is how to solve these optimization problems efficiently and accurately once they are formulated. This proposal aims at developing advanced portfolio strategies that are more flexible and responsive to today's changing investment environment, using optimization and signal processing tools borrowed from wireless communication systems. Our preliminary work shows that the considered portfolio strategies for different investing scenarios are meaningful and promising. 20世纪50年代，由哈利•马可维茨率先开创的现代投资组合理论彻底改变了金融世界。在此之前，人们主要依靠他们的专业知识或经验进行投资。现代投资组合理论的出现逐渐成为现代投资的基础并且使得投资成为一个数学化以及系统性的活动。毫不夸张地说，它是现代金融和投资的支柱之一。有趣的是，金融中的马可维茨均值方差投资组合设计和无线通信系统中滤波器/波束成形设计之间存在很强的数学关系。这就使得无线通信系统中使用的方法可以应用于金融工程中，反之亦然。 除了现代投资组合理论，还有其他许多针对不同投资目标的投资策略。指数跟踪在承认有效市场的前提下试图跟随市场指数。基于凯利公式的投资策略则是尽量提高长期投资的财富增长率。风险平价旨在将投资组合的整体风险平均分配给风险资产或均等化。统计套利是基于市场的随机波动来构建独立于市场的投资组合的逆向策略。从优化的角度来看，包括上述在内的投资策略，可以数学化地表示成优化问题。然而，这并非简单的工作，其难点可以归结为两个方面。首先是如何正确地公式化表示投资组合问题，使得设计的投资组合的行为符合预期并在金融市场有效运作。其次是公式化之后如何高效准确地解决这些优化问题。 本项目旨在借助无线通信中的优化和信号处理技术设计更先进的投资组合策略以适应当前日益复杂的投资环境。 我们的初步研究工作表明，针对不同投资方案设计的投资组合策略是富有意义和前景的。

16208917.label: Realisation of objectives
16208917.value: The main goal of this project was the development of advanced portfolio strategies using optimization and signal processing tools borrowed from wireless communication systems. In particular, the three proposed objectives focus around three main strategies: 1) index tracking, 2) Kelly portfolio, and 3) statistical arbitrage portfolio. All the objectives have been more than satisfactorily completed (in fact three extra objectives have been accomplished) and the output consists of one book, 11 IEEE top journal papers, 8 conference papers, and 6 open-source software packages (see https://www.danielppalomar.com/software.html for software details). Objective 1 focused on sparse index tracking. We proposed efficient and fast index tracking algorithms that automatically perform asset selection and capital allocation under a set of general convex constraints. A special consideration was given to the case of the nonconvex holding constraints and to the downside risk tracking measure. Furthermore, we derived specialized algorithms with closed-form updates for particular sets of constraints. Numerical simulations showed that the proposed algorithms match or outperform existing methods in terms of performance, while their running time is lower by many orders of magnitude. The main output consists of a journal paper, a book, and a software package (https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=sparseIndexTracking). Objective 2 revolved around four variations and extensions of Kelly portfolio; to be specific: portfolio combining stocks with options, risk parity portfolio, quantile portfolio, and high-order portfolio. The output corresponding to these four topics includes four journal papers, two conference papers, and two software packages (https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=riskParityPortfolio, https://github.com/dppalomar/highOrderPortfolios). Objective 3 considered statistical arbitrage (aka pairs trading). In statistical arbitrage, different assets are combined to form a “spread” that characterizes the “mis-pricing” of the assets. This spread is stationary and, hence, mean-reverting, which can be employed for trading purposes by buying the spread when it is low (i.e., underpriced) and by short-selling when it is high (i.e., overpriced). We considered a mathematical formulation for the construction of spreads based on the concept of cointegration and then proposed the design of portfolios within the cointegration subspace. The output consists of two journal papers and one conference paper. Extra objective 4 focused on the non-Gaussian nature of financial data to account for heavy tails and the missing data phenomenon. Heavy-tailed distributions cannot be ignored in financial applications but their characterization is more complicated. We developed optimization methods to deal with the arising nonconvexities of heavy tails. In addition, we considered the phenomenon of missing values in the price time series, which can undermine the subsequent portfolio design, by proposing imputation techniques to fill in the missing values. The output consists of two journal papers, three conference papers, and two software packages (https://cran.r-project.org/package=fitHeavyTail, https://cran.r-project.org/package=imputeFin). Extra objective 5 explored the topic of graph learning with applications in many areas such as financial markets, brain activity monitoring, social networks, etc. We developed efficient and provable convergent algorithms for the estimation of such graph connectivity. The output consists of a journal paper and a software package (https://cran.r-project.org/package=spectralGraphTopology).

16208917.label: Major findings and research outcome
16208917.value: The major outcomes of this project were the formulation of a wide variety of portfolio designs (namely, index tracking portfolio, asset-option Kelly portfolio, risk parity portfolio, quintile portfolio, and high-order portfolio) and the development of practical algorithms to solve the optimization problems formulated. We went the extra mile in further implementing the developed algorithms in the papers into open-source software packages that the community can easily use. In addition to the outcome corresponding to the three proposed objectives, we further considered related topics such as heavy-tailed data modeling, imputation of missing data values, and graph learning methods. The publication output consists of one monograph book, 11 IEEE top journal papers, 8 conference papers. In addition, we developed 6 open-source software packages under the programming language R (commonly used in statistics, machine learning, and finance) (see https://www.danielppalomar.com/software.html for details).

16208917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16208917.value: During this project we obtained many results, more than expected. Nevertheless, this only opened the door to many other future problems. Two main directions are foreseen for the future of our research group: i) improved graph estimation methods in the context of sparse contexts and financial markets, and ii) further developing the non-Gaussian modeling of data.

16208917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16208917.value: Portfolio design in finance bears a great similarity with beamforming or filter design in signal processing and communication systems. We have capitalized on such parallelism to advance the mathematical formulation of a great variety of portfolios (namely, index tracking portfolio, asset-option Kelly portfolio, risk parity portfolio, quintile portfolio, and high-order portfolio) and, most importantly, to develop fast and efficient algorithms to solve such portfolio designs with provable convergence. In addition, we have started the exploration of two topics: the modeling of data as non-Gaussian (typically the Gaussian assumption is made to simplify analysis but it is far from true in financial applications) and the estimation of financial graphs to make evident the relationships between pairs of assets. Not only papers have been written but also practical software has been produced in the open-source community with a superb acceptance in terms of downloads.

16209617.value: 用於液流電池的高能量密度懸浮電解液流變及傳輸特性研究

16209617.label: Project Objectives
16209617.value: Form suspension fluids by synthesizing active materials of different particle sizes and shapes to investigate the effects of particle size and shape on the flow and electrical resistance. Synthesize different electrical conductive additives, including 1D nanotubes, 2D graphene and 3D networks, to characterize the effects of additive structures on the conductivity and viscosity of suspension fluids. Perform nanoscale modeling and simulation to understand and provide insight into the rheological and electrically conductive behavior of suspension fluids. Design microfluidic electrode structures with minimum flow and electrical resistance. Design and fabricate a single lithium-sulfur flow cell to test the suspension fluids and microfluidic electrodes developed in the above tasks at various operating conditions to achieve an optimized single flow cell. Demonstrate a proof-of-concept lithium-sulfur flow battery pack with a capacity of 350 Wh/L or above.

16209617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16209617.value: 液流電池實現了在不同組件上分別進行能量存儲和電力輸出，不僅能革新可再生能源存儲模式，還有望作為下一代電動車的動力電源。然而，當前的液流電池技術受限於其電解液較低的能量密度，造成系統龐大，極大程度上阻礙了其實際應用。針對這一現狀，本項目提出了一種基於納米顆粒懸浮液的新型的液流電池體系。與傳統液流系統將電能儲存於溶解態的金屬鹽中不同，該系統可將電能儲存在懸浮於電解液中的具有電化學活性的納米顆粒中。由於突破了溶解度的限制，懸浮液液流電池有望能將液流電池的能量密度提升10倍以上。但是，該類液流電池發展瓶頸在於與懸浮液粘度相關聯的較大的流動阻力並伴隨著嚴重的泵功損耗，限制了系統的輸出功率密度以及能量效率。因此，本研究的主要內容為：1）借助先進的微納尺度模擬技術探究懸浮液的流變學、電學以及電化學行為特性；2）將傳統微米級懸浮液顆粒尺寸縮減至亞百納米，以實現懸浮液粘度的大幅降低；3）使用一維碳纖維或二維石墨烯替代傳統球型碳材料作為導電劑從而強化電荷傳遞過程，尤其在固態物質分數較低的情況下；4）構思和構築新型微流體電極結構，以達到最低的流動以及電荷傳遞阻力。該項目的完成將為新一代高能量密度、高效、低廉的研究和發展開闢新道路。同時，開發出的鋰硫懸浮液液流電池樣機的能量密度有希望超過350 Wh/L，可達到電動汽車指標要求。該研究所產生的核心技術也能有助於解決當今能源問題，香港乃至全球均可從中直接獲利。

16209617.label: Realisation of objectives
16209617.value: To address the issue of the incompatibility and the inferior interfacial contact between solid-state electrolytes and electrodes in lithium-sulfur batteries, we introduced the PEGDA/Pyr13TFSI ionogel into the interfaces between a NASICON-type Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) solid electrolyte and the electrodes via a simple drop-coating and in situ polymerization method. It is demonstrated that the formed robust and elastic ionogel interlayers not only preclude the adverse reactions between the LATP pellet and the Li metal anode but also significantly reduce the interfacial resistance. As a result, the cycling life of the Li/Li symmetric cell with the ionogel interlayers reaches up to 300 h, whereas the cell using the bare LATP dies after only 10 h. More notably, the Li/ionogel/LATP/ionogel/LiFePO4 full battery delivered a high capacity of 152.5 mAh g–1 at 0.5 C at 60 °C with retention of 91.5% after 200 cycles, in sharp contrast to the value of as low as 46 mAh g–1 even at 0.1 C given by the Li/ionogel/LATP/LiFePO4 cell. These encouraging results demonstrated that the interfacial modification strategy proposed in this work is effective in constructing stable, compact, and durable interfaces between solid electrolytes and electrodes, thereby paving the way for high-performance solid-state lithium metal-based batteries. The rechargeability of the lithium anode in lithium-sulfur (Li–S) batteries remained an issue for this type of battery. In this work, we demonstrated a Li–S full battery comprising a protected anode scaffold and a Li2S cathode. The stabilized performance was attained by an on-site fluorination strategy, using BiF3 for the interfacial coating of the anode. Unlike previously reported LiF protective coating derived from the vapor/solution depositions, BiF3 nanocrystals would be lithiated on-site to the anode surface and serve as the protective layer. The chemically inertial Li3Bi alloy can provide additional ion-conductive paths and stitch the LiF to form a seamless protective layer, thereby suppressing the dendrite propagation and parasitic reactions effectively. With the designed anode structures and compositions, the high-loading full battery (8.05 mg cm–2) can achieve an exceptional utilization of both sulfur (898 mAh gS–1) and lithium (1533 mAh gLi–1) over 200 cycles, marking a step toward cyclable Li metal batteries at a high capacity. We have developed an in-situ encapsulation strategy for sulfur/carbon (S/C) composite cathode to insulate the dissolve polysulfide intermediates from the reaction anode. However, there exists a trade-off between preventing polysulfide dissolution and facilitating the sulfur redox reactions. We employed antimony trifluoride as a bi-functional pre-coating layer on the S/C composite surface. During the in-situ encapsulation process, the liquid electrolyte can wet the S/C composite; while being catalyzed by antimony trifluoride, the liquid electrolyte can polymerize to form a dense lithium-ion-conducting solid polymer electrolyte (SPE) layer on the S/C composite surface. Additionally, antimony trifluoride proves to have strong anchoring effects on polysulfides, which works together with the SPE layer to suppress polysulfide dissolution. The in-situ encapsulated cathode enhanced the cyclability with a minor sacrifice in the rate capability. It is further demonstrated that the cathode can be directly paired with a non-protected lithiated silicon anode to achieve a practical capacity retention rate of 87% for 200 cycles. Since the lithiated silicon anode can offer a higher theoretical energy density and lower cost, however, this type of battery using conventional ether electrolytes suffers from a short lifespan, resulting from poor anode stability and severe polysulfide shuttle effect. To tackle the challenges and also to further investigate the feasibility of the lithiated silicon anode, we reported a fluorinated ether electrolyte to boost the performance of lithiated Si-S batteries. The newly developed electrolyte not only enabled the formation of robust solid-electrolyte interphase on the Si surface, which effectively accommodates the volume variation, thus stabilizing the Si anode, but also lead to quasi-solid-state conversion of S species, thereby considerably mitigating the polysulfide shuttle effect. As a result, a Si-S full battery using the fluorinated electrolyte was able to deliver a high initial capacity of 902 mAh g-1 and maintain capacity retention of 64.0% after 100 cycles. By contrast, the capacity of the cell using conventional ether electrolyte rapidly decays to 162 mAh g-1, which was only 17.5% of its original value. More impressively, for the first time, we demonstrated that the full cell can operate stably with a high cathode loading (6.2 mg cm-2) and lean electrolyte (< 10 μL mg-1), showing great potential for achieving high-performance and high-energy batteries. To investigate the rheology of nanofluid and the effect of particle size and particle content, we have also presented a three-dimensional lattice Boltzmann simulation of dilute suspensions containing porous particles. The fluid flow around and inside a porous particle was described by the volume-averaged macroscopic equations in terms of intrinsic phase average. The energy dissipation of the suspended particle in a Couette flow was calculated to obtain the relative viscosity of the suspension. Results showed that the relative viscosity of the suspension increases linearly with the particle volume fraction. A correlation equation was obtained for the intrinsic viscosity as a function of Darcy number. It was found that when the suspension is at the inertial flow regime, its intrinsic viscosity increases linearly with Reynolds number, and the increasing rate depends on Darcy number. This work has provided theoretical instructions on further experimental investigations on the nanofluid flow batteries. Finally, we have demonstrated an energy-dense, flowable electroactive material by suspending solid sulfur hosted in hollow carbon nanoshells (HCSs) in a liquid electrolyte without extra conductive additives for the pursuit of high-energy-density semi-solid flow batteries. Compared to conventionally used Ketjen Black (KB) additives, the conductive HCSs can confine the insulating active materials within their void space, while maintaining the electroactivity of the outer surface. More importantly, the liquid suspension of well-dispersed HCS/S nanoparticles shows much lower viscosity than that formed by aggregated KB particles with a hyperbranched structure. The cell with the liquid suspension paired with Li metal achieves an average volumetric capacity of ~80 Ah L−1 over 50 stable cycles in the static test and an energy density of 230 Wh L−1 in the intermittent flow test. Our energy-dense HCS/S suspension with high flowability shows great potential for high-energy-density energy storage systems.

16209617.value: To address the issue of the incompatibility and the inferior interfacial contact between solid-state electrolytes and electrodes, a simple drop-coating and in situ polymerization method was developed to form robust and elastic ionogel interlayers. To tackle the challenge of the rechargeability of the lithium anode, we demonstrated a Li–S full battery comprising a protected anode scaffold and a Li2S cathode. The newly developed electrolyte not only enabled the formation of robust solid-electrolyte interphase on the Si surface, which effectively accommodates the volume variation, thus stabilizing the Si anode, but also lead to the quasi-solid-state conversion of S species, thereby considerably mitigating the polysulfide shuttle effect. To investigate the rheology of nanofluid and the effect of particle size and particle content, we have conducted a three-dimensional lattice Boltzmann simulation. Results showed that the relative viscosity of the suspension increases linearly with the particle volume fraction. This work has provided theoretical instructions on further experimental investigations on nanofluid flow batteries. Finally, we successfully demonstrated a high-energy-density semi-solid lithium-sulfur flow battery by suspending solid sulfur hosted in hollow carbon nanoshells (HCSs) in a liquid electrolyte without extra conductive additives. 16209617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16209617.value: The volumetric capacity of the as-prepared liquid suspension paired with Li metal has now reached more than 80 Ah L-1. However, currently the capacity is limited by the anode side. We will develop suspension anodic electrolytes based on carbon-coated silicon nanoparticles with a high energy density. We will apply the surface-modified silicon nanoparticles as the precursor and coated the modified silicon with a layer of metal-organic frameworks. The all-suspension li-sulfur flow battery could reach a higher energy density of 84Wh L-1. Future work will be focused on improving the practical energy density and flowability by further optimizing the composition of the suspension and cell designs.

16209617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16209617.value: During the project period, we have firstly investigated two different li-sulfur batteries with two types of anodes, including the lithium metal anode and the lithiated silicon anode. To tackle the critical challenges that existed in the batteries, such as the dissolved polysulfide intermediates from the reaction anode, and the volume expansion in the silicon anode, we have developed several strategies from both the material and structure perspectives. Then we have conducted a three-dimensional lattice Boltzmann simulation to investigate the rheology of nanofluid and the effect of particle size and particle content. Finally, we successfully demonstrated a high-energy-density semi-solid lithium-sulfur flow battery by suspending solid sulfur hosted in hollow carbon nanoshells (HCSs) in a liquid electrolyte without extra conductive additives.

16209717.value: 泥石流是在山區發生，具破壞性的災害，通常由強降雨引發。泥石流發生時會裹挾大石高速滑下山坡，造成建築物的毀壞以及人命傷亡。全世界每年會有數以千計的人被泥石流奪去生命。在香港，日本，台灣等人口稠密地區，由於人類發展越來越趨近天然山坡，而氣候變化引起的頻繁極端降雨亦逐漸增多，泥石流的風險日益增加。 為了降低泥石流風險，工程師通常會沿著泥石流預測發生的地區安裝擋柱。陣列式的剛性擋柱能夠消散泥石流的能量。在陡峭的山坡上建造擋柱有很多好處，例如它們易於建造，並且比起鋼筋混凝土擋牆，更易融入自然環境。 由於人們對於泥石流與擋柱之間的相互作用機理缺乏根本的認識，工程上的泥石流擋柱設計大多基於經驗。依靠經驗設計的擋柱可能無法有效地消散泥石流的能量，從而無法保護受影響的建築物與基礎設施。同時，依靠經驗的設計有機會忽略擋柱之間的可能的巨石，堵塞的巨石會令泥石流溢過陣列的擋柱，並毫無阻礙地沖向下游。因此，我們有必要進行深入研究，更好地瞭解泥石流與擋柱之間的相互作用機理。 此項目將通過三部分來研究泥石流與擋柱之間相互作用的基本機理：（一）使用5米長的小型物理模型實驗，（二）使用基於有限單元法的數值模擬，（三）反演分析在韓國金布進行的全世界最大規模的物理模型實驗中得到，尚未發表的數據。該實驗通過釋放500立方米泥石流來衝擊下游陣列式的擋柱。小型物理模型實驗為本研究的主要內容。小型物理實驗的好處是能夠透過良好的儀器設備進行一系列可重複的實驗結果來研究擋柱系統，流動時能量消散和堵塞的影響。然後，由小型物理模型實驗得到的可靠數據將被用來標定數值模型，研究在小型物理模型實驗中不易發現的能量消散和內部流動應力變化過程。最後，分析韓國金布世界最大規模的泥石流實地數據，來驗證和評估小型物理模型實驗及數值模型。 該項目的開展及研究發現將促進當前對泥石流與擋柱結構之間相互作用機理的根本認識，有助提供科學性建議，對評估並推廣現有在世界不同的泥石流減災領域中擋柱系統的應用，具有重大意義。

16209717.label: Major findings and research outcome
16209717.value: Baffle arrays can be used to dissipate the flow kinetic energy and to filter boulders entrained in the flow. Both of these features will reduce the impact load exerted on barriers installed further downstream. However, current design guidelines provide limited recommendations on baffle design. In this study, a calibrated discrete element method model based on flume experiments was used to model boulders entrained in a bulk granular assembly interacting with baffles and a terminal rigid barrier. Different baffle spacings relative to the boulder diameter (1 < s/δ < 4) were examined. A relative spacing ratio of s/δ = 1 is recommended for reducing the impact load on downstream barriers by up to 80%, whilst a spacing ratio of s/δ = 4 renders an array of baffles inadequate for filtration of large boulders. The optimum configuration is a staggered array with three rows of baffles on a horizontal plane just upstream of a rigid barrier. This proposed layout reduces the peak discharge by up to four times more compared to the same array on sloping terrain, compared to channels without baffles. Also, the transition from a sloping terrain to a horizontal plane works in concert with the array of baffles to dissipate flow kinetic energy. On the horizontal plane, baffles attenuate the flow velocity more as the Froude number (Fr) increases. This implies that baffles should be used if high Fr values are anticipated. Finally, design guidance is provided on estimating load attenuation from boulder filtration.

16209717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16209717.value: During the course of this research, it was assumed that the baffles were completely rigid. This implies that the foundation of each baffle was not modelled. The loads induced on each baffle is high, thus research on the design of foundations for each baffle is warranted, especially if they are to resist concentrated dynamic impact from large boulders. The challenge in designing foundations for baffles is making them constructible on steep natural terrain and resists rotation and sliding. Also, the effects of channel bed entrainment and debris deposition was not considered. Instead, smooth immobile channel beds were modelled. Through this research, it was assessed that baffles play an essential role in trapping debris, which will minimize the effects of entrainment downstream. Only channeled conditions were modelled in this study, unchanneled conditions that enable flow spreading would be a more direct comparison to basins that are unchanneled. Unchanneled conditions would enable lateral flow spreading and dissipate more energy compared to channel conditions, which implies that baffles may be more effective than that concluded in this study.

16209717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16209717.value: Baffles are a form of engineered solution against landslide hazards. More specifically, baffles are an array of rigid obstacles installed along the predicted flow paths of a type of landslide called debris flow, which are mixtures of soil and water that surge downslope at high velocities. Baffles are supposed to attenuate the flow kinetic energy and trap large boulders. Baffles are ideal because they are compact in design and easy to install on steep natural terrain. However, there is very limited guidance for engineers and scientists to design baffles. This research project systematically investigated the key factors that govern the ability of an array of baffles to attenuate flow kinetic energy and to trap large boulders. As a result of this project, the optimum configuration of baffles in terms of spacing between baffles, spacing between rows of baffles, the height of baffles, and their position relative to downstream protection measures was proposed. Findings from this study can be used as guiding tools for practitioners to rationalize existing design standards. The scientific recommendations from this study help to strengthen the foundation for resilience and preparedness for mountainous communities around the world.

16209817.value: 许多重要的工程结构，如航空航天和精密科学仪器，将常常在大 幅度温度变化的环境中运行，此时对于这些结构和仪器的尺寸变 化将有严格的限制，必须使用具有很小的甚至负的热膨胀系数的 材料。材料的热膨胀性能的控制一直是科学家和材料工程师所面临 的挑战性的课题，已逐渐成为材料研究的一个专门的领域。每年 都不断有新的热膨胀性能的材料在文献中发表。 近年来国际学术界兴起采用两种方法来研制具有可控热膨胀性能 的形状记忆合金材料。一是采用化学成分调控，另一种是采用微 结构控制而不改变成份的方法。采用两种方法的研究均具有很强的挑战性。 本项目的前期预研表明，采取第二种方法，利用马氏体热膨胀 系数的强各向异性、控制材料纳米化后奥氏体和马氏体的体积分 数和织构、抑制变温下的相变过程，有望沿镍钛记忆合金薄板的 不同方向获取材料的正的、负的和几乎零膨胀的性能。 本研究项目将通过材料的微结构设计、材料冷轧和热处理的微结 构工艺控制以及微纳米尺度的高分辩表征和性能测试，来研发具 有负热膨胀和零热膨胀性能的镍钛记忆合金。本研究将镍钛纳米 多晶体材料的新型相变超弹性性能与独特的热膨胀性能相结合， 研究工作不仅具有重要的学术价值，同时也将大大拓宽该智能材 料的应用范围。

16209817.label: Realisation of objectives
16209817.value: Achieving low thermal expansion (TE) property (known as Invar effect) of polycrystalline NiTi shape memory alloys (SMAs) via microstructure control will add a new functionality to this important and widely used material. The existing practice to tailor the coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) of bulk SMAs mainly relies on trial-and-error experiment. In this project, we overcome many difficulties in design and fabrication and performed a modelling-and-experiment combined study to design and tune the CTE of bulk NiTi SMAs based on compensation and reorientation deformation mechanisms. We have fully achieved the project objectives. To achieve the objectives 1 and 2, we have successfully fabricated superelastic nanostructured NiTi plates by differently controlled rolling and annealing. The key effects of rolling texture, thickness reduction, grain size and annealing on the macroscopic CTE behavior of the material are revealed. Systematic first hand experimental data of the Coefficient of Thermal Expansion (CTE) of nanostructured NiTi are obtained and the underlying microstructure hierarchy are identified. We achieved in-plane low TE of NiTi sheets via controlled cross rolling. The in-plane coefficients of TE (CTEs) of the sheets are within a narrow range near zero (-2.7×10-6 K-1 ~ +3.0×10-6 K-1) and are smaller than those of the commercial Invar materials such as FeNi alloys. It is found that the intrinsic positive TE of B2 crystal and B19’ aggregate and the negative TE induced by the reversible B2↔B19’ phase transformation compensates each other over the temperature span from 70 K to 300 K on cooling/heating, yielding the overall in-plane low TE. To achieve the objective 3, we have development of mechanism-based models to quantify the contributions of the intrinsic lattice level TE of B19' and the extrinsic meso-level microstructures to the overall macroscopic CTE nanostructured NiTi. First, in using the cold-rolling and annealing approach, a Voigt-based theoretical model predicts that the proposed compensation mechanism can be used to achieve in-plane low TE of SMAs. The work provide a new modelling approach in fabrication and design of Invar-type SMAs for commercial applications. Second, in using reorientation mechanism and Landau theory of first-order phase transition, we proved that the martensite lattices of most SMAs possess intrinsic negative (positive) CTE along the directions of transformation elongation (contraction), and that the overall CTE of martensitic polycrystals decreases (increases) along the axial direction during martensite reorientation under uniaxial tension (compression). For 17 types of SMAs, macroscopic zero CTE via controlled reorientation deformation is predicted and supported by available experiment. Based on the modelling work, designed cross-rolling on polycrystalline martensitic NiTi sheets is performed and we successfully obtained in-plane near-zero CTEs (+0.13×10-6 K-1 ~ +1.4×10-6 K-1), which are smaller than those of the reported SMAs and even the commercial FeNi Invar alloy (+2.0×10-6 K-1). Our research outcome in realizing these objectives are published as 3 papers in top journals of metallic materials and solid mechanics (2 papers in Acta Materialia and 1 paper in J. Mech. Phys. Solids).

16209917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16209917.value: Strain sensors with good transparency, broad sensing range, and high sensitivity are highly desirable for use in many areas including electronics skins, human motion sensors, artificial muscle, and stretchable electronics. Unfortunately, conventional brittle strain sensors made of metals or semiconductors are not suitable for these new applications because of their low sensitivity and narrow sensing range. Due to graphene’s outstanding electrical and mechanical properties, graphene-based strain sensors show the advantages of flexibility and transparency. However, because of the fixed connection between graphene sheets, the produced strain sensors usually exhibit low sensitivity at low strain or relatively narrow sensing range. Recently, inspired by the sensory system of spiders, new types of crack-based strain sensors were fabricated. These sensors possess a high sensitivity owing to the reversible disconnection and reconnection. However, the stretchability of crack-based strain sensors is limited due to complete disconnection at large strain, which restricts its application in detecting the full range of human motions. To circumvent this issue, one promising approach is to combine low dimensional nanomaterials into hybrid nanostructures to achieve enhanced sensing properties. The PI and collaborators have recently developed a cracked graphene-based transparent strain sensor for detecting tiny skin deformation. The sensor showed extremely high sensitivity. In this proposed project, we would like to further study the application of low dimensional hybrid carbon materials for strain sensing by combining cracked graphene with a layer of atomically aligned thin single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWNTs) to make the detection capability superior to that of either graphene or SWNTs. Aligned SWNTs can bridge between buckled graphene ribbons, so an integrated hybrid strain sensor would possess both high sensitivity at small strain from the cracked graphene and good stretchability due to the bridging effect. Molecular dynamics simulations will be performed to fundamentally understand how the chemical functionalization, degree of buckling, and crack width affect the self-assembly process and interfacial bonding characteristics, which may play a major role in achieving both high sensitivity and stretchability. In summary, the proposed research aims at developing a novel transparent, ultra-sensitive, and stretchable strain sensor based on a cracked graphene/aligned SWNT hybrid structure to capture a wide range of human physical movements. 具有良好透明度，大範圍感應區和高靈敏度的應變傳感器在許多領域具有廣泛的應用，包括電子皮膚，人體運動傳感器，人造肌肉和可拉伸電子設備等。但是，傳統的金屬或半導體基脆性應變傳感器由於其靈敏度低和檢測範圍較窄而不適合這些新應用。石墨烯卓越的電學和機械性能使其具有柔韌和透明的優點。然而，由於石墨烯片之間的固定連接，目前所生產的石墨烯基應變傳感器通常在低應變區域內工作，並且靈敏度較低。受到蜘蛛感應系統的啟發，科學家們最近研制了新型的基於裂紋的應變傳感器，由於其可逆的斷開和重新連接，這些傳感器具有高靈敏度和較長的使用壽命。然而，由於裂紋在大應變下的完全斷開，基於裂紋的應變傳感器的可拉伸性受到限制，制約了其在具有較大應變的人體運動檢測領域中的應用。為了解決這個問題，一個有效的方法是將不同維度的納米材料結合在一起來獲得增強的感應性能。本課題組最近開發了一種用於檢測微小皮膚變形的含裂紋石墨烯透明應變傳感器，該傳感器顯示出極高的靈敏度。本項目擬通過將含裂紋石墨烯與單層碳納米管陣列相結合，進一步研究低維雜化碳材料在應變檢測領域中的應用，使其檢測能力同時優於石墨烯或單壁碳納米管。單層碳納米管陣列可以橋接褶皺的石墨烯條帶，這種集成的混合應變傳感器不但由於裂紋的存在而在小應變下具有高靈敏度，並且由於橋接效應而具有良好的可拉伸性。為從根本上了解化學官團，褶皺度和裂紋寬度如何影響自組裝過程和界面粘合特性，本項目將進行進一步的分子動力學模擬來研究這些因素在實現高靈敏度和可拉伸性方面所起的作用。總之，本研究旨在開發一種具有含裂紋石墨烯/單層碳納米管陣列復合結構的新型透明，超靈敏和可拉伸應變傳感器，以檢測各種尺度的人體運動。

16209917.label: Realisation of objectives
16209917.value: Significant and exceptional progress has been made, producing many original and interesting results that are published in high-impact journals. The major outcomes from the project are discussed in the following. (1) Objective 1 The basic technology of fabrication of graphene oxide via modified Hummers method using natural graphite and graphene via reduction of graphene oxide is first developed successfully. (J01, J02) Cracked graphene with periodic buckling patterns is then produced by applying a prestrain-release-buckling strategy. First, a highly stretchable silicone rubber substrate (Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS)) is uniaxially stretched to a large strain. Graphene film are then deposited through vacuum filtration and transfer printing. To obtain good adhesion and a uniform film, the silicone rubber substrates are treated with a silane coupling agent ((3- aminopropyl) triethoxysilane). Upon releasing the substrate’s pre-strain, delaminated buckling with periodic cracks are formed due to the uniaxial compression. The formation of periodic cracks is mainly due to the Poisson’s ratio effect, which generates transverse tensile stress in response to the uniaxial compression of the substrate. The transverse tension cracks the graphene film. Several variables that can affect the degree of buckling and the spacing of the periodic cracks including the reduction degree, size of graphene, the pre-strain, and the interfacial bonding are systematically investigated. (J05, J08) (2) Objective 2 Carboxyl-functionalized SWNTs is a crucial part of this study for the successful deposition of aligned arrays SWNT layers based on L–B assembly. In order to obtain amphiphilic SWNTs without harmful additives, SWNTs are partially oxidized by a mixture of sulfuric acid and nitric acid to activate the surface with oxygen functionalities. Carboxylic moieties are introduced non-uniformly along the SWNT length, making them amphiphilic and ready for the L–B assembly. The functionalized SWNTs are dispersed in water/methanol solution before spreading, which remained stable for months at room temperature. To produce cracked graphene/aligned SWNT hybrid films with uniform coverage, SWNTs are transferred on top of cracked graphene films by sequential, layer-by-layer deposition via the L-B technique with controlled density and degree of alignment by varying the surface pressure and the pulling speed of the substrate. (J04, J05, J08, J09) (3) Objective 3 Since aligned CNT can bridge between the buckled graphene ribbons, the integrated hybrid strain sensor possesses both high sensitivity at a small strain from the cracked graphene and good stretchability due to the bridging effect. The hybrid strain sensor not only maintains high sensitivity with a gauge factor greater than 100, but also performs greatly improved stretchability over 50%, making it capable of capturing a wide range of human physical movements. By seamlessly interconnecting the composite sensors, a Bluetooth module and an external device like a smartphone, a fully integrated wearable human motion monitoring system is developed. (J01, J04) Multidirectional strain sensors with an exceptionally high selectivity are fabricated using anisotropic CNF films. (J03) The single-layer aligned ACNF strain sensors exhibited anisotropic electromechanical behaviors, showing largely different GFs for the tensile strains applied parallel and perpendicular to fiber alignment, respectively. Cross-plied ACNF strain sensors consisting of two layers of ACNF films staked orthogonally were prepared to distinguish various complex bodily motions. The novel applications of the both single-layer and cross-plied ACNF strain sensors have been successfully demonstrated, including the facile control of LEDs and the distinction of multi-degrees-of-freedom synovial joint movements of human body. A high-sensitivity, flexible temperature sensor is designed using ACNF films by means of establishing the correlation between the atomic structure and its sensing performance. (J06) These sensors present a high measurement accuracy comparable to commercial thermometers, a good linearity, a quick response time of 1.2 s and excellent durability. They are only responsive to temperature variation amidst other external stimuli, such as pressure, bending and humidity, and maintained its exceptional sensing capability and insensitiveness to those unwanted stimuli even after repeated stretching cycles thanks to the highly aligned CNFs. CNFs at both the atomic and device levels is also designed towards all resistive-type multifunctional sensors capable of simultaneously detecting and distinguishing temperature and pressure without signal crosstalk. (J07) Notably, such stimulus discriminability was achieved by using only one type of output signal, namely the electrical resistance, which is the most convenient digital signal to track and process among others for device applications. An ultrasensitive, highly selective multidirectional sensor is developed by rational design of functionally different anisotropic layers. (J08) The bilayer sensor consists of an aligned carbon nanotube (CNT) array assembled on top of a periodically wrinkled and cracked CNT–graphene oxide film. The transversely aligned CNT layer bridges the underlying longitudinal microcracks to effectively discourage their propagation even when highly stretched, leading to superior sensitivity with a gauge factor of 287.6 across a broad linear working range of up to 100% strain. The wrinkles generated through a pre-straining/releasing routine in the direction transverse to CNT alignment is responsible for exceptional selectivity of 6.3, to the benefit of accurate detection of loading directions by the multidirectional sensor. Inspired by lotus roots whose fibers remain joined even after fracture, highly sensitive and stretchable strain sensors are designed using single-walled carbon nanotube (SWNT)/graphene oxide hybrid thin films with unique wrinkled and cracked morphologies. (J09) The distinctive wrinkled and cracked structure is created by tuning the pre-stretching releasing of the hybrid film on a silicone rubber substrate. Under tension, the myriad SWNTs connect the wrinkled film by sliding within the hybrid film giving rise to high stretchability, while the nano/microscale cracks provide the strain sensor with a high sensitivity through tunneling of adjacent cracks.

16209917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16209917.value: To further exploit the potentials of SWCT/cracked graphene hybrids and CNFs as the active materials for soft multifunctional sensors, several works are suggested in the future. Even though PAN is the most popular precursor to produce CNFs via electrospinning and SWCTs can be mass produced, they are relatively expensive compared to other precursor materials and requires the usage of organic solvents. Therefore, systematic studies on other precursor materials are necessary, such as lignin which is much more cost-effective than SWCTs or PAN. It is also safer to produce CNFs using PVA because water can be used as the solvent for PVA instead of hazardous organic solvents. It is also possible to in-situ incorporate different metal or metal oxide nanoparticles into CNFs. It would be interesting to probe the suitability of metal- or metal oxide-incorporated CNFs in serving as active materials for soft strain, temperature, and pressure sensors. For instance, nickel oxide possesses superior thermoresistive characteristic and the CNFs containing nickel oxides may be extremely sensitive to temperature. It is highly possible that metal or metal oxide nanoparticles and CNFs would have synergistic effects in enhancing the sensing performances of soft multifunctional sensors.

16209917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16209917.value: This project aims to develop a novel transparent, ultrasensitive, and wide range strain sensor based on a cracked graphene/aligned SWNT hybrid structures to capture wide-range physical movements. Inspired by recent work about cracked graphene films on an elastomeric substrate for highly flexible, transparent, and sensitive strain sensors, we developed a cracked graphene/aligned single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWNTs) hybrid structures to capture wide-range physical movements. Benefiting from the unique microstructure design, synthesis and transfer of graphene, controllable self-assembly of surfactant-free SWNTs, as well as solution-processability at room temperature, the final all-carbon devices exhibit great potential for use in strain sensing applications requiring large working range, high sensitivity, good optical transparency, and superior substrate flexibility. The current study on cracked graphene/aligned SWNTs hybrid thin films and highly aligned CNFs for strain sensing will not only represent a significant step towards facile and scalable fabrication of high performance and cost-efficient fabrication of high-performance strain sensing devices using all-carbon nanostructures, but also have a long-term impact on the fundamental understanding of the interactions between different carbon nanomaterials. The stretchable sensors can also provide potential functions for many emerging applications such as entertainment technology, robotics, and biomedicine.

16210017.label: Realisation of objectives
16210017.value: All three objectives proposed in the project has been fully achieved. (1) We have successfully developed a novel three-dimensional hierarchical multiscale framework for high-porosity granular rocks. The DEM model features a bonded contact model to account for the cenmentation in high-porosity sandstone, which enable us to reproduce the debonding and pore collapse mechanisms observed in experiments. The multiscale framework has been based on an early platform of coupled FEM-DEM developed in the PI’s lab. The new 3D hierarchical multiscale framework offers a powerful preditive capability for us to bridge grain-scale attributes and their mechanics and physics with the macroscopic material response in sandstone under either dry or saturated conditions and subjected to different loading/boundary conditions. (2) The developed multiscale framework has further been validated against the X-ray tomography observations of a high-porosity limestone (Tuffeau de Maastricht). The validation was carried out by a Ph.D. student (Dr. Huanran Wu) who paid a 3-month visit to 3SR Laboratory of Grenoble to work with Co-investigator Prof. Cino Viggiani. Over his visit, Huanran worked with Prof Viggiani and his group to corroborate their X-ray experimental observations on Tuffeau de Maastricht, a high-porosity limestone, with our multiscale modeling for rigorous calibration and validation. The multiscale predictions based on the calibrated DEM model captured well the initiation and propagation of the compaction band in the limestone. (3) With the aid of the multiscale framework, we have also identified the underlying microstructural mechanism associated with the strain localization in various loading conditions. Other key factors affecting the behavior and response of granular material, including particle morphology, grain crushing, and large deformation scenario, have also been systematically examined through multiscale modeling. Overall, the project team is happy and proud with what have been achieved from the project and appreciates the support of RGC through this project to make this research possible.

16210017.label: Major findings and research outcome
16210017.value: The major research findings from the project are summarized as follows (numbers referred in end of line brackets indicate research output in Part C, e.g., 8.1 means Item 1 in Section 8 of Part C): (1) An innovative three-dimensional multiscale framework (FEM/DEM) has been developed for high-porosity granular rocks which helps to establish a direct micro-macro link between microscopic characteristics of bonded granular media with the macroscopic observations of these materials, such as strain localization (see 8.1, 9.2, 9.3, 9.10) (2) The developed computational framework has been benchmarked and validated with the high-fidelity X-ray tomography observations on a high-porosity limestone (Tuffeau de Maastricht) and has revealed that debonding, the collapse of macropores and grain rearrangements are the major microstructural mechanisms causing the formation of compaction bands (8.9). (3) The multiscale framework has been extended to a multi-physics regime, allowing simulations of hydro-mechanical problems in saturated media (8.8, 9.4, 9.5). (4) The developed computational framework has been deployed to investigate diverse boundary value problems and has reproduced various types of deformation bands as well as their transition in high-porosity sandstone (8.10, 8.11). (5) To tackle large deformation problem, the multiscale framework has been further extended based on coupled MPM and DEM wherein Material Point Method (MPM) is employed to model macroscopic behavior and DEM for particle-scale simulations (8.3, 8.4, 9.1, 9.6, 9.9). (6) A novel hybrid approach has been developed for the simulation of particle crushing and the investigation of associated crushing criteria (8.5, 8.7, 9.7, 9.8). (7) In consideration of multiscale features of granular media, a novel continuum model based on mixture theory has been proposed to predict the mechanical response for gap-grades material (8.2, 8.6, 8.11). These research findings have been disseminated in 9 papers published in top journals such as Geotechnique, Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering, and International Journal for Numerical and Analytical Methods in Geomechanics, 2 book chapters and 10 conference papers. A full list can be found in Part C. They have drawn good attention in the community and have been well cited. Over 2018-2021, PI Zhao has been delivered 25 invited keynotes or webinars on the project research in prestigious international conferences and/or institutions and has won two best paper award (Section 11, Part C). Moreover, his Ph.D. student, Huanran Wu, who is mainly funded by this project to work on the proposed research, has won the prestigious 2018 Ringo Yu Prize for Best PhD Thesis in Geotechnical Studies by HKIE (Section 10, Part C).

16210017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16210017.value: Potential further developments of the research may be extended to the following aspects: (1) An implementation of a large-scale parallel scheme that could remarkably boost the multiscale simulation for large-scale practical problems. (2) Incorporation of the thermal field that facilitates the thermal-hydro-mechanical (THM) analysis in geomechanics. (3) The integration of particle morphology and crushing functionalities into the multiscale framework for better reproducing the mechanical behavior of realistic granular material. The above three future developments are indeed promising and may deserve to be developed into a future RGC/GRF project to further enhance the impact of this line of research.

16210017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16210017.value: This project has led to an innovative hierarchical multiscale framework for modeling the behavior of high-porosity sandstone. It enables us to rigorously establish a cross-scale connection between the material property and particle/pore scale physics and mechanics in sandstone with the macroscopic phenomena under different conditions. This computational framework can reproduce compelling results of the compaction band and shows an excellent agreement with the X-ray observations on a French limestone. This framework also enables the modeling of hydro-mechanical behavior of saturated sandstones, helping us to identify the key microstructural mechanisms and physical processes underlying interesting macroscopic deformation bands in high-porosity sandstone in the presence of pore fluid. The multiscale framework derived from this project not only greatly advances our understanding of the strain localization behavior in high-porosity granular rocks, but also leads to an effective analysis software for providing numerical analysis for practical applications such as oil/gas recovery and carbon sequestration. Moreover, this project has led to several useful numerical toolkits for investigating other relevant interesting problems in geomechanics, including large deformation, particle shape, grain crushing, and gap-graded materials. These research outputs (simulation toolkit, scientific finding, and constitutive models) help advance our fundamental understanding of geomaterials of key economic significance and prepare new-generation analytical tools to tackle future related engineering challenges.
