16213317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16213317.value: Genealogy, commonly referred to as “family history”, is the study of the lineage of a family tree from its root ancestor. Typically, a genealogical dataset contains a list for each individual in the family tree, providing information such as the individual’s name, gender, occupation, province, father’s name, mother’s name, spouse’s name, birth date, and death date. In addition, modern genealogists have refined the information available on historical context and economic context. These multifaceted big data, encoding multi-dimensional, temporal-spatial, and hierarchical information, pose special challenges for data analysis. Computational genealogical analysis, or the use of computational methods to solve genealogical problems, is a promising field. As traditional methods reveal only general information, the recent emergence of more granular data and more powerful computational resources has led to new research problems and solutions. One challenge involves the use of information on historical and economic context to identify individuals with the same family name in different historical settings. Other tasks involve investigating the root ancestor of a family in its larger context and comparing multiple families to determine the influence of the root on the growth of the family tree. Solutions to these problems have strong socioeconomic benefits. In recent years, more and more relevant work has been carried out, and both commercial and free genealogical-software packages have been developed and applied in real-life settings. Due to its intuitiveness, visualization has been widely used in these packages. However, existing methods provide only general information on social organization (e.g., occupation) and historical demography (e.g., location), and illustrate only individual aspects of family history. There still lacks a general framework to describe multifaceted genealogical information and support comprehensive analysis. In this project, we will work closely with social scientists to design and implement a novel visual-analytics framework, which supports multifaceted analysis of family history and can address some key issues in computational genealogy such as the correlation between the personal traits of a root ancestor and the growth of the whole family tree. We will apply our framework to analyze the China Multi-Generational Panel Dataset—Liaoning (CMGPD—LN) which comprises more than 1.5 million observations between 1749 and 1909, covering more than 260,000 residents from 698 communities. We will also develop an open-source software system, which allows experts and ordinary users to explore large-scale multivariate temporal-spatial trees. With the collaboration of social scientists, our work has the potential to advance the state-of-the-art of computational genealogy. 通常被稱為“家族史”的家譜是從其根祖先研究家譜的譜系。家譜學家使用口頭訪談、歷史記錄、遺傳分析，和包括從其他來源和其他方法來獲取一個家庭的信息。一個典型的家譜數據集包含家譜中每個人的列表，從而提供包括個人姓名（姓氏，名字），性別，職業，省份，父親姓名，母親姓名，配偶姓名，出生日期，和死亡日期等信息。此外，現代的家譜學家已經針對歷史背景和經濟背景對這些信息進行了修正。這些多方面的大數據包含多維度的、時空的和結構的信息，因此對數據分析構成特殊挑戰。 計算家譜分析，或是使用計算方法來解決家譜問題，是一個有希望的領域。由於傳統方法僅僅揭示一般性的信息，最近出現了更細粒度的數據和更強大的計算資源，導致新的研究問題出現和新的解決方案被提出。一個挑戰是使用關於歷史和經濟背景的信息來識別不同歷史環境中具有相同姓氏的個人。其他任務涉及在較大範圍內調查一個家庭的根祖先，並比較多個家庭，以確定根對家譜成長的影響。解決這些問題可能具有社會經濟效益，對於多民族、多文化的社會尤其如此。香港也是一個多文化的大熔爐，除了土生土長的香港人，還有從中國、印尼、加拿大、新加坡、日本、法國、印度、巴基斯坦和美國等地來的人。例如，普通用戶可能希望更好地了解他們家族在歷史上的地位，以獲得滿足感和自我價值。為了達到上面的任務，需要重新設計可視化家庭樹的方法，並構建視覺分析系統和軟件包來幫助專業人士和專家。當然， 家庭史可視化在講故事的應用中也可以是為非專家設計的。 近年來，越來越多的相關工作已經展開，商業版本和自由軟件包在現實生活中也得到了應用。目前這些可視化家庭樹的方法可以提供一般信息，包括社會組織（例如職業）和歷史人口統計（例如位置）。 然而上述的研究挑戰依然存在，因為現有方法只能說明家族史的某個方面，而不是為綜合分析提供工具。 在本研究中，我們將設計和實施一個視覺分析系統，從而為多方面信息的顯示和分析提供一個總體框架，並為該領域的關鍵研究問題提出解決方案。本項目我們將於社會科學家，歷史學家和人口學家一同協作，令我們的工作有潛力在計算家譜領域佔據領先位置。

16213317.label: Realisation of objectives
16213317.value: We have realised the objectives in the proposal. Q1. To propose a novel multi-generational family tree structure to describe multifaceted genealogical information We have closely worked with the domain experts and identified their requirements for the family tree structure: 1) Organizing the entire collection of family trees by depth; 2) Aggregating family trees by structural features; 3) Presenting the structures of family trees in details. Based on these requirements, we have designed a novel multi-generational family tree structure to describe multifaceted genealogical information called TreeEvo. The details of the tree can be found in our TVCG paper "How Do Ancestral Traits Shape Family Trees Over Generations?" [J1]. O2. To design and implement a novel visual-analytics framework which supports multifaceted analysis of family history We have worked with the domain experts and identified their analysis workflow which consists of four stages: 1) Data Cleaning; 2) Hypothesis Generation; 3) Variable Definition; 4) Data Analysis. Based on this, we have designed and implemented a novel visual analytics framework which supports structure identification and association analysis. It consists of three stages: 1) Summarizing Entire Tree Collection; 2) Displaying Details; 3) Analyzing with MLM. The details of the framework can be found in our TVCG paper "How Do Ancestral Traits Shape Family Trees Over Generations?" [J1]. In addition, some recent work using embedding technology to understand high-dimensional data such as the relationships between families in a community. However, despite the high efficiency and accuracy of learning an embedding model, people have little clue of what information about the original network is preserved in the embedding vectors. It poses special challenges if it is directly applied to the CMGPD-LN data because the results might not be easily understandable. Thus, we developed EmbeddingVis, an exploratory visual analytics system that supports the comparative visual interpretation of embedding vectors at the cluster, instance, and structural levels. To be more specific, it facilitates comparison of what and how node metrics are preserved across different embedding models and investigation of relationships between node metrics and selected embedding vectors. More details can be found in our IEEE VAST 2018 paper "EmbeddingVis: A Visual Analytics Approach to Comparative Network Embedding Inspection" [C1]. O3. To develop novel visualization methods for analyzing the correlation between the personal traits of a root ancestor and the growth of the whole family tree We have designed novel visualization methods which consist of three views: 1) Flow View, 2) a Detail view, and 3) an Analysis view. We especially proposed an enhanced Sankey diagram, which organizes thousands of family trees by growth and continuity, and provides detailed information of each family tree on the Sankey node. Also, it breaks the limit of traditional Sankey diagram, and allows a flexible partition for custom-defined Sankey nodes. More details can be found in our TVCG paper "How Do Ancestral Traits Shape Family Trees Over Generations?" [J1]. O4. To develop an open-source software system for analyzing large-scale multivariate temporal-spatial trees We have developed an open-source software system called TreeEvo for large-scale multivariate temporal-spatial trees and the system can be publicly accessed at https://github.com/fusiwei339/treeEvo. The system has been used by Q.5 To analyze the China Multi-Generational Panel Dataset—Liaoning (CMGPD—LN) data with social scientists and gain new insights into the history of this region We have analyzed the China Multi-Generational Panel Dataset—Liaoning (CMGPD—LN) data with social scientists and some new insights about the history of this region have been obtained. For example, we found that the social status of a founder of a family, measured by whether the founder held a salaried official position, had an influence on the inclination of his family. We found that poor (without official position) families have high probabilities of favoring first-/early-born, while rich (with official position) families care less about it or have more diversity. We found that when the initial family is big and probably rich, they may have different strategies and/or easily diversify growth in later generations while the long-term influence of the birth order preference is stronger when the family is small at the beginning (the founder has no more than four sons). We found that when a male had more than three sons, the probability of his family tree lasting for three or more generations is at least 80%.

16213317.label: Major findings and research outcome
16213317.value: We investigate how to visualize large multi-variate tree structures such as the genealogy documented in the China Multi-Generational Panel Dataset—Liaoning (CMGPD—LN) data which contain 54,128 family trees of 126,196 individuals. We first develop TreeEvo, an interactive visual analytics system that supports analysis of the association between ancestral traits and family tree structures, and then use it to analyze the CMGPD—LN data and gain some insights into the history of this region [J1]. As some recent work using embedding technology to understand high-dimensional data such as the relationships between families in a community, we developed EmbeddingVis, an interactive visual analytics system that helps analysts understand and compare different embedding models [C1]. We use the idea of genealogy to investigate the evolution of deep neural network architectures and develop the DNN Genealogy, an interactive visualization tool, to offer a visual summary of representative DNNs and their evolutionary relationships [J2]. We leverage our knowledge on digital humanities gained from this project and also our collaboration with Prof. Cameron Campbell who provides the genealogy dataset of this project to investigate the CGED-Q (China Government Employee Database-Qing) database which records the career trajectories of over 340,000 government officials in the Qing bureaucracy in China from 1760 to 1912. We developed CareerLens, an interactive visual analytics system for assisting experts in exploring, understanding, and reasoning from historical career data [J3]. We use the tree structure to show the temporal event sequences and develop StageMap, a novel visualization technique to summarize event sequence data into a set of stage progression patterns which can be displayed s with an icicle plot [C2].

16213317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16213317.value: The scope of the project can be further extended. For example, in order to obtain a deeper understanding of the associations between ancestral traits and tree structures, we can include personal traits of family members into the analysis, and also investigate the correlation of the family trees and environmental factors. We can also pursue comparisons across multiple datasets. For example, it would be very beneficial to compare how individual traits of ancestors have influence across generations in different countries, such as China, Japan, and the United States.

16213317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16213317.value: Many real-world problems can be modeled as multi-variate spatio-temporal tree structures. For example, the China Multi-Generational Panel Dataset—Liaoning (CMGPD—LN) data contain 54,128 family trees of 126,196 individuals in Shengjing, currently the northeast Chinese province of Liaoning, between 1749 and 1909. Due to data complexity and lack of efficient tools, most previous studies only focus on the transmission of socio-economic and behavioral traits between parents and children and, only recently, across three generations. In this research, the data visualization researchers team together with social demographers and historians to develop visual analytical tools for analysts to answer questions like “How many family trees grow, or at least continue, at each generation?” “How many kinds of family trees exist in the dataset?” and “How is the tree structure associated with characteristics of the male founders?”. These tools have been integrated into an open-source software system that can be used to visualize similar multi-variate spatio-temporal trees. We have also investigated tree structures in other applications and developed tools like the DNN Genealogy for showing the evolution of deep neural networks, the StageMap for summarizing temporal event sequences, and the CareerLens for exploring the careers of officials and their social networks.

16213417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16213417.value: In supply chain management, the coordination among different stakeholders to maximize the social welfare is one of the key concepts. To achieve this coordination, one business model coming into use is the vendor managed inventory (VMI) system, in which the supplier is responsible for managing the routing decisions and inventory replenishment decisions for various retailers. This combination of inventory management and vehicle routing gives rise to the inventory routing problem (IRP). This project aims to study the basic stochastic IRP when the demand is uncertain, in particular, to make vehicle routing decisions and inventory replenishment decisions jointly and adaptively over a finite discrete time horizon. In order to deliver a tractable model, we plan to make the routing decisions for all periods at the beginning of the first period, while making the ordering decisions at the beginning of each period after observing the demand realizations. We will present a new objective function based on risk measure to account for the risk when the uncertain inventory level at each period violates a pre-specified requirement window, e.g., between maximum backlog and capacity. Furthermore, since the uncertain demand is revealed sequentially as time progresses, the decisions should also be adaptive. We plan to use a decision rule approach, which assumes that the ordering decision is a function of the demand realization over previous periods. In addition, we plan to use a distributionally robust optimization framework to capture the uncertain demands by optimizing the worst-case performance amongst a set of possible distributions that is characterized by certain descriptive statistics. Finally, we plan to formulate the problem by a mixed-integer linear programming problem that can be solved efficiently. Assuming promising results, the model developed can be implemented to solve practical inventory routing problems and also enrich the current literature of the stochastic inventory routing problem. 如何協調不同利益相關方使得總社會收益最大化是供應鏈管理中的關鍵概念之一。要實現這一協調，供應商管理庫存（Vendor Managed Inventory）系統成為一種在供應鏈環境下的新的庫存運作模式。其中供應商負責決定各個零售商的產品的運輸配送和庫存補貨。這種庫存管理與路徑優化相結合，便形成了庫存路徑問題（Inventory Routing Problem）。 該項目旨在研究需求不確定時的隨機庫存路徑問題，尤其是在有限的離散時間範圍內，如何同時制定適應性的配送和庫存決定。我們在第一時段開始時制定對所有時段的路徑規劃決策，同時在每一時段開始時基於真實的需求作出訂貨決策。我們首先會提出一個新的目標函數用於度量缺貨和庫存積壓的風險；其次，為了使得訂貨決策隨著時間動態變化，我們計劃使用決策規則方法假定訂貨決策是需求的固定函數；最後，由於需求的不確定性，我們會使用分佈式魯棒的優化框架。基於以上三個步驟，我們可以將問題建模成為混合整數線性規劃問題，並有效地解決它。 此項目開發的模型既可以解決實際的庫存路徑問題，又可以豐富當前有關隨機 庫存路徑問題的文獻。

16213417.label: Realisation of objectives
16213417.value: 1. To formulate the stochastic inventory routing problem that can account for the risk concerns by proposing a new decision criterion; The first objective is achieved. We have proposed a new performance measure named the Service Violation Index to evaluate the risk of inventory violating the requirement window. We motivate this index from several axioms, including monotonicity, satisficing (attainment content and starvation aversion), convexity and positive homogeneity, dimension-wise additivity and define this index based on the certainty equivalent of the exponential function. This index can capture the risk of delay and idleness and allow us to develop a tractable model. 2. To make robust inventory replenishment and routing decisions that can immune against uncertainty by constructing the distributionally robust framework; The second objective is achieved. We proposed a scenario-based uncertainty set that integrates scenario-tree-based stochastic optimization and distributionally robust optimization into a unified framework. For each period, we consider random scenarios, which can formulate those covariates, for example, uncertain weather. Conditioning on the realization of the random scenario, the uncertain demand may have different distributional information. We assume the mean, bound support, and the mean absolute deviations are known. The uncertain demands over multiple retailers are also allowed to be correlated. 3. To make adaptive inventory replenishment decisions that can be updated with observable demand by carrying out a decision rule approach; The third objective is achieved. In order to have a tractable adaptive robust optimization model, we impose the replenishment decisions to be affinely dependent on the past demand realization. Different from the classical approaches, where the linear coefficients are universally identical for all demand realizations, with the scenario-based ambiguity set, we let the linear coefficients be dependent on the realization of the random scenarios. We further identify the relationship between our model and classical policies. We show that the order-up-to level policy and the maximum-level policy are special cases of our policy. In other words, our model definitely perform better than the two classical policies. 4. To provide algorithms that can solve the optimization problem efficiently by adding valid cuts; The fourth objective is achieved. Since the uncertain inventory routing problem is very complicated, we have to develop our own algorithms by exploring the problem’s structure. We first exclude suboptimal routes to reduce the size of the feasible set and then further exclude some infeasible routes by applying valid arc reduction techniques. After introducing different ways to expedite its computation, we show that our inventory routing problem under uncertainty can be formulated as a mixed integer linear optimization problem.We can use the Benders decomposition approach to solve it efficiently.

16213417.label: Major findings and research outcome
16213417.value: This project studies a stochastic inventory routing problem with a finite horizon. The supplier acts as a central planner who determines replenishment quantities and also the times and routes for delivery to all retailers. 1. Our project is the first one to study robust inventory routing problems from the service-level perspective. a. We formulate a model to minimize the risk of uncertain inventory levels violating a pre-specified acceptable range by adopting a service-level viewpoint. We quantify that risk using a novel decision criterion, the Service Violation Index, that accounts for how often and how severely the inventory requirement is violated. Our model also allows ambiguity in the probability of uncertain demand. b. We show that our model can include classical policies, e.g., order-up-to level (OU) policy and the maximum-level (ML) policy, as special cases. Therefore, our model performs no worse than these two policies. c. The inventory routing problem contains the routing decisions, which make the situation much more complicated to solve. Hence, we further explore the structure of the problem to expedite the computational process. Our problem only requires the routing decision to satisfy the constraint imposed by a transportation cost budge. Hence, we can identify a set of maximal visiting nodes that the truck can visit within the cost budget. We further apply valid arc reduction techniques to exclude some routing decisions that do not meet our service level requirements. d. Through the numerical studies compared with other objective functions, we can show that our solutions exhibit more appealing performance with the same transportation cost. Our computational times are also attractive. Based on the above findings, we have finished one paper studying the inventory routing problem (Research Output No. 1). The paper has been submitted to the journal Operations Research and now is under the third-round review. Since Operations Research is one of the two flagship journals in our area, its review period is extremely long. We have addressed all comments raised by the referees. Hence, we are quite optimistic about the result. This is a collaboration work with my post-doc Zheng CUI. 2. Inspired by this network routing problem, my post-doc Zheng CUI has conducted research in the target-oriented distributionally robust optimization model. In the model, they also propose a decision criterion similar to our Service Violation Index to establish the bound information for the tail probability of the loss at all levels. The service-level perspective can also be transformed into a target-oriented optimization model. The paper (Research Output No. 2) is published in the INFORMS Journal on Computing and has acknowledged this grant. 3. We further generalize the network idea to study the social network problem. In particular, we investigate the process of network formation and its potential structural property. This work is conducted with my PhD student Hao LI. Our paper (Research Output No. 3) is invited for resubmission to the journal Manufacturing and Service Operations Management.

16213417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16213417.value: Inventory routing problem plays an essential role in coordinating different stakeholders in supply chain management. Our formulation and algorithm bring a new perspective for studying such a problem . There are many possible directions to explore in the future. We next list the most important two in our opinion. 1. Firstly, more efficient algorithms or heuristics can be developed to expedite the computation. In our project, since our focuses are the performance measures for evaluating the risk and the characterization of uncertainties, we only use Benders decomposition to solve the reformulated mixed-integer linear optimization problem. We can investigate further to check whether those classical algorithms for solving the deterministic IRP can be used or certain valid inequalities can be developed to solve a larger scale of stochastic IRP. 2. Secondly, the binary decision rule approach may be adopted so that the visiting decisions can also be adaptive. Unfortunately, the study of binary decision rules is quite limited due to the computational challenge, and current studies can only solve examples with a few binary decisions. We can further propose different formulations to incorporate the binary decision rule and test the performance.

16213417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16213417.value: This project considers a stochastic inventory routing problem (IRP) with a finite horizon. The IRP aims to manage the inventory and vehicle routing jointly. It is a fundamental problem in the vendor-managed inventory system, a relatively new business model in supply chain management. The supplier acts as a central planner who determines replenishment quantities and the times and routes for delivery to all retailers. We allow ambiguity in the probability distribution of each retailer’s uncertain demand. Adopting a service-level viewpoint, we minimize the risk of uncertain inventory levels violating a pre-specified acceptable range. We quantify that risk using a novel decision criterion, the Service Violation Index, that accounts for how often and how severely the inventory requirement is violated. The solutions proposed here are adaptive in that they vary with the realization of uncertain demand. We provide algorithms to solve the problem exactly and then demonstrate the superiority of our solutions by comparing them with several benchmarks. We further extend our framework to study target-oriented distributionally robust optimization models and also the process of network formation.

16213617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16213617.value: We propose to develop a learning model for the joint control of robotic reaching and eye movements, and to implement it on a mobile robot platform with a seven degree of freedom robotic arm and an active vision system. The key novelty in this model will be the integration of sensory and motor information within a predictive framework. This framework will provide a quantitative and testable model for the concept of sensorimotor contingencies, i.e. regularities in how sensory stimulation depends upon the activity of the perceiver. These contingencies are an important component of embodied models of conscious perception in humans, where sensorimotor coordination is seamless and adaptive. However, in robotic systems, learning of sensorimotor cue integration is still an important outstanding problem, which we hypothesize can be addressed by the development of learning models for sensorimotor contingencies. In order to do this, we propose an approach that extends our prior work on the active efficient encoding framework and the generative adaptive subspace self organizing map (GASSOM). The GASSOM is an unsupervised algorithm for learning of invariant feature detectors based on the concept of temporal slowness or temporal coherence, which seeks feature detectors that encode information that varies slowly in comparison to the raw sensory signals. The underlying idea of slowness is that the stability of the environment leads to statistical regularities in the raw sensory input that can be extracted to form a representation of the environment. However, this perspective is passive: it does not take into account the fact that much of the variation in the raw sensory input is due to observer motion, and is therefore predictable. We propose to extend the GASSOM algorithm so that it can learn these predictions, and in doing so, encode sensorimotor contingencies generated by an active observer. 我們提出開發一種聯合控制機器人觸摸和眼動的學習模型，並在具有七自由度的機器人手臂和主動視覺系統的移動機器人平台上實現。這個模型的關鍵創新性是在預測框架下整合感知和運動的信息。該框架將為感覺運動列聯性的概念提供定量和可測試的模型，即感覺刺激如何依賴於感知者的活動。這些列聯性是人類意識覺知模型的重要組成部分，對於人來說，感覺運動協調是無縫的和自適應的。然而對於機器人系統中，學習感知和運動的結合仍然是一個重要的突出問題，我們推測可以通過開發感知運動列聯性的學習模型來解決。為了做到這一點，我們提出了一種擴展我們以前的工作，主動高效編碼（AEC）框架和生成自適應子空間自組織圖（GASSSOM）的方法。GASSOM是一個無監督學習的特徵提取算法，該算法基於時間慢度或者時間相干性的概念學習不變特徵檢測器，尋求與原始信號相比緩慢變化的信息。時間慢度的基本思想是，環境的穩定性導致原始感官信號的統計規律可以用環境表徵的方式被提取出來。然而這個角度是被動的：它沒有考慮原始信號中的許多變化是由觀察者的運動引起的，因此是可以預測。我們提出擴展GASSOM算法，以便它可以學習這些預測，並且在這樣做時，編碼由主動觀察者產生的感覺運動列聯性。

16213617.label: Realisation of objectives
16213617.value: Objective 1, the development of an extension of our previously developed GASSOM algorithm for modelling visual input to also model the effect of eye movements, was 100% achieved. Our previously developed model treated inputs from different time instances as being independently generated. In our developed extension, we added a predictive stage to our our original architecture, which allowed the network to make a prediction of its output in the next frame, given the output in the current frame, as well as information about the agents self-motion (e.g. the eye movement between the current and the next frame). In a stationary environment, an eye movement typically leads to image motion. For the GASSOM with two-dimensional latent subspaces, this image motion results in a rotation in the two-dimensional subspace, where the amount of rotation depends upon the magnitude of the eye movement. Thus, by predicting this rotation given the eye-movement, we can make a prediction about the GASSOM representation of the visual input in the next frame. We described this new model in output C.10.1. Objective 2, the application of our new combined visual input/eye movement modelling to sensorimotor inputs generated by a realistic model of eye movements, was 100% achieved. We applied our model to explain the autonomous development of active binocular vision and motion vision via the Active Efficient Coding (AEC) framework, as reported in output C.8.1. Previous work in applying AEC to model the development of eye movements focused on only a single task, i.e. EITHER binocular vision OR motion perception. Our new model enabled us to address the joint emergence of BOTH forms of perception simultaneously. Our results show that the model keeps improving until it hits physical constraints such as camera or motor resolution, or limits on its internal coding capacity. Furthermore, we show that the emerging sensory tuning properties are in line with results on disparity, motion, and motion-in-depth tuning in the visual cortex of mammals. We also developed a realistic model of eye movements in work reported in outputs C.9.1 and C.9.2. In these papers, we demonstrated that by incorporating a realistic model of eye movements into a sensorimotor control task (here autonomous driving), we we were able to improve the generalization and robustness of behavior. We studied two behaviors: following and overtaking. Incorporating our model significantly improved driving performance by up to 50%, as measured by the average distance travelled between two infractions. Objective 3, the extension of our model to include the effect of not only eye movements, but also other forms of self-motion, was 100% achieved. In work reported in output C.10.1, we extended the model to include the effect of proprioceptive measurements of arm movements as a robot learned to track its end-effector (i.e. hand) as it moved through space. Our model enabled the robot to track its end-effector in three cases: using both viaual and proprioceptive cues, using visual cues only and using proprioceptive cues. Our experiments using an iCub humanoid robotic simulator demonstrated that the incorporation of prediction improved performance significantly (effect size 4.2) when proprioceptive input was used, with no degradation in performance for the two cases where visual input was available. This finding is significant, as it enables better tracking in cases where visual input is unavailable (e.g. in darkness) or unreliable (e.g. due to occlusion). We also integrated our gaze model into another task, trajectory prediction, as reported in outputs C.9.3 and C.9.4. In particular, we developed a graph convolutional network (GCN) architecture for trajectory prediction that included the effects of both human attention as measured by gaze as well as the effect of visual field constraints. Our methods incorporating gaze modelling acheived state of the art performance on several different trajectory prediction benchmarks. Our ablation studies with networks without one or both of these additional cues demonstrated that the incorporation of attention and visual field constrants was critical in acheiving the improved performance that we observed. Objective 4, the application of our model to sensorimotor inputs generated by a robotic platform that executes both eye movements and random motions, was 100% achieved. In work reported in output C.10.1, we showed that random motions in the form of motor babbling by the arm are critical in enabling the system to learn the sensorimotor contingencies captured by the predictive model in our newly developed GASSOM extension. This aided in the development of hand-eye coordination of a humanoid robot. In work reported in output C.10.2, we showed that eye-hand coordination during a line tracing task is indicative of user engagement. In work reported in C.8.2, we also demonstrated generality of our proposed model by applying it to a different sensorimotor task, echolocation. Since bats hunt in darkness, they use sonar rather than vision, to localize their prey. Although they use different modalities (sound versus light), echolocation and vision are related in that they both seek to extract information about the environment using reflected energy received by the sensory apparatus. Thus, while not obvious, it is intuitively appealing that a model applicable for vision should also be applicable to echolocation. Our work shows that this is indeed the case, and that random movements called head waggles are important in improving localization accuracy, especially in the vertical direction, where interaural time differences are less informative.

16213617.label: Major findings and research outcome
16213617.value: In this project, we have developed an extension to our previously proposed Generative Adaptive Subspace Self Organizing Map (GASSOM) algorithm for building an internal neurally inspired represetation of the sensory input (output C.10.1), which can for the basis for subsequent action by a robotic agent, to include a predictive component. This predictive component enabled us to better account for the effects of self-motion by the agent, which leads to changes in the sensory input that are not necessarily correlated with changes in the environment, but rather more with changes in the relationship between the agent and its environment. Thus, our predictive processing framework provides a method for encoding not only the sensory input, but also sensorimotor contingencies, i.e. regularities in how sensory stimulation depends upon the activity of the perceiver. This makes the internal representation better suited as a basis for action in a robotic agent that is continually moving and interacting with its environment. We applied this new predictive model to a number of visually guided robotic applications: to modelling the joint emergence of vergence and smooth pursuite eye movements as driven by sensory representation encoding both bioncular vision and motion perception (output C.8.1), to imitation learning of autonomous driving where our models were able to improve the generalization and robustness of performance (outputs C.9.1 and C.9.2), to learning of hand-eye coordination for a robotic manipulator where our model significantly improve performance in environments where the visual input was degraded or unavailable (output C.10.1), to trajectory prediction where our models improved the fidelity between predictions and the ground truth (outputs C.9.3 and C.9.4). Because our model exploits unsupervised learning, it is well suited to handle situations where movements appear to be somewhat random (e.g. in the case of motor babbling by infants, who make random body movements as they explore the relationship between their motor actions and their received sensory input leading to better motor control). We have demonstrated this in two settings related to hand-eye coordination: reaching (output C.10.1) and line-tracing (output C.10.2). Finally, we demonstrated the generality of our predictive coding framework by applying it to a new sensory modality, audition (output C.8.2).

16213617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16213617.value: The work in this proposal focused mainly upon incorporating predictive models into visual perception and visually guided behaviors such as hand-eye coordination and related tasks like autonomous driving and visual navigation in crowded environments. However, the formulation we have developed in this project is generic. It can be applied to a variety of other sensory modalities. Our initial work in applying this predictive GASSOM formulation in auditory perception in the work on bat echolocation (output C.8.2) is a promising step in this direction. However, much more remains to be done. In particular, the formulation here may provide the basis for the treatment of multisensory integration, i.e. the combination of inputs from different sensory modalties, i.e. vision, audition, touch, etc. into a coherent perception of the environment. If successful, we expect that such an approach would significantly improve robustness in robotic settings, as it would enable robots to build a more complete model of their environment, and to compensate automatically to situations where one sensory input is temporarily degraded, e.g. due to sudden changes in illumination or to the sudden onset of noise from other agents in the environment.

16213617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16213617.value: Early hypotheses about sensory perception by the brain assumed that neurons were simply responding to the sensory input received from the environment. More recently, neuroscientists have been develeoped a predictive coding or predictive processing theory, which hypothesizes that the brain maintains a mental model of the environment, and updates this model by comparing predictions of the sensory input it expects to receive with the sensory input that it actuallly receives. Rather than viewing perception as a passive response to sensory input, it considers it an active response by an active observer. This predictive processing theory provides a model for the way in which the brain learns snensor-motor contingencies. contingencies, i.e. regularities in how sensory stimulation depends upon the activity of the perceiver. These contingencies are an important component of embodied models of conscious perception in humans, where sensorimotor coordination is seamless and adaptive. The work in this proposal developed new predictive processing models of the perception-action cycle, and applied them in a variety of robotic settings. Our results demonstrated that incorporating prediction into perception significantly improves performance.

16213717.label: Project Objectives
16213717.value: Develop a lens-specific fisheye camera calibration method that uses manufacturer data for the optical lens to assist with the intrinsic calibration, and develop online calibration approaches for stereo extrinsic calibration. Rectify the overlapping camera views into stereo image pairs and develop an omnidirectional spatial stereo matching pipeline for depth estimation in horizontal directions. Develop an omnidirectional visual-inertial state estimation method using tightly coupled, optimization-based sensor fusion, and achieve a level of accuracy that is sufficient to support omnidirectional dense motion stereo. Based on the state estimation results, develop an omnidirectional motion stereo method that uses spherical sweeping for blind spot-free dense depth estimation of the whole surrounding environment. Achieve volumetric fusion of the depth measurements from both the spatial and motion stereo methods, and demonstrate closed-loop autonomous navigation and obstacle avoidance on board a quadrotor testbed.

16213717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16213717.value: Over the past few years, we have witnessed the rapid growth of the consumer and commercial drone markets, with the increased use of multi-rotor aerial vehicles for inspection, aerial photography, and ”selfies”. Safety is undoubtedly the most important requirement in drone applications. Numerous efforts have been put to equip drones with GPS-free self-localization, obstacle sensing, and autonomous navigation capabilities. For commercial applications that are less sensitive to the platform cost and weight, active range sensors such as LiDARs and radars can be used. However, active sensors are unsuitable for consumer drones with tight cost and weight constraints. In these cases, vision-based approaches become the only viable options due to their excellent size, weight, and power (SWaP) characteristics. A representative vision-enabled consumer drone is the DJI Phantom 4, which is equipped with two pairs of stereo cameras for frontal obstacle detection and self-localization. Unfortunately, the sensing capability of these drones is still insufficient to achieve the required safety level. Given the increasing use of consumer drones in cluttered and densely populated areas, the lack of omnidirectional preception makes their use very risky. Although laws and regulations can be implemented to reduce the risk, safety for drone operations should also be ensured through technological capabilities. In the proposed project, drawing on our recent findings on visual-inertial state estimation, dense mapping, and system integration, we will develop a novel low-cost solution for omnidirectional dense mapping for consumer drones. We believe that full perception covering the entire spherical surroundings with no blind spot, and a dense map that aggregates past sensor measurements, are the best way to guarantee safety. Instead of adding more cameras for better coverage, we will develop a minimal sensor suite that consists of only two fisheye cameras, each with 220 degrees field of view, and a low-cost inertial measurement unit (IMU). We will begin by developing a special calibration pipeline to estimate both the intrinsic fisheye distortion models and extrinsic parameters. We will design an omnidirectional visual-inertial state estimator to serve as the backbone for closed-loop feedback control and motion stereo. We will propose a mapping pipeline that uses omnidirectional spatial stereo to cover horizontal directions, with the addition of spherical motion stereo to achieve blind spot-free mapping. We will develop the full system pipeline, from sensor selection and calibration, to state estimation and dense mapping, and ultimately close the perception-action loop by demonstrating autonomous navigation in complex and GPS-denied environments. 近幾年來，随着多旋翼飛行器在偵查、航拍和“自拍”方面的應用日益廣泛，消費级和商用無人機市場呈現迅速增長。對安全性的要求成為無人機應用的重中之重。前人付出了諸多努力，讓無人機擁有不依賴衛星導航系統的自主定位，障礙物感知和自主導航功能。對於平台成本和重量不太敏感的商業應用，可以使用如激光雷達和無線電雷達等主動測距傳感器。然而，對於受成本和重量嚴格限制的消費級無人機， 主動測距傳感器卻並不適用。在這種情况下，基於視覺的解決方案由於其尺寸小，重量輕和功率低的特性而成為唯一可行途徑。作為基於視覺的消費級無人機代表，大疆精靈4無人機配備了兩對立體相機，用於前視障礙物檢測和自主定位。但是，這些無人機的感知能力仍不足以達到所需的安全水平。鑒於消費級無人機越来越廣泛使用在人口稠密與環境雜亂的地區中，缺乏全方位感知會使其應用變得相當危險。雖然可以引入法律法規從而降低風險，但依靠提升技術水平來確保無人機操作的安全性仍然十分必要。 在本項目中，憑藉近期我們對於視覺慣導狀態估計，稠密建圖和系統集成的研究成果，我們將為開發一種創新且成本低廉的解決方案。我們認為可覆蓋全景環境且無盲區的完整感知能力，以及可累積過去傳感器測量结果的稠密地圖，是確保安全性的最佳方式。比起安裝更多的相機以期獲得更好的視覺覆蓋，我們將開發一個最小的傳感器套件，只包含兩個具有220度廣角的魚眼相機和一個低成本的。我們會首先開發一種可估計魚眼相機内部畸變模型和外在參數的特殊標定流程。然後我們將設計一個全景視覺慣導狀態估計器来作閉環反饋控制和運動恢復結構的主體。我們還會提出一種可在水平方向使用全景雙目視覺的建圖流程。此流程同时具有全景運動恢復結構來實現無盲區建圖能力。至此，我們將開發一個具有傳感器選擇與校準，狀態估計及稠密建圖的完整系統流程， 並在複雜環境和無法使用衛星導航系統的情況下演示自主导航。

16213717.label: Realisation of objectives
16213717.value: We developed a light-weight and low-cost omnidirectional perception system, which consists of two ultra wide field-of-view (FOV) fisheye cameras and a low-cost inertial measurement unit (IMU). The two fisheye cameras are mounted rigidly facing upward and downward directions and provide omnidirectional perception coverage: 360° FOV horizontally, 50° FOV vertically for stereo, and whole spherical for monocular. We also developed a novel optimization-based dual fisheye visual-inertial state estimator to provide highly accurate state-estimation. Real-time omnidirectional three-dimensional (3D) mapping is combined with stereo based depth perception for the horizontal direction and monocular depth perception for upward and downward directions. The omnidirectional perception system is integrated with online trajectory planners to achieve closed-loop, fully autonomous navigation. We developed an online approach for calibrating temporal offset between visual and inertial measurements. Our approach achieves temporal offset calibration by jointly optimizing time offset, camera and IMU states, as well as feature locations in a SLAM system. Furthermore, the approach is a general model, which can be easily employed in several feature-based optimization frameworks. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate the high accuracy of our calibration approach even compared with other state-of-art offline tools. The VIO comparison against other methods proves that the online temporal calibration significantly benefits visual-inertial systems. We also proposed a robust and versatile monocular visual-inertial estimator. Our approach features both state-of-the-art and novel solutions to IMU preintegration, estimator initialization, online extrinsic calibration, tightly coupled VIO, relocalization, and efficient global optimization. We show superior performance by comparing against other state-of-the-art open-source implementations. We open source both PC and IOS implementation for the benefit of the community. We developed FUEL, a hierarchical framework that can support Fast UAV ExpLoration in complex unknown environments. We maintain crucial information in the entire space required by exploration planning by a frontier information structure (FIS), which can be updated incrementally when the space is explored. Supported by the FIS, a hierarchical planner plans exploration motions in three steps, which find efficient global coverage paths, refine a local set of viewpoints and generate minimum-time trajectories in sequence. We presented extensive benchmark and real-world tests, in which our method completes the exploration tasks with unprecedented efficiency (3-8 times faster) compared to state-of-the-art approaches. Our methods are open sourced to benefit the community. We developed a dense mapping system for autonomous navigation. The proposed system has multithreads run asynchronously. This system was built on a presented sparse feature-based SLAM pipeline, which provides the latest poses for dense mapping. The key to our dense mapping approach is the presented map representation that combines the advantages of both metric maps and topological maps. By using this map representation, depth estimates at different locations are easily integrated and dense maps are flexibly deformed if loops are closed. For the benefit of handling dynamic objects, we introduced a subvolume wrapping and blending scheme that operated on TSDFs. Moreover, we have shown how to reconstruct local maps around instant poses in real time based on the presented map representation. The complexity of our method does not scale with respect to the travel time or the travel distance. In the end, we verified that our approach obtains a good tradeoff between the mapping accuracy, the mapping density and the outlier rate on the KITTI and NewCollege datasets, and a large-scale outdoor experiment. The built maps are suitable for real-time planning where safety is the first concern. We proposed a general GPS-aided omnidirectional visual-inertial state estimator capable of operating in ubiquitous environments and platforms. Our system consists of two parts: 1) the pre-processing of omnidirectional cameras, IMU, and GPS measurements, and 2) the sliding window based nonlinear optimization for accurate state estimation. We test our system in different conditions including an indoor office, campus roads, and challenging open water surface. Experiment results demonstrate the high accuracy of our approach than state-of-the- art VINSs in all scenarios. The proposed odometry achieves drift ratio less than 0.5% in 1200 m length outdoors campus road in overexposure conditions and 0.65% in open water surface, without a loop closure, compared with a centimeter accuracy GPS reference. We proposed a novel dense surfel mapping system that scales well in different environments with only CPU computation. Using a sparse SLAM system to estimate camera poses, the proposed mapping system can fuse intensity images and depth images into a globally consistent model. The system is carefully designed so that it can build from room-scale environments to urban-scale environments using depth images from RGB-D cameras, stereo cameras or even a monocular camera. First, superpixels extracted from both intensity and depth images are used to model surfels in the system. superpixel-based surfels make our method both runtime efficient and memory efficient. Second, surfels are further organized according to the pose graph of the SLAM system to achieve O(1) fusion time regardless of the scale of reconstructed models. Third, a fast map deformation using the optimized pose graph enables the map to achieve global consistency in real-time. The proposed surfel mapping system is compared with other state-of-the-art methods on synthetic datasets. The performances of urban-scale and room-scale reconstruction are demonstrated using the KITTI dataset and autonomous aggressive flights, respectively. The code is available for the benefit of the community.

16213717.label: Major findings and research outcome
16213717.value: We presented a dual‐fisheye autonomous aerial robot system with the minimum sensor setup for omnidirectional visual perception. The whole system is implemented on the small size and light‐weight quadrotor whose all modules are processed onboard and in real‐time. By adequately coordinating three major system modules, state estimation, dense mapping, and trajectory planning, we validate our system in both cluttered indoor and outdoor environments via multiple autonomous flight experiments. An omnidirectional tightly coupled visual-inertial state estimator is developed for providing high-accuracy odometry and vehicle velocity, metric scale, and IMU biases, which is used for both feedback control and dense mapping. And it is robust in textureless environments with omnidirectional perception. Without any prior knowledge of the environment, our dense mapping module extracts 3D omnidirectional information. The depth maps in the overlapping regions are generated via a fixed baseline stereo camera, and the depth maps in the monocular regions are calculated as motion stereo. After semiglobal optimization and postprocessing, the dense depth images are calculated and fed into our TSDF fusion approach, from which a live dense 3D map is produced. All modules are real‐time, onboard, and without any offline processing. With this map, a planning module generates a collisionfree trajectory. Benefit from the rapid increase of mobile computing power and sensor production level, we believe that our minimum sensor setup suggests a feasible solution for fully autonomous miniaturized aerial robots.

16213717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16213717.value: In the future, we will try to apply visual-inertial omnidirectional dense mapping techniques to consumer-grade UAV products truly, and use it to enhance the autonomous perception, flight capability of consumer-grade UAVs. In addition, we are developing aerial swarm using omnidirectional cameras and taking advantage of omnidirectional can extend the observability of the aerial swarm, which will lead to more secure, autonomous, high-performance decentralized and distributed aerial swarm.

16213717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16213717.value: We present a complete system solution to address all the challenges above. Specifically, we propose a dual-fisheye visual inertial system (VINS), which provides visual perception in all directions (frontward, backward, upward, downward, leftward, and rightward) with two fisheye cameras. The system-level contribution is the autonomous aerial robot platform using the minimalist omnidirectional visual perception system with fully onboard processing. It is challenging to use ultrawide fisheye images directly because of its significant distortion. To overcome this, we use a fisheye camera model to ensure accurate visual measurements. The backbone of our state-estimation algorithm package is a highly accurate, tightly coupled, optimization-based dual-fisheye omnidirectional visual-inertial state estimator with fisheye camera support, and camera-inertial measurement unit (IMU) extrinsic calibration. It is essential to provide different depth estimates since the various properties of the images: stereo-depth estimation for stereo vision coverage region and motion-stereo-depth estimation for the monocular region. The perception-action loop is closed by executing the desired trajectory using a standard multirotor controller. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to achieve such omnidirectional navigation capability using this minimum sensor suite. This study points out a direction towards omnidirectional autonomy for small aerial vehicles.

16214017.label: Major findings and research outcome
16214017.value: The first objective is to propose a query-efficient data structure such that for any two points on the surface of the terrain, the data structure could help to return the shortest distance/path between these two points efficiently on the surface of the terrain for each shortest distance/path query. We developed a novel indexing technique called “SE oracle” [C6] which could answer shortest distance/path queries efficiently and effectively. In particular, the building time of this index is short, the index size is small and the query time is short. These results were done by my PhD student called Victor Junqiu WEI. The second objective is to study some applications of the shortest distance queries in the context of the terrain using our proposed data structure. We studied different applications. The first application is to find the co-location pattern [C2]. The second application is to study the user's preference using a new concept called regret ratio [C1, C3, C4, J1] and another new concept called happiness ratio [C5]. The third application is to study how to recommend interesting items to users in the context of session-based recommendation systems [C7, C9]. The fourth application is to study speech recognition with some information retrieval techniques [C8]. The last application is to study how to use the shortest distance/path on the surface surface in the university campus navigation system called "Path Advisor" [C10]. Some of these results were done by my PhD student called Harry Kai-Ho CHAN.

16214017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16214017.value: There are further developments of the research studied in this project. Since the problem studied in this project is to study shortest distance/path queries in spatial databases. Since shortest distance/path queries are fundamental spatial queries, it is expected that there are more applications using these queries such as nearest neighbor queries. In addition, mobile data becomes much larger nowadays. It is interesting to study how our proposed method could handle larger data in a distributed manner (e.g., cloud computing).

16214017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16214017.value: [Nature] Due to the advance of the geo-spatial positioning and the computer graphics technology, digital terrain data become more and more popular nowadays, and it has been used in many applications such as Microsoft’s Bing Maps and Google Earth in the industry community. The terrain data has also attracted considerable attention from the academic industry. This is because it involves a variety of diverse applications including Geographical Information System (GIS), computer graphics and vision, scientific data 3D modeling (e.g., biology, chemistry, anthropology and archeology), online 3D virtual game and spatial data mining. [Significance and Values] Although there are existing studies focusing on studying how to compute shortest distances, none of the existing studies could return the solution within a short time. Our preliminary experimental results show that our proposed fast algorithm returns a solution within 1 ms but the best-known algorithm returns a solution more than 10 seconds in a small-sized dataset containing thousands of points only. It is expected that our proposed algorithm is still very fast but the performance of the best-known algorithm is not acceptable in a large-sized dataset (e.g., a dataset containing more than 1 million points) in the big data age. The findings of our project are expected to help companies to take the shortest distance queries and their applications in consideration for their companies’ goals to improve user’s experience.

16214117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16214117.value: Hong Kong has been practicing seawater toilet flushing since 1958, which saves 20% of freshwater resources [1]. This water-saving system has enabled us to develop a novel saline sewage treatment technology for cost-saving and space-efficient treatment of saline sewage through up to 70% biological sludge minimization, namely the Sulfate reduction, Autotrophic denitrification and Nitrification Integrated (SANI) process [2]. After more than a decade of development, this technology has been moved from laboratory study to large scale trials towards potential application (see blog of Financial Secretary of the Hong Kong SAR Government) [3]. The following upgrading is to develop the next generation of SANI for highly compact as well as energy-efficient sewage treatment in Hong Kong or coastal regions. Technological breakthroughs must be made to integrate current separate bioreactors (for sulfate reduction and nitrogen removal) with different functional organisms (anaerobic, aerobic and anoxic bacteria) into a single-sludge single-reactor system for simultaneous removal of carbon (C), nitrogen (N) and phosphorous (P) with mediation of sulfate. Granular sludge provides a possible solution for integration of different bioprocesses as demonstrated in the aerobic granular sludge (AGS) process for freshwater sewage treatment [4]. AGS is, however, not suitable for saline sewage treatment subjected to double inhibitions of high salinity and sulfide on its bioprocesses [5, 6]. Hence, a completely new version of granular sludge based sulfur conversion-associated C, N, and P removal is deemed necessary, i.e. the Single sludge Single reactor SANI (SS-SANI). This project is therefore, aimed at developing SS-SANI for integrating the three key microorganisms, sulfate-reducing bacteria, sulfide-oxidizing bacteria and nitrifiers in granules to remove C, N and P in a single reactor. Focus will be placed on investigation of process feasibility, determination of appropriate operation conditions, characterization of the microbial structure of granules, and revelation of the role of sulfate conversion in the process metabolism. These fundamental information are essential for optimizing operation of such a complex bio-treatment system as well as facilitating a pilot trial of this completely new SANI technology for scaling up to potential application in Hong Kong in the future. 香港自1958年起引入海水沖廁，現每天為全港節省約20%的淡水資源[1], 但同時產生了大量含鹽廢水，為新型高效污水處理工藝—SANI工藝的研發提供了契機[2]。與傳統污水處理工藝相比，SANI工藝除處理效率高、操作成本低外，更可減少高達70%的生物質污泥產量。經十餘年發展，該項技術已成功的走出實驗室，在香港特區完成了大型示範項目[3]。目前研究重點在為沿海地區開發佔地面積小、高效節能的新一代SANI工藝。如何整合現有三個獨立生物反應器（除碳脫氮）成為單污泥單反應器系統，在硫酸鹽協同作用下達到碳、氮、磷同步去除是工藝升級優化的關鍵技術問題。好氧顆粒污泥在淡水處理系統中成功應用，為多種生物反應整合提供了全新的平台[4]。然而有資料表明，好氧顆粒並不適合高鹽高硫廢水的處理[5,6]。因此，發展基於硫代謝協同去除碳、氮、磷的新型顆粒污泥系統—單污泥單反應器SANI工藝是該處理工藝升級換代的必然選擇之一。 通過新型顆粒污泥整合硫還原菌、硫氧化菌及硝化菌達到同步去除碳、氮、磷實現單污泥單反應器的目標，重點研究在該新工藝的可行性、控制參數的優化、生物群落的結構表征及硫代謝在系統中的機理與作用。該課題的基礎研究將對優化複雜生物處理系統、實現新一代SANI在沿海地區的應用至關重要。

16214117.label: Realisation of objectives
16214117.value: Objective 1 - Investigate this new SS-SANI process through the long-term operation with different sulfate mixing ratios and operation conditions The Single sludge Single reactor SANI (SS-SANI) process has been studied in lab-scale sequencing batch reactors over a long-term operation. Upon the successful completion of this task, the carbon/sulfate ratio, role of sulfate during the granulation and nutrients (Nitrogen and Phosphate) metabolism were investigated; sludge granulation was trialed as a means of improving the process performance; and the effects of pH, temperature, sludge retention time (SRT) and hydraulic retention time (HRT) on the performance of this process were investigated to optimize the process’ operating conditions. The granular sludge has successfully developed using various proportions of seawater mixed with synthetic municipal sewage. The addition of seawater (0–100%) or sulfate (0–1000 mg/L) significantly accelerated the granulation process in comparison with freshwater and resulted in a stronger granular structure. The increased presence of gel-forming alginate-like exopolysaccharides in the granules explains why a greater proportion of seawater leads to higher density and improves the cohesive strength of the granules. The formation of granular sludge (1.0–2.6 mm) for SS-SANI could realize better biomass retention and treatment capacity, achieving COD, ammonia and TN (total nitrogen) 90%, 99% and 55% removal, respectively. Sulfate concentration influenced phosphate removal efficiency via affecting available energy for phosphate uptake with poor phosphate removal at low (0 mg SO42-/L) and high (1000 mg SO42-/L) concentrations of sulfate and almost 90% removal achieved in the presence of 200 mg/L sulfate. A nearly two-fold improvement in the P removal efficiency and a 20%-cycle time reduction were achieved compared with flocculent sludge. Objective 2 - Analyze the microbial community and the structure of the granules for simultaneous removal of C, N and P The microbial communities, functional bacteria and their metabolism of the sludge samples were analyzed via high throughput sequencing of their 16S rRNA gene. The major functional bacteria, i.e. sulfate-reducing (Pseudomonas, Megasphaera, Stenotrophomonas, Desulfovibrio, Desulfobulbus and Veillonella) and sulfide-oxidizing bacteria (Comamonas, Pseudomonas, Brevundimonas, Delftia and Planctopirus), were shown to both participate synergistically in the process and be crucial for maintaining sulfur conversion at 150-550 mg SO42-/L. Such sulfur conversion pattern and synergistic microbial niche catered to the biological phosphate removal operation mode, i.e., alternating anoxic/aerobic conditions, and it is also in favor of various energy flows from internal polymers (i.e. polysulfide or elemental sulfur [poly-S2-/S0] and poly-β-hydroxyalkanoates [PHA]) for phosphorus removal. The optimal anaerobic/aerobic period ratio of 1:2 was determined based on further batch tests in terms of carbon and nutrients removal. Low-term evaluation displayed beneath a critical sulfate concentration (200 mg/L in this study), volatile fatty acid (VFA) uptake, PHA formation, poly-P storage and phosphate uptake were intensified with increasing sulfate concentration. Further increase in sulfate concentration beyond the level slowed down and inhibited these processes. Moreover, anaerobic batch experiments were conducted for elucidating the fundamental stoichiometric relationship of carbon uptake (PHA)/ phosphate release (0.5–0.92 mmol-C/mgP). Objective 3 - Investigate the biochemical and microbial reactions in the reactor with a special focus on sulfate and phosphorus transportation, metabolism, and metabolites The interactions among sulfur, phosphorus metabolisms, and sludge granulation towards efficient saline/sulfate-laden wastewater treatment were explored, focusing on energy and mass conservation through batch tests. It was observed that ATP consumption increased as sulfate concentration increased from 0 to 200 mg/L in the aerobic phase and the highest average consumption of ATP occurred at sulfate concentration of 200 mg/L. In the anoxic phase, sulfide is generated due to the anaerobic conditions caused by the layered structure of the granule. This leads to an increased requirement for sulfide detoxification coupled with proton pumping; thus partial ATP was allocated for detoxification. When the sulfate concentration is too high (500 mg/L and beyond as is the case in this study), more ATP will be used for sulfide release, leaving less or even insufficient ATP for PHA synthesis, which jeopardizes the subsequent phosphate uptake. Regarding the study of sulfate metabolism and bio-aggregation, adenosine phosphosulfate (APS) was first produced through sulfate reduction. The APS will be further converted into Cysteine (Cys) and Methionine (Met) in assimilatory sulfate reduction, which then participates in the Activated Methyl Cycle to form diverse sulfur-containing chemicals, including S-adenosylmethionine (SAM), S-adenosylhomocysteine (SAH), S-ribosylhomocysteine (SRH) and homocysteine. Subsequently, a protein encoded by LuxI gene utilizes SAM as a primer in the synthesis of AHLs, one kind of quorum sensing (QS) auto-inducer which facilitates aggregation of microorganisms via quorum sensing.

16214117.label: Major findings and research outcome
16214117.value: • The addition of seawater significantly accelerated the granulation process in comparison with freshwater and resulted in a stronger granular structure due to the abundance of metal ions and the increased production of gel-forming alginate-like exopolysaccharides. • A synergistic relationship exists between anaerobic sulfate reduction, sulfide oxidation and biological P removal, viz. efficient P removal could be achieved at the appropriate sulfate concentration (< 200 mg /L). • Sulfate-reducing bacteria (SRB) and sulfide-oxidizing bacteria (SOB) work synergistically for biological P removal in the SS-SANI process. At the steady-state, SRB and SOB were enriched by 16.2% and 11.6%, respectively. • The produced sulfide promoted VFA uptake of microorganisms, producing more energy for phosphate uptake when sulfate concentrations were beneath 200 mg/L. However, sulfide detoxification became energy dominating, leaving insufficient energy for PHA synthesis and phosphate uptake when sulfate content was further increased. • Granulation was accelerated with increasing sulfate levels by enhanced production of N-Acyl homoserine lactones (AHLs), a kind of quorum sensing (QS) auto-inducer, using an intermediate of sulfate reduction viz. S-Adenosyl Methionine (SAM) as a primer. • This study also discovered several bio-active sulfated polysaccharides (SP), including fucoidan, carrageenan and heparin, with considerable amounts in the extracellular polymeric substances (EPS) of the granular sludge in SS-SANI process, which offers an SP recovery opportunity from the waste stream.

16214117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16214117.value: During the execution of this project, we found high content of a scarce resource (i.e. SP) was produced by the granular sludge in SS-SANI process. SP is a high-value substance, can be extensively used as industrial feedstock in dyeing, paper-making, rubber, food, cosmetics and fertilizer production industries, as well as medical dressings and pharmaceutical intermediates. However, the production pathways, species, bioactivity and recovery methods are not clear; hence the recommendation for future studies are as follows: 1) the metagenomic and metatranscriptomic studies are necessary to obtain more detailed information about the microbial community as well as insights into the pathways of S conversion and SP production; 2) tests should be conducted to determine the SP production controlling factors including pH, temperature, sulfur source, sulfur concentration, carbon source, SRT, HRT and anaerobic/aerobic period; 3) sludge-based SP extraction method should be developed and optimized as no existing method can serve this purpose presently, and 3) deciphering biosynthetic pathways of SP in the biological wastewater treatment system and determining major influencing factors on the production of SP are important to maximize SP production and recovery in the future.

16214117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16214117.value: An innovative Single sludge Single reactor SANI (SS-SANI) process has been developed for for maximizing space- and energy-efficient treatment of saline sewage. This process has successfully integrated multi-bioreactions reaching sulfur (S), carbon (C), nitrogen (N) and phosphate (P) simultaneous removal; In addition, with a proper concentration of sulfate, the entire process such as granulation and P removal can be accelerated. To elucidate this new process, in this research, we have investigated the structure of the microorganism and fundamental bioreactions in the system, identified the biochemical pathways and assessed the operational and environmental factors on process performance as well as trials on process optimization.

16214217.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16214217.value: 基於SiGe納米柱和選擇性等離子吸收膜的高性能熱電紅外傳感器

16214217.label: Project Objectives
16214217.value: To develop a theoretical model that can predict the behavior of the infrared sensors based on the pillar design. The influence of various factors such as the geometry of thermoelectric pillars, contact resistance, absorber area and the heat loss caused by the ambient air will be explored using numerical simulation and theoretical modeling. To develop a thermoelectric infrared sensor based on SiGe nanopillars and plasmonic absorber layer to detect far infrared with a wavelength of 8-10 microns. The fabrication flow process will be developed to integrate the vertically standing SiGe nanopillars and selective plasmonic absorber to form an IR sensor with a compact structure (feature size below 30 microns), a high responsivity and a short response time (< 20 ms). To study the influence of surface plasmon on the spectral absorption, transmission and reflection of far infrared. The effects of various factors, such as the plasmonic pattern shape and distribution, thickness of the spacer layer, the dielectric functions of the spacer and substrate will be investigated. This study can provide useful information for the design of efficient plasmonic patterns for infrared detection. A theoretical model will be developed to guide the design of the plasmonic structure and evaluate the influence of surface plasmon on infrared detection. To fabricate and characterize a plasmonic structure that can enhance the selective infrared adsorption and trapping.

16214217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16214217.value: Infrared detection has been an active field in recent decades due to its significance in many applications. Seeking for solutions of low power, low cost, and high spatial and temporal resolutions is continuously driven by the great demands from various areas. Current high-performance infrared sensing systems are generally very expensive and bulky because an integrated delicate cryogenic cooling system is often indispensable for the suppression of thermal noise and temperature drift. Thermoelectric infrared sensors are passive sensors that can operate over a wide spectral band without current input and temperature control, therefore offering high reliability, high stability, compact system structure, low cost and low power consumption. The wide application of thermoelectric infrared sensors is currently hindered by the low responsivity and low spatial and temporal resolutions, which are mainly due to the conventional planar design and large device size (> 100 microns). It is difficult to significantly improve the sensor performance while keeping the sensing unit miniaturized with the conventional planar design. To overcome these issues, we propose a novel pillar design based on free-standing thermoelectric nanopillar array and selective plasmonic absorber. We will design and fabricate a thermoelectric pillar structure with large-aspect-ratio n and p-type SiGe nanowires connected in series on the basis of nanograined high-performance SiGe films, which can significantly improve the responsivity while minimizing the device size and response time. Meanwhile, we will develop efficient selective infrared absorber by taking advantage of plasmonic structure that can improve the absorbance and reduce the thermal mass. The influence of various factors on the optical behaviors of the plasmonic absorber will also be explored through experimental characterization and numerical simulations. Preliminary analysis shows that with the proposed new design, it is promising to achieve both a high responsivity (up to ~ 1000V/W) and fast thermal response (<10 ms) while keeping the dimensions of the sensing unit below 20 microns, making it very competitive in high-end infrared detection applications. It is expected that this new design can find many potential applications in the areas related to high-resolution thermal radiation or temperature sensing, such as thermal imaging, night vision and bio-sensing. 紅外檢測由於其在諸多領域的重要應用在近數十年來一直是一個活躍的領域。不同領域的巨大需求一直推動發展低能耗，低成本和高空間與時間解析度的紅外檢測解決方案。目前的高性能紅外檢測系統通常需要集成一個低溫冷卻系統以減小熱噪聲和溫度漂移，因此非常昂貴且累贅。熱電紅外傳感器是被動式傳感器，無需輸入電流和溫度控制，並具有很寬的工作頻譜，具有可靠性高，體積緊湊，低能耗和低成本等優勢。然而目前的熱電紅外感測器受限於低響應率和低時間空間解析度，沒有得到廣泛的應用，這主要是由於傳統的平面設計和較大的器件尺寸。按照傳統的平面設計，很難在縮小器件尺寸的同時顯著提升感測器的性能。 為克服這些問題，我們提出一種新型的柱型設計，該設計基於豎立的熱電納米柱陣列和等離子體吸收層。本項目將基於具有納米晶粒的高性能SiGe薄膜，設計製造熱電柱型結構, 該結構由相互串聯的高長徑比的n和p型SiGe納米線構成，能夠顯著提升響應率並減少器件尺寸和響應時間。同時，我們將利用等離子體結構發展高效選擇性紅外吸收膜，從而可以提升吸收率並減少熱慣性。我們將通過實驗測量和數值模擬來研究各種因素對等離子體結構的光學行為的影響。初步分析表明有望在實現高回應率和回應速度的同時使感測器尺寸小於20微米，這將在高端紅外探測領域具備競爭力。該新設計的潛在應用領域是在需要高解析度熱輻射或者溫度檢測方面的應用，如熱成像，夜視儀和生物檢測。

16214217.label: Realisation of objectives
16214217.value: Mr. Gongze Liu and Mr. Yang Li were admitted as PhD students to work on the project. Dr. Dezhao Li was also involved in the infrared fabrication and characterization as a postdoc and he left HKUST in February 2019. Thereafter, Mr. Gongze Liu continued to work on the project. Mr. Li conducted numerical simulations to design the selective infrared absorber. He received his PhD degree at HKUST in August, 2019. We have conducted numerical simulations to predict the performance of the infrared sensors consisting of SiGe nanopillars. The finite-element simulations for both steady-state and transient responses were conducted to predict the behavior of the pillar-based sensor with selected design parameters, including the temperature distribution, voltage output and thermal response. Meanwhile, analytical models have been built to predict the responsivity, relaxation time, detectivity and noise-equivalent temperature difference (NETD). The predictions from the analytical model and numerical simulations were compared to improve the analytical model. Thereafter, the improved analytical model was used to design sensors for different applications and the sensitivity analysis was also conducted to reveal the most important factors that influence the performance of the infrared sensors. A compact multiband selective absorber will be helpful in improving the response time and the signal to noise ratio. We have developed a multilayer selective absorber that shows strong selective absorption in the three major infrared windows, which is a hierarchical structure consisting of an impedance-matched structure, a quarter wavelength structure and a gradient refractive index structure. A lithography-free fabrication process flow compatible with standard IC fabrication processes has been developed based on the self-ensembling formation of SiOx nano forest. The fabrication flow process for SiGe-nanopillar-based sensors was developed. Process recipes for each step were tested. Two key steps are the definition of SiGe nanopillar and the top metal connections. Accurate definition of SiGe nanowires is important for the achievable maximum performance while the top metal connection determines the yield of the device and the noise level of the sensor. For nanopillars with a diameter larger than 800 nm, traditional photolithography technique were used to define the pattern. But for nanopillars with a diameter thinner than 800 nm, nanofabrication techniques based on nanoimprinting were used. Meanwhile, the recipe for the metal connection was tested to reduce the contact resistivity with SiGe. Based on the optimized design, we successfully fabricated thermoelectric sensors with SiGe pillars of diameters ranging from 1 micron to 300 nm. According to the international standards for the infrared sensor characterization, we have developed an infrared measurement platform, which comprises a blackbody radiation source, a vacuum chamber, an optical chopper and a set of data acquisition system. This platform was calibrated using commercial infrared sensors and can be used to characterize the responsivity, internal resistance, and response time of an infrared sensor. The other parameters could then be calculated based these two measured parameters. With the optimized device design and absorber structure, we developed the first thermoelectric infrared sensing structure based on vertically standing SiGe nanowires and the corresponding fabrication process. We successfully demonstrated the thermoelectric infrared sensors with selectively doped SiGe nanowires of 1 μm and 300 nm diameters, which have a size of 28×28 mm2 and a filling factor close to 100% and are the smallest thermoelectric infrared sensors reported in the literature. To overcome the micro contact issue between the electrodes and nanowires, special design of the nanowire base and tip connections was proposed and successfully implemented. Laser and blackbody radiation measurements were conducted to characterize the performance of the fabricated TE infrared sensors. The measured performance of devices with 1-μm-thick and 3-μm-long nanowires was very close to the theoretical prediction, with a responsivity reaching 160 V/W and a response time shorter than 3 ms, which is the shortest response time for thermal infrared sensors and may enable high-speed infrared detection using thermoelectric sensors. Meanwhile, the devices with 300-nm-thick nanowires show a rising response time of 4 ms, a falling response time of 9 ms, and a responsivity of 4000 V/W (almost 100% higher than theoretical prediction), achieving both high spatial and temporal resolutions as well as a high responsivity. The thermal contact resistance may be responsible for the observed abnormally high responsivity.

16214217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16214217.value: High-performance low-power uncooled infrared sensors are widely demanded in many emerging markets including smart phone, automobile, gas sensing and monitoring systems. Compared to traditional bolometers, uncooled thermoelectric sensors are the most suitable solution for low-power applications due to their passive nature, high stability, high dynamic range and low cost. However their low responsivity, slow response and large size hinders the wide applications of thermoelectric sensors. In this project we developed a high-performance infrared sensors with a size as small as 28*28 micron^2 based on vertical freestanding IC-compatible SiGe micropillars with diameters down to 300 nm instead of the traditional planar design, which leads to fast response, high responsivity and easiness of integration. Compared with current commercialized thermopile sensors, the developed sensors are about 100 times smaller while providing a much faster response and higher responsivity, overcoming the shortcomings of traditional thermoelectric infrared sensor design and showing great potential for those applications requiring extremely low power consumption and low cost.
