16214617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16214617.value: Materials with nano- and micro-scale structures have important applications in many engineering disciplines such as tissue engineering, computing, diagnostics, advanced functional materials, and chemical processing. To obtain the desired functionality and to avoid defects, the manufacture of such materials requires precise control over the formation of tiny structural features. Currently, ‘top-down’ lithographic methods are commonly used to fabricate well-defined small-scale structures. However, lithographic methods suffer from high investment costs and fundamentally limited spatial resolution. As a result, ‘bottom-up’ self-assembly processes have been widely investigated. Self-assembly is the spontaneous association of molecules or small particles into structures that is driven by non-covalent interaction forces. Self-assembly has great potential as a manufacturing technology as it proceeds spontaneously and, if the interaction forces can be well controlled, it allows for up to molecular spatial resolution. Future manufacturing processes based on self-assembly will need to be equipped with suitable automated process controls to compensate for design uncertainty and to reject disturbances. Two challenges in the development of the automated control of self-assembly processes are stochastic behavior and kinetic trapping. Consequently, self-assembly as a paradigm for material synthesis is currently severely limited, despite its great potential. The overall objective of this research is to develop novel automated process control strategies for ‘directed’ self-assembly. Suspended microspheres are proposed as an experimental model system. They are introduced into a small cell that contains patterned micro-electrodes. Preliminary data obtained in our pilot study demonstrate how such particles can be self-assembled under the influence of different types of interaction mechanisms, which can be easily manipulated by varying the electric field properties. The first objective of this research will be to characterize such interaction mechanisms as functions of electric field properties. The second objective will be to investigate a ‘multi-resolution control’ approach for systematic self-assembly of ‘non-periodic’ structures. The multi-resolution approach can be implemented as an open-loop control strategy (i.e., without real-time observation) or as a closed-loop control strategy. In the latter case, real-time observations and online image analysis provide feedback to the electric field properties based on the actual state of the process. The third objective of this research will be to design several feedback controllers for ‘directed’ self-assembly processes. Over the long term, this research will provide a technology platform for self-assembly as a novel strategy for synthesizing structured materials in high-tech and chemical industries. 具有納米微米尺度結構的材料在諸如組織工程，計算機運作，診斷，先進性功能材料，化學加工等許多工程領域有著重要的應用。為了可以獲得理想的材料功能以及避免材料結構缺陷，在生產這樣的材料時需要對一些微小結構特徵的形成有著精確的掌控。目前，“自上而下”（top-down）的平版印刷（lithography）技術被普遍用於製造小尺度的結構。可是平版印刷方法面臨著高成本和精度受限的問題。於是，“自底向上”（bottom-up）的自組裝過程已經開始被廣泛研究。自組裝過程是指分子或一些小的顆粒自發的結合在一起而形成特定的結構。這個過程是由非共價的相互作用力驅動的。自組裝在製造技術領域有著巨大的潛力因為它的自發性以及在相互作用力可以被比較好的控制下可以到達分子尺度的分辨率。 未來基於自組裝的生產過程需要裝備合適的自動化控制來彌補設計中的不確定性以及抵抗過程中的干擾。發展自組裝過程的自動化控制中存在的兩個挑戰是自組裝過程的隨機行為和動力學陷阱。因此，自組裝用作材料加工生產目前還是有著很大的局限性。 這項研究的總體目標是為定向自組裝開發新型的自動化控制方案。微球被使用當作模型系統。這些小球被引入到一塊狹小的，有著微米圖案結構的電極的空間。我們研究的初步資料顯示了在不同的相互作用機理下這些小球是如何自組裝的。這些不同的作用力可以被操控通過改變電場的性質。 這項研究的第一個目標將是表徵這些作用機理為電場性質的函數。第二個目標是研究一個“多分辨率控制”（multi-resolution control）方法來系統地自組裝非週期性結構。實施多分辨率方法可以通過開環控制（也就是沒有實時觀測）或者閉環控制。在後者中，基於過程的當前狀態，實時觀測和線上的圖片分析能夠給電場性質提供反饋。第三個目標是為定向自組裝過程設計反饋控制器。 從長遠的角度，這項研究為自組裝提供了一個技術平台，讓它可以在高科技和化工產業中作為一個新型策略來合成有著特定結構的材料。

16214617.label: Realisation of objectives
16214617.value: The first research objective was to characterize the different interaction forces in the proposed self-assembly system, which was achieved through a combination of experiments and simulations. An experimental device was fabricated mainly according to the descriptions provided in the original proposal (see item C1 for details). Furthermore, multi-physics simulations using the COMSOL Multiphysics® Modeling Software package have been conducted. The following electrokinetic phenomena were induced experimentally using patterned electrodes by changing the applied field frequency: 1. Electro-osmotic flow (EOF) at a low field frequency (~1 kHz) 2. Positive dielectrophoresis (pDEP) at an intermediate field frequency (60-90 kHz) 3. Negative dielectrophoresis (nDEP) at a high field frequency (> 160kHz) We have characterized experimentally the impact of voltage and frequency on the particle interactions that were relevant for the proposed multi-resolution control approach. The multi-physics simulations predicted the norm of the electric field strength in the device, which we compared with the experimental motion of the particles to characterize the type and impact of the electrokinetic phenomena. EOF caused the particles to self-assembly at the center of the electrodes (i.e., towards the local field minimum). pDEP caused the particles to move to the edges of the electrodes (i.e., towards the field maximum). Finally, nDEP caused the particles to self-assemble at the center of the photoresist (i.e., at the electric field minimum). Generally, the characterized electrokinetic phenomena showed sufficient flexibility to direct the self-assembly in a non-invasive way. The second objective involved the development of the multi-resolution control approach without feedback control. A basic implementation of the multi-resolution control approach involved a first step to create the desired density followed by a second step for particle alignment. To achieve this, several innovations have been developed. First, we fabricated a new type of microfluidic device that exhibited multiple electrodes that could be operated independently. We designed a sequence of lithographic steps that involved edging of the ITO to create electrodes that can be operated independently and patterning of photoresist atop of the ITO electrodes. The electrodes were connected to a function generator providing an AC signal in the range of 0.1V to 10V and a frequency in the range of 1kHz to 1MHz to apply AC electric fields over the microfluidic cell. An optical microscope equipped with a digital camera was used to continuously monitor the particles in the cell. Second, a novel control framework was developed that directed the self-assembly system through four different states to achieve a set particle density distribution between two neighboring regions. In short (please see item C3 for details), nDEP was first induced, which directed the particles towards the center of the two neighboring regions where an electric field minimum was found. Next, the voltage of the actuator in one region was increased and the voltage of the actuator in the neighboring region was decreased. This control action changed the location of the electric field minima, which caused the particles from one region to move closer to a center actuator in between both regions. Subsequently, EOF was generated using the center actuator, which directed the particles toward this center actuator for collection. Finally, nDEP was induced again to direct the particles from the center actuator to one of the regions. The specific electric field properties were optimized using the multi-physics simulations, mainly to avoid undesirable particle movements such that the particle density distribution ultimately converged to a desired set point. The control framework effectively enabled the transfer of particles between neighboring regions so that a desired density distribution could be achieved, which was the key technological principle of the multi-resolution approach to enable defect-free assembly of non-periodic structures. Experimental validation was achieved through successful implementation of the control framework in the microfluidic device. Third, a mechanistic model was developed to predict the optimal dynamic operation of the control framework. The multi-physics simulation was used to predict the electric field and the fluid flow field as function of operating conditions when EOF was the dominant electrokinetic phenomenon, which was used in combination with a force balance to predict the particle motion (see item C4 for details). The zeta potential of the electrode surface was the only parameter that needed to be fitted to experimental data. The dynamic model predicted the required time to transfer a specific number of particles between the regions, which permitted operation of the proposed scheme as an open-loop control approach. The mechanistic model was validated with experimental data from the microfluidic device. The third research objective involved the development of closed-loop control strategies to improve the performance of the multi-resolution control approach. To achieve this objective, several innovations have been developed. First, a novel closed-loop strategy for particle alignment has been developed, which constituted the final step of the multi-resolution approach. The novel design of the microfluidic device enabled the use of nDEP to direct the particles to areas where electric-field minima were present, which were created by patterning photoresist stripes on top of the ITO electrodes. A proportional-integral (PI) feedback controller was used for the alignment to obtain a structure with a set level of defects using voltage as the manipulated variable. An optical microscope with a digital camera and image analysis was used to continuously monitor the particles in the cell. The microfluidic device was integrated with a function generator and MATLAB such that electric field properties could be applied as inputs to the microfluidic cell automatically so that automated control could be achieved. Initially, we used an on/off type of controller for controlling the particle density as the first step of the multi-resolution approach before the alignment control step was executed. Adequate control for implementation of a basic scheme of the multi-resolution approach could be achieved with such simple controller. This controller was later extended to a PI controller, which has the potential for better performance. However, self-assembly systems typically exhibit non-linear behavior. Therefore, the tuning of a PI controller that performs well over a broad range of operating conditions is challenging. To address this problem, we have developed a novel gain-scheduling approach for the feedback controller of the density control step step. In such approach, the tuning parameters of the PI controller are adjusted depending on the applied electric field properties to schedule the optimal tuning parameters. An empirical model was developed from open-loop experimental data to estimate the process gain of the system from which the controller gain was derived using the internal model control tuning rules. Subsequently, the novel gain-scheduling control approach was implemented experimentally, and its performance was compared to the conventional PI controller (see item C2 for more details). Finally, we have extended the novel control framework to obtain a specific particle density distribution between two neighboring regions with feedback control. The overall structure of the framework was not altered, but the scheme was augmented with a feedback control loop in which time was the manipulated variable and the number of particles that were collected on the center electrode during the collection step was the controlled variable. The technical implementation of the feedback control loop in this part of the research was similar as the implementation of the feedback control loop for particle alignment discussed earlier. The performance of the approach was characterized experimentally with set-point tracking experiments.

16214617.label: Major findings and research outcome
16214617.value: We have developed new insights into the interaction forces between microspheres during electric-field-assisted self-assembly in a microfluidic device and exploited those interactions for control. We developed a novel automated control strategy for particle alignment, which was enabled by several technical innovations. We have developed a novel design for the device and its fabrication method, which was characterized by edged ITO electrodes with photoresist patterned on top. Furthermore, we developed a basic strategy for the implementation of the proposed multi-resolution approach. The electric field could be shaped such that first an optimal particle density around the target electrode was achieved followed by particle alignment. Both steps were under feedback control. Experimental validation demonstrated robustness of the approach with respect to initial condition, which is important as the initial condition is random due to the Brownian motion. Furthermore, we found experimentally that the level of defects was less when implementing the multi-resolution approach compared to a single step approach in which the particle density was not under feedback control. Since the particles assemble at the center of such stripes due to the shape of the non-uniform electric field, a higher resolution of the final structure can be obtained with the directed self-assembly approach compared to the resolution of the edging of the photoresist itself, which is a fundamental benefit of bottoms-up self-assembly. Furthermore, any specific non-periodic structure can in principle be obtained through this method by patterning the photoresist stripe(s) in a desired pattern. Please see reference C1 for further details. Self-assembly systems typically exhibit strongly nonlinear behavior. To improve the control of the particle density in the multi-resolution approach, we have developed a novel nonlinear control approach to directed self-assembly. The approach schedules the controller gain in real-time based on an empirical model, which is a novelty for the application of directed self-assembly. The gain-scheduling approach showed superior performance compared to a standard PI feedback when implemented experimentally in a microfluidic device. Please see reference C2 for further details. Finally, we have developed a novel control framework for controlling a particle density distribution between neighboring regions. The experimental results demonstrated the flexibility of this approach for shaping these density distributions from set-point tracking experiments. Finally, the incorporation of a model allowed for this framework to be operated in a fully open-loop mode, which is important when real-time observation is not feasible. Please see references C3 and C4 for further details.

16214617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16214617.value: This research has opened several new directions for future research. All the developed methods can in principle be applied to other self-assembly systems because the exploited electrokinetic phenomena are generic. For example, biological cells exhibit similar behavior so that they can be self-assembled with electric fields to form structures for biochemical applications. We have conducted some preliminary work in that direction with yeast cells that can be immobilized after self-assembly with promising results. Furthermore, there is opportunity to further extend on the modeling work. First, the empirical models developed in the project can be benchmarked against extended mechanistic models, which are currently under development in our group. Such models use force balances on the particles to predict their motion as a function of a wide range of electric-field properties. Second, probabilistic models can be developed, which explicitly consider randomness so that robust control strategies can be developed. Those novel mechanistic and possibly probabilistic models can be used for model-predictive control strategies. The development and validation of such approach is currently ongoing and expected to be a topic of a follow-up publication. These promising directions for future research are most suitable for follow-up GRF applications due to their fundamental research character.

16214617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16214617.value: Advanced materials with specific small-scale structural features are important for many engineering applications within areas such as computing, diagnostics and healthcare. Self-assembly refers to the spontaneous association of particles into ordered structures, which is attractive for the manufacture of such advanced materials. However, the potential occurrence of defects is currently a limitation. Externally applied electric fields can be used to direct the self-assembly of the small particles. This research has developed a novel approach for using such electric fields in a systematic way to direct the self-assembly toward a target structure. The approach first controls the local particle concentration to make defect-free structures attainable and then employs a novel method to align the particles precisely in a desired pattern. A key feature of the approach is the use of so-called feedback control, which refers to the ability of the system to shape the electric field properties based on microscopic observations or predictions from mathematical models in real-time in such a way that a target structure is always obtained. The entire method can be automated and works even when the initial position of the particles is unknown. The developed methodology is generic and can, therefore, be applied to various materials.

16214817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16214817.value: The spread of mobile devices and the variety of communication technologies such as WiFi- direct and Bluetooth empower mobile users to interconnect, interact and form opportunistic networks, known as OppNets. OppNets are a special type of ad hoc network that are formed by mobile devices joining and leaving the network dynamically and communicating and exchanging resources opportunistically. Cellular networks, in contrast, are composed of cellular towers with specific and powerful hardware placed in strategic locations that allow mobile devices to connect to them and thus connect with others or access information from the Internet. OppNets, by being self-organizing, have many structural differences from the conventional infrastructured networks. The deployment of OppNets compared with infrastructured networks lack geographical scalability. Hybrid OppNets that are composed of mobile devices, WiFi access points and cellular towers can function on a metropolitan area scale, but they have to be properly designed and configured. Various research proposals concerning such topics as traffic offloading, content caching, computation offloading, context aware applications, micropayments and disaster management applications have been based on hybrid OppNets. However, in such cases, the functionality of the cellular towers and WiFi access points has been limited to the simple store and forward operation. Further, these proposals have often been only partially evaluated and mainly using simulators. Scalability is one of the most important characteristics that determines the quality of the proposed algorithms and architectures of OppNets. It depends on parameters that are contained within the respective proposals and that describe their ability to handle growing demands. There is a gap yet to be filled: a big data driven approach that will evaluate the scalability of OppNets and, given knowledge about the fixed infrastructure and mobile users’ statistics, will describe how hybrid OppNets can function on the scale of a metropolitan area. In the proposed study, we will analyze two mobile big data datasets that contain information regarding the mobile device usage and the Internet browsing behaviour of mobile users and we will build a framework that models OppNet scalability based on a number of input (e.g. mobility, topology) and output metrics (e.g. throughput, routing table storage, end to end delay). This will be applied to a range of existing OppNet proposals to understand the tradeoff between these different measures of scalability. Based on our findings, we will then design, implement and evaluate a novel approach that can be configured to optimize on any scalability metric. 移動設備的普及以及各種通信技術的快速發展，如WiFi直連技術和藍牙技術，使得移動用戶得以互聯與交互，並進一步形成機會網絡(opportunistic networks, OppNets)。機會網絡是一種特殊類型的自組織網絡，其由移動設備互聯組成。其中的移動設備可以動態地接入和離開網絡，設備間的通信和資源的交換都建立在動態的機會連接上。另一方面，蜂窩網絡由具有特定和強大硬件的蜂窩基站組成，其基站被部署在重要位置並允許移動設備通過基站與其他設備連接並接入互聯網。與由基礎設施構成的網絡(如蜂窩網絡)不同，機會網絡為自組織網絡，其部署缺乏在地理上的可擴展性。雖然目前由移動設備，WiFi接入點和蜂窩基站組成的異構混合機會網絡可以在較大規模的城市范圍中得以應用，但其必須進行准確的設計與配置。目前有許多研究基於異構混合機會網絡，例如流量分流，內容緩存，計算遷移，上下文感知計算，微支付和災難管理等。在這種情況下，蜂窩基站與WiFi接入點的功能僅限於簡單的存儲與轉發操作。但是，現有的研究通常僅僅局限於理論仿真而不具有實踐意義。可擴展性描述了網絡處理不斷增長的需求的能力，是體現所提出的網絡算法與架構的優越性的重要指標之一，其主要取決於所以出的每個方案中的具體參數。通過移動大數據可以得知關於移動設備、蜂窩基站與接入點的統計信息，以此來評估機會網絡的可擴展性可彌補理論仿真與實際應用的差距，並可以進一步描述異構混合機會網絡如何在大規模城市中得以應用。 在本方案中，我們將研究移動大數據的數據集並構建出一個基於多輸入（如用戶移動性與拓扑結構和多輸出(如吞吐量，路由表存儲，端到端時延)的分析架構。這將被應用於評估目前所提出的機會網絡的架構與算法，比較不同方案的可擴展性並在不同的性能指標間取得權衡。基於我們的發現，我們將設計、實施和評估一種可以配置為優化任何可擴展性指標的新方法。

16214817.label: Realisation of objectives
16214817.value: Considering the four objectives of this project, we analyzed the mobile big datasets we have access to, examined the scalability factors of OppNets, and implemented the proposed framework. As a result, all objectives have been met successfully. In more detail: Analyzing the two aforementioned big datasets helped us better understand the long-term users' behavior in mobile applications and their mobility in urban environments. Our main findings with the first dataset show the importance of mobile application usage to predict and understand users' behavior. For example, according to the time of the day and the user's location, the mobile application usage will be different. Therefore the network requirements will change accordingly (e.g., faster speeds to download big files or fewer response times to play online games). This behavior can provide useful implications for app developers, market intermediaries, and service providers to design systems according to the users' application usage patterns. The second dataset gives us several insights regarding the individuals' urban mobility and how the future of vehicular networks can be designed. These mobile patterns allow us to propose several works where we implement different algorithms for the future of vehicular mobility. For example, collaborative approaches using edge-computing devices can leverage anomaly detection systems to predict traffic jams and, therefore, provide more efficient directions to drivers and autonomous cars within the city. We published an article titled "D2D Task Offloading: A Dataset-Based Q&A" in IEEE Communications Magazine (a technical magazine with high visibility), where we introduced two datasets and collected data from mobile users to examine the features of sophisticated device-to-device interactions (e.g., task offloading). Moreover, we published an article with the title "Measurement and Analysis of the Swarm Social Network With Tens of Millions of Nodes" in IEEE ACCESS. We conducted a data-driven study to get a comprehensive picture of the whole Swarm social network. This work provides a deep analysis of social interactions between Swarm users and reveals the relationship between social connectivity and check-in activities. Furthermore, towards the understanding of OppNets, we published an article on Physical Review with the title "Universal principles governing multiple random searchers on complex networks: The logarithmic growth pattern and the harmonic law" and an article in Chaos with the title "Predicting search time when hunting for multiple moving targets: A recursive harmonic law". Moreover, the latter dataset leverages several other works in the human-computer-interaction field, such as augmented reality (AR). AR applications can allow drivers to augment their view of the road with useful information such as GPS directions, collision detection that can improve not only the user experience but the safety of the road. These AR-based works published during this grant's duration show the importance of AR interfaces and the interaction methods (mid-air finger-based approaches) to control such interfaces, e.g., ring multimodal device. Towards implementing parts of the proposed framework, we published "CARS: Collaborative Augmented Reality for Socialization" in ACM HotMobile 2018, "Talk2Me: A Framework for Device–to–Device Augmented Reality Social Network" in IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications (PerCom) 2018, and "CIRCE: Real-Time Caching for Instance Recognition on Cloud Environments and Multi-Core Architectures" and "Jaguar: Low Latency Mobile Augmented Reality with Flexible Tracking" in ACM Multimedia 2018. We did not encounter any problems, nor did we deviate from the original plan.

16214817.label: Major findings and research outcome
16214817.value: The analysis of two mobile big datasets has been the source of several major findings regarding the mobility and scalability of OppNets. Vehicular communication applications, be it for driver-assisting augmented reality systems or fully driverless vehicles, require an efficient communication infrastructure for timely information delivery. Decentralized approaches such as OppNets overcomes the limitations of centralized approaches regarding latency and opens many possibilities for vehicular communication applications such as vehicle-to-vehicle and vehicle-edge. Decentralized deployments of edge computation nodes on the roadside combined with collaborative and context-aware computation allow low-latency communications to detect and inform nearby drivers of unsafe behaviors in real-time. This distributed approach overcomes other centralized models improving the detection of potential accidents and the scalability of the network according to the number of vehicles. The combination of edge nodes and collaborative and context-aware computation can scale in dense areas such as Shenzhen, a megalopolis of 12 million inhabitants with over 2 million concurrent vehicles at peak hours. The usage of mobile applications can have an impact on the requirements and features of OppNets. The long-term evolution of application usage exhibits a decline in the diversity of app-category, and the app usage shows the domination of a small group of apps. The identification of such behavior can shape the requirements of OppNets to provide a scalable and efficient interconnection of mobile users. To support the network requirements of OppNets, we propose several frameworks to optimize routines tasks (instance recognition) and low latency for mobile applications such as AR. We propose a real-time cache of instance recognition to support the requirements of OppNets. We propose the framework CIRCE, a similarity caching framework for IR applications. In CIRCE, query image codes and the corresponding results are stored into a cache structure in order to answer similar future IR tasks. The widespread use of AR solutions for mobile application and vehicular scenarios have pushed the research towards more efficient and less cumbersome interaction techniques to visualize and manage augmented information. Several works have been published in the human-computer interaction field to propose better interaction approaches for AR applications (e.g., Force9, Exploring visualization for virtual keys). Finally, privacy is an important aspect also for OppNets and the proliferation of smart devices such as wearables. The proposed framework allows users to share information in a decentralized manner while providing some privacy protection techniques (e.g., face identification) to share information only with desired recipients.

16214817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16214817.value: Developing data-driven OppNets leads to several new research questions and directions. First of all, developing such large-scale opportunistic networks can be used to model the propagation of infectious diseases, e.g., Covid-19. At the micro-level, the basis of infectious disease spread is an opportunistic communication, that is, the chance encounter of individuals in urban space. Based on big data of mobile behavior, we can combine the records of accidental encounters into our developed opportunistic network for dynamic evolution. As we have seen with the major outcomes of our work, the future of vehicular networks and mobility in cities will be a pillar in developing the future of smart cities. The visualization of information in such big data scenarios can be leveraged using AR as it is gaining increasing attention from both academia and industry. These connected cities can drive new developments in human interaction, emphasizing AR-driven interaction. Several under-explored issues in the Human-City Interaction and input techniques warrant further research, such as visualization of big-data-related information in constrained interfaces and embodied interaction for AR devices.

16215717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16215717.value: The allocation of scarce public resources is always an important yet challenging question. Examples include assignment of public housing, education opportunities, immigration visas, outdoor recreation, and access to medical resources, etc. Currently, there are three main approaches: (1) Price mechanism (e.g., auctions), (2) Non-price mechanism (e.g., lotteries and queues) and (3) Hybrid mechanism (combinations of both price and non-price mechanisms). Auctions are the most commonly used price mechanism. They are efficient and revenue based, helping price determination and improving the welfare of society as a whole. Lottery is a non-price mechanism that allocates everyone an equal chance of winning regardless of the value they place on the goods. By contrast to auctions and lotteries, which only consider efficiency or equity, a third approach combining both price and non-price mechanisms balances the tradeoff between efficiency and fairness. Based on these three approaches, several mechanisms have been developed and implemented in practice such as first-price auctions, Vickrey auctions, lotteries, lotteries with reserved price, first auction then lottery, simultaneous auction and lottery. As social planners face an increasing number of options when allocating resources, a theoretical framework is needed to compare the performance of the different methods in terms of economic efficiency and social fairness. Then our key question is to find the optimal allocation mechanism which maximizes efficiency for any given equality constraints or vice versa. The goals of the proposed research are three-fold. (1) To analyze current public resource allocation mechanisms. (2) To develop a theoretical framework to unify different mechanisms from all three approaches and compare them in terms of efficiency and fairness. (3) To develop formal theories to find the optimal allocation policy, which is incentive compatible, efficient, equity-guaranteed, and easily implemented. The proposed research will be the first comprehensive study of public resource allocation that targets the dual objectives of price efficiency and social fairness using a game theory approach. Because of the nature of this problem, it has drawn substantial attention from both practitioners and academic researchers worldwide. The theoretical framework developed in this research will serve an important role in developing public resource allocation policies, and has the potential to make a significant contribution to resource allocation, general auction theory and game theory. The research will also have a significant impact on Hong Kong, a big city with a large population and limited resources. 稀缺的公共資源的分配一直是一個重要而具有挑戰性的問題。例子包括公屋，教育機會，移民簽證，戶外休閒，醫療資源的分配等。目前，分配主要基於三種方法：（1）價格機制（如拍賣），（2）非價格機制（例如抽籤和排隊）和（3）混合機制（價格和非價格機制的組合）。拍賣是最常用的價格機制。它是效率和收益導向的，能幫助價格確定和改善整個社會的福利。抽籤是一種非價格機制，可以為所有人提供平等的機會，但並不考慮同一商品分配給不同人可能帶來的不同的社會效益。與僅考慮效率或公平性的拍賣和抽籤相反，結合價格和非價格機制的第三種方法有效平衡了效率和公平性之間的權衡。 基於這三大類方法，在實踐中已經開發和實施了幾種機制，例如一級拍賣，二價拍賣，抽籤，先拍賣再抽籤，以及同時拍賣和抽籤等等。面對著各種不同的機制，在分配資源時到底如何選擇最優的機制，需要我們建立一個理論框架，從而來比較不同方法在經濟效率和社會公平性方面的表現。這個項目的關鍵問題就是要解決如何找到最優的分配機制，使機制在任何給定的約束條件下能達到效率最大化。 擬議研究的目標主要有三個。 （1）分析現有的公共資源分配機制。 （2）制定一個理論框架，將不同機制統一起來，從而在效率和公平性方面進行直接比較。 （3）基於裡論推導，找到最優的分配政策，兼顧激勵相容，有效性，公平性，及易實施性。 本項目將從博弈和機制設計的角度開展針對效率和社會公平的雙重目標的公共資源配置的綜合研究。 本研究開發的理論框架，將在發展公共資源配置政策中發揮重要作用，有可能對資源配置，一般拍賣理論，博弈論作出貢獻。這項研究亦會對香港這個人口眾多，公共資源有限的大城市產生積極的影響。

16216017.value: 與集成電子學不同，集成光子學不太成熟，正在探索將其應用從電信擴展到數據通信。已知光子技術以高效率有效傳輸大量數據。除了速度之外，通過光子而不是電子發送數據消耗更少的功率。因此，實現高效的器件和電路是集成光子學領域下一代信息技術和計算的最高優先事項之一。主要的挑戰之一是將光子與電子集成在同一個矽平台上，用於數據通信和處理。目前的集成光子系統都是基於矽或基於復合的。前者可能是CMOS兼容的，但是包含由化合物半導體製成的用於發光體的集成有源器件一直是具有挑戰性的。已經努力將有效和高性能的有源器件結合到矽上以與Si光子學的無源器件和波導集成。迄今報告的大多數異構整合工作都使用了粘合技術。複合激光器在Si上的直接生長已被提出並嘗試。然而，通過直接異質外延生成的缺陷不允許高性能激光器的生長。限制在點內的輻射複合的量子點激光器不太可能受到生長缺陷的不利影響。因此，QD激光器是Si上集成光子學的潛在優秀發射極候選者。雖然Si光子學主要用於紅外傳統電信波長，但是具有更寬帶寬的較短波長也可以在片上或片上數據通信應用中獲得應用，因為最小化長距離光纖損耗可能不是最高優先級。 在我們的實驗室，我們在過去十年中為LED和晶體管開發了非常高質量的GaN/Si技術。這些器件的結晶質量已經通過各種材料表徵技術進行了驗證，並通過出色的器件性能證明。我們還展示了單片式GaN基晶體管和LED，實現了一種新穎的三端子壓控LED（HEMT-LED），可以以比分立LED更高的頻率進行調製。此外，我們已經成功開發了直接在矽上生長的長波長量子點（InAs）微型光盤激光器。在擬議的項目中，我們將在GaN / Si模板上開發InGaN量子點激光器。將製造光泵浦微盤激光器以優化增益介質。還將開發Si上的電泵浦激光器，以有效耦合到矽光子電路的其他部件。

16216017.value: All objects as listed have been achieved and reported in the literature. An investigation of self-assembled polar InGaN quantum disks (Qdisks) on c-plane sapphire substrates by metal-organic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD) is reported. The surface density and diameters of the Qdisks is approximately 1 ×1010 cm-2 and range from 60-75 nm, respectively. The exciton lifetime and the internal quantum efficiency (IQE) of uncapped Qdisks is determined to be 130 ps and 27%, respectively. The short lifetimes of these Qdisks suggests a reduction of the built-in fields in these polar InGaN Qdisks. With an optimized GaN capping layer grown by a two-step method, the optical properties of the passivated Qdisks are preserved.

16216017.label: Major findings and research outcome
16216017.value: An investigation of self-assembled polar InGaN QDs on c-plane sapphire and Si substrates by metal-organic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD) was carried out. The surface density and diameter of the typical truncated pyramidal QDs are approximately 1 E10 cm-2 and range from 60–75 nm, respectively. Time-resolved photoluminescence studies reveal a mono-exponential exciton decay with a radiative exciton lifetime of 480 ps for uncapped QDs. With an optimized GaN capping layer grown by a two-step method, a radiative exciton lifetime of 707 ps for the capped QDs is obtained. This short radiative exciton lifetime is much shorter than that for previously studied polar QDs and is even comparable with those grown along non-polar QDs, which is strong evidence of the reduction of built-in fields in these polar InGaN QDs. To improve the optical properties of InGaN QDs, novel vertically aligned and uniformly separated InGaN nanorods (NRs) underneath an InGaN QD active layer was achieved by selective lateral photoelectrochemical (PEC) etching. The mechanism of this PEC etching is examined in detail by characterizing it under different InGaN doping concentrations, potassium hydroxide (KOH) concentrations and etching times. A lateral etch rate of 80 nm/min was achieved for an n-type doping concentration of 1E19 cm-3 and a KOH concentration of 2.2 M. Raman measurements exhibit that around 210 MPa compressive residual strain is released for a GaN-based microdisk after 30 min PEC etching. In addition, the PL intensity of the InGaN QDs is enhanced by as much as 6 times after 30 min PEC etching. The magnitude of this increase is related to the increased light extraction efﬁciency due to additional light scattering from the InGaN NRs. GaN-based light-emitting diodes (LEDs) are important to lighting and display applications. We demonstrate green-emission (512 nm) InGaN QD LEDs grown on a c-plane sapphire substrate by MOCVD. The screening of the built-in ﬁelds in the QDs effectively improves the performance of QD LEDs. These high quantum efficiency and high temperature stability green QD LEDs are able to operate with negligible efficiency droop and with current density increased up to 106 A/cm2. Our results show that InGaN QDs may be a viable option to replace conventional quantum well devices. Furthermore, green InGaN QD microdisk lasers pivoted on a Si substrate with the lowest measured threshold at a record low of 76 W/cm2 at room temperature under continuous-wave optical pumping were studied. Vertically correlated stacking of well-separated InGaN QDs in a GaN matrix as the micro-cavity gain medium is achieved by MOCVD. A comparison of ~1 μm microdisk lasers with different sidewall roughnesses is demonstrated. The lasing threshold is improved from above 1 kW/cm2 to below100 W/cm2 by an improvement of the sidewall smoothness. Moreover, the cavity quality factor (Q-factor) is increased by three times. Our results provide new insights into QDs as the laser gain medium to obtain an ultra-low threshold.

16216417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16216417.value: Long known as the world’s factory, China has been a major growth engine driving the global economy for at least the past three decades. Less well known is the fact that a growing number of factories are struggling with the rising wages and acute shortage of workers. To counter this trend, local Chinese governments have drastically stepped up effort to promote the use of robots. However, robot penetration in parts manufacturing is currently less than 1/5 that of the auto industry, the traditional drive force for the automatic/robotic industry. This is because the automation scope of the parts manufacturing industry has exceeded that of the automobile industry. In part machining domain, although many independent machining processes have achieved nearly fully automation, i.e., CNC machining, programmed wire-electrode cutting (WE), electrical discharge machining (EDM), etc., amounts of workers are still involved in the production line to implement the supporting work which is beyond the ability of each automatic machining cell, such as picking up and placing, clamping, workpiece localization and transferring, etc. What is more, such non-machining manual work even takes more time than that in actual machining, which extremely drags down the overall machining efficiency. On this accounts, it is inevitable to realize robots displacing workers to perform the aforementioned manual work in parts manufacturing to improve the final productivity. Among these non-machining manual work, the most prominent problem is the workpiece localization which usually occupies 70%~90% of the preparation time (non-machining time). Thus, our research aims to propose an integrated solutions for totally automatic workpiece localization. We adopt a unified geometric theory of workpiece localization to deal with three types of workpiece localization, such as the general three-dimensional localization problem, the symmetric localization problem and the hybrid localization/envelopment problem. Several crucial problems are to be solved for the purpose of complete automation for implementing the workpiece localization, including sampling point determination, automatic sampling, symmetry extraction, etc..

16216417.label: Realisation of objectives
16216417.value: To realize unmanned localization for various workpieces of different shapes, we need to deal with the complexity of free-form surfaces and the surface measurement of these surfaces with CMM. Starting with a Computer-Aided Design (CAD) model, the path planning for free-form surface inspection needs to solve two major problems: which points on the surface should be measured and how to measure them, which is the first stage of our work. We developed a points sampling strategy for any free-form surface to sample a set of best-conditioned points for the localization algorithm and automatically measure these points using a CMM. The crux of measurement point determination is to seek a balance between measurement accuracy and time efficiency due to the obvious observation: higher measurement accuracy usually needs more measurement points but also longer inspection time. The methods of inspection point sampling are generally divided into two categories: geometric feature-based methods and adaptive methods. A uniform sampling strategy may probably suffice for relatively flat surfaces. However, for a complex surface, e.g., with highly varying surface curvature, it is more reasonable to sample the surface based on its complexity, such as the mean curvature-based method. Some hybrid approaches were developed to heuristically determine the sampling points on surfaces with different complexity levels by combining multiple sampling criteria, such as surface curvature, patch size, etc. Unlike feature-based point sampling methods, the adaptive point sampling methods are proposed from the point of view of reverse engineering. It first evaluates the deviation between the CAD model and a substitute surface, where the substitute surface is reconstructed from the predetermined sampling points. If the deviation is beyond a preset threshold, more sampling points are added accordingly. This process iterates until some stopping criteria are met. After the sampling points are determined, the next task is to design an effective collision-free probing path, mainly involving accessibility analysis and measurement sequence optimization. The accessibility analysis is to check whether a collision would happen during a measurement motion. Through accessibility analysis, all feasible orientations for the probe stylus approaching a measurement point could be found and often represented as a set, e.g., the concept of local accessibility cone and global accessibility cone. With the specified sampling points and their associated feasible approach orientations, another research topic is on how to reduce the non-measurement motion, which is actually a problem of finding an optimal sequence to pass through all the measurement points and is solved by a heuristic-based optimization strategy. After developing the algorithm, we collected a bunch of workpieces with different shapes, simulated the sampling point set generation and CMM path planning algorithms in Matlab. Then after programming the CMM control software through the CMM API, we finally have achieved real-time automatic CMM measurement of the automatically generated sampling points for an arbitrary workpiece. After acquiring a featured point set representing any workpiece, the next stage is to localize the workpiece is to extract the symmetry of the workpiece, and design the algorithm to register the point cloud to the CAD model of the workpiece. The workpiece can be either non-symmetrical, symmetric with one or more symmetry axes, or partial symmetric. We have treated the three cases separately. For an input CAD model, we will determine the symmetry information by randomly placing potential symmetry axes through the center of the model and evaluate the possibility of the part being symmetric. For the potentially partial symmetric parts, we will break the model into symmetric and non-symmetric pieces. For the general non-symmetric workpiece, we will apply the regular localization by using an efficient variation of the iterative closest point algorithm to find the Euclidean transformation in SE(3). The convergence will usually be achieved in several iterations. For localization of the symmetric workpiece, we will also input the symmetric axis/axes of the workpiece. Then we will find the transformation in only a subspace of the Euclidean space by disentangling the generation space composed of the symmetric axes. This operation will leave the transformation along the symmetric axes unattended and only focusing on the registration related to other symmetric axes. Then we deal with the partial symmetric workpieces and define this as the hybrid localization or an envelopment problem. The background of this kind of problem is generally when a workpiece is half machined, and the other half is going to be machined. So the unmachined part will envelop the ideal totally machined CAD model. For example, a mug-like workpiece consists of a cup and a handle, and a half-machined one may only have the symmetric cup machined, but the handle is going to be carved from a solid block. In this complex case, we will first apply the symmetric localization to the machined symmetric part (e.g., the cup), which will leave the rotation along the rotation axis of this part free. With this free rotation, we can then deal with the non-symmetric part to solve the envelopment problem. In the next step, we will let transformation be only in the left rotation subspace while keeping the already registered part still. We then iteratively transform in this limited rotation subspace, and if there’s an intersection of the unmachined part with the corresponding CAD, we determine if the intersection is an envelopment of the CAD. The transformation will be iteratively fine adjusted until it envelops the corresponding CAD part. We first evaluate our localization algorithms by designing CAD models and simulating point clouds with Matlab. According to the simulation experiment results, the convergence will usually be achieved in a short time. We then transplant the algorithm to C++ and combine it with our previous stage to place collected workpieces on the CMM machine, generate sampling points from the CAD, automatically sample the points using CMM, and try the localization algorithms with real sampled points clouds and the corresponding CAD model. Results show the performance of localization algorithms is robust. The last stage of the project is to build an integrated experiment platform that combines the vision-based grasping and placing system with millimeter accuracy. We’ve built a system to automatically localize any workpiece with the following steps: The workpiece can be put on either the desk or material shelf in any pose. With the help of a 3D camera and our vision-based localization algorithm, the system will get the information of the current pose of the workpiece. Then our smart robot gripper will pick up the workpiece and place it in the smart fixture. After the workpiece is fixed, the robot will take the fixture together with the workpiece to the CMM and inform CMM, three coordinate measurement machines to measure. The contact measurement and fine localization algorithm will further localize the workpiece to millimeter accuracy. We have tried different workpieces using this system and achieved millimeter accuracy. We also developed the user interface for real-time inspection.

16216417.label: Major findings and research outcome
16216417.value: We developed a points sampling strategy for any free-form surface to sample a set of best-conditioned points for the localization algorithm and automatically measure these points using a CMM. To balance the accuracy and time efficiency, we adopt a uniform sampling strategy for relatively flat surfaces. And for a complex surface, we sample the surface based on its complexity, such as the mean curvature-based method. We also developed algorithms to heuristically determine the sampling points on surfaces with different complexity levels by combining multiple sampling criteria, such as surface curvature, patch size, etc. The design of an effective collision-free probing path mainly involves accessibility analysis and measurement sequence optimization. The accessibility analysis is to check whether a collision would happen during a measurement motion. Through accessibility analysis, all feasible orientations for the probe stylus approaching a measurement point could be found and often represented as a set. The measurement sequence optimization is actually a problem of finding an optimal sequence to pass through all the measurement points and is generally solved by a heuristic-based optimization strategy. To localize the workpiece, we extract the symmetry of the workpiece and characterize them into three categories: non-symmetric, symmetric with one or more symmetry axes, and partial symmetric (envelopment). Then the input to the localization algorithm is the CAD model, the measured point cloud, and the axes for the symmetric and partial symmetric workpiece. For the non-symmetric workpiece, we apply the regular localization by using an efficient variation of the iterative closest point algorithm to find the Euclidean transformation. The convergence will usually be achieved in several iterations. For symmetric workpiece or symmetric part of partial symmetric workpiece, we find the transformation in only a subspace of the Euclidean space by disentangling the generation space composed of the symmetric axes. For the unmachined part of the partial symmetric workpiece, we keep the other part still and iteratively transform the unmachined part to envelop the corresponding CAD model. We finally built an integrated system that combines the vision-based grasping and placing system to automatically localize any workpiece lying on the desk in any initial pose. The 3D camera and our vision-based localization algorithm will firstly roughly localize the workpiece and inform the robot. Then the robot will place the workpiece onto the CMM machine to measure the point clouds and compute the localization information using the above-mentioned algorithms.

16216417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16216417.value: The algorithms and procedures of this project currently end only at the acquisition of the localization information of the workpiece. However, to further machine the workpiece, the current system in the industrial factories may not directly be compatible with this localization information. Thus the algorithms still have a gap between having actual effects in production. Therefore, there's a need to develop related algorithms for up-streams and down-streams production. For example, we can extend the current system to include a CNC machine: The localization information can be sent to the CNC machine. The CNC machine needs to modify its code correspondingly and cut the workpiece with the changed coordinate system. And after machining, the workpiece will be taken out by the robot and measured by CMM again for quality inspection. In this way, the algorithms developed in this project can be modified to satisfy different needs and further generalized to adapt to various production scenes.

16216417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16216417.value: Nowadays, workpiece localization has a significant role in the part manufacturing industry. For general part manufacturing, workpiece localization is always a rigid demand in between the processes of various machining such as milling, grinding, CNC machining, electric discharge machining, wire electric discharge machining, and polishing etc. However, due to the technology limitations, workpiece localization relies heavily on human resources to be manually done. Manual workpiece localization results in inefficiency, for it may take from half an hour to a whole day, depending on the workpiece and luck. Also, because of the terrible working environment, more and more people are unwilling to do this work. Though wages are rising, most factories are facing a shortage of workers. Therefore, our unmanned workpiece localization technology aims to solve this pain spot in the industry.

16216717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16216717.value: 鉛（Pb）是一種有毒的重金屬。長期攝取鉛可導致兒童的學習缺陷和令成人患上高血壓，兒童和孕婦最易受鉛的影響。若供水系統中配置了含鉛的部件，如管道，連接管道的焊料和其它配件等，鉛就可能釋出於食水中。研究顯示，即使在相當低的濃度下，鉛水仍會對健康構成不利影響。因此控制食水含鉛量至關重要，並應盡量將食水含鉛量保持在最低水平。 在人口稠密都市的高樓大廈供水系統中的鉛水濃度取決於眾多因素，包括鉛的源頭、用水時間、取樣方法、水管和配件的材料、食水水質，以及鉛在水流中的釋放和運輸等。現今還沒有對這類高層建築食水管網中的鉛釋放機理和運輸作出系統性的研究。 我們建議通過綜合的物理實驗和數值模擬，研究導致食水含鉛超標的機理。我們將設計和建造一個原尺寸的實驗室試驗模型，模擬食水在高層建築供水管線中的流動過程。在典型的流量和環境條件下，測量供水鏈部件中鉛的釋放率和濃度，並利用三維計算流體動力學模型來解釋測得的數據，以了解鉛在管線中的輸移和沉積。以及食水含鉛量的時空變化。 這項基本研究源於一項對香港公共房屋食水含鉛超標的實地調查。研究結果將為評估飲用水中鉛含量的健康風險和制定鉛污染控制措施提供科學依據，並有利於設計、維護城市供水服務。硏究數據將為香港的全方位水資源管理提供依據。

16216717.label: Realisation of objectives
16216717.value: Objective 1: The mechanism of lead leaching has been studied through systematic leaching experiments, experiments on prototype supply chains and galvanic corrosion experiments: A. Lead leaching tests Lead leaching experiments was performed on individual components (lead solder joints, brass fixtures and copper pipes with lead deposits) in both stagnant and flowing conditions. In the stagnant leaching tests, the lead-containing components were coupled with two copper pipe sections on either side. The specimen was fully flushed and filled up with tap water for stagnation for 0.5 to 24 hours, after that all water was collected for analysis of lead concentration to determine the total (dissolved and particulate) lead concentrations. The data reveal the non-linear built-up of lead concentration in water by diffusion, confirmed by 3D diffusion modeling. Dissolved lead is the dominated form of lead, accounting for 80-90% of total lead leached in stagnation. The leaching test data have been used to calibrate the equilibrium concentration for lead diffusion modeling in Objective 2. The details of the leaching experiments can be found in Chan et al. (2020, ES&T, under review). To study the lead leaching from components in flowing conditions, we have also carried out experiments on a recirculating flow system fabricated using lead-free components. A lead-containing component was installed on the system to measure the lead concentration resulted under a combination of recirculating flow periods and flow rates. Lead accumulates in the system with time; lead concentration increases sharply when flow velocity increased from 0.18 m/s to 0.35 m/s, indicating the sporadic nature pickup of particulate lead by the flow. B. Experiments on real life water supply chains With the support of Water Supplies Department (WSD), we carried out field experiments on full-scale test rigs resembling real-life residential water supply chains to study the tap water lead concentration under realistic water supply chains. The test rigs (length of ~20m) were re-assembled from lead-containing components dismantled from water supply chains from Public Rental Housing estate buildings, consisting of lead-soldered joints (elbows, sockets, tees), valves, water meters and faucets. Clean test rigs without the use of lead solder were also constructed with brass fixtures for control study. The water in the pipeline was first allowed to stand for 0.5-93 hrs to allow the diffusion of lead into water. Water samples were collected at multiple time intervals after the opening of the tap. Flow rates of 30-130 ml/s were used in the experiments to simulate the effect of flow velocity on lead release and transport. A total of about 400 samples were collected on experiments on three pipe rigs (one lead solder free). Lead concentrations were determined by Inductively-Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry (ICP-MS) by the accredited laboratory of the Health, Safety and Environment Office of HKUST and the WSD chemistry laboratory, with detection limit of 1 ppb. The measured time variations of Pb concentration were transformed into the distance from the tap using the flow velocity, revealing the locations of possible lead sources in the supply chain. Pb concentrations along the pipe generally increase with stagnation time but vary spatially in a complex manner. The experimental data were used for validating the numerical model in Objective 2. Selected components of the supply chain were extracted for stagnation leaching tests and dissected for examination of the crystal structure of lead deposits by Scanning Electron Microscope and Energy-Dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM/EDX), showing the lead carbonate deposits. The details of the experiments can be found in Chan et al. (2020) and Chang et al. (IAHR, 2019). C. Experimental study of galvanic corrosion In view of the importance of galvanic corrosion as a major mechanism for lead leaching, we have studied the electrochemical reactions of lead-solder joints. We have devised experiments to study the relationship between electric potential field, galvanic current, consumption of oxidants (residual chlorine, DO) and release of lead, using simulated lead solder joints. It is shown that galvanic corrosion induces a significant reduction of residual chlorine. The corrosion potential of lead deviates from its free corrosion potential, promoting the release of lead ions. The measured data are used for calibrating and validating an electrochemical model for galvanic corrosion. Details of the electrochemical experiments can be found at Chang et al. (under preparation). Objective 2 A. 3D Numerical modeling of lead leaching and transport A three-dimensional (3D) computational fluid dynamics (CFD) model is developed to predict lead accumulation in stagnation and its mixing and transport in flow conditions in the entire supply line. At the stagnant state, the leaching process can be described by the Fickian diffusion model, assuming that galvanic corrosion/lead scale dissolution results in a thin layer of constant equilibrium concentration E_0 next to pipe wall boundary. E_0 of soldered joints, brass valves and copper pipes with lead deposits were calibrated with measured lead concentration from stagnant leaching tests. The lead concentration distribution at the end of stagnation serves as the initial condition for lead transport modeling after tap-opening. (2) At the flowing stage, the steady-state continuity and momentum equations are solved with imposed discharge at upstream, providing the velocity field and turbulent diffusivity (solved using a two-equation turbulence model) for solving the unsteady lead concentration field by the advective-diffusion equation. The uniqueness of the 3D modeling is the full 3D velocity field is computed without the need for an assumed profile; hence shear dispersion of the distributed sources along the supply chain can be accurately simulated. The governing equations are solved numerically using an industry standard CFD code. The lead concentration variation at the consumer tap is validated with test-rig data on real-life water supply chains. The details of the numerical modeling can be found in Chan et al. (submitted to ES&T, under review) and Chang et al. (IAHR-APD, 2020). B. Galvanic corrosion modeling To study the galvanic corrosion mechanism on lead release, we proposed and developed an electrochemical modeling framework. When two dissimilar metals are electrically connected, both materials deviate from their free corrosion potentials, resulting in an electric current between them and accelerating the corrosion of anodic material (Pb). The electrons from the anode will be accepted by oxidants (e.g. residual chlorine, DO, Cu ions) on the surface of cathode (Copper). The potential field induced by lead-copper solder joint can be obtained by numerically solving the governing equation with the polarization curves at the surface of each material as boundary conditions. The corrosion current density distribution induced by the potential difference on the solder surface can be related to the lead release rate using the Faraday's laws of electrolysis, providing the strength of lead source in the diffusion modeling. The polarization curves of lead-tin solder and copper in tap water were measured by a three-electrode system with a potentiostat. Initial model predictions were validated with the measured data, showing a good comparison with the measured potential field. Details of the electrochemical model can be found at Chang et al. (under preparation). Due to the local social unrest in the second half of 2019 and the recent COVID-19 pandemic, the research progress on galvanic corrosion experiments and modeling has been delayed. The results are being summarized to conclude the study, expected to complete by the end of 2020.

16216717.label: Major findings and research outcome
16216717.value: This is the first experimental and theoretical study of lead contamination in water supply chains in densely populated high rise buildings with copper or non-lead pipes. The lead concentration at the consumer tap is successfully modelled by theoretical modeling, field sampling and laboratory experiments. The use of lead solder, causing elevated lead concentration in the residential water supply chains in the 2015 Hong Kong “lead water” episode is elucidated through systematic experiments. The lead concentration in stagnant leaching tests show non-linear increase with stagnation time, which can be reasonably predicted using the Fickian diffusion law with the equilibrium concentration at the wall boundary. The equilibrium concentration of copper pipe with lead deposits, brass fixtures and lead solder joints are in the order of 6, 260 and 1000 ppb respectively, which is related to the lead content of material and the corrosion mechanism (galvanic corrosion and/or dissolution of scales). The lead concentration in supply chains without lead-solder joints is below the WHO provisional guideline (10 ppb), induced by the brass components. The lead level at the consumer tap of real-life water supply chains with lead-soldered joints exceeds the WHO guideline value within a few hours’ stagnation, and can be affected by leaded components 20 meters away from tap. The 3D CFD model prediction of real-life water supply chains agree well with sampling experiment results, providing detailed time variation of lead concentration at consumer tap. The component material, the exposure area and the stagnation time determine the mass of lead released out. The flow velocity and pipe geometry (e.g. multiple bends) affects the turbulent mixing of lead clouds from the stand pipe outside the building to consumer tap. Galvanic corrosion of lead-solder joint was studied for the first time. The galvanic current measured in stagnant condition decreases with time, consistent with the leaching rate of lead. A local drop of residual chlorine and DO is observed in the proximity of the soldered joint, indicating rapid consumption of oxidants due to galvanic corrosion. Lead carbonate scales of cerussite and hydrocerussite are observed at the solder surface, which may be easily washed out by the flow. One journal paper has been submitted for review (Chan et al. 2020, ES&T) in a top international peer-reviewed journal with other works under preparation for submission. Two papers (Chang et al. 2019; 2020) have been published/accepted in conference proceedings of hydro-environment engineering research. One postgraduate PhD student has been trained under the project.

16216717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16216717.value: An electrochemical modeling frame work is proposed and developed for the leaching of lead in stagnation. The model solves the governing equation of electric potential field with polarization curves on the material surfaces as the boundary conditions. The corrosion current and the corrosion rate at the metal surface can thus be determined from the electric potential field. The diffusion of lead or other metals, residual chlorine and dissolved oxygen from the bulk water to the metal surface can be simulated using the diffusion equation. The model can be used to study the galvanic corrosion of metals in water supply chains subjected to advective-diffusion processes. More model validation will be required on measured galvanic current, potential field, and lead and oxidant concentrations. As lead-solder joints has been replaced in supply chains of affected buildings, the elevated lead level caused by brass components in the drinking water supply system is an emerging problem in recent years. The study of the mechanism of lead leaching from brass fixtures will be an increasingly important ssue of global importance – especially in view of the trend towards lowering the provisional guideline threshold of lead concentration from 10 ppb to 5 ppb. The CFD modeling also paves the way for other related studies - e.g. coupling the 3D model predictions with 1D models of the supply chain. Practical issues such as stochastic water demands, intermittent flows, and leaching rates can be addressed by calibrating a one-dimensional (1D) advective diffusion model against the 3D model calculations. The calibrated 1D models are well-suited for rapid assessment of various factors on health risks using Monte-Carlo simulations.

16216717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16216717.value: Lead is a toxic heavy metal that may be present in high-rise building household drinking water supply systems fitted with lead containing components, posing significant threats to public health. The lead concentration of drinking water at the consumer tap depends on many factors including the sources of lead, the method of sampling, pipe material and geometry, and water quality, and the interaction with the turbulent flow in the water supply chain networks. The mechanisms leading to excess lead in drinking water have been studied through comprehensive experiments on prototype water supply chains and mathematical modeling. The lead release rates of leaded components were measured under stagnant and flowing conditions. The lead leaching rate in stagnation can be well predicted using molecular diffusion theory with the equilibrium concentration assumption. Extensive sampling measurements were conducted on water supply chains of high-rise building households. The variation of lead concentrated measured at the tap can be reasonably simulated using a three-dimensional computational fluid dynamics model. Galvanic corrosion is determined as the dominant factor for lead release from solder joints, confirmed by electrochemical experiments and modeling. The findings provide insights into the health risk from lead in drinking water, suggest mitigation measures, and benefit the design and maintenance of water supply services in densely populated cities of developing countries with pressing demands on urban housing.

16300117.label: Project Objectives
16300117.value: To search for a magnonic topological material that is a cousin of electronic Weyl semimetals in which two bulk spin wave bands generically cross each other at points in momentum space (Weyl nodes) with linear dispersion relationships near the crossing points. The bands have non-trivial topological order (non-zero monopole charges) so that in the momentum-plane not containing Weyl nodes, spin waves are gapped in the bulk and gapless on surfaces. A fingerprint of such materials is that the equal energy contour near crossing points are arcs (Fermi arcs) on the sample surface. These arcs can be visualized by a density plot of magnon spectral function on the sample surface. To search for a magnonic topological material that is a cousin of electronic topological insulators in which the bulk spin waves are gapped while the magnonic bands have non-trivial topological order (non-zero Chern numbers) so that there are topologically protected gapless surface magnonic states (spin waves) that propagate unidirectionally. One could use such a magnonics topological material to make new functional magnonics devices such as spin wave beam splitters. It will be interesting to study the control of the beam splitters.

16300117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16300117.value: Topological states of matter have been studied intensively in recent years because of their exotic properties such as topologically protected surface chiral or helical states. The initial studies were exclusively for electronic systems, and topological states were believed to be a quantum phenomenon. It is now known that topological states can also exist in classical systems. Indeed, topologically protected edge states have already been found in mechanics and photonics. Despite active searches for topological states in many fields, studies of topological states in magnetism are rare although they are important and useful in magnonics such as spin wave transportation and manipulations based on the chiral nature of surface states. In this theoretical proposal, we will search for possible topological states in magnetic systems that are governed by either the quantum Hamiltonian or the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (LLG) equation. Magnonics or magnon spintronics is about the creation, detection, and manipulation of magnons that are the quanta of spin waves. Magnons are spin-1 particles whose motion generates a spin current, free from Joule heating, that can be used to encode and transmit information. Various magnon-based nanodevices such as the magnon-drag thermopile, spin-wave multiplexer, and magnon transistor have already been proposed and studied on the basis of normal spin wave properties. The emphasis of this proposal will be on two types of magnonic topological materials. One is similar to electronic topological insulators where spin waves have gapped bulk states and gapless topologically protected surface states. The second type is similar to the electronic Weyl semimetal where the bulk spin waves are linearly dispersed and cross at so called Weyl nodes. It is anticipated that magnonic topological materials can enhance the performance of magnonic devices, and even open doors for new functional magnonic devices because of the topologically protected chiral/helical states. 16300117.label: Realisation of objectives
16300117.value: We have investigated all areas proposed in this proposal, and have achieved our revised objectives. We clarified that topological phases are not privilege of quantum physics, it can also occur in classical world. In magnetic systems whose dynamics is govern by the highly nonlinear Landau-Lifshitze-Gilbert equation we showed magnonic topological insulators and magnonic Weyl semimetals and higher-order topological insulators can exists. We have clarified that topology in magnetics can be topological spin structures in real space and topological spin waves with well-defined momentum that is manifested as unidirectional propagating surface waves. One important topological spin structure is skyrmions. We have studied dynamics of skyrmions in disorders and explained experimental observation that skyrmion Hall angle can be enhanced by disorders. Also, we showed that Thiele equation can capture the skyrmion dynamics in disorders at very high accuracy. We derived a very accurate skyrmion size formula. We have also studied level spacing of disordered Weyl semimetal and found that they are described by Poisson distribution function, instead of Wigner-Dyson distribution. The surface states in the topological materials are robust against disorders and geometrical imperfections. We proposed topological magnonics, in which topological exchange spin waves are used as information carriers, that do not suffer from conventional problems of magnonic devices with additional nice features of nanoscale wavelength and high frequency. We showed that a perpendicularly magnetized ferromagnet on a honeycomb lattice is generically a topological magnetic material in the sense that topologically protected chiral edge spin waves exist in the band gap if a spin-orbit-induced nearest-neighbor pseudodipolar interaction (and/or a next-nearest-neighbor Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction) is present. The edge spin waves propagate unidirectionally along sample edges and domain walls regardless of the system geometry and defects. As a proof of concept, spin-wave diodes, spin-wave beam splitters, and spin-wave interferometers are designed by using sample edges and domain walls to manipulate the propagation of topologically protected chiral spin waves. Since magnetic domain walls can be controlled by magnetic fields or electric current or fields, one can essentially draw, erase, and redraw different spin-wave devices and circuitry on the same magnetic plate so that the proposed devices are reconfigurable and tuneable. The topological magnonics opens an alternative direction towards a robust, reconfigurable and scalable spin-wave circuitry.

We have also clarified that topology in magnetics can be topological spin structures in real space and topological spin waves with well-defined momentum that is manifested as unidirectional propagating surface waves. 16300117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16300117.value: One of important achievements in recent years in physics is the understanding of importance of topology in physics. Although topological structures are not new, such as magnetic domain walls in magnetism and various solitons in fundamental physics, topological surface states in topological insulators, superconductors, and topological semimetals are only the notion of recent years. In this project, we clarify that topological states are not the privilege of quantum physics. It can also exist in magnetic systems whose dynamics is govern by a nonlinear classical partial differential equation. We showed that many magnetic materials are magnonic insulators, high-order topological insulators, and magnonic semimetals. Their surface waves are good information carriers, and can be used to make useful magnonic devices because they are robust to disorders and imperfections. In this project, we have also derived a very accurate skyrmion size formula. Skyrmion size is a fundamental quantity. However, people do not have very good understanding of it before us although it has been studied for more than a decade with many very wrong results in the literature. Our formula provides a guide to people for searching smaller and stable skyrmions that is critical important in skyrmionics.

16300217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16300217.value: Many observable phenomena can be encoded in terms of objects such as graphs, matrices, trees or more general notions of networks, social or otherwise. In addition, relationships between individuals, or other entities, can be cluster-based, meaning individuals are separated into different classes by possession of a common single attribute; or feature based, where an individual may belong to several groups sharing some of the attributes of that individual. Relatively new technologies such as the Internet, and its various entities, including online social networks or shopping venues, in addition to data from mobile phones, present new challenges. With respect to data, the bulk of what we have described can be partly expressed in terms of some type of combinatorial structures. The uncertainty can be further quantified in terms of probabilistic mechanisms wherein various forms of statistical analysis can be applied. Using the parlance of statistical machine learning, one seeks basic generative models that should be relatively simple in a practical sense and allow for learning about uncertainties in the presence of incoming observations. This notion of sequential learning is very well suited to techniques that present themselves from the world of Bayesian statistics,, more precisely, Bayesian nonparametric statistics, which at its heart involves the calculus of various random measures in the presence of data. In other words, Bayesian updating. This framework, whose practical utility arises from modern advances in computer technology, has enjoyed many successes in machine learning in recent years. However, with such success has come the realization that more is needed in terms of development and identification of random measures, and suitable modifications of others that are more routinely employed, that make for more realistic and, indeed, implementable statistical procedures. An important component of our investigations, as in our past work, will be to continue to explore links with objects arising in related fields which are perhaps less concerned with the analysis of data. Specifically, we refer to phenomena arising in the area now collectively known as Combinatorial Stochastic Processes. This area connects path decompositions, and other properties, of processes such as Brownian motion with combinatorial structures linked to random partitions, multi0sets, trees and graphs. We, as well as others in the Bayesian nonparametric /Machine Learning statistical communities, have demonstrated in past work that such developments have proven to be quite important for developments of a more practical nature. 許多可觀察的現象可以用諸如圖形， 矩陣，樹或更廣泛的網絡概念，社會或其他方面。此外， 個人或其他實體之間的關係可以是基於群集的意思 個人通過擁有一個共同的單身分離成不同的階級 屬性;或基於特徵，其中個體可以屬於幾個組共享 那個人的一些屬性。相對較新的技術如 互聯網及其各種實體，包括在線社交網絡或購物場所 除手機數據外，還面臨新的挑戰。關於數據， 我們所描述的大部分可以部分地表現為某種類型 組合結構。不確定性可以進一步量化 可應用各種形式的統計分析的概率機制。 使用統計機器學習的說法，尋求基本的生成模型 這在實踐中應該比較簡單，並且允許學習 存在傳入意見的不確定性。這個連續的概念 學習非常適合從世界展示自己的技術 貝葉斯統計，更準確地說，貝葉斯非參數統計，其中心 涉及數據存在時的各種隨機措施的演算。其他 單詞，貝葉斯更新。这个框架的实际效用源于计算机的现代进步 技術, 近年來在機器學習上取得了很多成功。然而， 取得成功已經意識到在發展方面需要更多的工作 並確定隨機措施，並對其他人進行適當修改 更經常地就業，這使得更現實，更可實施 統計程序。我們調查的一個重要組成部分，就像我們過去一樣 工作中，將會繼續探索與相關領域相關的對象的鏈接 也許不太關心數據的分析。具體來說，我們提到現象 出現在現在統稱為組合隨機過程的區域。這個 區域連接路徑分解和其他屬性，如布朗型 運動與組合結構鏈接到隨機分區，multi-sets，樹和 圖表。我們以及貝葉斯非參數/機器學習中的其他人 統計社區在過去的工作中已經證明了這種發展 被證明對於更具實際性的發展來說是相當重要的。

16300217.label: Major findings and research outcome
16300217.value: While there are various results, we highlight three. 1. We obtain explicit tractable results in the form of stick-breaking representations for one of the most popular flexible classes of Bayesian nonparametric priors. Although this work has not been published yet. Some results from that investigation have been quoted and used in a recently published work by other authors. 2. Our work on the introduction and analysis of hierarchical latent feature models has, as an important component, indicators on how to sample and analyze for the first time multiple copies of popular (sparse) exchangeable graph models that have appeared in the recent literature. 3. Perhaps our most satisfying result is our work on Hierarchical Indian Buffet process (and its generalizations to spike and slab models). Our results provide explicit results for the HIBP, originally proposed in 2007, which now allows it to be practically implemented to wide range of applications. This includes for instance topic models involving multiple types of documents. We consider this a highly significant result.

16300217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16300217.value: Our work indicates extensions to the sampling, modelling and statistical inference for relational data structures that may be expressed in terms of multiple types of random graphs. Specifically we will explore further how to combine data from hypergraph and multi-plex networks which may exhibit sparsity. We believe that the results may be applied to to the study of some natural language processing models whose data structure may be represented as graphs. We anticipate applications to data structures arising in finance and e-commerce.

16300217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
