A byproduct of our work is that our analysis now allows for practical implementation of a variety of statistical models to real world data sets that involve sharing of information between and across groups. One my think of the analysis of various types of documents. That is to say, potential applications may be to topic models involving various types of documents, natural language processing, Poisson factorization models, random count matrix priors and neural network models. That is to say, applications to relational data structures arising for instance in finance, e-commerce, social networks, or genetic/biomedical studies.

16300617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16300617.value: 在石墨烯表面形成过渡金属原子的超晶格已经在理论上被预测是实现非平凡拓扑态的途径，包括量子自旋霍尔，量子反常霍尔和量子谷霍尔效应。正如2016年诺贝尔物理奖获得者所强调的那样，这些新现象不仅产生新的物理，而且在量子计算方面也有重要的技术应用前景。然而，在石墨烯上形成金属原子超晶格尚未在实验中实现。我们建议在石墨烯表面使用超分子自组装来实现这一设想。超分子自组装已被广泛用于在金属和石墨表面上形成周期性排列的金属原子结构。我们预计在适当的条件下，石墨烯之上也会发生类似的过程。我们将在石墨烯上沉积含有过渡金属中心的大环分子，将它们组装成具有金属晶格的有序超分子结构。这些晶格的对称性和晶格常数可以通过选择具有特定侧基的分子进行调整。下一步，我们将使用扫描隧道显微镜和光谱学来表征所制备的样品的结构和电子性质。我们将测量局部态密度，特别是在超晶格的边缘，探测非平凡边缘状态的特征。我们的两个合作组将使用角度分辨光电子能谱和密度函数理论来分析这些结构的能带结构。在第三部分，我们将在石墨烯器件上实现相同的结构，并且测量运输测量，并表征霍尔电导。

16300617.label: Realisation of objectives
16300617.value: Objective 1: Design and fabricate transition metal (Fe, Co, Ni, Ru, Pt, Ir, Cu or Au) adatom supercells on graphene. (1) We grew FePc films on monolayer and bilayer graphene substrates. (2) We designed and synthesized a Cu-adatom lattice on a Cu(111) substrate and (3) on a graphene substrate. (3) We designed and synthesized Fe, Co and Ni adatom lattices on Au(111) and Ag(111) substrate. Objective 2: Detect the signatures of the QAHE, in particular the edge states, using STS and resolve the band structure of the graphene decorated with the supercells using ARPES and DFT analysis. (1) We used STM to resolve the structures of the FePc, Cu, Fe, Co and Ni adatom lattices. (2) We used STS to probe the density of states of the adatom lattices. (3) We used DFT to study the band structure of the adatom lattices. Due to pandemic travel restriction, we could not use ARPES, which is located in Shenzhen, to study our samples. Objective 3: Measure the Hall conductance of the samples. We used local and nonlocal transport measurements to investigate the magnetic proximity effect of epitaxially grown FePc films on monolayer and bilayer graphene substrates transferred on hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) for high-quality electrical properties. Due to pandemic travel restriction, we could not perform more transport measurements since the instrument is located in Shenzhen.

16300617.label: Major findings and research outcome
16300617.value: (1) We have systematically investigated local and nonlocal transport properties of monolayer and bilayer graphene devices with epitaxial FePc films. The magnetic proximity effect from the FePc films results in a Zeeman splitting field. A canted antiferromagnetic ground state is observed on mono layer graphene, and a pronounced Zeeman Hall effect is realized on bilayer graphene. Our results reveal the magnetic proximity effect at the interface of graphene/organic magnetic insulator heterostructures and provide a new insight for using molecule-based magnets in two-dimensional spintronic devices. Publication: Chin. Phys. Lett. 38, 087201 (2021) (2) We have synthesized a 2D metal–organic framework (2D-MOF) on a Cu(111) substrate using benzenehexol molecules. By means of a combination of scanning tunneling microscopy and spectroscopy, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and density-functional theory, the structure of the 2D-MOF is determined to be Cu3(C6O6), which is stabilized by O–Cu–O bonding motifs. We find that upon adsorption on Cu(111), the 2D-MOF features a semiconductor band structure with a direct band gap of 1.5 eV. The O–Cu–O bonds offer efficient charge delocalization, which gives rise to a highly dispersive conduction band with an effective mass of 0.45 me at the band bottom, implying a high electron mobility in this material. Publication: Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 59, 2669 (2020). (3) We employ an on-surface Cu-catalyzed dehydrogenation reaction to synthesize a single layer of a 2D-MOF Cu2(C6O6) on silicon carbide epitaxial graphene. According to the DFT calculations, the free-standing structure is a conventional indirect semiconductor with a narrow band gap of 0.485 eV. The energy levels and band morphology of the coordination network adsorbed on graphene change slightly, indicating a weak interaction between the network and the graphene substrate. The narrow band gap behavior of this 2D-MOF makes it a potential candidate for infrared-active materials. Manuscript under preparation. (4) We have synthesized two-dimensional (2D) metal−organic frameworks M3(HAT)2 (HAT=1,4,5,8,9,12-hexaazatriphenylene, M=Ni, Fe or Co) using an on-surface self-assembly protocol. HAT molecules and metal atoms are deposited on a single-crystalline Ag(111) or Au(111) substrate in ultra-high vacuum conditions to assemble into single-atomic layer structures. We use scanning tunneling microscopy and density-functional theory analysis to resolve the structures at an atomic level. HAT molecules are linked by metal atoms via tris-bidentate chelating coordination, forming a hexagonal framework structure of HAT molecules and a Kagome lattice of metal atoms. Manuscript under preparation. The proposed ARPES and quantum transport measurements were not fully accomplished because the collaborating group s are located in Shenzhen so the samples and personals could not be exchanged as planned due to travel restriction.

16300617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16300617.value: It’s unfortunate that the proposed ARPERS and quantum transport measurements could not be conducted as planned. We will make up these measurements once the travel restriction is lifted. We anticipate that such measurements will provide in-depth insights of the quantum properties of the metal-atom functionalized graphene, in particular the quantum anomalous Hall effect.

16300617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16300617.value: Graphene is thought to be a star material for future electronics. Functionalization of graphene is extensively studied to enhance and broaden graphene’s applications. In this project, we have used a unique approach to funtionalize graphene, that is, to decorate metal adatom lattices on top of graphene. We have demonstrated a wide range of lattices of Cu, Fe, Co and Ni atoms can be realized. We have also shown that the metal lattices effectively modify the graphene properties. These results open new opportunities of using functionalized graphene in future elecgtronic devices.

16300717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16300717.value: Atomically thin transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) have opened new avenues to explore anomalous physical properties and potential applications in nanoelectronics and optoelectronics. Although novel optical phenomena have been studied extensively in TMDCs, the investigation of quantum transport properties has encountered a number of obstacles primarily because of the low carrier mobility and strong impurity scattering in TMDC devices. Recently, we successfully fabricated high-mobility TMDC field-effect transistors using our newly developed selective etching technique for boron-nitride-encapsulated TMDC structures. We observed interesting and unexpected transport properties, such as even–odd layer-dependent magnetotransport and unconventional quantum Hall transport. These transport properties are not yet fully understood. However, other experimental results clearly show that these unexpected and unique properties are highly relevant to layer thickness and interlayer interactions, indicating the possibility of building artificial layer or interface structures to modify or design the properties of atomically thin TMDC devices. Our understanding of the quantum transport behavior of few-layer TMDCs is still in its infancy. We propose to investigate the fundamental issues of interlayer coupling effects and their influences on transport properties further. We will focus on (1) the fabrication of ultrahigh mobility field-effect devices using mechanical exfoliation and chemical vapor deposition techniques; (2) the characterization of interface structures and their effects on electrical transport properties; (3) the relationship between interface structures, interlayer couplings, and transport property modulation. We plan to build artificially layered TMDC structures to understand the interlayer or interface coupling mechanisms and their effects on transport property modulation in TMDC devices. Our research group has established independent understanding of the physical properties of charge carriers at conduction and valence bands of different atomically thin TMDCs which can be thought as the building blocks of the studies on artificially layered TMDC systems. These studies will not only help elucidate the quantum transport behavior of atomically thin TMDCs but also establish the relationship between device structure, band structure modulation, and transport properties, which are useful for modifying or designing new properties, for example, through rearranging the transition of carriers in the energy bands in different TMDCs for potential applications in nanoelectronic and optoelectronic devices. 超薄的过渡金属二硫族化合物已经成为探索新物理现象及应用的新材料。尽管这些材料的光学特性已经被广泛的研究，量子输运的实验研究一直受到低样品质量和器件的质量及迁移率而停滞不前。我们目前开发了选择性刻蚀技术并用于制作高迁移率超薄的过渡金属二硫族化合物场效应器件取得了进展。我们观察到一些奇异的量子输运现象，例如奇偶数层的量子霍尔效应。我们计划对层间交互作用进行深入研究。1.制作更高迁移率的场效应器件；2.研究界面结构对电输运的影响；3.研究层间结构和交互作用对电输运的调制。我们计划建构不同的层状结构并研究层间作用调制量子输运的原理。这项研究计划将会解释超薄的过渡金属二硫族化合物的量子输运中关于器件结构，能带结构调制以及新特性的设计等问题，同时也会关注此类材料在纳米器件和纳米光电器件的应用。

16300717.label: Realisation of objectives
16300717.value: The research carried out in this project was well organized. We conducted research along the planned direction and achieved all objectives. We discovered a number of interesting phenomena in transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) structures. In the first stage of this research, we focused on the fabrication of field-effect devices from few-layer MoS2, MoSe2, WS2, WSe2 and NbSe2 through mechanical exfoliation. We have further improved the mobility and the contact issues. We developed a novel oxygen plasma etching technique to selectively etch the top-most layer of MoS2 only. The metal electrodes were directly deposited and connected to the top-most layer. In this case, the special interlayer coupling effects resulting in further reduced contact resistance and high mobility characteristics were achieved. The record high field-effect mobilities were achieved in bilayer MoS2 (Nano Lett. 2019, 19, 1736) and few layer of WSe2 FET devices (this work is under revision in Nature Comm. 2021). In MoS2, by further tracing the transport properties Landau level (LL) crossings in the Landau fan diagram, we unambiguously determined the density-dependent valley susceptibility and the interaction enhanced g-factor from 12.7 to 23.6. Near integer ratios of Zeeman-to-cyclotron energies, we discovered LL anti-crossings due to the formation of quantum Hall ising ferromagnets, the valley polarizations of which appeared to be reversible by tuning the density or an in-plane magnetic field. Our results provide evidence for many-body interaction effects in the conduction band of MoS2 and establish a fertile ground for exploring strongly correlated phenomena of massive Dirac electrons. We have proposed underlying mechanisms of the electron-electron interlayer interaction and interface effects in artificial TMDC devices. This work has been published in Nano Lett. 2019, 19, 1736. Moreover, we have also explained the effects of hexagonal boron nitride encapsulation on the electronic structure of few-layer MoS2 (J. Phys. Chem. C 2019, 123, 14797). Interlayer coupling in few-layer TMDCs can largely influence the physics property. We report the first observation of intrinsic valley Hall transport without any extrinsic symmetry breaking in the non-centrosymmetric monolayer and trilayer MoS2, evidenced by considerable nonlocal resistance that scales cubically with local resistance. Such a hallmark survives even at room temperature with a valley diffusion length at micron scale. By contrast, no valley Hall signal is observed in the centrosymmetric bilayer MoS2. The pronounced nonlocal signals are observed in our MoS2 samples with length up to 16 μm and at temperature up to 300 K. The valley diffusion lengths are also estimated to be in the order of micron. The low carrier concentration ensures the low possibility of bulk inter-valley scattering and maintains a long valley diffusion length. In addition, the mirror and T symmetries lock the spin and valley indices of the lowest sub-bands, preventing bulk inter-valley scattering via spin conservation. Working together with the CI of this project, K.T. Law and his students, we elucidate the topological quantum origin of valley Hall effects and mark a significant step towards the purely electrical control of valley degree of freedom in topological valleytronics. This research work has been published in Nature Communications 10, (2019) 611. We have characterized the interaction effects between substrates and TMDCs grown on the substrates. We find that a substrate plays a crucial role in controlled growth and property modulation of TMDCs, in particular the growth direction, band structure, and dimensions. Details can be found in Chem. Mater. 2020, 32, 2508. The most important discovery in this project is the interlayer coupling effects of twisted WSe2 which not only generate new moiré superlattices but also modify greatly the electronic properties. We first reported superconductivity signatures in this structure. Enhanced interlayer interactions are observed when the twist angle decreases to a few degrees as reflected by the high-order satellites in the electron diffraction patterns taken from the reconstructed domains from a conventional moire´ superlattice. We report that there is no specific magic angle for twisted WSe2. Flat band properties are observable at twist angles ranging from 1 to 4 degrees. Our work has facilitated future study in the area of flat band related properties in twisted transition metal dichalcogenide layered structures. This work was published in Nanoscale Horiz., 2020, 5, 1309. In addition to the superconductivity effects in WSe2 twist structures, we have also investigated the interlayer coupling effects in NbSe2-graphene heterojunction. We reported an interesting phenomenon of two-gap superconductivity characteristics (PHYSICAL REVIEW B 97, 060505(R) (2018)). This paper reports our preliminary work and partially supported by this project. This project supported an undergraduate physics student to carry out theoretical research on the interlayer coupling effect together with a collaborator from University of Delaware. We explored an interacting electron-hole bilayer structure and concluded that excitonic solid can form in bilayer two-dimensional electron-hole systems in transition metal dichalcogenides stacked on opposite sides of thin layers of BN. Properties of the exciton lattice are studied. We found that for the experimental parameters of interest, the solid by itself will melt. However, the solid can be stabilized by the potential due to the BN. We studied the possible manifestation of super solid behavior due to quantum transport of defects and found that it is manifested as an approximately quantized conductance in Coulomb drag measurements (PHYSICAL REVIEW B 102, 125420 (2020)).

16300717.value: Atomically thin transition metal dichalcogenides have opened new avenues to explore anomalous physical properties and potential applications in nanoelectronics and optoelectronics. This research mainly focus on the experimental study of interlayer coupling and transport property manipulation in artificially layered transition metal dichalcogenide devices. We discovered several interesting quantum properties which are important for new ultrathin and highly efficient quantum device design and technological applications in nanoscale electronic devices.

16300917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16300917.value: 含鈰化合物是很重要的材料,其廣泛應用在三元催化、儲能和催化氧化反應中。 常見的二氧化鈰負載金屬異相催化劑的催化功能主要受益于鈰的III/IV價態易變,以及這些複合物在金屬和二氧化鈰作用過程中的儲存、轉移和釋放氧的能力。 對過渡金屬/鈰異金屬配合物反應性的研究可以從分子層面闡明二氧化鈰負載金屬異相催化劑的催化機理,並有助於發展新穎且有效的鈰基催化過程。 最近,本課題組已經合成了Na/Ce=O雙金屬配合物,該物質表現出有趣的氧化還原性質和親核反應性,發現其Ce=O單元能和二氧化碳、一氧化碳反應分別生成四價和三價的鈰碳酸化合物。 為了拓展該工作, 本專案將探索含過渡金屬端氧/鈰(Ce/M=O)異金屬配合物的反應性。 通過配位不飽和的四價鈰配合物和含Ru=O單元化合物反應合成Ce/Ru=O類型的異金屬配合物,並研究其對有機底物如烷烴、烯烴的氧化反應 , 揭示金屬鈰對釕端氧基團反應性的影響。 含鑭系金屬端氧單元的雙金屬配合物已有所報導,但其等電子結構的端氮雙金屬配合物還不甚清楚。 因此,本專案的第二個部分旨在發展含金屬端氮/鈰(Ce/M≡N)異金屬配合物的合成路線,通過配位不飽和的四價鈰配合物和過渡金屬端氮配合物反應獲得氮基橋聯的鈰異金屬配合物,並且探索其在小分子(如二氧化碳、一氧化碳)活化中應用。

16300917.label: Realisation of objectives
16300917.value: The objectives of this research project are to synthesize heterometallic cerium complexes and to study their redox and catalytic properties. The influence of the cerium center on the reactivity of heterometallic Ce/M (M = transition or main group element) complexes has been investigated. In addition, the electronic structure of cerium-oxygen complexes has been studied to elucidate the factors that affect the redox reactivity of tetravalent cerium complexes. Our research has focused on cerium(IV) complexes supported by the Kläui tripodal ligand [Co(h5-C5H5){P(O)(OEt)2}3]- (LOEt-) because previous studies have shown that the [Ce(LOEt)2]2+ core displays well-defined redox behavior and the Ce center exhibits rich chemistry with pi-bonded oxygen ligands. Our approach to the synthesis of heterometallic Ce/M complexes involves the salt metathesis of [Ce(LOEt)2Cl2] and anionic metal-oxo and metal-nitrido complexes. Thus, the reactions of [Ce(LOEt)2Cl2] with metal catecholate nitrido/oxo complexes led to the formation of catecholate-bridged heterometallic complexes, such as [(LOEt)2Ce(cat)2M(N)] (M = Ru, Os) and [(LOEt)2Ce(cat)2V(O)], whereas a Ce(IV)/Mn(V) complex, [Ce(LOEt)2{Mn(N)(CN)4}], was produced from the reaction [Ce(LOEt)2Cl2] with [Mn(N)(CN)4]2-. The isolation of these Ce/M complexes has offered us an opportunity to study the influence of Ce on the reactivity of metal-oxo/nitrido moiety. A preliminary study showed that [Ce(LOEt)2{Mn(N)(CN)4}] is capable of O-H oxidation of substituted phenols, demonstrated the ability of the Ce center to activate the Mn-nitrido moiety. On the other hand, the reaction between the Ce(IV) oxo complex [Ce(LOEt)2(O)(OH2)]Me2CONH2 and the Ru(VI) nitride [Ru(LOEt)(N)Cl2] resulted in the formation of [(LOEt)2Ce(NHCOMe)RuCl2(LOEt)] via the hetero-coupling of the Ce-oxo and Ru-nitride moieties. This is a new reaction of a transition metal nitride that has potential application in metal-mediated N-O coupling. A series of Ce(IV) complexes containing highly oxidizing main group oxo compounds, including the iodate, periodate, persulfate and other hypervalent iodine species, have been synthesized. The isolation of a Ce(IV) complex with a chelating persulfate ligand, which is the first structurally characterize lanthanide persulfate complex, highlights the ability of Ce(IV) to stabilize highly oxidizing oxo species. The iodate complex can undergo oxygen-atom transfer to organic substrates such as thioethers. Electrochemical and reactivity studies indicated that the Ce(IV) center has an effect on the redox behavior of these Ce(IV) oxyanion complexes. In collaboration with Prof. Laurent Maron, University of Toulouse, we have conducted a combined experimental and theoretical study on the reactivity of the Ce(IV) oxo compound [Ce(LOEt)2(O)(OH2)]Me2CONH2. Computational and magnetometry results indicated that the ground state of the Ce(IV) oxo compound is multi-configurational in nature, comprising of 75% Ce(IV) and 25% Ce(III). The Ce(III)-oxyl character of the Ce(IV) oxo compound is believed to play a key role in its reductive addition with carbon monoxide, which led to formation of a Ce(III) bicarbonate. This is the first report on the effect of the multi-configuration ground state of a cerium(IV) complex on its chemical reactivity. This result can provide new insights into the reaction mechanisms of cerium-based homogeneous and heterogeneous oxidation catalysts. Another class of cerium(IV)-oxygen compounds that we have explored is cerium(IV) alkoxide complexes. Although cerium alkoxides are well-documented, the redox and oxidation chemistry of cerium(IV) alkoxide complexes has not been explored, owing to the fact that alkoxides are strong pi donors that stabilize Ce(IV). We have developed a new synthetic route to redox-active cerium(IV) alkoxides involving the protonolysis of the cerium(IV) oxo compound with alcohols. We have demonstrated that [Ce(LOEt)2(OR)2] can oxidize substituted phenols via a proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) pathway. To our knowledge, this is the first report of PCET oxidation by a tetravalent lanthanide complex. We have also synthesized Ce(IV) aryloxides by a similar method. A preliminary study showed that the Ce(III)-aryloxyl character of Ce(IV) aryloxide plays a role in their redox stability and reactivity. Finally, we have synthesized a series of heterometallic Ir/Ru nitrido complexes with oxygen and sulfur donor ligands, and studied coligand effect on the bonding of the Ir-N-Ru units. Generally, oxygen coligands can strengthen the Ir-N pi bonding presumably due to their ability to stabilize high-valent Ir. In summary, we have synthesized and structurally characterized heterometallic cerium complexes supported by the Kläui tripodal ligand. The Ce(IV) binding can stabilize metal ions in high oxidation states, thus allowing us to probe the redox and O-atom transfer chemistry of highly oxidizing transition/main group metal-oxo species. Our experimental and computational studies have shown that the Ce(III)-oxyl character of a Ce(IV)-oxo complex plays a role in its reductive addition with carbon monoxide and sulfur dioxide. This result can shed light on the mechanisms of catalytic oxidation by tetravalent lanthanide complexes and materials.

16300917.label: Major findings and research outcome
16300917.value: (i) We have synthesized the first catecholate-bridged heterometallic cerium(IV) complexes, e.g., [(LOEt)2Ce(cat)2Ru(N)], from reaction of [Ce(LOEt)2Cl2] (LOEt- = [CpCo{P(O)(OEt)2}3]-) with metal catecholates (cat). This provides us an opportunity to probe the influence of the cerium center on the reactivity of the metal-nitrido moiety in Ce/M nitrido complexes. (ii) We have synthesized a bimetallic Ce(IV)/Mn(V) nitrido complex, [(LOEt)2Ce{Mn(N)(CN)4}]. A preliminary study showed that this Ce(IV)/Mn(V) nitrido complex is capable of abstracting hydrogen atom from substituted phenols. (iii) We have found that the reaction between the Ce(IV) oxo complex [Ce(LOEt)2O(H2O)](MeCONH2) and [Ru(LOEt)(N)Cl2] led to hetero-coupling of the Ce-oxo and the Ru-nitride, and formation an acetamido-bridged Ce(IV)/Ru(III) complex, [(H2O)(LOEt)2Ce(NHCOMe)Ru(LOEt)Cl2]. To our knowledge, this is a new reaction of a transition metal nitride that can find potential application in metal-mediated N-O coupling. (iv) We have found that the ground state of the Ce-oxo complex [Ce(LOEt)2O(H2O)](MeCONH2) is of multi-configurational nature, being a mixture of 74% Ce(IV) and 26% Ce(III). The Ce(III)-oxyl character of the Ce(IV) oxo complex is responsible for its reductive addition with CO to give a Ce(III) bicarbonate. To our knowledge, this is the first report on the influence of a multi-configurational ground state of a lanthanide complex on its chemical reactivity. (v) We have synthesized and structurally characterized Ce(IV) complexes with iodate, periodate and persulfate ligands, demonstrating the ability of Ce(IV) to stabilize highly oxidizing oxyanions. The Ce(IV) iodate complex can oxidize organic substrates such as thioethers. (vi) We have developed a new synthetic route to Ce(IV) alkoxide complexes via protonolysis of the Ce(IV) oxo complex [Ce(LOEt)2O(H2O)] with alcohols. The Ce(IV) alkoxide [Ce(LOEt)2(O-i-Pr)2] can oxidize substituted phenols such as 2,4,6-tri-tert-butylphenol via a proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) pathway. This is the first report of PCET oxidation of organic substrates by a tetravalent lanthanide complex. (vii) We have synthesized heterometallic Ir/Ru nitrido complexes supported by oxygen and sulfur donor ligands. X-ray diffraction indicates there is extensive pi delocalization in the Ir-N-Ru units, consistent with the Ir(III)=N=Ru(IV) bonding description. Also, the Ir=N bond in the Ir-N-Ru complexes with O-donor ligands are shorter than those in the S-donor analogues, showing the ability of O-donor ligands to stabilize high-valent Ir. (viii) We have synthesized heterometallic Fe-N-Ru complexes supported by Schiff base ligands. Chloride abstraction of a Fe-N-Ru chloride complex with TlPF6 in air led to isolation of an oxo-bridged containing a Ru-N-Fe-(OTl)-Fe-N-Ru unit. This result demonstrates the facile formation of bridged oxo species by heterometallic Fe(IV) nitrido Schiff base complexes.

16300917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16300917.value: We have demonstrated that the Ce(IV) ion can stabilize highly oxidizing transition metal ions., and the Ce(IV) binding has an influence on the reactivity of metal-oxo species. Therefore, future research should be direct toward the isolation of Ce(IV) complexes containing hypervalent main group ions, such as selenium and bismuth. For example, Ce(IV)/Se(IV) and Ce(IV)/Bi(V) complexes will be synthesized via salt metathesis of Ce(IV) chlorides with Se=O and Bi=O species. The H-atom transfer and oxygen O-atom transfer reactivity of the synthesized Ce/Se and Ce/Bi complexes will be investigated. Furthermore, our studies have shown that the Ce(III)-oxyl character of a Ce(IV)-oxo complex has an impact on its redox reactions. Therefore, in the future, efforts should be made to explore the chemistry of other cerium(IV)-oxygen complexes that also possess cerium(III) ligand radical character. For example, in preliminary work, we found that Ce(IV) aryloxide complexes can oxidize substituted phenols via hydrogen atom abstraction of the O-H group. A computational study indicated that a thermally accessible triplet excited state of the Ce(IV) aryloxide plays a role in the H-atom transfer. The study of the reactivity of redox-active cerium(IV) aryloxide and related complexes is underway in this laboratory.

16300917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16300917.value: Tetravalent cerium compounds are of importance due to their diverse applications in catalytic oxidations. Knowledge of the reaction chemistry of molecular heterometallic cerium complexes can help us design efficient, selective cerium-based bimetallic oxidation catalysts. In this project, we have synthesized heterometallic Ce/M complexes (where M is a transition or main group metal) and investigated their redox and catalytic properties. In addition, to elucidate the reaction mechanisms of tetravalent cerium complexes, the electronic structure of cerium-oxygen complexes has been investigated. The isolation of heterometallic cerium/metal oxo and nitrido complexes has enabled us to probe the influence of the cerium center on the redox reactivity of the metal-oxo and metal-nitrido moieties. We have also isolated cerium(IV) complexes containing hypervalent iodine and persulfate ligands and studied their oxygen-atom transfer reactions. In a combined experimental and theoretical study, we have shown that the ground state of a cerium(IV)-oxo complex is multi-configurational, and the cerium(III)-oxyl character plays a key role in its reductive addition with carbon monoxide. We have shown that cerium(IV) alkoxide complexes can oxidize substituted phenols via a proton-coupled electron transfer pathway. These results provide new insight into the mechanisms of oxidation reactions with tetravalent cerium compounds.

16301117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16301117.value: Glasses are amorphous solids. They exist widely in nature, technologies and our daily life. The nature of glass transition is one of the most important unsolved problems in condensed matter physics and represents a broad class of problems in science [1]. The conventional way to make a glass is by rapidly quenching a liquid so that the disordered structure is frozen in an amorphous solid. Here we will study glass formation from crystals and vapors which involve drastic structural change and new behaviors. We propose a novel route to produce glasses by compressing binary crystals composed of hard and soft spheres so that the structure changes dramatically during glass transformation. This process enables us to explore an important open question: where is the boundary between polycrystal and glass? Our preliminary computer simulation revealed rich features at the boundary between polycrystal and glass and uncovered three glass regimes. We will change the mixing ratio, particle interaction and dimensionality to explore if these behaviors are universal. We plan to set the initial soft spheres larger than hard spheres to obtain a re-entrant glass-crystal-glass transition, and drive the transitions by either increasing or decreasing the pressure. Since the required pressure is too high to compress a real alloy into a glass, we will experimentally compress a much softer two-dimensional (2D) colloidal crystal into glass. In the second half of the project, we will explore the surface relaxation of vapor-deposited colloidal glasses. Recent studies discovered that vapor deposition can produce ultrastable glasses due to the effective relaxation in a surface mobile layer [2], but the microscopic relaxation kinetics has not been observed. Our preliminary experiment revealed the deposition growth of a glass at the single-particle level for the first time. We not only directly observed the relaxation kinetics in the surface mobile layer, but further discovered a deeper middle layer with a novel relaxation mode. We plan to repeat the measurements at different deposition rates and use monodispersed ellipsoids to understand how a free surface and the particle shape affect glass structure and dynamics. The proposed experiments are pioneering studies of the crystal-to-glass transition and microscopic relaxation of the vapor-glass transition. Based on the novel preliminary results and the broad future extensions both experimentally and in simulation, the proposed study will generate fruitful results which are of importance in both practical material design and the theoretical understanding of glass transition. 玻璃是無序固體。它們在自然界，工業生產和我們的日常生活中廣泛存在。玻璃化轉變的本質是凝聚態物理學中最重要的未解決問題之一，並代表了一類廣泛的科學問題。製造玻璃的常規方法是通過快速冷卻液體使得無序結構被冷凍成無定形固體。而在這裡，我們將研究晶體和蒸氣中如何形成玻璃，這些玻璃態轉變涉及強烈的結構變化並具有新穎的行為。 我們提出了一種壓縮軟、硬兩種粒子形成的二元晶體來生產玻璃態的新途徑。這個過程使我們能夠探索一個重要的問題：如何區分多晶和玻璃態？它們之間的邊界在哪裡？我們的初步計算機模擬揭示了多晶和玻璃之間邊界的豐富特徵。我們將改變軟、硬粒子的混合比例，粒子間相互作用和空間維度，以探討這些行為是否普遍。我們計劃將軟球初始直徑大於硬球，通過增加壓力獲得玻璃-晶體-玻璃這種新奇的兩次轉變。由於原子難以壓縮很多，因此將真正的合金壓縮成金屬玻璃需要的壓力太高而不易實現，因此我們將用更軟的二維膠體晶體壓縮成玻璃。 在第二部分，我們將探討氣相沉積膠體玻璃的表面弛豫。最近的研究發現，由於表面活動層可以有效地弛豫玻璃態，氣相沉積可以產生超穩定的玻璃，但是目前沒有實驗能觀察到其微觀動力學過程。我們的初步實驗揭示了單粒子尺度上的玻璃態沉積生長。我們不僅直接觀察了表面活動層的弛豫動力學，而且發現了具有一種新型弛豫模式的較深的中間層。我們計劃以不同的沉積速率重複測量，並使用單分散橢球來了解自由表面和顆粒形狀如何影響玻璃結構和動力學。 我們提出的這兩類新穎實驗已有了初步的實驗或計算機模擬結果，未來可以做各種拓展，相應的研究結果將對實際材料設計和玻璃化轉變的理論上有重要的作用。

16301117.label: Realisation of objectives
16301117.value: We successfully finished all the three objectives and did some extended studied. For objectives 1 and 2, we find an appropriate soft/hard mixture system which enable to achieve ultrafine grained polycrystals whose mean diameter ranges from 3 to 15 particles for the first time. Thus many things can be studied. The full spectrum of grain size provides an ideal platform to study polycrystal-glass transition. We observed various quantities peak at the same density with mean grain diameter 15 particles, i.e. the transition occurs at a sharp point rather than a continuous crossover. These quantities provide a phenomenological description about the mechanism. This is confirmed in 2D and 3D systems with various particle interactions. The results are published in Phys. Rev. X, 8, 041023 (2018). We further measured other properties in the glass regime and largely clarify a puzzle in metallic glasses: fractional power law. The results are published in Nat. Commun. 11, 2005 (2020) For objective 3, we fabricate monolayers of colloidal glasses by vapor deposition along a inclined plane in gravity and measure the microscopic kinetics by video microscopy. A novel intermediate layer is discovered. These results were published in Nature communications 8, 1. In contrast to this study using repulsive particles in gravity, we further fabricated colloidal glasses composed of tunable attractive particles without gravity which can better mimic the atomic glasses. We studied glass surface melting behaviors at the single-particle level for the first time and find that Landau theory for crystal premelting also works well for glass premelting. The manuscript is in preparation.

16301117.label: Major findings and research outcome
16301117.value: We compressed two-dimensional binary crystals composed of soft and hard spheres. This novel approach can continuously reduce the grain size of polycrystal to the glass regime for the first time. This enables us to explore the polycrystal-glass transition. Surprisingly, we found that it is a sharp transition rather than a continuous crossover. We discovered various structural, dynamical, mechanical and thermodynamical features at the polycrystal-glass boundary. These behaviors are robust in systems with different particle interactions or mixing ratios of soft and hard particles. We further systematically scanned the parameter space and found the conditions to form ultrafine-grained polycrystals. Such understanding could guide the future fabrication of ultrafine-grained polycrystals which is of great importance in materials science and metallurgy. These rich results about objectives 1 and 2 were published in a long article in the top physics journal Physical Review X in late 2018, but we acknowledged a wrong grant number GRF601613. It is apparently a mistake because our paper in Physical Review X in 2018 is clearly different from the title of GRF601613 (Video-microscopy study of glass transitions in colloidal glasses of ellipsoids 01/01/2014 - 31/12/2016) and passed its expiration date. We further studied 3D case and obtained a similar transition. The 3D results enable us to investigate a puzzle in metallic glass: fractional power law. These results are published in Nat. Commun. in 2020. For objective 3, we measured vapor-deposited colloidal glasses and experimentally confirmed the surface mobile layer at the single-particle level for the first time. More interestingly, we discovered a middle surface layer exhibiting usual dynamic heterogeneities. These results published in Nature Communications, 8, 362 (2017), one year after we submitted the proposal but before the starting date of the grant GRF16301117. Hence we did not acknowledge GRF16301117. We further discovered distinct surface roughening and premelting behaviors for monolayer and bilayer colloidal crystals, which demonstrates that 2D is a critical dimension with surprising impacts on crystals’ surfaces. This result is published in Soft Matter in 2021. We also discovered very rich critical behaviors in the glass transition of colloidal monolayers composed of ellipsoids. Critical behaviors have been found in glass transition of systems composed of various spherical particles and the first paper is ranked as the top 20 landmark papers in the history of Nature Materials; We further show that such critical behaviors also exist in non-spherical particle systems for the first time and the result is published in Science Advances in 2021.

16301117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16301117.value: We will perform the corresponding colloid experiment about crystal-glass transition and compare with our simulation results. To achieve the crystal-glass transition, we reduce the crystalline grain size in this project. In the future, we will try a novel alternative approach: expanding the thickness of amorphous grain boundaries to achieve the glass state. The polycrystallites embedded in an amorphous matrix is a new type of super-alloy with outstanding properties and has attract great interest in mechanical engineering and metallurgy in recent years. However, the corresponding crystal-glass transition has not been explored. We can apply our analysis in this project to the future project. Vapor deposited glasses in this project is composed of repulsive particles on an inclined plane under gravity. Recently we achieved vapor deposited glasses using tunable attractive colloids without gravity which can better mimic real materials which are all composed of attractive atoms or molecules. We will study the surface properties of such attractive colloidal glasses for the first time, especially about its melting behaviors which has rarely been explored.

16301117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16301117.value: Non-equilibrium phases often have blurry boundaries. For example, "Where and why does liquid end and glass begin?" is ranked as one of the 125 most important questions in science. Similarly we can ask “Where and why does polycrystal end and glass begin?" because polycrystals must become amorphous solids, i.e. glasses, when their crystalline grains decrease to merely a few atoms. The latter question has been rarely asked and poorly explored, partly because ultrafine-grained polycrystals are unstable and hard to fabricate. We find that mixtures of hard and soft particles can be compressed from crystal to glass with a full spectrum of grain size, which provide an ideal platform to study the polycrystal-glass transition. Surprisingly, our simulation shows that various quantities exhibit a peak at the same density, indicating a well defined polycrystal-to-glass transition point rather than a continuous crossover. We further studied various features about the transitions and glasses, and obtained rich results. Colloids are excellent model systems to study glasses because the micron-sized particles and their motions can be directly visualized by optical microscopy. Our experiment studied the surface of colloidal glasses at the single-particle level for the first time and discovered a surface layer with distinct properties.

16301717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16301717.value: Witten's top Chern class is the mathematical fundamental for defining Landau Ginzburg's enumerative geometry. Its analytic construction is referred as FJRW class. In a restrictive condition called ``narrow" its algebraic construction is given by the PI. In this project, we shall search for algebraic construction of FJRW class beyond narrow cases, namely cases with ``broad" sectors. We would also apply the construction to CY-LG correspondences. This project is the last step to complete the interaction between algebraic geometry and superstring theory for Landau Ginzburg spaces after 20 years of mathematical research. The project would also initiate the algebraic study of topological string theories in all phases with all sectors, including their interactions(phase transition. 藍道-根次伯格 記數幾何的數學基礎是威騰-陳類。 其解析的構造被稱為FJRW類。在所謂的“狹義”情形, 其代數構造之前已經由我們發現。 在這份研究計畫中, 我們將要尋找超過“狹義”情形的 FJRW類的代數構造, 也就是所謂的“廣義”情形。我們也將會應用我們的構造到 卡拉比-丘 與 藍道-根次伯格 理論的對應。 本研究計畫 將完成 20 年來 數學上 代數幾何和超弦理論 在 藍道-根次伯格空間 的相互理論發展。本計畫也將開啟拓墣弦論的所有相位（情形）的代數研究, 包括不同相位之間的變化（相變問題）。

16301717.label: Major findings and research outcome
16301717.value: We generalize the construction of cosection localized virtual cycles to a functorial setting. This leads to constructing full virtual cycles for 2D topological gravity with background in the Landau Ginzburg space ([C^n/G],W). We verified our algebraic virtual fundamental classes to satisfy deformation invariance and decomposition axioms. We also find that our construction is compatible with other different constructions. This unifies the theory to a whole piece and various aspects can share the advantages. The discoveries fits in well of a master space program via which we found striking applications in string theory's mathematics. The application proves a fundamental problem in string mathematics, and one of its paper with title: "Polynomial structure of Gromov-Witten potential of quintic 3-folds via NMSP" is published in one of the most prestigious journal: Annals of Mathematics in pure mathematics.

16301717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16301717.value: For nonaffine Landau Ginzburg spaces such as the total space of canonical line bundle over projective spaces, the construction should be able to be generalized to include broad sectors. A more illuminating further development would be on broad sector of Mixed Spin P field moduli's. It will open a direction of theory that can approach many difficult open conjectures. A part of the realization of the direction has appeared in 1. the paper "The theory of N-Mixed-Spin-P fields" published in Geometry & Topology, 2. and also the paper "An effective theory of GW and FJRW invariants of quintics Calabi-Yau manifold" published in Journal of Differential Geometry and 3. "Mixed-Spin-P fields of Fermat polynomials," published in Cambridge Journal of Mathematics. More phases of MSP program will attract attentions of groups in other topics, such as open Gromov Witten theory, D branes, Calabi-Yau Landau-Ginzburg correspondence, Homological Mirror Symmetry e.t.c.

16301717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16301717.value: The topological string theory, originated from physics, is now a core subject in moder geometry research. The topological string theory with Landau Ginzburg (LG) background, is discovered to govern the finest structural parts of various types of topological string invariants. In this project, a natural approach to obtain the LG topological string invariants is discovered with full mathematical rigor and beautiful geometric constructions. The discovery will lead to solution of many big conjectures in the subject.

16301817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16301817.value: Food-borne contamination has been a growing worldwide concern, especially in the developing world with large populations. Low-cost and rapid diagnostic platforms designed for large-scale deployment for the detection of these contaminants remain elusive and therefore many innovative approaches have been attempted to tackle this challenge. Although the detection of nucleic acid-based biomarkers is a widely adopted and commercially viable approach; most nucleic acid testing (NAT) methods require an extra step of sample enrichment either through a temperature-varied polymerase chain reaction or a constant-temperature amplification procedure, particularly for samples with dilute target analytes. These requirements simply cannot be met in the developing world, where innovative sensing strategies using few and affordable assay steps without a separate sample enrichment procedure and integrated into a cost-effective device format (e.g., paper, cellulose membrane) are urgently needed. One of the promising approaches to address the challenge of detecting dilute analytes without an enrichment procedure is to design a series of nucleic acid assembly and disassembly reactions through specific hybridization events between the capture probes and the analyte of interest. A salient feature of this nucleic acid circuitry is its autocatalytic characteristic, i.e. target recycling, where the target analyte displays itself as reactant and product at the same time. This provides an autonomous mechanism to release and recycle the analyte from each round of reactions for repetitive cycles, which amplifies the signal without amplifying the analyte itself. Leveraging our expertise on DNA self-assembly and electrochemistry-based sensing, we propose to develop a detection strategy based on target recycling compatible with practical assay time (e.g., 30 mins to 2 hrs) that can be integrated into a transduction platform suitable for a resource-limited setting. Our approach includes both enzyme-required and enzyme-free platforms but the underlying principle of the mechanism purely hinges on DNA hybridization interactions between the target and the designed nucleic acid substrates. Nontyphoidal Salmonella (NTS), which causes 1.03 million cases of food-borne illnesses annually in the US will initially be used as a model analyte in the proposed strategies on fluorescence and electrochemical transduction platforms. The success of this proposal will offer highly feasible sensing strategies, deployable in a low-cost point-of-care device in the developing world, and will ultimately benefit the long-term healthcare and welfare of a large population. 食品污染已日渐成为全球隐患，人口众多的发展中国家尤其受此威胁。为此，研究者们尝试研发各种创新手段来实现低成本，快速且可用于大范围推广的污染物检测。虽然核酸检测是一种切实可行，应用广泛的诊断方法，但多数核酸检测，尤其针对低浓度样品，需要先通过变温聚合酶链反应或恒温扩增的方法来实现样品的富集，而这一步骤在发展中国家通常难以实现。因此，研究者们迫切需要一种新的核酸检测方法，步骤简洁，成本低廉且无须进行样品富集，并能将其整合到高性价比的检测装置上。 研究者们基于核酸链的特异性杂交，设计了探针和检测物之间一系列核酸链组装和解链反应。此反应的自催化特性使其无需进行样品富集，便可实现低浓度样品检测。在反应中，检测物同时作为反应物和产物，每一轮反应后释放的检测物可以再循环参与下一轮反应，从而在不扩增检测物本身的情况下不断放大检测信号。 源于在DNA自组装和电化学检测方面的专业经验，我们提出一种新的基于检测物自循环的检测方法。该方法只需较短的检测时间（如30分钟至2小时），符合低资源环境的检测需求。我们提出有酶和无酶两种检测方法，并分别设计了用于与检测物杂交的相应核酸底物。非型沙门氏菌（NTS）将作为模型检测物，分别在荧光和电化学检测平台上进行测试。这一项目的成功将为发展中国家提供低成本，易实现的即时诊断方法，并终将有利于人口密集地区的长期医疗保健。

16301817.label: Realisation of objectives
16301817.value: This research aims to leverage our understanding of the thermodynamics and kinetics of nucleic acid-based reactions to construct an improved detection platform for Non-typhoidal Salmonella. We aim to introduce improvements in the specificity and the speed of the detection process. All three proposed objectives were achieved and along the process; five peer-reviewed papers were published; and two graduate students were trained with a pending patent application. In objective 1, we carefully characterized the thermodynamics of a mismatch-assisted target recycling mechanism aiming for an enzyme-free, simple, and ultrasensitive detection platform. The strategies we demonstrated and utilized in this objective have been documented in an invited review paper (output paper 1) and the PhD thesis by Tsz Wing Fan. In objective 2, we sought to increase the specificity of target-recycling reactions. Specifically, the discrimination factor of the reaction tends to decrease over time and is largely dependent on the abundance of the spurious targets. Thus, our goal was to construct a nucleic acid circuit that will remain highly selective for long periods of time, thereby making its selectivity more robust; and is able to tolerate off-target effects, even up to single-base differences. We accomplished this by introducing a destabilization motif onto the probe and adding assistant strands to introduce a kinetic barrier, so that, only when a perfectly complementary strand binds onto the probe, the assistant strand can then bind, to release the target (and undergo subsequent target recycling reactions) and fluorescence can also be detected. Our approach demonstrates a target-recycling-type reaction with (1) minimal leakage; (2) high DF against single-base mutants; (3) sustainable or even increased specificity for long period measurements; and (4) the ability to discriminate low frequencies of the target from spurious mixtures. We have also explored the use of a ‘sink’ or a nucleic acid probe that is perfectly complementary to the wild-type (WT) as opposed to the single-nucleotide variant (SNV). The preferential hybridization reactions between the pairs of SNV and SNV-specific probe and WT and WT-specific sink improve reaction selectivity, resulting in high SNV discrimination. We thus designed a new hybridization-based assay leveraging the approach of competitive DNA hybridization probes as described above, and couple it with a target-recycling reaction, only for the SNV-specific probe. This has significantly amplified the signal of SNV over the mutated target (WT), enabling an improved SNV discriminating power over that of the DNA hybridization probes relying solely on competition or amplification. Aside from selectivity, we have also conducted experiments that would speed up the target recycling reaction. In a simple DNA biosensor platform involving strand-displacement reactions, the kinetics is said to be pseudo first order at low analyte concentrations and sufficiently excess amounts of probes. In such a case, the signal produced is proportional to the amount of the analyte. In order to increase the signal one strategy commonly used is target recycling, wherein when the target undergoes several cycle of reactions repeats in an autocatalytic fashion, thereby increasing the signal over time without increasing the amount of the target itself. However, in order to compensate for the concentration of the analyte in very dilute samples, the reaction must be allowed to sit for a long time so that a detectable signal can be obtained. In particular, we addressed the issue on kinetics, since aside from sensitivity and selectivity, the total assay time is also considered a hindrance to the development of a useful point-of-care device. Thus, in this study, we limit the detection time to 15 minutes, and improve the kinetics of the detection by introducing the two-layer, three-pass exonuclease III target recycling pathway. Through this method, we provided a proof-of-concept that picomolar concentrations of target DNA can be detected within a reasonable time frame for point-of care devices, ie objective. 3. Moreover, we successfully demonstrated proof-of-concept device for nucleic acid sensing with high sensitivity based on the optimized parameters obtained from objectives 2. The strategy has also been promising for viral SARS-Covid-2 sensing. Our strategies are documented in the research output paper #5.

16301817.label: Major findings and research outcome
16301817.value: Through the completion of our project objectives, we have demonstrated an enzyme-free sensing strategy using synthetic nucleic acid circuits to control reaction kinetics. This sensing platform was shown to be potentially helpful for a prototype device for nucleic acid sensing for detection of nontyphoidal Salmonella and other analytes (output paper 1). Specifically, we were able to characterize nucleic acid self-assembly circuits and demonstrate the effective discrimination of single nucleotide variants (SNVs). We further showed a kinetically-enhanced DNA detection strategy using two signal-amplification nucleic acid circuits. Leveraging the enzyme-free detection and signal amplification strategies we learned from this project, we have further expanded innovative strategies by 1) exploiting CRISPR-Cas based strategy to improve detection specificity (output paper 2) and 2) expanding the detection of nucleic acid targets (viral pathogen, microbe, etc) to health-related small molecule detection (e.g., antibiotics, urine, etc) by integrating restriction enzyme and signal amplification system consisting of toehold mediated strand displacement (TMSD) (output papers 3-4). Moreover, we have made developed a patentable one-pot probe-mediated isothermal amplification (o-LAMP) coupled with a current target-specific detection readout. As shown in the research output (paper 5), this platform offers a readily scalable and highly specific diagnostic pathway for rapid and decentralized detection of communicable diseases (e.g., COVID-19, Nontyphoidal Salmonella).

16301817.value: The innovative ideas originating from this project has contributed to my group’s development of one-pot probe-mediated isothermal amplification (o-LAMP) coupled with a current target-specific detection readout. As shown in the research output (paper 7), this platform offers a readily scalable and highly specific diagnostic pathway for rapid and decentralized detection of communicable diseases (e.g., COVID-19, Nontyphoidal Salmonella)

16301817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16301817.value: With the support this GRF grant, we have successfully developed two robust and sensitive sensing strategies using synthetic nucleic acid circuitry and loop-mediated isothermal amplification scheme (o-LAMP). This development enabled our research group to expand our expertise for the development of two viable detection platforms for communicable pathogens, in particular SARS-CoV-2. With the further funding support for the Government and with success of our early data, we have been developing two sensitive and highly specific platform technologies, one aiming for large-population screening of viral pathogens at the airport or border entry points and the other disposable prototype targeting for nucleic-acid based at-home tests, with sensitivity and specificity potentially better than that of the rapid antigen test (RAT) kits.

16301917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16301917.value: The key attraction of particle physics is to search for new heavy particles and study their interactions. It is believed that the energy scale of cosmic inflation is much higher than the energy scale of any man-made particle physics colliders. Thus, it is hoped that inflation can play a role in particle physics discoveries. The Quasi-Single Field Inflation (QSFI) proposed by Chen and the PI in 2009 is an important step towards this goal. QSFI reveals the characteristic scaling structures from massive fields in cosmological correlation functions. This approach is further developed by Arkani-Hamed and Maldacena, under the name “cosmological collider physics”. The mass, spin and types of interactions are systematically studied. Recently, Chen, Xianyu and the PI studied the mass spectrum of the particle physics Standard Model (SM) during inflation. We showed the limitations of the previous thermal mean field estimation, and presented a full one-loop analysis of the inflationary SM mass corrections. We call this process the“calibration of the cosmological collider” because it matches the mass spectrum and couplings of the SM particles at the ground based collider scale and the scale of inflation. This enables further study of the particle physics during inflation. On the observational side, the past two decades saw an improvement of 300 times in the accuracy of measuring cosmological three-point correlation functions. The technology is available for another 10 times improvement in the near future, and there is further room for improvement in the distant future. Putting all the considerations above together, a research program emerges as follows: Given the SM baseline, what is the signature of Beyond Standard Model (BSM) particle physics in the sky, imprinted in the cosmological correlation functions? This is the focus of this proposal. The BSM physics includes the following aspects: The SM particles with BSM interactions, the BSM particles and extended objects such as string states and black holes. Indeed, we still need to wait for future experiments to achieve enough precision to probe the features that we are investigating. But devising theories that go beyond experiment is typical in high energy physics and cosmology. The research field is developing fast and we need support to start early so that Hong Kong can take the lead in this research direction. 粒子物理的核心內容是尋找新的重粒子以及研究它們之間的相互作用。一般認為，宇宙暴脹的能量標度遠高於人造粒子加速器。所以，人們希望通過研究暴脹來做出粒子物理領域的發現。 我與合作者陳新剛在2009年提出了准單場暴脹。這是聯繫暴脹和粒子物理的重要步驟。准單場暴脹解釋了重粒子在宇宙學中密度關聯函數中的作用。Arkani-Hamed和Maldacena進一步發展了利用准單場暴脹來研究粒子物理的方法，並將其命名為“宇宙對撞機物理”。他們系統地研究了重粒子的質量、自旋和相互作用種類對宇宙中密度關聯函數的影響。 最近，陳新剛，鮮於中之和我研究了暴脹期間粒子物理標準模型的質量譜。我們的研究顯示了之前利用熱平均場方法研究類似問題的局限性，並且進行了暴脹期間標準模型粒子質量譜的完整一圈圖計算。我們稱這個工作為“校準宇宙加速器”。這是因為，我們的計算為地面上人造加速器實驗和宇宙加速器中粒子物理標準模型的預言提供了聯繫。這使得進一步研究暴脹期間的粒子物理稱為可能。 在觀測方面，過去20年，測量宇宙密度三點關聯函數的精度提高了300倍。根據目前的技術手段，在不遠的將來，宇宙密度三點函數測量的精度可以再提高10倍。在遙遠的將來，這個測量的精度將有進一步的提升空間。 以上的討論為我們指明了一個研究計劃：將粒子物理標準模型作為基準，超越標準模型的粒子物理有何獨特信號（在宇宙密度關聯函數中）？這是本提案的核心主體。超越標準模型的物理有一下方面：標準模型粒子的非標準模型相互作用，超越標準模型的粒子，以及像弦以及黑洞這樣的延展物體。 的確，我們仍需要等待未來的實驗去驗證我們的研究。但是，在高能物理和宇宙學領域，理論的發展通常領先於實驗。這個研究領域發展很快。對這個提案的資助有助於我們儘早開展研究，並使香港引領這個研究領域。

16302117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16302117.value: 加速器是用来探索构成宇宙中物质的基本粒子以及描述他们相互作用的基本原理的工具。大型强子对撞机（LHC）是目前地球上最大的科学实验装置。基于其在8TeV的能标上收集的数据，粒子物理学家在2012年发现了“上帝的粒子” - 希格斯玻色子。随后，粒子物理学家将LHC成功升级到13-14 TeV的设计能标，并于2015年夏季恢复其运行并且开始积累新的数据。根据LHC运行路线，LHC将在2035年左右的高亮度阶段后停止运行。所以现在已经到了粒子物理学家探讨粒子物理学的未来发展项目的时候了（作为比较，尽管LHC在2009年才开始运行，但是该实验项目早在20世纪80年代初就已经提出）。 未来对撞机项目的物理动机主要源于粒子物理学标准模型不完整这一事实。自然界中仍然存在着不少待解的基本难题。这些难题无法通过希格斯玻色子的发现获得解决。例如，如何解决标准模型中希格斯质量接收到二次发散的量子修正，并由此导致的理论上的不稳定性问题。此外，在标准模型的框架下我们也无法理解例如在宇宙中占23％的暗物质是什么，为什么今天宇宙中的物质比反物质多。 为了解决这些问题，我们需要精确测量已知粒子的性质（探索由新的或者是未知的物理引起的粒子性质该变），并在高能标区域中搜索新粒子/新现象。该目标预计可通过建造希格斯工厂 （例如国际线性对撞机（ILC，日本），环形正负电子对撞机（CEPC，中国）或未来环形正负电子对撞机（Fcc-ee, CERN）），以及下一代质子 - 质子对撞机 （如超级质子-质子对撞机（SppC, 中国）或未来环形强子对撞机（Fcc-hh, CERN））获得实现。 在此基础上，PI提出探索未来对撞机上潜在的物理目标，例如测量希格斯自相互作用及研究希格斯质量的稳定机制，等等。需要提及的是，在中国提出的CEPC / SppC项目的初步概念设计报告中PI作出了重要贡献（参阅PI简历），现在PI正在继续参与其概念设计报告的撰写。 这些经历对于PI在建议的研究项目中取得成功将有重要的价值。

16302117.label: Realisation of objectives
16302117.value: In this project, we have published totally four papers. In No. 1 paper, we have developed a new strategy (i.e., by measuring the processes involving two Higgs bosons) to measure the strength of quartic Higgs self-interaction at future lepton (including the operation mode as a Higgs factory) and hadron colliders. This work addressed both Objectives 1 and 2. In No. 3 paper, we have performed a sensitivity analysis for detecting the violation of lepton flavor universality between the first two families and the third family leptons at future e-e+ colliders. This work mainly addressed Objective 1. In No. 2 paper, we have studied how to detect unexpected new physics signals at colliders (especially at future lepton and hadron colliders), using the deep-machine-learning techniques for novelty detection. This work addressed both Objectives 1 and 2. In No. 3 paper, we have developed strategies, using the advanced techniques of deep machine learning such as Convolutional Neural Network, to address information deformation and loss in jet clustering which are one of the major limitations for precisely measuring hadronic events at future at future e−e+ colliders. Because of their dominance in data, the measurements of such events are crucial for advancing the precision frontier of Higgs and electroweak physics in the next decades. This work mainly addressed Objective 1. Regarding the junior researcher training (Objective 3), the PI has engaged totally three students and three postdocs in this research project. Two of the three students have completed their PhD thesis defense and started their postdoctoral career at first-class research institutes in the world. The three postdocs have successfully completed their contracts at HKUST. Two of them started new postdoctoral career in first-class research institutes in the world. The details about their achievements can be found in Part C: Research Output (11. Other impact). Moreover, part of the research results and the relevant concepts involved in this project (e.g., how to explore new physics at future colliders; how to apply the tool of deep machine learning for this purpose) have been used by the PI as materials of the undergraduate courses that he has taught, to inspire the students' interest in particle physics.

16302117.label: Major findings and research outcome
16302117.value: No. 1: In this paper, we proposed to probe quartic Higgs self-interaction at future lepton and hadron colliders, via di-Higgs productions. We analyzed the one-loop contributions of the quartic Higgs coupling, including renormalization of the cubic Higgs coupling and modification of the VVhh form factor, to the vector-boson-fusion and the vector-boson associated di-Higgs productions. We pointed out that a combination of these two di-Higgs productions is important for optimizing the sensitivities. Using this guideline, we found that at ILC the constraints stronger than the theoretical unitarity bound for quartic Higgs self-interaction can be achieved. No. 2: In this paper, we explored applications of the machine-learning techniques of novelty/anomaly detections in searching for unexpected new physics signals at (future) colliders. Novelty detection is a machine-learning task to recognize data of an unknown pattern, without any priori knowledge. We pioneered development of isolation-based and clustering (density)-based novelty evaluators and synergization of them for detecting the signals with various unexpected signatures, using an autoencoder-based deep neural network. The designed algorithms are applied to detecting fermionic di-top partner and resonant di-top productions at a hadron collider, and exotic Higgs decays of two specific modes at an e+e− collider. No. 3: Information deformation and loss in jet clustering are among the major limitations for precisely measuring hadronic events at future e−e+ colliders. In this paper, we showed that this difficulty can be well-addressed by synergizing the event-level information into data analysis, using the deep-neutral-network techniques. For this purpose, we introduced a CMB-like observable scheme, where the event-level kinematics is encoded as Fox-Wolfram moments at leading order. We analyzed measuring Higgs decay width at e−e+ colliders with the data of 5ab−1@240GeV. The precision obtained is significantly better than the baseline ones presented in documents. No. 4: b→sτ+τ− measurements are highly motivated for addressing lepton-flavor-universality-violating puzzles. Z factories at the future e−e+ colliders stand at a great position to conduct such measurements because of their high production rates and reconstruction efficiencies for B mesons at the Z pole. In this paper, we performed a dedicated sensitivity study in four b→sτ+τ− benchmark channels, namely B0→K∗0τ+τ−, Bs→ϕτ+τ−, B+→K+τ+τ− and Bs→τ+τ−, at the future Z factories. We developed a fully tracker-based scheme for reconstructing the signal B mesons . The simulations indicate that branching ratios of the first three channels can be measured with a precision (10^(-7) - 10^(-6)) and that of Bs→τ+τ− with a precision (10^(-5)) at Tera-Z.

16302117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16302117.value: The proposed future collider projects provide a great opportunity to explore the fundamental puzzles in nature which remain unresolved. In this project, we have explored physics opportunities at both future lepton and hadron colliders, mainly including the measurements of quartic Higgs self-interaction and the detection of lepton-flavor-universality violation. Also, the strategies to promote the capabilities of future colliders are designed based on the techniques of deep machine learning. The research can be developed to explore dark matter physics (e.g., using soft collider processes to detect ultralight dark matter candidates), neutrino physics (e.g., searching for sterile neutrinos in high-energy collisions) and others at future colliders.

16302117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16302117.value: The discovery of the ``God Particle'' - Higgs boson in 2012 at Large Hadron Collider marks a great success of human in exploring the unknown. Yet, several fundamental puzzles in nature remain unresolved, such as why Higgs boson is so light, compared to standard theoretical prediction, and why there are three families of fermionic elementary particles with the same charges. To address these puzzles, we need to precisely measure the Higgs properties and to search for new phenomena. This has motivated the proposals of constructing new-generation lepton and hadron colliders within next decades. In this project, we have developed a new strategy to measure the strength of quartic Higgs self-interaction at future colliders in No. 1 paper and performed a sensitivity analysis for detecting the difference in properties between the first two families of leptons and the third family leptons at e-e+ colliders in No. 4 paper. In No. 2 and No. 3 papers, we have studied respectively how to detect unexpected new physics signals at colliders (especially at future colliders) and how to address information loss and deformation problem in jet clustering at future lepton colliders, using the advanced techniques of deep machine learning.

16302217.value: 分数阶Nirenberg问题以及相关研究

16302217.label: Project Objectives

16302217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16302217.value: 在这里我们主要研究几何中的一些关于共形不变量的非线性非局部方程。在共形变换下的两个高斯曲率由一个共形不变的二阶椭圆算子所联系。在高维情况下，如果把高斯曲率换成数量曲率，同样的结论也成立。这个二阶共形不变的椭圆算子叫做共形拉普拉斯算子。高阶的共形算子在不断的被发现。比如四阶的Paneitz算子，以及更加高的整数阶的GJMS算子，直到最近几年被发现的分数阶GJMS算子，从而引出所谓的分数阶Q曲率。我们感兴趣的问题是在高维标准球面上，什么样的函数可以成为标准共形度量的分数阶Q曲率。类似的问题最早由L.Nirenberg在50年代对二维球面的高斯曲率所提出。所以我们把刚才的问题命名为分数阶Nirenberg问题。这个问题等价于解一个非线性非局部方程。非局部的意思是我们需要解的全局信息才能验证这个方程。首先，我们这个非线性非局部方程不一定有解。其次，即使有解，解也不一定唯一，而且这个解的集合不一定紧。我们想要研究的是当这个先前规定的分数阶Q曲率变号的情况下，方程的解的存在性和紧性。同时，我们也要研究这个非线性非局部方程在存在孤立极点的情况下的解的性质。

16302217.label: Realisation of objectives
16302217.value: The PI has obtained a number of results on the fractional Nirenberg problems, including blow up phenomenon when the prescribed functions change signs and the asymptotic behavior of their singular solutions. In the joint paper with Xusheng Du, Hui Yang and Jingang Xiong, we constructed a sequence of solutions to the fractional Nirenberg problem that blows up in the region where the prescribed functions are negative. This is a truly different phenomenon from the classical Nirenberg problem, in which solutions are universally bounded in the region where the prescribed functions are negative, followed by a simple blow up argument together with a Liouville theorem. In the classical case, if a sequence of functions converges locally in the C^2 topology, then their Laplacian will converge locally as well. However, in the fractional Laplacian case, this is no longer true. We showed that if a sequence of nonnegative functions converges locally in the C^2 topology, then their fractional Laplacian converges, but may be differed by a nonzero constant from the fractional Laplacian of the limit function. This nonzero constant will lead to blow up phenomenon of the fractional Nirenberg problem in the region where the prescribed functions are negative. This result completely achieves our first objective, and is actually beyond our expectation. This paper has been uploaded to arXiv, and has been submitted for publication. It is currently under review. In the joint paper with Jingang Xiong, we studied the behavior of the singular solutions to the fractional Yamabe equations with isolated singularities. More generally, we studied a nonlinear integral equation with isolated singularities, and obtained the sharp asymptotic behavior of the solutions near the isolated singularity. This not only extends the classical results for second order equations, but also solves the cases of higher order differential equations and higher order integro-differential equations as corollaries. Moreover, our method is unified for the equations of all orders up to the dimension. We also proved the existence of nontrivial Fowler solutions of large periods. This paper has been published in Ann. Inst. H. Poincaré Anal. Non Linéaire. In the joint paper with Hui Yang, we further investigate behavior of the singular solutions to the fractional Nirenberg equations with "small" singular set. The smallness of the singular set is characterized by its upper Minkowski dimension. Under some flatness condition of the prescribed functions near its critical points, we obtained the sharp blow up rates of the singular solutions. The general method is the same as the one with Jingang Xiong in the above. But the blow up analysis for integral equations with non-constant functions are significantly more delicate than those for constants there, having an extra error term to estimate. This paper has been uploaded to arXiv, and has been submitted for publication. It is currently under review. The last two papers completely achieve our second objective.

16302217.label: Major findings and research outcome
16302217.value: In research output 1, we investigated higher order conformally invariant equations with isolated singularities. We achieved the goal by converting it into a nonlinear integral equation with isolated singularities, and obtained the sharp asymptotic behavior of the solutions to the nonlinear integral equation near an isolated singularity. Our approach uses blow up analysis for local integral equations, and is unified for all critical elliptic (differential and integro-differential) equations of order smaller than the dimension (where the dimension is the threshold for the differential order of the equations). We also proved the existence of periodic Fowler solutions to the global equations, and establish a sup ⁎ inf type Harnack inequality of Schoen for integral equations. In research output 2, we further investigated the above equations with a small singular set rather than a singular point, and with non-constant prescribed curvature functions. We obtained the asymptotic behavior of their singular solutions near the singular set. The smallness of the singular set is characterized by its upper Minkowski dimension. The analysis is more delicate than those for constants there, and we have to carefully estimate an additional error term in a very precise way. In the research output 3, we showed a convergence result of the fractional Laplacian for sequences of nonnegative functions without uniform boundedness near infinity. Then we constructed a sequence of solutions to the fractional Nirenberg problem that blows up in the region where the prescribed functions are negative. This is a different phenomenon from the classical Nirenberg problem.

16302217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16302217.value: The compactness of solutions to higher order Q-curvature equations when the prescribed functions change signs is very interesting but is still unknown. For non-integer cases, it might blow up as well in the region where the prescribed function is negative, due to the non-locality of the equations. For integer cases, it is not clear. It does not have the maximum principle. Moreover, the known blow up techniques for integral equations fail when the prescribed function change signs. The PI plans to continue to investigate them with collaborators.

16302217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16302217.value: The research projects discovered a truly different phenomenon from the classical Nirenberg problem for its fractional case. That is, the solutions for its fractional Laplacian equation will not be necessarily uniformly bounded in the region where the prescribed curvature function is negative. The research projects also obtained the sharp asymptotic behavior for the singular solutions of the fractional Yamabe equations and fractional Nirenberg equations near their singularities. Our method provided a unified approach to the equations of all orders up to the threshold. The techniques developed in the project, as well as the research outcome, are useful in the mathematical community.

16302417.value: 非線性幾何流的自我相似解的剛性

16302417.label: Project Objectives

16302417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16302417.value: Geometric flows are time-dependent evolution equations of geometric objects such as Riemannian manifolds and Euclidean hypersurfaces. Notable examples include the Ricci flow, mean curvature flow, inverse mean curvature flow, and Gauss curvature flow. The studies of these flows have a strong influence in the fields of mathematics, physics and engineering. For example, Hamilton and Perelman used the Ricci flow to resolve the long-standing Poincaré conjecture. The mean curvature flow was also studied by engineers on surface tensions. The inverse mean curvature flow was used by Huisken and Ilmanen to prove the Riemannian Penrose inequality. The Gauss curvature flow was first studied by Firey to understand the shape of a rolling stone. A solution of a geometric flow is said to be self-similar if it evolves by shrinking, expanding, or translation without changing the overall shape. The study of self-similar solutions under various geometric flows is crucial in the above-mentioned studies because these solutions often appear as singularity models, convergence limits, and canonical solutions to the flows. Many of the self-similar solutions constructed in the literature are rotationally symmetric, and exhibit conical or cylindrical asymptotic behavior near the ends of the shape. Accordingly, it is natural to ask how rigid rotational symmetry is for self-similar solutions. Results on rotational rigidity were obtained in works by S. Brendle, O. Chodosh, R. Haslhofer, L. Wang, et. al as well as by the PI and his collaborators on the Ricci Flow, mean curvature flow and inverse mean curvature flow. In the proposed study, we will build on and extend earlier works about rotational rigidity of self-similar solutions, by considering more general types of curvature flows, and more general ambient spaces. We will also expand the examples of rotationally symmetric self-similar solutions to more general types of curvature flows. We expected that this project will result in a more generalized and unified framework of rotational rigidity, which will help advance the knowledge of the singularity development of geometric flows. 幾何流是微分幾何學的重要題目，它被用作解決數學、物理學以至工程學中許多重要問題。許多幾何流的問題牽涉奇異點的分類，而那些奇異點都有一些自我相似性的特質，所以我們稱這些奇異點為自我相似解。 因此，要了解幾何流的奇異點分類，我們必須對它的自我相似解有充分探討。許多自我相似解都有旋轉對稱性，在這個項目中，我們會深入探討幾何流的奇異點、自我相似解、以及對稱性之間的關係。

16302417.label: Realisation of objectives
16302417.value: The goal of the project was successfully achieved. The PI extended some classification results of self-similar solutions to a wider class of curvature flows, in particular, flow by homogeneous degree -1 flow of principle curvatures. The PI also extend some results to self-conformal solutions as well -- this address Objectives 1 and 3. Two papers were published in relation to this project. One was accepted by Comm. Anal. Geom, another was accepted by Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. As for Objective 2, we find that some of our predictions would hold under additional assumption, and we will continue working on it to get a better picture of the problem.

16302417.label: Major findings and research outcome
16302417.value: In the article "Self-expanders to inverse curvature flows by homogeneous functions", co-authored by the PI, Aarow Chow, and Ka-Wing Chow, published by Comm. Anal. Geom., we studied self-expanding solutions to a large class of parabolic inverse curvature flows by homogeneous symmetric functions of principal curvatures in Euclidean spaces. These flows include the inverse mean curvature flow and many nonlinear flows in the literature. We first showed that the only compact self-expanders to any of these flows are round spheres. Secondly, we show that complete non-compact self-expanders to any of these flows with asymptotically cylindrical ends must be rotationally symmetric. Thirdly, we show that when such a flow is uniformly parabolic, there exist complete rotationally symmetric self-expanders which are asymptotic to two round cylinders with different radii. In the article "Uniqueness theorems of self-conformal solutions to inverse curvature flows", co-authored by the PI, Jingbo Wan, Nicholas Chin, published by Proc. Amer. Math. Soc., we proved that the round sphere is rigid in a stronger sense: under some natural conditions such as star-shapedness, round spheres are the only closed solutions to the above-mentioned flows which evolve by diffeomorphisms generated by conformal Killing fields.

16302417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16302417.value: In the above-mentioned works, the PI and his collaborator classified the type of singularity models under certain asymptotic conditions. It is expected that the results can be used to study the convergence behavior of geometric flows, as the self-similar solutions are tend to be the limit of solutions. The PI will continue working on this direction.

16302417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16302417.value: In this project, the PI succeeded in classifying the singularity model (called self-similar solutions) of certain type of geometric flows including the Inverse Mean Curvature Flow which plays an important role in general relativity. The PI and his collaborator proved that under a certain asymptotic conditions, the self-similar solutions become rotationally symmetric, and hence can be identified by solving ordinary differential equations. It is expected the results would give more insight about the convergence behavior of the geometric flows.
