16304117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16304117.value: Proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs), a type of clean energy conversion device, have attracted great attention for applications in electric vehicles. Yet, the high cost of platinum (Pt)-based electrocatalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) at the cathode has hindered the widespread adoption of PEMFCs. To increase cost-competitive of these fuel cells, advanced ORR catalysts with much higher activity and lower cost than state-of-the-art platinum/carbon (Pt/C) are required. Octahedral Pt bimetallic nanocrystals consisting of {111} facets have gained considerable attention due to their much higher activity than Pt/C. However, we have virtually no knowledge of how Pt octahedra form during the synthesis. This proposed project aims to establish the structural and composition evolution paths during the formation of octahedral Pt-based bimetallic nanocrystals (NCs), and clarify the roles of capping/shape selective agents in morphology control. In addition, this project will combine three strategies to design a new class of ORR catalysts: 1) a “core-shell structure” consisting of an inexpensive core and a Pt-based shell to improve Pt utilization; 2) a “platinum alloy shell” to improve the specific activity of Pt; and 3) an “octahedral core-shell structure” consisting of specific {111} facets only to optimize the structural effect of the Pt alloy. In this proposed research, we will investigate the synthesis, characterization, evaluation and stability of “shape-controlled core-shell electrocatalysts” with novel techniques and approaches. We will develop new protocols to synthesize sub-10nm octahedral core-shell nanoparticles with inexpensive transition metals such as Ni and metal oxides such as TiO2 as the core materials. A uniform Pt-Ni shell that is only 1-2 nm thick with an octahedral crystal structure will be the key to enabling the intended high ORR activity. The activity and stability of these shape-controlled catalysts will be evaluated in both liquid cells and fuel cells to demonstrate their feasibility in fuel cell applications. The results will aid the fabrication of highly active and cost-competitive electrocatalysts for PEMFCs. We will also explore thermally and chemically induced structural evolution using both experimental and theoretical approaches. The results will shed light on the pathways and kinetic energy barriers associated with atomic interdiffusion in core-shell structures. 質子交換膜燃料電池（PEMFC）是一種潔淨的能源轉換裝置，在電動車領域受到極大關注。但是其陰極中昂貴的鉑催化劑（用於催化氧氣還原反應）使得PEMFC商業化受阻。要使燃料電池成本降低，必須發展比負載鉑更高效、便宜的催化劑。具有八面體結構的鉑合金催化劑比負載鉑具有更高的活性，但是其形成機理還不清楚。本課題致力於研究八面體合金納米顆粒合成過程中結構和組分的變化路徑以及不同反應物種在形貌控制中的作用。 本課題還將結合三個策略設計一種全新的氧氣還原催化劑：1）具有便宜的核和鉑基壳的核-壳結構；2）可提高比表面活性的鉑合金壳；3）具有（111）晶面的八面體結構將結構效益最大化。我們將研究這種形貌可控的八面體核-壳結構的合成，表徵，測試和穩定性。我們將發展新的合成方法來製備過渡金屬或其氧化物壳（鎳或二氧化鈦）。還將鉑鎳合金壳厚度控制在1-2 納米。其活性和穩定性將在電化學池和燃料電池的測試。我們希望這種新型催化劑將大大降低燃料電池的成本。我們還將從實驗和理論上研究由溫度引起的結構變化機制，這將為探明核-壳結構在原子水平上結構變化指明方向。

16304117.label: Realisation of objectives
16304117.value: 1. To establish the structural and composition evolution paths of octahedral Pt bimetallic nanocrystals during their synthesis and durability testing and clarify the role of W(CO)6 in morphology control. This objective has been fully achieved. By combining high resolution TEM, elemental mapping, XPS, and electrochemical techniques, we concluded the following mechanism of formation of Pt-Ni octahedra: at temperatures below 140 °C, Pt(acac)2 were reduced with the assistance of W forming ~3 nm sphere-like pure Pt seeds, which began to transform into truncated octahedra at ~160 °C. At higher temperatures, Pt and Ni ions were co-reduced. With the assistance of CO generated from the decomposition of W(CO)6, Pt and Ni atoms might mainly deposit on (100) surfaces resulting in an octahedral shape. The morphology transformation to octahedron was nearly completed at 170 °C. Most of the Pt and Ni ions, however, were reduced between 180 and 210 °C with the edge length increasing from 5.7 to 9.0 nm. In this step, Pt and Ni atoms were deposited uniformly on the surface following an epitaxial growth mechanism, resulting in a core-shell structure consisting of a Pt-rich core and a uniform Pt-Ni shell. W(CO)6 not only provides CO to control the morphology of Pt-Ni, but also generates W0 to facilitate the reduction of Pt and Ni ions. During potential cycling, the distributions of Pt and Ni change significantly even though the ORR activity of Pt-Ni octahedra only drops slightly. The octahedral shape is maintained after 10000 cycles. The Ni atoms are removed from the surface and sublayers of Pt-Ni octahedra, resulting in an octahedral nanostructure consisting of a Pt-rich shell, a Pt-Ni alloy interlayer and a Pt-rich core . The excellent stability of Pt-Ni octahedra under the current testing condition can be ascribed to the formation of a thick (1-1.5 nm) and stable Pt layer. 2. To develop an optimized protocol for the synthesis of sub-10nm octahedral core-shell nanoparticles consisting of inexpensive transition metals and metal oxide cores and ultrathin (1-2 nm) Pt alloy shells. This objective has been fully achieved. The synthesis of Ru and Ru oxide seeds and following Pt-Ni shell deposition was optimized. In the synthesis of Ru@Pt-Ni core-shell nanoparticles, Ru nanoparticles with an average particle size of ~4 nm was synthesized via the following protocol: 5 mmol of Ru(acac)3 and 50 mmol of PVP were added to 20 ml EG in a 50 ml three-necked flask at room temperature. The stock solution was heated to 80°C and evacuated at this temperature for 20 min to remove water and oxygen under magnetic stirring. The solution was then heated to 180°C at a rate of 10°C min-1 and maintained at this temperature for 2 h under Ar. The mixture was cooled down to room temperature, centrifuged, washed with acetone and dispersed in 10 ml EG. Pure oxygen was purged into the colloidal Ru seeds for 3 hr. We found that if the surface of Ru seeds was oxidized, the morphology of the core-shell materials were better defined. Next, we deposited the Pt-Ni shell on Ru core. In a standard synthesis of Ru@Pt-Ni octahedra, 20 mg of Pt(acac)2 and 10 mg of Ni(acac)2 were mixed with 2 ml OAm, 1 ml OA and 2 ml Ru-EG seeds in 5 ml BE, followed by the addition of 50 mg of W(CO)6 at 130 °C under Ar protection. The mixture was then heated to 230 °C, while the Ar purging was stopped at the same time. The Ru@Pt-Ni were obtained after the reaction was allowed to proceed at 230 °C for 40 min. Then the product was centrifuged and washed by organic solvent. After loaded on carbon, the solid powders were collected and dried at 60 °C for 1 h. 3. To determine the mechanisms of thermally induced interdiffusion between core and shell atoms and the minimum temperature at which structural evolution commences through a combined experimental and theoretical study. This objective has been fully achieved. We used Vienna ab initio simulation package (VASP) to simulate the interdiffusion between the core and shell. The surface structure was modeled by a slab of six layers of metal and 14 Å vacuum between periodically-repeated surfaces to avoid spurious surface interactions. The two bottom layers of the slabs were fixed, while the upper layers were fully relaxed. A nudged elastic band (NEB) was implemented to determine the minimum energy path for the diffusion of a core atom from the subsurface layer to a vacancy introduced in the Pt monolayer at the surface of the model. The DFT calculation results indicate that it is kinetically favorable for Pd to migrate to the surface via a vacancy and consequently alloy with Pt in the surface above this critical temperature (270 °C). 4. To evaluate the activity and stability of the nanoparticles developed above in both liquid cells and fuel cells, and to assess the feasibility of the proposed catalyst in fuel cell applications. This objective has been fully achieved. The Ru@PtNi core-shell catalysts were tested in a membrane electrode assembly (MEA) and compared with Pt/C. In the low current density region, the core-shell catalyst exhibits a 40 mV improvement over Pt/C. However, the performance in the higher current density region was worse than Pt/C. Possible reasons include the formation of RuO2 which is hydrophilic causing flooding in the cathode, the dissolution of Ni and Ru resulting in a lower proton conductivity, and the un-optimized fabrication of MEA.

16304317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16304317.value: Factor models provide good fit and valuable insights for many important applications in finance and economics. In this project, we aim to advance statistical inference theory for large factor models. The main objects of interest are the principal eigenvectors, the covariance/precision matrix and their applications to portfolio management. We shall develop tests for principal eigenvectors, which can be used to compare observable economic factors with latent statistical factors, and to detect structural changes in factors over time. We will also study the estimation of covariance/precision matrix under factor models. Finally, we will investigate large portfolio optimization, under both the mean-variance and minimum-variance frameworks. 因子模型在很多重要的金融及經濟研究中被證明行之有效及能夠提供有價值的洞見。 在這項研究中，我們致力於推動關於大維因子模型的統計推斷理論。 主要研究對象包括主特徵向量，協方差及其逆矩陣，和它們在投資組合管理上的應用。 我們將建立關於主特徵向量的檢驗。這種檢驗能夠用來比較基於經濟因素的（可觀測到的）因子是否與基於統計推斷出的內在因子接近，還可以用來發現因子是否隨時間發生結構性的變化。 我們還會研究因子模型下協方差及其逆矩陣的估計。最後，我們會利用上面的結果來研究在均值-方差意義和最小方差意義下的大維投資組合優化。

16304317.label: Major findings and research outcome
16304317.value: 1. Jointly with Tony Cai, Jianchang Hu, and Yingying Li, we studied the estimation of high-dimensional minimum variance portfolio (MVP) based on high-frequency data. Under certain sparsity assumptions on the precision matrix, we propose estimators of MVP and prove that our portfolios asymptotically achieve the minimum variance in a sharp sense. Simulation and empirical studies demonstrate that our proposed portfolios perform favorably. The paper has been published in the Journal of Econometrics. 2. Jointly with my former PhD Xinxin Yang and postdoc Jiaqi Chen, we studied tests of high-dimensional covariance matrix under the elliptical model. The paper has been published in the Journal of Econometrics. 3. Jointly with our PhD student Yi Ding and Yingying Li, we studied the estimation of high-dimensional MVP under statistical factor models. Our estimator utilizes factor structure in returns and enjoys sharp risk consistency. In terms of covariance matrix estimation, we extend the theoretical results of POET (Fan, Liao, and Mincheva (2013, JRSSB) to a setting that is coherent with principal component analysis. The paper has been published in the Journal of Econometrics. 4. Jointly with Jianqing Fan, Yingying Li, and my former postdoc Ningning Xia, we developed tests for principal eigenvalues and eigenvectors under the large factor model setting. We're at the final stage of writing up the manuscript and will submit it to a top econometrics journal soon.

16304317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16304317.value: We have identified several interesting and important questions to be further investigated along the direction. In particular, we will study predictions of large cross-sectional returns/volatilities utilizing results obtained in this project.

16304317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16304317.value: The outcomes obtained in this project have significant values in portfolio allocation and econometric analysis of the financial market. We developed methods for estimating both mean-variance optimization and minimum-variance portfolios. Our methods have sound theoretical properties and also empirically perform well. Our tests for high-dimensional covariance matrices and principal eigenvalues/eigenvectors allow for a deep investigation into dependency in the financial market.

16304517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16304517.value: Wave control at the subwavelength scale has drawn much attention in recent years because of its fascinating applications in areas such as super-resolution in imaging, super-focusing, and cloaking. The control of waves can be realized with meta-materials made of subwavelength structures. Near the resonant frequency of the constituent subwavelength structure, meta-material exhibits macroscopic properties such as a negative reflective index, which cannot be found in ordinary materials. Away from the resonant frequency, such extraordinary properties may disappear. Many interesting mathematical questions related to resonance and homogenization theory have arisen. A two-scale convergence method is usually used to study periodically arranged microstructures, under the assumption that a uniform bound exists on the sequence of microscopic wave fields. However, this may not be true at the resonant frequency of the constituent subwavelength resonators. Moreover, the condition on the periodic arrangement of substructures imposes severe restrictions upon many applications, such as in transformation optics, in which the effective media needs to be inhomogeneous. To overcome the above restrictions, the principal investigator proposes to develop a homogenization theory for subwavelength resonators that are not necessarily arranged periodically and for which the frequency is near their resonant frequencies. He will consider a bulk meta-material with finite size that consists of a large number of subwavelength resonators and investigate the limit when the number of resonators increases to infinity, while the frequency remains near the resonant frequency for an individual resonator. The aim is to achieve the following goals: 1) identify the conditions on the configuration of the resonators such that an effective media theory holds; 2) determine the relationship among the effective parameters, and the individual resonator, and the configuration; 3) determine the dispersion relation near the resonant frequency. To illustrate the main ideas of the proposed non-periodic homogenization theory, the principal investigator will consider two types of meta-materials: one is made of plasmonic particles and the other of high-contrast particles. In the former case, the principal investigator will demonstrate the mechanism of fabricating high-contrast and high-anisotropy optical materials, and in the latter case, he will demonstrate the mechanism of fabricating double negative acoustic materials. The proposed homogenization theory is based on the layer potential theory, asymptotic analysis, multiple scattering theory, and point interaction approximation. 由于在超分辨率成像，超汇聚还有隐形等领域的应用， 在次波长尺度上对波的控制在最近变得热门起来. 对波的控制可以通过由次波长结构组成的超材料来实现。 在这些次波长结构的共振频率附近，超材料能够表现出一般材料不具备的奇特的宏观效应，例如负折射率。 而在共振频率外， 这些性质则消失了。 这里产生了大量的关于共振和同质化的有趣的数学问题。 一般来说，对于周期布置的微结构可以用二阶收敛方法来研究，这其中需要假设一个一致界限存在于微波场的序列上。但是，这个假设可能 在共振频率处不正确。此外，对于微结构的周期排列的这个条件限制了许多应用，如转换光学，那里的介质要求是不均匀的。 为了克服上述限制，该项目负责人提出一套同质化理论专门针对这种非周期性地布置的次波长共振器在共振频率附近的问题。 他将考虑一个尺寸有界的由许多次波长共振器构成的超材料，在共振器数量趋向无穷大，而频率保持在共振频率附近时的性质。 借此希望达到以下目的：1。识别谐振器排列的条件，使得同质化理论成立；2.确定有效参数和单个谐振器以及其排列之间的关系；3.确定在共振频率附近的色散关系。 为了说明所提出的非周期同质化理论的主要想法，项目负责人将考虑两种类型的超材料：一种是由等离子颗粒构成而另一种是由高对比颗粒构成。在前一种情况下， 他将揭示制作高对比度和高各向异性的光学材料的机制，在后一种情况下，他将展示 制造负折射声学材料的机理。这个同质化理论是建立在层势理论，渐近分析，多重散射理论和点相互作用近似的基础上的。

16304517.label: Realisation of objectives
16304517.value: For plasmonic particles in the dilute regime, we have rigorously justified the Maxwell–Garnett theory which gives the relation between the effective electric and magnetic parameters and the parameters (including the shape) of the constituent plasmonic particles and their volume fraction when the frequency is close to the resonant frequency of the constituent particles. It shows that the effective parameters are high-anisotropy and high-contrast. For the general case of no-periodical plasmonic particles, we resort to the multiple scattering formulation. Due to the fact that different plasmonic resonances are coupled, the scattering by multiple particles can be very complicated. We developed and analyzed three schemes for the scattering approximation. The first is the resonant expansion which uses the resonant modes of the system of particles computed by a conformal transformation, the second is the hybridized resonant expansion which uses linear combinations of the resonant modes for each of the particles in the system as a basis, and the last one is the multipole expansion with respect to the origin. We demonstrated the relations between these expansion schemes and their advantages and disadvantages both analytically and numerically. In particular, we showed the efficiency of the resonant expansion scheme in approximating the near field of the system of particles. These results have paved the way for the homogenization theory of a large number of non-periodic plasmonic particles. For the high contrast particles, we consider the model of air bubbles in the fluid. We have derived the asymptotic for the Minnaert resonance for a single bubble and justified the point scatter approximation. Based on this, we developed a homogenization theory for bubbly media. Under certain assumptions on the configuration, we showed that the effective media has a high refractive index and hence can be used to realize super-focusing. The dependence of the effective refractive index on the frequency and the configuration is also given explicitly. We further consider bubble dimers that are made of two identical bubbles. We have derived the asymptotic formula for the two hybridized Minnaert resonances. We further showed that the bubble dimer can be approximated by a point scatterer with monopole and dipole modes. Based on these results, we showed that for an appropriate volume fraction of bubble dimers with certain conditions on their configuration, a double negative effective medium when the frequency is near the anti-resonance of the hybridized Minnaert resonances can be obtained. The dependence of the effective mass and effective bulk modulus on the frequency and configurations of the bubble dimer is also derived.

16304517.label: Major findings and research outcome
16304517.value: 1. For the scattering by multiple plasmonic particles in the non-diluted regime, homogenization can be obtained through the scattering approximation under certain conditions. By comparing different approximation schemes, we found that the resonant expansion scheme is most efficient in approximating the near fields when the frequency is close to the resonant frequencies. The associated scattering is very dispersive and can be explained by the effective parameters that are high-anisotropy and high-contrast. 2. For a high contrast particle such as an air bubble in the fluid, a subwavelength resonance called the Minnaert resonance can be excited and the particle behaves as a resonant monopole scatterer. With a large number of such particles, effective negative bulk modulus can be produced. When the single bubble is replaced by a bubble dimmer which consists of two identical bubbles, the Minnaert resonances are hybridized and the dimmer behaves as a linear combination of resonant monopole scatterer and dipole scatterer. With a large number of such dimers near the resonant frequency, one can produce an effective double negative media. 3. We further investigate the anomalous scattering by a periodic array of narrow slit structures in a metallic slab which is another typical subwavelength resonator due to the Fabry-Perot type resonance. We showed that with a periodic arrangement of such slit structures where one periodic cell contains two, an embedded eigenvalue for the scattering problem exists under certain symmetry conditions. Under small perturbation which destroys the symmetry, the embedded eigenvalue dissolves into scattering resonance which further results in a Fano-type resonance in the transmission spectrum. Moreover, we further showed that without the symmetry conditions, but assuming that the two-slit structures in a periodic cell are strongly coupled, Fano-type resonance still can be produced in the transmission spectrum. Interestingly, this Fano-type resonance is not generated from the embedded eigenvalue.

16304517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16304517.value: In the project, by working on several typical models, the PI has developed a rigorous non-periodic homogenization theory for subwavelength resonators. The theory aims to address the following fundamental design questions in the field of meta-material: given electromagnetic or acoustic parameters that are not available in the usual materials such as high anisotropy, or negative, can one design and fabricate these materials with existing usual ones? The results obtained in the project provide guidance on the design of metamaterials using subwavelength resonators. They also provide a mathematical framework and foundation for the study of metamaterials.

16304717.label: Project Objectives
16304717.value: Design artificial EM wave structures carrying Weyl points in momentum space. We are particularly interested in structures that are easy to fabricate and those that possess exotic features, such as multiple Weyl points with high topological charge and type-II Weyl points. Fabricate these structures in the microwave regime and experimentally characterize their dispersions and surface states. Explore various novel phenomena, such as multimode one-way surface states, tunable power splitters and enhanced anomalous velocity effects. Extend the concept to other kinds of waves, such as the acoustic and/or elastic waves.

16304717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16304717.value: As demonstrated by the discovery of new phases of matter called topological insulators, topological physics has been one of the most active research fields in recent years. In mathematics, topology is concerned with properties that are preserved under deformation or perturbation (impurities, defects or changes in the parameters of a system). In physics, topological principles are manifested in phenomena such as quantized Hall conductance, bulk-surface correspondences and robust surface transport. Weyl point, a type of topological nodal point, is a band degeneracy point in three-dimensional reciprocal space. These degeneracy points are stable under perturbation, in the sense that parameter changes in the system can shift the position of a Weyl point but cannot lift the degeneracy. Its topological character is also manifest in the associated surface states, which are guaranteed by bulk-surface correspondence and do not rely on surface termination. Weyl nodal points have been theorized to occur, and experimentally observed, in “Weyl semimetals” such as TaAs. Many interesting phenomena can be found in these electronic systems, topologically-protected surface states, quantum anomalous Hall effect, and chiral anomaly, for example. However, experimentally realizing Weyl points and their associated topological properties remains challenging, as it is extremely difficult to fine-tune the properties of real (rather than theoretical) electronic materials. In the past decade, researchers have extended topological ideas from condensed matter physics to photonics. The exploitation of topological concepts has the potential to improve the robustness of photonic devices in the presence of imperfections. Weyl points with a charge of one have been predicted and observed in a “gyroid” photonic crystal. The robust surface states associated with single Weyl points have also been detected by our group. In addition, some exotic variations of Weyl points, such as multiple Weyl points and type-II Weyl points, have been proposed but have yet to be demonstrated in certain types of crystals. We aim to design and fabricate microwave photonic crystals with multiple and type-II Weyl points. These structures should be compatible with planar fabrication technology and can be constructed using printed circuit boards. The nature of the Weyl points can be experimentally confirmed by checking their dispersions in different directions using angle-resolved transmission measurements. We will also investigate the interesting phenomena associated with exotic Weyl points, such as the anomalous velocity effect induced by multiple Weyl points, the collimation effect due to type-II Weyl points and the multimode one-way surface states due to multiple charges. 隨著拓撲絕緣體這類新的物質相被發現，拓撲物理學已成為近年來最活躍的研究領域之一。拓撲是一個數學概念，它關注的是系統在連續形變或擾動（雜質、缺陷或系統的參數變化）下保持的特性。物理學中，系統的拓撲性質在量子霍爾電導、晶體的體邊緣對應關係、表面態的看散射傳輸這類現象中得到了體現。外爾點是一類受拓撲保護的節點，即三維倒空間中的能帶簡併點。這類簡併點在參數擾動下相當穩定，即系統的參數改變只會移動簡併點在倒空間中的位置而不會打破簡併（打開帶隙）。外爾點的拓撲性質還體現在，體邊緣對應關係保證了表面態的存在且不依賴於表面的截斷情況。外爾點已被理論預言、實驗證實存在一類被稱為外爾半金屬的晶體中，例如砷化鉭。研究者在這些電子體系中發現了許多有趣的物理現象，如拓撲保護的表面態、量子反常霍爾效應、手征性反常。然而實驗中實現外爾點及它們的相關拓撲性質頗具挑戰性，因很難對真實電子材料的材料參數進行微調。 在過去十年裡，研究者已將凝聚態物理中的拓撲概念拓展到光學領域。探索光學體系中的拓撲態有望用於提升光學器件性能的穩定性。人們已經在螺旋光子晶體中觀測到攜帶單一拓撲荷的外爾點。我們課題組已驗證了這類單重外爾點對應的表面態及其抗散射特性。此外，研究者還提出在特定對稱性的晶體中還存在多重外爾點、第二類外爾點，這些外爾點的奇異變體仍未被實驗證實。 我們將設計、製備具備多重外爾點、第二類外爾點的微波波段光子晶體。這些結構應與現有的平面製作工藝相容，可用印刷電路板實現。通過測量這類晶體的角分辨透射譜，我們可以驗證倒空間中外爾點附近的色散關係。我們還將研究這些變種外爾點相關的物理現象，如第二類外爾點的準直效應、多重拓撲荷導致的反常速度效應及多模單向表面態。

16304717.label: Realisation of objectives
16304717.value: We have designed various artificial EM wave structures carrying Weyl points in momentum space [Objective 1]. We fabricated them in the microwave regime and we have experimentally characterized their dispersions and surface states [Objective 2]. We demonstrated and explored various new and novel phenomena arising from such topological structures [Objective 3]. The objectives are all achieved and the achievements are detailed below. We found that some of Weyl point bearing structure has very unusual properties at low frequencies. A class of such structures, containing metallic scaffolds with chiral structures possesses very special long wavelength limit behavior. In particular, such EM structure carries multiple index ellipsoids located at nonzero k-points. The shift of index ellipsoid away from k=0 can be viewed as the consequence of a synthetic gauge potential, the characteristics of Weyl crystals. These EM structures have an orientation-dependent coupling effect when interfaced with an ordinary material. We experimentally observed the shifted index ellipse and the abnormal coupling effect in microwave regime using a 2D implementation. There several aspects of this work those are worth emphasizing. While almost all existing EM metamaterials are based on local resonances, the structure proposed in this work derive their properties from real space global topology/connectivity. This is a new concept. [Nature Communications 9 (1), 2086 (2018).] When a degenerate pair of Weyl points carrying opposite chirality collide in momentum space, 3D Dirac points can form if some specific symmetry forbids their annihilation. We designed, fabricated and experimentally realized metamaterials which carries such 3D photonic nodal points in the microwave regime. Two symmetrically placed Dirac points are stabilized by electromagnetic duality symmetry, which is unique to the Maxwell equations. Spin-polarized surface arcs on truncated surfaces were observed, which paves the way toward implementing spin-multiplexed topological surface wave propagation. [Phys. Rev. Lett. 122, 203903 (2019). ] We considered the realization of photonic topological semimetals in bianisotropic metamaterials characterized by a chirality tensor with a zero trace. We found that the strength of chirality component determines the topological character of the metamaterial. In particular, photonic quantum Hall states exist when the longitudinal chirality component exceeds the permittivity, whereas photonic quantum spin Hall states are present when the chiral nihility occurs. Considering the dispersion in the frequency domain, the bianisotropic metamaterial is a photonic Weyl system that supports the Weyl points and Fermi arcs. The topological features are further illustrated with the robust transport of edge states at an irregular boundary of the metamaterial [Scientific Reports 9:18312 (2019)]. Weyl points are counterparts of magnetic monopole in momentum space. We proposed a method to realize the nexus point as a new kind of magnetic monopole in k-space. We showed that in an AB-layer-stacked photonic crystal composed of anisotropic dielectrics, the unique photonic band connectivity leads to a new kind of symmetry-enforced triply degenerate points at the nexuses of two nodal rings and a Kramers-like nodal line. Berry fluxes are confined on the nodal lines due to PT symmetry, serving as a counterpart of cosmic strings connecting magnetic monopoles. We showed that spin-1 conical diffraction occurs at the nexus point, which can be used to manipulate the charges of optical vortices. [Light: Science & Applications 9:176 (2020)]. Berry curvature, the counterpart of the magnetic field in the momentum space, plays a vital role in the transport of electrons in condensed matter physics. In 3D systems, Weyl points serve as sources and drains of Berry curvature. We designed, fabricated and characterized a photonic metamaterial which carries a momentum space toroidal moment of Berry curvature with flux approaching to π. The Berry curvature exhibits a vortex-like configuration without any source and drain in the momentum space. Experimentally, the presence of Berry curvature toroid is confirmed by the observation of conical-frustum shaped domain-wall states at the interfaces formed by two metamaterials with opposite toroidal moments [Nature Communications, 12:1784 (2021)]. We designed, fabricated and characterized an electromagnetic metacrystal which carries topologically nontrivial nodal surface degeneracies and a charge-2 Weyl point. The nodal surface is protected by a combination of two-fold screw rotation and time-reversal symmetry. We have experimentally observed surface state arcs that are derived from helicoidal sheets of surface states connecting the nodal surface with the charge-2 Weyl point [submitted]. Weyl points are topological isolated points of degeneracy, and exist in the absence of PT symmetry. Nodal line are line degeneracies usually protected by mirror or PT symmetry. We realized photonic nodal lines with quadrupole Berry curvature distribution. We designed and realized a novel type of photonic straight nodal lines in a D2d microwave meta-crystal which are protected by roto-inversion time (roto-PT) symmetry. The nodal lines are located at the center and hinges of the Brillouin zone. They appear as sources/sinks of quadrupole Berry curvature distribution and allow for the precise control of the quadrupole strength. Interestingly, there exist topological surface states at all three cutting surfaces, and as frequency changes, the surface state EFCs evolve from closed to open contour, and become straight lines at a critical transition frequency, at which diffraction-less surface wave propagation and super-imaging are demonstrated [submitted]. We extended our concept to other kinds of waves [Objective 4], including acoustic waves and waves traveling in networks. We elaborate our achievements in the following. As Dirac/Weyl nodal points are not constrained by Lorentz invariance, they can exhibit tipped-over type-II cones that provide highly anisotropic physical properties. We proposed a band-folding scheme for constructing type-II nodal points, and realized such nodal points in acoustics. Samples were made and the type-II points are experimentally visualized using near-field mappings. As a direct effect of tipped-over Dirac cones, strongly tilted kink states originating from their valley-Hall properties are also observed. This deterministic scheme could serve as an acoustic wave platform for further investigations associated with various strongly Lorentz-violating nodal points [Physical Review Letters 124, 075501 (2020)]. We designed a network based from a structure that bears Weyl points in 3D space. In the z-direction, we impose a special boundary condition to induce a new type of angular-momentum and wave-vector locking, which is analogous to the spin-momentum locking in quantum spin Hall systems. The coupling between the angular momentum and the wave vector gives non-trivial topological effects. We demonstrated the idea experimentally with a transmission line network. We show experimentally that such systems exhibit angular momentum-dependent one-way topological edge states, and their properties can be described in terms of local Chern numbers [Nature Communications 10, 434 (2019)]. The physics behind the network system and their relationship with tight-binding model and topological physics is reviewed and discussed in an invited article [Acta Physica Sinica, 69, 150301 (2020)]. As a follow up work on twisting structures that give rise to Weyl points, we found that network with twisted connectivity can give rise to amazing topology. The global invariants of topological materials are usually characterized by integers, such as Chern numbers. We designed a PT symmetric network system in which the topological character is given by quaternions. We experimentally observed the non-Abelian topological quaternion charges in the network. We proposed non-Abelian bulk-edge correspondence, where edge states are found to be described by non-Abelian charges. Our work opens the door towards non-Abelian topological phase characterization and manipulation [Nature (accepted, 2021)].

16304717.label: Major findings and research outcome
16304717.value: We have designed various artificial EM wave structures carrying Weyl points in momentum space. We fabricated them in the microwave regime and we have experimentally characterized their dispersions and surface states. We demonstrated and explored various new and novel phenomena arising from such topological structures. We extended our concept to other kinds of waves. We used a material-by-design approach: • Start with abstract mathematics and physical intuition. • Formulate the problem mathematically and see what type of symmetry is required. • Use analytic or semi-analytic model (typically tight-binding and effective medium) to calculate the band structures that are compatible with the group symmetry. • Do simulations with real design parameters and compute the real band structures. Optimize the parameters to get a blue print. • Fabricate the structure according to the blue print. • Do field measurements. • Realize and understand interesting phenomena. The physics we learned: We found that artificial materials with a “twist” in their structure can generate Weyl points in momentum space [1,2,4,5,12]. The “twist” breaks PT symmetry, a requirement for the existence of Weyl points. Such structures can be fabricated with standard PCB technologies [1,3,9,12,13]. Weyl points can have charge more than one when Weyl points of the same chirality overlap and we realized charge 2 Weyl point which have quadratic in dispersion in two of the k-coordinates and they can be realized in twisting structures [12]. Weyl points of opposite charity can overlap without annihilation if they are protected by extra symmetries and in that case, they are called 3D Dirac points [3]. Weyl points serve as momentum space magnetic monopoles and such monopoles and other topological degeneracies can generate Berry flux, which can be considered as momentum space magnetic field or a synthetic gauge field [1,4,9,13]. In some structures, the Berry flux can be localized in nodal lines which can be considered as counterparts of cosmic strings. The nodal points that such “strings” meet are nexus points [10]. The Berry flux or synthetic gauge field can give rise to Chern numbers when the flux is integrated on a 2D subsystem that defines a 2D plane in momentum space. Due to bulk-edge correspondence, such bulk topological invariants give rise to chiral surface modes that are one-way going and are robust against disorder [3,11,12]. These concepts also apply to other kinds of waves such as acoustic waves and network systems [2,5,6,8]. *[The cited numbers refer to the ordering of the publications in Part C].

16304717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16304717.value: Weyl nodal points are topologically nontrivial two band degeneracy points. They are sources of momentum space Berry flux and as such they are momentum space magnetic monopoles. In this project, we have successfully demonstrated how they can be realized in microwave electromagnetic crystals and we generalized it to other kinds of wave. Most of the structures we have designed can be made with standard technology suitable for fabrication in the microwave regime. We can consider extending the work to optical frequencies. The Hamiltonian we have studied are Hermitian. Extending to non-Hermitian Hamiltonians (i.e. considering gain and loss) would be worth pursuing. We will write proposals to address these issues. Weyl nodes are two band two-fold degeneracy. When we extend our consideration from 2 bands to multiple bands, we would require a non-Abelian prescription to discuss the topology. We will write proposals to address these issues. Weyl points can be considered as a topological momentum space magnetic monopole. We can consider other structures that leads to momentum space electric and magnetic multipoles. The application potential of "Fermi arc" type of the surface modes can be further investigated.

16304717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16304717.value: When information is transported from one point to another by propagating a wave through a medium, interruptions are inevitable when the wave encounters disorder or imperfections, as the wave will be scattered to other directions. It would be highly desirable if electromagnetic signals can be transported uninterruptedly. If a one-way-only transport channel can be designed, the problem can be mitigated as the signal cannot be scattered back. It is known that for transmission of signals using electrons (as in electronic instruments), that are multiple ways to induce one-way-only transport, such as using diodes or by imposing a magnetic field. For classical waves, diodes are difficult to realize. Magnetic field is sometimes useful in classical waves, but usually inconvenient to implement. We showed here that some meticulously designed artificial materials (“metamaterials”) carry certain objects call Weyl points which can generate the equivalent of a magnetic field (called Berry flux) which can induce one-way-only transport channels for electromagnetic and acoustic waves on the surface of the metamaterial. Our results showed that a cross fertilization of ideas between physics and mathematics can potentially pave the way for new paradigms of wave control and manipulation and robust transport.

16304817.label: Project Objectives
16304817.value: To produce narrowband biphotons with polarization-frequency or time-bin entanglement and test their violation of the Bell’s inequality. To test and verify the quantum nonlocality of EPR continuous time-frequency entanglement of narrowband biphotons.

16304817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16304817.value: Nonlocality caused by entanglement, as one of the most fundamental properties of quantum mechanics, plays a key role in many applications of quantum communication, quantum computation, and quantum metrology. Violation of Bell’s inequality provides a standard testing platform for verifying the non-classical predictions of quantum entanglement and ruling out the local hidden variable theories that are in compatible with quantum mechanics. Previous studies have focused on wide-band entangled photon pairs (biphotons) with short coherence time and length produced by spontaneous parametric down conversion in nonlinear solid state materials. Here we propose to investigate the quantum nonlocality of narrowband biphotons with time-frequency entanglement generated from four-wave mixing in laser-cooled atoms, whose coherence time ranges from 100 to 1000 ns and coherence length ranges from 30 to 300 meters. We will make use of the time-resolved detection to reveal the rich quantum features of the biphoton nonlocal temporal and spatial correlations. Our research will lead to important applications in quantum information science and technology based on time-frequency entanglement. 作為量子力學最基本的特性之一，量子糾纏引起的非局域性在量子通訊，量子計算，和量子計量中發揮著非常重要的作用。違反貝爾不等式的實驗驗證不僅提供了一個驗證量子糾纏非經典性的平台，而且有助於排除與量子力學不兼容的局域隱變量理論。由於實驗條件的限制，以前的大多數研究侷限於寬帶光子對；這些寬帶光子對從非線性固體材料以參量下轉換的方式長生，具有很短的相干時間和長度。在這裡，我們提出一個研究時間-頻率糾纏的窄帶光子對的量子非局域性方案，其中窄帶光子對從激光冷卻原子中通過四波混頻的方式產生 。這些窄帶光子對的相干時間達到100到1000納秒，其相干長度達到30到300米。我們將利用具有時間分辨率的光子探測去揭示雙光子在非局域的時空光聯中所具有的豐富的量子行為。我們的研究對基於時間-頻率糾纏的量子信息科技具有重要的價值。

16304817.label: Major findings and research outcome
16304817.value: We have achieved the following major findings and research outcomes: (1) A quantum-memory-based beam splitter for single photons We have successfully generated time-frequency entangled narrowband biphotons and investigated their nonlocal behaviours on a quantum-memory-based beam splitter. As shown in Fig.1, time-frequency entangled narrowband photon pairs (biphotons) are produced via spontaneous four-wave mixing in cold atoms in MOT A. Upon detecting a Stokes photon at SPCMs, its entangled anti-Stokes photon is sent to the quantum-memory-based beam splitter at MOT B. In such a quantum-memory beam splitter, the photon wave packet is converted (stored) into a collective atomic spin state and later retrieved (split) into two opposing directions. We can dynamically control and configure the storage time, beam splitting ratio, and relative phase. The result supports that heralded single photons from time-frequency entangled biphotons with frequency anti-correlation can be in a pure state. We also experimentally confirm that such a beam splitter preserves the quantum particle nature of the single photon and its coherence. This work was published in Physical Review A 97, 063805 (2018). Representative Publications: [1] Phys. Rev. A 97, 063805 (2018). (2) Efficient quantum memory for single-photon polarization qubits Making use of heralded single photons from the produced narrowband (0.39 MHz) biphotons, we demonstrate the world most efficient (>85%) quantum memory for single-photon polarization qubits with >99% fidelity. A quantum memory is a key element for large-scale quantum networks and quantum computation, but all previous other works have efficiencies far below 50% for true single photons. Our result pushes the optical quantum memory a step closer to practical applications in quantum information processing. This work was published in Nature Photonics 13, 346 (2019) [2] and was selected as its cover story. Representative Publications: [2] Nature Photonics 13, 346 (2019). (3) Direct characterization of EPR energy-time entanglement We demonstrated the direct characterization of EPR energy-time entanglement and obtained a joint frequency-time uncertainty product of 0.063+/-0.0044, which is a new world record and satisfies the continuous variable EPR steering inequality. Our result shows, as compared to other wideband photon source, our narrowband energy-time entangled biphotons are more suitable for long-distance quantum steering, and thus will have important applications in quantum communication and network based on quantum nonlocality. This work was published in Physical Review Letters 124, 010509 (2020) [3]. Representative Publications: [3] Phys. Rev. Lett. 124, 010509 (2020).

16305117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16305117.value: The goal of the proposed experimental research is to study internal resonance in micromechanical resonators. Micromechanical resonators are widely used as sensors and actuators. In resonant sensors, vibrations of the micromechanical element are often excited by a periodic drive near the resonance frequency. By tracking changes in the resonance frequencies of a particular vibrational mode, the devices can be used in applications that range from inertial sensing to high-sensitivity force and mass detection. When an integer multiple of the vibrational frequency of one mode approaches the frequency of a higher mode, internal resonance occur, accompanied by efficient energy exchange between the modes. Researchers have shown that internal resonances can have a remarkable effect on vibrations, including stabilization of the frequency of a nonlinear oscillator. The emphasis of the proposed research will be placed on revealing the various mechanisms that internal resonance can affect the energy dissipation of mechanical vibrations and modify the spectral response. Two vibrational modes of a micromechanical resonator will be involved. The system can be tuned in and out of internal resonance by modifying the frequency of the higher mode by either its nonlinear dependence on the vibration amplitude or by spring softening due to electrostatic forces. Preliminary simulations indicate that internal resonance gives rise to anomalous nonlinear friction. In the ringdown of vibrations, the decay rate is no longer constant and instead varies non-monotonically with amplitude. We propose to explore how the energy exchange between the two modes can be utilized to stabilize the vibration frequency and enhance the detection sensitivity. Furthermore, we plan to perform a comprehensive study of the effects of internal resonance on the spectral response when the natural frequencies of the two modes are tuned to be integer multiples of each other. Successful implementation of the proposed projects will not only stimulate new theoretical research and verify the validity of various theoretical approaches, but could also lead to micromechanical detectors of improved sensitivity and functionality. The PI has extensive experience with fluctuational phenomena in micromechanical devices. In the past few years, his group performed an extensive investigation of the switching between coexisting vibration states induced by Gaussian and Poisson noise on a nonlinear micromechanical torsional oscillator under strong periodic drive. The PI will work closely with Prof. Mark Dykman, a theorist at Michigan State University to reveal novel behaviors in nonlinear friction and internal resonances in micromechanical resonators. 我們建議的實驗研究的目標是研究微機械諧振器中的內共振現象。微機械諧振器被廣泛應用于傳感器和致動器。在諧振傳感器中，微機械元件的振動通常由近共振頻率的週期性驅動力激發。通過監測特定模式共振頻率的變化，器件可被應用于從慣性傳感到高靈敏度的引力與質量的測量。當一個模式的振動頻率的整數倍接近另一個高頻模式的振動頻率，內共振會被激發，伴隨著兩個模式之間有效的能量交換。研究表明內共振對振動有顯著的影響，包括穩定非線性振蕩器的頻率。 提案中實驗的重點在於揭示內共振影響機械振動的能量耗散和改變頻譜響應的多種機制。研究將涉及微機械諧振器的兩個振動模式。通過其對振動幅度的非線性依賴性或通過靜電力的彈簧軟化來修改較高頻模式的頻率，該系統將被調諧進出內部共振。初步的模擬結果表明內共振會導致反常的非線性阻尼。在振動的衰減過程中，衰減速率不再是恆定的,而是隨著振幅非單調地變化。我們打算探究如何將兩個模式之間的能量交換運用到穩定振動頻率和提高探測靈敏度上。與此同時，我們計劃深入地研究當兩個模式的固有頻率被調節成倍頻關係時內共振對頻譜響應的影響。提案中實驗的成功實施不僅能夠推動新的理論研究，驗證多種理論方法的正確性，還能夠促進微機械探測器的發展，提高其靈敏度和功能性。 主要研究者在微機械器件的波動現象方面有豐富的經驗。過去幾年中，他的團隊在強周期性驅動力下非線性微機械扭轉諧振器在受高斯噪聲和泊松噪聲的激發而產生的共存振動狀態之間的跳轉方面做了大量的研究。主要研究者將會與來自密歇根州立大學的理論物理學教授Mark Dykman教授緊密合作，揭示微機械諧振器中的非線性阻尼和內共振現象

16305217.label: Project Objectives
16305217.value: We will study the dual pair consisting of a symplectic loop group and an orthogonal loop group. For an automorphic form of an orthogonal group, we view it as an automorohic form on the positive half of the loop orthogonal group via the evaluation morphism. Its theta lifting is given by an integral and is an automorphic form on loop symplectic loop group. We will prove Rallis constant term formula holds. Rallis constant term formula We will study the implications of Rallis constant formula. It suggests that the theta lifting satisfies the tower properties. The tower for loop groups has the new feature that terminates at a finite step. It starts from finite dimensional groups like SP(2), SP(4), ...., SP(2n), then finally the loop group LSP(2n). It is an open problem to construct cusp forms for loop groups. We hope that the theta lifting will given a first construction of cusps forms on loop sympelctic groups. We will investigate if the Rallis inner product formula can be generalized to loop groups. Our previous results about Siegel-Weil formula for loop group will play a fundamental role.

16305217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16305217.value: The notion of symmetry is closely related to harmony, beauty, and unity. The study of symmetry is systematized and formalized in the areas of mathematics called group theory and representation theory. The semisimple algebraic groups and the infinite dimensional generalizations, loop groups and Kac-Moody groups, are among the most important classes of groups. This project will study automorphic forms of loop groups. In previous GRF projects, we constructed Weil representation for loop symplectic groups over all of the local fields, and proved that the global Weil representation admits a theta functional that is modular invariant; we proved a version of the Siegel-Weil formula for loop symplectic and orthogonal groups. The present project will continue to study loop groups and Weil representations. We propose to generalize the theory of the classical theta lifting to the loop groups. Our research will give a first construction of cusp forms on loop groups. 对称的概念与和谐，美感和统一性密切相关。 数学中研究对称的领域称为表示理论。圈群和Kac-Moody群 是表示理论中最重要的研究对象之一。 在以前的GRF项目中，我们构建了辛群圈群的Weil表示； 证明了全局Weil表示有一个模不变的theta泛函;我们还推广了的Siegel-Weil公式。本项目将继续研究辛群圈群的Weil表示。我们计划推广经典的theta提升理论。我们的研究将给出第一个圈群自守形的尖点形式。

16305217.label: Realisation of objectives
16305217.value: This is the first study of theta lifting for automorphic forms. Almost the objectives are successfully realized. Our proposal in Objective (1), mainly about the set-up for loop theta lifitng, is now proved to be workable. For Objective (2), we extended the Rallis constant term formula successfully to the loop case, for orthogonal to symplectic theta lift. As a consequence of our constant term formula, we proved the tower property. For objective (3), we proved the exsitence of cusp forms on loop groups. This is the first work that confirms the existence.

16305217.label: Major findings and research outcome
16305217.value: This is the first study of theta lifting for loop groups in mathematics. (1) we find the right set-up for the theta lifting, starting from a classical cusp form on an orthogonal group, we view it as an automorphic form on the positive half of the loop orthogonal group via the evaluation map. Then we integrate it against the theta kernel. This set-up was suggested by our earlier work on Siegel-Weil formula on loop groups. Our work in this project has provesd it is the right set-up. (2) We extended Rallis costant term formula successful to loop group case. Our proof is modeled on the proof of the classical case, but is much more involved. We are able overcome many difficulties to obtain the formula. This formula shows that the classical tower property again holds for loop groups. Our new discovery is that the tower of theta lifitng starts from a list of classical groups and end-up with a loop group. For example, in the orthogonal-symplectic lifting, the tower is SP(2), SP(4), ...., SP(2n), then finally the loop group LSP(2n). If we obtain a non-vanishing lifting ar SP(2n) and also get an non-vanishing lifting for loop LSP(2n-2). (3) Our work confirms the existence of cusp forms on loop group. The simpliest case is the lifting of an automorphic character for SO(2) to loop SL(2), we showed that the lifting gives a cusp form for loop SL(2).

It is desirable to have an explicit formula for such a form. The simpliest case is the lifting of an automorphic character for SO(2) to loop SL(2), we show that the lifting gives a cusp form for loop SL(2). It would be interesting to give an explicit formula for the lifted cusp form.

16305317.label: Project Objectives
16305317.value: Realize a long-lived spin-orbit coupled Fermi gas of Yb atoms for the study of dipole collective mode. We will implement the Raman-induced SOC using a narrow 1S0-3P1 optical transition with minimal spontaneous heating in Yb fermions. Successful completion will allow one to study many-body effects including the dipole collective mode of the spin-orbit coupled Fermi gas. Raman-induced spin-orbit coupling modifies the energy dispersion and breaks the Galilean invariance due to spin-momentum locking. We will further investigate the dynamics of the spin-orbit coupled Fermi gas through the dipole oscillation, and address how the absence of Galilean invariance modifies the collective mode. Our study should provide a general understanding of dynamics in a spin-orbit coupled Fermi gas in the absence of Galilean invariance. Create a spin texture in both momentum and position space in a spin-orbit coupled Fermi gas. All-optical implementation of SOC in Yb fermions will enable us to couple atomic spins with both momentum and position space. By spatially modulating the light intensity, and thus the two-photon detuning of SOC, we will characterize a Fermi gas in the presence of spin-orbit-position coupling . The spin dephasing, momentum distribution and collective mode will be experimentally investigated. Our new SOC capability will bring greater understanding of how spin physics is related to and controlled by other physical variables.

16305317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16305317.value: Spin-orbit coupling (SOC) in solid-state matters, originating from the crystal’s intrinsic electric field, links particles’ quantum spin to their velocity, and is essential in various novel topological and spintronic phenomena. It has been recently become possible to engineer, and thus tune on demand SOC in an ultracold atomic system, allowing a variety of synthetic SOCs in a controlled manner. To date, most of the realizations of synthetic SOC in ultracold atoms have used alkali atoms, but the PI and his colleagues recently demonstrated SOC in a Fermi gas of alkaline-earth-like atoms for the first time. Together with the SOC that was realized very recently in lanthanide dysprosium atoms, the SOC in those non-alkali atoms is expected to expand our capability in the study of novel SOC physics. Interestingly, the spin-orbit coupled ytterbium system is distinct from the alkali system, and from the other non-alkali case, in that the ground spin states are of SU(N) symmetry and split by an optical light shift. This unique feature allows an all-optical implementation of SOC that exhibits several advantages. First, we can precisely control the splitting of spin states by optical means, with no need for the extreme magnetic field stability to reduce heating for the realization. Second, it is straightforward to implement a rich configuration of the spin splitting field, e.g. by locally manipulating the light shift, thus giving rise to a new family of spin texture in both momentum and position space. In particular, such an artificial spin texture would allow us to study the “spatial domain”, which actually renders spin-orbit-position coupling in the present ytterbium fermion system, and may bring about novel spin physics. In the proposed project, we will expand our capability in exploring SOC physics, and propose (1) the realization of a long-lived spin-orbit-coupled Fermi gas, (2) a study of the collective dipole mode of spin-orbit coupled fermions and (3) a study of position-dependent SOC. We will perform the experiments using currently working apparatus that produces a degenerate Fermi gas of ytterbium-173 atoms. We believe that successful completion of this project will further broaden our knowledge of the novel SOC physics. 固體物理中的自旋軌道耦合（SOC）來源於晶體的固有電場，將粒子的量子性質與其速度聯係在一起，是各種新奇的拓撲和自旋電子學現象中必不可少的因素。近來關於SOC的應用在工程領域中已經變得可能，通過在超冷原子體系中調節所需的SOC，各式各樣的可控的SOC產品得以出現。目前爲止，在超冷原子領域中，大部分SOC的實現使用的是鹼金屬原子，但PI和他的同事們首次通過類鹼土金屬原子在費米體系中實現SOC。另一方面，最近SOC在镧系元素镝中也得以實現，這些在非鹼金屬原子體系中實現的SOC有望使得新型SOC物理的研究進一步擴展。 值得注意的是，具有自旋軌道耦合的鐿原子體系不同于鹼金屬體系，也不同于其他的非鹼金屬情況。在鐿原子體系中，自旋基態具有n 阶特殊酉群（SU（N））的對稱性并且由於光的改變而劈裂，這種獨特的性質使得全光的SOC得以實現。全光學手段實現的SOC具有以下優點。第一，我們可以通過光學的手段精確地調控自旋態的劈裂狀態，從而不需要使用極爲穩定的磁場，進一步減少了加熱對系統的影響。第二，該系統可以直接實現多樣的自旋劈裂結構，通過局部操縱光場的改變，一系列新的自旋結構在動量和位置空間中得以出現。尤爲特別的是，如這樣的人工自旋結構使得我們能夠研究“空域”，這使得自旋軌道耦合在鐿費米子體系中更具研究價值，并且很有可能帶動新穎的自旋物理的發展。 在提議的項目中，我們將進一步擴展關於SOC物理的研究，計劃（1）實現長壽命的自旋軌道耦合費米氣體，計劃（2）用SOC研究集體偶極振蕩模式，計劃（3）空間位置相關的SOC研究。我們將使用當前的實驗裝置進行這些實驗，這些設備已經能夠產生鐿173原子的簡并費米氣體。我們相信這些項目的成功完成將進一步擴展我們對新型SOC物理的認知。

16305317.label: Major findings and research outcome
16305317.value: Synthetic topological matter with spin-orbit-coupled fermions Over the past few years, PI’s group has implemented synthetic spin-orbit coupling for ultracold ytterbium fermions by using two-photon Raman transition in various setting. Two hyperfine levels that are optically isolated from other internal levels are coupled in a momentum-sensitive manner, either in bulk or optical lattices. By engineering the band structure and its topological nature, we have realized 1D and 3D topological band structures in the following works: • Observation of symmetry-protected topological band with ultracold fermions Science Advances 4, eaao4748 (2018) • Observation of nodal-line semimetal with ultracold fermions in an optical lattice Nature Physics 15 911-916 (2019) Both studies highlighted the remarkable capabilities to realize and explore new topological states for ultracold atoms beyond natural conditions. Those two remarkable works have been highlighted in HKUST news, Phys.org, Croucher Foundation and etc. in 2018 and 2019, respectively. However, these studies were performed in the Hermitian regime where dissipation is suppressed. Recently, we generalized the notion of spin-orbit coupling into the non-Hermitian regime by introducing controlled atom loss: • Topological control of quantum states in non-Hermitian spin-orbit-coupled fermions arXiv:2106:04874 (2021) Interacting SU(N) fermions Interacting fermionic matter is the foundation of matter, and fermions with enlarged spin symmetry lead to qualitatively new physics. While ordinary spin- 1/2 electrons with SU(2) symmetry are the building blocks of most of this matter, large spins with enhanced SU(N) symmetry promise new quantum phenomena and provide insights into SU(2) electronic matter. The PI’s group has realized 2D SU(N) Fermi liquid and measured collective excitations for tunable spin N. Recently, thermodynamic studies have been performed by analyzing density fluctuations equivalent to compressibility or by recording the Tan’s contact of 3D SU(N) Fermi gas. With regard to the latter experiment, the PI’s group experimentally tested bosonization in a multi-component 3D fermionic system for large N; the findings suggested that the boundary between bosons and fermions can be blurred in SU(N) fermions. • Heurisitic machinery for thermodynamic studies of SU(N) fermions with neural networks Nature Communications 12 2011 (2021) • Evidence for bosonization in a three-dimensional gas of SU(N) Fermions Physical Review X 10 041052 (2020) • Collective excitations in two-dimensional SU(N) Fermi gases with tunable spin Phys. Rev. Research Rapid Comm. 2 012028(R) (2020)

16305317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16305317.value: The achievement of the project will lay out foundation for exploring spin-orbit-coupled quantum system under dissipation. Although spin-orbit coupling mechanism is the key principle behind various topological matter, less is known when the dissipation plays an important role. We envision that ultracold atoms with controllable spin-orbit coupling and dissipation will open an avenue toward the experimental investigation of such systems. We are now in the process of combining spin-orbit coupling and dissipation in the lattice. As an immediate follow-up experiment, we envision observing a parity-time symmetry breaking transition in a dissipative topological band system.

16305317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16305317.value: In this project, we aimed at creating complex quantum system with spin-orbit coupling that is a key mechanism behind various topological matter. For this goal, we exploited ytterbium ultracold fermions near the absolute zero temperature, and emulated the quantum behaviour of those atoms when their internal quantum state (i.e. spin) is strongly coupled to the their momentum (i.e. orbit). Especially, we realized such spin-orbit coupling in the periodic lattice, and successfully created exotic spin configuration as a result of such coupling. The finding reported in the project will lead to the better understanding of topological matter, and highlights the full benefits of quantum simulation with ultracold atoms.

16305817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16305817.value: Solvation plays an essential role in many important chemical and biological processes such as drug-receptor binding, protein folding, and molecular recognition. Among various solvation models, analytical integral equation theories (IETs) yield a good balance between computational efficiency and accuracy. However, a major challenge existing for current IET-based methods is to properly treat water density depletions around hydrophobic solutes when the solute size approaches the nanometer length scale. To address the above challenge, we propose to develop a new analytical IET, the P-YBG-HI theory, to accurately predict solvation structure and thermodynamic properties of organic and biological molecules, especially for those containing substantial hydrophobic groups. The novelty of our new theory is twofold: (1) an explicit consideration of the hydrophobicity-induced water density depletion at solute-solvent interface; (2) an appropriate treatment of impact on solvation due to long-range electrostatic interactions between solute and solvent. Preliminary results show that the P-YBG-HI theory can accurately compute solvation structures and hydration free energies of various hydrophobic organic compounds at a low computational cost. For drug-like compounds, precise predictions of hydration free energies are prerequisite for accurate estimations of binding free energies because partial or even full desolvation of drug is associated with its binding to receptor. We will employ the P-YBG-HI theory to compute hydration free energies of a wide range of drug-like organic compounds. Quantitative comparisons with experiment will allow us to validate and further improve our theory. We will also apply the P-YBG-HI theory to investigate the solvation of the GroEL-GroES Chaperon system. We aim to elucidate the role of solvation in the conformational expansion of the mis-folded protein substrate upon its initial binding to GroEL, a critical step in the operation of this Chaperon system to assist protein folding in vivo. 溶解過程在許多重要的化學和生物現像中起重要作用，例如藥物與受體的結合，蛋白質折疊和分子識別。在各種溶劑化學模型中，分析的積分方程理論（IETs）在計算效率和 準確度之間取得了良好的平衡。然而，當前基於IET的方法存在的主要挑戰是當疏水性溶質分子接近納米尺度時，無法適當地處理理疏水性相互作用引起的溶質周圍水密度下降的問題。 為了解決上述挑戰，我們建議開發一種全新的IET理論：P-YBG-HI理論，用於準確地預測有機和生物分子的溶劑化結構和熱力學性質，特別是對於含有大量疏水基團的分子。 我們的理論的新穎性在於兩個方面：（1）明確考慮溶質 - 溶劑界面上疏水性誘導的水分密度降低; （2）適當的處理由溶質和溶劑之間的長距離靜電相互作用對溶劑化的影響。初步結果表明，P-YBG-HI理論可以以較低的計算成本精確計算各種疏水有機化合物的溶劑化結構和水合自由能。 由於與受體結合時，藥物分子會部分甚至完全去溶劑化，因此水合自由能的精確預測是準確估計藥物分子與受體結合自由能的先決條件。我們將採用P-YBG-HI理論計算大量 藥物有機化合物的水合自由能同時與實驗的定量比較將使我們能夠驗證和進一步改進我們的理論。我們還將應用P-YBG-HI理論來研究細胞中幫助蛋白質折疊的GroEL-GroES複合物的溶劑化效應我們的目的是幫助闡明生物體內協助蛋白質正確折疊中的一個關鍵步驟：溶劑化效應如何幫助的GroEL的蛋白質底物糾正其錯誤的折疊。

16305817.label: Realisation of objectives
16305817.value: The analytical integral equation theories (IETs) provide a powerful approach to calculate solvation properties of chemical and biological molecules, as it yields a good balance between computational efficiency and accuracy. However, existing IETs are not sufficient to treat water density depletions surrounding hydrophobic solutes, that has greatly limited their applications. Research supported by this grant aims to address this challenge by developing a new IET theory. For the first objective, we have completed this objective and developed a new analytical IET to accurately predict solvation structure around hydrophobic solutes. Our theory is based on the 3D reference interaction site model (3DRISM). There are two key developments in our new theory: Firstly, we have introduced the hydrophobic-induced density inhomogeneity theory (HI) to explicitly consider the hydrophobicity-induced water density depletion at solute-solvent interface. Secondly, to further consider the impact on solvation due to long-range electrostatic interactions between solute and solvent, we developed the D2MSA closure, in which the short-range solute-solvent interactions are treated with the D2 closure, while the long-range electrostatic interactions between solvent and solute are considered by the mean spherical approximation (MSA). Altogether, our new IET theory: 3DRISM-HI-D2MSA can accurately predict the solvent distributions around solute molecules containing both hydrophobic and hydrophilic groups in aqueous solution (Mol. Phys., 116, 1003-1013, (2018) & Adv. Theory Simul. 1900049, (2019)). For the second objective that is focused on the drug-like organic compounds, we have successfully shown that our 3DRISM-HI-D2MSA theory greatly outperforms the popular 3DRISM-KH theory and yields consistent solvent radial distribution functions compared to explicit solvent MD simulations, when applied to calculate the density distributions of water and organic solvents (including acetonitrile, acetone, pyridine, tetrahydrofuran, and benzene) around drug-like solute. Moreover, we show that the solvation properties obtained from by our theory provides also lead to more accurate computation of solvation free energy of the organic solute compounds (Adv. Theory Simul. 1900049, (2019) & Chapter 3 of the M. Phil thesis of K.H. Choy). In addition, our IET theory also provides a promising alternative approach to the popular Poisson-Boltzmann theory in computing free energies for peptides binding to the surface (Adv. Sci. 6, 1801827, (2019)). For the third objective, we have applied our newly developed IET theory: 3DRISM-HI-D2MSA, to the GroEL-GroES Chaperon system (consited of >8,000 amino acid residues). Solvation properties such as radial distribtion functions predicted from our theory agree well with those from explicit solvent MD simulations for a wide variety of amino acid residues including hydrophobic, hydrophilic and charged residues. In sharp constrast, the popular 3DRISM-KH theory often overestimates the solvent density particularly in the first solvation shell in comparison with the explicit solvent MD simulations. In terms of computation efficiency, our IET theory provides over three orders of magnitude speedup in comparison with explicit solvent MD simulations (Chapter 4 of the M. Phil thesis of K.H. Choy). The success of our IET theory allows us to further study the change of the solvation of Chaperon during its conformational changes. Our IET theory holds promise to be applied to replace explicit solvent to study the solvation of protein complexes such as the light harvesting system (Faraday Discuss., 216, 94, (2019)). Finally, the accuracy of our 3DRISM-HI-D2MSA theory can be further improved if it can be used together with the polarizable solute force field such as AMOEBA. We have successfully developed the AW3C and AW5C water models that are compatible with AMOEBA solutes, and this will enable the further implement of the IET solvation with the AMOEBA solutes (J. Comput. Chem., 41, 1034, (2020)).

16305817.label: Major findings and research outcome
16305817.value: Solvation plays an important role in many processes in Chemistry and Biology. IETs provide a more efficient approach than explicit solvent models while retain reasonable accuracy compared to implicit solvent models. When introduced to aqueous solution, existing IETs are not sufficient to treat water density depletions surrounding hydrophobic solutes, and this has imposed a great challenge for current IET-based methods. With the support of this grant, we have developed a new analytical IET theory (i.e., 3DRISM-HI-D2MSA) to accurately compute solvation structure around hydrophobic solutes. Our IET theory is novel as we introduced both a new hydrophobic-induced density inhomogeneity theory (HI) and a new closure theory (D2MSA) that allow us to explicitly consider the hydrophobicity-induced water density depletion at solute-solvent interface (Mol. Phys., 116, 1003-1013, (2018) & Adv. Theory Simul. 1900049, (2019)). We show that our 3DRISM-HI-D2MSA theory greatly outperforms other popular IET theories in yielding more accurate solvent structural properties as well as solvation free energies for various solvents surrounding drug-like solute compounds (Adv. Theory Simul. 1900049, (2019) & M. Phil thesis of K.H. Choy). In addition, our IET theory also provides a promising alternative approach to the popular Poisson-Boltzmann theory in computing free energies for peptides binding to the surface (Adv. Sci. 6, 1801827, (2019)). We have also demonstrated that our 3DRISM-HI-D2MSA theory can accurately predict the solvation structures of the Chaperon protein, and also result in orders of magnitude speedup in comparison with explicit solvent molecular dynamics (MD) simulations (M. Phil thesis of K.H. Choy). The accuracy of the 3D-RISM-HI-D2MSA theory can be further improved together with the polarizable solute force fields such as AMOEBA. We have successfully developed the AW3C and AW5C water models that are compatible with AMOEBA solutes, and this will enable the further implement of the IET solvation with the AMOEBA solutes (J. Comput. Chem., 41, 1034, (2020)). Due to the above achievements, the team have been invited to give talks in prestigious international conferences. 1 Ph. D and 1 M. Phil. students partially supported by this grant have obtained their degrees. The PI has won the 16th China Youth Science and Technology Award in 2020, and the 2021 Pople Medal from the Asia-Pacific Association of Theoretical and Computational Chemists.

16305817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16305817.value: With the support of this grant, we have developed a new IET theory (i.e., 3DRISM-HI-D2-MSA) and demonstrated its accuracy when applied to calculate the solvation properties of drug-like compounds and proteins. Our future studies can further extend the applicability our IET theory to be combined with the polarizable solute force fields. These developments can greatly accelerate the convergence of solvation or binding free energy calculations of polarizable solute force fields. In the long term, the developed IET theory can facilitate the drug discovery via accurate predictions of the partition coefficients and aqueous solubility of crystalline drug-like compounds.

16305817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16305817.value: Solvation plays an essential role in many important chemical and biological processes such as drug-receptor binding, protein folding, and molecular recognition. Among various solvation models, analytical integral equation theories (IETs) yield a good balance between computational efficiency and accuracy. However, a major challenge existing for current IET-based methods is to properly treat water density depletions around hydrophobic solutes when the solute size approaches the nanometer length scale. Supported by this grant, we have successfully developed a new analytical IET theory (i.e., 3DRISM-HI-D2-MSA) to address this challenge. The novelty of our developed IET theory lies in twofold: Firstly, we have introduced the hydrophobic-induced density inhomogeneity theory (HI) to explicitly consider the hydrophobicity-induced water density depletion at solute-solvent interface; Secondly, we have developed the D2MSA closure theory to properly consider the impact of solute-solvent long-range electrostatic interactions on solvation. We show that our developed IET theory greatly outperforms other popular IET theories in yielding more accurate solvent structural properties and solvation free energy of drug-like compounds. Furthermore, we have demonstrated that our IET theory can accurately predict the solvation structures for proteins including the large Chaperon system. When applied to the Chaperon complex, our IET theory leads to orders of magnitude speedup in comparison with explicit solvent molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. Our developed IET theory can be widely applied to understand molecular mechanisms of many biological processes, in which solvation plays an important role. In the long term, our IET theory holds promise to facilitate the drug discovery via providing an accurate method to compute drug-receptor binding free energies.

16306117.label: Project Objectives
16306117.value: Fully characterise the steady-state optical properties of a range of model high-performance, non-fullerene OSC systems. The measurements involved will include electroabsorption, temperature-dependent UV-Vis absorption, photoluminescence and electroluminescence spectra. These steady-state characterisations we derive will help us in conducting analyses of time-resolved optical measurements, which will be performed later in the project. Quantify ultrafast charge separation in the model P3HEA:SF-PDI2 blend by using transient absorption (TA) spectroscopy. Performing TA measurements at low excitation densities should allow us to probe the weak electroabsorption signals that arise from the electrostatic field created upon charge separation. We will also use computational tools to isolate the absorption signals of excitons and charges, and thus establish a quantitative model that explains charge separation dynamics in this unique system. Characterise the dependence of charge separation on structural and morphological properties. We will compare the charge separation dynamics, morphology and performance of P3TEA-SF-PDI2 blends with the characteristics of other related systems that do not perform well at low levels of driving force. This comparison should allow us to identify the key structural or morphological properties of the the P3TEA:SF-PDI2 blend that enable its unique properties. Investigate the role of spin states in charge separation and recombination within the model non-fullerene OSC blends. Studying the formation of low-energy triplet spin states in these blends will allow us to better understand the energy landscape at the donor-acceptor interface.

16306117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16306117.value: Developing low-cost and commercially competitive solar cells is important for sustainable power generation. Organic solar cells (OSCs) are attractive because they are printable, mechanically flexible and they do not contain toxic materials that are harmful to the environment. The conventional state-of-the-art OSCs are based on fullerene acceptors, which reportedly have power conversion efficiencies of up to 12%. However, the efficiency of these devices is limited by their fundamental trade-off between photovoltage and photocurrent. It is generally believed that a significant energy offset between the donor and acceptor (typically 0.3-0.5 eV) is needed to provide a driving force to separate the electrons and holes created upon light absorption. This large energy offset unavoidably creates a large photovoltage loss for OSCs, thus limiting their cell efficiencies. For example, state-of-the-art OSCs based on fullerene acceptors have a photovoltage loss of about 0.88 V, which limits their highest achievable efficiency to about 12-13%. Recently, Prof Henry Yan’s group at HKUST developed a novel non-fullerene OSC system that overcomes this fundamental constraint. Based on a P3TEA donor polymer and an SF-PDI2 molecular acceptor, this system offers ultrafast and highly efficient charge separation with nearly zero charge separation driving force. This discovery provides the first example of an efficient OSC system with small photovoltage loss, and it strongly implies that efficiencies beyond 15% can be realised, provided that all other device parameters are fully optimised. However, several important questions remain to be answered, especially regarding how the P3TEA:SF-PDI2-based system can achieve efficient charge separation despite a nearly zero driving force. In fact, all of the other material systems developed to this date show significant losses in charge separation efficiencies when the driving force approaches zero. This project will aim to identify the crucial factors that enable efficient charge separation with small driving force. In collaboration with Prof Yan (HKUST) and Prof Richard Friend (University of Cambridge), we will perform in-depth studies on charge separation dynamics for a range of model non-fullerene OSC systems (including P3TEA:SF-PDI2) by using highly-sensitive ultrafast optical techniques. Through comparing P3TEA:SF-PDI2 with other material systems, we will identify the key structural and morphological features of this blend that enable its unique properties. Our results will provide important design rules for future OSCs with much reduced photovoltage loss, and will therefore facilitate the development of commercially competitive OSCs. 開發低成本和具有商業競爭力的太陽能電池對於發展再生能源是非常重要的。有機太陽能電池（OSC）是有吸引力的，因為它們是可利用打印技術來製造，並且不含有對環境有害的有毒材料。現有的OSC使用富勒烯做电子受体材料，據報導其功率轉換效率高達12％。然而，這些器件的效率受到光電壓和光電流之間的基本權衡的限制。一般認為，供體和受體之間的顯著的能量偏移需要提供驅動力以分離在光吸收時產生的電子和空穴（通常為0.3-0.5eV）。這種大的能量偏移不可避免地導致相對大光電壓損耗，因此限制了它們的電池效率。例如，基於富勒烯受體的OSC具有約0.88V的光電壓損失，這將其最高可實現的效率限制在約12-13％。 最近，科大顏河教授的團隊發現了具有幾乎零電荷分離驅動力的高效電荷分離系統 （P3TEA：SF-PDI2）。該發現提供了第一個具有小光電壓損耗的高效OSC系統。並且，只要所有其他器件參數都被完全優化，超過15％的效率的OSC是可實現的。然而，幾個重要問題仍有待回答，特別是關於這個系統如何能夠實現有效的電荷分離（儘管驅動力幾乎為零）。事實上，迄今為止開發的所有其他材料系統在驅動力接近零時顯示出電荷分離效率的顯著損失。 該項目旨在確定以小推動力實現高效電荷分離的關鍵因素。我們將與劍橋大學合作，使用超快光學技術來深入研究這系統的獨特性能。通過比較P3TEA：SF-PDI2與其他材料系統，我們將確定該材料系統的關鍵結構和形態特徵，使其具有獨特的高效電荷分離。我們的結果將為未來的OSC提供重要的設計規則，光損失將大大降低，因此將有助於開發具有商業競爭力的OSC。

16306117.label: Realisation of objectives
16306117.value: We have achieved all the project objectives. By performing detailed optical and structural measurements on P3TEA:SF-PDI2, along with other related material systems, we have successfully characterised the charge generation dynamics in non-fullerene organic solar cell materials with small driving force. We found that charge generation is an endothermic process that takes 100 ps to complete at room temperature. Based on these results we have established a quantitative model for charge and triplet dynamics in non-fullerene organic solar cells systems with small driving force. The results were published in Advanced Materials (Adv. Mater. 2018, 30, 1804215) and Nature Communications (Nat. Commun. 2020, 11, 5617).
