rows: Fully characterise the steady-state optical properties of a range of model high-performance, non-fullerene OSC systems. The measurements involved will include electroabsorption, temperature-dependent UV-Vis absorption, photoluminescence and electroluminescence spectra. These steady-state characterisations we derive will help us in conducting analyses of time-resolved optical measurements, which will be performed later in the project.

Quantify ultrafast charge separation in the model P3HEA:SF-PDI2 blend by using transient absorption (TA) spectroscopy. Performing TA measurements at low excitation densities should allow us to probe the weak electroabsorption signals that arise from the electrostatic field created upon charge separation. We will also use computational tools to isolate the absorption signals of excitons and charges, and thus establish a quantitative model that explains charge separation dynamics in this unique system.

Characterise the dependence of charge separation on structural and morphological properties. We will compare the charge separation dynamics, morphology and performance of P3TEA-SF-PDI2 blends with the characteristics of other related systems that do not perform well at low levels of driving force. This comparison should allow us to identify the key structural or morphological properties of the the P3TEA:SF-PDI2 blend that enable its unique properties.

Investigate the role of spin states in charge separation and recombination within the model non-fullerene OSC blends. Studying the formation of low-energy triplet spin states in these blends will allow us to better understand the energy landscape at the donor-acceptor interface.

16306117.label: Major findings and research outcome
16306117.value: The major research finding of this project is that photogenerated electron-hole pairs in high-performance non-fullerene organic solar cells require thermal energy in order to separate into free electrons and holes and create photocurrent. This process takes nearly 100 ps to complete at room temperature. This endothermic charge generation process is very different to traditional organic solar cells based on fullerene molecules and have large interfacial driving force, in which electron-hole pairs are able to separate exothermically at an ultrafast timescale (<100 fs). Our findings therefore clarifies the fundamental photochemical process in these exciting materials, and provide important design guidelines for future material and device development.

16306117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16306117.value: Newer non-fullerene organic solar cell materials with even higher performance than P3TEA:SF-PDI2 have been recently developed. These materials, such as PM6:Y6, are able to achieve up to 17% solar cell efficiency. Further work is to extend the quantitative model that we have developed in this project to reveal efficient charge generation mechanism in state-of-the-art material systems.

16306117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16306117.value: Organic solar cells are promising alternative to silicon solar cells because they are flexible, printable, semi-transparent and eco-friendly. Nevertheless, organic solar cells have lower efficiency than silicon, and therefore further development is needed. Recent advances in the development of non-fullerene acceptor molecules have greatly improved organic solar cell performance, now reaching over 15% efficiency. However, the fundamental photochemistry of these materials is not fully understood, thereby hindering further development and technology transfer. In this project we have revealed the basic photochemical mechanism in these materials. The results not only address a long-standing scientific question in this field, but also provide fundamental insights for how to further improve the performance of organic solar cells.

16306317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16306317.value: This proposal is focused on how to recover a low rank matrix from its limited information. Low rank matrices arise from many practical applications in machine learning, signal processing, computer vision, etc. Typically, the low rank matrix to be recovered is of a large scale and the number of linear measurements is small. Roughly, two types of algorithms are used to find a low rank matrix from its linear measurements: convex and non-convex optimization-based algorithms. In many convex optimization-based algorithms, singular value thresholding (SVT) is usually called in each iteration. In other words, it is necessary to compute a singular value decomposition (SVD) of a large matrix for each iteration which is usually inefficient. Recently, interest is growing in using non-convex optimization-based algorithms to recover low-rank matrices. Non-convex algorithms are usually more efficient than convex ones, especially for large-scale matrices. In this proposed project, we will design a group of non-convex optimization-based algorithms under the framework of iterative hard thresholding with subspace projection (IHTSP). Some preliminary work has been published recently. These algorithms are not only efficient, but also have theoretical guarantees to the correct solution. We will further explore their variants under different settings, their theoretical guarantees as well as other applications. For instance, subspace projection plays an important role in designing efficient algorithms under the IHTSP framework. We may creatively incorporate the subspace projection into the existing iterative algorithms to make them more efficient. The new design of algorithms will open opportunities to develop new theories on proving theoretical guarantees to their correct solution. In addition, there are so many applications involving low-rank matrix and we will adapt our algorithms to obtain state-of-the-art approaches for these applications. 本项目研究如何从其有限的信息中恢复低秩矩阵。低秩矩阵来源于机器学习，信号处理，计算机视觉等许多实际应用。通常，要恢复的低秩矩阵是大规模的，而且被我们测量到的信息很少。 大致有两种类型的算法可以从其线性测量中找到低秩矩阵：基于凸和非凸优化的算法。在许多基于凸优化的算法中，通常需要在每次迭代中调用奇异值阈值。换句话说，每个迭代都需要计算一个大矩阵的奇异值分解，这通常是低效的。最近，利用基于非凸优化的算法来恢复低阶矩阵越来越受到关注。非凸优化算法通常比凸优化算法更有效，特别是对于大尺度矩阵。 在本研究项目中，我们将在子空间投影迭代硬阈值 （IHTSP）的框架下设计一组非凸优化算法。我们已经发表了一些初步的结果。这些非凸优化算法不但有效，而且可以理论证明它们收敛到我们想要找的低秩矩阵。我们将在不同的设定下进一步探索其变体，理论分析以及其他应用。例如，子空间投影在IHTSP框架下设计高效算法中起重要作用。我们可以将子空间投影纳入现有的迭代算法，使其更有效率。新的算法设计将为开发新的理论提供机会，证明这些算法可以收敛到正确的低秩矩阵。此外，有很多涉及低秩矩阵的应用，我们将运用我们的算法到这些问题，期望得到解决这些实际应用问题的最先进的方法。

16306317.label: Realisation of objectives
16306317.value: All the objectives in the original application are achieved. For objective 1: We have expanded a family of non-convex optimization-based algorithms under the framework of iterative hard thresholding with subspace projection (IHTSP). In particular, we (i) incorporated the subspace projection to the alternating projection method to obtain accelerated alternating projection for robust principal component analysis (RPCA). (ii) incorporated the subspace projection to IHT to obtain the Riemannian Gradient algorithms for matrix completion. (iii) incorporated the subspace projection to IHT in structured matrix completion to obtain ASAP algorithm for spectrally sparse signal recovery. (iv) proposed projected gradient descent, Riemannian manifold optimization, and inexact ADMM for low-rank matrix recovery under various settings. All these algorithms are much more efficient than exiting approaches. For objective 2: We provided the theoretical guarantees to the true solutions for newly proposed algorithms. (i) For the accelerated alternating projection, we proved that the algorithm converges linearly to the true low-rank matrix and sparse matrix, under a very mild assumption that the low-rank matrix is not sparse and the sparse matrix is not low-rank. (ii) For Riemannian Gradient for matrix completion, we proved the recovery guarantee under nearly optimal sampling complexity with high probability. (iii) For ASAP, we have shown that the algorithm is guaranteed to give a successful recovery of the structured low-rank matrix and the sparse structured matrix under mild assumptions. (iv) For the projected gradient descent algorithm, under the assumption that the observed entries are obtained randomly, we have shown that this algorithm converges linearly to the underlying true solution with high probability. For objective 3: We have applied the resulting algorithms to applications. (i) The accelerated alternating projection method is applied to video surveillance. Our algorithm not only saves computational time, but also are able to solve large-scale problems that are prohibited for conventional algorithms. (ii) The Riemannian Gradient algorithm for matrix completion has been applied to recommendation systems. (iii) The ASAP algorithm has been applied to robust signal recovery in NMR spectroscopy with outlier noise. (iv) The projected gradient descent is applied to NMR spectroscopy signal recovery. Our algorithm can deal with large scale problems that traditional algorithms are prohibited. (v) Other non-convex algorithms are also applied to solve phase retrieval problems.

16306317.label: Major findings and research outcome
16306317.value: We have developed a framework of constructing provable non-convex optimization methods for low-rank matrix recovery problems. Convex optimization algorithms for low-rank matrix recovery usually use the singular value thresholding (SVT) operator, whose computational complexity if very high as we need to compute the many singular values and singular vectors of a large matrix. Traditional non-convex methods then may use truncated SVD. Although this can reduce the computational cost from SVT as a fixed number of singular values and singular vectors are computed, the computational cost is still too high and the algorithms might not provable. In this project, we incorporated the truncated SVD with subspace projection to bring two benifits: (1) The algorithm is much faster because only a small SVD is needed. (2) The resulting algorithms are provable to be guaranteed to converge to a global minimum. Our new framework is applied to low-rank matrix recovery problems under various settings to obtain efficient provable non-convex algorithms with a wide applications. -- In Jounral Publication 2, this framework is adopted to Robust PCA to obtain Accelerated Alternating Projection method, which can be 10 times faster than existing algorithms. Our algorithm come with a theoretical guarantee. -- In Journal Publication 5, this framework is adopted to data recovery on manifold in a very general setting. Some fundamental results on the sampling complexity are established. -- In Journal Publication 6, this framework is adopted to matrix completion, a core problem in low-rank matrix recovery. The algorithm beats state-of-the-art algorithm, and the successful matrix completion is theoretically guaranteed with a nearly optimal sampling complexity. -- In Journal Publication 10, this framework is adopted to structured low-rank plus sparse matrix separation, We obtain ASAP algorith, which can deal with large scale problems that are prohibited for existing algorithms. We also proved the recovery guarantee of the algorithm. -- In Journal Publication 4, we give a survey of this framework in the long-standing book series "Handbook of Numerical Analysis". In the rest publications, the framework is also extended and generalized to solve other low-rank matrix related problems such as phase retrieval, image restoration, joint color and depth image reconstruction, and NMR spectroscopy.

16306317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16306317.value: 1. The framework developed in this project are for low-rank matrix recovery. It can be extended to low-rank tensor recovery problems, which are fundamental in data analysis and scientific computing. Indeed, we have an on-going GRF grant to pursue this research. 2. The low-rank matrix model can be viewed as bi-linear generative model for data, and low-rank matrix recovery is an inverse problem with a bi-linear generative model. Recently, there are many research works on inverse problems with neural network generative models. Since bi-linear generative model can be viewed as a two layer linear network, it is interesting to extend our algorithm and theory to inverse problems with neural network generative models. We will apply grants from RGC on this.

16306317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16306317.value: In this research project, we have developed a framework for constructing provable non-convex optimization methods for low-rank matrix recovery problems, which has numerous applications in the real world such as nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy, recommendation systems, video surveillance, and medical imaging. Our algorithms not only come with a solid mathematical theory, but also are applicable to the scenario in which traditional approaches fail.

16306417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16306417.value: Proteomics, the high-throughput identification and quantification of all proteins in a biological system, is playing an increasingly prominent role in life science research. In contrast to reductionist approaches, proteomics allows the researcher to investigate the entire cellular machinery at once, providing unprecedented insights into biological phenomena. Similar to other “omics” technologies, however, proteomics experiments generate an enormous amount of data, which demand sophisticated data analysis methods that are unfamiliar to most life science researchers. Therefore, the development of effective and user-friendly data analysis methods is a critical challenge that must be met so that the full potential of proteomics can be realized. In the most commonly adopted proteomic work-flow, complex mixtures of proteins are digested into shorter peptides, which are analyzed by liquid chromatography coupled to mass spectrometry (LC-MS). To obtain sequence information, the peptide ions are isolated and fragmented. The resulting fragment ion spectra, also called tandem mass (MS/MS) spectra, are identified to the peptide sequence by specialized algorithms. Once identified, a fragment ion spectrum can function as the “fingerprint” of the peptide ion, and stored in a spectral library to facilitate future experiments. Spectral libraries thus represent concise summaries of the observed proteome, and are indispensable community resources in the same way as DNA sequence databases are in the field of genomics. In fact, a spectral library covering the entire human proteome is a key deliverable of the Human Proteome Project, a sequel to the Human Genome Project. This proposal aims to address the problem of building spectral libraries for proteomics in the Big Data Era. We would like to completely revamp the current protocol of library building, which was developed a decade ago for much smaller data volume in the early days of proteomics. Specifically, the research proposal will describe how we intend to cope with, and indeed take advantage of, the characteristics of proteomic “Big Data” – volume, velocity and variety – for spectral library building in proteomics. Our proposed method will (i) employ spectrum clustering to preserve data linkage and reduce reliance on error-prone identification methods, to enable incremental updates, (ii) utilize graphical processing units (GPUs) to perform clustering efficiently, (iii) develop a universal spectrum validation to automate error detection for spectral libraries. We also plan to integrate our method into existing data analysis pipelines and data repositories, which would require the development of a common library format, to deliver the maximum impact to the field. 蛋白質組學旨在把生物系統中所有蛋白質進行高通量鑑定和定量。在生命科學研究中蛋白質組學技術正發揮越來越突出的作用， 因蛋白質組學允許研究者一次性檢視整個細胞機器，為生物學現象提供前所未有的啟示。然而，與其他組學技術一樣，蛋白質組學實驗產生大量的數據，需要複雜的數據分析方法。這常常是 大多數生命科學家的大難題。因此，開發有效和容易使用的數據分析方法是實現蛋白質組學的潛力所必須克服的挑戰。在最常用的蛋白質組工作流程中，蛋白質混合物先被消化成較短的肽，然後通過液相色譜與質譜（LC-MS）進行分析。為了獲得序列信息，肽離子被逐一碎片化。所得到的片段離子譜，也稱為串聯質譜（MS / MS），可通過專門的算法鑑定到肽序列。一旦鑑定，這些片段離子譜可以視作肽離子的“指紋”，並存儲在質譜庫中，以方便將來的實驗。因此，質譜庫是蛋白質組學中不可或缺的共用資源，其地位與DNA序列數據庫在基因組學領域相同。事實上，建立一個涵蓋整個人類蛋白質組的質譜庫是人類蛋白質組學計劃的重要的目標。此研究計劃旨在解決在大數據時代建立蛋白質組學質譜庫的問題。我們希望徹底改革目前的質譜庫建立方法，因為目前所用的方法誕生在蛋白質組學早期，數據量比今天要小得多。具體來說，研究方案將描述我們打算如何處理並確實利用蛋白質組學的“大數據”特質 - 數據量，數據和產生速度和數據的多元化 – 在改良質譜庫建立的方法。我們提出的方法將（i）使用質譜聚類來保持數據鏈接，並減少對容易出錯的識別方法的依賴，以實現增量更新，（ii）利用圖形處理器（GPU）有效地執行聚類，（iii）開發通用的質譜驗證法，來達至質譜庫錯誤檢測的全自動化。我們還計劃將我們的新方法連合到現有的數據分析流程和數據存儲庫中，包括開發廣泛通用的質譜庫格式，以便讓新方法產生最大的影響力。

16306417.label: Realisation of objectives
16306417.value: The captioned project has been completed with full realization of the objectives. Objective 1 Our first objective is to develop an efficient and effective computational workflow for tandem mass spectral library building that is based on spectrum clustering, enables incremental update, preserves unidentified spectra, and is robust against identification errors. We proposed to use GPU-acceleration to compute pair-wise similarity of all spectra (including unidentified ones) in a collection. The clusters obtained are then analyzed to determine how best to build the consensus spectrum for each cluster to be included in the library. This objective has been completed through the work of two M.Phil. students. The GPU acceleration part has been fully coded and optimized, and the program (called ClusterSheep, https://github.com/kpto/ClusterSheep) is made available to the community in GitHub. We also demonstrated that spectral libraries built based on the spectrum clusters are superior quality to the one built by the traditional workflow of grouping the spectra by identifications. The work is disseminated in a recent publication (P. K. P. To. et al., Journal of Proteome Research 20(12), 5359–5367 (2021)). The further optimization of the similarity scoring function and the determination of cluster boundary was covered in the M.Phil. thesis of Justin Yik Yeung Lee and disseminated in a conference presentation (Lee, To, Wu and Lam, ASMS 2018). Briefly, the simple dot product similarity measure has been enhanced to take into account the precursor mass-to-charge ratio deviation as a score component to reduce the formation of mixed clusters, and the DBSCAN algorithm was adopted to help delineate clusters as an alternative to the more expensive cluster refinement procedure based on betweenness centrality. The updated algorithm is already released as a new version of ClusterSheep. Furthermore, the vision of this new way of building spectral libraries is shared with the community in an invited lecture: H. Lam. “Peptide MS/MS spectral libraries – current status and future directions.” 68th Annual Conference of the American Society of Mass Spectrometry (ASMS) Reboot, online (2020). Objective 2 Our second objective is to develop an automated and adaptive universal spectrum validator that can be deployed to detect and remove questionable spectra in spectral libraries. A context-free spectrum validator which depends only on information of the spectrum itself has been developed and disseminated as an open-source tool (https://github.com/wulongict/PSMValidator). We tried a large number of machine learning algorithms and features and settled on a Random Forest-based classifier trained on high-quality consensus spectra in spectral libraries. The unique advantage of this validator, as compared to other statistical validation methods in the field, is that no search engine scores or information about the search space or query space is used, such that it can be generally deployed in to validate one spectrum in isolation, and without the use of decoys. Despite the less information it uses, we have shown that its performance in terms of classification accuracy is comparable to popular tools such as PeptideProphet and Percolator which have access to more context-dependent information. This work has been presented in two conferences (Wu and Lam, ASMS 2018; Wu and Lam, AOMSC, 2020), and a manuscript has been written and will be submitted shortly. We have also explored combining the context-free validator with the clustering algorithm developed in Objective 1, for instance, including cluster connectivity information to help validation. Although we did not come up with a stand-alone validator that makes the classification decision automatically, we have developed a web-based application that, given any query spectrum, one can find and display its “spectral neighborhood” among millions of spectra in real time. This requires a novel indexing method based on dimensionality reduction that would place similar spectra in the same “bucket.” The classification score of the context-free validator is also displayed in the same user-interface for the query spectrum, enabling the user to make his/her own judgement with both the context-free and contextual information at hand. This computational advance to put any query in its spectral neighborhood very quickly is the basis of our next funded GRF proposal (Ref. 16207620), and we are now pursuing this idea as a full-feature spectral archive search engine, rather than a more limited validator. Objective 3 (removed due to partial funding) Our originally proposed Objective 3 was to develop an open, standardized, and community-wide format for spectral libraries in proteomics, along with the necessary software tools to read and write libraries in this format, under the framework of the Human Proteome Organization Proteome Standards Initiative (HUPO-PSI). Due to partial funding, we decided not to pursue the originally proposed Objective 3 within the project period. However, for full disclosure, we have been involved in the HUPO-PSI’s MS working group to define a new open spectral library format. A key component of the library format, a universal spectrum identifier, has been developed and gone through approval by HUPO, and disseminated in a manuscript by the working group (E. Deutsch, et al., Nat. Methods 18, 768-770 (2021)). Work is ongoing to develop the spectral library format in the past two years (https://www.psidev.info/mzSpecLib).

16306417.label: Major findings and research outcome
16306417.value: The major research outcome of this project was an efficient and effective spectrum clustering algorithm enabled by GPU acceleration, and a context-free spectrum validator trained from a large amount of prior data. Both of these methods are released as open-source software, and are part of an enhanced workflow for tandem mass spectral library building that is better suited to today’s data volume. Another outcome of the project was the training of one M.Phil. student Justin Yik Yeung Lee, and one Ph. D. student, Long Wu. Dr. Wu has continued his research in computational proteomics as a postdoctoral scientist, working on the spectral archive search engine project. The preparation for the project also helped train another M.Phil. student, Paul Ka Po To, who left the group soon after the project was funded, but was instrumental in initiating the work of ClusterSheep and generating the preliminary data to support the proposal.

16306417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16306417.value: As described above, we have taken a good first step in the ultimate goal of taking advantage of the massive amounts of proteomics data collected by the community. The vision of organizing billions spectra by similarity has led us first to a GPU-accelerated algorithm that can perform pairwise spectral comparisons, and then to an indexing scheme that can deal with even larger data volume, a starting point for a spectral archive search engine, which would be the first of its kind in proteomics. Thanks to the advances of this project, we have since obtained additional funding (GRF Ref. 16207620) to take the next step of developing the full-feature spectral archive search engine. In addition, we demonstrated the potential of a “Big Data” approach to a longstanding problem in proteomics in PSM validation, which is in contrast to the prevailing notion of the need for dataset-specific models employing contextual information. Our success prompts us to apply the same concept to another related problem in false discovery rate estimation, which we would pursue in our next project as part of the spectral archive search engine. The community effort to develop a new open spectral library format (the originally proposed Objective 3) will continue beyond the project period.

16306417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16306417.value: Proteomics, the high-throughput identification and quantification of all proteins in a biological system, is playing an increasingly prominent role in life science research. Similar to other “omics” technologies, however, proteomics experiments generate an enormous amount of data, but such data, though made publicly available, is currently poorly organized and reused. The best way to take advantage of prior data is to compile spectral libraries of the fragmentation patterns of peptides which will greatly facilitate future experiments. This research project aimed to address the problem of building spectral libraries for proteomics in the Big Data Era. We developed an algorithm utilizing graphical processing units (GPUs) to vastly speed up spectrum clustering while preserving the cluster structure for error detection and incremental updates of spectral libraries. We also developed a machine learning-based spectrum validator to automate error detection for spectral libraries, adopting a Big Data approach to the problem. Trained on a large amounts of existing data, the validator is context-free and universally calibrated, and performed comparably to existing tools that construct dataset-specific models based on more contextual information.

16306717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16306717.value: One of the major consequences of the 2007-08 financial crisis was the emergence of the so-called multi-curve models for the pricing of interest-rate derivatives. Before the financial crisis, the forward-rate curves of different tenors (or terms) were linked by the discount curve. For pricing and hedging purposes, it was sufficient to model only one forward-rate curve for, typically, the three-month tenor. During the crisis, this link was lost, and the quantitative finance community was forced to model the forward-rate curves of different tenors simultaneously. Today, barriers to the segregation by tenors are in place. Specifically, the derivatives of a particular tenor are priced by a model of the forward-rate curve of that particular tenor and then hedged by instruments of the same tenor. Yet, the dynamics of the forward-rate curves prescribed by the multi-curve models is, at least, at odds with the dynamics of the basis swap curves. In particular, the basis swap curves appear to be driven by one random factor only, thus rejecting the independent evolution of the LIBOR curves of different tenors, with or without correlations. In both theory and practice, the use of multi-curve models that are unable to model basis swaps leaves room for errors in the pricing and hedging of derivatives across tenors. In the proposed project, we will introduce a new strategy for modeling LIBOR rates that will 1) accommodate the basis swap curves and 2) price the LIBOR derivatives across tenors. The strategy will be to superimpose a model of the term structure of the expected loss rates, which account for the counterparty default and liquidity risk premiums, on some of the existing LIBOR rate models. By taking into account the premiums for the LIBOR panel review via the expected loss rates, we will achieve the two aforementioned objectives with such dual-curve modeling. To price derivatives and/or to model the implied volatility smiles, we will extend various existing single-curve LIBOR models to the dual-curve context. In addition, we will develop accurate or approximate pricing formulae for caplets/floorlets and swaptions under the dual-curve version of the LIBOR market model, the SABR-LMM model, and the affine LIBOR model. We will also develop Monte Carlo simulation schemes for various dual-curve models for the purpose of pricing exotic LIBOR derivatives. Finally, we will develop methodologies for credit valuation adjustments to interest-rate derivatives by utilizing our theories on derivatives pricing under the dual-curve LIBOR models. 在二零零八年的金融风暴以前，不同频率（一个月，三个月，六个月和十二个月）的远期利率期限结构（曲线）和折现率曲线可以互推，而且他们都产生相同的有效年度投资回报。因此，金融风暴以前，为了给利率衍生品定价和对冲我们只需要为其中一条期限结构曲线建模，三个月的期限结构当属最为常用的选择。金融风暴的其中一个后果是远期利率期限结构和折现率曲线之间的传统联系不再存在，而且远期利率期限结构之间的有效年度投资回报也不再一致。后金融风暴时代的多曲线利率模型由此催生：投行同时模拟所有的远期利率期限结构和折现率曲线，模型的使用取决于衍生品的标的利率的频率。从效果上看这样做促成了利率衍生品市场的割裂，同时使得投行无法准确评估一个依赖各种利率的投资组合的市场风险。更大的问题是, 多曲线的利率模型可能根本上是不正确的，应为其所描述的动态行为与在市场上观察到的基点掉期曲线的动态行为相抵触。这一点，分析师们大多都清楚，但又无计可施。 在本研究项目中，我们希望建构一个新的LIBOR市场模型。这个模型能够1）和基点掉期市场兼容，和2）给基于不同利率频率的衍生品定价。我们的策略是在已有的LIBOR市场模型之上加上一个远期损失率的模型。通过使用远期损失率我们可以把交易对手风险和流动性风险都考虑的定价中来。特别地，在定义远期损失率时，我们把LIBOR成员银行的定期检讨制度也考虑进来，这使我们从根本上理解了基点掉期曲线的形成机制。在双期限结构的框架之下，我们将定义推广的LIBOR市场模型，SABR模型和仿射模型，并且为主要的衍生品建立定价公式。为了给一般的衍生品定价，我们还将开发蒙特卡洛方法。在此之上，我们还会解决在双线模型之下xVA的计算问题，这是目前市场的另一焦点。

16306717.label: Major findings and research outcome
16306717.value: We have developed a term structural model which, for the first time, offers financial intuitions or insights on the emergence of the basis swap curves, a new normal in the aftermath of the financial crisis.. This model is perhaps the only model until today that can accommodate the basis swap curves. This model can be used for pricing interest rate derivatives. We in particular have developed quasi closed-form price formulae for caps, floors and swaptions, so-called the benchmark interest rate derivatives.

16306717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16306717.value: London Interbank Offer Rates, LIBOR for short, will cease to serve as benchmarks of interest rates in the interbank markets after 2021. However, the model and the methodologies developed in the project will certainly be adopted for modeling new benchmarks of interest rates, yet to be finalized, and pricing and risk-managing interest rate derivatives on the new benchmarks.

16306717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16306717.value: After the 2008 financial crisis, existent interest rate models of the time could no longer be used to price and risk-manage interest rate derivatives properly, due to the significant presence of default risk premiums in the interest rate benchmarks in the interbank markets. Through this project, we introduce a new model that connects closely to the literature yet accommodates both market risks and default risk, so that we can again price and risk-manage interest rate derivatives in a way similar to what market practitioners had been doing before the 2008 financial crisis.

16306817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16306817.value: Synchronization is a phenomenon commonly found in many natural and artificial systems over a broad range of areas such as physics, biology, and engineering. In a power grid, the phase synchronization of the 50 Hz (or 60 Hz) alternating current running between the power stations enables electrical power to be transmitted through the grid. In the steady state, the phases at the two ends of a link are synchronized with a constant phase difference. Power flows from the end with a leading phase to the other end with a trailing phase. However, if there is a large discrepancy among the power generated and consumed at the stations, phase differences become unstable and may lead to power outages. This issue is especially relevant to next-generation smart grids, in which volatile renewable energy sources such as wind and solar play important roles. To enhance the stability of synchronization, grid operators can optimally allocate generated power among the power generators. The same control measures can be applied to protect the links from overloading. In addition, load shedding is needed to prevent cascade failures when some links in the grid break down. Recently, we successfully developed an efficient stabilization algorithm provided that the supply and demand are known. In reality, only power supply and demand predictions in the form of probabilistic distributions are available to make prompt decisions. This issue of optimizing oscillator networks with probabilistic information has not been addressed. In the proposed project, we will formulate a theoretical framework that will allow us to include uncertain information in coupled oscillator networks, and to consider the changes in behavior relative to networks operating with deterministic information. We will develop algorithms for probabilistic inputs that can be applied to optimize synchronization stability, protect links from overloading, or shed load to prevent cascade failures. We will also propose improved algorithms for stations to pass messages to neighboring stations, enabling them to predict local power flow fluctuations and hence implement distributed control. 同步現象廣泛存在於許多自然和人工系統中，如物理、生物和工程等領域。在電網中，電站之間傳導的50Hz(或60Hz)交流電，便是以同步的相位，使電力能夠通過電網傳輸。在穩態下，線路兩端的相位差固定，處於同步狀態。電能從相位領先一端流向相位落後一端。然而，如果電站的發電量與消耗量之間存在較大的差異，相位便變得不穩定，導致停電。這問題對下一代智慧電網尤其重要，其中發揮重要作用的風能和太陽能等可再生能源，存在很大漲落。為了提高同步的穩定性，電網運營者可以在發電站之間把發電量進行最優分配。同樣的控制措施可以用來避免線路超載。此外，我們需要卸載措施用來防止電網中的某些線路故障時產生的連鎖故障。最近，我們成功開發了一種有效的維穩演算法，對已知的供應和需求求解。實際上，我們需要作出迅速的決策時，只能根據以概率分佈形式的電力供需預測。怎樣優化含概率資訊的振盪子網絡，是一個尚未得到解決的問題。 在擬議的項目中，我們將製定一個理論框架，使我們能夠在振盪子耦合網絡中，加入不確定的資訊，並考慮相對於使用確定性資訊運行的網絡的行為，有什麼變化。我們將開發可用於優化同步穩定性的概率輸入演算法，避免線路超載，或減輕負載以防止連鎖故障。我們還將提出改進的演算法，透過節點將消息傳遞給鄰近節點，使它們能夠預測局部功率波動，從而實現分佈式控制。

16306817.label: Realisation of objectives
16306817.value: The Network Stability Problem: This project addresses the stability problem in complex networks due to fluctuations of resources such as those in the power grid. Such resource fluctuations induce flow fluctuations that may exceed the capacity limit of the transmission links and cause them to fail, which in turn can easily trigger a cascading failure and cause a global failure in the network. The Optimization Algorithm: We introduced the message-passing algorithm and discrete Green's function to elucidate how resource fluctuations determine flow fluctuations [4]. To enhance the robustness of the network against fluctuations, we developed the schemes of optimal bandwidth allocation in links and optimal resources adjustment in nodes, such that the number of overloaded links or the amount of excess flows in networks under fluctuations can be minimized. Similarly, the approach of optimal resource adjustment is to minimize the number of overloaded links in networks under fluctuations with the total resource change in the network fixed. Results: Compared with the conventional approach of proportionate bandwidth assignment or resources reduction, we found that the optimized bandwidth allocation or resources adjustment greatly enhance the stability of the networks against fluctuations. Extension: While we have demonstrated the effectiveness of our optimization scheme assuming Gaussian fluctuations, it was recently found that the power grid frequency fluctuations are better described by long-tailed distributions. We have also verified the robustness of our scheme to long-tailed distributions such as the Lévy-stable distribution. Implications to Network Structure: Furthermore, we found that the changes of loads and currents prescribed by the optimal bandwidth allocation and resource adjustment schemes are correlated with each other. Exceptions are some nodes that serve as relays (connected to highly fluctuating links that relay their fluctuations to other links without their own participation in resource adjustments). Unsupervised Learning: The extraction of underlying patterns from fluctuating data can also be found in the unsupervised learning of noisy data. Using the message-passing algorithm we considered how two high-dimensional vectors can be learned from examples when the number of examples increases [3]. We found that when examples are too few, no information about the hidden vectors can be extracted. When the data size increases, we found a critical size at which the inferred vectors start to have correlations with the hidden vectors. Furthermore, the critical data size decreases with the correlation of the hidden vectors, implying that correlations facilitate learning. Simulation results of the critical size agree with the theoretical derivation using the replica method. Permutation Symmetry: Immediately above the critical data size, the inferred vectors can only learn the common components of the hidden vectors [3]. This means that the inferred vectors are symmetric with respect to their permutation. When the data size increases further, the permutation symmetry breaks, but even beyond that point, the inferred vectors remain unspecialized with respect to the hidden vectors, and a further symmetry breaking occurs on increasing data size where the inferred vectors become specialized. All simulation results have an excellent agreement with the theoretical predictions of the replica method. Importance of Prior Knowledge: Pattern inference with fluctuating data performs better if prior knowledge of the hidden information is available. This can be formulated as the prior distribution in Bayesian inference. In [6] we proposed a statistical physics model of unsupervised learning with prior knowledge. Compared with the prior-free scenario, we revealed that the prior knowledge strongly reduces the critical data size for symmetry breaking, and moreover, it causes the permutation symmetry-breaking phases to merge. We further verified that the prior can be estimated from data samples. Multisensory Integration: When fluctuating data are received through independent channels, the data from the same source should be integrated to improve inference, and otherwise segregated to distinguish different sources. We derived inspiration from the neuroscience discovery that there are two groups of neurons in the monkey’s brain whose tunings are either congruent or opposite when receiving stimuli from the visual and vestibular channels. We developed a network model with two reciprocally connected modules modeling interacting visual-vestibular areas [1]. Each module consists of both congruent and opposite neurons. We showed that congruent neurons implement integration, while opposite neurons compute cue disparity information for segregation, and the interplay between two groups of neurons achieves efficient multisensory information processing. Bimodular Networks: We studied bimodular networks when they receive information from two channels [5]. Inter-channel correlations are encoded by the inter-modular couplings. We found that excitatory couplings exert attraction on the inferred position in the efferent module, whereas inhibitory couplings exert repulsion. Efferent inferred magnitudes are primarily strengthened by the inter-modular couplings but, to a lesser extent, weakened by being displaced from the direct input. At low disparity, the inferred positions encode the posterior means in the Bayesian framework, whereas at high disparity, multiple states exist, and each can be accessed by varying the time delays of the inputs. When one input is moving, the efferent inferred position can be pinned, unpinned or tracking depending on the inter-modular couplings, the speed and strength of the moving stimulus. Data Fluctuations in Highway Traffic: We studied a tremendous volume of real traffic data obtained from the Taiwan highway system [2]. We monitored the evolution of traffic congestions, and found that congestion is characterized by a loopy trajectory in the flux-density space such that the area enclosed by the loop increases with the severity of congestion. There is a power law relating the area of the loop to the drop of influx during the congestion period. Data extracted from the time delays of individual vehicles show that the area enclosed by the loop is a measure of the economic loss due to congestion. The use of the loss area to understand various highway characteristics is also explored. Switching Effects on Highways: As an application, we studied highway traffic in Hsuehshan tunnel in Taiwan [8]. When there is traffic congestion, a remarkable fraction of vehicles switches to an alternative path, even if it cost more time than jamming on the highway. In addition, we evaluated through statistics and the government’s policy to improve the road condition of the tunnel. Data Fluctuations in Housing Price: As another application, we studied housing price in Hong Kong from 1992 to 2010 [7]. We found that there is an overall periodicity of approximately 30 months in housing price changes and a strong lead-lag relationship between housing price and transaction volume. Analysis of the cross-covariance of the housing price, transaction volume and prime lending rate reveals that this quasi-periodicity is potentially driven by prime lending rates. Incorporation of quasi-periodicity into the kernel of Gaussian processes further enables us to construct a predictive model of the Hong Kong housing price trends that outperforms other traditional kernel functions.

16306817.label: Major findings and research outcome
16306817.value: This project addresses the stability problem in complex networks due to fluctuations of resources such as those in the power grid. The Optimization Algorithm: We introduced the message-passing algorithm and discrete Green's function to elucidate how resource fluctuations determine flow fluctuations [4]. We developed the schemes of optimal bandwidth allocation in links and optimal resources adjustment in nodes. Results: Compared with the conventional approach of proportionate bandwidth assignment or resources reduction, our optimization schemes greatly enhance the stability of the networks against fluctuations. Extension: We have verified the robustness of our scheme for long-tailed distributions recently found in power grids. Implications to Network Structure: Furthermore, we found that the two optimization schemes are correlated except in relay nodes. Unsupervised Learning: We found a critical data size at which the inferred vectors in unsupervised learning start to have correlations with the hidden vectors [3]. The result is in excellent agreement with theory. Permutation Symmetry: When the data size increases above the critical point, the inferred vectors change from permutation symmetric to those with broken symmetry but unspecialized, and finally to specialized [3], in excellent agreement with theory. Importance of Prior Knowledge: We proposed a statistical physics model of unsupervised learning with prior knowledge, revealing its advantages when compared with the prior-free scenario [6]. Multisensory Integration: Inspired by the neuroscience discovery of congruent and opposite neurons, we developed a bimodular network model that integrates low-disparity information and segregate high-disparity information [1]. Bimodular Networks: We analyzed the behaviors of bimodular networks [5] and found the relations between inter-modular couplings, inferred positions and magnitudes. The dependence on disparity is consistent with the Bayesian framework. Data Fluctuations in Highway Traffic: We studied real traffic data and found that congestion is characterized by a loopy trajectory in the flux-density space [1]. The area enclosed by the loop is a measure of the economic loss due to congestion. Analysis of Real Fluctuating Data: We discovered switching effects in real highway traffic data, and quasi-periodicity in real housing market data. The latter enables us to construct a performing predictive model.

16306817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16306817.value: The message-passing algorithm is very effective in estimating the means of the flow distributions in networks, but seriously under-estimates the variances of the flow distributions due to the negligence of loop effects. We will develop Generalized Belief Propagation (GBP) algorithms to overcome this shortcoming. Our initial tests on Gaussian Markov Random Fields (GMRFs) of arbitrary topology showed that it converges fast and gives accurate means and variances estimations. In the area of multisensory integration, we will consider prior distributions consisting of a correlated component and an independent component, which is relevant to the issue of causal inference. We will extend the bimodular network by adding additional modules or gated inter-modular neurons. We will develop models with predictive ability inspired by recent biological experimental results showing that the mutual information between the visual signals and the responses of the bullfrog retina has a future component. We will extend the analysis of highway traffic data to study other types of fluctuating data, such as air traffic data in the terminal maneuvering area of the Hong Kong International Airport. Indeed, a collaborative project on air traffic data was recently funded.

16306817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16306817.value: This project addresses the stability problem in complex networks due to fluctuations of resources such as those in the power grid. We introduced algorithms to elucidate how resource fluctuations determine flow fluctuations. Then we developed the schemes of optimal bandwidth allocation in links and optimal resources adjustment in nodes. Compared with conventional approaches, our optimization schemes greatly enhance the stability of the networks against fluctuations. In the learning of hidden high-dimensional vectors through noisy examples, we found a critical data size at which the inferred vectors start to correlate with the hidden vectors. Above the critical point, the inferred vectors change from unspecialized and then finally to specialized. We also found that prior knowledge facilitates learning. Considering fluctuating data received from different channels, we developed a bimodular network model that integrates low-disparity information and segregate high-disparity information. Finally, we studied real fluctuating data in highway traffic and housing price. In highway traffic we found that congestion is characterized by a loopy trajectory in the flux-density space. The area enclosed by the loop is a measure of the economic loss due to congestion. In housing price data, we discovered periodic fluctuations and construct a predictive model accordingly.

16306917.label: Realisation of objectives
16306917.value: Regarding to the proposed objectives, we have completed all our targets. Through the comprehensive screening and analysis, we successfully achieved a redox sensitive peptide with a high transgene expression capability. The details are listed below: 1. Develop new strategies to improve DNA release efficiency. In our previous studies, we investigated four strategies to enhance DNA release efficiency, including: • Adding hydrophilic residues to lower the stability of the whole co-assemblies; • Adding pH-sensitive residues (histidine) in the central segment and the N-terminus of the peptide to shift the hydrophilic/hydrophobic balance in the acidic environment (late endosome or lysosome). This strategy could facilitate DNA release once the co-assemblies were internalized into cells. • Adding redox-sensitive residues (t-Butyl-S-S-Cysteine) into the peptide to decrease the stability of the co-assemblies and facilitate DNA release in the cellular reducing environment. • Adding amino acid with bulky side chains in the central segment to disrupt the peptide packing and destabilize the co-assemblies. • Changing the linker length and atom type adjacent to the aromatic residues to tune the π-involved interaction, eventually modulating the peptide self-assembly and peptide-DNA co-assembly properties and biological function. 2. Construct redox-sensitive nanococoons of different interface sensitivity against the reducing reagents. To explore the different interface sensitivity to reducing reagents, we have constructed several co-assemblies with varied peptide sequence, such as 1) varying the number of N-terminal histidines while keeping the same number of central redox-sensitive residues; 2) substituting hydrophobic leucine residues with hydrophilic histidine residues, and redox-sensitive residues. These peptides were co-assembled with DNA into different morphologies, such as cocoon-like for H1(StBu), berry-like for H3(StBu), H4(StBu), H8(StBu) and spherical particle-like for H10. The β-sheet peptide secondary structure was identified within all the peptide self-assemblies and peptide-DNA co-assemblies. The same β-sheet peptide secondary structure demonstrates that the redox-sensitive residues were packed in different interfaces. 3. Study redox-triggered nanococoon uncoating and DNA release, and related uncoating mechanism. We developed both the pH-sensitive and redox-sensitive co-assemblies, so their responsiveness to different stimuli were individually evaluated, respectively. H4 peptide contains pH-sensitive residues at the central segment and the N-terminus. It co-assembled with plasmid DNA into berry-like particles at neutral pH. At acidic pH, the solid particles disassembled into big loose aggregates. In the presence of heparin sulphate concentration of 2mg/ml, the acidic loose complex released DNA out, but the neutral nanoberry did not. This suggests that pH-sensitive nanoberries facilitate DNA release through disassembling at acidic condition. For the redox-sensitive H10-DNA co-assemblies, in the absence of heparin sulphate and reducing agent GSH, no DNA was released out. In the presence of 2mM GSH, increasing heparin sulphate from 0.1mg/ml to 0.4mg/ml facilitates DNA release from the redox-sensitive co-assemblies, but the control co-assemblies without redox-sensitivity kept DNA at the original spots. This suggests that the redox-sensitive units in H10-DNA co-assemblies could facilitate DNA release. 4. Evaluate intracellular DNA release and gene transfection of the redox-sensitive nanococoons. We evaluated the transgene expression efficiency of the redox-sensitive H10-DNA co-assemblies with GFP-encoded plasmid as the reporter gene. During our studies, we observed that H10-DNA co-assemblies could efficiently transfect Hek293 cells. Through functional screening by transfecting cells, we comprehensively optimization the combination of the peptide sequence, the concentration of peptide and DNA as the co-assembling components. We identified a peptide H10, which could co-assemble with DNA into spherical particles, and induce significantly high transfection over 90% efficiency. Besides, we also discovered that H10-DNA co-assemblies could transfect cells in complete cell medium in the presence of 10% FBS without medium replacement and very low amount of DNA could induce significantly high transfection efficiency. To identify the intracellular DNA release, we used Cy5-DNA as the probe and imaged the live cells with confocal microscope. After 24hr-incubation, we observed that Cy5-DNA (light blue colour) successfully entered into cells, and distributed into cytosol. Cy5-DNA was separated from red lysotracker, indicating the successful endosomal escape of DNA. Though no obvious Cy5-DNA signal was shown in nucleus, we believe it is because of low Cy5-DNA in the whole culture. Transfection efficiency of H10 in different cells (Hek293, Hela, RAW264.7) were tested with DNA. The transfection condition in different cells were optimized by altering the peptide (0.5-5uM) and DNA or mRNA concentration (200-1600pg/ul). The optimal condition for each cell line were those with the highest transfected cell percentage and lowest nucleic acid amount while keeping the cell viability higher than 80%. As shown in Fig. 6, H10 was competent in delivering DNA in Hek293 cells (~75%) and Hela cells (~80%) though the transfection efficiency was comparatively limited in RAW264.7 cells (~20%) (versus Lipo3000 shows <30%). In addition, we identified the optimal storage condition is freeze-dry the H10/mRNA or H10/DNA co-assemblies with 10% sucrose at 1:1 ratio. The resulted white powders can be reconstructed with water and the transfection efficiency in Hela cells showed no decrease.

16306917.label: Major findings and research outcome
16306917.value: 1) We constructed virus capsid subunit-like small nanodiscs with a rationally design peptide. The subunits are very uniform and could co-assemble with DNA into Adenovirus-like particles. This morphology similarity mimics the natural virus assembling process. This virus mimics could protect genetic cargoes and transfect cells efficiently. It is one of the good examples of nature-inspired biomimetic. 2) By correlating the constructed peptide-DNA co-assemblies with the peptide sequence and the transfection results, we discovered that the peptide self-assembly property was critical to regulate both the physical (morphology, surface feature) and biological properties of the co-assemblies. Therefore, this result indicates the importance of peptide sequence variation on regulation of biological function of peptide-DNA co-assemblies. 3) Introduction of pH-sensitive histidine residues into peptide H4 led to the construction of pH-sensitive nanococoons, with the morphology similar to parapoxvirus. Nanococoons showed the significant improvement of transgene expression, which is comparable to that by the commercially available gene transfection agent Lipofectamine. Therefore, this pH-sensitive peptide-DNA co-assembly is a promising gene delivery vector. 4) We constructed peptide-DNA co-assembled nanoberries, which displayed virus like subunits on the surface. This adenovirus-like artificial virus gradually disassembled in the acidic environment, mimicking virus-like disassembling process. 5)We systematic reviewed the synthetic approaches used for nucleic acid delivery and provided perspectives on how the chemical properties of different types of materials influence on the delivery and intracellular trafficking process of the genetic cargoes. 6) By altering the diphenylalanine analogues of different linker, we discovered the significant role of linker length and the atom type on the π-involved interaction, eventually influencing on the assembly property and transfection efficiency. This provides new tools to regulate the assembly property and biological function of peptide-DNA co-assemblies. Research outputs: two published papers, two submitted manuscripts, one review article and four conference papers.

16306917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16306917.value: To improve the transfection efficiency of the self-assembling peptide carrier, further modification of the peptide sequence to enhance endosomal escape and intracellular homing can be pursued. Thus far, the carrier has been investigated for the delivery of plasmid DNA. With advent of different classes of promising nucleic acid medicines, the potential of the self-assembling peptide carrier to deliver ODN, siRNA, miRNA and mRNA should be explored.

16306917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16306917.value: We explored two stimuli (pH and redox) as the main strategies to improve DNA release from peptide-DNA co-assemblies. By varying peptide sequence or aromatic residue linker property, we constructed peptide-DNA co-assemblies and buried redox or pH-sensitive residues in the different interfaces. In the presence of the stimuli, we observed disassembly of the co-assemblies, which is companied with DNA release. These stimuli-responsive peptide-DNA co-assemblies displayed high transgene expression.

16307117.value: To study Majorana fermions in multilayer transition metal dichalcogenides/nanowire heterostructures.
rows: To study Majorana fermions in multilayer transition metal dichalcogenides/nanowire heterostructures.

16307117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16307117.value: Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMD) are layered materials similar to graphene. A monolayer TMD material consists of a layer of transition metal sandwiched between two identical layers of chalcogen atoms. Importantly, TMD materials have rather high electron mobility and sizeable energy gaps. Due to the two-dimensional properties of TMD materials, they can be easily gated from an insulating state to a conducting state. These properties make TMD promising materials for transistors. Interestingly, it was shown that monolayer TMD such as MoS2 and NbSe2 are superconducting at low temperatures. Due to a special type of Ising spin-orbit coupling (SOC) of monolayer TMD, it was shown that the superconducting properties of TMD materials are very special. For example, the upper critical fields of superconducting TMD can be as high as 60 Tesla. We called superconducting TMD with Ising SOC, Ising superconductors. In more recent works, the PI and collaborators showed that, due to the strong Ising SOC in TMD, monolayer TMD can be used to create topological superconductors which support Majorana fermion zero energy modes. A Majorana mode can be regarded as half a fermionic mode. Two spatially separated Majorana modes form a fermionic mode. This fermionic mode can be filled or empty, which results in a 0 or 1 state of a quantum bit (qubit) for quantum computation. With these potential applications in quantum computation, the search for Majorana zero modes is one of the most important topics in physics in recent years. However, monolayer superconducting TMD materials are difficult to fabricate and only a few experimental groups in the world can make them. On the other hand, many experimental groups can fabricate superconducting multilayer TMD. Multi-layer TMD can have rather different band structure and even different point group symmetry than monolayer TMD. Similarly, bilayer graphene can have rather different properties than monolayer graphene. The question is, can multi-layer TMD be used to create Majorana modes? In this proposal, we propose that multilayer TMD can be used to create Majorana fermions. We also propose that superconducting bilayer TMD can be used to create a special type of time-reversal invariant Fulde–Ferrell–Larkin–Ovchinnikov (FFLO) state in which Cooper pairs formed by pairs of electrons carry finite momenta. We believe that our work will deepen the understanding of multi-layer TMD for their applications in quantum computation and for creating exotic superconducting states. 過渡金屬二硫化物（TMD）是類似於石墨烯的層狀材料。單層的過渡金屬二硫化物材料由兩個相同硫族原子層及夾於其中的過渡金屬層所組成。重要的是， 過渡金屬二硫化物材料具有有相當高的電子遷移率和相當大的能隙。由於過渡金屬二硫化物材料的二維特性，它們可以容易地從絕緣狀態被門控成導電狀態。這些性質使得過渡金屬二硫化物成為有希望的晶體管材料。 有趣的是，研究表明單層過渡金屬二硫化物材料（例如MoS2、NbSe2）在低溫下會成為超導體。由於單層過渡金屬二硫化物特殊的伊辛自旋-軌道耦合， 這些材料的超導性質非常特殊。例如，超導過渡金屬二硫化物的上臨界磁場可高達60特斯拉。我們稱有伊辛自旋-軌道耦合的超導過渡金屬二硫化物為伊辛超導體。 項目負責人（PI）及其合作者在最近的工作中指出，由於在過渡金屬二硫化物中存在的強伊辛自旋軌道耦合作用，單層的過渡金屬二硫化物可以被用於製作拓撲超導體，而該拓撲超導體中將存在馬約拉納零能模。一個馬約拉納模可以被視作半個費米態，而兩個在空間上被分開的馬約拉納模可以組為一個費米態。這個費米態可以被填充或不被填充，分別對應於量子計算中一個量子比特的1和0。由於在量子計算中的應用潛力巨大，對馬約拉納零能模的尋找在最近幾年已成為物理領域中最重要的課題之一。 然而，單層超導過渡金屬二硫化物很難製備，全世界也只有少數實驗團隊可以製作。另一方面，很多實驗團隊都能製備多層超導過渡金屬二硫化物。和單層相比，多層超導過渡金屬二硫化物會有很不同的能帶結構甚至點群對稱性。類似的，雙層石墨烯會有與單層石墨烯很不同的性質。 現在的問題是，多層超導過渡金屬二硫化物能否被用於創造馬約拉納模？在這份提案中，我們提出多層超導過渡金屬二硫化物可以被用於創造馬約拉納費米子。我們還提出，雙層超導過渡金屬二硫化物能被用於創造一種特殊的時間反演不變的Fulde–Ferrell–Larkin–Ovchinnikov (FFLO)態，其中電子形成具有非零動量的庫伯對。我們相信我們的工作會使我們深入認識多層超導過渡金屬二硫化物在量子計算和製備奇異超導態中的應用。

16307117.value: With the support of this project, we made several important steps in understanding the effect of spin-orbit coupling in multilayer transition metal dichalcogenides. 16307217.label: Project Objectives
16307217.value: To develop two dynamic network models with multiple-link data, with one model implying a parameter-driven model structure and the other related to an observation-driven model, and investigate the statistical properties of the two models. To derive Bayesian inference methods for the proposed network models, especially on the parameter estimation. We will compare the two classes of models, conduct Bayesian tests and determine the social space dimension. To develop network prediction procedures and conduct dependence analysis of multiple links. To evaluate and apply the dynamic network models to three empirical studies in the finance, information systems and education fields, with data collected from a financial database, a collaborative restaurant group and a university. To study the extension of our findings to nonlinear time series structures.

16307217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16307217.value: Network data appear in many areas, such as business, social sciences and biology. Current network models focus on analyzing one type of link data between nodes (e.g., people) in a network. However, it is not uncommon to have multiple links in a network. For example, in a student network, we can have three possible types of links between two students in month t: (1) whether the two students are in the same "range" of GPA in month t; (2) how many emails the two students exchange in month t; and (3) the total file sizes of the emails exchanged between the two students in month t. Modeling and analyzing multiple links in a network is indispensable to understanding how node/people in the network interact and how different types of interaction affect each other. With the modern development of information systems and technology, it is becoming more common to observe network data over time. Modeling multiple-link networks over time is complicated, as we have to capture both the time series dependence and the dependence between links simultaneously, which typically involves a large number of parameters. In this proposed project, we will develop dynamic network models that aim at tracing and quantifying the relationships between different links over time. Based on the hierarchical Bayes idea and dynamic linear models, Bayesian methodologies will be developed to estimate dynamic networks, make network predictions and conduct dependence analysis between links. The dynamic model will be applied to three empirical studies conducted in finance, information systems and education fields. Findings from this proposed project will not just provide a new modeling approach for the statistical analysis of multiple relationships dynamically, but also advance the application of multivariate network data in business, biological, education and social science research. 網絡數據出現在許多領域，如商業，社會科學和生物學。 現時的網絡模型側重分析網絡內節點（例如，人）之間單一類 的鏈接數據。 但是，網絡中有多種鏈接並不罕見。例如，在學生 網絡中，我們在月份t內可以有三種鏈接兩個學生的類型： （1）兩個學生是否在月份t內的GPA “分數範圍” 相同 （2）兩個學生在月份t內交換了多少封電子郵件; 和（3）兩個學生在月份t內交換的電子郵件的總文件大小。 網絡中多種鏈接的建模和分析對於了解節點或人們如何相互 影響及不同的互動類型是如何影響對方是不可或缺的。 隨著資訊系統及技術的現代化發展，根據時間變動的網絡 數據越來越普遍。 但隨著時間變動而建立的多鏈接網絡是 複雜的，因為我們必須同時抓住時間序列的依賴性和鏈接 之間的依賴關係，這通常涉及大量的參數。在建議的研究中， 我們會建立動態網絡模型，目的是跟踪和量化不同鏈接之間 的關係。建基於分層貝葉斯想法和動態線性模型，我們會 發展貝葉斯方法來計算動態網絡，進行網絡預測並在鏈接 之間進行依賴分析。該動態模型將應用在三項於金融， 資訊系統和教育領域上的實證研究內。 研究結果不只為 對多個關係的動態統計分析提供了一種新的建模方法， 而且還推動多元網絡數據在商業，生物，教育和社會科學 研究中的應用。

16307217.label: Realisation of objectives
16307217.value: In this project, we developed and worked on dynamic network models, related statistical methods and their applications. In particular, Ng, So and Tam (2021) introduced a new latent space model for incorporating information from two networks for understanding business relationships. This paper provides a starting point for dynamic network investigation in the project where the focus is on networks with two views (or two-dimensional networks). With the experience and foundation in Ng, So and Tam (2021), we extended the scope of applications to pandemic and financial networks in 2020 and 2021, when we collected COVID-19 and financial data, and investigated visualization tools, the use of network statistics, statistical methods for network modeling, and possible approaches in extracting useful information from one network for describing other networks. We documented our research experience and ideas using pandemic data in eight published papers. The results in Ng, So and Tam (2021) and the eight papers related to network analysis of COVID-19 data gave us good foundations to further develop modeling methods for dynamic multi-view networks. We completed a preliminary draft of the working paper on “Multi-view Dynamic Latent Space Model on Ordinal Network Data” which provides a generic approach to model multi-view networks. Applications to biological, financial and social networks can also be found in the manuscript. We prepared to submit this paper for publication in a few months. A proposed application to education is completed in a slightly unexpected way because of the pandemic that we found it hard to collect students’ data with online classes and other special measures during the pandemic. All the required methodology has been developed in the working paper, and an application to a social network (replacing a possible network formed by student engagement) have been done to demonstrate the potential use our proposed methodology in education. In addition, we will plan to collect relevant data in education so that we can apply our modeling framework to a network in education when everything is resumed to normal after the pandemic.

16307217.label: Major findings and research outcome
16307217.value: In the published paper, Ng, So and Tam (2021) “A latent space modeling approach to interfirm relationship analysis”, we built a bivariate dynamic latent space model which enables modeling of the probability of the simultaneous occurrence of two different kinds of link between a pair of nodes. A special feature of the proposed model in the paper is that we can study the interaction between two views of two different networks over time. The modeling of this time-varying interaction is important for us to understand dynamic network correlations, which capture the dependence of two networks over time. We applied the bivariate dynamic latent space model to study interfirm relationships and proposed Bayesian methods for statistical inference. A cluster of eight papers on network analysis using COVID-19 was published. In these papers, we studied visualization methods and network statistics to demonstrate the use of dynamic networks, in particular network connectedness, to quantify pandemic risk. We also applied the concept of network connectedness to financial markets in So, Chu and Chan (2021) “Impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic on financial market connectedness”. In So, Chu, Tiwari and Chan (2021) “On Topological Properties of COVID-19: Predicting and Assessing Pandemic Risk with Network Statistics”, we developed measures to quantify pandemic risk and risk contributions from nodes in the networks. This cluster of papers not only provided us good assets of possible applications of dynamic networks in healthcare and financial areas, but also gave us foundations on how to define multi-view dynamic networks. Based on the experience of the above nine papers, we proposed a generic multi-view dynamic network approach in “Multi-view Dynamic Latent Space Model on Ordinal Network Data”. We demonstrated that the modeling tools, including the proposed Bayesian inference, can be applied to modeling biological, financial and social networks. The above paper will be submitted to a journal for publication.

16307217.value: 1. Explore more applications of the proposed dynamic multi-view networks in social sciences and healthcare. 2. Study statistical methods other Bayesian for estimating dynamic multi-view networks. 3. Investigate on how to scale up the proposed dynamic network models to accommodate a few hundreds, or more than a thousand of nodes.

16307217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16307217.value: A main focus of this project is to develop modeling methods for dynamic networks. We studied how dynamic networks can be used to analyze relationships between business enterprises, co-movement of number of confirmed COVID-19 cases, dependence in biological sequence, dependence in financial returns of listed companies and social relationships. Modeling relationships or dependence over time in network models can help to visualize interesting patterns, extract useful network statistics and facilitate prediction. It is expected that the methodology and practical cases investigated in this project can be applied to a wide range of areas in business, social sciences and healthcare.

16307317.value: We consider several nonlinear equations such as the incompressible Euler and Navier-Stokes equations, surface quasi-geostrophic equations, alpha-patch equations and general nonlinear equations with nonlocal and singular transport, and possibly with inviscid or supercritical dissipation. We plan to study the fundamental existence, uniqueness and stability of solutions to these equations in borderline spaces with critical scaling regularity. 16307517.label: Major findings and research outcome
16307517.value: We provided a satisfactory theory about why the cyclic codes constructed by Ding are generally quite good with respect to the minimum distance, guided by the discovery, some new and good cyclic codes of composite length were discovered. This resulted in the published paper in 2018. We provided new constructions of cyclic codes many of which were shown to be optimal. In the opposite direction, we also showed that in some general sense, cyclic codes of composite length can not be good if the length of the code is supported by finitely many prescribed primes. This resulted in the published paper in late 2020.

16307517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16307517.value: It is known that cyclic codes of composite length can be use to construct convolutional codes. One development is to see if good and new convolutional codes can be obtained from these cyclic codes. Another development is to extend the previous results to cyclic codes of composite length over Galois rings.

16307517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16307517.value: In an interesting paper Ding provided three constructions of cyclic codes of composite length from quadratic residue codes, and it was shown numerically that these cyclic codes are with the best parameters among all cyclic codes. But very little is known about these codes. In this project we provide a satisfactory theory about Ding's construction and explain why these codes have large minimum distance in general. This new theory also enables us to construct new cyclic codes of composite length, which may be useful in the construction of convolutional codes. We also hope to extend this theory of cyclic codes to group-algebra codes and cyclic codes over galois rings.

16500617.label: Realisation of objectives
16500617.value: We summarize the realization of each objective below. More results can be found in the paper attached to this report. (1) Ingest the geo-data of water quality monitoring stations into ArcGIS and link them to water basin data, find upstream townships and downstream townships within 10 kilometers for each water quality monitoring station from 2000 to 2007. We collected water quality monitoring stations and geocoded all of them. We then link them to township boundary data and identify the upstream and downstream relationships from 2000 to 2007. Figure III in the paper provides the corresponding map. (2) Assemble and clean firm-level production data from 2000 to 2007 and match them to water quality monitoring stations. Geocode all the addresses. Our firm-level production information is based on the Annual Survey of Industrial Firms (ASIF) from 2000 to 2007. The ASIF data include private industrial enterprises with annual sales exceeding 5 million RMB and all the state-owned industrial enterprises (SOEs). The data are collected and maintained by the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) and contain a rich set of information obtained from the accounting books of these firms, such as inputs, outputs, sales, taxes, and profits. The ASIF data have detailed address information for sampled firms in each year. We geocode the location of the 952,376 firms that appeared in the sample and then compute the distance between each firm and its closest water quality monitoring station. Nearly 5% of the firms in the ASIF database belong to a parent multi-unit firm; we exclude them from subsequent analyses because the parent firm might avoid regulation by reallocating production activities across its subordinate firms. Please refer to the attached paper for details (III Data and Summary Statistics). (3) Collect firm-level emission data from 2000 to 2007 and geo-code all the firm addresses. To investigate whether water quality monitoring indeed reduces water-related emissions, we collect firm-level emission data from the Environmental Survey and Reporting (ESR) database, which is managed by the MEP. The ESR provides the most comprehensive environmental data in China that monitors polluting activities of all major polluting sources, including heavily polluting industrial firms, hospitals, residential pollution discharging units, hazardous waste treatment plants, and urban sewage treatment plants. In this study, we focus on the ESR firms that are in the same polluting industries as the ASIF firms. For every firm included in the ESR dataset, total output value, as well as various types of pollutant emissions, are documented. This enables us to construct total emission levels and emission intensity measures (emission levels divided by total output value) for large polluters across China. Among the different types of pollutants measured for each ESR firm, chemical oxygen demand (COD) is the most relevant one for this study. COD measures the amount of oxygen required to oxidize soluble and particulate organic matter in water and is widely used as an omnibus indicator for water pollution. A higher COD level indicates a greater amount of oxidizable organic material in the sample, which reduces dissolved oxygen levels. A reduction in dissolved oxygen can lead to anaerobic conditions, which are deleterious to higher aquatic life forms. In addition to COD emissions, we corroborate the firm emissions results by looking at two additional measures of water pollution: ammonia-nitrogen (NH3-N) emissions and wastewater discharge. (4) Estimate the impact of water quality monitoring on firm productivity using a regression discontinuity design and explore the channels through which firms are affected. Exploiting this spatial discontinuity in regulation stringency, we find that polluting firms immediately upstream of monitoring stations have more than 24% lower total factor productivity (TFP), and more than 57% lower chemical oxygen demand (COD) emissions, as compared to polluting firms in the near downstream. In addition, we provide a rich set of empirical results that shed light on the channels of the effect: (1) the upstream-downstream gap only emerged immediately after 2003, when the central government started to link water quality readings to political promotions; (2) the upstream-downstream gap is predominantly driven by prefectural cities with politically motivated leaders, and there is no significant spatial discontinuity when the local leaders don’t have promotion prospects; (3) only polluters within a few kilometers upstream are regulated, as emissions from farther upstream would dissipate quickly over space and have negligible impact on water quality readings; (4) upstream firms pay higher amounts of emission fees than downstream firms, although they actually emit significantly less, implying that local officials hold double standards in regulation enforcement; (5) the upstream-downstream gap gets particularly large when the monitoring stations are “automated” and therefore less susceptible to data manipulation, suggesting that local officials used to manipulate water quality readings for those traditional “manual” stations. Taken together, these findings consistently confirm that the salient spatial discontinuity in regulation enforcement arose from the misalignment between the national policy goal and local bureaucratic incentives. (5) Explore effect heterogeneity and figure out how different types of firms (large vs. small, SOE vs. Private) respond to environmental regulations. These results are summarized in Table II of the paper. Specifically, in Panel A of Table VII, we estimate the RD by firm ownership and find that the baseline TFP loss is driven mainly by private firms. Water quality monitoring has no significant impact on the TFP of state-owned enterprises (SOEs). This may reflect the fact that environmental regulations are not binding for SOEs as a practical matter, as they generally have greater bargaining power over local governments and thus face less stringent enforcement. However, given the relatively small number of observations for SOEs in our sample, this sub-sample null result should be interpreted with caution. In Panel B of Table VII, we investigate heterogeneity by firm size. In China, various levels of government practice a strategy known as “Grasping the Large and Letting Go of the Small” (“Zhua Da Fang Xiao”). “Grasping the large” means that policymakers mainly target large enterprises, while “letting go of the small” means that the government exerts less control over smaller enterprises. The phenomenon has been widely documented in the context of economic reforms and policy implementation for the minimization of implementation costs (e.g., Hsieh and Song, 2015). We investigate whether this phenomenon is true in environmental regulation. We define small firms as having fewer than 50 employees and estimate the effects of water quality monitoring separately for small and large firms. We find statistically significant effects only on larger firms, which is consistent with the general policy enforcement strategy adopted by Chinese local governments. In Panel C of Table VII, we explore regional heterogeneity. Here, we focus on China’s South-to-North Water Diversion project. The project is a large-scale water infrastructure project that diverts water from the Yangtze River in southern China to the Yellow River Basin in arid northern China, in an attempt to address water scarcity in the north. To do so, the central government imposed stringent requirements that the affected regions must ensure good water quality along the channeled river basins, which adds additional political stakes for the corresponding local governments. We thus split our sample into two sub-regions based on whether the location is designated as the water diversion project region. Our results show that the impact of water quality monitoring on firm productivity is indeed slightly larger in areas that are affected by the project.
