16503017.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16503017.value: 不确定性冲击和新兴市场经济周期

16503017.label: Project Objectives
16503017.value: Extend the one-sector small open economy model to a two-sector model and explore if the shocks emphasized in the literature can also explain the real exchange rate dynamics; Introduce uncertainty shocks to the model and estimate the volatility shocks using Bayesian estimation. Investigate if uncertainty shocks can help to explain business cycle of emerging market economies, especially real exchange rates dynamics.
rows: Extend the one-sector small open economy model to a two-sector model and explore if the shocks emphasized in the literature can also explain the real exchange rate dynamics;
Introduce uncertainty shocks to the model and estimate the volatility shocks using Bayesian estimation.
Investigate if uncertainty shocks can help to explain business cycle of emerging market economies, especially real exchange rates dynamics.

16503017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16503017.value: Understanding the characteristics of international business cycles has important empirical and policy implications. Recently, several papers show that the business cycle of emerging market economies exhibit different pattern compared to that of developed countries; namely, more volatile output, excess consumption volatility over output, and strong counter-cyclical trade balance. Standard real business cycle theory assumes agents will smooth their consumption across periods, which implies that the volatility of consumption should be smaller than that of output. Hence, explaining the real business cycle of emerging market economies remain a challenge for macroeconomists. Several shocks are discussed in the literature, including the shock to the trend (permanent productivity shocks) proposed in Aguiar and Gopinath (2007) and the interest rate premium shock emphasized in García-Cicco, Pancrazi and Uribe (2010). Uribe and Yue (2006) find VAR evidences to support that US interest rate and country spread shock could explain around 30% of aggregate movement in developing economies. These papers, however, mostly focus on one-sector models. Hence, real exchange rate dynamics and their comovement with major macroeconomics variables such as output, consumption and trade to GDP ratio are not considered. Given the high volatility and persistence of real exchange rate, a natural question is that if the shocks that can explain the emerging market business cycle could also explain the real exchange rate dynamics in these economies. Seoane (2016) show that standard one sector model with time-variant parameter could generate better estimation result and that these parameters are significantly correlated with exchange rate dynamics, implying real exchange rate should also be taken into consideration when analyzing business cycle properties in emerging market economies. Hence, in this project, we intend to extend the one-sector small open economy model to a model with tradable sector and non-tradable sector and explore quantitatively what kind of shocks can explain the business cycle of emerging market economies, especially the real exchange rate dynamics and the commove of real exchange rate and other macroeconomic variable. Instead of focusing on standard first-order shocks emphasized in the business cycle literature, we will introduce uncertainty shocks and use Bayesian estimation method to investigate if time varying second moments of shocks can help to explain business cycle of emerging market economies, as well as the extra volatility and high persistence of real exchange rates.

16503017.label: Realisation of objectives
16503017.value: Objective 1: completely realized. In the working paper attached in midterm progress report, we show that the comovement between RER and other macroeconomic aggregates are quite different between emerging economies and developed SOE. Motivated by these observations, we extend the standard one-sector model in to a two-sector small open economy model with tradable and non-tradable goods and estimate it using Bayesian estimation. We find that the standard two-sector model does well in generating RER persistence, but underestimate the real exchange rate volatility relative to output and its comovement with other macroeconomic aggregates observed in emerging market economies. Therefore, we incorporate two features into a standard two-sector model. First, we introduce imperfect substitution between home and foreign tradable goods to allow for deviation from law of one price in tradable goods. Second, we introduce a collateral constraint on firms’ borrowing which will be affected by real exchange rate fluctuations into the model. Our estimation result shows that this feature helps to explain the negative correlation between RER and real interest rate and countercyclical real interest rates. A model with these features does well in matching business cycle moments in emerging market economies, including those related to RER. Now we are working on some further development of this paper. This is motivated by strong negative comovement between the RER and the leverage ratio as well as positive correlation between real interest rate and the leverage ratio in emerging market economies. This provides evidence on how the RER and real interest rate affect firms’ borrowing cost in emerging market economies. So in a updated version of the paper, we will follow Bernanke et al. (1999) and Carlstrom and Fuerst (1997) and explore the role of collateral constraint in investment financing for emerging market economies. In particular, emerging market borrowers may find that interest rate and exchange rate fluctuations have large effects on their real net worth positions, and so, through balance sheet constraints that affect investment spending, have much more serious macroeconomic consequences than for developed economies. This financial friction may help to explain the observed comovements of RER and real interest rate in emerging markets. Objective 2: We met some technical problem when trying to complete it. Here I outline the problems. To compare the contribution of first-order and second-order uncertainty shocks, we need to solve the DSGE model up to third order and then we can use the particle filter suggested by Fernandez-Villaverde and Rubio-Ramirez (2005) to estimate uncertainty shocks by Bayesian method. Two challenges are found. 1. Issue on solving the nonlinear model To use the particle filter to evaluate the likelihood function of a standard nonlinear DSGE system, the nonlinear system should take the following state-space form: Measurement equation: y_t=φ(s_t,ϑ_t;θ)+u_t State Transition: s_t=ω(s_(t-1),ϑ_t;θ) θ is the parameters to be estimated. s_t is the endogenous state variables. u_t and ϑ_t are shocks. Usually, Dynare (a matlab toolbox) is used to solve the DSGE model up to third order. According to dynare manual, the linear approximation of DSGE model up to third order takes the following form: y_t=y^s +G_0+ G_1 z_t+G_2 (z_t×z_t )+G_3 (z_t×z_t×z_t ) where y^s is the steady state value of y_t, and z_t is a vector consisting of the deviation from the steady state of the state variables (including both endogenous and exogenous state variables). G_1 is the coefficient matrix on the first order linear approximation terms. G_2 is the matrix corresponding to the second order approximation terms. The matrix columns correspond to the Kronecker product of state variables. G_3 is the matrix corresponding to the third order approximation terms. The matrix columns correspond to the third Kronecker power of state variables. Unfortunately, this is NOT the state space form that can be used by particle filter algorithm. This is because the dynare does not distinguish between the endogenous state variables and the exogenous state variables (shocks). Therefore, we cannot use the dynare to solve the model to the third order. Furthermore, Dynare cannot directly conduct Bayesian estimation up to third order. Hence, we have to use other ways to solve the nonlinear model system up to the third order to apply the particle filter. We are trying to see if we can use the symbolic toolbox of Matlab to solve the system up to third order, but this may take a long time and we may need help from colleagues in math and engineering field to solve the technical problem. We plan to spend the next few months on this direction and figure out whether we can apply the particle filter to fulfil Objective 2. 2. Issue on the computational capacity Another obstacle of solving the model is the estimation time. Although we fail to solve the nonlinear model, we still evaluate the computation time required to solve a linear model using the particle filter in Dynare. Estimating a standard RBC model using Kalman filter may take less than one hours (with replication 1000000). When we evaluate the same model using particle filter by specifying 1000 particles, it takes more than 4 weeks to finish the estimation. Objective 3: 95% completed. Although we have met some technical difficulties in using Bayesian inference to retrieve volatility shocks, we follow other approaches in the literature to evaluate and model the role of uncertainty shocks in emerging markets and show empirically and theoretically that uncertainty shocks are important in driving the business cycles. We start by testing the role of financial frictions in the transmission of uncertainty shocks using a panel of emerging countries. Uncertainty is measured by the realized aggregate stock market volatility in the corresponding country during each quarter, an index widely used in the literature (e.g. Baker and Bloom, 2013). Our empirical findings suggest three main finding. First, a higher level of financial frictions exacerbates the positive reaction of interest rate to uncertainty shocks. We define it as the “interest rate channel" via which financial frictions reinforce the impact of uncertainty shocks on emerging market economies. Second, greater uncertainty is related to a larger decline in consumption than GDP for countries with lower financial development. Further decomposition of consumption into durables and nondurables show that it is the durable consumption that declines much more than output in response to a positive uncertainty shock at a higher level of financial frictions. These findings suggests that financial frictions amplify the impact of uncertainty on consumption more than the counterparts on GDP in emerging market economies. To explain the role of durable goods and financial frictions in propagating uncertainty shocks in emerging market economies, we develop a small open economy real business cycle model with banking sectors and durable goods. Uncertainty is specified as the time-variant standard deviation of productivity distribution of the bankers. Intuitively, when uncertainty is larger, the international lenders charge a higher risk premium and this leads to a higher real interest rate, which will affect households’ consumption of durable goods as well as investment. This characteristic generates excess volatility of durable consumption relative to the volatility of output in faces of uncertainty shocks. We then estimate this model by Bayesian estimation using Mexican data and show uncertainty shocks are also a main driving force of business cycles in emerging market economies, but through different propagation mechanisms.

16503017.label: Major findings and research outcome
16503017.value: Major Findings In the first working paper, we document difference in comovement of real exchange rates (RER) with other macroeconomic aggregates between emerging economies and developed small open economies, especially the significant and negative correlation between real interest rate and RER. To explain these features, we find that imperfect substitution between home and foreign tradable goods and the interaction of pecuniary effects of real exchange rate changes and collateral constraint on firms' borrowing are important. A model with these features does well in matching business cycle moments in emerging market economies, including those related to RER. Finally, our estimation results also identify country premium shock as the major force in driving RER dynamics and output fluctuations. In the second working paper, we find financial frictions amplify the impact of uncertainty on durable consumption more than the counterparts on GDP in emerging market economies. We develop a small open economy real business cycle model with banking sectors and durable goods to explain this finding. We show that when uncertainty is larger, the international lenders charge a higher risk premium and this leads to a higher real interest rate, which will affect households’ consumption of durable goods as well as investment. Bayesian estimation of this model using Mexican data shows that, like in developed countries, uncertainty shocks are also a main driving force of business cycles in emerging market economies, but through different propagation mechanisms. 16503017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16503017.value: I will keep working on the leverage ratio paper. I will also try to use other methods to solve the nonlinear DSGE model up to third order so as to estimate the uncertainty shocks using particle filter and Bayesian inference. This will help us to identify the contribution of first order and second order shocks in explaining business cycles in emerging market economies. Meanwhile, I will also extend the durable goods paper and see if the uncertainty shocks discussed in that paper can help to explain RER dynamics.

16503017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16503017.value: Real exchange rate is usually very persistent and volatile. What leads to the fluctuations in real exchange rate and how does the real exchange rate fluctuations affect the real side of the economy are important questions for policy makes as well as firms and households in the economy. In this project, we show that the real exchange rate is very volatile and negatively comoves with the real interest rate in emerging market economies. We also find when real exchange rate depreciates, the leverage ratio of firms increases. These facts are not observed in developed countries. This suggest that interaction of real exchange rate fluctuations and financial frictions in emerging market economies, especially the currency mismatch between income and foreign debt, may amplify the effect of country premium shocks on emerging market economies and lead to more volatile business cycles. We also show that financial frictions may amplify the impact of uncertainty shocks on emerging market economies through the channel of durable consumption. Therefore, like in developed countries, uncertainty shocks are also a main driving force of business cycles in emerging market economies, but through different propagation mechanisms.

16504017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16504017.value: The global financial crisis demonstrated that monetary policy and traditional regulation of banks and financial institutions are insufficient to prevent a build-up of systemic risk. Among policy-makers and academics there is a growing consensus that macroprudential policy should complement the existing policy frameworks of monetary supervisory authorities designed to address systemic risk. A key focus area for the new macroprudentual policies is the housing market because real estate and mortgages are the largest assets and liabilities on households' balance sheets. Some countries–for example, China, Hungary, Norway, Sweden and the United Kingdom–have recently adopted maximum loan-to-value (LTV) ratios on mortgages, referred to as LTV policy, as a macroprudential instrument to cool housing prices and reduce system risk in the financial sector. The LTV policy directly affects a household's ability to finance the purchase of real estate, as tighter (looser) LTV ratios require more (less) equity to finance a purchase. Whether such policies are effective in cooling housing prices depend on how important access to financing is for property prices. Accessing this question is difficult because such policies are hardly random, and are typically introduced when housing prices are booming. Separating the effect of the LTV policy from the counterfactual development in housing prices remains a challenge that existing literature has found difficult to solve. Hong Kong presents an interesting case for this ongoing discussion, as the tradition for an active LTV policy extends back to 1991. In November 1991, a maximum LTV ratio of 70% was adopted by the banking industry. The policy was later endorsed by the Commissioner of Banking as a prudential measure against overexposure to the property market. In 1997, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority introduced a 60% LTV ratio for properties priced above HKD 12 million. The maximum LTV ratios anchored on the value of the property have been adjusted multiple times in recent years. The differential LTV policy based on the level of property prices introduces a discontinuity, which the current project proposes to exploit to examine how effective regulation of LTV ratios is in cooling property prices. To this end, the project will deliver new insights that are relevant to policy-makers and market participants locally as well as globally. 全球金融危机表明，货币政策以及银行和金融机构的传统监管不足以阻止系统性风险的积累。越来越多的决策者和学者达成共识：宏观审慎政策应该作为中央银行和货币监管机构现有的政策框架的补充，旨在解决系统性风险。 新的宏观审慎政策的一个重点是房地产市场，因为房地产和抵押贷款是家庭资产负债表中最大的资产和负债。一些国家 - 例如中国，匈牙利，挪威，瑞典和英国最近已经采取了最大的按揭贷款（LTV）比率（简称LTV政策）作为一种宏观审慎手段来降低房价和减少金融部门的系统风险。 LTV政策直接影响到家庭融资购房的能力，因为更严格（更宽松）的LTV比率需要更多（少）的资产净值来融资。这些政策是否有效降低房价取决于获得融资对房地产价格的重要性。处理这个问题是困难的，因为这样的政策几乎不是随机的，它们通常是在房价激增时引入的。将LTV政策的影响与房价的反事实情况区分开来仍然是现有文献难以解决的挑战。 对于这个正在进行的讨论，香港提出了一个有趣的例子，因为活跃的LTV政策的传统可追溯到1991年。在1991年11月，银行业采用了最高的70％的LTV比率。该政策作为避免在房地产市场产生过多风险敞口的审慎措施，后来获得银行业理事认可。在一九九七年，香港金融管理局推出了针对价值超过一千二百万港元的物业百分之六十的LTV比率。根据物业价值来分层的最大LTV比率近年来已经多次调整。分层的LTV政策引入了不连续性，本项目旨在了解不连续的LTV比率政策在冷却房价时的有效性。为此，该项目将为本地和全球的决策者和市场参与者提供新的见解。

16504017.label: Realisation of objectives
16504017.value: The project has resulted in the working paper entitled "Loan-to-value limits and house prices?". All objectives have been achieved. The study finds that LTV policy is effective at cooling house prices. A 10 percent point reduction in the LTV ratio result in 8 percent lower house prices (Objective 1), and reduces transaction volume significantly (Objective 2). The effect is strong in the secondary housing market, and weaker due to subsidies by developers in the primary housing market (Objective 3). The policy is more effective when budget constraints of households are binding (Objective 4). The working paper has just been submitted for publication to a top finance journal.

16504017.label: Major findings and research outcome
16504017.value: The project evaluates the effect of loan-to-value (LTV) limits on house prices. The identification strategy exploits variation in LTV limits induced by Hong Kong Monetary Authorities’ decision to introduce differentiated LTV limits anchored on the value of the property, which allows us to identify the effect on LTV limits on house prices. We estimate that a one-percentage-point decrease in LTV limits reduces the house price growth by 0.8 percentage points. Overall, our results document that macro-prudential policies, which regulate access to financing, are an effective policy tool to control house price growth.

16504017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16504017.value: The findings from the project raises the question of how effective other macroprudential policies are in controlling house price growth, these include debt-to-income ratios and stamp duty for prospective buyers. The project offers a research design and methodological contribution that will be helpful for evaluating the effect of other macroprudential policies.

16504017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16504017.value: Hong Kong’s Monetary Authority (HKMA) is in charge of securing the stability of financial markets in Hong Kong. To do so, the HKMA has introduced so-called macroprudential policies to control house price growth and avoid systemic risk due to increasing house prices. The project evaluates the effectiveness of such policy tools, by estimating the effect of loan-to-value limits on house prices. They study finds that requiring higher down payments on real estate has a large effect on property prices. Increasing the down payment by 10% (i.e. allowing 10% less of mortgage financing) of the value of the property reduces property prices by 8%.

16504117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16504117.value: The proposal is to study the impact of accounting information in vertical integration. Although some relationships between suppliers and customers may be described as a series of spot transactions in a Walrasian market, many are better characterized as long-term relationships that lead parties to make non-transferable investments in each other. These ongoing relationships create substantial switching costs in the event that the other party suffers from economic distress (Cornell and Shapiro 1987; Bowen et al. 1995; Cachon and Lariviere 2001). Naturally, good financial reporting quality alleviates the information problem associated with supplier-customer transactions (Williamson, 1979; Bowen et al. 1995). For instance, contracts such as financial covenants can mitigate the possibility that managers may take advantage of information asymmetry to engage in moral hazard (Costello 2013). Unfortunately, these covenants effectively rely on transparent financial statements. This raises the question of what customers and suppliers can do when they benefit from prolonged relationships, but low reporting quality prevents them from using long-term contracts to protect their relationship-specific investments. One possibility is that the firm walks away from the relationship, but this may prove difficult if it has already sunk of lot of investment into it or if the counterpart offers a unique product. I hypothesize that, in this case, the firm buys its counterpart outright and vertically integrates. Vertical integration means better internal monitoring and information-sharing between the target and acquiring firms, once combined, effectively mitigates information concerns (Williamson 1971; Arrow 1975). Empirically, I propose to study whether firms with low financial reporting quality (restatements) are more likely to be acquired in a vertical integration than firms with high financial reporting quality. I also propose a series of cross-sectional tests to check whether the capacity of acquirers to absorb losses; the importance of target firms; and their degree of monitoring may affect the likelihood of vertical integrations. To better understand the theory, I also studies the consequences of acquisitions in terms of synergies created, the acquirer’s implied price volatility and operational volatility. This project has important academic and practical value. Academically, the proposal improves understanding of the contractual relationship in the supply chain. It also extends the vertical integration literature to accounting and shows that firms vertically integrate to overcome financial statement opacity in their counterparts. Practically, my project provides insights for: (i) regulators on implications of the product market for financial reporting regulations; and (ii) investors regarding assessing the synergies of vertical integrations. 該項目是研究會計信息對垂直整合的影響。雖然供應商和客戶之間的一些關係可能被描述為市場上的一系列現貨交易，但許多是長期關係，導致各方之間進行不可轉讓的投資。如果另一方遭受經濟困境，這些正在進行的關係創造了巨大的轉換成本。良好的財務報告質量可以緩解供應和商客戶交易相關的信息問題。例如，諸如金融契約之類的合同可以減輕管理人員利用信息不對稱來參與道德風險的可能性。不幸的是，這些契約依靠透明的財務報表，低報告質量阻止他們使用長期合同來保護他們的關係特定投資。一個可能性是公司離開和客戶之間的關係，但是如果它已經投資很多，或者對方提供了獨特的產品，這可能是困難的。我假設，在這種情況下，該公司直接購買其對應方並垂直整合。垂直整合意味著更好的內部監控目標公司與收購公司之間的信息共享，一旦結合起來，就有效地緩解了信息問題。我建議研究財務報告質量較低的企業是否更有可能垂直整合。我還提出了一系列測試，檢查收購方吸收損失的能力;目標公司的重要性; 其監測程度可能會影響垂直整合的可能性。為了更好地理解這一理論，我還研究併購產生的後果，即收購者隱含的價格波動和經營波動。該項目具有重要的學術和實踐價值。在學術上，這個建議提高了對供應鏈合同關係的了解。它還將垂直整合文獻擴展到會計，並顯示企業垂直整合，以克服對方的財務報表不透明度。實踐上，我的項目提供以下知識：（i）監管機構對產品市場對財務報告規定的影響 和（ii）投資者評估垂直整合的協同效應。

16504217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16504217.value: Labor economists have found that in the US, the relative share of routine jobs declined dramatically due to computers and/or outsourcing. Because these jobs tended to be middle-skill jobs, this decline contributed to wage polarization by hollowing out the middle of the wage distribution. Due to lack of data, no similar analysis has been conducted in a systematic way for China despite the fact that inequality has reached very high levels (Gini coefficient of 0.53). Descriptive evidence suggests that unlike the US, in China the share of middle-skill occupations actually increased significantly over the past 15 years, drawing into question the pervasive narrative of technology increasing wage inequality. The proposed project is the first to analyze the demand for job tasks in China using new survey data from a broadly representative sample of urban workers. The module on job tasks is comparable to that used recently in other countries. We use regional variation in job tasks within China and variation in job tasks across countries around the world to assess the extent to which structural change, globalization, technological change, and the supply of skills determine the assignment of workers to tasks and the demand for workers with different levels of education. Other research by the PI and a Co-I suggests that global production chains may be facilitating the insourcing of routine tasks into China. Understanding this question is of fundamental importance for understanding the causes of inequality in China and globally. In addition, we develop a methodology for predicting the task content of occupations in regions or time periods for which direct survey data are not available, which has the potential for significantly improving upon the existing practice of using US occupational benchmarks. We apply this method to Chinese census and urban household survey data for different years to generate more precise estimates of how the demand for tasks has changed over time in China. The results of this analysis promise to bring fresh insights about the sources of income inequality in China, and also about the relative importance of different driving forces in shaping patterns of inequality globally. 勞動經濟學家發現在美國，電腦的普及和（或者）生產外包使重複性工作的相對占比急劇下降。因為這些工作普遍是中等技能的工作，在工資的分佈中，中間部分的工作消失導致了工資的極化。儘管中國有非常高的不平等水平（中國的基尼系數是0.53），但由於缺乏數據，中國缺乏相類似的研究。描述性的證據表明，不像美國，中國的中等技能工作的勞動佔比在過去十五年裡有顯著增長。這一證據使我們質疑“技術帶來工資不平等”的論述。 本研究計劃是第一個使用嶄新且具代表性的中國城市勞動力調查數據來分析中國對不同工作任務需求的研究。調查中關於工作任務的部分可和其他國家的調查比較。我們使用中國國內工作任務的差異和世界其他國家工作任務的差異，來探究下面因素在什麼程度上決定勞動力的任務安排和對不同技能水平的勞動力的需求：結構性變遷，全球化，技術變化，和勞動力的技能供給。 PI和一位CO-I的其他研究表明，國際生產鏈可能加速了其他國家將重複性任務外包到中國的過程。研究這一問題對理解當今中國和世界不平等的根本原因具有關鍵的意義。另外，我們開發了一種預測在不同地區和不同時間內不同職位的任務內容的方法。由於預測的數據是現有調查數據不存在的，這可以改善現在以美國職位信息作為基準的做法。我們將這一方法應用到不同年份的中國人口普查和城市家庭調查數據，以更準確地估計中國對各種任務需求的變化。本研究的結果將會更新我們對中國不平等源頭的認識。同時，本研究的結果也會讓我們了解影響全球不平等的不同因素的重要性。

16504217.label: Realisation of objectives
16504217.value: The project has fulfilled each of the research objectives. Research results on the first two objectives are presented in the paper “Technology, Skills, and Globalization: Explaining International Differences in Routine and Nonroutine Work Using Survey Data” which is now a revised submission to the World Bank Economic Review, which we expect to be accepted soon. Research on the third objective is presented in a second paper titled “Global Divergence in the Deroutinization of Jobs” that was recently rejected by American Economic Review Insights (which we are revising before submitting to another journal soon). Research for the project has focused on international comparisons rather than narrowly on China, as we discovered that there is enormous interest in understanding cross-country differences in the nature of work, and China’s differences with the US and other countries fits a similar pattern as other countries. We have also completed more in-depth analysis of the determinants of job tasks in China and plan to complete a third paper that is more China-focused. The shift from routine work to non-routine cognitive work is a key feature of labor markets globally, but there is little evidence on the extent to which tasks differs among workers performing the same jobs in different countries. The main contribution of our research is that we analyze newly constructed survey-based measures of routine task intensity (RTI) of jobs for workers in 47 countries. Due to data limitations, previous cross-country comparisons have generally assumed that the task content of specific occupations is the same in other countries as in the US. Realizing the first objective, analysis in the first paper confirms that cross-country differences in the content of work within the same occupations are sizable. On average, workers in more developed economies perform less routine-intensive work. The relationship between routine task intensity and country GDP per capita differs quite markedly for different occupation groups. In high-skilled occupations (e.g., managers, professionals), there is a sharp negative gradient of RTI with respect to GDP per capita. However, for middle-skilled occupations like clerical workers, and low-skilled occupations like plant and machine operators and assemblers, we find a flat or inverse-U shaped relationship between RTI and GDP per capita. Our assessment of the second objective follows the originally proposed methodology closely. We start with a regression in which workers’ routine task intensity is regressed on individual, sector, and country-level variables. In our main specification, technology is captured by country-sector computer use, globalization is measured by the foreign share of value added in the country-sector and FDI share of GDP plus these shares interacted with GDP per capita, and structural differences are captured by 18 sector fixed effects and GDP per capita. Skills are captured by individual education, demographics (age, sex), and a direct test of literacy proficiency. We estimate a pooled regression for all workers, and separate task regressions for workers in high-skilled occupations (managers, professionals and technicians), middle-skilled occupations (clerks, sales and services workers) and low-skilled occupations (craft and related trades workers, plant and machine operators and assemblers, elementary occupations). We decided that it was more natural to categorize workers by occupation groups rather than education levels to capture differences in skill levels, but we note that occupation groups map perfectly with differences in average education levels. Using the coefficients from these regressions, we decompose the cross-country variance in mean routine task intensity across countries, as well as the difference between countries at different development levels and the US, into the contributions associated with each fundamental factor. We find that technology, the supply of skills, and globalization are all strongly associated with cross-country differences in RTI. International differences in technology are most important, especially in accounting for cross-country variation in RTI in high-skilled occupations, consistent with complementarity between non-routine tasks and technology. Globalization contributes more to cross-country differences in RTI among workers in middle- and low-skilled occupations compared to high-skill occupations. We also find that the supply of skills contributes to the cross-country differences in tasks mainly through its association with the employment shares of high-, middle-, and low-skilled occupations. Moreover, in low- and middle-income countries, lower supply of skills accounts for a large share of the difference in RTI compared to the US. We provide evidence that it in the poorer countries the skills gap predicts not only lower employment shares of high-skilled occupations but also more routine-intensive tasks performed by workers in high-skill occupations. Finally, we show that differences in occupational structure across countries account for a relatively small share of cross-country differences in task content, highlighting the importance of using comparable survey data to accurately estimate the extent of cross-country differences in task content. To address the third objective, in the second paper, we combine survey data and regression models to predict the country-specific routine-task intensity of occupations in 87 countries employing over 2.5 billion workers. We use regression estimates to predict the task content of different occupations in countries with different levels of technology, globalization, skills, and economic structure. We then apply these estimates to data on occupational structures and environmental factors for different countries and years to predict job tasks of specific occupations, even when survey data on task content is not available. Analyzing these predicted task measures at the country-occupation-year level, we establish new stylised facts about the global evolution of routine and non-routine work. We find that from 2000 to 2017, the shift away from routine work was much slower in low- and middle-income countries than in high-income countries, widening gaps in the nature of work. Not accounting for differences in occupation-specific job tasks across countries leads to significant overestimation of the role of non-routine tasks in less developed countries. Both papers have been presented at major international conferences and venues. The first paper was presented by the PI and Co-I Lewandowski at the Jobs and Development Conference 2018 in Bogotá, IZA World Labor Conference 2018 in Berlin, ASSA / AEA Annual Meeting 2019 in Atlanta, TASKS V conference 2019 in Bonn, Jobs and Development Conference 2019 in Washington DC, WIDER Development Conference 2019 in Bangkok, European Association of Labour Economists (EALE) annual conference 2019 in Uppsala, and 19th Conference on the Economics of Information and Communication Technologies, online, 2021. The paper’s results were also presented at seminars at the World Bank Research Department, HKUST, UCSD, Princeton University, and MIT. The second paper was presented at the 1st LISER/IAB Conference on Digital Transformation and the Future of Work in Luxembourg, 2020, the EALE-SOLE-AASLE 2020 annual conference (online), the Jobs and Development Conference 2020 (online), and the International Economic Association Online World Congress, 2021. The One sign of the research’s impact is that our method to predict the task content of occupations in specific countries is being utilized for a study sponsored by the United Nations University World Institute for Development Economics Research of task content and inequality globally. The study will produce an edited volume that will include a methodology chapter by the PI and Co-I Lewandowski, as well as country case studies from around the world that use our predicted task content estimates and country-specific occupation and income data to better understand how the changing nature of work is affecting inequality.

16504217.label: Major findings and research outcome
16504217.value: Using survey data for the first time to systematically document cross-country differences in the content of work, we find that the task content of work varies considerably even within the same occupations. Not surprisingly, workers in the more developed economies perform less routine-intensive work. However, the relationship between routine task intensity and country GDP per capita differs quite markedly for different occupation groups. In high-skilled occupations (e.g., managers, professionals), there is a sharp gradient with respect to GDP per capita, with work being more routine-intensive in poorer countries. However, for middle-skilled occupations like clerical workers, and low-skilled occupations like plant and machine operators and assemblers, we find a flat or an inverse-U shaped relationship between the relative routine-intensity of tasks and a country’s level of development. Analyzing the determinants of cross-country differences in routine task intensity (RTI), we find that technology, the supply of skills, and globalization are all strongly associated with cross-country differences in relative routine task intensity (RTI). International differences in technology are most important, especially in accounting for cross-country variation in RTI in high-skilled occupations, consistent with complementarity between non-routine tasks and technology. Globalization contributes more to cross-country differences in RTI among workers in middle- and low-skilled occupations compared to high-skill occupations, in line with the view that offshoring enables countries to specialize, within industries, according to their abundant factors. We also find that the supply of skills contributes to the cross-country differences in tasks mainly through its association with the employment shares of high-, middle-, and low-skilled occupations. Finally, we show that differences in occupational structure across countries account for a relatively small share of cross-country differences in task content. Analyzing predicted task content at the country-occupation-year level for most of the worlds workers based on cross-country regression estimates, we establish new stylised facts about the global evolution of routine and non-routine work, relaxing the common assumption that occupations are identical globally. We find that from 2000 to 2017, the shift away from routine work was much slower in low- and middle-income countries than in high-income countries, widening gaps in the nature of work. Not accounting for differences in occupation-specific job tasks across countries leads to significant overestimation of the role of non-routine tasks in less developed countries.

16504217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16504217.value: A third paper that focuses on China is in progress and should be completed in the next several months. The project first utilizes results from completed cross-country analysis to describe differences in the relative routine task intensity (RTI) of work in China and the US, as well as with other countries at different stages of economic development. Next it relaxes the assumption that one regression can explain the variation in task content for all workers in the world by estimating separate task regressions for China. This enables an assessment of whether technology, globalization, skills, and structure affect tasks differently in China than in other parts of the world. Part of the analysis also examines regional differences in task content within China. Another topic ripe for additional analysis is to study how differences and changes in task content can explain patterns of inequality both within and across countries, and over time, by studying the relationship between wage inequality and variation in task content. The PI and Co-I Lewandowski hope to next make progress on this important topic.

16504217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16504217.value: In this project, we analyze newly constructed survey-based measures of routine task intensity (RTI) of jobs for workers in 47 countries. We present new evidence on the global differences in job tasks, and their associations with four fundamental forces: technology, globalization, supply of skills, and structural change. Regression estimates also make it possible to predict the task content of occupations in countries and years for which survey data are not available, allowing us to describe the evolution of job tasks globally over time. We find that RTI varies considerably across countries even within the same occupation. In high-skilled occupations, RTI is negatively related to a country’s GDP per capita but there is no systematic relationship for middle and low-skill occupations. Technology differences (measured by computer use) are the most important factor explaining differences in RTI across countries, especially for high-skilled occupations, consistent with complementarity between non-routine tasks and technology. Globalization matters more for middle- and low-skilled occupations compared to high-skill occupations, and skills explain a large share of the gap between low-income and advanced countries. We find that from 2000 to 2017, the shift away from routine work was much slower in low- and middle-income countries than in high-income countries.

16504317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16504317.value: What is the optimal monetary policy for a committed central bank if the private sector is skeptical about the central bank’s ability to commit? This project is to answer this question in an economy with the following features: (1) the private sector entertains the possibility that the central bank is either a type that always carries out its promised inflation plans or a type that can deviate from the inflation plans; (2) the private sector is aware that actual inflation may deviate from the promised inflation plan due to shocks that are uncontrollable by the central bank; (3) the private sector is updating its belief about the central bank’s type after observing actual inflation each period; (4) the private sector understands that if the central bank is the type that can deviate from the inflation plan, it decides when and how much to deviate from the plan in an optimal way. 如果私營部門懷疑中央銀行的承諾能力, 中央銀行的最優貨幣政策是什麼？這個項目在具備以下特徵的經濟體裡研究這個問題：（1）私營部門認為可能有兩類中央銀行，一類會履行承諾的通貨膨脹計劃，另一類則會偏離計劃; （2）私營部門意識到實際通貨膨脹有時會因為中央銀行不可控的原因偏離承諾的計劃; （3）私營部門在每期觀察實際通貨膨脹後，會更新對現任央行是否會履行未來承諾的信心; （4）私營部門明白，如果央行是可以偏離承諾的類型，它會選擇最佳的時間和最佳的偏離程度。

16504317.value: 1. We found an efficient way to handle the high-dimensional expectation function and utilized it to identify the incentive compatible set, which allows us to obtain the solution to the optimization problem in a reasonable speed. 2. We investigated how the equilibrium policies change with the reputation (the private sector's belief about the central bank's type), with the standard deviation of the implementation error, with the cost-push shock, and with the implementation error. Moreover, we also investigated how key assumptions of the model affect the equilibrium, including the comparison between models with and without the opportunistic type being strategic, and the comparison between models with and without the private sector's learning. 3. In this paper, we learnt that having a strategic opportunistic type introduces a nonlinear effect of reputation on the optimal committed policy. We think this lesson can be applied to understand how the credit rating responds to the issuance of new sovereign debt by emerging economies. I am working with a PhD student now on developing this idea. 4. This paper has been accepted in various prestigious conferences and workshops, including but not limited to: 2019 China International Conference in Macroeconomics (CICM) 2019 Credibility Conference hosted by LAEF at UC, Santa Barbara 2020 World Congress of the Econometric Society We have been working hard recently to get the paper ready for submission to a top economic journal.

16504317.label: Major findings and research outcome
16504317.value: We study the optimal monetary policy in a setting where the private sector is forward-looking and learning about the type of central bank in place. We consider two types of central bank, one patient type that can commit and one opportunistic type that is myopic and cannot commit. Being able to commit or not, the central bank in place chooses inflation policies optimally, taking into account the learning and rational expectation of the private sector. We show that the equilibrium can be obtained as a solution to a recursive optimization of the committed type in which the actions of the opportunistic type are subject to an incentive compatibility constraint. The numerical solution to a calibrated model reveals that the committed central bank with good initial reputation adopts policies similar to the standard solution under full commitment, whereas the committed central bank with poor initial reputation aims at building reputation with anti-inflation policies that involve real costs. If the opportunistic central bank with good initial reputation is in place, there will be lengthy real stimulation with gradually rising actual and expected inflation, followed by stagflation when the history of positive inflation surprises depletes the central bank's reputation.

16504317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16504317.value: There are two routes for future development of the research: 1. to apply this reputation game modeling in other context, such as sovereign debt and default, or macroprudential policies. 2. to extend the model by allowing the opportunistic type to be patient.

16504317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16504317.value: Public trust in how likely the promised policy will be carried is crucial in determining the effectiveness of the policy. The current research project proposes a method to design optimal policy when the public does not completely trust the policymaker's promises, and shows when and how to gain the public trust with policy design and implementation. The current research project also helps to assess and forecast the effects of policy when the policymaker is facing a decline in public trust.

16504817.label: Project Objectives
16504817.value: Test the prediction that consumers feel differently when they buy a counterfeit compared to when they use a counterfeit. Specifically, we hypothesize that purchasing a counterfeit elicits positive emotions, whereas using a counterfeit elicits both positive and negative emotions. Test the prediction that counterfeit users feel more mixed during public versus private consumption. In turn, using counterfeits in public has a greater impact on the appeal of both counterfeit and genuine products compared to using counterfeits in private. Specifically, compared to private counterfeit consumption, public counterfeit consumption should be more likely to reduce the appeal of counterfeit products and increase the appeal of genuine products. Test the prediction that the mixed emotions elicited by counterfeit consumption differ among consumers who are high versus low in the motive to signal social status through brands (hereafter referred to as high signalers and low signalers, respectively). Prior research suggests that high signalers are more likely to buy counterfeit products in the first place (Wilcox et al. 2009). We aim to replicate this finding and extend it by demonstrating that these high signalers also are most likely to experience mixed emotions while using counterfeits and, consequently, are more likely to subsequently devalue counterfeit products in favor of genuine products. Test the prediction that Asian counterfeit users feel more mixed than Western counterfeit users. In turn, and all else being equal, using counterfeits in an Asian society (e.g., Hong Kong) should be more likely to reduce the appeal of counterfeit products and increase the appeal of genuine products compared to using a counterfeit in a Western society (e.g., the United States). Craft anti-counterfeiting campaigns that differ in the extent to which they activate social judgment concerns, and compare the relative effectiveness of these campaigns. Our theory predicts that campaigns that activate social judgment concerns most effectively reduce the appeal of counterfeit consumption.

Test the prediction that the mixed emotions elicited by counterfeit consumption differ among consumers who are high versus low in the motive to signal social status through brands (hereafter referred to as high signalers and low signalers, respectively). Prior research suggests that high signalers are more likely to buy counterfeit products in the first place (Wilcox et al. 2009). We aim to replicate this finding and extend it by demonstrating that these high signalers also are most likely to experience mixed emotions while using counterfeits and, consequently, are more likely to subsequently devalue counterfeit products in favor of genuine products.

Test the prediction that Asian counterfeit users feel more mixed than Western counterfeit users. In turn, and all else being equal, using counterfeits in an Asian society (e.g., Hong Kong) should be more likely to reduce the appeal of counterfeit products and increase the appeal of genuine products compared to using a counterfeit in a Western society (e.g., the United States).

Craft anti-counterfeiting campaigns that differ in the extent to which they activate social judgment concerns, and compare the relative effectiveness of these campaigns. Our theory predicts that campaigns that activate social judgment concerns most effectively reduce the appeal of counterfeit consumption.

16504817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16504817.value: 是此研究對於探討假貨消費的文獻有幫助，主要研究範圍包括 (1) 消費者在使用假貨時的感受、(2) 這些感受在不同的情況、個人以及文化上有何變化、(3) 這些感受對於假貨和真貨的吸引力有何影響，以及(4) 如何利用這些感受去計劃抑制使用假貨的需求的活動。 我們的理論假設導致消費者購買假貨的不同因素，特別是由於想對別人展示社會地位的動力 (Wilcox et al., 2009)，而在使用假貨時引起複雜的情緒。引起複雜的情緒主要是因為同時感受到正面及反面的情緒。我們主要的見解是，當社會評價是重要時，使用假貨的人會較為容易有複雜的感受。也就是說，當使用假貨的人看重別人對他們的看法時，他們同時感受到來源於品牌地位的價值所引起的正面情緒，以及來源於一旦被發現使用假貨而受到的社會評價所帶來的負面情緒。 這個見解對假貨消費在何時能引起複雜的情緒有一定意義。具體而言，它展示了複雜的情緒視乎情景、個人、文化上的不同因素所引起人際關係評價的重要性而定。我們建議仔細檢查這三個因素以測試我們的理論。第一個因素是公開以及私人使用的情況。如果複雜的情緒是因為人際關係評價的原因所引起的，那麼跟暗地使用假貨的私人情況比起來，在公開使用假貨的情況下，複雜的情緒應該更為明顯。 第二個決定使用假貨是否會引起複雜情緒的因素是消費者透過品牌去標示社會地位的動力。喜歡透過品牌去標示地位的消費者會因假貨的潛在價值感受到較強的正面情緒，反之亦然。但是，因為他們會較為關心所表達的價值會如何被解讀，他們也會感受到與害怕他人批評的有關的較強的負面情緒。 第三、我們預測不同文化背景的假貨使用者會有不同複雜感受的傾向。相比西方人來說，亞洲人普遍來說會較有動力去展示社會地位 (Wong & Ahuvia, 1998) 以及較為關心社會評價 (Lalwani et al. 2006)。這些因素加起來會導致亞洲人在使用假貨時有較為複雜的情緒。 複雜情緒會進一步影響假貨以及真貨的吸引力。複雜情緒會造成令人嫌惡的心理衝突，消費者應會盡量避免(Larsen et al., 2001)。因此，複雜情緒會減低購買假貨的意願，以及抑制未來購買假貨的意圖。複雜情緒也會增加與其無關的真貨的吸引力。 最後，這些複雜情緒的性質，建基於人際關係的評價上，暗示了最為有效減少購買假貨的市場營銷策略。現存策略通常注重增加假貨的意識以及訓練消費者看出假貨。但是，我們假設，一個策略有效與否，在於它能否引起對於人際之間的評價的注重，特別是能否令人在使用之前先考慮社會評價。這就是我們所建議在這裡測試的。

16504917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16504917.value: In a well-functioning financial market, asset prices reflect available information about future payoffs and this informational efficiency guide investment activities to achieve allocational efficiency. A well-functioning financial market also requires that insider trading is restricted and information disclosure is mandated, so that information held by entrepreneurs and insiders are fairly disclosed to outside investors. In practice, insider trading cases are difficult to prosecute due to the difficulty to collect evidence and disclosure requirements are complicated by the need to protect business secrets. As a result, financial economists lack proper measures to judge firms on how they behave in curbing insider trading and dealing with information disclosure. The goal of this project is to make some headway towards establishing such measures. It aims to establish that there are differences in the disclosure related strategies and outcomes for a large cross-section of firms, using the evidence gathered from the diffusive volatility and jump intensity around corporate event dates. The results of the project can be further developed in applications in investment, asset pricing, and accounting areas, in both academic and practical research. 在一个运作良好的金融市场，资产价格反映了未来收益的信息。 这个信息有效性指导投资活动从而实现分配有效性。 一个运作良好的金融市场也要求限制内幕交易并执行信息披露，使得企业家和内部人士的信息公平地披露给外部投资者。 但在实际上，内幕交易由于取证困难而难以立案，信息披露和保护商业秘密很难两全。 因此，金融经济学家至今缺乏对企业遏制内幕交易和处理信息披露的合适的度量。 这个项目的目标是为建立这样的度量取得进展。 从企业大事件期间的扩散波幅和跳跃强度的关系中找出企业在信息披露和遏制内幕交易上的差别。该项目的结果可以在投资学，资产定价理论和会计学的学术研究和实际应用中得到进一步发展。

16504917.label: Realisation of objectives
16504917.value: I managed to complete a paper with coauthors who are current and former students of mine. In the paper we use nonparametric methods to decompose returns on a large cross-section of individual stocks into jumps and diffusive components. In the paper, we address a few issues related to jumps and diffusive variance. First, as the evidence on the phenomenon is mainly obtained on stock indexes and just a handful of large stocks, whether such division between jumps and diffusive variance is necessary for all stocks is unclear. Whether individual stocks exhibit the same pattern as stock indexes is not clear either. As such, our first step is to modify methodologies groomed for indexes to be applied to all individual stocks in order to measure jumps and diffusive variance. Upon completing that, we gauge the extent to which jump intensity, jump size, and diffusive volatility are stochastic. Second, we examine the assumption made in the options pricing literature that jump intensity and the diffusive variance are positively related over time for a given underlying asset. In the development of options pricing models, stochastic diffusive variance represents a major breakthrough after the Black-Scholes model of options pricing with constant variance. It has been treated as the most important state variable in determining options prices, besides the underlying asset price. When jumps are added later to the model, and when the jump intensity is found necessary to be time-varying, it is very natural to specify the conditional jump intensity as an increasing function of the diffusive variance of the underlying asset. In popular affine jump-diffusion models, for example, the conditional jump intensity is specified as an affine function of the diffusive variance of the underlying asset with a positive slope coefficient (in non-trivial cases). It seems natural to think that the probability of a jump is high when the diffusive variance is also high. After all, both diffusive variance and jump intensity are measures of the magnitude of possible future price changes. In affine models encompassed in Duffie, Pan and Singleton (2000), the conditional jump intensity is an affine function of conditional diffusive variance of the return, which may be extended to include other state variables. Since the variance is unbounded from above and the intensity is positive, a positive slope coefficient is the only choice. As such, the assumption of positive relation between jump intensity and diffusive variance arises more from a technical viewpoint, rather than from economic rationale. The empirical evidence in Li and Zhang (2016) based on the S&P 500 index and a handful of large stocks, however, casts doubt on the assumption of a positive correlation between the two characteristics of the stock returns. We extend the inquiry to all stocks traded in the major US exchanges. Third, based on the findings of the first two issues, we address how options pricing depends on the covariation between the conditional jump intensity and diffusive variance, controlling for the diffusive variance, jump size, and volatility of volatility. This line of empirical examination has not been conducted explicitly in the literature, even for index options. We collect evidence from a large panel of options on individual stocks. The result can provide guidance on how to model option prices. We conduct our analyses on two data sets. One is for all stocks listed on major US stock exchanges from 1962 to 2019. The other is for stocks on which options are traded and options data are available from 1996 to 2019. The latter is a subset of the former in terms of both time-series observations and cross-sectional coverage. We dub the former as the stocks sample and the latter as the options sample. With the stocks sample, we apply a semi-nonparametric approach to daily stock returns for each firm, estimate the conditional diffusive variance, and detect jumps. Intuitively, a daily return whose magnitude is too large compared to the conditional diffusive variance is identified as a jump. We then construct a firm-quarter panel data sample of realized jump intensity, realized average jump size, and realized diffusive variance for a firm during a year between 1962 and 2019. Using this panel, we document the statistical properties of jump intensity, jump size, and diffusive variance. We also examine how jump intensity, jump size, and diffusive variance vary with macroeconomic conditions and find that both jump size and diffusive variance increase during recessions, but jump intensity does not vary with macroeconomic conditions. The principal component analysis suggests that jump intensity and jump size of negative jumps exhibit more commonality than those of positive jumps. We also find that the variations of negative diffusive returns comove more than those of the positive diffusive returns. We then investigate the relations among jump intensity, jump size, and diffusive variance. In the regressions of realized jump intensity on diffusive variance firm by firm, the slope coefficients (i.e., the jump-diffusion beta) tend to be more negative than positive, with a large amount of them being insignificantly different from zero. This is consistent with Li and Zhang (2016) for the case of the S&P index and a handful of large stocks. Using the options sample, we examine how the jump-diffusion beta affects options pricing. We choose implied volatility smile as the main characteristics of options prices. We view the jump-diffusion beta at the end of each quarter estimated with the past twelve quarters as a state variable/firm-specific characteristic and examine how implied volatility smile depends on jump-diffusion beta, among others. The result shows that implied volatility smile positively depends on jump-diffusion beta controlling for the diffusive variance, jump size, and volatility of volatility. We also show that the restriction of a non-negative relation between jump intensity and diffusive volatility imposed in the popular affine jump-diffusion option pricing models introduces biases to options pricing. If the jump intensity-diffusive volatility relation is negative, the models with affine jump intensity under (over) estimate the curvature of the implied volatility function when the diffusive volatility is low (high). These results provide valuable guidance on how options pricing models should be designed. We also address the issue of how diffusive variance, jump intensity, jump size and the jump-to-diffusive variance ratio are related to standard firm characteristics such as firm size, book-to-market ratio, leverage ratio, profitability, tangible investment, R&D, and information related characteristics such as analyst coverage, institutional holding, and disclosure frequency. The diffusive variance, which is the main part of the total variance, depends on these characteristics in usual, understandable ways. For example, diffusive variance is positively related to leverage, tangible investment and R&D, and negatively related to firm size, book-to-market ratio, profitability, analyst coverage and institution. Jump intensity is found to be positively related to book-to-market ratio, leverage and profitability, and negatively related to firm size, tangible investment, R&D and all information related special characteristics. Jump size has the same relation as jump intensity with most firm characteristics, with the exception of book-to-market ratio, tangible investment and R&D. The jump-to-diffusive variance ratio, which intrigues this project, is found positively related to profitability and negatively related to size, tangible investment, R&D and disclosure frequency. Its relation with other characteristics appears indeterminate.

16504917.label: Major findings and research outcome
16504917.value: I finished a working paper coauthored with a former Ph.D student, Li Gang, and a current Ph.D student, Li Ruicong, titled “Jumps and Diffusive Variance: A Granular Analysis of Individual Stock Returns.” The analysis in the paper contributes to the options pricing literature in the following sense. First, how jumps are useful in options pricing for individual stocks has never been thoroughly investigated. Our paper is the first to analyze the usefulness of jumps for options pricing for all individual stocks during 1996-2019. Second, the sign of jump-diffusion beta has been an issue for options pricing modeling. The limited evidence on the S&P 500 index and a handful of large stocks casts doubt on the assumption of positivity of jump-diffusion beta. The results in the paper provide further evidence against such an assumption based on all individual stocks. Third, the effect of jump-diffusion beta on options pricing has never been examined in the literature, not even for options written on the S&P 500 index. The results of this paper on all stocks with options fill a gap and provide a starting point for further analysis. The paper is currently under review by a journal. The paper is available from SSRN and at https://chu-zhang.github.io/JDV.pdf. I finished a working paper with a current Ph.D student Li Ruicong, tentatively titled “The jump-diffusive volatility ratio and firm characteristics” in which we address the issue of what firm characteristics determine the jump-diffusive volatility ratio. The identified determinants to jump variance and diffusive variance individually make sense for all firm characteristics. The identified determinants to jump-diffusive variance ratio, however, require further investigation for some firm characteristics. The paper is being polished before being sent to conferences and journals. The project also supported the work by the Ph.D student, Li Ruicong, whose dissertation is titled “Asymmetric News Repetition and the Cross-section of Stock Returns.” The work is related to corporate events and information disclosure, but is single-authored by the student as required by the Ph.D program of the department. The student is set to graduate at the end of the spring semester in 2021.

16504917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16504917.value: The direction in the second objective can be pursued further. Among certain firm characteristics such as analyst coverage, institutional holding, corporate governance score, and disclosure frequency, some are determined by outside investors and others are determined by firm managers. These variables are quite positively correlated, however. This correlation hinders interpretations of the discovered statistical relationships. It is difficult to attribute a high jump-diffusive variance ratio to firm's disclosure policy or to outside investors' price discovery activities. Their interaction also requires further analysis. I am not aware of similar research plans by other researchers, so it is likely that I will follow it through before others getting into the same area. To reduce the potential competition, I have not widely circulated the draft of the second paper.

16504917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16504917.value: Diffusive variations and jumps are different ways stock prices react to new information regarding the present value of future cash flows of the firms. Firms that have wide analyst coverage, institutional holding and frequent disclosure tend to have large diffusive variation relatively to jumps in returns, as information about future cash flows come to the market frequently in small amounts. Firms that are less followed by analysts and institutions and firms that rarely disclose information (to prevent imitation by competitors) tend to have jumps in their stock returns. The jump-to-diffusive variance ratio is an important and easily available firm characteristic. Its feature is useful in portfolio management and options pricing, as well as in other investment decisions and corporate decision. This important firm characteristic has not been studied in the existing literature. The current study fills a void and potentially will attract further attentions from other researchers.

16505017.value: 短视投资者与公司信息披露行为：来自法国的证据

16505017.label: Project Objectives
16505017.value: Identify the role of investors' horizon in explaining corporate disclosure strategies Evaluate the extent and the direction to which the horizon of investors matter for the provision of voluntary disclosure Participate to the worldwide debate on the causes and consequences of managers' short termism.

16505017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16505017.value: There is a vivid debate around the world regarding the negative impact of short-termism on how managers run their companies. That is, managers respond to the pressure by investors to deliver short term performance through choices (i.e., reduced investment or R&D expenses) that are detrimental for firms’ long-term value. Practitioners have blamed the issuance of quarterly earnings guidance as a reinforcing tools that constrain managers to immediately deliver the level of earnings they just forecasted. For example, in January 2016, Larry Fink, CEO of BlackRock (the world’s biggest fund), sent a letter to the CEOs of all the S&P500 companies and large European corporations. In that letter, he explicitly urged managers to stop providing earnings guidance by stating: “Over time, as companies do a better job laying out their long-term growth frameworks, the need diminishes for quarterly EPS guidance, and we would urge companies to move away from providing it. Today’s culture of quarterly earnings hysteria is totally contrary to the long-term approach we need. To be clear, we do believe companies should still report quarterly results – “long-termism” should not be a substitute for transparency – but CEOs should be more focused in these reports on demonstrating progress against their strategic plans than a one-penny deviation from their EPS targets or analyst consensus estimates.” This project investigates how investors’ horizon affect managers’ corporate disclosure choices. That is, I ask the question: do managers issue short term earnings guidance in response to investors demand for short term expectations? This question is difficult to answer because a naïve look at the disclosure behavior of companies relative to the composition of their investor base is subject to many statistical shortcomings (such as endogeneity issues). To bypass these concerns, I use a change in law that occurred in France in 2014, called “Loi Florange” that affected only a subset of French listed firms and changed voting rights to double voting rights if shares were held for at least three years. As such, this change in regulation constitutes a shift in the horizon of investors whose ability to influence firms’ policies now depends on holding shares for a longer time period. I am interested in using this particularly well-suited setting to investigate whether a change in investors’ horizon lead to a change in corporate disclosure strategies. 投资者短视行为是否会给管理者的公司经营带来负面影响？该问题引发了广泛讨论。支持者认为，当管理者面临来自于投资者的压力时，他们倾向于采取牺牲企业长期利益的策略来换取短期收益，例如通过减少投资和企业研发支出以提高短期利润。而公司频繁的盈余预测披露（如季度盈余预测披露）则进一步增加管理者的短期业绩压力，促使他们采取短视行为以提高短期利润来实现或超过自愿披露的盈余预测。 举例而言，黑石集团的首席执行官Larry Fink在一封致美国标普500家上市公司和欧洲大型企业的信中呼吁管理者们停止发布盈余预测自愿性披露。他在信中说道， “就目前而言，公司越来越注重长期发展。管理者应该停止发布季度盈余预测，因为频繁披露季度盈余预测与公司注重长期发展的经营策略是背道而驰的。当然，公司仍然应该发布季度经营报告，企业在注重长期发展的同时也应该维持和提高企业透明度。但是，首席执行官们在这些经营报告中应该着重强调和分析公司的经营环境与经营策略，而非强调他们是否实现盈余目标或者分析师的盈余预测”。 本项目旨在研究投资者视角如何影响企业的信息披露行为。具体而言，当投资者更关注短期业绩时，企业管理者是否会更加频繁地发布短期业绩预测？在研究过程中，这两者的关系往往受到遗漏变量、样本自选择和联立性偏误等内生性问题的干扰，因此研究者难以识别投资者视角与企业披露行为之间的因果关系。本文利用一个源自法国的自然实验来克服此类内生性问题，以提高研究结论的可靠性。具体而言，法国在2014年通过了弗洛朗日法案(Loi Florange)。该法案针对一部分法国上市企业，允许以自己名字登记股票并持股至少两年的投资者拥有双重投票权。换而言之，在该法案的约束下投资者对企业策略的干预能力受限于其股票持有期限，因此该法案可以视为对投资者的投资视角的一个外生冲击。本文将利用该自然实验，研究投资者投资视角和投资期限的变化如何影响企业的自愿披露行为。

16505017.label: Realisation of objectives
16505017.value: We have fully achieved our three objectives. To do so, we have compared French listed firms that had already adopted voluntarily tenure voting rights to firms that were forced to adopt tenure voting as a response to the Florange law passed in 2014 and effective in 2016. Regarding the first and second objectives, we did not find any evidence that a change in tenure voting rights that supposedly attracted more long-term oriented investors had an impact on corporate disclosure strategies. That is, comparing a treatment group of firms that were mandated by the law to switch to tenure voting to a control group of firms that already had voluntarily adopted this governance feature, we fail to find a change in the frequency, precision or type of voluntary disclosure, as measured through characteristics of earnings forecasts. This lack of result could be explained by the lack of power (small sample and few data points post regulation) or by a change in ownership, as detailed below. Regarding the third objective, our project is able to make a unique contribution to the literature. We have turned the focus of our project to examining the capital market consequences of the Florange Act, a regulatory intervention aimed at generalizing tenure voting in French public companies. We find that firms that adopt tenure voting because of the regulation experience a decrease in foreign institutional ownership and an increase in cost of capital relative to other firms. This might sound at odds with the initial prediction since tenure voting right directly aim at providing long-term investors with more power relative to short-term investors. However, we have realized that our result is more pronounced among firms with block holders (public or private). Furthermore, the market reacts positively to successful opt-out votes. Collectively, our evidence casts doubt on the merit of regulation-induced tenure voting as a desirable corporate governance mechanism. Instead, the results echo concerns that mandating double voting rights reinforces insiders’ entrenchment and enhance the agency conflict between majority and minority shareholders.

In the United States, tech companies from the Silicon Valley are pushing for a stock exchange that requires tenure voting to promote long term orientation. Instead, our results suggest that such provision will simply allow tech giants whose founders still own a large portion of their firm to maintain their control over the firm while slowly divesting stocks.
