16505217.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16505217.value: 國際網站的本土化, 網絡廣告及多元文化人士

16505217.label: Project Objectives
16505217.value: To investigate how the effects of website characteristics on multicultural individuals’ perceptions and behaviors is contingent on the localization elements of websites at the individual level. To investigate how the effectiveness of online advertising on multicultural individuals is contingent on the localization elements of websites.
rows: To investigate how the effects of website characteristics on multicultural individuals’ perceptions and behaviors is contingent on the localization elements of websites at the individual level.
To investigate how the effectiveness of online advertising on multicultural individuals is contingent on the localization elements of websites.

16505217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16505217.value: Global companies are leveraging the Internet to expand their reach to online consumers across different countries and cultures. To address individuals’ distinctive preferences for website design across cultures and regions, global companies tend to localize their international websites with local language, local content, and local ads (what we term as localization). eBay is one of the global companies that has generated huge revenues from its localized international websites in more than 30 countries. The existing literature has shown that the preferences for website design vary across countries and cultures, and individuals in different countries and regions typically prefer to use localized versions of the international websites rather than the international websites without localization. While some studies have examined the effects of localizing the international websites, they tend to make certain common assumptions about the individuals, the level of analysis and the outcomes of localizing the international websites. One assumption is to adopt a mono-cultural approach and assume that every individual in a country belongs to only one culture. Another assumption is to examine the mono-cultural impacts on the websites at the country-level of analysis. Finally, prior studies have tended to focus only on the positive effects of localizing the international websites. Our proposed project is intended to complement prior research by adopting an alternative approach and a different level of analysis, and focusing on both the positive and negative effects of localizing the international websites. We investigate how multicultural individuals who internalize more than one culture will perceive and interact with different localization features of the international websites. Further, we investigate how the effectiveness of online advertising will be contingent on various localization features of the international websites. We plan to conduct two experiments to test our research models. In terms of research insights, this project will contribute to our understanding of the interplay between multicultural individuals, localized international websites, and online advertising. In terms of managerial insights, the findings of this project can be translated into practical guidelines for designing optimal strategies for localizing international websites for effective online advertising. This project is also highly relevant to Hong Kong where its residents are multicultural individuals, having been exposed to the influence of both Chinese and Western cultures. Government agencies and companies intending to do online advertising to Hong Kong residents would need to take into account the multicultural nature of these individuals.

16505217.label: Realisation of objectives
16505217.value: We conducted three experiments to test the research objectives, and combined them into one paper. Please note that the project was delayed for a year due to the widespread local protest against the Hong Kong administration, followed by the Covid-19 pandemic which resulted in online classes only. As a result, the project was affected severely and since no students were allowed on campus, we could not conduct all the in-lab experiments, and decided to switch to online experiments to fulfill the research objectives. Research Objective 1: To fulfill the first research objective, we updated our literature review to include relevant articles published in the disciplines of information systems, psychology, human-computer interaction, communication, marketing, and management. To fine-tune the experiment design, we conducted pretests, focus groups, and pilot studies. We also collected feedback from other academics in terms of how our work can be improved to provide adequate contribution to the academic literature and the industry practitioners. We amended our tentative research model (in the original grant application) and extended the coverage of data collection to both Hong Kong and British multicultural individuals. Based on feedback from other academics, we were advised to focus on identifying and testing a potential mechanism for the observed effects of localized websites on multicultural individuals. Hence, we made the following changes to our tentative research model in the original grant application. We dropped the dependent variables—attitude and purchase intention—from the research model and focused on trust, because trust building is an a priori condition for any subsequent interaction with a website when it is first introduced into a new country. Next, we incorporated culture as a new mediating variable in the research model. This is to account for the mechanism through which the localized website can affect trust, as we proposed that the localization elements exerted effects on multicultural individuals’ trust in a website through the activation of specific cultural knowledge system, i.e., collectivism or individualism. For the independent variables, we dropped the member size construct and incorporated localized images (from research objective 2) as a new construct. The reason is that when we manipulated member size in a laboratory environment, the results showed that this manipulation was not successful, probably because participants could easily see how many members were currently online during a lab experiment. Perhaps, this variable might be better tested using a field experiment with a real website. Unfortunately, we do not have access to such a website during the time frame of this research project. Thus, we decided to examine other potential independent variables, i.e., image. Based on the literature review and because of the content variable we proposed in RQ2 (which we will elaborate on below), we identified localized images as another important localization element that could potentially affect trust building through culture activation. Specifically, both local language and localized images are cultural cues, which can activate different cultural knowledge systems among multicultural individuals, which in term affects their trust toward a localized website. We also looked at the potential interaction effects between these two localization elements, i.e., language and image. As a result of these modifications, our final research model is different from the tentative model we proposed initially when we submitted our grant application. In addition, in the initial grant application, we proposed to conduct experiments on Hong Kong multicultural individuals only. However, based on feedback from other academics, we decided to extend the coverage of data collection to include not only Hong Kong multicultural individuals, but also British multicultural individuals. We recruited Hong Kong and British multicultural individuals who are fluent in both Chinese and English and likely to have extensive exposure to both Chinese and Western cultures. Doing so can help to validate our findings across different groups of multicultural individuals, increasing the external validity of our research. Hence, we conducted three experiments. • An online experiment with 83 Hong Kong multicultural individuals who were fluent in both Chinese and English. This online experiment has one between-subject factor, i.e., language (English vs. Chinese). This experiment provided strong support for our theoretical proposition that language is a cultural cue that can activate specific culture of multicultural individuals, which is the core component of the revised research model. • A laboratory experiment with 220 Hong Kong multicultural individuals who were fluent in both Chinese and English. The 2x2 laboratory experiment had two between-subject factors, i.e., language (English vs. Chinese) and social presence (low vs. high). The results provided support for the proposed relationships in the revised research model, by demonstrating that the effect of social presence (an important website characteristic) is contingent on the cultural knowledge system that was activated by the localization elements. • An online experiment with 126 British multicultural individuals who were fluent in both Chinese and English. The 2x2 online experiment had two between-subject factors, i.e., language (English vs. Chinese) and image (Western vs. Chinese). The results largely supported the proposed relationships in the revised research model. Research Objective 2: Before we conducted the second experiment, we did another round of literature review, performed a few pretests to prepare the materials to be used on the experiment website, held a few focus groups discussion regarding the constructs we proposed in the second research model, and conducted a pilot study with Hong Kong multicultural individuals. During this process, we found the following: 1) Most of the modern online advertisements contain both text and images. Advertisements that contain only text or only images were deemed unreal by our subjects. Therefore, it is important to first untangle the individual effects of text and images, before we investigate their combined effects in an online advertisement. 2) Most subjects perceived advertisements posted on a website to be offered by a third-party company, rather than the website itself. As a result, the effect of the format of the ad on individuals’ trust in the website may be smaller than what we originally expected. 3) While most online advertisements contain images, there are other types of images on the localization website, such as the background image, product images, etc. Our literature review showed that image is another localization element that could serve as a cultural cue to activate different cultural knowledge systems. And multicultural individuals may pay more attention to other images on the website than the images in an advertisement, as the advertisement can easily be viewed as a distraction. Given the above findings, we decided to include localized image as another important independent variable in our research model. And we operationalized it as the background image and navigation bar image of the localized website, as these images are more likely to be viewed as an integral part of the website, and therefore has stronger effects on the trust building toward the website. We dropped the format of the advertisement variable, and integrated localized image into the research model, as our focus groups and pilot test results showed that localized image is another important cultural cue that could activate different cultural knowledge systems. The inclusion of localized image into the research model also allowed us to examine the potential interaction effect between localized language and localized image on culture activation, and arrive at a more complete understanding of the effect of localization on trust. Hence, we combined the two modified research questions together into one paper.

16505217.label: Major findings and research outcome
16505217.value: We have investigated the effects of two important localization elements (language and image) on multicultural individuals’ trust in a localized website, through their activated cultural knowledge system. Specifically, we found that presenting localized websites in Chinese or with Chinese images will activate collectivism in multicultural individuals who have extensive exposure to both Chinese and Western culture, while presenting localized websites in English or with Western images will activate individualism in these multicultural individuals. This finding implies that the localization elements can serve as cultural cues to activate specific cultural knowledge system among multicultural individuals who have internalized more than one cultural knowledge system. The effects of localization elements were found to be consistent across the British and Hong Kong multicultural individuals with different first languages. However, the combined effects of language and image are not necessarily stronger than the effect of implementing either language or image alone. The activated cultural knowledge system in turn affects multicultural individuals’ trust in the localized website, such that individuals with activated collectivism tend to trust the website more than individuals with activated individualism. Further, the activated cultural dimension was found to moderate the effect of an important website characteristic, i.e., social presence, on trust, with stronger effects observed for multicultural individuals whose collectivism has been activated. Our work contributes to the existing HCI research on website design by focusing on multicultural individuals, and uncovering the mechanism of how implementing localized websites can influence multicultural individuals’ trust in the website through activation of their collectivism cultural knowledge system. A paper (see attached) was submitted to a journal for publication consideration.

16505217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16505217.value: Our work can serve as a foundation for future research into human-computer interaction (HCI) in general, and more specifically, website design by investigating the perceptions and behaviors of multicultural individuals in the context of localized websites. To gain a comprehensive understanding of the utility of various localization elements and website characteristics, future research can develop other experiment websites to investigate the effects of other cultural cues (e.g., color) and other website characteristics (e.g., website layout) on the local customers. To increase generalizability of our findings, future research can also replicate our work with other multicultural individuals in other countries. Finally, researchers may partner with existing e-commerce websites which have multi-country presence, to conduct field experiments.

16505217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16505217.value: There are many international companies that have developed localized versions of their websites for different countries. To cater to local customers and gain their trust, these localized websites often feature local elements (e.g., using the local language and/or local images). At the same time, more and more people nowadays in many countries are multicultural individuals who are capable of speaking multiple languages and have been exposed to multiple cultures. As building localized websites involves significant additional investment, in terms of money, extra development time, programming complexity, coordination cost, hardware acquisition, etc., it is unclear whether they pay off in terms of increased local customer traffic, etc., for these international companies. In this project, we viewed the localized websites as containing cultural cues that can activate multicultural individuals’ specific cultural knowledge system, which in turn affects the degree to which these multicultural individuals will trust these websites. We conducted three experiments involving Hong Kong and British multicultural individuals using different websites developed with different combinations of language (Chinese vs. English) and images (Chinese vs. Western). We found that localized websites tend to increase multicultural individuals’ trust in the websites through activating their collectivism (but not individualism) knowledge system.

16505617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16505617.value: 在這個項目中，我們將研究基礎設施建設對融資和不平等分配的影響。許多國家花費數十億元建設基礎設施。中國目前的“一帶一路” 倡議是其中一個突出的例子。專家認為，當建成道路和鐵路，發展便會隨之而來。可是關於誰從基礎設施建設中受益的嚴謹證據卻寥寥可數。已擁有資產的富人，會否更能夠把握隨基礎設施帶來的融資機會而獲取更大的利益？還是在基礎設施建設之前被排除在正規金融體制之外的窮人因也能因基礎設施帶來的融資機會而受益？這是一個非常重要的問題，因為過去幾十年來許多國家急速發展加劇了不平等現象，而這現像正源於並非所有人都分享到這種增長的好處。 量化基礎設施影響的一個主要挑戰是缺乏適當的反事實或對照組。雖然我們可以觀察到在“受到處理的”地區建成新基礎設施之前和之後發生的情況，但是很難將改變歸因於基礎設施項目，而不是任何其他同時可能發生變化的環境或政策因素。如果基礎設施隨機配置，那麼很自然地，比較組就是因隨機配置下沒有建成基礎設施的地區。對於計量經濟學家來說，不幸的是現實中基礎設施並不是隨機分配的，因此將處理的區域與未經處理的區域進行直接比較會導致誤差。 在這個擬議的項目中，我們將利用圍繞印度一個旨在向未連接村莊提供全天候道路連接的主要公共道路施工方案政策。該計劃側重於將新道路優先於具有“較高”人口的村莊，其中“更高”是根據人數而明確定義的。該計劃優先考慮人口略高於某一數字的村莊，如500人。這樣的程序規則創造了在這些村莊人口門檻受到處理的概率不連續性，給予我們利用模糊回歸不連續性設計來研究基礎設施影響的機會。假設於同一地區，人口剛剛低於500人的村莊非常類似於人口剛剛超過500人的村莊，政策造成的道路變化幾乎是隨機的。因此，這種分析的結果將為道路連接對不同發展成果的影響（例如融資的可得性和分配）給予令人信服的估計。

16505817.label: Project Objectives
16505817.value: Building on the POS, we will propose a theoretical framework investigating the positive influence of nationality dissimilarity in terms of both IJV identification and creativity of top managers. Based on the identification literature, we will explicate how nationality dissimilarity enhances a top manager’s IJV identification through enhancing the perceived attractiveness of the IJV. On the basis of the creativity and cross-cultural management literature, we will demonstrate how nationality dissimilarity promotes top managers’ creativity by increasing their cognitive complexity. We will propose how organizational factors such as the IJV TMT learning climate enhance both the identification process and the creativity process. We will design and conduct an empirical study of IJVs in China to test the theoretical relationships proposed in this study.

16505817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16505817.value: An international joint venture (IJV) is an important form of cross-border cooperation between independent companies from different countries (Inkpen and Beamish, 1997; Yan and Luo, 2001), as it enables the partner firms to not only expand quickly to new geographic markets, but also capitalize on each other’s complementary resources such as advanced technology or local market knowledge (Barkema, Shenkar, Vermeulen and Bell, 1997; Hamel, 1991). However, IJVs face many challenges arising from cross-cultural differences (Barkema et al., 1997; Hambrick, Li, Xin and Tsui, 2001; Li and Hambrick, 2005). The influence of cultural and national differences has been extensively discussed in the international business literature (Earley and Mosakowski, 2000; Vaara, Sarala, Stahl and Bjorkman, 2012). Yet, previous studies tended to treat nationality difference as a liability (Stahl and Tung, 2015) and focused more on studying its negative influences such as frictions and ineffective interactions which are harmful for IJV operation (Julian, Wachter and Mueller, 2009) and less on the positive ones. We, however, propose that the nationality dissimilarity should function as an asset rather than a liability for both IJVs and their top managers, since an IJV that operates as a separate entity from the parent firms needs to deal on its own with the host country environment and can certainly benefit from the diverse institutional experiences and skills provided by managers of different nationalities (Lane, Maznevski and Mendenhall, 2004). This research project proposes to adopt positive organizational scholarship (POS) (Cameron, Dutton and Quinn, 2003) to investigate the positive influence of nationality dissimilarity in the IJV context. We will first propose a conceptual model of how nationality dissimilarity might impact top managers’ identification with their IJVs through influencing the attractiveness of the IJVs and affect their creativity by altering their creative self-efficacy. We will then examine how an IJV’s learning climate enhances the benefits of nationality differences by influencing the identification process and affecting creativity generation. We will design and implement an empirical study in the IJV context in China to test the theoretical relationships proposed. The results will provide a greater understanding of the benefits of nationality dissimilarity in IJVs, and under which conditions the benefits may vary.

16505817.label: Realisation of objectives
16505817.value: We have now completed the project and achieved the project objectives as listed above. In the first phase of the two-phase research project, we focused on building the theoretical framework, developing the constructs, and preparing for empirical data analyses. We have conducted a comprehensive literature review in building a conceptual model. In particular, we are very pleased to report the recent acceptance for publication of a top tier, UTD-24 journal article from this project in the Journal of International Business Studies, on a comprehensive literature review of top management teams, together with several coauthors (Cuypers, I., Patel, C., Ertug, G., Li, J.T., and Cuypers, Y., 2021. “Top Management Teams in International Business Research: A Review and Suggestions for Future Research,” Journal of International Business Studies, in press). In the second phase of the project, we have conducted two empirical studies in China to test the theoretical relationships proposed in this study. We are very pleased to report one more publication in a major international business journal and one working paper (which is currently under review). The first empirical paper examines the idea of cultural frictions for international business and was published in Journal of World Business, a leading journal in international business and an ABS 4 level journal (Li, J.T., Liu, B., and Qian, G., 2019. “The Belt and Road Initiative, Cultural Friction and Ethnicity: Their Effects on the Export Performance of SMEs in China,” Journal of World Business, 54: 350-359). The 2nd empirical paper examines nationality dissimilarity and organizational identification in international joint ventures, and is now under review at a special issue of a FT-50 journal, Human Resource Management (Li, J.T. and Zhou, J., 2021. “A Relational Demography Perspective on Nationality Dissimilarity and Organizational Identification in International Joint Ventures in China”). In summary, we have published one top-tier UTD-24 article (JIBS), an ABS 4 article (JWB), and have completed a working paper under review at a special issue of a FT-50 journal (HRM). In addition, based on the suggestion of the panel member, we have removed a SMJ paper (Li et al., 2019) from the output list for this final report. We want to thank the panel member for the suggestion.

16505817.label: Major findings and research outcome
16505817.value: This empirical study uses survey data from China to examine the effect of a top manager’s nationality dissimilarity with the other members of the top management team of an international joint venture (IJV) on his or her identification with the venture. The results show an inverted U-shaped relationship between nationality dissimilarity and organizational identification. Great nationality dissimilarity is found to enhance, up to a point, a manager’s perception of values and goal similarity between himself or herself and the venture. Beyond that point, negative feelings associated with isolation and exclusion are found to be dominant. A manager’s closeness to the chief executive of an IJV and the international market focus of the IJV are found to moderate this curvilinear relationship.

16505817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16505817.value: There are several areas for future research. For example, this research investigated only identification with an IJV rather than dual identification with both the IJV and the parent firm. Future research should examining the parent firm identification as a dependent variable. Parent firm identification might play some role in influencing IJV identification. Thus, this aspect could be an area for future research. Endogeneity might still have existed in the relationships examined in this study despite the efforts to address it in the design and the empirical tests. For instance, certain kinds of IJVs might tend to have both greater nationality diversity and stronger identification. This scenario might occur in more prestigious IJVs, more career-enhancing IJVs, IJVs that are more important to the parent firms, and certain kinds (or ages) of IJVs that are more likely to attract managers from one or the other parent firm. Further research is needed to explore these possibilities.

16505817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16505817.value: An international joint venture (IJV) is an important form of cross-border cooperation that companies from different countries use to help them navigate the complex global environment; this cooperation has generated much research interest over the past decades. However, one important yet neglected area of research is a top manager’s identification with the joint venture. Studies of multinational companies have shown that the organizational identification of their subsidiary managers benefits the subsidiaries in terms of enhancing knowledge sharing among employees and reducing turnover intentions. The top managers’ identification with an IJV is especially important for its operation because the managers normally come from different home countries and may have conflicting values, roles, and goals. This study has shown that a moderate level of nationality dissimilarity among the top managers within IJVs in China can be helpful in terms of triggering a top manager’s identification with the venture. IJVs should keep this in mind when recruiting foreign managers. They should attend to nationality differences given their significant effect on identification with the firm. Moreover, they need to care about top managers’ psychological acculturation while working with nationally dissimilar colleagues.

16506217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16506217.value: The purpose of this project is to examine whether managers, as corporate insiders, learn from external sell-side analysts in issuing management earnings forecasts. Early studies have presumed that managers, who are insiders running firms and making key business decisions, have an absolute information advantage over analysts and analysts would learn new information from managers and revise their forecast accordingly (e.g., Diamond, 1985; Baik and Jiang, 2006; Altschuler, 2009). However, management earnings forecasts are more accurate than analysts’ forecasts only about 50% of the time (e.g., Ruland, 1978; Hutton and Stocken, 2009; Hilary and Hsu, 2011; Hilary, Hsu, and Wang, 2014). Recently, Hutton, Lee, and Shu (2012) further show that analysts and managers have their own information advantages in forecasting earnings. However, it remains unclear whether managers would learn information from analysts and issue better forecasts. In this project, we plan to shed light on this question by examining how exogenous shocks to analyst coverage, resulting from broker closures and mergers, affect the properties of management earnings forecasts. We hypothesize that if analysts are an important source of information for managers, termination of analyst coverage will adversely affect the accuracy and precision of management earnings forecasts. Hence, we will first test whether the accuracy and precision of management earnings forecasts decreases after an exogenous drop in analyst coverage. We also develop a hypothesis with respect to the cross-section of the effect of an analyst coverage drop on management earnings forecasts. The learning hypothesis also implies that the effect of analyst coverage drop on management forecasts should be greater if the dropped analysts are more informed. Furthermore, analysts’ information advantages are more likely to lie in the ability to process macroeconomic and industry level information. Therefore, we will also test whether the impact of an analyst coverage drop on management forecast accuracy is stronger when the dropped analysts are more informed, when earnings move more in concert with macroeconomic factors, and weaker when stocks have more firm-specific information. 该项目的目的是研究管理人员，作为企业内部人士是否在发布管理层盈利预测时从分析师那里学期获取有用信息。早期研究 假设管理人员是内部人士，与分析师相比具有绝对的信息优势。分析师将从公司管理层那里学习新的信息，并相应地修改其预测 （例如，Diamond，1985; Baik和Jiang，2006; Altschuler，2009）。但是，管理层盈利预测的准确度只有大约50％的时间优于分析师预测的准确度（例如，Ruland，1978; Hutton and Stocken，2009; Hilary和Hsu，2011; Hilary，Hsu和 Wang，2014）。最近，Hutton，Lee和Shu（2012）进一步表明，分析师和 管理者在预测收益方面有自己的信息优势。但现在研究尚未回答管理层是否会从分析师那里学习信息。 在这个项目中，我们计划通过研究由经纪人倒闭和被并购导致的分析师覆盖减少对管理层盈利预测的影响来理解这一问题。如果分析师是管理人员的重要信息来源，分析师覆盖的减少将对管理层盈利预测的准确性和精度产生不利影响。因此，我们将首先检验分析师覆盖率下降后管理层盈利预测的准确性和准确性的变化情况。我们也分析了一些关于分析师覆盖面下降对管理层盈利预测的影响的横截面 假说。学习假设也意味着如果公司丢掉的是比较有信息的分析师，管理层预测的准确度的下降应该更大。另外，分析师的信息优势更有可能在于他们处理宏观经济和行业层面信息的能力。所以我们会的还测试分析师覆盖影响是否对管理预测的准确性.当分析师的消息更加了解时，企业的收益就会变得更强 更多与宏观经济因素相协调，股票走势更为疲软企业特定信息。

16600017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16600017.value: We will examine changes in rural marriage in mid-twentieth century People’s Republic of China (PRC) by constructing and analyzing a database of household registration forms compiled in the mid- to late-1960s. We will focus on three aspects of marriage: timing, assortative mating, and spatial patterns. First, we will examine how education, family class label, and other socioeconomic characteristics influenced the timing and prevalence of marriage. Second, we will explore how class labels, political developments, and other changes altered social boundaries as reflected in patterns of intermarriage. Third, we will look at how local economic and other changes altered the geography of marriage markets. The results of our study of marriage will fill a gap in our understanding of rural Chinese society during the mid-20th century by illuminating change during a crucial transitional period. On the one hand, data from contemporary retrospective surveys rarely offer much detail for the period before the 1970s. On the other hand, extensive qualitative and quantitative evidence before the middle of the twentieth century reveal features of traditional marriage patterns, but tell little about how patterns changed after 1949. However, between 1949 and 1970 the PRC experienced political and social transformations. The 1950 Marriage Law forbade arranged marriage and other traditional practices. Education expanded dramatically. Transportation improved, potentially expanding marriage markets. The assignment of class labels, meanwhile, changed preferences for spouse’s socioeconomic background. We will make use of family social class registration forms compiled during the Four Cleanups Campaign (1963-1966) from a selection of rural villages in Shanxi and Hebei. These represent the most comprehensive available records of rural life in the PRC for the mid-20th century. We will transcribe approximately 14,000 such forms from 70 villages (production brigades) in 4 counties, to complete the construction of a dataset containing nearly 20,000 forms from 100 villages in 11 counties. For each household, a form records detailed socioeconomic information on wealth and status from the 1940s to the 1960s, social relations, family history, and sociodemographic information. Our analysis of data for other locations in Shanxi confirms these data to be a rich source for the micro-level study of family dynamics in the PRC throughout the first two thirds of the twentieth century. We will apply methods already in use, including event-history analysis for marriage timing and contingency table analysis for assortative mating. For the geography of marriage markets, we will apply discrete-choice models. 我們的研究旨在探索中國農村的婚姻模式在二十世紀中葉所發生的系列變化。該研究將基於二十世紀六十年代中後期社會主義教育運動期間四清運動工作隊記載的階級成分登記表來建設數據庫並對該數據庫進行分析。該研究將聚焦於婚姻制度的三個層面：結婚時間，婚姻匹配以及婚姻市場的地理格局。第一，我們將研究教育程度，家庭階級成分以及其他社會經濟因素如何影響到結婚年齡以及婚姻的普遍性。第二，通過研究建國前後通婚模式的差異，我們著力於探討階級成分的劃分以及1949年後的一系列政治運動與變革如何改變了社會邊界。第三， 我們將研究家庭特徵以及地區性的經濟變化如何形塑了婚姻市場的地理特徵。 我們的研究將填補現階段研究關於二十世紀中期的中國社會的理解的空白。一方面，當代的回溯性調查數據所能提供的關於二十世紀七十年代以前的信息極為有限。另一方面，雖然大量定量與定性的證據對於二十世紀中期以前的傳統婚姻模式的特徵有所介紹，但對於婚姻模式在1949年後所發生的變化的介紹及解釋卻付之闕如。 在1949年到1970年間，中國社會經歷了巨大而深刻的政治和經濟轉型。1950年頒佈並施行的新婚姻法廢除了包辦婚姻以及童養媳等傳統的婚姻模式，並確立了婚姻自由的原則；建國初的基礎教育的迅速普及與文盲數量的顯著減少，以及階級成分的劃分亦改變了農村社會對配偶一方家庭的社會、經濟背景的偏好；日益發達的交通以及通訊技術，也潛在地擴大了婚姻市場的地理界線。然而，這裡所提到的1949年後婚姻模式可能受到的影響及發生的變化仍然缺乏實證研究的證據支持。 我們的研究將基於一類嶄新的材料： 來源於山西省和河北省的在四清運動（1963-1966年）間編制而成的家庭階級成分登記表。這些登記表是目前所發現的關於二十世紀中期的中國農村社會的最全面與最可靠的記錄之一。作為該項目的一部分，我們將錄入來源於12縣58個村莊（生產大隊）的大約10000份家庭階級成分登記表，並基於此建設數據庫。對於每一戶家庭，登記表記錄了該家庭在二十世紀四十年代到二十世紀六十年代期間的財產狀況，階級成分，社會關係，三代家史，以及其他重要的社會經濟與人口信息。我們基於山西省其他地區的數據的研究已經表明階級成分登記表為二十世紀中期中國農村家庭人口的微觀研究提供了豐富、堅實的素材。 我們將採用事件史分析方法來研究結婚時間的變化，列聯表分析方法來分析婚姻匹配模式，以及離散選擇模型來分析婚姻市場的地理特徵。

16600017.label: Realisation of objectives
16600017.value: (Organized According to Objective) 1. We completed transcription of the Hebei social class registration forms as well as forms from other provinces. This yielded information for 7,182 households in Hebei, 1,689 households in Guangdong, and approximately 8,000 additional households in Shanxi that were not in an existing dataset that we previously worked with the Shanxi University Research Center for Chinese Social History to construct. Entry and cleaning of these data continued right up to the end of the project period. 2. We processed and cleaned the data we entered to produce a consolidated dataset to be used. 3. We successfully constructed variables measuring community, household and individual context. For the first stage, we transcribed relevant text directly from the original forms. We then extracted the information that was the basis of the variables by automated parsing. Our additional investigations revealed that there was more information not extracted by the automated parsing, especially information on the spatial origins of social relations, and we initiated a manual review in the final year of the project period that yielded additional data. 4. We conducted analysis of marriage timing and proportion married by education and class label. Since as mentioned in the discussion of objectives 1 and 3 entry and cleaning continued of new data and extraction of new variables continued right up to the end of the project period, we have continued to work on this topic up to and after the conclusion of the project period. Because our work on this topic with the expanded dataset continues, we report this as only 90% complete. 5. We completed and published an analysis of changes over time in patterns of assortative mating in rural Shanxi. Since the completion of the project period, we have continued to work on this topic with the expanded and refined dataset. Because work on this topic is ongoing, we report it as only 90% complete. 6. We report this as 85 percent complete because while we conducted initial studies of spatial patterns of spousal origins and presented the results at the Social Science History Association and RC-41/RC-06 meetings in 2018, we are still continuing analysis using the expanded and refined dataset and working on manuscripts. 7. We published one paper in Research in Social Stratification and Mobility, have another paper on the distribution of private property 1949-1966 accepted for publication in an edited volume commemorating the 30th anniversary of the Shanxi University Research Center for Chinese Social History, and have another manuscript on the urban/rural divide in China 1949/1965 that will be submitted soon. At professional meetings in 2018 and 2019 we have presented work on spatial features of kinship networks, spatial aspects of marriage, and occupational mobility that are the basis for manuscripts in progress. One of our PhD students, Li Xiangning, used the data for two of the three chapters in her PhD dissertation, completed in 2020. She is turning these into papers for submission.

16600017.label: Major findings and research outcome
16600017.value: The most important outcome is that we have completed construction of a major new dataset covering the economic, social, family and demographic characteristics of 17,000 households in Hebei, Shanxi and Guangdong in the mi-20th century that will be a major resource for research on family organization, inequality, and economic change in China in the middle of the 20th century for the foreseeable future. In our published paper in Research in Social Stratification and Mobility, we showed that both education and class labels were salient influences on patterns of assortative mating. Contrary to expectations from published case studies of specific communities, there was little evidence that patterns changed as a result of the Land Reform and other developments. For couples who married before the Land Reform, the family landholding of prospective spouses was a salient consideration, and for couples who married after the Land Reform, class label based on pre-Land Reform landholding was also a salient consideration, so that there was little net impact on patterns of sorting. Previous case studies had suggested that the imposition of Class Labels increased sorting on pre-Land Reform landholding, but such studies neglected that sorting on socioeconomic characteristics before Land Reform was already substantial. Our HKPFS PhD student, Li Xiangning, collected data and oversaw data entry and then used the resulting data in two of her three dissertation chapters. Chapter 2 used the data to study the assignment and reassignment of class labels. This deepens our understanding of the class labels that we use in our ongoing studies of marriage. Chapter 3 studied changing occupational structure and mobility patterns in North China, again providing important context for our studies of assortative marriage. She finished in fall 2020 and is turning her dissertation chapters into papers to be submitted to journals. We have conducted a study of composition and distribution of private property using these data. The resulting paper will be included in an edited volume to be published next year. Like Li Xiangning's work, the results provide context for our future studies of marriage. We also have initial results on geographic exogamy presented at a meeting in Singapore in 2018 and initial results on kinship networks presented at a meeting in Chicago in fall 2018. These are being developed into manuscripts that we anticipate submitting for publication in the next year or two.

16600017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16600017.value: We are preparing manuscripts based on our unpublished results and continue our analysis of marriage and related topics using the complete expanded dataset and preparation Going forward, we will focus on the role of spatial context in patterns of assortative mating using the completed, expanded dataset. We will continue to focus on whether certain types of assortative mating were more or less likely to involve geographic exogamy, and if so, what the spatial patterns of the origins of spouses is. Building on work on occupations by Li Xiangning and work on property ownership by Matt Noellert and James Lee and their collaborators, we will consider these as dimensions in the study of assortative mating. We continue to use the data for studies of topics other than marriage, including further studies of social mobility, occupational structure and occupational mobility, and economic inequality.

16600017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16600017.value: This research has produced a valuable new resource for the study of society and economy in China in the middle of the twentieth century: a dataset that records the family relationships, property, occupations, and history of thousands of households in North China between the early twentieth century. In published work we have already shown that education and class label played a salient role in the formation of marriages during this period. We have also examined patterns of occupational mobility in rural areas close to cities that were experiencing industrialization, patterns of inequality in property ownership, and the spatial proximity of kin.

16600417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16600417.value: This project aims to examine animated filmmaking in the Manchukuo Film Association (Manying, 1937-1945), which played an important role in shaping wartime film culture in Northeast China and other Japanese-occupied areas such as North China and Shanghai. Some studies have been conducted on Manying films, but they have focused on documentaries, newsreels, and fictional live-action films, and do not systematically address the cinematic form of animation. Since animation is a different medium, an in-depth study of it will provide a unique perspective from which to understand Manying and the complicated wartime culture of Manchukuo, China, and Japan. The major theoretical problem that this project tries to address is the convoluted relationship between animation and politics. On the one hand, animation, often regarded as a fantasy art form intended for an audience of children, is widely known for its escapist and apolitical tendencies as it features fairytales, folklore, and talking animals. On the other hand, animation, due to its kinship with cartoon and caricature, can be used as a powerful weapon to disseminate ideologies to both children and adults. In a politically fraught time when the non-political could be politicized, how do we locate and dislocate Manying and its animation on the spectrum between escapism and political propaganda? To answer this question, the PI will pay critical attention to both the films and context. First, the PI will closely analyze individual Manying animated films, focusing on textual nuances to reveal hidden meanings beneath the surface interpretation. Second, she will contextualize Manying animation in the network of animated filmmaking under Japanese occupation in Northeast China, North China, and Shanghai. She will also analyze Manying animation in relation to wartime Japanese animation to see its degree of politicization. From the unique perspective of animation, this project will subvert our conventional understanding of Manying, wartime Manchuria, China, and Japan and fill in a blank page in the histories of Chinese and Japanese animation. This proposed new project differs from the PI’s first book manuscript, which discusses the impact of Manying on the animation industry in postwar China after 1945. In contrast, this new project will track animated filmmaking in Manying before 1945. The PI’s first book manuscript discusses wartime Shanghai animation, but does not cover other occupied areas such as Northeast and North China. This new project will serve as an important building block for the PI’s ongoing second book project. 這個項目旨在研究満洲映畫協會 （滿映，1937-1945）生產的動畫電影。滿映在二戰時期對日佔東北，華北和上海的電影文化有著舉足輕重的作用。目前已經有大量關於滿影電影的研究，但是它們的著重點都是紀錄片，新聞片，和由李香蘭主演的故事片， 沒有討論動畫片。動畫是一個與眾不同的媒介，若能從動畫片的角度來考察滿影電影， 必定會給我們提供一個全新的視角，對戰時複雜的滿洲國，中國，和日本電影文化將會有更深入更全面的理解。這個項目的理論框架是動畫和政治之間錯綜複雜的關係。一方面，動畫通常表現童話，神話，民間故事，和擬人化的動物，因而常常被看作是一門為兒童服務的幻想藝術，遠離逃避政治，甚至具有無政治的傾向。另一方面，動畫和手繪卡通以及諷刺漫畫關係緊密，可以被用作是對成人和兒童都有效有力的政治宣傳武器。在一個無政治都可以被高度政治化的特殊時代，我們應當如何在逃避主義和政治宣傳的兩個極端之間界定滿映動畫？

16600617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16600617.value: What forces bring expatriate entrepreneurs back to their home countries? How significant is the role of technology, the local government, and value conflicts in encouraging or discouraging reverse migration by overseas entrepreneurs?? In China in 2004, transferring technology helped returning entrepreneurs succeed back home, while that technology transfer has helped various cities and regions, if not the entire country. Such technology transfer by reverse migrants is particularly helpful for developing countries seeking to catch up with advanced economies by importing technology from them. Since the late 1990s, the Chinese government has encouraged overseas Chinese entrepreneurs to return and bring advanced technologies with them. A survey we conducted in 2004 showed that a significant number of returning Chinese had been attracted by the comparative advantage that they could gain from their access to these technologies, which remained scarce in China at that time. But does the link between reverse migration, technology transfer and business success still hold true today? Second, respondents to our 2004 survey reported more antagonistic relations with local authorities compared to local entrepreneurs, with only four of our 200 entrepreneurs viewing the local Chinese Communist Party (CCP) secretary as important to their efforts. Third, they also felt that they needed to conform to Chinese business norms – such as engaging in corruption and disregarding the environment – in order to succeed. But the CCP has since intervened in the reverse migration process, providing cities and regions with incentives to encourage overseas entrepreneurs to return. So, has the CCP’s intervention increased or decreased an entrepreneur’s likelihood of success; and do returnees continue to try to change Chinese business culture, or have they adapted to local norms? We will survey 99 entrepreneurs who returned within five years of having left China, as well as 99 local entrepreneurs in Beijing, Guangzhou and Chengdu to explore these questions. Using a questionnaire, similar to that we used in 2004, we will document important changes in the reverse migration of Chinese entrepreneurs in the last 13 years. 一個國家有什麼因素可以驅使外派企業家回流？ 技術、地方政府和價值衝突在鼓勵或阻礙海外企業家回流的作用有多大？ 在2004年的中國，轉移技術曾幫助企業家回歸家園。而雖未必是整個國家，然而不少城市和地區亦已受惠於技術轉讓。 從回流人士帶來的技術轉讓，對倚仗進口技術以追趕發達經濟體的發展中國家尤有幫助。 自1990年代末以來，中國政府鼓勵海外華人企業家回流及引進先進技術。 我們2004年進行的一項調查顯示，由於他們可以從這些在當時中國依然稀缺的技術中獲益，這些許多回流的中國人因此被這些比較優勢所吸引。 然而人才回流、技術轉讓和生意成功之間的關係，今天是否仍舊如一？ 第二，2004年度調查對象的調查報告顯示，回流企業家與與當地企業家相比之下，他們與當地政府的關係更為緊張，我們200位企業家中只有4人感到當地的中共黨員書記對他們的努力很重要。 第三，他們感到要取得成功就要符合中國的商業規範，比如涉及貪污和無視環境。 然而中共政府已經干預了回流移民的過程，為城市和地區提供了鼓勵海外企業家回歸的動力。 因此，中共干預增加或減少了企業家成功的可能性; 回歸者是否繼續嘗試改變中國的商業文化，還是適應當地的規範？ 我們將調查99位離開中國的五年內返回的企業家以及北京、廣州和成都的99位企業家，探討這些問題。我們將使用類似於2004年使用的調查問卷，記錄中國企業家過去13年回流移民的重大變化。

16600617.label: Realisation of objectives
16600617.value: We constructed a unique up-to-date dataset on returned entrepreneurs (REs) from three different parts of China and comparative data from local entrepreneurs (LEs) in the same localities. By employing a questionnaire very similar to the one co-I Zweig administered 17 years earlier, we are able to compare not only REs and LEs in 2020-21, but also compare REs and LEs between 2004 and 2020-21 for a diachronic perspective. As discussed below (in 6.1 Major findings and research outcome), significant changes occurred in the composition and attitudes of REs between these two periods. The particular timing of the two surveys occurred during transitional policy contexts: in 2004, the system was liberalizing following China’s entry into the WTO, while in the latter period, the domestic political economy was tightening under Xi Jinping’s anti-corruption drives and intensified scrutiny of the private sector. The outbreak of Covid-19 in January 2020 led to further tightening. Although we were able to complete 75% of the first project objective in the end (i.e., 148 out of 198 surveys), data collection proved to be difficult for three main reasons. First, the political climate in China after the 19th Party Congress in 2017 became more problematic for foreign-funded projects. As a result, Zweig (the original PI on this grant) was not permitted to carry out the interviews in person. Second, geopolitical tensions compounded the shrinking space for field research in China. In late 2017, then US President Trump called on the United States Trade Representative Office to initiate a Section 301 investigation under the US Trade Act of 1974, the results of which, released in March 2018, accused China of various trade infractions, including activities related to intellectual property (IP) theft. That announcement heralded the beginning of the US-China Trade War. As a result, returnee entrepreneurs were understandably hesitant to be interviewed for a survey asking numerous questions about technology transfer and the source of their business’ IP. Third, the Co-I, Dr. Wang Huiyao, with whom Zweig had worked closely and successfully for over a decade, was unexpectedly tasked with urgent projects that his Center on China and Globalization (CCG) was doing for the central government in Beijing. At the time of the project, Dr. Wang became a key player in China’s effort to build “soft power” by “telling China’s story in a more favourable light”—an initiative requested by Xi Jinping—so Dr. Wang was busy traveling and speaking all over the world. The CCG’s post-doctoral fellow on the project travelled with him, which disrupted the original schedule for data collection. Given these challenges, Zweig worked assiduously to get them to fulfil their obligations with partial success. He spent two years working with their representatives in Guangzhou/Shenzhen and travelled to GZ/SZ to encourage a new project manager there. We ultimately received 19 surveys from REs in that region, and 28 surveys from LEs (instead of the 33 plus 33 we had been promised). We had greater success in Qingdao, which we replaced Chengdu as our third research site, as the CCG had an office and a fulltime employee working there who was an excellent researcher. Zweig visited in December 2019. But the outbreak of Covid-19 in January 2020 complicated research in Qingdao. In the end, we received data from 25 REs and 25 LEs, rather than 66 responses (33 of each) that were to be delivered under the research agreement. Repeated requests for more interviews went unheeded. Finally, although the CCG team carried out 19 interviews with LEs in Beijing, it was able to arrange only one face-to-face interview in Beijing. So, in late 2021, they posted the survey on an online platform and contacted the directors of several high-tech parks, incubators, and some of their friends who are entrepreneurs or friends who had connections with entrepreneurs. That effort yielded 13 more REs and 10 more LEs, but because the number of cases was only 61 REs and 87 LEs, we are somewhat limited in our use of more advanced statistical methods for analyzing the data. Despite unanticipated setbacks in the survey implementation process (Objective 1), we completed the three other project objectives. We were able to assess the level of technology that the current crop of REs have brought back with them and, through the interviews, we were able to evaluate the extent to which that technology influenced their decision to return (Objective 2). Overall, we found that the quality of the technology being brought back from abroad has increased in terms of being cutting-edge internationally; and fewer of the returnees who returned because of the technology they had mastered were bringing back technology that was only new for the Chinese economy (i.e., not world class). Furthermore, we found that more of the technology used in the REs’ firms was actually developed within China rather than developed abroad, which lessens the extent of IP theft. We have also been able to assess the quality of ties between REs and the local state (Objective 3) and to demonstrate that relations between REs and the state have changed dramatically since 2004, with the recent cohort being much more willing to work with the state than the 2004 group. While in 2004, 28% of REs wanted “good” or “tight” ties, in 2020-21 those numbers had reached 63.9%. Still, in terms of financing the entrepreneurship, the ties between REs and LEs and the state did not change much. We also were able to assess the “quality” of the relationships by calculating the mean score for each cohort, in terms of their ties with particular agencies and overall with all government agencies. In fact, REs have significantly more negative views of local government agencies than the LEs, as the mean score for almost all of the REs’ attitudes, relative to the attitudes of the LEs, were negative. Finally, we have been able to assess the extent to which REs in 2020-21 constitute “agents of change” rather than conforming to Chinese business norms (Objective 4). The survey results indicate that not only were REs less likely to be agents of change compared to LEs in 2020-21, but they are actually more accepting of corrupt business behavior than both LEs and REs in 2004. This finding is counterintuitive, given that corruption has been aggressively targeted as a problem under Xi Jinping’s leadership since 2012. Therefore, based on the views of the 61 REs who were surveyed, one should not expect transnational forces to influence China’s market norms.

16600617.label: Major findings and research outcome
16600617.value: The background of surveyed Returned Entrepreneurs (REs) changed between 2004 and 2020-21. More held overeseas PhDs (48% in 2020-21 vs. 12% in 2004). Fewer REs in 2020-21 were children of workers (9.8% vs. 17%) or intellectuals (27.9% vs. 39%), and more had parents in business (11.5% vs. 6%). The level of transnational human capital for REs declined: 30% in 2004 were “relatively engaged” with overseas networks vs. 13.1% in 2020-21. Fewer REs in 2020-21 brought technology from abroad that was “highly competitive within China but not necessarily world-class.” In 2004, 47% returned due to technology, of whom 57% brought technology competitive only in China; in 2020-21, 45% returned for technology, but just 37% was only domestically competitive. The 2020-21 REs were less interested in exports than in 2004, and planned to focus on the domestic market. Entrepreneurs’ relations with the local state improved. In 2004, only 1.7% of REs and 3% of LEs reported government help finding customers; responses increased to 13.8% and 9.1% in 2020-21. In 2020-21, neither REs nor LEs deemed it wise to avoid the government and felt the need to establish “good” or “close,” ties with the state; but more REs sought “the tightest relations possible” (21.3% vs. 13.6%). Desire for “good” or “tight” ties with the state grew from 28% in 2004 to 63.9% in 2020-21. LEs wanting “good” or “tight” ties increased from 32.7% to 67%. RE’s reported higher quality ties in 2020-21and were more positive about working with the state than local counterparts. Unlike 2004 when REs saw their firms as “below average,” REs in 2020-21 ranked their firms above LEs on returns on investment, cash flow, sales growth and market share. While being a RE was correlated with success, only REs with technology “relatively short of supply” in China benefited from their overseas experiences. Finally, business norms detiorated. The 2020-21 group believed that success trumps morality, and that taking gifts, corrupt deals and infringing on intellectual property are acceptable. They believe that people need to join the CCP to succeed. But they don’t want to “lay low,” accept social responsibilities, repay society if they succeed, or pay taxes. Thus, while REs in 2004 could be seen as a transnational force disseminating overseas Corporate Social Responsibility, the 2020-21 cohort is unlikely to prioritize environmental concerns, uninterested in changing China, strongly motivated to succeed, and will do whatever it takes to maintain those advantages.

16600617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16600617.value: The escalation of anti-Chinese sentiment in OECD countries following the outbreak of covid-19 and continuing geopolitical tensions between China and western countries is likely to reinforce “push factors” for return migration of entrepreneurial talent. Given our findings that in 2020-21 returnees had fewer advantages over local entrepreneurs than those who returned in 2004, it would be informative to continue studying the experiences of the growing number of returnee entrepreneurs. Meanwhile, China’s efforts to cultivate “indigenous innovation” in strategic industries involving sensitive technology, coupled with the US’s suspicion of ethnic Chinese scientists and engineers, may limit the ease of technology transfer by returnees, while providing more state support for local entrepreneurs. However, the ongoing closure of China to foreign researchers and crackdown on domestic technology entrepreneurs poses constraints on extending our survey in at least the short-term. An interim approach to extending this research agenda would be to survey overseas Chinese entrepreneurs about their potential return migration plans and compare their responses with those from our earlier and existing study.

16600617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16600617.value: This project surveyed both returnee and local entrepreneurs in Beijing, Guangzhou, and Qingdao during 2020-21 to compare their attitudes and business experiences, and assess the extent to which returnees are bringing technology to China from abroad. In a similar survey of returned entrepreneurs in 2004, many returnees could not access world class technology while abroad and brought back technology that was “highly competitive within China but not necessarily world class.” By 2020-21, returnees brought more world-class technology. Other changes also occurred between the 2004 and 2020-21 surveys. The relationship between entrepreneurs and the local state has improved; both returned and local entrepreneurs seek closer ties with the local state than they did in 2004. However, business norms have deteriorated. Returnees in the 2020-21 survey believed that success trumps morality; and that accepting gifts, engaging in corrupt deals, and infringing on intellectual property rights are acceptable. They believe people need to join the CCP to succeed and are more avoidant of social responsibilities, repaying society if they succeed, and paying taxes. While returnees in 2004 were a force in disseminating international norms of Corporate Social Responsibility, the 2020-21 cohort is uninterested in changing China and will do whatever it takes to succeed.

16601217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16601217.value: While the performance of public-private partnership (PPP) projects in water sector varies greatly from one another, the empirical literature has so far offered limited insights about contributing factors for such variations. On the one hand, studies based on econometric analysis tend to focus on comparing the performance of private utilities with that of public utilities, in part as a modelling strategy to make do with the limited number of cases with private sector participation, but have little to say about why some PPP projects have succeed while others have failed. On the other hand, studies focusing on the determinants of success or failure of water PPPs are often based on single cases, making it difficult to draw causal inference that can be generalized to a broad context. China’s phenomenal growth in PPP in water sector in recent years offers unprecedented opportunities to understand why the performance of water PPPs may differ considerably from each other. Against the backdrop of the retreat of private sector participation in the water sector elsewhere globally, the country has seen a massive proliferation of PPPs in water sector in the last decade: 300 PPP projects reached financial closure in water sector in China from 2006 to 2015, accounting for more than 60% the total number of such projects in the world during the same period. The sheer number of such projects not only offers necessary variations among comparable water PPPs for econometric analysis, but also provides potential opportunities for conducting comparative case studies that are analytically rigorous. This research aims to contribute to a better understanding of factors and dynamics that may affect the performance and long-term sustainability of PPPs by systematically addressing a set of questions in the context of the rapid development of water PPPs in China. Why have some water PPP projects performed well while others have failed, despite of being situated under similar institutional environments? What are different pathways for water PPPs to succeed, and what are different pathways to failure? What are key factors or dynamics that can contribute to long-term sustainability of water PPPs? The answers to these questions will have significant impact not only in advancing the theories of PPP in public service delivery, but also in safeguarding the effectiveness, efficiency and equity in the provision of water services in China in an era of PPP. 水務行業公私合營（PPP）項目相互之間的績效差異很大，但是迄今為止，實証研究還未能對影響績效的關鍵因素提供真知灼見。一方面，不少研究以計量經濟學方法為手段來比較私營水務公司與國營水務公司績效之間的差別。這類研究從建模技術的角度看可以解決由於公私合營項目數量少而帶來的一些困難，但是無法回答有關PPP項目之間績效差異性的問題。另一方面，針對水務PPP成功或失敗決定因素的研究通常基於個案研究，但這類研究所得出的結論是否具有普遍性常常會受到質疑。 近年來中國水務行業PPP的驚人增長提供了前所未有的機會來研究水務PPP的績效的差異性。在全球范圍私營部門參與水務行業日益趨冷的大環境下，中國水務PPP大幅度增加：從2006年到2015年中國有300個PPP項目達成財務結算，佔全球此類項目總數的60％以上。中國水務PPP數量上的急劇增長及其差異性不僅為計量經濟學建模提供必要條件，也為嚴謹的比較案例研究提供了潛在的機會。 這項研究以中國水PPP快速發展為實証依據，對影響水務PPP績效和長期可持續性的決定性因素和內在機制進行系統分析。我們的研究致力於回答下面一些問題。為什麼處於類似的制度環境下，一些水務PPP項目表現不錯，而另一些PPP項目遭致失敗？影響水務PPP成功與失敗的途徑與機制是什麼？ 有哪些因素或內在機制能促進水務PPP的長期可持續性？對於這些問題的回答不僅能推進PPP在提供公共服務方面的理論水平，同時也對在目前中國PPP熱潮中如何保障水務服務的效率和公平性具有實踐意義。

16601217.label: Realisation of objectives
16601217.value: 1. To examine key factors accounting for fast development of PPP in water sector in recent years in China (100%) The first A factor for the rapid development of water PPPs is the central government’s persistent pursuit of PPP policy. The central government has made PPPs a policy priority since the mid-1990s, and has promulgated a range of policies to promote PPP projects. Second, the government has been highly adaptive in their support of PPPs under changing circumstances. In many of China’s successful PPP cases, marketization reforms and water tariff adjustments took place prior to the implementation of PPP. Third, the local governments have been innovative in implementing the national PPP policy via diﬀerent project forms according to their speciﬁc needs and prevailing local conditions. Diﬀerent approaches have been used to tailor the PPP strategy to ﬁt the local context. Fourth, the combination of the top-down approach and local government entrepreneurship ensures that national policy goals are carried out at the local level. The eﬀectiveness of this approach is unsurprising given the governance structure of the Chinese political system. 2. To identify key factors determining the performance of water PPPs and to develop a theoretical understanding of the dynamics of such effects (80%) Comparing with existing research on the topic, our study has identified a number of factors related to the characteristics of the local governments in determining the performance of PPP projects. The first key factor is the incentive structure of local government officials, especially in the face of potential future political shifts. Our analysis shows that a lack of long-term strategic consideration may lead to overinvestment, imprudent investment and the risk of corruption. The second key factor is the coordination among government agencies as Water PPP projects are typically governed by multiple public agencies at different levels of government. Coordination is thus essential in practice. Our case analysis shows that effective coordination between local government officials and central policy makers helped to avoid potential risks, and that the lack of coordination undermined the credibility of the local government. The third factor concerns government officials’ capability. PPPs are long-term relationships between governments and firms, which may expect uncertainties and complications during different stages. For example, when the new policies are in place or policy shocks occur, the capacity of government officials to appropriately adjust, negotiate with different parties and maintain their own credibility is tested. One area for potential improvement is the interactive effects of different factors. We are currently making use of the data collected to conduct QCA analysis to better understand the interactive effects of various factors. 3. To identify multiple pathways to success or failure of water PPPs (90%) There are two distinctive features of the water PPPs in the China. The first is the involvement of government linked companies (GLCs) in water PPPs. Rapid economic development, particularly in large cities like Beijing and Shanghai, has resulted in a large influx of taxes and public money, enabling local governments to establish their own financial vehicles for development projects. As a result, government linked companies (GLCs) have emerged as major investors in water PPP projects in China. Our research finds that investments from GLCs cab offer several potential advantages over typically private sector partners in PPP projects. Our results show that the participation of GLCs in PPP projects improves the performance of water utilities and the quality of their water supply services. Our findings point to a new model for PPP under which the GLCs might be uniquely positioned to tackle several inherent shortcomings of PPPs in water sector. Another key feature is the mechanisms for water tariff adjustment. As an essential good, the accessibility of water is considered as a basic human right for every citizen, the adjustments of water prices are subject to intense scrutiny and often met with strong resistance due to the politically sensitive nature of the water supply. The existing literature shows that low water tariff is among key barrier for the development of PPP in water sector, and failures to water tariff adjustments threaten the sustainability of water PPPs. This research identifies pricing mechanisms and measures to support the development of the water PPPs. We argue that the timing of the water tariff adjustments is not only determined by technical and financial considerations but also takes political factors into account due to the politically sensitive nature of water tariff increases. This study finds that water tariff adjustment in Chinese cities is influenced by the political cycle: local governments are less likely to initiate water tariff adjustments around the political conferences. We also argue that consumers' sense of perceived fairness will affect their acceptance of water tariff increases, and that there would be a high level of resistance to price increase if such adjustment might evoke a sense of injustice. In this research, we study the impact of perceived fairness on WTP for water quality improvement. We find that the perceived fairness has a significant positive impact on residents’ WTP for water quality improvements. One area for potential improvement is with regard to the mechanisms or pathways for failures. There are extremely small number of failed PPP projects reported in recent years, making is difficult to systematically study such mechanisms or pathways. 4. To identify main obstacles for sustaining PPPs in water sector as well as effective policy measures to overcome them (70%) Our research points to several critical institutional constraints that might have significant impact on the sustainability of PPPs based on case study. The first barrier is regulatory uncertainty with regard to central government’s commitment and approach to PPPs. For example, one of the issues in the early periods of the development of water PPPs concerned guaranteed rates of return to foreign investors. In 2002, the General Office of the State Council issued a circular that outlawed guaranteed fixed returns to foreign investors and extended this provision to existing contracts. The implementation of this circular led to a number of cancellations of PPP projects. The second barrier is perverse incentive for key government officials. Due the high level of commitment from the central government, key government officials can extremely zealous to secure PPP projects, because their career advancement was closely linked with the number of PPP projects. However, there might be mismatch between the local needs and PPP models, and the tension will be more pronounced after the initial stage of development of PPP projects. The third barrier is the lack of robust tariff adjustment mechanisms. The political and technical challenges for establishing such mechanisms are often not paid sufficient attention during the project design stages. From the perspective of local government officials, raising the price of water may undermine the accessibility and affordability for low-income residents, and attract media and public attention and discussion, which may bring negative public opinion and might undermine their career prospects. We have studied several measures to overcome these barriers, such as the engagement of government-linked companies in PPPs, the improvement of the governance quality of local government, and various mechanisms to deal with political sensitivity of price increase. But more work can be done in this area in applying the findings of our study.

16601217.label: Major findings and research outcome
16601217.value: Key findings and research outcome of the project are the following: • The key factors accounting for the fast development of PPP in water sector in recent years in China are the persistent pursuit of PPP policy by the central government, the adaptiveness of the government in their support of PPPs under changing circumstances, local government entrepreneurship and the hybrid mode between top-down and bottom-up approaches. • Based on empirical evidence from China, key factors determining the performance of PPP projects include: 1) incentive structure of local government officials in the face of potential future political shifts; 2) the level of coordination among government agencies; and 3) the government officials’ capability. • There are two distinctive features of the water PPPs in the China. The first is the involvement of government linked companies (GLCs) in water PPPs. Our results show that the participation of GLCs in PPP projects improves the performance of water utilities and the quality of their water supply services. Our findings point to a new model for PPP under which the GLCs might be uniquely positioned to tackle several inherent shortcomings of PPPs in water sector. Another key feature is the mechanisms for water tariff adjustment. Our study shows that the timing of the water tariff adjustments is not only determined by technical and financial considerations but also takes political factors into account due to the politically sensitive nature of water tariff increases. We find that the perceived fairness has a significant positive impact on residents’ WTP for water quality improvements. • Our research points to several critical institutional constraints that might have significant impact on the sustainability of PPPs based on case study. The first barrier is regulatory uncertainty with regard to central government’s commitment and approach to PPPs. The second barrier is perverse incentive for key government officials and the third barrier is the lack of robust tariff adjustment mechanisms.

16601217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16601217.value: First of all, one area for further development is to develop theoretical understanding of the dynamics of the key factors determining the performance of water PPPs. The data collected from the project would allow us to conduct QCA to examine the interactive effects of the different factors identified by the research. Second, the decline of the foreign investment in water sector in China provides an opportunity to study the role of the foreign investors in the development of PPPs in water sector. We have collected data on number of water PPPs with foreign investment, and we will conduct case analysis on the performance and dynamics of foreign investment. Third, our research points to several important findings with broad impacts to water sector reform in developing countries, such as the rise of the GLCs in water PPPs and mechanism of water tariff adjustments. More comparative work can be conducted to seek broad application of these findings regionally and globally.

16601217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16601217.value: Given the controversies and challenges involved in water PPPs, government must be consistent in policy design and implementation to pursue the development of PPPs. Such effort is critical to reduce regulatory uncertainty, a barrier for sustainability of PPP projects. Local government entrepreneurship, appropriate incentive structure, coordination among key agencies, and policy capacity are among key factors for driving successful PPPs. The extensive involvement of government linked companies (GLCs) in water PPPs in China provides an opportunity to overcome key challenges for PPPs in water sector due to their stronger financial capability and higher political risk resistance capacity. Reforms such as corporatization of water utilities and water tariff reform have played a key role in China’s rapid development of water PPPs. The public resistance to water tariff increase can be expected, but the politics of water tariff adjustment can be dealt with by considering timing and perceived fairness.

16601817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16601817.value: Intergroup conflict is pervasive. Nowadays, it is not uncommon to see news headlines depicting social unrest, armed conflict between groups, and wars between states or nations in different parts of the world. Given the pervasiveness of intergroup conflict, understanding how to attenuate intergroup bias and conflict is imperative. Existing intervention programs that aim to promote intergroup relations through intergroup contacts are difficult to implement because the ideal contact situations that are required for intervention success (e.g., the possession of equal status, the need for personalized contact) are often difficult to achieve. Other intervention programs that attempt to reshape personal values and beliefs directly (e.g., multicultural education and diversity training) are often met with reactivity (see Stephan & Stephan, 2008). Recognizing the importance of managing intergroup relations and the limitations of the existing approach to conflict reduction, the proposed research addresses this issue by examining the effects of wise reasoning and its associated psychological mechanisms on intergroup biases and conflict reconciliation. Although the term “wise reasoning” has not been used explicitly until recent years (see Grossmann et al., 2010; Kross & Grossmann, 2012), scholars have made reference to and pointed out the importance of the various concepts related to wise reasoning in the conflict management literature and intergroup literature indirectly (e.g., Ury, 1993; Galinsky, Maddux, Gilin, & White, 2008). Wise reasoning is a form of pragmatic reasoning processes that helps people resolve challenges (Grossmann et al., 2010). It involves the awareness that the world is in flux, that there are uncertainties in life, that people hold different values and goals, and that compromise of differences is possible by looking at the big picture (see Baltes & Smith, 2008; Basseches, 1980). It can be assessed as an individual difference and can also be shaped through intervention. This proposal provides a novel perspective for understanding and managing intergroup relations. Findings from pilot studies that provide preliminary support to the proposed framework are presented. This proposal presents an integrative and systematic framework to examine the effects of wise reasoning on intergroup relations. It contributes to both the intergroup relations literature and the conflict management literature theoretically and empirically. Furthermore, by integrating the wise reasoning intervention framework into education and training, the proposed research has important practical implications. 族群間的衝突是普遍的，現今社會中，我們常常看到頭條新聞描述著各種社會動亂、不同群體之間的武裝衝突和國與國之間的戰爭。考慮到族群衝突的普遍性，去了解怎樣可以減低族群間偏見和衝突實在刻不容緩。現有的介入計劃之目的是透過增加族群之間的接觸以改善關係，然而這些介入方法往往難以實行；因為需要有特定的環境和條件才能達到治療效果（例如雙方必須有同等的地位，並需要有個人化的接觸），而這些情境卻很難出現。其他介入計劃嘗試直接從塑個人價值觀及信念（例如多元文化教育及多元化訓練），卻往往使人不悅和反感（見 Stephan & Stephan, 2008）。 由於現有的介入方式皆有其限制，為解決族群間的衝突問題，本研究著眼於『智心思維』及其伴隨的心理機制對群際衝突和處理方法的影響。智心思維這個詞彙，於近年才被明確地使用（見 Grossmann et al., 2010; Kross & Grossmann, 2012），但事實上在此之前，學者已經有在衝突管理及群際關係的文獻中指出與智心思維相關的概念之重要性（如Ury, 1993; Galinsky, Maddux, Gilin, & White, 2008）。智心思維是幫助人們解決困難的一種務實推理方法（見Grossmann et al., 2010），它包含了：意識到世界是不斷地轉變，生活中有不明確的因素，知道不同的人都有其價值觀和目標，和透過考量大局去協商差異（見Baltes & Smith, 2008; Basseches, 1980）。智心思維可以視為個人差異去量度，也可以透過介入方式去改變，這個研究提供了一個理解和處理群際關係的全新觀點。先導性研究的成果也為這個理論框架提供了初步支持。 這個研究提供了一個整合性及系統性的架構，用以驗證智心思維對族群間關係的影響，為群際關係及衝突管理的文獻帶來了理論及實證上的貢獻。此外，本研究把智心思維的介入架構整合於教育及訓練當中，對實際應用也起著重要的意義。

16602117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16602117.value: 該項研究將基於三個歷史大數據庫，清代縉紳錄數據庫（約500000名官員）、民國中國大學生數據庫（約110000名學生）、中華人民共和國重點大學學生數據庫（約150000名學生），比較在四個不同時期中國考試精英的社會來源和地理來源。這四個時期包括清代洋務運動時期（1865-1900年）、清末新政時期（1900-1911年）、民國時期（1912-1949年）、共和國時期（1949-2014年）。初步分析表明，考試精英的社會及地理來源在每個歷史階段有著明顯的差異。我們的項目旨在研究這種多樣性和流動性的來源，以期更好地理解中國一個半世紀以來，相較於其他地區，考試精英的可變性和異質性。 本項目將比較和連接每個歷史階段的個人和他們的親屬，由此分析每一個新時期考試精英是否來自全新的家庭。除此之外，我們不僅會考察父子叔侄關係，還會跨越多代關注其他親屬關係。這樣一來可以更加全面地理解中國從帝國到民國再到當代的社會轉型，二來可以追蹤多代教育精英的轉變和延續。
