17106117.value: 這是世界上第一個隨機對照研究，用於評估木糖醇和氟化物牙膏在社區環境中預防有中度及高蛀牙風險的嬰幼兒的蛀牙的有效性。 該項目將持續3年。 蛀牙是世界上兒童最常見的問題之一。 這疾病不僅影響兒童的整體健康和生活質量，同時也對社會的醫療保健系統造成負擔。 儘管我們在促進口腔健康和教育方面已作出了大量的努力，但在香港，仍有超過一半以上的五歲兒童患有蛀牙，其中超過百分之九十更沒有接受任何治療。 過去十年，香港和其他國家的學前兒童蛀牙的程度更甚至有所增加。 蛀牙是可以預防的。 應該探索和建立新的口腔健康預防策略，以應對目前蛀牙這問題的全球危機。 我們制定了一套根據蛀牙風險去預防及處理學前兒童蛀牙的臨床實證指引（CPG），讓專業人士和一般民眾使用。 有證據顯示，根據蛀牙風險來預防蛀牙的措施應該在嬰孩六個月大時實施。 預防性的牙齒檢查也應及早進行。 研究也證實只有含至少1000 ppm氟化物的牙膏才能防止蛀牙。 然而，高濃度的氟化物可能會產生氟中毒的問題，特別是在幼兒和已有水氟化的區域當中。 有建議使用含有木糖醇牙膏作為替代品，但其預防蛀牙的有效性尚未確定。 在香港，嬰幼兒從出生至1歲半期間會在母嬰健康院（MCHC）按照「香港兒童免疫接種計劃」得到免費的免疫接種服務。在這項研究中，嬰幼兒會在六個月和十二個月在母嬰健康院接種疫苗時，會由非牙科專業人士替他們進行蛀牙風險評估。被確定有中度及高蛀牙風險的嬰幼兒將被邀請參加這項計劃。家長/照顧者將接受按蛀牙風險預防蛀牙的在家指導，當中包括根據蛀牙風險去預防及處理學前兒童蛀牙的臨床實證指引（一般民眾使用版）、飲食建議和口腔衛生指導。參加計劃的嬰幼兒將隨機分配到i）木糖醇（25％）（試驗）或ii）氟化物（1000ppm F）（對照）牙膏組。家長/照顧者將每天使用牙膏兩次。牙膏將每6個月郵寄給參加者。他們使用牙膏的情況將被定期監測。結果將通過家長/照顧者的問卷調查和嬰幼兒在1歲、2歲和3歲的臨床口腔檢查進行評估。嬰幼兒的口腔健康主要結果將會是蛀牙數目的增加、牙周健康和口腔微生物群落的變化。次要結果將會是家長/照顧者口腔健康知識的改變、對牙科保健的態度和對護理人員建議的口腔健康相關習慣的遵守。 在母嬰健康院（MCHC）進行基於實證按照蛀牙風險去預防及處理學前兒童蛀牙的方法是切實可行的，並且可以改善幼兒的口腔健康狀況。 建立良好的口腔健康習慣有助保障兒童的長遠福祉。 這研究可以提供木糖醇牙膏在預防蛀牙的有效性和兒童使用含高濃度氟化物牙膏的風險的證據。 長遠而言，研究結果可有作為香港及其以外地區建立有效口腔保健推廣計劃的基礎。 該框架如果有效，更可以在其他地區中使用，幫助世界的小孩達到更好的口腔健康。

17106617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17106617.value: Background: Influenza viruses circulate worldwide causing epidemics every year in every country. In temperate locations such as the United States, Europe and northern China, epidemics typically occur in the winter months, while seasonality is less regular in subtropical areas such as Hong Kong and southern China, or in tropical areas. Influenza vaccine is the most effective intervention in protecting susceptible population against infection, and currently all countries initiate annual vaccination in autumn before a typical winter season starts. Given the varied patterns of virus circulation and substantial influenza-associated disease burden observed worldwide, it is of great importance to study optimal influenza vaccination strategies particularly in subtropical and tropical areas with irregular influenza seasonality. Purpose: Our study has two objectives. 1: To characterize the seasonality of influenza virus epidemics in Hong Kong and in different regions of mainland China in the post-pandemic period, and identify changes from seasonality in the pre-pandemic period. 2: To determine the optimal timing and frequency of influenza vaccination in Hong Kong and different regions of mainland China. Methods: We apply a mathematical model to fit territory-wide influenza surveillance data and longitudinal population-based serologic data to investigate influenza virus transmission dynamics for each type/subtype of virus in different age groups of population at the same time allowing for seasonal force of transmission driven by environmental factors in the model. The established model is used to examine impact of various community-based vaccination strategies on prevention of influenza transmission in the population. Potential implications: The proposed model incorporates current knowledge and uncertainties on influenza transmission, protective immunity and potential virus interaction. An improved understanding of driving forces of influenza seasonality would inform the optimal timing of vaccination campaigns in Hong Kong and different areas of mainland China. Research findings from our project would have broader scientific value by informing influenza seasonality and vaccination policy globally. 研究背景：流感病毒每年在全世界廣泛流行並導致流感爆發。在溫帶氣候國家，譬如美國，歐洲和中國北方地區，流感爆發通常發生在冬季；而像香港和華南一帶的亞熱帶地區或熱帶地區，流感的季節性卻不甚明顯。流感疫苗是保護易感人群的最有效方法。目前全世界所有實施流感接種計劃的國家都在每年冬季流感季節開始之前的秋季啟動接種計劃。因為流感在全球範圍引致很高的疾病負擔而且流感病毒在各地區的流行趨勢並不相同，因此研究流感疫苗的優化策略，特別是在無明顯流感季節性的熱帶及亞熱帶地區，是極其重要的研究課題。 研究目的：本研究將實現以下兩個目標：1.研究香港及大陸不同地區2009年流感大流行后流感病毒爆發的季節性，以及與流感大流行前季節性的比較；2.探究和優化香港和大陸不同地區的流感疫苗接種計劃。 研究方法：我們將利用數學模型擬合不同地區收集的流感監測數據和血清學數據，以研究在不同年齡人群中各型/亞型流感病毒的傳播動力學。在模型中，我們將會納入由環境因素主導的季節性病毒傳播力。最終確定的模型將會用於研究不同的流感疫苗接種計劃對預防流感在人群中傳播的影響。 研究意義：此項研究中模型的構建將基於目前關於流感傳播，保護性免疫力以及病毒間潛在相互作用的已有知識。我們的研究將提升對流感季節性驅動因子的認識，將有助於優化香港和中國大陸不同地區的流感疫苗接種計劃。本研究對全球流感季節性和疫苗接種政策的研究也將產生影響。

17106617.label: Major findings and research outcome
17106617.value: We used weekly surveillance data on influenza virus activity in mainland China and Hong Kong from 2005 through 2016. We found that absolute humidity is a potential driver of influenza seasonality and had a U-shaped association with transmissibility across different climate zones. Absolute humidity was able to explain 4% to 15% of the variance in R_t, and was a stronger predictor of R_t in the subtropical locations. Mean daily temperature explained 3% to 13% of variance in R_t and was a stronger predictor of R_t in the temperate locations with higher latitude. In simulations of the optimal timing of influenza vaccination in Hong Kong, annual vaccination initiated in December results in lower number of influenza-associated respiratory deaths (452, 95% CI: 392, 512) and excess respiratory hospitalizations (6,888, 95% CI: 5,682, 8,116) compared with vaccination strategies in other months of a year. Based on seasonality in different parts of China, subtropical areas of China should also consider delaying annual vaccination until December.

17106617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17106617.value: In further research, we would like to investigate whether the same relationship between environmental factors and influenza transmission occur in other parts of south-east Asia.

17106617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17106617.value: Influenza epidemics occur every winter in temperate locations in the northern and southern hemisphere, while in Hong Kong we also have epidemics in the spring or summer. We do not fully understand the reasons for this seasonal pattern in influenza activity. In this study we examined data from Hong Kong and mainland China, and determined that temperate and absolute humidity do seem to affect influenza transmission, with influenza preferring to spread either when it is cool and dry or when it is very hot and humid. Because influenza rarely spreads in Hong Kong in November and December, we found evidence to suggest that the best time to receive annual influenza vaccination could be December each year. This is a little bit later than the current vaccination campaign which takes place in October and November.

17106917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17106917.value: 多種X連鎖基因（如LAMP2，DMD和GLA）的突變已証實能導致心肌病變。 基於不同的病理機制，X連鎖疾病的遺傳模式可為顯性或隱性。儘管如此，與常染色體病症不同，X連鎖基因病變的外顯率可能因X染色體失活模式不同而有很大變化。因此,X連鎖顯性突變的女性攜帶者通常較遲發病。相反，攜帶X連鎖隱性突變的雜合女性也可能發病。迄今為止，由於缺乏廣泛及臨床相關的疾病建模和藥物開發模型，大多數X連鎖心肌病都沒有有效的治療方法。 我們最近從具有嚴重心肌病的雜合女性患者中分製出具有獨特X染色體失活狀態的誘導性多功能幹細胞(iPSCs)，並將其分化為心肌細胞，以模擬與LAMP2缺乏症狀相關的自噬功能失調。 使用這種建於iPSC的模型，我們首次證明了沉默的X染色體（Xi-染色體）上的野生型LAMP2等位基因可以被DNA去甲基化劑（5-氮雜-2'-脫氧胞苷）再活化， 從而改善與Danon病相關的心臟功能障礙。 攜帶野生型等位基因的染色體的重新激活雖然被視作一種針對X連鎖疾病中新興的治療方法、但由於大多數X連鎖疾病均是罕見的，並且在決乏沒廣泛的基於人類細胞的模型的情況下，染色體重新激活藥物的研發在技術上仍然非常困難。 我們假設我們建立的具有不同X染色體失活狀態的iPSC細胞可作為一個平台，以評估現有藥物的治療效果，並篩選出針對不同X連鎖心肌病的新型染色體復甦藥物。 我們將首先評估並比較現有DNA脫甲基化劑對LAMP2缺缺乏症的治療功效和潛在的細胞毒性。我們將根據初歩獲得的結果進一步評估相關的X連鎖疾病模型。 我們的研究亦將評估將iPSC平台擴展到更大規模的藥物篩選系統的可能性。這項研究的結果預計將為X染色體重新激活對不同X連鎖心肌病和其他X連鎖疾病如Rett綜合徵的臨床應用提供重要的見解。

17108217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17108217.value: Being active and eating properly are vital for good health. Recent studies have demonstrated that time spent outdoors has additional health benefits, including increased physical activity, improved sleep, better eating habits and decreased stress levels. Despite this, most existing child health promotion programmes concentrate solely on physical movement and diet. None, to our knowledge, consider time spent outdoors, referred to as ‘connectedness to nature’ in what is an emerging research area. The latest research indicates that most Hong Kong pre-schoolers move considerably less than experts advise and are becoming progressively more sedentary, which puts them at risk of becoming overweight. We propose a Play & Grow programme for pre-schoolers (aged 2 to 4 years old) and their families that tests whether connectedness to nature (CN) impacts pre-schoolers’ physical activity and dietary habits. We utilise the best available interventions for pre-schoolers and include CN as a novel third component to the programme. Play & Grow (P&G) is a 10-session family-based, multi-component healthy lifestyle programme for families with preschool children aged 2 to 4. It was developed and tested in a pilot study (n=38) by the PI and her team (accepted for publication in Pediatric Reserach). The pilot study confirmed the design, protocols and logistics of the study. To further test the programme, we plan to run a randomised controlled trial (RCT) targeting 240 families with children aged 2 to 4 years old. Participating families will take part in a 45-minute structured session once a week for 10 weeks, followed by additional programme information (games and activity suggestions) for another 4 weeks. The sessions will include: guided active play involving both children and caregivers; interactive education and skill development for caregivers; simultaneous supervised active play with foods for children to promote acceptance of vegetables, and guided active nature games outdoors involving both children and parents. Healthy lifestyle surveys will be conducted before the programme begins, at completion, and at 6 and 12 months after completion of the programme. To measure CN in pre-schoolers, we will validate a new instrument: the Nature Relatedness Scale (NRS). The objectives of this proposal will be accomplished over a 36-month time frame. Analysis of the RCT is expected to contribute evidence for connectedness to nature as one of the key components of a successful early childhood healthy lifestyle promotion programme resulting in sustainable and enduring lifestyle changes. 17108417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17108417.value: The long-term enzootic Asian highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5 virus lineage has caused repeated outbreaks in poultry and sporadic human infections, which makes this virus one of the major concerns for pandemic threats. The most recent variants of this lineage, clade 2.3.4.4 viruses, have evolved into multiple subgroups, and disseminated into many Eurasian countries and even, for the first time, to North America. In China these variants have become predominant and responsible for most of the reported H5 human infections since 2014. Our investigation demonstrated that the clade 2.3.4.4 H5N6 viruses recently isolated from humans had an increased transmissibility in ferrets in comparison with other H5Nx viruses tested, and one of them was even airborne transmissible among ferrets. The viruses from different subgroups of clade 2.3.4.4 show heterogeneous pathogenicity and transmissibility in mammalian models. However, the molecular bases associated with these phenotypic changes are still unknown. Our ongoing influenza surveillance in mainland China has accumulated Asian HPAI H5 viruses from almost all clades or sublineages, including the precursors and descendent viruses of clade 2.3.4.4. In this proposal, we would first conduct systematic genetic analysis of the recent H5 isolates to understand the evolutionary dynamics of the clade 2.3.4.4 viruses, and to identify the possible adaptive residues that may be associated with the altered host range and transmissibility in mammals. Combined with the use of reverse genetic technique and animal infection studies, we would explore the mechanisms leading to the increased transmissibility of the H5 viruses in mammals. The findings generated in this proposal will enhance our understanding and provide insights into how avian influenza viruses evolve to increase their infectivity and transmissibility in mammalian systems, which may also apply to humans and so directly benefit pandemic prediction and preparedness. 高致病性禽流感（HPAI）H5病毒譜系在亞洲的長期流行，不斷引起家禽的反复爆發和人類的零星感染。這使得該病毒業已成為大流行威脅的主要問題之一。近年來，該譜系的最新變種2.3.4.4型病毒已經演變成多個亞組，並且陸續擴散到許多歐亞國家，甚至在歷史上第一次傳播到了北美。在中國，自2014年以來，這些變種已成為H5人類感染報導病例中最主要的致病原因。 我們的前期研究結果表明，與其他平行測試的H5Nx病毒相比，最近從病人身上分離出的2.3.4.4 型H5N6病毒，在雪貂動物模型中具有較高的傳播率，其中一株甚至可以空氣傳播。來自不同亞組的2.3.4.4型病毒在哺乳動物模型中顯示出不同的致病性和傳播性。然而，與這些表型變化相關的分子基礎仍然是未知的。 本研究組在中國內地持續進行的流感監測已經累積了幾乎所有進化分支或亞系的亞洲HPAI H5病毒，包括2.3.4.4進化分支的前體和後代病毒。本項目計劃首先將對最近分離的H5病毒株進行系統的遺傳分析，以了解2.3.4.4病毒的進化情況，並確定可能與哺乳動物宿主範圍和傳播能力有關的潛在適應性殘基。然後結合反向遺傳技術和動物感染實驗，探討H5病毒在哺乳動物中傳播能力提高的機制。預期本項目的結果將有助於提高我們對禽流感病毒的理解和認識，並提供有關這類病毒如何演變以增加人類感染性和傳播性的新見解，從而直接有助於大流行流感的預測和準備。

17108417.label: Realisation of objectives
17108417.value: < Objective 1 > To understand the evolution and genesis of the clade 2.3.4.4 H5N6 virus and to identify the consensus genetic changes possibly associated with the human infection cases, we have sequenced the whole genomes of over 2,244 avian H5N6 viruses isolated in Southern China during 2017-2021, and analyzed them with the downloaded sequences of 10,705 H5 viruses from the public databases of GenBank and GISAID. Phylogenetic analysis identified 5 major groups (A-E) of H5 viruses in clade 2.3.4.4, which were all found in China or the neighboring Asian countries since 2010. Two waves of intercontinental transmissions have occurred, one by group C (A/Duck/Korea/Buan2/2014-like) viruses since late 2013 and another by group B (A/duck/Korea/Gochang1/2014 [Gochang1]-like) from 2016 onwards. Group C viruses spread from Asia to North America and Europe, while group B spread to the Middle East, Egypt and Europe. Groups A, C and D were majorly reported in Asia, especially China. In addition to being geographically widespread, clade 2.3.4.4 H5 viruses have reassorted with the local gene pool viruses to obtain different NA subtypes and the internal genes. In China, H5N6 has become the predominant H5Nx subtypes since 2013, replacing the previously established H5N1 viruses. They also acquired genes from wild bird viruses and from clade 2.3.2.1c H5N1, H9N2 and H6N6 viruses, causing infections in poultry and mammals (swine, felines and humans). Notably, the Asian 2.3.4.4 H5Nx viruses were much more genotypically diverse than those from the other continents; and the vast majority of human infection cases were H5N6 reported by China. Increasing human and mammalian infections seemed to be associated with the novel genetic composition of the 2.3.4.4 H5N6 variants, including NA from H6N6 duck virus and internal genes from Y280-like H9N2 chicken viruses. < Objective 2 > To investigate which group of 2.3.4.4 H5Nx virus may pose more risks to mammals, and if the complete internal gene cassette (IGC) from the ZJ/HJ-like H9N2 virus lineage could enhance the infectivity and transmissibility of clade 2.3.4.4 H5 viruses in mammals, we first selected 9 representative viruses and characterized them in the mouse and ferret models. We found that in mice, traditional H5Nx viruses from groups 2.3.4.4-B and E (MLD50: 3.3-3.6) exhibited much higher pathogenicity than those from groups A, C and D (MLD50: 4.9-6.6). Strikingly, all three strains of group 2.3.4.4-D H5N6 virus with ZJ-HJ-like H9N2 IGCs (i.e. A/Shenzhen/SP373/2015 [SZ373], A/Shenzhen/SP378/2016 [SZ378] and A/Shenzhen/SP389/2016 [SZ389]) shown even higher pathogenicity, with their MLD50 as 2.63, 1.38 and 2, respectively. In ferrets, SZ378, SZ389 and a 2.3.4.3-E virus caused death in most infected ferrets, SZ373 and a closely related 2.3.4.4-D virus (A/chicken/Shenzhen/433/2013 [SZ433]) caused one death out of the 9 ferrets, while the other viruses were not lethal. Moreover, SZ378 was transmissible either by airborne exposure or close contact, while SZ389, SZ373, and the group E virus only shown limited transmission by direct contact. None of the other tested viruses were transmissible, including SZ433. In general, clade 2.3.4.4 H5Nx viruses were readily infectious in mice and ferrets, but H5N6 viruses with the H9N2-like IGC shown enhanced virulence and transmissibility. Of all the H5Nx viruses tested, SZ378 was the most virulent in mammals. To confirm this, we have reconstructed the parental SZ373, SZ378, and SZ433 viruses (RG1-3) using reverse genetic techniques. We then exchanged their IGCs and generated 6 reassortant viruses (RG4-9). Interestingly, acquisition of the H9N2-like IGC from SZ378 or SZ373 significantly enhanced the virus pathogenicity and transmissibility in both animal models. On the contrary, introduction of the SZ373- or SZ433-like IGC to SZ378 completely diminished its airborne transmissibility, and dramatically reduced its contact transmissibility in ferrets. In mice, the IGC from SZ433 impaired the virulence. Therefore, the ZJ/HJ-like H9N2-like IGC played an important role in the interspecies transmission of H5N6 to mammals. Additionally, the surface genes (HA+NA) of SZ378 contributed to the virus replication and transmission more than that of the SZ373 did, and SZ373 was better than SZ433. < Objective 3> To identify the individual gene segment or segments that contribute to the increased mammalian infectivity and transmissibility of H5N6 virus, we first reconstructed 6 reassortant viruses (RG10-15), exchanging their RNP gene complex amongst the SZ373, SZ378, and SZ433 viruses. We found that exchanging the RNP complex between SZ373 and SZ433 did not significantly change the virus pathogenicity in mice, but once obtaining the SZ378-like RNP complex, the H5 virus would show drastically enhanced virulence, and vice versa. Analysis on RNP activities between the different gene combinations (SZ433 vs SZ378; SZ373 vs SZ378; and SZ433 vs SZ373; overall n=48) using the minigenome assays found that the PB2 gene of SZ378 was the key determinant for the polymerase activity, and the PB1 gene of SZ373 also contributed to the RNP activity. The SZ373- or SZ378-like PB2 could synergistically enhance the function of SZ373-like PB1. Next, we reconstructed 16 reassortant viruses (RG10-25), which contained single segment replacement between the SZ433 and SZ373 viruses, and compared their virulence with those of RG1-9 viruses. Consistently, the H9N2-like PB2 and PB1 gene from SZ373 enhanced the virus pathogenicity in mice, while those of SZ433 decreased it. Obtaining the SZ373-like HA or NP gene could significantly increase the viral virulence. SZ373-like NA alone could slightly but not significantly enhance the virulence, but when combined with the SZ373-like HA, the enhancement would be more prominent than introducing the HA gene alone. When the PB2 gene of SZ378 was introduced into the SZ433 or SZ373, the virus shown higher virulence by causing more body weight loss and deaths in mice. Therefore, the internal genes, especially the PB2 gene of SZ378, played a vital role for the virus virulence in mammals. < Objective 4 > To identify the critical point mutations that have naturally occurred in the airborne transmissible human H5N6 isolate and confirm if they will enhance the infectivity and transmissibility of the H5 variants in mammals, we reconstructed recombinant viruses carrying single mutations in PB2, PB1 or HA gene. Unfortunately, we only found that PB2-E627K substitution was significant enough to change the virus virulence in mice and the transmissions in ferrets in the genetic context of SZ378. As the wildtype SZ378 contained the PB2-627K, mutation to E at this position abolished the virus transmission via airborne exposure, and reduced the physical contact transmissibility from all three ferrets to two of the three. Replacement of the PB2-627E with a K in the SZ373 virus was not sufficient to change the virus pathogenicity or transmissibility in ferrets. Therefore, the PB2-627K was essential to maintain the virulence of SZ378 in mammals, but when acting alone, it shown little effect on SZ373. Cooperation of the other residues was necessary in the genetic context of SZ373.

17108417.label: Major findings and research outcome
17108417.value: We have published a few related articles on the detection of Asian highly pathogenic H5Nx viruses, or the use of ferret model in the study of virus pathogenicity and transmissibility (see Part C). Another two major manuscripts on the molecular determinants of H5N6 viruses were under preparations. PI and the team members have attended multiple international conferences and gave presentations. They received several highly prestigious and competitive awards related to the control and prevention of avian influenza, especially the highly pathogenic H5 viruses. Over 30 research postgraduate students were trained at The University of Hong Kong or the collaborative base at Shantou University. Four students have graduated with their thesis work related to this H5 project. Details were given in Part C. Additionally, from 2018-2022, we have attended 9 biannual meetings held by the World Health Organisation (WHO) for consultation on the composition of H5 influenza virus vaccines for the Southern and Northern Hemispheres. We shared our surveillance data on the antigenic and genetic characteristics of zoonotic H5 influenza viruses and recommended candidate vaccine viruses to the WHO. Reports were available on the WHO website. Based on the results obtained from this study, we also helped WHO to conduct risk assessments on the 2.3.4.4 H5Nx viruses.

17108417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17108417.value: We have revealed the evolution and genetic diversity of the clade 2.3.4.4 H5Nx virus and identified the viral gene segments and some residues that may contribute to the interspecies transmission of H5N6 to humans and the enhanced infectivity, pathogenicity and transmissibility in mammals. Further investigation will be more focused on how these genes or residues would interact with the host factors and immune responses to lead to the overall pathogenesis and transmissibility. Continuous evolution of this virus lineage will also be followed up.

17108417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17108417.value: Since its emergence in 1996, the Asian H5Nx highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) virus has long been a continuous threat to agriculture and public health. In the past decade, the clade 2.3.4.4 has become dominant and diverged into at least five groups, spreading globally and causing repeated outbreaks in poultry and mammals. Reassortment with the local gene pool viruses have generated viruses with different NA subtypes and internal gene complexes. Notably, most human infection cases were caused by H5N6 subtype reported in China since 2014. Here we found that the H9N2 internal gene cassette that contributed to the genesis of H7N9 and H10N8 in China also improved the infectivity and transmissibility of clade 2.3.4.4 H5N6 viruses in mammals. Some strains with the H9N2 internal genes could be readily transmitted in ferrets via close contact or even airborne exposure. PB2 and PB1 played an important role in enhancing the viral polymerase activity and the virulence in the mouse and ferret models. PB2-627 served as one of the key amino acids for the viral virulence, but cooperation of the different genes or substitutions was essential to maintain the virus pathogenicity and transmissibility in mammals.

17108717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17108717.value: Background: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is a common childhood disorder characterised by symptoms of hyperactivity, inattention and impulsivity. Methylphenidate (MPH) is the most commonly used medication in ADHD when pharmacological treatment is considered appropriate. The use of ADHD medications in Hong Kong (HK) increased 14-fold from 2001-2013, with about 1% of children aged under 19 in the general population on ADHD medication in 2013. Although MPH is a useful drug for ADHD treatment, there is long-standing concern that this stimulant therapy may lower the seizure threshold and increase the risk of seizure and seizure-related morbidities. Clearly, there is a need to know more about the benefits and adverse effects of ADHD medication. Objectives: In addition to providing reliable incidence estimates of seizure during MPH treatment in HK, the proposed study will examine the association between MPH use and seizure, both incident and recurrent, to investigate the safety of this increasingly used medication. The study will also investigate the drug interaction effect of MPH and other psychotropic medications on the risk of seizure. Study Design: The underlying risks of seizure amongst MPH users and non-users are likely to differ owing to ADHD and its comorbidities, which are difficult to control in many observational study designs. Therefore, we will adopt a self-controlled case series design in which participants act as their own controls. This design allows all time-invariant confounders that vary between individuals, such as genetic factors, socioeconomic status and the severity of underlying diseases, to be controlled. The rate of events during periods of MPH exposure and non-exposure will be compared within individual patients. Study Contributions: The proposed study will be the first in a Chinese ADHD population to examine the relationship between MPH exposure and seizure, and will expand our knowledge of that link and the safety of this commonly used medication. The incidence of seizure in MPH users estimated in this study will inform treatment strategy and service planning. 17109417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17109417.value: The dynamics of evolutionary diversification are the result of an interplay between disparate facets of the biology, ecology and geographical distribution of species. Robust, well-sampled molecular phylogenies have the potential to allow these interconnected factors to be teased apart, allowing an assessment of the degree to which individual elements have contributed as evolutionary drivers. The proposed project focuses on the early-divergent flowering plant family Annonaceae, which forms an important component of many tropical lowland forest ecosystems. We aim to reconstruct the phylogeny of the species-rich lianescent genus Artabotrys (c. 100 species) based on extensive taxon sampling and a broad range of chloroplast and nuclear DNA markers. Preliminary results indicate that early diversification in the genus resulted in sister lineages that are markedly asymmetrical in species numbers: the main species-rich Artabotrys clade, characterised by flowers with basally strongly concave petals that form a tightly enclosed pollination chamber, has undergone considerable evolutionary diversification relative to the species-poor early-divergent grade. We hypothesise that the floral chamber may function as a pollinator trap, with the pollinators attracted by floral scents and initially provided with a nutritive reward, but with the pollinators subsequently prevented from leaving the flowers by the ‘rat trap’ closure of the chamber. This pollinator trapping mechanism is likely to increase pollination efficiency by increasing pollen loading on pollinators, promoting effective interfloral movement of pollinators, and increasing seed-set by enabling more rapid turn-over of flowers, thereby driving evolutionary diversification. A detailed morpho-anatomical study of the genus will be undertaken, providing insight into morphological synapomorphies; particular attention will be directed to floral morphology, with pollination ecology studies of exemplar species, involving assessments of floral phenology, thermogenesis, scent chemistry, pollinator identity, pollinator circadian rhythms, and plant breeding system. We will also use the molecular phylogeny to develop biogeographical hypotheses using evolutionary divergence age estimations and ancestral area reconstructions. Previous research indicates that the genus originated in Africa, with dispersal into Asia during the late Middle Miocene thermal maximum (17–15 Ma). We will use ecological niche models for extant Artabotrys species to generate phyloclimatic models for internal nodes in the phylogeny, thereby enabling an assessment of whether the lineages that dispersed into Asia were ancestrally better adapted to seasonally dry habitats. The impact of potential morphological key evolutionary innovations and founder biogeographical events as possible drivers of accelerated evolution in Artabotrys will be assessed using several contrasting analytical approaches that have recently been developed. 動態演化是物種的生物，生態，地理分佈等不同方面的因素共同作用的結果。 解析度和取樣量優良的分子系統進化樹具有梳理這些複雜因素的潛力，可以評估其中單獨某個因素作為進化推動力的貢獻程度。本專案以原始開花植物番荔枝科作為研究物件。這個類群是熱帶低地森林生態系統的重要組成部分。我們將選取鷹爪花屬來構建分子系統發育樹。鷹爪花屬植物是一類種類繁多的木質藤本，約100個物種。系統發育構建將基於大量的樣品採集和多個葉綠體和核基因片段。初步研究結果顯示該屬植物的早期分化形成的姐妹分支在物種數目上具有明顯的不對稱性：物種數目較多的一個大分支，具有花瓣基部凹陷的特點，並形成一個緊密閉合的傳粉室。和物種數目較少的基部分支相比，這個大分支經歷了較強的物種多樣化進化過程。我們假設傳粉室可能作為陷阱功能，開花初期產生花香味吸引傳粉者並為其提供營養回報，後期植物通過控制花室閉合形成陷阱，阻止傳粉者離開。這種陷阱傳粉機制可以提高傳粉效率，增加昆蟲身上的花粉負載量，提高有效的訪花運動，加快開花批次和種子結實，從而推動進化多樣化進程。我們將會對鷹爪花植物開展詳細的形態-解剖學研究，以助於理解形態上的共同衍征；重點關注花形態，選取一些有代表的種進行傳粉生態學研究，將會涉及到開花物候，花部產熱，花香味化學成分，傳粉者鑒定，傳粉者晝夜活動節律，繁育系統等方面的分析。我們也將運用分子系統框架估算物種分化時間，重建古老分佈區，從而探討生物地理方面的相關假說。早期研究指出該屬植物起源於非洲，在中新世中期至後期(15-17百萬年前) 遷移到亞洲。我們將會對現存的鷹爪花屬植物開展生態位元模型研究，根據系統樹內部節點的氣候模型評估該類群在遷移至亞洲的古老時期是否對季風性乾旱生境有更好的適應性。關鍵的進化創新性形態特徵和生物地理學奠基者事件對鷹爪花屬加速進化的潛在影響也將運用近來新起的對比分析方法來進行評估。

17109417.label: Major findings and research outcome
17109417.value: The phylogeny of Artabotrys was reconstructed based on 53 species (ca. 51% of species diversity), and four chloroplast and 10 nuclear DNA regions, using maximum likelihood, maximum parsimony and Bayesian analyses. The results indicate that Artabotrys is unequivocally monophyletic, with a species-rich main Artabotrys clade (MAC) comprising distinct African and Asian sister clades, and an early divergent grade (EDG) comprising two African species. Molecular divergence time estimation using a relaxed clock model and ancestral area and habitat reconstructions were performed to elucidate spatio-temporal diversification patterns. An ancestral range in Africa was inferred, with a single dispersal event to Asia. The most plausible explanation for the palaeotropical intercontinental disjunction involves overland migration across Arabia in the Miocene, prior to subsequent climate deterioration. The Late Miocene colonisation of Madagascar postdates the period conducive to rafting of vegetation mats from Africa to Madagascar. Dispersal across Wallace’s line occurred twice from the Late Miocene, when marine gaps diminished following convergence of the Sunda and Sahul shelves. Climatic niche conservatism is an underlying pattern in Artabotrys, with local niche shifts occurring rather recently. Considerable variation in habitat and fruit and seed morphology in Artabotrys renders the genus ideal for evaluating correlated evolution between seed functional traits and various ecological correlates. The relationships between functional traits and ecological correlates were examined using phylogenetic regression. The hypothesis that testa thickness and seed volume evolved towards distinct optima in lineages with different dispersal-related traits and precipitation regime was furthermore tested using model-fitting approaches. The two distinct trait optima inferred may correspond with two seed dispersal modes in Artabotrys: lineages with smooth testa and thin pericarp have evolved a thinner testa and smaller seeds, potentially reflecting dispersal by birds and primates with seed-spitting and seed-swallowing habits, whereas lineages with other combinations of testa texture and pericarp thickness have evolved a thicker testa and larger seeds, potentially reflecting dispersal by primates with more destructive mastication behaviour. Comparative field studies on floral phenology and pollination ecology were undertaken in two exemplar species, viz. A. blumei (MAC) and A. brachypetalus (EDG). The aberrant floral morphology of A. brachypetalus is associated with a generalist pollination system and the absence of a pollinator trapping mechanism. The firmly enclosed floral chamber is likely to be apomorphic for the MAC and associated with circadian pollinator trapping.

17109417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17109417.value: Our research has contributed to an understanding of the biotic and abiotic evolutionary drivers in early divergent flowering plants. This knowledge can now be transferred to other early divergent lineages: the knowledge gained on the frugivore-mediated selection of fleshy fruits is likely to be invaluable in other tropical fleshy-fruited lineages.

17109417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17109417.value: Evolutionary diversification is influenced by the biology, ecology and geographical distribution of species. This project used DNA sequence data to create robust evolutionary trees of Artabotrys, allowing an assessment of the degree to which individual elements have contributed as evolutionary drivers. Early diversification resulted in sister lineages that are markedly asymmetrical in species numbers: the main species-rich Artabotrys lineage, characterised by flowers with a tightly enclosed pollination chamber, has undergone considerable evolutionary diversification relative to the species-poor early lineages. The floral chamber functions as a pollinator trap, with pollinators attracted by floral scent and food rewards, but prevented from leaving by the closure of the chamber. This optimises pollination efficiency by increasing pollen loading on pollinators, promoting interfloral movement, and increasing seed-set, thereby driving evolutionary diversification. Our morphological study linked floral morphology with pollination ecology. We also used the evolutionary tree to develop biogeographical hypotheses using evolutionary divergence age estimations and ancestral area reconstructions. We used ecological niche models species to generate evolutionary climatic models, enabling an assessment of whether the lineages that dispersed into Asia were ancestrally better adapted to seasonally dry habitats. The impact of potential morphological innovations and founder biogeographical events as evolutionary drivers were also assessed.

17110017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17110017.value: Hypercholesterolemia is a major cardiovascular risk factor and lowering LDL cholesterol with pharmacotherapy like statin which up-regulates the low density lipoprotein-receptor (LDLR) has been shown to significantly reduces cardiovascular events and mortality. The importance of the LDLR pathway in controlling plasma levels of LDL is well-recognized and a novel regulator of this pathway, the inducible degrader of the LDLR (IDOL), has recently been identified. IDOL is an E3-ubiquitin ligase, and ubiquitination of the intracellular tail of LDLR by IDOL targets the receptor for lysosomal degradation. Latest genome-wide association studies have identified IDOL as a potential novel genetic locus affecting LDL cholesterol levels in humans, and inducing IDOL expression in the liver raises plasma cholesterol in animal studies. IDOL is ubiquitously expressed but very little is known about the extra-hepatic role of IDOL in peripheral tissues. We have found that IDOL is abundantly expressed in human macrophages. We postulate that IDOL may be one of the major determinants of LDLR expression in macrophages and may be involved in protecting peripheral cells like macrophages from excess cholesterol uptake and prevent foam cell formation. We will investigate the role of IDOL in regulating macrophage uptake of cholesterol and foam cell formation by silencing or inducing IDOL in vitro, and assess the effects on atherosclerosis in vivo by specifically knocking out macrophage IDOL in mpeg1:EGFP zebrafish. The advantage of using mpeg1:EGFP zebrafish rather than rodents or rabbits is that mpeg1:EGFP zebrafish constitutively express enhanced green fluorescent protein (GFP) in macrophages, and the optical transparency of the larvae provides the opportunity to visualize and investigate lipid accumulation by macrophages in early atherosclerotic lesion development. Furthermore, we will determine whether IDOL is an important determinant of LDLR expression in macrophages in human type 2 diabetes and its relationship to metabolic parameters. Improving our understanding on the functional importance of the local role of IDOL in macrophage cholesterol metabolism and atherosclerosis on top of its role in systemic lipoprotein metabolism may allow development of novel strategies to treat atherosclerosis.

17110017.label: Realisation of objectives
17110017.value: The inducible degrader of LDL receptor (IDOL), also known as the myosin light chain interacting protein (MYLIP), is an E3 ubiquitin ligase. By promoting ubiquitination of the intracellular tail of LDLR, IDOL induces lysosomal degradation of LDLR. Both IDOL and proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) are involved in the post-transcriptional regulation of LDLR. In objective 1, we have shown that PCSK9 is not expressed in macrophages and IDOL is the major determinant of LDLR expression in macrophages. Our in vitro studies have demonstrated that IDOL knockdown in human monocyte-derived macrophages resulted in increased LDLR expression. This was accompanied by an increase in LDL binding and uptake, as well as intracellular lipid accumulation. The reduction in IDOL expression and the concomitant increase in intracellular lipid accumulation resulted in macrophages having a pro-inflammatory phenotype. On the other hand, activation of IDOL by LXR agonists reduced LDL binding and lipid accumulation and prevented foam cell formation. To evaluate the effect of selectively increasing macrophage IDOL expression in vivo, a transgenic zebrafish model, Tg(mpeg1:mylipA-Tol2A-eGFP;cry:eGFP) over-expressing mylipA gene (ENSDARG00000008859) under the control of the macrophage-specific mpeg1 promoter was developed. The Tol2A-GFP sequence was employed to label mylipA-expressing cells with the green fluorescent protein. The cry:GFP sequence promoted the expression of the GFP in the fish lens and was employed as transgenesis marker. Plasmids were injected into one-cell-stage wild-type embryos, together with the mRNA of the tol2 transposase. Positive embryos were grown until adulthood and subsequently screened to identify a founder carrying the transgene in its germline cells. Hepatic IDOL and LDLR expression in transgenic zebrafish over-expressing IDOL in macrophages was similar to wildtype zebrafish and there was no significant differences in serum cholesterol levels. Macrophages infiltration in blood vessels and foam cell formation/fatty streak was significantly reduced in transgenic zebrafish compared to wildtype zebrafish when zebrafish were fed a high fat diet, suggesting that IDOL played a role in regulating macrophage cholesterol homeostasis and function (manuscript under preparation). In objective 2, we have evaluated IDOL expression in circulating monocytes in subjects with and without type 2 diabetes. We have shown that the expression of intracellular IDOL was significantly lower in individuals with diabetes than non-diabetic control and this resulted in increased intracellular lipid accumulation. We have further investigated the mechanisms of diabetes-mediated down-regulation of IDOL and in vitro studies demonstrated that the down-regulation of IDOL in diabetes was mediated by hyperglycemia and fibroblast growth factor-21 (manuscript submitted to Journal of Lipid Research and currently under revision). Furthermore, we have discovered that statins can also modulate IDOL expression. To avoid the potential confounding effect of glycaemia on IDOL expression, we have examined the effect of statins on IDOL in subjects with familial hypercholesterolaemia. Although IDOL is a cytosolic protein, we have shown that IDOL can be detected in the circulation. Statins exert opposite effects on IDOL and PCSK9 in vivo, and statins increased serum PCSK9 while lowering serum IDOL levels in patients with familial hypercholesterolemia. Further experimental studies have shown that statins modulate IDOL expression by reducing LXR activation (manuscript published in Endocrine Connections). These data improve our understanding on how IDOL is regulated.

17110017.label: Major findings and research outcome
17110017.value: The LDLR mediates the endocytosis of LDL and the level of expression and activity of the LDLR is tightly regulated. Post-transcriptional regulation of LDLR involves the control of the degradation of LDLR and is mediated by PCSK9 and IDOL. Since both IDOL and PCSK9 are involved in the degradation of LDLR, it has been suggested that IDOL and PCSK9 might be differentially utilized in a tissue-specific manner in the post-translational regulation of LDLR, and IDOL may have a physiological role beyond systemic cholesterol homeostasis. For instance, it has been reported that IDOL is highly expressed in the hippocampus and loss of IDOL impairs plasticity and memory formation in animal studies. In this project, we have investigated the pathophysiological role of IDOL in macrophages as macrophages play an important role in the pathogenesis of atherosclerosis by developing into foam cells after uptake of cholesterol. We have shown that IDOL is the major determinant of LDLR expression in macrophages as PCSK9 is not expressed in macrophages. Knockdown of IDOL in human monocyte-derived macrophages led to an increase in LDLR expression and intracellular lipid accumulation, and resulted in macrophages having a pro-inflammatory phenotype. On the other hand, activation of IDOL by LXR agonists reduced LDL binding and lipid accumulation and prevented foam cell formation. Transgenic over-expression of IDOL in macrophages in zebrafish reduced macrophages infiltration in blood vessels and foam cell formation even when zebrafish were fed a high fat diet, suggesting that selective over-expression of IDOL in macrophages might potentially be anti-atherogenic. In our clinical studies, we have shown that the expression of intracellular IDOL in monocytes was significantly reduced in individuals with type 2 diabetes compared to non-diabetic control and this was accompanied by an increase intracellular lipid accumulation in monocytes. We have further determined the mechanisms of the down-regulation of IDOL in diabetes and this was mediated by hyperglycemia as well as by fibroblast growth factor-21 (submitted to Journal of Lipid Research, currently under revision) Furthermore, we have found that statins can also modulate IDOL expression and statins exert opposite effects on IDOL and PCSK9 in vivo (published in Endocrine Connections 2022:11:e220019). These data improve our understanding how IDOL is regulated. In conclusion, IDOL plays an important role in regulating macrophage cholesterol homeostasis and function, and modulating IDOL in macrophages may potentially influence the process of atherogenesis.

17110017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17110017.value: 1. IDOL is a cytosolic protein and we have shown that IDOL can be detected in the circulation. How IDOL is secreted into the bloodstream is unclear. The mechanism by which IDOL is secreted and whether extracellular IDOL has any physiological function warrants further investigation. 2. Since we have shown that macrophages have a proinflammatory phenotype after knockdown of IDOL expression, we intend to investigate the underling mechanisms and signalling pathways involved. The potential anti-inflammatory role of macrophage IDOL in vivo can be further evaluated using murine models 3. IDOL expression is reduced in patients with type 2 diabetes and high glucose concentration can down-regulate IDOL expression in vitro. Hence, we plan to determine whether improving glycemic control can correct these abnormalities.

17110017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17110017.value: The low density lipoprotein receptor (LDLR) takes up LDL into cells and plays an important role in the metabolism of cholesterol. Degradation of LDLR is controlled by proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) and the recently identified inducible degrader of the LDLR (IDOL). We have investigated the extra-hepatic role of IDOL and focused our investigations on macrophages as macrophages develop into foam cells and are involved in the pathogenesis of atherosclerosis. We have shown that IDOL is the major determinant of LDLR expression in macrophages since PCSK9 is not expressed in macrophages. Reducing IDOL in macrophages led to an increase in LDLR expression and intracellular lipid accumulation, and resulted in foam cell formation. Selectively stimulating IDOL expression in macrophages in zebrafish reduced foam cell formation, suggesting that selective over-expression of IDOL in macrophages might potentially be anti-atherogenic. In our clinical studies, we have shown that the expression of IDOL in monocytes was reduced in patients with type 2 diabetes and both glucose and fibroblast growth factor-21 were involved in the regulation of IDOL expression. In conclusion, IDOL plays an important role in regulating macrophage cholesterol homeostasis and function, and modulating IDOL in macrophages may potentially influence the process of atherogenesis.

17111517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17111517.value: T cells recognize virus-infected cells and are crucial for immune control. T cell based vaccines are being developed against influenza viruses to provide broad protection, as T cells can cross react between different strains of influenza and typically recognized conserved regions of the virus. Next generation vaccines that utilize T cells could overcome limitations of current commercial vaccine methods that use antibodies to provide narrow protection, require worldwide surveillance and yearly update of vaccine strain selection. However, mutations in the viral fragments can also result in immune escape from T cell recognition, and have already been observed in some situations for influenza and this issue needs to be addressed for vaccine development. Our current understanding of influenza T cell escape is based on mutations deduced from sequence databases of population consensus virus sequences, and may under estimate the frequency of influenza T cell escape mutation. We have previously found during mouse infection that influenza virus escape from CD8 T cell recognition occurs as early as 5 days post infection in multiple mice, and it is not a rare phenomenon. CD4 T cell responses are the cornerstone of anti-viral immunity, coordinating B cell and CD8 T cell responses. Yet it is unknown whether influenza viruses escape CD4 T cell responses due to their inadvertent helper functions and potential cytolytic killing activity. This study aims to establish how common T cell mediated immune escape is in CD8 killer and CD4 helper epitopes during natural influenza infection and to investigate vaccine mediated immune pressure, using a model T cell-activating vaccine. This will be accomplished by direct next generation sequencing of the virus after influenza infection from the lungs of infected vaccinated mice. By studying the virus and how it mutates in response to immune pressure within an individual, we can be guided for optimal vaccine design to limit viral escape, ensuring a T-cell based vaccine that is viable for widespread population use. 17111517.label: Realisation of objectives
17111517.value: 1. To determine the capacity of the influenza virus to adapt to T cell responses, by studying epitope mutation rates in a mouse model of infection and vaccination. To quantify vaccine mediated immune pressure by a T cell activating vaccine, we used a vaccinia viral vector encoding five influenza genes and IL-15 cytokine as a molecular adjuvant. The next generation vaccine, Wyeth/IL-15/5flu, is a universal vaccine candidate with broad heterosubtypic protection against H7N7, H5N1, H3N2 and H1N1 influenza A viruses. We vaccinated C57BL6 and BALB/c mice with inactivated quadrivalent seasonal influenza vaccines (S-QIIV, NH 2016/17 season), Wyeth/IL-15/5flu or PBS. Mice were vaccinated twice and then challenged 3 weeks later with 0.1LD50 of H1N1 (A/California/07/2009) and H3N2 (A/HKx31 (H3N2), a reassortment of A/PR/8/1934 internal genes with A/Aichi/1/1968 HA and NA) viruses. The lungs of infected mice were harvested at 3, 5 and 7 days of infection and RNA extracted for whole genome next generation sequencing using Illumina and NovaSeq. We developed a whole genome sequencing approach from infected mouse tissues up to day 7 of influenza infection, when viral loads are close to clearance but T cell immunity is at its peak during acute infection of vaccinated mice. We developed a reverse transcription PCR and workflow enabling us to reach high read coverage for the whole influenza genome despite low quantity of template RNA. This was a difficult approach and required many rounds of troubleshooting (timepoints, PCR polymerase, primers, RNA extraction) but was ultimately successful. We compared the genetic flexibility of the known epitope region of mice by comparison with consensus sequences from the NCBI influenza genome repository isolated during human infection. As the MHC restriction is not maintained between species the mutation rate in database sequences represents background mutations compared to those generated in mice. We found that the NCBI influenza sequences at epitope regions often had higher rate mutations than those generated during infection of mice in any conditions Mutations were assessed by nonsynonymous SNP cumulative count and frequency, and diversity index (Shannon Entropy Index). Comparison of mutational rate between our next generation vaccine and inactivated vaccines showed that there were more frequent mutations in next generation vaccine mice, albeit at low frequency. However, there was no enrichment of mutations in known T cell epitopes. Furthermore, when mutations >10% were identified and peptide representing the region were used to stimulate T cell responses (by IFNg cytokine induction) they did not correspond to T cell responses. Furthermore, mutations in T cell epitope regions did not reduce T cell responses when the mutated epitope was used for stimulation. The Shannon Entropy analysis showed an increase in diversity in non-epitope regions. Therefore, Wyeth/IL-15/5Flu vaccination induced mutations are stochastic in nature and not targeted at T cell epitope regions. There was a similar SNP incidence (>0.01 Alelle Frequency) between S-QIIV and Wyeth/IL-15/5Flu at day 3 and day 5 of infection. Whilst at day 7, there was an increased SNP frequency in Wyeth/IL-15/5Flu vs S-QIIV in 5 of 8 influenza genes. There was an accumulation of SNPs over time in Wyeth/IL-15/5Flu vaccination groups. Therefore, Wyeth/IL-15/5Flu is increasing the incidence and degree of mutation at day 7 post infection compared to mock-vaccinated and S-QIIV vaccination groups At day 7 PBS vaccinated mutations predominantly on HA-head region, whilst for Wyeth/IL-15/5Flu vaccinated mutations on both head and stem region. Specifically, the mutation at HA 289, a glycosylation site arose at a 14.5% frequency in day 5 Wyeth/IL-15/5Flu vaccinated mice (1 out of 5 mice) which could alter virulence of virus or mask receptor binding sites. Further comparison of mutations in NGS data set and beneficial mammalian adaptation mutations in PB2 identified (Lee Nat Sci Rep 2020), corresponded to 6 mutations which enhanced polymerase activity were identified in NGS dataset in both day 7 p.i. PBS and Wyeth/IL-15/5Flu groups. The PB2-E158G mutation arose across vaccination groups in 9 of 9 PBS vaccinated mice and 4 of 6 Wyeth/IL-15/5Flu vaccinated mice, at a frequency of 90.8% frequency in a Wyeth/IL-15/5Flu mouse. Therefore Wyeth/IL-15/5Flu vaccination may enhance host adaptation or drive immune evasion 2. Assess whether a T cell based vaccine increases the amount of T cell mediated virus escape, especially for CD4 T cells. Wyeth/IL-15/5Flu vaccination increases incidence and degree of mutation across the IAV genome. Wyeth/IL-15/5Flu vaccine mediates protection via recall T cell responses. Therefore we conducted depletion experiments to assess the effect of T cell mediated immune pressure on the IAV genome. We used in vivo T cell depletion using monoclonal antibodies αCD4 and αCD8, prior to and during infection time course. CD4+ T cell depletion lead to increased viral lung load at day 7, but overall vaccination still significantly reduced viral titre at day 7 in depleted conditions compared to PBS mice. The CD8+ T cell population was preserved in CD4+ depleted conditions. However, CD4+ T cell depletion significantly reduces total SNP incidence in Wyeth/IL-15/5Flu vaccinated mice in 3 of 8 genes (HA, NA and PA) compared to undepleted vaccinated mice. Therefore, CD4+ T cells are contributing to mutational rates of IAV in Wyeth/IL-15/5Flu vaccinated conditions We complemented our studies with CD8+ T cell depletion. CD8+ T cell depletion leads to increased viral lung load, however vaccination still significantly reduced viral titre at day 7 in depleted conditions. Again the CD4+ T cell population was preserved in CD8+ T cell depleted conditions. CD8+ T cell depletion significantly reduces total SNP incidence of mutation in Wyeth/IL-15/5Flu vaccinated mice in 3 of 8 genes (HA, NA and NP). Therefore CD8+ T cells are contributing to mutational rates of IAV in Wyeth/IL-15/5Flu vaccinated conditions Overall the mutation degree and incidence (>1%) decreased by both CD4+ and CD8+ T cell depletion. The mutations appear to be stochastic in nature and were not increased in T cell regions. 3. To determine the factors that influence T cell driven immune escape of influenza virus. As above we conducted sequencing over a time-course, in the absence of T cell subsets, in different mouse backgrounds, viral challenge strains, and vaccine types. From the time course of infection and subsequent sequencing showed with time the frequency of mutations, S-QIIV and Wyeth/IL-15/5flu vaccinated mice, day 7 was significantly increased compared to day 3 of infection, which is inverse to viral loads. Whilst in unvaccinated mice the frequency of mutations peaked at day 5 post infection. At all timepoints Wyeth/IL-15/5flu vaccinated mice had higher frequency of mutations than inactivated vaccines in a number of genes. Therefore the vaccine mechanism of protection, and squeeze it places on viral loads can determine the residual virus capable of adaptation. 4. To confirm that newly identified influenza mutant viruses escape existing T cell responses and establishing new responses. Despite repeated attempts (up to 10 trials, different plasmid backgrounds and serial passage) we were unable to rescue mutant viruses containing point mutations identified in vaccinated mice using the 8 plasmid reverse genetics approach, despite positive wild type controls being rescued. Thus, viruses containing the single mutations appeared to be non-viable. We therefore used peptides to represent mutated regions and stimulated wild type vaccine induced T cells to determine cross-reactivity. We did not find reduced T cell recognition of the mutated peptide compared to the wild type peptide in known epitopes, neither were high frequency mutations at T cell epitopes.

17111517.label: Major findings and research outcome
17111517.value: Influenza viruses have the demonstrated capacity to adapt to anti-viral drugs and antibodies by antigenic drift. T cell responses are essential for influenza viral clearance and can recognize conserved epitopes, providing cross-clade protection. However, during heterologous infection, T cell activating vaccines do not provide sterilizing immunity. To determine the potential for viral adaptation, we probed the full influenza virus genome by next generation sequencing directly ex vivo from infected mice, in the context of an experimental T cell-based vaccine, a H5N1 based viral vectored vaccinia vaccine Wyeth/IL-15/5Flu, versus the current standard of care, seasonal inactivated influenza vaccine (IIV) and unvaccinated conditions. Wyeth/IL-15/5Flu elicited robust T cell immunity and reduced viral loads upon heterologous H1N1 infection. This was coincident with increased mutation incidence and frequency across the influenza genome compared to unvaccinated and IIV conditions, but mutations were not enriched within T cell epitope regions. High frequency mutations within conserved HA stem regions and PB2 mammalian adaptive mutations were observed to have the capacity to arise in Wyeth/IL-15/5Flu vaccinated conditions. Depletion of CD4+ and CD8+ T cell subsets led to reduced frequency of mutants in vaccinated mice, therefore vaccine mediated T cell responses were important drivers of virus diversification but did not select for T cell escape mutations but increased virus host adaptation. Our findings suggest that Wyeth/IL-15/5Flu does not generate T cell escape mutants by targeted immune pressure but does increase stochastic events, which could lead to immune driven adaptation at the population level after widespread T cell-based vaccine usage.

17111517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17111517.value: Despite repeated attempts (up to 10 trials) we were unable to rescue mutant viruses identified in vaccinated mice using the 8 plasmid reverse genetics approach, despite positive wild type controls being rescued. Thus the single mutations appeared to be non-viable. However combination mutations could next be assessed, and if viable viral fitness determined by in vitro time course experiments and mouse infection. Further experiments on T cell cross reactivity and mapping of mutations by T cell stimulations using overlapping peptides may reveal cryptic epitopes. Based on our identification of mutations in regions of the influenza genome not included in the next generation vaccine, and importantly in the HA-stem and viral polymerase essential for replication and host adaptation, we advise on full genome sequencing during surveillance of circulating influenza viruses, especially if next generation vaccines are used widespread.

17111517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17111517.value: Inactivated influenza vaccines have been in use for nearly 80 years but can not address pandemic influenza and rapid adaption of influenza viruses. Next generation broadly reactive influenza vaccines are becoming a clinical reality. The selection impact of current and next generation vaccines, especially T cell immunity, on the virus genome within an individual is unknown. We developed a new technique for full influenza virus genome sequencing directly ex vivo from infected mouse lung tissues at low viral titers in the context of inactivated and next generation vaccines. We found that the mutational frequency of influenza viruses was increased in T cell activating influenza vaccine conditions compared to unvaccinated and inactivated vaccine conditions. However these changes were not enriched in T cell targeting areas but there was an increased rates of mutation across the IAV genome that may lead to viral variant emergence, including the viral polymerase proteins and HA-stem. Overall, there was a dynamic relationship of the influenza virus genome and the timing of sampling, T cell depletion and vaccine platform used. Due to the cross-over of inactivated influenza vaccines in use and next generation vaccines, this study has clinical relevance to impact translational medicine.

17111917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17111917.value: Esophageal cancer is the sixth most common cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide and the prognosis is generally poor. China alone accounts for approximately half of all new esophageal cancer cases per year, with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) being the predominant histologic subtype. The lethality of esophageal cancer is attributed to early systemic tumor dissemination. Development of treatment strategies that can prevent the migration and invasion of cancer cells are therefore essential to tackle this highly aggressive disease. In recent years, studies of tumor suppressive microRNAs have gained impetus because of their potential use in cancer therapy. We have established human ESCC cells that are highly metastatic and invasive as cell line models that can be used to identify metastasis-associated microRNAs. MicroRNA profiling showed that miR-338-5p was downregulated in the metastatic ESCC cells. Data from one of our ongoing studies show that miR-338-5p can directly target Id1 (inhibitor of DNA binding 1) to modulate chemosensitivity of ESCC cells but whether the same mechanism allows miR-338-5p to regulate metastasis remained unexplored. We found that although forced expression of miR-338-5p in ESCC cells significantly suppressed cell migration and invasion, rescue of Id1 expression failed to fully restore these properties, suggesting that additional targets(s) of miR-338-5p are involved in mediating its anti-metastatic function. Further analysis showed that miR-338-5p inhibited the expression of PAK4 (p21-activated protein kinase 4), which was one of the potential targets of miR-338-5p as predicted by computational microRNA target prediction tools. Moreover, higher PAK4 expression was detected in the metastatic cancer cells compared with the parental cells. We therefore hypothesize that PAK4 is a novel direct target of miR-338-5p and that it mediates the function of miR-338-5p in suppressing cancer invasion and metastasis. This regulatory mechanism has not been reported previously and relatively little is known about the significance and roles of PAK4 in esophageal cancer. In the proposed study, we will explore the clinicopathological significance of this regulatory pathway by studying and correlating the expression levels of miR-338-5p and PAK4 in primary esophageal cancer and lymph node metastases. We will also perform in vitro and in vivo experiments to examine the suppressive effects of miR-338-5p, and the mediating role of PAK4 and its downstream pathways on esophageal cancer metastasis. The therapeutic potential of systemically administered miR-338-5p in suppressing tumor metastasis will be studied using animal models to obtain preclinical data that may translate into novel therapy for esophageal cancer.

17111917.label: Realisation of objectives
17111917.value: OBJECTIVE 1: To study the clinicopathological significance of the miR-338-5p/PAK4 pathway in esophageal cancer metastasis By mining and analyzing GEO datasets, we found that miR-338-5p was also downregulated in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) but not in esophageal adenocarcinoma, which suggests that downregulation of miR-338-5p might have special significance in the ESCC subtype of esophageal cancer. Although no significant difference was found between ESCC patients with high tumor miR-338-5p expression and patients with low miR-338-5p expression in terms of overall survival rate, there was a trend toward better outcome in the former group. PAK4 mRNA was significantly upregulated by ~24% in esophageal tumor samples in the TCGA database. We extracted protein and miRNAs from 45 primary ESCC tumors in our collection and analyzed the expression level of miR-338-5p and PAK4 in these specimens. The results showed a significant negative correlation between miR-338-5p and PAK4, which seemed to support our initial hypothesis that dysregulation/downregulation of miR-338-5p may attenuate its inhibitory effect on PAK4 translation in ESCC. However, subsequent experimental work (see Objective 2) showed that epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and tyrosine-protein kinase Met, also known as hepatocyte growth factor receptor (cMET), instead of PAK4, were direct targets of miR-338-5p, so we turned our attention to the clinicopathological significance of the miR-338-5p/EGFR and miR-338-5p/cMET regulatory axes. Significant inverse correlations were found between miR-338-5p and the protein expressions of EGFR and cMET in our ESCC samples. RNA sequencing data showed that mRNA level of EGFR and cMET were negatively correlated with miR-338-5p in ESCA data cohort from TCGA database. Importantly, negative correlations were also found between miR-338-5p and the downstream signaling molecules of EGFR and cMET in the TCGA ESCA cohort. Given that EGFR and cMET were reported to be frequently overexpressed in ESCC tumors, especially in patients with metastasis, this further suggests that the miR-338-5p/EGFR and miR-338-5p/cMET regulatory axes have functional significance in patients with esophageal cancer. Thus, despite not pursuing PAK4 as a target of miR-338-5p, we had achieved this objective by validating that miR-338-5p was downregulated in ESCC and therefore likely to be as a tumor-suppressor miRNA in this cancer type. We also confirmed that its aberrant expression in ESCC corresponded with increased expression of two frequently overexpressed oncoproteins. OBJECTIVE 2: To study the suppressive effects of miR-338-5p and the mediating role of PAK4 on esophageal cancer cell motility and invasion in vitro Gain- and loss-of-function experiments were performed to study the role of miR-338-5p in ESCC cell invasion and migration. The results confirmed that miR-338-5p had inhibitory effect on these cellular functions in vitro. We also found stable overexpression of miR-338-5p downregulated matrix metalloproteinase 2 (MMP2) expression, but did not affect cell proliferation and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). In the mid-term report, we mentioned that the results from dual luciferase reporter assays did not support a direct targeting effect of miR-338-5p on PAK4, while data from stable miR-338-5p expression experiments showed that miR-338-5p had limited regulatory effect on PAK4. We therefore proceeded to search for other miR-338-5p–targeted genes that can directly mediate the suppressive effects of miR-338-5p on malignant phenotype of ESCC cells. Multiple computational algorithms and profiling of potential mRNA targets using reverse phase protein array (RPPA) platform were performed to identity potential target genes amongst which were EGFR and cMET. The direct targeting effect of miR-338-5p on EGFR and cMET was validated by dual-luciferase reporter assay. Our results showed that there are two predicted binding sites of miR-338-5p within the EGFR 3’UTR, located at 235-241 bp and 2244-2250 bp respectively, with the second binding site being especially crucial for miR-338-5p to exert suppressive effect on EGFR expression. The 3’UTR of cMET mRNA also has two predicted miR-338-5p binding sites, and both were important in the suppressive effect of miR-338-5p on cMET expression. Western blot results showed that the mRNA and protein levels of EGFR and cMET were obviously decreased in stable miR-338-5p overexpressing ESCC cell lines, and that transfection of miR-338-5p mimic or miR-338-5p expressing plasmid reduced EGFR and cMET expression, as well as suppressed their downstream signaling cascades. Re-introducing EGFR and cMET into ESCC cells rescued the metastatic phenotype abolished by miR-338-5p overexpression in vitro, indicating that EGFR and cMET mediated the inhibitory function of miR-338-5p on ESCC cell motility and metastasis. In vivo ex-experimental metastasis assay involving intravenous injection of luciferase-labeled ESCC cells expressing (i) miR-338-5p, (ii) miRZip-338-5p, (iii) miR-338-5p and EGFR, (iv) miR-338-5p and MET, or (v) control vectors. into different groups of nude mice was also performed to consolidate the in vitro findings. In conclusion, this objective was fully accomplished in that novel targets have been identified for miR-338-5p that can directly mediate its metastasis-suppressive function in vitro and in vivo. OBJECTIVE 3: To evaluate the therapeutic potential of systemically administered miR-338-5p in inhibiting metastasis of esophageal cancer using animal models Luciferase-labeled ESCC cells were injected into nude mice via the tail vein. MicroRNA-338-5p mimic oligonucleotide formulated with a polymeric vector (i.e. in vivo-jetPEI) was then injected intravenously into nude mice with established lung metastasis of ESCC cells. The results showed that systemically administered miR-338-5p significantly reduced lung metastasis of ESCC in nude mice, compared with non-target miRNA control. The body weight of mice was monitored during treatment, and results showed no significant difference among the experiment groups throughout the experiment, indicating that in vivo delivery of miR-338-5p did not have adverse effect on the physical condition of the animals.

17111917.label: Major findings and research outcome
17111917.value: (i) miR-338-5p suppresses invasion of ESCC cells by negatively regulating the expression of matrix metalloproteinases (MMP) 2 and 9: Analysis of clinical samples showed that miR-338-5p was downregulated in the primary tumor and serum samples of patients with ESCC (Part C #1), which suggests that miR-338-5p has tumor suppressive function. In vitro, silencing miR-338-5p in ESCC cell lines resulted in decreased invasiveness, and increased expression and secretion of two well-known gelatinases (namely MMP2 and MMP9) in vitro, whereas overexpressing miR-338-5p had the opposite effects (Part C #3). Manipulation of miR-338-5p expression had negligible effects on epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). These results indicate that miR-338-5p can repress ESCC cell invasion by suppressing degradation of extracellular matrix (Part C #3). (ii) cMET and EGFR are direct targets of miR-338-5p that mediate its anti-invasive function: We have identified several novel targets of miR-338-5p. While Id-1 was found to be an important target that mediates the ability of miR-338-5p to reverse chemoresistance in ESCC cells (Part C #1), our results showed that cMET and EGFR were more important in mediating the inhibitory effect of miR-338-5p on invasion and metastasis of ESCC cells. The significance of this inhibitory regulation was further confirmed by the inverse correlation between the expression level of miR-338-5p and the protein levels of cMET and EGF in clinical ESCC tumor samples. By directly targeting the 3’UTR of these genes, miR-338-5p can disrupt mRNA translation of cMET and promote mRNA degradation of EGFR, and thereby inhibits their downstream effectors including Gab1, AKT, and ERK1/2, as well MMP2 and MMP9 (Part C #3). (iii) Systemically delivered miR-338-5p mimicking oligos can inhibit metastasis of ESCC cells in vivo: Using an experimental metastasis approach, we found that intravenously administered miR-338-5p mimicking oligonucleotides formulated with a polymer-based reagent In vivo-jetPEI® significantly reduced metastasis of circulating ESCC cells to the lungs, without any obvious toxic effect (Part C #3). These results demonstrated the potential therapeutic benefit of administrating miR-338-5p for treating metastatic ESCC. (iv) miR-29c also has metastasis-suppressive function in ESCC: Besides miR-338-5p, our investigation revealed that miR-29, which was also downregulated in ESCC, had similar metastasis-suppressive function in ESCC, but it does so by targeting and inhibiting FBXO31/p38 signaling (Part C #2). This supports the notion that replacement therapy using multiple tumor-suppressive miRNAs may have a useful application in cancer therapy (as reviewed in Part C #4). With this approach, multiple target genes can be silenced simultaneously.

17111917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17111917.value: In recent years, we have identified several novel miRNAs including miR-338-5p, miR-29c and miR-377 that are aberrantly expressed in ESCC. Both miR-338-5p and miR-29c can suppress invasiveness, as well as have chemosensitizing-effect, on ESCC cells. MicroRNA-377 can suppress initiation and progression of esophageal cancer by inhibiting stem cell marker CD133 and VEGF. The efficacy of these miRNAs in inhibiting tumor-growth and metastasis had been tested individually in in vivo in mouse models. Since these miRNAs target different genes and signaling pathways, we are interested to find out if a cocktail of these miRNAs can further enhance anti-cancer effects, as compared with single-miRNA-based therapy. A detailed in vivo study, preferably with the use of in vivo ESCC orthotopic animal model, will provide useful data on the potential of a miRNA cocktail replacement therapy. The longer-term goal will be to translate the findings into novel therapy for esophageal cancer.

17111917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17111917.value: MicroRNAs regulate many pathological processes including cancer metastasis. In this study, we demonstrated that miR-338-5p had metastasis-suppressive function in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). We manipulated the expression level of miR-338-5p in ESCC cells, and found that miR-338-5p overexpression decreased the invasive ability of the cancer cells. This was attributed to decreased expression and secretion of gelatinases such as MMP2 and MMP9, thereby resulting in impaired extracellular matrix degradation and cell invasion. Silencing miR-338-5p had opposite effects. Our results showed that miR-338-5p directly targeted the 3’ untranslated regions of the messenger RNAs of two receptor tyrosine kinases, namely cMET and EGFR. As a result, miR-338-5p inhibited the downstream signaling of cMET and EGFR, and repressed cMET- and EGFR-mediated ESCC cell invasion. In ESCC tumors, the expression levels of cMET, EGFR, MMP2 and MMP9 were all inversely correlated with that of miR-338-5p. Most importantly, our in vivo experiments showed that treatment with intravenously administered miR-338-5p mimic significantly inhibited metastasis of ESCC cells in nude mice. Taken together, our results uncovered a previously unknown regulatory mechanism by which miR-338-5p suppresses ESCC invasion and metastasis, and highlighted the potential significance of miR-338-5p-based therapy in treating patients with metastatic ESCC.
