17112117.value: 基因排序顯示人類季節性流感病毒自引入到人類後，其序列有迅速演變，病毒蛋白基因排序除了得到更適應新宿主的非同義突變外，它亦有着大量同義突變。以至令到病毒改變了密碼子使用偏好。為了進一步認識密碼子使用偏好對病毒複製的影響，我們過去曾將季節性流感病毒的密碼子使用偏好改動到與禽流感偏好相似並作出研究，我們發覺這變異病毒在哺乳細胞中減毒，這過去的研究不僅開創了一種製生減活疫苗的方法，其發現也帶出非同義實變對病毒複製具有重大的影響。 我們認為以上的病毒變異體和其衍生物可成為有用的實驗模型，可為密碼子偏好和其他基因序列特徵對病毒複製作出深入研究，例如過去亦得知人類流感病毒中的CpG二核苷酸頻率越遠低放在禽流感病毒中所發現的，由於CpG二核苷酸頻率和密碼子偏好是兩個密切相關但明顯不同的因素，因此我們有興趣測試這兩個因素對病毒複製是否有協同或獨立的作用。 在這研究項目中，我們會使用同義突變去改變合成病毒的密碼子偏好和CpG二核苷酸使用頻率。我們會研究 1) 這些基因序列變異令病毒減活的機制，2) 人類細胞對密碼子偏好和CpG二核苷酸使用頻率的選擇壓力，3) 製造其他類似病毒去確認我們所得的結果，我們亦會使用新的測序方法來分析我們的病毒。我們相信這研究能幫助我們更了解病毒的演化，並為設計新的疫苗提供關鍵信息。

17112117.label: Realisation of objectives
17112117.value: The project contained 3 project modules. a) Project modules 1: Design and rescue codon bias mutants with different CpG contents We have analysed about 160 thousand influenza viral open reading frames (ORFs) from human and avian influenza viruses. The yearly change of CpG and other possible dinucleotide motifs for each segment have been studied. A Monte Carlo type method is applied to identify underrepresented or overrepresented dinucleotide motifs, among different segments and different groups, in influenza viral sequences. After excluding the potential biases caused by codon usage and amino acid sequences, CpG and UpG are found to be underrepresented in all viral segments from all groups, whereas CpG and UpG are found to be overrepresented. We have further explored the temporal changes of usage of these dinucleotides. It is observed that some human viral gene segments have significant decrease of certain dinucleotide motifs (e.g. CpG). Such temporal variations are mainly contributed by the dinucleotide changes at the codon positions 3-1 and 2-3 where silent mutations play a major role. The depletions of CpG and UpA through silent mutations lead to over-representation of UpG and CpA. We have also found that dinucleotide preference directly results in significant synonymous codon usage bias. Thus, our work suggest that the codon usage bias can be partly regulated the dinucleotide usage bias in these viruses. Our findings was published in a peer reviewed journal (Gu et al., Virus Evol, 2019). Based on our in-silicon-findings, we developed an in-house program to design influenza genomic sequences with our desired sequence features (i.e. dinucleotide frequency and codon usage). We made this program freely to public (https://github.com/Leo-Poon-Lab/SynMut/pulse). Using this in-house program, we introduced different set of silent mutations into a human H1N1 influenza viral genome and designed a panel of with different combinations of CpG frequency and codon bias. A total of six synthetic viral genomes were designed: 1. Viral genome with human virus-like codon bias and high CpG frequency 2. Viral genome with human virus-like codon bias and low CpG frequency 3. Viral genome with avian virus-like codon bias and high CpG frequency 4. Viral genome with avian virus-like codon bias and low CpG frequency 5. Viral genome with maximum CpG frequency 6. Viral genome with minimal CpG frequency Amongst these mutants, recombinant virus with maximum or minimum CpG frequency cannot be recruited. These suggested that influenza viruses cannot tolerate viral sequences with extremely high or low CpG motif. Amongst mutants that can be rescued by us (Mutants 1-4), we tested that virus replication properties in human (A549), canine (MDCK) and chicken (egg) cells. We observed that these viruses have different replication properties in these models. Mutant 2 had wild-type replication properties in these cells. Mutants with high CpG contents (Mutants 1 and 3) were highly attenuated in A549 cells. By contrast, only Mutant 3, but not all tested mutants, was highly attenuated in MDCK cells. Interestingly, these 4 mutants had similar titres in chicken embryonic eggs. These results suggested that different animal species have different levels of host restriction on these “isogenic” viruses. This finding might explain our observation that the CpG motif is actively deselected in seasonal influenza viral segments. Due to the emergence of SARS-CoV-2 in December 2019. We used the established sequence analytic pipelines to study SARS-CoV-2 and other SARS-CoV-related viral genomes (i.e sarbecoviruses). Findings from this additional study was published in a peer reviewed journal (Gu et al., Virus Evolution 2020). b) Project modules 2: Characterization of codon bias mutants in human cells In order to determine whether the attenuation of high CpG mutants in human A549 cells was due to the activation of innate immune antiviral responses, we tested this virus panel in gene-edited A549 cell lines that do not express representative viral RNA sensing proteins (RIG-I and ZAP). Their replication properties were similar to those observed in wild-type A549 cells. We further used different assays (e.g. RIG-I reporter system, RT-PCR and flow cytometry) and cells (e.g. THP-1 derived monocytes and dendritic cells) to characterize these mutants. However, we did not observe any significant difference amongst these mutants in these assays. Overall, these results suggest that there might be other antiviral mechanisms account for the attenuation of high CpG mutants in human cells. Further studies on this topic are needed. In the process of characterizing these mutants, we invented a multiplex cytotoxicity assay. We expanded the conventional in vivo cytotoxicity assay from two parameters to twenty-four parameters. This functional assay allows testing multiple viral epitopes in a single reaction. Our findings were published in a peer reviewed journal (Poh et al., Front Immunol. 2020). We also serially passaged these mutants and the wild-type control virus in MDCK and A549 cells for 30 times. Viral RNA samples of these progeny viruses were subjected to the next generation sequences (Illumina). We did not any reverse mutation in the passaged mutants. The number of mutations in each studied viral segment ranged from 0 to 8. Surprisingly, none of these mutants had a statistical higher number of mutations than the wild-type control. We also did not observe a significance increasing or decreasing trend of dinucleotide frequency in this experiment. We further stratified the data by silent/non-silent mutation and obtained similar conclusions. Overall, we did not detect a significant change of sequence motif in the passaged viruses. c) Project module 3: Characterization of replicative influenza viruses carrying exogenous sequences with different sequence features. The mutations introduced into the above viral genomes might affect unknown critical motifs that are essential for virus replication. We subsequently generated a set of mutants (N=4) carrying a GFP ORF in between NS1 and NS2 ORFs as proposed. These GPF ORFs had silent mutations, resulting in different degrees of codon bias and CpG usage as described above. All recombinant viruses could be rescued and characterized in different cell lines (A549, MDCK and chicken eggs). Because of the insertion of an exogenous gene into the viral genome, all of these mutants were slightly attenuated as expected. Nonetheless, the mutant with a GFP ORF that has high CpG content and avian virus-like codon usage had the most attenuated phenotype. We also generated a panel of mutants (N=4) with an insertion of 120 nucleotide long untranslated sequence in between in the ORFs of NS1 and NS2. Mutants with the highest CpG content in this untranslated region also highly attenuated in mammalian cells. We further used RT-PCR assays to measure the viral mRNA expression of the GFP-expressing mutants, and confirmed these mutants have similar NS1 and NS2 mRNA expressions. Interestingly, GPF ORFs that have a high CpG content had a higher translation efficiency and this observation were confirmed by 3 different methods (fluorescence image, Western blotting, and flow cytometry analyses). In the process of characterizing these mutants, we developed a microfluidic platform which allows real-time monitoring of single cells infected by GFP-expressing virus mutants. This study was published in a peer reviewed journal (Nan et al., Small 2020). Conclusion: Results from these 3 project modules that the deselection of CpG motif is the major driving force for the change of codon usage bias in seasonal influenza virus. Influenza virus with high CpG content in its genome is highly attenuated in human cells. This virus attenuation was not due to differences in viral RNA expression levels, viral mRNA translation efficiency or studied innate viral RNA sensing pathways.

17112117.label: Major findings and research outcome
17112117.value: Our results have the following impacts: 1. This study reveals the selection of dinucleotide motif is a major driving force in shaping the viral codon usage bias and viral sequence space. 2. The study provide highly comprehensive data which help to develop a better strategy for creating attenuated influenza mutants for other applications (e.g. live-attenuated influenza vaccines). 3. Several novel sequence analytic and biological platforms were established in the study. These novel tool can be used in other influenza studies and beyond. 3. This work resulted in 4 peer-reviewed publications (Virus Evolution: 2; Frontiers in Immunology: 1; Small: 1) 4. One PhD student was trained in this study (Haogao Gu). After his graduation, he was hired as a post-doctoral fellow and involved several SARS-CoV-2 studies. Thus far, he published at least 15 articles after his graduation, reflecting he was extremely well-trained in his PhD studies.

17112117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17112117.value: This project can lead to further investigations: 1. The established computation program can allow us to design other synthetic genomes with other sequence feature for further investigation; 2. Our sequence analytic pipelines can be used for studying other non-influenza viral genomes; 3. The established virus panels can be used for identify potential host specific restriction factors for influenza virus replications; 4. The established microfluidic system and immune assays can be used for studying influenza virus replication and host responses at single cell level in a much more robust and systematical manner.

17112117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17112117.value: We studied about 160 thousand influenza virus sequence and observed that the CpG content of seasonal influenza virus is less than avian influenza virus. Besides, we also found seasonal and avian influenza viruses have distinct codon usage bias. We further used different panel of isogenic viruses to characterize the roles of influenza viral codon bias and CpG dinucleotide usage frequency on virus replication. Our findings indicate the selection force against the CpG motif in seasonal influenza virus might be the factor that control codon usage bias. Influenza virus with high CpG contents is attenuated in human cells, suggesting human host imposes a selection pressure against CpG dinucleotide sequences in seasonal influenza virus. The increase of CpG content in the viral genome, however, would not affect viral RNA expression or its viral mRNA translation. In addition, increasing the CpG content in the viral genome was found to have no effect on innate immune responses. Our results suggested that there might be other cellular and/or viral factors that shape the sequence motif of influenza virus genome. Further characterization of these virus panels will be needed to reveal the underlying mechanism accounted for our observations.

17112317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17112317.value: G-protein coupled receptors (GPCRs) are the most widely used molecular signaling devices by cells to connect extracellular stimuli to intracellular responses, and hence they are currently the major targets for therapeutic drugs in the market. Comparative approaches providing information on conserved functional and structural domains aid our understanding in the process of evolution and design of novel drugs targeting GPCRs. Cumulative data from our laboratory have provided evidences for the expansion of class B1 GPCRs in parallel with the two rounds of whole genome duplications (2WGD) in early vertebrate evolution, which have permitted enhanced capability for sensing and responding to changes in the environment as well as endorsing more complex homeostatic regulations that are essential to species innovation in the invertebrate/vertebrate transition. More recently, our group has reported data confirming the presence of the first invertebrate B1 ligand/receptor pairs in amphioxus, demonstrating that functional homologs of vertebrate pituitary adenylyl cyclase-activating polypeptide/glucagon (PACAP/GCG) arose before the divergence from the ancestor of vertebrates. Studies in vertebrates have shown that pituitary growth hormone (GH)-release is always regulated by class B1 peptides such as PACAP and GH-releasing hormone (GHRH). By investigating functions of amphioxus PACAP/GCG peptides to regulate GH homolog expression and release, in relationship to development of an anterior pituitary-like structure known as Hatschek’s pit that mimics the developmental process of hypothalamo-pituitary structures of a vertebrate embryo, the ultimate goal here is to understand the roles of class B1 GPCRs in the evolutionary relationship of Hatschek’s pit and hypothalamo-pituitary axis during invertebrate/vertebrate transition. In the past, studies in the field of molecular evolution relied heavily on sequence comparison, while recent advancement in structural biology enables novel understanding of the interactions of this family of ligand-receptor at atomic level. It was previously reported that the binding pockets of GCG receptor involve both transmembrane (TM) and extra-cellular (EC) domains whereas, for PACAP receptors, the EC domain alone is sufficient for ligand interaction. The differences between the bindings of the 2 subfamilies of ligands with their receptors have implications in future ligand-specific drug design and innovation. The discoveries of the PACAP/GCGR in amphioxus have therefore provided opportunity in studying the functional and structural co-evolution of B1 ligand/receptor with subsequent development of 2 models of receptor binding pockets from invertebrates to vertebrates, and our approach may also provide a new direction for investigating co-evolution of ligand/receptor pair in the future.

17112317.label: Major findings and research outcome
17112317.value: This study investigated the origin of the most important endocrine structure, the pituitary, in a key evolutionary positioned extant species amphioxus that diverged immediately before vertebrates. The Hatschek’s pit in the cephalochordate amphioxus, an invertebrate deuterostome basal to chordates is suggested to be the functional homologue structure of the vertebrate hypothalamus, adenohypophysis and neurohypophysis based on anatomy and expression of homologous neuroendocrine genes. However, the endocrine potential of the cephalochordate Hatschek’s pit remains to be demonstrated as well as the physiological actions of the secreted neuropeptides. In this study, we have explored the distribution and characterized the potential function of the amphioxus PACAP/GLUC precursor, which is the orthologue of the hypothalamic PACAP neuropeptide in vertebrates. Immunofluorescence staining detected their expression around the nucleus of Rohde, supporting that this structure may be homologous of the neurosecretory cells of the vertebrate hypothalamus where abundant PACAP is found. PACAP/GLUCa was also detected in the infundibulum‐like down growth approaching the Hatschek’s pit, indicating diffusion of PACAP/GLUCa from the CNS to the pit via the infundibulum‐like down growth. Under a high salinity challenge, PACAP/GLUCa was upregulated in amphioxi head and PACAP/GLUCa treatment was found to increase expression of GHl in Hatschek’s pit in a dose-dependent manner, suggesting that PACAP/GLUCa may be involved in the regulation of GHl via HP-like axis in a similar manner than in vertebrates. Our results support that the amphioxus Hatschek’s pit is likely to be the functional homologue of the pituitary gland in vertebrates.

17112317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17112317.value: The origin of class B GPCRs and ligands is a big scientific question to ask and to be answered. Our work pioneers this research area in addressing some important issues such as the origin of the pituitary and the evolution of class B GPCR from invertebrates to vertebrates. The newly developed transgenic amphioxus lines in this study will definitely be important tools in the near future to understand these processes and the modification and change of the neural system during this important time in evolution. We will continue to work on this interesting topic in the future.

17112317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17112317.value: G-protein coupled receptors (GPCRs) are the most widely used molecular signaling devices by cells to connect extracellular stimuli to intracellular responses, and hence they are currently the major targets for therapeutic drugs in the market. Comparative approaches providing information on conserved functional and structural domains aid our understanding in the process of evolution and design of novel drugs targeting GPCRs. Cumulative data from our laboratory have provided evidence for the expansion of class B GPCRs in parallel with early vertebrate evolution, which has permitted enhanced capability for sensing and responding to changes in the environment as well as endorsing more complex homeostatic regulations that are essential to species innovation in the invertebrate/vertebrate transition. In this report, our group has confirmed functions of amphioxus PACAP/GCG peptides to regulate GH homolog expression and release, in relationship to development of an anterior pituitary-like structure known as Hatschek’s pit that mimics the developmental process of hypothalamo-pituitary structures of a vertebrate embryo, the ultimate goal here is to understand the roles of class B GPCRs in the evolutionary relationship of Hatschek’s pit and hypothalamo-pituitary axis during invertebrate/vertebrate transition.

17112617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17112617.value: Ubiquitylation is one of the most commonly utilized cellular post-translational modifications (PTM), routinely targeted by pathogens to deregulate and hijack host intracellular pathways. Severity of infections or progression of cancer is often determined by how robust host immune responses are. Cells use ubiquitylation to change subcellular localizations, accessibility between enzymes and interacting proteins, formation of sub-complexes and signaling platforms or alter protein conformation, hence providing a tunable process that allows for rapid changes in protein function. Interestingly, most viruses and bacteria utilize ubiquitylation to target central signaling pathways such as NFκB and MAPK that are crucial for their replication, propagation and immune evasion. The ubiquitylation machinery has been implicated in several diseases, hence promoting advancement of numerous drugs into clinical trials with the likes of botezomib and thalidomides being FDA-approved. Hence, identification of such regulatory components that function during infection, paves the way for elucidating fundamental mechanisms of virus-host interactions as well as development of novel therapeutics. We employed an activity-based proteomics screening strategy to uncover deubiquitylases (DUBs) that specifically function during influenza virus infection. Two main goals underlie our approach: (1) to discover novel components of the ubiquitylation machinery that are targeted during infection (2) to determine their function in normal physiology and in the context of virus infection. Apart from the potential “druggability” of DUBs, such studies also provide valuable insights into the biology of the virus-host interactions. We used a C-terminal vinylmethylester modified HA-tagged ubiquitin (HA-Ub-vme) to isolate DUBs that are specifically expressed in influenza virus infected cells. We had previously applied a similar strategy to identify DUBs that function during T-cell receptor signaling. This application is centered on OtuB1, a DUB that is induced upon virus infection and interacts with the virus polymerase PB2. Our preliminary studies show a cellular redistribution of OtuB1 upon flu infection as a function of time. Knock-out of OtuB1 in A549 cells results in reduced cytokine production upon infection. We have generated several variants of OtuB1 with mutations in specific domains that will be tested in an OtuB1-/- background. Our current data support a role of OtuB1 in regulation of SMAD2/3 complex-mediated signaling and cytokine response, which in turn is hijacked by influenza to remove ubiquitin chains from viral proteins to prevent their degradation. Understanding the role of OtuB1 will not only shed new light on the mechanisms installed in virus infection, but also provides a promising opportunity for therapeutic interventions. 流感病毒已经成为全球威胁，造成世界各地数百万人的发病率和死亡率。为了在宿主中建立感染和复制，流感病毒已经发展了各种策略来劫持宿主细胞因子并抑制宿主免疫应答。该提案旨在了解流感病毒劫持宿主细胞机制逃避免疫应答的机制，这将有助于今后研究发病机制和抗病毒治疗的发展。 关键问题1：我们对流感病毒生物发生过程中主要因素被利用的信息非常有限。特别是对病毒出口过程的机理理解受到严重限制。使用甲型流感病毒和功能性蛋白质组学筛选策略，我们确定了流感病毒感染引起的几种脱嘌呤类。一种这样的酶是OtuB1，其还被发现是流感聚合酶PB2蛋白的相互作用剂。我们的目标是确定这是否是在一系列流行性感冒病毒株（包括季节性和致病性变种）中被劫持的普遍因素。此外，我们的目的是了解是否是一种宿主限制性蛋白，其功能是激活信号通路以提醒免疫系统。为此，我们建议在感染的背景下对其表达，定位和周转进行详细的生化表征。 关键问题2：蛋白质的泛素化已经成为调节功能的显着手段，包括通过形成亚细胞复合物以及通过引发蛋白质降解来开启和关闭特异性酶活性。当感染流感时，OtuB1被特异性激活，并最终被降解。我们的目标是确定OtuB1在感染背景下的目标，以及通过产生敲除细胞（使用最近开发的CRISPR / Cas9策略）在流感感染过程中如何发挥作用，并对流感病毒进行挑战。 关键问题3：OtuB1在细胞核和细胞溶质感染后发生亚细胞再分配。与其相互作用的宿主因素的整体概述将使我们了解在感染流感过程中蛋白质复合物的运行情况。为此，我们打算将BioID（一种接近依赖性标记策略）应用于流感感染细胞核和细胞溶质中的相互作用。这种蛋白质组学方法将全面概述OtuB1在正常生理学和病毒感染过程中发挥作用的生化途径。

17112617.label: Realisation of objectives
17112617.value: Specific objective 1: Intracellular expression and turnover of OTUB1 upon virus infection. We completed this section and provided a summary in the previous progress report. We had demonstrated that a chemical proteomics based screening strategy, using an activity-based probe targeting DUBs is extremely efficient in uncovering those that are functionally relevant in cellular contexts such as in host-pathogen interactions and immune signaling cascades. OTUB1 was identified in both screens (in TCR signaling as well as in influenza infection) supporting its role in a signaling pathway that might be a target of influenza virus. To establish whether this occurred in a strain specific manner, we detected bulk ubiquitylation in IAV-infected A549 cells expressing wild-type ubiquitin. K48-, K63-, and M1-linked ubiquitylated proteins from mock- and virus-infected cells were isolated by linkage-specific tandem ubiquitin-binding entities (TUBEs). Although K48-linked ubiquitylation was consistently lower in infected cells, K63-ubiquitylated species were more pronounced in IAV-infected cells compared with mock-infected cells. To isolate the infection specific DUBs, mock- and H1N1 pandemic IAV-infected primary lung epithelial cells or A549 cells were permeabilized using perfringolysin O and activated DUBs were isolated with ubiquitin-vinylmethylester (Ub-vme) carrying a TAMRA or hemagglutinin (HA) tag. Ub-vme-reactive materials from control and infected cells were resolved by SDS-PAGE and visualized by fluorescence scanning or enriched on anti-HA beads first and detected by silver staining. Potential candidates were identified by trypsin digestion, mass spectrometry, and spectral counting of peptides on immunoprecipitated material. We validated the mass spectrometry (MS) hits in lysates prepared from mock-infected, IAV-infected, or IFN-I-treated samples by immunoblotting and detected a shift in molecular weight in proteins that reacted with Ub-vme. Our investigations revealed that OTUB1 is upregulated and redistributed from the nucleus to the cytosol upon flu infection, culminating in its degradation at the proteasome. In the first aim, we performed a detailed biochemical characterization on its expression, subcellular localization and turnover in infected cells as a function of time. Analyses on the kinetics of its expression, intracellular transport and degradation also allowed us to determine its role in innate immune signaling, specifically in IRF and NFkB activation. In addition, we validated the role of OTUB1 as a general phenomenon with different strains of influenza virus (exhibiting different pathogenicity) as well as other RNA viruses such as Zika, but not with DNA viruses such as Vaccinia. Findings from this aim was published in Cell Reports (Jahan et al, Cell Reports, 2020). Specific objective 2: Genetic validation of OtuB1-function in the context of virus infection Apart from the biochemical characterization of endogenous OtuB1 in infected cells, we aimed to create OtuB1 knock-out cells using the CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing strategy. These were created in A549 lung epithelial cells as a constitutive deletion. OtuB1-/- cells were then challenged with different strains of influenza virus to determine whether its deficiency has any effect on virus production. To verify specificity and rule out off-target effects, rescue of the knock-out gene were performed by reconstitution of wildtype OtuB1 in the OtuB1-/- background. Infection by RNA viruses and subsequent RIG-I signaling is accompanied by activation of NF-κB and IRF3, which can be detected by phosphorylation of the p65 subunit of NF-κB and dimerization of IRF3. To monitor their activities in OTUB1−/− and rOTUB1 cells, we measured the appearance of IRF3 dimers and phosphorylated p65. In both instances, OTUB1 deficiency resulted in loss of these activities, but they were rescued in rOTUB1 cells. Defective IRF3 activity was also verified in primary lung epithelial cells upon small interfering RNA (siRNA)-mediated depletion of OTUB1. To establish how universal this effect was, we infected A549dual cells (WT, OTUB1−/−, RIG I−/−, or OTUB1−/−RIG I−/− double knockout) with different strains of IAV, Zika, encephalomyocarditis virus (EMCV), and a DNA virus (Vaccinia) in the sample set. Supernatants collected at different time intervals were quantitated for NF-κB activity by measuring the absorbance of secreted alkaline phosphatase at 620 nm. For all strains of influenza as well as for poly(I:C) treatment, a significant reduction in NF-κB activity was recorded in OTUB1−/− cells, comparable with RIG-I−/− cells. No additive effect was noted in the double knockout cells, suggesting that they most likely function in the same pathway. As with NF-κB activation, OTUB1−/− cells displayed significantly diminished IRF activity upon infection with different strains of influenza as well as with poly(I:C). Findings from this aim was published in Cell Reports (Jahan et al, Cell Reports, 2020). Specific objective 3: Deciphering the biochemical pathway of OtuB1 function using proximity dependent labeling OtuB1 exhibits dual localization in the context of flu infection; it shuttles between the nucleus and the cytosol depending on the timeframe in the virus life cycle. To determine with what OTUB1 associates in IAV-infected cells, we measured its localization by confocal imaging and neighboring partners by proximity-based labeling. In uninfected cells, OTUB1 resided largely in the nucleus; upon infection, it relocalized from the nucleus to the cytosol and mitochondrial membranes. A significant fraction colocalized with TOMM20, a mitochondrial marker, specifically in infected cells but not in mock-infected cells. Phosphorylation-defective mutants of OTUB1 S16A (phospho-deficient) and S16E (phosphomimetic), were enriched in the cytosol and nucleus, respectively, whereas C91S, the catalytically dead variant, and the D88A mutant, defective in binding E2 enzymes, displayed a similar intracellular distribution as that of the wild type. To identify its potential interactors in mock- and IAV-infected cells, we first expressed a BioID-OTUB1 construct in the wild-type (WT) or OTUB1−/− background and cultured cells in biotin-supplemented medium. Biotinylated proteins were captured by streptavidin beads, resolved by SDS-PAGE, and identified by LC-MS/MS. Identified candidates were sorted by functional enrichment of pathways using Ingenuity Pathway Analysis. The isolated candidates indicated that OTUB1 preferentially associated with components of the RIG-I signaling pathway in IAV-infected samples compared with mock-infected samples, in which it primarily associated with RNA helicases in the nucleus. To confirm the MS data, we separated lysates from mock- and IAV-infected cells by sedimentation on glycerol gradients, where OTUB1 co-migrated with high-molecular-weight RIG-I oligomers in IAV-infected but not in mock-infected cells. To determine whether formation of the RIG-I signaling complex requires OTUB1, we transduced myc-RIG-I into RIG-I−/− A549 cells carrying a deletion of OTUB1 or expressing a WT copy and infected with H1N1(pdm). IFN-α production was completely lost in OTUB1−/− cells and rescued when reconstituted with WT OTUB1 but also partially in cells stably expressing myc-RIG-I, suggesting that compensatory mechanisms might be activated in these cells. Findings from this aim was published in Cell Reports (Jahan et al, Cell Reports, 2020).

17112617.label: Major findings and research outcome
17112617.value: In this study, we applied activity-based profiling to uncover DUBs that function during influenza A virus (IAV) infection and identified OTUB1 as a critical regulator of RIG-I activation. We established that OTUB1 is key for optimal RIG-I signaling and functions via a coordinated mechanism of hydrolyzing K48 chains and forming an E2-repressive complex. Knockout of OTUB1 resulted in loss of oligomeric RIG-I, disassembly of the signaling complex, and failure of NF-kB and interferon regulatory factor (IRF) activation in IAV-infected cells. We recapitulated this phenomenon in a reconstituted cell-free system to define the underlying mechanism of OTUB1 function in this pathway. Hydrolysis of K48 polyubiquitin chains and sequestration of UBCH5c by OTUB1 were prerequisites for K63 polyubiquitylation of RIG-I. Catalytically inactive OTUB1 displayed partial loss of IRF3 dimerization; on the other hand, mutants that did not form the E2-repressive complex or failed to relocalize to mitochondrial membranes abolished IRF3 activation. This phenomenon was antagonized by IAV NS1, which triggered proteasomal degradation of newly synthesized OTUB1. Our results therefore provide fundamental insights into the mechanism of maintaining fidelity and optimal magnitude in the RIG-I signal transduction cascade and highlight the complex interplay between immune responses and viral antagonism.These findings were published in Cell Reports (Jahan et al, Cell Reports, 2020)

17112617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17112617.value: Our current research focuses on the cross talk of OTUB1 with that of other deubiquitylases that have been shown to play a role in RIG-I signaling and in influenza A virus infection. We are also investigating whether the interaction of NS1 and OTUB1 can be targeted to boost innate immune responses against flu infection.

17112617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17112617.value: Deubiquitylases (DUBs) regulate critical signaling pathways at the intersection of host immunity and viral pathogenesis. Although RIG-I activation is heavily dependent on ubiquitylation, systematic analyses of DUBs that regulate this pathway have not been performed. Using a ubiquitin C-terminal electrophile, we profiled DUBs that function during influenza A virus (IAV) infection and isolated OTUB1 as a key regulator of RIG-I-dependent antiviral responses. Upon infection, OTUB1 relocalized from the nucleus to mitochondrial membranes together with RIG-I, viral PB2, and NS1. Its expression depended on competing effects of interferon stimulation and IAV-triggered degradation. OTUB1 activated RIG-I via a dual mechanism of K48 polyubiquitin hydrolysis and formation of an E2-repressive complex with UBCH5c. We reconstituted this mechanism in a cell-free system comprising [35S]IRF3, purified RIG-I, mitochondrial membranes, and cytosol expressing OTUB1 variants. A range of IAV NS1 proteins triggered proteasomal degradation of OTUB1, antagonizing the RIG-I signaling cascade and antiviral responses. Our study defines the intricate balance that exists for optimal immune signaling and viral strategies of dysregulating these pathways.

The sprouts grew significantly faster when SCAPs were encapsulated within the hydrogel, reaching their maximum length on day 7, while those with no SCAPs encapsulation took 12 days. In the group of 5% GelMA hydrogel seeded with a 1:1 cell ratio in a .04 taper microchannel, the length of HUVECs sprouting was significantly longer in the middle portion (201.1 ± 24.1 μm) compared with the apical portion (150.3 ± 14.3 μm) and the coronal portion (70.3 ± 9.6 μm) (P < 0.05). 2. Objectives 1 and 2 have been fully achieved in vivo studies. 2.1 Analysis of pulp-like tissue In the in vivo study, root segments with an engineered construct with a tapered microchannel generated full-length regenerated pulp-like tissue at 4 weeks after transplantation, and there was no significant difference between the .04 taper and .06 taper groups. While in the group of parallel channels, pulp tissue only grows to about half the length of the root canal. In contrast, root fragments without microchannels contain little regenerated pulp tissue, less than a third of the length of the canal. This result indicated that tapered microchannel could improve the ability to integrate into the host tissues and vasculature and allows the crown tissue which is away from the apical foramen to survive. In these two groups, the concentration of GelMA was 7.5% and 10%, the pulp tissue generated had hydrogel residue. And in the group of 7.5% GelMA, pulp-like tissue grew close to the entire length of the root canal, although the GelMA was not completely degraded. However, in the 10% GelMA group, pulp-like tissue only grew to a third of the length of the canal. These results indicate that the degradation rate of the hydrogel can affect the growth of root canal tissue. 2.2 Analysis of neovascularization The development of the microvessels was examined using hematoxylin and eosin staining. It was shown that enhanced vasculature was observed in the engineering tissue construct with tapered microchannels. The coronal portion of the root canal in the groups with tapered microchannels had a high density of microvessels and the middle of the root canal had larger vessels, probably created by pre-implanted microchannel remnants, and the apical part of the root canal had larger vessels were observed, which connected the host tissue to the implanted tissue scaffold. Even though the crown of the root canal was not covered by the formation of pulp tissue in the parallel microchannel group, the longitudinal section of the blood vessels created by the microchannels in the core of the root canal was still visible. In 7.5% GelMA hydrogels, the formation of microvessels was similar to that in 5% GelMA, but the number of microvessels was significantly reduced. In the 10% hydrogels and no microchannels group, pulp-like tissue was much shorter and had fewer microvessels. Quantification of the number of vascular lumens showed significantly more (p<0.05) vessels in the groups with microchannels than in the groups without microchannels, and the groups of 5% GelMA hydrogel also showed significantly more microvessels than the groups of 7.5% and 10% GelMA hydrogel. Immunohistochemistry demonstrated that almost all of the transplants lumen structures stained positively for human CD31, proving that ECs and SCAPs implanted on the inner surface of the microchannel within GelMA scaffolds, not only the host's murine cells, were responsible for producing the microvessels. The staining in the groups with tapered microchannel was more pronounced than in groups without microchannel, and the vessels created by 7.5% and 10% GelMA also showed positive staining for human CD31. In parallel channel and no channel groups, the number and intensity of the CD31 staining were less than in the other groups. GelMA scaffold sections were immunohistochemically stained with the human anti-α-SMA antibody in order to further analyze the function and localization of SCAPs in the transplants. The α-SMA -positive cells were seen to surround the lumen structures, demonstrating the continued maturation of the vascular system and the assistance provided by SCAPs in maintaining the development of microvessels.

17112717.label: Major findings and research outcome
17112717.value: 1. This study developed a simple and easy-to-operate microchip to create microchannels inside the GelMA hydrogel. Microchannels fabricated with 5%, 7.5%, and 10% GelMA hydrogels had sufficient mechanical strength to support the preservation of their spatial structures. However, microchannels created by less than 5% of GelMA hydrogel collapsed immediately after removing the sacrificial templates. 2. With the increase of its concentration, GelMA hydrogel inhibited the cell abilities of elongation and migration inside the gel, and the formation of networks with neighboring cells. Cell survival rate was significantly reduced in 10% or 15% gel compared to that in 5%. Our results showed that 5% GelMA hydrogel was the most suitable concentration for HUVECs to sprout inside, with an average sprouting length of 200 µm. When the concentration of GelMA hydrogel increased to 7.5%, HUVECs could grow around the microchannel, but without observed cell invasion into the hydrogel. In 10% hydrogel, the perfused cells could not form a complete layer of endothelial cells on the inner surface of the microchannels, let alone sprout. 3. Compared with the parallel and .06 taper microchannels, HUVECs in the .04 taper microchannels grew and extended much longer into the hydrogel. According to the calculation, the inner surface areas of the .04 taper are the smallest, and that of the microchannel with the .06 taper is the largest. To further compare the angiogenic sprouting at different portions of the microchannel, it was clearly shown that the middle portion of the .04 taper microchannels had greater angiogenic sprouts. 4. Single culture of HUVECs in the microchannel only formed the endothelial layer on the inner surface of the microchannel after being cultured for 12 days, and barely almost no cell growing inside GelMA hydrogel. In the process of coculture of HUVECs-GFP and SCAPs, it was observed that after the formation of the endothelial layer, the endothelial cells invaded the hydrogel and formed angiogenic sprouts. Prominent sprouting structures were observed around the fourth day of culture, and the maximum length was reached on the twelfth day. HUVECs and SCAPs cell combination at a 1:1 ratio produced greater angiogenic sprouting in the microchannels. 4. Root segments with an engineered construct with a tapered microchannel generated full-length regenerated pulp-like tissue at 4 weeks after transplantation. This result indicated that tapered microchannel could improve the engineered construct to integrate into the host tissues and vasculature.

17112717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17112717.value: This study provided a unique engineered scaffold for pulp regeneration by fabricating tapered microchannels to generate prevascularized structures. The findings indicated that tapered microchannel played a significant role in connecting the host blood vessels with the grafted prevascularized scaffold during the angiogenic process in vitro. The findings also showed that 5% GelMA hydrogel would be the most suitable concentration, on the one hand, it can provide a suitable microenvironment for cell growth, proliferation, and differentiation, on the other hand, it can also have enough strength to support microchannels and degrade at a proper time. Our results highlight the significance of designing a microchannel that offers enough nutrition and oxygen, both are beneficial for dental pulp regeneration. Future transplantation research may find fabrication of the prevascularized pulp tissue constructs with microchannel to be potentially clinically applicable.

17112717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17112717.value: Fabrication of prevascularized scaffold with taper during the angiogenic process plays a significant role in dental pulp regeneration. Our studies showed that the fabrication of 0.04 taper fluidic microchannels with 5% (w/v) GelMA hydrogel encapsulated with SCAPs and the coculture of SCAPs and HUVECs-GFP at a ratio of 1:1 within the microchannel were found to be the optimal condition to enhance angiogenesis. This finding demonstrate a novel cell-based strategy of formulating hydrogel scaffolds with fluidic microchannels to study the process of endothelialization and angiogenic sprouting. Furthermore, this mode simulates canal morphology and ensures that the seeded cells within the wider coronal portion of the pulp construct could have sufficient vascular exchange with the nearest microchannel. Our findings emphasize the value of creating a microchannel with adequate nutrition and oxygen, both of which contribute to the creation of the optimum environment for dental pulp regeneration. The construction of the constructs of prevascularized pulp tissue by this technology may be informative for future transplantation studies.

17113117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17113117.value: Liver cancer (hepatocellular carcinoma, HCC) is one of the most prevalent malignancies worldwide and in Hong Kong. Because of the late diagnosis of the disease, the prognosis of HCC patient is often undesirable. So far, the chemotherapy option for HCC is also extremely limited. Cancer Stem Cell (CSC), which represents a subpopulation of cancer cells with stem-like properties, has been suggested to play a central role in carcinogenesis and to contribute significantly to the relapse and chemo-drug resistance of cancers. The cell surface marker, CD133/Prominin-1, has been identified as a biomarker for CSC in various cancers, including liver. Very little is known about the function of CD133 and how it promotes cancer formation, but CD133 was found in membrane particles released from microvilli, primary cilia and midbodies of neural progenitor and epithelial cells, suggesting a role in intercellular communication. Centrosome, also known as microtubule-organizing center in cells, is a subcellular structure that regulates diverse cellular processes, such as cell movement, polarity and proliferation. Aberrant increase in centrosome number is a common phenomenon in cancer cells and is closely associated with cancer formation by inducing chromosome instability. However, the reason why the centrosome number is increased in cancers remains elusive. Recently, a novel centrosome protein, we named TAX1BP2, was identified as a blocker for centrosome amplification in cells. Further analyses show that loss of TAX1BP2 expression will result in HCC formation and an increase in chemo-resistance of HCC cells. To understand the role of CD133 in hepatocarcinogenesis, we expressed CD133 in HCC cells and found that CD133 could significantly promote cell growth. In addition, we showed that deletion of C-terminal tail region of CD133 completely abolished the translocation of CD133 onto the cell surface. Upon prolong expression of CD133, a high percentages of cells were found to have abnormal increase in chromosome and centrosome numbers, suggesting that CD133 causes chromosome instability in cells. Interestingly, CD133 also repress the expression of TAX1BP2 at both transcript and protein levels, offering a mechanism by which CD133 promotes centrosome amplification. With these observations, we propose to further investigate how CD133 promotes cancer formation. The mechanism by which CD133 enhances chromosome instability and whether downregulation of TAX1BP2 is important for the effect of CD133 will be examined. Results derived from our study should provide novel insight in the tumorigenic role of CD133 and may develop CD133 as a novel molecular target for HCC therapy. 肝癌（HCC）是一種在全球範圍以及在香港最流行的惡性腫瘤疾病。由於該疾病通常在晚期才能被發現，對於肝癌病人的預斷并不理想。至今，對于肝癌化療的方案也十分有限。癌幹細胞（CSC）是一種有幹細胞特性的癌細胞亞群，已被認為在癌症形成、複發以及其對化學藥物耐藥性起到重要的作用。CD133/突結合蛋白1是一種細胞表面標誌物, 在肝癌以及其他多種癌症中被認為是癌幹細胞生物標誌物。對於CD133的功能及其如何促進癌症形成，學界所知的甚少，但CD133能夠在從微絨毛，原發性纖毛和神經祖細胞和上皮細胞釋放的膜顆粒中被發現，表明其在細胞間通訊中有所作用。 中心體，也被稱為細胞中的微管組織中心，是一種調節細胞運動，極性和細胞增殖等多種細胞進程的亞細胞結構。中心體數量的異常增加是一種癌細胞中常見的現象，並且與通過誘導染色體不穩定而產生的癌症密切相關。然而，中心體的數量在癌細胞中增加的原因仍然不為人所知。最近，我們新發現了一種中心體蛋白並且命名為TAX1BP2。我們證明其能夠抑制細胞內中心體數目的增加，且在進一步的研究中發現失去TAX1BP2的表達將導致肝癌的形成和肝癌細胞的化學抗藥性的增加。 為了解CD133在肝癌形成中的作用，我們在肝癌細胞中表達CD133并發現CD133可以顯著促進細胞生長。另外，我們發現移除了羧基末端尾段的CD133能夠完全消除其向細胞表面的移位。在CD133長期表達的情況下，高比例的細胞被發現擁有染色體與中心體數目的異常增加的表徵，表明CD133能引起細胞染色體不穩定。同時，在轉錄和蛋白層面上CD133抑制了TAX1BP2的表達，為CD133促進中心體擴增提供了機理。基於以上的觀察，我們提議進一步研究CD133如何促進癌症形成，包括研究CD133增強染色體不穩定性的機制，以及TAX1BP2的表達下調對CD133其作用的重要性。我們研究的成果將會對CD133在癌症形成中的作用提供新的見解，並可能使CD133成為肝癌標靶治療中的新對象。

17113117.label: Realisation of objectives
17113117.value: Objective 1: To characterize the function of CD133 in HCC cells, we generated stable inducible CD133 expressing clones of wild type and three cytoplasmic domain deletion mutants (CD133 ΔC1 (cytoplasmic domain (CD) 1, a.a. 130-158), CD133 ΔC2 (CD 2, a.a. 455-487) and CD133 ΔC3 (CD3, a.a. 814-end)) in HLE and PLC/PRF/5 (PLC) HCC cells. First, to examine the localization of the CD133 deletion mutants, deletion mutants were fused with a C-terminal- red fluorescence protein. Interestingly, deletion of CD1 yielded a mutant with very low, if not no, expression, indicating that this region may be important for the stability of CD133. Using immunofluorescence staining, we observed that while the wild-type (WT) CD133 was primarily found on the cell surface, both CD133 ΔC2 and CD133 ΔC3 mutants were localized in the Golgi apparatus. To investigate the role of CD133 in HCC tumorigenicity, the cell proliferation rate of stable inducible CD133 expressing clones were examined. In both HLE and PLC clones, overexpression of CD133 promoted the HCC cell proliferation significantly, whereas the CD133 ΔC2 and CD133 ΔC3 did not show any difference in the proliferation rate as compared to the uninduced controls, suggesting that the CD2 and 3 are important for cell proliferative property. Apart from the cell proliferation assay, the anchorage-independent growth of stable clones was assessed by soft agar growth assay. The number of colonies formed in WT was significantly higher than that of ΔC2 and ΔC3, indicating that CD133 promotes anchorage-independent growth. To address if CD133 promotes HCC cell invasiveness, matrigel invasion assay was used. The induced CD133 WT cells had a significantly increased number of migrated cells compared to the uninduced control. Meanwhile, the deletion of CD2 and 3 abolished the effect on the invasiveness of the HCC cells. To address if CD133 promotes the stemness property of HCC cells, the tumorsphere formation efficiency (TFE) test was conducted to estimate the self-renewal and multipotency of the HCC cells. In stable inducible CD133 HLE clones, the CD133 WT overexpressing cells maintained a statistically significantly higher TFE when compared to uninduced cells, suggesting that CD133 overexpression upregulated the stemness nature of HCC cells. For CD133 mutants, CD133 ΔC2 overexpression upregulated TFE, but was lower than the WT, while ΔC3 completely abolished the promotion in stemness. A similar trend was also observed in PLC cells, except that the increase in TFE was not as drastic. To further understand the mechanism by which CD133 promotes the stemness of HCC cells, several stemness-related transcription factors, i.e. OCT4, KLF4 and SOX2, were examined. Surprisingly, the expressions of these TFs were not correlated with the expression of the CD133. To understand how CD133 promotes HCC formation, we also examined the potential role of CD133 in the HIPPO/YAP signalling pathway. We observed that in the CD133 induced cell, the phosphorylated-YAP/total-YAP (p-YAP/T-YAP) ratio was lower than the uninduced control. Importantly, the CD133 ΔC3 cells did not show a decrease in the p-YAP/T-YAP ratio, indicating that the cytoplasmic tail is required for the regulation of YAP. Using immunofluorescence staining, a significantly higher population of cells with nuclear YAP was observed in induced CD133 cells, suggesting that CD133 stabilizes YAP, possibly promoting cell proliferation and stemness. For the anti-apoptotic effect, we did not observe any significant changes in the apoptotic rate in the induced CD133 expressing cells as compared to uninduced control. Objective 2: To characterize the effect of CD133 on chromosome instability, the metaphase spreading, FACS flow cytometry analysis and confocal immunofluorescence staining experiments were performed using the inducible CD133 expressing HCC cells. The metaphase experiment showed that induction of CD133 resulted in a significant increase in the number of cells with a higher amount of chromosomes when compared with naïve cells. Using FASC flow cytometry analysis, we further verified that upregulation of CD133 promoted aneuploidy in CD133 expressing HCC cells. With the induction of CD133, we observed a higher proportion of cells that contained multiple centrosomes and divided in a multipolar fashion as compared to uninduced control. To evaluate the potential gene regulated by CD133, we have employed the cDNA microarray approach. Using the Human Gene Expression Microarray (v3 8×60K Microarray Kit) and the RNAs extracted from uninduced and induced WT and CD133 ΔC3 deletion mutant clones, we showed that in the WT clone, the expression of 153 genes was changed, whereas, in the CD133 ΔC3 deletion clones, only 132 genes were altered. To validate the cDNA microarray data, qPCR analyses were performed on selected genes, including OASL, ISG15, JAG1 and CENP-T. Interestingly, CENP-T was reported to correlate with centrosome over-duplication. Further analysis was continued to validate the result. To investigate the effect of CD133 on chromosome instability, flow cytometry was used to analyse the cell cycle profile and the aneuploidy status. The result showed that CD133 expression did not affect cell cycle patterns. However, the overexpression of CD133 WT led to a moderate increase in the aneuploidy. Metaphase spreading analysis was also used to confirm the effect of CD133 on aneuploidy. Both CD133 WT and ΔC2 mutant, but not ΔC3, increased the number of chromosomes, suggesting that the cytoplasmic tail is important for the chromosome instability induced by CD133. To examine if there was centrosome amplification, immunofluorescence staining was performed. Only cells overexpressing CD133 WT exhibited an increased population cell with multiple centrosomes. Also, a population of cells with multipolar phenotype was observed in CD133 WT and ΔC2, but not ΔC3 mutant cells. Overall, these results suggested that CD133 promotes chromosome instability and the C-terminal cytoplasmic tail of CD133 plays a critical role in these effects. Objective 3: To understand how CD133 promotes centrosome amplification and aneuploidy, we examined the effect of CD133 on the expression of TAX1BP2. TAX1BP2 is a centrosome linker protein that plays an important role in centrosome amplification and tumour suppression. The results showed that the expression of CD133 WT and ΔC3 downregulated endogenous TAX1BP2 levels, but not the ΔC2, suggesting that CD2 is required for the regulation of TAX1BP2. Since TAX1BP2 was previously reported to suppress HCC tumorigenicity through p38/p53/p21 pathway, the p53 level was probed by Western blotting. Consistently, downregulation of p53 was observed in CD133 WT and ΔC3 expressing cells. To examine the transcription regulation of TAX1BP2 by CD133, we cloned the promoter of TAX1BP2 and performed the luciferase reporter assay. The result showed that CD133 suppressed TAX1BP2 transcriptionally. To understand if CD133 affects the degradation of TAX1BP2 by proteasomal ubiquitination degradation, we performed the ubiquitination assay. However, there was no difference in the ubiquitination level of TAX1BP2 in the presence and absence of CD133. Finally, we characterized the effect of CD133 in chemo-resistance by performing the survival assays. The stable CD133 expressing cells with or without Dox induction were treated with chemotherapeutic drugs, including cisplatin, doxorubicin, 5-Fu, in an increasing dosage and duration manner. Surprisingly, we did not observe any significant change in the survival rate of the cells. Overall, we have achieved most of the aims set out in the proposal. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, our animal experiments were greatly disrupted many times. Thus, we have extended our work to study the effect of TAX1BP2 on HBX-mediated HCC and the role of centrosomal kinase, PLK4 in the pathogenesis of HCC. Currently, the manuscript of CD133 is under preparation.

17113117.label: Major findings and research outcome
17113117.value: Despite numerous studies attempting to isolate CD133 positive cancer stem cells from cancer samples, few studies characterize the functional role of CD133 in tumorigenesis. This project provides a new perspective to investigating this field. Our data confirmed that CD133 plays a role in cell proliferation, invasion, stemness and centrosome amplification, not simply a cancer stem cell surface marker protein. Our data offer insight into the molecular mechanism by which cancer stem cell promotes HCC tumorigenesis. With the investigations through different truncated mutants of the CD133 protein, we showed that the cytoplasmic domains are crucial to the functions of CD133, including cellular localization, stemness and centrosome-related phenotypes. We demonstrated that deletion of cytoplasmic domains 2 and 3 abolished the plasma membrane localization of CD133. Removal of cytoplasmic domain 3 likely affects the glycosylation of CD133, leading to the Golgi apparatus retention. Further investigation showed that CD133 inhibited the phosphorylation of YAP and enhanced the nuclear localization of YAP. This result suggested that YAP may act downstream of CD133 to promote the transcription of genes that extend the tumorigenic activity. Our result also demonstrated that the expression of CD133 enhanced the efficiency of sphere formation in the HCC cells. It is noted worthwhile that the cancer stemness property can also be enhanced by the Hippo signalling pathway when CD133 is overexpressed. In our study, we observed that the numbers of chromosomes and centrosomes of HCC cells were perturbed by the expression of CD133. The overexpression of CD133 induces an increase in aneuploidy. It also promotes multiple centrosomes and multipolar mitotic division. TAX1BP2, a tumour suppressor, is found to be downregulated by CD133. Furthermore, p53 was also inhibited by the overexpression of CD133. As previously reported, TAX1BP2 can induce the activation of p53/p21 pathways. Thus, CD133 is shown to inhibit the p53 pathway and suppress the centrosome surveillance ability. Functional domains of CD133 were also examined in the above research. The cytoplasmic domain 3 was found to be the most crucial region of the protein. With the deletion of the cytoplasmic domain 3, CD133 lost its localisation to the cell surface, and such mislocalization may account for the incapability of the deletion mutant to promote proliferation, invasiveness, cancer stemness, aneuploidy and centrosome amplification. In summary, CD133 is found not only as a potential cancer stem cell marker but also plays a crucial role in maintaining tumorigenicity and stemness of HCC cells.

17113117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17113117.value: The detailed molecular mechanism of how centrosomes were dysregulated, under the influence of CD133, can be further investigated. Whether it is related to the dysregulation of the Hippo pathway, particularly the MST2 kinase, warrant further investigation. In addition, the dysregulation of centrosomes is not limited to the numerical level but also their structure and functions in vivo. Since the Hippo pathway is important for the pathogenesis of liver cancer, it is critical to better understand the interplay between the Hippo pathway and CD133 expression. Further investigation on the regulation of TAX1BP2 by CD133 at transcriptional, translational, post-translational and stability levels should be performed. Apart from identifying the regulatory components that lead to the downregulation of TAX1BP2, it is also worth dissecting the correlation of the p53/p21 and the CD133 in greater detail. As ectopic overexpression system or doxycycline-inducible expressing system of mammalian cell lines are commonly used in in vitro protein research, it would be ideal if the CRISPR/Cas9 inducible knockout system can be adapted to modify the generic CD133 in HCCs, such that the readout of the functions of CD133 can be investigated. It will also be extremely interesting to verify our findings genetically using the CD133 knockout mouse model.

17113117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17113117.value: Cancer is a global health problem that causes thousands of lives. Liver cancer is one of the most fatal cancers locally. Although surgery and radiotherapy ablation are curative treatments for the early liver cancer patient, these therapies may not be applicable for advanced-stage patients. Therefore, a new treatment strategy is much awaited. Recently, a specific population of cells in a tumour, called cancer stem cells, has been recognized as a major cause of metastasis and drug resistance. Here, we showed that a protein, called CD133, which is commonly known as a biomarker for cancer stem cells, plays an important role to maintain tumours overtimes. CD133 promotes cell growth, increases cell mobility and induces abnormal cell division by generating an excess number of the centrosome, an important cellular regulator of cell division. An abnormal number of centrosomes results in inaccurate chromosome segregation, leading to uneven distribution of chromosomes in the divided daughter cells. Our data suggest that this dysregulation is due to the inhibition of another protein, TAX1BP2, which suppresses cancer growth. Therefore, our result leads a direction in not only using CD133 as a marker to identify cancer stem cells but also as a potential therapeutic target.

17113217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17113217.value: 黃酮醇是一類黃酮類化合物，廣泛參與到植物的生長發育過程。大量研究報導表明，食用含有一定量水準的黃酮醇及其他類黃酮類化合物的食品，可有效降低患心血管疾病及癌症風險。近年來，我們實驗室以水稻這一單子葉模式植物為材料，對黃酮類合成途徑的結構基因進行了一系列研究。最近，我們分析到一個編碼黃酮醇合成酶的基因（OsFLS），其編碼的蛋白可以將二氫黃酮醇催化為黃酮醇。將此基因在擬南芥黃酮醇合成基因缺失型突變體中表達，可檢測到黃酮醇的存在。然而，此基因在水稻中的功能卻依然未知。通過對水稻基因表達資料庫及我們的基因表達結果分析，表明水稻的雌蕊和雄蕊特異表達OsFLS和OsF3H。OsF3H編碼上游的黃烷酮3-羥化酶，通過催化黃烷酮為OsFLS提供底物二氫黃酮醇。黃酮醇只可在雄蕊中檢測到，這與OsFLS和OsF3H的基因表達模式一致。此研究的目的在於揭示OsF3H，OsFLS和黃酮醇在雄蕊（花粉）發育中的作用。我們將研究水稻生殖組織中OsF3H和OsFLS的時間和空間表達模式，以及黃酮醇的水平。同時，我們將構建水稻的基因敲出突變體和過表達株系，用於研究黃酮醇的代謝情況以及水稻表型變化。另外，我們將分析一些特異表達於雌蕊的轉錄因子，分析其在調控OsF3H和OsFLS表達方面的功能。這些研究將有助於增加我們對水稻及其他穀物類作物中黃酮醇生物合成過程的瞭解。另外，這些新鑒定到的轉錄因子可能是一類新型的調節雄性不育的重要調控因子。在農業生產中，雄性不育系在雜交育種應用中具有重要價值。此外，OsF3H，OsFLS及其轉錄因子可以運用到植物代謝工程，用於產生富含有益健康的黃酮醇的可食用植物組織，如胚乳，這將有重要經濟價值。

17113217.label: Realisation of objectives
17113217.value: Objective 1 Spatial and temporal investigation of OsF3H and OsFLS gene expression Promoter-GUS transgenic rice plants have been generated for OsF3H and OsFLS, which catalyze the final two steps in flavonol biosynthesis. More than 10 primary transformant lines were obtained for each of them. After confirmation by genomic PCR, primary transformants were propagated to maturity for T1 seed collection. T1 plants for each promoter-GUS construct were grown to maturity to investigate the expression pattern of the respective promoters. GUS staining results demonstrated strong promoter activities in maturing anthers and pollen for both OsF3H and OsFLS genes, hence confirming the anther and pollen expression of these two flavonol biosynthesis genes. Objective 2 Generation of osf3h and osfls by CRISPR-cas9 genome editing and characterization Initially, we proposed to generate CRISPR-Cas9 mutants for the enzymes OsF3H and OsFLS which work sequentially along the flavonol biosynthesis pathway. As we found that knocking out the first enzyme (i.e. OsF3H) is sufficient to block flavonol production, we decided to generate osf3h mutant alone. On the other hand, preliminary metabolite experiments revealed that rice anthers accumulate different structural classes of flavonoids (flavonols, flavanones, flavones, flavone C-glycosides). Accordingly, we expanded the investigation to include other flavonoid biosynthesis branch pathways in order to fully understand the functional roles of different flavonoid classes in male reproduction of rice plants. At the beginning, a publicly available OsCHS1 T-DNA insertion mutant was acquired and characterized. CHS (chalcone synthase) is the key branch-point enzyme catalyzing the first committed step in flavonoid biosynthesis. The OsCHS1 mutant is completely sterile with no seed formation. Hence, the mutation can only be maintained as a heterozygous genotype in rice. Reciprocal crossing of the mutant with wild-type rice demonstrated that OsCHS1 is essential for male fertility. On the other hand, female fertility is unaffected in the OsCHS1 mutant as seed formation was formed when pollinated by wild-type pollen. Using a combination of cytological, histochemical, and scanning electron microscopy analyses, it was determined that anther development and pollen formation in the OsCHS1 mutant were unaffected and pollen size, structure, and viability were also normal when compared to wild-type pollen. On the other hand, mutant pollen germination and tube growth were impaired, hence the pollen tube was not able to travel far enough through the style to reach the ovule for fertilization, resulting in complete sterility (i.e. no seed formation). LC-MS/MS analysis was then employed to determine the flavonoid profile in mature wild-type anthers, which is consisting of different flavonoid structural classes including flavanones, flavonols, flavones, and flavone C-glycosides. However, none of these flavonoids were detected in the OsCHS1 mutant anthers. Analysis of oschs1/+ heterozygous lines shows that pollen flavonoid deposition is a paternal effect and male fertility is independent of the haploid genotypes (i.e. whether it is OsCHS1 or oschs1). To understand which structural classes of flavonoids are involved in male fertility, we conducted detailed analysis of rice mutants for branch-point enzymes of the downstream flavonoid pathways, including flavanone 3-hydroxylase (OsF3H; flavonol pathway entry enzyme), flavone synthase II (CYP93G1; flavone pathway entry enzyme), and flavanone 2-hydroxylase (CYP93G2; flavone C-glycoside pathway entry enzyme). Rice osf3h and cyp93g1 cyp93g2 CRISPR/Cas9 mutants, and cyp93g1 and cyp93g2 T-DNA insertion mutants showed altered flavonoid profiles in anthers, but only the osf3h and cyp93g1 cyp93g2 mutants displayed reduction in seed yield. Our findings indicate that a combination of different classes of flavonoids (flavanones, flavonols, flavones, and flavone C-glycosides) in anthers are essential for complete male fertility in rice. This is in contrast to the critical roles of flavonols alone (e.g. kaempferol and/or quercetin) that has been previously reported for proper pollen functioning in several flowering plant species (e.g. maize and tomato). Objective 3 Identification of transcription factors regulating OsF3H and OsFLS gene expression At the beginning, R2R3-MYB and bHLH transcription factors co-expressed with flavonoid biosynthesis in rice anthers were identified. We have selected 14 MYB genes and 1 bHLH gene for investigations. Initially we attempted to request publicly-available T-DNA mutants for these genes from laboratories in Mainland China and South Korea. However, some mutant seeds were unavailable, some could not be successfully propagated in our lab, and some did not contain the mutations specified in the public records. Subsequently, we decided to use gene-editing technology to generate useful mutants in collaboration with Dr Hongjia Liu at Zhejiang Academy of Agricultural Science (Hangzhou). As such, we constructed CRISPR-Cas9 vectors for the genes mentioned above and performed Agrobacterium-mediated transformation of rice (Nipponbare). After obtaining the primary transformants for the different potential mutant lines, they were propagated to maturity for seed harvest. On average, we obtained 5 independent primary transformants per each CRISPR-Cas9 construct, taking between 9-12 months from rice transformation to collection of T1 seeds. Afterwards, we conducted the labor-intensive and tedious tasks of genomic PCR and DNA sequencing for individual T1 plants for each mutant line. Finally, we were able to identify potentially useful mutations for at least 12 selected genes. They were mainly INDEL mutations that result in frameshift and/or premature termination of translation. For each gene, at least two independent lines with different mutation types were isolated and propagated to maturity to collect the T1 seeds. All the mutations were confirmed to be inheritable in subsequent generations (T1 and T2 so far). Rice transformation, genotyping (PCR and sequencing), and propagation tasks are still ongoing in our laboratory to generate mutant lines for the remaining genes and collect enough seeds for all mutants for further functional investigations. Unfortunately, the project duration coincided with the prolonged period of social events in 2019 and the ongoing global COVID-19 pandemic since early 2020. Although the project was extended for six months, some of the tasks could not be executed successfully. It is estimated that ~50% of this objective has been achieved but this could be compensated by expanded investigations for Objective 2 with at least 150% achievement. Importantly, the collection of mutants generated will be highly useful for further investigations.

17113217.label: Major findings and research outcome
17113217.value: This project has trained one undergraduate student (Gan Yiming BSc 2021; Part C – 10: no. 2) who worked on his final year project and one postgraduate student (Wang Lanxiang PhD 2019; Part C-10: no. 1) who worked on flavonoid biosynthesis in rice and sorghum for her PhD thesis. Previously, it was reported that flavonoids are essential for male fertility in some but not all plant species. A key finding in this project is that flavonoids are essential for male fertility in rice, which in turns is essential for seed formation. We further demonstrated that a combination of different flavonoid classes (including flavanones, flavonols, flavones, and flavone C-glycosides) produced during anther development is apparently required for complete male fertility leading to normal seed yield. These findings have been published in Journal of Experimental Botany (Part C-8: no. 1) and presented at the Plant Biology 2021 Worldwide Submit organized by the American Society of Plant Biologists (Part C-9: no.1). During our investigation of different flavonoid enzymes potentially required for male fertility, we actually discovered that a flavonoid B-ring hydroxylase (CYP75B3) is involved in generating 3’-hydroxylated flavonoids for the biosynthesis of flavone C-glycosides in vegetative tissues. CYP75B3 participates in an independent pathway together with flavanone 2-hydroxylase and C-glycosyl-transferase. The pathway is highly conserved in the grass family leading to the widespread accumulation of flavone C-glycosides in grass biomass. These findings constitute part of the data published in New Phytologist (Part C-8: no. 2) Recently, we have written up a review manuscript on flavonoids in the grass family. Research findings on male fertility generated from this study were discussed in details in this manuscript which is currently under review by Phytochemistry Review (Part C-8: no. 3). Furthermore, this project has resulted in successful international collaboration with Prof. Toshiaki Umezawa and Dr Yuki Tobimatsu of Kyoto University as well as Mainland collaborations with Prof. Fu-Yuan Zhu of Nanjing Forestry University, Dr Hongjia Liu of Zhejiang Academy of Agricultural Sciences, Dr Mo-Xian Chen of Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology (CAS, Shenzhen). Together with their research team members, they participated as co-authors in the publications listed in Part C.

17113217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17113217.value: The CRISPR-Cas9 rice mutants for the different MYB genes represent valuable resources for in planta investigations. Many of them encode uncharacterized MYB transcription factors in rice. Our major research focus is their potential regulatory roles on flavonoid biosynthesis. Preliminary data are being collected and analysed, and they will be used for future grant applications. In addition, we will perform detailed phenotypic analyses to reveal other potential functional roles during growth and development or under different environment and stress conditions. We will actively seek new collaborators specialized in the respective disciplines to work together and submit new funding applications. Meanwhile, the collaborations established with the Mainland Chinese and Japanese scientists have continued despite completion of this project. For example, we have recently published another paper on the characterization of flavonoid and lignin profiles in several flavonoid deficient mutants [Lam et al. (2022) Plant Physiol. 188:1993-2011].

17113217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17113217.value: Rice is a staple food feeding more than 50% of the population in Asia. It is also a research model for the grass family which contains many agriculturally important crops globally. Flavonoids are a large group of widely distributed phytochemicals with diverse functions in plant growth and development. Using an array of genetic, histological, physiological, and biochemical analyses, we established that flavonoids are absolutely required for male reproductive functions in rice. In the absence of flavonoids, pollen germination and tube elongation are impaired, leading to unsuccessful fertilization of female reproductive cells without seed formation. Besides, a combination of different structural classes of flavonoid is important for complete male fertility and hence normal seed yield. This study also established the specific role of a flavonoid modifying enzyme (flavonoid 3’-hydroxylase) in the production of a specific class of flavonoids called flavone C-glycosides which are abundantly present in leaves/stems of rice and other plants in the grass family. Results from this project have advanced our knowledge on rice reproductive biology which provide insights into biotechnological improvement of grain yield. This project also serves to strengthen our collaborations with international and Mainland Chinese scientists with the publication of papers in reputable plant science journals.

17113717.label: Realisation of objectives
17113717.value: 1. To reveal the inhibitory role of VN interneuron subtypes on learned versus reflexive behaviours. Cell type specific expression of functional chemogenetic receptors in inhibitory interneurons (specifically those expressing parvalbumin (PV) or somatostatin (SST)) was established in the bilateral medial vestibular nuclei (MVN) of adult PV-Cre and SST-Cre mice. This was validated by immunohistochemistry as well as whole-cell patch-clamp recording. Significant deficits in Rotarod test and dead reckoning test were observed when activity of PV neurons in the MVN was perturbed by chemogenetics. This demonstrated activity of PV neurons to be crucial for both motor-coordination/motor-learning as well as spatial cognition. On the other hand, activity of SST neurons was not crucial for completion of the tasks. Chemogenetic activation of SST neurons in the MVN, however, was correlated with improved performance in Rotarod test. This suggests that SST neuron activity may play role in motor learning. We then asked whether there existed physiological mechanism to regulate inhibitory interneurons within the MVN. Specific chemogenetic activation of serotonergic projections to the MVN from the dorsal raphe nuclei resulted in transient deficits in motor control of adult rodents. We were able to pinpoint activation of 5-HT1A receptors as the cause for decrease in inhibitory activity of MVN neurons. 2. To delineate selective connectivities of PV, SST and CCK interneurons with VN projection pathways Aim 2 a) To show selective synaptic connection between interneuron and projection neuron Major brain areas receiving projections from the MVN were identified using retrograde tracing with retrobeads (stated in 2a.2 of the Mid-Term Progress Report). This areas included (1) ascending pathway to the forebrain for spatial cognition, (2) descending pathway to the spinal cord for balance and motor coordination, and (3) contralateral pathway to VN on the opposite side. Viral transduction of cell-filling fluorescent protein revealed extensive long-range projections of PV neurons in MVN, both to the contralateral MVN and to neighboring brainstem nuclei. This was different from that of SST neurons, the axons of which were confined within the MVN. Similar labelling of downstream nuclei along the ascending pathway for spatial cognition revealed that SST neurons mediated back-projections from these nuclei back to MVN. Viral-genetic trans-synaptic anterograde tracing was implemented in adult PV-Cre and SST-Cre mice to map the post-synaptic partners of these PV and SST neurons. We found postsynaptic partners of PV neurons in the MVN to project along the ascending pathway for spatial cognition, while postsynaptic partners of SST neurons in the MVN did not. This was validated by electrophysiological recording of the postsynaptic neurons with simultaneous optical excitation of the presynaptic PV or SST neurons in the VN circuit. Our results demonstrated distinct axonal projection pattern and synaptic connectivity between PV and SST neurons in the MVN. We further showed that cholecystokinin (CCK) receptors on inhibitory neurons within the MVN were responsible for triggering activity-dependent presynaptic plasticity during the early postnatal period for formation of functional circuits in the MVN. This suggests that CCK plays a role in tuning developing GABAergic circuits in the MVN. Aim 2 b) To reveal the subcellular clustering and compartmentalization of synapses Tissue clearing technique (OPTIClear) was used to visualize thick sections (2 mm) of MVN of PV-Cre:Ai9 and SST-Cre:Ai9 fluorescent reporter mice in collaboration with Dr LAI Hei Ming (CUHK; Nat Commun 2018; 9:1066). A number of significant hurdles were encountered during investigation of the subcellular clustering and compartmentalization of synapses: (1) cell type-specific sparse labelling needed for accurate 3D reconstruction of the dendritic tree of individual neurons could not be achieved in these transgenic mice, (2) efficiency of immuno-labelling of synaptic compartments was low in cleared samples. Further optimization of imaging techniques for large volume of tissue is required for us to unfold the fine structure of synapses in the VN. Aim 2 c) To find if new PV/SST neurons can be recruited into the VN microcircuit Results from both electrophysiological recording and transynaptic tracing established that PV neurons in the MVN provide strong inhibitory input to SGN-projecting neurons. In vitro whole-cell patch-clamp measurement of inhibitory postsynaptic currents (IPSCs) from these projection neurons (retrogradely labelled from the SGN) was used to assess the change in their connectivity with PV neurons. In adult PV-Cre mice, large IPSC was recorded in projection neurons upon optical excitation of PV neurons. With pre-treatment bicuculline to the MVN at P1 to block GABAergic transmission in the neonatal stage, PV neurons no longer innervated SGN-projecting neurons. We further devised a protocol utilizing targeted vestibular stimulation during periods of pharmacologically enhanced neuronal plasticity to restored PV neuron mediated inhibition of SGN-projecting neurons. These show a key role for neonatal GABAergic transmission in consolidation of inhibitory circuits in the MVN. Results further suggest potential for rewiring of microcircuits by recruitment of new neurons into mature circuits. 3. To demonstrate importance of differential AMPA receptor expression on interneurons to signal processing Aim 3 a) To characterize the AMPA receptor composition of PV, SST and CCK neurons The differential expression of AMPA receptor subunits GluA1 and GluA2 on different interneuron subtypes in the mouse MVN was identified by immunohistochemistry. The number and staining intensity of GluA2 was unchanged over the course of neonatal development (P4-21). Notably, surface expression of GluA1 increased sharply at P7, accompanied by increased incidence of long-term potentiation (LTP). This signifies unsilencing of glutamatergic synapses in early development and coincides with emergence of negative geotaxis, an innate vestibular reflex. As such, we focused on the behavioral consequence of manipulating the developmental timepoint of GluA1 insertion. Aim 3 b) To alter the receptor subunit composition Using a GluA1 carboxyl terminal peptide fused to HIV TAT-peptide for cell membrane penetration, we were able to delay surface insertion of GluA1 from P7 to P9. This resulted in corresponding delay in postnatal emergence of negative geotaxis reflex. Higher order vestibular-dependent functions such as spatial navigation, on the other hand, was permanently deranged in adulthood. This suggests that timely maturation of VN circuits impacts consolidation of spatial cognitive networks along the ascending pathway in forebrain centres.
