17113717.label: Major findings and research outcome
17113717.value: PV neurons are essential for vestibular-dependent behaviour. Bi-directional modulation of PV neuron activity in the MVN with use of chemogenetics both caused significant deficits in vestibular-related behavior. The projection pattern and synaptic connectivity of PV neurons support their role in mediating MVN function as (1) output neurons that convey vestibular information to neighboring brain centres along the ascending pathway for spatial cognition, and (2) interneurons that provide inhibitory gating of output neurons of the MVN. SST neurons within the MVN act as true interneurons, with little to no projections outside the MVN. Postsynaptic partners of SST neurons are also interneurons within the MVN although their identity was not elucidated. Notably, modulation of SST neurons activity by chemogenetics did not significantly impact performance in vestibular-dependent tasks. We further revealed a role for 5-HT1A receptors in the suppression of inhibitory neurotransmission in the VN (Han et al. Journal of Physiology. 2020). This sunveils an intrinsic mechanism for tuning of inhibitory networks in modifying behavioral outcomes. Consolidation of PV neurons synaptic connectivity in the MVN is dependent on neonatal GABAergic transmission. Blockade of GABAergic transmission in the MVN of neonatal mice deranged PV neuron connectivity resulting in significant deficits in both vestibular reflexes and spatial cognitive function. Notably, we show that with suitable sensory stimulation, and sufficient level of neuronal plasticity, it was possible to rewire PV neurons in the MVN to support effective processing of vestibular input leading to rehabilitation of spatial cognitive behavior (Jiang et al. Neuron. Submitted). Results suggest that GABA directs the connectivity of developing circuits before the circuit is switched on towards the end of the fist postnatal week by unsilencing glutamatergic synapses with postsynaptic insertion of GluA1 subunit.

17113717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17113717.value: We developed a protocol for re-wiring of interneuron circuits in the mature MVN. Such a strategy led to rehabilitation of network function in rodents suffering from neurodevelopmental deficits. Further investigation will be needed to find the cell source of these newly established connections within the MVN, and to reveal how reconnection of inhibitory interneuron networks with output neurons supports behavioral recovery. We will demonstrate that targeted sensory training during drug-induced periods of enhanced neural plasticity is applicable across sensory systems for neurorehabilitation via rewiring of interneuron circuitry. As better tissue clearing methods are continually reported, we will take advantage of methods that are more compatible with immunostaining to reveal the fine synaptic/ dendritic structure of diverse interneuron networks in the hindbrain.

17113717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17113717.value: How does one sensory input inform diverse behaviours? We show that two major groups of neurons (those with parvalbumin (PV) versus those with somatostatin (SST)) in the brainstem vestibular nucleus (VN), distinctly process head motion input from the inner ear to support different behaviours. SST neurons only linked to neurons within the VN, the latter neurons themselves also form connections within the VN. On the other hand, PV neurons linked to both neurons within the VN and to neurons that disseminate VN output to surrounding brain areas. Such segregation in neural connectivity underlies distinct behavioral outcomes when either type of neuron was inactivated. Inactivating PV neurons in VN significantly reduced balance and navigation performance of rodent, but inactivating SST neurons did not. Neurotransmission in the neonatal stage is key to correct formation of these neuronal networks. Deranged development of such networks was considered permanent, but we were able to reveal intrinsic modulators that alter neuronal activity in the adult VN, and to devise strategies for rewiring brain circuits in adult rodents for behavioral recovery. Such results form basis for the design of effective strategies in the treatment of diseases resulted from derangement in brain development.

17113817.label: Project Objectives
17113817.value: Delineating the molecular details of BDNF-mediated mitochondrial activity change Besides the central nervous system, a substantial amount of BDNF is also produced in skeletal muscles, but the metabolic roles of myogenic BDNF are not clear. Therefore, we will determine the metabolic activities of BDNF in skeletal muscles through examining the BDNF-induced signaling pathways, gene expression profile, and mitochondrial activity and biogenesis in myotubes. Results obtained will reveal the molecular mechanism of BDNF-induced metabolic modulation in muscles. Studying the metabolic outcomes of muscular BDNF deficiency To assess the functional roles of BDNF in a tissue-specific manner, we will use muscle-specific BDNF knockout (MBKO) mice as the in vivo model. Physiological parameters including growth rate, blood biochemistry, signal transduction, and energy expenditure profiles will be studied in MBKO mice and their Fl/Fl littermates. In addition, changes in these parameters will be measured in mice fed with a high-fat diet to mimic the pathological conditions of energy surplus. Results obtained will provide in vivo data to demonstrate the important roles of muscular BDNF in systemic energy metabolism. Testing the beneficial effects of BDNF signaling restoration in obesity To determine whether restoring BDNF signaling in skeletal muscles can alleviate obesity-related metabolic disorders, TrkB agonist 78DHF will be administered to HFD-induced obese mice. We will monitor their body weight, blood biochemistry, signal transduction in skeletal muscle, and systemic energy metabolism. Results obtained will form a strong pre-clinical basis for developing BDNF-based therapeutic strategies against obesity.

17113817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17113817.value: 線粒體功能障礙會導致脂肪於肌肉中積聚和胰島素抵抗，但我們對引起粒體功能障礙的機制却所知極小。我們的初步實驗數據發現肥胖症會減少肌肉中的腦源性神經營養因子（BDNF）含量，説明了BDNF是一種能調節生陳代謝的肌肉荷爾蒙。我們還發現BDNF能刺激肌肉细胞中的線粒體的呼吸和脂肪氧化反應。BDNF並能激活肌肉中的BDNF受體（TrkB）來提高小鼠體內的能量消耗。此外，我們的試點研究亦發現長期激活小鼠肌肉中的TrkB會減輕高脂飲食導致的線粒體損傷，從而緩和肥胖症和其關連的胰島素抗性。另一方面，敲除小鼠肌肉的BDNF基因會減少肌肉中的線粒體數量，並引致體重增加。基於這些新的數據，我們懷疑肌肉中的BDNF / TrkB通路對粒體穩定性有重大作用，如此一信號通路受阻（例如肥胖症），肌肉的能量與脂肪代謝將會受到影響，導致脂肪於肌肉中績聚，並引發胰島素抗性。為了證明這個假設，我們將會（1）找出BDNF增加線粒體活性變化的分子細節，（2）研究缺乏肌肉BDNF對全身能量代謝的影響，（3）測試補充肌肉BDNF會否減輕肥胖症引致代的謝紊亂。這些研究將會建立一種新的分子機制來解釋肥胖症如何引致肌肉線粒體的功能失調，並有利於發展新的方法來治療肥胖症和其相關的代謝問题。

17113817.label: Realisation of objectives
17113817.value: In this proposal, we hypothesize that the brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) has an autocrine role in skeletal muscle that provokes lipid oxidation and energy expenditure via increasing the activities of CREB, PGC-1α, and AMPK. In obese muscle, expression of BDNF is abolished by the ectopic deposition of circulating lipids. The entire BDNF pathway is thus blunted, leading to reduced mitochondrial content and FA oxidation, which eventually causes further lipid accumulation and insulin resistance. To test this hypothesis, we have performed a variety of molecular, biochemical, and cellular assays in cultured muscle cells. Moreover, the physiological parameters, energy and glucose homeostasis, and signaling mechanism were examined in mice. Specific assays done are listed below: We have delineated the metabolism action of BDNF in muscle cells (Specific Aim 1). Using C2C12 myotubes as the study model, we have assessed the effect of Bdnf depletion and BDNF stimulation on 1) mitochondrial activity using extracellular flux analysis; 2) mitochondrial content using real-time PCR and immunoblotting, 3) expression of key regulators of mitochondrial biogenesis, and 4) the key signaling pathways in mitochondrial biogenesis and lipid oxidation. We have also studied the outcomes of BDNF-depletion in energy metabolism using our homemade muscle-specific BDNF knockout (MBKO) mice. Body composition, tissue weights, blood glucose and lipids [triacylglycerides, (TG), free fatty acid (FFA), and cholesterol], various hormones (leptin, insulin, TNFα), tissue metabolites (TG, FFA, cholesterol, and glycogen) were measured in chow diet- or HFD-fed Fl/Fl and MBKO mice. Systemic energy metabolism, including O2 consumption, CO2 production, energy expenditure, food intake, water uptake, locomotion, lipid oxidation, mitochondrial biogenesis and turnover, were also determined using indirect calorimetry and immunoblotting. The insulin sensitivity in the HFD-fed MBKO has also been examined using glucose/insulin tolerance tests and hyperinsulinemia-euglycemic clamp. Lastly, we have studied the effect of 7,8-dihydroxyflavone (7,8-DHF), the non-peptidyl BDNF mimetic, consumption on body weight regulation. Obese mice were treated with H2O or 7,8-DHF for 3-months, and their body composition, tissue weights, blood glucose and lipids [triacylglycerides, (TG), free fatty acid (FFA), and cholesterol], various hormones (leptin, insulin, TNFα), tissue metabolites (TG, FFA, cholesterol, and glycogen) were compared. Systemic energy metabolism, including O2 consumption, CO2 production, energy expenditure, food intake, water uptake, locomotion, lipid oxidation, mitochondrial biogenesis in 7,8-DHF-treated mice were also determined using indirect calorimetry and immunoblotting. Moreover, we have determined the insulin sensitivity of 7,8-DH-treated mice using glucose/insulin tolerance tests. In summary, we have performed a large number of assays that have thoroughly addressed all Specific Aims set in the proposal.

17113817.label: Major findings and research outcome
17113817.value: In this project, we have proved that muscle-derived BDNF is essential for energy homeostasis in mice. BDNF expression in the glycolytic muscle is enhanced when the mice have fasted. On the other hand, its expression in muscle is reduced when the mice are fed with HFD. These changes of BDFN expression in different metabolic conditions are regulated by the transcription factor CREB. When muscle cells are stimulated with BDNF, the AMPK-ACC, and PGC-1α, PINK1-Parkin pathways are elevated, which increases mitochondrial biogenesis, mitofission, mitophagy, and lipid oxidation. On the other hand, these cellular processes are diminished in muscle cells with BDNF depletion. When the BDNF gene is ablated in the muscle of mice, the muscle of the mice displays less fatty acid oxidation, higher intramyocellular lipid content, more insulin resistance, jeopardized mitophagy, and accumulation of damaged mitochondria. Eventually, the animals thus have lower energy expenditure, poor metabolic flexibility, less contractile force generation and locomotion, and diabetes. These pathological symptoms were further exaggerated when the MBKO mice were fed with HFD. Our data suggested that the pathological features found in MBKO mice are commonly seen in obesity. Thus, we treated diet-induced obese mice with the non-peptidyl BDNF mimetics, 7,8-DHF, and found that this phytochemical effectively alleviates body weight gain and reduces ectopic lipid accumulation, improving insulin sensitivity, enhancing energy expenditure, and facilitating mitophagy via the AMPK-PGC-1α-PINK1 pathways. The results of these data were reported in 4 international journals in “Metabolism - Clinical and Experimental (Wood et al. 2018 87: 113), “Science Signaling (Yang et al. 2019 12: eaau1468)”, “Autophagy (Ahuja et al. 2021 doi: 10.1080/15548627.2021.1985257)”, and “Antioxidants (Pang et al. 2021 10: 179). Moreover, the projects have provided training opportunities to 3 PhD candidates and 1 undergraduate student at the University of Hong Kong.

17113817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17113817.value: We found in this project that BDNF is a novel regulator of AMPK-PGC-1α-PINK1 pathways to regulate mitochondrial dynamics, lipid oxidation, and muscle force generation in skeletal muscle. These pathways are also crucial for fasting-induced metabolic flexibility. Therefore, stimulating the BDNF signaling is useful to treat those diseases with altered lipid oxidation and mitochondrial turnover such as metabolic myopathies. Moreover, these signals are also important in response to metabolic challenges in physiological conditions such as endurance exercise. Hence, the role of BDNF signaling in muscle physiology can be further investigated in these pathological and physiological conditions. More importantly, the current study shows the beneficial actions of the bioavailable 7,8-DHF in muscle, which sets a solid foundation for the future development of 7,8-DHF as a new exercise-improving agent and a drug for obesity and metabolic myopathies treatment.

17113817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17113817.value: Abnormal lipid metabolism is commonly found in the muscle of obesity patients, but the underlying mechanism is not well-understood. In this project, we identified the role of a protein called brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) that links obesity, lipid metabolism, and insulin resistance in skeletal muscle. Using various experimental methods, including cell culture assay, gene expression measurement, biochemical analysis, and knockout mice phenotyping, we demonstrated that BDNF is an essential factor in maintaining the mitochondria activity via the AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK). Moreover, we have shown that enhancing the level of BDNF in the mice could effectively reduce diet-induced body weight gain and insulin resistance. This finding has profound implications in designing new therapeutic strategies against obesity and its related disorders.

17114117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17114117.value: 白血病是由骨髓中未成熟母細胞的原始群體造成的。MLL基因重排的白血病患者有比較差的預後結果及有較高的早期復發風險。所產生的MLL融合蛋白可以在白血病細胞中引入異常表觀遺傳修飾，包括DNA甲基化。基因調節元件（如啟動子和增強子）的表觀遺傳調節已經證明對於正常和癌細胞的生長和分化至關重要。CCAAT/增強子結合蛋白（C/EBP）在骨髓譜系中具有重要功能。C/EBPε的表達在血液粒細胞的成熟過程中增加，同時在急性骨髓性白血病細胞的分化期間被誘導。 但是C/EBPε的功能抑制與阻礙MLL基因重排的白血病細胞分化是否相關仍不清楚。我們先前產生了一個Mll-Een逆轉小鼠模型，發現MLL-EEN可以介導Hox基因啟動子上的異常DNA甲基化，導致Hox基因的高表達。在表達MLL-EEN的造血幹細胞和祖細胞上,基因組DNA甲基化譜分析也顯示差異甲基化位點主要位於基因內基因調控區，這可能與1801個蛋白質編碼基因的失調表達有關。重要的是，C/EBPε基因及其下參與細胞分化的下游靶基因的表達在表達MLL-EEN的造血幹細胞和祖細胞中受到強烈的抑制。此外, 低C/EBPε表達的急性骨髓性白血病患者的生存率比較差。我們重新分析了造血細胞的可用表觀遺傳資料，發現C/EBPε基因中±20kb內有一些開放性的域位是於差異DNA甲基化區域附近，意味着DNA甲基化可能參與在MLL基因重排的白血病中C/EBPε的轉錄調控。有趣的是，我們注意到負責去除DNA甲基化的Tet家族蛋白在MLL-EEN表達時被下調。因此，我們假設由MLL融合蛋白介導的異常DNA甲基化可以調節增強子活性並抑制C/EBPε的基因表達，導致白血病細胞的分化阻礙。這個項目的目的是通過表觀基因組學方法鑑定C/EBPε的增強子，並了解DNA甲基化如何參與C/EBPε的轉錄調控以維持MLL基因重排白血病中未成熟的細胞狀態。該項目將為白血病細胞分化的表觀遺傳調控提供新的見解，並促進分化治療的發展，以作為白血病有效的治療方法。

17114817.label: Realisation of objectives
17114817.value: Objective 2: Investigating the molecular events by which DEPDC1B regulates melanoma proliferation and metastasis We did not examine the molecular events of DEPDC1B in regulating melanoma proliferation as another group has addressed the issue but not metastasis and published the findings in Experimental Cell Research in 2019 [1]. We therefore focused on studying the role of DEPDC1B in melanoma metastasis. We used two different shRNA lentiviral constructs to stably silence DEPDC1B transcripts (KD1, KD2) in BRAF-mutated WM266-4, A2058, and SK-MEL-28 melanoma cell lines. Both DEPDC1B KD1 and KD2 cells showed reduced invasiveness and lung metastasis. In contrast, lentiviral-mediate overexpression of DEPDC1B (DEPDC1B OE) significantly promoted colony formation and cell invasion in vitro compared with the vehicle control. Accordingly, subcutaneous and tail vein injection of DEPDC1B OE cells in immunodeficient mice resulted in enhanced tumor growth and lung colonization. Notably, histological and immunohistological analysis of sections from tumor xenografts showed DEPDC1B OE promoted the formation of CD31+ microvessel with lumens containing red blood cells in the periphery compared to the vehicle control suggesting an enhancement of angiogenesis by high level of DEPDC1B expression. We obtained similar observations in lung nodules. These data demonstrate the oncogenic role of DEPDC1B in promoting melanoma metastasis and angiogenesis. Chromatin immunoprecipitation, luciferase reporter assay and epistasis analysis showed that SOX10 transactivates DEPDC1B expression through direct binding to its promoter region and DEPDC1B partly mediates the role of SOX10 in melanoma growth, metastasis, and angiogenesis. Our results showed that both DEPDC1B KD and OE can reduce and increase peripheral microvessel density in lung nodules respectively, indicating DEPDC1B can induce the expression of secreted pro-angiogenic factors to promote angiogenesis and metastasis. Indeed, the conditioned media (CM) from DEPDC1B KD and OE cells significantly inhibited and increased the total length, segments and branches of the tubular network of human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) which served as a cellular model of angiogenesis, suggesting the presence of pro-angiogenic factors in the CM secreted by DEPDC1B-expressing melanoma cells. By mass spectrometry of the CM from DEPDC1B KD and OE cells, we identified SCUBE3 which has been shown to regulate early lung cancer angiogenesis and metastasis [2]. We found the SCUBE3 protein instead of mRNA expression was markedly reduced and increased in DEPDC1B KD and OE cells. Similarly, SOX10 KD did not affect SCUBE3 mRNA, but reduced SCUBE3 protein expression level, which was partly restored by DEPDC1B OE. These results suggest that DEPDC1B functions downstream of SOX10 in regulating the expression of secreted SCUBE3 protein. To further investigate whether SCUBE3 secreted from melanoma cells contribute to angiogenesis, we designed two shRNAs to deplete SCUBE3 mRNA (SCUBE 3 KD1 and KD2) and proteins, and generated lentiviral vector-mediated SCUBE3 overexpression (SCUBE3 OE) in both WM266-4 and A2058 cells. The results showed that HUVECs treated with CM from SCUBE3 KD and OE resulted in a marked reduction and increase of the tubular network, respectively. To evaluate the secretory role of SCUBE3 in angiogenesis, HUVECs were treated with different dosages of human recombinant SCBUE3 protein which resulted in a considerable increase in the tube length with 150 ng mL-1 SCUBE 3 compared with nonsupplemented M200 HUVEC CM control. No further increase in the length of the tubular networks were observed with 300 or 600 ng mL-1 SCUBE3, implying a saturated response in HUVECs at the lower dosage of recombinant SCUBE3 protein. To further demonstrated the in vivo role of SCUBE3 in angiogenesis, we performed the Matrigel plug assay in wild-type mice. The plugs recovered from 7 day post-implantation showed that recombinant SCUBE3 protein stimulate angiogenesis as shown by an increase in hemoglobin level compared with control Matrigel which contained heparin alone and exhibited low level of hemoglobin in trace of vessels. Similarly, we observed intense vascularization in plugs containing CM from different volume of DEPDC1B OE lentiviruses. Hemoglobin content was higher in plugs containing CM from 150 uL DEPDC1B OE lentivirus than in the plug containing CM from 100 uL DEPDC1B OE lentivirus and from vehicle control, indicating a dose-dependent angiogenic response. These results demonstrate the pro-angiogenic role of SCUBE3 and DEPDC1B in vivo. In DEPDC1B KD cells, the reduction of SCUBE3 protein expression instead of mRNA raises the possibility that DEPDC1B regulates SCUBE3 protein stability. To address this issue, we performed cycloheximide chase analysis which showed that DEPDC1B KD and DEPDC1B OE resulted in a shorter and longer SCUBE3 half-life respectively compared with their respective controls. We further found that SCUBE3 destabilization is likely mediated by the ubiquitin-proteosome instead of the autophagy pathway in DEPDC1B KD cells. Indeed, elevated and reduced levels of ubiquitylated SCUBE3 were detected in DEPDC1B KD and OE cells, respectively, compared with scramble and vehicle controls, suggesting that DEPDC1B inhibits the ubiquitin-dependent degradation of SCUBE3. To elucidate the molecular mechanism by which DEPDC1B regulates SCUBE3 stability, we performed immunoprecipitation on endogenous and ectopic expressions of DEPDC1B in lysates extracted from both WM266-4 and A2058 cells followd by mass spectrometry. Among all the protein candidates, we identified CDC16 which plays a role in regulating protein stability as part of the anaphase-promoting complex/cyclosome (APC/C) E3 ubiquitin ligase [3]. Immunoprecipitation studies confirmed interactions between DEPDC1B and CDC16, as well as between SCUBE3 and CDC16 in both cell lines. However, there was no interaction between DEPDC1B and SCUBE3. In addition, CDC16 KD enhanced SCUBE3 protein levels without altering mRNA expression, confirming its functional requirement for regulating SCUBE3 stability. The ability of CDC16 to interact with DEPDC1B and SCUBE3 prompted us to presume that DEPDC1B might stabilize SCUBE3 through competitive binding of CDC16. Indeed, overexpression of DEPDC1B in melanoma cells reduced the degree of CDC16 binding with SCUBE3, but not in a dose-dependent manner compared with the vehicle control. Consistently, elevated levels of SCUBE3 protein were detected in DEPDC1B OE cells. Similar results were obtained using protein lysates from DEPDC1B OE xenografts. Altogether, both in vitro and in vivo studies suggest that DEPDC1B stabilizes SCUBE3 by inhibiting its interaction with CDC16 to prevent subsequent ubiquitin-dependent degradation. Lastly, by immunofluorescence in melanoma tissue microarrays, we demonstrate that SOX10 and DEPDC1B are clinically correlated with SCUBE3 and CD31 expressions in advanced stages of melanoma, consistent with their regulatory relationship in promoting melanoma angiogenesis and metastasis. 17114817.label: Major findings and research outcome
17114817.value: Major findings: 1. Analysis of TCGA database reveals that increased transcript levels of DEPDC1B in skin cutaneous melanomas is significantly associated with a poor prognosis. Immunofluorescence of melanoma tissue microarray shows extensive overlap in the expression of DEPDC1B and the expression of oncogenic driver SOX10 in the different stages of melanoma. 2. Accordingly, loss- and gain-of-function studies demonstrate that DEPDC1B is required and sufficient for melanoma growth, metastasis, angiogenesis, and functions as a direct downstream target of SOX10 to partly mediate its oncogenic activity. 3. In contrast to other cancer types, the ability of DEPDC1B to enhance melanoma metastasis does not depend on the activities of Rho GTPase signaling and canonical Wnt signaling, but is acquired through the secretion of SCUBE3, which promotes angiogenesis in vitro and in vivo. 4. Mechanistically, both in vitro and in vivo studies demonstrate that elevated expression of DEPDC1B enhances SCUBE3 protein stability through the competitive interaction with ubiquitin ligase CDC16, thus preventing SCUBE3 from undergoing degradation via the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway. 5. The SOX10-regulated DEPDC1B expression to stabilize SCUBE3 for promoting angiogenesis and metastasis is further supported by their positive correlation of expression with microvessel density in metastatic melanoma specimens. Research outcome: My PhD student (Miss Feng Hu, 4th year) presented the above findings through poster presentations twice in American Association for Cancer Research in 2021 and 2022. She also gave poster and oral presentations in our annual research postgraduate symposiums in 2020 and 2021 respectively. She was awarded best poster and oral presentation awards. Her research findings have recently been published in Advanced Science and widely reported by the mass media locally and internationally.

17114817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17114817.value: Considering the role of SCUBE3 in promoting melanoma angiogenesis and metastasis, we plan to generate a neutralising antibody that specifically targets SCUBE3 (SCUBE3 N ab) activity in melanoma progression. A previous study reported the generation of a monoclonal functional antibody specific for SCUBE2 for suppressing pancreatic tumor growth and angiogenesis. Using a similar strategy, we will commission GenScript to generate a SCUBE3-specific neutralising antibody by conventional hybridoma technology. The specificity of anti-SCUBE3 binding to cells expressing SCUBE3, but not SCUBE1 and 2, will be determined by immunoprecipitation and Western blot analysis. Recombinant SCUBE3 protein will be used as the positive control. To evaluate the neutralising activity of anti-SCUBE3 against SCUBE3, we will treat HUVEC cells with CM from SCUBE3 OE cells or recombinant SCUBE protein as the positive control, together with SCUBE3 N ab or control IgG and then compare the total tube lengths between treatments. To evaluate the anti-tumor efficacy of SCUBE3 N ab on metastasis, luciferase-labeled tumor cells will be injected into the tail vein of NOD/SCID mice. These mice will be intraperitoneally injected with SCUBE3 N ab (10 mg/kg) or control IgG twice and the inhibition of lung metastasis and angiogenesis will be evaluated 4 weeks later.

17114817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17114817.value: Our research findings have unraveled a new SOX10-DEPDC1B-SCUBE3 regulatory axis that promotes melanoma angiogenesis and facilitates its metastatic progression, suggesting the possibility of targeting secreted SCUBE3 as a therapeutic strategy against metastatic melanoma. Our findings underlie the possibility of using both DEPDC1B and SCUBE3 to serve as diagnostic and prognostic markers to improve the clinical assessment of patients with suspected malignant melanoma. Since secreted SCUBE3 is druggable, it is possible to generate SCUBE3 neutralising antibody for the early intervention of melanoma growth, angiogenesis and metastasis. Considering DEPDC1B is oncogenic in other cancer types, our studies have broader implications of DEPDC1B involved in stabilisation of other secreted factors to promote angiogenesis and metastasis in other tumor types.

17115017.label: Major findings and research outcome
17115017.value: (1) Chemotherapy resulted in significant elevations in the levels of the pro-inflammatory cytokines interleukin 6 (IL-6) and tumor necrosis factor-α(TNF-α) and in significant decreases in the levels of the anti-inflammatory cytokines IL-4 and IL-10 in most of the sera and brain tissues examined. The IL-6 and TNF-αlevels of several sera and brain tissues showed strong inverse correlations with the duration and number of entries in the target quadrant of the water maze and with the hippocampal neuroimaging signal intensity, but also showed striking positive correlations with spine elimination and loss. These results indicate that chemobrain is associated with cytokine dysregulation and disrupted neuroplasticity of the brain. This is the first to successfully establish the animal model of chemobrain. (2) Chemobrain mice with resveratrol displayed signiﬁcantly lower levels of TNF-α and IL-6, but markedly higher levels of IL-4 and IL-10 in several sera and brain tissues than those co-treated with vehicle. Resveratrol modulated the cytokine-regulating pathway peroxisome proliferator activated receptor (PPAR)-γ/nuclear factor kappa-light-chain-enhancer of activated B cells (NF-κB), and protected against chemotherapy-induced decreases in the expression of the neuroplasticity biomarkers, brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), tropomyosin receptor kinase B (TrkB), amino acid neurotransmitter receptors, and calmodulin-dependent protein kinase II (CaMKII). These results demonstrate the eﬃcacy of resveratrol in preventing chemobrain and its association with cytokine modulation and neuroprotection. (3) Rg1 also significantly improved chemobrain-like behavior, reversed chemotherapy-induced decreases in prefrontal and hippocampal neuronal activity, and ameliorated cortical neuronal dendritic spine elimination. It normalized chemotherapy-caused abnormalities in the expression of multiple neuroplasticity biomarkers in the two brain regions. Rg1 suppressed chemotherapy-induced elevation of the proinflammatory TNF-α and IL-6, but increased levels of the anti-inflammatory cytokines IL-4 and IL-10 in multiple sera and brain tissues. Rg1 also modulated cytokine mediators and inhibited chemotherapy neurotoxicity and microglial neuroinflammation. These results indicate that Rg1 exerts its anti-chemobrain effect in an association with the inhibition of neuroinflammation by modulating microglia-mediated cytokines and the related upstream mediators, protecting neuronal activity and promoting neuroplasticity in particular brain regions associated with cognition processing. (4) The anti-chemobrain effects of Rg1 appeared to be superior to resveratrol. The two agents did not show the synergistic effects, but may have additive effects.

17115017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17115017.value: As a large portion of cancer patients seek ginseng and Ganoderma lucidum (Lingzhi) as supplementary during chemotherapy and other therapies, the results of our study have encouraged to further conduct translational studies in clinical settings to test the anti-chemobrain efficacy of Rg1 in clinical settings.

17115017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17115017.value: Cancer patients under chemotherapy often experience poor memory and concentration and decreased multiple working capacity. This is often called "chemobrain" or chemotherapy-induced cognitive impairment. In this study, we examined whether resveratrol, a natural constituent contained in grape peel and Rg1, a natural constituent from ginseng, could protect against chemobrain. We revealed that the two constituents exert anti-chemobrain effects in an animal model. This may support cancer patients who seek ginseng and Ganoderma lucidum (Lingzhi) as supplementary during chemotherapy.

17115417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17115417.value: Tumor-induced immunosuppression is a hallmark feature of head and cancers. Previous findings indicated that natural killer (NK) cells can recognize and are able to infiltrate into the cancer sites. However, these NK cells are usually inactivated and the mechanisms remain to be explored. Deciphering the mechanistic rationale behind is important for the development of specific immunotherapeutic regime for head and neck cancer treatment. The proposed study is based on our new data that head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) with high reactive oxygen species (ROS) content is resistant to NK cell-mediated lysis. By profiling the expression patterns of ROS generating enzymes, we identified that NADPH oxidase 5 (NOX5) is a key ROS generating enzyme which is differentially expressed and is responsible for ROS generation in HNSCC. Additionally, we discovered that production of nerve growth factor (NGF), a putative inactivator of human NK cells is stimulated by NOX5 signalling. Given the novel preliminary data, we hypothesize that HNSCC activates NGF production by overexpressing NOX5. NGF has an immunomodulating impact on NK cells and hinders their cytotoxic actions against HNSCC. These hypotheses will be addressed in the experiments with the following specific aims: (1) to determine whether NOX5 in HNSCC impairs the anti-tumor response of NK cells; (2) to determine how NOX5 regulates NGF production and the clinical significance of NOX5/NGF; and (3) to determine and evaluate the use of NOX5/NGF inhibitor to enhance NK cells cytotoxicity against HNSCC. Successful accomplishment of the proposed studies will provide novel paradigm for designing target treatment which employs the innate immune cells to target HNSCC. 腫瘤誘導的免疫抑制是頭頸部位腫瘤的特徵。研究發現自然殺傷（NK）細胞能識別並滲透到腫瘤當中。然而，腫瘤組織中的NK細胞活性大都受到抑制。腫瘤利用何種機制抑制NK細胞活性仍有待研究。我們的前期數據顯示具有高活性氧（ROS）含量的頭頸鱗狀細胞癌（HNSCC）能抵抗來自NK細胞介導的細胞殺傷。通過分析ROS產生酶的表達譜，我們發現NADPH氧化酶5（NOX5）在頭頸鱗癌中出現明顯的過表達。 NOX5是頭頸鱗癌的主要活性氧產生酶。另外，我們發現NOX5介導的信號通道能加強NK細胞抑制因子NGF的產生。我們假設頭頸腫瘤通過過量表達NOX5來激活NGF的生成。 NGF對NK細胞具有免疫調節作用，能抑制其對頭頸腫瘤的殺傷作用。我們將通過以下具體的目標來驗證這些假說：（1）探討NOX5在頭頸腫瘤中是否會損害NK細胞的抗腫瘤反應；（2）闡明NOX5如何調節NGF的產生以及剖析NOX5 / NGF表達的臨床意義；（3）評估使用NOX5 / NGF抑製劑以增強NK細胞對頭頸腫瘤殺傷的可行性。破譯當中的機制能為開發頭頸部腫瘤的特異性免疫治療法提供基礎和證據。

17115417.label: Realisation of objectives
17115417.value: Aim 1: We hypothesized that NK cells in contact with HNSCC cells become dormant and will be less active upon external stimulation. Thus, we cultured effector NK cells in HNSCC cell lines with or without IL-2 stimulation. All selected activation markers in this study are expressed at low/ undetectable on the unstimulated NK cell surface. When NK cells co-cultures with HNSCC, expression of CD336 (NKp44), CD337 (NKp30), and the classical class II molecules HLA-DR (a delayed activation marker) become significantly increase. Thus, the results indicated that contact activation exists in the cancer-infiltrating NK cells. Upon stimulation, NK cells can still be activated. Active NK cells will release the lytic lysosomes containing perforin and granzyme. At the resting stage, the lysosome-associated membrane protein-1 (CD107a) resides in the lytic granule together with perforin. Activated NK cells release the cytotoxic granules by exocytosis leading to the appearance of CD107a on the NK cell surface. By measuring the surface change of CD107a, we noticed that degranulation is inhibited significantly in the NK cells HNSCC co-culture. Further, the serine protease granzyme content of NK cells was significantly reduced in the co-cultures. Together, the data reflected that HNSCC has an inhibitory role in NK cells activity. To address whether NOX5 impairs the NK cell-mediated anti-tumor responses, NOX5-overexpressing and NOX5 shRNA-expressing HNSCC lines were constructed. The resulting mRNA and protein changes were confirmed by QPCR and Western blot analysis. We have tested the NK cell sensitivity of NOX5-overexpressing lines using different effector:target ratios. Generally, NOX5-overexpressing HNSCC has low sensitivity to the cytotoxic action of NK cells. Especially at a low effector:target ratio, the cytotoxic activity of NK cells was completely inhibited in the co-culture. The sensitivity of NK cells in response to the NOX5 content was also evaluated in the nude mice model. The immunocompromised nude mice did not have B and T cells, but the NK cell activity remained high. Thus, xenograft generated in the nude mice must have substantial resistance to murine NK cells. We noticed that NOX5-expression has a direct impact on xenograft size and affect the success rate of HNSCC inoculation. NOX5-overexpressing HNSCC cells and mock cells were injected subcutaneously into nude mice. Xenograft volume over time and final tumor weight was significantly increased in NOX5-overexpressing HNSCC cells in nude mice. In contrast, NOX5-shRNA-expressing HNSCC cells showed a significant reduction of tumor volume over time and final tumor weight compared to scramble controls. The results suggest that NOX5 can promote HNSCC progression in the presence of NK cells. Aim 2: At present, whether NGF is produced by the HNSCC tissue is not clarified yet. Therefore, we measured the circulating NGF level in our patients before surgery and compared the results with post-operative (7 days) plasma NGF level. The significant reduction in the circulating NGF level in the post-operation plasma implies that HNSCC cancer tissue is the primary NGF producing source in HNSCC patients. We hypothesized that human NGF could inhibit the cytotoxicity of the NK cells. To test the hypothesis, NK cells were pre-incubated with recombinant NGF before adding into the HNSCC culture system. Significant reduction in the NK cell cytotoxicity in the HNSCC co-cultures were observed. The results suggested that NK cells could possibly be inactivated in the microenvironment with high NGF content. To explore association between NGF and NOX5 in clinical samples, we performed correlation analysis on NGF and NOX5 transcript levels using head and neck cancer tissues in our tissue bank. The high and significant correlation coefficient indicates a potential expression correlation between NGF and NOX5. In order to address the increased NGF production is resulting from NOX5 activity, we incubated HNSCC cells with the superoxide inducer (rotenone) using an increasing concentration range and measured the changes of NGF transcription. Rotenone treatment increased the intracellular ROS level and NGF level. The correlation between ROS-production and NGF induction is further supported by the observation that HNSCC showed a dose-dependent increase in NGF level in response to the rotenone used. Together, the data strongly support that NGF induction in HNSCC is regulated by NOX5-mediated signalling cascade. To validate the hypothesis that NOX5 in HNSCC is responsible for the high NGF tumor microenvironment, NOX5-suppressing cells were used to develop 3D-spheroid cultures. Western blot and ELISA results showed that NGF protein level was decreased in NOX5-suppressing cells. Although the results implied a link between NOX5 and NGF expression/secretion in HNSCC, whether NOX5 overexpression has a direct impact on the responsiveness of HNSCC to NK cells remains unclear. The results so far prompted us to suggest that HNSCC with high NOX5 content might be more resistant to the cytotoxic actions of NK cells. We established NOX5-overexpressing spheroids using the established protocol. After NK cell addition, unaltered HNSCC spheroids showed a significant reduction in spheroid volume compared to the NOX5-overexpressing spheroids. Mock spheroids exhibited substantial decrease in the spheroid volume compared to NOX5-overexpressing spheroids at all time points (day 4, day 11, and day 12). To delineate the mechanism underlying NOX5 induced NGF upregulation, we performed in silico analysis on the promoter region of NGF to identify potential cis-acting elements. Computation analysis indicates the presence of 2 antioxidant responsive elements (AREs) situated at -74~-68 bp and +35~+42 bp from the transcriptional start site (+1) of NGF gene. ChIP assay showed a significant increase in the level of NRF2 binding to the AREs of NGF promoter in comparison with IgG control. The results supported that endogenous NRF2 could interact with the predicted AREs in the NGF promoter, To explore the clinical association between NOX5 and NGF in our HNSCC patients, NGF and NOX5 expression in HNSCC tissues were examined by immunohistochemical staining. In total, 106 tissues were examined. Pearson correlation analysis showed that NGF was not correlated with NGFRAP1 in terms of protein level. NGF and NOX5 expression was not associated with clinicopathological variables, including gender, age, clinical T stage, clinical N stage, smoking, and drinking. The lack of association could be caused by the relatively small sample size and heterogeneity of head and neck cancer tissues. Aim 3: Two different locked nucleic acid (LNA) antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) gapmers against NOX5 transcript had been designed. Their efficacy to silence NOX5 expression are validated in the in vitro HNSCC cells. Murine NK cell clearance assay has been carried out on Balb/c athymic mice by administration of anti-Asialo GM1 antiserum intraperitoneally (i.p.). The spleenic NK cell contents are used as an indicator of NK cell depletion. The optimal doses for anti-Asialo GM1 with highest NK cells depletion rate in nude mice had been determined. However, due to COVID19 outbreak, clinical research activity was suspended in our institute. We cannot obtained fresh human NK cells from volunteers in our clinic in the study period. We did approach Hong Kong Red Cross (HKRC) to collect inadequate volume whole blood for our study purposes. However, due to significant reduction of the number of blood donors, fresh blood samples cannot be arranged. We did perform in vitro expansion of NK cells on blood sample from 2 donors (which has been stored at low temperature for around 20 days) in order to isolate sufficient NK cells for the in vivo test. The low number of viable NK cells prevents us to perform the NK cells infusion step.

17115417.label: Major findings and research outcome
17115417.value: NK cells are infiltrating immune cells in the head and neck cancer tissues but their cytotoxic actions are largely suppressed. Treatment regime which can re-activate NK cells might possibly be used as an alternative therapy in solid cancer treatment. Active NK cells will release lytic lysosomes containing perforin and granzymes. At the resting stage, the lysosome-associated membrane protein-1 (CD107a) resides in the lytic granule together with perforin. Activated NK cells release the cytotoxic granules by exocytosis leading to the appearance of CD107a on the NK cell surface. By measuring the surface change of CD107a, we noticed that degranulation is inhibited significantly in the NK cells in contact with HNSCC. Further, the serine protease granzyme content of NK cells was significantly reduced in the co-cultures. Together, the data reflected that HNSCC has a strong inhibitory role in NK cells activity. IL-2 can activate NK cell cytotoxicity and stimulate expression of activation receptors. At present, multiple activation receptors have been reported to be useful to discriminate the activated NK cells. We discovered that NK cells in contact with HNSCC express unique activation makers on NK cell surface. As compared with the unstimulated NK cells, IL-2 stimulates CD336 (NKp44), CD337 (NKp30) and the classical class II molecules HLA-DR (a delayed activation marker) expression. Other reported NK cells activation makers we have tested including CD16 (essential for antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity for NK cells), CD62L, and CD69 (early activation marker) and CD335 (NKp46). They all did not show significant increase in response to IL-2 treatment. Cancer boosts production of reactive oxygen species (ROS) actively and employs ROS as second messenger to drive the oncogenic signalling cascade. We found that NADPH oxidase 5 (NOX5), which is differential expressed in the HNSCC tissues, affecting the responsiveness of HNSCC to NK cells. NOX5 can stimulate expression and secretion of nerve growth factor (NGF), a neurotrophin that can stimulate and promote survival and maturation of sympathetic fibers and sensory nerves. We measured the circulating NGF level in our patients before surgery and compared the results with post-operative (7 days) plasma NGF level. The significant reduction in the circulating NGF level in the post-operation plasma implies that HNSCC cancer tissue is the primary NGF-producing source in HNSCC patients. The regulatory functions of NOX5 on NGF is on expression level and is mediated through the antioxidant responsive elements (AREs) in the promoter region of the NGF gene.

17115417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17115417.value: NK cells are infiltrating immune cells in the head and neck cancer tissues but their cytotoxic actions are largely suppressed. Treatment regime which can re-activate NK cells might possibly be used as an alternative therapy in solid cancer treatment. IL-2 is used for ex vivo activation of the NK cells in the co-culture and the use has been approved in clinical trials. We first demonstrated that it is feasible to re-activate NK cells in contact with head and neck cancer with IL-2. It is warranted to explore and validate the in vitro findings in the HNSCC animal models. Second, we have established that ROS-generating enzyme NOX5 is the key regulator in controlling NGF expression and secretion in head and neck cancers. NOX family has multiple isoforms and their expression levels varied in different cancer tissues. Thus, the NOX/NGF signalling cascade might be controlled by different NOX isoforms depending on the cancer context. Exploring and validating the relevant NOX signalling cascade could allow further development of NK cells therapy in more human cancer types.

17115517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17115517.value: Introduction There were >1,800 new cases of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) in HK in 2011 and it’s the second leading cause of cancer death in man. In Asia, only 10-15% HCC patients have resectable/ transplantable disease. Instead, majority of our patients have intermediate stage HCC, where transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) is the standard but it is just a palliative treatment. Our previous randomized trial showed that TACE offered survival benefits in HCC patients. Stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) was developed in recent years and a few series showed promising results with good local control for HCC. In this randomized trial, we aim to compare SBRT vs. TACE for unresectable HCC. Objective Primary Endpoints To compare progression free survival of HCC patients who received SBRT to TACE. Secondary Endpoints 1) To compare overall survival of HCC patients who received SBRT to TACE. 2) To compare disease control rate of HCC patients who received SBRT to TACE. 3) To correlate metabolic activity of tumor on positron emission tomography (PET) before and after treatment, as monitoring of treatment response and predictors for survivals. 4) To evaluate safety of SBRT in HCC patients. 5) To evaluate time to symptomatic progression. Study design This is a 3 centers, randomized controlled trial comparing the efficacy of SBRT to TACE in unresectable HCC. Patients will be randomly assigned to SBRT or TACE. All treatment procedures and follow up protocol are standardized between 3 centers. For SBRT, patients will receive high dose radiation in 5 sessions over 10-14 days to tumors while limiting exposure to surrounding organs. For TACE, patients will have cisplatin followed by gelfoam embolization twice, at 8-week interval. Treatment response will be assessed every 3 months. A multidisciplinary panel will discuss treatment response/failure and need of subsequent treatment every 3 months. PET scan will be done before and at 6 months after treatment to assess treatment response and prognosis. Quality of life will be monitored with questionnaires every 3 months. Anticipated results and long-term impact Our study will help to define the role of SBRT in unresectable HCC, which is lacking in literature. We anticipate that SBRT is superior to TACE as local control and will offer survival benefits in HCC patients. We will also investigate and establish the role of PET in HCC after SBRT and TACE. Should our hypothesis be proven, this will lead to a major change in management and international guideline for HCC. 研究背景輿目的 肝動脈化療栓塞 (TACE) 是目前對於不適合接受肝臟移植，手術切除或射頻消融的肝細胞癌的標準治療。以往研究發現肝動脈化療栓塞有助延長病人壽命。 立體定位放射治療 (SBRT) 是較新的方法，它應用立體定位技術和特殊射線裝置，一般可在最多五次治療過程達致縮少腫瘤的效果。 希望通過這個研究，比較立體定位放射治療輿肝動脈化療栓塞的療效，為無法手術的肝细胞癌患者尋找更有效的治療方法。 研究病人數目 這是一項多中心聯合進行的前瞻、隨機研究，將招募170無法手術切除的肝细胞癌患者參予。

17116417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17116417.value: In many mammalian species, including humans, the oviduct functions as a sperm reservoir which is created by the binding of the sperm to the oviductal epithelial cells (OECs). This interaction is a species-specific event that involves the recognition of defined carbohydrates on the OEC by the sperm. When ovulation is imminent, these stored sperm are released from the reservoir to move to the fertilization site. Sperm reservoir formation in the oviduct serves to maintain the fertilizing capacity of spermatozoa until ovulation. Adhesion to the oviduct also plays a key role in the selection of sperm with normal chromatin structure and superior fertilization ability. Most of our knowledge on the roles of the sperm reservoir in fertilization comes from studies in other mammalian species. The functions and mechanism of sperm reservoir formation in human is still unknown. Our previous study demonstrated that sperm fucosyltransferase-5 (sFUT5), a carbohydrate-binding protein on spermatozoa, is responsible for spermatozoa-OEC interaction in humans. Our preliminary data further suggest the involvement of sFUT5-mediated OEC adhesion in maintaining sperm fertility and selecting fertilization-competent sperm. These observations include (1) OEC membrane proteins prolong human sperm viability in vitro; (2) human sperm possess different binding affinities to sFUT5-binding protein on OECs within the same ejaculate; and (3) OEC-bound sperm have higher DNA integrity when compared to the unbound sperm. We hypothesize that sFUT5-mediated OEC adhesion is a crucial step for maintaining the fertilizing capacity of human spermatozoa and the selection of spermatozoa endowed with superior fertilization competence. The hypothesis will be tested by studying the functions and mechanism of spermatozoa-OEC interaction, and by correlating them with the fertilizing competence of spermatozoa. Treatment of human infertility with assisted reproduction technologies (ART) bypasses the natural selection processes for high quality sperm. Most of the current sperm selection techniques in ART show distinct limitations in that they do not necessarily select spermatozoa according to their functional competence and/or genetic quality, as is achieved in the female genital tract. Therefore, there is a need for new approaches for better sperm selection in ART. The results of the project will enhance our understanding on the physiological role of the human oviduct on sperm functions. They will give clues on whether sFUT5-binding protein on OEC can be applied clinically as a natural molecule for functional sperm selection, as well as a protein supplement during sperm processing in ART to lengthen the fertilizing capacity of human spermatozoa. 在許多哺乳動物物種（包括人類）中，輸卵管作為精子的儲存器，主要使精子與輸卵管的上皮細胞（OEC）相結合。這種相互作用是一個物種特異性事件，涉及到由精子識別OEC上特定的碳水化合物。當排卵即將到來時，這些儲存的精子從儲存器釋放以移動到受精部位。輸卵管中的精子儲層形成有助於維持精子的能力能力直到排卵。對輸卵管的粘附也在選擇具有正常染色質結構和優良受精能力的精子中起關鍵作用。 我們大多數關於精子儲存在受精中的作用的知識來自其他哺乳動物物種的研究。人類精子儲層形成的功能和機制尚不清楚。我們以前的研究表明，精子岩藻糖基轉移酶-5（ sFUT5）是精子上的碳水化合物結合蛋白，負責人類精子與OEC的相互作用。我們的初步數據進一步表明sFUT5介導的OEC粘附參與維持精子生殖力和選擇受精能力的精子的過程。包括（1）OEC膜蛋白在體外延長人類精子活力; （2）人精子對同一射精內的嗅鞘細胞具有與sFUT5結合蛋白的結合親和力;和（3）與未結合的精子相比，OEC結合的精子具有更高的DNA完整性。 我們假設sFUT5介導的OEC粘附是維持人類精子受精能力和選擇具有優良受精能力的精子的關鍵步驟。通過研究精子與OEC相互作用的功能和機制，並將其與精子的受精能力相關聯，來驗證該假設。 用輔助生殖技術（ART）治療人類不育症繞過了高質量精子的自然選擇過程。目前大多數ART技術中的精子選擇技術顯示出明顯的局限性，因為它們不一定根據其功能能力和/或遺傳質量選擇精子，而這個選擇過程是在女性生殖道中所實現的。因此，需要在藝術中有更好地選擇精子的新途徑。該項目的結果將增強我們對人類輸卵管對精子功能的生理作用的認識。他們將提供關於OEC上的sFUT5結合蛋白是否可以臨床應用於功能性精子選擇的天然分子以及ART精子加工過程中的蛋白質補充以延長人類精子受精能力的提示。

The functions and mechanism of sperm reservoir formation in human is still unknown. By using OEC cell line as a model, our previous data demonstrated that sperm fucosyltransferase-5 (sFUT5), a carbohydrate-binding protein on spermatozoa, is responsible for spermatozoa-OEC interaction in humans. In this project, we hypothesize that sFUT5-mediated OEC adhesion is not only beneficial for maintaining the fertilizing capacity of human spermatozoa but also represents a crucial step for the selection of spermatozoa endowed with superior fertilization competence. OBJECTIVE 1. To characterize the sFUT5-binding proteins on primary human OECs We have used affinity chromatography to purify sperm fucosyltransferase-5 (sFUT5) -binding proteins from the plasma membrane extracts of OE-E6/E7 cells (a human oviductal epithelial cell line). Mass spectrometric analysis identifies cell adhesion molecule 4 (CADM4), CD44 and annexin A2 as potential sFUT5-binding proteins. The interaction between purified sFUT5 and CADM4 protein was studied by coimmunoprecipitation followed by Western blot analysis. CADM4 immunoreactivity was found in sFUT5-interacting complex. This indicated that CADM4 interacted with purified sFUT5 and was immunoprecipitated by the anti-FUT5 affinity column. Anti-FUT5 affinity column alone did not interact with CADM4. Moreover, the sperm-CADM4 interaction is not affected by the inclusion of sialy-Lewis X glycan (a reported sperm binding carbohydrate ligand) or galectin protein (a reported sperm surface glycan-binding protein), indicating the specificity of the sperm-CADM4 interaction. Biologically active CADM4 with molecular size ~70 kDa has been purified from primary human oviductal epithelial cells (OECs) using chromatography-based immunoaffinity method. Purified Alexa Fluor® 488-conjugated CADM4 binds to the acrosomal region of human spermatozoa. Interestingly, the CADM4 binding are not universal, with weak or not detectable binding in many human sperm. CADM4 immunoreactivity, but not CD44, was detected in cultured OE-E6/E7 cells as demonstrated by immunostaining. The expression of CADM4 in OE-E6/E7 cells was further confirmed by Western blot analysis of OE-E6/E7 membrane proteins using anti-CADM4 antibody. Human oviduct of different regions (infundibulum, ampulla and isthmus) and phase of menstrual cycle (follicular and luteal phase) were collected for immunohistochemistry analysis using specific antibodies. CADM4 protein was mainly localized in the luminal epithelium of the human oviduct. No difference of CADM4 expression can be detected between infundibullary, isthmic and ampullary regions in both follicular and luteal phase. On the other hand, the expression of CADM4 in infundibullary region was significantly higher (P< 0.05) during follicular phase when compared to that of luteal phase. A similar increasing trend can also be observed for isthmic region. The results suggested that the menstrual phase together with the oviducal region, affects sperm binding to OECs. OBJECTIVE 2. To determine the role of sFUT5-binding proteins in spermatozoa-OEC interaction In this objective, we established a novel assay for studying spermatozoa-OEC interaction in human. The assay was based on the binding of human spermatozoa to immortalized oviductal cell (OE-E6/E7) spheroids. To validate the accuracy of the assay, an increasing number of spermatozoa were added to the spheroids and co-cultured for different time periods. Our results showed that the number of bound spermatozoa per OE-E6/E7 cell spheroid increased linearly with increase in the time of co-culture at the sperm concentration of 4×106/ml. Consistently, compared with other sperm concentrations tested, 4×106/ml gave the strongest linear relationship between the number of bound spermatozoa and the co-culture time (r2=0.63). By using the 3D co-culture model for human spermatozoa and OECs, anti-sFUT5 antibody was demonstrated to significantly suppress the binding capacity of human spermatozoa to the OE-E6/E7 cell spheroids, indicating the relevance of using sperm-OE-E6/E7 cell spheroid 3D co-culture model as a tool for assessment of spermatozoa-OEC interaction in humans. The contribution of CADM4 on spermatozoa-OEC interaction was demonstrated by the inhibitory effect of anti-CADM4 antibody on the binding of Alexa Fluor® 488-conjugated OE-E6/E7 membrane proteins to the spermatozoa. OBJECTIVE 3. To establish the relationship between capacitation and spermatozoa-OEC interaction In other mammalian species, sperm release from the oviductal reservoir is mainly depended on sperm changes that are associated with capacitation. In the first part of the study, the binding abilities of capacitated sperm to fluorescence labeled OEC membrane protein/purified sFUT5-binding protein were compared with the uncapacitated population. Our results showed that capacitation was associated with significant (P<0.05) reduction in the percentage of spermatozoa with bound OEC membrane protein/purified sFUT5-binding protein. In another part of the study, we investigated the effect of capacitation in evoking spermatozoa release from OECs. Uncapacitated sperm were first incubated with fluorescence labeled OEC membrane protein/purified sFUT5-binding protein. Afterward, capacitation was induced in the OEC-bound sperm by incubation in capacitation medium. The amount of sperm surface OEC membrane protein/purified sFUT5-binding protein were then be quantified. Our results showed that capacitation have no significant (P>0.05) effect on the percentage of spermatozoa with bound OE-E6/E7 membrane proteins/purified sFUT5-binding protein, indicating that in vitro capacitation alone is not enough to release the sperm from OEC interaction. OBJECTIVE 4. To study the role of sFUT5-mediated OEC adhesion in maintaining the quiescent state of human spermatozoa Sperm are maintained in a quiescent state when bound to the OECs resulting in delayed capacitation, motility suppression and extended lifespan of spermatozoa. Our results showed that sperm viability declined over time and had decreased by about 90% after 48 hours in medium (Earle's Balanced Salt Solution) alone. Interestingly, the inclusion of OE-E6/E7 membrane proteins significantly (P<0.05) prolongs the human sperm viability by 55%. Moreover, OEC-bound sperm was characterized by low [Ca2+]i, reduced protein tyrosine phosphorylation and stabilized sperm membrane as demonstrated by fluo-3-AM staining assay, Western blotting and annexin V/propidium iodide staining, respectively. However, OEC binding had no effect on sperm motility, capacitation and acrosome reaction as determined by computer assisted sperm analysis, chlortetracycline staining and FITC-Pisum sativum agglutinin staining, respectively. OBJECTIVE 5. To study the role of sFUT5-mediated OEC adhesion in selecting fertilization competent sperm. After co-culture, the bound sperm on the OEC spheroids were recovered by aspiration using a glass micropipette. Unbound spermatozoa that were freely swimming in the co-culture wells were used as the control. Their DNA integrity were assessed by the alkaline comet assay. The results demonstrated that the OEC-bound group contained less spermatozoa with DNA damage (long comet tail) when compared to the unbound group as shown by a lower value of % tail DNA (22.1% v.s. 33.8%) and tail moment (19.8 A.U. v.s. 30.6 A.U.) when compared to the control without treatment (P<0.05). The results were further confirmed by Tunel Assay using a commercially available kit. The fertilizing competence of the OEC-bound sperm were also determined by analyzing the sperm ZP-binding ability and acrosome reaction. OEC-bound sperm have significantly higher capabilities in ZP interaction as determined by flow cytometry-based solubilized ZP binding assay and ZP-induced acrosome reaction.

17116417.label: Major findings and research outcome
17116417.value: - A novel 3D co-culture model using fluorescent-labeled spermatozoa and cell spheroids of immortalized oviductal epithelial cell line, OE-E6/E7, was established. The relevance and applicability of model in assessing sperm-oviductal epithelial cells (OECs) interaction in humans was demonstrated. - Sperm fucosyltransferase-5 (sFUT5) as a transmembrane carbohydrate-binding protein on human spermatozoa mediates the spermatozoa-OEC interaction - Cell adhesion molecules, CADM4 and CD44, were identified as sFUT5-interacting proteins in OECs. The expression of CADM4 in primary human oviduct of different regions (infundibulum, ampulla and isthmus) and phase of menstrual cycle (follicular and luteal phase) was demonstrated. - Sperm-CADM4 interaction is not affected by the inclusion of sialy-Lewis X glycan (a reported sperm binding carbohydrate ligand) or galectin protein (a reported sperm surface glycan-binding protein), indicating the specificity of the sperm-CADM4 interaction. - Capacitation process is associated with the binding capabilities of human spermatozoa to OECs. - OEC-bound spermatozoa possessed more intact DNA and superior fertilizing ability when compared with the unbound spermatozoa. - OEC binding prolongs human sperm viability in vitro and maintain them in a quiescent state characterized by low [Ca2+]i, reduced protein tyrosine phosphorylation and stabilized sperm membrane.

17116417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17116417.value: Infertility is affecting 15% of the couples at reproductive age. Assisted reproduction treatment (ART) is an effective treatment of infertility. However, treatment of human infertility with ART bypasses the natural selection processes for high quality sperm. Most of the current sperm selection techniques in ART show distinct limitations in that they do not necessarily select spermatozoa according to their functional competence and/or genetic quality, as is achieved in the female genital tract. This increases the risk of transferring paternal defects such as fragmented DNA and genomic abnormalities in sperm to the resulting child. Therefore, there is a need for new approaches for better sperm selection in ART. Sperm reservoir formation in the oviduct serves to maintain the sperm fertilizing capacity and plays a key role in the selection of sperm with normal chromatin structure and superior fertilization ability. The results of the project indicate the possible use of OECs or sFUT5-binding protein on OECs as a natural molecule for functional sperm selection in ART, as well as a protein supplement during sperm during sperm processing in ART to lengthen the fertilizing capacity of human spermatozoa. The clinical value of our results can be evaluated in future using more clinical samples.

17116417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17116417.value: In many mammalian species, the oviduct functions as a sperm reservoir which is created by the binding of the sperm to the oviductal epithelial cells (OECs). This oviductal reservoir serves to maintain the fertilizing capacity of spermatozoa and selection of spermatozoa endowed with superior fertilization competence. Most of our knowledge on the roles of the sperm reservoir in fertilization comes from studies on other mammalian species. The functions and mechanism of sperm reservoir formation in human is still unknown. In this study, we have developed a novel 3D OEC-binding assay for quantifying the binding capacity of human spermatozoa to OECs. Sperm fucosyltransferase-5 (sFUT5) was demonstrated to be an OEC receptor in human sperm. By using immuno-affinity chromatography and mass spectrometry analysis, cell adhesion molecule 4 (CADM4) was then identified as a sFUT5-interacting protein on OECs. OEC-bound spermatozoa possessed more intact DNA and superior fertilizing capacities than the unbound spermatozoa. OEC binding also prolongs human sperm viability in vitro and maintain them in a quiescent state. The results of the project enhance our understanding on the physiological role of the human oviduct on sperm functions and indicate the possible use of OECs for functional sperm selection in assisted reproduction treatment.

17117017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17117017.value: 肥胖是心血管，肾脏和代谢疾病的主要驱动因素， 是导致老年人群死亡的主要原因，称为“心脏代谢性肾综合症-CMRS”。目前，超过世界人口30%，约21亿的人是肥胖或者超重的。这种与生活方式相关的流行病已经并将继续成为现代化国家的社会，医疗和经济问题。 脂肪功能障碍是肥胖相关型心脏代谢肾综合症CMRS的主要罪魁祸首。脂肪细胞在脂肪组织中是高度异质的，胚胎起源不同，不同的增殖/分化或能量存储和利用能力的不同，不同的促分泌抗炎因子。在向心性肥胖患者中，从内脏脂肪分泌的过剩的炎症细胞因子在CMRS中起着举足轻重的作用。其中，脂质运载蛋白-Lipocalin-2是影响葡萄糖耐量和胰岛素抵抗，血管内皮功能障碍与高血压，以及慢性炎症-CMRS的重要危险因素。 在CMRS的发展过程中，组织纤维化逐渐损伤心脏和肾脏等器官的结构和功能，最终导致多器官衰竭。目前，缺乏有效的治疗和防止组织纤维化发生和发展的手段。然而，我们最近的研究显示，Lipocalin-2基因缺陷的小鼠对肥胖引起的或醛固酮激素引起的CMRS的器官组织纤维化起到保护作用。我们在脂肪组织， 心脏和肾脏中都观察到了这些保护作用，这表明Lipocalin-2是预防和控制早期肾脏和心脏纤维化损伤的重要药物靶点。 这里，我们设想在CMRS发展过程中，间皮细胞祖细胞过度产生的Lipocalin-2介导了心脏，肾脏和脂肪组织的纤维化损伤。所以，本研究计划旨在探索Lipocalin-2在促纤维化中的潜在细胞分子机制。特别是在组织纤维化中，Lipocalin-2的确切来源由严格的细胞谱系追踪确定。Lipocalin-2介导的分子间的相互作用，信号通路在其组织纤维化的发生发展被研究。研究结果將揭示Lipocalin-2起源于间皮细胞的病理生理作用，也有利于针对CMRS病人基于lipocalin-2靶向治疗的发展和管理。

17117017.label: Realisation of objectives
17117017.value: The two Objectives have largely been achieved. 1. The mice with selective deletion of Lcn2 alleles in mesothelial (progenitor) cells have been successfully established. The results from our study demonstrate that there is a more complex relationship between the mesothelial (progenitor) cells and mature adipocytes. The differentiation route towards fibrogenic and adipogenic lineages of cells need to be further investigated. 2.The mice with selective deletion of Lcn2 alleles in mature adipocytes have been successfully established. The adipocyte-derive lipocalin-2 was found to be responsible for mediating glumerular injury during the development of CMRS in mice.

17117017.value: The project demonstrated that 1) adipose-derived lipocalin-2 represents one of the major pathological forms of this molecule to induced renal injuries; 2) different lipocalin-2 variants exist in the human body; 3) targeting the pathological forms of lipocalin-2 holds great potential for the development of novel therapeutics for CMRS. 17117017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17117017.value: As the results demonstrate that differential lineage development of lipocalin-2-expressing cells contributes to cardiac fibrosis. Currently, the group is establishing platforms for single-cell analyses to trace the developmental route and regulatory mechanisms. During the present study, a potential role of lipocalin-2 variants, such as those derived from liver, in modulating brain function have also been uncovered. To this end, PI will apply for new funding to support the continuous investigations.

17117017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17117017.value: Lipocalin-2 is a pro-inflammatory molecule with a complex pattern of tissue expression and function. It protein variants play an important role in causing obesity and the associated cardiometabolic renal syndrome (CMRS). Under pathological conditions, induction/overexpression of pathological forms of lipocalin-2 promotes fibroblast differentiation, modulates adipogenesis and switches epithelial phenotypes, in turn causing fibrotic damages in heart, adipose tissue and kidneys. Thus to delineate the precise source of pro-fibrogenic lipocalin-2 will lead to the development of novel therapeutics for CMRS, the leading non-communicable diseases around the world.

17117217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17117217.value: Myocardial ischemic disease is a leading cause of death worldwide. Clinically, the most effective way is restoration of blood flow, but reperfusion itself may cause additional tissue injury called “ischemia/reperfusion injury (I/RI)”. The diabetic heart is more sensitive to I/RI. Although the mechanism governing the vulnerability of the diabetic heart to I/RI is not fully understood, alterations in cardiac metabolism have been suggested to play an important role in its pathology. In diabetes, fatty acids (FA) metabolism is favored, while the glucose oxidation rates are relatively decreased. This contributes to adenosine triphosphate (ATP) generation inefficiency, and increases the generation of toxic FA intermediates, further increasing diabetic heart susceptibility to I/RI. Thus, examining ways to down-regulate cardiac FA metabolism may provide new strategy to combat I/RI in type 2 diabetes, the most prevalent kind of diabetes mellitus. The telomeric protein repressor activator protein 1 (Rap1) is an identified regulator that regulates gene transcription by binding to non-telomeric sites. Particularly, Rap1 can bind to nuclear peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha (PPARα, an important transcriptional regulator of lipid metabolism) loci in the liver, and regulate the transcription of PPARα and its target genes, including the lipid transporter cluster of differentiation 36 (CD36). Furthermore, Rap1 is also found in the cytoplasmic fraction of various cell lines and enhances NFκB signaling, and in turn the activation of NFκB initiates the gene expression of Rap1. Our preliminary studies showed that Rap1 level is significantly increased in the heart of high fat diet-induced type 2 diabetic mice, with concomitant activation of NFκB, higher expression of PPARα and CD36 and progressively increased susceptibility to myocardial I/RI, as compared to the non-diabetes. Currently, the scope of Rap1 in managing cardiac energy metabolism in diabetes is not clearly defined. We hypothesize that, in type 2 diabetes, cardiac expression of Rap1 is increased, which may be a major mechanism that increases the susceptibility to myocardial I/RI through facilitating cardiac FA metabolism via PPARα/ CD36 signaling. Therefore, the proposed research aims to 1. Investigate if Rap1 increases myocardial susceptibility to ischemia/reperfusion injury in type 2 diabetic rodents. 2. Observe if Rap1 regulates cardiac energy metabolism via PPARα/CD36 signaling during myocardial I/RI in type 2 diabetic rodents. The proposed studies will improve our understanding of the pathophysiology of this phenomenon and may help facilitate the development of novel and better therapies for the management of ischemic heart disease in diabetes in whom this complication is very common. 缺血性心臟病目前已成為全世界範圍患病和死亡的主要原因。臨床上心臟再灌注是降低心肌缺血損傷最有效的辦法，但其本身卻可誘導額外的心臟損害和綜合症，稱為“心肌缺血再灌注(MI/R)損傷”。而糖尿病進一步增加了MI/R損傷的敏感性，儘管其潛在的分子機制尚未明朗，但伴隨著糖尿病的心臟能量代謝的改變/紊亂有可能起到至關重要的作用。在糖尿病中，心臟脂肪酸代謝上升，糖代謝速率相應降低，從而使得心肌細胞中三磷酸腺苷產生效率下降，脂毒性中間產物產生增加，進一步增加了糖尿病心臟對MI/R損傷的敏感性。因此，研究降低心臟脂肪代謝對尋找治療糖尿病MI/R損傷的作用靶點具有重要的臨床指導意義。 端粒結合蛋白Rap1作為端粒蛋白複合體中的其中一個亞基，能結合於非端粒序列，從而發揮轉錄調控因數的作用。研究已證實在肝臟中，Rap1能結合位於染色體臂上的PPARα（調控脂肪代謝的重要調控因數）啟動序列，進而介導PPARα及其下游調控基因，如CD36（脂肪酸轉運蛋白）的轉錄啟動。此外，研究也發現，Rap1存在於不同種類細胞系的細胞質中並增強炎症信號通路NFκB的活性。而增強的NFκB信號通路能促進Rap1的基因表達，從而形成正回饋迴圈。我們的前期研究也證實高脂食物誘導的2型糖尿病心肌中Rap1高表達，同時伴隨著心肌中增強的NFκB活性，PPARα和CD36的高表達以及加重的MI/R損傷。然而，到目前為止，Rap1在糖尿病心肌中對心肌脂肪酸的調控機制仍未清楚闡明。因此，我們提出假設，在2型糖尿病中，心肌高表達的Rap1可能通過PPARα/CD36信號通路增強心肌脂肪酸代謝從而導致糖尿病MI/R損傷加重。 因此，本課題主要是在2型糖尿病小鼠模型上，探討Rap1啟動在糖尿病MI/R損傷加重中所扮演的角色並闡明其潛在機制。本課題的實施及完成，將為糖尿病患者在再灌注干預過程中進行藥物治療提供理論及實驗依據，對減輕糖尿病心肌梗死的程度及減少心血管併發症將有重要意義。

17117217.label: Realisation of objectives
17117217.value: The first objective of the current project is to investigate whether or not Rap1 increases the susceptibility to myocardial I/RI in type 2 diabetic rodents (in vitro, in vivo). Our answer to this question is YES based on preliminary studies, and we went on further into the mechanism why this happens and identified the impact on Rap1 on STAT3, the unknown key molecule in myocardial ischemia protection. The related study was published in FASEB J. 2020 Mar;34(3):4482-4496. And, the further in depth study regarding how Rap1 may impact on myocardial I/RI via modulating cardiac energy metabolism, we diverted a bit to first address the impact of Rap1 on metabolism in aging hearts which are less resistant to ischemic insults. The related study was published in 2021 (Theranostics. 2021 Mar 4;11(10):4710-4727). This basically addressed the mechanism proposed in objective 2, and partly the objective 3. To further elucidate the role of CD36 in myocardial ischemia in the functionally impaired diabetic heart, we went on further the address its impact on diabetic cardiomyopathy, a pathology known to render the heart to more vulnerable to ischemic insult. The related findings was published (Biochem Biophys Res Commun. 2021 Apr 9;548:196-203. ), and further publication is expected.

17117217.label: Major findings and research outcome
17117217.value: Our studies result in the clear conclusion that Rap1 deficiency protects the heart from ischemic damage through STAT3-dependent reduction of cardiomyocyte apoptosis, which may yield viable target for pharmacological intervention in ischemic heart disease. This is based on the findings that Stattic (selective STAT3 inhibitor) pretreatment canceled the abovementioned protective effect. Furthermore, co-immunoprecipitation assay revealed a direct interaction between Rap1 and STAT3, but not JAK2, suggesting that the association of Rap1 with STAT3 may contribute to the reduced activity of STAT3 (Ser727 ) upon H/R stimulation. Furthermore, we find that EP4 tightly coordinates the rates of cardiac fatty acid uptake and ATP generation via FOXO1/CD36 signalling axis. Our study provides evidences for the link between EP4 and cardiac fatty acid transport and further pointed out that EP4 could be a potential target for modulating fatty acid metabolism and curbing cardiac tissue-specific impairment of function following diabetes, which may represent a major mechanism why diabetic heart is less resistant to myocardial I/RI.

17117417.label: Major findings and research outcome
17117417.value: 1. We found that PORCN mRNA expression was highly up-regulated in human HCC relative to their corresponding NT tissues in 100 cases of human HCC patients. In addition to HCC, PORCN over-expression was also found in colon adenocarcinoma, lung adenocarcinoma, renal cell carcinoma, bladder cancer, and breast cancer. IHC staining also confirmed PORCN over-expression in human HCC. High PORCN expression was found to correlated with poor disease-free survival in human HCC patients. 2. To better understand which hypoxia-induced molecular events are essential to HCC development, we performed transcriptome sequencing in a HCC cell line, MHCC97L, which were exposed to 20% and 1% O2 for 24 hours. We found that PORCN was significantly induced by hypoxia. HIF is the master regulator of hypoxia-mediated responses. We have located a putative hypoxia response elements (HIF-binding site) HRE region in the promoter of PORCN. Chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) with HIF-1α antibody in hypoxic MHCC97L cells confirmed the binding of HIF-1α to the putative HRE of PORCN. Furthermore, we found that PORCN expression in human HCC and NT tissues were positively correlated with two strong HIF-1 transcriptional targets LOXL2 and NDUFA4L2. Knockdown of HIF-1α but not HIF-2α reduced hypoxia-induced PORCN expression in MHCC97L cells. Hypoxia-induced PORCN expression was almost fully abrogated in HIF-1α knockout cells. PORCN functions to facilitate the secretion of Wnt ligands. Secreted Wnt ligands activate the Wnt pathway leading to the stabilization of β-catenin. We found that hypoxia profoundly induced β-catenin protein expression which could be reduced upon knockdown or knockout of HIF-1α. Constructs encompassing PORCN WT or Mut HREs were cloned into Firefly luciferase constructs and transfected together with construct of Renilla luciferase into HCC cells. We found that hypoxia induced the luciferase activity of cells transfected with constructs containing PORCN WT HRE but not the Mut HRE. 3. To investigate the functions of PORCN, we established PORCN over-expressing (OE) stable MHCC97L subclones. Over-expression of PORCN led to a marked increase of a well-known β-catenin transcriptional target, C-MYC and stemness genes, OCT4, NANOG, CD44, CD24, and CD90. Over-expression of PORCN increased sphere formation. Knockdown of PORCN reduced the number of spheres in hypoxic condition with only a modest effect in cell proliferation. Knockdown of PORCN significantly repressed HCC growth. 4. Next, we tested the efficiency of two PORCN inhibitors, LGK974 and Wnt-C59, in HCC. Both PORCN inhibitors suppressed β-catenin protein expression. Both PORCN inhibitors reduced tumor sphere formation, the size of the orthotopic HCC tumors, tumor incidence in different mouse HCC models with no obvert toxicity such as weight loss.

17117417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17117417.value: PORCN inhibitors could be potentially employed as HCC therapies especially targeting hypoxic liver cancer. Our preclinical studies might lead to clinical trials involving PORCN inhibitors in HCC patients. Our study also provides the basis of the biological importance of PORCN in other hypoxic HCC tumors and knowledge could be applied and extended to other cancer types including colon, lung, renal, bladder and breast cancer. Also PORCN could be used as a prognostic indicator of HCC in the future.

17117417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17117417.value: Hypoxia, oxygen deprivation, is a common feature of liver cancer due to abnormal tumor blood vessels and insufficient blood supply. Hypoxia is associated with aggressive phenotypes that result in unsatisfactory clinical outcomes in HCC patients. Therefore, novel therapeutic strategies are urgently needed to combat hypoxic HCC. We found that PORCN is a transcriptional target of HIF-1, the master regulator of hypoxic adaptation and response. PORCN activates canonical WNT/β-catenin signaling pathway that induces cancer cell stemness, thus promoting liver cancer growth and metastasis. Genetic knockdown or pharmacological inhibition of PORCN significantly reduced stemness in HCC cells cultured in hypoxia as well as suppressed tumor growth and progression in mice. Clinically, PORCN was overexpressed in various hypoxic tumors, including HCC. Upregulation of PORCN was correlated with poor survival and prognosis in HCC patients. Our study reveals PORCN as a biomarker of hypoxic HCC. Targeting PORCN represents a promising therapeutic approach for HCC treatment.

17118117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17118117.value: Hunting and wildlife trade together constitute a key driver of biodiversity loss, particularly in tropical forests. These activities have caused the extirpation or substantial population declines of targeted species, including elephants, which have disappeared from large portions of their former range. Defaunation can effect major changes on ecosystem composition and function, leading to cascading changes in abundance or diversity of faunal groups at lower trophic levels. Elephants – the largest terrestrial animals on the planet – play important roles in the savanna and forest ecosystems where they reside, and previous studies have recorded their importance to other taxonomic groups including vertebrates and invertebrates. However, most research on the subject comes from Africa, and little is known about the role of Asian elephants in tropical forest systems. Here, we aim to fill this gap by systematically surveying multiple assemblages of plants, invertebrates, and vertebrates to gauge the impact of elephants on tropical forest ecosystems. We will include surveys of trees, small mammals, anurans, lizards, and butterflies with which to relate to differences in elephant density as well as the density of other large herbivores or carnivores spanning multiple forest sites in Thailand and Peninsular Malaysia. As this part of the world suffers from among the highest rates of forest loss and hunting/poaching, our efforts to understand the impacts of such defaunation will be imperative to understand the impact of this loss as well as to guide future conservation directions in the region. 狩猎和野生动物贸易共同组成生物多样性丧失的关键驱动因子，这一事实在热带雨林生态系统中尤为突出。人类的这些活动已经带来包括大象在内的目标物种的灭绝或种群数量的锐减。亚洲象已经从绝大多数的历史分布区域内消失。脱共栖物将改变生态系统的组成和功能，导致在较低营养级上动物区系丰富度或多样性的级联变化。大象，地球上现存的最大的陆栖动物，在它们生存的森林和热带草原生态系统中发挥着极其重要的作用，以往的研究曾经记录它们对包括脊椎动物和无脊椎动物在内的其他分类群发挥的重要作用，但这些研究项目多集中在非洲，目前对热带雨林生态系统中亚洲象发挥的生态作用还知之甚少。因此，本研究将通过对包括植物、无脊椎动物和脊椎动物在内的多个群组进行系统性调查，评估亚洲象在热带雨林生态系统中的作用，填补这一研究空白。我们将在泰国和马来西亚半岛，按不同的亚洲象密度以及不同密度的其他大型食草动物或食肉动物设置不同的森林样地，调查其中的树木、小型哺乳动物、无尾两栖类、蜥蜴和蝴蝶。作为世界上遭受最高比例的森林丧失和高狩猎、偷猎率的区域，本研究对此区域脱去栖物的影响的理解，将对理解这种丧失带来的生态影响和引导此区域未来保护的方向至关重要。
