17118317.label: Project Objectives
17118317.value: Sample and evaluate habitat associations of mycalesine species across forest and ecotone sites in Cameroon. By surveying species across forest and ecotone sites and determining habitat preferences we will provide the context for thermal performance as a function of habitat. Determine upper thermal tolerance limits (Ctmax) of different mycalesine species, for larvae and adults, from forest and ecotone sites. By sampling broadly across the mycalesine group, and incorporating phylogenetic structure into our analysis, we will examine how habitat and evolutionary history affects thermal tolerance. Compare plasticity in thermal tolerance of open habitat associated species (Bicyclus dorothea and Bicyclus vulgaris) and forest associated species (Bicyclus sanaos and Bicyclus smithi). We’ll take a more in-depth approach in these four common mycalesine species of differing habitat associations (forest vs. open habitat) to assess how plasticity might be important in determining habitat’s role in structuring climate change vulnerability. Relate thermal tolerance traits, habitat associations and plasticity to spatial distributions of species (across elevation and latitude) to examine possible macroecological consequences of physiological patterns observed in the study. We will bring together all of the spatial, thermal and habitat data collected throughout the study duration and use this to model the relationship between distributions, phylogeny and thermal tolerance. Synthesize all results to evaluate how habitat structures thermal tolerance and ultimately climate change vulnerability, using mycalesine butterfly species as a model system. At each level of the study, we are examining unique and important levels at which habitat might influence thermal tolerance. Once all experiments and data collection are complete, we’ll examine the study as a whole and determine which levels (e.g. population, species, and phylogeny) affect thermal performance and therefore vulnerability to environmental change.

17118317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17118317.value: Both climate change and habitat destruction are two of the biggest concerns for conservation science at present with increasing extinction risks arising from both threats for taxa worldwide. How these two forces might interact is also of concern but not well understood, particularly in tropical ecosystems where warming and habitat loss threaten the majority of Earth’s biodiversity. In this study, we’ll assess the thermal tolerance of species across the diverse and model system mycalesine butterfly group in Cameroon to determine whether forest associated species, already vulnerable to habitat loss, might also be additionally vulnerable to warming in the future. Bicyclus anynana, an East African mycalesine butterfly species, represents a key and model species for understanding evolutionary development and ecology and will serve as primary comparative system for our research in Central Africa. Within this framework, we’ll first determine whether the upper thermal limit (critical thermal maximum/Ctmax) is lower for forest associated species relative to ecotone (savanna and forest transition zone) associated species. This will require field surveys of mycalesine species across a 400km latitudinal gradient and collection of specimens for laboratory thermal tolerance assays. Next, we’ll focus on two forest associated species (Bicyclus sanaos and Bicyclus smithi) and two open habitat associated species (B. dorothea and B. vulgaris) and determine plastic responses of thermal tolerance traits of each of the species to evaluate whether the forest species has lower plasticity relative to the disturbance associated species. Finally, using distribution and phylogenetic data we’ll evaluate how thermal tolerance relates to spatial distribution and long-term evolutionary patterns within the mycalesine butterflies. Altogether this research will elucidate how thermal tolerance relates to habitat associations in tropical species and how climate change might differentially impact forest restricted species relative to open habitat associates. 氣候變化和棲息地破壞及由此提升的全球生物滅絕風險是生態保育面臨的兩個最大問題。同樣值得關注而我們了解不多的議題是這兩種因素之間的相互作用 ，尤其在受到氣候暖化和棲息地損失嚴重威脅的熱帶生態系統。 我們以Bicyclus anynana，一種東非mycalesine蝴蝶物種為示範物種，去理解蝴蝶的進化發展及相關生態，並以之和我們在中非的研究相比較。在這個框架內，我們將探索森林相關物種是否比交錯群落（草原和森林過渡帶）相關物種有較低耐熱上界限（耐熱臨界最大值/ Ctmax）。 這將需要在400公里緯度梯度上進行實地調查，並收集mycalesine樣本用於實驗室內的耐熱性測定。 隨後，我們將專門研究兩個森林相關物種（Bicyclus sanaos 和Bicyclus smithi）和兩個開放棲息地（有人為破壞痕跡）相關物種（B. dorothea和B. vulgaris），並確定每個物種的耐熱性狀的適應性，以評估森林物種相對於被干擾棲息地相關物種是否有較低的適應性。 最後，我們使用地理分佈和系統發生學的數據，評估mycalesine属各蝴蝶物种耐熱性與其空間分佈和長期進化模式的關係。 這項研究將阐释熱帶物種的耐熱性与其棲息地的關联，以及氣候變化可能對森林物種和開放棲息地物種的不同影響。

17118317.label: Realisation of objectives
17118317.value: Objective 1. Sample and evaluate habitat associations of mycalesine species across forest and ecotone sites in Cameroon. By surveying species across forest and ecotone sites and determining habitat preferences we will provide the context for thermal performance as a function of habitat. In both ecotone and forest sites, we conducted a 20 day mycalesine butterfly survey during the wet and dry seasons to assess the association of Bicyclus species with microhabitats (opened areas vs closed understories). We set banana-baited traps in opened areas and closed understories of each habitat, and recorded daily, the number of Bicyclus captured in each trap. In order to relate the microhabitat associations of these butterflies with ambient temperature, we recorded the temperature of each microhabitat during the survey period using Thermochron iButton data loggers. Through this effort, we collected important microhabitat preference information of Bicyclus butterflies during the wet and the dry season in ecotone and forest sites of Cameroon. This is important data itself but particularly crucial for contextualizing results for the remaining objectives. Objective 2. Determine upper thermal tolerance limits (Ctmax) of different mycalesine species, for larvae and adults, from forest and ecotone sites. By sampling broadly across the mycalesine group, and incorporating phylogenetic structure into our analysis, we will examine how habitat and evolutionary history affects thermal tolerance. From a wild stock of four Bicyclus species (B. dorothea, B. vulgaris, B. sandace and B. sanaos) sampled in both ecotone and forest sites, we established laboratory colonies under controlled environments using the common garden approach. Each species was reared under two temperature regimes (20 and 30°C); we determined the upper (CTmax) and the lower (CTmin) thermal limits of the subsequent larvae and adults of all the species obtained under the two rearing temperatures. However, we encountered some difficulties in rearing all populations and species due to both difficulties in finding sufficient numbers of individuals across all sites and also difficulties in rearing all populations. Initial species targeted were B. dorothea, B. vulgaris, B. smithi and B. sanaos; but in the end conducted the study with B. dorothea, B. vulgaris, B. sandace and B. sanaos. We were not able to establish B. smithi colonies in the laboratory. It was then replaced by B. sandace. Also, we failed to establish laboratory populations of B. sanaos from forest sites after many trials. For that reason, we were not able to determine the thermal tolerance for B. sanaos population from the forest. Our results indicated very clearly that ecotone populations generally had higher plasticity in thermal tolerance (for both larvae and adults) across all species (Dongmo et al. in prep). Objective 3. Compare plasticity in thermal tolerance of open habitat associated species (Bicyclus dorothea and Bicyclus vulgaris) and forest associated species (Bicyclus sanaos and Bicyclus smithi). For the four target species, from Objective 1, we confirmed that B. vulgaris and B. dorothea are more open associated than both B. sanaos and B. sandace. And from the thermal tolerance data collection we learned that all species generally had higher plasticity in thermal tolerance in the ecotone (with the exception of B. vulgaris CTmin). For the two open associated species (B. dorothea and B. vulgaris) we found that adult CTmax was higher than the two closed habitat associates (B. sanaos and B. sandace). We also found that B. sanaos, the most closed habitat associated species, had a higher CTmin indicating that its thermal tolerance was significantly narrower than the other three species. The combination of higher plasticity in ecotone populations and narrower thermal tolerance of the closed forest species indicates a likely higher vulnerability of forest butterflies to climate change. Objective 4. Relate thermal tolerance traits, habitat associations and plasticity to spatial distributions of species (across elevation and latitude) to examine possible macroecological consequences of physiological patterns observed in the study. We will bring together all of the spatial, thermal and habitat data collected throughout the study duration and use this to model the relationship between distributions, phylogeny and thermal tolerance. Due to the difficulties encountered in the field, and field work taking longer than anticipated, we ultimately ran out of time to conduct the spatial analysis as planned. However, our intense focus on field-collected data for habitat associations, thermal tolerance data (for the four target species), and locality data leaves open the possibility to conduct this analysis. We hope to execute this in the near future. Objective 5. Synthesize all results to evaluate how habitat structures thermal tolerance and ultimately climate change vulnerability, using mycalesine butterfly species as a model system. At each level of the study, we are examining unique and important levels at which habitat might influence thermal tolerance. Once all experiments and data collection are complete, we’ll examine the study as a whole and determine which levels (e.g. population, species, and phylogeny) affect thermal performance and therefore vulnerability to environmental change. As discussed above, our results together suggest that tropical forest species are likely to be more vulnerable to climate change than open-associated species. While this has been shown in earlier studies, our results additionally point to important evolutionary underpinnings to differences in thermal tolerance and capacities to respond to warming temperatures. Even within species, populations from thermally variable environments (e.g. ecotone) may have higher plasticity in thermal tolerance traits. While genetic variation wasn’t explicitly within the scope of our study, we understood the importance of this in dictating warming responses. During our work, we re-established a long-standing collaboration with Prof. Tom Smith at UCLA and Dr. Ying Zhen at Westlake University to investigate the relationship between thermal tolerance traits in B. dorothea and standing genomic variation. Interestingly, we found very little evidence of population structure across its distribution in Cameroon despite clear morphological and thermal tolerance differences (Ying, Dongmo et al., in review). We believe that natural selection is likely then structuring variable traits in B. dorothea between forest and ecotone but that high gene flow results in surprisingly low genetic structure. Finally, during the course of the study we were struck by the challenges we faced in collecting data and frequently reflected on the difficulty of conducting conservation research on insects in Central Africa. Building on our experiences from this work, we’ve written a synthetic perspective aimed at directing and influencing key tropical butterfly research in Central Africa in the future (Dongmo, Hanna, and Bonebrake in prep). One of our key conclusions is that climate change is likely to be a key threat (among others) to species in tropical Africa… but large obstacles to conservation, including armed conflict, corruption, and socioeconomic issues, will hamper abilities to conserve African biodiversity. We recommended steps for overcoming these challenges in our perspective piece (Dongmo, Hanna, and Bonebrake in prep). Education Plan. Due to an armed conflict that emerged soon after the project initiation, we decided against bringing students to Cameroon during the study. However, we did integrate elements of our Cameroon research into courses at HKU as planned. We devoted lectures to the subject in Conservation Biology (BIOL3303) and Globalization in Question: Human and Economic Consequences (CCGL9022), including live Zoom sessions with the project postdoc (Dr. Michel Dongmo) from the field in Cameroon.

17118317.label: Major findings and research outcome
17118317.value: Our results revealed an important effect of developmental temperature on thermal tolerance traits of the larvae and adults of all Bicyclus species tested. Specifically, low developmental temperature (20°C) leads to lower CTmax and higher CTmin, and high developmental temperature (30°C) has the opposite effect, that is low CTmin and high CTmax in both larval and adult butterflies. We also found that habitat was a key determinant for thermal tolerance traits in Bicyclus butterflies. Ecotone populations of B. dorothea and B. vulgaris showed important variation in CTmin and CTmax in larvae and adults across developmental temperature while in the forest populations, there was a little variation of these traits except in B. vulgaris. Our results also revealed that the lowest CTmax and highest CTmin in adults for both developmental temperatures were for B. sanaos, the most forest associated species. Over the developmental temperature range (10°C), plasticity was estimated as the variation in upper and lower thermal limits. In both larvae and adults, ecotone populations were generally more plastic in CTmax and CTmin compared to forest populations with the exception of CTmin in B. vulgaris. Among all species, B. dorothea and B. vulgaris showed the highest plasticity in CTmax in both habitats while B. sanaos showed the lowest. Habitat surveys showed that throughout the wet and the dry seasons, B. dorothea and B. vulgaris were more abundant in open microhabitats (characterized by greater temperature fluctuation) in both forest and ecotone while B. sanaos were mostly restricted to thermally stable understories. Altogether, these results suggest that habitat and microhabitat associations are critical determinants of thermal tolerance for tropical insects and that climate change vulnerability is likely to be associated with these habitat associations. Climate change will be a major force in driving biodiversity changes in Central Africa and our work here provides some mechanistic understanding of this with respect to tropical butterflies. However, we also found during our research that major obstacles to conservation will challenge effective interventions. Building on our experience from this study, we recommend a range of steps for enhancing capacity for conservation of Central African butterflies and insects: 1) enhance museum collections in the region, 2) ensure that socioeconomic realities are always incorporated into planning, 3) oversee projects to ensure corruption does not disrupt work, and 4) solidify scientific collaboration and avoid “helicopter research” such that local researchers can be effectively trained and skills developed.

17118317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17118317.value: Our work shows how habitat can structure plasticity in thermal tolerance for Bicyclus butterflies. This finding has a range of intriguing implications for climate change vulnerability of tropical biodiversity? but many open questions remain. For example, what are the genetic or molecular mechanisms that drive this variation across habitats? Further investigation of these mechanisms will provide answers as to the pace of adaptation or responses to warming. We plan to work with collaborators in the future to explore this issue. We also had some difficulty in collecting data on the most forest-restricted species. This is a perpetual problem in the study of tropical butterflies, and it?s concerning that some of the most vulnerable species may be the ones we understand the least. By building on our experience here we hope to learn more about forest-restricted species and vulnerability to climate change in the near future. Finally, we believe there is an urgency required for focus on the biodiverse rich communities of Central African insects. We plan on conducting, encouraging, and facilitating further research on a variety of aspects of African butterflies and other understudied species in a responsible way that enhances local capacity and builds socioeconomic resilience.

17118317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17118317.value: Global climate change is threatening the most diverse ecosystems on the planet. In response to the environmental changes including climate, organisms rely on a variety of mechanisms such as phenotypic plasticity (trait changes resulting from developmental conditions). However, divergent selection across a landscape can lead to differential sensitivity of animals to heat due to contrasting conditions experienced during pre-adult development. In this context, we studied plastic responses in thermal tolerance coupled with microclimate preferences and habitat associations in African Bicyclus butterflies. Our results revealed that developmental temperature and habitat types (ecotone vs forest) strongly influence thermal sensitivity in butterflies. Specifically, low developmental temperature leads to high lower thermal limits and low upper thermal limits, while high developmental temperature has the opposite effect. We also found that ecotone populations were more plastic in thermal tolerance compared to forest populations. These results together indicate the key role of habitat in structuring organismal climate change responses and vulnerability. We also emphasize the importance of considering a diversity of threats (including climate change) to the poorly studied but incredibly diverse and unique community of Central African butterflies.

17118517.label: Realisation of objectives
17118517.value: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is one of the deadly cancers with dismal survival rates, highlighting the unmet need for early detection to improve patient survival. Genome-wide association study, familial aggregation in the high-risk region and the historical migration patterns implicate genetic factors as playing an etiological role. The current understanding of the genetic pathogenesis of rare deleterious variants with large effects on ESCC is still poor. This current study provided the first comprehensive and in-depth next-generation sequencing (NGS) study utilizing deep target capture sequencing of an oncology panel of 598 genes including RAD50, ZNF208, and CNTRL, with a large validation cohort of ESCC patients from Henan to understand the genetic basis for this cancer. We provided thorough investigation of the entire RAD50, (also includes MRE11A and NBS1) for the genetic predisposition role of the evolutionarily conserved MRN complex in the high-risk ESCC region. We utilized a gene-based association test and revealed no significant association of elevated cancer risk in Henan familial ESCC patients carrying rare deleterious and LOF variants in RAD50-MRE11A-NBS1. Further detailed data analysis in the RAD50 gene, two rare pathogenic LOF variants in the zinc hook domain of RAD50 were identified to only be present in familial ESCC patients but were not found in the sporadic ESCC patients and controls. These zinc hook variants, RAD50-Q672X and RAD50-K722fs, were about 10-fold and 100-fold less frequent in East Asian and all populations including African, Latino, Jewish, European, South Asian, and East Asian populations in the genomAD database. The incidence of two zinc hook pathogenic mutations of RAD50 is rare, however, they are clinically important. The ClinVar database reported one breast cancer and four hereditary cancer predisposing syndrome patients carrying either RAD50-Q672X and RAD50-K722fs. Importantly, when we consider the RAD50 zinc hook domain localized to amino acid residues at 635–734, three more zinc hook LOF pathogenic mutations (RAD50-S653X, RAD50-R656X, and RAD50-E676X) were reported in one NBS-like disorder and another six hereditary cancer predisposing syndrome patients from the ClinVar database. Our study is the first to suggest the association of two rare RAD50 zinc hook LOF mutations with familial ESCC in Northern Chinese and implicate the potential genetic predisposition role of the RAD50 zinc hook domain in ESCC genetic pathogenesis. Functional studies on RAD50 suggest that the dominant negative effects of the RAD50-Q672X mutant impair cellular responses to DSB repair and enhance sensitivity to genotoxic agents including checkpoint inhibitor AZD7762 and formaldehyde-induced replication stress. The project objectives 1 and 2 were fully achieved. Aim 1: The current study performed validation of the multi-gene contribution of RAD50, ZNF208, and CNTRL in larger independent cohorts of 3055 individuals from the high-risk Henan collected during 2001–2014 from Northern China high-risk Linxian and Anyang counties (Henan, China) provided by Lidong Wang (Zhengzhou University). In the combined analysis, a total of 3289 participants consisted 1044 familial ESCC, 1074 sporadic ESCC, and 1171 geographically matched controls without ESCC. In the discovery phase, the 234 family history-positive (FH+) ESCC involved two generations and ≥2 family members diagnosed with ESCC including proband while the 810 FH+ ESCC in the validation phase only involved one generation. The gnomAD database contains variations in ~141,000 individuals resulting from the aggregation of exomes and genomes from case-control sequencing studies of common adult-onset diseases including cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes, and psychiatric disorders. Due to the budget constraint, we used the hybridization-based target capture approach with the SeqCap EZ probe kit (Roche) instead of the original proposed amplicon sequencing of the three candidate genes with the 48.48 Fluidigm Access ArraysTM. Target capture with NimbleGen SeqCap EZ capture kits (Roche, Switzerland) were performed according to standard protocol after libraries constructed by KAPA HTP library preparation kit and sequencing on the Illumina Hi-seq platform. The data from 3289 individuals were processed using the analysis pipeline following the GATK guidelines and annotated by ANNOVAR . The rare missense variants of unknown significance with Combined annotation dependent depletion (CADD) score of ≥25 (version1.4) are considered deleterious variants. In NGS analysis, for the rare RAD50, ZNF208, and CNTRL LOF and RDV variants, the Fisher’s exact test (two-tailed) was used for calculation of the odds ratio (OR) between cases and control using a Python package SciPy and a p<0.05 was considered statistically significant. Gene based association analysis with rare RAD50, ZNF208, and CNTRL LOF and RDV variants did not detect significant association with familial ESCC risk. A total of seven pathogenic RAD50 LOF variants were detected at exons 8, 13, 17, 19, and 23 in 15 individuals consisting of seven familial ESCC, four sporadic ESCC patients, and four control individuals. Four of the fifteen carriers (26.7%, 4/15) had LOF RAD50 variants mapping to exon 13 containing the zinc hook domain. Based on the observation of the absence of the RAD50 zinc hook LOF mutations in both sporadic ESCC and control cohorts, they were combined and defined as the nonfamilial control population to estimate the risk of familial ESCC patients. In the familial ESCC patients, the frequency of two pathogenic variants, p.Q672X and the other recurrent p.K722fs variant (4/2088, 0.19%), is statistically higher than that in the nonfamilial controls (0/4490, 0%) (OR inf, p = 0.010). An increased risk with large effect in familial ESCC patients carrying these two pathogenic RAD50 LOF variants is also observed, when compared to East Asians from the gnomAD database (4/19,954, 0.02%) (OR 9.57, p = 4.1 × 10−3) and all populations from gnomAD (5/282,670, 0.0018%) (OR 108.51, p = 3.5 × 10−7). Aim 2: We encountered difficulty for stable expression of the RAD50 mutants in ESCC cell lines, KYSE150 and KYSE450. Since the RAD50 mutant protein expression levels in ESCC gradually decreased over a few passages in 1-2 weeks, functional characterization was performed in the U2OS cells. The RAD50-Q672X mutant resulted in DSB repair delay, no sensitization of cells upon cisplatin or PARPi treatment. The dominant negative LOF RAD50 mutant did not enhance the therapeutic efficacy of platinum-based drugs. Interestingly, our study suggested novel insights for the potential synthetic lethal therapeutic options for zinc hook mutations and AZD7762, CDK1 inhibitor, as the functional characterization of the RAD50-Q672X suggested a dominant negative effect in DSB repair and replication stress. Thus, we deviated from the original plan for potential new treatment options by exploring synthetic lethality targeting ATR/CDK1 for checkpoint inhibition for hypersensitivity of U2OS cells to cell death upon replication stress. Immunofluorescence using H2A.X antibody on RAD50 mutant-expressing U2OS cells (Q672X and L1264F) treated with AZD7762 showed an elevated percentage pan-nuclear H2A.X foci positive cells. The larger proportion of cells were under extensive replication stress due to ATR-CHK1 mediated cell death. RAD50-L1264F is relatively more frequently detected in 4 FH+ ESCC, 4 sporadic ESCC, 3 controls in our cohort, and 80 East Asians but absent in 64517 Europeans from gnomAD. RAD50-L1264F is an East Asian-specific deleterious missense mutation with CADD score of 30 ranked among top 0.1% predicting deleteriousness. It lies within the C-terminal ATPase between D-loop and the H-loop/switch. Although the deleterious mutant RAD50-L1264F did not associate with higher familial ESCC risk, our functional study suggested patients carrying this East-Asian-specific heterozygous RAD50-L1264F may have a dominant negative effect upon induction of replication stress by formaldehyde treatment and the CHK1 inhibitor, AZD7762.

17118517.label: Major findings and research outcome
17118517.value: Massive parallel target sequencing approaches in familial esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) initially prioritized RAD50 as a candidate cancer predisposition gene. The combined study with 3289 Henan individuals from Northern China identified two pathogenic RAD50 protein truncation variants, p.Q672X and a recurrent p.K722fs variant at the zinc hook domain significantly conferring increased familial ESCC risk. Effects of ~10-fold higher familial ESCC risk were observed, when compared to East Asians from the gnomAD database. Functional characterization suggested that the RAD50-Q672X mutation contributes a dominant-negative effect in DNA repair of double-stranded breaks. Overexpression of the RAD50-Q672X and RAD50-L1264F missense mutation also sensitized cell death upon replication stress stimuli induced by formaldehyde treatment and the CHK1 inhibitor, AZD7762. Our study suggested the novel insight of the potential for synthetic lethal therapeutic options for RAD50-Q672X and the East-Asian-specific RAD50-L1264F variants and CHK1 inhibitors. The dominant negative effect of RAD50-Q672X upon formaldehyde and AZD7762 treatment leaded us to hypothesize RAD50-Q672X might pose an inhibitory effect on ATR functions and sensitized cell death towards DNA replication stress. The data provided valuable insight for understanding genetic susceptibility to this deadly cancer and lead to the identification of clinically useful gene panels for assessment of ESCC risk in high-risk individuals for early detection to prevent progression to advanced stage cancer. Identified alterations will allow us to better understand the key genes and signaling pathways that may be the driving factors in ESCC development and provide novel strategic insights of drugs that inducing replication stress and CHK1 inhibitors for potential therapeutics. The lessons learned from familial ESCC may be applied to sporadic cases in Hong Kong. This information is crucial for enhancing prevention and early detection of this deadly cancer. In line with these pioneer efforts in candidate gene mutation screening, the current study revealed the genetic role of DNA repair genes, especially RAD50, underlying genetic predisposition for familial ESCC. Our findings were published in two international peer review journals in “Cancers” and “International Journal of Cancer”. We also participated in two international conferences and presented posters in the American Association for Cancer Research Annual Meeting (AACR) 2018 and the 1st International Electronic Conference on Cancers: Exploiting Cancer Vulnerability by Targeting the DNA Damage Response. Details about the manuscripts and the posters are available in Part C of this final report. This project is in collaboration with Professor Tanya Paull of the University of Texas for the donor vector containing the complete coding sequence of human wildtype RAD50 fused to a C-terminal 6x-His epitope tag involved in the functional studies. A MPhil student was trained.

17118517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17118517.value: Our study is the first to suggest the association of two rare RAD50 zinc hook LOF mutations with familial ESCC in Northern Chinese and implicate the potential genetic predisposition role of the RAD50 zinc hook domain in ESCC genetic pathogenesis. Several other DNA repair genes including BRCA2, MSH2, and POLQ were previously reported to be associated with a higher risk of familial ESCC. Further development of non-invasive genetic profiling tests targeting a sequence constellation of these DNA repair genes associated with hereditary cancer for cancer risk assessment may benefit high-risk individuals from ESCC FH+ families. The current study suggested the novel insight of the potential for synthetic lethal therapeutic options for RAD50-Q672X and the East-Asian-specific RAD50-L1264F variants and CHK1 inhibitors upon replication stress. Further research exploring other deleterious RAD50 mutants including several other zinc hook mutants RAD50-K722fs ,RAD50-S653X, RAD50-R656X, and RAD50-E676X , for the potential therapeutic strategy combining replication stress induction, e.g. topoisomerase inhibitors and CHK1 inhibitors, is warranted for enhancing treatments of this deadly disease

17118517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17118517.value: Two deleterious RAD50 loss-of-function germline mutations were identified from the blood DNA of a cohort of 3289 Henan individuals by next-generation sequencing. These rare loss-of-function RAD50 variants were associated with a substantial increased risk of familial esophageal squamous cell carcinoma in high-risk Northern China. A functional study suggested that the RAD50 mutations may affect DNA repair and cell survival upon replication stress. Our preliminary functional study provided novel insight and the potential clinical implication that patients with heterozygous RAD50-L1264F and RAD50-Q672X status may have a potential synthetic lethal therapeutic option with CHK1 inhibitors. Further study is warranted for validation of the implicated genetic susceptibility role of the RAD50 Zinc Hook mutants were previously reported to be associated with a higher risk of familial ESCC. The current study provided additional genetic information for the role of RAD50 underlying genetic predisposition for familial ESCC. Several other DNA repair genes including BRCA2, MSH2, and POLQ were previously reported to be associated with a higher risk of familial ESCC. High-risk individuals from ESCC FH+ families may benefit from non-invasive genetic profiling tests targeting a sequence constellation of these DNA repair genes associated with hereditary cancer for cancer risk assessment.

17118717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17118717.value: Ischemic stroke is a major disease burden worldwide and 40% patients are accompanied with acute hyperglycemia (high glucose). Hyperglycemia is highly associated with increased brain damage, hemorrhage transformation (HT), mortality and poor functional recovery in ischemic stroke patients. However, the underlying mechanisms of hyperglycemia-mediated HT and poor outcome are largely unknown. Oxidative stress-mediated blood-brain-barrier (BBB) disruption is a key pathological process contributing to HT and poor outcome in ischemic stroke. Matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs) activity is an important biomarker for BBB disruption and HT. Plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 (PAI-1) is a crucial biomarker for guiding stroke thrombolysis and preventing HT. During thrombolytic treatment, cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury could aggravate oxidative stress by producing superoxide and nitric oxide, etc. Peroxynitrite, produced from the reaction of superoxide and nitric oxide, mediates MMPs activity, exacerbating BBB disruption and HT in ischemic brain. The presence of hyperglycemia could accelerate oxidative stress, inducing BBB disruption and HT in ischemic stroke. However, the roles of peroxynitrite in hyperglycemia-mediated BBB disruption and HT are unknown yet. Thus, we conducted a pilot study to address the question. Our preliminary data revealed that acute hyperglycemia increased peroxynitrite level, up-regulated MMPs expression/activity, down-regulated PAI-1 expression and increased the BBB hyperpermeability and HT in ischemic stroke rat model. Treatments of peroxynitrite scavenger uric acid or peroxynitrite decomposition catalyst blocked those changes. Therefore, we hypothesize that peroxynitrite could play critical roles in mediating HT and worsen neurological outcome in ischemic stroke with hyperglycemia. To confirm this hypothesis, in this proposal, we will address following questions: (1) Whether hyperglycemia could increase peroxynitrite production and whether peroxynitrite would contribute to hyperglycemia-mediated HT and poor functional recovery in ischemic stroke? (2) How peroxynitrite affects PAI-1/MMPs signaling cascades and leads to HT and poor outcome in ischemic stroke with hyperglycemia? Furthermore, we have screened active compounds from herbal medicine by using our newly developed high sensitive and specific fluorescent probes for peroxynitrite detection and found that Sodium Danshensu had a strong peroxynitrite-scavenging property with neuroprotective effects. Thus, we will use Sodium Danshensu as an example to explore whether peroxynitrite could be used as a molecular target for drug discovery to alleviate hemorrhagic transformation and improve functional recovery in ischemic stroke with hyperglycemia. With our unique technical platforms, preliminary data and the expertise, we expect to prove the hypothesis, publish several high-impact papers and provide scientific training for postgraduate students. The success of this project should have great clinical application potentials.

17118717.label: Realisation of objectives
17118717.value: With the support of the GRF grant, we have conducted a series of experiments and achieved all the goals designed in our original proposal. Objective 1: (1) To test whether hyperglycemia increases peroxynitrite production (ONOO-) during rat cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury and ischemic stroke patients: By using rat middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO)-reperfusion model, we demonstrated that acute hyperglycemia significantly induced the production of peroxynitrite in the ischemic cortex and striatum as detected by using our newly developed specific and sensitive probe HKYellow AM. Moreover, by using immunostaining and western blot analysis, we confirmed the increased level of 3-nitrotyrosine (3-NT, a footprint of peroxynitrite) in the rat ischemic brain tissues. We further analyzed the expression of the NADPH oxidase and nitric oxide synthase (NOS) expression in the ischemic brain tissues, which is a major source for the productions of superoxide, nitric oxide, and peroxynitrite. We found that acute hyperglycemia increased the expression of NADPH oxidase subunits p47 phox and p67 phox and iNOS in the ischemic brains, which aggravates peroxynitrite production. We further conducted a clinical study and found that the level of 3-NT in the plasma of acute ischemic stroke patients was positively correlated with the increased glucose level within 72 hours of ischemic onset. (2) To test the role of peroxynitrite in mediating hemorrhagic transformation and neurological deficit: We used a peroxynitrite decomposition catalyst (PDC) named FeTmPyP and uric acid to decrease or scavenge peroxynitrite respectively in the animal model of ischemic stroke. We observed that FeTmPyP treatment at a dosage of 3 mg/kg (i.v.) significantly decreased hemorrhagic transformation (HT) in the ischemic brains at 24 hours after ischemic onset, as indicated by the decrease of hemoglobin level and the hemorrhagic scores. FeTmPyP treatment significantly improved neurological outcomes. Consistently, uric acid treatment at a dosage of 16 mg/kg in Locke’s buffer also significantly decreased the hemorrhagic transformation and improved the neurological outcomes at 24 hours after ischemic onset. We then stepped forward to investigate the role of FeTmPyP on the long-term outcomes of ischemic stroke with hyperglycemia. We found that FeTmPyP treatment significantly increased survival rates and bodyweight after one-week treatment. Moreover, FeTmPyP significantly reduced the hemorrhagic transformation and improved neurological outcomes. These results suggest that peroxynitrite plays an essential role in mediating hemorrhagic transformation and neurological deficit in ischemic stroke with acute hyperglycemia. Objective 2: To investigate whether ONOO-/PAI-1/MMPs signaling cascades contribute to HT and poor outcomes in ischemic stroke with and without hyperglycemia in vivo: We detected the expression of PAI-1 and t-PA by using western-blot analysis and measured MMPs activity with gelatin zymography. We found that acute hyperglycemia significantly increased the expression of PAI-1 and t-PA, and up-regulated the expression and activity of MMP-9 and MMP-2/3 in ischemic brain tissues. FeTmPyP treatment significantly inhibited the expression and activity of MMP-9 and the expression of MMP-2/3 in the ischemic brains. Those results suggest that peroxynitrite production plays a crucial role in MMPs activation, contributing to the BBB disruption, HT, and poor outcome in ischemic stroke with acute hyperglycemia. Objective 3: To elucidate whether targeting ONOO- could be a promising strategy for drug discovery to alleviate hemorrhagic transformation and improve neurological outcome in ischemic stroke with hyperglycemia: Using Sodium Danshensu as an example: In this study, we first detected the effects of Sodium Danshensu (SDSS) on scavenging Sodium Danshensu (SDSS). We found that SDSS has the property of scavenging peroxynitrite directly as detected by liquid chromatography (HPLC). In the in vitro cultured cell system, SDSS dose-dependently reduced the fluorescent signaling of peroxynitrite and inhibited the formation of 3-NT in the cultured SHSY-5Y cells treated with the synthesized authentic peroxynitrite. By using DAF-FM staining, we found that SDSS treatment reduced SNAP (a nitric oxide donor)-induced NO level, suggesting the scavenging capacity of SDSS on nitric oxide. By using the EPR spin trapping technique, we demonstrated that SDSS could directly scavenge superoxide. Thus, SDSS is a promising antioxidant with scavenging effects on superoxide, nitric oxide, and peroxynitrite. We further confirmed the neuroprotective effects of SDSS in primary cultured rat cortical neurons in vitro. By using HKYellow AM probe, we found that SDSS treatment reduced peroxynitrite level in the neurons after treated with SIN-1, a peroxynitrite donor. SDSS also showed neuroprotective effects on the primary cultured neurons when exposed to oxygen and glucose deprivation and reoxygenation (OGD/RO) conditions. We also performed animal experiments to test the neuroprotective effects of SDSS on the rat model of cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury. Adult SD rats were subjected to 2 h of middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) to induce cerebral ischemia and followed with the release of the occlusion for 22 h of reperfusion. SDSS (20 mg/kg) was intravenously administrated at the onset of the reperfusion stage. SDSS treatment remarkably reduced infarct volume in the ischemia-reperfusion injured brains. Meanwhile, SDSS treatment significantly reduced the level of peroxynitrite in the plasma of the MCAO cerebral ischemic rats. Consistently, the immunostaining assay revealed that the level of 3-nitrotyrosine was remarkably increased in the ischemic brain tissues of the MCAO cerebral ischemia-reperfused rat model. The increased 3-nitrotyrosine was apparently reduced by SDSS administration. TUNEL assay showed that SDSS treatment reduced TUNEL- positive cells in ischemia-reperfusion brains. In summary, SDSS can efficiently protect brain tissues against ischemia-reperfusion injury, and the neuroprotective effects could be attributed to the bioactivities of scavenging peroxynitrite. Meanwhile, SDSS treatment (20 mg/kg) reduced the Evans blue leakage in the ischemic brains, indicating the protection of the blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity. We also found that SDSS significantly improved the neurological outcomes as measured by the modified NSS scores at 24 hours after MCAO ischemic onset. At the dosage of 20 mg/kg, SDSS treatment significantly decreased the activation of MMP-9 in the ischemic brains as determined by the gelatin zymography assay. Therefore, SDSS treatment could protect the integrity of the BBB and improve neurological outcomes in ischemic stroke. Interestingly, we found that hyperglycemia could abolish the neuroprotective effects of SDSS in an acute ischemic stroke rat model. We found that hyperglycemia aggravated the production of peroxynitrite in the ischemic rat brains. Although SDSS at the dosage of 20 mg/kg originally showed strong bioactivity of scavenging ONOO- in the ischemic stroke rats under normal glucose level, the scavenging effects of SDSS on scavenging ONOO- were abolished by hyperglycemia. Furthermore, SDSS at the dosages of 20, 40 mg/kg had no effect on both hemorrhagic transformation and infarct volume in the MCAO ischemic brain with hyperglycemia. The expression of tPA and PAI-1 and activity of MMPs were similar. Under the ischemic stroke with normal glucose, SDSS (20 mg/kg) effectively prevented the increased expression of t-PA and PAI-1 and inhibited the activity of MMP-9. However, with hyperglycemia, SDSS treatment has no effect on the expression of t-PA, PAI-1, and MMP-9 in the ischemic brains. In conclusion, SDSS treatment could protect the integrity of the BBB and improve neurological outcomes in ischemic stroke via scavenging peroxynitrite and inhibiting MMP activation. However, hyperglycemia could abolish the neuroprotective effects on SDSS, which is inconsistent with our expectation in our original proposal. In addition, We found that several active compounds from medicinal plants including rehmapicroside, glycrrhizin, naringin, and Astragali Radix isoflavones are promising drug candidates for scavenging or inhibiting peroxynitrite and have neuroprotective effects against cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury. Therefore, we have achieved the research goals.

17118717.label: Major findings and research outcome
17118717.value: 1. Hyperglycemia aggravates peroxynitrite (ONOO-) production, contributing to the BBB disruption, HT, and neurological outcome in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury. The major discoveries include: (1) Acute hyperglycemia significantly induced the production of peroxynitrite in the ischemic cortex and striatum; (2) Acute hyperglycemia increased the expression of NADPH oxidase subunits p47 phox and p67 phox and the iNOS expression in the ischemic brains, subsequently mediating peroxynitrite production. (3) As a representative peroxynitrite decomposition catalyst (PDC), FeTmPyP treatment at a dosage of 3 mg/kg (i.v.) significantly decreased hemorrhagic transformation (HT) in the ischemic brains, and uric acid treatment at a dosage of 16 mg/kg in Locke’s buffer also significantly decreased the hemorrhagic transformation and improved the neurological outcomes. The work has been published in Free Radical Biology and Medicine (Chen HS et al. Free Rad Biol Med 2021 Mar;165:171-183.); (3) Our clinical investigation found that plasma 3-NT level was positively correlated with blood glucose level in acute ischemic stroke patients within 72 hours of ischemic onset. The work has been published in Translational Stroke Research (Chen HS, et al. Translat Stroke Res 2020 Oct;11(5):967-982.) 2. Peroxynitrite is important for the MMPs activation in ischemic stroke with acute hyperglycemia. (1) Acute hyperglycemia significantly increased the expression of PAI-1 and t-PA in the ischemic brain, as well as the expression and activity of MMP-9 and the expression of MMP-2/3 in the ischemic brains; (2) FeTmPyP treatment significantly decreased the expression and activity of MMP-9, and inhibited the expression of MMP-2/3 in the ischemic brains with acute hyperglycemia . The work has been also published in Free Radical Biology and Medicine (Chen HS, et al. Free Rad Biol Med 2021 Mar;165:171-183.) 3. SDSS treatment (20 mg/kg) has a protective effect on the ischemic brains in an experimental ischemic stroke rat model with normal blood glucose level, whose effects were abolished in the MCAO ischemic rats with acute hyperglycemia. The results showed that (1) SDSS treatment remarkably reduced infarct volume and BBB disruption and improved neurological outcome in the MCAO ischemic rats; (2) SDSS treatment significantly decreased the expression of t-PA and PAI-1 and inhibited the activity of MMP-9 in the ischemic brain tissue; (3) SDSS treatment downregulated the expressions of apoptosis-related proteins including PARP1, cleaved-caspase 3, Bcl 2 and Bax; (4) SDSS treatments (20, 40 mg/kg wt.) has no effect on hemorrhagic transformation and infarct volume in the experimental ischemic stroke rat model with acute hyperglycemia; (5) Although SDSS (20 mg/kg wt.) originally showed strong bioactivity of scavenging ONOO- in the ischemic rat brains with normal blood glucose level, the ONOO- scavenging effects were abolished in the ischemic rat brains with acute hyperglycemia. The expressions of tPA and PAI-1, the activity of MMPs, and the expressions of apoptosis-related proteins showed similar responses.

17118717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17118717.value: Based on the achievement of our studies, we expect the following potential directions for further studies: (1) Using peroxynitrite as a molecular target for drug discovery to prevent hemorrhagic transformation (HT) and improve therapeutic outcome in the treatment of ischemic stroke with acute hyperglycemia, as well as extension of the therapeutic window of tPA and reducing the risk of HT in the treatment of ischemic stroke. (2) Given that SDSS is one of the major active compounds in the medicinal plant Danshen, the results could be useful to guide the application of Danshen in ischemic stroke with or without hyperglycemia or diabetics. Further investigation would benefit for the medical application of Danshen in ischemic stroke treatment in TCM practices. It is desirable to explore the underlying mechanisms why the neuroprotective effects of SDSS are lost in ischemic stroke with hyperglycemia. Our study impacts on guiding the applications of SDSS and its original medicinal herb Danshen in ischemia stroke patients, especially for patients with acute hyperglycemia. We will seek funds from RGC GRF grants or other funding sources to continue our studies in this direction.

17118717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17118717.value: Hyperglycemia arises in 30-40% of the patients with acute ischemic stroke with or without pre-existing diabetes. Hyperglycemia is positively correlated with severe brain injury, hemorrhage transformation (HT), poor functional outcomes, and high mortality. However, there is a knowledge gap about how hyperglycemia mediates hemorrhagic transformation and worsens neurological outcomes. With the support of RGC GRF grant, we conducted a series of experiments to test our hypothesis that peroxynitrite could play a critical role in mediating HT and worsen neurological outcomes in ischemic stroke with hyperglycemia. We demonstrate that hyperglycemia aggravates peroxynitrite (ONOO-) production, contributing to the BBB disruption, HT, and neurological outcome in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury. After exploring the underlying mechanisms, we demonstrate that peroxynitrite could be an important pathological factor and therapeutic target in ischemic stroke with acute hyperglycemia. Targeting peroxynitrite could be an important strategy for drug discovery to reduce hemorrhagic transformation, increase survival rates and improve neurological outcomes in ischemic stroke with hyperglycemia. Sodium Dansensu (SDSS) is an active compound from Danshen, a commonly used medicinal herb for ischemic stroke treatment in Chinese Medicine practice. SDSS has neuroprotective effects against cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury via scavenging peroxynitrite in ischemic stroke under normal blood glucose. However, acute hyperglycemia remarkably reduces the neuroprotective effects of Dansensu on ischemic brains. Those results bring caution of using Danshen in ischemic stroke patients with acute hyperglycemia or diabetics. Further studies are needed to guide the clinical application of Danshen and its active compound SDSS. This project yields 8 original articles and 4 review articles published in prestigious international academic journals and trained 3 postgraduate students.

17118917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17118917.value: 連接母體和胎兒的胎盤在整個懷孕期間提供足夠的血液灌注。該過程是通過稱為絨毛外滋養層的胎盤細胞侵入蛻膜並將螺旋動脈重塑成低阻力和高流動血管完成的。 該過程中的失調導致稱為先兆子癇的疾病。 巨噬細胞是螺旋動脈外膜中最豐富的免疫細胞群體。在懷孕早期，骨髓中的單核細胞遷移到蛻膜的子宮內膜中，於局部微環境中分化為蛻膜特異性巨噬細胞。蛻膜巨噬細胞通過確保適當的螺旋動脈重塑和對半同種異體胎兒的免疫耐受，幫助懷孕成功。蛻膜巨噬細胞的異常水平與先兆子癇和胎兒流產相關聯。儘管蛻膜巨噬細胞在懷孕中是重要的，但調節其分化的因素尚不清楚。 細胞外囊泡是由細胞釋放的亞微米尺寸的脂質容器，它在細胞通信中起關鍵作用。細胞外囊泡通過允許生物分子的轉運調節多種生物現象。正常懷孕伴隨著母體循環中胎盤來源的細胞外囊泡（pEV）數量的增加。pEV上一種名為siglec-6的人類胎盤特有的聚醣結合蛋白的異常表達與先兆子癇相關。 我們的數據顯示，在macrophage colony-stimulating factor誘導的單核細胞分化期間添加了pEV所得的巨噬細胞增加了蛻膜巨噬細胞標記indoleamine-2,3-dioxygenase-1和neuropilin-1的表達。所得的巨噬細胞也具有較高interleukin-6的表達和較低C-X-C motif chemokine 10的表達，分別有助於滋養細胞侵襲和內皮細胞血管發生。pEV對單核細胞的結合和活性由siglec-6調節。 我們假設pEV通過siglec-6與單核細胞相互作用，使單核細胞分化為蛻膜巨噬細胞，從而幫助將母細胞界面上的螺旋動脈重塑和調節對胎兒抗原的免疫耐受。該假說將通過研究pEV在調節蛻膜巨噬細胞分化和功能中的作用，並調查siglec-6對pEV的結合和對蛻膜巨噬細胞分化的機制來測試。 該項目的成果將促進我們在分化和蛻膜巨噬細胞的功能的理解。長遠來看，本研究的結果將表明使用pEV上的siglec-6表達作為早期預測先兆子癇的試驗，和表明siglec-6脂質體作為特定藥物遞送劑治療胎盤相關並發症的的可能性。

17118917.label: Realisation of objectives
17118917.value: The maternal immune system is altered during pregnancy to tolerate the semi-allogeneic fetus. The alterations occur locally at the maternal-fetal interface. Failure to induce immune tolerance to paternal antigens may result in pregnancy complications, such as recurrent pregnancy loss and pre-eclampsia. Macrophages are the most abundant immune cell population in the spiral artery adventitia, and comprise approximately 20% of the immune cells in the pregnant uterus. Monocytes from bone marrow migrate into the decidualized endometrium, exposure to the local microenvironment, and differentiate into decidua-specific macrophages. Decidual macrophages help to establish a successful pregnancy by ensuring proper placenta development and conferring immune tolerance to the semi-allogenic fetus. They contribute to immunotolerance towards fetal antigens and regulate spiral arteries remodeling by trophoblast. Despite the importance of decidual macrophages in pregnancy, the factors regulating their differentiation remain unclear. Placenta extracellular versicle (pEV) are inter-cellular signal carriers which modulate a wide range of biological phenomena in an autocrine and paracrine manner. pEV cargoes (i.e. lipids, miRNAs, proteins) can exert biological actions in recipient cells upon internalization of exosomes. During pregnancy, pEV are shed from the syncytiotrophoblast into the circulation and their concentration in maternal blood increased as pregnancy proceeds. However, their biological role in pregnancy is poorly understood. In this project, the roles of pEV in mediating decidual macrophage differentiation and functions were studied. Objective 1. To study the role of placenta-derived extracellular vesicle (pEV) in polarizing decidual macrophage differentiation Human first-trimester placenta was obtained with written consent from women undergoing surgical abortion. Placental explant was cultured in medium containing 10% vesicle-free fetal bovine serum in 2% O2 hypoxic condition to simulate the oxygen tension of the 1st-trimester placenta. The conditioned medium was collected for pEV isolation by differential ultra-centrifugation. Peripheral blood CD14+ monocyte cells, the tissue-specific macrophage cells precursors, were isolated by CD14 MicroBeads. Monocytes were differentiated into macrophages by culturing with MCSF (50 ng/mL) with/without pEV (10 μg total protein/mL) for 8 days. Decidual macrophage (dM) cells were isolated from first-trimester termination of pregnancy tissues. Our data suggested that pEV-polarized macrophage has a higher expression of CD163, IDO-1 and neuropilin-1 (NRP-1), when compared to the control. Control and pEV-polarized macrophages were cultured in serum-free medium for 24 hours. The spent culture media were semi-quantitatively analyzed by the human cytokine antibody array and ELISA. pEV-polarized macrophage had increased secretion of IL-10 and IL-6, similar to decidual macrophages. In addition, pEV treatment did not affect the total cell number and viability of the macrophages. To further assess whether pEV affected macrophage differentiation, CD14+ blood monocytes were differentiated into macrophages with or without pEV and submitted for mRNA-seq analysis. Our data demonstrated that M2 macrophage markers (CCL1, CCL2, CCL23, CCL24, CCR2, CHI3L2, CXCL13, CD163, SOCS3, SLAMF1) were increased in the pEV-polarized macrophages when compared to the control macrophages. Consistently, GSEA revealed that the pEV-polarized macrophages resembled the M2a macrophages. The bioinformatics observation was confirmed by RT-PCR analysis of the M2 macrophage marker genes (CD163, CD206, CD209, IL10, IDO-1, CCL2, CCL8) in the treatment group. Taken together, our data indicated that the pEV promoted M2 macrophage differentiation of blood monocytes. Objective 2. To study the role of pEV on decidual macrophage-mediated functions The vascular remodeling activity of trophoblast was determined by the ability of the trophoblast to migrate/invade and then integrate towards the endothelial cells network. Spent medium derived from pEV-polarized macrophage-induced invasion of primary extravillous trophoblast and JEG-3 cells. The medium did not affect the migration of the trophoblast. On the other hand, pEV-polarized macrophage conditioned medium induced endothelial cell angiogenesis. Such effect was abolished by the addition of the anti-angiogenic chemokine CXCL-10, which is highly expressed in the serum of preeclamptic patients. The effect of pEV-polarized macrophage on T cell proliferation and Treg differentiation were examined. Using autologous monocytes which did not influence T cell proliferation, the inclusion of pEV reduced the proliferation of CD3+CD4+ and CD3+CD8+ T cells in comparison to the untreated control. pEV treatment did not affect viability and apoptosis of the CD3+CD4+ and CD3+CD8+ T cells. Consistently, cytokine profiling showed decreases of cytotoxic cytokines, IFN-γ and TNF-α concentrations in the conditioned medium from co-culture with pEV when compared to the control. Direct co-culture with, but not the spent medium of, pEV-polarized macrophage decreased the CD3+CD4+ or CD3+CD8+ T cell proliferation in the absence of pEV. Together, the data indicated that the pEV-induced suppression of T cell proliferation required direct T cell-monocyte contact. The numbers of systemic CD4+CD25+FoxP3+ regulatory T cells (Tregs) increase during the first and second trimester of pregnancy. Our data showed that the frequency of CD4+CD25+FoxP3+ Tregs was doubled when the cells were co-cultured with pEV polarized macrophage. On the other hand, pEV-polarized macrophage has similar phagocytotic activity as the control macrophage. Objective 3. To investigate the siglec-6 mediated binding of pEV and the mechanism for pEV-mediated decidual macrophage differentiation Our data indicate that pEV has a strong siglec-6 protein expression. Anti-siglec-6 antibody inhibits pEV binding to monocytes and IDO-1 expression of the resulting pEV-polarized macrophages. We have also shown miRNAs were the major component of the small RNA population in pEV. miRNA-seq revealed more than 1000 mature miRNAs exist in the pEV. The top 9 miRNAs were selected for validation based on a high read count and literature review. Transfection of miR10a-5p, miR10b-5p, miR22-3p and miR29a-3p enhanced the programmed cell death ligand-1 (PD-L1) expression, a well-known surface receptor that suppresses the adaptive immune system. TargetScan 7.2 identified Phosphatase and tensin homolog (PTEN) as a target gene of miR10-5p, miR22-3p and miR29a-3p. PTEN is involved in suppressing PD-L1 expression in different cell types. We further confirm the suppressive action of miRNA-29a-3p on PTEN expression in monocytes. In addition, miR-99a-5p and miR-148a-3p also suppressed the expression PTEN though they were not predicted by TargetScan 7.2. Most importantly, we confirm the up-regulation of PDL-1 and PTEN in monocyte/macrophage isolated from pregnant women. Together, our findings suggested that pEV miRNA-29a-3p increased PD-L1 expression by down-regulating PTEN. On the other hand, the expression of miR-148a-3p was highest among these angiogenesis-related miRNAs. To study the potential effect of this miRNA on uterine spiral artery remodeling, miR-148a-3p was overexpressed in human umbilical vein endothelial cells. After transfection, endothelial cell tube formation was impaired compared with the control group. The miRNA-148a-3p target FLT1 and RTN4 were greatly downregulated after transfection, the downregulated of these angiogenesis-related molecules indicating its potential role in endothelial functions.

17118917.value: - pEV and decidual macrophage play a key role in the establishment of maternal immune tolerance, which is critical for a successful pregnancy. (Bai et al., 2021; Vijayan et al., 2020; Xia et al., 2020). - pEV enhanced the differentiation of monocyte into decidual (CD163, IDO-1 and NRP-1) and M2 (CCL1, CCL2, CCL23, CCL24, CCR2, CHI3L2, CXCL13, CD163, SOCS3 and SLAMF1) macrophage phenotype. (Bai et al., 2021, under review) - Compared to control macrophage, pEV-polarized macrophage cells regulate the vascular remodeling activity of trophoblast and angiogenic activities of endothelial cell. (Bai et al., 2021, under review) - pEV-polarized macrophage mediate maternal immune tolerance of T-cell. Direct co-culture with pEV-polarized macrophage decreased the number of CD3+CD4+ or CD3+CD8+ T cell proliferation, and increase the number of CD4+CD25+FoxP3+ Tregs. Consistently, cytokine profiling showed decreases of cytotoxic cytokines such as IFN-γ and TNF-α. (Bai et al., 2021, under review) - pEV trigger its biological activities on monocyte/macrophage via the regulation of miRNA-29a-3p-PTEN-PDL-1 and miR-148a-3p. 17118917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17118917.value: There are two important areas for further development: 1. Based on the important role of siglec-6 in regulating pEV activities during early pregnancy, it is reasonable to speculate that deficiency in the normal functions of siglec-6 on pEV may contribute to the pathophysiology of various pregnancy-associated diseases. We have submitted a grant application (HMRF 09202056, recommended for support) to determine the expression of siglec-6 in the pEV in early maternal serum from women who suffer from preeclampsia at term pregnancy. We aim to measure the serum levels of siglec-6 on pEVs from pregnant women at different gestational ages, to determine the expression level and characteristics of siglec-6 on pEV in maternal blood from women who develop PE at term pregnancy, and to further study the role of siglec-6 on pEVs in the vascular remodeling of trophoblasts. 2. pEV binding to siglec-6 on monocyte and macrophage via carbohydrate recognition. Removal of sialic acid, the outmost sugar residue of the glycan chain, has lost the binding and thus the pEV-mediated biological functions on monocyte/macrophage. Further study of monocyte/macrophage with sialic acid knockout (Sialidase) is required to define the mechanistic aspects of these glycans.

17118917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17118917.value: The placenta is a transient organ essential of providing adequate blood perfusion throughout pregnancy. It is accomplished by a placental cell termed trophoblast that invades the decidua and remodels the spiral arteries into low-resistance and high-flow vessels. Macrophages are the most abundant immune cell population in the spiral artery adventitia. In early pregnancy, the monocytes from bone marrow migrate into the decidualized endometrium and differentiate into decidua-specific macrophages. Decidual macrophages help to establish a successful pregnancy by ensuring proper spiral arteries remodeling and conferring immune tolerance to the semi-allogenic fetus. Aberrant spiral artery remodeling and decidual macrophages are associated with fetal loss and pregnancy complications. Placenta extracellular vesicles are submicron-sized lipid containers released by the placenta which play a crucial role in cell-cell communication. It polarizes the differentiation of monocytes into decidual macrophages, which subsequently regulates the vascular remodeling activity of trophoblasts, angiogenic activities of endothelial cells, and maternal immunotolerance of T-cells. In sum, this project enhances our understanding of the differentiation and functions of decidual macrophages. In a longer-term, the result of this study will indicate the possible use of siglec-6 expression on pEV as a test for early prediction of preeclampsia.

17119117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17119117.value: About 1 out of 6 couples of reproductive age have fertility problem. In vitro fertilization and embryo transfer is an effective treatment of infertility. In the treatment, embryos are cultured before they are transferred back to patients. However, our culture system is suboptimal, resulting in only about half of the embryos can be cultured to blastocyst stage when the embryo is ready for implantation. The low rate of development to blastocyst is partly due to our deficiency in understanding the physiology of blastocyst development. A sperm fertilizes an oocyte to form a zygote, which cleaves to a multicellular embryo. In the first few cell divisions, the developmental potential of all cells of an embryo are similar. At late morula stage, the cells undergo differentiation. The first cell differentiation occurs at the blastocyst stage with the formation of two types of cells, namely trophectoderm cells and inner cell mass cells. The former enclose the latter in the blastocysts. How these differentiation processes are regulated is not fully clear. MicroRNA is a class of small ribonucleic acids (RNA). They do not produce proteins. Instead, they inhibit expression of their target proteins. One of the microRNA families is lethal-7 (let-7), which is well-known for its actions on cell differentiation. Cell differentiation in preimplantation embryos is associated with expression of cell type specific markers. One the trophectoderm specific markers is caudal type homeobox 2 (Cdx2). In mouse, three signaling pathways in embryos have been reported to regulate the expression of Cdx2. Bioinformatic analyses and our preliminary observation suggest that let-7 acts on key molecules of these pathways, and thus may affect cell specification of embryos. Our unpublished data show that perturbation of let-7 level in early mouse embryos affects their subsequent development to blastocysts. Interestingly, when undifferentiated embryonic cells are forced to produce more let-7, they tend to form the inner cell mass cells of the resulting blastocysts. Therefore, this project hypothesize that let-7 modulates the essential signaling pathways to regulate cell differentiation in early embryos. The present study addresses our knowledge gap on regulation of early embryo development. The results also have potential clinical implications. They may be used to explain causes of failure of blastocyst formation in some IVF cases. Aberrant expression of let-7 has been reported in blastocysts of infertile couples. In the long term, the outcome could provide the scientific rationale for enhancement of blastocyst formation via manipulation of let-7 expression. 約6對生育年齡的夫婦中有1對有生育問題。 體外受精和胚胎移植是不育的有效治療方法。 在治療中，胚胎在體外培養後移植回患者。 然而，我們的培養系統不是最佳的，只有大約一半的胚胎可以培養成植入前的囊胚階段。 囊胚發育率低的部分原因是我們對於囊胚發育的生理學的認知不足。 精子使卵母細胞受精以形成合子，其發育成多細胞胚胎。 在最初的幾個細胞分裂中，胚胎的所有細胞的發育潛力是相似的。 在桑椹胚晚期，細胞進行分化。 第一細胞分化發生在囊胚階段，形成兩種類型的細胞，即滋養外胚層細胞和內細胞團細胞。在囊胚中，前者包圍後者。 這些分化過程如何受到監管並不完全清楚。 微RNA是一類小核糖核酸（RNA）。 它們不產生蛋白質。 相反，它們抑制其靶蛋白的表達。 其中一個微RNA家族是let-7，這家族對細胞分化的作用是眾所周知的。 植入前胚胎中的細胞分化與細胞類型特異性標誌物的表達相關。 一種滋養外胚層特異性標記是尾狀型同源異型2（Cdx2）。 在小鼠中，已經報導了胚胎中的三種信號通路調節Cdx2的表達。 生物信息學分析和我們的初步觀察表明，let-7作用於這些通路的關鍵分子，從而可能影響胚胎的細胞類型規範。 我們未發表的數據顯示，早期小鼠胚胎中let-7水平的干擾影響其隨後的囊胚發育。 有趣的是，當未分化的胚胎細胞被迫產生更多的let-7時，它們傾向在所產生的囊胚形成內細胞團細胞。 因此，這項目假設let-7調節基因信號通路以調節早期胚胎細胞的分化。 本研究縮短了我們在早期胚胎發育調控方面的知識差距。 結果也有潛在的臨床意義； 它們可用於解釋某些不育治療病例中囊胚形成失敗的原因。研究也報導了部份不育夫婦的囊胚有異常的let-7表達。 從長遠的角度來看，結果可以作為通過詷控let-7表達來增強囊胚形成的科學依據。

17119117.label: Realisation of objectives
17119117.value: After fertilization, the zygote develops into a cleavage-stage embryo. Morphologically distinguishable change of the blastomere occurs at the morula stage, when the cells on the outside (outer cells) of the embryo become flattened, polarized and enclose the apolar inside cells (inner cells). These changes lead to the differentiation of trophectoderm (TE) and inner cell mass cells (ICM) of blastocyst, resepctively. The aim of the project is to study the action of microRNA let-7 (lethal-7) in regulation of blastocyst formation and function in mice. There are three objectives in this project to study the action, the downstream and upstream regulators of let-7 in the mouse preimplantation embryos. The COVID-19 pandemic slowed down the progress of the project in the past 2 years. Nevertheless, all the objectives were addressed and achieved. Objective 1: To investigate the actions of let-7 on TE and ICM fate in mouse embryos. A. Spatial expression of let-7 isoforms in pre-implantation embryos Two approaches were used. First, we determined the let-7 isoforms in embryos at different developmental stages using the 238-plex miRNA assay and validated by qRT-PCR. To compare the expression of let-7 in ICM and TE, immunosurgery and microdissection were used to isolate the ICM and the TE, respectively before their expression of let-7 isoforms was determined. The original plan of the second approach was to determine spatial expression of let-7 in embryos from a mouse line carrying a mRNA version of a published let-7-GFP (green fluorescent protein) reporter. Unfortunately, the reporter did not work in mouse embryos. We eventually generated a let-7-tdTomato fluorescent protein reporter that could be expressed in mouse embryos. The reporter has 5 tandem repeats of a sequence perfectly complementary to the seed region of let-7 isoforms to enable high binding efficiency and specificity to let-7. The mouse line with the reporter was mated to another mouse line constitutively expressing GFP. The signal ratio of the tdTomato to GFP was used to semi-quantify the expression of let-7 in the mouse preimplantation embryos. The mice were kept in Shenzhen and the experiment was done at the University of Hong Kong-Shenzhen Hospital to avoid the difficulties in sending the mice to Hong Kong during the COVID-19 pandemic. B. Determination of the most sensitive period for the action of let-7 We force expressed let-7 in preimplantation embryos by microinjection of precursor let-7a (pre-let-7a) at the zygotic and the 2-cell stage and electroporation of pre-let-7a or let-7a inhibitor at the 4-cell and the 8-cell stage. Microinjection was used with the 2-cell embryos because these early embryos were very sensitive to electroporation, which damaged the embryos and induced blastomere fusion in a significant portion of the treated embryos. C. Effects of let-7 isoforms on blastulation Precursors of let-7 isoforms (let-7a, -7b, -7f and -7g) were electroporated at the 4-cell stage. Their effects on blastulation were compared. We determined the actions of let-7a and let-7g on expression of Oct4, Cdx2, and 14 other genes differentially expressed between diapausing and activated blastocysts, and on embryo implantation, attachment and outgrowth. D. Contribution of let-7 to ICM and TE formation Two approaches were used. First, we microinjected pre-let-7a and GFP mRNA (lineage tracer) into one blastomere of 2-cell embryos to force express let-7 and GFP. The development of the GFP+ cells in blastocysts was determined. Second, we generated mice carrying a doxycycline inducible chimeric let-7g stem/miR21 loop fusion gene. The embryos from the transgenic mice produce let-7g when exposed to doxycycline. We microinjected one blastomere from a 2-cell embryo of the transgenic mice with GFP mRNA and used it to produce a chimeric embryo by aggregation with another blastomere from a wildtype 2-cell embryo. The chimeric embryos were then cultured with or without doxycycline. The developmental fate of the GFP+ cells in blastocysts was monitored. Objective 2: To study the actions of let-7 on molecules important for blastulation and cell fate A. Actions of let-7 on hippo, Ras-MAPK and notch signaling in blastocyst formation We studied the action of let-7 on its potential targets namely tead4, Hras and Rbpj in the 3 signaling pathways. We studied the effect of perturbation of let-7a expression by transfection of pre-let-7a or let-7a inhibitor on the mRNA and protein expression of these molecules in mouse trophoblast stem cells (TS) or human trophoblast cells (Jeg-3). Luciferase reporter assays were used to confirm the binding of let-7a to the 3’UTR of the genes. The functional roles of these molecules were determined by co-electroporation of pre-let-7a and Tead4, Hras or Rbpj T7 mRNA vector into 4-cell embryos, and determination of their actions on nullification of the action of let-7 on blastulation and Cdx2/Oct4 expression in the treated embryos B. Differences in let-7 expression levels among blastomeres affect cell specification We produced the doxycycline inducible lin28b mice. Lin28b is natural negative inhibitor of let-7. We generated 2-cell chimeric embryos having different combination of blastomeres from embryos with inducible lin28b, inducible let-7g or WT mice and cultured them in the presence of doxycycline to create differences in let-7 expression among blastomeres. The contribution of the blastomeres to the ICM was determined. Objective 3: To study the regulatory factors of let-7 expression in mouse embryos. A. Role of lin28b The expression let-7 in and development of blastocyst of the doxycycline inducible lin28b transgenic mice as well as their implantation potential were determined in the presence and absence of doxycycline. The role of lin28b in ICM/TE cell fate development was determined by generating chimeric 2-cell embryo from the transgenic mice and the wildtype mice. The blastomere of the transgenic mice was labelled with Qtracker as lineage tracer. B. Feedback regulation of let-7 in mouse preimplantation embryos Nf2-Amot-Yap1 works with Tead4 in determining the TE cell fate, and cell-cell contact induces dephosphorylation of NF2-Amot, which sequesters cytoplasmic Lin28B and allows maturation of pri-let-7. Here, we confirmed that Nf2 and Amot were let-7 targets by determining their expression in the Jeg-3 cells after let-7 forced expression, and binding of their 3’UTR to let-7 by the luciferase reporter assay in the Jeg-3 cells. The relationship of let-7/lin28b and Nf2 was determined by gain-of and loss-of-function approach. C. Exogenous let-7 Mouse and human endometria produce extracellular vesicles (EVs) containing miRNAs. We determined the miRNA content in the mouse estrus cycles. Transfer of let-7 from EVs to embryos in mice was determined by (1) comparing the expression patterns of let-7 in endometrial cells, EVs from uterine lumen fluid (ULF) and intrauterine blastocysts in the delayed implantation model; (2) transfer of WT embryos to foster mother carrying inducible let-7g transgene and quantification of the transgene in the transferred wildtype embryos; (3) incubation of embryos with EVs enriched with let-7 and determination of expression of let-7 target in the treated embryos. The effect of the up-taken let-7 on mouse blastocyst implantation and differentiation of TE/trophoblast in a human blastocyst surrogate model, BAP-EB was determined by coculture of blastocysts or BAP-EB with let-7-containing EVs. The effects of estradiol (E2) and progesterone (P4) in regulation of let-7 production in endometrial EVs were determined.

17119117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17119117.value: An unexpected observation is the preferential development to the ICM with forced expression of let-7 in blastomere of 2-cell embryos. The time when lineage fate of blastomere is fixed is not fully known, though the blastomere of 2-cell embryos with higher LincGET expression contributes more to the ICM. The possible early cell fate commitment is supported by differences in mRNA profile and number of nuclear CARM1 speckles of the individual blatomeres of 2-cell embryos. The mechanism of action of let-7 on early cell fate commitment is a fundamental embryology question worth investigation. Asynchronous development between the embryo and the endometrial window of implantation causes infertility. Displayed endometrial window of implantation have been reported. The ability of endometrial let-7-enriched EVs to delay trophoblast differentiation in the human BAP-EB model suggest a new mechanism for asynchronization of the embryo and endometrium development. Should the dysregulated endometrium produce EVs with inappropriate amount of let-7 and other miRNAs, the development of the embryos could be reduced or accelerated, and thus could not match with that of the endometrial window of implantation. Further research to elucidate the microRNA composition in EVs of human endometrium and embryos, and their actions on embryo development and implantation are warranted.

17119117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17119117.value: About 1/6 couples of reproductive age have fertility problem. Assisted reproduction is an effective treatment of infertility. Due to our inadequate knowledge on development of preimplantation embryos, the culture system in the treatment is suboptimal, resulting in low percentage of the cultured embryos reaching the blastocyst stage when the embryo should implant. This study determined the actions of microRNA let-7 on development of mouse blastocysts aiming to bridge our knowledge gap on regulation of early embryo development. The study shows that perturbation of the embryonic let-7 levels from the zygote to the 8-cell stage affects embryo development to blastocysts. The Hippo, MAPK and Notch signaling mediate the actions of let-7 on blastocyst formation. Interestingly, when one cell of 2-cell embryos is forced to produce more let-7, the cells tends to form the inner cell mass cells of the resulting blastocyst. In addition, endometrial-derived let-7 can be transferred to embryos affecting the development and implantation of blastocysts. In summary, let-7 modulates cell differentiation and implantation of blastocysts. The results may be used to explain the cause of failure of blastocyst formation and implantation in some IVF cases. The outcome suggests that manipulation of let-7 expression may enhance blastocyst formation.

17119917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17119917.value: 當專業牙齒清潔後或者修復材料暴露於口腔環境，一旦和唾液接觸，就會即刻被唾液覆蓋形成一層唾液薄膜，稱為獲得性唾液膜，是牙齒和修復體表面選擇性吸附唾液成分的結果。這層唾液膜在牙齒和其周圍口腔環境之間提供了一層物理和化學的中界面，但與此同時提供口腔菌斑先鋒細菌粘結點，其他細菌隨之接合而形成牙菌斑。這種牙齒表面微生態的凝聚，如果沒有干擾，便有機會形成致病菌群，而導致齲病或牙周病。 牙科修復材料用於填補牙齒齲損後缺失的的牙齒結構。理想的修復材料應具備永久粘接（或者完美/無瑕疵的邊緣）於剩餘牙體組織，同時具備和剩餘牙體組織類似的機械以及視覺的性能。此外，修復材料應該具有抵抗在口腔環境中降解的能力，和在牙齒修復體界面抗齲能力。更甚者，修復材料應能夠強化牙周軟，硬組織的抗齲/牙齦疾病的能力。 然而，牙齒修復體和種植體表面為非剝脫性表面，利於致病菌斑的聚集，致病菌斑已被證實可導致多種慢性感染，例如繼發齲和牙齦炎，前者為牙體修復治療的主要原因，同時也是牙醫和患者的主要挑戰。上述事實推動了近期對細菌和材料相互作用，包括生物膜形成方面的調查研究，然而，細菌於牙體表面附著的機制至今尚未被完全理解。 牙釉質表面上獲得的薄膜的大分子組成已經通過使用不同的分析方法來闡明，如石英晶體微量天平（QCM）和液相色譜 - 串聯質譜（LC-MS / MS）。以前的研究表明釉質薄膜肽和附著菌群之間有多種相關性，但是對於牙齒修復體上的唾液膜的組成及其對細菌粘附的功能的理解仍未完善。因此，我們的實驗目的是確定吸附在各種修復材料表面上的蛋白質，並發掘其相應的微生物組，以便進一步了解/理解相應的的初始細菌附著/粘附。 潛在的成果和好處： 為了研究和驗證唾液蛋白與細菌黏附之間可能的相關性，此項實驗會應用先進的實驗方法和分析來研究唾液膜的組成成分，並將其結果應用於相關的微生物學研究。此項分析將在易發齲和 無齲人士（根據其過去的齲齒經驗定義）中進行。該實驗所獲得的知識可為從業人員提供進一步的關於牙科修復材料相關微生物/生物學理解，這可能有助於臨床嘗試預防/減少牙菌斑形成，並希望可以幫助牙醫和患者的減少牙患。這項研究也將為新的修復材料開發提供可能是靶向關鍵的生物膜形成唾液蛋白吸附的信息，並預防/減弱/停止疾病如二次齲齒。
