17120217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17120217.value: Background: Untreated dental caries in the primary teeth is common among the young children in Hong Kong and in many places around the world. Effective caries treatment methods that are at low cost and efficient, and can reach out to preschool children in the community are urgently needed. New non-invasive treatments would be preferred. Objectives: The main objective of this clinical trial is to compare the clinical outcomes over a 24-month period of using atraumatic restorative treatment (ART) restorations and those of semi-annual application of silver diamine fluoride (SDF) solution in treating decayed primary teeth. The cost of using these two treatments will be compared, as well as their impacts on the children’s oral health-related quality of life. Parents’ acceptance of the treatment outcomes will also be assessed. Methods: This proposed study is a randomized clinical trial using a parallel group design. A total of around 480 children with anticipated 1,440 decayed teeth will be recruited from kindergartens in Hong Kong. They will be randomly assigned to two groups to receive either placement of ART restorations or semi-annual application of SDF solution as treatment for their decayed primary teeth. This sample size is sufficient for statistical analysis of non-inferiority of the non-restorative approach (SDF application) compared to ART restoration with a non-inferiority margin set at 10% and power set at 90%. The clinical outcomes of the treatments will be assessed in clinical examinations carried out every 6 months. Treatment success is defined as no active caries, no pain and the treated tooth being vital. A successful ART restoration also needs to be retained and without major defects. The time and material cost of each of the two types of treatment will be recorded and the mean per treated tooth will be calculated. Information about the children’s oral hygiene and dietary habits and oral health related quality of life (OHQoL) will be collected at baseline and after 24 months through the use of a parental questionnaire and a validated OHQoL measurement tool. Impacts: Findings of this randomized trial will provide high level clinical evidence for dentists and dental programme planners. It is anticipated that the clinical success rate of SDF solution application is not lower than that of placing restoration and the use of this cheaper, simpler and more efficient non-restorative approach can greatly reduce the burden of treating dental caries in young child populations in Hong Kong and worldwide. 背景：未治療的蛀牙在香港和世界許多地方的幼兒中很常見。有迫切需要應用低成本高效的方法，在社區為學齡前兒童治療蛀牙。 新的非侵入性治療將是優先的選擇。 目的：本臨床研究的主要目的是比較使用非創傷性修復治療或以半年一次塗上氟化氨銀溶液來治療幼兒成洞蛀牙的24個月效果。另外，研究將比較使用這兩種治療方法的成本及它們對兒童口腔健康相關生活質量的影響，也會評估父母對治療結果的接受程度。 方法：本隨機臨床研究使用平行組的設計。從香港的幼稚園共招募約480名兒童，預期有4400顆蛀牙。他們將隨機分配到兩組，以接受非創傷性修復治療或半年一次塗上氟化氨銀溶液來治療他們的成洞蛀牙。該樣本量足以對這 兩種治療方法的非劣效性進行統計分析，而非劣效率差距設置為10％，功率設置為90％。治療的臨床結果將在每6個月進行的臨床檢查中評估。治療成功定義為無活躍的蛀壞，無疼痛，而治療牙齒還活著。非創傷性修復的充填體也需要保留在牙齒上，沒有重大缺陷。研究將記錄使用每一種治療所需的時間和材料成本，以計算平均每顆蛀牙的治療成本。另外將通過使用家長問卷和經過驗證的測量工具，在基線和24個月後收集有關兒童的口腔衛生和飲食習慣，和他們口腔健康相關生活質量的數據。 影響：本隨機臨床研究的結果將為牙醫和牙科項目規劃者提供高水平的臨床證據。預計應用氟化氨銀溶液的臨床成功率不低於非創傷性修復治療，而使用這種更便宜，更簡單和更有效的非充填治療方法可以大大減輕治療幼兒蛀牙的負擔。

17120217.label: Realisation of objectives
17120217.value: This study was a randomized clinical trial with a 24-month follow-up to evaluate the outcomes of using atraumatic restorative treatment (ART) restorations and that of semi-annual application of silver diamine fluoride (SDF) solution in treating decayed primary teeth in young children. Through the successful implementation of this clinical trial involving 426 children in 23 kindergartens in Hong Kong, all four study objectives have been fully achieved. Regarding the first objective to compare the clinical outcomes of the two study treatment methods for decayed primary teeth, through conducting regular clinical examinations of the study children, it was found that the 24-month treatment success rate of SDF application was higher than that of ART restoration (71% vs 36%, p<0.001). Regarding the second objective to compare the cost of using SDF applications and that of ART restorations to treat decayed primary teeth, through recording the time and the materials used in the two treatments, it was found that it required less time and lower material cost to use SDF applications (<1 minute vs 4.2 minutes; and approximately $2 vs $4). Regarding the third objective to compare the oral health-related quality of life of the study children after having received the two treatments, through the use of a parental questionnaire survey, it was found that there was no statistically significant difference in the mean measurement scores between the two groups (3.8 vs 2.3, p>0.05). Regarding the fourth objective to compare the parents’ acceptance of the two treatment methods, through the use of a parental questionnaire survey, it was found that there were no significant differences in the parental satisfaction with their child’s tooth status and tooth appearance between the SDF and the ART groups.

17120217.label: Major findings and research outcome
17120217.value: This randomized clinical trial was conducted in 23 kindergartens in Hong Kong. At baseline, 426 children aged 3 to 4 years were randomly assigned to two groups and their decayed primary teeth were treated. In the first group, the treatment was semi-annual application of 38% silver diamine fluoride (SDF) solution to arrest/stop the dental caries (tooth decay) process. Children in the second group received atraumatic restorative treatment (ART) in which dental restorations (fillings) using glass ionomer cement were placed. All treatments were carried out in the kindergartens and 1,195 dental caries lesions were treated. Due the large sample size and quantity of treatment, it took more than a year to complete the recruitment of study children and treatment of their decayed teeth. Unfortunately, there have been several waves of COVID-19 in Hong Kong since early 2020 and the kindergartens were closed for long periods of time during the implementation of this study. Many follow-up examinations had to be conducted through home visits. Inevitably, the process was slow and completion of this study was delayed. Despite the difficulties mentioned above, this clinical trial was successfully completed. A total of 380 (89%) children and 1,044 (87%) treated lesions were followed for 24 months. In 71% of the SDF treated lesions, the tooth surface was hard and there were no signs of active caries or discomfort, i.e. achieving the clinically successful outcome. For the ART restored lesions, 36% of the fillings were retained with no need for replacement. The treatment success rate in the SDF group was significantly higher (p<0.001). Regarding the cost of providing the two treatments in this study, on average it took less than one minute to apply SDF on a carious lesion while the mean time to place an ART restoration was 4.2 minutes. The material cost for applying SDF was approximately HK$2 per lesion while that for ART was approximately HK$5 per restoration. In both study groups, there was a slight deterioration in their oral health-related quality of life from baseline to the 24-month follow-up as measured by the Early Childhood Oral Health Impact Scale (ECOHIS). The changes in mean ECOHIS score were 3.8 and 2.3 in the SDF and the ART groups, respectively (p>0.05), out of a maximum possible score of 52. There were no significant differences in the parental satisfaction with their child’s tooth status and appearance between the SDF and the ART groups.

17120217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17120217.value: Since this randomized clinical trial show that application of SDF solution have a higher treatment success rate than restoring decayed primary teeth in preschool children in outreach dental services, this approach should be promoted and tested in a community setting on a large sample. In the current kindergarten children oral health project provided by the Faculty of Dentistry of the University of Hong Kong which serves over 500 kindergartens a year, annual application of SDF is used and a research project (funded by RGC, ref #17100220) is being conducted to evaluate the impact of the service on the dental caries experience, treatment need and quality of life of school children. Our research team continues to advance our research on SDF to study its effectiveness in preventing new dental caries. Two randomized clinical trials on SDF have recently obtained research funding, one from Health and Medical Research Fund (HMRF ref #17181481) and one from RGC (ref #17100421), and are being conducted on kindergarten children in Hong Kong. We have also prepared other proposals for clinical studies on the use of SDF to prevent and treat dental caries in young children and in older adults. These proposed projects are applying for research funding from the HMRF and the RGC.

17120217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17120217.value: This study is a 24-month clinical trial which compared the clinical outcomes of topical applications of silver diamine fluoride (SDF) solution and those of placing dental filling in treating decayed primary teeth of kindergarten children in an outreach dental service setting. It was found that the clinical treatment success rate of applying SDF was higher than that of placing dental restorations and that the cost of applying SDF was lower. Furthermore, there were no significant differences in parental satisfaction with their child’s tooth status and appearance between the two types of treatment. Thus, this study provides good clinical evidence to support the use of SDF in managing tooth decay in preschool children, a dental public health problem in Hong Kong and also in many places around the world. The use of SDF application, a simple, low-cost and effective treatment for tooth decay, in outreach dental services will greatly improve the oral health of numerous young children.

17120517.label: Major findings and research outcome
17120517.value: Human mesenchymal stromal cells (MSC) are one of the oldest progenitor cells that have been introduced for “regenerative medicine”, as well as in modulation of a range of immune and inflammatory-mediated conditions. Today, several somatic tissue-derived MSCs productions have been approved for clinical applications in some countries, such as Ministry of Food and Drug Safety of Korea has approved allogeneic umbilical cord-derived MSC for degenerative arthritis (Cartistem) and autologous adipose tissue-derived MSC (Cupistem) for anal fistula (Crohn’s disease). However, MSCs are susceptible to senescent in culture and molecular mechanisms have not been fully elusive yet . Krüppel-like Factor 4 (KLF4) is critical in cell cycle regulation and mitochondrial biogenesis during the generation of induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs). Here, we explored the function of KLF4 in mesenchymal cell biology using human iPSC derived mesenchymal stem cells (iPSC-MSCs), a cell line generated previously by our lab. Our major findings in this project are summarized as follows . 1. high expression of KLF4 strongly suppressed cell proliferation indicating KLF4 as a negative cell cycle regulator in iPSC-MSCs. Cell cycle analysis showed an increase in G1-stage population while a decrease in G2/M-stage population after cell cycle synchronization by G1-stage inhibitor L-mimosine, suggesting a block in G1-S transition by KLF4. 2. Senescence-associated β-galactosidase (SA-β-gal) staining revealed an increase in cellular senescence after KLF4 overexpression. In surprise, KLF4 overexpression had no significant effect on mitochondrial oxidative function examined by mitochondrial oxygen consumption rate (OCR) test. 3. RNA-sequencing (RNA-seq) was performed on iPSC-MSCs with KLF4 overexpression or knockdown, and revealed a large group of genes associated with cell cycle downregulated by both KLF4 overexpression and knockdown, suggesting that fine-tuned expression of KLF4 is important for normal iPSC-MSCs function. 4. Consistent with its roles in epithelial differentiation and skin barrier function, a set of epithelial-specific genes were significantly induced by KLF4 overexpression in iPSC-MSC. A subset of TGF-βs signalling genes and YAP1/TAZ target genes were significantly suppressed by KLF4 overexpression. Immunofluorescence staining of YAP1 confirmed a decrease in nuclear YAP1 translocation, indicating a reduction in YAP1/TAZ mediated signalling which probably contributed to cell cycle inhibition as well. 5. Moreover, we observed a mesenchymal-epithelial phenotype transition ( MET) in iPSC-MSCs was fully blocked by KLF4 overexpression, supporting the function of KLF4 as a regulator in mesenchymal cell MET/EMT phenotype transition.

17120517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17120517.value: Human mesenchymal stromal cells (MSC) have been introduced for “regenerative medicine”. However, MSCs are vulnerable to senescence that has hindered scale-up expansion of MSC for therapeutical application. The fine-tuned expression level of KLF4 is important for normal MSCs function. In the future, correcting skewed expression level of KLF4 will be developed to rescue MSC ageing in regenerative medicine, and restore retarded mesenchymal-epithelial phenotype transition in cancer therapy .

17120517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17120517.value: Human mesenchymal stromal cells (MSC) hold great potential for regenerative medicine. However, MSCs susceptible to senescence has limited us to achieve a large amount of MSC required by therapeutics. Here, we found that the fine-tuned expression level of Krüppel-like Factor 4 (KLF4) is important for normal MSCs function. Our study revealed that skewed expression level of KLF4 resulted in reduced cell proliferation , inducing MSC senescence independent on mitochondrial oxidative function. RNA-sequencing (RNA-seq) revealed a subset of TGF-βs signalling genes and YAP1/TAZ target genes were significantly suppressed by KLF4 overexpression. Moreover, a phenotype of mesenchymal-epithelial transition in MSCs was fully blocked by KLF4 overexpression. correcting skewed expression level of KLF4 will be developed to rescue MSC ageing in regenerative medicine, and restore retarded mesenchymal-epithelial phenotype transition in cancer therapy . Our study provides a novel role of KLF4 in regulating MSC functions . The findings allow us to manipulate KLF4 to rescue MSC ageing in regenerative medicine, and restore retarded mesenchymal-epithelial phenotype transition in cancer therapy .

17121417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17121417.value: 体外稳定HIF-1α信号通路提高移植后牙干细胞的存活率及血管生成能力 研究背景：理想的微环境对于组织工程学中细胞的存活，分化以及新血管的生成有着至关重要的作用。我们的研究表明，依赖牙干细胞-支架材料的牙髓再生方法能够获得类牙髓的新生组织，但由于植入细胞的低生存率，全根管的牙髓组织再生仍然很难实现。 关键问题：缺血模型显示当细胞移植到大面积组织缺损区域后，只有10-60%的比率可以存活下来。而在牙髓组织再生移植手术中，因为根管解剖结构的特殊性，根管内的组织只能通过根尖孔获得血液供应，细胞的生存率将会更低。同时由于血管仅以每天小于1mm的速度生长，而距离毛细血管200µm以外的植入细胞无法通过扩散作用获得营养支持，提高移植后细胞的生存率显得至关重要。近来的研究表明，在缺氧条件下，缺氧诱导因子1α（HIF-1α）被激活，致使细胞的活性氧（ROS）水平降低而能量水平增高，从而细胞的生存率得以提高。然而，相关的此类研究并未在牙源干细胞及牙髓再生领域中被探索或报道过。 研究目的和方法： 目的一：探讨HIF-1α信号通路在人脱落乳牙干细胞体外存活与功能中的作用。研究HIF-1α基因沉默对血管生成，成牙本质/成骨向分化以及细胞存活与凋亡的影响。 目的二：探讨在体外缺氧条件下，HIF-1α在减少氧耗量与清除ROS中的作用。研究缺氧条件下，HIF-1α基因沉默的人脱落乳牙干细胞的氧消耗率，糖酵解效率，ROS水平和能量水平的变化。 目的三：探讨HIF-1α稳定在人脱落乳牙干细胞生存与血管生成中的作用。我们通过基因沉默技术或者采用抑制剂使脯氨酰羟化酶2（PHD2）失活从而使HIF-1α在人脱落乳牙干细胞中稳定表达。探究HIF-1α稳定表达人脱落乳牙干细胞相应的血管生成和成牙本质/成骨向分化能力，存活与凋亡率以及氧消耗率，糖酵解效率，ROS水平和能量水平变化。 目的四：利用HIF-1α稳定表达的人脱落乳牙干细胞探究体内牙髓再生实验。我们用PuraMatrix水凝胶支架包裹HIF-1α稳定表达的人脱落乳牙干细胞并注入到人牙根切段中，随后一起移植到重症联合免疫缺陷性小鼠背部皮下组织。3到4周后，移植物将被取出并检测细胞的存活率，血管生成以及牙髓再生的效果。 研究意义：本课题将首次探究体外HIF-1α稳定对移植后牙干细胞存活与血管生成的作用。本项目如获得成功，将对牙髓组织再生研究和治疗产生革命性的影响以及显著的指导意义。

17121417.label: Realisation of objectives
17121417.value: Objective 1. To elucidate the role of HIF-1α signaling in stem cells from human exfoliated deciduous teeth (SHED) survival and function in vitro. We aimed to explore the role of hypoxia inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α) in post-implantation survival and angio-/vasculogenesis of SHED. HIF-1α in SHED was suppressed using siRNA or chemical inhibitor (YC-1) and used in Matrigel plug assay conducted on severe combined immunodeficient (SCID) mice. The plugs were retrieved on day 3 or 7 post-injection and analyzed for hypoxia status, ki67 expression, DNA fragmentation (TUNEL), cellularity, and vascularization by histology and immunohistochemistry for CD31, HIF-1α, pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase-1 (PDK1), hexokinase 2 (HK2), and glucose transporter 1 (Glut1). Histological analysis of Matrigel plugs showed significantly reduced cell survival in HIF-1α silenced or chemically inhibited SHED groups, which could be attributed to diminished metabolic adaptations as shown by decreased PDK1, HK2, and Glut1 expression. HIF-1α inhibition in SHED also resulted in significantly low blood vessel formation as observed by a low number of perfused and non-perfused vessels of human or mouse CD31 origin. The cell viability of HIF-1α silenced SHED was significantly affected under hypoxia, H2O2, and low-glucose conditions in vitro as shown by CCK-8 assay, which was reflected in increased cytoplasmic and mitochondrial ROS levels detected via CM-H2DCFDA and MitoSOX Red, respectively. Secretory protein levels of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and the respective paracrine effects on endothelial cell proliferation and migration were detected by ELISA, CCK-8 assay, and trans-well assay, respectively. Significantly reduced levels of VEGF in HIF-1α silenced SHED resulted in decreased paracrine angiogenic effects as shown by low proliferation and migration of endothelial cells. Taken together, we demonstrated that HIF-1α plays an indispensable role in post-implantation survival and angio-/vasculogenic properties of SHED by maintaining ROS homeostasis, inducing metabolic adaptations, and VEGF secretion. Objective 2. To investigate the role of HIF-1α in reducing oxygen consumption and scavenging ROS in hypoxia. HIF-1α stabilization in SHED was achieved by knockdown of prolyl hydroxylase domain-containing protein 2 (PHD2) using premade target shRNA lentiviral particles. PHD2 and HIF-1α expression levels were confirmed by RT-PCR and western blotting. Cell viability in vitro was tested by MTT assay after exposing cells to different concentrations of exogenous H2O2 (0, 100, 200, 300, 400 and 500μM) for 24 hours. HIF-1α-stabilized-SHED demonstrated significantly higher cell viability under stress conditions compared to that of SHED that did not express HIF-1α (p<0.05). Oxygen Consumption Rate, ATP and p-AMPK levels were significantly decreased in HIF-1α-stabilized SHED (p<0.05) indicating less O2 consumption by the cells. Expressions of reactive oxygen species (ROS) related genes, Cox4-1 and Cox4-2, were down-regulated, which signified a reduced ROS generation; whereas expressions of genes involved in ROS such as scavenging glucose transporter 1 (Glut1), hexokinase 2 (HK2) and 6-phosphofructo-2-kinase/fructose-2,6-bisphosphatase isoform 3 (PFKFB3) were upregulated following HIF-1α stabilization (p<0.05). The total level of glutathione, a mitochondrial superoxide scavenger, was increased in HIF-1α-stabilized SHED illustrating enhanced ROS scavenging (p<0.05). Additionally, we explored the effects of HIF-1α stabilization on post-implantation cell viability during dental pulp regeneration in vivo, and found out that HIF-1α-stabilized-SHED undergo reduced cell apoptosis and demonstrate increased cell survival significantly as shown by DNA damage and ki67 staining at day 7. Furthermore, we revealed that HIF-1α downstream signaling activates PI3K/AKT pathway, up-regulates expression of PDK1, HK2, Glut1 and Smad7, which synergistically contribute to reduced apoptosis and maintenance of ROS balance and metabolic adaptations in hypoxia. Taken together, we demonstrated that HIF-1α stabilization promotes cellular adaptation under stress condition through down-regulating the intracellular ROS levels in SHED, which can be attributed to increased ROS scavenging, reduced oxygen consumption and ROS production. Objective 3. To examine the effects of HIF-1α stabilization on SHED survival and angiogenesis. HIF-1α stabilization in SHED in turn significantly increased the expression of an angiogenic factor: vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF). When conditioned medium from HIF-1α-stabilized SHED was used to treat human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs), increased migration and proliferation were observed indicating enhanced paracrine signaling of SHED following PHD2 knockdown (P < 0.05). Furthermore, the coculture of HIF-1α-stabilized SHED with HUVECs directly and in fibrin beads demonstrated significantly longer vascular sprouts through juxtacrine and paracrine effects (P < 0.05). When HIF-1α-stabilized SHED were added to a preformed HUVEC vascular tube network on Matrigel, it not only stabilized the vessels, as shown by the increased thickness (P < 0.05) and junctional area (P < 0.01) of tubes, but also gave rise to new sprouting (P < 0.01). This observation, with the morphologic changes and increased CD31 expression, suggested that HIF-1α stabilization enhanced the endothelial differentiation capacity of SHED through autocrine signaling, mainly via VEGF. In vivo Matrigel plug assay demonstrated that HIF-1α-stabilized SHED alone could give rise to a vasculature that was significantly higher than that of control SHED ± HUVECs and similar to that of HIF-1α-stabilized SHED + HUVECs. In addition to vasculogenesis by endothelial differentiation, HIF-1α-stabilized SHED recruited host blood vessels into the implant by exerting a significant paracrine effect. Taken together, our results confirmed that HIF-1α-stabilized SHED could replace the function of HUVECs and act as the sole cell source of vascularization. Thus, targeting PHD2 to stabilize HIF-1α expression is an appealing strategy that enables the use of a single cell source for achieving vascularized tissue regeneration. Objective 4. To utilize HIF-1α stabilized SHED in dental pulp regeneration in vivo. In order to examine the effects of hypoxia preconditioning of SHED in dental pulp regeneration, HIF-1α-stabilized-SHED were encapsulated in PuraMatrix peptide hydrogel, injected into full-length human tooth fragments and implanted subcutaneously into the dorsum of severe combined immunodeficient mice (CB.17 SCID). Tetracycline hydrochloride was injected at day 10, 15, 19, and 24 subcutaneously. Samples were retrieved after 7 days or 28 days. After 28 days, the macroscopic and H&E stained images showed that the HIF-1α-stabilized-SHED injected tooth fragments contained significantly higher number of vessels as well as vascular lumens with increased diameter within the regenerated pulp-like tissue. Quantification of human CD31 and vWF positive vessels revealed that HIF-1α stabilized SHED have differentiated into endothelial cells and contributed to functional vessel formation significantly (p < 0.01, p < 0.001) more than the Control-SHED in pulp-like tissue in vivo. In addition, HIF-1α stabilized SHED had recruited significantly higher (p < 0.05) number of host vessels compared to that of Control-SHED as indicated by the number of mouse CD31 positive vessels. These results confirmed that HIF-1α stabilized SHED can enhance both angiogenesis and vasculogenesis during dental pulp regeneration in vivo. Additionally, we assessed the odonto-/osteogenic capacity of HIF-1α-stabilized-SHED in regenerated pulp-like tissue. Significant fluorescent line corresponding to the tetracycline injections was detected in the dentin of the tooth fragments injected with HIF-1α-stabilized-SHED in contrast to a faint line in Control-SHED injected group (p<0.01). In accordance, immunohistochemistry for DSPP showed significantly higher positivity in HIF-1α-stabilized-SHED group (p<0.001) in the odontoblast-like cell layer at the dentin-pulp interface, which also appeared to have processes extending into the dentinal tubules compared to the control group. Taken together, our results showed that HIF-1α stabilization could significantly enhance the odonto-/osteogenic differentiation of SHED and promote dentinogenesis during pulp-like tissue regeneration in vivo.

17121417.label: Major findings and research outcome
17121417.value: 1. The current project for the first time revealed the indispensable role of HIF-1α in mediating post-implantation survival and angio-/vasculogenic properties of stem cells from exfoliated deciduous teeth (SHED) by maintaining ROS homeostasis, inducing metabolic adaptations, and VEGF secretion (Han et al., 2021). These results indicated that if stabilization of HIF-1α expression can be achieved ex vivo, cells would be more resistant to hypoxic stress. 2. Furthermore, we demonstrated that HIF-1α stabilization could promote cellular adaptation under stress condition through down-regulation of the intracellular ROS levels in SHED, which can be attributed to increased ROS scavenging, reduced oxygen consumption and ROS production. 3. Subsequently, through in vivo Matrigel plug assay, we demonstrated that HIF-1α-stabilized SHED alone could give rise to a vasculature that was significantly higher than that of control SHED ± HUVECs and similar to that of HIF-1α-stabilized SHED + HUVECs. In addition to vasculogenesis by endothelial differentiation, HIF-1α-stabilized SHED recruited host blood vessels into the implant by exerting a significant paracrine effect. (Han et al., 2020) Taken together, our results confirmed that HIF-1α-stabilized SHED could replace the function of HUVECs and act as the sole cell source of vascularization. Thus, targeting PHD2 to stabilize HIF-1α expression is an appealing strategy that enables the use of a single cell source for achieving vascularized tissue regeneration. 4. The use of HIF-1α stabilized SHED in an in vivo dental pulp regeneration mouse model showed that HIF-1α stabilization can enhance both angiogenesis and vasculogenesis during dental pulp regeneration in vivo. Moreover, the results showed that HIF-1α stabilization could significantly enhance the odonto-/osteogenic differentiation of SHED and promote dentinogenesis during pulp-like tissue regeneration in vivo. (Han et al., 2022) 5. Furthermore, we revealed that PI3K/AKT activation contributes to the low caspase 3 expression and in turn low apoptosis in HIF-1α stabilized SHED in hypoxia. And this HIF-1α induced cell survival also relied on the maintenance of ROS balance and metabolic adaptations in hypoxia with up-regulated expression of PDK1, HK2, and Glut1. Furthermore, we also identified Smad7 as one of the top 3 upregulated genes by bioinformatic analysis and proved its essential role in HIF-1α induced HK2 and Glut1 improvement. (Han et al., 2022) 6. Therefore, HIF-1α stabilization can enhance cell survival through modulating various target genes and potential signaling pathways, and angiogenesis through VEGF dependent autocrine and paracrine actions, which is an appealing strategy for dental pulp regeneration and other stem cell-based therapy in general.

17121417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17121417.value: As the results of our current study demonstrated HIF-1α stabilization in dental stem cells as a promising strategy in enhancing post-implantation cell survival and angiogenesis, our next aim is to develop a clinically applicable model to recapitulate the results. In a prospective study, we aim to replace the lentiviral-mediated gene knockdown method that we used in the current study as this cannot be applied in the clinical setting due to safety concerns. To successfully address the challenge of translating our strong experimental data into preclinical/clinical applications, we need to develop safe non-viral methods. Therefore, it is crucial to identify and characterise the optimal compounds and dosage-setting for applying the hypoxic preconditioning phenomenon in SHED. We were able to successfully secure funding from RGC to use a systematic bioinformatic and scientific experimental approach to identify, characterize, and optimize SM compounds that can be used to stabilize HIF-1α under normoxia in SHED. Furthermore, we aim to examine underlying HIF-1α downstream signaling mechanisms responsible for enhancing dental stem cell survival under hypoxia in depth in order to broaden our understanding on hypoxic preconditioning approach.

17121417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17121417.value: Tooth derived stem cells are a promising type of cells that can be used in tooth tissue regeneration. However, once introduced into the human body, cellular grafts solely depend on oxygen and nutrients receive by diffusion from the nearest blood vessel. The diffusion serves only up to 200 um distance, therefore, achieving a sufficient blood supply and maintaining cell viability until they receive adequate oxygen and nutrients via circulation are two of the most important factors for the successful outcome in tissue regeneration. Cells have developed natural mechanisms to adapt to harsh environmental stimuli specifically via activation of certain genes, which is inhibited in normal oxygen conditions by expression of a specific gene (PHD2). We hypothesised that if dental stem cells can be primed to low oxygen conditions by inhibition of PHD2 before transplantation, the adaptive mechanisms will be activated prior to cells experience harsh transplantation conditions and perform better following transplantation. Accordingly, the current project for the first time, demonstrated that priming dental stem cells for reduced oxygen conditions before transplantation could stimulate the cells to express genes and proteins that enhance their survival and blood vessel formation during tooth pulp tissue regeneration.

17121517.label: Project Objectives
17121517.value: We aim at a series of technical developments to enable the measurement of 3D inter-shot phase variation and improve the scan throughput for 3D multi-shot DW-EPI sequence, thereby further optimizing acquisition efficiency for 3D dMRI. First, we plan to embed an echo-volume imaging (EVI) based navigator echo into 3D multi-shot DW-EPI sequence to directly measure the 3D phase profile at each sampling of signal. Second, we plan to incorporate multi-band imaging technique into 3D multi-shot DW-EPI sequence equipped with EVI based navigator to double the scan coverage for a given repetition time. We aim to develop a new reconstruction method to eliminate the artifacts in the 3D multi-shot DW-EPI data acquired with either single- or multi- band imaging technique. First, the newly developed reconstruction method will enable 3D phase correction by using the information derived from navigator data. Second, a new concept will be introduced that the slab excitation profile and multi-band imaging will be incorporated into newly developed reconstruction method as a part of spatial encoding, thereby eliminating slab boundary artifacts and separating overlapped slab data. We will conduct a comprehensive study to quantitatively evaluate our newly developed techniques: 1) image quality (i.e., in terms of distortion, SNR, artifact level, and phase correction efficacy); 2) influence of scan parameters on acquisition efficiency and artifact reduction; and 3) influence of spatial resolution on connectivity mapping on healthy subjects.

17121517.label: Realisation of objectives
17121517.value: 1. Brief background: Diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (dMRI) has become an indispensable tool for improving the understanding of numerous neurological diseases and disorders. Despite the fact that various 3D dMRI techniques has been proposed to achieve high-resolution dMRI, there are still few shortcomings that have to be addressed before 3D dMRI can be brought into routine clinical practice and research applications. 2. Goal: The ultimate goal of this project is to develop an advanced 3D dMRI technique with high image quality and reasonable acquisition time, and possibly benefit future neuroscience researches. 3. Research activities and outputs: In the projection duration of total 36 months, we have completely achieved three objectives proposed in the original proposal, and also extended the technical developments to benefit other applications of dMRI. Below are the brief summaries. Objective 1: We have successfully developed a 3D interleaved DW-EPI pulse sequence equipped with 3D single-shot EPI navigator echo that can enable the measurement of inter-shot 3D phase variation (i.e., data inconsistency among the acquisitions of different segments of k-space data). The k-space trajectory of 3D single-shot EPI navigator echo is based on an echo-volume imaging method that is also combined with three strategies to minimise the echo time. In addition, to minimize the off-resonance effect along kz for the 3D single-shot navigator echo, we incorporate a calibration scan into the data acquisition of T2-weighted data. This calibration scan can correct the distortion along z for the 3D single-shot EPI navigator echo that can maintain exactly same geometric profile between imaging and navigator data. Besides, incorporating calibration scan into the data acquisition of T2-weighted data do not increase the total scan time, thereby improving the feasibility of 3D dMRI without sacrificing scan efficiency. With the development described above, we can successfully measure the inter-shot 3D phase variation with a low spatial resolution 3D volume image as 128 x 32 x 12 during each acquisition of the k-space segment. After successful development of above 3D multi-shot DW-EPI sequence with 3D single-shot navigator echo, we have successfully incorporated multi-band (MB) acquisition into it for doubling the scan coverage with a given repetition time. We have carefully considered technical realization of MB EVI-based navigator echo, and then adopted a split-echo scheme to acquire the MB 3D single-shot navigator echo. Our development has demonstrated successful measurement of 3D phase variations for two simultaneously excited slabs. Moreover, during the in-vivo test, we found that the oblique slab orientation may lead to insufficient ghost artifact correction by using conventional 1D phase correction. In light of this, we further modified the pulse sequence with alternating readout that can enable self-referenced 2D phase correction for oblique slab acquisition by combining virtual coil technique. This development can also benefit the multi-oblique diffusion-weighted echo-planar imaging with parallel imaging used in routine scan by eliminating the residual aliasing artifact that resembles brain lesion. In summary, we have completely achieved Objective 1 and further extended our development to address other technical challenges. Objective 2: We have successfully developed a new reconstruction framework, namely 3D multiplexed sensitivity encoding and reconstruction (3D-MUSER), for eliminating the artifacts associated with data inconsistency existing in 3D multi-shot DW-EPI data acquisition. The developed reconstruction algorithm is an extension of the 2D-MUSE framework from image-domain-based (i.e., solving aliased pixels) to hybrid k-space-based reconstruction (i.e., solving the signal equation). Our developed 3D-MUSER can enable 3D phase correction by using the information derived from 3D single-shot EPI navigator data (i.e., successful development in Objective 1), and also consider non-linear 3D inter-shot phase variations. We have demonstrated that 3D-MUSER can eliminate the aliasing artifacts and signal corruptions due to 3D inter-shot phase variations in thick slab 3D dMRI acquisition, thereby improving the feasible slab thickness. With those developments, we can achieve near whole brain 3D dMRI at 1.5T clinical MRI with 1.3mm-isotropic voxel size. In addition, our preliminary investigation also demonstrates that 3D-MUSER can improve the efficacy of phase correction for the 3D dMRI data acquired with high b-value. Afterward, we have further developed 3D-MUSER for reconstructing the 3D dMRI acquired with multi-band (MB) technique. The overlapped 3D MB dMRI data can be successfully reconstructed with 3D phase correction, resulting in 50% improvement of scan coverage. Beside to the improvements in feasible slab thickness and scan efficiency of 3D dMRI, we have further addressed the slab-boundary artifact (SBA) issue present in multi-slab 3D dMRI with sliding-slab profile encoding (SLIPEN). Our proposed SLIPEN technique relies on the slab profile as a part of spatial encoding, and we have further incorporated sliding-slab acquisition into the 3D-MUSER pulse sequence developed in Objective 1. Through the design of proper acquisition order of the slabs, the slab profiles of each slabs can be internally measured from the T2-weithged data. Compared with previously developed methods for address SBA by other researchers (e.g., PEN and SPEN), our developed SLIPEN method can eliminate the need of extra calibration scan with efficient correction of SBA, therefore improving the feasibility of 3D dMRI for neuroscience research. With the technical achievement mentioned above, the SLIPEN method was awarded first place for poster presentation in the workshop of “Data Sampling and Reconstruction” hosted by “International Society for Magnetic Resonance in Medicine”. In summary, we have completely achieved Objective 2 to develop several advanced 3D dMRI techniques that can address current limitations and improve the feasibility of 3D dMRI. Objective 3: We have successfully conducted a comprehensive study to quantitatively evaluate our newly developed techniques, namely 3D-MUSER, by performing a series of comparisons to 2D-MUSE technique (only being capable of 2D phase correction) on both phantoms and healthy subjects. We have evaluated the developed 3D-MUSER technique for the data acquisition of 3D dMRI in terms of point spread function, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), level of residual artifacts after data reconstruction, and the efficacy of artifact reduction. Our evaluation results show that the developed 3D-MUSER technique can more effectively and robustly eliminate the data inconsistency (i.e., inter-shot phase variations) for 3D dMRI acquired with relatively thin slab thickness (e.g., < 20 mm), while maintaining the SNR comparable to 2D phase correction method (i.e., 2D-MUSE). In addition, the systematic evaluation of artifact reductions in different slab thicknesses shows that 3D-MUSER can also effectively and robustly eliminate the data inconsistency present in thick slab 3D dMRI (e.g., from 20mm to 100mm). In contrast, the conventional 2D phase correction method (i.e., 2D-MUSE) cannot successfully eliminate the artifacts in the 3D dMRI data associated with thick slab acquisition (e.g., > 30mm) that demonstrates the superiority of developed 3D-MUSER method. Moreover, we have evaluated the efficacy of artifact reduction for the 3D dMRI data acquired with high b-value (i.e., inversely proportional to the slowest diffusivity encoded) which can lead to severer through-slab phase variation. In our study, 3D-MUSER can better suppress the artifacts in 3D dMRI associated with high b-value acquisition that demonstrates the wider application of 3D dMRI enabled by 3D-MUSER. Furthermore, the evaluation on spatial resolution of 3D dMRI preliminarily shows that high-resolution 3D dMRI can discover more structure connections between different brain regions, suggesting more information obtained from high-resolution 3D dMRI data. In summary, we have completely achieved Objective 3 to quantitively evaluate our developed technique, and shown that it has better performance than previously proposed techniques in term of artifact reduction.

17121517.value: The Major findings and research outcomes can be summarised in two main aspects at below. I) Technical development: 1. Completion of the development of 3D multi-shot DW-EPI sequence embedded an echo-volume imaging (EVI) based single-shot 3D navigator echo and multi-band imaging technique that can improve the efficacy of artifact reduction and efficiency of data acquisition for 3D dMRI (Part C. 8.1, 9.8, and 9.9). 2. Completion of the development of 3D multi-shot DW-EPI sequence with sliding slab profile encoding that can address slab boundary artifact without the need of extra calibration (Part C. 8.6, and 9.9). 3. Successful development of a reconstruction pipeline (i.e., 3D-MUSER) to eliminate the artifacts in the 3D multi-shot DW-EPI data acquired with either single- or multi- band imaging technique (Part C. 8.1, and 9.8). 4. Successful development of an iterative reconstruction method (i.e., SLIPEN) that incorporates slab profile encoding into data reconstruction for simultaneously eliminating artifacts associated with data inconsistency and non-ideal profile. (Part C. 8.6 and 9.8) 5. Successful development of a self-reference Nyquist ghost correction method for both 2D and 3D interleaved-EPI acquisition with oblique plane, and for Propeller-EPI acquisition (Part C. 8.2, 8.4, 8.5, 9.1-9.4, 9.6, 9.10-9.13, and 9.15). II) Technical evaluation: 1. Successful evaluation of developed 3D-MUSER technique in terms of point spread function (PSF), signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), level of residual artifacts after data reconstruction, and the efficiency of artifact reduction demonstrates the superiority of 3D-MUSER to conventional 2D phase correction for 3D dMRI applications (Part C. 8.1 and 9.8, and 9.9). 2. Successful evaluation of developed reconstruction pipeline for effective artifact reduction and robust data reconstruction (Part C. 8.1-8.3, 9.5, 9.7, 9.14, and 9.15).

17121517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17121517.value: After successful development of proposed 3D dMRI technique with effective artifact reduction, we plan to further improve the scan efficiency and conduct a cohort study. The brief descriptions of future plans are summarised at below. 1. We plan to enable compressed sensing for further improving the scan efficiency of proposed 3D dMRI technique. Although incorporating multi-band imaging into 3D dMRI acquisition has already improved the scan efficiency, attaining higher spatial resolution still requires relatively long scan time. To improve the feasibility of 3D dMRI for the data acquisition on challenging population, it requires further reduction of total scan time with higher acceleration. 2. We plan to acquire the data from more healthy subjects for the deeper investigation and understanding of the influence of spatial resolution on structural connectivity mapping . We will work with local neurologists and scientists in neuroscience research for the interpretation of the results.

17121517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17121517.value: Three-dimensional diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (3D dMRI) is an advanced medical imaging technique that can non-invasively depict the neural fibers in human brain, therefore mapping the structural connectivity like the wiring diagram of brain. However, the scan time of 3D dMRI requires around half an hour that limits the applications in neuroscience research. The long scan time of 3D dMRI is partly due to the limited scan parameters caused by suboptimal correction method for the data inconsistency. In addition, the reconstruction of 3D dMRI data also requires the correction of slab boundary artifact present in multi-slab acquisition. In this project, we have successfully developed an advanced 3D dMRI technique that can enable better correction of data inconsistency, thereby improving the image quality and feasible scan parameters. In addition, we have further reduced the total scan time of proposed 3D dMRI technique by doubling the scan coverage using multi-band technique. Furthermore, we have successfully developed a sliding slab profile encoding method to effectively correct the slab boundary artifact without the need of extra calibration scan. The successful development of this project is expected to improve the feasibility of 3D dMRI in neuroscience research, and potentially benefit the understanding of brain activities.

17122417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17122417.value: The cardioprotective effects of adenosine and adenosine receptor agonists have been extensively studied. However, their therapeutic outcomes in treating ischemic heart disease are limited by the systemic side effects (e.g. hypotension, bradycardia and sedation). Equilibrative nucleoside transporter (ENT) inhibitors may be an alternative. By reducing the uptake of extracellular adenosine, ENT1 and ENT2 inhibitors amplify and prolong the cardioprotective and vasodilatory effects of endogenous adenosine. ENT1 and ENT2 inhibitors should have fewer systemic side effects because they selectively increase the extracellular adenosine levels in the tissues undergoing accelerated adenosine formation (e.g. in ischemic myocardium). Nonetheless, ENT1 and ENT2 are involved in nucleoside uptake for salvage pathways of nucleotide synthesis. Theoretically, long-term inhibition of ENT1 and ENT2 may adversely affect tissues that lack or have low capacity for de novo nucleotide biosynthesis (e.g. erythrocytes, leukocytes and intestine). Another potential problem is that ENT1 (and ENT2) inhibitors may affect the cellular transport and hence the efficacies of anti-cancer and anti-viral nucleoside analogs used in chemotherapy. ENT4, a novel type of ENT that can transport adenosine, is also abundant in heart. Interestingly, the activity of ENT4 is greatly increased in acidic environment. Therefore, ENT4 may contribute to the regulation of extracellular adenosine concentrations in heart, in particular under the acidotic conditions associated with ischemia. However, no investigation has hitherto been attempted to prove this idea. This project aims to investigate the role of ENT4 in cardioprotection during ischemia. First, we will confirm that ENT4 contributes to the adenosine transport in cardiomyocytes during ischemia. Extracellular adenosine level and [3H]adenosine uptake will be measured in cardiomyocytes with the ENT4 being pharmacologically inhibited or knocked out by siRNA silencing. Second, we will compare the expression and activity of ENT4 in cardiomyocytes in normal and diabetic conditions. Cardiomyocytes cultured in high glucose medium and diabetic mouse model will be used. Third, we will study the effect of inhibition/knockout of ENT4 on cardioprotection against myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury in diabetic conditions. Both in vitro cell model and in vivo animal model with ligation of coronary arteries will be used. Emphasis will be put on studying the effect of inhibition/knockout of ENT4 on the cardiac functions and pathological/morphological changes in cardiomyocytes during ischemia-reperfusion injury. We hope that this study could advance our knowledge on the physiology and pathophysiology of ischemia heart disease. The findings will also be useful for the development of cardiovascular protective drugs. 腺苷和腺苷受體激動劑的護心效應已被廣泛地研究了。然而，它們在治療缺血性心臟病的治療效果受到其系統性副作用所限制（如低血壓、心跳過緩、鎮靜等）。平衡型核苷轉運蛋白（ENT）抑制劑可能是比腺苷和腺苷受體激動劑更好的替代品。通過減少對胞外腺苷的吸收，ENT1 和 ENT2 抑制劑放大和延長了內源性腺苷的心肌保護和血管舒張作用。ENT1 和 ENT2 抑制劑的系統性副作用應該更少，因為它們只選擇性地把正在加速腺苷形成的組織（如缺血心肌）的胞外腺苷水準進一步增加。 儘管如此，ENT1 和 ENT2 參與了核苷酸補救合成途徑中的核苷攝取。理論上說，長期抑制 ENT1 和 ENT2 可能對一些缺乏從頭核苷酸合成能力的組織有壞影響（如紅細胞、白細胞、腸等）。另一個潛在問題是ENT1（或ENT2）抑制劑可能會影響癌細胞運輸抗腫瘤和抗病毒的核苷類似物，從而影響了化療的療效。 ENT4是一種在心臟內很豐富的新型平衡型核苷轉運蛋白。有趣的是，ENT4的活性在酸性環境中大大增加。因此，ENT4可能有助於調節心臟細胞外的腺苷濃度，特別是與缺血有關的酸中毒環境下。然而，到目前為止還沒有研究證明這個假設。 本課題旨在研究缺血期間ENT4於心肌保護中的作用。首先，我們將確認ENT4於缺血時有助心肌細胞的腺苷運輸。心肌細胞的ENT4將被藥物抑制或被基因敲除，然後測量胞外腺苷水平及腺苷的吸收。之後，我們將用高糖培養基培養的心肌細胞和小鼠糖尿病模型來比較心肌細胞ENT4在正常和糖尿病環境下的活性和表達水平。接著，我們將用細胞模型與冠狀動脈被結紮的動物模型來研究抑制及基因敲除ENT4後，糖尿病中心肌缺血再灌注損傷期間的心肌保護作用如何受影響。重點將放在心臟病理學變化與心臟功能的影響。我們希望這項研究能增進我們對心臟生理學和缺血性心臟病病理生理學的知識。研究結果也有助心血管保護藥物的發展。

17122417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17122417.value: The results has shown that ENT4 is involved in the regulation of adenosine transport in heart under ischemic condition. The contribution of ENT4 is even higher in diabetes. It may explain why diabetic patients suffer more from ischemic heart diseases. Regarding the implication, It is clear that inhibition of ENT4 is a promising approach to protect heart from ischemic injury. However, until now, there is still no specific inhibitor of ENT4 available. Therefore, the development of specific, effective and safe ENT4 inhibitor as novel cardiioprotective agents will be the next step in research.

17122417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17122417.value: Diabetes is a risk factor of ischemic heart disease. In this study, we have proved that the activity of equilibrative nucleoside transporter type 4 is highly increased in our heart when there is not enough blood supply over there. The increased activity of this transport can reduce the amount of adenosine and hence the lower the protective effect of adenosine on our heart. This situation is even worse in diabetes. It may explain why diabetic patients is more vulnerable to ischemic heart attack. If we can develop a drug to stop the function of equilibrative nucleoside transporter, it is possible for us to increase and prolong the protective effect of adenosine on our heart. Such drug has not been available but it will be a novel and attractive drug used in clinical practice.

17122517.label: Project Objectives
17122517.value: To investigate the correlation between mitochondrial impairment and marginal graft injury both in clinical transplantation cohort and rat liver transplantation model using small-for-size fatty liver graft To study the role and regulating mechanism of mitochondrial function and biogenesis on marginal liver graft injury through a series of in vivo (transgenic mice models) and in vitro experiments To explore the potential therapeutics to attenuate hepatic ischemia reperfusion injury by promoting mitochondrial function and biogenesis in animal models

To study the role and regulating mechanism of mitochondrial function and biogenesis on marginal liver graft injury through a series of in vivo (transgenic mice models) and in vitro experiments
To explore the potential therapeutics to attenuate hepatic ischemia reperfusion injury by promoting mitochondrial function and biogenesis in animal models

17122517.label: Realisation of objectives
17122517.value: The successful application of liver transplantation has been deemed to be optimal even only choice for patients suffering end stage liver diseases such as acute liver failure, severe decompensated liver cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. The discrepancy between huge demand for grafts and shortage of donor pool in Asia urged clinical practitioners to expand criteria of donors to marginal grafts such as fatty graft from living donor. However, severe hepatic ischemia/reperfusion injury (IRI) on marginal grafts made them more vulnerable to primary graft non-function or late dysfunction, even led to higher incidence of acute or chronic rejection. In the current RGC/GRF project, we have investigated the role of mitochondrial impairment and AMPK regulation both in clinical cohort as well as in rat liver transplantation models. Also, the dynamic function of mitochondria has been examined both in rat liver transplantation model and AMPK transgenic mice model underwent hepatic ischemia-reperfusion using intravital imaging system longitudinally. Furthermore, the mechanism of AMPK modulating mitochondrial function during marginal graft injury has been studied both in vivo and in vitro. Finally, the therapeutic value of regulating AMPK activity on attenuating graft injury has been also explored in animal model. Therefore, exploring underlying mechanism and possible therapeutic target in marginal graft injury would be important for improving the outcomes of patients as well as expanding donor pool for transplantation. Overall, representing the efforts for basic, translational and clinical research, our study has successfully tackled the basic issues of molecular mechanism for AMPK regulating mitochondrial dysfunction during marginal graft injury after transplantation. Our well-established clinical tissue/blood/data bank together with various animal models and research platforms have enabled us to conduct the current proposed study. Elucidating the precise molecular mechanism for the marginal liver graft injury will lay the foundation for further development of therapeutic strategies to prevent graft non-function and late phase consequences. With the support from this RGC/GRF grant, we have published 8 papers in international peer reviewed journals including the top journal of surgery (Annals of Surgery). There are also 8 abstracts have been presented in international congresses by trained PhD/PDFs.

17122517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17122517.value: The therapeutic potentials based on our findings about mitochondrial regulation for marginal liver graft injury will be worthwhile for further investigation in liver transplantation and liver surgery settings. It will also open a new window for the collaboration with local and international industries for the further development of new therapies, specifically targeting at mitochondrial biogenesis. It will be important for improving the outcomes of patients as well as expanding donor pool for transplantation. On the other hand, the acute phase inflammatory response induced immune suppressive environment will be important for cancer recurrence after liver transplantation or liver surgery. Therefore, the precise mechanisms involved and potential treatment targets will be also worthwhile for further exploration.

17122517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17122517.value: Through the integrated clinical, basic and translational studies, we have not only successfully demonstrated the clinical significance of mitochondrial regulation in marginal liver graft injury after transplantation in our clinical cohort, but also investigated the underlying molecular in various animal models. Most importantly, the possible therapeutic targets and potential treatments have been further explored in our animal models with encouraging outcomes. Therefore, we RGC project has successfully tackled the basic issues of molecular mechanism for AMPK regulating mitochondrial dysfunction during marginal graft injury after transplantation. Elucidating the precise molecular mechanism for the marginal liver graft injury will lay the foundation for further development of therapeutic strategies to prevent graft non-function and late phase consequences, especially for marginal liver grafts. Due to the discrepancy between huge demand for grafts and shortage of donor pool in Asia, it urged clinical practitioners to expand criteria of donors to marginal grafts such as fatty graft from living donor. The research outcome from current RGC project will also open the new window for expanding the donor pool.

17123217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17123217.value: 來自我們組和其他組的實驗結果越來越多顯示，外周系統炎症（全身炎症）可以迅速地引發大腦中的神經免疫反應。然而，儘管許多實驗研究集中在細胞因子，巨噬細胞和迷走神經上，但其生物機制仍不清楚。病理學上重要性意義在於，神經炎症可能導致疾病反應，譫妄甚至認知功能障礙。這導致阿爾茨海默病（AD）癡呆的風險增加或AD病理學上加速發展，例如增加tau蛋白的磷酸化。Tau蛋白是微管結合蛋白，並且其超磷酸化導致影響軸突運輸的微管的不穩定性。因此，全身性炎症引發的神經炎症是神經退行性疾​​病和關於術後認知功能障礙的麻醉領域的重要問題。 鄭博士團隊研究了全身炎症如何影響神經炎症。 他的團隊已經研究中樞神經系統（CNS）的微環境下調節神經免疫反應。 PI最近發表了關於全身炎症，神經炎症和疾病反應關係的兩個重要評論。 此外，我們最近發表的論文表明，E.Coli的皮下感染如何影響神經炎症。 與其他研究一起，研究得出結論，巨噬細胞可引發神經炎症。 鄭博士團隊已經建立了剖腹術作為術後認知功能障礙（POCD）的實驗模型，導致全身炎症。該模型優於使用細菌內毒素脂多醣的其他模型，因為剖腹手術對認知功能和tau病理學具有長期影響。為了解剖巨噬細胞如何觸發神經炎症和認知功能障礙的潛在機制，該組長期以來一直在研究激素雙鏈RNA依賴性蛋白激酶（PKR），其上調巨噬細胞/小膠質細胞中的免疫應答並影響神經元中的認知功能。假設PKR在調節巨噬細胞轉導大腦炎症信號和調節膽鹼能神經元的認知功能方面發揮關鍵作用。我們將使用cre-lox方法在巨噬細胞和膽鹼能神經元中特異性敲除PKR。通過結合經典染色，Western印跡方法與新型磁共振光譜（MRS），microPET掃描，執行功能的新認知測試和快速透明腦方法，我們將研究巨噬細胞的浸潤，腦代謝和神經膠質的激活。結果將在活體動物和組織/生物化學檢測中得到證實。因此，該研究不僅促進了我們對系統性觸發神經炎症的理解，而且還對術後患者使用MRS的治療干預和診斷具有翻譯意義。

17123217.label: Realisation of objectives
17123217.value: For the three objectives, we have successfully accomplished the first and third objectives, although the results are not entirely what we anticipated. We are currently working on the second one and will complete it in August. For objective 1, we found that there was a significant increase in the number of vessel-associated macrophages in the frontal cortex following laparotomy when compared with the control counterpart. Owing to the limitation of the confocal imaging, it is challenging to tell whether the vessel-associated macrophages were being infiltrated into the brain. Therefore, we moved on to examine it by flow cytometry. By utilizing the C57BL/6-Tg(CD68-EGFP)1Drg/J mice, we successfully sorted out GFP-containing macrophages in the brain, and a significant increase was observed in the percentage of GFP-containing macrophages in both the frontal cortex and hippocampus. For objective 2, LysM-CrefPKR mice are required to study the roles of PKR in macrophages on modulating systemic inflammation-induced neuroinflammation. To generate the LysM-CrefPKR mice, floxed PKR (fPKR) mice were mated with the LysM-Cre mice. However, due to the prolonged shipping and processing time under the pandemic, we could not obtain a sufficient number of mice for experiments until last month. We have already performed the laparotomy in the LysM-CrefPKR mice, and currently working on the immunohistochemical analysis. Before obtaining the LysM-CrefPKR mice, we have also investigated the role of PKR in modulating systemic inflammation, neuroinflammation, and cognitive function using the PKR knockout mouse model. By genetic deletion of PKR, we demonstrated the critical role of PKR in regulating both peripheral and neural inflammation. Knockout of PKR could help alleviate neuroimmune responses, phosphorylation of tau, and cognitive impairment induced by laparotomy. For objective 3, we have demonstrated that inhibition of PKR in cholinergic neurons could modulate cognitive functions in the laparotomy model. Due to the unavailability of the ChAT-IRES-CrefPKR mice, we performed stereotaxic injection of rAAV-DIO-PKR-K296R into the lateral ventricle of the ChAT-IRES-Cre-eGFP mouse to inhibit the activation of PKR in cholinergic neurons. Different behavioral tests were performed. To further investigate the impact of PKR inhibition in cholinergic neurons on brain glucose metabolism, MS-based targeted metabolomics was performed. Tricarboxylic acids and glycolysis intermediates were quantified in the frontal cortex. We found that inhibition of PKR in cholinergic neurons could alleviate the laparotomy-induced changes in glucose metabolism and cognitive deficits. Taken all results together, we conclude that PKR plays a critical role in regulating both peripheral and neural inflammation. Furthermore, PKR in neurons could modulate glucose metabolism and cognitive functions. Therefore, PKR could be a pharmacological target for treating systemic inflammation-induced neuroinflammation and cognitive dysfunction.

17123217.label: Major findings and research outcome
17123217.value: For objective 1, we demonstrated a significant increase in the number of vessel-associated macrophages in the frontal cortex following laparotomy. These macrophages could be recruited from the peripheral system or various brain regions, including but not limited to the choroid plexus and perivascular space. Vessel-associated macrophages may infiltrate into the brain to help the resident microglia in removing undesired debris and dead cells. Additionally, by using the flow cytometry, we found that laparotomy could induce a notable increase in the number of GFP-containing macrophages in both the frontal cortex and hippocampus of the C57BL/6-Tg(CD68-EGFP)1Drg/J mice. This suggests the potential infiltration of the macrophages into the brain after laparotomy. In this part of the study, different behavioral tests were also performed. Cognitive impairment was observed in wild-type mice following laparotomy in terms of the decline in problem-solving abilities, impaired short-term and long-term memory in the puzzle box test; reduced recognition memory with a lower discrimination index in the novel object recognition test; and impaired spatial working memory with the reduced percentage of alteration in the spontaneous Y-maze. For objective 2, we elucidated the roles of PKR in modulating systemic inflammation-induced neuroinflammation. By genetic knockout of PKR in mice, it ameliorated the laparotomy-induced activation of microglia and neuroinflammation with downregulation of the increased IL-1β expression induced by laparotomy in both the liver and frontal cortex at 4 h and day 1 after the surgery. Meanwhile, knockout of PKR significantly reduced the laparotomy-induced tau protein phosphorylation (AT8 and pS416) and elevated COX-2 level in the frontal cortex. Furthermore, in wild-type mice, cognitive impairment was observed following laparotomy; while for PKR-KO mice, cognitive flexibility, spatial working memory, short-term and long-term memory remained intact after laparotomy. For objective 3, our study demonstrated the role of PKR in cholinergic neurons in regulating glucose metabolism and cognitive functions in the laparotomy model. Based on behavioral tests, blocking PKR in cholinergic neurons alleviated laparotomy-induced impairment of spatial working memory, short-term memory, and problem-solving ability, without affecting the motor activity. After evaluation of cognition, brain glucose metabolism was further investigated by metabolomics. This allowed us to detect minor changes which can reflect the changes in brain functions. We detected that laparotomy led to glucose hypometabolism, which is a common hallmark of various neurodegenerative diseases in the preclinical stages including AD and PD. By blocking PKR in cholinergic neurons, laparotomy-induced changes in glucose metabolism could be rescued in the frontal cortex.

17123217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17123217.value: In this study, we demonstrated that laparotomy induces both systemic inflammation and neuroinflammation in the adult, wild-type mouse model. Meanwhile, knockout of PKR alleviates both peripheral and neural inflammation followed by laparotomy. In reality, patients may be exposed to multiple surgeries or suffered from chronic inflammation (e.g., autoimmune disorders and metabolic disorders). All these factors affect immune responses. Further study can be performed on studying how PKR affects immune priming or immune tolerance. We found that PKR in neurons influences glucose metabolism and cognitive functions. The role of PKR in regulating neuronal metabolism deserves further study. PKR has been demonstrated to play a critical role in body metabolism. In obese mouse models, inhibition of PKR improves glucose intolerance and enhances insulin sensitivity. Additionally, PKR could form a complex with TRBP and subsequently activate JNK. Meanwhile, inhibiting TRBP in the liver could improve insulin resistance, glucose tolerance, and glucose metabolism and reduce inflammation in the obese mice. Given the TRBP-PKR interaction in the liver is critical for regulating metabolism and inflammatory signaling, the TRBP-PKR interaction in the neuron may also play an essential role in neuronal metabolism. Future studies can be focused on how PKR influences glucose metabolism in neurons.

17123217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17123217.value: Alzheimer's disease is a chronic neurodegenerative disease that slowly destroys patients’ memory. There is not a single cause of Alzheimer's disease. Different factors including genetics, lifestyle, and environment can contribute to Alzheimer's disease. Inflammation can also affect the development of Alzheimer's disease. Perioperative neurocognitive disorder describes a decline in a patient’s cognitive ability following surgery. Here, we used laparotomy, as an experimental model to induce systemic inflammation and study how it affects neuroinflammation and cognitive function. In this study, we have found that a signaling molecule, PKR, is involved in regulating both systemic inflammation and neuroinflammation. Moreover, we have also demonstrated the role of PKR in neurons in affecting glucose metabolism and brain functions. Understanding the role of PKR in manipulating systemic inflammation, neuroinflammation, and cognition helps us to develop a new therapy approach for combating neuroinflammation and Alzheimer's disease.

17123517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17123517.value: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a female-biased autoimmune disorder which primarily being considered as a disease effected by dysregulation of autoreactive T and B lymphocytes. Multiple genome-wide association studies have discovered a myriad of genetic risk loci for SLE, revealing the pathological components from innate immunity. Inflammasome is an innate immune response triggered by harmful stimuli derived from invading pathogens as well as endogenous molecules associated with cellular damage and cell death, which are the major sources of autoantigens fueling SLE development. Inflammasome activation results in the maturation and secretion of proinflammatory cytokines IL-1β and IL-18, and increased levels of these cytokines have been reported in SLE patients. Thus, inflammasome likely plays an important role in SLE pathogenesis. In this project, we will perform comprehensive characterization of the dysregulated AIM2 inflammasome components in correlation with clinical manifestations in SLE patients. We will further examine the mechanistic relationship between type I interferon and inflammasome activation in SLE disease by both expression and functional analyses on biological samples from patients and healthy volunteers. Findings from this study would add new knowledge in comprehending inflammasome regulation and teasing out its contribution to lupus disease.

17123517.label: Realisation of objectives
17123517.value: For research objective 1: to fully characterize the dysregulated AIM2 inflammasome response in correlation with SLE disease, the study was designed to evaluate (I) the expression of inflammasome components; and (II) inflammasome functional activity in correlation with SLE disease status and parameters. Both of these sub-sections were fully realized and addressed in the first progress report. In brief, we found significant upregulated expression in inflammasome components including AIM2, NLRP3, ASC, CASP1 in monocytes of SLE patients. Specifically, we focused on AIM2 inflammasome and the identified a significant correlation of AIM2 expression in patients with medium SLE disease activity of SELENA-SLEDAI score of 1-5. Significant correlations with interferon (IFN) activities were also observed. In terms of functional inflammasome responses, significant elevated AIM2-induced IL-1beta and IL-18 cytokines production in SLE monocytes was found. Sera from SLE patients were able to mediate enhanced AIM2 functional responses in monocytes. Collectively, we generated data to support our working hypothesis that dysregulated monocyte AIM2 expression and functions are associated with SLE disease in patients. For research objective 2; to elucidate miRNA regulatory mechanism that contributes to type I IFN mediated AIM2 inflammasome dysregulation in SLE monocytes, we employed RNA sequencing to detect both miRNA and mRNA levels in monocytes stimulated with type I interferon and SLE patient sera. Bioinformatics analyses revealed four potential miRNA candidates. However, validation analyses using an independent set of samples however did not yield consistent miRNA targets and we therefore sought to look for alternative regulatory mechanism. We then tried to study regulatory mechanism at two different levels. First, we looked for alternative epigenetic regulatory mechanism by examining the methylation status of the AIM2 promoter. No significant difference could be found between the two experimental groups. Second, we looked for transcriptional regulatory elements. Using mRNA sequencing data, we performed bioinformatics analyses to study pathway and reactome enrichment in relation to AIM2 and type I IFN. We identified several transcription factors that might regulate AIM2 expression and response. We then revised our hypothesis that type I IFN mediates AIM2 responses through the transcriptional factor STAT1, STAT2 and IRF9. We then successfully proved this hypothesis by (i) expression evaluation of these transcription factors in patient samples and healthy controls using independent set of samples, and observed over-expressions of STAT1 and STAT2 but not IRF9 in SLE monocytes; (ii) western blot analysis to show elevated STAT1 and STAT2 phosphorylation, and hence functional activities in SLE monocytes; (iii) chromatin-immunoprecipitation (Ch-IP) analysis and proved that STAT1 and STAT2 were recruited to specific interferon-sensitive responsive element (ISRE) to AIM2 gene promoter region to mediate higher AIM2 expression. In summary, objective 2 was also fully achieved and we have identified the underlying regulatory mechanism that is responsible for mediating type I IFN induced AIM2 dysregulated functions in SLE monocytes.

17123517.label: Major findings and research outcome
17123517.value: Pertaining to the two key research objectives, several major findings and research outcome were summarized below. 1. Significant upregulated expression in inflammasome components including AIM2, NLRP3, ASC, CASP1 were found in monocytes of SLE patients. Specifically, significant correlation of AIM2 expression with medium SLE disease activity and interferon gene signature was observed. 2. Functionally, SLE monocytes showed heightened AIM2 inflammasome response in producing inflammatory cytokines IL-1beta and IL-18. 3. The dysregulated AIM2 inflammasome response in patients can be attributed to the elevated circulating type I interferon in SLE patients Collective findings 1-3 were reported as poster presentation in 23rd and 24th Medical Research Conference (Hong Kong, 2018 and 2019) and in World Immune Regulation Meeting XIII (Davos, Switzerland, 2019) 4. Expression of transcription factors STAT1, STAT2 and IRF9 were significantly elevated in monocytes cultured with SLE plasma or type I IFN, and showed positive correlation with AIM2 expression. 5. SLE monocytes also expressed elevated levels of total STAT1, STAT2 as well as their phosphorylated forms. 6. Mechanistically, type I IFN could promote binding of phosphorylated STAT1 and STAT2 to specific interferon-sensitive element in the AIM2 gene promoter region, thereby enhancing the expression and hence the functions of AIM2 in SLE patients. Collective findings 4-5 were reported in oral presentation in 17th International Congress in Immunology (Beijing, China, 2019) and in 25th Medical Research Conference (Hong Kong, 2021) Findings 1-6 were used to prepare a manuscript titled “Circulatory type I interferons promote AIM2 inflammasome dysregulation in monocytes of SLE patients via STAT1 and STAT2” which will be submitted to international peer-reviewed journal for consideration of publication in early 2022. A draft of the manuscript is attached.

17123517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17123517.value: In this study, we elucidated the mechanism to account for the dysregulated AIM2 inflammasome response observed in SLE patients. A functional link is established between the pathogenic type I interferon and inflammasome function by in vitro method. This project has been expanded to evaluate its impact in SLE disease development and progression using in vivo animal model. Additionally, AIM2 is also expressed by other adaptive immune cells including T and B cells, and its impact in SLE and other diseases (e.g. cancers) has not been fully explored. Along these two different directions, we have already started on-going collaboration with Prof Qianjin Lu’s team in The Second Xiangya Hospital of Central South University, Changsha, China. Specifically arising from this study, we are currently evaluating the role of AIM2 in monocytes in promoting disease in a lupus mouse models with pending results. Taken together, we aim to study AIM2 as a disease modifying molecule which can be further explored as therapeutic target for SLE management.

17123517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17123517.value: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is the most complicated autoimmune condition that primarily affects females of child-bearing age with clinical manifestations in multiple organs. Its pathogenesis is not completely clear and there is a lack of effective target-specific therapeutics in treating SLE patients. Recent discoveries reveal critical pathological components from innate immunity. In this study, we have unravelled the role of AIM2 inflammasome in contributing immune dysregulation in SLE patients. AIM2 inflammasome is a part of the innate immune system that senses danger signal in form DNA released in cell death, which is a major source of stimuli fuelling SLE development. Our findings showed that circulating immune cells from SLE patients had elevated AIM2 expression and secreted higher levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-1beta/IL-18 that cause cell damages. Such dysregulated AIM2 inflammasome response was caused by another key inflammatory cytokine, type I interferon. The mechanism accounting for the dysregulated functional association between type I interferon--AIM2--IL-1beta/IL-18 in SLE patients was also delineated. These findings have added new knowledge in comprehending inflammasome regulation and teasing out its contribution to lupus disease. AIM2 can be further explored as a potential target for developing new therapeutics for SLE management.

17123717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17123717.value: Associating liver partition and portal vein ligation for staged hepatectomy (ALPPS) has been recently introduced as a novel procedure to augment future liver remnant (FLR) in patients with marginal liver volume contemplating for major hepatectomy. Early experience of ALPPS has been hampered by the high incidence of postoperative complications and the high incidence of mortality. With cumulative experience and modification of operative techniques, the short-term outcomes of ALPPS have improved. Recently, we have published our experience in a cohort of 17 patients. The median gain in FLR volume was 48.7% over a median of 6 days. The morbidity and mortality rate was 11.8% and 5.9% respectively, much lower than that reported in the International ALPPS Registry. As the short-term outcome of ALPPS procedure for HCC has been confirmed, the next pertinent question would be its potential effect on the tumor biological behaviour and its long-term oncological outcome. The rationale for the study of any possible change in the tumor biological behavior induced by ALPPS was based on the fact that after right portal vein ligation during stage I of ALPPS, the function and viability of right liver became solely dependent on the right hepatic artery. Intraoperative Doppler ultrasound in fact showed increased flow signal in the right hepatic artery after stage I ALPPS. Since it is known that 80% of the tumor blood supply is derived from the hepatic arterial system, it is not known if the enhanced hepatic arterial flow within the next 7-10 days after stage I ALPPS would enhance tumor growth, and eventually affect the tumor aggressiveness that would increase tumor recurrence rate. In order to evaluate this issue, our study will be divided into two parts: the first part is to evaluate the oncological outcome of ALPPS in comparison with upfront conventional hepatectomy based on three parameters: tumor recurrence rate, overall survival, and serum levels of prognostic-related biomarkers; the second part will focus on the effect of ALPPS on tumor behaviour based on changes in tumor size before and after stage I ALPPS, and the utilisation of rat models to study the expression of tumor-related biomarkers before and after stage I ALPPS. Our objective is to define the oncological effects of ALPPS, if any, on the outcome of HCC after resections via clinical and animal models. 「大範圍肝切除」往往因病人的未來餘肝或會不足而受制，而近來備受關注的「聯合肝臟離斷和門靜脈結紮的二步肝切除術」(一般簡稱ALPPS) 正是一項新穎的針對方案：切肝前先增大未來餘肝。ALPPS實行之初，併發症率和死亡率俱偏高，難以推廣。然而，隨著經驗的累積和技術的調整，其短期成果已有所改善。 最近我們發表了一組病人接受了ALPPS的結果。在這17名病人中，未來餘肝在 6天 (中位數) 內增大了48.7% (中位數)，併發症率為11.8%，死亡率5.9%。這併發症率和死亡率遠低於 International ALPPS Registry 的紀錄。 ALPPS應用於肝癌治療的短期成果如今已確知，接著的問題就是ALPPS對「腫瘤生物學行為」和「腫瘤控制之長期成果」的潛在影響。在ALPPS的第一步手術中，右門脈被結紮，這使右肝的生存和功能完全依賴右肝動脈。「ALPPS對肝腫瘤的生物學行為的改變」這一課題正是奠基於此。事實上，術中多普勒超聲顯示，ALPPS第一步手術後，右肝動脈血流增加。肝腫瘤的血供八成來自肝動脈系統，但未知ALPPS第一步手術後的7-10天中增強了的肝動脈血流會否助長腫瘤生長，進而加強其侵略性，提高腫瘤復發率。今次的研究，就是要解答這疑問。 是項研究分為兩部份。第一部份：比較ALPPS和常規直接肝切除的腫瘤控制成果。從三方面作比對：腫瘤復發率、整體生存率、與預後相關的生物標記在血清的水平。第二部份：檢視腫瘤大小在ALPPS第一步手術前和後之分別，以評估ALPPS對腫瘤行為的影響，另設大鼠模型，比對與腫瘤相關的生物標記在ALPPS第一步手術前和後之表達。我們的目的是運用臨床和動物模型，釐清ALPPS會否以及如何影響肝腫瘤的行為以至肝癌切除的治療成果。

17123717.label: Major findings and research outcome
17123717.value: From 2002 to 2018, 148 patients with HCC (hepatitis B: n ¼ 136, 92.0%) underwent FLR modulation (ALPPS, n ¼ 46; PVE: n ¼ 102). One patient with ALPPS and 33 patients with PVE failed to proceed to resection (resection rate: 97.8% vs 67.7%, P < 0.001). Among those who had resections, 65 patients (56.5%) had cirrhosis. ALPPS induced absolute FLR volume increment by 48.8%, or FLR estimated total liver volume ratio by 12.8% over 6 days. No difference in morbidity (20.7% vs 30.4%, P ¼ 0.159) and mortality (6.5% vs 5.8%, P ¼ 1.000) with PVE was observed. Chronic hepatitis and intraoperative indocyanine green clearance rate 39.5% favored adequate FLR hypertrophy in ALPPS. Five-year overall survival for ALPPS and PVE was 46.8% and 64.1% (P ¼ 0.234). Tumor immunohistochemical staining showed no difference in expression of PD-1, V-EGF, and AFP between ALPPS, PVE, and UH.
