17124017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17124017.value: Recent genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have contributed important insights into the genetic architecture of common diseases. However, the sequence variants studied to date collectively explain only a modest proportion of the overall heritability, even for the best-studied diseases. The most likely contributors to this "missing heritability" are sequence variants that have escaped detection because of their rarity or small effect size. As exome-sequencing (or whole-genome sequencing) studies with sample sizes comparable to those of current GWAS consortia become feasible, the true contribution of rare single nucleotide variants (SNVs) to complex diseases will begin to be revealed. However, the statistical testing of rare variants for association with complex diseases is challenging because of their low expected frequencies in cases and controls. The aggregation of the rare variants within a gene has been suggested as a way to increase statistical power. A variety of gene-based statistical tests for rare variants have been proposed, but a limitation of these tests is their lack of consideration of functional information. One overlooked biological aspect is that risk variants may cluster in particular regions of the gene that are critical for the gene product’s structure or regulation. Therefore, we propose a novel rare-variant association test based on the difference between cases and controls in the distribution of rare variants within the gene. The new test is orthogonal to existing tests that assess excess of rare variance in cases versus controls, and can therefore be combined with them to enhance statistical power. The proposed method is based on the two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test (KS) for equality of empirical cumulative distribution functions of the positions of rare variants found in cases and controls, with modifications to overcome potential problems such as violation of assumptions and population stratification. In addition we propose a potentially more powerful version of the KS test by incorporating functional information. Using bioinformatic predictions of the potential deleteriousness of all possible sequence changes at each nucleotide position within a gene, we will score each position for potential deleteriousness. We will then re-order the nucleotide positions in ascending order of potential deleteriousness, and apply the KS test to compare the rare variant distribution in cases versus controls on this reordered basis. The reordering should increase the discrepancy between the empirical distribution functions of cases and controls, and therefore increase the power of the test. The methods will be implemented in freely available computer software. 近年來全基因組關聯分析（GWAS）研究為常見疾病的基因遺傳結構提供了重要的方向。然而目前已知之序列變異，即使在已被深入研究的疾病中，僅能解釋部分的遺傳度。關鍵可能是由於罕見的序列變異尚難以檢測或序列變異的效應值過小。不過，外顯子序列（或全基因組序列）研究的樣本數已可逐漸與現時的GWAS聯盟媲美，罕見單核苷酸變異（SNVs）影響複雜疾病的真正成因亦會逐漸揭露。 然而，因為病例及對照組的預期頻率過低，使複雜疾病相關的罕見序列變異之統計分析具有一定的挑戰性 。因此，目前已提出了一系列以基因為基礎的統計測試，從而集中單一基因中的罕見變異來提高統計檢定力，但目前這些測試的限制在於它們缺乏對生物體功能信息的考量。一個常被忽視的生物學上觀點是，高風險序列變異有機會結集在特定的基因區域 ，從而影響著基因產物的結構或調節系統。因此，根據病例和對照組之間罕見變異的組成分佈，我們提出了一種嶄新的罕見序列變異關聯檢測方法。新檢驗方法能承繼現有檢驗方法中，評估病例具有過多於與對照組的罕見變異情況並同時考慮上述生物學因素，因而提高統計檢定力。本研究所提出的方法是基於雙樣本Kolmogorov-Smirnov測試（KS），對病例和對照組之間罕見變異的位置以及經驗累積分佈函數進行檢驗，並針對是否違反假設和人口分層進行修改。 另外，我們提出一個透過整合功能性信息的KS測試，使之有機會成為更有效之方法。使用生物信息學預測在單一基因內每個核苷酸位置中所有可能的潛在有害性序列變化，並針對每個位置評估其潛在的有害性。然後，我們將核苷酸位置的潛在有害性重新排列，並應用KS測試在重新排序的基礎上來比較病例和對照組的罕見變異分佈。重新排序應可增加病例和對照組的經驗分佈函數之間的差異，從而增加測試的檢定力，而這些方法會將其建置於免費軟體中。

17124017.label: Major findings and research outcome
17124017.value: (1) We showed that haplotypes of multiple genomic variants can control gene expression (eQTL haplotypes) and influence complex disease risk. We further developed a method for detecting eQTL haplotypes and testing them for association with disease (Research Output 1) (2) We developed the KS test and combined KS-burden test for association analysis of rare variants, and showed by simulation that these tests were powerful for detecting rare variant association, especially for large genes. (Research Output 2). (3) We detected significant rare variant association for treatment response in schizophrenia, specifically in genes involved in glutamatergic synaptic function (Research Output 3). This suggests genetic heterogeneity in schizophrenia affecting neurotransmitter imbalance and the response to dopamine antagonists (Research Output 3) (4) We developed a new statistical framework for association testing of cancer-driver mutations. This method uses an iterative regression modelling approach to calculate background mutation counts. We showed that this results in greater statistical power, and enable cancer driver genes to be identified even in small samples. (5) We developed an application for the use of results of genetic association tests, by which the tissue that drive disease occurrence can be inferred. Using this methodology, we identified the frontal and anterior cingulate cortices to be the driver tissues for schizophrenia and bipolar disorder, and the cerebellar cortex to be an additional driver tissue for bipolar disorder. These findings converge with results from brain imaging studies (Research Output 5). (6) We developed a simple transformation for the effect size of a genetic variant calculated from a logistic regression model to approximate its effect size on the liability scale. This transformation unifies different measures of effect size and simplify the interpretation of association analysis results (Research Output 6).

17124017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17124017.value: There is potential for further refinement of the methodologies that have been developed, as well as application to real datasets. We are currently performing rare variant association analysis on a number of diseases, including schizophrenia, Hirschsprung disease and biliary atresia.

17124017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17124017.value: The genome contain sites that show differences in few (under 1%) individuals. Such rare variation are known to affect gene function and contribute to the development of disease. However, the detection of rare variants associated with disease is challenging because of their low frequency in the population. In this project, we have developed several novel approaches to rare variant association testing, in particular the KS test which assesses uneven distribution of variants within a gene. We showed that this test, when combined with a test which assesses the overall increase in variants within a gene, is powerful for detecting rare variant association. In addition, we also showed that patients with schizophrenia who have rare variants in the genes involved in a particular neural transmitter, glutamate, are more likely to respond poorly to current anti-psychotic drugs. This has important implications for further research to understand the differences among patients with schizophrenia and how to optimise treatment for individual patients according to their genetic profile and underlying disease mechanisms.

17124117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17124117.value: Cell, the most basic unit of living organism is small in size, but is vibrant in many aspects. Enclosed by lipid bilayer plasma membranes, cells synthesize important proteins and lipids and utilize them to orchestrate a wide variety of functions. For example, F-actin cytoskeleton network and myosin play a vital role in how cells migrate, adhere, and assemble the tissue. F-actin, the microfilament polymerized by actin monomer, is a highly dynamic three-dimensional network. One of the key factors to regulate F-actin network is the rare species of phosphatidylinositol lipids on the plasma membrane. Membrane-associated myosin-1 can interact with these rare phosphatidylinositol lipids, move along F-actin tracks, and organize F-actin organization. In ill cells, misregulated myosin-1 often unable to perform their regular function and result in diseases. Particularly, myosin-1e (MYO1E) has linked to various diseases, such as breast cancer development and immune cells dysfunction. In addition, mutated MYO1E that lacks tail domains causes impaired F-actin assembly in the kidney cells. Cell adhesion, such as podosome is one of the best cellular structures to study the functional role of MYO1E. Podosome is rich in phosphatidylinositol lipid PIP3, and MYO1E is the only myosin-1 isoform participating in the podosome. We have recently found that inhibition of MYO1E by RNA interference can largely suppress podosome formation in macrophage cells, and the tail domain of MYO1E controls phosphatidylinositol lipid binding. Moreover, the oligomerization of wild type MYO1E tail occurs before F-actin polymerization at the podosome, while lipid-binding mutant does not. This indicates that MYO1E utilize the tail domain to exploit and deliver upstream lipid-based stimulus to downstream effectors. Based on these preliminary findings, we aim to reveal how MYO1E tail domain interacts with phosphatidylinositol lipid and regulates F-actin polymerization in live cells. In addition, we will also reveal the functional role of MYO1E in releasing matrix degradation enzymes at the podosome. Regulation of extracellular matrix integrity is a critical factor in cancer development. With our expertise in adhesion signaling, we will apply modern molecular cell biological approaches, advanced high-resolution fluorescence microscopy techniques, and quantitative imaging analysis to carry out the scientific investigation. Taking together, our finding will provide a better understanding of cell biological mechanisms in MYO1E-related diseases. Pharmaceutical and biotech industries will be potentially interested in applying our findings to develop new compounds and technologies to ameliorate patient’s condition.

17124117.label: Realisation of objectives
17124117.value: Summary of the investigation: In this investigation, we combine quantitative fluorescence microscopy and molecular biology to reveal the mechanistic role of myosin1e at the podosome. In particular, we find that myosin1e concentrates at the ventral layer of the podosome where the protrusive F-actin polymerization takes place. The C-terminal tail domain of myosin1e specifically binds to PI(3,4,5)P3 lipids on the plasma membrane and acts as the critical factor to convert phosphatidylinositol signals to cytoskeleton assembly. We carefully examine the functional role of myosin1e in both macrophage podosome (RAW264.7 cell) and cancer invadopodium (MEF-Src and A375 melanoma cells) and find that the TH12 domain within truncated myosin1e tail is the key motif to bind to PI(3,4,5)P3 lipids. Blocking the phosphatidylinositol signals by overexpression TH12 domain impedes the N-WASP and Arp2/3 mediated F-actin polymerization and suppresses the assembly of podosome. We find that the C-terminal tail domain, rather than N-terminal ATPase motor domain, contribute to membrane binding of myosin1e. The C-terminal tail of myosin1e is comprised of TH1, TH2, and TH3 domain. We further examine the membrane association of each myosin1e tail domain by quantitative fluorescence microscopy [Part C, #7, Figure 3]. We found that TH12 (TH1 and TH2 combined) are enriched on the plasma membrane, while individual TH1, TH2, TH3, and TH23 are not. TH12 with KR2A mutations (TH12 KR2A, K772 and R782 of full-length myosin1e both mutated to alanine) fail to be recruited to the plasma membrane. Reduction of PI(4,5)P2 on the plasma membrane by phospholipase C activator m-3M3FBS (5 mg/ml) causes a prominent dissociation of TH12 from the plasma membrane. It is known that PI3K activation triggered by epidermal growth factor (EGF) can cause the production of PI(3,4,5)P3 lipids on the plasma membrane. In live cells, we find that the level of TH12 on the plasma membrane increases upon EGF stimulation (100 ng/ml). The level of TH12 subsequently returns to the pre-stimulated level after PI3K inhibitor Wortmannin (200 nM) is introduced. It appears that TH12 of myosin1e is the key domain to interact with both PI(4,5)P2 and PI(3,4,5)P3 lipids on the plasma membrane. Therefore, we have achieved the investigation of Objective 1. [Objective 2] Determine the role of MYO1E in F-actin polymerization and matrix degradation at the podosome. Percentage of completion: 100%. We utilize phosphatidylinositol species-specific probes and find that PI(3,4,5)P3 (marked by PH-BTK), rather than PI(4,5)P2 (marked by PH-PLCdelta), are locally enriched at the podosome [Part C, #7, Figure 2B]. It is known that negatively charged phosphatidylinositol, such as PI(3,4,5)P3 lipids, can activate N-WASP and promote F-actin polymerization. We examine whether the interaction between myosin1e’s TH12 domain and PI(3,4,5)P3 alters lipid-mediated F-actin polymerization. When TH12 is introduced, lower levels of PH-BTK and N-WASP at the podosome in TH12 expressing MEF-Src are observed, as compared with lipid-binding mutant TH12 KR2A [Part C, #7, Figure 5]. In addition, the subcellular localization of PH-BTK and TH12 exhibits in a mutual-exclusive pattern. The formation of podosome arc/rosette is suppressed when TH12 is overexpressed. Blocking PI(3,4,5)P3 production by PI3K inhibitor Wortmannin (200 nM) results in similar suppression of podosome arc/rosette formation. We next examine the functional impact of TH12 on the dynamics of F-actin polymerization. In the initial phase of podosome formation, the level of TH12 increases before N-WASP, and the subsequent F-actin polymerization is unstable and short-lived [Part C, #7, Figure 5J]. During the depolymerization phase of F-actin, the level of TH12 persists and subsequently decreases after podosome disassembly. The inhibition of podosome formation by TH12 expression is also validated in other cell types. RAW264.7 macrophages with the expression of TH12 show few numbers of podosomes, as compared with TH12 KR2A [Part C, #7, Figure 6C]. Likewise, A375 melanoma cells can degrade extracellular matrices in proximity by forming the invadopodium, which exhibits similar cytoskeletal components as the podosome. In TH12-expressing A375 cells, invadopodium formation is suppressed, and the area of degraded gelatin is significantly decreased [Part C, #7, Figure 7D]. It appears that TH12 blocks the upstream PI(3,4,5)P3 signals, suppresses F-actin polymerization, and impedes matrix degradation. Therefore, we have also achieved the investigation of Objective 2.

17124117.label: Major findings and research outcome
17124117.value: Podosomes are integrin-mediated adhesions with distinct three-dimensional F-actin organization. The regulation of F-actin polymerization plays a critical role in podosome assembly. Here, we quantitatively examine axial distributions of F-actin-binding proteins and find that myosin1e is uniquely enriched at the ventral layer of the podosome. We also utilize photoconversions of mEOS2-actin and demonstrate that F-actin polymerization takes place in the ventral layer of the podosome. We further identify that C-terminal tail domain, rather than N-terminal ATPase domain, plays the critical role of myosin1e’s spatiotemporal distribution at the podosome. In particular, TH12 domain of myosin1e is the key membrane binding motif and orchestrates F-actin polymerization and cell migration. These results have been published in a peer-reviewed journal [Part C, #7], and here are the major findings. 1) Myosin1e is specifically enriched at the ventral layer of the podosome 2) F-actin polymerizes from the ventral layer of the podosome 3) PI(3,4,5)P3 lipids recruit myosin1e to the podosome 4) Myosin1e’sTH12 domain is the key motif responsible for plasma membrane association 5) TH12 defines spatiotemporal dynamics of myosin1e at the ventral layer of podosome 6) TH12-PI(3,4,5)P3 interaction hinders F-actin polymerization and podosome arc formation 7) TH12 suppresses podosome formation in RAW264.7 macrophages and matrix degradation in A375 melanoma cells

17124117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17124117.value: Myosin1e plays critical roles in various human diseases. The high expression level of myosin1e is associated with the decreased survival in patients with basal breast cancer (Hallett et al., 2012). Loss of myosin1e delays breast tumor progression and suppresses lung metastasis (Ouderkirk-Pecone et al., 2016). In addition, mutations of myosin1e, including mutations at A159P, T119I, or Y695X, have been discovered in various human diseases related to steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome (Mele et al., 2011; Al-Hamed et al., 2013). Podocytes with myosin1e mutations exhibit disruptions of membrane integrity in the glomerulus and cause protein leakages into the urine. Particularly, Y695X mutation results in loss of myosin1e tail domain. Here, our study reveals the mechanistic role of myosin1e tail domains in orchestrating the lipid-cytoskeleton interaction. We find that myosin1e is stably enriched at the ventral layer of the podosome and interacts with PI(3,4,5)P3 lipids via its TH12 domain. Further studies are required to extend these findings to other physiological functions of myosin1e, including motor activation, cargo recognition, and adhesion regulation.

17124117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17124117.value: Cytoskeletons are the dynamic framework and support many important cellular activities. In particular, actin are the building block of F-actin network that orchestrates cell migration and tissue regeneration. Myosin1e is one of the key regulator on the cell membrane and controls the dynamic organization of F-actin network. Here, we dissect of the molecular function of myosin1e in invasive podosomes that are often identified in metastatic cancer cells and macrophages. We find that carboxyl-terminal tail domain, rather than amino-terminal ATPase domain, is responsible for the spatiotemporal distribution of myosin1e at the podosome. Specifically, TH12 domain in myosin1e’s carboxyl-terminus is the key membrane binding motif. Further investigation suggests that TH12 domain can block the upstream PI(3,4,5)P3 signals, suppress F-actin polymerization, and impede invasive cell migration. Mutations of myosin1e are involved in various human diseases, including breast cancer and steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome. Thus, our investigation reveals the molecular basis of myosin1e’s function and sheds light on the innovation in the pharmaceutical development to treat myosin1e-related diseases.

17124317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17124317.value: 在過去幾十年中，甲型流感病毒感染引致數百萬人死亡。雖然有效的疫苗可用於保護季節性流感，但甲型流感病毒通過抗原性轉移和抗原漂移不斷進行變化，籍此逃避我們的免疫系統所控制。因此通過深入理解病毒與宿主之間的相互作用從而研發新抗病毒藥物或疫苗，才能加強控制甲型流感病毒感染。 先天免疫反應是控制各種呼吸道病毒感染的第一道防線。例如甲型流感病毒，受感染細胞會貞測到病毒RNA，并誘導產生一型或三型干擾素。未感染或已感染的細胞會受干擾素刺激從而開啟抗病毒狀態和控制病毒感染。在這個研究項目中，我們將會全面探討一個受干擾素所刺激的基因，名為IFIRM，以及IFIRM對甲型流感病毒感染的作用。除了研究IFIRM在抑制甲型流感病毒中的分子機制，我們會利用轉基因小鼠模型，確定甲型流感病毒感染過程中IFIRM的生理作用。總而言之，這個研究將揭示一個病毒與宿主相互作用的新機制，從而為控制甲型流感病毒感染提供重要基本知識。

17124317.label: Realisation of objectives
17124317.value: Objective 1 To examine the functional role of IFIRM during influenza A virus infection As stated in the proposal, we completed 1.1 Generation of tetracycline-inducible IFIRM cells and IFIRM-knockout cells and 1.2 Evaluation of the antiviral potential of IFIRM during influenza A virus infection. (Data were presented in the Figure 1 and 2 of the attached manuscript) Objective 2 To dissect the antiviral mechanism of IFIRM during influenza A virus infection As stated in the proposal, we completed 2.1 Determination of the interaction between IFIRM, YTHDF proteins and viral RNA and 2.2 Assessment of the regulatory role of IFIRM in viral mRNA translation and/or stability. (Data were presented in the Figure 3, 4 and 5 of the attached manuscript) Objective 3 To determine the physiological role of IFIRM during influenza A virus infection We proposed to generate IFIRM transgenic mouse for the study of 3.1 Examination of influenza A virus replication; and 3.2 Evaluation of influenza A virus pathogenicity. However, the IFIRM transgenesis was lethal to the mouse. With the help of transgenic core facility, University of Hong Kong, pronuclei microinjection of IFIRM expression construct was successful but at the very low successful rate. We further repeated another two rounds of pronuclei microinjection and the successful rate of transgenesis was still very low. The successfulness of transgenesis was determined by quantitation of integration of IFIRM cascade in mouse genome (classical method). After we accumulated enough IFIRM positive mice for setting up the breeding colonies, a pilot infection experiment was carried out as proposed. However, no significant difference of lung viral load, disease scores or pathogenesis was observed between wild-type PR8 and m6A-null HA PR8; as well as between wild-type mice and IFIRM transgenic mice. This was unexpected and we further validated the protein expression of IFIRM in IFIRM-positive transgenic mouse. We figured out there was no IFIRM transgene protein expression in mouse lung but they were IFIRM transgene integration, possibly defective in protein expression. One of the possible reason for this observation is that IFIRM transgene is embryonic lethal to the mouse, and this can explain why the successful rate of the transgenesis in several attempts was very low. The overall time spent on this part was over a year.

17124317.value: Through the examination of IFIRM expression in various human tissues and cancer cell-lines, we found that IFIRM expression was lost in almost all cancer cell-lines (As exemplified in Figure 1D and E of the attached manuscript). We further proposed that IFIRM may be a tumor suppressor gene and have proved this using other cancer cell models. 17124317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17124317.value: C19orf66 (also known as RyDEN, IRAV, SHFL) is an interferon-stimulated gene that has been shown to suppress various virus infections, including dengue virus, Zika virus and human immunodeficiency virus. Here, we revealed a novel regulatory mechanism that c19orf66 restricts influenza A virus (IAV) infection in a m6A-dependent manner, and hence named as interferon-inducible regulator of m6A (IFIRM). We demonstrated that IFIRM suppressed the replications and viral protein expressions of heterologous IAV strains. We also showed that IFIRM directly and primarily bound to viral mRNA, but less to vRNA, and with a preference to m6A-RNAs. Through proteomic analysis, we identified that IFIRM associated with several key m6A readers including YTHDF1/2/3 and IGF2BP1/2/3. Knockout of the key player of m6A writer METTL3 in cells abolished the inhibitory effect of IFIRM on IAV infection. A mutant IAV with HA segment lacking m6A was less prone to the IFIRM suppressive effect. Taken together, our data indicated a new role of IFIRM in suppressing IAV replication in a m6A-dependent manner, possibly through the regulation of viral mRNAs and m6A machinery.

17124717.label: Realisation of objectives
17124717.value: O1. Comparative metabolomics study on macrophage cells infected with WT TM vs Mp1p knockout strain.(100% achieved) We have performed comparative metabolomics profile study on J774 macrophages infected with wild type (WT) and Mp1p knockout (KO) strains of TM to reveal the biomarkers and pathways affected by Mp1p (Fig. 1). The metabolites were extracted at an infection time point of 30 hours. PLS-DA and T-test statistical analysis indicated that the WT and KO strains could be well distinguished with a list of significantly changed biomarkers. Identified biomarkers and pathways were summarized in Fig. 1. O2. Use site-directed mutagenesis method to weaken the AA binding affinity of Mp1p-LBD2 to probe the effect of altering binding affinity and oligomeric state of Mp1p-LBD2.(100% achieved) We have performed crystal screen on AA bound Mp1p-LBD2 mutants including L264W, I268W, V309D, I328D and I328W. We have successfully obtained the crystals of L264W (Kd=3.1uM), V309D (Kd=3.8uM), I328D (Kd=4.5uM) and I328W (0.2uM) and measured x-ray diffractions on these crystals in the National Synchrotron Radiation Research Center (NSRRC, Taiwan). Figure 2 displays the solved structures of the 4 mutants of Mp1p-LBD2, highlighting the conformation of AA molecules. The mutants on top (V309D and I328D) have similar conformations of AA compared to WT, meaning they do not significantly interfere with the capturing mechanism. However, for the lower two mutants (L264W and I328W), the conformation is significantly changed due to significant steric interference, which is highly pronounced in the case of L264W where the “tail” of AA have been forced out of the core of the protein. Although the binding affinities varies from 0.2 to 4.5 uM between the four mutants, which are significantly weaker than that of WT Mp1p-LBD2 (Kd=13 nM), they all showed a monomeric structure. O3. Solve the solution structure of the apo-Mp1p-LBD2 by NMR methods and to investigate whether it will be a monomeric or dimeric structure.(100% achieved) We have overexpressed and purified 13C15N-Mp1p-LBD2 and carried out a series of NMR experiments including triple resonance experiments HNCACB, CBCA(CO)NH, HNCA, HNCOCA and HNCO for backbone resonance assignment; HCCH-COSY, HCCH-TOCSY experiments for side-chain resonance assignments; and 1H-15N NOESY-HSQC[19], 1H-13C NOESY-HSQC experiments for inter-proton distances measurements. Structure calculations were carried out by the program CNS using simulated annealing restrained molecular dynamics protocols. The program ARIA was used to implement ambiguous distance constraints and to assist the iterative cycles of NOE assignments for structure refinement and solvent solvation. Fig.3A showed the ribbon plot of the best 10 NMR structures of apo form Mp1p-LBD2. The structure showed a well-folded 5-helix bundle structure in monomeric form. O4. Perform backbone dynamics studies of Mp1p-LBD2 to compare the flexibility of apo-Mp1p-LBD2 and ligand bound Mp1p-LBD2.(100% achieved) We have prepared 15N-Mp1p-LBD2 samples in both apo and 1:1 AA bound forms then carried out protein backbone 15N relaxation rates measurements of the longitudinal relaxation time (T1), transverse relaxation time (T2) of backbone 15N nuclei, and the heteronuclear NOE between backbone 15N and the attached 1H were measured by standard Bruker pulse sequences (hsqct1etf2gpsi3d, hsqct2etf2gpsi3d and hsqcnoef2gpsi). using a Bruker Avance 600 MHz NMR spectrometer. Data was processed using CCPNMR analysis to determine T1, T2 and NOE values of each backbone amide. The program ModelFree was used to estimate the order parameters of each residue. Fig. 4 showed the plot of order parameter S2 vs residue number of the apo and 1:1 AA bound forms Mp1p-LBD2. Overall S2 follows the trend of close to 1 at the well-ordered helical regions and significantly lower than 1 at the flexible terminal and loop regions. The third loop (Q59-S65) is relatively longer and more flexible than other shorter loop regions. The overall tumbling correlation time are 8.83 and 8.86 ns, respectively indicating that their effective molecular sizes are similar in solution and compatible with that of a monomeric state. The present backbone dynmics study is supporting that the structure of apo Mp1p-LBD2 single binding domain in solution is a monomer not the dimeric form as seen in the PLM bound form Mp1p-LBD2 reported by X-ray crystallography study previsouly (Fig. 3B PBD 3L1N). O5. Systematic structure and function characterizations of the Mp1p-LBD2 homologue:Mp1p-LBD1.(100% achieved) We have obtained crystals and determined the structures of PLM and AA bound Mp1p-LBD1 as shown in Fig. 5 showing that the Mp1p-LBD1 is similar to Mp1p-LBD2 having a plasticity of bound either one or two AA molecules. We have performed pull-down experiment on TM infected macrophage cell lysate by affinity trapping of His-tagged Mp1p-LBD1. These results indicated that Mp1p-LBD1 is capable of binding various lipid substrates but AA is the dominant ligand in vivo even though AA was the least abundant in the pool of cellular lipids and under limiting bait LBD1 condition (Fig. 6A). The identities of AA, PLM and oleic acid in the pull-down lipid extracts were confirmed by using their pure standards. For example, in negative mode, the peak at m/z 303.2323 and eluted at RT 16.16 min was found to be a significant mass features in all three pull-down extraction samples matches the AA standard (Fig. 6C). The identity of each LPC was not characterized. All LPC ions give rise to the same characteristic fragment ion (m/z = 184.0735) in high energy mode (Collison energy=30-50eV). The general structure and the predicted fragmentation positions were given in the inset of (Fig. 6D). We also carried out isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) to characterize the binding of AA to Mp1p-LBD1. Figure 7 shows the ITC raw heats of binding and isotherms of AA titrated into wild-type Mp1p-LBD1. The isotherm for titration of AA into wild-type Mp1p-LBD1 shows a two-step curve and is best fitted with a two-state model similar to that previously observed in Mp1p-LBD2. Fitting of the ITC isotherm with two-site model gives the first binding site a high affinity Kd of 24 nM while the second binding site has a moderate affinity Kd of 2.3 µM. Compared with Mp1p-LBD2 having 13 nM and 2.3 µM for the first and second AA binding Kd’s (11), respectively, Mp1p-LBD1’s first AA binding Kd is lower but its second AA binding Kd is similar. O6. Determine the full-length Mp1p structure to investigate whether Mp1p-LBD1 and Mp1p-LBD2 interact with each other.(100% achieved) We have obtained crystals and determined the structures of AA bound full-length Mp1p-LBD1-LBD2 as shown in Fig. 8 showing a pseudo-dimeric structure with the dimeric interfaces located at LBD2. The Mp1p-LBD2 domains adopt a domain-swapped open conformation exactly the same as the Mp1p-LBD2 structure in complex with PLM (PDB 3L1N). Despite parallel SLS measurement showed that Mp1p-LBD1-LBD2 remains monomeric in solution regardless of bound ligands, this structure disfavors the explanation that the unusual domain-swapped open conformation of Mp1p-LBD2 is due to crystallization because the two structures, Mp1p-LBD2-PLM (PDB 3L1N) and Mp1p-LBD1-LBD2 both reported here, were crystallized in different conditions and space groups, hence different chemical environments for the ASU. Taken together, these observations suggest a model that Mp1p-LBD2 in full-length Mp1p still adopts an open conformation when not bound to AA in solution. Once bound to the released AA from host’s pro-inflammatory responses, Mp1p-LBD2 undergoes conformational changes to adopt a closed conformation. Mp1p-LBD1 possibly goes through a different mechanism from Mp1p-LBD2 for AA to enter the central cavity as the closed conformation is the only conformation observed so far.

17124717.label: Major findings and research outcome
17124717.value: Dimorphic fungal pathogen Talaromyces (Penicillium) marneffei (TM) is an important cause of systemic mycosis in immunosuppressed or AIDS patients. How this intracellular pathogen evades the host defense of macrophage remains unclear. In our previous GRF project, we have showed that the abundantly secreted Mp1p is a novel virulence factor of TM by performing knockout and knockdown experiments using intracellular survival assay with murine macrophage cells and mice challenge models. We also found that the second ligand binding domain of Mp1p (Mp1p-LBD2) can bind to several proinflammatory lipids. In particular, we discovered that the key proinflammatory lipid mediator, arachidonic acid (AA), is the dominant cellular target of Mp1p-LBD2 by pull-down and immunoprecipitation assays. In this study, we continue our structure and function investigations on Mp1p to better clarify the virulence mechanism of Mp1p. Functionally, we have performed comparative metabolomics profile study on J774 macrophages infected with wild type and Mp1p knockout strains of TM to reveal the biomarkers and pathways affected by Mp1p. Molecularly, we have used NMR spectroscopy, backbone relaxation dynamics methods to showed that Mp1p-LBD2 existed as monomeric form in solution. The weakening of the AA binding affinity by site-directed mutagenesis up to 100 fold still showing crystal structures of AA bound Mp1p mutants of monomeric form. We have also studied the previously uncharacterized LBD1 of Mp1p, Mp1p- LBD1. The crystal structure of Mp1p-LBD1 in complex with copuriﬁed PLM was ﬁrst solved, providing the ﬁrst structural proof that Mp1p-LBD1 is also a fatty acid-binding domain. Pulldown assay with Mp1p-LBD1 further suggested that, similar to the previously characterized Mp1p-LBD2, AA is the dominant physiological target of Mp1p-LBD1. Liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) quantiﬁcation on isolated endogenous full-length Mp1p from an infected murine macrophage cell line showed that the molar ratio of pulled down full-length Mp1p and bound AA is 1 to 4, supporting the idea that both LBDs of Mp1p bind AA molecules in full-length Mp1p in vivo. By X-ray crystallography, NMR titration experiment, and ITC assays, the binding mode of AA molecules in the enclosed hydrophobic cavity of Mp1p-LBD1 was further characterized. The crystal structure of Mp1p-LBD1-LBD2 was also solved, suggesting independence between the two LBDs in a full-length Mp1p monomer. Thus, the present study enhances our understanding of Mp1p, a novel virulence factor of T. marneffei playing a central role in a novel virulence mechanism to target and suppress inﬂammation in hosts.

17124717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17124717.value: Homologous proteins with similar structure and function as Mp1p-LBD1 and Mp1p-LBD2 have been identified in other fungal pathogen such as Afmp1p, Afmp2p and Afmp4p of A. fumigatus. This novel mechanism of host innate immune evasion through capturing of proinflammatory signaling lipid may have a broad implication on fungal and bacterial pathogenesis. Further investigation of Mp1p-LBD1 and Mp1p-LBD2 like proteins in other types of pathogens will be of interest. The knowledge obtained in such work may lead to the development of better chemotherapeutic intervention of related diseases in future.

17124717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17124717.value: Talaromyces marneffei infection causes talaromycosis, a very important opportunistic systematic mycosis in immunocompromised or AIDS patients. In the sera of patients with talaromycosis, Mp1p protein, a secretory galactomannoprotein antigen with two tandem ligand-binding domains (Mp1p-LBD1 and Mp1p-LBD2), was found to be abundant. It was hypothesized that capturing of lipids from human hosts by expressing a large quantity of Mp1p is a virulence mechanism of T. marneffei. It was shown that expression of Mp1p enhanced the intracellular survival of T. marneffei by suppressing proinﬂammatory responses. Mechanistic study of Mp1p-LBD2 suggested that arachidonic acid (AA), a precursor of paracrine signaling molecules for regulation of inﬂammatory responses, is the major physiological target of Mp1p-LBD2. In this study, we used metabolomics, crystallographic, NMR spectroscopy, backbone relaxation dynamics and biochemical techniques to further our investigations on the structure and function of Mp1p. We demonstrated that Mp1p-LBD1 is also a strong AA-binding domain in Mp1p. These studies on Mp1p-LBD1 support the idea that the highly expressed Mp1p is an effective AA-capturing protein. Each Mp1p can bind up to 4 AA molecules. The crystal structure of Mp1p-LBD1-LBD2 has also been solved, showing that both LBDs are likely to function independently with a ﬂexible linker between them.

17125317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17125317.value: Obesity, which represents a major risk factor for a cluster of cardio-metabolic diseases, is caused by the positive energy balance (more energy in than out). While white adipocytes serve to store excess energy, brown adipocytes facilitate energy expenditure by converting ATP production to heat dissipation due to the presence of the unique mitochondrial inner membrane protein uncoupling protein-1 (UCP1) and densely-packed mitochondria in the cells. Besides classical brown adipocytes which are constitutively active and anatomically clustered in specific adipose depots (such as interscapular), another inducible type of brown adipocytes-like cells (named as beige cells) are scattered within white adipose tissue (WAT). A growing body of evidence suggests that enhancing the activity or biogenesis of these two types of brown adipocytes represent a promising therapeutic strategy for obesity and its related medical complications. However, the precise mechanisms that control adaptive thermogenesis in these types of brown adipocytes remain poorly understood. Our recent studies in UCP1-null mice have uncovered a novel thermogenic program in subcutaneous WAT (scWAT) which is controlled by classical brown adipose tissue (cBAT). We found that UCP1-null mice do not have obese phenotype and paradoxically exhibit less adiposity after prolonged feeding with high fat diet (HFD), primarily due to the compensatory elevation of UCP1-independent energy expenditure in sscWAT. These changes in UCP1-null mice are associated with obvious increases in mitochondrial number and activity in scWAT, although the structure and function of mitochondrion in cBAT are obviously impaired. Furthermore, we have identified a number of circulating factors in UCP1-null mice with potential activities to enhance thermogenesis in scWAT. Based on our preliminary data, we propose the existence of a novel cBAT-scWAT regulatory loop controlling thermogenesis and energy expenditure. Ablation of UCP1 causes mitochondrial stress responses in cBAT, leading to the secretion of defense signals (peptide hormones or metabolites) which travels to scWAT and induces UCP1-independent energy expenditure to compensate for dysfunctional BAT. To test this hypothesis and to unravel the underlying mechanisms, we will employ both in vivo and in vitro approaches to characterize cBAT-derived circulating factors mediating the crosstalk between cBAT and scWAT, to elucidate the molecular events on how these factors are produced in cBAT in response to UCP1 depletion and exert thermogenic functions in scWAT. The findings will not only enrich our understanding on biology of brown adipocytes and thermogenesis, but also provide knowledge base for future development of anti-obese therapies by targeting novel thermogenic pathways.

17125317.label: Realisation of objectives
17125317.value: Realization of objective-1: Confirmation of existence of humoral factors in UCP1-null mice mediating UCP1-independent energy utilization: We performed a series of experiments to confirm our hypothesis that interscapular brown adipose tissues (iBAT) from UCP1-deficient mice secreted secrete factors into the bloodstream, which then acts on subcutaneous adipose tissues (scWAT) to induce UCP1-independent thermogenesis. First, we injected serum collected from UCP1-deficient mice into high fat diet (HFD)-fed obese mice for a period of two weeks, followed by measurement of body mass and composition, local temperature with a thermos-camera, whole body energy expenditure (VO2) as well as histological and biochemical analysis of scWAT. Second, we performed parabiosis to surgically combine the circulating system between UCP1-null mice and wild-type (WT) littermates, followed by feeding with HFD, measurement of body weight, fat mass, local and systemic oxygen consumption, browning of scWAT with biochemical and morphological analysis. The results from both approaches demonstrated the existence of serum factors from UCP1-deficient mice which promotes thermogenesis and oxygen consumption in scWAT through a UCP1-independent mechanism, thereby reducing fat mass and body weight. Furthermore, by co-culturing conditioned medium harvested from UCP1-deficient iBAT with mature adipocytes from scWAT, we found that secreted factors from iBAT directly promote oxygen consumption of adipocytes from scWAT. Realization of objective-2: Identification of iBAT-derived secretory factor(s) for remodeling and compensatory energy expenditure in scWAT. We used both hypothesis-driven and omics-based approaches for searching such factors. First, we tested whether fibroblast growth factor (FGF)21, a stress-responsive hormone with thermogenic activities, is one of the iBAT-secreted factors conferring UCP1-independent thermogenesis in sWAT mice. By comparing the expression of FGF21 in different adipose depots and its circulating levels in UCP1-deficient mice and WT controls, we found that FGF21 gene expression is selectively increased in iBAT of UCP1 KO mice by approximately 30 folds, accompanied by ~4 fold elevations in circulating FGF21 compared to WT littermates. Afterwards, we assessed the effects of anti-FGF21 neutralization antibody on the body weight and thermogenesis in UCP1-null mice. Our results showed that neutralization of circulating FGF21 with the antibody exacerbated HFD-induced obesity in UCP1-null mice, but not in WT mice. Such an effect was accompanied by reduced energy expenditure and decreased mitochondrial density and oxygen consumption in scWAT, but not in IBAT. Furthermore, we have discovered a novel role of FGF21 in mediating exercise-induced metabolic benefits by remodeling sWAT. These data suggest that FGF21 is at least partly responsible for mediating the crosstalk between cBAT and sWAT for maintain energy homeostasis Through integrated metabolomics and transcriptomics analysis, we have also identified two additional metabolites and hormones involved in cross-talk between iBAT and scWAT, including hypoxanthine and triiodothyronine (T3). We found that the production of hypoxanthine from iBAT and circulating hypoxanthine were markedly increased UCP1-deficient mice, whilst systemic administration of pharmacological doses of hypoxanthine increased energy expenditire in scWAT of UCP1-null mice through a yet-unknown mechanism. Furthermore, our RNA-seq analysis has identified a marked upregulation of Iodothyronine Deiodinase 2 (Dio2), a key enzyme which catalyze the conversion of thyroid hormone from its inactive form (T4) to active form (T3). Furthermore, we observed a obvious elevation of T3 in UCP1-deficient mice. By developing a nanoparticle delivery system modified with a peptide which selectively target drugs to adipose tissues, we found that selective delivery of T3 to white adipose tissue was sufficient to counteract dietary obesity by inducing browning of scWAT, leading to improved glucose tolerance, insulin sensitivity and reduced vascular inflammation. Thus our findings not only identified three circulating factors (FGF21, hypoxanthine and active T3) which are elevated in response to UCP1 deficiency in iBAT, consequently induce thermogenesis in scWAT. Realization of objective-3: Elucidation of the molecular mechanisms whereby UCP1 deletion alters production of thermogenic factors in classical BAT: Through RNA-seq analysis, we have identified mitochondrial unfolded protein response (UPRmt) pathway as a key downstream effector whereby UCP1 deficiency in cBAT selectively induces the expression of s set of thermogenic factors including FGF21 and Dio2. Both our real-time PCR analysis and Western blots demonstrated upregulation of several UPRmt proteins including chaperones Hsp60, Hsp10, mtDnaJ, MPPβ, Trx2, ClpP, YME1L1 and Tim17A in iBAT of UCP1-deficient mice. In brown adipocytes differentiated from stromal vascular fraction (SVFs) of UCP1-deficient mice, we found that lentiviruses-mediated knockdown of Atfs-1 (the key transcription factor mediating the UPRmt activation) abolished UCP1 deficiency-mediated induction of FGF21 and DIO2, suggesting UPRmt –activated Atfs-1 is responsible for increased FGF21 and Dio2 expression in cBAT. Furthermore, we found perivascular adipose tissues (PVAT) expressed high level of UCP1 thus phenotypically-resembling cBAT, and uncovered a previously unappreciated role and mechanism whereby UCP1 inhibits inflammatory responses by controlling mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP), thus decreasing generation of mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (mtROS) and activation of the NLRP3-inflammasome and caspase-1–mediated maturation of interleukin-1β (IL-1β). In both UCP1-deficient mice and pigs which lack functional UCP1, we obtained a series of evidence showing increased MMP, mtROS, and elevated activation of Caspase-1 and production of IL-1β, which in turn diffuse into the surrounding blood vessels to trigger endothelial dysfunction, vascular inflammation and atherosclerosis. By treatment of mice and pigs with mitochondrial uncoupler, anti- IL-1β antibody, we have confirmed the existence of the UCP1-MMP-mtROS-NLRP3-inflammasome-IL-1β signaling axis in mediating the crosstalk between brown adipocyte in PVAT and blood vascular cells. Furthermore, we validated the novel role of this UCP1-elicited pathway in pigs by utilizing a transgenic pig model generated by Dr. Jianguo Zhao’s group at Institute of Zoology, Chinese academy of Sciences. Realization of objective-4: Investigation of UCP1-independent pathways responsible for the compensatory thermogenesis in scWAT of UCP1-deficient mice. First, we explored the effects of UCP1 deficiency on several recently-identified UCP1-independent thermogenic pathways, including creatine cycle and/or biosynthesis of lipidated amino acids by measuring the level of creatine, ratio of phospho creatine/ total creatine and lipidated amino acids (C18:1-Phe, Leu and Val) in serum and scWAT of UCP1-deficient mice and WT controls on HFD for eight weeks using targeted metabolomics analysis, and found that there is no difference between the two groups. Therefore, we have launched a comprehensive RNA-seq analysis and proteomics analysis to compare the gene and protein expression profiles in sWAT between UCP1-deficent mice and WT littermates housed under both thermoneutral and cold temperatures, followed by bioinformatics analysis. This analysis showed that in addition to the metabolic pathways, such as electron transport chain and TCA cycle, cation transmembrane transport pathway was significantly upregulated by T3 in scWAT OF UCP1-deficient mice. Among them, Atp1a2, the key subunit in sodium potassium pump caught our attention since its expression was expressed at the highest level in scWAT after both T3 administration and cold adaptation. Our further analysis showed that Atp1a2 is the predominant form of ATPase Na+ /K+ transporting alpha subunit in white adipocytes. Furthermore, when treated in vitro, both WT and Ucp1-deficient adipocytes exhibited an elevated expression of ATP1A2 at both mRNA and protein level. By constructing the mouse Apt1a2 promoter driven-luciferase reporter system, we demonstrated that in the presence of thyroid hormone receptor β (TRβ), mouse Apt1a2 promoter driven-luciferase activity was significantly enhanced by T3, indicating that Atp1a2 gene is transactivated by T3-TRβ complex. Through pharmacological intervention and knockdown approaches, we demonstrated that Apt1a2 as a novel UCP1-independent thermogenic uncoupler which may explain increased browning and thermogenesis in scWAT of UCP1-deficient mice.

17125317.label: Major findings and research outcome
17125317.value: 1. UCP1 deficiency in cBAT causes mitochondrial unfolded protein response (UPRmt), which in turn triggers production of FGF21 (a well-known stress-responsive hormonel) and its release into the bloodstream. FGF21 then acts on scWAT to induce mitochondrial biogenesis and UCP1-independent thermogenesis, thereby increasing energy expenditure and reducing fat mass. Furthermore, FGF21 induces production of adiponectin in scWAT, thus counteracting obesity-induced metabolic inflammation, insulin resistance and glucose intolerance (see Publication item#1). Thus increased FGF21 production from cBAT represents a compensatory mechanism in UCP1-deficient mice. 2. UCP1 ablation also causes a marked upregulation of Dio2 in cBAT, a key enzyme converting thyroid hormone from its inactive form (thyroxine, T4) into active form ( triiodothyronine, T3), which in turn travel through bloodstream to scWAT, where T3 promotes mitochondrial biogenesis and induces both UCP1-dependent and –independent thermogenesis. Selective delivery of T3 into white adipose tissue with nanoparticles modified with an adipose-targeting peptide is sufficient to induce browning and thermogenesis of scWAT and counteract diet-induced obesity, glucose tolerance, insulin resistance, vascular inflammation and atherosclerosis, with minimal side effects on hearts and bone (see Publication item#3). 3. In brown adipocytes of perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT), UCP1 exerts anti-inflammation function independent of thermogenesis, by acting as a gatekeeper to prevent obesity-induced elevation of mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP) and mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (mtROS), thereby leading to reduced activation of the NLRP3-inflammasome and caspase-1–mediated maturation of interleukin-1β (IL-1β), a cytokine playing a central role in initiating vascular inflammation and atherosclerosis. UCP1-deficient mice exhibit exacerbated vascular inflammation and atherosclerosis, which can be reversed by administration of mitochondrial potential uncoupler BAT15 or anti- IL-1β neutralizing antibody. Furthermore, transgenic expression of a functional UCP1 in adipose tissues of pigs is sufficient to alleviate high cholesterol and diabetes-induced endothelial dysfunction and coronary stenosis by decreasing MMP, mtROS and IL-1β. These findings uncover suppression of the MMP/mtROS/ NLRP3-inflammasome/Caspase-1/IL1β signaling axis as a novel pathway whereby UCP1 exerts its cardiometabolic benefits (see publication item#2& #5 in review) 4. The ATPase Na+ /K+ transporter Atp1a2 is a potential novel player mediating UCP1-independent thermogenesis in beige adipocytes of scWAT through Na+ K+ futile cycle. UCP1 deficiency in cBAT leads to increased level of T3, which acts in scWAT to induce a drastic elevation of Atpla2 through thyroid hormone receptor β (TRβ). Pharmacological inhibition or knockdown of Atpla2 abolishes thermogenesis in beige cells, especially in UCP1-deficient mice. Thus, Atp1a2 may represent a novel anti-obese target independent of UCP1 (see item#4 &5).

17125317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17125317.value: Activation of brown/beige adipocytes has multiple beneficial effects for prevention and treatment of obesity-related cardiometabolic complications and is the major research focus in metabolic medicine and pharmaceutical science. Whilst previous studies focused on the thermogenic function of UCP1 (a hallmark of brown/beige adipocytes), UCP1 knockout mice are not obese, which has been puzzled many researchers in this field. The findings in this study enable the explanation of this paradox phenomenon, and uncover a previously unappreciated thermogenesis-independent, anti-inflammation pathway to protect vascular inflammation and atherosclerosis. This opens a completely novel filed for further investigation of thermogenesis-independent function of brown/beige adipocytes. We will use unique mouse models and pig models with adipocyte-selective UCP1-transgenic expression for further exploration of this pathway and to develop therapeutic strategy for cardiometabolic diseases by targeting UCP1. Furthermore, our study also identified the ATPase Na+ /K+ transporter Atp1a2 as a novel UCP1-independent player for thermogenesis. We will use adipocyte-specific Atp1a2 knockout mice established in this study further interrogate the role of Atp1a2 in whole body energy homeostasis and elucidate the molecular pathways involved. We will apply for RGC CRF and impact fund to continue these proposed studies.

17125317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17125317.value: Overweight/obesity caused by the positive energy imbalance represents a major risk factor for a cluster of cardio-metabolic diseases, such as diabetes and cardiovascular diseases). While white adipocytes store excess energy, brown and beige adipocytes facilitates energy expenditure by converting ATP production to heat dissipation through the mitochondrial uncoupling protein-1 (UCP1). However, there is currently no approved anti-obese pharmacotherapy available by targeting brown/beige adipocytes due to insufficient understanding of their functional mechanisms. This study identified several metabolic hormones (FGF21 and triiodothyronine) as key players mediating the crosstalk between classical brown adipocytes and beige adipocytes in subcutaneous white adipose tissues (scWAT) in maintaining energy homeostasis, and also uncovered a previously-unappreciated thermogenesis-independent function of UCP1 against obesity-induced metabolic inflammation and atherosclerosis by serving as a gatekeeper to block production of mitochondrial reactive oxygen species and interleukin-1β. These findings shed new light on the function of brown/beige adipocytes and provide a promising therapeutic strategy for obesity-related cardiometabolic diseases. Furthermore, we discovered a novel UCP1-independent pathway which can effectively promotes thermogenesis in beige adipocytes and thus open a new research field in investigation of how our body controls energy balance and core temperature in response to environmental and nutritional changes.

17125917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17125917.value: 在所有的真核細胞中，染色質是壹種高度動態的結構。除了為DNA提供結構支持，染色質還參與調控基因表達，DNA復制以及DNA損傷修復等需要DNA可及性的細胞過程.小體是染色質的基本結構單元。每個核小體由含有約147個堿基對的DNA纏繞壹個組蛋白八聚體構成。眾多研究表明組蛋白的翻譯後修飾在調控染色質動態結構的重要性。組蛋白修飾參與多種功能來促進正常生理功能的發揮，而異常的組蛋白修飾會擾亂染色質結構, 增加基因組的不穩定性，常與癌癥等疾病的發生發展密切相關。因而，檢測及表征組蛋白修飾對於全面的解析眾多細胞過程的調控機理至關重要。目前已檢測到了不少於30種的組蛋白翻譯後修飾，然而僅有極少數的組蛋白翻譯後修飾被進行了深入的研究。而對於大多數，尤其是最新發現的組蛋白修飾，國內外對其生物學意義和功能的研究鮮有報道，領域內對這壹修飾是否會影響，以及如何影響核小體和染色質結構知之甚少。此信息真空亟待填補以解析其生物學意義。 此項目中，我們將集中研究壹種最新發現於組蛋白離氨酸殘基的修飾，離氨酸戊二酰化。已有研究顯示離氨酸戊二酰化廣泛存在於哺乳動物細胞的線粒體蛋白上, 然而我們最新數據表明在組蛋白多個離氨酸位點上也檢測到了戊二酰化的存在。戊二酰化不僅抹除了離氨酸側鏈原有的正電荷，更因引入壹個羧酸片段而使其帶有負電荷。在染色質中，這壹電性反轉將顯著改變核小體和染色質的結構, 從而影響基於染色質的生物學過程。為驗證此假設，我們將綜合運用化學，生物物理，生物化學，酵母基因操縱以及細胞生物學的手段，來闡釋組蛋白離氨酸戊二酰化影響核小體和染色質結構的分子機制以及其在基因調控中的生物學意義。完成此研究將有助於解析組蛋白離氨酸戊二酰化如何在基於染色質的生物學過程中發揮其生物學作用。從長遠來看，此項目的研究成果將能為治療組蛋白離氨酸戊二酰化異常調控所導致的疾病打下理論基礎。

17125917.label: Realisation of objectives
17125917.value: Objective 1: To examine the direct influence of histone lysine glutarylation on nucleosome stability in vitro. In our study, we developed protein chemical synthesis strategies to synthesize the site-specifically modified histones, including H4K91glu, H2BK34succ and H4K77succ. We performed nucleosome reconstitution and then combined a series of biochemical/biophysical analysis approaches to reveal that the negatively charged histone modifications could interrupt histone-DNA or histone-histone interactions to influence the nucleosome assembly process. We then used a Forster resonance energy transfer (FRET) approach to quantify the effect of histone Kglu/Ksucc modifications on structural transitions during nucleosome disassembly. We also expanded our study to Ksucc modification on non-histone proteins (HMGN2Kc17succ, HMGN2Kc30succ, and HMGN2Kc17/30succ). We found that introduction of succinyl on lysine 30 of HMGN2 can significantly disrupt its association with mononucleosome, therefore lead to an increased nucleosomal DNA accessibility. Objective 2: To probe the functions of histone lysine glutarylation in modulating chromatin structure and gene transcription in budding yeast In our study, we constructed Saccharomyces cerevisiae strains carrying mutation of lysine (K) into glutamine (E) to mimic negatively charged glutarylated lysine. We found that H4 K91E mutant conferred growth defect and enhanced sensitivity to DNA damage agents. To seek direct evidence that H4K91glu influences chromatin compaction structure, we isolated chromatins from wild-type and H4 K91E strains and performed micrococcal nuclease (MNase) digestion assay and found that chromatin extracted from the H4 K91E mutant cells are more relaxed compared with wild-type one. We also demonstrated that the H4 K91E mutant can not only disrupt the telomere structure to promote the expression of reporter genes, but also had global effect on gene transcription, especially for lowly-expressed genes. These discoveries agree well with the observed nucleosome instability caused by H4K91glu in vitro (see objective 1). Objective 3: To determine how histone lysine glutarylation is regulated for transcriptional control in mammalian cells In our study, we identified histone Kglu as an evolutionarily conserved and reversible modification. We demonstrated that KAT2A, coupled with the a-KADH complex, which catalyzes the oxidative decarboxylation of a-ketoadipate to glutaryl-CoA, can act as “writer” enzyme for histone Kglu. Knockdown of either KAT2A or DHTKD1, a component of a-KADH complex resulted in a significant reduction in H4K91glu. We also showed that Sirt7 can function as an ‘eraser’ enzyme for histone Kglu both in vitro and in cells. The Sirt7-catalyzed H4K91glu downregulation is tightly associated with chromatin condensation during mitosis phase and in response to DNA damage. In addition, the chromatin precipitation (ChIP) coupled with quantitative PCR (qPCR) experiments revealed that H4K91glu is mainly enriched at promoter regions of highly expressed genes, from which 4,742 chromatin regions were occupied by both H4K91glu and KAT2A; these regions represented 5.9% of the H4K91glu peaks and 38.3% of the KAT2A-occupying peaks, suggesting that the binding of KAT2A to chromatin for glutarylation is transient and dynamic.

17125917.label: Major findings and research outcome
17125917.value: With the support of this GRF, we have investigated the regulatory mechanisms and biological functions of negatively charged posttranslational modifications (glutarylation and succinylation). The major findings and outcome are: (1) To study how histone negatively charged modifications can influence nucleosome assembly process and structure stability, we developed several protein chemistry strategies to synthesize homogenous histones with site-specific Ksucc/Kglu marks installed at stoichiometric level. We demonstrated that H2BK34succ could destabilize nucleosomes by affecting histone-DNA interaction and is likely to case defects in chromatin compaction in vivo (Cell Chem Biol 2018; STAR Protoc. 2021). Study on H4K91glu revealed that this modification can affect (H2A/H2B) dimer and (H3/H4)2 tetramer interaction to interrupt nucleosome assembly process and destabilize nucleosome structure (Mol Cell 2019). In addition, research on H4K77succ illustrated that the modification promotes nucleosome unwrapping and thereby increases DNA accessibility (Nucleic Acid Res 2020). These studies suggest general effects of negatively charged histone lysine modifications to impact nucleosome structure and dynamics in vitro. (2) Using Saccharomyces cerevisiae as a model, we demonstrated that H4K91E mutant can not only delays the DNA replication and mitosis phase progression, but also enhance cell sensitivity in response to various DNA-damaging agents. More importantly, the H4K91E mutant can directly affect not only the telomere regions but also the global chromatin structure. As a result, hundreds of genes were upregulated in the H4K91E mutant cells compared with wild-type ones, especially for the lowly expressed genes in the compacted chromatin regions. (Mol Cell 2019). Both the H2B K37E and H4 K77E mutants can reduce the nucleosome stability by promoting H2A-H2B dimer release. (Cell Chem Biol 2018; Nucleic Acid Res 2020; STAR Protoc. 2021). (3) To understand the cellular functions of histone Kglu, we developed an anti-H4K91glu antibody and identified histone Kglu as an evolutionarily conserved modification. Histone Kglu is also a reversible process, for which, KAT2A and Sirt7 acts as “writer” and “eraser” enzymes, respectively. The Sirt7-catalyzed H4K91glu downregulation was revealed to tightly associate with both chromatin condensation during mitosis and in response to DNA damage. The KAT2A-mediated addition of glutaryl group at H4 Lys91 is mainly enriched at gene transcription starts sites to have potential to promote gene transcription. (Mol Cell 2019) These discoveries, for the first time, provided evidence for how these negatively charged histone modifications were regulated in living cells. At the same time, they also provided new insights for the non-acetylation-related roles played by sirtuin deacetylase family members as well as acetyltransferases in epigenetic regulation. (4) We also expanded our study to lysine succinylation on non-histone proteins, i.e., HMGN2. The nucleosome-binding domain (NBD) of HMGN2 is required for binding to the acidic patch on the histones and the DNA at the entry/exit region to decrease the nucleosomal DNA accessibility by constraining the nucleosomal DNA breathing. The introduction of negatively charged succinyl group on K30 of HMGN2 can significantly disrupt the association between HMGN2 and the mononucleosome to enhance nucleosomal DNA accessibility. The HMGN2K30succ can also increase the nucleosomal DNA accessibility by promoting nucleosomal DNA unwrapping in the entry/exit region. This study reveals a novel mechanism of non-histone protein succinylation on altering chromatin recruitment, which can further affect nucleosome and chromatin dynamics. (RSC Chemical Biology 2021).

17125917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17125917.value: In our current study, we systematically mapped the Kglu sites in histones. Among the 27 identified histone glutarylation sites, we focused on the study of a Kglu mark on the globular domain of histone H4 at Lys 91 (H4K91glu). Different from H4K91glu, the Kglu sites localized at the internucleosomal interface may have function to regulate high-order chromatin compaction. The effects and mechanism need further characterization. In our current study, we characterized the deglutarylase activity of Sirt7 and discovered that Sirt7 is involved in modulating DNA damage repair process via its deglutarylase activity. Sirt7 can also catalyze the hydrolysis of H3K122succ and H3K18ac, aiming to promote chromatin condensation for DNA repair. However, it is not clear whether H4K91glu, H3K122succ, and H3K18ac function independently or in a synergistic manner when challenged with DNA damage, which needs further characterization. In our current study, we characterized KAT2A as a histone glutaryltransferase enzyme and discovered histone lysine glutarylation and KAT2A are mainly enriched at transcription starting sites of highly expressed genes, suggesting that histone Kglu may serve as an active mark for gene expression. It is interesting to further determine the functions of histone Kglu (H4K91glu and other histone Kglu sites) in gene regulation in different model systems (e.g., stem cells), and how the levels of histone Kglu marks are controlled by the regulating enzymes to realize its functions in gene regulation. The above questions will be explored in our further studies. In fact, we have already applied for fundings (as PI and Co-I) to support our continuous studies, including chemical biology approach to molecular medicine (AoE/P-705/16), developing bio-orthogonal and photo-cross-linkable amino acids for identification of cell-type-specific protein-protein interactions in physiological context (CRF 17121120), and institute of metabolic medicine (AoE/M-707/18).

17125917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17125917.value: Posttranslational modification (PTM) of histone is one of the essential mechanisms that underlie the regulation of fundamental cellular events, such as gene expression, DNA replication and damage repair. Histone lysine glutarylation (Kglu) and succinylation (Ksucc) are newly identified PTMs. Due to the presence of negatively charged carboxylate group, these PTMs can induce significant changes in the physicochemical properties of the modification sites, and could potentially affect protein structure, folding and function. However, the regulatory mechanisms and biological functions remain poorly understood. In this project, we use multidisciplinary approaches to characterize the impact of histone Kglu/succ marks on nucleosome structure stability and dynamics, identify the enzymes that add/remove the Kglu marks and investigate the biological functions/consequences of histone Kglu/succ. Our results greatly advance our knowledge on histone negative modification and their regulating mechanism. Moreover, the information may help the development of potential therapeutic strategies for the treatment of human diseases associated with the abnormalities in the regulation of histone Kglu/succ.

17126017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17126017.value: 乙型肝炎病毒感染在香港和中國相當普遍，導致罹患肝癌的機會大爲增加。乙型肝炎病毒基因組可在感染細胞內形成具有超螺旋結構的cccDNA，爲現有之抗病毒藥物所不能清除。cccDNA又是乙型肝炎病毒轉錄的模板，所有病毒RNA均由cccDNA轉錄而産生。了解cccDNA之形成、維護與功能，爲發展新型抗病毒藥物所必需；而其關鍵之一，就是確定並研究被募集到cccDNA並參與調節乙型肝炎病毒轉錄的細胞蛋白。我們在過往研究中發現，作爲MLL甲基轉移酶複合體重要組成蛋白的WDR5可被募集到cccDNA並調節乙型肝炎病毒的轉錄。在本課題中，我們將從三方面對WDR5在乙型肝炎病毒轉錄中的調節作用作更深入之研究。首先，我們將採用過表達及敲減敲除等多種方法，確立WDR5在乙型肝炎病毒轉錄中的必要性。其次，我們將研究WDR5調節乙型肝炎病毒轉錄的機理，重點是確定MLL所催化的H3K4組蛋白三重甲基化的影響及WDR5與長非編碼RNA的相互作用。再次，我們將確定WDR5及相關蛋白與長非編碼RNA在乙型肝炎病毒感染細胞的表達與活性。最後，我們將進行初步試驗，探討WDR5小分子抑制劑對乙型肝炎病毒複制的抑制作用。本課題不僅會提供乙型肝炎病毒分子生物學的新知識，也有望發現可用于治療乙型肝炎病毒感染的新標靶及新藥物。

17126017.label: Realisation of objectives
17126017.value: All four parts of our project as stated in our original proposal have been executed fully. All proposed experiments have been done and many additional studies have also been conducted. Unfortunately, when our study was almost completed, a research article on the role of WDR5 in HBV replication with findings largely consistent with ours was published by another group in Hepatology (Gao W, Jia Z, Tian Y, Yang P, Sun H, Wang C, Ding Y, Zhang M, Zhang Y, Yang D, Tian Z, Zhou J, Ruan Z, Wu Y, Ni B. HBx protein contributes to liver carcinogenesis by H3K4me3 modification through stabilizing WD repeat domain 5 protein. Hepatology 2020;71:1678-1695. doi: 10.1002/hep.30947). Although we might not be able to publish similar results in an international journal, we have adjusted our research plan and would publish some of our related findings in another one or two papers focusing on PRMT5 and CTCF. The field is very competitive. We are glad that others have made similar findings and published in a well-recognized international journal. That has provided strong support to our hypothesis. However, it also sets a new bar for publication and completion of our project. Based on our own findings, we have started and performed multiple lines of experiments on two other positive regulators of HBV transcription, PRMT5 and CTCF, which were found to recruit WDR5 to cccDNA. Our new findings are summarized in the next two paragraphs. We are eager to have our findings published as soon as practically possible. We have performed extensive gain-of-function and loss-of-function assays to show that WDR5 promotes HBV transcription. To identify our new niche in the study of the role of WDR5 in HBV replication so that we can still contribute substantially to the field after publication of a paper on WDR5 in Hepatology by another group, we have decided to focus more on our new finding that PRMT5 promotes HBV transcription by recruiting WDR5. We showed that PRMT5 exerts a positive regulatory effect on HBV transcription. Both PRMT5 mRNA and protein were upregulated in HBV-infected hepatic cells and tissues. Overexpression of PRMT5 significantly increased pgRNA, cccDNA and secreted HBsAg levels in HBV-infected HepG2-NTCP cells, while knockdown of PRMT5 resulted in the opposite. Mechanistically, on one hand, PRMT5 stimulated the activity of HBV preS2/S promoter by promoting the recruitment of CRTC1 to cccDNA as a result of symmetric dimethylation of arginines in CRTC1. On the other hand, PRMT5 was also found to affect the recruitment of symmetrically dimethylated histone mark H3R2me2s to cccDNA resulting in epigenetic activation of HBV gene expression. Thus, PRMT5 targets both histone and non-histone arginines in its activation of HBV transcription. We also provided evidence that the PRMT5 inhibitor EPZ015666 effectively suppressed HBV transcription in HBV-infected HepG2-NTCP cells, suggesting that HBV replication might be disrupted by the chemical inhibition of PRMT5. Finally, we showed that WDR5 was recruited to cccDNA by PRMT5. Taken together, our findings revealed not only a new function of PRMT5 as a positive regulator of HBV transcription but also a new strategy for anti-HBV therapy through pharmaceutical activation of PRMT5. We hope that we can publish these new findings on WDR5 in one research article in an international journal. In addition, we also found that CTCF, a chromosomal architectural protein and another new stimulator of HBV transcription, can also recruit WDR5. Knocking down CTCF expression repressed HBV transcription, whereas overexpression of CTCF facilitated HBV transcription. The data from HiChIP suggested that Enhancer II contacts the preS2 promoter via CTCF-mediated DNA looping that enables Enhancer II to stimulate the activity of the preS2 promoter. Such CTCF-mediated DNA looping was further validated by 3C-ChIP, which indicated that anti-CTCF antibodies rather than irrelevant IgG enriched CTCF- mediated DNA loop and that knocking down CTCF decreased CTCF-mediated DNA loop. In addition, CTCF facilitated the recruitment of HBx and WDR5 to the HBV genome. We hope that we can publish our new findings related to WDR5 in another research article in an international journal. In summary, we have performed all proposed studies on WDR5. We found that: i) WDR5 promoted HBV transcription through H3K4me3. ii) WDR5 cooperated with HBx in the activation of HBV transcription. iii) WDR5 inhibitors are suppressors of HBV transcription. Unfortunately, others have already published similar findings. We therefore focused on the recruitment of WDR5 by two new regulators of HBV transcription, PRMT5 and CTCF. We will try our best to publish our findings on the roles of PRMT5 and CTCF in HBV transcription with the addition of a few key results.

17126017.value: 1. We performed gain-of-function and loss-of-function experiments in HBV-infected HepG2-NTCP cells and pHBV1.3-transfected HepG2 cells to demonstrate WDR5 promotion of HBV transcription through H3K4me3. We further showed that WDR5 cooperates with HBx in the activation of cccDNA transcription. Consistent with these results, WDR5 inhibitors including are potent suppressors of HBV transcription. These findings are generally consistent with a paper published by another group in Hepatology when our study was well underway (Gao W et al. We therefore had to adjust our research plan to focus on the following two directions that are closely related to the positive regulatory role of WDR5 in HBV transcription. 2. We showed that PRMT5 exerts a positive regulatory effect on HBV transcription partially through recruitment of WDR5. Levels of PRMT5 mRNA and protein were found to be elevated significantly in HBV-infected hepatic cells and tissues. Whereas knockdown or inhibition of PRMT5 suppressed pgRNA, cccDNA and secreted HBsAg levels in HBV-infected HepG2-NTCP cells, enforced expression of PRMT5 had the opposite effect. Further analysis revealed that PRMT5 stimulated HBV transcription through at least three distinct but related mechanisms. First, PRMT5 activates HBV preS2/S promoter by promoting the recruitment of CRTC1 to cccDNA as a result of symmetric dimethylation of arginines in CRTC1. Second, PRMT5 was also found to affect the recruitment of symmetrically dimethylated histone mark H3R2me2s to cccDNA resulting in epigenetic activation of HBV gene expression. Thus, PRMT5 targets both histone and non-histone arginines in its activation of HBV transcription. Third, PRMT5 recruits WDR5 to cccDNA. Furthermore, PRMT5 inhibitor EPZ015666 effectively suppressed HBV transcription in HBV-infected HepG2-NTCP cells, suggesting that HBV replication might be disrupted by the chemical inhibition of PRMT5. Taken together, our findings revealed not only a new function of PRMT5 as a positive regulator of HBV transcription but also a new strategy for anti-HBV therapy through pharmaceutical activation of PRMT5. We need a few more months to complete our study on PRMT5 and publish our new findings related to WDR5 in one research article in an international journal. 3. We also found that CTCF, a chromosomal architectural protein and another new stimulator of HBV transcription, can also recruit WDR5. Knocking down CTCF expression repressed HBV transcription, whereas overexpression of CTCF facilitated HBV transcription. The data from HiChIP suggested that Enhancer II contacts the preS2 promoter via CTCF-mediated DNA looping that enables Enhancer II to stimulate the activity of the preS2 promoter. Such CTCF-mediated DNA looping was further validated by 3C-ChIP, which indicated that anti-CTCF antibodies rather than irrelevant IgG enriched CTCF- mediated DNA loop and that knocking down CTCF decreased CTCF-mediated DNA loop. In addition, CTCF facilitated the recruitment of HBx and WDR5 to the HBV genome. Since we focused more on the study of CTCF only in the middle of our project, we need a few more months to publish our new findings related to WDR5 in another research article in an international journal.

17126017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17126017.value: We will work really hard to push our two papers on PRMT5 and CTCF through in the coming months so that they appear in decent international journals. Both studies are derived directly from this project and most experiments have been done as reported above, although significantly more results are required for publication of these two papers. More experiments are underway. We are glad that in Hong Kong we can still conduct top-notch basic research on HBV that have the potential to create significant impact in the field. Our ongoing and future studies will continue to focus on the mechanism by which PRMT5, CTCF and WDR5 activate HBV transcription. Developing some small-molecule inhibitors of PRMT5, CTCF and WDR5 into anti-HBV agents is another direction we might explore, although my main interest is still in basic research on mechanism of HBV transcription. In particular, there are more interesting questions about CTCF-mediated DNA looping that we can further study. With plenty of interesting leads generated in this project, we are highly confident that we can make other important contributions to the field, as long as we can get new funding. However, my funding on HBV research will soon come to a major gap. Lack of stability and sustainability is the nature of research funding in Hong Kong, which we have to face and tackle. In order to support my group, I just have to work harder to obtain new funding from RGC or other sources so that our research on HBV transcription will not be interrupted in the next few years.

17126017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17126017.value: Up to 10% of the adult population is chronically infected with hepatitis B virus (HBV) in Hong Kong and China, resulting in a much increased risk for liver failure, cirrhosis and liver cancer. HBV DNA is assembled into a form known as cccDNA, which is bound with multiple viral and cellular proteins. Cure of HBV infection remains a challenge because cccDNA is refractory to anti-HBV therapy. It is therefore critical to understand the mechanism of cccDNA maintenance and function. Particularly, identification and characterization of additional cellular proteins that are recruited to cccDNA to regulate HBV transcription are an important task in cccDNA biology. In this project, we have identified and characterized WDR5 as a novel positive regulatory factor of HBV transcription. Our further analysis revealed that two other activators of HBV transcription named PRMT5 and CTCF function, at least partially, by recruiting WDR5 to cccDNA. Our study has derived a better understanding of WDR5-dependent regulatory mechanism of cccDNA transcription. Based on our model, suppressing WDR5, PRMT5 or CTCF with small-molecule inhibitors might be a new strategy to inhibit HBV replication. Thus, our study has not only generated new knowledge in cccDNA biology, but also provided new targets and new lead compounds for anti-HBV therapy.

17126317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17126317.value: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infects over 95% of the population worldwide, and is associated with several human malignancies. EBV-induced lymphoproliferative disease (EBV-LPD) in the immunocompromised patients after transplantation or at late stage of HIV infection remains as a serious and life-threatening complication. Our previous studies have demonstrated phosphoantigen pamidronate can control EBV-LPD in humanized mice by enhancing human gammadelta-T cell immunity, suggesting a novel therapeutic strategy for treating EBV-LPD by targeting human gammadelta-T cells. However, one drawback of gammadelta-T cell-based immunotherapy is the rapid exhaustion of proliferation and effector responses by these cells after repeated treatments with phosphoantigens. Another drawback of gammadelta-T cell-based immunotherapy is the immunosuppressive effects of cellular and viral interleukin-10 (cIL-10 and vIL-10) within the tumor microenvironment. 4-1BB is a costimulatory molecule expressed on T cells. 4-1BB signal can stimulate CD3+ T cell expansion, increase cytokine production and prevent activation-induced cell death. However, little is known about the role of 4-1BB signal in human gammadelta-T cells. Our preliminary study showed that human 4-1BB+ gammadelta-T cells displayed more potent cytotoxic activity against tumor cells than their 4-1BB- counterpart, and this superior cytotoxic effect was mediated by 4-1BB engagement. Moreover, 4-1BB+ gammadelta-T cells exhibited potent resistance to immunosuppressive effects of cIL-10 and vIL-10 by rescuing the cytotoxic activity of gammadelta-T cells. Here, we will test our hypothesis that 4-1BB signal can stimulate the activation and expansion of human gammadelta-T cells, and enhance their antitumor activity against EBV-LPD in cIL-10- and vIL-10-mediated immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment in vitro and in vivo. This study will improve our understanding of the role of 4-1BB pathway in enhancing antitumor activity of human gammadelta-T cells against EBV-LPD. It will also provide a novel strategy to overcome the obstacle from cIL-10 and vIL-10-mediated immunosuppressive microenvironment by targeting 4-1BB to improve the efficacy of gammadelta-T cell-based immunotherapy.
