17126517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17126517.value: 维甲酸（RA）是维生素A的代谢产物，在高浓度下可以干扰脊椎动物胚胎或胎儿的发育。实验室研究表明，9-顺式维甲酸（9c-RA）可以诱导海洋腹足类动物疣荔枝螺（Reishia clavigera）雌性个体长出雄性性器官的异常发育（性畸变）。最近一项研究表明，中国太湖淡水蓝藻能够产生这些具有致畸效应的维甲酸。 此外，我们最近首次证明：一些海洋微藻和蓝藻同样可以产生维甲酸，并且这些维甲酸可以诱导雌性疣荔枝螺头神经节和消化腺中性畸变和应激相关基因的上调。我们还观察到，环境相关浓度的全反式维甲酸（at-RA）可以延迟海洋桡足类动物日本虎斑猛水蚤（Tigriopus japonicus）的发育时间。然而，维甲酸对其他海洋生物的毒理作用及其潜在毒性作用机制仍然未知。 香港作为一个都市化的沿海城市，每天都有大量未经完全处理的废水和受污染的地表径流进入海洋环境。因此，香港海水营养丰富，属于富营养化水体，并且频繁发生有害藻类水华（红潮）。 如果海洋微藻和蓝藻可以产生并且释放高浓度的维甲酸，尤其是在藻类水华发生期间，这些维甲酸可能诱发海洋生物的异常发育，并对海洋生物多样性和自然资源造成破坏性影响。 此外，维甲酸可以通过人和动物的尿液排入环境中，因此它们通常发生在未经完全处理的废水出水及其接纳水体中。 本研究将利用香港的海洋环境作为全球都市化沿海生态系统的一个例子，首先将调查海水中维甲酸类型和数量的时空变化及来源（即废水、雨水、海洋微藻和蓝藻）。其次，我们将开展标准的生态毒性试验，研究维甲酸以及具有维甲酸产生能力的微藻和蓝藻对各种海洋生物（如藤壶、桡足类、腹足类、海胆和管虫）幼虫的毒性作用。通过将维甲酸环境分布研究和对海洋生物毒性效应研究相结合，我们将大致地评估目前维甲酸在香港沿海海洋生态系统中的生态风险。最后，我们将利用下一代测序和实时定量PCR技术来研究维甲酸对日本虎斑猛水蚤的分子毒性机制。

17126517.label: Realisation of objectives
17126517.value: Objective 1 To address Objective 1, we measured environmental concentrations of retinoic acids (RAs) and their oxidative metabolites (4-oxo-RAs) in three saline sewage treatment plants (STPs) and the coastal marine environment of Hong Kong. We found that the ranges of the total concentrations of RAs and 4-oxo-RAs in influents and effluents of three STPs in Hong Kong were 7.1–29 ng/L and 3.7–9.1 ng/L, respectively. RAs and 4-oxo-RAs were dominated by at-4-oxo-RA or 13c-4-oxo-RA in wastewater, whereas at-RA and 13c-RA were the most abundant in sludge. Removal efficiencies of RAs and 4-oxo-RAs in the aqueous phase ranged from 41% to 82%. Hence, the adjacent seawaters (i.e., receiving water bodies) exhibited measurable concentrations of RAs and 4-oxo-RAs (2.0–4.3 ng/L in seawaters), which posed medium ecological risks to local marine ecosystems (i.e., hazard quotients: 0.1–1). We further investigated the removal efficiencies of RAs and 4-oxo-RAs in six local STPs via collecting 24-hour composite samples for influent, effluent and sludge. These STPs employ either chemically enhanced primary treatment (CEPT) or secondary biological treatment (n=3). Total concentrations of RAs and 4-oxo-RAs in influent, effluent and sludge from the six selected STPs ranged from 21.5–33.1 ng/L, 12.0–20.4 ng/L, and 4.33–7.02 ng/g dry weight, respectively. The compounds were dominated by at-RA and 13c-RA, together accounting for 46.9–65.6%, 38.4–56.7%, and 62.8–82.8% of the total RAs and 4-oxo-RAs in influent, effluent and sludge, respectively. The studied RAs and 4-oxo-RAs could not be satisfactorily removed by both treatment processes with removal efficiencies ranging from 25.4% to 47.4% only, without a significant difference in their removal between CEPT and secondary treatment. Based on hazard quotients of all-trans-RA (i.e., at-RA) equivalents (0.248–0.521), the treated effluents from all the six STPs exhibited medium ecological risks to the receiving coastal environment. We also examined spatial and temporal variations of environmental concentrations of RAs and 4-oxo-RAs using a systematic sampling method. Seawater samples were collected from 30 coastal locations of 10 Water Control Zones (WCZ) of Hong Kong, i.e., each WCZ with three sampling locations as replicates, and samplings were carried out during dry season (January to March) and wet season (June to August) in 2018. Results showed that total concentrations of RAs and 4-oxo-RAs in seawater were up to 0.790 and 0.427 ng/L in dry and wet seasons, respectively. 9c-4-oxo-RA and 13c-4-oxo-RA were the predominant compounds in seawater in both seasons. Deep Bay Water Control Zone was identified as the most enriched area with the studied compounds, probably due to the semi-enclosed nature and the influence from the Pearl River input. During algal blooms, the total concentration of RAs and 4-oxo-RAs was detected up to 4.74 ng/L with the presence of 9-cis-RA which was previously evidenced to induce imposex in marine female gastropods. Overall, there was no immediate risk of RAs and 4-oxo-RAs to coastal marine environments of Hong Kong regardless of the occurrence of algal bloom. We further tested the stability or persistence in seawater, and found that retinoic acids were relatively unstable in seawater. For instance, we added the stock of at-RA in artificial seawater and extracted immediately with dichloromethane for chemical analysis. Five compounds, i.e., at-RA, 13c-RA, 9c-RA, at-4-oxo-RA, and 13c-4-oxo-RA, were found, and they accounted for 28.4%, 44.4%, 20.0%, 6.8%, and 0.4% of the total, respectively. The results clearly demonstrated that at-RA can be isomerized and metabolized instantly in seawater. Hence, the project Objective 1 has been fully achieved. Objective 2 To address Objective 2, we conducted acute toxicity tests on six marine species towards the exposure to at-RA, which is the most widely distributed RA in the environment. Six marine species included microalga Isochrysis galbana, copepod Tigriopus japonicus, brine shrimp Artemia franciscana, gastropod Monodonta labio, mussel Xenostrobus securis, and medaka fish Oryzias melastigma embryos. Results showed that the embryo of O. melastigma was the most sensitive towards the exposure of at-RA while the gastropod M. labio was the least sensitive. The 72-h median effective concentration (EC50) of at-RA to I. galbana was 1.31 mg/L, while the 96-h median lethal concentrations (LC50s) of at-RA to T. japonicus, A. franciscana, M. labio, X. securis and O. melastigma embryos, were 1.13 mg/L, 0.90 mg/L, 2.08 mg/L, 1.44 mg/L and 0.11 mg/L, respectively. A species sensitivity distribution (SSD) was constructed based on the experimental results generated from the present study. A marine-specific predicted no-effect concentration (PNEC) of at-RA was derived at 2,212 ng/L. By computing the hazard quotients using the marine-specific PNEC and available measured and predicted concentrations of RAs and 4-oxo-RAs, we found the current levels of RAs and 4-oxo-RAs posed relatively low risks to the marine environment of Hong Kong, which was generally consistent with the findings obtained in Objective 1. The marine-specific PNEC was more than 500-fold of freshwater-specific PNEC (i.e., 3.93 ng/L), indicating that marine species were generally less sensitive than their freshwater counterparts towards RAs. This was the first study to document the concentration-response of various marine species towards at-RA exposure and construct the marine-specific SSD for assessing the ecological risk of at-RAs and 4-oxo-RAs towards the marine environment. Since various forms of RAs and 4-oxo-RAs often coexist in aquatic environments, further studies should investigate their combined toxicity to an array of marine species of different trophic levels with consideration of chronic exposure scenarios at environmentally relevant concentrations, so as to better understand the environmental risk of this group of chemicals in the marine environment. Thus, the project Objective 2 has also been fully accomplished. Objective 3 To address Objective 3, we firstly conducted chronic toxicity tests of at-RA at environmentally relevant concentrations (10-2400 ng/L) on the marine copepod Tigriopus japonicus that was collected from Hong Kong coastal rock pools. Our results showed that at-RA at environmentally relevant concentrations could delay the developmental time of nauplii and maturation stages of T. japonicus. Fecundity of the copepods was, however, not statistically significantly affected. Similarly, at-RA with the concentration of 100 ng/L or above delayed the developmental time from nauplius to copepodid stage, and from nauplius to adult stage of the same species of the copepod T. japonicus that was collected from South Korea. Toxic mechanisms of at-RA on T. japonicus were further elucidated using the quantitative real-time PCR and RNA sequencing tools. Ecdysteroids are signaling molecules in regulating the molting process, the toxicity of at-RA to the copepods may occur through binding to toxicants to the ecdysteroid receptor (EcR). EcR forms a heterodimer with ultraspiracle (USP), which is called RXR in vertebrates and can bind with RAs. The binding of at-RA to the EcR and USP would likely result in inhibition of ecdysteroid signaling and developmental retardation. We found significant up-regulations of EcR and USP after exposure to at-RA at environmentally relevant concentrations of 10-500 ng/L level. The transcriptomics analysis also revealed that the molting retardation of T. japonicus occurred through downregulating chitin metabolic pathways related genes (e.g., chitin metabolic process and chitin binding genes), probably due to the participation of these genes in molting and metamorphosis of the copepods. The project Objective 3 has been completed. Meanwhile, we are preparing a manuscript for the results of transcriptomics study. Overall, the three project Objectives have been fully achieved.

17126517.label: Major findings and research outcome
17126517.value: The research findings regarding levels and fate of retinoic acids (RAs) and their metabolites (4-oxo-RAs) in sewage treatment plants (STPs) and seawaters in Hong Kong were published in Environment International (Part C, #1 publication), Water Research (#3 publication) and Chemosphere (#4 publication). The results about the stability or persistence of retinoic acids were published in Environmental Science & Technology Letters (#5 publication). Furthermore, we have published a review article on the current understanding of ecological risks of RAs and their metabolites in aquatic environments (#2 publication). A manuscript (#6) about the toxicity of at-RA to six marine organisms and derivation of predicted no effect concentrations (PNEC) of at-RA have submitted to a journal, and is now at the revision stage. Another manuscript (#7) related to chronic toxicity of at-RA on marine copepods and its toxic mechanisms is under preparation. Additionally, we are also preparing another manuscript (#8) about the occurrence and ecological risks of retinoic acids in the marine environment of Hong Kong. We found that sewage treatment processes of the STPs in Hong Kong could only partially remove RAs and 4-oxo-RAs from wastewater. There was no significant difference in their removal between chemically enhanced primary treatment and secondary biological treatment. Hence, elevated concentrations of RAs and 4-oxo-Ras were found in local coastal waters, posing medium ecological risks to the marine ecosystem. In the marine environment, there was no significant difference in their concentrations between dry and wet seasons, while their concentrations were greater during algal blooms. Among sites, Deep Bay Water Control Zone was identified as the most enriched area with the studied compounds, probably due to the semi-enclosed nature and the influence from the Pearl River input. We found that embryos of medaka fish Oryzias melastigma were the most sensitive towards the exposure of at-RA while the gastropod Monodonta labio was the least sensitive. Based on the method of species sensitivity distribution (SSD), a marine-species-specific PNEC of at-RA was derived at 2,212 ng/L, which was more than 500-fold of freshwater-specific PNEC (i.e., 3.93 ng/L). We also found that at-RA at environmentally relevant concentrations could trigger expression of imposex-related genes in female whelks Reishia clavigera, as well as delay the developmental times of the copepod T. japonicus. The main toxic mechanisms of at-RA on the copepod may involve upregulation of molting-related genes like EcR and USP, and downregulation of chitin metabolic pathways related genes.

17126517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17126517.value: Given that the discharge of sewage effluent is a significant, continuous source of RAs and their metabolites in coastal marine environments of urbanized coastal cities, it is desirable and essential to continuously monitor these compounds and develop new wastewater treatment technologies to improve their removal efficiencies. As concentrations of these chemicals in seawater are greater during algal blooms, their occurrence and distribution should be closely monitored in coastal waters with frequent occurrence of algal blooms. Since these chemicals often coexist in aquatic environments, future studies should investigate their combined toxicity to marine organisms with consideration of chronic exposure scenarios at environmentally relevant concentrations. Similarly, combined toxicity tests of RAs and other widespread contaminants like organotin compounds should be conducted for more marine species, because these compounds may trigger synergistic or additive effects to marine organisms. To better reveal their ecological impacts, bioaccumulation and biodegradation of these chemicals by marine organisms should be investigated. Further investigations could also consider the effect of RAs under the influence of multiple stressors such as temperature, pH and salinity, because global climate change impacts (e.g., ocean acidification, global warming and intensified rainfall) may alter their physicochemical properties, degradation and thus toxicity to marine organisms.

17126517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17126517.value: Retinoic acids (RAs) and their metabolites (4-oxo-RAs), which are the derivatives of vitamin A, play crucial roles in various physiological processes of animals. However, excessive intake of these chemicals can result in abnormal development in animals. This study has demonstrated that these chemicals can only be partially removed by sewage treatment plants (STPs) in Hong Kong. Therefore, the discharge of effluent from STPs is a significant source of these chemicals into the marine environment. Additionally, RAs and 4-oxo-RAs can be released from algal blooms and benthic cyanobacteria, which are also important sources of these compounds in the marine environment. All-trans RA (at-RA), which is the most widely distributed RA in the environment, can trigger acute toxicity to marine organisms including algae, copepod, brine shrimp, gastropod, mussel and medaka fish. The chronic exposure of at-RA at environmentally relevant concentrations can trigger up-regulation of imposex-related genes in the gastropods, and delay the development of copepods by regulating their molting-related genes. Results of this study have advanced our understanding on the behavior and environmental fate of RAs in sewage treatment plants and the coastal marine environment, as well as their adverse effects on marine organisms and ecological risks in the marine ecosystem.

17126717.label: Realisation of objectives
17126717.value: Objective 1: Determine how histone chaperone LIN-53 assembles HCP-3 to holocentromeric chromatin in vivo CENP-AHCP-3 could not be detected in the soluble nucleoplasm fractions. LIN-53 can be co-purified with chromatin-bound CENP-AHCP-3 for immunoprecipitation, and such interaction was confirmed reciprocally. LIN-53 can also be co-purified with KNL-2. In consistent with previous studies, the above results show that LIN-53 may concomitantly target CENP-AHCP-3 to the centromere and interact with KNL-2 at the licensed centromeric chromatin. In C. elegans, injecting foreign DNA, even devoid of C. elegans sequences, into its gonad could form episomal extra-chromosomal arrays, also known as artificial chromosomes (ACs), in the embryonic cells. We used the ACs system to study how RbAp46/48LIN-53 assembles CENP-AHCP-3 to the AC chromatin in vivo. We found that RbAp46/48LIN-53 deposits CENP-AHCP-3 on endogenous chromosomes, but HAT-1 depletion has no effect on CENP-AHCP-3 on endogenous chromosomes. Mis18BP1KNL-2 and CENP-AHCP-3 are interdependent for each other’s localization on endogenous chromosomes of C. elegans. On endogenous chromosomes, RbAp46/48lin-53 depletion only reduced CENP-AHCP-3 level but did not affect Mis18BP1KNL-2 level. We monitored the M18BP1KNL-2 signal on the chromatin of nascent ACs in lin-53 RNAi-treated embryos. Surprisingly, at de novo centromeres on nascent ACs, RbAp46/48LIN-53 depletion also leads to the loss of initial Mis18BP1KNL-2 deposition, which suggests that while Mis18BP1KNL-2 could be a self-directing factor for centromere maintenance in the existing centromeres, it is downstream of RbAp46/48LIN-53 in de novo centromere establishment. Objective 2: Elucidate the physical interaction between LIN-53 and HCP-3 in vitro Proteins containing 6xHis fusion tags were captured and immobilized to Ni-NTA agarose beads. Upon incubation with histone H3 and H4, it was found that 6xHis-SUMO tagged LIN-53 could successfully pull-down H3 and H4 individually. Besides, LIN-53 was also pulled-down by purified 6xHis-tagged CENP-A protein immobilized on beads. Together, these findings have demonstrated that LIN-53 can physically interact with histone H3, H4 and CENP-AHCP-3 individually. Interestingly, the binding of CENP-AHCP-3 can be out competed by titrating in H3. Purified C. elegans histone H3 and H4 were mixed in equimolar to reconstitute (H3-H4)2 tetramers, using adapted protocol from the reconstitution of Xenopus laevis histones subunits (Dyer et al., 2003; Luger et al., 1999). To assess the oligomeric state and purity of the reconstituted (H3-H4)2 tetramers, the sample was purified over a size-exclusion chromatography column. The chromatography trace showed that C. elegans histone H3 and H4 can be successfully reconstituted to tetrameric (H3-H4)2 form with high homogeneity. It is found that (H3-H4)2 tetramers, like histone H3 and H4, can be pulled-down by 6xHis-SUMO tagged LIN-53. It is found that (H3-H4)2 tetramers could be pulled-down by 6xHis-SUMO tagged LIN-53 under [NaCl] concentrations ranging from 150 mM to 1000 mM. However, (H3-H4)2 tetramers showed salt-dependent decrease in binding to 6xHis-SUMO tagged LIN-53. The quantification result showed that over 60% of (H3-H4)2 tetramers would be retained to bind LIN-53 under high ionic concentration (1000 mM NaCl) when compared to binding under physiological salt concentration at 150 mM NaCl. Objective 3: Decipher the effect of LIN-53 and transcription on the genome-wide localization of holocentromeres by DNA Adenine Methyltransferase Identification (DamID) i. Creating C. elegans DamID strains and validation of DamID fusion proteins by immunofluorescence (IF) After the construction of Dam::CENP-A transgenic strain and verification of expression by immunofluorescence and Western as stated in the mid-term report, we continue in the DamID sample collection and analysis. ii. Low input DamID Methodology 10 worms or a single worm was put directly into a PCR tube containing 3 μl lysis buffer. Subsequent sample processing involves a few steps: DpnI digestion, which is highly specific for Dam-methylated GmATC motifs, followed by a specific double strand adaptor ligation and then a PCR amplification. The gel electrophoresis was performed after PCR amplification. Result showed that all the samples yielded a clear smear between 500 bp and 2 kb. The PCR products were then used to prepare sequencing library for Illumina sequencing. iii. Analysis pipeline for DamID-Seq and analysis of Dam::CENP-A Data In total, 11 DamID-seq samples were generated for sequencing, two 10-worms Dam::CENP-A samples, six single-worm Dam::CENP-A samples, one GFP::Dam 10-worms sample, one GFP::Dam single-worm sample, and one 10-worms Dam::lamin sample. First, sequencing raw data in fastq format from each sample went through a series of quality control to find and keep the “DamID reads”. Each read (250 bp) is scanned for the presence of the different parts specialized for DamID-seq: I. the first 4 random bases (“NNNN”); followed by II. 15 bp of adapter sequence (“GTGGTCGCGGCCGAG”); followed by the III. DpnI motif (“GATC”). “DamID reads” are cut after the adapter sequence “GTGGTCGCGGCCGAG” to remove the DamID adapters. Then the remaining sequences are mapped to the C. elegans reference genome (wbcel235) using BWA. iv. CENP-A proteins are highly enriched at discrete, dispersed loci on C. elegans genome Finding out the chromatin domains to which CENP-A associates is a central part of DamID-seq data analysis, although by mapping to the reference genome I have obtained the information of CENP-A binding sites. For this, I needed to assign regions with significant numbers of mapped reads (Peak Calling). As peak calling software packages have typically been developed for ChIP-seq, we must choose a peak calling tool considering the balance between specificity and sensitivity, and adapt it to the CENP-A DamID-seq. To obtain CENP-A enriched domains, we do the peak calling by using MACS2 (threshold q value < 0.05) under narrow peak setting. The number of peaks with different peak width in each sample is then calculated. From the summary of peak calling we can find that 10-worms samples have around 900 CENP-A peaks, which were significantly more compared to the single-worm samples, which have around 600 peaks. We checked the distribution of peak width on both 10-worms and single-worm samples. We find that under narrow peak setting, they have similar pattern, in which most of the CENP-A peaks are around 400 to 1500 bp in length of DNA. We then located each of the CENP-A peaks onto the C. elegans genome to obtain the genome-wide distribution of peaks for each sample. The number of the peaks mapping to the chromosome and its distribution can reflect the distribution of the CENP-A binding sites. CENP-A peaks are found distributed throughout the C. elegans genome as discrete, dispersed loci. CENP-A peaks are enriched towards the arm regions relative to the centers of the autosomes, however, the distribution of CENP-A peaks on the X chromosome is relatively even. This peaks distribution pattern is very similar to the previously published C. elegans CENP-A N-ChIP-seq data (Steiner, 2019, eLife), which identified a total of 707 well-defined CENP-A high occupancy loci discretely located on the whole genome, despite using a different methodology. Furthermore, we compared genome-wide distribution of CENP-A peaks among the 10-worms samples and single-worm samples. In general, the pattern of CENP-A peaks on each chromosome is similar between two 10-worms samples, with some variations on specific positions. On each chromosome, single-worm samples have less CENP-A peaks than 10-worms samples. In addition, each single-worm samples has different CENP-A peak distribution pattern on each of the chromosomes, although most of the CENP-A peaks on the different single-worm samples can be found on the 10-worms samples. This finding suggests that the CENP-A distribution may have worm-to-worm variation.

17126717.label: Major findings and research outcome
17126717.value: This project aims to understand how histone chaperone RbAp46/48/LIN-53 assemble CENP-A/HCP-3 to the permitted holocentric locations. Through in vivo reciprocal co-immunoprecipitation assays, we found that RbAp46/48/LIN-53 interacts with CENP-A/HCP-3 and the licensing factor KNL-2. By in vitro pull down assays, we found that RbAp46/48/LIN-53 can bind to CENP-A/HCP-3, H3, H4, (H3-H4)2 tetramers. Interestingly, the interaction with CENP-A/HCP-3 can be out competed by titrating in H3. By using artificial chromosome (AC) system in C. elegans, we found that RbAp46/48/LIN-53, together with HAT-1, a histone acetyltransferease, facilitates the acetylation of H3 and H4 acetylation on the AC, initial deposition of CENP-A/HCP-3 to the newly formed artificial chromosomes. Interestingly, while RbAp46/48/LIN-53 does not affect KNL-2 centromeric localization on endogenous chromosomes, it does affect the initial deposition of KNL-2 onto the newly formed artificial chromosomes. This suggests that while Mis18BP1KNL-2 could be a self-directing factor for centromere maintenance in the existing centromeres, it is downstream of RbAp46/48LIN-53 in de novo centromere establishment. We have published this work in Nuclei Acids Research 49:9154–9173. On the genome map, we have applied a low-input transgenic method called DNA Adenine Methyltransferase Identification (DamID) to analyze protein-DNA interaction. We have constructed Dam::CENP-A/HCP-3, in which Dam will methylate the G in GTAC in the vicinity of CENP-A/HCP-3. We have analyzed the CENP-A/HCP-3-enriched regions and compared among 10-worm samples and 1-worm data. Interestingly, there are worm-to-worm variations in the CENP-A/HCP-3-enriched regions. We also show exclusion of germline gene body in most CENP-A/HCP-3-enriched regions. We are preparing the manuscript for publication.

17126717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17126717.value: For the biochemical analyses, we will further identify the binding domain between HCP-3 and LIN-53, by expressing protein truncates of HCP-3 and LIN-53 from bacteria, for testing the required protein domain(s) involved in their interactions in pull-down assays. For the DamID analyses, we will further analyze and compare the DamID of LIN-53 and KNL-2 with that of HCP-3. This will allow us to understand the binding landscape of the upstream factors that affect HCP-3.

17126717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17126717.value: This project set out to understand how histone chaperone RbAp46/48/LIN-53 assembles CENP-A/HCP-3 onto specific permitted holocentromere locations on the genome. Through in vivo and in vitro biochemical analyses, we gain insight into the interactions of RbAp46/48/LIN-53 with CENP-A/HCP-3 and the centromere licensing factor KNL-2. On the other hand, RbAp46/48/LIN-53 also acts as H3-H4 chaperone. The binding of RbAp46/48/LIN-53 with KNL-2 on centromeric chromatin, and the interaction of CENP-A with KNL-2 may have brought CENP-A/HCP-3 specifically to existing holocentromere locations. Consistently, for new centromeres on artificial chromosomes, KNL-2 also depends on RbAp46/48/LIN-53 and the initial deposition of CENP-A/HCP-3. For the where question, we have applied a low-input transgenic method called DNA Adenine Methyltransferase Identification (DamID) to analyze protein-DNA interaction, specifically the localization of CENP-A/HCP-3 on the genome. Using as little as a single worm in a sample, we were able to identify CENP-A/HCP-3-enriched regions and show worm-to-worm variations in the pattern. The findings of this project has shed light on the assembly dependency of CENP-A in endogenous chromosomes and in new artificial chromosomes. In addition, the low input localization analysis shows where CENP-A/HCP-3 localizes in a single worm, and how the localization can overlap but also vary from worm-to-worm.

17127417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17127417.value: Psychotic disorders are severe mental illnesses causing enormous burden to patients and society. Early intervention for psychosis has been the major focus in mental health care development worldwide in the past decade with particular emphasis on identifying individuals at clinical high-risk for psychosis. It is suggested that intervention in this pre-psychotic period may prevent progression to full-blown psychosis. However, the major challenge is to accurately differentiate those who will become psychotic from those who will not before illness onset. Until now, no robust predictors of psychosis transition have been identified and the sensitivity of operationalized criteria for clinical high-risk categorization is low. Despite extensive research, neurobiological basis underlying psychosis development remains unknown. Literature indicated that dysregulated glutamatergic neurotransmission is critically implicated in the pathophysiology of psychosis. Previous studies using proton magnetic-resonance-spectroscopy (MRS), a non-invasive in-vivo measurement of brain glutamate function, demonstrated glutamatergic abnormalities in chronic schizophrenia and first-episode psychosis. Thus far, glutamatergic dysfunction is under-studied in clinical high-risk for psychosis. Emerging evidence from proton MRS research revealed altered glutamate levels in clinical high-risk samples. Some prior investigations further found that glutamatergic abnormalities were associated with psychosis transition from clinical high-risk state, thereby suggesting that glutamatergic indices measured by proton MRS may represent a promising biomarker for psychosis prediction. Nonetheless, previous proton MRS studies are hampered by several major methodological limitations. Most studies used cross-sectional design without clinical follow-up assessment which precludes estimation of predictive capacity of glutamatergic measures on psychosis development. Only one study had baseline and follow-up MRS assessments to examine longitudinal changes of glutamate levels across clinical high-risk transition period. Majority had small sample size which compromises statistical power to detect significant differences between clinical high-risk samples versus healthy controls and transition versus non-transition groups. Predictive value of glutamatergic alterations on functional outcome has rarely been investigated. In this project, we will conduct a prospective 2-year follow-up study on clinical high-risk subjects using proton MRS applied at baseline and at 24 months to examine whether glutamatergic abnormalities are observed at presentation, whether baseline glutamatergic indices independently predict psychosis transition and functional outcome, and whether there are progressive longitudinal changes of glutamate levels across the period of psychosis development. We hypothesized that measurement of glutamatergic indices using proton MRS will enhance psychosis prediction and functional outcome estimation which may facilitate pre-emptive intervention for psychosis in the future. Additionally, our findings will provide insights in neurobiological underpinnings of psychosis development. 谷氨酸異常和預測思覺失調高風險人士的臨床和功能結果：兩年縱向質子磁共震光譜掃描研究: 思覺失調疾病是一種對患者及社會帶來沉重負擔的嚴重精神病。思覺失調疾病的早期治療已成為近十年全球精神健康服務發展的重點，其中特別強調使用各種臨床標準去辨識思覺失調高風險人士。有研究指出在高風險時期作出介入治療可阻止病情發展至全面的思覺失調疾病。然而，如何有效地判斷哪些人會患上思覺失調疾病是一個重大的挑戰。儘管世界各地都有很多的研究，我們對思覺失調演變過程中的神經生物學成因機制仍然未有透徹的了解。 文獻顯示谷氨酸的神經傳遞失衡對思覺失調的病理起了關鍵性的影響。有研究利用質子磁共震光譜掃描(MRS)–一種非入侵式的活體掃描，用於測量大腦谷氨酸的功能–發現在慢性精神分裂症患者和首發性思覺失調患者的腦中察覺有谷氨酸異常。迄今為止，思覺失調高風險人士腦中的谷氨酸活動則甚少被探討。近年的質子磁共震光譜掃描研究顯示高風險人士腦中的谷氨酸傳遞活動失衡，而早期的調查亦證實了谷氨酸的異常和高風險人士的發病率關係顯著，由此可見，質子磁共震光譜掃描量度的谷氨酸指數有可能是預測思覺失調病發的重要生物指標。 儘管過往的質子磁共震光譜掃描研究已獲得不少成果，但以往的研究方法亦有不足的地方。大部分研究使用一次性的橫向設計–沒有任何臨床跟進評估–這嚴重地局限了谷氨酸指數在預測思覺失調發展時的潛能。至今，只有一個研究有利用基線和跟進評估來查證谷氨酸在高風險人士過渡成思覺失調患者期間的演變。再者，大部分研究的樣本數量偏少，因此難以從數據上找出高風險人士對比健康參加者以及發病組與非發病組之間的差距。此外，很少研究使用麩胺酸異常去驗證和預測功能結果。 在這計劃中，我們將在基線和第24個月為臨床高風險人士進行質子磁共震光譜掃描，以驗證 一）谷氨酸異常是否在病發前已出現；二）基線的谷氨酸指數能否預測發病率和功能結果；三）谷氨酸活動會否隨著病情的演變而推進。我們推論利用質子磁共震光譜掃描來測量大腦谷氨酸指數能改善思覺失調發病和功能結果的預測，從而有助研發出更有效的早期介入治療。最後，我們期望此研究能有助釐清思覺失調發展的神經生物成因機制。

17127417.label: Realisation of objectives
17127417.value: 1. Objective 1 -This was successfully achieved. We recruited 106 clinical-high-risk (CHR) subjects and 50 demographically-matched healthy controls. Removing those subjects with poor-quality MRS imaging data, resulting in 102 CHR subjects and 50 controls as the final sample for baseline analysis. Clinical, functional and cognitive measures, alongside MRS scanning, were successfully conducted. We compared CHR and control groups in terms of baseline brain glutamate metabolite levels in three a priori region-of-interest including associative striatum, thalamus and medial prefrontal cortex (MPC). Our results showed that CHR and control groups did not significantly differ from each other in glutamate metabolite levels of these three brain regions. Although some previous findings suggested significant difference of glutamate metabolite levels between schizophrenia and controls in these regions, and between CHR and controls particularly in striatum, however, our results are consistent with a recent meta-analysis (McCutcheon et al. 2021) which revealed no significant difference between at-risk individuals and controls in glutamate metabolite levels in prefrontal cortex, basal ganglia or hippocampus. The review only indicated that genetic high-risk, but not CHR subjects, may exhibit significantly higher glutamate metabolite levels in thalamus than controls. 2. Objective 2 -This was achieved. Owing to the COVID-19 pandemic and subsequent stringent infection control measures, in particular restriction and suspension of clinical studies to be conducted in both outpatient and inpatient facilities of public hospitals under Hospital Authority, dropout rate (including those initially consented for follow-up assessment but finally declined due to the need to visit university-affiliated hospital area for neuroimaging and clinical assessments) was higher than expected, especially CHR subjects. A total of 72 (out of 102; 70.6%) CHR subjects and 40 (out of 50; 80%) controls participated 2-year follow-up assessment. Eighteen CHR subjects converted to psychotic disorder by the end of 2-year follow-up (but only 12 completed follow-up MRS assessment), with transition rate of 18% which is generally similar to those reported in the recent CHR studies. Our analysis showed that baseline glutamate metabolite levels of CHR sample did not significantly predict psychosis conversion status over 2 years. Until now, however, only one study with sufficient sample size demonstrated that baseline glutamate metabolite levels (but in hippocampus rather than in our a priori regions-of-interest) significantly associated with psychosis conversion at follow-up (Bossong et al. 2019). Of note, our negative findings might partly be attributable to our modest sample size (due to increased dropout rate amidst the pandemic resulting in modest sample size, and modest transition rate resulting in small sample size of CHR-converted subjects), which would compromise the statistical power to detect subtle yet potentially significant group difference. 3. Objective 3 -This was achieved. We examined predictive value of baseline glutamate metabolite levels on functional outcome at follow-up by subdividing the CHR sample into good versus poor functioning based on ratings of Social and Occupational Functioning Assessment Scale (SOFAS). Our results found that thalamic glutamate metabolite levels, but not in striatum or MPC, predicted functional status at follow-up. This is in line with one prior study which observed that lower levels of thalamic glutamate metabolite levels at baseline were associated with poor functioning at follow-up in CHR sample (Allen et al. 2015). On the other hand, discrepant findings were observed in the literature as a recent study revealed that hippocampal glutamate levels were associated with functional outcome at follow-up (Boosong et al. 2019), while another recent study failed to demonstrate any association (Allen et al. 2021). 4. Objective 4 -This was achieved. Our findings revealed lack of significant changes in glutamate metabolite levels in CHR sample over follow-up. We further examined the relationship between glutamate metabolite levels and clinical outcomes other than psychosis transition at follow-up. Our results found no significant associations of glutamate metabolite levels in either associative striatum or MPC with CHR remission versus non-remission status at follow-up or change of positive symptom severity during follow-up. We noted trend-wise significance between thalamic glutamate metabolite levels and remission / non-remission status, but did not survive correction for multiple comparisons. Our findings thus echoed with an earlier study suggesting that thalamic glutamate levels at baseline were lower in non-remission than in remission group (Egerton et al. 2014). Likewise, the longitudinal and prediction analyses might be limited by our modest sample size in CHR subjects at follow-up, which may obscure potential significant associations. Otherwise, it is noted that mixed findings were observed across limited studies in this respect. 5. Objective 5 -This was achieved. We examined whether incorporating MRS glutamate data into clinical and cognitive variables might improve prediction of psychosis transition from CHR status. Given that MRS glutamate metabolite levels was not significantly associated with converted status, our analysis failed to demonstrate superiority of integrating this variable into our conventional clinical-cognitive measures for psychosis prediction. On the other hand, we observed that inclusion of baseline MRS thalamic glutamate levels into clinical-cognitive variables improved prediction of functional outcome at follow-up. This indicates that MRS glutamate measures may enhance prediction profile of our clinical and cognitive assessment variables in CHR sample.

17127417.label: Major findings and research outcome
17127417.value: Major findings of the project are summarized as follows: Individuals with clinical high-risk (CHR) for psychosis did not significantly differ from healthy controls in glutamate metabolite levels (measured by magnetic resonance spectroscopy, MRS) at baseline in three a priori regions-of-interest including associative striatum, thalamus and medial prefrontal cortex. In our representative cohort of Chinese CHR subjects, 18% converted to full-blown psychotic disorders over 2 years. Our results failed to demonstrate that baseline glutamate metabolite levels significantly predicted psychosis transition from CHR status during follow-up. Glutamate metabolite levels, however, were found to be associated with functional outcome status at follow-up in CHR sample. Otherwise, glutamate metabolite levels were not significantly related to other clinical outcomes including remission versus non-remission status from CHR, and positive symptom severity over time. Notably, negative findings in longitudinal analyses might partly be attributable to modest sample size because of increased attrition rate during COVID-19 pandemic with consequent prolonged period of suspension of clinical study recruitment, and modest psychosis transition rate. Notwithstanding, incorporation of MRS glutamate measures was suggested to further improve the performance of prediction model for functional outcome at follow-up, on top of the conventional clinical and cognitive variables.

17127417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17127417.value: To further build on our study findings, several courses of action could be implemented: First, future research should consider to adopt multi-modal neuroimaging approach, incorporating MRS glutamate with MRI measurement, especially functional connectivity, which has been shown to be significantly associated with glutamate levels in CHR relative to controls; Second, MRS measurement should also include GABA metabolite assessment so as to evaluate the excitatory-inhibitory neurotransmitter associations in CHR and psychosis transition; Third, recent data suggested abnormal hippocampal glutamate levels might predict psychosis transition. Further investigation should therefore verify whether this could be replicated (as hippocampus was not included in the current project); Fourth, modest sample size and transition rate very likely constrain the statistical power for our longitudinal analysis. Collaboration with participation in CHR consortium for MRS and other neuroimaging research including our dataset will facilitate generation of novel MRS / MRI markers and validation of existing significant findings to enhance psychosis risk stratification. Such collaboration will also facilitate development of future larger-scale CHR research project for both psychosis and non-psychosis outcome evaluation, thereby benefiting the potential translation of research findings into real-world clinical practice.

17127417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17127417.value: Schizophrenia and related psychoses (i.e., psychotic disorders) are a group of severe mental disorders affecting 3% of the population and constitutes one of the leading causes of disability worldwide. Early intervention on individuals at imminent clinical high-risk (CHR) for full-blown psychosis development is of critical clinical significance. Dysregulation in glutamate neurotransmission has been proposed as one of the important neurobiological mechanisms contributing to psychosis manifestation, and neuroimaging measuring brain glutamate metabolite concentrations may represent a potentially useful assessment to enhance prediction model for psychosis transition in CHR sample. This 2-year follow-up study aimed to explore potential role of brain glutamate measures for psychosis transition and other outcomes. Our results showed that CHR and healthy-control groups did not differ in brain glutamate measures at baseline. Further analyses did not reveal significant association of baseline brain glutamate measures with psychosis transition from CHR over 2 years. Although we observed lack of significant relationships of brain glutamate measures with other clinical or symptom outcomes at follow-up, our results found that glutamate measures could enhance prediction of functional outcome in CHR sample. Hence, our results highlight potential utility of incorporating brain glutamate measures into clinical variables in predicting outcomes in CHR populations.

17127917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17127917.value: In most eukaryotic cells, more than half of nuclear transcription is ribosomal RNA (rRNA) synthesis that is critical for proper cell growth and proliferation. Deficiencies in rRNA transcription lead to reduced ribosome biogenesis, altered cellular growth and increased cell death. Transcription of rRNA genes is generally carried out by RNA polymerase I (Pol I) transcription machinery in the nucleolus. Within human genome, there are several hundred copies of tandemly repeated rRNA genes clustered into nucleolar organizer regions (NORs) in euchromatin and heterochromatin states. Thus, various epigenetic mechanisms modulate chromatin structure to regulate transcription of rRNA genes. Generally, silent rRNA gene repeats are characterized by extensive DNA methylation, and histone H3K9 methylation at the promoter region, whereas active rRNA genes are enriched with histone H3K4 and H3K36 methylation marks. Accordingly, transcription of rRNA genes has been shown to be tightly modulated by a number of epigenetic regulators. Recently human Spindlin1 has been shown to localize at active ribosomal DNA loci and stimulate the expression of rRNA genes in mouse embryonic fibroblast cells. Spindlin1 consists of a triple Tudor-like Spin/Ssty repeats that recognize H3K4me3 and H3R8me2a combinatorial epigenetic marks. Spindlin1 mutants that lost the binding to methylated histone H3 also significantly impaired its ability to stimulate the expression of rRNA genes. However, no protein has been reported so far to interact with Spindlin1 in the nucleolus, this has seriously limited our understanding of how exactly Spindlin1 facilitates rRNA gene expression. We have just made an unexpected discovery that an uncharacterized nuclear protein c11orf84 physically interacts with Spindlin1 in the nucleolus. Our preliminary data shows that depletion of c11orf84 significantly reduced pre-rRNA levels in human U2OS cells. We also found that c11orf84 is overexpressed in many different cancer cell lines. In this project we will develop a new structure-based paradigm for functional profiling of human Spindlin1-c11orf84 complex including the following aims: (i) To determine the functional consequence of the interaction between Spindlin1 and c11orf84. (ii) To determine crystal structure of Spindlin1-c11orf84 complex. (iii) To characterize the structure and function of c11orf84 Cys2His2 zinc finger domain. 在大多數真核細胞中，超過一半的核轉錄是對於細胞生長和增殖至關重要的核醣體RNA（rRNA）合成。大量的研究証明在許多癌細胞中rRNA和 蛋白質合成是升高的。在最近在小鼠胚胎成纖維細胞中的實驗表明人體蛋白Spindlin1 在活性核醣體DNA位點定位並刺激rRNA基因的表達。 Spindlin1由能夠識別H3K4me3和H3R8me2a組合表觀遺傳標記的TUDOR/Ssty三聯重複體組成。 Spindlin1失去與K4 及R8甲基化的組蛋白H3 結合的突變體顯著減弱其刺激rRNA基因表達的能力。然而，目前尚無報導在核仁中有蛋白質與Spindlin1相互作用，這嚴重限制了我們對Spindlin1如何促進rRNA基因表達的機制的理解。我們最近的研究獲得了一個意想不到的發現，我們觀察到一個從未表徵過的核蛋白c11orf84在核仁中的與Spindlin1有直接相互作用。我們的數據初步顯示，通過siRNA處理來抑制c11orf84的表達能顯著降低人的U2OS細胞中的pre-rRNA 水平。我們還發現c11orf84在許多不同種類的癌細胞系中過量表達。在這個項目中，我們將在解析Spindlin1-c11orf84蛋白複合物結構的基礎上進一步進行功能剖析，包括以下目標：（i）解析Spindlin1-c11orf84蛋白複合物的晶體結構。 (ii) 確定Spindlin1和c11orf84之間相互作用對rRNA合成的影響，以及調控兩蛋白的相互作用對癌細胞生長的影響。

17127917.label: Major findings and research outcome
17127917.value: Spindlin1 is a unique multivalent epigenetic reader that facilitates ribosomal RNA transcription. Human Spindlin1 has been found to be highly expressed in various types of cancer cells. Fuctional analyses suggested Spindlin1 could regulate multiple cellular signaling pathways such as PI3K-Akt, WNT-TCF4, RET and RPL5-MDM2-p53 pathways that are highly relevant to human cancers(1-4). Additionally, Spindlin1 has been demonstrated to be targeted by miRNAs that restrained the effects of Spindlin1 on promoting cell migration and invasion, chemoresistance and metastasis in human cancer cells. In this reporting period, we determined the high-resolution crystal structure of Spindlin1/C11orf84/H3K4me3K9me3 ternary complex, showing Spindlin1 We further provided the mechanistic explanation to show that the Spindlin1/C11orf84 complex can displace HP1 from H3K4me3K9me3-enriched rDNA loci and facilitate histone demethylase KDM4A and PHF8 to access to their favourite substrate H3K4me3K9me3, eventually promotes the conversion of these poised rDNA repeats from the repressed state to the active conformation, and the consequent recruitment of RNA Polymerase I for rRNA transcription activation. We published our research results in Nature Communications and BioEssays.

17127917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17127917.value: Although we established that Spindlin1/C11orf84 complex is a genuine H3K4me3K9me3 reader, a number of outstanding questions remain to be addressed: (i) H3K4me3K9me3 bivalent mark is likely to be transient given that H3K4me3 and H3K9me3 are perceived to be mutually exclusive. If this is the case, why does a Spindlin1/C11orf84 complex bind with such a strong affinity toward a supposedly transient bivalent H3K4me3K9me3 mark? (ii) We reason that KDM4A likely acts as a downstream factor of Spindlin1/C11orf84 complex, but how Spindlin1/C11orf84 complex is released from H3K4me3K9me3-enriched loci for KDM4A to access to its preferred substrate for demethylation remains elusive. (iii) How exactly H3K4me3K9me3 is established. In other word, which methyltransferases are responsible for generating H3K4me3K9me3 bivalent mark? (iv) Spindlin1 has been shown to be a druggable epigenetic reader and Spindlin1 inhibition slowed down tumour growth, so to develop chemical compounds that specifically block the interaction of Spindlin1 with H3K4me3K9me3 dual mark may provide the novel therapeutic strategy for cancer prevention and treatment.

17127917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17127917.value: Cancer is a leading cause of death worldwide. As a hallmark of cancer, abnormal cell growth and proliferation is sustained by increased ribosome biogenesis. Ribosomal RNA (rRNA) transcription, as the first key step of ribosome biogenesis, is tightly regulated by multi-layered epigenetic mechanisms. Spindlin1 is a well-established epigenetic reader that plays a critical role in activating rRNA transcription. We recently identified a stable Spindlin1/C11orf84 protein complex preferentially recognises a non-canonical bivalent histone H3K4me3K9me3 mark and promotes rRNA transcription. The study has opened a new therapeutic avenue to design inhibitors targeting Spindlin1/C11orf84 complex for cancer therapy.

17128817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17128817.value: Osteogenesis imperfecta (OI) is cause by rare mutations in genes necessary for bone formation and maintenance, causing bone fragility and low bone mass. OI is classified base on the clinical features, severity and mode of inheritance. Most mutations are found in genes coding for type I collagen or it’s post-translational modification enzymes. Recently, a novel recurrent mutation in the IFITM5 gene was identified in patients with OI type V (OI-V), creating a new translation start-site adding 5 amino acids to the N-terminus of the protein. Little is known about the function of this gene, and inactivation in mice did not result in significant bone abnormalities in adult mice. In addition to bone fragility and low bone mass, OI-V patients also present with a distinguish feature of hyperplastic callus formation and calcification of the interosseous membrane, and the reason is unknown. Not able to prevent or manage hyperplastic callus formation is a dilemma for surgical decisions as it is a painful outcome with long-term complications. Thus, the clinical features of OI-V are complex. On the one hand, the overall bone structure is osteoporotic, but in the healing process of a fracture, it induces an active calcification process. Our studies of patient osteoblasts showed an impaired localization of IFITM5 proteins to the cell membrane. As OI-V patients are heterozygous for the mutation, this is consistent with a dominant-negative effect. However, hyperplastic callus formation is likely due to a gain-of-function (neomorphic) effect of the mutant IFITM5 protein, deregulating the mineralization process in fracture repair. This is consistent with our observation that while in vitro mineralization of bone nodules is delayed in patient osteoblasts, but once initiated, it is very rapid to a level exceeding normal osteoblasts. We propose that in vivo, upon mineralization of a fracture callus, a chain-reaction initiates following the onset of mineralization, promoting differentiation of progenitor cells and mineralization in the surrounding tissues, inducing ossification. Here, we will dissect the molecular basis of hyperplastic callus formation using in vitro pulse-SILAC proteomic analyses of patient osteoblasts to address the molecular changes in loss- and gain-of-function consequences of normal and mutant IFITM5 proteins, respectively; correlation with in vivo developmental and fracture repair findings in a mouse model for the disease. 17128817.label: Realisation of objectives
17128817.value: Osteogenesis Imperfecta type V (OI-V) is a genetic bone disease caused by mutation in Interferon‐Inducible Transmembrane 5 (IFITM5) gene. Patients exhibit low bone mass and frequent fractures leading to bone deformities. All reported cases share a single heterozygous c.-14C>T mutation in IFITM5, leading to five extra amino acids (MALEP) added to the N-terminus. Unlike other IFITM proteins, IFITM5 is not involved in immune responses but is highly expressed in the osteoblast lineage. The function of IFITM5 or the consequence of the mutation are not clear. In this project, we leverage on the available OI-V bone specimens and primary osteoblasts to provide insights into the pathogenesis that support a gain-of-function as a molecular consequence, although a neomorphic function for MALEP-IFTM5 is also possible. W set three objectives to understand the molecule pathogenesis of OI-V, in which we have completed, and a manuscript describing the major findings, ready for submission to the Journal of Bone and Mineral Research for consideration. While the social unrest and COVID19 pandemic have caused delays, we have successfully completed the project. With reduced funding, we revised the scope of objectives 2 and 3 to meet the budget requirement, and enhanced objective 1 to include in vivo studies in human OI-V sample to correlate finding of the in vitro osteoblast proteomics findings, and to include key in vitro studies of metabolic changes as a logical sequence for the new proteomic findings to build a comprehensive manuscript for publication. Pulsed-Stable Isotopic Labeling with Amino acids in Cell culture (pulsed-SILAC) was performed to obtain unbiased proteomic data for insights of the global protein changes that is consistent with a gain-of-function or neomophic effect of MALEP-IFITM5 mutation OI-V. This approach assesses the newly synthesized proteins for 24 hours before harvesting at days 0, 13, 17 and 21 during osteogenic induction towards mineralization. Proteins extracted from cellular and medium fractions were analyzed by LC MS/MS, and the acquired data analyzed using MaxQuant v.1.5.3.30. This was a major exercise that showed an intrinsic change in OI-V osteoblasts induced by previous expression of IFITM5 could induce a cellular stress response, changes in energy metabolism (glycolysis and oxidative phosphorylation) in OI-V osteoblasts prior to and during in vitro mineralization. Moreover, in OI-V osteoblasts, there are changes in the production of extracellular matrix proteins and matrix remodelling enzymes. We validated and showed the relevance of these findings in vivo using bone samples from OI-V patients collected during surgery; thus completing objective 1. The intrinsic effect of OI-V osteoblasts induces an elevated level of mineralization, and is consistent with our findings in objective 2, where we show that OI-V osteoblast can also induce an extrinsic effect on surround non osteoblast cells such muscle progenitor (C2C12) cells to differentiate towards osteoblast and mineralization. This provided a hint to the mechanism of ectopic mineralization and the hyperplastic callus formation during fracture repair. Although this will need further assessment that may require a true mouse model of OI-V. We consider that objective 2 is completed. Importantly, this could be linked to gain-of-function for an activation of inflammatory process that was also identified in our SILAC proteomic finding, and consistent with a recent publication for a role of an inflammatory response for hyperplastic callus formation. Of interest, our clinical collaborator, Dr Michael To, has showed that the use of COX2 inhibitors prior to surgery can suppress hyperplastic callus formation following surgical bone corrections for OI-V patients. Gene inaction in mice showed very mild impairment in bone mineralization. Given transgenic and mice heterozygous for a gene-targeted Ifitm5c.-14C>T allele are lethal that we have shown as well, this presents a major challenge in studying the pathogenesis of OI-V in mice. While we have also completed the assessment of the OI-V mouse chimeras and the heterozygous mice that we have generated. The information is majorly in the developing growth plate that showed enlarged proliferating, pre-hypertrophic, and hypertrophic chondrocytes in the chimera growth plate compared to wild-type but at a lesser extent than heterozygous mutant. Of particular interest is a population of chondrocytes that do express SOX9. We have not manage to decipher the reason for this. Given the limited funding and scope of his project, we have not pursuit this further, but can be addressed in the future to study the impact of MALEP-IFITM5 on the linear growth of long bones. Assessment of IFITM5 expression in prenatal mouse bone is consistent with the potential osteogenic outcome in human. The newly discovered relationship between cellular stress, metabolic flex and biomineralization was further tested in vitro. We showed that there is an increase in ATF4 expression, which has a normal function in osteoblasts for glucose metabolism. We propose this occurs when MALEP-IFITM5 is first expressed in cells of the osteogenic lineage, leading to a permanent intrinsic change that is captured by OI-V osteoblasts, promoting the high energy demand process of biomineralization, and more fragile bones because of the high mineral content. Activation of cellular stress may also be responsible for an observed delay in osteocyte maturation in vivo, such that the normal negative feedback via SOST to suppress osteogenesis at the bone surface is impaired resulting on hypercellularity observed in OI-V bones. Together, on completion of this project, we have provided molecular insights supporting a gain-of-function outcome for a relationship between activation of cellular stress with metabolic changes, osteoblast proliferation, osteocyte maturation and mineralization; providing vital clues to the pathogenesis of OI-V. We have trained two students (one graduated, and the other near completion), one review article on the transcriptional regulation of osteogenesis and disease published, and a completed manuscript for submission, and are included in this report as reference.

17128817.label: Major findings and research outcome
17128817.value: OI-V is a complex and unique type of OI, with distinct cranio-facial features, and formation of hyperplastic callus (HPC) during facture repair, which are not common in other types of OI. While the causative gene, IFITM5, is well established with a common missense mutation (c.-14C > T) identified in all OI-V patients, its molecular consequence is unclear. The function of IFITM5 was studied by gene inactivation in mice that showed no gross phenotype, although mild bone fragility is observed due to changes in biomineralization. Thus, it is hypothesized that the MALEP-IFITM5 protein with 5 amino acid residues added at the N-terminus results in a gain-of-function or a neomorphic function outcome. There were three major research outcomes from this project. (1) From a detailed assessment of the OI-V bone samples, a defective osteocyte maturation in OI-V bone was uncovered. We then aimed to model this early process of osteoblast maturation and transition to osteocytes using an in vitro osteoblast mineralization, and through detailed proteomic assessment to showed that (2) there is an intrinsic alteration of cellular stress response, likely to be part of the integrated stress response (ISR), linked to hypermineralization, and made correlation with in vivo assessment of the OI-V bone samples. The resultant impaired osteocyte maturation will have a negative impact on SOST expression, normally suppress osteogenesis. This could lead to the observed hyperproliferation seen in OI-V bones. (3) Finally, we showed an altered energy flex in OI-V osteoblasts. In normal bone, ATF4 is thought to regulate all functions of osteoblasts linked to the maintenance of bone mass through glucose metabolism, balancing the energy requirement. There was an endogenous elevated rate of mitoATP and glycoATP production captured by OI-V osteoblasts that could facilitate active cellular proliferation and mineralization. Further, under UPR/ISR, activation of the PERK-eIF2α-ATF4 senor increases mitochondrial respiration by promoting assembly of respiratory supercomplexes that may further enhance the high level of energy demand of mineralization

17128817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17128817.value: The completion of this project has provided important insights into the impact of MALEP-IFITM5 causing OI-V. This supported a gain-of-function outcome although a neomorphic outcome cannot be rule out. Nevertheless, the intrinsic and potential further activation of cellular stress linked to the pathogenesis provided the potential to assess existing drugs that can modified the unfolded protein response and or the integrated stress response as a valuable treating for OI-V patients. With this, the availability of suitable animal models for OI-V is needed. While this could be challenging as this mutation is heterozygous lethal in mouse, a conditional mouse should be considered with specific expression in osteoblasts or osteocytes would be informative. The precise activation events following expression of MALEP-IFITM5 is still not resolved, and the cell lines that we have generated could be useful for this, and the subcloning to produce clones with varying expression levels of MALEP-IFITM5 using the Tet-on system will be useful. Indeed, combination of these experimentation and together with the current finding can form the basis of future grant application for both basis and translation research programmes.

17128817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17128817.value: Osteogenesis imperfecta (OI) is a rare genetic disorder of bone. Children with this condition are born with deformed and brittle bone, with considerable suffering and poor quality of life. There is one subgroup of OI, type V (OI-V) that we know very little about. Interestingly, all patients with OI-V have the same mutation, suggesting that if we focus on understanding what happens when bone cells start to express this mutated gene. This was the aim of this project and discover that there is a change in early bone formation (osteogenesis) when this gene is expressed, and proteins are made. This causes the cells to be “stressed”, and a response is activated, changing the cellular outcomes such as the transition of osteoblasts to osteocytes (more matured bone cells), energy needs and speed of mineral deposition. This led to a faster mineralization rate, changing the balance with less organic (collagen) and more inorganic (minerals) in the bone; and like a porcelain will break easily. These are important findings provided vital clues not only for the pathogenesis of OI-V, but potential reasoning for the treatment using drugs that can modulate cellular stress that will form the basis of future studies.

17129017.label: Realisation of objectives
17129017.value: Objective 1: a) Identify and define transition states and lineage hierarchy in the HC-Ob lineage extension and b) determine the molecular impact of Ctnnb1 deficiency on HC-Ob transition states. We employed single cell transcriptomics to identify transition states of the HC-Ob lineage. We identified 9 subpopulations of HC descendants: hypertrophic chondrocytes (HC), late hypertrophic chondrocytes (LHC), and 2 new populations we designated Transitioning 1 cells (T1; expressing Mettl20, Gdf5, Rarb and Steap4), and Transitioning 2 cells (T2; expressing Lars2 and Cox1). We also identified mesenchymal-like cells (ML; expressing Pdgfrb, Cxcl12), proliferating cells (PC), and subclasses of osteoblasts designated OB1, OB2, and OB3. RNA velocity analyses using ScVelo (PMID: 32747759) to reveal the lineage hierarchy of these populations predicted two potential trajectories from HC to OB: HC -> LHC -> T1 -> ML -> PC -> OB1, or a direct one, HC -> LHC -> T2 -> OB1, suggesting the transition from HC to OB may involve alternative differentiation paths. We identified the tdTomato+ HC-derived T1, ML and PC transition populations in Col10a1Cre;Tdtomato mice: tdTomato+ labelled HC-derived cells: T1 cells expressing, Steap4+, ML cells expressing MMP14+, and PC cells labelled by EdU+, were found in the region next to the chondro-osseous junction. HC-derived osteoblasts (tdTomato+Col1a1+) were identified by Col1a1, the marker of mature osteoblasts. The data confirm the existence of T1 and ML states in the HC-Ob transition. Their location adjacent to the chondro-osseous junction is consistent with the predicted lineage trajectory. We were unable to detect T2 cells because of the lack of suitable antibody/ in situ hybridization probes. To understand the temporal dynamics of HC-OB transition, we used HC-specific tamoxifen inducible Col10a1Cre-ERT2;tdTomato mice. We activated Cre activity by Tamoxifen injection at postnatal day 5 and analysed after a chase period of 36 hours. We found tdTomato+ Steap4+ T1 cells, MMP14+ ML cells and EdU+ PC cells were labelled, indicating HCs enter the transitioning state within 36h. No tdTomato+Col1a1+ HC-derived osteoblasts were found within 36 hours chase period, suggesting that it may take longer for HC- T1 and ML derivatives to become OB. Extending the chase period to 72 hours, we found tdTomato+Col1a1+ HC-derived osteoblasts in proximal tibia trabecular bone. These data suggest that the HC-Ob lineage transition to Ob takes between 36 hours to 72 hours. To understand the role of Wnt signaling and molecular impact of Ctnnb1 deficiency on HC-Ob transition states, we analyzed the single cell transcriptomes of HC-derivatives in HC-Ctnnb1 conditional mutants Col10a1Cre;Ctnnb1-flox mice (Ctnnb1 CKO). In mutants we found differentiated HC-derived osteoblasts were virtually absent but instead found an additional population, which we named as CKO population. Compared to wildtype mice, RNA velocity analyses using ScVelo to reveal lineage trajectory showed these CKO cells clustered close WT-ML cells but were distinct suggesting key differences despite some similarity to the wildtype ML (WT-ML) population. This result suggests that Ctnnb1 deficiency impairs the transition of ML to PC state and these cells are unable to differentiate further. Objective 2 Determine the roles and relationship between Ctnnb1-mediated Wnt signaling, and Irx3 and Irx5 in HC-Ob lineage transitions and control of osteogenesis versus adipogenesis. To understand the downstream cellular consequences of impaired WNT signaling in the HC-Ob transition, characterized the impact on trabecular bone formation in the Ctnnb1 CKO. Compared to wild-type and heterozygous control mice, Ctnnb1 CKO mice is found to have impaired trabecular bone formation at postnatal day 10 and 4 weeks old, implying that WNT signaling and HC descendants are indispensable for normal trabecular bone formation. Interestingly, cortical bone formation in Ctnnb1 CKO mice is unaffected compared to the control, suggesting that HC descendants may play minimal role in cortical bone formation. Significantly there was elevated bone marrow adiposity (BMAT) as revealed by Micro-CT analysis coupled with osmium tetroxide staining in Ctnnb1 CKO mice. Loss of β-catenin affected both constitutive BMAT (distal tibia BMAT) and regulatory BMAT (proximal tibia BMAT). The data show that HC descendants can become both types of BMAT and that WNT signaling regulates both types of bone marrow adiposity. We found that there was a significantly increased number of HC derived adipocytes in Ctnnb1 CKO mice. In contrast, the amount of non-HC derived adipocytes were not affected suggesting that the increase of adipocytes is a cell autonomous effect. The percentage of HC derived adipocytes among all HC descendants is over 10% in Ctnnb1 CKO mice compared to less than 2% in WT, and the percentage of HC derived adipocytes among all adipocytes is nearly 80% in Ctnnb1 CKO mice compared to less than 40% in WT. These data shows that with removal of β-catenin, HC descendants undergo a cell fate shift to adipogenic fate. We determined the impact of Ctnnb1 deficiency by bulk RNA sequencing and found reduced Irx3 and Irx5 expression. To understand the contribution of Irx3/Irx5 to the HC-Ob lineage we generated HC-specific Irx3/5 mouse mutants. Loss of Irx3 and Irx5 also causes bone loss in a dosage dependent mechanism, revealed by the correlation between bone mass of trabecular bone and the number of functioning Irx3 and Irx5 alleles in single and compound mutants (Irx3/5 CKO). Loss of IRX3/5 in HC lineage results in impaired trabecular bone formation and reduced number of HC derived osteoblasts. Therefore Irx3 and Irx5 play important roles in determining the osteogenic fate of HC descendants and bone marrow adiposity is elevated in Irx3/5 CKO. The bone marrow adiposity is negatively correlated with the number of functional Irx alleles suggesting Irx3/5 controls the bone marrow adiposity in a dosage-dependent manner. In the Irx3/5 CKO we found a significantly increased number of HC derived adipocytes. In contrast, the amount of non-HC derived adipocytes were unaffected, demonstrating that the increase of adipocyte number is a HC-specific cell autonomous effect. The percentage of HC derived adipocytes among all HC descendants is 5% in Irx3/5 CKO mice compared to less than 2% in WT, and the percentage of HC derived adipocytes among all adipocytes is nearly 50% in Irx3/5 CKO mice compared to around 30% in WT. These data show that with removal of Irx3/5, HC descendants undergo a cell fate shift to adipogenic fate. We found β-catenin-bound regions in the promoter and intergenic regions of Irx3 and Irx5. To investigate the relationship between WNT signaling and Irx3/5 we tested the effect of overexpressing Wnt3a ligand on transactivation of the proximal promoter regions of Irx3 and Irx5 containing conserved TCF/LEF binding motifs in luciferase reporter assays. Wnt3a overexpression drove dose-dependent increases in Irx3 and Irx5 promoter-driven luciferase reporter activities. These data are consistent with regulation of Irx3/5 by Wnt/β-catenin signaling. Objective 3. Integrate results and formulate mechanistic model of Ctnnb1-Irx3/5 gene regulatory network control of HC cell fate. We propose a regulatory model in which IRX3 and IRX5, downstream of Wnt/β-catenin, regulates the cell-fate decision of HC-derived osteoprogenitors, in which osteogenic differentiation is promoted while adipogenic differentiation in inhibited. In the physiological state, the Wnt/β-catenin - IRX3/5 regulatory axis maintains the balance of osteogenesis and adipogenesis of HC descendants. When β-catenin or Irx factors are depleted, bone marrow adiposity is abnormal revealing the importance of these factors in maintaining appropriate bone-fat balance, which may be the key for proper skeletal and metabolic homeostasis.

17129017.label: Major findings and research outcome
17129017.value: Bone function critically depends on the presence of proper proportions of different cell types in the bone marrow. We previously discovered that HCs become osteoblasts providing an additional source of bone cells in trabecular bone. However whether the process is a direct transdifferentiation process or is multi-step with transition states followed by differentiation is poorly understood. In this project we have identified the spectrum of different populations in the HC-Ob lineage through determining their transcriptomes at single cell resolution. In combination RNA velocity analyses and with validation of markers in in vivo tissue samples we identified 6 steps from HCs to Obs, implying a multi-step process in which HCs mature (LHC), enter a transition state (T1,T2), followed by differentiation to a mesenchymal-like state (ML) and re-entry to the cell cycle (PC) and further differentiation into osteoprogenitor-like stages and mature osteoblasts (Ob1, Ob2, Ob3). A minor proportion of HC-ML cells can become adipocytes. We found that the process takes at least 36-72 hours. The transcriptional regulation of the HC-Ob lineage progression is not well understood, By generating and analyzing HC conditional mutants of Ctnnb1, we identified WNT signaling and Irx3/5, as key regulators of HC cell-fate decision during the lineage progression from ML to Obs. We found different combinations of functional alleles of Irx3 and Irx5 combine to regulate osteogenesis in a dosage-dependent manner. Loss of Ctnnb1 and Irx3/Irx5 nulls, caused a severe deficit of Obs and an accompanying increase in HC-derived bone marrow adipocytes. Ctnnb1 loss of function and gain of function specifically in HCs in mutants affected expression of Irx3 and Irx5. Transactivation assays suggest IRX3 and IRX5 function downstream of WNT signaling. We therefore propose a gene-regulatory model in which WNT signaling and its downstream targets IRX3/5 control fate decisions in the transition of HCs to osteoblasts and to marrow adipocytes with significance to maintaining bone homeostasis.

17129017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17129017.value: Our study shows that WNT signaling and its control of IRX3 and IRX5 factors regulate cell fate choice of HC-derived cells between osteoblasts and adipocytes so that there is the correct balance of cell types in the bone marrow. Deficiency in Ctnnb1 and Irx3/5 results in increased bone marrow adiposity but the specific stage affected by loss of Irx3/5 is unclear. In the future it would be important to identify the downstream critical genes and gene regulatory networks for the normal transition states that maintain the spectrum of skeletal stem/progenitor cells identified in developing and mature bones. The potential impact of ?-catenin, IRX3 and IRX5 gene regulatory axis that controls the HC-osteoblast transition and BMAT on whole-body metabolism should be studied. The identification of these molecular switches controlling osteogenesis and adipogenesis has broad implications for bone biology and clinical application, and is relevant to bone diseases such as osteoporosis, metabolic disorders and age-related bone loss, and fracture healing.

17129017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17129017.value: Maintaining adequate bone mass and the correct proportions of different cell types such as bone cells and fat cells, in the bone marrow is critical for bone function and skeletal health. Our study identifies a critical role for WNT signaling and its control of two transcription factors IRX3 and IRX5 factors, in ensuring correct fate choice of chondrocyte derived cells between osteoblasts and adipocytes so that there is the correct balance of cell types in the bone marrow. Perturbing the function of these factors result in increased adiposity and reduced bone mass. Our discovery has broad implications for bone biology and clinical application, and is relevant to bone diseases such as osteoporosis, metabolic disorders and age-related bone loss, and fracture healing.

17200017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17200017.value: The aim of this project is to elucidate the vibrational and thermal-transport properties of the partially liquid-like crystalline solids (i.e., AgCrSe2 and Cu3SbSe3) using a combination of first-principles calculations and neutron scattering measurements. Partially liquid-like materials in which certain constituent atoms have large vibrational amplitudes or even flow in rigid sub-lattices were recently found to exhibit a record-low thermal conductivity (~0.2 W/mK) in inorganic crystals. Materials with low thermal conductivity are needed in various engineering fields for a range of applications such as thermal barrier coatings, optical phase change applications, and thermoelectric devices. Increased intrinsic phonon coupling that can suppress thermal conductivity to the theoretical minimum limit is key for inhibiting heat conduction. Intrinsically suppressed thermal transport is a topic of great interest because it alleviates the need for artificial nanostructures that may coarsen or become unstable at high temperatures. However, a quantitative microscopic understanding of the phonon coupling mechanisms in the partially liquid-like materials remains elusive because of the difficulties associated with conducting phonon measurements using standard in-house facilities and the limitations of the existing theoretical methods. In a preliminary effort, the PI has recently discovered that the thermal conductivity of AgCrSe2, a partially liquid-like crystalline solid, is largely overestimated by the quasi-harmonic approximation (QHA). This failure of the conventional QHA arises from the chemical bond hierarchy, which is expected to induce a novel phonon coupling for the extreme suppression of the thermal conductivity; this hypothesis will be thoroughly investigated in this project. To verify this hypothesis, a more sophisticated theoretical approach and state-of-the-art phonon measurement techniques are needed. In the proposed project, we will develop a nonperturbative approach for accurate phonon coupling calculations based on the Wiener-Khintchine theorem and efficient Born-Oppenheimer molecular dynamics integrating the density matrix extrapolation scheme. Furthermore, inelastic neutron scattering will be performed in one of the world’s most advanced neutron sources (J-PARC) to collect the phonon spectra and experimentally validate the new method. In addition to the partially liquid-like AgCrSe2 and Cu3SbSe3, we will also include AgBiSe2 and Cu3SbSe4 as model systems because these systems exhibit different thermal transport properties despite their seemingly similar chemical compositions. Successful implementation of this project will contribute to a more complete understanding of the microscopic mechanisms suppressing intrinsic thermal transport in crystalline solids and expand the ability to engineer materials for important industrial applications. 此項目擬基於第一性原理計算與中子散射技術研究含遊離原子態晶體材料（如AgCrSe2和Cu3SbSe3）中的晶格振動與熱傳導行為。研究表明，無機晶體材料中部分原子的遊離態可以極大地降低熱導率。低熱導率材料在多個工程領域有重要應用，例如熱障塗層、相變材料以及熱電轉換等。通過增強聲子間的相互作用可以有效地抑制熱能的傳導。相對於其它類型的聲子散射，該機制具有明顯的優勢；例如，納米結構雖然可以有效地散射聲子，但是高溫下納米相可能變得不穩定。然而，由於實驗測量與理論方法的局限性，目前尚缺乏對具有遊離原子態晶體材料中聲子相互作用機制的系統認識。 初步研究表明通過準簡諧近似預測的AgCrSe2的熱導率遠大於其實驗測量值。準簡諧近似的失效與化合物中由多元化學鍵所引起的聲子相互作用直接相關。在此項目中，我們將結合理論與實驗方法針對聲子相互作用進行深入研究。我們將基於維納理論與博恩奧本海默分子動力學發展一種非微擾方法計算聲子頻率與壽命。另外，我們還將通過非彈性中子散射測量聲子並與理論計算進行比對以驗證理論方法的正確性。除了含遊離原子態的AgCrSe2和Cu3SbSe3，我們還將對比研究具有相似成分但熱學性能截然不同的AgBiSe2和Cu3SbSe4。此項目的成功執行將有助於理解低熱導率晶體材料中的聲子相互作用微觀機制並為特定材料的設計提供理論指導。

17200017.label: Realisation of objectives
17200017.value: Objective 1: We have developed a computational scheme to calculate the mode-projected power spectrum density of AgCrSe2 and Cu3SbSe3, which exhibit superionic transitions at elevated temperatures, based on ab-initio molecular dynamics simulations. Phonon dispersions at 0 K have been calculated using the small displacement method. Lattice dynamics at elevated temperatures including disorder phonon scatterings in Cu3SbSe3 has been investigated, and the results are compared with Cu3SbSe4, a closely related compound but with different phonon scattering mechanisms. Phonon spectra of representative superionic compounds including full phonon coupling effects have been obtained based on a nonperturbative computational approach. Objective 2: Lattice dynamics of AgCrSe2 powder sample have been studied based on inelastic neutron scattering measurements at different temperatures. The results clearly indicate a dramatic phonon scattering effect due to the superionic transition at elevated temperature. Consistent results have been obtained based on the inelastic neutron scattering measurements and the theoretical mode-projected power spectrum density calculated from ab-initio molecular dynamics simulations, which take into account the disorder phonon scattering effects. Raman spectra of Cu3SbSe3 and Cu3SbSe4 have been measured under different temperatures to unveil the effect of superionic transition on the phonon properties. Supplementing the experimental study, we have calculated the phonon group velocities and lifetimes for further insight into the lattice dynamics of the partially liquid-like crystalline solids. Objective 3: Distribution of valence electrons in the partially liquid-like crystalline solids have been calculated based on density functional theory. Extremely weak chemical bonds are unveiled from the calculations. The loosely bonded atoms exhibit large atomic displacement parameters at low temperatures and have a diffusive behavior at elevated temperatures. The different nature of chemical bonding in Cu3SbSe3 and Cu3SbSe4 results in different phonon scattering mechanisms and distinct thermal transport properties. The thermal conductivity of AgCrSe2 has also been measured as a function of temperature using the laser flash technique. The electronic and lattice contributions to the thermal transport have been obtained. The effects of superionic transition on the phonon lifetimes of partially liquid-like crystalline solids are analyzed.
