17200017.label: Major findings and research outcome
17200017.value: Superionic crystals such as AgCrSe2 and Cu3SbSe3 manifest a part-crystalline, part-liquid state and have emerged as potential high-performance thermoelectric materials. The behavior of phonon quasiparticles, which conduct heat, however, has been long debated in the superionic state, where the sublattice is kinetically disordered. In this project, novel phonon scattering is unveiled during superionic transition of AgCrSe2. The specific low-energy transverse phonons dominated by Ag atoms totally collapse, whereas the longitudinal optical phonons arise from CrSe6 cages remain largely intact. Diffusive phonon dynamics is found to dominate the ultralow thermal conductivity of AgCrSe2 with an atomic level structural heterogeneity. A new intermediate state of Cu3SbSe3 through the mixture of quasi-1D/2D Cu nearest-neighbor vacancy hopping is discovered. Our results also reveal that phonon quasiparticles dominated by Cu atoms are strongly scattered across the superionic transition along the diffusion channel, while the diffusion is too slow to completely collapse the propagation of all transverse phonon modes in Cu3SbSe3.

17200017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17200017.value: The study of lattice dynamics signifies the critical role of liquid-like ion mobility in diffusive phonon scattering. Results of this project also suggest that large selective phonon diffusive scattering in superionic materials may be counteracted by hydrostatic pressure induced deactivation of liquid-like flow of atoms. The results facilitate an alternative phonon engineering strategy and design of related superionic materials. Large-scale simulations using accurate machine learning interatomic potentials may provide further insight into the thermal transport mechanisms of this class of materials.

17200017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17200017.value: Materials with a low thermal conductivity are required in various fields such as optical phase-change applications and thermal barrier coatings. Semiconductors with a low thermal conductivity also have a potential application in energy harvesting, e.g., the energy conversion efficiency of thermoelectric materials is inversely proportional to thermal conductivity. In insulating crystalline solids, thermal transport is dominated by lattice vibration, which is also known as phonon. In this project, we study the phonon scattering mechanisms in partially liquid-like crystalline solids and obtain a deeper insight into the strongly suppressed thermal transport of this class of materials.

17200817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17200817.value: This project will investigate diffusion processes on hypergraphs, in which each vertex has some measure and an arbitrary number of vertices can be contained in a hyperedge. Among vertices in the same hyperedge, measure will flow from vertices with maximum measure to those with minimum measure, at a rate proportional to the difference in measure. We will study new diffusion models for more general classes of hypergraphs, which will not only bring theoretical advances in spectral (hyper)graph theory and convex optimization, but also make practical impacts on applications such as semi-supervised learning and market modeling. Classical spectral graph theory relates the edge expansion properties of a normal graph, such as convergence rates of random walks with the spectral properties of its corresponding Laplacian operator. Our preliminary work completes the framework in a recent groundbreaking STOC 2015 paper that studies a diffusion process on (undirected) hypergraphs, from which a hypergraph Laplacian can be defined. Analogous to the classical results, the spectral properties of a Laplacian can be related to hypergraph edge expansion and the convergence rate of the diffusion process. We will explore diffusion processes for more general models such as directed hypergraphs, in which each hyperedge consists of a tail subset of vertices pointing to a head subset of vertices. A directed hyperedge can therefore capture a causal relationship between multiple agents. For instance, in a coauthorship network , each hyperedge contains the coauthors of a paper and its direction models how senior coauthors can influence the research direction of junior coauthors. With our recent advances in hypergraph spectral techniques, we are in an excellent position to pursue the following directions. (1) Investigate the mathematical properties of more general diffusion models. For instance, a formal framework on directed hypergraph diffusion process will shed light on how the directed version of the Laplacian can capture the underlying combinatorial properties. (2) Develop related optimization and approximation algorithms. A hypergraph induces a convex quadratic form, which is the objective to be minimized in mathematical programs for approximating eigenvalues of the Laplacian operator or assigning labels in semi-supervised learning. (3) Employ our framework for practical applications. We will test our models and optimization algorithms on real-world datasets, and compare them with existing methods. 本項目將對超圖（hypergraph）中的擴散過程進行研究，其中每個頂點有權值，且超邊（hyperedge）可以包含任意數量的頂點。在包含於同一個超邊的頂點中，權值將從最大權頂點流向最小權頂點，其速率與權值的差值成正比。我們將研究更通用的超圖擴散模型。這不僅將在譜（超）圖論和凸優化中帶來理論進展，而且還將對半監督學習和市場建模等應用產生實際影響。經典譜圖論把圖的邊擴展性，例如隨機遊走的收斂速度，與拉普拉斯算子的譜特性相關聯。我們的初步研究完善了一篇開創性的STOC 2015論文。該論文研究了（無向）超圖上的擴散過程並定義了超圖拉普拉斯算子。類似於經典結果，拉普拉斯算子的譜特性與超圖的邊擴展性以及擴散過程的收斂速度有關。我們將探索更通用的模型（例如有向超圖）的擴散過程，其中有向超邊由頂點的頭子集指向頂點的尾子集組成。因此，有向超邊可以表達多個元素之間的因果影響關係。例如，在共同作者網絡中，每個有向超邊包含論文的作者們，而超邊的方向表達了資深作者如何影響初級作者的研究方向。憑藉我們在超圖譜方面的最新進展，我們非常適合探求以下方向。 （1）研究更通用的擴散模型的數學性質。例如，關於有向超圖擴散過程的理論框架將揭示有向拉普拉斯算子如何刻劃超圖的潛在組合屬性。 （2）開發相關的優化和近似算法。超圖的凸二次公式作為數學規劃問題中的最小化目標被用於近似拉普拉斯算符的特徵值以及半監督學習中的標籤分配問題。 （3）在實際中應用我們的框架。我們將用現實世界的數據集對我們的模型和優化算法進行測試，並將其與現有方法進行比較。

17200817.label: Realisation of objectives
17200817.value: Objective 1 In a previous work [STOC 2015: Louis], a continuous diffusion process was considered on hypergraphs to define a Laplacian operator, whose spectral properties satisfy the celebrated Cheeger's inequality. However, one peculiar aspect of this diffusion process is that each hyperedge directs flow only from vertices with the maximum density to those with the minimum density, while ignoring vertices having strict in-between densities. The previous work [STOC 2015] has overlooked that in order for the diffusion process to be well-defined, the flow has to be determined by a hypergraph densest subset problem. As a first step, we have fixed this issue and established the relationship between the hypergraph Laplacian and densest subset problem. The result has appeared in JACM 2018. We have generalized the diffusion process, in which vertices in a hyperedge can act as mediators to receive flow from vertices with maximum density and deliver flow to those with minimum density. We show that the resulting Laplacian operator still has a second eigenvalue satisfying the Cheeger's inequality. Our generalized diffusion model shows that there is a family of operators whose spectral properties are related to hypergraph conductance and provides a powerful tool to enhance the development of spectral hypergraph theory. Moreover, since every vertex can participate in the new diffusion model at every instant, this can potentially have wider practical applications. This result has appeared in COCOON 2018 and TCS 2020. In addition to mediators as mentioned above, we have refined and developed a diffusion operator on a directed hypergraph in which some vertices are stationary. This unified framework is general enough for the following two applications: (i) Cheeger’s inequality for directed hyperedge expansion, and (ii) quadratic optimization with stationary vertices in the context of semi-supervised learning. Despite the crucial role of the diffusion process in spectral analysis, previous works have not formally established the existence of the corresponding diffusion processes. We have given a proof framework that can indeed show that such diffusion processes are well-defined. In the first application, we use the spectral properties of the diffusion operator to achieve the Cheeger’s inequality for directed hyperedge expansion. In the second application, the diffusion operator can be interpreted as giving a continuous analog to the subgradient method, which moves the feasible solution in discrete steps towards an optimal solution. The result has appeared in TCS 2020. Objective 2 We have designed approximation algorithms for the edge expansion and sparsest cut with product demands problems on directed hypergraphs, which subsume previous graph models such as undirected hypergraphs and directed normal graphs. Using an SDP formulation adapted to directed hypergraphs, we apply the SDP primal-dual framework by Arora and Kale (JACM 2016) to design polynomial-time algorithms whose approximation ratios match those of algorithms previously designed for more restricted graph models. Moreover, we have deconstructed their framework and simplified the notation to give a much cleaner presentation of the algorithms. This result has appeared in COCOON 2018. As aforementioned, the diffusion operator can be interpreted as giving a continuous analog to the subgradient method, which moves the feasible solution in discrete steps towards an optimal solution. We have used this intuition to consider semi-supervised learning on hypergraphs, where our method uses a convex program whose objective function is not everywhere differentiable. Based on the subgradient method, we have given a simple approach for solving the convex program. The results have appeared in TKDE 2020. The aforementioned subgradient method is based on a convex potential function. We have extended our work to consider an opinion diffusion process in which the objective function may not be convex with respect to the input parameters. Specifically, we have revisited the opinion susceptibility problem, in which agents influence one another’s opinions through an iterative process. Each agent has some fixed innate opinion. In each step, the opinion of an agent is updated to some convex combination between its innate opinion and the weighted average of its neighbors’ opinions in the previous step. The resistance of an agent measures the importance it places on its innate opinion in the above convex combination. The goal is to select the resistance of each agent (from some given range) such that the sum of the equilibrium opinions is minimized. Even though the objective function is neither convex nor concave, we have still analyzed the structure of the objective function and developed a local search algorithm that solves the problem optimally. The result has appeared in WWW 2019. Objective 3 We have also evaluated our methods using real-world datasets. For the semi-supervised learning problem on hypergraphs, our experiments on real-world datasets confirm that our confidence interval approach on hypergraphs outperforms existing methods, and our subgradient method gives faster running times when the number of vertices is much larger than the number of edges. Our experiments also support that using directed hypergraphs to capture causal relationships can improve the prediction accuracy. Furthermore, our model can be readily extended to capture multiclass learning. For opinion susceptibility problem, to investigate the practical impacts of our approaches, we have combined the iterative process and the local search paradigm to design very efficient algorithms that can solve the problem optimally on large-scale graphs containing millions of nodes. As we have established the relationship between hypergraph Laplacians and densest subset problem, we have developed practical algorithms for the k-clique densest subset problem that can be viewed as a special case of the densest subset problem in hypergraphs, which also has applications in community detection. Our algorithms can handle graphs with millions of nodes and more than a billion edges. The result has appeared in VLDB 2020. We have also considered practical fully dynamic algorithms for various clustering and partitioning problems. For the approximate maintenance of k-core decomposition, our algorithms can efficiently run on hypergraphs with millions of nodes and edges; the result has appeared in TKDD 2020. For maintaining an approximate k-center clustering, we have developed a low-memory variant that can handle millions of updates efficiently; the result has appeared in TKDE 2022.

Furthermore, we have also considered practical fully dynamic algorithms for various clustering and partitioning problems. For the approximate maintenance of k-core decomposition, our results has appeared in TKDD 2020. For maintaining an approximate k-center clustering, we have developed a low-memory variant that has appeared in TKDE 2022.

17200817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17200817.value: After this project has developed the theoretical foundation for spectral hypergraph theory that recover the basic Cheeger inequality, the next question can be whether higher order eigenvalues and eigenvectors have any significance for multi-way hypergraph partitions. Moreover, recently hypergraph cuts have been generalized to submodular functions, and it will be interesting to explore if the higher order spectral properties can also be relevant to these generalized functions. Furthermore, as cut and spectral sparsifiers have been investigated to preserve the cut or the quadratic form by a subgraph with few number of edges, it will also be interesting if the sparsifiers for submodular cut functions have any connections with the spectral properties of the hypergraphs. Finally, another interesting direction is to introduce noise in the hypergraph diffusion process. This can be relevant to applications where the communication channels are noisy, or vertices would like to protect the privacy of their sensitive data by introducing noise in the communication. Spectral techniques can be further developed to analyze the convergence behavior of such processes.

17200817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17200817.value: In this project, we have investigated various diffusion processes on hypergraphs, which have brought significant theoretical advances in spectral hypergraph theory and convex optimization and made practical impacts on applications such as semi-supervised learning. We have generalized the model to directed hypergraphs, which can capture causal relationship between multiple agents. In particular, we have used the diffusion processes to define Laplacian operators, which we have used to develop approximation algorithms for theoretical problems such as sparsest cut in hypergraphs and subgradient methods for practical problems such as semi-supervised learning on hypergraphs. Moreover, we have utilized our framework to practical application scenarios such as social network analysis and community detection. We have tested our models and optimization algorithms on large real-world datasets containing millions of nodes. This project has made significant impacts on not only theoretical research but also other areas in the wider computer science community such as machine learning and data mining.

17201017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17201017.value: Tissue engineering offers promising means for solving difficult medical problems. In human tissue repair, it involves using living cells to form implantable devices for tissue regeneration. In scaffold-based tissue engineering, scaffolds play crucial roles in cell response and new tissue formation. Simple scaffolds have been used to successfully regenerate tissues such as bone. Scaffolds developed in recent years have also incorporated growth factors (GFs) for enhancing tissue formation. But regenerating tissues such as articular cartilage, tendon and ligament are still major challenges. The extracellular matrix of human tissues is generally nanofibrous and is made of aligned-nanofibers in tendon and ligament. Electrospinning is very attractive for scaffold fabrication because electrospun nanofibrous scaffolds provide nanotopographical cues for cells. It can produce aligned-nanofiber scaffolds and can also encapsulate GFs for local delivery. However, electrospun scaffolds have several shortcomings. Lack of deep cell infiltration in electrospun scaffolds is a major obstacle. Scaffold thickness is also very limited. GFs in scaffolds normally exhibit initial burst release. Therefore, major breakthroughs in electrospinning technologies are required for realizing the great potential of electrospinning in tissue engineering. Cell electrospinning emerged recently, which can be employed for making advanced cell-scaffold constructs for enhancing tissue regeneration. This project will investigate a new electrospinning technology/process for efficiently fabricating advanced GF-incorporated cell-scaffold constructs. This technology will use concurrent emulsion electrospinning and cell electrospinning to form constructs, employing both positive and negative voltage emulsion electrospinning. For regenerating different body tissues, construct designs are different: having required thickness and different fibrous architectures (nonwoven or aligned-fiber) and using different cells and growth factors. This new technology is adaptable, accommodating different requirements. Using this technology, two types of constructs - for regenerating articular cartilage and tendon/ligament, respectively - will be designed and produced. Cell electrospinning for mesenchymal stem cells will be established first. Parallelly, formulating suitable GF-containing emulsions and emulsion electrospinning of GF-encapsulated nanofibrous scaffolds will be investigated. Using optimized parameters, advanced cell-scaffold constructs for cartilage or tendon/ligament regeneration will be formed by the new electrospinning technology. Cell-laden fibers, scaffolds and cell-scaffold constructs produced at different stages of the project will be characterized and evaluated in terms of their structure, properties and biological performance. Interplays between cells, growth factors, and scaffolds will be studied, building up a knowledge base for construct developments. The research in this project will address several important issues in tissue engineering and will provide a new, innovative approach for fabricating advanced cell-scaffold constructs.

17201017.label: Realisation of objectives
17201017.value: Through RGC’s grant support, the proposed work was performed over 42 months and all project objectives have been realized. (The original project duration was 36 months. Due to delays in experimental work and also the additional explorations in the research topic area performed by PI’s team with the full use of funds provided by the RGC, an extension of 6 months was applied for and subsequently granted by RGC.) Many journal articles and conference papers have been published for the results obtained in this project, and new manuscripts are planned and will be prepared for submission to journals. The PI (M.Wang) supervised the research and ensured the progress of the whole project and publication of results, and the Co-I (W.W.Lu of HKU’s Faculty of Medicine) had made contributions to this project. Furthermore, another of PI’s long-term collaborators (Dr. L.Zheng of HKU’s Faculty of Dentistry) was involved in this project, also assisting in the in vitro research part of this project. The research conducted in this project has addressed a wide range of problems/issues in the research topic area of this project. On the scientific side, research was performed in areas such as the formation of core-shell structured nanofibers as growth factor delivery vehicles through emulsion electrospinning, formation of core-shell structured microspheres for cell delivery through coaxial electrospray, cell fiber formation through the formulation and use of stable cell suspensions and the application of blend electrospinning, influences of electrospinning or electrospray parameters on incorporated growth factors and encapsulated cells, dual delivery of growth factor and drug, in vitro degradation behaviors of growth-incorporated scaffolds and cell-encapsulated microspheres or cell fibers, growth factor release kinetics, cell release processes and control, effects of growth factors on cells, cell-scaffold interactions, etc. On the technological side, three main technologies were investigated and developed in this project: (1) coaxial electrospray of microspheres for cell encapsulation and delivery, (2) blend electrospinning to make cell fibers (“cell electrospinning”) for cell encapsulation and delivery, (3.1) concurrent electrospinning and electrospray and (3.2) concurrent emulsion electrospinning and cell electrospinning. In addition, the emulsion electrospinning process and parameters for growth factor (or drug) incorporation were further investigated following our previous research. The design and fabrication of growth factor-incorporated and cell-encapsulated complex scaffolds (the “advanced cell-scaffold constructs”) for regenerating the targeted body tissues and many other aspects of constructing complex scaffolds were investigated. On the medical side, growth factor-incorporated and cell-encapsulated complex scaffolds for regenerating the targeted body tissues (e.g., gastrointestinal tract and tendon/ligament) were successfully made, and their in vitro biological performance was assessed. All of aforementioned work has contributed to realizing the project objectives. The RGC funding for this project has partially supported the research of three PhD students (GUO Lin, SUN Haoran and LI Huihua) and one research assistant (ZHAO Qilong). In addition, a number of MSc students and undergraduate final-year students were involved in this GRF project with their respective MSc or FYP projects. The PhD students and research assistant (as well as MSc and FYP students) were well trained in their respective research areas and their work also contributed to the successful completion of this RGF project. The PhD students had attended many international conferences, including premier conferences in our field, to present their research work and had won awards. Therefore, there are many conference papers/abstracts arising from this GRF project.

17201017.label: Major findings and research outcome
17201017.value: 1. Blend Electrospinning for Making Cell Fibers for Cell Delivery (“Cell Electrospinning”) Different cell suspensions using different types of cells (including MSCs) and different hydrogels were used to make cell fibers. Cell suspensions and hydrogels were blended for electrospinning. Key issues included cell suspension stability and achieving desired cell density in cell fibers and also controlling hydrogel biodegradation to release live cells. Some results have been presented in the publications (see Part C). This is one foundation for the project. 2. Coaxial Electrospray for Obtaining Core-shell Structured Microspheres for Cell Delivery This is another foundation for the project. Research was performed on using different polymers (and their blends) and on optimizing processing parameters to form desired, core-shell structured microspheres that could encapsulate cells in the core. Cell viability was an important issue. Detailed studies were performed some results have been presented in the publications (see Part C). 3. Emulsion Electrospinning for Making Nanofibrous Delivery Vehicles for Growth Factors (and Drugs) This is the continuation of our previous research, focusing on the polymers and growth factors used in this project. The investigations laid another foundation for this project, with journal and conference publications (see Part C). 4. Concurrent Electrospinning and Electrospray On the basis of our previous research of dual-source dual-power electrospinning, the concurrent electrospinning and electrospray technology was developed for constructing growth factor-incorporated and cell-encapsulated complex scaffolds, with colonies of high cell densities existing in scaffolds. Some research results have been published (see Part C). 5. Concurrent Emulsion Electrospinning and Cell Electrospinning For the regeneration of tendon/ligament, it is ideal that cells in scaffolds are aligned, mimicking the structure of the natural tissue. The developed concurrent emulsion electrospinning and cell electrospinning technology can produce such scaffolds. Some research results have also been published (see Part C). 6. Systematic Studies of Simple and Complex Scaffolds The different scaffolds fabricated in this project were systematically studied for their structures, properties and biological performance. These extensive studies have created a large body of new knowledge, resulting already in many publications (see Part C). 7. Extended Research Two PhD students (GUO Lin, SUN Haoran) involved in this project also performed work that opened up new research areas in tissue engineering, supplementing/complementing the originally proposed research for this project. 8. Publications Many journal and conference publications arising from this project have already appeared. New manuscripts are planned and will be prepared for submission to journals.

17201017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17201017.value: There are quite a few areas in which significant developments can be made following the research conducted in this project. For example, cell fiber technologies can be further developed. There is a growing interest in cell fibers for biology and medicine. This project has focused on producing cell fibers via electrospinning and on incorporating cell fibers in scaffolds for tissue regeneration purpose, and the project objectives have been achieved. However, there are wider uses of cell fibers and efforts can be made to widen the investigations on both cell fiber technologies (e.g., making cell fibers using other methods such as microfluidics or wet-spinning) and applications of cell fibers. Even in the tissue engineering field itself, following the research of this project, with the advantages of electrospinning (ease for fiber fabrication, versatility, etc.), concurrent emulsion electrospinning and cell electrospinning can be employed to fabricate cell-scaffold constructs for regenerate complex, layered tissues such as osteochondral tissue which require different cells and different growth factors for different layers. Furthermore, two students’ other work in their PhD projects, i.e., combination device for cancer patients by GUO and cell delivery via bijels-based scaffolds by SUN, are emerging areas in tissue engineering and requires further research.

17201017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17201017.value: In scaffold-based tissue engineering, scaffolds play crucial roles in regenerating human body tissues. Electrospinning is very attractive for scaffold fabrication because electrospun nanofibrous scaffolds provide nanotopographical cues for cells and hence enhance new tissue formation. Furthermore, growth factors, which can promote cell growth and differentiation and therefore new tissue formation, can be incorporated in electrospun fibers easily. However, lack of deep cell infiltration in electrospun scaffolds poses a major obstacle to their development for tissue regeneration. This project firstly studied cell electrospinning, i.e., using blend electrospinning to produce cell-encapsulated fibers. The cell release process and control were subsequently investigated. Moreover, electrospray of core-shell structured microspheres to encapsulate cells was further investigated. Emulsion electrospinning was refined for incorporating and delivering growth factors from nanofibers. Two technologies were finally developed for fabricating advanced cell-scaffold constructs: concurrent emulsion electrospinning and cell electrospinning, and concurrent electrospinning and electrospray. Advanced scaffolds with different cells and growth factors were produced for gastrointestinal or tendon/ligament tissue engineering. Live cells and bioactive growth factors could be released from scaffolds through scaffold biodegradation. The advanced scaffolds exhibited much enhanced biological performance. The scaffold fabrication technologies and scaffold design concepts thus developed can be used for other human body tissues.

17201217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17201217.value: Ridesharing, which involves trips of more than one participant sharing a vehicle, is a good means of dealing with traffic-induced problems (e.g., congestion, insufficient parking space, and poor roadside air quality problems) in many urban cities, including Hong Kong. Ridesharing does not require large investments. Ridesharing studies have mainly focused on the matching mechanisms of ridesharing services provided by matching agencies (e.g., Avego and Flinc) or private operators (e.g., Uber and Lyft). However, few have focused on the resultant traffic assignment problem—the problem of determining the traffic flow pattern of solo drivers, ridesharing drivers, and passengers. The resultant models can be used to evaluate the effectiveness and robustness of the transportation policy measures or incentives used to promote ridesharing. However, the current static network traffic assignment models cannot capture the departure time choice of travelers, their penalty costs for late arrivals, and the spatial effects of queues, which are important considerations for morning commutes in urban areas with short streets. Moreover, the current equilibrium dynamic traffic assignment (DTA) models and studies do not consider ridesharing in a general highway network setting, taxis and autonomous vehicles as ridesharing vehicles, different ridesharing market regimes with shared-ride taxis, and the effects of tolling, access control, and subsidization strategies on the percentage of ridesharing and system performance. Based on nonlinear complementarity problem theory, this project will aim to develop an analytical network equilibrium modeling framework and a solution method to solve and analyze a DTA problem with real-time ridesharing and shared-ride taxi services. The shared-ride taxi service can be provided by single or multiple private operators and even the government. Both normal and autonomous vehicles including autonomous taxis as ridesharing vehicles will be considered. The link transmission model will be used to depict the traffic dynamics in the presence of both normal and autonomous vehicles. This project will also aim to examine different tolling, access control, and subsidy policy measures to increase the percentage of ridesharing. It should help the government to determine the best transportation policies and ridesharing market regimes to mitigate traffic congestion and limited parking space problems under a given budget. It will also provide a case study to help the Hong Kong government to determine whether and how to promote ridesharing in Hong Kong. The modeling framework could also be easily extended to evaluate the effects of vehicle emissions or other traffic-induced externalities. 乘車共享是一種涉及多於一個乘客共用一部汽車的行程的活動。它是在許多現代化都市（包括香港）中用於處理交通相關問題（例如擁堵，停車位不足，道路旁空氣質量惡劣）的一個較好的方法。乘車共享並不需要大量投入。乘車共享的相關研究通常集中於乘車共享服務中的匹配機制。此類服務通常由匹配機構（例如Avego和Flinc）或私人（盈利性）運營商（例如Uber和Lyft）運營。然而很少有相關研究集中於與考慮到乘車共享的交通流量分配問題：如何確定自駕司機、共乘司機、共乘乘客各自的交通流量的問題。所得出的模型可被用於 促進共乘的交通政策或獎勵措施 的有效性與可靠性評估。然而，現存靜態路網交通流量分配模型並不能模擬旅客的出發時間選擇、他們的遲到懲罰成本，以及隊列的空間效應。這些都是市區短街中早上通勤時的重要考慮因素。此外，現存均衡動態交通流量分配（DTA）模型與研究並沒有考慮到以下問題：在一般公路網設置中考慮乘車共享；出租車以及無人駕駛車輛作為共乘車輛；乘車共享與出租車共乘所不同的市場製度；收費、出入控制以及津貼策略對乘車共享比例與系統表現的影響。 基於非線性互補問題理論，此項目旨在建立一個分析網絡均衡建模框架，與一個 用於求解與分析帶有實時乘車共享與出租車共乘服務的動態交通流量分配問題的求解方法。出租車共乘服務可由一個或多個私人（盈利性）運營商甚至政府提供。普通車輛與無人駕駛車輛包括無人駕駛出租車都將被作為共乘車輛考慮。鏈路傳輸模型將被用於描述同時存在普通車輛與無人駕駛車輛的交通動態。此項目還將旨在檢驗用於提高乘車共享比例的不同收費、出入控制以及津貼策略。此項目將能為政府在確定用有限預算解決交通擁堵與有限停車位問題的最佳交通政策和乘車共享市場製度時提供有用參考。此項目亦能為香港政府確定應否與如何促進香港乘車共享提供一個研究案例。此項目中的建模框架亦可被簡單地擴展用於評估車輛排放或其他交通引起的外部效應的影響。

17201217.label: Realisation of objectives
17201217.value: There were two main difficulties to realize the objectives. First, due to Covid 19, the research progress was greatly affected. Most non-local research students under the supervision of the PI returned to mainland China for more than 6 months in 2019. They thought that Mainland China was safer than Hong Kong because of having better control over the number of infected cases in most parts of Mainland China. The closure of the Hong Kong border and the lower number of infected cases in Mainland China also created difficulty in hiring new non-local research assistants or recruiting new non-local research students to work on this project. Moreover, local civil engineering students did not prefer to pursue MPhil or PhD degrees as the job market was good. Therefore, the PI could only rely on existing human resources and his research collaborators at other universities to work on the project and deliver project outputs as many as possible. Second, there was a long review process for some of the papers submitted to international journals for publication consideration so that these papers could only be published in 2021. To address objective (1), a stochastic dynamic equilibrium ride-sharing model was first developed [J1], in which travel time was assumed to be stochastic and follow a time-independent general distribution that has a positive lower bound. Due to travel time uncertainty, travelers may not arrive at their destinations on time. Different from the traditional models taking time windows as hard constraints, the proposed ride-sharing system only requires each participant to announce a role and the desired arrival time window. In the model, the generalized trip cost consists of the cost of driving a vehicle, the cost of travel time, and the cost of schedule delay early and late. The effect of the unit variable cost of driving, travelers’ values of time, and travel time uncertainty on the cost-saving of ride-sharing trips compared to driving-alone trips were investigated. A ride-sharing matching model was proposed to maximize the weighted sum of the total generalized trip cost-saving and the number of matches [J1]. The proposed ride-sharing model was further extended to consider time-dependent travel time uncertainty, and the Monte Carlo simulation method was developed to evaluate the mean generalized trip cost [J1]. [J1] indeed lays down a framework for subsequent research. For example, a dynamic equilibrium model was then developed to examine park-and-ridesharing under different parking charge schemes [J7], in which park-and-ridesharing allows drivers to park their vehicles in a designated parking lot with a fee, walk to a meeting point to wait for ride-sharing vehicles, and become riders. Moreover, a dynamic model and a solution algorithm were developed to deal with ride-hailing sharing in a general road network [J8, C1]. To address objective 2, [J4] was prepared and published. In that paper, a logit-based multi-class ridesharing user equilibrium assignment framework was introduced, which can incorporate different policy measures such as car restrictions, cordon tolling, and subsidization. The framework was formulated as a mixed complementarity problem (MCP). Numerical studies were conducted to illustrate the model properties and compare the effects of these measures under different circumstances. The result was presented at an international conference [C2]. To achieve objective (3), some background studies were first carried out [J2, J3, J5]. The first one is to propose a methodology and introduce a standard to measure the quality of taxi services [J2]. The standard had not been found yet but the level of service of taxis has to be evaluated when analyzing different transport markets with taxis. The second one is to capture the behavior of taxi owners and drivers for operating different types of taxis [J3], which is also important to be modeled to accurately evaluate the performance of a transport market with taxis. The third one aims to model vacant taxi drivers' customer-search decisions on whether to enter or bypass recommended areas while the drivers are cruising along a road with a series of taxi calling signals [J5]. These vacant taxi drivers' customer-search decisions are also important to be captured to accurately assess the performance of transport markets with taxis. A Ph.D. student was trained to deal with two of these studies. He got an outstanding student paper award from an international conference based on one of these studies. With the consideration of taxi driver behavior and the quality of taxi service as well as the models developed in [J1, J7, and J8], different market regimes were then examined, including the shared taxi or ride-hailing sharing regime [C1, J8], the ridesharing market with travel time uncertainty [J1], and the market with park-and-ridesharing [J7]. According to our literature review [J6], these regimes had not been examined at that time.

17201217.label: Major findings and research outcome
17201217.value: The research outcomes (in forms of the modeling framework, submodels, solution methodologies, and properties of studied models) and major findings were published in eight journal papers [J1]-[J8] and presented at international conferences [C1, C2]. 3 papers were published in the prestigious international journal in the field of transportation, namely Transportation Research Part B. The following summarizes the major findings. [J1] shows that the unit variable cost of driving, travelers’ value of time, travel time uncertainty, and the selection of the weight in the objective function have significant impacts on the performance of a stochastic ride-sharing system. The results also show that a feasible ride-sharing match based on deterministic travel time can become infeasible in a stochastic ride-sharing system. It is therefore important to consider travel time uncertainty when determining the matches. [J4] shows that the effectiveness of different policy measures can be greatly influenced by the performance of the transit mode compared with that of the ridesharing (or driving) mode and the users’ preference for traveling by car. The “cordon toll” policy can be better than the “access control” policy in terms of the improvement in social surplus when the performance of the competing transit system is poor. Subsidizing ridesharing (transit fares) using the toll income is the most effective when the performance of the competing transit system is poor (good). It was also found that the implementation of the cordon toll policy cannot effectively promote ridesharing when the performance of the transit system is good. [J7] illustrates that the differentiated parking charge scheme can lead to better system performance than the non-differentiated counterpart. Moreover, the time-varying parking charge scheme has a better implementation effect than the flat counterpart. In addition, the proposed park-and-ridesharing strategy can have better performance if the proportion of commuters who are ride-sharing potential participants is higher or the number of commuters is larger. [J8] demonstrates that (a) considering both travel cost and travel time ratios in the objective can achieve a better sharing percentage, and balance the increase in the travel time ratio and the decrease in the travel cost ratio compared with the objective that misses either the travel time or cost ratio; and (b) the passengers can gain a large out-of-pocket cost saving in the case of ride-hailing sharing while enduring a relatively small increase in travel time compared with the case without ride-hailing sharing.

17201217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17201217.value: One of the models assumes that the distributions of link travel times are independent of the choice of the users of the ride-sharing platform (i.e., endogenous congestion-free). In reality, the interaction and competition among users in the whole network may not only endogenize the travel time, but also impact the match and price of ride-sharing, which is one of the main revenue sources of the private platform. In the future, the interaction and competition among users in a network will be considered in the model. Moreover, another source of uncertainty, namely the demand uncertainty, will also be captured in the model.

17201217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17201217.value: This project developed methodologies to examine various transport market regimes with ridesharing activities under different policy measures such as car restrictions, cordon tolling, subsidization, and time-varying parking fee policies. The methodologies and insights from this project can help the government to make policy decisions for a transport market with ridesharing activities to mitigate traffic congestion and limited parking space problems under a given budget.

17201717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17201717.value: 建成建築信息模型（BIM）表徵著建築物的實際狀況，在建築的全生命週期中有多種應用：如施工品質檢測、設施及應急管理、修繕建議、能耗分析及拆卸等。生成建成BIM首先需要測量建築物的實際情況，一些新型非接觸式測繪技術——如激光掃描及攝影測量學等——已可以自動收集大量數據。但是，從測量數據生成建成BIM ——尤其在考慮到諸如機械特性、熱力學或材質等非幾何語義信息時——依然十分具有挑戰性。 本研究旨在開發一類基於無導數優化（DFO）的、系統化及自動化的方法，用於生成語義豐富的建成BIM。該方法採用先進的DFO算法，選擇並擬合參數化BIM組件，從而生成與測量數據最為匹配的建成BIM。例如，我們獲獎的CMA-VNS（可變鄰域搜索的協方差矩陣適配）算法將作為研發基準。本研究的可行性已在一項先導研究中獲得證實。 本研究的成果將增強運用現代數學方法開發建成BIM的認知；亦可通過分析和理解相關最優化問題的適應性景觀，從理論上闡釋建成BIM生成過程的難點。在實用性方面，本研究將為建築工程施工/設施管理（AEC/FM）行業提供一種低成本、自動化及高復用性的建成BIM的生成方法，亦可能改變整體商業技術競爭格局。

17201717.label: Realisation of objectives
17201717.value: 5.1 Scope of investigation -- BIM is the information hub of buildings and city, but it is very challenging to reconstruct from 2D images and 3D point clouds. It is more challenging to have rich semantics at the same time. -- This project presents a brand-new "Semantic Registration" method for semantically rich BIM reconstruction. -- We apply the modern DFO (derivative-free optimization) algorithms in Applied Mathematics to realize a fully automatic semantically-rich as-built BIM creation. -- Furthermore, we looked into the integration of semantics and BIM for facilities and blockchains. 5.2 Objectives achieved -- Objective 1 achieved. The formulation was first presented in a journal paper [2] (as listed in Sect. 8, Section C) and furthered in [4] and [7]. [4] named it as a new method "Semantic Registration" to the research field. A pilot study (Conference [5]) extracted from the proposal won the Best Paper Award of CRIOCM2016. -- Objective 2 achieved. In [2] and [4], we have developed a systematic way of annotating, data converting, down-sampling and organizing BIM components for Semantic Registration. A pilot study of Objective 2 (Conference [4]) won the Special Award from LC3 Innovation Competition 2017, Heraklion, Greece. -- Objective 3 achieved. The most popular DFO algorithm, CMA-ES, was benchmarked and its parameters' sensitivities were analyzed in [2] and [4]. We further compared more DFO methods, of which the results were reported in journal papers [5] and [7] formally and invited lectures (Sect. 11 [2] and [3]) verbally. 5.3 Deviations from the original plan -- N.A. 5.4 Extensions and success beyond the original plan Apart from the successful execution of the project, we also looked into a few topics related to the project. -- Journal paper [3] extends the BIM semantics with real-time updates from the Internet of things (IoT). -- [5] extends the 3D point cloud data sources, and later triggered another GRF project (17200218, HK$ 0.5M) on architectural semantics (symmetry and parallelity) to point clouds without explicit BIM components. -- [9] extends the BIM semantics with blockchain, and later led to another GRF project (17200221, HK$ 0.8M) and an ITF project (ITP/029/20LP, HK$ 10M). -- The various optimization study for the expensive processes later triggered a Theme-based Research Scheme (T22-504/21-R, HK$34M) as Co-PI.

17201717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17201717.value: BIM is the information hub of buildings and city, but it is very challenging to reconstruct from 2D images and 3D point clouds. It is more challenging to have rich semantics at the same time. This project presents a brand-new "Semantic Registration" methodology for semantically-rich BIM reconstruction. The challenging BIM reconstruction is defined as a nonlinear optimization problem first; then, semantically-rich BIM components (e.g., Revit families and SketchUp Warehouse 3D parts) can be collected freely online. We apply the modern DFO (derivative-free optimization) algorithms in Applied Mathematics to realize a fully automatic solving of the nonlinear optimization, which is visualized as a "trial-and-error" style automated creation of semantically-rich as-built BIM. Besides, we found that semantically-rich BIMs can be well integrated into smart facilities and blockchains; while DFO is also applicable to other expensive sciences and engineering problems, like generative designs of outdoor thermal comfort zones.

17201817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17201817.value: Understanding the urban air flows in calm wind conditions is crucial, as most urban heat wave and severe air pollution episodes occur when wind calmness and inversion coexist, leading to formation of a heat dome or urban heat island circulation (UHIC). UHIC comprises a convergent inflow at the lower atmospheric level, divergent outflow at the upper, and a dome-shaped flow field resulting from entrainment and overshoot at the top. Numerous field studies worldwide have confirmed the existence of UHIC during the day and night in many cities. However, most theoretical studies focus on circular or 2D heat domes. Knowledge is lacking on the effects of dome size, shape and merging, which are essential for urban planning at the city and regional levels. Our preliminary experimental study identified a new shape effect for a simple square urban area: a non-uniform flow pattern with four dominant diagonal inflows at the ground level and four dominant side outflows at the upper. We hypothesise that for a polygon city, the diagonal inflows are stronger at the surface level due to the greater development length of horizontal natural convection relative to the sides, whilst the diagonal outflow at the upper layer is weaker due to surface flow shear. This polygon city UHIC hypothesis is supported by the results of a 2003 field study in Beijing, a square-like city, which revealed, probably for the first time, that in calm wind conditions the shape of an urban area may significantly affect the winds within a city, and thus the urban air temperature or urban haze distribution would not be uniform. This shape effect also leads to the complex merging of multiple cities, i.e. the dome cluster merging hypothesis. Opportunities thus exist to optimise building density in poorly ventilated areas. Recognising the complexity of urban atmospheric air flows, the proposed study will constitute a systematic investigation of heat domes in ideal settings in terms of a city shape’s impact on 3D UHIC. The proposed methodologies include theoretical modelling, improved water tank modelling, computational fluid dynamics simulations using a newly developed city scale method and mesoscale simulations. Our HeatDome study will thus provide the first dataset on the impact of an urban area’s shape and morphology on city air flows under ideal conditions, thereby informing urban planning at the city and regional levels and paving the way for more realistic research and applications. 17201817.label: Realisation of objectives
17201817.value: Objective 1: Explore the physical mechanisms contributing to UHIC size. (Task 1.1) We reviewed the existing field measurements and numerical simulations on the horizontal extension of the urban heat dome flow. We developed an energy balance model for predicting the horizontal extension of the urban heat dome flow for night-time condition. The ratio of the horizontal extension of the urban heat dome flow to the urban diameter has an order of 1.5-4. This dome size theory has been very useful in our subsequent analysis. Additionally, we also realized that the vertical extend of the dome is important for the inversion breakup process. We used the water tank experiments to study the characteristics of the mean and turbulent flow structures of the inversion breakup process as affected by the dome height. Three stages of inversion breakup were identified, the two-dome stage, the wing-shrinking stage, and the perforative-plume stage. A journal paper has been published, i.e. Fan Y, Hunt J, Wang Q, Yin S & Li Y 2019. Building and Environment, 164, 106342. Objective 2: Elucidate the impact of an urban area’s shape and morphology on its 3D UHIC, with a focus on the complexities of the near-surface wind flows and temperature distribution (Task 1.2 and 1.3) We used a water tank model to explore the 3D UHIC flow and temperature fields in urban areas of different ideal shapes. Unlike circular heat sources, no theoretical solutions exist for non-circular sources. This is the most important part of this project. We successfully demonstrated the effects of the various ideal urban shapes, i.e. circular, triangular, square and rectangular. The urban dome flow over an equilateral polygon city is found to be characterized as a convergent inflow along the interior angle bisector at the lower level, an upward flow near the urban center and a divergent side outflow perpendicular to the side at the upper level. It is also interesting that the characteristics of the urban dome flow over a rectangular urban area highly depend on the aspect ratio of the long side to the short side. As the aspect ratio increases, the divergent flow of the short sides disappears, and those of the two long sides dominate. Moreover, recirculation exists between the divergent outflow perpendicular to the long edges and the convergent inflow near the short edges. Similar findings were also confirmed in numerical simulations as expected. Two journal papers are published, i.e. Wang Q, Wang Y, Fan Y, hang J and Li Y 2019. Building and Environment, 148(15), 433-447, and Fan Y, Wang Q, Yin S and Li Y 2019. Building and Environment, 162, 106288. Objective 3: Investigate dome cluster merging, with a focus on the cluster pattern, including the urban area shape and morphology, and the distance between cities with the cluster. (Tasks 21.-2.3) We first considered two circular cities, i.e. two interacting urban heat island circulations (UHICs) in the presence of weak background wind. The Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model was used with ideal settings without the Earth’s rotation effect. UHICs were simulated over circular cities of the same size arranged in tandem or side by side with respect to the background wind direction, at different spacing distances. We analyzed the flow structures and city ventilation arising from thermally driven UHICs and background wind. The arrangements of the cities had a significant modifying effect on the interaction between UHICs and winds. Additionally, we also consider a simpler model of triple buoyant plumes to further study the interaction mechanisms. We further determined how city shapes influence the merging of multiple domes. Again, we will consider twin, triple and quadruple domes. The combination of non-circular cities, with or without circular cities, poses a challenge for determining how the non-uniform flows of a polygon city. We have realized that we probably considered too many combinations in the original proposal with 2-4 tests to be conducted. This turned out to be impossible and probably unnecessary. However, the good thing is that we now have a robust WRF version for the idealized settings, which means that we are able to perform a large number of computer simulations for different combinations. On the other hand, we continued an early related work on interacting plumes, i.e. without inversion, also in a water tank. We considered triple buoyant plumes. We studied the flow structure, flow region parameters, and self-similarity properties at different spacing ratios S/W (source spacing S divided by source width W). From velocity fields and axial velocity profiles, a similar stream-wise developing trend is identified in different source configurations. Such a preliminary study serves the foundation for the interacting dome study. A sufficiently strong version turns the plume into a dome. We investigated a more realistic urban area of Beijing, which is a square- or kite-shaped city in appearance. We used the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model and studied the urban heat island circulations over Beijing and Tianjin during a severe UHI event in 2012. It was shown that in the daytime, various UHICs over Beijing and Tianjin developed separately under a southerly background wind. Two of these UHICs formed over Beijing due to multiple hot regions, involving a chain flow mechanism in which the outflows from one UHIC over nearby mountains were connected to the inflows to the other UHICs in a west-to-east direction. At night, more robust UHICs occurred and a chain flow mechanism again formed over the Beijing-Tianjin region, as the upper-level outflows from the UHIC over Tianjin were connected to the inflows of the UHIC over Beijing. Moreover, the rotary air movements formed by the flows over the mountain and the down-slope winds formed a convergent region in the northwest of Beijing. The city shape was found to affect the UHIC over Beijing at night, as the convergent zones were distributed diagonally and the wind speeds were higher in the diagonal. During our study, we have realized that the morphology of Chengdu is more interesting, as it is located in Sichuan Basin, with annual mean wind around 1 m/s only. Only very preliminary work is available, but not analysed as more tests are needed. This additional effort will not be wasted, and new proposal will be submitted in the near future. Two published journal papers are Yin, S, Li, Y, Fan Y and Sandberg M. (2019) Building and Environment, 149, 79-89; and Wang, Q., Zhang, C., Ren, C., Hang, J., & Li, Y. 2020. Building and Environment, 180, 107063. Note: The PI apologize that in 4 of the 7 published papers, he wrongly acknowledged GRF 17202618 instead of 17201817. The PI will ensure that no double-counting will be submitted when his project report 17202618 is submitted.

17201817.label: Major findings and research outcome
17201817.value: Less winds in a city lead to accumulation of heat, airborne moisture, and pollutants. In such a situation, a urban heat island circulation, i.e. heat dome forms. There is a convergent inflow at the lower atmospheric level, divergent outflow at the upper, and a dome-shaped flow field resulting from entrainment and overshoot at the top. There exists minimum exchange with air outside of the dome. Our major new finding is that the shape of city built-up area affects the urban heat island circulation (Fan et al., 2019, Building and Environment, 106288). For a square urban area, a non-uniform flow pattern exists with four dominant diagonal inflows at the ground level and four dominant side outflows at the upper. Using both laboratory experiments and computer modelling, we found for a polygon city, the diagonal inflows are stronger at the surface level due to the greater development length of horizontal natural convection relative to the sides, whilst the diagonal outflow at the upper layer is weaker due to surface flow shear. This is the new polygon city urban heat island circulation theory. We also found that a line city and a circulation city become two extreme cases of the polygon city theory. Two subsequent significant findings are associated with how to “destroy” such a dome, and at what conditions domes from neighbouring cities can interact. First, we identified the inversion breakup process is affected by the dome height (Fan et al., 2019, Building and Environment, 106342). Three stages of inversion breakup were identified, the two-dome stage, the wing-shrinking stage, and the perforative-plume stage. This finding is meaningful to new intervention methods of urban or regional air pollution. Second, we learned that the horizontal extension of the urban heat dome flow can be much larger than the urban diameter, with a ratio of 1.5 to 4 between the two. This provides a quantitative measure about the critical distance between neighbouring cities when multiple city heat domes may be merged or interacted. Merging of multiple heat domes means a transition from urban warming/pollution to regional scale. When two domes are interacting, a chain flow may be formed when the polluted air from one city may enter another neighbouring city. Our new theory is demonstrated over Beijing and Tianjin during a severe UHI event in 2012, as simulated by a meso-scale computer modelling (Wang et al., 2020, Building and Environment, 107063).

17201817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17201817.value: Two immediate implications lie in the minimum background wind conditions that can destroy the city heat dome, and its effects on extreme heat events. This has been followed up by PI in successfully applying for two other research grants, one from RGC on synergistic effects of heat dome and foehn wind on extreme heat events in 2018 and the other from NSFC on urban heat island circulation under weak wind conditions in a stratified environment in 2017. These two additional projects have enabled the team to synergize our research efforts. Our development has the potential to be used for city planning and design. However, it is believed that in addition to city-scale and regional impacts of the heat dome phenomenon to air pollution and warming, as a heat dome can extend 1.5-4 times of the city diameter, and up to 1 km tall, each city heat dome looks likes thermal mountain, which can block atmospheric winds. Rapid development and urbanization in China mean an increased number and intensity of large city heat domes. These heat domes might explain the wind weakening phenomenon in parts of China. Further study is being planned.

17201817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17201817.value: Most urban heat wave and severe air pollution episodes occur when wind calmness and inversion coexist. Such conditions lead to formation of a heat dome, comprising a convergent inflow at the lower atmospheric level, divergent outflow at the upper, and a dome-shaped boundary at the top. Heat dome exists during the day and night in many cities such as Hong Kong. A new city shape effect is found, i.e. the shape of city built-up area affects the urban heat island circulation. For a square urban area, a non-uniform flow pattern exists with four dominant diagonal inflows at the ground level and four dominant side outflows at the upper. Similar effects exist in a polygon city. A weak off-diagonal inflows at ground level means a low removal ability of city heat and pollutant. How to destroy such a stable heat dome is challenging. The horizontal extension of the urban heat dome flow can be 2-3 times larger than the city diameter. Multiple city heat domes may be merged or interacted if they are not sufficiently far apart, representing a transition from urban warming/pollution to regional scale, and suggesting a need for both city and regional scale design and planning.

17201917.value: 雖然建築被認為是人類有史以來最重要的發明之一，但建築也為現代社會帶來諸多挑戰，如消耗大量不可再生資源，污染自然環境，溫室氣體排放和導致的地球變暖等等。為應對這些挑戰，綠色建築運動風靡全球。在綠色建築認證系統中，認證機構會根據綠色建築項目得到的分數頒發不同等級的綠色建築證書。雖然各個綠色建築認證系統有所不同，但它們都旨在改善建築能耗，節約水資源，選址的可持續性，建築材料回收利用，以及提高室內環境質量等。當前已經有許多研究確定了綠色建築認證對環境表現和/或房屋租售價格的影響。然而，建築業產生全球固體廢物的總量多達20-30％左右，卻至今沒有研究去檢驗綠色建築認證系統對建築減廢的影響。 該研究以香港的BEAM Plus為例，檢驗綠色建築認證系統對建築減廢的影響。該研究逐步實現兩個目標。第一個目標是確定綠色建築認證系統對建築減廢的實際效果。該研究使用歷史數據來檢驗其效果：即檢驗到參與評估的綠色建築是否達到了綠色建築評級系統要求的減廢目標。該研究提出一個假設：一個項目送去垃圾填埋場的建築廢棄物量與綠色建築的得分之間應存在負相關關系。本研究從多方收集了大量數據，將充分利用這一組“大數據”來驗證這一假設。這一組“大數據”包括了過去六年來香港綠色建築經BEAM Plus的評級結果，香港所有建築廢物產生的詳細記錄，和建築項目本身的資料（如合同額，樓面面積，功能，業主等）。本研究利用這一組“大數據”來檢驗綠色建築認證系統對建築減廢的影響，這樣的二手客觀數據會使結果具有更高的置信度。第二個目標是找出並理解導致這影響的原因。該研究結合定性的“厚數據”與定量的“大數據”進行交叉驗證。其中，“厚數據”由案例研究，檔案研究，專題小組會議，以及對綠色建築專業人士的訪談的內容所組成。這項研究將幫助我們了解開發商是如何迎合政府提出的綠色建築運動，也有利於我們了解開發商的綠色建築戰略是否符合政府的期待。了解了這些，才能提出循證的建議，以更好地將建築減廢只目標融入到綠色建築認證系統中。 總體而言，本研究的結果將為綠色建築議會和其他相關機構持續改進綠色建築認證系統提供科學依據。本研究不僅會剖析出香港的綠色建築認證和建築減廢因果關系，其方法和內容也會為其他方面的類似研究提供參考，以達到促進綠色建築發展和建築減廢的長遠目標 。鑒於綠色建築認證已在全球商業化，兼之建築廢棄物管理也是全球關注的問題，因此這一研究會具深遠影響。這項研究也存在理論上的貢獻。首先，它會促進人們批判性地思考大數據分析和傳統定量分析方法的結合的利弊，同時批判性地回應現在大數據炒作現像。

17201917.label: Realisation of objectives
17201917.value: All the research objectives have been realized. For the first objective, we have explained the casual effects between getting green building certificates and willingness to minimize construction waste generation. The casual cause is explained from the perspectives of both the big data and thick data. From the side of big data, which is also the purpose of the second objective, we collected data from lorries’ load of C&D waste recorded in the Environmental Protection Department (EPD) and green labels of Hong Kong BEAM Plus that contractors applied for (Lu et al., 2018). On the flip side, the side of thick data also provides insightful perspectives from the industry. The research here was mainly qualitative and fulfilled through the semi-structured interviews with the experts from construction companies, waste recyclers, and government officers, whose combination of big data is the purpose of the third research objective. We found out that the application for green building labels in the BEAM Plus framework caused 36.19% waste reduction in demolition projects, whose effectiveness disappeared in foundation or building works. In addition, BEAM Plus building projects averagely spend 24% more than other projects but brought the limited result of waste reduction (Chen et al. 2018). Such phenomenon is explained by Illankoon and Lu (2020), where we highlighted that the current green building rating systems apparently failed to provide enough incentives for contractors to conduct with minimization, which has a higher marginal cost but earns limited credits even if all the waste reduction efforts have been made. To further enhance the internationalisation of our research works, we (Chi et al., 2020) also evaluated the impact of green buildings certificates on waste minimisation in mainland China and the US. The study is based more on archival data research and semi-structured interview. We identified that the causal effects of LEED certification on construction waste minimisation also depends on political, economic, social, and technological (PEST) conditions, which means that local governments can play an effective intermediary role in bridging the issuers of green building certificates and construction contractors. At last, the fourth research objective is to provide evidence-based suggestions for better integrating construction waste management and earning green building credits. We suggest that an isolated item of construction waste efforts should be appeared on the list of the rating system, and give it enough credits so that contractors may have more incentives to conduct waste minimization. We also called for stronger communications between stakeholders (i.e., designers (Laovisutthichai and Lu, 2020), construction contractors (Xu et al., 2020), waste recyclers (Bao et al., 2020)) and the government so that a commonly engaged design of green building certifications can be achieved.

17201917.label: Major findings and research outcome
17201917.value: We first aim to identify the causal effect between earning green building certificates and putting on efforts to minimise construction waste generation, with the application of supervised regression analysis using big data. We have successfully realized these two objectives, where four papers were published. First of all, by using cost-benefit analysis, Chen et al. (2018) identify that the BEAM Plus building projects are averagely 24% more than the regular projects. Based on the analysis results, we suggested that when Hong Kong Green Building Council (HKGBC) makes a green building rating system (GBRS), the relevant consultants should consider waste minimization as an independent indicator with more attainable credits in reward for innovation. Second, in Lu et al. (2018), we discovered that the implementation of BEAM Plus leads to 36.19% waste reduction in demolition projects, whose effectiveness fails to be observed in foundation or building works. This paper first triangulates big data with thick data in the field of waste management, where both the big data regarding waste generation rates, green building labels, building types, contract sum, etc. and thick data regarding eight semi-structured interviews (July-November, 2017) with green building professionals, construction contractors and waste recyclers are combined to give the results. We urged the raters of greening buildings to consider more of the 3R principle. I Moving forward, the comparative studies of GBRSs in an international context were also given. Lu et al. (2019) evaluated the US’s, mainland China’s, and Hong Kong’s GBRS considering construction waste management. The analysis was based on the desktop archive analysis and semi-structured interviews. The result shows that the current popular GBRSs fails to sufficiently recognize the efforts to reduce construction waste, and the contractors tend to be hesitant to fulfil the waste reduction requirement in the GBRs due to the high cost of learning and the complex document preparation. In addition, Chi et al. (2020) gave a more detailed comparison between the GBRs in China and the US through the combined analysis of the LEED certification 2009 database (big data) and semi-structured interviews with stakeholders in the construction waste recycling industries (thick data), which found out that the effectiveness of GBRs on construction waste minimisation also depends on each country’s political, economic, social, and technological (PEST) conditions. Therefore, we urged policymakers to create a suitable environment for waste reduction activities. More importantly, the making of GBRs should be cooperation among local authorities and stakeholders, which leads to consensus-based (instead of biased) green building guidelines. At last, from the perspective of life cycle analysis (LCA), Illankoon and Lu (2020) pointed out that the earning of credits of waste reduction in Hong Kong’s BEAM Plus has a higher marginal cost than other green improvement efforts such as lighting, HVAC, etc. Such a finding indicates that contractors may share a lower willingness to pay for construction waste minimisation, which weakened the effectiveness of green building rating systems in waste management.

17201917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17201917.value: This GRF has provided us with a great opportunity to reexamine the currently popular green building rating system (GBRS), and its impact on local construction contractors. Although some positive causal effects of GBRS on less-waste construction have been identified, such influence has a huge improvement space, not only in the context of Hong Kong but also the major economies such as mainland China and the US. As practitioners, we aim to propose concrete suggestions to edit the current GBRS (e.g., BEAM Plus and LEED). For example, how to optimize the on-site construction process so that the major proportion of construction waste may be sorted and recycled rather than sent to the waste fills. Another future work direction is the positive policy interventions. We argue that if the waste reduction credits issued by GBRS are not enough, we could still develop a trading platform that is similar to emissions trading scheme (ETS), where each construction project is given with a certain quantity of credits that can be sold to other contractors should they choose to actively engage in waste minimization. This solution aims to fully use the power of the market to regulate waste generation behaviors.

17201917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17201917.value: In its unique position, the construction industry consumes much more natural resources than other industrial sectors, whose generated solid waste threatens Hong Kong’s ambition for a zero-waste city. The popularity of the green building rating system may shed a light on construction waste minimisation progress. Therefore, we studied the causal effects of green building certifications on construction waste management in Hong Kong, mainland China, and the US. The research method innovatively adopts the triangulation of big data (which means real-world statistics) and thick data (which means the observation and experiences of stakeholders and policymakers). By doing so, we seek to better understand the waste generation behaviors under real market status from the collected data while correcting its potential deviations by thick data. Our results show that a positive push is witnessed where contractors under Hong Kong’s BEAM Plus green building crediting system are willing to reduce 36.19% of their waste generation in exchange for more green credits. However, the effectiveness is limited, which is why we urged closer cooperation between the government and industry to push the green building practice to a higher level.

17202317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17202317.value: 頭頸鱗狀細胞癌在世界範圍內影響著約55萬人，是全球第五大常見癌症。 在香港，截至2013年，僅鼻咽癌（NPC）在最常見的癌症排名中已位列第十，在男性常見癌症中排名第六。除去NPC，頭頸癌（HNC）仍是男性中第九大常見癌症，且患病者絕對數量仍在持續增加。 針對該癌症的治療通常圍繞著手術，放射治療和化學療法三種手段進行，後兩者有其自身的毒副作用。然而，採用開放式手術治療HNC，將引致顯著的發病率。在此基礎上，微創手術的引進將為減少手術創傷提供可能性，同時有助於降低涉及言語、吞嚥和面部美觀等關鍵結構的長期損傷。 目前針對HNC的微創手術，即便輔以機器人，仍缺乏在三維中進行充分的手術計劃的能力，並且依賴於外科醫生的經驗，特別是當需要切除腫瘤中不易直接觀察到的深層部分。而藉助於磁共振圖像（MRI），腫瘤切緣可在三維中進行計劃，然後采用激光切除。該手術方法將在保留了關鍵結構的基礎上，保證足夠的手術切緣。 此外，HNC和激光誘導的生理變化在術中的可視化將通過T2加權或擴散張量的MRI成為可能，從而允許外科醫生迅速判斷腫瘤切除術是否完成或安全執行。 該項目的總體目標是開發和驗證磁共振安全/條件磁共振兼容的內窺鏡機器人系統，其中包括液力致動、術中MRI和具有快速磁共振溫度成像的增強激光導航三個部分，以提高腫瘤在口鼻咽（ONP）腔中的切除準確性。我們提出了一種能夠牢固錨定到牙科手術防護裝置上的小型經口機器人設計，該機器人能在狹小腔道中靈活地抵達ONP的病變部位。它將為儀器遞送提供穩定的內窺鏡平台，以及在期望的消融裕度內的激光束導航。 使用基於磁共振的低誤差（<0.4mm）高頻率（> 30Hz）射頻半主動位置跟踪，以及利用磁共振測溫法進行在線消融溫度監測，將有助於在相同的MRI坐標中為原位視覺反饋提供可靠指導。先進的基於學習的控制方法也將構建，以對現有方法所存問題進行改進。現有方法的問題是，不能在狹小空間中為長、細、柔性的連續體機器人提供穩定，平順和一致的運動學控制。該系統將與現有的遠程操作機器人系統有根本區別。現有的遠程操作機器人受制于相機圖像的單一引導，無法進行高效率地組織切除。本項目提出的系統將是首次同時集成了術內MRI和在線磁共振測溫，以實現激光顯微外科手術的高精度柔性機器人/內窺鏡導航的系統。基於實驗室和MRI的詳細定量驗證實驗也在本項目中提出。 該項目的成功將代表著該手術向更安全、更準確和更有效的發展方向邁出的重要一步。 它將顯著增強腫瘤切除精度，以保持最佳的解剖和功能完整性，並且還可以解決經口儀器在對接/定位過程中的複雜程序，從而通過切除后切緣即時原位的MRI評估來減少手術時間（至少40-50％）。這些成果將建立針對早期癌症的治療新標準，為易引致眾多副作用的傳統放射治療提供替代方案。

17202317.label: Realisation of objectives
17202317.value: The PI and his collaborators have developed a magnetic resonance (MR)-safe endoscopic robot system allowing flexible access to lesions in the confined oral and pharyngeal. The system provides a stable platform for laser beam delivery and navigation to the targeted lesions under MR imaging (MRI) guidance. The robot is compact and lightweight, enabling mounting on the patient and operation with standard imaging coils under MRI. Integrated with an optical laser fiber, the robot enabled endoscopic laser delivery and operating in the oropharyngeal region with submillimeter accuracy (<~0.2 mm) which meets the clinical requirements on laser spot targeting (<1 mm). A patient-specific dental guard was designed to create an open-jaw cavity for robot anchorage and access of auxiliary instruments such as a fiberscope. The entire robotic system passed MR compatibility testing with no EM artifacts, which allows full robot operation during imaging even at the MRI scanner isocenter. The team also conducted pre-clinical validation of the system on cadaver with CUHK surgeons, Dr. Po-Ling Chan, Prof. Jason Ying-Kuen Chan, Dr Danny Chan Tat-ming, and MRI scientist, Dr. Hing-Chui Chang. The feasibility of this innovation has been proved in the current clinical setup. By introducing MRI guidance, clinicians could have intuitive and precise feedback of the ablation process, which is critical for function preservation of surrounding structures. The robot comprises two actively steerable soft continuum segments that are driven by microvolume liquid flow (<0.004 ml) to the internal elastomer chambers, which are individually integrated with spring reinforcement constraints. The spring reinforcements were designed and optimized through finite element analysis (FEA) to balance between robot bending stiffness and maximum local stresses, thus enhancing robot response with minimized hysteresis while maintaining adequate robot durability. The distal laser manipulator actuation is effectively decoupled from the active bending section, allowing stable and repeatable kinematics and thus high-accuracy laser control. The active bending section offered a 60° omnidirectional bending workspace for coarse navigation to the region of interest. The distal laser manipulator allowed fine laser beam pan-tilting (±26°) in a local target area, with a maximum scanning area of 15 mm by 15 mm at a 15-mm projection distance. A learning-based modeling method was implemented to characterize the robot kinematics, which establishes the mapping from laser spot movements on the projection plane to robot actuation. A visual servoing controller was implemented to achieve automatic targeting of the laser spot that could be projected along any trajectory that is prescribed in situ on the endoscopic view. The controller was tested via path-following experiments with various patterns, e.g., a symbol of a bat and zigzag filling, which demonstrated submillimeter accuracy in both tracking a boundary and filling an area. Three MR fiducial markers fabricated from capsulized gadolinium-doped water (concentration: 10 mM) were integrated with the dental guard to localize the robot base in MRI coordinates. Specifically designed miniature wireless MR resonators were integrated into the fiducial markers to locally amplify their signal, providing high SNR even under low flip angle excitation (1°). The resonators are flexible printed LC circuits tuned to the Larmor frequency (63.87 MHz). The fiducial markers show high contrast in anatomical MR images, thus enabling positional localization. On the basis of the preoperative 3D imaging, positions of the markers can be identified from the anatomical background. With 3D positions of three markers inside the dental guard, point-based rigid registration can be performed to locate the dental guard and the robot base in MR image coordinates. Alternatively, using 1D-projection gradient readouts, the marker positions could even be obtained in real time (~30 Hz). Besides the above-mentioned research efforts, this innovation has just been reported in the international journal Science Robotics, which is the top-ranked journal in robotics field. This work was also reported in a press conference on “CUHK and HKU Successfully Develop a Soft Robotic Manipulator for Intra-operative MRI-guided Transoral Laser Microsurgery”, which was covered by 13 media outlets.
