17202317.label: Major findings and research outcome
17202317.value: A magnetic resonance (MR)-safe endoscopic robot system is proposed that allows flexible access to lesions in the confined oral and pharyngeal. The system provides a stable platform for laser beam delivery and navigation to the targeted lesions under MR imaging (MRI) guidance. The robot is compact and lightweight, enabling mounting on the patient and operation with standard imaging coils under MRI. Integrated with an optical laser fiber, the robot enabled endoscopic laser delivery and operating in the oropharyngeal region with submillimeter accuracy (<~0.2 mm) which meets the clinical requirements on laser spot targeting (<1 mm). Miniature spring reinforcement constraints (SRCs) were integrated into the laser manipulator to enable repeatable and accurate steering of laser beam. FEA was conducted to simulate the robot characteristics upon pressurization, thus facilitating the design optimization. A visual servoing controller was implemented to achieve automatic targeting of the laser spot that could be projected along any trajectory that is prescribed in situ on the endoscopic view. Reference Publication: Part C [18] [10][8] Three MR fiducial markers fabricated from capsulized gadolinium-doped water (concentration: 10 mM) were integrated with the dental guard to localize the robot base in MRI coordinates. Specifically designed miniature wireless MR resonators were integrated into the fiducial markers to locally amplify their signal, providing high SNR even under low flip angle excitation (1°). The resonators are flexible printed LC circuits tuned to the Larmor frequency (63.87 MHz). The fiducial markers show high contrast in anatomical MR images, thus enabling positional localization. On the basis of the preoperative 3D imaging, positions of the markers can be identified from the anatomical background. With 3D positions of three markers inside the dental guard, point-based rigid registration can be performed to locate the dental guard and the robot base in MR image coordinates. Reference Publication: Part C [12] A hydraulic actuation approach is taken for its intrinsic MR safety and ability to miniaturize the robot design by allocating the larger actuator systems to outside of the MRI room. A rolling-diaphragm sealed hydraulic motor was integrated to advance the bending sections. The hydraulic motor provides a maximum linear stroke of 20 mm, driving each pinion by 100.6° and corresponding to a 50-mm robot insertion that is capable of reaching the oropharyngeal area. Reference Publication: Part C [5] [6]

17202317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17202317.value: In our future work, we plan to implement real-time MRI sequences customized for the laser ablation monitoring, optimizing for higher temporal resolution while maintaining sufficient imaging (spatial) resolution. Custom real-time sequences interleaving multislice anatomical and thermometry images bring the potential for greatly enhanced ablation monitoring and could enable automated laser ablation control based on MRI feedback. We also aim to overlay in situ MRI on the fiberscope camera view, providing an augmented reality environment to further assist surgeons in evaluating the ablation process. A promising extension of this work is to couple optical coherence tomography (OCT) with the ablation setting by adopting the lens-pigtailed optical fiber as an OCT sampling arm, which can provide tissue depth images in micrometer-scale resolution. Alongside with the proposed laser steering mechanism, scanning paths/patterns could be performed to form 3D forward-viewing OCT images underlying the lesion. Visual servo of the laser spot projected on tissue would enable the operator to prescribe any preferred OCT scanning profile in situ in the endoscopic view, thus facilitating tissue/tumor characterization at the cellular scale, apart from using MRI.

17202317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17202317.value: This work proposed the first-ever soft robotic manipulator for magnetic resonance image (MRI) guided transoral laser microsurgery. The system generates zero electromagnetic (EM) interference, allowing the introduction of intra-op MRI guidance to evaluate the laser/tissue interaction process, which plays an important role in balancing adequate tumor resection and function preservation. The system provides a stable platform for laser beam delivery and navigation to the targeted lesions under MRI guidance. The soft robotic system is compact (Ø12 × 100 mm) and lightweight (~200 g), while providing five degrees of freedom (DoFs) motion under MRI. Integrating with a laser fiber, the robot enables flexible delivery and precise targeting of surgical lasers. A miniaturized laser manipulator is designed with optimized reinforcement to provide delicate laser beam steering (±26°) in a confined area. The manipulator is actuated through microvolume (<0.004 ml) fluidic inflation of elastomer chambers, which are regulated with a learning-based controller. During laser ablation, MR thermal imaging can be conducted to evaluate the heat diffusion in tissue, thus offering real-time monitoring of the ablation margin. 3D MR scanning can be performed intraoperatively to enable in situ assessment of the ablation completeness.

17202617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17202617.value: Open space is an essential part of a livable city. Parks, playgrounds, green spaces and public space do not only contribute towards improving the environment of a city, but they also enhance the physical and mental health of its urban population. The benefits of open space are well proven and documented in the existing research literature. What has been less explored, however, is about whether urban open space is indeed spatially planned, distributed and provided in such a way that it becomes easily accessible to urban users. This question is particularly relevant to the city of Hong Kong. Land costs are extremely high in this city due to the scarcity of urban land and a huge demand for urban development. Government planners are under enormous political pressure to identify suitable vacant land and convert it into affordable housing and other competing land-uses. Supply of public open space in Hong Kong is further complicated by the separation of bureaucratic responsibilities between planning and management of this land use. In other words, public open space that exists on town plans may not actually get developed and implemented by the government authority. This study examines the supply and spatial distribution of open space in Hong Kong with a specific focus on exploring its disparity across different localities and its access to potential users. This proposal seeks to extend the PI’s completed GRF projects on this topic, which have identified a number of important findings and interesting observations. First, huge inconsistency exists in the zoning and actual development of public open space projects. Second, preliminary analysis of the land-use zoning pattern on town plans has unveiled some spatial logic of the planners, which may support a disproportionate distribution of open space in the territory. Third, recreation has not been the sole purpose of the authority in the provision of public open space. A historical review of urban development of Hong Kong elucidates that open space planning has been influenced by factors related to colonial politics, racial harmony, public hygiene considerations and democratization. Finally, the recent trend of Hong Kong in expanding new open space network in strategic waterfront locations and near commercial zones, for the purposes of place marketing and urban competitiveness, may encourage its commodification and deprive the right of access to the underprivileged community. This study is intended to assemble additional data to support more rigorous analysis of these issues. 休憩空間是宜居城市的重要組成部分。公園，遊樂場，綠地和公共空間不僅有助於改善城市的環境，也增強了城市人口的身心健康。休憩空間的好處在現有的研究文獻中已得到了很好的證明和記錄，但是關於空間分佈和提供給市民便捷使用的問題則較少研究。這個問題對香港特別重要。由於城市土地稀缺和城市土地需求旺盛，令土地成本極高。政府規劃師面對巨大的政治壓力，要找出適當的空地，並將其轉化為經濟適用房和其他經營性土地利用。加上在香港提供規劃和管理公眾休憩用地的責任由政府不同的行政機關執行，城市規劃中存在的公共空間實際上可能並沒有開發。本研究旨在探討香港休憩空間的供應及空間分佈，特別側重於探索不同地區之間的差異及與使用者的連接問題。本計劃旨在延續和擴大PI在已完成的GRF項目主題，該項目已經有一些重要的發現和有趣的結果。首先，休憩空間在分區規劃和實際發展上存在巨大的矛盾。二是休憩空間在分區規劃的初步分析中看到，可能出現空間分配不成比例的情況。第三，休憩娛樂並非提供公共休憩空間的唯一考慮，回顧香港的城市發展歷史發現，休憩空間規劃受到殖民政治，種族和諧，公共衛生，民主化等因素的影響。最後，香港近期不斷擴大在海濱地區和商業區附近的新休憩空間網絡，加強地方營銷和城市競爭力，可能更進一步鼓勵公共空間商品化，剝奪弱勢社區的權利。這個研究旨在搜集相關數據去分析以上的問題。

17202917.label: Project Objectives
17202917.value: The present proposed study expands on the PI’s previous works by assessing the effectiveness of a number of text enhancement methods on the accuracy of look-alike drug name differentiation in a computer-based “same-different” differentiation experiment among nurses. The study aims to evaluate (i) whether or not and which text enhancement methods would render look-alike drug names more visually distinct and thus improve name differentiation performance, and (ii) the nurses’ visual scanning strategies and detection during the drug name differentiation process, by analyzing data of differentiation accuracy, frequency of eye fixations, and fixation durations. For eye-tracking data, we will measure the fixation frequency and durations on two areas of the experimental drug name stimuli: (i) the whole names (area of interest 1 in Figure 1) and (ii) the differing letters being highlighted in text enhancement conditions (area of interest 2 in Figure 1).

17202917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17202917.value: 令人混淆的藥物名稱可能會導致藥物辨別出錯，和對處理這些藥物的醫護人員 (如前線護士) 造成挑戰，並可能導致藥物分配和管理錯誤，從而對病人安全構成威脅。為了使醫護人員更容易地辨別擁有相似藥名的藥物，本研究評估 (i) 使用 “文本增強方法” (就是改變藥物名稱的不同字母的視覺屬性，例如，大小，筆劃寬度，以使它們的外觀看起來更加顯眼，更易區分) 是否能夠改善或增強醫護人員在辨別類似藥物名稱之能力，以及使用護士的視覺掃描策略和藥物名稱分別過程中的視覺行為數字作分析。

17202917.label: Realisation of objectives
17202917.value: The objectives of the study were examined and realized through a series of experiments (see Liu et al., 2019 and Wang and Or, 2019 listed in Part C section 8 of this report). More specifically, five experiments that tested 150 human subjects with nursing background were conducted to examine (i) whether or not and which text enhancement methods would render look-alike drug names more visually distinct and thus improve name differentiation performance and (ii) the visual scanning strategies and detection. Outcomes that were used to indicate the differentiation performance and visual behaviors included differentiation accuracy, recognition memory accuracy, response time, frequency of eye fixations, fixation durations, pupil diameter, perceived mental effort, and perceived error likelihood. In two of the experiments, we evaluated the following text enhancement methods: lowercase (i.e., no text enhancement; for example, lamivudine vs. lamotrigine), Tall Man (e.g., lamiVUDine vs. lamoTRIgine), reverse Tall Man (e.g., LAMIvudINE vs. LAMOtriGINE), boldface plus red (e.g., lami[vud]ine vs. lamo[tri] gine; the letters in brackets are presented in red boldface), and boldface plus contrast (e.g., lamivudine vs. lamotrigine). We also examined the impacts of disfluency text format in three experiments. Other factors that were hypothesized to influence visual differentiation and eye behaviors were also assessed, including exposure time, visual cues, identical prescription-package names, and verbal provocation.

17202917.label: Major findings and research outcome
17202917.value: The two experiments reported in Wang and Or (2019) showed that text enhancement had no significant effect on the drug search. Nurses selected the target drugs more quickly and easily when the prescriptions and drug packages shared identical drug name formats. The use of a visual cue to direct nurses’ attention facilitated their visual searches and improvedtheir eye gaze behaviors. The nurses reported greater mental effort if they were provoked verbally during the drug search. The three experiments reported in Liu et al. (2019) indicated that making drug names disfluent did not significantly improve differentiation or memory accuracy, but even impaired differentiation accuracy. Enhanced text and longer exposure time significantly improved differentiation accuracy. However, the enhanced text did not improve recognition memor. We suggest that making look-alike drug names disfluent is not favourable. Enhanced text and longer exposure times are effective in supporting visual differentiation of look-alike drug names.

17202917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17202917.value: Based on the findings of the experiments, we concluded that efficient and practical strategies should be adopted for designs that facilitate accurate drug search. Among these strategies are using identical name appearances on drug prescriptions and packages, using a visual cue to direct nurses’ attention, and avoiding rushing nurses while they are concentrating. We also emphasized that confusion arising from look-alike drug names may compromise patient safety. Three experiments examined the effects of disfluent format, text enhancement and increased exposure time on visual and memory performances. Making drug names more difficult to read did not improve performance. Enhancing text design and increasing exposure (i.e. reading) time improved visual differentiation between medications, but did not improve the recognition of medications from memory. Research is needed to test the impacts of the recommendations and suggestions on safety performance in actual practice.

17202917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17202917.value: Look-alike drug names can create confusion which can lead to perceptual and memory errors in the preparation and administration of the drugs. It is therefore important to find ways to avoid such errors. We used simulation and eye tracking in multiple lab-based experiments to examine the effects of text enhancement, identical prescription-package names, visual cues, verbal provocation, processing difficulty, and exposure time on visual searches and differentiation accuracy of look-alike drug names. Nurses selected the target drugs more quickly and easily when the prescriptions and drug packages shared identical drug name formats. The use of a visual cue to direct nurses’ attention facilitated their visual searches and improved their eye gaze behaviors. The nurses reported greater mental effort if they were provoked verbally during the drug search. Enhancing text design and increasing exposure (i.e. reading) time improved visual differentiation between medications, but did not improve the recognition of medications from memory. Making drug names more difficult to read did not improve performance. Confusion arising from look-alike drug names may compromise patient safety. Our research findings aim to inspire recommendations for work system and task designs that will improve the accuracy of the visual search and differentiation of look-alike drug names.

17203017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17203017.value: In the majority of countries traffic drives on the right, including the People’s Republic of China, the U.S., and European countries. Around 65% of the world’s population lives in these countries where traffic is right-drive (RD), with the remaining 35% in countries with left-drive (LD) traffic, including Hong Kong. Different traffic rules obviously lead to different attitudes and conventions when people cross roads, and the risk of injury to foreign visitors is higher when they use the roads as pedestrians. Pedestrian safety is an important social topic, as every year over 270,000 pedestrians lose their lives on roads, constituting 22% of all road traffic fatalities. Hong Kong is one of the most densely populated areas in the world, with a substantially high rate of pedestrian fatalities, accounting for over 60% of all traffic deaths. As a major Asian city, it receives many foreign visitors, but no studies have been conducted on the risk of traffic injury to them. Considerable research has been conducted to evaluate the risk-taking factors associated with pedestrian injuries and fatalities at road crossings, and mainly focus on crossing configurations, pedestrian characteristics, and pedestrian behavior. Studies on the personality characteristics of pedestrians, such as their cognitive perceptual skills, have also been carried out from the psychological perspective. Most studies have, however, evaluated unsafe pedestrian crossing performance from a single viewpoint. A comprehensive risk assessment, integrating the perceived intention in the decision-making to cross and the actual crossing performance, is required to fill this research gap. To study the perceived intention, a tailor-made questionnaire based on the theory of planned behavior will be used to examine the age-related physical and cognitive perceptual skills of pedestrians. By taking advantage of mature CAVE-based virtual reality (VR) technology, a well-developed fully immersed pedestrian simulation test will be conducted, to measure the actual pedestrian crossing performance. A comprehensive risk perception assessment using a series of hierarchical mathematical models will be provided, aimed at integrating pedestrian crossing intentions and the behavior of pedestrian from countries with different traffic rules. 目前世界上約有65%的人口生活在左舵右駛規則的地區，例如：中國、美國和歐洲等國家，而餘下的人口則生活在右舵左駛規則的地區，包括香港。因為左右舵駕駛規則會影響行人過路的態度和習慣，所以行人在不同的左右舵駕駛規則的地區過路時可能面臨更大的風險。行人安全是一個重要的社會課題。據統計，每年有超過27萬的行人因交通意外而死亡，佔交通意外死亡總人數的22％。香港作爲世界人口最稠密的地區之一，行人的死亡人數佔全部交通意外死亡人數的60％以上。雖然香港每年接待大量的外國旅客，但並沒有學者對他們在香港面臨的交通意外風險進行研究。為了解行人過路的受傷和死亡的風險及其原因，學術界已進行了大量針對路口設置、行人特徵和行為的研究。部分研究亦從心理學的角度探討了行人過路時的認知及感知能力。可是大多數的研究只從單一的角度評估行人的危險過路行為。有見及此，我們須要進行一項結合行人過路時的感知意向和其實際過路行為的研究來評估行人過路風險以填補這個研究空白。本研究會根據「計劃行為理論」設計問卷以調查與年齡相關的行人感知意向。另一方面，我們會利用基於「CAVE」的虛擬現實技術進行完善的行人仿真實驗，以觀察實際的行人過路情況。最後，為了解不同的左右舵駕駛規則對行人過路的風險，本研究將結合問卷調查和虛擬現實技術仿真的結果，使用一系列的數學模型以分析行人過路時的心理感知和實際過路行爲。

17203017.label: Realisation of objectives
17203017.value: To achieve Objective (1), the immersiveness of CAVE-based VR technologies was examined by administering four carefully designed questionnaires to the participants during the VR experiments: a background information questionnaire, a simulator sickness questionnaire (SSQ), the Independent Television Commission–Sense of Presence Inventory (ITC–SOPI), and a pedestrian characteristics questionnaire. Upon registration, the participants were required to complete a background information questionnaire to provide information on their sex, age, nationality, driver’s license, and contact details. This information was used to allocate the participants to the experimental groups in a demographically balanced manner. The SSQ contains questions pertaining to nausea, oculomotor disturbances, and disorientation, and was used to record the extent of sickness experienced by the participants in the imseCAVE-based VR pedestrian simulator. The ITC–SOPI was used to assess the participants’ perception of the virtual environment, in terms of its spatial presence, engagement, ecological validity/naturalness, and negative effects. Spatial presence is the essential element for performance in both teleoperated and virtual environments, and thus typically enhances the intended outcome of a system. For example, in training simulations, spatial presence enhances training transfer. Hence, spatial presence is practically relevant in system evaluations. The ITC–SOPI is commonly used as a metric in spatial presence questionnaires and has been introduced in driving simulator studies, clinical settings, usability studies, and industrial applications to measure the sense of spatial presence in various media systems and evaluate the experiences putatively related to spatial presence. The ITC–SOPI was also used to evaluate the immersiveness of the imseCAVE-based VR pedestrian simulator and thereby determine the reliability of the results obtained from the VR experiment, and immersiveness scores ranged from 1 to 5. The pedestrian characteristics questionnaire was used to record the characteristics of pedestrians from areas with different traffic systems. To minimize the simulator sickness experienced by the participants, the SSQ was administered before the experiment and after each experimental scene. Although the simulator sickness increased over time, the imseCAVE-based VR pedestrian simulator was found to be immersive, and the experimental results were reliable. To achieve Objective (2), the relationship between pedestrian performance and intention factors (e.g., head movement behavior, traffic accidents, and near-miss scenarios) and independent factors (e.g., traffic environment settings and pedestrian demographic information) was investigated by examining pedestrian behavior in video recordings made on site. Additionally, a questionnaire survey was conducted to collect the views and perceptions of road users (participants) from two driving systems: the left-hand-side driving system of Hong and the right-hand-side driving system of mainland China, respectively). To obtain an adequate sample of mainland Chinese participants (i.e., visitors to Hong Kong), surveys were administered at many sites popular with tourists in seven locations in Hong Kong. Well-trained research assistants administered the questionnaires face-to-face with participants. The questionnaire consisted of three sections of questions regarding participants’ demographic information, whether they habitually looked right before crossing a street, and the extent of their maladaptation to the left-hand-side driving system of Hong Kong, respectively. The participants’ demographic information consisted of their sex, age, education level, driver status, hometown driving system, length of stay in Hong Kong (in applicable), and travel purpose. A structural equation model was applied to determine the relationship between the participants’ hometown driving system, length of stay, right-looking habit, and maladaptation. The findings of this study are empirical evidence of pedestrians’ looking habits and maladaptation to unfamiliar driving systems, and can thus facilitate the development of measures to ensure the safety of foreign pedestrians. Moreover, the findings can serve as reference for the design of VR experiments to clarify pedestrians’ actual crossing behaviors in various environments. To achieve Objective (3), participants who were resident in an area with a left-hand-side driving system (Hong Kong) and those who were resident in an area with a right-hand-side driving system (mainland China) were recruited for CAVE-based VR experiments. First, the participants were introduced to the imseCAVE system and allowed to familiarize themselves with its operation. Next, each participant was exposed to two practice scenarios and eight experimental scenarios consisting of various road-crossing combinations. Each scenario contained five parallel one-way streets with randomly allocated driving directions to simulate the different driving systems. The scenarios to which participants were exposed depended on their place of residence and the traffic direction. That is, participants from Hong Kong were exposed to scenarios in which traffic approaching from the left was traveling on the right-hand side of the street and traffic approaching from the right that was traveling on the left-hand side of the street, and participants from mainland China were exposed to scenarios in which traffic approaching from the left was traveling on the left-hand side of the street and traffic approaching from the right was traveling on the right-hand side of the street. The participants were subjected to Raven’s IQ test after they crossed each pair of virtual streets to enhance their engagement, hold their attention, motivate them to complete all of the scenarios, and clarify their habitual street-crossing behaviors. Each test question requires the participants to use a controller to interact with the “question box” to identify the missing element that completed a pattern of shapes from six or eight candidate elements. The graphical interface of this test enables its application to any situation, irrespective of the language spoken by participants. To determine the direction in which the participants habitually looked first when crossing a street, a generalized estimating equation was used to conduct a first-look analysis of the longitudinal data consisting of repeated measurements of each participant’s behavior. A quasi-likelihood-based model-selection criterion was used to select the working-correlation structure and model. To address the unobserved heterogeneity associated with repeated measures, a random-effects approach was used to model the participants’ crossing performance measures. To explore the crossing behaviors of drunk pedestrians in unfamiliar traffic systems, the temporal profile of alcohol concentration—which indicates the effects of nonlinear nature of alcohol absorption, peak breath alcohol concentration (BrAC), and elimination—of a Chinese population after a light meal was determined. This profile is useful for designing VR experiments that can realistically capture the full range of effects of alcohol concentration on pedestrian behaviors. Subsequently, VR experiments were conducted to examine the street-crossing behaviors of local pedestrians before and after alcohol intake and in familiar and unfamiliar traffic systems. To evaluate the crossing behavior of drunk participants in unfamiliar traffic systems, they were required to repeatedly cross many streets in similar VR simulations of unfamiliar traffic systems, before and after alcohol consumption. To ensure a fair comparison, the experiments conducted before and after alcohol consumption were identical; however, the sequence of scenarios after alcohol consumption was randomized for each participant to avoid possible correlations between BrAC and scenario settings. During the experiment, the participants’ body movements and reactions to traffic environments were recorded using the imseCAVE system. Because the participants crossed multiple VR-simulated streets, and their crossing behaviors were observed over time, the collected data were panel data. Thus, these data could not be analyzed using traditional models, as these can only process cross-sectional or time-series data. Accordingly, to account for any unobserved heterogeneity, the panel data were analyzed using random-effect modeling. The findings help to quantify the negative effects of alcohol consumption on pedestrians’ crossing performance in unfamiliar traffic systems.

17203017.label: Major findings and research outcome
17203017.value: The analysis of pedestrian crash records helped to identify the risk-taking decisions of pedestrians attempting to cross a street [J1]. The observational survey findings clarified participants’ walking behaviors, which revealed the key behavioral attributes of pedestrians [J2]. These studies enhanced understanding of pedestrian-crossing behaviors and patterns, and will assist the design of questionnaire surveys and VR experiments. The questionnaire survey responses indicated that participants’ hometown driving system and length of stay were positively correlated with their right-looking habit, and that their hometown driving system was negatively correlated with their maladaptation to the Hong Kong left-hand-side driving system. Moreover, right-looking habit partially mediated the effect of hometown driving system and fully mediated the effect of length of stay on maladaptation to the Hong Kong left-hand-side driving system. When mainland Chinese pedestrians were in areas that had an unfamiliar driving system, they tended to practice their hometown looking habits, especially mainland Chinese pedestrians who had been in these areas for a short period. This behavior differed significantly from that of Hong Kong pedestrians and led to more severe maladaptation [J4]. The results of the VR experiments show that the direction in which the participants habitually looked first before crossing a street differed significantly, depending on where the participants lived. When mainland Chinese participants were crossing streets in an unfamiliar driving system (i.e., a system in which oncoming traffic was approaching from a direction inconsistent with the direction it approaches in the mainland Chinese driving system), they were 2.93 times more likely to exhibit erroneous looking than when they were crossing streets in a familiar driving system. Road markings and traffic sounds did not correct the looking behavior of these participants. Moreover, the inattentive-looking behavior and time-to-collision were negatively correlated (and significant at the 1% level), as the errors decreased the time-to-collision and increased the risk to participants [J3]. To explore the crossing behaviors of drunk pedestrians in scenarios with unfamiliar traffic systems, the temporal profile of BrAC was established to guide the design of the VR experiment [J5]. The experimental data were used to establish random-effect regression models, which indicated that the perceptual-motor response was deteriorated by alcohol consumption, particularly for young adults. In addition, aspects of the street environment, such as the unfamiliar direction of oncoming vehicles and the presence of traffic direction indicators (i.e., road markings), also contributed to the correct habitual-looking behavior of participants [J6].

17203017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17203017.value: The project findings demonstrated the debilitating effects of alcohol on the participants’ physiological responses and cognitive abilities. Drunk walking is believed to be a key factor that increases pedestrians’ risk of being fatally or severely injured, regardless of the provision of pedestrian warning facilities. Many clinical and human health studies have explored the impacts of alcohol on physical responses and cognitive abilities. Furthermore, numerous road safety studies have been conducted to explore the risk factors associated with pedestrian injuries and fatalities at walking facilities, focusing on the types of facilities, pedestrians’ personal characteristics, and traffic conditions. The results of this study highlight that pedestrians’ physical responses, the psychological components of their motor and cognitive abilities, their conformity tendencies, and other factors combine to influence pedestrians’ decision-making, and that the unsafe walking behavior of drunk pedestrians is a research gap that must be urgently and comprehensively studied by integrating theories from different fields. Based on the findings of this project, a proposal for research on drunk walking will be submitted to the Research Grants Council’s General Research Fund.

17203017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17203017.value: Approximately one-third of the world’s population lives in areas in which traffic drives on the left-hand side of the road, such as the UK, Japan, and Hong Kong. This means that pedestrians exhibit different attitudes and conventions depending on the traffic system in their hometown, and consequently the risk of injury to foreign visitors is high when they are pedestrians in regions with unfamiliar traffic systems. This project comprehensively examined pedestrian crossing behaviors using techniques such as questionnaire surveys and VR experiments. The results demonstrate that pedestrians from an area that has a different driving system to the area in which they are walking show a significantly different right-looking habit and extent of maladaptation to the traffic system of the area than pedestrians from the latter area. Moreover, these results show that the design and management of road-crossing facilities must consider pedestrians’ habitual looking behavior and inattentive looking behavior, the correlation between their inattentive looking behavior and the time-to-collision, the influence of alcohol, and the use of road markings, particularly in areas with a high percentage of tourists from places with a driving system that is different from the local driving system.

17203117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17203117.value: Carrier collaboration is one kind of horizontal collaboration that utilizes effective approaches or mechanisms to reassign carriers’ loaded lanes (shipment requests) among a transportation network. This project is among the first attempt to extend the existing market design theory to the field of supply chain and logistics management. It is known that money flow is not allowed in the matching markets like stable marriage, house allocation, and kidney exchange. In this project, we will explore the potential of lane exchange among a number of self-interested truckload carriers in a collaboration network (i.e., carrier collaboration). We will consider two cases of money flow in carrier collaboration: (i) a carrier who fails to exchange his lane may join the procurement mechanism as a transportation service purchaser; and (ii) a carrier who fails in lane exchange can always transfer his lane to the platform by making a fixed payment. We will propose the (price-compatible) top trading cycles and deals (TTCD) mechanism for case (i) and the price-compatible top trading cycles and chains (PC-TTCC) mechanism for case (ii). It is expected that both mechanisms are effective in terms of the compatibility with money flow, strategy-proofness, the realized welfare of carriers, and budget balance. We will also conduct experiment simulations to investigate the magnitude of cost saving for the collaboration network and (ex post) budget balance for the platform. There will is no collaboration in the benchmark case. The experimental study aims to provide some important practical and managerial implications of designing and operating the collaboration network. Overall, this project will open the door to the solutions of a host of price-compatible matching problems. 承載商合作是一種橫向協作，利用有效的方法或機制來重新分配運輸網絡中承載商的裝載車道（裝運請求）。該項目是將現有市場設計理論擴展到供應鍊和物流管理領域的第一個嘗試。眾所周知，在穩定的婚姻，房屋分配和腎臟交換等匹配市場中，不允許貨幣流動。在這個項目中，我們將探討在一個協作網絡（即承載商協作）中的一些自主興趣的卡車運營商之間車道交換的潛力。我們將考慮兩種貨運流程合作的情況：（一）未能交換車道的承運人可以作為運輸服務購買者加入採購機制; （ii）無法進行車道交換的承載商，可以通過固定付款方式將車道轉移到平台上。我們將為案例（i）和案例（ii）的價格兼容的最高交易週期和鏈（PC-TTCC）機制提出（價格兼容）最高交易週期和交易（TTCD）機制。預計這兩個機制在貨幣流動，戰略規劃，實現承載商福利和預算平衡方面的兼容性方面都是有效的。我們還將進行實驗模擬，以調查協作網絡的成本節省數量以及平台的（事後）預算平衡。在基準案例中將不會有合作。實驗研究旨在為協作網絡的設計和運營提供一些重要的實踐和管理意義。總體而言，這個項目將為大量與價格兼容的匹配問題的解決方案打開大門。

17203117.label: Realisation of objectives
17203117.value: Overall speaking, all research objectives have been achieved. The work entitled “Auction-based city logistics synchronization” has been published in IISE Transactions. This work has focused first two objectives, (1) To propose a new modeling approach for carrier collaboration based on market design theory. This approach will take into account money flow and (2) to develop Pareto-efficient, strategy-proof, price-compatible matching mechanism for carrier collaboration. The proposed matching mechanisms will extend the will extend the existing market design theory while objective 3 “To explore the similarities and differences between our price-compatible matching mechanisms, as well as the magnitude of cost saving in realistic collaboration settings” has also been addressed through simulation analysis. This work is the first that proposes an efficient auction mechanism for the city logistics synchronization (CLS) problem, which aims to capture both logistics punctuality and simultaneity in a city or region. The main motivation of CLS is that if the delay has already occurred or will occur, customers tend to pursue simultaneity. We develop the one-sided Vickrey-Clarke-Groves (O-VCG) auction for the CLS problem. The proposed O-VCG auction realizes incentive compatibility (on the buy side), approximately allocative efficiency, budget balance, and individual rationality. The vehicle routing problem (VRP) faced by the logistics companies is formulated as the lane covering problem with CLS requirements. Three effective heuristics are developed: Merge, Exchange, and Mutate. Our computational results show that the three operators are effective but sensitive to the bid duration. A hybrid operator significantly outperforms each individual operator. We also numerically analyze the impacts of five key factors: the strategic behavior of the 3PL company, flexible due dates, the maximum bid duration, the radius of a city or region, and the number of depots. Emphasizing Objective 3 while also addressing objectives 1 and 2, our research has intensified through the work entitled “IoT-enabled parking space sharing and allocation mechanisms” has been published in IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering. This work is among the first proposing an integrated auction and market design method for the parking space sharing and allocation problem. Drivers (agents) who fail to exchange their own parking spaces can then rent them to the platform. The platform receives private parking spaces from agents and meanwhile manages some public parking spaces. We first develop the urban parking management cloud platform through Internet of Things (IoT). Based on this systemic framework, parking spaces are shared among agents via a PC-TTCC (price-compatible top trading cycles and chains) mechanism and the platform’s parking spaces are reassigned via an O-VCG (one-sided Vickrey-Clarke-Groves) auction. Both the PC-TTCC mechanism with rule (PC-TTCC [e]) and O-VCG auction are effective in terms of strategy-proofness and (allocative or Pareto) efficiency. In the PC-TTCC [e] mechanism, the platform’s payment rule used in private parking space sharing is determined based on historical O-VCG auction prices. Our experimental results further show that the proposed mechanism results in system profitability of 20%-30% and ex post budget balance for the platform. The relationship between the two research activities is stated as follows. The first work directly contributes to the project because it considers the auction-based carrier collaboration problem in the context of city logistics. The second work indirectly contributes to the project since it further considers the city parking problem faced by the logistics companies. Also, the second work integrates the auction approach proposed in the first work and a novel market design method to solve the city parking problem. Therefore, both research activities are closely in relation to the (revised) project objectives 1, 2, and 3. Objective 4 focuses on more practical aspects. As there are some constraints on real/near-life applications of the proposed auction model, our research activities diversified along some different but related directions. We carried out an extensive literature review on auction logistics for cold supply chain trading (Publication 4 on the list). We investigated the usages of auction mechanism under different scenarios such as product auction (publication 5), cloud manufacturing service auction (Publication 6). Publications 7 and 8 are non-auction-based and used other approaches to deal with the similar domain problems. These provide some comparative insights about the various available methods.

17203117.label: Major findings and research outcome
17203117.value: In terms of research outcomes, this project has enabled the research team members to produce a number of research papers in reputable journals. We are very pleased to report that the IISE Transaction paper (2018) has won the best paper award. The paper reports on the first effort to propose an efficient auction mechanism for the city logistics synchronisation problem. The model captures both punctuality and simultaneity in a city or region. Based on this fundamental exploration, the team has been able to extend the efforts along the lines of cloud manufacturing services, cold supply chain trading, and product auctions. With the partial funding from this GRF grant, we have been able to train three PhD research postgraduate students in the area of ecommerce logistics. The Co-I (Dr Sunny Xu) worked very closely with Dr Melody Zhang and Dr Mandy WANG to set up their PhD research topics motivated partially from this project. Auction research has been a research area of the team in the past 10 years or so. This GRF project has helped us to understand much better how auction can be used for supply chain trading in transportation service procurement (TSP). We have proposed to extend and apply auction mechanism in a cyber-physical internet (CPI) marketplace to automate forwarders' services for carriers and shippers in our recent proposal under Theme-Based Research Scheme which has been successful in 2022.

17203117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17203117.value: One area identified for further research is how to extend and innovate auction mechanisms for IoT-enabled smart logistics with real-time visibility and traceability. This has been incorporated into the new forthcoming TRS project. Another area worth further investigation is how to derive information credibility and authenticity measures and incorporate them as confidence factor into utility functions of the auction mechanism. It is not clear how we could develop and incorporate incentives for enhancing credibility and authenticity. The last area is related to practical applications. The gap has existed and this has been a continuous challenge in our auction research. We have made several attempts to put auctions models. into real/near-life applications. However, we ended up with some computational algorithms to seek more pragmatic solutions as in some of related papers resulting from this project. It is not clear if and how real-time information visibility and traceability would simplify the auction models for practical applications.

17203117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17203117.value: Carrier collaboration is one kind of horizontal collaboration that utilizes effective approaches or mechanisms to reassign carriers’ loaded lanes (shipment requests) among a transportation network. This project is among the first attempt to extend the existing market design theory to the field of supply chain and logistics management. It is known that money flow is not allowed in the matching markets like stable marriage, house allocation, and kidney exchange. In this project, we have explored the potential of lane exchange among a number of self-interested truckload carriers in a collaboration network (i.e., carrier collaboration). We considered two cases of money flow in carrier collaboration: (i) a carrier who fails to exchange his lane may join the procurement mechanism as a transportation service purchaser; and (ii) a carrier who fails in lane exchange can always transfer his lane to the platform by making a fixed payment. The result shows cost savings for the collaboration network and (ex post) budget balance for the platform. Overall, this project opened the door to the solutions of a host of price-compatible matching problems.

17203217.label: Project Objectives
17203217.value: Our first objective focuses on the computational DH system: We aim to prototype a novel incoherent DH imaging system that records a large hologram. The targeted resolution will be larger than the electronic sensor, necessitating the recording of a series of raw holographic data. We aim to enable this without requiring physical motion of the object, but instead devise synthetic aperture technology to allow diversity in the data capture. Our second objective focuses on the computational algorithms: We aim to devise effective and computationally efficient algorithms to synthesize a large hologram from the series of raw capture. In line with most modern super-resolution techniques, we envision that the algorithms will be iterative, and we will pay particular attention to minimize oscillation and trapping in the local minima, to develop a suitable initialization scheme, and to incorporate robustness against variations such as nonuniform illuminations across different raw hologram captures. In addition, we will compute quantitative image data such as phase and volume from the holograms. Our third objective focuses on optimization: This entails a careful co-design of the optical system and the hologram reconstruction algorithms, where the chief purpose is to reduce the amount of data capture, minimizing information redundancy in the raw holograms. We also aim to exploit prior information, such as low-dimensionality in the digital hologram structure, and learning-based approaches, through which the hologram synthesis can adapt by means of a training process, to further advance the reconstruction and image quantification computations. Our fourth objective focuses on applications: While this project is engineering in nature and the long-term impact is on pushing the technological frontier of DH imaging, the technology will not be influential without demonstrating applicability. As such, we aim to investigate its employment in two specific applications: in 3D inspection, where we intend to demonstrate its use in semiconductor manufacturing for integrated circuit packaging, and in 3D tracking, where we intend to demonstrate its use in biological imaging for visualization of a heterogeneous cell population.

17203217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17203217.value: Imaging systems are foundational to our observation and understanding of the world. Ideally, we wish one can capture all the spatial, directional, spectral, even statistical information about an object with infinite precision; practically, the optics and detector impose significant constraints, forcing us to choose among accepting various tradeoffs depending on the specific applications. In recent years, computational algorithms are effective in pushing these limitations. For example, fringe projection profilometry reconstructs fine object surface with phase shift algorithms, and Fourier ptychography enables high-resolution microscopy using iterative phase retrieval. In this proposal, we seek to advance computational technology to empower imaging that is holographic, i.e., with the axial information encoded in the digital holograms. This has tremendous values in a wide array of applications, from inspecting semiconductor components where axial information is needed for the increasingly 3D structure of integrated circuit packages, to biological imaging, where identifying and tracking a dynamic specimen at different depths can lead to new insights in life science. We aim to tackle these challenges -- specifically 3D inspection and tracking -- first through a custom design of the digital holographic microscopy, incorporating synthetic aperture to produce a series of holograms with information diversity, so we can develop stitching algorithms to synthesize a large hologram. Our initial focus is on robust methods to combine these image captures, with a further goal of seeking to record the least amount of additional data to enhance imaging efficiency. Then, we tackle the two main application tasks. For inspection, we will investigate a learning-based approach, which shows success in image processing tasks including compression, super-resolution, and deblurring; in optical tomography, it models multiple scattering to improve the reconstructed image quality. Its use in digital holography, however, is still nascent, and we aim to pioneer how machine learning can improve processing specific to holographic imaging, such as sectioning, and integrate with the subsequent task of image understanding and classification. As for tracking, we aim to leverage our recently developed stochastic method using a nonparametric Bayesian approach, first developed in the context of intelligent transportation. While we have demonstrated unsupervised tracking using the doubly stochastic Dirichlet process mixture model for accurate human and car trajectory detection, it is a nontrivial extension to 3D with holographic data, with specific challenges in computational efficiency and anisotropic resolution in the spatial and axial resolutions. 成像系統是我們對這世界觀察和理解的基礎。最理想就是我們能夠以無限精度捕獲關於物體的所有空間，方向，光譜，甚至統計信息; 可是實際上，光學和檢測器帶著顯著的限制，迫使我們根據具體應用選擇接受各種權衡。近年來，計算算法往往能夠有效衝破一些限制。舉例說，邊緣投影輪廓測量法利用相移算法重建精細物體表面，傅里葉片狀圖則可以使用迭代相位檢索實現高分辨率顯微鏡。 在這個研究計劃，我們尋求推進計算技術來增進全息圖像成像，即在數字全息圖中編碼的軸向信息。這在廣泛的應用中具有巨大的價值，從檢查需要軸向信息的集成電路封裝的三維結構，到生物成像---其中識別和跟踪不同深度的動態樣本可以加深我們對生命科學的了解。我們的目標是解決這些挑戰 --- 特別是三維檢測和跟踪 --- 首先通過數字全息顯微鏡的定制設計，結合合成孔徑產生一系列具有信息多樣性的全息圖，以致我們可以開發拼接算法來合成大型全息圖。我們初步的重點是結合這些圖像捕獲的強大方法，另一個目標是尋求記錄最少量的附加數據以提高成像效率。然後，我們處理兩個主要的應用任務。我們將研發一種基於機器學習的方法，這些方法已證明能成功應用在圖像處理任務，例如壓縮，超分辨率和去模糊;在光學斷層攝影中，它模擬多次散射以提高重建的圖像質量。然而，它在數字全息術中的應用仍然是新興的，我們的目標是開創機器學習如何改進特定於全息成像的問題，並與後續的圖像理解和分類相結合。對於跟踪，我們的目標是使用非參數貝葉斯方法，那是我們最近在智能交通的背景下開發的隨機方法。雖然我們使用雙重隨機過程混合模型準確達到人和車輛軌跡的檢測，但對全息數據，在計算效率和各向異性分辨率的空間和軸向分辨率方面我們仍要面對特定的挑戰。

17203217.label: Realisation of objectives
17203217.value: This project consists of 4 objectives: development of a computational digital holographic system, devising associated computational algorithms, optimizing the co-design of the optics and reconstruction computation, and applications of the resulting system for 3D inspection and tracking. These objectives have been realized with the conclusion of this project. Regarding the first objective, we reported a 60% completion in the mid-term progress report. At that point, we have constructed an incoherent digital holographic imaging system following the approach of optical scanning holography, and used this system to capture a set of raw hologram data. Further work during the second half of the project has focused on the diversity of the hologram data and increasing the size of the resulting hologram to overcome the limitation of the electronic sensor. We show that with a learning-based method, specifically by training a convolutional neural network (CNN), it is possible to increase the space-bandwidth product of a holographic imaging system without the need of any advanced hardware. Consequently, we demonstrate fringe pattern improvement and super-resolution in digital holography. Regarding the second objective, we reported a 50% completion in the mid-term progress report. At that point, we have devised a simple algorithm to reconstruct sectional images from the holographic data. Noting that the existence of noise poses challenges for its accuracy, we have further devised an image despeckling method that combines nonlocal self-similarity filters with machine learning. The former uses block matching, such that we can take advantage of the similarity across image patches as a regularizer. The latter achieves data-driven denoising, and combines with the block-matching to form 3D groups of similar patches, which are then filtered through a wavelet-domain shrinkage. This combination of model-based and data-driven techniques laid the foundation for further computational methods. In addition, we have also stated the need to extract phase information from the holograms. To achieve this, we developed a method to compensate for phase aberrations automatically based on sparse optimization. Without manually selecting a sample-free background, the compensation is cast as a surface-fitting problem, which is tackled by using the L1 norm as the loss function and by minimizing an appropriate objective function in order to fit the aberrations and then remove them numerically. Regarding the third objective, we reported a 15% completion in the mid-term progress report. At that point, we have only started the investigation of learning-based approaches for hologram reconstruction and image quantification. We published a manuscript on learning-based nonparametric autofocusing for digital holography in the high impact journal Optica, which as of this writing has been cited 132 times (Google Scholar). We have continued along that direction for further optimization of the system and reconstruction. This has resulted in the work on end-to-end deep learning framework for digital holographic reconstruction, showing that it is possible to reconstruct a noise-free image without requiring prior knowledge, and can handle phase imaging as well as depth map generation. The manuscript, published in Advanced Photonics, was highlighted as Editors' Pick in the journal and in SPIE news feature, and was a top download in the first year of this publication. This work has since been further improved in our development of RedCap, which stands for residual encoder-decoder capsule network, to improve its computational efficiency. Regarding the fourth objective, we reported a 10% completion in the mid-term progress report. At that point, we have conducted some initial testing on 3D inspection and tracking for machine vision and biological applications. In the proposal, we had envisioned one of the uses in semiconductor manufacturing for integrated circuit packaging, through collaboration with industrial partners. Unfortunately, the global pandemic that plagued the last third of this project duration meant we could only conduct feasibility tests in our own lab. Meanwhile, we also looked into a related machine vision problem of inspecting microplastics and delineating their physical characteristics for further analysis, as well as for automatic classification.

17203217.label: Major findings and research outcome
17203217.value: In this project, the major findings and research outcome center on demonstrating that the combination of the computational optical imaging paradigm and digital holography can enable 3D inspection and tracking in the microscale. At the beginning of this project, learning-based methods were still at its infancy in holographic reconstruction. Our work in autofocusing and end-to-end reconstruction had contributed to advancement in this area, and a wider variety of deep learning methods are now routinely used in digital holography and other forms of optical imaging. In addition, we have also been a proponent of combining model-based and data-driven techniques, and demonstrated its use in speckle reduction for digital holography. Such an approach has also been steadily gaining traction. In large part due to advancements in computational algorithms, including 3D inspection and tracking which are the focus of this work, digital holography has continued to expand its applications in different domains.

17203217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17203217.value: The research has room for further development on a couple of directions. In terms of computational algorithms, there remains a wide unexplored area as to how imaging model and learning from data can be efficiently combined. It is envisioned that further development in this area can lead to more efficient algorithms and more powerful results, such as in resolution enhancement, noise suppression, and phase quantification. In terms of uses, we can continue to expand the applicability of digital holography to different situations, such as under insufficient lighting conditions and for imaging fast moving objects. Our initial investigation on holographic imaging for microplastics also indicates ample opportunities for its use in environmental monitoring. The above will be explored through new research grants and focused projects.

17203217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17203217.value: Holography is a unique form of imaging, which preserves the 3D information of the object. However, a lot of computation is needed for reconstructing holographic images. This project seeks to develop better computation techniques to push the technological frontier of holographic imaging. This involves not only building the optical system, but also advancing the algorithms for noise reduction and resolution enhancement. In particular, we focus on enabling holographic imaging in terms of 3D inspection and tracking of micro-objects, which will significantly enhances its applicability in various industrial applications.

17203417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17203417.value: Synthetic water repellent granular materials have been tested for water harvesting and proposed as landfill and slope covers. By adjusting the magnitude of water repellency, they offer the unique advantage of controlling water infiltration and allow their deployment as semi-permeable or impermeable materials. Other advantages include (1) volumetric stability (comparing to clays which swell-shrink), (2) high air permeability and low water permeability (preventing the built-up of air pressure while allowing condensation from water vapour), (3) suitability for flexible applications i.e. the water-tight behaviour is not lost if the material deforms (e.g. settlement) – this represents an advantage over geotextiles and geomembranes, (4) improved adhesion aggregate-bitumen (depending on the type of coatings). Application areas include hydraulic barriers (e.g. for engineered slopes and waste containment), pavements and other waterproofing systems. Water repellency can be achieved through chemical treatments whereby particles are coated with waxes, oils or silicone films, and it is particularly powerful at sub-millimetric scales, when the interfacial forces dominate gravity. To date, our research has been aimed at demonstrating their use as slope covers and establishing the chemical compounds that develop high and stable water repellency. It has long been established that surface roughness increases water repellency (the lotus leaf effect). Nano- and micro- topography features are used to develop superhydrophobic materials; those in which water does not wet and water drops roll off easily. For soils, roughness is an appealing technology because (1) the decay of water repellency depends on mineral weathering, which develops at geological timescales (thousands of years), (2) it allows the use of granular materials with unique particle attributes, from natural soils to waste materials and, (3) it may reduce the need for chemical compounds to impart water repellency, contributing to the sustainability of the solution. This project will aim to enhance the water repellency of granular materials through roughness by experimentally altering the particle surface topography and particle shape and size. The project will be delivered by an international and interdisciplinary team made of the PI Lourenço (synthetic water repellent granular materials) at the University of Hong Kong, Co-I McHale (world leader on surface wettability) and Co-I Wells (wetting and surface modification) at Northumbria University (UK) and Co-I Baudet (soil particle morphology) at University College London (UK). The project will represent the first major attempt to use particle morphology to control soil wettability for ground engineering purposes and will provide the basis for many further investigations. 人工合成的防水颗粒材料被用来进行集水试验，同时被建议用作填筑场地和边坡的覆盖层。通过调节防水性能等级，这种材料在控制水体下渗和调节半渗透或不渗透性能上具有独特优势。材料防水性可以通过对颗粒表面涂抹蜡、油或者硅胶薄层这些化学处理方法来获得，这种方法在毫米级以下尤其奏效，这时颗粒间的表面力（气-固-水）起主要作用。材料表面的粗糙度会影响材料的防水性能已经被人们充分认识到了（荷叶效应）。纳米和毫米级的形态观测被用来研究发展超防水材料；水滴在这种材料表面可以轻易地滚动同时不会引起潮湿。对于土体，粗糙度反映在四个方面：颗粒表面形态，颗粒形状，粒径大小以及它们在颗粒混合体中的综合效应。通过前期研究工作，我们认识到了构成土体表面的颗粒（1）颗粒形状越圆防水性能越高（2）颗粒大小越小防水性能越高。本项目将通过在实验中改变颗粒表面形态，颗粒形状，粒径大小的方法来改变土体粗糙度，从而对增强土体的防水性能进行研究。

17203417.label: Realisation of objectives
17203417.value: In this projected we investigated the role of physical characteristics of soils in enhancing soil water repellency. Soil water repellency or hydrophobized soils represent a new research area, and this proposal fully delivers on it. We were inspired by the superhydrophobicity of the lotus leaf and attempted to mimic its effect in soils. This was achieved by assessing the role of particle size, particle shape, particle surface roughness, soil density on soil water repellency. Soil water repellency was measured by the sessile drop method (to obtain the contact angle), water drop penetration time (to assess its persistency), and later in this study, through water-entry pressure measurements in bulk soil samples. All soil samples were silanized (with dimethyldicholorosilane) to induce hydrophobicity. All objectives were delivered in full as will be detailed next. [Objective 1]: This objective concerned the development of methods to measure roughness in soils. At first, different scales of roughness were established. In this study, we mostly addressed two scales: particle shape (through the aspect ratio, sphericity and convexity) and particle surface roughness. Particle shape was measured by means of dynamic image analyser (QicPic), while roughness was measured by white light interferometry. Other methods were employed, the case of a confocal microscope. All publications listed in the research outputs, journals 1-7 and conferences 1-3, used the methods listed above. [Objective 2]: This objective is core to the proposal, addressing the specific role of particle characteristics on soil water repellency. Testing was conducted in granular materials of various particle size and shape, including powders with known size and shape. All materials were silanized at first, with a polydimethylsiloxane deposited on top of the particles, prior to any manipulation of the physical characteristics. This was to ensure that the intrinsic hydrophobicity was the same for all samples, with any measured deviations of hydrophobicity reflecting changes in the physical characteristics of the samples. Results are described in outputs 1, 2 and 4, 5. [Objective 3]: Tested granular materials included various granular materials: silica sand, crushed glass, silica powder and clays (kaolinite and halloysite). While these materials can be categorised as natural or man-made, addressing objective 3, future work could test other materials, mostly granular wastes. Results are described in outputs 4 and conference output 3. [Collaborations with foreign and local researchers] This project strongly benefitted from the collaboration with Prof Jorg Bachmann group (Leibniz University Hannover) contributing to output 1. Dr Beatrice Baudet (University College London) assisted with the roughness measurements in output 4. In Hong Kong, all tests described in output 3 were conducted with Dr Kostas Senetakis at City University of Hong Kong. Seminal research work was also conducted with Prof Glen McHale group (now at the University of Edinburgh) on the properties of the hydrophobic coatings. [Quality of publications] As a proof of the significance of the findings and quality of the results, all publications are in Q1 journals. Géotechnique and Acta Geotechnica are the leading journals in geotechnics. To enhance exposure, we also published in journals from related fields, Powder Technology, Physical Review E and European Journal of Soil Science. Conference publications and presentations are in accredited events sponsored by the International Society of Soil Mechanics and Geotechnical Engineering, the case of E-UNSAT 2020 (held in Lisbon) and UNSAT 2018 (held in Hong Kong).

17203417.label: Major findings and research outcome
17203417.value: The core findings are as follows: [Role of particle shape and particle size in enhancing soil water repellency] Finer soils and angular particles have a stronger effect on soil water repellency. An increase in CAs was measured as particle size decreased. In addition, as particles became more angular, CAs increased. The infiltration water drop dynamics was also investigated in substrates with particle sizes of different dimensions. Results are detailed in output 1 (Saulick et al., 2018) and output 2 (Kang et al., 2018). [Role of particle surface roughness in enhancing soil water repellency] Powder-coating enhances the hydrophobicity of sands in comparison to the sole use of a chemical method to induce water repellency. Silica powder was able to increase the hydrophobicity of sands from 109 to 123 degrees. Results are detailed in output 4 (Saulick et al., 2021). [Role of particle size distribution, density, particle size and shape in enhancing soil water repellency] This research strand largely follows the study above on the role of particle size and shape on soil water repellency. However, both density and particle size distribution are accounted for. Testing is also conducted in bulk soil samples, with water repellency assessed by the water entry pressure method. A major outcome is that the coefficient of uniformity delivers a higher water repellency (through higher water-entry pressures). Results are detailed in output 5 (Xing et al., 2022). [Thickness of hydrophobic particle coatings] A persistent question throughout the project was the lack of information about the thickness of the hydrophobic coatings. A method was devised based on the surface topography providing a thickness in the nm range for the polydimethylsiloxane coatings. Results are detailed in output 5 (Yang et al., 2021). [Specific role of particle coatings on soil shear strength] While not listed as an objective, the specific role of the hydrophobic coatings on the soil micro and macromechanical behaviour was investigated. Triaxial tests and interparticle loading tests revealed an acute sensitivity to confining pressure and normal stress, respectively, due to the soft nature of the coatings and their propensity to be teared or punctured. Results are detailed in outputs 3 and 6 (Liu et al., 2019; Liu et al., 2021).

17203417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17203417.value: [Database with synthesized water repellent granular solids] The concept of physically modifying granular materials to tune hydrophobicity can potentially be extended to a wide variety soils and powders of different shapes and of finer sizes (e.g., nanosilica) for their eventual deployment in ground engineering. To deliver this, a database could be constructed to assist industry in selecting the most appropriate for each application. A major challenge to address at first, is to ensure the compatibility of the granular material with the hydrophobic compound, i.e. the chemical method to induce water repellency. For instance, silanization is successful in silicates but its performance in other granular materials remains unknown.

17203417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17203417.value: Functionalizing granular materials such as sands (an important constituent of concrete, mortar, asphalt and plaster) to render them hydrophobic can singularly lead to several applications in the construction industry, e.g. these novel materials are able to water-proof ground infrastructures and therefore prevent their long-term degradations. In this project, we develop procedures to enhance the hydrophobicity of coarse, medium and fine sands. By following both a chemical approach (by silanization) and a physical approach (by modifying the sands and their surfaces) together, the aim is to render the sands more hydrophobic than what is achieved by the conventional method of relying on solely either their chemistry or their particle characteristics. We envision the potential of deploying such valuable water-resistant materials in ground infrastructures as a long term substitute for the conventional and more intrusive ground improvement techniques.

17203517.label: Project Objectives

17203517.label: Realisation of objectives
17203517.value: This project is related to the study of ball-joint structure for wireless power transfer applications. After the research proposal was submitted to RGC and while waiting for the outcome of our GRF application, we investigated an inductive wireless power transfer technique for a ball-joint structure with coil-resonators comprising manually wound coils and discrete capacitors. Very soon, we confirmed that inductive wireless power transfer could be achieved in such ball-joint structure. Then we turned to study the capacitive wireless transfer technique for ball-joint structure. Because we can maintenance constant coupling, the power flow can be found to be independent of the angular position of the ball joint with respect to the ball socket. The successes in confirming both inductive and capacitive wireless power transfer in these two sets of experiments have met our Objective 1. With the feasibility of wireless power transfer confirmed in the ball-joint structures, we further investigated other control aspects of wireless power transfer according to Objective 2. In particular, we considered the series-series compensated wireless power structures, because such compensation circuits were adopted in the ball-joint structures under investigation in this project. It should be noted that the voltage and current waveforms in a wireless power consist of both fundamental and harmonics. However, the majority of most papers in this topic conducted analyses based on the fundamental component only (i.e. ignoring the harmonic components). This simplified assumption often leads to large errors in the prediction of system performance. In responses to this changes, we developed an enhanced harmonic analysis method that includes both the fundamental and harmonic components. This improved method provides accurate results for system prediction. Control of wireless power systems requires the knowledge of the mutual coupling. Based on the use of an active rectifier in the receiver circuit, we have successfully developed a fast method to estimate the mutual coupling in the order of milliseconds. This is the fastest method of mutual coupling in existing literature.

17203517.label: Major findings and research outcome
17203517.value: This project is related to the study of ball-joint structure for wireless power transfer applications. After the research proposal was submitted to RGC and while waiting for the outcome of our GRF application, we investigated an inductive wireless power transfer technique for a ball-joint structure with coil-resonators comprising manually wound coils and discrete capacitors. This paper appeared as Journal-Paper-1 in our publication list. To assist us in visualizing the energy flow in a ball-joint wireless power structure, we developed a visualization method that was reported in an IEEE Wireless Power Conference (Conference-Paper-1). After confirming that inductive wireless power transfer could be achieved in such ball-joint structure, we turned to study the capacitive wireless transfer technique for ball-joint structure. Because we can maintenance constant coupling, the power flow can be found to be independent of the angular position of the ball joint with respect to the ball socket. The feasibility of capacitive wireless power transfer was reported in Journal-Paper-2. We further investigated other control aspects of wireless power transfer according to Objective 2. In particular, we considered the series-series compensated wireless power structures, because such compensation circuits were adopted in the ball-joint structures under investigation in this project. It should be noted that the voltage and current waveforms in a wireless power consist of both fundamental and harmonics. However, the majority of most papers in this topic conducted analyses based on the fundamental component only (i.e. ignoring the harmonic components). This simplified assumption often leads to large errors in the prediction of system performance. In responses to this changes, we developed an enhanced harmonic analysis method that includes both the fundamental and harmonic components. This improved method provides accurate results for system prediction and now forms an accurate tool for predicting wireless power transfer systems. This method was reported in Journal-Paper-3. Control of wireless power systems requires the knowledge of the mutual coupling. Based on the use of an active rectifier in the receiver circuit, we have successfully developed a fast method to estimate the mutual coupling in the order of milliseconds. This method was reported in Journal-Paper-4 and believed to be the fastest method of mutual coupling in existing literature.

17203517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17203517.value: We are in the process of contacting industry to explore the possibilities of commercialization.

17203517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17203517.value: In this project, we studied wireless power transfer technology in a ball-joint structures. Such structures are commonly found in mechanical systems such as robotic arms and mechanical joints. Traditionally, electrical energy transfer across the joints was achieved by electric cables. Because of the frequent movements in the mechanical joints, frequent bending of the cables could drastically reduce the reliability of such systems. Our investigations have confirmed that wireless power can be wirelessly transferred across mechanical ball-joint structures without the use of any cable. This breakthrough opens a new door to wireless electrical energy transfer in robotic designs.

17203717.value: 到目前为止，分析多用户系统的机制效率的主要方法是由Roughgarden提出的以分析机制的光滑性为基础的框架。在这个项目中，我们将深入研究最近由Kulkarni等提出的基于数学规划及其对称性的新框架，致力于改进目前已知的机制效率分析结果，以及提出基于这个框架的设计高效率机制的方法。

17203717.label: Realisation of objectives
17203717.value: Objective 1: We have successfully reproduce all major PoA bounds in congestions games, auction games, and scheduling games. The results have been summarized in a survey article to be submitted to a major journal. Objective 2: We found that the two frameworks are indeed closely related. The smoothness inequality in the smoothness framework naturally corresponds to approximate dual feasibility in the primal dual framework. Objective 3: We successfully design auction mechanisms with small PoA from the primal dual framework. For scheduling games, however, we only obtain partial results due to a technical difficulty. The difficulty can be viewed as a matrix distortion minimization problem that is non-convex. Resolving this technical challenge seems to require developing novel mathematical tools, beyond the scope of the current project. Objective 4: The situation is similar to objective 3. The same technical difficulty about matrix distortion minimization arised and as a result we only partially achieve the original goal.

17203717.value: For systems that involve strategic participants, the PoA is a metric for measuring how efficient the equilibrium outcome is, and how far it is compared to the optimal outcome should a central principal make the socially optimal decisions for all. This project develops a new framework for analyzing the PoA and for designing systems with small PoA.
