17204017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17204017.value: Reliable infrastructure systems are crucial to the development of modern societies. Despite that, infrastructure systems are more and more susceptible to failure due to exacerbated climate change and evolving human-behaviors. Therefore, governments around the world have begun to introduce various programs to ensure infrastructure systems are more resilient to changes to best serve the communities. Unfortunately, there are lots of challenges facing the operationalization of community resilience programs as there is no agreeable mechanisms to assemble, assimilate and analyze fragmented data maintained by owners and/or operators of various infrastructure systems. Advance in crowdsourcing might help bridge the information gap as data related to the condition of a series of different but yet interdependent infrastructure systems can be solicited and shared through crowdsensing technologies which can ultimately be used to support decision making. Moreover, citizen behaviors towards the use of infrastructure systems can be crowdsourced to help improve the reliability of community resilience programs. Through crowdsourcing, government departments, utility companies and citizens can co-provide data, co-analyze the condition of infrastructure systems and co-produce community resilience strategies. Crowdsourcing should help realize the whole-community resilience idealism as the community can play a proactive role in resilience planning, development and implementation. Despite that, crowdsourcing may result in many useful or otherwise irrelevant data from various sources. The aim of this investigation is to improve the operationalization of community resilience through the development and use of a crowdsourcing framework and platform to capture and analyze data pertinent to the condition of infrastructure systems and user behavior in a well-structured and reliable manner. The research will begin with literature review, interview, case study, focus group meeting and Delphi study to unveil the data required for community resilience and identify the most suitable crowdsourcing approaches. A workshop will be convened to devise a crowdsourcing framework which is expected to include a crowdsourcing operations reference process, a master data model, and the software architecture of a master data management system. A prototype platform will then be developed to orchestrate the crowdsourcing and resilience building activities. Two case studies will be conducted to validate the developed framework and prototype platform. The findings of this research shall contribute significant to the existing resilience research and practices by resolving the data bottleneck of interdependent infrastructure systems. The engagement of the crowds in community resilient decision through the crowdsourcing approaches should help foster harmonious cyber-physical communities and promote community-centered resilience strategies. 可靠的基建設施系統對現今社會發展尤其重要。儘管如此，由於急劇氣候變化和人類行為改變，基建系統越來越容易發生故障。因此，世界各國政府已經開始採取各種方案，以確保基建設施更有韌性，以應對社區的變化。然而，因為缺乏一個各方接受的機制來組合、統一和分析從不同基建系統運營商持有的數據，實施社區韌性計劃面臨極大挑戰。 大眾資料搜集的發展有助彌補信息差距。現今之人群感應技術可以徵集和共享一系列不同但相互的基建系統狀況數據，從而協助作出決策。而大眾資料搜集平臺更可用作收集有關公眾使基建設施的行為之數據，以幫助提高社區韌性計劃的可靠性。通過大眾資料搜集，政府部門、公用事業公司和市民不但可一起提供數據，而他們也可分析基建系統的狀況及共同製定社區韌性的策略。正因社區可以在韌性規劃、開發和實施上發揮更積極的作用，大眾資料搜集應能有效實現全社會韌性主義。 儘管如此，大眾資料搜集不單引入有用的數據，但亦可能收集不少不相關的信息。這項研究的目的是通過開發和使用大眾資料搜集框架和平台、以良好的結構和可靠的方式採集和分析與基建系統和使用者行為狀況相關的數據，從而改善社區韌性的實施。 研究將從文獻綜述，訪談，案例研究，焦點小組會議和德爾福研究開始，以揭示社區韌性所需的數據、並確定最適合的大眾資料搜集方法。研究團隊將透過研討會，設計一個以大眾資料搜集為基礎的框架落實大眾資料搜集之運作流程、主數據模型及主數據管理系統的軟件架構。研究團隊亦將開發一個原型平台、並且組織大眾資料搜集和恢復力籌建活動，最後透過兩個案例驗證開發框架和原型平台之可靠性。 本研究的結果將有助解決相互依賴的基建系統的數據瓶頸，為現有的韌性研究和實踐做出重大貢獻。通過大眾資料搜集方式及讓群眾更有效參與社區韌性決策，應有助培育和諧的智慧社區、並促進以社區為中心的韌性戰略。

17204017.label: Realisation of objectives
17204017.value: Objective 1: To investigate the potentials and best practices of crowdsourcing data for infrastructure networks management and community resilience A thorough desktop study was carried to unveil the best practices of infrastructure networks management and community resilience. Detailed investigations were conducted to examine the representative community resilience frameworks and indicators, in particular their ability to model the time-evolving characteristics and dynamic network features of the community [Conference Paper 1]. Case studies were then followed to analyze the common hazards they are facing, as well as the common grounds and gaps of their infrastructure resilience policies and practices based on four well-known bay areas, i.e.: San Francisco Bay Area, New York Metropolitan Area, Greater Tokyo Area and the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macau Greater Bay Area [Conference Paper 2]. Comparison of resilience policy were performed to identify the policy interdependencies and gaps when conducting infrastructure networks management and community resilience [Conference Paper 3]. Interviews were designed and organized with experts to unravel their insights, concerns and needs regarding community resilience. Based on the that, a suite of built environment oriented metrics was established. Objective 2: To formulate a suitable crowdsourcing strategy to acquire, integrate and analyze infrastructure networks data and co-produce resilience A news mining approach was adopted to solicit information from news to help acquire, integrate and analyze infrastructure networks data and co-produce resilience under a certain infrastructure failure condition. In the absence of a suitable dictionary to drive the data mining process, a city infrastructure dictionary was established in this research to supplement the default natural language processing lexicon to improve the accuracy of entity identification. The city infrastructure dictionary (version 1.0) established in this research contains nearly 30,000 items, which were collected from official websites, open databases and call APIs provided by commercial maps. Apart from that, the passenger traveling data between 2019 and 2020 was collected from the Mass Transit Railway Limited. Data mining approaches were adopted to unveil the traveling patterns at times of disruptions, such as during social movement and pandemic. Finally, computer vision was integrated with traffic modeling for near-real-time signal timing optimization, and this include configuring real-time video sources, conducting transfer-learning to develop the vehicle detector, comparing and selecting vehicle trackers, collecting traffic parameters, establishing and running the traffic model, and operating simulation-based optimization. Objective 3: To design a master data model to collect, integrate, cleanse and analyze the crowdsourced data and data solicited from the infrastructure asset management systems A master data model was designed and developed to collect and analyze the news items related to burst pipe incidents, the affected infrastructure systems, and the stakeholders being affected by the incidents. For the preparation of domain knowledge components, we used the dictionary of city infrastructure developed in the preceding stage, couple with the index words and synonyms of potentially affected infrastructure and stakeholders, and index words of infrastructure damages to facilitate the data extraction process. The master data model also help integrate, cleansed the analyzed the data solicited from the passenger data collected from the Mass Transit Railway Limited as well as the traffic data captured from the real-time video sources to facilitate holistic interdependent infrastructure resilience decision support. Objective 4: To devise an open framework to crowdsource data related to the condition and use pattern of infrastructure networks A 3M framework is devised based on the existing literature alleged to have already achieved data-driven and physics-based integration. The framework consists of three components: determine motivations, select methods, and design connection modes [Conference Paper 4]. Given that diverse information is maintained by different infrastructure asset owners and operators in heterogenous formats, a building information modeling, geographic information system and domain-specific computation engine (BIM-GIS-DCEs) enabled framework was out forwarded and developed to assess the vulnerability of interdependent infrastructure networks. To facilitate seamless integration, Semantic web technologies were used for information integration. The designed framework is composed of four modules: (i) cross domain linkage based on ontology development; (ii) multiple-source heterogeneous data integration through automated ontology instantiation and RDF; (iii) information retrieval by the RDF query language; and (iv) logical inferencing supported by rule language and logic engines. The first two modules create a common data sharing environment for heterogenous data available in various systems. The last two modules support various stakeholders in performing information retrieval and automatic logical reasoning to make rational decisions. Objective 5: To implement a software prototype of data crowdsourcing platform to enhance the operationalization of community resilience With the master data model built and the open framework for crowdsource data developed, analyses were performed. First, the resilience performance of interdependent infrastructure system with the condition-varying components was synthetically assessed by leveraging the physics-based approaches in order to delineate the intricate operating scheme of each infrastructure system. Moreover, a federated pre-event community resilience approach which assembles the topological-based evaluation, physics-based performance simulation and multicriteria decision analysis was adopted to evaluate the physical and social sub-systems under the influence of various disruptions. To more accurately characterize the failures of interdependent infrastructure systems, the crowdsourced data was combined with the physics-based approach. The entropy weight method and the technology for order preference by similarity to an ideal solution method (EWM-TOPSIS) were implemented to examine the viability of multiple recovery strategies after a disruption so as to enhance the operationalization of community resilience. Objective 6: To validate the proposed framework and the prototype through case studies The proposed framework was applied to assess the resilience performance of interdependent infrastructure systems. A case study was used to investigate the resilience performance of interdependent stormwater drainage system, building and road transport system in Hong Kong against heavy rainfall. Wanchai was selected for this case study as the district is one of the flooding blackspots in the city. Compound failure scenarios were considered, and the impacts to the transportation networks were carefully examined based on the developed master data model, open framework for crowdsource data and the software prototype. The results of validation help the investigators examine the applicability and the accuracy of the crowdsourcing approaches in improving the operationalization of community resilience.

17204017.label: Major findings and research outcome
17204017.value: Infrastructure failure interdependencies and associate stakeholders can be systematically delineated through the news mining approaches. However, it is challenging to implement a generic entity recognition tool to extract the infrastructure-related entities. Therefore, a dictionary of city infrastructure is developed to enrich and supplement the existing natural language processing lexicons that lack consideration of the infrastructure domain [Journal Paper 1]. On the other hand, computer vision is a power crowdsourcing approach for community resilience. Through real-time surveillance videos, three critical information items including the traffic volumes, vehicle compositions, and vehicles’ turning ratios can be derived. The extracted information can be automatically incorporated into the traffic model to optimize the signal timings of inter-connected intersections in a near-real-time manner [Journal Paper 2]. Synchronizing available toolkits like building information modeling, geographic information system and domain-specific computational engine would not only help eliminate the needs for developing cost intensive and resourceful gigantic software, but it could also facilitate system-of-systems-based infrastructure vulnerability assessment [Journal Paper 3]. To achieve seamless data integration between different infrastructure systems, however, requires the adoption of the Semantic web technologies to integrate the heterogeneous data integration through automated ontology instantiation and resource description framework schema. With that, machine automatic logical reasoning can be derived by rule languages and logic engines to provide informed interdependent infrastructure resilience decision making support [Journal Paper 4]. A component condition modeling section can be incorporated to the physics-based resilience assessment to reflect the influence of the varying component conditions on system-wide resilience performance assessment [Journal Paper 5]. Besides, social dimension should be consolidated into the community resilience analysis framework. Empirical evidence solicited through crowdsourcing means should be leveraged during the comparative assessment of social resilience through the multi-criteria decision analysis models [Journal Paper 6]. It is imperative to integrate diverse crowdsource data with the physics-based model to help demystify the failure propagation among interdependent infrastructures. The data-driven methods serve to supplement the physics-based approaches to increase the accuracy of near-real-time decision support in community resilience decisions [Journal Paper 7]. Various methods in particular the entropy weight method and the technology for order preference by similarity to an ideal solution method (EWM-TOPSIS) can be applied to unveil the criticality of certain nodes within an infrastructure system [Journal Paper 8]. Using the crowdsourced data, EMW-TOPSIS can be applied to examine the viability of multiple recovery strategies and to evaluate the recovery ability of an infrastructure system after a disruption [Journal Paper 9].

17204017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17204017.value: From the perspective of text mining, there is still improvement rooms for the natural language processing tools’ capabilities regarding the accuracy, precision, recall, speed, and reliability in processing and analyzing natural languages. The potential solution for resolving the errors results from ambiguity and out-of-vocabulary words, and negators should be actualized. Despite extensive research in computer vision, its application should be further examined under different scenarios in more cities. By reason of the public security and privacy policies, researchers are restricted in getting access to real-time surveillance videos, and this impedes large-scale experiments to better validate the computer vision approach and tools through case study. The field surveys would also provide more factual pollutant emissions than the estimations based on the traffic simulation. While the integration of BIM, GIS and DCEs constitutes a novel, practical and versatile paradigm in modeling interwoven infrastructure systems and identifying the intangible vulnerabilities when hazard occurs, it is interesting to investigate the vulnerabilities of interconnected infrastructure systems caused by super typhoon, pandemic, etc. The study should be extended to soft infrastructure which covers the facilities or services which are required to maintain the economic, health, educational, and social standards of a population, as opposed to the physical infrastructure.

17204017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17204017.value: A crowdsourcing framework and platform have been developed to capture and analyze data pertinent to the condition of infrastructure systems and user behavior. The framework has filled the research gap of ensuring infrastructure systems are more resilient to changes to best serve the communities. Through the crowdsourcing framework and platform, useful data pertinent to the passenger patterns, traffic conditions, affected infrastructures and affected stakeholders can be systematically delineated to help decision-makers identify the resilience of infrastructure systems against failure and to examiner which recovery strategies should be put in place to ensure a speedy recovery of the affected infrastructure systems. In this research, a series of approaches, viz. news mining and computer vision, have been proposed to capture the data. The captured data is integrated with the physics-based approaches to enhance the modeling accuracy. Acknowledging the heterogeneity of the data in different infrastructure systems, an integrated building information model, geographic information system and domain-specific computational engines framework has been developed to assess the vulnerability of interdependent infrastructure systems. The approaches and framework can be used for analyzing different types of hazards in an accurate and near-real-time manner, and this should help improve the resilience of the community against future hazards.

17204117.label: Project Objectives
17204117.value: Achieving a new scheme of room-temperature ligand-promoted formation of high-quality organic-inorganic hybrid/ all-inorganic perovskites. We will demonstrate a new scheme of room-temperature ligand-promoted formation of perovskites (e.g., CH3NH3 PbxSn1-xI3, HC(NH2)2CH3NH3PbxSn1-xI3, and CsPbxSn1-xI3) featuring pinhole-free, impurity-free and high crystalline structures. The scheme includes two stages: (I) ligand-induced formation of nanostructure-based mixed MX2(L)y complex films (M= Pb, Sn, Bi or alloy; L=ligand for perovskite formation; X = I, Br, Cl, or mixtures, 0≤y≤ 2) from MX2 film and ligand vapors at room temperature that favors the perovskite transformation; (II) ligand-facilitated formation of perovskite film through ligand exchange reactions between MX2(L)y complex and organic ammonium halide or inorganic halide salts with advantage of ligand exchange at room temperature. Using our method for the crystallization of perovskite films at room-temperature, we aim to construct high-performance PSCs that achieve a power conversion efficiency (PCE) toward 20% (the current best PSCs based on perovskite fabricated at room temperature have a PCE of <16%). This room-temperature scheme can (i) avoid the unexpected generation of defects/trap states caused by thermal annealing; and (ii) allow all steps of device fabrication to take place at room temperature (through leveraging with other room-temperature solution-processed layers in the multilayered PSC structure) toward the realization of large-scale and low-cost production of rigid and flexible PSCs. Demonstrating a new approach of post-device ligand-induced regional modification of perovskites for improving PSC stability. We propose a new approach for the post-device ligand treatment of perovskites using ligand vapors to chemically modify the non-operated regions of the perovskite layer in fabricated PSC devices to improve their stability. We will (I) realize ligand-enhanced PSC stability for different perovskites, (II) identify the origins of the improved moisture stability, and (III) investigate the changes of electrical and optical properties of PSCs due to the ligand treatment. Consequently, the post-device treatment can improve PSC stability and reduce the risk of introducing unwanted impurities during the fabrication, and can be easily adopted to other perovskite devices. We also aim to demonstrate that the treated PSCs (without encapsulation) will retain 90% of the initial efficiency after 500hrs of the standard moisture stability test. Theoretically understanding the mechanisms of ligand-promoted high-quality perovskite formation and post-device ligand-induced perovskite modification. We will elucidate the mechanism of ligand-enhanced high-quality perovskite formation through thermodynamics and kinetics studies. Thermodynamically, we will study and minimize the formation enthalpy of perovskite from MX2(L)y complex (∆Hf) to achieve the spontaneous perovskite formation from MX2(L)y complex. Kinetically, we will study the formation rate of perovskite by investigating the activation energy (Ea) of perovskite formation via different pathways. We will also elucidate the mechanism of post-device ligand-induced perovskite modification through thermodynamics and molecular dynamic studies. Thermodynamically, we will minimize the formation enthalpy of MX2(L”)y complex from perovskite (∆Hd) where L” is the ligand for post-device treatment to realize spontaneous MX2(L”)y formation. We will also study the adsorption energy, diffusion pathways, and diffusion barriers of water molecules in MX2(L”)y complex for understanding the improved PSC stability. Establishing ligand selection rules for high-quality perovskite formation and stability-improved perovskite modification. For the ligand-promoted perovskite formation, we will establish ligand selection rules through (i) understanding the reactivity of various ligands (obtained from Objective 3) on the formation kinetics; and (ii) investigating the effects of the ligand properties (e.g., solubility, molecular size, and volatility) on the morphology and film quality of perovskites. For the post-device ligand treatment, we will identify the rules through (i) systematically analyzing the reactivity of different ligands (obtained from Objective 3), and (ii) understanding the effects of the water-proofing properties of MX2(L”)y complex films and the ligand properties on the moisture stability of PSCs. ***Note: as proof of concept and to show feasibility of the project, we have conducted preliminary studies on the ligand-enhanced perovskite formation and the post-device ligand-induced perovskite modification. By using the CH3NH3PbI3 perovskite formed using our room temperature approach, we fabricated PSCs that could reach PCE > 17% (see “Research Plan and Methodology” for details).

We will demonstrate a new scheme of room-temperature ligand-promoted formation of perovskites (e.g., CH3NH3 PbxSn1-xI3, HC(NH2)2CH3NH3PbxSn1-xI3, and CsPbxSn1-xI3) featuring pinhole-free, impurity-free and high crystalline structures. The scheme includes two stages: (I) ligand-induced formation of nanostructure-based mixed MX2(L)y complex films (M= Pb, Sn, Bi or alloy; L=ligand for perovskite formation; X = I, Br, Cl, or mixtures, 0≤y≤ 2) from MX2 film and ligand vapors at room temperature that favors the perovskite transformation; (II) ligand-facilitated formation of perovskite film through ligand exchange reactions between MX2(L)y complex and organic ammonium halide or inorganic halide salts with advantage of ligand exchange at room temperature. Using our method for the crystallization of perovskite films at room-temperature, we aim to construct high-performance PSCs that achieve a power conversion efficiency (PCE) toward 20% (the current best PSCs based on perovskite fabricated at room temperature have a PCE of <16%). 17204117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17204117.value: 由於其低成本和高性能，鈣鈦礦被廣泛研究用於形成光電器件，特別是太陽能電池。大多數有效的鈣鈦礦電池需要針對多層結構的每層進行層依賴的高溫處理，這增加了製造複雜性。此外，高溫工藝阻礙形成高質量的溫度敏感的無鉛鈣鈦礦（例如錫）和鈣鈦礦在柔性器件中的應用。近來，已經開發了用於在室溫下處理的鈣鈦礦光電器件的各種載流子傳輸層和電極。因此，在室溫下開發鈣鈦礦薄膜可控加工方法，可以簡化複雜的器件工藝，促進出現的柔性器件技術。在這個項目中，我們將提出一種新的室溫方案，用於可控配體促進形成無小孔，無雜質，並具有高結晶度的高質量鈣鈦礦薄膜。我們將通過實驗研究不同配體對鈣鈦礦膜的形態和膜質量的影響，以及研究器件性能，通過使用由該方案製成的鈣鈦礦膜。我們還將在理論上研究熱力學和動力學，以了解配體促進的鈣鈦礦形成的機制。因此，我們將建立識別配體以形成高質量鈣鈦礦膜的選擇規則，目的是提高鈣鈦礦電池性能。 水分穩定一直是鈣鈦礦電池的根本挑戰。在這個項目中，我們提出了一種在室溫下在製造器件上配體誘導的鈣鈦礦區域修飾的新方案。配體將在所選擇的橫向區域中引起化學修飾，特別是多層鈣鈦礦電池內的鈣鈦礦層的化學修飾。這些修飾被設計成防止水分子擴散到活躍的鈣鈦礦區域，從而提高鈣鈦礦電池的穩定性。我們理論上研究了處理過的鈣鈦礦的熱力學和防水性能，揭示了鈣鈦礦電池配體增強水分穩定性的機理。因此，我們的目標是利用這些知識來識別和理解用於器件後處理的最佳配體，以提高鈣鈦礦電池的穩定性。 本研究將提供對配位體對鈣鈦礦形成和室溫下器件後處理的基礎理解，以便將來設計高性能，穩定和低成本的基於鈣鈦礦的光電子器件。這項工作還將為實現新興的柔性鈣鈦礦裝置提供新途徑。

17204117.label: Realisation of objectives
17204117.value: In objective 1, we have continuously investigated various ligands and additives to promote the quality of different perovskites. For conventional MAPbI3 perovskite, by introducing methylamine gas, we can liquefy the MAPbBr3 crystals [ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2020, 12, 24498]. Through comprehensively understanding the material and crystallization properties of the precursor, we achieve dense MAPbBr3 films with crystallographically oriented grain arrangements that show single-crystal-like properties. For these conventional organic perovskites, we have achieved a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 21.2% [ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2020, 12, 57165]. We further study inorganic CsPbI3 perovskites which are expected to be more stable by eliminating the organic A-site cation. We demonstrate the decoration of CsPbI3 with ABA and NGBr [Adv. Mater. 2020, 2000186]. The ABA or NG cation adsorb onto the grain boundaries/surface of CsPbI3 anchors the PbI6 octahedra, which maintains the continuous array of corner-sharing PbI6 octahedra and kinetically stabilizes the photoactive phase CsPbI3. Moreover, the ABA and NGBr interact with shallow- or deep-level defects in CsPbI3 to significantly reduce defect density, and improve energy-level alignment between the CsPbI3 and the charge transport layers. Finally, the champion CsPbI3 PSCs deliver 18.27% efficiency. After optimization, we achieve CsPbI3 PSCs with PCE of 22.37% [Adv. Funct. Mater. 2021, 31, 2101438]. To increase the absorption band of perovskite, we also study Sn-Pb alloy perovskite. We introduce Sn(II) complex into the perovskite film during the anti-solvent process [Adv. Energy Mater. 2020, 10, 1903013]. Interestingly, uniquely formed is the quasi-core-shell structure of Pb-Sn perovskite: tin(II) complex as well as heterojunction perovskite structure. The unique structure effectively passivates the trap states and suppresses the nonradiative recombination, leading to a longer carrier lifetime. By optimizing the growing process of the Sn-Pb perovskite film, we also enhance the crystallinity and form block-like perovskites with thickness over 1um [Adv. Funct. Mater. 2021, 31, 2010532] to improve the absorption properties. Overall, the mixed Pb-Sn low-bandgap PSCs achieve a high PCE of 19.03% with a fill factor over 0.8, which is among the highest fill factor in high-performance Pb-Sn PSCs. Remarkably, the device fail time under continuous light illumination is extended by over 18.5-folds. In objective 2, the approaches which can improve the quality of perovskites as stated in objective 1 can be used to improve PSC stability and efficiency in both Pb-based and Sn-Pb alloy perovskites. Additionally, we have studied the approaches to further reduce perovskite defects. Particularly, we introduce additives to suppress the unexpected chemical reaction of perovskite and defects between the perovskite and hole transport layer (HTL). For instance, by introducing NaPSS additives, both the reaction and defects are diminished [Adv. Funct. Mater. 2019, 1905339]. For another popular HTL of PEDOT, MoOx is introduced to improve the crystallinity of perovskite [ACS Nano, 13, 11800, 2019]. Meanwhile, we find that by introducing imidazole bromide functionalized graphene quantum dots (I-GQDs), we can suppress the defects between FAPbI3 perovskite and electron transport layer and thus improve its stability [Adv. Funct. Mater. 2021, 31, 2101438]. These all improve the optical and electrical properties of PSCs. The best-performed PSCs reach very good stability and remain 90% of the initial value of PCE over 2000 h. [ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2021, 13, 27179]. In objective 3, we study the mechanisms of improving the quality and properties of perovskites. By introducing the ABA and NGBr into CsPbI3 perovskites, we theoretically study Cs terminated and ABA-terminated CsPbI3 (Figure 2e,f) through the density functional theory (DFT) calculations [Adv. Mater. 2020, 2000186]. The calculated formation energies for Cs and ABA terminated perovskite surfaces are 0.058 eV and -0.218 eV, respectively. The ABA terminated surface is, therefore, more stable than that of the Cs terminated one. The DFT model is further used to understand the ligand effects on the defects between perovskite and HTL. When the ligand of KSCN is introduced, the interfacial defects between MAPbI3 and NiOx HTL are reduced [Small Methods 2020, 2000478]. From the DFT results of the two-dimension slices of charge density distribution, the main interactions at the interface come from the Ni-Pb and Ni-I. Because of the rearrangement at the interface, the I atoms close to the interface show a more positive charge compared with the inner. The theoretical results confirm that the KSCN can effectively passivate incomplete coordination of Ni atoms on the surface. Meanwhile, there is an electrostatic force between S and Pb, which makes the Pb atomic layer closer to the perovskite side to restrain the I atom. Furthermore, the I atoms show the charge close to that of the inner layer. The DOS of I shows that the highest occupied states shift to a lower energy state, which closes to the inner layer. Therefore, with KSCN, the iodine atoms at the interface are more stable. Consequently, the SCN- offers a double passivation effect as an interface modification layer between NiOx and MAPbI3 and thus improves PSC stability and performance. Notably, by introducing 2-dimensional perovskite with different ligands as cations, we can further improve the stability and performance [ACS Energy Lett. 2020, 5, 2569; Adv. Mater. 2020, 2005570]. which are explained by the photophysics analysis and the model of spare-charge limited. We also study the optical properties of perovskite devices with different nanostructure morphologies. By using full-wave simulation through the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method, the absorption and emission properties of the structured perovskites have been explained [ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2021, 13, 27313]. Overall, the mechanisms of the performance and stability improvement of various perovskites have been theoretically explained. In objective 4, various families of ligand derivatives have been introduced into perovskite for understanding their effects on the selection of different functional groups. We have introduced Lewis base organic ligands (namely 2-mercaptobenzimidazole (MBI), 5-nitro-2-mercaptobenzimidazole (MBI-NO2), and 5-methoxy-2-mercaptobenzimidazole (MBI-OCH3)) to modify MAPbI3 perovskite for improving the performance and stability of PSCs [ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2020, 12, 57165]. Interestingly, MBI without any functional group and its derivative MBI-OCH3 with the electron-donating functional group OCH3 show a positive effect on PCE improvement, but there is a negative effect for MBI-NO2 with the electron-withdrawing functional group NO2. Our studies show that the defect passivation effect and energy level alignment with NiOx HTL in PSCs can be modulated via rationally modulating functional groups. This suggests that functional groups in interface molecules play a critical role in final device performance. In addition, a series of inorganic ligand derivatives have been studied on the effects on the perovskite and carrier transport layer. In our study of KSCN, KCL, and CH3COOK on the perovskite [Small Methods 2020, 2000478], we show the workfunction modification of KSCN is the largest which offers the best alignment of band structure between perovskite and NiOx HTL. From XPS studies, the relative content of Ni3+ species increases significantly by introducing the KSCN modification on the NiOx film whereas there is a slight change when KCl and KAc treated the NiOx films. Therefore, the KSCN surface modification has more potential to change the electronic property at the region between perovskite and NiOx HTL. In addition, the quality and film morphology of perovskite will not degrade by incorporating the additives. Consequently, different families of organic and inorganic ligands have been investigated for understanding their effects and thus obtaining selection guides for using them in perovskites to improve PSC performance and stability.

Funct. Mater. 2021, 31, 2101438]. With further optimization of device structure and carrier transport layer, the stability of more stable PSCs can reach an operation lifetime of over 2000hours [ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2021, 13, 27179]. (1) Different ligands have been demonstrated to improve the quality of different perovskites including organic and inorganic Pb and Pb-Sn-based perovskites. The results are been published in [Adv. Energy Mater. 2020, 10, 1903013, Adv. Funct. Mater. 2021, 31, 2010532, ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2020, 12, 24498 and Adv. Mater. 2020, 2000186]. (2) New approaches of ligand-induced modification of perovskites have been proposed and demonstrated to improve the stability and performance of PSCs. The results have been published in [Adv. Mater. 2020, 2000186, Adv. Energy Mater. 2020, 10, 1903013, ACS Nano, 13, 11800, 2019, Adv. Funct. Mater. 2019, 1905339, Adv. Funct. Mater. 2021, 31, 2101438, J. Mater. Chem. A, 9, 371, 2021 and Adv. Funct. Mater. 2019, 29, 1902600]. (3) The work offers a better understanding of the mechanism of the improved perovskite quality and performance. The theoretical studies of the perovskite from first principle have been carried out using DFT and the optical properties of the perovskite with different nanostructure have also been investigated by the full-wave model. The results are reported in [Adv. Mater. 2020, 2000186, Small Methods 2020, 2000478, ACS Energy Lett. 2020, 5, 2569, Adv. Mater. 2020, 2005570, ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2021, 13, 27313]. (4) The selection guides of ligands for improving perovskite quality and PSC performance have been described by studying the derivatives of organic and inorganic ligands for understanding the effects of different functional groups. The results have been reported in [Small Methods 2020, 2000478, ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2020, 12, 57165, Small 2020, 16, 2002628, ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2020, 12, 24498, and Adv. Funct. Mater. 2019, 1904684]. It should be noted that the outputs stated in this progress report are achieved through the financial support from this GRF fund together with some other grants from RGC as stated in the acknowledgement of the publications.

17204117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17204117.value: With the demonstrated approaches and the understanding of their effects on perovskite quality and optoelectronic properties from comprehensive theoretical and experimental studies, our work can contribute as guides for scientists to improve the crystalline and quality of perovskites covering organic and inorganic based A site cations as well as Pb and Sn-Pb B sites ions. Besides, the knowledge of achieving high-quality perovskites in this project can be adopted into other the development of optoelectronic devices such as photodetectors and light-emitting diodes. The series of low-temperature solution-processed perovskite materials can be explored for developing emerging flexible optoelectronics.

17204117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17204117.value: In this work, we have proposed and demonstrated the simple low/room temperature scheme of ligand promoted the formation of high-quality organic and inorganic perovskites. Our results show that the perovskite performance (PCE > 22%) and stability (T90> over 2000 hrs) have been significantly improved through the suppression of the defects and enhancement of the crystallinity of perovskite materials. The fundamental understanding of the mechanism of the influences of the ligands on the perovskites and devices has been theoretically and experimentally explained. The selection requirements of organic and inorganic ligands and the effects of different functional groups of ligands have need summarized for improving perovskite optoelectronic properties. The project covering modeling, and materials to devices provide not only a fundamental understanding of ligands of perovskite solar cells but also new material design for improving device efficiency and stability. The work, therefore, contributes to promoting perovskites for practical and low-cost applications in photovoltaics.

17204317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17204317.value: Electric vehicles (EVs) have been identified to be the greenest road transportation. Nevertheless, there are two fundamental problems of EVs that limit their popularization – short driving range and high initial cost. Instead of establishing more charging stations and developing faster chargers to alleviate the problems, EVs can harness wireless power from electromagnetic field in air and then charge their batteries when running on the road. This roadway-powered EV technology can fundamentally solve their problems of short driving range due to limited battery storage or high initial cost due to the use of a large number of batteries. In recent years, many researchers have actively developed various wireless power transfer technologies for EV charging. Nevertheless, the security issue is nearly unexplored, which is vitally important for the roadway-powered EV technology. Namely, the roadway-powered EV system needs to selectively charge the authorized EVs when those unauthorized EVs are running on the same road. Triggering from signal encryption for wireless communication, the idea of energy encryption for wireless power transfer is born. In essence, the transmitter buried beneath the road wirelessly transfers the energy which is encrypted by a security key (technically, the operating frequency and its duration are programmed to vary with a chaotic sequence) so that the pickups of those authorized EVs which know the security key can decrypt the energy by tuning their resonant frequency accordingly. Without knowledge of the security key, the unauthorized EVs cannot extract the encrypted energy because of the nature of high impedance under frequency mismatch. The purpose of this proposal is to develop a novel energy-encrypted wireless power transfer system for roadway-powered EVs. The objectives are: (1) design a new configuration of energy-encrypted wireless power transfer system, which can selectively charge the authorized EVs while preventing the unauthorized EVs from stealing the energy; (2) develop a novel energy encryption scheme, which can offer high security and high feasibility while maintaining efficient and effective power transfer; (3) formulate new analytical models, with emphasis on power transfer efficiency and power delivery as well as steady-state and frequency responses; (4) perform electromagnetic field analysis and dynamic simulation to optimize the system parameters, and to assess the encryption performance, safety issue and electromagnetic compatibility; (5) develop new control strategies to achieve energy encryption while optimizing the power transfer efficiency and power delivery; and (6) implement the whole system for experimentation, hence evaluating its technical performances and cost-effectiveness. 電動車已被確定為最綠色的公路運輸。然而，電動車有兩個基本問題限制了其普及性: 行駛里程短、初始成本高。在不需要建立更多的充電站和開發更快的充電器來減輕這些問題的情況下，電動車可以利用來自空中電磁場的無線電力，在路上運行時對其電池充電。這種電動車在行駛中無線電力傳輸技術可以從根本上解決他們由於有限的電池存儲而導致的行駛里程短或由於使用大量電池而導致的初始成本高的問題。 近年來，許多研究人員積極開發了各種用於電動車充電的無線電力傳輸技術。然而，其安全問題幾乎沒有被探索，這對於電動車在行駛中無線充電技術至關重要。也就是說，無線充電系統需要選擇性地對授權的電動車在行駛中進行充電，未經授權的電動車同時也能在相同的道路上運行。無線電力傳輸的能量加密構想是從無線通信的信號加密所啟發。原理上，埋在道路下方的發射器無線地傳輸由安全密鑰加密的能量（技術上，操作頻率及其持續時間被編程為隨混沌序列而變化），那些授權的電動車的接收器可以通過相應地調諧其諧振頻率來解密能量。在不知道安全密鑰的情況下，未經授權的電動車的接收器需要面對由於頻率不匹配下的高阻抗性質，因而不能提取加密的能量。 本項目的目的是開發一種用於電動車在行駛中的新型能量加密無線電力傳輸系統。目標是：（1）設計一種能量加密無線電力傳輸系統的新配置，從而可以選擇性地對授權的電動車進行充電，同時防止未經授權的電動車竊取能量;（2）開發一種新穎的能量加密方案，可以提供高安全性和高可行性，同時保持有效用和高效率的電力傳輸;（3）制定新的分析模型，並專注於電力傳輸效率、功率輸送、穩態響應和頻率響應;（4）利用電磁場分析和動態仿真去優化系統參數，並評估其加密性能、安全性和電磁兼容性;（5）制定新的控制策略去實現能源加密，同時優化電力傳輸效率和功率輸送;（6）落實整個系統去進行實驗，並評估其技術性能和成本效益。

17204317.label: Realisation of objectives
17204317.value: The 1st objective has been fully completed. A new configuration of energy-encrypted wireless power transfer (WPT) system has been proposed for roadway-powered electric vehicles (EVs), namely the rail-transmitter design. The pad-transmitter design can selectively perform WPT to charge authorized EVs by switching on and off a particular set of transmitter coils, but suffers from complex installation and huge investment cost. The proposed rail-transmitter design can selectively charge the authorized EVs when both authorized and unauthorized EVs are running on the same section of electrified roadways. Consequently, the wireless energy emitted from the transmitter is encrypted in such a way that only the authorized EVs which know the security key can retrieve the wireless energy while those unauthorized EVs cannot steal the energy. The rail-transmitter design has been critically compared with the pad-transmitter design, which takes the definite advantages of much lower installation complexity and much lower investment cost. Moreover, rather than using a switched-capacitor array at the transmitter to create multiple resonant frequencies for energy encryption, a new switched-capacitorless energy-encrypted transmitter has been proposed, which can maintain high power transfer efficiency while achieving flexible operating frequencies. Rather than limiting the resonant frequencies at particular discrete values, a novel continuously variable-frequency energy-encrypted WPT system has been proposed, which makes use of the LCC-compensated transmitter and static variable capacitors to continuously encrypt and decrypt the wireless energy. Furthermore, the proposed WPT system has been extended to simultaneously energize multi-standard receivers that are installed in various EVs. The 2nd objective has been fully completed. The key of the proposed energy encryption is to borrow the concept of wireless communication for radio broadcasting and the idea of spread spectrum for secure communication. Namely, when the frequency of wireless energy emitted from the transmitter is online varied in accordance with a pre-defined chaotic sequence (so-called the security key), the receiver of authorized EVs can online tune its compensation network to retrieve the wireless energy based on the knowledge of security key. To prevent the encrypted energy package from being illegally decrypted by unauthorized EVs while enabling authorized EVs to effectively pick up the energy, the chaotic sequence should be robust enough. A novel two-dimensional chaotic frequency-and-duration encryption scheme has been proposed and implemented for the energy-encrypted WPT system. Moreover, a new full-range soft-switching pulse-frequency modulation scheme has been developed, which can suppress the switching frequency and power losses while maintaining the full-range soft-switching feature for efficient and effective power transfer. Hence, it can achieve high security and high feasibility while offering high efficiency and high controllability for energy-encrypted WPT. The 3rd objective has been fully completed. Based on circuit modeling of the proposed energy-encrypted WPT system, the corresponding analytical models have been formulated. In particular, three multilayer rectangular coil structures including the spiral, concentrated and uneven compound types are analytically modeled, which identifies that the uneven compound coil can provide more uniform magnetic flux density distribution and hence achieve better tolerance of misalignment. Consequently, the power transfer efficiency and power delivery can be analytically derived. It indicates that the system efficiency increases with the increase of mutual inductance, which is governed by the coupling between the transmitter and the receiver. Moreover, the mutual inductance between the transmitter and receiver coils of the energy-encrypted WPT system is analytically derived. By properly selecting the transmitter compensated capacitance, the harvested wireless power can be optimized with fewer fluctuations. Thus, the corresponding steady-state performances and frequency responses can be deduced. The 4th objective has been fully completed. The electromagnetic field analysis of the proposed uneven compound coil structure has been performed, which includes the magnetic flux density distribution and electric potential distribution, hence minimizing the difference of magnetic fields that can be picked up by multiple receivers and determining the maximum input current at the desired operating frequency. Consequently, the encryption performances of the proposed energy-encrypted WPT system are simulated and assessed. By using the co-simulation of JMAG and Simulink, the system parameters such as the mutual inductance and compensation capacitance can be iteratively optimized to improve the system performances, especially the power transfer efficiency and power handling capability. Meanwhile, dynamic simulation of the whole system has been conducted to confirm the selectivity of the proposed energy encryption scheme. Moreover, electromagnetic interference and electromagnetic compatibility of the proposed system have been simulated, which confirms that the electromagnetic fields in the vicinity are within various international standards and exhibit no harmful or safety issue on human bodies. The 5th objective has been fully completed. The control strategies that are specially devised for the proposed energy-encrypted WPT system have been developed. Namely, by using the proposed two-dimensional chaotic frequency-and-duration control algorithm, the desired energy encryption can be realized while optimizing the power transfer efficiency and power delivery. Rather than taking the initiative to deliver the wireless power and its security key to the authorized EVs, the system can nominate the authorized receiver to take over the initiative and generate a well-defended security key based on two-dimensional frequency-and-duration chaos. This concept is so-called the energy-on-demand WPT, alike the video-on-demand service in multimedia platforms. Thus, a novel magnetic quasi-resonant coupling scheme has been proposed to realize this concept. Meanwhile, a new low-frequency-switching phase-shift control scheme has been developed for high-frequency-resonating WPT, which can effectively reduce the current fluctuations and switching losses. The 6th objective has been fully completed. The proposed energy-encrypted WPT system, including the circuit configuration, coil structure, encryption algorithm and control strategy, has been implemented. A system prototype has been built for experimentation, which confirms that the proposed energy encryption and control strategies work well. The corresponding technical performances such as the power transfer efficiency, power delivery, controllability and selectivity are tested and measured, which agree with the theoretical values and computer simulation results. Moreover, the corresponding material cost, manufacturing cost and operating cost are calculated based on industrial standards. Hence, the cost-effectiveness of the whole system is deduced, which confirm that it has high commercial and market values. Additionally, the proposed system has been further extended to automatic guided vehicles, which desires efficient and effective operation with minimum sensors. Thus, a new move-and-charge system adopting current threshold control has been developed for automatic guided vehicles, which not only performs the desired wireless charging, but also automatically navigates the vehicle without using guiding sensors.

17204317.label: Major findings and research outcome
17204317.value: The research outcome is very fruitful, namely 8 international journal papers [J1]-[J8] and 5 international conference papers [C1]-[C5]. Meanwhile, 3 PhD students have been trained. Concerning the design of system configuration, we have first conducted a critical overview of wireless power transfer (WPT) for electric vehicles (EVs) [J1]. Then, a novel switched-capacitorless energy-encrypted transmitter has been proposed for roadway-charging EVs, which does not rely on using a switched-capacitor array in the transmitter while transferring power to multiple receivers [C1], [J3]. Meanwhile, a new move-and-charge system has been developed for automatic guided vehicles, which not only performs wireless charging, but also automatically navigates the vehicle without using guiding sensors [C3], [J4]. Consequently, a novel continuously variable-frequency energy-encrypted WPT system using the LCC-compensated transmitter and the concept of static variable capacitors has been proposed, which can continuously encrypt and decrypt the wireless energy [J5]. Furthermore, a novel multiple-frequency multiple-power WPT system has been proposed, which can utilize one single transmitter embedded underground to simultaneously energize multi-standard receivers in various EVs [J6]. Concerning the analysis of the proposed system, we have newly analyzed three multilayer rectangular coil structures for multiple-frequency multiple-receiver WPT, hence identifying that the uneven compound coil can provide more uniform magnetic flux density distribution [C2], [J2]. Then, the mutual inductance between the transmitter and receiver coils of the energy-encrypted WPT system is analytically derived, hence optimizing the harvested wireless power with fewer fluctuations by selecting an appropriate transmitter compensated capacitance [C4]. Concerning the control of the proposed system, a novel 2-D chaotic frequency-and-duration encryption scheme has been proposed, which can generate a well-defended security key to improve the security performance for roadway-charging EVs [C1], [J3], [J5]. Then, a new soft-switching pulse-frequency modulation has been developed, which can guarantee full-range soft-switching operation, hence offering high efficiency, controllability, selectivity, and security for energy-encrypted WPT [J7]. Moreover, a novel magnetic quasi-resonant coupling scheme has been proposed to realize the concept of energy-on-demand WPT, which can nominate the authorized receiver to take over the initiative and generate a well-defended security key [J8]. Meanwhile, a new low-frequency-switching phase-shift control scheme has been developed for high-frequency-resonating WPT, which can effectively reduce the current fluctuations and switching losses [C5].

17204317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17204317.value: The project has been focused on developing the converter topologies, encryption algorithms and modulation schemes for energy-encrypted wireless power transfer (WPT). For the sake of simplicity, the realization of the whole system has assumed that the transmitter embedded underground and the receivers installed in mobile EVs have good communication so that there is no synchronization problem between the transmitter and receivers. Once there is a loss of synchronism, the receivers will not be able to decrypt the wireless energy even they fully know the security key. This is one of the areas that needs further development for the proposed energy-encrypted WPT system. Another important area that needs further development is the continuously variable-frequency energy-encrypted WPT system. The use of static variable capacitors to realize online tunable capacitance has been preliminarily investigated in this project, which is very promising to provide continuously time-varying resonant frequencies for energy encryption with high security. Currently, it relies on using a bridge converter and a LC tank to realize the static variable capacitor, which is relatively complicated for practical high-power application. Thus, it is highly desirable though challenging to develop a new static variable capacitor with minimum hardware count and high power handling capability.

17204317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17204317.value: There are two fundamental problems of electric vehicles (EVs) that limit their popularization – short driving range and high initial cost. Instead of establishing more charging stations and developing faster chargers to alleviate the problems, EVs can harness wireless power from electromagnetic field in air and then charge their batteries when running on the road. This roadway-powered EV technology can fundamentally solve their problems of short driving range due to limited battery storage or high initial cost due to the use of many batteries. The project has successfully developed a novel energy-encrypted wireless power transfer system for roadway-powered EVs. The key is that the transmitter buried beneath the road wirelessly transfers the energy which is encrypted by a security key (technically, the operating frequency and its duration are programmed to vary with a chaotic sequence) so that the receivers of those authorized EVs which know the security key can decrypt the energy by tuning their resonant frequency accordingly. Without knowledge of the security key, the unauthorized EVs cannot extract the encrypted energy because of the nature of high impedance under frequency mismatch. In conclusion, the proposed energy-encrypted wireless power transfer system exhibits excellent technical performances and high commercial values.

17204517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17204517.value: 自從過去十年來，柔性電子產品出現了令人矚目的進展。有機半導體在柔性電子器件的製造中的獨特性質，如其靈活性，可拉伸性和透明度，已經導致了許多成功的新穎應用。與單個設備相比，結合生物信息的空間變化的多個傳感器對於診斷是非常有實用價值的。因此，我們提出開發一種與加熱器相結合的新型大面積溫度傳感器陣列，用於消融手術和臨床熱療。所提出的保形裝置特別適用於治療難以進行射頻消融的器官表面的小規模腫瘤。除了外科應用外，所提出的超適形傳感器和加熱器也可以應用於表皮，以進行肌肉疼痛或關節炎的非侵入性熱療。施加到所提出的裝置上的每個加熱器的功率將由集成的溫度傳感器陣列反饋控制。將通過使用3D熱傳遞模型來模擬具有不同尺寸和相應熱傳播路徑。該項目的成功不僅是實現生物醫學應用中革命性傳感器技術的重要一步，也為香港的公共衛生提供立即和廣泛的影響。

17204517.label: Realisation of objectives
17204517.value: Objective 1 Objective achieved. We have developed two types of medical catheter integrated with a conformal temperature sensor and ablator. The first one is based on resistive temperature heater fabricated from silver thin film. The heater has a resistance value between 330 ohm to 630 ohm, depends on the length of the heating element. The heaters can achieve around 133 oC, which is enough for the ablation purpose. The second heater we have utilized is IR laser type connected to the optical fiber. The fiber was inserted into the medical catheter which has temperature sensors outside, as a result, one can monitor the level of ablation by real time monitoring the temperature increases of the tissues. For the temperature sensor part, we used thin metal traces with 5 nm Cr/50 nm Au, and have a width between 20 and 40 μm. This temperature sensor is patterned by photolithography in the geometry of Archimedean spiral pattern with interconnects for external wiring. The whole device is deposited on a 1.5 μm thin layer of parylene and encapsulated by another 500 nm parylene. The TCR is given by dR/dT=R where R, T, and αR are the resistance, temperature, and temperature coefficient of resistance of the metallic element, respectively. The spatial resolution of the device in temperature sensing is 4 mm, which is the same as the diameter of the device. The sensitivities of the devices are found to be ranging between 5.69 Ω K-1 and 18.5 Ω K-1. The variation of the TCR in the whole operating temperature range is within 5%. For the conformal study of the device, we have explored the adhesion energy between the device and the organ (gamma). gamma=B/(2R^2) where B is the bending stiffness of the substrate and R is the bending radius. It can be noticed that a thickness of substrate down to less than 10 um can easily satisfy a bending radius of 0.5 um. Based on this governing equation for the conformality requirement, we have developed a new fabrication recipe to deposit metal electrodes onto the medical catheter directly. The catheter were slowly dipped into and withdrawn from NLOF 2020 negative photoresist at about 800 μms-1. Due to capillary effect, photoresist will be drawn into the capillary tube. Kim wipes were used to slowly absorb out the photoresist from the tube. After prebaking at 110 ◦C for 1 minute, the samples were aligned and exposed under 365 nmUV light for a dosage of 66 mJcm-2 followed by post exposure baking at 110 ◦C for 1 minute. Resist pattern was developed in 2.38 wt% TMAH for 30 -40 seconds. 50 nm of gold (Au) was deposited by thermal evaporation using 5 nm chromium (Cr) as an adhesion layer. The photoresist sacrificial layer together with the metals on top were lift-off by 80 ◦C DMSO. The samples were then immersed into an adhesion promoter (0.5% volume ratio 3 (Trimethoxysilyl)-propyl methacrylate (C10H20O5Si) in 1:1 mixture of DI water and IPA) for 20 minutes. For the ablation test, we utilized the conformal heater to perform thermal ablation continuously for 5 minutes. The collapse of the cell walls on the heated zone can be clearly observed. For the heater with the length and width of 15 mm and 7 mm, the effective area is around 28 mm x 13 mm which is around 2 times of the heater characteristic lengths. Other than the lateral heat spreading, the heat also penetrates into the liver from the surface for around 8 mm. The penetration depth can be further increased by increasing the ablation time and input power. The correlation between the penetration depth as a function of bias conditions will be one of the focuses of the upcoming work. One may also notice that after the tissues have been damaged by the thermal ablation, there would be winkle patterns on the surface of the liver. As the ablation heater is highly conformal, it can provide can continue heating without inducing air gab between the heaters and liver. Based on these experimental results, the following work of the ablation heater would be applying them onto different organs under different heating power, and measure the ablation effect of the organs under test. For the laser ablation process, it is achieved by the high energy, coherent and monochromatic infrared laser light source to induce localized heating on the tissues. As the light can transmit over a long distance in glass fiber with little energy loss, it can be integrated with the endoscope for minimally invasive surgery applications. When laser light is pointed to the biological tissue, scattering and absorption will occur, and the laser-induced thermal therapy (LITT) actually involves the study of radiative transport considering the absorption and scattering coefficient of tissues. Usually, the biological tissues are considered as turbid media, and the effective transport scattering coefficient is much larger than the absorption coefficient. For the near-infrared radiation utilized here, the penetration depth can reach around 10 mm. Studies had also shown that a higher temperature would facilitate light attenuation and local heat generation. The fiber we used is a 200 μm diameter glass fiber, and it was about 0.5 mm exceeding the tip of the capillary tube. The laser wavelength is near infrared at 1064 nm and the power supply was set at 2W. Objective 2 Objective achieved. Firstly, we have modelled the heat propagation in the liver by both theoretical solution based on semi-infinite object, and 3D finite element model (EFM). For the first scenario, the width of the heater needs to be comparable with the liver so that the heat can propagate one dimensional into to liver without being affected by the boundary conditions at the end side of the liver. By solving the standard 1D heat transfer equation with a heat source at the boundary (heater), the temperature of the kidney at different region of the heater can be expressed theoretically. By comparing the temperature obtained by the analytical solution and the experimentally measured temperature, we can obtain the thermal diffusivity of the liver to be 1.51  10-7 m2/s, and the thermal conductivity of the liver is 0.53 W/m-K. Based on these fitting values, a more detailed 3D heat transfer model is under development to simulate the heat transfer paths in the liver by using a more precise ablation heater with smaller size. Secondly, the commercial software COMSOL Multiphysics was used to validate the extracted thermal properties and determine temperature profile in the organ during heating. The boundary conditions were set to be constant heat flux between the heater and organ. The heat flux is set by the power delivered to the heater as well as the optical fiber. The other boundary conditions were set to be undergone natural convection with coefficient h = 0.5 Wm-2K-1. From the simulation results, we obtained the heater temperature under a 600mW input can be close to 100 oC in 30 seconds which is sufficient for the ablation. Similarly for the laser ablation, the heating up to 100 oC just need around 8 seconds. It implies both heaters are good enough for the ablation. By comparing the simulation result and the experimental results, we can obtain the thermal properties required to characterize the heat propagation in the organ.

17204517.label: Major findings and research outcome
17204517.value: In this project, we have successfully developed a conformal metal heater which can serve as a temperature sensor and at the same time a thermistor for ablation purpose. We have optimized the structures of the metal thin film such that it can provide sufficient heating power to damage the cells through thermal energy. Based on the porcine liver we used for demonstration, a penetration depth of 2-3 mm is observed under a 50 C heating. The device demonstrates its potential for the cancer treatment. Besides the electrical power ablation, we further integrated the temperature sensor onto the catheter surface for in-situ IR laser ablation. The demonstration of the devices on ultrathin 1.5 um parylene and medical catheter provides valuable information in integrating the conformal biomedical sensors onto medical apparatus. Based on the thermal information obtained from the conformal sensor, we developed an analytical solution for a semi-infinite heat propagation model. By comparing the measured temperature distribution, we have evaluated the thermal diffusivity and thermal conductivity of the porcine liver. Our device can be utilized as a thermal property extraction tools for the organs or tissues. From the temperature profile of the conformal 2D temperature sensors, we noticed an even heat spreading in the organs. However, when the heat propagation is close to the arteries, the heat dissipation due to blood flow must need to be considered. 17204517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17204517.value: The potential for the further development of the project would be applying the device onto more different types of organs or even animals. The applications on different organs such as heart, brain and etc would allow us to develop a database of thermal diffusivity and conductivity, which is extremely useful for us to choose the thermal ablation power. Another direction that worth for the further study would be down tune the heating power to generate thermal stimulations instead of ablation. The correlation between the thermal stimulation and the body response such as electrophysiological signal would be an interesting direction for further investigations.

17204517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17204517.value: Each year more than 25 million of human life are taken away by the cancers. Although the treatment approaches have been improved a lot, they are still have quite a lot of limitations for example the resection type open surgery is always dangers for elderly patients. While chemotherapy or radiotherapy also have different side effects on the normal organs or tissues. The proposed conformal heater/temperature sensor for the ablation process provides a new path to treat cancers in a small localized scale. The proposed device for conformal thermal ablation is a medical tool that can bring minimally invasive surgery to a higher level of clinical application. The proposed structure facilitate immediate information to the clinician about the ablation process This ablation device is an important cornerstone for the development of the next generation of conformal bioelectronics. Further developments in conformal sensors and heaters mean that they can be integrated with other new technologies to perform drug delivery or provide other in-vivo medical treatment.

17204617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17204617.value: 在故障發生後正確判斷故障的類型，是確保繼電器在適當的保護方案下進行動作的關鍵步驟。雖然一系列基於提取故障後穩態階段特征的傳統故障分類法已被採用多年，但是這類方法表現出以下缺陷：首先，對於安裝在每條電纜上的繼電器，都需要進行閾值的預標定；其次，由於故障形式複雜多樣（例如，不同故障地點、短路電阻等），預標定的閾值在某些狀態下可能無法達到而導致故障分類錯誤；再次，因為故障分類在故障后的穩態時刻中進行，繼電器的動作實際上已經發生延誤。最後，因為傳統穩態故障分類法需要同時測量電纜電壓和電流，現場佈線變得複雜。近來，雖有一系列基於暫態特征的故障分類法，但這類方法仍然需要將每條電纜的繼電器實施預標定。並且，這類方法可能受到電磁干擾產生誤動作，或者本身無法識別三相短路故障。 該項目旨在開發一種基於配電電纜磁場測量以檢測電流中的衰減直流分量的故障分類法。當電纜發生短路故障時，故障相發生較大的電流變化，而由於電力系統網絡的構成高度感性（系統存在大量發電機、變壓器等）， 電流電感中的電流在短路瞬間不能突變，因而出現衰減的直流分量。基於直流分量的故障分類法將有效解決上述問題：（1）由於衰減的直流分量只在故障時出現，因此本方法可以正確的識別故障相和非故障相；（2）無需預標定；（3）電磁干擾（高頻）並不會影響直流分量的特征。與此同時，我們將發明從電纜周圍測量磁場以提取三相中可能存在的直流分量的算法。我們將在實驗室驗構建一個平台雛形以驗證該方法的可行性，並且和我們的工業搭檔合作以在現場環境下進一步驗證方法的有效性。 作為一個更有效的故障分類法，該方法的貢獻包括確保繼電器動作的有效性，提高配電系統自我修復能力以促進智能電網的實現，節省在繼電器安裝和校準的人力資源投入， 控制故障的不利影響以促進智能城市的發展等。我們團隊由學界和業界人員構成，研究經驗豐富：例如，在從磁場中提取和分析電力訊號這一領域投入超過八年。因此，我們有能力接受這項研究挑戰并將該項成果付諸現實。

17204617.label: Realisation of objectives
17204617.value: Objective 1: We have developed a robust algorithm for extracting three-phase DC component from the magnetic fields around the multi-core distribution power cable. The algorithms were studied and established for reconstructing the phase currents from the magnetic sensing, and further extracting the DC components as follows: (i) Current reconstruction: we have successfully completed work on reconstructing the phase currents of overhead transmission lines from the sensor on the ground. We continued to use this program to reconstruct the phase currents of power distribution cables. (ii) DC component extraction: the task is to further extract the potential DC components from the reconstructed currents of power distribution cables. The problem is that the traditional Fourier transform or the wavelet transform cannot be used because they would result in distortion at the front and back ends of the waveform (i.e., the fringe effects). Thus, we have developed a new method based on mathematical morphology to achieve the DC component extraction. This method was successfully validated based on different functions with decaying component. Objective 2: Regarding fault classification in simulation, we have established a virtual power distribution network in the simulation to validate the feasibility of our proposed method. Different fault currents were attained based on four different short-circuit faults (i.e., phase-to-ground short-circuit fault, phase-to-phase short-circuit fault, phase-phase-to-ground short-circuit fault, and three-phase short-circuit fault). The method was validated to extract the DC-components based on the reconstructed currents from the magnetic sensing. Objective 3: Platform has been established for conducting fault classification on multi-core distribution power cables. The magnetic field distribution around a power distribution cable is totally different from that of overhead transmission lines. Thus, we have studied the magnetic field distribution around a power distribution cable under different operating currents. After attaining these results, we have the knowledge of how to install our magnetic sensors, and what linear range should the sensors have. We have established a real-time measurement platform, and tested the function of magnetic-field measurement and current reconstruction both in the lab and power substation. Objective 4: The feasibility of DC-component-based fault classification was validated by experiment. We established a scaled power distribution network in the lab, and generated different fault currents. First, the three-phase currents are reconstructed by magnetic sensing with a stochastic optimization algorithm, which avoids the waveform distortion in the measurement by current transformers that incurred by the dc bias. Then, the dc component is extracted by mathematical morphology (MM) in phase currents to identify the fault type together with the polarity of dc components. This method was verified successfully for various fault types on a 22-kV power distribution cable in simulation and also a scaled power distribution network experimentally. The proposed method can enhance the reliability of the power distribution network and contribute to smart grid development. The fault category was successfully identified by our method.

17204617.label: Major findings and research outcome
17204617.value: There are two major findings and research outcomes. A new fault-classification technique by detecting decaying dc components in fault currents with magnetic sensing was proposed and verified. The dc component was extracted by the MM method from the current reconstructed by magnetic sensing. The feasibility of the method was validated both by simulation and experiment. This method does not require precalibration in terms of network, does not suffer the dc bias issue as in CTs [47], is invulnerable to EMI, and can reliably identify three-phase short-circuit faults. The impacts of this method are summarized as follows. First, the reliability of fault classification in distribution networks can be enhanced for ensuring the proper function of relays and facilitating the repair work. Second, the workforce of the precalibration process for installing relays on each underground power cable can be eliminated, and thus the power system can be more cost-effective. Last but not the least, this work can facilitate the smart grid construction by improving the self-healing ability in distribution systems and boost the smart city development by safeguarding the continuity of power supply. This finding and outcome have been published in K. Zhu, Philip W. T. Pong, “Fault Classification of Power Distribution Cables by Detecting Decaying DC Components with Magnetic Sensing”, IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement, vol. 69, 2016 (2020) which is also reported in Part C of this project completion report. A current-measurement technique for power distribution cables with magnetic sensing and computational intelligence is proposed in this paper. This technique can successfully measure the DC offset in fault currents, which can then be used to identify the phase-to-ground fault and faulty phase. The deployment of DC component for fault identification is advantageous: firstly, the serviceman does not need to set a threshold for each individual power distribution cable. Secondly, the DC component is free from the effect of electromagnetic coupling or EMI. The current-measurement technique based on magnetic-field sensing also enables the double-ended current method to locate the fault since it can be implemented with magnetic sensors at a low cost to both ends of a cable. The implementing procedure of this technique to identify and locate faults is presented for guiding its usage in practical scenarios. This finding and outcome have been published in K. Zhu, K. H. Lam, Philip W. T. Pong, “Identification and Location for Phase-to-Ground Fault with Magnetic Sensing in Power Distribution Network: Principle and Practical Implementation”, IEEE Power and Energy Society Asia-Pacific Power and Energy Engineering Conference (APPEEC), Macau, 2019, Paper No. 1570574301 and K. Zhu, Philip W. T. Pong, “Curved Trapezoidal Magnetic Flux Concentrator Design for Current Measurement of Multi-Core Power Cable with Magnetic Sensing”, IEEE Transactions on Magnetics, vol. 55, 4001809 (2019) which are also reported in Part C of this project completion report.

17204717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17204717.value: Over the last decade, with the increasing interest in robot-assisted minimally invasive surgery (MIS), a number of surgical systems such as concentric tube robots, STIFF-FLOP, and multi-backbone tendon-driven robots are proposed. MIS is less invasive compared with traditional open procedures and leads to reduced hospitalization time for patients. However, the manual performance of MIS is non-trivial due to the intrinsic difficult-to-access sites, and the requirement of high dexterity surgical tools such as for vascular surgery, cardiac surgery, and otolaryngology. As a result, robot-assisted MIS has always attractive in the successful deployment of the procedure. One of the innovations in robotics research is the emergence of tendon-driven mechanisms that has remarkable potential for surgical operations like single port access laparoscopy (SPAL) and natural orifice trans-luminal endoscopic surgery (NOTES). Surgical robotic systems with miniaturized flexible tendon-driven serpentine manipulators (TSM) have attracted increasing attention among surgeons and researchers for their capability of working in constrained and torturous human lumen, i.e., oral cavity and upper GI tract. However, they suffer from nonlinearities and model uncertainties due to high order dynamics, friction, varying tension, and other challenges in tendon-driven mechanical design. Traditional model-based control is often not able to overcome the challenges in performing surgical operations. The objective of this project is therefore to develop a methodology to perform real-time automatic control of serpentine manipulators in order to alleviate surgeon fatigue and enhance the quality of surgical task performance in a kinematics free and sensor free circumstances. A data-driven approach for motion planning and control is proposed based on the notion of learning from demonstration (LfD) that utilizes statistical machine learning models to encode system underlying dynamics and generalize smooth motor trajectories by direct actuation space learning. Motion segmentation is adopted with soft margin Support Vector Machine (soft-SVM) in tackling complicated tasks. The research also aims to retrieve task-specific properties by Locally Weighted Regression (LWR). We evaluate the approach on two surgical related tasks, namely, compliant insertion and simplified Endoscopic Sub-mucosal Dissection (ESD) with a prototype two-segment TSM robot. Also, we will identify and collect several benchmark surgical movements from surgeons, i.e., cutting, targeting, and segment such movements into motion primitives, then LfD is used to encode these primitives with parametric models. The learned models will be stored in a human robot interaction (HRI) library which can be used and adjusted by surgeons to automate part of the surgical interventions. 研究項目利用數據統計學習模型（Learning from Demonstration 或 LfD）的概念來建構一個智能控制方案來有效控制蛇形外科手術機械人。

17204717.value: For achievement of objectives 3, 4 and 5, design and implementation of the prototype serpentine robot with soft structure driven by cables for experimentation was completed. Evaluation of the proposed control method is undertaken with bench-marking case studies of driving the robot to various defined trajectories. Trajectories tracking experiments are performed to verify the learned inverse kinematics of the presented system with different predefined trajectories in 3D Cartesian space. Based on the concept of learning from demonstration (LfD), benchmark surgical movements are transferred to the experimental system which forms the DMPs of the HRI library.
