17205717.label: Major findings and research outcome
17205717.value: (a) The systematic experiments show that the small strain constrained modulus of sands depends on void ratio, effective confining stress and grading (fines content). At a given confining stress, the constrained modulus corrected for void ratio tends to decrease in an approximately linear manner with increasing the coefficient of uniformity (Cu). For the same test materials, the small strain shear modulus values have been measured and similar findings have been obtained. Based on regression analysis of the experimental data, a new formula has been proposed which can be used to predict the constrained modulus as affected by void ratio, confining stress and grading. A new formula has also been proposed for predicting the shear modulus as affected by these factors. In the framework of CSSM, a unified characterization of the state-dependent moduli is developed for more rational constitutive modeling. (b) The dependency of constrained modulus on confining stress is different from the dependency of shear modulus on confining stress and this difference can be characterized by the stress exponent. This finding suggests that the assumption widely used in current research and practice that they have the same stress exponent is conceptually inappropriate. Also, the decreasing rate of constrained modulus differs from that of shear modulus. The constrained modulus appears to be more significantly affected by grading than the shear modulus. The effect of grading on the modulus reduction curve and the damping ratio curve appears to be minor. (c) The constrained modulus is associated with the compression wave while the shear modulus is associated with the shear wave. Wave signals under various conditions have been recorded in the experiments. The characteristics of wave signals (including frequency content and dispersion property) are affected by confining stress, void ratio, and particle properties. The Rayleigh law of scattering generally holds. Experimental evidence has been obtained showing that the propagation of compression wave in saturated sand specimens is differing from that in dry sand specimens, and this difference is attributed to the influence of pore water. In real situations the condition of saturation can therefore influence the vertical ground response. Numerical modeling has been conducted for site response under 1D, 2D and 3D earthquake motions and further research needs are identified.

17205717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17205717.value: The difference in the state dependency of constrained modulus and shear modulus and its impact on constitutive modeling of soil behavior deserve further investigation, both experimentally and theoretically. Effort to model wave propagation in granular materials (both compression wave and shear wave) using the discrete element method to develop fundamental understanding should also be continued. Several more papers on research findings are expected to be published in future.

17205717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17205717.value: Earthquakes remain one of the most destructive natural hazards to our built and social environment. The Wenchuan earthquake of 12 May 2008 in the province of Sichuan, China caused more than 69,000 deaths and economic losses in excess of US$100 billion. Research with the aim of reducing the potential hazard caused by earthquakes is a matter of national interest. This project was aimed to develop a better understanding of the characteristics of constrained and shear moduli of granular soils through specifically designed experiments in conjunction with numerical analysis and modeling. The research has produced new datasets and insights that are useful for clarification of the existing uncertainties in relation to the state dependency of constrained and shear moduli and to the earthquake ground response analysis. It has also suggested several research needs in future. The outcome of the project can contribute to the development of more rational engineering designs against earthquake hazard.

17205817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17205817.value: There is growing interest in R&D works on developing single-phase power converters (rectifiers and inverters) with small, non-electrolytic capacitors in their dc-links, for domestic and commercial applications. Such “small-dc-link single-phase power converters” possess the advantages of being more long-lasting, and allow a more compact design of the capacitor bank, especially at medium and high power ratings. Active power decoupling (APD) is a well-proven technique that can effectively reduce the energy storage requirement of single-phase converters. Small dc-link single-phase power converters are achievable via modifying and integrating conventional single-phase converters with APD function. Nevertheless, this concept of “small-dc-link single-phase power converters” presents two new challenges. (i) Existing APD-based single-phase converters generally require the addition of many passive, active, gate driving, and sensing components, which substantially increase the overall system’s cost, volume, and possibly power losses. There are attempts to reduce the power component count of the converter through the principle of component sharing. Still, the achieved solutions are unacceptable for many space- and cost-stringent applications. Meanwhile, there is no reported work aimed at reducing sensor’s requirement. To attain truly cost-effective and high-power-density small-dc-link single-phase converters, further investigations are required to explore new topologies and control techniques that are either sensor-less or use fewest sensors. (ii) Applications of small capacitors “destabilizes” the dc-link. A small-dc-link single-phase converter is inherently more susceptible to disturbance and more difficult to control. Currently, most studies are focused on ideal (disturbance-free) and steady-state (constant load) operations. With real grids, the line voltage contains rich content of background harmonics, undergo sudden voltage sags/swells, and can be peak-clipped. Many applications also present time-varying power profiles, and require fast and precise power control. For instance, in grid-connected PV inverter applications, maximum-power-point-tracking control is performed in real time, corresponding to changing solar irradiance, ambient temperature, shading condition, etc. There is no reported research work on such issues for these converters, and related investigations are important. With increasing penetrations of LED lightings, renewable sources, and electric vehicles, where reliability is of utmost concern, billions of small-dc-link single-phase power converters will be required. Investigation into advanced topologies and control of APD-based single-phase power converters will be useful. Successful completion of this project will lead to greater interests in and wider use of such converters. The outcomes will be an enrichment of the theory of power electronics (new single-phase power converters, dynamic control methods, and sensor-less control techniques), and practical results verifying their potential for applications. 近年來，一類新型單相交直流電力變換器（包括整流器和逆變器）逐漸成為民用和商用的研發工作熱點。這類單相交直流電力變換器使用了非常小的非電解電容作為其直流母線電容。這類“微直流母線電容單相交直流電力變換器”有著諸多優點，例如，它們的使用壽命更加耐久，而且，尤其在中、高功率的應用場合，它們的直流母線電容的體積可以大幅度的減小。主動功率解耦技術是一種已被理論證實的、可有效降低單相交直流變換器直流母線儲能要求的技術。通過應用和集成這類主動功率解耦技術於現有的單相交直流變換器中，我們便可以得到全新的“微直流母線電容單相交直流電力變換器”。儘管通過主動功率解耦減小直流母線電容的理論已為人熟知，真正實現“微直流母線電容單相交直流電力變換器”的這一新的概念仍舊面臨著兩大全新挑戰： （i）現有的基於功率解耦技術的微直流母線電容單相交直流電力變換器通常需要在傳統的單相交直流變換器的基礎上增加許多被動元器件，主動元器件，門驅動電路，和許多傳感器。這些額外增加的元器件極大的增加了整機系統的成本，體積，還可能增加系統的功率損耗。過去，通過“元器件集成”這一概念，很多研究人員努力嘗試並成功降低了功率器件數目。然而，這些研究結果仍然無法被應用於很多對體積和成本有嚴格要求的場合。為了真正實現高性價比，高功率密度的“微直流母線電容單相交直流電力變換器”，我們需要研發新的電路拓撲結構，以及研發新的無需或僅需少量傳感器的控制技術。 （ii）基於微直流母線電容的單相交直流電力變換器很容易令其直流母線電壓不穩定。這是因為相較於傳統的單相交直流電力變換器，“微直流母線電容單相交直流電力變換器”本身更易受到外界干擾，而且其係統控制難度更高。目前，多數的研究集中在了理想（無外界干擾）和穩態（例如：負載恆定不變）的場合。在真實的電力系統應用中，電網電壓往往含有較高的高頻諧波成分，其電壓可能會忽然升高、降低，而且其峰值還會被強行箝制在一定的電壓等級。另外在許多的應用場合中，負載功率往往是隨著時間變化的，而且要求電力變換裝置能夠迅速而準確的提供電力至負載側。例如，在並網太陽能逆變器應用中，我們便經常需要根據太陽的輻射強度，環境溫度，陰影情況等因素的變化，對逆變器進行實時的“最大功率追踪”控制。目前，還沒有研究對“微直流母線電容單相交直流電力變換器”的暫態以及穩定性等問題進行深入的研究。因此，進行相關的研究非常的重要。 隨著LED照明，新能源，以及電動汽車的廣泛普及（這些應用對單相交直流變換器的可靠性，功率密度等有極高的要求），我們將需要數以萬計的“微直流母線電容單相交直流電力變換器”。對其拓撲和控制方面的研究將有實際的意義。成功的完成這一項目，將會令社會各界對這一類新交直流電力變換器產生廣泛興趣並帶來廣泛的使用。該項目的研究成果將會進一步的完善電力電子理論（全新的單相交直流電力電子變換器，動態控制方法，和無傳感器控制技術）。該項目的實際測試結果將會進一步證實這類新型單相交直流變換器的應用前景。

17205817.label: Realisation of objectives
17205817.value: With reference to objective 1, our target was to derive new types of small-dc-link single-phase power converters. In our preliminary attempt, we manage to developed a component-minimized and low-voltage-stress single-phase power factor correction rectifier without electrolytic capacitor. The component minimization is achieved by embedding an active pulsating-power-buffering (PPB) function within each switching period, such that typical add-on power electronic circuits for PPB are no longer needed. Additionally, with a three-level flying-capacitor configuration, the voltage stresses of switching devices can be reduced more than 50% as compared to existing solutions that are based on embedded PPB. The relationship between the inductance requirement and the patterns of the modulation carriers, and how it can be utilized to minimize the magnetics of the rectifier, is also discussed. A 110 W hardware prototype is designed and tested to demonstrate the feasibilities of the proposed rectifier. An input power factor of more than 0.97, peak efficiency of 95.1%, and an output voltage ripple of less than 4.3% across a wide load range have been experimentally obtained. This work has been published as "A single-phase three-level flying capacitor PFC rectifier without electrolytic capacitors," IEEE Transactions on Power Electronics, vol. 34, no. 7, pp. 6411–6424, Jul. 2019." Active pulsating power buffering (PPB) function can effectively reduce the twice-line frequency energy storage requirement in a single-phase rectifier. Existing single-phase solutions with active PPB must utilize more than two active switches in their circuits. Compared with conventional single-active-switch solutions without active PPB, the cost of additional semiconductor switches and gate drive circuitry in an active PPB-based rectifier may not be justified for low-power applications. Therefore, in our subsequent attempt, we developed a family of single-switch single phase rectifier with active PPB. Taking advantage of the ON-time and OFF-time of a single switch, the proposed rectifiers are formulated by merging two converters that are duty and frequency controlled. The steady-state characteristics of these converters are analyzed. A step-by-step design procedure is provided, and an active control method for limiting the maximum switching frequency for wide-load-range operation is presented. A 100-W prototype is built for the demonstration of the proposed single-switch rectifier concept. It is envisaged that this concept, when combined with other circuit formulation techniques, e.g., partial power processing, dc-voltage feedback, may lead to new derivatives of single-switch rectifiers with more advanced features. This work has been published as "Minimum active switch requirements for single-phase PFC rectifiers without electrolytic capacitors,” IEEE Transactions on Power Electronics, vol. 34, no. 6, pp. 5524–5536, Jun. 2019. Subsequently, along the line of this research on active PPB, we have also proposed a single-phase three-level flying-capacitor PFC rectifier with PPB-embedded switching. Here, the flying capacitor not only clamps the voltage stresses of all power devices but also functions as a PPB capacitor. The proposed rectifier is shown to achieve nearly 50% reduction of the voltage stresses, 72% reduction of the buffering capacitor’s volume, and 23.8% reduction of the magnetic core size, as compared to a state-of-the-art two-level solution recently proposed. This new approach of formulating single phase PFC rectifiers with active PPB could dramatically boost the system’s efficiency and power density whilst reducing cost. This work is published as “High-power-density single-phase three level flying-capacitor buck PFC rectifier,” IEEE Transactions on Power Electronics, vol. 34, no. 11, pp. 10833–10844, Nov. 2019." With reference to objective 2, a nonlinear controller is presented for regulating an emerging class of high power density, high power conversion efficiency, and high reliability (H3) single-phase power converters featuring small buffering capacitors. The proposed controller combines the best features of input–output feedback linearization and an automatic-power-decoupling (APD) control strategy, and achieves enhanced dynamic performances as compared to existing solutions based on linear control techniques. By feedback linearization, the plant models of H3 single-phase converters are fully linearized and decoupled, and thus fast dynamics, large-signal asymptotic tracking, and global stability can be achieved with simple linear controllers. Additionally, the APD strategy further strengthens the robustness of the closed-loop system as active pulsating power buffering (of the instantaneous power difference between the ac-port and the dc-port of the converter) of basically any form can be achieved. With the proposed nonlinear controller, we are able to further exploit the potential and unlock several new features intrinsic in H3 single-phase converters, e.g., active voltage holdup function, allowing extended holdup time (comparable to existing products with large dc-link capacitors) with only a small energy storage. The general theory, design procedures, and practical considerations of the nonlinear controller are detailed. A 100-W hardware prototype is also built to demonstrate the advantages of the proposed solution. New opportunities of H3 single-phase power converters with the aid of the proposed nonlinear control are are important for our development of the sensorless control techniques for the proposed converters. This work has been published as "On nonlinear control of single-phase converters with active power decoupling function," IEEE Transactions on Power Electronics, vol. 34, no. 6, pp. 5903–5915, Jun. 2019. Additionally, a voltage sensorless controller is developed for a two-switch single-phase rectifier that involves power factor correction and active pulsating power buffering without electrolytic capacitors. While a two-switch rectifier normally requires four sensed signals for control, only one current sensor is required in this proposal, thereby offering advantages such as low cost, high compactness, isolation between control and power circuits, and improved reliability. While the basic operating principle follows that of a conventional voltage sensorless controller for single switch converters, several critical design considerations are the key to the success of the implementation which is explained in detail in the published paper, "Design considerations for voltage sensorless control of a PFC single-phase rectifier without electrolytic capacitors,” IEEE Transactions on Industrial Electronics, vol. 67, no. 3, pp. 1878–1889, Mar. 2020. Furthermore, as single-phase power converters with the active pulsating-power-buffering (PPB) function are essentially highly coupled and nonlinear systems, advanced control techniques are needed for this emerging class of converters to achieve fast transient response and large-signal stability. Existing control solutions are based on either 1) linear control techniques that are operating-point specific or 2) nonlinear control techniques that are generally topology-dependent. Our proposed work is an evolved generalized feedback-linearization (FBL) control approach that incorporates the direct Lyapunov control method. The proposed control provides good stabilization of the internal dynamics of the system (which is unviable with FBL control) while still retaining all the best features of FBL control. We have shown that FBL control naturally destabilizes the system and that the proposed control can globally stabilize the system under various operating conditions while yielding fast dynamics, see our published paper “Internal dynamics stabilization of single-phase power converters with Lyapunov-based automatic-power-decoupling control,” IEEE Transactions on Power Electronics, vol. 35, no. 2, pp. 2160–2169, Feb. 2020. Finally, as the new type of converter generally requires more sensors than converters without a PPB due to the additional PPB circuitry, which may compromises the power density, reliability, and cost of the overall system, in our research, an algebraic-estimation-based method is proposed to solve this high-sensor-count problem. Specifically, a general theory of employing algebraic observers to reduce the number of sensors is developed. The work is published on “Sensor count reduction for single-phase converters with an active power buffer using algebraic observers,” IEEE Transactions on Industrial Electronics, vol. 68, no. 11, Nov. 2021.

17205817.label: Major findings and research outcome
17205817.value: In this research, the active PPB technique is further explored. Four PFC circuits without E-caps are proposed, and a complementary voltage sensorless control method are is also proposed for these circuits. The contributions are summarized as follow: 1. Proposed a single-phase AC/DC converter without additional active switches and. I its control method is also proposed. Its The achievable efficiency of the circuit are is even improved higher than that achievable as compared with the H-bridge converter in some operation range. 2. Proposed a two-switch single-phase buck-boost PFC rectifier as well as its closed- loop control method. This rectifier can achieve good PFC, output voltage regulation and active PPB, all in a single stage. 3. Proposed a single-phase three-level flying-capacitor buck-boost PFC rectifier and its control method. The flying capacitor serves two dual purposes of clamping the voltage stresses of all power devices and operating as a PPB capacitor. By virtue of the three-level configuration, the voltage stress and the inductance requirement are also reduced significantly. 4. Proposed a single-phase three-level flying-capacitor buck PFC rectifier and its control method. The proposed solution is found to have lower voltage and current stresses, reduced magnetic and capacitive footprints, as well as a unity power factor (PF) and a lower total harmonic distortion (THD), as compared to those of a conventional buck PFC converter. 5. Proposed a voltage sensorless control method for a type of active PPB-based single-phase rectifier featuring only one inductor (applicable for the rectifiers in contributions 2, 3, and 4). Three voltage sensors together with their associated isolated power supplies are saved from the circuit with this control.

17205817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17205817.value: As shown, it is possible to realize a buck-boost type PFC rectifier with three-level flying-capacitor and that for a buck type PFC converter using a modified three-level flying-capacitor configuration. So far, the same concept has not been successfully applied to a boost PFC rectifier. Nevertheless, it will be interesting to explore if this concept might still be viable for a boost PFC rectifier by employing a modified flying-capacitor switching cell. In the future, this concept might be extended to multi-level (>3) flying-capacitor converters to further reduce the inductance and capacitance requirements. These research works are open for the future. The key idea of using the flying capacitor in three-level converter for PPB might be extended to other type of multi-level converters such as the neutral point clamped (NPC) and cascaded H-bridge (CHB).

17205817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17205817.value: Adoption of bulky electrolytic capacitors (E-caps) is a crucial obstacle for single-phase power-factor-correction (PFC) rectifiers toward high power density and high reliability. Active pulsating-power-buffering (PPB) is an effective technique to reduce the energy storage requirement, leading to thereby eliminating the usage of E-caps. Existing active PPB solutions, however, generally suffer from some issues or limitations, such as e.g. (i) extra power electronics are required to form PPB active filter; (ii) high voltage stresses for semiconductors and (iii) limited output dc voltage range. These issues or limitations inevitably lead to an increased system cost, degraded energy efficiency, and limited application.

17206717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17206717.value: The construction industry has over an extended period consistently been berated for its under-performance, and criticised for perceived high costs, slow delivery, unsafe working practices and a failure to innovate. Much of this criticism is commonly attributed to the highly fragmented delivery structure used in the industry, where a myriad of loosely coupled organisations frequently deliver to lowest cost agendas. Over the past decade there has been a growing belief in the power of digital technologies in overcoming many of these problems. In particular, the package of digital technologies commonly known as ‘Building Information Modelling’ is increasingly portrayed as a specific solution that could be applied to address the many perceived performance failings of the industry. There is currently great optimism in policy circles that BIM will facilitate the integration of the design, construction and operation of built assets to achieve whole-life value. Consequently, several countries already have, or are in the process of putting in place, BIM mandates for public sector construction projects. These mandates differ in breadth and scope in terms of segments of the public sector and size of projects, but they have in common that they attempt to enforce the adoption of BIM through procurement processes. In other words, participating firms need to ‘do’ BIM and be ‘BIM compliant’. However, not all firms have the same possibility to become BIM compliant. Indeed, compliance requires firms having the necessary capacity for uptake, as well as operating in a business environment where it is considered favourable and necessary to do so. So far, the size of the firm has shown to be a significant determinant of engagement with BIM, with small to medium sized enterprises (SMEs) falling well behind their larger counterparts in terms of uptake. This is significant in terms of the Hong Kong construction industry as 97% of the firms have less than 50 employees. Hence, the aim of this research project is to critically explore the impact of BIM mandates on small and medium sized enterprises (SMEs), and the resistance that the introduction of BIM might face within these types of firms. The particular focus is on exploring the extent to which SMEs are able and willing to mobilise the resources necessary to become BIM compliant, and identify the barriers they face in this transition. 建造業長期以來一直被指為表現欠佳，批評其成本高昂、交貨緩慢、作業方式不安全，同時行業墨守成規、欠缺創新的作風亦為人詬病。而形成問題的主因往往歸根於業界種種鬆散耦合的組織體系以最低成本去完成工程。於過去十年間，業界逐漸認為可以憑藉著科技的力量去解決這些問題；而其中通常被稱為「建築信息模擬」(BIM) 的技術更普遍被視為可用於根治業內大部份困境的一門出路。現時決策者都抱持樂觀的態度，認為BIM將促進設計、建設和營運一體化，從而實現建築資產的全周期價值。因此，若干國家已經或正在制定政策指定於公共建設項目必須採用BIM。儘管有關的應用於項目的大小或範疇上有所不同，但總體而言各項目均嘗試於採購過程中加強採用BIM。換句話說，參與項目的公司皆需要使用BIM並符合其標準。然而，並不是所有公司都有對等的能力去符合相關標準。事實上若要達成標準，公司需要有一定的實力，而且需要一個有利的營商環境以表現出來。目前公司的規模已經成為應用BIM與否的重要因素，而中小型企業 (SMEs) 在這方面則遠遠落後於行內其他規模較大的業者。由於香港的建造業中有九成七的公司僱員不足五十人，這一論點對本地業界更突顯其重要性。因此，本研究旨在探討如強制採用BIM對中小型企業的影響，以及於這類型企業中引入BIM所可能面對的阻力。其焦點將特別集中探討中小型企業為符合採用BIM的規格，所能夠及願意調動必要資源的程度，並辨識出他們在這一轉型中所要面對的各種障礙。

17206717.label: Realisation of objectives
17206717.value: When putting together research proposals investigators are asked to be novel and take risks. This is also what I did when conceptualising and putting together this proposal. The idea in itself was rather simple – to investigate the effect a new government mandate enforcing the use of BIM on public sector projects would have on contracting SMEs. This was to be achieved by using the theoretical framework of the ‘digital divide’. Both of these two main premises turned out to be very problematic. In terms of the mandate, this came into effect as of 1 Jan 2018. One would have expected that given the threshold of HKD30million there would have been a significant number of projects that would have been affected. This turned out not to be the case. Looking at the official statistics of the Architectural Services Department, who are responsible for most of the ‘buildings’ projects, they awarded 17, 17 and 22 projects respectively for the period 2018-2020. For the projects in 2018 these had been tendered for before the mandate kicked in and did therefore not contain a BIM component. What this meant for the research project was that the mandate was not having much of an effect on the overall construction market in terms of volume and there was therefore not much to study. In terms of the theoretical framework this was originally developed to explain the behaviour of individuals within different populations. At the time of writing the proposal there was a small but growing literature set that was applying the theoretical constructs in the organisational/business environment and it was this that we aimed to build upon and develop. This turned out to be problematic. At a general (superficial level) the framework works fine and it is easy to make arguments around ‘material access’, ‘motivational access’ and ‘usage access’, e.g. how SMEs do not have the resources to invest in hardware and software and how employees might not be motivated to change their working behaviour. The problem we encountered when we started operationalising the constructs in terms of collecting data was that it was originally developed to deal with what can be considered ‘fixed’ technologies. It turned out to be much less useful in investigating how a technology such as BIM, which is a combination of software and hardware, is adopted as it is anything but a ‘fixed stable technology’. This provided us with a real dilemma, as we could not see a way forward using this particular theoretical framework. For objective 1, we conducted formal interviews with staff from a number of SMEs and we also held numerous informal conversations with SME representatives. The very clear message coming out of these interviews/discussions was that the mandate was not really on their radar, many were not even aware of it. For those who were, there was still great uncertainty in terms of what the mandate actually entailed and what, if anything, it would mean for their firms. In order to look into the latter, we tried our best to get hold of tender documents and awarded contracts. Our, as it turned out, very naïve belief was that this would fall under a freedom of information act, or the ‘Code on Access to Information’ as it is called in Hong Kong, as would be the case in many other countries. We were sorely mistaken. It has, throughout the research project, turned out to be as good as impossible for us to get any kind of information on the details of gazetted and awarded projects despite repeated requests. We did in the end, via personal contacts, get hold of the tender documents for 4 projects and what they showed us was that there was little synchronisation between them when it came to what was asked for in terms of BIM. When tracking the changes in the mandate over time it is clear that those responsible have attempted to rectify this somewhat by adding more detail, but from our interviews and informal conversations what we have learnt is that the mandate is not seen as onerous and that the biggest affect it has had on the market is the creation of a BIM consultant niche, rather than construction firms investing heavily in their in-house BIM capabilities. This leads us on to objective 2 and the main barriers for SMEs when it comes to becoming BIM compliant. Significant for how the research progressed was that the rather obvious answer to this question is that there is no need for them to be BIM compliant. If looking at the Hong Kong BIM mandate it has very little, if any effect, on the main contractor’s supply chain and as such does not affect the work of SMEs (this is something we investigate/discuss in the two papers that are currently under review). Hence, there are no client requirements pushing SMEs to invest in BIM. As an aside, this finding was later replicated in the CIC BIM adoption survey in 2020 (CIC, 2021), where it was concluded that the overwhelming majority of SMEs were ‘BIM laggers’ and that the main reasons for this was “The lack of client requirement[s] and the absence of government policy”. Acting on realisation that the main barrier, in simple terms, was that there was no need for SMEs to invest in developing their BIM capabilities we took the decision to refocus our research to look more closely at the government’s BIM policies. This decision was not taken lightly, but it was made easier due to what was happening in society at the time. The ‘civil unrest’ and the shut-down of society due to covid made it impossible for us to conduct empirical research on projects and in firms. There is also an underlying problematic with conducting qualitative organisational research in Hong Kong as there is an inherent resistance among both public and private sector firms in researching what can be seen as ‘weaknesses’. Hence, we refocused objective three to instead of looking at responses within firms and actions that could potentially be taken to facilitate the development of BIM compliance within the individual SME firms, we targeted the mix of policy instruments developed and implemented by the government and its agents to increase BIM use in the industry. We, therefore, conducted a comprehensive archival analysis of the development of BIM policy over time (complemented with whatever other data we could get hold of in terms of interviews, attending events of different kinds and informal discussions). We sought to identify all the different policy instruments that were deployed, when and what effect they had on the organisations that were supposed to enact/enforce them. The end result is that we can point to issues that might actually incentivise (or force) a greater uptake of BIM in the industry (we will leave to others to decide whether or not this is necessarily always a good thing). In summary, the project as it was conceptualised was initiated too early and it was significantly adversely affected by external events from 2019 and onwards. We asked for a 6-month extension, but in reality it would have been better with a 3 year extension, as that time frame would have given us very different empirical opportunities.

17206717.label: Major findings and research outcome
17206717.value: The BIM mandate has so far had very little effect on the working practices of SMEs. At present the majority of the SMEs have very little reason to invest in BIM technologies and in the subsequent training of staff. Those who have invested in BIM, cannot be argued to have done so on the basis of becoming BIM compliant or seeking to get public sector contracts. Hence, that the majority of SMEs are BIM adoption laggers (see CIC (2021) for an estimated percentage) this is at the moment best explained by that they have no real need to invest in BIM. That they would face difficulties in doing so thus becomes a secondary explanation. As far as our research shows, the key effect that the HK BIM mandate has had is the emergence of a BIM consultant market. It is noteworthy that the ‘BIM consultant’ label did not exist in the national business classifications prior to June 2019. These individuals and firms take on a significant role in enabling the project team to deliver on their commitments under the mandate. What this leads to, however, is that the involved firms do not necessarily develop their in-house BIM capabilities. This might be fine in terms of the client getting their as-built digital model at the end of the project, but it does very little to change the construction process and the institutionalised practices of the project suppliers. Our findings point to the need for starting at the client side if progress is to be made in achieving a greater adoption of BIM technologies (and the various permutations). We have shown in the two journal papers that the mandate in and by itself is not a very effective policy instrument. This is of course not lost on those involved and a variety of other policy instruments have been deployed, but not in as a synchronised manner as what is possible. A key issue that we have not been able to get around in this research is that whilst most in the industry would agree that adopting BIM is a good thing, there is very little agreement on what BIM is. This is by no means a new insight, but it will continue to dog any study on BIM adoption/uptake and it will continue to also disrupt the adoption of BIM in industry, making the term BIM compliant very vague indeed.

17206717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17206717.value: There are a couple of research streams that are worth pursuing going forward: First, there are now a number of ongoing projects that have been initiated under the BIM mandate. This allows for project specific studies investigating whether or not the BIM mandate has any effect on the supply chain. There are clear signs of an emerging BIM consultant market with at least 40 companies currently active in Hong Kong. Further study of the role these consultants take on projects is worth pursuing, i.e. what role they play in the forming of the mandated ‘BIM team’ on the project. Of particular interest is to what extent hiring such consultants allows for the contractors to not develop their own in-house BIM capabilities. Finally, as we argue in our submitted journal papers a mandate is only one in a mix of policy instruments. So far, the HK government has not been successful in terms of achieving the sought after BIM uptake in industry and the question becomes if other policy instruments than the mandate are more likely to be successful in doing so.

17206717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17206717.value: The Hong Kong construction industry has long been criticised for its under-performance in terms of high costs, slow delivery, unsafe working practices and failure to innovate. Over the past decade the idea that the increased use of technology, in particular what has become known as Building Information Modelling (BIM), can be effectively used to overcome many of the problems the industry faces has grown in strength. The adoption of BIM, it is believed, would help transform the construction industry. This research project took as its starting point that ~97% of the roughly 24000 firms active in the construction industry are small to medium sized enterprises (SMEs) commonly employing 1-10 staff. They, therefore, face considerable difficulties in investing in new technology, both in terms of hardware and software and in training of staff. Our findings show that regardless of all believed positive effects of adopting BIM, the uptake of the technology remains low amongst SMEs, which effectively limits the positive impact of the technology on construction projects. We see this as a policy failure and suggest a shift in focus from coercion in the form of mandates to incentives in the form of policies that encourage SMEs to adopt BIM.

17207117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17207117.value: To process the rapidly increasing amount of data, more and more software applications run within a datacenter containing massive computing resources. To harness these resources, applications are typically run by either of two independent infrastructures: schedulers and virtual machines (VM). Unfortunately, as an application runs on more computers, computer errors will occur more likely at runtime and can shut down the entire application, causing disasters such as the 2015 New York trading halts and recent Facebook outages. Existing infrastructures lack a high availability support for applications. This GAIA project takes a holistic methodology to greatly improve application availability via three objectives. First, we will create APUS, a fast distributed consensus protocol for general applications. Distributed consensus, a strong fault-tolerance theory, runs multiple replications of the same application and makes these replications behave consistently as long as a majority of them work normally. An open challenge is that traditional consensus protocols are slow because their protocol messages go through various software layers (e.g., OS kernels). APUS will introduce a new consensus algorithm with an ultra-fast OS kernel bypassing technique called Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA). Preliminary results presented in [SOSP '15] show that APUS supports unmodified real-world applications, and its latest development is 32.3X to 85.8X faster than traditional consensus protocols. Second, we will construct a first scheduler for application availability by integrating APUS with popular schedulers. A main challenge is that existing schedulers’ resource allocation schemes can be conflicting with replication schemes, because the former schemes abstract away computer identity, but the latter schemes must deploy replications on different computers. Our scheduler introduces a replication-aware resource allocation scheme to resolve conflicts efficiently. Our prototype scheduler presented in [APSys '16] incurs only 3.22% performance overhead on popular key-value applications. Third, we will build a new VM for application availability by integrating APUS with popular VMs. One performance problem in existing VM fault-tolerance techniques is that they need to transfer all memory modified by applications across VM replications. Our new VM integrates APUS into the hypervisor layer to enforce same application inputs across VM replications, then VM replications maintain mostly same memory. We also propose a new algorithm to efficiently track and transfer minor different memory. This GAIA project will greatly strengthen the reliability of many real-world applications and will benefit almost all computer users and software vendors, including many HK financial platforms. GAIA will also advance broad reliability techniques (e.g., VM migration) and infrastructures. 为了获取更多的计算资源来处理越来越多的数据，越来越多的软件应用正运行在数据中心里。为了充分利用数据中心里的计算资源，软件应用主要运行在两种主要的数据中心的容器里：虚拟机和调度器。很不幸的是，随着一个应用运行在越来越多的计算机硬件中（例如CPU），计算机硬件错误发生的概率也会变得越来越大，甚至会使得整个应用下线、停止对数据中心外部的服务请求。比如说，2015年纽约证交所的整体下线，就是由于其数据中心的硬件错误造成。现有的数据中心容器缺乏对软件应用提供高容错服务的功能。 本GAIA项目旨在利用一个全面、彻底的方法，通过实现三个研究目标，极大地提高运行在数据中心里的应用的容错能力。首先，我们会创建APUS，一个快速的、通用的分布式一致性协议。分布式一致性，是一个强大的分布式容错理论：它运行一个应用的多个版本在不同的物理计算机（备份）上，然后使这个应用的行为在不同的计算机上高度一致，只需要过半数的备份工作正常并且协商一致即可。目前已有的分布式一致性协议的一个主要问题就是他们协商的延迟太大，因为协商的网络消息需要经过很多软件层（例如操作系统内核）。APUS将会利用RDMA，一种快速绕开内核的硬件技术，来构建一个新型的快速分布式一致性协议。我们的初步结果已经发表在SOSP 2015国际会议上，显示我们的APUS协议可以支持多种现实世界的应用程序、而不需要修改他们的源代码，而APUS的近期研发成果已经比传统的基于TCP/UDP的分布式一致性协议，快了32倍到85倍。 第二个研究目标：我们将会构建一个新型的调度容器，来提高通用程序的可靠性。我们通过把APUS集成到已有的调度容器来实现此目标。该目标的一个主要研究挑战，就是已有的调度器的资源分配策略和APUS的冗余容错策略会有冲突，因为亦有的调度策略是把物理计算机的标识给虚化的、去掉的，而冗余策略需要把同一个应用或者计算任务，分配在不同的物理计算机之上。我们将会创建一个新型的“冗余可知的资源分配策略”，来很高效地协调资源调度和冗余调度的问题。我们的初步调度器原型发表在了APSys 2016国际会议上，显示我们的新型调度器只有3.22%的性能延迟，几乎和一个应用不使用调度器的原始性能一样快。 第三个研究目标：我们将会构建一个新型的、为通用应用提供容错的虚拟机。我们将通过把APUS和已有的虚拟机平台相整合来达到目标。已有的虚拟机容错技术存在一个重大的性能问题：它们需要传输过多的脏内存来往于各个虚拟机备份之间。我们的新型虚拟机将会通过APUS来使得各个虚拟机之间的的外部客户端输入及其顺序高度一致，这样就可以使得各个虚拟机备份之间的脏内存内容，绝大部分都相同，这样就可以极大地减少内存的传输量，提高虚拟机及其运行的应用的性能。我们还提出一个新算法来告诉地比较和传输内存。 本GAIA计划，将极大地提高数据中心中的应用软件的可靠性，由此可以使得几乎所有的计算机用户和软件公司都获益，包括香港的很多金融应用平台。GAIA还将会促进一系列其他软件可靠性技术的进步。

17207117.value: The research outcomes funded by this GRF grant contains two parts. First, Dr. Cui has developed a series of effective software systems and algorithms on protecting the confidentiality, integrity and privacy of big-data computing. These systems and algorithms are published in a series of international top conferences and journals on computer systems and security, including NSDI, SOSP, ATC, SOCC, TPDS, and TDSC. For instance, Dr. Cui's secure system papers (e.g., [Uranus AsiaCCS 2020] and [DAENet TDSC 2021]) on distributed systems have become a core component of Huawei's Trusted and Intelligent Cloud Services (see the UTEE component in TICS https://www.huaweicloud.com/product/tics.html). Due to this industrial impact case, Dr. Cui received the HKU Faculty Knowledge Exchange (KE) Award in 2022.

17207817.value: 潮灘雖然具有重要的生態學意義，但是面對環境影響卻顯得非常脆弱。 因此，評估潮灘對不同環境影響下生態水力學的響應顯得急切而重要。本項目特別關注半封閉海灣中的潮灘，因為它與海灣內部的環境高度耦合，從而使此類研究更具有挑戰性。本研究首先檢驗海灣內地表水體與地下水體的水動力學耦合過程。然後，分析潮灘在地下水文，營養鹽和鹽度方面對周圍環境變化（海岸線和水下地形，入海徑流和水體質量的變化）的響應。最後，本研究以潮灘內大型底棲動物作為生態學指標，來評估環境變化對潮灘可能帶來的生態學影響。 本項目使用中國香港地區的米埔自然保護區作為案例開展研究。米埔位於一個拉姆塞自然保護區中，為每年超過55，000的候鳥提供重要的覓食場地，其中包括瀕危的物種黑臉琵鷺。然而，在米埔所處的深海灣內，海岸線和水下地形，入海徑流和水體質量等環境因素在近幾十年中經歷了重大的變化。本項目將針對這些環境變化，評估其對潮灘的地下水文，營養鹽和鹽度方面所產生的影響。此外，本項目還將檢驗這些環境影響對潮灘中灘涂內大型底棲動物的生態影響，並試圖找出近幾十年內潮灘地區海水鹽度下降和大型底棲動物生態多樣性下降這兩個現象的主要原因。 本項目將在米埔的潮灘區域開展地下潛流和鹽度的連續觀測。同時，在灘塗地區建立三維地下水模型來模擬地下水流和鹽度的遷移運動過程。一個已開發的海灣水動力數值模型將為此研究中的地下水模型提供邊界條件。然後，設計情景實驗來分系地下水文，營養鹽和鹽度對周圍環境變化的響應。最後，本研究將根據泥灘大型底棲動物的生態學參數（生物量，丰度和多樣性）與環境影響因子（水體質量和地下水鹽度）之間的關係來建立一個統計學生態模型，用以模擬和評價環境變化對大型底棲生物所產生的可能影響。本研究將從多種來源（例如：已發表文獻資料和政府部門）收集數據，並與本項目實地採集的數據相結合來開發和驗證地下水模型和生態模型。為了選擇對大型底棲生物影響最密切的環境因子來建立生態統計學模型，大型底棲動物的生態學參數將與所有可獲取的觀測數據和海灣數值模型提供的水動力學模擬數據進行相關性分析。 總之，本項目的結果將對半封閉海灣內潮灘的保護工作提供實際有效的指導作用，提高我們對灘涂的科學認知，尤其在灘涂地區地表水與地下水交互耦合和大型底棲生物在時間尺度上隨環境因子演進的研究方面。本項目中所開發的生態學模型在使用其他地區的本地數據進行訓練後便可以直接進行實地應用。該模型也允許進行更深入的擴展，以在地表水和地下水方面納入更多可能的環境變化條件，進而用來評估這些新的環境變化對灘涂的地下水環境和生態系統所產生的生態水文影響。

17207817.label: Realisation of objectives
17207817.value: This project has three major objectives, all of which have been successfully achieved. 1. Objective 1 Objective 1 aims to examine the coupling of the surface hydrodynamics to the subsurface hydrology of tidal marshes in semi-enclosed bays. The existing methods were first reviewed, and several challenges were identified. Field methods combined with statistical analysis and numerical modeling were then identified as potential solutions. The first challenge is related to the field method selection. Natural geo-chemical tracers such as radon and radium have recently been used to analyse the relationship between tidal variation and groundwater hydrology in tidal marshes. However, these studies did not consider differences in the concentrations of the tracers in the different soil zones of the aquifer. Moreover, these studies required additional surface water information based on mass balance models. In addition, through lack of automated monitoring methods and because of the large number of samples required for radium measurements, these studies were often conducted over the short term (e.g., several days or weeks). There were studies that have used the recorded piezometric head and salinity data to investigate the relationship between tidal and groundwater hydrology in conventional coastal aquifer without vegetation coverage. These studies showed that monitoring of piezometric head and salinity can reveal the relationship between tide and groundwater, which may also be applicable in aquifers of tidal marshes. In addition, compared to method applying natural geo-chemical tracers, direct monitoring the piezometric head and salinity of groundwater allows long-term investigation into different parts of the coastal aquifer of tidal marshes, especially the top 1 m of tidal marsh soils, which is enriched with carbon, nitrogen, and other nutrients. The second challenge is due to the complex topography, soil types, and the interactions of groundwater with fauna and flora in coastal wetlands. To fully understand the quantitative relationships between surface hydrodynamics and groundwater hydrology, sampling locations involving different soil zones and topographic types were selected in a mangrove swamp in a semi-enclosed bay. The temporal fluctuations of the piezometric head and salinity of groundwater were monitored. Tidal signals were then extracted from high-resolution time-series groundwater data using a Bayesian statistics modeling method-based code (Baytap08). Different time lags between tidal elevation fluctuations and the fluctuations of the piezometric head and salinity were detected. This project also applied a groundwater model, SUTRA, to simulate the groundwater dynamics (i.e., piezometric head and salinity) with tidal variations as boundary condition. The modeling results were validated with the observations of the field data, confirming the relationship between tide and groundwater determined in the statistical analysis. In summary, this project identified the relationship between coastal surface water (i.e., tide) and groundwater of tidal marshes at different soil zones and topographic types. Therefore, objective 1 was successfully addressed. 2. Objective 2 Research objective 2 aims to analyse the hydrological and salinity responses of tidal marshes to changes in the surrounding environment. Through literature review, the major environmental factors that could possibly affect the hydrodynamic responses of tidal marshes were first selected. Numerical modeling was also identified as the potential solution to address this objective. The existing studies were first reviewed to determine the environmental factors of interest. Although wind plays a key role in governing estuarine circulation in bays, few studies have evaluated its ecohydrological effects on tidal marshes and the interactions of its effects with those of anthropogenic activities such as land reclamation. Besides, like many rivers around the world, the Pearl River has in recent years experienced more frequent and more severe flow variations. It was hypothesized that Pearl River flow variation with land reclamation would affect the environment surrounding the tidal marsh. This project then built a three-dimensional coastal numerical models to simulate the water and salt transport processes in the vicinity of the tidal marsh in a semi-enclosed bay under various scenarios. The coastal numerical model was developed with the Environment Fluid Dynamic Code, which is widely used in solving hydrological and environmental problems at hundreds of surface water bodies. This code is also robust in simulating the wetting and drying of intertidal areas, which can ensure accurate simulations of intertidal mudflats in the vicinity of the tidal marsh in the semi-enclosed bay. The built model was calibrated and validated with observed hydrodynamic data. Finally, scenario experiments with numerical models were then designed to evaluate how the tidal marsh in the bay would respond to land reclamation, different wind regime change and different levels of Pearl River flow variation and assess the potential environmental impacts. Different coastline shapes were digitalized in different land reclamation phases. This project applied the Sverdrup, Munk, and Bretschneider model that was coupled with the Environmental Fluid Dynamic Code model to calculate the wind-induced wave. The Pearl River flow scenarios were generated based on the multi-decadal annual flow records. In summary, through numerical modeling, this project quantified the hydrodynamic changes caused by the combined action under land reclamation and wind regime change or river discharge variation at the tidal marsh in a semi-enclosed bay. Thus, objective 2 was successfully addressed. 3. Objective 3 Research objective 3 aims to evaluate the possible response of macrobenthic infauna in intertidal mudflats through a statistical ecological model. Macrobenthic infauna biomass was selected as an ideal ecological indicator to represent the health status and productivity of the tidal marsh because of its sedentary lifestyle in the tidal marsh and sensitive nature to surrounding environment. To assess the ecological responses to changes in environmental condition, model outputs of the built coastal numerical model such as surface water hydrodynamic, water quality and meteorological variables were used as inputs in developing the statistical ecological model. The developed ecological model is capable of predicting the benthic infauna biomass dynamics in response to future environmental changes, facilitating the assessment of ecosystem service of tidal marshes. Governing environmental factors derived from the coastal numerical model in benthic infauna biomass dynamics were first identified using Kendall rank correlation analysis. Then, Pearson correlation was performed for the selected high-impact variables to identify linearly correlated environmental variables. These linearly correlated variables were removed in the following Bayesian regression model development to avoid multicollinearity. Different Bayesian regression models were generated using the selected environmental variables and compared for performance. The Bayesian model with best performance in depicting and predicting benthic infauna biomass variations was finally determined. In summary, this research identified the governing environmental factors in benthic infauna biomass dynamics using correlation analysis, simulated the temporal dynamics of benthic infauna biomass with a Bayesian regression model based on time-varying environmental variables selected from correlation analysis, and investigated the ecological impact of reclamation and wind Regime changes with the ecological model. The insights generated from this study can be beneficial for better management and conservation of the ecological environment of coastal regions. Therefore, objective 3 was successfully addressed.

17207817.label: Major findings and research outcome
17207817.value: This research project focuses on assessing the hydrodynamic and ecological responses of tidal marshes within semi-enclosed bays to the environmental changes. As listed in Part C, this research project has generated four peer-reviewed research articles in leading international journals and two conference publications. This project has trained two PhD students. The major findings and outcome are discussed as follows. Long-term groundwater monitoring data were obtained, and the relationships between surface water hydrodynamics and subsurface hydrology were quantitatively evaluated, which is presented in (journal paper #3). The results revealed that the groundwater fluctuations were highly dependent on tidal variations. The results also suggest that the topography of the tidal marsh and the properties of the soil zones together affect the hydrodynamic responses of the groundwater to surface water hydrological variations. In addition, a three-dimensional groundwater model was built to simulate the hydrodynamic responses of coastal aquifer to tidal variations in a tidal marsh in a semi-enclosed bay, the application of which was presented in conference publication #2. A series of three-dimensional coastal surface water models were built in this research project. The horizontal simulation domain of these models covered the entire Pearl River Estuary region and some adjacent sea areas. The model simulation results of water and solute transport all showed good agreement with the field observations. The models have been used to examine the hydrodynamic responses of tidal marshes to various environmental changes. This includes examination of effects from land reclamation and wind regime variation (journal paper #1) and examination of effects from land reclamation and river discharge changes (journal paper #4). A statistical ecological model relating the macrobenthic biomass to the most relevant environmental factors derived from the outputs of coastal surface water models was also developed in this research project, which is presented in journal paper #2 and conference publication #1. Key factors that influence the macrobenthic infauna biomass were identified, and combination of key factors with best performance in evaluating the possible response and the temporal evolution of the macrobenthos under scenarios with different surface water properties was determined. In general, this project generated practical insights that are beneficial to the conservation of tidal marshes within semi-enclosed bays. It also improved our scientific understanding of tidal marshes, particularly those involving the coupling of groundwater–surface water interactions and the temporal evolution of macrobenthic infauna.

17207817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17207817.value: This research project generated a set of coastal numerical models with practical insights including surface water models and groundwater model. The scenario simulation results of surface water models that evaluate the effects of land reclamation, wind regime changes, and Pearl River flow changes in the coastal three-dimensional model could be used as inputs to other coastal studies, which may produce more meaningful findings. For example, the model results under combined effects from land reclamation and wind regime variations were used as inputs in the macrobenthic infauna study. In addition, the modeling results of the coastal numerical models can also be applied to coastal aquifer studies because the boundary conditions required for groundwater models are often hard to obtain, especially when historical records are unavailable. Similarly, the built groundwater model can also be used to generate results that could be useful for surface water studies (e.g., effects from submarine groundwater discharge on coastal nutrient circulation) and coastal wetland studies (e.g., interactions between coastal groundwater and vegetation). This project also developed a framework for generating a statistical ecological model to reflect the health and productivity of tidal marshes. The framework has implications for similar tidal marshes worldwide.

17207817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17207817.value: Tidal marshes are of critical environmental and ecological importance. However, they are at risk of severe degradation worldwide due to negligence and mismanagement. Better understanding is therefore required to guide management and conservation. This research project focuses on assessing the potential eco-hydrological disturbance of tidal marshes by human activities and nature. Relationships between surface water and groundwater in tidal marshes with complex topography and soil properties were revealed through statistical analysis. A set of numerical models were also built to investigate the temporal variations of water flow and salt transport of tidal marshes under different settings of human and natural effects. The results of the numerical models were used to develop a statistical ecological model that simulates the variation of macrobenthic infauna biomass with hydrological changes. As macrobenthic infauna biomass is an ideal indicator of ecosystem health and productivity, the developed statistical model can facilitate the management of tidal marshes. In summary, this project improved the scientific understanding of the subsurface hydrology and its coupling with the surface hydrodynamics of tidal marshes. The results are also beneficial to the management and conservation of many tidal marshes within semi-enclosed bays worldwide.

17208817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17208817.value: During the 1980-90's, the main problem for analytical (including theoretical) studies in power grids was the then new phenomenon of voltage collapse after numerous major system collapses at transmission network level around the world. These related largely to larger (electrical) distances between generation and load and increasing system stress. There followed a large research output in related areas of load modelling, both static and dynamic, new stability concepts, systems analysis, basic theory, collapse proximity indicators, security enhancement and emergency control all focussed on voltages. Some continuing work in this line notwithstanding, new issues can now be identified which demand a fresh look at voltage stability problems. Future electrical power systems will feature high penetration of renewable power at all voltage levels, energy storage and new loads, possibly with demand response mechanisms, as well as continuing growth in interconnections and stress levels, all of which makes power systems voltage behaviour more complex. A recent high voltage (transmission level) blackout in Australia (28 September 2016) and the more familiar voltage rise issue on low voltage (distribution level) feeders show a range of new voltage issues across the whole system related to renewable power. Traditional stability analysis in power systems has not kept up with these changes and has some deficiencies that will prevent it from doing so as the new features accelerate. For example, the analysis tools should be able to give rapid assessment of stability limits and their sensitivities to a large number of changes under greater uncertainty. The research project will be based on a complete revision of the dynamical models to a network-based framework expressed to include the features of future grids following an earlier GRF project focussed on angle stability. The proposed research aims to establish a new framework for stability analysis in terms of network-based models and new computational methods to give foundations for the improved analysis. We will focus on voltage stability issues as parts of the overall stability problem in power systems. With this basis, techniques for identification of modes of instability and stability sensitivity will be developed. Particular attention will be paid to the impacts that renewable power sources, storage and demand-side control (type, placement and size) placed at all voltage levels will have on stability of the system. 上世紀八十到九十年代，輸電網在多重嚴重故障後產生的新現象—電壓崩潰現象逐漸成為電力系統工程和理論研究的主要問題。該現像在很大程度上與電源負荷之間的電氣距離太遠以及系統重載有著密切的聯繫。沿著這一思路，對於電壓崩潰的研究得到了廣泛重視，並在諸如：動靜態負荷建模、新穩定性概念、系統分析方法、基礎理論、電壓崩潰臨界指標、電壓安全優化以及緊急控制等相關領域取得了大量成果。現在一些研究人員仍在沿用這一傳統思路。然而電力系統中呈現出的諸多新問題都亟待開發新的研究方法。 未來的電力系統將具有諸多新特性，例如：可再生能源在各電壓等級電網中的高滲透率、新型儲能設備和負荷、具有需求側響應能力以及不斷增長的互聯規模和負荷量。在這些新特性的共同作用下，未來的電力系統將具有更加複雜的電壓特性，並且將面臨一系列與可再生能源有關的新問題。例如：2016年9月28日發生在澳大利亞高壓輸電網的停電事故以及世界各地常見的配電網低壓饋線中的電壓升高現像都證明了這些趨勢。 由於自身缺點，傳統的穩定性分析方法沒有考慮電網新特性對電壓穩定性的影響。隨著上述新特性的不斷增加，該方法更將無法適應未來電力系統的新需求。例如，電力系統分析工具需要在運行參數具有較大不確定性的情況下，快速給出穩定極限評估以及穩定極限對參數變化的靈敏度信息，而傳統方法無法達到這一要求。 本研究計劃將沿用我們在針對電力系統功角穩定性研究的GRF項目中所提出的基於網絡科學的分析方法，改進現有的電力系統動態模型，使其能在網路框架下更好的刻畫未來電網的主要特徵。在此基礎上，建立新的穩定性分析框架，設計新的數值計算方法來改善分析效率。 作為電力系統穩定性問題的重要組成部分，我們將在本項目中重點研究電壓穩定性問題，並以此為基礎，研發電壓失穩模式辨識技術以及穩定性靈敏度計算方法。我們將重點研究各個電壓等級電網中的可再生能源、儲能設備、需求側控制（如設備類型、裝設地點、容量等）對電壓穩定性的影響。

17208817.label: Realisation of objectives
17208817.value: SCOPE OF INVESTIGATION The scope is across all the objectives stated in the original proposal. Briefly we aimed to revisit the subject of voltage stability and collapse, which was the main topic in power systems during 1980-90's, to study new aspects including distributed energy resources and a new focus on the role of network structure. The following topics were addressed in the project (with objectives indicated): A. Network-based analysis of voltage stability (Objective 1) There had been no prior work on how system structure as expressed in the network graph influenced voltage stability. Here we followed our earlier work on how structure influenced small and large disturbance angle stability using statistical methods. This work investigated the impact of network structures on small-disturbance voltage stability of power systems in the long-term. A differential-algebraic model was established in terms of network topology characteristics and the aggregate nonlinear recovery load model. We defined the weighted load connectivity (WLC) as an index to indicate the stability of network structures. Then robust stability assessment was used to eliminate the impact of uncertain recovery time of loads. The Monte Carlo method is used to study the relationship between WLC and small-disturbance voltage stability (SDVS) for a broad range of network topologies and parameters. We discover from the simulation results that the network with a larger value of WLC has a stronger ability to maintain SDVS. To further study the impact of renewable energy sources (RESs), we improved the system model by including an inverter-based distributed generator in parallel with each aggregated nonlinear dynamic load. The simulation results of the Hong Kong power grid show that the WLC can still indicate the stability of network structures effectively, and the systems with more stable network structures are less impacted by the penetration of RESs. The proposed WLC appears useful in providing guidance for power network planning and operation. B. State-in-mode analysis of the power flow Jacobian for static voltage stability (Objective 3) In static voltage stability analysis, participation factors have been used as an index that measures the contribution of the critical mode of power flow Jacobian in the system states. However, this index as usually defined is in a mode-in-state manner that cannot adequately reflect the impact of system states on voltage collapse. In this project, we take a new state-in- mode viewpoint to study the power flow Jacobian. We express the critical mode into a weighted sum of system states, which gives rise to the definitions of state-in-mode participation factor (SIMPF) and state-in-mode sensitivity (SIMS). The SIMPF measures the contribution of a system state to the critical mode, and the SIMS measures the control sensitivity of the system state to the critical mode. The proposed SIMPF and SIMS apply to both node states and network states including active/reactive power injections and active power flows across lines. They provide new insights into the mechanism of saddle-node bifurcation and limit-induced bifurcation, two most common types of voltage instability, by revealing the role of system states. The SIMPF and SIMS can also guide the system dispatch for voltage stability enhancement. C. Static voltage stability analysis of distribution systems based on network-load admittance ratio (Objective 3) It is well known that a single (constant power) load infinite-bus system reaches a static voltage stability limit point, or equivalently, a singularity point of the power flow Jacobian, at the unity line-load admittance ratio, i.e., the equivalent admittance of the load has the same modulus as the transmission line admittance. In this project, we rigorously extend this result to generic distribution systems with distributed generators (DGs). We introduce a new concept called the network-load admittance ratio that is in terms of the parameters of power network, loads, andDGs. This concept is a generalization of the line-load admittance ratio that characterizes the loading status of a distribution system with the effects of DGs included.We prove that the power flow Jacobian is singular if and only if the network-load admittance ratio is unity, which provides new insights into the mechanism of voltage stability. In addition, we establish a new voltage stability index by using the network-load admittance ratio. Numerical simulations on several IEEE test systems show that the index has good linearity with load increase and estimates voltage stability margin with high precision. The index also reflects the impact of DG penetration level and control mode on voltage stability. The obtained results can be extended to ZIP load models, unbalanced three-phase networks, and mesh networks with slight modifications. D. Distribution network reconfiguration for reducing the voltage volatility induced by distributed generation (Objective 4) Volatile voltage profiles in distribution systems caused by the fluctuating nature of renewable distributed generation (DG) are drawing growing concern. In this project, we develop a new formulation of network reconfiguration to mitigate voltage volatility. This formulation provides new insights into the voltage regulation problem with high renewable penetration that is commonly addressed by power electronic controllers. From the linear DistFlow equations, we first propose a novel index that measures the voltage volatility of each bus in the system. This index is a function of distribution network parameters that characterizes the role of network structure in voltage volatility. Then, we formulate a new reconfiguration model that minimizes the network loss and restricts the voltage volatility indices with the coordination of switched capacitor banks. A Benders decomposition-based approach is designed to solve the problem using mixed-integer quadratic programming. The simulations on the IEEE 69-bus system show that the reconfiguration scheme is able to: 1) minimize network loss when DG outputs are as predicted; and 2) significantly reduce the risk of voltage violations when DG outputs deviate from the prediction. The proposed formulation unleashes the distinctive power of network reconfiguration in reducing voltage volatility level, by which the cost of power electronic voltage controllers can be saved. E. Connection between impasse surfaces and voltage collapse in DAE models (Objective 2) In this work we establish a new condition for post-fault trajectory hitting the impasse surface, which reveals how the interactions between power grid and load dynamics induce/prevent short-term voltage collapse. F. Data-based analysis and control of voltage (Objectives 1, 2, 4) This work introduced an alternative data-based approach to addressing the objectives. Based on the knowledge accumulated off-line and feature extractions, novel data-based learning and control methods were proposed for the long-term voltage stability analysis and control problems in this paper. All the spatial-temporal data is considered and the features of different emergency events are extracted by AI methods which can reduce the dimension and reveal the significant internal structure of the data. AI methods were used to build a classifier to reinforce the relationship directly between the system dynamics and stability outcomes and optimal control actions. With the prepared control knowledge, it is faster to find an optimal control action online with a good system performance. Simulation results on the 6-bus system, New England 39-bus system and Iceland 189-bus system are given to show the potential of this method for on-line control. RESULTS ACHIEVED Each of the topics A-F described above has been reported in at least one full journal paper. Each topic was rather broad in nature with followup work possible, so we regard the objectives as fully addressed within the resources available.

17208817.label: Major findings and research outcome
17208817.value: Overall the project has developed a significant approach to using structural features and data-based methods to achieve stability analysis and control, including reconfiguration to deal with renewable power. The work has revived the subject of voltage stability and control to deal with renewable power sources.

17208817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17208817.value: The work for this project addressed all Objectives 1-4 with emphasis on the role of structure in stability, reconfiguration and control and voltage collapse. The topics in current followup work are: - Distributed voltage control in distribution networks - Short-term voltage stability assessment - Theory for impasse surfaces and voltage collapse in DAE models - Theory and algorithms for topology transition Professor Hill has retired from HKU and follow-up work is being supervised by Assistant Prof Yue Song. The topology transition work is very novel with four full papers currently submitted and two appeared.

17208817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17208817.value: The capability of a power network to deliver secure, quality energy for consumers at scale depends on the control of voltages from low levels at street level up to high voltages in the transmission network. The development of definitions and some basic analysis and control tools was a major achievement in the 1990's. But some issues remained incomplete such as the influence of different networks structures and how to efficiently control cascading collapses. Then in the last decade further complexity has arisen with the influence of renewable power at all voltage levels. In brief the real power injected creates a disturbance which causes voltage variations. This project revisits some of the prior unresolved questions and addresses the new issues arising from renewable power.

17209017.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17209017.value: 高速螢光壽命成像技術 - STEP

17209017.label: Project Objectives
17209017.value: Spatiotemporal engineering of STEPS tailored for time-domain FLIM – Harnessing the spatiotemporal encoding nature of STEPS, we will design and optimize the spatial and temporal properties of STEPS respectively, by an interleaved three-dimensional delay-path strategy, with the aim of maximizing the scan rate and the spatial density of scan-spots of time-domain FLIM. Development of the STEPS-FLIM prototype – We will establish the STEPS-FLIM microscope, built upon the knowledge of the desired STEPS specifications, with the optical sectioning capability enabled by either a single-photon confocal or a two-photon implementation. System characterization will be carried out in terms the noise performance and its trade off with the imaging speed. Exploration of the potential applications – We will exploit the STEPS-FLIM prototype for enabling new approaches in high-speed dynamical study of molecular interactions with local microenvironments, especially high-speed FLIM-FRET for visualizing dynamical changes in subcellular organization (e.g. nucleosomal DNA); and real-time in-vivo FLIM for monitoring metabolic changes associated with drug response in the context of bacterial cancer therapy.

17209017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17209017.value: 在現今眾多生物顯微技術中，螢光壽命顯微鏡 (Fluorescence Lifetime Imaging Microscopy (FLIM))具有獨特能力對活細胞內生物分子與其局部微環境的相互作用，作出仔細測量，從而了解細胞內不同功能背後複雜機制，例如蛋白質相互作用和局部酸鹼值變化或氧合反應。但要令FLIM於生命科學研究及醫學診斷中普及，當中需要同時解決三大現時技術上挑戰：高速拍攝率，準確測量螢光壽命，以及具"光學切片"能力。 此研究項目主要目標是，透過採用本研究團隊最近研發的全光學激光掃描技術，開發全新高速螢光壽命成像技術-STEP。STEP能夠以每秒一百至一千萬掃描的速度，讀出每個像素的螢光壽命高速螢光壽命成像技術。此外它具備復用單光子檢測的能力，從而提升測量敏感度，有利於準確測量螢光壽命。更重要是它可用於單光子共焦和雙光子成像 - 即代表具有"光學切片"顯微成像能力。此研究項目亦會開拓以往未能應用到FLIM的範疇，例如高速監測核小體DNA結構變化，以及實時研究腫瘤血管系統對藥物反應相關的代謝變化。

17209017.label: Realisation of objectives
17209017.value: We have successfully designed and established the experimental setup that enabled ultrafast spatiotemporally-encoded pulsed source (STEPS). As proposed in this project, this is essentially a high-speed laser-scanning strategy that could accelerate a number of different optical microscopy modalities and thus open up new opportunities in a wide range of imaging applications. For example, by engineering the spatial and temporal properties of the pulsed source using this technique, we have demonstrated the STEPS prototype that achieved high-speed two-photon fluorescence imaging for recording neural activity in vivo at the record high 2D frame rate, at 3000 fps, and at submicrometer spatial resolution (Nature Methods 2020) . We applied this technology (taking into account the knowledge of the flourescence lifetime of the probes) to ultrafast monitoring of calcium activity, glutamate release and membrane potential, and demonstrated 2PFM imaging of spontaneous and sensory-evoked supra- and subthreshold electrical activity in awake mouse brains in vivo. In this project, we further demonstrated that the STEPS engineering’s application can be extended to light-sheet imaging technology. Using this spatiotemporally-encoding technique, we demonstrated a novel fluorescence imaging approach, called coded light-sheet array microscopy (CLAM), which allows complete parallelized 3D imaging without mechanical scanning (Light: Sci. & App. 2020). We applies this fully parallelized 3D imaging technique to a range of different imaging applications at a volumetric frame rate above 10 vol/s, and with lower risk of photo damage. We also applied the system to perform systematic analysis that correlates the biophysical and biochemical information of cells, and provide new mechanistic insights into biophysical heterogeneities in many biological processes (APL Photonics 2021). Most importantly, we made the imaging protocol and design available to the researchers (Nature Protocols 2021) with the aim to disseminate the imaging technology and thus extend its applications.

17209017.label: Major findings and research outcome
17209017.value: - By engineering the spatial and temporal properties of the pulsed source, we have demonstrated the STEPS prototype that achieved high-speed two-photon fluorescence imaging for recording neural activity in vivo at the record high 2D frame rate, at 3000 fps, and at submicrometer spatial resolution (Nature Methods 2020), e.g. ultrafast monitoring of calcium activity, glutamate release and membrane potential, spontaneous and sensory-evoked supra- and subthreshold electrical activity in awake mouse brains in vivo. - We further demonstrated that STEPS engineering’s application can be extended to light-sheet imaging technology. Using this spatiotemporally-encoding technique, we demonstrated a novel fluorescence imaging approach, called coded light-sheet array microscopy (CLAM), which allows complete parallelized 3D imaging without mechanical scanning (Light: Sci. & App. 2020). We applies this fully parallelized 3D imaging technique to a range of different imaging applications at a volumetric frame rate above 10 vol/s, and with lower risk of photo damage. We also applied the system to perform systematic analysis that correlates the biophysical and biochemical information of cells, and provide new mechanistic insights into biophysical heterogeneities in many biological processes (APL Photonics 2021). Our study provide a new biological insight that suggested an underlying mechanism tightly controlling the change in both cell size and cellular contents such that homeostasis of mass density is achieved in both the nucleus and cytoplasm of cells. Most importantly, we made the imaging protocol and design available to the researchers (Nature Protocols 2021) with the aim to disseminate the technology and thus extend its applications. We provide (i) a comprehensive guide and design specifications for the hardware; (ii) step-by-step optical implementations of the module including the key custom components; and (iii) the overall image acquisition and reconstruction pipeline.

17209017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17209017.value: Built upon this research work, we anticipate that the technology could be further extended to many other applications that require comprehensive image-based profiling of cellular/tissue phenotypes. It could result in a new repertoire of the single-cell library for systematic understanding of the correlations between biophysical and biochemical information of cells/tissue in response to different stimulations or perturbation, e.g., screening of genetically altered cells.

17209017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17209017.value: We have developed a new laser-scanning imaging technology that allows real-time high-speed monitoring of biological dynamics cells. This technology holds the key to dissect the complex mechanisms behind health and diseases - finding its applications in efficient clinical diagnostic as well as drug discovery process.
