17300317.label: Major findings and research outcome
17300317.value: (1) Optimal compression of large quantum ensembles. We identified the smallest amount of memory needed to store a large ensemble of identically prepared quantum systems, proving a form of asymptotic equipartition theorem. We showed that a small amount of quantum memory permits a faithfully storage, which would be impossible with a purely classical memory. [Published in IEEE Transactions on Information Theory] (2) Quantum stopwatch. We designed a device that stores time information in the minimum amount of memory, and can measure the total duration of a sequence of events with quantum enhanced precision [Published in Proceedings of the Royal Society A] (3) Learning quantum states in the presence of noise. We showed how to achieve the ultimate precision limits for the estimation of quantum states, developing a technique to treat the presence of noise that disturbs the estimation. [Published in Communications of Mathematical Physics] (4) Quantum speedup in identifying cause-effect relations. We developed a protocol for determining whether there is a causal relation between two quantum variables, and we demonstrate that quantum entanglement and quantum memories can offer a speedup over classical setups. [Published in Nature Communications] (5) Optimal programming of quantum gates. We solved the long-standing open problem of determining the minimum size of a quantum system needed to specify a desired quantum gate with a given level of accuracy. This problem had remained open for more than 20 years, despite many attempts by various authors. Our work provides the complete solution of the problem, and establishes fundamental relations between quantum programming, quantum learning, and quantum metrology. [Published in Physical Review Letters, Editors' Suggestion] (6) Communication cost of quantum channels. We determined the ultimate limit to the compression of general quantum processes, represented by "quantum channels." Our bound determines the minimum size of a quantum simulator for the dynamics of a general quantum system, and establishes a fundamental relation between this simulation task and the precision limits of quantum metrology. [Published in IEEE Journal of Selected Areas in Information Theory]

17300317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17300317.value: This project opened up several new research directions. One is the use of quantum memories for precision measurements, following the ideas of our "quantum stopwatch" protocol. This research direction includes a combination of techniques from quantum metrology and techniques from quantum Shannon theory, and has applications to the study of sensor networks powered by quantum effects. This research direction is at the basis of an ongoing GRF project 17300918, in which our group is currently involved. Another research direction is the development of quantum algorithms for the compressed simulation of quantum dynamics. This point can be seen as a continuation of Objective 3 of this project: while in the project we explored the Shannon-theoretic limits to the compression of quantum processes, the next step would be to design good heuristic algorithms that can implement such compression on real world quantum devices. We currently working on this problem, and our preliminary results indicate that it is possible to design a quantum machine learning algorithm (technically, a quantum autoencoder) that produces a compact representation of quantum gates acting on high dimensional systems.

17300317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17300317.value: This project explored the ultimate limits to our ability to reliably store information into quantum systems. This question is crucial for the development of quantum communication networks and quantum computers, both of which require a special type of devices known as quantum memories. The problem with quantum memories is that they are a limited and expensive resource, and therefore it is essential to use them in the most efficient way. Our research determined the minimum amount of memory needed to store quantum data, to program, and showed that very small amounts of quantum memory can sometimes offer large advantages. For example, quantum memories can in principle be used to build an ultraprecise stopwatch, to efficiently store programs for quantum computations, and to simulate the dynamics of large physical systems using simulators of exponentially smaller size. Moreover, quantum memories can be used to speed up the discovery of cause-effect relations at the quantum scale, giving rise Our results have the potential to inform the realization of control mechanisms at the ultimate limit of miniaturization, and to extend the ranges of applications of the small quantum simulators available in the near future.

17300417.label: Realisation of objectives
17300417.value: The project aims have only been partially achieved for various serious reasons outside of my control. Firstly, the funding received was only a fraction (~40%) of that requested. This effectively guarantees that only a fraction of the intended project effort could be applied to achieve the intended aims. Secondly, my two RAPs working with me on this project as Co-Is both left before the end of their contracts to return to Australia (1 year early in the case of Dr. Frew and 6 months in the case of Dr. Bojicic, both out of 3 year contracts). This likewise removed 1.5 FTE of important effort from the project at a crucial time. The single PDF left and my restricted effort, given my significant other commitments, inevitably led to much less progress on the project than intended. In attempts to redress the lack of effort I was able to recruit a 2 year MPhil student to dedicate to the project. Indeed for "Aim 2" we have obtained and reduced and analysed a very considerable amount of ESO VLT 8m spectra and imaging data. We were able to win significant amounts of time on the ESO VLT 8m class telescopes in open, peer reviewed competition over 4 years between 2015 and 2018. The 130 Planetary nebulae observed for ~1-1.5hours each amounted to the equivalent of 195 hours or about 18.5 nights of time on the VLT. For an estimate of the financial value of these awards to HKU the ESO VLT is costed at about $100,00USD/night. Hence, our time, shared with our main collaborator at the University of Manchester, was worth ~$1.85million USD or ~$HK14.4million over 4 years. The spectroscopic and narrow-band imaging data is currently being analysed by this excellent MPhil student who started work in late 2020. She has made excellent progress with some important preliminary results obtained and being prepared for publication. In parallel with the ESO VLT reduction and analysis of Bulge PNe the project PI and the remaining PDF has spent considerable efforts over the life of the project improving the robustness and reliability of the Bulge PNe sample. This has involved extensive assessment of the angular sizes, central star detections, morphologies and improved positions and new discoveries for Galactic Bulge PNe, Indeed the key project aims need the most complete and precise Bulge PNe sample possible.

17300417.label: Major findings and research outcome
17300417.value: Despite the severe manpower issues several items of major progress have been made nevertheless. 1. Many more central stars of PN (CSPN) in the Galactic Bulge have been discovered during this study thanks to the quality and high angular resolution of the ESO VLT narrow-band imaging. These provide the basis for future spectroscopic follow up of these CSPN to address aims 2 and 3 in particular and are important discoveries in their own right as prior to our HASH projects <25% of all PNe had unequivocally identified CSPN. 2. Refinement and improvement of the Morphological classifications for many more Bulge PNe have been made thanks to access to the VLT narrow-band imaging data that accompanied our spectroscopy. This is coupled also with the availability of the PANSTARRS multi-wavelength, high resolution photometric data now available in our HASH database. 3. Our extensive work on the sample of BULGE PNe discovered and characterised in the HASH database has also provided the solid foundation necessary to progress this project. This has involved very extensive assessment of the angular sizes, central star detections, morphologies and improved positions and new discoveries for all Galactic Bulge PNe.

17300417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17300417.value: This project concerns a major problem: what is the structure, formation and evolutionary history of the central region of our Galaxy (the Galactic Bulge)? We tackle this using planetary nebulae (PNe). PNe are powerful tools that provide an independent, traceable, population compared to normal stars. Across the Bulge their ages, chemistry and velocity structure will be investigated with greater clarity than for other tracers. PNe provide the new data and discriminatory power to choose between competing Bulge formation and evolutionary models and its star formation history. PNe derive from stars ~1-8× the Sun's mass, representing 90% of stars more massive than the sun. They form near the end of a stars life as an ejected gas shell. The shell exhibits strong emission lines making them detectable out to the Galactic Bulge at ~8 kiloparsecs. Their strong emission lines permit the size, expansion velocity and PN age to be determined. We can use them to derive luminosity, temperature and mass of their central stars, and the chemical composition of the ejected gas. Their complex shapes provide clues to their formation, evolution, mass loss and likely shaping agents. These properties make them ideal age, abundance, mass and kinematic probes for this project.

17300817.label: Project Objectives
17300817.value: We shall develop adaptive numerical methods for long-time integration and model reduction for the particle transport models. We aim to investigate both the Lagrangian approach and Eulerian approach in computing effective diffusivity. We shall develop adaptive numerical methods for long-time integration and model reduction of the Schrodinger equation with random potentials. We aim to investigate both the Lagrangian approach and Eulerian approach in computing Anderson localization. We shall carry out many numerical simulations to test the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed numerical methods. Most importantly, we aim to gain critical insights into the mechanisms behind these physical phenomena, such as the relationship between the chaotic and stochastic velocity field and effective diffusivity (if exists) and how the random potential influences the Anderson localization. We shall investigate the geometric ergodicity of the particle transport models studied in the Objective 1 and provide analysis on the convergence rate of the Markov chain generated by the solution to its invariant measure (if exists).

17300817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17300817.value: 自然科学和工程领域的许多问题都充满了不确定性因素，例如地下水或空气中的污染物的扩散，电子在不纯净的导体中传播，光子在光纤中的传播。 对这些问题中的不确定性因素进行建模，并且量化分析这些不确定性因素对人们关心的计算量的影响，这方面的研究非常重要。 例如，这可以帮助决策者们及时采取行动，减少污染物扩散造成的损害，或者帮助制造商生产高质量的电子设备和光纤。不确定性量化是研究这些问题的一个新兴研究领域。 随机微分方程和随机偏微分方程，由于方程中包含随机变量或随机过程，所以很自然地被用来对复杂问题进行建模，并且量化分析相应的不确定性因素的影响。对于随机微分方程和随机偏微分方程的研究，人们已经付出了很多努力，并且得到了许多非常有效的数值方法。 然而，当随机问题的解空间维数很高时，问题变得非常困难，这类问题也被成为维数灾难问题。对于这类问题，构造相应的数值计算方法仍然是很困难的。另外，当我们需要计算随机问题的长时间解时，问题变得更加困难。这极大地限制了人们研究许多现实问题的能力。 在这个研究课题中，我们的研究目标是针对一类随机微分方程和随机偏微分方程，构造计算问题的长时间数值解以及模型降阶的自适应数值方法。我们将考虑两个模型问题：（1）计算粒子传输模型中的有效扩散系数，（2）计算带有随机势函数的薛定谔方程中的安德森局部化现象。对于每个问题，我们将分别考虑拉格朗日方法和欧拉方法。我们将研究几个具体的问题，如构造保结构计算格式、高阶计算格式、自适应控制时间步长、研究方差减少方法、构造压缩基函数、动态低维近似等。然后，我们将进行许多数值模拟来测试我们的方法的准确性和计算效率。我们期待能够通过这些数值结果，可以深入了解这些物理现象背后的物理机制。此外，我们将分析粒子传输模型的几何遍历性以及分析这个模型产生的马尔可夫链收敛到其不变测度的收敛速度。 我们期待着这个课题的研究结果将在高维随机微分方程和随机偏微分方程的数值方法方面取得一些进展，特别是用来计算随机问题的长时间数值解方面。通过这些新方法，我们可以计算许多具体问题，如污染物的扩散模拟，半导体器件仿真和光纤设计。最近，安德森局部化模型的研究方面得到了一个令人振奋的应用结果。 威斯康辛大学密尔沃基分校的马菲教授设计了一种可以通过使用安德森局部化现象的原理来调控光束在光纤中传播率，从而能够控制信息的传播量。这一发现可以被用来设计下一代的数据传输方式。 因此，这个研究课题得到的研究结果有望在科学和工程界产生广泛的影响。

17300817.label: Realisation of objectives
17300817.value: We have made tremendous efforts for the objectives proposed in this project, and are very pleased that the objectives of the proposal are fully achieved. Nine papers have been published, one paper has been accepted, and one paper is under review. Many papers were published in top journals of computational mathematics. We have successfully developed stochastic structure-preserving schemes for computing effective diffusivities, including computing effective diffusivities in steady chaotic flows [1,2], computing effective diffusivities in time-dependent chaotic flows [4], and computing effective diffusivities in random flows [3]. The numerical accuracy, convergence, and stability of the proposed structure-preserving schemes were also studied in these papers. For example, we obtained sharp error estimates (which are uniform in time) on the structure-preserving schemes in computing effective diffusivities of 3D chaotic flows in [2]. The PI was invited to report his results at the 8th International Congress of Chinese Mathematicians (Beijing 2019), and a paper was published in the ICCM Proceedings 2019 [5]. As a further extension of the structure-preserving schemes developed in this project, we developed a convergent interacting particle method to compute KPP front speeds in chaotic flows and obtained the error estimate of the proposed method [11]. We have also developed very efficient numerical methods to solve Schrödinger equations with multiscale potentials in the semiclassical regime, including the model reduction approach to computing eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of Schrödinger equations [6], multiscale finite element methods for Schrödinger equations with multiscale potentials [7], multiscale finite element methods for Schrödinger equations with time-dependent potentials [8], and multiscale reduced basis method for the Schrödinger equation with multiscale and random potentials [9]. The numerical accuracy, convergence, and stability of the proposed multiscale methods for semiclassical Schrodinger equations with multiscale potentials were studied in [10]. Some research outputs were presented by PI and his students in their invited talks and posters at four international conferences. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, some international conferences were canceled since 2020. Two Ph.D. students, Dr. Zhongjian Wang and Dr. Junlong Lyu were trained with support from the project. Dr. Wang joined the faculty of the University of Chicago as a William H. Kruskal Instructor in 2020 and Dr. Lyu joined Huawei Theoretical Research Lab in Hong Kong in 2021.

17300817.label: Major findings and research outcome
17300817.value: Computing effective diffusivity for particles moving in chaotic and stochastic flows is a fundamental problem in studying diffusion enhancement phenomena in fluid advection, which is of great theoretical and practical importance. Many existing works use numerical methods (e.g. FEMs and spectral methods) to solve a convection-diffusion type corrector problem to compute effective diffusivity, which becomes extremely expensive when the diffusion coefficient is small and/or flows are in 3D space. We developed robust structure-preserving schemes in the Lagrangian framework to compute effective diffusivity for chaotic flows (including 3D ABC flow and Kolmogorov flow) and provided a sharp and uniform-in-time error estimate for the numerical schemes. Specifically, we compute effective diffusivities in steady chaotic flows [1,2], time-dependent chaotic flows [4], and random flows [3], respectively. We also investigate the convection-enhanced diffusion phenomenon for these complicated flows, including the ABC flow and the Kolmogorov flow in 3D space. Our computation of convection-enhanced diffusivity in 3D chaotic flows and random flows appears to be the first in the Lagrangian framework. We also developed a convergent interacting particle method to compute KPP front speeds in chaotic flows and obtained the error estimate of the proposed method [11]. In recent years, people use Schrodinger equations to model quantum hetero-structures with tailored functionalities, such as heterojunctions and quantum metamaterials. The potentials in these models can be aperiodic and/or discontinuous, bringing challenges to existing methods such as asymptotic-based methods (e.g. WKB method), Bloch decomposition methods, and spectral methods. To address this challenge, we proposed a multiscale finite element method (MsFEM) to solve this problem in the semi-classical regime [7]. In addition, we developed an enriched MsFEM to solve Schrodinger equations with time-dependent potentials for studying electron dynamics under external controls [8] and a multiscale basis method to compute eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of Schrodinger equations [6]. Later, we combined the MsFEM with the quasi-Monte Carlo method to solve Schrodinger equations with random potentials, which allows us to simulate the famous Anderson localization phenomenon [9]. Our work appears to be the first one in the uncertainty quantification community to compute the Anderson localization phenomena for Schrodinger equations. The numerical accuracy, convergence, and stability of the proposed multiscale methods for semiclassical Schrodinger equations with multiscale potentials were studied in [10].

17300817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17300817.value: Based on this project, there are several possible research problems in the future: (1) develop interacting particle methods to compute front speeds in reaction-diffusion-advection equations with Kolmogorov Petrovsky Piskunov (KPP) nonlinearity in random flows; (2) develop multiscale finite element methods to solve nonlinear Schrodinger equations (NLSE) with random potentials. The NLSE with a random potential is a fundamental problem. In spite of extensive mathematically rigorous, analytical, and numerical explorations, the elementary properties of its dynamics are not known; (3) develop deep neural network-based deep learning methods to solve long-time integration and model reduction problems and study their applications in computing effective diffusivity and Anderson localization.

17300817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17300817.value: Stochastic differential equations (SDEs) and stochastic partial differential equations (SPDEs) play important roles in modeling complex problems and quantifying the corresponding uncertainties. Considerable amounts of effort have been devoted to studying the solutions of SDEs and SPDEs. Researchers have made advances with the successful development of many efficient numerical methods in solving SDEs and SPDEs. However, it is still very challenging when we need to compute long-time solutions. In this project, by developing robust structure-preserving schemes, we have developed efficient numerical methods to solve SDEs and compute effective diffusivities in chaotic and random flows. By exploring the intrinsic low-dimensional structures in the solutions, we have developed multiscale finite element methods to solve Schrodinger equations with multiscale and random potentials. Moreover, we provide rigorous convergence and stability analysis for these new methods and conduct numerical simulations to verify the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed methods. With these new methods, we can compute many real-world problems, such as pollutant transport simulation, semiconductor device simulation, and optical fiber design. By computing the effective diffusivities in the oil spills, we can estimate the location and range of the damage and help engineers make better decisions and reduce the damage. Therefore, the results obtained in this project will have a broad scientific impact on the fast-developing UQ field.

17301017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17301017.value: The major concern of this proposal is an in-depth study of the extensions of the famous I-MMSE relationship, a recent result of ours obtained in exploring the connections between information measures and estimation measures. Unveiling an important link between information theory and estimation theory, the I-MMSE relationship, which was recently discovered by Guo, Shamai and Verdu, and its numerous variants are of fundamental significance to relevant areas in these two fields and have been exerting far-reaching influences over a wide range of topics. Undertaking a newly proposed approach (dubbed the "independent probability space" approach in this proposal) we have extended the I-MMSE relationship to channels with feedback and memory. It turns out that our new approach can circumvent hindrances that are otherwise present with all previous approaches. This proposal will be dedicated to a thorough examination of many possible applications of the extended I-MMSE relationship and our new approach. More specifically, in this proposal, we plan to 1) further extend the I-MMSE relationship to colored Gaussian feedback channels, general feedback channels and its limiting version in terms of mutual information rate; 2) explore the properties of the extended MMSE; 3) explore the applications of the extended I-MMSE relationship to Gaussian feedback and memory channels, and their multi-user and MIMO versions; 4) explore the applications of our new approach to other information-theoretic quantities, higher order derivatives, information-theoretic inequalities, sampling theorems. This proposal, if successfully carried out, will certainly deepen our understanding on a number of fundamental aspects of information theory, estimation theory and many other related fields. 基于我们最近得到的关于信息理论和估计理论之间的关联的一个结果，本項目的一個主要的目的是深入研究I-MMSE關係的拓展和各種可能的應用。 這個經典的關係是在大約十年前由Guo，Shamai和Verdu發現，其揭示了信息论和估计理论的一个重要联系，在信息論和各種相關的領域有著廣泛的應用和深遠的影響。 我们在近年来用一些新颖的方法把这个重要的关系推广到了有反馈和记忆的高斯信道。事实证明，我们的方法可以克服以前的一些方法遇到的好多难以克服的问题。 本項目会從數學理論和電子通訊的各種角度來繼續研究這個拓展的關係和我们的方法的应用。 详细来说，我们计划：1）进一步拓展这个关系到更一般的高斯信道；2）探索拓展的MMSE的各种属性；3）探索这个拓展关系的应用， 包括有反馈和记忆的高斯信道；4）探索我们的方法在信息论其他方面的应用。 本项目的顺利执行势必极大的加深我们对信息论，估计理论和众多相关领域的理解

17301017.label: Major findings and research outcome
17301017.value: Unveiling a fundamental link between information theory and estimation theory, the I-MMSE relationship by Guo, Shamai and Verdu has great theoretical significance and various practical applications. On the other hand, its influences to date have been restricted to channels without feedback or memory, due to the absence of its extensions to such channels. In this project, we have successfully extended the I-MMSE relationship to discrete-time and continuous-time Gaussian channels with feedback and/or memory and discussed their applications to various scenarios. More specifically, we have established [1, 5] causality-preserving connections between continuous-time Gaussian feedback/memory channels and their associated discrete-time versions in the forms of sampling and approximation theorems, which we believe will play important roles in the long run for further developing continuous-time information theory. As an immediate application of the approximation theorem, we propose the so-called approximation approach to examine continuous-time white Gaussian channels in the point-to-point [3] or multi-user setting [4]. It turns out that the approximation approach, complemented by relevant tools from stochastic calculus, can enhance our understanding of continuous-time Gaussian channels in terms of giving alternative and strengthened interpretation to some long-held folklore [1], recovering “long known” results from new perspectives [2], and rigorously establishing new results predicted by the intuition that the approximation approach carries.

17301017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17301017.value: The tools and methodologies developed in this project can be expected to be applied to various scenarios. A very promising direction is to analyze the rate of information-theoretical convergence for continuous-time additive white Gaussian channels. More specifically, for a continuous-time additive white Gaussian noise channel , it has been shown that as sampling gets infinitesimally fine, the mutual information of the associative discrete-time channels converges to that of the original continuous-time channel. We believe that it is possible that with the enhanced understanding, we can give more quantitative strengthenings of this result, which, among other implications, can characterize how over-sampling approaches the true mutual information of a continuous-time Gaussian channel with bandwidth limit.

17301017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17301017.value: Unveiling an important link between information theory and estimation theory, the I-MMSE relationship, which was recently discovered by Guo, Shamai and Verdu, and its numerous variants are of fundamental significance to relevant areas in these two fields and have been exerting far-reaching influences over a wide range of topics. On the other hand, all the applications of the I-MMSE relationship to date have been restricted to channels without feedback and memory, due to the lack of extensions of the I-MMSE relationship to such channels. In this regard, a “plain” generalization of the original I-MMSE relationship to feedback channels should not be expected, which has been noted by Guo, Shamai and Verdu in their seminal paper, where an example is given to show that the exact I-MMSE relationship fails to hold for some continuous-time feedback channel. Given the striking influences of the original I-MMSE relationship, we expect that our extended I-MMSE relationship can help bridge the gaps between non-feedback and feedback channels and deepen our understanding of the latter. What’s more, we believe that our new approach can yield insights on many aspects on information theory from refreshingly new perspectives, and may even help us solve some fundamental problems therein.

17301317.label: Realisation of objectives
17301317.value: Over the course of the project, a better understanding of Hecke eigenforms was achieved in two different directions. Firstly, a paper investigating the degenerate part of the regularized inner product on meromorphic modular forms was produced. In this paper, we obtain a classification of meromorphic modular forms in terms of the degenerate subspace, obtaining a bijection with the space of cusp forms after factoring out by the degenerate subspace. Moreover, the inner product on the quotient space coincides with the inner product on the space of cusp forms; due to the fact that the space of cusp forms is positive-definite with respect to the inner product, there is a unique element of the quotient space that corresponds to each Hecke eigenform. The construction can b realized as a theta lift. This is entirely analogous to the weakly holomorphic case, where a similar quotient is taken. This helps to realize objectives 1, 2, and 4. By studying the quotient space for weakly holomorphic modular forms, another paper was produced that fulfills objective 3. In addition, a new definition of Hecke eigenforms was obtained over the course of the project. The preprint, just completed, yields a link with the work of Gross and Zagier (and their algebraicity conjecture in particular) and places the meromorphic modular forms into a framework connected to weakly holomorphic modular forms, achieving objective 6. The observed congruences, while they seem to be a consequence of the definition related to Gross and Zagier's work, are still elusive to understand and prove. Further work needs to be conducted to understand the relationship between this definition and the congruences. For this reason, the relationship with the p-adic modular forms in objective 1 and the proof of the congruences found in objective 5 are only partially achieved; essentially, the relationship appears to follow from this definition, but a proof of this fact needs to be found.

17301317.label: Major findings and research outcome
17301317.value: A number of papers and preprints have come out of the research conducted. There were separate papers related to the degenerate subspace under the regularized inner product, the computation of the unary theta function via inner products and harmonic Maass forms, and another paper outlining the connection between meromorphic Hecke eigenforms and the algebraicity conjecture of Gross and Zagier. The most significant progress is probably in understanding the structure of the regularized inner product and in identifying and defining meromorphic Hecke eigeforms, as classical versions of both have been influential in the theory of modular forms and its applications to combinatorics and in solving diophantine equations.

17301317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17301317.value: There is still potential for further understanding of the p-adic properties of coefficients of meromorphic Hecke eigenforms. Now that the objects have been identified and the source of the observed congruences seems to have been found, it opens up the possibility for them to be further studied in an attempt to prove these observed properties.

17301317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17301317.value: Roughly speaking, an inner product of two vectors measures how much length the vectors have in common; if the inner product is zero, then the vectors go in completely different directions and are orthogonal. Some inner products are degenerate in the sense that there are vectors which are orthogonal to everything. We extend an inner product to a larger space (of an object called modular forms) than it was previously defined on and study the degenerate part of this space. This extended definition and the determination of the degenerate part helps us to understand the behaviour of the underlying space and to identify and define an important type of modular form that comes from the generating vectors of the non-degenerate part.

17301517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17301517.value: The intriguing luminescence behaviour and interesting structural and bonding properties of polynuclear gold(I) clusters associated with their strong propensity to form non-covalent short gold–gold contacts arising from aurophilicity, have established them as a unique class of materials. In particular, there have been much interest in the controlled synthesis of discrete metal clusters and the understanding of their structure and bonding as well as structure-property relationships since the development of discrete molecular gold clusters of controlled tunable sizes and shapes may serve as model compounds to aid the understanding of the optical properties and the structure-property relationships of the related nanomaterials. However, the preparation of discrete gold nanoclusters with controllable size and well-defined structures that are soluble and remain intact in solution is still a great challenge. Even more challenging will be to use these discrete gold nanoclusters as the building block to assemble more sophisticated higher-ordered structures, networks, oligomers and inorganic-organic hybrids and to study the influence of intermolecular interactions between discrete polynuclear molecular complexes/clusters. In this project, we will mainly focus on the design and synthesis of soluble discrete molecular clusters of gold. Unlike the majority of gold clusters, which are mainly supported by monodentate phosphine or thiolate ligands, the project will focus on the use of various multidentate bridging ligands, especially those bearing active or functional groups, for the post-synthetic modification and construction of novel luminescent polynuclear gold(I) clusters and small gold nanoclusters (<2-nm size). Efforts will be made to employ the reaction-based approach for cluster-to-cluster transformation and for the construction of higher-ordered metal cluster networks, assemblies, oligomers and inorganic-organic hybrids via post-synthetic modification, and to study the reaction mechanisms and growth dynamics as well as the inter-cluster interactions. Incorporation of reaction-based functional units in the ligands is believed to produce versatile functional gold nanocluster-based building motifs for the construction of clusters-of-clusters and higher-ordered metal cluster assemblies, networks, oligomers and inorganic-organic hybrids with interesting functions and properties. It is envisaged that a systematic study and delineation of the various factors that control the assembly and oligomerization process through a systematic variation of the different active functional groups and reaction-based building motif, together with their correlation with spectroscopic, electronic absorption, luminescence and various functional and morphological properties, would provide important insights and guiding principles for the controlled assembly and construction of metal cluster assemblies, networks, oligomers and inorganic-organic hybrids with interesting functional properties. 多核一價金簇具有奇妙的發光行為、有趣的結構與結合性質、以及親金作用誘導下所形成的短非共價金-金相互作用的強烈傾向等特性，因此它們已經成為一類獨特的材料。尤其是，由於離散分子金簇具有受控及可調大小和形狀的條件，並可用作模型化合物來幫助理解相關納米材料的光學特性和結構與性能之間的關係，吸引了不少科學家對離散金屬簇的受控合成，它們的結構和鍵合，以及其結構與性能之間的關係方面作深入研究。然而，製備可溶及在溶液中能保持完整的，和具有可控大小和結構規整的離散金納米簇仍是一個巨大的挑戰，而利用這些離散的金納米簇作為構築塊來組裝更高層次有序的精密結構、網狀物、低聚物及無機-有機雜化物，並研究離散多核分子配合物或簇之間的分子間相互作用的影響將會是個更大的挑戰。在這個項目中，我們主要研究可溶性離散分子金簇的設計和合成。但與主要由單齒膦或硫醇鹽配體支持的大多數金簇不同之處是，此項目將主要採用各種多齒橋連配體，特別是帶有活性或功能基團的多齒橋連配體來進行後合成修飾和構建，從而合成新型發光多核一價金簇和細小尺寸的金納米簇（小於2納米）。我們將致力研究採用基於化學反應的方法來實現簇到簇的轉化，通過後合成修飾來構建更高層次有序的金屬簇網狀物、組裝體、低聚物和無機-有機雜化物，並研究它們的反應機理和生長動力學以及簇之間的相互作用。把基於化學反應的功能單元掺入配體中相信能合成多功能的金納米簇的構築基元，這些多功能基元可用來構建具有趣功能和特性的簇集群和更高層次有序的金屬簇組裝體、網狀物、低聚物以及無機-有機雜化物。通過系統地改變不同的活性功能團和基於化學反應的構築基元來研究和劃定組裝和低聚過程的控制因素，以及研究相關的光譜、電子吸收、發光和各種不同的功能和形態特性，將為具有趣功能特性的金屬簇組裝體、網狀物、低聚物以及無機-有機雜化物的受控組裝和構建提供重要的見解和指導原則。

17301717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17301717.value: Quantum spin Hall effect is a two-dimensional topological phase of matter, in which the bulk is insulating while a pair of edge conducting states with opposite spins move in opposite directions around the boundary of system. The edge conducting channel is robust against irregular boundary and disorder under protection from time reversal symmetry. In the system an external electric field can produce a transverse pure spin current, an indispensible constituent in next generation of spin-based electronic devices. The effect has been first predicted theoretically and confirmed experimentally in HgTe/CdTe and InAs/GaSb quantum well. The bilayer InAs/GaSb quantum well provides a platform to explore physical properties of quantum spin Hall effect as the top and back gates allow independent controlling the density of charge carriers and band offset such that the system can be tuned from the topologically trivial to nontrivial regimes. While quantized conductance due to the edge transport was measured experimentally, there are a series of unexpected consequences that directly challenge the existing theories of simple quantum spin Hall model. For example, the edge states are insensitive to external magnetic fields; the edge resistance is independent of temperatures up to 30K. The observation of helical Luttinger liquid in the edge indicates the important role of electron-electron interaction. More surprising, several experimental groups reported the evidences to support the edge transport in the topologically trivial region. The primary objective of this project is to understand the unexpected phenomena in the edge transport in the InAs/GaSb quantum wells. It will focus on the band structures of the InAs/GaSb quantum wells, magnetic response to external fields, the electron-electron interaction in the edge states, and the formation of the edge states in various conditions. This project will help us to understand exotic properties of topological phases of matter, and explore possible development of this new field in the future. 量子自旋霍爾效應是一種二維的拓撲物相，其體態是絕緣的，而邊界具有一對運動方向和自旋皆相反的導電狀態。邊緣導電通道在時間反演對稱性的保護下，對不規律的邊界和雜質都是穩定的。在系統中，外部電場可以產生橫向純自旋流， 它是基於自旋的下一代電子設備中一個不可缺的成分。這個效應先是在理論上預言，並在HgTe / CdTe和InAs / GaSb量子阱中得到實驗上證實 。雙層InAs / GaSb量子阱 為探索量子自旋霍爾效應提供了一個物理平台。雖然邊界態的輸運在實驗上得到了驗證，然而有一系列意想不到的結果直接挑戰了 現有的簡單量子自旋霍爾理論。例如，邊緣狀態對外部磁場不敏感; 邊緣電阻在溫度達30K也沒有實質變化。實驗表明電子 - 電子相互作用起了重要作用。更令人驚訝的是，幾個 實驗組報告邊解運輸在拓撲平庸區域出現的證據。這個項目的主要目標是想理解在InAs / GaSb量子阱中的邊緣傳輸中出現意想不到的現象。它會 關注InAs / GaSb量子阱的帶結構，對外磁場的響應，邊緣狀態下的電子 - 電子相互作用以及形成邊緣狀態在各種條件下。這個項目將幫助我們了解拓撲物項的奇異物性，探索這個領域的新的發展方向。

17301717.label: Realisation of objectives
17301717.value: The main objective of the project is to construct an effective model for quantum spin Hall effect in the InAs/GaSb bilayer quantum well, and to study the formation of the edge states for quantum spin Hall effect. It also aims to study the quantum transport and its stability in various conditions and systems. The quantum spin Hall effect has been observed in InAs/GaSb bilayer quantum well. While quantized conductance due to the edge transport was measured experimentally, there are a series of unexpected consequences that directly challenge the existing theories of simple quantum spin Hall model. For example, the edge states are insensitive to external magnetic fields; the edge resistance is independent of temperatures up to 30K. Over the last few years, PI studied the problem, and published 5 papers relevant to this project, 2 in Physical Review B and 3 in Physical Review Letters. PI believed that he has achieved the project objectives. The robustness of quantum edge transport in InAs/GaSb quantum wells in the presence of magnetic fields raises an issue on the fate of topological phases of matter under time-reversal symmetry breaking. A peculiar band structure evolution in InAs/GaSb quantum wells is revealed: the electron subbands cross the heavy hole subbands but anticross the light hole subbands. The topologically protected band crossing point (Dirac point) of the helical edge states is pulled to be close to and even buried in the bulk valence bands when the system is in a deeply inverted regime, which is attributed to the existence of the light hole subbands. A sizable Zeeman energy gap verified by the effective g factors of edge states opens at the Dirac point by an in-plane or perpendicular magnetic field; however, it can also be hidden in the bulk valance bands. This provides a plausible explanation for the recent observation on the robustness of quantum edge transport in InAs/GaSb quantum wells subjected to strong magnetic fields. In this work, PI has achieved the main objective of this project. (Phys. Rev. B 97, 045420 (2018)) Topological phase transition in disordered electric quadrupole insulators: We investigate disorder-driven topological phase transitions in quantized electric quadrupole insulators in two dimensions. We show that chiral symmetry can protect the quantization of the quadrupole moment, such that the higher-order topological invariant is well defined even when disorder has broken all crystalline symmetries. Moreover, nonvanishing quadrupole moment and consequent corner modes can be induced from a trivial insulating phase by disorder that preserves chiral symmetry. The critical points of such topological phase transitions are marked by the occurrence of extended boundary states even in the presence of strong disorder. We provide a systematic characterization of these disorder-driven topological phase transitions from both bulk and boundary descriptions. In this work, we address the stability of the edge states in disorders. (Phys. Rev. Lett. 125, 166801 (2020)) Majorana-Josephson interferometer: We propose an interferometer for chiral Majorana modes where the interference effect is caused and controlled by a Josephson junction of proximity-induced topological superconductors, hence, a Majorana-Josephson interferometer. This interferometer is based on a two-terminal quantum anomalous Hall bar, and as such its transport observables exhibit interference patterns depending on both the Josephson phase and the junction length. Observing these interference patterns will establish quantum coherent Majorana transport and further provide a powerful characterization tool for the relevant system. (Phys. Rev. B 99, 100504(R), (2019)) Quantum interference theory of magnetoresistance in Dirac materials: Magnetoresistance in many samples of Dirac semimetals and topological insulators displays nonmonotonic behavior over a wide range of magnetic fields. Here a formula of magnetoconductivity is presented for massless and massive Dirac fermions in Dirac materials due to quantum interference of Dirac fermions in scalar impurity scattering potentials. It reveals a striking crossover from positive to negative magnetoresistivity, uncovering strong competition between weak localization and weak antilocalization in multiple Cooperon channels at different chemical potentials, effective masses, and finite temperatures. This work sheds light on the important role of strong coupling of the conduction and valence bands in the quantum interference transport in topological nontrivial and trivial Dirac materials. (Phys. Rev. Lett. 122, 246601 (2019))

17301717.value: The quantum spin Hall effect has been confirmed in the InAs/GaSb quantum well. The effect was also observed in more and more 2D systems. 17301717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17301717.value: Quantum spin Hall effect is a two-dimensional topological phase of matter, in which the bulk is insulating while a pair of edge conducting states with opposite spins move in opposite directions around the boundary of system. The edge conducting channel is robust against irregular boundary and disorder under protection from time reversal symmetry. The effect has been first predicted theoretically and confirmed experimentally in HgTe/CdTe and InAs/GaSb quantum well. While quantized conductance due to the edge transport was measured experimentally, there are a series of unexpected consequences that directly challenge the existing theories of simple quantum spin Hall model. The primary objective of this project is to understand the unexpected phenomena in the edge transport in the InAs/GaSb quantum wells. In this project, the effective model was established to reveal the band structure. It is found that the topologically protected band crossing point (Dirac point) of the helical edge states is pulled to be close to and even buried in the bulk valence bands when the system is in a deeply inverted regime. This provides a reasonable explanation for the recent observation on the robustness of quantum edge transport subjected to strong magnetic fields, and in strong disorders.

17301817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17301817.value: 在合成化學中，通過金屬催化的氮賓轉移/插入反應構建C-N鍵是非常重要的反應。儘管人們在這一領域作出了巨大的努力，但是與類似的氧賓和卡賓轉移反應相比，高效、高選擇性的金屬催化氮賓的轉移反應仍然相對較少。其中一個主要的挑戰是設計和合成穩定的過渡金屬催化劑，使其可以在溫和的條件下高效地產生活潑的金屬-亞氨基/氮賓中間體，同時也能為那些能夠發生選擇性氮賓轉移/插入反應的中間體提供足夠的穩定性。最理想的過渡金屬催化劑是源自地球含量豐富的過渡金屬，尤其是具有生物相容性的金屬鐵，它是本研究的重點。在本項目中我們也會研究其它金屬催化劑，例如釕和銥，雖然相比鐵更昂貴且不俱生物相容性，但是，眾所周知的是，其能夠幫助形成更加穩定的金屬-亞氨基/氮賓中間體，從而實現對中間體更詳細的表徵和保證選擇性氮賓轉移/插入反應的順利完成。通過光譜的手段和計算的方法，以及研究中間體的形成和隨後其與有機底物反應的機理，從而實現了對活潑的金屬-亞氨基/氮賓中間體的全面了解，並提供用來提高反應活性和選擇性的必要信息，比如，通過合理的修飾配體的空間位阻和電子效應和/或金屬中心的氧化態。空間擁擠的四齒配位配體，如卟啉或手性席夫鹼，與活性金屬-亞氨基/氮賓基團的配位指導了其接近有機底物的方向，並提供了分離這些活性物質用於X射線晶體分析和其他光譜分析的可能。 在這個項目中，我們將研究烷基疊氮化物，苯甲酰疊氮化物和羥胺的新的氮賓轉移反應以及可見光誘導的氮賓轉移反應。本研究的重點主要集中在烷基氮賓和苯甲酰氮賓上。近年來，它們被用於一些新的化學反應，使新的構建C-N鍵的策略能夠具有廣泛的底物範圍和良好的反應選擇性成為了可能。到目前為止，文獻中僅有少數關於活性金屬-亞氨基/氮賓中間體的結構和反應機理的報導。我們預見無保護的“NH”的轉移將意味著氮賓轉移反應發展進入了新時代。 該項目將在申請人以前由香港研究資助委員會資助的“活性金屬配體多重配合物”和“過渡金屬催化的原子和基團轉移反應”工作基礎上展開。該項目的幾個重要特點分別是：（1）探索烷基氮賓和未保護的“NH”基團的新的轉移/插入反應，以及可見光誘導的氮賓轉移反應; (2) 發展穩定的金屬催化劑用於氮賓轉移反應，重點放在鐵，釕和銥絡合物的合成上; (3) 分離出活潑的金屬-亞氨基/氮賓中間體用於光譜表徵/研究和，如果可能，X射線分析; (4) 研究控制金屬催化的氮賓轉移反應的反應活性和選擇性的關鍵因素。該項目的研究計劃可能會帶來重要的發現，其可用於滿足設計新型金屬催化的C-N鍵構建反應。這是一項基礎研究，但研究結果將影響工業上應用於精細化工行業的發展。這項研究將延續香港在無機化學領域，包括金屬催化原子和基團轉移/插入反應中表現卓越的悠久傳統。

17301817.label: Realisation of objectives
17301817.value: In accordance with the foregoing objectives, we have published 22 papers in leading international chemistry journals including five in Angewandte Chemie International Edition, one in Journal of American Chemical Society and three in Chemical Science. Objective 1: We have reported that [FeIII(TF4DMAP)Cl] can efficiently catalyze intermolecular sp3 C–H amination using arylazides (49 examples; up to 98% product yield) and intramolecular sp3 C–H amination of alkylazides (12 examples; up to 90% yield). At catalyst loading down to 1 mol%, the reactions displayed high chemo- and regioselectivity with broad substrate scope and are effective for late-stage functionalization of complex natural/bioactive molecules. Mechanistic studies suggest that the reaction should proceed via a radical intermediate with the cleavage of the C-H bond as the rate-determining step. We also reported [RuIV(Por)Cl2] catalyzed C−N bond formation using acylazides as the nitrene source. This catalytic method is applicable to aziridine/oxazoline formation from alkenes (29 examples; up to 99% yield), amination of substituted indoles (13 examples; up to 88 % yield), alpha-amino ketone formation from silyl enol ethers (12 examples; up to 81% yield), amination of C(sp3)−H bonds (13 examples; up to 96% yield), and functionalization of natural products and carbohydrate derivatives (6 examples; up to 98% yield). In addition, we reported the use of trans-dichloroiridium(IV)-salen complexes as catalysts for intramolecular C–H amination of arylazides under microwave-assisted conditions, leading to dihydroquinazoliones or quinazolinones in moderate to good yields (up to 96% yield) Objective 2: As a follow-up study to the foregoing work, we discovered that [FeIII(TF4DMAP)Cl] can catalyze sp3 C–H amination and alkene aziridination with selectivity using alkylazides or arylazides as the nitrene source under blue LED light (469 nm) irradiation. The photochemical reactions display chemo- and regio-selectivity and are effective for the late-stage functionalization of natural and bioactive compounds with complexity. Objective 3: In order to identify the reactive intermediate of [RuIV(Por)Cl2] catalyzed C−N bond formation reactions using acylazides as the nitrene source, various spectroscopic analyses were performed. HR-ESI-MS and EPR spectroscopy point to the intermediacy of a porphyrin-supported RuV(NCOR) species as the intermediate. Further study by Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations also lends evidence for the formulation of the Ru(NCOR) acylnitrenoid as a RuV-imido species. HR-ESI-MS analysis on the reaction mixture of trans-dichloroiridium(IV)-salen complex with mesitylazide after microwave irradiation suggested the involvement of Ir-imido species as the reaction intermediate. We have also synthesized complexes [RuVI(Por)(NAd)(O)] and [RuVI(2,6-F2-TPP)(NAd)2], with the latter characterized by X-ray crystallography to have Ru=NAd and Ru=O bond distances of 1.778(5) Å and 1.760(4) Å (∠O–Ru–NAd: 174.37(19)°), respectively. These complexes are capable to catalyze aerobic oxidation with alkenes. High valent iron porphyrin nitrido species [Fe(por)N] could be generated by laser flash photolysis of [Fe(Por)N3]. Reactivity study on the C–H activation by the sterically encumbered [Fe(TTPPP)N] (H2TTPPP = meso-tetrakis(2,4,6-triphenylphenyl)porphyrin) in solution state was undertaken by nanosecond laser flash photolysis (LFP) coupled with various spectroscopies (mass spectrometry, nanosecond transient absorption, resonance Raman, etc.), labelling experiments, and DFT calculations. Objective 4: We have explored the effect of axial N-heterocyclic carbene ligands on iron(III) porphyrin catalyzed intramolecular C(sp3)–H amination of a wide variety of alkylazides under microwave-assisted and thermal conditions. Selective amination of tertiary, benzylic, allylic, secondary, and primary C−H bonds were achieved in up to 95% product yield. 14 out of 17 substrates were cyclized selectively at C4 position to give pyrrolidines. The regioselectivity at C4 or C5 position could be tuned by modifying the reactivity of the C5–H bond. Mechanistic studies revealed a concerted or a fast re-bound mechanism for the amination reaction. The reaction has been applied to the syntheses of tropane, nicotine, cis-octahydroindole, and leelamine derivatives. In addition to nitrene transfer reactions, we also studied the metal-catalyzed oxidation reactions and carbene transfer reactions. We have developed the ruthenium and iron catalysts supported by chiral tetradentate amine (N4) ligands for hydrocarbon oxidations, trisubstituted alkene cis-dihydroxylations with H2O2, asymmetric addition of silyl enol ethers to alpha, beta-unsaturated 2-acyl imidazoles, and asymmetric alkylation of N-heteroaromatics. We also developed the Fe-BPsalan system for the highly enantioselective Diels-Alder reaction of alkylidene beta-ketoesters, and dearomative chlorination of 2-hydroxy-1-naphthoates. Several metalloporphyrin systems (where M = iron, ruthenium, cobalt) for carbene transfer reactions using N-tosylhydrazones, diazo quinones, perfluoroalkyl aziridines and diaryldiazo compounds as the carbene sources. Cross-coupling of diazo quinones with catechol boronic esters can be performed without metal catalysts, giving biaryls and alkenyl phenols in up to 96% yield under mild conditions.

17301817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17301817.value: Incorporation of N-containing functionalities onto hydrocarbons is crucial to synthetic organic chemistry for the creation of new compounds having novel biological and therapeutic properties. In this project, new metal catalysts supported by sophisticatedly designed macrocyclic and auxiliary ligands have been developed for catalytic nitrene transfer reactions having broad substrate scope with alkylazides and acylazides as new nitrene sources under mild reaction conditions (light irradiation or under microwave-assisted conditions). The usefulness of these catalytic reactions have been well-illustrated by the application of these reactions in the synthesis/post-modifications of natural products. Spectroscopic and DFT studies revealed the involvement of reactive high valent metal-imido species as the reaction intermediates. The remarkable findings from this project have been published in prestigious international chemistry journals including Journal of the American Chemical Society, Angewandte Chemie International Edition, Chemical Science and Chemical Communications. The aforementioned achievements expedite the development of metal-catalyzed organic transformation reactions in a world-class level.

17302017.label: Project Objectives
17302017.value: To devise a combinatorial polynomial-time algorithm for solving the fractional edge-coloring problem (FECP) exactly; To employ and develop the novel techniques invented for the FECP to attack the Goldberg-Seymour Conjecture, and to design a substantially improved approximation algorithm for multigraph edge-coloring; To devise a combinatorial polynomial-time algorithm for solving the fractional edge cover packing problem (FECPP) exactly, and to design a good approximation algorithm for the edge cover packing problem (ECPP) using the techniques created for the FECPP; and To explore the possible connection between the Goldberg-Seymour Conjecture and Gupta's conjecture on the ECPP.

17302017.label: Realisation of objectives
17302017.value: I have carried out Objectives 1-3 completely (in particular, jointly with G. Chen and G. Jing, we have successfully proved the famous Goldberg-Seymour Conjecture). For Objective 4, we have established the best existing bound on the cover index of a multigraph, which differs from the bound conjectured by Gupta only by at most one. (Gupta's conjecture is the dual version of the Goldberg-Seymour Conjecture.)

17302017.label: Major findings and research outcome
17302017.value: (1) In the paper entitled "Densities, Matchings, and Fractional Edge-Colorings" (joint with X. Chen and Q. Zhao, SIAM J. Optim. 29 (2019), 240-261), we have successfully devised a combinatorial polynomial-time algorithm for the weighted density problem, thereby resolving an important open problem posed by several European mathematicians; using this algorithm as a subroutine, we have further obtained a combinatorial polynomial-time algorithm for the fractional edge-coloring problem (FECP). (Note: SIAM J. Optim. is one of the most prestigious international journals in operations research.) (2) In the paper entitled "Proof of the Goldberg-Seymour Conjecture on Edge-Colorings of Multigraphs" (joint with G. Chen and G. Jing), we have successfully proved a famous conjecture in the areas of combinatorial optimization, theoretical computer science, and graph theory, which was made independently by Goldberg and Seymour in the early 1970s. Over the past four decades this conjecture has been a subject of extensive research, and has stimulated an important body of work. Our proof, which is highly sophisticated and difficult, actually emerged from more than 10 years of unceasing dedication. At invitations of organizers, we have delivered lectures on this proof at a number of international conferences and universities (including Department of Mathematics at Princeton University, invited by Professor Seymour). We have also accepted invitation to give a 4-hour lecture series on this proof at the Workshop on Combinatorial Optimization to be held in Cargese, Corsica, France in October 2022. Our paper has been under review at a flagship mathematical journal. (In my research areas the refereeing process sometimes takes a very long time. For instance, it took eight years from submission to publish the article: M. Conforti, G. Cornuejols, and M. Rao, Decomposition of Balanced Matrices, J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 77 (1999), 292-406. This important paper was awarded the prestigious Fulkerson Prize in 2000, and G. Cornuejols is a world-leading expert on Combinatorial Optimization and Operations Research.) (3) Our paper entitled "On Gupta's Co-density Conjecture" (joint with Y. Cao et al.) is devoted to the study of the co-density conjecture proposed by Gupta in 1978, which is the dual version of the above Goldberg-Seymour Conjecture. In this paper we have established the best existing bound on the cover index of a multigraph, which differs from the bound conjectured by Gupta only by at most one. Since our proof is based on the validity of the Goldberg-Seymour Conjecture, we have to postpone submitting our paper until after the preceding paper has been accepted for publication.

17302017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17302017.value: A complete proof of Gupta's Co-density Conjecture, which, I believe, is within reach, with hard work.

17302017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17302017.value: The present project has both great theoretical interest and practical value. First, the proposed problems are all fundamental and attractive; solution to any of them yields not only a beautiful mathematical theorem but also a combinatorial polynomial-time algorithm for the corresponding problem. In particular, our proof of Goldberg-Seymour Conjecture implies that (a) there are only two possible values for the chromatic index of a multigraph; (b) although it is NP-hard in general to determine the chromatic index of a multigraph, we can approximate it within one of its true value; and (c) the fractional edge-coloring problem has a fascinating integer rounding property. Second, in our proof of the Goldberg-Seymour conjecture, we have developed many new proof techniques and exhibited a wealth of new structural properties. All of them, I believe, can be further extended to tackle some other well-known edge-coloring problems, such as the Berge-Fulkerson conjecture. Finally, since the edge-coloring and edge cover packing problems arise in a rich variety of applications, the results obtained in this project can be applied to solve many important real-world problems.

17302317.label: Project Objectives
17302317.value: To recognize the exact tectonic boundary of the orogenic system around the Kazakhstan microcontinent with the arc system along the Siberian margin. To determine the timing of collision between the Kazakhstan microcontinent and the Siberian Craton. To constrain the structural and magmatic response to the collision between the Kazakhstan microcontinent and the Siberian Craton. To reconstruct the amalgamation processes between the Kazakhstan microcontinent and the Siberian Craton, and to unravel the role of this collisional event in the formation of the curved orogenic system in the western CAOB.

17302317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17302317.value: The Late Paleozoic evolution of the western Central Asian Orogenic Belt (CAOB) is poorly understood. It involved the collision/amalgamation of a number of arc systems and continental blocks, bending of orogenic systems and the development of large-scale strike-slip shear zones, accompanied by widespread polymetal and gold mineralization. This project will combine structural, petrological, geochronological and geochemical study to unravel when, where and how major orogenic systems around the Kazakhstan microcontinent and the Siberian Craton collided. We will test the hypothesis that the collisional processes led to the bending of the whole orogenic belt around the Kazakhstan microcontinent, thus contributing to the general understanding of the role of oroclinal bending in accretionary orogens. The outcome will build a geodynamic framework for the tectonic evolution of the western CAOB in the late Paleozoic, which could facilitate future mineral exploration in Central Asia. During the past decades, the accretionary and collisional tectonics of the CAOB has drawn widespread attention from the international community. However, the research progress on the CAOB has suffered from a limited access across the political borders. The recent IGCP 592 project, funded by the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (the C.I., Dr Inna Safonova is the leader and the P.I. is a co-leader), provides a platform for international collaboration, which will be further strengthened in the scope of this project. We will bring Chinese, Russian and Australian scientists together to address a key problem across the China/Kazakhstan border. The project will ensure the direct participation and training of Hong Kong postdoctoral researchers and students in frontier sciences. 目前我们对中亚造山带(CAOB) 西缘的晚古生代演化历史还认识不清。其涉及到多个弧陆体系的碰撞/拼合、造山带的弯曲变形和大规模的走滑剪切带的发育，并伴有广泛的多金属和金矿化。这个项目将结合区域地质构造、岩石学、年代学和地球化学证据，以揭示哈萨克斯坦微陆块和西伯利亚板块之间的主体造山作用的时间、位置及方式。我们将检验碰撞过程导致了哈萨克斯坦微陆块周缘整个造山带弯曲这一假设，从而进一步了解弯曲变形在增生造山过程中的作用。这一结果将为中亚造山带(CAOB) 西缘晚古生代的构造演化提供相关的地球动力学框架，为中亚未来的矿产勘查提供帮助。 在过去的几十年里，国际社会对中亚造山带的增生造山作用产生了广泛的关注。然而，关于中亚造山带的研究进展受到了政治边界争议问题的制约。最近的联合国教科文组织支持的IGCP 592项目 (由合作者Inna Safonova博士牵头，申请人合作领导)，为国际合作提供了一个平台，这将进一步加强该项目的研究深度。我们将同中国、俄罗斯和澳大利亚的科学家们一起合作，探讨这个跨越中国/哈萨克斯坦边界的关键科学问题。该项目将确保香港博士后研究人员和研究生直接参与前沿科学研究。

17302317.label: Realisation of objectives
17302317.value: Objective 1: Two shear zones (Irtysh and Char shear zones) are exposed along the collisional zone of the Kazakhstan microcontinent and the arc system along the Siberian margin in Kazakhstan. They bound three tectonic units, i.e. the Rudny Altai, Irtysh-Zaisan Complex (also termed the Kalba-Narym terrane) and Zharma-Saur Arc, from north to south. We conducted U–Pb dating and Hf isotope analysis for detrital zircons from clastic rocks across the collisional zone of the Kazakhstan microcontinent and the arc system along the Siberian margin. Our results demonstrate that the Irtysh-Zaisan Complex carries abundant early Paleozoic detrital zircons and a few Precambrian zircons, but there is a lack of such zircon populations in the Zharma-Saur Arc. Devonian to Carboniferous detrital zircons appear in all sampled tectonic units, in which εHf(t) values of Carboniferous zircons from the Zharma-Saur Arc are characterized by a narrow range (~10–17) that is different from a relatively wider range of εHf(t) values of ~5–18 for the Carboniferous zircons in the Irtysh-Zaisan Complex. The distinct sedimentary provenances of the Irtysh-Zaisan Complex and the Zharma-Saur Arc show that the exact tectonic boundary of the Kazakhstan microcontinent and the arc system along the Siberian margin lies along the Char Shear Zone in Kazakhstan (Publication 12). Furthermore, we conducted geochronological and geochemical studies on the ophiolite along the Char Shear Zone, and concluded that the ophiolite was likely recycled from fragments of middle Devonian and Early Carboniferous intra-oceanic arcs that might develop within the Paleo-Asian Ocean (Publication 1). Objective 2: Our provenance study shows that the Late Carboniferous sedimentary rocks from the Zharma-Saur Arc do not receive detritus from the arc system along the Siberian margin. Therefore, we consider that the Ob-Zaisan Ocean between the Kazakhstan microcontinent and the arc system along the Siberian margin was closed later than the deposition of these sedimentary rocks (<321 Ma; Publication 12). The Char Shear Zone extends southeastward into NW China, where it merges into the Irtysh Shear Zone. The timing of the sinistral strike-slip deformation along the Char Shear Zone should be consistent with the active time of the sinistral strike-slip deformation along the Irtysh Shear Zone that was constrained to be at ~283-265 Ma (Publication 4 and 10). Thus, the Ob-Zaisan Ocean must have been closed before the sinistral strike-slip shearing along the Char Shear Zone given that the strike-slip shearing along the suture zone can only be active after the collision of the Kazakhstan microcontinent and the arc system along the Siberian margin. In a summary, the Ob-Zaisan Ocean between the Kazakhstan microcontinent and the arc system along the Siberian margin was closed within a period of ~321-283 Ma (Publication 12), which caused the collision of the Kazakhstan microcontinent and the Siberian Craton system. Objective 3: The collisional zone between the Kazakhstan microcontinent and the arc system along the Siberian margin is characterized by the occurrence of a series of shear zones (e.g., Char and Irtysh shear zones). Our structural and geochronological work, which is combined with published data, demonstrate that sinistral strike-slip shearing deformation along these shear zones was active at ~283-265 Ma. This deformation event was synchronous with the collision of the Kazakhstan microcontinent and the arc system along the Siberian margin, indicating that such a collision was dominated by the oblique convergence of two tectonic units (Publication 4 and 12). In order to understand the magmatic response to the collision of the Kazakhstan microcontinent and the Siberian margin, we conducted geochemical and geochronological study on late Paleozoic magmatic rocks along the collisional zone. Our results show that magmatism can be divided into three main episodes, i.e., middle to late Devonian, middle to late Carboniferous and Early Permian. Granitoids of the first two episodes were likely formed by the subduction of the Ob-Zaisan oceanic lithosphere, and a retreating episode of subduction possibly occurred in the Devonian (Publication 5, 6 and 9). The Early Permian magmatic rocks, which involved the contribution of the asthenosphere component, are considered to develop in response to the collision of the Kazakhstan microcontinent and the Siberian margin, with the possible effect of the Tarim mantle plume (Publication 7 and 11). Objective 4: Our work reconstructed late Paleozoic tectonic evolution along the Siberian margin. In the Devonian to Carboniferous, the subduction of the Ob-Zaisan Ocean characterized the Siberian margin, to generate a large amount of subduction-related magmatic rocks (Publication 3, 5, 6 and 9). This was followed by the amalgamation of the arc system along the Siberian margin with the Kazakhstan microcontinent farther south from latest Carboniferous to Permian (Publication 12). The amalgamation of these two tectonic units was accompanied by the development of sinistral shearing along the Char and Irtysh shear zones in the north and the dextral shearing farther south in Tianshan, indicating the eastward escape of the Kazakhstan microcontinent in response to the convergence of the Siberian, Baltic and Tarim cratons during the Permian (Publication 4 and 12). The geochemistry of the Permian magmatic rocks also demonstrates the possible overprint of the Tarim mantle plume on this amalgamation event (Publication 8 and 11). Our studies on the Kazakhstan Orocline that was developed around the Kazakhstan microcontinent demonstrate that the formation of the orocline might mainly occur before the collision of the Siberian margin with the Kazakhstan microcontinent. In other words, this collision event does not significantly contribute to the curving the orogenic system in the western CAOB, to form the Kazakhstan Orocline. Alternatively, the development of the orocline was linked to the trench migration of the Junggar subduction system (Publication 7).

17302317.label: Major findings and research outcome
17302317.value: The amalgamation of the Kazakhstan microcontinent and the arc system along the Siberian margin shapes the architecture of the CAOB. To unravel when, where and how these two tectonic units collided, it is crucial for the tectonic reconstruction of the CAOB. In this project, we conducted structural, petrological, geochronological and geochemical studies along the suture zone between the Kazakhstan microcontinent and the late Paleozoic arc system along the Siberian margin across the border of eastern Kazakhstan and NW China. Our results demonstrate that the Char Shear Zone represents the exact tectonic boundary of the Kazakhstan microcontinent and the arc system along the Siberian margin in Kazakhstan, and it extends into NW China to merge with the Irtysh Shear Zone that bounds the Siberian margin with the Kazakhstan microcontinent in NW China (Publication 1, 2 and 12). The suturing time of these two tectonic units was constrained after the deposition of Late Carboniferous sedimentary rocks (<321 Ma), but before the large-scale sinistral shearing along the Char and Irtysh shear zones (>283 Ma) (Publication 4 and 12). The amalgamation of the Kazakhstan microcontinent and the Siberian margin was synchronous with the Permian development of the large-scale sinistral strike-slip shearing along the suture zone, indicating oblique collision of the two tectonic units (Publication 4, 10 and 12). Such a collision event was accompanied by the widespread occurrence of Permian magmatic rocks along the Char and Irtysh shear zones in both Kazakhstan and NW China, which involved the contribution of the asthenosphere component, and was chemically distinctive from the Devonian to Carboniferous arc-related magmatism (Publication 5, 6, 8, 9 and 11). In addition, our study demonstrates that the collision of the Kazakhstan microcontinent with the Siberian margin did not contribute much to the development of the Kazakhstan Orocline that was likely formed in response to the trench migration of the Junggar subduction system (Publication 5). In general, our work provides a classic case for studying an ancient suture zone with a particular emphasis on the way to unravel the exact suturing position, time and dynamic processes.

17302317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17302317.value: This project makes a significant contribution to our understanding of the collision between the Kazakhstan micro-continent and the Siberian marginal arc system. This collisional event seems not to drive the formation of the Kazakhstan Orocline (that was developed around the Kazakhstan microcontinent). Alternatively, oroclinal bending was likely driven by the variable trench migration along the orogenic strike. It is worth investigating how each segment of the arc system around the Kazakhstan Orocline migrated laterally in the Devonian to Carboniferous, which would be beneficial to understand the geodynamics of oroclinal bending in general.

17302317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17302317.value: The upper part of the Earth is made of several rigid plates. Such plates move horizontally and interact with each other along plate boundaries, to shape the Earth’s morphology through the past 4.55 billion years. It has been challenging to reconstruct the ancient plate movement and to understand how ancient plate boundaries evolved. The Central Asian Orogenic Belt is a natural lab to study the evolution processes and mechanism along the boundary of two convergent plates. This project investigates the interaction history of two ancient plates, i.e. the Siberia and the Kazakhstan in Central Asia, via a combined study of structural geology, igneous petrology, geochemistry and geochronology. Our results demonstrate that the oceanic basin between the two ancient tectonic systems of the Siberia and the Kazakhstan was closed in the latest Carboniferous to earliest Permian along the Char Shear Zone in eastern Kazakhstan and the Irtysh Shear Zone in NW China, respectively. The subsequent convergence of the two tectonic systems was dominated by oblique collision rather than orthogonal amalgamation, to generate a series of large-scale transform fault systems. In general, this research provides a fundamental view for how to unravel the suturing position, time and processes in an ancient orogen.

17302617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17302617.value: Atomically thin 2D crystals and their van der Waals heterostructures have opened up exciting new possibilities for exploring fundamental physics and device applications. Heterostructures stacked by different 2D semiconductors realize, in the ultimate 2D limit, the semiconductor heterojunctions that have played key roles in modern device physics and discoveries of fundamental physics. While many 2D materials have the common hexagonal lattice structure, the mismatch in their lattice constants and in their crystalline orientations in the van der Waals heterostructures leads to the formation of Moire pattern where interlayer atomic registry varies from place to place. In long-period Moire pattern, the atomic registry at any local region (with length scale smaller than the Moire period) resembles certain lattice-matched bilayer, but has local-to-local variations in the long range. As the interlayer atomic registry determines the form and strength of coupling between the layers, it can be expected that the electronic structures get spatially modulated by the local-to-local variation of atomic registry in the Moire pattern and quasiparticle excitations thus experience a lateral superlattice (i.e. Moire superlattice). This is a unique aspect of van der Waals heterostructures, which has not been available in conventional semiconductor heterojunctions. In this theoretical project, we propose to study electronic, optical and topological properties in such Moire superlattices. We will investigate the Moire superlattice effects on excitons and their optical properties in heterobilayers with normal type-II band alignment. In heterobilayers of inverted type-II band alignment (broken gap), we will investigate topological band inversions and the possible formation of superstructures of topological insulators in the Moire pattern. Excitonic effects on the topological band inversion and excitonic insulator in the heterobilayer Moire superlattices will also be studied. These topics will be addressed in different heterobilayers formed by nonmagnetic 2D semiconductors such as monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides, as well as 2D semiconductors recently discovered with magnetic orders such as chromium trihalides, which allow us to explore the effects of magnetic orders on the heterostructure physics. 僅有原子尺度厚度的二維晶體的發現以及由他們構成的範德瓦爾斯異質結為探索基礎物理和應用提供了新的機遇。半導體異質結曾經在現代物理及器件方面的很多重要進展中扮演了關鍵。現在通過堆疊不同的二維半導體材料來實現異質結使得異質結在尺寸上達到了理想中的最小極限。盡管大部分二維材料具有類似的蜂窩狀晶格結構，但是他們的晶格常數各異，而且堆疊過程中產生晶軸方向的不匹配，這就導致這樣的異質結中會不可避免的出現莫爾條紋，即異質結中不同的局域的原子堆疊方式各不相同。在大尺度的莫爾條紋中， 原子的層間堆疊方式在每一個局部的小區域跟一個晶格匹配的雙層相比幾乎看不出來區別，但是到了大的空間尺度下，比較不同局域的堆疊方式會有明顯的區別。由於層間原子的堆疊決定了層間電子態的耦合方式和強度，我們可以預期這樣的範德瓦爾斯異質結中的電子結構會被莫爾條紋所調制，各種準粒子激發會體驗到一個平面內的超晶格 （莫爾超晶格）的影響。這種現象是傳統半導體異質結所不具備的，是二維材料範德瓦爾斯異質結的一大特征。在這個理論研究項目中，我們準備研究在這樣的莫爾超晶格中的電學，光學，和拓撲屬性。在由異質雙層構成的二型常規異質結中，我們準備探索莫爾超晶格效應對激子和他們的光學屬性的影響。 在反帶的二型異質結中，我們準備探索拓撲能帶反轉，由莫爾條紋所可能帶來的拓撲絕緣體超結構，以及在拓撲反帶發生時的激子效應。各種非磁性的單層半導體（即過渡金屬二硫化物），以及一些新近發現的具有磁性的二維材料，給我們研究這些現象提供了豐富平臺。

17302617.label: Realisation of objectives
17302617.value: Objective 1 This objective has been achieved. In semiconducting transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) heterobilayers featuring the type-II band alignment, we find that the formation of moire pattern naturally realize superstructures of nanodot confinements for long-lived interlayer excitons, which can be either electrically or strain tuned from perfect arrays of quantum emitters to excitonic superlattices with giant spin-orbit coupling. Such exciton features location dependent optical dipole and valley optical selection rule in a moiré supercell. The electric field can be exploited to tune the energy minima of the moire potential and thus the trapping location in the moire supercell, therefore allowing the electrically controlled inversion of the spin-valley optical selection rule of the emitter arrays. We further show that in moiré pattern of relatively small periodicity, the hopping of excitons between the trapping sites feature complex amplitude. This has made possible the emergence of exciton mini-band dispersion that features a Dirac node and two Weyl nodes in a honeycomb superlattices, as well as spin-momentum-locked topological exciton edge modes. These findings are published in Science Advances 3, e1701696 (2017) (publication #1). Together with our experimental collaborators, we also reported the first experimental evidence of moiré trapped interlayer exciton emitters, which feature quantum dot like narrow resonances in photoluminescence with strong circularly polarization (Nature 567, 66 (2019), as publication #4). Objective 2 This objective has been achieved. We have investigated the topological band inversion in the moire superlattices of inverted type-II heterobilayers, including TMDs heterobilayers, as well as heterobilayer of monolayer TMD and hexagonal boron arsenide (BAs). We found that the form and strength of interlayer hopping for the valley electrons hosted by the monolayer building block are sensitive to the stacking registry. This determines that the electronic structure undergoes either a topologically trivial avoided crossing or a non-trivial topological phase transition upon the band inversion, which is controlled by the atomic registry. We find TMDs/BAs heterobilayers of certain the high symmetry stackings to be quantum spin Hall insulator with large gap upon the electrically controlled band inversion, as a result of the hybridization by interlayer hopping between the spin-valley locked valence band edges in TMD and the BAs conduction band edges. In the non-interacting limit, the double spin degeneracy of BAs leaves an un-hybridized conduction band inside the gap, so the heterobilayer is a spin-valley locked metal instead of a quantum spin Hall insulator. With the Coulomb interaction accounted in the double-layer geometry, the interaction with the hybridization induced electric dipole shifts this un-hybridized conduction band upwards in energy, giving rise to a sizable global quantum spin Hall gap. In the long-period moiré pattern with the spatial variation of local stacking-configurations, the competition between Coulomb interaction and interlayer hopping leads to superstructures of quantum spin Hall insulators and excitonic insulators. These findings are published in 2D Materials 6, 045037 (2019) (publication #5). Objective 3 This objective has been achieved. In type-II heterobilayers of the transition metal dichalcogenides, we have investigated the many-body ground states near the inversion point in the presence of both interlayer hopping and interlayer Coulomb interaction between the electron and hole, and discovered intriguing excitonic effects on the topological band inversion. We show that at certain high symmetry stacking between the layers, near the band inversion point, a rich phase diagram arises from the coexistence and competition of strong Coulomb interaction that favors spontaneous s-wave interlayer electron-hole coherence and a chiral interlayer tunneling that creates/annihilates electron-hole pairs in the p-wave channel only. Through an interlayer bias that tunes the band gap near the inversion point, such heterobilayers can be switched between an exciton superfluid dominated by the Coulomb interaction and hopping dominated topological phases. At a relatively strong dielectric screening, the bias drives transitions from a normal insulator to three nontrivial phases sequentially: (i) excitonic superfluid, (ii) coexistence of quantum anomalous Hall in spin-up and excitonic insulator in spin-down species, and (iii) quantum spin Hall insulator. At weak screening, magnetic order spontaneously develops along with the inter-layer coherence, where the heterobilayer can be gate tuned between (iv) a magnetic excitonic superfluid and (v) a quantum anomalous Hall phase. Remarkably, the topologically distinct phases are connected through spontaneous symmetry breaking without gap closing. The gate switchability, together with the sizable topological gap that can exceed room temperature, points to practical spintronic highways at the electrically reconfigurable topological interfaces. These results are published in Science Advances 5, eaau6120 (2019) (publication #3).
