17302617.label: Major findings and research outcome
17302617.value: (1) We find moiré superlattice in TMDs heterobilayers realize superstructures of nanodot confinements for long-lived interlayer excitons, which can be either electrically or strain tuned from perfect arrays of quantum emitters to excitonic superlattices with giant spin-orbit coupling (SOC). The electric field can invert the spin optical selection rule of the emitter arrays. This unprecedented control arises from the gauge structure imprinted on exciton wave functions by the moiré, which underlies the SOC when hopping couples nanodots into superlattices. We show that the moire hosts complex hopping honeycomb superlattices, where exciton bands feature a Dirac node and two Weyl nodes, connected by spin-momentum–locked topological edge modes (publication #1). (2) In WSe2/BAs heterobilayer, when the type II band alignment gets inverted in an electric field, we find the hybridization by interlayer hopping between the spin-valley locked valence band edges in TMD and the BAs conduction band edges leads to a stacking-configuration dependent topological band inversion in the presence of strong Coulomb interaction. In the non-interacting limit, the double spin degeneracy of BAs leaves an un-hybridized conduction band inside the gap, so the heterobilayer is a spin-valley locked metal instead of an insulator. With the Coulomb interaction accounted in the double-layer geometry, the interaction with the hybridization induced electric dipole shifts this un-hybridized conduction band upwards in energy, allowing a sizable quantum spin Hall gap. In the long-period moiré pattern with the spatial variation of local stacking-configurations, the competition between Coulomb interaction and interlayer hopping leads to superstructures of excitonic insulators and quantum spin Hall insulators that can possibly survive room temperature (publication #5). (3) We show that heterobilayers of TMDs can be tuned through interlayer bias between an exciton superfluid, a quantum anomalous Hall insulator, and a QSH insulator. The tunability between these distinct phases results from the competition of Coulomb interaction with the interlayer quantum tunneling that has a chiral form in valley semiconductors. Our findings point to exciting opportunities for harnessing both protected topological edge channels and bulk superfluidity in an electrically configurable platform (publication #3). (4) Together with experimental collaborators, we also reported the experimental evidence of interlayer valley excitons trapped in a moiré potential in MoSe2/WSe2 heterobilayers (publication #4). Our collaboration with McGill group also demonstrated using first principle calculations the idea of a long-period 1D moire pattern of graphene on hBN for realizing high-density arrays of 1D topological helical channels (publication #2)

17302617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17302617.value: Findings of this project have pointed to an interesting directions for further development of the research. We have shown that the moiré in heterobilayer transition metal dichalcogenides realizes superlattice potential for the interlayer excitons which have long population lifetime and valley lifetime, but at the same time is coupled to photon. In the moire superlattice potential, these interlayer excitons have a unique spin-dependent complex hopping, leading to giant spin-orbit splitting in the exciton mini-bands. This has provided an exciting platform to explore many-body phenomena of the bosonic interlayer excitons with their strong dipole interactions due to the permanent electric dipole. A phenomenon that we plan to look into is the superfluid to Mott insulator transition of the excitons in the moire superlattice.

17302617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17302617.value: Atomically thin 2D crystals and their layered heterostructures have opened up exciting new possibilities for exploring fundamental physics and device applications. In the van der Waals bond heterostructures, the small mismatch in lattice constants and in crystalline orientations between the building blocks leads to the formation of Moire pattern where interlayer atomic registry varies from place to place. In long-wavelength Moire pattern, the electronic structure at local region with length smaller than the Moire period approximates that of the corresponding lattice-matched bilayer, but has local-to-local variations in the long range, leads to the formation of lateral superlattice with a nanoscale periodicity. This is a unique aspect of van der Waals heterostructures, which has not been available in conventional semiconductor heterojunctions. In this theoretical project, we have explored electronic, optical and topological properties in such Moire superlattices. We discovered novel Moire superlattice effects on excitons and their optical properties in heterobilayer transition metal dichalcogenides with the type-II band alignment, which makes possible moire-defined arrays of excitonic quantum emitters, as well as excitonic superlattice with intrinsic spin-orbit coupling. In heterobilayers of inverted (broken) band gap, we investigated topological band inversions, and discovered a rich phase diagram arising from the competition of the interlayer quantum tunneling and the interlayer electron-hole Coulomb interaction, where interlayer bias can tune the bilayer from topological phases such as quantum spin Hall and quantum anomalous Hall to excitonic superfluid. In the long-wavelength moire superlattice, the stacking registry dependence of the interlayer hopping, combined with the spatial variation of the registry in the moire, can lead to superstructures consisting of alternating spatial regions in different phases.

17302817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17302817.value: 針對生物靶標進行大規模化學分子庫篩選是生物醫學研究和藥物發現中最重要的研究手段之一。其中通過在分子模塊之間採用可逆化學反應，動態組合分子庫（DCL）已經成為發現蛋白質配體和藥物候選物的有效工具。然而，DCL的應用受到分子庫多樣性的限制，大多數的分子庫只有不到100種化合物，已經成為DCL進一步發展的嚴重障礙。當今迫切需要能夠進行大規模DCL分子庫合成和篩选的新方法。DNA編碼分子庫（DEL）是近年來新興的一種前沿化學分子庫合成與篩選方法。由於DNA分子的高編碼能力，DEL中可以包含數億甚至數十億的化合物。 DEL已經在實際研究中得到了應用，對各種生物靶標的選擇產生了許多新型配體。同時DEL已經被製藥公司廣泛應用於新藥發現研究之中。因此，將DNA編碼的策略引入DCL可能是一個有希望的解決傳統DCL低多樣性的一種有效策略。 在本研究項目中，我們將開發新的DNA編碼動態庫（DEDL）方法，結合DCL和DEL的優點，實現大規模動態分子庫的構建。更為重要的是，由於化學分子庫的真正科學價值是針對生物和藥物的選擇，因此我們將採用DEDL分子庫針對於具有高生物學和醫學意義的靶標進行篩選。本項目提出的研究包括三個階段。首先，我們將開發單結構單元展示DEDL方法，第二，我們將進一步開發雙結構單元展示DEDL方法，用於合成含有數百萬種化合物的DEDL。最後，我們將針對一系列生物靶標進行這些化合物庫的篩選，旨在發現新的配體和候選藥物用於未來進一步的研究。此外，我們將利用最近在本實驗室開發的一種新的分子庫篩選新方法，以使DEDL能夠對以前難以處理的目標，為分子庫的合成和篩選提供了強大的工具。我們預計DEDL還將適用於許多其他重要目標，從而在生物醫學研究和藥物發現中得到廣泛應用。

17302817.label: Realisation of objectives
17302817.value: For the four objectives of this project, we have achieved all of them and exceeded the original goals on several aspects. 1) We have achieved Objective 1, the development of single-display DNA-encoded dynamic library (sd-DEDL) method. The methodology development and library synthesis have been completed, and we have applied the method in the selections of protein targets including streptavidin, carbonic anhydrase 2 and 12, and estrogen receptor. 2) We have achieved Objective 2, the development of double-display DNA-encoded dynamic library (dd-DEDL) method. The methodology development and library synthesis have been completed, and we have applied the method in the selections of many protein targets and novel ligands/inhibitors have been identified. 3) We have achieved Objective 3, the preparation of million-compound-scale DEDL libraries. As a matter of fact, our DEDL libraries have already reached ~30-million-compound-scale, and these libraries are being used in Objectives 1 and 2 to interrogate the protein targets. 4) For Objective 4, the library selection against various protein targets, we have selected the DEDLs against ~30 different proteins, including the ones initially proposed. Some of the selection results have already been published along with the results from Objectives 2 and 3.

17302817.label: Major findings and research outcome
17302817.value: Dynamic combinatorial library (DCL) is a powerful tool for ligand discovery in biomedical research; however, the development and applications of DCL have been significantly hampered by the low chemical diversity due to the lack of methods to resolve large libraries. Recently, the concept of DNA encoding has been employed in DCL to create DNA-encoded dynamic libraries (DEDLs) to address this issue. In 2015, we reported the initial concept of DEDL. During the research of this project, we further developed the 2nd and 3rd generations of DNA-encoded dynamic library (DEDL) methods. The 2nd generation (published in 2018; JACS) realized the synthesis and selection of large-scale dynamic libraries. In the 3rd generation (published in 2020; ACIE), we report a novel anchor-directed DEDL approach that can identify full ligand structures, instead of individual fragments, from large-scale DEDLs. Moreover, this method is able to convert the unbiased, “general purpose” libraries to “focused” ones targeting specific protein classes. Furthermore, in a 2021 publication (Nat. Chem.), we showed that the DEDL approach has facilitated the direct on-cell selection of DELs against endogenous membrane proteins. In addition, we optimized the DEDL technique by using a different photo-crosslinker (published in 2020; BBRC) and reported more applications of these methods (published in 2021; BMC). All together, these research outcomes have advanced the DEL technology and provided a set of tools for drug discovery or probe development in chemical biology research.

17302817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17302817.value: Currently, we are developing the 4th generation DEDL, aiming to eliminate not only fragment linking (the 1st and 2nd generations), but also the need for a known ligand (the 2nd and 3rd generations)in library synthesis. Furthermore, we also aim to develop the DEDL technique to be amendable to more complex biological targets, such as live cells (without a designated target), protein complexes, and organoids.

17302817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17302817.value: In the past two decades, DNA-encoded Chemical library (DEL) has emerged and become a major technology platform for ligand discovery in drug discovery as well as in chemical biology research. Although based on a simple concept, i.e., encoding each compound with a unique DNA tag in a combinatorial chemical library, DEL has proven to be a powerful tool to interrogate biological targets by accessing vast chemical space at a fraction of the cost of traditional high throughput screening (HTS). Today, DELs have been adopted by nearly all major pharmaceutical companies and are also gaining momentums in academia. This project merges a classic chemical technology Dynamic Combinatorial Library (DCL) with DEL and has created a novel technique to interrogate biological targets for drug discovery. The ability to perform library selections against soluble proteins in their native environment may be further exploited to discover chemical entities with higher biological relevance and therapeutic significance.

17303017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17303017.value: Water is essential to the well-being of natural environment and human society. River flow is a major source of water resources, and has undergone marked changes in most large watersheds worldwide. It is imperative to understand long-term river flow variability and the key driving factors for global sustainable development. However, modern gauge records are generally short and inadequate for the investigation of natural river flow variability and the relative contribution of climate change and human disruption on recent flow anomalies. This is particularly the case for the Yangtze River and the Yellow River, the two Mother Rivers of China. Tree-rings are a valuable source for understanding hydroclimate variability over the past few centuries to millennia. Tree-rings are widely distributed in the Yangtze and Yellow river watersheds, but have not been employed properly to study long-term flow variability of the two rivers. In this project we will employ tree-rings to investigate the middle Yangtze and Yellow river flow variability over the past millennium through the development of large-scale, multi-species tree ring network in the two watersheds. Tree-rings will be used to develop annually resolved flow reconstructions, while other high-resolution proxy records from speleothems, lake sediments, and historical archives will be used to verify the reconstructions independently. The reconstructions will be analyzed for perceiving the characteristics of long-term river flow and the major forcing factors. They will also be used for assessing whether recent flow trends and variability are unprecedented from a millennial perspective, and the relative contribution of climate change and human disruption on recent flow anomalies. Our project will be the first integrated research that aims at revealing long-term variations of the mainstream Yangtze and Yellow river flow and their major driving factors over the past millennium. It will allow the characterization of the preferred timescale, duration, and magnitude of flow anomalies and their response to natural and anthropogenic forcings. It will also provide the much-needed long-term perspective necessary to detect and attribute recent flow anomalies. Moreover, the flow reconstructions will provide a testing and validation target for improving hydroclimate models, an effort that will lead to more reliable drought and flow prediction for better water resources management in the two largest river watersheds of China. 水是自然環境和人類社會不可或缺的資源。河川徑流是水資源的一個重要來源，但全球範圍內主要流域的河川徑流已經發生了顯著改變。為了實現可持續發展，必須認知和理解河川徑流的長期變化特征及其主要驅動因素。然而，現代器測資料短缺，不足以理解自然狀態下河川徑流的變化特征以及自然和人文因素對近期徑流變化的相對貢獻。這一問題在中國的兩條母親河--長江和黃河--尤為突出。 樹木年輪是理解過去千百年水文氣候變化的重要手段。樹輪在長江、黃河流域分布廣泛，但還沒被很好地用以研究兩條河流的長期徑流變化。此項目將在這兩個流域建立大範圍、多樹種的年輪網絡，並在此基礎上重建長江、黃河中遊徑流過去千年的變化特征。我們將利用樹輪重建徑流的逐年變化，然後利用石筍、湖泊沈積、歷史文獻等高精度代用指標對徑流重建進行獨立驗證。重建結果將被用以分析徑流長期變化特征以及主要驅動因素，近期徑流變化是否仍在歷史時期波動範圍內，以及氣候變化和人類活動對近期徑流變化的相對貢獻。 此項目為首次對長江、黃河幹流徑流過去千年變化特征及其驅動因素進行集成研究。項目的完成將揭示兩條河流徑流變化的典型時間尺度，持續時間、強度範圍、以及近期對自然和人文因素的響應特征。研究結果將提供急需的徑流長期變化數據，以便評估近期徑流變化是否異常，並為利用水文氣候模型模擬和預測徑流變化提供可靠的驗證信息。此項目的完成將有助於提高中國長江、黃河兩大河流流域的水資源管理。

17303017.label: Realisation of objectives
17303017.value: We have achieved the five objectives outlined in the proposal of the project. Specifically: 1. Develop large-scale, multi-species tree-ring network in the Yangtze and Yellow river basins for flow reconstruction. From the start of the project on Jan 2018 till the outbreak of Covid-19 in November 2019, we conducted three field trips in order to collect tree-ring samples for the development of a large-scale, multi-species tree-ring network. During the trips we newly collected samples from four sites in Yunnan province and eight sites in Sichuan province. We could not collect more samples due to the close of the border between HK and mainland China thereafter. Thankfully, we obtained 11 sites of tree-ring data from mainland collaborators, including five sites from Sichuan province and six sites from Qinghai province. Together with our previous collection, we have built a tree-ring network totaling 159 sites, including 81 sites in the Yangtze River basin and 78 sites in the Yellow River basin. We have identified and collected over 18 tree species that are long-lived and suitable for tree-ring studies in the region, such as Abies fargesii, Abies georgei, Fokienia hodginsii, Juniperus tibetica, Picea likiangensis, Pinus fenzeliana, Sabina przewalskii, and Tsuga chinensis. All the samples were properly prepared and cross-dated with conventional dendrochronological techniques. Ring-widths were measured to 0.001 mm precision using a Velmex measuring system. The raw series were conservatively standardized in order to remove biological growth trends that are unrelated to climate. The standardized series were merged to develop robust mean chronology for each site, which was retained for subsequent hydroclimatic reconstructions. The statistics indicate that most of the tree-ring chronologies cover the past 200-1500 years, with the longest covering the past 2100 years. These data provide a solid basis for the study of long-term climate and river flow change in the two river basins. 2. Reconstruct the middle Yangtze and Yellow river flow for the past millennium from tree-rings, and verify the reconstructions with other independent proxy records from each basin. We have collected monthly gauged flow records at Yichang and Shanxian station in the middle of the Yangtze and Yellow river, respectively. The Yichang records started from April 1877. Since the first major dam (i.e., Gezhouba Dam) on the upper Yangtze River was completed in December 1988, there were 112 years of natural flow records that were used for regression model development. Likewise, modern Yellow River gauge records started in May 1919. Considering that the first major dam (i.e., Liujiaxia Dam) on the upstream of the Yellow River was completed in October 1968, we used the Shanxian gauge records from 1919-1968 for regression model development. We performed monthly to seasonal correlation analysis between tree-ring and river flow records, and found that tree-rings in the Yangtze river basin are most sensitive to warm season (May-October) river flow, while those in the Yellow river basin are most sensitive to river flow of a hydrological year from prior October to current September. Therefore, we reconstructed the middle Yangtze River flow in current May to October and Yellow River flow from prior October to current September. A nested Principle Components analysis was employed for the reconstructions. The regression models were calibrated on the gauged Yichang and Shanxian flow records during 1878-1988 and 1920-1968 respectively, during which the river flow ran naturally without heavy human disruptions. The split sample calibration and verification were used to assess the fidelity of each model. The final flow reconstructions were achieved by splicing all the regressions together, with their mean and variance adjusted to be the same as the most replicated nest. For the Yangtze River, the reconstruction using 81 tree-ring chronologies explains 62% of the actual flow variance back to AD 1500, and 38% variance back to AD 1000. For the Yellow River, the reconstruction using 78 tree-ring chronologies explain 73% of the actual flow variance back to AD 1500, and 41% variance back to AD 800. Paleo-records from historical documents, speleothems, and lake sediments in the two river basins were employed to verify the flow reconstructions independently. Overall, our results indicate that tree-rings can be successfully used to reconstruct the Yangtze and Yellow river flow over 1000-2010 and 800-2010, respectively. 3. Investigate the general features of long-term flow variability for each river, in particular whether recent flow anomalies are unprecedented from a millennial perspective. The tree-ring reconstructions allowed us to examine the general features of the Yangtze and Yellow river flow over the past millennium. We statistically characterized the occurrence of extreme dry and wet periods, and identified the preferred timescale, duration, and magnitude of flow anomalies over the reconstruction period. We performed wavelet analysis to determine the significant periodicities that are intrinsic to the reconstructed flow. Moreover, we assessed whether the observed trends and variability in recent decades are unprecedented over the past millennium, and determined whether there has been a response of river flow to global warming and/or human activities. For the Yangtze River, recent flow are within the range of natural variability during the past millennium. For the Yellow River, recent flow should reach the highest level of the past 1,200 years, but a major reduction was observed mostly due to human disruptions. These results and findings help understand long-term flow variability of the two major rivers at both time and frequency domain. 4. Reveal the linkages between river flow variability and large-scale climate modes at different timescales. On the basis of the reconstructions, we investigated the linkages of Yangtze and Yellow river flow variability with large-scale climate modes. For the Yangtze River, we found that the river flow was mostly influenced by long-term changes in the Asian monsoon and the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO). For the Yellow River, the flow fluctuations varied coherently with the Tibetan Plateau and Northern Hemisphere temperature anomalies, with increased flow during warm periods and vice versa for a reduction. The above records generally show a good coherency with solar radiation record during the past millennium, suggesting that changes in solar radiation may have largely set the pace for the temperature and flow anomalies. Overall, our assessment of the linkages between river flow and large-scale climate modes revealed the response of regional hydroclimate and river flow to both internal and external climate forcings. 5. Assess the relative contribution of natural and anthropogenic forcings on recent flow anomalies by comparing the actual and reconstructed flow during the dam construction era. Large dams and reservoirs have been constructed on both Yangtze and Yellow rivers during the past few decades. Whether recent flow anomalies are due to climate change or human disruption is a major question that awaits critical assessment. For the Yangtze River, we found that human influence on river flow was statistically non-significant, and the river flow reduction since the early twentieth century was mostly caused by natural factors, in particular the weakening of the East Asian monsoon. For the Yellow River, we found that recent flow should have increased to the highest level of the past 1,200 years if there were no human disruption. However, human activities have caused a loss of nearly half of natural flow since the late 1960s and are the main culprit for recent downstream flow reduction. These findings are critical for future water resources management in the two large river basins.

17303017.label: Major findings and research outcome
17303017.value: Under the generous support of this GRF grant, we built a large-scale, multi-species tree-ring network in the Yangtze and Yellow river basins, including 81 tree sites in the Yangtze River basin and 78 sites in the Yellow River basin. These data provided a solid basis for studying long-term hydroclimate and river flow in the two river basins. Based on this network, we reconstructed the Yangtze and Yellow river flow for the past 1,000 and 1,200 years, respectively. With the reconstructions we characterized the occurrence of extreme dry and wet periods, and identified the preferred timescale, duration, and magnitude of flow anomalies over the reconstruction period. For the Yangtze River, we found that river flow was mostly influenced by long-term changes in the Asian monsoon and the El Niño-Southern Oscillation. For the Yellow River, the flow fluctuations varied coherently with the Tibetan Plateau and Northern Hemisphere temperature anomalies, with increased flow during warm periods and vice versa for a reduction. The above records generally show a good coherency with solar radiation record, suggesting that changes in solar radiation may have largely set the pace for the temperature and flow anomalies. Moreover, we assessed whether the observed flow in recent decades are unprecedented over the past millennium, and determined whether there has been a response of river flow to global warming and/or human activities. For the Yangtze River, we found that recent river flow are within the range of millennial natural variability. Human influence on river flow was statistically non-significant, and recent river flow reduction was mostly caused by natural factors, in particular the weakening of the East Asian monsoon. For the Yellow River, recent flow should have increased to the highest level of the past 1,200 years if there were no human disruption. However, human activities have caused a loss of nearly half of natural flow since the late 1960s and are the main culprit for recent flow reduction. These results and findings should help understand long-term flow variability at both time and frequency domain, and are valuable for future water resources management in the two river basins. Our findings about hydroclimate and river flow were reported in seven academic papers published in journals such as Nature Climate Change, Geophysical Research Letters and Climatic Change. In particular, our work about the Yellow river flow published in Geophysical Research Letters was featured by AGU in its publication Eos.

17303017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17303017.value: The tree-ring network developed through this project provides a solid basis for the study of long-term climate change in the Yangtze and Yellow river basins. We will continue to update the network by sampling more tree species and new sites in the next 2-3 years. The updated network will be used to extend our river flow reconstruction for the past fifteen hundred years or so, which will help better understand recent flow anomalies with a longer perspective and identify the preferred timescale, duration, and magnitude of drought occurrence in the basin. Moreover, we will make a comparison with the reconstructed river flow of the Pear River in southern China, which will enable a full understanding of river flow anomalies across China and their responses to various anthropogenic and climatic forcing. We plan to apply for a new grant to support this work in the next round of RGC grant application.

17303017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17303017.value: Recent significant changes in streamflow in the Yangtze and Yellow river basins call for a better understanding of their long-term variability. In this project, we built a large-scale, multi-species tree-ring network in the two river basins and employed it to reconstruct the Yangtze and Yellow river flow for the past millennium. With the reconstructions we characterized the occurrence of extreme dry and wet periods, and identified the preferred timescale, duration, and magnitude of flow anomalies over the reconstruction period. We further assessed whether the observed flow in recent decades are unprecedented over the past millennium, and determined whether there has been a response of river flow to global warming and/or human activities. Overall, this project is the first integrated research that investigated both Yangtze and Yellow river flow millennial variability, which provided the much-needed long-term perspective necessary to detect and attribute recent drought and streamflow anomalies in the basins. Our results should help policy makers and the general public understand long-term changes of basinwide droughts and streamflow, and will help plan for sustainable water resource management, mitigate impacts of floods and droughts, and reduce conflicts among stakeholders.

17303417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17303417.value: Particle physics is the study of fundamental particles, which are basic elements of matter and fundamental force carriers. The Standard Model (SM) of particle physics is a successful theory describing the interactions among fundamental particles. However, the SM raises as many questions as it answers. One of such unsolved key questions is why different fundamental particles have different mass. For example, the heaviest fundamental particle discovered so far, top quark, is 10^5 order of magnitude heavier than an electron. A hypothesis widely accepted is that mass origin of fundamental particles is related to symmetry breaking such as the Electroweak Symmetry Breaking (EWSB), which predicts the existence of a Higgs boson. As a scientific breakthrough in 2012, the Higgs boson was discovered at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC), the world's largest and highest-energy particle accelerator, which is located at the European Organization for Nuclear Research (CERN). It is a great success of particle physics. However, the EWSB is still not fully understood. In the SM, the Higgs boson mass is not stable due to the quadratically divergent corrections at the quantum level. Particle physicists are looking for new physics models beyond the SM which in general provide solutions not only to stabilize the Higgs mass but also to other unsolved problems in the SM. These new physics models have rich signatures in the particle detector at the LHC. The PI proposes a set of searches for those promising new physics models in final states containing top quarks with Run II data at the ATLAS experiment of the LHC. These searches, well motived in both theoretical and experimental point of views, will provide a great potential to explore the unknown world. 粒子物理學研究基本粒子，包括組成物質的最基本元素和它們之間相互作用力的傳播子。粒子物理學的標準模型是一個描述基本粒子之間的相互作用的成功理論。但是標準模型還有很多未能解決的問題，其中一個未解決的關鍵問題是為什麼不同基本粒子具有不同的質量。例如，目前為止發現的最重的基本粒子，頂夸克，比電子重10^5個數量級。廣泛接受的一個假說是基本粒子的質量來源與電弱對稱性破缺有關，而這一過程引入了希格斯玻色子。作為2012年的科學突破，希格斯玻色子在位於歐洲核子中心（CERN）的世界最大和最高能量的大型強子對撞機（LHC）上被發現，粒子物理學取得了巨大的成功。然而，電弱對稱性破缺的機制仍然沒有被完全理解。在標準模型中，由於量子修正引入的平方發散項導致希格斯玻色子質量不穩定。粒子物理學家正在尋找新的物理模型，這些新物理模型一般不僅能夠穩定希格斯粒子的質量， 而且能夠解決一些標準模型中其他未解決的問題。這些新的物理學模型在LHC的粒子探測器中具有豐富的特徵。 PI提出了在LHC的ATLAS實驗中使用Run II數據在包含頂夸克的衰變末態中搜索那些有希望的新物理模型的研究課題。這些研究課題，無論在理論和實驗上都有很好的研究動機，它們具有探索未知的世界的巨大潛力。

17303417.label: Realisation of objectives
17303417.value: 1. Search for beyond Standard Model Neutral Heavy Higgs associate production via final states with top quarks in Run II at the ATLAS. 2. Search for beyond Standard Model Charged Heavy Higgs associate production via final states with top quarks in Run II at the ATLAS. Before we perform the searches for heavy Higgs, we first performed a search for flavour-changing neutral current decays of a top quark into an up-type quark (q=u,c) and the Standard Model Higgs boson, t→Hq. The search is based on a dataset of pp collisions at 13 TeV recorded in 2015 and 2016 with the ATLAS detector at the CERN Large Hadron Collider and corresponds to an integrated luminosity of 36.1 fb^−1. Two complementary analyses are performed that search for top-quark pair events in which one top quark decays into Wb and the other top quark decays into Hq, and target the H→bb¯ and H→τ+τ− decay modes, respectively. The high multiplicity of b-quark jets, or the presence of hadronically decaying τ-leptons, are exploited in the two analyses respectively. Multivariate techniques are used to separate the signal from the background, which is dominated by top-quark pair production. No significant excess of events above the background expectation is found, and 95% CL upper limits on the t→Hq branching ratios are derived. The combination of these searches with ATLAS searches in diphoton and multilepton final states yields observed (expected) 95% CL upper limits on the t→Hc and t→Hu branching ratios of 1.1×10^−3 (8.3×10^−4) and 1.2×10^−3 (8.3×10^−4), respectively. The corresponding combined observed (expected) upper limits on the |λtcH| and |λtuH| couplings are 0.064 (0.055) and 0.066 (0.055), respectively. The paper has been published JHEP (IF: 5.833 (2018), 5.541 (2017); ranking: 5/29 (1/25 excluding reviews) in Physics, Particles and Field). With post-docs and students trained in the above analyses and based on the analysis strategies developed in the a search for four-top-quark production (described in the following), we targets the associated production of a heavy (pseudo)scalar Higgs boson A/H with a top-antitop quark pair with the subsequent decay A/H-->ttbar leading to a 4-top final state. Multivariate techniques are used to enhance the sensitivity of the search in the mass region between 400 and 1000 GeV. We use Full Run 2 (2015+2016+2017+2018) dataset with140 fb^-1 for better sensitivity. The relevant paper will be submitted this summer. 3. Search for vector-like quarks via final states with top quarks in Run II at the ATLAS. We performed a search for pair production of up-type vector-like quarks (T ) with a significantvbranching ratio into a top quark and either a Standard Model Higgs boson or a Z boson is presented. The same analysis is also used to search for four-top-quark production in several new physics scenarios. The search is based on a dataset of pp collisions at 13 TeV recorded in 2015 and 2016 with the ATLAS detector at the CERN Large Hadron Collider and corresponds to an integrated luminosity of 36.1 fb−1. Data are analysed in the lepton+jets final state, characterised by an isolated electron or muon with high transverse momentum, large missing transverse momentum and multiple jets, as well as the jets+Emiss T final state, characterised by multiple jets and large missing transverse momentum. The search exploits the high multiplicity of jets identified as originating from b-quarks, and the presence of boosted, hadronically decaying top quarks and Higgs bosons reconstructed as large-radius jets, characteristic of signal events. No significant excess above the Standard Model expectation is observed, and 95% CL upper limits are set on the production cross sections for the different signal processes considered. These cross-section limits are used to derive lower limits on the mass of a vector-like T quark under several branching ratio hypotheses assuming contributions from T → Wb, Zt, Ht decays. The 95% CL observed lower limits on the T quark mass range between 0.99 TeV and 1.43 TeV for all possible values of the branching ratios into the three decay modes considered, significantly extending the reach beyond that of previous searches. Additionally, upper limits on anomalous four-top- quark production are set in the context of an effective field theory model, as well as in an universal extra dimensions model. The paper has been published in JHEP( IF: 5.833 (2018), 5.541 (2017); ranking: 5/29 (1/25 excluding reviews) in Physics, Particles and Fields). 4. Search for four top quark productions beyond the SM in Run II at the ATLAS. We also performed a search for four-top-quark production. It is based on proton-proton collision data with a center-of-mass energy 13 TeV collected by the ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider during the years 2015 and 2016, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 36.1 fb−1. Data are analyzed in both the single-lepton and opposite-sign dilepton channels, characterized by the presence of one or two isolated electrons or muons with high-transverse momentum and multiple jets. A data- driven method is used to estimate the dominant background from top-quark pair production in association with jets. No significant excess above the Standard Model expectation is observed. The result is combined with the previous same-sign dilepton and multilepton searches carried out by the ATLAS Collaboration and an observed (expected) upper limit of 5.3 (2.1) times the four-top-quark Standard Model cross section is obtained at 95% confidence level. Additionally, an upper limit on the anomalous four-top-quark production cross section is set in the context of an effective field theory model, which has been published in JHEP (IF: 5.833 (2018), 5.541 (2017); ranking: 5/29 (1/25 excluding reviews) in Physics, Particles and Fields)

17303417.label: Major findings and research outcome
17303417.value: Our goal is to search for new physics which provides solutions to the hierarchy problem in the Standard Model. We developed experimental strategies to search for some heavy particles productions predicted in the new physics models including vector like quarks, heavy Higgs and four top quark productions. These productions share a common feature in the final states i.e. containing top quarks. One of the top quarks is required to decay leptonically, while the other top quarks decay hadronically, in order to suppress the hadronic background and benefit from the large branching ratio of hadronic decay mode. Eventually the final states contain one lepton plus multiple (b-tagged) jets and missing transverse momentum. Therefore, some common analysis strategies have been developed and applied. 1. we find no significant excess of events above the Standard Model expectation. 2. we set 95% CL lower limits on the mass of the vector-like T quark which lie between 0.99 TeV and 1.43 TeV depending on the values of the branching ratios into the different decay modes. 3. we set upper limits on the four-top-quark production cross section are set in several new physics scenarios. 4. we employ multivariate techniques to discriminate between the signal and the background on the basis of their different kinematics in different analyses. 5. we derived 95% CL upper limits on the t → Hq branching ratios. 6. for the four-top- quark Standard Model production, an observed (expected) 95% C.L. upper limit on the production cross section of 47 fb (33 fb), corresponding to 5.1 (3.6) times the SM prediction, is obtained.

17303417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17303417.value: Currently, the LHC is carrying out its Phase I upgrade. Our physics data analyses with full ATLAS Run II data are going on. We are also preparing for the ATLAS Phase II muon detector upgrade and physics data analyses for the subsequent Run III, from 2021 to 2023, in which the center-of-mass energy will be increased to 14 TeV, and the delivered integrated luminosity will be increased to 300 fb−1. The relevant research will keep going until we reach the High-Luminosity Run of the LHC after 2025.

17303417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17303417.value: The project is very valuable towards understanding the origin of Electroweak Symmetry Breaking (EWBS) and mass of fundamental particles. The discovery of the Higgs boson in 2012 is a milestone of this global endeavor. However, the mechanism of the EWSB is still not fully understood. In the Standard Model (SM), the Higgs boson mass, which defines the EWSB scale, is not stable due to the quadratically divergent corrections at quantum level. To solve this so-called hierarchy problem, physics beyond the SM is required. These physics models predict the existence of new particles, which are typically heavy and are produced rarely, e.g. vector-like quarks (T ), and heavy Higgs bosons. Searching for these new physics is high-profile research in the field.

17303517.label: Realisation of objectives
17303517.value: We have successfully and productively accomplished all the four goals and objectives of this project. This success was possible because of the recruitment of the highly talented graduate student from mechanical engineering (and interdisciplinary) background and great cooperation from both local (Haimin Yao) and overseas collaborators (Maggie Cusack). Our team has also brought few other collaborators to make sure we have made use of the all the data collected from this project – e.g. we have collaborated with a biomedical expert from The University of Hong Kong (Kelvin Yeung) and an oyster aquaculture expert from Chinese Academy of Science (Zinu Yu). The students who has worked for this project had great access to work in three different institutions, the University of Hong Kong, Polytechnic University of Hong Kong and South China Institute of Oceanology – as a result we have accomplished more than what was promised to deliver for this project – e.g. published 10 high quality papers (all attached with this report) and trained over three graduate students (also listed here). One of the major outcomes of this project is interdisciplinary (science and engineering) and comparative (three different species) approach adapted to achieve all the four objectives. The listed papers in this report shows such interdisciplinary and inter-institutional collaboration. Here, we will briefly explain how we have accomplished those four objectives. Objective 1 (Crystal orientation in oyster shells – modulating effect of ocean acidification): This is one of the key and major objectives of this project. Our graduated student (now working as Associate Professor in mainland China), Dr Yuan Meng – served as a backbone for the execution of this project. She has come with mechanical engineering background and then we have trained her basic skills required for shell structural analysis and also to run ocean acidification experiments. She has quickly learned those biological skills. Immediately, she had run ocean acidification experiments to collect shell samples of the two oyster species. Then, she has employed variety of material analysis tools, e.g. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) – to study crystal orientation in oyster shells of two different species. In no time, she has become a local expert in EBSD analysis – thanks to her visit to UK (University of Glasgow to work with Prof Maggie and Dr Susan) for few weeks to learn this technique. As a result, she has published FOUR high quality papers (Meng et al., 2019a, 2019b, 2019a and 2019b) and also successfully defended her PhD thesis in 2019. Objective 2 (oyster shell proteomics): Realization of this objective is one of the difficult part of this project. This is because, extraction of adequate amount of proteins from oysters shells which is having only less than 5% of its volume, especially from tiny early life stages. Therefore, we are forced to recruit another graduate student, Miss Alessia Cairini in 2018, using RGC-HKPF support, to carry out this task. She has made good progress and developed a methodology to isolate adequate amount of proteins from oyster shells using unique protocol – which is under preparation for publication. Moreover, our other graduate student, Miss Kanmani Rajan, was able to use this protocol and isolated proteins from oyster shells to study ocean acidification effects on oyster shell proteomics (find attached PhD thesis chapter). These two drafted manuscripts will be published somewhere soon. Objectives 3 and 4: These two objectives are highly interlinked and heavily dependent on tools borrowed from mechanical engineering and our collaborator Dr Haimin Yao. Our team, led by graduate student (Yuan Meng), has successfully accomplished these two objectives and developed Finite Element Analysis (FEA) models to project oyster shell mechanical properties. These results have also been published (Meng et al 2019a). Indeed, this model now has been widely used in several related research field.

17303517.label: Major findings and research outcome
17303517.value: Finding 1 (Crystal Growth & Designs, 2018b, Biofouling 2019): Shells of oyster species belonging to the genus Crassostrea have similar shell micro-structural features comprising well-ordered calcite folia. However, the mechanical strengths of folia differ dramatically between two closely-related species. Detailed analyses of shell structural and mechanical features support the hypothesis that crystallographic interdigitations confer elevated mechanical strength in C. hongkongensis oyster shells compared to C. angulata shells. The innovative combination of material science techniques and mechanical modelling approach developed in this study, that integrated electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) data into finite element analysis (FEA) helped us to model systems to investigate the relationship between crystallography and mechanical behavior (Interface, 2018). The relationships between oyster shell structure, crystallography and mechanical properties provide an insightful context in which to consider the likely fate of these two species in future climate change scenarios. Finding 2 (Biogeosciences 2018a, Marine Pollution Bulletin 2019b): Shells produced by marine organisms under ocean acidification (OA) are expected to be corroded with disorganized or impaired crystal orientation or microstructures with reduced mechanical strength (Marine Environmental Research 2020, 2021a). We have tested this hypothesis using two oyster species that tend to make shells with different mechanical and structural features. Our comparative study revealed bottom-up deterioration induced by OA on oyster shells, especially in their early juvenile life stage. This knowledge is critical to forecast the survival and production of edible oysters in future ocean. Finding 3: We have identified a novel methodology to isolate organic matrix proteins from shells of the two oyster species (this methodology report is under the process of publication). Also we have characterized those shell proteins and identified their functional role in shell making process using variety of modern proteomics tools (see the attached PhD thesis report of Dr Kanmani Rajan). These results have implications on understanding progression of oyster shell formation in future oceans with high variability in OA (Frontiers in Mar Science 2021, Marine Environmental Research 2020). Overall outcome: 1) Besides 10 publications, two PhD thesis report have been completed; 2) A post doc was trained, Dr Yuan Meng, from 2019-2020. 3) The result has been used to develop hypothesis for a new RGC-GRF proposal to study crystal orientation rotating proteins. 4) The project has been effectively used to strengthen our interdisciplinary and interinstitutional collaborations, e.g. authors listed in almost all the 10 papers published from this project are showing such collaboration.

17303517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17303517.value: The outcome of this project leads us to advance our 1) biomaterial research, 2) propose two major grant proposals, and 3) further strengthened our interdisciplinary and inter-institutional collaboration. Briefly, • Established “Hong Kong Oyster Hatchery and Innovation Research Unit (HKO-HIRU)” to enhance the scientific value of oysters as cultural heritage, for biomedical inspiration and as an environmental model through the development of sustainable oyster aquaculture technologies; • Now we are in the process of developing a collaborative research fund (CRF) proposal to identify the interaction between shell calcification and biomechanics of oyster shells in response to climate change – which is expected to develop oyster-derived biostructures as adhesive construction materials, pollutant adsorbents and scaffolds for bone regeneration. • Impact case study and knowledge exchange activities: This project has helped us to move forward with knowledge exchange related activities, i.e. we are currently investigating the significance of community engagement for the sustainability of local oyster aquaculture under climate change – and use this new approach to transfer technology from academics to stakeholders to provide integrated solutions to manage the impacts of climate change.

17303517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17303517.value: Edible oysters build structurally complex shells to defend predators using CaCO3 crystals through highly controlled mineralization process. However, they are now facing a novel threat from the human-carbon dioxide induced ocean acidification (OA) process – which is not only slow down the mineralization rate but also impair shells made through this process. This inability by oysters to form their protective shell with proper structure and mechanical features in current and future oceans with high-human carbon dioxide is a major threat to oysters and thus, global seafood security. This is a serious issue for China, which is accounting >84% of global production. Therefore, this project has investigated how oysters arrange crystals to make error free microstructure under OA – especially we were concerned about the oyster species that produce a mechanically weaker shell, the Portuguese oysters. With tools borrowed from mechanical engineering, we have revealed the novel relationship between crystal orientation and mechanical properties in oysters. Also, we have successfully integrated the investigated oyster shell microstructural features with the ultimate mechanical strength through finite element analysis models. Now this model has been widely used to project oyster shell structural and mechanical features under various projected climate change scenarios around the world.

17303617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17303617.value: Biocompatible organic transformations enable native protein to be conjugated with other moieties, which have found many applications in biomedical research and biologic-based drug discovery. These bioconjugation methods involve the reaction taking place selectively at specific nucleophilic side chains of the amino acids present in proteins in aqueous solution. The thiol group of the cysteine residue and the amino group of the lysine and N-terminus are the most common sites for native protein bioconjugation. For instance, the NHS ester chemistry has been widely used to modify native proteins at the Lys sites, but this method presents several limitations, such as cross-reactivity and proneness to hydrolysis. In an effort to search for alternative Lys-specific methods for native protein bioconjugation that feature simple operation, robustness, high chemoselectivity, and usage of non-hydrolysable reagents, we recently developed a chemoselective amine bioconjugation via phthalimidine formation, termed PT ligation. We found that ortho-phthalaldehyde (OPA) and its derivatives could rapidly react chemoselectively with amino groups, such as ε-amine of lysine and N-terminus, of peptides and proteins under physiological conditions (e.g., PBS buffer, pH 7.2) via phthalimidines formation. In the proposed study, we will continue these efforts by further developing and extending the repertoire of PT ligation in native protein bioconjugation. We will address several aspects in this project: (1) development of the versatile synthesis of bi-functional OPA derivatives, (2) exploration of the structure-activity relationship of OPA derivatives toward amine reaction and ligand-guided Lys site-specific modification, and (3) application of PT ligation in the synthesis of cyclic peptides and bi-cyclic peptides. The success of this project will facilitate the application of PT ligation for wider use, including the generation of peptidomimetics, polyethylene glycol (PEG)-protein conjugate drugs, antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), carbohydrate-protein conjugate vaccines, fluorescence-labeled proteins, and so on. 具有生物相容性的有機化學反應可以用來合成在生物醫學和藥物發現中廣泛應用的蛋白質綴合物。這些生物偶聯的辦法通常是利用蛋白質氨基酸的特定親核性側鏈在水溶液裡選擇性地發生化學反應。 半胱氨酸殘基的巰基、 賴氨酸的氨基和N-末端氨基是最常見的蛋白質生物偶聯位點。NHS酯化學是廣泛用於修飾天然蛋白質賴氨酸的氨基位點，但這種方法存在一些局限性，如此反應的交叉反應性和NHS酯傾向於水解。為了開發新型的、更加簡潔高效的蛋白質生物偶聯辦法， 我們發現鄰苯二甲醛（OPA）及其衍生物可以快速地、特異性地在生理條件下（例如，pH7.2 的PBS緩衝液）與賴氨酸的ε-胺和N-末端氨基進行反應， 我們稱之為PT連接法。在此研究中，我們在此基礎上將繼續開展深入性擴展性的研究工作， 包括以下方面的研究 （1）開發雙功能 性OPA衍生物；（2）探索OPA衍生物的結構 對其和氨基反應活性的影響，以及開發配體引導的定點特異性修飾；（3）研究PT連接在環肽和雙環肽合成中的應用。該項目的成功將有助於PT連接法的廣泛應用，包括產生肽模擬物，聚乙二醇 - 蛋白質的綴合物藥物，抗體 - 藥物偶聯物（ADCs），碳水化合物 - 蛋白質綴合物 等。

17303617.label: Realisation of objectives
17303617.value: Re. objective 1: To develop the versatile synthesis of bi-functional OPA derivatives We have successfully developed synthetic strategies to prepare several types of bi-functional OPA linkers. Firstly, we prepared three OPA-alkyne derivatives, including ether-linked, C-linked and amine-linked, among which the OPA-amine-alkyne showed the best solubility in the aqueous buffer for protein bioconjugation. We continued to use the OPA-amine-alkyne for protein profiling in bacteria. This work was published in Biochemistry (2020, 59, 175-178). Secondly, we have prepared several OPA-N-maleimide bi-functional linker, and we studied and compared their utilities for the preparation of antibody-drug conjugation. With Kadcyla as the example, OPA-maleimide connector showed enhanced performance superior to the commercial SMCC connector, in term of bioconjugation efficiency and protein aggregation. Thus, OPA chemistry will provide a new strategy for protein bioconjugation and ADC synthesis. A joint patent was filed together with Wuxi Biologics “Ortho-phthalaldehyde containing linkers and use for preparation of antibody-drug conjugate PCT/CN2018/117257”. Re. objective 2: To explore the structure-activity relationship of OPA derivatives toward the amine reaction and ligand-guided Lys site-specific modification. We have synthesized substituted OPA derivatives and thiophene dialdehyde derivative as proposed. From our studies, thiophene dialdehyde showed much less reactivity towards amine reaction, which shows the promise for the ligand-guided Lys site-specific modification. This new chemistry has been used for protein stapling and phage displayed peptide cyclization. A manuscript is under preparation. Re. objective 3: To apply PT ligation in the synthesis of cyclic peptides and bi-cyclic peptides Amino acid derived OPA analogues have been synthesized and effective OPA protecting group have been identified. With these building blocks, we have applied PT ligation chemistry for the synthesis of cyclic peptides. Five model cyclic peptides have been successfully prepared. In addition, as a serendipity finding, we have found that ortho-phthalaldehyde (OPA) can react with the lysine/N-terminus and cysteine within one unprotected peptide sequence effectively to form the isoindole-bridged cyclic peptides. This reaction is carried out in the aqueous buffer and features tolerance of diverse functionalities, rapid and clean transformation, and operational simplicity. Moreover, OPA peptide cyclization can also be combined with native chemical ligation-mediated cyclization to generate bicyclic peptides. This work was published in J. Am. Chem. Soc. (2019, 141, 12274-12279).

17303617.label: Major findings and research outcome
17303617.value: Development of effective chemical methods for peptides/proteins labeling and modification is currently being actively pursued in the field of chemical biology, biochemistry, medicinal chemistry and so on, which is also a daunting task, considering the diverse functional groups present in native peptides and proteins. Our laboratory has discovered the new reactivity of ortho-phthalaldehyde (OPA) which can be used for amine-specific peptide/protein modifications and bioconjugations, termed PT ligation or OPA bioconjugation. This method features simple operation, robustness, high chemoselectivity and usage of non-hydrolysable reagent. Based on the OPA bioconjugation, we have developed bi-functional OPA derivatives which can be used for protein profiling and generating antibody-drug conjugates. This method has been widely adopted by the community now, such as for protein crosslinking, protein polymer conjugation, protein-DNA conjugation and so on. In addition, we have identified another new reactivity of OPA, which can react with the lysine/N-terminus and cysteine within one unprotected peptide sequence effectively to form the isoindole-bridged cyclic peptides, termed OPA-thiol-amine cyclization. This OPA cyclization is carried out in the aqueous buffer and features tolerance of diverse functionalities, rapid and clean transformation, and operational simplicity. In addition, we have developed an OPA derivative, which can be used for native protein stapling and phage displayed peptide cyclization. OPA was first synthesized in 1887 by Gautier. Our findings bring a renaissance to the OPA chemistry. The studies in this project will facilitate and promote the OPA chemistry for wider applications in protein chemistry.

17303617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17303617.value: The successful completion of this project has laid the solid foundation for establishing the new OPA chemistry for peptide/protein modification and bioconjugation. Our future efforts will be directed for the applications in two areas. Firstly, we will apply the OPA cyclization method to build a cyclic peptide library for drug screening. Secondly, we will apply the OPA bioconjugation for generating protein-drug conjugate, protein-carbohydrate conjugate and so on to develop new therapeutic biologics.

17303617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17303617.value: We have developed the new chemistry of OPA bioconjugation and OPA cyclization for modifying peptides and proteins. Our chemistry features operational simplicity, robustness, high chemoselectivity and fast kinetics. These two methods have promising applications for developing new biomolecules with therapeutic applications.

17303717.label: Realisation of objectives
17303717.value: The experiment was successfully completed at RIKEN with 14O beam on solid hydrogen target. Analysis on the beam identification, energy calibration, extraction of desirable observables was done. Simulations were built and performed to extract the Bp and flight length functions of SAMURAI magnet. We also debugged the error in the FDC2 analysis for the SAMURAI international collaboration group including 1) HV connection problem of the two layers of FDC2 v2v2' and the corresponding modification on analysis code for the FDC2 tracking; 2) Corrections on some misconnection channels in FDC2. We obtained particle identification of the fragments in SAMURAI. The 13O and 13N PID gates contained some backgrounds and the associated uncertainties were evaluated. The one-nucleon removal residues (13N and 13O) could be clearly identified with offline improvement on the A/Q resolution. We also found the magnetic field was 2%-3% stronger than expected (~1.5T). We successfully extracted the 14O(p,2p)13N and 14O(p,pn)13O one-nucleon removal cross sections and made first comparison with theoretical predictions. The momentum distributions were also extracted. However, the momentum resolution estimated with the 14O beam is about 3 times worse than expected (1/230 vs 1/700). The worse momentum resolution was found due to the unexpected liquefied water in the entrance and exist windows of the solid hydrogen target chamber. We evaluated the water thickness, the target thickness and the target thickness error using the beam momentum distribution measured by SAMURAI with target and empty target run. Therefore, the analysis became much more complicated than expected and took much longer time. We expect to finalize the data analysis in a few months. On the other hand, the theoretical calculations of cross sections and momentum distribution were made and compared to our preliminary analysis results for physics interpretation. The agreement between data and model prediction is reasonable, which provides important clarification on the reaction mechanism. The publication is in preparation which would be submitted to Physical Review C in 2022. The preliminary result was only presented in the SAMURAI international collaboration meetings. The main reason this preliminary result is not presented in any conferences is because many conferences in our field are postponed or cancelled due to COVID pandemic.

17303717.label: Major findings and research outcome
17303717.value: We measured the cross sections and momentum distributions from proton-induced knockout reaction of exotic nuclei at intermediate energies for the first time. This experimental data using proton target 14O(p,pn) and 14O(p,2p) at 100MeV/u are essential to verify if such this model can qualitatively describe the reaction mechanism at stake. Our very preliminary data shows asymmetric parallel momentum distribution (P//) of the residual nuclei, with shape characterized by a steep fall-off on the high momentum side and a long-ranged tail on the low momentum side. This could be described by the new calculations based on the distorted-wave impulse approximation (DWIA) which predicts the large asymmetric P// momentum distribution. This asymmetry is understood as the results from the phase volume effects in the energy and momentum conservation (high momentum side), and the momentum shift of the outgoing two nucleons inside an attractive potential caused by the residual nucleus (low momentum side). The data validates the reaction mechanism described by DWIA and support this reaction framework as well-established tool to extract reliable nuclear structure information.

17303717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17303717.value: The result would serve as clarification of the reaction mechanisms at intermediate energies which is essential to resolve the long-standing inconsistency between transfer and knockout reactions and provide well-estabished framework to extract reliable nuclear structure information for exotic nuclei in future experiments.

17303717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17303717.value: The origin of such a discrepancy between the spectroscopic factors extracted from transfer and knockout reactions is not clear. Such an intriguing puzzle must be solved in order to achieve a unified description of the nature of correlations and the underlying physics in nuclei with extreme isospin asymmetry. The incompatibility of different reaction techniques tends to suggest that our understanding of the underlying reaction mechanism is incomplete. Our data in this work 14O(p,pn) and 14O(p,2p) at 100 MeV/u at RIKEN (Japan), in addition with the proton and neutron-transfer measurements of 14O(d,3He) and 14O(d,t) data from the experiment performed at GANIL (France) and the inclusive and exclusive knockout measurements using Be/C targets performed at NSCL (USA) and RCNP (Japan), respectively, and (p,pn) & (p,2p) at 500-700 MeV/u at GSI (Germany) on the same nucleus 14O, will represent a benchmark for direct nuclear reaction mechanisms and target-dependence studies involving deeply-bound nucleons. Particularly our data in this work could pin point the origin of the long-standing puzzle of the large asymmetry of momentum distributions and provide clear support to the DWIA reaction model. This establishes an essential reaction framework for reliable extraction of structure information in exotic nuclei.

17303917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17303917.value: The proposed project is an integrated experimental and numerical study of the mechanical behavior of rocks under compression. It is motivated by the demand for realistic modelling of the progressive degradation of material integrity together with the influence of inherent texture, fabric, and mineralogical composition on the rock response. The main objective is to develop a calibrated 3D grain-based modelling (GBM) procedure based on the discrete element method (DEM) for simulating rock behaviour. The 3D models will be made up of interlocking polyhedrons (grains) that in turn are composed of particles “glued” together. Breakages along grain boundaries and within grains are allowed to resemble real rock deformation processes. The 3D models will take into account actual grain size distribution, grain shape, mineralogical composition, as well as the fabric. Different strength and stiffness properties will be assigned to the minerals and mineral boundaries. The 3D GBM will be calibrated against three major plutonic rock types in Hong Kong. Micro-mechanical parameters to be calibrated will be divided into three classes based on their relevance to the macroscopic measureable parameters. The calibration will be supported by results obtained from thin section examination, uniaxial loading tests (strength and modulus; cracking and failure mode revealed from high-speed imaging) and triaxial tests (failure envelope) conducted on rock specimens. We will also monitor acoustic emission (AE) signals associated with micro-cracking events, which will provide a quantitative assessment of the spatial and temporal evolution of the density and distribution of various crack types to calibrate the model. Currently, micro-cracking attributes revealed from AE signals are seldom used to calibrate numerical models. Using the developed 3D GBM, identical calibrated numerical specimens can be re-tested under different loading conditions, which is impossible in laboratory test. The material properties can be investigated without any influence from the initial sample preparation method. The salient factors affecting the mechanical and deformation behaviour of rocks under loading (and to what extent) can be isolated and studied. This approach has a strong potential for investigating other plutonic rock types, which have not been directly calibrated. The applicability of this numerical approach will be demonstrated at the final stage of the project by examining the influence of special geological features and weathering grades on fracturing, deformation and failure processes of rocks. This research outcome can be used in the future to assist interpretation of geological deformation features in the study of geodynamics and structural geology, etc. 研究項目採用數值模擬與室內試驗相結合的方法，探究壓縮條件下岩石強度性質劣化及細觀結構損傷破碎過程，並揭示該過程中岩石內部結構、構造和礦物成分對其宏觀力學性質的影響。 數值模擬主要基於離散元方法，以香港的三類火成岩為對象，建立一種三維晶質模型，模擬火成岩微觀結構。該模型由球顆粒膠結而成的多面體晶體顆粒構成，晶體內部球體以及晶體邊緣均可發生破裂，以進一步模擬荷載作用下岩石的變形破壞和細觀裂紋演化過程。三維晶質模型可考慮實際礦物顆粒的粒徑、形態、礦物組成和結構，不同的礦物被賦予晶體內部和晶體顆粒間不同的強度和剛度性質。模型的細觀參數基於室內試驗獲得，但數值試驗可對校準的試樣在不同加載條件下反複測試，彌補了室內試驗不能重複對同一岩樣進行力學測試的不足；此外，數值試驗由於不受制樣誤差等因素的影響，故相比於室內試驗可以更加客觀、準確地反映荷載作用下試樣的變形破壞性質。 室內試驗包括岩石薄片鑑定、單軸及三軸壓縮試驗等，旨在獲得岩石內部微觀結構、力學參數和變形破壞特徵，並用於校核數值模擬中模型的細觀參數；此外，壓縮試驗過程中將採用聲發射技術監測岩石內部裂紋擴展過程，定量評估不同類型裂紋密度和分佈的時空演化特徵，聲發射反映的微觀裂紋擴展特性與數值試驗校核的研究目前鮮有報導。 最後，本項目研究方法將用於揭示不同地質特徵對岩石的破裂、變形和破壞等力學性質的影響，項目研究成果將為地球動力學、構造地質學等領域中地質變形特徵和成因提供新的闡釋。

17303917.label: Realisation of objectives
17303917.value: 1. Laboratory experimental study. An integrated experimental programme consisting of compression tests, high-speed video imaging, acoustic emission monitoring and thin section examination were carried out to provide the data to calibrate the numerical model. Uniaxial compressive test and semicircular bending test are conducted in laboratory on Kowloon granite to support the present model calibration. 2. Development and calibration of grain-based model (GBM) The GBM development involved three aspects, namely an in-depth literature review, two-dimensional (2D) model and three-dimensional (3D) model. A comprehensive literature review identified that the macro-mechanical behavior of crystalline rocks including strength, deformability and failure pattern are dominantly inﬂuenced by their grain-scale structures. Numerical technique is commonly used to assist understanding the complicated mechanisms from a microscopic perspective. Each numerical method has its respective strengths and limitations. Four categories of numerical methods are examined: particle-based methods, block-based methods, grain-based methods, and node-based methods. Focusing on the grain-scale characters, speciﬁc relevant issues including increasing complexity of micro-structure, deformation and breakage of model elements, fracturing and fragmentation process are examined. The intrinsic capabilities and limitations of different numerical approaches in terms of accounting for the micro-mechanics of crystalline rocks and their phenomenal mechanical behavior are thoroughly assessed. The 2D GBM has been developed calibrated against different rock types, including Kowloon granite (laboratory test performed in this project), Carrara Marble (laboratory test NOT performed in project) and Jinping T2b marble (laboratory test NOT performed in project), based on the respective laboratory-obtained data. Carrara Marble and Jinping T2b marble are also included in the present study to demonstrate the applicability of the developed model to other geological conditions. Take Kowloon granite for example, the calibrated model is simulated under semicircular bending testing to investigate the microcracking behavior and mechanical properties. For the uniaxial compressive test, the experimental specimen and the 2-D numerical counterpart are prepared in the same dimensions (100 mm in height, 50 mm in length, and 25 mm in width for the laboratory one). However, a smaller numerical model is used in the semicircular bending test to reduce computation time in the subsequent simulations. Previous studies suggest that reducing model size has no signiﬁcant inﬂuence on the results but signiﬁcantly improves the computing efﬁciency. Considering that each mineral should comprise several particles to allow the breakage of intragranular contacts, particle radius is set as a uniform distribution between 0.09 and 0.18 mm. The semicircular model includes 20,265 particles. The specimen geometry and the loading arrangement follow the ISRM suggested semicircular bending testing method. The key scientific question associated with the 3D GBM development is the adoption of a suitable mesh generator. Tessellations can be generated from (i) morphological cell properties (e.g. a size distribution), (ii) the generation of multiscale tessellations (i.e. including cell subdivisions). During the mesh generation, broken cells were unexpectedly obtained, and some cells were missing. We then turned to Rhino, which involves another mesh generator software called Griddle. Tetrahedrons/hexahedrons can then be generated, which provides the basis for the development of 3D GBM. 3. Application of the developed calibrated model The influence of some special mesoscopic geological features on the mechanical properties of cylindrical rock specimens were simulated by modifying the calibrated models accordingly. The two key applications are (i) brittle fracturing in low-porosity rock and implications to fault nucleation, (ii) formation of strike‐slip en echelon faults due to the growth and connection of preexisting fractures.

17303917.label: Major findings and research outcome
17303917.value: The two-dimensional GBM proposed by Potyondy in 2010 is an advanced modeling approach for simulating the mechanical behaviors of crystalline rocks. GBM implemented in PFC2D (particle flow code, GBM-PFC2D) mimics the rock material as an assembly of deformable, breakable polygonal grains cemented along their adjoining sides. Despite the distinctive advantages of GBM over many other rock models in mimicking the crystalline structure and allowing grain breakage during rock deformation, two key issues in the conventional GBM have been identified: (1) using a Voronoi-tessellated network is insufficient to capture the geometric complexities of real mineral grains, and (2) GBM approach is currently confined to laboratory-scale simulations. This project demonstrates the robustness of the developed GBM for more realistic simulation of the microstructures and thus the mechanical behaviors of crystalline rocks, and bridges the geological investigations of faulting mechanisms and the theoretical context of microfracture growth. This project first reviews the state-of-the-art methods, particularly the conventional Voronoi GBM-PFC2D in modeling crystalline rocks. In the GBM-PFC2D formulation, both stochastic and deterministic methods for more realistic characterization of rock microstructures are developed. Based on the results of thin-section examination, the stochastic method is demonstrated to be capable of reproducing some salient microstructural features in dominating rock mechanical behavior, namely grain size, grain shape and the shape-preferred crystallization orientation. Using the digital image processing technique, the deterministic method provides an algorithm to directly map the image-based rock microstructures into GBM-PFC2D. Meanwhile, the effect of initial microcracks on the mechanical behavior is incorporated into the GBM by the application of a discrete fracture network model. As compared with the conventional Voronoi GBM, the developed stochastic and deterministic GBMs fill the research gap in simulating the more realistic microstructures of monomineralic and polymineralic rock, respectively. The geological applications of the developed GBM begin with the field characterization of fault damage zone, by uniaxial compression tests on rock specimens containing different configurations of en-echelon fractures, which are indicative of fault evolution. The mechanisms of en-echelon fractures evolution into visible damage zones are revealed. Then, the stress-induced local fracturing processes under biaxial compression are quantified with respect to the location, moment and degree. This revolutionizes the numerical approach for examining the fracturing mechanisms involved in fault nucleation. Last, the seismicity activity and its correlation with local stresses along sheared smeared fault interfaces are investigated, which generates valuable insight into the mechanisms of fault reactivation and seismic hazard migration.

17303917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17303917.value: After the completion of this GRF project, further research was performed to enhance the developed GBM by considering grain expansion upon heating. By examining the thermally-induced cracks and comparing the stress-strain behaviors, it is concluded that the thermal damage was rare in mildly heated rocks, instead the more compacted structure resulted from thermal expansion of minerals would increase the frictional resistance between mineral grains, consequentially enhancing rock strength. Based on the preliminary simulation results, the pure “thermal-expansion” GBM is extended to incorporate the heating effect on grain-boundary properties. The new thermo-GBM approach can not only replicate the expansion-induced strengthening effect, but also capture the transition from strengthening to weakening in a larger temperature range 25-400 °C. The above preliminary results became the basis for another recently awarded GRF project entitled “Rock Strengthening Mechanisms Upon Heating (Project Number: 17200721)”, the research of which has just begun in Jan 2022. As the temperature of the earth's crust rises with the increase of the burial depth, making it a vital factor governing the mechanical behavior of rock, the future research outcomes will be of significant importance to a wide range of underground rock engineering, such as geothermal energy extraction and nuclear waste repository.

17304017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17304017.value: Biological organelles and cells exhibit complicated morphologies and dynamics in nature, enabling the functions and activities essential for living systems. One such signature is the ability of living cells to self-replicate through their spontaneous division, a property which is essential for the growth of organisms and for the replacement of old cells but whose driving force and mechanism are to a large extent still unclear. Emulsion droplets have been used as templates to generate cell-mimicking microcapsules, liposomes and polymer vesicles. The droplets’ spherical shape facilitates the adoption of a cell-like shape in the final microcapsules. In addition to maintaining their spherical shape, the relatively strong interfacial tension between the water and oil can also prevent the resultant drops from deforming and cause different drops to merge rather than divide. Notably, oils can also degrade the activity of biomolecules. Hence, a more biocompatible approach to achieving droplet division would likely exclude the use of oils. An emerging type of oil-free emulsion is formed between two or more immiscible aqueous phases containing high concentrations of multiple water-soluble additives. These all-aqueous emulsions typically suffer from poor stability because conventional strategies developed for their oil-water counterparts are no longer effective as a result of the significantly lower interfacial tension. Recently, we discovered that the growth of proteins into nanofibrils can enhance emulsion stability without increasing interfacial tension, rendering the droplets superior deformability and potentially allowing morphological transformation. This advance thus opens up entirely new avenues for employing all-aqueous emulsions as biocompatible simplified model systems to mimic cell-like behavior. However, to determine the strategies that induce changes in their shape, we require a better understanding of the dynamic interactions among the proteins in the droplets and at the aqueous-aqueous interfaces. The aims of the proposed project are to (1) elucidate the physics behind the stabilization of all-aqueous interfaces by proteins, (2) devise strategies to induce the budding-like division of all-aqueous droplets containing proteins, and (3) engineer biomimetic droplet-based capsules and fibers that exhibit potential toward self-replication. In the short term, the project will provide a fundamental understanding of the interactions between proteins within droplets and at their interfaces as well as the driving forces that induce self-replication in these system, and in this manner suggest a physico-chemical strategy for achieving new biomaterials. In the long term, it will contribute to unraveling the intricate dynamics and functions of biological systems and the development of synthetic “living” hierarchical materials. 在自然環境中，細胞和細胞器展現出了十分複雜的形態和動力學特徵。正是由於這些形態和特徵，才能夠使生命體具備了必要的功能及活動。在細胞中，最具代表性的功能即為通過自發分裂進行的自我複製。這個功能對於生物體生長更新十分重要。然而，自我複製的驅動力很大程度上仍是未解之謎。 液滴曾被研究者作為模板來生產模擬細胞的微囊，脂質體以及高分子囊泡。液滴的球體形狀便於生產的微囊呈現細胞狀。油水系統的界面張力較高，使得其產生。的液滴始終保持球狀然而較高的界面張力致使液滴很難變形，液滴之間更傾向於融合而非分裂。並且，油的使用降低了與之接觸的生物分子的活性。因此，急需一種非油的高生物相容性液滴來模擬分裂過程。 研究發現，當兩種或多種水溶性溶劑在水中的濃度較高時，可以形成兩個或多個互不相容的非油全水相。然而，由於全水相體系界面張力較低，傳統的用以穩定油水界面的方法無法適用在全水相體系中。因此，用全水相體系形成的液滴並不容易被穩定， 最近，我們研究發現全水相液滴可以由蛋白纖維來穩定，同時保持不同水相之間的界面張力不變。這種蛋白纖維由蛋白質分子連接而成，賦予液滴極強的變形能力，使得液滴形態發生變化。這項研究進展為研究者們開闢了一條模擬細胞行為的新途徑，即利用簡化的高生物相容性的全水相液滴作為模型來模擬細胞行為。然而，為了確定引起形變的因素，我們首先需要研究在水相液滴中及其界面上蛋白質之間的動態交互作用。 本項目的研究目的為：（1）說明蛋白質穩定全水界面的物理學機制;（2）設計引起含有蛋白質的全水相體係出芽型分裂的方法;以及（3）設計以液滴為模板的，能夠自我複製的仿生膠囊及纖維。 短期內，這個項目將會從根本上理解液滴中及界面上蛋白質的交互作用，以及在此系統中引發自我複製的驅動力，並且通過這一物理 - 化學機制製作新型生物材料未來，這個項目將會致力於闡釋生物體系中複雜的動態變化及功能，並且用以合成“活的”多相材料。

17304017.label: Realisation of objectives
17304017.value: The objectives have been achieved: 1. We have investigated the stabilization of aqueous-aqueous interfaces by proteins under different conditions, such different concentrations, types, shapes and solvents. We have characterized the behaviors of droplets with different stabilizing structures, including liposomes, and during the emergence of new interfaces driven by changes, such as osmotic flows. 2. We have studied and devised strategies that may induce changing shapes, including budding, of otherwise spherical or almost spherical droplets, by varying the types of stabilizers, such as proteins. The studies allow us to identify approaches to control the stability of all-aqueous droplets formed under different conditions and from different stabilizing materials. 3. We have introduced the concept of forming material structures by assembling proteins at aqueous-aqueous interfaces. In addition, we have also looked into the intricate and intertwining effects between stabilization and aqueous phase separation, which is a pre-requisite for the emergence of aqueous-aqueous interfaces. By freezing the structures at different stage of phase separation, we demonstrate the possibility to have different structures, not limited to core-shell and porous structures. We have also outlined the potential to incorporate this concept into printing and robotic applications, and believe these can inspire new functional cyto-mimetic materials.
