17304017.label: Major findings and research outcome
17304017.value: - Understand the observations behind stabilization of all-aqueous interfaces, particularly, droplet interfaces, by stabilizing molecules, such as proteins, at different concentrations - Investigate the ability of different all-aqueous droplets containing different macromolecules, such as proteins, to change shape, merge, or divide, under different conditions - Evaluate the role of microscaled hydrodynamics on phase behaviors of all-aqueous droplets containing macromolecules, such as proteins - Demonstrate approaches to generate different functional materials fabricated using all-aqueous systems Most of the results have been presented in various international conferences (e.g. MicroTAS 2021, World Laureate Forum, iCANX 2020, IAAM Advanced Materials Lecture Series 2021, International Youth Conference of Bionic Science and Engineering 2021, 9th World Congress of Biomechanics, etc.) and published in respected international journals (e.g. ACS Nano, Journal of Materials Chemistry B, Analytical Chemistry, Chemical Society Reviews, Advanced Science, etc.), as shown in Part C. While some papers have been submitted and are being reviewed, other results are being integrated with other applications and wrapped up for publication due to their potential to combine for a greater impact.The potential of all-aqueous based materials combined with biological macromolecules, such as proteins, is exciting, and more works should be done in this direction. Some of the project outcomes also benefit other research projects indirectly.

17304017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17304017.value: The completed research project demonstrated that there are still many biological or cell-inspired phenomena with potentially a physico-chemical origin. The division of droplets is just one of them. On the one hand, we can continue to harness our expertise in forming and manipulating all-aqueous droplets to discover more potentially biologically relevant dynamics. This will have implications not just for cell biology, but also for fundamental interfacial phenomena. On the other hand, it will be important to confirm the relevance of these dynamical processes using systems that are even closer to their biological counterparts. For example, instead of just using synthetic molecules, such as polyelectrolytes and synthesized proteins, it will be helpful to directly extract proteins from cellular systems. This would require significant resources and expertise, due to the availability of the relevant cellular samples, and the skills required. The proposed course of action includes publishing the remaining works, while discussing the above aspects with potential academic collaborators that have the skills to work with more relevant proteins and provide them or train us to extract them in large quantities. To support these collaborative activities, we will apply for potentially relevant fundings from agencies, such as the Research Grants Council (RGC) of Hong Kong. The physico-chemical aspects also have implications to materials application, for instance, in forming coacervates and coacervate-based materials. We also propose to explore these through collaborations with industries, facilitated by research grants, such as the RGC and Innovation and Technology Fund (ITF).

17304017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17304017.value: Water is Nature’s choice of solvent for life and living systems. Intricate dynamics can be observed in aqueous solutions consisting of a complicated mix of macromolecules, such as proteins. While technologies, such as droplet microfluidics, traditionally rely on use of mixture of water and oil, cell biology is mostly dominated by aqueous solution alone. Therefore, the study of completely aqueous systems that contain macromolecules is highly relevant. In this project, we start by addressing the stability of these all-aqueous systems in the presence of proteins and other macromolecules. We then also devise strategies to induce and trigger different dynamics in these droplets. We also combine the assembly of these macromolecules with the phase behaviors of aqueous systems. These suggest new all-aqueous-based materials with new functions and structures, which we also demonstrated some as examples. Our findings will not only inspire the relevant study of the fundamental questions surrounding interfaces that are relevant to biology and cells, but will also create new opportunity to generate cyto-mimetic materials. Our works also suggest one possible type of synthetic system for studying the physico-chemical phenomena in their biological counterparts.

17304417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17304417.value: A successful class of nonlinear time series in the last 30 years has been the threshold time series models. Recently the hysteretic or buffered time series models have been proposed which include the threshold models as a special case. This broader class of nonlinear time series models allows for different switching boundaries during the upward movement and the downward movement of the time series. Hence, it is more flexible than the threshold models where regime changes occur when the series up crosses or down crosses the same threshold boundary. Therefore the new model is possible to mimic a much large set of phenomena including but not limited to regime changes in the economy, stock prices, exchange rates, sunspots and many others. However, recent studies concentrate on essentially two aspects namely: (A) Stationary time series and (B) the overall behaviors of the time series and ignore tail events. In reality non-stationarity is common in many economic and financial time series. Extending the stationary models to the nonstationary case will greatly enhance the usefulness of the hysteretic models. It will also provide a better understanding and interpretation of the data generating mechanism underlining many nonlinear time series. This project proposes to extend the buffered or hysteretic feature to two important classical nonstationary situations namely (1) Unit root processes under the hysteretic or buffered structure and (2) Nonlinear cointegration process with a hysteretic cointegration vector. Unit root testing is important as determining whether a time series has a unit root or not is equivalent to determining whether it is nonstationary. This is also related to the second problem: whether or not cointegration exists between two or more than two nonstationary time series. Cointegration implies that the different time series under consideration trend together in a stochastic sense which, at least, in economics has significant implications. The more general nonlinear approach under the proposed framework will provide us with new tools to better understand how nonstationary time series related to each other. Finally, this project will also consider the modelling of tail events in time series using the hysteretic approach. A robust procedure for statistical inference, the quantile autoregression will be considered as a first step in this direction. The approach will place more emphases on the modelling of extreme behaviours and will provide us with new tools in the study of tail events in many real applications such as quantitative risk management. 門限時間序列是過去30年最成功的非線性時間序列模型。緩衝時間序列則比門限時間序列更為靈活，因其序列上升時或下降時的結構改變受控於不同的門限。門限時間序列也因此是緩衝時間序列的特殊例子。過去的研究集中在平穩的緩衝時間序列，也忽畧了時間序列的重尾(極端)效應。在經濟應用上這兩者都十分重要。本項目將探討以下問題：1. 如何對緩衝時間序列作單位根的檢驗以確認其為非平穩；2. 如有多於一條非平穩時間序列，它們之間是否存在協整(平穩的線性組合)的關係？如有，此協整關係是否有緩衝序列的性質？反過來，如其平穩部分有緩衝序列的性質，如何可檢測協整關係的存在？3. 分位數自回歸模型是研究重尾或極端效應的重要工具，本項目將把分位數自回歸模型的方法推廣至含有重尾的緩衝時間序列。以上的研究將大大加強我們對緩衝時間序列，以致非線性時間序列的了解及分析的能力。

17304417.label: Realisation of objectives
17304417.value: All objectives are realized. Objective 1 is reached by deriving tests for the presence of unit root non-stationarity under the presence of buffered (hysteretic) non-linearity. In addition, a sup-Likelihood Ratio (sup-LR) test for the presence of buffered structure under unit root is obtained. See Paper 2. As these tests have nonstandard asymptotic distributions the wild bootstrap is used to obtain the asymptotic critical values. This approach is shown to be robust under unknown heteroscedasticity. The unit root tests out perform the classical Dickey-Fuller test in simulation studies. Applications to some real exchange rates time series cast some insights into the purchasing power parity debate. Objective 2 is realized by the recent paper on buffered error correction models (paper 4). This turns out to be very difficult mathematically. However, a non-classical sup-Wald test is obtained for testing for the presence of buffered error correction. . A bootstrap method is proposed to obtain the p-value for the sup-Wald test. Least squares estimation and reduced-rank estimation are discussed, and the consistency of the estimators on the delay parameter and threshold parameters are derived. Successful application has been made to the US treasury bond rates. Objective 3 is realized by paper 1 which studied conditional quantile estimation (a robust procedure) for buffered models. It is shown that classical results for parameter estimators under hysteretic or threshold type models such as super-consistency for the estimators of buffered threshold parameters can be extended. The result has been applied successfully to model US unemployment rate. An additional outcome is paper 3 which defines and studies the smooth transition buffered auto-regressive models. This extends the corresponding classical result of Chan and Tong (1986) for smooth transition threshold models. Here estimators for the transition function is root n consistent and not n consistent. Successful application has been made to the annual sunspot numbers.

17304617.label: Project Objectives
17304617.value: Develop a hybrid conditional quantile estimation for GARCH models. This will be achieved by introducing a simple yet nontrivial function to transform the conditional quantiles of GARCH processes into a tractable structure, employing the quasi-maximum likelihood estimation to obtain an initial estimator for conditional variances, and finally performing linear quantile regression estimation to obtain the fitted conditional quantiles. We also consider a bootstrap method based on the random weighting to approximate the corresponding asymptotic distributions. Introduce a new conditional heteroscedastic model, the quantile GARCH model. This will be achieved by figuring out the form of the model, and deriving the conditions for the existence of a unique strictly stationary and ergodic solution. We also consider the quantile estimation for the new model, and the bootstrap method is used again to approximate asymptotic distributions. Design two diagnostic tools for the GARCH and quantile GARCH models, respectively. This will be achieved by figuring out the test statistics, deriving the asymptotic distributions, and using the bootstrap method to approximate the asymptotic distributions. Box-Pierce type test statistics will then be formed. Computer programs will be developed to verify the large-sample property and to demonstrate the finite-sample performance of results in Objectives 1-3 and applications to real data such as the estimation of VaR will be considered. Clearly, the objectives only reflect part of the possible developments in this area. Many other developments are also possible if time permits.

17304617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17304617.value: Time series models with conditional heteroscedasticity have become extremely popular in financial applications since the appearance of ARCH models in 1982 and GARCH models in 1986. These models are widely used in the assessment and management of financial risk, including the estimation of quantile-based measures such as the Value-at-Risk (VaR) and the Expected Shortfall (ES). For this reason, estimating conditional quantiles of financial time series is crucial to both academic researchers and professional practitioners in many areas of economics and finance. As conditional quantiles can be directly estimated by quantile regression, it is important to study the conditional quantile inference for conditional heteroscedastic models via quantile regression. Moreover, it is especially appealing to develop new quantile time series models whose conditional quantile processes admit varying structures across a continuum of quantile levels. Among the large number of conditional heteroscedastic models, the GARCH process is the most popular and influential one. However, so far feasible quantile regression methods for this task have been confined to a variant of the GARCH model, the linear GARCH model, owing to its tractable conditional quantile structure. This project introduces a simple albeit nontrivial transformation, based on which an easy-to-implement hybrid conditional quantile estimation procedure is developed for the widely used GARCH model. Secondly, the conditional quantiles of GARCH processes at different levels are exactly proportional, and this may not be true in some applications. This project applies the idea of quantile regression models to the ARCH(infty) form of the GARCH model, and hence a more flexible quantile GARCH process is introduced. The quantile estimation of the new model is further discussed. Finally, according to the Box-Jenkins' three-stage modeling strategy, it is another important problem to construct diagnostic tools for the adequacy of the above fitted time series models. Moreover, a (conditional) density function will be expected to enter all asymptotic distributions in this project, and the bootstrap method based on the random weighting is hence employed in this project. 自從1982年ARCH年模型和1986年GARCH年模型的提出，具有條件異方差性的時間序列模型在實際應用中變的非常受歡迎。這些模型廣泛應用於財務風險的評估和管理，包括VaR和ES等各種基於分位數的度量。因此，估計時間序列的條件分數不管是對於經濟金融領域的學術研究者或者是專業從業者都是至關重要的。由於條件分位數可以通過分位數回歸直接估計，因此通過分位數回歸來研究條件異方差模型的分位數變的非常有必要。此外，一個靈活的在不同的分位數具有不同的結構的時間序列模型在本領域也特別有吸引力。 一般來說，GARCH模型是一個最有影響力的條件異方差模型。然而，迄今為止可行的分位數回歸方法僅僅局限於線性GARCH模型。該項目對GARCH模型提出了一個簡單的變換，從而我們可以建立一個易於實現的混合條件分位數估計。 其次，對於GARCH模型來說，不同分位數是成比例的。這極大地限制了它在實際中的應用。本項目利用了ARCH（infinite）模型的概念，提出了一個更靈活的分位數GARCH模型。此外，我們還進一步討論了新模型的分位數估計。 最後，在箱詹金斯的三階段建模策略中，模型診斷是一個重要的環節。因此本項目還構建了一些相應的模型診斷工具。此外，由於很難估計的密度函數也捲入漸近分佈中，因此在實際應用中，本項目還提出了一個bootstrap方法來具體實施。

17304617.label: Major findings and research outcome
17304617.value: 1) This project proposed an easy-to-implement hybrid quantile regression estimation procedure for the GARCH model, where we overcame the intractability due to the square-root form of the conditional quantile function by a simple transformation. The proposed method takes advantage of the efficiency of the GARCH model in modelling the volatility globally as well as the flexibility of quantile regression in fitting quantiles at a specific level. This finding was published at the Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B (one of top 4 statistical journals); see Zheng, Zhu, Li and Xiao (2018) at Part C. 2) This project proposed a novel conditional heteroskedastic model, called quantile double autoregression. The proposed model just fills this gap. This finding was published at the Econometric Theory; see Zhu and Li (2021) at Part C. 3) This project studied linear quantile regression models with GARCH-X errors, which include the most popular generalized autoregressive conditional heteroscedasticity (GARCH) as a special case, and incorporate additional covariates into the conditional variance. This finding was published at the Statistica Sinica; see Zhu, Li and Xiao (2021) at Part C. 4) This project novelly transformed lack-of-fit tests for parametric quantile regression models into checking the equality of two conditional distributions of covariates. Accordingly, two tests were constructed to check the lack of fit for low and high dimensional quantile regression models. This finding was published at the Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B (one of top 4 statistical journals); see Dong, Li and Feng (2019) at Part C. 5) This project considered a conditional quantile estimation for hysteretic autoregressive models to study the hysteretic patterns at different quantiles. This finding was published at the Statistica Sinica; see Li, Zeng, Zhang, Li and Li (2020) at Part C. 6) This project investigated a functional additive quantile regression that models the conditional quantile of a scalar response based on the nonparametric effects of a functional predictor. This finding was published at the Statistica Sinica; see Zhang, Lian, Li and Zhu (2021) at Part C. 7) This project developed a novel one-step estimation method to conduct quantile regression for a large dataset on a distributed system, and it can fix the problem that the popularly used one-shot estimation is statistically inefficient if data are not randomly distributed across different workers. This finding was accepted for publication by the Journal of Business & Economic Statistics; see Pan, Ren, Guo, Li, Li and Wang (2022) at Part C.

17304617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17304617.value: This project can be extended in several directions. First, it is well known that financial time series can be so heavy tailed such that the fourth moment is infinite. For such cases, we may alternatively consider methods that are more robust than Gaussian QMLE for initial estimation of the conditional variances, e.g. the least absolute deviations estimator. Second, our procedure can be applied to conditional quantile estimation for other conditional heteroscedastic models, including the asymmetric Glosten–Jagannathan–Runkle–GARCH model. Third, although the multivariate GARCH model has been widely used for volatility modelling of multiple asset returns, conditional quantile estimation for the corresponding portfolio return is still an open problem. This project offers some preliminary ideas on this, which we leave for future research.

17304617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17304617.value: This project proposed a novel idea of transforming the quantiles, and it enables us first to turn a highly intractable quantile regression problem into a much simpler linear quantile regression, making the conditional quantile estimation for the GARCH model an easy job. The accomplishment of this project will completely overcome the difficulty of calculating quantile-based measures based on the GARCH model, and hence have an important impact on the literature. In the meanwhile, several conditional heteroscedastic time series models have been proposed for the assessment and management of financial risk, and the corresponding inference tools, including diagnostic tools, were also established. Moreover, this project also applied quantile regression to other topics, including functional additive models and threshold models. These new models and estimation methods contributed to the literature with more feasible methodology, and will certainly trigger more developments in the area.

17304817.label: Project Objectives
17304817.value: Age and Metallicities of Star Clusters in NGC 1275: We plan narrowband imaging in the Strömgren v, b, and y filters of all the star clusters in NGC 1275 using the 4.2-m William Herschel Telescope to separate out old metal-poor globular clusters from younger metal-rich star clusters. Based on the latter, we will be able to trace the star formation history of NGC 1275 further back in time, currently limited to ~1 Gyr, to at least to ~3 Gyr and potentially as far back as ~9 Gyr. Furthermore, we plan spectroscopy of the brightest star clusters (other than globular clusters) using OSIRIS on the 10.4-m Gran Telescopio Canarias in the multi-object spectroscopy mode to determine the metallicity of these clusters. By stacking together spectra, we will be able to attain the necessary sensitivity for measuring the equivalent widths of metal lines. Their metallicity is key for determining the origin of the gas from which these star clusters formed. A metallicity similar to the X-ray emitting intracluster gas of about half solar metallicity would imply a gas origin from cooling of the X-ray gas. If on the other hand we find a near solar metallicity, this result would imply a gas origin from mergers involving metal-enriched gas-rich galaxies, or if an intermediate metallicity then a combination of both cooling and mergers. Star Formation Histories of Younger BCGs: From the experience gained on work currently being performed on deriving the star formation histories of two BCGs observed in the CLASH program with the Hubble Space Telescope, we plan to complete our study of the remaining seven that show spatially extended star formation. This study extends our work on NGC 1275 to many more BCGs, looking back in time to nearly half the age of the Universe. We also plan to study other BCGs in the CLASH program that only exhibit UV continuum emission from their centers, to see whether we can differentiate between star formation and UV emission from red giant stars or AGN activity. It may be that many BCGs exhibit substantial star formation at their centers that cannot be verified without the data quality provided by the CLASH program. Nature and Origin of Cool Interstellar Gas: By subtracting images taken in the CLASH program in adjacent filters, one of which contains the Hα or the [OIII] line, we aim to determine the morphology of the ISM in each BCG. For studying the cool molecular gas, we will first search for CO emission using the James Clerk Maxwell Telescope or the IRAM 30-m telescope, and then aim to image the spatial distribution and kinematics of this gas with the Atacama Large Millimeter and SubMillimeter Array. Conditions for Star Formation: Observations in multiple transitions of CO and perhaps also in other trace molecules will be interpreted with radiative transfer modeling to constrain the physical properties of the molecular gas. Comparisons with the spatial distribution of newly formed stars will allow us to deduce the conditions under which the molecular gas turns into stars. Feedback: Where the required images do not exist, we will image the synchrotron radio emission of the BCGs in the CLASH program with the Very Large Array to study jets from their supermassive black holes. By comparing these images with X-ray images of the CLASH clusters already taken by Chandra, we aim to study the dispersal of the ISM and ICM, and perhaps also their compression to identify regions of enhanced cooling.

This study extends our work on NGC 1275 to many more BCGs, looking back in time to nearly half the age of the Universe. We also plan to study other BCGs in the CLASH program that only exhibit UV continuum emission from their centers, to see whether we can differentiate between star formation and UV emission from red giant stars or AGN activity. It may be that many BCGs exhibit substantial star formation at their centers that cannot be verified without the data quality provided by the CLASH program.

Nature and Origin of Cool Interstellar Gas: By subtracting images taken in the CLASH program in adjacent filters, one of which contains the Hα or the [OIII] line, we aim to determine the morphology of the ISM in each BCG. For studying the cool molecular gas, we will first search for CO emission using the James Clerk Maxwell Telescope or the IRAM 30-m telescope, and then aim to image the spatial distribution and kinematics of this gas with the Atacama Large Millimeter and SubMillimeter Array.

Conditions for Star Formation: Observations in multiple transitions of CO and perhaps also in other trace molecules will be interpreted with radiative transfer modeling to constrain the physical properties of the molecular gas. Comparisons with the spatial distribution of newly formed stars will allow us to deduce the conditions under which the molecular gas turns into stars.

Feedback: Where the required images do not exist, we will image the synchrotron radio emission of the BCGs in the CLASH program with the Very Large Array to study jets from their supermassive black holes. By comparing these images with X-ray images of the CLASH clusters already taken by Chandra, we aim to study the dispersal of the ISM and ICM, and perhaps also their compression to identify regions of enhanced cooling.

17304817.label: Major findings and research outcome
17304817.value: Meeting the scientific objectives of this project requires telescope observations granted free-of-charge through competitive proposals or archival data. To guard against the fact that not all, and sometimes only a small fraction of, proposals for telescope time are successful, we list more scientific objectives than can possibly be accomplished – with the aim of meeting as many of these objectives as is possible. Hence, our inability to meet some of the stated scientific objectives should not be regarded as failures. Furthermore, we are very conservative in our assessment of the percentage achievement of any objective – as there is always more work that can be done to attain a better understanding. The highlight of our achievements must surely be our discovery, using archival data from the HST, that globular clusters continue to form around the giant elliptical galaxy at the center of the Perseus clusters (Paper 2 in Part C). Published in Nature Astronomy, this work has broad implications, perhaps the most interesting of which is a better understanding of how globular clusters might have formed in the early universe – by studying how those around this nearby giant elliptical galaxy formed. This paper has received considerable attention in both the popular press and online (see https://www.nature.com/articles/s41550-019-0909-6/metrics). Our observation of the same galaxy with the ALMA has led to the discovery of a rotating disk and outflow of cold molecular gas at its center (Paper 1 in Part C). This disk most likely formed from infalling gas that cooled from the intracluster medium, and held responsible for fueling the supermassive black hole at the center of the galaxy. Using archival data from Keck telescope and the HST, we showed that the infalling cooled intracluster gas also likely produced a spiral disk centered on the galaxy (Paper 5 in Part C), which itself is surrounded by its own population of progenitor globular clusters (Paper 6 in Part C). Finally, we have demonstrated, using archival data from the HST, that the giant elliptical galaxy at the center of another cluster seen ~5 Gyr ago also exhibits star formation that is extended in both space and time (Paper 3 in Part C). Finally, we have mapped the cool molecular gas in a giant elliptical galaxy at the center of a galaxy group on scales of giant molecular clouds (Paper 2 in Part C) to address why some but not all of these galaxies exhibit star formation.

17304817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17304817.value: Giant elliptical galaxies at the centers of galaxy clusters (groupings of up to a thousand galaxies) are the largest and most massive galaxies in the universe. In addition, they host the richest population of globular clusters (ancient star systems, containing up to about 10 million stars, found around nearly all galaxies) numbering up to tens of thousands. How these galaxies attained their enormous masses and sizes, as well as their large populations of globular clusters, pose a strong challenge to our understanding of galaxy formation and growth. Surprisingly, some of these galaxies exhibit luminous gas nebulae and continue to form stars to the present time, the nature of and reason for which remain poorly understood. The central aim of our project is to address the aforementioned questions. Our work reveals that the star formation in these galaxies is extended not only in space but also in time. Furthermore, the giant elliptical galaxy at the center of a nearby galaxy clusters continues to form star clusters that resemble globular clusters. The next generation space telescope, the James Webb Space Telescope, will be able to reveal whether such progenitor globular clusters also are forming around more distant giant elliptical galaxies at cluster centers.

17305017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17305017.value: Many compounds having polycyclic frameworks are found in nature, drug molecules, bioactive compounds, and materials. Among these, the cyclopentane is a ubiquitous subunit, occurring only less frequently than the six-membered cyclohexane moiety. Intramolecular cycloadditions are a highly efficient strategy to construct fused ring compounds. Six-membering ring synthesis can be readily approached by employing (4+2) cycloadditions. Analogously a (3+2) cycloaddition could be used for synthesizing five-membered ring carbocycles. Whereas the intramolecular (4+2) cycloaddition is well-known and vastly applied as a method to generate fused six-membered carbocycles, the corresponding intramolecular (3+2) cycloaddition to produce fused five-membered carbocyclic rings occurs much less frequently. There is a need to develop (3+2) cycloadditions that are able to generate cyclopentane derivatives in an asymmetric manner, in order that the reactions may be applied to the synthesis of natural products or chiral drugs. This project aims to examine and develop an intramolecular (3+2) cycloaddition based on epoxy and aziridinyl enolsilane derivatives as the electrophilic, three-carbon component. Preliminary results show that tethered electron-rich alkenes react in a highly diastereoselective manner to generate stereochemically defined fused cyclopentanones in good yield. This reaction has been shown to be able to synthesize fused cyclopentanes in optically enriched forms, starting from an enantiomerically enriched epoxide precursor. Due to the high occurrence of fused cyclopentanes among natural products and bioactive drug molecules, this cycloaddition could have tremendous application in the syntheses and production of such compounds. 天然產物，藥物分子，生物活性化合物以及材料中普遍含有多環結構，其中環戊烷的結構是比較常見的，在環狀結構單元中僅少於環己烷。 分子内的環加成反應可以高效地構建稠環化合物。分子内的（4+2）環加成反應應用於合成六員碳環化合物已經有很多的研究，並且被廣泛地使用。然而相應的（3+2）環加成反應相對較少，因而有必要發展可以實現五員碳環的不對稱合成的方法學，從而應用在天然產物和手性藥物分子的合成當中。 本課題拟研究和發展以氧烯醇硅醚和氮丙啶烯醇硅醚類化合物為親電的三碳組分的分子内（3+2）環加成反應。初步的研究表明，連有富電子的烯烃底物，可以以非對影選擇性，及產率好的方式得到具立體化學既定的稠合環戊酮。當使用光學純的環氧底物時，該反應可以順利得到光學純的稠合環戊烷。由於稠合的環戊烷廣泛存在於天然產物和生物活性的藥物分子當中，該環加成反應在這些分子的合成中具有廣闊的應用前景。

17305017.label: Major findings and research outcome
17305017.value: An extensive study of the intramolecular (3+2) cycloaddition was carried out, by synthesizing over 40 substrates that have the epoxy/aziridinyl enolsilane tethered to various pi-systems, through multi-step syntheses, then examining their reactions. The first group of substrates are those that have conjugated dienes as the pi-system. It was unusual that all of these substrates underwent almost exclusively the intramolecular (3+2) cycloaddition, instead of the more typical (4+3) cycloaddition. To understand the mechanistic details behind this outcome, we collaborated with the group of Dr. Elizabeth Krenske of the Univ. of Queensland for computational studies, and it was found that in this stepwise formal cycloaddition, firstly an exo bond formation led to the formation of the first ring that, without having been in a cisoid formation, favored the (3+2) cycloaddition. This outcome was different from the cycloadditions with the previous dienes such as furan. Not only is this computation study meaningful to explain the (3+2) cycloaddition results, it also sheds light on the course of cycloadditions of other typical oxyallylic cations. The second group of substrates are those that have simple alkenes as the pi-system. Many of these also underwent successful intramolecular (3+2) cycloadditions, to generate trans-indanones as products, with up to 4 contiguous stereocenters, densely functionalized, and in up to 97% yields. Furthermore, optically enriched cycloadducts can also be generated from the enantiomerically enriched epoxy or aziridinyl enolsilanes. The findings of these two substrate groups as well as the computational studies on the mechanism have been assembled into a first publication on the intramolecular (3+2) cycloaddition, which is under review. The third group of substrates are those that have indoles as the pi-system, and intramolecular (3+2) cycloadditions were also successful, resulting in dearomatization and the formation of highly functionalized, quadricyclic cyclopentaindoline compounds bearing up to four stereocenters, of which two are quaternary, in yields of up to 88%. Optically enriched cycloadducts can also be obtained. The results of the intramolecular (3+2) cycloaddition of these indole-tethered substrates will be the subject of the paper which is being prepared now.

17305017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17305017.value: Due to the interruptions and difficulties experienced in the past 1.5 years, an even wider scope of the study could not be carried out. With more time and opportunities in the future, additional pi-systems can also be examined for this (3+2) cycloaddition. Interesting enes that could be studied include enynes, and allylsilanes. There is also a synthetic potential to apply this reaction as the key reaction toward the total synthesis of hydrindanone natural products, such as oplopanone.

17305017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17305017.value: Carbon ring systems constitute the core of many natural products and drug molecules. Therefore, to obtain these ring compounds, reactions to assemble rings in efficient and stereoselective ways are crucial and need to be developed in the chemical synthesis laboratory. The more there are of such reaction tools, the more the chemist is equipped to tackle synthetic challenges with a higher efficiency and a reduction in costs. This project studied an intramolecular (3+2) cycloaddition to simultaneously assemble a fused bicyclic framework of a five-membered and six-membered carbocycles, which are also called hydrindanes. This framework is also found as a substructure in steroids. The cycloaddition produced molecules are stereochemically defined and bearing up to 5 stereocenters. Importantly, the cycloadducts can also be obtained in enantiomerically enriched forms, which is particularly important in the synthesis of drugs and pharmaceuticals. The cycloadducts are also well-endowed with functional groups to facilitate further chemical transformations to achieve different possibilities.

17305117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17305117.value: The general objective of this proposed study is to achieve a fundamental understanding of the radical-mediated reaction mechanisms, structures, energetics, and kinetics underlying the activations, isomerization, and dissociations of new radical peptide ions. The ability to (i) synthesize, in the gas phase, various non-interconverting isomeric peptide radicals with well-defined radical sites and (ii) capture the products of those reactions will allow us to significantly broaden the scope of our experimental and theoretical explorations and allow us to begin to answer the following questions. What novel radical-mediated chemical steps—ranging from backbone to side chain cleavages—can occur in the absence of solvent? To what extent do the locations of the radical sites of the non-interconverting radical peptide isomers influence the types of radical-mediated reaction mechanisms and structures of their products? Our preliminary results have demonstrated a diversity of non-interconverting radical peptide cationic isomers, introducing the possibility of novel structures and radical-mediated chemical reaction mechanisms; furthermore, unprecedented novel backbone and side chain cleavage reactions lead to novel cyclic structures as products. Mechanistic, energetic, kinetic, and spectroscopic elucidation of the precise characteristics of selected novel radical-mediated reactions will be conducted to reveal the controlling factors behind some of these intriguing chemical processes. We will then attempt to establish the structural, energetic, and kinetic features that facilitate these new reactions, using an integrated approach involving gas phase synthesis of a variety of prototypical non-interconverting radical carrier–specific peptide radical precursor isomeric strictures, collision-induced dissociation (CID) and surface-induced dissociation (SID) experiments, isotopic labeling experiments, and UV–Vis action ion spectroscopy, in combination with density functional theory (DFT) calculations and Rice–Ramsperger–Kassel–Marcus (RRKM) modeling. 這項研究的總體目標是實現對激進，異構化和解離自由基肽離子的新的自由基介導的反應機制，結構，能量學和動力學的基本理解。 （i）在氣相中合成具有明確定義的自由基位點的各種不可轉換的異構肽基團;(ii）捕獲這些反應的產物以擴大實驗和理論探索的範圍-在沒有溶劑的情況下，可以發現從骨架到側鏈裂解的新型自由基介導的化學步驟？不可轉換自由基肽異構體的自由基位點的性質和位置有多大程度上影響反應機制和其產物結構的類型？特別是前所未有的新型骨架和側鏈裂解反應，導致新的環狀結構作為產物。將對進行選擇的新型自由基介導的反應的精確特徵進行機理，精力充沛，動力學和光譜分析，以揭示一些這些有趣的化學過程背後的控制因素。嘗試建立促進這些新反應的結構，能量和動力學特徵，使用涉及氣相合成各種原型不可轉換自由基載體特異性肽自由基前體異構體狹窄的集成方法，碰撞誘導的解離（CID）和表面誘導解離（SID）實驗，同位素標記實驗和UV-Vis動作離子光譜，結合密度泛函理論（DFT）計算和Rice-Ramsperger-Kassel-Marcus（RRKM）建模。

17305217.label: Project Objectives
17305217.value: We will investigate the finite temperature effects on the normal density of a spin-orbit coupled Bose gas. Contributions from the single and multiple quasi-particle will be discussed explicitly. Corrections to Landau formula for the normal density will be derived. We will discuss the lifetime of long wave length phonons due to phonon scattering. Effects of gapped spin excitations in the phonon lifetime will be discussed. We will try to extend the Landau two fluid model to include the effects of spin-orbit coupling of the type that is realized in experiments. Investigation will be made to determine if any novel hydrodynamic mode will be present due to spin-orbit coupling.

17305217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17305217.value: The study of synthetic spin-orbit coupling in degenerate quantum gases is one of the most exciting and fruitful directions in cold atom research. It extends the studies of spin-orbit coupling in electronic systems to neutral atoms, and in particular, to the studies of bosons. So far, many novel condensate structures (stripe, plane wave and zero momentum phases) have been discovered in spin-orbit coupled bosons and their excitations differ significantly from the standard Bose alkali gases and liquid Helium. These differences arise mainly from two facts. The first is that the Galilean invariance is broken due to spin-orbit coupling. The second fact has to do with the multiple long wave length excitations, which, apart from usual phonon mode, also feature the gapped spin excitation. One important consequence of such modifications is that the normal density of a spin-orbit coupled boson does not vanish even at zero temperature. In fact, it was shown that the entire fluid becomes normal at the transition between the plane wave and the zero momentum phase. In this proposal, we will explore two important aspects of the spin-orbit coupled Bose gas that are intimately related to the differences mentioned above. (1) How do the long wave length excitations (phonon and spin excitations) modify the normal density at finite temperature and in particular, whether the classic Landau formula for the normal density is still valid when spin-orbit coupling is present. We will also explore the lifetime effects of phonon and spin excitation. (2) How can one extend the Landau two fluid model to include the effects of spin-orbit coupling and investigate the possibility of second sound at finite temperature. In the first part of the proposal, we will base our calculations and discussions on the Bogolyubov approximation and distinguish between the single and multiple quasi-particle contributions to the normal density. To investigate the lifetime effects, we will go beyond the Bogolyubov approximation and use either a quantum hydrodynamic formalism or diagrammatic theory to compute the phonon lifetime. In the second part, we will construct a hydrodynamic theory that describes the relative motion of superfluid and normal components. This will allow us to determine if there are new hydrodynamic modes due to spin-orbit coupling. In both parts, we shall focus our attention on the one-dimensional spin-orbit coupling that has been most extensively studied experimentally. 最近，简并自旋轨道耦合玻色子的研究引起了极大的兴趣。原先仅电子才有的一些有趣性质，现在可以在中性原子，尤其是玻色子中来研究了。到现在为止，许多新的凝聚体在自旋轨道耦合玻色子中被发现；它们具有和一般玻色子以及液氦不同的激发谱。其来源有二。第一自旋轨道耦合玻色子的伽利略变换对称性破缺。第二自旋轨道耦合玻色子长程激发有多重，除了声子外，还有有限能量的自旋激发。这导致一个重要的结果，自旋轨道耦合玻色子的正常态密度在零温下不为零，尤其是在从平面波态到零动量态的转变点，整个体系的超流密度等于零。在这个项目中，我们主要研究这些不一样的长程激发怎么改变体系在有限温度下的性质，尤其是是否一般的朗道是否成立。另外我们还希望推广一般的朗道二流体模型到自旋轨道耦合玻色子中，并讨论第二声的可能性。在第一部分，我们将主要依赖Bogoliubov的近似以及超越其近似的量子流体力学来研究有限寿命效应。在第二部分我们将试图构建二流体模型。在这个项目中，我们将只关心一维自选轨道耦合的情形。

17305217.label: Major findings and research outcome
17305217.value: All three objectives have been achieved as detailed below. 1. The finite temperature effect has been discussed with the conclusion that the multi-particle contribution, as well as the spin excitations on the upper branch of the excitation contribute significantly to the normal density. The correction to Landau's formula for normal density is also discussed. Relevant materials are given in a paper that still awaits final polishing (specific discussions are given in Sec. III) (attached). 2. The lifetime of the long wavelength collective mode in a spin-orbit coupled gas has been discussed and is part of the Ph.D thesis of my student Dr. Wai-Ho Tang (attached). In it we have calculated the life time of the long wave length phonon and showed that due to anisotropic nature dictated by the spin-orbit coupling, there is a modified dependences on the wave vector of the long wave length phonon. A detailed study was carried out emphasising on the anisotropic nature of the decay. 3. The hydrodynamic equations have been derived and new hydrodynamic mode, in particular, the existence of persistent spin helical structure, is discussed in a publication in PRL. Its life time is also investigated.

17305217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17305217.value: A promising directions for future study in my opinion is the applications of the set of hydrodynamic equations derived in the work to varying experimental configurations that may be useful in extracting other informations of the spin-orbit coupled Bose gas system. Spin dynamics is in general a less well studied direction in the context of dilute Bose gas, and it is of interest to see what other new phenomena are encoded in these equations, especially in connection with the possible spin-echo type of experiments.

17305217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17305217.value: Spin-orbit coupling is responsible for many of the interesting phenomena in condensed matter physics, including the emergence of topological insulators. In Bose systems, however, such spin-orbit coupling is not natural, but requires engineering using light-atom interactions. Using Raman beams, it is now possible to create spin-orbit coupled Bose gas and investigate its novel physical properties. The study that is carried out in this proposal deals with the hydrodynamics of a many-body system where coarse-grained physical quantities are being investigated. We derive those equations which should be capable of dealing with all situations where one is only interested in low-frequency and long wave length phenomena.

17305317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17305317.value: Erosion redistributes mass at the Earth’s surface and thus act as a major driver of landscape and tectonic evolution across a wide range of length and time scales. However, the upper limits of vertical rock motions and localized mountain-building that may be caused by erosion are newly recognized as poorly understood. On the one hand, focusing of erosion by river and/or glacial processes may generate Earth’s most extreme vertical rock motions. The main evidence for this hypothesis is close spatial association of huge focused-erosional systems with mountain massifs that host Earth’s most rapid crustal-scale rock exhumation, deepest gorges, and youngest exposed intrusions of crustal-melt rocks. On the other hand, the leading examples of such erosion-dominated systems all overlie sharp bends between adjoining convergent plate boundary segments. In this tectonic setting, the down-going plate buckles between the adjoining segments, such that indentation by the folded down-going plate could force dramatic local uplift and exhumation in the overlying crust. Therefore, relative contributions of focused erosion and tectonics at these key sites are unclear. What extremes of vertical rock motion and associated features may result from focused erosion, both for active systems and throughout the geologic record? We can improve our understanding by investigating regions with high rates of rock exhumation that show local erosional focusing against a backdrop of homogeneous tectonics. The Sutlej River of the northwestern Indian Himalaya offers an opportunity: it is the largest of all rivers crossing tectonically-uniform portions of the Himalayan arc. Here, early work shows that the relief, rock exhumation, deformation patterns, and relative youth of exposed crustal-melt rocks are all extreme relative to the bulk of the range. To articulate the crustal response to focused erosion here, we will conduct [1] field-based structural mapping to determine deformed crustal geometries and [2] analytical determinations of mineral cooling ages to constrain rock exhumation rates. Furthermore, these studies will inform – and be informed by – [3] analogue modeling exploration of focused river erosion. Synthesis of our findings will permit reconstruction of the deformation kinematics that respond to focused erosion along the Sutlej River, and thereby provide a comparative framework for future exploration of erosion’s capacity to shape Earth’s crust. 西北印度喜馬拉雅薩特萊傑河沿岸關於集中剝蝕對地殼動力的影響的研究 摘要: 剝蝕作用對地表物質有重新分配的作用, 因此它在很大範圍的時間與空間尺度上是地貌和大地構造的演化的主要推動力。 然而,剝蝕作用所造成的岩石垂直移動與局部造山運動的上限仍是一個新穎卻不甚明瞭的課題。 從一方面來說,河流與(或)冰川的集中剝蝕有可能帶來地球上最強烈的岩石垂直移動。 支援這個假說的主要的證據是在空間上,大型的集中剝蝕系統與高山地塊這一個擁有地球上最迅速的地殼規模的剝露,最深的峽谷與最年輕的殼源岩漿侵入體的地質系統有著強烈的聯繫。 從另一個方面來說,這種集中剝蝕系統的代表性地點全部都與會聚性板塊邊緣的彎折處相重合。 在這種構造背景下,俯衝板塊于彎折處受到擠壓產生褶皺形變,這種形變同樣會造成上覆板塊的強烈局部抬升和剝露。 因此在這些地點,集中剝蝕和構造運動對地殼抬升與剝露的具體貢獻並不是很清楚。 對於曾經或正在活躍的地質系統,集中剝蝕所能製造的岩石垂直運動以及各種伴生現象的極限在哪呢? 通過對擁有均一構造背景以及剝蝕作用所造成的高剝露速率的地區的調查研究,我們可以增進我們對這一問題的理解。 西北印度喜馬拉雅地區的薩特萊傑河給了我們一個機會:這是在所有穿過喜馬拉雅山脈均一構造地區的河流中最大的一條。 對此區域的早期研究證明這裡的地形,岩石剝露情況,構造樣式以及相對年輕的殼源岩漿岩與整個山脈都有著緊密的聯繫。 為了展示地殼對集中剝蝕作用的回應,我們將會(1)進行野外構造填圖從而確定地殼變形構型,以及(2)分析確定礦物冷卻年齡從而約束岩石剝露速率。 更進一步地說,這些研究將會為(3)集中剝蝕作用的類比模型的研究提供資訊,反之亦然。 綜合我們的發現可以允許我們重建薩特萊傑河沿岸對剝蝕作用的變形運動學回應,從而為未來對塑造地 表的剝蝕作用的研究提供一個可參考的案例。

17305317.label: Realisation of objectives
17305317.value: All aspects of this research project are near completion despite major setbacks that have limited our ability to conduct fieldwork and laboratory experiments required for the successful completion of the research project. In the following, we highlight major progress and indicate specific limitations that have delayed the completion, and publication of major findings of the overall research objectives. For Objectives 1 and 2, our initial efforts were limited by our inability to get the PhD student assigned to this study to visit the field site for onsite investigations and data collection. He was denied a visiting visa by the Indian Consulate in Hong Kong, which limited the possibility of conducting fieldwork in the northwestern Indian Himalayan mountain between 2018 and 2020. This was despite many attempts and support from the University of Hong Kong. Achieving Objectives 1 and 2 depends solely on our ability to conduct fieldwork in the target region of the Himalaya mountain. To achieve the objectives, we later attached an MPhil student who conducted the field mapping for objective 1 and also collected rock samples for objective 2, which the PhD student used for the optically stimulated luminescence thermochronometric dating. Presently, all required field sampling, sample analyses, and data modelling have been completed. Data interpretation and initial draft of the manuscripts are ongoing. Below we highlight major progress for the two objectives. Objective 1: This aspect of the overall project has produced an MPhil student Dissertation. All field-related studies, data analysis, and interpretation are completed. She is currently making corrections to examiners' comments on the orally-defended thesis, which is due for submission by the end of July 2022. Preliminary writing of the manuscript is underway as we make an effort to publish our major research findings. Potentially, we hope to submit the original manuscript on or before the end of October, 2022. Objective 2: This aspect will soon be submitted as a part of a PhD Dissertation before the end of October, 2022. The interpretation of the major research findings is nearly complete. We are presently developing the manuscript for our major research findings. Our present major setbacks on some aspects of the manuscript relate to delays from collaborators with regard to the critical modelling aspect of the work. We are on top of this, as we await feedbacks from all the collaborators involved. Major findings will be presented at the 2022 Geological Society of America conference holding at Denver, USA. Eventually, we hope to submit the first draft of the manuscript for publication by the fall of this year. Objective 3: In 2019, our initial efforts yielded very little progress with respect to limitations in the sandbox (analog) experimental setup available at our collaborators laboratory at the Nanjing University, China. Realizing this, our collaborators and I made efforts to setup a more adequate sandbox experimentation that can accommodate two decollement layers (i.e., two geological and mechanically weak layers parallel to bedding that will allow concomitant detachment of deformed layers above the two weak layers from the undeformed layers below). The laboratory was being prepared to achieve this until COVID-19 happened. Our ability to continue the experiment was limited by the Chinese government's restriction on visiting researchers to the University of Nanjing due to the COVID-19 virus (since January 2020). To achieve this, we shifted our effort to adopting three-dimensional kinematic modeling using MOVE software. As the principal investigator, I ensured that the MOVE student license was donated to us at the Department of Earth Sciences, HKU for the purpose of carrying out this aspect of the research project and providing general training to our geology major students up to date. Therefore, our efforts here are still in the pioneering stages, albeit with some major results. Initial efforts have produced one HKU undergraduate dissertation by contributing to the processing and interpretation of the three-dimensional kinematic development of focused erosion-type orogenic development. Ongoing efforts are handled by the PhD student attached to the work, and potentially, our newly employed post-doctoral staff will finalize the validation of all modelling outcomes under my supervision. We hope to complete the first draft of the manuscript for the major research outcome for publication on or before the end of the Fall of 2022. Objective 4: This aspect of the research project depends on the major outcomes of the first three objectives. Since most of these major outcomes required as input data for achieving these objectives are near completion, our speculations for initial draft of the manuscript would be by the end of Winter in 2023. Due to delays and problems mentioned above, we also investigated similar phenomena - how river processes (or river morphology) might inform the kinematic development of an orogenic system - via a somewhat similar contractional system, the Kuqa fold-thrust-belt in NW China. Major outcomes from this study have been accepted for publication in the Journal of Structural Geology (the premier journal for major structural geological studies). This was effectively a means to explore project concepts via an accessible avenue in the light of the other logistical difficulties.

17305317.label: Major findings and research outcome
17305317.value: 1. Our thermochronometry result shows a correlation between shifts in rock cooling during the expansion of the upstream section of the Sutlej River within the last 1 million years. Such a correlation best describes potential focused erosion-controlled rapid rock exhumation along the Sutlej River. This finding is arguably globally unique to the Sutlej River region. 2. Other major shifts in the cooling history of the rock exhumations are related to the period of global climatic change about 2.3 million years ago (i.e., during the Pliocene-Pleistocene transition) and potentially during the Last Glacial Maximum, which peaked around 20–15 thousand years ago. 3. The Sutlej River potentially has the highest rock exhumation rates ever recorded in any orogenic belt in the world since the last 100 thousand years. 4. Our numerical modelling is at a pioneering stage. However, the present simulated results can help inform how and why along-strike structural heterogeneities develop along contractional mountain belt systems worldwide. Major structural predictions from this modelling point out important segments of the mountain belt that could be explored for focused erosion deformation styles.

17305317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17305317.value: With no potential indenter-driven uplift in the Sutlej River region, our newly research findings of rapid exhumation rates along the restricted portion of the Sutlej River region may potentially be a type-example of a focused erosion-dominated mountain building processes. However, the youngest exhumation rates have been obtained in a very limited section along the Sutlej River during this project. Further analysis conducted northward and southward (Wangtu and Baspa Rivers, respectively) may be key to further deepening our understanding of the 3D evolution of this area and better define exhumation rates' acceleration through time. Very low-temperature thermochronology is an appropriate tool to determine exhumation rates and their regional patterns. However, rapidly changing topography distorts the isotherms close to the surface, which commonly introduces complexities to interpreting the cooling ages. Therefore, characterization of the fast and rapid exhumation histories along the Sutlej river requires a thermokinematic modelling approach. For these reasons, future investigation may include numerical modelling of the thermal history using the 2-to-3D thermokinematic program Pecube. Thus, different tectonic models of mountain building processes, will be tested and predicted cooling ages will be compared with observed cooling ages from the huge thermochronological dataset obtained from the Sutlej River region.

17305317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17305317.value: We investigated how river processes may or may not control the development of active mountain ranges, because flowing water can mobilize and remove rock, processes called weathering and erosion. Rapid river erosion of mountain rock can produce concentrated zones of rock deformation, potentially making mountains rise rapidly. To constrain such processes we explored the Sutlej River region of the Himalayan mountains. We used dating methods that can provide timing knowledge for near-surface rock cooling, in combination with a computer modelling approach to visualise the structural variations that may be caused by river erosion during mountain belt development. Our results show a correlation between shifting rates of rock cooling with the timing of a predicted upstream expansion of the Sutlej River within the last 1 million years. Furthermore, newly obtained rates of rock exhumation over the last 10,000 years in the Sutlej region are higher than rates reported from any other mountain belt for this period. Potentially, the Sutlej River region may record the world's most rapid river erosion processes and resultant vertical rock motions during at least the last 1 million years.

17305517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17305517.value: The Dark Matter Particle Explorer (DAMPE) is the first Chinese astronomy space mission in a series of five to emerge from the Chinese Academy of Sciences Strategic Priority Program on Space Science, which was initiated in 2011. After five years of construction and preparation, DAMPE had a successful launch on December 17, 2015 from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in Gansu Province. The science goal of this mission is to hunt for the elusive dark matter, the existence of which is clearly proven by observable gravitational effects, but it has not been directly detected by electromagnetic emissions. Ever since evidence for dark matter was found decades ago, it has been one of the fundamental mysteries in particle physics and cosmology. DAMPE has the thickest calorimeter of any high energy detector ever launched, and it will be able to measure electrons/gamma-ray photons up to 10 TeV (protons to several PeV), which could reveal the particle nature of dark matter. DAMPE will survey the sky at energies much higher than those of existing detectors, such as the Alpha Magnetic Spectrometer (AMS), which is currently attached to the International Space Station, and the NASA's Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope. This proposed research project is going to take advantage of the DAMPE data sets and search for monoenergetic gamma-ray lines as a smoking gun signature of dark matter annihilation. In addition, by forming a diffuse gamma-ray working group, and we expect to make the most sensitive GeV-TeV full sky maps and explore the high energy gamma-ray sky with great precision. DAMPE finished its successful commissioning phase in March 2016, and has already started to collect science data. We have successfully detected the highest energy of electrons and photons ever detected in space up to several TeV. This proposed research program will explore the potential of the gamma-ray science outcome from the DAMPE mission, enhancing the Hong Kong participation to the first Chinese astronomy satellite. 暗物质粒子探测卫星（英文：Dark Matter Particle Explorer，缩写：DAMPE）是中国科学院空间科学战略性先导科技专项中首批立项研制的4颗科学实验卫星之一，是目前世界上观测能段范围最宽、能量分辨率最优的暗物质粒子探测卫星。DAMPE于2015年12月17日8时12分，在酒泉卫星发射中心用长征二号丁运载火箭发射升空。暗物质虽然通过多种天文学效应被广泛认可它的存在，但是暗物质是否具有粒子属性仍然是一个重要的尚未回答的问题。DAMPE具有能量分辨率高、测量能量范围大和本底抑制能力强等优势，将对正负电子与光子探测能力提升至10 TeV，与AMS02、Fermi等空间项目相比有独特的优势。本项目将充分利用伽马射线光子的探测能力去研究暗物质可能产生的电磁信号，并对伽马射线天图成像开展研究，开展高能辐射天体的TeV能段的辐射探测。

17305517.label: Realisation of objectives
17305517.value: The measurement of the energy spectrum of cosmic ray helium nuclei from 70 GeV to 80 TeV using 4.5 years of data recorded by the Dark Matter Particle Explorer (DAMPE) is reported in this work. A hardening of the spectrum is observed at an energy of about 1.3 TeV, similar to previous observations. In addition, a spectral softening at about 34 TeV is revealed for the first time with large statistics and well controlled systematic uncertainties, with an overall significance of 4.3σ. The DAMPE spectral measurements of both cosmic protons and helium nuclei suggest a particle charge dependent softening energy, although with current uncertainties a dependence on the number of nucleons cannot be ruled out.

17305517.label: Major findings and research outcome
17305517.value: Precise measurements of the GCR spectra, particularly for individual species, are mainly from magnetic spectrometers such as the payload for antimatter-matter exploration and light-nuclei astrophysics (PAMELA) and alpha magnetic spectrometer (AMS-02) whose maximum measurable rigidity can reach only few teravolts. Direct measurements at higher energies were mostly done with balloon-borne calorimeter experiments in the past decades, and the uncertainties (both statistical and systematic) are somewhat large, hindering a good understanding of the spectral features above tera-electron-volt energies.

17305517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17305517.value: Galactic cosmic rays (GCRs) are ener- getic particles traveling across the Galaxy as high-energy beams, and are a unique probe to explore the astrophysical particle accelerators and the interstellar medium of the Galaxy [1]. The energy spectrum of GCRs is expected to be a power-law form for energies below the “knee” (at 3–4 PeV) according to the canonical shock acceleration of particles. However, several experiments surprisingly observed changes in the power-law spectral indices γ for protons, helium, and heavy nuclei [2–9]. Specifically, the spectra of GCRs become harder by Δγ ≃ 0.1 − 0.2 at kinetic energies (or rigidities) of several hundred GeV=n (or GV), and become softer again by Δγ ≃ −0.3 at energies of 15–30 TeV (for protons and possibly helium). The deviations from single power law of the spectra motivate extensive investigations for deeper understanding of the acceleration and propagation mechanisms or of new pos- sible GCR sources (e.g., [10]).

17305517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17305517.value: The GCR helium spectrum from 70 GeV to 80 TeV is measured with 4.5 years of the DAMPE data. We confirm the hardening feature of the helium spectrum reported by previous experiments. The hardening is smooth with a hardening energy of ∼1.3 TeV. The DAMPE data further reveals a softening feature at ∼34 TeV with a high significance of 4.3σ. Combined with the proton spectrum, the softening energy is well consistent with a dependence on particle charge, although a dependence on particle mass can not be ruled out yet. These results will provide important implications in understanding GCR acceleration or propagation processes. Extending the DAMPE measure- ments to even higher energies is possible with new data and improved analysis performance.

17305617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17305617.value: One central theme of the contemporary research in number theory is the investigation of equidistributions. The Sato-Tate conjecture is one of the famous problems in this topic, which concerns about the equidisbribution of the Hecke eigenvalues of a GL(2) form over the family of primes. Switching the roles of the prime and the form, Sarnak showed three decades ago the equidistribution of the Hecke eigenvalues at a prime over some families of GL(2) forms. Remarkably the same problem (for different families of forms) was studied and resolved by Serre and independently by Conrey, Duke & Farmer. Nonetheless, the Lang-Trotter conjecture -- a speculation of the precise distribution at each attainable value -- is more challenging and still open today. These problems occupy a salient position in the study of GL(n) Hecke-Maass forms as well. Some fruitful results for the GL(3) case were obtained by Blomer, Buttcane & Raulf, and separately by Zhou. In 2015, Matz & Templier showed, in a preprint, the Sato-Tate equidistribution for the family of GL(n) Hecke-Maass forms. This provides a route to understand the Satake parameters and hence the Hecke eigenvalues associated to the Hecke-Maass forms. In this project, we undertake an investigation toward the Lang-Trotter conjecture for the GL(n) forms. It is known that the Hecke algebra intertwines with many objects in combinatorics. We shall explore new applications on the arithmetic properties underlying the trace formula and on the Littlewood-Richardson rule.

17305617.label: Realisation of objectives
17305617.value: For Objective 1: We gave the first non-trivial estimate for the number of GL(n) Hecke-Maass forms whose Satake parameters at any given prime failing the Generalized Ramanujan Conjecture. For Objective 2: The Lang-Trotter Conjecture in the GL(2) case is generalized to the setting of Satake parameters in the GL(n) case. We derived a quantitative result towards this generalized Lang-Trotter problem. We also showed that the generalized Sato-Tate conjecture is true on average. For Objective 3: We established an explicit result on the main term which gives a sufficient condition for its vanishing. For Objective 4: We derived a multiplication rule for the product of two Schur polynomials under the condition that one of them is of a specific type, and hence we have a method to compute Littlewood-Richardson coefficients of a specific type. For Objective 5: Unfortunately no graduate student is finally recruited.

17305617.label: Major findings and research outcome
17305617.value: In Output 1, the main term of the unweighted trace formula is determined, which is used to demonstrate a vanishing case. A product formula in the spirit of Pieri's rule for Schur polynomials is also derived. In Output 2, a two-dimensional central limit theorem for the eigenvalues of GL(n) Hecke-Maass cusp forms is established. In Output 3, we implement some formulas shown in Output 1. In Output 4, the natural density of primes at which the Satake parameters of a fixed GL(3) Hecke-Maass cusp form fail the Generalized Ramanujan Conjecture is evaluated under certain conditions. In output 5, the number of GL(n) Hecke-Maass forms whose Satake parameters at any fixed prime fail the Generalized Ramanujan Conjecture is evaluated.

17305617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17305617.value: The current research is based on the automorphic Plancherel density theorem for GL(n) Hecke-Maass forms. It would be interesting to consider more general context, i.e. automorphic forms on other groups.

17305617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17305617.value: We successfully extended some important results of GL(2) Hecke-Maass eigenvalues to the setting of GL(n). The generalization from n = 2 to other n's is non-trivial and challenging. In fact the case of GL(3) has attracted plenty of attention and investigations. Our approaches based on the automorphic Plancherel density theorem of Matz and Templier expose some new properties on these eigenvalues.

17305717.label: Project Objectives
17305717.value: We aim to develop the concept of global topology for gapless crystalline topological phases, which may extend the current local topology merely for a single gapless Fermi point to the global one for the whole system of a crystalline (semi)metal. New mathematical techniques would be introduced and developed by us for classifications and characterizations of the crystalline topological phases. In particular, find proper ways to apply the equivariant real K theory for band theories with crystal symmetries, and formulate corresponding topological invariants for topological phases. Our proposed work on crystal-symmetry-enforced topological (semi)metals would deepen our understandings of the relations among the quantum criticality, crystal symmetries, and particularly topology. New fermions are expected to be discovered in this project. In contrast to the Poincaré symmetry for elementary particles in high energy physics, these new fermions may respect certain crystal symmetries and have topological charges, which would lead to exotic structures of internal degrees of freedom, and anomalous responses to external sources including electromagnetic fields, strain, and thermal perturbations. We intend to make theoretical proposals about the simulations of the crystalline topological phases by utilizing cutting-edge technologies for artificial systems, in particular cold atoms and superconducting cirsuits, which may provide persuasive experimental tests with high tunability. Note that physical parameters in real materials are usually restricted in certain ranges which are not very adjustable.
rows: We aim to develop the concept of global topology for gapless crystalline topological phases, which may extend the current local topology merely for a single gapless Fermi point to the global one for the whole system of a crystalline (semi)metal.

New mathematical techniques would be introduced and developed by us for classifications and characterizations of the crystalline topological phases. In particular, find proper ways to apply the equivariant real K theory for band theories with crystal symmetries, and formulate corresponding topological invariants for topological phases.
Our proposed work on crystal-symmetry-enforced topological (semi)metals would deepen our understandings of the relations among the quantum criticality, crystal symmetries, and particularly topology.

17305717.value: 由於拓撲絕緣體的發現，拓撲能帶理論得到了充分的發展。最近人們越來越多地關注無能隙拓撲相，包括外尔和狄拉克半金屬，狄拉克線狀半金属和无能隙的拓扑超导体，並且开始研究由symmorphic和nonsymphic晶體對稱性保護的晶體拓撲相。在這個項目中，我們計劃研究具有晶體對稱性、時間反演對稱性和電荷共軛對稱性的由第一布里淵區全局拓撲屬性保護的無能隙和有能隙的拓撲相。該項目由三個相互關聯的課題組成。首先，我們將根據代數拓扑的K理論或KRG理論，對具有晶體對稱性，時間反轉和電荷共軛對稱性的半金屬和絕緣體的全局帶結構進行拓撲分類。請注意，迄今為止，大部分拓撲半金屬的文章僅僅是動量空間中的局部拓撲分類的應用。雖然不可能窮盡所有的晶體對稱性，但我們將致力於尋找最有理論代表性和最有實驗相關性的拓撲群。第二，我們將探索一類新的晶體拓撲半金屬。由於第一個布里淵區全局性的對稱群表示和可定向性，空間對稱性能夠在這類晶體中直接導致能帶交叉點。我們預計這種空間對稱強制的能帶交叉結構普遍存在於晶體中，奇異的費新型費米子將是它們的準粒子。此外，這將有助于縮短晶體拓撲絕緣体和超導體的對稱性列表。第三，我們將使用包括冷原子和超導電路在內的人造量子系統來模擬拓撲相位及其奇异的拓扑運輸特性，如手性反常，手征磁效應和手征量子反常。與現實的材料相比，量子人造系統的優勢在於它們的高可調性。請注意，在高能物理學中，通常只考慮一個具有龐加萊對稱性的費米點，但在晶體中，通常存在保持晶體對稱性的一組拓撲費米點。

17305717.label: Realisation of objectives
17305717.value: Objective 1 has been satisfactorily achieved. In previous study of topological semimetals, the topological charges of Dirac or Weyl points, nodal lines, nodal surfaces, are mainly individually studied. The famous Nielsen-Ninomiya theorem provides a constraint that the total topological charge of Weyl points in a Brillouin zone is zero. We generalize the theorem to a more general context by considering crystal symmetries and more generally semimetals not only with Fermi points but also higher-dimensional nodal objects, like nodal surfaces and nodal lines. For instance, we find a Weyl point can be accompanied by a nodal Wall, which can absorb the Berry fluxes emitted from the Weyl point. Both the nodal surface and the Weyl point are required by the crystallographic group and time-reversal symmetry, and hence they are not only topologically related, but also related by symmetries. Objective 2 has led to new techniques to analyze both crystal symmetries and topological charges. The conventional kp method can only deal with crystal symmetries, while traditional theory of topological phases is established on KR theory, and therefore can only study topological charges with some internal symmetries, such as time-reversal and particle-hole. We advanced the traditional topological theory of semimetals by analyzing the symmetry structures at high symmetry points in the Brillouin zone by the kp method. In other words, we systematically investigate possible topological semimetals for all kp models at all high symmetry points for all space groups, with new equivariant topological charges being formulated. Furthermore, it is important to observe that these crystalline topological semimetals can be regarded as critical points separating crystalline topological insulator phases. By breaking certain crystal symmetries, some topological semimetals may be gapped and are transformed into crystalline topological insulators. Some of them are typically higher-order topological phases, a recent hot topic. We also systematically investigated possible novel crystalline topological insulators derived in this way. Traditionally the phases of condensed matter systems were classified by Landau’s paradigm of symmetry breaking. Recently, topological orders, particularly symmetry protected topological orders, were introduced into classifying many interesting quantum phases beyond Landau’s paradigm. In the beginning of this field, only a few symmetries, such as time-reversal, particle-hole, mirror and inversion symmetries, were included for symmetry-protected topological orders, and these symmetries have relatively simple structures. Hence, topological concepts are really important, and play a major role in analyzing condensed matter systems with these symmetries. However, when more and more sophisticated symmetries, e.g., some complicated space groups, were included into the paradigm, from our works and other recent works, we found that symmetries play more and more important roles. In some special cases, the constraints from crystal symmetries are so strong, and the symmetry group alone can determine whether the system is in a topological phase or not. Thus, as we expected when proposing the project, there are indeed numerous cases of symmetry-enforced topological phases of matter. With the Poincare symmetry, relativistic fermions like Weyl and Dirac fermions can only take unit topological charges, and have only linear dispersion relations. In our works, we found many new topological fermions protected or enforced by crystal symmetries. These topological fermions may take higher topological charges, and may have non-linear dispersion relations. For instance, a fourfold degenerate Fermi point with linear dispersion relation has Chern number 2, which is determined by space group 52. Moreover, Fermi points with quadratic and cubic dispersion relations are identified by us with nontrivial topological charges usually greater than 1. On the other hand, our thorough studies also show that there is no topological fermion whose order of dispersion relation is greater than 3. Moreover, we also systematically searched nodal-line and nodal-surface topological (semi)metals protected by crystal symmetries. While the topological charges are diverse, the orders of dispersion relations are always less than or equal to 3. For interesting cases of above-mentioned topological fermions, we studied their Landau bands and anomalous topological transport properties. The chiral anomaly plays an elementary role in anomalous transports. For instance, the chiral magnetic effects can be derived from chiral anomaly. Moreover, we show that the patterns of Landau bands can be used as an indicator for nontrivial topological charges. Especially, we recently formulated topological invariants for topological Fermi points through constructing a lattice model for the Landau-level Hamiltonians. Then, the topological invariant is defined as the conventional topological invariant for topological insulators. Furthermore, we proved a mathematically rigorous index theorem which asserts that the topological charge of a topological Fermi point is equal to the topological invariant of the Landau-level Hamiltonian. We proposed how to realize 4D topological insulator in general by artificial systems, that is to project the 4D lattice model onto a 2D or 3D map. We implemented the idea by simulating time-reversal invariant 4D topological insulators in class AI through LC electric-circuit arrays. This is the first experimental proposal to simulate the topological phase. We explicitly demonstrated that the exceptional property of the topological insulators, i.e., their topological invariant is the second Chern number but valued in even integers. We also presented for the first time a simulation of the miminal model of Weyl semimetal by superconductor qubits coupled with microwave cavity. Particularly, the topological charges of Weyl points were clearly verified, and the signature property, namely the chiral magnetic effect, was simulated. Note that the effect has not been realized in any condensed matter system.
