17305717.label: Major findings and research outcome
17305717.value: We have systematically explored topological semimetals, metals and insulators with crystal symmetries. Particularly, we researched all 230 space groups for higher-order topological semimetals, without relativistic symmetry, but protected by crystal symmetries at high symmetry points of the Brillouin zone. Not only numerous Dirac and Weyl like semimetals were identified, more interestingly, higher-order nodal-line semimetals, and even nodal surface metals were systematically investigated in the framework of 230 space groups. Importantly, their topological charges were always elucidated and the topological properties were addressed. Remarkably, the nodal surface metals have recently been experimentally confirmed. Moreover, we found the mixed states of nodal lines, nodal surfaces, and nodal points in the Brillouin zone are constrained by some global conservation laws of topological charges. This is a meaningful generalization of the famous Nielsen-Ninomiya no-go theorem. In the thorough investigation, we have been particularly paid attention to the cases where the topological charges are completely determined by crystal symmetries. That is the topological charges are symmetry enforced when more and more sophisticated symmetries are included into consideration. These observations can help us to have a more balanced view on the concept of symmetry-protected topological orders, complementary to conventional wisdoms. Symmetry may not leave enough degrees of freedom for various topological configurations. In some cases, symmetry constraints are so strong as to enforce topological nontrivial configurations. During the investigation of the relation between topological charges and anomalous transport properties, we established the relationship between topological charges and topological modes of Landau bands. This laid a solid and rigorous foundation for using magnetic fields as a tool to indicating topological charges of fermions. We have successfully simulated topological phases, which cannot be realized by condensed matter systems. Particularly, new methods for simulating higher dimensional topological phases were provided. The minimal model of Weyl semimetals was simulated by superconducting qubits. This demonstrated a new platform for simulating topological phases. More importantly, the chiral magnetic effect was simulated for the first time.

17305717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17305717.value: We propose two directions for further exploration. The first is to analyze the intrinsic relations between symmetries, gauge fields and topological phases. As already observed in the Haldane model of Chern insulators, crystals with gauge fields can host topological charges. But so far, crystal symmetries have not been systematically studied with gauge fields for forming topological phases. The second direction is to compare the groups derived from equivalent K theory and recent development of non-atomic topological insulators. Although for internal symmetries, such as time-reversal and particle-hole, real and complex K theories exactly give the topological classifications of topological phases. But crystal symmetries are more complicated. The directly expected version of K theory for crystal symmetries is the equivariant K theory. But it seems the groups derived from equivariant K theory do not exactly give the topological classifications of crystalline topological phases. It could be possible that even trivial equivariant bundles in equivariant K theory correspond to topological insulators because they cannot be realized by atomic insulators.

17305717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17305717.value: Topology and symmetry are nowadays two fundamental concepts of physics. Symmetry has been a central concept in physics and thoroughly studied, while topology is quite modern and has been emphasized to distinguish it from symmetry properties. In this project we have investigated several interesting aspects of their integration. Our studies show that the two concepts can be closely related, rather than completely distinct concepts. Particularly, sometimes symmetry constraints can enforce topological properties. That is, by preserving certain crystal symmetries, the system can automatically acquire topological properties. Moreover, we show that crystal symmetries can lead to more interesting forms of fermions, such as nodal-line and nodal-surface fermions, which are completely different from relativistic Dirac and Weyl fermions. Furthermore, we provide artificial systems to realize some particularly interesting topological phases. Based on our findings, we have published 14 papers in leading physics journals, including 2 in Phys. Rev. Lett., 10 in Phys. Rev. series, 1 in Optics Express, and 1 in Nat. Sci. Rev..

17305917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17305917.value: 由于生物醫學和低成本納米加工中的潜在价值，納米機械的研究在近期受到了广泛的关注，並制成了各種合成的自驅動微/納米顆粒來模仿能動的藻類細菌的運動。在化學家、 物理學家和電氣工程師的共同努力下，這一領域在過去的幾十年中取得了一些重大進展。從分子到微米級尺度下了許多的奈米機器原型被發展出來。這項擬議的工作將集中在微米和亞微米級的納米機器人技術的發展。 在微/納米馬達系統可以被廣泛應用之前，還面臨幾個重大的挑戰。第一，大多數微/奈米馬達系統中，隨機遷移和不能被遠端控制成為應用的一項困難。第二，大多數奈米馬達的工作需要使用劇毒的化學燃料，如 H2O2和 N2H4，這使納米馬達不能用於體內的應用程式。 受天然的趨光藻類的啟發，我們建議進發展一種基於光電化學反應，並且可以由光驅動和控制的微/納米馬達系統。我們的設計有幾個關鍵的優勢，包括 1） 良好的操縱性、 遷移速度、 3） 生物相容性燃料和 4） 長長波響應，這些優勢將成為納米機器人邁向實用的關鍵。 最近，我們開發了世界上首例可編程式納米樹機器人，成為微/納米馬達研究領域的最新突破。本研究將進一步發展更多的功能的微米機器。此外，我們將發展基於基本的化學和物理原理的數學模型，用來理解納米/微米機器人的運動行為。 本研究將基於幾十年的對光電反應電池 (PEC)的的研究，藉以將光子能量轉換成電能。因為我們的系統與光電反應電池擁有相似的關鍵元件和工作原理，很多以前光電反應電池中使用的材料可以直接應用於我們的系統，以開發高性能通用微/納機器人系統。 我們也將讓本科生有機會參與開創性的研究，以及通過把我們的研究結果向一般公眾發布給一般大眾，使以激發大眾對科學和技術的興趣。

17305917.label: Realisation of objectives
17305917.value: This research is trying to address 5 objectives, where most of them has been fully or exceedingly realized as detailed bellow: 1. Develop high-efficiency light powered micro/nanomotor based on dye sensitized TiO2 which response to visible illumination 2. Develop technique to independent control multiple micro/nanomotors Objectives 1 and 2 are realized by proving that dye-sensitized TiO2 nanomotor demonstrated in aqueous solution, which can be independently addressed with different colors of light. In this work, three different dyes of different absorption spectral is selectively loaded onto the nanotree microswimmer. This is the world-first multicolor controllable nanorobot system. The work is published on Nature Communications (Nat. Commun. 8, (1), 1438). Furthermore, we developed a full spectrum tunable nanomotor system based on the alloyed nanowire, which enables the response spectrum from blue to infrared sensitivity. The work is published on Advanced Functional Materials ( Adv. Funct. Mater. 29, 1901768 (2019)) Additionally, the independent control is also realized with the polarization control mechanism. In this work, a Sb2Se3 nanowire is used, which can strongly respond to linear polarized light. By incorporating two polarizing sensitivity nanomotor, we developed the world's first polarization navigated nanorobot. This work is published on Advanced Materials (Adv. Mater. 1903329) 3. Develop silicon-based micro/nanomotor powered by ultra-low intensity visible and infrared illumination This objective is fully realized with publication on Advanced Materials (Adv. Mater.29, (30), 1701451), where infrared light can be used to power the nanomotor. However, as our research found the energy transfer process is not efficient, we switched our research to the mechanism study and tried to enhance the propulsion efficiency, as the research target 5. 4. Develop optical and fluid dynamic simulation protocol to evaluate light-powered micro/nanomotor This objective is partially realized, where the numerical simulation is used to simulate the propulsion of nanomotor. However, due to limited funding support, no software development is realized. Only a commercial software package is used. 5. Develop bio-compatible redox shuttle for light-powered micro/nanomotor This objective is partially realized, where we studied the energy conversion mechanism in nanomotor propulsion and find a high conversion efficiency, low toxicity redox for biocompatible propulsion. The work is published on ACS Nano (ACS Nano 14, 3, 3272-3280 (2020)). However, this research only addressed the fundamental mechanism due to insufficient funding, which gives a guideline of how to design bio-compatible redox without optimizing the chemical structures. The discovered redox couple is currently commercially available chemicals, while the designed targeted compound is not synthesized.

17305917.label: Major findings and research outcome
17305917.value: In this research, we successfully developed a theory for light-propelled nanomotor and developed a series of controlling mechanisms to navigate the nanomotor inside a complex environment. With this development, we have demonstrated high degree of freedom controlling nanorobot and enhanced the propulsion efficiency of previous light-controlled nanomotor by over 100 times. These findings prepared well for the next level of research for biological compatible nanorobot and application for medical research and beyond. Due to the limited time and funding, this research is mainly focused on fundamental mechanism study and proof-of-concept prototype, where we find it is possible to design nanorobot working in biocompatible environments and control them for designed functions.

17305917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17305917.value: In this research, we developed nanorobot and nanomotor on single-particle level, where the detailed control can be realized. In principle, the biocompatible microswimmer and nanorobotic system can be designed and tested. The next stage of research can be extended into more applied research in two directions: 1. The application of single nanomotor. Although in this research, we demonstrated the nanomotor in a biocompatible environment, it is still a challenge to incorporate all demonstrated functions into single nanorobot. Further research is needed to further integrate our findings and optimize the material system for applicable nanorobot. It is also likely to find novel functions for nanorobot system beyond single nanorobot. 2. The development of nanoswarm. This research developed the nanomotors and robot on single-particle level, it is interesting and important to study how to establish an effective collaboration mechanism between nanorobots and create nanoswarm. As a complex system, many nanorobot can work together for more complex functions, while this mechanism is not available in the current system.

17305917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17305917.value: This research brings dreamed nanorobot a step closer to reality, where we demonstrated micrometer-scale robot could be controlled/navigated and assembled in a complexed environment. Particularly, we demonstrated that the light can be used as a perfect tools for controlling nanorobot with complex maneuvers as well as high-efficiency power sources to propel nanorobot swim at high speed.

17306117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17306117.value: The efficient management of energy conversion and transfer in an ionization process is one of the most important and challenging tasks in mass spectrometry for enhancing detection sensitivity and controlling the extent of ion fragmentation. Surface-Assisted Laser Desorption/Ionization Mass Spectrometry (SALDI-MS) has emerged as an important MS method for sensitive and specific detection of small molecules. In SALDI, noble metal nanoparticles (e.g., gold and silver) are commonly adopted as laser-absorbing substrates, due to their distinctive surface plasmon resonance property for the efficient absorption of photo energy and conversion of energy for analyte desorption/ionization. However, apart from the efficiency of photo absorption and energy conversion, we have recently found that the rate of energy transfer, i.e., the energy flux, for analyte molecules is also critical in enhancing the analytical performance of SALDI-MS, such as detection sensitivity and accessible mass range. Here, we aim to develop a series of Au@metal sulfide nanoparticles (noble metal@semiconductor NPs, including Au@PbS, Au@Ag2S, Au@CdS, and Au@ZnS NPs) as a new class of SALDI substrates. The combination of noble metals and semiconductors in a nanosystem can create a distinctive synergistic property induced by plasmon-exciton coupling, which enables the efficient absorption of laser photo energy, followed by the ultrafast conversion and transfer of energy to analyte molecules. This coupling effect can intensify the energy flux to enhance the laser desorption/ionization efficiency. Specifically, we attempt to utilize the plasmon-exciton coupling to manage the energy conversion/transfer in the nanosystems of the SALDI substrates, so as to control their laser desorption/ionization properties, and thus improve the analytical performance of SALDI-MS. We are going to investigate the effects of AuNP core size, the thickness of the semiconductor shell, and band gap energies on the SALDI-MS detection sensitivities for a variety of small molecules. Theoretical calculation of plasmon-exciton coupling strength of the Au@metal sulfide NP systems and mass spectrometric determination of heat transfer in the SALDI process will also be performed for rationalizing the experimental results. Finally, we will develop this new class of Au@metal sulfide NP substrates for various SALDI-MS-based bioanalytical applications. 在電離過程中，有效地管理能量轉換及轉移，對增強質譜分析的靈敏度及調節離子碎裂的幅度都十分重要。表面輔助激光解吸電離質譜法(Surface-Assisted Laser Desorption/Ionization Mass Spectrometry, SALDI-MS)擁有高檢測靈敏度及高特異度的特點，近年已被廣泛地應用於小分子的分析。由於貴族金屬(如金、銀)納米粒子一般都有表面電漿子共振的特性，能有效地吸收特定波長的光子，加上可以轉換及轉移所吸收的光能，因此經常被用作SALDI-MS中負責吸收激光的基質。另外，我們最近發現，除了基質的吸光和能量轉換效率外，能量從基質轉移到樣本分析物的速率(即能量通量)對SALDI-MS的分析效能(如檢測靈敏度、質量範圍)， 也有關鍵的影響。 本項目計劃製備和鑑定一系列的金@金屬硫化物核殼納米粒子(即貴族金屬核@半導體殼納米粒子，包括金@硫化鉛、金@硫化銀、金@硫化鎘、金@硫化鋅)，以作為新型的SALDI基質。通過結合貴金屬和半導體而成的核殼納米粒子，其具備了表面電漿子與激子耦合的特質，因此擁有高吸光率，而且可以超快地轉換及轉移能量到樣本分析物，並進行解吸電離。我們相信通過表面電漿子與激子耦合而出現的超快能量轉移，可以有效地加強從基質轉移到樣本分析物的能量流，從而提升激光解吸電離的效率和改善SALDI-MS的分析效能。本項目會探討金@金屬硫化物核殼納米粒子的不同參數，如金核心納米粒子的大小、金屬硫化物殼層的厚薄、及金屬硫化物材質的能隙等，對使用金@金屬硫化物核殼納米粒子作為SALDI-MS基質進行小分子分析時的影響。我們會以理論計算方法，找出各種不同金@金屬硫化物核殼納米粒子的表面電漿子與激子耦合的強度，並以質譜法量度不同金@金屬硫化物核殼納米粒子於進行SALDI-MS時對分析物的熱能轉移，綜合各項結果，嘗試拆解金@金屬硫化物核殼納米粒子基質的不同參數，對SALDI-MS小分子分析效能的影響。總括而言，本項目的目標是開發出以貴族金屬核@半導體殼納米粒子的新系列SALDI基質，並藉著它們的表面電漿子與激子耦合特質，開發更有效的SALDI-MS的生物分析方法。

17306117.label: Realisation of objectives
17306117.value: Dr. Kwan-Ming Ng was the original PI when the project began in August 2017. In August 2019, Dr. Ng left HKU to take up the post of Professor at the Department of Chemistry of Shantou University, and Prof. Chi-Ming Che, the Head of Department of Chemistry of HKU, has kindly agreed to take up the role of PI of the project. Nevertheless, Dr. Ng was appointed as an Honorary Assistant Professor of the Department of Chemistry of HKU and became a co-investigator of this project to work closely with Prof. Che to complete this project. All stated objectives have been achieved, including publication of six research articles (and one manuscript is currently under review) and delivery of one presentation at an international conference. The important findings are summarized below: [Objective 1] Synthesis and characterization of Au@metal sulfide core@shell nanoparticles (Au@metal sulfide NPs), including Au@PbS, Au@Ag2S, Au@CdS, and Au@ZnS NPs, have been accomplished. Au@CdS NPs, with Au core diameters of 10 nm, 20 nm, and 40 nm have been prepared and characterized. Spherical Au@Ag2S, Au@PbS, and Au@ZnS with core diameters of 20 nm and 40 nm have also been prepared and characterized. In addition, a new type of materials, plexitonic AuNP-semiconductor quantum dots (AuNP-QDs) assemblies, where QD are CdS, TiO2, or SiO2, have been prepared and characterized, and have been included in the investigation on the effects of plasmon-exciton coupling on laser desorption/ionization (LDI) efficiency. Two research articles have been published in Analytical Chemistry (2020, 92, 5645-5649; 2020, 92, 10262-10267). One has been published in Journal of the American Society for Mass Spectrometry (2021, 32, 815-824), and one submitted to an international journal is currently under review. [Objective 2] To investigate the effect of plasmon-exciton coupling on the LDI efficiency, it has been revealed the AuNP-CdS QD assembly is the best substrate among the assemblies tested. The strongly coupled AuNP-CdS QD assembly generated a large amount of hot electrons with minimal heat loss, resulting in efficient energy transfer to the surrounding molecules to promote desorption and ionization. In contrast, despite the weakly coupled AuNP-TiO2 QD assembly exhibited the strongest local electric field enhancement at the hot spot, the hot electrons in the AuNP-TiO2 QD assembly only have a short lifetime which hinders their transfer and the majority were dissipated as heat by electron-phonon coupling. (Manuscript is currently under review). For the Au@metal sulfide NPs, charge transfer between the core and the shell materials has been discovered to be a critical factor affecting the LDI performance of the core-shell NPs (Analytical Chemistry, 2020, 92, 10262-10267). In particular, the charge separation efficiency of the photoexcited Au-metal sulfide core-shell NPs (Au@PbS, Au@Ag2S, Au@CdS, and Au@ZnS NPs) with shell bandgaps ranging from 0.4eV to 3.8eV was investigated. It has been revealed that the charge separation efficiency in the core-shell NPs is inversely proportional to the shell bandgap (i.e., better charge separation with narrow bandgap shell material), which is believed to be the key reason for the improved LDI performance by narrow bandgap semiconductors. The effect of charge generation on LDI performance has also been studied in details and a new desorption mechanism, namely “charge-driven desorption” has been discovered (Analytical Chemistry, 2020, 92, 5645-5649). Moreover, it was found that the number of hot spots in closely packed AuNPs also significantly affects the LDI performance (Journal of the American Society for Mass Spectrometry, 2021, 32, 815–824). The hot spots of densely packed AuNPs are critical in increasing the average energy of the excited electrons, which could be due to their excitation to much higher energy states with a longer energy tail, by gaining extra electrical potential from the highly enhanced electric field localized at the hot spots. Other parameters including laser fluence and bias voltage also affect the LDI process by increasing the population of photoexcited electrons. [Objective 3] For the development of new LDI-MS bioanalytical applications, plasmonic metal NPs have been developed as efficient mass tags for ion signal amplification and ultrasensitive detection of protein markers in complex biological samples, including urine, cancer cell lysate, and animal tissue samples (Analytica Chimica Acta, 2019, 1055, 1-6; Chemical Communications, 2019, 55, 2761-2764; Analyst, 2020, 145, 6237-6242). The AuNP mass tag has been optimized to achieve a better signal-to-noise ratio for the detection of HPV proteins via immune-capture laser ionization mass spectrometry (Analyst, 2020, 145, 6237-6242). Moreover, the AuNPs have been developed as a multifaceted probe for tissue imaging, providing optical, electron microscopic, enhanced fluorescence, and mass spectrometric signal readouts (Chemical Communications, 2019, 55, 2761-2764). Different small molecules of biological relevance, including drugs (codeine, verapamil, berberine), hormone (testosterone), nutrient (choline), and tetrapeptide (GLLG), were also selected as the model analytes for studying the LDI efficiency (Analytical Chemistry, 2020, 92, 5645-5649). Moreover, a new mass spectrometry method namely “Laser Excitation Mass Spectrometry” for material analysis has been developed. Multiple material properties have been characterized through this technique, including (i) hole generation efficiency (Analytical Chemistry, 2020, 92, 5645-5649), (ii) charge separation efficiency (Analytical Chemistry, 2020, 92, 10262-10267), (iii) energetics and population density of photoexcited electrons (Journal of the American Society for Mass Spectrometry, 2021, 32, 815–824), (iv) hot electron transfer and heat transfer efficiency on plexcitonic system (manuscript is currently under review).

17306117.label: Major findings and research outcome
17306117.value: [1] Closely packed AuNPs has been successfully prepared as the effective substrate for studying the mechanism of SALDI-MS. The number of hot spots in the closely packed AuNPs is identified to be critical in increasing the average energy of the excited electrons. With the extra electrical potential from the highly enhanced electric field localized at the hot spots, electrons are excited to much higher energy states with longer energy tails for promoting the laser desorption/ionization processes. [2] AuNP-CdS QD assembly has been successfully prepared. The outstanding LDI performance of strongly coupled AuNP-CdS QD assembly is attributed to the generation of Rabi state for energy trapping, allowing the generation of a large amount of hot electrons with minimal heat loss, resulting in efficient energy transfer to surrounding molecules to promote the laser desorption/ionization processes. [3] With the use of juglone as an electron scavenger, the quantity of holes in the photoexcited AuNPs can be controlled and charge-driven desorption mechanism has been discovered as a vital desorption mechanism in the laser desorption/ionization processes. [4] Au@PbS, Au@Ag2S, Au@CdS and Au@ZnS nanoparticles have been successfully synthesized and characterized. In the Au core-metal sulfide shell nanoparticles, the charge separation efficiency was found to be inversely proportional to the bandgap of shell material. [5] The plasmonic AuNPs has been successfully developed as a multifaceted probe for tissue imaging, providing optical, electron microscopic, enhanced fluorescence, and mass spectrometric signal readouts. [6] A new mass spectrometry method based on the laser ionization of plasmonic metal nanoparticles for the analysis of proteins has been developed. Ultrasensitive detection of protein markers in complex biological samples has been achieved, including urine, cancer cell lysate, and animal tissue samples. [7] A novel mass spectrometry method namely “Laser Excitation Mass Spectrometry” for material analysis has been developed. Multiple material properties have been characterized through this technique, including (i) hole generation efficiency, (ii) charge separation efficiency, (iii) energetics and population density of photoexcited electrons, (iv) hot electron transfer and heat transfer efficiency. [8] The above major findings and outcome have been published in the leading international chemistry journals, including two articles in Analytical Chemistry, one in Chemical Communications, one in Analytica Chimica Acta, one in Analyst, one in Journal of the American Society for Mass Spectrometry. Among them, two research articles have been selected as front covers. One manuscript is currently under review. One presentation has been made at an international conference.

17306117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17306117.value: [1] Development of new LDI substrate by maximizing the hot electron generation and charge transfer efficiency. [2] Development of new mass tags with outstanding ion generation efficiency for promoting the sensitivity of protein detection and quantification.

17306117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17306117.value: Surface-assisted laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry (SALDI-MS) has become an important MS method for the analysis of small molecules, and has been widely applied to various aspects of bioanalysis, environmental, food, pharmaceutical and forensic sample analysis. However, the detection sensitivity of the method is highly dependent on the efficient utilization of laser energy for the desorption and ionization processes. In this project, we have successfully developed plasmonic metal nanoparticles, including gold nanoparticles, gold nanoparticle-based core-shell and self-assembly type of substrates, to enhance the utilization of laser energy for promoting the analytical performance of SALDI-MS, for the sensitive detection of different biomolecules, ranging from small molecules (including drug, hormone, nutrient, peptide) to macromolecule (protein). Apart from new analytical applications, a novel method “Laser Excitation Mass Spectrometry”, has also been developed for photoactive material analysis. Several important material properties have been characterized using this technique, including energetics and population density of photoexcited electrons, hole generation efficiency, charge separation efficiency, hot electron transfer and heat transfer efficiency. With a thorough understanding of how the LDI process is controlled by the material properties, laser absorbing substrates can be rationally designed to achieve ultrasensitive detection of biomolecules, which remains to be a challenge for SALDI-MS. These remarkable findings have been published in various international academic journals including Analytical Chemistry, Chemical Communications, Analytica Chimica Acta, Analyst, and Journal of the American Society for Mass Spectrometry.

17306217.label: Project Objectives

17306217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17306217.value: South China is one of the most important continental blocks that constitute present-day Southeast Asia. The early Paleozoic to early Mesozoic development of South China was largely involved in crustal reworking punctuated by two stages of orogenesis, i.e., the Kwangsian and Indosinian orogenies. In the Chinese literature, both the Kwangsian and Indosinian orogenies are interpreted to have occurred in an intraplate setting due to the lack of ophiolites and arc magmatism. However, how the intraplate geodynamics evolved and the role of subduction and collision of boundary plates in controlling the South China’s development are poorly understood or controversial as reflected in various mutually-excluded tectonic models. Specifically, the Kwangsian intraplate deformation is attributed to northwestward underthrusting or overthrusting of the Cathaysia continent, or combined underthrusting of the Yangtze continent and an eastern terrane beneath the Cathaysia continent, whereas the Indosinian orogeny in South China is variously interpreted as resulting from boundary continental collision to the south and north, or slab subduction to the southeast, or intraplate oblique subduction. All of these controversies rise from the lack of rigorous structural and metamorphic constraints, which has hampered the further understanding of the regional geological framework during crustal reworking. North Cathaysia is an ideal area to resolve the above controversial issues as it consists of numerous Proterozoic basement rocks with various key structural elements and metamorphic assemblages. This forms the justification for this project in which we will undertake an integrated study, combining structural, metamorphic, geochronological and thermochronological analysis, in order to determine geometries, kinematics, ages and P-T conditions of key structural/metamorphic units in north Cathaysia. The outcomes of the project will serve to establish a well-constrained, episodic tectono-thermal history of north Cathaysia during Ordovician-Triassic time. A synthesis of our data with previous work concerning many other adjacent regions will enable us to test existing models and invoke more plausible explanations for the Kwangsian and Indosinian crustal reworking of South China. The explanations will provide important insights into understanding of (1) the link between South China’s Kwangsian reworking and the Gondwana assembly; and (2) the role of Indosinian slab subduction, terrene accretion/collision in shaping East Asia. 华南是东亚最重要陆块之一。华南早古生代至早中生代的发展主要受控于加里东期和印支期两个阶段地壳再造。由于缺乏蛇绿岩和弧岩浆作用，一般认为这两期造山作用发生于板内环境。 然而，板内动力学如何作用和板缘俯冲碰撞如何控制华南的演化目前还不清楚，这反映在目前所提出的各种构造模式和动力学解释上， 其中包括加里东期板内变形是控制华夏陆块北西向俯冲或仰冲还是导致扬子陆块与一个东部地块一起想华夏陆块下俯冲？ 华南印支期造山事件也有各种解释，包括该事件是华南陆块南、北缘碰撞的结果，是板片向东南方向俯冲的结果，或是板内斜向俯冲的结果。所有这些争论都是源于缺少足够的变形与变质的限制，这也限制了对华南地壳再造地质格架的进一步了解。华夏北部广泛出露元古代基底岩石以及韧性组构和变质矿物组合，它们是解决上述争论和了解地壳完整再造历史的一把钥匙。在这个项目中，我们将开展构造、变质、年代学和热年代学综合研究，以便确定华夏北部主要关键构造变质单元的几何形体、动力学标志、 形成年龄和温压条件。项目研究结果将有助于限定华夏北部奥陶至三叠时期构造热演化历史。在结合前人工作基础上，本项目新数据将有助于检验现存的各种模式并建立一个新的有关华南加里东期和印支期地壳再造的可行解释，以便更好地理解（1）华南加里东期再造与冈瓦纳聚合的关系和（2）印支期板片俯冲及地体增生碰撞在东亚大陆形成中的作用。

17306217.label: Realisation of objectives
17306217.value: We have successfully completed all parts of the six objectives designed for this project as follows: Objective 1 is to determine the spatial distribution of major structural units in the north Cathaysia, and to clarify the geometric and kinematic features, mineral assemblages of individual structural zones through field investigations. This objective was completed through four times of fieldwork (January 3-13, 2018; October 31-November 15, 2017, March 2-20, 2019 and June 1-15, 2020). In the field, the Principal Investigator (Guochun Zhao), three CIs (Changqing Yin, Jianhua Li, and Jinlong Yao) and their postgraduates carried out extensive field investigations along two NW-trending transects in the north Cathaysia. We conducted large amounts of structural measurements, including fold axes, foliations, lineations, and shear criteria (e.g., s-c fabrics, asymmetrical boudins, and σ and δ porphyroclasts), clarified the overprinting relationships of main structures, and finally established the deformation sequences. In addition, we collected a total of ~200 rock samples and conducted petrographic, structural and geochronological studies on these samples; their results will be described below. Objective 2 is to carry out microstructural and quartz lattice-preferred orientation studies, aiming at (1) determining the kinematics and deformation temperatures of individual ductile shear zones, and (2) establishing correlations with adjacent kinematically compatible structures. This objective has been completed through combined structural, microstructural and EBSD analyses. We clarified the early Paleozoic and early Mesozoic structural features in different domains. The early Paleozoic deformation in the Wuyishan and Chencai domains is featured by sinistral oblique shearing along NE-trending steep zones; the shear deformation was accompanied by amphibolite facies metamorphism at temperatures of >550 °C (locally even>650 °C). The early Mesozoic deformation in the Badu domain is featured by at least three episodes (D1 to D3): D1 features rootless, tight-isoclinal folds (F1), a shallowly-dipping foliation (S1), and local top-to-E shear; D2 a gentle-dipping foliation (S2), and orogen-parallel, top-the S shear; D3 ~ open to tight, upright folds with subhorizontal axes reflective of orogen-normal, ~E-W shortening. The research outcomes of this objective have led to publication of a paper in Journal of Structural Geology (See Research Output No. 6). Another paper entitled “Localized Triassic orogen-subparallel crustal flow in South China: structural and time constraints from the Badu complex” has been finished and will be submitted to Tectonics. Objective 3 is to undertake metamorphic studies on mineral assemblages, reaction relations, mineral compositions, thermobarometric P-T calculations and SIMS zircon U-Pb ages of high-pressure mafic granulites in the Badu complex, aiming at reconstructing their metamorphic sequences and P-T paths during Indosinian reworking. We determine the mineral assemblages of three metamorphic stages: eclogite-facies stage (M1): garnet + clinopyroxene (omphacite) + hornblende + rutile + quartz; high-pressure granulite-facies stage (M2): garnet + clinopyroxene + plagioclase + hornblende + rutile + quartz in the matrix; and amphibolite retrograde stage (M3): hornblende + plagioclase + ilmenite + quartz symplectites as rims of garnet porphyroblasts. Conventional geothermometers and geobarometers in combination with phase equilibria modelling constrain P-T conditions to 15.8-18.2 kbar/625-690 ℃ (M1), 11.8-14.5 kbar/788-806 ℃ (M2) and 5.4-6.4 kbar/613-668 ℃ (M3), respectively. They define a clockwise P–T path involving a nearly isothermal decompression. SIMS zircon U-Pb dating coupled with trace element analysis dates the high-pressure metamorphism at 240-244 Ma. The research outcomes of this objective have been reflected in a manuscript entitled “Metamorphism and geochronology of high-pressure mafic granulites (retrograded eclogites?) in East Cathaysia Block of South China: Implications for its tectonic evolution in the Mesozoic” that has been submitted to GSA Bulletin and is now in revision. Objective 4 is to determine the timing of deformation and metamorphism by dating pre- to post-kinematic igneous dykes/veins and metamorphic rocks using the U-Pb zircon geochronology. This objective has been completed by utilizing LA-ICP-MS/ SHRIMP U–Pb zircon dating of igneous dykes/veins and metamorphic rocks from the Wuyishan, Chencai and Badu domains. Our geochronological data suggest that the sinistral oblique shearing along NE-trending zones in north Cathaysia, accompanied by amphibolite facies metamorphism and syn-orogenic crustal anatexis, initiated at ~460 Ma and might have lasted till ~420 Ma. This shortening-related event was followed by post-orogenic extension that was featured by 415-400 Ma A-type granitoids and diabases. In the Badu domain, we constrain the time of D1 to 251-237 Ma, and D2-D3 to ~250-221 Ma, respectively. Totally 2 papers reflecting the research outcomes of this objective have been published (see Research Outputs No.6, No. 7 in the next section). Objective 5 is to clarify syn-kinematic flow and tectonic exhumation of the north Cathaysia during crustal reworking, by conducting Ar-Ar dating of minerals (amphibole, muscovite, and biotite) with overlapping closure temperatures from ductile shear zones. In the Chencai and Wuyishan domains, our thermochronological data demonstrate that the sinistral oblique shearing terminated before 400 Ma and was followed by cooling through ~450–350°C at ~400-370 Ma. In the Badu domain, we established its cooling paths using the published P–T–t data and the available Ar/Ar cooling ages as follows: from ~850 to 650 ℃ between ~249–240 Ma, with rates of ~22–50 °C/Myr, from ~650 to ~375 ℃ between ~245–228 Ma, with rates of ~16–23 °C/Myr, and from ~375 to ~325 ℃ between ~228–204 Ma at ~2 °C/Myr. Parts of the research outcomes have been published in Research Output No.6. Objective 6 is to establish a well-constrained, Ordovician-Triassic tectono-thermal history of the north Cathaysia, to give more plausible explanations for the Kwangsian and Indosinian crustal reworking of South China. The synthesis of our results with published data allows delineating an Early Paleozoic orogen that extends through the Jiangnan domain into the northeast Cathaysia domain, with the southeast Yangtze acting as a foreland belt. The early Paleozoic orogeny possibly resulted from the continued Yangtze-Cathaysia convergence, externally driven by the suturing of south China with Australia. In the Badu complex, the combination of our and published data allows tracing a ~25-km-wide, ~NNE-striking, high-strain zone that represents a local but distinct Triassic anomaly in the vast (~1600-km-wide) South China continent. Therein the relic high-pressure metamorphism, orogen-subparallel crustal flow, and ~E-W shortening imply localized underthrusting of the Coastal terrane beneath the Wuyishan terrane within the regional intraplate tectonic setting. Total 6 papers reflecting the research outcomes of this objective have been published (see Research Outputs No1, No.2, No. 6, No. 7, No. 10, No. 12 in the next section).

17306217.label: Major findings and research outcome
17306217.value: In the last three years, the PI and his research group have carried out extensive and comprehensive investigations on Paleozoic and early Mesozoic structures and plutons in north Cathaysia and obtained large amounts of new data and interpretations which are reflected in 13 refereed papers published in leading international journals including EPSL, Tectonics, GSA Bulletin, Earth-Science Reviews, etc (see Publications listed in Part C). We summarize our major findings and research outcomes as follows: 1. Early Paleozoic NW-SE contraction, dated at 460–420Ma, gave rise to sinistral oblique shearing along NE-SW striking zones, accompanied by amphibolite facies metamorphism in the Wuyishan and Chencai domains, north Cathaysia. The synthesis of our data with previous work allows us to delineate an Early Paleozoic orogen that extends through the Jiangnan domain into the northeast Cathaysia area, with the southeast Yangtze acting as a foreland belt. This orogeny might result from the continued Yangtze-Cathaysia convergence externally driven by the suturing of south China with Australia. (see Research Outputs No. 1, 2 and 6). 2. The localized intense ductile shearing and high-grade metamorphism along the Shaoxing-Jiangshan fault zone reflect tectonic reactivation of this pre-existing mechanical weakness during the early Paleozoic orogeny. (see Research Output No. 6). 3. We recognized ~415-400 Ma A-type granitoids and diabases that are interpreted as post-orogenic, formed during extensional collapse of thickened crust. Their generation indicates that South China experienced crustal exten¬sion during the Early Devonian. The exten¬sion occurred coevally with global rifting that led to the separation of the continental blocks of eastern Asia from eastern Gondwana, which was associated with the Early Devo¬nian opening of the paleo–Tethys Ocean. (see Research Outputs No. 1, No. 2 and No. 7). 4. We define three deformation episodes (D1-D3) dominating structural evolution of the Badu complex. D1 characterizes rootless, tight-isoclinal folds (F1), and a relic shallow-dipping foliation (S1) with unclear kinematics; D2 a gentle-dipping foliation (S2) and a ~N-S lineation (L2) with orogen-subparallel, top-S shear; D3 extensive ~N-trending folds with subhorizontal axes reflecting orogen-normal, ~E-W shortening. By combining our data with published work on the Badu complex, we trace a ~25-km-wide, ~NNE-striking, high-strain zone that represents a local but distinct Triassic anomaly in the vast South China continent. Its generation implies the localized underthrusting of the Coastal terrane beneath the Wuyishan terrane during the intraplate orogeny within South China.

17306217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17306217.value: Our results from this project suggests that the Badu complex involved significant orogen-parallel flow followed by orogen-normal, ~E-W shortening in Triassic time. Based on a compilation of our and published data, we identified a ~25-km-wide, ~NNE-striking, high-strain zone that represents a local but distinct Triassic anomaly in the vast (~1600-km-wide) South China continent. We interpret that the high-strain deformation and high-grade metamorphism within this zone indicate localized underthrusting during the intraplate orogeny within South China. The localized nature of the high-strain zone calls for the reactivation of a pre-Triassic lithospheric heterogeneity, the Zhenghe-Dapu fault zone; this mandates tectonic studies to clarify its evolution. In addition, the origin of the localized crustal underthrusting within an overall intraplate tectonic setting will stimulate more numerical and deep-seismic studies. The above-stated statements consistently point to a key issue that is extremely important for clarifying the Mesozoic tectonic framework of eastern South China, i.e., the surface structural deformation and deep crustal architecture of the Zhenghe-Dapu fault zone, which forms a justification for a potential RGC GRF project that will be submitted to RGC in future.

17306217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17306217.value: South China is one of the most important continental terranes that constitute present-day Southeast Asia. Its Paleozoic to Mesozoic tectonic evolution involved significant crustal reworking. However, how the continental crust was reworked and the related association with boundary plate subduction and collision geodynamics remain poorly determined, due to the lack of careful structural fieldwork and the resultant weakly linked analytical work. This project (Hong Kong RGC 17306217) aims at overcoming such weaknesses by undertaking an integrated study, combining structural, geochronological and thermochronological analyses of key tectonic units in the north Cathaysia. We recognized that the north Cathaysia involved crustal shortening accommodated by coeval thrusting and sinistral oblique shearing along NE-SW striking zones under amphibolite facies conditions in the early Paleozoic (~460-420 Ma), which were followed by significant orogen-parallel flow and orogen-normal, ~E-W shortening in the Triassic (~250-228 Ma). The results of this project lead us to propose a new model involving the continued Yangtze-Cathaysia convergence externally driven by the suturing of south China with Australia during the early Paleozoic, and the localized underthrusting during the Triassic intraplate orogeny within South China.

17307017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17307017.value: 含鉍化合物用於治療各種疾病已超過 150 年。鉍化合物與抗生素的三聯和四聯療法廣泛應治療幽門螺桿菌感染。更重要的是，鉍化合物是有效地消除抗生素耐藥菌種的幽門桿菌並對人體的健康無任何毒性，說明鉍的潛在藥用應用。 為了生存和寄生在人類的胃腸道，幽門螺桿菌採用複雜的金屬蛋白為代謝提供能量，保持增長的最佳 pH 值，獲得基本金屬營養和環境壓力的防禦系統。這種系統的功能中斷會導致細菌定植及發病機制。已發表的報告指出銀、 鎵和鉍金屬-製劑可能會中斷細菌多個通路和過程，從而發揮優良其的抗菌作用。 我們最新的金屬組學和金屬蛋白質組學結果清楚顯示鉍藥物也表現出多靶點，揭示其抑制幽門螺桿菌的獨特機制。為了驗證生物學信息結果，我們在發現的藥物靶標進行了生物活性測定，證明幽門螺桿菌酶的活性受到鉍的明顯抑制後。因此，我們的目標是運用生物化學和生物物理技術，全面研究有關提示幽門螺桿菌臨床批准鉍藥物的抗菌作用的分子機制。 具體而言，申請人打算： (1) 假定蛋白質標分子的克隆，表達和純化; (2) 表徵藥物-蛋白質相互作用; (3) 通過生物鑒定，驗證基於鉍的抗菌藥物如何影響蛋白質標靶; (4) 基於鉍金屬劑對其他病原體，銅綠假單胞菌、 葡萄球菌等致病細菌的生物信息學研究; (5) 通過 x 射線晶體學分析藥物-蛋白質相互作用， 闡明金屬藥物的設計新穎見解。 本研究將會拓展我們的金屬-殺菌藥物對致病性微生物，特別是那些耐藥菌株。這項研究的長期目標是建立金屬在醫學中的數據庫並建立新穎的平臺用於設計更好的殺菌劑。

17307017.label: Realisation of objectives
17307017.value: Human bodies host exceedingly large numbers of bacteria, which are closely related to human health and disease, with the majority of them being found in the guts. A bacterial infection may occur when harmful bacteria intrude into our body. Bacteria have been known to require certain metal ions for their survival and virulence, particularly those under extreme conditions (e.g. Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori)). Ironically, some metal complexes show antibacterial effects and in fact, have been used clinically for decades for the treatment of some pathogenic diseases even after the wide application of antibiotics. Increased incidence of the gut dysbiosis has been known to be associated with several diseases from gastric ulcer diarrhea to life-style-relevant diseases such as diabetes. Bismuth-based drugs have been used for the treatment of H. pylori infection and diarrhea. Based on the PI and Co-I’s expertise on metalloproteomics in combination with quantitative proteomics, bioinformatics, metabolomics and bioassay, we have built up an integrative approach consisting of metalloproteomics, metabolomics, transcriptomics and even deep learning. We then employed this systemic approach to unveil the molecular mechanisms of the antimicrobial action of bismuth drugs in pathogens. We have successfully completed the five objectives as revealed from the granted patents and publications. Through this project, we also open a new revenue for fighting against infections caused by superbugs and new projects were awarded (RGC and ITF). (i) The PI and Co-I have established a leading integrative platform for matching ‘metals-to-proteins’. We have synthesized a series of fluorescent agent, consisting of a ﬂuorophore with an arylazide (N3-), a linker and a chelate (nitrilotriacetate, NTA). Upon metal bound (e.g. Bi3+), the probe, i.e. metal-NTA-fluorophore, can enter into cells readily and anchor the target protein via photo activation. Bismuth-bound protein in H. pylori can be subsequently identified and analyzed. New information was obtained. A Chinese patent was granted in March 2020, for the novel fluorescent agent (Chinese Patent: ZL201580010957.7). A series of papers was published based on the probe (please see publication lists). (ii) We have integrated metalloproteomics with transcriptomics and metabolomics to examine cellular responses to stimuli or uncover the mechanism of action of a drug (using bismuth antibacterial drug as a showcase) at a system level. Our multi-omics data together with bioassays demonstrated the impact of bismuth on a diverse array of intracellular pathways, particularly, disruption of central carbon metabolism is systematically evaluated as a primary bismuth-targeting system in H. pylori. Through temporal dynamics proﬁling, we show that bismuth initially perturbs the TCA cycle and then urease activity, followed by the induction of oxidative stress and inhibition of energy production, and in the meantime, induces extensive down-regulation in H. pylori metabolome. Our study provide critical knowledge on the inhibitory actions of bismuth and provides a novel systematic perspective of H. pylori in response to a clinical drug, sheding light on enhanced therapeutic methodologies. The approach can readily be extended to other metalloagents. Upon publication of the work in Chemical Science (2018, 9, 7488), a commentary was published in ChemistryWorld (2018, September issue, pp44-45) entitled “bismuth drugs kill bacteria by disrupting metabolism” to promote the potential of the ‘kitchen sink of omics techniques’. We have used the approach to dig out proteome of silver and silver nanoparticles in bacteria for the first time (PLOS Biol. 2019 and Nature Comm 2021). (iii) We then developed an approach to predict loss-of-function mutation in metal-binding proteins using deep learning. Identification of ‘cracks’ will be invaluable to biologists and medical doctors for our understanding and treatment of disease. This work opens a new horizon on metalloproteins, metals in medicine and even protein-protein recognition. A news&views was published together with the paper in the same issue of Nature Machine Intelligence (2019, 1(12), 553-554). (iv) We have used the Bi-loased fluorescence probe and found that bismuth drugs suppress the key pathogen of periodontal disease, i.e. Porphyromonas gingivalis, in its planktonic, biofilm and intracellular states, through perturbing iron acquisition, disturbing energy metabolism and virulence, as well as deactivating multiple enzymes (Metallomics, 2019, 11, 1207). The work was also featured on the back cover of the issue. (v) We have trained junior scientists as revealed from their publications and awards. An agreement was also signed between the Chinese Academy of Sciences and HKU to establish a join laboratory on ‘metals on health and environment’. As proposed, the long-term goal of this proposed research is to establish a leading “Center for Metals in Medicine” in the region using integrative Metalloproteomics and Metabolomics (M2-omics). In summary, we have successfully completed the project and RGC is acknowledged in all publications and reviews. The only minor suggestion is to increase the fund size of GRF project.

17307017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17307017.value: Human bodies host exceedingly large numbers of bacteria with the majority of them being found in the guts. Bacteria have been known to require certain metal ions for their survival and virulence. Bismuth-based drugs have been used for the treatment of Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection and diarrhea caused by bacterial infection, surprisingly remains to be effective with no drug resistant bacteria being observed. In this project, we have developed a systemic approach for matching metals-to-proteins, and subsequently employ it to unveil the molecular mechanisms of the antimicrobial action of clinically-approved bismuth drugs in pathogen using H. pylori as a showcase. We then have integrated metalloproteomics with transcriptomics and metabolomics and examined the response of H. pylori to a bismuth drug. Our multi-omics data together with bioassays reveal the impact of bismuth on a diverse array of intracellular pathways. Through temporal dynamics proﬁling, we demonstrate that bismuth initially perturbs the TCA cycle, urease activity followed by the induction of oxidative stress. Our discoveries improved our understanding on the mechanism of action of metallodrugs against pathogens, accordingly providing a basis on the design of new antimicrobial agents including against resistant bacteria. Junior scientists have been trained through this project.

17307117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17307117.value: Loess/palaeosol sequences in Chinese loess plateau have been studied for reconstruction of past climate change because their depositional processes change with climate. The loess deposits interbeded with palaeosols in Chinese loess plateau have been equated with alternations of Pleistocene arid and humid periods. It has been regarded as the best territorial records of climate change. The fifth palaeosol is one of the most well developed soils in the Chinese loess plateau, and has been used as a ‘marker’ for correlation. It has been regarded as a signature of “three red stripes”. The chronology of the Pleistocene loess is poorly established, because of lack of suitable dating methods for ages older than 300 thousand years (ka). Alternatively, correlations with deep-sea sediments were used to get relative ages for the climate changes of Pleistocene, except the last 300 ka. For the fifth palaeosol, different age ranges, 479-621 ka of deep-sea oxygen isotope stages 13 and 15, and 479-531 ka of stage 13, were suggested from such correlations, consequently lead to different warm/cool cycles of the climate change. This project aims to develop the methodology of luminescence dating for older loess samples, and provide reliable chronological evidence to the fifth palaeosol. The similarity and differences of climate change between recorded in loess and deep-sea sediments will be explored. 黃土的沉積過程會因氣候而改變，由此黃土高原的黃土／古土壤序列廣泛應用於古氣候的重建。黃土和夾插中間的古土壤分別反映了乾旱和潮濕的氣候時期。黃土成為陸地上氣候變化的最好紀錄。 第五古土壤是發育最好的土壤，被稱作“紅三條”為標記用於黃土高原的標誌和對比。可是，由於缺乏適用於比300千年老的測年方法，它所形成的年代並不明確，而且充滿爭議。同深海沉積物對比得到兩組年齡範圍。一是在479-621千年之間；對應於深海氧同位素的第13和15節之間。另一範圍在479-531千年之間；對應於深海氧同位素的第13節。由此導致不同的冷／熱（乾／濕）氣候迴旋下形成了第五古土壤。 本項目以開發釋光測年方法為目標，用於年老黃土樣品測定。同時為第五古土壤提供可靠的年代學依據。研究將揭示黃土和深海沉積物對全球氣候變化紀錄的異同之處。

17307117.label: Realisation of objectives
17307117.value: Fieldwork and sample collection Fieldwork and sample collection were carried out in the first two years of the project. Luochuan and Jingbian sites were investigated. Intensive sampling with the sections Potou and Guojialiang was achieved in the exposed profiles. An interval of 20 cm was applied to sampling loess/palaesol for the whole section above the fifth palaesol in Potou section. These samples were used to study the continuality and deposition rates in the region. For the fifth palaeosol, OSL samples will be collected in the interval of 10cm. Modern dust deposits, analogous to loess/palaeosol, were collected to study the luminescence characteristics, in particular the saturating doses. They provide direct information on the saturation doses, resetting and regenerating of OSL signals. Samples from the 15th loess were collected, as they were treated as the “field saturated” samples. Which have more grains in fine sand sizes. They will be used as testing samples for dose recovery and other justifying tests for the protocols. Special containers and sampling strategies were used to meet the requirements; these include using light tight container and water content measurement. Development of suitable protocols for luminescence dating Several protocols were developed and tested. For the same sample K-feldspar grains, we used MET-pIRIR, pIRIR (50,290), pIRIR(200,290) and MAR protocols to identify the most appropriate one for loess dating. It is found that the MAR protocol gives the largest equivalent doses/ages. This protocol was widely used in the late stage of the study to dating samples in Potou section. We have studied the apparent age gap shown in the results of OSL dating in Luochuan site. An age hiatus of 10 – 20 ka is found at the top of L2 of the loess/palaeosol sequences, with the age of the calcrete nodules located on the S1/L2 boundary is significantly older than the palaeosol sample immediately above. The overestimation of the age of calcrete nodule is a result of changing in the dose rate due to Ca accretion post to deposition. The dose rate decreased with the accretion of calcium carbonate materials. Age hiatus at the top of L2 is also an apparent result of underestimation of dose rate. We have developed protocols using standard growth curves. Standardised growth curves (SGCs) were established for extracts of potassium feldspar (K-feldspar), plagioclase and polymineral grains from various geological settings (deserts, loess, lake or fluvial deposits) from Northern China. Regenerative-dose normalisation was applied for the SGC construction. The shapes of the SGCs of K-feldspar vary between IRSL signals measured at different temperatures. For coarse grains (63-180 μm), the SGCs of the K-feldspar, plagioclase and polymineral fractions are close to each other. However, the polymineral fine grains (4-11 μm) have a distinct SGC from the coarse-grain fractions. It may be caused by the difference in alpha irradiation. With the same test dose used, the SGC De values estimated from the SGCs are identical with the De values generated from individual dose response curves. Several attempts have been made to date samples older than the fifth palaesol. However, it was found that only samples younger than 400ka can be dated with the protocols studied. This is largely due to the combined problems of anomalous fading of pIRIR signals and saturation of the traps. As a result, the equivalent doses for samples bellow fifth palaesol were underestimated and given equilibria equivalent doses about 1600~1800Gy. With uncertainties and difference in dose rates among the samples, we concluded that the current developed protocols can reliably date samples younger than 450ka, i.e. above and including the fourth palaesol. Protocols for very young sediments and poorly bleached samples were also studied. It is suggested that single grain dating can be effectively achieved when the quartz grains were extremely dim. The protocols have been used for poorly sorted fluvial sediments. Dating programme for loess samples We have dated more than 160 samples from Potou section. As mentioned above, only samples younger than 400ka can give reliable ages. Here we conduct high-resolution luminescence dating, back to ~350 ka. Bacon age-depth modelling was performed to obtain an age framework based on luminescence ages. An frame-work of chronology was established for loess and palaesol sequences in Chinese loess plateau. Results indicate that loess accumulation in Luochuan was continuous on the orbital scale over the last three glacial-interglacial cycles. We compared stratigraphic and proxy records of the Luochuan section with the Xifeng, Jingyuan, Gulang and Jingbian sections, spanning a wide region of the Chinese loess plateau (CLP). The similarity of the stratigraphic and proxy records between Luochuan, Xifeng and Jingyuan sections indicates that loess accumulation is probably continuous on the orbital scale across the main body of the central CLP, and that the age model of the Luochuan loess-paleosol sequence might be applicable to other loess sections in the central CLP. However, the overall similarity of stratigraphic and proxy records of sections in the central CLP does not guarantee similarity in millennial time scales. Implications of Quaternary studies from results of Potou section The new age framework resolves discrepancies between orbitally-tuned chronologies at several boundaries. Our luminescence age model provides an independent test of previous correlation-based or orbitally-tuned age models for East Asian monsoon records of Chinese loess-paleosol sequences. For the base of S3, our modelled age of 327 ± 14 ka is roughly consistent with the MIS 9/10 boundary age of 337 ka. The slight underestimation is possibly a result of signal instability for the old samples. Above this boundary, comparison of the luminescence age model and correlation-based or orbitally-tuned age models can be made with higher reliability, as the signal instability has less effect and the ages errors also become smaller. The most significant discrepancy in previous astronomical chronologies of the last 350 kyr pertains to the L3/S3 boundary , corresponding approximately to the MIS 8/9 boundary. Tuned ages of 276 ka have been given for this boundary, while another study giving an age of 307 ka. There is a difference of up to ~30 kyr, which is slightly greater than the duration of a precessional cycle. Our luminescence age model provides a boundary age at 276 ± 9 ka which is consistent with the former two studies. The calibration of the age of the MIS 8/9 boundary sheds new light on the diversity of interglacials and global glacier dynamics. It has been recognized that the close alignment of obliquity and Northern Hemisphere precessional insolation minima favors transitions from interglacial to glacial climates, as is the case in the onset of MIS 4 and MIS 6. Despite of the small deviation between our luminescence chronology and some indirect age models, the general consistency supports the robustness of the chronology of loess accumulation derived using correlation-based methods, as well as the related regional and global climatic interpretations. Our results also indicates that the published astronomical timescales for the loess deposits on the CLP over the last ~2.6 Myr are generally reliable, as well as for the related regional and global climatic interpretations.

17307117.label: Major findings and research outcome
17307117.value: We have conduct high-resolution luminescence dating, back to ~350 ka for the first time, in the classical Luochuan loess section in the central Chinese loess plateau (CLP) (Zhang et al. Geology under review). Results indicate that loess accumulation in Luochuan was continuous on the orbital scale over the last three glacial-interglacial cycles. The new age framework resolves discrepancies between orbitally-tuned chronologies at several boundaries, and provides support for re-calibrating the MIS 8/9 boundary age from 300 ka to ~280 ka. Our results also indicates that the published astronomical timescales for the loess deposits on the CLP over the last ~2.6 Myr are generally reliable, as well as for the related regional and global climatic interpretations. We have compared five protocols used in post infrared IR stimulated luminescences (pIRIR) dating (Zhang et al., 2021. Geochronometria) . The results show that when the equivalent dose (De) of the sample was less than 500 Gy, all of the protocols gave consistent results; however, when De exceeded 750 Gy, all of the SAR protocols underestimated De. We suggest that only the ‘MAR with heat’ protocol is suitable for samples with De exceeding 750 Gy and should be used for dating of samples older than 200ka of loess/palaesol samples. We found that the age of the potassium feldspar from the calcrete nodules along the S1/L2 boundary is significantly older than those of the paleosol and loess samples lying above and below the boundary (Zhang et al., 2018). The age overestimation of the potassium feldspar from calcrete nodules is caused by the underestimation of the dose rate, because accretion of carbonates could dilute the radioactivity. The age hiatus at the top of L2 also resulted from the underestimation of the dose rates of four loess samples beneath this hiatus, having high CaO concentrations. Ages of these samples are overestimated in the similar way as the no- dules, but with smaller degrees. All results suggest that the accretion of carbonates happened after the loess deposition. We have developed simplified procedures were introduced in OSL dating of young samples with dim and poorly bleached quartz grains (Hu and Li, Quaternary Geochronology, 2019). Large data sets of aliquots enable to have statistical analysis and application of age models for poorly bleached samples. Finite mixture model (FMM) was applied to the data sets. Only aliquots meeting the objective selecting criteria are analyzed further for determining the equivalent dose (De) values. As a result, reliable De estimates were obtained using the proposed simplified procedures, with the advantage of saving substantial machine time. Single grain measurements have been effectively achieved with the single aliquots for the dim samples. Standardised growth curves (SGCs) were established for extracts of potassium feldspar (K-feldspar), plagioclase and polymineral grains from various geological settings (deserts, loess, lake or fluvial deposits) from Northern China (Zhang and Li, Quaternary Geochronology, 2019.).

17307117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17307117.value: Further development of dating protocols were recommended. Results from this study indicate that aliquots with multiple grains of K-feldspar can only apply to samples younger than 400ka. However, it is also found that some “super” grains saturate/reach equilibria ages at old ages (larger equivalent doses). We suggest to carry out single grain dating to utilise such grains. The impacts of disequilibrium of U, Th decay series on the dose rate should be studied, particularly for older samples. The movement of radioactive elements in the boundaries of loess/palaeosol are especially important. The calcrete nodules desired further studies for directly dating. The growth of calcrete nodules is environmentally significant. It is closely related to climate changes in loess plateau.

17307117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17307117.value: We have studied the formation ages of loess and palaeosol in central Chinese loess plateau, using luminescence from minerals of feldspar. We have focused our attention on the old dating limit for the materials. It is found that the technique can only be applied to samples younger than 400 thousand years. It is the first time that the samples of last 350 thousand years old (top 30 meters or so) were dated intensively in a sampling interval of 20cm. We have revealed that loess deposition was rather continuously in the time scale of thousand years. Such age frame work provide crucial information for correlating studies of the climate changes between marine and terrestrial materials.

17307417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17307417.value: This work will involve two major components: 1) remote sensing of Mars and 2) laboratory analyses of hydrothermal minerals. The remote sensing analyses will be focused on characterizing the geology, mineralogy and geochemistry of crust exhumed from the Martian subsurface by meteor impact. Impact craters are nature’s natural excavators as their central peaks, uplifted rims and ejecta contain fractions of crust exhumed from deep in the subsurface. I will use visible remote sensing images to map textural and structural relationships between different units and infrared remote sensing to determine the mineralogy and geochemistry of these exhumed materials. The Noachian crust contains 100s of examples of impact craters that have exhumed crustal alteration minerals such (e.g. serpentine, smectite and chlorite) likely formed at depths of 100s to 1000s of metres. Most of these are yet unexplored in detail. This project will characterise the detailed geology and geochemistry of 50-100 high priority targets with the goal of constraining the availability of fluids, nutrients, and energy sources that might have been available to ancient, subsurface life. Central to this goal will be characterising the Fe-mineralogy of exhumed hydrothermal systems, given that Fe is thought have been a key ingredient for early chemotrophs on Earth. In order to interpret the infrared reflectance spectra of Mars accurately, it is necessary to compare these data to analogous laboratory spectra of well-characterised minerals. While many library spectra are available, there are also significant gaps where critically important minerals are not available. With regard to hydrothermal processes, these gaps include many Fe-rich clays in the serpentine, chlorite and and talc-pyrophylite groups, as well as Fe-Mn-rich carbonates. This project will carry out detailed structural and crystal-chemical analyses of Fe-rich clays and Fe-Mn-carbonates in order to relate the details of infrared spectral shape and wavelength of key absorptions to mineralogy and chemistry. These new insights will provide key insights into the details of complicated Fe-rich clays, and will feed directly into efforts to characterise habitable subsurface environments on Mars using detailed remote sensing analyses. This project will contribute critical results describing the habitability of the ancient Martian hydrothermal and subsurface environments that operated at the same time when life formed in analogous environments on Earth. These results will not only provide key insights into the viability of a deep biosphere on Mars, but will help to guide future exploration of habitable environments on the surface by landed spacecraft. 这项工作将涉及两个主要部分：1）火星遥感和2）实验室 水热矿物分析。遥感分析将重点在于 描述了火星人挖出的地壳的地质学，矿物学和地球化学特征 地面受流星影响。撞击坑是大自然的天然挖掘机作为其中心峰， 隆起的轮辋和喷射物含有从地下深处挖掘出来的一些地壳。我会用 可见的遥感图像来映射不同单位之间的纹理和结构关系 和红外遥感，以确定这些挖掘的矿物学和地球化学 材料。诺亚加西亚地壳含有已经挖出的100个冲击坑的例子 地壳变质矿物质（如蛇纹石，绿土和亚氯酸盐）可能形成于深部 100至1000米。其中大部分尚未详细探讨。这个项目的特点 详细的地质与地球化学50-100个高优先目标为目标 限制可能可用的流体，营养物质和能源的可用性 到古代，地下生活。这个目标的中心将是Fe矿物学的特征 考虑到Fe被认为是早期的关键因素，被挖出的水热系统 地球上的化学物质。为了准确地解释火星的红外反射光谱 有必要将这些数据与良好表征的矿物质的类似实验室光谱进行比较。 虽然有许多图书馆谱，但也有重要的差距 矿物质不可用。关于水热过程，这些差距包括许多Ferich 蛇纹石，亚氯酸盐和滑石 - 叶蜡石组中的粘土以及富含Fe-Mn的粘土 碳酸盐。本项目将对富铁富集进行详细的结构和晶体化学分析 粘土和Fe-Mn-碳酸盐，以便关联红外光谱形状的细节 关键吸收波长对矿物学和化学的影响。这些新的见解将提供关键 了解复杂的富含Fe的粘土的细节，并直接进行努力 使用详细的遥感分析来表征火星上的可居住的地下环境。 这个项目将为描述古代火星人的适应性作出贡献 水热和地下环境，同时生活在同一时间 地球上的类似环境。这些结果不仅可以提供关键的见解 火星深度生物圈的生存能力，但有助于指导未来的可居住性探索 落地飞船表面的环境。

17307417.label: Realisation of objectives
17307417.value: The core goal of this project was to evaluate the role of Fe in Fe-rich phyllosilicate spectra and to determine the mineralogy, geochemistry and spectroscopy of Fe-phyllosilicates (clays) with regard to the habitability of Mars. In our view, the project has been extremely successful. Like many projects, our pathway to success was slightly different than what we envisioned at the outset, but to our great pleasure, the results have at the same time been much better than what we imagined. As planned, we have analyzed a large suite of Fe-clay-bearing samples from the Natural History Museum in London as well as some other sources. We originally planned to analyze 45 clay samples from the NHM, but in after further discussion with curators there, we agreed to analyze 60 samples. However, while we did anticipate that impurities would be a challenge to this study, the impurities turned out to quite abundant and in some cases, intimately mixed. This is not a problem, but just one more issue to consider. We were able to account for the issue by measuring Mossbauer spectra, which allowed us to assign the Fe-content to different crystals and crystallographic positions, and via high-resolution imaging that allowed us to characterize the amounts of and relationships among clays and non-clay impurities. In addition to samples from the NHM, were able to acquire more samples of Fe-rich chlorite and serpentine from sources in Wuhan and other colleagues in Mainland China. Taken together, we were able to investigate the mineralogy and spectroscopy of a large suite of Fe-rich clay mineral samples of various levels of impurity. In addition to analysis of pure clay samples, we have supplemented that dataset with a large suite of core samples through altered, Fe-rich basalt from Hainan Island – samples we did not know we could possibly have access to. So, while our work on spectroscopy of very Fe-rich samples from museum collections remains central to the study, and we have written multiple manuscripts on this topic – we have supplemented the work with many additional samples. The original objectives of this work included more ambitious goals of studying samples and then applying those results to studies of Mars using remote sensing data. But some of the original remote sensing objectives were descoped once the awarded budget was decided, as this was significantly lower than expected. Despite these challenges, I was able to add back in remote sensing applications of our lab results to great success. In short, this project achieved its stated objectives and produced outputs far beyond what we had originally hoped to achieve. I am extremely grateful for the funding and am hopeful that the results from this project convey my team’s commitment to professionalism and scientific discovery.

17307417.label: Major findings and research outcome
17307417.value: This work resulted in a number of new discoveries. Specifically, we have illustrated how various types of spectral index of alteration can be applied to Fe-bearing rocks sampled in the field (Liu et al., Applied Clay Science, 2021), and the extrapolation of those results to spectral interpretations of alteration zones on Mars. The application to Mars resulted in a Nature Astronomy paper (Liu et al., 2021) showing geological evidence for reducing early surface conditions. Those trends were also applied to data from NASA’s Mars rover Curiosity to show that the altered rocks seemingly formed in a subaerial setting, not a lake (Liu et al., Science Advances, 2021). Our analysis of Fe-rich clays has contributed fundamentally new results to our understanding of Fe-rich clay minerals from infrared measurements (Liu et al., in prep) and those results have informed a paper about characterization of clay minerals from Mars rover camera spectra (Cuadros et al., in revision) and a paper describing relationships among the infrared and raman spectra of Fe-rich clays (Baumgartner et al,. 2021). In addition, our work showed spectral characteristics of Fe-rich illite formed through K-metasomatism on Earth, resulting in a publication on similar alteration on Mars described in Geophysical Research Letters (Michalski et al, 2021). These results are all listed in part C of this report.

17307417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17307417.value: One very positive outcome of this project is that it has helped position me to be included as a research fellow in the Canadian Institute for Advanced Research (CIFAR) Earth 4D Program, which has begun in 2019 and continues today. This is a high talent, high impact global thinktank group that helps solve big problems. They are focused on how the surface of planets affects the subsurface and vice versa. Our expertise with this project helps feed into the goals of that program, resulting in my role as fellow and resulting in a number of impactful papers. The findings from this project will lead naturally and directly into a pending CRF project to study the geology and mineralogy of lakes on Mars, which contain Fe-rich clays and for which our team will be well-positioned to make new discoveries about lake mineralogy and habitability.

17307417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17307417.value: Mars is a currently an extremely cold, desolate work composed of fine-grained silicate dust, colored red by iron oxides. In fact the planet is overall more iron-rich than the Earth and therefore this element, which played a critical role in the geological and biological evolution of the Earth is even more important on Mars. Our work has focused on the mineralogy of clays that formed when water interacted with the martian volcanic crust. We used analog studies in the Planetary Spectroscopy and Mineralogy Laboratory at HKU to understand the how to interpret infrared remote sensing spectra of clay-rich rocks on Mars with regard to their mineralogy and iron content. Our results have illuminated many key factors surrounding iron occurrence and chemical substitutions in clay minerals. One of the most important discoveries we have made is that a global layer of weathered rock and soil on Mars is actually extremely Fe-poor – and that this Fe-poor material overlies a thick layer of Fe-rich rock. This discovery is important because it shows that ancient Mars had a reduced atmosphere allowing for the downward migration of iron, which is mobile under reducing conditions but not mobile under oxidizing conditions.

17308017.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17308017.value: 收縮代數，奇點和計數幾何

17308017.label: Project Objectives
17308017.value: Study the conjecture of Donovan and Wemyss, which says that the contraction algebra is a complete invariant for 3 dimensional flopping contraction. Study the intrinsic definition of Gopakumar-Vafa invariants from the contraction algebra, without using deformation theory.
rows: Study the conjecture of Donovan and Wemyss, which says that the contraction algebra is a complete invariant for 3 dimensional flopping contraction.
Study the intrinsic definition of Gopakumar-Vafa invariants from the contraction algebra, without using deformation theory.

17308017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17308017.value: Donovan和Wemyss在2013年提出的收縮代數的概念可以被視為導出範疇和非交換代數在代數幾何上的一個完美應用。他們證明了在三維有理收縮的情形，收縮代數提供了一個全新的不變量，並且證明在flop的情形收縮代數可以用於構造導出範疇的等價。另外Donovan和Wemyss猜想一個三維flop收縮的奇點的解析領域完全由收縮代數決定。這個猜想是本項目的主要驅動力。 在申請人與Yukinobu Toda的工作中，我們給出了收縮代數的一個等價定義。利用這個新定義，我們證明了收縮代數的很多性質。特別的，我們在收縮代數上構造了一個自然的A無窮結構。我們相信這個結構對於最終證明Donovan－Wemyss猜想將起到關鍵的作用。另外我們用幾何的方法證明一個一般的收縮代數可以形變成為一個半單代數。而這個半單代數的共型分塊的個數恰恰等於flop收縮的Gopakumar－Vafa不變量。在這個項目中我們將進一步研究如何用純代數的方法給出GV不變量的內藴定義。這對於Gopakumar-Vafa 不變量的研究具有重要的意義。

17308017.label: Realisation of objectives
17308017.value: We are able to prove a slightly weaken version of the conjecture of Donovan and Wemyss. For each 3-dimensional flopping contraction, we may associate to it a finite dimensional algebra, i.e. the contraction algebra. By the work of Van den Bergh, the contraction algebra is the Jacobi algebra for a quiver with potential. In the 0-th Hochschild homology of the contraction algebra lies a class represented by the superpotential defined up to algebra isomorphisms. In the joint paper with Bernhard Keller, we prove that the derived Morita equivalence class of the contraction algebra together with the above class determine the singularity underlying the flopping contraction. The original conjecture of Donovan and Wemyss says that the derived Morita type of the contraction algebra along will determine the singularity, which remains open. In order to prove the above statement, we have proved noncommutative analogue of several classical results in hyper surface singularity theory. These results are contained in a series of papers joint with Gui-song Zhou (research associate ) and Bernhard Keller respectively. They are also closely related to the GRF project no.17303420. We have proved that GopaKumar-Vafa invariants can be computed from the DT invariants of the quiver with potential by applying a wall-crossing formula. To be more precise they are the exponents of a product expansion formula. We have been seeking for a conceptional way to understand the Gopakumar-Vafa invariants of contraction algebra. Before we succeed this has been recently established by Ben Davison (Edinburgh), partially motivated by the paper of the PI and Toda and the paper of the PI and Keller.

17308017.label: Major findings and research outcome
17308017.value: 1. In a joint paper with Gui-song Zhou, we prove a noncommutative Mather-Yau theorem. It says that the right equivalence class of a potential is determined by the isomorphic type of its Jacobi algebra (suppose it is finite dimensional) together with the class in the 0-th Hochschild homology represented by the class. 2. In a joint paper with Gui-song Zhou, we prove for n-loop quiver and a potential with finite dimensional Jacobi algebra, suppose the class of the potential is zero it must be right equivalent to a weighted homogeneous one. 3. In a joint paper with Keller we prove a). the Z-graded dg category of isolated hypersurface singularity determines the isomorphic type of the singularity. b). the derived contraction algebra determines the dg category of singularities up to equivalences. Together with the noncommutative Mather-Yau theorem, we have proved that the derived Morita type of the contraction algebra together with the class represented by the potential recovers the isomorphic type of the singularity underlying the 3-dimensional flopping contraction.

17308017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17308017.value: 1. The Mather-Yau type theorem on infinite dimensional Jacobi algebra is still unknown. One possible way to obtain such a result is to introduce convergence property for potential. A partial goal of GRF project no. 17303420 is to settle down foundations for convergent potentials. 2. Given a rational curve in CY 3fold, one can define a noncommutative algebra pro-represent the noncommutative deformation functor of the curve. When the curve is contractible, this algebra is precisely the contraction algebra of Donovan and Wemyss. Kawamata asks a question: whether finite dimensionality of this algebra can imply contractibility. This will be an extremely interesting problem.

17500117.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17500117.value: 参数不确定性和均衡消费波动

17500117.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17500117.value: Dr Nie, Jun Prof Young, Eric

17500117.label: Project Objectives
17500117.value: To construct a tractable continuous-time CARA-Gaussian heterogeneous-agent equilibrium model to link two research lines: (i) parameter uncertainty and learning and (ii) the equilibrium household consumption-income dynamics. To solve the model explicitly and explore how parameter uncertainty and learning affects the real rate of interest and the cross-sectional distributions of individual consumption and income in general equilibrium in the presence of uninsurable labor income. To estimate the income process with stochastic mean using the US panel data on household consumption and income, and to quantitatively evaluate how parameter learning has the potential to better explain the low real interest rate and high consumption-income volatility we observed in the US economy. To compute the welfare costs of parameter uncertainty using the plausibly estimated and calibrated parameter values. To extend the benchmark model to allow for model misspecifications proposed by Hansen and Sargent (2007), and study the relative importance of two types of uncertainty: (i) uncertainty over the key structural parameter and (ii) uncertainty over the model specification itself.
