17500117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17500117.value: 现实生活中，普通消费者不仅需要面对繁杂的不确定性，更需要在这样一个模型参数/模型结构不确定的环境下做出有关消费/储蓄的最优选择。大量理论与实证研究发现，模型参数信息的不完整在消费者最优决策过程中扮演者重要的角色。例如，Sampson (1994) 发现，在影响未来收入不确定性的因素中，收入模型中参数的不确定性比未知的未来收入冲击更重要。Guvenen (2007) 为“劳动收入增长因人而异，而个人很难获得完整的关于自身收入增长参数的信息”这一观点提供了实证支持。Wang (2009) 发现，关于劳动收入增长信息的不完整很大程度上影响着人们优化消费-资产组合的决策。因此，了解理性的、前瞻性的消费者在面对重大风险与不确定性（例如，未知的未来收入以及未知的预期收入增长率）时如何决策就变得十分重要了。Hansen and Sargent (2015) 将模型参数的不确定性以及关于参数的学习、更新列为了在文中“四种无知”中的一种。并且强调，这种“无知”在研究者使用宏观经济模型进行量化研究时可能会对模型给出的结论产生重大的影响。 理论和实证研究都证实， 由消费者风险厌恶与无法预测的未来收入风险互动所产生的预防性储蓄在个体及总量两个层次都对消费者财富的累积起着重要的作用。Wang (2003) 在一般均衡的框架下研究了消费者的预防性储蓄，并发现在一般均衡下，消费者的年消费量由消费者总资产的年金值决定。然而，Luo, Nie and Young (2017) 则指出，在Wang(2003) 的完全信息与理性预期 (FI-RE) 假设下，模型无法得出在美国经济中观测到的低实际利率与高个人消费收入波动比。因此，在这个项目中，我们计划构造一个连续时间下异质性消费者的消费-储蓄一般均衡模型，并运用此模型研究劳动收入参数的不确定性以及参数的学习、更新如何帮助我们更好地解释在美国经济中观测到的低实际利率与高个人消费收入波动比的现象。

17500117.label: Realisation of objectives
17500117.value: All objectives of this project are realized during the period. Specifically, we developed and solved a tractable continuous-time recursive utility (RU) version of the Huggett (1993) model to study the effects of model uncertainty due to a preference for robustness (RB, or ambiguity aversion). We also carefully constructed a panel data set for the US individual household consumption, income, and wealth, estimated the exogeously specified income processes, and computed the relevant moments of the joint dynamics of consumption, wealth, and income. We show that RB reduces the equilibrium interest rate and the relative dispersion of consumption to income, making them closer to the data, but our benchmark model cannot match the observed relative dispersion. An extension to a RU-RB model with a risky asset is successful at matching this dimension. Our analysis implies the welfare costs of model uncertainty are sizable: a typical consumer in equilibrium would be willing to sacrifice about 15 percent of his initial wealth to remove the model uncertainty he faces. In addition, we also explored how parameter uncertainty due to unknown income growth and showed that parameter uncertainty is also crucial to understand the observed low interest rates and the relative dispersion of household consumption to income.

17500117.label: Major findings and research outcome
17500117.value: In the main paper generated from this project, we show that RB reduces the equilibrium interest rate and the relative dispersion of consumption to income, making them closer to the data, but our benchmark model cannot match the observed relative dispersion. An extension to a RU-RB model with a risky asset is successful at matching this dimension. Our analysis implies the welfare costs of model uncertainty are sizable: a typical consumer in equilibrium would be willing to sacrifice about 15 percent of his initial wealth to remove the model uncertainty he faces. In addition, we also explored how parameter uncertainty due to unknown income growth and showed that parameter uncertainty is also crucial to understand the observed low interest rates and the relative dispersion of household consumption to income. During the whole period, we completed three working papers: (1) "Ambiguity, Low Risk-Free Rates, and Consumption Inequality"; (2) "Portfolio Choice with Information-Processing Limits"; (3) "Ignorance, Pervasive Uncertainty, and Household Finance"; and (4) "Growth and Welfare Gains from Financial Integration under Model Uncertainty". The first and second papers are now published at Economic Journal and Annals of Economics and Finance, respectively. The third one is under revise and resubmit at Journal of Economic Theory.

17500117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17500117.value: In the future, we will submit the unpublished working paper mentioned above (Growth and Welfare Gains from Financial Integration under Model Uncertainty) to Journal of Political Economy for possible publication. In addition, we will use the same methodology developed in this paper to address a companion important question in macroeconomics and household finance: How individual households who pervasive uncertainty make optimal consumption-portfolio decisions when the expected return of the equity market is stochastic? This question is very important because in the existing literature the expected return of equity is viewed as a constant and known parameter, which contradicts to the empirical fact that the expected equity return is stochastic and unknown.

17500117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17500117.value: Ordinary households face pervasive uncertainty in the real world, and have to make optimal consumption/savings decisions in an environment in which they are uncertain about the model parameters and/or model structure. Many empirical and theoretical studies have found that incomplete information about the relevant model parameters plays an important role in affecting agents's optimal decisions. For example, Guvenen (2007) provided empirical evidence to argue that labor income growth is individual specific and it is difficult for individuals to have complete information about their own income growth. It is therefore important for us to understand how rational consumers make optimal decisions when faced with major types of risk and uncertainty. Both empirical and theoretical studies showed that the precautionary saving motive due to the interaction of risk aversion and unpredictable income risk plays an important role in wealth accumulation at both individual and aggregate levels. In this project, we constructed a tractable general equilibrium consumption-saving model to explore how model uncertainty about labor income can help explain the low risk free rate and high relative volatility of consumption to income we observed in the US economy.

17500217.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17500217.value: 打包付費制度對於醫療衛生系統運營績效的影響

17500217.label: Project Objectives
17500217.value: To develop hypotheses on how the bundled payment (BP) scheme affects a health care system’s operational performance, such as length of stay, readmission rate, cost, etc. To empirically test the hypotheses developed, and to provide empirical evidence on how BP affects operational performance. To explore the moderating factors of the effects of BP on the performance of health care systems.
rows: To develop hypotheses on how the bundled payment (BP) scheme affects a health care system’s operational performance, such as length of stay, readmission rate, cost, etc.
To empirically test the hypotheses developed, and to provide empirical evidence on how BP affects operational performance.
To explore the moderating factors of the effects of BP on the performance of health care systems.

17500217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17500217.value: In many countries, including the US, the health care reimbursement policy has traditionally been the fee-for-service (FFS) scheme. The FFS payment scheme compensates the service provider based on the service volume without factoring in the quality of service, and thus incentivizes service providers to increase the service volume and also the eventual health care cost. The bundled payment (BP) scheme was proposed as an alternative approach to address the problems of FFS. BP compensates the service provider for a whole episode of care using a lump sum, which does not depend on the exact services provided. China is also implementing the BP scheme to replace the original FFS scheme in some regions. The proposed research will empirically investigate the impact of implementing BP on the operational performances of a health care system, using a data set collected from Anhui Province in China. The research has several important practical implications. First, the results will help identify the benefits and potential issues of the BP scheme, and highlight the tradeoffs involved. Second, if the proposed research finds evidence that the BP scheme outperforms the FFS payment scheme, it will also serve as a strong argument for promoting the BP scheme as a measure to improve the health care system and to reduce the health care cost. Third, by studying the moderating factors of the effects of BP on health care performances, the proposed research will help provide guidelines on when a BP scheme should be adopted. In addition, the proposed research will also contribute to the academic literature. Several theoretical studies on the BP scheme exist in the operations management literature. The proposed research will complement these studies by testing their theoretical predications. Little empirical research on the BP scheme has been undertaken to date due to its short history. To the best of our knowledge, this will be the first empirical study of how the implementation of BP affects the performance of health care systems. This research will provide the first empirical answer to the question of how BP affects performance, and it will therefore contribute to the literature studying payment schemes in health care. 包括美國在內的許多國家，醫療報銷政策歷史上都采用傳統的按項目付費制度。按項目付費制度基於服務數量而不是服務質量來補償醫療機構，這種機制會激勵醫療機構增加服務數量進而導致更高的醫療成本。為了解決按項目付費制度的困境，壹種新的付費制度--打包付費制度應運而生。它對壹段時間內的治療費用設置壹個補償給醫療機構的定額，而該定額並不依賴於具體的醫療費用。中國的某些地區也開始使用打包付費制度代替按項目付費制度。 我們的研究將運用實證研究方法，通過安徽省的數據，來研究打包付費制度對於醫療衛生系統的運營績效的影響。這項研究有幾個重要的實際意義。第壹，研究結果將用來指出打包付費制度的優點以及存在的潛在問題。第二，如果研究結果能夠證實打包付費制度優於按項目付費制度，那麽本研究可以成為推廣打包付費制度的有力例證，因為該制度能夠提高醫療系統的效率、降低醫療成本。第三，通過研究打包付費制度對於醫療衛生系統績效所產生效果的調節因素，我們的研究將會對什麽情況下應該采用打包付費制度提供指導意見。 此外，我們的研究也將會對學術文獻做出貢獻。在運營管理領域，已經有壹些關於打包付費制度的理論性研究。我們的研究將通過檢驗他們的理論預測，使得他們的研究更加完善。鑒於打包付費制度的短暫歷史，至今關於該制度的實證性研究還是很少。據我們所知，這是第壹個研究打包付費制度的實施如何影響醫療衛生系統運營績效的實證研究。本研究給出的實證性答案，將對有關醫療衛生系統付費制度的研究做出貢獻。

17500217.label: Realisation of objectives
17500217.value: We developed three sets of hypotheses on how the bundled payment (BP) scheme affects a health care system’s operational performance, including length of stay, readmission rate, and cost. We used data from Anhui Province in China to empirically test the hypotheses developed. The empirical resutls provide empirical evidence on how BP affects operational performance. We explored the moderating factors of the effects of BP on the performance of health care systems. In particular, we adopted a hospital-level analysis and used the percentage of patients under a BP scheme in each hospital in each quarter to show the nonlinear effects of policy implementation on hospital outcomes. We also investigated the different impacts of BP implementation on treatment costs with a relatively loose or tight BP price. We defined a price-cost index (PCI) to evaluate the relationship between historical cost and BP price.

17500217.label: Major findings and research outcome
17500217.value: We study the impact of bundled payment policy on healthcare cost, efficiency, quality, and shift of care. Using insurance claim data, we empirically offer a more nuanced understanding of the impact of bundled payment policy on hospital operations and provide new evidence from China. Our evidence suggests that transitioning from fee-for-service to bundled payment reimbursement resulted in declines in treatment costs and length of stay. Along with that decline, there was an increase in planned revisits to outpatient clinics, which indicates a shift of care from the inpatient to the outpatient setting, as well as a rise in unplanned revisits, indicating a decline in service quality. The increase in readmission rate to inpatient wards is very small and not statistically significant. In addition, we discuss the design and implementation of bundled payment. Our results imply that careful bundle design is vital to encouraging providers to implement the new program without sacrificing quality.

17500217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17500217.value: The BP intervention studied in our article is limited to payments to a single institutional provider and for a single service type (i.e., inpatient service). Because of this, our study can shed only limited light on newer programs including multiple service types or multiple providers; this limitation suggests a path for future research. Besides the BP price, there are other important design features of BP to be studied in the future, features that may potentially impact study outcomes. Some programs include quality measurement in program monitoring and evaluation, but not as a component of the payment method. Policymakers and researchers can consider including quality metrics or incentives (e.g., pay-for-performance components) into future BP systems, which may mitigate the potential adverse effects on quality measures. Policymakers can also use risk adjustment and outlier payments to account for patient risk in bundled payment programs.

17500217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17500217.value: We provide evidence about how BP intervention versus fee-for-service impact healthcare outcomes. Our results show that BP can reduce medical treatment costs and length of stay. In addition, we verify that the effect is nonlinear, which indicates that hospitals enjoy a large degree of cost reduction when the proportion of patients under BP is small. However, the effect weakens as the proportion of patients under BP increases. The nonlinear effect on length of stay shows a different pattern which decreases sharply when the proportion of patients under BP is large. The possible explanation is that hospitals may cut unnecessary costs at first and later shorten the length of stay. Our findings show that BP intervention slightly impacts readmission rates but has a significant positive impact on the likelihood of revisits. Our findings suggest that BP programs focusing on single-provider types resulted in a shift of services to other provider types (e.g., shift from inpatient to outpatient care), and an increase in patient risk (e.g., patients’ likelihood of unplanned revisits increased following BP). However, the positive side of shifting service from inpatient to outpatient care is that the total treatment cost is reduced since the outpatient cost is less than inpatient cost.

17500317.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17500317.value: 同一幣的兩面：探討觀點代入對員工創造力的相反影響

17500317.label: Project Objectives
17500317.value: To test a process model that relates individual-level PT to employee creativity for the first time. To demonstrate that seeking the best ideas and seeking the most accepted ideas are distinct creative goals, a distinction often ignored. To jointly consider the cognitive and affective PT processes, which has seldom occurred in previous studies. To propose and test for the first time the theoretical premise that PT can both increase and decrease employees’ creativity, thus giving greater complexity to the widely assumed functional view of the effects of PT at work. To examine the workplace and social context in which PT occurs by addressing the distinct roles of task interdependence and emotional interdependence in the process model. To illustrate the dynamic effects of PT by investigating how within-person changes in employees’ PT are related to within-person changes in employee creativity over time.

17500317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17500317.value: 許多研究人員和管理者認為，促進員工的觀點代入(例如多為員工設想) 對於職場和諧和生產過程很重要。本研究提出觀點代入並不總是有利於創造力，並提出一個過程模型來理解觀點代入對員工創造力的相反影響, 從而增强我們對觀點代入的了解。 首先，創造力和觀點代入都需要對進行大量資料的認知處理，但是對這兩個領域的研究郤偏偏分開進行; 研究人員很少會考慮到個人的觀點代入對創造力的影響。這項研究探討員工的觀點代入與其創造力的關係, 而填補這個空隙。 第二，在創造力研究中，研究人員通常都會假設員工只有一個創造目標，就是要想出有創意的點子。然而，員工在創造時或許會有其他目標，例如尋求同事或管理層可接受的點子，即使這些點子只有微弱的創造性。探討不同的創意目標是很重要的，因為它可以開闢新的研究途徑。所以，這項研究會探討兩個不同的創意目標：尋求最好的點子和尋求最受歡迎的點子。 第三，觀點代入可以有兩個不同的流程, 而這兩個流程很少被比較。首先, 認知觀點代入是試圖用別人的角度看事情，而情感觀點代入是試圖感覺別人的感覺。雖然這兩個過程的效果在許多生活領域中都類似，但是對員工創造力的影響可能是相反的，因為創造力可能需要高認知能力，而情感觀點代入則是一個阻礙。填補這個空隙是很重要的，因為它揭示了觀點代入的複雜性質。第四，觀點代入被普遍認為是一種非常理想的個人特質，有利於組織和關係，但很少有關於它的缺點的硏究。填補這一空隙可讓研究人員更加平衡和準確地評估在工作場鼓吹觀點代入的好處和風險。針對這兩個空隙，這項硏究提出的過程模型既包含認知和情感觀點代入過程，也解釋了為什麼它們可能分別增強和破壞創造力。 第五，觀點代入是一個社會過程，它不能與員工的脫節。研究很少考慮到周圍的環境因素對觀點代入的影響。例如，如果員工在日常工作中需要大量團體工作，他們的觀點代入對創造力可能有非常巨大的影響。為了尋找這些變素，這項硏究會探討兩種員工的相互依存關係，包括是工作上的相互依存關係和情感上的相互依存關係。 簡而言之，這項研究將會探討觀點代入對創造力的正面和負面影響, 並解決上述五個研究領域的空隙。這項硏究對管理層也有影響。管理者大多側重於怎樣促進員工的觀點代入，但忽視了促進觀點代入對創造力所帶來的負面影響。例如，如果觀點代入令員工的創造力下降，那麼管理層必須監督或調整促進觀點代入的管理。這項硏究也可以幫助解決這些管理問題。

17500617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17500617.value: In this study, we attempt to examine how stock market indexing affects the options market quality in terms of option liquidity and trading continuity, by adopting the Russell index reconstitution as an identification strategy. To proxy for the option liquidity and trading continuity, we employ the number of zero trading days, which captures the insight that the absence of trading activities in all options with that underlying stock manifests the degree of illiquidity. We expect that firms at the top of Russell 2000 index would have discontinuously lower number of zero trading days than firms at the bottom of Russell 1000 index. To provide additional corroborating evidence, we implement a two-stage instrumental estimation method and expect that higher instrumented institutional ownership results in lower number of zero trading days in options. Moreover, we break down firms’ total institutional ownership ratio (IOR) based on the classification in Bushee and Noe (2000) and Bushee (2001), including quasi-indexer IOR, transient IOR, and dedicated IOR. As we conjecture that most of the indexing effect is probably due to more trading from transient investors who benchmark their performance to indexes and tend to trade options as part of their complicated strategies, we expect that only transient IOR is significantly and negatively correlated with the number of zero trading days in options. As for the potential channel through which stock market indexing affects options market quality, we focus on the plausible liquidity spillover effect. Boone and White (2015) find that firms at the top of Russell 2000 index have discontinuously higher stock liquidity compared with firms at the bottom of Russell 1000 index. As more trading activities in stock market encourage informed investors to engage in additional trading activities in options market, we expect that the improved options market quality could be attributed to the increased stock liquidity. Finally, to probe into the implication of the indexing effect on options market quality, we explore whether and how the better options market quality due to stock market indexing affects the return predictability of informed options trading. In particular, as prior literature has shown that price-based measures, such as the implied volatility spread (IVSpread) and implied volatility skew (IVSkew), have the ability to predict future equity returns, we are interested in whether the indexing effect could enhance the association between IVSpread/IVSkew and future equity returns (Cremers and Weinbaum (2010) and Xing, Zhang, Zhao (2010)). 在本項目中，我們通過使用Russell Index的重組信息作爲機構投資人持股比例的内生性識別策略，來檢驗股票市場的指數組成變化對於期權市場質量的影響。關於期權市場質量，我們關注期權交易的流動性和交易的連續性，并使用期權零交易量的交易日的數目作爲代理變量。使用這個代理變量可以擷取到如果某隻股票對應的所有期權無交易活動給期權市場質量帶來的流動性問題。我們期望在Russell 2000指數頂部的公司相對於在Russell 2000指數底部的公司會有比較少的期權零交易量的交易日。爲了給出更多穩健性證據，我們使用了兩階段工具變量估計方法，并期望能發現與我們假設一致的結果。 另外， 我們根據Bushee and Noe (2000) 和Bushee (2001), 將公司的總的機構投資人持股比例(IOR)分解成爲被動機構投資人(quasi-indexer), 短期機構投資人（transient investors），和長期機構投資人(dedicated investors)。因爲短期機構投資人會使用期權作爲他們複雜交易策略的一部分，所以我們預測指數變化對於期權交易的影響完全來自於短期機構投資人。相應的，我們期望衹有短期機構投資人的持股比例會與期權零交易量的交易日的數目有負顯著的關係。 我們進一步研究是否因爲股票市場流動性溢出效果，使得股票市場的指數變化對期權市場質量產生影響的。Boone and White (2015)發現在Russell 2000指數頂部的公司相對於在Russell 2000指數底部的公司有更高的股票流動性。因爲更多股票市場的交易行爲會導致投資者參與更多的期權市場交易，所以我們期望Russell 2000指數重組給股票市場流動性帶來的改善會進一步增加期權市場的流動性。

17500617.label: Major findings and research outcome
17500617.value: Using local linear regressions based on Russell index reconstitution, we examine how option price efficiency is affected by stock market indexing. We find that put-call parity deviation, a proxy for options price efficiency, is significantly smaller if a stock is at the top of the Russell 2000 index, compared with a similar-sized stock at the bottom of the Russell 1000 index. The stocks at the top of the Russell 2000 index also have higher options trading volume and smaller option bid-ask spreads. Our results collectively suggest that the stock market indexing effect improves the option price efficiency through higher options market liquidity.

17500617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17500617.value: In the revised version of the project, we use local linear regressions based on the Russell index reconstitution to examine the stock indexing effect on options market price efficiency via improved options market liquidity. The local linear regression circumvents the drawbacks of the instrumental variable approach and regression discontinuity approach identified in the literature. However, it also makes the test of our third objective regarding the options return predictability challenging. We could potentially further develop our project based on informed options trading before corporate events.

17500617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17500617.value: Our paper contributes to the literature by providing the first evidence regarding the stock indexing effect on options markets. The prior studies mainly examine the indexing effect on the underlying stocks. Given the literature showing that options markets are important venues for informed trading and have a real effect on corporate decisions, our finding provides an undocumented and significant liquidity spillover of the stock indexing effect to options markets. More importantly, the option price efficiency improves as a result and is likely to be driven by the options supply-side channel.

17500817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17500817.value: Treatment effects (or causal effects) evaluation is one main objective of microeconometrics. Usually, the average treatment effects (ATEs) are considered. Recently, the quantile treatment effects (QTEs) get much popularity because the QTEs can provide a more complete picture on the treatment effects than the ATEs. There are three frameworks on the QTEs in the literature. The first framework does not impose endogeneity, while the other two frameworks assume endogeneity of the treatment status. The form of endogeneity in the second framework allows for identification of "global" QTEs, just like what can be done in the first framewok, while the form of endogeneity in the third framework allows for identification of only "local" QTEs. Global QTEs have better external validities, i.e., can be extraploated from one program to another, and are the main concern of this project. To give a causal interpretation to the QTE estimation in the first framework, we require the unconditional rank preservation (URP) assumption. To obtain identification of the QTE in the second framework, we need to impose the conditional rank similarity (CRS) assumption. In other words, the URP and CRS assumptions are critical to apply the estimation schemes in these two frameworks. This project tries to test these two assumptions, so the tests developed in this project can serve as "pretests" to these two estimation schemes. The tests for both URP and CRS are essentially overidentification tests. The overidentification information in the tests for URP comes from covariates, i.e., we are testing whether the rank is preserved across covariates values. The overidentification information in the tests for CRS comes from instruments, i.e., we are testing whether the rank is similar across instruments values. Both groups of tests are easy to conduct in practice through bootstrap procedures. 处理效应(或因果效应)评估是微观计量学的一个主要目标。通常，人们考虑平均处理效应(ATE)。最近，分位数处理效应(QTE)越来越受欢迎，因为QTE可以提供比ATE更完整的处理效应图。在文献中QTE有三个框架。第一个框架不假设内生性，而另外两个框架则假设处理状态的内生性。第二个框架中的内生形式允许识别“整体”QTE，就像在第一个框架中可以做到的那样，而第三个框架中的内生形式仅允许识别“局部” QTE。整体QTE具有更好的外部有效性，即可以从一个项目扩展到另一个项目，所以是该课题的主要关注点。 为了对第一个框架中的QTE估计作出因果解释，我们需要无条件秩不变（URP）假设。为了在第二个框架中识别QTE，我们需要条件秩相似（CRS）假设。换句话说，URP和CRS假设对于在这两个框架中的估计方案至关重要。该课题试图检验这两个假设，因此在本课题中发展的检验可以作为这两个估计方案的“预备检验”。 对URP和CRS的检验本质上都是过度识别检验。 URP检验中的过度识别信息来自协变量，即我们试图检验秩是否在不同的协变量值之间保持不变。 CRS检验中的过度识别信息来自工具变量，即我们试图检验秩是否在不同的工具变量值之间保持相似。在实践中，这两组检验很容易通过自助法实现。

17500917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17500917.value: The twentieth century has seen a phenomenal increase in longevity. For example, in the United States, life expectancy at birth increased from 54.9 in 1900 to 80.9 in 2000. Demographic changes of this magnitude are likely to have substantial effects on economic variables. Several researchers have investigated how these changes affect life-cycle variables such as retirement age (Kalemli-Ozcan and Weil 2010; d’Albis, Lau and Sanchez-Romero 2012) and schooling years (Hazan 2009; Cervellati and Sunde 2013). One common feature of these studies analyzing life-cycle variables is that they use the age-dependent approach: modeling survival probabilities by age-specific mortality rates. In this approach, the representative agent of a particular age faces the same mortality rate (usually given by the data). As a result, the mortality pattern at the aggregate level matches the data exactly. However, there is usually not much heterogeneity in the behavioral outcomes (such as retirement age) in this framework. This project deals with this disadvantage of the age-dependent approach by taking an alternative approach: a state-dependent approach. We will first investigate the effect of mortality decline on retirement age using a two-health-state model modified from Gertler (1999). In Gertler (1999), it is assumed that when moving from the first to the second state, the individual retires and has a higher mortality rate simultaneously. However, it is better to regard health state and the work/retire decision as two different life events. In the proposed project, these two events are separated: the health state is determined stochastically, but labor supply versus retirement will be treated as choice variables. The state-dependent approach of the proposed project is expected to generate richer interaction effects of various factors (health, wealth, and education) on retirement behavior. We also plan to study the effect of mortality decline on schooling years using the same approach. Similar to the idea mentioned above, the analysis is likely to allow for interesting interaction of retirement, education, wealth and health factors. The analysis will be more complicated, because there are more value functions in this setting. It is expected that the analysis will be manageable and generate more heterogeneity in behavior. Time permitted, we will try to modify the simplest two-health-state model into a more complicated, but still reasonably parsimonious, specification of the survival probabilities. This may deliver the benefit of bringing the resulting aggregate survival function closer to the data, but with the cost of extra computational difficulty. 20世紀以來人的壽命顯著增長。例如在美國，出生時的預期壽命從1900年的54.9歲延長到2000年的80.9歲。如此重大的人口變化可能對經濟變量產生很大的影響。一些學者已經研究了這些變化如何影響生命週期變量（life-cycle variables）, 如退休年齡(Kalemli-Ozcan and Weil 2010; d’Albis, Lau and Sanchez-Romero 2012)和受教育年期 (Hazan 2009; Cervellati and Sunde 2013)。 以上關於生命週期變量研究的共同特點是使用年齡依賴法（age-dependent approach）：根據不同年齡的死亡率來為存活率建模。在使用這種方法時，某一特定年齡段的人群面臨著相同的死亡率（通常由數據而定）。因此，總體死亡率和真實數據是一致的。但是，這種框架呈現的結果是行為（如退休年齡）的差異性較少。 本項目使用另一種方法來克服年齡依賴法的缺點：狀態依賴法（state-dependent approach）。第一，我們使用和修正Gertler (1999)的兩健康狀態模型（two-health-state model）， 研究死亡率下降對退休年齡的影響。Gertler (1999)假設當一個人身體狀況從第一個狀態發展到第二個狀態時，他身體變差而同時退休。但是身體狀態和退休決定是兩個不同的人生事件，理應區別考慮。在此項目中，這兩個事件是分開考量的：健康狀態隨機確定，但勞動力供給與退休決定將被視為選擇變量。我們希望通過兩健康狀態模型來找到多種變量（健康狀況，財富狀況，教育程度）對退休行為有更豐富的交互作用。 第二，我們還希望使用相同的方法研究死亡率下降對受教育年期的影響。類似於上面提到的方法，我們的分析將考慮退休，教育，財富和健康等不同因素間有趣的互動。 這個分析會更複雜，但我們預計這種分析是可行的，並產生更多的行為差異性。 如果時間允許，我們還會嘗試將簡單的兩健康狀態模型再作改進。這方法會增加計算難度, 但可以使總體存活率函數更接近實際數據。

17500917.label: Realisation of objectives
17500917.value: Objective 1: To prepare for suggesting “an alternative (state-dependent) approach to analyze the effects of mortality decline on life-cycle variables such as retirement age and schooling years” (Objective 1), we use the standard time-dependent approach as the benchmark. In this process, a paper “Mortality decline, productivity increase, and positive feedback between schooling and retirement choices” (co-authored with Zhipeng Cai and C. Y. Kelvin Yuen) was written and accepted for publication by Journal of Demographic Economics (as reported below in Section 8). We then moved to the state-dependent model. We encountered two problems. First, in applying the proposed state-dependent model to study how retirement age varies systematically for different educational groups, we discovered that the schooling choices of different individuals do not vary much in a state-dependent model. The reason is that schooling occurs in early years of the life cycle of the individuals, but in matching with the actual survival data, it is found that most economic agents in the state-dependent model have not yet received the adverse health shock in these early years. Without enough variation in the schooling variable, we cannot say much regarding the original Objective 3. (We stated the above reasons when we applied to replace the original Objective 3 with the revised one. The request was approved in December 2019.) Second, related to Task (1) of Section 6.5 of the last Progress Report, we have studied the effects of mortality decline on retirement age in the constant transition probability version of the two-health-state model, using dynamic programming techniques. However, we found that this version of the state-dependent model does not fit the lifetable data well. (See more discussion in “Objective 3” below.) On the other hand, the logistic transition probability version of the two-health-state model fits the data well, but the analysis of the economic model using this version of the two-health-state model is more complicated, with the problems arising when we use numerical methods to solve the agent’s decision rules based on dynamic programming. We have not solved this problem satisfactorily. According to our assessment, 75% of Objective 1 is achieved. Objective 2: As mentioned above (related to “Objective 1”), we have used dynamic programming methods to formulate the agent’s decision rules based on the constant transition probability version of the two-health-state model. However, similar analysis based on the logistic transition probability version of the two-health-state model becomes much more complicated. Given the time constraint, especially because of the increase in teaching and administrative workload during 2019 and 2020, we decide to first focus on Objectives 1 and 3 and postpone the analysis related to Objective 2. According to our assessment, 30% of Objective 2 is achieved. Objective 3: The revised Objective 3 is closely related to Objective 1. Our original plan is to develop the state-dependent approach to model the survival probability, so as to sharply contrast with the time-dependent approach. The state-dependent approach to model the survival function has the nice property that most people receive adverse health shock some time in their lifetime but the precise time in receiving is random rather than deterministic. As a result, people of the same age may exhibit different health states. We start with a simple two-health-state model. However, after some analysis, we found that while it provides useful alternative interpretation and is convenient to use, it does not fit the data well. We tried different modifications, including the N-state extension (with N up to 5) and still encountered the poor fitting problem. After trying different modifications, we finally found that the model fits the data well if we relax the constant transition probability and replace it by the assumption of logistic transition probability. The Co-I and I plan to report the above results in a working paper, tentatively entitled “A hybrid model of survival probability with state-dependent and age-dependent elements” (as reported below in Section 8). Our tentative conclusion is that a pure version of state-dependent model does not fit the data of survival probability well, but a hybrid model could provide the solution (see Figures 3 and 4 of the draft of working paper “A hybrid model of survival probability with state-dependent and age-dependent elements”). The model is still quite parsimonious, with only 4 parameters to be estimated. We have an incomplete draft of the working paper currently, containing the model formulation and estimation results of the two main versions of the model. We are now applying the hybrid model to explore the main changes of the various components of the hybrid model over the last century. We expect to finish the analysis and produce the complete draft of the paper in a few months’ time. According to our assessment, 90% of Objective 3 is achieved.

17500917.label: Major findings and research outcome
17500917.value: There are 3 main findings in this project. First, a pure state-dependent model seems to be unable to fit the survival data well. The clearest illustration can be seen from Figures 1 and 2 of the working paper “A hybrid model of survival probability with state-dependent and age-dependent elements,” which is based on the constant transition probability version of the two-health-state model. We have tried to increase the number of health states up to 5, and the improvement is very minor. We have also tried to model different sub-categories of the morbid state (say, associated with cancer and cardiac issues, respectively) but the improvement is limited. Our tentative conclusion is that a pure state-dependent model is less capable in fitting the survival data well. Second, a hybrid model combining age-dependent and state-dependent elements is promising. The two-health-state model with logistic transition probability, which is still quite parsimonious with only 4 parameters, can fit the survival data well. Moreover, the logistic transition probability assumption of the hybrid model has a nice property that “older people have on average higher mortality risk than younger people,” which can be regarded as the counterpart of the property of the age-dependent approach that an individual’s mortality risk (potentially after reaching adulthood) is monotonically increasing in age. Such a hybrid model allows us to provide an alternative perspective to analyze issues related to mortality decline such as how different health states (say, healthy and morbid states in a two-state model) and how the transition process from the healthy to morbid state changes systematically over the last century. The above points are about the statistical contributions of this project. In terms of applying the state-dependent models to analyze economic issues, the results of this project suggest that we can apply a pure state-dependent model with constant transition probability to analyze the impact of mortality decline on life-cycle variables such as retirement age. The agent’s decision rules based on dynamic programming have been worked out, and the economic intuition behind the decision rules can easily be seen. However, if fitting the data well is also an important objective and the hybrid model with logistic transition probability is used instead, then the agent’s decision rules are more complicated, leading to less clear interpretation of the decision rules as well as difficulties in computational analysis.

17500917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17500917.value: There are two potential areas for further development of this research. First, we notice that there are gender differences in the estimated coefficients of the hybrid model. It is interesting to see how these differences translate into differences in the death rate in each health states, as well as in the transition from health to the morbid state. Since the hybrid model fits the data well (for both genders), the above differences in the estimated parameters will eventually link to the gender differences in life expectancy and other aspects of the survival functions. Another idea is to examine the sub-category version of the two-health-state model. The sub-categories of the morbid state can be interpreted as different major factors (such as cancer, cardiac diseases etc.) causing human mortality. As mentioned in Section 5.3, we have modified the two-health-state model with constant transition probability by assuming that there are two sub-categories in the morbid state, but the empirical fit of the model is not satisfactory. We conjecture that if we incorporate logistic transition probability specification into this model, the model fit will likely to be good. However, the model will now involve 7 parameters and is less parsimonious. Further work needs to be done to see whether some compromises can be found.

17500917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17500917.value: Many studies of the economic consequences of mortality decline model survival probabilities by age-specific mortality rates. As a result, the mortality pattern at the aggregate level matches the data exactly. However, there is a major disadvantage. Provided that there is no other heterogeneity in the model, every one of the same age would behave in the same way with respect to the variables under consideration (e.g., retirement). In reality, there is huge variation in retirement age and/or other economic choices for people born in the same year. To generate richer and more heterogeneous behavioral outcomes, this project investigates the alternative state-dependent approach. We assume that there are two health states, such that the death rate in each state and the probability from one state to another are constant and do not depend on age mechanically. However, this pure version of the state-dependent model fits the data poorly. We then consider a model with both age-dependent and state-dependent components. In particular, logistic transition probability from the healthy to morbid state is assumed. We find that this hybrid model fits the data well and is still parsimonious. This hybrid model could further be enriched to capture other aspects of human mortality.

17501417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17501417.value: The aim of the proposed project is to investigate the relation between mandatory risk disclosure and investor risk perception. There is ongoing debate in the literature over whether greater risk disclosure in corporate filings leads to investor perceptions of higher risk, and the findings are mixed. I plan to explore this question within a unique Chinese setting with three key characteristics. First, in 2012, Chinese regulators enhanced the mandatory risk disclosure requirement for Chinese firms traded on the main board of the country’s stock exchanges. This new legal requirement serves as an exogenous shock in the research design. Second, some firms traded on the main board are also listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. Stock market listing does not alter firm-specific characteristics and operating environment. Cross-listing therefore provides an opportunity to conduct a difference in differences test investigating the difference in risk perceptions between two markets. Third, since the difference in risk perceptions is driven by market difference, the setting can be further used to investigate this mechanism by examining firms’ investor composition in the two markets. We will carry out an empirical study to address the research question. We will hand-collect and process the mandatory risk disclosure items from the annual reports of firms traded in both the Chinese and Hong Kong stock markets in the 2009 to 2015 sample period. For each annual report, we will design a quantitative measure to capture the risk disclosure level. This measure will allow us to investigate investor perceptions of risk disclosures after the 2012 change in legal requirement. We will examine whether the reactions differ in the Chinese and Hong Kong stock markets. Finally, we will classify the investors into three types and examine whether the different types cause the difference in risk perceptions. The project will contribute to the literature in the following ways. First, it will add change model-based evidence to the existing mixed findings in the literature. The existing findings are more or less cross-sectional in nature, and the exogenous shock in the proposed research will provide for a better causality inference. Second, we will provide evidence as to whether the Chinese and Hong Kong markets react differently to increased risk disclosure. Third, we will determine whether this difference is due to investor composition, providing insights into the role of investor sophistication. 本项目试图研究强制性风险披露与投资者风险感知之间的关联性。既有研究就增加强制性风险披露是否会提高投资者风险感知这一问题给予了高度关注，但对两者之间的因果关系，学术界尚未得出统一的结论。本文拟采用中国上市公司数据研究这一问题，运用中国数据有如下三点优势。一，中国监管机构于2012年提高了对主板上市公司有关风险披露的要求。利用这一外生事件可以观察强制性风险披露水平的变化。二，一部分在中国主板上市的公司，同时也在香港交易所发行股票，及交叉上市。交叉上市不会影响公司本身的特征与经营环境，而不同市场对同一公司监管要求的差异提供了使用双重差分这一研究设计的机会，由此可缓解内生性问题对研究结果的影响。三，由于投资者风险感知的差异源于资本市场的不同，该研究可通过检验同一公司在不同市场中投资者结构的差异，进一步研究影响投资者风险感知的决定因素。 本项目拟采用实证研究的方法探讨此问题。我们将手工收集在中国大陆与香港交叉上市公司年报中有关风险信息的披露，研究样本期间为2009至2015年。我们将计算每家公司各个年度风险水平的量化指标。运用该指标可对比2012年前后投资者风险感知水平的差异。我们将进一步研究主板市场与香港市场投资者风险感知的差异。最后，我们将投资者分进行分类并检验投资者结构对投资者风险感知的影响。 该项目将对既有研究产生如下贡献。一，现有文献的结论主要依据横截面分析的结果，而该项目将提供基于面板数据分析的实证证据，这有利于识别强制性风险披露与投资者风险感知的因果关系。二，该项目将通过研究同一组公司对比中国主板市场与香港市场对风险披露反应的不同。三，从投资者复杂程度的角度出发，该项目将对投资者进行分类并检验投资者结构对投资者风险感知的影响。

17502217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17502217.value: 全球市场对人才需求的增长正在改变创新的地理位置。 为了在当今的知识经济中取得成功，参与的企业必须从世界各地的创新人才库中寻找最聪明的人才。 创新者对迁移已有准备，这更加加剧企业为吸引他们的压力。 那么，政策制定者可以做些什么才能让本土企业在这次招聘比赛中处于优势地位？ 移民政策当然能发挥明确作用，本研究要特别评估知识产权政策所能发挥的微妙作用。 现有的研究（包括我们的研究在内）已经揭示了知识产权保护在通过国际贸易和外国直接投资刺激技术转让方面发挥的重要作用。建立在这些文献基础上，本研究课题是要通过研究知识产权与创新者迁移与技术传播之间的相互作用。我们计划进行四项研究（两个理论和两个实证）来回答以下的问题：知识产权保护（来源国和东道国）如何影响创新移民决策，创新激励和技术传播？创新者的迁移如何影响知识产权的保护？新兴和发展中国家对知识产权的保护是鼓励或限制人才外流？创新者移民如何影响知识流通和技术传播？ 在研究一中，我们会建立一个理论框架，解释知识产权对创新者移民决策的影响，对创新的激励，以及对新技术的转让和采用。在研究二中，我们创立一个政治经济学模式，模型包括创新者的游说活动和潜在的移民可能是如何激励知识产权的改革。我们利用这一模式评估创新者移民是否导致来源国加强其知识产权保护。在研究三中，我们对知识产权对创新者移民的影响进行实证分析。我们要解决移民和知识产权可能互相共同决定的问题。我们使用最近发布的创新移动数据库，并补充有关国家知识产权实力的数据，以确定更强的知识产权是否加剧或限制人才流失。在研究四中，我们将使用实证数据来研究创新者移民对发明的传播的影响。该分析利用“跨国技术历史采用技术数据”。这数据库详细介绍了自1800年以来在150多个国家采用的100多种技术。 我们的研究和两个文献有关：创新者迁移和知识产权技术转让效应。这项研究预计将能为决策者和经济规划者提供比需的信息和答案，以提高他们的能力，并使国际政府和非政府组织能更好地管理高技能人员的移徙对所有人的利益所带来的影响。

17502217.label: Realisation of objectives
17502217.value: Based on several stylized facts, we construct a theoretical framework to address most of the questions raised in the four objectives of the project. Specifically, we introduce an occupational choice model of an innovative North and an imitative South with two dimensions of heterogeneity: product varieties spread over a continuum of quality and individuals differing in their entrepreneurial ability. This framework allows us to study the impact of high-talent migration and IPRs policies on the composition of innovated and imitated products, while accounting for competition between innovated varieties in the North, between imported innovated and domestic imitated varieties in the South, and also between imitators with different talent in the South. Objective 1: How does IPRs protection in source and host countries affect innovator migration decisions, incentives to innovate, and technology diffusion? In the real world, IPRs protection in the North is stronger than that in the South. To reflect such a difference in the model and for simplicity, we assume that the IPRs protection in the North is perfect while that in South is imperfect. We can vary the level IPRs protection in the South to examine its effects on innovation and imitation (which is also considered as technology diffusion). That is, we do not have to check the effects of the changes in the Northern IPRs protection. As there are too many endogenous variables in the model, we decide to assume exogenous number of talent people from the South to migrate to the North to become innovators. As a result, our model can examine the effects of migration on other equilibrium outcomes, but not the effects of IPRs protection on migration decisions. However, it is not difficult to draw implications on effect based on the analyses and results from the current model. In item 6 “Research Outcome”, we will provide our answers to all questions raised in Objective 1 based on our research findings. For example, we find that strengthening IPRs in the South reduces the expected rents of imitators and so, some low-talent entrepreneurs exit imitation. Thus, the policy restrains imitation but only of low-quality varieties. Although we do not include the endogenous decision of migration, as explained above, our analysis and findings allow us to obtain the implications on this decision easily, and thus, we claim that we have achieved 100% of this objective. Objective 2: How does the migration of innovators affect the protection of IPRs? Section 5 of our paper is devoted to analyzing the effects of migration of innovators on innovation and imitation. Section 6 analyzes and compares the effects of migration and IPRs policies on innovation, imitation and welfare. When we were working on the project, we found that it is more interesting and important to investigate the positive questions (i.e., how the policies affect the equilibrium outcomes) than exploring the normative questions (i.e., what are the optimal policies) because in reality, governments are far from offering the optimal policies. Thus, without deriving optimal policies, we cannot answer the above question directly because IPRs protection is taken exogenously in the model. Another reason for not including the optimal IPRs policy in the current paper is that the model is already too complicated. Hence, we decided to leave this question to a separate paper. Unfortunately, the outbreak of Covid-19 slowed down the collaboration of the three investigators, especially with me in Hong Kong and the other two in Canada and Italy, respectively. Although we have not written down another paper to address the question of Objective 2, we have obtained many results. The preliminary draft of our second paper first simplifies the model of the first paper in many aspects and then extends the model by introducing Southern government’s decision on IPRs protection. We explain the findings in item 6 “Research Outcome”. In fact, our analyses and results in Sections 5 and 6 of the first paper have provided sufficient preliminary understanding for us to explore the question of Objective 2 indirectly. For the above reason, we claim that we have achieved around 90% of this objective. Objective 3: Do stronger IPRs in emerging and developing countries nurture or limit brain drain? The work to achieve this objective includes two parts, one being theoretical and the other being empirical. The theoretical part has been, by and large, completed as explained in Objective 1. In particular, the South in our model represents developing countries. Our theoretical analyses imply that stronger IPRs in the South should limit brain drain if the high-talent people in the South are potential innovators there, but nurture brain drain if the high-talent people in the South are simply imitator there. As for the empirical part, we have already collected and processed data. We have compiled a dataset on migration of innovators from developing countries to developed countries. We have also obtained data of the strength of IPRs protection in developing countries. We have run some regressions based on the data and obtained some preliminary results. The main regression models are already given in the grant proposal. We are in the stage of writing up the draft based on the results obtained. We claim that we have achieved 90% of this object. Objective 4: How does innovator migration affect knowledge circulation and technology diffusion? Similar to Objective 3, this objective also has two parts. The theoretical part has also been, by and large, completed as explained in Objective 1. For example, we have analyzed how migration of talent people from the South to the North affects innovation in the North and imitation in the South, which captures the phenomenon of knowledge creation and technology diffusion. However, the empirical part has not been completed. The main reason is as follows. When we started to work on the project, I was still at the University of Hong Kong. We planned to guide one of my PhD students to work on the empirical part of this objective. However, I moved from HKU to Lingnan University in January 2020. I did not have a PhD student at Lingnan University in the first year (2020). I started to supervise a PhD student in 2021 but she could not work on this project in her first year of study. She began to work on the data and the empirical analysis in January 2022. We will guide her to work on this project in 2022. For the above reasons, we claim that we have achieved 80% of this object.

17502217.label: Major findings and research outcome
17502217.value: We have completed one paper “Migration and Imitation”, in which, we introduce a model that is the first in the literature to include innovation, imitation, occupational choice, migration, heterogenous agents, IPRs protection, migration policy and two countries. This model allows us to study the effects of high-talent migration and IPRs policies on the composition of innovated and imitated products. First, the effects of IPRs protection. We find that strengthening IPRs in the South reduces the expected rents of imitators and so, some low-talent entrepreneurs exit imitation. Thus, the policy restrains imitation but only of low-quality varieties. In the North, the competitive pressure on entrepreneurs falls, the innovators' rents rise, and low-ability individuals enter innovation and introduce a wider range of low-quality products. Second, the effects of migration. Allowing migration of high-talent Southern entrepreneurs to the North implies their exit from high-quality imitation in the South and entry into high-quality innovation in the North. A direct “brain drain” reduces the mass of high-talent entrepreneurs in the South, contracting the range of high-quality products that are imitated. At the same time, a higher mass of high-quality varieties now innovated by the migrants reduces spending on each individual variety, creating a negative competition effect. Third, policy comparison of the two policies, i.e., IPRs protection and migration. Migration shifts imitation from high- to low-quality products. This result is in sharp contrast to the policy of strengthening Southern IPRs, which limits low-quality imitation. Moreover, while migration shifts innovation from low- to high-quality products, strengthening IPRs in the South promotes low-quality innovation in the North. With migration, the aggregate income in the production sector falls in the South and rises in the North. But a strengthening of IPRs in the South has the opposite effect. Migration increases average quality of products innovated in the North and also, of products imitated by high-talent entrepreneurs in the South, whereas a strengthening of IPRs in the South decreases the average quality of innovated products and increases the average quality of those imitated by low-talent entrepreneurs. We have also obtained interesting results not reported in “Migration and Imitation” paper, but in other drafts. For example, migration will result in stronger IPRs protection in the South. Stronger IPRs protection in the South reduces (increases) brain drain in countries where high-talent people are also (not) innovators. Finally, migration generates more innovation in the world, but may increase knowledge diffusion.

17502217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17502217.value: There are two potentials for further research work. The first is to complete the empirical work specified in Objectives 3 and 4 of the original grant proposal. The second is to explore other issues. The first work is relatively straightforward. As explained in 5.3 “Realisation of objectives” and 6.1 “Major findings and research outcomes”, our theoretical analyses have already shown that stronger IPRs in the South should limit (nurture) brain drain if the high-talent people in the South are potential innovators (imitators) there. We have already collected and processed data which allow us to test this prediction empirically. We have also analyzed how migration of talent people from the South to the North affects innovation in the North and imitation in the South. Again, we have some basic data and will further collect more data to investigate this issue empirically. We have discussed with a professor in Kyoto University, Japan, about using Japanese data to investigate issues related to international migration, IPRs protection, innovation and imitation. As we do not have detailed information of the data yet, we are not able to pin down the exact research questions to be investigated. In any case, this work will be inspired by the research findings of our current work.

17502217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17502217.value: Our research project examines the effects of international migration and IPRs protection on innovation and imitation. According to conventional wisdom, strengthening IPRs protection in developing countries will decrease imitation and stimulate innovation, which is generally true. However, we show that the weak IPRs protection results in a phenomenon of missing innovation, i.e., a range of relatively low-quality innovative products are not introduced. As a result, strengthening IPRs protection allows us to see more innovative products, but not the high-quality ones. Some people in developed countries advocate that allowing for high-talent people from developing countries to migrate to developed countries can mitigate the effects of weak IPRs protection. We show that a key benefit comes from having more innovations in the high-quality products. We specify conditions under which strengthening IPRs protection in developing countries helps limit brain drain, but brain drain could be severer if the condictiones are not met. Our research sheds new insights on the old but important questions about IPRs protection and innovation. It also shows a clearer and more complete picture about the world which includes innovation, imitation, IPRs protection and talent migration. Our findings have clear policy implications.

17502717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17502717.value: This paper investigates the optimal selling mechanism in auctions in which bidders incur participation costs and they bid with securities whose values depend on not only the bid paid by the auction winner, but also the ultimate (stochastic) payoff of the asset won by the bidder. The paper aims to provide guidance to sellers on how to optimally structure auctions, taking into account bidders' entry costs, number of potential bidders, the level of restrictions on the securities, and degree of heterogeneity among bidders. 本文研究了特定条件下的最优拍卖机制，即竞标者在拍卖中产生参与成本并以证券进行竞价，证券的价值不仅取决于中标方的中标价格，也受中标物品未来产生的现金流影响。本文在考虑竞价者的准入费用、潜在竞价者的数量、对证券的限制条件和竞价者之间异质化程度的基础上，研究最大化卖方收益的定价机制。

17502717.label: Realisation of objectives
17502717.value: The paper was published at Journal of Economic Theory this year (2002). We have achieved all these objectives (with the exception of “whether bidders incur entry costs before or after knowing their valuations for the auctioned asset”; see more on this at the end). Concretely, we analyze optimal auction mechanisms when bidders base costly entry decisions on their valuations, and bidders pay with a fixed royalty rate plus cash. With sufficient valuation uncertainty relative to entry costs, the optimal mechanism features asymmetry so that bidders enter with strictly positive but different (ex-ante) probabilities. When bidders are ex-ante identical, higher royalty rates--which tie payments more closely to bidder valuations--increase the optimal degree of asymmetry in auction design, further raising revenues. When bidders differ ex-ante in entry costs, the seller favors the low cost entrant; whereas when bidders have different valuation distributions, the seller favors the weaker bidder if entry costs are low, but not if they are high. Higher royalty rates cause the seller to favor the weaker bidder by less, and the strong bidder by more. In terms of policy implications, our paper provides theoretical foundations for negotiated break-up fees that favor one bidder over another in a takeover auction or the favoring of a particular supplier in procurement auctions. A firm seeking a buyer often elicits an initial bid from one bidder by promising to reimburse it for its efforts if it is outbid, thereby committing the target firm to excluding other bidders unless their valuations are sufficiently high. In procurements the US government often provides preferential treatment to domestic firms and small businesses. Ayres and Cramton (1996) show such preferential treatments enhance seller revenues in auctions for paging licenses by the FCC, in which winning bids of favored bidders are subsidized by a fixed rate. In a setting with ex-ante asymmetric bidders, McAfee and McMillan (1989) show that favoring ex-ante weaker bidders can enhance auction revenues. In addition to revealing the revenue-enhancing effect of bid preference policies in a general framework with heterogeneous bidders, our endogenous entry model provides guidance on how the optimal design regarding the identity of which bidder to favor and the extent of that favoritism should vary with the sizes of entry costs and royalty rates, and the nature of bidder asymmetry. We did not pursue the investigation of how the optimal mechanism depends on whether bidders incur entry costs before or after knowing their valuations for the auctioned asset, because per referee’s suggestion, we went into greater details on how bidder heterogeneity affects the optimal design, and there we derived more interesting and significant results. We show that (1) there is a discontinuity in the optimal degree of asymmetry with respect to the underlying bidder heterogeneity, and (2) We establish the robustness of our results beyond small deviations from the baseline model, and show that the consequences are non-trivial for large deviations. The optimal bidder to favor and the extent of such favoritism depends on the royalty rate (this relates to the level of restrictions placed on the securities allowed) and the size of entry costs in non-monotonic and discontinuous ways.

17502717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17502717.value: This paper investigates the optimal design of auctions when bidders base costly entry decisions on their valuations, and bidders pay with a fixed royalty rate plus cash. Such auctions are common: Oil and gas lease auctions typically feature equity payments in the form of royalties; 70% of mergers and acquisitions involve some equity; Venture capital financing, procurement auctions, and lead-plaintiff auctions often use similar payment structures. We establish that as long as there is sufficient valuation uncertainty relative to entry costs, the optimal mechanism features asymmetry so that bidders enter with strictly positive but different (ex-ante) probabilities. When bidders are ex-ante identical, higher royalty rates---which tie payments more closely to bidder types---increase the optimal degree of asymmetry in auction design, allowing the seller to raise revenues further. When bidders differ ex ante, strategic interactions become more subtle. We show that the optimal bidder to favor, the extent of such favorism, and the impact of the royalty rate hinge on the nature of the heterogeneity and the sizes of entry costs. We provide a unified intuition for the driving forces underlying these findings.

17502817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17502817.value: The U.S. Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (PCAOB) recently proposed that auditors be required to report on “critical audit matters” (CAMs) that involve challenging, subjective, or complex judgments to be made. Proponents suggest that enhanced disclosure not only assists investors in evaluating the usefulness of audit opinions and thus facilitates investors’ investment decisions, but also provides incentive for auditors to improve audit quality. However, there is growing concern among auditors that the additional disclosure requirement may increase auditor litigation risk. Opponents also argue that investors may be induced to rely unduly on the audit opinion, neglecting to acquire their own private information in making investment decisions. Some recent experimental studies have examined the potential effect of CAM disclosure, focusing mainly on the impact on auditor liability (Brown et al. 2015; Gimbar et al. 2016; Kachelmeier et al. 2014). Therefore, this research project provides an economic-based analysis of the consequences of CAM disclosure on audit quality, investors’ private information acquisition and investment efficiency in a setting where audit quality is not only motivated by auditor liability in the event of audit failure, but also influences investors’ private information acquisition and investment decisions. The proposed model emphasizes the strategic interaction between auditing and investors’ private information acquisition in the determination of quality of audited financial statement information and investment efficiency. We use this model to investigate how this strategic interaction varies with the proposed disclosure of CAMs. We will make predictions regarding the effects on auditor’s choice of audit quality and investors’ private information acquisition and investment decisions. We hope that this project will contribute to the ongoing debate regarding the costs and benefits of making disclosures of CAMs mandatory, and provide some insights into its potential unintended consequences. Further, these results from our theoretical model could inform the PCAOB before finalization of this proposed regulation on CAM disclosure. 美國公共會計監督委員會（PCAOB）最近提出，審計師需要報告涉及挑戰性、主觀或複雜判斷的“關鍵審計事項”（CAM）。支持者建議，加強披露不僅有助於投資者評估審計意見的有用性，從而促進投資者的投資決策，而且還為審計師提供了提高審計質量的激勵。然而，審計師越來越關注額外的披露要求可能會增加訴訟風險。反對者還認為，投資者可能會被不必要地依賴於審計意見，忽視在作出投資決策時應該尋找自己的私人信息。 一些最近的實驗研究已經研究了關鍵審計事項披露的潛在影響，但主要側重於對審計師責任的影響（Brown et al.2015; Gimbar et al. 2016; Kachelmeier et al. 2014）。有見及此，本研究項目將對關鍵審計事項披露進行全面的經濟分析，這包括對審計質量的影響，以及其對投資者私人信息獲取和投資效率的影響。我們提出的模型不僅強調了審計和投資者私人信息獲取的戰略互動, 還強調了他們在確定審計財務報表信息質量和投資效率方面的重要角色。我們使用這個模型來研究這種戰略互動如何隨著關鍵審計事項披露而變化, 並對審計師對審計質量的選擇和投資者私人信息獲取和投資決策的影響作出預測。 我們希望這個項目的成果將有助於關於強制關鍵審計事項披露的成本和收益的爭論，並指出一些其潛在的意想不到的後果。此外，我們希望這個理論模型的結果可以在PCAOB未完成關於強制關鍵審計事項披露的提案前提供有用的參考。

17502817.label: Realisation of objectives
17502817.value: The objectives of this study are 100% achieved. A theory paper titled “Critical Audit Matter Disclosure, Audit Quality, and Investment Efficiency” has been written and presented at the 2019 Hong Kong Inter-Campus Accounting Theory Mini Workshop on October 26, 2019 and received good comments and suggestions from workshop participants. I was also invited to present the paper at the accounting research workshop at the University of Graz, Austria, on June 22, 2020, but the visit was subsequently cancelled due to the COVID-19 pandemic. On February 25, 2020, I and my coauthor, Dr. Nanqin Liu at the Southern University of Science and Technology, submitted the paper to The Accounting Review, one of the top peer-reviewed international journals in accounting that has an acceptance rate of less than 10%. After going through three rounds of extensive reviews, on June 22, 2022, we received the decision letter from The Accounting Review that our paper is accepted for publication. Our paper will appear in the March 2023 Issue of The Accounting Review.

17502817.label: Major findings and research outcome
17502817.value: The results obtained in the paper titled “Critical Audit Matter Disclosure, Audit Quality, and Investment Efficiency” are summarized as follows: ABSTRACT: We study the effects of the disclosure of critical audit matters (CAMs) on an auditor’s audit effort and an investor’s scrutiny effort decisions, as well as investment efficiency. Both the auditor and the investor can prevent a bad investment by respectively auditing and scrutinizing the firm’s financial reports to detect misstatements about the investment value. Investment efficiency is determined by the investor’s total mix of information. The disclosure of CAMs helps the investor assess investment risk and infer the auditor’s effort, and thus enables the investor to fine-tune scrutiny effort, which can in turn adversely influence the auditor’s effort decision. We show when and why the disclosure of CAMs increases or decreases ex ante audit effort, ex ante investor scrutiny, and investment efficiency. Our analyses have both testable empirical implications and policy implications.

17502817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17502817.value: Since 2019, the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board has required auditors to disclose critical audit matters (CAMs) beyond the binary pass/fail opinion. CAMs are likely to be identified in areas where investors have a particular interest, such as significant management estimates and judgments, areas of high financial statement and audit risk, and significant unusual transactions. Proponents argue that CAM disclosure will add to investors’ total mix of information and will focus investors’ attention on key financial reporting areas that deserve more attention, thus contributing to investors’ ability to make investment decisions. However, although CAM disclosure helps investors assess investment risk and fine-tune effort in scrutinizing the project they intend to fund, its impact on audit effort cannot be overlooked. To the extent that CAM disclosure improves investment decisions, the associated decrease in investment loss might disincentivize audit effort by decreasing auditors’ expected legal liability. Therefore, whether CAM disclosure can increase investors’ total mix of information is unclear. This paper presents a theoretical model to study how CAM disclosure would influence the strategic interactions between the auditor’s and investor’s effort decisions in detecting financial misstatements and examine when and why the disclosure increases or decreases investors’ total mix of information.

17503117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17503117.value: 摘要 企業的會計程序把所發生的各項業務歸總為各類帳戶，並編制為財務報表。單個企業的會計記帳為複式記賬法：每筆交易至少被紀錄在兩個不同的帳戶中，並且紀錄金額相等，一個記借方，另一個記貸方。在多個企業的經濟體系中，企業之間彼此發生交易。當兩個企業發生一項交易時，每個企業都分別用複式記帳法紀錄這筆交易，意味著一共有四個帳戶受到影響，也就是一個四式記帳系統。四式記帳體系使對等交易的雙方所紀錄的借項和貸項彼此一致。因而，以四式記帳為基礎，我們可以研究在一個經濟體系中企業彼此之間的關聯和交易。我們希望利用四式會計體系的結構，建立一個基於會計體系的網絡分析框架。 複式記賬過程可以用一種特殊的矩陣來表示，這個矩陣可以被稱為“關聯矩陣”。通過關聯矩陣，各種交易被轉換為會計帳目的總額。我們把單個企業的會計“關聯矩陣”擴展為多個企業的“關聯矩陣”，可以覆蓋符合四式記帳法的企業之間的交易。這個擴展的關聯矩陣可以把企業的所有交易，包括彼此之間的交易，轉換為一套涵蓋所有企業財務報表帳目的總額。 這個項目的主要目標是為財務報表讀者提供一個如何利用所有企業“關聯矩陣”來推測產生這套報表數據的最有可能的企業之間的交易。這個目標依靠單個企業的報表是不可能得到的，因為企業和不同外部企業之間的交易常常被歸總到一起，無法準確的區分開。我們可以藉著多個企業的會計關聯矩陣來進行推測，並且推導出在哪些條件下可以更準確的估計出企業之間的交易。 我們的理論框架可以被應用在不同的實際情況中，用來估測觀察不到或者是數據缺乏的企業間交易的情況。其中一個應用是用來估測上市公司之間的跨行業交易總額。美國的BEA提供了一些收入產出的統計數據，但是這些數據並不一定準確，上市公司只代表了經濟中的一部分企業。用基於會計四式記帳的多個企業關聯矩陣，我們可以更好的估測跨行業的交易量。另外，我們的框架還可以用於估計企業之間的信用借貸情況，公司在公開的信息披露中通常不會提供這個數據 。如果我們可以估測企業互相借貸的情況，就可以檢測企業在供應鏈中的議價能力和財務融資決定。

17503117.label: Major findings and research outcome
17503117.value: We explore the representation of accounts and transactions of multiple entities when (1) each entity practices double-entry bookkeeping and (2) inter-entity transactions take place. As such, entity-to-entity links created by ``real'' inter-entity transactions and account-to-account links within an entity created by ``artificial'' double-entry bookkeeping are integrated into an account network through the well-known quadruple-entry bookkeeping of the inter-entity transactions: each inter-entity transaction is recorded in four accounts (two within each entity). We focus on loops in such an account network and distinguish loops created from different accounting events (such as cash transactions, non-cash inter-entity transactions, and non-cash intra-entity transactions) and how these loops are affected when the account-network expands. Applications of the representation and some results from simulations are also presented.

17503117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17503117.value: We plan to apply the framework in this project to the supply chain data with customers and suppliers network, and utilize the financial statement data including sales, cost of sales, accounts receivables and accounts payables to infer the network structure of the supply chain. This may be further applied to detect potential manipulations of accrual basis sales and untimely recognitions of bad debt expenses, etc.

17503117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17503117.value: The bookkeeping network of the accounting process, including various accounts and their classification (into various categories of financial statement captions and line-items, etc.), is a foundation for the modern accounting system. Our project helps organize an accounting system and facilitates the meaningful representation of real-world transactions as dollar amounts recorded in the accounts and the assumed account categories. We also have implications for the audit firms if the auditors can utilize the network relations among client firms and more efficiently detect accounting errors/misbehavior/fraud.
