17503317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17503317.value: The overarching question we plan to address in this project is whether firm managers cater to investor demand in choosing corporate policies. We focus on one particular policy – the dividend policy. To be specific, firm managers rationally cater to investor demand – they pay or increase dividends when investors value dividends more, otherwise they cut dividends (Baker and Wurgler 2004a, b). The core challenge in this literature is to quantify investors’ dividend demand, which is not related to firms’ other characteristics, such as growth opportunities. To quantify the dividend demand from current investors, we propose a novel measure based on the short-term price effect on dividend payment days. Drawing on the observation that investors who do not consume their dividends usually reinvest them on payment days, and that such uninformed trades tend to outstrip liquidity and can lead to a short-term price impact, we measure current investors’ demand for dividends by looking at the price pressure pattern around dividend payment days. Specifically, when a large fraction of a dividend payment is reinvested, there should be a large short-term price effect, which are informative about the fraction of investors who do not need dividends – to the extent that these investors are not tax-exempt, dividend payments cause an unnecessary tax burden. Based on this measure, we study how firms change their dividend policies in response to current investors’ dividend demand and why firms cater to this demand. The contribution of our study is twofold. First, we propose a novel and purely cross-sectional measure for investors’ dividend demand. Prior literature uses the valuation difference between dividend payers and non-payers as a proxy for market-wide dividend demand. One clear issue is that the valuation measure, M/B ratio, is also highly correlated with growth opportunities. A more recent study (Becker et al. 2011) uses local senior density to measure dividend demand at the county level (again not the firm level). Two assumptions are needed for this proxy: a) senior investors like dividends more than other investors, and b) investors tend to overinvest local stocks in their portfolios. However, since local senior density has little variation over time, their analysis is essentially based on two cross-sections. Second, our study also contributes to the literature which studies how stock markets affect corporate policies, such as Baker, Stein and Wurgler (2003), and Polk and Sapienza (2008), Chen, Goldstein and Jiang (2007). 本文基于股利政策研究了管理层在制定公司政策时是否迎合投资者需求。根据股利政策的迎合理论（Baker and Wurgler 2004a，b），管理层会在投资者更偏好股利时发放更多的股利从而理性地迎合投资者的需求。此类文献在实证研究中的难点在于构建出能够衡量投资者股利需求且与其他公司特征无关的指标。 本文基于股票在股利发放日的短期价格效应，提出了一个新的指标来衡量股票现有投资者的股利需求。在股利发放日，不将股利用于消费的投资者通常会进行再投资。这类投资者的非知情交易需求超过流动性供给时，就会产生短期价格效应。根据此现象，本文以股利发放日附近的股票价格趋势来衡量现有投资者的股利需求。具体而言，当一只股票所发放的大部分股利被用于再投资时，会表现出强的短期价格效应。由于接收股利并再投资的过程中会产生税收上的损失，将股利用于再投资的投资者实际上没有股利需求。因此，股利发放日再投资引起的短期价格效应的强度能够衡量无股利需求的投资者占现有投资者的比例。基于这一新的衡量指标，本文研究了公司如何根据现有投资者的股利需求调整股利政策，以及公司为什么要迎合这一股利需求。 本文的贡献有两点：（1）本文提出了一个新的横截面指标以衡量投资者股利需求。以往的研究用支付股利与不支付股利的公司之间在估值上的差额作为市场层面股利需求的代理变量。其缺陷在于衡量公司估值水平的变量，比如市账比，通常与公司成长性高度相关。一项最近的研究（Becker et al，2011）用本地老年人口密度来衡量郡县层面的股利需求。这一代理变量依赖两个假设：（a）老年投资者相比其他投资者更偏好股利。（b）投资者倾向于在投资组合中过多地配置本地股票。由于本地老年人口密度缺少时间上的差异，这项研究的实证分析主要基于横截面上的差异。（2）本文补充了研究股票市场对公司政策影响的文献（Baker，Stein and Wurgler，2003；Polk and Sapienza，2008；Chen，Goldstein and Jiang，2007)。

17503317.label: Realisation of objectives
17503317.value: I summarize the outcome of the project and how we achieved the outcome of this project. Overall, this project aims to study the effect of stock markets on corporate policies. I argue that stock markets have useful information that can guide corporates to make corporate policies, such as investment or dividend payout. In the proposal, I planned to focus on one particular corporate policy-dividend payout. I hypothesize that firms learn information from the stock market and adjust the dividend policy to cater to investor demand of dividends. I propose a novel measure based on the short-term price pressure on dividend payment days to capture the dividend demand from current investors. When investors do not consume dividends but reinvest them on payment days, there will be a short-term price impact. Thus, I measure investors’ demand for dividends by looking at the price pressure patterns around dividend payment days. Specifically, when a large fraction of a dividend payment is reinvested, there should be a large short-term price effect, which then informs us of the fraction of investors who do not need dividends – to the extent that these investors are not tax-exempt, dividend payments cause an unnecessary tax burden. Based on this measure, I study firms’ dividend catering behaviors and how firms cater to investors’ demand. I have some empirical results to find that firms learn information from price pressure around dividend payment days. Specifically, I have found that (1) there exists strong price pressure around dividend payment days; (2) Firms respond strongly to the price pressure around dividend payment days by adjusting their dividend payout. I have reported these results in the mid-term progress report. This work achieved objectives 1, 2, and 3. After the mid-term progress report, I planned to address the causal effect and provide more convincing evidence for the hypothesis (see objectives 4 and 5). However, I occurred several challenges during this process. First, when I planed to use to income tax changes as a shock to study how firms learn information from the stock prices in making dividend payout, I found that this shock is uncorrelated with the price pressure around dividend payment. This suggests that the income tax changes are not good instrumental variables for dividend demand. This is potentially due to the feature of our measure of dividend demand, which is daily price pressure around dividend payment. That is, when there are income tax changes, the market has anticipated the tax policies and the effect of tax policies on dividend demand or dividend policies have already been reflected in the market. I have been struggling with this technical issue and could not perfectly solve it. However, this technical issue is the key to publish my research project in top finance journals. Meanwhile, when I was attempting to solve the aforementioned technical issue, I found that there are two competing research papers that have been published in top finance journals. The first paper, titled “DRIPS and the Dividend Pay Date Effect” (Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis, August 2017), has similar results on the price pressure on dividend payment days, which I reported in the proposal and the mid-term progress report. This means that I could not only use the results on the price pressure around dividend payment to write a publishable paper. The second paper, titled “Monetary Policy and Reaching for Income” (Journal of Finance, forthcoming), has similar ideas with my proposal and found that investors flow into income-generating assets such as high-dividend stocks and high-yield bonds when interest rates are low. Meanwhile, this paper found that firms actively change their dividend payout policies to cater to investor demand for dividend due to low-interest rate. In fact, the role of interest rate is similar to the role of income tax. In this sense, even if I could solve the technical issue, there is limited potential to publish the results on dividend catering in top finance journals. After carefully thinking about how to conduct this project and make this project’s outcome publishable at top finance journal, I used similar economic intuitions and some preliminary results of this project to further a new direction of corporate policy. I still stick to the big pitch of this project. That is, I study the effect of stock markets on corporate policies and attempt to show that how firms learn information from the stock market in making corporate policies. Now I switched to focus on another important corporate policy-firm investment. I also use the price pressure as an important signal for corporate and still stick to objective 3 and study heterogeneities among firms in learning behavior. More importantly, after focusing on corporate investment, I have successfully solved the causality problem (objective 5). Finanly, based on the outcome, I have finished one completed research paper, titled “Managerial Overconfidence and Market Feedback Effects” and the research paper is quite promising, and I have submitted this paper to top finance journals. For example, I attempted to submit this paper to Journal of Finance (the best academic journal in finance) and got reject an resubmit from the Journal of Finance. I summarize the extent the project objectives have been achieved. In the paper titled “Managerial Overconfidence and Market Feedback Effects”, I argue and show that managerial learning from stock prices can lead to feedback loop vulnerability: liquidity-induced trading can impose a negative externality on the ﬁrm’s investment decisions, inducing liquidity unconstrained investors to sell their stock holdings. Interestingly, overconﬁdent managers that dismiss stock price information may be less vulnerable to the price impact of liquidity-driven trades. To make this argument clear, I develop a theoretical model of managerial learning and highlight the role of managerial overconfidence. Meanwhile, we conduct empirical evidence based on managerial overconfidence and price pressured induced by mutual fund fire sales. The empirical evidence strongly supports the model’s underlying premises and predictions: First, investment decisions of overconﬁdent CEOs are signiﬁcantly less responsive to stock price ﬂuctuations. Second, the price impact of liquidity shocks, e.g., mutual fund ﬁre sales, is substantially smaller for ﬁrms with overconﬁdent CEOs. Third, probably most importantly, I use mutual fund fire sales and the mutual fund trading scandal of the 2003-2003 period as an exogenous shock to mutual fund fire sales to successfully solve the causal issue. In a summary, in this project, I am to study the effect of stock markets on corporate policies. Specifically, we argue that stock markets have useful information that can guide corporates to make valuable corporate policies, such as investment or dividend payout. Although I have rich empirical results based on dividend payout, I could not solve the causality issue in the setting of dividend payout and the two published papers make the results based on dividend payout have limited chances to be published in top finance journals. Following the big pith and similar novel measures/methodologies proposed in this project, I have successfully solved the causality issue and have completed one research paper with high potential to be published in top academic journals. Meanwhile, given that corporate investment is the first-order question in both academic and practice, this paper’s outcome potentially has larger impacts than the original outcome based on dividend payout.

17503317.label: Major findings and research outcome
17503317.value: I have two bathes of research outcomes. I summarize them as follows. First, closely following the original plan in the proposal, I have found that (1) there is a large price pressure around dividend payment days; (2) firms respond strongly to the price pressure measured in (1) in changing their dividend payouts. These two results are consistent with the main argument of this proposal that stock markets have important impacts on corporate policies. That is, firm managers learn useful information from stock markets to make corporate policies. The second outcome of this project is a complete and promising research paper, titled "Managerial Overconfidence and Market Feedback Effects”. This research paper follows similar economic intuitions, similar novel measures (price pressure), and similar cross-sectional tests, but focus on corporate investment, which is the most important corporate policy. More importantly, after focusing on corporate investment, I have successfully solved the causality problem (objective 5). The details of this research paper titled "Managerial Overconfidence and Market Feedback Effects” based on this project has two important findings. First, I develop a theoretical model of managerial learning and highlight the role of managerial overconfidence. This theoreical model contributes to the thoereical literature on how stock markets guide corporate policy. The second finding is empirical one. We sart by establishing empirical support for our premise that overcon-ﬁdent managers and other managers signiﬁcantly diﬀer in their investment response to stock prices in the contexts of corporate investment and mergers and acquisitions. We next ﬁnd that non-overconﬁdent managers do cut their investments in response to the stock price drops driven by mutual fund ﬁre sales. Overconﬁdent managers are, however, less sensitive in their investment response to such stock price movements. We further conduct empirical analyses based on mutual fund ﬁre sales and mutual fund trading scandals of 2003-2004, which are arguably among the most well-studied non-fundamental shocks in ﬁnancial markets, and we find similar results. In summary, the results in the research paper "Managerial Overconfidence and Market Feedback Effects” have achieved the big pitch of this research proposal and shown that firm managers learn useful information from stock markets to make corporate policies--corporate investment. For your reference, please see the attached file in Part C.

17503317.value: Although the research paper titled "Managerial Overconfidence and Market Feedback Effects” based on this project is completed and I have finished all work, there is still some room in improving this paper. I plan to take several actions. First, I plan to improve the theoretical model of this research paper. A fully-fledged model itself has a large contribution and has the potential to be published in top finance journals. Second, this research paper got the reject and resubmit from the Journal of Finance. I am following the comments from referees to revise the paper. The referees' comments are insightful and can largely help me improve this paper. I believe that this paper finally can find a good patch to be published on decent finance journals.

17503317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17503317.value: The research paper titled "Managerial Overconfidence and Market Feedback Effects” contributes to both theoretical and empirical literature on managerial learning and the effect of stock markets on corporate policies. This theoretical model in this paper is the first one to formalize and highlight that managerial attribute plays an import role in the process on how stock markets affect corporate policies. Second, this study contributes to this strand of literature on managerial learning. This study is the first to propose a novel way to test the mangeral learning, in which the empirical test always has causality issues and it is quite challenging to pin down the causal effect. That is, I show that heterogeneity in managerial attributes, such as overconﬁdence, that aﬀect their sensitivity to stock price information provides a new way to test the feedback eﬀect. Third, this paper can help understand some large non-fundamental drops in financial markets. In fact, financial markets often experience large non-fundamental drops, the recovery from which takes considerable time. One example is the Financial Crisis of 2007–08 and Individual stocks also frequently experience non-fundamental “ﬁre sales” from mutual funds which are subject to investor redemption. My study shows that material learning plays an important role here.

17504117.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17504117.value: 高管激励的效用：基于中国国企改革的实证研究

17504117.label: Project Objectives
17504117.value: We will examine how the “pay-cap” reform affects shareholder value. We will examine how the reform shapes a broad range of corporate policies including investment and operating efficiency, innovation, profitability and etc. We will examine whether the reform drives the competent executives to work in private companies and leads to a loss of managerial human capital. We will examine how manager’s political promotion propensity moderates the effect of the reform.

We will examine whether the reform drives the competent executives to work in private companies and leads to a loss of managerial human capital.
We will examine how manager’s political promotion propensity moderates the effect of the reform.

17504117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17504117.value: As a central issue in financial economics, incentive schemes align the interests between managers and shareholders and thus alleviate the agency problems within firms (Shleifer and Vishny 1997; Tirole 2001). It is well documented that managerial incentives affect firm performance and corporate policies (Jensen and Murphy 1990; Coles et al. 2006; Bebchuk and Weisbach 2010). But because incentive arrangements and firm performance are simultaneously determined, a causal interpretation for prior findings has been difficult (Coles et al. 2012). We approach to this issue by evaluating an important and unanticipated reform in China. In 2014, Politburo announced a regulation to limit executive compensation at state-owned enterprises (SOEs), which subsequently leads to a significant cut in executive pay. Before the reform, a market-oriented incentive system has been gradually established in Chinese SOEs and executive compensation was tied to firm performance (Groves et al. 1995). This marketization process has been reversed by this recent reform. Setting cap for executive pay and associating the compensation to the wage of average workers, the reform provides a compelling “reverse” experiment to examine the impact of managerial disincentives. Specifically, the reform is enacted due to political reasons instead of economic reasons. As a part of the anti-corruption campaign to combat the “unreasonably high” executive salaries in SOEs, the reform is exogenous to firm fundamentals. Moreover, the reform creates variation at different levels facilitating a difference-in-differences analysis. By bringing the compensation back to a uniform level, the reform impacts firms heterogeneously according to the deviation of their pay level from market-based standards. Based on a sample of Chinese listed firms, we explore how managerial incentives matter in our novel setup. We first assess the market reactions to the announcement of the reform and examine a broad range of corporate policies including investment efficiency, operating efficiency, innovation and profitability. Importantly, we extend the literature by testing whether the reform triggers human capital migration across firms and leads to a loss of managerial talent among Chinese SOEs. We analyze the manager turnovers after the reform, market reactions to these turnovers, and further investigate whether managerial characteristics, such as general managerial skills and risk aversion, moderate the effect. Last, we utilize a unique institutional feature in Chinese political promotion and uncover how political promotion propensity plays role in substituting the effect of pecuniary compensation arrangement. These findings provide evidence for existing theories and also shed lights on studies concerning SOE inefficiency. 作为金融经济学的核心问题之一，激励机制将管理者和股东两者之间的利益保持一致, 从而减轻公司内的代理问题（Shleifer和Vishny 1997; Tirole 2001）。有文献证明，管理激励影响企业绩效和企业政策（Jensen和Murphy 1990; Coles et al。2006; Bebchuk和Weisbach 2010）。但是由于奖励安排和企业绩效同时确定，因此先前发现的因果解释是困难的（Coles et al。2012）。 我们通过评估中国的重大意外改革来处理这个问题。 2014年政治局宣布了一项限制国有企业（SOE）行政薪酬的法规，随后导致其大幅削减高管薪酬。改革前，中国国有企业逐步形成市场化激励机制，执行薪酬与企业绩效挂钩。这个最近的改革已经扭转了这个市场化进程。在最新的改革中， 高管薪酬的上限和薪酬与平均工人的工资相关联，从而提供了一个新颖的“反向”实验来检验薪酬对绩效的影响。具体来说，改革是由于政治体制改革的一部分而不是经 济原因而颁布的。所以与公司基本面没有直接关系。此外，改革创造了不同层次的变化，促进差异分析。通过把薪酬调整到一个统一的水平，改革根据薪酬的偏差而不均匀地影响各种类型的企业。 基于中国上市公司的样本，我们首先评估市场对改革公告的反应，并研究投资效率，经营效率，创新和盈利能力等广泛的公司政策。重要的是，我们通过测试改革是否引发人力资本迁移到企业，导致中国国有企业失去管理人才，从而延伸文献。此外，我们会根据中国独特的制度特征，揭示政治晋升倾向如何取代金钱补偿安排的效果。这些研究结果为现有理论提供了证据，也揭示了国有企业效率低下的研究。

17504117.label: Realisation of objectives
17504117.value: After the approval of this proposal, we noticed that another group of authors had completed a paper on almost the same topic and started circulating it online. Their paper entitled “Restricting CEO Pay Backfires: Evidence from China”, which can be retrieved from https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=3081822, examines the effects of pay restriction on CEO behaviour and firm performance. They found that CEOs of central state-owned enterprises (CSOEs) in China increase self-dealing activities following the pay cuts, such as consuming more perks and diverting corporate resources for their own benefits. Corporate performance also decreases subsequently. In view of the competing paper and to better contribute to the literature, we explored the following alternatives in a similar spirit to achieve the objectives of our research. First, we evaluate the impact of another important and unanticipated regulation of the same anti-corruption reform in China which removed government-related personnel from independent directorships of publicly listed companies (hereafter “de-politicization” or “File 18”). With respect to objective 1, we estimate the value effect of the removal of politicians from boards in the short and long run, respectively. We conduct an event study of the stock market response around the time of the announcement. We form a sample of more than 1,100 listed private firms and a hand-coded dataset of corporate directors. To measure short-run impact on shareholder value, we focus on the five-day event window around File 18, and calculate the cumulative abnormal returns (CAR[-2,+2])) for connected firms and unconnected firms. We also construct buy-and-hold returns (BHAR[-1,+3yr]) to capture the longer-term effect on firm value. With respect to objective 2, we construct a 13-year panel dataset spanning the 2007–2019 period to estimate the real effects of File 18. The identification is based on the director resignation events among firms. Using a difference-in-differences strategy based on a matched sample, we explore the changes in a broad range of corporate outcomes and policies, including financing (measured by access to cheap loans), innovation (proxied by R&D), investment (proxied by import of machinery), self-dealing activities (measured by related party transactions), and operational efficiency (measured by total factor productivity (TFP)). Second, as the above study focuses on private firms because the inherent political connections of SoE management make them less affected by or largely immune to the File 18 rule, we conduct another study to extend our analysis to SOEs to achieve the objectives in a similar spirit. Specifically, we examine on how the State Capital Operation Program in China, i.e., regulation that requires parent CSOEs to contribute part of their consolidated income to a new fiscal fund affect CSOEs’ policies and outcomes. This project realizes objective 1 and 2 in the sense that it examines the effect of the program on firms’ payout policy and shareholder value. We use a sample for 2003-2014 and employ a difference-in-differences (DiD) identification strategy to study impact of the program on payout policies and value of listed CSOEs in which parent CSOEs hold controlling yet partial stakes. We consider and test two channels through which the state controlling shareholder can shift resources away from the listed CSOE, i.e., (1) intercorporate loans with the listed CSOEs as creditors, and (2) the listed CSOEs’ commercial purchases from related parties within the CSOE group. We also check and find postprogram valuation (measured by Tobin’s Q) decreases for listed CSOEs, suggesting the expropriation hurts minority shareholders’ interests. It also achieves objective 3 & 4 as the tendency for parent CSOEs to maintain resources within the group and the ensuing dividend reduction of listed CSOEs can be traced to group managers’ political incentives. Specifically, we measure such incentives using the evaluation year or the rating in the last evaluation of the manager of the parent CSOE and estimate the effect of the program on listed CSOEs’ dividend policy as a function of group managers’ political incentives / career concern. The four objectives are considered fully achieved. The research output of the first study has been accepted by Journal of Law, Economics and Organization, one of the top two law and economic journals. The research output of the second study received (invitation to revise and resubmit) R&R at Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis, one of the top four finance journals.

17504117.label: Major findings and research outcome
17504117.value: Our research examines the impact of two important and unanticipated reforms in China on shareholder values and corporate policies. 1. In the first study, we study the impact of China’s File 18 on a variety of firm outcomes. Our results show there is a short-term valuation reduction for firms but a long-run reversal. Specifically, we find that for the five-day event window around File 18, the cumulative abnormal returns for connected firms fell significantly. We also construct buy-and-hold returns to capture the longer-term effect on firm value but find the effect is insignificant. 2. We further explore the real activities of the affected firms to understand the valuation effect. We find evidence consistent with a “cost” channel, whereby connected firms lost the benefits of their connections and their value initially declined. This is consistent with the view that political connections have value for firms because they provide government concessions such as favourable regulations, government contracts, and cheap finance and bailouts. 3. We also find evidence of a “dynamic adjustment” channel, whereby File 18 incentivized connected firms to transform their corporate strategies and operate more competitively by importing machinery, investing in R&D. Consequently, their cost of debt had recovered; their market valuation had bounced back from losses around the time that File 18 was enacted. This paper has been accepted for publication at Journal of Law, Economics and Organization. 4. In the second study, we find a significant reduction in listed CSOEs’ cash dividends upon the inception of the program compared with a control group of non-state-owned enterprises (NSOEs) unaffected by the program and the reduction is economically sizable. The result is consistent with our hypothesis that experiencing mandated resource reductions, the parent CSOEs will reduce the listed CSOEs’ pro-rata dividends to maintain the preprogram levels of group resources. Corroborating this notion, we find that the dividend reductions of the listed CSOEs are concurrent with increases in intercorporate loans and related-party transactions within their inhabiting business groups. 5. We also find that when a parent CSOE manager serves his or her political evaluation year or has received a lower rating in the last evaluation, the postprogram dividend reduction becomes greater, consistent with the argument that the program has induced expropriation of shareholders by parent CSOE managers to meet their political incentives. The research output received R&R at Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis.

17504117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17504117.value: In the future, we could extend the research by exploring the impact of the program on the innovation of the listed CSOEs. There is relevant little evidence in the literature about the determinants of corporate innovation among SOEs. Nevertheless, understanding how resource allocation within giant SOE groups affects their innovation (development and transaction) is critical for both managers and policymakers. To implement the research, we need to process patent information carefully within the groups and trace their ownership among different parties.

17504117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17504117.value: It is well understood that when firms receive favourable treatment from the government because of their political connections and not necessarily their economic merits, they may operate inefficiently while enjoying market advantages over their unconnected peers. However, just how firms respond to the sustained removal of their political connections has not been carefully studied. Our study evaluates an unanticipated reform in China that removed government-related personnel from independent directorships of publicly listed companies, and provides evidence on whether the weakening and removal of these connections encourages and enables firms to adapt and operate more competitively. Our research also examines SOEs’ payout policies by evaluating the impact of the State Capital Operation Program in China that imposes a significant and measurable shock on state controlling shareholders’ incentives.

17504217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17504217.value: The Post-earnings announcement drift (PEAD or drift) is a long-standing capital market anomaly that has been widely documented in the US and international markets for over 40 years. It refers to the phenomenon that stocks experiencing positive earnings surprises continue to earn positive excess returns for an extended period even after the announcements, while the opposite is true for stocks with negative earnings surprises. The PEAD presents a challenge to the efficient market hypothesis, which implies that, once earnings are announced, investors quickly process the news and trade on it, resulting in stock prices adjusting quickly to fully reflect the information contained in the news, and as a result, no post-announcement drift should be expected. Despite many attempts to understand the phenomenon, researchers have not yet agreed on the cause of PEAD, and whether the continuous price drift after announcements is compensation for risk or rather represents market inefficiency. We intend to contribute to the literature by showing a direct channel in which information uncertainty combined with limited investor attention can explain a significant portion of the PEAD. In particular, we show strong empirical evidence that a firm’s PEAD decreases when its customers or suppliers announce earnings prior to its own announcement. In other words, the interconnectedness of firms provides a rich source of information and helps to reduce mispricing in asset markets. Our project is made possible by a novel dataset of supply chain relationship, which, compared to the commonly used Compustat Segment data, has much wider coverage and unambiguous firm identifications. By pinning down a particular channel, our research helps to further our understanding of the important and long-standing PEAD anomaly. 盈利公告后的漂移现象(PEAD)是资本市场研究中最重要的市场异象之一。研究表明该现象已经在美国和其他国家存在超过40年啦。盈利公告后的漂移现象针对市场对会计盈余信息的反应：如果实际盈利超出预期，股票价格在盈利公布后持续上涨；相反如果实际盈利低于预期，股票价格在盈利公布后持续下跌。也就是说，市场对盈余信息的反应将会在盈余公告发布之后持续一段时间，这与有效市场假说相悖。有效市场假说则认为，盈利信息一旦公布，投资者迅速作出反应并交易，股票价格迅速调整，新的价格充分反应了盈余信息，从而不会出现盈利公告后的漂移现象。 尽管PEAD存在良久，学术界仍然不确定PEAD存在的原因。现有的学术研究提供了两种解释。一种可能性是PEAD是对风险的补偿，另一种解释是无效市场。本研究目的在于提供另外一个解释：信息不确定性和有限的投资者的关注结合在一起可以解释相当一部分的PEAD。具体来说，如果一个公司的供应商或者客户在该公司公布盈利信息之前发布盈利信息，该公司的PEAD会减低。换句话说，企业之间的业务上的联系提供了丰富的信息来源，额外的信息有助于减少资产市场的错误定价。我们的研究将基于一个新的供应链数据库。与PEAD研究通用的Compustat Segment数据库相比，该新数据库不仅包括更多的公司和数据信息，更重要的是，含有更精确的公司信息，可以更精确的和其他数据库联系在一起，从而能够进行更详细的分析。通过提出新的一种新的解释，我们的研究能够然增进大家对盈利公告后的漂移现象(PEAD)，资本市场研究中最重要的市场异象之一的理解。

17504417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17504417.value: Governments around the world have generally resorted to promoting market competition for healthcare provision as a way of ensuring cost-effective provision of quality healthcare. However, the available studies have uncovered mixed findings about the impact of competition on quality of hospital service. One possible reason for the mixed findings is that patients have asymmetric information about the quality of hospital service, which may impact on the use of quality improvement as hospitals’ response to competition. Moreover, in dealing with competition, hospitals may have responses other than quality improvement. Here we propose to fill in the gaps in the literature by investigating possibly heterogeneous responses of hospitals to competition using a data set of Chinese hospitals where information asymmetry about the quality of hospital service is partially alleviated by the government’s grade certification of hospitals. The proposed study departs from the literature on two fronts. First we construct a refined competition measure that is grade-specific, physical distance weighted, medical specialties adjusted, and size controlled. This refined competition measure can more precisely capture the intensity of competition across hospitals. Second we look at a whole range of possible responses hospitals might have when dealing with competition, such as quality of service (emergency room mortality and nurse to bed ratio), operational efficiency (average length of stay, bed occupancy staffing rate, and expenditure per patient for hospitals), user charges and markup of medicine, and service mix (the number of specialties and degree of specialization). To address the potential endogeneity problem of the competition measure when estimating the impact of competition, we will take advantage of two government policy shocks in 2009, which suddenly opened the gate for existing hospitals to upgrade and encouraged new ones to enter. Based on the refined competition measure and a battery of hospital performance measures, we will investigate if hospitals respond to competition heterogeneously and what determines their heterogeneous responses. We will highlight the role of quality certification, as a way of alleviating information asymmetry and regulating competition, in determining how hospitals respond heterogeneously to competition. We expect to find that the grade certification system of China makes competition more impactful on one hand and restricts how hospitals respond to competition on the other hand. This project will provide a fuller and more nuanced picture of how hospitals respond to competition differently, and will generate policy implications regarding cost-effective provision of quality healthcare. 各国政府尝试鼓励市场竞争来保证低成本有效的医疗服务。遗憾的是现有的研究却没有发现市场竞争对医疗服务质量的明确影响。一个可能的原因是病人并不知道医疗服务的质量；在这种情况下医院自然是不会因市场竞争加剧而提高医疗服务质量的。此外医院会采取其他方式应对市场竞争。中国政府通过医院评级消除病人对医疗服务质量的信息不对称。本研究项目应用中国医院数据分析在信息对称情况下医院应对竞争的多种策略。 本研究具体有两方面创新。一是我们构造一个更准确的医院市场竞争指数，二是我们构造医院多种应对竞争的策略。此外我们利用2009年中国政府政策的变化来解决医院市场竞争的内生性问题。我们会着重关注医院评级制度如何影响医院应对竞争的策略；评级制度会使竞争压力加剧，同时也会限制医院应对竞争的策略选择。本研究项目的研究成果会带来一些政策的建议。

17504417.label: Realisation of objectives
17504417.value: We have achieved all the objectives as per original application. 5.3.1 Competition measures We have constructed a set of competition measures that alleviate the degree of information asymmetry about the quality of hospital care and better capture changes in the market structure. Given the hospital grading system in China, we expect that the competition a hospital faces mostly come from hospitals of the same grade as the concerned hospital. Hence, we refine the competition measure used in Bloom et al. (2015) by differentiating within-grade and cross-grade competition. Specifically, we focus on within-grade competition as measured by the number of other hospitals of the same grade in the city, while we control for the potential cross-grade competition. We make three further adjustments to refine the measures of competition. First, we consider the role of physical distance in measuring competition. Hospital competition has a strong geographical element. Hence, following Forder and Allan (2014), we construct distance-weighted competition measures using the inverse of the distances between the hospital concerned and its competing hospitals as weights. Second, we adjust the competition measure using the specialty similarity defined as the Manhattan distance between the hospital concerned and its competitors as weights. Finally, we adjust the competition measures by the relative sizes between the hospital concerned and its competitors. 5.3.2 Responses to competition We have developed a full range of possible responses of hospitals to competition. Quality. We use two variables to measure hospital quality: the ED mortality rate and the nurse-to-bed staffing ratio. The ED mortality rate is defined as the death rate for all causes following admissions in the emergency department each year, like Bloom et al. (2015). The nurse-to-bed staffing ratio is defined as the number of registered nurses divided by the number of beds in a hospital each year, following Tay (2003) and Lin (2015). Prices. Following a similar idea of Dafny (2009) and Dafny et al. (2016), we use (logarithm) the ratio of a hospital's total patient revenue to its total number of patients in a given year to measure the average price the hospital charges. This price is the overall charge by a hospital for all the services and drugs it provides to an average patient, and it obviously influences patients’ choice of hospital. We similarly define two related price measures, focusing on outpatients and inpatients separately. Outpatient price (OP price) is defined as the total outpatient revenue divided by the total number of outpatients, in logarithm, and inpatient price (IP price) is defined as the total inpatient revenue divided by the total number of inpatients, in logarithm. Operational efficiency. If hospitals respond to competition by improving the quality of hospital care or lowering prices, one expects them to make related changes in their operations. Hence, we further examine the impact of competition on hospital operational efficiency using a series of measures of hospital operations that are associated with quality and price responses. The first operational efficiency measure, following Gaynor et al. (2013), is hospital operating expenditure per patient (average cost). The second is the bed occupancy rate, defined as the ratio of the total number of inpatient days to the total number of available bed days each year. Third, we measure the scope of hospital service or service mix using the number of specialty departments for which a hospital offers inpatient and outpatient services (number of departments). 5.3.3 Endogenous market structure and heterogeneous responses of hospitals We use a simulated instrumental variable (SIV) approach (e.g. Gruber and Saez, 2002; Dahl and Lochner, 2012) to address the endogeneity of market structure, employing the impacts of two government policy shocks in 2009. The policy changes were initiated by the central government as a national campaign, and therefore it is reasonable to have confidence in exogeneity of the policy shocks to the sample city. The policy shocks suddenly opened the gate for existing hospitals to upgrade to a higher level and encouraged private capital to establish new, mostly Grade 1 hospitals. They not only dramatically increased the total number of hospitals, but also changed the distribution of hospitals across grades and geographic areas. The impacts of the policy shocks were heterogeneous on hospitals of different grades in different locations, although all hospitals were exposed to the same shocks. Specifically, by taking advantage of the policy shocks, we simulate the market structure of the hospital industry by predicting individual hospitals' decisions on de novo entry, outright exit, and grade changes based on the policy shocks, localized market condition, and the lagged state variables at the hospital level. Then we calculate the simulated competition measures from the predicted market structure as the IVs for the actual competition measures and estimate the model using two-stage least squares (2SLS). Compared with the conventional IV approach, the SIV approach has two advantages in our application. First, it recognizes that the impact of the policy shocks on the competition measures may be nonlinear by affecting decisions of existing hospitals on grade changes (upgrading and downgrading) and outright exit, and decisions of new entrants. Hence, the approach constructs the IVs based on the predicted individual decisions of all (existing and potential) hospitals. Second, it recognizes that the five endogenous competition measures (within-grade and cross-grade) capture different facets of the same market structure and thus are closely related to each other. The solution to this interdependence is to predict the market structure and calculate the five simulated competition measures simultaneously based on the simulated market structure as the IVs for the five endogenous variables. Owing to the two advantages, in our context the simulated IVs are stronger than the linear-interaction IVs typically used in the conventional IV approach. 5.3.4 Factors determining hospitals’ heterogeneous response and policy implications We find that it is hospital grading that determines hospitals’ heterogeneous responses to competition. Competition drives hospitals to improve quality when such quality improvement can be revealed to patients in the future. Grade 1 hospitals and Grade 2 hospitals improve quality when facing competition, because they have the chance to reveal their quality improvement to patients through future upgrading. Grade 3 hospitals do not improve quality, because they are already at the top grade and have no means to reveal their quality improvement through further upgrading. However, Grade 3 hospitals reduce prices in response to competition to stay competitive. Our findings highlight the importance of comprehensive and discriminative quality certification in ensuring what we desire to have from competition. It is natural that if patients cannot recognize the quality improvement through quality certification, hospitals would have no incentive to do so when facing competition. More importantly, this study reaffirms our belief in market competition, by showing that competition makes hospitals of the highest grade reduce prices while pushing lower-grade hospitals to improve quality and maintain their prices, leading to higher consumer welfare through different channels. Government may initiate pro-competition policy and at the same time improve/adjust quality certification to provide cost-effective quality healthcare. If patients demand ever higher quality of hospital care, more transparent and discriminative quality certification might be needed; if increasing medical expenditure puts too much pressure on the fiscal budget, a less discriminative quality certification might be more desirable.

17504417.label: Major findings and research outcome
17504417.value: We find that competition drives hospitals to improve quality when such quality improvement can be revealed to patients in the future. When facing intensified competition, Grade 1 hospitals and Grade 2 hospitals reduce the ED mortality rate and increase the nurse-to-bed staffing ratio, because they have the chance to reveal their quality improvement through future upgrading. However, Grade 3 hospitals neither reduce the ED mortality rate nor increase the nurse-to-bed staffing ratio, presumably because they are already at the top grade and have no means to reveal their quality improvement through further upgrading. Rising costs due to quality improvement and increased competition pressure could push hospitals to adjust prices to a higher or lower level. We find that when facing competition, Grade 3 hospitals reduce prices to attract patients, because the hospitals have no incentive to improve quality as the top-grade providers and must resort to price reduction to remain competitive. However, Grade 1 and Grade 2 hospitals have no statistically significant changes in their price levels in response to competition, although they do improve quality. The reason is that it takes time for them to be upgraded to signal their quality improvement, but patients can immediately observe price changes. To offset the increased costs due to quality enhancement or decreased revenue due to price reduction, hospitals are further found to improve operational efficiency when facing competition. Grade 3 hospitals reduce their operating expenditure per patient (average cost). Given that Grade 1 and 2 hospitals increases quality when facing competition, their insignificant changes in average costs implies improvement in operations too. The efficiency improvement may be achieved by reallocating resources across different specialty departments or improving the bed occupancy rate. Grade 2 and Grade 3 hospitals, with considerably more specialty departments to begin with, cut the number of departments, presumably to achieve specialization; whereas Grade 1 hospitals, with much fewer specialty departments to begin with, do not change the number of departments significantly. All hospitals generally increase bed occupancy rates to improve efficiency.

17504417.value: Using a data set of hospitals which are graded based on a comprehensive matrix, this study analyzes the effects of competition on hospital quality, price, and operational efficiency. The study finds that hospitals improve quality in response to competition when such improvement could be revealed to patients through future upgrading. The top-grade hospitals, in contrast, reduce prices in response to competition. All hospitals improve operational efficiency. The study emphasizes the role of informational asymmetry between hospitals and patients and explains the puzzle of the mixed findings in the literature on the impact of competition on hospital quality.

17600117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17600117.value: We propose to investigate the rich case marking and its striking variation in Bumthang, an endangered language spoken by ~20,000 people in north-central Bhutan. Case marking is often thought to exist only to indicate structural relations, such as with “I” (subject) and “me” (object) in English. However, in languages with a range of case markers, there is often case variability: cases may be omitted, or a non-canonical case marker may be used to mark structural relations. Such variability is often treated as a grammatical “quirk,” but more recent work suggests that there are often underlying rules governing the apparent quirkiness in case variation, dictating what each case may mark, the specific contexts in which cases occur, and what variation is permitted. The proposed project will focus on the case marker that is typically used to indicate the subject (of a verb that has an object): the ergative case. In previous work, we investigated the use of the ergative in a range of contexts, unearthing an astounding set of non-structural factors involved in its licensing, including whether the subject is focused, verb type and “mood,” even the properties of the subject (e.g. singular/plural). Some of these factors are known to influence case marking options in other languages, but no language to date has been described as relying on all of them. We thus propose to examine the full set of contexts in which they occur in Bumthang and to test the results in a searchable corpus of the transcribed recordings of natural discourse. We also plan to investigate the range of case marking variation across the four Bumthang dialects, using language tasks that enable comparable data to be obtained, as such microvariation is often revealing of linguistic constraints. We will seek to establish the precise conditions in which the ergative case marker is used in Bumthang, as well as to establish the dialectal variation, and in so doing establish the desiderata for a theory of case. We will explore the complex interaction of meaning and structure, with pragmatics and discourse, in the use of case marking. The results will pave the way for new insights for case theory and for a typology of case. Our data will be obtained in the field, and we will ensure that all recordings are of archival quality. An annotated corpus will be deposited in a public archive as a necessary first step to documenting this endangered language. 我們計畫研究布姆唐語豐富的格標記系統，及其氣象萬千的變化。布姆唐語是不丹中北部的瀕危語種，使用人數約二十萬[，多變的格標記系統是其語法特點之一]。傳統認為格標記的作用僅限於標示結構關係，如英語的「I」（主語）和「me」 （賓語）。然而，格標記種類繁多的語言，頻頻出現微妙的格變異：部分格標記可以省略，格標記也可以附著在與其典型功能不吻合的句子成分上。這種特徵一直被視為異常語法現象，可是近年研究發現，這些看似「異常」的變化往往源自隱藏著的語法規則，這些規則決定每種格標記附著在哪種句子成分、出現在何種上文下理之間和怎樣變異。 擬定的研究項目將集中探討布姆唐語的作格標記。作格一般標示帶賓動詞的主語，我們過往的研究曾探討它在不同語境中的作用，發現作格的出現受一系列因素影響，包括主語是否話語焦點、動詞的類型和「語氣」、甚至主語的特徵（如單眾數）等。其他語言的格標記偶爾也會受到當中一兩項影響，但迄今未有發現其他格標記系統同時受制於這幾種因素。因此，我們計劃研究布姆唐語的作格標記可在哪些上下文之間出現，並利用自然話語的逐字稿，建立一個可搜索的語料庫，以測試研究結果。我們也計畫查考布姆唐語的四種方言之間，作格標記運用有何區別，因為這類微變異往往有助揭曉語法的規範。 我們會嘗試判斷布姆唐語作格標記在哪些特定的情況下出現，探討這些情況在不同方言之間有何異同，從而確立格理論需要具備的條件。我們會透過格標記的運用，探索意思、結構、語用和話語之間錯綜複雜的互動。這些結果會為格理論和格類型學的新見解鋪路。我們會從田野中蒐集數據，並確保錄音檔達到檔案存放質素標準。所得的標註語料庫將會存放在公共檔案中，作為記錄這個瀕危語言的第一步。

17600117.label: Realisation of objectives
17600117.value: SUMMARY ‘Understanding Case in Bumthang’ aimed to explore key issues in an aspect of the grammar of an endangered Himalayan language. To investigate the ‘ergative case’, an innovative approach was taken, bringing experimental methods to the field to ensure suitable controls were adhered to, making the data maximally comparable between speakers, and allowing us to explore very subtle, nuanced contexts. Contra the standard assumption that case is a purely grammatical phenomenon, we found that case in Bumthang (and likely related Himalayan languages), primarily determined by semantic and information structural factors. This is a key finding not only contributing to our working typology of case, but also forcing syntactic theoreticians to find a way to accommodate these data in their models. The results were presented at seven international conferences and published in two journal articles. There are many further directions for future research that have emerged from this project and are being pursued. In addition to the theoretical and typological impact of the key results, the project also contributed to ongoing documentary efforts for this language and its community. The data collection involved recordings of interviews, stories, songs, and conversations from all Bumthang dialects, now archived in publicly accessible repositories. A website was also made to showcase the language, the work being undertaken and give easy access to the data in the archives. THE PROJECT OUTCOMES This project aimed to investigate issues of case marking in Bumthang, an endangered language spoken by ~20,000 people in north-central Bhutan. In particular, the project’s focus was on the subject case marker, the ‘ergative case’ and its variable usage. The use of the ergative case is notoriously elusive in languages of the region, perhaps because it has not been the focus of previous research. The primary goal of this project was to reveal the precise nature of the ergative case in Bumthang. We decided that a fruitful novel approach would be to develop a comprehensive set of language tasks (Objective 3) that would help facilitate the comparison of these complex case data, exploring different contexts and environments. In addition to a thorough study of the ergative case in Ura dialect of Bumthang (Objective 1), we also wanted to address a critical need to document this endangered language, so to facilitate this, we employed an approach that would support the documentary efforts for Bumthang. We ensured that we recorded a range of genres from different speakers (Objective 2), of archival quality, and from all the Bumthang dialects in our study (Objective 4). Our project goals were broken down into six main objectives, all of which were met. The PI carried out two successful field trips to Bhutan. The first focused on the Ura dialect, while the second carried out a valley-wide survey of all four dialects. In addition to interviews, recordings were made of conversations, stories, and songs (Objectives 2 and 6). A specific set of language tasks were created and administered survey-style on a tablet in the field, which not only collated the results well, but also generated interest in participating and ensured adequate controls were in place while investigating nuanced contexts. The ergative case, by definition, is the case marker used to indicate the subject of a transitive verb, a verb with an object (e.g. ‘He’ in ‘he hit the dog’ but not in ‘he ran’). However, the features defining the contexts in which the ergative is required were found to be mostly not syntactic, but pragmatic or semantic instead, drawing, for example, on notions such as agentivity, or the perfectivity of the verb, or whether the argument is in focus. Given the nature of these factors, we extended our study to examine similar conditions for arguments of intransitive verbs (e.g. ‘he’ in ‘he ran’), not a licensed context for arguments to receive ergative case if structural conditions were uniquely determining case, but which is naturally subject to the same factors. We found that there are indeed some contexts in which the sole argument of an intransitive verb can bear ergative case, relying on some of the same features to those relevant for transitive verbs. The results included a precise formulation of when an argument will receive ergative case in both transitive and intransitive clauses. This use of the ergative case confirms clearly indicate that extra-grammatical factors must be taken into account to arrive at a predictive account of case licensing, thus challenging approaches that require case marking to be assigned (usually by default) in the syntactic component of the grammar. These results, together with a discussion of possible reasons for the differences between transitive/intransitive verbs, was published in Himalayan Linguistics, a University of California journal and a main outlet for work in this area. We also found interesting tangential issues during the project, namely aspects of valency changing, and morphosyntactic restrictions on Negation in Bumthang. The study on negation was also published in Himalayan Linguistics. Finally, the interviews with speakers from across Bumthang in the second fieldtrip explored issues of linguistic vitality and language maintenance as well as case marking and documenting different genres. This has resonated well with work being carried out in a separate project on another Himalayan language, Nubri, and there is a paper in preparation which will report on these sociolinguistic issues. This will be submitted to a journal and acknowledge the GRF grant that made it possible. In addition to the two journal articles, results and issues arising from our project were presented in the form of seven different conference presentations, addressing the incorporation of language tasks in the field, the results of our investigation of the ergative case: for Bumthang as well as theoretical and typological implications, and other related issues (including valency changing, language vitality). DOCUMENTARY EFFORTS As noted, the PI carried out two field trips to Bhutan, made possible by the teaching relief. The first trip focused on Ura dialect, while the second trip involved visiting all four villages in Bumthang. We were fortunately able to recruit three outside contractors to help with data processing and checking translations. The recordings of the Ura dialect from the first fieldtrip are archived in PARADISEC Collection ID KJZ3: Bumthang Materials https://www.paradisec.org.au. Data from the second fieldtrip are currently in the final stages of posting to the archive at the Tibetan and Himalayan Library, hosted by the University of Virginia https://av.mandala.library.virginia.edu/collection/tibetan-and-himalayan-library. All archived recordings acknowledge the generous support of the RGC and are publicly accessible. Finally, a website was created to assemble information about the Bumthang, the language, our linguistic work and easy links to the archives. This is currently hosted at https://www.linguistics.hku.hk/bumthang SETBACKS Unfortunately, the Co-I experienced a number of personal setbacks at the start of the project which delayed the start of the work. Ultimately Co-I was unable to travel, but the PI was able to successfully undertake the fieldwork alone. While this meant significant savings in funding that could be returned to the RGC, it did also mean that the project took a little longer to complete than originally anticipated.

17600117.label: Major findings and research outcome
17600117.value: Results of the study were presented at seven international conferences, covering not only the ergative case and our findings, but also its impact for typology, for work on related languages, and theoretical impact, as well as the methodological innovations, issues of linguistic vitality. Two major studies were published in Himalayan Linguistics, a major journal in this field. The major result of this project is that we have shown that in Bumthang the ergative case marker, thought to be a purely structural marker of a transitive subject, is instead sensitive to pragmatic, semantic and information structural features of the clause and the argument. This changes dramatically how we must conceptualize case. Initially driven by the fact that optionality of the ergative case marker in other Himalayan languages had been reportedly impossible to pin down, this study contributes greatly to the understanding of related phenomena in the region, and thus our understanding of how case marking works and its role in the grammar, growing our understanding of case typology significantly. The results also create significant challenges for theoretical models of case that rely on strict notions of structural case assignment. Many contemporary frameworks hold the assumption that case is a default morphological manifestation of a structural relation. However, now we have shown that case marking may be non-structurally determined, it is necessary to develop specific ways in which these data can be incorporated into current theoretical models of case. We have made a significant contribution to the documentation of Bumthang through the deposit of high-fidelity recordings in publicly accessible archives (PARADISEC, Collection ID KJZ3; Tibetan and Himalayan Library, Collection ID forthcoming), which incorporates a range of genres and a range of speakers, and representative samples from each dialect. We have also made a webpage collating linguistic and general materials about Bumthang to help generate community interest in the language and public interest in the work we are doing. Copies of the resulting publications and conference abstracts are available at the HKU institutional repository and other publicly accessible locations.

17600117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17600117.value: The results of this project are multifold and contribute to several aspects of linguistics. As such there is great potential for developing the work undertaken here beyond the listed outcomes. Having shown case to be much more complex than typically assumed, the PI is now investigating aspects of non-canonical case in another Himalayan Language, Nubri, to further contribute to case typology and theory. The second fieldtrip involving interviews with villagers from across the Bumthang district revealed certain issues of linguistic vitality and language endangerment not previously though to exist. PI has presented on this topic and is drafting a paper to report on this. Indeed, these echo findings emerging in the PI’s Nubri project Drawing on the insights being developed in the Nubri work I plan to continue to explore similar issues in Bumthang, involving broader-scale surveys and data from the contact languages, while simultaneously evaluating and assessing the impact that this interference has on language vitality. With the linguistic vitality of Bumthang decreasing, further work on the documentation is necessary. In addition to adding to the growing repository of quality recordings, I hope to work with the community to develop ways we can contribute to language maintenance.

17600117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17600117.value: This project investigated the case marking and its variation in Bumthang, an endangered language spoken by ~20,000 people in north-central Bhutan. Case marking is when there is a change in form to indicate structural relations such as “I” (subject) and “me” (object) in English. However, in many languages with rich case marking, cases may often be ‘optional’, but with little understanding of what governs this optionality. We focused on the ergative case marker, typically used to indicate the subject (of a verb with an object), exploring the extent to which we may delineate the contexts in which it occurs. We found that its use is complex and determined by primarily non-structural aspects, including the meaning of the verb, of the subject, or even whether the subject is focused in the sentence. The results contribute to our understanding of case marking, contributing to typology, but also challenge key assumptions in current theoretical approaches by showing that case is much more than a default structural marker and that non-strutural information must be incorporated into frameworks to properly model its use. The publicly available recordings contribute to the documentation of (all dialects of) this endangered language drawing on a range of speech genres.

17600417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17600417.value: There is a rich corpus of literature on how Asian courts have participated in and even reshaped human rights discourse in their respective jurisdictions. However, little academic literature has examined how Asian courts have responded to deficiencies in electoral processes and the problem of partisan self-dealing. Partisan self-dealing occurs when political actors devise electoral rules designed to entrench themselves in power. This project's purpose is to carry out the first holistic and comprehensive study of how Asian courts have addressed and should address this challenge to democratic governance. In this project, I shall investigate and examine nine Asian jurisdictions, i.e. Bangladesh, Hong Kong, India, Malaysia, Pakistan, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, and Thailand. These jurisdictions represent three types of democracies, i.e. dominant-party democracies, dynamic democracies, and fragile democracies. Hong Kong, Malaysia and Singapore are what I term “dominant-party democracies” – democracies where a dominant political party or coalition has remained in power since independence/decolonization. India, South Korea, and Taiwan are what I term “dynamic democracies” – democracies where there have been extended periods of competing political parties taking turns in office. Thailand, Pakistan, and Bangladesh are what I term “fragile democracies” – democracies where the armed forces are not under firm control of the civilian government and the country oscillates regularly between military and civilian rule. This project's purpose is to explore how the type of democracy the courts operate within affect the courts' ability to address deficiencies in electoral processes. My hypothesis is that Asian courts have greater policy space when divided government exists, as opposing parties in the legislature have to cooperate to effectuate disagreements with the judiciary. In dominant-party or fragile democracies, courts can only take limited action before they outrun the government’s “zone of tolerance” as the government or army can respond to confrontational judicial decisions by deploying constitutional or unconstitutional means to overrule or “punish” the courts. My research findings will result in one academic monograph and one academically refereed article. The findings will also provide courts, policy-makers, and scholars with insight on the role that courts can shape a jurisdiction’s democratic development. 這項研究將探討亞洲不同地區的民主體系如何影響該地法院解決選舉「民主缺陷」的能力。 於這個項目，我將查證和剖析九個亞洲區域，即孟加拉國，香港，印度，馬來西亞，巴基斯坦，新加坡，南韓，台灣和泰國。這些區域代表三類民主政體，即一黨主導民主政體，活躍民主政體和脆弱民主政體。 香港，馬來西亞和新加坡是我所指的「一黨主導民主政體」—自獨立/解除殖民後由一黨或聯盟一直掌權的民主政體。 印度，南韓和台灣是我所指的「活躍民主政體」—不同政黨長期競爭及輪流上任的民主政體。 泰國、巴基斯坦和孟加拉國是我所指的「脆弱民主政體」—武裝力量不完全受平民政府控制，和國家時而由軍人政府掌權的民主政體。

17600417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17600417.value: This project has demonstrated convincingly how there is a symbiotic relationship between the strength of a jurisdiction's democracy and the power of its courts. In ‘dominant-party’ democracies, (e.g., Singapore, Malaysia, and Hong Kong), courts play a more limited role in shaping their political environments. In ‘dynamic’ democracies (e.g India, South Korea, and Taiwan), the courts can improve the political system . In ‘fragile’ democracies, (e.g., Thailand, Pakistan, and Bangladesh), activist judges can precipitate a hostile takeover by the armed forces that lead to the demise of the rule of law, the countries are better served if the judges seek to defend the court's institutional autonomy. At the same time, this Project also systematically explains why Hong Kong, Taiwan, and South Korea have the only courts in Asia that regularly use a structured four-stage Proportionality Analysis to invalidate laws, and routinely apply innovative constitutional remedies such as Suspension Orders and Remedial Interpretation to rectify constitutionally flawed legislation. This project explains this constitutional convergence in East Asia by investigating the political context impacting judicial behaviour.

17600817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17600817.value: Participating throughout the 1950s and early 60s in the reknitting of a global economic tapestry that had frazzled during the first half of the century, the Soviet Union wove itself irrevocably into European economic life through a series of gas-for-pipes and oil-for-pipes deals in the second half of the 1960s. The 1970s saw Soviet energy resources course through the world economy even as finance was extricated from the straightjacket of a Bretton Woods system that transformed itself in 1971. For the Soviet Union this meant a shift from a trading regime that relied on finance-facilitated barter (oil for pipes, timber for turnkey projects, etc.), to one that increasingly relied on the Western financing of Soviet debt based on the vast potential of the Soviet Union’s newly discovered and seemingly inexhaustible energy resources. This project will examine the last two decades of what has been called the Soviet experiment, a period that has only very recently become the subject of historical research. It will examine the political consequences to the Soviet Union of the shift from the relative egalitarianism of barter exchange with the West to the hierarchy implicit in a debt relation with the West. It will combine my previous work into the imbrication of Soviet politics with the world economy and the recent literature on the global transformations of the 1970s to improve our understanding of Soviet and global history of the 1970s and 80s, and the world those seminal decades created for us. It is both a study of the Soviet Union’s last two decades as well as a study of the development of global capitalism toward its current financialized form. The study of Soviet interaction with global capitalism will provide a unique angle from which to study the details and periodization of the world’s structural, ideational and political changes during the last quarter of the 20th century. 苏联在20世纪60年代后期，通过一系列天然气、石油换管道的交易不可逆转地将自己融入欧洲的经济生活中，从而也加入到整个五十年代和六十年代初期，对那个世纪上半叶极不景气的全球经济进行重组的过程中。 20世纪70年代，即使金融从经过1971年演变的Bretton Woods 系統中脱离出來，苏联能源资源还是遍及世界经济。对于苏联来讲，这意味着从一个依靠金融助力的物物交易（用石油换取管道工程、用木材换取交钥匙工程等）的贸易政权转型到西方对苏联债务的更多资助，这是基于苏联新发现的、取之不尽的能源资源的巨大潜力。这个项目将分析过去二十年所谓的苏联实验，这个时期只是最近才成为历史学研究的课题。研究将具体分析苏联从与西方的物物交易和这种贸易形式所带来的相对平均主义转移到与西方后来产生的债务关系及隐含的等级制度所带来的政治后果。此课题将把我以前关于苏联政治与世界经济的融合以及最近真对20世纪70年代全球转型的文献相結合，从而提高我们对20世纪70年代和80年代苏联及全球历史的了解，同时对这些年代所塑造的世界有更多的了解。这个课题既是对苏联过去二十年的研究，也是对全球资本主义如何发展到今天的状态的研究。关于苏联与世界资本主义的互动的研究将给予我们一个独特的角度，透过这个角度我们可以更加深入的探索20世纪最后一个四分之一的世界结构，思想和政治变化的细节和周期。

17601317.label: Realisation of objectives
17601317.value: I have achieved all five of the objectives that I set and stated in my original proposal. I will explanation how I have done so in the paragraphs below, along with some qualifying remarks for objectives 2 and 5. Objective 1: During the full duration of the project, I collected sources from a variety of repositories and through my professional network, reviewed them to determine what evidence would be pertinent to my dataset, and identified the relevant evidence for input. I encountered some obstacles beyond my control during the second half of 2019 and throughout 2020 (COVID-19 pandemic and collaborations with partner institutions in mainland China that were affected by political conditions in Hong Kong) which prevented me from conducting the fieldwork and consultations that I had developed. However, I made up for those suspended opportunities by pursuing alternative ways to gather sources and to solicit feedback from fellow experts. Objective 2: As of this final report, the dataset resulting from this research is now available to the public through a website. As such, I have fulfilled the self-determined criterion of making my data searchable and accessible throughout the world. As for the print version, I decided that users of the website may choose to print out their search results. However, because the database will be continuously updated and enriched with more content, it would not be optimal to publish a print version which would only represent the content in the database as of the printing time. Nevertheless, since the database exists in spreadsheet form (which is printable) and can be printed by users, I consider the objective of organizing the data in both digital and print versions to be complete. Objective 3: I have studied the data that I have gathered to scrutinize and refine my own conceptions of "Chinese," "non-Chinese," "native," and "borrowed" names in the context of Northeast China during the period covered in the dataset (converted into the online database). Such analysis has led to the production of two papers, which are described in the Research Outcome section of this report. Objective 4: I have consulted with colleagues in my major fields of study as I have developed the dataset in order to make my findings relevant and useful to them. I have received feedback that my dataset will be an important resource for both general users, who will use it as a reference tool, and for specialists to perform further analysis of the content. Objective 5: As of this final report, the postgraduate student is continuing her studies and making solid progress towards the completion of a doctoral dissertation in China Studies using data curation. I consider this objective to be completion because the student has developed the expected aptitudes in both China Studies (concentrating on history) and data curation.

17601317.label: Major findings and research outcome
17601317.value: 1) This project has generated evidence to substantiate the evolving understanding of Northeast China as an integral part of Northeast Asia during the early modern period of history. Data about names that are similar or identical for individuals identified as belonging to discrete social and cultural groups suggest that contact between these groups shaped components of a shared culture that was as important as the features that distinguish them from one another. This data is valuable because many of the groups studied in the project have highly incomplete historical narratives. Although names constitute a limited segment of historical evidence, they nevertheless shed light on how self-identification and identification by others were influenced by cross-cultural communication and knowledge-sharing. 2) This project engenders deeper links between ethnic classification and ethnic belonging in the modern and contemporary periods of China’s history. Since ethnic classification became a legal and political mechanism in the 1950s, retroactive applications of such criteria have proven to be misrepresentative of how the groups subject to such identification describe their own ancient and premodern histories. In the absence of extensive historical records about many groups in the region now known as Northeast China, names are crucial “fragments of the past” that give some clues about these groups’ own interpretations of how they were similar or different from others. As conceptions and expressions of ethnic belonging (or ethnic consciousness) continue to develop and change in contemporary China, it is important for both current ethnic groups and for descendants of those that were not legally recognized in the ethnic classification process to understand how group and individual traits in the past were molded by cultural contact and exchange. 3) This project has greater implications for not only the history of Northeast China and Northeast Asia, but also the study of Chinese names. Names are significantly mutable, individualized components of identities, and for most of human history, were not recorded for all but a select group of individuals who were elite or privileged enough to be remembered. In the study of Chinese names, members of the Han ethnic group have been most represented. Non-Han people have been largely subject to limited study and thereby limited understanding of naming practices and traditions. The dataset created in this project demonstrates the diversity of names in a particular region and how what we consider as a “Chinese name” has been greatly enriched by many non-Han elements.

17601317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17601317.value: This project will make progress after the official grant period is over. A group of volunteer scholars will continue to input and edit data and to maintain the online database under the principal investigator (PI)’s supervision and leadership. The dataset will grow naturally as relevant sources are identified, and data is extracted from them. All contributors will be welcome to develop their own research projects and publications based on the data, either on an individual or collaborative basis. The pace of the dataset’s growth will depend on the amount of time that contributors can invest in the work. The PI considers the dataset to have infinite potential to expand, and will keep it on her research agenda for the duration of her career. Maintenance manuals for the dataset and database have been written so that new contributors may join the project and that current contributors may pass on their roles to others.

17601317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17601317.value: This project generated a dataset of names associated with individuals who were identified or could be identified as non-Han people in the region now known as Northeast China from the fourteenth century to the present. The project team selected names from a variety of sources related to the history and contemporary characteristics of Northeast China. The team then organized these names into a dataset that is searchable by multiple variables including gender, communal identity (tribe, ethnic group), and time period. The dataset is multilingual, with Chinese, Manchu, and English translation components. The completed content of the dataset will be available to users on an open online searchable database [www.regionalstudiesofchina.net] starting in April 2021. The dataset and the resulting publications from this project are significant because they show how social groups in Northeast China had different identities but shared cultural traits such as names. The common use of names by people who belonged to different groups shows how languages and cultures developed through contact. This research furthermore reveals the diversity of names in China, both in non-Chinese languages and as incorporated into the Chinese language through transcription by Chinese characters.
