17601917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17601917.value: 本研究項目的首要目標是透過研發一個基於「樂高認真玩®」而設計的有效干預之替代方案，從而改善現有的減壓干預計劃。為了達到這目標，我們的研究團隊將進行一個隨機對照試驗研究，去比較新研發的認真玩干預計劃（遊戲化研究狀況）相對於現有的認知行為干預計劃（傳統教授研究狀況）的學習機制和成果間之差異。本研究項目將會在香港和華南地區的私人機構招募多個真實工作小組，然後把這些小組隨機分配到其中一個研究狀況。我們將使用多種研究方法進行綜合成果評估，並採用縱向研究設計來測試在實際工作環境中應對靈活性和團隊工作有效度所作出的假設變化。我們還會使用半結構式訪談進行流程評估，旨在從用者角度揭示對動態干預流程的重要見解。

17601917.label: Realisation of objectives
17601917.value: In the present project, all five objectives have been completely achieved, and the details are described below: Our research team has designed and empirically evaluated a new gamification-based intervention, namely Serious Play Training (SPT). The SPT was constructed based on a conceptual model derived from our meta-analysis (see Output 1 in Part C). We assessed the efficacy of our new intervention using a randomized controlled trial, and the outcomes derived from our new intervention were compared with those derived from a widely adopted Cognitive-Behavioral Training (CBT) program (Objective 1). We delivered both intervention programs to work teams in various private organizations. A total of 250 Chinese working adults took part in our RCT study. After the participants had been recruited, we randomly assigned them to the SPT, CBT, and waitlist conditions. Adopting a multi-wave longitudinal design, the outcomes were assessed before and after the intervention at three time points (Objective 2). We adopted a multi-method strategy for a more comprehensive assessment of the outcomes (Objective 3). In addition to the self-report questionnaire methodology, we also employed other-report method and behavioral observation in real-life decision-making tasks. The results derived from our outcome evaluation study showed that only the group of participants who had taken part in the new SPT reported greater team effectiveness over time, and the results further indicated that this psychological improvement could be explained by an increase in group cohesion. In addition, the participants who had attended either the SPT or the existing CBT similarly displayed higher levels of coping flexibility over time, and such psychological improvement could be accounted for by an enhancement in discriminative thinking. In summary, all these findings provide empirical evidence that demonstrates the efficacy of adopting the gamification approach in corporate training for fostering team-building and coping ability to deal with stress. These findings are published in a refereed journal (see Output 2 in Part C). In addition to the quantitative RCT study, we also conducted a qualitative interview study with both the employee participants and their supervisors (Objective 4). The interview findings were analyzed using thematic analysis. The results showed that the participants were generally positive about their learning experiences. The theme analysis further identified four major themes that reflected the major changes mad by the participants after taking part in our newly developed SPT: bonding with colleagues, mutual understanding, cooperation, and team spirit. Upon completion of the entire project, we worked closely with the Personnel Office from the various organizations to share our best practices in corporate training regarding team building and stress management (Objective 5). Adopting a train-the-trainer approach, our team provided training to staff from the Personnel Department to empower their staff to run the in-house intervention programs.

17601917.label: Major findings and research outcome
17601917.value: Research output 1: Cheng, C.*, & Ebrahimi, O. V. (2023). A meta-analytic review of gamified interventions in mental health enhancement. Computers in Human Behavior, 141, 107621. https://doi.org/https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chb.2022.107621 In this article, our research team conducted a multilevel meta-analysis that evaluated the efficacy of gamified interventions in bolstering mental health. Overall, the meta-analytic findings provided empirical support for the beneficial role of using gamification in interventions for enhancing mental health. More importantly, such beneficial effects were found much larger for interventions targeting at bolstering mental wellness than those targeting at mitigating psychological symptoms. The results also showed sex differences in the extent of intervention effectiveness, and clarified that specific measures of mental health outcome should be used instead of general measures. Finally, the beneficial role of gamified interventions was demonstrated in not just clinical samples but also non-clinical ones. All these encouraging results have laid a solid foundation for the implementation of our newly developed gamified intervention in this GRF project, and our design and implementation were guided by the findings of this meta-analysis. Research output 2: Cheng, C.*, & Chau, C. (2022). Gamification-based intervention for enhancing team effectiveness and coping flexibility: Randomized controlled trial. Frontiers in Psychiatry, 13, 941252. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyt.2022.941252 The results derived from this outcome evaluation study showed that only the group of participants who had taken part in the Serious Play Training (SPT) reported greater team effectiveness over time, and the results further indicated that this psychological improvement could be explained by an increase in group cohesion. In addition, the participants who had attended either the SPT or the Cognitive-Behavioral Training (CBT) similarly displayed higher levels of coping flexibility over time, and such a psychological improvement could be explained by an increase in discriminative thinking. In summary, all these findings provide empirical evidence that demonstrates the efficacy of adopting the gamification approach in corporate training for fostering team-building and coping ability to deal with stress.

17602017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17602017.value: China’s educational heritage is rich. Yet, few people can articulate the relevance of Chinese classical educational values to today’s policy and reform. Since the West came to China with immense prestige in the 19th century, China’s educational traditions have never been packaged well in light of established and dominant Western knowledge and values. While it is agreed that contemporary views of education are heavily embedded in social and cultural roots, little is known about how Chinese educational traditions influence current policy and practice within China’s modern Western-style education system. This becomes increasingly inappropriate against a backdrop of a rising China. This project will seek to understand the most important lessons traditional Chinese educational thought and practice have for contemporary development. Through exploring how China’s educational heritage has been interpreted differently in the Chinese and Western literature, it attempts to identify and reevaluate the fundamental features of Chinese traditional education, and investigates how such traditions inform China’s contemporary educational development. The project is divided into two parts. The first reviews the literature on Chinese educational traditions in both Chinese and English. Unlike previous approaches that separate the multitudinous forces to which China is exposed and neglect their interactions, a new lens will be adopted to incorporate them and focus on their interplay to analyze the literature. It will revisit the Chinese educational traditions during their evolution in different historical periods, how Confucianism, Daoism and Buddhism have interacted in the sphere of education, and how Chinese educational traditions together have interplayed with their Western counterparts. The second stage is an empirically-based policy study, using semi-structured interviews with policymakers, researchers and practitioners as its main data collection approach. Data analysis will use the 5-step method developed by McCracken (1988). It will explore the implications of Chinese educational traditions for contemporary development in a context of great Western influences. It will probe into how educational thought in Chinese traditions has informed China’s current education policy and practice, in order to find possible ways in which traditional Chinese educational values can be effectively integrated with the dominant streams of Western educational influence within a Chinese framework. Positioned at the interface of Chinese and Western traditions in education, the PI is well equipped to tackle this project to identify and classify scholarly materials in both traditions. The project is expected to lead to new intellectual developments that both build on existing hybridizations and conceive new hybridizations of the two traditions. 中國教育歷史悠久，擁有豐富的遺產。然而，如今卻很少有人能夠清楚地說明中國教育傳統如何影響當前的教育政策和改革。自19世紀西方強勢進入中國以來，中西教育傳統就從未真正地實現融合，唯以西學為獨尊。可是，教育的發展是不可能脫離其歷史文化土壤的。對於本民族教育傳統如何影響當代的政策和實踐的無知極其不利於教育的改革和發展。在中華民族走向復興的當下更顯得不合時宜。此課題試圖厘清中國教育傳統對當代教育發展的意義何在。通過探討關於中國教育傳統在中西文獻中的各種詮釋，重新界定這些傳統的特點及其當代意義。 課題分為上下兩個部分。第一階段主要是中西文獻研究。與前人研究不同的是，此階段的工作將特別關注於綜合考察不同來源的對中國社會發展施以影響的力量，它們之間的相互關係，以及它們與西學的關係。從這種角度解讀文獻，包括不同歷史時期的教育傳統，儒道釋之間的同與異和相互影響，以及它們與西學的相互作用。第二部分是包括實地調查的經驗性研究。通過對教育政策制訂者、理論工作者和實踐人員的質性訪談，收集第一手資料，並使用McCracken的五步法對之加以分析，探索中國教育傳統在當前以西學為主流的形勢下對於當代教育實踐的意義，以及如何更好地發揚和利用這些傳統。 該研究的主持者長期置身于中西思想文化的交匯之處，因而尤其適宜于承擔這項研究任務。此研究將在中西思想文化傳統的交融方面作出顯著的理論貢獻，並具備突出的現實和實踐意義。

17602017.label: Major findings and research outcome
17602017.value: The project has sorted out how Chinese educational traditions have evolved in their complex contexts and varied transformations. It interrogates and re-conceptualizes some long-held perceptions of the evolution of major Chinese educational traditions. By so doing it fills the gap in the literature. It finds that although traditions have their enduring influence in the Chinese society, few people nowadays can articulate how the impact is actually exerted within the contemporary Western-style knowledge system. A series of publications in English and Chinese have been produced, with many are still on the pipeline. A number of keynote and plenary speeches that were entirely and/or greatly based on the project have been delivered in Chinese and English at international and national conferences and symposiums. Specifically, those as the direct results of the project include five chapters and/or entries in books, handbooks and encyclopedias; eleven journals articles in both English and Chinese; and eight invited keynote and/or plenary speeches delivered in English and Chinese. It is also important to note that the project has been able to contribute significantly to my scholarly thinking as I have been working on it. The impact is evidently expressed in my scholarly work. For instance, many of the findings have informed my latest book The Chinese Idea of a University: Phenix Reborn (Forthcoming in 2022, HKU Press). However, as the book is mainly a result of my previous GRF project and in consideration of its length, I will not list it as a direct outcome of this project. Similar situations are also found in my teaching and other academic activities. The point I want to make here is that the impact of the project goes much beyond the outcomes I have reported here.

17602017.value: The more I do research on the theme, the more I realize its theoretical and practical significance. Following the project, a natural second step is how to integrate Chinese and Western intellectual traditions in today's educational policymaking, research, and education, as well as how to educate people/students at various levels to obtain such important abilities. Therefore, as its continuity, another GRF application was submitted. Due to COVID influence, the research design proposed in the new application was required to be reconsidered. The application was not successful, with an overall score of 3.5. I am prepared to revise the proposal and re-submit the application.

17602017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17602017.value: China has long and rich educational traditions. Yet it is unclear how they have evolved over the time. This project finds different features of different historical periods. The first stage ranged from the pre-Qin period to the end of the Han dynasty and was featured by political orientation. The second period was from the Wei-Jin dynasties until the rise of Neo-Confucianism and focused much on seeking the nature of things. The third spanned from the Northern Song dynasty to the end of the Ming dynasty with a particular inward-looking attitude. The last phase is from the Ming-Qing transition to the present. It is featured greatly by practical concerns. Based on the empirical evidences, this project finds that China's educational heritage is much alive today. Although people have different understanding and interpretation of traditions, they agree with the enduring influence of traditions in contemporary educational reform and development, as well as the challenges and opportunities in carrying forward such traditions. After critically reviewing familiar approaches such as “taking the essence and discarding the dregs,” “Chinese essence and Western utility” and “the wholesale Westernization,” this study calls for combining Western and Chinese traditions in a highly globalized context of knowledge production and dissemination.

17602717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17602717.value: 過去三十年來亞洲國家的法律專業快速增長。由於律師在司法制度中發揮重要的作用，有關其價值取向的研究有助於評估有關國家司法質素及其法律制度。對法學生價值觀的研究有助於預測他們未來的行為及在法律實務中的倫理決定。在西方國家有關律師和法學生的價值研究已非常普遍，但在亞洲國家有關研究仍相當缺乏。 這項研究對中國、印度、泰國和菲律賓，其中四個增長最快的亞洲國家的法學生價值觀進行比較研究。這四個國家在國際貨幣基金組織的國際生產總值分別在亞太地區排行第二、第四、第十一及第十三位。但同時這四個國家在聯合國的性別不平等指數在2014年是世界排行第九十、第一百三十、第九十三及第一百一十五位。 本研究試圖回答五個問題。首先，在中國、印度、泰國和菲律賓法學生，哪些價值對他們行為和道德決策方面是重要的？第二，這四個亞洲國家的法學生有沒有共同的核心價值？第三，這四個亞洲國家的法學生在價值觀上有何差異？第四，這四個國家的法學生的價值觀是否存在性別差異？最後，這四個亞洲國家的法學生的價值取向有何異同？ 這些研究問題將通過對中國、印度、泰國和菲律賓的法學生進行問卷調查和半結構訪談來解答。本研究將建立在本計劃三位學者之前的四項研究基礎之上，包括澳洲、大中華地區、三個亞洲普通法司法管轄區和四個亞洲大陸法系國家。它將根據之前在澳洲進行研究中使用的調查問卷，對這四個亞洲國家的法學生專業價值觀進行分析。這項研究將西方世界律師和法學生價值取向的研究，推展至亞洲特別是這四個國家。這研究將有助法律專業道德和專業精神的教學，以及亞洲地區及全球法律學院的課程改革。

17602717.label: Major findings and research outcome
17602717.value: 1. Law students in the four fastest-growing Asian countries demonstrate strong personal values of family loyalty and family members’ well-being, especially those in India and China. 2. Law students in the four fastest-growing Asian countries show strong interest in participating in pro bono work, commonly driven by the value of ‘access to legal justice’. 3. Law students in the four fastest-growing Asian countries displayed different ethical values in decision-making process. The responses to the scenarios are similar to the trend of the Western counterparts but the motivating values of the responses are distinctive. 4. Law students in China and India developed work ethical values like ‘obedience to the law firm partner/supervisor’ and ‘loyalty to your firm’. 5. Students in India and the Philippines rated higher in personal values over professional values, such as ‘employment prospects’ and ‘commercial advantage’. 6. There is a common pattern of feminization in legal education in the four Asian countries. 7. Law schools in the four Asian countries should strengthen the ethical values of law students by developing their “personal conscience”, “ethics of duty” and “ethics of aspiration” to equip them to address ethical dilemmas in the future.

17602717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17602717.value: The research provides the foundation for further research on law students' personal and professional values in other fast growing economies other than China, India, Thailand, and the Philippines, such as Vietnam. It is also proposed to expand the research to law students in other parts of the world like Africa. On basis of the findings of this project, Dr Wu (PI) applied for another GRF grant to study the ethical values of law students in four emerging and transitional economies (China, Russia, South Africa, and Kazakhstan). He was awarded a sum of HK$918,160 (Project No. 17601018) in 2018.

17602717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17602717.value: This research is a study on the ethical values of the four fastest-growing Asian countries: China, India, Thailand, and the Philippines. It found that law students in the four fastest-growing countries focussed more on personal values than professional values in their decision making processes. This study recommends law schools in these four fastest-growing countries should promote legal ethics education to cultivate the awareness of legal professionalism among their law students. This project is crucial in understanding the values of the law students in China, India, Thailand, and the Philippines. The findings reveal the importance of improving legal ethics and professionalism among future lawyers in these four fastest-growing countries. Overall, the project is significant as it represents the first study of the values of law students in these four fastest-growing countries in Asia. It has contributed to the academic discourse on the ethical values of law students in Asia.

17603617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17603617.value: Since economic reforms in 1978, China’s economy has transformed from industry, to services, and now to producer services. As a result, the urban landscape has changed significantly. Central business districts (CBDs) have been one of the most visible new urban landscapes in many Chinese cities. Different from those in Western cities, many recently developed CBDs have been built in new business districts rather than developed in the old city propers. For the development of a new CBD, how to fill the office spaces is often a major problem worldwide. However, in China, the state plays a significant role in the planning and development of these new CBDs. State Own Enterprises (SOEs) are often used as pioneer firms to be first located in the new CBDs for attracting other firms to be located subsequently in them. The objective of this study is to examine the development dynamics of new CBDs in China by testing a proposed Public Enterprise-Led Model which uses SOEs as catalyst for attracting other firms in their early years of development. A quasi-experimental staging time-series research design will be used in the study by examining whether there is a development pattern of succession of ownerships, types, sizes, and investment sources of producer service firms in the new CBDs that were developed in different periods of time. It will use Chinese economic census at multiple years to reconstruct the profile of producer service firms in the new CBDs to examine the process of spatial concentration and succession of firms. The research will help to identify the role of SOEs in triggering off the spatial concentration process. It will examine the development process, characteristics and dynamics of firm succession. The project will study four cities that developed new CBDs in different time periods, namely Shanghai (Lujiazui financial and trade zone in the 1990s), Guangzhou (Pearl River New Town in the 2000s), Nanjing (Hexi new business district in the 2000s), and Shenzhen (Qianhai in the 2010s). Besides using economic census to examine the proposed Public Enterprises-Led Development Model and business succession, in-depth interviews with government officials and managers of SOEs and non-SOEs will be conducted to understand the planning process and development dynamics of these new CBDs. The study will contribute to our understanding of the development of post-industrial spaces in China and rethinking of the role of the state in constructing new CBDs in other countries. 自1978年經濟改革以來，中國經濟已從工業轉向服務業，現在亦已提升為生產性服務業。城市景觀也隨著經濟轉型發生了重大變化，中心商業區(CBD)已成為中國許多城市最明顯的“新城市空間”之一。在經濟改革前，中國城市中心商業區是不存在的，因為社會主義城市規劃非常重視工業生產而不是服務業。與西方城市不同的是近期發展的CBD不是在舊城開發，而是在新區開發。如何填滿新CBD辦公樓的辦公室是一個常見的新區開發問題。不過，中國的新CBD似乎在填滿辦公樓的辦公室方面一般都是成功的。本研究的目的是研究“製造”這些新CBD的成功秘訣。中國自1978年以來引入市場機制推動經濟發展，但國有企業(SOE)的作用不容忽略。除了國家直接干預外，國有企業往往是新CBD的先驅拓荒企業，帶領和引進其他企業到新的CBD去。鑒於國家與國有企業之間的親密關係，國家利用國有企業在初期階段對新CBD的發展做出催化和先驅的作用。本研究將通過半實驗分期的研究方法，探討政府企業在中國新CBD發展模式中所扮演的角色。將對上海，南京，和廣州這三個不同時期發展的新CBD的生產性服務企業的所有權，種類，規模，空間格局，投資來源的時空變化進行分析，以探討國有企業在不同發展階段的作用。通過深入訪問這三個城市CBD的政府官員和國有企業管理層，以及深圳新開發的前海商業區，以便瞭解國有企業如何培育新的CBD的地域優勢和聚集經濟。這項研究將有助我們瞭解中國後工業城市空間的發展，也為中國其他城市及其他發展中國家城市的CBD規劃和發展提供寶貴的參考經驗。

17603817.label: Project Objectives
17603817.value: To investigate whether mental rotation ability longitudinally predicts and causally influences performance in subtraction but not in addition. Establishing a prospective relation will indicate that the mental rotation ability that children acquire naturally bears a connection to their learning of subtraction in real-world settings, whereas establishing a causal relation will suggest that training in mental rotation can promote children's success in subtraction learning. To examine whether mental rotation longitudinally predicts and causally influences the use of the counting-down strategy, but not other strategies, in solving subtraction problems. Focusing on strategy use will help to clarify the behavioral mechanism underlying the relation between mental rotation and subtraction. In the proposed longitudinal and intervention studies, we expect to establish prospective and causal relations between mental rotation and strategy use in subtraction problem-solving in both natural and experimental settings.

17603817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17603817.value: Addition and subtraction are the two central forms of arithmetic problems in preschool and early elementary school. Studies of brain injury indicate that the two forms are dissociated in the human brain. However, we know little about the cognitive mechanism that contributes to the difference between children’s learning of subtraction and that of addition. Simple addition is taught at school via rote verbal learning, whereas subtraction is normally acquired by mental transformations of numerical quantities. Spatial ability has long been associated with success in arithmetic problem-solving, and recent neuroimaging evidence further indicates that mental rotation or transformation, an important spatial ability, has an anatomical overlap with subtraction but not addition in the brain. The brain region (i.e., the posterior superior parietal cortex) that is activated when a figure is mentally rotated is also activated when subtraction, but not addition, is performed. Surprisingly, however, there is a dearth of research examining whether mental rotation can explain the difference in the cognitive process between subtracting and adding. The aim of the proposed research, which will comprise two studies (one longitudinal study [N = 150] and the other a randomized controlled intervention [N = 180]), is to investigate whether mental rotation makes a specific contribution to young children’s learning of subtraction in discriminative contrast to their learning of addition. Moreover, we will measure both the outcome (i.e., performance) and process (i.e., strategy use) of subtraction problem-solving. Focusing on strategy use will help to clarify the behavioral mechanism underlying the relation between mental rotation and subtraction. We expect mental rotation to exert significant predictive and causal effects on performance and the use of a particular strategy (i.e., counting-down) in subtraction but not on performance in addition or the use of other strategies in subtraction. The proposed research will help to delineate the fundamental cognitive mechanism that underlies children’s learning of subtraction. We also expect the findings to shed light on early childhood mathematics education by indicating which type of spatial learning opportunities best helps children to learn particular types of mathematical content. For example, activities that improve mental rotation ability, such as puzzle play, may be particularly helpful for young children's later learning of subtraction, whereas non-mental rotation activities may be more helpful for the learning of addition. 加法與減法是幼稚園與小學低年級階段最重要的兩種算術運算。對腦損傷的研究發現，這兩種算術運算在人類大腦中是相互分離的。然而，對于兒童加法與減法學習之差異的認知機理，我們所知甚少。學校中的加法教學很多是靠口頭的死記硬背，而減法教學往往並非靠死記硬背，而是依賴對數量的心理操作。最近的大腦掃描研究發現，心理旋轉或心理操作所激活的腦區與減法運算所激活的腦區有一定重疊，而加法則不同。本研究計劃由兩項研究組成（一項爲縱向研究，另一項爲介入研究），旨在探討心理旋轉是否會影響兒童的減法運算而與加法無關。不僅如此，我們既測量減法的運算結果（即成績）又測量它的運算過程（即策略使用）。我們預期，心理旋轉對減法運算的成績和倒數策略使用具有明顯的預測和影響作用，而對加法運算成績或其它減法運算策略則無明顯作用。本研究計劃有助于我們理清兒童減法學習的基本認知機理。研究結果還有望對幼兒數學教育有所啓示，比如告訴我們哪些類型的空間學習經驗更可能幫助兒童掌握減法、哪些類型的學習經驗更可能幫助兒童掌握加法。

17603817.label: Realisation of objectives
17603817.value: Objective 1 has been fully achieved, and Objective 2 has been partially (50%) achieved owing to the COVID-19 pandemic. The pandemic caused repeated school closures in Hong Kong, which disrupted our data collection again and again. This is especially true for Study 2. In 2020, we hired a full-time RA and completed the pilot study of Study 2. Yet owing to the pandemic, our participating kindergartens were suddenly closed, and we had no choice but postponed Study 2. In 2021, we hired another full-time RA and even completed the pretest of Study 2. Yet the fifth wave of the pandemic suddenly arrived in Hong Kong in December 2021 and caused school closures again, and we had to terminate Study 2 again. Despite the challenges, we have finally completed both Study 1 and Study 2, and we have also completed the data analysis for Study 1 and part of the data analysis for Study 2. Unfortunately, we were unable to complete all the data analysis of Study 2. We have analyzed part of the data to address the two project objectives and summarized our findings as follows: As for Objective 1, the results from Study 1 showed that children's mental rotation ability longitudinally predicted their performance in subtraction but not in addition, and the results of Study 2 showed that children who received mental rotation training had more improvements in subtraction performance than their peers who did not receive such training. As for Objective 2, the results from Study 1 showed that children's mental rotation ability longitudinally predicted their use of the counting-down strategy in solving subtraction problems. Unfortunately, we were still in the process of coding children's strategy use in Study 2, owing to the pandemic's disruption of our data collection. We expect that Objective 2 can be fully achieved in 2023.

17603817.label: Major findings and research outcome
17603817.value: Major findings: Children's mental rotation ability was found to longitudinally predict and causally influence their performance in subtraction but not in addition. That is, children with stronger mental rotation ability had higher performance in subtraction, and children who received mental rotation training had more improvements in subtraction performance than their peers who did not receive such training. In contrast, mental rotation ability was not related to children's performance in addition. The results also showed that children's mental rotation ability longitudinally predicted their use of the counting-down strategy, but not other strategies, in solving subtraction problems. In other words, children who had stronger mental rotation ability were more likely to use the counting-down strategy to solve subtraction problems. Research outcome: (1) Based on this project, we have produced six papers, among which five have been published in high-impact international journals (e.g., Journal of Educational Psychology, Cognition, and Early Childhood Research Quarterly) and one is now under revision and resubmission to Contemporary Educational Psychology. Finally, based on this project, one PhD student, Xiangzi Ouyang, was successful in developing her thesis work and publishing her findings in Child Development. (2) Based on this project, two poster presentations and two oral presentations were given at recognized international conferences (e.g., SRCD and MCLS). (3) The research team is planning to present the final research findings of the completed project at one or two more international conferences and is preparing at least two more manuscripts for publication in high-impact international journals.

17603817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17603817.value: We will continue to analyze the remaining data of this research project and publish the findings in international conferences and academic journals. Spatial training is a hot topic in the field of educational psychology. Based on the findings of this research project, a five-year Research Fellowship Scheme project has been developed to further explore the role of spatial skills in children's development of mathematics learning disability and design an intervention program to enhance young Chinese children's spatial and arithmetic skills.

17603817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17603817.value: Addition and subtraction are the two central forms of arithmetic problems in preschool and early elementary school. The two forms, according to studies of brain function after injury, are dissociated in the human brain. However, we know little about the cognitive mechanism that contributes to the difference between children’s learning of subtraction and that of addition. Simple addition is taught at school via rote verbal learning, whereas subtraction is not normally acquired by rote verbal learning but by mental transformations of numerical quantities. Recent evidence from neuroimaging studies further indicates that mental rotation or transformation has an anatomical overlap with subtraction but not addition. The results of this research projects showed that children's mental rotation ability was related to their performance in subtraction but not addition. The findings help delineate the fundamental cognitive mechanism that specifically underlies children’s learning of subtraction. They also shed light on early childhood mathematics education by indicating activities that can improve mental rotation ability, such as puzzle play, may be particularly helpful for young children to learn subtraction later on.

17604117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17604117.value: Hong Kong and cities in the Pearl River Delta (PRD thereafter) are facing critical challenges in urban sustainability for architecture and urban spaces on their environmental performances. The accelerating urban development resulting from China’s economic reform after 1978 produced high-density metropolis across the region, creating drastic changes in microclimate for urban spaces, facilitating problematic conditions of urban-heat generation with poor outdoor environmental performances. Through development model of podium-tower, the increasing demand of floor area efficiency in architectural design also exacerbates contrasting thermal condition between air-conditioned indoor and hot-humid outdoor urban space. Lingnan Architecture of traditional courtyard houses in the region demonstrates environmental sustainability by the use of three-dimensional atriums to accommodate climatic condition as well as to facilitate natural ventilation and lighting. Urban Courtyardism is a design method adopted by the PI to transform typologies of traditional courtyard in the high-density urban context (Wang, 2011). Through a series of design projects exploring different strategies on re-inventing traditional courtyard types for contemporary buildings, it establishes an innovative design system shaping open spaces of outdoors and semi-outdoors at different datum of multi-leveled buildings. In the humid and hot weather of Southern China, the designs generate microclimate conditions providing semi-shaded public spaces opening up to sky or the front, creating openings that allow hot air to travel across the multiple-leveled urban court-yards (Chow, 2010). Rather than using conventional podium-tower typology, these designs identify multi-storied modules of massing block, adopt strategies of interlocking and overlapping, and create three-dimensional sky patios for urban greenery. In addition to shaping a sequence of connected courtyards at multiple levels, it also enables upper-level functional spaces to share greenery in sky-terraces. Through moderating scale and proportion, light and shade of spaces in a three-dimensional manner, the designs establish sense of places and spatial identities for communities. The Project is a post-occupancy evaluation on environmental and social performances addressing 9 built projects adopting design strategies of urban courtyard in Hong Kong, Shenzhen, and Dongguan. By comparing to traditional courtyard houses in the region, it looks into their condition of use and thermal comfort of varies types of indoor/outdoor public and semi-public urban courtyard spaces, building up methods and criteria of post-occupancy evaluation in environmental performances and spatial use. It also provides us database and knowledge for improving the established green building design principles, and developing new architectural design strategies for urban courtyard in cities of South China. 近幾十年來香港和華南珠三角地區的建築與城市空間， 面臨了城市環境績效與可持續性的嚴峻挑戰。四十年來中國快速的經濟發展，替這個區域的大都會帶來高密度的城市型態， 而高層塔樓域裙樓的建築發展模式，加速了戶外空間的城市熱效應和環境惡化的危機。而開發商對建築設計面積效率的要求，犧牲了室內外之間應有的過渡性空間，強化了空調室內與濕熱戶外空間的溫差對比。 嶺南傳統建築的四合院利用三維的中庭空間，成功的引入了自然通風與採光，調控了舒適的建築環境。透過都市合院主義的設計方法，王維仁建築設計研究室成功的將傳統合院的空間型態，轉化為高密度城市的多層合院建築型態。王維仁透過一系列已完成的建築設計，探討了不同的設計策略，思考如何將傳統合院原型，轉化為當代城市的新建築型態。這些設計建立了一套創新的系統，在多層建築發展出一套結合戶外與半戶外的空間體系。在濕熱的華南，這些設計發展出一種半戶外的微氣候狀態，提供一種對上下或對前後開放，讓空氣對流與遮蔭而舒適的公共合院空間。 經由對都市合院主義在香港與華南的九個完成項目的探討，透過環境科學測量與使用後評估的方法，本研究試圖建立一個都市合院主義的環境科學模型，評估如何選擇不同的設計方法，提供不同形式的多層三維都市合院，以及它們的不同環境效應表現。長遠的來說，這個研究期望能提倡一種設計規劃策略，更科學的推展高密度城市環境的都市合院，改善都市戶外公共空間的環境質量。

17604617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17604617.value: Over the last century, as intensifying global interactions expanded food choices in certain Chinese cities, dietary intake came to represent consumers’ imageries of modernity and economic progress. Conditioned by their cultural background and their exposure to foreign notions of science, these urban populations consumed bottled beverages that promised them bodily health and engendered aspirations as well as anxiety. Introduced by Westerners, cow milk appealed to aspiring consumers in the Treaty Ports as it embodied notions of modernity, technology, and public health. In post-war Hong Kong and Taipei, cow milk presented an alternative to varietals of liquid protein intake such as soymilk, itself being an import from other regions in China. Local Chinese residents did not embrace the non-local products until after the Second World War, as socioeconomic transformations imbued meanings in the consumption of these products. Drawing on their expertise in their respective areas, the two investigators of this project connect the experience of the dairy industry in the Treaty Ports of Shanghai and Canton as well as the British colony of Hong Kong with the cow milk and soymilk consumption in post-war Hong Kong and Taipei. Although the rise of these products happened decades apart, similar factors had fuelled their popularity in these Chinese peripheries under heavy Western influences. The team examines the interactions between the consumers and the businesses producing and marketing such products as a discursive process in which the various participants produced and received confusing signals in the race towards modernity and economic prosperity. This project probes how “culture” is utilized to market milk and soymilk and how consumers shape their cultural discourse with their consumption pattern. In the Treaty Ports, milk was first promoted as Western, and hence the product assumed a superior image as a consumable that fitted into the “modern Chinese lifestyle” that their residents aspired to lead. In post-war Hong Kong and Taipei, dissimilar socioeconomic conditions and cultural dispositions resulted in the popularity of both cow milk and soymilk in Hong Kong but the predominance of soymilk in Taipei. This discourse bore tremendous financial significance in the post-war period, and commercial enterprises took an active interest in steering consumer perceptions. The results of this project will break new theoretical and empirical ground, and contribute novel paradigms and fresh data to ongoing debates about food studies, business history, as well as global and regional differences in the articulation of modernity and progress in East Asia. 二十世紀，隨著全球互動的加劇，中國某些城市的食物選擇擴大，飲食代表了消費者對現代性和經濟進步的想像和體會。由於他們的文化背景和對外國科學觀念的理解，這些城市消費者在購買和飲用號稱對身體有益的包裝飲料時，表達了他們的渴望和焦慮。從西方人引入的牛奶，因帶有現代，技術和公共衛生意義，對在條件港口的消費者俱有吸引力。 。在戰後香港和台北，“進口”的牛奶為消費者提供了跟本身也是中國東北引進大豆加工而成的豆奶另外一個選擇。不同地區的華人沒有理所當然地接受了非本地生產的飲食品，而是第二次世界大戰結束，社會經濟轉型為這些消費帶來新意義後，牛奶和豆奶才漸為廣大市民認受。 根據他們在各自領域的專業知識，此項目的兩名調查員將戰前上海、廣州和香港的乳業，及戰後香港和台北的牛奶和豆漿消費情況聯繫起來。縱使這些產品的興起相隔數十載，在這些西方影響下的中國週邊地區，該等產品的流行其實是基於同樣的因素。此研究團隊將調查消費者與生產商在出產和營銷這些商品時的互動，以了解各參與者在現代和經濟繁榮的競爭中產生和接受混亂信號的話語過程。 此項目探討生產商如何利用“文化”來銷售牛奶和豆漿，而消費者又如何以他們的消費模式塑造文化話語。在“條約港口”，牛奶最初被視為西方產品，帶有優越的形象，又適合渴望“現代中國生活方式”居民的口味，在戰後的香港和台北，不同的社會經和濟條件及文化差異，導致在香港牛奶和豆奶的普及，但在台北豆漿卻佔主導地位。這個話語在戰後期間具有巨大的經濟意義，商業企業也積極地引導消費者的看法。此項目的成結將在理論和實證上帶來突破性的發展，為飲食文化，商業歷史以及全球和地區發展的辯論中提供新的範式和數據。

17604617.label: Realisation of objectives
17604617.value: Thanks to the generous sponsorship of the RGC and the work of a collaborative team (the PI, the Co-I, and RAs), this project has largely fulfilled all the objectives the team set out to accomplish. The team explored critically the production, marketing, and consumption of cow’s milk and soymilk in multiple Chinese communities along the frontier of Chinese interactions with western practices. Our project has produced numerous studies that reveal how food precipitated differently multilayered identities in various locations. Complicating issues of local versus foreign in terms of food and beverage, our research findings detailed the transmission, proliferation and acculturation of consumption practices. Our comparison of these practices cut across time and space. Extending beyond the original design of interdisciplinary collaboration across modern Chinese history and anthropology, the team has broadened its reach to history of science, business history and business studies. Through our focus on cow’s milk and soymilk, the team has developed an approach that showcases a toolbox that bridges multiple disciplines and area focuses. As the team responded to sociopolitical uncertainties and intensifying COVID-related restrictions, we applied this framework to the related food product of soy sauce and examined its role in identity articulation in different locales. In terms of publications, this project has produced to date an article in a top business history journal and an accepted article at a leading journal focusing on Asian area studies. Yet another article is under review. “‘Made in Hong Kong’: Deriving Value from the Place-of-Origin Label, 1950s and now,” Modern Asian Studies (accepted). “Making Vitasoy ‘Local’ in Post-WWII Hong Kong: Traditionalizing Modernity, Engineering Progress, Nurturing Aspirations,” Business History Review 95:2 (2021): 275-300. DOI: https://doi.org/10.1017/S0007680521000210. “The Rise of Reconstituted Milk in Hong Kong, 1590s – 1960s,” Business History (under review). Extending our impact to Chinese readership, the project has also produced a monograph printed first in Hong Kong in traditional Chinese, which subsequently appeared in simplified Chinese for the mainland Chinse market. 《母乳與牛奶：近代中國母親角色的重塑，1895-1937》（上海：華東師範大學出版社，2020）。 Mother’s Milk and Cow’s Milk: Reconstruction of Motherhood in Modern China, 1895-1937 (Simplified Chinese version). Shanghai: East China Normal University Press, 2020) --第十六屆中國國家圖書館文津獎社會科學推薦書(2021) (recommended book in the category of social science for the 16th Wenjin Book Prize organized by the National Library of China in 2021). Reaching a different audience, an article produced by this study debuted in a Chinese journal specializing in food practices, and was reprinted in an edited volume in Taiwan. “豉油小碟裏的香港：從生曬醬油到港製頭抽” “Soy Sauce in Hong Kong: From Sun-Dried Sauce to First-Brewed Premium” (co-authored with Sidney Cheung), 中國飲食文化 Journal of Chinese Dietary Culture 14:2(2018): 215-238. Reprinted as in 《醬・文化：記憶、技藝與身體》, edited by Chen Chien-Yuan 陳建源, 397-420. Taichung: NCHU Research Center for Humanities and Social Sciences, 2021. Synthesizing our findings for the project as a whole, we are exploring further publication opportunities, potentially in conjunction with other food studies situated in like locales. Such future publications would focus on articulating the framework of layered identities around food against the backdrop of socioeconomic developments and cultural articulations which did not march to the same drumbeat in different areas in modern China. This stellar publication record was only possible through constant exchange with the scholarly community and the public at large. The team initiated such exchange in the early stages of this project as we communicated our research findings readily with our target audience. By the second year of the project, we were already refining our ideas at symposia hosted by leading research institutes in Guangzhou and Shandong, an SSRC-sponsored workshop in Vietnam, and a conference in Kyoto. Eager to frame our studies in a broader international context, we presented at a business history conference in Columbia, the biggest annual event for Asian studies in Thailand, and an international convention of Asian scholars in the Netherlands. As travel came to a grinding halt, we turned our attention to the local audience in Hong Kong and explored online venues to share our findings. Our efforts bore fruit as we found ready reception at publication outlets and responsive readership. We have continued our efforts after the conclusion of the grant period as we take our messages to such locations as the Singapore Heritage Festival where we not only found further comparative potential for our project but also opportunities for knowledge exchange and transfer. The enduring impact of our research initiative is evident in the forthcoming article which extends our analysis to soy sauce. This article demonstrates our identification of key aspects of food studies in China and our longitudinal approach to our historical inquiry. More significantly, this extension of the methods we developed from our examination of the cow’s milk and soymilk cases showcases the application of our procedural tools that combines business history, cultural history, and the study of disparate areas of China. We look forward to further applications of this approach as we pursue future publication outlets and collaborative research opportunities.

17604617.label: Major findings and research outcome
17604617.value: As global interactions intensified in select Chinese communities in the twentieth century, the novelty of food and beverages, be they imported products or foreign inspired inventions, engendered appeal while at the same time aroused suspicion. Acceptance and consumption of such products were only possible after technological improvements put them in physical and economic reach of the masses, local adaptations and modifications overcame cultural resistance, and enterprising businesses translated scientific propositions and non-native notions into consumable items. These interlocking elements not only stylized consumption and fashioned identities at their locales but also channeled flows through a global catchment area. At the turn of the twentieth century, Western nutritional sciences introduced cow’s milk as an alternative to mother’s milk, transforming the dynamics of motherhood in select urban areas in China (Lo 2018, 2021). Billed as a Chinese substitute, soymilk emerged as a potential fortifier for what was supposedly a dietarily impoverished China. Yet, soymilk was not deemed non-native in such locales such as Hong Kong where soybeans were imported items. A commercially packaged option won the approval of local consumers in Hong Kong only in the post–World War II period as its producer capitalized on the discourse of modern nutritional science, leveraged technological breakthroughs, and positioned the soy beverage to respond to a growing clientele experiencing economic growth and lifestyle transformation (Wong 2021). At the same time, cow’s milk came within the masses reach in Hong Kong in the form of reconstituted milk. The rise of dairy intake in the Hong Kong diet through this specialty product underscores the impact of geopolitics, international material flows, technology transfer, and the mediation of commercial interests on local consumption of what has become a global commodity (Lo and Wong, under review). Extending our research through soybeans to the international markets, this research project examined soy sauce exports from Hong Kong to the United States. Hong Kong’s processing of soybean into soy sauce demonstrates how politically motivated US trade policies steered businesses in Hong Kong to pursue commercial opportunities by leveraging geopolitics, both global and local. In successive rounds of US-initiated trade disruptions, the place-of-origin label reflected Hong Kong’s changing place in global geopolitics and the city’s position vis-à-vis the PRC (Wong, forthcoming). Against the backdrop of geopolitical shifts and socioeconomic transformations, commercial forces channelled cultural articulations through food and beverage on which multilayered identities developed.

17604617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17604617.value: Although the team managed to make full use of the grant period by redirecting our attention to related food products when travel became problematic, this research project was handicapped to some extent from certain trip cancellations. We had to curtail our trips to Guangzhou, originally scheduled to be undertaken in the second half of the grant period. While we can now claim a firmer grasp of developments in Shanghai and Taiwan, we need to conduct further research in some locales once travel resumes. Travel difficulties notwithstanding, the team explored other comparative and collaborative opportunities with colleagues in Singapore, Japan, and Korea. We shall seek to synthesize our findings in conjunction with food studies situated in these locales. With colleagues working at Asian locations animated by similar elements, we will work on publications that focus on articulating the framework of layered identities around food against the backdrop of socioeconomic developments and cultural articulations.

17605917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17605917.value: English law remains central to the history of former British colonies, and is still widely acknowledged by Hong Kong citizens today as a core contributing factor to the city’s development and economic success. The traditional narrative is that English rule of law, which offers such safeguards of individual liberty as freedom of expression, is the most important legacy of British rule in Hong Kong, a legacy that is very often used to distinguish the legal and societal development of Hong Kong from that of mainland China. The proposed study will argue that such a narrative does not stand up to archival scrutiny of the media censorship widely practised in British Hong Kong during most of its history (1850s-1980s). This book-length project will constitute the first in-depth study of media censorship in British Hong Kong. By revealing how the mass media, including the press, literary works, broadcasters, film and theatrical productions, were continually and systematically monitored, pervasively censored, and regularly prosecuted and convicted through the collaborative efforts of executive actions, legislative provisions and judicial decisions during most of Hong Kong’s colonial period (1850s-1980s), it promises to reveal that such purported safeguards of English rule of law as equality before the law, freedom of expression and judicial autonomy remained subordinate to sovereignty, state power and geopolitics. The study will further challenge the widely accepted narrative that the rule of law is a legacy of British colonial rule in Hong Kong. Rather, I argue that it is more a ‘legacy’ of the decolonisation process of the British Empire that began in the 1980s. The rule of law that the people of Hong Kong are eager to preserve today, as with many aspects of what is commonly construed as good governance in Hong Kong (for example, measures against corruption, protection of human rights), appeared rather late in the colonial era, as colonialism erected a kinder façade in the decolonisation stage. The proposed study’s significance lies in the richness of the unexplored archived historical data on the practice and experience of media censorship in British Hong Kong that it will make use of and the long timespan it will cover. The aim is to demythologise the well-rehearsed history of the rule of law in Hong Kong and to add the legal history of colonial Hong Kong to the emerging body of scholarship on the global and comparative study of law and colonialism. 英國法律在香港殖民地歷史中佔舉足輕重的地位。傳統的殖民歷史學家將其論述為殖民者給予被殖民者的恩物，很多香港市民都督信英式法治，包括司法獨立，和言論自由的保障，是英國殖民統治在香港的最重要遺產，它經常被引用來區分香港的法律和社會發展與毗鄰中國大陸發展的主要分別。 本研究計劃將證明，類似理想化殖民時期英式法治的論述，罔顧歷史事實。本研究計劃的目的是研究1850至1980年代，港英政府如何透過立法，行政措施和司法判決合力廣泛地政治審查大眾媒體（包括報紙，文學作品，廣播媒體，電影和舞台表演），並試圖證明，香港歷史上實行的普通法制度，在絕大部分的殖民地時期打壓市民言論和政治表達自由，以鞏固殖民地政府的專制權力，和保護英國的外交與地緣政治利益， 有時更罔顧司法獨立和法律底下人人平等的原則。本研究計劃旨在對廣為香港市民接受的「法治作為最重要的殖民遺產」的論述，提出嚴正質疑，本研究計劃認為今天香港人享有並珍惜的法治，是英帝國1980年代開始解殖過程才出現的產品。 本研究計劃透過未被研究的檔案史料，試圖撕破殖民歷史學家建構的香港法治歷史神話，把香港法律史置於環球比較殖民地法律史的學術視野中。

17605917.label: Realisation of objectives
17605917.value: Despite the obstruction and delay in archival data collection in Hong Kong and London caused by the social movements in 2019 and the pandemic that followed in 2020, I managed to complete this project by achieving the following 2 objectives as originally proposed. Objective 1. To construct a narrative of the practice and experience of media censorship in British Hong Kong (1850s-1980s) and situate that narrative in the legal history of colonial Hong Kong. The traditional scholarly narrative is that English rule of law, which offers such safeguards of individual liberty as freedom of expression, freedom of assembly, equality before the law and judicial independence, is the most important legacy of British rule in Hong Kong, a legacy that is very often used to distinguish the legal and societal development of Hong Kong from that of mainland China. These confident claims are made despite the fact that no monographic archival work on Hong Kong’s colonial legal history exists. Drawing on previously unexplored archival materials, the findings of this project (which will be published as the first archival research monograph on HK legal history that covers most of the entire colonial period) challenges the widely accepted narrative – or myth – that freedom of expression is a legacy of British rule of law in Hong Kong, arguing that it simply does not stand up to scrutiny of the archival record. By unfolding the history of how the media and schools were consistently and pervasively censored during most of the colonial period, this project finds that the free press, freedom of speech and even judicial independence that so many people in Hong Kong are eager to preserve today are the result of the larger China strategy that Britain employed in preparing Hong Kong for its return to China. Any discussion of freedoms and the rule of law in Hong Kong needs to be situated in an informed understanding of this history. This project, however, is not solely concerned with repeating the claims of scholarship showing imperial-era colonial law and legal systems to have been characterised by racism, inequality and oppression of the colonised. Rather, it explains these and other features of colonial rule in Hong Kong in light of the historical context, thereby revealing the complex factors, both local and global, that drove and constrained the ‘legal imperial’ in running its silencing regime in the British Empire’s most important trading post in East Asia. What has defined and confined the Hong Kong people’s right to speak has not, unfortunately, been how dearly held the values of common law are or how hard the Hong Kong people have fought to secure that right. What has mattered more, this study argues, has been the bigger picture of global and regional politics: the political-economic situation of China, China’s relations with the major world powers and those powers’ China strategies over time, as revealed by this project’s archival discovery. Hence, well-rehearsed narratives that attribute the freedoms enjoyed in Hong Kong to common-law traditions without situating them in the global history this study tells are seriously inadequate, if not misleading. More specifically, this project has answered the following questions. What drove the colonial Hong Kong government to enact laws and regulations aimed at censoring the media? How were its political censorship measures carried out, and how did they evolve over time? What kinds of media were targeted for censorship? How was the notion of freedom of expression understood by the colonisers and the colonised? How was that notion negotiated and compromised in practice? How was such compromise and negotiation justified by colonial officers, judges and legislators in Hong Kong, as well as by government officials in London, in light of the domestic governance, national interest and international relations issues faced by the Hong Kong and London governments? How did the political, social and economic situation of China and China’s relationship with the major world powers, especially Britain, Japan and the United States, influence the evolution of the law and practice of political censorship in Hong Kong? This project provides the first in-depth empirical study of the practice and experience of the political censorship of mass media and schools in British Hong Kong in a broader historical context connecting the history of Hong Kong with the histories of China, Britain and global geopolitics in Asia in the 19th nineteenth and 20th twentieth centuries. It constructs a ground-breaking narrative that demythologises the well-rehearsed history of the rule of law in Hong Kong, and unfolds the history of freedoms in colonial Hong Kong that was unrelated to the ideal of the rule of law told by jurists or historians in the past. It adds the legal history of this important former colony in East Asia to the emerging body of scholarship on the global and comparative study of law and colonialism. Its significance also lies in the richness of the unexplored archival data on censorship practice of which it makes ample use. It places Hong Kong's legal history in the context of world history, demonstrating how deeply Hong Kong's development was impacted by geopolitics. The history of freedom of expression and the law in Hong Kong told by this project also informs us that regardless of how the rule of law is idealised as transcending the governing authority, its operation has seldom taken place in isolation from politics, global geopolitics and power structures in the modern era, particularly when the government is not democratically elected. Objective 2. To publish at least two articles in reputable international refereed journal and a book manuscript on the history of media censorship in British Hong Kong (1850s-1980s). The findings of this project will form four chapters of the 6-chapter research monograph manuscript entitled Political Censorship in British Hong Kong: Freedom of expression and the law (1942-1997), which has been accepted for publication by Cambridge University Press. The titles of the first four chapters of the book are as follows: 1. Punitive censorship and libel lawsuits against the press 2. “Reading every line”: Era of the daily vetting of newspaper proofs 3. “Communist China now contiguous to Hong Kong”: Censorship imposed by the “free world” 4. “Patriotism to you can be revolutionary heresy to us”: Hardened control of media, schools and entertainment Certain findings of this project have also been published in a refereed journal article: “Who but the Governor in Executive Council is the Judge?”: Historical Use of the Emergency Regulations Ordinance,” Hong Kong Law Journal (2020) 50.2: 425-461. (co-authored with Zhang Shengyue and Max Wong) Findings of this project will also be published as a book chapter of an edited volume that has been accepted for publication by Cambridge University Press. The chapter is entitled “Empires Collaborate: Geopolitics of Colonial Policing in Hong Kong (1880s-1970s)” and will be included in the edited volume entitled Beyond Regime Type: The Transformation of Police in Asia, edited by Prof Fu Hualing (HKU) and Dr. Chen Weitseng (NUS).

17605917.label: Major findings and research outcome
17605917.value: This study finds that unfettered freedom of expression was nearly undreamt of in Hong Kong during most of the colonial era. Editorial independence was subject to the government’s political concerns, both local and global. Newspaper publishers and editors were regularly sued for criminal libel for criticising senior British officials, and were also prosecuted for criticising Britain’s allies such as Japan and France for military aggression against China. By law, all Chinese-language newspaper articles had to be pre-censored, not only during emergencies but even in peacetime. Failure to comply with the pre-censorship regulations led to heavy fines and the imprisonment of publishers and editors. Both KMT- and CCP-controlled newspaper presses were shut down for political reasons. During the height of the cold war, journalists, school principals, teachers and students were detained and deported without trial. School textbooks, syllabuses and activities were subject to pre-censorship, and students who engaged in activities or discussions of a political nature could be expelled. Government Information Services “fed” news bulletins and scripts to radio and television stations for broadcasting. Even when these stations were allowed to produce their own news reports in the 1970s, they could obtain information only from “approved” news sources according to the law. RTHK’s senior management pre-censored even non-news entertainment programmes and gramophone recordings to ensure that minimal political elements were contained in radio programmes. Licence conditions and so-called “programme standards” for radio and television stations imposed restrictions on programme content on political grounds such as provoking hatred of the government, damaging good relations with other territories or being undesirable in the public interest. Well-rehearsed common law cases and remedies that safeguarded freedom of the press and freedom of expression were not applicable to Hong Kong in practice because they were simply watered-down or overruled by repressive colonial legislation until the late 1960s and early 1970s, when the future of Hong Kong after 1997 first appeared on London’s policy agenda. Despite the open opposition of the press and Chinese elites to restrictions on the press and freedom of expression since the early twentieth century, it is clear that what happened in mainland China, in global geopolitics, and in China’s relations with Britain, the US and their allies mattered much more to the British and colonial governments than did the common law-values in determining the freedoms they enjoyed.

17605917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17605917.value: The findings of this project which cover the colonial period up to 1980 should provoke three questions that would bear significant research potential: 1. How and why were such authoritarian law and political censorship practice in colonial Hong Kong phased out, and liberal notions of the rule of law and freedom of speech awakened, as a pressing political agenda in the final decades of colonial rule prior in its run-up to 1997? 2. To what extent was the practice of judicial independence and equality before the law in colonial HK different from the well-rehearsed common law values. If there is a difference, what are the reasons and historical contexts behind such difference. Some of these aspects will be covered in my next GRF project.

17605917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17605917.value: The findings of this archival research project challenge the widely accepted myth that freedom of expression is a legacy of British rule of law in Hong Kong, arguing that it simply does not stand up to scrutiny of the archival record. This project unfolds the history of how the media and schools were consistently and pervasively censored and prosecuted during most of the colonial period, it finds that the free press, freedom of speech and even judicial independence that so many people in Hong Kong are eager to preserve today are the result of the larger China strategy that Britain employed in preparing Hong Kong for its return to China. The project also finds that what has defined and confined the Hong Kong people?s right to speak has not, unfortunately, been how dearly held the values of common law are or how hard the Hong Kong people have fought to secure that right. What has mattered more, this project argues, has been the bigger picture of global and regional politics: the political-economic situation of China, China?s relations with the major world powers and those powers? China strategies over time, as revealed by this project?s archival discovery.

17607517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17607517.value: Writing is at the heart of higher education. In a postgraduate professional development (PPD) programme, writing occurs at the juncture of academia and the professional world, and is the primary medium by which student professionals are assessed. In the proposed project, we aim to further theoretical understanding of what it means to write in a PPD programme, by investigating the kinds of written assignments and feedback given in an MEd programme (a type of PPD programme), and exploring how lecturers’ and students’ perspectives on the purposes and requirements of written assignments may diverge. Theoretically we draw upon the “academic literacies” perspective on writing, an emergent and significant field of study in higher education, which, in contrast to the traditional, skills-based approach, focuses on the social practices surrounding writing, foregrounds issues related to epistemology, identity and power, and ideologically adopts an explicitly transformative stance towards the object of study. Our research site will be the Faculty of Education of the University of Hong Kong, which offers the largest MEd programme in Hong Kong, with over 400 new MEd students admitted each year. A mixed-methods exploratory sequential design combining qualitative study and survey methods to gather qualitative and quantitative evidence will be adopted. In the qualitative stage of the study, we will collect assignment specifications, feedback sheets and related documents; we will also conduct semi-structured interviews with lecturers (N = 30-36) and students (N = 30-36), with the participant selection criteria taking into account the diversity of the disciplinary areas, courses and assignments represented. In the quantitative stage, two purposively designed and validated questionnaires drawing upon findings from the qualitative stage will be developed and administered respectively to all lecturers (N = 70) teaching on the focal MEd programme and to a complete intake (N = 400) of MEd students across specialisms in the same programme to map out the broad patterns of the significant issues emerging from the qualitative stage and to test the generalisability of the qualitative findings. Our project will address the lack of systematic research on writing in the context of Master-level PPD programmes and hence shed light on the relationship between academia and the professional world in this context. Ours will be the first study in Hong Kong on writing in higher education conducted from the academic literacies perspective, and we will aim to develop this research field at theoretical, methodological, and applicational levels. 連接大學與社會：職業發展碩士學位課程中的寫作與反饋 寫作處於高等教育的中心位置，而在職業發展學位/證書課程中，寫作連接著大學與社會，並且是考評學生的主要途徑。在本項研究中，我們的目標是瞭解究竟在職業發展學位/證書課程中寫作意味著什麼，以此從理論層面提供新的視角。為此，我們將調查在一個教育碩士課程體系中（一種職業發展學位/證書課程），書面作業及反饋是以怎樣的形式呈現的，並探索教師與學生們對於寫作任務的目的和要求的理解可能有著怎樣的分歧。 我們採納“學術素養”理論為本研究提供理論指導。與傳統的強調技能為中心的寫作理論相比較，該理論著眼於研究圍繞著寫作的社會行為，探索寫作行為所體現的認識論、身份、權力等方面的意義，在意識形態上強調改革傳統的教育理念。我們選擇有著香港最大的教育碩士課程體系，每年招收教育碩士新生達400多人的香港大學教育學院為研究地點。我們採納探索式順序性的混合研究設計方案，結合質性方法和問卷調查方法以獲取質化和量化的資料。在質性研究階段，我們將收集書面作業的要求細則，教師對學生作業的反饋意見及相關資料。我們將與教師和學生（分別達30-36人）進行半結構式訪談。在受訪者的選擇方面，我們將考慮所代表的教育學科、課程及作業種類的多樣性。在量化研究階段，我們將根據質性研究階段的研究發現設計兩份問卷，在對問卷進行信度檢驗之後，碩士課程的所有教師（約70人）及在讀的某一屆全部學生（約400人）將被邀請分別填寫這兩份問卷，從而為質性研究階段的研究發現尋找出在更廣泛層面上的規律，並檢驗這些發現的普適性。 在職業發展教育碩士學位課程的教育環境下，尚未進行過系統的寫作研究。我們的研究將填補這一空白，從而幫助瞭解在此教育環境裡大學與社會之間的關係。這亦將是香港本土第一項運用學術素養理論研究高等教育中的寫作現象的課題，因而我們將由理論、方法及應用層面推動此領域的研究。

17608517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17608517.value: Japanese popular culture was no doubt an important cultural presence in Hong Kong between the 1980s and the early 2000s. Despite its declining cultural sway due to recent explosion and proliferation of ‘Korean wave’ in Hong Kong, Japanese popular culture has played an important role in shaping the Hong Kong culture and the everyday life experience of the Hong Kong people during the post-war period. There are a certain number of studies which examine the spread of various Japanese cultural products in Hong Kong, but none of them has systematically studied the arrival, diffusion and consumption of Japanese popular culture in Hong Kong in relation to the formation of the local Hong Kong culture. Our study is an anthropological attempt to examine the relationship between Japanese popular culture and the cultural formation of Hong Kong society (1970s–early 2000s). Through examining the spread of four Japanese cultural products, namely the Japanese television dramas, popular music, retail formats and food in Hong Kong, we intend to investigate four sets of interrelated issues: 1) the spread of Japanese popular culture in Hong Kong; 2) the consumption of Japanese cultural products by the Hong Kong people; 3) the impact of Japanese popular culture on the daily life of the Hong Kong people and 4) the relationships between Japanese popular culture and the development of the Hong Kong culture. In this project, we do not simply focus on analyzing the texts of the Japanese cultural products and the audience experience like what many previous studies on the subject have done. Instead, we propose to study the mediations among the different Japanese cultural products, between the exporting and receiving societies of the products and among the producers, intermediaries and consumers. We will conduct intensive archival research, literature review, in-depth interviews and fieldwork to investigate the nature and impact of Japanese popular culture in relation to the specific social context of the Hong Kong society. This project will help enhance our understanding not just of the history of Japanese popular culture in Hong Kong but also of the formation and constitution of the local Hong Kong culture. We aim at demonstrating that the importance of studying the cultural formation of Hong Kong society in relation to other cultures and societies. The project will also result in an open-access database containing the details of the Japanese popular cultural products in Hong Kong. 從八十年代到千禧年初期，香港社會一直深受日本流行文化影響。此後，日本流行文化的地位雖然受到「韓流」的衝擊，甚至被超越取代，但它對戰後香港社會的影響卻非常深遠。日本流行文化不但與香港本土文化發展息息相關，還在香港人的日常生活中扮演了重要的角色。儘管有不少先行研究曾探討過各種日本文化產物在香港傳播的情況，但暫時還沒有研究對日本流行文化在香港的傳入、傳播和消費，以及日本流行文化與香港本地文化的形塑作出系統而全面的分析。 本研究旨在以人類學的視角探究從七十年代到千禧年之間，日本流行文化與香港社會的文化建構關係。通過集中研究四種日本文化產物—電視劇、流行音樂、零售模式和食品與料理—在香港的傳播，本研究主要分析四組相關的議題：一）日本流行文化在香港的傳播、二）香港人在消費日本流行文化的行為和模式、三）日本流行文化對香港人日常生活的影響、四）日本流行文化與香港文化發展的關係。 不同於其他的先行研究，本研究不受文本或受眾經驗分析的侷限，嘗試釐清不同日本文化產物之間，輸出方社會和輸入方社會之間，以及生產者、中介者和消費者等角色之間的三組互動關係。通過進行文獻研究、文獻回顧、深度訪問及田野調查，我們希望探究日本流行文化在香港社會的特定脈絡下之性質及其影響。 本研究不但能加強我們對日本流行文化在香港的歷史和發展的理解，更重要的是，可以加深我們對香港本土文化的建構和組成的認知。要理解香港文化就必須研究香港文化和其他文化及社會的關係與互動，而這正是我們的研究所印證的觀點。同時，我們的研究會建立一個公開的資料庫，讓公眾可以有機會查閱有關日本流行文化在香港的資料。

17608517.label: Realisation of objectives
17608517.value: Overall speaking, the project objectives have been achieved to a large extent. However, we were not able to complete all the scheduled fieldwork and interviews in the last phase of our research due to the escalating political contention in Hong Kong in the summer of 2019. We will explain how each objective has been achieved. 1) We have traced and examined the different trajectories of the dissemination of Japanese television dramas, popular music, retail formats and food in Hong Kong. For the retail formats, we focused on reconstructing the history of the spread of Japanese general merchandise stores in Hong Kong. For Japanese food, we examined the proliferation of Japanese restaurants in general and the dissemination of Japanese ramen and sake in particular. We have also collected a substantial amount of historical materials including the old television listings and guides, trailers of Japanese television dramas, old local music magazines and newspaper clippings related to the Japanese popular cultural products in Hong Kong. 2) We have applied the ‘art world’ approach proposed by Howard Becker to analyse the process of the dissemination of Japanese popular culture in Hong Kong. We have identified the major actors constituting the ‘art worlds’ of the circulation of different Japanese cultural products in Hong Kong. We have examined the connection between the exporting and receiving sides and how the Japanese cultural products reached the hands of Hong Kong consumers. 3) We have found out that the mediations between Japanese cultural products and the local Hong Kong society were subject to not just cultural but also business logics. We have examined how the intermediaries in the spread of Japanese popular cultural products adjusted their business strategies and changed the form of their products to accommodate the cultural logic of the local people. For instance, we examined the localization of a Japanese restaurant chain s and itsthe introduction of the concept of ‘dining oriented bar’ in Hong Kong. We argue that the business practices of the intermediaries shaped and were shaped by the local cultural understanding of food. 4) We have identified the key actors in facilitating the spread of Japanese popular culture in Hong Kong. We have examined the functions and roles of both Japanese and local intermediaries and their interactions. For instance, we have studied the role of local agents in promoting Japanese popular music through local music magazines. We have also examined how the local agents interacted with the Japanese suppliers to introduce the Japanese general merchandise stores into Hong Kong. In addition, we have conducted in-depth interviews with Japanese seafood suppliers and Hong Kong sake brewers and several site visits. 5) We have found out that the spread of the different Japanese popular cultural products each constituted their own ‘art worlds’ characterised by specific conventions and mode of interactions. These ‘art worlds’, we have observed, were not separated from each other. Instead, they were connected with each other and shaped the ways how each of them were consumed by people of Hong Kong. For instance, the proliferation of Japanese television dramas and Japanese popular music went hand in hand and contributed to the consumption of Japanese idols in Hong Kong. On the other hand, the spread of Japanese supermarkets enabled the people Hong Kong to be familiar with Japanese food culture which in turn facilitated the rise of Japanese restaurants in the territory. 6 & 7) We have examined, through in-depth interviews with Hong Kong consumers, how Japanese popular cultural products were consumed for different purposes. We have found out that often cited ‘fondness of Japanese society and culture’ was an oversimplified explanation of the consumption of Japanese culture by the local consumers in Hong Kong. Instead, the consumption of Japanese culture was a strategy employed by the consumers to express their own values and identifies. We have studied the process of how local consumers appropriated different Japanese cultural products to express the newly formed middle class identity. The spread of Japanese popular culture, we would like to emphasize, has become an integral part of the formation of middle class in Hong Kong society. We would also like to discuss some of the limitations that we faced in the research and our attempts to overcome the problems. In terms of the research on the spread of Japanese food in Hong Kong, some major local regional operators refused to take part in the interviews due to the increasingly polarized political situation in the summer of 2019. We managed to collect and analyse the annual reports of the companies to gain a better understanding of their businesses. With regard to the research on Japanese retail formats, it was difficult for us to contact the Japanese suppliers as some of the Japanese general merchandise stores have already been out of business. We attempted to trace the spread of the Japanese stores by conducting in-depth interviews with former local employees. For the research on Japanese popular music, we did not have the access to Japanese singers. We focused on conducting interviews with local DJs, music magazine publishers, and pop music producers who have established strong personal ties with the Japanese personnel. Lastly, regarding the research on Japanese television dramas, we did not have the access to Japanese television broadcasters. We turned to local buyers and scriptwriters to reconstruct the history of the dissemination of Japanese TV dramas in Hong Kong.

17608517.label: Major findings and research outcome
17608517.value: There are three major findings of our research. First, we have clarified the process of the migration of Japanese popular culture from Japan to Hong Kong and reconstructed the cross-border industrial chains by identifying the key actors in exporting, importing and disseminating different Japanese popular cultural products in Hong Kong. We have also identified the major functions of the Japanese and local intermediaries and their relationships. Second, we have clarified the process of localization of Japanese popular culture in Hong Kong. We argue that cultural explanations alone cannot account for the ways Japanese popular culture were consumed by the people of Hong Kong. We have found out that commercial considerations, business regulations, and political circumstances all played an important role in shaping the behaviors of the intermediaries, which in turn shaped the consumption of Japanese popular culture. We have also found out that the consumption of Japanese popular culture was closely related to the class formation in Hong Kong. The popularity of Japanese popular culture products in Hong Kong cannot be understood simply as an argument for the prevalence of pro-Japanese sentiment in the Hong Kong society. Third, we have found out that the paths of the spread of the four Japanese popular cultural products in Hong Kong were different from but interconnected with each other. The implication is that we have to study Japanese popular cultural products as discrete parts in a wider network instead of a homogenous group or isolated phenomena. The last phase of our research was significantly affected by the series of protests and social movements as a number of scheduled interviews and fieldwork arrangements were cancelled. Despite the unexpected situation, we managed to conclude a book contract with Routledge. The tentative title of the book is Japanese Popular Culture in Hong Kong. We are working on the manuscript at the moment and we plan to deliver it to the publisher by the end of December 2020. We also plan to develop four monographs on the spread of each of the Japanese popular cultural items examined in the current project in Hong Kong: Japanese television dramas, Japanese popular music, Japanese retail formats and Japanese ramen.

17608517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17608517.value: During our research, we found out that the spread of Japanese popular culture in Hong Kong was not an isolated phenomenon, and it should be understood as part of the transnational flow of Japanese popular cultural products in the Greater China region. Hong Kong, as we discovered, was a key nexus in this multidirectional network. On the one hand, some Japanese popular cultural products arrived in Taiwan first and were then brought to Hong Kong; on the other hand, Hong Kong played a key role in the dissemination of Japanese popular culture in mainland China in the 1980s and 1990s. The implication is that we cannot regard the migration of Japanese popular culture to Hong Kong as a simple one-to-one relationship. It is thus important to study the interrelationship among the spread of Japanese popular culture in Hong Kong, mainland China and Taiwan. We are currently conducting another GRF project on Japanese popular culture in mainland China. We plan to submit a new GRF proposal to study the dissemination of Japanese popular culture in Taiwan to gain a comprehensive understanding of the mediation between the transnational flow of Japanese popular culture and the three local Chinese societies.

17608517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17608517.value: This research is an anthropological study of the spread of Japanese popular culture in Hong Kong (1970s–early 2000s). It highlights the importance of studying Japanese popular cultural products not just as texts but also as commodities. It identifies the key agents involved in and facilitating the flow of Japanese popular cultural products from Japan to Hong Kong and examines the context in which they formulated and implemented their business strategies. It also explains how the consumption of Japanese popular culture in Hong Kong has been shaped by a combination of cultural, economic and political conditions. The research contributes to the field of business anthropology of popular culture in general and the studies of globalization of Japanese popular culture in particular. First, it helps clarify the relationship between culture and commerce in the creative industries by examining the composition of the different ‘art worlds’ of Japanese popular culture in Hong Kong and the role of the intermediaries. Second, it enhances our understanding of the history of Japanese popular culture in Hong Kong by illustrating the different trajectories of the spread of Japanese television dramas, popular music, retail formats and food in Hong Kong and their interconnectedness.
