17608917.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17608917.value: 转型社会中的警权：从比较视野看中国

17608917.label: Project Objectives
17608917.value: To better understand the nature of the authoritarian legality, including its resilience and fragility, in a Communist Party state through a detailed examination of police power and police accountability; To examine the role of police in authoritarian states in transition and the evolving relationship between the Communist Party and the police at the macro and micro levels; To explore the possibility of regulating and limiting police powers through law and legal mechanisms, in particular prosecutorial supervision and judicial review, and the development and acceptance of legal accountability; To study the degree to which political and legal reform may affect the bureaucratic accountability of the police; and To place police power in China in the larger comparative context of democratic transition and police accountability, especially successful transition in the East Asian context.
rows: To better understand the nature of the authoritarian legality, including its resilience and fragility, in a Communist Party state through a detailed examination of police power and police accountability;
To examine the role of police in authoritarian states in transition and the evolving relationship between the Communist Party and the police at the macro and micro levels;

To explore the possibility of regulating and limiting police powers through law and legal mechanisms, in particular prosecutorial supervision and judicial review, and the development and acceptance of legal accountability;

To place police power in China in the larger comparative context of democratic transition and police accountability, especially successful transition in the East Asian context.

17608917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17608917.value: Midnight knock on the door is a primal fear for the Chinese - the fear of a dark and lawless society in which police detain, torture, or otherwise pray on vulnerable people. In the Chinese folk tradition, the police are, at best, a necessary evil to be guarded against. The Chinese Communist Party has reinforced the fear by making the police a dictatorial apparatus and then using it to exert cradle-to-grave control. To reform the political system, the police have to be changed, and a key aspect of legal reform in China in the past three decades or so has been to regulate and tame police power. With the social and economic transition, the Party cannot merely rely on repression to hold on to power and to govern an increasingly advanced and pluralistic society and economy. If rule of law is needed in China to develop the economy, to control local government, and to legitimize the Party rule, the police have to be legally accountability and subject to effective legal control. The Communist Party, while determined to continue to use the police as a repressive tool for political control, has also promoted a degree of legal accountability and professionalism within the police. While there is no doubt that political control remains a central aspect of police accountability, the Party has also relied on legal mechanisms to check and balance police power in areas that are not regarded as politically sensitive and are marginal to its political survival. This proposed research examines the effectiveness of legal control of police power in China's authoritarian system and the possibility to bring about an institutional and cultural change within the police. The focal point of the examination includes: 1) the relationship between the Communist Party and the police at the macro and micro levels; 2) judicial review of police power; 3) prosecutorial control of police discretion; and 4) the internal accountability mechanisms of the police. This research will be contextualized in a larger comparative perspective so that accountability of Chinese police will be studied in light of the experiences of jurisdictions with successful transition to democratic and legal accountability and those which are still in the process of transition. 半夜敲门是中国人具有的一种原始的恐惧 -- 一种对警察可以肆无忌惮的无序社会的恐惧。在中国的民间文化里，警察经常是一种必不可少的、但需加以防范的恶。共产党政权更是把警察当成一中专政工具，并通过警察对社会实施全方位的控制，因而强化了民众对警察的恐惧感。因此，中国的法律制度改革的过程也是一个规范和驯服警察权的过程。 随着中国的社会和经济的转型，共产党政权不能只依赖打压的方式去实施统治和管理一个进步的、多元的社会与经济。如果法治对发展经济，政府施政，和政权的合法性是有必要的，那么警察也必须对法律负责并接受法律的控制。对执政的共产党而言，警察必然是实现政治控制的暴力工具， 但警察的法律问责和警察的专业化也具有同样重要的意义。毫无疑问，警察的政治责任是警察问责制的核心，但法律机制也起到了越来越多的功能。 本项研究考察中国威权制度之下法律机制对警察权的控制，以及法律对警察机构和文化的产生变化的可能。研究的核心问题包括：1） 执政党对警察在宏观和微观层面的控制；2）对警察权的司法审查； 3）检察机关对警察裁量权的制约；4）警察权利规范的内部制约机制。 本研究从比较的视角去探讨中国警察的问责制，并通过分析其他转型社会的经验与教训来看中国警察问责制的可行性及其局限。

17608917.label: Realisation of objectives
17608917.value: This GRF project has yielded important findings on the police and policing in China’s authoritarian political system. Those findings are likely to enrich our understanding of authoritarian policing and contribute to the literature on the Chinese political system and comparative police studies. The basic theoretical frame to explain Chinese policing in transition and the significance of socialist legality is the dual state theory (DST), which offers a powerful analytical tool in making sense of the developments in the larger context of rule of law reforms in China since the late 1970s. The starting point is an essential understanding that China is a Party State that necessitates the monopoly of political power in the hands of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) and the monopoly over political power sets China sharply apart from liberal democracies. Under this system, in its original design, no institutional autonomy is possible and law is not an autonomous field that can be separated from the CCP dominated political process. In the final analysis, the legal system is an integral part of the larger political system, bearing the same political identity and sharing the same fundamental interests. In constitutional doctrines and real political practice, the police serve the CCP as its repressive arm. Under that framework, this research makes three key points. First, political control over the police force is thorough, direct, and absolute. The entire police system, from the minister in the Ministry of Public Security down to a community police officer on his beat, from investigating subversive offenses to settling family disputes, is equally subject to the Party control. This is a well-known and important premise. Second, a rule-of-law-like project has been developing in China for over 40 years with far-reaching consequences for social and economic activities and governance. A legal field has been growing and developing that has few transformative impacts on the police in terms of autonomous decision-making but has enhanced legal accountability. Legal rules are crowding out and replacing some of the political rules in police matters and have become consequential and effective in guiding the police in their exercise of power. Since legal rules are the common standard of reference for all stakeholders in the legal system in which the police are an integral part, the police themselves have to buy in and join a community of common legal discourses like judges, prosecutors, and lawyers. The legal system demands separate and granular accountability independent of political accountability. Because of the reliance on legal rules, police increasingly embrace their identity as a law enforcement agency diluting their political identity in some areas and pushing it to the background. Legality and legalism are now at the heart of police work as well, and the debate has shifted to how authoritarian it has become and the implications of that classification. Third, the “mass line” (群众路线) remains a core and indispensable part of Chinese police work. The police remain embedded in the communities in which they serve and control through the provision of law enforcement services. The “peoples’ will” (人民的意志) is a guiding principle in the Chinese constitutional doctrine of the “people’s democratic dictatorship” (人民民主专政) and, translating that doctrine to routine police work, it means service-oriented police, reliance on public support, and a unique design of popular accountability. Because of the trinity of demands, a key finding in this research is that, even under monopolistic control, the authoritarian police can be and should be properly pluralized to capture the nuance, diversity, and detail within the overarching authoritarian conceptual framework. The DST offers a useful tool to highlight and explain plural developments in policing. Under the DTS model, there are two parallel systems of policing under the CCP’s overarching leadership. There is a prerogative state in which authoritarian police preempt and remove political risks according to the Party’s imperatives while leaving conventional, i.e. non-political, matters to the regular legal rules of a normative state. As neo-authoritarianism advances, the Party moves to the front stage and becomes hands-on in managing politically sensitive affairs (PSA), leaving little room for legal rules and institutions. It has expanded and solidified the prerogative state to solve PSA through substantively extra-legal methods. This research has focused on Chinese political policing from historical and comparative perspectives, highlighting the dominance of the CCP’s political concerns and the irrelevance of legal rules while paying particular attention to the interactions between the prerogative state and the normative state. In the shadow of, but largely parallel to, the extra-legal regime, there is a normal police system, less politicized, reform-oriented, and semi-autonomous, which continues to evolve toward maturity and grow in institutionalization and sophistication by offering rules-based solutions to a wide range of social conflicts. The police, traditionally an arm of Party repression, are showing more deference to legal rules and the trial-centric legal process. This research has used the examples of changing evidentiary rules on police interrogation practices, judicial review of police decisions, and community accountability in serving at the intersection between the Party state and resilient society. How can we explain the coexistence of two parallel and potentially opposite polar norms, institutional designs, and practices? The prerogative state is necessary for the maintenance of order and stability in the normative state, and without the extra-legal power of the Party in the background, and increasingly in the forefront, any legal normalcy that people desire and the market demands will collapse. There has always been a siege mentality in China’s party-state, and it has been gaining new momentum in recent years. Indeed, the Party’s de facto sovereign power is accustomed to keeping its challengers, real or imagined, at bay, thus maintaining China’s political stability. The Party creates and sustains a normal legal system for good governance. While there may be little, if any, moral commitment to rule of law, in particular the use of law to curb arbitrary power, a well-functioning police system renders credibility to the otherwise undemocratic and more than the occasionally repressive system. This research confirms that, while the Party has been expanding and consolidating the prerogative state, it has also recognized, and to a significant degree demanded, a normal police system that is well-functioning, disciplined, legitimate, and rules-based, full of Chinese characteristics, of course. A symbiotic relationship thus exists in the development of Chinese police between the normalcy and its exception, with each depending on the other for its existence. But the balance remains uncertain and fragile.

17608917.label: Major findings and research outcome
17608917.value: The starting point is an essential understanding that China remains a Party State that necessitates the monopoly of political power in the hands of the Chinese Communist Party. Under that system, no institutional autonomy is possible and law is not an autonomous field that can be separated from the CCP-dominated political process. In the final analysis, the legal system is an integral part of the larger political system, bearing the same political identity and sharing the common interest. This research makes three key findings. 1) the Party control over the police is thorough, direct, and absolute, but the control is more subtle and nuanced; 2) a rule-of-law-like project has been developing in China with far-reaching consequences in social and economic activities and in governance. A legal field has been developing that has had few little transformative impacts on police in terms of autonomous decision-making but is likely to enhance the legality and legal accountability of police work; and 3) the mass-line remains a core and indispensable part of Chinese police work. The police remain embedded in the communities in which they control. In this research I have covered four topical issues relating to political policing: 1) a comparative study of protest policing in mainland China, Hong Kong, Taiwan, and other jurisdictions; 2) the return of political policing in Hong Kong in the National Security Law context; 3) policing human rights lawyers in China; and 4) the evolvement of legal regulation of police power in China. All publication outputs, as listed below, focus on the Chinese police and political policing in particular from historical and comparative perspectives, highlighting the dominance of CCP’s political concerns and the place of legal rules, while paying particular attention to the interaction and the mutual impact between the prerogative state and the normative state. In the shadow of, but largely parallel to, prerogative state using police as an instrument, there is a normative, regularized police system, less politicized, reform-oriented, and more rule-based, which continues to evolve toward maturity and grow in institutionalization. The police are showing more deference to legal rules and a court-centric legal process, in which regular issues of rights in the criminal process can be contested and adjudicated. I continue to write on the prospect of legal/judicial control of police power from a large comparative perspective.

17608917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17608917.value: China has created and sustained a normal policing system to improve governance. It has grown more professionalized, institutionalized, and rule-bound. Legality, coupled with legal accountability, is likely to play a meaningful role in reining police power. At the same time, the Party has become sharp and decisive in carving out an area out of the legal system for enhanced or even exclusive political control. The Party has been consolidating the prerogative state while recognizing and even demanding an institutionalized normative state with a police force that is well-functioning, legitimate in the eyes of the public, and rule-based. A symbiotic relationship thus exists between the spheres, contradictory yet mutually reinforcing, offers opportunities for further research. The danger is that the normative legal system in China is not autonomous, and exists largely, if not principally, to serve particular instrumental values. If the law is simply another tool that the Party uses to govern, the duality that is conceptualized could be a superficial distinction that is bound to collapse. There is a delicate and fragile balance to strike between the political imperatives and the demand for a legal system, and the demarcation between the two systems is fluid and uncertain. This project highlights this ultimate risk for further research.

17608917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17608917.value: Under the Chinese political system, the leadership of the Communist Party is absolute. The institutional autonomy of the police in decision-making and law enforcement is therefore limited, and the legal system, in general, is not regarded as an autonomous field that can be separated from politics. In the final analysis, the police system is an integral part of the larger political system and serves to maintain that political order. At the same time, the Party has promoted legality in the police work and promoted legal rights in the criminal process, offering legal remedies against abuse of power in ordinary criminal cases that are not politically sensitive. In a range of cases, legal rules have become consequential and effective in reducing the arbitrariness in police work. Since legal rules are the common standard of reference by all stakeholders in the legal system in which the police are an integral part, the police have to participate in the community of common legal discourses with judges, prosecutors, and lawyers. Because of the reliance on legal rules, police have increasingly embraced their identity as a law enforcement agency, which may somehow dilute the political identity in police practices. The two co-existing spheres of policing, sometimes contradictory but mostly mutually reinforcing, are fertile ground for further research to examine the resilience of the system.

17609117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17609117.value: 研究表明眼球運動可以反映潛在認知過程，所以眼球運動已經被廣泛地用於一系列不同學科的人類行爲研究。之前關於眼球運動模式的研究都集中在檢測在不同條件下的群體行爲。然而，最近的研究發現認知任務中眼球運動模式存在大量個體差異。這些不同的眼球運動模式顯示了不同的認知過程，而這些認知過程反過來可能導致不同的任務表現。所以，瞭解個體差異與任務表現的關係會對提高大衆以及臨床人群的表現有重要啓示。 然而，現有的分析眼球運動數據的方法并不能反映個體差異。而且，這些方法主要集中在注視點位置，卻忽略了不同注視區域之間的轉換信息。爲了解決這些問題，我們最近提出了用隱馬爾科夫模型（一種機器學習的時間序列模型）以分析眼球運動數據。包括個體化的興趣區和興趣區之間的轉換信息的每個個體的眼球運動模式可以被總結為一個隱馬爾科夫模型。多個個體眼動模型可以被區分成兩種或多種的常見眼動模式，而且每個個體與常見眼動模式之間的差異可以被定量化地評估。我們已經成功地運用此方法挖掘到了現有方法不能揭示的關於人臉識別記憶新發現，包括發現與更佳的人臉識別表現所關聯的眼球運動模式，以及同通過功能性核磁共振檢測發現的這些模式的神經關聯區域。 在此我們一方面致力於開發針對其他人臉識別任務的此類方法，另一方面致力於更加深入的研究眼球運動與人臉識別記憶表現的關係。我們首先會將此方法運用到兩個具有重要現實意義的開發中：人臉配對和人臉表情識別。我們會開發一個包括在每個注視點被感知的圖像内容在内的新模型來更好地捕捉參與者在任務中所使用的信息。這個新模型可以讓我們以後把在具有不同特點結構的刺激物的任務中的眼球運動建模，例如場景感知和網頁瀏覽。 爲了探究眼球運動的變化是否能提高人臉識別記憶，我們會根據隱馬爾科夫模型分析結果來訓練參與者採用與最佳表現關聯的眼球運動模式。該探究會對提高人類和電腦在人臉識別中的表現有重要指導意義。 最近的研究表明情感狀態能影響人臉處理方式。由於我們之前的研究已經揭示了眼球運動模式和人臉識別表現之間的關聯，參與者的情感狀態可能會改變眼球運動模式，而此種改變可能會影響識別表現。探究此聯係會加深我們對於情感狀態是如何影響眼動模式和人臉識別表現的理解， 而這種理解在目前的文獻中都被忽略了。 此研究極具開創性和跨學科性。它將會闡明眼動模式和在人臉識別任務中表現的關係。研究結果將會對於通過眼動數據分析來提高認知任務中的表現以及認知缺陷的早期發現有重要啓示。本研究提出的方法論將會對不同學科的研究人員如何運用眼球運動來瞭解認知行爲有深遠和持續的影響。

17609117.label: Realisation of objectives
17609117.value: Objective 1: To use our HMM-based approach for eye movement data analysis to examine the association between eye movements and performance in recognition tasks that have important real-life implications such as face matching and facial expression judgments. This objective has been 100% achieved. We have used our HMM-based approach (now being referred to as Eye Movement analysis with Hidden Markov Models, EMHMM) to examine the association between eye movement patterns and performance in face recognition, face matching, and facial expression judgment tasks. Objective 2: To develop a new model that includes perceived image content to better capture what information participants use in recognition tasks. This objective has been 100% achieved. However, we found the model did not work as well as expected. Thus, instead of using this method, we have developed a new method called EMHMM with co-clustering. In this method, instead of summarizing eye movements when viewing different images into one HMM as in the original EMHMM method, we use one HMM to summarize eye movements during viewing each image, and then use the data mining algorithm co-clustering to discover participants groups within each of which group members exhibited similar eye movement patterns to one another across images. This method is particularly useful for tasks involving stimuli with different feature layouts such as scene perception. Objective 3: To investigate whether we can train participants to use eye movement strategies that lead to better performances in face recognition. This objective has been 100% achieved. We found no significant improvement in recognition performance when training adult participants. This finding is consistent with other similar studies in the literature. Some have argued that due to our expertise in face processing, adults may have reached their capacity limit for face recognition and thus their performance could not be further improved through training. In contrast, we speculate that this phenomenon may be because adults already developed a stable visual routine for viewing faces, and thus their eye movement strategies are difficult to change through short-term training. We have planned follow-up studies to examine training effects on children instead, since their eye movement patterns may be more malleable to change. Objective 4: To investigate the modulation of affective state on eye movement patterns and performance in face recognition. This objective has been 100% achieved. We found that affective state modulated eye movement pattern slightly, and the change was insufficient to change recognition performance.

17609117.label: Major findings and research outcome
17609117.value: Face processing: Affective state modulated eye movement pattern slightly, and the change was insufficient to change recognition performance (An & Hsiao, 2021) Flexibility in adjusting eye movement strategy when viewing neutral vs. angry faces predicts one’s social anxiety symptoms (Chan, Barry et al., 2020) Individuals with more negative interpretation of illness-related scenarios engaged a more nose-focused eye movement pattern when passively viewing faces (Chan, Suen et al., 2020) Eyes-focused eye movement pattern is associated with better performance in both face recognition and face matching tasks. Artists' advantage in face processing is specific to tasks similar to their drawing experience such as face matching but not face recognition (Hsiao, An et al., 2021). Adults’ face recognition performance did not improve through short-term training, and this may be related to well-developed visual routines that are inflexible to change (Hsiao, An & Chan, 2020). Development of EMHMM and applications: We have developed Eye Movement analysis with Switching Hidden Markov Models (EMSHMM) to to model both participants’ cognitive state and eye movement transitions, we discovered two major decision-making styles: one reveals earlier but weaker preference looking behaviour and thus the decision can be inferred earlier, whereas the other reveals later but stronger preference, leading to higher decision inference accuracy prior to the decision (Chuk et al., 2020) Using eye tracking and EMHMM with co-clustering, we resolved a puzzle in the visual search literature that while both orientation contrast and collinearity increase target salience, a combination of the two counterintuitively masks a local target (i.e., collinear masking effect). We showed that this masking effect could be predicted by eye movement consistency before the search display, suggesting that it is related to attention shift away from a saccadic goal in expectation of the search display (Hsiao, Chan et al., 2021). We have developed a Variational Bayesian method to cluster hidden Markov models (Lan et al., 2021). When learning from audio lessons with videos of relevant images, adopting a more centralized eye movement pattern was associated with better comprehension since viewers could better concentrate on the audio lesson content and less distracted by irrelevant video features (Zheng et al., 2022) In sentence reading, music reading experience modulates eye movement pattern in English reading but not in Chinese reading due to higher similarity in perceptual demands on processing sequential symbol strings separated by spaces between music notation and English sentence reading (Liao et al., 2022)

17609117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17609117.value: In Objective 3, we found that eye movement training did not work well on adults: participants who received training did not perform significantly better than those who did not receive training in the post-training test. We speculate that this phenomenon is because adults have developed a stable visual routine that is difficult to change through short-term eye movement strategy training. Indeed, in another study, we found that adults’ eye movement patterns had higher consistency (lower entropy) across trials than children, suggesting that children may not have developed a visual routine as stable as adults’. Thus, we plan to examine whether eye movement strategy training will work better on children since their eye movement pattern may be more malleable to change.

17609117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17609117.value: Using a machine-based approach EMHMM to analyze eye movement data, we discovered two representative eye movement patterns in face recognition in adults: nose-focused and eyes-focused patterns. The eyes-focused pattern is associated with better performance. Across face processing tasks (including face recognition, passive viewing, face matching, facial expression recognition, etc.), individuals have person-specific and task-specific eye movement patterns unaffected by real-time mood changes. There is limited facilitation effect of drawing training on face recognition, and artists' advantage in face processing is specific to tasks similar to their drawing experience such as face matching but not face recognition. We have also developed new EMHMM methods: (1) EMSHMM, in which we use switching HMM to model both participants’ cognitive state and eye movement transitions. Applying it to decision making led to the discovery of two different decision-making style among individuals. (2) EMHMM with co-clustering, which allows us to discover participant groups where group members shared similar eye movement patterns to each other across stimuli with different feature layouts. Applying it to scene perception led to the discovery that individuals who focus on the foreground object had better selective attention, whereas those switching between the foreground and the background had better scene memory.

17609417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17609417.value: Stroke is a devastating illness that induces numerous impairments of body function and structure, and limitations to activities in all aspects of life. With an improved survival rate following stroke and increasing number of young and pre-elderly stroke survivors (<65 years old), maintaining total well-being becomes a pressing aim in stroke rehabilitation. To help younger stroke survivors cope with the multifaceted concerns during rehabilitation, there is a need for holistic intervention program targeting bio-psycho-social-spiritual aspects as adjuvant to conventional physical and occupational rehabilitation regimens to buffer against mental health issues, reduce psychosocial stress, resume social connections, and reinstall hope. Among the non-pharmacology approaches, expressive arts-based intervention has become increasingly popular due to its engaging, safe and joyful nature. However, systematic research on its effectiveness on different dimensions of life during stoke rehabilitation has yet to be conducted. Expressive arts-based intervention utilizes multiple arts modalities to facilitate the process of reflecting and responding to human sufferings. Such variety multiplies the avenues by which participant in therapy may seek meaning, clarity, insight and healing. Adopting a 2-arm randomized controlled trial design, this study investigates the short (post-intervention) and longer-term (up to 6 months) effects of an 8-week Expressive Arts-based Intervention for younger and pre-elderly Chinese stroke survivors compared to treatment-as-usual controls on depressive and anxiety symptoms, stress, perceived social support, hope, subjective and spiritual well-being, stroke-related and general quality of life, and on stress biomarker of salivary cortisol. The study will also examine the associations between cortisol patterns and psycho-social-spiritual variables in younger stroke survivors, and the changes of such associations across time points. 154 Chinese adults aged between 18 and 64 with ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke will be recruited and randomized into (i) Expressive Arts-based Intervention group, or (ii) Treatment-as-usual control group. Participants will be assessed on 3 time points: baseline prior to randomization, post-intervention, and 6-month post-intervention. Recruitments will be done in collaboration with Community Rehabilitation Network, Hong Kong Society for Rehabilitation, and Department of Rehabilitation Sciences, the Hong Kong Polytechnic University. The present study contributes to existing knowledge of the effectiveness of an expressive arts-based rehabilitation program on younger stroke survivors. Findings will help stroke survivors and healthcare professionals make better choices in selecting practices that will yield maximum benefits, satisfaction, adherence, and sustainability. This study will also offer better understanding on the associations among psycho-physical-social-spiritual factors in younger stroke survivors, so as to help develop better holistic clinical practices. 中風是一種會造成多種不同程度的肢體傷殘及影響個人日常生活的嚴重疾病。隨著存活率的提高，以及年輕中風患者 (45歲或以下) 及 老年前復康者(46-64歲)人數的增長，令如何幫助中風患者在復康過程中感到整全的身心健康，成為中風復康服務的主要目的。一套以整全健康為本的輔助模式，能有效幫助年輕患者面對因中風而遇到的各種身體、心理、社交及靈性層面上的挑戰。整全的介入模式輔以現行的各種職業治療對患者的精神健康有保護性的作用，亦可減緩身心社交層面的壓力、增強個人的社交網絡，能讓患者重燃生活中的希望感。近年來，表達藝治療 (其中一種非藥物治療手法) 的臨床應用日益普遍；在治療過程加入表達藝術的元素，能夠為患者提供一個安全而有趣的治療環境，從而令患者更投入治療過程中。雖然表達藝術治療的應用日趨普及，但表達藝術介入在不同階段的中風康復過程中所擔當的角色仍有待作深入探討。表達藝術治療就是透過不同類別的藝術元素引導患者反思及面對個人所遇到的困境，讓參加者以多方面的角度重整生命的意義、看待及反思自身的生活遭遇，從而達至治療的功用。 此計劃採用隨機對照實驗的研究方式，透過與「對照組」比較，探討一個為期八星期，為年輕中風患者及老年前的中風患者而設的表達藝術介入手法對參加者的抑鬱及焦慮情緒、壓力、社交支援、希望感及靈性健康層面等方面的短期 (參加小組後) 及長期成效(參加小組後六個月)。研究亦會探討參加者的唾液皮質醇與其各種身心靈健康指標的關係及其改變。 研究對象為 154 名 18-64 歲的出血性或缺血性中風復康者。合資格的參加者將會被隨機分配到「表達藝術介入小組」或「對照組」。所有的參加者會分別在計劃的前期、八星期後、及後續的六個月後進行評估。研究計劃將會與香港復康會社區復康網絡及香港理工大學聯手進行。 此項研究將會讓我們更理解表達藝術介入手法對年輕中風患者的好處。研究結果將有助中風患者及前線員工更了解年輕患者的身心靈健康，亦為前線員工及患者提供一個擁有最徍效度、易於投入、及有持續性果效的復康計劃，從而推動全人健康模式的應用與實踐。

17609417.label: Realisation of objectives
17609417.value: The primary and secondary objectives of this study were all achieved. We conducted a 2-arm randomized controlled trial on 181 Chinese young and pre-elderly stroke survivors. In this RCT, we examined the physio-psychosocial-spiritual effects of Expressive arts-based intervention on young and pre-elderly stroke survivors compared to a waitlist control group. Participants were assessed through a self-administered questionnaire on the level of hope, stress, depression, anxiety, self-esteem, social support, spiritual wellbeing, and stroke-specific and general quality of life, as well as biomarkers measures of salivary cortisol. Please refer to the finding section (6.1) and the research outputs (sections 8 & 9) for details of the published study protocol and academic journal manuscripts and those under review. To achieve the primary and secondary objectives of the study, we proposed to recruit 154 stroke survivors who experienced a stroke within 12 months, modified Rankin Scale level 2 to 3, and without a prior or current diagnosis of major medical or psychiatric disorders other than stroke. However, the team experienced challenges in recruiting eligible participants as the study period overlapped with the social unrest in 2019 and the COVID-19 pandemic (since 2020). The team remedied the situation by immediately lining up with the HKU stroke team to recruit eligible participants from major hospitals, like Queen Mary Hospital, Tung Wah Hospital, and Ruttonjee Hospital. The study also recruited participants from the Hong Kong Stroke Association, which is the largest patient self-help group of stroke patients in Hong Kong, and different rehabilitation or community centers run by different NGOs. In order to recruit more participants, the inclusion criteria were also relaxed after careful consideration of whether the adjusted criteria will impact the study rigors and outcomes. First, since the focus of the study is more on the psychosocial sides rather than physical functioning, participants who had a stroke longer than 5 years could benefit from the program. The time-lapse from the latest stroke event was thus adjusted from within 5 years to within 20 years to allow more participants to join. Second, distress and depressive symptoms are not uncommon in stroke survivors due to the drastic changes in their lives and families. Many stroke survivors seek help from medical practitioners and thus receive a clinical diagnosis. The study originally excluded stroke survivors with a clinical diagnosis of major medical or psychiatric disorder; it was then changed to only exclude those with a clinical diagnosis of major medical or severe psychiatric disorders (i.e., schizophrenia). Survivors with depression and depressive symptoms could join if they were in a stable condition, e.g., stable doses of medication and regular follow-up with out-patient clinics. We also conducted an intake session for all participants to ensure they were suitable and eligible for the study. At the end of the study, 181 eligible participants were finally recruited and completed the baseline assessment, which exceeded the calculated sample size of 154. In the proposal, we assumed there was an attrition rate of 25% and at the end of the study, a total of 28 participants dropped out, which is equivalent to 15.5% attrition. The reasons for drop-out included passing away, hospitalization, and personal reasons. During the study, many participants mentioned their altered body perception. Being aware of this and also the quantitative focus of the study, the research team also looked into the qualitative part of this study, in particular, participants' views related to embodiment and body perception, which is important for the rehabilitation of the stroke survivors. A subset of participants was then invited for individual interviews to explore their lived experiences of living with the post-stroke bodies. Their changes in body perception after participating in the Expressive arts-based intervention were also investigated by semi-structured interview supplemented with a drawing task. It was really a hard time for the study during the pandemic period. The intervention was suspended due to social isolation policy and health concerns during the major waves of the pandemic. Nevertheless, participants were eager to join the study between the pandemic waves. Our researchers also reached out to individual participants to collect follow-up data. Grateful for giving the permission to extend the project for 6 months, this study could finally be completed with all objectives well-achieved. Please refer to the finding section (6.1) for a summary of the main findings. This study yielded 8 academic journal manuscripts, although some of them are still under review (the pandemic situation also leads to an extra length of the journal review process). The study protocol of this study was published [8.2]. Two systematic reviews were conducted to synthesize the existing literature on the effectiveness of different arts-based interventions on stroke survivors [8.1] and their embodied experiences [8.6]. The participants' lived experiences with the post-stroke bodies were investigated [8.4]. The psychometric properties of the 12-item Stroke-specific quality of life scale [8.3] and the indirect effects of social support and hope on quality of life via emotional distress [8.5] were also examined. The manuscripts on the main findings of the study [8.8] and a study about the changes in body perception after participating in the Expressive arts-based intervention [8.7] were also prepared. In total, 11 conference abstracts were also generated based on the preliminary findings of the above topics and accepted for presentation at international conferences (section 9).

17609417.label: Major findings and research outcome
17609417.value: Primary objective: Results from this study indicated specific short- and long-term benefits of EABI on stroke survivors in several domains of their bio-psycho-social-spiritual wellbeing compared to the control group, which did not differ at baseline in the demographic characteristics, psychosocial measures, and cortisol levels. In more detail, from T0 to T1, EABI exhibited significant short-term intervention effects on hope and self-esteem. From T0 to T2, significant long-term intervention effects for EABI on stroke-specific physical QoL, physical QoL, and wake-up cortisol were found. Besides, the EABI group displayed significant and positive changes in most outcome variables across the study. The EABI benefited both the hemorrhagic and ischemic stroke survivors. Hemorrhagic stroke survivors experienced significant short-term intervention effects on perceived social support, perceived stress, and significant long-term improvement in functional impairment. Ischemic stroke survivors experienced a significant short-term improvement in hope and a positive long-term effect on SF12 physical QoL. Findings of the primary objective were documented in the manuscript [8.8]. Secondary objective: The secondary objective attempted to explore the associations between the psychosocial and physiological variables and their changes across the study. At T0, steeper diurnal cortisol slopes were significantly correlated with a higher degree of functional impairment and stroke-specific psychological QoL. At T1, higher depressive symptoms correlated with higher levels of wake-up cortisol and steeper diurnal cortisol slopes. At T2, wake-up cortisol was significantly associated with higher levels of hope and generic mental QoL. Steeper diurnal cortisol slopes were significantly correlated with higher levels of hope, generic physical QoL, and generic mental QoL. Significant long-term intervention effects were observed on the wake-up cortisol level. These results were documented in publication [8.8]. Besides, Hope was found to play a mediating role in the relationship between social support and QoL and had a stronger protective effect on perceived stress in survivors with greater functional impairment [8.5]. In sum, findings indicated that the psychosocial well-being of stroke survivors is strongly related to their cortisol level and HPA-axis functioning. Since cortisol and HPA-axis functioning could have profound impacts on the health condition of a person, i.e. immunity and endocrinology, this study calls for special attention to the psychosocial health of stroke survivors. In addition, this study also looked into the changes in the subjective perception of the body in stroke survivors after participating in EABI. Findings indicated that EABI could help participants re-establish a positive body perception, thereby also helping promote psychosocial wellbeing among survivors [8.7].

17609417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17609417.value: This is the first study to examine the bio-psycho-social-spiritual effects of EABI on stroke survivors. Findings suggested that EABI produced short-term and long-term effects in the intervention group compared to the control group. We also observed the long-term intervention effects on physical-related QoL. Given the special attention to the recovery of physical functioning in stroke survivors, further study should include assessments of motor functions to elucidate the effects of EABI on physical functionings. The findings suggest that EABI could alleviate stroke survivors' blunted diurnal cortisol pattern which is related to the HPA-axis functioning. Further studies could investigate the potential mechanisms underlying the physiological effects of EABI. Besides, most participants in this study experienced stroke within five years. The dataset did not have sufficient samples for conducting subgroup analysis. Further studies can examine the effects of EABI on long-term stroke survivors. This study focused primarily on quantitative measures. Qualitative measures can shed light on the process and mechanism of EABI. The comparative effectiveness of EABI on stroke survivors with other interventions is worthy of investigation. Further applications of EABI to other populations, particularly those with physical impairment e.g. Parkinson's disease, which are at risk of experiencing psychosocial difficulties, are also recommended.

17609417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17609417.value: This study investigated the holistic (bio-psycho-social-spiritual) effects of an Expressive arts-based intervention (EABI), an intervention that adopts multiple art modalities, on adult stroke survivors. The results showed significant short-term improvements in the level of hope and self-esteem, and long-term improvements in the physical domain of quality of life and wake-up cortisol in the intervention group compared to the control group. Hope was found to play a mediating role in the relationship between social support and QoL and had a stronger protective effect on perceived stress in survivors with greater functional impairment. Besides, the intervention benefited different stroke survivors regardless of the type of stroke the survivors had experienced. Findings also indicated that salivary cortisol level and diurnal cortisol slope were associated with different psychosocial measurements in stroke survivors. This study also examined the 12-item stroke-specific QoL. Results indicated its suitability for Chinese stroke survivors. The survivors also reported that their bondings with their bodies was disrupted after stroke. However, these body perceptions could be changed and the bonding could be restored by EABI. EABI impacts holistic wellbeing. It can be recommended to supplement the existing rehabilitation services for providing holistic support to stroke survivors, particularly psychosocial support.

17609517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17609517.value: Music and science, especially the scientific study of human beings, are closely intertwined by metaphors borrowed from each other. The bodies of musical instruments, for example, have served as powerful analogies in understanding human beings. In 19th-century life sciences, mechanical instruments emerged as a new illustrative conceptual image of the human nervous system. For example, nerves are compared with the keyboard and damper pedal of a piano, and the relationship between the mind and the brain with that of a melody and a music box. These body metaphors reveal not only constitutional similarities but conceptual features common to both domains. They function as “shorthand theories,” disclosing different epistemological understandings of music and human beings. The significance of these metaphors extends beyond the physical form to a wider sense of the body as matter or concrete object, which is linked intricately to the question of force. The body exerts force and force is exerted on the body. Who or what is the agency setting the body, nerves, or mind into motion in modern scientific conceptualizations? This brings us from investigation of musical metaphors in scientific literatures to that of scientific metaphors in musical literatures. Here, force is the most prominent metaphor and that which embraces most comprehensively the scientific conceptual images occurring in contemporaneous music-theoretical discourse. As physical force causes motion, feeling engenders musical motion. Music is often described within this discourse as has having “life-force” or “kinetic/potential energy.” The body-force pair underlies apprehensions of music and runs as a leitmotiv throughout various intertwined contexts in history. Notions of body and force enclose multiple layers of ideological frameworks, and it is precisely this trait that enables conceptualization of music in diverse terms. The two may suggest mechanical and physical contexts combined as “Body and Force”; at other times, “Body vs. Force” may indicate countering frames of reference such as physical/mechanical vs. metaphysical/ organic. This project investigates notions of music represented through the metaphoric lenses of body and force in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. The implications of these metaphors are examined in four divergent contexts: (i) music theories and psychological theories dealing with the procedural modeling of music perception and cognition in the listener’s mind, (ii) pedagogical theories on the mechanism of the performer’s body, (iii) selected theories of musical rhythm, and (iv) aesthetical discussion of the power of music. 音樂和科學緊密相連，這種聯繫尤其能在有關人類的科學研究中體現，因為我們能從兩者中看到大量互通的類比。例如，學者常用樂器的構造類比人體的構造。在19世紀的生命科學中，包括樂器在內的各式機械儀器逐漸成為學者用來類比解釋人體神經系統的新語言，比如鍵盤以及弱音踏板會被用來類比神經，又比如心智和大腦的關係可以用旋律以及音樂盒來類比。這些形象的類比不僅使我們看到兩者間的物理共性，更揭示了其概念認知上的共性。 這些類比發展到後來已經超出了事物本身的具體形象和性質，變成一個更加宏觀的問題，就像物體之間力的相互作用關係，同樣一個力，我們既可以理解成物體向外施力，也可以理解成力作用於物體。在當今的科學理念中，到底什麼才是這個力的施加主體，使得物體，神經以及心智這些概念都能進入到科學研究的理念中？鑒於這個問題，我們必須從審視科學文獻中用音樂作類比的情況轉到審視音樂文獻中用科學作類比的情況，惟其如此才能一窺究竟。在當今音樂理論的文獻語境中，力作為科學理念形象最重要的類比，出現在了絕大部分的研究領域中。正如在物理學中力的施加能使物體產生運動，情感作為一種力也能在音樂中產生運動。正因為如此，音樂通常被描述成「生命之力」或「運動能量」。 利用「物體與力」的概念去理解音樂與科學之間的關係已經成為一個重要途徑，其概念包含了多層意識形態的理念，正是這一特徵使之成為音樂多重角度概念化的基礎。「物體與力」既可以指將機械和物理的結合，亦可表示彼此對立的參考框架，如物理/機械與形而上學/有機的對比。 本研究旨在探討19世紀晚期到20世紀早期音樂概念中的「物體與力」的類比，並從四個不同領域的文獻去理解該類比的含義：1)有關音樂感知及聽者認知的音樂理論以及心理學理論；2) 演奏者肢體動作原理的教育學理論；3) 音樂節奏的理論；4) 音樂力量的美學討論。

17609517.label: Realisation of objectives
17609517.value: I am grateful that I was able to achieve the four objectives stated above in conducting the research project “Body and Force in Music.” The research outcome most immediately arisen from this project is my monograph with the title of Body and Force in Music: Metaphoric Constructions in Music Psychology (Routledge). The book is to be published as a part of SEMPRE Studies in the Psychology of Music series. In this monograph I examine the two central conceptual metaphors underling musical understanding: the body-force pair. This pair runs like a leitmotiv throughout various intertwined contexts in history. Both body and force enclose multiple layers of ideological frameworks, and precisely this trait enables the conceptualization of music in diverse terms. This book investigates the implications of body and force metaphors in various studies that can be collectively designated as early music psychology. Its discursive space consists of a multifaceted web of neighboring disciplines. Instead of imposing current disciplinary perspectives on early music psychology, which is much more complex, the present book takes the complicated and even problematic context of early music psychology into consideration. It examines a field of which “disciplinary identity” was being constructed in relation to these scholarly discourses in acoustics, anatomy, physiology, psychology, aesthetics, the human body studies, music pedagogy, and music theory in speculative, practical, and analytical traditions. In doing so, I was able to achieve the objectives of current research objectives, in particular, to examine the metaphoric constructions of a broader discursive space in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, including music-theoretical and psychological discourses. The book discusses the metaphors of body and force in various contexts, including musicking body machine and rhythm as activity, singing and tracing voice, motion and force in piano playing, minding gaps and musical energy, and force at distance. In addition to such a broader discussion, I developed a more focused journal article on the topic of “Music Psychology of the Piano-Playing Hands in Historical Discourse” and published it in Journal of Musicology, one of the leading journals in the field (University of California Press). This study begins with the idea that music-making hands have drawn considerable scholarly attention, featuring prominently in recent investigations in biomechanics, paleoanthropology, and cognitive sciences. Yet already in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, piano pedagogy theories were evolving not only in response to changing musical styles but also to scientific conceptualizations of the human body. Taking piano-playing hands as a platform for human/machine interaction, this article analyzes the historical discourse on piano-playing hands in relation to the contemporary scientific context and via the framework of cognitive science. In this process, these scientific and pedagogical writings that have been previously discussed only dispersedly and marginally emerge more than didactic instruction. This historical discourse on music psychology of piano-playing hands points to music cognition that is extended beyond the body, situated in activity, and distributed beyond the individual. With this more focused article, I was able to achieve the third and fourth objectives of examining body metaphor in the past and present conceptualizations and the significance of materiality in both historical and modern scholarship. The initial plan was to develop a single monograph, but I worked on this journal article, following the suggestion from one of the external reviewers, to whom I am grateful. In addition to the two publications, I developed more research outcomes in the form of conference papers and invited lecture. In these works, I tried make connections between the historical pedagogy and the recent scholarship in cognitive sciences, particularly via the notion of the 4E cognition (embodied, embedded, extended, enacted). I will pursue this line of inquiry in the future both theoretically and empirically.

17609517.value: Two publications have been immediately arisen from the project (See Part C, Number 8): 1) A monograph, with the title of “Body and Force in Music: Metaphoric Constructions in Music Psychology” As can be seen from the title of the book, this is the outcome most directly emerged from the current research project. I am pleased to report that the book will be published by Routledge as a part of SEMPRE Studies in the Psychology of Music series (Series editors: Graham Welch, Adam Ockelford, and Ian Cross). 2) A journal article, “Music Psychology of the Piano-Playing Hands in Historical Discourse.” Journal of Musicology 38, no. 1 (2021 forthcoming). Whereas the book covers a broader discursive space of body and force in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, I was also able to write an article focusing a more concrete case of music psychology of piano -playing and publish it in a leading journal of the field, Journal of Musicology. The final page proof pdf file is attached. In addition to the above two direct outcomes, I was able to produce two conference papers presented at international conferences and deliver an invited lecture at Edinburgh University (see Part C, Number 9). While conducting an individual research on analyzing and investigating the metaphors of body and force in the historical discourse, I also probed into the critical conceptual analysis of the present studies on the musicking bodies. In order to the significance of the body in the modern scholarship (research objective #4), I collaborated with researchers in the fields of neuroscience and psychology and participated in a few studies on the topics of music score reading and rhythm perception. I am pleased to report that these co-authored articles appeared in Scientific Reports and PLOS One (see Part C, Number 11).

17609517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17609517.value: Our account of music is inherently metaphorical, and metaphoricity pervades all sorts of musical discourses, be they theoretical, analytical, philosophical, pedagogical, or even scientific. The notions of “body” and “force” are the two most prominent and comprehensive scientific metaphors in musical discourse. Throughout various intertwined contexts in history, the body–force pair manifests multiple layers of ideological frameworks and enables the conceptualization of music in diverse terms. This research project investigates the concepts of body and force in the emerging field of music psychology in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. The discursive space of the field embraces divergent contexts, including theories of auditory perception and cognition in psychology, pedagogical theories on the mechanism of the performer’s body, speculative and practical theories of musical rhythm, and aesthetical discussion of the power of music. This study of body and force aims not only to illuminate the past scene of music psychology but also to shed light on the notions of music that are being constructed at present.

17609617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17609617.value: BACKGROUND: Treatments for mental illness are largely based on the medical model, although recent research demonstrates that strengths-based approaches that mobilize individual and environmental resources can better facilitate recovery. Existing evidence, including our own work on recovery-oriented services for individuals with mental illnesses, suggests that Strengths Model Case Management (SMCM, developed by Rapp and Goscha) offers a structured and innovative intervention. However, data on the effectiveness of strengths-based interventions come primarily from studies that lack methodological rigor, have failed to assure fidelity to the model, and were conducted mainly in the West. OBJECTIVE: The proposed randomized controlled trial will test the effectiveness of high-fidelity SMCM for the recovery outcomes of clients with mental illness, and will identify the critical components of the strengths model that exert positive impacts on clients. RESEARCH TEAM: The research team comprises local and international experts in recovery and strengths-based interventions, including a founding author and evaluator of SMCM. METHOD: We will recruit 210 clients of mental health services from three community-based mental health centers operated by three local non-governmental organizations. The clients will be randomly assigned to SMCM groups or control groups called SMILE. The SMCM groups will receive strengths model intervention from case workers using the Strengths Assessment and Personal Recovery Plan to help them identify their individual and environmental strengths and set goals to facilitate their recovery. Weekly strengths-based supervision (i.e., group supervision and field mentoring) will support the SMCM case workers to assure effective use of the strengths model tools and methods. The SMCM groups will maintain high intervention integrity throughout the study with support from the leadership team, measured by the validated Fidelity Scale every six months. In contrast, the SMILE groups will receive generic, recovery-oriented care from case workers with an attention placebo. All participating clients will complete questionnaires (e.g., recovery, self-efficacy and level of psychiatric symptoms) at baseline and 6 and 12 months after recruitment. Functional outcomes such as employment and hospitalization will be tracked by case workers monthly. We will also conduct qualitative evaluations to identify the therapeutic ingredients and conditions that lead to successful implementation and outcomes using grounded theory along with fidelity assessment data . IMPACTS: This study will generate new knowledge of SMCM that will significantly extend and refine the existing literature on strengths-based practice in mental health. SMCM also offers a structure and tools for mental health practitioners to provide interventions likely to benefit many individuals.

17609617.label: Realisation of objectives
17609617.value: 1) Execution of the Project to achieve the Research Objectives: The first objective of the present study is to assess the effectiveness of SMCM when implemented among service users in community mental health centres, using RCT design. Specifically, we hypothesized that users in the high-fidelity SMCM group will experience higher levels of personal recovery, as well as symptom reductions, improved hope, community integration, mattering, working alliances, and goal attainment, relative to their counterparts in a control group, which incorporates an attention placebo. The second objective is to evaluate the fidelity features of SMCM implementation and the major therapeutic ingredients that influence users’ outcomes. 1.1 First objective: Outcome evaluation. This study consisted of two arms: an SMCM intervention group and a control group. The service users in both arms were recruited from the community mental health centres or Integrated Community Centre for Mental Wellness (ICCMW) of three non-governmental organisations which were in different districts in Hong Kong. Service users attending ICCMWs were individuals with either suspected mental health problems or diagnosed mental illnesses. We recruited a total of 209 participants (original target, N=210) of three ICCMWs from November 2017 to May 2019. A trained social worker at each centre was responsible for screening the eligibility of service users based on the inclusion and exclusion criteria. After screening for their eligibility, all users completed a face-to-face baseline questionnaire. The social worker contacted the research team to obtain group allocation information and participants were randomly allocated to either the SMCM or control group in a 1:1 ratio, according to a pre-determined randomisation list generated by an online randomisation program (www.randomization.com). Block randomisation was performed to reduce bias and achieve balance in allocating participants into the SMCM and control groups. After group assignment, participants were followed up by caseworkers using the SMCM or control protocol and were asked to complete the same questionnaires at the 6th and 12th month. Participants were informed which intervention they were allocated to, but they only knew that they were two forms of psychosocial intervention. The paid field workers who were individuals with lived experience of mental illness were recruited and trained by the research team to collect data during the trial. They were blind to the group allocation information. In order to minimize contamination, caseworkers in the control group did not use any of the tools related to SMCM (e.g., strengths assessment, personal recovery plan) or received any strengths-based supervision. To ensure the integrity of the intervention used in the SMCM and control groups, as well as the adherence to the model, two raters with a thorough understanding of SMCM conducted fidelity check for both SMCM and control groups by using the Fidelity Scale at baseline (T0), 6th (T1) and 12th (T2) months after the intervention started. The fidelity check consisted of interviews with staff and service users, site observations, and reviews of the SMCM tools and charts. The Fidelity Scale is composed of nine items across three areas: structure, supervision/supervisor, and clinical/service. The Scale’s cut-off is that the SMCM teams should achieve an overall fidelity score of 36 (out of 45) on the Scale including an average rating of four out of five in each of the three areas. In this study, all the trial sites achieved high fidelity review scores (4 out of 5). Results showed that: 1. Only working alliance (rated by worker) differed across group and time; 2. Marginal effect (p = .1) of RAS-reliance on others was found; 3. Young (18-39 years old) and middle-aged (40-59 years old) participants in the SMCM group showed improvement in goal progress at the 12th-month measure. 4. With regard to within-participant change, the growth curve modelling revealed a significant growth pattern for SMCM middle-aged (40-59 years old) participants in relation to goal progress and RAS-total; no similar pattern was found in the control group. 5. Although no difference existed between SMCM and control, there was a time effect for some variables e.g., mattering, working alliance (rated by worker), goal progress. 6. Exploratory data analysis showed that change of recovery total score reduced or even deteriorated as age increased among service users in the control group (verified by the regression model). In other words, there was a desirable stabilizing effect for improved recovery scores among service users in the SMCM group regardless of age. 1.2 Second objective: A process evaluation. To evaluate the fidelity features of SMCM implementation and the major therapeutic ingredients that had an effect on service users’ outcomes, 38 individual interviews with service users and their caseworkers from both SMCM and control groups were completed in 2018-2019. Each interview was conducted by the same person (Lo) lasted between 30 and 90 minutes and it was carried out in the interview room at the ICCMWs. The data collection was directed by a semi-structured interview guideline which included the following domains: the perceived therapeutic ingredients, perceptions of the benefits, challenges in the care and support taking place in their experience, and suggestions for improvement among the service users and staff participants. Prior to conducting the interviews, consent for audio-recording was obtained from all participants. The audio recordings were saved in an encrypted folder and were transcribed verbatim in Chinese by professional transcribers for subsequent analysis and interpretations. All identifying information was removed from the texts to ensure confidentiality. Quality checks were performed by Lo by comparing recordings to transcripts. Only the direct quotes cited in the present manuscript were translated into English. It was found that only a weak relationship or overlap existed between SMCM’s fidelity profile and service users’ personal recovery outcomes. Major therapeutic ingredients identified by workers were about the quality of therapeutic alliance, users’ qualities, workers’ qualities and other elements. 2) Challenges: The drop-out rates were from 3.0% to 18.4% among participants who have completed the T1 questionnaire in the three agencies. It was reported that the participants felt taking quite a long time (about an hour) to complete the questionnaire affected the participation rate. The frontline workers who assisted in making contacts with the participants worried that further drop-out would be expected during the follow-up period. In view of the comments, the research team took the following remedial actions with approval of ethics amendment: (1) A “Certificate of Appreciation” to recognize the participations’ contribution to the research; (2) As this is a study of strengths-model case management, a strengths-based planner (a book which has a year planner and words of encouragement throughout the copy; donated by one of the partnered agencies) was distributed to the participants. These two items were given to the participants when they completed the follow-up questionnaire (only the last one T2) to appreciate their time and effort. 3) Beyond Achieving the Objectives. To disseminate the research findings to the frontline caseworkers and supervisors, a sharing session was held in June 2019. Other activities (e.g., presenting conference, press conference, items published in local Chinese newspaper and international book) were completed to create a greater impact on different sectors of the community. For details of the research results, please see Section 6 Research Outcome and the FULL MANUSCRIPTS attached in the Report, Regarding further dissemination of the results, see Part C- Research Output of this Report.

To qualitatively examine the major therapeutic ingredients that have impacts on clients’ recovery outcomes and the fidelity features of SMCM that facilitate successful implementation of the case management system.

17609617.label: Major findings and research outcome
17609617.value: Quantitative results Result 1. Compared to baseline measures, members improved in several domains after going through the 12-month psychosocial services provided by the ICCMWs. The domains were: Mattering, user-caseworker therapeutic alliance, and goal-related performance (e.g., number of goals and progress). Result 2. There were six major findings when comparing the results obtained from the SMCM and control groups. Implementation 1. SMCM was implemented successfully in the ICCMWs monitored by the fidelity measure during the 12-month trial. Group by time (by age) 2. ICCMW members benefited from the SMCM intervention in terms of building a strong therapeutic alliance with professionals as perceived by caseworkers; and potentially in the area of reliance i.e., user’s acceptance of others (and self), compared with the control group. 3. It was found that the research participants in different age groups showed different reactions to the SMCM. Young and middle-aged (18-59 years old) ICCMW members were making better progress towards their goals under the SMCM regime compared with the control group by the end of the 12-month intervention. 4. For older adults (60 and above years old; especially those who were less educated) benefited from SMCM interventions in terms of personal recovery and hope; the same pattern was not found in ICCMW members in the control group. Within-participant change (growth curve modelling) 5. Middle-aged (40-59 years old) ICCMW members in the SMCM group showed improvement in their personal recovery and goal progress, then the rate of improvement decreased gradually. This pattern was not found in the control group. SMCM was an effective tool for early-career mental health workers 6. Workers in the SMCM group had 3.8 years of working experience and they achieved similar intervention outcomes compared with workers in the control group who had 6.6 years of working experience. Qualitative results 1. Compared the experience of receiving/ delivering the SMCM and control group interventions (e.g., therapeutic relationships treatment ingredients) as perceived by service users and workers, both workers and users in the SMCM group were able to describe the features of the intervention such as the use of the forms, the emphasis placed on “strength” (and being more self-critical) than counterparts in the control group. 2. SMCM users were expressive in describing their deep therapeutic alliance with their workers. 3. SMCM workers tended to use a range of words (theoretical concepts) and sound clinical reasoning to talk about their experience of delivering the services.

17609617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17609617.value: Research and clinical implication: 1) ICCMW members made statistically significant improvements in several domains throughout the study period. Given the deceleration of improvement or drop in measurement scores at the 12th-month time point, it demands further study to examine if the newly gained therapeutic effects will be maintained. 2) SMCM produces added benefits such as therapeutic alliance, users’ reliance, and goal progress, compared with regular services provided in ICCMWs. Measurement of goals could be adopted as part of the robust assessment of recovery outcomes in future. Feedback from the users’ significant others could be collected to explore their further potential changes. 3) SMCM offers a useful structure and tools to less-experienced workers who eventually produce similar outcomes compared with more experienced workers. More attention could be paid to the array of therapeutic ingredients identified by the workers as well as the challenges and critical driving forces for continuous implementation. 4) Findings from the present study indicated that close to four (out of “5”) of the scores in fidelity review (FR) is good enough across the scale. Future research can be extended to examine the effectiveness of localized fidelity items, and also the relationship between fidelity items and treatment outcomes.

17609617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17609617.value: The Strengths Model Case Management (SMCM) implemented in some Integrated Community Centres for Mental Wellness (ICCMWs) in Hong Kong. The current study aimed to assess the effectiveness of SMCM when implemented among mental health service users at ICCMWs using a randomized controlled trial design. 209 service users from three ICCMWs took part in this mixed-method research study using quantitative and qualitative methodologies. The participants and their caseworkers completed questionnaires before any intervention (baseline), 6 months into the study and after 12 months. Comparing the experience of receiving and delivering the SMCM and control group interventions (e.g., therapeutic relationships treatment ingredients) as perceived by service users and caseworkers, it is found to be more effective to focus on a person’s strengths, aspirations, and goals rather than their problems all the time. Medical treatment together with strengths-based community interventions better supports a person’s recovery from mental illness. Caseworkers in the SMCM group with 3.8 years of working experience achieved valued-added intervention outcomes compared to colleagues in the control group with 6.6 years of working experience. This showed that SMCM gives early-career workers a professional tool and structure to deliver effective psychosocial services.

17610217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17610217.value: The trust is a long-established legal institution in the common law world. Despite its versatility, the traditional concept of a trust as a form of property holding by one party (trustee) for the benefit of another (beneficiary) remains largely constant. In the past few decades, however, as the trust becomes more widely utilised in a greater variety of settings for tax mitigation, asset protection and wealth management, the boundaries of the trust are also evolving. In order to attract trust businesses, trust planners have little hesitation in catering to the wishes of potential settlors, who do not wish to lose control over their assets, by manipulating some features of the trust, such as trust protectors and settlor’s reserved powers. These trends are sanctioned if not bolstered by many jurisdictions, both onshore and offshore. As the modern international trust evolves, it has also come under increasing attack and scrutiny. In light of these developments and challenges, our research has two objectives. First, we will explore the role of the Legislature and the Judiciary in these modern developments, focusing in particular on transnational trust litigation preserving or enforcing beneficiaries’ rights in a trust. We will examine how trust-related legislation enables courts to vary the beneficial provisions of a trust, and how judicial activism may lead to a breakdown of the trust as an asset protection device. At the same time, the modern international trust is often established offshore. While offshore courts almost invariably enforced the court orders on the grounds of judicial comity in the past, these offshore jurisdictions have now also enacted stronger local firewall legislation against the recognition and enforcement of foreign judgments. Our research seeks to examine how the judiciary interacts with the legislation in the tug of war between the integrity of the trust concept and enhancing the attractiveness of the trust. Secondly, we will critique the impact of these developments on the nature and content of the trust obligation, in particular whether the innovative features of the modern international trust lack theoretical foundations, may inevitably curtail the scope of the trustee’s independent exercise of discretion, and ultimately undermine the delicate balance of rights and obligations in the trust relationship that is at the core of the trust concept. We will write at least 4 journal articles to disseminate our research findings, which will contribute to the academic literature on the use and abuse of the modern international trust. 信託是普通法系長期確立的法律制度。儘管信託十分多元化，但其傳統概念，即作為一方（受託人）為另一方（受益人）持有產業的一種形式，仍大致維持不變。然而，在過去的幾十年中，隨著信託在減稅、資產保護和財富管理等各式各樣的領域中得到廣泛應用，信託的邊界也在不斷演變。為了吸引信託業務，信托設計者通過操縱信託的一些特徵（如信託保護者和委託人的權力保留），毫不猶豫地滿足那些不希望對資產失去控制的潛在委託人的願望。 這些趨勢更受到了許多在岸和離岸司法管轄區的認可和支持。 隨著現代國際信託的發展，它受到越來越多的攻擊和審查。鑒於這些發展和挑戰，我們的研究有兩個目標。 首先，我們將探討立法機關和司法機構在這些現代發展中的角色，並以保留或執行信託受益人權利的跨國信託訴訟為焦點。我們將研究與信託相關的法律如何使法庭能夠改變信託的受益條款，以及信託作為一種資產機制如何在司法積極主義下被導致瓦解。同時，現代國際信託往往是離岸建立的。雖然離岸法庭過去總是以司法禮讓原則為由執行法院命令，但現在這些離岸司法管轄區在外國判決的承認和執行上，紛紛制定了更強大的本地法律防火墻。在信託概念的完整性和增強信託吸引力的這場角力中，我們的研究旨在探討司法機構與立法機關如何互動。 其次，我們將評論這些發展對於信託義務的性質和內容的影響，尤其是現代國際信託的創新特徵是否缺乏理論基礎，是否必然會限制受託人獨立運用自由裁量權的範圍，並最終破壞了信託的核心概念：權利與義務的精巧平衡 。 我們的研究成果將對現代國際信託的使用和濫用方面的學術文獻作出貢獻。

17610217.label: Realisation of objectives
17610217.value: There was complete achievement of all 4 Objectives on schedule. Objective 1: We thoroughly examined the trust and trust-related (eg matrimonial) legislation in major Common Law jurisdictions (England, Australia, New Zealand, Singapore and Hong Kong), and the possible attacks on the trust in transnational matrimonial and succession litigation. Objective 2: We undertook research to compare relevant laws, regulations in major offshore jurisdictions (the BVI, Jersey, Bermuda, and the Cayman Islands). Specifically, we reviewed how offshore jurisdictions have modified their laws to make their jurisdictions more attractive to settlors setting up trusts. These include more relaxed rules against perpetuities, greater scope of reservation of powers by settlors, the use of protectors, weakened obligation of the trustee to be involved in the management of trust-owned companies, etc. An inventory of materials was collected. Objective 3: We applied the research findings from Objectives 1 and 2 to examine the interaction between the Legislature and the Judiciary in transnational trust developments. In the context of trusts in matrimonial disputes, we saw increasing tension between family and trust law in grappling with the relevant matrimonial legislation. Further, as trusts are increasingly settled offshore, there is also the additional tension between onshore divorce and offshore trust legislation. We attended several international conferences to disseminate the research findings. Objective 4: We examined the implications of the modern international developments of the trust and detailed our conclusions in a number of publications. These developments have transformed the main features of a modern private trust and raises questions such as accountability of trustees, control of settlor’s reserved powers etc. These developments also pose immense challenges for the trust industry in regulatory and doctrinal dimensions. The research findings in Objectives 3 and 4 were published 2 journal articles and 2 book chapters. The publications arose from invited participation in specialised journal issues / book projects based on high-level academic conferences, participated by eminent academics in the field. Item 3 was published with a top US journal and the book chapters were published with a prestigious academic press in Law.

17610217.label: Major findings and research outcome
17610217.value: We have made two major theoretical findings about this area of law as follows :- (1) The modern international developments in trusts have transformed the main features of a modern private trust in a few fundamental aspects, including the role of the settlor, the powers and duties of the trustee, as well as the diminishing role of the beneficiaries. In short, the bilateral relationship between the trustee and the beneficiary has radically been transformed into a tripartite and more dynamic relationship among the settlor/protector, trustee, and beneficiaries, and raises questions such as accountability of trustees, control of settlor’s reserved powers etc (see Part C, item 3 (Lee) and item 2 (Ho)). (2) These developments have also led to increasing tension between the Legislature and the Judiciary, as highlighted in the attacks on trusts in divorce litigation (see Part C, item 1 (Lee)). Based on these findings, we have examined the immense challenges for the trust industry in at least two dimensions and proposed responses thereto: (1) The regulatory dimension: the trust industry is not immune from the need to negotiate the tension between tightening international regulation of trust and mounting commercial pressure to stay competitive (see Part C, item 4 (Ho)). (2) The doctrinal dimension: the trust industry in many onshore jurisdictions (including Hong Kong) has exerted and will continue to exert pressure on their respective governments to introduce more innovative reforms to enhance their competitiveness in attracting offshore trust business. It is necessary to appreciate the need to re-examine core trust concepts (see Part C, item 3 (Lee)). We attended several international conferences to disseminate the research findings. We were able to publish 4 journal articles / book chapters as stated in the objectives.

17610217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17610217.value: Whilst our current research project has examined the implications of the modern international developments of the trust in the context of wealth transfer, our research has also identified major developments in the use of the trust in other contexts. These include commercial investments and the use of trust-owned companies; wills and testamentary trusts; evolution and use of trust in philanthropy; AI and digital money; special needs financial planning and cognitive impairments giving rise to issues of decision-making capacity. Our current research has enabled further work on these specific issues. We have already done some preliminary research on these areas and propose to conduct further research. We also plan to seek further collaborative and/or interdisciplinary research funding in the near future for this purpose.

17610217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17610217.value: The trust is a long-established legal institution in the common law world. In the modern era, however, the trust’s development has not been dominated by English law, but by various modern developments pioneered by offshore jurisdictions, with the result that some classic features of a traditional trust have been eroded. Our project examined the growing use and evolution of trusts in wealth transfers from two perspectives, namely, the innovative features of the modern international trust that render the use of a trust more palatable to settlors and the challenges posed by those features for both the validity of the trust and integrity of the trust concept. Our research examined the features of a modern trust, as well as conceptual requirements of the modern trust, including the content of the fiduciary duty, and the irreducible core of trusteeship. Our research led to the publication of conference papers, book chapters and journal articles which has enriched the intellectual debate both locally and internationally.
