17610517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17610517.value: Early childhood development has received considerable research and policy attention because of research that has shown the positive impact of participation in preschool programmes on child development. Preschool attendance has increased throughout the world, and in China the gross enrolment rate in pre-primary education for 4- to 6-year-olds has increased from 36% in 1999 to 70% in 2012 and to 82% in 2014. However, nationwide studies reveal regional disparities in preschool quality. Against this background, this study will investigate the impact of preschool quality on school readiness and early achievement in 2 of the 31 major administrative divisions in China- the province of Jiangxi and the municipality of Shanghai–wherein levels of economic and educational development vary widely. The proposed study will focus on 500 children aged 4-5 years. Children in Shanghai will be randomly selected from three kindergartens with varying government ratings of educational quality while children in Jiangxi will be selected from kindergartens in a prefectural-level city, a county-level city and a village. This is because preschool quality may vary with the size of the population in the city or village. We will assess the development of children when they are in Kindergarten 2 and 3; their school readiness before they enter Primary 1 in September 2019; and their literacy and mathematics achievement at the end of Primary 1 (June 2020). We will also assess teacher quality, instructional quality and the physical settings of their preschools in 2017-18 and 2018-19. This will allow us to determine the impact of preschool quality and early schooling on achievement, controlling for early development and family characteristics. We hypothesize that preschool quality will be positively associated with school readiness and academic attainment at the end of Primary 1. We also assume that the achievement gap between children from Shanghai and Jiangxi will decrease over time because of the homogeneity of the primary school curriculum and government efforts to mitigate regional disparities. Mediation, multiple mediation, and moderated mediation analyses will be used in the statistical treatment of the longitudinal data and multivariate analyses will be deployed for cross-sectional comparisons. Findings will have theoretical implications for developmental science and will add to the international literature on preschool effectiveness. Such research is particularly important for China at a time of unparalleled development in early childhood education policy. 研究顯示，學前教育能為兒童發展帶來正面的影響，因此幼兒發展受到研究者和政策制定者的廣泛關注。縱觀全球，學前教育入學率正快速增長。而中國的四至六歲幼兒的學前教育入學率也從1999年的百分之三十六上升至2012年的百分之七十，及至2014年的百分之八十二。儘管如此，全國調查發現不同地區的學前教育質量存在很大差距。有見及此，本研究將從中國大陸三十一個省級行政單位中選取兩個在經濟和教育發展上存在較大差異的地區——江西省及上海市，研究學前教育質量對兒童的入學準備度及早期成績的影響。 本研究將聚焦於五百名四至五歲的幼兒。在上海，三所由政府評定為不同教育質量等級的幼稚園將被隨機抽選幼兒參與研究。在江西，考慮到幼稚園教育質量可能受城市和鄉村人口分佈所影響，我們將分別從地級市、縣級市和鄉村幼稚園中隨機抽選幼兒參與研究。我們會先在幼兒讀中班及大班時評估他們發展的情況；在2019年9月幼兒進入小學一年級之前評估他們的入學準備度，並在小學一年級結束時（2020年6月）評估兒童的語文和數學學業成績。此外，我們還將在2017至2018 及2018至2019學年間評估幼稚園的教師素養、教學質量和幼稚園整體教學環境。在減除了幼兒發展和家庭相關因素之後，我們將能辨析學前教育質量和早期學習經歷對兒童成績的影響。 我們假設學前教育質量與兒童入學準備度及小學一年級末的學業成績有正面相關關係。我們也假設上海和江西的兒童發展差距將隨時日逐漸縮小皆因全國的小學課程內容相近，及國家為減少地區差異的努力。。我們將使用中介分析、多重中介分析和有調節的中介分析處理追蹤研究的數據。多變量分析方法也將被用作比較各項數據。 本研究的調查結果將為兒童發展科學理論作出貢獻，並增添國際上關於學前教育價值的研究。此外，本研究對於當前中國學前教育政策的發展也有非常重要的意義。

17610517.label: Major findings and research outcome
17610517.value: Children in China attend full-day preschools wherein education is typically provided in age-segregated classrooms - Kindergarten 1 (K1), Kindergarten 2 (K2), and Kindergarten 1 (K3). Participants in our study resided in Shanghai and Guizhou, regions that vary markedly in economic development. In Wave 1, participants were 681 4- and 5-year-olds from 52 K2 classrooms in Shanghai and in Guizhou. We assessed participants again when they were in K3 (Wave 2). Wave 3 occurred when participants were in Grade 2. We could not collect data when children were in Grade 1 because of the severity of the COVID-19 pandemic restrictions at that time. We were able to locate 317 children from our original sample. They had been in 47 K2 classrooms in 27 preschools in Shanghai and in Guizhou. Children completed tests when they were in K2, K3, and Grade 2. Preschool quality had been assessed when children were in K2 when parents had also provided information about the home learning environment. Results from Wave 1 indicated that preschool quality was higher in Shanghai than in urban and rural Guizhou and lowest in rural Guizhou. Preschool quality was positively associated with child outcomes, after adjusting for child, family, and programme characteristics and area of residence. Moderation analyses showed a weaker association between preschool quality and child development in urban Guizhou and urban Shanghai than in rural Guizhou, suggesting that preschool quality may be particularly beneficial for children living in poor, rural areas (See Research Output 1). In every Wave, child outcomes were better in Shanghai than in Guizhou (See Research Outputs 3 and 2). Controlling for covariates, early experiences in neither homes nor preschools contributed to prediction of child outcomes in K3 and in Grade 2, but region of residence predicted Grade 2 literacy (β =.76) and mathematics (β =.86) attainment. Policy efforts are needed to mitigate these early and persistent achievement gaps.

17610517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17610517.value: We plan to follow this cohort of children as they move through primary school. We also plan to leverage data from the China Family Panel Studies to gain a better understanding of urban-rural differences in early childhood development and education in China.

17610517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17610517.value: This study examined associations between preschool quality, home learning environments, early development, and achievement in Grade 2, in Shanghai and Guizhou. We selected these two regions because they vary in economic development and we were interested in determining factors that contributed to place-based disparities in early achievement. Our initial sample included 710 4-year-olds from 52 K2 classrooms in 29 kindergartens in October 2017. Children completed tests when they were in K2, K3, and Grade 2, and their parents were surveyed. The following findings are based on 317 children who completed all three assessments. As expected, we found that preschool quality, home learning environments, and child outcomes were better in Shanghai than in Guizhou. However, when we controlled for family wealth and parents’ education, early experiences in neither homes nor preschools contributed to the prediction of child outcomes in K3 and in Grade 2, but the region of residence predicted Grade 2 literacy and mathematics attainment. The findings from this study illustrate the complex interplay between factors related to the child, family, preschool, and place of residence in determining early achievement in China. We have shown that early achievement gaps persist and evidence-based inventions are needed to close place-based gaps in child outcomes.

17610717.label: Project Objectives
17610717.value: Achieve a systematic and quantitative understanding of the content of national constitutions at the linguistic level, around the world and throughout history. Break down disciplinary barriers by importing automated content analysis and topic modeling techniques from computational linguistics into legal scholarship. Demonstrate that computerized techniques can be used to analyze legal texts at the linguistic level, and to identify ideological and substantive themes in legal texts. Test empirically the competing hypotheses of constitutional diversity, constitutional convergence, and competing constitutional models via the computer-assisted analysis of constitutional texts. Document and describe patterns in constitutional drafting that cannot be reliably and precisely identified using either traditional empirical techniques or unassisted human reading. Test empirically whether and to what extent variables such as geographical region, colonial history, overall length, and constitutional age explain or predict the linguistic content of national constitutions. Demonstrate the increasingly intimate relationship between constitutional law and international law, and the growing influence of international human rights law on national law, by measuring the linguistic similarity between national constitutions and international human rights treaties.

17610717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17610717.value: Since World War II, it has become standard practice for countries to adopt formal constitutions. Whether there is also a standard way of writing constitutions, however, is a matter of considerable debate. The view long held by comparative legal scholars—dating back at least as far as the French political philosopher Montesquieu (1689-1755)—is that constitutional law is necessarily unique and cannot be borrowed from other countries because it must reflect local conditions and circumstances in order to operate successfully. The rise of globalization, however, has prompted some scholars to question the traditional view and to posit the existence of global standardization and convergence in constitutional drafting. The application of innovative empirical techniques to the text of over six hundred national constitutions adopted over the past two centuries suggests that neither of these views is correct. Using automated content analysis techniques from computational linguistics and political science, I will show empirically in the proposed research that constitutions are characterized neither by diversity nor by convergence, but instead by clustering into three ideologically distinctive models of constitutional drafting that I call the liberal model, the statist model, and the universalist model. Each model is defined by a distinctive type of justification for the existence and organization of the state and draws nourishment from a distinct legal tradition. The liberal model has its origins in the common law tradition and views the state with suspicion as a potentially oppressive concentration of authority that must be regulated and restrained. The statist model, in contrast, is associated with the civil law tradition and rejects the idea that state power is a threat to be minimized. It instead conceives of the state as the embodiment of a community and a positive and necessary force for the achievement of the community’s collective goals. The universalist model, the most recent of the three, is symbiotically intertwined with international law. It prioritizes respect for supposedly universal norms and principles (such as human rights and nonaggression in international relations) over respect for national sovereignty. Its emergence reflects global, post-World War II trends in favor of both the incorporation of transnational norms into domestic law and the intermingling of international law and constitutional law. The proposed research will capture empirically the prevalence of these competing models over time and, in particular, the rising importance of universalist and internationalist themes in constitutional drafting since World War II. 自第二次世界大戰起，采用正式憲法已成爲國家間的標準做法。然而，編寫憲法的標準方法是否存在則頗具爭議。比較法學者——至少能追溯至法國政治學家孟德斯鳩(1689-1755)——一貫的觀點是憲法必然是獨一無二的。而且，由於一國憲法必須反映本地情況以成功實踐，因此難以借鋻他國憲法。不過，全球化的興起促使部分學者開始質疑傳統的觀點，並提出憲法草擬存在著全球標準化和趨於一致的現象。 以創新的實證研究方法對過去兩個世紀、超過六百套國家憲法的文本進行分析的結果卻指出，上述兩種觀點皆不正確。通過運用電腦語言學及政治學的自動化内容分析方法，本人將在此研究中證實憲法並不是以多元性或一致性區分；而應該被歸類為三個各自具有獨特意識形態的憲法草擬模型——本人稱之為自由主義模型，國家主義模型及普世主義模型。 上述模型可按照其各自對國家存在及其組織的正當性的獨特解釋所劃分，並可從不同的法律傳統中取得養分。 自由主義模型源自普通法傳統，對國家抱著懷疑的態度，並視國家為一個潛在的壓迫人民的集權。因此，此模型認爲國家必須被管理及限制。相反，國家主義模型則與大陸法傳統相關，並否定國家權力是一種威脅並需要被減到最少的觀點；此模型視國家為社會的象徵及一種正面而必要的力量以達致社會共同目標。普世主義模型——三個模型中最新的模型，與國際法如共生般密切相關。比起尊重國家主權，此模型更優先尊重普世標準和原則（例如人權和國際關係中的不侵略原則）。此模型的出現反映把跨國準則融入本地法律並將國際法與憲法相互融合的二戰後的全球趨勢。 本研究將以實證方法説明，上述互相競爭之模型在過去的流行情況，特別是普世和國際主義對憲法草擬日益上升的重要性。

17611917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17611917.value: 本研究項目將以三維角度（包括歷史、功能與比較法角度）探討衡平法就受託人違反責任的賠償制度。首先，項目將從歷史角度，集中研究十七至二十世紀的普通法案例，以追溯衡平法賠償制度的起源及其背後的指導原則。第二，項目從功能角度，理解衡平法賠償制度與普通法賠償制度功能上的差異。第三，項目從比較法角度，比較六個主要普通法適用地區（如: 英國、澳洲、紐西蘭、加拿大、新加坡、香港及美國）的衡平法賠償制度，並評價它們各自的優點。這三維角度的探究有助建立一個建基於理論、歷史和實質功能的衡平法賠償制度。

17611917.label: Realisation of objectives
17611917.value: There was complete achievement of all 3 Objectives on schedule. Objective 1: We thoroughly examined the historical rules of equitable accounting, the genesis of equitable compensation, and their functional roles amongst other equitable remedies. In particular, we considered the jurisdictional root of equitable accounting, the unique mode of operation of equitable accounting through falsification and surcharging, the comparison of equitable accounting with common law damages as well as gain-based equitable remedies such as account of profits and the constructive trust. Objective 2: We undertook research to compare relevant case law in all the jurisdictions listed (namely England, Australia, New Zealand, Singapore and Hong Kong). The remedial rules were exclusively judge-made, and therefore our comparative research focused on judicial decisions at state- and national level in these jurisdictions. We also reviewed the rich and burgeoning academic commentaries on these decisions, particularly those in response to a recent controversial decision of the UK Supreme Court. To fully understand the functional role of equitable compensation, we also collected materials about equitable account for profits and proprietary relief and defences. We now have a comprehensive database of first-instance and appellate-level court decisions of all the jurisdictions considered, as well as secondary materials (books and journal papers) on the research topic. Objective 3: After a close review of the research findings in Objectives 1 and 2, we identified a theoretical perspective in understanding the existing law and put forward suggestions in reinvigorating the law. We wrote and improved broad arguments set out in conference papers to produce the research outputs. We disseminated our findings through international conferences, journal publications and book chapters. Instead of 5 peer-reviewed journal articles, we published 2 journal articles in top generalist and specialist journals and 3 book chapters. The book chapters were invited participation in specialised book projects based on high-level academic conferences, participated by eminent academics in the field, and published with top academic presses in Law.

17611917.label: Major findings and research outcome
17611917.value: We have made two major theoretical findings about this area of law as follows :- (1) Our survey of the historical origin of the traditional accounting mechanism enabled us to identify the rationale of traditional accounting rules and theorized them in the context of modern approaches to loss-based compensation. (2) We have situated the functional role played by equitable compensation for loss in association with gain-based remedies and unjust enrichment remedies in providing a full range of remedies for breach of trust and breach of fiduciary duty. In essence, these rules ensure that whatever factual consequences happen to the beneficiary as the result of a breach of trust or fiduciary duty, he will be placed in a position as close as practically possible to the performance that was promised to him. Based on these findings, we have proposed improving the law along the following lines: (1) recognition of the unique emphasis in equitable compensation on the performance interest of the beneficiary and rejection of the requirement of causation for recovery of misapplied funds (see Part C, item 4, Ho and Nolan) (2) appreciation and characterisation of the idea of deemed performance as the guiding principle in awarding remedies for breach of trust and fiduciary duties (see Part C, item 1, Ho) (3) rationalisation of a number of equitable defences for breaches of trust and the remedies for dishonestly assisting a breach of trust (see Part C, item 3, Lee and item 2, Ho); and (4) affirmation of the performance basis and consequential rejection of an exclusively unjust enrichment basis for proprietary liability and third-party recipient liability for breaches of trust, as situated in the broader theoretical interface between equity and unjust enrichment (see Part C, item 5, Ho) We attended several international conferences to disseminate the research findings. We were able to publish 5 journal articles / book chapters as stated in the revised objectives. All except two of the research outputs have been published; two are forthcoming around July 2020.

17611917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17611917.value: In the course of our current research project, which examined a broad spectrum of issues in relation to equitable compensation and its interrelationship with gain-based remedies, we have identified areas that warrant further analysis. These include: equitable remedies for breaches of the duty of care; compensatory liability of third parties who assist in a breach of trust or fiduciary duty; and the theoretical basis of trust obligations. We have already conducted preliminary research in these areas and plan to take the research a step further through securing funding for future related projects.

17611917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17611917.value: When a trustee or a fiduciary agent commits a breach of trust, she is required to make compensation to the beneficiary. Such remedies are granted through a technical process that reaches back many centuries, and differ from the remedies granted when a contracting party breaks her contract or a tortfeasor causes harm to a victim. The discrepancy in these laws has led to a recent trend to assimilate equitable rules with other areas of private law. The research investigates the historical root and theoretical rationale for the discrepancy, and argues that the historical approach reflects the need to protect the unique nature of the trust institution. The discovery in the research is significant in protecting the integrity of the trust as a crucial institution for wealth management. The value of the research lies in reinvigorating the historical rules without sacrificing the special protection they offer to beneficiaries, and achieving greater coherence between the rules of different areas of law through appropriate differentiation rather than rigid assimilation.

17612017.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17612017.value: 資助房屋的轉售市場：其定價和流動性

17612017.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17612017.value: Prof Chau, K.W. Dr Deng, Kuang Kuang

17612017.label: Project Objectives
17612017.value: To investigate, through real options theory, the conditions under which subsidized homeowners would choose to privatize their units To develop empirical models for the pricing and liquidity of subsidized housing vis-à-vis privatized housing in order to test real options theory
rows: To investigate, through real options theory, the conditions under which subsidized homeowners would choose to privatize their units
To develop empirical models for the pricing and liquidity of subsidized housing vis-à-vis privatized housing in order to test real options theory

17612017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17612017.value: In Hong Kong, the subsidized housing market, known as Home Ownership Scheme (HOS), has been running in parallel with the private housing market since the 1970s. In both markets, owners can re-sell their housing units for profit. What segments the two markets is that subsidized owners can only re-sell their units to a restricted group of lower-income buyers. However, there is a way for subsidized owners to tap the private market. They have an irreversible option to lift the resale restriction by returning their subsidies to the government. This is effectively a privatization option – just that it is exercised by individuals rather than the government. Through the “real options” approach originated in financial economics, this research aims to study the pricing and liquidity of subsidized housing (with the privatization option) vis-à-vis privatized housing (without the privatization option). It is predicted that the option value changes over time; in particular, market segmentation and housing price volatility are the key to determine the option value as well as the optimal timing of a privatization sale, hence liquidity. Based on the transaction records of subsidized and privatized housing units, option pricing models will be devised to verify the predictions. The results will have direct policy implications on the privatization mechanism for subsidized housing. This research is novel in that it offers the first attempt to link “real options” theory to the bottom-up privatization of a subsidized housing market. 「居者有其屋計劃」（居屋）為香港的資助房屋市場。自七十年代至今，居屋與私樓市場並轡而行，業主均可在各自的市場中出售其物業圖利。居屋與私樓的最大分別在於居屋業主只能將其單位轉售予受限制的低收入買家，除非居屋業主先向政府補回資助（補地價），才可於私人市場上出售其物業。通過補地價以解除居屋轉售限制實際上一種不可逆的「私有化期權」，其獨特之處在於行使該權利的是個人而非政府。透過金融經濟學中的「實物期權」理論，本研究旨在考證未補地價居屋（即擁有私有化期權）與已補地價居屋（即喪失私有化期權）的定價和流動性。研究預期，「私有化期權」的價值會隨著時間變化，而市場劃分和房價波動等因素將決定私有化的最佳時機，因此也是流動性的關鍵。本研究項目將根據居屋和私樓市場的交易記錄建立私有化期權的定價模型，以驗證上述的預測。研究成果不但有助政府檢視資助房屋的私有化政策，還首次將「實物期權」理論應用到由下而上的私有化選擇。

17612017.label: Realisation of objectives
17612017.value: Objective 1 has been achieved through these investigations: • The subsidized homeownership policy in Hong Kong, especially the mechanisms for subsidized owners to sell their units, has been reviewed. • The Hong Kong’s homeownership policy has been compared with other shared-equity arrangements in the world, including Australia, Mainland China, Norway, the UK and the US. • Relevant theories and models, including capital constraints, housing affordability, housing ladder, real options, residential mobility, and spatial mismatch, have been reviewed to understand and identify possible conditions under which subsidized owners would sell their units. • Theoretical models have been developed to derive hypotheses on the factors that could affect or distort the selling decision of subsidized owners and buying decision of starter home buyers. Objective 2 has been achieved through these empirical strategies: • Data of property transactions and housing characteristics have been collected from Land Registry, Hong Kong Housing Authority, and Census and Statistics Department, with subsidized units identified through a matching algorithm. • On the pricing of subsidized housing, two empirical approaches have been used to extract the price difference between subsidized and privatized housing. One is a hedonic pricing model that explicitly controls for housing characteristics with over 70,000 observations. The other is a difference-in-differences model that matches subsidized units with their nearest privatized units. For both approaches, statistical analysis has been further performed to test whether the price difference varies with the option to relax capital constraints in a manner as hypothesized above. In line with theoretical predictions, it is found that subsidized housing tends to be overpriced when the units are heavily subsidized, the units are of lower quality, and the private market is highly unaffordable. • On the liquidity of subsidized housing, a home-moving decision is modeled as a function of the costs and benefits of not moving. The costs comprise various spatial mismatches such as a long commute to work. The benefits comprise the in-kind subsidies provided by the government. A panel-data approach has been used to estimate the turnover rate of subsidized housing across building blocks and over time, controlling for location fixed-effects and the turnover rate of private housing. In line with theoretical predictions, it is found that the turnover of subsidized housing is much lower than private housing, especially for units heavily subsidized by the government and for households with less mismatches. A counterfactual test based on privatized, instead of subsidized, housing has been further conducted to confirm that the findings were specific to subsidized housing.

17612017.label: Major findings and research outcome
17612017.value: In research output 8(1), after comparing six subsidized homeownership models in the world, it is revealed that while shared-equity arrangements can improve the affordability of households to own a subsidized housing unit, they may become an obstacle when subsidized households subsequently want to ‘upgrade’ to private housing, depending on how capital gains are to be shared with the government. New measures of entry and exit affordability are proposed to compare and evaluate subsidized homeownership models against their private counterpart. In research output 8(2), by using a quasi-experiment to compare the adjusted price of subsidized units with that of privatized units of similar quality, it is discovered that the former is higher by 4.5% to 6.8%. This premium is attributed to various measures of down-payment constraints faced by starter home buyers, including the size of government subsides, the affordability of subsidized units relative to the low-price segment of private housing, and the affordability of the private housing market in general. The pricing of starter homes is based not only on their quality but also on their option to relax capital constraints. In research output 8(3), by using panel-data analysis to examine the liquidity of subsidized housing, it is found that a) subsidized housing’s liquidity is only a quarter of its privatized counterpart after accounting for the initial resale restriction period; b) given the same level of spatial mismatches, a 1% increase in the housing subsidy reduces the turnover rate by about 2%; c) privatized housing’s liquidity, as a counterfactual test, is correlated with private housing’s liquidity but not driven by spatial mismatches and subsidies as in the case of subsidized housing.

17612017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17612017.value: In recent years, the government has formulated new policy to assist more households to buy their own homes. For example, the White Form Secondary Market Scheme has relaxed the eligibility for buying homes in the resale market of subsidized housing. Further work can be done by using such policy shocks to develop quasi-experiments to examine and evaluate the impact on the pricing and liquidity of subsidized housing.

17612017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17612017.value: Subsidized housing is an important policy tool for the government to tackle the problem of housing unaffordability. Given limited land supply or government budget, not all eligible families will be provided with subsidized housing. The question then hinges on the efficiency of the resale market: what drives current beneficiaries out so that others in need could move in? Through analyzing the turnover rate of subsidized housing units, this research finds that the more in-kind subsidies owners receive, the longer they would hold on to their units in spite of spatial mismatches. This also explains why the liquidity of subsidized housing is much lower than that of private housing, even after accounting for resale restrictions. On the other hand, when housing becomes highly unaffordable, the most affordable units in the market, notably those with more in-kind subsidies, become the only homeownership option to capital-constrained buyers and experience greater price appreciation. This can be generalized to explain the outperformance of the low-price housing segment in this decade. Understanding the intended and unintended consequences of in-kind subsidies is the key to the success of subsidized housing policy.

17612317.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17612317.value: 自由市場的憲制基礎──比較視角下的香港基本法經濟條文

17612317.label: Project Objectives
17612317.value: Uncover the historical, political, and economic factors that led to the adoption of the economic provisions of the Hong Kong Basic Law. Analyse the constitutional rules that regulate the relations between the Hong Kong and mainland China economies. Analyse the constitutional rules that regulate the relations between the Hong Kong economy and the international economy. Compare and contrast the economic provisions of the Hong Kong Basic Law with analogous or similar provisions in relevant constitutional documents from the rest of the world. Examine the future prospects of the economic provisions of the Basic Law, especially after 1 July 2047, the earliest date of their expiry.

Analyse the constitutional rules that regulate the relations between the Hong Kong economy and the international economy.
Compare and contrast the economic provisions of the Hong Kong Basic Law with analogous or similar provisions in relevant constitutional documents from the rest of the world.
Examine the future prospects of the economic provisions of the Basic Law, especially after 1 July 2047, the earliest date of their expiry.

17612317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17612317.value: The proposed project seeks to produce a comprehensive and definitive account of the origins and evolution of the constitutional foundations of free markets in Hong Kong, an under-researched area that deserves much greater scholarly attention, despite this jurisdiction’s global reputation for economic liberty and the rule of law. It examines all of the Basic Law’s provisions on economic and monetary policy as well as the ways they were interpreted by the common law courts, in the context of Hong Kong’s peculiar relationship as a Special Administrative Region with its sovereign the People’s Republic of China under the “One Country, Two Systems” constitutional framework, which conserves multiple indicia of Hong Kong’s external economic sovereignty, but at the same time facilitates the rapid integration of the two economies. Thoroughly comparative and international in approach, the project is bound to contribute significantly to our understanding of the effects of constitutions on economic policy, of comparative law and economics in East Asia, and of Hong Kong’s future, as 1 July 2047, the earliest expiry date of the “One Country, Two Systems” experiment, edges closer. 本研究項目，旨在為香港自由市場憲制基礎之起源和演變，提供一個全面而明確的解釋。儘管香港的經濟自由和法治在全球享有聲譽，這方面的研究仍然不足，而且值得更多學術關注。本項目檢示《香港基本法》所有關於經濟、貨幣政策的條文，以及它們如何在普通法法院的解釋下實施。在這個過程之中，本項目將特別留意，「一國兩制」憲政框架，如何保存了香港對外經濟政策的多個自治標記，卻同時促進香港與內地在經濟上的融合。可以預料，本項目將對比較法學和國際法學，作出重大貢獻，亦會加深我們對憲法的經濟效果、東亞經濟發展、和香港「一國兩制」制度未來的認識。

17612317.label: Realisation of objectives
17612317.value: The completion of this project has been delayed due to largely unforeseeable events that began with the outbreak of the prolonged turmoil in relation to the Fugitive Offenders Bill of 2019, which triggered a series of event that led to previously unthinkable changes to law and politics in Hong Kong as well as the Region's relations with the rest of the world. Of particular concern was the fact that the Heritage Foundation had decided to remove Hong Kong altogether from its ranking of the world's freest economy. Much of our analysis has to be constantly re-oriented in order to keep our project relevant to these drastic developments. Objective 1 has been completely achieved. In our research monograph, we the PI and Co-I argued that the economic provisions of the Basic Law, set on a ‘principle of continuity,’ have their early origins in the uncodified Victorian constitution of Hong Kong under British colonial rule. True to the common law tradition at the time, it was an expression of classical economic liberalism. By the time China resumed the exercise of sovereignty over Hong Kong, the territory had developed a rule–of–law ideology providing both the rationality and predictability requisite to a free, competitive, and efficient market through the enforcement of property and contract rights, and the independent judicial scrutiny of a government accountable to the legislature. The practice of positive non–interventionism created a legal space for economic liberty to raise an international financial centre over an erstwhile fishing village; an economic charism, in brief, free of rent–seeking intervention, subjected only to private property rights, low taxes, balanced budgets, an absence of foreign exchange controls, the free movement of capital and goods, a free port, and minimal, facilitative economic planning. Objective 2 has been completely achieved. In Chapter 3 of our monograph, we reconstructed the drafting process of the Basic Law under the auspices of Deng Xiaoping, then paramount leader of China, and argued that the economic element of the Basic Law was sensitive to the characteristics of Hong Kong’s free market constitutionalism. The Basic Law gives effect, within the Region, to China’s basic policies regarding Hong Kong further to the Sino–British Joint Declaration of 1984; thus, it conserves and codifies the continuity of the common law tradition and, thereby, divides Hong Kong’s capitalist economic system from mainland China’s mixed economic system under the authority of a formally Marxist-Leninist Constitution. The Basic Law restates elements of that tradition in a code of principles and policies, which preserves personal, property, and contractual rights instinct in the Victorian constitution, and allows the market’s invisible hand to freely allocate rents among competitive entry forces. The Drafting Committee codified, in Articles 107 and 108 of the Basic Law, a balanced budget principle and a low tax policy to avoid the economic crisis and currency depreciation consequent upon deficit spending along with the rise in taxes, obtention of foreign loans, issuances of government bonds, and increase in money supply. Freedom of finance under Article 110(2), freedom of trade under Article 115, and free movement of capital under Article 112 bring up the rear. In Chapter 4 of our monograph, we outlined Hong Kong’s economic constitution in the Basic Law, and its judicial interpretation and application. The Basic Law establishes a capitalist system, which it maintains apart from the officially socialist system of mainland China. The unplanned spontaneity of Hong Kong’s free market constitutionalism compelled the kind of discretionary toolkit that the Basic Law makes available for the sake of a proportionate public interest policy. The allowance of Basic Law provisions for economic coordination and social welfare is optimal in its restraint and only serves to enhance the economic liberty that it affords to Hong Kong. It enhances the economic liberty ideal with a triad of policy provisions — Articles 109, 118, and 119 — that allow the Government of the Region to fashion whatever legal and economic environment it deems right for Hong Kong. These provisions do not necessarily entail social welfare interventionism; instead, they allow the Region to stimulate and signpost the market’s freedom as necessary. Objective 3 has been completely achieved. In Chapter 6 of our monograph we extended our analysis to demonstrate that Hong Kong’s external economic policy, further to the Basic Law, seeks precisely to promote and protect the free market. The Basic Law confers on Hong Kong external economic personality and capacity as a ‘separate customs territory,’ under Article 116, to pursue ‘the policy of free trade,’ under Article 115. The Region is the world’s largest free port, a member of the World Trade Organization (WTO) since its establishment, and a signatory to trade agreements and arrangements with many other customs territories. These instruments and instrumentalities of trade have given Hong Kong’s free market constitutionalism a global reach. The Region’s external economic policy thus revolves around membership of the WTO — with the twin objectives to support the multilateral trading system and to make it freer and more open — and a dynamic free trade agreement portfolio with a consistent concern for the liberalisation of trade in services. The free trade qualities of the Basic Law enable ever closer economic integration between Hong Kong and the rest of China through the Closer Economic Partnership Arrangement and participation in such economic development strategies as the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area plan and the Belt and Road Initiative. Objective 4 has only been partially achieved, as we eventually noticed that few constitutions contain the same, unusually high level of constitutional protection of free markets as in the Hong Kong Basic Law, arguably not even the Macau Basic Law, which was modelled on the former. We did demonstrate the constitutional origins of the Basic Law's economic provisions in the laws of England during the Victorian era and earlier, and we contrasted the same with the economic provisions of the Constitution of the People's Republic of China. Objective 5 has been fully realised. We started by studying how the Basic Law was interpreted and applied locally. In Chapter 5 of our monograph, we studied the implementation of free market constitutionalism under the Basic Law, with reference to the economic philosophies of the Region’s first four Chief Executives and the economic jurisprudence of the Hong Kong courts. We argued that Hong Kong’s internal economic policy remains within the broad contours of free market constitutionalism in spite of some deviation from the positive non–interventionist tradition. State intervention in the economy, though still comparatively modest, has been on the rise, and the Government of the Region has, increasingly, adopted the rhetoric of proactive economic governance. Hong Kong’s internationalised financial system has proved to be highly resilient, and weathered through the Asian financial crisis of 1997 and the global financial crisis of 2008. And the courts have consistently closed judicial review as a backdoor for the promotion of welfarism under the cover of constitutional interpretation. In the last chapter, we surveyed Hong Kong’s income inequality, social polarisation, the changes to the electoral and legal system, the coronavirus 2019 disease (COVID–19) pandemic, and the economic future of the Region in an increasingly confident China in the midst of renewed tensions between East and West.

17612317.label: Major findings and research outcome
17612317.value: The research outcomes of this project include (1) a peer-reviewed research article entitled 'Constitutional Finance: The Role of the Hong Kong Basic Law during the Global Financial Crisis' authored by the PI alone of almost 6,000 words, excluding footnotes, published by the Hong Kong Law Journal in 2019; and (2) a co-authored research monograph entitled 'The Freest Market in the World: The Constitutional Logic of Economic Liberty in China’s Hong Kong' by the PI and the Co-I, of almost 43,000 words, excluding lengthy footnotes, to be published by Routledge in late 2022. This monograph will feature two important forewords, one from Lord Neuberger, currently a non-permanent judge of the Hong Kong Court of Final Appeal and formerly President of the UK Supreme Court, and another from Professor Albert Chen, Chair of Constitutional Law at HKU Law and Member of the Basic Law Committee under the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress. The above-mentioned research article argued that the Hong Kong Basic Law performed satisfactorily in supporting financial stability during and after the global financial crisis of 2007-2009. That stability hinges on widespread beliefs held by all the interested parties about the uncompromisingness of the government’s commitment to private property protection and contract enforcement, its self-interest in conserving Hong Kong’s status as an international financial centre, and China’s aversion to the breakdown of the Basic Law, all of which together constituted a successful self-perpetuating economic constitution. In the above-mentioned research monograph, we explored through 6 chapters the concept of ‘free market constitutionalism’ that we propose, the history of Hong Kong’s free market constitutionalism prior to and during the drafting of the Basic Law and how the economic provisions of the Basic Law were interpreted, applied internally, and externally. We then brought our findings to bear on its future, in the light of Hong Kong’s income inequality, polarisation, electoral changes, COVID–19, and renewed tensions between East and West. Our approach is premised on the premise of constitutional economics that constitutional design critically shapes economic outcomes. We argued that the constitutional design of the Basic Law is decisive on maintaining Hong Kong’s status as a world-leading competitive, free, and open economy and that whether Hong Kong stays relevant to China depends, in large part, on the continuity of its free market constitutionalism, which, in turn, depends on the continued commitment of the central authorities and those of the Region’s to this ideal.

17612317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17612317.value: Our project offered a rich and detailed case study of Hong Kong as the embodiment of free market constitutionalism par excellence. It has open up possible avenues for us to develop the idea of free market constitutionalism further as an useful conceptual and analytical tool to evaluate the economic design and performance of constitutional instruments in other jurisdictions. This would enable us to make a distinct contribution to the research programmes of constitutional economics and public choice and the law. Separately, we are also interested in exploring the normative connotations of free market constitutionalism: whether it is in itself a good thing, or - from Marxian perspectives, little more than a mask for capitalist exploitation, and how does it relate to, or differ from, general normative concepts of constitutionalism. That would allow us to contribute to constitutional theory and political philosophy. We would explore which of these two avenues, one positive and the other normative, is of greater priority to our research agendas. Once a choice is made, we will draft a new research proposal to apply for the requisite funding to carry out the work.

17612317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17612317.value: This project resulted in an article and a book that jointly offer a comprehensive account of the origins and development of the constitutional basis of free markets in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China, commonly regarded as the freest economy of the world for decades. The economic provisions of the Basic Law as well as their interpretation by the common law courts were closely examined in the context of Hong Kong?s relationship with Mainland China and the rest of the world. This project allows a wider and deeper understanding of the effects of the Basic Law on Hong Kong?s economic policy and performance, in the light of the plethora of challenges ranging from the 2019 turmoil to COVID-19, as well as the territory's future, as the year 2047, the earliest possible date of the Basic Law's expiry, edges ever closer.

17612817.label: Project Objectives
17612817.value: Systematically apply my comprehensive account of just war theory and the ethics of violence to several special issues in just war theory, such as guerrilla warfare, drone warfare, private military companies, targeted killing, autonomous weapons, preventive war, and humanitarian intervention. Demonstrate the scope, limits, and implications of different justifications of the use of force in these special contexts. Clarify the moral status of different types of non-state combatants and new military technology. Draw some general conclusions about the nature of war and recommend an attitude towards war which, while not embracing pacifism, is even more skeptical towards war than much of present-day just war theory.

17612817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17612817.value: This project is the continuation of my previous GRF project “Just War Theory and the Ethics of Violence.” While I anticipated writing one book, the project has now grown into a book trilogy: the first volume deals with basic justifications for the use of force, the second volume with the core of just war theory, and the third volume with special issues of just war theory. The first volume is finished, the second volume will take a few months more. I am now applying for a GRF grant for the third volume. In the trilogy I describe and analyze at length different justifications of the use of force, such as self-defense, law-enforcement and punishment, and in particular a number of justifications that are often lumped together under the headings of “lesser evil” or “necessity” (but which have to be carefully distinguished from each other), and then systematically consider the scope, limits, and implications of each of these justifications with respect to the ethics of war, regarding both the moral conduct of combatants in war (jus in bello) and the morality of the (political) decision of resorting to war in the first place (jus ad bellum). In the third volume, the subject of this application, I apply these findings to special issues, such as humanitarian intervention, targeted killing, preventive war, mercenaries and private military companies, guerrillas, warlords, remote controlled weapons (drones), and fully automated weapons. A noteworthy feature of my approach is that it runs counter to the currently popular focus on the self-defense justification and on the “liability” of persons to attack (that is, on their having forfeited their right not to be attacked). Instead, I argue that what German law calls a justifying emergency justification should take center stage and demonstrate that such an approach leads to a far more differentiated account of justifiable harming in war and that it has profound theoretical and practical implications for the special issues of just war theory that I discuss in this third volume. Given that my discussion of these special issues is firmly grounded in my previous in-depth studies of both basic justifications for harming (first volume) and the core of just war theory (second volume), my study of these particularly controversial topics in just war theory is, I submit, superior in terms of theoretical cohesion and systematicity to comparable studies in the field. 這個項目是我此前的優配研究金項目“正義戰爭論和暴力倫理”的延續。我當初預計寫一本書，但該項目現在已發展成三部曲：第一卷研究對使用武力的基本辯護，第二卷是關於正義戰爭理論的核心，第三卷则研究正義戰爭論中的特殊議題。第一卷業已完成，第二卷將需要多幾個月。我在此申請第三卷的優配研究金撥款。在三部曲中，我詳細描述和分析對使用武力的不同辯護，例如自衛，執法和懲處，還有特別是一些常被籠統地概括為“兩害取其輕”或“必要性”的辯護(但我們必須仔細區分兩者) 。然後我會系統地考量上述辯護在戰爭倫理中的應用範圍、界限和含義，論題涉及交戰雙方的道德操守（戰時法）和最初應否訴諸戰爭之（政治）決定的道德性（訴諸戰爭權）。在第三卷中（本申請的研究項目），我把這些研究結果應用於一些特殊議題，如人道主義干預，針對性殺戮，預防性戰爭，僱傭軍和私營軍事公司，游擊隊，軍閥，遙控武器（無人機），以及全自動武器。我的研究徑路值得關注的一點是，它跟當前流行的研究徑路不同，後者把關注點放在基於自衛的辯護和被攻擊對象本身的“責任” (也就是說，他們已喪失不被攻擊的權利) 。相反，我把德國法律中所謂“可作辯解的非常情況”的辯護放在論述的中心位置，並證明，關於戰爭中的合理傷害，我的研究徑路能指向一個相對於其他理論更具識別性的論述，以及對於我在第三卷中討論的正義戰爭論的特殊議題，具有深遠的理論和實踐含義。我對這些特殊議題的討論是牢固地建基於我此前關於對傷害的基本辯護（第一卷）和正義戰爭論的核心（第二卷）的深入研究，因此，我認為，我對正義戰爭論中這些特別具爭議性的話題的研究，在理論凝聚力和系統性方面都優於此領域其他可比較的研究。

17612817.label: Realisation of objectives
17612817.value: The objectives are completely met. I have written a chapter (or chapters) on almost each of the topics (some chapters cover more than one issue). The only two exceptions are: I have not yet written a separate chapter on preventive war, nor on terrorism, but the research on these topics is concluded, that is, I know exactly what to write. (I will present my research on terrorism at a conference in Salzburg in July.) I also would like to draw attention to three points where I have overachieved. The first regards the doctrine of double effect. While one cannot deal with terrorism from a philosophical perspective without dealing with said doctrine, I have done far more. To wit, I have published three articles on the doctrine of double effect that together comprise more than 33,000 words. Only a small part of this will go into the book (anything else would be overkill). I have also recently developed ideas on the moral force of widely accepted laws. This was not part of my original proposal, but now plays a significant role in it (see under 6.1). These ideas culminated so far in two papers (under review) of more than 25,000 words together. I have also produced a short paper on “border coercion,” applying my theories on the use of force to a very contested topic in immigration theory. In fact, this paper constitutes the bridge to the next GRF project I applied for, a project on global justice and the obligations towards (and also of) the poor.

17612817.label: Major findings and research outcome
17612817.value: This project is the third volume in a book trilogy that analyzes different justifications of the use of force, such as self-defense, law-enforcement and punishment, and a number of justifications that are often lumped together under the headings of “lesser evil” or “necessity,” and then systematically considers the scope, limits, and implications of each of these justifications with respect to the ethics of war, regarding both the moral conduct of combatants in war (jus in bello) and the morality of the (political) decision of resorting to war in the first place (jus ad bellum). In this third volume I apply these findings to special issues, such as humanitarian intervention, targeted killing, preventive war, mercenaries and private military companies, guerrillas, warlords, remote controlled weapons (drones), and fully automated weapons. Perhaps my main practical findings are that none of the usual fundamental moral doctrines – like, in particular, the jus ad bellum criteria of right intention and legitimate authority, and the jus in bello criterion of distinction (which is usually accompanied with an insistence on the doctrine of double effect) – that are invoked by some just war theorists (or politicians and the wider audience) successfully delegitimize the participation of unconventional actors in war; in fact, they cannot even absolutely delegitimize unconventional tactics like terrorism. On the constructive side, however, I argue that we need not rely on fundamental moral principles alone. To wit, I explain why instead of claiming that the laws of armed conflict must simply follow a pre-existing immutable morality or can otherwise be broken, we should (not uncritically, but with an eye to further improvement) regard widely accepted legal norms as themselves a civilizational achievement with moral force (and I explain in detail what mechanisms produce this moral force). This civilizational achievement should not be endangered by fundamentalist challenges – whether they come, for instance, from Eastern interpreters of the Quran or from Western philosophers interpreting their armchair intuitions. Humanity itself can, so to speak, cooperatively change the morality of war by converging on an international consensus. This leaves the playing field neither to fundamentalists nor to pacifists, but to rational political agents trying to hedge the destructive force of war without giving in to aggressors and bullies. Note: The first volume is under review with Routledge, if they accept it, they will also review the second volume. I have to wait until then before offering the third volume.

17612817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17612817.value: There is an emergent debate on whether "the global poor" may use force, including lethal force, against "the global rich" in order to make them abide by certain distributive duties the former allegedly have towards the letter. Much of this debate us conducted by political philosophers who appear to understand very little of the ethics of violence. I have applied for a research grant for a book on global justice, and a part of this project will consist of applying my research on the ethic of violence to said emerging debate.

17612817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17612817.value: In this project I apply my philosophical accounts of the justified use of force in general and of just justified warfare in particular to special issues, such as humanitarian intervention, targeted killing, preventive war, mercenaries and private military companies, guerrillas, warlords, remote controlled weapons (drones), and fully automated weapons. I argue that none of the usual fundamental moral doctrines invoked for this purpose by some theorists succeed in delegitimizing the participation of unconventional actors, or the use of unconventional tactics, in war. On the constructive side, I argue that we need not rely on fundamental moral principles alone. I explain why instead of claiming that the laws of armed conflict must simply follow a pre-existing immutable morality or can otherwise be broken, there are actually good reasons why we should (not uncritically, but with an eye to further improvement) regard widely accepted legal norms as themselves a civilizational achievement with moral force. Humanity itself can, so to speak, cooperatively change the morality of war by converging on an international consensus. This leaves the playing field neither to fundamentalists nor to pacifists, but to rational political agents trying to hedge the destructive force of war without giving in to unjust aggressors.

17613117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17613117.value: Some refugee law scholars and practitioners have questioned the continuing relevance of the 1951 Convention relating to the Status of Refugees and its 1967 Protocol (Refugee Convention). International human rights law has expanded rapidly since 1951 and, in principle, applies to all human beings including refugees. General and specialised United Nations (UN) treaties and the interpretive materials produced by human rights monitoring bodies have further clarified states’ obligations to protect refugees and other migrants beyond the confines of the Refugee Convention. As a result, some have argued that the broader remit of international human rights law could supersede, or at least supplement, the Refugee Convention’s more conditional provisions (Chetail, Harvey). Others have maintained that the Refugee Convention’s specialised rights are of particular relevance to the refugee experience and that it provides a workable framework for balancing the needs of refugees with the rights of states to control their borders (Hathaway, McAdam). This study aims to contribute to this debate by examining the application of international human rights law to refugee protection in Asian states not party to the Refugee Convention. The potential impact of more recent international human rights treaties on the protection of refugees has particular significance in Asia since only nine of twenty-seven states and jurisdictions in three Asian sub-regions have acceded to the Convention. Given this relatively small number and continuing resistance to accession, some claim that Asia has essentially “rejected” refugee law (Davies). Others suggest that these states have nevertheless developed some legal refugee protection responses – and there is potential for further reform - even in the absence of the Refugee Convention (M Jones, Loper). Asian states, however, have all ratified at least two core UN human rights treaties: the Convention on the Elimination of all forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) and the Convention on the Rights of the Child (CRC). CEDAW's monitoring body has clarified that states parties must ensure refugee women and girls are protected from discrimination, including serious violations if sent to another state. Article 22 of the CRC requires that states take appropriate measures to protect the rights of child refugees. Although this study will consider all UN core international human rights instruments, it will focus on the application of CEDAW and the CRC in Asia in particular. It will analyse the impact of states’ interaction with the international human rights regime on the development of refugee law in the region. 一些難民法學者和工作者質疑「1951年難民地位公約」及其1967年之議定書（「難民公約」）的持續相關性。國際人權法自1951年以來迅速擴大，原則上適用於包括難民在內的所有人。聯合國的一般及專門條約及人權監督組織編寫的詮釋材料，進一步澄清了各國保護難民和其他移民的義務超越「難民公約」的限制。因此，有人認為，國際人權法更廣泛的職權可以取代或至少補充「難民公約」較有條件的條款。另外有人則認為，「難民公約」的專門權利與難民經驗尤其相關，為平衡難民需求及國家控制邊界的權利提供​​一個可行的框架。針對這辯論，是次研究旨在探討國際人權法在非「難民公約」締約國之亞洲國家在難民保護上的應用。近期有關難民保護的國際人權條約對亞洲的潛在影響尤為重要，因為在三個亞洲區域二十七個國家和地區中只有九個加入了「公約」。鑑於較少地區加入「公約」及其對加入「公約」持續抗拒，有人提出亞洲本質上是「拒絕」了難民法。儘管如此，有人則認為，儘管沒有「難民公約」，這些國家仍然制定了一些合法的難民保護措施，並有進一步改革的潛力。然而，亞洲國家已經批准了至少兩項核心聯合國人權條約：「消除對婦女一切形式歧視公約」和「兒童權利公約」。「消除對婦女一切形式歧視公約」的監察機構解釋，締約國必須確保難民婦女和女孩得到保護，不受歧視，包括在被送往另一個國家的情況下的嚴重違規行為。「兒童權利公約」第22條要求各國採取適當措施保護兒童難民的權利。雖然是次研究將考慮所有聯合國核心的國際人權文書，但會將重點放在「消除對婦女一切形式歧視公約」和「兒童權利公約」在亞洲的應用。它將分析國家與國際人權制度相互作用對各地區之難民法發展的影響。

17613117.label: Realisation of objectives
17613117.value: Objective 1: My research team analysed the interpretive materials produced by the United Nations (UN) human rights treaty monitoring bodies for the core UN human rights treaties from 2013 until 2020 to clarify the content of international human rights law as it applies to refugee protection. These materials were accessible on the website of the Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights. We searched the treaty bodies’ general comments, views on individual communications, and concluding comments on state reports for key words including refugee(s), asylum, asylum seeker(s), migrant(s), and (non-)refoulement and collated the results in tables. We went beyond the initial focus on the Convention on the Elimination of all Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) and the Convention on the Rights of the Child (CRC) to include all of the core UN human rights treaties which apply to at least one jurisdiction in the region not bound by the 1951 Convention relating to the status of Refugees or its 1967 Protocol (Refugee Convention). In addition to CEDAW and the CRC, these instruments include: the Covenant on the Elimination of all forms of Racial Discrimination, the Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR), the Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, the Convention against Torture and other Forms of Cruel, Inhuman or Degrading Treatment or Punishment (CAT), the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, the Convention on the Protection of the Rights of all Migrant Workers and their Families, and the Convention for the Protection of all Persons from Enforced Disappearances. We also extended the timeframe to include documents produced through the end of 2020 to account for the effect of the COVID-19 pandemic on the treaty bodies’ work. The pandemic has had a profound impact on state responses to refugees and human rights protection generally. This generated initial data on how treaty bodies have factored these developments into their interpretations. For example, the data supplies new insights about when states can legitimately restrict rights, an important unresolved question in international law. During this period, all treaty bodies increasingly called on states to ensure refugee rights. The data, therefore, supported several conclusions about the nature of states’ obligations toward refugees which are particularly relevant to states not party to the Refugee Convention. Objective 2: While reviewing these materials, we identified the particular concerns raised by the treaty bodies when reviewing the reports of Asian states not party to the Refugee Convention. This data contributed to an evaluation of the treaty bodies’ approach to refugee-related concerns when states deny that specific refugee norms apply. We also conducted qualitative interviews with advocates in Hong Kong, India, Bangladesh, Malaysia, Thailand, and Indonesia. These conversations provided background information and views on whether (or how) international human rights law has influenced advocacy strategies and the effectiveness of treaty body interventions on states’ policies toward refugees. Events in Hong Kong in 2019 and the global pandemic since 2020 presented some obstacles. Since I was unable to travel as originally planned, I could not conduct interviews in person with advocates outside of Hong Kong (except for 3 interviews when attending the 7th Asia Pacific Consultation on Refugee Rights in October 2018). I was also unable to acquire a first-hand perspective on refugee issues in context. I completed interviews via Zoom, but received fewer responses than expected. The difficulties the pandemic posed for advocates in their work as well as their personal lives may partially account for the low response rate. I also needed to spend significantly more time than expected on teaching responsibilities to redevelop courses for online teaching. Face to face classes were impacted by the Hong Kong protests in 2019 and the pandemic in 2020 and 2021. Objective 3: Based on the analysis of treaty body materials and interviews, the study tested and supported the proposition that international human rights law has greater potential to contribute to legal protections for refugees in Asian states not party to the Refugee Convention. For example, the results support the emergence of stand-alone non-refoulement duties in specialised treaties beyond CAT and the ICCPR. In CEDAW, this duty is clarified through the CEDAW Committee’s interpretation of the nature of gender-based violence as a form of discrimination against women. This is especially important in jurisdictions not bound by CAT, the ICCPR or the Refugee Convention such as Malaysia, which hosts large numbers of asylum seekers. The treaty body materials have also expounded a richer understanding of the nature of torture and other forms of cruel inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment, socio-economic rights, the right to equality, principles of human dignity, and associated state obligations as they apply to refugees. The project team also sourced domestic case law from Hong Kong, India, and Bangladesh. These judgments illustrate methods employed by advocates and courts when applying international human rights norms to refugee rights claims. Despite the difficulties presented by dualist legal systems, and other barriers to local incorporation of international human rights, advocates have developed creative strategies. Objectives 4 and 5 The project’s output has contributed, and is expected to continue to contribute, to debates about 1) the continuing relevance of the Refugee Convention in light of developments in international human rights law and 2) the effectiveness of international human rights law generally, in Asia, and in relation to refugees. This has been achieved by sharing the study’s results with academic and non-academic audiences in scholarly publications, conference presentations, and knowledge exchange and other research activities (listed in Part C). I will continue to produce output based on the study and identify new opportunities for contribution and ongoing impact. For example, the following research output is in progress: 1. Book: International Human Rights Law and Refugee Protection in Asia (under consideration by Cambridge University Press). 2. Journal article: “The right to freedom of movement in international human rights law, exit restrictions and refugee protection” (peer-reviewed submission for a special issue of International Migration). 3. Conference paper: “Equality and non-discrimination and the rights of refugees in international human rights law” (Berkeley Center on Comparative Equality & Anti-Discrimination Law, 22-24 June 2022). 4. Conference paper: “Refugee Law in Hong Kong and China” (University of Virginia, 11-12 August 2022). 5. Conference paper: “The right to freedom of movement in international human rights law and exit restrictions” (American Political Science Association, Montreal, 15-18 September 2022). The project’s initial output focuses on the application of international human rights law in Hong Kong. In Asia, Hong Kong has gone the furthest in developing legal responses to refugees based on international human rights obligations. In particular, a successful litigation strategy resulted in a Unified Screening Mechanism which considers a range of non-refoulement claims. Because of the incorporation of the ICCPR into Hong Kong’s constitutional framework and the judiciary’s openness to citing comparative human rights materials, international human rights law has had a significant impact. Hong Kong also illustrates the limits of international human rights law in the absence of more specific Refugee Convention rights. Pandemic travel restrictions made it easier to conduct interviews and access materials locally. Additional publications will consider other jurisdictions in the region and provide comparative perspectives.

17613117.label: Major findings and research outcome
17613117.value: The results support empirical, doctrinal and normative conclusions. UN human rights treaty bodies have provided increasing detail on the application of general human rights norms to refugees. These developments have informed refugee-related advocacy, judicial decisions, and policies in jurisdictions not bound by the Refugee Convention. The study’s findings illustrate real impact and contribute to debates about the effectiveness of international human rights law, especially in Asia. They also indicate, however, that human rights law has been underutilized. Some specific findings include: Treaty body interpretations have extended the non-refoulement obligations in CAT and the ICCPR. Specialised treaty bodies, especially CEDAW, have articulated stand-alone non-refoulement duties and contributed to a fuller understanding of the nature of ill treatment. The right to equality in international human rights law has particular potential. All jurisdictions in Asia are bound by specialised treaties which emphasise substantive equality. Treaty bodies have also recognised intersectional discrimination experienced by refugees. Although decision-makers in Hong Kong and elsewhere have paid insufficient attention to intersectionality, there is greater scope for creative legal arguments. Hong Kong courts have developed a robust equality jurisprudence grounded in international human rights that might be better leveraged in refugee rights advocacy. (See Part C: e.g. “Gender and Constitutionalism in Hong Kong”, “Exponential Crises and Intersecting Inequalities: The View from Hong Kong”, “Domestic Refugee Law: Hong Kong and China”, “Dignity as a Constitutional Value in Hong Kong: Toward a Contextual Approach?”). The treaty bodies have provided guidance on determining justifiable limits on certain rights, such as freedom of movement, which impact refugees. In recent years, national security concerns have presented obstacles to refugee protection in many jurisdictions, including Hong Kong. Materials from 2020 also highlight the impact of restrictive COVID-19 policies. The study’s output examines the capacity of international human rights law to resolve these tensions. Paradoxically, crisis can create momentum and present opportunities for reliance on international human rights when advocating for better refugee responses (“Exponential Crises and Intersecting Inequalities: The View from Hong Kong”). The study identifies gaps in international human rights law’s ability to realise refugee rights and therefore reaffirms the significance of the Refugee Convention. Although the findings support a holistic approach to refugee rights, states in the region are likely to continue to resist accession to the Refugee Convention. In this context, building on available legal norms is preferable to reliance on political pressure or humanitarian impulses alone.

17613117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17613117.value: There is significant potential for further development of the research. For example, I intend to build on the study’s empirical observation that international human rights bodies are increasingly concerned with the rights of refugees when interpreting general human rights norms. I am particularly interested in the capacity of the right to equality to address intersectional discrimination experienced by non-citizens. This includes individuals and groups who face disadvantage based on their immigration status as well as other characteristics such as sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, ethnic origin, age, etc. States have frequently justified differential treatment toward non-citizens through a single-axis lens without taking intersectional realities into account. Related output will also continue to contribute to doctrinal and normative theories about when rights can be legitimately restricted. The research will also extend my work on human dignity in international human rights law, including its relevance for theories about the nature of citizenship and concepts of democratic participation. Questions about the rights of non-citizens are at the frontiers of scholarship on international human rights law as well as comparative equality law. I plan to apply for an external research grant to pursue this project in 2022.

17613117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17613117.value: Most Asian jurisdictions, including Hong Kong, have consistently rejected calls to accept application of the specific refugee rights set out in the Refugee Convention. As a result, many governments in the region claim they have no particular international legal obligations toward refugees arriving at their borders. At the same time, the number of refugees in these countries has increased and any real prospects for durable, long-term solutions remain dim. This study clarifies that international human rights treaties which apply to all states in Asia also create legal duties to realise a range of refugee rights. While these international standards have already impacted refugee policy in some jurisdictions, recent interpretations of international norms expand our understanding of the nature of refugee rights and suggest that advocates, courts and policy-makers could make better use of human rights instruments to achieve progressive change. Despite ongoing challenges, such as weak international enforcement mechanisms and domestic implementation, the study concludes that international human rights law has greater potential than previously realised. It contends that government responses to refugees grounded in binding international human rights law are preferable to sporadic reactions based solely on political or humanitarian considerations.

17613217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17613217.value: With the advent of new media, it is not surprising that in many places around the world people have been convicted of crimes based on speech that they made online, just as people may commit the same crimes offline. Common offences associated with online speech include threat, intimidation, incitement, solicitation, and the like. Criminal convictions based purely on speech need to receive particular scrutiny for their direct impact on the freedom of speech. Communication on new media has characteristics that distinguish itself from face to face communication and communication on traditional mass media. For example, the boundary between spoken and written language has become blurred in speech made on new media, and so has the dichotomy between public and private speech. These characteristics have profound implications for the analysis of criminal speech acts made on new media. The proposed interdisciplinary project investigates the challenges that communication on new media poses to the legal analysis of language crimes, both in the determination of mens rea (guilty mind) and of actus reas (guilty act). Adopting analytical frameworks from interaction linguistics and linguistic pragmatics, the first part of the project seeks to identify contextual factors that are potentially pertinent to the analysis of alleged language crimes committed on new media. Through studying recent case law, legal enforcement actions and legislative changes from different common law jurisdictions (especially UK, US, India and Hong Kong), the second part of the project will compare how jurisdictions meet with such challenges and comment on divergence in approaches. Finally, the third part of the project considers the implications of my findings for freedom of speech, and contributes to the debate on the impact of Internet on public discourse. Together the proposed project paints a picture of crime and its enforcement in the modern communication environment, critiques shortcomings in existing approaches to the tackling of language crimes, and raises broad questions about individual liberty, freedom of speech, and collective safety. 無論在網絡或現實世界 ， 言論都可以構成罪行。 隨著新媒體的流行， 近年在很多國家都有不少人因網上言論而觸犯法律。常見罪行包括威脅、恐嚇、煽惑和唆使他人犯罪等。 純粹由言論構成的刑事定罪涉及言論自由的領域， 所以特別需要仔細檢察。 人與人在新媒體上的互動， 有一些別於面對面溝通或傳統媒體的特質。 例如，在新媒體發表的言論是屬於口語抑或書面語、 該平台是公共或私人空間， 區別都變得不明顯。 這些區別可能影響對涉嫌違法言論的推理。 本計劃研究新媒體如何為言論罪行(language crime)的法律推理帶來挑戰，牽涉到「犯罪心態」(mens rea) 與「犯罪行為」(actus reas) 的考慮。利用互動語言學(interactional linguistics)和語用學(pragmatics)的分析框架， 本計劃的第一部份旨在識別新媒體有何特殊語境可能影響言論罪行的推理。 本計劃的第二部份繼而比較不同普通法地區(如英、美，和香港) 的案例和執法手段， 探討各地如何應付這些挑戰。 第三部份衡量研究成果對網民和國家的含義， 並解讀社會上意識形態(尤其針對網上言論的責任問題)的改變如何觸及法律思考。 整個計劃展示出現代溝通環境下以言犯罪和執法的景象， 評論現行處理言論罪行方法的不足， 並提出關於個人自由、 言論自由和公共安全的宏觀問題。

17613217.label: Realisation of objectives
17613217.value: Due to the social movement and the subsequently the pandemic, the project has experienced delays. I was able to participate in various online events that helped me refine some of my research ideas, but my ability to travel overseas to conduct in-depth cross-jursidictional analyses were more limited than intended. Consequently, there is a sizable unspent budget. My original plan was to publish three shorter articles (7000-8000 words), each tackling a particular area of the online-offline equivalence problem. However, my plan changed as my research developed. In the end, it makes more sense for the work to be published as a longer piece. My main research output uses interdisciplinary approach to examine how online language crimes are analyzed, which was published as a journal article (16452 words) in the Journal of International Media & Entertainment Law, a publication of the Donald E. Biederman Entertainment and Media Law Institute at Southwestern Law School in cooperation with the American Bar Association’s Forum on Communications Law and the ABA’s Forum on the Entertainment and Sports Industries.

17613217.label: Major findings and research outcome
17613217.value: My project has generated an extended research journal article in a top-tier law journal, six conference presentations/invited talks, one news report, and one podcast interview. My journal article identifies and dissects three distinctive features of the digital audience, including audience agency, audience obscurity, and audience dislocation, and illustrates their pertinence in the legal interpretation of online speech crimes. The analysis shows that these digital audience characteristics have the effect of enlarging existing jurisprudential gaps. The judicial challenge is particularly evident when judges have to apply laws that were developed in the mass communications era to digital communication, because such laws often contain assumptions about the audience that are no longer accurate. Case law from different common law jurisdictions in public order offenses, harassment and stalking, and threat are used as illustrative examples, along with recommendations about context-sensitive adjustments in the legal interpretation of each of these language crimes. Overall, I demonstrate the kind of interdisciplinary contextual analysis that would benefit a legal system in adapting to the challenges of a new and rapidly evolving speech environment.

17613217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17613217.value: Apart from the journal publication, I have obtained data and conducted analyses that will inform further research. Specifically, I have won the Humanities and Social Sciences Prestigious Fellowship Scheme which will allow me to further examine the topic and produce further work.

17613217.value: This project studies the changing ways in which people express themselves and interact with one another in the digital age, and how their expressions are regulated by private and public bodies. I compare different jurisdictions to see how their online speech crimes cases are analysed. My research shows that digital audience characteristics have enlarged existing jurisprudential gaps.

17613417.label: Project Objectives
17613417.value: To chart out the genealogies of cultural security discourse among epistemic and academic communities in China and Saudi Arabia, explain their evolution in light of changing domestic and international trends relevant to each country, and analyze the dynamics underlying the state’s adoption of this discourse. To understand how states practice cultural security through a number of case studies, showcasing the multiple types of cultural security threats confronting such regimes as a result of their legitimacy matrixes, the coherence and common logic of regime responses across these disparate case studies, and the contradictory pressures facing such regimes in both protecting regime legitimacy on the one hand and upholding their modernization projects in the other. Explaining how the conceptualization and practice of cultural security in these two states emanates as a response to the dialogic interaction between the regime types of China and Saudi Arabia and the international conditions they face.
