17616217.label: Major findings and research outcome
17616217.value: The two quantitative studies offer important insights into the dynamics of policy attention under different types of leadership in an authoritarian context. Under more established leaders who rule as "strongmen", policy attention tends to be more unstable across time, inter-organizationally more aligned, and more concentrated than more contested leaders who see themselves as stewards and hence rule co-optatively. In the qualitative follow-up, we study the behavioural foundations to this contrast in the pattern of policy attention. We draw qualitative observations on how Chinese bureaucrats handle their mandate to review and regulate film production differently under two different leaders. Authoritarian leaders who engages in preference articulation more frequently may trigger strategic response among bureaucrats that create macro-level patterns documented in the quantitative analysis.

17616217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17616217.value: Further research should cover more of the issues that are brought up in the qualitative analysis, with a focus on specific domains that vary in key policy attributes such as salience, the degree of wickedness, and complexity. While our study has addressed the behavioural foundation of policy attention, further studies that draw upon experimental design can help further decipher how human cognitive architecture can affect attention allocation at the individual level. Another problem of interest that our project brought up is concerned with the link between leadership style and policy attention in different political context. Our study has focused only on the authoritarian regime; further research can compare the link between the democratic and authoritarian contexts.

17616217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17616217.value: 4. Public policymaking is often assumed to be a linear rational process that goes through the stages of problem identification, policy formulation, decision making, and policy implementation. Prior research, however, has suggested that public policymaking in real-life is more complex and recursive, often driven by agenda-setting dynamics underlined by institutions and also the cognitive architecture of human beings. This study deciphers how the dynamics of agenda-setting play out in China where policymaking takes place in an authoritarian institutional setting. Among various institutional and contextual factors, we have found that the leadership style of the supreme leader significantly affects other policy actors’ behavioural responses, giving rise to unique patterns of attention allocation and hence agenda-setting. An interesting pattern is that while the “strongman” leadership style can bring about better alignment of attention across sectors, it also causes policy instability and rapid changes.

17616517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17616517.value: Emerging natural resources are naturally occurring substances that were not previously considered valuable natural resources but are increasingly subject to economically viable exploitation resulting from technological advances or socioeconomic changes. Novel legal issues inevitably accompany these newfound sources of economic value, particularly in the case of resources that could not be meaningfully interfered with or modified by human endeavor prior to recent technological advances. The most prominent of these issues is property rights: who owns, or should own, emerging natural resources. The state? The landowner? The people—however defined? Some other entity and/or ownership arrangement? Another pertinent issue is uncertainty. By their very definition, emerging natural resources are exploited by recently developed and typically still-evolving technologies. How should the law, regulation and state policies respond to this state of flux and to the uncertainties concerning the effects—both intended and unintended—that commonly plague new technologies? I propose to address these key legal issues through an analysis on China’s regulatory regime for climate resources. Climate resources as a category of emerging natural resources is a good candidate for the research given how it contain several distinct emerging natural resources (e.g., sunlight, wind, atmospheric moisture) that have meaningful distinction in resources characteristics and utilization patterns while sharing the broad similarity of being connected with the atmosphere. I have chosen to focus on China because of its official recognition on the importance of climate resources in general, unlike the more piecemeal treatment in other jurisdictions. This renders the investigation of the Chinese regime of important practical significance, whether in terms of assisting legal practitioners, or informing relevant legal reforms in other jurisdictions. I will write a monograph that synthesizes the legal and normative insights from these case studies of how specific climate resource are regulated in China into an overarching theoretical framework for evaluating the management of emerging natural resources. The theoretical framework would focus on the aforementioned twin salient issues of property rights arrangements and the handling of scientific uncertainties, but with an eye towards the factors affecting when and how particular forms of state intervention (e.g., regulation, tax, state ownership, public contract, government speech) are more efficacious than others. 17616617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17616617.value: Depression in late life is a common and costly psychiatric disorder. It is one of the leading cause of disability worldwide and accounts for a significant contribution to the global disease burden. It is estimated that 15.7% of the total population in Hong Kong will be aged 65 or over by 2021, where more than 50% has only received no to primary level of education and between 9.3% and 9.7% are presented with clinically significant depressive symptoms and an elevated suicidal risk. Findings also indicated that 26% of the elderlies attending primary care clinics demonstrated clinically significant symptoms of depression or anxiety. This would impose a substantial burden to the health care system and the society at large. The development and provision of a broader range of evidence based interventions that can be delivered at an earlier stage for elderlies with depressive symptoms is needed. This study will ride on our research project, Holistic Support Programme on Mental Health for Older People and will constitute an important extension. It will be the first to compare the effectiveness of CBT/ExAT intervention treatment protocols for depression in late life with treatment as usual control. CBT a verbally inclined and relatively cognitively demanding psychotherapy model. It is considered to be an efficacious treatment for depression with substantial empirical evidence and is one of the recommended treatment of choice. Yet, it is conceded that further empirical research in application of CBT in late life depression is needed. ExAT is another potential choice of intervention and is considered to be a non-verbally inclined psychotherapy model. It is also relatively less demanding in skills and cognitive performance. In a pilot research of the ExAT intervention on 11 elderlies, improvement in depression, anxiety, and life satisfaction were observed. The preliminary data demonstrates the model's feasibility and potential. If proven to be effective, the service implication of the results will not only be the provision of empirically proven effective non-pharmacological treatments to elderlies with depression, but will also be deployable to elderly community centers that are readily accessible to elderlies in need at the local community level. Knowledge wise, the findings of the study will contribute to further research on the role of verbal/non-verbal psychological construct processing with socio-education-economic factors taken into consideration. The possibility of being able to mainstream these intervention protocols and professionals into existing elderly service may also pose an impact on the development of elderly social policy.

17616817.label: Project Objectives
17616817.value: An examination of the tendency to challenge the urban context in literary and filmic texts written and produced in the 2000s, which adopt an ecocritical theoretical framework to highlight the intricate relationship between the human and non-human. A study of how the mutation of urban and rural landscapes is used to convey not only the perpetual cycle of demolition and construction but also the destruction of hope within the nation. A discussion of the relationship between rural and urban landscapes, and the way that the former is reimagined by portraying new relationships with land, water, animals and other entities that have been transformed by China’s current market economy. An expansion of the scope of the field of literary and film studies by including the spheres of everyday life, the renewed relationship with the non-human world, and urban culture. An examination of the significance of ecological reflections and a focus on the quotidian in dealing with transformations of post-socialist China. A contribution to the established field of ecocriticism in the West, which demonstrates the power of this type of criticism to illuminate a variety of texts across cultures.

17616817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17616817.value: In China, as well as other parts of the world, works that connect urbanization, ruins and art reflect a growing trend and tell an inconvenient truth. The past decade was witness to China’s exhibition of its power. The same decade, however, saw a massive loss of life in natural disasters, and a perpetual demolition and construction that led to the displacement of Chinese people in the name of progress. A sense of the uncanny has become part of the daily life of China. The proposed project explores the relationship of ruins, everyday life and creativity in post-socialist Chinese literary and filmic texts. It examines the ways in which literature and independent films have become effective means of drawing attention to both the reckless development and the depletion of rural life due to marketization and globalization. The project will shed light on the impact of urbanization and modernization on nature, urban landscapes and the quotidian by analyzing literary and filmic texts. This projects looks at five subjects that are of great consequence to contemporary Chinese writers and filmmakers – the rural landscape, water, animals, the city, and commodities – and traces the ways these subjects are discussed, appropriated, challenged, and reflected upon. Rather than dealing directly with environmental issues, these writers and filmmakers forge a new relationship with nature and the countryside, which shapes their identity and allows them to come to terms with the realities of post-socialist China. This project surveys the shared concerns and interests of selected contemporary Chinese writers and filmmakers, and explores their strategies to address the uncontrollable urban development that has caused damage on many levels – ideological, social, cultural and even personal. Their works lend themselves to ecocritical analysis and open up new subjects for reflection. The discussion section of the proposed project will draw from the rich scholarship of ecocriticism to provide a framework broad enough to encompass the non-human world. The main objectives of the project are to provide an overview of the trends of literature and independent filmmaking in post-2000s China, to explore the ways in which contemporary Chinese writers and filmmakers recuperate the essential elements of the non-human world to make sense of the post-Socialist reality, to examine the new nexus between rural and urban landscapes, and to provide a preliminary report on the way these authors imagine their identity and their position in China’s cultural history. 當代的中國藝術與廢墟意象及都市化有著緊密的關係, 在過去的十年, 因著發展之名, 民眾承受著天災及過度發展的結果, 不少人因都市化而失去家園, 或為了尋找工作, 離開農村過著散居的生活。本計劃以後社會主義時期中國的文學及獨立電影作研究的文本, 旨在探討日常生活、廢墟意象及創作之間的關係, 反思這兩種藝術媒介如何有效討論一種欠缺周詳計劃的城市發展, 及對市場及全球經濟的盲目亢奮, 在在對自然、城市生態、及民眾日常生活造成破壞。 本計劃以鄉郊、水、動物、城市、及物件五個主題作為討論的重心, 揭示並分析作家及獨立導演如何通過對這些命題的處理及想像, 重新建構城市與鄉郊、人與及動物、個人與國家的關係。本計劃探討當代中國作家及獨立導演對過度發展及生態被破壞的共同關注, 反思個人、文化、社會及意識形態與創作的千絲萬縷關係。以豐富的中國當代獨立電影及文學為縱, 以當下的西方生態研究為軸, 本計劃將有效梳理自2000年以來, 當代中國文學及獨立電影的面貌, 分析作家及導演處理後社會主義時期的現實狀況, 反思城鄉之間的互補、人與動物之間的關係、審視自然、人與物的互為緊扣, 並討論這一批重要的作家及導演在中國文學及獨立電影景觀中的位置。

17616817.label: Realisation of objectives
17616817.value: The six stated objectives have been achieved in the following ways: 1. Examining the Urban Context in Literary and Filmic Texts via an Eco-critical Lens At the early stage of the project, an extensive library research has been conducted with the help of the Research Assistant which located and identified the important literary works and films that touch upon landscape, waterscape, animals and urbanscape in post-socialist era. These data provided me an essential overview of how Chinese writers and filmmakers appropriated environmental approaches in articulating social reality, and served as important resources for my papers and invited talks. 2. Studying the Mutation of Urban and Rural Landscapes The project examined the ways in which literature and independent films have become effective means of drawing attention to both the reckless development and the depletion of rural life due to marketization and globalization. The research data shed light on the impact of urbanization and modernization on nature, urban landscapes and the quotidian by analyzing literary and filmic texts. The three subjects: rural landscape, the city, and commodities are discussed, appropriated, challenged, and reflected upon by contemporary Chinese writer Yan Lianke and filmmaker Wang Bing. Their works exhibit the way they imagine their identity and their position in China’s cultural history by recuperating the essential elements of the non-human world and examining the nexus between rural and urban landscape. (“Liminal Space and Uncanny Landscapes: In Search of Ecotopian Visions in Post-Socialist Chinese Literature and Film”) 3. Discussing New Relationships with Land, Water, Animals and Other Entities under China’s Current Market Economy Works of contemporary Chinese writers reflect an awareness of the combined social and economic consequences of China’s post-socialist experience. The project analyzed the way these works portrayed the ruin of nature and the withering of human and non-human life under the uncontrollable forces of globalism. By focusing on the consequences of progress for the non-human world, Jian Rong and Mo Yan writers insist on the interconnectedness of humans with all other living things. The research data provided a critical analysis on the role of animals in literary texts in post-Socialist China and illuminate the ways animals are juxtaposed with the Chinese people and become channels for desire, instinct and emotion. (“Consuming Animals in Post-socialist Chinese Literature”) In Jia Zhangke’s Still Life (2006), Yung Chang’s Up the Yangtze (2007), and Dong Jun’s Flood (2008), human actions are embodied in their waterscapes. The selected works articulate a kind of ethical ecology that infuses the material world with the moral consequences of historical events. Borrowing Stacy Alaimo’s discussion of posthumanism and trans-corporeality, I see the waterscape as an idea that binds together various eras of Chinese history, while representing a new mode of inquiry. The research project unveiled nature as a space through which individuals project their feelings regarding the land and their cultural lineage, and their frustration with the dominant ideology, which often insists on the necessity of urban development. In the case of rivers, mega-dams and uncanny landscapes, the subtle, invisible changes associated with globalism, post-socialism and urbanization are brought to visibility. These spaces serve as sites of empowerment, where filmmakers can use artistic experiments to challenge the existing order and unleash the energy of creation. (“The Recurrent Dream of Currents and Undercurrents: Revisiting the Cultural Imaginary of Waterscape in Post-socialist Chinese Independent Cinema”) 4. Revisiting the Notion of Everyday Life in the Age of the Anthropocene The growth of consumerism in post-socialist China, particularly in cities such as Beijing and Shanghai, are important pointers to examine the socio-cultural scene of Mainland China. While critiquing the way spectacular cities promote empty promises and contribute to the disillusionment of the masses, Wang Anyi and Yu Hua reveal everyday spaces as the sites of ethical discussion at the current critical juncture when China is consolidating its role as world power. The multifaceted everyday world is infernal, oppressive, and highly commodified; however, both writers, in their different ways, also show the possibilities of forming alternative communities and creating alliances (“Commodification, Everyday Life and the Spectral Urbanscape”) 5. Examining the Significance of Ecological Reflections In understanding the significance of ecological reflections in the age of the Anthropocene, analyses of the relationship between human and non-human world in literary and filmic texts would be particularly instructive. Jia Zhangke’s films and Mo Yan’s historical fictions present the development of modern Chinese society from the perspective of animals, and deal with humans’ carnivorous cravings, consumption and production. By using animal metaphors for human actions and giving animals human attributes, Mo and Jia mock the cannibalism of the new China. The theories of scholars such as Jacques Derrida, Timothy Morton, Cary Wolfe and Stacy Alaimo inform the foundation of this research. (“Animalscape and the Condition of Existence in Jia Zhangke’s Two Films”) 6. Contributing to the Field of Ecocriticism in the West through Cross-cultural Dialogues Subjects of this research project are crucial to the general debates related to the Anthropocene and climate change. Examples and analyses of Chinese literary and filmic texts facilitate further reflections of urbanization and globalization in cross-cultural contexts. My project allowed me to engage in dialogue with international scholars and explore collaborative initiatives with scholars from different disciplines who share a commitment to building a sustainable future. I took part in in-depth discussions circled around recent debates of representation of environment and nature and subsequently many rigorous debates are provoked in relation to China, cinema and literary studies. (“The Urban in the Ruins: Ecotopian in Chinese Literary Texts”; “Disenchantment and Re-enchantment in the Ruins: Jia Zhangke and His Experiments in Chinese Urban Cinema”).

17616817.label: Major findings and research outcome
17616817.value: This focused study on post-socialist Chinese literature and cinema from an ecocritical point of view has produced 2 journal articles, 5 conference papers, 2 invited talks and 1 book manuscript. Proposal of the book project has been sent to varied university presses and to be followed up. The full manuscript is expected to be sent out for full review in the course of 2022. The items are as follows: Journal articles: (1) “Writing the Therapeutic Waterscape: Bodies, Memories, and Nature in Post-socialist Chinese Texts.” (2) “Ghostly Chronotopes: Spectral Cityscapes in Post-2000 Chinese Literature.” Conference papers: (3) “The Recurrent Dream of Currents and Undercurrents: Revisiting the Cultural Imaginary of Waterscape in Post-socialist Chinese Independent Cinema,” (4) “Liminal Space and Uncanny Landscape: In Search of Ecotopian Visions in Post-Socialist Chinese Literature and Film.” (5) “Consuming Animals in Post-socialist Chinese Literature” (6) “Commodification, Everyday Life, and the Spectral Urbanscape.” (7) “Animalscape and the Condition of Existence in Jia Zhangke’s Two Films,” Invited talks: (8) “Disenchantment and Re-enchantment in the Ruins: Jia Zhangke and His Experiments in Chinese Urban Cinema.” (9) ““The Urban in the Ruins: Ecotopia in Chinese Literary Texts.” Between ruination and urbanization In this project, the connections between the urban uncanny, the alienation from rural landscapes, and the portrayal of the quotidian in Chinese literature and independent films of the 2000s have been examined. Contemporary texts provide reflections on the subtle changes that are more clearly registered in the quotidian space and urge us to deal with the problems that have emerged in post-socialist China. These arguments are made in (2), (6), and (8). Between the human and the non-human worlds Rural landscapes represent an alternative, utopian, home that one longs to return to, in contrast to the alienating urban world. Discussions of their varied depictions of urban life and reconfigurations of the rural-urban relationship illuminate the complex history of post-socialist China, and the relationship between the human and the non-human worlds are examined in (1), (3), (5), and (7). The creativity of the quotidian space This project stresses the ways in which the quotidian space is intimately associated with creative experimentation. It examines the constant negotiation between rural and urban landscapes in today’s China, and in the world of the authors and filmmakers who grew up in China’s countryside. Discussions about ghosts, distorted landscapes, neglected animals and uncontrollable nature in an effort to rewrite the current image of China are recorded in (2), (4), and (9).

17616817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17616817.value: In this study, the ways Chinese literary writers and filmmakers witness, articulate, and challenge our relationship with the world have been pointed out. Their works represent a range of perspectives—ethical, affective, and quotidian. The current project has critically reflected on the human and non-human relationship, the detrimental impact of irresponsible urban development, and the ways narratives have to make sense of social reality. While continued attention should be paid on how Chinese authors respond to the age of the Anthropocene, the research output also opens up other kind of dialogues within Asia. While Asian nations face their own set of ecological challenges, all share a concern for their effects on urban life and the state of the environment. China’s waste issue; Thailand and Vietnam suffer from water pollution; and Japan struggles to cope with both natural and nuclear disasters. Documentaries and literary works produced in these countries in the past decades show the ways in which rapid urban development has led to the massive destruction of nature and has had a negative impact on everyday life. A comparative study of these works would enable us to determine how environmental issues have brought about a change in perspective in Asia.

17616817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17616817.value: In China, works that connect urbanization, ruins and art reflect a growing trend and tell an inconvenient truth. This study explores the relationship of ruins, everyday life and creativity in post-socialist Chinese texts. It examines the ways in which literature and independent films have become effective means of drawing attention to the reckless development and the depletion of rural life due to marketization and globalization. Through exploring five subjects – the rural landscape, water, animals, the city, and commodities – and tracing the ways these subjects are discussed, appropriated, challenged, and reflected upon, this study confirms that Chinese writers and independent filmmakers have successfully addressed the uncontrollable urban development that has caused damage on many levels – ideological, social, cultural and even personal. Their works lend themselves to ecocritical analysis and open up new subjects for reflection. This study provides an overview of the trends of literature and independent filmmaking in post-2000s China, explores the ways in which contemporary Chinese writers and filmmakers recuperate the essential elements of the non-human world to make sense of the post-Socialist reality, examines the new nexus between rural and urban landscapes, and provides a preliminary report on the way these authors imagine their identity.

17617617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17617617.value: 二十世紀中葉，在熾熱的地產發展和城市擴張的背景下，香港婦女的勞動力得到解放，而城市中的公共與私人領域亦逐漸結合起來。合成建築，結集了家居及家居以外的功能，蘊含了歷史上城市與家庭、公共與私人、生產者與消費者、殖民者與華人、現實與理想、男性與女性之間的角力。因此，這在香港甚為常見的建築類型，可以讓我們建構一個有用的理論框架，無論在概念抑或實踐的層面上，都可以從跨學科的角度去探討城市與家居之間的關係。 香港正在工業化的一九五〇至七〇年代，在其特殊的地緣政治及社會經濟環境下，家庭及殖民管治者都建立了一套值得研究的物質和空間使用習慣。《密集家居城》將會是首本以這為專題的學術著作，探討這座城市的資本化過程、城市政策、對密度的各種論述三者如何形成了香港建築界的建作模式、家居生活習慣，以及城市的空間形態。 目前關於香港戰後勞工階層房屋的學術研究，一般以描述政府部門如何逐步解決一系列危機（如火災、難民、木屋區等）所衍生出的「房屋問題」為主。而香港的城市環境，則被刻畫成在市場運作下，經濟效率所驅使的必然成果。本研究旨在揭露這等房屋歷史中被隱藏了的一面，強調整個城市環境、家居體驗、建築之間不可分割的關係，並且拆解眾多參與者：政府（發展政策）、地產商（炒賣活動）、建築師（樓宇圖則）、居民（生活習慣）、女性和家庭（日常規律）之間的多重角力。 是次研究圍繞多被學術界所忽略的合成建築。每個故事均嘗試探討廣泛地緣政治，如冷戰及文化大革命，為都市帶來的焦慮，如何透過真實居住情況與居民自我印象兩者之間的差別呈現出來。結合起來，這些例子為香港發展成亞洲最具代表性的資本主義城市這過程中，房屋建築與城市論述所扮演的重要角色，提供了嶄新的觀點。 透過繪畫出合成建築在其經濟、社會、文化背景中的出現與發展，本研究強調建築、民眾、制度、經濟，和城市環境之間密不可分的關係，而這關係正製造了延續至今，附帶矛盾的家居空間。藉着深入探討合成建築這向來被受忽視的建築類型，本研究嘗試重新撿視其中的關鍵元素，補充家居性與城市空間如何產生這學術上的空隙，為建築學、城市學、女性主義研究，及香港史等學科同時作出貢獻。

17618117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17618117.value: Introduction: Liver cancer is the second most common cause of cancer-related death in Asia-Pacific region. Sorafenib is the standard of treatment in advanced patients but the median overall survival is only 9-12 months. Thus, an unmet medical need remains to develop more effective therapeutic agents in this disease. Polo-kinase 4(PLK4) represents an attractive therapeutic target in cancer treatments as cancer cells heavily rely on PLK4 to reproduce centrosomes for cell division. Notably, HCCs are genomically unstable and commonly aneuploid with abnormal karyotypes. Our provocative preclinical findings clearly demonstrated that PLK4 is an attractive and promising molecular target for HCC therapy. Thus, we propose to conduct a phase 1b study of CFI-400945 to determine the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) and safety of CFI-400945 in advanced HCC patients. It will then further evaluated for efficacy, tolerability, pharmacokinetics and potential biomarkers in a dose expansion cohort. Settings: This trial will be conducted at the Phase 1 Centre at the Queen Mary Hospital, The University of Hong Kong. Subjects: Advanced liver cancer patients not suitable for surgery or various loco-regional therapies and are refractory to sorafenib will be recruited. Study Design and Assessment: This is an open label, single center, Phase 1b study that will be conducted in two parts--- a Dose Escalation and Dose Expansion part. Dose escalation will follow a standard 3+3 cohort design until the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) is determined. Once the MTD was determined, an additional 24 patients will be recruited to receive CFI-400945 at the MTD in the expansion cohort to determine the anti-tumor activity and tolerability of CFI-400945. Disease assessment will be evaluated at baseline, and then repeated every 8 weeks by Computed Tomography according to RECIST 1.1. Pharmacokinetic study will be done in both the dose-escalation and expansion phases. Immunohistochemistry study of PTEN expression level in the biopsy tissues will be assessed and correlated with outcomes. Sample size: The sample size determination used is per standard Phase 1 “3+3” dose escalation format to determine the MTD. Once the MTD is reached, up to a total of 24 patients will be enrolled at MTD in the dose expansion cohort. 18100117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18100117.value: Abstract Subjective tinnitus is defined as the perception of sound in the absence of an acoustic stimulus. It is a common condition in the general population. Most patients who suffer from subjective tinnitus have no identifiable causes, and for some tinnitus can seriously affect their quality of life. Despite a variety of therapeutic alternatives, a consistently effective treatment remains elusive. Most treatment methods have not been verified by research, and there is no widely accepted treatment that has been shown to be effective in controlled investigations. Thus, prospective, controlled studies are needed to provide clear evidence for the efficacy of specific treatment methods. Sound therapy is one of the most commonly employed treatment methods for tinnitus. Sound, usually music, environmental sound, and noise have all been known to provide relief from tinnitus-associated distress, distract attention away from tinnitus, and reduce the contrast between tinnitus and the background acoustic environment to facilitate habituation. For tinnitus sufferers who have hearing loss, the use of hearing aids can provide acoustic enrichment and improve communication. Despite their extensive application in tinnitus management, strong evidence for treatment efficacy with hearing aids is unavailable and has not been verified in well-designed randomized controlled trials. The use of hearing aids in tinnitus sufferers with significant hearing loss will always be associated with an improvement in hearing handicap and that complicates the interpretation of how much hearing aids specifically affect tinnitus. The study thus aims to investigate the treatment efficacy of tinnitus in people with mild hearing loss. We propose carrying out a randomized controlled trial of sound therapy efficacy on tinnitus with the use of hearing aids and audio devices with customized music. To achieve sufficient statistical power to detect the treatment difference, 156 subjects will be recruited and randomly assigned into one of the three groups: 1) hearing aid; 2) customized music; and 3) a no-treatment waiting list control group. Immediate and sustained outcomes will be compared using the 1) Chinese Tinnitus Functional Index, 2) Chinese Tinnitus Handicap Inventory, 3) Chinese Tinnitus Questionnaire, 4) self-rated visual analogue scale on tinnitus loudness, 5) tinnitus loudness matches measured psycho-acoustically, and 6) Chinese version of the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale. Intention-to-treat analysis will be employed. By using the rigorous study-design of randomized controlled trials, results from this study will provide strong evidence in support of clinical decision-making in tinnitus management, and a greater understanding of tinnitus mechanisms.

18301117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18301117.value: 設計高效並具有實際應用價值的光催化劑需要滿足三個重要因素，分別是：（1）具有強的光吸收性能；（2）具有良好的電荷分離效率；（3）具有很高的量子產率。為了實現光催化技術的實際應用，本專案系統研究並開發出了一系列高效（高的光利用率和量子產率）等離子光催化劑。我們都知道，通過在光催化劑表面負載具有等離子共振效應的貴金屬（例如Ag和Au）納米顆粒可以有效提高光催化劑的活性。這主要是因為這些貴金屬納米顆粒一方面對光具有很好的吸收或散射性能，另一方面可以在催化劑表面構建一個局域的電場。然而，Au和Ag在地球上非常稀缺，價格過於昂貴。所以用它們製備等離子體光催化劑進行實際應用受到了很大的限制。因此，開發價格低廉、含量豐富且具有等離子共振效應的助催化劑是非常必要的。相對於貴金屬，貧金屬是指元素週期表中p區過渡金屬，主要包括Al，In，Sn，Ga，Tl，Pb，Bi等金屬。它們具有很強的電負性，並且在紫外（UV）區具有等離子共振效應，這說明這類金屬可能可以取代貴金屬Au和Ag。在本專案中我們主要以Al為研究物件來合成等離子體光催化劑。眾所周知，金屬顆粒對光的吸收性能與其形狀，尺寸以及周圍介質的介電性密切相關。所以本專案根據不同形貌的Al納米顆粒合成了一系列等離子體光催化劑，並且深入討論了光催化劑中電荷傳輸方式。另外，我們還通過理論計算以及實驗表徵研究了Al納米顆粒的不同形貌對光催化劑活性，光催化反應過程的影響。本專案旨在開發一系列高效的Al金屬相關的等離子光催化劑，可以用來取代Au，Ag等貴金屬相關的等離子體光催化劑。本專案的成功實施可以促進光催化技術的實際應用，具有很好的研究價值。

18301117.label: Realisation of objectives
18301117.value: Objectives 1: Two plasmonic photocatalyst have been developed, i.e. Bi/Bi2O3-x/g-C3N4 and POMs@Bi2O3-x/Bi (POMs = PW12O403-) (i) Preparation of Plasmonic Bi/Bi2O3-x/g-C3N4 photocatalysts To synthesize the Bi2O3/g-C3N4 composite Bi(NO3)3·5H2O and Urea were placed into a crucible together firstly and treated under continuous magnetic stirring with 200℃. The mixture was placed into the muffle furnace under 600℃ under air atmosphere. Finally, the Bi2O3/g-C3N4 composite was then was placed into a beaker with ultrasonic oscillating for 30 mins. To reduce the metallic Bi from the Bi2O3, NaBH4 was added into the beaker without heating. Finally, the product was centrifuged and washed with distilled water following by ethanol several times to remove the NaBH4. The final product was marked as BBC-0.75. XRD demonstrates the composition of BBC-0.75. The BC-x samples exhibits a series peaks at 24.6°, 30.1° and 32.5° can be assigned to the characteristic peaks of Bi2O3. After treated with NaBH4, BBC-0.75 has five new peaks, which can be attributed to the diffraction peaks of metallic Bi. Typical morphology and microstructure of BBC-0.75 was investigated by SEM and TEM. High resolution TEM exhibits two individual lattice fringes with lattice spacing of about 0.24 nm and 0.27 nm, which can be indexed as the (110) planes of Bi and the (220) planes of Bi2O3-x, respectively. However, the amorphous lamellar structures at the edge of Bi/Bi2O3-x nanoparticles belong to g-C3N4. Therefore, BBC-0.75 can be described as Bi/Bi2O3-x nanoparticles dispersed on g-C3N4 nanosheets, thus forming a good heterojunction structure. Compared with g-C3N4, the absorption of BC-x, after NaBH4 treatment, the UV-Vis spectral absorption of BBC-0.75 in range of 400-800 nm was significantly enhanced, which can be attributed to the plasma resonance absorption of reduced Bi. (ii) Preparation of Plasmonic POMs@Bi2O3-x/Bi (POMs = PW12O403-) photocatalysts In a typical preparation step, PW12/Bi2O3 composite nanofibers was dispersed into a aqueous solution, followed by sonication. Then, designed a series of different amount of NaBH4 aqueous solution added dropwise into the above solution with vigorous magnetic stirring. The final PW12/Bi2O3-x/Bi composite materials were collected and named as BiOPW-x. In XRD, when modified by H3PW12O40xH2O, the characteristic peaks of Bi2O3 become broaden. This shows that H3PW12O40xH2O has been successfully introduced into the Bi2O3 lattice. SEM reveals the morphological changes of BiOPW during the reduction process. The original BiOPW electrospun samples show the shape of nanorods with many bubbles distributed on the surface. With the deepening of reduction degree, the structure of the nanorods is destroyed, and the layers gradually wrapped on the surface of the nanorods. The transmission electron microscopy (TEM) tests of BiOPW-0.75 sample. The high resolution TEM image of BiOPW-0.75 displays that the crystal lattices of both Bi2O3 and Bi NPs are coexistence. XPS was used to further investigate the chemical composition and elemental valence states of Bi2O3 and BiOPW-0.75. After introduced H3PW12O40xH2O into Bi2O3, additional W element was also observed in BiOPW-0.75. Objective 2: NOx removal of Plasmonic Bi/Bi2O3-x/ g-C3N4 photocatalyst Photocatalytic removal of NOx was used to detect the photocatalytic activity of samples. Under visible light (λ ≧ 420 nm ) irradiation, about 34 % 600 ppb of NO2 can be removed in 30 min using g-C3N4 as photocatalysts. However, the photocatalytic activity of BC-x are lower than that of g-C3N4, and its activity increased first and then decreased with the increase of Bi(NO3)3 content in raw material. BC-0.75 has the best performance. About 29% of NO2 can be removed in 30 min. Therefore, the optimal BC-0.75 was used for subsequent processing. After NaBH4 treatment, the photocatalytic of BBC-0.75 has been largely enhanced. About 58 % of NO2 can be removed in 30 min. This remarkably enhanced photocatalytic activity is due to the formation of Z-scheme heterojunction between Bi/Bi2O3-x/g-C3N4. BBC-0.75 also shows excellent photocatalytic activity for NO removal. Under visible light irradiation, about 90 % of 600 ppb NO can be removed. After five cycles, the removal efficiency of NO2 was reduced by nearly 50%. Therefore, it is necessary to rationally design the composition and structure of photocatalyst to ensure the removal efficiency of NOx, while enhance the photocatalytic stability. NO removal of Plasmonic PW12/Bi2O3-x/Bi photocatalyst The optimal sample of BiOPW-0.75 was further used for removal of NO under visible light (LED) (λ > 420nm, 0.16 W m−2) in a continuous flow reactor system. Bare Bi2O3 (54.7%) shows lower photocatalytic activity than that of BiOPW (61.6%), which indicates that PW12 has an improvement effect on the photocatalytic removal of NO. After NaBH4 treatment, 81.8 % of NO could be removed for 30 min using BiOPW-0.75 as photocatalysts, which is significantly higher than that of Bi2O3 and BiOPW samples. This can be attributed to the synergistic effect of reduced PW12 and surface Bi nanoparticles. By monitoring the concentration change of NO2 products, the reduction pathways of Bi2O3, BiOPW and BiOPW-0.75 are different. For Bi2O3, the concentration of NO2 shows a continuous increasing trend, reaching 55.7 ppb at 30 min, suggesting that the major mechanism in this case was oxidation. After introducing PW12 into the Bi2O3, the concentration of NO2 was first increases and then decreases, and finally the concentration of NO2 can be restored to the initial concentration. While for BiOPW-0.75, the reduced PW12 and the Schottky junction effect of Bi NPs can further improve the removal of NO2. Therefore, the conversion of NO2 was reduced to 0 within 10 minutes. In order to further investigate the NO removal mechanism of photocatalyst, N2 was used to replace air. Under the same conditions, the removal of NO was still about 30%, which demonstrates the photocatalytic reduction mechanism of NO. Although the activity of the photocatalyst is much lower than that under air condition, this may be due to the fact that O2 or water vapor molecules in the air accelerate the separation of photogenerated carriers, thus promoting the photocatalytic activity of photocatalysts. It is worth mentioning that the photocatalytic stability of BiOPW-0.75 is greatly enhanced compared with BBC-0.75. After 5 cycles, the samples still maintain good photocatalytic activity, and the NO removal efficiency is only reduced by less than 2%, indicating the good photocatalytic stability of BiOPW-0.75. Objective 3: In order to reveal the reason for the good photocatalytic stability of BiOPW-0.75, a possible mechanism of NO removal was proposed based on the experimental results. Under visible light irradiation, both Bi2O3-x and reduced PW12 can be excited. The photogenerated electrons of PW12 heteropoly blue may be transferred to the outer Bi2O3-x and then combined with the photogenerated holes of Bi2O3-x, thus forming a S-scheme of photocatalytic mechanism. And the photogenerated electrons on Bi2O3-x are transferred to Bi nanoparticles due to the Schottky junction effect. NO is reduced to N2O or N2 by taking electrons from Bi. While the holes in PW12 heteropoly blue oxidize the polyoxoanions itself or transfer to Bi2O3-x, thus avoiding the oxidation of Bi nanoparticles, endowing the excellent photocatalytic stability of BiOPW-0.75. Although the more specific photocatalytic mechanism needs to be further proved, this work confirms that the rational design of the composition and structure of poor-metal-based plasma photocatalyst is expected to guarantee the excellent photocatalytic removal efficiency of NOx while maintaining good stability. This work brings new promising for the practical application of photocatalytic NOx removal.

18301117.label: Major findings and research outcome
18301117.value: Plasmonic Bismuth-based photocatalysts are a class of excellent visible-light photocatalysts, but their redox activity is relatively poor, and the efficiency of photogenerated carrier separation is low, which limits their application and development in the field of photocatalysts. To solve the above problems, a series of polyoxometalate PW12O403--doped Bi2O3-x/Bi Schottky photocatalysts PW12@Bi2O3-x/Binwas prepared by simple electrospinning/calcination/in-situ NaBH4 reduction. In this composite photocatalyst, the doping of PW12 could effectively adjust the electronic structure of Bi2O3-x and improve its redox property. And as a shallow electron trap, PW12 promoted the separation of photogenerated carriers. The good Schottky junction between metal Bi nanoparticles and PW12@Bi2O3-x further accelerated the separation of photogenerated carriers. Under visible light irradiation, the catalysts showed excellent and durable photocatalytic performance for the degradation of model pollutant in the removal of NO in gas phase. The synergistic effect of the above factors endowed PW12@Bi2O3-x/Bi with excellent photocatalytic activity in NO removal. This study provides new inspiration and reference for the rational design of low-cost, efficient, stable and versatile photocatalyst and promotes the application of photocatalytic technology in the efficient removal of environmental pollutants. In addition, a novel Bi-bridge Z-scheme β-Bi2O3/Bi/g-C3N4 heterojunction photocatalyst is developed via a simple one-step in-situ thermal reduction method. The metallic Bi that in-situ thermal reduced from Bi2O3 can also improve the NO removal efficiency over the Bi2O3/g-C3N4 photocatalyst because of the surface plasmon resonance (SPR) effect. Construction of a heterojunction between Bi2O3 and g-C3N4 under the metal Bi SPR effect assist could significantly inhibit the recombination of photogenerated carriers and enhance the absorption of visible light. We found that the photocatalytic degradation over this Z-scheme photocatalyst not only exhibited high degradation percentage (88.7%) for NO, which is significantly higher than that of the pristine g-C3N4 (60%), but also depressed NO2 generation under LED light irradiation, Interestingly, both oxidation of NO into NO3- and reduction of NO into N2 exist synchronously in the system. The increased degradation efficiency and the efficient reduction pathway occurring should be ascribed to the enhanced generation, separation, and transfer of the photogenerated carriers through the Bi-bridge Z-scheme heterojunction. This study has provided a new route for regulating the photocatalytic reaction pathway for NO removal through a simple synthesis method.

18301117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18301117.value: Conventional photocatalytic decomposition of nitrogen oxides (NOx) mainly oxidizes nitrogen monoxide to nitrogen dioxide (NO2) which is still a toxic air pollutants, and other nitrate species which may deactivate the catalyst. Compared with the oxidation products, the photocatalytic reduction of NOx to nitrogen (N2) would neither cause secondary pollution nor lead to catalyst poisoning. However, in the reaction process of NOx removal, the selectivity for NOx to generate N2 through photocatalytic reduction is extremely low. In the study of bismuth bridge Z-scheme β-Bi2O3/Bi/g-C3N4 heterojunction photocatalyst, compared with g-C3N4 and β-Bi2O3 photocatalysts, the photocatalytic degradation over this Z-scheme photocatalyst not only exhibited high degradation percentage (88.7%) for NO, which is significantly higher than that of the pristine g-C3N4 (60%), but also depressed NO2 generation under LED light irradiation, Interestingly, both oxidation of NO into NO3- and reduction of NO into N2 exist synchronously in the system. Instead of the traditional fully photocatalytic oxidation of NO that may cause the final products to poison the photocatalyst, the efficient and economical method presented in this study provides a new route for regulating the photocatalytic reaction pathway for degrading the atmosphere's low level of NO into environmentally friendly N2 through a simple synthesis method.

18301117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18301117.value: Numerous crucial challenges still exist in using photocatalysis in air purification, e.g. NOx removal, such as low solar light absorption, fast charge carriers recombination, low quantum efficiency, and ambiguity of photocatalytic mechanisms. Surface plasmon resonance metal photocatalysts possess unique properties because of their strong interaction with resonant incident photons by excitation of the localized surface plasmon resonance (SPR), which forms strong electromagnetic fields near the nanostructures of the SPR metal photocatalysts. Previously, most interests are paid to investigate the properties of the noble metal as cocatalsyt. In this study, abundant and economically feasible plasmon resonance photocatalyst with various shapes and ideal size are fabricated for obtaining photocatalysts with exceptionally high photocatalytic capability. Our work focuses on tailor-making and optimizing the nanostructures, surface state, nanoparticle sizes and the best wavelength of incident light of two plasmonic photocatalyst for the target air pollutants. For example, the Z-scheme β-Bi2O3/Bi/g-C3N4 photocatalyst, not only exhibited high degradation percentage (88.7%) for NO, which is significantly higher than that of the pristine g-C3N4 (60%), but also depressed NO2 generation under LED light irradiation. This efficient and economical method may open a new opportunity for degrading the atmosphere's low level of NO into environmentally friendly N2.

18301217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18301217.value: Black-box optimization corresponds to a class of optimization problems with a complicated or an unknown objective function, i.e. a “black-box” function, such that its output values at specific inputs can only be measured by expensive or time-consuming processes. They are very challenging and cannot be tackled by conventional optimization algorithms which are based on the knowledge of a known objective function. Nevertheless, they are crucial in a wide range of applications in science and engineering. Yet, unlike conventional “white-box” optimization problems where physicists have devoted decades of efforts in developing a fundamental understanding of their macroscopic properties which has led to insightful developments, the awareness of black-box problems in the physics community and the attempts to address them are very limited. This is partly because an unknown objective function is incompatible with conventional statistical physics tools. As a result, research on black-box optimization is dominated by algorithm-oriented approaches without a thorough understanding underlying black-box optimization problems. In the proposed research, we will overcome the obstacle of an unknown objective function and apply statistical physics tools to (1) develop a fundamental understanding of the nature of black-box optimization problems, (2) derive a macroscopic description of their behaviors and understand the effectiveness of their existing solution methods, and (3) apply these insights to improve existing solution methods, and devise new physics-inspired and understanding-driven algorithms for black-box problems. Specifically, we will establish a theoretical framework to study black-box optimization problems with statistical physics. We will apply tools from statistical physics to (a) understand the effectiveness of various sampling strategies in relation with the nature of black-box objective functions, (b) reveal the relation between the objective function fitting stage and the subsequent optimization stage in conventional modeling-fitting-optimizing approaches for black-box problems, (c) map black-box problems to spin glasses and disordered systems of noisy information retrieval and associate memory, (d) coarse-grain black-box problems and examine the validity of the coarse-grained systems as representatives of the original systems with reduced dimensionality, and finally (e) use all the above theoretical insights to improve and inform existing black-box solution methods, and devise new physics-inspired and understanding-driven algorithms for black-box optimization problems. 黑箱優化問題，是一類擁有未知或復雜目標函數的優化問題，而目標函數在不同參數及情況下的輸出值，亦只能透過昂貴或耗時的過程來測量，是科學和工程領域中常常遇到的問題。由於缺少了目標函數的表達式，黑箱優化問題不能透過一般優化算法來解決，而解決問題的難度亦相繼增加。物理學家利用統計物理學的技術，己對一般己知目標函數的優化問題有了深入理解。但由於傳統的統計物理學工具，不兼容一個未知目標函數的系統，因此我們對黑箱優化問題的理解有限，而黑盒優化問題的主要研究方向亦以算法為主。 在此研究中，我們將利用統計物理學工具（1）理解黑箱優化問題的物理性質，（2）理解其宏觀特性及現有解決方案的有效性，（3）改進現有解決方案，並發展以理解為基礎的優化算法。 我們將建立一個理論框架以統計物理學的工具研究黑箱優化問題。我們將利用統計物理學的工具來（a）了解各種測量策略，對於不同性質的黑箱目標函數的有效性，（b）了解擬合目標函數階段及後續優化階段之間的關係，（c）將黑箱問題聯繫到自旋玻璃模型，信息檢索模型及關聯記憶模型並加以理解，（d）了解簡化後及減少維度後的黑箱問題，與原問題的關係，（e）利用以上結果改進現有解決方案，並發展以理解為基礎的優化算法。

18301217.label: Realisation of objectives
18301217.value: OBJECTIVE (1) Several theoretical frameworks were explored for black-box optimization: (a) In [1] (Xu, Yeung, Zhou and Saad, 2018), we studied “Simulated Annealing” (SA), a widely adopted physics-inspired algorithm capable to optimize black-box objective functions by simply probing the energy of individual variable configurations without knowing the explicit form of objectives. We examined the effectiveness of SA on a special kind of combinational optimization problems characterized by an inflection point in their entropy-energy profiles. Interestingly, we found that in contrary to our common belief, SA is unable to identify the ground state of the problems as temperature decreases. These findings reveal one fundamental challenge for black-box optimization. (b) In [6] (Po and Yeung, under review), we introduced a new approach called “Partial Coarse-grained Energy Landscape” (PCEL) to extract a specific regime of the energy landscape of combinatorial optimization problems by sampling variable configurations and their energy, without knowing the explicit form of objective functions, i.e. black-box optimization. In [6], we applied this approach on spin glasses and K-Satisfiability problems, and showed that this approach enables us to obtain the characteristics of the problems, e.g. the statistics of local minima, the non-equilibrium trapping dynamics, etc., out of reach by existing approaches. The PCEL thus represents a new framework for the analyses of black-box optimization problems. (c) In [7] (Li, Saad and Yeung, under review), we studied optimization problems which require “bilevel” optimization, e.g. optimization at the upper level for hyper-parameters in black-box objective functions and at the lower level for variables. In [], we demonstrate our approach on two bilevel optimization problems, namely setting road tolls in routing games and identifying control parameters in flow control problems. This approach thus represents a generic framework and can be readily applied for analyzing black-box optimization problems. OBJECTIVE (2) (a) In [6] (Po and Yeung, under review), to extract the PCEL we described for Objective (1), we introduced a Markov-chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) approach with a tunable sampling temperature to extract the configuration-energy relationship in black-box optimization problems. As shown in [6], only a single sampling temperature is needed in the extraction of the PCEL, which can then be used to obtain the system behavior in a wide range of temperatures. Moreover, different choices of sampling temperature would lead to different regimes of the energy landscape, which is useful for probing the low-energy configurational space in black-box optimization problems. OBJECTIVE (3) We introduced various approaches to analyze optimization problems with two levels, stages or types of variables: (a) In [7] (Li, Saad and Yeung, under review), the forementioned bilevel optimization process which consists of a two-level optimization, can be used for optimizing hyper-parameters in the fitting stage and the variables in the optimization stage. Our results show that the two stages depend crucially on each other, but given a protocol to optimize the two stages in an alternating manner, an approximate optimization in each alternating round is already sufficient to direct the system towards the global optimum. (b) In [3] (Po, Yeung and Saad, 2021) and [4] (Tai and Yeung, 2021), we introduced a new theoretical approach, modified from existing cavity approach in statistical physics, to solve two-stage optimization problems. In particular, we applied this new approach in [3] to reveal the relationship between the two optimization stages of a routing game where the global optimum is first identified, and then some users optimize their own objective function; in [4], we applied this approach for two-stage optimization in transportation networks before and after some links are broken. This new theoretical cavity approach can be readily applied to reveal the relationship between the fitting and optimization stages of black-box optimization problems. (c) In [5] (Xu, Po, Yeung and Saad, 2022), we introduced a new generic approach such that the first type of variables (e.g. variables in the optimization stage) is optimized within a single layer of network, while the second type of variables (e.g. hyper-parameter in the fitting stage of the black-box objective functions) manifest themselves through the different layers of network. The optimization of the multi-layer networks thus optimizes the two different types of variables, e.g. the fitting and optimization stages, simultaneously. OBJECTIVE (4) (a) In [2] (Rocchi, Saad and Yeung, 2018), we related self-sustained clusters (SSC, introduced by the PI and the Co-I for studying spin glasses in 2013) in the real space, with local minima in the configurational space in 3-spin models. By introducing an algorithm to identify variables in SSCs, we found that spins in SSCs are less likely to flip, which we call “slow-spins”. By using sampling dynamics such as the one introduced for PCEL [6], we can identify the “slow-variables” in black-box problems which hinder their optimization. This study thus relates phenomenon observed in spin systems to hard optimization problems. (b) In [6] (Po and Yeung, under review), the PCEL (see Objective (1)) introduced have been used to analyze both spin glasses and combinatorial optimization problems; some common characteristics such as the non-equilibrium trapping in local minima, an optimal non-zero temperature which mitigates trapping, etc. are observed. These results again enhance our understanding of the black-box optimization problems through an analogy with spin systems. OBJECTIVE (5) Coarse-graining and dimensionality reduction of black-box systems are examined through the following approaches: (a) In [2] (Rocchi, Saad and Yeung, 2018), as we have mentioned for Objective (4), we studied the emergence of SSCs in 3-spin models, which are spin clusters in the real space that are self-sustained within the clusters and are less affected by spins outside the clusters; we showed that spins in SSCs are highly likely to be slow evolving, with a predictability outperforming that obtained by local fields. Those slow-evolving spins can thus be grouped and coarse-grained as a single slow-evolving spin, which can facilitate black-box optimization. (b) In [6] (Po and Yeung, under review), our newly introduced “Partial Coarse-grained Energy Landscape” (PCEL) is based on coarse-graining connected variable configurations with the same energy, such that the high dimension of the configurational space can be greatly reduced, which facilitates our analyses on black-box systems. OBJECTIVE (6) (a) In [7] (Li, Saad and Yeung, under review), the newly introduced message-passing algorithms are useful for black-box optimization problems, such that the upper level optimally infers the unknown parameters in the black-box objective functions, and the lower level optimizes the variables based on the inferred objective functions. By alternating the optimization stages in the upper and the lower level, the black-box objectives can be optimized; examples are found in [7]. (b) In [5] (Xu, Po, Yeung and Saad, 2022), through the generic approach of multi-layer network we described for Objective (3), we introduced a new algorithm to optimize both wavelength and route assignment for communications in optical networks, which a demonstration of the capability of the approach in optimizing two-level variables in black-box problems. (c) In [6] (Po and Yeung, under review), our newly introduced PCEL corresponds to an algorithm to reveal part of the energy landscape of black-box problems through a MCMC sampling approach, which provide us with useful information for inferring of low-energy variable states potentially without the knowledge of explicit form of the black-box functions.

18301217.label: Major findings and research outcome
18301217.value: (1) IMPROVED UNDERSTANDING (a) In [7] (Li, Saad and Yeung, under review), our study on “bilevel” optimization problems enhanced our understanding of the simultaneous optimization of two levels of variables, e.g. optimization variables and black-box functions’ hyper-parameters. (b) In [1] (Xu, Yeung, Zhou and Saad, 2018), although simulated annealing can be used for black-box optimization, they are ineffective for problems with an inflection point in their entropy-energy profile; in this case, lowering temperature does not lead to the ground states, a new finding on optimization problems. (c) In [6] (Po and Yeung, under review), “Partial Coarse-grained Energy Landscape” (PCEL) was introduced to reveal partially the energy landscape of optimization problems without knowing the explicit form of the objective function. Interesting phenomena such as non-equilibrium trapping are observed. (2) ADVANCES IN METHODOLOGY (a) In [7] (Li, Saad and Yeung, under review), we introduced a new framework for analyzing and deriving message-passing algorithms for bilevel optimization problems. (b) In [3] (Po, Yeung and Saad, 2021) and [4] (Tai and Yeung, 2021), we modified the cavity approach in statistical physics to establish a new theoretical framework to analyze two-stage optimization. In this case, two sets of cavity functions were simultaneously iterated, and information from the former is fed to the later for optimization. (c) In [5] (Xu, Po, Yeung and Saad, 2022), we introduced a new multi-layer approach to simultaneously optimize two types of variables, where the first type is optimized within a layer of network, while the second type is manifested through the different network layers. (3) APPLICATIONS (a) In [7] (Li, Saad and Yeung, under review), we used to the new bilevel optimization framework to derive message-passing algorithms for optimizing routing games and flow control. (b) In [5] (Xu, Po, Yeung and Saad, 2022), we used to the new multi-layer approach to derive algorithms to optimize both wavelength and route assignment for optical networks; this work attracted the interest of Huawei and a presentation was given. (c) In [6] (Po and Yeung, under review), PCEL can be used to reveal part of the energy landscape of black-box and general optimization problems. (d) In [1] (Xu, Yeung, Zhou and Saad, 2018), we introduced a new clamp-energy optimization algorithm for problems with an inflection point in their entropy-energy profile. (e) In [2] (Rocchi, Saad and Yeung, 2018), we derived a new message-passing algorithm to identify slow-evolving variables, which can be coarse-grained for optimization.

18301217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18301217.value: To further develop a new understanding and methodologies for black-box optimization, we will apply our introduced frameworks to study other black-box optimization problems not studied in the forementioned works. Specifically, we will apply the various bilevel or two-stage optimization approaches developed in our reported works to further examine the simultaneous optimization process of the variables and the unknown hyper-parameters in the black-box objective functions. In addition to the works we have reported above, we have also attempted other approaches and problems of black-box optimization. These include (a) a classic black-box optimization problem called the “multi-armed bandit” problem, where we have used dynamical generating functional and large deviation analyses to analyze the sequence of bandit selection in maximizing the accumulated gain from the system; (b) a new approach called “batch-sampling” to sample a group of related configurations for the construction of an inferred factor graph for the identification of potential optimal variable configurations using message-passing algorithms; (c) the application of replica analyses in the study of spin glasses in statistical physics to enhance our understanding of the optimal sampling sequence for black-box functions. Investigation will continue in the above direction and manuscripts are in preparation to disseminate the new results.

18301217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18301217.value: In this project, we applied tools in statistical physics to establish new theoretical frameworks to analyze and derive optimization algorithms for black-box optimization problems. Specifically, we introduced various approaches capable to simultaneously optimize two level of variables, where one level can be considered as the unknown hyper-parameters in the black-box objective functions, while the other level consists of the optimization variables based on the inferred objective functions. Based on these new frameworks, we introduced new methodology for analyzing optimization problems which involve two levels of variables, leading to readily applicable optimization algorithms for different applications. These include routing games for optimizing the toll on roads and the traffic flow subject to the tolls, the set of resistance on a network and the corresponding optimal network flow, the optimal wavelength and route assignment in optical communication networks, the path configuration for all road users and then the individual paths when some users minimize their own cost, the traffic flow before and after some links are broken in transportation networks, etc. All these examples enhanced our understanding of black-box optimization problems and demonstrate how optimization algorithms can be derived for them.

18600417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18600417.value: Traditionally, budgetary scholars have focused on discussing deficit politics in the context of Western democracies (Buchanan and Wagner, 1996), with much emphasis placed on the budgetary conflicts between governments and legislatures over different strategies to balance budgets (Rubin, 2014: 31-32). In recent years, there has seen a particularly rich and urgent vein of commentary, debate and research on deficit politics, as budget deficits soared in many Western democracies following the 2008 global financial crisis. A large body of empirical research was developed to discuss the global public debt crises and to examine the budgetary politics arising from the management of public debts (e.g. Braga and Vincelette, 2011; Eichengreen et al., 2011; Lemieux, 2011; Reinhart and Rogoff, 2013). While it is true to say that most countries around the globe are experiencing consecutive years of budget deficits, the fact remains that there are quite a number of countries and regions experiencing budget surpluses. However, surplus politics, and its comparison with deficit politics, has so far remained under-theorized (Fong, 2015). As far as academic research is concerned, a deeper investigation into the budgetary politics of countries and regions with consistent budget surpluses will help enrich our understanding of public budgeting and also offer budgeting researchers new theoretical and empirical insights. Hong Kong, as a city that has consistently run budget surpluses, is in a unique position to spearhead research in this area. This study is a pioneer project that investigates the nature and characteristics of “surplus politics” of Hong Kong and Singapore in a comparative perspective. Within budgeting literature, “deficit politics” is defined as budgetary conflicts among multiple actors with different spending and revenue preferences over the balancing of budget deficits (Rubin, 2014: 172-214). This research project aims at broadening the research focus from “deficit politics” to “surplus politics” by specifically addressing the following two central research questions through a comparative study of Hong Kong and Singapore: What are the nature and characteristics of surplus politics? What are the similarities and differences between deficit politics and surplus politics? Through the development of a new set of comparative case studies on Hong Kong and Singapore, this research project will make an important original contribution to comparative budgeting literature by providing a theoretical and empirical framework for future comparative studies on deficit politics and surplus politics. The results will also have useful policy implications for Hong Kong and other budget surplus countries and territories. 傳統上，預算學者大多集中研究西方民主國家下的「赤字政治」，著重探討政府和議會就如何平衡預算的角力。近年，不少西方民主國家在2008年金融海嘯後都面對巨額赤字，進一步推動了有關「赤字政治」的研究。 雖然全球大部分國家地區都面對連年赤字，但不容忽略的事實，是同時有一定數量的國家地區長期享有盈餘。但有關「盈餘政治」的研究、以至其與「赤字政治」的比較，卻一直受到忽視。因此，開拓有關「盈餘政治」的研究，將為比較預算研究帶來重要貢獻；而香港由於長期享有盈餘，將是其中一個重要研究個案。 本研究計劃以香港和新加坡作為比較個案，將是首項探討「盈餘政治」的比較研究，希望能夠解答兩個研究問題：「盈餘政治」的性質和特徵是甚麼？「盈餘政治」和「赤字政治」有何異同？本研究計劃希望透過建立香港和新加坡的研究案例，為比較預算研究作出理論和實證貢獻。本研究計劃的結果和結論，亦將對香港等長期享有盈餘的國家地區，帶來重要的政策制定參考。

18600417.label: Major findings and research outcome
18600417.value: In accordance with the objectives and research framework of this project, I have successfully compared the similarities and differences between deficit politics and surplus politics through investigating the budgetary demands / budgetary outputs of Hong Kong and Singapore in both red-ink years and black-ink years. The major research findings are as follows: ● First, surplus politics is no less dynamic than deficit politics and consistent budget surpluses are a source of recurring budgetary conflicts the same as the cases of consistent budget deficits. There was no significant difference on the empirical pattern of ‘media salience’ and ‘politicization of debate’ across Hong Kong and Singapore's ups and downs in budget cycles. ● Second, both deficit politics and surplus politics are structured by the larger political system, including the characteristics of media and opposition politics. Both deficit politics and surplus politics in Hong Kong are generally more dynamic than that of Singapore. This finding conforms with existing literature about Hong Kong’s more competitive media and opposition politics, when compared with Singapore’s well-known less dynamic under one-party rule by the People’s Action Party. ● Third, the responsiveness of governments to the budgetary demands of non-government actors is not only structured by the nature of the political regimes, but also by constitutional rules and economic growth strategies. It is comprehensible that the limited correlation between the published opinion of non-government actors in Hong Kong and Singapore and the budgetary output of their governments the result of their non-democratic regimes, codification of the principles of fiscal conservativism into their constitutional documents, and their growth strategies as international financial centers. The research findings of this project have been produced into a journal article, which was accepted and published by the International Public Management Journal (5-Year Impact Factor: 2.865) on 1 April 2021 at DOI: https://doi.org/10.1080/10967494.2021.1903633. Please refer to Annex I for the PDF file of the article. In addition, the research findings of this project, together with those Hong Kong’s budgetary datasets, archives, and materials that I have directly developed in the course of conducting this project, were expanded into a single author book titled Hong Kong Public Budgeting: Historical and Comparative Analyses. A book contract was signed with Palgrave on 19 December 2019, with the book manuscript just completed and submitted to Palgrave for production (expected to be put on sale by the end of 2021). Please refer to Annex II for the book contract and the book manuscript.

18600417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18600417.value: This project is the first comparative case study to explore the dynamics of deficit politics and surplus politics, using Hong Kong and Singapore as binary cases. Looking around the word, there are quite a number of countries and regions that have experienced cycles of both budget deficits and budget surpluses over the years. Building upon the idea of media content analysis, the comparative framework developed in this project has the potential to be developed into large-N comparative studies across fiscal jurisdictions of varying political, socio-economic, and cultural backgrounds. I am now exploring the feasibility of extending this project into another GRF grant proposal that compare budget deficits and budget surpluses through large-N studies.

18600417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18600417.value: Traditionally, budgetary scholars focus on deficit politics in Western democracies, emphasizing budgetary conflicts among budgetary actors over different strategies to balance budgets. While most countries are facing budget deficits, some countries and regions are experiencing budget surpluses. However, surplus politics, and its comparison with deficit politics, remains underexplored. This study is a pioneer attempt to compare the similarities and differences between deficit politics and surplus politics, using Hong Kong and Singapore as binary cases. The findings of this study show that surplus politics is no less dynamic than deficit politics and consistent budget surpluses are a source of recurring budgetary conflicts the same as the cases of consistent budget deficits. It also demonstrates that both deficit politics and surplus politics are structured by the larger political system, constitutional rules, and economic growth strategies

18602217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18602217.value: The present study arises from the belief that early school readers play a major role in the socialization of children’s lives and their gender development. Given that schooling is an important medium of reproducing cultures and of perpetuating the existing mechanisms of domination, the present study aims to examine how males and females are represented in early readers. The Education Bureau (EDB) has been implementing two reading schemes to promote a reading culture in Hong Kong schools: (1) the Primary Literacy Programme – Reading and Writing (Key Stage 1), and (2) Reading to Learn across the Curriculum. The Advisory Teaching Team of the Native-speaking English Teacher (NET) Section of EDB developed the books for (1). The second scheme is for schools to establish cross-curricular linkage to other Key Learning Areas (e.g., Science Education, Technology Education). Despite the popularity of the schemes, so far no attempt has yet been made to investigate how the two genders are represented in the recommended readers. The aim of the present study is to examine how female and male characters are constructed in the readers recommended by EDB as well as in those produced by local publishers. A total of 180 readers for Key Stage 1 (Primary 1-3) will be selected for the analysis. The texts will be examined at the macro and micro levels to investigate how the experiential, relational and expressive values associated with the two genders are manifested. At the macro level about story development, the problem-solution pattern will be examined. At the micro level, categories such as the frequency of appearance of the two genders, the activities they are engaged in, their occupational roles and domestic roles will be coded. The analysis also includes manual and computerised examination of lexical choice, word order, word collocation and discourse structure. Tools for critical discourse analysis will be employed to investigate the representation of social actors and social action, and the relationships of moods and speech acts in mixed-sex dialogues. The study will also include multimodal investigations of gender representation in pictures and the image-text relations. The value of the present study is that it will help heighten the public awareness of the power of book authors to position the two genders through various means, and advance our knowledge about language and gender studies in Asian regions, which is a field that has not yet been explored adequately. 為了促進香港學校的閱讀文化，香港教育局一直推行兩項閱讀計劃：（1）小學識字計劃(閱讀及寫作)；（2）跨課程閱讀。「小學識字計劃」是教育局之英語教師組開發的英語教學計劃，由以英語為母語的英語教師設計。「跨課程閱讀」計劃是讓英國語文教育與其他主要學習領域（如科學教育，科技教育）建立跨學科的銜接。教育局在兩項計劃中建議一批讀物。 這項研究認為學校讀物在兒童社會化和性別發展中發揮重要作用，尤其是學校教育是傳種文化和延續現有兩性權力關係的重要媒介。儘管上述兩項閱讀計劃一直很受歡迎，但至今仍沒有對計劃內的推薦讀物中兩性的描述進行研究和分析。本研究將選出180本教育局推薦的讀物以及本地出版讀物（小學1-3年級），分析兩性在這些讀物中如何構建及定位。 本研究包括宏觀和微觀兩個層面，探討作者在兒童讀物中如何表現跟兩性相關的經驗，關係和價值觀。在宏觀層面上，我們會探討在故事發展的過程中兩性如何解決問題和衝突。在微觀層面，我們將檢視兩性的出現次數，以及他們從事的活動，職業角色和家庭角色等類別。此外，我們也會分析語言文字特徵，包括詞彙選擇、兩性在句子中出現的次序和他們的話語結構。本研究並會通過批判話語分析（critical discourse analysis)來研究男女混合對話中兩性的角色和行為，以及兩性的情緒和言語行為之間的關係。除了文字之外，本研究也會從多模角度(multi-modal)探討讀物中跟兩性有關的圖像，以及圖像和文字之間的關係。這項研究的結果將有助我們進一步了解讀物作者如何通過各種手法對兩性進行描述和定位，並提升我們對亞洲地區語言和性別研究的認識。

18602917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18602917.value: 近年來，雖然大衆對網絡欺凌的認識有所增加，但對於網絡欺凌旁觀者的行為，我們依然所知甚少。過去只有極少數的研究去探討香港網絡欺凌旁觀者的行爲，以香港青少年作為研究對象的文獻更是相當缺乏。因此，本研究的主要目標有四：第一，探討不同網絡欺凌的情境因素如何影響網絡欺凌旁觀者的想法及行爲；第二，利用問卷（縱貫研究）來調查網絡欺凌旁觀者的想法會如何影響他們對網絡欺凌的反應; 第三，測試網絡欺凌旁觀者對受害者特徵的歸因及其與受害者的關係，會否影響他們的想法及行爲; 第四，測試加強網絡欺凌旁觀者對網絡欺凌的了解和認識會否影響他們的行爲。 本研究的結果將闡明影響網絡旁觀者行為的因素。研究成果有望能為將來制定預防網絡欺凌的干預措施奠定基礎。

18602917.label: Realisation of objectives
18602917.value: All the objectives were achieved. To address Objectives 1 and 2, we conducted interviews to examine participants’ beliefs about situational factors that explained their intervening (or non-intervening) behavior when witnessing cyberbullying. These data informed the design of the questionnaires and experiments and the training workshop. We finished two waves of data collection from secondary school and college students. Participants responded to several measures where they rated the time spent on types of online activities, cyberbullying experiences, beliefs about and awareness of cyberbullying, and psychological well-being. We also measured their belief system, and intervening behavior when witnessing cyberbullying and situational factors including their self-efficacy or felt responsibility to intervene. Confirmatory analysis showed that all of the measures had good reliabilities and factor structures. To answer Objective 2 about how individuals’ belief systems, intentions to intervene, and intervening behavior were related, we used structural equation modelling to examine participants’ intervening behavior. To address Objective 3, a simulated Social Networking Site (SNS) which involved a cyberbullying situation was built. Participants read through the scenarios (with pictures and dialogues between a victim and the bullies) and then answered the questionnaires. The scenarios were differed in terms of how the characteristics of "the victim" was being portrayed, alongside messages left by cyberbullies: the 4 conditions were: 1. Victim as non-provocative and active; 2. Victim as non-provocative and passive; 3. Victim as provocative and active, and 4. Victim as provocative and passive. Participants read the simulated dialogues before responding to the questions, such as: How negative did you find the victim? How likely will you intervene in the incidents (Likert scale 1 to 7). The four conditions manipulated the participants’ perceptions of the victim. Manipulation checks using ANOVAs showed that the manipulation of the four scenarios was successful, Our results showed that participants had the most negative feelings toward the victim in condition 4. Results of manipulation checks remained the same no matter the scenarios portrayed the victim as a stranger (simply “a woman” was victimized), or as an acquittance (who carries a name on social media platform), which implies that being provocative (trying to say mean or even discriminative responses) and passive (not trying to explain or defend themselves) elicited the most negative feelings for the bystanders, regardless of who the victim was. Due to the pandemic, this study was completed later than we expected. The data analysis was just completed, and the manuscript is still in preparation. To achieve Objective 4, we recruited over 150 participants who were randomly assigned into an experimental group that received a short 3-week-6-session online training workshop, or into a control group. The goal was to test if a training program would increase the likelihood of cyber-bystanders’ intervening in cyberbullying in a positive way. With 144 participants completing the study, results of the training were promising (see findings below). Finally, to improve the rigor, integrity, and transparency in our analyses, and to avoid fishing the results and developing “data-driven” hypotheses, the protocols and hypotheses for the data from the wave 1 questionnaires were submitted as a pre-registered report before the commencement of data collection. This effort resulted in a theory-driven paper (see below). Another paper on the effectiveness of the training programme was also published. Two papers were presented at international conferences. One paper is under review, and two additional papers are in preparation.
