18613017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18613017.value: Does the Confucian virtue of filial piety-- and its requirement to "love with distinction"-- encourage corruption? This question has received recent interest from philosophers, but has not been addressed empirically. Despite the intuitively appealing nature of the accusation, we propose that being highly filial, as a virtue, should in fact protect one from temptations to participate in self-enriching corruption; but conversely, it may morally motivate one to help particular others in one’s social circle (particularism), if the social institutions of one’s surroundings are inadequate. The role of culture in corruption has been under debate for some time, with conflicting results. Though large-scale studies have suggested that economics and government regulation are a greater predictor of corruption at the national level than culture (Rabl & Kühlmann, 2008; Robertson & Watson, 2004), more specific cultural values such as trust in particular relationships (vs. generalized trust) have been associated with greater corruption (e.g. Pena López & Sánchez Santos, 2014). Mainland Chinese philosopher Qingping Liu has argued that filial values, which encourage valuing particular relationships over the good of the public, lend themselves to support of corruption (Q. Liu, 2007, 2009). Can we combat corruption without weakening filial values? Corruption has often been studied as if it were a single phenomenon, but its forms are in fact diverse (Khatri, Tsang, & Begley, 2006; Ko & Weng, 2011). For example, particularism, when an actor chooses the good of an associate over principled application of rules (Stouffer & Toby, 1951), could under some circumstances be motivated by moral obligations. Though there is some evidence that filial values are associated with particularism (Yeh & Bedford, 2003), this relationship has not been studied within the context of morally motivated corruption. More importantly, ways of reducing the moral pressure from filial piety to commit particularistic acts—such as through social transparency, which reduces the expectation and need for such actions—have not been studied. In a set of 5 studies, we will address how cultural values can morally motivate some forms of corruption by showing that filial piety can create genuine moral obligations to be particularistic, but not self-servingly corrupt; and we will show that societal transparency is the underlying problem that causes filial piety to have this negative outcome. The studies will have implications for how to fight corruption, while retaining the viability of traditional Chinese values in modern Chinese societies. 儒家美德中的孝道及其要求的「愛有差等」會鼓勵腐敗嗎？我們能否在沒有削弱孝道的前提下遏止腐敗？這些問題已引起哲學家的關注，但尚缺乏實證檢驗。我們提出孝道在中國社會是高尚的品質，因而會預防人們從事自利性的腐敗；但不幸地是，如果身處在社會制度不健全的情況下，孝道則會在道德上促進人們幫助其社交圈內的“關係戶” (即所謂的「特殊主義」)。 我們將通過五項研究檢驗孝道是否會引起道德責任，從而推動個體做出特殊主義的而非自利性的腐敗，從而探討孝道能否道德化並促進某種類型的腐敗；同時我們將檢驗社會透明度是導致孝道產生這一負面結果的根本原因。本研究將為如何對抗腐敗，同時在當代中國社會傳承傳統的價值觀帶來啟示。

18613017.label: Realisation of objectives
18613017.value: OVERALL SUMMARY Does the Confucian virtue of filial piety-- and its requirement to "love with distinction"-- encourage corruption? This question has received interest from philosophers, but has not been addressed empirically. The research supported by this grant problematized this intuitive and overly-simplified accusation. We examined two different kinds of abuse of power: simple corruption (the misuse of power for personal gain) versus particularism (the misuse of power for the gain of particular others). We also examined different forms of filial piety and values, finding important evidence for what kinds of individual differences, and environments, are protective against particularism. In addition to providing new theoretical insights for philosophers and psychologists, we believe these findings can have important implications for anti-corruption education. Our studies showed that in terms of individual differences, it is too simple to say that a broad concept like “filial piety” leads to corruption or particularism. The specific individual differences that are preventative against particularism are different from those that are preventative against bribery-type corruption (Objective 1; the focus of Paper 1 below). Moreover, both filial piety and collectivistic self-concepts have two aspects; one of these aspects is problematic, and the other is sometimes protective and sometimes neutral (described in Paper 1 and Paper 3 below). These findings suggest that for anti-corruption campaigns, particularism should be addressed separately from simple bribery. Character traits such as having high integrity (refusing to make excuses for ethically questionable behavior), high trust in rules, and identifying with the larger community or country (instead of identifying with “being a good friend”), were specifically preventative against Particularism. The studies supported by this grant also showed that moral motivations to engage in particularism increase when the environment is perceived to be non-transparent (Objective 2; the focus of Paper 2), and that certain kinds of personal moral values can lead to more moral motivations to engage in particularism (Objective 3, the focus of Paper 3). Specifically, both Paper 2 and 3 show that feeling morally obligated to help friends/family is associated with tolerating or engaging in particularism (that is, abusing one’s power / breaking rules in order to help a friend or family member). As hypothesized, Paper 2 shows evidence that when the social environment is perceived as corruption-prone, this increases the likelihood of engaging in particularism, more than engaging in bribery-type corruption. That is, in corruption-prone environments, moral motivations to help one’s friends and family by engaging in particularism increase. These findings suggest that to reduce particularism, it is also important to increase trust in the fairness of rules and the social environment. Paper 1 (under review), addressing Objective 1, combines sophisticated scale development process with Bayesian SEM to address the question of which individual differences predict tolerance of Particularism vs. Corruption, in Hong Kong and mainland China. Paper 2 (in preparation), addressing Objective 2, uses results of behavioral and survey-experimental studies to address the question of how perceptions of the environment affect moral guilt and particularistic vs. corrupt behavior. Paper 3 (in preparation), addressing Objective 3, uses results of experimental and correlational studies to address the question of how filial piety and collectivistic self-concepts affect sense of moral conflict and proclivity towards engaging in particularism. CHALLENGES A major disruption to research progress was experienced in 2019/20, when social movements first delayed the arrival of a replacement RA, and then on-campus activities were cancelled due to the social movements, and finally the COVID-19 situation disrupted data collection in both Hong Kong and Mainland China (which continued to slow data collection through the 2020/21 year). Through careful management of the resources available and adjustments to continued COVID restrictions in the 2020/21 academic year, we were finally able to complete the project successfully. We are very grateful for the quickly-approved extensions given first by our university and then by the RGC.

18613017.label: Major findings and research outcome
18613017.value: Findings will be published in 3 articles: Paper 1 combined a sophisticated scale development process with Bayesian SEM to address the question of which individual differences predict tolerance of Particularism vs. Corruption, in Hong Kong and mainland China. Development of a new measurement tool allowed us to test if certain traits uniquely weaken defenses against particularism, vs. bribery-type corruption. Most virtues helped prevent against corruption, but were not additionally protective against particularism, which was only uniquely related to moral excuse-making. Filial piety had surprising associations specific to corruption tolerance: While authoritarian filial piety was problematic, relational filial piety was preventative. In sum, only strict internal integrity and belief in rules helped protect against particularism; and while filial piety is not uniquely related to particularism, authoritarian filial piety is associated with more tolerance of bribery-type corruption. Paper 2 uses behavioral and survey-experimental studies to show how perceptions of the environment affect moral guilt and particularistic vs. corrupt behavior. Study 1 manipulated participants’ perception of the social environment, showing that when others commonly break rules for friends and family, the moral pressure to do the same increases; moreover, this effect is stronger for particularism than corruption. Study 2 used a behavioral study with pairs of friends, who used their own real prize money to help a friend win a contest by bribing a judge. Participants offered more money when it would help their friend vs. help themselves, and felt guilty if they did NOT bribe to help their friend. Moreover, when they knew other participants commonly bribed, this increased rates of bribing. In sum, corrupt environments increase the moral pressure to engage in particularism. Paper 3 uses both experimental and correlational methods to examine how different aspects of filial piety and collectivistic self-concepts affect likelihood to help and sense of moral conflict. In Study 1, we experimentally induced different forms of collectivistic self-aspects, showing that priming relational collectivism led to increased likelihood of saying yes to misusing power to help a family member, but group collectivism led to less likelihood of helping. Study 2 replicated and extended Study 1 with correlational evidence, showing that self-rated group collectivism and reciprocal filial piety were protective against tolerance of particularism (different from relational collectivism and authoritarian filial piety), but also that reciprocal filial piety was related to feeling a greater amount of moral conflict about the decision.

18613017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18613017.value: We found that positive attitudes towards following the rules were especially protective against tolerating particularism (over and above corruption), and conversely environments where rules were frequently broken especially increased rates of particularism (compared to corruption). But what if the rules themselves aren’t fair? An important avenue of research is to study the effects of environments where rules are perceived as overly competitive or complex. In such environments, rules may no longer be perceived as objective, fairness-enhancing mechanisms. Such environments may also increase selfish motivations such as expected reciprocity, as one might need to depend on similar help in the future. Thus, we hope that the dissemination of these findings will lead to research on the effects of different cultural and social environments, and on how to prevent self-serving motivations to engage in particularism. Interventions can also be pursued with the support of Knowledge Transfer or PPR grants. We have communicated with the Youth & Moral Education Office (YMEO), Community Relations Department of the ICAC, and hope that their department will consider our recommendation to specifically address particularism, which is morally ambiguous compared to bribery. I look forward to working with them to develop more community and school education resources.

18613017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18613017.value: Does the Confucian virtue of filial piety-- and its requirement to "love with distinction"-- encourage corruption? Can we combat corruption without weakening filial values? We developed a new measure of temptation to misuse power to help friends and family (called Particularism) vs. to get bribes, and found that certain kinds of filial values make people prone to taking bribes (being overly obedient to parents, instead of having an equal but loving relationship with them). Tolerance of particularism was specifically avoided by people who have very high personal integrity and a strong belief in following rules. We also found evidence that particularism is often morally motivated, as people feel guilty if they refuse to help friends and family, even though it would break the rules and disadvantage other people. Moreover, when we think that other people commonly “do favors” for friends and family, it increases moral pressure to do the same. Finally, we found that identifying more with “being a good friend” than “being a good community member” increases tendencies to engage in particularism. We suggest that anti-corruption campaigns should pay special attention to preventing moral temptations to engage in particularism, by changing perceptions of the environment and inculcating personal integrity.

21101917.value: 細胞平面極性化（PCP）是指細胞結構和活性在組織平面上的不對稱分布，其對於生物的發育和健康都具有重要的意義。但是我們目前對PCP在腫瘤發生和發展過程中的作用所知甚少。近來研究表明PCP信號通路對細胞遷移和侵襲有重要調節功能，提示其在腫瘤轉移中的潛在作用。我們之前的工作發現PCP信號通路中的Pk1和Smurf2蛋白通過調節乳腺癌細胞細胞骨架和外形的動態變化來控制腫瘤細胞的遷移和轉移，然而PCP信號通路在癌症轉移中作用的分子機制尚不明確。 泛素-蛋白酶體系統是細胞調節蛋白水平和功能的重要通路。研究發現一系列PCP信號蛋白，例如Dvl 和Pk的水平受到泛素-蛋白酶體的精密控制。我們的前期研究發現Pk1與泛素-蛋白酶體系統中的去泛素化蛋白USP7相互作用，並且USP7的敲減導致Pk1水平的降低和對細胞遷移的抑制。在分子水平，USP7拮抗Smurf2介導的Pk1的泛素化和降解。本研究項目將基於這些發現繼續深入研究USP7對PCP信號通路和癌症轉移的調節作用和機制。我們的目標是理清USP7通過Pk1對PCP信號通路的整合調節。我們將綜合運用生物化學，分子生物學和共聚焦顯微成像來開展研究。首先我們會闡明USP7與Pk1相互作用的分子基礎以及其在腫瘤細胞遷移中的功能。另外我們將研究USP7-Pk1復合體與其他PCP信號蛋白如Vangl, Fzd, Dvl功能的潛在交叉。同時我們將利用三維培養體系研究USP7-Pk1通路在腫瘤侵襲中的作用。我們的研究將闡明泛素-蛋白酶體系統與PCP信號通路在腫瘤發展過程中的整合機制，同時可以提示PCP信號通路中潛在的癌症轉移的潛在治療靶點。

21102517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21102517.value: The brain consumes very high levels of energy, which represents approximately 20% of the total amount of energy consumption of the whole organism, while representing only about 2% of body weight. Thus, alterations of brain energy metabolism are closely associated with the neuropathogenesis of neurological disorders. Glucose is the essential energy substrate for the function and development of the central nervous system (CNS). However, in certain conditions such as oxygen and glucose deficiency, monocarboxylates, including lactate and ketone bodies, are significantly consumed by the CNS as alternative energy fuels. For example, during the neonatal period, lactate and ketone bodies, including beta-hydroxybutyrate and acetoacetate, are enriched in the blood; they enter into the CNS, and play a key role for the developing CNS as energy substrates, bioprecursors, and developmental signals. The movement of monocarboxylates is mainly dependent on proton-linked monocarboxylate transporters (MCTs). Among MCTs, monocarboxylate transporter 1 (MCT1) is the most abundant monocarboxylate transporter in the CNS. In previous experiments, we found that MCT1 was highly enriched in oligodendroglia, and also in subsets of neurons. Furthermore, we found that MCT1 was mainly present in the myelin sheaths of oligodendroglia, and that its insufficiency in vivo induced axonopathy and neurodegeneration in the CNS, suggesting impaired metabolic support of axons by myelinating oligodendroglia via MCT1. However, the effect of complete loss or gain of oligodendroglial MCT1 function on the developing CNS has to be elucidated because the conventional knockout of the MCT1 gene is embryonically lethal in the homozygous state. Thus, we have established a novel conditional MCT1loxP/loxP mouse line via Cre/LoxP technology. Particularly, previous reports indicated that monocarboxylates, including lactate and ketone bodies, could stimulate the differentiation of OPCs and the expression of myelin genes in vitro, and our preliminary work in vivo using a conditional MCT1loxP/loxP mouse indicated that MCT1 could play a key role in proper myelination presumably by facilitating monocarboxylate uptake into oligodendroglia. In addition, the expression of myelin genes and MCT1 appeared to be upregulated by optogenetic stimulation in the co-culture of neurons and OPCs in a microfluidic system. Thus, we hypothesize that neuron-derived signals, such as axonal stimulation, can increase MCT1 expression, by which developing oligodendroglia can facilitate the uptake of monocarboxylates, leading to stimulating myelination to wrap the axons. As a result, complete loss of oligodendroglial MCT1 function in the neonatal brain could induce defects in myelination, which is associated with abnormal axon- and synapse- maturation.

21201217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21201217.value: The brain’s function is closely related to electrical activity. During hearing, sound enters the ears and the information is transformed into brain electrical activity. Electrophysiology studies the electrical properties of cells and tissues and is important for hearing research and neuroscience in general. Electrophysiology using methods such as extracellular recordings measures the activity of single or multiple cells in vivo. Such recordings require placing fine electrodes into sound processing centers in the brain. One significant challenge in recordings is placing the electrode precisely within a center as the brain is large. This challenge is common to related methods such as those using electrode arrays, optogenetics, site-targeted injections, and deep brain stimulation. Electrode placement is typically guided by atlases of the brain. This method has several limitations: (1) Precise placement depends on close agreement between the atlas and the subject’s brain. Many factors can affect agreement, such as age and inter-species differences. (2) Brain injury, or plasticity, can also change the precise size, shape, location, and function of sound processing centers. Unfortunately, the changes are known only after extensive research, which significantly complicates electrode placement for performing that research. Brain mapping using noninvasive imaging has guided surgical procedures, including electrode placement. Guidance has typically been provided by anatomical images acquired with technology such as magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and computed tomography. For in vivo recordings from sound processing centers, functional images are also required to precisely locate the centers, especially in situations such as (2) above. This project will develop novel anatomical and functional imaging guided electrode placement methods for rat hearing models. Rats are widely used in hearing research and our group recently developed functional MRI (fMRI) for rat hearing models. Noninvasive MRI and fMRI images will be acquired of the living brain with sound stimulation. State-of-the-art MRI sequences will be employed that significantly reduce the impact of scanner acoustic noise. The locations of sound processing centers and anatomical landmarks, visible in images and during surgery, will be determined with 500 µm precision. These locations will set subject-specific coordinates, using which the electrode will be precisely placed in the target center. This imaging guided electrophysiology method will be applied to study the impact of long-term, low sound level noise on sound processing in the brain. Noise pollution is a serious health concern and the resulting multi-modality imaging and electrophysiology data will significantly advance our understanding of the impact on hearing.

21201217.label: Realisation of objectives
21201217.value: We developed the brain mapping guided electrode placement method using standard structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and sound-evoked functional MRI (fMRI). This was applied to study the neural correlates of hyperacusis, a potentially debilitating hearing condition. Electrode placement was guided by imaging and accuracy of one voxel (0.5 mm) was achieved in the axial direction and two voxels in the transverse direction. Combining imaging with conventional behavioral and electrophysiological assessments revealed a progressive enhancement of sound-evoked neural activity ascending the auditory pathway from the midbrain up to the cortex. In other words, the neurophysiological effects of hyperacusis are most severe in the cortex. These results were published in the leading journal Hearing Research and a summary is given below. METHODS Subjects: Normal male Sprague-Dawley rats underwent behavioral reaction time-intensity measurement (N=4), sound-evoked functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) (N=6), or electrophysiological recordings (N=10). Sodium salicylate administration: Subjects were given an intraperitoneal injection of sodium salicylate (Sigma-Aldrich). Salicylate was dissolved in saline solution at a dose of 250 mg/kg body weight. Data collection for the salicylate condition began approximately 2 hrs following salicylate treatment when salicylate-induced hyperacusis and hyperactivity are present. Reaction time-intensity measurements: Auditory reaction time-intensity measurements are strongly correlated with perceived loudness in humans and have been used as a reliable surrogate of loudness perception in animals [1-4]. In this study, we obtained reaction time-intensity functions using broadband noise bursts to confirm that high-dose salicylate induced changes consistent with hyperacusis (i.e., shorter than normal reaction times at high sound levels) [5]. fMRI: Subjects (N=6) were lightly anesthetized with 1% isoflurane. A custom delivery tube with a needle was inserted into the peritoneum of the subject for delivering saline and salicylate. The tube was attached to the syringe containing the solution. For sound stimulation delivery, a 1.7 m long, 8 mm inner diameter (tapered to 2 mm over the last 5 cm) nylon tube was connected to a 6.5 cm long, 2 mm inner diameter polyurethane tube that entered the left ear canal [6]. Scanning was performed inside a 7 T MRI scanner using a transmit-only birdcage coil. Electrophysiological recordings: Sound-evoked multi-unit spike discharge recordings and local field potentials (LFP) were obtained from the IC, MGB, and AC to corroborate fMRI findings. Electrode localization was confirmed by imaging a rat implanted with electrodes in the IC and AC. Accuracy within one voxel (0.5 mm) was obtained in the axial direction and within two voxels in the transverse direction by comparing with the sound-evoked fMRI images overlaid on standard anatomical images. The electrophysiological recordings were obtained in an electrically shielded sound booth. A 16-channel linear silicon microelectrode array was used to record spike discharges from multiunit clusters and LFP from the IC (N=4), MGB (N=3) or AC (N=3). RESULTS Faster reaction times (RTs) for high sound level stimuli: We found a significant main effect of sound level, indicating that RTs get faster with increasing stimulus intensity. Importantly, we observed that high-dose salicylate has a significant impact on loudness growth. We found a significant interaction between experimental condition (baseline, saline, and salicylate) and sound level. Pairwise comparisons between salicylate and saline RTs indicated a significant effect of salicylate on RT at 90, 80, and 40 dB. As in our previous studies [5, 7], RTs after high-dose salicylate administration were longer for low SPLs (<50 dB), likely due to temporary outer hair cell dysfunction and associated hearing loss. In contrast, at high SPLs (≥80 dB), RTs were shorter than normal, indicative of a hyperacusis-like percept (i.e., shorter RTs indicate louder than normal percept) consistent with our earlier publications in which salicylate shortened RTs at high sound levels for both broadband noise as well as tone bursts [5]. fMRI observes enhanced central auditory gain: Sound-evoked fMRI responses were observed in the contralateral lateral lemniscus (LL), inferior colliculus (IC), medial geniculate body (MGB), and auditory cortex (AC), key regions along the ascending auditory pathway. In the midbrain (LL and IC), t-values were slightly higher during salicylate, compared with saline, at 8 and 16 kHz. The LL BOLD responses, obtained upon analysis of the time series, were similar. Pairwise comparisons between saline and salicylate indicated that IC responses to 16 kHz tones presented at 80 dB were greater during salicylate than saline. Higher up the auditory pathway in the MGB, the number of activated voxels at 8 and 16 kHz was greater during salicylate. In the AC, both t-values and number of activated voxels were considerably greater during salicylate. This enhancement occurred across all three frequencies. AC BOLD responses to 8 and 16 kHz sounds were considerably greater during salicylate. Given that salicylate reduces the neural output of the cochlea by more than 50%, these results are consistent with enhanced central auditory gain in higher auditory structures during salicylate-induced hyperacusis [8, 9]. Electrophysiology confirms fMRI: In the IC, LFP amplitudes measured after saline and salicylate treatments were generally similar across all SPLs and frequencies. In the MGB, salicylate LFPs were slightly larger than saline LFPs. In the AC, salicylate LFPs were considerably larger than saline LFPs, particularly at higher intensities where the responses had increased by almost 2-fold. The salicylate-induced increases relative to saline increased with SPL with largest differences occurring between 4-30 kHz. Altogether, our LFP results show that suprathreshold response amplitudes in the IC were generally normal (i.e., similar saline) even though this dose of salicylate has been shown to reduce the neural output of the cochlea by more than 50%. Normal responses in the IC provide evidence of significant gain enhancement between the cochlea and IC [8, 10]. LFP amplitudes in the IC are largely consistent with the noninvasive fMRI results. LFP amplitudes in the AC were greatly enhanced at suprathreshold intensities, particularly between 8 and 16 kHz, consistent with our noninvasive fMRI data which showed a robust increase in fMRI amplitude at 8 and 16 kHz. Functional images will be acquired with functional MRI (fMRI) using sound stimulation. The images will set subject-specific coordinates with 500 µm precision for guiding surgical placement of extracellular recording electrodes in sound processing centers. The accuracy of placement will be verified by repeating MRI with the electrodes in place.

21201217.label: Major findings and research outcome
21201217.value: Hyperacusis is a debilitating hearing condition in which normal everyday sounds are perceived as exceedingly loud, annoying, aversive or even painful. The prevalence of hyperacusis approaches 10%, making it an important, but understudied medical condition. To noninvasively identify the neural correlates of hyperacusis in an animal model, we used sound-evoked functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) to locate regions of abnormal activity in the central nervous system of rats with behavioral evidence of hyperacusis induced with an ototoxic drug (sodium salicylate, 250 mg/kg, i.p.). Reaction time-intensity measures of loudness-growth revealed behavioral evidence of salicylate-induced hyperacusis at high intensities. fMRI revealed significantly enhanced sound-evoked responses in the auditory cortex (AC) to 80 dB SPL tone bursts presented at 8 and 16 kHz. Sound-evoked responses in the inferior colliculus (IC) were also enhanced, but to a lesser extent. To confirm the main results, electrophysiological recordings of spike discharges from multi-unit clusters were obtained from central auditory pathway regions with fMRI responses. Salicylate significantly enhanced tone-evoked spike-discharges from multi-unit clusters in the AC from 4 – 30 kHz at intensities ≥ 60 dB SPL; less enhancement occurred in the medial geniculate body (MGB), and even less in the IC. Our results demonstrate for the first time that non-invasive sound-evoked fMRI can be used to identify regions of neural hyperactivity throughout the brain in an animal model of hyperacusis.

21201217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21201217.value: The structural and functional imaging guided electrode placement developed in this study can be applied to other animal disease models and clinical use. At present, electrode placement is primarily guided by structural imaging. However, functional imaging, such as by fMRI, provides metabolic and evoked neural response information not present in structural images. This can be very valuable for recordings and stimulation based on neural activity. Further, the imaging method can be extended to guide the placement of optical probes/stimulators, not just electrical. We envision multi-modal structural and functional imaging to be the standard for guiding probe/stimulator placement in the brain in the coming years. In this study, we also expanded understanding of the neural basis of hyperacusis. With imaging verified by electrode recordings, we established that the ascending auditory pathway overamplifies sound-evoked neural activity in hyperacusis. This is likely related to the percept of everyday sounds being too loud in hyperacusis patients. This understanding of the neural basis will help with future development of treatments for hyperacusis based on reducing the over-amplification.

21201217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21201217.value: This project has developed structural and functional imaging technology for accurate placement of electrodes in the brain. Electrodes are used routinely to monitor brain activity and stimulate brain activity. However, their effectiveness depends very much on accurate placement in the target brain region. Traditionally, electrode placement has been guided by structural imaging technology, such as conventional computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging. Structural imaging gives detailed brain anatomy information, but does not inform the functional status of the brain. For example, a living and recently deceased brain are structurally very similar, but functionally very different. In this project, we further applied the imaging guided electrode placement technology to study the neural basis of hyperacusis, a debilitating hearing condition where everyday sounds are perceived as too loud. We identified that the brain, especially the cortex, over responds to sound in hyperacusis, likely leading to the percept of everyday sounds being too loud.

21202517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21202517.value: It is well known that trade-off between strength and ductility in metallic alloys is a long-standing challenge for material scientists and solid physicists. In high entropy alloys, the simultaneous improvement of both properties at cryogenic temperatures shows a promising prospect to conquer it. Deformation-induced nano-twin with unexpected low formation energy is apparently one major reason for the property improvement. This counterintuitive phenomenon, that is, why introducing a defect such as twins can in fact take a system down to a more stable state, remains an unknown puzzle attracting a broad research interest at the present time. Our preliminary study based on density functional theory (DFT) offers a clear physical explanation that the surprisingly negative stacking fault energy is caused by three factors: (1) energy preference of the HCP phase and the meta-stability of FCC phase at low temperatures, as well as (2) atomic composition around the stacking fault and influence from (3) lattice distortion. This proposal will address four important issues in order to further understand the origin of deformation mechanism. The first issue is to continue our preliminary static stacking fault energy and work on dynamics aspect of it. Unstable stacking fault energy (USFE) and sluggish diffusion will be carefully studied through DFT calculations. The second issue is to further analysis the atomic concentration around stacking faults by focused ion beam and atom probe tomography (APT), since preliminary results also strongly hint that stacking fault deformation may start from cobalt-rich or nickel-lean layers. The third issue is to investigate phase stability and precipitate concentration. Critical shear strain and atomic percentage to produce precipitate will be calculated by DFT and spatial atomic concentration will be examined by APT and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS). The last issue is to develop the most common FeNiCrCo potential function for molecular dynamic simulation purpose. In conclusion, our simulation and APT ability as well as support from collaborator including sample preparation, mechanical test and TEM technique, outcome of this research will bring in a whole new perspective to the understanding and design of HEAs for structural applications in cryogenic temperatures. Beyond the common rule of thumb of choosing low stacking-fault-energy elements, this study will reveal a scientific base to control the twin formability from thermodynamic stability in different lattice structures. Under this guideline, much previous trial and error efforts can be substantially reduced, and greatly accelerate HEA alloy design in the future. 高熵合金（HEAs）是2004年首次報導的新型合金。它不具有任何特定的主要元素作為傳統合金的基礎溶液。構成HEA的所有元素幾乎等於原子百分比，從而使構型熵最大化。這種新的合金設計理念帶來了許多驚人的性能，包括非常高的強度（> 1 GPa），優異的延展性（斷裂應變70％）和高斷裂韌性（KJIC> 200 MPam1 / 2）。晶格畸變是高熵合金的一個獨特特徵。由於嚴重的變形，可以防止高熵合金內的擴散速率，這就是所謂的擴散現象遲緩。其他機制如變形誘導納米攣晶，微帶，甚至轉變誘導塑性輔助雙相高熵合金（TRIPDP-HEA)已被觀察和報告具有不同的高熵合金組成。 眾所周知，金屬合金的強度和延展性之間的折衷是材料科學家和固體物理學家長期存在的挑戰。在HEAs中，在低溫下同時改善了兩種性能，這顯示出有希望征服它。具有意想不到的低地層能量的變形誘導納米攣晶顯然是物性改進的一個主要原因。這種違反直覺的現象，也就是說，為什麼引入諸如攣晶的缺陷實際上可能使系統處於更穩定的狀態，仍然是目前未知的難題，吸引了廣泛的研究興趣。我們基於密度泛函理論（DFT）的初步研究提供了一個明確的物理解釋，令人驚訝的負堆垛層錯能源是由（1）HCP相的能量偏好和FCC的元穩定性低溫下的相，以及（3）堆垛層錯的原子組成以及（3）晶格畸變的影響。 為了進一步了解變形機理的起源，我們提出了四個目標來實現這一目標。首先，我們將繼續我們的初步靜態堆垛層錯能量，並在其動力學方面進行工作。不穩定的堆垛層錯能（USFE）和緩慢的擴散將通過DFT計算進行仔細研究。除此之外，初步的結果也強烈地暗示堆垛層錯變形可以從富鈷或貧鎳層開始。為了驗證這一觀點，我們將通過聚焦離子束和原子探測層析成像（APT）進一步分析堆垛層錯的原子成分分佈。此外，將研究相穩定性和偏析。臨界剪切應變和產生沉澱物的原子百分比將通過DFT計算，空間原子濃度將通過APT和透射電子顯微鏡（TEM）X射線光譜（EDS）進行檢測。最後，我們將開發用於分子動力學模擬目的的最常見的FeNiCrCo潛在功能。 我們的模擬和APT能力以及來自合作者的支持，包括樣品製備，機械測試和TEM技術，本研究的結果將為低溫結構應用的HEAs的理解和設計帶來全新的視角。除了選擇低堆垛層錯能量元素的常見經驗之外，本研究將揭示一種科學基礎，以控制不同晶格結構中熱力學穩定性。在此準則下，以前的大部分嘗試和錯誤的努力可以大大減少，並在將來大大加快了HEA合金設計。

21202517.label: Realisation of objectives
21202517.value: Object 1: To study on unstable stacking fault energy, sluggish diffusion phenomenon Progress: Stacking faults, as defects of disordered crystallographic planes, are one of the most important slipping mechanisms in the commonly seen lattice, face-centered cubic (FCC). Such defects can initiate twinning which strengthens mechanical properties, e.g. twinning-induced plasticity (TWIP), of high entropy alloys (HEAs) at cryogenic temperatures. We used density functional theory (DFT), to discuss twinning initiated from stacking faults regarding to two different solute elements, Al and Mo, in the FeNiCoCr HEAs. Our results show that adding aluminum (Al) has noticeable enhancement of twinnability while molybdenum (Mo) only induces more stacking faults in the FeNiCoCr-based HEAs. More results are listed in research output. Object 2: To investigate local atomic environment through DFT and APT Progress: Multi-component random solid solutions have caused much interest for research because they often exhibit excellent mechanical properties. Many computational efforts have been made through various length scales, by first principles, molecular dynamics or finite elements. We developed a quasi-simulated-annealing (Markov Chain Monte Carlo algorithm) with prior burn-in procedure using chemical short-range order parameters as input values is developed for searching the global optimal distribution of species with regard to the phase stability of face-centered cubic CoCrNi alloys. Our results show that this new approach could effectively generate the stable structures with a desired concentration and moreover, the stacking fault energies of these configurations have less uncertainties statistically. Atom probe Tomography analysis for atomic local environment is done and published together with density functional theory calculation. It is shown in our papers that local atomic environment does affect the nanotwin and stacking fault formation possibility. Object 3: To analyse phase stability and precipitate concentration using DFT, TEM-EDS and APT Progress: The FeNiCoCr-based high entropy alloys (HEAs) exhibit excellent mechanical properties, such as twin-induced plasticity (TWIP) and phase transformation plasticity (TRIP) that can reach a remarkable combination of strength and ductility. In the present work, the face-centered-cubic (FCC) single-crystal FeNiCoCrAl0.36 HEAs were studied, using the density functional theory (DFT) combined with the phonon calculation to estimate the stacking fault energies, temperature-dependent phase stabilities of different structures. And the kinetic Monte Carlo (kMC) was used to predict the substructures evolution based on the transition state energies obtained from DFT calculations. We proposed two different formation paths of nano-twins in this Al-composited HEA and found that short-range hexagonal-close-packed (HCP)-stacking could occur in this HEA. The DFT calculations suggest that this HEA has negative stacking fault energy (SFE), HCP formation energy, and twin-formation energy at 0 K. Phonon calculations indicate that at the finite temperature, the competing FCC/HCP phase stability and propensity for twinning make it possible to form HCP-like twin boundaries. The kMC simulations suggest that under deformation, TWINs could form within the HCP laths which differs from the study of others. With the great agreement of results from kMC simulations and experiments, this twin-hcp laminated substructure formation path offers a new concept of designing TWIP HEAs containing tunable twin structures with HCP and TWIN lamellae structures, which could result in better mechanical properties of HEAs. Object 4: To develop DFT HEA potential function for further MD applications Progress: MEAM potential form is chosen for our purpose precipitate hardening and second phase stability are examined by both experimentally and theoretically. The modified embedded-atom interatomic potential of quaternary high entropy alloy (HEA) FeNiCrCo is developed combination of first-principles calculations. The potentials can reproduce various fundamental physical properties (lattice constant, vacancy and stacking fault properties) in reasonable agreement with experimental data or first-principles and other calculations. The potential parameters can be used for the studies of atomistic simulations of FeNiCrCo microstructures, and the strength properties about FeNiCrCo alloy are studies. Manuscript is under preparation.

21202517.label: Major findings and research outcome
21202517.value: In general, the entropy of a material can be decomposed into configurational, vibrational, electronic, and magnetic entropies. The entropies differ for body-centered-cubic (BCC), face-centered-cubic (FCC), hexagonal-close-packed (HCP), and other crystal structures. Among them, the configurational entropy calculations borrowed from the ideal gas mixing remain the same for all crystal structures. For many years, this difference was neglected in the theorems of traditional physical metallurgy with the dilute solid-solution assumption, but it should no longer be ignored for high-entropy alloys (HEAs), which are composed of at least five elements in equiatomic or non-equiatomic percentages. However, the precise definition for crystal configurational entropy is unknown. Here we show that the configurational entropy of FCC and HCP differ based on combinatorial mathematics and rotation-point-group calculations. Our results suggest that the HCP structure has a higher configurational entropy than the FCC one, especially on a small scale. To conclude, distinguishing configurational entropy differences not only provides a possible explanation for current critical issues of superior strength-toughness combinations in cryogenic HEAs and FCC-to-HCP phase transition in highly-pressurized HEAs, but also challenges the traditional computations of entropy across metallurgy, crystallography, statistical mechanics, and all other related research fields.

21202517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21202517.value: Configurational entropy is very critical for phase transformation beginning from nanoscale dimensions, because the free-energy change during phase transformation must consider the nano-size effect. This finding for the configurational entropy difference between various crystal structures in nanoscale dimensions thus opens a new world for scientists to reconsider all related conventional theorems so far. Diffusion theorems may require serious modification efforts before appropriate application on HEAs in both pre-exponential term and activation energy distribution. And precise value of cofigurational entropy as a function of temperature should be carefully studied. Potential for further developments can include the following four important configurational entropy issues in current high entropy alloys research field: (1) To calculate configurational entropy based on point groups (2) To calculate configurational entropy based on space groups (3) To verify the relationship between configurational entropy and sluggish diffusion (4) To verify the relationship between configurational entropy and temperature.

21202517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21202517.value: Although the connection between symmetry and entropy is not clear, researchers calculate configurational entropy with an ideal gas mixing model all along regardless of which structure they are considering. However, it is obvious that crystalline structures have symmetry, while an ideal gas does not. Therefore, the same ideal gas mixing value should not be assigned to other structures, such as face-centered-cubic (fcc) and hexagonal-close-packed (hcp) structures. Here, we offer a precise definition for determining the configurational entropy of crystals. We calculate the difference in configurational entropy between fcc and hcp structures based on Burnside's lemma in combinatorial mathematics and crystallographic rotation-point groups. This work generalizes the conventional concept of configurational mixing entropy (S) ordering from S_gas > S_liquid > S_solid , to , S_gas > S_liquid >⋯> S_hcp>⋯> S_fcc>⋯>⋯ with clearly mathematic statement of relation between symmetry and entropy. where FCC and HCP stands for different crystal structure.

21210217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21210217.value: 隨著香港和中國土木工程及建築業的飛速發展，事故頻繁發生，工人的不安全行為被認為是主要事業。基於行為的安全（BBS）是修改工人不安全行為的一種有效方法，但很少注意工人的個人特徵。因此，本研究提出了大型項目建設中的基於移動設備的個性化工作者行為修改體系。首先，通過大數據驅動平台探索個性化推薦機制，包括基於內容的個性化推薦和基於MapReduce的協同過濾個性化推薦。為香港土木工程和建築施工建設安全規劃和普遍存在的風險評估提供了廣泛的數據。根據中國武漢地鐵3號線1年試點研究和香港相關研究，我們的團隊建議使用大型數據驅動平台自動規劃，分類，收集和存儲建築工人的數據，不安全的行為。這個目標是通過這些數據有效地修改工作人員的不安全行為，因此通過結合傳統的BBS方法和個性化推薦支持工具提出了一種基於移動設備的個性化工作者行為修改平台。大數據的有利發展有助於快速提取有價值的數據，並協助科學預測，學習和管理。作為大數據技術之一，個性化推薦可以通過分析他們的行為模式來準確地推動用戶感興趣的信息。同樣，通過使用這種技術，可以探索個性化工作者行為修改的機制。基於此，設計了平台：將施工現場工作人員不安全行為的圖像作為數據源，匹配行為修改內容與不同工人的行為模式相匹配，然後通過該平台修改不安全行為。

21210217.label: Realisation of objectives
21210217.value: This study explores the relationship between fluctuation in economic and industrial development and work-related fatalities of Chinese construction workers. Methods: The data for work-related fatalities in housing and civil engineering in China from 1996 to 2016 were tested for fluctuation and trends of both general economic and industry-specific indicators using the Engle-Granger cointegration analysis and the augmented Granger Causality test the with modified Wald method. Results: Both the long-run equilibrium associations and short-run dynamic interactions between construction safety and macroeconomic development in China were determined. According to the estimates, fatalities in the construction industry appeared to be more significantly associated with changes in the gross output value of the industry, and the improvement in the workers' efficiency also contributed to the decline of fatalities. It initially revealed that the changes in growth rate, instead of growth itself, had a more significant influence on construction safety in China, while a marginal decreasing trend of positive effects exerted by the growth can be expected with the gradual maturity of the industry. Significance: The application of econometrical methods explored an untapped data source for gaining an insight into the underlying rules of occurrence of construction fatalities, thus strengthening the body of knowledge of construction safety by providing a new research perspective that some safety indicators can be treated as the macro-level socioeconomic index. Practical applications: The findings reminded policymakers and practitioners to be aware of potential challenges from the slowing or even declining trend facing the industry in the near future, and offered a reference to relevant authorities for establishing a more targeted and effective governance strategy.

21301517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21301517.value: Integral inequalities that concern the weighted positivity of a differential operator have many important applications in the qualitative theory of elliptic boundary value problems. In this study, we focus on the 3D linear elastostatic (Lame) system for an isotropic, homogeneous elastic medium and propose to extend our previous results obtained in (Luo and Maz'ya 2010, Luo and Maz'ya 2015) to a larger range of elastic parameters, by considering a new class of weight functions first proposed and systematically studied in (Mayboroda and Maz'ya 2009, Mayboroda and Maz'ya 2014). The weighted inequalities, if successfully established, will lead to many new interesting results, including Wiener type criteria for the regularity of a boundary point, and pointwise estimates for Green's functions and solutions of the 3D Lame system in arbitrary domains. If a uniform, positive lower bound for the constant occurring in the weighted inequality can be obtained, the results may even be extended to the 3D linear hydrostatic (Stokes) system, which would settle many important problems in the theory of the Navier-Stokes equations in general domains. 關於微分算子加權正定性的積分不等式在橢圓邊值問題的理論中有著很多重要的應用。在本項目中，我們致力於研究描述各向同性的均勻彈性介質的三維線性 Lame 系統，並嘗試將我們之前取得的部分結果（Luo and Maz'ya 2010, 2015）進行推廣，使之適用於更大範圍的彈性參數。我們采用的方法是考慮一類新的權重函數，該類函數（在積分不等式中的應用）首先由 Mayboroda 和 Maz'ya （2009, 2014）提出並進行系統研究。如果這類帶有權重函數的積分不等式能夠成功在 Lame 系統中得到證明，那麼基於它們將推導出一系列（關於 Lame 系統）的重要結果，包括關於邊界點正則性判定的 Wiener 準則，格林函數及解在任意域上的逐點估計，等等。如果不等式的下界能夠被證明一致非負，那麼上述結果甚至可能被推廣至三維線性 Stokes 系統，這將為 Navier-Stokes 方程組在任意域上的理論研究帶來許多重大突破。

21301817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21301817.value: Separation of gas mixtures into their pure components represents a dominant technology in chemical engineering – accounting for up to 60% of total cost in many industrial processes. The objective of this project is to develop a new “active sieving” technology that enables radically high efficiency molecular separation. This can potentially bring tens of billions of dollars in profits for industries relying on gas separations, such as fuel gas production, carbon capture and sequestration, and environmental protection. Unlike the conventional size-selective molecular sieving adsorbents that are incapable of distinguishing between small molecules of similar sizes, here, a new class of active sieving adsorbents are developed that feature exclusive admission of target molecules by regulating their interactions with the pore-keeping groups of the materials. This has been described by a new “molecular trapdoor” effect that we reported recently. Modulation of the trapdoor allows for highly selective and thus cost-effective molecular separation. By extending on the molecular trapdoor mechanism, the proposed study will combine experimental and theoretical simulation investigations to establish guidelines to construct the active sieving adsorbents and explore the employment of external stimuli, including temperature, chemical species, and electric field, to regulate the active sieving behaviour. This affords a revolutionary strategy to obtain highly selective adsorbents for purpose-orientated separations. To demonstrate the design potential of the new active sieving mechanism, candidate adsorbents will be explored from zeolites to selected metal-organic frameworks. This will substantially enrich the materials design toolbox and present a major step forward in future generation of tailor-made adsorbents. Mixture gas separation experiments and further pressure/temperature swing adsorption process tests will showcase the real-world performance of this active molecular sieving technology. In addition, these active sieves could also enable highly selective membranes, sensors, and catalysts. 气体分离在化工领域中是一项非常重要的单元操作，在很多工业产出过程中占到多达60%的成本。本项目致力于开发一种全新的“主动筛分”技术以从根本上实现高效的分子分离。本项目的成功完成将会为依赖于气体分离技术的工业生产部门带来巨大的潜在经济效益，包括能源气体的生产，碳捕捉和地质封存，以及环境保护领域。 与传统的基于尺寸效应实现分子筛分不同，我们致力于开发一类“主动筛分”吸附材料—基于调控目标客体分子与主体吸附材料的“堵孔基团”的相互作用来实现选择性的气体分离。我们已经把这种“主动筛分”过程命名为“分子陷阱门”效应。调控“陷阱门”能使我们实现低成本高效的选择性分子分离。 通过拓展“分子陷阱门”效应，本项目将结合利用实验和分子模拟手段研究来建立一套准则用于设计“主动筛分”吸附材料，并且探索运用外加刺激因素（包括温度，化学刺激物，和电场）调控“主动筛分”行为。这将会提供一种革命性的手段来获得以特定分离目的为导向的高效吸附剂。为了展示这种“主动筛分”机制的在吸附材料上的设计潜力，典型的多孔吸附材料包括沸石和金属有机框架化合物将会被设计合成。这将极大程度地丰富材料设计的“工具箱”，并且有力推动新一代“量身裁定”吸附材料的发展。我们将开展混合气体分离实验以及变压/变温吸附过程实验来展示“主动筛分”技术在实际工业应用中的表现。此外，这些“主动筛分”材料还可以用于高选择性膜分离，传感器，和催化领域。

21301817.label: Realisation of objectives
21301817.value: Regarding the objective of developing an in-depth understanding of our recently discovered “molecular trapdoor” effect and establishing guidelines for designing and developing active adsorbents that allow for highly selective molecular separation, we have focused on regulating the operating temperature in the desired range by tuning the density of door-keeping agents and constructing a mathematic model for predicting the gas uptake due to successful admission. As the separation performance of our active adsorbents directly depends on their ability to admit/exclude guest molecules and the operating temperature would affect such ability and the energy cost of a separation process, we attempted to tune the operating temperature by adjusting the density of extraframework cations in active zeolite adsorbents. Our molecular simulation study established that in a potassium-form chabazite (an active-sieving zeolite adsorbent), an optimal density of door-keeping cation potassium corresponding Si/Al ratio of 1.5~2 would enable exclusive admission of CO2 (while still reject N2 and CH4) at room temperature, relevant to industrial post-combustion carbon capture and natural gas/biogas purification. Accordingly, we attempted to prepare potassium chabazite with Si/Al ratio of 1.5~2 and examined gas adsorption and turned out to achieve the best separation performance (the highest in the physisorption separation) at 303 K with Si/Al ratio of 1.9. The results were published in Chemical Communications (2018, 54, 3134−3137). This demonstrates the efficacy of establishing design guidelines in advancing the developing our highly selective active adsorbents. On the other hand, to accurately predict the gas uptake of our active adsorbents for separation process design and implementation, we built a new model by introducing one parameter (pore opening percentage factor) into the conventional dual-site Langmuir equation and successfully applied this model in designing natural gas separation process using a potassium chabazite with Si/Al ratio of 1, with the results published in Industrial & Engineering Chemistry Research (2020, 59, 7857−7865). Regarding the objective of establishing techniques to regulate the active sieving behaviour using external stimuli, we have been focused on using an external electric field to control the movement of door-keeping agent and thus the admission/rejection of guest molecules into the porous host. We have designed and fabricated an in situ sample cell for conducting gas adsorption measurement in an adjustable electric field. Using this unique facility, we have tested CO2 and N2 adsorption in our representative molecular trapdoor chabazites of potassium and cesium form with Si/Al ratio of 2 at room temperature up to 1 bar. Analysis of the measured single-component gas adsorption-desorption data in the presence of electric field at room temperature showed remarkable hysteresis loop, suggesting a potential influence of applied external stimuli on the gated adsorption. Apart from exploring the electric field as a stimulus, we further study the temperature as a stimulus in zeolite LTA – a potential active adsorbent system of different pore framework from our established study in CHA zeolite. We have prepared LTA adsorbents with different cation type and density for gas adsorption study with temperature as the stimulus to control the sieving behaviour and found that unparalleled high CO2-over-N2 selective adsorption can be achieved on a potassium form LTA with Si/Al ratio of 2 at a substantially higher temperature range (50 to 120 °C) which has been not possible in our previous active sieving adsorbents. Accordingly, we for the first time demonstrate that temperature-controlled active sieving behaviour governs the separation process in zeolite LTA which has long been deemed to be the model system of size-sieving. We have prepared a manuscript compiling these new findings and plan to submit soon. Regarding the objective of demonstrating the process of using such active adsorbents for key applications in energy and environment fields, we have prepared a representative molecular trapdoor zeolite adsorbent, i.e., a potassium chabazite with Si/Al ratio of 1, of around 70 gram and shaped the adsorbents into pellets. A simple two-bed pressure-vacuum swing adsorption (PVSA) cycle experiment was designed to understand and verify the adsorption characteristics and behavior of our highly selective trapdoor material in CO2/CH4 separation (15 vol % CO2 balanced with CH4). The performance of separating CO2 from synthesized natural gas with our designed PVSA cycle was investigated under different operating conditions. An optimized five-step PVSA cycle operated at 293 K led to a methane purity of nearly 100% along with more than 95% recovery, with the results published in Industrial & Engineering Chemistry Research (2020, 59, 7857−7865).

21301817.label: Major findings and research outcome
21301817.value: The first major finding is that the non-gate-keeping cations in the molecular trapdoor zeolite affect the behaviour of gate-keeping cations, allowing for regulating the gas admission temperature. This was experimentally demonstrated by comparing the threshold gas admission temperature on potassium chabazites with Si/Al ratio of 1, 1.5 to 2, and 2, which are corresponding to decreasing cation density and thus decreasing number of non-gate-keeping cations per unit cell. This finding affords a handle for fine-tuning threshold gas admission temperature of active sieving adsorbents. The results were published in Chemical Communications (2018, 54, 3134−3137). The 2nd major finding is a mathematical model for describing the temperature-dependent gas uptake in active sieving adsorbents. The model was successfully applied to describe CH4 adsorption uptake in a representative molecular trapdoor zeolite adsorbent at temperatures below and above the threshold gas admission temperature. The accurate description/modelling of gas uptake is essential for process design. In our case, it enabled us to design gas separation process (a pressure swing adsorption process) to successfully demonstrate CO2/CH4 separation. The results published in Industrial & Engineering Chemistry Research (2020, 59, 7857−7865). The 3rd major finding is that the well-acknowledged conventional size-sieving behaviour in zeolite 3A can actually be accounted for by the molecular trapdoor mechanism, thus opening the avenue for developing active sieving adsorbents. This new understanding allowed us for developing zeolite LTA with different type and density of extra-framework cations as active sieving adsorbents that realized unprecedently high CO2 selectivity over N2. The 4th major finding is the active sieving mechanism can enable to maintain highly selective gas adsorption in binary gas mixtures with acceptable adsorption kinetics, as demonstrated by a simple two-bed pressure-vacuum swing adsorption (PVSA) cycle experiment for CO2/CH4 separation (15 vol % CO2 balanced with CH4) using a potassium chabazite with Si/Al ratio of 1. This successful demonstration addressed the two concerns: the guest-induced gate-opening process may result in the slip-in of unwanted gases and thus resulting in compromised selectivity; the guest-induced gate-opening process could inevitably lead to a slow adsorption kinetics that prevent from practical process operation. The results published in Industrial & Engineering Chemistry Research (2020, 59, 7857−7865).

21301817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21301817.value: Following the demonstration of the molecular trapdoor mechanism in zeolite LTA, we expect to further develop active sieving adsorbents in zeolite with hetero atoms in the framework, e.g., SAPO, to fine-tune the degree of difficulty of relocating the gate-keeping cation and thus finely tuning the threshold gas admission temperature. We also expect to develop active sieving adsorbents based on metal-organic frameworks with gate-keeping cation or gate-keeping anions. The exceptionally rich tunability of metal-organic frameworks would allow for realizing wider range of threshold gas admission temperature for a wider range of gas molecules, which will substantially increase value of the active sieving adsorbents for gas separation applications. The successful design and fabrication of an in situ sample cell to fit our gas adsorption analyzer (Micromeritics 3Flex) for conducting gas adsorption measurement in an adjustable electric field took tremendous time and efforts. Till now, we have investigated the effect of electric field on the active sieving behavior on representative molecular trapdoor zeolites. We will continue to explore the “handle” of electric field by examining more “electric field sensitive” adsorbents as well as conducting advanced spectroscopy and computational study for establishing a suit of methods to explore this new research direction.

21301817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21301817.value: This project developed an in-depth understanding of our recently discovered “molecular trapdoor” effect, established guidelines for designing and developing active adsorbents that allow for highly selective molecular separation, attempted to regulate the active sieving behaviour by using electric field as an external stimulus, and demonstrated the process of using such active adsorbents for key gas separation applications in energy and environment fields. The findings of this project can potentially enable highly efficient and economical molecular separation. By offering tunable purpose-orientated high selectivity, the active sieving technology has the potential to significantly reduce the operation and capital costs in a wide range of gas separation processes, including natural gas purification and carbon dioxide capture, which would help achieve carbon neutrality through saving energy for key chemical separation processes and curbing the emission of major greenhouse gases.

21302317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21302317.value: The structure of nucleic acids often governs the biological function of many cellular processes. Guanine-rich sequences in nucleic acids can fold into intricate structural motifs known as G-quadruplexes, and they are of special interest due to their peculiar structural scaffolds and potential associations with gene regulatory features and human diseases. A number of reports have suggested that G-quadruplexes can regulate gene expression and cellular processes, ranged from replication, transcription, RNA processing to translation. Recently, DNA and RNA G-quadruplexes have been detected in human cells and tissues using G-quadruplex-specific antibody, providing substantial evidence for the existence of G-quadruplexes in humans. Bioinformatics-based searching and experimental-based sequencing profiling in human genome and transcriptome reported more than thousands of G-quadruplexes, in which a few of the specific examples have been verified to possess gene regulatory roles, offering a glimpse of the overall potential of G-quadruplexes functions in living cells. Compared with its DNA counterparts, current understanding of RNA G-quadruplexes is still rudimentary and the biological consequences of myriad RNA G-quadruplexes formation remain elusive, making establishment of G-quadruplex structure-function relationship particularly challenging. Our recent computational search among the human precursor microRNAs has predicted almost a hundred of putative RNA G-quadruplexes, and we have demonstrated in selected example that the formation of RNA G-quadruplex in precursor microRNA affect the Dicer processing and mature microRNA maturation. Driven by these initial findings, Our central hypothesis of this proposal is that RNA G-quadruplex structures are stable in the human precursor microRNAs, generally affects Dicer processing, and can function as a regulatory element to affect gene expression in living cells. To directly test this hypothesis, we propose to employ chemical and biochemical experimental approaches to address three central questions: A) Are RNA G-quadruplexes forming in precursor microRNA hairpin? B) Does the formation of RNA G-quadruplex in precursor microRNA affect Dicer processing and reporter gene expression? C) Does the formation of G-quadruplex in precursor microRNA control the native protein expression of targeted mRNAs? The proposal presented here is timely, original, and inter-disciplinary that integrates chemical biology, structural biology, and molecular biology. Successful execution of this proposal will provide us profound insights into the role of RNA G-quadruplex structures in non-coding RNAs on post-transcriptional regulation. Our group is one of few labs that have the necessary expertise and facilities to carry out this proposal, thus we are confident that the proposed research project will be accomplished in time if funded.

21302317.label: Realisation of objectives
21302317.value: We have successfully achieved the project objectives and reported novel research findings, and in addition to that, during the course of project execution, we have gained new research insights that led us to explore on a few related ideas on RNA G-quadruplexes (rG4s) (see section 6.1), which altogether yielded a number of high-quality research outputs, and these results are useful for further development of the research (See section 6.2). In summary, we have published 21 publications, including papers in prestigious journals including Nature Methods (IF 28.547), Nature Communications (IF 14.919), Nucleic Acids Research (IF 16.971), Angewandte Chemie International Edition (IF 15.336), Briefings in Bioinformatics (IF 11.622), Genome Biology (IF 13.583), Chemical Science (IF 9.825), Chemical Communications (IF 6.222) and etc. Moreover, several awards/patents were received, a number of invited talks were given, a few PhDs were being mentored, several undergraduates have been trained, and strong collaboration networks have been established with top institutions in Hong Kong and around the globe (see part C). With regards to research findings and realization of objectives, we have performed bioinformatics analysis on potential rG4 formation on precursor microRNAs (pre-miRNAs) and microRNAs (miRNAs) obtained from microRNA database, and found that there are about 100 of them in human. We showed that many of these rG4s are conserved, suggested that they may be evolutionarily selected to form rG4 structure to carry out specific functions in miRNAs. Based on the rG4 prediction score and conservation, as well as the miRNAs’ association with cancers, we have highlighted several cases for pre-miRNAs and miRNAs for structural and functional investigation. We performed multiple spectroscopic and structure probing to verify the formation and structural features of these rG4s. For pre-miRNAs, we have focused on pre-miR149 and investigated the effect of rG4 on mature miR149 level and gene expression of its downstream mRNA target. We have detected through quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) that there was more pre-miR149 and less mature miR149 expressed after pre-miR149 wild-type construct transfection in cell, when compared with the pre-miR149 mut construct. We also studied the effect of rG4 on interaction between miR149 targeting genes, FOX1 and ZBTB2 by comparing the reporter gene level after the transfection of pre-miR149 wt and mut constructs. Overall, we have observed rG4 inhibition effect on miRNA-mRNA interaction. For miRNAs, we have studied 4 mature miRNAs, and showed that the formation of rG4 in miRNAs can be suppressed by the presence of mRNA targets, which allow rG4 conformation to be in equilibrium with RNA duplex, suggesting that miRNA-mRNA complex formation can be mediated by the rG4 folding in miRNA. To verify the findings in cells, we have designed reporter gene plasmid and transfected selected rG4-containing miRNA wildtype and mutant (i.e. miR765 and miR765 mutant in this case) and observed rG4’s impact on reporter gene activity in the presence or absence of G4 stabilizing ligand N-methyl mesoporphyrin IX (NMM). The result showed that with the addition of NMM, rG4 conformation was favoured in miR765, and thus it could not target the mRNA region and the reporter gene was not suppressed. No effect was observed for the miR765 mutant version with or without NMM treatment, supporting that the effect observed was rG4-specific. Overall, these works reported rG4’s new and important roles in controlling post-transcriptional gene regulation in cell for the first time. By performing rG4 prediction and analysing transcriptome-wide rG4-seq data, we also examined the formation and roles rG4 on messenger RNAs (mRNAs). In particular, we studied the formation of an rG4 within the 3’untranslated regions (3’UTR) of amyloid precursor protein (APP) transcript, that is linked to Alzheimer’s disease. We performed biophysical assays to understand the rG4’s topology and thermostability, structure probing assays to report the structure feature of rG4 at single nucleotide resolution, and cell imaging assays to demonstrate rG4 formation in human cells. Importantly, we have also designed different rG4 wildtype and mutant constructs in reporter gene system to study the functional role of this APP 3’UTR rG4, and illustrated that it acts as a translation repressor in cells. We also assessed the formation of an rG4 within the 5’untranslation regions (5’UTR) of Adenosine deaminase acting on RNAs (ADAR) transcript, that is responsible for the editing of RNA and its dysregulation has been associated with cancers. Similarly, we first performed biophysical assays, structure probing and cell imaging to report the structure feature of this 5’UTR rG4. We then designed rG4 wildtype and mutant constructs in reporter gene, as well as native transcript to assess the function of rG4, and discovered the down-regulatory role of this rG4 in cells. To investigate the potential binding partners of this rG4, we tested on one of the well-studied rG4 protein DHX36, and found that it can bind and unwind ADAR 5’UTR. We next constructed DHX36 knockout cell line and compare the native protein level expressed to study the role of DHX36 on ADAR 5’UTR rG4 folding status and its impact on gene expression. Collectively, as these UTR rG4s are important for gene regulation, they are promising structural targets for controlling APP and ADAR protein production and may be targeted in the future for therapeutical applications. Besides human, we have also conducted studies to map and characterize rG4s in other biological systems. For bacteria, we have characterized 2 rG4 candidates, bswR and hemL at the CDS region, and found that rG4 play key regulatory roles in bacterial pathogenicity and metabolic pathways. We also reported that rG4s can be detected in a wide range of bacterial species. For mouse, we have characterized the 5’UTR rG4 in the Gnai2 mRNA, and showed that DHX36 regulates the translation of Gnai2 mRNA by unwinding its 5’UTR rG4 structures and identify GNAI2 as a downstream effector of DHX36 for skeletal stem cell function. For plasmodium, we have characterized the rG4 formation in Rad54 and Ap2 genes, and found that the detected rG4s were mostly located in the CDS region in P. falciparum transcriptome of protein coding genes. We also reported that rG4s control the translation of P. falciparum genes, demonstrated that rG4 can have functional role in species with highly AT-rich genome/transcriptome (~80% for P. falciparum). For plant, we have characterized the rG4 region on 3’UTR of HIRD11 and showed that it serves as an important regulators of plant development and growth. We also reported that hundreds of rG4 structures are strongly folded in Arabidopsis and rice, providing substantial evidence of rG4 formation in living eukaryotic cells. These examples clearly indicated the formation and roles of rG4 in different biological systems, underscoring that rG4 have evolutionary and functional role in gene regulation. These findings also provide a repertoire of rG4s for further structural and functional characterization. Last but not least, as the SAR-CoV2 occurred in late 2019, we predicted rG4 formation in this RNA virus, found about 20 putative rG4, and performed biophysical assays to verify a few cases. In particular, we focused on the top-ranked putative rG4-forming sequences at positions 13385 and 24268 which were shown to form rG4 in vitro, and we reported that they interacted with the nsp13 viral helicase. This finding should provide attractive approaches for inhibiting the pandemic-causing virus via targeting viral rG4s or helicases.

21302317.label: Major findings and research outcome
21302317.value: The major findings and research outcome are as follows: First, we successfully demonstrated RNA G-quadruplex (rG4) formation in microRNAs (miRNAs) and reported their significant roles in mediating post-transcriptional gene regulation in cells for the first time. This work was published in Chemical Communications (IF 6.222). Second, we have used spectroscopic, structural, imaging techniques to determine the formation of rG4 within the 3’untranslated regions (3’UTR) of amyloid precursor protein (APP) transcript and illustrated that this 3’UTR rG4 have important function in suppressing APP translation process in human cells, providing a target for controlling APP production in the near future. This work was published in Chemical Science (IF 9.825). Third, we have carried our transcriptome-wide studies to profile rG4 formation in different biological systems, such as human, bacteria, plant, plasmodium, and mouse, and detected hundreds to thousands of rG4s in each system. We later also showcased the post-trancriptional and/or translation role of some of the nominated rG4 examples located in the coding regions (CDS) or UTRs. These works were published in Mbio (IF 7.867), Genome Biology (IF 13.583), Nucleic Acids Research (IF 16.971), Nature Communications (IF 14.919), RNA Biology (IF 4.652), and Scientific Reports (IF 4.379), respectively. Last, due to the emergence of SARS-CoV2 RNA virus in late 2019, we have predicted the rG4 in the viral genome, validated a few rG4 examples, and showed that they interacted with viral helicase, which provide attractive approaches for potentially inhibiting the pandemic-causing virus. This work was published in Briefings in Bioinformatics (IF 11.622). In addition, our findings and reputations in the associated fields have attracted top tiers journals to invite us to write reviews, and we have highlighted the above-mentioned major findings and acknowledge the RGC funding in these publications as well, including Trends in Biochemical Sciences (IF 13.807), Cold Spring Harbour Perspectives in Biology (IF 10.005), Nucleic Acid Research (IF 16.971), Molecules (IF 4.148). All info can be found in part C. Other relevant research activities: Besides the main research activities described above (a total of 14 publications), we have also published 7 other research articles, including Nature Methods (IF 28.547), Angewandte Chemie International Edition (IF 15.336), 2 Nucleic Acid Research (IF 16.971), Analytical Chemistry (IF 6.986), Chemical Communications (IF 6.222), and Biochemical Biophysical Research Communication (IF 3.575), on research topics that are relevant to this project, and we have acknowledged the RGC funding. All info can be found in part C.

21302317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21302317.value: There are at least 3 potentials for further development of the research. First, from earlier study we have identified more than hundreds of rG4-containing human microRNAs, however, only handful of cases were studied so far. In the near future, we will be investigating other rG4-containing human microRNAs on our list and to explore their formation and role in cells. Also, we plan to examine the effect of rG4 helicases such as DHX36 on these miRNA rG4s and decipher the molecular basis of this rG4-mediated regulatory mechanism. Second, we have showcased a few coding region (CDS) and untranslated region (UTR) rG4 examples from this project, and next we plan to investigate more rG4 candidates in mRNA, and examine its effect on its translation or RNA metabolism, its potential partners and the biochemical mechanism. Last, with these rG4 being identified and demonstrated to have crucial role in cells, we plan to develop a novel suite of rG4 targeting tools to achieve gene control via selective recognition of rG4 of interest. These are ongoing research in my laboratory, and once promising and sufficient preliminary data are generated, we will apply for funding support in RGC and other agencies.

21302317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21302317.value: G-rich sequences in RNA can form special structure motifs referred as RNA G-quadruplexes (rG4s), and in this research project, we have investigated rG4s in non-coding RNAs such as microRNAs (miRNAs), and through the experiments conducted, we demonstrated their formation and roles of rG4s in human miRNAs in cells for the first time. As some of these microRNAs, such as miR432 and miR765, are associated with cancers, these findings suggested that rG4 can be an important structure element to regulate post-transcriptional gene expression, and rG4 in miRNAs can be a potential drug target for controlling cancer development. Besides miRNAs, we also reported rG4s in different regions of messenger RNAs (mRNAs) in human, mouse, plant, plasmodium, bacteria and virus, illustrating that rG4s are prevalent in different classes of RNA across the tree of life. As current research on rG4 is underexplored, our research project’s findings shed new lights and provide novel research directions for future investigation and understanding of rG4s for both functional and mechanistic studies in biology, as well as further applications in biomedical and biotechnological purposes.

21500517.label: Realisation of objectives
21500517.value: We believe that we are able to achieve the major objectives of the proposed study. We elaborate the details as follows. We are able to achieve the first and second project objectives 100%. We proposed to extract useful information from the free-text triage notes so that we can predict the admission decision of a patient from the emergency department to the hospital inpatient units. We obtained comprehensive patient-level data from a Canadian hospital. However, these triage notes involve high dimensional, noisy, and sparse text data, which make model fitting and interpretation difficult. To address this issue, we propose a novel semiorthogonal nonnegative matrix factorization for both continuous and binary predictors to reduce the dimensionality and derive word topics. The triage notes can then be interpreted as a non-subtractive linear combination of orthogonal basis topic vectors. Our real data analysis shows that the triage notes contain strong predictive information toward classifying the disposition of patients for certain medical complaints, such as altered consciousness or stroke. We show that the document-topic vectors generated by our method can be used as features to further improve classification accuracy by up to 1% across different medical complaints, for example, 74.3%–75.3% accuracy for patients with stroke symptoms. We are able to address the third project objective to a large extent. Specifically, we build a novel queueing model and use a Markov decision process formulation to study the optimal policy on TNO (triage nurse ordering). However, it turns out that the model dimension is high and we are unable to characterize the optimal TNO policy. Instead, we build simulation models and try to apply simulation optimization methods to tackle this difficulty. We are able to obtain policies that significantly improve over some naive policies. Hence, we believe that we have addressed about 90% of our proposed objective. Our simulation model is also useful to answer the last project objective. That is, to evaluate the impact of TNO decisions on emergency department performance metrics. Hence, we are able to address the fourth objective 100%. In addition to the proposed study objectives, our investigation identifies other important operational issues and we performed in-depth studies which include an investigation on the triage decision in hospital emergency departments and how to improve emergency department physician staffing by incorporating the shift-hour-dependent service rates among heterogeneous physicians. We provide useful insights to the management of emergency departments and help hospitals make better staffing planning.
