21500517.label: Major findings and research outcome
21500517.value: The major finding of this completed project is that we are able to provide an answer to the question: can the free-text triage notes provide useful information for the prediction of patient admission decisions from the emergency department to hospital inpatient units? The answer is yes, but the implementation is not trivial. We elaborate below. The triage notes involve high dimensional, noisy, and sparse text data, which make model fitting and interpretation difficult. To address this issue, we propose a novel semiorthogonal nonnegative matrix factorization for both continuous and binary predictors to reduce the dimensionality and derive word topics. The triage notes can then be interpreted as a non-subtractive linear combination of orthogonal basis topic vectors. Our real data analysis shows that the triage notes contain strong predictive information toward classifying the disposition of patients for certain medical complaints, such as altered consciousness or stroke. We show that the document-topic vectors generated by our method can be used as features to further improve classification accuracy by up to 1% across different medical complaints, for example, 74.3%–75.3% accuracy for patients with stroke symptoms. To summarize, with the help of sophisticated statistical tools, we can extract useful information from triage notes, which has a significant impact on admission predictions. We propose a novel method and use a case study based on real data to evaluate its effectiveness.

21500517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21500517.value: We have been successful in answering the statistical question on extracting useful information from free-text triage notes to predict patient admission decisions from emergency departments to hospital inpatient units. However, the operational question, i.e., the optimal decision on applying triage nurse ordering, is not fully answered. Specifically, it remains unclear what is the structure of the optimal policy. Hence, we believe it is worth to further develop theoretical results on the optimal decisions on triage nurse ordering, especially when the system congestion information is explicitly considered.

21500517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21500517.value: Emergency department overcrowding is a worldwide problem impairing the ability of hospitals to provide emergency care within a reasonable time frame. One initiative to improve patient flow and reduce waiting time is to triage nurser ordering, i.e., triage nurses initiate some tests at triage so that patients can go through the testing procedure while waiting to be seen by a physician. A key to implementing such an initiative is the ability to accurately predict what tests a patient may need. Motivated by this problem, we aim to develop statistical techniques to extract useful information from the free-text triage notes, in addition to other information from triage. We propose a novel method called semiorthogonal nonnegative matrix factorization. Our case study using a big dataset from a Canadian hospital finds that the triage notes contain strong predictive information toward classifying the disposition of patients for certain medical complaints, such as altered consciousness or stroke.

21503517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21503517.value: 发生在21世纪初的诸多企业丑闻揭露了公司管理团队是如何一起操纵收益的事实(e.g., WorldCom, Enron)。正如这些丑闻所揭示的，不仅仅是CEO或CFO，而是整个管理团队为这种欺骗行为创造了条件。尽管监管者知道监管二线管理部门的重要性，但现有的大部分研究仍集中于研究CEO和CFO。然而，在最近的一篇论文中，Khanna et al. (2015) 研究了CEO和其它领导者之间的联系在公司内部所起的作用，发现这些联系增加了公司欺诈行为的可能性，并降低了被监测的可能性从而导致公司固有风险和控制风险的增加。然而，市场参与者是否感知到了CEO和其它管理团队间联系的风险性还鲜为人知。 在本研究中，作者将通过检测审计师是否感知到了CEO和管理团队间联系的风险来填补现有研究的这一空缺。作者认为CEO与高层管理人员之间有着密切联系的公司拥有高质量审计师的可能性相比其它公司更小。此外，作者预期来自这些联系的风险性将提高审计师索要的审计费用。作者还研究了信息不对称是否对以上两者产生影响。本研究主要有以下四大贡献：首先，本研究通过探究审计师在审计过程中是否评估高层管理团队延伸了现有的审计文献。尽管美国公众公司会计监督委员会(PCAOB)已经观察到高层管理团队与审计风险间的联系，但是这个领域仍然有待研究。其次，本研究将补充对公司内部联系的文献研究。现有研究大部分探究了这些联系对公司管理的消极影响，但是市场参与者是否感知到了这些联系的风险仍然不为人知。因此本文将通过研究这些联系如何影响审计师的选择决策和审计费用来解决这一问题。第三，本文的研究结果将为监管部门，特别是PCAOB，提供一些见解。PCAOB已经知道一些与管理问题相关，不易被观察但应当在审计中纳入考虑的因素的存在。但是这些因素是否为审计师所了解，多大程度上在审计过程中被考虑为风险仍然未知。作者将尝试在本文中为这些问题的解释提供初步依据。最后，作者希望本文能够为研究定性数据和软数据如何帮助市场其它监管者评价高层管理人员及其所属公司的固有风险的论文提供一定的指导。

21504617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21504617.value: Attention is a scarce resource and it matters for individual and corporate actions. A growing literature in finance and economics studies the consequences of limited attention for corporate actions and financial markets. Limited attention causes investors’ under-reaction to information (e.g., Hirshleifer, Lim, and Teoh, 2009) and fixation on high volume and high return stocks (Barber and Odean, 2008). This raises the question of whether managers strategically time bad news recognition when large shareholders are distracted. In this paper, we explore whether institutional shareholder inattention affects the likelihood of bad news recognition using a novel dataset to capture an exogenous shock to shareholder attention. Specifically, our shareholder distraction sample is defined as the firms held by institutional investors that engage in corporate activism targeting other firms. As the institutional investors allocate more time and efforts to the targeted firms, the attention paid to other firms in their holdings will be negatively affected. We predict that firms with distracted shareholders will take advantage of this opportunity to clean up the ‘bloat’ in their balance sheet and time their personal insider sales. Specifically, we predict a decrease in abnormal accruals, and an increase in recognition of special items and write-downs. To directly capture the distraction effect, we test shareholders’ response to the bad news recognition during the distraction period and expect a lower ERC. In addition, we examine whether managers seek private benefits when the monitoring intensity decreases by examining the likelihood of insider sales before the bad news release and whether such insider sales earn an abnormal profit. We further explore cross-sectional variation. The lack of shareholder monitoring could be mitigated by other monitoring mechanisms. We expect to see a stronger effect of shareholder distraction in firms that have weaker corporate governance, lower trading volume, and lower analyst following. The main contribution of this research is summarized as follows. First, we develop a measure of shareholder distraction that is more transparent and is plausibly exogenous to the firm. Second, we provide new evidence about the effect of shareholder inattention on firms’ financial reporting and managers’ opportunistic behavior. Third, we provide evidence on determinants of cross-sectional variation in this effect. Fourth, we show that monitoring intensity of institutional investors for a given portfolio holding varies systematically with such investors’ attention which is diverted by activist campaigns. The prior literature has generally assumed that institutional investor attention is homogenous across all firms in their portfolio. 个体注意力作为稀缺资源，会对公司决策造成影响。金融和经济学领域越来越多的研究表明个体注意力的有限性会对公司决策和金融市场造成影响。文献表明，投资者同样受有限注意力的影响。本文建立在投资者注意力有限的假设上，来研究公司经理层会否策略性进行公司信息披露。具体来讲，我们研究机构投资者的注意力缺位会否导致更多公司负面信息披露。 机构投资者对于公司的治理结构和公司决策有着重大影响。因此他们的关注与否会对公司经理产生重大的影响，进而影响公司的信息披露。我们会专注于公司财务应计数变化，损失计提变化，和特别项目变化。更进一步，考虑到金融市场对于公司财务信息的反馈机制，我们会市场如何对信息披露做出反应以及内部人员交易会否在机构投资者注意力缺位阶段发生系统性变化。最后，我们会基于公司治理水平、交易量水平和研究员跟踪水平进行截面差异研究。 本文会提供关于投资者注意力对于公司财务披露的影响的实证支持以及截面性差异。同时，我们也提供了如何在实务上测量投资者注意力。最后，我们验证了机构投资者的注意力分配有系统性变化，而非对于所有被投资公司具有同质性。

21505117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21505117.value: Information asymmetry between corporate managers and external shareholders prevents the capital market from functioning well. Various external institutions, such as financial regulators, financial analysts, and bond rating agencies, exist in the capital market to mitigate such information asymmetry and reduce the market friction. On the other hand, managers themselves have incentives to voluntarily disclose proprietary information to seek strategic interests, such as a lower cost of capital. Thus, the observed level of voluntary disclosures should reflect the interactions between the external information production and insiders’ disclosure incentives. This proposed study seeks to examine the role played by rating agencies in producing external information and its causal effect on firms’ disclosure decisions. In 1982, Moody’s refined its previous nine credit rating categories, creating nineteen categories. This refinement provided more precise information about firms’ relative competitiveness. But, as claimed by Moody’s, the refinements were not driven by any new information about firms’ fundamental changes. Therefore, the refinements imposed an exogenous shock on firms’ credit rating and provide an ideal setting to identify the causal effect of credit rating changes on firms’ voluntary disclosures. A finer credit rating, releasing more information about a firm’s relative competitiveness, would reduce the firm’s benefits from disclosing proprietary information. But the rating refinement does not change the proprietary cost of voluntary disclosures. Therefore, I predict that firms will reduce the level of voluntary disclosures after the rating refinement. In addition, I expect that the main result is stronger for firms facing higher proprietary costs, as proxied for by the ex ante product market competition. This project can contribute to the literature concerning the role played by bond rating agencies. As an important information provider, bond rating agencies’ role in shaping firms’ voluntary disclosure decisions is largely overlooked in empirical studies. The lack of evidence on the causal effect of credit rating changes is primarily due to the endogenous nature of the information disclosed by bond rating agencies. The proposed study would employ a natural experiment (Moody’s rating refinements) to get around the endogeneity issue and, thus, has the potential to generate the first evidence of the causal effect of credit ratings on corporate disclosures. Second, it will advance our understanding of how firms’ optimal disclosure decisions respond to changes in external sources of information. The proposed project has the potential of documenting a crowd-out effect associated with the finer information provided by rating agencies. 企業內部管理者和外部投資者之間的信息不對稱是資本市場順利運行的障礙。資本市場中存在著各種各樣的外部機構來提供信息，從而降低信息不對稱和市場摩擦。這些機構包括金融監管者、金融分析師、以及債券評級機構。另一方面，基於現有信息，企業管理者本身也會自願披露一部分專有信息來達到一些戰略目的，比如降低資本成本。所以，我們觀察到的企業自願披露水平是內部管理者的動機和外部信息生產量共同決定的。這篇研究計劃的目的就是研究債券評級機構提供的信息是怎樣影響企業的信息披露水平的。 1982年，穆迪評級公司（Moody’s）改善了評級分類，把之前的9個分類細化成為19個。這次細化使得企業之間相對競爭力的排名更加精確了。同時，根據穆迪的宣稱，這次細化是根據此前穆迪業已掌握的企業信息做出的，而不是由於企業基本面的新變化導致的。從這個意義上來說，穆迪的評級細化導致了企業信用評級的外生變化，從而提供了一個用以檢驗信用評級對企業信息披露的因果效應的理想實驗。 更精確的信用評級提供了更多關於企業相對競爭力的信息，從而降低了受影響的企業披露專有信息的好處。然而評級細化卻並沒有改變披露專有信息的成本。因此，本研究預測，受影響的企業將會在評級細化之後降低信息披露水平。並且，當企業事前所面臨的專有信息披露成本較大時（所處行業市場競爭更激烈），這一結果應當更明顯。 本研究項目的貢獻如下。首先，它將對研究債券評級機構的文獻做出貢獻。作為一個重要的市場信息提供者，債券評級機構在影響企業信息披露方面的作用在文獻中鮮有證據。造成這方面證據不足的最主要原因是，評級信息都是內生於企業的經營狀況的，這使得我們很難說明信用評級和企業信息披露之間的關係是否是因果關係。本研究計劃利用穆迪的評級細化這一外生事件，可以有效地解決內生性問題，有望成為提供關於信用評級和信息披露之間因果關係的第一批研究。其次，本研究項目可以增進我們對外部信息生產如何影響企業的最優決策這一課題的理解。我們有望發現債券評級機構提供的公共信息對其他信息的擠出效應。

21505117.label: Realisation of objectives
21505117.value: As stated in the mid-term report, there was a small change in project objectives. I originally planned to examine the effect of credit rating changes caused by Moody’s rating refinement. To this end, I collected the rating refinement data, merged it with Compustat, and conducted some preliminary tests. However, the regression results are not significant. One probable reason is the small sample size: back in the 1980s, the available information about corporate disclosure is limited (we have tried our best to collect the data from various sources). However, the insignificant results do not necessarily mean that credit ratings have zero effect on corporate disclosure. I thus moved on to my backup plan: using a related setting to examine the same topic: in the current version, we look at the effect of credit rating downgrade due to sovereign ceiling rule on mandatory corporate disclosure. Therefore, the main objective of the project remains the same, but some sub-objectives do change according to the specific setting of sovereign rating downgrade. In the completed version of the study, we take advantage of sovereign credit rating downgrades that exogenously changed firms’ credit ratings due to the ceiling rule (firms rated above the sovereign rating are likely to be mechanically downgraded), and examine the effect of credit rating changes on these bound firms’ discretionary accruals. We show that bound firms report lower discretionary accruals following sovereign downgrades. This finding survives various robustness tests, including instrumental variable approach, regression discontinuity design, propensity score matching, stacked regression approach, placebo test, and alternative measures of downward earnings management. Further findings reveal a reversal of earnings subsequent to the reduction of discretionary accruals. Our evidence is consistent with the notion that managers strategically employ a big bath accounting and attribute poor performance to a mechanical credit rating downgrade and associated economic downturns. We also conduct various additional tests to substantiate the main finding. We show that bound firms’ earnings response coefficients are similar to those of unbound firms following the sovereign downgrade, suggesting that investors do not fully see through the degree of earnings management around sovereign downgrade events. In addition, we find significant increases in the impairments of goodwill and other intangibles following sovereign downgrade events. These tests provide evidence on the incentives and tools, respectively, for bound firm managers to employ big-bath accounting following a sovereign downgrade. In cross-sectional tests, we find that the accrual-reducing effect of sovereign ceiling rule is more pronounced when bound firms are located in countries with a more stringent institutional environment, when the sovereign rating falls into a lower rating bin, and when bound firms are less geographically diversified. We also write a toy model to generate predictions consistent with the above cross-sectional results. We presented the paper at the ABFER conference, Asian Finance Association annual meeting, Shanghai Fudan University, Korean University, and Seoul National University. After each presentation, we revised it according to the gathered feedback. The paper is currently under review at the Review of Accounting Studies for four months. We hope to publish it in the top-tier journal soon. In this sense, despite necessary deviations (as stated above), the original objectives of the project are 100% complete.

21505117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21505117.value: We examine the effect of sovereign credit rating downgrades on firms’ earnings management. Using the exogenous variation in credit ratings caused by sovereign rating downgrades from 61 countries, we show that firms reduce discretionary accruals after sovereign downgrades and are likely to experience a reversal of earnings subsequent to the accrual reduction. The reduction in discretionary accruals is more significant in countries with a better institutional environment and when the sovereign rating falls into a lower bin. Our study provides new evidence that managers strategically employ downward earnings management in response to the negative shock on sovereign credit ratings.

21601417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21601417.value: The early twentieth century witnessed the boom of Chinese newspapers in colonial Hong Kong, and their contributions to the development of printing media in China has been acknowledged. Meanwhile, China experienced one of the great ‘waves of translation’ in the late Qing period: Pollard observes that ‘in the first decade of the twentieth century there occurred in Chinese language publications the rare phenomenon of translated works of fiction exceeding in number original works of fiction’ (1998:5). It is not sheer coincidence that many of the translated works were initially serialized in the Chinese newspapers. While the translations in these newspapers on the Chinese mainland, Shanghai in particular, have gained increasing attention, the translations in Hong Kong Chinese newspapers around the turn of the twentieth century have remained largely unexplored. According to Chen, there are more than 25 Chinese newspapers in circulation in Hong Kong between 1853 and 1911, and there are many Chinese translations of foreign literary works, detective stories in particular, in these newspapers. Some tentative studies have been conducted on how the foreign detective stories are adapted to meet the expectations of local readership. However, the state of affairs leaves much to be desired. This project will start with translation archaeology, which, in Pym’s terms, are “a set of discourse concerned with answering all or part of the complex questions ‘who translated what, how, where, when, for whom and with what effect?’” (Pym, 1998:5). With the archaeology at hand, the research will move onto historical criticism and explain translation issues. Firstly, the study will compare the similarities and differences between Hong Kong and Shanghai in terms of literary translation, especially those serialized translations in Chinese newspapers. Secondly, sociological approach will be applied to study specific cases of translations with the focus on gender issues in translation, the contrastive and conflicting legal systems in detective fictions, the translation of forensic sciences, medicine and photography in particular, etc. Thirdly, the project will dwell upon those relay translations into Chinese via the pivot language of Japanese and delineate the trajectories of text moving among East Asian communities. It is expected to generalize some patterns of translation practice in Hong Kong and elaborate on knowledge transfer through translation in East Asia.

21601817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21601817.value: 創新作為企業和區域競爭力的核心，是當前政策設計和學術討論的熱點。然而，研究顯示，發展中國家在推進創新上的成功案例很有限，尤其是在全球生產網絡框架下以技術轉移為核心的策略中。這項研究以中國汽車產業為例，從經濟地理、政治經濟學角度解釋這一困難的原因所在。中國從二十世紀八十年代起，以“市場換技術”的戰略在其汽車產業中尋求技術轉移和產業發展，在近二十年的發展中取得了顯著的成果。而在2001年以後的 “後WTO” 時期，這一政策的有效性變得值得重新商榷。這項研究同三個相互關聯的理論對話：1）探討技術的特性，質疑技術中性論和技術中心論；2）合資過程中制度改革的區域間差異；3）中國汽車產業在全球生產網絡中角色的變化。本文用定性的研究方式，審視中國這個發展中國家尋求和支持創新很積極的一個，分析的不僅是其成功特點，更著重於從理論和系統上分析其過程中的困難和阻礙，同時認為在引進學術和政策概念（如：技術轉移）時，要嚴格審視其政治經濟學內涵。

21603817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21603817.value: In 1977, Israeli academic Leslie Sebba published two articles comparing constitutional arrangements for executive clemency the world over (Sebba 1977a & 1977b). Despite some thematic coverage in comparative constitutional law or death penalty textbooks, and several smaller-scale comparative studies, Sebba’s work remained the leading scholarship on executive clemency across national borders for almost 40 years, until Professor Andrew Novak (the Principal Investigator’s proposed Collaborator) published his ambitious new monograph ‘Comparative Executive Clemency: The Constitutional Pardon Power and the Prerogative of Mercy in Global Perspective’ in 2016. There are good reasons for the historical scarcity of empirical literature on executive clemency across national borders, clemency being broadly defined as the executive branch reducing or abrogating lawfully-imposed punishment. Unlike judicial decisions, clemency deliberations by executive decision-makers are usually performed in secret, with public justification for clemency grants rarely given. Aggregate clemency statistics, while more widespread than any official reasoning, tend only to be released to researchers and the public in democracies. Moreover, interviews with the final decision-makers on clemency petitions are exceedingly difficult to arrange, given their usual exalted status in the political hierarchy. Accordingly, pardons and commutations are rarely analysed in any systematic way within a single jurisdiction, let alone comparatively. However, despite the lack of information about how clemency decisions are made, how many are made, and the factors that contribute to their frequency or scarcity, they usually determine whether or not a prisoner sentenced to death ultimately lives or dies, and hence are vitally important in criminal justice systems that retain capital punishment. Moreover, even for abolitionist jurisdictions, clemency may operate as a final level of ‘appeal’ in cases of innocence or excessive punishment, or as a means to show leniency for reasons outside of those permissible by parole. In this context, the Principal Investigator’s plan for a three-year Early Career Scheme project involves composing several research pieces that will expand on the scarce global comparative and empirical literature on executive clemency. The project’s central research question is: “what accounts for similarity and difference in clemency laws and practice across different jurisdictions?”. In greater detail, the project’s three main research objectives are as follows: 1.To compare constitutional provisions on clemency on a global scale; 2.To juxtapose jurisdictions where clemency is very often granted with those where it is not; and 3.To account for variation and similarity in clemency laws and practice across the globe, employing empirical research methods. 項目名稱：以新的比較及實證方式研究赦免權 項目負責人：Daniel Pascoe博士 1977年，以色列學者Leslie Sebba發表了兩篇論文，比較世界各國對憲法之下的行政寬赦(executive clemency)的安排。雖然現時一些關於比較憲法或死刑的書籍都有涵蓋行政寬赦這一主題，而另外亦有一些關於行政寬赦的小規模比較研究，但是在2016年之前的過去接近40年間，Sebba的著作仍然是世界各國有關行政寬赦的權威學說。2016年，Andrew Novak教授(即本研究項目的負責人建議的合作研究員)發表了他那非常成功，名為 《比較行政寬赦：從全球角度研究憲法之下的赦免權與行政特赦權》(Comparative Executive Clemency: The Constitutional Pardon Power and the Prerogative of Mercy in Global Perspective)的新專著。 有史以來，世界各國都少有關於行政寬赦的實證研究文獻，原因是寬赦被廣泛定義為行政機關對罪犯被合法施加的刑罰作出減刑或取消。與司法判決不同，行政寬赦的決定是由行政機關決策者一般在秘密的情況下作出的，而作出有關行政寬赦決定的公眾理由亦鮮有公開。雖然我們可以見到關於行政寬赦決定的整體統計數據比官方公開其對作出行政寬赦決定的理由為多，但事實上，有關統計數據一般只有民主國家才會對研究人員和公眾公開。再者，由於最終批准行政寬赦申請的人士一般都具有很高的政治地位，因此安排採訪他們相當困難。基於以上原因，即使在一個國家之內，都很少有關於赦免和減刑的有系統性分析，所以更不用說相關的比較研究。 不過，雖然我們缺乏關於行政寬赦決定如何作出、行政寬赦決定的數目，以及導致行政寬赦決定頻繁或罕有作出的原因的資料，但這些卻通常是決定一個死刑犯最終生死的考慮因素，同時亦是對仍保留死刑的刑事司法制度非常重要的資料。再者，即使在主張廢除死刑的國家，行政寬赦亦可在犯人自稱無罪或認為判刑過重的情況下作為最後「上訴」，又或是作為在准許假釋的原因之外顯示寬大的手段。有鑑於此，本研究項目的負責人計劃進行一個為期三年的「傑出青年學者計劃」(Early Career Scheme)研究項目，當中包括撰寫數篇研究論文，藉以增加目前為數稀少，以全球比較角度和實證角度研究行政寬赦的文獻的數目。本項目要研究的核心問題是：“哪些因素導致不同國家和地區在行政寬赦的法律和實踐上出現異同？”本項目的三個主要研究目標如下： 1) 比較世界各國關於行政寬赦的憲法條文； 2) 列出哪些國家經常頒布行政寬赦、哪些國家不經常頒布行政寬赦；及 3) 以實證研究方式，找出世界各國在行政寬赦的法律和實踐上存在異同的原因。

21603817.label: Realisation of objectives
21603817.value: Most of the objectives for the ECS project the PI, Collaborator and other co-authors have achieved. The PI and Collaborator compared global constitutional provisions on clemency (objective #1), juxtaposed clemency practice (#2), explained the reasons for difference in this practice (#3), and designed best practice recommendations (#4) all within the edited collection Executive Clemency: Comparative and Empirical Perspectives (Routledge 2020), featuring two chapters written by the editors, a foreword by a prominent senior criminologist and seven other chapters on diverse topics and geographical regions. Several of the other publications arising from the project also addressed the same four objectives, in particular 'Towards a global theory of capital clemency incidence' (objectives #1,2,3); 'Making sense of the victim's role in clemency decision-making' (objectives #1,4); 'Deadly justice without mercy in East Asia?' (objectives #1,2,3,4), and 'Executive clemency during the coronavirus pandemic (objectives #2,4). Objective #5 was met by the data placed on the PI's personal website on constitutional clemency provisions around the world and clemency practice case studies on roughly 20 countries. This data is publicly accessible, adding to the clemency data presented within the various research outputs which are not open access at the time of writing. Of the objectives only partially met, objective #3 could only be addressed by qualitative research methods rather than quantitative methods. The reasons for this were a) insufficient data points to conduct a full regression analysis of the explanations for different levels of clemency frequency throughout the world and b) the PI's inability to recruit a quality PhD student with quantitative analysis skills during the years of the project. Nonetheless, as Part 6 of the research report will describe below, qualitative research methods still enabled the PI, Collaborator and other co-authors to come to explanations for clemency difference. Objective #6 was somewhat stymied by the disruption brought to teaching by the 2019 civil unrest in Hong Kong and the Covid-19 pandemic in 2020 and 2021. However, of the 10 undergraduate students who worked on the project as research assistants, several have expressed a desire to go on to PhD studies in the future, inspired by their contributions here. Other students who did not work directly on the project were able to learn about the methodology and findings of the PI and Collaborator at two public seminars delivered in 2019 and 2021, and during a co-taught class in 2020.

21603817.label: Major findings and research outcome
21603817.value: A summary of the relevant findings for each publication is as follows. Executive Clemency: Comparative and Empirical Perspectives - compared with the position at the time of the first global academic study on executive clemency laws in 1977, clemency is still constitutionally ubiquitous, still typically granted by the head of state, the head of state still receives advice on the decision, the types of clemency listed in national constitutions largely remain the same, and the scope of the clemency power typically remains unrestricted - a global analysis reveals four policy recommendations: all jurisdictions that retain the death penalty should provide a mechanism by which condemned prisoners may seek commutation or pardon; clemency applicants should enjoy a right to legal representation during this phase; advisory committees assist the quality of clemency decision-making, and clemency outcomes (whether grants or denials) should be made public Towards a Global Theory of Capital Clemency Incidence - death penalty retentionist states evince a great variety of capital clemency incidence - the most theoretically convincing explanations for such wide variation are: the political status of the final decision-maker; the extent to which cases less deserving of death are filtered away at earlier stages; how bureaucratised or regulated the clemency power has become, and the length of time that prisoners spend on death row before a decision is made Making Sense of the Victim's Role in Clemency Decision-Making - based on the literature on victim contributions to criminal justice decision-making, there are sound reasons to incorporate victims' views into the clemency decision-making process. Several common law jurisdictions have already done so - victim participation in clemency decision-making can be justified from a retributive, rehabilitative, or utilitarian standpoint Deadly Justice Without Mercy in East Asia? - the People's Republic of China, the Republic of China and Japan are three East Asian jurisdictions unique in world perspective for not having granted a single pardon or commutation in a death penalty cases over several decades - what links these three jurisdictions are: a) post-appellate opportunities to mitigate death sentences, and b) the inability of condemned prisoners to directly access the key decision-maker(s) on clemency Executive Clemency During the Coronavirus Pandemic: A Global Analysis of Law and Practice - the Covid-19 pandemic has stimulated the use of executive clemency to reduce prison populations in an unprecedented manner - however, this does not count as a new justificatory paradigm in the clemency literature: there are numerous examples of clemency being used to reduce prison populations in the past

21603817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21603817.value: If the PI can recruit a PhD student in the coming years who has quantitative research skills, then several of the theoretical ideas developed in this project may be 'tested' in new regression analysis featuring statistical data on executive clemency grants and denials. Examples are the statistical relationship between regime type / democratisation and clemency incidence, and the relationship between the length of time spent on death row and the likelihood of receiving clemency. Other research ideas developed from the current set of outputs include the following: - more thorough exploration on which aspects of executive clemency regulation are emerging as norms of customary international law on the basis of widespread state practice (e.g. the availability of clemency appeals in death penalty cases); - a survey of state practice on the victim's role in clemency decision-making, complementing the work already done in this project on the legal status-quo; - a theoretical exploration of the relationship between the various definitions of the 'rule of law' and the permitted use of clemency; - comparative constitutional law research on the six UN members that have no legal allowance for any executive clemency (whether constitutionally, by legislation, or by convention): El Salvador, Nicaragua, Guatemala, Switzerland, San Marino and Uruguay.

21603817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21603817.value: This research aimed to compare and contrast the law and practice of executive clemency across the globe. Executive clemency involves the executive branch of government temporarily or permanently mitigating a criminal punishment imposed by the judiciary. In this project, the PI and Collaborator focused particularly on pardons (outright releases from prison) and commutations (reductions in sentence or a change in sentence type) as two kinds of executive clemency. Clemency is a traditionally under-researched topic in law and in criminal justice, mainly because its decision-making processes and outcomes are typically shielded from the public, unlike criminal punishments imposed by the judiciary. Nevertheless, whether a prisoner receives a pardon or commutation, or not, can make the crucial difference between life and death, or between serving a long and a short prison sentence. This research project featured a global comparative study of clemency provisions in national constitutions, a comparative study of death row clemency practice in East Asia, a review of the changes to global clemency practice brought on by Covid-19, an account of the justifications for victim contribution to clemency decision-making, and a series of recommendations aimed at improving the transparency and fairness of clemency outcomes, among other topics.

21603917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21603917.value: Climate change and global warming, as the results of greenhouse gases emissions over last decades, have become one of the most sophisticated challenges on the globe, and hence attracted increasingly both the public concerns and the governmental communications. The CO2 emissions have been rising continuously in Hong Kong since 2000, amounting to over 40 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent in 2012. Specifically, Hong Kong government has set its plan to achieve a reduction in carbon intensity by 50 to 60 percent from the 2005 level by 2020. The government has also set the energy saving targets and a new fuel mix for electricity generation after 2020. Climate or energy policies have important economic consequences. Emission mitigation and energy saving plan can substantially affect the energy use, the supply of energy goods, stakeholder investment, economic structure, as well as the economic growth of the city. An accurate study of the impacts of climate and energy policies on the local level requires that, a macroeconomic model of the Hong Kong economy needs a detailed representation of energy production, sectoral investment, and induced innovation. The underlying research question of this project is to estimate the impacts of environmental change and mitigation of GHGs on the structural change, economic growth, and consumer welfare in Hong Kong. This project will develop a macroeconomic framework with endogenous growth, coupled with climate-energy models of carbon cycle. The generation and supply of energy/electricity are specified by technology details. In terms of methodology, the project will utilize several economic methods: econometric analysis, data disaggregation, numerical simulation. The contributions of this project are multiple. First, by providing a detailed representation of the economic structure of the Hong Kong economy, it develops a workhorse which can be used as the core for the numerical investigation of the macroeconomic effects of any public policies. Second, it develops a disaggregated climate-energy model, which is a powerful tool to assess several novel dimensions of Hong Kong’s climate and energy policies. Third, the disaggregated climate-energy model is linked to the macroeconomic model. This brings about a brand new modeling workhorse for future research on climate-economy-energy nexus. Fourth, this pilot project will fuel a further discussion in the modeling community of how economic models can take into account realistic climate-energy related specific technology features and finally reconcile the aggregate economic index with disaggregate climate-energy details. 由于过去几十年温室气体的排放，气候变化已经成为全球范围内最严峻、最复杂的问题之一，并吸引了公众的关注和政府的重视。香港二氧化碳气体的排放自2000年开始逐年递增，到2012已经达到了40 Mt的排放量。为此，香港政府已经承诺：到2020年，在2005年水平的基础上将本港的碳排放强度降低50%-60%。同时政府也设定了相应的节能目标。节能减排在很大程度上会影响能源需求与供给、投资者行为、经济结构和城市的GDP增长。因此，我们需要对这些政策的经济后果进行系统的、有效的分析。通过构建宏观经济模型，引入内生经济增长理论，同时结合气候-能源模型，本研究项目主要探讨气候变化和温室气体减排对香港经济结构和增长的影响。本研究项目构建的模型将会是第一个专门针对香港地区的动态一般均衡综合评价模型，除了作为本研究的数量工具外，还可以作为以后研究香港的其他能源、环保、经济相关的公共政策的平台。

21603917.label: Realisation of objectives
21603917.value: The PI and co-Is have completed the project with success. We have successfully demonstrated objective 1 by constructing a macro-economic model with detailed representation of the specific economic structure in a theoretical framework. In the paper “Green tax reform, endogenous innovation and the growth dividend”, we study theoretically and numerically the effects of an environmental tax reform using endogenous growth theory. In the theoretical segment, mobile labour between manufacturing and R&D activities, and elasticity of substitution between labour and energy in manufacturing lower than unity allow for a growth dividend, even if we consider pre-existing tax distortions. The scope for innovation is reduced when we consider direct financial investment in the lab, or elastic labor supply. We then apply the core theoretical model to a real growing economy and find that a boost in long-run economic growth following such a carbon policy is a possible outcome. Redistribution of additional carbon tax revenue by lowering capital taxation performs best in terms of efficiency measured by aggregate welfare. In terms of equity among social segments the progressive character of lump-sum redistribution fails when we consider very high emissions reduction targets. For objective 2, we have developed a framework to study the interactions among energy, emission, and pollution. In the paper “Regulation-induced structural break and the long-run drivers of industrial pollution intensity in China”, we examine the effect of the regulation-induced structural break on the nexus between industrial pollution intensity (IPI) and energy use structure in China. The results show that while a higher share of coal energy use increases IPI, stricter environmental regulation shifts the long-run IPI curve downwards. When we interact both variables, the results reveal that stricter environmental regulation induces a significant structural break in industrial use of coal energy, in a manner that reduces the associated emissions. In the paper “Long-run dynamics of sulphur dioxide emissions, economic growth, and energy efficiency in China”, we have estimates the linkages among total Sulphur dioxide (SO 2 ) emissions, total GDP and energy use efficiency. Our analysis shows that GDP has a positive impact on total SO 2 emissions in the short run and gains in energy efficiency have a significant negative effect on emissions in the long run. We argue that economic growth itself is an emission generator. Therefore, the government needs to establish a long-run strategy to curb emissions by improving energy efficiency. We further study the energy efficiency transition by using our framework developed in objective 1 and 2. In the paper “Energy Efficiency Transitions in China: How Persistent are the Movements to/from the Frontier?”, energy efficiency transitions is carefully investigated. Sustainable progress in energy efficiency achievement is beneficial to energy security and the achievement of the Paris Agreement. The estimated energy efficiency scores show significant regional and provincial heterogeneity. Also, while human capital development, urbanization, and foreign direct investment promote energy efficiency, price and income per capita reduce it. The transition probabilities indicate that the high energy-efficient state is less sustainable, and the movement towards the frontier seems less persistent than movement from the frontier. Thus, it appears that China is not making sustainable progress in energy efficiency. The unsustainable nature of the high energy-efficient state suggests that in China, there are weak energy efficiency efforts and energy efficiency policies lack robustness. We have achieved objective 3 to conduct the integrated analysis by combining the models developed in Objective 1 and 2. In the paper “Environmental regulation, energy structure change, and industrial pollution”, we find the implementation of stringent environmental regulation and resource-based economy reform shift the long-run industrial pollution intensity curve downwards, and stimulate the decrease of industrial pollution via adjusting the structure of coal energy consumption. In the paper “Emission mitigation and social cost of energy transition”, we investigate how innovative an economy needs to be in coping with energy transition towards renewable energies in the future. We study three important and frequently debatable assumptions that may affect the policy cost significantly: the capital growth rate, the intertemporal discount rate and the innovativeness of an economy. By incorporating new results from recent empirical studies, we find that deviations from previous assumptions can change the results significantly. This analysis shows that the energy transition can be achieved with certain degree of welfare loss. However, future investment environment can affect the sectoral growth differently, leading to significant change of the economic structure. Discounting of future generations has only mild effects on sectoral growth. Knowledge intensive sectors suffer drastically if the economy is less innovative and lower innovation can result in negative effects on substituting fossil energies. Finally, objective 4 has been achieved by studying GHGS mitigation related policies. All the three papers mentioned above include sections on the discussions of the GHGs mitigation related policies. In addition, in the paper “Potentials and opportunities towards the low carbon technologies – From literature review to new classification”, six categories of Low carbon technologie (LCTs) are classified based on two dimensions, which are the emission reduction potential and the technology usage purpose. We further identify the investment strategy for each type of LCT by sectors and stakeholders. In the paper “Economics of wastewater management in China’s industry”, we examine the direct and the structural break-induced effect of environmental regulation on industrial wastewater emissions. The results show that strict environmental regulation can partially offset the energy-induced effects imposed by the scale effects of foreign direct inflows and cause positive behavioral responses by either limiting coal usage or improving upon coal usage technology and shift towards clean energy sources. In the paper “Estimation of energy efficiency for educational buildings in Hong Kong”, we have proposed a fundamental framework for analysis of energy efficiency and policy effectiveness for Hong Kong building sector.

21603917.label: Major findings and research outcome
21603917.value: In this project, we have developed a multi-sector fully dynamic model for the Hong Kong economy with detailed representation of the specific economic structure in Hong Kong. We focus on two aspects of capital accumulation and innovation to understand the climate impact: the substitution between capital and intermediate goods, and innovation development with green technologies. We find that investment in the energy sectors declines with a higher value for the elasticity of substitution. This is because easy substitution will lower the demand for energy inputs and increase the demand for investment in new varieties, resulting in higher investment in non-energy sectors. By investigating various environmental taxation possibilities, we find redistribution of additional carbon tax revenue by lowering capital taxation performs best in terms of efficiency measured by total welfare. In terms of equity among social segments, the progressive character of lump-sum redistribution fails when we consider very high emissions reduction targets. We have developed a framework to study the interactions among energy, emission, and pollution. Our analyses reveal that stricter environmental regulation induces a significant structural break in industrial use of coal energy, in a manner that reduces the associated emissions. We also find that strict environmental regulation can partially offset the energy-induced effects imposed by the scale effects of foreign direct inflows and cause positive behavioral responses by either limiting coal usage or improving upon coal usage technology and shift towards clean energy sources. Sustainable progress in energy efficiency achievement is beneficial to energy security and the achievement of the Paris Agreement. We find that, while human capital development, urbanization, and foreign direct investment promote energy efficiency, consumer price and income per capita reduce it. The transition probabilities indicate that the high energy-efficient state is less sustainable. We further illustrate that economic growth has a positive impact on SO2 emissions in the short run and gains in energy efficiency have a significant negative effect on emissions in the long run. We thus suggest that the government needs to establish a long-run strategy to curb emissions by improving energy efficiency.

21603917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21603917.value: We have illustrated that energy efficiency is one of the key determinants to achieve climate change mitigation target. However, efficiency improvement is not very sustainable and the high efficiency can decay relative quickly. Therefore, the government should revisit its efficiency standard more frequently in order to keep the continuous improvement. Moreover, it would be of interest to investigate the energy efficiency at firm levels for different sectors in Hong Kong. Current discussions on the corporate environmental sustainability could be also an important channel for firms to engage in environmental protection. However, it seems the level of environmental sustainability is relatively low in Hong Kong. Therefore, future research shall seek ways to promote the corporate environmental sustainability.

21603917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21603917.value: This project studies the development of green city with sustainable economic growth in the presence of climate policy. In order to mitigate global climate change, many governments have started to implement various climate and energy policies to reduce domestic greenhouse gas emissions. In Hong Kong, the Hong Kong Climate Action Plan 2030+ report defines emission reduction target for Hong Kong’s contribution to the Paris Agreement. Energy-intensive sectors will have to bear the costs of carbon emission mitigation, while energy less intensive sectors such as finance and insurance can be beneficial. Strong economic growth can bring positive environmental benefits by investing more in green technology innovation. We also find that although many efforts have taken to improve energy efficiency. The high status of energy efficiency is not very sustainable. This suggests that the government needs to review its efficiency standard or related regulations more often in order to keep with the technology development. We highlight that stringent environmental regulation causes positive behavioral responses, as firms tend to update their technology and shift towards clean energy sources.

21606517.value: 中國法庭上的性別不平等：以外嫁女土地權益案件為中心

21606517.label: Project Objectives
21606517.value: To determine the effectiveness of the Chinese civil justice system in enforcing MOW rights to state compensation in compulsory rural land acquisitions. In particular, how do the claimants (MOW) and defendants (village collectives) fare in these civil lawsuits and what the trends and patterns are in different provinces/regions in China. To assess how the will of policy-makers (especially the provincial high court) influences the judicial outcome in MOW civil lawsuits. To understand how the local court’s connection with (and reliance on) the governing authorities of towns and villages influences the judicial protection of MOW rights. Explore possible practical and appropriate ways to revise existing villagers’ charters that are gender-bias to make them in line with state law. The objective of this exercise is devise a workable plan to help revise villagers’ charters, drafting a pro forma villagers’ charter (that upholds MOW rights) that takes into account practical issues facing village communities. Propose detailed procedural guidelines for handling MOW civil lawsuits (i.e. in the form of the Proposed Interpretation for the Supreme People’s Court to consider) for courts to follow so that both substantive and procedural rights of MOW litigants are protected. Provide useful information and data on the MOW issue to women’s rights NGOs in China.

21606517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21606517.value: Gender inequality, especially in the context of women’s rural land rights, is a persistent social problem in China. The problem is particularly acute for women married to outsiders but chose to retain their household registration in their home village. In other words, these women chose to keep their household registration of their village of origin instead of transferring their registration to their husbands’ household registration (usually in the cities). They are commonly known as “married-out women” (外嫁女) (“MOW”)). It is a common phenomenon in rural China that vested interests in village communities rely on traditional customs to deny MOW’s land rights, as MOW are considered “outsiders”. The problem can essentially be summed up as follows. When the government acquires rural land for development, the village collective in question will receive monetary compensation from the state. Under state law, the village collective must distribute this monetary compensation in the form of “dividends” to its members. However, many village collectives refuse to distribute dividends to MOW on the basis of discriminatory provisions in villagers’ charters. These provisions are designed to revoke (but without any legal basis) the village collective membership of MOW (once they are married), thereby stripping them of the rights to a share of the state compensation. This project examines the effectiveness of the Chinese civil justice system in dealing with cases brought by MOW. The project involves a review of over 1600 civil judgments in Chinese courts since 2009 to identify trends and patterns. Following the review, the project proceeds to interviewing judges in six local courts (in six different provinces) with reputation of strong inclination towards MOW disputes to test and confirm findings in the judgments review exercise. A series of focused groups will be conducted with the MOW litigants. The objective of the focused groups is to identify the magnitude and nature of the problem of court dockets refusing to accept civil lawsuits brought by MOW. This project will also examine sample village charters to identify discriminatory provisions and recommend ways to amend the charters with the view to uphold MOW rights. To date, there has been no comprehensive empirical study of the MOW problem from a civil litigation perspective. This project will fill an important gap in the literature. 性別不平等，尤其在涉及婦女土地權益的情形中，在中國是一個頑固的社會問題。這一問題對於出嫁之后戶籍仍然登記在娘家的女性尤為嚴重。換言之，這些女性選擇將戶籍繼續保留在其出生地，而不將戶口遷移到丈夫戶籍所在地（一般是在城市）。他們通常被稱之為“外嫁女”。這種現象在中國農村地區很普遍，農村地區在進行利益分配時會按照傳統習慣剝奪外嫁女的土地權益，而外嫁女被認為是“外人”。這一問題本質如下。當政府需要農村土地進行發展時，相關村集體可以從國家獲得經濟補償。根據中國的法律，村集體必須將經濟補償按照“紅利”的方式分配給其成員。但是，很多村集體基於村規民約拒絕向外嫁女分配“紅利”。這些規定剝奪（但是無任何法律依據）了外嫁女（一旦結婚）的村集體經濟組織成員資格，進而剝奪了他們分享國家補償的權利。本研究將檢討中國民事司法制度處理外嫁女案件的效能。本研究將對自2009年的1600份民事裁判文書進行分析，以識別裁判的趨勢和類型。除了對裁判文書的分析，本研究將對傾向於支持及不支持外嫁女權益的六家基層法院（在六個不同省份）的法官進行訪談，以測評和確認裁判文書分析中的發現。本研究還將對外嫁女訴訟的當事人進行小組座談。小組座談的目標是發現法院拒絕受理外嫁女提起的訴訟這一問題的嚴重性及其本質原因。本研究還將分析具歧視性的村規民約，並提出修改村規民約以支持外嫁女權益的方案。目前為止，還沒有從民事訴訟的角度對外嫁女問題的綜合性實証研究。本研究具有填補理論空白的重大意義。

21606517.label: Realisation of objectives
21606517.value: Objective 1 was to determine the effectiveness of the Chinese civil justice system in enforcing MOW rights to state compensation in compulsory rural land acquisitions. This objective is fully achieved to the extent that MOW cases are accepted by the courts. By empirically examining 858 sampled judgments of rural land dispute lawsuits between married-out women and village collectives throughout China from 2009 to 2017 (supplemented by interviews with judges), we have shown that MOW are winning by a substantial margin. MOW won 93.90% of the time, combining “complete win” (76.50%) and “partial win” (17.40%). MOW only lost 6.20% of the time. The rate of recovery by MOW in monetary claims are on the high side as well, with 77.63% of MOW recovering the full amount (i.e. 100%) of their claims. This shows the Chinese civil justice system (to the extent that cases are accepted by the courts) is effective in protecting MOW rights. The quantitative study also shows the variation of case outcome under different conditions (e.g. with temporal and geographical variables and variables such as legal representation). What the quantitative study does not explain is what happens to the cases that were not accepted by courts. In the latter part of the project, we interviewed MOW litigants and their lawyers in Guangdong Province. We were given access to MOW litigants from four villages near Shenzhen (Changyan Village, Dachang Village, Nangang Village and Tanglang Village). We were also given access to MOW litigants in Zhejiang Province and Beijing. We supplemented these interviews with an in-depth interview with the partner of a public interest law firm that specializes in protecting women’s rights in Beijing (北京千千律师事务所). We discovered that different local courts adopt divergent policies in accepting MOW cases. Some courts (especially those with close connection to villages) tend to side with the village collective and use village customs as a ground to deny MOW access to court. We have identified three stages in the courts’ treatment of MOW cases throughout the years, which addresses Objective 1. The first stage is an almost complete rejection of MOW cases as civil lawsuits, the second stage is an almost complete acceptance of cases, and the third stage is a selective acceptance of cases. Prior to 2009 (first stage), courts are unwilling to accept MOW lawsuits as civil cases. The MOW litigants would seek an administrative ruling on their village collective membership. If dissatisfied with the ruling, the MOW can challenge it in court. From 2009-2017 (second stage), courts were generally willing to accept MOW lawsuits as civil cases. There are two main reasons for this change. First, judges believe that the national laws that protect women and their rural land rights need to be enforced. Second, judges generally sympathized with MOW litigants and wanted to provide them an avenue for redress. This period coincided with the period of our quantitative study in which we found MOW winning by a substantial margin. From around 2018 onwards (third stage), courts have become selective in accepting MOW lawsuits as civil cases as courts face pressure from village collectives which are dissatisfied with MOW winning in court. We coded key provincial statutes and judicial rules to assess whether these provincial instruments presented any significance in the variations of the MOW litigant’s success rates. The quantitative study shows that when courts applied provincial statutes that protected women’s rights, the MOW litigants’ success rate was 100%. This partially addressed Objective 2. As we were not allowed access to policy-makers at provincial high courts, we addressed Objective 2 through interviewing frontline judges who handled MOW cases. These judges have said that provincial and intermediate court policy-makers play a role in shaping judicial outcome as lower courts generally follow the policies of the higher courts. The policy of the higher-level court influences whether MOW cases are accepted in lower courts. If the higher court has a pro-MOW policy, the lower court is more likely to accept the MOW’s case. If the policy is anti-MOW, the local court is more likely to cite village rules that suppress women’s rural rights as its ground to deny access. Regarding Objective 3, while there is no solid evidence that shows all courts that denied MOW access to court are closely connected to village collectives, the MOW whom we have interviewed expressed that courts closely connected with village committees tend to deny MOW access. Since 2018, courts increasingly face pressure from village collectives which are dissatisfied with MOW winning in court. With connections with local governments and their ability to create public attention, village collectives are able to exert considerable amount of pressure on courts and in some cases forcing courts to reject MOW cases. Since 2018, courts tend to only ratify the MOW’s membership of village collectives by referring to the existing administrative policies and regulations, while they are generally reluctant to review the legality of local government regulations and decisions on land rights. This is an indication of judicial deference to the local administration on issues relating to MOW’s rural land rights. We have coded DADs that made references to villagers’ charters (in response to Objective 4). For results, see first output in Part C. We have also collected a number of villagers’ charters (both pro-MOW and anti-MOW). From our interviews with MOW litigants, the villagers’ charters that tend to afford more protection to MOW are those that incorporate the relevant state law that protects women and their rural property rights (e.g. the Law on the Protection of Women’s Rights and Interests). We understand (at least in Guangdong) most villagers’ charters do not mention such state law at all. The general principle is that the villagers’ charter must incorporate MOW-friendly state law or regulations for it to be effective in protecting MOW rights. This finding will be published (in the second article) and later translated into Chinese. Regarding Objective 5, we have come to the conclusion that it may not be practical for the Supreme People’s Court (“SPC”) to adopt any recommended procedural guidelines. Rather, we would inform the policymakers the situation of violation of MOW rights (i.e. modifying Objective 5). It is an imperative that policymakers of higher courts are fully aware of the circumstances under which local courts reject MOW cases or adjudicate in a way that violates state law. The second article, when translated and distributed within the circle of senior Chinese judges of the PI (especially SPC judges), will be useful in informing policymakers at higher courts of these circumstances. Regarding Objective 6, the quantitative study (the article in Hastings Law Journal - first output in Part C), when translated into Chinese, would be an invaluable reference for women’s rights NGOs in China to understand the position of MOW for cases accepted by courts. The second article will capture the position of court’s acceptance of MOW cases and the position of MOW in such cases since 2018. The second article, entitled “When Do They Mobilize Law? - Legal Mobilization of Married-Out Women on Rural Land Rights in China” is currently under preparation. A draft will be ready by around end of July 2021.

21606517.label: Major findings and research outcome
21606517.value: By empirically examining 858 sampled judgments of rural land dispute lawsuits between married-out women (“MOW”) and village collectives throughout China from 2009 to 2017 (supplemented by interviews with judges), this project has shown that MOW are winning by a substantial margin (see first output in Part C). Out of the 858 sampled cases, MOW won 93.90% of the time, combining “complete win” (76.50%) and “partial win” (17.40%). MOW only lost 6.20% of the time. The rate of recovery by the MOW litigants in monetary claims are on the high side as well, with 77.63% of the MOW litigants recovering the full amount (recovered 100%) of their claims. This shows the Chinese civil justice system (to the extent that cases are accepted by the courts) is effective in protecting MOW rights during this period. The quantitative study also shows the variation of case outcome under different conditions (e.g. with temporal and geographical variables and variables such as legal representation). What the quantitative study does not shed light on is what happens to the cases that were not accepted by courts. Through fieldwork in Guangdong, Zhejiang and Beijing (see second output in Part C), we have identified three stages in the courts’ treatment of MOW cases throughout the years. The first stage (prior to 2009) is an almost complete rejection of MOW cases as civil lawsuits, the second stage (2009-2017) is an almost complete acceptance of cases, and the third stage (2018-present) is a selective acceptance of cases. We discovered that since 2018 (third stage), different local courts adopt divergent policies in accepting MOW cases. Some courts (especially those closely connected with village committees) tend to side with the village collective and use traditional rules/village customs as a ground to deny MOW access to court (which in fact is a breach of state law). From our fieldwork, we found that (since 2018) the courts tend to only ratify MOW’s membership of village collectives by referring to the existing administrative policies and regulations, while they are generally reluctant to review the legality local government regulations and administrative decisions on land rights and interests. This is an indication of judicial deference to the local administration on issues relating to MOW’s rural land rights.

21606517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21606517.value: A potential development of the research is to conduct an ethnographic study of the acceptance rate of MOW cases in a local court in China. This project found that the court system is generally effective in enforcing the rural land rights of MOW litigants for cases that entered the court system (i.e. cases accepted by the courts). While the fieldwork helped us better understand trends of MOW case acceptance by courts, it did not quantify the extent to which MOW cases were accepted/rejected by courts. To be able to conduct this ethnographic study, the researcher first needs to identify a court that frequently handles MOW cases. The researcher has to have access to the docketing division of the court over an extended period of time (e.g. 6 months). Over that period, the researcher is to be allowed to observe the docketing process of MOW disputants and record the result (i.e. whether the case could be registered). The researcher should also be able to record the reasons of the docketing judge for accepting or rejecting the MOW cases.

21606517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21606517.value: Gender inequality, particularly in the context of women’s rural land rights, is a persistent social problem in China. The problem is particularly acute for women married to outsiders but chose to retain their household registration in their home village (or married-out women (“MOW”)). This project found that the court system is generally effective in enforcing the rural land rights of MOW litigants for cases that entered the court system (i.e. cases accepted by the courts). By empirically examining sampled judgments of rural land dispute lawsuits between MOW litigants and village collectives throughout China from 2009 to 2017, this project has shown that MOW are winning by a substantial margin. Out of the 858 sampled cases, MOW won 93.90% of the time, combining “complete win” (76.50%) and “partial win” (17.40%). MOW only lost 6.20% of the time. However, this project also found that some courts (especially courts with close connection to villages) reject MOW cases. In other words, some MOW litigants never get the chance to have their cases heard before a court. This casts doubt on the overall effectiveness of the Chinese court system in enforcing MOW rural land rights.

21607917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21607917.value: The theoretical debate over trust and its role in the criminal world remains a contentious topic of study in criminology. Why do criminals trust and co-operate with one another? How do they ensure that their fellow criminals will not betray them, cheat them by informing the police of their competitors’ actions and honour their agreements? Scholars have examined these questions as they apply to cyber hackers (Lusthaus 2012; Decary Hetu & Dupont 2013; Holt et al. 2015; Dupont et al. 2016) and organised crime groups such as the Mafia (Varese 2001; Campana & Varese 2013). However, questions of trust and how criminals cooperate with one another remain largely unexplored in the field of green criminology, an emerging field focusing on crimes against the environment and the illegal trade in protected and endangered wildlife. Drawing on primary data collected from fieldwork conducted in Guangzhou and Zhuhai, Guangdong Province, and supplemented by open sources, the proposed study will explore a specific branch of illegal wildlife trade : the supply of state-protected wildlife for human consumption as delicacy in China, and examine the issues of trust and co-operation amongst criminals in this illegal market. In essence, the study will aim to 1) understand the dynamics of the illegal trade of state-protected wildlife as delicacy in China, 2) explore how criminals trust and co-operate with one another in such a setting and 3) explore which informal mechanisms (if any) facilitate trust and co-operation in this trade. The proposed study will make the following contributions. First, it will make theoretical contributions to the debate on trust in the underworld and to the general development of green criminology. Second, it will inform policies that address the illegal trade of state-protected wildlife in China, issues of animal welfare and security enforcement. Third, it will make educational contributions by transferring the knowledge it generates to the wider community via academic journals and conferences. I will also incorporate the findings from this proposed study into my teaching to inspire the younger student body to be more conscious of issues related to wildlife conservation and animal welfare. 犯罪世界中， 信任及其扮演之角色在學術辯論上是一個具爭議的題目。為什麼罪犯會信任及與其他人合作？他們如何確保其共犯遵守彼此之間的協議，不會通知警察或競爭對手；背叛、出賣他們？ 是次研究計劃以重點保護野生動物的非法貿易為研究基礎：探討在中國供應國家重點保護野生動物作人類食用及關於在非法市場中罪犯的信任與合作問題。 該研究計劃旨在：（1）理解中國的國家重點保護野生動物以作佳餚的非法交易；（2）探索罪犯如何在該情境中信任及與他人合作；（3）探索非正規的機制（如有）如何促使貿易中的信任及合作。 是次研究之成效如下：（1）理論：為地下世界中對信任的辯論及犯罪學整體的發展作出貢獻 ；（2）政策：為如何執行國家重點保護野生動物非法貿易的政策提出建議；（3）教育：通過學術期刊及會議將是次研究的成果廣泛傳播，並將研究的結果透過課堂傳達給學生，令他們更關注動物權益及野生動物保育的事宜。

21607917.label: Realisation of objectives
21607917.value: The findings of this research supported by my ECS were reported in five papers and two talks (1 conference and 1 virtual seminar). I will give a summary of each paper and talk and outline how the project objectives were met in each research activity. The first paper was published in 2018 in Asian Journal of Criminology (SSCI, impact factor = 2.297). The paper addresses the issue of trust in wildlife trading networks with my collaborators from the Netherlands. This paper examines how trust is established and maintained between actors trading in wildlife products in mainland China and how such transactions can succeed. The paper also explores the role of ethnicity, kinship, and social networks in the formation of trust in the underworld. Objectives 1, 2 and 3 are achieved in this study. The second paper was published in 2019 in Geoforum (SSC1, impact factor = 3.901). This study addresses how demand reduction campaigns are centered around a stereotypical “Asian Super Consumer” which promotes racist narratives in addressing the illegal wildlife trade. The study argues for a deeper cultural understanding of the consumption of illegal wildlife products to develop effective reduction campaigns. This study successfully captured the attention of Global Scan, an independent research consultancy that has conducted substantial wildlife reduction campaigns and we published a reply to their comments which led to our third study. The third paper was published in 2020 in Geoforum, it is a reply to our previous piece in 2019 at the same journal. In our reply, we argued that it is important to recognize the fact that Western consumers are also responsible for driving the illegal wildlife trade and such practices are often ignored by policy and campaigns thus generating a potentially racist narrative of the illegal wildlife trade. Objectives 4 and 5 are achieved in both studies published in Geoforum since they speak to addressing gaps in policy campaigns on the illegal wildlife trade and a successful engagement with an agency responsible for developing the campaign. The fourth paper was published in 2021 in China Information (SSCI, impact factor = 1.676). This study explores how criminal networks trading in tiger parts and pangolins engages in illegal economies and how they can take advantage of the Belt and Road Initiative to further their illegal operation. This paper also discusses the blurring of the formal and informal economy, resulting in the carving out governance spaces in which they impose their managerial systems, thus making prosecution of underground wildlife businesses difficult. Objectives 1, 2, 3 and 4 are achieved in this study. The fifth paper was published in 2021 in Trends in Organised Crime (SSCI, impact factor = 2.8). This study explores how criminal groups in the illegal wildlife trade diversify and outsource their activities when smuggling wildlife products from Laos and Myanmar into mainland China. Objective 1 is met in this study. With the support of my ECS, I have spoken on two occasions about my research. I was an invited speaker at a seminar series organised by Wildlife Trade Futures in April 2020, namely the ‘Blind Sports in Research on Covid – 19 and Wildlife Economies: Marginalised Perspectives and Neglected Trends: A Virtual Seminar Series’. I spoke about the illegal wildlife trade, and criminal networks and addressed missing gaps in consumer awareness. The seminar was attended by students, researchers, representatives of NGOs and members of the public thus achieving Objective 5. I spoke as an invited panelist at the American Geographers Association in April 2020. The title of my panel was ‘More than Humans: Geographies of Covid 19: human, species, and inequalities.’ I spoke on the issue of illegal wildlife trade and addressed the dynamics of criminal networks trading in wildlife at the panel. The conference was attended by students and researchers thus achieving Objective 5.

21607917.label: Major findings and research outcome
21607917.value: There are three major findings from my research. First, my study provided original data on the interaction of criminal networks specialising in the illegal wildlife trade and how cooperation is fostered in this illegal setting. In our paper published in the Asian Journal of Criminology, we show that trust is heavily dependent on ethnic and kinship ties while the reputation of being reliable and honest is equally important when trading illegally in wildlife products. Repeated encounters and personal experience also aid cooperation and foster trust between buyers and suppliers of illegal wildlife. Further, the paper published in Trends in Organised Crime demonstrated that criminals involved in the illegal wildlife trade outsource their illegal activity to other criminal groups thus there is more than one criminal network involved in various stages of trading protected wildlife. Second, my research findings point to how criminal networks operate in tandem with actors and institutions from the formal economies and infrastructure. This is published in my paper in China Information, where it also demonstrates how gaps in existing policies can pave the way for criminal networks to exploit wildlife in the Belt and Road Initiative. This paper highlights that conservation measures and protection for wildlife along the Belt and Road Initiative must be safeguarded to prevent further loss of wildlife. Lastly, the illegal wildlife trade is a universal issue, and we cannot blame a specific region or ethnicity for the decline of wildlife, this is demonstrated in my publications in Geoforum. It is important to recognize that consumers from the West are also buying these products illegally and campaigns should no longer focus the blame on consumers from the East to avoid racists narratives about the illegal wildlife trade. My research endeavors to speak to those responsible for designing reduction campaigns that are not bound by any racial stereotypes but instead address the exploitation of wildlife as a global issue.

21607917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21607917.value: This research has inspired me to research two forms of crime against animals and wildlife. I have developed a grant for studying mercy releases submitted to Environmental Conservation Fund in 2021. I was awarded the grant in 2022. I have also developed a research proposal on illegal puppy breeding farms and submitted it to the General Research Fund in 2021.

21607917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21607917.value: The global illegal wildlife trade is threatening the survival of various endangered and protected species. Trading in protected wildlife is attractive to criminal groups since it promises high monetary profit with minimal risks of enforcement. This study seeks to understand how criminals involved in the illegal wildlife trade operate and they foster trust and cooperation in their illegal undertakings. This study also examines the effectiveness of regulations that are in place and addresses any missing gaps in existing policies. This study discovered that there is more than one criminal group involved in the illegal wildlife trade while outsourcing and diversification of tasks is common in illegal dealings. Trust is built upon the ethnicity and the reputation of the criminal while the reputation of being reliable and trustworthy is an asset. To prevent further exploitation of wildlife, reduction campaigns are essential in increasing awareness of the general public. However, such campaigns failed to grasp the fact that illegal wildlife products are also demanded by consumers in the West, and centering campaigns on Asian consumers is inaccurate and could even lead to discrimination and prejudice.

21609017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21609017.value: 移動影像媒體以廣告，電視和虛構電影為主體，植根於電影現實主義（Bordwell等，1985）。 香港和國際新一代抽象動畫製作者挑戰這一範式。視頻作品如<<玻璃體>>（Robert Seidel 2015），<<黑動>>（陳好彩 2015）或<<視化功夫運動>>（Tobias Gremmler 2016）呈現了顛覆， 擾亂和質疑我們日常感知的抽象。在今天同一媒體形象越來越飽和的世界中，抽象動畫可以提供一個從現實中抽離的空間，這使得與日常經驗（Fuxjäger2011）有定性差異的觀念，以及可以協商的替代含義（Hattler＆Wardman 2015）。是次研究的主張是抽像也創造了敘述。 提出的研究將通過訪問創造敘事抽象的實踐者來探討這個顯然矛盾的立場。 雖然藝術史學家批判性地讚揚了抽象繪畫的原因和影響（Greenberg 1995，Mitchell 1989），及電影理論家已經討論了傳統敘事剪輯的細分，好像結構主義電影的製作; 然而, 集中討論以抽像作為敘事時間媒體的影響和作用的研究卻很少 -- 一個罕見的例子，可見Dirk De Bruyn（2014）以重新審視前衛和唯物主義的電影作為創傷的表達。 為了更好地了解本地和國際新冒起的藝術表現形式, 以及對基於電影現實主義的主流媒體訊息的解讀, 更好地理解抽象動畫中的編碼和解碼（Hall 1980）的敘述和意義是必要的。 這項研究將包括人種學研究性質（採訪以抽象移動影像為創作題材的當代藝術家）及研究創作性質（基於實踐的敘事抽象動畫研究）。調查的結果將顯示在一個中長度的抽象電影中，以五個分題去探討不同的敘事策略。基於已證理論（Strauss＆Glaser 1967）, 這個以觀眾去評估的設計將有助明白人們對抽象動畫理解的意義。評估結果將在會議和學術期刊分享, 而製成電影將在香港的Videotage，倫敦的onedotzero及各地的藝術節展出。

21609017.label: Realisation of objectives
21609017.value: Objective 1 has been achieved. Based on interviews with four Hong Kong-based artists (Carla Chan, Tobias Gremmler, Choi Sai-Ho, and Chris Cheung Hon-Him) and four international artists (Matt Abbiss, Robert Seidel, Ryoichi Kurokawa, and Sabrina Ratté), and saturated by a review of pre-existing related literature and abstract animation works, a taxonomy of terms, concepts and strategies towards narrative abstraction and abstract narrative was developed. Objective 2 has been achieved. Interviews were conducted with four Hong Kong-based artists (Carla Chan, Tobias Gremmler, Choi Sai-Ho, Chris Cheung Hon-Him) and four international artists (Matt Abbiss, Robert Seidel, Ryoichi Kurokawa, Sabrina Ratté) about their conceptual frameworks and narrative-aesthetic strategies and approaches to meaning-making in the abstract moving image. The interviews were transcribed, coded and analysed to form a taxonomy of terms, concepts and strategies. This, in turn, formed the basis of the scholarly publications arising from this research and informed the creation of the animation films, which were screened to audiences to test their understanding and appreciation of the works. Objective 3 has been achieved. However, instead of a long film with several chapters, four independent, individual works were created. We opted for the creation of separate works since it became clear during the research that the works would be too different to be easily combined. ‘Concrete Abstraction: Road Triptych’ is a 3-screen work which requires three monitors. As such, it cannot be meaningfully combined with single-screen works. ‘+’ is a quasi-loop and works best projected in an exhibition space. And while ‘Matter and Motion’ and ‘Serial Parallels’ work best in a film festival/cinema setting, ‘Serial Parallels’ also exists as an expanded version where the main film is supplemented by several monitors of additional looping footage that is spread out through the exhibition space. In this way, different exhibition and screening venues were approached for different films. Objective 4 has been achieved. The research outputs were disseminated to a larger community for further exploration and discussion by way of two academic journal publications, ten conference presentations, and a very large number of presentations in festivals, screenings, and exhibitions. Objective 5 has been achieved. Hong Kong-based moving image artists were included in this research. We hope that this will lead to further research into and appreciation of these artists, and Hong Kong arts and culture in general.
