21609017.label: Major findings and research outcome
21609017.value: This research results in manifold matter by necessity, across practice and theory. Developed as artistic animation research, the study employs practice and theory as a form of visual thinking, utilising the format and politics of a taxonomy, and, in correspondence with it, the creation of new artistic works. In this study, abstract animation is understood as a thinking space that adapts narrative processing in and through experimental moving image. The below figures form part of the overall emergent theory and point to the focus of the debate: ◉ Process-based reading of animation. ◉ Reading the figural – the former sign becoming figural. ◉ In-animate transhuman – forms based on transformations in the status of images and ‘life’ (after Deborah Levitt). ◉ Naturalness of technologies – technology and society understood in planetary terms (after Benjamin Bratton). ◉ Saturated image forms (Paul Wells). ◉ Absolute spiritual. ◉ Narrative as a spectrum. ◉ Movement abstracted from form. ◉ Sculpting time. ◉ Abstracted Real. The key argument of the research is found across the study/taxonomy due to the methodology chosen and adapted for the research – essentially pointing to one argument: Meaning-making in abstract animation can no longer be validated against, or even disclosed, by a particular ‘code of narration,’ that organises our perceptual apparatus from within some filmic perspective only. As we encounter what the animate or inanimate today implies, we need to approach the problem of meaning-making as other than via a narrative device, or unifying ‘code of narration.’ Any prioritisation of narration over figuration via representation requires new conceptual frameworks to grasp the unique effect of today’s abstract animation in its force and potential to produce experiences for the viewer through which meaning and thought can be negotiated. The research is centred on the notion of a Taxonomy and hence comprises several distinct, interacting and interrelating, conceptual and experimental, artistic interventions: while the conceptual outcome is staged as a series of mini-debates across different outputs – papers, conference presentations, an extended curatorial statement, screenings and exhibitions – the practice-based outcomes function as the crystallisation and condensation of these theoretical threads. Four new abstract-narrative animation works were created by the PI, highlighting different aspects of narrative-abstraction: single-channel works ‘Matter and Motion’ (2018), ‘+’ (2018-2019), and ‘Serial Parallels’ (2019), and the 3-screen work ‘Concrete Abstraction: Road Triptych’ (2019-2021). The works were screened widely at international festivals and exhibitions, receiving critical acclaim and awards.

21609017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21609017.value: Inspired by the findings from this research, the PI aims to develop a journal article or more extensive study focusing on animated abstraction as a unique mode for rethinking artistic research and its largely exclusive knowledge formations in limited contexts. The PI is also planning to create several new animated works, to experiment with other audio, visual, and narrative expressions than previously done. For example, looking into the relationship between abstraction and archive, or thinking of animated abstraction as a form of documentation. Another potential approach is to work more closely with a younger generation of experimental animation artists in Hong Kong who have started to become more active in the recent past, to further develop what’s been discovered through this study.

21609017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21609017.value: This research project has been developed as artistic animation research, employing practice and theory as a form of visual thinking. It was conducted as a number of conceptual and experimental, artistic interventions that use the format and politics of a taxonomy: The result demonstrates the formation of new knowledge in the field. It is crucially tied to studying a range of artists working with abstraction, narrative and meaning in the moving image, and to the PI’s respective practice – specifically, the four new animated works produced within this grant project. The significance of the study runs across two major and interconnected lines: firstly, unique conceptual discoveries are made through the lens of abstract animation around notions including the ‘abstracted real’, a process-based reading of animation, and ‘reading the figural’. Secondly, applied animation research through the practices of Hong Kong and international artists – and the PI’s own artworks created in response – present innovative modes of narrative processing, which can be understood as resonating with the larger socio-political shifts of our time. A crucial value of the project is seen in the way it creates knowledge through the practice of animation: Abstract animation as a thinking space.

22103017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22103017.value: Epidemiology suggests that consumption of high fat diet (HFD) is associated with colorectal cancer growth. Understanding the molecular mechanisms that underlie the HFD-associated colorectal cancer growth will have a great implication. Our data clearly showed that HFD increased tumor size and tumor weight in xenograft models compared to matched control diet (CD). Interestingly, the growth of the tumors in the HFD-feeding models slowed down if HFD was replaced by CD, while tumors were getting bigger if HFD feeding persisted. Lipidomics studies showed that HFD increased palmitic acid and stearic acid levels in the tumors of the xenograft models. These 2 fatty acid levels in the tumors of the xenograft models were significantly reduced if HFD was replaced by CD. Furthermore, RNA sequencing showed that HFD upregulated toll like receptor 4 (TLR4) expressions in the tumors of the xenograft models, and the TLR4 expression levels were significantly reduced if HFD was replaced by CD. In addition, in CRC cell models, we found that only palmitic acid but not stearic acid upregulated TLR4 expressions. Palmitic acid also significantly increased CRC cell proliferation measured by CyQUANT® Cell Proliferation Assays. The palmitic acid-increased CRC cell proliferation was reduced in the presence of TLR4 inhibitors; these TLR4 inhibitors did not significantly affect the proliferation of control CRC cells. Based on our preliminary data, we hypothesize that palmitic acid upregulates TLR4 expression in CRC, and the palmitic acid-TLR4 axis contributes to the HFD-associated CRC cell proliferation. We will set up different in vivo and in vitro models for this study. We will investigate the underlying mechanism of how palmitic acid upregulates TLR4 expression in CRC. Furthermore, we will study whether palmitic acid activates TLR4 in CRC cells. The contribution of the palmitic acid-TLR4 axis in HFD-associated CRC cell proliferation will also be investigated. This study not only increases our understanding on the pathology of HFD-associated CRC, but also provides scientific rationale to suggest dietary intervention for the CRC patients.

22103017.label: Realisation of objectives
22103017.value: We have completed the 3 objectives. The findings of the study have been submitted to a Journal and is under major revision. Objective 1: To investigate the mechanism underlying how palmitic acid upregulates TLR4 expression in CRC We have found that HFD feeding increases TLR4 expression in CRC by performing RNA sequencing with the xenograft tissues dissected from DIO and control mice and validated with qPCR and Western blot. The next question was, how HFD could affect TLR4 expressions in CRC. Since mice were received high-fat dietary intervention, we studied the lipid profiles of the tumor tissues and examined whether the lipid changes would affect the TLR4 expressions. Our lipidomics data showed that HFD feeding increased palmitic acid and stearic acid levels in the tumors. Furthermore, palmitic acid significantly increased TLR4 mRNA levels and protein levels in the CRC cells. However, stearic acid did not affect the TLR4 expression. Since palmitic acid increased TLR4 mRNA levels, we investigated whether the acid affected TLR4 gene transcription. Our data showed that palmitic acid treatment significantly increased the expressions of both PU.1 and Sp1 transcription factors which are essential for TLR4 transcription. To investigate whether Sp1 and PU.1 were involved in the palmitic acid-increased TLR4 expressions, we separately knockdown Sp1 and PU.1 in the CRC cells before palmitic acid treatments. Results showed that the acid treatments significantly increased TLR4 expressions in Sp1-knockout cells but not in the PU.1-knockout CRC cells, suggesting that PU.1 is essential for the palmitic acid-increased TLR4 expression in CRC. Furthermore, mutation at PU.1_1, PU.1_2 and PU.1_5, but not at PU.1_0, abolished the palmitic acid-increased promoter activity. These data suggest that PU.1 binding site at -106, -172 and -204 are essential for the palmitic acid-mediated TLR4 transcription. Objective 2: To study whether palmitic acid activates TLR4 in CRC cells Our data with surface plasmon resonance (SPR) showed that palmitic acid did not bind to TLR4 protein. The KD of the dissociation equilibrium constant of palmitic acid binding to TLR4 protein was 35.56 M which was obtained by computer fitting. The lower the KD value, the better the binding of the sample to the protein. The KD value suggests that it is less likely to have a binding between palmitic acid and TLR4 protein. Instead, as reported by other study, palmitic acid binds to MD, an accessory protein of TLR4 and hence activates TLR4. We also showed an enhanced phosphorylation of NFκB in CRC cells after palmitic acid treatment. Objective 3: To investigate the contribution of the palmitic acid-TLR4 axis in high saturated fat diet-associated CRC cell proliferation Our data also showed that palmitic acid increased CRC cell proliferation which was abolished in the presence of TLR4 inhibitor C34. To further suggest that TLR4 mediated the palmitic acid-increased CRC cell proliferation, we knockout TLR4 in the HCT116 cells (TLR4_KO). Data showed that palmitic acid failed to increase the proliferation of the TLR4_KO. These data evidently suggest that palmitic acid increases CRC cell proliferation in a TLR4-dependent manner. Next, we examined whether TLR4 mediated the HFD-associated CRC growth in vivo. We subcutaneously inoculated wild-type HCT116 cells or TLR4-knockout HCT116 cells (HCT116TLR4_KO) into the nude mice. When the tumor volume reached to ~80 mm3 in volume, we randomly divided them into HFD group and CD group. Besides, for another batch of mice were fed a palmitic acid-rich diet (PAD) (Research Diets), which contains 106.5 g of palmitic acid in 262.8 g fatty acids, in which palmitic acid accounts for 40.5% of the total fatty acids. The control mice were fed the corresponding match control diet (C-PAD) (Research Diets). For the mice that were inoculated with the wild-type HCT116 cells, both HFD and PAD significantly increased the tumor volume and tumor weight when compared to CD and C-PAD, respectively. Interestingly, for the mice that were inoculated with the HCT116TLR4_KO cells, both HFD and PAD failed to increase the tumor volume and tumor weight. These data suggest that HFD and PAD increase CRC growth in a TLR4-dependnet manner in vivo. Next, we explored whether TLR4 promoted CRC growth under HFD condition by regulating the cancer metabolism. We found that knockout of TLR4 in the tumor tissues abolished the HFD-enhanced expressions of acetyl-CoA carboxylase (ACC), fatty acid synthase (FASN), carnitine palmitoyltransferase-1 (CPT-1), medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (MCAD), glucose transporter GLUT1 and also sterol regulatory element-binding transcription factor-1 (SREBP-1c). iTRAQ-based proteomics with the tumor tissues also showed that knockout of TLR4 changed the metabolism of CRC and also regulated other metabolic enzymes that the changes of many of these enzymes were not due to the dietary intervention. Further analysis showed that these metabolic enzymes were either located in mitochondria and cytoplasm. More importantly, they were mainly involved in energy production and took part in triglyceride biosynthesis, glucose metabolism, fatty acid activation, fatty acid, triglyceride and ketone synthesis in a cooperative manner, suggesting the regulatory role of TLR4 on CRC metabolism under HFD condition is not attributed to a single metabolic enzyme but a collaborative work of the enzymes. Indeed, changes of the metabolism affected ATP production as knockout of TLR4 abolished the HFD-increased ATP level in the tumor tissues. Interestingly, our data also showed that knockout of TLR4 abolished the HFD-enhanced β-catenin expressions in the tumor tissues, suggesting the energy homeostasis regulated by β-catenin in CRC under HFD feeding condition is in relation to TLR4 activity. Taken together, these data suggest that TLR4 regulates CRC growth under HFD feeding condition by re-programming the cancer metabolism.

22103017.label: Major findings and research outcome
22103017.value: Our study shows that HFD feeding increases TLR4 expression in CRC, in which, palmitic acid plays an important role. Palmitic acid significantly increases the activity of the TLR4 promoter (-1 to -385 TLR4-E). However, mutation at PU.1_1, PU.1_2 and PU.1_5, but not at PU.1_0, abolishes the palmitic acid-increased promoter activity. These data suggest that PU.1 binding site at -106, -172 and -204 are essential for the palmitic acid-mediated TLR4 transcription in CRC. We also find that palmitic acid does not bind to TLR4 protein as demonstrated in the surface plasmon resonance study. Besides, we have demonstrated that palmitic acid promotes CRC growth in a TLR4-dependent manner both in vitro and in vivo. Under HFD feeding condition, TLR4 regulates CRC metabolism, that may explain the enhanced CRC growth under HFD feeding.

22103017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
22103017.value: Understand the role of TLR4 in promoting CRC growth under obesity or HFD feeding condition may help us to develop therapeutic agents for the treatment of obesity-associated CRC. Agents that can reduce TLR4 expression or antagonists for TLR4 that inhibit TLR4 activity may be developed as alternative therapeutics for the cancer treatment.

22103017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
22103017.value: Epidemiology suggests that consumption of high fat diet (HFD) is associated with colorectal cancer (CRC) growth and development. Understanding the molecular mechanisms that underlie the HFD-associated colorectal cancer growth will have a great implication. Our study clearly shows that HFD feeding increases TLR4 expression in CRC, in which, palmitic acid in the HFD increases TLR4 gene transcription. The enhanced TLR4 expression increases CRC growth by regulating the cancer metabolism. Our study has identified TLR4 is a critical regulator of CRC growth under HFD feeding condition; and provides evidence to support the development of TLR4-targeting therapeutics for the treatment of obesity-associated CRC.

22201617.label: Project Title(Chinese)
22201617.value: 基於聚簇的文本流數據的發布/訂閱系統

22201617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22201617.value: Massive amount of textual data are being generated on an unprecedented scale. Such textual data, which can be modelled as continuously arriving streams, often offer first-hand information for a variety of events of different types and scales. To allow web users to stay informed about the events, trending activities, public concerns, and so forth that are of personal interest to them, we will take the first step towards developing cluster-based publish/subscribe systems for textual data streams. In particular, for each subscription we will continuously deliver clusters that are relevant to the subscription. Each cluster is generated by an online text clustering algorithm. Compared with the delivery of single-granularity messages to subscribers in the traditional message-based publish/subscribe systems, delivering clusters to subscribers has the following benefits: (1) Since the messages in the same cluster are inclined to cover the same topic, the content of a cluster can be expressed in an informative and laconic way by applying some visualization techniques (e.g., "Word Clouds''). (2) Based on the clustering algorithm, near-duplicated messages are likely to be merged into the same cluster. Thus, a subscriber would neither be overwhelmed by a large number of messages nor suffer from receiving many near-duplicate messages. We shall propose efficient algorithms to support the delivery of clusters for a large number of subscribers. The major challenge is to achieve high performance for a matching process between clusters and subscriptions as the system is required to support millions or even tens of millions of subscriptions and find the matching subscriptions of each evolving cluster in milliseconds. To meet this high-performance requirement, we plan to develop novel group evaluation and filtering mechanisms based on a filter-verification framework to efficiently find the matching subscriptions for each new/updated cluster generated by an online text clustering algorithm. Our planned research agenda for this project is as follows: (1) Definition of the problem of cluster-based publish/subscribe over textual data streams; (2) Design of the subscription indexing schemes and filtering algorithms to quickly handle the matching process between subscriptions and clusters; (3) Optimizations to enhance the filtering efficacy; (4) Performance evaluation of our proposed indices and algorithms; (5) Development of a system to demonstrate the feasibility of our proposals. With our extensive research experience in publish/subscribe problems, we hope that the outcome of this project will improve the quality, efficiency, and personalization of publish/subscribe based information dissemination, thereby benefiting both individuals and society as a whole. 在如今的大數據時代，我們需要面對大量的文本流數據。這種文本流數據往往提供了各種新聞和事件的第一手信息。為了讓用戶能夠實時地獲取他們感興趣的事件和話題，我們計劃設計一個基於聚簇的文本流數據的發布/訂閱系統。該系統會實時地向每一個訂閱者推送他們感興趣的事件或者話題的聚簇。其中，每一個聚簇是由多個相似度高的消息組成。與傳統的基於單個消息的發布/訂閱系統相比，基於聚簇的發布/訂閱系統有如下幾方面的優點：（1）聚簇裡的語義可以通過已有的可視化方法而清晰簡潔的表達出來；（2）由於一個聚簇裡的消息相互之間具有高度相似性，用戶可以避免接收相似的內容。該項目的工作是設計能夠支持大量訂閱者的聚簇推送算法。其中，主要難點在於當一個新的消息到來時，如何快速地為每個訂閱者更新聚簇推送結果。為了解決這一難點，我們計劃設計一個在過濾-確認框架下的分組匹配機制，從而在每一個消息到來之時高效地更新每一個訂閱者的聚簇推送結果。項目的研究內容分為如下幾個步驟：（1）基於聚簇的文本流數據的發布/訂閱問題的定義；（2）訂閱索引結構和相應過濾算法的設計；（3）過濾效果的優化；（4）索引結構和算法的效率和結果質量的實驗評估；（5）訂閱/推送系統的實現。基於我們之前在發布/訂閱系統設計方向的研究經驗，我們希望該項目的研究成果可以提升個性化推送/訂閱系統的信息傳遞質量和效率，從而使得每個用戶和整個社會受益。

22300017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22300017.value: The aim of this project is to apply algebraic and combinatorial tools to analyse a large class of Markov chains. Markov chains are probabilistic algorithms commonly used in statistical physics, bioinformatics, economics and other sciences to simulate a random process (e.g. changes in demand for various products) or to sample from a desired distribution (e.g. to create typical particle configurations of different densities to study phase transitions). In the majority of applications, there are few theoretical results on how many steps of the algorithm are required to produce a useful result. The situation is being improved by several recent studies of Markov chains with algebraic or geometric connections, where it is possible to obtain exact formulae for many features of their long term behaviour, such as the required runtime. Powerful comparison techniques then extend these results to more realistic and irregular chains which are not so directly tractable. This project will study Markov chains whose transition probabilities arise from two new families of linear transformations on combinatorial Hopf algebras. The first family comprises permuted descent operators, whose associated Markov chains model breaking a combinatorial object, such as a permutation, tree or graph, into random pieces and reassembling them in a different order. The second family comprises hyperoctahedral descent operators, which in addition apply involutions to some of the pieces before the reassembly. We intend to derive formulae, valid for all combinatorial Hopf algebras, for the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of these linear transformations, using structure theorems of Hopf algebras. We will then specialise this eigendata to numerous particular Hopf algebras to deduce the long term properties of their associated Markov chains. Cases of particular interest include various dynamic storage allocation schemes, the rearrangement of phylogenetic trees, and models of rock-breaking. In addition to these practical applications, the connection between Markov chains and combinatorial Hopf algebras is expected to also contribute to the theory of the related algebraic combinatorics. The novel probabilistic viewpoint will likely motivate new variations of classical combinatorial Hopf algebras, and identify new subalgebras of the hyperoctahedral Solomon descent algebra. The computation of eigenvectors for the hyperoctahedral descent operators will then illuminate the structure of these new subalgebras, through the construction of idempotents. There will also be results for other branches of mathematics and theoretical physics where combinatorial Hopf algebras appear, including the representation theory of Lie groups over finite fields, Coxeter group theory, and quantum field theory. 本研究項目的目的是應用代數和組合數學來研究各種各樣的馬爾可夫鏈。馬爾可夫鍊是常用於統計物理學，生物信息學，經濟學和其他科學的隨機算法，用於模擬隨機過程（例如不同產品的需求變化）或從某概率分佈中抽樣。應用起來，最緊要是掌握需要多少算法步數,但在這方面,往往幾乎沒有理論準則。 針對這種情況，一些比較近期的研究集中在來自代數或幾何的馬爾可夫鏈。這些鏈比較容易分析,可以用確切公式表達其長期行為的許多特徵,例如所需的運行時間。雖然這些鏈科學比應用上的鏈簡單得多,但有辦法擴展部分的結果到類似的鏈。 本項目中馬爾可夫鏈的轉移概率源自組合霍普夫代數上面的兩種新的線性算子:置換下降算子和B型下降算子。置換下降算子所產生的馬爾科夫鏈模擬將組合論中的常見物件, 如排列、樹、圖形等, 隨機分解成幾部分，然後以不同的次序重組。B型下降算子產生的馬爾科夫鏈與之前所述的很相似,但在重組前對某些分解部分進行對合變換。 我們打算求這兩種新算子的特徵值和特徵向量。這將使用霍普夫代數的結構定理, 而所得到的公式將適用於所有組合霍普夫代數。 然後,我們將此公式應用於許多特定霍普夫代數，並且推斷其相關馬爾可夫鏈的極限行為。我們特別關注各種動態存儲分配方案，系統發育樹的重新排列和破碎模型。 除了這些實際應用之外，馬爾科夫鏈和組合霍普夫代數之間的聯繫也有助於相關代數組合的理論。新穎的概率觀點可能會激發古典組合霍普夫代數的新變化，或識別B型所羅門下降代數的新子代數。用於計算B型下降運算符的特徵向量的方法還可以提供這些新子代數的冪等，從而揭示其結構。 本項目的結果更會影響有限李群表示論、考克斯特群論、量子場論等應用到組合霍普夫代數的數學和理論物理學範疇。

22300017.label: Realisation of objectives
22300017.value: Objective 1 is completely settled. The conjectural spectrum and stationary distributions of both families of operators, as stated in the proposal, have all been confirmed as follows: For permuted descent operators, [1, Th. 2.7] showed that their eigenvalues and multiplicities are the same as their unpermuted counterpart. Theorem 4.11 in [1] devised a Markov chain out of an arbitrary permuted descent operator acting on an arbitrary Hopf algebra. Theorem 4.12 in [1] then proved that the stationary distribution of such chains are equal to those of their unpermuted counterparts. For hyperoctahedral descent operators, [2, Th. 17] gave an expression for their eigenvalues in terms of set-compositions and double-partitions. The main new ingredient of the proof is [2, Lem. 23]: the matrix for a hyperoctahedral descent operator on a cocommutative algebra is triangular in the PBW basis, and the diagonal entries (i.e. the eigenvalues) are easily computable. This step replaces, in the previous case of descent operators, the implicit construction of a basis of eigenvectors out of the PBW basis. Theorem 34 of [2] constructs a Markov chain out of an arbitrary hyperoctahedral descent operator acting on an arbitrary Hopf algebra. Theorem 35 obtained their stationary distributions - these are not equal to those of ordinary descent operator chains (assuming the degree 1 subspace is not fixed under the involution), but they do not depend on which hyperoctahedral descent operator is used. Objective 2 asked for eigenvector formulas for particular operators; two families of operators were analysed: In [1, Sec. 3], we find expressions for eigenvectors of the permuted “top or bottom to random” operators LeftTB2R, RightTB2R, LeftTB2R*, RightTB2R* and LeftRightTB2R. Each eigenvector is constructed out of elements of degree one, and elements in the kernel of certain coproducts. On commutative Hopf algebras, these operators agree with the previously-studied descent operator T/B2R, and our new formula provides more eigenvectors than in the previous study. In [2, Ths. 26, 27, 29], we construct eigenvectors for the hyperoctahedral riffle-shuffle operators BRiffle(a)+ and BRiffle(a)- for all values of a; the behaviour is different for odd and even values of a, which need to be treated separately. On a cocommutative algebra, our eigenvectors form a complete basis for the non-zero eigenspaces. As for ordinary riffle-shuffle operators, these are built from primitive elements, but for the hyperoctahedral case one must restrict to primitive elements that are invariant or negating under the associated involution. Objective 3 asked for the analysis of specific Markov chains using the eigenvalue and eigenvector formulas; three families of chains were analysed: Firstly, [1, Sec. 5] considered the RightTB2R chain on the Malvenuto-Reutenauer algebra of permutations, which describe the relative order of tasks on a to-do list. The stationary distribution is uniform. We produced a set of eigenvectors that we conjecture to be a full basis. Furthermore, the eigenvectors gave the expectations of a weighted enumeration of descents, peaks, and analogous longer patterns. Secondly, [1, Sec. 6] addressed the chains on binary trees (Loday-Ronco Hopf algebra) driven by LeftT/B2R. At each step of this chain, a coin is flipped: if it lands heads (resp. tails), the leftmost (resp. rightmost) vertex is removed, and then attached to a uniformly-chosen leaf. We find that its stationary distribution is given by the proportion of increasing trees. One eigenvector for each eigenvalue is expressed in terms of descendant and ancestor relationships. For the case of LeftT/B2R with q=1, we additionally obtained a recursive expression for the subdominant eigenvector, which gave an upper bound on the probability of the right subtree being empty. In [3], this algebra of binary trees is extended to planar trees which, when given different kinds of labels, produce new visualisations of generalised Sterling permutations and parking functions. The chains on these new algebras operate similarly. Thirdly, [2, Sec. 5] examined the action of BRiffle(a)+ and BRiffle(a)- on the signed shuffle algebra, for two different underlying involutions. These model card-shuffles where a deck is cut into a multinomially-distributed piles, then every alternate pile is either flipped over or rotated by 180 degrees, before all piles are riffled back together. Specialisation of the general formulas gave a complete basis for the non-zero eigenspaces in the language of Lyndon words. From these eigenvectors we obtained the expectation of an unconventional type of descent and the probability of having sign +1, after repeating these two types of shuffles. References: [1] The Eigenvalues of Permuted Descent Operators, and Markov Chains on Permutations and Trees, pdf under Section 8 of this report. [2] The Eigenvalues of Hyperoctahedral Descent Operators and Applications to Card-Shuffling, pdf under Section 8 of this report. [3] Hopf algebras of parking functions and decorated planar trees, pdf under Section 8 of this report.

22300017.label: Major findings and research outcome
22300017.value: This project defined two families of operators on combinatorial Hopf algebras: the permuted descent operators and the hyperoctahedral descent operators. The main results are: - a uniform expression for the eigenvalues and multiplicities of these two families of operators, - the construction of a Markov chain from the action of such operators on arbitrary combinatorial Hopf algebras under mild conditions, and a uniform expression of their stationary distributions. - a formula for the eigenvectors of the specific operators, namely LeftTB2R, RightTB2R, LeftTB2R*, RightTB2R*, LeftRightTB2R and BRiffle(a)+, BRiffle(a)- for all values of a. We specialised the above universal results to three classes of Markov chains corresponding to different algebras: a model of a weather-dependent to-do list (Malvenuto-Reutenauer algebra of permutations), remove-and-readd chains on binary trees (Loday-Ronco Hopf algebra), and riffle-shuffles which flip or rotate alternate piles (signed shuffle algebra). In each case, the eigenvector formulae gave bounds for the expected value or probability of interesting statistics or events.

22300017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
22300017.value: We suggest two main directions of further research. The first is to apply the dervied eigenvalue and eigenvector formulas to the various algebras of planar trees defined in one of the research outputs of this project. This will further generalise the analysis of Markov chains on binary trees that was carried out within this project. Trees are important in the study of phylogenetics in biology, and it was discovered during this project that various other combinatorial objects, such as Sterling permutations, can be encoded as trees. Thus a chain on planar trees would allow uniform analysis of Markov chains on a range of objects. The second research direction follows an idea from one of the undergraduates involved in this project: a new multivariate version of the dual graded graph theory may be a more general setting for studying the permuted, hyperoctahedral and other variants of top-or-bottom-to-random. Such study would begin with selecting suitable axioms for the definition of multivariate dual graded graphs, and proving their connection with combinatorial Hopf algebras. Then we may derive the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of various operators, and their composition laws, and analyse the associated Markov chains.

22300017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
22300017.value: Markov chains are simple random processes often implemented on computers as “random object generators”, e.g. to model a random particle configuration in statistical physics. An instructive example is a card-shuffle that cuts a deck into many piles, then riffles the piles together back into one pile - iterating the shuffle results in a random order of cards. Analogous break-and-recombine chains on graphs, trees or words can be formulated algebraically as the action of “descent operators” on “combinatorial Hopf algebras”. This project studied two extensions of descent operators: the “permuted descent operators” correspond to changing the order of the cut piles before riffling them together, whilst the “hyperoctahedral descent operators” flip or rotate the cut piles before riffling them together. We obtained a unified expression for all eigenvalues of these operators, and a formula for the eigenvectors for specific operators of additional interest; both results are applicable to all combinatorial Hopf algebras. This data gives important insight into the long-term behaviour of the chains, such as the mixing time, i.e. the number of steps required to achieve randomness. We then specialised our analysis to three particular algebras to examine their associated Markov chains in detail, deriving many probabilistic estimates.

22503117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22503117.value: In the past decades, global trade volumes have grown much faster than global GDP. The surge in global trade can not only be attributed to the global reduction of trade costs, but also to the widespread phenomenon of international fragmented production. Under fragmentation of production, more intermediate goods are traded between countries, and “double counted” in the gross trade volumes. The “double counting” of values of intermediate goods in gross trade, when the final product is re-exported, makes estimation of the traditional gravity equation based on gross trade volumes, as well as the implied welfare impact, inaccurate. To address this issue, I propose to build a multi-country, multi-sector general equilibrium model of international fragmented production with inter-country input-output (ICIO) linkage. In the model, there are gains from trade from both trade in intermediate goods and trade in final goods. By allowing the different trade elasticities for trade in intermediate goods and trade in final goods, a more precise evaluation of welfare gains from trade for each country can be carried out. The model will allow us to study the following: (1) The driving force of the differences between trade in intermediate goods and trade in final goods in the global trading system. (2) The trade elasticities for trade in intermediate goods and trade in final goods respectively, and their differences. (3) Corresponding gains from trade for each country when fragmentation of production is pervasive. (4) The welfare impacts of trade policies in the world under the international fragmentation of production. By studying the above topics, the proposed work helps us to understand more deeply the current world trading system. It is likely to lead to practical implications for the conduct of trade policies of countries, as fragmentation of production has become a key determinant of the current trade landscape. 在過去的數十年間，國際貿易的增長速度遠快於全球GDP的增長速度。除了國家間日益降低的貿易成本外，國家間生產與貿易的碎片化也是國際貿易快速增長的主因。隨著生產貿易碎片化，中間產品的貿易越來越多，但中間產品的價值在國際貿易額統計會被重復計算。 中間產品的價值除了在作為中間產品出口時被計入，在加工成最終產品並再度出口時會被再一次計入國際貿易額。因此，基於現有的貿易額統計，使用引力模型所估計出的貿易彈性，以及基於此彈性所估算的貿易收益都是不準確的。在此項目中，我將建立一個多國多行業，融入國家間的要素產出聯系的，生產貿易碎片化的一般均衡模型來解決這個問題。在此模型中，貿易收益不僅來自於最終產品貿易，也來自於中間產品貿易。在分別對中間產品和最終產品的貿易彈性做出估計後，我們可以對各國的貿易收益做出更準確的估算。 此模型可讓我們了解以下幾點：（1）在國際貿易體系中中間產品與最終產品貿易的不同；（2）中間產品貿易和最終產品貿易不同的貿易彈性；（3）在生產貿易碎片化的情境下各國的貿易收益；以及（4）在生產貿易碎片化的情境下，貿易政策的改變對貿易收益的影響。 隨著對以上問題的研究，本項目可幫助我們更深入的了解現有的國際貿易體系。隨著生產貿易碎片化在現有的國際貿易中不斷深化，本項目可以幫助各國更好的制定符合自身利益的貿易政策。

22503317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22503317.value: The auditors’ role is to plan and perform audit procedures and to express opinions on client firms’ compliance with the accounting standards. As an important institution in the financial reporting process (Francis et al., 2003; Wysocki, 2011), high-quality auditors increase financial reporting quality as reflected in several properties (DeFond and Zhang, 2014, p. 287). Francis et al. (2013) were the first to show that clients audited by the same office-level auditors have more comparable financial statements. This phenomenon is called auditor style. In this study, we seek to extend Francis et al. (2013) and investigate whether individual auditors have their own style by examining their clients’ financial statement comparability. Following Francis et al. (2013), we define individual auditor style as an individual auditor’s idiosyncratic approach to implement audit standards and enforcing accounting standards. Drawing on the literature, we propose two competing views on individual auditor style. On the one hand, the behavioral auditing literature suggests that an individual auditor has style as one’s judgement is affected by his/her distinct and nontransferable experience and ability (e.g., Libby and Luft 1993; Nelson and Tan, 2005). On the other hand, audit firms adopt several policies to standardize their audits (Ferguson et al., 2003; Francis et al., 2013) and therefore the individual auditor’s style should not be salient. As a result, it is ex ante unclear whether individual auditors have their own unique style as reflected in the comparability of their audited financial statements (individual auditor style hypothesis). We plan to further examine whether individual auditor style differs among disparate types of organizations (international Big Four versus local Big Six auditing firms) and audit expertise. We plan to take advantage of China’s unique setting and examine our research questions in the post-IFRS (international financial reporting standards) period. By doing so, this study will extend that of Francis et al. (2013) and the individual auditor literature and show whether individual auditors have a style as reflected in their comparability. This study will also advance our understanding on the role of the micro-level (individual auditor) rather than the macro-level institutions observed in the IFRS implementation process. Given that investors and financial analysts routinely use multiple methods to predict firm value, this study will also be of interest to practitioners. 22503317.label: Major findings and research outcome
22503317.value: We investigate whether individual auditors are associated with the comparability of their clients’ financial statements, based on a sample of Chinese companies audited by 10 large audit firms. We first confirm the existence of office-level effect on clients’ financial statement comparability (Francis et al., 2014) in China. More importantly, we demonstrate that individual auditors have an incremental effect on comparability, beyond the office-level effect. We also find that the style of individual auditors is stronger when they are affiliated with Big 4 audit firms (compared to non-Big 4 large audit firms) and when they are industry experts. In addition, two possible channels of enhanced comparability are identified: (i) a client’s accounting flexibility, which provides opportunities; and (ii) individual auditor’s characteristics such as age, position, and academic degree, which affect auditors’ abilities to exert influence. Our results are robust to alternative comparability and industry specialist measures, to various sampling methods, and to corrections for potential endogeneity problem.

22503317.value: We may consider individual auditor data to examine how auditors' demographic characteristics influence audit outcomes.

22603717.label: Project Objectives
22603717.value: To develop a culturally appropriate adventure-based cognitive behavioural intervention program in a class setting for Chinese university students in Hong Kong To test the effectiveness of this program in improving various mental health outcomes for Chinese university students in Hong Kong To test the maintenance effects of this program at 3-month follow-up assessment

To test the effectiveness of this program in improving various mental health outcomes for Chinese university students in Hong Kong
To test the maintenance effects of this program at 3-month follow-up assessment

22603717.label: Realisation of objectives
22603717.value: Objective 1 has been 100% achieved. A culturally appropriate adventure-based cognitive behavioural intervention (aCBI) program has been developed in the form of an interdisciplinary general education course “Improving Mental Health for University Students” in Hong Kong Baptist University, which was offered 3 hours on a weekly basis for 13 weeks. The program consisted of three components. The first component comprised six lectures which provided an introduction of the basic concepts of adjusting to university life, the mental health of university students, theories on stress and coping, and a variety of CBI skills. The lectures were delivered to the entire class, in which the teaching approach involved briefing and debriefing, case demonstration, group sharing, in-class exercises and homework assignments. The second component comprised 5 workshops, which allowed the students to practice the cognitive behavioral skills that were learned in the lectures to manage their own daily life stress. The students were divided into two groups with each group led by a university counselor or social worker. The workshops were conducted in the form of mini-lectures, and offered group activities, opportunities for sharing and discussion, and in-class exercises and homework assignments. The third component involved adventure-based activities, including a one-day camp of adventure training and various adventure-based warm-up activities for 40 minutes before each workshop took place. The one-day camp training was designed following the suggestions of briefing-activities-debriefing proposed by Human (2006). Specifically, safety measures were demonstrated, and information of the upcoming activities were given in the briefing session. Activities included warm-up exercises and high-altitude ropes challenge courses, such as the Giant’s Ladder and High V. At the end of the camp, an invitation was extended to the students to participate in a 1-hour debriefing session led by a counselor or social worker to collectively reflect on their experience and learnings at the camp. The briefing session focused on reviewing the application of the CBI skills in the adventure activities. Examples of the review questions in the debriefing session were: (1) What is the most impressive moment for you today? (2) What was your body feeling during these activities? What did you do with that feeling? (3) What did you learn from the experiences today? How to apply this to your future life? The adventure-based warm-up activities before each workshop included trust, problem-solving and team building exercises, which encouraged the students to build and strengthen relationships and facilitate communication during the workshop. The lecture notes were shared with the adventure trainers so that they could integrate the CBI skills in the activity design and a short debriefing at the end of each activity. Workshop facilitators were also invited to observe students’ involvements in the adventure-based warm-up activities so that they could link these activities with the workshop content. A case demonstration video called “Sorrow (煩惱)” were produced to demonstrate how to use a variety of cognitive behavioral skills to cope with university stress. An e-learning platform were created for students to complete and submit in-class exercises and homework assignments and for teachers to give comments and feedbacks on students’ assignments. A 3-session online course was also developed on FutureLearn to enhance students’ e-learning experiences. A total of 386 undergraduate students took this course in 9 classes. A showcase video of this course can be found at https://drive.google.com/file/d/0Bw-fqeTPi3Wbd2lCRXZ0VjVremM/view?ts=59f96df1&resourcekey=0-ApjZqdJyfd1NKzVRAfTTOg Objective 2 & 3 have been 100% achieved by a pilot study and a randomized controlled trial to test the program effectiveness. Students were asked to fill in an online questionnaire at pre-test when they were enrolling the course, at post-test when they immediately complete the course, and a follow-up test three months after they completed the course. In the pilot study, a total of 217 students successfully enrolled the course. A total of 193, 124 and 78 online questionnaires were collected at pre-, post- and 3-month follow-up tests for data analysis. In the randomized controlled trial, a total of 751 students enrolled the course and 207 were excluded due to ineligibility. The rest of the students were randomized into the experimental group and control group. A total of 197 students successfully enrolled the course as the experimental group. A total of 197, 126 and 80 data were collected at pre-, post- and 3-month follow-up tests for the experimental group, and 347, 71 and 57 data were collected at pre-, post- and 3-month follow-up tests for the control group, respectively.

22603717.label: Major findings and research outcome
22603717.value: The results of the pilot study showed that students’ negative emotions and thoughts, psychological distress, perceived distress and depressive symptoms significantly reduced, and their positive emotions and thoughts significantly increased immediately after taking the course. The positive effects can be maintained for three months after participation. Preliminary evidence has shown that the integration of cognitive behavioral intervention and adventure training in a class setting might be an effective and feasible approach for the mental health counseling of university students. The positive effects of the aCBI program has been further confirmed by a randomized controlled trial study. In the RCT study, results of the multilevel modeling analyses showed that time  treatment interaction effects were found for all the outcome variables: there were significantly greater improvements in negative thoughts and positive thoughts, negative emotions and positive emotions, psychological distress and perceived stress, depression and resilience across time among participants in the experimental group when compared to their counterparts in the control group. The Cohen’s d values showed that the changes on all outcome variables, except sense making coping, in the experimental group achieved small to moderate effect sizes from pre-test to post-test, and from pre-test to follow-up test. The positive effects can be maintained for at least 3 months. These results further demonstrated aCBI program in a class setting as an effective mental health counselling approach not only to improving their mental health, but also to enhancing their resilience for university students in Hong Kong.

22603717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
22603717.value: Due to the outbreak of COVID-19 pandemic, it is impossible to deliver the adventure training in the course. Thus, the PI has revised the course proposal by removing the adventure training to sustain this course in Hong Kong Baptist University (HKBU). A revised course proposal has been submitted to the General Education Office in Oct. 2021 to apply for the general education course for the category of Healthy Lifestyle for approval. If approved, the new course will be delivered to HKBU students in AY2022/23 Semester 1. Data collection can be continued to test the course effectiveness of the cognitive behavioral intervention program for Hong Kong university students in a class setting. Another direction for potential development is to collaborate with local NGOs by adapting the aCBI program to other forms, such as group work or program, to work with young people.

22603717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
22603717.value: This study developed an adventure-based cognitive behavioral intervention (aCBI) program and tests its effectiveness in improving the mental health of Chinese university students in Hong Kong. A total of 464 undergraduate students participated in an aCBI program in the form of an interdisciplinary general education course in a university in Hong Kong. A battery of standardized online questionnaires was administered to the students before joining and upon completion of the course, and at a 3-month follow-up test. The participants showed a significant reduction of psychological distress, perceived stress, depressive symptoms, and negative thoughts and emotions and a significant increase of positive thoughts and emotions, and resilience upon immediate completion of the program. The positive effects maintained at the 3-month follow-up test. The results showed that the integration of cognitive behavioral intervention and adventure training in a class setting might be an effective and feasible approach for the mental health counseling of university students. It is suggested to including aCBI program in the general education curriculum in the local universities in Hong Kong to improve university students’ mental health.

22604217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22604217.value: China’s low-carbon city initiative, launched in 2010, is one of the most important climate change responses from the world’s largest carbon polluter. Departing from conventional top-down governance approaches, the initiative aims to encourage bottom-up climate policy experimentation without imposing strict rules for local governments to follow. Under the initiative, a total of 36 cities have been tasked to experiment with innovative responses to decarbonisation. Despite its significance as a climate change response, the initiative as well as the participating low-carbon cities have attracted little research attention. Consequently, climate policy experimentation at the local level remains a poorly understood component of China’s climate governance, which has been, by and large, analysed from a rather narrow perspective, emphasising the dominant role of the central government over local authorities and non-state actors. This study aims to address this neglected yet important research area. The proposed mixed-method approach has two parts. First, to gain an overview of bottom-up climate policy experimentation and the performance of the initiative, the research team will conduct a comparative study to develop a database of policy experiments in all low-carbon cities. The following data will be collected: (1) the timing, location, and local contexts of the experimentation; (2) the specifications of the experimentation, such as policy instruments and targets; and (3) the actors. The database will allow us to identify patterns of climate policy experiments and how these patterns correlate with the geographical, socioeconomic, and political characteristics of low-carbon cities. Second, the research team will conduct in-depth case studies in five low-carbon cities (Baoding, Shenzhen, Hangzhou, Jilin, and Urumqi) to examine the different approaches to climate experimentation. Through semi-structured interviews, the research team will focus on: (1) the roles and visions of local stakeholders in climate policy experimentation; (2) the challenges and barriers in fulfilling these roles and visions and how they have been overcome; and (3) how the actions and visions of local stakeholders are embedded in institutional structures. The findings will be conceptualised into five different models of low-carbon experimentation and their implications for authoritarian environmentalism theory will be explored. This three-year study will not only add to the practical understanding of what works, why it works, and how climate governance can be improved in China, but also advance the field of climate governance by introducing new perspectives where bottom-up climate experimentation coexists with top-down governance in an authoritarian rather than democratic context. 中國是全球最大的碳排放國。中央政府2010年開展國家低碳城市計劃以控制碳排放。該計劃不是傳統自上而下的治理方式，而是採用自下而上的方式鼓勵地方政府進行氣候政策實驗。到2016年為止，已有三十六個城市成功參與。但關於該計劃何其參與城市的研究少之又少，直接影響我們對中國氣候政策實驗的認識，也導致現有文獻過於強調中央政府的作用。本項目將研究這個重要課題。 本項目有兩個組成部分。第一，為了全面了解中國地方氣候政策實驗與實施請看，研究小組將建立一個低碳城市政策實驗數據庫，並將收集一下數據：（1）政策實驗的時間和地點；（2）實驗詳情,包括政策工具與目標；（3）利益相關者。第二，研究小組將在五個低碳城市（保定，深圳，杭州，吉林，烏魯木齊）進行深入案例研究。通過深度訪談，研究：（1）利益相關者在政策使用中的作用和願景；（2）履行任務和願景的挑戰和障礙，以及如何克服挑戰和障礙；（3）影響利益相關者的製度結構。 本研究為其三年，將會增加我們對中國氣候治理的有效性與實際可行性的了解，從而得知如何改善中國氣​​候治理。同時也會對氣候治理理論引進新觀點，尤其是氣候政策實驗和環境專制兩種的關係。

22604217.label: Realisation of objectives
22604217.value: Objective 1: This part of the project involved the collection of policy documents through desktop research. The task has been completed with success. In addition to collecting climate policy information from 42 low-carbon pilot cities, as stated in the original research plan, the team collected information from other Chinese cities. This expanded dataset allowed us to conduct comparative analysis between the official “low-carbon” cities and other cities in China. Objectives 2-4: This part of the project involved fieldwork and interviews. Thanks to the generous support by the RGC, we were able to meet, indeed exceed, the original targets. We conducted multiple rounds of fieldwork in 2018, 2019, and 2020, despite the immense and unexpected challenges posed by COVID-19. The original plan was to conduct fieldwork in 5 cities. We were able to study 8 cities by the end of the project (Guangzhou, Jilin, Qingdao, Changchun, Foshan, Zhuhai, Zhongshan, and Shantou). The main reason of expanding the number of field sites was to examine the different experiences of climate experimentation more comprehensively. These cities were visited to study different forms of climate experimentation: Guangzhou and Jilin (low-carbon city pilots), Qingdao (international eco-city), Changchun (photovoltaics for poverty alleviation pilot), Foshan, Zhuhai, Zhongshan and Shantou (near zero-carbon pilots). Semi-structured interviews were the main strategy of data collection. A total of 185 interviews were conducted. To recruit the informants, we first identified the main stakeholders of the pilots by desktop research and personal networks. These stakeholders include government apparatuses (provincial, prefecture/municipal, district/village), non-governmental organizations, research institutes, and companies. Furthermore, we interviewed local residents and villagers to learn their experience with the impact of climate experimentation. The objective of the interviews was to understand: (1) the roles and visions of local officials and other stakeholders in climate policy experimentation; (2) the planning, design, and management of climate experiments; (3) the key challenges and barriers that hinder the stakeholders from fulfilling their roles or achieving their expectation and the actions taken to overcome these barriers; (4) how actions and visions of stakeholders are embedded in multileveled institutional structures; and (5) the socio-economic impact of climate experimentation. Moreover, the funding enabled a Research Assistant/PhD student to serve as an intern in an eco-city Qingdao Sino-German Ecopark. Through participatory observation, we were able to collect first-hand evidence about the success and failure of climate experimentation, as well as the strategies, plans, and actions taken by stakeholders. Data was also collected from multiple secondary sources, including official documents and reports, media news, and websites. The collection of rich empirical data allowed us to progress the theorization work. A number of new discoveries about China’s climate experimentation have been made (please see next section for more details). Objective 5: This objective aims to develop the theory of authoritarian environmentalism. Departing from the conventional analysis of authoritarian governance, this project illustrates how China’s climate governance is not simply about hierarchical central-local relations, but also consists of a mixture of horizontal and vertical governance interactions. Furthermore, climate experimentation, as an important policymaking mechanism in China, does not adhere to the notion of non-participatory and elite-led policymaking typically associated with authoritarianism. Experimental practices are often conducted through local and international policy networks, which provide important solutions to mobilization, organization, and collective action. Objective 6: Policy recommendation is another objective of the study. Drawing on both the empirical evidence and conceptual insights, we developed several suggestions to improve the coordination of climate policy experiments in China. These include providing better support for local experimentation to avoid overburdening local governments, lengthen the experimentation period to prevent pressuring local governments into chasing quick results, and improve transparency by releasing local experimentation performance to the public regularly, and integrate climate policy innovation into the cadre target responsibility to strengthen the political incentive for local experimentation. Furthermore, the findings highlight the political merits of taking a more inclusive and just approach to climate experimentation, especially in resolving territorial conflicts. Our recommendation for policymakers is to incorporate the tripartite framework of justice (distributional, recognitional, and procedural) into climate experimentation projects. Objective 7: The objective is to publish 5-6 journal articles by the end of the project. This goal has been achieved. At the moment, 8 journal articles from this project have been published. These papers have been published in well-regarded international journals, such as Cities, Geoforum, Global Environmental Change, and Environmental Planning and Management. Furthermore, four papers are currently under review, bringing the final total output of the project to 12 articles. Furthermore, the PI has trained a PhD student who completed a thesis on climate experimentation in China. The title of the thesis is “China's Eco-city Initiative: Multilevel Governance, International Cooperation, and Climate Governance Experimentation”.

22604217.label: Major findings and research outcome
22604217.value: First, international cooperation is an important element of urban climate experimentation in China. International cooperation is enabled by Chinese multilevel governance, which allows the (re)shaping of the (inter)national visions at the local level, according to local conditions. At the same time, international cooperation is shaped by political economy forces, and the priorities of powerful local or foreign actors may limit the scope for collaboration and distorted the original purpose. In general, the discussion on climate experimentation cannot be confined to domestic actors; it must take into account the interactions between Chinese and foreign actors, as international cooperation plays a key role in these projects. Second, climate experimentation is primarily an urban phenomenon and therefore is strongly influenced by the modernization of urban governance. This involves the modernization of hierarchical governance to enhance top-down control and the modernization of horizontal governance to improve state-society cooperation. Furthermore, climate experimentation in China is closely related to urban expansion, which is a controversial process where territorial conflicts of differing interests and objectives become manifest. Therefore, climate experimentation also manifests a territorial political process, where multifaceted bargaining arenas (such as administrative adjustment and land compensation) contribute to the smooth operation of climate experimentation by identifying and resolving potential territorial conflicts. In short, climate experimentation must be understood from an urban governance perspective. Third, while climate experimentation in Western liberal democracies is typically a fragmented and decentralised process characterised by municipal voluntarism, climate experimentation in China can be understood as a hierarchical process. The central government has established numerous mechanisms to incentivize and steer local climate experimentation. However, there are limits to these steering mechanisms. Consequently, understanding the limitation of hierarchical control, as well as local processes such as leadership support, communities of practice, and the alignment of interests, are important in making sense of the local variation of climate experimentation. Fourth, climate experimentalism is not always associated with radical innovation but is also characterized by incrementalism. Climate experiments are the means whereby the central government gathers information about what works and what does not through local experiences and then refines the policy in a step-by-step fashion. This is reflected in the frequent changes in policy that aim to address perceived policy failures and popularize successful policy lessons. However, decentralising policy experimentation pushes the burden of policy development and the risk of failure on to local governments, and thus may become a source of central-local conflict.

22604217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
22604217.value: This project reveals the complexity of climate experimentation in China. It opens new research directions where a wide variety of actors (state/non-state, local/international) as important drivers have been incorporated into the research framework of Chinese climate governance. More empirical studies are needed to generate further insights. Whether the governance models exemplified by the cities we studied can be extended to other cities in China remains to be discussed. Furthermore, while climate experimentation is a global phenomenon, it is also deeply rooted in local realities. As such, more international or comparative studies are needed to fully understand how climate experimentation is structured in different political economic settings and other place-specific characteristics. Last but not least, it is the task of academics to challenge the dominant climate policy discourse by highlighting the saliency of justice issues. In particular, integrating the socio-environmental justice perspective to the study of climate experimentation, such as by engaging with the fields of just transition, energy justice, and climate justice, is important as climate experimentation may create new or worsen existing social inequality.

22604217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
22604217.value: Climate experimentation plays an important role in China’s low-carbon transition. This project comprehensively examined different types of climate experimentation at different locations. The key findings are: (1) international cooperation is an important element of urban climate experimentation in China. Therefore, the discussion on climate experimentation cannot be confined to domestic actors; it must take into account the interactions between Chinese and foreign actors. (2) Climate experimentation is primarily an urban phenomenon and therefore is strongly influenced by the modernization of urban governance. Therefore, climate experimentation must be understood from an urban governance perspective. (3) While climate experimentation in Western liberal democracies is typically a fragmented and decentralised process characterised by municipal voluntarism, climate experimentation in China can be understood as a hierarchical process. (4) Climate experimentalism is not always associated with radical innovation but is also characterized by incrementalism. Climate experiments are the means whereby the central government gathers information about what works and what does not through local experiences and then refines the policy in a step-by-step fashion. These new discoveries lead to the development of several policy recommendations to improve the performance of climate experimentation in China.

23500417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23500417.value: Over the past few decades, waves of trade liberalization have transformed global economies enormously. The episode in China, coupled with a sustained period of miraculous growth, has attracted particular attention from international communities and academic institutions. While many studies have examined the effects of China’s trade liberalization on industry and firm productivity (e.g., Brandt et al., 2012), there is little micro-level evidence on how individual firms respond to trade-induced competition. In this paper, we propose to study whether and how trade liberalization in China, which officially began upon its accession to the World Trade Organization (WTO) in 2001, has lead firms to transform their operational strategies and growth routes. We hypothesize two broad forms of transformation that firms can potentially undertake. First, firms can transform their organizational structures to reduce risk and uncertainty that heighten upon trade liberalization. Vertically, they can integrate product lines along the supply chain to reduce the volatility of input costs and to enhance operational efficiency (Williamson, 1971). Horizontally, they can change their sectoral exposure by extending businesses to other segments. This diversifying activity broadens the opportunity set for firms and reduces firm-specific risks (Amihud and Lev, 1981). It also facilitates firms to exploit investment opportunities by forming an internal capital market (Shin and Stulz, 1998). Second, firms can transform their endogenous growth modes by altering investment in production factors. They can develop new technologies to preserve market shares from intense competition (Aghion et al., 2005). They can also adjust investment in physical capital and improve the quality of human capital by providing training to labor (Becker, 1962). Using a comprehensive census dataset on industrial firms in China between 1998 and 2007, we can construct the various measures for corporate transformation precisely and we will test the hypothesis using a difference-in-differences specification. As we focus on a large spectrum of corporate policies that trade-induced competition could potentially shape, the paper will add to the broad literature on trade, firm performance, and social welfare, especially to the recent literature on the micro mechanisms that underlie the social and economic changes (e.g., Bloom et al., 2016). Finally, we will explore the heterogeneous responses of firms in terms of state ownership and regional marketization. This will enable us to draw some useful inferences on the roles of political influences and institutional features in shaping corporate transformation and will provide important implications for China’s current economic and institutional reforms. 在過去的幾十年間，貿易自由化給全球經濟帶來了巨大的變化。而其中中國的貿易開放，在給中國帶來增長奇跡的同時也吸引了大量的業界和學界關注。盡管已有相關研究關注中國的貿易開放對企業生產力和行業發展的整體影響，仍然僅有較少研究關注企業個體在具體轉型上的策略。因此，本研究旨在從微觀層面探索中國加入世界貿易組織後給企業轉型帶來的影響。具體來說，本研究將探討企業在兩類道路上的轉型策略。其一，企業如何通過改變自身的組織模式（例如，縱向整合產業線、提高運營效率；或跨行業並購實現多元化經營）來降低貿易自由化帶來的風險和不確定性。其二，企業如何通過改變內在生產要素，如提高人力資源質素和加強創新科技的開發和使用，來促進增長。本研究將利用中國國家統計局工業普查數據庫、通過雙差分模型來估算貿易競爭給企業各種轉型策略帶來的影響。研究也將進一步探索不同行業、不同市場不同類型的企業受貿易競爭影響的差異性。

23500417.label: Realisation of objectives
23500417.value: In this project, all the three objectives have been fully achieved. First, to identify the causal impact of trade-induced competition on various forms of corporate transformation, we use China's WTO accession in 2001 as a plausibly exogenous shock to industry competition to establish the causality. As the milestone of China's trade liberalization, its WTO accession had led to the reductions of import tariffs across a range of industries to a relatively low level. Since there is a huge heterogeneity in import tariffs prior to the accession, industries with higher pre-WTO tariffs experience larger subsequent rate reductions, and are hence forced to contend with greater product market competition as a result of import penetration. Therefore, we differentiate firms by their exposures to the competitive shocks, assign them into the treatment (control) group if they operate in industries with higher (lower) pre-WTO import tariffs, and employ a difference-in-differences strategy to examine the causal effect of product market competition on corporate transformation. Specifically, we examine whether trade-induced competition affects (1) the rate of privatization in China and (2) foreign ownership of domestically-owned private firms. Given that corporate ownership structure is a fundamental part of business organization, understanding corporate transformation along these dimensions could help delineate a strategically important view about firms' responses to heightened competition. Second, we explore heterogeneous responses of firms' ownership changes in the following ways. (1) we examine whether the effect of trade-induced competition on ownership changes is more pronounced for firms that are lagged further behind the advanced economy in their technological development, operational efficiency and productivity. (2) we examine whether the effect of trade-induced competition on ownership changes is more pronounced when firms rely more on external finance. (3) we also assess whether the impact of competition on private and foreign ownership varies with the development of market and legal institutions, measured by regional marketization index and sub-indexes. Third, regarding policy implications for economic and institutional reforms in China, we have identified product market competition as an important determinant of privatization and foreign ownership dynamics. Therefore, our evidence sheds light on the potential configuration of competition policy in order to deepening the privatization and internationalization process.

23500417.label: Major findings and research outcome
23500417.value: In the first part of the project, we identify product market competition as an important driver for privatization decisions. This leads to a paper that receives a Revise and Revise decision at Management Science. In this paper, we find that state-owned enterprises (SOEs) subject to greater competitive shocks introduce more private ownership. The responses are stronger when SOEs operate in industries with greater technology or productivity gaps from frontier economies, or have excess costs that impose larger fiscal burdens on local governments. The findings are consistent with the incentives of politicians to boost economic growth for potential career development and to shed off burdens when rents decreased. In the second part of the project, we documents a causal effect of trade-induced competition on the ownership dynamics of domestic private firms (i.e., whether they introduce foreign vs. state ownership to help with the transformation). This leads to a paper that receives a Revise and Resubmit decision at the Journal of Development Economics. In this paper, we find that domestic private firms that are more affected by competitive shock experience a larger relative increase in their foreign shareholdings compared to those less affected. However, there is no significant changes in the state ownership. We also find a stronger relative effect among firms with a greater demand for external financing and technology, which indicates the strategic role of foreign shareholdings in empowering domestic firms to obtain financing and new technologies in a competitive market.

23500417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
23500417.value: In the future, we can explore more dimensions of corporate transformation beyond ownership dynamics. For example, whether competition affects the innovation strategy of firms - are they more likely to take conservative approaches by exploiting existing knowledge or are they pushed to become more explorative by developing technologies that utilize more frontier knowledge beyond firms' existing knowledge pool and that are more likely to lead to significant breakthroughs? Moreover, we can leverage on the findings of the existing research concerning ownership transformation to examine whether the innovation strategies vary with ownership dynamics in face of greater competition. To pursue this research, we need to collect detailed data on the patents of Chinese firms, including the citations they made. Then, we can construct specific measures to gauge different innovation strategies to examine the proposed research.

23500417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
23500417.value: In this project, we examine whether and how firms respond to greater product market competition. Trade liberalization, globalization, and privatization are remarkable trends in the recent decades. It is almost unavoidable for firms to compete with others, either domestically or globally. Hence, in this research, we examine whether firms change their ownership dynamics to cope with greater competition, and whether such changes could help explain the contemporaneous privatization wave as well. By establishing a causal relationship among these important economic trends, the research can help the audience develop a deeper understanding on the interactions between macro forces and micro policies, and cast relevant policy implications for both firms and authorities.
