23600017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23600017.value: The 21st century has marked an unprecedented era in the history of translation in China. Under the “Going out Policy”, translating Chinese culture into English is considered as an essential means of promoting China’s soft power. Chinese institutions’ efforts in translating Chinese culture actually started from the 1950s, but what is different in the new millennium is that more and more Chinese works are translated under a new form of patronage, that is, joint patronage from both Chinese and Western institutions. For example, among others, “CPG China Library” (中國現當代文化經典文庫), so far the most ambitious Chinese-English translation project, is under joint patronage of China Publishing Group Corp. (CPG) 中國出版集團, China’s largest and most influential publishing group, and leading Western publishers such as Cambridge University Press and Princeton University Press. Why is there a change of the form of patronage? What are the advantages and disadvantages of joint patronage? Will the influence of Chinese patrons be diluted by the involvement of the Western patrons? As Western patrons may have different purposes and criteria of translation, conflicts of opinions are inevitable. How can the Chinese and Western patrons resolve the conflicts as well as other challenges joint patronage may bring about? Will the translators get more freedom or more restrictions under joint patronage? These are indeed very important issues in the field of translation studies but still remain unsolved. This research attempts to solve these issues and have an in-depth investigation on joint patronage in translating Chinese culture into English on the basis of a case study of the gigantic project “CPG China Library”, which, launched in 2014, involves the translation of 500 Chinese scholarly/literary works. Through analyzing the latest first-hand materials, interviewing Chinese and Western patrons, translators, editors and other agents involved, and describing the process of producing the first two translations of “CPG China Library”, this research project attempts to provide a theoretical framework on joint patronage and fill the gap in the research on patronage. In addition to contributing to the scholarship in translation studies, this research will provide insights for Chinese and Western patrons, translators and editors into the practical issues that may arise in the process of translation under joint patronage. 二十一世紀是中國翻譯史上一個前所未有的時代。隨著中國政府“走出去”戰略的實施，中國文化英譯成為發展中國軟實力的一個重要舉措。早在二十世紀五十年代，中國有關出版機構就已經致力於向海外翻譯中國文化，但在新的世紀，越來越多的中文著作則是在一種新的贊助形式下進行，即中國與西方國家的有關機構的聯合贊助 (joint patronage)。“中國現當代文化經典文庫”為迄今最大型的中英翻譯計劃，該項目就是在中國最大及最有影響力的出版機構中國出版集團與西方重要的出版機構聯合贊助下進行的。這些西方出版機構包括著名的劍橋大學出版社、普林斯頓大學出版社等。為什麼會出現贊助形式的改變？聯合贊助有什麼優缺點？中國贊助機構的影響力會否因此而削弱？西方贊助者會有不同的翻譯目的及原則，與中方贊助者在觀念上的衝突自然難以避免。中西方贊助者如何應對這些衝突以及聯合贊助帶來的其他挑戰？在聯合贊助下，譯者會有更大的自由還是更多的局限？這些都是翻譯研究中未得到探討的重要問題。本研究將針對這些問題，通過個案研究對中國文化英譯的聯合贊助現象進行深入探討。選擇的個案是“中國現當代文化經典文庫”， 這一大型項目於二〇一四年啟動，涉及五百種中文學術或文學著作的翻譯。本研究通過分析最新的一手資料，採訪中西方贊助機構的負責人、譯者、編輯以及其他相關人士，考查該項目最初兩部譯作的翻譯過程，以期在理論層面剖析聯合贊助這一新現象，填補贊助問題研究方面的空白。除此之外，本研究也會對中西方贊助者、譯者及編輯解決跨文化、跨語言的文化生產之下的聯合贊助翻譯中出現的實際問題有一定的啟示意義。

23600017.label: Realisation of objectives
23600017.value: I initially planned to study the first two “cultural products” of “CPG China Library”, that is, the English versions of The History of Famine Relief in China (中國救荒史) and Chinese Culture and Army (中國文化與中國的兵), which should have been published by September 2017. But from the translators and editors, I got to know that the date of submission of the translations to the publisher was postponed first to the end of December 2018, and then to the end of September 2019. (The two books were finally published in September 2020.) Because of the such an unexpected situation, I have decided to achieve my research objectives through investigating not only “CPG China Library”, but also two other important translation projects, namely “Culture and Civilization of China Series” (CCC project) (中國文化與文明叢書), a project under joint patronage of China International Publishing Group (CIPG) and Yale University Press, and “Chinese Literature Overseas Dissemination Project” (中國文學海外傳播工程), which is under joint patronage of Beijing Normal University, the Confucius Institute at University of Oklahoma, and the University of Oklahoma Press. Such an adjustment has led to even better achievement of the research objectives and more fruitful research outcome. Objective 1: To develop a theoretical framework on joint patronage in translation through a case study on “CPG China Library”. The study indicates that joint patronage is a new form of patronage, which involves two or more patrons (either individuals or institutions) generally from both the source culture (SL) and target culture (TC), that offer financial support or use their influence to support a translation activity. Translation under joint patronage involves the agents including patrons and professionals (editors, critics, scholars, etc.) from both source culture and target culture, translators, and sometimes also writers. The close collaboration among different agents including the institutions, translators, writers and editors may ensure the full use of their tremendous cultural, social and symbolic capital, realize the greatest potentials possible from them, and enhance the quality of translation and its acceptance in the Western book market. During this process, the cultural, social and symbolic capital different agents already have may be further increased or even multiplied. Therefore, this is a fruitful and win-win cooperation which may benefit both sides and all the agents involved. Objective 2: To examine the procedure of translation under joint patronage through a case study on the first two “cultural products” of “CPG China Library”. I have interviewed Dr. Gao Jianwu, the translator of The History of Famine Relief in China (中國救荒史), Mr. Wei Lingcha, the then Chief Publishing Officer of China Publishing Group Corp. at USA, Mr. Li Zhenguo, the former Editor-in-Chief at the Foreign Language Press, Prof. Taiping Chang, the former Executive Chief Editor of the CCC project, Prof. Liu Hongtao of Beijing Normal University and Prof. Jonathan Stalling of University of Oklahoma many times, and have got to know the detailed procedures of translation under joint patronage. The study indicates that the patrons and professionals from both the source culture and target culture not only have close collaboration in terms of the selection of appropriate translation materials and appropriate translators, but also have close collaboration during the whole process of translating, revising and editing. With a better understanding of the Western market, the publishers and editors from the target culture generally are responsible for distribution and promotion of the published works. Objective 3: To analyse the translation methods used and whether such methods are more conducive to Western readers' acceptance of the translated works. I have analysed the translation methods used in several representative translations produced under joint patronage, including the translations of The History of Famine Relief in China (中國救荒史), Key Concepts in Chinese Philosophy (中國古典哲學概念範疇要論) and Chinese Calligraphy (中國書法藝術), and found that translators generally work together with the editors from the target culture (sometimes also with the writer) on the translation so as to make sure that the most appropriate translation methods are used and the translations are accessible to the target readers. For example, when translating Chinese Calligraphy (中國書法藝術), the translators have made necessary adaptations, which include considerable omissions and additions, so as to make sure that the translation would be well received by the Western readers. In addition to the hard work of the translators and editors at the Chinese side, the team at Yale University Press further improved the quality of the translation and made the book more accessible to Western readers. Objective 4: To explore the advantages and disadvantages of joint patronage in translating Chinese culture to the outside world. The study indicates that joint patronage can to a great extent remedy the shortcomings of sole patronage and make a difference in introducing Chinese culture to the Western world. The translations under the patronage of one Chinese institution have three major shortcomings: 1) the translated works may give Western readers an impression that such translations are merely propaganda; 2) the Chinese publishers are unfamiliar with the needs of target readers and the norms of the target culture; 3) Chinese publishers are not knowledgeable about the book market in the West. Because of the involvement of the agents in the target culture, who are more familiar with the target readers and target culture and the Western book market, the three shortcomings can be well overcome. The translation as a result of the co-operation between native and foreign translators/patrons/professionals will become an amalgam of different “personalized social and cultural histories”, the result of clashes, negotiations, and mediations between different ideologies and poetics. In this process, the translation may gain greater immunity, tenacity and vitality to survive in the foreign land. Objective 5: To investigate possible conflicts of ideologies and poetics within joint patronage and to identify the mechanisms through which such conflicts are resolved. The study indicates that the patrons and professionals from the source culture and target culture do have conflicts of ideologies and poetics, but these conflicts can be resolved through discussions and negotiations. According to Taiping Chang, the Executive Chief Editor, when she represented Yale in working with the Chinese colleagues, differences could always be resolved “amicably”. For example, discussions about the map of China (including the borders, islands and provinces) lasted for several weeks, but the issue was finally resolved to both sides’ satisfaction. Objective 6: To provide research-informed insights of practical relevance to publishers, policy-makers and other agents engaged in joint-patronage translation projects. This project has provided significant research-informed insights of practical relevance to publishers, policy-makers and other agents in finding the most appropriate means of introducing Chinese culture and literature to the Western world. The study indicates that, compared with sole patronage, joint patronage is a better form of introducing and translating Chinese culture for the Western audience, and can to a great extent remedy the shortcomings of sole patronage. Objective 7: To make contribution to the research literature in a hitherto very under-researched field. This is the first project which raised the issue related to joint patronage in the field of translation studies. This research has provided a definition on joint patronage, developed a theoretical framework on it, and filled a gap in the study of patronage and joint patronage in the field of translation studies.

23600017.label: Major findings and research outcome
23600017.value: The study demonstrates that, compared with sole patronage, joint patronage is a better form of introducing and translating Chinese culture for the Western audience. Translation, which involves communication between two different cultures, will be ideally carried out by agents from both sides. The change from sole patronage to joint patronage in translating Chinese literature into English is a change from unilateral communication to bilateral communication, from monologue to dialogue. A bilateral communication or dialogue between two cultures will be more effective in facilitating mutual understanding and cultural exchanges. The translated works as the result of discussion, negotiation and mediation of the different agents involved may gain greater immunity and vitality, and thus have a better chance to survive in the target literary system. This research proposal originally intended to produce only two academic articles, but it turns out that seven research articles have been published. Among these publications, the following two were published in leading international journals listed in A&HCI and SSCI: 1) (2020) "Translating Chinese Culture into English: from Sole Patronage to Joint Patronage", Perspectives: Studies in Translation Theory and Practice, 28(5), 689-701. https://doi.org/10.1080/0907676X.2020.1718169 2) (2020) "Joint patronage in translating Chinese literature into English: A case study on the Chinese Literature Overseas Dissemination Project". Babel, 765-779. https://doi.org/10.1075/babel.00171.bai Right after the publication of the article entitled "Translating Chinese Culture into English: from Sole Patronage to Joint Patronage" in 2020, it was immediately cited by Roberto A. Valdeón in his article entitled “Translation: From Mediation to Gatekeeping and Agenda-setting” in the international journal entitled Language and Intercultural Communication (DOI: 10.1080/14708477.2020.1833903). Roberto A. Valdeón also informed me that he would include my article in an anthology to be published in a leading publisher in the near future. In addition, I presented my research findings in six international or regional conferences in America, South Korea, Italy and China, and was a keynote speaker at The Third National Forum on the Frontiers of Translation Studies held in Ningbo University in October 2019. I was also invited to give two talks on my findings of this project at the Department of Translation of Lingnan University and School of Foreign Studies of University of Science and Technology Beijing respectively (Please refer to Part C).

23600017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
23600017.value: This research demonstrates that, compared with sole patronage, joint patronage by both Chinese and Western institutions is a more effective way to translate Chinese culture and literature for the Western audience and that the involvement of the agents in the target culture plays an important role in promoting Chinese culture and literature to the Western world. Then there arises another question: Is the translation mainly initiated by organizations from the target culture even more efficient in introducing Chinese culture and literature to the Western world? According to Wang Yougui (2013:72), “translation needs”, which refers to the internal driving force to initiate, advance and complete a translation activity, may come from the export country or the import country, and the needs from the import country play a dominant role in determining whether the translation can be carried out successfully or not. If there are agents from the target culture who actively initiate the translation of Chinese culture to the Western world, this to some extent may mean that there are translation needs in the target culture. In my next research project, I plan to further study the issues related to the translation projects mainly initiated from the target culture.

23600017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
23600017.value: In this research, I have made an in-depth investigation on joint patronage in translating Chinese culture into English on the basis of the case studies of the “CPG China Library”, a project under joint patronage of China Publishing Group Corp. and leading Western publishers, “Culture and Civilization of China Series”, a project under joint patronage of China International Publishing Group and Yale University Press, and the “Chinese Literature Overseas Dissemination Project”, which is under joint patronage of Beijing Normal University, the Confucius Institute at University of Oklahoma, and the University of Oklahoma Press. The study demonstrates that, compared with sole patronage, joint patronage by both Chinese and Western institutions is a more effective way to promote Chinese culture for the Western audience and may make a great difference in promoting Chinese culture to the Western world. This is the first research in the field of translation studies which provides a definition and theoretical framework of joint patronage and has filled the gap in the research in this field. In addition to contributing to the scholarship in translation studies, this research has provided insights for the practical issues related to the translation of Chinese culture and literature for the Western audience.

23600117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23600117.value: 本計劃旨在研究社群的數字化呈現，對香港和新加坡的南亞離散社群的網站，進行多模社會符號學分析。 南亞離散社群是世界上最大的離散社群之一，在過去十年間成為全球學術界的炙手可熱的研究題目。一直以來南亞社群在東南亞佔據著重要的位置，對當地社會作出了巨大的貢獻。世界各地許多南亞社群都得到了持續的關注，但是關於南亞社群的學術研究仍然非常缺乏。香港和新加坡兩座城市都是至關重要的場域，各種的離散身份在當地形成了多層次、多族群、多元文化的社會。然而，南亞社群在當地社會常常面對社會融入和社群呈現不足的問題。因此，近年來南亞離散社群開始探索在網絡空間進行社群呈現的可能性。隨著當代通訊的網絡科技越來越多模態化（Kress and Van Leeuwen，2001），網站具有表現文化的符號資源，成為理解離散社群的關鍵。新近呈現的族群在新媒體科技的助推下不斷進化，這些日漸湧現的網絡空間，作為身份的符號學面貌和文化面貌，缺乏微觀層面的分析。香港和新加坡的南亞社群開始通過上網來應對文化身份危機，有見於此，本研究深入研究他們的網站呈現的文化身份。 本研究採用多模態社會符號學針對網站進行的文化分析作為研究框架（Pauwels，2012），分析南亞社群生活方式的界面，並對其進行多種調查，包括網站和數字化民族誌的多模態社會符號、訪問網站製作人和使用者，務求在更廣闊的社會文化語境中細緻地理解離散主題。本研究透過探索網站的多模態的方方面面，例如網絡話語的模型、符號資源、符際關係等，也嘗試揭示香港和新加坡當今的南亞社群的形成、位置和經驗，以及它們通過網絡空間來超越各種離散觀念的可能性。 本研究對於多模態研究和離散研究等領域都將有所貢獻，它的分析可以揭示數字化呈現的文化過程。本研究還可以增進當地對南亞離散社群異質性的認知，擴寬對全球南亞網絡離散的概念化理解。

23601317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23601317.value: Taking an economic perspective, this proposed project aims to study the translation decision-making processes (linguistic and non-linguistic) of business and literary translators in Hong Kong, Shanghai and Taipei. In this project, economics is understood to be the study of any human action in which cost and benefit considerations are involved. The practice of translating has yet to be thoroughly studied from this perspective. The region of greater China was chosen for this proposed project because the demand for translation in China, Hong Kong and Taiwan combined was estimated to account for about 15% of the world translation market in 2014. In the past, Translation Studies (TS) have concentrated on textual end-products. Only in the recent decades has more attention been paid to the process or agents of translation. Based on my previous work using the tools of economics to study translator status, the translation profession and the translation market in Hong Kong, this proposed project will aim to further investigate the linguistic and extra-linguistic decision-making processes of business and literary translators. These two types of translators were chosen because they were perceived to be operating with different motives and constraints. This proposed project will specifically aim to: 1) Investigate the professional background, job profiles, monetary and non-monetary motives, and perceptions of the translation market by surveying 90 translators based in Hong Kong, Shanghai and Taipei; and 2) Analyse the data obtained from face-to-face interviews with six translators from the above locales (one male and one female business/literary translator in each locale) regarding the linguistic and extra-linguistic decision-making processes in their professional work and the motives and constraints behind such processes. This proposed project will seek to address the following research questions: i) What are the personal, institutional and social motives or constraints behind the translatorial actions of business and literary translators? ii) Are there any significant differences in the linguistic and extra-linguistic decision-making processes of these two types of translators? If so, what are they and what are the reasons for these discrepancies? iii) How do the differences, if any, in the linguistic and extra-linguistic decision-making processes inform the learning and teaching of business and literary translation and the professional development of these translators? The outcome of this proposed project will include three to four papers on the personal and social motives or constraints behind the translatorial actions of business and literary translators and the linguistic and extra-linguistic decision-making processes involved. 本研究項目旨在從經濟學角度來審視香港、上海和台北商業和文學譯者的翻譯決策過程（語言內和語言外）。在這個項目中，「經濟學」應理解為任何涉及成本和效益考慮的人類行為之研究。從這個角度來分析翻譯實踐尚未有深入研究。中國內地、香港和台灣為本研究的主題，蓋因2014年三地的翻譯活動估計佔世界翻譯市場約15%，其重要性可見一斑。 過往翻譯學研究往往集中於文本。近幾十年來，研究者更多關注翻譯過程或當中所涉及的實體。本人曾以經濟學作為工具探討譯者地位、翻譯專業以及香港的翻譯市場。此一研究項目旨在進一步檢視商業和文學譯者的語言內和語言外決策過程。選擇這兩種類型的譯者是因為人們認為他們有著不同的動機和限制。 更具體地說，本研究的目的如下： 1) 通過對香港、上海和台北90位筆譯人員的調查，審視其專業背景、工作範圍、金錢和非金錢動機以及對翻譯市場的看法；及 2) 面對面訪問上述地區六位筆譯人員（每個地區的一位男性和一位女性商業/文學譯者），蒐集相關數據以瞭解有關其專業工作中語言內和語言外決策過程之動機及限制。 此一項目擬探討以下的研究問題： i) 商業和文學譯者翻譯行為背後的個人、制度和社會動機或限制為何？ ii) 這兩類譯者的語言內和語言外決策過程是否有著顯著差異？如有，這些差異為何？導致這些差異的原因是甚麼？ iii) 此等語言內和語言外決策過程中的差異（如有），對商業和文學翻譯的學習和教學以及這些譯者的專業發展有何啟示？ 此一項目的研究結果將包括三至四篇論文，內容關於商業和文學譯者翻譯行為的個人和社會動機或限制，以及當中所涉及的語言內和語言外決策過程。

23601317.label: Realisation of objectives
23601317.value: 1. To review the existing TS literature in relation to the economics of translation, the translation profession and the decision-making processes of translators: A literature review of studies related to the economics of translation, the translation profession and the decision-making processes of translators was carried out. Since the economics of languages and translation is a new sub-field, not many papers and monographs have been published but the situation is somehow improving after 2016. For example, The Palgrave Handbook of Economics and Language edited by Victor Ginsburgh and Schlmo Weber (2016) examines the interplay between economic decisions and social behaviour in multilingual societies. The Bloomsbury Companion to Language Industry Studies (2020) is another important work which looks into the key issues shaping the language industry. These two monographs have been the guiding force of this research. 2. To provide current job profiles for business and literary translators in Hong Kong, Shanghai and Taipei: Of the business and literary translators surveyed through an electronic questionnaire, it is found that the backgrounds of these translators are quite similar –– they have either a bachelor’s or master’s degree, 13-15 years of translation experience and work for around 30 hours per week. It is less likely for business translators to have language or translation-related degrees but interestingly, quite a number of them have received training in literary translation. Most literary translators work for publication houses while business translators mostly work for translation agencies. 3. To put forward a descriptive model on how business and literary translators make linguistic and extra-linguistic decisions: The translators interviewed reckon that the translation process is envisaged as a set of constraint-motivated strategies. The final shape of the target text is seen as a result of a process in which translators try their best to accommodate the linguistic constraints imposed on them and to adopt what they deem to be appropriate translation strategies. This entails that translators do not work randomly, but are influenced by particular constraints that are extra-linguistic. Translators sometimes receive specific information (e.g. translation brief) from the translation commissioner (e.g. client, agent, project manager or publisher) which implicitly or explicitly indicates as to what global translation strategy to adopt. 4. To search for the differences, if any, in the linguistic and extra-linguistic decision-making processes of business and literary translators, and explore how these differences can inform the learning and teaching of business and literary translation and the professional development of these translators: According to the interviews, literary translators believe that they have to combine content and style while business translators think that content is king. They also think that literary translation requires more literary skills as well as an understanding of both languages and cultures on a very deep level. The learning and teaching of business and literary translation and the professional development of business and literary translators should take into account these differences in curriculum planning and course delivery.

23601317.label: Major findings and research outcome
23601317.value: This two-year project used an economic perspective to study how business and literary translators in Hong Kong, Shanghai and Taipei make linguistic and extra-linguistic decisions in their professional life. A two-phase mix-method (quantitative and qualitative) approach has been adopted. Some of the quantitative findings were disseminated in the Fourth International Conference on Research into the Didactics of Translation in Barcelona, Spain in June 2018. For the qualitative findings, I planned to present them in the “Translation Studies in East Asia: Tradition, Transition and Transcendence” conference in Hong Kong in December 2019 but the conference was postponed to June 2021 due to the CO-VID 19 pandemic. The researcher is finalizing articles in preparation from the existing data for submission for publication. From the research findings, I have developed a better understanding of the job profiles of business and literary translators in Hong Kong, Shanghai and Taiwan. There are similarities as well as differences between these two types of translators. Of the 106 business and literary translators surveyed through an electronic questionnaire, it is found that the backgrounds of these translators are quite similar except It is less likely for business translators to have language or translation-related degrees but interestingly, quite a number of them have received training in literary translation. Most literary translators work for publication houses while business translators mostly work for translation agencies. The translators interviewed reckon that the translation process is envisaged as a set of constraint-motivated strategies. The final shape of the target text is seen as a result of a process in which translators do their best to accommodate the linguistic constraints imposed on them and to adopt what they deem to be appropriate translation strategies. This entails that translators do not work randomly, but are rather influenced by particular constraints that are extra-linguistic in nature. The translator sometimes receives specific information (e.g. translation brief) from the translation commissioner (e.g. client, agent, translation project manager or publisher) which implicitly or explicitly gives indications as to what global translation strategy to adopt. According to the interviews, literary translators believe that they have to combine content and style while business translators think that content is king. Literary translators also think that literary translation requires more literary skills as well as an understanding of both languages and cultures on a very deep level. The learning and teaching of business and literary translation and the professional development of business and literary translators should take into account these differences in curriculum planning and course delivery.

23601317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
23601317.value: This completed ECS project can serve as a solid foundation for future research on the economics of translation and the translation profession. For economics of translation, there could be research on economic theory-driven explanations of translation phenomena which may shed lights on the relationships between various variables. Besides, other types of translators (e.g. legal and media translators) could be studied from an economic perspective.

23601317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
23601317.value: This project studies the translation decision-making processes of business and literary translators in Hong Kong, Shanghai and Taipei using an economic perspective. The practice of professional translating, particularly in the context of China, Hong Kong and Taiwan, has yet been thoroughly studied from this perspective even though the demands for translation in these regions have been on the rise. In this research, a two-phase mixed-method approach (including quantitative and qualitative surveying methods) was adopted to gain a better understanding of the topic. The data gathered is of great importance to this region as a whole, since translation plays an increasingly important role in the business and cultural activities of these three locales. In particular, the findings also benefit translation teachers in business and literary translation as well as those involved in the design of continuing professional development (CPD) programmes for these translators.

23601417.label: Project Objectives
23601417.value: To conduct an empirical study of digital infrastructures and data flows in various contexts of practice by examining their integration with governance styles as well as dynamics of struggle and breakdown. To deploy an Inter-Asia methodology devising new frames of reference based on comparison of parallel processes in Hong Kong and Istanbul. Beyond gaining ethnographic details, the aim is to interrogate and theorize tendencies toward divergence concomitant with the globalization of digital infrastructures. Hence I develop a tripartite framework. To contribute to the rethinking of ‘power’ and ‘difference’ and, in doing so, integrate debates in cultural studies, materialist media studies, and science and technology studies. My intervention explores 'power' in relation to multiple techno-political modes and scales and 'difference' in relation to emergent socio-technical ways of being.

23601417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23601417.value: Situated in Hong Kong and Istanbul, this research investigates the role of digital data in the management of urban populations and environments. New technologies induce political shifts by engendering new endeavors, visions, and styles of governance. Hence there is a need to study technologies such as smart city sensors, surveillance tools, Open Data standards, specialized software, and localized apps in terms of their implication in techniques of governance and the production of social order. I analyze data’s mobility, namely its route, directionality, and points of transition into knowledge; its integration with governance styles and expedient practices; and affiliated discourses, imaginaries and aesthetics generating contested conceptions of transparency/secrecy, ownership, and sovereignty. Using an Inter-Asia methodology, I compare parallel developments in Hong Kong and Istanbul and produce new frames of reference to understand them. These two cities are historically seen as “bridges” between East and West, and more recently, profiled as “ICT Hubs.” Rather than approaching these cities as ideal-typical hubs advancing a proverbial “flat” world, I highlight tendencies toward techno-political and socio-technical divergence and the constitution of various modes and scales of operation. The aim is to rethink both ‘difference’ and ‘power.’ I trace how a paradoxical sense of difference arises from the adaptation and localization of globalizing digital infrastructures such as smart city infrastructure and Open Data applications. Such a sense can be appropriated for new configurations of statecraft and sovereignty in the urban context. But it can also instigate the invention of alterity and forms of dissent mediated by digital infrastructure. Although I draw on materialist media studies’ emphasis on infrastructural dispositions, my analysis addresses articulations of material affordances with new and existing rationalities of governance, alongside the emergence of tactics of dissent and occurrences of breakdown. For instance, (perceived) disruptions, incompatibilities, failures, or even excesses of connectivity and data flow turn data-driven apparatuses of governance into sites of struggle. My first case study explores Istanbul’s smart urbanism and its coalescence with censorship measures. Activist practices seek “outsides” that go unregistered by dominant networks. The second case study addresses tensions between Open Data initiatives and discourses of 'transparency' in Hong Kong. It inquires into activists' generating of unchecked data mobilities and data-driven self-governance. The third and fourth case studies examine data’s role in remediating breakdown in the urban environment. These cases respectively highlight data’s role in urban environmentalism and e-waste activism, which intersect ecological and informational struggles. 這處於香港和伊斯坦堡的研究探討數據資料在都市人口和環境管理上的角色。新媒體產生了新的管治嘗試，願景及樣式，帶來了政治上的改變。因此我們需要研究不同科技，例如智慧城市感測器，監控工具，開放數據標準，專門軟件及本地化的應用程式，在管治技術和社會秩序的生產所帶有的意義。我分析數據的流動性，包括它的路徑，方向性，形成知識的轉化點；它和管治樣式的結合及權宜措施；以及產生各種不同對透明度／私密性，所有權和主權的理解的想像和美學。 通過使用亞際方法，我比較香港和伊斯坦堡兩地的平衡發展，以提出理解兩地的參考性框架。歷史上，這兩個城市同被視為連接東方和西方的橋樑，以及近來同樣被描繪成資訊及通訊科技樞紐。我嘗試突出科技－政治性－社會性的差異以及眾多不同模式和操作規模的形成，而不是視這兩個城市為達至“扁平” 世界的理想－典型樞紐。我的目標在於重思“差異性” (difference) 和“權力”。從對全球數據基建的接收和本地化，例如智慧城市基建和開放數據的實施，我追溯一種自相矛盾的差異感(sense of difference) 的形成。這種差異感能被配合成為在城市中，主權和國家手段(statecraft) 的新配置。但它亦能以數據基建為中介，產生找尋差異性的建立 (invention of alterity) 和不同形式的異議。 儘管我分享物質性媒體研究對基建的內在性質的重視，我的分析亦嘗試處理不同物質環境賦使(material affordances)，伴隨反抗策略和故障(breakdown)的出現中，跟嶄新或現存的管治思維所作的扣連。我第一個個案有關伊斯坦堡智慧都市計畫和審查措施的聯合，及行動者實踐找尋“在外” (“outsides”) 以脫離主流網路。第二個個案處理香港開放數據的倡議以及透明度的張力，並理解行動者生產不受控制的數據流通和受數據所驅動的自我管理。第三和四的個案考察數據在都市環境中作為修復故障的角色。這些案例重點提出在都市環保主義和電子垃圾運動，環境和資訊抗爭的並行上，數據的角色。

23601417.label: Realisation of objectives
23601417.value: When I moved from my previous to my current institution, the requirements for tenure shifted from a book publication to journal articles. The result of this different form of output is that my work has been somewhat more fragmented than I initially imagined it would be, had I worked toward a monograph. A degree of fragmentation was the more hard to prevent since Turkey went through a political transformation that impacted the relevancy and feasibility of research on smart city digital infrastructure, as explained in my interim report and approved request for project extension in March 2020. These were the main obstacles I encountered, which demanded creative adaptation and flexibility from me as a researcher. Despite the circumstances, I did manage to realize my objectives. For instance, the publications “Aggregations of the opaque: Rethinking datafication and e-waste” and “From Open Data to “grounded openness”: Recursive politics and postcolonial struggle in Hong Kong” speak to Objective 1. The article “Platforms for populism? The affective issue crowd and its disconnections” does so too, but it focuses more on the national level and a decidedly populist style of governance. Though the type of politics at stake is different, what runs through all the research is the focus on the political implications of digital infrastructures and data. These may support explicit ideologies, values, and norms but they can also divert from them or operate in more covert ways via collection of data, ordering of spaces and bodies, and managing of resources. Critical possibilities, as my research proves, lie at the intersection of such material-technological and discursive forces. Moreover, despite the seeming distance between the research on Open Data in Hong Kong and platforms for populism in Turkey, I also found thematic and theoretical resonances around questions of digital infrastructure and popular sovereignty. Actually, responding to recent political volatility in both Turkey and Hong Kong, both the publications “Platforms for populism” and “From Open Data to ‘grounded openness’” address how digital infrastructures mediate, or are implicated in, governance as well as popular struggle. Instead of writing a monograph, I took up two editorial projects that allowed me to develop the theoretical framework that I proposed in the initial funding application. I am the editor of the published special issue “Via Asia: Digital Infrastructure, World-making and Liminality,” which was published by International Journal of Communication. Second, I act as first editor, alongside Gladys Pak-Lei Chong, of the book volume Critiquing communication innovation: New media in a multipolar world, published by Michigan State University Press (in press). The introduction to the special issue develops Objective 2. It challenges the presumption of ubiquitous connectivity and infrastructure integration, which lies at the root of both celebratory and critical dominant frameworks, by highlighting liminality. I elaborated the tri-partite framework at the center of my original funding proposal and articulated the articles of the special issue to it. As my introduction explains, digital infrastructures touch on something external that they do not fully control and therefore spur tensions and paradoxes of integration/disruption and convergence/excess. What I call the “infrastructural politics of liminality” unpacks such tensions and paradoxes. Accordingly, this section explores infrastructural world-making by mapping digital–material connections running “via Asia” that touch ground in Asia but that also produce its spaces, borders, and global extensions. The introduction to the book especially develops the themes and theoretical problematics underlying Objective 3. It focuses on communication innovation, namely the shifting ways of communication and social organization as they are mediated by changing infrastructural designs and platforms. The volume investigates such innovation exactly at the moment when Silicon Valley’s dominant role in conjuring and ‘patenting’ technological futures is challenged, yet the role of Asia and other places in shaping techno-diverse futures needs to be explored critically. The introduction (first author, with Chong) focuses on questions of power and difference in multipolar communication innovation. Both the introduction to the special issue and the book engage digital infrastructure and the question of comparative research. I made two research trips to Turkey, one from May to June and one in December 2019. These trips covered in total a period of over 9 weeks. Assisted by two Research Assistants in Istanbul, I deployed insights and methods from infrastructure and platform studies, using interview, (visual) discourse analysis, and digital methods to analyze the relation between digital platforms and populist governance as well as, separately, populism, urban infrastructure, and ecology. In addition, as indicated in my request for project extension, I have focused on the digital infrastructures and platforms of fintech, which broadly speaking falls within the scope of smart city development and governance. Concerning Hong Kong, I have conducted research on Open Data and datafication in the smart city, which led to a publication as well as a top faculty paper award at the International Communication Studies Association Convention in May 2020. Parallel to the research in Istanbul, I also conducted research on fintech and datafied finance in Hong Kong. I worked with a local Research Assistant as well as two student helpers employed through the funding of the Education Plan. I have done internet-based research combining interview, discourse analysis, walk-through method, and digital methods. I presented some of my findings at an international conference themed Data Power in Bremen in Fall 2019 and have a paper under review with the journal Cultural Studies. The Education Plan has supported the hiring of student helpers who have assisted with research such as interviews and transcription as well as digital media research in Hong Kong. Furthermore, I deployed the fund to train a multi-disciplinary team of undergraduate students to do research about platforms and even design a platform of our own. We have produced an electronics repair platform, called OpenRepair Hong Kong (https://openrepair.com.cuhk.edu.hk). By connecting repairers (to start with, currently just one) and users with broken electronic devises (currently the CUHK student and staff population), its aim is to encourage repair and, in doing so, fight planned obsolescence and the tremendous amount of electronic waste this causes. This project has stimulated the students to critically investigate digital infrastructures and think of alternative, environmentally conscious platforms and smart-city applications. I have been guiding the students in doing relevant fieldwork and interviews, executing market research, studying platforms, design thinking, and setting up a promotional campaign. I also organized a public event on the use of digital data, visualizations, and platforms in tackling ecological problems in collaboration with the Internet Society of Hong Kong. The event was originally planned for Spring 2020 but due to the Covid-19 outbreak got postponed. It was eventually held on 23 October, over Zoom. Invited were several local environmental NGOs, Open Data advocates, and researchers from other universities in Hong Kong. The event furthermore targeted students. We attracted over 60 attendants and the video recording has received over 1.5k views on Facebook. In order to reach out to the public, I also wrote two essays published via the London-based Open Access press Open Humanities and one essay (co-authored with my Mphil student Sherry Shek) published via the newsletter of the Internet Society of Hong Kong (see part C).

23601417.label: Major findings and research outcome
23601417.value: As the introduction to the book “Critiquing communication innovation” argues, communication innovation has become multipolar. Yet does this global spread make a difference? How do we critically analyze the processes of global integration of digital infrastructures, along with their localization and differentiation? If global digital-infrastructural integration is less all-encompassing than assumed, what is the role of liminality? What I call the infrastructural politics of liminality in the introduction to the special issue I edited concerns, first, the incorporation of liminal difference through the workings of digital infrastructure that advance technical interoperability and spatial integration. I draw on Gilbert Simondon’s critique of the cybernetic view of information that treats the latter as abstract; reduces all life to this abstraction; and is geared toward command and control. However, infrastructural integration and control should not be taken for granted, but considered as sites of struggle. At every switch or extension, (human and nonhuman, social and material) forms of resistance can put smooth connectivity and infrastructural integrity at peril. For instance, as my publication “Aggregations of the Opaque” argues, electronic waste belies the dream/nightmare of total control through datafication. In recycling industries, invisibility, opacity, and uncertainty persist despite worldwide networks of surveillance, datafication, and algorithmic calculation. Looking at datafication through e-waste teaches us that critique should not start from the presumption of increasingly all-encompassing datafication, but instead analyze the (constitutive) limitations and (productive) excesses at stake in data assemblages. The liminal spaces of e-waste recycling in Hong Kong manifest this problematic. The second axis of the infrastructural politics of liminality I outlined attends to sociotechnical territorializations, whereby digital/smart infrastructures become part and parcel of geopolitics as well as the governance of territories and populations. However, digital infrastructures are not simply subjected to geopolitics and claims to sovereignty per se. At stake is sociotechnical emergence reconfiguring governance, statecraft, statehood, and leadership. This dynamic was explored in the paper “Platforms for populism?,” taking the case of Turkey, as well as the book introduction (see Part C). The third axis examines the emergence of sociotechnical novelty. My paper “From Open Data to ‘grounded openness’” explores this in the case of Hong Kong. Looking at data activism in Hong Kong, this article highlights the (post)colonial histories that have shaped the reception of Open Data. Furthermore, it explores how the techno-materialities of data infrastructures affect and reconfigure postcolonial struggle.

23601417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
23601417.value: Work stemming from the research: One paper is under review with Theory, Culture and Society, which builds on my previous research into the digital infrastructures governing electronic waste. This research interest is also carrying over to my current Direct Grant project and submitted GRF application. One more paper is being prepared about the infrastructures of speculative digital finance. Being on maternity leave has delayed the submission of this manuscript. One collaboration, which is in progress, with my MPhil student builds on the questions of Open Data, looking at Hong Kong and mainland China.

23601417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
23601417.value: “Techno-politics” may seem ugly hyphenated jargon, but for me the term serves as the very concept that allows me to investigate societies. This ECS project has investigated digital infrastructure as a formative force operating in the contexts of governance, breakdown, and struggle. It has focused on the various political implications of digital infrastructures and the ways in which they give rise to both the technologically informed gaze of governance and its limitations and outsides. Infrastructures may support and enact explicit ideologies, values, and norms but they can also divert from them or operate in a more covert ways to collect data, order spaces and bodies, and manage resources. New infrastructures induce political shifts by engendering new endeavors, visions, and styles of governance. Furthermore, in order to avoid decontextualized and hence rather universalizing approaches to digital infrastructure, this project has theorized processes of global infrastructural integration and differentiation and it has situated the analysis in specific geographical locales, mainly Istanbul and Hong Kong. Collaborations with international scholars as editor of a book and special issue respectively has served to strengthen the comparativist and multipolar dimension of this research and the theoretical framework it offers.

23602717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23602717.value: Photographs are ubiquitous. It is sometimes said that we live in an “image society” and what this typically means is that we live a “photographic image society.” Today, photographs appear not only in art galleries, one’s private photo albums, newspapers, etc., but perhaps primarily instead on various social media such as Facebook, Flickr, or Instagram. Despite the ubiquity of photographic images, it was only rather recently that philosophers started to take a genuine interest in this medium (although researchers outside the discipline have said many intelligent and philosophically minded things about it long before that). But photography does indeed raise philosophical questions: what is special about photography, in relation to “handmade image” such as paintings, drawings, and computer generated images?; how do photographs have “meaning”?; is it OK, from a moral perspective, to photograph whatever one likes, perhaps also posting the images on Instagram or Facebook?; and what does it mean to theorise about a medium that seems to be in flux? For some time now, the philosophy of photography has focussed on various claims regarding the allegedly merely causal nature of photography, and related to this, its medium-specificity. I will add to this debate, too, by aiming to offer a deeper understanding of what it means to say that a medium is causal, in the first place. More importantly, however, I will address topics that the traditional theory has largely neglected: in particular questions regarding the possible contents of photographs, and ethical considerations regarding the medium (something which strangely has been absent in recent philosophical discussions). The present project is intended as a book-length treatment of photography from a number of philosophical perspectives, discussing what photography is, how photographs have meaning, and what ethical considerations one might have in relation to various photographic practices. I will draw not only on philosophical literature, but also on material from art-theory and criticism. As indicated, philosophical accounts of photography are rather few (and mostly new). The planned book would decidedly fill a lacuna in the extant relevant literature: as far as I am aware of, no philosophical monograph on the subject to date treats photography from such a wide perspective as I plan to do in the book.

24104517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24104517.value: 胚胎植入是哺乳動物成功妊娠的先決條件。胚胎植入的失敗導致了70％以上的人類自然妊娠失敗，並是現階段輔助生殖技術成功率低的主要原因。胚胎植入的異常可能導致妊娠後期的許多危及生命的病症，包括流產、胎盤功能不全、先兆子癇和早產。然而，由於其複雜性，胚胎植入過程並不被人們清楚地認識。 Wnt /β-catenin和前列腺素（PGs）介導的信號傳導通路已被證明在胚胎植入中發揮關鍵作用。在其它細胞類型中，前列腺素E2（PGE2）被報導具有調節Wnt /β-catenin的能力，但PGE2和Wnt /β-catenin在胚胎植入過程中的相互作用並未被闡明。多重抗藥性蛋白4（MRP4）的主要作用是介導排除細胞毒性藥物，因此被認為是潛在的化療靶標。有趣的是，MRP4亦能轉運內源性信號分子，如PGE2。我們的初步結果表明，MRP4在胚胎植入時表達上升並與β-catenin相關。因此，我們提出假設：MRP4可能通過調節Wnt/β-catenin信號通路，在胚胎植入中起到重要作用。本研究項目將檢驗該假設內容，研究結果將使我們进一步地理解胚胎植入過程的机制。並且，鑒別MRP4在胚胎植入中的潛在作用將有助於研發治療胚胎植入相關疾病的分子靶標。此外，鑑於Wnt/β-catenin在各種生理和病理過程中的重要性，該研究項目可能對胚胎植入以外的研究領域亦具有重要意義。

24106317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24106317.value: HIV is an important public health threat and Men who have sex with men (MSM) constitute a high risk group for transmission of HIV in Hong Kong due to their high level of risky sexual behaviors. There is evidence that difficulty in regulating emotions is strongly associated with risky sexual behaviors, however, interventions targeting risky sexual behaviors among MSM mainly focused on improving their knowledge, beliefs, and skills, and very few of them focused on improving their emotion regulation. Evidenced-based Positive Psychology Intervention (PPI) has recently been developed and its effect on improving emotion regulation, mental health and health behaviors has been demonstrated. However, from our knowledge, no study to date has examined the effect of PPI on changing risky sexual behaviors among MSM. Moreover, the proliferation in the use of Internet allows health interventions to be delivered in a convenient and cost-effective manner. Online PPI hence has great potential to improve risky sexual behaviors among MSM. The aim of the proposed study is to develop and evaluate a novel and evidence-based online PPI to improve emotion regulation and reduce HIV risky behaviors among MSM in Hong Kong. A 2-armed randomized controlled trial is proposed, Chinese men who self-reported having anal sex with another man in the past six months will be recruited and randomly allocated into the intervention (N=170) and the control group (N=170). Participants in the intervention group will be invited to take part in a 4-week online PPI which contains various exercises designed to improve positive emotions towards the past (gratitude exercise), in the present (savouring), and towards the future (optimism exercise). Participants in the control group will only receive didactic information about HIV online. Participants will be evaluated at baseline, and one month and three months after the intervention. The primary outcome will be unprotected anal intercourse (UAI); secondary outcomes will include emotion regulation, depression, gratitude, positive and negative affect, optimism, and well-being. The online intervention, if found successful, will have important implications for practice as it can be adopted by the MSM NGOs or other related websites, it can reach many MSM at a very low cost and thus has the potential to reduce the increasing HIV epidemic among MSM in Hong Kong. 愛滋病是一個重要的公共衛生威脅，男男性接觸者（MSM）因高風險性行為而成為香港愛滋病毒的高風險群體。有證據表明情緒調節困難與風險性行為密切相關，但針對MSM危險性行為的干預措施主要集中在改善他們的行為知識，信代和技能，卻没有專注於改善情緒調節。以證據為基礎的積極心理干預（PPI）對改善情緒調節、心理健康和行為健康的影響已被證明。然而，到目前為止並沒有針對PPI對MSM風險性行為改變的研究。此外，互聯網的廣泛使用令干預措施能夠在一個方便，經濟有效的方式進行。網上PPI因此具有很大的潛力能改變MSM的風險性行為。 本研究的目的是開發和評估一個循證的網上PPI，以改善MSM的情緒調節及降低愛滋病風險行為。本研究提出一項隨機對照試驗，男男性接觸者將被隨機分為干預組（N = 170）和對照組（N = 170）。參加干預組的參加者將被邀請參加為期4週的網上PPI活動。對照組的參與者只接受有關的健康信息。參與者將在基線，干預後一個月和三個月進行評估。主要結局將是無保護的肛交（UAI）;次要結局將包括情緒調節，抑鬱，感激，積極和消極情緒，樂觀主義和幸福感。本干預如果成功，將對實踐有重要影響，因為它可以被MSM非政府組織或其他相關網站採用，它能以非常低的成本接觸許多MSM，因此有可能減少本港MSM中日益增長的愛滋病毒感染率。

24106317.label: Realisation of objectives
24106317.value: 1. Development of the intervention The content of the intervention was first designed and produced based on a review on mental health, PPI and HIV-related sexual behaviors among MSM in Hong Kong, and the draft was discussed among the research team. A focus group discussion with six MSM was then conducted to test the feasibility, relevance and acceptability of the intervention. The feedbacks collected was brought back to the team and further revisions were made based on that. An intervention website, “HeHe Journals”, was developed. A content management system was established to enable the automated intervention delivery and the real-time monitoring of each participant’s engagement. Auto-reminders were delivered through an external email system. The preliminary online platform was tested and revised. Animations and videos were developed to introduce each PPI exercise covered in the intervention, i.e. Three good things, gratitude letter, savoring exercise and optimism exercise. 2. Implementing a randomized controlled trial to test for the intervention efficacy First, prospective participants were recruited from both online (social networking sites and advertisements placed on local websites) and offline (popular gay venues) sources in Hong Kong. For offline recruitment, participants were approached and briefed about the goals and the logistics of the study. All eligible participants were asked to provide their contact information. The aim, significance, logistics, benefits and potential risks of participation were explained through contact by a research assistant. Informed consents were obtained from those who wish to participate in this study and were invited to complete the baseline survey following the instruction to the intervention website. During recruitment process, both automated and human verification approaches were used to avoid fraudulent and duplicate respondents. Each participant had a unique password-protected account, and their progression through all phases were automatically recorded. All enrolled participants (n=420) were randomly allocated by the computerized system to either the intervention group (n=204) or the control group (n=216). Participants assigned to the intervention group received a 4-week online intervention. The intervention incorporated with PPI exercises that targeted positive emotions, and the exercises were structured in a way that it first addressed positive emotions about the past (gratitude exercise), followed by positive emotions about the present (daily savoring experience), and positive emotions about the future (optimism exercise). The PPI exercises included were as follows: Three good things, Gratitude letter, Savoring exercise and Optimism exercise. In addition to the PPI exercises, participants were guided to develop a plan to reduce risky sexual behaviors. The first intervention session was open to access immediately upon the completion of baseline assessment and next session was made accessible to them in the coming week. Participants were asked to perform some of the exercise daily and record their progress on the intervention site. Weekly reminders were sent to participants to encourage them to visit the intervention site. Participants in the control group only received weekly information about HIV and safe sex behaviors during the study period. Post-intervention survey was released online immediately after the 4-week intervention and a follow-up survey was released after 3 months. An incentive of supermarket coupon of HKD 50 was given to participants of both groups for each completed survey, HKD 150 for completing all three evaluation surveys. Database of evaluation responses could be automatically generated from the online system. 3. Evaluation To examine the efficacy of the intervention, participants were asked to report the number of different types of sex partners, sexual behaviors, the frequency of condom use with different types of sex partners before and after the intervention. Measurements that target emotion regulation (Difficulties in Emotion Regulation Scale), Depression (Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale (CES-D)), Gratitude (The Gratitude Questionnaire (GQ)), positive/negative affect (Positive and Negative Affect Schedule (PANAS) scale), Optimism (Life Orientation Test-revised (LOT-R) scale), Well-being (Psychological Well-being of Mental Health Inventory (MHI-5)), were also included in all three assessments. Background variables (e.g. age, highest education level, sexual orientation, working status) were measured at baseline and follow-up assessments, respectively. A total of 275 and 252 participants completed the post-intervention and 3-month follow-up assessment and were included in the analyses.

24106317.label: Major findings and research outcome
24106317.value: 1. The prevalence of condomless anal intercourse (CAI) among MSM in Hong Kong At baseline, 52.3% of total participants had regular sex partner(s) in the last month, 41.1% of which had CAI with regular partners in the last month; 39.5% reported having casual sex partner(s) in the last month, 48.1% of which had CAI with casual partners in the last month (see Appendix-Table 1). 2. The efficacy of the PPI intervention in improving sexual behaviours and psychological variables In the intention-to-treat sample (n=420), both the intervention group and the control group had a significant decrease in presence of any casual sex partner(s) at 3-month follow-up, and the decrease appeared to be larger in the intervention group. The intervention group also had a significant decrease in the number of regular sex partners at 3-month follow-up. In addition, both groups had a significant decrease in difficulties in emotion regulation at post-intervention and at 3-month follow-up, and the decrease appeared to be larger in the intervention group. At 3-month follow-up, the intervention group had a significantly decrease in negative affect while the control group had a significantly increase in gratitude (see Appendix-Table 2 and 3). Among the as-treated sample (n=347), a similar pattern was shown for the within- and between-group differences in sexual behaviours and difficulties in emotion regulation at both follow-up waves. Unlike to the intention-to-treat sample, this intervention group who had engaged in intervention activities had a significant increase in the gratitude and well-being at post-intervention. Compared with the control group, the intervention group had a significantly larger increase in well-being and appeared to have a larger increase in gratitude (see Appendix-Table 4 and 5). 3. Factors influencing the attrition across study phases Around 65.5% and 60% of total participants completed the post-intervention survey and 3-month follow-up survey, respectively; 64.2% of the intervention group engaged in the PPI intervention (see Appendix-Figure 1). The control group had more participants completing the follow-up surveys. Participants who had an education level of university or above and had an intention of consistent condom use with regular partners were more likely to engage in intervention. In addition, participants who had an education level of university or above and did not have any CAI with casual partners in the last month were more likely to complete the follow-up surveys (details in Appendix-Table 6). After all, despite the occurrence of attrition, the baseline characteristics did not significantly differ between the intervention conditions across study phases.

24106317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24106317.value: Results of the present study provide important insights for further development. First, a more complex study design is needed to delineate the effect of each individual intervention component, so that the most effective PPI exercise can be identified and integrated to maximize the synergistic effects on promoting behavioral change. Also, the mechanism underlying the positive effects of the online intervention and the most optimal dosage for effects should be explored in future study, in order to inform the translation of theory and evidence-based constructs into intervention design. In terms of the practical applications, the present study suggests that positive psychology interventions are potentially useful in promoting HIV preventive behavior and improving well-being. It can facilitate the future incorporation of positive psychology interventions as part of the HIV prevention services for MSM. Given the rigorous development and testing procedures, the present intervention can be adapted to other populations and high-risk populations. Moreover, this self-guided intervention requires minimal professional guidance and thus has the potential to be scaled-up and integrated into regular prevention services in a cost-effective manner.

24106317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24106317.value: PPIs are theoretically-grounded and empirically-validated activities that are designed to enhance health and well-being. They focused on promoting positive emotions and strengths as means to promote health and well-being. The present study tests the efficacy of a 4-week online PPI in promoting HIV preventive behaviors among men who have sex with men using a randomized controlled trial. Rigorous developmental procedures were followed during the design and implementation of the intervention. Results showed that the participants who took part in the intervention appeared to report a decrease in the number of sex partners, and an increase in gratitude and well-being after the intervention. Its efficacy in promoting well-being and HIV preventive behavior is thus supported. The present study also demonstrated the feasibility and acceptability of utilizing the internet to deliver HIV prevention interventions among Chinese MSM. Most importantly, this self-help intervention did not require trained professionals to communicate the messages and could be easily operated through an online platform. Hence, it has the potential to be scaled up and reach many MSM in a cost-effective and sustainable way. This intervention can also be easily incorporated into existing HIV prevention services.

24107017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24107017.value: 項目撮要 背景 人類鼻病毒最常引致上呼吸道感染、喘鳴和導致哮喘惡化。有研究報告指出，兒童早期頻發與鼻病毒相關的喘鳴與預測學齡期的哮喘風險是息息相關的。早在1956年，科學家發現了鼻病毒-A和鼻病毒-B。而鼻病毒-C，則到了五十年後的2006年才被發現。此後，以往未知的嚴重的小兒下呼吸道感染個案，便與鼻病毒-C感染結下關聯。 雖然，我們發現了鼻病毒-C已有十年，但科學界對鼻病毒-C的研究卻十分缺乏。這是由於鼻病毒-C不像其他鼻病毒一樣能感染常規的細胞系，要把鼻病毒-C在樣本中分離和吉養是十分困難的。因為一般我細胞都沒有把鼻病毒-C的受體表達在細胞膜上。直至2014年，研究發現鈣粘素相關家族成員3（CDHR3）能作為鼻病毒-C的受體。這為鼻病毒-C的研究奠定了基礎。然而，這種受體在呼吸道的功能和分佈尚未到確定。再者，關於鼻病毒-C在下呼吸道中的向性仍有待研究，更需要進行有系統的調查。 目標與假設 我們的目的是檢測鼻病毒受體人呼吸道上皮細胞中的分佈和進行鼻病毒-C組織向性研究。我們假設CDHR3的分佈和可及性決定了宿主的對鼻病毒-C易感染程度。另外，我們也假設CDHR3在哮喘和非哮喘患者的表達情況可能不同。再者，鼻病毒-C的基因型，也可能導致它們有所不同的組織向性和復制能力，以演示在臨床病徵的差異。 項目規劃 我們將在人類的呼吸道細胞和組織進行對鼻病毒受體表達和分佈評估。而CDHR3表達細胞類型將通過細胞特異性基因或蛋白質標記物的共表達來定位。CDHR3的受體功能，將通過鼻病毒-C感染人類呼吸道體外培植模型實驗進行評估。 我​​們會用表達CDHR3的細胞系去培養不同基因型的鼻病毒-C。而培養出來的鼻病毒-C，將用作感染鼻病毒-C在我們呼吸道的組織向性。通過病毒基因表達，病毒蛋白表達和鼻病毒-C複製能力的評估，將讓我們更了解有關鼻病毒-C的組織向性，病毒受體的作用和發病機制。 調查結果將成為後續的鼻病毒-C研究基石。

24107017.label: Realisation of objectives
24107017.value: Objective 1: The cell entry factor for RV-C, cadherin-related family member 3 (CDHR3) was characterized by immunohistochemistry in human respiratory tissue paraffin blocks archive; immunofluorescence assay in vitro human respiratory epithelial air-liquid interface cell culture and organoid culture; and gene expression levels in the fresh human respiratory biopsy, in vitro human respiratory epithelial air-liquid interface cell culture and organoid culture. The pseudostratified columnar epithelia of adult bronchus and terminal bronchioles; the pseudostratified columnar epithelia paediatric terminal bronchioles and the pneumocytes; and the reticular and pseudostratified columnar epithelia of the paediatric tonsil were stained positive with CDHR3. Submucosal glands in the bronchus region also stained positive. However, adult pneumocytes did not express CDHR3. To quantify and compare the expression of CDHR3 between asthmatic and non-asthmatic subjects. The CDHR3 expression was normalized by the expression of a housekeeping gene (beta-actin) and measured by quantitative PCR. A pair-wise comparison between non-asthmatic(n=9) and asthmatic (n=10) school-age children was done on the nasal and nasopharyngeal epithelial cell directly obtained from subjects by scraping the inferior turbinate and swabbing the nasopharyngeal epithelial lining. The expression of CDHR3 on the nasal scrape and nasopharyngeal epithelial swab did not differ between the two sites and between non-asthmatic and asthmatic children. The limitation of this result is that we could not obtain bronchial and lung tissues from asthmatic subjects during the study period. Those subjects who underwent lobectomy were not diagnosed with asthma. Further analysis of the CDHR3 expression in the NP-epithelium of subjects from different age-groups and disease entities was done by evaluating the flocked nasopharyngeal swab (FNPS) specimens (n=78). School-age children aged 12-15 recruited in a rhinitis study(n=20) expressed a significantly higher level of CDHR3 than the pre-school children aged 3-6 years-old recruited in a community study and tested positive with influenza virus (n=19), the adult subjects who had to undergo a minor operation to remove nasal or NP-obstructing tissue (n=19) and patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) (n=20). The corresponding RV genotyping for the COPD subject was published (Part C, Section 8.2). To compare the expression of CDHR3 amongst the proximal and distal airways in vivo, we extracted the mRNA of the fresh human NP, bronchial, and lung tissue. CDHR3 gene expression was the highest in the nasopharyngeal epithelial tissue, followed by bronchial tissue. Lung tissue expressed the lowest CDHR3, and it was significantly lower than those in NP-epithelia (p <0.05). Lastly, we quantified the CDHR3 expression in the in vitro models. Basal cells of the human nasopharyngeal epithelial cell (HNPEC) and human bronchial epithelial cell (HBEC) cultures did not express any CDHR3 mRNA. Along the air-liquid interface (ALI) culture, the CDHR3 was upregulated. On day 21 ALI, the HNEC and BEC expressed an average of 29±18 copies per 100,000 beta-actin expression and1303±2 copies per 100,000 beta-actin expressions, respectively. In the nasopharyngeal and bronchial organoid, they expressed 98±2 and 298±2 copies per 100,000beta-actin expression, respectively. Objective 2: Ex vivo bronchial and lung tissues were collected from subjects who underwent lung lobectomy. Tissues were cut into standard size and subjected to sterile saline washing before the inoculation of RVs. Tissue snippets were submerged in equal volume and concentration of RVs for2 hours at 37oC for virus attachment. The tissue snippets were then washed3 times in 5ml sterile saline. Next, infected snippets were transferred onto a sterile surgical sponge in a 12-well plate with 1.5ml culture medium to create an air-liquid interface. At 2, 24, 48, 72 hours post-infection (hpi), 140ul of the culture supernatant were collected for virus quantification. The replication kinetics of RV-A16, RV-B14, and RV-1b was evaluated by virus titration using H1-HeLa cell in a 96-well plate format and expressed as 50% tissue culture infectious dose per ml (TCID50/ml). In contrast, that of RV-C15 was evaluated by viral gene quantification by qPCR. The viral load along the experiment time course was plotted subject by subject, and the area under curve was calculated as the overall viral load for comparison. RV-A16 replicated significantly more in bronchial than in lung ex vivo cultures (p<0.04), while RV-C15 had a trend to replicate more in the lung than in bronchial cultures (p=0.079).RV-B14 and RV-1b did not have tropism differences between these two respiratory ex vivo cultures. In bronchial ex vivo culture, RV-A16 (p<0.016) and RV-B14 (p<0.018) replicated significantly more than RV-1b while no difference was found in lung culture. Ex vivo culture of nasopharyngeal biopsy had been available for infection experiments in the early stage of the project. However, due to the procedural change in the ENT clinics, the nasopharyngeal biopsies were no longer accessible when the funding became available. Earlier results in our laboratory indicated that RV-A30 replicated better than RV-A81 (p<0.016)and RV-A89 (p<0.008) significantly. To supplement the lack of RV-C tropism data in the nasopharynx, we used 2D differentiated ALI cultures and novel 3D airway organoids(AOs) derived from the nasopharynx and bronchus to address the susceptibility of these models to RV-A16 and RV-C15. HNPECs and HBECs were dislodged from the FNPS or isolated from the bronchus after protease digestion and cultured in expansion medium. Basal cells were seeded on 24-well transwells and air-exposed with ALI-Differentiation medium. Cultures on ALI-D21 onwards were used for infection. To construct 3D AOs, ALI cultures at ALI-D18 were detached and cultured in matrigel. These epithelial fragments were cultured with AO medium to form 3D organoids. AOs were used until the average AO diameter >200μm with ciliary movement. ALI cultures were infected on the apical side with RV in a viral titer of 2×10^8 viral RNA (vRNA) copies/ml for 2h at 37oC. Infected cells were washed and replenished with 600μl ALI-Diff medium in the basolateral compartment. Supernatants were collected by incubating 200μl of ALI-Diff medium in the apical compartment for 20min at 2, 6, 24, and 48hours post-infection. Viral RNA was extracted for viral RNA copy quantification. NP organoids (NPOs) and bronchial organoids (BOs) were washed with Advanced DMEM/F12 twice to remove matrigel and mechanically disrupted by pipetting up and down with a P10 pipette tip until openings of the organoids can be observed. Disrupted AOs were immersed inRV at 2×10^8 vRNA copies/ml at 37oC for 2h. AOs were washed and re-embedded in matrigel. Supernatants were harvested at 2, 6, 24 and 48hpi. Viral RNA levels at 2 hpi represented viral binding and the net increase in the viral gene copies from 2hpi to later time point represented viral replication. RV-A16 bound significantly better than RV-C15 in ALI cultures (p<0.01) and replicated better than RV-C15 with significantly higher viral load detected in ALI-HNPECs and ALI-HBECs. The net increase in RV-A16 level (24hpi-2hpi) in ALI cultures was also higher than RV-C15. RV-C15 failed to replicate in ALI-HNPECs and a robust viral replication of RV-C15 was only observed in ALI-HBECs. In AOs, the binding affinity of RV-A16 and RV-C15 were comparable. RV-A16 replicated productively in NPOs and BOs, while productive replication of RV-C was only found in BOs. Nevertheless, the net increase (48hpi-2hpi) was lower in BOs infected with-C15 when compared to RV-A16. We found a significant positive correlation between CDHR3 and FOXJ1 gene expressions amongst the ALI and AO cultures. The viral load of RV-C represented by a net increase in vRNA copy numbers correlated positively with CDHR3 and FOXJ1 gene expressions.

24107017.label: Major findings and research outcome
24107017.value: 1. Distribution of the cell entry factor of Rhinovirus C in the respiratory samples Cadherin related family member 3 (CDHR3) gene expression was the highest in the nasopharyngeal (NP) epithelial tissue, followed by bronchial tissue. Lung tissue expressed the lowest CDHR3, and it was significantly lower than those in NP-epithelia (p < 0.05). Further analysis of the CDHR3 expression in the NP-epithelium of subjects from different age-groups and disease entities was done by evaluating the NP-flocked swab specimens (n=78). School-age children aged 12-15 recruited in a rhinitis study (n=20) expressed a significantly higher level of CDHR3 than the pre-school children aged 3-6 years-old recruited in a community study and tested positive with influenza virus (n=19), the adult subjects who had to undergo a minor operation to remove nasal or NP-obstructing tissue (n=19) and patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) (n=20). The corresponding RV genotyping for the COPD subject was published (Part C, Section 8.2). 3. Rhinovirus tropism in human ex vivo respiratory organ cultures The prototype virus of the RV-A16, RV-B14, and RV-C15 were selected as the representatives to study the virus tropism in human bronchial and lung tissues. RV-A16 replicated more in bronchus than in lung organ cultures (p = 0.04) while RV-C15 had a trend to replicate more in the lung than in the bronchus (p = 0.08) (Part C, Section 9.1). 4. CDHR3 distribution and Rhinovirus infection in primary human nasopharyngeal and bronchial epithelial cells in air-liquid interface cultures We utilized the human NP and bronchial epithelial cell in an air-liquid interface (ALI) culture to measure the distribution of the RV-C receptor and assess the susceptibility of RVs. The RV-C receptor expressed on ciliated cells and populated more in the bronchial than the NP-epithelium. The paired ALI-cultures derived from the same donor indicated that RV-C replicated better in the bronchial than the NP epithelial cells. The RV-C infectivity positively correlated with the expression of the transcription factor for ciliogenesis (FoxJ1) and CDHR3. In general, RV-C replicated less effectively on the airway epithelial cultures than RV-A. (Part C, Sections 8.1) 5. Rhinovirus infection in primary human nasopharyngeal and bronchial epithelial organoids Nasopharyngeal and bronchial organoids were established for further assessment on the RVs susceptibility. Similar to ALI cultures, RV-A16 had a higher replication competency than RV-C15 in organoids derived from the human nasopharynx and bronchus (Part C, Sections 8.1, 9.2, and 12).

24107017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24107017.value: With the current findings, it is understandable that the number of infected cells on the airway epithelium was low. The overall effect that the rhinovirus induces on the epithelium might be better addressed in a single-cell RNA sequencing setting. The contributing cells can be picked up for further analysis. Besides, the subtle innate immunity induction observed on the epithelium might infer the importance of immune cells' contribution to the disease severity. The interactions of rhinovirus with neutrophil and eosinophil, and their cross-talk to airway epithelium would be the next step to explore. The unavailability limited number of lower respiratory tract tissue from paediatric subjects, especially for healthy control, is a common problem in studying respiratory disease pathogenesis. The development of subject-specific airway organoid may ease the future study comparing the virus interactions in organoid originating from asthmatic and non-asthmatic or healthy donors. This will certainly bring more insight into the differential responses to viruses associated with the host determinants.

24107017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24107017.value: Rhinovirus (RV) contributes to > 40% of respiratory infection, within which RV-C is a recently discovered virus. Little is known about its interaction with human airway cells. We utilized the human upper (nasopharyngeal) and conducting airway (bronchial) air-liquid interface (ALI) culture and bronchial and lung organ culture to investigate the target cells of RV and measure the distribution and the density of the RV-C receptor. In ex vivo organ cultures, RV-A16 replicated more in bronchus than in lung organ cultures, while RV-C15 had a trend to replicate more in the lung than in the bronchus. The RV-C receptor expressed on ciliated cells and populated more in the conducting than the upper airways. RV-C replicated less effectively on the airway epithelial cultures than the RV-A. The paired upper and conducting airway ALI-cultures indicated that RV-C replicated better in the conducting airway than the upper airway epithelium. The RV-C infectivity correlated positively with the expression of a transcription factor for ciliogenesis and RV-C receptor. The result indicates the critical role of ciliated cells in RV-C infection, which warrants further investigation. It also indicated that the contribution of RV tropism might at least partly reflect its disease presentation.

24163117.label: Project Objectives
24163117.value: Aim 1. Investigate the role of PPARδ in the regulation of miR-181b. The promoter region of pri-miR-181b contains a PPAR-binding site and our preliminary data shows that increasing PPARδ level increases miR-181b expression, suggesting but not proving that PPARδ directly increases miR-181b transcription; the mechanistic link between PPARδ and miR-181b is not known. We propose to: 1.1. Delineate the expression profile of PPARδ and miR-181b in inflamed human microvascular endothelial cells (HMVECs) induced by oxidized low-density lipoprotein (ox-LDL) and in aortic endothelial cells isolated from high-fat-diet treated apolipoprotein E-deficient (ApoE-/-) mice; 1.2. Investigate the effects of overexpression/knockdown by adenovirus and pharmacologically activation/inhibition of PPARδ on the expression of miR-181b and endothelial inflammation; 1.3. Reveal whether PPARδ directly binds to the pri-miR-181b promoter using chromatin immunoprecipitation and electrophoretic mobility shift assays (EMSA); 1.4. Confirm whether PPARδ increases the transcription activity of pri-miR-181b by the luciferase reporter assay. Aim 2. Examine the roles of PPARδ/miR-181b in endothelial inflammation. We showed that both PPARδ and miR-181b inhibit the expression of inflammatory cytokines and that miR-181b down-regulates nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH) oxidases (NOXs). Given that NOX4 contains a miR-181b binding site in its 3’ untranslated region (3’-UTR), we hypothesize that miR-181b directly targets NOX4. We propose to: 2.1. Examine the effects of PPARδ activation and miR-181b mimic/anti-miR on the production of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and on endothelial cell inflammation by testing for expression of inflammatory cytokines and for adhesion of monocytes to endothelial cells and; 2.2. Test whether miR-181b inhibition abolishes the effect of PPARδ on endothelial cell inflammation; 2.3. Evaluate whether miR-181b directly targets NOX4 using a 3’UTR luciferase reporter assay; 2.4. Test whether pharmacological inhibition of NOX4 or antioxidant 4-hydroxy-2,2,6,6-tetramethylpiperidin-1-oxyl (TEMPOL) blunts the pathological effects of anti-miR-181b on endothelial cells.
