24163117.label: Realisation of objectives
24163117.value: In Objective 1, we proposed to investigate the role of PPARδ in the regulation of miR-181b expression in vascular endothelial cells. To realize this objective, we first detected the expression profiles of PPARδ and miR-181b in endothelial cells and in aortic tissue of ApoE-/- mice to investigate whether there are correlations between PPARδ expression and miR-181b transcription. Our data showed that expression of PPARδ and miR-181b were suppressed in IL-1β-inflamed endothelial cells and in aortic intima of high fat diet (HFD)-fed ApoE-/- mice. Whereas the inhibited expression of PPARδ and miR-181b in IL-1β-inflamed endothelial cells and in aortic intima of HFD-fed ApoE-/- mice were both recovered by butyrate co-treatment. The similar expression profile of PPARδ and miR-181b to each other in endothelial cells and in aortic intima of ApoE-/- mice support our hypothesis that PPARδ might play a role in regulating miR-181b expression. We then examined the effect of PPARδ activation on miR-181b expression in both normal and inflamed vascular endothelial cells to verify he regulatory effect of PPARδ on miR-181b expression. Our results suggested that PPARδ activation by its agonist GW0742 and butyrate enhanced miR-181b expression in both normal and IL-1β-inflamed endothelial cells, while both enhancement effects vanished when endothelial cells were pre-treated with PPARδ antagonist, suggesting that PPARδ activation up-regulated miR-181b expression in vascular endothelial cells. Based on aforementioned data, we demonstrated that the miR-181b expression is regulated by PPARδ. The objective 1 was well achieved. In objective 2, we aimed to elaborate the roles of PPARδ/miR-181b in endothelial inflammation. Firstly, we treated endothelial cells with IL-1β and examined ROS generation and the expression of enzymes related to ROS generation and scavenging in endothelial cells in the presence or absence of butyrate. We detected increased ROS generation together with enhanced NOX2 expression in IL-1β-inflamed endothelial cells as well as in aortic endothelium of HFD-fed ApoE-/- mice, all of which were abolished by butyrate co-treatment. We also examined the expression of NOX4, iNOS, SOD1, SOD2, and XDH in endothelial cells and in aortic endothelium of ApoE-/- mice. We found that IL-1β, HFD, and butyrate had no effects on their expressions in endothelial cells. Furthermore, we activated PPARδ in endothelial cells using its agonist GW0742 and observed that PPARδ activation by GW0742 reduced ROS generation and NOX2 expression in inflamed endothelial cells when compared to IL-1β-treated endothelial cells. However, the inhibitory effects of both butyrate and GW0742 on ROS generation and NOX2 expression vanished when endothelial cells were pretreated with PPARδ antagonist GW0660. Furthermore, we both globally and endothelial cell-specifically knocked out PPARδ and investigated their effects on endothelium-dependent relaxation (EDR) and endothelial ROS generation. Data showed that both global and endothelial cell-specific removal of PPARδ abolished butyrate-mediated improvement to IL-1β-impaired EDR and abrogated butyrate-mediated prevention of endothelial ROS generation. These data suggest that PPARδ plays an important role in regulating endothelial function. To elaborate the role of miR-181b in modulating endothelial dysfunctions, we applied miR-181b inhibitor to endothelial cells via lipid transfection and investigated its effect on endothelial ROS generation and NOX2 expression in endothelial cells. Data showed that, when miR-181b was inhibited in endothelial cells, the regulatory effects of IL-1β and butyrate on endothelial NOX expression and ROS generation in endothelial cells disappeared. This confirms that miR-181b also plays an important role in regulating endothelial functions. Therefore, the objective 2 was well achieved.

24163117.label: Major findings and research outcome
24163117.value: 1. MiR-181b expression is regulated by PPARδ in endothelial cells. We observed similar expression profile of PPARδ and miR-181b in endothelial cells and aortic intima of ApoE-/- mice. By using PPARδ antagonist, the regulatory effect of IL-1β and butyrate on miR-181b expression in endothelial cells disappeared. 2. PPARδ and miR-181b mediate the protective effects of butyrate against endothelial dysfunctions. We demonstrated that butyrate protects against endothelial dysfunctions by reversing impaired endothelium-dependent relaxation (EDR) and inhibiting ROS generation and NOX2 expression in endothelium. Whereas, by using PPARδ antagonist and miR-181b inhibitor and knocking out PPARδ, we showed that butyrate-mediated protections against endothelial dysfunctions vanished. These two parts of results have been published in Pharmacological Research. Qinqin Tian, Fung Ping Leung, Francis M. Chen, Xiao Yu Tian, Zhenyu Chen, Gary Tse, Shuangtao Ma, Wing Tak Wong. Butyrate protects endothelial function through PPARδ/miR-181b signaling. Pharmacological Research, July 2021. 169: p. 105681.

24163117.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24163117.value: These studies demonstrated for the first time that PPARδ regulates miR-181b expression and have helped us to better understand the important roles of PPARδ and miR-181b in regulating endothelial function, particularly in mediating the protections against EDR and prevention of endothelial ROS generation and NOX2 expression. We will further cross-breed ApoE-/- mice with endothelial cells specific PPARδ knockout mice to look into the in-vivo role of PPARδ in protecting against endothelial dysfunction.

24163117.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24163117.value: Endothelium is a gatekeeper of cardiovascular health for its contribution to the maintenance of vascular homeostasis and vessel tone by balancing the production of vasodilators and vasoconstrictors. Loss of endothelial functions causes impaired vaso-relaxation and increased vaso-constriction, which can progress to the formation of atherosclerotic lesions and subsequent adverse cardiovascular events. PPARδ, as the most recently identified isoform of PPARs, has been demonstrated in several studies to be cardio-protective. MicroRNAs are a class of non-coding RNAs and functions by silencing gene expression post-transcriptionally. Protective roles of miR-181b against vascular inflammation and disorders have also been demonstrated in animal models and patients. However, whether miR-181b expression is regulated by PPARδ and whether PPARδ and miR-181b play roles in regulating endothelial dysfunctions remains largely unknown. We demonstrated that PPARδ plays an important role in regulating miR-181b expression and that PPARδ and miR-181b protect against endothelial dysfunction by improving impaired endothelium-dependent relaxation and inhibiting ROS generation and NOX2 expression in inflamed endothelial cells. These results demonstrated that miR-181b may be a downstream mediator of PPARδ in protecting against endothelial dysfunctions, which may become potential research and therapeutic target for cardiovascular diseases.

24209017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24209017.value: Shrinking transistor feature size through advanced lithography techniques is considered as a holy grail for the whole semiconductor industry. However, due to the delay of next generation lithography techniques, industry lithography system is stuck at 193nm wavelength, thus multiple patterning lithography (MPL) is the most viable solution in advanced technology nodes. However, even equipped with MPL, modern chip and memory designs are greatly challenged by the manufacturability and reliability issues. To overcome the issues, layout optimization is of prime importance in whole IC design flow. We argue that the conventional separate layout optimization is one of the bottlenecks to overcome the emerging manufacturability issue, while the current lithography simulation may introduce severe runtime overhead to the design closure. In this project we aim at developing systematic CAD algorithms and next generation tools for unified layout optimization and high performance printability estimation, where there is very little study to date. We will study the first unified framework analytically solving layout decomposition and OPC simultaneously, which are handled separately in conventional flow. Our methodology is able to explore whole continuous solution space, thus has great potential achieving better masks than previous flow. Besides, to overcome the limitation of conventional printability estimation, which is an important engine in both layout optimization and physical verification, we will develop an online learning method to dynamically improve the learning model. In addition, we will further investigate high performance and scalable deep learning tools for the printability estimation. New feature representation customized for this problem will be studied as well. We will partner with ASML and Cadence, both of which are leading semiconductor companies. The academia-industry collaboration promises innovative and high-risk academia research coupled with realistic industry data/benchmarks, and timely technology transfer through ASML and Cadence can benefit the 300 billion semiconductor and equipment industry. The project will also contribute to the education plan, including curriculum development, undergraduate / graduate student training, and research mentoring. 半導體行業一直在不懈的縮小晶體管的特征尺寸。在193納米工藝的限制下，多版圖光刻一直是最可靠的製造解決方案。然而，即使採用了多版圖光刻現代芯片和內存的製造一直存在著可製造性和可靠性的雙重隱患。在傳統的芯片設計流程中，分階段版圖優化也加重了這些設計隱患。在這個項目中，我們將提出一套完整的系統的CAD框架，將版圖分解和版圖優化這兩個階段高效的統一起來。我們的方法將有效地擴展芯片設計的解空間。同時，我們將探索高效的深度學習進行可製造性預測。我們將和業界領先的公司ASML和CADENCE合作，以獲得工業界的實際測試用例和重要問題。這個項目同樣將會促進相關課程設計，學生的培養。

We studied the first unified framework analytically solving layout decomposition and OPC simultaneously (A Unified Framework for Simultaneous Layout Decomposition and Mask Optimization), which are handled separately in conventional flow. Besides, to overcome the limitation of conventional printability estimation, which is an important engine in both layout optimization and physical verification, we developed an online learning method to dynamically improve the learning model. In addition, we further investigated high performance and scalable deep learning tools for the printability estimation. Moreover, we proposed an open-source framework for the layout decomposition problem. (OpenMPL: An Open Source Layout Decomposer)

24209017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24209017.value: The developed framework can be further applied for some large industrial cases under collaboration with partner companies such as Cadence and Huawei. Such sophisticated and large-size tests can enhance the flexibility and robustness of our method. At the same time, the method may contribute to practical industrial manufacture by matching our methods with industrial requirements. For example, we plan to focus on very-large layout decomposition problem, whose problem size is thousands and even millions of times the original problem. Besides the industrial extension, we plan to explore more deep learning techniques that are specifically for the target problem such as geometric deep learning.

24209017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24209017.value: Electronic Design Automation (EDA) is a term for a category of software products and processes that help to design electronic systems with the aid of computers. With the advance of the integrated circuit, a chip design and manufacture without the assistance of EDA system is no longer possible. Our project mainly handles layout optimization and printability estimation, where both of them are two indispensable steps in EDA. Also, the two steps are two main challenges in the whole EDA workflow, therefore, our research project is able to contribute to the development of EDA.

24301217.label: Realisation of objectives
24301217.value: We have successfully realized all the objectives listed in section 5.2: 1. We have developed a host of novel methods to synthesize trifluoromethylated molecules of diverse structures, including CF3-containing heterocycles, arenes, alkynes and carbonyl compounds, using fluoroform-derived CuCF3 reagents. 2. The generality of the developed methods has been thoroughly studied in each class of trifluoromethylation reaction with specific reagents to synthesize various trifluoromethylated building blocks. These include: (1) domino cyclization/trifluoromethylation using fluoroform-derived CuCF3 reagent and TMSCF3 for the synthesis of trifluoromethylated indoles, benzofurans and isoxazolines; (2) trifluoromethylative difunctionalization of arynes using fluoroform-derived CuCF3 reagent for the synthesis of trifluoromethylated arenes; (3) alpha trifluoromethylation of diazoesters and diazoketones using fluoroform-derived CuCF3 reagent for the synthesis of trifluoromethylated carbonyl compounds; (4) light-promoted trifluoromethylation and silver-catalyzed trifluoromethylalkynylation of unactivated alkenes using TMSCF3 for the synthesis of trifluoromethylated alkenes and alkanes; (5) trifluoromethylation of thiosulfonates using TMSCF3 for the synthesis of trifluoromethyl sulfides.

24301217.label: Major findings and research outcome
24301217.value: In this project, we have developed highly efficient and selective strategies for synthesizing trifluoromethylated molecules. Trifluoromethylated heterocycles are important for drug discovery. New methods employing the CuCF3 reagent derived from fluoroform (an industrial byproduct) were reported by our lab to synthesize pharmaceutically relevant trifluoromethylated indoles and benzofurans (Org. Chem. Front. 2018, 5, 1511; Org. Lett. 2018, 20, 1676; Asian J. Org. Chem. 2019, 8, 702). Trifluoromethylated isoxazolines were also synthesized using TMSCF3 as the reagent (J. Org. Chem. 2018, 83, 2971). These reactions rely on the novel copper-mediated domino cyclization/trifluoromethylation mechanism. Furthermore, we have extended the domino strategy to trifluoromethylative difunctionalization of arynes. Using the fluoroform-derived CuCF3 reagent, multicomponent reactions including trifluoromethylation-allylation and 1,2-bis(trifluoromethylation) were successfully developed to synthesize various trifluoromethylated arenes (Org. Lett. 2018, 20, 1179; Chem. Sci. 2018, 9, 8871). The utility of these reactions was demonstrated in the preparation of trifluoromethylated drug analogues such as melatonin, the human hormone estrone and antispasmodic papaverine. One of the newly synthesized benzofuran derivatives was identified as a promising antibacterial and antifungal agent. Encouraged by these results, we have subsequently expanded the applications of new trifluoromethylation methods to increase the structural diversity of trifluoromethylated building blocks. We reported the trifluoromethylation of alpha diazo carbonyl compounds to synthesize alpha-CF3 carbonyl compounds (Org. Chem. Front. 2019, 6, 27). Our trifluoromethylation of alkynes was applied to the preparation of anthraquinone derivatives for n-type organic semiconductors (J. Org. Chem. 2020, 85, 44). Using unactivated alkenes as a common feedstock, we developed light-promoted trifluoromethylation and silver-catalyzed trifluoromethylalkynylation protocols to synthesize CF3-containing alkenes and alkanes (Org. Lett. 2019, 21, 1521; Org. Lett. 2019, 21, 8625). More recently, we were able to use the CuCF2CF3 reagent to achieve the radical pentafluoroethylation of unactivated alkenes for the construction of allyl-CF2CF3 moieties (Org. Lett. 2020, 22, 4562). Also, perfluoroalkylation of thiosulfonates was reported by us for the synthesis of perfluoroalkyl sulfides (Org. Lett. 2020, 22, 6155). The above studies have inspired new catalytic transformations of organofluorine compounds. To this end, we reported novel Pd-catalyzed stereoselective C-F bond alkynylation and hydrodefluorination of tetrasubstituted gem-difluoroalkenes (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2020, 59, 11293; Org. Lett. 2020, 22, 5193). This project has led to the publication of 14 original research articles in international peer-reviewed journals and 7 international conference oral presentations. A total of 6 students (4 Ph.D. and 2 M.Phil.) have received training from this project.

24301217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24301217.value: The domino cyclization/trifluoromethylation strategy can be further investigated to broaden the scope of trifluoromethylated heterocycles beyond indoles and benzofurans, for example, benzothiophenes, isoxazoles and indolizines. Electrophilic trifluoromethylating reagents such as Togni and Umemoto reagents can be considered for the transformations. Recently employed CuCF2CF3 reagent can be incorporated in the domino reaction to install pentafluoroethyl groups in the heterocyclic cores which is attractive for medicinal chemistry. The newly found radical pentafluoroethylation of the CuCF2CF3 reagent has great potential and can be used to develop new radical reactions in combination with photocatalysis to synthesize perfluoroalkylated bioactive compounds. Difunctionalization of arynes and unactivated alkenes incorporating perfluoroalkylation can be explored further to construct multiple C-C and C-heteroatom bonds in one step. For example, trifluoromethylation of arynes using CuCF3 with other electrophiles such as alkyl and propargyl bromides can potentially lead to the incorporation of these groups into the trifluoromethylated arenes. Also, trifluoromethylation-functionalization of substituted alkenes is amenable to enantioselective synthesis of molecules containing stereogenic C-CF3 centres.

24301217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24301217.value: Trifluoromethylated molecules play an important role in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals and materials. With the financial support from RGC in this Early Career Scheme, we were able to develop new strategies to synthesize a great variety of trifluoromethylated compounds in high efficiency and selectivity. These methods have allowed the access to structurally diverse trifluoromethylated heterocycles, arenes and building blocks from simple precursors. Moreover, we have employed the trifluoromethylating reagent that is derived from fluoroform, an industrial byproduct and greenhouse gas, towards sustainable and environmentally friendly rection development. The outcome of the project has led to the publication of 14 original research articles in peer-reviewed international journals and 7 conference presentations. A total of 6 students (4 Ph.D. and 2 M.Phil.) have received training from this project and successfully obtained their degrees.

24301617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24301617.value: Stein's method is a powerful tool for proving limit theorems along with error bounds. Such quantitative limit theorems are useful in real applications where the sample size is finite. The method works for both normal and non-normal approximations for random variables with various dependency structures. In general, it is more challenging to use Stein's method to obtain optimal error bounds on non-smooth function distances between two distributions such as the Kolmogorov distance in one dimension and its multidimensional version. We refer to such error bounds as Kolmogorov bounds. Moreover, when applying Stein's method to a particular problem in other subjects of study, domain-specific techniques have to be developed. In this project, we plan to investigate the theory of Stein's method with regard to Kolmogorov bounds and related problems, in particular, (i) based on our previous work on Stein couplings and multivariate normal approximations, we will propose a general framework of dependency structures suitable for multivariate non-normal approximations and obtain useful Kolmogorov bounds; and (ii) develop techniques to prove concentration inequalities for multivariate distributions. We expect these new theoretical advancements of Stein's method will facilitate its further application in many other subjects of current research interest. We also plan to obtain Kolmogorov bounds by Stein's method for the following problems: (iii) normal and non-normal approximations for degenerate U-statistics, for example, De Jong's central limit theorem for homogeneous sums of independent random variables and its connections to the fourth moment phenomenon; (iv) the central limit theorem for the logarithm of the determinant and more generally linear eigenvalue statistics of random matrices; and (v) steady-state diffusion approximations in queuing models where the limit is typically non-normal and can be multidimensional. By using Stein's method together with the domain-specific techniques developed in this study, we expect to gain new perspectives and insights into these problems and to obtain new and interesting results. Stein方法為極限理論中的誤差控制提供了有力的工具。在樣本量有限的實際應用中，這種誤差控制尤為重要。 Stein方法可以用於證明相依隨機變量的正態與非正態逼近。但一般而言，用其證明在非光滑檢驗函數下的最佳誤差控制較為困難。這種誤差包含兩個一維分佈函數的Kolmogorov距離及其在高維空間的推廣。我們將對於這種誤差的控制統稱為Kolmogorov誤差控制。當Stein方法被用於解決具體問題時，我們還需要發展該問題所在領域的特殊技巧。本研究項目將針對以下幾方面發展Stein方法的理論：（1）基於我們先前關於Stein耦合和多元正態逼近的工作，提出一類適合非正態多元逼近的相依性描述框架，並得到相應的Kolmogorov誤差控制；（2）發展關於證明多元分佈的集中不等式的技巧。我們希望這些新理論能夠促進Stein方法在其它領域的應用。本研究項目還會將Stein方法用於以下問題中的Kolmogorov誤差控制：（3）退化U統計量的正態與非正態逼近，這包括De Jong的同質和的中心極限定理及其與四階矩現象的聯繫；（4）隨機矩陣行列式對數及一般的特徵根線性函數的中心極限定理；（5）排隊模型的平穩分佈的非正態及多元逼近。我們期望通過發展Stein方法和這些應用領域的特殊技巧，來得到對於這些問題的全新的處理角度和有趣的結果。

24301617.label: Realisation of objectives
24301617.value: This project aims to develop one- and multi-dimensional distributional approximations with explicit absolute error bounds, mainly by Stein’s method, and explore their applications. In Fang, Shao and Xu (2019, Probability Theory and Related Fields), we proposed a general framework of dependency structures using exchangeable pairs and obtained explicit error bounds in multivariate non-normal approximations. This addressed Objective 1. In Chen and Fang (under preparation), we initiated the study of optimal Kolmogorov bounds in multivariate normal approximations by Stein’s method of concentration inequalities. In Fang and Koike (2021c, under review), we further obtained fourth-moment error bounds with the best known rate for the convex set distance and the optimal rate for probability approximations on Euclidean balls. In Fang and Koike (2021a, Annals of Applied Probability), we considered high-dimensional central limit theorems for random vectors with general Stein identities. This addressed Objective 2. In Fang and Koike (2021b, accepted for publication by Annals of Applied Probability), we established normal approximations with optimal error bounds on the Wasserstein distance for degenerate U-statistics, in particular, De Jong’s central limit theorem for homogeneous sums of independent random variables. The error bounds are expressed in terms of fourth moments. This addressed Objective 3. In Fang and Koike (2021b, accepted for publication by Annals of Applied Probability), we also established optimal error bounds on the Wasserstein distance for the central limit theorem for Wishart random matrices. The distinguished feature of our new result compared with those in the literature is that we only need to assume existence of finite moments. This addressed Objective 4. In Braverman, Dai and Fang (2021, under review), we obtained error bounds for steady-state diffusion approximations in various queuing models where the limit is non-normal. This addressed Objective 5.

24301617.label: Major findings and research outcome
24301617.value: It is of wide interest to bound the absolute error in probability approximations and this is the main topic of this project. Our main tool is Stein’s method. In Fang, Shao and Xu (2019, Probability Theory and Related Fields), we proposed a general framework of dependency structures using exchangeable pairs and obtained explicit error bounds in multivariate non-normal approximations. In Fang and Koike (2021c, under review), we obtained fourth-moment error bounds in multivariate normal approximations with the best known rate for the convex set distance and the optimal rate for probabilities on Euclidean balls. In Fang and Koike (2021a, Annals of Applied Probability), we considered high-dimensional central limit theorems for random vectors with general Stein identities. In Fang and Koike (2021b, accepted for publication by Annals of Applied Probability), we established normal approximations with optimal error bounds on the Wasserstein distance for degenerate U-statistics, in particular, De Jong’s central limit theorem for homogeneous sums of independent random variables. The error bounds are expressed in terms of fourth moments. we also established optimal error bounds on the Wasserstein distance for the central limit theorem for Wishart random matrices. The distinguished feature of our new result compared with those in the literature is that we only need to assume existence of finite moments. In Braverman, Dai and Fang (2021, under review), we obtained error bounds for steady-state diffusion approximations in various queuing models where the limit is non-normal. Other related work includes: (i) Wasserstein-2 bounds in normal approximation under local dependence (Fang (2019)), (ii) A refined Cramér-type moderate deviation for sums of local statistics (Fang, Luo and Shao (2020)), (iii) Arcsine laws for random walks generated from random permutations with applications to genomics (Fang et al. (2021)), (iv) Normal approximation and fourth moment theorems for monochromatic triangles (Bhattacharya, Fang and Yan (2022)), (v) Cramér-type moderate deviation for quadratic forms with a fast rate (Fang, Liu and Shao (2021)).

24301617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24301617.value: Several problems are left open by this project, in particular, regarding multivariate and high-dimensional approximations. (i) Moderate deviations in chi-square approximations for dependent random vectors with explicit dependence on dimension. Motivated by chi-square tests, when a random vector W is asymptotically standard normal, it is desirable to obtain a relative error bound on the approximation of P(|W|>r), where | | denotes the Euclidean norm. However, such a bound is only known for the independent case. With the recent development of Stein’s method for Cramér-type moderate deviations, we can deal with sums of locally dependent random vectors and multivariate U- statistics, which are most relevant for statistical applications. We are currently investigating improved relative error with explicit dependence on dimension in chi-square approximations with skewness correction. (ii) Open problems in high-dimensional central limit theorem. High-dimensional CLT is a relatively new topic, but has already attracted researchers from the fields of probability, statistics, and econometrics. Thus, I believe the next few decades will see high-dimensional CLT become an extremely fruitful and exciting area of research. Notably, two fundamental questions in high-dimensional CLT remain open, one regarding the optimal Berry-Essen bound and the other regarding self-normalized high-dimensional CLT.

24301617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24301617.value: Probability approximations with finite sample error bounds are of wide interest in practice. This project established new error bounds in normal and non-normal approximations for both one- and multi-dimensional approximations of possibly dependent random variables. The main tool we used is Stein’s method. In this project, we have proposed a general framework of dependency structures using exchangeable pairs and obtained explicit error bounds in multivariate non-normal approximations. We have also obtained the best known error rate for the convex set distance and the optimal error rate for probabilities on Euclidean balls and hyperrectangles. We have applied our theoretical results to normal approximations of degenerate U-statistics, Wishart random matrices, and steady-state diffusion approximations in various queuing models where the limit is non-normal. We expect these new theoretical developments as well as applications will enrich the asymptotic theory in probability and large sample theory in statistics and many other areas.

24301817.value: 有機塗覆水滴的分子模擬

24301817.label: Project Objectives
24301817.value: To study the mechanism of gas uptake by water droplets and how this is affected by different organic coatings To explicitly study how two coated water droplets interact with each other and how the organic coats will provide possible mechanisms for coalescence of water droplets To construct a reactive model that takes into account the reactions of N₂O₅ in water droplets and investigate how this affects gas uptake of coated water droplets

24301817.label: Realisation of objectives
24301817.value: Objective 1) Gas sorption by atmospheric droplets is one of the important pathways for atmospheric droplets to grow. We first started our project by understanding how common atmospheric gases (H₂O, N₂O₅, SO₂, and O₃) are absorbed by pure aqueous droplets. We analyzed these systems in terms of thermodynamics to understand the driving forces of the solvation. In particular, we calculated the free energies of solvation for these gases and analyzed them in terms of the energetic and entropic contributions. For the energetic contribution, the details largely depend on the intermolecular interactions between the gas molecule and water and do not appear to have a general trend. However, for the entropic contribution, an important discovery was the link between the entropic change of solvation and the change in the dynamics of water as measured in the mean-squared displacement. With the simulation techniques and experience from modeling the gas sorption for pure water droplets, we then introduced organic matter into these systems to understand how such organic coatings on water droplets can alter these sorption processes. One of the most important parameters for gas uptake is the mass accommodation coefficient α, and we determined how different organic coatings as well as different gases affect α and how these changes in α correspond to the changes in the free energy profiles of gas sorption. Objective 2) We studied the coalescence of water droplets as one of the objectives in the project to understand the growth mechanism of atmospheric droplets. We first studied the coalescence problem with pure water droplets and analyzed this problem in terms of both thermodynamic and dynamical properties. In terms of the free energy change of coalescence, similar to the gas sorption problem, we discovered once again the relationship between the dynamics of water and the entropic change. In addition to understanding the thermodynamics of coalescence, the water droplets were brought together at various initial speeds, collision angles, and impact parameters to understand the possible outcomes of such collisions. The simulated outcomes were found to be consistent with the experimental outcomes on macroscopic scales in terms of the Weber number. With our experience of studying coalescence of pure water droplets, we then added organic matter to form coatings on the droplets. With organic coatings, one might expect the coalescence of water droplets would be hindered. Instead, what we found was that it is possible that the organic coatings from two different water droplets can first form a bridge that can help bring the droplets together. Whether organic matter hinders or aids coalescence will depend on factors, such as the chain length of the organic matter and functional groups. The possible outcomes of the collisions between two organic-coated droplets become more complicated than pure water droplets. We determined the critical velocities at which these coated droplets will shatter when they collide and compared with the uncoated results. Objective 3) Dinitrogen pentoxide N₂O₅ is one of the most common air pollutants in the atmosphere. It reacts with water to form nitric acid in the atmosphere. To simulate this reaction, ideally, one would carry out a full quantum mechanical (QM) calculation to account for the bond breaking and formation. However, such QM calculations would be exceedingly expensive for a reasonably large droplet containing a few hundred water molecules or more. Our solution to this problem was to build a reactive classical model parameterized using data from the first-principles QM calculations based on the framework of multiscale models, which utilize accurate reference data from a small system to obtain model parameters that are used to study larger systems. We obtained such reference data from ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations based on density functional theory (DFT). While it is challenging to collect enough reference AIMD data to calculate converged properties of the droplets, we gathered enough of such data from CV-path sampling for parameterizing our classical reactive model. With the reactive model, we then analyzed its behavior in the water droplets in the presence and absence of an organic coating in the context of gas uptake. In summary, we have realized all the objectives, and a summary of the major findings is provided below.

24301817.label: Major findings and research outcome
24301817.value: By molecular dynamics simulations, we determined the free energy of solvation for different common atmospheric gases in pure and organic-coated aqueous droplets. By analyzing the energetic and entropic components, we elucidated the driving forces for gas uptake in each setup. We calculated the mass accommodation coefficient α for estimating the probability of gas uptake upon a collision and analyzed how an organic coating would alter α. (J. Chem. Phys. 2018 & J. Phys. Chem. C 2019 [this paper acknowledged the internal CUHK codes 2191132 and 2192132 for this RGC grant instead of the RGC code 24301817]) In particular, dinitrogen pentoxide N₂O₅ is one of the most important atmospheric gases, and we utilized multiscale modeling to have successfully built an efficient reactive N₂O₅ model. This accuracy of the model compares well with that of AIMD since it utilized AIMD as reference data. Moreover, its efficiency is orders of magnitude faster because no explicit electronic degrees of freedom are taken into account. This model allowed us to understand how the reactivity affected the free energy of solvation and the gas uptake. We also analyzed how the dynamics of a solute molecule changes as a function of distance away from the interface, and were initially surprised by the observed slower dynamics near the interface. It turns out that such observations are related to the rich topic of hindered diffusion near both fluid-fluid interfaces and fluid-solid interfaces (Soft Matter 2018 & Langmuir 2020 (ACS Editors’ Choice)). We also sought to understand how organic coatings affect the coalescence of water droplets and found that organic coatings do not necessarily hinder the coalescence of water droplets. Instead, in certain cases, the organic coatings from two different droplets can first form a bridge that can sequentially bring the droplets together. By varying different initial conditions of collisions, such as initial speed, collision angle, and impact parameter, we mapped an outcome diagram as a function of these initial conditions that shows which initial conditions lead to shattering, stretching separation, or coalescence. For the case of pure water droplets, our results compared well with experimental data in terms of Weber Number. (J. Phys. Chem. C 2018 & J. Phys. Chem. C 2020) In summary, with the support of this project, we were able to train three PhD students who subsequently received their PhD degrees, published six peer-reviewed international journal papers, and presented our findings in 6 regional and international conferences as listed in Part C.

24301817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24301817.value: Organic matter is ubiquitous in the atmosphere. It is critical to understand how organic matter affects the physical and chemical properties of atmospheric aerosols. With better computing power and algorithms, while we are now able to simulate bigger droplets, we should also add additional complexity to the simulated droplets to achieve a more realistic representation of atmospheric aerosols. Adding organic matter to the water droplets, as in this funded project, was a major step in the direction of simulating more realistic droplets. Furthermore, what we would like to do next is to incorporate inorganic salts that commonly exist in these droplets and see how the ion effects can alter the different properties of the droplets, especially for the gas sorption and coalescence processes. Another important area that we would like to understand more is the concentration effects of the gas in the context of gas sorption. Most experiments have been concerned with the gas solubility/uptake when the concentration is low (where Henry’s law is applicable). It is both practically and theoretically important to understand how the gas sorption is altered when higher concentrations are considered.

24301817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24301817.value: While organic matter can contribute up to 90% by mass in atmospheric aerosols, our understanding of their roles in different atmospheric processes remains limited. This project sought to elucidate how the presence of organic matter alters gas uptake and coalescence of water droplets in terms of the molecular details revealed by computer simulations. It is exceedingly difficult to study these atmospheric processes that happen near the aerosol interfaces experimentally because of the large surface fluctuations. However, molecular simulations that we carried out in this project allowed us to study these problems with molecular details, collect sufficient statistics of these systems at well-controlled temperature and pressure, and analyze the different properties of droplets in the presence and absence of organic matter. Not only could our results be compared against published experimental data, but these simulation results also revealed the driving forces of the gas sorption and coalescence processes. Our simulations served as an early example of simulating atmospheric aerosols with more realistic composition on molecular scales.

24304317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24304317.value: The aim of this proposal is to test the strong-field dynamics of gravity using the Advanced LIGO-Virgo network. In particular, we propose a program to further develop and deploy our Bayesian-model-selection-based test of general relativity that has been shown to be statistically more robust and better suited for combining information from multiple sources. Gravity is the weakest force known, yet it controls most of the Universe's large-scale behaviour. Despite the importance of Einstein's general relativity to our understanding of gravity, it was relatively poorly tested in the dynamical strong-field regime where its effects are the strongest. Moreover, some scientists consider Einstein's description of gravity incomplete due to its inability to be unified with the other quantum forces of Nature. Instead, it is usually assumed that general relativity is the classical limit of some quantum gravity theory. An important aspect of the dynamical nature of gravity is the existence of gravitational waves, ripples in the fabric of spacetime. These waves encode the dynamics of the merger of two black holes and therefore carry information about the strong-field regime of gravity, a regime where we might find a sign of a quantum gravity theory. In February 2016, LIGO-Virgo collaboration announced the first ever direct detection of gravitational waves, and a second detection was reported soon after. These two detections, emitted by binary black holes systems, have enabled us to test general relativity close to black holes where the environments are extreme. So far, these tests have not reported any significant deviations from general relativity. Nevertheless, these tests are either assume a specific alternative theory (of which there are many), or do not allow the combination of multiple detections to arrive at better insight. We propose a multi-level program that targets the utilisation of our Bayesian model selection method, which has been shown to be theory agnostic and makes optimal use of multiple sources. To achieve this, we propose to enhance our software algorithms, to improve the description of binaries, and increase our understanding of the systematic effects of neglected physics. As the era of regular gravitational-wave detections is approaching, this program will shine a unique light on the force that dominates the Universe. 這個計劃的目的是要使用先進雷射干涉重力波天文台-處女座干涉儀網絡(Advanced LIGO-Virgo network)來測試重力的強場動力學行為。我們計劃進一步發展及改良我們的基於貝斯模型選擇的分析方法(Bayesian-model-selection-based)，並用此來檢驗廣義相對論日是否和現象吻合。該方法已經在統計學上被証明是較為強大和更適合用於整合多個訊號來源的資訊的方式。 重力是我們知道自然界最弱的作用力，但是它卻主宰著宇宙大部分大尺度的行為。縱使愛因斯坦的廣義相對論對理解重力是十分重要的，在重力效應最強的動態強場的範圍下對該理論的測試卻相對地少。此外，由於愛因斯坦對重力之描述並不能兼容自然界其他的量子作用力，科學家們普遍認為廣義相對論是某些量子重力理論之古典近似。 重力波，即時空的漣漪，是重力的動態性質中重要的一個特性。這些重力波含有兩個黑洞合並時的資訊，因此這些波帶有和重力強場範圍有關之資訊。通過研究這個範圍之現象，我們或許可以找到發展量子重力理論的線索。LIGO-Virgo 合作機構於2016年2月公佈了第一個被直接測量成功的重力波之報告，不久後更發表了第二次探測之報告。 這兩次重力波信號都是由雙黑洞系統所輻射出來的，這使得我們可以檢驗在黑洞附近的極端環境下，廣義相對論是否和現象吻合。然而，目前的檢驗不是假設了特定的替代理論(這種理論有很多種)，就是不允許整合多次探測結果，結果顯示並沒有和廣義相對論有明顯的偏差。 我們提出了多層次的計劃，旨在使用我們的貝斯模型選擇方法來分析重力波，以及最佳化使用多個來源的訊號。為了達到這個目的，我們計劃去優化我們的演算法、改良對雙星系統之描述以及進一步了解被忽略的物理對系統的影響。一個規律地探測重力波的時代即將來臨，在了解主宰宇宙的作用力的路途上，這個計劃將會為我們點上一盞特別的明燈

24304317.label: Realisation of objectives
24304317.value: NB: Citations from the (numbered) research output (Part C) are denoted with curly brackets {}, whereas external citations are denoted with square brackets [] and can be found at the end of the text. The overall achievement of the objectives has been very successful, leading to eleven published articles, eleven presentations at international conferences and six postgraduate theses (including a postgraduate thesis award). It should be further noted that the PI is an active member of the LIGO Scientific Collaboration, which is a scientific collaboration of international physics institutes and research groups dedicated to the search for gravitational waves using the United States-based LIGO detectors. In particular, the PI is the co-chair of the Testing General Relativity Working Group of the LIGO Scientific Collaboration. As stated in the proposal, the work of this project is therefore also in part for publications of the collaborations. These publications have not been included in the research output, because it is impossible to acknowledge individual project codes in an author list with more than 2000 authors. However, in the assessment of the realisation of the research objectives, work done for the collaboration is taken into account. 1. Bayesian methods have been used in tests of general relativity since the first seminal paper that analysed the first detection of gravitational waves [1]. While the development of the Bayesian analysis tools to compute the Bayes factor needed to do model selection has been concluded (not suitable for publication). However, the lack of computational resources remains the biggest limitation in fully conducting model selection in tests of general relativity. Nevertheless, ongoing research from our group is designed to address this issue by using alternative methods to characterise and integrate the posterior distribution, including variational Bayes. Although this work is beyond the scope of this project, it was initiated to address this objective. This objective remains unsolved but significant progress is on the way and we hope to finalise this item soon. 2. The biggest improvement in tests of general relativity since the first detection of gravitational waves [1], is the combination of information from multiple sources. This is a collaboration-wide paper on tests of general relativity using events from the first observation run of the LIGO detectors. My role in this paper is the development of the combination of information from multiple sources (Figs. 3 and 4), which represents the tightest constraints on General Relativity at that moment. This work was further extended in Ref. [2], for which the work was developed within the scope of this project, but the publication was outside of the period of this proposal. While improvements can always be made, this objective as stated in the original proposal can be considered complete. 3. In many ways, this objective has the broadest scope of the objectives. We have conducted research on a broad set of additional physical effects, including alternative dispersion relationships {3}, ultra-light boson {6, 11}, and core-collapse supernovae {1} and primordial black holes {10}. While improvements can always be made, this objective as stated in the original proposal can be considered complete. 4. Although the space of 'excluded' physical effects is infinitely large, we have conducted the first realistic study of the effects of excluded physics on tests of General Relativity. In Ref. {7}, we show how the omission of higher modes can lead to false deviations from general relativity when these effects are strong enough. Moreover, we study the effects of deviations from General Relativity, such as alternative polarisation content {9}, breaking of the no-hair theorem {5}, horizon effects {4}, dark matter {8} and echoes off the surface of the compact objects {2}. These publications also sparked the larger-scale paper on relating the standard set of null tests of General Relativity applied to LIGO-Virgo detections [3]. While improvements can always be made, this objective as stated in the original proposal can be considered complete. 24304317.label: Major findings and research outcome
24304317.value: NB: Citations from the (numbered) research output (Part C) are denoted with curly brackets {}, whereas external citations are denoted with square brackets [] and can be found at the end of the text. The major finding and research outcomes can be categorised as follows: Development of tests of general relativity in the context of the LIGO Scientific Collaboration. Here we have made major contributions to collaboration papers on tests of general relativity, in particular (Objectives 1 and 2) - We present tests of the consistency of the data with binary black hole gravitational waveforms predicted by general relativity. These results both for individual events and also results obtained by combining particularly strong events from the first and second observing runs of Advanced LIGO and Advanced Virgo. We do not find any inconsistency of the data with the predictions of general relativity and improve our previously presented combined constraints by factors of a few [1]. We have tested the exclusion physical effects on tests of general relativity and extended tests of general relativity with these additional physical effects (Objective 3 and 4) - We show how the omission of higher modes can lead to false deviations from general relativity when these effects are strong enough {7}. - We demonstrate the capability of measuring the physical parameters of the remnant black hole, determining parameterized deviations from the ringdown of black holes, and probing the existence of echoes {5,6}. - We introduce a test for the arbitrary mass and spin growth of inspiralling black holes {4}. - We devise methods to probe the propagation properties of gravitational waves, including polarisation and modified dispersion relationships {9, 3} - We show dark matter affects tests of general relativity and how we can devise tests to probe dark matter {6, 8, 10, 11}. - We simulate core-collapse supernovae in self-interacting massive scalar-tensor gravity {1}. [1] Abbott et al., Tests of general relativity with binary black holes from the second LIGO-Virgo gravitational-wave transient catalogue, Physical Review D, Volume 103, Issue 12, article id.122002 (2021)

24304317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24304317.value: Further development can be considered in two primary axes. Firstly, the further construction of faster and stable means for analysing gravitational waves is essential to perform Bayesian inference (model selection in particular). This work is ongoing and may be the subject of future grant proposals. Secondly, we will continue our efforts in including additional physics into tests of general relativity. These could be targeted on specific astrophysical effects (e.g. environmental effects) or generalised classes of extensions to general relativity (e.g. effective field theories).

24304317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24304317.value: Gravitational waves, ripples in the fabric of spacetime, are predicted by Einstein's theory of General Relativity. These waves encode intimate information about the movement of massive celestial objects and allow us to see the Universe in a way not possible before. Gravitational waves can also be used to test General Relativity by accurately tracking the movement of black holes and comparing them to the motion predicted by General Relativity. This project has expanded the area of validity of these tests and made them more robust against errors, paving the way for the most precise test of the theory that has far-reaching consequences for our understanding of the Universe.

24304617.value: 量子網絡對於可擴展量子計算和量子通訊都很重要。量子中繼器是量子網絡的核心，他需要有足夠長的相幹時間，能夠通過光子實現臨近節點的糾纏。量子中繼器沒有被完全的實現，因為目前的量子光學存儲的相幹時間不足以持續到實現臨近節點的糾纏，也沒有辦法做遠距離糾錯操作。最近，我們實驗了把光子的量子態存入鑽石的氮缺陷的單個核自旋上，並實現了存儲了超過11秒的新的記錄。由於氮缺陷有好幾個量子比特的存儲功能，用作量子通訊糾纏功能的糾纏蒸餾算法有可能被實現。這樣就可以做出完整功能的量子中繼器。 在這個項目裏，我們的目標是演示出基於氮缺陷的量子網絡。在這個項目中，我們要搭建糾纏光子源，他們的頻率和氮缺陷的共振頻率一致。我們用這個糾纏光子源去糾纏兩個氮缺陷，並實現量子糾纏蒸餾算法。 我們計劃用光子吸收的辦法實現這個方案。同光子發射方案比，這個方案可以糾纏不同種類的量子系統。這個系統有兩個部分組成，鑽石裏的氮缺陷做的量子節點和糾纏光子對。我們準備用兩種方案。一個方案是，糾纏光子對一個光子在637nm，一個在通訊頻率。通過對通訊頻率光子做貝爾態測量和把637nm光子存入氮缺陷裏，實現兩個氮缺陷的糾纏。第二種方案是做兩個光子都是637nm的糾纏光子對。 這個項目為基於鑽石系統的量子網絡奠定了基礎。

24304617.label: Realisation of objectives
24304617.value: In this project, the target is to develop quantum node consisting both electron spin and nuclear spins for building quantum repeater network based on NV center in diamond. We have built a low temperature confocal microscope and optically detect magnetic resonance system which consists optical cryostat, magnetic field coils, coherent light sources including lasers and photon pair source, microwave system and control system. The system can address single NV center both via coherent optical photon and microwave photon with high fidelity. With this setup, we studied NV center and nearby nuclear spins' dependence on different physical parameters such as electrical field, magnetic field and pressure/stress in both cryogenic temperatures and ambient conditions (Science 366, 1355(2019), PR Applied 13, 024041 (2020), Nature Comm12, 2457 (2021)). These studies not only bring deeper understandings on optimizing NV center properties, but also introduce new methods for quantum sensing. Furthermore, to fabricate integrated electric structure around NV center for electric controls, we invented a novel direct laser writing material method (Nature Comm.11, 5334 (2020)). With this method, we can make microwave antenna around NV center and deliver fast microwave controls. These results address Objective 1, and partially address Objective 2 and 3. We systematically studied photon interaction with electron spin of NV center and nearby C-13 nuclear spin systems (PRA 100, 022307 (2019)). The electron spin and nuclear spins are entangled via hyperfine interaction among them. Depending on the time of evolution, the photon that in resonance with ms=0 spin state can project the C-13 spin into one of two eigenstates. Besides a new way of polarizing nuclear spins, this method can also be used to make information storage in remote qubits. We then developed a new method to readout this information stored in these remote qubits spin with high fidelity (manuscript currently under review in PRL). This method can even readout stored quantum information spin despite strong classical noise around the qubit. Combing all these new method, one can input and retrieve information from remote qubits. These results address Objective 2, 3 and partially Objective 4. While entangling two qubits via dipole-dipole coupling has been accomplished, entanglement via photon link is much more challenging. We have made estimation on the success rate of establishing entanglement between two NV centers with optical photon. With around photon absorption rate below 0.001 in our current setup, the entanglement rate will be lower than one per 5 seconds. This makes the experimental realization difficult. We are currently developing high finesse optical cavity system that works in closed cycle cryostat despite existing vibrations in order to boost up the absorption rate. Although we didn't accomplish this during the period of this grant, this target will certainly be addressed in the very near future. In this project, we have explored research areas bigger than the original proposal. We have also developed much more techniques in various fields. During those researches, we spent majority of the grants on equipment and parts via general expenses. The total value of them matched with the proposed equipment cost and GE costs in the original proposal. On the other hand, we focused on educating our students and let them lead the research in early stage. For example, the paper published in Science was led by three MPhil students. In this way, we saved funding on manpower part but achieved high quality research works and education results.

24304617.label: Major findings and research outcome
24304617.value: We have designed and constructed a single NV center addressable low temperature confocal microscope and optically detect magnetic resonance system with high fidelity readout and controls. It consists optical cryostat, magnetic field coils, coherent light sources including lasers and photon pair source, microwave system and control system. We have designed a novel way of using resonant photon and interactions between electron spin and C-13 nuclear spin to project C-13 nuclear spins into different eigen states. This gives a novel way of optical control of nuclear spins. We have invented a new way of reading out remote spins despite enormous classical noise around it. Therefore, the stored quantum information in these quantum memory can be retrieved in noisy conditions in quantum communications. We have studied NV center's dependence on stress, electrical field, magnetic field. Based on these knowledge, we have developed novel methods of using NV centers to sense in large ranges of working conditions for field distributions, quantum phase transitions. We have invented a novel method of direct laser writing of patterned materials on various substrates with high conductivity and performance. With this method, we can write high quality electric structure near chosen NV centers.

24304617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24304617.value: Now we can manipulate C-13 nuclear spins further from NV center than before, we can study their interaction with resonant photon. With several of these nuclear spins under control, we can make the system a small quantum simulator. On the other hand, by using high quality optical cavity, we can boost up the optical cross section of NV center under resonant excitation by orders of magnitude. We can then use single photon for quantum gates and optical control of both electron spin and nuclear spins. These operations will be useful for quantum information devices such as quantum repeater, quantum switches and quantum computing nodes.

24304617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24304617.value: Quantum network is believed to be ultimate secure due to quantum non-clone theorem. Long distance quantum network requires the quantum version of "router" which is called quantum repeater. Quantum repeater has to be able to store or retrieve resonant photons which work as the flying qubit to create long distance entanglement. This project is to design quantum repeaters based on nitrogen vacancy center in diamond. In this system, one can use single electron spin, nuclear spin as quantum memory for quantum information and use them to communicate with resonant photon. In this project, we experimentally establish the platform. We managed to use photon to control the state of C-13 nuclear spins. these information can be readout with high fidelity via novel measurement scheme. Also we developed fabrication methods for creating devices in diamond materials. We also invented new quantum sensing methods to probe various quantum phase transitions.

24500417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24500417.value: Informed traders play a central role in price formation in financial markets. With their information advantage, informed traders exploit other trading parties by trading before information is widely available. Insiders, by definition, have favored access to private information about a given firm and are subject to increased scrutiny. Regulations require that insiders publicly reveal their trades within a short time window to limit information asymmetry. However, the market’s reaction to insider trading disclosure is surprisingly slow. Instead of a one-time price jump right after the full revelation of insider trading, the insider trading report predicts a slowly accumulated abnormal market return. In this project, we will propose and test a rational explanation for this sluggish price discovery process. In standard microstructure models (Kyle, 1985; Glosten and Milgrom, 1985), traders are uncertain about the shock at the final date, and an insider’s private information will be fully revealed once her position is reported. In this project we introduce the uncertainty of shock timing. The insider knows information about both the level and the timing of the shock. Conditional on the same insider trading position, different shock timings are associated with various levels of shocks. Based on the reported insider trading activities, the market is not able to fully infer this information and faces the uncertainty of shock timing. The passage of time functions as a natural information device to confirm or exclude potential candidates of shock timing. Even when there is no further release of information, the fact of no news itself is still informative, thus reducing the uncertainty over time. The sluggish price discovery process reflects this information revelation process driven by the passage of time. Our project will contribute to the literature on the insider trading. It will identify the channel for the sluggish price discovery process. It will also enhance our understanding of heterogeneity in the patterns of price movement given different ex -post shock realization horizons. This project may also shed light on the content of private information possessed by insiders. 內部人交易在金融市場價格的信息傳導機制中扮演了重要角色。憑借他們的信息優勢，持有內部消息的交易者可以在信息未公開披露前從與其它投資者的交易中獲得收益。為了應對這壹問題，市場監管通常要求公司內部人士在任何公司相關股票交易之後立即披露其交易行為。然而，面對這壹公開的信息披露，市場的價格並未立即對其作出全面反映，而是表現出壹段長時間的緩慢變化。 本文嘗試對這壹現象提出壹個理性框架下的解釋並對其進行檢驗。傳統不對稱信息交易模型通常假設資產價值只在最後壹期體現，而壹旦內部人交易被完全披露，其內部信息會迅速被市場認知。在本文中，除了資產價值本身，我們還考慮另壹個因素：資產價值的變化時間。內部交易者的信息不僅包含未來資產價值的變化，同時也包含變化的時間。當市場觀測到內部交易人的交易行為時，其可能對應於多個關於價值變化和變化時間的組合。市場價格的緩慢反應來源於時間的流逝本身包含了信息：沒有價值變化意味著價值變化之可能在未來，從而排除了近期變化的可能性。價格的時間變化本身反映了隨時間變化的內部交易披露所對應的信息。

24500417.label: Realisation of objectives
24500417.value: The project produces a working paper titled "Information Cascades and Threshold Implementation: Theory and An Application to Crowdfunding". In this paper: 1) We successfully build a model to analyze the crowdfunding platforms and AoN designs. 2) Our analysis generates interesting predictions on investor behavior in the presence of AoN policy. To be more specific, we show that investors are less concerned about potential DOWN information cascades, and are more likely to contribute when they have positive private signals. 3) On the predictions of endogenous pricing and threshold policy for the entrepreneur, our analysis shows that the entrepreneur will take the investors' behavior into account and set a higher price to increase his/her expected total proceeds. 4) We also show that as the size of the investor base increases, the entrepreneur sets a higher price. To justify the high price, the entrepreneur also sets a higher AoN target, which enhances the information aggregation in the crowdfunding process. 5) Our analysis shows that AoN design helps information aggregation and improves funding efficiency. As we discussed above, all objectives have been reasonably achieved.

24500417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24500417.value: This project studies the ``All or Nothing'' (AON) rule. It is a predominant mechanism in the crowdfunding market that returns contributions to investors if the project fails to achieve a predetermined level of support --- an ``all-or-nothing'' (AoN) threshold. The crowdfunding market involves sequential actions from privately informed investors, observational learning, and is prone to information cascades. We incorporate endogenous all-or-nothing thresholds in a classic model of an information cascade and show that the threshold implementation leads to uni-directional cascades and prevents agents' herding on rejections. Early supporters effectively delegate their investment decisions to a later ``gate-keeper'', defined as the agent that the project would be implemented for sure when she supports. Agents with positive signals are willing to do so because the ``gate-keeper'' observes more actions and may make more efficient investment decisions. On the other hand, investors with negative signals do not want to support because if they deviate, their actions would mislead follow investors, leading to inefficient project implementations. Consequently, entrepreneurs are no more concerned about herding on rejections. They commit a higher ``AoN'' threshold to encourage more information aggregation to justify higher prices they charge. As a result, proposal feasibility, project selection, and information aggregation all improve, even when agents have the option to wait. Novel to the literature, equilibrium outcomes depend on the crowd size, and in the limit, efficient project implementation and full information aggregation ensue.

24502017.label: Realisation of objectives
24502017.value: We first collect data from China's industry yearbooks and compile a new dataset on the country’s television sector from 2005 to 2017. Additionally, we extend our data collection to also include data of China’s radio programs for the same period of time. We observe information on annual program broadcasting hours at the province level for different genres of media content, such as news, public-service programs and entertainment, in addition to information on annual advertising level and revenue. We use the dataset to examine not only the quantity of media provision (in terms of program time length) but also media quality measured by the proportion of non-ad content to all broadcasting. This aspect of our data makes it considerably more detailed than existing data on other media (like newspapers), for which we typically observe only the difference between ads and non-ad content, or “newsholes.” Furthermore, we obtain from a proprietary source a rich micro-level dataset on television viewership to study the private valuation of media programs among different demographic groups. The dataset covers real-time, demographic-specific viewing information for some 500 programs over a 15-day period in 2015 for 21 distinct groups, and altogether it yields more than 120,000 observations for our analysis. We then build a structural model of China's television market. On the media consumer side, there are two stages of consumer decision-making. In stage one, in each year, consumers make a binary choice of whether to subscribe to the cable service provided by a regional state monopolist. In stage two, conditioned on having cable subscription, consumers choose a television channel to watch at any occasion of time. In our model, consumers rationally expect the value of watching TV programs when making their cable subscription decision in the earlier stage. To estimate the demand function for advertising, we follow Rysman (2006). Due to the complex modeling and computation issues in running counterfactual simulations, in order to promptly make available some of our empirical results, in a working paper resulted from this project, we also study a simplified version of our media demand model. We provide a discussion of the advantage of model, especially combined with our fine dataset on program-level TV ratings. The approach is also framed as the revealed-preference approach in parallel literatures. To estimate our structural model, we estimate separately taste parameters in utility functions and the ad demand function. For estimation of consumer taste parameters, we use the Method of Simulated Moments (MSM). To identify the structural parameters, we address the potential endogeneity problem of a few main variables in the analysis by using high-frequency data on TV ratings. With the data, we can use fixed-effects at a highly disaggregated level. Because of unforeseen difficulties in running counterfactual simulations, in a main working paper, we organize and deliver a set of our important findings by specifically focusing on the spillover effects of China’s rising broadband Internet development on traditional TV and radio markets. We investigate the causal effects of broadband expansion on public radio and television in China and find that rising broadband penetration has substantial negative impacts on media provision and quality. Through estimation of TV viewers’ preferences, we identify the groups of individuals who are most adversely affected in the digital age.

24502017.label: Major findings and research outcome
24502017.value: Our newly complied data-set on China’s TV and radio markets allows us to deliver a number of important stylized facts about these media industries. For instance, over the 13-year period for this study, the growth of daily broadcasting hours on public media in China is very limited (with growth rates around 0% to 3%). In comparison, radio carries proportionally more news and public-service content, while television has proportionally more leisure-oriented programs. Overall, in both radio and television, a considerable number of broadcasting hours (around 10%) go to commercial ads. In terms of ad revenue, television stations make more than radio does, and they together make about 2 billion Chinese yuan (approximately 0.3 billion U.S. dollars) annually, or about half the total amount of public expenditure on cultural activities in a province. Our main empirical findings including results from both regression analysis and structural estimation are included in a completed working paper that mainly focuses on the unintended effects of Internet development on China’s traditional media markets and another work-in-progress paper that was accepted for presentation at various international conferences (see Part C). For instance, we find significant negative spillovers of broadband Internet on both the quantity and quality of media content in China's radio and television broadcasting. By program genre, the rising broadband development leads to 29% less news, 46% fewer public-service programs, 58% fewer radio/TV series, and almost 50% less entertainment. These large effects are due to changes in both extensive margin (i.e., channel shutdown) and intensive margin (i.e., less broadcasting per channel). Moreover, the increase of broadband penetration causes the proportion of non-ad programs to decline significantly and advertising intensity to rise. By using additional micro-level dataset on television viewership, we find that individuals who are older (aged 55 and above), have a low education level (elementary school and below), or are unemployed/retired have strong preferences for news, public-service programs, and radio/TV series, while younger and college-educated individuals have strong preferences for entertainment content but show almost no interest in other genres. On the advertiser side, over the sample periods, rising broadband penetration has caused advertisers' willingness to pay per-minute of ads to drop by 84 percent. In the context of this structural model, it translates to that the value per viewers' look has gone down by 84 percent on average.

24502017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24502017.value: We will strive to extend our current results and to continuously push our counter-factual analysis. Those simulation results, together with some of the structural estimation results currently not included in the working paper (on the influence of China’s broadband Internet development on traditional media sector), will be reported in a separate, follow-up research report.

24502017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24502017.value: As broadband infrastructure provides easy access to information on the Inter net, it has large impacts on traditional media and advertising markets. In countries where media are heavily regulated, broadband Internet is often viewed as a threat to state-owned media. In this paper, we provide a first study on the spillover effects of broadband Internet on the traditional public media sector, which often has a unique social role in developing countries. Exploring new industry data and variation in China's centralized roll-out of digital infrastructure, we find that rising broadband penetration has substantial negative impacts on the provision of media content (including news, public-service programs, and entertainment) and media quality in China's local radio and television. Using additional novel micro audience data, we take a revealed-preference approach to recover the private value of media content to different demographic groups. Our results suggest that broadband spillovers on public broadcasting have the most pronounced effect on the elderly, the less educated, and the unemployed.

24503417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24503417.value: The theory of games with incomplete information has a wide range of applications in economics and other social sciences. Examples include optimal taxation, auctions, signaling models, and the insurance markets. A basic solution concept for the analysis of such models is the so-called Bayesian Nash equilibrium. There is a substantial literature that addresses the equilibrium existence problem for games with incomplete information, and has achieved great success by imposing various structures on types/actions/payoffs. Among those studies, a key technical condition has been imposed on agents’ information structures. This condition requires the information among all the agents is sufficiently disparate, and excludes many important cases. In particular, the situation that agents have (highly) correlated common information and private information is not allowed. As a result, the question on the existence of equilibria in a variety of practical environments still remains unanswered. This project aims to understand when economic settings characterized by strategic interactions possess Bayesian Nash equilibria. We plan to provide a comprehensive study of games with incomplete information, and prove new equilibrium existence results that unify and go beyond those previous works. Specifically, we shall relax the key technical restriction as mentioned above, and restore the existence of Bayesian Nash equilibria. As a byproduct, we expect to cover settings that cannot be handled by the extant results, such as auctions and price competitions with both common values and private values. In this sense, this project provides a theoretical foundation for a wide class of economic applications. Because game theory has been widely adopted as a modeling tool by a variety of fields, including economics, political science and computer science, the present research will also have a significant interdisciplinary impact. 不完全信息博弈理論在經濟學與各類社會科學中都有著廣泛的應用，比如稅收制度，拍賣制度，保險合同等具體問題的設計與分析。在研究分析這類問題時，常用的基本概念叫做貝葉斯均衡。通過添加各種條件，不完全信息博弈模型中貝葉斯均衡的存在性問題已經在過去的幾十年中被深入研究，並且取得了豐富的成果。然而在這些研究中，一個關鍵性的假設是在模型中的信息結構里，每個人所掌握的信息都需要非常不同。這個假設排除了很多我們真實生活中的常見場景，例如在一場拍賣中，每個人對於拍賣品所掌握的部分信息，會和拍賣方所散佈的公開信息緊密相關。 本項研究旨在理解貝葉斯均衡在不完全信息博弈模型中的存在性問題，其目的是對不完全信息博弈提供一個系統性的分析，並在沒有上面所提到的額外假設下證明貝葉斯均衡的存在性，以此為許多實際問題（包括拍賣，不完全信息價格競爭市場等）提供理論基礎。鑒於博弈論在經濟學，政治學，計算機科學等領域的廣泛應用，這項研究也可能會在經濟學之外的其他領域有所應用，並產生跨領域的影響。

24503417.label: Realisation of objectives
24503417.value: This project focuses on strategic environments with incomplete information. Economic applications range from auctions, to contests, to oligopolistic markets. In real-life examples, agents often have some private information regarding the underlying states; for example, in auctions, bidders typically have private valuations or some private source of information about the good. In addition, bidders may also share common information about some obvious aspects. As discussed in the proposal, existing models of Bayesian games often impose restrictive assumptions, and hence are not applicable when analyzing these applications. A key assumption in the literature is to impose some kind of “disparate information”, requiring that players’ information be sufficiently independent. As a result, games with both private and common information cannot be accommodated within such framework. In this project, I study models with both private and common information, in both static and dynamic settings. Specifically, I have analyzed the incomplete-information models in three settings. The first two settings propose new conditions for static Bayesian games with finitely or infinitely many actions. The key is that both private and common information can be formally formulated in those games. In the third setting, I propose a new model of stochastic Bayesian games in which private and common information could evolve over time. I believe these results could enhance our understanding in various important economic settings with incomplete information (Objective 1). In the three models, I show the equilibrium existence results and discuss relevant properties (purification, monotonicity, symmetry, etc.) that are important for economic applications. To demonstrate the applicability and usefulness of the results, I provide various concrete examples and show how one can analyze those examples based on our models. These new equilibrium results will be applicable and useful for applications (Objectives 2 and 3).

24503417.label: Major findings and research outcome
24503417.value: We have considered three incomplete-information settings. First, we study static Bayesian games with finitely many actions in the paper “Pure-strategy equilibria in Bayesian games”. In this work, we investigate the sensitivity of equilibrium outcomes to modeling assumptions. It is shown that the equilibrium property remains under small perturbations on the game structure. In particular, the closed graph property is characterized via the condition of “coarser inter-player information”. Second, we extend the analysis to the setting with general action spaces in the paper “Characterizing some properties of pure-strategy equilibrium in general Bayesian games”. This paper considers the general Bayesian games with infinitely many actions, correlated types and interdependent payoffs. We introduce a new condition of “coarser density weighted payoff-relevant information” and show that this condition is sufficient and necessary for the existence of pure-strategy equilibria and the existence of conditional purifications. As an application, we obtain new equilibrium existence results in discontinuous Bayesian games, which unify all the existing results in this literature. In the last paper “Discontinuous stochastic games”, I introduce the condition of “continuation payoff security”, and prove for a large class of stochastic games with discontinuous payoffs, a stationary Markov perfect equilibrium exists. I illustrate this equilibrium existence result via an application of stochastic dynamic oligopoly with firm entry, exit, and price competitions. We show that this condition is easy to verify and holds in many economic games. Importantly, in all the three settings, we allow for both private and common information, correlated types and interdependent payoffs. As a result, we are able to cover various new economic applications.

24503417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24503417.value: In the static setting, an interesting potential direction is to apply our results to concrete economic applications to obtain new results. For example, there is a large literature studying the existence of monotone equilibrium in auctions. Previous papers in that literature typically assume that bidders have private values and single-dimensional types, while in applications bidders often have interdependent payoffs and multi-dimensional types. In addition, even if one can obtain the existence of a monotone equilibrium, it is in general unclear whether such an equilibrium is Pareto efficient or not (compared with non-monotone equilibrium). As an application of our equilibrium results in static Bayesian games, we show that a monotone equilibrium exists in a class of all-pay auctions with risk-averse bidders, interdependent payoffs, and multi-dimensional types. We also show that within this class of auctions, there exists a Pareto-efficient monotone equilibrium. We expect that our results can be useful in other applications as well. In the dynamic setting, we focus on stochastic Bayesian games. As a result, we can adopt the standard recursive framework, which significantly simplifies the analysis. A promising research direction is to study general dynamic Bayesian games, which may call for new methodological development.

24503417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24503417.value: The theory of games with incomplete information has a wide range of applications in economics and other social sciences. Examples include auctions, signaling models, and the insurance markets. A basic solution concept for the analysis of such models is the so-called Bayesian Nash equilibrium. The current project provides a comprehensive study of games with incomplete information, and proves new equilibrium existence results that unify and go beyond previous works. Specifically, we study three incomplete-information settings in both static and dynamic environments. The results shed light on how to analyze strategic interactions in real-life environments. We illustrate the applications in examples of auctions, contests, and oligopolistic markets.
