24504417.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24504417.value: 金融與社會穩定：用自然災害的實證研究

24504417.label: Project Objectives
24504417.value: Evaluate how regulatory changes in the banking sector shape social resilience (as measured by employment and crimes) to natural hazards Explore the bank lending channels and assess how banking deregulations affect the patterns of bank credit to disaster-affected regions
rows: Evaluate how regulatory changes in the banking sector shape social resilience (as measured by employment and crimes) to natural hazards
Explore the bank lending channels and assess how banking deregulations affect the patterns of bank credit to disaster-affected regions

24504417.label: Realisation of objectives
24504417.value: Regarding the first objective, we aimed to evaluate how bank credit supply shapes economic and social resilience to adverse shocks induced by natural hazards. Our research achieves this objective by showing a strong connection between bank credit and local resilience to adverse economic shocks induced by the COVID-19 pandemic. We examine the ramifications of the COVID-19 pandemic as many influential economists describe the pandemic as very different from the past crises or economic downturns with respect to the cause, scope, and severity. The 2020 pandemic triggered an abrupt constriction in economic activity and thereby a surge in credit and liquidity demand. These unique features help distinguish our research from existing studies on the role of bank lending in shaping economic recoveries from natural disasters, such as hurricanes (Schuwer, Lambert, and Noth 2019) and floods (Koetter, Noth, and Rehbein 2020). To gauge economic and social resilience, we focus on how (a) total employment, (b) the employment of low-, medium, and high-income workers, and (c) domestic violence in each county respond to local COVID-19 infection rates. To measure local financial structure and provisions of bank credit, we use the proportion of small banks operating in a county, as small banks have a comparative advantage over large banks in using “soft” information for evaluating and financing small businesses. Thus, we investigate whether small banks foster economic resilience through countercyclical lending to small firms that limits reductions in employment, especially among low-income workers. We discover that employment—especially the employment of low-income workers—falls by less in counties with a greater share of small banks in response to COVID-19 cases. In particular, we find that aggregate employment falls by less and unemployment insurance claims increase by less in response to COVID-19 among counties with a greater share of small banks. We also uncover strong results regarding the income distributional implications of small banks. In response to COVID-19 infections, we find much smaller declines in the employment of low-income workers—but not smaller declines in the employment of high-income workers—in counties with a higher proportion of small banks. This finding is consistent with the view that bank credit shapes the income distributional effects of the economic disruptions triggered by COVID-19. In addition, we use the same methodology to examine whether—and show that—the intensity of domestic violence increases by less in response to COVID-19 in counties with a larger proportion of small banks. To enhance identification, we reassess the findings using an IV strategy. That is, we use an instrumental variable to identify the impact of the share of small banks on cross-county resilience to the pandemic. The instrument equals the number of mergers by out-of-state banks that affect branch structure in a county during the decade prior to the pandemic, where both the acquiring and target banks have at least one branch located in the county prior to the merger. Specifically, for a county c located in state s, the merger involves two banks that are not headquartered in state s, where each bank has at least one branch in county c. Such mergers will tend to give the consolidated bank a competitive advantage, reducing the role of small banks in the county. This is what we find: the merger instrument is negatively associated with the share of small banks. The identifying assumption is that the merger decision of two banks headquartered in states different from county c during the 2010-2019 period does not reflect local conditions that drive the county’s resilience to the 2020 pandemic. Regarding the second objective, we aimed to explore how bank lending changes in response to adverse shocks induced by hazards. We achieve this objective by showing a significant increase in credit supply, especially by small banks, in counties more heavily exposed to the adverse shocks induced by COVID-19. In particular, we evaluate the connection between changes in a bank’s lending and the exposure of its business clients to COVID-19. To measure the exposure of a bank’s business clients to the economic duress triggered by COVID-19, we first measure a county’s exposure to COVID-19, ln(cases per capita), as the logarithm of one plus the number of confirmed COVID-19 cases per 100,000 people. We then measure the exposure of a bank’s business clients to COVID-19, by computing the weighted average of ln(cases per capita) across counties in which the bank has branches, where the weights are the shares of deposits held by the bank in those counties. We call this measure Bank exposure. We define small business loans as loans with origination values of $1 million or less following the classification of Community Reinvestment Act (CRA) and measure changes in a bank’s lending to small firms in two ways: growth in the dollar amount of loans to small businesses and growth in the number of loans to small businesses. We then regress the two measures of small business loan growth on Bank exposure, while controlling for each bank’s size, profitability, capital-asset ratio, and the U.S. state in which it is headquartered. We find a positive relation between a bank’s growth in lending to small firms and Bank exposure among smaller banks but not among larger banks. The findings indicate that smaller banks increase lending to small firms more than larger banks during the pandemic. These analyses are consistent with the view that small banks have a comparative advantage in funding small firms during periods of economic duress, consequently enhancing the economic and social resilience to the COVID-19 pandemic.

24504417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24504417.value: Our research enhances understanding on bank financing and economic resilience to adverse shocks. We examine the ramifications of the COVID-19 pandemic that many influential economists describe as very different from the past crises (e.g., Bernanke 2020; Reinhart 2020). For example, the 2020 pandemic was at its core a public health emergency that triggered an abrupt constriction in economic activity and an especially severe decline in employment, whereas the GFC arose from concerns about overall financial system stability and the safety of individual banks. In light of these differences, our research offers the first investigation of the role of local bank structure in shaping economic and social resilience to the COVID-19 pandemic by exploiting high-frequency, real-time data on employment and other economic indicators. We provide novel evidence that a larger share of small banks in a county cushions the impact of COVID-19 cases on employment, especially the employment of low-income workers, and other important economic indicators.

24505917.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24505917.value: 更可能在最後時刻行騙：盈餘操縱和CEO變更

24505917.label: Project Objectives
24505917.value: I focus on following aspects of governance structure. First, taking into account earnings reversal, is manipulation incentive still exacerbated by increased pay-performance sensitivity (PPS)? Second, given this link between PPS and earnings manipulation, what is an optimal CEO-turnover decision? Third, is enhancing internal control (board monitoring function) always optimal for shareholders? Finally, in this unified governance structure, I plan to study whether exogenously enhanced reporting scrutiny (manipulation cost) mitigates CEOs' incentive to manipulate accounting reports.

24505917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24505917.value: 本文研究了增長的操縱成本對盈餘操縱、董事會監督以及CEO變更決策之間關係的影響。以往研究強調了誘發生產力和受約束的盈餘操縱之間的權衡。本文將盈餘反轉納入分析後發現這種權衡關係可能會消失：為了保證未來可操縱盈餘的範圍，CEO即使在面對增強的薪酬業績敏感性時也有可能不會提高當期盈餘。模型顯示，CEO只有在任期處於危險狀態時才會操縱盈餘，即當董事會收到一個已選項目的壞信號或收到重複的較差業績時。作為回應，董事會僅在可能發生盈餘操縱的時候對CEO進行密切監督。換句話說，在大多數情況下，董事會會戰略性地選擇做一個“橡皮圖章”。本文的結果表明，由於存在這種內生性，董事會監督和盈餘操縱會呈現出經驗研究中所得到的正相關關係。最後，模型預測指出，儘管增長的操縱成本在初始期間並未產生影響，但在達到一個特定的門檻值之後，它會開始降低盈餘操縱的程度。

24506617.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24506617.value: 高層管理團隊人力資本資源對CEO繼任與企業績效關係的影響

24506617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24506617.value: Although CEO succession is a critical event to have a great impact on firm performance, CEO succession literature shows mixed findings that CEO succession sometimes positively, negatively, or insignificantly contribute to post-succession firm performance. Based on this research gap, I propose that positive or negative effect of CEO succession can be determined by fit between origins of new CEOs (i.e., insider vs. outsider) and organizational capabilities. More specifically, I suggest that outside CEO succession can positively contribute to post-succession firm performance when top management team has sufficient generic human capital resources because they can effectively handle with uncertainty resulting from initiating new strategic change and breaking down preexisting strategic inertia of new CEO externally hired. I also suggest that inside CEO succession is beneficial for firm performance when top management teams have more firm-specific human capital resources because pre-established firm-specific and tacit knowledge of both CEOs and senior executives can facilitate more cooperation, coordination, and communication with less conflict. This study provides a theoretical implication that the effect of CEO succession is contingent upon top management team’s capability. Also, this study provides a practical implication that board of directors necessarily need to consider CEO origins and top management team’s human capital resources to determine effective new CEOs. 雖然CEO繼任是對企業績效產生重大影響的關鍵事件，但是過去有關CEO繼任的研究得出了不一致的結論，即CEO繼任對繼任后績效的影響可能是積極的、消極的或不顯著的. 爲了填補這項研究空白，我提出CEO繼任的積極或消極影響可能由新CEO的來源（即內部或外部人士）與組織能力之間的匹配程度來決定. 具體而言，我認爲，當高層管理團隊擁有足夠的通用人力資本資源時，外部CEO繼任可以為繼任后企業績效做出積極貢獻，因為他們能夠有效地處理由於啟動新的戰略變革以及打破新CEO原有戰略慣性而導致的不確定性. 此外我還推斷，在高層管理團隊擁有更多企業專屬人力資本資源的情況下，内部CEO繼任有利於公司績效，因為前後兩任CEO和高管人員的預先確定的企業專屬和隱性的知識可以促進更多的合作、協調、以及較少衝突的溝通. 這項研究的理論貢獻在於指明CEO繼任的作用受到高層管理團隊能力的影響. 此外，這項研究的實踐啓示是建議董事會需要考慮CEO的來源和高層管理團隊的人力資本資源來確定有效的新CEO.

24601617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24601617.value: The inadequate provision of open spaces in urban areas is one of the most recurrent challenges for the Hong Kong government. High-quality open public spaces can significantly increase a city’s attractiveness by encouraging business investment and improving living conditions. The aim of the proposed research is to study and assess the open public spaces in Hong Kong’s Central and Western District to provide a set of clear and practicable urban design guidelines for enhancing the district’s open spaces and thereby improving the quality of life of its residents. Hong Kong’s existing ordinance and other planning strategies do not address the design and implementation of guidelines regarding public space. As a result of the pursuit of economic development and the morphological characteristics of the territory, public space has become a marginal element of the city’s structure. Several scholars have detailed the inadequacy of Hong Kong’s public spaces, but few have suggested strategies to enhance the use of this important resource in such a high-density environment. In various districts of Hong Kong, the provision of open public spaces is well below the standard set by the Planning Department; in addition, the spatial quality of these spaces is questionable. The unsatisfactory quantity and quality of Hong Kong’s public spaces can no longer be underestimated. The aim of this project is to help to fill this gap in theory and practice by developing a pilot Public Space District Plan (PSDP) for the neighbourhoods of Central and Sheung Wan to encourage comprehensive open-space planning in these areas. A systematic survey of the study area will be conducted. The social and spatial characteristics of the district’s open public spaces will be comprehensively analysed to determine their existing resources and conditions; short- and long-term strategies to address the community’s needs will be identified; a series of guidelines and recommendations will be established to enhance the design and use of open public spaces; and comprehensive guidelines will be provided for district-level open-space planning. The results will help to compensate for the lack of a planning vision shared by stakeholders and government authorities. The urban design guidelines established will also provide a valuable point of reference for public space policy makers in Hong Kong’s Planning Department, facilitating the creation of a comprehensive and integrated planning approach at district level. The PSDP will also represent a more sensitive approach to urban renewal in the territory, offering a model for other Hong Kong districts. 市區內供應不足的開放空間已成為香港政府經常需要面對的挑戰之一。 高質量的、開放的公共空間可通過鼓勵商業投資和改善居住條件來有效地增加城市的吸引力。本項目致力於研究和評估位於香港中西區的開放的公共空間，提供一系列的清晰可行的城市設計指導方針來優化該區域的開放空間，從而改善居民的生活質量。 市區內供應不足的開放空間已成為香港政府經常需要面對的挑戰之一。 高質量的、開放的公共空間可通過鼓勵商業投資和改善居住條件來有效地增加城市的吸引力。本項目致力於研究和評估位於香港中西區的開放的公共空間，提供一系列的清晰可行的城市設計指導方針來優化該區域的開放空間，從而改善居民的生活質量。

24602217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24602217.value: 在國際政治，領導人通常以面對面談判的形式來化解衝突。若要達成協議，他們就需要清楚表明其意圖。然而，為了取得更有利我方的談判結果，領導人有時候還是會選擇回避隱暪。於是領導就陷入了這樣的兩難：邀請對方來談判可能是真誠的，但亦可能是倒過頭來利用他人的策略；表示決心的話可能是認真的，但亦可能是言過其實；說自己不能再讓步了，但可能只是為了提高自己的「保留價格」；承諾自己一定會獻忠，但可能只是為了引誘別人來實現自己不會遵守的諾言。動機可以是正面或反面，這代表著無論人說什麽，都不能直信其言。可是，領導人究竟怎樣才能表達和估計各自的意圖？ 現有的國際關係理論往往有兩個漏洞。首先，它們總認為談判是「廉價」的，忽略面對面外交為可信任渠道的可能性。於是面對面外交就與其他理論如新現實主義和理性主義成對立。其次，理論如規範建構主義和溝通行動理論，應更多從面對面外交更深理解到領導人之間猜測對方言論真假的張力。 我在本文中研究的是雙方在面對面外交時，如何以情緒助其交流意圖。借助社會心理學的最新研究，我建構了詳細的框架和假設不同情緒能有助解決不同的兩難局面。比如喜愛和希望表現出交談的興趣；憤怒傳達決心；痛苦、惱怒、憤慨指不可能再讓步；害怕協議不能達成表達出其真誠。為了測試我的假設，我藉大量的檔案如日記、回憶錄、外交電報、政府備忘錄、會議記錄、外交通訊，進行歷史上涉及面對面外交的個案研究——當中包括了1978年以色列和埃及雙方領導人在戴維營的協議，以及1980年代美國和蘇聯之間的領導人峰會。 這研究為讀者帶來數個重要消息。首先，一般而言，國際關係認為結構因素的解釋力最強——無論是物質的（如權力平衡），還是觀念的（如規範和身份）。然而，本文顯示透過面對面外交，個體因素（即領導人）也能影響國際政治的軌跡。其次，過去社會心理學家通常都是在實驗室，透過模仿和實驗研究人與人之間的交流。本文的個案研究指出，它們的研究結果即便在實驗室以外也適用。最後，透過本文理論上討論情緒的溝通作用，以及為一些歷史上具深遠影響的面對面外交進行深度個案研究，外交官員可以學習如何更妥善管理自我情緒，同時認清他人在談判時的情感。

24602217.label: Realisation of objectives
24602217.value: In the four article manuscripts I produced throughout this project, I developed a theory of the microsociology of face-to-face diplomacy based on germane insights from disciplines beyond International Relations (IR) and political science, particularly from psychology, sociology and linguistics. This theory directly contributes to the first three stated objectives. First, it provides an understanding on how leaders, in their personal interactions, ascertain each other’s intentions despite the incentives to misrepresent them. My theory posits how different emotions and communicative mechanisms (such as the leaders’ choice of words, bodily expressions, and their performance of interaction rituals) serve not only as “tells” of one’s intentions; they also derive their meaning from the particular context of diplomatic etiquette, protocols and norms of conduct (Objectives #1 and #2). Second, by redirecting scholarly attention to what transpires in the “last three feet” (i.e. at the “micro” level) of interactions between leaders as a source of change and causal significance to larger “micro” international political outcomes, this research offers a theory of agency (as opposed to structure) in international politics (Objective #3). Second, empirically, the grant has enabled me to conduct archival research and focus on writing (particularly with the hiring of a “relief teacher”) on some of the most important cases of face-to-face diplomacy between leaders in international politics (e.g. Kennedy and Khrushchev in the early 1960s; more recent examples of Donald Trump’s interactions with Kim Jong-un, Western European leaders, etc.). Thus, Objective #4 is accomplished. Finally, as said, I have produced four article manuscripts (three accepted for publication and one currently under review) with the support of this grant. This exceeds my original intention as stated in Objective #5 (i.e. to produce “two to three articles”).

24602217.label: Major findings and research outcome
24602217.value: In this research, I find that contrary to traditional wisdoms in the discipline of International Relations (IR), which has focused on more structural factors (e.g. balance of power and interests, identities, institutions, norms, [a]symmetry of information, etc.) as explanations for international politics, personal interactions between leaders – i.e. their “performance” towards each other, their “chemistry”, their temperament and personal skills, etc. – can have disproportional impact on the international relations they embody. This was clearly demonstrated in the cases I have studied.

24602217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24602217.value: More empirical research can be done beyond the mostly Western cases I have studied. I have proposed to do so in the most recent GRF proposal.

24603017.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24603017.value: 威兮其祖: 北宋改革中的禮儀政治與禮臣

24603017.label: Project Objectives
24603017.value: To examine the relationship between ritual and politics during the Minor and the Major Reforms of the Northern Song dynasty in terms of imperial ancestral rites. To explore the mentality of Song ritualists, especially the discrepancy between their political stances and intellectual interests. To demonstrate the intellectual approach of the New Learning ritualists in reviewing imperial ancestral rituals, with a special focus on the efforts made by Wang Anshi’s early disciples in ritual reforms. To shed new light on the spatial dimension of imperial rituals, such as the spatial arrangement of imperial ancestral architectures and the settings of various ritual utensils. To provide insights on the modern conception of the relationship between knowledge and power by reflecting on traditional “rule through ritual,” in which ritual scholarship served as an effective means to define, regulate, and legitimate authority.

24603017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24603017.value: Ancestral ritual serves as one of the key elements of Chinese culture. Considering the pivotal role played by ancestral ritual in shaping Chinese identity and traditional political culture in China, the proposed research explores the relationship between ritual and politics in Northern Song China (960-1127), during which ritual scholarship and statecraft underwent fundamental changes. With a focus on imperial ancestral rites, this research aims to demonstrate how Northern Song scholar-officials interpreted imperial ancestral rites as an effective ideological tool to influence real politics, such as the legitimacy of the ruling house, the degree of governmental centralization, and the role of the emperor. Specifically, this research examines scholar-officials’ endeavors to promote appropriate rituals in ancestral worship. The eleventh century witnessed the rise of new intellectual communities and the implementation of several significant institutional reforms. By scrutinizing the writings of Song scholar-officials, this research shows how scholar-officials with different political stances actively participated in the discussions on various imperial rites, including the arrangement of ritual spaces, the performance of state sacrifices, and the creation of new ritual utensils. Through an in-depth analysis of ritual discussions, the proposed research elucidates not only the shifts in ritual scholarship throughout the eleventh century, but also the political interests underlying these discussions. It deepens our understanding of the mentality of Song scholar-officials by revealing the tension between their intellectual interests and political ends. A better understanding of their mentality contributes to a rethinking of Song political conflicts, especially the factional politics in the two celebrated reforms of the Northern Song period, the Minor Reform of the Qingli era 慶曆新政 and the Major Reform of the Xining-Yuanfeng eras 熙豐變法. Hence, this research challenges the conventional portrait of Song political history as merely a confrontation between the two rival camps of reformers and conservatives. Additionally, this research also attempts to present what has been a missing link in Chinese intellectual history by analyzing the interactions among Northern Song scholar-officials in terms of ritual theories. In addition to memorials and face-to-face debates at the court, commentaries and annotations on Confucian ritual Classics served as a significant way for Song ritual experts (ritualists 禮臣) to communicate with one another and present their own opinions. In this light, this research on imperial ancestral ritual provides an insightful example of traditional Chinese scholars inventing new intellectual traditions based on the adaption and revision of established ones. 祖先崇拜及相關禮儀在中國文化中一直具有重要地位。考慮到祭祖禮儀在傳統政治中的重要性, 與及十一世紀北宋時期朝廷禮儀方面的深刻變革, 本研究計劃決定以這段時期的皇家祭祖禮儀作為切入點, 集中探討當時的禮儀政治問題。研究主要用意在於展現皇家禮儀作為一種意識形態工具如何具體影響政治和政策, 包括皇權合法性問題、皇帝個人在禮儀政治中的作用和地位, 還有儀式變化與中央集權之間的關係。 深入而言, 本研究注重的是北宋當時士大夫針對祭祖禮儀規範化的相關思考。眾所週知, 十一世紀在中國歷史上是因改革變法而被銘記的時代。慶曆、熙寧-元豐兩次變法對傳統帝制中國影響深遠。晚期帝制中國政治、社會的各方面發展都和這段時期的變化息息相關。通過仔細考察北宋士大夫的相關文字, 尤其是他們講解禮經的各類註疏, 本研究試圖顯示不同政治立場的學者和官員們在討論諸種朝廷禮儀時是如何展現分歧和共識的。這些禮儀討論包含了一些具體禮儀細節, 比如新禮器的創作, 行禮空間的改變, 或者郊祀大禮中祖先位置的安排。透過分析這些細節, 我們不單想知道禮儀討論背後的知識理念--比如當時學者們怎麼理解作為論辯論據的禮經文字, 我們更想瞭解這些討論背後所蘊含的政治因素。換言之, 我們想知道當時士大夫怎麼理解禮儀的政治含義; 在政治立場與禮儀興趣之間, 又是否存在著某種張力或落差。傳統政治史論述中, 十一世紀北宋史是保守和革新兩大政治集團之間衝突的發展史。從禮儀與政治之間的關係出發,我們或許會發現政見之別並不足以定義當時的士大夫乃至他們書寫的大歷史。更複雜的圖像蘊藏在具體細節之下。本研究集中研究皇家禮儀問題, 正是希望為反思北宋傳統政治史提供一些新視野, 發掘歷史大論述中個體思想的分與合。 最後, 本研究著重從北宋士大夫中提煉出「禮臣」這一專業團體。盡管北宋禮儀機構中的禮臣清晰認知到了他們自身的專業屬性, 由於北宋官制的特殊架構與及儒家傳統「君子不器」的說法, 時時予人一種錯覺北宋禮臣與其他士大夫官員無異, 只不過任職機構偶而不同而已。本研究從思想史角度重新審視北宋禮臣群體, 透過分析他們的奏疏和禮學撰著, 力求揭示帝制中國知識體系中新專業傳統的塑造是如何具體展開的。

24604317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24604317.value: Counseling is an emotionally intense endeavor. Most research done on emotions in counseling has focused on client emotions. This approach makes sense given the need to understand client distress so that interventions can be tailored and investigated. However, emotions also impact the counselor. Clarifying how counselors’ affective experience may influence counselors and their counseling effectiveness can improve client gains. In a previous study (Chui, Hill, Kline, Kuo, & Mohr, 2016), counselor pre-session positive and negative affect have been found to be associated with higher and lower client-rated session quality, respectively. However, it is unclear through what mechanism counselor affect influences session outcome. A potential mediating factor is empathy; a promising variable because it has been shown in other studies to change with affect and to predict counseling outcome. Nevertheless, empathy has different dimensions (e.g., physiological, behavioral, subjective), suggesting that a multimethod approach may be needed to delineate nuanced relations between affect and empathy. Counselor differences in affect regulation may also moderate the affect-empathy relation. Hence, in Study 1, empathy will be examined as a mediator between counselor pre-session affect and counseling outcome. Using counselor-client dyads from a training clinic, counselors will rate affect before sessions, and clients will rate session quality, symptom severity, and counselor empathy after sessions over the course of counseling. To reduce common method variance and to advance a multidimensional approach in empathy research, empathy will additionally be assessed and analyzed using videotapes by observer ratings and by synchrony in voice and language style. To further investigate the direct impact of affective states on empathy, an experimental design will be used in Study 2. Counselors will first be induced to experience positive, negative, or neutral affect before a session. They will then provide simulated counseling to volunteer clients (i.e., undergraduates who talk about some life problem for a small incentive). This procedure is repeated over three weekly sessions with the same client (different affect induced each time). Levels of empathy, as measured by client- and observer-ratings, and by synchrony in skin conductance and cardiac activity, will be compared across affect conditions. Counselor affect regulation will be examined as a moderator of the affect-empathy relation in both studies. Results from these studies will inform counselors about potentially counterproductive affect that interferes with empathy. Based on the findings, in- and out-of-session affect regulation strategies can be designed and tested in future studies to see if they can enhance counselor empathy and counseling outcome. 輔導是一項對輔導員情感要求高的工作。大多數有關輔導過程的研究都集中在受助者的情感上。這些研究方法對了解受助者的困擾確實有其重要性。然而，情緒也會影響輔導員。輔導員的情感如何影響輔導員及其輔導效果的釐清或許可以提高受助者從輔導中所得到的益處。 從過往的研究（Chui，Hill，Kline，Kuo，＆Mohr，2016）發現，輔導員訪談前的正面和負面情緒會分別提高及降低受助者對訪談質素的評分。然而，輔導員的情緒是如何影響輔導成效到目前尚未清楚，而輔導員的同理心可能是潛在的中介因素。這個因素值得研究的原因是在其他文獻中顯示同理心會隨著情緒而改變，亦有研究顯示同理心能夠預測輔導成效。儘管如此，同理心也有不同的向度（例如生理，行為，主觀評分）。不同的向度代表可能需要多種方法來測量同理心以釐清情緒和同理心之間微妙的關係。輔導員調節情緒能力的差異也可能影響情緒和同理心之間的關係。 因此，在研究一，我們會研究輔導員的同理心會否是輔導員訪談前的情緒和輔導成效之間的中介因素。在培訓輔導員中心，輔導員將在輔導之前評估自己的情緒，受助者會在訪談後對輔導質素和輔導者的同理心進行評分。為了減少因使用單一測量方法帶來的偏差，本研究會使用多度向方法測量同理心: 輔導員的同理心水平將透過觀察者評分及受助者和輔導員聲音和語言風格的同步進行評估和分析。 為了進一步確定輔導員情感狀態對他們同理心的直接影響，研究二將以實驗設計進行。在訪談之前，輔導員首先被引導體驗正面，負面或一般的情緒。然後，他們將向志願者提供模擬輔導。通過受助者評分，觀察者評分以及受助者和輔導員皮膚電導和心跳活動的同步，輔導員的同理心水平與不同情緒的狀態下進行比較。我們也會觀察輔導員調節情緒能力會否影響情緒和同理心的關係。 此項研究希望能加深我們對一些有可能影響輔導員同理心的情緒的了解。根據調查結果，我們在未來的研究中可以測試一些讓輔導員調節情緒的策略，探究這些策略是否能夠增強輔導員的同理心並提高他們的輔導成效。

24604317.label: Realisation of objectives
24604317.value: The four objectives were achieved via two studies. In Study 1, data from 69 clients and 49 therapists were collected over their course of therapy. The number of participants recruited exceeded the proposed 40 dyads because data collection occurred in a counselling training clinic where clients and therapists were relatively accessible. We also kept more participants in case of dropout. For Objectives 1 and 2, therapists and clients were asked to rate their mood before and after a session, and clients were asked to rate therapist empathy and session outcome after each session. Data collection was completed before the pandemic, and so all the sessions were conducted face-to-face. To minimize missing data, questionnaires were administered to therapists and clients by research assistants on site. For Objective 3, therapists completed the Difficulties in Emotional Regulation Scale before seeing any clients. Their scores were used in the analysis as a moderator to see if therapists’ emotion regulation ability changes the relationship between therapist affect and client ratings of therapist empathy and session outcome.We did not find a significant moderating relationship. The null finding was included in the initial submission of Publication #1, but it was dropped during revision at the suggestion of the editor, which explains the absence of the moderator finding in the published paper. For Objective 4, four sessions from 40 dyads were selected as proposed to investigate therapist empathy using multiple methods. Besides having client-rated empathy scores, these 160 sessions were examined in terms of (1) observer-rated empathy and (2) acoustic/linguistic indicators of empathy. (1) We recruited seven graduates from the master’s in counselling program who expressed interest in research and learning more about the counselling process. They were trained by the PI and collaborator on the Therapist Empathy Scale. After attaining good interrater reliability, they rated therapist empathy from the 160 counselling session videotapes. (2) To conduct the analyses, we collaborated with Prof. Tan Lee from the Department of Electronic Engineering at CUHK. Prof. Lee is an experienced researcher of speech signal processing and language analysis, particularly in spoken Cantonese. One of Prof. Lee’s doctoral students developed a thesis proposal, Characterizing empathy in psychotherapy via speech analytics, based on this ECS project. Features of therapists’ prosody and speaking styles were first extracted from the 160 session recordings. Based on client- and observer-ratings of empathy, cluster analysis was performed to determine the features that are associated with high (versus low) ratings of therapist empathy. For linguistic analyses, the 160 sessions were transcribed by 30 undergraduate research assistants. An average of 13 hours were needed to transcribe each 50-min counselling session, a number higher than transcribing sessions in English because of the complexity of spoken Cantonese. The transcripts were then analyzed. For language style analysis, the Linguistic Inquiry and Word Count (LIWC) Traditional Chinese Dictionary was adopted. However, because this dictionary was based on written Chinese, an enhanced version for spoken Cantonese was created from a subset of the transcripts. To ensure client confidentiality, instead of uploading session transcripts to the LIWC website, a computer programmer was hired to develop a local analysis platform. For the analysis of linguistic features, such as particles, a graduate research assistant with a background in linguistics and an undergraduate research assistant were recruited to annotate the 160 transcripts, conduct data analysis, and help in manuscript/conference abstract preparation. In Study 2 (experimental study), 34 volunteer clients and 34 therapists were recruited to conduct three 50-min counselling sessions. The number of dyads recruited exceeded the proposed 30 dyads because more volunteers answered to the recruitment call than expected, but were kept in case of client dropout. For Objectives 1 and 2, therapists were induced to experience elation, depression, or neutral mood before a session using the Velten. Thirty mood-inducing statements were used for each condition, and they were translated to Chinese and backtranslated to English to ensure accuracy before use. In addition, music was played to enhance the mood inducing effects. For Objective 3, we administered the Difficulties in Emotional Regulation Scale to therapists as in Study 1 and analyzed its moderating effects (which was again found to be non-significant). Nevertheless, we also administered the Interpersonal Reactivity Index to assess therapists’ trait empathy and found interesting interaction effects, which are described in 6.1 of this report. For Objective 4, the assessment of empathy was conducted by client- and observer-rating (similar procedure as in Study 1), and electrocardiogram (ECG). ECG was collected from therapists and clients simultaneously throughout the three sessions. A medical specialist reviewed the participants’ ECG for follow-up action if abnormality is noted. The ECG data were cleaned with the help of a research assistant and the analysis of heartbeat synchrony was aided by Prof. Wolfgang Tschacher from the University of Bern.

24604317.label: Major findings and research outcome
24604317.value: From Study 1, we found that therapist pre-session affective state alone did not predict clients’ rating of session quality or therapist empathy. However, sessions in which clients’ and therapists’ affective states got closer over a session had better session quality, and the relationship was mediated by therapist empathy. Therapist affect thus interacts with client affect to influence clients’ perception of therapist empathy, which in turn influences clients’ session ratings. These findings have been presented (Conference #3) and published (Publication #1). Also from Study 1, we investigated how empathy may be related to therapists’ linguistic features. First, therapists who used more sentence final particles with high-level tone (i.e., imperative intonation) were rated by observers as being less empathic, particularly in the later phase of therapy (Conference #4). Next, therapists who used more discourse particles (i.e., sounding less formal) had lower observer-rated empathy (to be presented at the Society for Psychotherapy Research, July 2022; Publication #3 under review). To further understand particle use, we took clients’ particle use into account and found that when clients used few particles (i.e., sounding formal) early in therapy, therapists who used more particles (i.e., sounding more casual) were rated as more empathic (to be presented at the North American Conference on Chinese Linguistics, September 2022). These results highlight that empathy may not only reflect how therapists speak, but also the dynamic interaction between therapists’ and clients’ speaking styles. For example, we found that clients’ rating of therapist empathy was directly related to the extent to which they followed their therapists’ language style (Conference #2). Beside linguistics features, empathy may be associated with acoustic features, such as volume, pause, and speech rate. Preliminary findings, and the engineering aspects of acoustic feature detection, will be presented over three papers at the 23rd INTERSPEECH Conference (September 2022). From Study 2, we found that mood induction in therapists did not have an effect on client-rated therapist empathy or session quality, or the heart rate synchrony between therapists and clients. However, mood induction had an effect on observer-rated therapist empathy. Specifically, when induced to feel elation, therapists with high trait empathy were observed to be more empathic, whereas those with low trait empathy were perceived to be less empathic. Therapists’ personal characteristics thus moderated the effect of mood induction on psychotherapy process. The findings have been presented (Conference #1) and the manuscript is currently under review (Publication #2).

24604317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24604317.value: After studying how therapists’ mood may impact the psychotherapy process, we extend the investigation to how therapists’ emotion word use in session may influence clients and sessions. Such extension allows us to examine therapist emotion more comprehensively. Study 1 of this ECS project resulted in 160 Cantonese counselling session transcripts that provide rich material for future research. Emotion words used by therapists in sessions that received high ratings from clients were extracted to form the word list for therapist training, and the effects of pre-session emotion word training on psychotherapy process are currently being investigated (GRF Ref. #: 14601120). Another way that we further our research is having a closer examination of psychotherapy speech. The collaboration with engineers and linguists that began from this ECS project has led to several ongoing research endeavors. For example, an automatic transcription system is currently being developed to reduce the time and cost of transcribing Cantonese counselling sessions. We are also looking into additional acoustic and linguistic features of therapists’ and clients’ speech in relation to traditional process and outcome variables to better understand the characteristics of effective and less effective counselling practice. In turn, this knowledge will enhance counsellor training in the future.

24604317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24604317.value: This project advances our appreciation of how counsellors’ affect influences the counselling process. Specifically, counsellors’ affect does not work in isolation, but may have complex interactions with client and counsellor variables to impact counselling sessions. For example, in a naturalistic study, counsellors who shared increasingly similar affect as their clients over a session were perceived by clients as having higher empathy, and the session quality was rated higher. In an experimental study, induced elation before a session helped counsellors with high trait empathy to better express empathy, but hindered those with low trait empathy to express empathy. Thus, the findings highlight dynamic interaction between counsellor and client variables that should be considered in future research. This project also furthers our understanding of therapist empathy. Through multidisciplinary collaboration, we explored the acoustic (e.g., tone) and linguistic features (e.g., particles) of psychotherapy speech that are associated with therapist empathy. This knowledge has implications for training/practice as it illuminates how counsellors can better convey empathy. These studies also further research. For example, therapists’ use of particles was related to observer- but not client-rated empathy, offering a potential explanation for the weak correlation often found between different raters' ratings of the same psychotherapy process.

24604417.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24604417.value: 台灣性娛樂產業中婚姻移民工作者的生活與勞務研究

24604417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24604417.value: 本研究將透過台灣低階性娛樂產業之興衰，檢視在此性娛樂產業中從事小姐工作的東南亞和中國大陸婚姻移民女性其生活與勞動，挑戰“假結婚，真賣淫”的社會污名。通過深入審視這些女性如何在家庭、工作和社會領域間協調作為母親、女兒、妻子、勞動者和/或公民的身份，本研究致力於打破這些女性是不道德的，性工作的受害者，或是認為性工作和母職是不能兼容等簡化的社會成見。 自1990年代末以來，台灣跨國婚姻仲介的激增導致了從中國及東南亞湧入的婚姻移民潮。這一股移民潮帶來了許多所謂的“社會問題”。例如，大眾媒體頻繁報導驚悚的新聞故事，講述外國女性通過婚姻來台灣從事性工作，從而將全體婚姻移民與道德可疑的社會污名關聯起來。確實，自1990年代後期的婚姻移民潮以來，台灣見證了小姐工作的按摩廳和歌廳在街角湧現。然而，這些女性是誰？她們為何及如何進入性娛樂產業？ 本項目研究方法包括參與式觀察、深入訪談，以及文本分析。參與式觀察將分別在兩個經營性娛樂產業的場所進行：一者在台灣中南部提供陪酒服務的小吃店；另一者在台北萬華紅燈區的傳統茶室。深入訪談的對象是與這些性產業經營相關的人，包括小姐、經營者和當地政府機關。此外，本研究也將分析相關的資料，例如新聞故事和官方報告，以此來檢驗這些資料如何以刻板化的方式來呈現婚姻移民的性娛樂工作者，無視她們所身處的多層面現實。 本研究將細緻而謹慎地反思關於跨國婚姻移民、全球性工作和販賣女性的相關論述。通過闡述這些移民女性如何協調她們的勞動、家庭和其它社會關係，本研究將挑戰一系列二元對立的分類，例如將這些女性視為不是被強迫的就是自願的，因而需要被同情或處罰，或是純潔的/不潔的主體。研究結果將豐富現有關於亞洲婚姻移民的學術成果，並透過案例研究為相關的政策制定提供參考。

24606617.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24606617.value: 《新潮》雜誌（1919-1922）的翻譯與民國期刊中「五四」的經典化

24606617.label: Project Objectives
24606617.value: To create a database for New Tide Journal, which includes indexes of all published items in the journal, periodicals, institutions and individuals related to the journal, and a parallel textbase of translated texts in the journal and their source texts. To examine the practice and conceptualization of translation in New Tide in the linguistic and social context of early Republican periodical press. To define the role of translation in the canonization of the May Fourth discourse by examining translated texts in New Tide that were involved in the interactions between the May Fourth elites and the coexisting intellectual groups in the context of periodical press. To contribute to the research literature on translation studies and translation history, with case studies on first-hand materials from the early Republican print media. To reinterpret the May Fourth era and reevaluate the “grand narrative” of Chinese modernity with a focus on translation.

24606617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24606617.value: The May Fourth Movement (五四運動) in 1919 and the decade that followed constitute a crucial period in early Republican China. During this period, the May Fourth protagonists attempted to secure a central position in the emerging modern cultural landscape. To do so, they introduced Western culture enthusiastically and established the import as the new literary canon; meanwhile, they critiqued their own legacies and marginalized the concurrent bodies of traditional, “old-fashioned” literature. Such a “new-versus-old” narrative had been characteristic of the historiography of May Fourth, until it was challenged in recent academic discourse. This project aims to add a key element to the reevaluation on this narrative: translation. Based on a study on the leading May Fourth journal New Tide (新潮，1919-1922), the project shows that translation in the journal was pivotal in the canonization of May Fourth in the early Republican periodical press. By compiling a database of the journal, the project observes that a significant portion of the contents was translated from Western literature and scholarship, which contributed to the volume and repertoire of the May Fourth discourse that proclaimed itself as “new” against literary traditions. Moreover, the project shows that the translated texts should not to be taken at face value, for they took diverse forms and (mis)represented the sources in so many ways that they contradicted the common assumption of May Fourth translation as truthful representations of their source texts. The assumption creates the illusion that a May Fourth translation was unproblematic, and inevitably veils any manipulation of the source materials. By examining the translated texts from both linguistic and contextual approaches, the project reveals that these concealed misrepresentations, in fact, was central to the May Fourth elites' strategies for marginalizing traditional literature. The project then observes that despite the lack of a strong counter-discourse, the more tradition-minded literary groups reoriented translation choices in their journals in order to find new niches and re-position themselves against the emerging May Fourth canon. Such dynamics surrounding translation in rivaling periodicals in this period has to date been overlooked in the history of translation or of Chinese modernity. The project will fill this gap by establishing the role of translation in shaping the intelligentsia in early Republican China, seeking to challenge the simplistic assumption of May Fourth translation as an unproblematic medium for cultural import, and to reinterpret the May Fourth Movement with a focus on translation. 五四運動及其後十年乃民初中國的一段重要時期。在此期間，現代文化圖景初現，五四精英文人欲進駐文化場域中心位置，一方面輸入西方文化，據此建立文學新經典，另一方面批評自身傳統，力將同期的「傳統」、「舊派」文學群體逐至邊緣。「新」「舊」對立，素為五四歷史敘事主調，近年中外學人不時提出反思。本研究將為再思五四的討論加入一項關鍵要素：翻譯。 本研究聚焦於五四時期重要雜誌《新潮》（1919-1922），旨在證明該刊翻譯對於五四話語在民初期刊中的經典化過程，實有至關重要的作用。研究步驟大致有三。首先，根據《新潮》原刊，建立資料庫，指出刊中不少內容均譯自西方文學與學術文本，不論就數量或文類而言，皆有助於自謂為「新」的五四話語之形成。其後，研究將進入文本，表明《新潮》翻譯具有多種形式，對於源文文本亦有各種呈現及誤現。時人有一普遍印象，即五四文人的翻譯是外國文本的忠實反映。研究者若止於固見，不加追問，則無從察覺譯者對源文材料的操縱。本研究將結合語言和語境分析，發掘刊內翻譯中的種種操縱，並表明相關翻譯手法，恰恰是五四精英建立新文學經典、驅逐傳統文學的重要策略。此後，研究亦將考察同一時期傳統文人的期刊活動，表明這些文人面對新生的五四經典，未必提出強力抗衡，卻在不斷調整其期刊雜誌的翻譯實踐，以另覓空間，重新定位。 上述以期刊為基地、藉翻譯為手段的競逐場景，至今鮮為人注意，不論翻譯史或中國現代史，皆不見詳述。本研究望起補白之效，從《新潮》一刊入手，探索翻譯在民初文人群體流變中的複雜作用，衝擊五四翻譯即為文化傳播的單純印象，以翻譯為焦點重讀五四。

24606617.label: Realisation of objectives
24606617.value: OBJECTIVE 1 is materialized in the project's dataset (doi: 10.6084/m9.figshare.7428434). The dataset contains: 1. published items.xlsx – a record of all published items in New Tide, with items containing translation(s) marked with (a) the nature of translation (full/partial rendition, citation, mention or summary) and (b) the textual level involved (word-, sentence- or text-level). Each item is provided with basic bibliographical information as seen in the original publication and the disambiguated names of the contributors; 2. advertising network.gephi – a record of the advertised affiliations of New Tide, recovered from advertisements in the journal. 3. text map.xlsx – a set of spreadsheets that record the connections between New Tide articles containing contained translations with the sources that were translated, cited, mentioned and referenced, in the format of Gephi node–edge sheet. 4. text map.gephi – a network graph based on Item 3, which visualizes New Tide’s western and Chinese textual sources, their intertextual relations with New Tide articles, and the intertextual relations within New Tide articles. The text map is colored-coded and manipulated in a way to bring to front most resourceful articles, most-translated sources/authors, and the most discussed Chinese classics; and finally 5. New Tide advertising network visualization.pdf, a visual output of item 2. The project’s dataset is cited in the PI's three conference papers in 2018 (with private share link, when dataset was in preliminary shape) and in the 2020 journal article (with the permanent doi); all these publications are the project’s output. The project’s dataset is modeled upon the pilot study published in my journal article (2018) “Expanding Translation: A Text Map of New Youth (1915–1918)”. This article adopts a quantitative approach to translational sources of New Youth, a May Fourth leading journal which had decisive impact on New Tide’s conception, format, content and personnel. The pilot study is a methodological preparation for the project’s dataset. The paper acknowledges ECS as funding source and is cited my other outputs in this project. OBJECTIVE 2, which is to examine the practice and conceptualization of translation in New Tide, is realized in the following publications. In “Translation in New Tide (1919–1922) and the Canonization of May Fourth” (2018), presented in the 6th IATIS Conference, I examined representative examples of “recognized” translations (translations of full or abbreviated texts, translations explicitly marked as translations), unmarked translations (the use of translated materials in fragmentary quotations, summary, citations, or notes), and translation criticism in essays, fiction, book reviews, editors and readers’ columns in the journal. This paper revealed that New Tide made strategic use of translation to (mis) represent the sources in order to proclaim May Fourth values as inevitable replacement of those of Chinese traditions. The paper suggested that the same use of translation would be found in other students’ journals based in Peking University in the May Fourth era. This group of alliance journals, uncovered from New Tide’s advertisements and recommendation columns, were presented in the paper with reference to Item 2 and 5 in the project’s dataset. In “The New and the Translated: A Text Map of the New Tide Journal” (2018), presented at EACS Biennial Conference, I disclosed all the identified translation sources of New Tide, citing the project’s dataset and particularly the text map (Item 3 and 4). I offered a macroscopic description of the sources, and argued that the sources were the basis of the modern knowledge on which the journal’s core contributors developed the narrative of the “new” (xin) – an ambiguous and politically-charged keyword often associated with the May Fourth tenets. Combining network graph reading and textual analysis, I estalished the role of New Tide translation in demonstrating the evolutionist, “new-versus-old” paradigm, which was characteristic of the grand narrative of Chinese modernity. Proceeding from the above conference papers, I continued to explore whether translation in New Tide did more than a demonstration of the May Fourth paradigm. I examined further the nature, mechanism and consequence of translation in my publications that followed. In the paper “A Space of Their Voice: Apologies for Translation in New Tide (1919–1922)” (2018), presented in “A Space for Translation: Threshold of Interpretation” Conference, I contrasted two sets of materials: 1) apologetic translation prefaces and in-text gloss, which revealed the student translators’ habitual dissatisfaction with their translations and which consistently projected translation as a tentative, provisional text type in the journalistic discourse; and 2) unapologetic appropriations of foreign sources, which illuminated the nature of translation as a mode of writing that suspended skepticism. In the paper “Inventing Enemies: Translation, reference and criticism in New Tide (1919–1922)” (2019), presented in the May Fourth centennial international conference “4 May 1919: History in Motion”, I focalized the prolific New Tide contributor-editor Luo Jialun and his partial translations, which were infused with references to and criticism of prior translations done by traditional-minded intellectuals of his time. Luo’s translations showed signs of canonizing an elusive May Fourth “Self” and of marginalizing its “Other”, which included not only influential Chinese translators Lin Shu and Yan Fu, sinologists Herbert A. Giles and Alexander Wylie, but also the commercial periodicals contemporary with New Tide. My view of the aggressive role of New Tide translation in canonizing May Fourth took a mature shape in the article “A Space for Their Voices. (Un)apologies for Translation in the May Fourth Journal New Tide” (2020). From the editorial documents and translators’ notes written by influential contributors such as Fu Sinian, Luo Jialun, Wu Kang and He Siyuan, I identified two characteristics of the frame space of New Tide: the collective awareness of academic rigor and humility, and the students’ self-identity as a group of inexperienced and diverse-minded young scholars. Examining more partial translations done by Luo Jialun, I substantiated the argument that translation in such frame space was a liminal, un-scrutinized mode of writing of dual purposes of criticizing the students’ concurrent traditional-minded intellectuals, and of validating – hence canonizing – the tenets of May Fourth. My forthcoming monograph (2021) addressed OBJECTIVE 2 and also OBJECTIVE 3 from a different angle. The monograph, with a focus on early Republican Shanghai journals, foregrounds the role of translation in activating and sustaining the mutual positioning between popular periodical press and New Tide-centered May Fourth elite press in the 1910s and 1920s, a process that has been a precursor to the canonization of May Fourth claims about literature, historiography and philosophy. In this monograph, Chapter 7 provided a close reading of New Tide translations that embedded criticism of pre-existing Chinese translations and translators. I believe that the above publications are products and exhibits of the project’s method that marries digital humanities and conventional text analysis, of my intended critical discussion that centralizes the role of New Tide’s translation and student translators in May Fourth, and of the hard efforts in establishing translation in periodicals as loci and mechanism for canonization of May Fourth. These publications have realized OBJECTIVE 4, which is to invigorate translation studies and translation history, and OBJECTIVE 5, which is to re-evaluate May Fourth with a focus on translation. The project’s outcomes also challenge the assumption of May Fourth translation as transparent medium for cultural import that made China modern, and the prevailing explanation of Chinese modernity as a result of diffusion from the West.

24606617.label: Major findings and research outcome
24606617.value: Here are the findings, each supported by research outcomes: 1. The project recovers the sources of translations in New Tide (hereafter NT), using a qualitative approach piloted in my paper (2018, JTS). The “text map” and related papers (7/2018; 9/2018; 12/2018) show that NT appropriated non-Chinese sources from over 800 publications, including academic works, literary works and periodicals in English, French, German and Japanese languages, and crediting 660 authors, among which most were philosophers, psychologists, sociologists, politicians and scientists active in the late 19th to early 20th century. NT mainly translated introductory works on sociology, political science, historiography, psychology, and religious studies. These works, mostly translated partially and some misrepresented, formed the basis on which NT configured a “new” paradigm for theorizing China’s past and present. The most translated authors were Bertrand Russell, John Dewey, William James, H. G. Wells, E. A. Ross, Romain Rolland, and F. C. S. Schiller. 2. The project discovers that unmarked translation of Western-centric academic sources in NT often appeared in juxtaposition to references to Chinese sources, which included about 485 works and 149 writers native to ancient and modern China (conference paper 9/2018). NT also made references to over 40 Chinese periodicals. 3. In the above source-tracking, the project observes a conception of the “new” born in translation in NT. The “new” was inseparable from and in service to a reconfiguration of the “old” and the mutual positioning between NT and its contemporaries. 4. The project explains how translation in NT, given its partial nature, was carried out by a cluster of 43 contributors (out of 75) who published translated materials and was accepted by a readership presumably covering most universities in China then. As argued in my conference paper (12/2018) and explained in Part B 5.3 in this report, translation in NT’s frame space was conceptualized as a liminal, tentative mode of writing, something with unavoidable limitations but not to be invalidated by skepticism about the limitations. 5. The project reveals that resulting from its conceptualization and practice of translation, NT’s partial representations of foreign sources were accepted and weaved deeply into the journal’s new-versus-old discourse that was integral to the May Fourth paradigm. Translation in NT had the dual effect of marginalizing the journal’s concurrent traditional-minded intellectuals, and of canonizing the central aim of May Fourth to break from and at the same time to reconfigure Chinese traditions. These dynamics are examined in my paper (2020) and monograph (2021).

24606617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24606617.value: The below may follow the project: 1. Research adopting the project's methodology can be done on translation in more May Fourth (MF) student journals. The project has identified (1) journals which New Tide (NT) allied to, e.g. 少年中國, 曙光 and 國民; (2) journals which NT debated with, e.g. 國故, 時事新報 and 上海潑克; and (3) student journals which distanced themselves from political and cultural matters, e.g. 理化雜誌, 數理雜誌 and 數理化雜誌. These periodicals contain many translation materials, thus call for an extended project on translation, young generation and periodical press in MF. 2. Research can be done on the appropriation of specific scholars in MF periodicals. The works of William James, H. G. Wells, E. A. Ross and F. C. S. Schiller were proved statistically important in this project, but remained unexplored in existing scholarship about MF. These scholars can be studied individually for their influence on MF. 3. The dataset of NT translation may be integrated to that of the pilot study on New Youth (2018) for a more accurate overview of the MF translators’ sources. These data, especially the network graphs, may be published in more user-friendly and interactive format to maximize impact.

24606617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24606617.value: The project examines translation in the journal New Tide (1919-1922) and assesses its role in the canonization of May Fourth. The project explores translation in varied forms, which ranged from “obvious” translations of full or abbreviated texts, to “hidden” translations in fragmentary quotations, summary, citations, or notes. The project traces the sources of translations, compares sources to translations, and examines the usage of translation in the journal. The translation data reveal a process through which a range of foreign sources were appropriated through partial translation in the journal to establish an evolutionist, “new-versus-old” rhetoric, and in which translation had dual effects of criticizing – hence marginalizing – the journal’s concurrent traditional-minded Chinese intellectuals and of validating – hence canonizing – the central ideas of May Fourth, which were integral to what we know as Chinese modernity. These dynamics surrounding New Tide translation are discussed in a series of papers published in international conferences and journals in translation studies, Chinese studies and May Fourth studies, as well as in part of the PI’s monograph. The project has an open dataset (doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.7428434), where readers can navigate the translation data, including a network graph that connects translation in New Tide to their sources.

24609017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24609017.value: The aims of this study are to examine the effects of a modelling-based narrative intervention on care-seeking behavioural intention and prehospital care-seeking delays in acute myocardial infarction (AMI) patients, and to explore how this intervention affects care-seeking decisions from the patients’ perspective. AMI is a medical emergency that warrants immediate medical attention to initiate life-saving treatments. However, prolonged delay by patients in making care-seeking decisions remains the most significant limiting factor for effective AMI management despite decades of research. The major challenge may be related to the fact that the cause of delay is multifaceted and patients make their decisions within a complex framework. Work carried out by the principal investigator showed that people’s care-seeking behaviours are mainly driven by two perceptual-cognitive processes in labelling and interpreting the illness accurately. To address the complicated decision-making course in AMI patients, an effective intervention needs to guide patients through these processes, so as to attain behavioural changes. An eclectic approach which integrates teaching principles as suggested by Social Cognitive Theory and a narrative approach maybe the best to empower patients in the cognitive, perceptual and behavioural perspectives. Education through such means can offer a vivid experience for patients to internalise the teaching content. This mixed-method study includes a randomised controlled trial and an exploratory qualitative study. A total of 630 patients, who are ≥18 year-old, living in the community, with a prior history of AMI will be recruited from the cardiac clinics of two regional hospitals. These patients will be randomly allocated to the intervention or controlled groups, and will receive a modelling-based narrative intervention or a didactic education, respectively. The hypothesis is that AMI patients who receive the modelling-based narrative intervention will report better changes in care-seeking behavioural intention, more likely to use ambulance and show shorter prehospital delays when AMI symptoms occur at 3, 12, and 24 months after the intervention, than those who receive didactic education on AMI care-seeking. A subsample of 30 patients in the intervention group will be invited for a qualitative interview to explore their perceptions of the intervention. This study is the first of its kind to adopt an eclectic approach to optimise care-seeking behaviours in patients with AMI by using a modelling-based narrative intervention. The findings will advance our understanding of the AMI care-seeking course and provide a new educational approach to enhance timely care-seeking decisions in AMI patients.

24609017.label: Realisation of objectives
24609017.value: Objective 1: The investigation team used the first four months to develop the modelling-based narrative intervention. In order to enhance the acceptability and relevancy of the intervention for patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI), a patient participatory approach was adopted to involve end users in co-designing the intervention. Ten patients with AMI were invited to attend qualitative interviews, in order to solicit their views on the facilitators and barriers to prompt care-seeking, how to assist them in the decision-making process when they encounter symptoms suggestive of AMI. Based on their suggestions, a modelling-based narrative intervention was developed. It comprised five sessions to be spread through 8 weeks, including four weekly sessions and a booster session 4 weeks later. For the first 4 weekly sessions, each session began with a brief educational presentation on a relevant topic. The weekly topics were consistent with the critical junctures commonly encountered by AMI patients while making their care-seeking decisions, including: (a) symptom recognition and risk identification, (b) emotional responses to a possible AMI attack, (c) perceived barriers and facilitators to care-seeking and (d) means of care-seeking and transportation to use. These sessions emphasized enhancing the patients’ understanding of the disease manifestations, appropriate care-seeking behaviors and the significance of prompt care-seeking. After the structured education, the participants were offered an interactive video-based virtual AMI attack experience to consolidate the knowledge gained in previous sessions. The video captured a model patient enacting scenes to depict the perceptual-cognitive processes, including the experience and interpretation of symptoms and the care-seeking process. The storyline of the video was based in the actual experience shared by patients during the co-design interviews. The video was paused at different critical junctures to allow participants to outline their own decision-making process. During the pause, the intervener, who was a registered nurse, encouraged the participants to discuss their feelings, concerns and difficulties regarding care-seeking decision-making, then participants were assisted to applying the knowledge gained during previous sessions and making appropriate judgements and decisions. The nurse also guided the participants to brainstorm methods of resolution for each barrier identified during the session and clarified all misbeliefs. A half-day booster session was delivered one month later. A scenario-based approach was used to optimize the participants’ perceptual-cognitive processes. Three scenarios involving various perceptual, social and contextual circumstances were developed, based on the suggestions given by patients during the intervention co-design. The participants were encouraged to express perceived barriers and concerns that existed during the decision-making course, and the nurse encouraged them to recall and use the knowledge and skills acquired during previous face-to-face sessions to resolve every situational dilemma. The content of the intervention was reviewed by an expert panel that consisted of nursing academicians, cardiologists and cardiac nurses. The panel members rated the appropriateness and quality of the content on a 10-item content validity survey, each item to be rated on a 1 - 4 Likert scale, a higher score represented higher quality. The mean score for the content validation was 3.88, indicating good content validity. They commented the intervention content was highly relevant to prepare AMI patients in responding swiftly for symptoms indicating a recurrent AMI. The video would provide a vivid experience for them to experience the decision-making process in advance, so that they could be prepared and rehearsed. Two review panel members suggested to add more scenarios in the booster session. We added 3 more scenarios accordingly. After finalizing the design of the intervention, subject recruitment was commenced in June 2018 from the cardiac clinics of two regional hospitals in Hong Kong, including the United Christian Hospital and the Queen Elizabeth Hospital. To maximize the impacts of the project and to raise the awareness of the public and patients about the importance of prompt care-seeking for AMI symptoms, the investigation team publicized this study in a press conference held by the Care For Your Heart in 2018, the largest cardiac patient mutual support organization in Hong Kong. During the event, the principal investigator (PI) shared with the press about the importance of quick response to symptoms suggestive of AMI and the information about this study. The news was reported by major printed media in Hong Kong, such as Sing Tao Daily, Metro Daily, Headline Daily and Hong Kong Economic Times. This study was extended to two more hospitals, including the Prince of Wales Hospital and Pok Oi Hospital, in order to speed up the progress. The project implementation was smooth and uneventful until the social unrest happened in 2019. A series of large protests happened across the city during the period from June 2019 to January 2020. A substantial number of patients were reluctant to join the study, as they felt unsafe to attend the in-person intervention sessions in the study sites. Unfortunately, the study progress was further hindered by the COVID-19 pandemic since January 2020. The Hospital Authority of Hong Kong escalated its alert system to the Emergency Response Level to contain the outbreak of COVID-19 in public hospitals, the study was suspended periodically according to the infection controlled guidelines set by the study hospitals. The application of study extension for 6 months was approved by RGC in 2020. During the study period, a total of 1,033 patients underwent eligibility screening, 638 of them agreed to join the study. However, 30 of them did not turn up for the baseline assessment and randomization. Finally, a total of 608 participants were successfully recruited and being randomized to receive either the modelling-based narrative intervention (n = 304) or didactic education (n = 304). The mean age of the participants was 67.2 (standard deviation [SD] = 8.3) years. Majority of them were male (77.1%), married (84.7%), and retired or unemployed (75.3%). Approximately one-third of them had a primary education or no formal education (29.4%). The two study groups were homogenous except that the intervention group had a higher percentage of women. The attrition rates for both study groups at T1, T2 and T3 were 7.2% - 7.9%, 14.8% - 16.4%, and 16.9% - 20.7%, respectively. A total of 97 participants, including 52 in the intervention group and 45 in the control groups, had experienced another episode of AMI during the 2-year follow-up period. Data including the symptom onset time, the time arriving the hospital, the transportation means to travel to the hospital were collected by patient’s self-report, and these data were cross checked with that recorded in the electronic health record system if available. Objective 2: Among the patients who have participated in the modelling-based narrative intervention, 33 of them were invited to attend a qualitative interview for the purpose of soliciting their engagement experience in the intervention. They were selected on the basis of the changes in the prehospital delay time when they experienced another AMI episode within the follow-up period, and changes in care-seeking attitudes and beliefs. We also recruited participants by maximizing the representatives from different gender, age groups and education levels. Guided by a semi-structured interview guide, these participants were elicited to discuss how the intervention affected their care-seeking attitudes, beliefs and decisions. Each interview lasted from 41 to 76 minutes. All the audio-taped interviews were transcribed verbatim and checked for accuracy, before subjecting to analysis.

24609017.value: With respect to Objective 1, the generalized estimating equation analysis indicated that compared to the control group, the intervention group showed significantly greater improvements in their attitudes of care-seeking for AMI from T0 to T1 (ꞵ=-1.053, 95% CI=-1.714 – -0.391, p=0.002). This improvement was sustained at T2 (ꞵ=-0.797, 95% CI=-1.477– -0.117, p=0.022) and T3 (ꞵ=-0.645, 95% CI=-1.231– -0.106, p=0.031). There was also a significant between-group difference in the change in beliefs regarding care-seeking from T0 to T1 (ꞵ=-0.692, 95% CI=-1.354– -0.180, p=0.044), and this difference was maintained at T2 (ꞵ=-0.692, 95% CI=-1.309– -0.012, p=0.047) but not at T3. The Cohen’s d values ranged from 0.39 to 0.58, and 0.32 to 0.39 for attitudes and beliefs, respectively, indicating small to medium effect sizes. There was no significant between-group changes in AMI knowledge across all time points. Among the participants who had another AMI episode during the follow-up period, the median delay times for the intervention and control groups were 3.35 hours (interquartile range [IQR]: 1.19–6.52 hours) and 5.03 hours (IQR: 2.22–9.18), respectively. The linear mixed-effects model analysis indicated that the prehospital delay time was significantly shorter in the intervention group than in the control group (ꞵ=-0.09 [95% CI -0.14– -0.02], p=0.022). There was no between-group difference on their use of ambulance (p=0.429). With respect to Objective 2, the qualitative data revealed that the modelling-based narrative intervention was well received by the participants. All of them commented that the intervention had improved their knowledge about AMI symptoms and the importance of prompt care-seeking decisions. Among those participants who exhibited short (≤2 hours) care-seeking delays, they highlighted the interactive story-telling approach as very useful for them to practice the complex decision-making, which they could recall the information and skills when they experienced symptoms suggestive of AMI. Moreover, the sharing of other patients who successfully recognized and responding symptoms also impressed them a lot, which they could model the desirable behaviors under the stressful scene of recurrent AMI. Among those participants who showed long delay time (>6 hours), the major barriers were relating to COVID-19. They expressed strong fear of contracting COVID-19 in the hospital setting. Moreover, these patients had persistent non-specific symptoms, rendered them difficult to recognize the vague symptoms presented in the recurrent attack. Regarding the areas for improvement, participants suggested the intervention to be delivered through an online platform and with a more flexible schedule to attend the sessions.

24609017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24609017.value: It is timely to increase the accessibility of this evidence-based intervention to benefit a wider community, including patients with coronary artery disease who have not yet developed an acute event of AMI. The absence of prior experience as a reference to guide their decision-making renders them particularly at risk for prolonged delay. This health promotion strategy should also be extended to the general public, as more than 70% of the coronary events occur in people without a prior history of AMI. Moreover, other people may act as confidants in advising persons experiencing an AMI attack. Therefore, preparing the general public and the high-risk population in responding to AMI symptoms is equally important. Based on the results and experience of this GRF study, the investigation team proposed a translational research project titled ?A territory-wide Blended Eclectic program to optimize the community?s Preparedness (BE Prepared) for responding to heart attack symptoms? and submitted to bid for the Research Impact Fund 2022/23 (R7005-22). The BE Prepared project will make use of the online platform to target both patients with coronary artery disease and the general public. The preliminary proposal has been shortlisted for submitting a full proposal.

24609017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24609017.value: AMI is a medical emergency that warrants immediate medical attention to initiate life-saving treatments. However, prolonged delay by patients in making care-seeking decisions remains the most significant limiting factor for effective AMI management. This study developed and examined the effects of a comprehensive modelling-based narrative intervention to promote prompt care-seeking in AMI patients. The intervention integrated teaching principles and a narrative approach to empower patients to go through the perceptual-cognitive processes in making the care-seeking decision for possible AMI symptoms. By randomly assigning 608 patients with a history of AMI to the modelling-based narrative intervention or an education about AMI with a didactic approach, this study demonstrated favorable effects in promoting positive attitudes and beliefs regarding care-seeking for AMI symptoms and shortening the care-seeking delay among those with a recurrent attack within the study period. This study provided empirical evidence on an effective and novel strategy to promote timely care-seeking behaviors in AMI patients, which will be of great significance in curtailing AMI-related morbidity and mortality. The investigation team has proposed an impact research project for bidding further funding support to the translation of research knowledge in order to benefit a wider community.

24614817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24614817.value: Boosting is one of the most popular machine learning methods. To investigate its statistical properties, the machine learning community and statisticians, however, focus on settings with independent random sampling and Gaussian errors. Little work has been done in time series and panel data, an area of tremendous importance in empirical economics and finance. This project aims to understand the theoretical property of boosting in time series and panel data as well as its performance in simulations and empirical applications. The principle of repeated fitting is versatile and potentially useful in studies of various problems. The three topics in this proposal will explore: (i) prediction consistency in high-dimensional time series regression; (ii) test treatment effect after variable section in the high-dimensional time series regression; (iii) repeatedly fitting the Hodrick-Prescott filter for time series trending extraction. Boosting是最流行的機器方學習方法之一。然而，統計學家們專注於獨立隨機抽樣和正態分佈的設定。雖然時間序列和麵板數據對於經濟學和金融學非常重要，但是boosting幾乎沒有得到研究。通過這個項目，我們希望理解boosting方法在時間序列和麵板數據下的統計性質，以及它在仿真模擬和實證研究中的表現。 Boosting的重複擬合原理在各種不同問題中都有廣泛應用。在本提案中，我們將研究以下三個問題。 1. 在高維時間序列回歸中的預測一致性；2. 高維時間序列完成變量選擇後treatment effect的檢驗; 3. 通過重複擬合Hodrick-Proscott filter來抓取時間序列中的趨勢。

24614817.label: Realisation of objectives
24614817.value: The project objectives are all achieved. 1. After two years of hard work, the research have culminated in three papers. 1. “Forward-Selected Panel Data Approach for Program Evaluation” (Paper One) shows that in the panel data approach for treatment estimation can use boosting for control variable selection. Even if the model is a dense one, we can attain a certain optimality property. Moreover, it is possible to conduct valid inference based on the variables selected by boosting without extra adjustment. 2. “Boosting: Why You Can Use the Hodrick-Prescott Filter” (Paper Two) is the first paper to illustrate that boosting method can be applied to non-stationary time series. It establishes the underlying theory of consistent trend estimation. The insight lies in the observation that a non-stationary time series admits a series representation of orthonormal basis. Empirical applications show its wide applicability with an automated data-driven method that automatically terminates iterations. 3. As a by-project of this research of boosting, we also understand better the behavior of Lasso in nonstationary time series in “On LASSO for Predictive Regression” (Paper Three) . Lasso is closely related to boosting. We show that the conventional adaptive Lasso cannot achieve variable selection consistency, which was a surprise given that all papers of adaptive Lasso did so. Furthermore, we follow the spirit of Boosting (repeated fitting) to devise a "twin adaptive Lasso", which is essentially "twicing", to restore consistency of variable selection in a mixed predictive model with nonstationary, non-stationary and cointegrating regressors. 2. Each of these papers include empirical examples to demonstrate the applicability of these methods. 1. Paper One first revisted Hsiao, Ching and Wan (2012). Then we draw a new dataset of 88 time series of China's imports. We can only use our componentwise boosting method for variable selection. 2. Paper Two contrasts Hamilton (2018)'s AR(4) filter by the single time series of US industrial production time series for demonstration. Then in the data rich environment, we use the 40 international time series to check the Okun's law, and 78 time series from 26 countries to measure the relative persistency of the macroeconomic variables. 3. Paper three uses an updated version of Welch and Goyal (2008) dataset. It is shown that the twin adaptive Lasso method performs well in various rolling window widths and forecast horizons. 3. Paper Two has been accepted for publication on International Economic Review. The other two papers are both under R&R at the Journal of Econometrics. Given the positive feedback in the referee reports, it is likely that both will be accepted soon. 4. All papers are accompanied by open source code on Github. 1. Paper One https://github.com/zhentaoshi/fsPDA 2. Paper Two https://github.com/chenyang45/BoostedHP; https://github.com/zhentaoshi/Boosted_HP_filter 3. Paper Three: https://github.com/zhan-gao/Alasso_Predictive_Regression; https://github.com/zhan-gao/LasForecast 5. Three students participated in open-source coding. Huang Jingyi (Ph.D. student co-author) did Paper One, Chen Yang helped with Paper Two, and Gao Zhan (M.Phil. student co-author) did Paper Three.
