24614817.label: Major findings and research outcome
24614817.value: Boosting works widely in econometric contexts. It theoretical proofs are somewhat more complicated than Lasso. * Paper One: In the potential outcome framework, the panel data approach (Hsiao, Ching and Wan, 2012) constructs the counterfactual by exploiting the correlation between cross-sectional units in panel data. The choice of cross-sectional control units, a key step in their implementation, is nevertheless unresolved in data-rich environment when many possible controls are at the researcher's disposal. We propose the forward selection method to choose control units, and establish validity of post-selection inference. Our asymptotic framework allows the number of possible controls to grow much faster than the time dimension. The easy-to-implement algorithms and their theoretical guarantee extend the panel data approach to big data settings. * Paper Two: This paper proposes an easy-to-implement practical procedure of iterating the he Hodrick-Prescott (HP) smoother that is intended to make the filter a smarter smoothing device for trend estimation and trend elimination. We call this iterated HP technique the boosted HP filter in view of its connection to L2-boosting in machine learning. The paper develops limit theory to show that the boosted HP (bHP) filter asymptotically recovers trend mechanisms that involve unit root processes, deterministic polynomial drifts, and polynomial drifts with structural breaks. A stopping criterion is used to automate the iterative HP algorithm, making it a data-determined method that is ready for modern data-rich environments in economic research. These examples show that the bHP filter is helpful in analyzing a large collection of heterogeneous macroeconomic time series that manifest various degrees of persistence, trend behavior, and volatility. * Paper Three: We explore the pitfalls and possibilities of LASSO methods in this predictive regression framework with mixed degrees of persistence. In the presence of stationary, unit root and cointegrated predictors, we show that the adaptive LASSO asymptotically breaks cointegrated groups although it cannot wipe out all inactive cointegrating variables. This new finding motivates novel post-selection adaptive LASSO, which we call the twin adaptive LASSO (TAlasso), to fix variable selection inconsistency. TAlasso's penalty scheme accommodates the system of heterogeneous regressors, and it recovers the well-known oracle property that implies variable selection consistency and optimal rate of convergence for all three types of regressors. On the contrary, conventional LASSO fails to attain coefficient estimation consistency and variable screening in all components simultaneously, since its penalty is imposed according to the marginal behavior of each individual regressor only.

24614817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24614817.value: Paper One can be used for other method of treatment effect evaluation, for example the synthetic control method, in which many more variables are involved. Paper Two can be further extended into other time series filters, for example the band-pass filter which is another popular algorithm to decompose macroeconomic time series. The current setting of Paper Three allows fixed dimension in order to make the intuition clear enough. It can be extended to incorporate high-dimensional regressors. This extension will involve random matrix theory to control the minimal eigenvalue of the high-dimensional matrix.

24614817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24614817.value: The project have delivered three papers on boosting and Lasso. Boosting, based on a weak base learner, is versatile in econometric contexts. It can be used for variable selection, or repeated shrinkage estimation. Lasso, a machine learning shrinkage method closely related to boosting, can behave very differently in nonstationary time series. We work out adaptive Lasso's variable selection results following the spirit of boosting --- repeated fitting. Although boosting is not as popular as Lasso in econometric research mainly due to the difficulty in theoretical proofs, we show in this project that asymptotic theory can be rigorously established. Moreover, the idea of boosting can help improve Lasso. These machine learning methods are widely applicable in panel data, stationary time series as well as non-stationary time series models.

24617417.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24617417.value: 重源和俊芿：宋代宗教文化及日本淨土佛教的影響

24617417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24617417.value: This research aims to broaden our understanding of the impact of Song (960-1279) religious culture of China on the dynamic Buddhist environment of the late Heian (784-1185) and early Kamakura Periods (1185-1333) in Japan, a time that witnessed the founding of new “sects” of Buddhism, as well as appeals from temples and religious societies for sponsorship from a changing set of political actors. I hope to show that the importation and piecemeal adoption of Song Buddhist trends was an important part of this process, contributing to the broader literature on “Ningbo studies,” Sino-Japanese history, and East Asian religious studies. During the late Heian, after a period of stagnant trade, numerous Japanese Buddhist monks traveled to China for study, returning to Japan with a treasure-house of knowledge about recent continental scholarly developments, religious society organization, architectural trends, and Buddhist statuary and painting. Among these monks were Chōgen and Shunjō, known for the reconstruction of the Tōdaiji and Sennyūji temples, respectively. While each introduced new architectural concepts from China that ultimately failed to gain traction, they also imported Song Pure Land commentaries and knowledge of the Pure Land society based at Yanqingsi temple in Ningbo, texts and praxis that would impact the nascent Japanese sectarian Pure Land societies forming at the end of the 12th and beginning of the 13th centuries. These sectarian societies have sometimes earned the characterization “New Kamakura Buddhism,” standing in contrast with older Buddhist schools established centuries before. Scholarship has questioned the degree to which New Kamakura Buddhism defined the religious landscape of the time, as well as the relations between new and established forms Buddhism. However, the dominant understanding remains that sectarian Pure Land schools tracing themselves to the monks Hōnen and Shinran were indigenous Japanese developments. I suggest that the story is more complex: these sectarian societies in fact borrowed organizational principles introduced from southern China by Chōgen for his far-flung Pure Land network that he established to fund the reconstruction of Tōdaiji. They also borrowed doctrines from Song Pure Land commentaries imported by Shunjō for the defense of their teachings. In these ways, sectarian Pure Land in Japan in fact participated in an emerging East China Sea religious macroculture that transcended political and territorial boundaries. 這項研究涉及中國宋代宗教文化如何影響日本平安時代（784 - 1185）晚期和鎌倉時代（1185-1333）早期的動態佛教的環境。在此期間的日本佛教，新“教派”建立，而且寺廟和宗教社會從不斷變化的政治行為者收到了新資金來源。我希望表明，宋代佛教趨勢的進口和零碎採用是這一進程的重要組成部分。這項研究與“寧波研究”，“中日曆史”，和“東亞宗教研究”有關。 在平安晚期，經過一段時間的貿易停滯，許多日本僧人前往中國讀書。回到日本，他們掌握了最近大陸學術發展，宗教社會組織，建築潮流，佛教雕像和繪畫有關的知識。這些僧人中有重源和俊芿，分別以東大寺和泉涌寺寺廟的重建而聞名。雖然他們引進中國的新建築概念最終都沒有得到牽引，但他們從寧波的延慶寺還進口了宋代淨土佛教的經疏和淨土社會的知識。這些文字和實踐將影響到在十二世紀末和十三世紀初之間形成的日本淨土社會。 這些宗派社會有時被稱為“新鎌倉佛教”，與幾百年前建立的老佛教學校形成鮮明對比。學者質疑了新鎌倉佛教在那個時期的宗教景觀有多重要，以及新形式的佛教和已建立的佛教之間有何關係。然而，主要的理解仍然是，跟隨僧侶法然和親鸞的日本淨土教派是日本土著的發展。我認為這個故事更為複雜：這些宗派社會實際上從中國南方採用了重源為資助東大寺的重建引進的淨土組織原則。這些日本淨土教派還借用了俊芿輸入的宋代淨土經疏來捍衛自己的教義。在這些方面，日本淨土宗派實際上參與了一個超越政治和領土界限的新興東海宗教文化。

24618417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24618417.value: With the growth of 24/7 economies, nonstandard work schedules (NWS), defined as those outside the typical daytime span of 6 am to 6 pm, have become increasingly common in developed countries. In particular, NWS are prevalent among low-income parents with young children, which has raised concerns about the possible influence of parental NWS on young children’s well-being and their developmental outcomes. It is not clear a priori whether parental NWS affect childern either positively or negatively. Work-family conflict theory and work-family enrichment theory, which are two major perspectives on the link between work and family, have completely different views on the relationship between parental NWS and child development. Work-family conflict theory regards parental NWS as a sources of parental role conflicts that may have detrimental effects on children, whereas work-family enrichment theory indicates that parental NWS can be used as a family-friendly work option that may in turn have positive impacts on children. These competing theories suggest that empirical research is required to ascertain the link between parental NWS and child development. However, empirical research on the association between parental work schedules and child development has just recently emerged, resulting in lack of understanding of how and under what conditions parental NWS affect child development. More importantly, given the fact that most empirical studies have been conducted in Western contexts, the effects of parental NWS on young children have not been identified in the Hong Kong context, despite the potential implications for Hong Kong families who juggle the competing demands of work and family. This study addresses this knowledge gap by collecting longitudinal data on Hong Kong parents and their young children (aged 5–6), to examine how and under what conditions parental NWS affect young children’s developmental outcomes. This study is expected to enhance our understanding of the work-family conflict faced by Hong Kong families, which may guide the development of family-friendly workplace and childcare policies that buffer or offset the potential negative effect of parental NWS on young children. 隨著全天候經濟的發展，越來越多發達國家使用非標準工時制(nonstandard work schedules, NWS)。NWS指的是在非慣常的白天工作時間 (即上午6時至下午6時之外) 工作的制度。NWS在有年幼子女的低收入家庭中的採用較為普遍，這引起外界關注父母採用NWS對於其年幼子女的身心健康及個人發展的影響。但是，目前，尚未了解父母採用NWS對其子女的影響是正面的抑或是負面的。有關理論，例如，工作-家庭衝突理論(work-family conflict theory)與工作-家庭增益理論(work-family enrichment theory)是在工作與家庭之間的關係方面主要的兩個視角，它們對於父母採用NWS與其子女發展之間的關係有著完全不同的觀點。工作-家庭衝突理論認為，NWS會導致父母角色產生衝突，對子女有著負面的影響。然而，工作-家庭增益理論指出，NWS可作為父母的家庭友善的工作選擇，對子女有著正面的影響。這些觀點不同的理論意味著我們需要用實證研究探討父母採用NWS 與其子女發展之間的關係。但是，目前，有關父母採用NWS與其子女發展的關係的研究仍處於起步階段，所以我們無法深入了解父母採用NWS如何及在什麼條件下影響子女的發展。更重要的是，儘管大部分這方面的實證研究來自於西方，並可能對香港那些追求工作與家庭平衡的家庭有潛在啟示，現時尚未有研究探討香港父母採用NWS對其子女發展的影響。為填補這空缺，是項研究將收集有關香港父母及其年幼子女（5-6歲）的縱向數據，測量父母採用NWS如何、在什麼條件下影響其子女的發展。是項研究旨在了解香港家庭的工作與家庭衝突，對家庭友善的工作場所與育兒政策作出指引，從而緩解或消除父母採用NWS對其子女潛在的負面影響。

24618417.label: Realisation of objectives
24618417.value: The research project involves longitudinal data collection (Wave 1 and Wave 2) to examine the interplay among parental nonstandard work schedules (NWSs), parenting, and child development, with a focus on young children and their parents in Hong Kong (HK). Prior to Wave 1 data collection, the PI developed a survey questionnaire, based on additional literature reviews and consultations with international/local experts in work-family research and child development, so as to effectively measure parental work schedules, parenting stress, and child development outcomes. During the process, it was determined to additionally include scales to measure parents’ work-family conflict and parenting behaviors, along with scales stated in the proposal (parenting stress, parental involvement, and child development), in that the additional measures can also serve as important mediators for the association between parental NWSs and child outcomes. For data collection, the PI recruited a representative sample of preschoolers and their parents, using multi-stage sampling methods. As a sample frame, the Education Bureau’s district preschool list, which includes information about all registered kindergarten in the 18 districts of HK, was used. Specifically, the kindergartens in the list were grouped into three groups, according to district-level median household income (i.e., group 1, 2, and 3 included kindergartens in top 6 income districts, middle 6 income districts, and bottom 6 income districts, respectively) to ensure the inclusion of low-income parents who are more likely to work nonstandard hours. Kindergartens randomly selected from each group were invited, which resulted in 39 kindergartens (15, 10, and 14 from the high-, middle-, and low-income group, respectively) joining the study. With the permission of the kindergarten principals, the PI invited parents with an upper-class child, which is the target population. After sharing information about the research, 633 parents expressed their interest and agreed to join the project. The vast majority of the parents expressed stronger preferences for mail survey, in that in-person survey, which was initially considered, might cause scheduling-related challenges. Based on the parent’s scheduling needs, mail survey was used. Though the mail survey has generally limitations in terms of return rates, the Wave 1 data collection, coupled with the PI’s continuous efforts to encourage the parents to complete and return the questionnaire, resulted in high return rates (85.3%; N= 540). Based on the data, the PI was able to examine the prevalence of parental NWSs among HK parents with young children (Objective 1). As revealed by the 1st paper in Part C, a substantial number of Hong Kong parents with preschoolers were employed on nonstandard hours. Specifically, 25.2% of fathers and 14.4% of mothers were estimated to work NWSs. Such a prevalence is comparable to those found in Western countries (e.g., US) and slightly greater than those of other Asian countries (e.g., Korea). The data also allowed the PI to achieve Objective 2 investigating the association between parental work schedules and child development outcomes. The aforementioned paper (i.e., the 1st paper in Part C) conducted regression to see whether parental NWSs are associated with early child development outcomes, controlling for potential confounders. It found empirical evidence that paternal NWSs may have adverse effects on child development outcomes. Particularly, working evenings or nights had significant negative effects. In contrast, maternal NWSs were found to be a non-significant predictor, suggesting a gender difference in the association between parental NWSs and child development. To achieve Objective 3, the PI also conducted moderation analyses designed to examine whether the association between parental work schedules and young children’s developmental outcomes differs by family characteristics. Moderation analyses found that the negative association between paternal NWSs and child development was salient among low-income families, but was not observed for middle and high-income families, suggesting that the adverse effect of paternal NWSs was not evenly distributed. Taken together, the aforementioned analyses and findings provide empirical evidence to assess the validity of two competing theories (i.e., work-family conflict theory and work-family enrichment theory) as a conceptual framework of the association between parental work schedules and child development in Hong Kong (Objective 4). While work-family conflict theory, highlighting the negative aspect of nonstandard work schedules, has been a dominant perspective, a growing body of research has emerged and illuminated the potential positive aspect of such work schedules, at least in the Western context. For instance, one of the PI’s paper (i.e., the 3rd paper in Part C) pointed out that a significant proportion of Western parents purposefully and voluntarily chose NWSs for child care reasons (e.g., maximize parental care during daytime hours), suggesting the validity of work-family enrichment theory. In the HK context, nevertheless, it appears that the finding of the project offer support for work-family conflict theory, suggesting that it is imperative to develop and implement policies and/or program to address challenges faced by local HK children whose parents work NWSs. However, it is also noteworthy that this project is the first to examine the interplay of parental NWSs and child development in the HK context, and thus it should be seen as providing an important beginning point for additional investigations. In an effort to shed light on the mechanism by which parental NWSs affect children, the PI has also conducted mediation analyses to examine whether the association between parental NWSs and child development is mediated by 1) parenting stress, 2) parental involvement in children’s education, and 3) perceived work-family conflict. For the mediation analyses, it is imperative to establish temporal order of the predictor, mediators and outcome variables. Thus, the mediation analyses rely on longitudinal data (i.e., both Wave 1 and Wave 2 data). It should be noted that the second wave of data collection experienced a significant disruption due to the restrictions posed by the COVID-19 pandemic. Indeed, the outbreak of the pandemic, which occurred just a few weeks before the scheduled start of the Wave 2 data collection, unavoidably delayed the data collection process. After a few months of wait-and-see, moreover, the PI had to switch to online data collection, so as to address the restrictions posed by the COVID-19 pandemic and thereby complete the Wave 2 data collection in a timely manner. Though the transition required additional months for preparation and administration, the PI was able to manage to collect Wave 2 data from a sizable number of the Wave 1 participants (retention rate was approximately 60%), which makes it possible for the PI to conduct longitudinal mediation analyses. While collecting the Wave 2 data, moreover, the PI examined the psychometric properties of some scales whose reliability and validity were unknown in the Chinese context. For instance, the 2nd paper in Part C demonstrated the reliability/validity of the Chinese version of the Work and Family Conflict Scale. The paper provides a methodological justification to use the scale to measure and examine work-family conflict for medication analyses. At the time of writing this completion report, the findings of the mediation analysis indicate that parental involvement in children’s education and work-family conflict serve as mediators that link parental work schedules and child development outcomes. A manuscript containing the mediation findings are in progress and will be submitted to a high impact journal, such as Applied Research in Quality-of-Life.

24618417.label: Major findings and research outcome
24618417.value: This project firstly examined the prevalence of parental nonstandard work schedules among Hong Kong parents with young children, which revealed that a substantial number of Hong Kong parents with preschoolers were employed on nonstandard hours. Specifically, 25.2% of fathers and 14.4% of mothers were estimated to work nonstandard hours. Such a prevalence is comparable to those found in Western countries (e.g., US) and slightly greater than those of other Asian countries (e.g., Korea). In addition, the study also examined the association between parental work schedules and child development outcomes. Paternal nonstandard work schedules were found to have adverse effects on child development outcomes. Such negative associations were particularly salient when father worked night or evening shifts, and among low-income families. By contrast, maternal nonstandard work schedules were found to be a non-significant predictor, suggesting a gender difference in the association between parental nonstandard works schedules and child development. To shed light on the mechanism by which parental nonstandard work schedules affect child development, mediation analyses were also conducted. The findings, though preliminary, indicated that parental involvement in children’s education and work-family conflict scores (validated by a psychometric study using this project data) serve as mediators that link parental work schedules and child development outcomes. Taken together, the findings of the study offer support for work-family conflict theory, which conceptualizes parental nonstandard work schedules as a work characteristic that may have negative repercussions for family life.

24618417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24618417.value: 1. A follow-up study: As noted above, this project found a gender difference in the association between parental nonstandard work schedules and child development outcomes. A follow-up study will be conducted to shed light on the nature and reason of the gender difference. Specifically, the study will examine whether the difference is due to a gendered pattern of how working parents allocate their time to paid work and child rearing (e.g., working mothers, unlike working fathers, tend to sacrifice their personal time to maintain the time they spend with children). 2. Conducting research in mainland China. The PI had opportunities to share the project findings with colleagues from mainland universities, which led to collaborative research to examine the effect of parental nonstandard work schedules on children in the mainland context. Data collection process has been already started with an expected completion date in early 2022.

24618417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24618417.value: With the emergence of 24/7 economies, the practice of working nonstandard schedules (often called shift work) has become increasingly common. This trend raises a concern about how parental nonstandard work schedules affect child development outcomes, in that parents working nonstandard hours may find it difficult to maintain regular parent-child interaction. In addition, they are likely to have less physical and mental energy for effective parenting, which in turn may have adverse impacts on the children. This study, based on data from families with young children (age 5–6) in Hong Kong, found that fathers’ nonstandard work schedules were negatively associated with overall child development. This association was particularly salient among low-income families. By contrast, mothers’ nonstandard work schedules were not associated with child development outcomes. These findings suggest that it is important to equip parents, in particular low-income fathers, to address challenges resulting from their nonstandard work schedules.

25100017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25100017.value: 由於耐藥性病菌的滋生，細菌感染再次成為威脅人類健康和全球經濟的重要問題。具有獨特藥理活性的新型抗菌藥物的發現為解決這個問題提供了可能性。 根據對細菌基因轉錄過程的機制研究，我們發現在細菌基因表達過程中重要的蛋白與蛋白間相互作用可以影響到細菌的生存，如RNA聚合酶與sigma轉錄起始因子的相互作用。根據與此相互作用相關的氨基酸結構，我們設計並篩選出一個對好氧和厭氧細菌的生長都具有抑制作用的小分子化合物。 在本研究計劃中，我們將對這個活性分子的結構進行化學改造，通過生物化學和抑菌實驗等方法比較並確認結構優化的方向。我們希望在本研究中總結出可以抑制RNA聚合酶與sigma轉錄因子相互作用的構效關係，並提供數個有抑菌活性的候選化合物進入之後階段的體內藥理研究。這項科研計劃的實施亦將提供一個針對細菌基因轉錄過程進行藥物開發的平台，對將來其他以轉錄為藥物靶標的新藥候選化合物的開發提供技術支持。

25100017.label: Realisation of objectives
25100017.value: Bacterial infectious diseases pose serious problems to human health and the economy. The World Health Organization published a priority pathogen list for guiding the R&D of antibiotics in 2017. Bacterial transcription is a valid but underutilized target for antimicrobial agent discovery; rifamycins and fidaxomicin are the only two types of antibiotics used in clinics that target bacterial RNA polymerase (RNAP). Bacterial RNAP core enzyme composed of five subunits (α dimer, β, β’ and ω) is capable of RNA synthesis on synthetic single-stranded DNA templates but requires accessory σ factors to initiate transcription at promoters. Bacterial σ factor binds to RNAP to form a holoenzyme, specifically recognizes promoter DNA elements, and triggers DNA strand separation to expose the transcription start site to initiate RNA synthesis. Housekeeping σ factors (named σA in most bacteria, σ70 in Escherichia coli) required for transcription of most genes are highly conserved and essential for cell functions and viability. Determination of high-resolution structures of RNAP holoenzyme complexes paved a road toward the structure-guided discovery of antimicrobial agents targeting the RNAP-σ interaction. The interactions between the clamp helices (CH) domain of the RNAP β′ subunit and σ70 region 2.2 are thought to play a dominant role in the holoenzyme formation. Focusing on key amino acid residues at the β′CH-σ2.2 interface, we designed a pharmacophore model and carried out in silico screening for protein-protein (PPI) inhibitors. We were particularly interested in a triaryl compound due to its drug-like properties and the presumed efficiency of structure modification. Using the ELISA-based inhibitory assay and the protein complement assay, we have confirmed that the compound specifically inhibited the β′CH-σ interaction in vitro. it displayed mild antimicrobial activity against Streptococcus pneumoniae ATCC 49619 with a minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of 256 μg/mL. Preliminary structural optimizations were carried out. We first investigated the contribution of the left benzene ring while keeping the right benzoic acid moiety intact, because the latter was predicted to form strong ionic bonds to two β′ arginine residues R278 and R281 (E. coli numbering). A simple modification from 2-aminobenzene to 3,4-dichlorobenzene significantly improved the antimicrobial activity against S. pneumoniae to an MIC of 8 μg/mL; in addition, the inhibitory effects on S. pneumoniae toxin production were comparable to those of antibiotics currently on the market. In this study, we modified the right benzoyl benzoic acid motif to explore the appropriate chemical space required for binding to the β′CH and the resulting changes in the antimicrobial activity. According to the pharmacophore docking model, the right benzoic acid is pincered by the β′CH residues R278 and R281. Therefore, we explored the substituents on the right benzene ring and test their effects on antimicrobial activity. Additionally, we verified the importance of benzoic acid for activity by using modifications to other functional groups. The results showed that structural flexibility at the benzyl group did not affect the antibacterial activity and that the rigid benzoyl structure may present the active conformation for activity. Substitution on the right benzene ring is important, as reflected by changes in both protein-binding inhibition and antibacterial activities. Electron-withdrawing and donating substituents can both improve the antibacterial activity, while electron-withdrawing groups were preferred, probably because of increased ionic bonding interaction between benzoic acid and β′CH residues R278 and R281, which are critical for σ binding. Para-substituted derivatives demonstrated greater activity than meta isomers. The best result was obtained against S. epidermidis, with an MIC value of 0.5 μg/mL equal to that of vancomycin, the last-resort antibiotic in clinical practice. In addition, the representative compounds displayed antibacterial activity against C. difficile, including type strain and clinical isolates. C. difficile, an opportunistic pathogen causing fatal diarrhea and associated diseases, produces cytotoxins responsible for hypervirulence. The representative compounds inhibited toxin secretion of C. difficile at sub-MIC levels without affecting cell growth, similarly to fidaxomicin, another inhibitor of transcription that has been approved for the treatment of C. difficile infections. antibiotic drug. The toxin secretion inhibitory effect of the representative compounds was even more significant compared to vancomycin as a common therapeutic choice in clinics for treating C. difficile infections. Mechanistic studies were first carried out using in vitro protein complement assay. Several representative compounds were evaluated, and IC50 values of these compounds reached the sub-μM level, suggesting structural modifications maintained the protein-ligand affinity. When the experiment was carried out within the whole-cell system, fluorescence microscopy demonstrated the representative compounds started to disrupt the normal functions of RNAP and cause nucleoid delocalization in cells even at a sub-MIC level. Likewise, cell content quantification demonstrated that bacteria treated by sub-MIC of the representative compounds reduced RNA production as rifampicin, a transcription inhibitor antibiotic drug, while normal cell growth was maintained. Finally, cytotoxicity measurement showed that these series of compounds exhibited exceptionally low toxic effects on two human cell lines, and rat liver microsomal metabolism assay demonstrated significant stability compared to carbamazepine. The experimental results suggest that these series of compounds are potential for further studies towards antibiotic development. In summary, we could conclude the successful achievement of each project objective: Objective 1: We used the established procedure and developed new assays for bioactivity evaluation of the designed inhibitors of bacterial transcription initiation. A series of biochemical and biophysical assays were applied to confirm the bioactivity and in vitro mechanism of the inhibitors as designed. Objective 2: We synthesized the inhibitor derivatives rationally against the pharmacophore features for structure-activity relationship study and optimization. Several series of compounds (~100) were obtained to construct a compound library as a pool of antimicrobial candidates for further development. The inhibitors identified from the virtual screening underwent modifications and provided the optimal bioactivity. Objective 3: We assessed the antimicrobial activity of the synthesized derivatives of bacteria under treatment of these derivatives. The antimicrobial activity was evaluated and compared among inhibitor derivatives. The representative compounds demonstrated excellent antimicrobial activity against Gram-positive bacterial with minimum inhibitory concentrations of ~1 μg/mL. The best result was the MIC of 0.5 μg/mL against S. epidermidis, a clinically significant Group B Staphylococcus (GBS) pathogen. Objective 4: We confirmed the cellular mechanism of inhibitor derivatives. The in-cell mechanism was examined to ensure that the derivatives exhibit antimicrobial activity through targeted site inhibition as designed. The detailed results have been published in top medicinal chemistry journals.

25100017.label: Major findings and research outcome
25100017.value: In summary, we designed and identified a hit compound with the diaryl benzoic acid structure showing antimicrobial activity and inhibitory activity targeting the protein-protein interaction between bacterial RNA polymerase and initiation factor sigma. Consequently, we designed a high-throughput screening method to test the inhibitory activity of protein-protein interactions for activity screening (Research output 1). With the activity screening method in hand, we performed structural modifications and demonstrated the improvement of antimicrobial activity and additional inhibition to bacterial toxin release (Research output 2). Finally, we synthesized several series, in total about 100 derivative compounds, and perform antimicrobial activity measurement, mechanistic studies using biochemical, in vitro transcription assay, and cell-based methods, as well as in vitro pharmacokinetic evaluation (Research output 5 and 6). As shown by the biological testing results, the derivative compounds improved the antimicrobial activity to 1 μg/mL against Streptococcus pneumoniae and other clinically significant pathogens, while they maintained low cytotoxicity and drug-like properties. Therefore, the representative derivatives are promising candidates for further development as novel antimicrobial agents.

25100017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25100017.value: In this project, we successfully identified a series of new class small molecules that demonstrated potential as antimicrobials. A compound library was synthesized to provide a pool of drug candidates for further development. Currently, more structural modifications are carried out to explore the structural diversity for antimicrobial activity. In parallel, animal experiments such as in vivo pharmacokinetic study and antimicrobial efficacy tests using infectious mouse models are undergoing in the laboratory. Moreover, our approach continues to pave the way for a solid platform of novel antimicrobial discovery, with a focus on bacterial transcription as a drug target. In addition to their potential future therapeutic value, this series of compounds could be developed as chemical probes for studies of σ factor-mediated transcription regulation.

25100017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25100017.value: Infectious diseases caused by bacteria have re-emerged to become a crisis for human health and the global economy. Bacterial strains resistant to all current antibiotics have been reported. Therefore, there is an urgent need for structurally novel antimicrobial agents with targets and mechanisms distinct from those of the existing drugs. Structure-based drug design and synthesis have been adapted to identify novel antimicrobial agents by exploring novel biological targets, and the synthetic antimicrobial agents have several advantages over antibiotics developed from natural products: structural simplicity, amenability to efficient synthetic modifications, and a lack of innate resistance mechanisms. We rationally designed and synthesized a class of triaryl derivatives of one hit compound targeting the protein-protein interaction between bacterial RNA polymerase and initiation factor sigma, and succeeded in drastically improving the antimicrobial activity against Streptococcus pneumoniae, with the minimum inhibitory concentration reduced from 256 to 1 μg/mL. Additional characterization of antimicrobial activity, inhibition of transcription, in vitro pharmacological properties, and cytotoxicity of the optimized compounds demonstrated their potential for further development.

25100217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25100217.value: Diabetes mellitus is a risk factor for dementia, cognitive impairment and neurodegenerative disorders. Effective treatment of diabetes-associated neurodegeneration will therefore significantly reduce the incidence of cognitive impairment associated with diabetes. Adiponectin is a major adipokine that plays an essential role in diabetes-linked metabolic abnormalities, making adiponectin-based therapeutic treatment a major focus of diabetes treatment. Therapeutics targeting adiponectin receptors are also under active investigation. AdipoRon, a newly discovered adiponectin receptor agonist, displays promising antidiabetic metabolic effect in mice. However, its effects on improving cognitive impairment associated with diabetes have not yet been examined. Physical exercise is effective in treating diabetes, and may be effective, in part, because it enhances adiponectin levels. Moreover, exercise is known to promote cognitive learning and memory performance. These cognitive benefits are known to be partly due to exercise-induced structural and functional plasticity in the hippocampus, an important brain region for learning and memory formation. Moreover, increasing adiponectin levels can increase the number of new-born neurons (adult neurogenesis) and synaptic plasticity (strengthening of synapses) in the dentate gyrus of the hippocampus. Our pilot data has shown that adiponectin enhances synaptic plasticity and is required for exercise to enhance hippocampal neurogenesis in diabetic mice, suggesting its potential as an exercise mimetic to promote hippocampal function. An important next step in our research program is to determine if AdipoRon improves diabetes-associated cognitive impairment similar to physical exercise. Because AMP-kinase (AMPK)/BDNF/PGC-1α signalling pathway mediates adiponectin’s action on metabolism and is important for synaptogenesis and neurogenesis, we hypothesize that AdipoRon exerts its cognitive benefits via adiponectin receptor-mediated activation of AMPK/BDNF/PGC-1α pathway, which enhances adult neurogenesis, dendritic complexity and synaptic plasticity in the hippocampus of streptozotocin-induced diabetic mouse model. We aim to evaluate the pro-cognitive effects of AdipoRon by comparing hippocampal-dependent learning and memory performance in diabetic or normal mice with/without AdipoRon treatment in comparison to those with/without voluntary wheel running. Hippocampal plasticity will be examined using immunostaining for adult neurogenesis, Golgi staining for dendritic complexity, electrophysiology and Western blot analysis for synaptic plasticity, and culture neurons for examining signalling molecules. This work will enable us to establish a link between therapeutic effects of AdipoRon, and changes in hippocampal plasticity in preventing diabetes-related cognitive impairment. The results will clarify AdipoRon’s role in promoting hippocampal function and its potential as an “exercise pill” for enhancing cognition. The findings will also help to identify new and novel therapeutic targets for treating cognitive impairment.

25100217.label: Major findings and research outcome
25100217.value: Our results have provided the evidence that chronic treatment with adipoRon which can activate adiponectin signaling can effectively restore diabetes-induced learning and memory impairment. This behavioral results could be due to AdipoRon's action on restoring hippocampal adult neurogenesis, dendritic remodeling, spine density and synaptic plasticity. The molecular assays has confirmed that adipoRon treatment promotes hippocampal neuroplasticity in diabetic mice via AMPK/PGC-1alpha/BDNF pathway in the hippocampus. The results have demonstrated that chronic adipoRon treatment can mimic the neuroprotective effects of physical exercise on protecting against diabetes-associated hippocampal dysfunction, hence enhance cognitive learning and memory impairments. Our results have provided evidence that AdipoRon could be a potential physical exercise mimetic to improve hippocampal plasticity and hence rescue learning and memory impairment typically associated with diabetes. Th results have been published in two peer reviewed journals, 4 conference abstracts.

25100217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25100217.value: Further development will aim to examine whether manipulating adiponectin receptor downstream adaptor protein APPL1 activity could lead to the similar neuroprotective effects of physical exercise since this target will be more specific and more downstream to the adiponectin signaling pathway to induce hippocampal neuroplasticity. This will advance pharmacological development with more specific treatment target in a more specific manner. Since hippocampal dysfunction is also involved in other different neurological disorders, and impairment hippocampal function could be linked to depression, future experiments will also aim to examine the effects of exercise mimetic drug AdipoRon on depressive phenotypes associated with diabetes.

25100217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25100217.value: Diabetes is associated with lower adiponectin levels and higher risk of dementia. Physical exercise show opposite effects in preventing dementia and increasing adiponectin levels. Adiponectin is an adipokine that regulates diabetes-linked metabolic abnormalities, making adiponectin-based therapeutics a potential diabetes treatment. AdipoRon is an adiponectin receptor agonist which can activate adiponectin downstream signaling and shows anti-diabetic effects similar to adiponectin. The current project has demonstrated the significant effects of chronic treatment with AdipoRon on restoring learning and memory impairment in diabetes-induced learning and memory impairments, resembling the neuroprotective effects of performing physical running in diabetic mice. In diabetic mice, adipoRon treatment restores learning and memory impairment by increasing hippocampal functions in terms of increased structural and functional plasticity in the hippocampal subregion named dentate gyrus. This effect is dependent on AMP/PGC-1alpha/BDNF molecular signaling. The treatment effects is similar to that obtained with physical running in diabetic mice, suggesting chronic pharmacological treatment with adipoRon could elicit similar effects to physical exercise to restore learning and memory impairment associated with diabetes. The results have provide evidence that neuroprotective effects of physical exercise could be obtained with pharmacological treatment targeting adiponectin signaling in diseased brains like diabetes.

25101017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25101017.value: 背景: 失眠是一種非常普遍的問題。針灸是改善睡眠質素的一種另類治療，可是其療效及對失眠的治療機制仍有待進一步研究。針灸可能減輕氧化應激。氧化應激被認為是失眠帶來的重要的病理性因素。 研究目的: 評估一個半個人化的針灸治療對失眠的療效及其安全性，以及檢驗針灸治療對原發性失眠患者的氧化應激參數的影響。 研究方法: 這是一個隨機對照試驗，對象為140個符合精神疾病診斷與統計手冊第五版的失眠症患者，當中排除因疾病、精神問題或睡眠障礙而可能引致失眠症狀的參加者。參加者將以1:1的比例隨機分配到針灸組或假針灸組 (對照組)。針灸組將接受採用半個人化的治療方案的針灸治療。假針灸組將會以相似的方式，接受以經已驗證、不具穿透性的假針灸針實施的針灸。主觀評核結果 (睡眠情況問卷和睡眠日記) 與客觀評核結果 (腕動計) 均會在研究基線、治療後第一週及第五週被紀錄。空腹血液樣本將會在這些評估時間點的早上收集，以量度氧化應激參數，包括丙二醛（MDA）水平和穀胱甘肽過氧化酶（GPx），對氧磷酶（PON）和芳酯酶（ARE）的活躍程度。研究的主要評核結果包括在完成治療後第一週的睡眠日記所量度的睡眠效率以及各種氧化應激參數。 數據分析: 兩組之間的睡眠與氧化應激參數在每一個時間點的改變會以混合效果模型作比較。睡眠參數及氧化應激參數的關聯會透過皮爾森相關分析作驗證。研究會進行中介效應檢驗以探討氧化應激參數對睡眠可能存在的中介變項效應。 重要性: 失眠嚴重程度與氧化應激參數的關係尚在研究中。據我們現時所知，尚未有研究驗證針灸對失眠患者的氧化應激的效應。本研究不只為針灸作為失眠治療提供了高質量的證據，亦同時為氧化應激參數的相關變化提供證明。這將會引導未來對失眠的病理及治療機制的研究。

25101017.label: Realisation of objectives
25101017.value: To achieve objective 1 (evaluating the safety and efficacy of semi-individualized acupuncture treatment in improving sleep in subjects with insomnia disorder using non-invasive sham acupuncture as a control), we conducted a randomized controlled trial (RCT). The RCT aims to evaluate the safety and efficacy of 4-week semi-individualized acupuncture in improving sleep and examine its effects on oxidative stress parameters in subjects with insomnia disorder. A total of 140 subjects with DSM-5 insomnia disorder were recruited from the community through advertisements on the internet, mass email, and recruitment posters in universities and university clinics in Hong Kong. Eligible subjects were randomly assigned to either electroacupuncture group or sham acupuncture group according to a computer-generated block randomization list in a 1:1 ratio. Sequentially numbered, sealed and opaque envelopes were also adopted to ensure the concealment of group allocation before the completion of baseline assessments. Subjects in two groups were comparable as no significant group difference was detected in all the socio-demographic data and outcome measures at baseline (all p > 0.05). During each treatment visit, the acupuncturist assessed the participants according to TCM theory. There are 8 fixed acupoints and the acupuncturist will be allowed to select another 8 additional acupoints depending on clinical judgment. This allows flexibility for the acupuncturist to adjust the acupoint selection across the treatment course. In the treatment group, the acupuncturist used acupuncture needle to treat their patients and the needles were connected to an electric-stimulator to deliver electric-stimulation. In the control group, all the acupuncture procedures delivered in identical procedures, length of each treatment visit, treatment frequency, except that validated non-invasive sham needles were used. The sham needles are also connected to the same electric stimulator, but no current was applied. The setting of the control group allows investigation of the importance of needle insertion and electric stimulation in the acupuncture treatment. The sham intervention was adopted as a control in this study to control other non-specific effects related to electroacupuncture, including the practitioner-patient interaction, needling procedure, contact time with the research personnel, and placebo effects. Therefore, it allows the investigation of effective components of acupuncture such as skin penetration, deqi sensation, and electric-stimulation. Participants’ sleep and other outcomes were assessed at baseline, 1-week post-treatment (week 5) and 5-week post-treatment (week 9) for intermediate and short-term effects. The primary outcome was the sleep efficiency (SE) estimated by the total sleep time (TST) over time in bed (TIB) derived from the 7-day standardized sleep diary. Other secondary outcome measures include the sleep parameters (sleep onset latency, wake time after sleep onset, and total sleep time) assessed by sleep diary, self-rated severity of insomnia symptoms by Insomnia Severity Index, anxiety/depressive symptoms by Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS) and health-related quality of life by Short-Form Six-Dimension (SF-6D). These Chinese questionnaires had been widely used and validated in previous studies. Objective outcome measures were included as a subsidy of patient-reported outcomes. The primary objective outcome was the oxidative stress parameters including the malondialdehyde (MDA) level, and the glutathione peroxidase (GPx), paraoxonase (PON), and arylesterase (ARE) activities. Actigraphy, as an objective measure of sleep/wake parameters, was recorded for seven consecutive nights concurrently with the subjective sleep diary. To assess the safety of the interventions, adverse events were asked at each visit, and reasons for withdrawal were recorded for incomplete cases. Collected data was double-entered and inspected for data cleaning before performing analyses. Both intention-to-treat and per-protocol analyses were adopted that missing data were handled by mixed-effect model to examine the group by time point interaction effect on the between-group difference in changes in all outcome measures across study time points. A sensitivity analysis was performed with the multiple imputations of 10 sets of imputations to evaluate the impact of missing data on outcome measures. Therefore, all the participants can be included in analysis even some of them may miss one time point under the assumption of random missing. Associations between a list of pre-specific covariates, such as age and the presence of chronic medical illness, and treatment responses were explored with Pearson's correlation. Objectives of exploring the effect of acupuncture on improving sleep and oxidative stress parameters can be achieved if the pre-specific covariates have no impact on treatment responses. The prevalence of adverse events was compared between acupuncture and sham acupuncture group using Chi-square test for investigating the safety of acupuncture treatment. To achieve objective 2 (examining the changes in oxidative stress parameters in subjects with insomnia disorder after receiving semi-individualized acupuncture and non-invasive placebo acupuncture), we had taken the blood sample from the subjects at baseline and week 5 (1-week post-treatment) to analyse their oxidative stress parameters. Venous blood samples (2 ml), were collected from all subjects between 8:00 a.m. and 9:00 a.m. after an overnight fasting period. Four oxidative stress parameters were measured, namely MDA, GPx, PON, and ARE. MDA is a commonly used marker of lipid peroxidation and an indicator of oxidative stress. These oxidative stress parameters had been found to be different between subjects with insomnia and good sleep controls. MDA, a secondary end product of the oxidation of polyunsaturated fatty acids, was measured using Cayman TBARS (thiobarbituric acid reactive substances) assay kit (cat. no. 10009055) to indicate cell membranes lipid peroxidation and cells damage. GPx enzyme activity was determined with Glutathione Peroxidase Cellular Activity Assay from Sigma Chemical (cat. no. CGP1). It was measured directly by a coupled reaction with glutathione reductase (GR). A decrease in absorbance at 340nm was recorded due to the oxidation of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH) in the coupled reaction and was indicative of GPx activity. Concentrations of human PON were measured using a commercial ELISA Kit (Cusabio; cat. no. CSB-E09484h) which employs the quantitative sandwich enzyme immunoassay technique. ARE activity was determined using a commercial arylesterase/paraoxonase assay (Zeptometrix Corporation, Buffalo, New York; cat. no 0801199), which is based on the principle that PON1 catalyses the cleavage of phenyl acetate, yielding the phenol. An increase in absorbance at 270 nm at 25°C due to phenol formation was monitored to determine the arylesterase activity. To achieve objective 3 (examining the correlation of oxidative stress parameters with subjective sleep efficiency and other sleep parameters measured by subjective sleep diary and objective actigraphy), we had conducted a correlation analysis between the sleep parameters and the oxidative stress parameters. The possible mediation effects by oxidative stress parameters will be examined using the methodology described by Baron and Kenny. The association of group allocation and post-treatment subjective sleep efficiency (both 1- and 5-week post-treatment) adjusted for baseline measures and the association between group allocation and change in oxidative stress parameters from baseline to 1-week post-treatment will be determined by linear regression. The mediated effect is in effect the regression coefficient for the association of group allocation with subjective sleep efficiency multiplied by the regression coefficient for the association of oxidative stress parameters with subjective sleep efficiency. Bias corrected 95% confidence intervals with 5000 bootstraps resamples were estimated using the SPSS macro developed by Preacher and Hayes. The mediation effects of oxidative stress on other sleep parameters had also been explored.

25101017.label: Major findings and research outcome
25101017.value: Efficacy and Safety (Objective 1) We found both Traditional and Sham acupuncture would improve insomnia but no significant between-group difference. Traditional Acupuncture is a safe and well-tolerated intervention. For the primary outcome measure, the Traditional Acupuncture and Sham Acupuncture groups did not differ in the primary outcome measure - sleep efficiency (SE) by sleep diary at week 5 and week 9 (all p > 0.05). However, Traditional Acupuncture showed significantly higher increases in both sleep-diary-derived and actigraphy-derived total sleep time (TST) at week 5 (mean difference in sleep diary = 22.0 min, p = 0.01, actigraphy = 18.8 mins., p = 0.02) compared to the Sham Acupuncture. There was also no significant between-group difference in other secondary measures. Regarding safety, the most commonly reported adverse events are pain and bruises around acupuncture sites and dizziness during the treatment period (12.9%, 9.3%, and 5.0% respectively). Most of the reported adverse events were mild and moderate in severity. Only bruise and bleeding around acupuncture sites were more frequently reported in the Traditional Acupuncture group (p < 0.001 and p = 0.03). Withdrawal due to adverse events was 1.4% for both groups, which was not significantly different. No serious adverse event was reported. Oxidative stress parameters (Objective 2) Both Traditional Acupuncture and Sham Acupuncture groups showed a significant decrease in GPx activity level after the intervention (22.0% in the Acupuncture treatment group, P <0.001 and 21.5% in the Sham acupuncture group, P = 0.001). However, there were no significant between-group differences after the intervention. The results indicated that subjects’ oxidative stress levels may decrease after receiving a 4-week acupuncture intervention. Correlating oxidative stress and sleep parameters (Objective 3) We investigated the possible correlation between oxidative stress parameters and sleep parameters. Significant correlations were observed in baseline GPx with baseline sleep-diary total sleep time (r = .26, P =0.002) and sleep-diary SE (r = .28, P =0.001). The indirect and direct effects of Traditional Acupuncture for alleviating insomnia on sleep-diary-derived SE in comparison with Sham Acupuncture at week 5, mediated by changes in the OS parameters from baseline to week 5 post-treatment (MDA, GPx, PON, and ARE) were examined. All the mediation analyses were adjusted for the OS parameters at baseline. Both the direct and indirect effects of group allocation on sleep-diary-derived SE were not significant at 5%, showing that the changes in sleep-diary-derived SE were not mediated by these OS parameters.

25101017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25101017.value: The present study found both traditional acupuncture and sham acupuncture groups showed a significant improvement at week 5 and 9, but no significant difference between the two groups in the primary outcome. The results showed that the specific effects of traditional acupuncture, including the electric-stimulation and skin penetration did not make a difference in the therapeutic effects of acupuncture on insomnia, indicating a high non-specific effect of acupuncture. Since insomnia has been reported to be responsive to placebo treatment, further studies may include a placebo run-in period to exclude the placebo responders. Our mediator analysis did not find the oxidative stress parameters were associated with sleep improvement. Other possible mechanisms, such as melatonin or inhibition of the sympathetic activity of the effects of acupuncture on insomnia may be explored. Our team is planning to investigate the alternation of melatonin in older adults with insomnia after receiving acupuncture. We found both traditional and sham acupuncture improve sleep, but their mechanism of actions may be different. Further investigation using functional MRI may be useful to examine the difference in receiving traditional acupuncture and sham acupuncture.

25101017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25101017.value: This research project found that both traditional acupuncture and non-traditional acupuncture (non-invasive needling at points near to the acupoint sites) produced similar effects on the improvement of sleep efficiency (sleep percentage in bed) for participants with insomnia disorders. However, traditional acupuncture may produce a greater improvement in the total sleep time when compared to the non-traditional acupuncture, which was supported by both subjective and objective sleep measures. The findings suggest that non-traditional acupuncture which does not involve skin-penetration and electric-stimulation may lead to subjective (sleep diary and questionnaire) and objective (wrist-worn watch-like actigraphs) sleep improvement that is comparable to the traditional acupuncture. Overall, both traditional and non-traditional acupuncture are generally safe and well-tolerated interventions that may lead to sleep improvement in individuals with insomnia disorders. Previous studies reported that individuals with insomnia will have a higher level of oxidative stress when compared to good sleepers. Our study found that the activity of glutathione peroxidase (GPx), an anti-oxidative enzyme that protects the organism from oxidative damage, decreased in both traditional and non-traditional acupuncture groups after receiving the intervention. However, further investigation is needed to confirm the role of oxidative stress in the mechanism of acupuncture for relieving insomnia.

25101817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25101817.value: 腰背痛是世界上最容易導致殘疾的健康狀況。雖然腰背痛的主要原因仍然難以捉摸，但因為腰椎多裂肌對腰椎穩定和本體感受扮演重要角色, 這個肌肉被視為會影響腰痛發展的重要因素之一。雖然這個推論是由於觀察到腰背痛患者的腰椎多裂肌比無症狀人士有顯著的形態/功能缺陷，但也有調查沒發現這結果。 這些相矛盾的結果突出了澄清腰椎多裂肌與腰背痛關聯的重要性，以優化腰背痛治療。由於單單檢查腰椎多裂肌的形態是無法得知腰椎多裂肌的功能，評估多種腰椎多裂肌的特徵（形態，機械特性和功能）可以提供更好的腰椎多裂肌評估和腰背痛的預測。此外，由於先前的研究沒有考慮到其他脊椎退化和心理因素的影響，這些因素可能會導致不一致的發現。因此，必須解決以前的研究的局限性，以便確定腰椎多裂肌在腰背痛發展的作用。 最近，我們的研究發現，手法治療後腰椎多裂肌收縮能力的改變是與腰背痛或相關殘疾改善有關。然而，以前的研究只評估一個腰椎多裂肌的特徵，我們擬議的新研究項目將通過評估多個腰椎多裂肌的特徵，脊椎退化和心理因素以確定是否可以更有效地預測背痛患者和無症狀人士的腰背痛的結果。以下的假設將被測試： 1) 腰椎多裂肌的形態，機械特性和功能是相互關聯的。 我們將量化分別已有和沒有腰背痛人士各種腰椎多裂肌的特徵在體內的相互關係。 2) 最初的腰椎多裂肌特徵能夠預測未來腰背痛。 我們將進行一項為期兩年的前瞻性研究，以確定最初的腰椎多裂肌特徵能否在已有和沒有腰背痛人士身上預測未來腰背痛的結果(調整其他脊椎退化和心理因素的影響後)。 3) 一些腰椎多裂肌的特徵轉變與腰背痛結果有關。我們將通過進行逐步線性回歸分析來確定這一假設，在考慮到脊椎退化和心理因素後，以確定哪幾個腰椎多裂肌的特性的改變是跟腰背痛轉變有關。 這研究項目將採用全面的方法來闡明各種腰椎多裂肌特性與腰背痛之間的關係。 它可以幫助早期識別容易患有新的/持續性腰背痛的高風險人士，以便及時地進行預防/治療以盡量減少痛楚和醫療成本。

25101817.label: Realisation of objectives
25101817.value: In total, we recruited 78 volunteers with chronic LBP (CLBP) and 73 without CLBP in the current project at baseline. Because our follow-up period was coincided with the COVID-19 pandemic, many participants decided to delay their follow-ups or refused to undergo the follow-up magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans or physical assessments. Therefore, only 55.1% (n=43) and 56.1% (n=41) of participants with and without CLBP completed the questionnaires. The average attrition rate for completing questionnaire was 44.4%. Their data was used to evaluate the roles of various lumbar multifidus characteristics in predicting LBP intensity or LBP-related disability in people with and without CLBP. It is noteworthy that only 27 participants with and 24 without CLBP underwent the MRI scans and physical assessments. Therefore, the attrition rates for participants with and without CLBP who completed all the follow-up were 65.4% and 67.1%, respectively. Despite these high attrition rates, those completed the questionnaire or physical assessments follow-ups were not significantly different from original participant groups based on demographic data (e.g., age, gender ratio, body mass index, and durations of CLBP). Therefore, they were still representative samples of the two groups. Overall, despite the attrition of participants, the current project have completed all the planned objectives. This project has resulted in three publications in two Q1 and one Q2 peer-reviewed journals with impact factors ranging from 3.133 to 4.157). The findings have also been presented at three local and four international conferences. One of the presentations won the The Hong Kong College of Orthopaedic Surgeons 15th Rehabilitation Symposium Best Paper Award 2021. Currently, we are preparing two more manuscripts for the submission to The Spine Journal. Because of the high attrition rates, the expenditures of the follow-up MRI scans were relatively low. Further, because the MRI centre at The University of Hong Kong (HKU) charged our scans based on the duration of a participant staying within a MRI scanner (in terms of seconds) rather than number of scanned participants, the originally set MRI budget based on number of cases was higher than the actual amount. Because HKU MRI centre and the other private MRI clinic, which obtained approval from the UGC panel sent their invoice after the project end dates. Their MRI charges were not deducted from this project account. Instead, those expenses were settled by the principal investigator. Because of some overseas conferences were canceled or were changed to online format, some of the predetermined conference attendance budget was not used.

25101817.label: Major findings and research outcome
25101817.value: For objective#1 We revealed that young adults with chronic low back pain (CLBP) displayed poorer proprioception sense than age-matched healthy controls. Interestingly, both middle-aged adults with and without CLBP showed inferior proprioceptive sense than young healthy individuals. This indicates that young adults with CLBP have suboptimal lumbar multifidus (LM) proprioception similar to middle-aged people. However, the inferior lumbar proprioception in middle-aged people may be unrelated to LBP (Research Output#3). Compared to asymptomatic individuals, participants with CLBP displayed significantly higher LBP intensity, Roland Morris Disability Questionnaire (RMDQ) scores, as well as more fear avoidance belief, pain catastrophizing, and insomnia. The latter also had less percent thickness changes of LM at the L4/5 level during contraction as measured by ultrasonography. MRI scans found that people with CLBP had smaller LM lean muscle volume over the L3-S1 regions, more severe intervertebral disc (IVD) and facet degeneration from L3/4 to L5/S1, more Modic changes at L4/5, and more facet tropism at L5/S1 than healthy controls. However, baseline LM characteristics or lumbar phenotypes were unrelated to the corresponding LBP intensity or RMDQ scores. Conversely, higher fear-avoidance behaviour questionnaire (FABQ) work scores and higher Insomnia Severity Index (ISI) scores together explained 24% of LBP intensity variance, while FABQ-total scores explained 34% of RMDQ scores in people with CLBP (Research Output#1). For Objective#2 Repeated MRI scans, ultrasonography, and shear wave elastography at the 2-year follow-up showed that people with CLBP had significantly more severe IVD degeneration at L4/5 and L5/S1 levels, more facet trophism at the L5/S1 level than asymptomatic controls. Only baseline FABQ-work scores in people with CLBP predicted 19% of LBP intensity variance at the follow-up. Likewise, higher baseline Pain Catastrophizing Scale-helplessness scores and greater ISI scores together explained 38.4% of RMDQ scores at the follow-up. For objective#3 There were no significant temporal changes in all LM or phenotype parameters in participants with and without CLBP at their follow-up. Therefore, no correlation was found between temporal changes in LM characteristics and the corresponding changes in LBP intensity or RMDQ scores. We also conducted a systematic review to evaluate whether temporal changes in LM characteristics following motor control exercises (the most common treatment for LBP) were related to the corresponding changes in LBP intensity or LBP-related disability. We found low-quality evidence that there was no significant correlation between post-exercise changes in LM morphometry and the corresponding LBP intensity/LBP-related disability (Research Output#2).

25101817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25101817.value: This is the first study to use multiple advanced technologies to comprehensively investigate the roles of various lumbar multifidus (LM) characteristics in predicting the current and future chronic low back pain (CLBP) symptoms/disability after considering lumbar phenotypes (e.g., intervertebral disc and/or facet degeneration) and various demographic and psychological factors. Our findings did not support the hypothesis that decreased lean muscle sizes in LM was related to CLBP intensity or LBP-related disability, although people with CLBP had more fatty infiltration in LM than healthy controls. Interestingly, LM size and fatty infiltration percentage in people with and without CLBP did not change over time. This indicates that other factors (e.g., genes) may predetermine the percentage of fat in LM, which may imply that some people are more likely to experience CLBP than others. Future studies should investigate the genetic contribution to the morphometry of paraspinal muscles. Importantly, future large-scale studies should validate our findings. Given the significant role of baseline sleep quantity/quality and some psychological factors in predicting LBP intensity and disability in people with CLBP, future studies should determine the effectiveness of various treatments for sleep, fear avoidance belief, and pain catastrophizing in managing clinical outcomes of people with CLBP.

25101817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25101817.value: Low back pain (LBP) is a common debilitating musculoskeletal condition. Recent studies suggested that people with chronic LBP were characterized by changes in sizes and/or position sense of deep back muscle (lumbar multifidus, LM) and more degenerated intervertebral discs. However, no studies had determined whether baseline LM characteristics (e.g., volume, stiffness, and/or position sense) in people with and without chronic LBP were related to the current or future clinical outcomes (LBP intensity or LBP-related disability). The current study found that after considering insomnia, pain catastrophizing, and fear avoidance belief in people with and without chronic LBP, LM characteristics (i.e., volume, stiffness, amount of intramuscular fat tissues, and position sense) and disc degeneration were unrelated to their LBP intensity or LBP-related disability at baseline and the 2-year follow-up. Likewise, temporal changes in LM characteristics over two years were unrelated to the corresponding changes in LBP intensity or LBP-related disability. Conversely, the presence of insomnia, fear avoidance belief, and/or pain catastrophizing were related to baseline LBP intensity or LBP-related disability. The presence of insomnia and fear avoidance belief at baseline predicted high LBP intensity two years later. Likewise, insomnia and perceived helplessness at baseline predicted more LBP-related disability at the 2-year follow-up.

25104017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25104017.value: Accidental damage of peripheral nerves during surgery is a leading cause of critical patient morbidity such as sensory loss, chronic pain or permanent paralysis. Nerves are usually identified by their appearance and anatomical location, however, sometimes overlooked due to similarity of shape and color to non-nerve tissues. Electromyography using local electrical stimulation has been the only available technique to detect nerves in current operating room, which cannot provide any visual guidance. Non-linear and tomographic methods have shown potential for in vivo nerve imaging, these technologies require complex and expensive instrumentation and time-consuming processing which is practically challenging for surgical use. Fluorescence imaging with exogenously injected probes has attracted increasing interest in recent years. However, as yet none of nerve-specific peptides or fluorophores is approved for clinical use due to concern of toxicity. Devastating complications by intraoperative nerve injury and significant weakness of current nerve detection techniques highlight the urgent need for new development of specific nerve visualization method in surgical setting. In this project, we aim to develop a novel label-free imaging system using a polarization sensitive spectral reflectance imaging technique for the optimized intraoperative nerve detection without any concern of toxicity. Our idea to specifically visualize peripheral nerves is that to utilize their intrinsic optical properties, i.e., 1) wavelength-dependent reflectance based on thin film interference phenomenon induced from myelin structure of nerve fibers and 2) polarization sensitive contrast due to birefringence induced from regular arrangement of lipids and proteins in nerve fibers. We have identified strong candidates for specific nerve reflectance in near-infrared wavelength region. Based on such compelling evidence, we will first investigate optical characteristics of peripheral nerves in terms of reflectance, absorption, transmission, and polarization using our custom-built spectroscopy. Then, a polarization sensitive spectral reflectance imaging setup to provide concurrent color anatomy and nerve highlighting images in real-time will be constructed using easy-to-implement optics with multiple-bandpass filter and polarizer. Finally, we will showcase the imaging performance metrics of the developed system using phantoms, tissues, and normal and cancer mouse models. To this end, we provide, for the first time, a powerful navigation tool highlighting the exact location of peripheral nerves with high specificity and no toxicity to guide surgeons, which allows complete preservation of nerve structures. A new cutting edge technique developed and its successful demonstration can potentially cause a paradigm shift in surgical treatment, facilitating minimally invasive surgery and personalized medicine to improve overall patient outcome. 手術中意外造成的周邊神經損傷是引起包含知覺喪失、慢性疼痛甚或永久癱瘓等術後病症的主因之一。神經通常能夠直接以肉眼或是相關解剖構造辨識，然而，有時仍因形狀或顏色與非神經組織太過相似而導致誤判。利用局部電刺激的肌電圖是當前臨床唯一有效能於術中偵測神經的技術，但無法提供視覺上的指引。非線性斷層技術具備活體內神經造影的潛力，但複雜且昂貴的儀器與耗時的後處理令此技術難以應用於手術中。近來注射螢光探針的造影技術備受矚目，考量到潛在的毒性，目前仍缺少具備神經特異性的多肽或是螢光質素。術中神經損傷造成的併發症加上現時明顯不足的偵測技術闡明了開發具備神經特異性的術中成像技術著實刻不容緩。 本研究中，我們計畫應用偏振敏感光譜反射技術(polarization sensitive spectral reflectance)開發一項適合手術中使用、無毒且無需標誌的新式神經顯影工具。我們之所以能將周邊神經專一地顯示出來，其概念建立於神經組織特殊的光學特性，例如 1) 由包裹神經纖維的外圍髓鞘組織所產生的薄膜干涉現象誘發特定的反射波長以及 2) 由神經纖維中脂質與蛋白質正常分佈產生雙折射造成的特殊偏振敏感對比等。我們已經在近紅外光的波段找到數個可能具專一性的神經反射頻譜。首先，我們將使用自行設置的光譜儀探討周邊神經的反射、吸收、傳導及偏振效應等光學特性。緊接著，我們將利用簡易光學構造搭配多通濾波器及偏光片等配件組合成一個可經偏振敏感光譜反射成像技術提供即時彩色解剖資訊及強化神經影像的裝置。最後，我們將在假體、組織、正常以及癌症動物模式中展示我們系統開發的造影成果。 總結來說，我們首屈一指地建構了一項有力的導引工具能夠在高專一性且無毒的前提下準確地為外科醫師標定周邊神經的位置，藉此使得周邊神經於手術中得以保全完好。這樣劃時代科技的研發與成功的展示能夠為手術治療開啟新頁；結合最小化的侵入性治療與個人化醫學以增進醫療成效。

25104017.label: Realisation of objectives
25104017.value: Objective 1. Investigation of novel optical characteristics of peripheral nerve using spectroscopic analysis: reflectance, absorption, transmission, polarization The objective 1 was 100% achieved through 1) spectroscopic analysis and measurement of reflectance, absorption, and transmission using custom-built spectroscopy setup with integrating sphere and 2) ex vivo spectral reflectance test using spectral imaging with two photon microscope. Based on strong wavelength-specific reflectance from myelin sheaths surrounding nerve fiber by thin film interference phenomenon, we hypothesized myelin induced reflectance imaging can be useful to specifically visualize peripheral nerves during surgery without any exogenous label or other invasive procedures. Spectroscopic analysis showed unique optical properties of peripheral nerves, in particular strong reflectance in the range of 410-540 nm. With this candidate, spectral imaging was performed with isolated nerve and non-nerve tissues using two photon microscope equipped with tunable laser and reflectance detection filters (Nikon A1R MP+) in 820-1080 nm wavelength regions for illumination which are corresponding to single photon illumination of 410-540 nm. Two photon imaging was used to check deep tissue information. The detected patterns highlight several peripheral nerves with myelin showing strong reflectance at 820-900 nm over other non-nerve tissues including muscle, fat, and vein. This finding provided a basis for developing a novel label-free intraoperative imaging technique for specific visualization of nerves. Objective 2. Design and construction of polarization sensitive spectral reflectance imaging system to specifically detect peripheral nerves The objective 2, development of sensitive spectral reflectance imaging technique to specifically image peripheral nerves was 100% achieved. However, this was not achieved using combination of spectral reflectance and polarization property. Instead, this aim was achieved using combination of spectral reflectance and deep learning approach. Originally, polarization property was expected to differentiate nerve and tendon. However, polarization at different angles showed differentiation ability of polarization imaging was not good enough. Utilization of polarization rather decreased overall signal intensity. Nerve to tendon ratio was recorded as 0.51 under in vivo condition which is insufficient for clear distinction between nerve and tendon. To solve this problem, we decided to apply deep learning technology for automatic segmentation of peripheral nerves especially compared to tendon. Therefore, we developed a multi-tasks artificial intelligence-based visualization system (MTAIVS) consisting of two deep learning models (DenseNET201 and DoubleU-Net) with transfer learning approach for serial multi-tasks of nerve classification and segmentation with reflectance images. The successfully constructed deep learning algorithm, MTAIVS showed outstanding recognition for the images containing nerves achieving Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.9654 and successful delineation of nerve location from all other non-nerve tissues with Intersection-Over-Union (IoU) of 0.8056. Moreover, our MTAIVS shows real-time guidance performance with process video frame rate of 14.7 fps. Our MTAIVS consistently outperformed other start-of-the-art deep learning models (4 for classification and 5 for segmentation) in highlighting peripheral nerves with pseudo-color in real-time during complicated surgical procedures in murine cancer models. In conclusion, we achieved the objective 2 successfully by the alternative but powerful method, deep learning. Objective 3. Intraoperative imaging of peripheral nerves in normal mice using the developed imaging system and comparison with conventional fluorescence imaging techniques The objective 3 was achieved 100% by comparison study of the developed nerve reflectance imaging with conventional fluorescent nerve staining dye, fluoromyelin. Fluoromyelin based nerve imaging has intrinsic limitation because it requires exogeneous injection of fluorescent agent which gives concern on toxicity if it goes for clinical application. However, we performed comparative study to prove better imaging performance of the developed technique to detect peripheral nerves over fluoromyelin based in vivo staining. As a result, reflectance imaging showed higher contrast than fluorescent imaging with fluoromyelin under heterogenous in vivo condition, 1.83~2.6 nerve to background tissue ratio. Excellent nerve-to-muscle contrast was shown using spectral reflectance technique (contrast value of 5.1 at 850nm) compared to conventional nerve staining dye, fluoromyelin (contrast value of 1.9 at 850nm). This result indicated our developed imaging technique could potentially replace conventional fluorescence imaging technique for nerve identification even in preclinical animal imaging studies. Objective 4. Demonstration of intraoperative imaging performance of the developed imaging system to selectively identify peripheral nerves around tumor tissues during murine cancer surgery The objective 4 was 100% achieved using various rigorous studies to demonstrate and evaluate the developed imaging system for intraoperative visualization of peripheral nerves in murine models. First, evaluation of intraoperative imaging performance of our developed technique was performed using various cancer models using a modified two photon intravital imaging setup. Breast cancer model and myelogenous leukemia model were generated using subcutaneous injection of 4T1-GFP breast cancer cells and K562-GFP leukemia cells. Two photon intravital imaging using 890-960nm illumination depicted high accuracy and sensitivity of the developed technique in both cancer models. Notably, this imaging showcase demonstrated significantly higher nerve-to-muscle contrast in specific wavelength regions in cancer models compared to normal mice. Imaging in breast cancer model depicted contrast value of 4.99 at 900nm and 7.04 at 960nm whereas normal model imaging showed 1.84 at 900nm and 2.26 at 960nm. Similar signal boost was also observed in leukemia model, i.e., nerve-to-muscle ratio of 3.26-4.00 in leukemia model and 1.38-2.60 in normal model at 850-950nm. These results implicate structural change of nerves by interaction with cancer cells resulting in enhanced myelin-induced reflectance signal which provides high potential for clinical translation of our developed nerve identification technique in real cancer surgery. Spurred by two photon based spectral reflectance imaging results in cancer models, we then modified the conventional surgical microscope with specific reflectance detection filter setting for 440-460nm to perform a more realistic large field of view imaging. It shows excellent imaging performance to highlight peripheral nerves with nerve-to-muscle ratio of 2.72. However, it also shows relatively high tendon-to-muscle ratio, 2.76. Tendon also has similar layered structure with nerve which is likely to be the source of reflectance signal. Therefore, we applied deep learning strategy to solve this problem by real-time pseudo highlighting of peripheral nerves over tendon or other non-nerve tissues. To achieve this goal, a deep learning algorithm was developed as described in the section for objective 2. Then, surgical reflectance imaging video was used for manual annotation by experienced researchers to provide ground truth images of nerve locations. Then, training of the network was conducted particularly focusing on tendon images which is the major counterpart of nerve. As a result, we could achieve state-of-art imaging performance with the developed MTAIVS, i.e., AUC of 0.9654, Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of 0.8312, and accuracy of 91.29% for classification and AUC of 0.9589, MCC of 0.8105, and accuracy of 90.07%. Overall, we successfully completed the project to develop a novel imaging system to delineate accurate location of peripheral nerves during cancer surgery. Our novel technique presents high potential for clinical translation as a powerful navigation tool pinpointing the exact location of peripheral nerves with high specificity and no toxicity to guide surgeons, which could significantly reduce complications and morbidity associated with intraoperative nerve damage. It is noteworthy that we applied powerful cutting-edge deep learning technologies to circumvent the problem of similar in vivo contrast between nerve and tendon. Strong reflectance signal enhancement of nerves in cancer environment is also extremely interesting indicating that the developed technique may serve as a promising clinical tool for cancer surgery guidance to achieve minimally invasive surgery.
