25104017.label: Major findings and research outcome
25104017.value: We developed a novel intraoperative imaging technique to visualize peripheral nerves during cancer surgery using specific nerve reflectance and deep learning. First, we provided comprehensive investigation on specific nerve reflectance property. Through spectral imaging analysis using two-photon microscope, we found that two-photon illumination wavelength at 900nm (single-photon illumination wavelength at 450nm) shows superior nerve to background tissue ratio, nerve to muscle ratio of 3.28 and nerve to adipose ratio of 2.23. Moreover, reflectance imaging showed higher contrast than conventional fluorescent imaging with fluoromyelin under heterogenous in vivo condition, 1.83~2.6 nerve to background tissue ratio. In vivo imaging in 4T1 breast cancer model depicted contrast value of 3.2 at 900nm whereas normal model imaging showed 2.0 at 900nm. Intrigued by spectral reflectance measurement results on peripheral nerves, we demonstrated a large field of view surgical imaging capability by modification of the conventional surgical microscope with specific reflectance detection filter setting for 440-460nm. Surgical reflectance imaging was successfully performed in multiple murine cancer models including 4T1 breast cancer and K562 myelogenous leukemia. However, it was not easy to differentiate nerve from tendon, i.e., nerve to tendon ratio of 0.51. To address this challenge, we developed a multi-tasks artificial intelligence-based visualization system (MTAIVS) consisting of two deep learning models (DenseNET201 and DoubleU-Net) with transfer learning approach for serial multi-tasks of nerve classification and segmentation with reflectance images. Our MTAIVS consistently outperformed other start-of-the-art deep learning models in highlighting peripheral nerves with pseudo-color in real-time during complicated surgical procedures in murine cancer models. With all these valuable findings and highly translational technology developments, we successfully submitted US provisional patent application (No. 63/265, 158) which indicates high potential to generate intellectual property rights in near future. We also presented our research in many renowned international conferences including World Molecular Imaging Congress 2020, Focus on Microscopy 2022, etc. One PhD was successfully registered through this project and he also awarded a Certificate of Excellence for outstanding standard of oral presentation with his presentation on this research in the 2018 International Symposium on NanoBiotechnology, Biosensors and Biochips. Recently, we submitted the manuscript with our research to the journal “Science Advances” which is under revision now. Although journal paper publication was a bit late because securing patent was more important, we strongly believe the paper will be published soon with high impact to the field of intraoperative imaging research.

25104017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25104017.value: The presented research has high translational value to apply for intraoperative imaging of peripheral nerves during cancer surgery. We will further test its capability to visualize human peripheral nerves. Since the developed technique is based on label-free reflectance imaging technology, there is less hurdle to go into clinical studies. Whereas fluorescent imaging with exogenous agent should go thorough strict verification processes similar to new drug development, our technique can be used in the clinics directly if we keep maximum light intensity limit set by regulation body. Therefore, next step will be clinical application using the developed technique by modification of currently available surgical imaging modalities such as Zeiss Blue 400. For this purpose, we will further optimize deep learning efficacy for automatic segmentation of nerves in real-time to avoid any miss of nerves in real clinical human surgery. At the same time, we will find clinical collaborator and move into clinical trial study. Patent application in various countries is also essential to maximize benefits of this development. Eventually, we hope this technique helps surgeons to avoid any accidental damage to nerves thus improve patients’ overall outcome.

25104017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25104017.value: Surgery is a cornerstone for current medical treatment in various diseases. Nerve injury could cause one of the most common and feared postoperative complications including chronic neuropathies and more severe ability loss. Heterogenous disease tissue environment and fine size of peripheral nerves make nerve delineation challenging even for experienced surgeons which can cause accidental nerve trauma. Electromyography has been a gold standard technique to identify peripheral nerves. Ultrasonography, photoacoustic tomography, fluorescence imaging, optical coherence tomography, and confocal endomicroscopy have been also used for intraoperative imaging of peripheral nerves. Unfortunately, none of them could provide reliable technique to identify peripheral nerves in the current operating room due to lack of specificity and contrast, limited field of view, and safety issue. In this study, we developed a novel label-free surgical imaging technique to provide specific and safe intraoperative visualization of peripheral nerves in real-time using spectral reflectance and deep neural networks. Our novel technique presents high potential for clinical translation as a powerful navigation tool pinpointing the exact location of peripheral nerves with high specificity and no toxicity to guide surgeons, which could significantly reduce complications and morbidity associated with intraoperative nerve damage. This technique will eventually revolutionize modern surgery.

25203717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25203717.value: Although professional drivers constitute only a small proportion of overall driver population, their exposures on roads are remarkably higher than that of general drivers. Indeed, crash involvement rates of professional drivers, in particular taxis, minibuses and buses, are higher than that of general drivers. Besides, the consequences of crashes involving professional drivers are often fatality and severe injury of other innocent road users. Fatigue, reduced vigilance and aggressive driving behavior are important risk factors for crash involvement of professional drivers. In Hong Kong, a driving improvement course was introduced to enhance safety awareness of and promote safe driving to problematic driver groups in 2002, and mandatory attendance at this course for severe traffic offenders was empowered in 2009. Recently, a pre-service course targeting passenger vehicle drivers was introduced. It is of paramount importance to evaluate the effectiveness of various legislation, enforcement and training programs in enhancing the safety of professional drivers. Perception, attitude, and behavior are different between professional and general drivers because of the variation in skills and experiences, and also the influences of operation characteristics and management practices (including work hour, delivery schedule, dispatch policies and work compensation methods). In this project, we aim to reveal the fundamental relationship between explanatory factors and crash risk of professional drivers from the empirical, physiological and perceptional perspectives. From an empirical perspective, the effects of road environment, traffic and driver characteristics on the safety of professional drivers, controlling for the effect of exposure, will be examined using integrated traffic, crash and injury data. From the physiological perspective, the relationship between personal factors, fatigue and degradation of driving performance will be revealed using a driving simulator experiment. Furthermore, perception and attitudes towards the enforcement and penalty measures deterring risky driving behavior, taking into account the effects of personal and operation characteristics, will be evaluated using a questionnaire survey. From this evidence, effective operation, health and safety management, and regulatory measures can be developed for the transport operators and authorities, and to reduce the crash and injury risk related to professional drivers in the long run. 雖然職業司機數目在整體司機數目中只佔一小部分，但職業司機在馬路上的時間相對一般司機明顯地高。尤其是，的士、小巴及巴士等職業司機的交通意外率較一般司機為高，這些交通意外，往往導致其他無辜道路使用者嚴重受傷或死亡。疲勞駕駛、集中力下降及不良的駕駛態度是導致涉及職業司機的交通意外的主要原因。在2002年，香港運輸署推行駕駛改進計劃，以加強司機的安全意識及推廣安全駕駛。由2009年起，運輸署更規定違反嚴重交通規例的司機須強制參加駕駛改進課程。由2015年起，公共小巴司機更須參加職前課程，以提升其駕駛態度及公共小巴的安全。因此，適時檢討及分析有關法例、執法及司機訓練的成效，對提升職業司機的安全非常重要。基於駕駛技巧、路面經驗、營運特徵及管理模式（如工作時間、行車時間、編更制度及薪金計算方法）的不同，職業司機與一般司機的意識、態度及行為有明顯差異。 是項研究的目的為，從觀察、生理及心理的角度，探討職業司機的交通意外風險與相關因素的基本關係。從觀察角度，我們會運用綜合交通流量、交通意外及傷亡的資料，考慮曝光率的影響，探討道路環境、交通狀況及司機特徵與涉及職業司機的交通意外的關係。從生理角度，我們會運用模擬駕駛實驗，分析個人特徵、疲勞駕駛、駕駛時間與駕駛表現下降的關係。從心理角度，我們會利用問卷調查方法，研究個人特徴、營運模式、安全意識、法例與職業司機對違反交通條例的態度的關係。總括而言，研究結果對將來制定職業司機的職業安全與健康管理方法，提供重要基礎，長遠有效減少涉及職業司機的交通意外。

25203717.label: Realisation of objectives
25203717.value: All project objectives have been achieved. Research outcomes are published in the top journals in related subject areas. Objective 1: This project has examined the effects of factors including road class, road geometry, network configuration, speed limit, adverse weather, visibility, vehicle class, and traffic composition on the occurrence and severity of crashes involving professional drivers using Bayesian approach, with which the space-time variation of exposure is accounted [J3, J6, J7, J9, J10 and J11 in Part C]. Non-linear and lag effects of weather condition on the relationship between crash, time and distance exposure, and other influencing factors are also considered, using high-resolution meteorological data (e.g., rainfall, wind speed and direction) in short time interval and of small geographical scale [J4 in Part C]. On the other hand, surrogate safety measures including time-to-collision that consider vehicle weight are proposed to model the space-time propagation of potential crash risk involving heavy trucks along the motorway [J13 in Part C]. Furthermore, advanced econometric models including Bayesian generalized ordered model, Bayesian Tobit model, and correlated grouped random parameters logit model are proposed to compensate for the bias attributed to unobserved heterogeneity, panel data, and spatial correlation in the crash analysis [J9, J10 and J14 in Part C]. Furthermore, an iterative aggregation approach is proposed to address the boundary crash problem in the spatial analysis [J1 in Part C]. Last but not least, resampling and deep generative approaches are proposed to address the excessive zero observation problem in the disaggregated analysis of crashes involving buses and trucks [J11 and J12 in Part C]. Objective 2: This project has examined the effects of road environment, weather condition, traffic flow, driver age, and driving time on the safety performance of professional drivers, using high-fidelity driving simulator system [J2, J6 and J7 in Part C]. In addition, effects of cognitive distraction by radio system and visual-manual distraction by mobile application on the behaviours of taxi drivers for the use of in-vehicle ride-hailing system are also investigated [J15 in Part C]. Metrics including mean and standard deviation of speed, steering control, lateral control, and time-to-collision are proposed to indicate the performances of professional drivers [J2 in Part C]. In addition, time-exposed and time-integrated time-to-collision are adopted to account for the time duration and severity of traffic conflicts in safety analysis [J7 and J8 in Part C]. Furthermore, metrics including brake reaction time, maximum acceptable speed, and normalized heart rate are adopted to evaluate the physiological performance of professional drivers [J6 and J8 in Part C]. Findings of this project suggest that professional drivers are more capable of mitigating the potential crash risk by adopting the compensatory strategy, even that the physiological and cognitive performances of older drivers may deteriorate with age [J8 in Part C]. Objective 3: This project has employed a stated preference approach to evaluate the deterrent effect of penalty and enforcement strategies on the tendency to violate traffic rules of professional drivers [J5 in Part C]. For example, effects of monetary fines, driving-offence point, presence of warning sign, operation characteristics (e.g., salary system, driving hour, work time, vehicle type), and driver characteristics (e.g., gender, age, driving violation record, and safety perception) on the tendency are considered [J5 in Part C]. In addition, effects of traffic operation, traffic management, and enforcement strategy on the safe car-following behaviours of drivers in term of time and distance headways under different weather and traffic flow conditions are also considered [J7 and J9 in Part C]. Furthermore, space-time varying heterogeneities are also accounted when modelling the effects of operation characteristics (i.e., distributions of truck volume, vehicle weight, and speed) on the safety risk [J10 and J13 in Part C].

25203717.label: Major findings and research outcome
25203717.value: This research finds that there are significant interactions between road geometry parameters (e.g., horizontal curve, vertical grade, and road width) and weather condition (e.g., rainfall, wind speed, and fog) on the risk of crashes involving professional drivers, after controlling the time and distance exposure, random effect, and space-time correlation [J3, J4, J6 and J7 in Part C]. In addition, time variation in traffic composition, particularly proportion of goods vehicle in the traffic stream, can intervene with the association between crash risk, road geometry, weather condition, and other influencing factors [J10 and J11 in Part C]. Furthermore, prevalent modelling issues including unobserved heterogeneity, spatial correlation, and imbalanced crash data are also addressed using advanced econometric models [J1, J11, J12, and J14 in Part C]. Considering the physiological performance and driving behaviour, this research finds that driver age and driving time can affect the safety performance of professional drivers using the metrics like heart rate, reaction time, steering control, and speed control [J2 and J6 in Part C]. In addition, compensatory strategy of professional drivers can mitigate the potential crash risk attributed to age, driving time, and driver distraction [J8 and J15 in Part C]. On the other hand, novel safety metrics like time-exposed and time integrated time-to-collision, with which the effect of vehicle weight is accounted, are proposed to assess the safety of professional drivers [J7 and J8 in Part C]. Last but not least, this research finds that effective legislation and enforcement strategies can deter against traffic violation offenses of professional drivers. Also, it is necessary to account for the driver (e.g., gender, age, and driving experience) and operational characteristics (e.g., salary system, driver training, and traffic management) for the optimal policy and management measures that can enhance the overall safety of professional drivers [J5 in Part C].

25203717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25203717.value: Future research could be focused on the calibration of crash frequency models, addressing the issues like heteroscedasticity, endogeneity, temporal correlation, and missing data. When comprehensive traffic and safety data are available, econometric models calibrated in this research could give robust estimation for the effects of environment, traffic, and human factors on the crash risk of professional drivers. Another direction of research will focus on hierarchical paradigm for the data synthesis process. This is crucial for multi-objective optimization of engineering design, transport management, and policy strategy that can promote the safe driving behaviours of professional drivers, when more contextual characteristics are considered. Lastly, future research could be extended to actual field experimental design and field observations. Hence, studies based on the real time microscopic traffic and behavioural characteristics using advanced image processing algorithm can enhance the credibility of the relationship estimated.

25203717.value: This project has developed advanced driving simulator experiment to examine the effects of road environment, traffic volume, driver age, and driving time on the behaviour and safety of professional drivers. This research shows that professional drivers are capable of compensating the accident risk related to age, driving time, and adverse weather conditions, by adaptive driving behaviours. On the other hand, this project has applied a choice experiment to evaluate the perception and attitudes of professional drivers towards existing and hypothetical enforcement and penalty against traffic violation offenses. Findings can shed light on the development and implementation of optimal driver education, legislation, and policy strategies that can promote safe driving of professional drivers. Furthermore, this project has adopted more efficient algorithm to tackle the complex mathematical problem of accident analysis. The proposed econometric models can accurately estimate the effects of road design, weather, traffic flow, and driver characteristics on the accident risk of professional drivers, even with incomplete and missing data.

25203917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25203917.value: To essentially provide the solution to emission reduction, large-scale wind energy is developed and utilized in an environmentally friendly manner and plays an indispensable role in the sustainable development of society, which has been supported by most countries and organizations in the world (e.g., Paris Agreement). However, with the integration of wind generation, the dynamics of modern power systems becomes quite different from that of traditional power systems. Power system angular stability, as one of the critical aspect of power system dynamics, could be significantly impacted by the increasing penetration level of wind generation, and hence should be carefully examined. Full converter based wind power generation (FCWG, i.e., direct driven wind generation), as a comparatively novel wind technology, is very promising to replace other types of wind generation (such as Doubly-Fed Induction Generator (DFIG)) in future market owing to rapid development of power electronics. Although quite many efforts have been devoted to impact studies of wind power grid connection by researchers including the PI, however, they are mostly on non-converter connected wind power technologies like DFIG. The project aims to systematically investigate the grid integration of FCWG, which has a different electromechanical transient characteristic (or inertia response) due to the special full-scale converter structure and thus significantly changes its mechanism in influencing system dynamic angular stability. This has also posed a crucial challenge that traditional mechanism analysis of dynamic angular stability might not be suitable for the study of FCWG. Aa a result, two main scientific questions have been raised from above accordingly: 1. What is the proper way to assess the impact mechanism of FCWG on system dynamic angular stability? 2. How does FCWG actually interact with conventional generators and affect system dynamic angular stability? Therefore, the project will essentially tackle these scientific questions by exploring how the dynamics of FCWG changes the distribution of system inertia sources and thus affects angular stability margin. A completely new assessment method as well as damping margin index will be developed to analyze power system dynamic angular stability from the aspect of network inertia distributions for the first time, so as to fill the theoretical gap in this field of existing angular stability analysis. All the theoretical findings of project will be tested and validated with a range of real power system data and useful advice provided by the project will undoubtedly bring significant benefits to power system operators and planning worldwide. 以環保的方式開發和利用大規模風能可從本質上解決節能減排問題，並在建設可持續發展社會中發揮著必不可少的作用，現已受到世界上大多數國家和組織（如巴黎協定）的支持。然而，風力發電的接入大大改變了現代電力系統的動態特性。作為電力系統動態的壹個重要方面，電力系統功角穩定性會隨著風能穿越水平的提升而受到顯著影響，因而需要細致研究。隨著電力電子技術的飛速發展，全功率型變流器風力發電（如直驅風力發電）作為壹項較為新穎的風力技術，在未來市場中極有可能取代其他類型的風力發電技術（如雙饋風力發電）。盡管包括課題負責人在內的學者們對風能聯網的影響進行了大力研究，但是其主要研究對象是如雙饋之類的非全功率型變流器風力聯網技術。本課題旨在系統地研究全功率型變流器風力發電的聯網技術，此類風電因其特殊的變流器結構從而具有不同的電磁暫態特性（或慣性響應特性），故而顯著地改變了其影響系統動態角穩定性的機理。這也使得傳統的動態功角穩定性機理分析面臨嚴峻的挑戰，可能不再適用於對於此類風電的研究。因此基於上述情況提出了2個主要的學術問題：1.評估全功率型變流器風力發電對系統動態角穩定性的影響機理的適用方法是什麽？2.全功率型變流器風電機組是如何與傳統發電機組相互作用並影響系統動態功角穩定性的？所以本課題將系統研究全功率型變流器風電動態特性如何改變系統慣性源分布進而影響角穩定性裕度，從而根本上解決上述科學問題。本課題將采用壹項全新的評估方法和阻尼裕度指標，首次從網絡慣性分布方面來分析系統功角角穩定性，以填補現有功角穩定分析方法的在理論方面的不足。本課題將采用大量的實際電力系統數據對所有理論成果進行測試和論證，相信所給予的理論指導將無疑會使世界範圍內的電力系統運行和規劃受益。

25203917.label: Realisation of objectives
25203917.value: The original project objectives have been revised after the project is granted based on the actual given funding and resources as well as the comments from the reviewers. To date, all the revised objectives of the project have been achieved. Part of the original objective 4 has also been achieved. The details are provided as follows. Revised objective 1: General method to assess the impact of conventional SG distribution (size and network topology) on power system dynamic angular stability; and development of a damping margin index to provide an effective measure for the impact of system inertia distribution on angular stability A general method to analyze the impact of the conventional synchronous generator (SG) as well as full converter-based wind power generation (FCWG) on power system dynamic angular stability has been proposed based on an intentionally designed two-open-loop-subsystem dynamic model and bilateral damping torque analysis (BDTA). Then a damping margin index namely the resonance excitation index (REI) according to a per-unit open-loop modal distance indicating the intensity of modal interactions is proposed and employed together with the shift of critical eigenvalues to provide an effective measure for the impact analysis of SG and FCWG on system angular stability. Modal analysis in the frequency domain and time domain simulation are also used to validate the proposed method and index. For more details, please refer to Journal Paper 3, and Conference Paper 1 in Part C. Revised objective 2: The modeling of electromechanical transient characteristic (quasi inertia) of FCWG & virtual controllers and their impact on system inertia profile The electromechanical transient (quasi inertia) models of both FCWG and the potential virtual damping controllers including wind turbine side controller, DC capacitor side controller and Phase-locked loop (PLL) side controller are derived and their impact on the power system dynamics especially the oscillatory dynamics are analyzed and compared. For more details, please refer to Journal Paper 6, and Conference Paper 1 and 3 in Part C. Revised objective 3: The impact mechanism of FCWG together with virtual controllers on dynamic angular stability; and validation of theoretical findings in a real power system The impact mechanism of FCWG together with virtual controllers on system dynamic angular stability has been extensively investigated in this project. Almost all the journal papers are directly or indirectly addressing this important key issue. In order to have an in-depth and comprehensive understanding on the impact mechanism of FCWG, the impact mechanism of fixed-speed and variable-speed induction generator-based wind power generation is firstly studied and systematically compared. Then a novel modal superposition theory is proposed to classify the modal interactions between FCWG oscillation mode (FOM) and SG electromechanical oscillation mode (EOM) in the complex plane. The modal coupling mechanism is graphically visualized to investigate the dynamic interactions. A modal shift evaluation (MSE) method by using BDTA is proposed to accurately quantify the interaction effect of FOMs and EOMs on each other and effectively explain their complex interaction mechanism. Then the modal shift sensitivity (MSS) with respect to various PMSG controller parameters is derived to dig the essential modal resonance mechanisms according to the defined REI. The participation of FCWG in electromechanical dynamics is also extensively investigated, and particularly, an unusual transition of the electromechanical oscillation mode (EOM) is uncovered. Two new mode identification criteria, i.e., FCWG dynamics correlation ratio (FDCR) and quasi-electromechanical loop correlation ratio (QELCR) are proposed to quantify the FCWG participation in electromechanical dynamics. On this basis, the impact of different wind penetration levels and controller parameter settings on the participation of FCWG is investigated. It is revealed that if an FOM has a similar oscillation frequency to the system EOMs, there is a high possibility to induce strong interactions between FCWG dynamics and system electromechanical dynamics of the external power systems. In this circumstance, an interesting phenomenon may occur that an EOM may be dominated by FCWG dynamics, and hence is transformed into a quasi-EOM, which actively involves the participation of FCWG quasi-electromechanical state variables. Besides the impact studies of FCWG, three possible options for virtual controller installation are identified based on some derivations of the conventional control model of FCWG. The damping support mechanism of three virtual controllers is revealed based on a suitable and generic configuration structure of the controller. The three virtual controllers are equipped to contribute to damping by utilizing the potential energy and dynamics hidden in different inertia source components (i.e., the wind turbine rotor and DC capacitor, respectively) of FCWG. The impact mechanisms of the three controllers in suppressing modal resonance and improving system oscillation stability are intensively compared with their potential practical applications indicated. The impact mechanism of a hybrid renewable energy source (HRES) system including FCWG and full converter-based photovoltaic generation on system dynamic angular stability and modal interaction is also examined. For more details, please refer to Journal Paper 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 in Part C. Part of original objective 4: Parameter tuning of FCWG together with virtual controllers in order to improve power system dynamic angular stability By using the proposed two tools, i.e., MSS and REI, a novel methodology for the optimal parameter tuning of FCWG and three virtual controllers to avoid the dynamic interactions between the FCWG and external power systems and maximize resonance mode damping is designed. The optimized dynamic interactions (i.e. modal counteraction) can significantly enhance the power system dynamic angular stability, the effectiveness of which is verified by both modal analysis and time domain simulations. For more details, please refer to Journal Paper 3, 4 and 6, and Conference Paper 2 and 4 in Part C.

25203917.label: Major findings and research outcome
25203917.value: The major findings and research outcome are summarized associated with the selected research outputs of the project. It is observed in the project that full converter-based wind power generation (FCWG) is generally “decoupled” from the grid, which has a very minor impact on power system dynamic angular stability in normal conditions. However, it is also found that strong dynamic interactions between FCWG and grid can be induced in some special conditions, which can incur severe system dynamic angular instability incidents. During the strong interaction, an unusual transition of the system electromechanical oscillation mode (EOM) to quasi-EOM dominated by FCWG dynamics is uncovered. Two new mode identification criteria, i.e., FCWG dynamics correlation ratio (FDCR) and quasi-electromechanical loop correlation ratio (QELCR) are proposed to characterize this unusual transition and quasi-EOM. It is revealed that if an FCWG oscillation mode (FOM) has a similar oscillation frequency to the system EOMs, there is a high possibility to induce strong interactions between FCWG dynamics and system electromechanical dynamics of the external power systems. (Associated with Journal Paper 5 in Part C) In order to accurately quantify this strong dynamic interaction and effectively provide an in-depth impact mechanism of FCWG on system dynamic angular stability, the project develops a modal shift evaluation (MSE) method by using the intentionally designed two-open-loop-subsystem dynamic model and proposed bilateral damping torque analysis (BDTA). The two proposed important concepts, i.e., modal shift sensitivity (MSS) and resonance excitation index (REI) can dig the essential interaction mechanisms. (Associated with Journal Paper 3 in Part C) In order to effectively prevent potential strong dynamic interactions and hence enhance system dynamic angular stability, the project adopts two options: 1) modal interaction optimization (MIO) through parameter tuning of FCWG; 2) installation of three virtual damping controllers on wind turbine, DC capacitor and phase-locked loop (PLL) side respectively. The two options have been compared and found to be both effective in the project. (Associated with Journal Paper 3, 4 and 6 in Part C) In order to have a clear understanding on the different types of dynamic interactions between FCWG and grid, the project then develops a novel modal superposition theory to classify the dynamic interactions (modal coupling) in the complex plane, and the classification is also graphically visualized. (Associated with Journal Paper 4 in Part C)

25203917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25203917.value: The methodology developed in this project will be packed into relevant software and implemented in the industry with its accuracy and efficiency validated for further commercialization. Then the theory and methodology proposed in the project can be applied to the impact mechanism investigation of other types of converter-based resources (sometimes called inverter-based resources), including PV generation, energy storage system, HVDC and FACTS. The focused stability area can be also extended to other types of oscillation/resonance issues (especially new converter-driven stability and resonance stability) such as the dynamic interactions between full converter-based wind power generation (FCWG) converter and HVDC converter. Hence, the internal oscillation/resonance problems with wind and PV farms can be investigated, with the aggregated dynamic model substituted by the precise individual models. The project team will carry out the above-mentioned research and development aiming for a general method to evaluate and improve the system stability margin and explain the impact mechanism of diverse inverter-based resources on the emerging stability issues of future power grids.

25203917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25203917.value: To limit global warming to 1.5 degrees compared to pre-industrial levels, the Carbon Neutrality target by 2050 has become a consensus among many countries and regions worldwide. It can be certainly foreseen that wind power generations will be continuously promoted by the electricity industry and finally account for a dominant proportion of future global power generations. This project aims to provide effective and economic solutions to power system security issues induced by high penetration of wind power generation, and essentially tackle the technical bottleneck of large-scale wind power integration and prevent the real-time curtailment of wind power generation. The outcome of the project has been very fruitful and of both substantial theoretical and practical values. The project has provided theoretical guidance and technical support to power system operators for the secure planning and operation of wind power generation. The theoretical method and findings of the project can also be extended to other relevant fields for future research.

25204017.value: 改善電能質量和效率的新能源智能並網技術

25204017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25204017.value: To replace the polluting and depleting traditional sources of energy, renewable energy generation has increased in recent years. Hong Kong power generators have installed their first wind and solar systems and plan to speed up the development of their clean energy generation. Without intelligent grid integration, these new energy sources can degrade power quality and affect the distribution network. For example, intermittent power output, due to solar or wind variation, can lead to grid voltage dips or spikes, which can affect utility grid stability. The research about intelligent grids, in which the new sources of energy share in a smart way their output with the existing energy sources according to the needs of the consumers, is still at the beginning at the world level. Despite some research efforts that have been made previously about distributed generations and the so-called microgrids, further development of grid integration is still under investigation. This proposal presents a pioneering research plan, putting thus our efforts in line with the most up-to-date researches in the world looking for solutions to such an important and challenging topic. The breakthrough idea of this proposal is to develop original control methods for a distribution network with integrated renewable energy sources. An innovative method of the DC-AC inverters using model predictive control will be developed for effective and reliable islanded operation and grid connection. An analytical model illustrating the relationship between the power flow and the grid voltage profile will be derived. A novel localized control for the grid voltage quality will be developed, in which the reactive power supplied by the grid-connected inverters is coordinated; these inverters are distributed near the consumers to avoid traditional centralized equipment and energy losses. The research will provide solutions to grid integration of renewable energy into the existing power system, and will address development of the technology and future prospects. The proposed methods will be verified using a laboratory scale prototype. Real-world generation and load data will be used and the results will be tested in simulation on an electrical distribution network. The confirmed theoretical findings and experimental results will be disseminated in international journals and conferences; the proposed research will have a direct impact in the Hong Kong economy, allowing for a better integration of renewable energy sources into the Hong Kong grid, assuring high power quality and maximizing energy efficiency. 隨著傳統能源的日益減少和污染加重，近年來新能源發電逐漸興起。香港電力公司已經安裝了風力和太陽能發電系統，並計劃加速清潔能源的開發利用。然而，沒有智能的並網技術，這些新能源會對現有的電網造成衝擊，影響電力負載的正常運行。例如，太陽能和風能的波動性輸出會導致電壓跌落或升高，影響電網穩定性。當今全球對於新能源並網發電和智能電網的研究還處於初級階段，當中應用到的技術還需要深入開發和完善。鑒於這個發展契機和技術缺口，我們將會致力於尋找有效的解決方案，開發先進的分布式發電系統電網集成技術。首先，本項目將會開發一個基於模型預測控制算法的新型DC-AC逆變器控制技術，以實現有效可靠的孤島和並網運行。其次，我們將會推導能量流動和電壓波動之間的內部機理。然後在此基礎上開發一個分布式的電網電壓調節策略。每個新能源並網逆變器將會在用戶則協調地為電網注入無功功率，從節省了傳統大型而昂貴的集中式無功功率補償設備，減少能量損失。本項研究提出的方案將會在實驗室裡驗證，然後利用電網真實的發電和用電數據進一步測試。這項新技術將會促進新能源的開發利用，有效提高現有配電網絡的電能質量和電力輸送效率。

25206317.label: Project Title(Chinese)
25206317.value: 可審計的隱私保護認證:基於抗量子密碼的新方案

25206317.label: Project Objectives
25206317.value: To develop a modular design framework for accountable anonymous credentials. We plan to study systematically the design philosophy of existing constructions and the impact of quantum attacks on their security, privacy and accountability. We will decompose any anonymous credentials into a number of building blocks and formalize their requirements. The outcome is a unified security model and a design framework, which will be used to guide our study on various types of anonymous credentials (objectives 2-4), all of which do not have a quantum-safe version. To design reputation-based blacklistable anonymous credentials (BLAC-R) with reduced trust. All existing blacklistable anonymous credentials assume honesty of some authority for credential generation and blacklist management. We will investigate the possibility to replace them with a decentralized counterpart. As a stepping stone, a hybrid approach consisting of post-quantum and classical techniques will first be employed. Then we will investigate a post-quantum construction which involves designing new building blocks such as post-quantum universal accumulators. To design practical post-quantum accountable anonymous credentials. We plan to investigate methods to construct practical post-quantum accountable anonymous credentials. This involves improving the representation of a credential and the underlying zero-knowledge proof systems. We will also consider marking additional assumptions such as timely evaluation of whether an anonymous session should be blacklisted and non-colluding authorities. To design post-quantum anonymous credentials with TTP-Free de-anonymization. Some variants of anonymous credentials support TTP-free de-anonymization. Examples include k-times anonymous authentication and electronic cash. We propose to study constructions and proofing techniques for this kind of anonymous credentials in the post-quantum setting. To conduct security analysis and complexity analysis on the schemes from objective 2-4.

25206317.label: Realisation of objectives
25206317.value: We have achieved all objectives of the project. The details of the achievements of each objective are given below. For objective 1, we propose the systematically design of anonymous credentials via presenting the basic building blocks for the generic framework and the associated requirements for the blocks. Specifically, we find that the construction of anonymous credentials needs the help of the following sub-protocols, i.e., 1) a key generation algorithm, 2) a ticket generation algorithm, 3) a signature proof of knowledge protocol proving the passion of the secret key, 4) a signature proof of knowledge protocol proving the validity of a public key and a ticket and 5) a signature proof of knowledge protocol proving the fulfilment of a policy. Then, we give the generic construction of anonymous credential from the above five building blocks. The relevant research output is published on ACISP 2018. For objective 2, we present the first reputation-based blacklistable anonymous credential (BLAC-R) without the need of trusted third party. In particular, by the novel use of blockchain technique, which serves as a public append-only ledger to store the credentials and blacklists, no third party is needed to setup the system, generate the credential and manage the blacklist as it does in the traditional BLAC-R system. In addition, towards achieving the post-quantum construction of anonymous credential, we also explore the design of post-quantum safe building blocks for it. Specifically, we present the first construction of post-quantum universal accumulators. The relevant research outputs are published on ACISP 2018. We achieve objective 3 by presenting a new approach for constructing efficient zero-knowledge arguments of knowledge for a large class of lattice-based relations. Based on our argument systems, a series of common privacy-preserving primitives can be constructed in the standard lattice setting, including an anonymous credential, a group signature, a ring signature, an electronic cash system, and a range proof protocol. The relevant research output is published on Crypto 2019. We complete objective 4 by proposing the first construction of lattice-based blacklistable anonymous credential system, which is post-quantum safe. The relevant research output is given in a manuscript of the project members. We have conducted security analysis and complexity analysis for all above constructions of anonymous credential systems. Thus, objective 5 is achieved.

25206317.label: Major findings and research outcome
25206317.value: In the development of the project, we have many valuable findings. Firstly, starting from the existing schemes of anonymous credentials based on traditional number theoretical assumptions, we decompose the constructions into several basic building blocks, present a generic framework, and thus, simplify the construction of anonymous credential system into the constructions of the underlying building blocks. It is also of great significant in helping us present the first construction of decentralised reputation-based anonymous credentials without the need of trusted party as well as the construction of post-quantum anonymous credential. Secondly, zero-knowledge proof is an essential part in constructing anonymous credential, which is not only related with achieving the functionality of anonymous credential, but also an important factor to the efficiency of the anonymous credential. Based on our new zero-knowledge proof system, the constructions of post-quantum anonymous credentials with TTP-free deanonymization are one to three orders of magnitude more efficient than the state of the art (in standard lattice). The research outcomes of this project contain 12 conferences papers, including 2 Crypto papers and 3 ASIACRYPT papers, and 2 graduated PhD students from the Hong Kong Polytechnic University. Moreover, our work in post-quantum cryptography has led to the establishment of the Monash-PolyU-Collinstar Blockchain Research Joint-lab in 2018. This multi-million AUD project has produced a great impact to the community in both Hong Kong and overseas, attracted over 260 reports from major local newspaper including Ming Pao Daily News, Hong Kong Economic Times, Sing Tao Daily, Sky Post, Wen Wei Po and international media such as Washington Business Journal, New York Business Journal, Sohu.com, Eastmoney.com, etc.

25206317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25206317.value: Our research conducted during the project has potentials for further developments of theoretical research in the area of lattice-based cryptography as well as for the design of post-quantum safe cryptocurrency. Specifically, the construction of efficient lattice-based zero-knowledge proof is always a concern in this area. Our new method given in the project is helpful in inspiring other construction of efficient lattice-based zero-knowledge proofs. One possible method is reducing the proof size by utilising other suitable standard lattice assumptions. In addition, since anonymous credential system can provide authentication for the server while preserve the anonymity of users, it is also widely applied in constructing some decentralised cryptocurrency supporting accountability. In this case, our research of the project is useful to the construction of post-quantum cryptocurrency. Future works in this area include enhancing other basic component for cryptocurrency to be quantum safe and improving the efficiency of the post-quantum anonymous credential.

25206317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25206317.value: In this project, we simplify the construction of anonymous credential and present a generic framework for it. Based on that, we further enhance the functionality and security of traditional anonymous credentials. In terms of functionality, we present the first constructions of decentralised anonymous credential with reduced trust. In the aspect of security, we propose the constructions of post-quantum anonymous credentials by introducing some new techniques to the constructions of some post-quantum building blocks of anonymous credential. To summarise, the project is of great significance in providing accountable privacy-preserving authentications in the area of post-quantum cryptography. Furthermore, the completion of the project also has further impact on the research in the other area of cryptography like lattice-based cryptography and post-quantum cryptocurrency.

25209417.label: Project Title(Chinese)
25209417.value: 细胞力学特性调控肝细胞癌癌症干细胞的致瘤能力

25209417.label: Project Objectives
25209417.value: Demonstrate the critical roles of cell stiffness in the generation and growth of HCC CSCs. 3D soft fibrin method will be used to select tumorigenic CSCs from human HCC cells. To explore the effects of cell stiffness, HCC cells will be genetically modified to modulate cellular contractility and stiffness. The influence of stiffness modulation on CSC generation and growth will be determined. We expect that fibrin-selected HCC cells are tumorigenic and that increase (decrease) in cell stiffness may suppress (maintain and/or promote) CSC generation and growth. Unveil the indispensable and regulatory roles of cell stiffness in CSC’s tumorigenicity and elucidate the underlying mechanisms. The roles of CSC’s low stiffness in their high tumorigenicity will be determined. To elucidate the underlying mechanisms, mechanistic studies will be conducted to examine the influence of stiffness modulation on mechanotransduction and the key genes and signaling pathways related to self-renewal and proliferation. We hypothesize that low cell stiffness not only correlates with but also directly regulates CSC’s high tumorigenicity. (Optional) Develop a laboratory and lecture course module of stiffness regulated CSC’s tumorigenicity to enhance subject teaching and provide a training opportunity for undergraduate students to explore various fields in biomedical engineering. (see Education Plan for more details)

25209417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25209417.value: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), a primary type of liver cancer, ranks as the sixth most prevalent cancer and the second leading cause of cancer deaths in the world, where ~50% of all cases occur in China alone. It has become the fourth most common cancer and the third leading cause of cancer deaths in Hong Kong. HCC is organized as a hierarchy with cancer stem-like cells (CSCs) at the apex, a rare and tumorigenic subset of cancer cells with the ability to generate tumors and spread to distant organs. CSCs have thus been proposed to drive tumor progression and dissemination, posing serious challenges to the prognosis and treatment of HCC. Therefore, understanding the mechanisms underlying CSC’s malignancy is essential for developing effective therapeutic strategies. Considerable alterations in cell cytoskeleton and mechanics are associated with tumor progression. Compared to healthy cells, cancer cells exhibit lower stiffness that is correlated with malignancy and poor clinical outcomes. Tumorigenic CSCs are even softer than common cancer cells. However, it remains unclear whether cell mechanics contribute to tumor progression. This project, as an important part of the long-term research, will address whether low stiffness is necessary for CSC’s malignancy. This study aims to unveil the essential roles of cell stiffness in CSC generation and tumor formation ability. To this end, we will 1) genetically modulate cell stiffness and dissect its roles in CSC generation; 2) demonstrate the indispensability of low stiffness in CSC’s tumor formation ability and explore the underlying mechanisms. We expect that cell stiffness not only regulates CSC generation and growth but also directly dictates CSC’s malignancy. This project is potentially at the edge of a breakthrough that solves a critical and decades-old issue. Successful completion of the proposed research will, for the first time, unveil the necessity of low cell stiffness in CSCs, leading the evolution of cancer therapeutics into a new paradigm that targets cell mechanics. The indispensable roles of cell mechanics may identify cell stiffness as a mechanical marker for cancer diagnosis and as a therapeutic target for cancer treatment. This study will facilitate the development of novel strategies against cancer cell stiffness, which will benefit patients with liver cancer. The key findings will support the notion that cancer may be not only a genetic but also a ‘mechanical’ disease, which will extend and even transform our traditional views on cancer and considerably push the boundaries of cancer research. 肝细胞癌是肝癌中的一种主要类型，已经成为全世界范围内第六最流行的以及第二最致死的癌症，而且仅仅中国的肝癌病例就占全世界大约一半左右。在香港，肝癌是第四最普遍及第三最致命的癌症。肝细胞癌呈现层级结构，而且癌症干细胞位于层级的顶端，这种细胞是肿瘤中一小部分具有高致瘤能力的癌细胞，能够产生局部肿瘤以及扩散到远端器官形成转移肿瘤。所以研究已经提出癌症干细胞是驱使肿瘤发展和转移的关键因素，这给目前肝癌的预后和治疗提出了挑战。因此，理解癌症干细胞恶性的内在机制对开发有效的癌症治疗方法意义十分重大。 癌症发展中细胞骨架与力学特性发生显著变化。癌细胞的细胞硬度比正常细胞低，而低细胞硬度与肿瘤恶性及较差的临床结果相关。研究发现致瘤性强的癌症干细胞比普通癌细胞更软。然而，细胞力学性质变化能否促进肿瘤发展还不清楚。作为长期研究的一个重要组成部分，本项目着重阐释低细胞硬度是否是癌症干细胞保持恶性的必要条件。这项研究旨在揭示细胞硬度对癌症干细胞的产生及高致瘤能力的关键作用。为了达到这一目标，我们将采取以下手段：1）通过基因修饰调整肿瘤细胞硬度从而阐释其在癌症干细胞形成中的作用；2）揭示低细胞硬度在癌症干细胞高致瘤能力中的必要性，并进一步探索其潜在的调控机制。我们预想细胞硬度不仅能调控癌症干细胞的产生和生长，而且可以直接决定其恶性。 本项目将解决一个存在几十年的关键问题，并可能成为癌症研究领域的一项重大突破。本项目的成功完成将在全世界首次揭示低细胞硬度对癌症干细胞不可或缺的作用，将引领癌症治疗进入靶向细胞力学的新时代。这一发现将首次证明细胞硬度可以作为癌症诊断的力学指标，同时也可以作为癌症治疗的标靶。本研究将促进新颖的癌症治疗方法的发展，即直接靶向细胞力学硬度，这一成果将惠及众多肝癌病人。这些关键的研究发现将提供新的证据支持一个全新的论点，即癌症不仅仅是基因变异也可能是一个“力学”因素引起的疾病，而这将大大拓展甚至转变人们现有对癌症的认识和理解，并极大地推动癌症研究的发展。

25210917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25210917.value: Construction workers are exposed to a high risk of work-related musculoskeletal disorders (WMSDs) due to physically demanding manual handling tasks in awkward postures. Previous research efforts have developed diverse postural ergonomic assessment methods to identify the risk of WMSDs by classifying and analyzing working postures. However, the use of these methods are constrained in construction practice because of time-consuming and manual procedures, observation errors, and the lack of trained experts. In this regard, this research proposes a vision-based approach to automating existing postural ergonomic assessment methods. Specifically, research objectives are 1) to develop computer vision and machine learning algorithms to automatically classify working postures on video images and to evaluate WMSD risks based on existing ergonomic assessment tools; and 2) to test the algorithms to prove the feasibility of automatically evaluating exposure to ergonomic risks and refine its applicability to real sites. The central hypothesis of this research is that different postures on images create unique image pixel patterns, and thus by learning these patterns from virtual images (i.e., training images), classification algorithms can differentiate between postures on real world images more accurately than human expert observers. The performance of posture classification algorithms relies on extensively on training images that contain diverse postures for different conditions (e.g., viewpoints, anthropometry of workers). The substantial novelty of the proposed research is the development of virtual human modelling to create extensive training image datasets without a significant effort to manually collect massive datasets. The proposed approach will enable people who are not well-trained analysts to evaluate ergonomic risks during performing tasks in a practical manner. Vision-based ergonomic evaluation has the great potential to quickly evaluate all tasks in the workplace, and then to identify ergonomically risky tasks that need immediate interventions, enabling more effective use of resources to improve construction tasks.

25210917.label: Realisation of objectives
25210917.value: Objective #1. Develop computer vision algorithms which can automatically classify and evaluate working postures on images using virtual training datasets. Computer vision-based postural classification algorithms aim to classify different body postures defined by existing postural ergonomic evaluation methods from video or time-lapse images. Its underlying mechanism is that different postures on images create distinguishable image pixel patterns (i.e. image features), allowing classification algorithms to learn the patterns from training images and to differentiate the postures in test images. One of the key challenges of vision-based approaches is the creation of comprehensive training images reflecting variations in real-world conditions (such as viewpoints or workers’ physical attributes). To address this challenge, training image datasets obtained through virtual human modeling were developed. In addition, the current study applied an algorithm for vision-based posture classification using image features from body silhouettes obtained by background subtraction. The proposed algorithm is able to automatically classify diverse working postures to identify potential ergonomic risks of construction workers, indicating that Objective #1 has been successfully achieved. Below is a brief explanation on the developed algorithms. 1.1. Creating Virtual Training Datasets Training images for diverse postures were obtained by using virtual human modeling, an emerging technology for motion simulation in a virtual environment (VE). A virtual human model with specific physical attributes such as height and weight is inserted and animated according to human motion-capture data in a 3D virtual space to generate virtual training image datasets of the type. To create virtual training data, motion data from workers at real-world construction sites were collected using motion-capture systems such as an RGB-D sensor and an IMU-based motion capture system. Then, the virtual human model could be manipulated into any postures from any viewpoints, with substantial variability in physical attributes, without requiring new motion data from actual workers. 1.2. Obtaining Body Silhouettes through Background Subtraction The proposed method aims to recognize postures by using image features from body silhouettes. Accurate posture classification is dependent on techniques for deriving clear body silhouettes from images. The present study employed background subtraction and noise removal algorithms to obtain clear body silhouettes, with a bounding box serving as a Region of Interest (ROI) to extract image features at the next step. Background subtraction algorithms define the current pixel as foreground when the difference between its value and those of pixels in the background model exceeds the threshold value. This study applied one of the state-of-the-art background subtraction algorithms, ViBe, which is robust to lighting changes and the appearance of new objects on the scene as it updates the background model over time. 1.3. Extracting Image Features from Body Silhouettes At the next stage, image features representing body postures are extracted from body silhouettes. In this study, attributes of body shapes were used as image features from body silhouettes. Those attributes include: 1) the aspect ratio of the bounding box; 2) the ratio of the minor to the major axis of the ellipse that is fitted to the silhouette; and 3) the orientation of the ellipse itself. These features are intended to reflect morphological variations in body silhouettes according to different postures. To extract more detailed shape-based features, the bounding box is further divided into 2×1 (2 subsets) and 2×2 (4 subsets) sub-windows, and the features are extracted from each sub-window. 1.4. Classification Algorithm Once the image features have been constructed, a classifier has to learn the features from virtual training datasets in order to classify postures in new testing images. As a classifier, Support Vector Machines (SVMs) are applied, as SVMs are widely-used discriminative classifiers in action recognition. The SVM classification aims, in brief, to separate the set of training vectors belonging to two separate classes. Even though it was originally developed for two-class classification, it can be extended to multi-class classification by combining a number of two-class classification SVMs to form a multi-class classifier. Objective #2. Test the developed algorithms to prove the feasibility of automatically evaluating exposure to ergonomic risks through laboratory experiments Objective #2 of the study has been also successfully achieved as the developed algorithm was able to accurately classify diverse postures on images using the algorithms developed in Objective #1. The testing results strongly support the utility of virtually created training datasets with high adjustability for these factors. The detailed testing procedure, conditions and overall results are described below. 2.1. Testing Postures For this test, three representative postures involving different body parts, such as back-bending for back posture, arm-raising for arm posture, and knee-bending for leg posture were selected. Eight male student subjects with different physical attributes, such as height and Body Mass Index (BMI) were recruited to represent human variability in silhouettes. The subjects were asked to simulate each posture 10 times. For example, they began by standing up straight, and then 1) bent their backs up to 90 degrees; 2) raised their arms to the tops of their heads; or 3) bent their knees as if they were squatting, followed by standing up straight once more. They were given repeated practice so that they were able to simulate the postures identically. 2.2. Testing Conditions and Measures To test the performance of the proposed method under different conditions (i.e. viewpoint and physical variation), laboratory tests were conducted. Laboratory testing of the proposed method served three purposes: 1) assessing the overall classification performance by viewpoint, without taking the selection of optimal training images into account (Test #1); 2) establishing the effect of viewpoint-choice on classification performance (Test #2); and 3) measuring the effect of the virtual models’ physical attributes on classification performance (Test #3). 2.3. Testing Results The results from Test #1 indicate that the proposed algorithms performed better when testing images from the left view (88.6%) than when testing those taken from the left-diagonal perspective (85.6%) or from the rear (78.4%). More specifically, there was no confusion between back-bending, arm-raising and knee-bending postures in the left view, whereas confusion between these postures increased as the viewpoint shifted from the left toward the rear. This implies that a side view will likely yield the best classification results. Most classification errors occurred as a consequence of confusion between standing and other postures. The results of Test #2, which investigated postural variability by viewpoint, underline the importance of training-image viewpoint selection. Mean accuracy was 88.7% when the same views were used for both training and testing images, but it fell to 80.8% when an alternative view was used for training images. Classification errors would increase as the mismatch between training- and testing-image viewpoints became more marked (e.g., if training images from the rear were combined with testing images from the left). Test #3 shows training images taken from virtual models with similar physical attributes to those of the real-world subjects were identified with greater accuracy (mean: 85.8%, standard deviation: 2.4%) than the ones that used other virtual models (mean: 83.0%, standard deviation: 3.7%; p = 0.004). These results indicate that variations in silhouette shape that were linked to individuals’ physical attributes would affect classification performance, and thus, that posture-classification algorithms must take individual differences in height and body mass into account.

25210917.label: Major findings and research outcome
25210917.value: This study has developed a 2D image-based posture-classification method based on machine-learning algorithms, with the wider aim of automating current postural ergonomic evaluation methods. To assess the proposed method under diverse conditions, laboratory-based tests were conducted with eight male subjects possessing different physical attributes. These tests established that the proposed algorithm is capable of robust posture-classification accuracy comparable to that attained by human observers. In particular, considering that the use of customized training datasets created and manipulated in a virtual environment showed better classification performance, the proposed approach has great potential for dealing with high variability of human postures that has been one of the challenges in the computer vision domain. The proposed approach creates a range of opportunities for both research and practice. On the research side, it could be used to tackle several persistent challenges to vision-based posture classification, including 1) insufficient numbers of training images for machine learning, 2) how to deal with changes in color, texture and contrast in images, and 3) the complexity of representing postures across a range of different observational viewpoints and workers’ anatomical differences. First, a novel method of using training datasets for diverse postures from a virtual environment was suggested to minimize the effort associated with collecting training images from the real world. Also, the above test results show that the use of body silhouettes can address potential errors caused by differences between virtual and real-world images and/or by variations in image quality. In addition, the proposed approach is robust to intra- and inter-class variability as a consequence of changing viewpoints and individual differences in workers’ physical attributes that could lead to variations in the imaged postures. By using virtual human models, this approach can create training images in which body mass and viewpoint can be adjusted as required.

25210917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25210917.value: Despite the validity of the proposed approach in the experiment setting, the proposed approach may need to be further tested in real conditions whether more complex postures during dynamic construction tasks would exist. It should be also tested on the images that are taken at a vertically high angle that can reduce obstacles on the field of view of the camera. Also, the use of training images from a virtual model can be used for vision-based object detection of other types of construction entities such as construction equipment, which will be further explored in the future study.

25210917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25210917.value: Construction workers are at high risk of work-related musculoskeletal disorders (WMSDs) due to physically demanding manual-handling tasks in awkward postures. This study developed a computer vision-based assessment method to identify ergonomically risk postures by automatically analysing site videos collected during performing construction tasks. In construction especially, those responsible for on-site health and safety are few in number and generally lack the expertise needed to perform ergonomic assessments when identifying WMSD risks. The proposed approach can help even those practitioners who lack sufficient ergonomic knowledge to perform postural ergonomic risk assessments simply by making videos of workers. In short, computer vision-based ergonomic assessment could open the door to proactive control of WMSDs among construction workers by quickly evaluating all tasks, identifying potential risks, and taking timely action to eliminate those risks. Ultimately, it could help to prevent WMSDs during diverse occupational tasks.

25211817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25211817.value: 本項目的主要目標是探究新興污水處理技術—光催化燃料電池中的物質和電荷傳輸現象。光催化燃料電池可以在光激發下，將污水中具有毒性的有機物分解成無害物質，并同時將儲存在有機物中的化學能轉換為電能。然而，傳統光催化燃料電池由兩個巨大的半反應腔室和離子交換膜組成，正是由於反應腔室的體積過於龐大，大大降低入射光吸收率和被降解有機物和氫氧根離子的傳輸效率，嚴重限制有機物降解速率和產電能力。此外，光陽極中光生電子空穴複合速率過高也是導致光催化燃料電池性能低的一個重要原因。 與傳統光催化燃料電池不同，我們通過結合微流控技術提出了一種新型的光催化燃料電池，它具有多层孔隙結構，可以在時間和空間上實現對有機物濃度的控制。我們初步的性能測試結果表明：該電池可將降解效率和產電能力提高20%-30%。雖然我們的獨特設計很有吸引力，但是在廣泛應用之前，電池性能需要進一步提高。電池性能的提升不僅依賴於高性能光催化材料的開發來增加入射光的吸收率，還依賴於大幅減少光生電子空穴的復合及光陽極的結構優化設計，這需要對光陽極內物質和電荷的傳輸過程及其機理有著深刻理解和認識。 不同於傳統燃料電池，光催化燃料電池中物質和電荷的輸運過程及機理更為複雜；因為除了物質、離子、電子傳輸過程，還涉及到光子與空穴傳輸過程。本項目將通過創新實驗和先進建模來探究以下問題：1）設計及製造多層並且具有孔徑大小呈梯度分佈的光陽極，這種設計不但可以增強光吸收效率及降低光生電子空穴複合率，還可以提升物質和電荷在微孔中的傳輸速率；2）構建多尺度模型來幫助研究多孔結構中物質和電荷傳輸過程，從而確定最優結構設計參數；3）實驗評估光陽極性能。完成本項目將會進一步提升新型光催化燃料電池性能，從而推動光催化燃料電池技術的發展，加快該技術的商業化進程。

25211817.label: Realisation of objectives
25211817.value: During this project, we have achieved the three objectives as follows: Objective #1: To design and fabricate a multi-layered, composite porous structure with a pore-size gradient, which enables a multi-step light absorption, reduces the electron-hole recombination, as well as enhances the mass and charge transport. Realisation: Three-dimensional porous electrodes, a thin nano-porous catalyst layer uniformly distributed on the matrix surface of a foam-like structure, are typically employed to improve the mass/ion transport. Such a three-dimensional porous structure brings two critical advantages: (i) reduced mass/ion transport resistance for the delivery of the reactants via shortening the transport distance and (ii) enlarged electrochemical surface area, via reducing the dead pores, isolated particles and severe aggregations, for interfacial reactions. In this project, three types of three-dimensional porous structure are fabricated via different preparation methods. As a comparison, a conventional dual-layer design is also prepared via direct painting method. It is shown that the use of the three-dimensional porous structure in fuel cells results in a peak power density of 45.0 mW cm-2 at 60°C, which is two times of that achieved by using a conventional dual-layer design (19.5 mW cm-2). This performance improvement is mainly attributed to the unique three-dimensional structure design, which effectively enhances the mass/ion transport through the porous electrode and enlarges the electrochemical surface area (accessible active area) for interfacial reactions. In addition, a cost-effective poly(vinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene) is used to replace the conventional and expensive Nafion and polytetrafluoroethylene as the binder in the porous electrode fabrication. It is found that this new electrode binder shows the lowest cost at $0.18 kW-1, while both PTFE and Nafion offer the higher cost at $0.80 kW-1 and $145.59 kW-1, respectively. Objective #2: To develop a multi-scale model for the simultaneous transport of mass, ions, electrons and holes through the porous structure, which allows the proposed photoanodes be numerically studied so that the optimal design parameters can be determined. Realisation: A mathematical model is developed, involving mass/charge transport through the porous electrode, electrochemical reactions at the solid/electrolyte interfaces, and ion migration through the membrane. Different from the previous models that typically treated the catalyst layer as an interface, our model also considers the thickness of the catalyst layer and examine the effect of various structural and operating parameters on concentration and potential/current distributions. Moreover, we also consider the competitive adsorption between molecules and ions at active sites, in addition to mass/charge transport and electrochemical reactions. Therefore, this model is not only capable of predicting the polarization curves to evaluate the fuel cell performance, but also able to give more in-depth insights into physical and chemical phenomena occurring in fuel cells, e.g., the concentration distributions of reactants/products, the distribution of local current density, and the distribution of electrode potential. Objective #3: To develop a photoelectrochemical testing system, with which the porous photoanodes screened in the foregoing tasks can be tested and evaluated. Realisation: A three-electrode testing system is developed to conduct characterizations at electrode level, where the fabricated electrode, the Pt foil, and the Hg-HgO (MMO, 1.0 M KOH) are used as the working electrode, the counter electrode and the reference electrode, respectively. In addition, a characterization and diagnostic platform at cell level is also constructed.

25211817.label: Major findings and research outcome
25211817.value: With this project, we have the following major findings and research outcome: 1) In this project, three types of three-dimensional porous electrode are fabricated, via different preparation methods, for direct formate fuel cells: (i) Pd/C nanoparticles coating on the nickel foam matrix surface (Pd-C/NF) via a dip-coating method, (ii) Pd nanoparticles depositing on the nickel foam matrix surface (Pd/NF) via reduction reaction deposition, and (iii) Pd nanoparticles embedding in the nickel foam matrix (Pd/(in)NF) via replacement reaction deposition. It is shown that the use of the three-dimensional porous structure in fuel cells results in a more than 100% improvement in power density. This performance improvement is mainly attributed to the unique three-dimensional structure design, which effectively enhances the mass/ion transport through the porous electrode and enlarges the electrochemical surface area for interfacial reactions. Major part of this find is included in paper titled "Three-dimensional porous electrodes for direct formate fuel cells" published in Science China Technological Sciences included in Part C. It is also utilized in other related work in Part C. 2) A mathematical model is developed, involving mass/charge transport through the porous electrode, electrochemical reactions at the solid/electrolyte interfaces, and ion migration through the membrane. In addition, we also consider the competitive adsorption between molecules and ions at active sites, in addition to mass/charge transport and electrochemical reactions. The simulation results show that the cell performance improves initially with the increasing concentration of the anolyte, while undergoing a decline at the high current density region, which might be attributed to the enhanced ohmic loss. In addition, the cell performance increases over the whole current density region with increasing the concentration of the catholyte. Meanwhile, the numerical results exhibit that the cell performance is elevated when the anode exchange current density or the cathode exchange current density is increased, which emphasizes the significance of developing novel catalyst with superior catalytic activity. Moreover, the increase of diffusion layer thickness has a negative effect on the cell performance. The resistance of mass-transport increases when the diffusion layer becomes thicker and influences both the delivery of reactants and the removal of reaction products. Major part of this find is included in paper titled "Mathematical modeling of direct ethylene glycol fuel cells incorporating the effect of the competitive adsorption" published in Applied Thermal Engineering included in Part C. It is also utilized in other related work in Part C.

25211817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25211817.value: With the results from the project, the further development of the research and the proposed course of action will be to demonstrate a micro fuel cell system by using the unique three-dimensional structure design. It will consist of a three-dimensional electrode, a microchannel, and an air-breathing cathode. The mixed solution containing methylene blue and electrolyte, and the electrolyte solution are fed into the anode and cathode compartments by a syringe pump. During all experiments, the solution flow rates at both sides are always the same to ensure the laminar flow.

25211817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25211817.value: Photocatalytic fuel cells, which can simultaneously treat organic wastewater and generate electricity, meet the global demands on energy and environment. Although promising, the conventional cell, which consists of two big compartments separated with an ion exchange membrane, has exhibited extremely low performance. Our solution to this issue is to introduce a three-dimensional porous structure into the cell design. This idea effectively enhances the mass/ion transport through the porous electrode and enlarges the electrochemical surface area (accessible active area) for interfacial reactions. In term of cell performance, it is shown that the use of the three-dimensional porous structure in fuel cells results in a more than 100% improvement in power density. In terms of electrode fabrication cost, it is significantly decreased from $145.59 kW-1 to $0.18 kW-1. This performance improvement is mainly attributed to the unique three-dimensional structure design and robust model development. This project has achieved a substantial improvement in the fuel cell performance, making the technology closer to reality.

25215417.label: Project Title(Chinese)
25215417.value: 就改變中的工作模式對金融企業未来辦公室需求影響的實踐式調研

25215417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25215417.value: To face today’s highly competitive global business environment many organizations in the West increasingly embrace ICT-enabled new working practices (NWPs) (hot-desking, team-working, home-working, and business process-reengineering) to realize financial and productivity benefits as these new work-patterns enhance employee and organizational business performance resulting in long-term cost savings through less use of expensive real estate, and hence to maintain competitiveness. NWPs in turn have brought changes to corporate office space usage patterns in terms of space per person (SPP). However, whether NWPs are really taking place in firms and in what ways have NWPs influenced organizational changes and space usage patterns in Asia in general and Hong Kong in particular, remain under-explored. In fact, a study of this nature in Hong Kong has never been made. During his doctoral research, the Principal Investigator (PI) analyzed how the location, type and quality of office space is influenced by the growth of FIREB (finance, insurance, real estate and business service) firms in Hong Kong. One of his main findings is that rapid investment in ICT has some implications for space usage. Building on the PI’s own research and a growing body of new international findings in the field, this newly proposed research aims to identify key changes in work patterns (i.e. NWPs), if any, and to analyze their implications for office space usage (through SPP) among finance firms in Hong Kong. Using sets of cross-sectional data obtained through a questionnaire survey of all Hong Kong Monetary Authority authorized finance firms, 266 in total, the research will adopt a quantitative approach to first check if NWPs are indeed being implemented in those finance firms. A comprehensive and robust approach to analyzing the space usage implications will then be made based on multiple regression modelling and structural equation modelling. The research will add new knowledge to the limited literature on the effect of NWPs in Asian organizations and will enrich the growing body of international literature on how today’s competitive global-business organizations should revisit their workplace strategies to accommodate the rising agile workforce and NWPs. The findings will provide new insights to the ongoing debate on the impact of ICT-enabled NWPs on SPP. Some claim SPP is reducing. Others claim otherwise. From the real estate perspective, the findings will inform policy making towards the better planning ahead of office properties able to accommodate NWPs, helping Hong Kong to remain competitive as a key financial centre.

25216617.label: Project Title(Chinese)
25216617.value: 高比电容合金在锂离子电池领域的应用，以及材料合成，材料结构和机械性能的研究

25216617.label: Project Objectives
25216617.value: To synthesize silicon-based thin-film alloys which are strategically designed to optimize the cells volumetric and gravimetric capacity while maintaining stability over a large number of cycles. To use the thin-film electrodes for in situ mechanical characterization during anode lithiation. The wafer-curvature methods employed use stress signals to track the electrode evolution as it incorporates increasing amounts of lithium. These mechanical stress signals can explain the fundamental atomic or phase-related mechanisms which govern the alloying pathway between lithium and the electrode host material. To develop in situ optical microscopy methods for tracking the electrode surface morphology and the growth of lithium whiskers on the surface of the thin film electrodes in real time. This will allow us to quantify the critical current density threshold for the transition from lithium alloying to lithium-on-lithium deposition. To combine the results of mechanical and optical testing with those from electrochemical cycling to provide a rational, scientific basis for the capacity enhancements and improved stability of this next generation of lithium-ion battery anode materials.
