25504517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25504517.value: A large amount of work has used queueing theory to model and study service systems. The classical literature mainly focuses on solving theoretical models under the assumption that all of the system information is known a priori. However, such an assumption is usually invalid in practice, and more attention has turned to research that combines theoretic study with real data in recent years. In this project, we will study the capacity provisioning problem of a service system when the system information-such as the arrival rate, service rate, and abandonment probabilities-is unknown. Such a system requires costly service capacity and is operated by a firm that charges every customer who requests service a service fee. The firm's objective is to maximize its expected profit by dynamically adjusting the service capacity over a finite planning horizon. Since the system information required for decision making is unknown a priori, the firm must learn it from real data collected during the system operation, which introduces a tension between exploration (information learning) and exploitation (profit maximization) into the decision process. The more time a firm spends learning the information, the less time remains for it to maximize the profit. In contrast, spending less time on learning can yield a higher chance of making sub-optimal decisions in the exploitation phase. In the proposed research, we will develop data-driven optimization approaches that help a firm estimate the system information effectively and efficiently, identify the current operations issues from the estimation results, and make online capacity decisions as more data are revealed. By adopting existing data-driven optimization techniques and developing new methodologies, our algorithm will properly balance the exploration-exploitation trade-off and achieve near-optimal performance in the long run. From a practical perspective, our research could help improve the operations of service systems in many industries. By developing data-driven approaches that can avoid making sub-optimal decisions due to the lack of information, we aim to find a socially optimal solution that will simultaneously increase the profit of a service provider and improve the service quality experienced by customers. Our work will contribute to the current literature on data-driven optimization, develop new methodologies for managing queueing system using real data, and stimulate the data-driven queueing research. 學術界中已有大量的科研工作利用排隊論來為各式服務系統建模並進行研究。傳統的文獻大多在假設所有系統信息已知的情況下專注于如何求解理論模型。然而這樣的一個假設在實踐中通常並不成立，因此更多的研究者在近年來把目光轉向如何把理論研究與實際數據結合起來。 在此計劃中，我們將研究當系統信息（譬如顧客的到達速率、服務速率和放棄等待概率）未知時如何為系統配置服務容量。我們選擇研究的此類服務系統的設立需要昂貴的設施，而負責運營的公司會向每一位使用系統服務的顧客收取一定的服務費用。故此，公司在運營時需考慮如何動態地調整服務容量以使得其在某有限決策時段内獲得最大的期望利潤。因爲可供用作決策參考的系統信息並未能預先獲知，公司必須利用從系統運行中收集到的實際數據去學習這些信息。此需求為決策過程引入了探索（信息學習）與開發（利潤最大化）之間的衝突。當越多的時間花在學習信息上，留給公司最大化利潤的時間就越少。相反地，花費更少的時間去學習系統信息將會導致一個更大的在開發階段作出非最優決策的概率。在提議的研究中，我們將會開發出一類基於數據的優化方法去幫助公司有效及高效地估計出系統信息、從估計結果中發現現有運營問題、以及隨著更多數據的逐漸顯露實時地作出服務容量調整的決定。通過博采現有的數據驅動優化技術及開發新方法，我們的算法將會恰當地平衡探索-開發之間的權衡，並在長遠規劃中達到近最優的表現。 從實踐的角度出發，我們的研究會幫助改善許多行業中服務系統的運營效果。通過開發出數據驅動方法來避免企業因缺乏系統信息而做出非最優決策，我們旨在找出一個可同時增加服務提供商利潤及改善顧客服務體驗的社會最優決策。我們的研究工作將有助於完善現有的數據驅動最優化文獻，為排隊系統的管理提供新的基於實際數據的方法，及進一步刺激數據驅動的排隊論研究。

25504517.label: Realisation of objectives
25504517.value: All proposed research objectives have been realised in the project. Details are as follows. In this project, we study the capacity provisioning problem of a service system when the system information-such as the customer arrival rate, service rate, and customers' abandonment probabilities-is unknown. The firm's objective is to maximize its expected profit by adjusting the service capacity, which is costly, over a finite planning horizon. Because the system information required for decision making is unknown a priori, the firm must learn it from data collected during the system operation, which introduces a tension between exploration (information learning) and exploitation (profit maximization) into the decision process. To study the problem, we first build queueing models for typical service systems in which we use various parameters to capture the operating characteristics of the systems (Objective 1). Specifically, we consider a service system with multiple servers serving impatient customers who arrive according to a Poisson process and request an exponential amount of service time. Arriving customers who find no idle server may decide to join the queue to wait for service or abandon (balk) the system without service depending on the queue length and the system capacity. Based on this basic model, we include different features to study different types of systems that may appear in practice. The features include (i) customers' abandonment behavior that is dependent on or independent of the system capacity, (ii) observable or unobservable lost sales, and (iii) multi-class customers. We assume that the above system information required for decision making is unknown a priori, and hence the firm must learn it from real data collected during the system operation. Note that one challenge of our study is that we don't assume functional form of customers' decision function because customer behavior in practice is complicated in general. Based on the model, we develop data-driven learning algorithms that help the firm learn the system information effectively and efficiently and make capacity decision on the fly as more data are collected (Objective 2). Intuitively, we start with estimating the inter-arrival time, service time, and customers' joining probabilities by using sample means of the random variables. However, estimating all these parameters to a certain degree of accuracy will require a substantial (even infinite) amount of time because the time needed to obtain enough observations for customers' joining/balking instances grows exponentially as the size of the state space increases. To overcome this difficulty, we first analyze the problem and obtain several structural properties that can guide us to reduce the complexity of building a data-driven decision model. We show that the profit function is quasi-concave in the number of servers provisioned and that the approximated profit function will be sufficiently close to the true profit function as long as we can accurately estimate some parameters that play dominant roles among all. These properties suggest that the problem of finding a global optimal solution can be reduced to that of finding a local optimal solution, and that estimating some dominant parameters may be enough for making correct decisions. The question that remains is how to determine the number of parameters to learn accurately when they are unknown. We solve it by exploring all options when new data are available. We then design a confidence-based decision (CBD) policy for learning the system information and finding the optimal capacity. The design ideas are as follows. To control the chance of mistake, we adopt a conservative approach and use confidence intervals instead of sample means in evaluation of the benefit of changing capacity. We refer to the upper and lower bounds of the confidence intervals as optimistic and pessimistic estimations of an unknown value. First, if the profit with n+1 servers under pessimistic estimation is higher than the profit with n servers under optimistic estimation, then we can conclude with high confidence that it is profitable to add one more server. Otherwise, if the profit with n+1 servers under optimistic estimation is lower than the profit with n servers under pessimistic estimation, then we can also conclude with high confidence that it is not profitable to add one more server. If none of these two conditions is met, making a conclusion may be risky and hence we should continue learning. Noting that a suboptimal decision will result in a larger negative impact if it is used for a longer period, we set the size of the confidence level increasing in the planning horizon T so as to strike a balance between exploration and exploitation. We further conduct performance analyses of our algorithms and evaluate the regret, which is defined as the relative loss compared to the full information optimal profit, of using our methods (Objective 3). Under an assumption that the impact of changing capacity on the profit is always non-zero under perfect information, we prove that using our CBD policy can achieve asymptotically optimal performance, having an average regret that diminishes in the order of O(log(T)/T). We have also incorporated the features of unobservable lost sales and multi-class customers into our model extensions (Objective 4). When the lost sales are unobservable, we have adapted our algorithm to learn the state-dependent effective arrival rates. The main idea that simplifies the learning remains the same: to learn only the dominant parameters. For systems with multi-class customers, we look into two special cases. In the case where customers form a single queue without priority, our algorithm can be applied to learn the information of different classes of customers separately. Asymptotic optimality is guaranteed. In the case where higher customers have preemptive priority in the queue, we use a cmu-rule based on the profit rate received to prioritize different classes of customers. We adapted our algorithm to learn the high-dimensional customers' behavior in this case. We discuss the performance under the condition that the higher class customers are less patient and have lower arrival rate. We have conducted extensive numerical experiments to evaluate the performance of our algorithms and shown that our algorithms perform efficiently as we expected (Objective 5). We find that when the current capacity level is far from the optimal one, our algorithm can quickly learn and suggest the firm to increase the capacity level to a level much closer to the true optimal. It is observed that it takes no more than 2log(T) time on average to reach a capacity level that is within 5 percent from the true optimal. This demonstrates the efficiency of our algorithm in reducing loss from using suboptimal decision. We also examine the sample paths in the numerical studies and observe that the capacity adjustment slows down once the capacity level is already very close to the true optimal, and that the learning process extends for a significant period even after the true optimal capacity is provisioned. This is because at close-to-optimal range, we need more data and time to make confident conclusion. These observations confirms the effectiveness of the error control mechanism used in our algorithm. In general, our algorithms perform excellently and robustly in finding the optimal capacity and minimizing the asymptotic regret.

25504517.label: Major findings and research outcome
25504517.value: We study the capacity optimization problem of service systems where customer information is unknown and develop a confidence-based decision policy that balances the trade-off between exploration (information learning) and exploitation (profit maximization). We derive bounds on the profit loss when using our policy against the optimal profit when decisions are made under known information. We prove that the average loss diminishes to zero as the time horizon increases, achieving near-optimal performance in asymptotic sense. In the development of our learning algorithms, we find that the optimal capacity is mainly determined by some parameters although the number of unknown parameters are many and even infinite because of diversified customer behavior. This structural property of the problem allows us to focus on some dominant parameters only and greatly reduces the cost and time required for learning. Using our algorithm, the firm should first goes through a learning phase, which is expected to take a logarithmic amount of the total time, to learn key customer information. We propose to use confidence interval (CI) estimation instead of point estimation so that we can control the chance of mistakes in decision making. After sufficient operation data have been collected, a final optimal decision will be concluded if the profit using a specific capacity level under a pessimistic estimation (lower bound of the CI) is higher than the profit of using other capacity levels under an optimistic estimation (higher bound of the CI). Our algorithm design highlights the fact that structural properties, obtained from theoretical analysis or by managerial insights in practice, can be extremely useful in reducing complexity of data-driven decision making and help people better utilize the data. In practice, our methodologies and insights can be applied to many service systems with costly servers, such as restaurant service, self-ordering kiosks in cafeteria, vehicle sharing transportation systems. A paper that summarizes the basic algorithm is being revised and will be submit to a top journal the area. The methodology has been applied to study capacity dimensioning problem of vehicle sharing systems, which yields a paper that has been published in Management Science and another subsequent working paper on its application. Based on the basic model in this project, we have also finished a theoretical paper that studies optimization of queues when customers have irrational sunk cost affected behavior. This work is under revision after receiving a "reject-and-resubmit" recommendation from Manufacturing & Service Operations Management.

25504517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25504517.value: We develop data-driven capacity provisioning policies for service systems where customer information is unknown a priori. While the project focuses on the setting where demand rate is constant, it lays out foundations for studying the more complex case where demand rate is uncertain or time-varying. Thus, it would be interesting to further study the problem in an uncertain or changing market environment. Another important direction of further development would be to consider more types of customer behavior. In addition to the time-consistent abandonment behavior currently formulated, it would be interesting to consider customer retrial after balking, reneging after joining, or re-visit after service. These further development can potentially be done under the parametric framework we use in our study, e.g, by introducing new parametric components that characterize the various concerned features into the model. Note that derivation of certain structural properties in the new model is necessary for simplifying the learning algorithm and guaranteeing its performance.

25504517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25504517.value: We study profit maximization problem of a service system where system information is unknown and the firm must make capacity decision on the fly as more data are collected. With unknown information, the firm faces the well-known exploration-exploitation tradeoff between learning and doing. If the firm spends more time on learning the information (exploration), it then has less time to maximize the profit (exploitation). Conversely, spending less time on learning will yield a higher chance of making sub-optimal decisions in the exploitation phase because of a less accurate estimation. We develop data-driven learning algorithms that balance the above tradeoff and help the firm to obtain near-optimal profit. Our finding that the optimal capacity is solely determined by some dominant parameters helps to greatly reduce the cost and time needed to learn sufficient information for correct decision making. The insights herein can be applied to more general decision analytics problems when complicated market environment and diversified customer behavior must be characterized by a large number of parameters. Our study also highlights that in addition to computational methodologies that are indispensable in data science, managerial insights obtained from operations research can play a crucial role in efficient and full utilization of data.

25505517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25505517.value: Firms often grapple with these questions when contemplating adopting a new technology: Is adopting the technology profitable? When will my competitor adopt it? Should I wait for a next generation of the technology? The vast existing studies on technology adoption only tackle these questions separately. Hence, they cannot capture the interplay among these factors: (a) uncertain profitability of the technology, (b) technological progress, and (c) competition effects. Furthermore, they implicitly assume an exogenous innovation process so that a technology supplier's decision on improving the technology is not affected by the technology's market reception. Therefore, prior studies ignore the impact of downstream market demand on a supplier's incentive to allocate its R&D resources. This project aims to address these issues by considering an adoption problem in a market-pulled technology supply chain, in which a supplier provides an unproven technology to two adopters. In the context of a market-pulled technology supply chain, this project specifically focuses on two different aspects: (a) information sharing among adopters who are rivals, and (b) the design of subsidy program for spurring green technology adoption. The motivation of the first aspect comes from a counter-intuitive phenomenon that sometimes a firm publicly discloses their success of adopting a new technology. The preliminary result of this project shows that an early adopter may find it beneficial to disclose information regarding the technology's profitability in order to deter its rival's adoption. With this new insight, this proposed project examines the incentives of sharing information with rivals in a supply chain with an endogenous innovation process, and investigates the impact of horizontal sharing information upon the technological evolution. The results will contribute to the literature on information sharing in a supply chain, which typically focuses on vertical information sharing, but also will shed light on empirical studies by exploring under what conditions would a firm be more likely to disclose the success of a particular technology. In addition to information sharing, this project aims to give some policy implications for green technology adoption. More specifically, if the government would like to provide subsidies to encourage the technology innovation and adoption, should the policy maker subsidize the supplier to improve her R&D capability to innovate, or subsidize the adopters to decrease their procurement costs? The project will use a continuous-time real options game to investigate these two aspects. 在考虑采用新技术时，公司经常会遇到这些问题：采用该技术是否有利可图？我的竞争对手何时会采用它？我是否应该等下一代技术？目前关于技术采用的大量现有研究仅仅分别考虑这些问题。因此，他们无法捕捉以下三个因素之间的相互作用: (a) 技术盈利能力的不确定性; (b)可能出现的技术进步; (c)竞争效应。此外，目前已有的研究隐含地假设创新过程是主动性的，即上游技术供应商关于是否改进技术的决定不受下游市场需求的影响。因此，以前的研究忽略了下游的市场需求会如何激励和影响技术供应商分配研发资源。该项目旨在考虑市场驱动型技术供应链下的技术采用问题，而同时新技术的盈利能力具有不确定性。 在市场驱动型技术供应链的背景下，该项目专门关注两个方面：（a）互为竞争对手的两个技术采用者之间的信息共享，（b）如何设计促进绿色技术采用的补贴计划。第一个方面的研究来源于一个现实中的现象： 有悖于传统的理解认为一个理性公司不应该分享有利于竞争对手的信息，现实中有时会有一些公司主动披露他们采用新技术并获得了成功，而这样的披露会告诉竞争对手这种新技术是可盈利的。该项目的初步结果表明，早期的新技术采用者可以通过适当披露有关新技术盈利能力的信息而延缓其竞争对手采用同样的新技术。有了这个新的见解，这个项目将考察在市场驱动型供应链中与竞争对手共享信息的动机，并调查这种横向分享信息对技术演进的影响。这个项目会有助于研究供应链中的信息共享，而目前这方面的文献通常侧重于垂直信息共享。 而且，这个项目还将通过探索企业在什么条件下更有可能披露特定技术的成功而对实证研究有所帮助。除了信息共享，该项目亦旨在为绿色技术的采用提供一些政策影响。更具体地说，如果政府想通过提供补贴来鼓励技术创新和采用，政策制定者应该补贴供应商来提高它的研发创新能力，还是补贴技术采用着来降低采用成本？该项目将使用连续时间的实物期权博弈模型来考察这两个方面。

25508217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25508217.value: When implementing the Markowitz (1952, 1959) portfolio theory, the mean vector and variance-covariance matrix of the return must be obtained to calculate the optimal portfolio weights and maximize the expected utility. However, the estimated mean vector and variance-covariance matrix using historical data cannot be exactly the same as the true parameters. As a result, the expected utility is not maximized due to the difference in the estimated parameters and true parameters. The consequence is also known as the estimation risk, which is the most critical issue in implementing the portfolio theory. Later Kan and Zhou (2007) theoretically and empirically analyze the estimation risk and conclude that the standard plug-in method replacing the parameters by the sample / moment estimators performs poorly when the estimation window is not long enough. Further they propose their two-funds (w ̂(c)=c/γ Σ ̂^(-1) μ ̂) and three-funds rules (w ̂=1/γ(dΣ ̂^(-1) μ ̂+e Σ ̂^(-1) 1_N)), which optimally combine the risk-free assets, the sample tangency portfolio and the sample global minimum-variance portfolio and effectively reduce the estimation risk. However, another estimation risk exists in their forms of two-funds and three-funds rules – the parameters (i.e., c, d and e) involved in the rules actually are functions of the parameters in the portfolio theory assumptions (the true mean vector and variance-covariance matrix) – therefore how to improve the estimation of the parameters in the two-funds and three-funds rules becomes another challenge. In this proposal, I plan to propose an alternative approach to estimate the two-funds and three funds rules by applying the trimmed mean approach in repeated cross-validation practice. Some recursive estimation techniques are further raised to reduce the computational and memory complexity. Further I plan to conduct a comprehensive empirical study with ten different weighting schemes across seven well diversified portfolio universes, and several out-of-sample performance measures are also implemented to compare the above-mentioned weighting schemes’ performances. The findings add to the growing literature in portfolio theory and shed a light on both academic study and industry application. 實施Markowitz（1952,1959）投資組合理論時，需要獲知回報的平均向量和協方差矩陣，以計算最優投資組合權重並最大化預期效用。然而使用歷史數據估計的平均向量和協方差矩陣並不能與真實參數完全相同。由於估計參數和真實參數的差異，預期效用難以最大化。該現象也被稱為估計風險，是應用投資組合理論最關鍵的問題。其後Kan和Zhou（2007）從理論上和實證上分析了估計風險，並得出結論：當估計窗口不夠長時，使用樣本估計替代參數的標準方法表現不佳。此外，他們提出二基金 (w ̂(c)=c/γ Σ ̂^(-1) μ ̂)和三基金規則(w ̂=1/γ(dΣ ̂^(-1) μ ̂+e Σ ̂^(-1) 1_N)), 將無風險資產，樣本切線資產組合和樣本最小方差組合進行優化組合，以有效降低估計風險。然而，另一種估計風險存在於其二基金和三基金規則中 - 規則中涉及的參數（即c, d和e）實際上是投資組合理論假設中的參數（真實的平均向量和協方差矩陣）的函數 -- 因此如何改進二基金和三基金規則中估計參數是另一項挑戰。在這個研究中，我提出一種替代方法，通過應用修正平均法在重復交叉驗證試驗來估計二基金和三基金規則相關參數。同時進一步提出了一些遞歸估計方法，以減少計算和存儲復雜性。此外，我計劃在七個投資組合範圍內進行十個不同權重算法的實證研究，並且還應用了一系列樣本外績效指標以比較上述權重算法的表現。本研究探索了投資組合理論在學術研究和金融行業的相關應用及進一步發展。

25508217.label: Realisation of objectives
25508217.value: During the funding periods, we have worked on the project and achieved most of the objectives of the proposal. The detail background and interpretation are provided as follows: Kan and Zhou (2007) two-funds rule and three-funds rule provide the theoretical optimal solution to the portfolio theory (w ̂(c)=c/γ Σ ̂^(-1) μ ̂, and w ̂=1/γ(dΣ ̂^(-1) μ ̂+e Σ ̂^(-1) 1_N) , respectively) However, in practice another estimation risk issue exists in the two-funds and three-funds rules. Note that the parameters c^*,d^*,e^* involve the true values of μ,μ_g,Σ. To implement the Kan and Zhou (2007), one possible solution is to apply the sample / moment estimators to calculate the value of c,d,e. When the estimation window is not long enough, the estimated c ̂,d ̂,e ̂ have strong distortion to the true value of c^*,d^*,e^*, as a result the estimated portfolio weights based on the two-funds rule and three-funds rule will be significantly different from the theoretical optimal weights. In the project, we consider another approach of estimating the portfolio weights under the forms of two-funds and three-funds rules: robust cross-validation. Cross-validation is a model validation technique to search for the parameter estimators and provides the “pseudo” out-of-sample test within limited number of observations. The objective is to implement the cross-validation technique to establish the robust estimators of the parameters in the two-funds and three-funds rules. When the distribution is not normal, the moment estimators are sometimes significantly affected by the outliers (a.k.a. not robust). Instead in this proposal, I would like to search for the robust estimators, i.e., the estimators have relatively small variance and will not drive the out-of-sample performance too far away. A typical cross-validation practice in portfolio theory is named as “Leave-one-out cross-validation”, which randomly selects one period of observations as the testing sample (say, t-period), and the remaining T-1 periods of the observations are regarded as the training sample. The estimated portfolio weights, for example the two-funds rule, w ̂_t (c)=c/γ (Σ_t ) ̂^(-1) (μ_t ) ̂ Where (Σ_t ) ̂ and (μ_t ) ̂ are the sample variance-covariance matrix and the mean vector of the excess returns in the training sample (the whole sample without the t-period observation). After obtaining the portfolio weights, I calculate the out-of-sample returns using t-period data as w ̂_t (c)^T R_t. 25508217.label: Major findings and research outcome
25508217.value: We appreciate the funding supported by Early Career Scheme, and well used the funding to develop several projects: 1. We create robust versions of Two-Funds, Three Funds Rules and improved two-funds rules using cross-validation approach, though we got some difficulty in selecting the suitable optimization engine (lpSolveAPI and lpSolve) as mentioned in the mid report. We have been successful achieved using the Grid Search, to ensure the robustness and convergence speed. We presented the preliminary work in a boutique workshop on Recent Developments in Mean-Field Game, Machine Learning and Quantitative Finance, and other conferences are canceled due to the covid-19. The preliminary results show that the robust two-funds and three-funds perform reasonable well compared with value weighted and equal weighted portfolios and plug-in methods, though it is still sensitive to the mean vector and covariance matrix estimation. Thus we modify the procedure using the shrinkage estimation, to improve the out-of-sample performance, and effectively reduce the overall risk (given the risk aversion coefficient 5). 2. By training students and using the funds and education group, my RAs and students (Lixin Cai, Qiulin Qi) collect the China market data, which contains all the information of the SSE 50 index members in the Shanghai Stock Exchange from January 2006 to December 2015. The SSE 50 index consists of the 50 largest stocks from the Shanghai Stock Exchange. We compared multiple portfolio weighting schemes and explored how smart beta strategies that are applied in the Chinese A-share market, and find the superior performance of the existing enhanced portfolio weighting schemes. The work has been titled as “A comprehensive study on smart beta strategies in the A-share market” and published in Applied Economics (PolyU A List), and has been cited in several journal publications and degree dissertations. 3. When we faced the challenge mentioned in the mid report, we seek for solving the issue by adding benchmark and using LASSO algorithm, and further developed another project, named “CVaR-LASSO Enhanced Index Replication (CLEIR): outperforming by minimizing downside risk”. By using the LASSO method to minimize the conditional value-at-risk of the tracking error (and select the tuning parameter using cross validation), we propose a new method to create an enhanced indexation (portfolio weighting) algorithm. Using 50-80 large stocks in the S&P 500 index, the methods closed tracked the benchmark with an alpha 2.55%, and an improved Sharpe Ratio.

25508217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25508217.value: The projects developed in this grant has great potential for further development: we discussed the parameter optimization using cross validation in two-funds and three-funds rules; there are also theoretical definitions of the parameters however need additional estimation of true Sharpe Ratio. How to accurately estimate becomes another possible research questions. Based on the third project I mentioned above, using LASSO can significantly improve the estimation (in high-dimension) but resulting in biased estimation. To balance the biasness and variance, we may consider correction for the estimated portfolio weights by adding debias terms. We see few research in verifying the different weighting schemes using Asia-Pacific data including mainland China, Hong Kong. The industry wants to see more empirical findings using the domestic / international data with advanced portfolio weighting methods. By searching “smart beta” and “China” in Google, there are more than 700 items and many of them are industry reports; while by searching “smart beta” and “China”, there are only two related papers – one is the paper developed in project 2, and the other is in Chinese. This area is deserved to be explored in both academia and industry (I have incorporated into my course “Security Analysis and Portfolio Management”).

25508217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25508217.value: This project discusses how to better construct the portfolios – Kan and Zhou (2007) theoretically and empirical analyze the estimation risk issue (estimated parameters do not equal the true parameters thus results in bad performance in the future) when applying Markowitz’s modern portfolio theory, and they proposed two-funds and three-funds rules to alleviate estimation risk concerns and improve the performance. We further improve the two-fund and three-fund rules to a robust version using cross-validation to estimate the parameters in original versions. Using multiple data, we find the performance is reasonable well (than the plug-in method) and can be further improved by using the shrinkage estimated parameters. Further we analyze different portfolio weighting schemes in Chinese A-share market, which provides additional empirical evidence to validate the portfolio weighting methods using China market data – the smart beta strategies are workable in China. And we also derive another work to use cross-validation methods to minimize the downside risk of the tracking error, and have a superior performance with alpha 2.55%, compared with the benchmark index.

25508417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25508417.value: Equity mutual funds lend securities in their portfolios to market makers or short sellers to generate additional returns. Although practitioners have emphasized the major benefit of securities lending by mutual funds, i.e. generating almost risk-free returns, it has been overlooked that securities lending can result in unintended consequence on firm-level governance by transferring voting rights from mutual funds to borrowers. To vote on proposals of stocks that have already been lent out, mutual funds have to recall these stocks and give up associated income from securities lending, which can be very costly. Shleifer and Vishny (1986) argue that a shareholder’s willingness to monitor the firm decreases with the cost of monitoring. Accordingly, securities lending can impedes mutual funds’ incentive to exert governance via shareholder voting. While this unintended effect of securities lending on firm governance is intuitive and appealing, prior theoretical studies debate the mechanism through which shareholder voting impacts firm governance. Christoffersen, Geczy, Musto, and Reed (2007) find that volume of vote trading increases around vote record dates while price of voting rights remains unchanged. They conclude that asymmetric information motivates the vote trade ‒ less informed voters offer their votes to more informed voters to obtain an optimal outcome on a particular proposal. In contrast, Aggarwal, Saffi, and Sturgess (2015) find that supply of lendable shares decreases and price of voting rights increases on vote record dates. They conclude that investors’ preferences motivate the vote trade ‒ investors that have particular preference over the proposal restrict lendable supply to exercise voting rights. These empirical studies use aggregated lending information at the stock level and fail to consider the heterogeneity of investors. This proposal attempts to collect a novel dataset of securities lending by mutual funds that allows me to identify voters who are also lenders of stocks. As shown by the data I have collected, around half of the funds participate in securities lending (Figure 1). This dataset allows me to explore interplay of securities lending and shareholder voting at fund level. Specifically, I plan to investigate whether securities lending income impedes mutual funds’ incentive to exert governance via shareholder voting and the mechanism through which shareholder votes impact governance. This project contributes to the literature by uncovering an unintended consequence of securities lending on governance. Moreover, the project will also provide insights to policy makers when they consider the regulations of securities lending and shareholder voting. 股权共同基金将投资组合中的证券借给卖空者，以产生额外的回报。虽然从业人员强调了共同基金的证券借贷的主要收益，即几乎无风险的回报，但是由于共同基金将投票权转移给借款人，证券借贷可能会对公司治理造成意想不到的后果。为了对已经借出的股票投标，共同基金必须回收这些股票，放弃证券借贷的相关收入，这可能是非常昂贵的。 Shleifer和Vishny（1986）认为，股东监督企业的意愿随着监督成本而下降。因此，证券借贷可能会阻碍共同基金通过股东投票发起治理的意愿。 虽然证券借贷对公司治理的这种无意的影响是直观的，但以前的理论研究对股东投票是如何影响公司治理存在争论。 Christoffersen，Geczy，Musto和Reed（2007）发现，投票权交易量在投票记录日期之前增加，而投票权价格保持不变。他们得出结论，不对称信息激励投票交易 -知情较少的选民将自己的投票权卖给知情较多的选民，以获得一个特定提案的最佳结果。相比之下，Aggarwal，Saffi和Sturgess（2015）发现，可供出售股份的供应减少，投票权价格在投票记录日期当天上升。他们得出结论，投资者的偏好激励投票交易 - 对提案特别偏爱的投资者限制可供给行使投票权的供应。这些实证研究使用股票级别的汇总贷款信息，但却没有考虑投资者的异质性。 这个提案试图收集股权共同基金证券借贷的新数据集，这样我们可以识别哪些股权共同基金在将其持有证券借给卖空者。如我收集的数据所示，大约一半的股权共同基金参与证券借贷（图1）。该数据集允许我探讨证券借贷和股东在基金级别投票的相互作用。具体来说，我打算调查（1）证券借贷收入是否阻碍共同基金通过股东投票施加治理的意愿; （2）股东投票影响治理的机制。 该项目通过发现证券借贷对公司治理的意想不到的后果，扩充我们对相关领域的理解。此外，该项目还将为政府决策者如何监管证券借贷和股东投票提供一些独到的见解。

25508417.label: Major findings and research outcome
25508417.value: In the working paper completed based on this project, titled "Are passive investors also passive voters? Evidence from securities lending by mutual funds", is under review at Management Science. The abstract of the paper: I study the effect of mutual funds’ securities lending activities on their participation in proxy voting using hand-collected fund securities lending data. Consistent with Shleifer and Vishny’s (1986) argument that a shareholder’s willingness to monitor a firm decreases as the cost of monitoring increases, I find that mutual funds that lend securities are less likely to vote in the shareholder meetings of their portfolio firms. The negative effect is weaker if a fund holds a larger stake in the stock, especially poorly performing stocks, suggesting that lending funds are more likely to give up securities lending income and recall stocks to vote when the potential gains from voting are greater. This negative effect of securities lending on voting participation is also weaker if other funds in the same fund family are active voters. Although securities lending impedes fund voting on average, I find that it increases fund voting, due to a “lock-in” effect, in a subset of fund families in which funds are restricted from selling upon short-selling signals and vote more actively.

25508517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25508517.value: Anecdotal evidence and prior research suggest that the need to acquire human capital could motivate firms to undertake mergers and acquisitions (M&As) (Coff 2002; Ouimet and Zarutskie 2011). But the literature has given little thought to the consideration of synergies that can be achieved through efficient allocation of human resources. This project aims to provide direct evidence on human capital synergies in M&As, with particular emphasis on synergies from patent inventors. I propose to study whether and how inventor synergies affect merger pairing, inventor retention, and post-merger innovation and accounting performance. Inventors contribute to innovation outputs several times greater than firm-level factors do (Liu et al. 2016). As such, inventor synergies can be substantial for M&As. Takeovers break firm boundaries and eliminate frictions that hinder knowledge diffusion, and thereby reduce the costs of collaboration between the acquirer’s inventors and the target’s inventors. Inventor collaboration in the merged firm boosts innovation and contributes to merger synergies. Prior social network studies posit that connections based on past co-authorships facilitate the formation of new collaboration (Fafchamps et al. 2010). Accordingly, firms that are more closely connected through their inventors’ collaboration prior to the merger can expect greater synergies. Thus, I predict that pre-merger inventor connections will be positively associated with the incidence of deal between a connected pair, the likelihood of a particular inventor (target) being retained, and post-merger invention outcomes and profitability. I will follow the innovation literature (e.g., Singh 2005) and use the U.S. patent inventor data provided by UC Berkeley’s Fung Institute for Engineering Leadership to construct a patent inventor collaborative network based on pre-merger co-authorship ties. I will employ three main tests to examine the relation between pre-merger inventor connections and merger pairing, inventor retention, and post-merger innovation and accounting performance, respectively. I will account for endogeneity using a quasi-exogenous setting that involves failed M&As for reasons unrelated to innovation. This project can contribute to the M&A synergy literature by incorporating human capital into the playground. I expect to provide evidence that inventor synergies are incremental to the synergies in the areas of product market, technology, and organizational capital; and to convey the message that acquirer-target connections through past inventor collaboration contribute to greater value creation in M&As. Moreover, this project will add to human capital research in finance and accounting, a subject that has received much less attention than other intangible assets due to difficulties of measuring human capital. 摘要 公司通過收購或兼並來實現協同效應 (Bradley et al. 1988)。由收購或兼並產生的協同效應可以出現在產品市場，技術和組織資本等方面 (例如，Hoberg and Phillips 2010)。軼事證據和過往的研究發現對人力資源的需求是公司進行收購或兼並的驅動力之一 (Coff 2002; Ouimet and Zarutskie 2011)，但是現有文獻極少涉及從人力資本的有效配置而產生的協同效應。此研究項目旨在通過著眼於一類在創新中起到重要作用的特定員工—專利發明者，而提出關於從人力資本而來的協同效應的直接證據。 在收購或兼並中，從專利發明者而產生的協同效應是可觀的。收購打破了公司之間的界限，從而減少了收購公司和被收購公司之間知識流通和專利發明者合作的障礙。創新在很大程度上需要依靠團隊合作。在合並後的公司裏，專利發明者之間合作的增加可以推動創新，協同效應由此產生。以往關於社會網絡的研究發現建立在從前合作基礎上的社交關系能促成新的合作 (Fafchamps et al. 2010)。因此，我預測若公司之間有更多通過專利發明者在並購前的合作建立的聯系，則有望在收購或兼並中實現更大的協同效應。此項目將研究從專利發明者而來的協同效應能否影響收購公司對被收購對象的選擇和收購公司對被收購公司旗下的專利發明者的續聘決定，以及在多大程度上由專利發明者而來的協同效應能增強合並後的公司在創新和財務方面的業績。 為了研究從專利發明者而來的協同效應，我將會根據現有的創新文獻 (例如, Singh 2005)，使用the UC Berkeley Fung Institute提供的美國專利發明者數據來建立一個基於並購前合著關系的專利發明者合作網絡。我將通過三個主要的測試來研究以下問題：(1) 收購公司是否更願意收購一間在專利發明者合著方面與它有著更多聯系的公司；(2) 被收購公司的專利發明者與收購公司的專利發明者之間的合作關系是否增加他/她留在合並後的公司的可能性；(3) 收購公司和被收購公司之間的聯系是否增強合並後的公司的創新成果和利潤率。我還將通過使用一個包含了非創新相關因素導致的收購或兼並失敗案例的擬外生設定來控制可能存在的內生性問題。 對上述問題的研究可以從三個方面對現有文獻做出貢獻。首先，此項目將著眼於收購或兼並的一個重要方面—人力資本，來探索一種協同效應的新來源。我預期通過此項目提出關於從人力資本而來的協作效應的證據。其次，此項目將發現收購公司和被收購公司之間基於專利發明者合作的聯系是合並後的公司創新業績的一項重要決定因素，從而拓展現有的創新文獻。再次，此項目可以增加我們對於社會網絡相關文獻中的一個核心議題—人際關系如何促進知識擴散和產生經濟價值—的理解。最後，此項目將增添會計和金融領域中現有過少的關於人力資本的研究。

25508517.label: Realisation of objectives
25508517.value: This research project was originally titled “Achieving Human Capital Synergies: Inventor Collaborative Connections and M&A Performance”. The following activities were carried out to achieve the original research objectives: (1) data collection: I obtained and consolidated the CRSP-matched patent data from Kogan et al. (2017) and other sources. In addition, the data on patent inventor name (disambiguated) were collected from Google Patents Public Datasets and Harvard Dataverse-Patent Network Dataverse. (2) constructing key variables: the disambiguated inventor dataset, which contains patent number and disambiguated inventor ID, were used to identify the co-authorship ties and construct the inventor collaboration network. Three key network measures were computed: (1) weighted tie count (the sum of co-authorship ties between a pair of firms); (2) closeness (the distance of the shortest path between a pair of firms); (3) centrality (the importance of a firm in the inventor collaboration network). (3) literature review and hypothesis improvement: after reviewing the innovation literature and the literature on knowledge diffusion in the social network literature, the hypotheses were better developed. (4) empirical analyses: the three network measures constructed were used to test the three research questions specified as the original research objectives. However, in the later stage of working on this research project, I discovered an existing study on a similar topic, titled “Inter-firm Inventor Collaboration and Path-breaking Innovation: Evidence from Inventor Teams Post-merger” and accepted by Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis. That study also focuses on inter-firm inventor collaboration in the M&A setting and finds evidence consistent with the collaboration between acquirer and target inventors leading to better post-merger innovation performance. The large overlap between this research project and that study made it hard for me to further pursue the original research objectives, because the originality of these research objectives has largely been lost due to the existence of a similar study that has moved further ahead into the publication process, causing the chance of publishing any resulting output to plunge. Therefore, the focus of this research project had to be redirected to a new and different aspect of human capital. Specifically, I examined in the revised study whether employee turnover is informative about future firm performance, a fundamental question on the relation between human capital and firm performance. The following revised objectives have been fully achieved in the revised study: 1) to examine whether employee turnover is informative about future firm performance. 2) to examine firm and labor market factors that likely affect the relation between employee turnover and firm performance. 3) to examine whether investors fully incorporate the information contained in employee turnover into stock prices. The primary activities conducted to achieve the objectives include: 1) data preparation, sample construction, and variable measurement: we used in this study a large panel of employee turnover data extracted from employees’ online profiles. The key measure is employee turnover for a quarter, calculated by aggregating monthly employee separations over the quarter and then scaling the total separations by the average monthly employee count for that quarter. The final sample consists of 3,612 distinct firms and 85,334 firm-quarter observations, representing all Fama-French 12 industries. 2) empirical tests: we first conducted the main test to examine the relation between employee turnover and future firm performance measured as one-quarter ahead return on assets and sales growth, and then ran the following tests: • Robustness tests, to show that the relation found in the main test is not sensitive to the inclusion of additional controls and fixed effects. • Cross-sectional tests to investigate factors that affect the turnover-performance relation, including firm size, firm age, labor intensity, local labor supply, and whether the firm needs to replace departing employees. • Additional test to explore the possible nonlinearity of the relation documented. • Additional test to examine whether employee turnover is informative about the uncertainty of firm performance measured as the standard deviation of future ROA. • Additional test to examine whether investors fully incorporate turnover information into stock prices by checking the predictability of employee turnover for returns around the next quarter earnings announcement. 3) writing and circulating for feedback: after empirical tests had been finished, the paper was written and presented at seminars at universities/conferences including the National University of Singapore, the University of California Irvine, the University of California Los Angeles, and the University of Illinois at Chicago, etc.. 4) journal submission and acceptance: the paper was submitted to and accepted by Management Science. Meanwhile, we submitted comment letters based on the findings of the paper to the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and the International Accounting Standards Board (IASB). The SEC cited this paper in the final rule for Modernization of Regulation S-K Items 101, 103, and 105, which became effective on November 9, 2020, to support the inclusion of required disclosure of certain human capital metrics in the final amendments to Item 101(c).

25508517.label: Major findings and research outcome
25508517.value: The main findings are: (1) employee turnover is negatively associated with future firm performance (one-quarter ahead return on assets and sales growth). (2) the negative association between employee turnover and future firm performance is stronger for small firms, for young firms, for firms with low labor intensity, when the local labor market is tight, and when the firm is trying to replace departing employees. (3) the negative association between employee turnover and future firm performance disappears when turnover is very low, suggesting that a certain amount of employee turnover can be beneficial. (4) there is a significantly positive association between employee turnover and the uncertainty of future firm performance, which is consistent with the concern that employee turnover increases operational uncertainty. (5) employee turnover positively predicts future stock returns, suggesting that investors do not fully incorporate information contained in employee turnover.

25508517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25508517.value: Further studies could explore the relation between human capital and firm performance in a specific domain of firm activities, for instance, the relation between the turnover of R&D personnel and a firm’s innovation performance.

25508517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25508517.value: Employee turnover is a significant cost for businesses and a key human capital metric that is of great investor interest, but firms do not disclose this measure. Using a large panel of turnover data extracted from employees’ online profiles, this study documents that employee turnover is informative about future firm performance but investors do not fully incorporate turnover information. This paper contributes to the research on the relationship between human capital and firm outcomes by studying the implications of employee turnover for future financial performance and studying how firm and labor market factors affect the turnover-performance relationship. In addition, the findings of this paper answer the call from the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) for evidence on the importance of turnover disclosure to investors and are cited by the SEC in the final rule for Modernization of Regulation S-K Items 101, 103, and 105, which became effective on November 9, 2020, to support the inclusion of required disclosure of certain human capital metrics in the final amendments to Item 101(c).

25508617.value: 節假日之前的注意力缺失和投資回報

25508617.label: Project Objectives
25508617.value: To test whether investors pay less attention to financial market (indicated by fewer orders submitted and longer Time-to-Cancellation) on trading days before holidays. To examine the heterogeneity of pre-holiday effects among different investor types and among individual investors with various levels of cognitive limitation. To investigate whether the limited attention caused by pre-holiday distraction is associated with poor investment performance.

25508617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25508617.value: Previous literature has shown that investors have limited attention on Fridays, which contributes to an underreaction to Friday’s earnings announcements and a larger post-announcement drift (Dellavigna and Pollet, 2009). This project aims to extend the literature by investigating the effect of limited attention on the quality of investment decisions and investment performance. Specifically, I intend to explore the investors’ order submission and cancellation decisions as well as the return of executed orders during the days immediately before holidays. Taking advantage of the order submission, execution, and cancellation records in the Taiwan Futures Exchange (TAIFEX), I infer the investors’ attention from a) the number of orders submitted and b) the Time-to-Cancellation of the limit orders that are not successfully executed. In TAIFEX, if investors actively monitor their limit orders, they could timely cancel their unexecuted orders; otherwise, these orders would become stale after staying in the market for a long period of time (Linnainmaa, 2010). For investors who do not actively monitor the market, it may take longer time for them to cancel their stale orders. Thus, the time interval from limit order submission to cancellation indicates the inattention of investors. The uniqueness of our data allows us to explore the heterogeneity of the pre-holiday effect among various investors. To the extent that the pre-holiday distraction reflects investors’ inadequate discipline over their own cognitive resources, I hypothesize that the professional institutional investors and the more sophisticated retail investors are less affected by the pre-holiday distraction. Retail investors who have low cognitive ability, on the other hand, are expected to pay less attention to the financial market on pre-holiday trading days. Furthermore, this project intends to diagnose the poor performance of retail investors by investigating the impact of pre-holiday inattention. Previous papers have shown that retail investors have worse performance compared to institutional investors. I will test whether institutional investors outperform retail investors by a larger margin on days before holidays. In addition, I will explore whether the retail investors with better cognitive ability outperform those with lower cognitive ability by a larger margin on those pre-holiday trading days. 摘要 之前的文獻發現投資人在周五會出現注意力缺失的現象，這種現象使得周五的收益公告得不到市場的充分反映，並且導致收益公告後漂移的現象(Dellavigna and Pollet, 2009)。本項研究的目標是探索注意力缺失對投資決策和投資回報的影響。我會研究節假日之前投資人的下單和撤單行為，以及成交的訂單的回報。 本項目利用台灣期貨交易市場的下單，成交和撤單記錄來衡量投資人的注意力缺失：1）投資人的下單數量，2）投資人撤銷未成功成交的限價單所花的時間。在台灣期貨交易市場，如果投資人積極監控他們的限價單，當市場發生變化時他們可以及時撤銷未成交的訂單；反之，如果這些未成交的訂單在市場中存在太久，就會變得過時(Linnainmaa, 2010)。那些不能積極監控訂單的投資人，他們會等更久的時間撤銷過時的訂單。因此，下單和撤單之間的時間差可以描述一個投資人是否發生了注意力缺失。 我採用的數據的特殊性在於，它可用來探索節假日之前對投資人影響的異質性。如果節假日之前的注意力缺失是來自於投資人沒有足夠的認知能力，那麼機構投資人和更加有智慧的個體投資者應該會比較少的受到節假日的影響而分心。另一方面，那些認知能力比較差的個體投資人會在節假日之前將更少的注意力放在股市上。 此外，此項研究旨在通過探索節假日之前的注意力缺失為個體投資人的低迴報做出診斷。之前的文獻指出，相比機構投資人而言，個體投資人的整體回報比較差。本項研究會測試個體投資人和機構投資人的回報差距是否在節假日之前更為顯著。另外，我還會研究更加有智慧的投資人和認知能力較差的投資人，他們之間的回報差距是否在節假日之前更加明顯。

25508617.label: Realisation of objectives
25508617.value: In the two-year project, I have made the effort to clean up the quote and trade data and have done some analyses along with the project objectives. I have written a research paper using the analyzed data, and presented the paper in several conferences and research seminars. The paper is now under review at the Financial Analysts Journal. 1. Data Preparation 1.1 Data Cleaning The analysis on investor inattention largely relies on the order submission, order cancellation, and order execution information in Taiwan Futures Exchange (TAIFEX). Thus, I have spent some time to collect and clean up the data obtained from TAIFEX. Since the data contains the entire records of quotes and trades in TAIFEX, the size of the data is really big, and a significant amount of time has been spent to process the data cleaning. To gauge the lack of order monitoring due to limited attention, the information on order submission time and order cancellation time is particularly important. However, such information is in two separate databases: the TAIFEX order submission data and the TAIFEX execution data. For orders that are executed, TAIFEX execution data shows the information on execution time. For orders that are not executed right away and are voluntarily canceled by investors, the TAIFEX execution data shows that information on cancellation time. For orders that are failed as unfilled by the end of the day, TAIFEX order submission date still keeps a record of order submission, but the TAIFEX order execution data does not have any related execution information. I have matched each quote with its corresponding transaction (either successfully executed or canceled voluntarily by investors) by trading date, product ID, investor order submission number, investor account ID, and investor broker ID. The time interval between order submission and cancellation is defined as Time-to-cancellation, which is the main measure for investor inattention. Although only those orders that are canceled can be used to calculate the inattention measure, the actual execution of orders is important to generate inferences of investor profitability. Thus, I keep both the order cancelation and execution records for further analyses. 1.2 Collecting Data on Holidays in Taiwan. In order to gauge the investor inattention before holidays, I have collected data on holidays in Taiwan. TAIFEX is closed on both Saturdays and Sundays. In addition, TAIFEX observes break on nine official public holidays during the year. These holidays include: New Year's Day, Chinese New Year's Eve, Spring Festival, 228 Peace Memorial Day, Children's Day, Labor Day, Dragon Boat Festival, Mid-Autumn Festival, and National Day. I marked the trading days right before the weekend and public holidays to test the pre-holiday order submission and cancellation behaviors accordingly. 1.3 Variable construction I have calculated the investor level investor inattention measure, Time-to-cancellation, based on the average time interval from order submission to order cancellation. I then followed Kuo, Lin, and Zhao (2015) to quantify levels of financial sophistication among retail investors. Specifically, I calculated the investor-level cognitive ability measure is the proportion of limit orders submitted at the round number prices. Both measures for investor inattention and the cognitive ability are first calculated for each order and then averaged up (both equal-weighted and dollar-weighted) for each investor. 2. Empirical Analyses The biggest challenge to the empirical analysis is the size of the data, since I employ the entire quotes and trades data in TAIFEX. Some of the data was lost during the social unrest in 2019, when PolyU was one of the major disaster areas. I had to re-transfer the data from my coauthor from Taiwan and redo a section of the analysis. The Covid-19 shortly after that also slowed the data analysis, because I had to work from home using my laptop which is not as high-performing as the computers on Campus. Nevertheless, I managed to finish the project and submitted the paper to peer-reviewed journals. The proposed Objectives are as follows: Objectives 1: To test whether investors pay less attention to financial market (indicated by fewer orders submitted and longer Time-to-Cancellation) on trading days before holidays. This objective is 100% accomplished. To accomplish Objectives 1, I examined the trading volume and the Time-to-cancellation on days before the holidays. I did not find significant findings in my Mid-term Report, because my first RA was careless in classifying the holidays. I asked her to redo the data collection and I collected the holiday information myself and do a cross-check of the holiday information collected by the RA. The new data collected is more accurate, and I have found significant results using the new data set. Although the TAIFEX does not experience a very significant increase in trading volume, yet, the Time-to-cancellation is significantly higher on Fridays and on days immediately before public holidays. The effect of a public holiday is 60% larger than a normal weekend. Objectives 2: To examine the heterogeneity of pre-holiday effects among different investor types and among retail investors with various levels of cognitive ability. This objective is 100% accomplished. To accomplish Objectives 2, I have performed empirical analyses to investigate the investor inattention and its relation to cognitive ability. Specifically, I separated the investors into two groups: institutional investors (those that arguably have the high cognitive ability) and retail investors (those that arguably have the low cognitive ability). The results show that retail investors have longer Time-to-cancellation compared with institutional investors. I further perform a regression analysis of the investor-level Time-to-Cancellation and the cognitive ability measure in Kuo, Lin, and Zhao (2015). The results show that investors with low cognitive ability have longer Time-to-cancellation. Objectives 3: To investigate whether the limited attention caused by pre-holiday distraction is associated with poor investment performance. This objective is 100% accomplished. To accomplish Objectives 3, I have performed regression analyses to investigate the association between investor attention and its relation to investment performance. Time-to-cancelation is negatively related to investment performance for retail investors, after controlling for several factors that are known to be related to investment performance, such as cognitive limitation, trading experience, etc. I also show that, if investors can overcome the limited attention and cancel the stalest limit orders in time, their performance and be improved. 3. Paper Writing I have written the findings into a research paper on investor attention. (Some of the None-findings such as the trading volume part are neglected for concision of the paper.) There are several papers on investor attention that just got published in the year of 2018 (after the original ECS proposal is approved), and I have incorporated them into the literature review section. 4. Research Dissemination I have discussed the findings of this project with researchers when they come to visit our school. I have also benefited from the feedback and constructive comments from researchers in conferences and seminars. The paper has got the Best Paper Award in the 2019 Camphor Conference for Finance. 5. Funding Expensed: A research assistant has been hired to help cleaning and to process the data. Besides, since the data is very big, I have purchased two hard drives to store and transfer the data. I also spend some money on conferences and seminars.

25508617.label: Major findings and research outcome
25508617.value: I have written a paper that investigates the association between limited attention and investment performance. The paper was presented at the following conferences and seminars: • International Conference on Management and Education, July 4-7, 2019, Tokyo. • Camphor Conference for Finance, May 25-26, 2019, Wuhan. • ICAFEL Conference, April 22-23, 2019, Nanjing. • Research Seminar at Fudan University, November 2019, Shanghai. The paper was awarded the Best Paper Award in Camphor Conference for Finance, May 25-26, 2019, Wuhan. The major findings are as follows: Taking advantage of the order submission, execution, and cancellation records in the Taiwan Futures Exchange (TAIFEX), I infer the investors' attention from the Time-to-Cancellation of the limit orders that are not successfully executed. If investors actively monitor their limit orders, they could timely cancel their unexecuted orders; otherwise, these orders would become stale after staying in the market for a long period of time (Linnainmaa, 2010). We show that Time-to-Cancellation is shorter in days with more extreme market conditions but longer on Fridays and on days immediately before public holidays. Based on a measure of investor-level inattention, we find that the investor-level inattention is persistent and related to other investor characteristics such as lower cognitive abilities, less trading experience, and more disposition effect. We find a negative relationship between individual investor inattention and investment performance. Individual investors with longer time-to-cancelation, i.e., less attentive to the market, experience significantly lower intraday, 1-day, and 5-day returns. A two-stage regression approach helps mitigate the potential concern of confounding factors affecting the investor attention and performance at the same time. Furthermore, we show that investor performance and improve if the stale limit orders are canceled in time. These results suggest that inattention hurts individual investors' performance. Nevertheless, our paper suggests that there is room for financial education to improve the investment efficiency of individual investors, as we show that they can learn from their past trading experience and become more attentive to the execution process.

25508617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25508617.value: As the welfare of individual investors is of great importance to researchers and policymakers, we think it necessary to investigate how they behave in financial markets and the associated consequences. Based on a measure of investor-level inattention, we find that the investor-level inattention is persistent and related to other investor characteristics such as cognitive limitation. It is possible that the investors' behavioral biases are also affected by their attention allocation. As a follow-up project, I am examining whether the behavioral biases are stronger on Fridays and on days immediately before holidays. Examples of behavioral biases include but not restricted to the herding behavior, disposition behavior, self-reinforcement behavior, superstition behavior, etc. Abnormally strong behavioral biases of individual investors on those days may lead to price distortions, which will affect the social welfare of various market participants.

25508617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25508617.value: To the best of our knowledge, our paper is the first study to identify the association between the individual investors' attention in the execution process and their investment performance. The previous literature presents mixed evidence on the effect of attention for searching for information (Da, Engelberg, and Gao, 2011; Gargano and Rossi, 2018). Using a novel brokerage account data set, Gargano and Rossi (2018) investigate how individual investors search for information online and whether the searching effort contributes to superior performance. Our paper calls for attention to another aspect of limited attention, i.e., failing to cancel the stale limit orders in time. Lack of monitoring may leave the order being picked up by more sophisticated investors when new information shocks hit the market. Further, our paper conducts a cross-sectional study of investor attention and documents the heterogeneity in the attention limitation as well as investment outcomes. Some investors persistently pay less attention than others. Some investors can learn from their trading experience and become more attentive to the order execution process. In this sense, our paper provides important implications for individual investors to improve their trading prowess and welfare benefits in the financial market.

25508817.value: 審計師的政治貢獻和SEC對審計師的執法

25508817.label: Project Objectives
25508817.value: To construct a dataset on auditors’ political contributions in the United States including the campaign contribution made and lobbying expenditure incurred by each audit firm. To describe and discuss auditors’ campaign contributions and lobbying expenditures over time in the United States. To investigate whether auditor’s political contributions affect SEC enforcement/lawsuits decisions against auditors and the related settlements.
rows: To construct a dataset on auditors’ political contributions in the United States including the campaign contribution made and lobbying expenditure incurred by each audit firm.
To describe and discuss auditors’ campaign contributions and lobbying expenditures over time in the United States.
To investigate whether auditor’s political contributions affect SEC enforcement/lawsuits decisions against auditors and the related settlements.

25508817.label: Realisation of objectives
25508817.value: All the three objectives are fully realized. Specifically, Our sample consists of all SEC enforcement actions (specifically, the AAERs) for U.S. firms’ financial misrepresentation from January 1, 2001 to December 31, 2016. We manually identify the observations in which the firm’s auditor is also named in the AAER. We next collect PAC contributions from the Federal Election Commission’s (FEC) website and lobbying data from Center for Responsive Politics (CRP), which has compiled lobbying information from the semi-annual lobbying reports filed with the Secretary of the SOPR since 1998. (objective 1). We also conduct a thorough description and discussion of auditors’ campaign contributions and lobbying expenditures over time in the United States. (Objective 2) We first examine how PAC contributions and the lobby expenditures affect the likelihood of auditor being named in the AAER and find that the amount of PAC contributions and lobby expenses spent by audit firms are associated with lower probability of SEC enforcement actions against auditors. We further identify the PAC contributions and lobby activities linked to SEC and find that the likelihood of AAER against auditors is further reduced if the audit firm’s lobby expenses are related to SEC. (objective 3) We next examine whether the auditors having political connections are less likely to be imposed harsher penalties in the actions naming an auditor as a defendant. Following Kedia et al. (2018), we build up a penalty score to measure the strength of the penalties against auditors. Specifically, we focus on the following three types of the penalties against auditors, denial of privilege (including temporary and permanent), cease and desist order and a censure. Among the three types, denial of privilege is the most severe penalty, followed by cease and desist order and censure. We do not find the significant association between total PAC contributions/ (lobbying expenditures) and the milder penalties against auditors, but find that only the PAC contributions and lobbying expenditures linked to the SEC are associated with the milder penalties, indicating that the political connections lobbying activities can influence the penalty decisions of the SEC if those connections are directly related to SEC, as well as the decisions whether to charge the auditors in the actions. We also conduct some additional tests to rule out alternative explanations to our results. (Objective 3).

25508817.label: Major findings and research outcome
25508817.value: By examining how PAC contributions and the lobby expenditures affect the likelihood of auditor being named in the AAER, we find that the amount of PAC contributions and lobby expenses spent by audit firms are associated with lower probability of SEC enforcement actions against auditors. We further identify the PAC contributions and lobby activities linked to SEC and find that the likelihood of AAER against auditors is further reduced if the audit firm’s lobby expenses are related to SEC. We do not find the significant association between total PAC contributions/ (lobbying expenditures) and the milder penalties against auditors, but find that only the PAC contributions and lobbying expenditures linked to the SEC are associated with the milder penalties, indicating that the political connections lobbying activities can influence the penalty decisions of the SEC if those connections are directly related to SEC, as well as the decisions whether to charge the auditors in the actions. This project has been presented in seminars and major conferences as mentioned in Part C, and will be submitted to a top Accounting journal in a month.

25508817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25508817.value: Auditors play an important role in the capital market with their reputations for integrity and independence. It seems that auditors are more and more heavily involved in political activities. Prior studies find that firms having political connections obtain favorable treatment when engaging in fraud , suggesting that such firms benefit from political rent-seeking activities, although these findings may not be generalizable to audit firms. Thus, it is important to understand whether auditors benefit from political connections. This paper has examined the influence of political contributions on the SEC enforcement decisions against auditor, but I construct a dataset on auditors’ political contributions in the United States including the campaign contribution made and lobbying expenditure incurred by each audit firm. This dataset will be used for some future studies that examine the benefit(or cost) of auditor's political contributions from different aspects, such as (but not limited to) the effect of auditor political contributions on private litigations against auditors.

25508817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25508817.value: Using the setting of SEC regulatory enforcements against auditors, we empirically examine the two stages of the regulatory process: the decision to initiate an enforcement and the penalties related to the enforcement. Specifically, using hand collected data of SEC enforcement against auditors, political action committee (PAC) contributions and lobby expenses spent by the audit firms, and penalties imposed on the audit firms by the SEC, we find auditor’s political connections reduce the likelihood of SEC enforcement against auditors and the amount of penalties incurred by the enforcements. This study provides evidence on whether political connections add value to audit firms which has indications on how political connections affect auditor’s incentives. This study shows that auditor’s relationship with the regulatory agencies affect the decisions on enforcement against auditors.

25602517.label: Project Title(Chinese)
25602517.value: 中國實習、非正規就業與職業技能培訓

25602517.label: Project Objectives
25602517.value: Understand work and training experiences from the perspective of student interns in China’s changing state-labor-capital relations. Inform contemporary analyses of skill upgrading and labor informalization through comprehensive research on student internships in China. Generate information that could contribute to enhancing the quality of China’s vocational education and training and the protection of student interns’ rights.
