26100617.label: Major findings and research outcome
26100617.value: We have characterized the free swimming strike in larval zebrafish and have used that information to develop a head fixed strike paradigm, which allows us for the first time to study the final phase of prey capture while controlling the visual stimulus and conducting functional imaging. We also pioneered the use of a UV capable projector to evoke prey capture behavior and strikes, and found that this method is far superior to commercial projectors. We further characterized the dependence of prey capture behavior on stimulus wavelength, and found that UV stimuli evoke much more behavior than blue, green or red wavelenghts. Moreover, prey capture in response to blue and green wavelenghths is mediated by UV cones. We developed a novel head-fixed preparation for strike behavior, and showed that we could observe the previously described signature of the strike in the preparation, and use these to objectively analyze the behavior. By manipulating the distance between the larva and the screen, we showed that we can recapitulate the distance dependence of prey capture using artificial stimuli and identify the cues to trigger the stike. These results are currently being prepared for publication as mentioned in Part C. Our monocular vs. binocular imaging experiments have allowed us to identify neurons that are activated specifically by binocular presentation of prey stimuli, and we are doing further experiments to identify the functional and behavioral roles of these neurons.

26100617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26100617.value: We are working to identify the functional role of the binocular neurons we identified. We will ask whether binocular information provides these neurons with more information about prey location. Another type of analysis will combine behavioral and imaging recordings to ask whether the neurons are correlated with prey capture behavior or more sensory in nature. We will also use the UV projector in conjunction with the eyeblocker to determine whether strikes are evoked in the monocular condition, and study the neural correlates of this behavior.

26100617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26100617.value: The mechanism of visual depth perception remains mysterious in humans and other animals. Using larval zebrafish as a model system with easy access to functional imaging, we developed a method to study how they capture prey, a process that requires distance estimation. We also found neurons that are specifically activated when they get input from the two eyes, and are studying how they use this information. This line of research will shed light on how all binocular animals process this incoming information.

26100917.value: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) belong to a class of small non-coding RNAs (approximately 22 nucleotides) which are present in virtually all plants and animals. To date, thousands of miRNAs have been found in a variety of organisms, including ~ 2500 miRNAs in humans. They have been demonstrated to participate in the regulation of critical cellular processes and associated with a wide range of pathological conditions. Therefore, the proper expression and sequence fidelity of miRNAs, which are largely governed by miRNA biogenesis, must be achieved for their normal functions in cells. The miRNA biogenesis is a multiple-step process in which precursors of miRNAs or pri-miRNAs are initially cleaved by a complex, called Microprocessor. This step is believed to significantly contribute to the accuracy of miRNA expression and sequence fidelity. Our latest work has established an innovative molecular mechanism of Microprocessor, elucidating the way it ensures the efficient and precise processing of pri-miRNAs. The studies have not only addressed numerous critical questions but also revealed different aspects of the mechanism of Microprocessor. Microprocessor turns out to be a trimeric complex of one DROSHA and DGCR8 dimer. Within the complex, DROSHA acts as a “ruler” that recognizes the basal junction and measures one helical turn (~ 11 bp) from the junction on pri-miRNAs. DGCR8 dimer otherwise interacts with the apical loop of pri-miRNAs, including the UGU motif, to precisely locate and orient Microprocessor on pri-miRNAs. However, how does DGCR8 recognize the apical loop with the UGU motif? In addition, how do cells regulate miRNA expression through manipulating Microprocessor activity? This proposal study aims to unveil the architecture of the DGCR8-UGU interaction and eventually addresses two above-mentioned questions by utilizing multiple approaches such as biochemistry, integrated UV-crosslinking with mass-spectrometry, and crystallography. Here are three specific issues we want to investigate and have also gained some preliminary promising data, including: 1. The potential UGU-binding motif in DGCR8. 2.The expression of miRNAs in vivo are likely differentiated according to the presence of UGU in miRNA precursors. 3.The possible involvement of a small molecule, such as hemin, in regulating the interaction between UGU and DGCR8, resulting in the differential miRNA expressions. 26100917.label: Major findings and research outcome
26100917.value: - In this study, we demonstrated that Rhed (i.e., the RNA-binding heme domain, amino acids 285–478) of DGCR8 interacts with UGU. In addition, we identified three amino acids 461–463 in Rhed, which are critical for the UGU interaction and essential for Microprocessor to accurately and efficiently process UGU-pri-miRNAs in vitro and UGU-miRNA expression in human cells. Furthermore, we found that within the DGCR8 dimer, the amino acids 461–463 from one monomer can discriminate between UGU- and noUGU-pri-miRNAs. - We find that hemin, a ferric iron-containing porphyrin, enhances the specific interaction between the apical UGU motif and the DGCR8 dimer, allowing Microprocessor to achieve high efficiency and fidelity of primiRNA processing in vitro. Furthermore, by generating a DGCR8 mutant cell line and carrying out rescue experiments, we discover that hemin preferentially stimulates the expression of miRNAs possessing the UGU motif, thereby conferring differential regulation of miRNA maturation. - Our findings improve the current understanding of the substrate-recognizing mechanism of DGCR8 and implicate the roles of this recognition in differentiating miRNA expression in human cells. In addition, we reveal the molecular action mechanism of hemin in pri-miRNA processing and establish a novel function of hemin in inducing specific RNA-protein interaction.

26100917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26100917.value: - Hemin level is known to be fluctuated during red blood cell differentiation and in some diseases. It is interesting to see how the hemin level changes affect the miRNA expression in these contexts. - DGCR8 is subjected to many types of protein modifications; therefore, it is also essential to study any change occurring in the UGU-interacting amino acids identified in our study in any cellular contexts or human diseases. These potential changes will further show the physiological functions of these amino acids. - Pri-miRNAs can also be modified by multiple mechanisms such as single nucleotide polymorphisms, RNA editing, or somatic mutations. These mechanisms might alter the UGU motif, affecting miRNA expression via controlling DGCR8-UGU interaction. Thus, it is essential to identify any changes in the UGU motif by any mechanisms, as mentioned above, in any cellular contexts or human diseases.

26100917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26100917.value: Typical actions of genes in our bodies determine our adequate growth, development, gender, ages, and healthiness. If the genes abnormally function, we might face many problems in developing diseases. microRNAs (miRNAs) play essential roles in controlling most of the genes' proper actions in our bodies. Therefore, the adequate activities of miRNAs must be archived for the normal gene functions. Our study focuses on understanding how miRNAs are produced in human cells by a microprocessor complex. This study reveals how this enzyme interacts with the miRNA precursors and cooperates with a small molecule, called hemin, to produce precise amounts and sequences of miRNAs. Our study reveals the fundamental mechanisms of miRNA production. Besides, it provides a foundation to develop any therapeutic approaches to control and restore the abnormal miRNA expression to a proper level by manipulating Microprocessor activity via small molecules such as hemin or its derivatives.

26101117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26101117.value: Enormous progress in single-molecule fluorescence techniques allows researchers to observe movements and interactions of single proteins. We built a state-of-the-art real-time three-dimensional (3D) nanometer-accuracy tracking microscope at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, which enables us to track a single synaptic vesicle (40 nm in diameter) containing a brighter quantum dot with ~20-nm accuracy in the x-y plane and with ~30-nm accuracy along the z-axis, at 10 Hz imaging frequency in three dimensions in real time. Using this microscope, we can observe the movement of single synaptic vesicles up to the moment of exocytosis, and we can directly monitor the fusion mode of vesicles in live neurons. We found that synaptic vesicles from the readily releasable pool (RRP) of most excitatory synapses reside close to their fusion site, and that the fusion mode depends upon the location of a vesicle relative to the active zone, revealing the link between fusion mode and synaptic transmission. In the central nervous system, the balance between excitation and inhibition plays important roles in neuronal processes. Thus, the imbalance between excitation and inhibition is believed to contribute to several neurological disorders, including autism spectrum disorder, schizophrenia, and epilepsy. Mature GABAergic synapses are inhibitory and hyperpolarize postsynaptic neurons; in contrast, glutamatergic synapses are excitatory and depolarize postsynaptic neurons. Although GABAergic synapses play important roles in neurotransmission (including the modulation of action potential firing and synaptic strength), they have received considerably less attention compared to glutamatergic synapses. Thus, less is known about synaptic vesicles in GABAergic synapses compared to glutamatergic synapses. In this proposal, we will directly measure the exocytosis and mobility of single GABAergic synaptic vesicles (i.e., synaptic vesicles containing the neurotransmitter gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA)) in mature hippocampal and striatal rat neurons using our real-time 3D nanometer-accuracy tracking microscope as well as electron microscopy and electrophysiology measurements, and we will compare obtained results with measurements of excitatory synaptic vesicles. We will then investigate whether synaptic vesicles from the readily releasable pool (RRP) in mature GABAergic synapses are located in close proximity to their release sites (as is the case for excitatory synapses). Finally, we will measure where single GABAergic vesicles fuse. The results of this research will reveal whether and how single GABAergic vesicles differ from excitatory vesicles at the single-vesicle level. This information will advance our understanding of inhibitory synaptic vesicles and can be used to identify therapeutic targets for treating neurological disorders. 單分子熒光技術的巨大進步使研究人員能夠觀察單一蛋白質的運動和相互作用。我們在香港科技大學建立了最先進的實時三維（3D）納米精度跟踪顯微鏡，使我們能夠跟踪單個突觸小泡（直徑40納米），含有在xy平面上具有〜20-nm精度的較亮的量子點，並且在z軸處具有〜30nm的精度，在10Hz成像頻率的三維實時。使用這種顯微鏡，我們可以觀察單個突觸囊泡到胞吐時的運動，我們可以直接監測活神經元囊泡的融合模式。我們發現大多數興奮性突觸的容易釋放的池（RRP）的突觸小泡位於其融合位點附近，並且融合模式取決於囊泡相對於活性區的位置，揭示融合模式和突觸之間的聯繫傳輸。 在中樞神經系統中，激發和抑制之間的平衡在神經元過程中起重要作用。因此，激發和抑制之間的不平衡被認為有助於幾種神經障礙，包括自閉症譜系障礙，精神分裂症和癲癇。成熟的GABA能突觸是抑制性和超極化突觸後神經元;相比之下，谷氨酸能突觸是興奮性和去極化突觸後神經元。雖然GABA能突觸在神經傳遞（包括動作電位發射和突觸強度的調製）中發揮重要作用，但與穀氨酸能突觸相比，它們受到的關注較少。因此，與穀氨酸能突觸相比，GABA能突觸中的突觸小泡知之甚少。 在這個建議中，我們將使用我們的實時3D納米精度跟踪直接測量成熟海馬和紋狀體大鼠神經元中單個GABA能突觸小泡（即含有神經遞質γ-氨基丁酸（GABA）的突觸小泡）的胞吐作用和移動性顯微鏡以及電子顯微鏡和電生理測量，我們將比較獲得的結果與興奮性突觸小泡的測量。然後我們將調查來自成熟GABA能突觸中容易釋放池（RRP）的突觸小泡是否位於其釋放位置附近（如興奮性突觸的情況）。最後，我們將測量單個GABAergic囊泡融合的位置。 這項研究的結果將揭示單個GABA能囊泡是否以及如何與單囊泡水平的興奮性囊泡不同。這些信息將促進我們對抑制性突觸小泡的理解，並可用於鑑定治療神經系統疾病的治療靶點。

26200017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26200017.value: Extreme floods have a long history of being an important cause of death and destruction worldwide. It is estimated by Munich RE and Swiss RE that floods and severe storms dominate all other natural hazards globally in terms of average annual property loss and human fatalities. The top 5 most disastrous floods in the period from 1900 to 2015, ranked by economic damage, are all in the Asian monsoon region (Thailand (2011) US$40 billion, China (1998) US$30 billion, China (2010) US$18 billion, India (2014) US$16 billion and Korea (1995) US$15 billion), which highlights the importance of improving the current predictability of the spatiotemporal characteristics of flood-triggering precipitation events in the monsoon regions that have been devastating to find a solution. Southeast Asia is the area that urges such a solution, not only because of those recorded disastrous events, but also due to its future as the next economic center of gravity of the world. Various climate change projections have suggested that both the frequency and intensity of extreme precipitation events are likely to increase in the future. The associated risks of catastrophic flooding for the coastal regions, including the third global financial center, Hong Kong, are expected to further increase due to sea level rise. The proposed study aims to address these emerging problems by improving our understanding of the dynamical ocean-atmosphere system associated with such catastrophic events on different timescales, from daily to extended range, and seasonal, to support managerial and operational decision-making, from inter-annual to decadal for sustainability management, risk mitigation and adaptation. This will potentially provide significant socio-economic returns in both short- and long-term by optimizing the benefits of monsoon rainfall and reducing the impact of extreme events. This proposal is an initiative of interdisciplinary research between hydrology, atmospheric science, data science and water resources management for targeted scientific advancement. It will facilitate multi-directional integration among these fields, along with consulting engineers, to develop scientific methods for flood risk and resiliency assessment. The research is cast in a practical context using mainland China and Hong Kong as examples, where the methodological and practical relevance will be directly assessed. We anticipate that the results of the project have the potential for revolutionizing how real time water resources and climate risk management is conducted in the future, by replacing the static operational planning based criteria that are currently in vogue with a more dynamic risk assessment and management procedure. 在世界範圍內，洪水作為造成死亡與財產損失的重要誘因已有很長的歷史。慕尼黑再保險公司與瑞士再保險公司根據平均年資產與人口死亡數據評估後發現，洪水與颶風在全球範圍內主導了其他自然災害。 從1900年到2015年，造成經濟損失數額排名前5的洪澇災害都發生在亞洲季風區（泰國$400億美金（2011），中國$300億美金（1998），中國$180億美金（2010），印度$160億美金（2014），韓國$150億美金（1995））。以上事實說明，在季風區域乃至全球範圍，加深對引發毀滅性洪水的強降水的時間和空間結構的了解，對實現對降水及洪水的精確預測至關重要。 目前，眾多自然變化都暗示著極端降水的頻率和強度，在未來都將呈現上升趨勢，加之海平面上升，包括全球第三金融中心香港在內的沿海地區乃至整個東南亞，發生洪災的風險大大升高。而在不久的將來，該地區很可能成為下一個世界經濟中心，洪災必將成為阻礙該地區經濟發展的重要因素。因此，制定更為準確全面的洪水預測方案迫在眉睫。 本次研究的目標是，在不同的時間標準下，加深對於與極端洪水相關的動態海洋大氣系統的理解，以此設定與執行更加合理的洪澇災害應對決策，並將決策的可持續性由年際擴大到年代，在此基礎上將風險控制在平穩可控的範圍內。一方面優化季風降雨的效益，另一方面減少洪澇災害的影響，無論短期或長期，都將為該地區帶來顯著的社會經濟回報。 本研究內容將涉及水文地理學，大氣科學，數據科學以及水資源管理等學科，是一次有目的的學科融合與科學進步。在方法上，本研究取百家之長又與實際工程應用相結合，目的是在洪水風險預測和彈性評估上有所突破。本次研究是以中國大陸以及香港作為背景提出的，所用方法和與實際聯繫的程度將直接被進行評估。

26200017.label: Realisation of objectives
26200017.value: The proposed project objectives have been achieved. We have published four top journal articles and seven conference presentations/papers. Two students (Dai Lun and Pan Mengxin) developed their PhD theses from this project and now graduated. They are both working as postdoc research scientists in the PI's group. Another ongoing PhD student (Tat Fan Cheng) also developed his Master of Philosophy thesis from this project. Objective 1. Identifying the space-time structures of the occurrence of extreme precipitation, the occurrence of floods and the spatiotemporal association and relation between precipitation and floods using state-of-the-art data science techniques Multi-source data were used for this objective, including global flood record by the Dartmouth Flood Observatory (DFO), reanalysis meteorological data (ERA-Interim) by the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) and daily rainfall in Southeast China by China Meteorological Administration (CMA). We used the “Global Active Archive of Large Flood Events” data since 1985 to present by the DFO to extract the flood records in the entire Southeast Asia region. We established the relationship between extreme rainfall and floods using the identified flood events. We verified our hypothesis that most of these extreme floods are associated with persistent rainfall over many days. For rainfall to sustain over a large area and an extended period of time, persistent external moisture supply is essential. Therefore, this leads to the second objective. Objective 2. Developing a quantitative approach to identify and relate the causative factors of floods from a climatic perspective, by identifying the climate and atmospheric patterns that are associated with intensive and persistent precipitation We investigated the associated atmospheric circulation patterns, hotspots of moisture sources and climate indicates to quantify the relationship among flood – precipitation – moisture – climate. Multi-spatiotemporal scale mechanisms were investigated through the key phrase “moisture transport”. Built upon previous work paving to this proposal, we have one article published (Cheng et al., 2019) in the most prestigious journal Journal of Climate. It focused on the climatic regulation on the moisture transport and allocation in the EA region. To further complete this objective, we developed our own algorithm to systematically identify the flood-triggering precipitation sequences and generate moisture transport trajectories, featured by the “Atmospheric Rivers” phenomenon. The algorithm achieved unprecedented feature extractions. A journal article (Pan and Lu, 2019) is published in the journal Water Resources Research. We have received positive and encouraging comments, and rapid growth of citation. We are also extending our collaboration work based on this algorithm. We also published another paper (Pan and Lu, 2020) based on the big data constructed by this algorithm. Objective 3. Establishing a statistical framework based on the physical mechanisms that are learnt from the first two steps with suitable statistical and data mining tools Given the mechanisms and enhanced moisture transport path identified by (Cheng et al., 2019; Pan and Lu, 2019), we used an unsupervised data mining algorithm, the self-organizing map (SOM), to extract prominent summer rainfall patterns based on station records. It advances the use of the SOM to identify the summer monsoon rainfall patterns over Southeast China (SEC). Three distinct rain belts over the Huai River basin (HRB), the Lower Yangtze River basin (LYRB) and the South Coast region (SCR) are found. Their subseasonal variability strongly agrees with the northward progression of the East Asian Summer Monsoon (EASM) front in a stepwise fashion. We find that precipitation in the SCR and HRB rain belts exhibit significant changes in the mid-1990s, while the 1990s is the most active decade for the LYRB rain belt. Promising predictability of average daily rainfall over these three regions is obtained, with about 39% to 50% of the total variance explained by the circulation informed regression models. Both leave-one-year-out cross-validation and blind prediction verify the regression performance. The western North Pacific Subtropical High phases (Cheng et al., 2019), mid-latitude blocking high anomaly over northeast China and upper-level divergence in SEC are found to best explain the variability of the rain belts. The newly proposed Russia-China wave patterns (western/central Russia  north of Tibetan Plateau  SEC) and teleconnection between the El Niño-Southern Oscillation and the rain belts also offer additional predictability. Findings from this work may advance the understanding of the EASM rain belts, and offer insights to the source of bias for numerical simulations of daily summer monsoon rainfall in the region. Objective 4. Building a strong interdisciplinary education component with students' involvement through the project A group of local and international students joined the education component of the project in 2018. They were actively involved in the preliminary data gathering, preliminary analysis, poster design, research group meeting and literature summary. A few blogs were posted by them on the PI’s website. Unfortunately, a sequence of unexpected situations since 2019 until now prohibited the educational activity to grow bigger, but we were still able to work with a few undergraduate students on a remote basis.

26201217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26201217.value: Bi-continuous nanoporous (BNP) metal is a unique class of high specific-area material that particularly suits catalysis applications. Its continuous pores and solid phase maximize the accessible surface area while retaining structural integrity. The highly-curved metal surface preserves catalytic-active defect sites, placing BNP metals among the best catalysts for CO oxidation, hydrocarbon dehydrogenation, and oxygen reduction. However, as BNP metal is fabricated through the selective dissolution of a homogeneous alloy (i.e. dealloying), its application is largely limited by the demanding alloy preparation. We aim to eliminate this technical barrier by developing a new fabrication technology based on reduction-induced decomposition (RID). Previous work by the applicant showed that via chemical reduction, selective dissolution of anionic component(s) from a compound crystal can also produce BNP metal. This novel approach would offer a low-cost and flexible alternative to dealloying. However, to realize its potential, we still need to acquire fundamental knowledge of the structure evolution in RID, so as to enable rational designs of functional BNP metals. We will achieve this goal through the completion of the following tasks: i) identifying the requirements for a BNP structure to form through RID, ii) employing in-situ and ex-situ techniques to elucidate the mechanism of BNP metal evolution under a variety of conditions, and iii) building mathematical models that predict RID structural outcomes. At last, we will demonstrate the technological significance of the findings by designing BNP catalysts for CO2 reduction. The success of this project will not only deepen our scientific understanding of selective dissolution (i.e. dealloying and decomposition) but also enable wider adoption of BNP metals as highly active yet affordable catalysts. 雙連續納米多孔金屬是一種獨特的高比表面積材料。它連續的孔相和固相在最大化表面積的同時保證了結構的完整性，而其高度彎曲的金屬表面也能容納大量的活性缺陷，使其成為一氧化碳氧化、氧氣還原等反應絕佳的催化材料。但是此類結構通常由均相合金的選擇性溶解（脫合金）制得，因此其製備受限於合金的製備。 為了移除合金製備的限制，我們在此項目中會研究一種基於化合物還原分解的新型製備方法。我們先前的實驗結果已經證明，通過化學還原，選擇性地溶解金屬鹽中的陰離子，我們同樣可以製備得到雙連續納米多孔金屬。這一方法將極大地降低製備成本，但是我們目前對此過程中的結構演化知之甚少，所以尚無法利用此過程進行多孔結構的可控製備。 因此，我們計畫完成以下的研究任務，深化我們對此過程的理解：i）確定化合物分解過程中雙連續結構形成的條件；ii）藉助前沿表徵技術理解結構演化機理；iii）建立數學模型預測結構特徵。最後，我們也會將制得的多孔金屬應用于二氧化碳還原，以證明其在催化領域的應用。此項目不僅會加深我們對各類選擇性溶解機理的認識，更能拓寬雙連續納米多孔金屬在催化等領域的應用。

26201217.label: Realisation of objectives
26201217.value: Through the project, we have realized the overall objective of developing reduction-induced decomposition (RID) as a general, versatile fabrication method of bi-continuous nanoporous (BNP) structures. For the first objective on characterization, we have developed a suite of methods to quantify key characteristics. Most notably, we applied atomic force microscopy to image the grain boundary groves on the surface estimating the grain sizes and underpotential deposition of lead on silver for measuring the specific area accessible to an electrolyte. We have also adapted methods broadly used on dealloyed materials, including scanning and transmission electron microscopies, to characterize the morphology of BNP structures. At last, in an effort of extending the mechanism behind RID beyond electrochemical reactions, we applied small-angle neutron scattering to characterize the homogeneity of a AgCl-NaCl alloy precursor, which is prone to spinodal decomposition that can be hardly captured by any other means. The suite of characterization methods underpins our ongoing development of BNP materials for a variety of functional applications. For the second objective on the processing-structure relationship, we have revealed how temperature, reductant composition, and precursor composition determine the ligament and pore width, the porosity, the structural hierarchy, and the orientation of BNP structures. The effect temperature is understood based on the surface-diffusion controlled coarsening kinetics. The reductant composition tunes the relative rates of the surface diffusion and the RID reaction; when the latter approaches the (bulk) diffusional limit and the former is slow, a unique, oriented BNP structure forms. The precursor composition determines the porosity via the molar volume change. By using a precursor undergoing two types of selective dissolution, we can further partition the porosity into two levels to achieve structural hierarchy. For the third objective on mechanisms, we have elucidated the kinetics of the interface-controlled self-organization in RID. The kinetics controls the ligament and pore sizes through a quarter-root time dependence, activated via surface diffusion, similar to that in dealloying. When the kinetics is rapid enough to hit the bulk diffusion limit, the morphology transition towards the oriented structure can be intuitively explained through the diffusional layer thickness. At last, we also develop a precursor composition-porosity relationship to quantitatively guide the design of BNP structures in general. For the last objective, we have used the high tunability of BNP Ag from RID to understand how the structure determines the current density and the selectivity of CO2 reduction towards CO. By controlling the thickness of BNP Ag sheets and their porosity, we explain how mass transport through the structure affects the reduction rate, corroborated by finite element simulation. We further apply the hierarchical and the oriented BNP Ag’s, whose expected faster transports further increase the current densities, in agreement with rough estimates of diffusional lengths based on the effective rate of transport.

26201217.label: Major findings and research outcome
26201217.value: We developed reduction-induced decomposition (RID) as a versatile fabrication method towards bi-continuous nanoporous (BNP) metals with controllable ligament sizes, porosities and structural hierarchies, all significant to their functional applications as electrocatalysts and battery electrodes. (Part C, 8, No. 1). We elucidated the kinetics root of a unique structural evolution in RID and thereby establish a much-needed approach of fabricating oriented BNP metals to address the issue of sluggish mass transport in their functional applications. (Part C, 8, No. 2). We extended the mechanism to the selective dissolution of ionic solid solutions and reveal the structural evolution of BNP compound, analogous to RID and dealloying. (Part C, 8, No. 3). We further applied the materials and the method to address functional needs in alkaline Zn batteries, redox flow batteries, and CO2 electrocatalytic reduction. (Part C, 10, No. 1 and 2).

26201217.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26201217.value: The research has led to three ongoing projects on the development of BNP Zn for alkaline batteries, the further investigation of evolution mechanisms of oriented BNP structures, and the application of BNP in energy storage and conversion. Along these paths, the PI will continue to advance the functionalities of the materials towards practical applications and to understand structure-property relationships that will enable new functions and optimize the existing ones.

26201217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26201217.value: Metal atoms on the surface tend to organize themselves to minimize the area for low energy. Yet, this process rarely comes close to an equilibrium; more often, it is far from the equilibrium, giving rise to a variety of exotic nanostructures of large, complex surfaces that are significant in applications like catalysis, sensing, and batteries. Reduction-induced decomposition, the selective dissolution of anions (e.g., chloride) from a compound (e.g., silver chloride) is among the self-organization processes far from equilibria. It creates a bi-continuous nanoporous metallic structure, where the metal phase, in the form of curvy ligaments, and the pores are respectively percolating with individual widths tens of nanometers. The widths, the relative ratios, and the orientations of the metal ligaments and the pores can be controlled in the fabrication, enabling the design of nanostructures to realize the efficient conversion of carbon dioxide to other value-added chemicals and the storage of energy in advanced batteries.

26201617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26201617.value: Network externality refers to the phenomenon that each additional user of a good or service makes it more valuable to other customers. Many products of the modern era have network externality, including social games on Facebook and electric cars (having more customers incentivizes the firm to build more charging stations). The increase of network externality has significantly changed customer behavior and presents new challenges to firms attempting to launch or promote new products. In the proposed project, we seek to investigate the market growth of a product with network externality and the firm’s optimal operational decisions. The interactions between customers are complex and it is crucial to identify the major forces driving product adoption, e.g., the existence of a “super star” or the average connectivity. If successful, we should be able to extract a few interpretable market indicators from a complex process, relieving decision makers (firms, marketers) from “information overload”. The results will greatly streamline the decision-making process and lead to rich managerial insights. We propose to analyze the firm’s optimal pricing policy, in particular, for how long the firm should offer a discount when launching a product and how much the regular price should be when the product becomes popular. Those decisions highly depend on the structure of the customer network. Although similar strategies are implemented in practice (e.g., limited-time-free), they are mainly rely on rules of thumb and can lead to disastrous marketing failures if not conducted correctly. Our research is expected to provide a rigorous and analytical framework in which the firms can quantitatively devise their strategies with theoretical guarantees. Hong Kong is widely known as a “shopping paradise”. Recently, its retail landscape has been evolving rapidly as the new “online to offline” business model emerges through ever-growing connectivity. The outcome of the proposed project will lead to insightful implications for the transformation of the local retail and marketing industries. 市場上的很多產品都有網絡外部性。當用戶數量增多，用戶對這個產品產生的效用也會相應提升。社交遊戲，文件共享平台等等都是典型的網絡外部性產品。網絡外部性的存在顯著的改變了用戶的消費習慣。它對公司的定價和推廣策略也提出了不同的要求。在這個項目中，我們希望通過研究產品在網絡外部性下的市場份額變化來制訂最優的公司市場策略。在外部性的影響下，公司需要對不同的網路結構制訂不同的策略，比如星狀的網路和同一化的網路。我們希望抽象出一個網路中最重要的指標，從而簡化公司的決策分析，提供簡潔優化的決策指導。我們會分析一種常見的限時減價定價策略。這種策略在產品推出初期採用低價來吸引用戶從而產生大量的網路外部性。當產品佔有一定的市場份額以後再採用高價來賺取利潤。我們的理論模型會量化這種定價策略，比如最優的低價持續的時間以及價格。我們希望通過這個項目讓公司根據不同的市場環境和產品採用相應的最優決策。 香港作為公認的消費天堂，也在經歷著前所未有的變革。有很大一部分的零售業從線下慢慢地轉向線上渠道，從而能夠更好的利用網絡外部性。我們希望通過這個項目能夠更好的了解這一轉型並且提供運營方面的理論支持。

26201617.label: Realisation of objectives
26201617.value: 1. We use a network to model customers interaction between each other. When the network effects are strong, customers focus less on the quality or price of the product and are willing to follow the decision of their friends and neighbors in the network. As a result, the network structure greatly alters the purchasing behavior. We show that the network effects reinforce itself and create huge revenue potentials for the market leader or the monopoly. This results in the convexity trajectory of product adoption: at the very beginning, the sales volume increases slowly; after passing a critical mass, it picks up rapidly. An unintended consequence is that the entry barrier for new firms becomes high. 2. We have come up several measures to describe the network effects, which are by nature high-dimensional and hard to analyze. The first measure is the aggregate network effects, which sums up all the network effects received by customers in the market. This measure captures the first-order effect of network strength. The second measure is the eigenvector corresponding to the largest eigenvalue. By the Perron–Frobenius theorem, the first eigenvector is positive. Our results indicate that it is closely related to the importance of customers in the network. For example, if a customer has a large value, then it is essential for the firm to capture the user which can potentially exert network effects to the neighboring customers. The two measures developed are much more compact the the whole network, and yet are able to capture the strength and imbalance of the network. Our subsequent results show that they play important roles in the revenue earned by the firm. In particular, both network strength and imbalance benefit the firm. Accordingly, we provide a managerial suggestion for the firms to conduct market surveys to estimate the two measures before entering a market. 3. We have proposed two frameworks to model the decision making under network effects. The first framework is dynamic and based on linear network effects. We show that the dynamic programming depends on the spectral decomposition of the network. The new finding provides a tractable framework to tackle dynamic problems with linear network effects. We view it as a bridge between graph theory, which is combinatorial, and spectral graph theory, whose methodologies are mainly algebraic. Our second framework builds on the choice model with random utilities. Although random utility models have been popular in revenue management, we are not aware of its use in the context of network effects. Models with network effects mainly use linear-quadratic frameworks. We take a first step to combining the choice behavior using more realistic choice models, which yields fruitful results. In particular, unlike linear-quadratic models that always predict symmetric equilibrium for symmetric firms, we show that two symmetric firms can lead to market dominance of one of them. This is consistent with our intuition. For products with strong network effects such as Dropbox and OneDrive, although they have almost identical features and stability, Dropbox is used predominantly in academia. Our model gives a clear answer: the strong network effects create discontinuous best responses and lead to the non-existence of symmetric equilibira. That is, the two firms cannot hope to evenly split the market and there is always a winner emerging. The framework has brought great success in analyzing network markets. 4. From our models, we have generated useful managerial insights and suggestions for policymakers. First, we show that when facing a network market, the firm is better off offering products for free while monetizing the network effects later despite the future discounting. Second, both the network strength and the network imbalance help the firm. Third, when network effects are week, the market can provide access to multiple firms. When the network effects are strong, oligopoly is almost unsustainable and a single winner will emerge. To foster competition, the policymaker should design policies to encourage and provide access to new entries, as a monopolized market reduces customer surplus. Fourth, first-mover advantage is important in network markets. As a first mover, the firm is easy to retain the market share with an inferior product. It is crucial for the regulators to shock the market sufficiently and periodically so that superior products have a chance to gain market share and survive.

26201617.label: Major findings and research outcome
26201617.value: There are two research papers produced due to the support of the grant: "Duopoly Competition with Network Effects in Discrete Choice Models" and "Impact of Network Structure on New Service Pricing". The first paper is under second-round major revision in Operations Research, and the second paper is to be resubmitted to Operations Research. In the first paper, we consider two firms that sell substitutable products to a market of network-connected customers. The customers make purchases based on the multinomial logit model and the firms compete for their purchasing probabilities. We characterize possible Nash equilibria for homogeneous network interactions and identical firms: when the network effects are weak, there is a symmetric equilibrium that the two firms evenly split the market; when the network effects are strong, there exist two asymmetric equilibria additionally in which one firm dominates the market; interestingly, when the product quality is low and the network effects are neither too weak nor too strong, the resulting market equilibrium is never symmetric although the firms are ex ante symmetric. In the second paper, we analyze a firm's optimal pricing of a new service when consumers interact in a network and impose positive externality on one another. The firm initially provides its service for free, leveraging network externality to promote rapid service consumption growth. The firm raises the price and starts earning revenue only when a sufficient level of consumer interactions is established. Incorporating the local network effects in a non-stationary dynamic model, we study the impact of network structure on the firm's revenue and optimal pricing decision. We find that the firm delays the timing of service monetization when it faces a more strongly connected network, despite the fact that such a network allows the firm to monetize the service sooner by resulting in faster consumption growth. We also find that the firm benefits from network imbalance, ie, the firm prefers a network of consumers with varying degrees of connections to that with similar degrees of connections. We also study the value of knowing the network structure and discuss how such knowledge impacts the firm's profitability.

26201617.value: The research projects have potentials to lead to exciting future research. I will keep working on the topic with my students, with the support of other research grants.

26201617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26201617.value: When the customers in the market have network effects, the strategies of the firms display distinct features. For a monopoly firm, it is willing to offer products for free for a long time, in order to cultivate the network of users. For competing firms, market dominance is more often, especially when the network effects are strong. The results accurately predict the market outcome, and explain why many online games are switching to the free-to-play model, and why winner always takes all in many industries like social networks and collaboration tools. We characterize the optimal strategies of firms and give regulatory suggestions.

26206717.label: Project Objectives
26206717.value: Objective 1. Socialized Text Representation and Cleaning. We will develop fundamental text representation algorithms using the individuality and connection of social media users to reduce the ambiguity of social media text data. This will address the “semi-structure and sparsity” challenge of social media data. We will build positive-unlabeled learning from the representation to clean the “noisy social media data.” Objective 2. SocialSnowball for Bootstrapped Activity Extraction and Classification. We will develop a SocialSnowball bootstrapped information extraction framework to leverage the social connection of users in order to handle the “ambiguity” and “sparsity” challenges of activity extraction. For activity classification, we use the same SocialSnowball framework and leverage the structural similarity measure to develop a classification algorithm with minimal supervision from the annotated activity dataset. The bootstrapping framework can be used to extract the knowledge incrementally to maintain the freshness of the knowledge graph. Objective 3. Indirect Social-Supervision for Activity Organization. For the “lack of definition of activity relationships” challenge, we will build a systematic framework to construct a novel knowledge graph of activities and their relationships, based on using indirect or distant supervision obtained from social media to classify activity relationships. We will develop indirect supervision based on the side information provided by the social media platforms. Objective 4. Tools, Evaluation, and Prototype Development. We will develop both direct (based on human annotation) and indirect evaluation for the knowledge graph we construct. We will disseminate the research results in the form of high-quality publications, and make the software and algorithm available publicly.

26206717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26206717.value: 知識圖譜是一種描述人類知識的語義網絡。他可以用來幫助很多信息檢索和自然語言理解問題。自從2012年Google發佈了其知識圖譜，知識圖譜相關的概念被更為廣泛接受和使用在很多領域，例如：問答、推薦、廣告等系統。然而，現有的知識圖譜通常是對本體和它們關係的知識，例如< LarryPage; Foundero f;Google >。對於人類活動（如“cooking,” “jogging,” “watching movie,” “playing basketball,”）卻沒有建模。這種活動知識在話語分析中非常有用，例如可以用來分析句子之間的語義關係，如因果、時序等等。在這個項目中，我們將建立人類活動的知識圖譜，包含活動的類別和關係。由於社交媒體中包含了很多人的活動，我們從社交媒體中提取這種活動信息。 為了能夠提取活動知識，我們首先對社交媒體生成社交語言的表達。這個文本表達可以使用個性化和社交化的信息。然後我們提出一個SocialSnowBall的框架來對社交媒體的信息進行抽取。SocialSnowBall使用盡量少的標註信息來對信息進行抽取和分類。另外，給定活動抽取的結果，我們提出使用間接監督信息的方法來對活動之間的關係進行識別。間接監督信息包括用戶的地點、時間、用戶好友關係、對話關係等等。在社交媒體上抽取活動知識圖譜具有很大的挑戰，因為社交媒體的數據通常有很多噪聲。因此，在整個項目中我們將考慮這些噪聲并通過算法類小心處理。 我們的活動知識圖譜相對於之前的知識圖譜是比較獨特的，因為我們考慮了社交媒體上的開放領域的活動信息。我們將發展出基礎的方法，使用直接或間接的評價方法來評測。特別是提取出的活動信息可以作為先驗知識在其他話語分析中進行使用。

26206717.label: Realisation of objectives
26206717.value: We have built up the socialized word embedding for social textual documents representation [20]. We have shown that word embeddings can be used as an unsupervised way to find users’ representations. As representation learning plays an important role in many applications, we also developed more complicated representation learning for social and information networks. In particular, we have developed biased random walk in network embeddings for socialized word embeddings [20, 22], multiplex network embedding for social networks [26] and word embeddings [24], vertex-reinforced random walk for network embedding [19], controlled random walk on hyper-graphs for hyper-graph representation learning [8], and heterogeneous spacey random walk for HIN embedding [6]. For deeper graph neural networks, we also developed a graph CNN approach to text classification [13], heterogenous graph CNN for fine-grained event classification [12], relational graph isomorphism network for subgraph isomorphism counting [11], and social explorative attention networks for recommendation [17, 18]. Besides modern deep learning based approaches, we also developed a random walk based semisupervised learning algorithm for HINs [9], matrix factorization (MF) + factorization machine (FM) for recommendation over HINs [27], and multi-kernel learning for multi-metapath fusion in HINs [7, 15]. We have built the bootstrapping framework for knowledge graph construction [25]. We have tried more powerful deep learning models to improve general text classification so that it can be potentially used for bootstrapping with better base classifiers [13]. We develop frameworks to use distant/weakly supervision or indirect supervision for information extraction. Here are several different directions. Information extraction. In this direction, we have studied how to incorporate human’s knowledge about a social network to improve the entity linking task in social media [4]. Then we also tried to use entity linking to incorporate the knowledge from Wikipedia to improve fine-grained entity typing [1]. We further use other linguistic knowledge reflected in language such as IsA relations and semantic role labeling (SRL) relations to improve typing [3]. For relation discovery, we developed a variational learning framework to incorporate out-of-relation knowledge in external knowledge base to improve the discovery results [10]. For aspect and opinion term extraction, we developed several rules based on linguistic knowledge to construct some weak supervision and boost the extraction performance [2]. Text classification. For text classification, we leverage the explicit semantic analysis based on Wikipedia to perform zero-shot text classification for hundreds of languages [14]. We then improve the bootstrapping algorithm in the zero-shot classification using path prediction for hierarchical labels [16]. We further use posterior regularization to improve weakly supervised text classification [21] under the variational framework [23]. We have tried many downstreaming tasks to evaluate knowledge graphs and extracted knowledge. 26206717.label: Major findings and research outcome
26206717.value: We have produced the world's largest eventuality-centric knowledge graph ASER based on this project. The paper was presented at WWW 2020, and the code and data have been published at https://github.com/HKUST-KnowComp/ASER. There have been several extensions based on ASER, including TransOMCS: population of a commonsense knowledge base in the format of OMCS transferred from linguistic patterns in ASER (paper was presented at IJCAI 2020; code and data are available at https://github.com/HKUST-KnowComp/TransOMCS), and DISCOS: population of ATOMIC if-then inferential commonsense knowledge base with the discourse relations in ASER (paper was presented at WWW 2021; code and data are available at https://github.com/HKUST-KnowComp/DISCOS-commonsense). Apart from the knowledge bases we released, we have published 6 journal papers and top and visible 42 conference papers. All the code and data related to the papers have been published on our group's GitHub page: https://github.com/HKUST-KnowComp. After this project, there have been four MPhil and five PhD students graduated who have conducted related research to this project.

26206717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26206717.value: The development of ASER was very fruitful. We have got another GRF grant accepted to further build ASER with conceptualization. We have released our knowledge bases for the public to use. The project has received more than 200 stars so far. The papers we have published also triggered a lot of follow-up ideas, either can be done by us or others. We will choose some of the important ideas to extend our existing research work.

26206717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26206717.value: This project has leveraged publicly available social media data to construct a social life-related eventuality-centric knowledge graph. We have conducted extensive experiments, solid research to build such as knowledge graphs. During the construction, we have identified many interesting and important research problems to solve. The proposed ideas have been published at many top and visible venues in the research community.

26301517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26301517.value: For a large complex system, a statistical study is usually a practical and efficient way to investigate some typical properties of the system, considering the details of the system are often not explicitly known. High-dimensional random matrices turn out to be suitable for modeling many problems of large linear or linearizable systems. A random matrix is nothing else, but a matrix with random variables as its entries. For example, a random Hermitian matrix with i.i.d. random variables (up to symmetry) has been used for studying the energy levels of heavy nuclei; a sample covariance matrix can be used to explore the correlation pattern of big data set; a random adjacent matrix of random graph can help to study a large complex network. In random matrix theory (RMT), "local eigenvalue statistics" refers to the statistics consisting of a single or a few eigenvalues, such as the gap between two eigenvalues, and the largest eigenvalue. A central issue in RMT is the "universality" conjecture for local eigenvalue statistics, which states that the limiting behavior of these statistics should not depend on the details of the distribution of the matrices. This is the random matrix analogue of the law of large numbers and the central limit theorem. Universality is tremendously useful in many applied fields such as Statistics, Economics and Engineering, not to mention its theoretical importance in Probability Theory and Mathematical Physics. Universality has been proved for many classical random matrix ensembles such as Wigner matrix and sample covariance matrix. However, recent developments in RMT and the related fields beg a study on the local eigenvalue statistics for more complicated random matrix ensembles, which can be often written as a polynomial in more classical random matrices. Polynomials in random matrices are ubiquitous in statistics, and the largest eigenvalue of different models can be used in various porblems. In this project, we will study the local eigenvalue statistics of polynomials in classical random matrices, with a focus on the addition and multiplication of random matrices, which are two building blocks for every polynomial. Moreover, we will work with the high-dimensional setting. Our aim is to develop a systematic approach for universality of various local eigenvalue statistics for our matrix ensembles. Several extensions of our ensembles will also be considered. At the end, we will apply our methods and results to some practical random matrices from high-dimensional statistics. 在這個項目中，我們將研究經典隨機矩陣的多項式矩陣的局部特徵根統計量。我們主要集中在兩個隨機矩陣的加和以及乘積模型 。 我們的目標是研究高維情形下的特徵根統計量的極限性質。我們將發展一套系統性的方法證明這些矩陣模型以及一些擴展模型的局部特徵值統計量的普適性。最後，我們將把我們的理論結果應用到高維統計中。

26301517.label: Realisation of objectives
26301517.value: The models of addition and multiplication of random matrices lie in the intersection of Random Matrix Theory and Free Probability Theory. Since the seminal work of Voiculescu in 1990s which bridges these two fields, the global behaviour of the spectrum of these random matrix models have been well understood. Specifically, the limiting spectral distribution of these models are given by free convolutions on global scale. However, from the random matrix point of view, the local spectral statistics are more interesting and challenging. The study of the asymptotic behaviour of local spectral statistics had been out of the reach via the standard Free Probability techniques for long time. Meanwhile, in the last decade, significant progress has been made towards the understanding of the local spectral statistics for more classical random matrix models such as the Wigner matrices. Some methodology developed in this duration sheds some light on the local spectral statistics of the addition and multiplication of random matrices. However, unlike the Wigner matrices, which have independent matrix entries (up to symmetry), the source of the randomness of the addition and multiplication of the (unitarily or orthogonally invariant) random matrices comes from the Haar distributed unitary or orthogonal matrices, which has correlated entries. Therefore, essentially new ideas are required to find the limiting behaviour of the local spectral statistics of these models. In order to study the limiting behaviour of the local statistics, the first step is to establish a local version of Voiculescu’s weak convergence of the spectral distribution. Such kind of results is usually called “local law” in the literature. It can show that Voiculescu’s result holds down to the optimal local scale, slightly larger than the eigenvalue spacing. A consequence of the local law is a rigidity estimate of the eigenvalue locations, which can also be regarded as a precise large deviation estimate of the eigenvalue. It is widely believed that such a large deviation control is necessary (very often is the key) for the study of some finer property such as the precise limiting distribution of the local eigenvalue statistics. In order to establish the local law for addition and multiplication of random matrices, we first use a partial randomness decomposition of the Haar measure that enables us to take partial expectations of the Green function entries. Exploiting concentration only for the partial randomness surpasses the more general but less flexible Gromov–Milman technique. Second, to compute the partial expectations of the Green function entries, we establish a new system of self-consistent equations involving only two auxiliary quantities. Third, to connect the partial expectation with the subordination functions from free probability, we rely on the optimal stability result for the subordination equations which was established in our previous work. This approach is then used to solve Objective 2. We then turn to study a non-Hermitian random matrix models whose limiting spectral distribution is given by the famous single ring law. Especially, we established a local version of the Single Ring Theorem down to the optimal scale. By applying Girko’s Hermitization, we are able to translate the local law of this non-Hermitian single ring model to the local law of an Hermitian model which is a block version of the addition of random matrices. This solves Objective 1. It is well known that the limiting behaviour of the eigenvalues at the edge quite much depends on the type of the edge singularity of the limiting spectral density function. Hence, before the derivation of the edge eigenvalue distribution, one has to first investigate the edge singularity of the free convolutions. Particularly, we proved that the decay of the free additive convolution at the edge is square-root if both two probability measures have power law behaviour with exponent s between 1 and -1. This solves Objective 3. Then our local laws and the edge singularity results for free convolution become a part of technical inputs in the recent results on bulk/edge universality for local statistics by Che-Landon, and Ahn, and for mesoscopic statistics by the PI and collaborators, and thus Objective 4 is achieved. Finally, we considered the eigenvalue and eigenvector distribution of the signal-plus-noise model and the spiked covariance matrices, and discussed statistical applications of these results. These two models can be regarded as examples of the summation and multiplication of random matrices. Hence, Objective 5 is achieved.

26301517.label: Major findings and research outcome
26301517.value: We first establish the local law for the summation of unitarily invariant random Hermitian matrices. The approach starts from a partial randomness decomposition of Haar unitary/orthogonal matrices, and relies on a system of self-consistent equation of two auxiliary quantities which are closely related to the Steiltjes transform and subordination functions. The approach is novel and universal in the sense that it can be applied to other models whose randomness is from Haar unitary or orthogonal matrices. These type of results are contained in the papers published in Advances in Mathematics (2017) and Journal of Functional Analysis (2020). Further, we find that with Girko’s Hermitization, we can study the eigenvalue of general unitarily invariant non-Hermitian random matrices, using similar method. This help us establish the local single ring theorem. The result is contained in the paper published in Annals of Probability (2019). Then, regarding the singularity of the density function of the free additive convolution, we rely on methods from function theory. It is known that the Stieltjes transform of the free additive convolution is related to the Stieltjes transforms of the original measures through analytic subordination. By studying the subordination functions more quantitatively, we are able to prove the square-root decay of the free additive convolution at the boundary. This result is contained in the paper published in Journal d'Analyse Mathematique (2020). Then, we study the eigenvalue behaviour of the summation of random matrices on mesoscopic scale, by considering the mesoscopic statistics. Especially, we prove a CLT for the mesoscopic eigenvalue statistics for this model. The CLT matches those for the classical random matrix models such as Wigner matrices, and thus it is universal. This result is contained in the paper published in International Mathematics Research Notices (2020). Last, we study the asymptotic distribution of the outlying eigenvalues and corresponding eigenvectors of the signal-plus-noise model and the spiked sample covariance matrices. Especially, the eigenvector distribution of the signal-plus-noise model is non-universal in the sense it may depend on the distribution of the noise matrix. These results are contained in the paper accepted by Annals of statistics (2021) and the preprint arXiv: 2008.11903.

26301517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26301517.value: In our works, we raise a general approach to deal with the local law for the random matrices models with Haar unitary/orthogonal matrices. Such an approach have been applied to the sum of two random matrices and the product of two random matrices. A natural direction to further explore this approach is the local law for general polynomials in Haar unitary/orthogonal matrices and deterministic matrices. We intend to establish the local law, for general polynomials and even the rational functions of random matrices. In the edge regime, this will require us to first study the singularity behaviour of the limiting spectral distribution of the general polynomials. This shall be the second possible direction for the future work. Finally, the bulk and edge universality for local spectral statistics of the summation of random matrices have been established in recent works. However, these works still impose very strong restrictions on the spectral distribution of individual summands. Since free convolution can strongly smooth out the irregularity of the probability measures, it is believed that these restrictions are not needed. In order to establish the universality under essentially lightest assumptions, significantly new ideas are needed. This will be the third direction for further development.

26301517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26301517.value: In this project, we work on the spectral properties of the summation and multiplication of Hermitian random matrices. The key problem is to understand the limiting behaviour of the eigenvalue and eigenvector statistics of these models on microcscopic scale. We have successfully developed a novel approach to derive the local law for the spectrum of such models, and extend the approach to non-Hermitian matrices. We also investigate the edge singularity of the limiting spectral distribution of these models, which are known as the free convolutions. We further study several models in this category, arising from High-Dimensional Statistics, and apply our results to real applications. The results of this project is important in the fields of Random Matrix Theory, Free Probability Theory, and High-Dimensional Statistics.

26305017.value: 从第一性原理出发研究高温高压下C-H-O流体的物理和化学性质

26305017.label: Project Objectives
26305017.value: Compute Raman spectra of C-H-O fluids at elevated pressure (P) and temperature (T), and study how the Raman intensities of carbon species [(bi)carbontate ions, hydrocarbons, etc.] change with P and T. The intensity of Raman peaks is used to calculate solute concentrations, but at supercritical conditions it is not clear how Raman intensities change with P and T. Understanding the P-T dependence of Raman scattering helps us relate the concentration of chemical species to the measured Raman signals under extreme conditions. Develop a method from first principles to calculate the polarizabilities of molecules and ions in the condensed phase and study how they change with P and T in C-H-O fluids. The existing method only takes into account dipole-dipole interactions when evaluating intermolecular contributions, but in supercritical fluids the dipole-dipole approximation may not be good enough to describe the complex interactions between molecules. A rigorous method is needed to examine the validity of the dipole-dipole approximation. This method will also help us to understand the electrical response of molecules and ions under extreme conditions. Compute infrared (IR) spectra of C-H-O fluids at high P and high T, and study the vibrational fingerprint of supercritical fluids. Theoretical IR spectroscopy may serve as a reference for the development of the IR technique at high temperature. Study hydrocarbon reactions under the conditions of the deep Earth at the atomic level. This will help us to understand the formation of diamonds in the Earth's deep interior and will reveal possible reaction paths related to the origin of abiogenic petroleum.

26305017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26305017.value: In view of the threat of global warming, the task of understanding the Earth's carbon cycle becomes critical and urgent. For millions to billions of years, the Earth's surface and interior have actively exchanged carbon through the deep carbon cycle, in which C-H-O fluids are the major carbon-bearing geofluids, carrying and transporting significant quantities of carbon. The deep carbon cycle inside the Earth influences global climate change substantially. However, many fundamental questions about the deep carbon cycle are still a matter for debate. For example, how does carbon transport occur inside the Earth? Is carbon accumulating or diminishing in our planet's interior? In order to answer these questions, it is of essential importance to investigate the physics and chemistry of C-H-O fluids at pressure (P) and temperature (T) conditions found in the deep Earth. It is challenging to study C-H-O fluids at extreme P-T conditions experimentally, both because they may be too corrosive to be held in experimental containers and because obtaining clear vibrational spectra of fluids at high temperatures is difficult. Furthermore, the interpretation of measured spectroscopic signals is often controversial, because the relationship of the chemical species to the vibrational peaks at supercritical conditions is not yet clear. In this project, we propose to conduct simulations of first-principles molecular dynamics to study C-H-O fluids at high P and high T conditions. We will compute the Raman and infrared (IR) spectra of C-H-O fluids to see how the Raman scattering and IR absorption change with P and T. We will develop a new method to calculate the electrical response of molecules and ions in supercritical fluids and we will obtain the molecular pictures of how hydrocarbons react in the Earth's mantle. Using the results obtained by first-principles simulations, we will establish the equation of state of water in a P-T range beyond the reach of current experiments. The proposed research will connect theoretical modeling and experiment, and will make an important contribution to deep carbon science. 受地球气候变暖的威胁 ，理解地球碳循环变得严峻而迫切。从几百万年到上十亿年的时间里，地球表面和内部一直不停地通过深部碳循环交换着碳。其中，C-H-O流体是主要的携碳地质流体，携带和运送了大量的碳物质。虽然地球内部的碳循环深刻地影响了地球的气候变化，但是它的许多基本问题仍然存在争论。例如，地球内部碳的输运是如何进行的？地球内部碳的含量是在增多还是减少？为了回答这些问题，研究在地球内部极端温度压强条件下C-H-O流体的物理和化学性质至关重要。 实验上研究极端温度压强条件下的C-H-O流体具有相当挑战性，原因在于极端条件下C-H-O流体会变得非常具有腐蚀性而损坏实验容器，同时高温下流体的光谱很难被清晰地观察到。不仅如此，因为我们不知道在超临界条件下如何将观测到的振动谱同化学组分相联系 ，所以对实验得到的光谱信息的解释也常常存在争议。 在本项研究中，我们打算采用第一性原理分子动力学模拟的办法研究高温高压下C-H-O流体。我们将计算C-H-O流体的拉曼和红外振动谱以观察它们如何随温度和压强变化。我们将开发一个新的方法计算超临界条件下分子和离子的电极化率。我们将得到地幔中碳氢化合物反应的分子图像。本项研究将结合理论模拟和实验，对深部碳科学做出重要贡献。

26305017.label: Realisation of objectives
26305017.value: Objective 1: Compute Raman spectra of C-H-O fluids at elevated pressure (P) and temperature (T), and study how the Raman intensities of carbon species [(bi)carbontate ions, hydrocarbons, etc.] change with P and T. We presented a strategy, based on first-principles simulations, to determine ratios of Raman scattering cross-sections of aqueous species under extreme conditions, thus providing a key quantity that can be used, in conjunction with Raman measurements, to predict chemical speciation in aqueous fluids. Due to the importance of the Earth’s carbon cycle, we focus on carbonate and bicarbonate ions. We found that the ratio of the Raman scattering cross-sections of carbonate and bicarbonate ions in water decreases with increasing pressure, while it increases with increasing temperature, up to ~10 GPa and 1000 K. Our results indicate a higher concentration of bicarbonates in water than previously considered at conditions relevant to the Earth’s upper mantle, with important implications for the transport of carbon in aqueous fluids in the Earth’s interior. The paper is published in Nat Commun 11, 421 (2020), where I am the corresponding author. Objective 2: Develop a method from first principles to calculate the polarizabilities of molecules and ions in the condensed phase We proposed a first-principles method to compute polarizabilities of sub-entities of solids and liquids, which accounts for multipolar interactions at all orders and is applicable to semiconductors and insulators. The method only requires the evaluation of induced fields in the condensed phase, with no need of multiple calculations for each constituent. As an example, we presented results for the molecular polarizabilities of water in a wide pressure and temperature range. We found that at ambient conditions, the dipole-induced-dipole approximation is sufficiently accurate and the Clausius-Mossotti relation may be used, e.g., to obtain molecular polarizabilities from experimental refractive indexes. However with increasing pressure, this approximation becomes unreliable and in the case of ice X the Clausius-Mossotti relation is not valid. The paper is published in J. Chem. Phys. 149, 051101 (2018), where I am the corresponding author. Objective 3: Compute infrared (IR) spectra of C-H-O fluids at high P and high T, and study the vibrational fingerprint of supercritical fluids. Theoretical IR spectroscopy may serve as a reference for the development of the IR technique at high temperature. We introduced a neural network dipole model, which combined with molecular dynamics, can be used to compute P–T dependent dielectric properties of water as accurately as first-principles methods but much more efficiently. We found that ϵ0 may vary by one order of magnitude in Earth’s upper mantle, suggesting that the solvation properties of water change dramatically at different depths. Although ϵ0 and the molecular dipole moment increase with an increase in pressure along an isotherm, the dipolar angular correlation has its maximum at 5 GPa–7 GPa, which may indicate that hydrogen bonds become weaker at high pressure. We also calculated the frequency-dependent dielectric constant of water in the microwave range, which, to the best of our knowledge, has not been calculated from first principles, and found that temperature affects the dielectric absorption more than pressure. Our results are of great use in many areas, e.g., modeling water–rock interactions in geochemistry. The computational approach introduced here can be readily applied to other molecular fluids. The frequency-dependent dielectric constant can be directly related to IR spectra. The paper is published in J. Chem. Phys. 153, 101103 (2020), where I am the corresponding author. Objective 4: Study hydrocarbon reactions under the conditions of the deep Earth at the atomic level. This will help us to understand the formation of diamonds in the Earth's deep interior and will reveal possible reaction paths related to the origin of abiogenic petroleum. We performed extensive ab initio molecular dynamics simulations and free energy calculations to study the water–gas shift reaction, which is one of the most important reactions in industrial hydrogen production and plays a key role in Fischer–Tropsch-type synthesis, widely believed to generate hydrocarbons in the deep carbon cycle. We found the direct formation of formic acid from CO and supercritical water at 10–13 GPa and 1400 K without any catalyst. Contrary to the common assumption that formic acid or formate is an intermediate product, we found that HCOOH is thermodynamically more stable than the products of the water–gas shift reaction above 3 GPa and at 1000–1400 K. Our study suggests that the water–gas shift reaction may not happen in the Earth’s upper mantle, and formic acid or formate may be an important carbon carrier in reducing environments, participating in many geochemical processes in deep Earth, such as the formation of diamonds and the origin of abiogenic petroleum. The paper is published in J. Phys. Chem. Lett. 12, 4292 (2021), and also featured by ACS Editors' choice. .

26305017.label: Major findings and research outcome
26305017.value: We developed a first-principles strategy to determine ratios of Raman scattering cross-sections of aqueous species at ambient and extreme conditions, thus providing a key quantity that can be used, in conjunction with Raman measurements, to predict chemical speciation in aqueous fluids. We introduced a neural network dipole model, which combined with molecular dynamics, can be used to compute P–T dependent dielectric properties of water as accurately as first-principles methods but much more efficiently. Our results are of great use in many areas, e.g., modeling water–rock interactions in geochemistry. The computational approach introduced here can be readily applied to other molecular fluids. The frequency-dependent dielectric constant can be directly related to IR spectra. By applying extensive ab initio molecular dynamics simulations at pressure and temperature conditions similar to those in Earth’s upper mantle, we found that carbonic acid can be the most abundant carbon species in aqueous CO2 solutions at ∼10 GPa and 1000 K. The mole percent of carbonic acid in total dissolved carbon species increases with increasing pressure along an isotherm, while its mole percent decreases with increasing temperature along an isobar. The effects of pH buffering by carbonic acid may play an important role in water–rock interactions in Earth’s interior. Our findings suggest that carbonic acid is an important carbon carrier in the deep carbon cycle. When the C-H-O fluids are not fulled oxidized, we found the direct formation of formic acid from CO and supercritical water at 10–13 GPa and 1400 K without any catalyst. Contrary to the common assumption that formic acid or formate is an intermediate product, we found that HCOOH is thermodynamically more stable than the products of the water–gas shift reaction above 3 GPa and at 1000–1400 K. Our study suggests that formic acid or formate may be an important carbon carrier in reducing environments, participating in many geochemical processes in deep Earth, such as the formation of diamonds and the origin of abiogenic petroleum. In addition, to interpret experimental Raman data at extreme conditions, we performed ab initio molecular dynamics simulations coupled with the modern theory of polarization to calculate Raman spectra of methane, ethane and propane up to 48 GPa and 2000 K. Our method includes anharmonic temperature effects. We studied the pressure and temperature effects on the Raman bands and identified the characteristic Raman modes for the C–C and C–C–C bonds.

26305017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26305017.value: In our current study, we focus on some simple hydrocarbons, such as methane, ethane, and propane, and the simplest carboxylic acid, formic acid. In the future, we plan to study more complicated hydrocarbon reactions, the role of water on the hydrocarbon reactions, and the effects of oxygen fugacity. We have generated many trajectories from ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations. We will try to see if we can build accurate and efficient machine learning force fields (MLFFs) using our trajectories. The MLFFs can be used to calculate reaction pathways of C-H-O fluids, which are usually too computational demanding for direct AIMD simulations.

26305017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26305017.value: C-H-O fluids are the major carbon-bearing fluids, carrying and transporting significant quantities of carbon in deep Earth, which substantially influences global climate change. In this work, we applied the fundamental principles in physics to study the physical and chemical properties of C-H-O fluids. We developed a method to quantify the concentrations of ions and molecules in liquids or supercritical fluids together with experimental Raman spectroscopy. By applying data-driven machine learning approach, we introduced a a neural network dipole model, which combined with molecular dynamics, can be used to compute P–T dependent dielectric properties of water as accurately as first-principles methods but much more efficiently. The dielectric properties determine how well water can dissolve ions. We found that carbonic acid can be the most abundant carbon species, which is very different from at ambient conditions. We also discover the formation of formic acid, which may play an important role in many geochemical processes in deep Earth, such as the formation of diamonds and the origin of abiogenic petroleum.

26500217.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26500217.value: Contests are widely used to study competitive environments where all players exert costly effort to win prize(s). In procurement of innovative goods or competition for job promotion, the goal of a contest is typically to maximize total effort by all players because effort by contest losers has positive externality to the contest designer. There are many theoretical insights into how to design contest rules to best provide incentive. For example, Moldovanu and Sela (2001) show that whether offering one or multiple prizes would maximize effort depends on the shape of cost function. To implement such a result in policy practice requires knowledge of the contest environment based on empirical studies, but there are only a few empirical studies of contests because a player's effort is generally unobserved by researchers. In this research project, we obtain a unique data set from proposal contests for architecture design procurement, which contains internal cost estimates of design firms. As an initial stage, we have connected with two leading design firms in Guangdong and construct a pilot data set covering 109 projects. The samples for both firms are complete records of all participation and contest outcomes in 2015. One novel feature of proposal contests is that multiple prizes (subsidies to contest losers) are widely used. The effectiveness of offering multiple prizes is doubted by many researchers, as it dampens the competitiveness of single-prize contests, for example, Glazer and Hassin (1988), Barut and Kovenock (1998), Clark et al. (1998), and Szymanski and Valletti (2005). However, none of these studies accounts for the endogenous entry of players. From the pilot data, we observe that offering multiple prizes attracts more firms, which may lead to higher total effort and more desirable proposals. Using this data set, we expect to unveil several key aspects of proposal contests including a player's entry decision, cost function, and the effect of multiple prizes. Based on data patterns and existing results in Moldovanu and Sela (2006) and Liu and Lu (2014), we set up an all-pay contest model with incomplete information and multiple prizes. We add an endogenous entry stage to the model that captures how multiple prizes attract more bidders and maximize total effort. From the data, we structurally estimate model primitives including effort externality, cost function, type distribution, and entry behavior. We use the estimation results to conduct a counterfactual study of various prize schemes and entry restriction for policy reference. 競賽模型常被用於研究多參與者付出努力爭奪獎項的環境。為著採購創新產品或是競聘，競賽設計者一般希望最大化總的付出水平，因為所有參與者的付出對競賽設計者都是有利的。在理論上，文獻中已經有許多競賽設計以提供激勵的方法。例如，Moldovanu and Sela (2001) 指出，是否應該設置多個獎項取決於成本函數的形狀。而要在實際中應用這項成果，需要相應的實證研究，然而由於缺乏可觀測的付出數據，對於競賽的實證研究非常少。在這項研究課題中，我們得到從建築設計採購的方案競賽，得到了很好的數據，其中就包括一些企業的成本估計。作為第一步，我們已經拿到了兩家廣東省的設計院，關於109個設計競賽的數據。這些樣本記錄了這兩家企業2015年所參與的全部設計競賽。設計競賽常有多獎項（給未中標企業設計補償款）的特點。在理論上，許多研究者（例如Glazer and Hassin (1988), Barut and Kovenock (1998), Clark et al. (1998), and Szymanski and Valletti (2005)）質疑設置多獎項不是有效的提供激勵的方法，因為多獎項可能會淡化競賽的競爭性。然而，上述這些研究結論，並沒有考慮到參與者是選擇性的進入競賽的。從現有的數據看，我們發現設置多獎項會吸引更多企業參加，因此可能增加總付出，採購方也更可能得到理想的設計方案。用這些數據，我們希望來探索設計競賽的幾個關鍵方面，包括企業的進入決策，付出成本函數，以及多獎項帶來的效果。目前，基於數據的特點和現有理論成果（Moldovanu and Sela (2006), Liu and Lu (2014)），我們設置了一個多獎項不完全信息競賽模型。我們加入了一個外生進入的環節來研究多獎項對於吸引更多參與者的效果。從數據中，我們估計出重要的模型參數，並且用這些估計結果，來回答一些與政策先關的問題。例如如何最優的設計獎項，以及是否應該限制企業進入。
