26500217.label: Major findings and research outcome
26500217.value: We provide novel identification results for a large class of contest models that can accommodate asymmetric CSFs and asymmetric players type distributions. Based on the identification results, we propose an estimation procedure for the parameters in the CSF and the quantile functions of private costs. We establish their consistency and root-n asymptotic normality and propose estimators for the asymptotic variances. We apply our newly developed structural econometric method to study election campaigns and incumbency advantage using data from U.S. House of Representatives elections. Our method separates and quantifies the incumbency advantage from two sources: At the contest level, we estimate the asymmetric parameter of the CSF and find that the asymmetry increases in the incumbent's tenure. At the candidate level, we find that the private costs of challengers are significantly higher than those of incumbents on average. Our explanation is that this difference maybe due to the candidates' difference in fundraising abilities. These two sources of asymmetry jointly generate the empirical fact that incumbents spend more than twice as much as the challengers and are reelected more than 94\% of the time. Based on the estimated model primitives, we conduct a counterfactual study of campaign policy reforms including imposing a term limit, setting a spending limit, and providing public campaign financing. We find that imposing spending limits is the most effective at reducing both incumbent winning probability and total campaign spending.

26500217.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26500217.value: Since the seminal work by citet{tullock1980efficient}, contests are widely used to study competitive environments in which players exert costly effort to compete for a prize. We study the econometrics of an asymmetric Tullock contest model with incomplete information. Identification results are established for parameters in the asymmetric contest success function and for the quantile functions of players' private costs. We propose the corresponding estimators, derive the asymptotic properties, and demonstrate their good finite sample performances by simulation. We also propose an easy-to-implement parametric estimation method that can incorporate contest-specific covariates. Our method is used to study U.S. House of Representatives elections. We quantify the incumbency advantages and conduct policy experiments to evaluate how imposing a term limit or launching campaign finance reforms affect incumbency advantage.

26500517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26500517.value: In today’s competitive business environment, recent developments such as product proliferation and reduction in product life cycles in the consumer markets have been placing increasing pressure on manufacturing firms to effectively respond to unpredictable and volatile consumer demand. The ability to match supply and demand is arguably key to a firm's success in many industries. Unfortunately, resource capacity investment decisions typically frozen far in advance before the uncertain demand is realized, misalignments between supply and demand are usually inevitable and often times bear severe economic consequences. To hedge against demand uncertainty and heterogeneity, firms have adopted an operations strategy known as process flexibility to better match supply with demand, where flexibility refers to the firm's ability to make each resource “multi-functional” and capable of serving multiple demand classes. There has been evidence that even just a little flexibility, if configured in a right way, can accrue most of the benefits of full flexibility and be extremely effective in mitigating supply-demand mismatch. In particular, the chaining concept has received much attention in the literature and has been applied in practice. In the flexibility literature, the theoretical investigation of the effectiveness of the chaining strategy has mainly focused on balanced (the numbers of resources and demand classes are equal) and symmetric (identical capacities among resources and homogeneous demand) systems, and researchers have used the total sales in units as the evaluation criterion for measuring the performance of different designs. In this proposed project, we seek to investigate effective flexibility designs for general unbalanced and asymmetric systems: given a constrained budget, what is the most effective way to invest flexibility into the system? Since precise knowledge of the full probability distribution of the random demand is rarely available in practice, we plan to adopt a robust optimization approach by only assuming limited distributional information of the random demand and propose a minimax regret framework to study the process flexibility design problems. Moreover, we also plan to introduce price differentials into the system and consider a profit maximization problem, which can arguably capture a wider range of business practice in real applications. 在当今竞争激烈的商业环境中，例如产品扩张和产品生命周期缩减等近来消费市场的发展迫使制造业企业设法有效应对不可预测和不稳定的消费需求。 匹配供需的能力是公司在许多行业取得成功的关键。 但不幸的是，资源产能的投资决策通常远远早于不确定的需求实现之前，因此供需之间的不匹配通常难以避免并且往往会导致严重的经济后果。 为了对抗需求的不确定性和异质性，企业采取了一种称为过程柔性的运营策略以更好地匹配供应与需求，其中柔性是指企业使得每种资源“多功能”从而能够服务多种需求的能力。 有证据表明，即使只有一点点柔性，如果配置得当，可以获得完全柔性的大部分优势并且有效减轻供需不匹配。 其中长链的概念尤其在文献中受到诸多关注，并在实践中得以应用。 在过程柔性的文献中，有关长链策略有效性的理论研究主要集中在平衡（资源和需求的种类数量相等）和对称（相同数量的资源和均质需求）的系统，并且研究人员通常使用总销售数量作为衡量不同设计的绩效的评价标准。在此项目中，我们试图研究对于一般性不平衡和非对称系统的有效柔性过程设计：在有限的预算下，为系统投资柔性的最有效的方法是什么？由于随机需求的准确概率分布在实际应用中几乎不可得，我们只假设已知随机需求的有限分布信息并采用鲁棒优化的方法提出一个极小极大遗憾框架来研究柔性设计的问题。此外，我们还计划在系统中引入价格差异并考虑利润最大化问题，从而可以应用到更广泛的实际问题中。

26500517.label: Realisation of objectives
26500517.value: The objectives of this ECS research project (26500517) have been fully achieved. We next summarize the research activities and outcomes related to the three project objectives stated in the initial proposal. First, we have developed a model that adopts a robust optimization approach to study process flexibility designs for general unbalanced and asymmetric systems. Our model has several prominent features. First, our model considers general production systems that may be unbalanced and/or asymmetric. In particular, the number of products may not be equal to that of the plants, the capacities of the plants may not be identical, and the products demand may not be i.i.d. Second, instead of assuming the exact distributional knowledge of the random demand, our model assumes that each product’s demand belongs to a given uncertainty set, and we propose robust measures that evaluate the worst-case performance of a system against all possible demand realizations in the uncertainty set, which adds robustness of our solution. Finally, our model takes into account the possibility that there may exist profit margin differentials among the products. In the existing operations literature, the theoretical investigation of effective sparse designs has mainly focused on performance metrics based on the maximum sales in units. However, this could lead to substantial profit losses when there exist considerably large profit margin differentials among the products. It is well known that margin differentials are an essential element that affects the value of flexibility. This motivates us to develop a model that assumes product-dependent contribution margin. Second, based on our proposed model, we have developed a new performance metric, which we name as "Dual Margin Group Index (DMGI)", that was proven to provide a sufficient characterization of any flexibility design's worst-case performance under a general class of uncertainty sets and robust performance measures that incorporates product margin differentials. The DMGI uses the dual-variable information of an optimization problem that maximizes the total profit. Intuitively speaking, this dual variable represents the shadow price associated with a product, which captures the marginal profit of an additional unit of demand from this product. For a fully flexible network, it has the best capability to route plant capacities to the appropriate products to achieve the maximum profit potential. However, if a design is sparse with only limited flexibility (i.e., each plant can only fulfill demand from a small subset of products), a subset of plants and a group of products may form a bottleneck that blocks the system from fully utilizing the available plant capacities. The DMGI captures such a bottleneck in the worst case under a given set of dual price vectors. We prove that our proposed DMGI lead to a partial ordering that enables us to evaluate and compare the worst-case performance of different flexibility designs for general asymmetric and unbalanced systems with contribution margin differentials, where designs with larger DMGI values have a better worst-case performance. Third, we have developed an easy-to-implement heuristic based on the DMGI index to generate effective sparse flexibility designs, i.e., designs with limited degree of flexibility. Our proposed DMGI heuristic starts with an initial base flexibility design and iteratively adds arcs sequentially to improve the design’s performance until a pre-determined arc budget is exhausted. The key idea of the algorithm is that, in each iteration, we add an arc that is not yet in the current design to increase the values of DMGI to the greatest extent possible. We have conducted extensive numerical studies to evaluate the effectiveness of our proposed DMGI heuristic. Our numerical results suggest that the sparse designs generated by the DMGI heuristic capture most of the benefit of full flexibility from the expected profit point of view, and has quite satisfactory performance in the worst case for small to moderate levels of demand uncertainty compared with a fully flexible system when product exhibit margin differentials. To further understand the effectiveness of our DMGI heuristic, we have also compared its performance with various algorithms proposed in the literature, most of which do not account for profit margin differentials. We have chosen several well-known heuristics for constructing flexibility designs, including the plant cover index heuristic, expander heuristic, the chaining structures, the sample average approximation approach, the stochastic optimization-based heuristic, the thresholded probabilistic construction algorithm, and the generalized chaining gap based heuristic. Our extensive numerical analysis suggests that the DMGI heuristic achieves superior or comparable performance to the existing benchmarks. Finally, from this research project, we have also achieved additional results beyond the original three project objectives. Based on the characterization that the worst-case performance of a flexibility design can be expressed as functions of a design’s DMGIs and the given uncertainty set, we establish the optimality of a special class of the long-chain designs. More specifically, we proved that a class of long-chain designs, the so-called alternate long chain, is optimal among all long-chain designs where there are two product categories and the number of high-margin products is equal to that of low-margin products, under the so-called partwise independently symmetric uncertainty sets and a broad class of worst-case performance measures. This implies that within the class of long-chain production systems (which is well known for its superior performance among designs with limited flexibility), it is most beneficial to evenly spread out the products from the two product groups in an alternate manner and to equip each plant to be able to produce both high- and low-profit products. Intuitively, in this way the high-profit products never have to directly compete for shared resources. Through extensive numerical studies, we have confirmed that this “spread-out” insight is also robust in more general flexibility designs with multiple profit margin levels.

26500517.label: Major findings and research outcome
26500517.value: The major findings of this research project are summarized as follows. First, we have developed a model that adopts a robust optimization approach to study process flexibility designs where the profit margin differentials among the products are taken into account. Based on our proposed model, we have developed a new performance metric, which we name as "Dual Margin Group Index (DMGI)", that was proven to provide a sufficient characterization of any flexibility design's worst-case performance under a general class of uncertainty sets and robust performance measures that incorporates product margin differentials. Based on this characterization, we further prove that our proposed DMGI index leads to a partial ordering that serves as a tool to compare the worst-case performance of different flexibility designs for general asymmetric and unbalanced systems with contribution margin differentials. Second, we proved that under the so-called partwise independently symmetric uncertainty sets and a broad class of worst-case performance measures, a class of long-chain designs, the so-called alternate long chain, is optimal among all long-chain designs where there are two product categories and the number of high-margin products is equal to that of low-margin products. This implies that within the class of long-chain production systems (which is well known for its superior performance among designs with limited flexibility), it is most beneficial to evenly spread out the products from the two product groups in an alternate manner and to equip each plant to be able to produce both high- and low-profit products. Intuitively, in this way the high-profit products never have to directly compete for shared resources. Finally, we have developed a heuristic based on the DMGI index to generate effective sparse flexibility designs, i.e., designs with limited degree of flexibility. Our numerical results suggest that the sparse designs generated by our DMGI heuristic capture most of the benefit of full flexibility from the expected profit point of view, and has quite satisfactory performance in the worst case for small to moderate levels of demand uncertainty compared with a fully flexible system when product exhibit margin differentials. This project has led to two publications in top-tier journals in the field: Asadpour, Wang and Zhang (2020) published in Management Science; and Wang, Wang and Zhang (2020) published in Manufacturing & Service Operations Management.

26500517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26500517.value: There are several potential avenues to further develop this research, and the PI plans to explore along the following directions. First, we have proposed the DMGI index to compare the worse-case performance of different flexibility designs, and the DMGI heuristic requires solving a series of integer programs. For small-to-medium sized systems, our numerical results suggest that the associated optimization problem can be solved efficiently. However, it is important to develop efficient approaches to make the DMGI heuristic applicable in large-sized systems. Another interesting direction is to investigate whether it is possible to allow profit margins to be plant-product pair specific. In our current model, a product’s contribution margin only depends on the product, but does not depend on from which plant this product is produced.

26500517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26500517.value: In today’s competitive business environment, consumers’ demands have become increasingly uncertain and volatile, which results in misalignment between supply and demand. One operations strategy to mitigate supply-demand mismatch is to introduce flexibility into the system where each plant/resource can fulfill multiple demand classes. It is usually prohibitively expensive to implement a fully flexible system, which calls for the need to find effective sparse systems with limited flexibility. In the existing operations literature, the theoretical investigation of effective sparse designs has mainly focused on performance metrics based on the maximum sales volume. However, this could lead to substantial profit losses when there exist considerably large profit margin differentials among the products. It has been shown in the literature that margin differentials are an essential element that affects the value of flexibility. To address this issue, we developed a model that studies flexibility designs by accounting for contribution margin differentials among the products. We introduced an index that can characterize and compare the performance of different flexibility designs, and developed a heuristic based on this index to construct effective sparse flexibility designs in the presence of product contribution margin differentials.

26501417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26501417.value: In many markets, different products share common or similar attributes. In this research, we consider alternatives with correlated attributes and show that although different alternatives in a choice set are naturally substitutes, demand for them can exhibit complementary effects, if consumers need to search for or learn information about these alternatives. We term this effect "informational complementarity". We investigate when and how this effect arises and examine its robustness, and test the complementarity effect using field experiments. The proposed research can shed light on several important topics in marketing and economics including measuring consumer demand and price elasticities, product line design, and competitive pricing. 许多商品之间是相互关联的。相同品牌下的不同型号可以拥有类似的品牌形象，产品设计，销售服务等等，譬如宝马汽车的不同系列。甚至不同竞争品牌之间的产品在某些维度上也是相似的，譬如宝马和奔驰都有着德国工业制造的印记和类似的引擎技术。 本文通过理论分析发现，即使相关联的产品之间是相互替代的关系，这些产品也会产生互补效应 –– 其中一个产品价格的降低会导致另一个产品的需求增加。这种效应产生的根本原因是消费者需要通过搜索来获取足够的产品信息来做决策。譬如当宝马电动车的价格降低后，消费者会对此感兴趣而搜索相关的产品信息。在搜索的过程中，如果消费者发现宝马电动车的外观设计并不如人意，但电动引擎的性能相当吸引人，他们便会考虑搜索其他电动车如奔驰电动车。那么消费者最终很有可能购买的是奔驰而不是宝马电动车。本研究旨在探索这种基于信息关联的产品互补效应在哪些情况下会出现，以及对价格竞争和产品线设计的影响。

26501417.label: Realisation of objectives
26501417.value: A general theory is successfully developed to model consumers' optimal search for correlated products. The theory characterizes the nature of complementarity among products and identifies the conditions under which complementarity can arise. We apply the mechanism in competitive pricing and show that complementarity can lead to higher equilibrium prices.

26501417.label: Major findings and research outcome
26501417.value: We show that when these attributes are uncertain for consumers, a complementarity effect can arise among competing products, in the sense that the lower price of one product may increase the demands for the others. This effect occurs when consumers sequentially search for information about both common and idiosyncratic product attributes prior to purchase. We characterize the optimal search strategy for the correlated search problem, provide the conditions for the existence of the complementarity effect, and show that the effect is robust under a wide range of alternative assumptions. We further explore the implications of the effect for pricing. When firms compete in price, although product correlation may weaken differentiation between the firms, the complementarity effect due to correlated search may raise equilibrium price and profit.

Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26501417.value: This research looks at a common purchase scenario where consumers choose among multiple options that share some common features. Because of the uncertainty associated with the products, consumers need to search for information before making the decision. We find that this scenario can lead to some degree of complementarity: if one product lowers its price (e.g., through promotion), it will benefit another product even consumers are only interested in purchasing one product. This type of complementarity is due to information search: when consumers acquire information for one product, they will can learn about other products as well. This mechanism has implication for how firms should price in a market with product correlation.

26501617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26501617.value: Mergers and acquisitions (M&As) constitute a huge part of today’s business activities both in China and worldwide. In 2015, there were 9,420 deals worth 734 billion US dollars in China alone. Merger activities pose a challenge to antitrust agencies: antitrust agencies must make sure a merger does not hurt consumers. To achieve this goal, they utilize economic theories and existing merger research to evaluate potential mergers. Most existing merger literature uses price as the key determinant of consumer welfare, and only focuses on price changes caused by a merger. However, it is evident that a large portion of mergers induce firms not only to change price, but also to change two other operational decisions: product quality and variety. It is not clear how such product repositioning interacts with price and affects consumers in a merger. Our goal is to bridge this gap and seek answers to the following question: When product repositioning is considered, do the results and intuitions obtained in existing studies focusing on price changes still hold? We aim to gain a comprehensive understanding of how firms change their price, quality and variety as a result of mergers, and how such changes affect consumers. Given the large numbers of mergers in China, understanding them thoroughly will be socially influential for both firms and consumers. We propose to construct a game-theoretic model to understand the role of quality and variety decisions in a merger. We plan to study a merger of two firms in a market with more than two firms. In this market, firms have identical cost structures, but may offer product of different qualities and charge different prices to compete with each other. Consumers in this market all prefer higher quality, but differ in their willingness to pay for higher quality. We hope to find how fundamental economic forces, such as competition, cost reduction, and positions of merging firms, affect firms’ operational decisions after mergers. Using these findings, we can provide concrete guidelines for making optimal post-merger decisions. Moreover, we will study how these forces affect consumer welfare following mergers. We expect to use these findings to generate policy implications for antitrust agencies and help them to evaluate potential mergers better. As a result, consumers in China and in other countries where mergers are regulated can benefit from optimal decision making. Finally, we will enrich the current literature on mergers with new insights into quality and variety. 併購是當今商業活動的重要組成部分。在2015年中國總共有9420項總價值達7340億美元的併購活動。反壟斷機構必須要認真核查每一項併購申請以確認併購不會傷害到消費者。反壟斷機構用已有的併購研究來審核併購申請。大部分併購文獻用商品價格作為主要的指標來衡量併購是否會對消費者產生消極影響。但是很多併購不僅會改變價格，同樣也會改變併購後售賣商品的質量和種類。這 種商品的重新定位是否會影響到消費者在已有的研究文獻中尚不明確。我們的目標是回答這個問題：如果併購會造成商品的重新定位，那以前研究文獻中關於價格的結論是否成立。 我們將建立一個博弈論模型來分析商品質量和種類在併購中的角色。我們將要研究研究以下市場的併購：在這個市場中有三個或以上的公司出售不同質量的產品；消費者更加傾向於購買高質量產品，但他們願意付的價格是不一樣的。 我們希望找到競爭，成本和市場定位對於公司併購後的產品策略的影響，用以指導公司在併購後的決策。我們會更加進一步研究這些產品策略對消費者的影響， 給反壟斷機構決策提供理論支持，以幫助他們更加有效地審核併購申請。

26501617.label: Realisation of objectives
26501617.value: 1. To investigate the relationship between fundamental economic forces and firms’ post-merger equilibrium decisions of price, quality, and variety. This objective has been fully achieved. The PI has investigated the following economic forces that can affect firms’ decision of price, quality and variety after a merger: consumer valuation, market sizes, tariffs, uncertainty, competition, regulation, and cost reduction. In the research output “The Impact of the Tariffs and Price Premiums of Locally Manufactured Products on Global Manufacturers’ Sourcing Strategies,” the PI investigates how consumer valuation, tariffs, and market sizes affect a firm’s decision whether to conduct a merger of sourcing business units across different manufacturing sites and the firm’s subsequent decision on price and quality. The firm sell products overseas and in the domestic market. The firm can source product from each market separately. The firm can also conduct a merger of sourcing business units across different manufacturing sites and source all product from overseas and gain bargaining power against the foreign supplier. Consumers regard the product sourced domestically of higher quality and possess higher valuation on them. The paper finds that higher valuation of product sourced domestically can discourage the merger of sourcing business units and promote the firm to produce higher-quality products. Different market sizes of the foreign and domestic market can encourage the firm to conduct the merger and produce lower-quality products. Tariffs can promote the merger and lower-quality products when the tariff rate is sufficiently large. In the research output “Green Technology Development and Adoption: Competition, Regulation, and Uncertainty—A Global Game Approach,” the PI investigates how uncertainty and competition affect firms’ collusion in improving product quality to achieve less environmental impact. Such collusion and coordination can be created after a merger of multiple firms. The PI finds that firms’ collusion in improving product quality is strongly affected by uncertainty and competition. Specifically, when competition is intense, uncertainty can promote firms’ collusion in improving product quality to achieve less environmental impact. Furthermore, government regulation that encourages collusion among firms can perform better at promoting higher quality product that have less environmental impact compared to government regulation that is independent of firms’ collusion. In the research output “Mergers, Quality and Variety: Evidence from the Airline Industry,” the PI analyzes how heterogeneous consumer valuation, competition, and cost reduction affect firms’ price and variety decisions. If cost reduction is small, the firm that is created by a merger of two firms should continue the pre-merger product offerings. If cost reduction is sufficiently large, the firm should consolidate its product offering and reduce variety. After reducing variety, the firm should choose quality and price levels between those of the two pre-merger products. 2. To provide guidelines for firms to make optimal decisions in post-merger markets. This objective has been fully achieved. In the research output “The Impact of the Tariffs and Price Premiums of Locally Manufactured Products on Global Manufacturers’ Sourcing Strategies,” the PI provided the following guideline for firms that make decision whether to conduct a merger of their sourcing business units across different sites. First, if consumers’ valuation on products sourced domestically is sufficiently high, or the import tariff rate is moderate, then the firm should not merge the sourcing business units; instead, the firm should source products from suppliers within the same countries as the consumers. In this way, the firm can produce higher-quality product for the domestic market and charge higher prices. Second, if the foreign and domestic market sizes are very different, the firm should conduct the merger and source all products from the foreign supplier. In this way, the firm can gain greater bargaining power against the supplier. The firm should produce lower-quality products and charge lower prices. In the research output “Mergers, Quality and Variety: Evidence from the Airline Industry,” the PI provided the following guidelines. If cost reduction is small, the firm that is created by a merger of two firms should continue the pre-merger product offerings. If cost reduction is sufficiently large, the firm should consolidate its product offering and reduce variety. After reducing variety, the firm should choose quality and price levels between those of the two pre-merger products. In the research output “Green Technology Development and Adoption: Competition, Regulation, and Uncertainty—A Global Game Approach,” the PI provided the following guidelines for firms to collude in achieving higher quality for lower environmental impact. If competition is mild, or regulation is stringent, then the firms should collude in achieving the higher quality. If uncertainty is large, a firm can initial the collusion and try to achieve the higher quality. 3. To generate policy implications through which antitrust agencies can evaluate potential mergers better. In the research output “Mergers, Quality and Variety: Evidence from the Airline Industry,” the PI provided the following policy implications. Cost reduction generated in a merger can actually reduce variety and hurt consumers if the cost reduction is moderate. Therefore, the government should treat cost reduction in a merger with cautions In the research output “Green Technology Development and Adoption: Competition, Regulation, and Uncertainty—A Global Game Approach,” the PI provided the following policy implications. If the payoff for improving quality to reduce environmental impact is small, the government should enforce a more stringent regulation to encourage collusions among firms. This objective has been fully achieved. In the research output “The Impact of the Tariffs and Price Premiums of Locally Manufactured Products on Global Manufacturers’ Sourcing Strategies,” the PI provided the following policy implications for a government. Increasing the tariff rate can sometimes encourage a firm’s decision on a merger of its sourcing business units, but such a merger might hurt consumers. This happens when consumer valuation is sufficiently large. 4. To provide a framework for future research on mergers with quality and variety decisions. This objective has been fully achieved. The research output “The Impact of the Tariffs and Price Premiums of Locally Manufactured Products on Global Manufacturers’ Sourcing Strategies” provides a framework to analyze a merger of business units and its impact on quality in different manufacturing sites. The research output “Mergers, Quality and Variety: Evidence from the Airline Industry” provides a framework to analyze a merger in a vertically differentiated market and its impact on subsequent price and variety decisions.

26501617.label: Major findings and research outcome
26501617.value: Our works contribute to both theoretical and empirical merger research by jointly evaluating the roles of quality, variety and prices. Specially, the research output “Mergers, Quality and Variety: Evidence from the Airline Industry” develops an analytical tool to study mergers between vertically differentiated firms with subsequent product repositioning decisions, as well as providing empirical support for the theoretical findings. This work finds that cost reduction in a merger can promote variety reduction and hurt consumers. The research output “Green Technology Development and Adoption: Competition, Regulation, and Uncertainty—A Global Game Approach” provides insight into how the uncertainty of the payoff of a higher quality and the strategic complementarity induced by regulation, jointly affect firms’ incentive to collude on improving quality. The strategic complementarity and uncertainty have not been examined in literature. This work finds that if the government adopts a regulation scheme that takes into account firms’ collusion, the government can better promote higher quality for less environmental impact if the payoff for the higher quality is small. The research output “The Impact of the Tariffs and Price Premiums of Locally Manufactured Products on Global Manufacturers’ Sourcing Strategies” analyzes the strategic interaction between a manufacturer and its supplier when the manufacturer can conduct a merger of its sourcing business units and face import tariffs and heterogeneous valuation on its products. This work finds that the merger can enhance the manufacturer’s bargaining power and reduce wholesale price, which can benefit consumers. But the merger also causes the manufacturer to reduce perceived product quality. Such a merger might benefit consumers if consumers’ valuation on higher perceived quality is not sufficiently large. Raising tariffs might hurt consumers.

26501617.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26501617.value: In the current research, the price and quality decisions are analyzed in a two-tier supply chain, but the variety decision is studied without analyzing the impact of supply chains and suppliers. This is because typically a supply chain consists of multiple tiers with several players. Most papers on supply chain analyze a single product. Using a single product setting we can analyze firms’ price and quality decisions, but we cannot analyze variety decisions, which require multiple products. A potential further development of research is to study the variety decision in a supply setting. The basic setting in “The Impact of the Tariffs and Price Premiums of Locally Manufactured Products on Global Manufacturers’ Sourcing Strategies” is about the supply chain of a single product. The setting can be modified to analyze multiple products. We might have to simplify some other part, such as abstracting away from competition.

26501617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26501617.value: A merger can create collusion among firms and hurt consumers. Most existing research on focuses on merger-induced price change and its impact on consumers. However, a merger might also induce firms to change quality and variety, and it can also cause strategic responses of players in other tiers of a supply chain. In addition, government regulation can also affect firms’ collusion on achieving higher quality. It is not clear how the merger-induced quality and variety changes and strategic responses of players in other tiers of a supply chain affect consumers. Our work analyzes the impact of these factors in different scenarios, including a vertically differentiated market, a global supply chain with multinational firms selling in different countries, and a market in which firms have pressure to improve quality and reduce environmental impacts. The findings of this project provide understanding on when these factors can have positive impacts on consumers as well as the society.

26505117.label: Project Objectives
26505117.value: To develop a theory of political spillovers To empirically test the predictions of the theory using the data from the US Senate
rows: To develop a theory of political spillovers
To empirically test the predictions of the theory using the data from the US Senate

26505117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26505117.value: The decisions of elected politicians can affect the welfare of not only their own constituency, but the constituencies of other politicians. For example, if Arizona elects a governor that makes it easier for undocumented immigrants to pass through the state, Californian farmworkers may see their wages drop and vote for a higher state minimum wage. A theory is needed to understand the nature of political spillovers and the dynamics of transmission of shocks in one region's election to other region's elections. We propose to study political spillovers in a dynamic setting. Two regions elect politicians to bargain over the allocation of resources to the production of local goods for the regions and a global public good. The voters face a trade-off: they would like to elect a "nationalist" to get more local goods now, but they would like also to elect an "internationalist" to increase future resources and give incentives for the other region to elect an "internationalist". Informed by the theoretical model, we intend to test the spillovers empirically. We construct a measure of how much each US senator has managed to allocate federal spending to his constituency, and use this measure for the senators not up for re-election to predict the measure for the incoming class of senators. Our research will further our understanding of political dynamics. For instance, if the complementarity in policies explains why sometimes political change happens in waves, like the recent rise in right-wing populism in many European countries. Our findings can have important policy implications for the span of control of political entities such as the European Union and the value of shared production of public goods for political stability. 當選政客的決策不僅可以影響所在選區的福利，也可以對其他政客的選民產生影響。比如，如果亞利桑那州的選舉使得非法移民更加容易穿越本州，加利福尼亞州的農場工人可能會發現工資降低，因而投票支持提高最低工資。為了研究政治溢出效應的性質，以及沖擊的跨選區動態傳遞，我們需要建立一個理論模型。我們將在動態的設定下研究政治溢出效應。兩個選區投票選舉政客來商議資源應如何在生產地區性商品和全球性公共商品間分配。選民們面對如下權衡：支持“本土派”會帶來更多地區性商品，但人們也想通過支持“國際派”來增加未來可用資源以及激勵另一選區共同支持“國際派”。在理論研究的基礎上，我們將實證檢驗溢出效應。我們構造指標來衡量每個美國參議員曾分配多少聯邦支出到自己的選區，並利用不繼續參選議員的該指標來預測新一批議員的相應指標。我們的研究將幫助進一步理解政治動態效應。比如，政策的互補性能否解釋為何政策變化時常呈波浪式出現，例如最近許多歐洲國家正在興起的民粹主義。我們的發現會對於歐盟等政治實體的控制範圍問題和為確保政治穩定的公共商品的共同生產及其利益共享等問題產生重要的政策建議。

26505117.label: Realisation of objectives
26505117.value: The project includes both theoretical and empirical analysis. Most of the theory work has been completed. But the empirical work is still in progress. Two main reasons that the project has not been completed so far are i) my coauthor, Artturi Bjork, left academia and took up a governmental position in Ministry of Finance in Finland, and ii) the data collection for the empirical work took longer than expected and still requires effort to clean. I hired a part-time research assistant to collect the data. She worked around 9 months on part-time basis. But then in the middle of the data collection process she started her PhD studies in Estonia and left Hong Kong. Once the data collection and cleaning is completed, the empirical analysis will not take long. I expect data to be ready by Summer 2022 and the project to be completed by the end of 2022.

26505317.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26505317.value: The extant literature on CEO fixed effects and auditor fixed effects documents substantive influence of the CEO's and audit partner's personal characteristics on corporate decisions and financial reporting quality. Recent studies even suggest that CEO fixed effects are strengthened rather than mitigated over time, and that the cross-sectional variation in CEO fixed effects matches company demand for CEO styles. While financial reporting quality is jointly determined by key corporate personnel and external auditors, studies of CEO fixed effects and studies of individual auditors appear to ignore the potential influence of each other. Will companies take into account the confrontation between a conservative audit partner and an aggressive CEO when appointing a new CEO or engaging a new audit partner? Will companies waste resources by engaging a conservative auditor when it already has a risk-averse CEO? In addition, to what extent do the attitudes of an audit partner and a senior manager affect each other? This study aims at understanding how the psychological characteristics and traits of the key corporate personnel and external auditors interact in the accounting process. It will rely on a new dataset of personal background information to execute the empirical analyses. 研究文獻指出公司經理人與外部會計師的個人特質對公司財報品質與公司決策皆有顯著影響. 近年來的研究更指出公司經理人的個人特質對公司的影響隨著時間增強而非減弱, 而且這種個人特質與公司所需要經理人類型恰好吻合. 雖然公司財報品質是由公司重要決策人士與外部會計師共同決定的, 但是目前的研究並沒有將他們的互動考慮在內. 公司在選擇新會計師時, 會同時考慮他和原有經理人的類型是相同或相異的嗎? 公司經理人和會計師對財報態度的差異會如何影響最終財報結果? 本研究將利用個人背景資料庫, 探討公司經理人和會計師的心理特質和行為模式如何影響會計決策.

26600717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26600717.value: This project will apply marriage networking approach to examine about 70-odd elite families in three counties with focus on their respective marriage betrothal patterns. The purpose is to revisit the prevalent assumption that Chinese elites’ approach to marriage contracts during the Qing remained locally focused, with marriage arranged mainly among the local elites at county or township level. Specifically, this proposed project posits that higher status elites, namely those with government positions of county magistrate level or above and those who held jinshi and juren degree statuses, were more likely to marry their offspring to other members of the national elite, irrespective of their hometown’s location. In this way, their concern is the maintenance and extension of a national network that was useful in the sociopolitical arena of a national elite, rather than one that was primarily focused on the local area. If shown to be true, then this pattern represents a significant shift from the model of marriage strategy dominant in the field since the 1980s and suggests that a network of nationally oriented elites might be in operation at least in some important localities during the Qing. It will invite further investigation on a broader geographic scope and suggest qualification of the aforementioned prevailing assumption in scholarship. This neglected Qing phenomenon of national-oriented marriage strategy of Chinese elites could have important bearing on our understanding of the family-based characteristics of Chinese national elites through the 20th century. It is well known that princelings, now a term used to describe descendants of high ranking Communist Party of China members, is an important component of the top leadership of the People’s Republic of China. The proposed project promises to shed new light on this current political power structure by suggesting the continuity of a Chinese elite marriage pattern dated back to the 18th century. 在１９８０年代以來的歷史研究角度看來， 清代士族延續了南宋以來”地區菁英”的模式，主要以鞏固自己家族的在地勢力與身分為目的。其中一種鞏固家族身分的策略是與同一地區的其他士族通婚。這個課題會以清代士族的婚姻策略為主題，重新探討清代江南菁英士族的通婚策略。主要的研究對象是身分地位比較高的家族分支，把每個家族的各個分支作出區別，來仔細分析家族成員在官僚體制中的身分高低對下一代的通婚策略的影響力，尤其是全國性的通婚網絡在官員家族中的普遍性。研究計畫先以幾個縣為出發點，集中研究當地士族的婚姻網絡與通婚策略，從而分析清代官員家族中互相聯婚的網絡，重新評估清代再次出現一個全國性的通婚網絡與菁英階層的可能性。

26600717.label: Realisation of objectives
26600717.value: This project aimed to revise our understand of marriage strategy of Qing dynasty elites. The original conception was to use snowball sampling to generate a network of marriages among elites of the Qing, especially in the mid to late Qing, and to try to map out how they married each other, whom they married, and to differentiate such marriages by social stratum. The hypothesis was that higher status family branches were more likely to marry out of county, and that local marriages were predominantly for lower status members of the same families. Thus, the discourse surrounding “local” elites needs to be revised for the Qing as there emerged a group of elites with a national-outlook and who married each other without reservation when it comes to geographic location. The main thrust of research for this project was to conduct a time consuming coding effort of a significant number of genealogies with relevant cases. While some genealogies are available online, many are not and require physical presence in local archives and libraries to photocopy and then transcribe onto a spreadsheet. I had made one trip to the Shanghai municipal library, where they have a significant holding of genealogies, and found a number of genealogies that were useful. Coding of information was also ongoing throughout 2018-2019 with information that I could glean online and on hand with the aid of a research assistant. While planning for a second trip that was to take place in early 2020, the Covid-19 pandemic hit and essentially halted all in-person research activities in terms of visiting libraries and archives. While waiting for the borders to reopen, I revised down the objectives from the more ambitious goal originally to something more manageable with materials I already had and that I could muster online. While many genealogies are available in theory, the number of useable ones are much less as most genealogies available online are from families that contain little to no official elites from the Qing dynasty. Combing through them to find useable ones is a time consuming process, and quite often when they do not connect with any other existing genealogies the value of a lone datapoint for one lineage is very low. Therefore, the amount of useable information online is much less than it seems. In the end, I was able to code about 30 useable genealogies for my project. Using some of the earlier-gathered information, I have presented an early set of findings at the annual meeting of Association for Asian Studies in 2021. I have also submitted a revised version of that paper to the journal T’oung Pao for review, using data from about seven families that I have examined in closer detail. At the moment as the borders are still closed, it is difficult to see how I can continue to extend the scope of the research project to approach some of the more ambitious goals of my original proposal, such as a mapping of datapoints on a GIS project. While I have worked with students here to produce visualizations of the data I have at hand, the fact of the matter is the density of the data is not sufficiently large for me to feel comfortable to draw firmer conclusions on some of the major points I would like to make originally. While the submitted article does make arguments regarding points outlined in objectives 2-4, more data would be welcomed to make firmer claims on these points. This is not at all to say that the project was a failure. The collection of data that I have conducted is already quite extensive, and likely larger than information anyone else has gathered specifically on the marriage pattern of elites of the Qing dynasty. I intend to build upon the work done here as borders finally reopen and I am able to visit the document depositories in order to collect further information, especially using the approach originally proposed in focusing on a few counties and then to branch out from there using a snowball sampling method. Looking ahead, I hope to write additional articles using materials I have gathered here to examine the questions I had posed in the project, and what I have built already is a solid foundation for a more fundamental reenvisioning of elite marriage strategy in the Qing dynasty.

26600717.label: Major findings and research outcome
26600717.value: I have found that elite families in the mid to late Qing arranged marriages for their members according to their own sociopolitical status. Using a number of case studies, the article "We are all a family" argues that branches of elite lineages preferred to marry for political advantage, instead of focusing on consolidating local status. This is contrary to prevailing assumption that elites in the Qing were still following the Song-Yuan-Ming model of localism. I suggest that there may be multiple reasons why this change in strategy appeared. One was the existence of office purchase, which guaranteed official status for families and thus made it more appealing to find political allies in the civil service through marriage. Another reason is that the late Qing disruptions, especially the Taiping Rebellion, drove elites together into safe-havens and also put them in contact with each other in a way that earlier dynasties did not. Therefore, they had more reason to engage with each other in arranging marriages. While I have been able to conduct the majority of the research goals outlined in the proposal, I have been unable to use any of the conference or education grants. As we well know, Covid-19 had completely stopped academic conferences, and our university disallowed work-related travel since the outbreak began in 2020. The one major conference that I would have attended was canceled and moved online, and no new conferences were held that would have allowed me to use any of the funds allocated. Likewise, while I was able to work with an undergraduate in her advanced coursework using the data I have gathered, since she was doing so under the guise of enrolling in a course there was no monetary compensation paid to her. A student I had arranged to work with me in 2019 who would have been paid for some work left Hong Kong abruptly in summer of 2019 as the social unrest spread. Since then because of the mostly online nature of pedagogy and the general difficulty of planning and working around such limitations, no money was spent from the educational funds.

26600717.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26600717.value: I would very much like to extend the research into a social network analysis type of project with the collection of more data as time and opportunity would allow. As much of the genealogies in various collections are virtually untapped resources, it is simply a matter of time in order to exploit them for further research. The unfortunate timing of Covid-19 and the still-suspended travel between Hong Kong and mainland China has made this research virtually impossible, but with the eventual resumption of travel I look forward to collecting more data to further study this question and to prove more comprehensively the points I have made so far in my research article.

26600717.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26600717.value: This project finds that elites in the Qing dynasty married for political advantage in a way that previous scholars have assumed to not occur. As one's social status rose, the likelihood of one's marriage being away from one's home county also rose. This applied equally to the men and women of these elite families, and suggest a conscious strategy to form alliances that were useful politically in advancing careers of the family's members in the civil service.

27106417.value: 香港的自然環境仿如一個”運行中”的實驗，為我們提供了一個極好的研究機會。本港的原始森林在數世紀前被完全砍伐，而現存的植被則呈梯度變化，從草原以至成熟的次生林，共佔全港土地面積的40％。 這些生境的環境條件各異，是形成不同物種群落的重要因素。而要預測整個物種群落及目標物種的演替，其研究關鍵在於理解物種分佈及其功能性狀（如形態）於植被梯度的變化。 在此研究中，我將沿植被梯度調查非生物和生物因子於構建物種群落的重要性。本項目將側重測試在三個不同時間維度下螞蟻群落的變化，包括長期（> 22年）﹑季節性和晝夜，並作以下假設：在早期的植被演替過程中，非生物因子將會主導物種選擇及其組成；而到植被演替的後期階段，生物因子將取代非生物因子成為影響物種選擇及其組成的主要因素。而在更短的時間維度中，由於非生物因子的晝夜和季節變化，將允許具有不同功能性狀的物種在相似的生境內共存。本研究將以功能多樣性研究法，结合群落中各物種的形態﹑生理和行為上的性狀差異，來量化非生物（例如表面溫度，太陽輻射）和生物（例如種間競爭）因子對物種群落組成和活動週期的影響。長期的螞蟻群落研究方面，將以22年前於本港主要不同植被類型內137個不同樣地收集得來的資料，結合最新調查和行為實驗所得的數據，共同分析群落中物種豐度﹑組成﹑優勢和功能性狀在長時間維度下的變化。而螞蟻群落的短期變化，則會結合冬夏兩季以晝夜兩段時間為單位的採樣模式和行為觀察，量化評估溫度﹑太陽輻射和種間競爭對螞蟻群落結構的重要性。這項研究將有助了解各功能性狀如何於不同的生境有利或限制物種的分佈。為今後本地和毗鄰區域的螞蟻品種多樣性及群落組成機制奠定基礎。在受到高度干擾和生物入侵的本港自然生境，鑑定出有利或限制物種生存的有關性狀，可有助塑造利於本地物種和限制外來物種傳播的生境。

27106417.label: Realisation of objectives
27106417.value: To this point all objectives have been fully completed, while the results of the objective five are not yet published (one manuscript under review and more manuscripts to be submitted in the Fall 2022-early 2023). Objective 1. An extensive collection of the ants of Hong Kong has been developed and is now hosted within the Insect Biodiversity and Biogeography Laboratory of the P.I. The material collected during this project, as well as in other projects, has already allowed the publication of two major taxonomic reviews for the genera Strumigenys (Tang et al. 2019) and Polyrhachis (Wong & Guénard 2021) in Hong Kong. These studies have allowed the discovery of 12 and 8 new species records, including the descriptions of 3 and 4 species respectively. Additionally, more taxonomic work, using the material collected, is being currently developed including the preparation of a completed checklist of the ants of Hong Kong. Objective 2. The trait database developed allows a functional ecology approach in several of the studies performed during the past years. The data collected have allowed to determine the inherent sampling biases emerging in functional trait measurements in function of two sampling methods commonly used in ecology (Lee & Guénard 2019); the value of different forest habitat types (Nooten et al. 2021); the importance of particular groups of ants in function of their body-size while performing decomposition function (Nooten et al. 2022), and to determine the importance of stochastic processes within disturbed forests of Hong Kong (Nooten & Guénard submitted). This dataset has also been used in two studies focusing on the impacts and mechanisms of biological invasions on local ant communities (Wong et al. 2021; submitted). Objective 3. Early in this project, it appeared that a major gap in literature existed while performing measurements of Critical Thermal maximum in ants. A review of literature indicated that no standardized protocol existed; with different methodologies in the ramping rates used generating results with wide variation, ultimately influencing the conclusions reached within a particular study. We decided to use 27 species of ants to investigate and identify the approach generating the most reliable and biological relevant results through the use of two experimental and one observational datasets. Our results show that the use of slow ramping rate (e.g. 0.2ºC min-1) generate inconsistent and contradicting results in comparison of field data, hindering the detection of a phylogenetic signal during analyses. On the contrary, faster ramping rate (e.g. 1ºC min-1) provides more robust estimate of the upper critical thermal limit in ants and is thus recommended (Leong et al. 2022). Objective 4. We studied the taxonomic, functional and phylogenetic changes of ant communities between open (grasslands & shrublands) and closed-canopy (forests with > 75% canopy cover) habitats over a two decades’ period. Our results shown high species turnover of ant species in both open- and closed-canopy habitats over a two decades’ period. These changes were mainly driven by high temperature and to a lesser extent by leaf-litter cover in open habitat, but not in forests. In contrast, within forests, the impacts of high temperature were mainly buffered by the presence of tree canopy, except for sites with limited canopy cover (young forest) were shifts toward smaller body-size communities were observed. Overall, these results show the dynamism of communities over multiple decades as well the relatively high species richness and distinct composition between habitats. It also highlights the importance of restoring canopy cover within forested habitats to limit the effects of high temperature and climate warming on particular species communities (Lee et al. 2021). Objective 5. At this point, some of the data analyses and writing are still in progress, while a manuscript is currently being considered for publication. In the latter, we investigate the niche-based or neutral assembly mechanisms in ground dwelling ants, from community data and used fine-scale resolution climatic data to understand the drivers of taxonomic, functional and phylogenetic diversity. Using the wide range of topographic and climatic differences observed at a relatively small geographic scale within Hong Kong, our results highlight the importance of precipitation in shaping community richness, while stochastic processes underlay phylogenetic diversity. A fourth corner analyses assessing the interaction strength of species traits and environmental variables revealed a functional homogenization towards shorter appendages length at wetter sites. Overall, this research shows that phylogenetic and functional diversity within incipient tropical ant assemblages underlie different drivers, with the former being neutral and the latter niche-based. In a separate study (in preparation), we investigated the fine-scale changes in species composition and activities over 24 hours’ period in open- and closed-canopy habitats and across the dry and wet seasons. Our results showed the significant temporal overlap of ant activities and the high species composition changes (beta diversity) of ant communities within a day, especially for communities in open habitats. The high composition changes of ant community are mainly driven by species replacement (i.e. turnover,), especially for communities of open habitat during the dry season. However, ant communities in closed-canopy habitat during dry season present significantly lower temporal foraging overlap and turnover. Thus, the diel dynamics of ants are influenced by both seasonality and habitat structure, with communities in open habitat being consistently dynamic along the diel cycle in different seasons while ant species in closed-canopy habitat are more restricted in diel foraging activities during the dry season. In addition, we quantified the spatial aggregation and average temporal dissimilarity of ant composition over time (every 2 hours) within the community and used a null model approach to test for significance. A strong and significant species turnover is observed in ant communities within open habitat during the warmer periods of daytime, with the turnover being higher during the dry season than in the wet season; while a stronger nestedness is encountered within ant communities of closed-canopy habitat during the dry season. This suggests that daily dynamics of ant communities are highly structured, rather than random, with fluctuating assembly processes influenced by both seasonality and habitats. Thus, ant species present larger temporal tolerance to microhabitat heterogeneity in open habitat and larger spatial tolerance in closed habitat. It reveals that species in open habitat are more likely to shift their activity period to avoid extreme temperatures or dominant competitors while in closed-canopy habitats, the heterogenous microhabitats provide more opportunities for foraging. The analyses of fine-scale microhabitat characteristics and its influence on ants were measured with thermal guns and infrared camera to capture the temperature of ground surface and foraging ant bodies. The results show a high heterogeneity of thermal landscape in ant microhabitats based on the high-resolution thermal images, in which the temperature difference within 0.3 m2 can reach over 6 °C on average and even 20 °C during the daytime in wet season. The thermal heterogeneity and average temperature are significantly higher in the open habitat than closed habitat. The body temperature of foraging ants closely tracks the average ground surface temperature with the average variation lower than 1°C which is significantly lower than the difference with maximum or minimum ground temperature. These results highlight the behavioral regulation of ants avoiding the extreme temperatures and suggest that average ground surface temperature can predict ants’ body temperature.

27106417.label: Major findings and research outcome
27106417.value: This project has allowed several advancements on the understanding of the factors structuring small ground-dwelling ectotherms communities and identify the complexity of the variables influencing species composition, richness and activity over space and time and at different scales. In particular, our results demonstrate the importance of closed-canopy habitats in buffering the effects of high temperature. Two studies in particular have shown the importance of canopy and of its extent in mitigating impacts of high temperature on species composition and body size of ants (Lee et al. 2021) and of forest age in preserving diverse ant communities, including specialist species, and in limiting biological invasions spread (Nooten et al. 2021). The development of a trait database has also opened up new opportunities for the study of entire communities in functional ecology, and provided a strong baseline for understanding underlying mechanisms during biological invasions. Those results are particularly important to establish future plans to mitigate the effects of global change and predict shift in species composition. Understanding species composition shift is paramount as, under the effects of disturbance, species extinctions are not random but affect principally larger species (Lee et al. 2021). We thus studied the consequences of the extinction of particular body size range on ecosystem functions (e.g. decomposition) and discovered the disproportionate role played by large ants, while medium and small species effects remain limited (Nooten et al. 2022). The rise of the functional ecology approach over the past decade in ant ecology has led to a plethora of studies, but not of a systematic test of a number of assumptions during data collection. Here, we used the data collected to directly investigate potential biases emerging from the use of particular sampling methodology or through the measurement of ecophysiological traits. Our results clearly demonstrate the importance of such biases and illustrate how ecologists should consider those in their study design and in their interpretation of the results. To this point, this project has directly or partially contributed to the publication of eight articles in various fields of research including taxonomy (2 publications) and ecology (six publications), with a further two manuscripts currently under review (one with minor and one with major revisions) and five more manuscripts being prepared (2 in ecology and 3 in taxonomy).

27106417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27106417.value: The different datasets assembled and specimens collected during this project represent a rare extensive example of data from a subtropical region. Without doubt, the exploitation of those samples will continue to refine the understanding of the taxonomic and functional diversity of ants in Hong Kong, as well as of the mechanisms leading to community assembly rules within subtropical regions and along a wide vegetation gradient (e.g. Lee et al. submitted). The values of this dataset is particularly important as a debate on the response of insects to global change has emerged in recent years, with long-term datasets on insect community within tropical regions being particularly scarce. As a result, in the future, a proposal allowing to resample those sites while continuing the recording of abiotic variables at a fine-scale level would be invaluable. Finally, the material collected is invaluable to perform taxonomic revisions in a region considered as one of the hotspot for biodiversity, but limited by a lack of modern revisions for numerous taxa. Lee R.H., I.H.Y. Kwong, T.P.N. Tsang, M.K.L. Wong, & B. Guénard (Submitted) Remotely-sensed vegetation structures, topography and disturbances history predict subtropical ant diversity in a degraded landscape. Journal of Ecology (invited).

27106417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27106417.value: Understanding the factors driving species diversity and composition represents one of the main goals of ecology. In this project, extensive surveys conducted across a wide range of vegetation types in Hong Kong and using taxonomic, functional (species traits) and phylogenetic (evolutionary relationships) approaches have allowed to identify some of the key factors structuring ant communities over space and time. The results highlight the importance of canopy cover and forest age in limiting the effects of global changes, either by mitigating impacts of high temperature on species composition and body size, or by limiting the spread of invasive species. In open habitats, however, species communities are characterized by their extreme flexibility and dynamism to cope with temporary extreme conditions leading to strong composition changes during the hottest period of the year. The effects of temperature on ants appear as a strong structuring factor over both long- (>20 years) and short (24 hours) periods of time; highlighting the importance of successfully assessing species ability to cope with temperature. To that extent, a new approach to measure the maximum thermal limits of insects was developed, to accurately predict future effects of global warming on community composition, structure and ecosystem functions.

27115317.label: Major findings and research outcome
27115317.value: In this project, by analyzing several lines of phospho-deficient mouse models, including phospho-mutant and phospho-reduced knock-in mouse models, we demonstrated that Wnt-induced Vangl2 phosphorylation is dose-dependently required for PCP in mammalian development (Cell Res 2017). We revealed that CK1 is the kinase responsible for Vangl2 phosphorylation in response to Wnt stimulation and CK1 genetically interacts with Vangl2 (Cell Res 2017). We also showed that Wnt5a functions as a global instructive cue for PCP in limb development and Wnt5a-induced Vangl2 phosphorylation mediates this process (Development 2018). In a more recent study, we found that phosphorylation inhibited Vangl2 degradation in the ER and promoted Vangl2 export from the ER to the cell surface, where hyper-phosphorylated Vangl2 are stabilized to function as key Wnt/PCP signaling molecules (Sci Adv 2021).

27115317.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27115317.value: 1. Based on the results from this project, we proposed a phosphorylation-regulated “Vangl activity gradient” model in addition to the well-documented “Fz activity gradient” model in Wnt/PCP signaling. This provided a basis for further dissection of the mechanism of Wnt-regulated PCP signaling. 2. The study of Vangl2 phosphorylation in this project found that phospho-mutant Vangl2 is highly ubiquitinated. This prompted us to study the mechanism of Vangl2 ubiquitination, and we successfully identified the E3 ubiquitin ligase complex that ubiquitinate Vangl2. Supported by another GRF grant, we studied the regulation of Vangl2 ubiquitination and its crosstalk with Vangl2 phosphorylation, leading to a publication in Sci Adv recently.

27115317.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27115317.value: Wnt/PCP signaling plays critical roles in cellular, developmental, and physiological processes and its dysregulation causes a growing list of human diseases such as spina bifida, skeletal disorders, neurological disorders, and various cancers. Our work identified a key regulatory mechanism of Wnt/PCP signaling, in which phosphorylation of one of the core proteins, Vangl2, mediates the upstream Wnt signaling to regulate PCP establishment. As aberrant activation of Wnt/PCP signaling is strongly associated with cancer progression, our findings reveal new directions to develop therapeutic tools targeting Wnt/PCP-associated cancers, such as breast cancer and rhabdomyosarcoma.

27200917.value: 隨著世界人口的增加，不安全的淡水供應的令人不安的現實仍然是公共衛生和糧食安全的嚴重威脅。據估計，這個行星可接近的淡水的70％被農業部門使用，這也是水降解和污染的主要來源和受害者。廢水和污染的地表/地下水的特殊用途已經被證明是新鮮的，原始消費的水果和蔬菜的致病性污染的可能來源，特別是通過糞便污染的灌溉水系統。 無論淡水的來源或質量如何，設計用於通過各種形式的管道進行配水的基礎設施將不可避免地以生物膜的形式暴露於微生物的定居：嵌入自生產的外來物質的表面微生態系統（ EPS）。不幸的是，缺乏連接微生物多樣性，功能和結構的信息導致了這些灌溉水分配系統（IWDS）的微生物學知識的知識差距，特別是與其在保護和增殖水源性病原體方面的具體作用有關。因此，對這些相互作用的基本了解對於識別與入侵病原體的庇護有關的生態，結構和環境因素以及其分散所涉及的機制至關重要。本研究的基本目的是量化由人類活動和環境變化引起的劣化淡水質量對IWDS內形成的生物膜的時間發展的影響，同時評估其與入侵細胞的相互作用和反應性。 這將通過將高通量測序技術與EPS化學分析和最新技術顯微鏡技術結合在模擬IWDS條件的生物膜環境反應器中形成的生物膜上實現。從該項目獲得的知識將提供對IWDS內社區多樣性和功能作用的基本了解，以及這些與EPS組成和機械性能的關係。對入侵細胞的生物膜相互作用和反應性的新見解，作為改變淡水質量的直接後果，將為製定和優化風險評估和製定乾預策略以減輕這些風險提供基礎。這反過來將有助於通過增加糧食安全和安全來改善公共衛生。該項目產生的可交付成果也將為使用基於生物膜的微生態系統分析作為評估淡水生態健康的可靠和敏感的生物學指標鋪平道路。

27200917.label: Realisation of objectives
27200917.value: 1A. The project's overwhelming success lies on the development of a multispecies freshwater biofilm model. This work has since been published in two Science of the Total Environment papers. The results of which demonstrated the suitability of this laboratory-based experimental system for studying the impacts of selected pollutants on irrigation water distribution systems. 1B. In parallel, the BIOMASS project also led an in initial study to establish the impacts of freshwater pollution on microbial benthic biofilms at a larger environmental scale, which would allow a justifiable basis for testing and simulating the effect of selected pollutants on the newly developed laboratory-based experimental system. Here, bulk water and benthic bioﬁlms were sampled from three Hong Kong streams having various pollution proﬁles, and subsequently compared via high-resolution microscopy, metagenomic analysis, and analytical chemistry. The results, now published in Environmental Pollution indicated that bioﬁlms were, indeed, reservoirs of environmental pollutants, having different proﬁles compared with that of the corresponding bulk water samples.. Moreover, our ﬁndings point to signiﬁcant discrepancies of the active community structure proﬁles resulting from the various RNA extraction strategies, with some methods being suited for studying eukaryotic organisms, while others for bacteria. The results reported in this study suggest the importance of carefully considering the choice of RNA extraction method on freshwater bioﬁlm samples, as this may strongly aﬀect the downstream NGS sequencing results. The biases of using one extraction method from another include shifts in active microbiomes and functional attributes. This work resulted in a recent manuscript accepted for publication in Frontiers in Microbiology. 2A. Given the fact that the BIOMASS project depended mostly on performing fundamental investigations using a multispecies biofilm model, the issue of simulated naturally occurring low‑nutrient medium rather than artificial nutrient‑rich medium was raised. However, since biofilm development under low‑nutrient growth media is slow, natural media are often supplemented with an additional carbon source to increase the rate of biofilm formation. However, there are knowledge gaps in interpreting the effects of such supplementation on the resulting multispecies biofilm in terms of structure and microbial community composition. The BIOMASS project therefore investigated the effects of supplementation of a simulated freshwater medium with sodium citrate on the resulting structure, bacterial community composition, and microbial network interactions of an early‑stage multispecies biofilm model. Qualitative and quantitative analyses of acquired confocal laser scanning microscopy data confirmed that sodium citrate supplementation distinctly increased biofilm biomass. Sequencing data revealed that the microbial community structure of biofilms grown in sodium citrate‑supplemented conditions was characterized with increased relative abundance and dominance of Proteobacteria compared with that of biofilms grown in sodium citrate‑free conditions. Our findings suggest that the supplementation of a low‑nutrient medium with a carbon source in experiments involving multispecies biofilms may lead to structural and compositional biases of the microbial community, causing changes in biofilm phenotype. This work has since been published in Scientific Reports. 2B. With the experimental setup finally established, the BIOMASS sought to understand the reactivity of our multispecies biofilm towards a selected pollutant, erythromycin. The presence of antibiotics such as erythromycin, even in trace amounts, has long been acknowledged for negatively impacting ecosystems in freshwater environments. Although many studies have focused on the impact of antibiotic pollution at a macroecological level, the impact of erythromycin on micro-ecosystems, such as freshwater bioﬁlms, is still not fully understood. This knowledge gap may be attributed to the lack of robust multispecies bioﬁlm models for fundamental investigations. Here, we used a lab-cultured multispecies bioﬁlm model to elucidate the holistic response of a microbial community to erythromycin exposure using metagenomic and metabolomic approaches. Metagenomic analyses revealed that bioﬁlm microbial diversity did not alter following erythromycin exposure. Notably, certain predicted metabolic pathways such as cell to cell communication pathways, amino acid metabolism, and peptidoglycan biosynthesis, mainly by the phyla Actinobacteria, Alpha/Beta-proteobacteria, Bacteroidetes, and Verrucomicrobia, were found to be involved in the maintenance of homeostasis-like balance in the freshwater bioﬁlm. Further untargeted metabolomics data highlighted changes in lipid metabolism and linoleic acid metabolism and their related molecules as a direct consequence of erythromycin exposure. This work has since been published in Environmental Pollution. Our metatranscriptomic analysis revealed obvious changes in the relative expression of Proteobacteria, Microsporidia, Bacteroidetes, Actinobacteria, and Planctomycetes after erythromycin exposure.Further analyses suggested that erythromycin induced distinct functional activities, such as increased relative expression in translation, transcription, cell motility, cell wall biogenesis, and defense mechanisms. A confocal laser scanning microscopic analysis further revealed significant structural differences in biofilm roughness, which further validated the above-mentioned observations from the perspective of the biofilm phenotype. Further analysis of specific genes revealed significant increases in the expression of both erythromycin-resistance genes and stress-related genes after erythromycin exposure. Hence, significant changes were observed in the biofilm structure, active microbiome, and functional attributes following biofilm exposure to erythromycin. An expression analysis of specific genes suggested that biofilms actively initiated a defensive system under sub-inhibitory erythromycin pressure. Our findings provide an in-depth analysis at the gene expression level that could be instrumental in evaluating the health of freshwater ecosystems. This metatanscriptomic study has been submitted for peer review. 2C. Exposure of the biofilm model to physical pollutants such as nano silver particles, was also investigated using the same experimental design described in 2B. Contrary to erythromycin, the nanoparticles impact on biofilm biomass development was immediately observed leading reduced biomass available for nucleic acid isolation. Consequently, sufficient biomass was collected for metagenomics and metabolomics analyses, unfortunately disallowing for metatransciptomic analysis. The results generated from this study are so far being compiled and a manuscript is currently being prepared for peer review. 3. The BIOMASS project attempted to study biofilm reactivity towards planktonic invading E. coli cells. It was found that this labelling strategy was not ideal for performing subsequent metatranscriptomic analysis. We there sought to look at this question from another angle. Comprehensive global profile of the distribution of ARGs in freshwater biofilms are lacking. Here, we utilized metagenomic approaches to extensively reveal the diversity, abundance, transferability and hosts of ARGs in 96 freshwater biofilm samples from 38 sampling sites across four countries. The abundant ARGs were associated with bacitracin, multidrug, polymycin, macrolide-lincosamide-streptogramin (MLS) aminoglycoside, β-lactam, chloramphenicol, sulfonamide and tetracycline resistance, consistent with the spectrum of antibiotics commonly used in human or veterinary medicine. As expected, the resistome in freshwater biofilm habitats was significantly influenced by geographical location and human footprint. Based on the co-occurrence pattern revealed by network analysis, mdtC, kdpE, and emrB were proposed as ARG indicators in freshwater biofilms that can be used to evaluate the abundance of 46 other co-occurring ARG subtypes quantitatively. Metagenomic assembly analysis revealed that the identified ARGs were hosted by more than 46 bacterial phyla, including various pathogens, which greatly expands the knowledge of resistome diversity in freshwater biofilms. Our study points to central roles of biofilms in harboring and exchanging ARGs. The results could be used to enhance the understanding of the distribution and dissemination of ARGs in freshwater habitats, thereby strengthening the global environmental risk assessment and management of ARGs. In the shorter term this finding may be used for horizontal gene transfer experiments using the freshwater biofilm model developed in this project. A paper describing these findings is now currently under review in Journal of Hazardous Materials.

27200917.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27200917.value: Future research will further explore the mechano-chemical profiles of IWDS biofilms caused by water quality by analyzing the chemical and microrheological profiles of the exopolymeric fraction of sampled biofilms. Moreover, defining factors that dictate cell recruitment and detachment under relevant environmental conditions will also be investigated using a GFP-tagged model microorganism coupled with confocal microscopy, flow cytometry, and further transcriptomic studies. Such a fundamental experimental approach is necessary for identifying environmental queues responsible for cell capture or detachment under relevant IWDS biofilm systems. The resulting knowledge acquired from this project will provide a fundamental understanding of the functional role of microbial communities within IWDS and will serve as a basis for formulating and optimizing risk assessments to develop intervention strategies to mitigate these risks in agricultural production. This future work will also provide freshwater ecologists and conservationists with powerful and practical tools for monitoring aquatic ecological health, on a wider scale. All these elements would contribute significantly towards improving and safeguarding our fragile freshwater supply.

27200917.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27200917.value: The BIOMASS project led to significant achievements in the standardization of complex multi-species freshwater biofilm models for the purpose of conducting fundamental pollution studies involving chemical and physical pollutants. The response of biofilms towards single pollutants at structural, meta genomic, metabolomic and metatranscriptomic dimensions were investigated, and provided insights on biofilm reactivity in polluted environments. It is expected that the biofilm model developed in this project will set the foundation of subsequent research relevant to environmental toxicology, focusing on the impact of either emergent environmental pollutants or synergistical effects of multiple pollutants on freshwater biofilms. Overall, the study presented a unique picture of how multispecies bioﬁlms respond to single environmental stress exposures. Moreover, the study demonstrated the feasibility of using lab simulated multispecies bioﬁlms for investigating their interaction and reactivity of speciﬁc bioactive compounds or pollutants at a fundamental level.
