27207517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27207517.value: 三維打印已經成為一種顛覆性技術，其可以改變生活方式，世界的工業以及經濟。特別地，三維打印 – 一類被稱為添加製造的技術 – 可以提供創建複雜對象的最簡單方法， 潛在地統一了傳統的製造步驟：成型，雕刻，焊接和裝配。儘管一些熱衷者相信三維打印將引領“下一次工業革命”，但是相對較慢的建造速度（生產量）以及低精度（空間分辨率）仍然限制了它在原型製造中的應用。為了實現飛躍，成為先進光電子工業真正的製造平臺，三維打印技術從根本上應擁有“圓晶級”生產量以及“納米級”空間分辨率。儘管一些聰明的策略不斷的被提出來，但是沒有一種技術能夠同時滿足這些要求。 我們提議研究一種新的並行彎月面引導的三維打印方法，其目的是在單桌面系統中實現高生產量以及納米級空間分辨率。核心想法是產生和利用多噴嘴打印頭上的“並行油墨半月面”來刻畫可複寫的三維結構。流體狀油墨半月面的機械靈活性保證了可以通過拉伸來控制特徵尺寸到100 納米以下，同時蒸發誘導的快速凝固有效的保持了獨立的結構。我們的初步實驗結果證明了此方法在連續打印中的可行性以及適用性。然而，並行化方法的實現仍然面臨一系列重要的挑戰，其需要研究多個油墨半月面的精確控制以及大規模並行噴嘴的製造。 此項目的目標在於（1）瞭解亞飛升半月面的熱力學穩定性，（2）開發多噴嘴打印頭的多尺度製造工藝以及（3）通過校準和裝配過程說明打印頭的可模塊化，以用於提高可擴展性以及靈活性。該項目的成果可用於並行和多材料 – 從金屬和聚合物到碳材料，如碳納米管以及石墨烯 – 在納米級的三維集成，從而提供了一種更有效的方法來創建先進的電子系統，而不需要反復的顯影蝕刻步驟。我們期望該項目能提供一種革新的方式來同時提高速度以及精度，實現長期的夢想，推動三維打印成為下一代製造業的主要工具。

27207517.label: Realisation of objectives
27207517.value: The objectives have been achieved: 1) We have investigated the formation of an ink meniscus containing various functional materials and its thermodynamic stability under different 3D printing conditions. We have developed non-contact, engineering routes to produce and manipulate nanoscale liquid inks for nanoscale 3D printing and applied the developed routes to diverse functional materials such as metals, polymers, carbon nanomaterials, quantum dots, and perovskites. To this end, the material growth dynamics of such diverse materials confined in nano-ink have been studied. 2) We have established multi-nozzle 3D printer heads consisting of 2 or 3 parallel nanopipettes. 3) We have developed a non-contact leveling protocol of the parallel printing nozzles. These research works have improved the throughput and printability of nanoscale 3D printing of diverse functional materials on unusual substrates, resulting in various 3D nanostructures with programmed geometry and composition.

27207517.label: Major findings and research outcome
27207517.value: Major research outcomes include 1) practical realization of parallel nanoscale 3D printing to improve the throughput and reliability, 2) diversification of 3D printable materials by using material-laden ink meniscus, and 3) fabrication of freeform 3D nano-architectures. These outcomes provide an insight into how to practically realize nanoscale 3D printing of functional materials. Most of the results have been published in internationally recognized journals (e.g. Advanced Materials, ACS Nano, Small, Nano Letters, etc.) and presented in international conferences (e.g. Materials Research Society Fall Meeting 2019 and 2021, IEEE Nanomed 2021, etc.), as shown in Part C. Some of the project outcomes also benefit other research projects indirectly.

27207517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27207517.value: The completed research project demonstrated the potential to improve the throughput and reliability of nanoscale 3D printing. This work is directly related to the practical use of 3D printing techniques and the developed techniques/protocols will facilitate a broad range of materials and applications, not limited to specific materials and structures. We propose to explore the development of new types of 3D printed electronic, photonic, and/or energy devices, facilitated by research grants such as the General Research Fund (GRF) and the Environment and Conservation Fund (ECF). Some of the project outcomes achieved are also benefiting other on-going research projects indirectly.

27207517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27207517.value: 3D printing is emerging as a disruptive technology that can transform manufacturing industries. However, the technological challenges associated with relatively slow printing speed and low precision remain unresolved. In this project, we investigated a strategy to develop parallel nanoscale 3D printing process that exploit nanoscale ink menisci formed on multi-nozzles. We established a nanotechnological protocol to produce and manipulate multiple ink menisci and tested it for nanoscale 3D printing of diverse materials from metals, polymers, graphene, to perovskites. These results provide the foundation and engineering protocols for improving both speed and precision of 3D printing and suggest a number of interesting applications of 3D printing for mass customization of electronic and photonic devices.

27209817.label: Project Objectives
27209817.value: To investigate the aerodynamic and structural performance of wind turbines under the most favorable and unfavorable stop position that causes destruction of composite blades impacted by super typhoons. At the stage of elastic design, Hashin’s theory is applied as the failure criterion and no post-failure progressive degradation will be considered; To develop an isogeometric elastoplastic damage model for the composites that exhibit significant nonlinearity or plasticity before the collapse of the structure. The model will be validated against extensive experimental data including notched composite laminate under uniaxial stress; To establish the coupled FSI and the elastoplastic damage formulation and devise the optimal control strategy to brake the composite turbines for risk mitigation of structural failure; To couple the free-surface fluid-structure interaction and the fatigue damage model to evaluate the service life of large offshore floating wind turbines, starting from damage initiation, to damage progression and then to eventual failure.

27209817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27209817.value: In recent years, more wind farms have been built in the southeastern coast of China where abundant wind resources satisfy large energy demands of the region. The maximum limit of wind turbine blade length has steadily increased to 80 m over the past decades. Failure of large turbines that may threaten the structural integrity can be categorized as the following two major types: short-term failure under high-speed wind conditions such as typhoons, and long-term accumulative failure such as high-cycle fatigue under aerodynamic forces over the service life of 20 years. Unfortunately current aerodynamic modeling is performed using low-fidelity methods subject to the operational wind speed lower than the cut-out speed of 25 m/s. Very little research has been carried out to investigate the failure mechanisms subject to typhoon with wind speeds over 60 m/s or the turbulent wind loading over decades. Our previous work of numerical methodology involves (1) a coupled fluid-structure interaction (FSI) framework, wherein the 3D time-dependent aerodynamics is computed using a finite-element-based ALE-VMS technique; and (2) isogeometric rotation-free Kirchhoff-Love shell formulation equipped with a continuum damage mechanics framework to model the composite blades. The primary objective of this proposed project is to use high performance computing to develop high-fidelity FSI simulation techniques capable of characterizing the failure behaviors under extreme wind conditions. The great challenges of this project include the following: (1) under the impact of a typhoon, a strongly coupling FSI method should be robust enough to achieve good convergence to deal with flow instability due to turbulent boundary layer separation and flutter induced vibration of the blades in torsional mode; (2) in progressive failure analysis, the current elastic damage model may underestimate the energy absorption capacity of composite blades; and (3) for offshore floating wind turbine, subject to violent sea waves, a free-surface flow solver should be accurate to capture the evolution of air-water interface. The proposed project may constitute the following parts: (1) isogeometric regularized elastoplastic damage modeling of composite to take account of significant plasticity; (2) coupling of the FSI and the elastoplastic damage model and investigate the optimal strategy to brake the turbines under the typhoon impact; and (3) coupling of the free-surface FSI and the fatigue damage model to evaluate the service life of the offshore floating wind turbines. It is expected that the outcome may provide input for the design guidelines to mitigate the risk of structural failure under extreme wind conditions. 近年来在中国东南沿海修建了越来越多的风机场，其丰富的风资源能满足当地的巨大的能源需求。在过去的几十年风机叶片的极限尺寸也稳步增加到80米。能导致大型风机结构失效可归结为以下两方面的原因：（1）诸如台风等短期高速风荷载的失效；（2）在使用寿命20年的风荷载下引起的高周疲劳破坏。遗憾的是目前的空气动力学模型多是运行风速低于最大运行风速25米/秒下的低精度模型。对于在风速高于60米/秒的台风或数十年的脉动风作用下叶片的破坏机制鲜少研究。 我们过去的数值建模方法包括：（1）建立流固耦合平台，其中空气动力学的计算是基于有限元方法的三维时变的ALE-VMS方法；（2）用带有连续损伤模型的同几何无转动的基尔霍夫板单元模拟风机叶片。本项目的目标是采用高性能数值计算进行风机叶片在极度风环境下的疲劳仿真。该项目的挑战在于：（1）台风作用下流固耦合程序必须有足够鲁棒性使得算法在由湍流和结构大变形引起的流体的不稳定性下仍有好的收敛性；（2）在渐进失效模型中，目前的线弹性破坏模型低估了复合材料叶片的吸能能力；（3）在剧烈的海浪冲击的近海浮动风平台时，自由界面流体的求解器能够精确的计算水和空气界面。 本项目拟包括以下部分：（1）同几何复合材料的弹塑性模型；（2）流固耦合与复合结构弹塑性模型相结合，用于模拟在台风作用下风机叶片的最优的锁定位置；（3）基于自由面的流固耦合模型与复合材料弹塑性模型相结合，用于模拟近海风机的疲劳寿命。本项目的结果将对降低风机结构在极端风环境下的风险提够设计的参考。

27209817.label: Realisation of objectives
27209817.value: 1.1 Objective 1: To investigate the structural and aerodynamic performance of wind turbines/wind farm Two designs of 10MW 85-m wind turbine blades with the initial configuration scaled up from the NREL 5-MW baseline blade are implemented, including design 1 without shear web and design 2 with the shear web. For initial designs, blade mass significantly decreases after adding shear webs. Compared to their initial design, both two optimized designs are thinner with the reduction in the chord length and significant decrease in blade mass, which makes full use of the material while satisfying the tolerances of composite failure constraint and deformation constraint. As shear webs are added, Initial Design 2 only has approximately 1/3 of the blade mass of Initial Design 1. In Design 1, the tip deflection of the optimal is increased from 7.025m to 8.499m, the maximum Tsai-Wu is reduced from 0.572 to 0.380, and the objective function value is reduced from 100% to 87.1%. However, in Design 2, the maximum deformation is raised from 4.605m to 8.499m, maximum Tsai-Wu also decreases from 0.524 to 0.374. According to the measurement of the objective function, the optimal design behaves 12.9% and 21.1% improvement in performance, respectively. On the other hand, the ANN-based prediction of the wake effect in the wind farm show acceptable agreement with the CFD results, LES data, and measurement, which indicates that the robust ANN is capable of establishing the sophisticated spatial relationship between inflow conditions and the wake flow fields and has the potential to improve the wake predictions with favorable accuracy. Compared with the time-consuming LES simulations, the ANN model can produce the flow fields in a few seconds, dramatically accelerating the prediction. The total power results of the ANN model agree with the LES data well under various wind directions. In order to gain more accurate results, the linear superposition model is used to calculate the power. The wind farm power shows a remarkable decrease near wind directions representing the full-wake conditions, i.e., 180°, 222°, 270°, 312°, and 350°. Compared with analytical models, the ANN wake model significantly improves the total power predictions and agrees with LES data. 1.2 Objective 2: To develop an elastoplastic damage model for the composites As a novel class of weight-efficient engineering materials, the functionally graded porous (FGP) beam has great potential for application to wind turbine structures. A unified analytical model is established to study the vibration behavior of moderately thick functionally graded porous deep curved and straight beams with general boundary conditions. The first-order beam theory, which considers the influence of shear deformation, inertia rotary, and deepness terms, is adopted in the formulation. The theoretical solution model is obtained through a modified series solution. The core soul uses the modified Fourier series, including a standard cosine Fourier series with two auxiliary terms to expand the admissible function. The exact solution for the FGP beam with general boundary conditions is derived by utilizing a reasonable spring stiffness value at both ends. A series of numerical examples show that the current model has superior convergence characteristics, computational accuracy, and stability. Furthermore, the free vibrations of functionally graded porous (FGP) rectangular plates with uniform elastic boundary conditions are investigated through an improved Fourier series method (IFSM). It is assumed that the distributions of porosity are uniform or non-uniformly along a particular direction, and three types of porosity distribution are considered, among which the material property of two non-uniform porous distributions was expressed as the simple cosine. The size of the pore in a rectangular plate is determined by the porosity coefficients. Using the first-order shear deformation theory (FSDT), the energy expression of the FGP rectangular plate is created. The IFSM is employed to obtain the admissible function of displacement for functionally graded porous rectangular plates. Then, the Rayleigh-Ritz method is used to solve coefficients in the Fourier series, which determine natural frequencies and modal shapes. Convergence and comparative research are performed to prove the current method's convergence, reliability, and accuracy. Finally, dynamic analysis of functionally graded porous (FGP) plate with reinforcement of graphene platelets (GPLs) resting on elastic foundation and restrained by elastic boundary condition is investigated. The GPLs-FGP plate, with the geometric parameters, is demonstrated on the Winkler–Pasternak elastic foundation. The neighboring segments are connected by the virtual springs. The analytical model of the GPLs-FGP plate is formulated by the first-order shear deformation theory and the multi-segment partition technique. The dynamics of the GPLs-FGP plate analysis model are solved by the Rayleigh-Ritz method. Based on the above investigation, a series of parametric studies about the free, forced vibration, and transient analysis are conducted, which provide reference data for future research. The effect of the elastic boundary condition is studied by comparing the models with/without the Winkle-Pastnernak elastic foundation. It is implied that the increase in the stiffness of the boundary conditions is related to the instability of the forced response. 1.3 Objective 3: To establish the coupled FSI and the elastoplastic composite framework Failure of a composite (i.e., the complete loss of its loading capacity) under high impact load is due to the elastoplastic degradation of the material stiffness. In the continuum damage mechanics (CDM) for fiber-reinforced composites, space- and time-dependent damage variables are evolved to predict damage growth with the load quantitatively. The in-house code has been developed and validated against carbon fiber reinforced composite laminate (AS4/3501-6) with layup [0/±45/90]s under biaxial tensile loading. A standalone and two back-to-back full-scale tidal turbines using an in-house computational free-surface flow code are investigated. The proposed method on a single turbine configuration is first validated. A mesh refinement study is conducted to ensure the result is converged. We then quantify the wake effect and free-surface effect on tidal turbine performance using a case study and perform pure hydrodynamics and free-surface simulations to investigate the effect. In both pure hydrodynamics and free-surface flow simulations, thrust and production coefficients of the downstream turbines drop significantly due to the velocity deficit in the wake. By comparing the result between free-surface flow and pure hydrodynamics simulations for the configuration considered here, we find that the free-surface does not affect the upstream turbine but significantly affects the downstream turbine. In conclusion, the numerical framework based on the in-house computational continuum damage mechanics (CDM) and free-surface flow code are capable of coupling the FSI and the elastoplastic composite formulation. 1.4 Objective 4: To couple the fluid-structure interaction and the fatigue damage model to evaluate the service life of large offshore floating wind turbines Generally, the block-iterative coupling strategy is the most efficient choice for the present application. Since we are interested in high-cycle fatigue for wind-turbine blades and adopt the CDM (continuum damage mechanics) that assumes that damage growth occurs on a time scale that is much slower than a single rotor revolution, it is sufficient to use a "frozen" damage state during FSI computations of the spinning rotor. The preliminary FSI-simulation and blade fatigue-damage prediction results for the full-scale Micon 65/13M wind turbine are investigated, which is a fixed-pitch, upwind horizontal-axis turbine with rated power production of 100 kW, and with the rotor comprised of three CX-100 blades.

27209817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27209817.value: This research focuses on the fluid-structure interaction modeling for failure analysis of wind turbines under extreme wind conditions at the micro-scale for a standalone turbine. Furthermore, the large-scale problems of multiple turbines in wind farms are also of great significance to the renewable energy industry. The proposed course of action may include (1) establishing simulation-based low-fidelity machine learning models of the macro-scale wind farm system, incorporating the dynamic wake meandering neural network (DWMNN) of wind flow and the spatial-temporal long short-term memory (LSTM) wave network; (2) establishing a high-fidelity reinforcement learning (RL) wake and wave models driven by the scarce measurement data for wind power prediction and loading estimation; (3) assessing the structural performance of the micro-scale wind turbines subject to the joint action of inhomogeneous wind and wave loading in the various positions of the wind farm by considering the soil-foundation-fluid-structure interaction; (4) improving the productivity of smart offshore wind farms by multi-objective layout optimization and real-time cooperative wake steering by applying the multi-start Bayesian optimization and multiscale data-driven machine learning framework.

27209817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27209817.value: With the gradual reduction of available fossil fuel reserves and the impact on the environment of fossil fuel use, wind energy holds much promise in Hong Kong and elsewhere around the world. It is estimated that the region where offshore wind farms can be built along the coastline of Hong Kong has a mean water depth of less than 30 m, and it is suitable for direct wind turbine installation. Failure of large wind turbines under extreme conditions can be categorized into the following two major types: short-term failure under high-speed wind conditions such as typhoons and long-term accumulative failure such as fatigue damage under turbulent aerodynamic loading over the service life of 20 years. Meanwhile, one major threat that wind turbines withstand in Hong Kong is typhoons. This research provided references for design guidelines and extended wind turbine systems' life expectancy under extreme wind conditions, which can significantly reduce the maintenance cost, improve the turbine's service life, and improve the economic benefits of the wind power industry.

27303817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27303817.value: In nature, biological systems have evolved to perform sophisticated life functions: they move, grow, adapt, tune, self-assemble, interact, and operate under different conditions with high fidelity. For example, cells divide and wounds heal. These emergent behaviors are possible for two important reasons. First, biological systems are made of tens of thousands of structure-complex structures and information-rich entities (e.g., DNA, proteins, and cells) that work individually or in unison to function. Second, biological systems are living and active, meaning that they consume energy while operating. Learning from nature, the aim of this project is to create synthetic materials that are complex, active, and multifunctional. More specifically, the research team will develop a strategy for designing and synthesizing active “colloidal” materials bearing advanced functionalities, for instance, completing microscopic tasks or forming dynamic patterns. The ultimate goal is to create novel, intelligent, and dynamic materials with new structures and cutting-edge properties such as the ability to deliver drugs, self-assemble, self-heal etc. The idea of creating artificial active materials has long been pursued, and has led to the synthesis of a rich variety of active molecules such as “molecular machines”, “motors”, and “cars”, and active nano-particles such as “nano-swimmers”. Within the colloidal regime (micrometer and sub-micrometer scale), however, the kinds of active systems (i.e., active colloids or micromotors) that have been built are rare, and are limited to a few simple designs (e.g., Janus particles), despite that such colloids may be used in micro-robotics or serve as model systems to study the energy-driven, collective out-of-equilibrium behaviors in biology. Other functions commonly found in living systems such as sensing, recognition, loading/unloading have yet to be integrated. To address these limitations, we propose the synthesis of “active patchy colloids”, a new design platform to create active colloids with tunable properties and functions, based on the hypothesis that colloids may be engineered to have multiple localized surface areas (patches) that are independently addressable. Using the proposed method, diverse particles shapes, controlled particle motions, and particle recognition/binding etc. will be accessible. In addition, novel dynamically assembled structures can be realized. The thrust of our strategy is its versatility, and the enormous flexibility it enables in designing colloids of particular properties. It will thus have a significant impact in materials science, biophysics, and nanotechnology. As an EARLY CAREER projects, the research outcome will also lay the foundations for self-organization and out-of-equilibrium systems for future in-depth studies by the research team. 在自然界中，生物系統通過演變已經可以執行複雜的生命功能：它們可以在不同條件下准确地移動，成長，適應，調整，自組裝，或者交互。例如，細胞分裂和傷口癒合。這些複雜的集體行為有可能出於兩個重要原因。首先，生物系統由數以萬計的結構複雜和信息豐富的實體（例如，DNA，蛋白質和細胞）組成，他們單獨或一致地起作用。第二，生物系統是具有生命活性的，在運行時不斷地消耗能量。我們從這些自然系統中受到啟發，提出這個這個項目，其目的是創造出複雜，有活性和多功能的合成材料。更具體地說，研究團隊將探索具有高級功能的活性膠體材料的設計和合成策略。這種材料可完成微觀任務或形成動態結構。此項研究最終的目標是創造出具有全新結構和尖端特性的智能活性材料，並應用在藥物傳送，自我組裝，自我修復等領域。 人們對活性材料科學探索歷史悠久，並已合成了“分子機器”，“分子馬達”，“分子汽車”等多種活性分子的合成，以及“納米游泳粒子”等活性納米粒子。然而，在膠體尺度上（微米和亞微米級），已經建成的活性體系（即活性膠體粒子或微電機）的種類很少，並且僅限於幾種簡單的設計，然而這樣的膠體粒子可以用於微型機器人或作為模型系統來研究生物學中能量驅動的集體非平衡態行為，諸如傳感，識別，裝載/卸載等生命系統中常見的其他功能 。為了解決這一局限性，該項目旨在開發一種具有可調諧性和多功能的合成活性膠體的方法。研究的假設是膠體可以被設計成具有多個表面區域（patch），且每個表面可以被獨立的修飾已具備不同的功能。所提出的方法可以實現不同的粒子形狀，受控的粒子運動和粒子識別/綁定等。此外，新穎的動態組裝結構也可能出現。 該研究方法的最大特色是多功能性，以及在設計特定屬性膠體時所具有的巨大靈活性。因此，它將對材料科學，生物物理學和納米技術產生重大影響。作為一個早期工作項目，研究成果還將為團隊未來深入地研究自組織和失衡系統奠定基礎。

27303817.label: Realisation of objectives
27303817.value: Object 1. To introduce the new concept of “active patchy colloids” for creating multifunctional active materials. This Objective aims to introduce a new design concept for making active colloids, by synthesizing patchy particles that are multifunctional and active. The objective has been successfully realized (100%). Active colloids are nano/microparticles able to self-propel or “swim” within a fluid by consuming external energy, giving rise to rich out-of-equilibrium phenomena. The unique characteristics have endowed active colloids with great promise in creating microscale machinery or robotics, where control of motion and coordination of the moving parts are the essential elements. Previous design of active particles, known as Janus particles, consist of two parts, an active “engine” and an inert matrix, which are distinct in composition, polarizability, or surface chemistry, and are arranged in an asymmetrical fashion. Although such systems served Such system served a good model for investigating the mechanism of particle activities but were not able conduct more sophisticated tasks. Yet, synthetic strategies for more complex particles are yet to be developed. To tackle the issue, we proposed to introduce patchy particles—surface with multiple surfaces, to act as multifunctional active colloids with tunable shapes and dynamic behaviors. To realizes Objective 1, we have done a thorough survey on literature papers and confirmed that 1) development of multi-functional active colloids are needed and 2) the use of patchy particles for active colloids have not been reported. Indeed, the proposed concept is unique, and as we proved in other Objectives, can offer dedicate control over particle dynamics and lead to various intriguing colloidal interactions and behaviors. Object 2. To establish a modular synthetic strategy to make patchy colloids whose patches are independently tunable regarding the number, size, and surface chemistry. This Objectives aims to develop synthetic strategy for highly tunable patchy particles is to be developed. The objective is well executed (100%). We approached this objective by establishing a method for encapsulation of colloidal clusters and controlling the extent of encapsulation by stimulated “dewetting”. First, we verified this idea by using polymeric TPM particles with a dense layer of Cl- (i.e., TPM-Cl) groups as the seed. The encapsulation and dewetting on TPM-Cl spheres works as planned, leading to mono-patch particles with controllable patch sizes. We then tested the encapsulation of dimer and trimer clusters and the encapsulation and dewetting process leads to produce particles with bent patchy configurations. Although the functionality of spheres are the same, such particles are already new; the results proved the mechanisms of our synthetic routes. We also used simulation tools—in this case Surface Evolver—to verify the synthetic method. We confirmed that the dewetting by surfactant addition is due to minimization of surface energy of the system when certain particle shapes are adopted. And the surface energy is related to the contact angle of the encapsulation, which can be adjusted by introducing to the system surfactant. With the above success based, we have tested iterative steps trying to synthesize clusters with different sizes. This requires the dewetting of each step to a relative large extent so that the encapsulating materials forms a separate sphere at the desired position, making the clusters. We first explored the effect of surfactant type on the extent of dewetting. Also, how surface of the clusters is sensitive to the dewetting process. We found that the dewetting was not sufficient for TPM without the Cl- groups but can be done easily with hydrophobic modification These findings have led to an alternative method for the final goal. That is, we can functionalize the surface with hydrophobic alkyl molecules with a selective end group functionality. We have also investigated such opportunities. As proposed, we tended to introduce different functional groups at the encapsulation steps. We have tested the inclusion of carboxylate groups by adding methyl acrylic acid. However, due to the hydrophilic nature, the amount of acid groups that can be anchored on the particle surface has been limited. This has led us to modify our plan by using hydrophobic molecules and use silane chemistry for surface functionalization. Although the four different functionalization is listed in the proposal, we had not pushed the system to that point, as the particles with two (amine, chloride, hydrophobic) is already a very large toolbox for us to study (see below). Object 3. To explore orthogonal functionalization methods to install multiple materials/ligands on colloid surface, enabling multiple functions such as particle propulsion and recognition. For this Objective, the goal is to use surface modifications to enable and tune the propulsion of active patchy particles. The objective has been successfully implemented and realized (90 %). Although we have also proposed other routes, the gold-coating functionalization has been fruitful. We have successfully demonstrated that elemental Au can be plated selectively on the patches originated from the Cl-patches. A two-step nucleation and growth method has been used. We found that the successful of Au coating has largely to do with the density of Cl-groups on surfaces. If dense, thick gold layer with small Au particles (10-30 nm) can be obtained, which is good for serving as particle engines under AC electric field. We have also started to try to functionalize other type of materials on particle surfaces, such as titania, which can be used for propelling particles under other types of energy sources such as light. Combined with the wide variety of particle shapes and patch sizes, the ability to coat gold on the patch surface led to active particles of many forms. The show shape-dependent dynamics including size-selective recognition and assemblies (see Objective 4). Object 4. To investigate new propulsion mechanisms, packing, and other collective behaviors of various colloids to be synthesized. With the large collection of active patchy particles, we explore their propulsion and dynamic assembly in this Objective. We have achieved subtle control over the behaviors and assembles structures. The Objective has been fully realized (100%). We have further extended the system to integrate with biological systems (cells and bacteria) (not originally proposed), which led to more publications and new ideas for further studies. For example, the prepared patchy particles can be driven by AC electric field to propel. We have then tested if particles shapes enabled by our synthetic methods can have an influence for the propulsion behavior, as shapes will change the environment around particles when they are driven to propel. Indeed, patch size can change the speed of propulsion under a electroosmosis mechanism. We have also used simulation tools to help visualize the asymmetric flows that were generated around particles, which rationalizes the speed of particles under different situation. We have further studied the propulsions of particles adopting other morphologies we can make. For particles with one patch, the asymmetry and the exposed gold surface determines the propulsion speed. While for two-patch particles, the particles can perform complex motions such as steering and brake, etc. The particles also show directional interaction with spherical passive particles and led to various micromachines by assembly. For example, two mono-patch particles can be trapped underneath the passive sphere giving rise to spinning clusters. The particles can also bind with cells to form static or spinning assemblies. The binding is highly selective and with the direction tuned by the particle size and shape.

27303817.label: Major findings and research outcome
27303817.value: The major findings of the project is the introduction of a new type of active colloids—the active patchy colloids—that are multifunctional with tunable shape, surface chemistry and therefore dynamics. The new particles can propel and assemble with unprecedented flexibility, giving rise to active behaviors that are previously not possible. The synthetic scheme, the propulsion mechanism, and the assembly principles have been well investigated, which are valuable contribution to the field. These findings have led to three high-profile publications in peer-reviewed international journals (Part C, Research Output, 8). In the first case, the introduction of active patchy particles and their synthesis/dynamics are reported in “Active Patchy Colloids with Shape-Tunable Dynamics” in Journal of the American Chemical Society. In the second case, we found that patchy particles with specific shapes can assemble to active molecules with directional interactions. The results are reported in “Active Colloidal Molecules Assembled via Selective and Directional Bond” in Nature Communications. Finally, using particles with two-patches, reconfigurable and directional assembly have been realized, which has been published in ACS Nano as “Directional and Reconfigurable Assembly of Metallodielectric Patchy Particles”. By working on the project, post- and under-graduate students have been trained (Part C, Research Output, 10). One student, Dr. Zuochen Wang, who primarily worked on this project, has graduated. He has published multiple papers and won Outstanding Thesis Award of HKU. He is now pursing postdoctoral training in a top University in the US. Another graduate student, Mr. Zhisheng Wang, has also gained vigorous training and has produced first author publications and shall be graduated with PhD soon. The education of undergraduate students is also successful (refer to Realization of Education Plan). With the demonstrated publication and promising results, the PI has been awarded Croucher Innovation Award 2019, from the Hong Kong Croucher Foundation, and National Natural Science Foundation of China Excellent Young Scientist Fund, 2020 (Part C, Research Output, 12). These are all highly competitive awards. Finally, the results of the project have been discussed in local and international meetings (Part C, Research Output, 9). We note that due to the pandemic, the PI and students could not participate in many conferences and visits.

27303817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27303817.value: In this project, we have introduced the concept and synthesis of multifunctional active patchy particles, which showed a much-extended dynamic behaviors as compared to traditional Janus particles. While we have realized the original objectives, many of the observations deserve further exploration. First, the synthesis of multi-patch particles in high purity and high yield. Currently, although showing intriguing dynamic behaviors, the particles are not produced in a high yield, which prevent us from assembling extended structures. For example, the two-patch particles can be used to assemble Kagome lattice or other structures enhanced by particle activity. Second, higher order of particles with symmetrical or asymmetrical patches may be tailored to achieve complex trajectories. Currently, only 2D particle trajectories have been realized, the use of more complex particles may allow 3D motion control such as helical trajectories. Finally, the particle’s ability to propel and assemble should allow directional cargo delivery. To achieve this, cargos such as drug molecules may be attached on the particle surface and transported to specific location. These explorations would take other projects/years and shall yield interesting results.

27303817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27303817.value: Biological systems have evolved to perform sophisticated life functions: they move, grow, adapt, tune, self-assemble, interact, and operate under different conditions with high fidelity. Active materials are synthetic in essence but capture the key characteristics of biological and living systems; they consume energy and are motile and interactive. They hold great potential in creating dynamic and reconfigurable materials. Among such materials, active colloids are the model systems, which are micrometer-sized particles able to propel and self-assemble. Yet, in previous works, active colloids have often possessed simple morphologies and functions limiting their utility. In this project, we have developed a modular approach to synthesizing active colloids with tunable shapes and multiple functions. Based on this design, diverse particles shapes, controlled particle motions, and particle recognition/binding have been realized. Novel dynamically assembled structures are realized. The strategy is versatile and have enormous flexibility in designing colloids of various activities. It has a significant impact in materials science, biophysics, and nanotechnology, and lays the foundations for self-organization and out-of-equilibrium systems.

27304117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27304117.value: The quantile regression method has been widely used in analyzing the survival data. However, the methods of handling time dependent covariates are under-developed. The first project in this proposal fills such a gap by developing a quantile regression survival model with time-dependent covariates. Following the model, consistent procedures will be proposed for the parameter estimation. The property of the resulting estimator will be studied in the large sample settings. The asymptotic variation of the estimators will be derived for the statistical inference. Simulation will be conducted to evaluate the finite sample property for the proposed procedure. The usefulness of the new method will be illustrated with real data. Data analysis is quite challenging when covariates are measured with errors because the underlying true covariates are often unobservable. The existing deconvolution estimation methods require prohibitively large sample size to obtain proper estimators. The second project in the proposal addresses this problem. A new estimation procedure under mild conditions on the support of the covariates will be proposed. The properties of the estimation procedure will be studied both theoretically and empirically through simulation. Finally, the method will be used in a real example. In the Bayesian hypothesis testing, the non-local priors were proposed to balance the rates of convergence of the Bayes factor in favor of the true null and alternative hypotheses. The third project in this proposal extends the existing non-local prior to a more general form, namely the reflected non-local prior. The reflected non-local prior is intuitively appealing, and is constructed simply by slipping the normal distribution density upside down. The large sample property of the resulting Bayes factor will be studied. The choices of tuning parameters will be discussed both theoretically and empirically. 27305417.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27305417.value: Evolution of the continental crust is intimately linked with Earth’s habitability because plate tectonic–crustal processes play first-order roles in modulating ocean-atmosphere chemistry and climate, primarily through the carbon and oxygen cycles. The timing and nature of continental growth, however, remains a topic of debate. The continents are characterized by possession of a largely felsic-intermediate upper crust, and relatively flat stable interiors with zones of high topography and tectonic activity mostly confined the outer continental margins. Determining when and how the continental crust differentiated and when continental interiors stabilized is critical to understand Earth system evolution as a whole. Our proposed research aims to markedly improve understanding of the growth history and compositional evolution of the continents via novel applications of geochemical and thermochronometric data. Specifically, we will generate new detrital zircon U-Pb, Hf isotopic, and trace element (TE) data, as well as detrital white mica Ar/Ar (“M-Ar”) and detrital zircon (U–Th)/He (“Z-He”) thermochronometric data from globally sampled ancient and modern sediments that will provide a >3.5 billion-year record of continental crust evolution. Zircon TE data reflects the degree of liquid-crystal fractionation of the melts from which the zircon crystallized and thus can track the compositional evolution of felsic magmas. The difficulties associated with linking TE composition with zircon U-Pb age have hindered global-scale assessment of zircon TE data; however, recent technological advances now afford us the opportunity to simultaneously measure TE and U-Pb data in the same analytical volume. We will provide the first systematic characterization of detrital zircon TE composition – and by inference, arc magma TE evolution – over the last ~3.5 billion years. This approach has the potential to fill ‘gaps’ in the petrogenetic record and identify previously under-represented time periods of continental evolution. We will also assess the stabilization of continental interiors by means of M-Ar and Z-He thermochronometry. These methods elucidate different cooling histories of the host rock, which will help constrain the most recent time craton interiors passed through distinct cooling windows and experience deep, likely orogeny-driven exhumation. The difference between these ages also provides insight into the long-term rates of crustal erosion, which is import for understanding the biogeochemical history of Earth. This proposed research program will allow us to 1) track magmatic fractionation processes through time, which directly correspond to changes in crustal composition and thickness, and 2) determine the long-term exhumation and erosion histories of continental interiors. 大陆地壳的演变与地球的可居住性密切相关，因为板块构造 - 地壳过程主要通过碳和氧循环在调节海洋大气化学和气候中起一级作用。然而，大陆增长的时机和性质仍然是一个辩论的话题。大陆的特点是拥有大部分为中等厚度的上层地壳，相对较平坦的内陆地形，高地貌和构造活动区主要集中在外大陆边缘。确定大陆地壳何时以及如何区分，何时大陆内部稳定是了解整个地球系统进化的关键。 我们提出的研究旨在通过地球化学和热时钟数据的新应用，显着提高对大陆的增长历史和组成演变的了解。具体来说，我们将生成新的碎屑锆石U-Pb，Hf同位素和微量元素（TE）数据，以及碎屑白云母Ar / Ar（“M-Ar”）和碎屑锆石（U-Th）/ He “Z-He”）全球采样的古代和现代沉积物的热时钟数据，将提供35亿年的大陆地壳演化记录。锆石TE数据反映了锆石结晶的熔体的液晶分级程度，从而可以跟踪熔融岩浆的组成演变。将TE组合与锆石U-Pb年龄相关联的困难阻碍了锆石TE数据的全球尺度评估;然而，最近的技术进步现在使我们有机会在相同的分析量中同时测量TE和U-Pb数据。在最近〜35亿年的时间里，我们将首先提供碎屑锆石TE组成的第一次系统表征，并推断出电弧岩浆TE演化。这种方法有可能弥补成岩记录中的“差距”，并确定以前在欧洲大陆演化的时间不足的时期。我们还将通过M-Ar和Z-He热时间测量法评估大陆内部的稳定性。这些方法阐明了主体岩石的不同冷却历史，这将有助于限制最近时间的克拉通内部通过不同的冷却窗口，并经历深刻的，可能的造山驱动的挖掘。这些年龄之间的差异也提供了对地壳侵蚀长期发展的了解，这是了解地球生物地球化学历史的进口。 这个提出的研究计划将允许我们1）通过时间跟踪岩浆分馏过程，直接对应于地壳组成和厚度的变化，以及2）确定大陆内部的长期挖掘和侵蚀历史。

27305417.label: Realisation of objectives
27305417.value: Objective 1 -- We completed 3 field-seasons in total that spanned the Bundlkhand, Dharwad, and Aravalli cratons. This work included 2 RPG students. Objective 2 -- We generated an extensive dataset of detrital zircon U-Pb, Lu-Hf, and trace elemental data from new samples collected during this study and our existing repository samples. These data have contributed to numerous publications already. Objective 3 -- We generated and large amount of zircon apatite (U-Th/He) data from cratonic basement rocks and sedimentary cover sequences. Due complications with lab access and general quality of the rocks, we opted to conduct apatite U-Pb analyses in place of Ar/Ar analyses— apatite U-Pb informs on a similar thermal window as mica Ar/Ar. The apatite U-Pb approach proved to be a very successful alternative (see results published in *Colleps et al., 2020, Precambrian Research). Objective 4 -- Both the craton thermal data, and our large zircon TE databased yielded exciting results covering this objective, the summary of which is now under review at Science Advances.

27305417.label: Major findings and research outcome
27305417.value: The rapid stabilization of the central Indian craton ~2.5-2.4 Ga was constrained (*Colleps et al., 2021, Precambrian Research). Furthermore modeling of low-temperature thermal data from the sedimentary cover required a thermal heating event at ~66 Ma, coincident with the eruption of the Deccan large igneous province (*Colleps et al., 2021, EPSL). This indicates a larger original expanse of the Deccan basalts, which has implications for Cenozoic climate evolution and the end-Cretaceous mass extinction. Additionally, our thermochron data show a response to the formation of the Gondwana ice sheet in India during the late Paleozoic icehouse (*Colleps et al., in prep). Our zircon trace element database indicated a transition from mafic to felsic upper crust during the Archean, a reduction in crustal magmatism throughout the Proterozoic, and a transition to steep subduction with enhanced slab-roll back and extensional tectonics during the Neoproterozoic — this latter transition has broad implications for overall changes in biogeochemical cycling and surface processes since (*Liu et al., under review, Science Advances). Additional data on the thermal history of northern India, as they pertain to Himalayan evolution, are being written up now (this was the work of my MPhil student who just completed their dissertation in December 2021). [*=RPG student author supported by this project]

27305417.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27305417.value: This study demonstrated the importance of integrating thermal data from the sedimentary cover of cratonic basement to understand long-term burial and erosional histories of continents – the approaches refined herein will need to be further explored on global cratons. Additionally, the results from our zircon trace element dataset were quite provocative as they indicated secular changes in subduction dynamics since ~800 Ma. This hypothesis will need to be rigorously tested.

27305417.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27305417.value: Results from the this project contributed to our understanding of the Archean formation and stabilization of felsic cratons, the formation of Proterozoic intra-cratonic basins, and the long-term preservation of those Proterozoic strata. These results also helped elucidate how changes in subduction dynamics during the Neoproterozoic followed mantle cooling, which may have reshaped biogeochemical cycles on Earth's surface for the past ~800 million years.

27307517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27307517.value: Electronic structure methods to describe the correlated behavior of electrons dancing in molecules and materials are invaluable tools in exploring modern chemistry, materials and life sciences at the atomistic level. The quest to predict the electronic states of molecules based on quantum mechanical principles has a long history ever since the first milestone quantum chemistry study of the hydrogen molecule. Over the past several decades, a large amount of research effort has been invested into developing numerically feasible quantum chemistry approaches towards larger molecules and solids, driven by growing computational needs and emerging computing facilities. Consider a solid such as molecular crystal. The interplay of the highly packed structure and complex weak forces such as dispersion or hydrogen bonding manifest a series of polymorphic phases that are usually separated by only small energy differences. The subtlety of resulting energetics falls often within the error of empirical computations that are of little help in identifying correct polymorphic structures. For problems relevant to excited states, a charge-transfer exciton that spreads in photoexcited conjugated polymers has a binding energy of only a fraction of hydrogen atomic energy, e.g., a few kcal/mol. Other challenging examples can be drawn from the computational studies of heterogeneous catalysis, photochemical pathways, optoelectronics of van der Waals materials, and so on. The major difficulty is largely due to the correlated electron problem over a long length scale, for which existing many-body approaches are typically inaccessible in terms of computational expense. Here we propose to develop a framework of highly efficient and accurate electronic structure methods. The key methodological ingredients of our approach are as follows. First we solve for individual site-states of each structural unit by transforming the original difficult problem to the simpler one that can be treated efficiently for low-energy states in the model space. Following the bottom-up strategy, we then construct the wavefunction of the entire extended system through the real-space renormalization group method that leads to sparse Hamiltonian structure for diagonalization. The associated algorithmic and computational complexities will be heavily reduced towards simulations of realistic material by integrating the cutting-edge low-scaling and parallelization techniques of modern electronic structure theory. The suite of our methods will greatly enhance the performance of electronic structure study of complex systems, with the primary focus on the energetics of both ground- and excited-states as well as the interplay with structure modifications, and open further opportunities to inform atomistic multiscale modeling. 電子結構方法描述電子在分子和材料體系中的相關行為，已經成為人們在原子層面上研究現代化學，材料學和生命科學的重要方法。然而，儘管高性能計算機已得到空前發展，人們在使用量子力學的從頭算原理來精確處理大分子和固體材料體系時仍然面臨很大的困難。比如分子晶體，由於其分子排列和堆積方式取決於結構單元的分子特性和分子間弱相互作用力（如色散力或氫鍵）的微妙平衡，往往表現出晶體結構多態性，而當前流行的固體量子化學計算方案無法系統性的正確區分這些多態性結構。另外，對於一類在材料體系中的電子激發態，比如有機共軛聚合物中非定域的電荷轉移激子，常規量子化學方法計算的電子-空穴對結合能通常極不可靠。在其它領域例如計算非均相催化，光化學反應途徑，范德華材料等等，人們面臨的主要困難之一是如何在複雜尺度上快速準確的處理電子相關問題, 這是當代量子化學面臨的核心問題和挑戰性難題之一。 在這個項目裏，我們旨在開發針對分子聚集體的高效精確電子結構理論和計算方案。首先，我們通過在模型空間內構建非酉變換的有效哈密頓量，嘗試獲得單獨結構單元的定域分子態波函數。其次，通過實空間重整化群的方法構建全體系的哈密頓稀疏矩陣，並快速角化從而獲得整個擴展分子體系的近似全波函數。最後，我們還將嘗試現代電子結構理論的低標度方案和計算機並行化技術。通過以上步驟，本研究課題即將發展的相關算法旨在減少計算複雜度和相關成本，提高算法效率，並能夠系統精確的處理一類複雜體系的電子結構問題。本課題新發展的方法將適用於研究分子聚集體系電子能態性質及其同分子結構的關係，並為今後發展精度可控的普適多尺度模擬技術提供新的方向。

27307517.label: Realisation of objectives
27307517.value: Objective 1: We formulated a sparse Hamiltonian approach representing the geometric relaxation and evolution of local electronic states governed by correlated electrons at the second-order perturbation theory level (OSV-MP2 analytical gradient), rather than traditional density functional approximations. The first series of OSV-MP2 works was published on J. Chem. Theory Comput. (IF: 6.006, ACS) in January of 2020. For computing molecular excited states, we also proposed and developed a downfolded configuration interaction method capable of correlating a large amount of excited electrons with mean errors for excitation energy below 0.05 eV and for state energy below 0.5 kcal/mol. This work was presented as invited oral in International Chemical Congress of Pacific Basin Societies 2021 (Hawaii, USA, virtual), and is presently under preparation for publication in 2022. Extension of these methods for treating crystalline bulk states is being carried out by enforcing periodic boundary condition, with preliminary results which correctly predict crystal shapes from PBC-OSV-MP2 calculation of inter-cell interaction energies. More implementation works are needed for computing band structures by including the dispersion of k points customised to OSV-MP2 level of theory, which aims for publication in 2022-23. Objective 2: This objective has been fully achieved. By using the low-rank parametrisation of the wave function exploring correlation locality, our algorithm substantially reduces the number of parameters for optimising and evolving molecular structure at a similar accuracy to that by the full wave function parameter space. On a single-processor, the computing time is shortened by 1-2 orders of magnitude. The results were comprehensively benchmarked and demonstrated in our 2020 publication on J. Chem. Theory Comput. For excited state computations, we developed downfolded configuration interaction method that compresses the number of many-body electronic configurations by at least four orders of magnitude, as shown to benzene molecule, which substantially improves the affordability of computing resources such as memory and CPU costs. This result will be submitted for a series of publications in 2022. Objective 3: This objective has been largely realised. Beyond the traditional DFT-based band method, The current development of OSV-MP2 theory for treating aggregated molecular crystal is implemented only for a single Gamma-point in the k-space, which enables a single k-point prediction of crystal energy and shapes at the second-order perturbation theory. The computational efficiency is much improved for molecular crystal containing large chromophores in each unit cell. More implementation works are needed for including dispersive k points customised to OSV-MP2 level of theory, which will be used for band structure calculation. Objective 4: This objective has been fully completed. We implemented fully paralleled algorithm based on MPI-3 data communication parallelism through shared memory one-sided communication, which enables massive parallel scalability and memory accessibility across a multi-core multi-node computer architecture, supporting both global and local data structures. We applied this implementation to study two challenging chemistry problems: the optimal structure of three mechanically interlocked Cu-catenane supramolecular complexes, and the dynamical evolution of porphycene molecule revealing the presence of N-H protonic tautomerism and conformers. This work constitutes the second series of OSV-MP2 works and has been published on J. Chem. Theory Comput. (IF: 6.006, ACS) in October of 2021.

27307517.label: Major findings and research outcome
27307517.value: The major findings of this project are the theory and algorithm advancements which allow large-scale full quantum mechanical simulation of electron-electron and electron-nucleus correlations in addressing many-body chemistry problems. (1) We developed OSV-MP2 wave function theory to compute full quantum forces as the first-order geometric gradients of correlation energy by formulating and deriving OSV orbital relaxation and rotation [IF=6.006, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2020, 16, 196-210]. (2) We proposed and implemented the many-body expansion MBE(3)-OSV-MP2 ansaetz of OSV-MP2 analytical gradient method for complex molecules [IF=6.006, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2021, 17, 6841-6860]. As an application, this development was used to benchmark ab-initio molecular dynamics of porphycene molecule by correlating electrons at the MP2 level of theory for the first time, and we proposed to attribute the presence of N-H protonic tautomerism to electron correlations which could not be consistently captured by traditional density function theory, rather than proton quantum effects as claimed previously by others in literature. (3) The series of such developments of (1) and (2) delivers one of the fastest algorithms and program implementations in the world for molecular structure optimization and longer-time ab-initio molecular dynamics simulation, which allows full quantum mechanical applications to much larger molecules containing a few tens of thousands of atomic orbitals on massively parallel computer architecture (Tianhe-2 supercomputer), which was previously impossible at a similar length scale. The relevant findings were presented as invited oral talks at several international conferences/seminar. (4) We joined the active field of treating vibronic problems by contributing a new electron-nucleus correlation formulation based on the exact factorisation of molecular wave function [IF=3.488, J. Chem. Phys. 2021, 155, 104111] and by implementing DMRG-based Holstein-Peierls vibronic couplings [IF=9.825, Chem. Sci. 2021,12, 12928-12938]. These methods were presented at 2018 "Molecular Electronic Structure Conference" in Metz, France; 2019 "NSFC/RGC Joint Conference on Advanced Materials for Energy Related Applications" in HKU; 2019 "10th Biennial International Conference of the Asian Consortium on Computational Materials Science"; 2021 "30th International Conference on Photochemistry" in Geneva, Switzerland (virtual); 2021 ACS Publication Symposium "the Power of Chemical Transformations" in HKU (virtual). (5) We proposed the "downfolded configuration interaction" theory for computing discrete electronic states aiming for 0.05 eV accuracy or better by correlating a much larger amount of electrons, critical to the ability of distinguishing optoelectronic performance of chemistry and materials systems. This work was presented as invited oral talk at 2021 International Chemical Congress of Pacific Basin Societies (Hawaii, USA, virtual).

27307517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27307517.value: The theory, algorithm and program advanced in this research create new application scenarios in which a full quantum mechanical treatment can be now possible for some used-to-be-difficult chemically relevant problems. (1) Using MBE(3)-OSV-MP2 method, we will perform high-level molecular dynamics simulation on revealing multiphase reaction landscape and pathways between zwitterionic reactive Criegee intermediates (typically formed from precursive ozonolysis reactions) and atmospheric pollutant species (such as trace SO2, NO2) at aerosol-air interface. Their chemistry is relatively unexplored and debatable with respect to Criegee intermediate's hydrophobic substituents, oxidative states and aqueous environment. (2) Using the effective Hamiltonian dCI method we developed, we will conduct accurate determination of characters and levels of strongly correlated electronic excited states at different spin manifolds. This is to address the importance of exciton's many-body characters in managing singlet-triplet gap, spin-flip electron transfer and emissive performance of luminescent chromophores such as singlet fission or TADF emitter complexes. (3) Our periodic OSV-MP2 aims for targeting crystalline electronic correlations, such as dispersion and other non-covalent quantum forces governing the aggregation in molecular crystal. For instance, we can predict polymorphic shapes of drug molecular crystals by combining electronic structure calculation with spiral growth kinetics model.

27307517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27307517.value: Electron-electron and electron-nucleus many-body correlations are fundamentally important to chemistry, but are challenging to compute for complex molecule. We formulated and implemented a series of new theories and algorithms for computation of electronic states and structural evolution in complex molecules that exhibit important quantum mechanical many-body effects. Our developments represent one of the most advanced techniques in the field of low-scaling electronic structure theory by putting together low-rank molecular quantum mechanics theory, applied mathematics and computer science techniques, which creates new chemistry application scenarios that were previously difficult to study, such as ab-initio prediction of supramolecular geometries, time-dependent structural evolution, strongly correlated electronic states and electron-nucleus vibronic interactions.

27503517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27503517.value: Product anthropomorphism occurs when people perceive products as having humanlike intentions, feelings, and motivations. When a product possesses humanlike features in its visual design, when it incorporates an artificially intelligent conversational interface into its functional design (e.g., Siri in iPhone), or when it looks, talks, or moves like a human being in an advertisement, consumers are likely to perceive the focal product as a human being. Whereas prior research has shown that consumers may perceive an anthropomorphized product as a social, intentional, or intelligent entity, I propose that anthropomorphic features of a product may also make consumers perceive the focal product as a biological entity. Consequently, they misapply known principles about biological properties or constraints of human bodies to their evaluation of the focal product. I focus on two specific biological properties or constraints—susceptibility to infectious diseases and vulnerability in physically extreme conditions—in two related projects. In the first project, I propose that consumers will evaluate an anthropomorphized product less favorably than a non-anthropomorphized product when the prevalence of local epidemics (e.g., flu or Zika virus) is made salient. This effect results from disgust toward the anthropomorphized product and will be mitigated for products with which consumers have no physical contact during product usage and for consumers with low chronic disgust toward biological substances. In the second project, I aim to show that consumers will evaluate an anthropomorphized product less favorably than a non-anthropomorphized product when they intend to use the product in physically extreme conditions (e.g., desert, plateau, or icefield) because consumers expect that the "body-build" of an anthropomorphized product may lead to ill-functioning in these physically extreme conditions. I will further demonstrate that this effect will be reduced for products with a visually masculine appearance and for products that originate from extreme environments similar to the intended usage conditions. Theoretically, in both projects, the proposed mechanism is that consumers perceive an anthropomorphized product as a biological entity. By documenting convergent evidence for this biological consideration account, the current research program will contribute to the literature by establishing a new mechanism underlying the anthropomorphism effects. Practically, these two projects will provide direct managerial implications for how to tailor marketing communications (e.g., presenting a product as either a human being or simply an object in advertising) according to seasons (regular vs. epidemic) and product usage conditions (regular vs. physically extreme environments). 产品拟人化是指消费者感觉到产品与有着人类一样的意图、感觉和动机。当产品在视觉外观上具有人类的特征，当产品将人工智能界面融入其功能设计，或者当产品在广告中看起来，说起话来，或者动起来像一个人时，消费者有可能将当前产品感知为人类。 之前的研究表明消费者有可能将拟人化产品感知为具有社会性、具有意识性、或者具有智能性的实体，而我则提出产品的拟人化特征还有可能使消费者将当前产品感知为一个生物体。相应地，消费者会将其所了解到的有关人体生理属性或者限制的原理应用到产品的评价上面。在两个相关项目中，我将注意力集中在两个特定的生理属性和限制——易受传染性和在极端环境中的脆弱性。 在第一个项目中，我提出当区域性传染病（比如流感和寨卡病毒）被提及时，消费者对拟人化产品的评价会低于其对非拟人化产品的评价。这个效应来源于消费者对拟人化产品所产生的恶心感觉。当消费者在产品使用中与产品没有身体接触，以及当消费者对生化物质感到恶心的倾向很低时，这个效应将会被消除。 在第二个项目中，我试图揭示当消费者打算在极端物理环境中（例如，沙漠、高原、冰原）使用产品时，消费者对拟人化产品的评价会低于其对非拟人化产品的评价。这是因为消费者预期拟人化产品的“身体构造”会导致其在极端物理环境中的功能障碍。我会进一步揭示，当产品有着男性化的外观设计，以及当产品的原产地有与使用环境有着类似的极端环境时，这个效应将会被消除。 理论意义上，在两个项目中，预期的内在机制是消费者将拟人化产品感知为生物体。通过提供各方面支持基于这种有关生物性考虑的解释的证据，该研究将揭示拟人化影响的一个新的驱动机制。 实践意义上，这两个项目将会为如何根据季节（常规季节或是传染病流行季节）和产品使用环境（常规环境或是极端物理环境）来制定营销沟通策略（例如，在广告中是将产品展现为人类还是仅仅展现为物体）。

27503517.label: Realisation of objectives
27503517.value: 1. Systematically investigate when product anthropomorphism can negatively affect product evaluation. --In one published paper, the PI has demonstrated that product anthropomorphism can negatively affect product evaluation when a product, for which consumers prefer a small (vs. large) size, is animated to move in a slow (vs. fast) manner in a video advertisement. In another paper in preparation for submission, the PI has shown that anthropomorphizing a base product (e.g., a printer) can negatively influence consumers’ evaluation of the replacement parts (e.g., ink cartridges) for the focal base product offered by a different brand. 2. Develop a comprehensive framework of how product anthropomorphism influences consumer decision making by triggering a biological consideration. --The PI has examined different aspects of the biological consideration. In one published paper, the PI has shown that due to biological constraints, movement speed and physical size are in general negatively associated for animate agents, and consumers apply this biological consideration when they observe that products are animated to move in a similar way as humans or animals do in video advertisements. In another paper in preparation for submission, the PI has shown that humans are in general averse to the invasion of bodily substances from foreign entities, and consumers apply this biological consideration to products which they perceive to be like humans. 3. Provide convergent evidence for the proposed biological consideration mechanism by examining different domains of decision making. --The PI has examined the downstream consequences of the proposed biological consideration mechanism across various domains, such as product size assessment, willingness-to-pay for a product, purchase of product replacement parts, and product retention decisions. 4. Validate research findings in an ecological experimental setting by having participants interact with real marketing stimuli and make actual product choices. --In all experiments conducted for this project, the PI has employed experimental stimuli adapted from real-world brands, product designs, and advertisements to make sure that the study scenarios are relevant and realistic and can simulate real-life consumption decision contexts. The PI has also provided actual products for research participants to interact with and choose from to demonstrate that the proposed effects are consequential. 5. Provide managerially actionable implications for marketers to better manage anthropomorphic product features in marketing communications. --Human-like features can be directly incorporated into the visual appearance of a product (e.g., marketers can make the front of a car or that of a printer look like a human face), and anthropomorphic qualities can be perceived from interactive conversational features of a product as well (e.g., people are more likely to perceive a smartphone as a human being when they talk to the phone using Siri or Cortana). In addition, marketers can present products as human beings in print or video advertisements by making the product move or talk the way as humans do. For these reasons, the findings on the effects of product anthropomorphism can be easily utilized in marketing practice. The findings of this project provide implications for how to make better use of human-like product features to manage product size expectations and promote same-brand replacement parts.

27503517.label: Major findings and research outcome
27503517.value: Supported by the ECS project, the PI and collaborators have completed two papers, which examine different aspects of the biological consideration mechanism triggered by product anthropomorphism. --The first paper has been published in the Journal of Marketing (one of the top four journals in the field of marketing) in 2020: Jia, He (Michael), B. Kyu Kim, and Lin Ge (2020), “Speed Up, Size Down: How Animated Movement Speed in Product Videos Influences Size Assessment and Product Evaluation,” Journal of Marketing, 84 (5), 100–16. This paper examines how consumers’ knowledge about biological constraints of animate agents (e.g., humans and animals) influences consumers’ perception of products. Due to biological constraints, movement speed and physical size are in general negatively associated for animate agents. We demonstrate that consumers apply this negative association between movement speed and physical size to their evaluation of products, such that they perceive a product to be larger when the product moves slower in a video advertisement. Furthermore, the effect of movement speed on product size perception is more evident when consumers anthropomorphize the product. --The second paper has been prepared for a journal submission: Jia, He (Michael), B. Kyu Kim, Echo Wen Wan, and C. Whan Park, “I Need My Own Substance! Effects of Product Anthropomorphism on Brand Choice of Replacement Parts,” working paper. This paper examines how consumers’ knowledge about biological principles of animate agents influences their brand choice of replacement parts (e.g., hard drive) for a base product (e.g., computer). Humans are in general averse to the invasion of bodily substances from foreign entities. We demonstrate that such a biological consideration drives a greater choice share of same-brand replacement parts when consumers anthropomorphize the base product. --In addition to the aforementioned journal publication/submission, the PI also presented the major findings in the seminars at City University of Hong Kong, Fudan University, Shanghai University of Finance and Economics, and University of International Business and Economics, as well as at leading international conferences, such as the Association for Consumer Research Annual Conference, the Theory + Practice in Marketing Conference, and the China Marketing International Conference.

27503517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27503517.value: First, future research can explore what specific anthropomorphic features may have a greater potential to trigger a biological consideration. For example, a product has a cute-looking appearance that is associated with infantile visual features may strongly trigger a biological consideration, such that consumers may perceive the product as physically vulnerable and weak. Second, further studies can investigate what characteristics of consumers, products, or decision contexts can systematically activate different types of considerations regarding an anthropomorphized product, for instance, examining when the biological consideration focused on in the current project is more likely to be triggered by anthropomorphism, against other considerations of social relationship or intentionality examined in prior research on anthropomorphism. These research endeavors will contribute to an overarching framework that deepens our understanding of the mechanisms underlying the anthropomorphism effects. Third, our proposed biological consideration mechanism may extend beyond consumers’ responses to products with human-like features to their responses to products with animal-like features, given that all creatures are made of flesh and blood, to which the biological consideration should be similarly applicable. Future research on products with animal-like features will broaden the implications of the biological consideration proposed and examined in this project.

27503917.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27503917.value: Firms do not make their decisions on disclosure independently. Inter-firm relationships such as strategic alliances and customer-supplier relationships influence a firm's strategic decisions on disclosure. An example of the interdependence of disclosure is the clustering of bad news during times of crisis, which implies that firms take into consideration strategic disclosure decisions of other firms that they have relationships with. In this proposed project, we investigate the network effect of inter-firm relationships on the asymmetry in the clustering of disclosure of good and bad news. More specifically, we examine 1) how the network structure (e.g., centrality) as well as the strength of inter-firm relationships influences a firm’s disclosure decisions, and 2) how central firms can stimulate the propagation of disclosure. To understand the effects of inter-firm relationships on disclosure, we develop a multi-firm model based on a network economy. The customer-supplier network consists of many customer-supplier relationships. A certain company that is a customer in one customer-supplier relationship can be a supplier in another customer-supplier relationship. Thus, a firm can be more connected with other firms by locating more centrally in the customer-supplier network. Firms with high centrality—for instance, Walmart, Ford, and HP—may have different incentives to disclose their financial information and trigger stylized patterns of disclosure in the economy. The network-based model highlights the effects of not only the externality of disclosure but also the network structure of inter-firm relationships. This proposed project will make related contributions. First, it will help to explain interesting patterns of firms’ disclosure by introducing the network effect on disclosure. To our best knowledge, this research will be the first attempt to study firms’ disclosure decisions in a network economy. Second, it will enable standard setters to implement adequate regulations through an understanding of the externality of disclosure in the network. Because the externality of disclosure varies with the structure of networks, policymakers need to carefully consider the network structure of real activities of firms in the economy. Lastly, the project will provide important guidance for future empirical research on disclosure.
