28601017.label: Project Title(Chinese)
28601017.value: 認知靈活性對幼兒閱讀能力的重要

28601017.label: Project Objectives
28601017.value: To identify the unique role and underlying mechanism of CF to Chinese word reading at preschool level. To construct a path model regarding the structural relationship among CF, linguistic skills, and word reading in Chinese.
rows: To identify the unique role and underlying mechanism of CF to Chinese word reading at preschool level.
To construct a path model regarding the structural relationship among CF, linguistic skills, and word reading in Chinese.

28601017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28601017.value: Learning to read is a complex process that requires one to flexibly manage multiple features of print (e.g., orthography, sound, meaning). Among all languages, Chinese is an opaque language that has extremely complicated mappings among the features of print. A high level of flexibility is thereby demanded for processing these features. Despite this challenge, children in Hong Kong start to learn reading Chinese words early at preschool ages (4 to 6 years old). Cognitive flexibility (CF) – defined as the mental ability to manage multiple dimensions of a stimulus at one time and actively switch between them during a task performance – is thus hypothesized to play a significant role in preschool reading. It is known that CF emerges in children at age 4 when they begin able to manage multiple dimensions of objects (e.g., color-shape flexibility); however, whether Chinese preschoolers further develop reading-specific CF (e.g., sound-meaning flexibility) remains largely unknown. Furthermore, the role of CF in Chinese word reading acquisition, as well as whether it is a key to reading success, have yet been examined. The current project takes the initiative to examine the unique contribution and underlying mechanism of CF in word reading skills among Chinese preschoolers. In addition to prove the theoretical significance of CF, the current project also aims to demonstrate the practical effectiveness of CF training in improving Chinese word reading skills. These will be achieved by two empirical studies – a cross-sectional correlational study (Study 1 - 200 participants) and an interventional training study (Study 2 - 150 participants) – with Chinese preschool children aged 5 to 6. In study 1, a path model regarding the structural relationship among CF, linguistic skills, and word reading in Chinese will be constructed using path analysis method. One major focus of the model will be on testing whether CF has a direct path to word reading via facilitating the flexible use of sound-meaning information of words. In Study 2, a total of five experimental groups will be administered in which participants will receive different trainings on CF and/or other controlled skills. The study will demonstrate the cause-and-effect relationship between CF and word reading, as well as provide practical evidence that CF training is effective. Overall, the findings of the two studies have important practical implications for early diagnostic assessment and reading instruction for Chinese preschool children.

28601017.label: Realisation of objectives
28601017.value: The current longitudinal study collected data from 190 Cantonese-speaking Chinese children (105 boys and 85 girls) who were recruited from 5 kindergartens in Hong Kong. Each child was individually assessed twice when they were at 5.29 years old (Time 1) and 5.79 years old (Time 2). The assessment included a range of executive function tasks (i.e., cognitive flexibility [CF], working memory, and inhibition control), linguistic tasks (i.e., phonological skill, semantic skill, and orthographic skill), and reading tasks (i.e., word reading, fluency, and reading comprehension). Since one novel aspect of this study was to identify the potential importance of reading-specific CF, the children were also assessed on two self-developed measures of reading-specific CF – sound-meaning CF and orthographic CF tasks. The collected data was analyzed to address two project objectives. Objective 1: To identify the unique role and underlying mechanism of CF to Chinese word reading at preschool level. First, to distinguish the unique role of CF from other executive function components, we conducted separate measures on children’s CF, working memory, and inhibition control. We found that CF uniquely predicted children’s reading abilities after other executive function components were controlled. Second, we proposed and tested a possible mechanism that might account for the role of CF in reading. We hypothesized that children with better CF are more effective in managing the multiple aspects of linguistic features in word (e.g., sound, meaning, and orthography) and thus resulted in better reading performance. To test the hypothesized mechanism, we designed a sound-meaning CF task and an orthographic CF task to capture children’s efficiency in manipulating multiple linguistic features in Chinese words. Children’s performance in these reading-specific CF tasks were used to predict reading abilities both concurrently and longitudinally. We found that reading-specific CF uniquely predicted reading abilities even after basic CF and relevant linguistic skills involved in the tasks were controlled. Specifically, sound-meaning CF uniquely predicted reading after basic CF, phonological skill, and semantic skill were controlled, while orthographic CF uniquely predicted reading after basic CF and orthographic skill were controlled. Such findings demonstrated that sound-meaning CF and orthographic CF are two possible mechanisms explaining the role of CF in early Chinese reading acquisition. Objective 2: To construct a path model regarding the structural relationship among CF, linguistic skills, and word reading in Chinese. While CF and linguistic skills are known to be essential for Chinese reading, it is unclear how the two might contribute to Chinese reading by functioning interactively. We proposed a novel view that CF and linguistic skills collectively contribute to Chinese reading through facilitating reading-specific CF. A path model was constructed based on our view, and the model was found to fit the data reasonably well. Results of path analysis showed that CF and linguistic skills at Time 1 significantly contributed to word reading at Time 2 both directly and indirectly via the mediation of reading-specific CF. The path model provides a theoretical framework to understand the structural relationships among CF, linguistic skills, and early Chinese reading. Such knowledge serves to be a major step towards building a more comprehensive model of Chinese reading. Taken together, the two objectives of the current project were fully achieved. The original third objective “to determine the effectiveness of CF training in facilitating word reading skills among Chinese preschoolers” was removed based on the funding condition suggested by the RGC panel.

28601017.label: Major findings and research outcome
28601017.value: The current findings help us to better understand the role of CF in Chinese reading: First, previous Chinese studies have yet to examine CF as an independent executive function component. We filled the research gap and demonstrated that CF has a unique contribution to early reading beyond IQ and other executive function components (including working memory and inhibition control). Based on the findings, we advocate that the role of CF should not be considered as merged under the broad umbrella of executive functions. Second, previous researchers seldom studied the mechanism of how CF contributes to reading. Our findings suggest that preschool readers need CF to manipulate various linguistic elements in Chinese words: the first mechanism is to manipulate the sound and meaning features of words (Fong & Ho, under preparation), while the second mechanism is to manipulate the different orthographic features (e.g., configuration and radical) of words (Fong & Chung, 2019). These findings were the first to confirm the existence of reading-specific CF in Chinese language, and that sound-meaning and orthographic CF are two fundamental types of reading-specific CF. The findings suggest a direction for future studies of other possible mechanisms between CF and reading development. Third, we found that Chinese poor readers showed early signs of CF weakness at kindergarten. We identified two groups of readers (i.e., higher-achieving readers and lower-achieving readers) among the 190 kindergarten children based on their word reading score and other matching variables. We found that lower-achieving readers performed significantly poorer in CF and reading-specific CF (Fong & Ho, under review). The above findings were published in peer-reviewed journals (e.g., Educational Psychology) and international conferences (e.g., International Congress of Psychology).

28601017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
28601017.value: This project provides a theoretical basis for further research on the instructional value of CF training. While current reading instruction typically involves teaching the sound and meaning of words, it seldom focuses on how flexibly or quickly children can switch from processing a words’ sound to its meaning (or vice versa). They current findings suggest that such flexibility training could be essential. Even though preschool readers might have developed adequate individual linguistic skills, they were found to further need efficiency in applying multiple aspects of linguistic skills during the act of reading. A direction for future interventional research is to examine whether preschool readers need explicit training in reading-specific CF. If affirmative results are obtained, teachers shall be advised to make use of flexibility training as an additional strategy to improve the reading abilities of children. To address this practical question, we secured an internal research funding and conducted a pilot study to preliminarily examine the effectiveness of CF training. Based on the initial evidence, external funding will be obtained to further investigate the potential benefits of CF training systematically and comprehensively.

28601017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
28601017.value: Learning to read is an important curricular objective in early childhood education. Previous studies informed us that learning to read requires children to acquire the sound, meaning, and orthographic knowledge of words. This study further suggests that gaining knowledge in these individual aspects of words is not enough. Children further need to exercise an important cognitive capacity – cognitive flexibility (CF) – for coordinating the multiple aspects of words simultaneously during the act of reading. We found that most K3 children have rudimentary flexibility in processing different aspects of words. For example, they could sort a bunch of words into categories by considering both the sound and meaning of the words simultaneously. More importantly, we found that such reading-specific CF had a unique role in facilitating children’s reading abilities both concurrently and across time. Taken together, the current project raised both theoretical and practical insights into preschool reading acquisition. Theoretically, it initiates the use of a novel concept ‘reading-specific CF’ to better understand the cognitive demand of reading. Practically, it provides valuable insights to improve reading instruction in preschool classrooms. Future studies are recommended to explore the feasibility and potential benefits of integrating CF into early childhood reading instruction.

28601617.label: Project Title(Chinese)
28601617.value: 在香港看中國大陸電視劇：年輕人，身分認同與跨文化消費

28601617.label: Project Objectives
28601617.value: producing timely empirical data on watching mainland drama in Hong Kong; reworking theories of transcultural audiences’ viewing motivations; extending our understanding of contemporary Hong Kong youngsters by examining their negotiations in local and national identities.
rows: producing timely empirical data on watching mainland drama in Hong Kong;
reworking theories of transcultural audiences’ viewing motivations;
extending our understanding of contemporary Hong Kong youngsters by examining their negotiations in local and national identities.

28601617.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28601617.value: 作為最流行的藝術形式，電視劇具有重大的經濟、政治和社會意義。香港電視劇曾經幫助定義香港身分，輸入中國大陸后也影響了好幾代大陸觀眾。但是，最近幾年出現了一股「 逆流」：許多香港出生的年輕人發展出對中國大陸生產的電視劇（以下簡稱陸劇）——如《步步驚心》、《何以笙簫默》、《花千骨》和《瑯琊榜》等的興趣甚至偏好。這個現象頗不尋常，因為（1）以前，陸劇被認為只能吸引來自大陸的新移民群體，或者中老年觀眾；（2）香港人的國族認同均在2008年之後下滑，這個趨勢在年輕人中尤其明顯。所以，為什麼香港年輕人會在「反中抗陸」的社會氣氛中觀看陸劇？本研究試圖回答這個充滿矛盾的觀眾動機問題。 在前期研究中，我用焦點小組訪談法調查過香港大學生的電視劇消費，研究發現，比起本地劇和外國劇，陸劇是小組討論中最具爭議性的話題，很多香港大學生都看陸劇，其動機導向四個理論：首先，陸劇是新舊媒體上最易獲得的媒體資源；其次，最近走紅的陸劇絕大部分改編自年輕人寫的、寫給年輕人看的中國網絡小說；然後，香港大學生喜歡陸劇呈現的「烏托邦感性」，特別喜歡陸劇獨有的類型如「仙俠劇」；最後，因為很多來自香港的台前幕後的人才在陸劇生產過程中扮演關鍵角色，稱呼這些劇集為「合拍劇」，而非「陸劇」，可能更能把握全球在地化趨勢中的劇集特質。 前期研究只關注大學生，本研究打算擴展到所有18-30歲的香港年輕人，邀請其中看過陸劇的觀眾參與。研究方法分為三部分：「網絡民族誌」分析媒體報道和網上的香港觀眾對陸劇的討論；生產研究和文本分析提供背景性的知識；最重要的還是觀眾訪談，我將以一對一的、半結構式、面對面的深入訪談為方法，採訪大概34位看過陸劇的香港年輕人。 本研究是一個跨學科的嘗試，將與電視劇、觀眾、跨文化消費、青年研究、文學改編和全球在地化的理論進行對話。香港的電視劇觀眾研究長期處於匱乏狀態，本研究將提供及時的經驗性的數據。對於青年研究和青年教育來說，本研究也將有助於了解香港年輕人對本地和國族身分的探索。同時，由於電視劇是一國展示「軟實力」的重要前鋒，本研究將為香港的文化政策制定者提供洞見，在所謂的「大國崛起」的語境下重新定位香港的流行文化及香港的位置。最後，因為傳統的收視率在這個用不同媒體收看電視劇的新時代越來越失去可靠性，這個定性的觀眾研究將幫助電視工業從業者更好地理解青年觀眾——這樣一批難以理解卻又無比珍貴的收視群體。

28601617.label: Realisation of objectives
28601617.value: Objective 1: producing timely empirical data on watching mainland drama in Hong Kong; Textual Analysis: I have elected 10 representative mainland Chinese TV dramas which are liked by Hong Kong young people in recent years, and my criteria are: (1) mainland dramas that are rated highly in Douban.com, a Chinese version of IMDb; (2) mainland dramas that are bought and aired by Hong Kong TV stations, such as TVB, ViuTV and Hong Kong Open TV; (3) mainland dramas that are frequently reported by Hong Kong mass and new media, including but not limited to: Apple Daily, Ming Pao, ON.CC, Ta Kung Pao, Wenwei Po, South China Morning Post, and HK01, etc’ (4) mainland dramas that are mentioned and (dis)liked by my interviewers. As a result, these 10 mainland dramas meet all 4 or 3 of these above-mentioned criteria:  Empresses in the Palace 《後宮·甄嬛傳》（2011）  Scarlet Heart 《步步驚心》（2011）  Nirvana in Fire 《琅琊榜》 （2015）  Once Upon a Time 《三生三世十裏桃花》（2017）  Addiction 《上癮》（2016）  The Romance of Three Kingdoms 《三國演義》 （1994）and Three Kingdoms《三國》（2010）  The Heaven Sword and the Dragon Saber 《倚天屠龍記》（2019）  A Love So Beautiful《致我們單純的小美好》（2017）  Story of Yanxi Palace 《延禧攻略》（2015）  My Chief and My Regiment《我的團長我的團》（2009） Objective 2: reworking theories of transcultural audiences’ viewing motivations” Theory: Romance According to research, compared to other TV drama genres, romance can be easily exported to other countries and districts (Yang, 2008); in addition, romance is the safest and unpolitical genre which can easily pass the censorship systems in different counties and districts. In this case, 6 of 10 dramas fall into this genre: Empresses in the Palace, Scarlet Heart, Once Upon a Time, The Heaven Sword and the Dragon Saber, A Love So Beautiful, Story of Yanxi Palace. Based on popular American romance novels in 1980s, Janice Radway’s book (1985) proposes a formula of romance: the hero must be intelligent, gentle, and gets a sense of humor, as well as protect the heroine; the heroine is supposed to be intelligent, independent, strong, fiery, gets a sense of humor, and is capable of defy the hero. Actually, these 6 mainland dramas’ heroes and heroines are almost the same with Radways. Theory: queer studies Boys’ Love (BL). BL is the East Asian version of Slash in the West, which is a cultural text written by and for heterosexual female, and descripts male-male love and sex. Addiction is a story of 2 high school students who go beyond the barrier of homophobia and be with each other eventually. BL is not a gay art, but it does show sympathy toward them and raise gay communities’public awareness. According to several of my interviewees, there is no BL Hong Kong TV drama which can cater to BL fans’watching needs; and mainland BL TV drama started at an early stage, so it becomes an object of fandom of some Hong Kong young people. Theory: hybridity According to Stuart Hall, we should move away from the problematic understanding of essentialism in notions of “purity” and “authenticity” (1990). The concept “hybridity” enables us to take a historical view on cultural texts. Mainland Chinese TV dramas, in this line of thinking, should not be considered as having an essentialized “Mainlandness” that is different from “HongKongness”. Because most of popular mainland TV dramas which are liked by Hong Kong youngsters are actually co-productions which are products of mainland, Hong Kong, Taiwan, and other districts’ staff. For instance, Ada Tsoi, the Hong Kong actress, plays a leading role in Empresses in the Palace; Lam Yuk-fun the Hong Kong director has directed many hit mainland dramas such as Scarlet Heart and Once Upon a Time. Objective 3: extending our understanding of contemporary Hong Kong youngsters by examining their negotiations in local and national identities. After re-theorizing the above-mentioned theories, we can find that all support one conclusion: you want to be fascinated by mainland TV dramas, but you do want to be conquered by it; in other words, watching mainland TV drama does not mean embracing its ideologies, either good or bad, completely and whole-heartedly. Because romance is an international common language, my interviewees are not dedicated to mainland romance dramas; rather, they watch all “good” romance dramas, such as South Korea’s Descendants of The Sun (2016), and Taiwan drama Someday or One Day (2019). Similarly, since what some of my interviewees like is BL stories, their object of watching is not limited to mainland produced ones, but to all BL texts. When History (2017) is released online, they found it is more interesting than Addiction, thus they became fans of History. Meanwhile, many of this research’s participants love Charmaine Sheh when she was in TVB, therefore, watching her performance in Story of Yanxi Palace is enjoying How a Hong Kong actress’ outstanding acting skills enhance this drama’s quality. Mainland-HongKong relations has been going down since 2008 (Chiu, 2016). Although Hong Kong young people’s consuming of mainland Chinese TV dramas helps dispel some misunderstanding of mainlanders, but eventually media consumption alone is not an effective tool to improve mainland-HongKong relations.

28601617.value: Textual Analysis: (2018) 「從親密關系研究看宮鬥劇提供的婚戀指南」，《戲劇與影視評論》6（2018）： 110-120. “Mating Advice in Palace-manipulations Television Dramas”. Stage and Screen Review 6 (2018): 110-120. Textual Analysis of Empresses in the Palace and Story in Yanxi Palace, which are among the favorite mainland TV dramas of my female interviewees. 28601617.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
28601617.value: Nature: This is an audience study of why Hong Kong young people watch mainland Chinese TV dramas when mainland-HongKong relationships deteriorated after 2008. By integrating textual analysis and empirical audience studies, this project provides a relatively broad picture of transcultural cultural consumption. Significance and value: 1. for cultural studies: this project re-theorizes major concepts by scrutinizing an interesting media contra-flow case: romance, queer, hybridity, etc. 2. for Hong Kong studies: mainland-HongKong relationship is not only an academic topic, but also a reality that nearly every HongKonger has to face every day. This project contributes by researching one dimension of such relationships: transcultural media consumption. The result indicates that although such transcultural media flow enables Hong Kong youngsters to understand mainland more thoroughly; however, such consumption has not changed their cultural identities. They love mainland dramas, but they do not want to take a subjective position of mainlanders.

28601717.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28601717.value: 關於中國小說的起源，過去多以魏、晉為伊始，至唐代發展成熟。近年來出土文獻研究提供了戰國、秦漢時期，早期小說的材料。但是有關中國早期小說的起源、文體特徵以及社會意義，由於史料不足，學界尚乏共識。本研究認為，《穆天子傳》恰可以彌補這一個缺環。 作為中國史上最早出土並完整流傳至今的出土文獻，《穆天子傳》的研究涉及文獻學、古文字學、文學史與歷史地理學等多個學科，具有深遠意義。基於本人過去在西周史的研究基礎，本研究欲對《穆天子傳》作一次通盤研究。首先，從古文字學與版本學的角度，重新檢閱其文本與文字隸定的正確性。其次，以年代明確的金文為時間標尺，分析《穆天子傳》包含的多時代成份。在這些基礎之上，本研究進一步從文學史的視角，探討《穆天子傳》的文獻性質。本研究希望超越真、偽二分的傳統框架，改由史實與想像互動的文學創作過程，解釋《穆天子傳》包含真實與想像成份的原因，進而探討戰國時期史學傳統蛻變出小說的背景與歷程，以及早期小說的作者、讀者、傳佈以及閱讀方式等議題。最後，本研究將以《穆天子傳》保存的地理訊息，探討戰國時期魏國的地理知識及其西北地理想像，為早期小說真偽雜糅的文本特質提供又一例證。 本研究涉及《穆天子傳》的文本基礎以及歷史意義，期許其對文獻、歷史、地理與文學史，均作出貢獻。 The prevalent theory traces the origins of Chinese fiction to the Wei and Jin Dynasties and considers the Tang Dynasty the time when they emerged fully fledged. With the advancement of archaeological works in China, this theory is gradually being challenged by excavated works of fiction dated to the Warring States and the Qin and Han periods. However, questions such as what are the stylistic features of early Chinese fiction and how did the fiction genre developed from that of historical writing remain to be answered. The purpose of this project is to focus on Mutienzi zhuan (The Travels of King Mu) to answer the above questions. As the earliest excavated text that survives into the modern age in Chinese history, our research on Mutienzi zhuan involves multiple aspects. We will start with a textual study of the text from a paleographical perspective, then move on to date its contents by comparing the text against documented bronze sources. The third step is to analyze the stylistic features of Mutienzi zhuan by comparing it with selected early fiction from other cultures, such as The Golden Ass, One Thousand and One Nights, and Mesopotamian mythologies, and to investigate the authorship, readership, transmission, and consumption of early Chinese fiction from a social perspective. The last step is to distinguish between the real and imagined geography in the text and reconstruct the transportation geography of King Mu’s travels using a historical geographical approach. It is hoped that this comprehensive research on Mutienzi zhuan will contribute to the study of Chinese paleography, history, geography and literature.

28602517.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28602517.value: 睡眠障礙是患有自閉症譜系障礙（ASD）兒童的常見問題，很多家庭困擾亦因而伴隨而來。質素差的睡眠可能會加劇ASD的核心症狀，包括刻板行為，人與人之間的互動和患者的健康。因此，怎樣有效地去改善ASD兒童的睡眠障礙可見是非常重要的。以往的方法通常是透過行為治療或攝取有補充褪黑激素的藥物為主。然而，行為治療的可持續性及患者本身服用其他藥物（例如抗抑鬱藥和興奮劑）通常會其有效性。另一方面，研究證明體力活動對正常發育（TD）的兒童的睡眠障礙問題是十分有效的。因此，人們很自然地會問用體力活動作為治療正常ASD兒童的睡眠障礙問題措施是否適合。此項的研究目的就是要調查體力活動能否是有效地改善ASD兒童的睡眠質素。在褪黑激素的研究框架下，我們將研究體力活動對ASD兒童睡眠的影響。根據以往用在TD兒童的研究經驗，體力活動將有助改變褪黑激素水平, 從而影響生理的晝夜規律。 ASD兒童的褪黑激素水平通常低於TD兒童，而褪黑激素的補充劑通常用於治療該群體的睡眠障礙。在此研究計劃裡，三十二名的ASD兒童將會被安排參與慢跑的活動。我們將通過客觀的行為評估及睡眠記錄來監測參與者睡眠質素的變化，如五個睡眠參數（睡眠期，睡眠效率，睡眠喚醒期和持續睡眠時間）。除此之外，所有參與者將被安排收集24小時的尿液樣本以測量其褪黑激素的水平。我們將透過從樣本中的「6-氨基槲皮素」(一種肌酸酐調節的褪黑激素)作為代表參與者的褪黑激素水平。所有評估將在慢跑活動之前 ( T1)，在慢跑活動或常規治療12週後 (T2)和完成後的12週後（T3）進行，以檢查效果的有效性及其可持續性。該研究的結果可以讓我們明白體力活動對ASD兒童睡眠的影響及其背後機制，而這結果將有助設計有效的干預活動來改善兒童的睡眠質素。

28602517.label: Realisation of objectives
28602517.value: The project has been completed on schedule with four research outputs - three peer-reviewed articles (two are published and one is submitted and under review) and one conference paper. More than 100 children with ASD have been recruited for study related to the current related to the study. All the objectives have been successfully achieved and details are as follows: Objective 1: To examine the association between physical activity and sleep quality in children with ASD. Two studies generated from the projects showed that physical activity (morning jogging) could improve sleep in children with ASD. For example, in the first study, the exercise intervention has shown effective in increasing sleep efficiency and shortening the sleep onset latency after the intervention period (see Tse et al., 2019 for more information). In contrast, the second study showed different findings, where the physical exercise did not have any effect on sleep efficiency, sleep onset latency and wake after sleep onset. Nevertheless, it still indicated a significant increase in sleep duration after the exercise intervention. Therefore, we believed that physical exercise was feasible to drive sleep improvement in children with ASD. Objective 2: To examine the possible sustained effects of physical activity on improving melatonin secretion and sleep quality in children with ASD. The second study (submitted and under review) has investigated the impact of physical exercise on endogenous melatonin secretion level in children with ASD and whether the effect can be sustained 6 weeks after intervention. Results showed that the exercise effect on both sleep and melatonin secretion cannot be sustained, which implied that regular exercise habit might be needed for the sleep benefits of physical exercise. This finding was pioneer in the literature as no previous studies have examined this aspect in exercise-sleep relation. Further research is needed to compare the effect of regular exercise and non-regular exercise on sleep quality in children with ASD. Objective 3: To investigate how physical activity impacts sleep via the melatonin-mediated mechanism model. Despite the overall sleep benefits were shown in the study, there was no significant exercise effect on endogenous melatonin secretion. We suspected this was due to two reasons. First, there was a lack of inclusion criteria on participants’ sleep quality. Without such criteria, we may have recruited participants without any sleep problem, and therefore the real impact of exercise on sleep may not be examined. Future research should consider recruiting participants whose sleep quality is below average (e.g., sleep efficiency ⩽ 80%). Second, the measurements of melatonin should be conducted immediately following the physical exercise, or at least within the same day of the exercise intervention, in order to detect any effect of exercise on melatonin secretion in children with ASD. In sum, the study is regarded as pioneer in linking exercise, sleep and melatonin secretion. The three research papers have provided direction and advice for implementing future research to examine how different exercise parameters (e.g., various intensity, frequency, duration and time for exercise) impacts on sleep and melatonin, particularly in those children with ASD and sleep disorder.

28602517.label: Major findings and research outcome
28602517.value: There are three major findings yielded from the project: First, in lines with previous studies, physical exercise at moderate intensity level is shown beneficial to sleep in children with ASD. Second, physical exercise in the present study had no effect on modulating endogenous melatonin secretion as measured by 24-h and first morning urinary aMT6s level. Finally, the sleep benefits cannot be sustained 6 weeks after the exercise intervention, which suggested that exercise should be on regular basis in order to induce such benefits in children with ASD. Additionally, this research project also discovered that the potential cognitive benefits (e.g. inhibition control as shown in one study) and behavioral benefits (as shown in the under-review study) of physical exercise in children with ASD. These additional findings open many research opportunities to manipulate different exercise parameters (e.g. frequency, duration, time, intensity etc) on sleep, cognition and behaviors in children with ASD.

28602517.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
28602517.value: There were several limitations of the current research projects that require further investigations First, there is a lack of inclusion criteria on participants’ sleep quality. Without such criteria, we may have recruited participants without any sleep problem, and therefore the real impact of exercise on sleep may not be examined. Future research should consider recruiting participants whose sleep quality is below average (e.g., sleep efficiency ⩽ 80%). Second, the measurements of melatonin should be conducted immediately following the physical exercise, or at least within the same day of the exercise intervention, in order to detect any effect of exercise on melatonin secretion in children with ASD. Meanwhile, further research should be continued with the focus on tracing the underlying mechanism of how physical exercise impacts sleep. Apart from the aforementioned suggestion, other biomarkers such as BDNF, saliva cortisol level that may plausibly drive the sleep improvement should be examined. In that way, the underlying mechanism could be unveiled, which in turns lead to optimization of exercise intervention to treat the sleep disorder in children with ASD and other populations.

28602517.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
28602517.value: Sleep problems are commonly found in children with ASD and disturbed their daily lives the present study is to investigate whether physical exercise can benefit we aim to investigate whether physical activity is an effective intervention to improve sleep quality for children with ASD. Moreover, we will also investigate how physical activity impacts on sleep in children with ASD through a melatonin-mediated mechanism model. According to this model, it is suggested that physical activity could affect circadian rhythm by altering melatonin levels. Melatonin levels are generally lower in children with ASD than in their typically developing counterparts and supplemental melatonin medication is often used to treat sleep disturbance in this population. In this study, we will conduct a parallel-group randomized controlled trial of 32 child participants with ASD that compares a jogging intervention group and a control group receiving standard care. We will monitor the changes of their sleep quality as depicted by four sleep parameters (sleep onset latency, sleep efficiency, wake after sleep onset and sleep duration) through objective actigraphic assessment and parental sleep logs. To measure melatonin level, all participants will be instructed to collect a 24-h urine sample. 6-sulfatoxymelatonin, a creatinine-adjusted morning urinary melatonin representative of the participant’s melatonin levels, will be measured from the sample. All assessments will be carried out before the intervention (T1), immediately after the 12 weeks of physical activity or regular treatment (T2), and 12 weeks post-intervention (T3) to examine the sustainability of the intervention effects. The findings of this proposed study can provide information on the mechanism by which physical activity impacts on sleep in children with ASD, which may ultimately lead to the design of an effective intervention to improve the sleep quality of children with ASD.

28603817.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28603817.value: Using paid domestic labor is becoming increasingly common in Hong Kong and many other post-industrial societies. In 2011, about 15% of domestic households with married couples employed a live-in domestic helper. Unlike many Western societies where the households tend to hire part-time domestic help, nearly 90% of Hong Kong households using paid domestic labor employed foreign live-in helpers at home. Therefore, the knowledge from Western societies may not help us to fully understand the role of domestic help in the Hong Kong context. As the well-being of a large number of families is related to this family practice, a study dedicated to this issue would contribute significantly to the empirical and theoretical literature of family sociology, and provide valuable policy insights into Hong Kong society. The scope of previous studies on this topic is limited in three ways: (1) Most studies rely on cross-sectional data only and take choosing to hire domestic help as a simple dichotomous one-off decision. None of these studies incorporated a temporal dimension to consider the timing, frequency and length of employment of the domestic helpers; (2) While some past studies have revealed the potential problems with using paid domestic labor, these studies were mostly based on a small non-representative sample, making it difficult to estimate the prevalence of the problems; (3) The factors related to employing foreign domestic helpers are mostly limited to the characteristics within the households, without much consideration on factors external to the families, such as the economic environment and social network. This proposed study is innovative theoretically and methodologically. Theoretically, the proposed study aims at developing a theoretical framework that integrates the social capital and life-course perspectives with existing theories in housework and domestic outsourcing literature to investigate the prevalence, timing and duration of employing live-in domestic help among married couples in Hong Kong, and to examine the factors, patterns and familial consequences of having a live-in helper. Methodologically, a mixed-methods research approach will be adopted. The first phase of the study consists of a large-scale representative household survey. The household survey will be the first of its kind to collect both cross-sectional and event-history data related to paid domestic labor. The second phase of the study consists of in-depth interviews with couples at different stage of employing foreign domestic helpers (informants will be sampled from the household survey) to reveal the deeper meanings of the relationships between the variables. 近年來香港雇用家庭傭工的比率越趨上升。在2011年，香港大約有15%的核心家庭聘用了全職家傭。在西方社會，一般家庭主要按時薪聘用工時較短的家務助理。然而，在雇用家傭的香港家庭中，有近九成家庭雇用全職居家外傭。故此，過往在西方家庭研究文獻中的研究成果並未能夠完全幫助我們了解家庭傭工在香港家庭關係中所擔當的角色。鑑於雇用全職家傭在香港家庭中的普遍性和重要性，本研究所得的數據將對家庭社會學的實證及理論文獻均作出貢獻，並為香港社會提供政策層面上的建議。 過往研究文獻主要有三方面不足。第一，大部分研究只依靠橫截面數據作研究分析，並且把雇用家傭簡單視為一項「二元」、「一次性」的決定。過往並無研究深入探討雇用家傭的時間軸因素(如雇用家傭的次數、時機和持續時間); 第二，雖然過去有些香港的研究已經指出了雇用家傭對家庭關係帶來的潛在問題，這些研究卻主要依靠小型和非代表性樣本的數據，故此難以估量這些問題在香港社會的普遍程度; 第三，過往研究主要集中探討家中因素和雇用家傭的關係，卻很大程度上忽略了家庭以外的因素(如經濟環境和朋輩間的資訊)如何影響雇用家傭的決定以及其對家庭關係的效果。 這項研究在理論和方法論方面均有其原創性。在理論方面，這項研究將致力把「社會資本」和「生命歷程」視角結合到現有的家務和家庭關係文獻中，並建立一個綜合的理論框架以分析香港家庭雇用家傭的普遍程度、時機、持續時間以及探討雇用家傭的因素、模式和對家庭的影響。在方法論方面，本研究將採用混合研究方法。在本研究的第一階段，研究員將在各區地址中抽取有代表性樣本並進行一項大型的住戶問卷調查。是項住戶問卷調查將會是同類研究中首個同時收集關於住戶聘用家傭的橫截面數據及回顧性事件歷史數據。在本研究的第二階段，研究員會在住戶問卷調查的受訪者中，抽取各類雇用家傭的家庭進行深入訪談以更深入了解是次研究中各變項之間的關係。

28603817.label: Realisation of objectives
28603817.value: All objectives have been achieved successfully. A representative household survey of married couples was successfully conducted. In total, 2,003 respondents (out of 2,943 addresses sampled) have completed the face-to-face interviews between October 2018 and June 2019. The response rate of the household survey was 68.1%. 25 in-depth interviews were conducted between 2019 and 2020. 1. With the representative household survey data that collected retrospective life-event histories, I estimated the one-year and longer-term prevalence rate of hiring live-in foreign domestic helpers (FDHs), timing and length of each employment. In the survey, 18.5% of the respondents were in the process of employing FDHs at the time of the survey, and 25.7% had employed FDHs in the past. A cohort-based event-history analysis revealed that married couples’ demand for FDHs has increased substantially in Hong Kong over the past 40 years. The proportions of respondents married in the 1980s who began to employ FDHs within one, five and ten years of their marriage were found to be 1.3%, 5% and 8%, respectively. The proportions rose substantially to 5.4%, 21% and 30% respectively for respondents who married in the 2010s. In addition, it is found that employing FDHs is a durable practice for many families. Survey data showed that married couples are now employing FDHs for longer periods of time. The proportions of respondents who married in the 1980s, previously employed FDHs, and had stopped hiring FDHs in the past one, five and ten years were 9%, 38% and 68%, respectively. The proportions dropped to 4%, 18% and 32% respectively for respondents who married in the 2010s. These findings were reported in the first publication (Journal of Family Issues). 2. In the project, I integrated the social capital and life-course perspectives in examining the factors of hiring FDHs. The survey data and in-depth interview data both showed that hiring domestic help is closely related to the transition to childbirth. Childbearing is an important factor in hiring help. Couples without children are much less likely to employ domestic help. The existing theoretical framework in domestic outsourcing often emphasizes resolving work-family conflict through hiring help. The survey and interview data showed that the main concern of hiring help was to focus on the demanding tasks of parenting. Couples hire help for a more refined division of labor that the mothers focus on parenting (especially education-related childcare tasks) while the chores are outsourced to the helpers. Besides, the data also showed that the decision of hiring help is not only associated with economic resources but also with the information and resources that are embedded in the social networks. Past studies often focus on the role of economic resources. This study contributed to the literature by showing that couples with family members and friends with live-in domestic helpers are more likely to hire help, controlling for their economic resources (such as income and wealth). The interview data show that lack of information and knowledge about handling the employer-employee relationship is a major barricade for couples to hire help. These findings were reported in the first publication (Journal of Family Issues). 3. This project examined the experience of employing FDHs with representative quantitative data. It is discovered that the practice of employing FDHs is unstable. Out of all the respondents who had employed FDHs, one-third of them had previously changed their helper. A quarter of them had replaced their helper in the first four years of their hiring history. Employers’ average satisfaction score for their FDHs was only 6.16 on a scale of 1 to 10. For respondents who are satisfied with their FDHs, and who grew up in families that had previously hired FDHs, their employment relationship with FDHs is more stable. However, the employment relationships for respondents who have more children, and an Indonesian FDH, tend to be less stable. Being economically well off, having the youngest child who is older in age, and an FDH who was recruited through personal networks were the factors associated with employers’ higher satisfaction with FDHs. To follow-up, I conducted in-depth interviews with couples who employed FDHs to examine the strategies in stabilizing the employment of FDHs. I found that the strategies are class-based, in which both economic, cultural and social capitals are important. In other words, lower-class families who employ FDHs face more difficulties in employing FDHs and hence with a lower level of stability and satisfaction with the practice. These findings are reported in the fourth paper (being invited for resubmission after revision). 4. The study also looked into the impact of the practice of employing FDHs on families, including time allocation, satisfaction with housework, and fertility rates. The research team focused on working married couples with at least one child who had employed FDHs. Analysis showed that this group of working fathers and mothers spent an average of 3.6 and 6.5 hours less per week respectively on housework, such as cooking, grocery shopping, cleaning, laundry and dish-washing compared to their counterparts who have not hired FDHs. It was also found that these working fathers and mothers spent an average of 2.9 and 3.4 hours more per week respectively on childcare, as compared to their counterparts without hiring FDHs; and they spent 1.7 and 3.7 hours per week respectively on managing the FDHs, including assigning tasks, providing training and performing quality control, after they had hired FDHs. The results are reported in the second publication (Current Sociology). I also conducted event-history analyses to examine the relationship between hiring FDHs and fertility behaviors. The survey data also suggests that the practice of hiring FDHs is positively associated with married couples’ fertility rates. Focusing on couples married after 2010, for those with one child who had employed FDHs, six years after their first child was born, there was a cumulative probability of 43.3% for giving birth to their second child, compared to 29.9% for those who had not employed FDHs. The results are reported in the fifth paper (invited by a journal for resubmission after revision). Besides, when compared with those who had not hired FDHs, it was also discovered that couples who had employed FDHs were on average 5% more satisfied with the housework arrangements and 9% happier with the spousal input in domestic labour. The results are reported in the sixth paper (being revised for another submission). 5. I examined how certain public policies are related to the trends and patterns of hiring FDHs. The lack of public housing is associated with smaller apartment sizes, which is associated with the lower tendency of hiring FDHs. On the other hand, the minimum salary for FDHs is relatively low as compared to the median income level of local residents. The relatively low wage level for FDHs has made it possible for lower-class families to employ FDHs over time. Analyzing the class composition of the employers over time, I found that a significant portion (around 25%) of employers of FDHs are not from a middle-class background. This has contributed to the trend of destabilization of employing FDHs (tendency to replace FDHs). This finding has been reported in the third publication (Asia-Pacific Migration Journal), in which I examined the middle-class thesis of domestic outsourcing that is commonly held in the literature.

28603817.label: Major findings and research outcome
28603817.value: 1. Recently married couples have a higher rate of employing FDHs. More than 30% of the recently married couples employed FDHs within the first ten years of marriage. Need-based, resource-based and willingness-based factors were positively associated with hiring FDHs (Journal of Family Issues). Yet, it is erroneous to assume that employing FDHs is a middle-class practice, 25% of the families employing FDHs are with an SES score below the median (Asia-Pacific Migration Journal). 2. Employing FDHs is a durable practice in Hong Kong. Most families with FDHs hire help for more than 15 years now. The proportions of respondents previously employed FDHs, and had stopped hiring FDHs in the past one, five and ten years were 4%, 18% and 32%, for respondents who married in the 2010s. Wealth, the presence of young child and wife's full-time employment are positively associated with the length of employing FDHs (Journal of Family Issues). 3. The practice of employing FDHs remains unstable. A quarter of them had replaced their helper in the first four years of their hiring history. Employers’ average satisfaction score for their FDHs was only 6.16 (out of 10). For respondents who are satisfied with their FDHs, and who grew up in families that had previously hired FDHs, their employment relationship with FDHs is more stable. However, the employment relationships for respondents who have more children, and an Indonesian FDH, tends to be less stable (The fourth paper). 4. The time-saving effect of employing FDHs is not significant. Working fathers and mothers with FDHs spent an average of 3.6 and 6.5 hours less per week on housework, but also an average of 2.9 and 3.4 hours more per week on childcare, as compared to their counterparts without hiring FDHs; and they spent 1.7 and 3.7 hours per week respectively on managing the FDHs. (Current Sociology) 5. Couples with FDHs are generally more satisfied with housework arrangements and perceive their partners' domestic labor input as adequate. However, hiring FDHs is not associated with fairness perception and marital conflict (The sixth paper) 6. The practice of hiring FDHs is positively associated with married couples’ fertility rates. Focusing on couples married after 2010, for those with one child who had employed FDHs, there was a cumulative probability of 43.3% for giving birth to their second child when the first child is six years old, compared to 29.9% for those without FDHs (The fifth paper).

28603817.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
28603817.value: There are several findings that shed light on new directions of future research. First, it is found that fertility behaviors differ between families with and without FDHs. However, the research design has its limitation in providing solid evidence of causal effects. More research will be conducted in the future with quasi-experimental data to further confirm whether causal effects exist. Second, I showed that there is now a significant portion of employers of FDHs are from a working-class background. Most of the past studies mainly targeted middle-class families in studying the experience of employing FDHS. This study provides interesting data to study the experience among some working-class families. To further explore the experience among working-class couples that employ FDHs, I will further conduct more in-depth interviews with employers with a lower-class background. Lastly, Hong Kong is not the only society with a high rate of employing FDHs. Singapore also has a high rate of employing FDHs. Some families in Taiwan also employ FDHs as caregivers of family members in need. The data collected from this study can serve as a basis for comparative study in the future, helping sociologists to understand how factors, patterns and consequences of employing FDHs vary across contexts.

28603817.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
28603817.value: The researcher has conducted a household survey and interviews between 2018 and 2020. It is found that married couples’ demand for FDHs has increased substantially over the past 40 years. The practice of employing FDHs is also becoming more durable. Married couples are now employing FDHs for longer periods of time. However, the practice is unstable. Out of all the respondents who had employed FDHs, one-third of them had previously changed their helper. A quarter of them had replaced their helper in the first four years of their hiring history. The study categorized the factors that affect married couples’ decision-making about whether they should hire or stop hiring FDHs into need-based, resource-based and willingness-based factors. Need-based factors. The decision to start employing FDHs is closely related to the wife’s employment commitments and childcare needs, as well as the respondent’s personal experience and perception of the practice of hiring FDHs. The practice of employing FDHs brought some impacts on the families. While couples employing FDHs spent fewer hours in housework, they spent additional hours on childcare and managing FDHs, offsetting the time-saving effect. Yet, couples with FDHs are happier with the housework arrangement, and hence, more likely to have an additional child.

28604017.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28604017.value: In teaching and teacher education, while much attention has been paid to teacher expertise and its influences on classroom teaching, there is a lack of research on teacher educators’ expertise and how it exhibits and develops in their everyday work. In fact, expertise emerges from and continues to (re)shape teacher educators’ professional work and social interactions. Given their multiple responsibilities (e.g., teaching, research and community service) and the complex higher education context they belong to, teacher educators are constantly developing and modifying their expertise in order to promote the effectiveness of teacher education. A focus on teacher educators’ expertise can thus shed light on how they practice teacher education and seek continuing development in their embedded institutional and socio-cultural contexts. Over the past decades, with the growing importance of English as a lingua franca in international business and cultural communication, the field of second language education has become an important enterprise in many English-as-a-foreign-language (EFL) contexts, including Hong Kong. Central to this enterprise is a large number of EFL teacher educators who play a pivotal role in preparing future generations of English teachers in order to serve an increasing number of students of diverse linguistic and socio-cultural backgrounds. However, as residents in the higher education academe, EFL teacher educators may face a range of challenges (e.g., limited professional support and the “publish-or-perish” syndrome) in their daily practice and development. Against such a backdrop, there is a need for research on how EFL teacher educators develop their expertise in order to navigate potential contextual obstacles and improve their teacher education practice. To date, teacher educators’ expertise remains an underexplored and poorly understood concept in teacher education. In particular, we know little about what it means to be an effective EFL teacher educator and how he/she demonstrates and develops expertise in the complex higher education settings. To fill this gap, the proposed study, drawing on a complexity theory perspective and adopting an ethnographic case study design, seeks to explore EFL teacher educators’ expertise in Hong Kong. The study will make a theoretical contribution to our understanding of teacher educator expertise by shedding light on its subject-specific and context-sensitive nature as well as its developmental process mediated by various influencing factors at personal, institutional and societal levels. The study can also generate implications on how to support teacher educators’ professional development at different stages of their career in higher education. 在教學和教師教育中，大部分學者都在關注教師專長及其對課堂教學的影響，卻缺少對教師教育者專長及其在職業工作中發展的研究。教師教育者專長來源於其專業工作和社會交往，又反過來對其專業工作和社會交往產生重大影響。考慮到教師教育者的工作的多樣性（例如教學、研究和社群服務），以及他們所處的複雜高等教育環境，教師教育者需要不斷發展和完善自身專長並提升其工作的有效性。關注教師教育者專長可以揭示他們如何從事教師教育實踐以及如何在其所屬的組織和社會文化背景下尋求可持續發展。 過去幾十年裡，英語作為國際商務和文化交流通用語的重要性不斷提升。第二語言教育在很多英語作為外語的國家，包括香港，已成為一項重要事業， 而這項事業的核心是大量的“以英語為外語”的教師教育者。為了能服務越來越多的不同語言和社會文化背景的學生，教師教育者在培養未來的英語教師方面起著關鍵作用。然而，作為高等教育領域的專業人員，外語教師教育者的日常工作和專業發展可能面臨一系列挑戰，如有限的專業支持和研究發表壓力等。在此背景下，研究外語教師教育者如何為了應對潛在的環境阻礙並發展自身專長就顯得尤為必要。 到目前為止，教師教育者專長在教師教育領域仍是一個不被足夠瞭解、有待探索的概念。我們對外語教師教育者如何在複雜的高等教育環境下運用並發展其專長知之甚少。為了填補這一空白，本研究基於複雜性理論視角，採用民族志案例研究設計，探索香港外語教師教育者的專長。通過探究教師教育者專長的學科特異性、環境敏感性的本質，理解其發展過程和個人、制度的和社會層面的影響因素，本研究可增強對教師教育者專長的理解。同時，本研究還能為如何支持高校教師教育者職業生涯不同階段的專業發展提供啟示。

28604017.label: Realisation of objectives
28604017.value: The three research objectives have been achieved through a rigorous process of data collection and analysis in the project. In the following, the research process is first presented in detail. Then, how the three research objectives are met in the project is explained. The research process While the research proposal stipulated six participants would be recruited in the project, the PI invited seven language teacher educators from different local universities to join the study in order to enrich the dataset. Among the seven participants, two were regarded as experienced teacher educators with more than 20 years of teacher education experience, three as mid-career teacher educators with more than 10 years of experience, and two as novice having one to two years of experience. Despite their different career stages and professional titles (one professor, one senior lecturer, and five assistant professors), all the teacher educators had been involved in various activities in language teacher education, including teaching pedagogy courses, supervising teaching practicum, and conducting academic research about language teaching/learning. Their experience can shed light on EFL teacher educators’ expertise attributes and its development in their situated institutional and socio-cultural context. Based on the ethnographic case study approach, multiple sources of data, including interview, field observation, relevant artefacts, and informal conversation, were collected from the participants over an academic year. At the beginning of the project, all the seven teacher educators joined an individual semi-structured interview with the PI, which focused on their professional backgrounds, their motivations to become teacher educators, and their previous experiences in language teaching and teacher education. Based on the conceptual framework (i.e., complexity theory), the participants were also asked to reflect on how they practiced teacher education and interacted with pre- and in-service language teachers, their personal values and beliefs about language teaching and teacher education, as well as the opportunities and challenges involved in their daily practice and expertise development. In the second interview (conduced with six teacher educators except TE2) at the end of the academic year, with reference to the field observational data, the participants were guided to reflect on how their expertise informed their practices (e.g., classroom teaching, practicum supervision, and research) and how their professional engagements in turn contributed to their expertise growth (if any). Furthermore, they were asked to identify the critical factors that may facilitate or impede their teacher education practices and expertise development. Each interview, around 90 minutes, was conducted in English and audio-recorded for transcription and analysis. In-between the two rounds of interview, field observation was conducted to examine the participants’ expertise and its development in their daily practice. The frequency and time of observation depended on the participants’ availability, preference and their institutional policy. The participants were observed in their teacher education courses with different focuses such as grammar and vocabulary teaching, technology use in language classrooms, as well as educational reforms and teacher leadership. A total of eight courses (27 sessions and around three hours per session) were observed by PI and his research assistant. In addition, the participants were also observed in other professional activities such as research seminars, practical workshops and project meetings (with local school teachers and other teacher educators) to enrich the dataset. Based on the research questions and conceptual framework, the observations mainly focused on how the teacher educators demonstrated and applied their expertise in their situated work (e.g., how they designed and implemented teaching tasks and how they interacted with language teachers in professional activities) to promote teacher learning. The observations were audio-recorded with field notes taken. Relevant artifacts such as course handouts and personal reflections were also collected to offer additional information about the participants’ expertise as language teacher educators. Furthermore, the PI and the participants engaged in continuing informal communication (e.g., email and WhatsApp exchanges) about their teacher education practice over the academic year. Such informal communication served as an additional source of data for understanding their teacher educator expertise. A qualitative and inductive data analytic approach was adopted to analyze the data. First, informed by the complexity theory perspective, the transcribed interview data were coded to identify the components of the participants' expertise and influencing factors. Following the interview analysis, the observation data and relevant documents were repeatedly reviewed, which served to confirm, modify and refine the expertise attributes identified in the interview data. The analysis resulted in various critical episodes that illustrated the participants' expertise attributes (e.g., engaging in reflective dialogues with student teachers and responding to their emotional needs) in practice. Afterwards, a cross-case comparison was conducted to compare, contrast, and integrate the various forms of expertise exhibited by the participants, leading to the final interpretation of language teacher educators’ expertise as a multi-faceted, adaptive, and contextualized process. To ensure the validity of the findings, the PI and his research assistant analyzed the data individually and engaged in rounds of discussion to reach a consensus on the analysis results. Member checking was also conducted by inviting the participants to comment on the preliminary findings. Meeting the three research objectives The project has generated rich and in-depth data to meet its three research objectives. First of all, data collected from interviews and field observation shed light on the critical attributes of the EFL teacher educators’ expertise at different career stages as well as how they applied such expertise to their professional practice (i.e., the first objective). Specifically, through semi-structured interviews, the participants shared their critical knowledge (e.g., about language teaching practice and research) and dispositions (e.g., reflective thinking and a sense of mission) in guiding their everyday work. Based on an analysis of field observation data and relevant documents, their professional qualities and practice (e.g., a flexible and student-centered teaching approach) also came to light as evidence of their teacher educator expertise. Based on the data from in-depth interviews and informal communication over one academic year, the second objective, which concerns the participants’ expertise development and influencing factors, was also met. By inviting the participants to reflect on their past and ongoing learning experience (particularly their gains and challenges), the project reveals a complex and dynamic process of their expertise development arising from their constant negotiation of meaning within and across their situated communities. A range of personal (e.g., emotions and self-agency) and contextual factors (e.g., collegial support and university policy) were also identified by comparing and contrasting their professional experiences in different institutional contexts. Finally, based on the findings in relation to the first two research objectives, the project has generated practical implications on teacher educator development in higher education (i.e., the third objective). Specifically, the findings can serve as a frame of reference for teacher educators to examine their current professional practice and identify directions for future expertise development at cognitive (e.g., contextualized knowledge), emotional (e.g., maintaining emotional wellbeing) and social levels (e.g., boundary crossing engagement). Furthermore, the project offers recommendations for university management on how to create a positive and balanced work environment to facilitate (language) teacher educators’ long-term expertise development in the complex, shifting professional work context.

28604017.label: Major findings and research outcome
28604017.value: Informed by the complexity theory perspective, this projects sheds light on the multi-faceted, adaptive, and dynamic nature of language teacher educators’ expertise in the higher education context of Hong Kong. Specifically, the findings reveal that language teacher educators' expertise entails various attributes including 1) a dialogic teaching approach informed by research-based and contextualized knowledge; 2) emotional intelligence for maintaining personal emotional wellbeing and channeling emotions for effective teaching; 3) a reflective and agentive mindset for continuous learning; and 4) willingness and capacity to promote and distribute expertise in dynamic systems. The participants’ expertise, derived from their reflective practice and continuing engagement (e.g., course teaching, practicum supervision, and research practice), is not a fixed product but an ever-changing process influenced by a wide array of personal (e.g., personal visions and self-agency) and external factors (e.g., students’ needs, collegial support, and institutional requirements). In terms of their expertise development, despite their personal backgrounds and career stages (i.e., novice, mid-career or experienced), the participants always try to foster and hone their expertise though social practice and interactions, and their newly acquired expertise reciprocally inform their daily practice and add fuel to their continuing expertise growth within and across their situated communities. Further, the participants’ expertise growth is accompanied by their identity (re)construction as they constantly created and transformed their self-understanding as language teacher educators. On the other hand, the project reveals that the ‘publish-or-perish’ syndrome prevalent in current higher education setting can exert detrimental influences on language teacher educators’ professional practice and expertise development. Particularly for novice teacher educators, they are likely to withdraw from their investment and efforts in teacher education in the face of stringent requirement on research productivity in higher education. So far, the research findings of the project have been reported in two research papers published in SSCI-indexed journals (please see Part C). While one paper (Yuan, 2020) analyzes how novice teacher educators developed their expertise and identities at the beginning years of their work in language teacher education, the other paper (Yuan & Yang, 2020) sheds light on the power of boundary crossing in facilitating language teacher educators’ expertise building. In addition, the PI disseminated the research findings through three presentations in different international conferences. In the future, the PI will continue to probe the data from diverse perspectives and produce more outputs (i.e., research seminars and publications such as book chapters and journal articles).

28604017.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
28604017.value: Based on the research findings derived from the project, three directions are identified for future research: 1. The findings of the project point to the need for teacher educators to maintain their own emotional balance and to create an open and safe learning environment for language teachers. Thus, it is meaningful to further explore how language teacher educators cope with emotionally challenging situations (e.g., ethical dilemmas) and construct their emotional intelligence for continuing development. 2. Future research can also recruit language teacher educators from different socio-cultural contexts (e.g., Macau, Taiwan, and mainland China) and investigate their professional practice and expertise. Such a comparative perspective can expand our knowledge of teacher educator expertise and its development in relation to specific socio-cultural settings. 3. Methodologically, the study followed the participants (two novice, three mid-career, and two experienced) for one academic year. It would be meaningful to adopt a longitudinal research design and track the participants’ expertise growth as they move across different career stages (e.g., from novice to mid-career) over time. In light of the proposed research directions, the PI will apply for new research grants in collaboration with scholars with similar research interest in Hong Kong and other educational contexts.

28604017.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
28604017.value: This project examines English-as-a-foreign-language (EFL) teacher educators’ expertise in the higher education context of Hong Kong. The project reveals a complex set of EFL teacher educators’ expertise attributes, such as their rich and contextualized knowledge about language learning and teaching, their adaptive and flexible teaching approaches, as well as their reflective and agentive abilities. Despite their career stages, the teacher educators’ expertise derives from their ongoing engagement in different forms of professional practice (e.g., classroom teaching, practicum supervision and academic research) within and across different communities (e.g., university and schools). Their expertise development is also influenced by a wide range of personal (e.g., previous teaching experience and personal values) and contextual factors (e.g., university support and policy). In particular, the participants are subject to the “publish-or-perish” system in higher education, which poses challenges to their professional engagement and expertise growth in university settings. The findings of the project can help EFL teacher educators analyze and evaluate their current professional practice and influencing factors as well as identify directions for future expertise development. Some useful implications are also provided for university management on how to facilitate EFL teacher educators’ continuous learning in Hong Kong and other similar EFL contexts.

28604117.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28604117.value: This project attempts to thoroughly study the melodies of tōgaku (Tang music) in Motomasa no Fue-fu (The Flute Score of Motomasa), an early twelfth-century Japanese source. Tōgaku was a repertory of entertainment music imported from China between the seventh and the ninth centuries, and was widely performed by musicians and aristocrats at the imperial court until its decline in the late fourteenth century. Japanese musicians compiled a large number of musical scores for the purposes of preservation and transmission of this repertory in Japan. Numerous reliable manuscript copies of these historical scores, together with a small number of the originals, have survived in Japan to the present. Although substantial research has been conducted on the development of tōgaku in the light of the music recorded in historical scores compiled before the end of the fourteenth century, a crucial question remains to be answered. This pertains to the background for the emergence of a new system of rhythmic signs in the notation compiled in the eleventh and the twelfth centuries. This system of rhythmic signs signifies a slightly different rhythmic structure of the melodies when compared with the structure indicated by the standard system. As historians of Japanese music know only too well, the importation of Chinese entertainment music was in fact part of the large-scale adoption of Chinese culture. This adoption was followed by a long process of assimilation of the imported culture in accordance with the needs of the Japanese. Given that the new system of rhythmic sign emerged in the period when the assimilation of Chinese culture reached its peak, it was likely the product of this assimilation. A thorough study of the tōgaku notation in Motomasa no Fue-fu may, therefore, shed important light on the development of this system of rhythmic signs since the score notates the tōgaku melodies performed during the apogee of adaptation of Chinese culture, namely the tenth and the eleventh centuries. This project will first elucidate and decipher the tablature signs and notational symbols in Motomasa no Fue-fu, and then followed by a transcription of the tōgaku notation. Through a comprehensive analysis of the transcribed melodies together with the textual information in Motomasa no Fue-fu, the project aims at uncovering the background for the use of a new system of rhythmic signs in the tōgaku notation and its cultural implications for the assimilation of Chinese cultures in Heian-period Japan.

28605717.label: Realisation of objectives
28605717.value: 1. APPLY interdisciplinary research methods and INTERSECT cultural studies, anthropology, and critical theories in the area of museum study of China. [Ethnography] During field trips to Shanghai, structured around long-term personal relationships with various players in the art world, the PI has gathered first-hand experience and novel insights concerning how day-to-day practice, social action, and built environment inform the institutional structure and fabrics of the broader live-world. [Topology] This project also adopted Heidegger’s notion of “topology” in order to understand how spatial setting and constituent parts of the three museums are interrelated or arranged. This concept offered the PI a framework to observe and portray the stories of the three museums in order to map the interconnectedness of the objects they contain. The PI’s experiences in these locations further offered insights into how various distinct locations are interconnected in a set of relationships. [Insights concerning museum study] By synthesizing various field experiences, such as observing exhibition designs, collections, architectural arrangements and audience interactions, as well as understanding the rationale of the key players through in-depth interviews, this project explores the roles of the three museums in Shanghai society. In addition to the exploration of activities and audience engagement, collecting and curatorial direction, public program and education, this project expanded the scope of museum studies by exemplifying a phenomenon in China—the establishment and operation of museums being mediated by private collectors, real estate companies, the state within expanding field of contemporary art as a strategy to facilitate economic growth, increase the cultural profile of the city, produce middle-class values, and sustain the state’s power structure. As such, this project intersected various theories and further articulated museology in China in a broader context. 2. QUESTION the relationship of contemporary art to the state under the backdrop of the current cultural policy. This project studied the cultural policy of the 19th CCP National Congress and questioned how the establishment of the three museums are mediated by the policy framework characterized by the promotion of “cultural soft power.” Particularly, this project studied how the 19th CCP National Congress contemplated the integration and development of leisure life and culture, as well as the promotion of cultural heritage and revolutionary culture to deepen role of the collective “socialist spiritual civilization” and acknowledged the present moment as a decisive period for building a “moderately well-off society” in all areas. The cases studied in this project show a coexistence of top-down mandates and bottom-up initiatives where commercial, artistic, and political pursuits increasingly converge. At Long Museum, the West Bund branch discursively linked with other newly established recreational and cultural activities, the promenade complex provided residences with a chance to exercise and relax. At the Pudong branch, the permanent collection “Revolutionary Art Since the Yan’an Era” aligns with the cultural policy which emphasized the promotion of historical narrative concerning the CCP’s past, which subsequently serves as a tool to nurture and edify the public through exhibition and educational programs. As such, this project illustrated how the state- and history-induced pictures of selfhood has been articulated in the consumption of art. 3. STUDY how the establishment of contemporary art museums has become an important benchmark of cultural reform and urban renewal. This project studied how urban renewal projects are closely related to museum establishments, as well as how urbanization in Shanghai occurs under the framework of its cultural reform initiatives. In order to demonstrate the extent to which culture has become a major motivating factor behind the urbanization trajectory, this project studied the history of how land has been altered by studying the locations of the three museums. For example, Minsheng Art Museum, founded by financial institution Minsheng Banking Corporation, was first established in Red Town on Huaihai Middle Road in 2010, which subsequently opened another branch in the former French pavilion of the 2010 World Expo. This case reeals that museums enjoy a relatively short life-span in Shanghai in which both branches were closed alongside with the rapid process of gentrification. This project illustrated how the two branches of Minsheng Art Museum have helped transform the formerly low-value area, such as an abandoned steel plant and a former exhibition building, into highly valued districts. Museum’s functions, including its role economically and socially, have proven to be short-lived. The former world expo district is transforming itself into a larger art, commercial and residential district, including a new museum in collaboration with the Pompidou and a film production warehouse working with Dreamworks. Many of these museums are further replaced by bigger culture-led urban regeneration projects, making cultural development an endless cycle enveloped by the real-estate market. 4. ILLUSTRATE the social networks and geographic spaces of art in relation to a broader cultural and urban landscape of Shanghai. The PI has interviewed several key players associated with the museums, including Justine Alexandria, Director of Yuz Museum; Zoe Cheung, Assistant Curator of HOW Museum, Ramen Hsieh, Senior Curator of Rockbund Art Museum, Vivian Li, Operation Manager of of Rockbund Art Museum; Yu Yuan; Media Relation Officer of Rockbund Art Museum; and many artists such as Lu Yang. This project took the spatial dimensions into account and acknowledged how the newly established museums enable players in the charismatic-networking game within the art world. For example, Justine Alexandria transformed herself from an environmental science graduate to a museum director. As the daughter of a billionaire who owns one of the biggest food processing companies, she learned art from scratch and now manages all aspects of her father’s museum, from collecting art to fundraising for her foundation and networking with government officials. The daily routine of her exemplifies how players and art institutions function together by forming social networks through the establishment of museums. Under the logic of market-driven economy, these players deployed strategies to their own ends, networked with other players within and outside the art world, and ultimately have survived by breaking, playing by, or re-inventing rules in their everyday life. In addition, these museums attracted the newly emerged middle-class shoppers, businessmen and residents, forming a much broader complex chains of commodity culture. 5. ARCHIVE photographs, found text and exhibition catalogues by using visual anthropological methods. This project collected over 2000 pictures and 50 exhibition catalogues, books, and other printed materials. By comparing the collected materials with pictures the PI has taken previously, this project sheds light on the process of change, the relationships between place and culture, and the dynamics of museum and urban developments in Shanghai. 6. ORGANIZE a seminar with museum practitioners and artists to share and test the findings. The PI has curated a seminar at Photofair Shanghai, panel members includes artist Hon Ho, Kelvin Kyung Kun Park and Birdhead, as well as art critic Li Bowen. 7. Produce two journal essays: 1) ANALYZE the conceptual underpinnings in contemporary Chinese art history 2) REPORT critically my ethnographic data and CONCLUDE my research with an evaluation of the sustainability of cultural industry in China. The PI is consolidating the two journal essays and they are ready for journal submission by the first quarter of 2021.
